El-Sayed and Rogers are vying for the seat held by retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters in a race that could determine whether Democrats gain the four seats needed to take control of the Senate. Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority. El-Sayed has built a narrow lead in opinion polls by focusing on affordability, healthcare and reducing the influence of money in politics. Rogers has sought to undermine El-Sayed’s support among Jewish voters by highlighting his criticism of Israel’s offensive in Gaza and alleging longstanding family ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, one of the Arab world’s oldest and most influential Islamist groups. Strategists said the focus on the Muslim Brotherhood also seeks to exploit economic tensions between Black voters and Michigan’s large Arab-American community. Rogers has cited old social media posts by El-Sayed’s half-sister alleging that their mother was involved with the organisation in the 1970s. El-Sayed has disavowed the Muslim Brotherhood, denied any connection to the group and said he was not raised by his mother. His parents divorced when he was three, and he was raised by his father and stepmother. Asked about Rogers’ strategy, campaign spokesperson Alyssa Brouillet said El-Sayed’s “extremist positions” on issues ranging from prisons to the Muslim Brotherhood were alienating Michiganders. El-Sayed campaign spokesperson Roxie Richner said Rogers was trying to distract from the economic effects of Trump’s agenda. “Independent fact-checkers have repeatedly debunked Mike’s lies, but their campaign continues to use bad faith attacks on Abdul’s faith and family,” she said. ‘Proud to be an American’ Rogers emphasised the Muslim Brotherhood issue during this week’s televised debate, questioning El-Sayed’s loyalty to the United States. “If you are going to go to the United States Senate, we need to know: are you for America or are you for these terrorist groups overseas?” Rogers asked. El-Sayed, the son of Egyptian immigrants who would become the first Muslim elected to the US Senate if he wins, called the question shameful. “It’s actually quite beneath you, Mike,” he replied. “I am proud of America. I’m proud to be an American. I’m proud of our Constitution that guarantees all of us the right to pray as we choose to pray.” Rogers, a former congressman, US Army officer and FBI agent, later appealed directly to Democrats who had voted for Stevens, saying they had a place with him if they considered El-Sayed too “extreme”. Michigan Senate race a ‘toss-up’ It remains unclear whether the Republican strategy is working. Independent political analysts rate the race a toss-up, while polls show El-Sayed with an average lead of 2.6 percentage points, according to RealClearPolling.com. El-Sayed has recently campaigned with prominent Black political figures, including Senator Raphael Warnock of Georgia, Representative Ayanna Pressley of Massachusetts and 2024 Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris. Former President Barack Obama, who has endorsed El-Sayed, is due to campaign with him on Saturday. Michigan Democratic Party Black Caucus Chair Keith Williams, who backed Stevens in the primary and is now working to rally support for El-Sayed, acknowledged tensions between the Black and Arab-American communities. Read More: US, South Korean officials see little chance of Trump-Kim meeting this year “We have to work through our differences,” Williams told Reuters. “At the end of the day, this election is bigger than our differences because we cannot have a senator going to Washington and supporting Donald Trump’s policies.” Some strategists said the attacks may have come too late to reshape the race and could backfire if voters view them as anti-Muslim. “I don’t know what this does for them,” said Jim Zogby, a longtime pollster and co-founder of the Arab American Institute, which advocates for the Arab-American community. “There are people who think Haitians eat cats and dogs and think anybody with an Arabic name is either a terrorist or a member of the Muslim Brotherhood. But that’s a much smaller group of people — and it’s already a Republican group of people.” Overwhelming support from black voters A September Emerson College poll showed El-Sayed had 81% support among Black voters, who make up about a quarter of Michigan Democrats. “There was no sign there in mid-September of erosion of Black support for El-Sayed. I would not suspect that the number would have changed much over the last month,” said Matt Taglia, senior director of Emerson College Polling. Democrat Jocelyn Benson, who is running for Michigan governor, scored four percentage points higher in the same poll, while Harris received 86% of the Black vote in 2024. Michigan pollster Steve Mitchell said weaker support among Black and Jewish voters could cost El-Sayed as many as 20,000 votes. Rogers lost his 2024 Senate bid to Democrat Elissa Slotkin by a similar margin.

title: 31,000 consumers denied petrol subsidy
description: Govt orders audit of fuel stations, rectification of registration errors
content: Thousands of petrol consumers have been denied subsidies, announced last month to provide relief to motorcycle, rickshaw and small car owners in the face of elevated international oil prices, but the system has exposed faults. Sources told The Express Tribune that a high-level meeting was held where the issue was taken up. During the meeting, it was informed that 31,000 consumers had been denied subsidy. The minister for petroleum asked about progress on the removal of token expiry, where the meeting was informed that 10,344 tokens had expired. The minister for IT and telecom highlighted that a survey message went to approximately 31,000 citizens whose tokens had expired, offering four reasons for non-redemption. Of these, 11,000 cited lack of time while work continued with the Petroleum Dealers Association (PDA) on the expired tokens. The chair observed that refusal at fuel stations and technical failure should be read together, since a citizen learnt about the system fault from the station staff. It was emphasised that the IT ministry should send a follow-up message to approximately 13,000 citizens, who cited refusal or a technical fault, encouraging them to visit a station again and rebook. A brief complaint sheet should also be prepared. The IT minister revealed that 3,000 calls had been received by the 9771 helpline, of which around 400 were resolved at the first level. Punjab accounted for 1,700 calls and Sindh 618. Around 972 complaints were related to registration matters, 414 pertained to province mismatch, 72 were about incomplete registration and 250 were related to duplicate registration attempts, which required verification. Punjab reported negligible refusal due to continuous field inspection, Sindh below 1% and Gilgit-Baltistan none. Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa reported that out of the 200 complainants contacted directly, four cited refusal, with each traced to a temporary internet outage. The chair nonetheless cautioned against reliance on helpline statistics alone as citizens sometimes left without lodging a complaint. The chair noted that four million redemptions across about 8,000 stations yielded a national average of nearly 500 per station and set a benchmark of 50 redemptions below which a station must be audited. The minister said that deputy commissioners could now download city-wise station lists from the dashboard. The minister of state for finance said that visits to 40 to 45 stations revealed that both citizens and station staff mistakenly believed that a motorcycle must be registered in the applicant's name. He noted that inter-city stations primarily served motorcycles, while highway stations catered to long-haul traffic. Additionally, he mentioned that Qingqi drivers with valid documents were encountering system errors. It was decided that provincial and district administrations should audit every station recording fewer than 50 redemptions, monitor the highest-volume stations in each city and deploy additional devices where queues were found. Also, the provincial administrations shall publicise the requirement to lodge a complaint in the event of refusal. The IT ministry shall circulate city-wise station lists to public affairs units for station-by-station feedback on the refusal of service. The meeting was further informed that the Ministry of IT would obtain from the call centre the specific causes of incomplete registration and would brief the relevant committee. It will share the remaining complaint logs with K-P for making direct contact with complainants. The ministry shall correct through public messaging the belief that a motorcycle must be registered in the applicant's name and shall report within two days the proportion of registered motorcyclists whose identity cards match the title. Assistant commissioners will compile the list of Qingqi rickshaw drivers holding a valid identity and excise documents to facilitate their registration.

title: Minister seeks loan relief as 25% rates bite
description: Says rescheduling loans could revive industry; PM tells LCCI govt working closely with private sector
content: Federal Minister for Communications Abdul Aleem Khan has called for measures to reduce industrial production costs, including rescheduling loans of affected businesses, acknowledging that running enterprises at an interest rate of 25% was extremely difficult, and has urged the government to direct banks to consider relief for industrialists hit by economic difficulties. Addressing a meeting at the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) on Saturday, Khan said he had already submitted proposals to the prime minister to reduce production costs and would present the business community's recommendations to the government, adding that he would continue efforts to resolve business-related issues within his authority. "It was extremely difficult to run a business by borrowing at an interest rate of 25%," he said, arguing that rescheduling could help affected firms resume operations. Briefing business representatives on the National Highway Authority's (NHA) finances and infrastructure projects, the minister said the authority's annual revenue stood at around Rs66 billion when he assumed responsibility approximately two and a half years ago, and that its target for the current year has been set at Rs160 billion. He said a substantial portion of NHA revenue was consumed by salaries, road repairs, routine maintenance and rehabilitation of bridges and roads damaged by floods. Expenditure had been capped at around Rs50 billion, while additional revenue from toll taxes and other sources was planned to be channelled into new road projects. Khan said Rs224 billion had been allocated for ongoing projects under the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP), with most funds earmarked for national highways in Balochistan. On connectivity, he said work was under way on a proposed Lahore-Islamabad route that would reduce the distance between the two cities from approximately 380 kilometres to 280 kilometres, improving connectivity for Gujranwala, Gujrat, Lala Musa, Kharian and Jhelum. He said additional toll revenue from the Faisalabad Motorway had helped make the project possible, and announced plans to expand the Sialkot Motorway from four lanes to six, while the Lahore-to-Khyber Motorway was targeted for completion in 2027. The Balochistan Expressway was expected next year and the Peshawar Northern Bypass next month. Separately, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif told a delegation of the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) Founders Group that the government was working with the private sector to promote economic activity and create an environment conducive to business, at a meeting that discussed the economic situation, trade promotion and industry's challenges. The delegation apprised the prime minister of the issues faced by the business community and shared its proposals, and emphasised mutual cooperation in promoting industry, increasing investment and expanding trade. It acknowledged the services he rendered to the chamber during his tenure as its president. Federal Ministers for Law and Justice Azam Nazeer Tarar, for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar and for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik also attended. WITH ADDITIONAL INPUT FROM APP

title: Glitch bars new resident taxpayers
description: IRIS portal does not allow returning Pakistanis to enter wealth balance in returns
content: With only a week left in the twice-extended deadline for filing income tax returns, the previously non-resident but now resident Pakistanis are facing a unique problem as they are barred from disclosing their wealth in this year's returns. The restriction on stating the opening wealth position for the tax year seemed a technical glitch on the part of Pakistan Revenue Automation Limited in return documents for the last tax year. The deadline to submit returns with all benefits of being a filer is going to end next Saturday. The Karachi Tax Bar Association has written to the member operations of the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to fix the glitch, which otherwise could create serious legal problems for people who have become resident Pakistanis. The association stated that a specific restriction in the Wealth Reconciliation Statement was creating difficulties for individuals returning to Pakistan after a period of non-residence. Under the income tax law, if a Pakistani lives abroad for a certain number of days in a year, the person becomes a non-resident Pakistani for tax purposes. The tax bar stated that the difficulty arose because the Inland Revenue Information System (IRIS) web portal automatically populated the opening wealth balance from the last filed Wealth Statement and did not allow that balance to be edited. Where an individual resumes resident status after the intervening years of non-residence, the system therefore retains the wealth balance reported before that period, rather than allowing the appropriate opening balance for the relevant tax year to be entered. "This has created a reconciliation difficulty where no wealth statements are required under Section 116(2) of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 during the intervening years," it added. The individuals who have returned to Pakistan and become residents are now required to furnish the Wealth Statement and Wealth Reconciliation Statement for tax year 2026. However, the IRIS automatically carries forward the wealth balance for the last period of being the resident Pakistani into the non-editable opening balance field. This prevents the individual from entering the appropriate opening wealth balance for tax year 2026 and reconciling the movement in wealth for that year, as contemplated by Section 116(2). The Karachi tax bar stated that under the self-assessment and declaration framework of income tax laws, a taxpayer should have the liberty to declare the opening wealth balance on the basis of relevant information and records, subject to applicable provisions of the law. It asked the FBR, that without prejudice to this broader position, to resolve the matter by modifying the relevant validation on IRIS to permit returning individuals to enter the appropriate opening wealth balance for the relevant tax year. This will enable them to reconcile the movement in wealth for that year without requiring a reconciliation spanning the intervening years of non-residence. The FBR is currently undergoing a period of uncertainty after a proposal to either establish a new tax agency or outsource some of the functions was shot down by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. The Inland Revenue Service officers had threatened to observe a pen-down strike against any such move. The association had taken back the deadline following assurance from the FBR member operations that no adverse action would be taken. However, subsequently, the FBR suspended two officers and posted another seven in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan on suspicion of being behind the pen-down strike move. This has created uncertainty in the organisation and could also undermine its work, according to multiple taxmen who spoke to The Express Tribune on condition of anonymity.

title: 'Indian duty-free access threatens GSP Plus edge'
description: Exporters say EU-India, UK-India trade deals could erode advantage; call for lower costs
content: Textile exporters have warned that duty-free access for Indian textile products to European Union (EU) and British markets under the EU-India free trade agreement and the United Kingdom-India trade agreement could erode Pakistan's competitive advantage under the Generalised Scheme of Preferences Plus (GSP Plus), saying improved trade concessions for competing countries would intensify competition and hurt the country's export potential. SITE Association of Industry President Abdul Hadi said Pakistan's GSP Plus status with the EU had been a cornerstone of its export performance, providing duty-free access to the European market for approximately 89% of textile and apparel exports, but that this advantage was gradually eroding. He said rising industrial production costs and changes in global trade patterns had also emerged as threats, and that modernisation and value addition had become essential alongside policy stability and the exploration of new, non-traditional markets. The textile sector accounts for approximately 60% of the country's export earnings, with exports of $18 billion in fiscal year 2025-26. During the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27, textile exports increased 5.26% year-on-year to $5.026 billion, although maintaining this growth remained a major challenge because of rising production costs and global competition. He said Pakistan continued to rely heavily on exports of relatively low-value-added products, including yarn, fabric and home textiles, limiting opportunities to generate higher earnings, and urged industries to adopt modern technology and the government to offer investment incentives for technical textiles, branded garments and other high-margin products. Declining domestic cotton production has increased the industry's dependence on imported raw materials, with expenditure on cotton imports rising 54.9% in fiscal year 2024-25, and he called for measures to improve domestic output and strengthen links between the agricultural and industrial sectors to ensure quality raw materials at affordable prices.

title: NHA told to classify projects by viability
description: Cheema says external financing must not cut PSDP allocation, seeks plan with clear timelines
content: Federal Minister for Economic Affairs and Establishment Division Senator Ahad Cheema has directed the National Highway Authority (NHA) to prepare a practical business plan with clear timelines and an assessment of its own capacity, calling for realistic project appraisals and sound financing decisions to strengthen the authority's financial sustainability. He issued the direction while chairing a meeting to review measures for developing the authority's business plan, the ongoing assessment with an Asian Development Bank (ADB) consultant and ways to achieve financial viability, according to a press release issued by the Ministry of Economic Affairs. Officials briefed the meeting on the initial findings of the study with the ADB consultant, and different models and options were presented to improve the authority's performance, strengthen its operations and support financial sustainability. The minister called for a thorough review of projects under consideration, with the planning commission proforma, or PC-I, setting out their commercial viability through more realistic indicators to facilitate appraisal by the Central Development Working Party (CDWP). He asked the authority to classify projects according to their viability and financing requirements, including those requiring government or foreign funding, and said initial project studies should clearly assess viability and be shared at an early stage with the Central Monitoring Unit (CMU) of the Ministry of Finance for comments. The minister underscored that government or external financing for NHA projects should not lead to a reduction in the authority's Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) allocation, saying the government was not in favour of cutting the allocation, as PSDP funding remained essential to the development programme. He stressed that commercially, economically and socially viable projects should be prioritised to strengthen financial sustainability and help the authority avoid an unsustainable debt-servicing burden, while projects that are not commercially viable should undergo a thorough study and review before any decision is made. He also urged the authority to expedite its work with the ADB consultant, whose input is expected to strengthen project mapping, feasibility assessments and financial analysis. Finance Secretary Imdadullah Bosal, Communications Secretary Ali Sher Mehsud, NHA Chief Executive Officer and other senior officials attended the meeting.

title: Task force asks industry for export proposals
description: Leather, sports goods, cutlery and carpets named priority sectors at Islamabad meeting
content: Adviser to the Prime Minister on Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan has invited industry representatives to submit concrete and actionable proposals addressing sector-specific challenges, improving productivity, enhancing product quality and opening new international markets, as he chaired a meeting of the Task Force on Export and Industrial Enhancement. The meeting was attended by Joint Secretary Freedoon Akram Sheikh and representatives of various industrial sectors, including leather, sports goods, cutlery, carpets and other export-oriented industries, according to an official statement issued by the Ministry of Industries and Production on Saturday. The task force was constituted to discuss measures for boosting exports, revitalising industrial activity and promoting sustainable economic growth, and to identify challenges faced by industries, explore new opportunities for growth and develop practical measures to strengthen export performance. The adviser said meaningful consultation with industry representatives was essential for developing effective and result-oriented policies, and noted that a series of consultative meetings was being held, with further engagements planned to ensure that the concerns, recommendations and practical experiences of the business community were considered in the policymaking process. On sector potential, he underscored the importance of promoting leather, sports goods, cutlery and carpets, which he said offer significant opportunities for increasing exports, generating employment and strengthening the national economy. He said the government was facilitating the business community and engaging relevant stakeholders to promote industrial revival, improve competitiveness and create an environment for businesses to expand operations. Participants were assured of support for initiatives aimed at industrial development and export growth, with the adviser stating that the government would continue working with the private sector to identify bottlenecks, facilitate businesses and develop policies responding to the actual needs of industry. He said the establishment of the task force was an initiative aimed at identifying the challenges industries face and developing measures to strengthen export performance, and that export growth and industrial expansion remained government priorities.

title: PSX down 4,045 points amid ME wars
description: KSE-100 index slides below 163,000 as selling intensifies
content: The Pakistan Stock Exchange's (PSX) benchmark KSE-100 index fell 2.4% during the outgoing week, shedding 4,045 points to close at 162,375, as escalating geopolitical tensions, rising oil prices and domestic economic uncertainty weighed on investor sentiment. The index declined for the fifth consecutive week, slipping below the key psychological levels of 166,000, 164,000 and 163,000 amid broad-based selling pressure. On a day-on-day basis, the PSX commenced the trading week with a lacklustre session, where the KSE-100 index declined 454 points (-0.27%) to close at 165,966, slipping below the 166k level. On Tuesday, rising oil prices weighed on the PSX, which registered a negative trading session, losing 814 points (-0.49%) to 165,152. Nevertheless, the bourse witnessed a positive session on Wednesday, finding support around 165,000, with the benchmark index gaining 779 points (+0.47%) to end trading at 165,931. However, the market lost even 164k on the second last session as geopolitical risks escalated. The KSE-100 dived 2,007 points (-1.21%) to 163,924. Geopolitical headwinds pushed the index below the 163,000 mark on the final trading day on Friday, when the market fell 1,550 points (-0.95%) to close at 162,375. Arif Habib Limited (AHL) noted that the KSE-100 index declined 2.4% week-on-week to 162,375, shedding 4,045 points, primarily due to persistent geopolitical uncertainty. At the start of the week, Pakistan's FY26 GDP growth was revised down to 3.65% from 3.70% (FY25 revised to 3.11% from 3.18%), with quarterly growth of 3.89%, 4.31%, 4.42% and 2.0% from Q1 to Q4. Agriculture, industry and services grew 3.50%, 3.34% and 3.81%, respectively, while the economy's size reached Rs126.4 trillion ($450.4 billion), with per capita income at $1,896. AHL mentioned that power generation in Sept'26 increased 5% year-on-year to 13,217 gigawatt hours (GWh), driven by higher hydel, local coal, imported coal and wind generation. The cost of generation rose 32% YoY to Rs9.35/kilowatt-hour due to a higher share of RLNG, high-speed diesel and furnace oil, along with elevated oil prices. Consequently, distribution companies sought a positive fuel cost adjustment of Rs2.56/kWh for Sept'26. A committee reviewing Automotive and Auto Parts Manufacturing Policy 2026-31 proposed reforms to boost exports, accelerate New Energy Vehicle (NEV) adoption and enhance competition. Key measures included lower sales tax on NEVs, reduced import tariffs, mandatory export targets for original equipment manufacturers, localisation requirements and incentives for incremental exports. Cotton arrivals increased 8% YoY to 4,081k bales as of October 15, 2026, led by Sindh (+7% YoY to 2,443k bales) and Punjab (+8% YoY to 1,638k bales). Sowing reached 1.79 million hectares, 82.8% of the 2.16-million-hectare target, while the government had set an FY27 production target of 9.64 million bales, compared to 7.05 million bales in FY26. Petroleum prices recorded a 3.2% WoW decline in motor spirit to Rs377.71/litre and a 1.3% WoW decline in HSD to Rs391.75/litre, driven by lower ex-refinery prices (MS: -4.5% WoW, HSD: -1.8% WoW), while the levy and margins remained unchanged, AHL said. JS Research Head Muhammad Waqas Ghani commented that the KSE-100 index declined for the fifth consecutive week, shedding 4,045 points (-2.4% WoW) to close at 162,375, amid persistent domestic and geopolitical uncertainty. Average volumes dropped 13% to 393 million shares, while traded value inched up 7% WoW to $69.7 million. Brent crude rose further, closing the week above $114/barrel, compared with last week's average of $106. On the macro front, Pakistan's trade deficit widened 21.1% to $9.33 billion during 1QFY27 as imports grew nearly twice as fast as exports, highlighting pressure on the external account. Large-Scale Manufacturing (LSM) posted a 0.67% growth in Aug'26, signalling a slowdown in the industrial sector. The government revised the GDP growth for FY26 slightly downwards to 3.65%. The size of the economy now stands at $450.4 billion, while per capita income hovers around $1,896. In other news, PM Sharif approved a 1% sales tax on EVs and major import tax cuts under a five-year auto policy, subject to IMF and cabinet approval, potentially lowering vehicle prices. National Savings' profit rates were increased by an average of around 24-40 basis points across major schemes. State Bank's reserves remained stable at $21.5 billion, Ghani said.

title: Gold falls Rs7,000 as bullion hits 3-month low
description: International spot gold slips below $4,000 since mid-July
content: Gold prices in Pakistan fell sharply on Friday, shedding Rs7,000 per tola as international bullion prices dropped to a three-month low amid rising inflation concerns and expectations of higher US interest rates. The price of gold per tola declined to Rs424,536 in the local market, according to rates released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association. Similarly, the price of 10-gram gold decreased by Rs6,001 to Rs363,971. On Thursday, gold had already fallen by Rs3,000 per tola to Rs431,536. Internationally, spot gold fell 0.6% to $4,000.59 per ounce by 1520 GMT, after briefly slipping below the $4,000 threshold for the first time since mid-July. Prices touched an intraday low of $3,975.23 per ounce, as per Reuters. Bullion had declined around 4% during the week, putting it on course for its steepest weekly loss since June. US gold futures for December delivery also dropped 1.1% to $4,014.60 per ounce. Rising energy prices have heightened concerns about inflation, strengthening expectations that US interest rates could remain elevated. Higher interest rates tend to weigh on gold, which does not pay interest, by making yield-bearing assets more attractive. Brent crude touched a more than five-month high after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia raised concerns about further disruptions to energy supplies. Higher oil prices could add to inflationary pressures and complicate the outlook for monetary policy. Investors are also awaiting the US Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision and personal consumption expenditure inflation data due next week, which could influence expectations for the future path of monetary policy. Meanwhile, silver prices in Pakistan declined by Rs221 per tola to Rs5,865. In India, gold demand strengthened as lower prices encouraged purchases ahead of the festive season, highlighting how price declines can support physical demand even as global financial conditions weigh on bullion. Meanwhile, the Pakistani rupee continued its marginal gains against the US dollar on Friday, appreciating by Re0.03 in the interbank market to close at 276.82, compared with Thursday's closing rate of 276.85.

title: PSX slides towards 162,000 amid ME war
description: KSE-100 index sheds 1,549 points as US-Iran tensions escalate
content: The Pakistan Stock Exchange's (PSX) benchmark KSE-100 index fell almost 1,550 points on Friday, extending its weekly decline to 2.43% amid escalating US-Iran tensions, rising oil prices and profit-taking ahead of the State Bank of Pakistan's monetary policy decision. At the close of trading, the benchmark KSE-100 index posted a decline of 1,549.44 points, or 0.95%, and settled at 162,374.88. Arif Habib Limited (AHL) noted that the KSE-100 closed down by 1,549.4 points, or 0.95% on the day, and 2.43% for the week, extending a recent sequence of declines amid broad-based selling pressure. Of the index constituents, 26 shares advanced while 73 declined. The largest positive contribution came from Fauji Fertiliser Company, Pakistan Services and Askari Bank, whereas the heaviest drags were Meezan Bank, Engro Holdings and Lucky Cement. A brief note, in the AHL report, highlighted Pakistan's position in critical minerals given its deposits of copper, gold, chromite and other resources, while the technical commentary pointed to potential downside towards 160,000 with resistance near 166,000. The KSE-100 closed at 162,375 after oscillating between the intra-day range of 162,292 and 163,967, it said. Topline's market review said that the KSE-100 index extended its bearish trend, declining by 0.95% to close at 162,375 points, amid escalating tensions between the US and Iran and a further rise in international crude oil prices. In terms of traded value, Pakistan Petroleum (Rs723 million), Thatta Cement (Rs699 million), Hub Power (Rs547 million), Maple Leaf Cement (Rs504 million) and NBP (Rs473 million) dominated the day's activity. The top negative contribution to the index came from Meezan Bank, Engro Holdings, Lucky Cement, Hubco and Pakistan Petroleum, as they cumulatively erased 637 points. Traded volume and value for the day stood at 399 million shares and Rs18 billion, respectively. Topline further said that the KSE-100 index declined 2.43% week-on-week amid geopolitical tensions, rising oil prices and profit-taking ahead of the SBP's monetary policy decision. Overall trading volumes were recorded at 398.94 million shares compared with the previous session's tally of 367.09 million. The value of shares traded during the day was Rs18.20 billion. In the ready market, shares of 495 companies were traded. Of these, 136 stocks closed higher, 311 fell and 48 remained unchanged. Pervez Ahmed Consultancy Services was the volume leader with trading in 32.67 million shares, gaining Rs0.31 to close at Rs3.33. It was followed by Macpac Films with 26.69 million shares, losing Rs6.58 to close at Rs59.25 and Pakistan Refinery with 23.50 million shares, losing Rs0.60 to close at Rs94.52. Foreign investors sold shares worth Rs416.6 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

title: Unnecessary rules being removed
description: Adviser says complex regulations impeding foreign investment
content: Adviser to Prime Minister for Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan has said that the government is undertaking reforms to simplify business environment, remove unnecessary regulatory hurdles and promote domestic and foreign investment in Pakistan. Addressing a press conference alongside Gilgit-Baltistan chief minister and members of his cabinet, the adviser said that complexity of the regulatory framework and difficulties in doing business had been among the major factors discouraging foreign investment in Pakistan. "Over the past 78 years, laws and regulations have been introduced to meet different needs. However, with the passage of time, unnecessary complexities and overlapping requirements have accumulated, making it tough for businesses to run efficiently," Khan said. He explained that the government was conducting a comprehensive review of regulators, laws and regulations affecting businesses across the country. The reform process has made substantial progress, with approximately 60-70% of the overall work completed. Reform proposals submitted by various institutions recommend eliminating, on average, 70-75% of unnecessary or duplicating regulations. The adviser said review meetings were being held every two weeks to ensure progress and implementation of several proposed reforms had already begun, while further measures were being developed to improve the ease of doing business and strengthen investor confidence. Highlighting the proposed Asaan Karobar Act, Khan said the government was working to establish a business environment aligned with international best practices. The initiative aims to simplify regulatory procedures, reduce compliance costs and create a more predictable and investor-friendly framework for businesses. He stated that 170 amendments to the Companies Act, 2017 had been approved by the federal cabinet and the relevant bill was forwarded to parliament. The proposed amendments will facilitate company registrations and business operations while modernising Pakistan's corporate regulatory framework. The PM aide mentioned that international regulatory systems, particularly those of Delaware in the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada, had been studied as benchmarks for the proposed reforms. The government had also engaged a senior international consultant with experience in regulatory reforms across 135 countries to support the process. Khan said that regulatory reviews were underway in several sectors, including dairy, maritime, beverages, oil refineries, pharmaceuticals and restaurants.

title: Envoy seeks shift from 'CT to IT' with US
description: Washington forum showcases 16 Pakistani tech firms in AI, cloud, fintech and health tech
content: Pakistan wants to move its relationship with the United States from counterterrorism to information technology, Ambassador of Pakistan to the United States Rizwan Saeed Sheikh told a tech forum in Washington, describing the shift from "CT to IT" as the goal that would yield a mutually rewarding partnership. "A key goal is to make a transition in the bilateral relationship from 'CT to IT,' moving from counterterrorism to information technology," the ambassador said at Pakistan-US Tech Connect 2026, hosted by the embassy with the Ministry of IT and Telecommunication, OPEN Global and the Pakistan Software Export Board (PSEB). The forum brought senior leadership from 16 Pakistani companies in artificial intelligence, cloud computing, data analytics, fintech and healthcare technology together with American counterparts, according to a statement issued on Thursday. It was designed as an executive networking forum to unlock partnerships across enterprise solutions, digital transformation, product development and strategic IT collaboration. Attendees included Sindh Governor Syed Nehal Hashmi, representatives of major US technology and financial firms, multilateral institutions, government agencies and the Pakistani American business community. Structured executive panel discussions and curated business-to-business sessions sought to convert Pakistan's IT export capacity into commercial relationships. The ambassador said the showcase aimed to display the "best and brightest" from the Pakistani tech industry directly to stakeholders in Washington, and its ability to meet international standards in fields such as AI. "Each time Pakistan and the United States have come together, we have produced results, and results not only for ourselves in the bilateral domain, but results for the whole world," he said. Hashmi urged the delegation to convert digital capabilities into tangible outcomes, including qualified business opportunities, pilot projects and high-value contracts, saying US enterprises seek partners able to deliver long-term value. PSEB Chief Executive Officer Faisal Jeddy, Ignite CEO Bilal Abbasi and OPEN Global DC Chapter President Hassan Khalid cited the expansion of Pakistan's technology sector, noting that the country offers technical talent while the US offers market opportunities. Panel discussions addressed a shift away from routine IT services and labour arbitrage towards proprietary intellectual property and scalable product innovation.

title: Govt pushes China for tariff concessions
description: Exporters raised the Punjab infrastructure cess
content: Pakistan is seeking improved preferential access with major trading partners, including China, South Korea, Türkiye, Japan and Vietnam, and has been advocating greater tariff concessions from Beijing in line with the treatment extended to other countries, Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan told a consultative meeting with exporters on Thursday. He said discussions on preferential trade arrangements with South Korea were progressing, while engagement with other partners continued through diplomatic missions and bilateral consultations. The meeting reviewed industrial energy costs, particularly the gas levy, and was told the Ministry of Finance had constituted a committee with government and industry representatives to review the levy policy and calculation formula. Exporters raised the Punjab infrastructure cess, certification charges and repeated documentation amendment fees at the Department of Plant Protection, and proposed proportionate super tax relief linked to export-derived income. The meeting reviewed the Export Facilitation Scheme's procedural requirements and eligibility criteria, and discussed business visa restrictions and insurance costs.

title: Eric Bauza  Emmy winning voice of Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck  dies at 46
description: Bauza   s family confirmed his death in a post on his Instagram account on Sunday  October 25  2026
content:
Bauza’s family confirmed his death in a post on his Instagram account on Sunday, October 25, 2026
Eric Bauza, the Emmy-winning voice actor known for bringing Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and other iconic Looney Tunes characters to life, has died aged 46, his family has announced.
Bauza’s family confirmed his death in a post on his Instagram account on Sunday, October 25, 2026. The announcement described his passing as sudden, with further details yet to be released.
“Eric Bauza, Emmy Award-winning voice actor and the modern voice of iconic Looney Tunes characters Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, along with dozens of other beloved cartoon characters, has passed away suddenly. More details to come,” the statement read.
Channing Dungey, chairman of Warner Bros. Television Group and US Networks, paid tribute to the actor, highlighting his contribution during 15 years with Warner Bros. Animation.
“Eric Bauza was a unique voice talent who brought joy and laughter to millions around the world,” Dungey said.
She added that he had followed in the footsteps of legendary voice actor Mel Blanc, whose performances established many of the characters Bauza later portrayed.
Born in Toronto on 7 December 1979, Bauza began his animation career as a character designer before establishing himself as a prominent voice actor.
His credits included Looney Tunes Cartoons , Space Jam: A New Legacy , Coyote vs. Acme , Muppet Babies and The Adventures of Puss in Boots .
He also voiced characters in Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles , The Powerpuff Girls and Forgotten Island .
Bauza received nominations for Daytime Emmy, Children’s & Family Emmy and Annie Awards for his voice performances.

title: Peshawar to clear bazaars

title: Peshawar school collapse exposes gaps in safety
description: Peshawar school collapse exposes gaps in safety
content:
Residents allege warnings about the building's dilapidated condition were ignored
Tahir Khan managed to pull several children alive from the rubble of a collapsed private school in Peshawar's Dir Colony, but the tragedy left him with an unbearable loss: he could not save his two nephews and a niece, who were among the children caught in the disaster.
More than 30 children died in the heartbreaking incident, while several others sustained injuries. Khan, an eyewitness who helped rescue children from the debris, said the loss of his own family members had left him devastated and demanded severe punishment for those responsible.
"What is the point of running a school like this? It would be better to open a livestock farm instead," he said, criticising the school's management for what he described as negligence. He said the owner should receive the strictest possible punishment for the loss of young lives.
Police have arrested the school owner, and an investigation into the incident is under way.
However, the tragedy has raised serious questions about whether warnings regarding the building's condition were ignored and whether the authorities are adequately monitoring the safety of educational institutions across Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).
Shahab Khan, a resident of Dir Colony, told The Express Tribune that local residents had repeatedly approached the school principal to warn that the building was in a dilapidated condition and could collapse at any time. However, he alleged, their concerns were not taken seriously.
The incident has brought renewed attention to the condition of school infrastructure across the province, where thousands of classrooms in government schools reportedly require reconstruction or repairs.
According to a report on the condition of public-sector schools in K-P, 36,967 classrooms are in a dilapidated state. The province has 34,784 government schools, of which 19,284 classrooms require reconstruction, while another 17,743 need repairs.
The figures highlight the scale of the infrastructure challenge facing the education sector and raise concerns about the safety of students attending schools in buildings that may require urgent maintenance.
In response to the risks posed by deteriorating school buildings, the Elementary and Secondary Education Department has issued directives to suspend teaching activities in dilapidated schools.
However, concerns extend beyond government institutions to the private education sector, where regulatory oversight remains a challenge.
According to the available report, no records are available for 11,542 private schools in K-P. The figure has raised questions about the registration, documentation and monitoring of private educational institutions operating across the province.
Irshad Jadoon, administrative officer at the Private Schools Regulatory Authority (PSRA), told The Express Tribune that more than 12,000 private schools operate in the province, while the authority has a staff of only 45 people.
He said the limited workforce made it extremely difficult to monitor private schools across the province and ensure compliance with safety and regulatory requirements.
Jadoon called for the establishment of a PSRA sub-office in every district to strengthen oversight and enable authorities to respond more effectively to complaints concerning school buildings and their management. "A more decentralised regulatory system could help improve monitoring and reduce the risk of similar tragedies in the future," noted Jadoon.
For families in Dir Colony, however, the consequences of the school collapse are irreversible. While the investigation into the incident continues, the deaths of the children have intensified calls for accountability, effective regulation and urgent action to ensure that schools remain safe places for learning rather than sites of preventable tragedy.

title: Another Shangla youth dies in coal mine
description: Another Shangla youth dies in coal mine
content:
Another young man from Shangla has lost his life while working in a coal mine, adding to a grim toll that has claimed 83 local miners this year alone.
Hanifullah, son of Momin Khan and a resident of Mian Kalle, Pirabad in Darra Adam Khel, was engaged in labour at a coal mine when the fatal accident occurred.
News of his death plunged the locality into mourning. An announcement for his funeral prayer was made at the mosque in Mian Kalle, Pirabad. Hanifullah's body is the 83rd Shangla miner to die in coal-mine accidents this year and the third such fatality in just the past week.
The relentless sequence of tragedies has once again highlighted serious concerns about miners' safety, the scarcity of alternative employment, and the deep economic deprivation gripping Shangla. Young men who leave home in search of work continue to return in coffins, turning hope into permanent grief for their families. Parents send their sons away with dreams of a better future, only to see those hopes shattered by accidents in hazardous mines.
According to Abid Yar, an official of a non-governmental organisation advocating for the rights of mine workers, more than 83 Shangla miners have already perished in various accidents this year, while hundreds more have been injured. These figures underscore the urgent need for effective protective measures. Each death not only deprives a family of its breadwinner but also places the education, healthcare and daily expenses of remaining members under severe strain.
Shangla's economic landscape offers few local opportunities. The absence of large factories, industrial units and significant commercial activity forces a large number of young people to seek work in other districts and provinces. Many end up in coal mines, where hard labour is matched by constant danger. Available information indicates that nearly 66 per cent of Shangla's population depends, directly or indirectly, on mining for its livelihood. Such heavy reliance ties the district's economy to an inherently risky occupation in which a single accident can wipe out a household's income and plunge it into lasting hardship.

title: JUI F tells leaders to quit advisory council
description: JUI F tells leaders to quit advisory council
content:
Party sets three-day deadline for members to leave K-P council or face expulsion
The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam Fazl (JUI-F) chapter has issued show-cause notices to its members serving on the provincial advisory council, directing them to resign within three days or face suspension of their party membership.
The party also rejected the imposition of governor's rule and an emergency in the province, describing the move as an undemocratic step. It expressed concern over what it termed irresponsible and controversial remarks by the provincial information adviser linking religious seminaries to terrorism.
The decisions were taken at a meeting of the JUI-F provincial executive committee held at the party's provincial secretariat, Mufti Mahmood Centre, in Peshawar, under the chairmanship of provincial chief Senator Maulana Attaur Rehman.
Provincial General Secretary Senator Maulana Attaul Haq Darvesh briefed the committee on decisions taken at a recent meeting of the party's central Shura. Senator Attaur Rehman also discussed the prevailing political tensions, the party's efforts to mediate between the opposition and the ruling party, and the situation arising from the proposed imposition of governor's rule and an emergency.
According to a statement issued by the JUI-F media cell, the provincial executive committee termed the federal government's decision regarding governor's rule and an emergency in K-P a negation of democratic principles.
The meeting rejected the establishment of the advisory council and directed JUI-F members who had not yet resigned to step down within three days. Failure to comply would result in their party membership being considered suspended, the statement said.
The committee also expressed serious concern over what it described as irresponsible remarks by the provincial information adviser about religious seminaries. It maintained that linking seminaries to terrorism was contrary to facts and deeply regrettable.
Religious seminaries, the party said, were centres of peace, love and tolerance and had consistently supported the state in its fight against terrorism. Hundreds of religious scholars had themselves fallen victim to terrorism and sacrificed their lives, it added.
The meeting described the information adviser's remarks as frivolous and urged him to exercise responsibility, restraint and regard for facts while commenting on national issues. It said the remarks had sparked resentment among religious circles and amounted to an attempt to undermine the sacrifices of those who had lost their lives in the fight against terrorism.
The committee also deplored what it called a smear campaign against the JUI-F and its chief, Maulana Fazlur Rehman, allegedly conducted on social media by certain groups and paid vloggers. It said fabricated narratives could not undermine the party leadership's role and principled political stance.
The party's media team had previously countered such narratives and would continue responding to what it described as misleading propaganda, the statement added.

title: Bulgaria election exposes Ukraine war divide
description: Bulgaria election exposes Ukraine war divide
content:
Bulgaria's President Iliana Iotova narrowly led the first round of presidential elections Sunday, exit polls showed, in a vote held amid security concerns following a series of drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea.
Iotova, who favours dialogue with Moscow and opposes military aid to Ukraine, scored between 35 and 36.5 percent of the vote, according to three polls.
She will face Andrey Gyurov, a banker and former caretaker prime minister backed by the pro-Western opposition who came second with between 32.2 and 32.5 percent, in the November 1 runoff.
The result was closer than expected, with surveys ahead of the vote predicting a comfortable win for Iotova.
Turnout was only around 20 percent, according to the polls.
After casting her vote, Iotova said she wanted to address "the dire issue of poverty" in the EU's poorest member state, "alongside inequalities and regional disparities".
"I believe that there must be peace, stability, and security," added the 62-year-old, who has made the war in Ukraine a central theme of her campaign, promising to be a "president of peace".
Gyurov meanwhile said he wanted "a Bulgaria that looks forward, a country that is European, free, and proud... and where the state works as it should".
Four vessels were struck off Bulgaria's coast this month, leaving 21 people missing, in suspected spillover from the Russia-Ukraine war.
While Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the attacks appeared to serve Russian interests and summoned the Russian ambassador, his government insists there is so far no evidence directly linking Moscow to them.
Iotova took over this year as president of Bulgaria, a European Union and NATO member state, when Radev stepped down to run in parliamentary elections.

title: Fresh clashes rock France as protesters march on
description: Fresh clashes rock France as protesters march on
content:
Clashes erupted across France on Saturday as protesters took to the streets, a week after marches that degenerated into violence and prompted a firm security backlash from President Emmanuel Macron, who is scrambling to restore order.
Police arrested nearly 1,000 people as officers faced "an extremely elevated level of violence" from black-clad "ultra-left" extremists, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said.
Riot police squads fired tear gas at protesters in the capital as well as in Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nantes.
Two people were "seriously" injured, Nunez said: one man in Toulouse, who reportedly had fingers blown off, and another person in Clermont-Ferrand. He did not give details of either case.
Authorities had deployed 70,000 security personnel across the country for the new marches, called to protest the cost of living.
The violence came a week after rioting that saw public buildings vandalised, hundreds of shops looted and 2,700 people arrested, casting a pall over the country six months before an election to choose Macron's successor.
Nunez said Saturday's outcome was more "positive" than a week ago, with more police on the streets acting more rapidly, conducting more pre-demonstration checks and better protecting businesses.
But there was widespread anger at the government over a protest crackdown viewed as an assault on the right to protest.
Saturday's demonstrations drew between 410,000 and 800,000 people across the country, according to different estimates by authorities and the organising CGT union.
The main Paris march had between 110,000 and 250,000 attendees, according to those sources.
Macron's government has ordered police to prevent protesters reaching city centres, where shops are concentrated, and in Paris and some other cities, partial curfews were imposed in certain urban zones.
The French president had ordered non-union demonstrations be banned as "illegitimate".
In Paris, where many shops had boarded up windows to prevent looting, and the Louvre and the Musee d'Orsay museums shut for the day, the main demonstration passed off largely peacefully.
The march had been pushed to the capital's southeast rim under a last-minute order by authorities.
Afterwards, though, clashes broke out as the crowd was dispersing, with Nunez blaming "500 rioters" at the back of the march.
AFP journalists saw police charge several times, blasting tear gas and using batons against some, mostly young, protesters.
"They were just taking people down, you know, beating protesters," one demonstrator bleeding from a baton blow to his face, who gave his first name as David, told AFP.
Thousands of protesters in the western city of Nantes broke through lines of police firing tear gas and a water cannon to reach the city centre, an AFP journalist witnessed.
Emma, 23, who came out in the northwest city of Rennes, denounced the bans on demonstrations and the "repression" of protests by high school students demanding better learning conditions.

title: Suspect in businessman s murder sent to jail
description: Suspect in businessman s murder sent to jail
content:
A suspect arrested for the murder of industrialist Mian Rehan Ashraf during a carjacking was transferred to the district jail for an identification parade, police said on Sunday.
The suspect, identified as Umair Khalid, was produced before Area Magistrate Asadullah Khattak by Sadar police investigation officer Sub-Inspector Atif before being sent to jail.
Police said the identification parade would be arranged, during which the complainant would be asked to identify the suspect.
According to police, Ashraf was shot dead on Jaranwala Road on the night of October 15 after he pursued his stolen vehicle.
The car had allegedly been snatched from an employee of a valet parking service outside Chenab Club in the Civil Lines police station area.
Police said Ashraf tracked the vehicle and followed it after receiving an alert that it had left the parking area.
Believing that the valet employee had driven away with his car, he also informed police through Rescue 15 and began pursuing the vehicle using its tracking system.
The stolen car was eventually found amid traffic near a restaurant on Jaranwala Road. When Ashraf reached the vehicle, he allegedly opened the door and reprimanded the valet employee, who had been forced at gunpoint to drive the car.
As Ashraf sat in the front seat, Khalid, who was allegedly hiding in the back seat, opened fire.
A bullet struck Ashraf in the neck, killing him at the scene, police said.
Investigators said the suspect had allegedly threatened the valet employee with a weapon before forcing him into the driver's seat and escaping in the vehicle. He later abandoned the car and fled.
Police teams led by City Police Officer Tanveer Hussain and SSP Operations Imran Malik used CCTV footage to identify the suspect.
He was arrested in the Shahkot area five days after the incident. Police said they had recovered the alleged murder weapon, a motorcycle and the clothes he was wearing on the day of the incident.
During preliminary interrogation, Khalid told investigators that he had been struggling with financial hardship and wanted to move to Saudi Arabia in search of a better life.
An overseas employment agent had reportedly demanded Rs1.5 million to arrange his travel, but he did not have the money.
Police said Khalid, a kabaddi player and father of two, was allegedly influenced by films and believed that robbing wealthy people would provide a shortcut to achieving his ambitions.
Investigators said he had targeted Chenab Club because he expected affluent people to be present there.
According to the police account, Khalid parked his motorcycle at the Hilal-e-Ahmar Hospital parking area and walked to the club's car park.
Seeing the valet employee in a suit approaching the vehicle, he allegedly mistook him for the car's owner and forced him at gunpoint to drive.

title: Road caught in cycle of excavation
description: Road caught in cycle of excavation
content:
Recurring sinkholes, cable damage cause concerns
The Sargodha Road has been excavated for the fifth time in two and a half years, disrupting traffic, affecting local businesses and raising questions about coordination among the development agencies.
Residents said the municipal corporation had reconstructed the road about six months ago. However, sinkholes had appeared at the same location on four previous occasions, in March 2024, June and November 2025 and February this year. The Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA) carried out repairs following the incidents, but the underlying problem apparently persisted.
Excavation of the same stretch has been started now to repair damaged telephone and internet cables.
The work has forced authorities to divert traffic to one side of the road, while the other side remains closed.
Sources attributed the recurring damage to water seepage from underground pipelines, causing the road surface to sink and damaging telecommunications infrastructure.
They said WASA had installed the main sewerage line along the road in 1982 and it had exceeded its expected service life about five years ago.
Temporary repairs, however, had continued without fully addressing the underlying defects.
An assistant manager at PTCL, Muhammad Sajid, said the company's underground cable was damaged after excavation and the subsequent formation of a sinkhole.
The cable carries telecommunications services between Faisalabad and Sargodha as well as strategic communication circuits, he said.
He said the damaged cable had initially been restoted, but continued soil settlement caused by water seepage had led to further damage.
He alleged that inadequate coordination during excavation had left existing underground services vulnerable.
Municipal Corporation spokesperson Muhammad Haseeb said the PTCL had obtained a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the civic body to repair its cable infrastructure before development work began.
However, WASA Operations Director Farhan Akra said the agency had not carried out any repair work at the site during the past six months.
The agency had only repaired a manhole slab a few days earlier, he said, describing the work as superficial, extending half a foot below the surface.
An architect, Wazir Khan, said the Traffic Engineering and Planning Agency could not coordinate development work among departments without adequate staff and budget.
A grocery store owner on Sargodha Road, Muhammad Ali, said repeated excavation had increased dust and pollution and reduced customer traffic, affecting sales.
A local medical store owner, Abdul Hameed, said the work had created difficulties for pedestrians, commuters and businesses.

title: LPG sells for Rs570 per kg in Lahore
description: LPG sells for Rs570 per kg in Lahore
content:
Consumers accuse vendors of restricting open sale amid govt crackdown
Residents of the city are struggling with soaring liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices, with vendors selling the fuel for as much as Rs570 per kilogramme despite the official rate of Rs279, adding to the financial pressure on households already grappling with rising living costs.
Consumers said some LPG vendors had suspended open sales following government action to control prices but continued selling the gas discreetly to customers willing to pay high rates.
A resident, Muhammad Ali, criticised the government for failing to regulate LPG prices and ensure supplies at affordable rates.
Another citizen said the government had also failed to provide piped natural gas reliably, even in the provincial capital, forcing consumers to rely on alternative fuels for cooking and other household needs.
The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) has fixed the consumer price of LPG at Rs279 per kg for October, with the price of a domestic cylinder set at Rs3,350. However, the prevailing open-market rates reported by consumers and traders are substantially higher, widening the gap between the regulated price and what households are being asked to pay.
The price surge comes amid supply disruptions following the closure of key trading crossings between Pakistan and Iran. The Gabd-Rimdan and Taftan crossings were closed on October 17, disrupting LPG imports and contributing to shortages in the domestic market.
Pakistan relies on both domestic production and imports to meet its LPG requirements. Local production is estimated at 2,000 to 2,500 tonnes a day, while daily consumption stands at 4,000 to 4,500 tonnes. Demand typically rises to over 6,000 tonnes a day during peak winter, when households increasingly depend on LPG for cooking and heating.
The interruption has raised concerns about whether supplies will be sufficient to meet demand as temperatures fall. The Gabd-Rimdan crossing subsequently reopened for Pakistani exports of perishable items.

title: CM approves film royalty law
description: CM approves film royalty law
content:
35% rebate for Punjabi movies receives the nod
Preparations have been finalised for the launch of Pakistan's first state-of-the-art Film City on December 15.
According to an official statement, Key decisions aimed at reviving the film industry, promoting modern filmmaking and restoring Lahore's position as its centre were approved at the first meeting of the Punjab Film Authority, chaired by Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb.
Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has approved the formulation of Pakistan's first royalty law for the film industry and directed that it be presented at the next meeting of the authority.
She has approved a rebate of 35 per cent for Punjabi and 20% for Urdu films produced in Punjab to support the local industry.
The proposed city will feature a film and music school, museum, trading house, post-production facility, studio complex, and convention centre.
The rebate policy is expected to provide financial support to filmmakers, encourage quality film production and attract investment to the industry.
It was decided in the meeting to introduce an online one-window facility to help filmmakers identify suitable shooting locations.
The Film City Authority's budget of over Rs589 million for the financial year 2026-27 was referred to a financing committee for review.
Approval was granted to recruit 26 employees in the first phase against 53 sanctioned posts. The authority's board will have the power to make appointments and dismissals.
The participants reviewed progress on the formation of six committees, including the Punjab Film Fund Committee.
It also approved measures for the restoration of old cinemas, installation of solar systems and provision of affordable entertainment facilities to the public.
A decision was made to introduce an online booking system for cinemas.
A training programme was approved for young filmmakers from international experts in modern filmmaking techniques.
Marriyum Aurangzeb said on the occasion that Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz wanted Punjab to become a global-standard screen tourism destination within five years.
She said Punjab's unique and valuable culture and rare heritage would be showcased to the world through the camera lens.
"Film City is a complete ecosystem for reviving the film industry, attracting investment, creating employment opportunities and providing quality and affordable entertainment to the public," she said.
Chairing a meeting of the Punjab Saaf Pani Authority, Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz set a target for the completion of 5,734 water filtration plants by June 2027.
She assigned the responsibility of monitoring the plants to the assistant commissioners. Public committees will also be constituted under the supervision of the ACs to oversee the plants located in neighbourhoods.
It was decided to establish mobile maintenance units in every tehsil to ensure the repair and rehabilitation of the filtration plants. Each mobile workshop will have plumbers and other technical staff to ensure timely maintenance and uninterrupted access to clean drinking water.
The chief minister also approved the Last-Mile Water Supply Project for the worst-affected areas of Chakwal, Rajanpur and Rawalpindi. Water supply schemes covering 256 kilometres in Chakwal and 1,780km in Rajanpur will be prioritised.
CM Maryam Nawaz was informed that plants in Khushab, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rahim Yar Khan and Bahawalpur were producing 10,000 19-litre water bottles daily, benefiting 4.8 million people. Over 75,000 bottles of water have been delivered to households under the initiative.
The chief minister said clean drinking water was the right of every citizen. She said that, for the first time in Punjab, the government had taken the initiative of delivering clean drinking water to households.
CM Maryam Nawaz said water supply schemes would also be launched in other areas and people would no longer have to travel miles to fetch drinking water.

title: Bride shot dead on wedding reception day in Gujranwala
description: Bride shot dead on wedding reception day in Gujranwala
content:
CCTV footage shows two motorcycle riders intercepting couple's car
A newlywed woman was shot dead inside a car on the day of her wedding reception in Gujranwala, allegedly by a man who had wanted to marry her, police said.
The incident took place near Samanabad Chungi in the Gulshan Colony area, within the jurisdiction of Aroop police station, on October 24. Saba married Sufyan on October 23, and the couple's walima reception was held the following day.
According to the First Information Report (FIR), the couple were returning home after the reception when two men on a motorcycle intercepted their car.
One of the suspects, identified as Sarfraz, allegedly opened fire on Saba at close range, hitting her in the chest and abdomen.
She was rushed to hospital in critical condition but succumbed to her injuries.
The complainant alleged that Sarfraz wanted to marry Saba and attacked her after she refused. A case has been registered, while both suspects have fled and remain at large.
Closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage of the incident, reportedly shows two motorcycle riders waiting on the road as the couple's car approaches.
The suspects then move towards the vehicle and stop it.
According to the footage, one of the men opens the car door, prompting a woman to get out and run for safety.
The attacker then allegedly opens fire repeatedly at Saba, who remains inside the vehicle.
The car's driver is seen getting out and lying on the ground, apparently attempting to protect himself from the gunfire.
The suspects are then seen fleeing on their motorcycle while firing shots.
The footage reportedly captures the suspects' faces as they escape, which investigators may use to help identify and trace them.
The Crime Control Department (CCD) has registered a case and launched an investigation. Regional police officials said efforts were under way to arrest the suspects soon.

title: Over 9k doctors seek postgrad admission
description: Over 9k doctors seek postgrad admission
content:
Test held in Lahore, Rawalpindi, Faisalabad and Multan
A total of 9,008 doctors appeared in the Postgraduate Entrance Test (PGET) conducted by the University of Health Sciences (UHS) simultaneously in Lahore, Rawalpindi, Faisalabad and Multan on Sunday.
The test is mandatory for admission to Level III postgraduate medical and dental programmes, including the FCPS, MD, MS and MDS. It was conducted through two question papers, beginning at 10am and concluding at 2:30pm, with a 30-minute break.
Of the candidates, 4,579 were women and 4,429 men. Lahore recorded the highest number of candidates at 4,107, followed by Multan with 2,353, Rawalpindi 1,516 and Faisalabad 1,032.
The Punjab University Examination Halls on Wahdat Road served as the examination venue in Lahore, while the respective medical universities hosted candidates in the other three cities.
The provincial government had arranged the PGET for the first time, replacing the Joint Centralised Admission Test previously used for admissions to the programmes.
The results are expected to be announced next week, according to the UHS.

title: Border curbs cloud Bhagwant Mann invite | The Express Tribune

Border curbs

content:
Indian Punjab CM's participation in Lahore conference hinges on bilateral policies
An invitation to Indian Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann for the upcoming World Punjabi Conference in Lahore is facing uncertainty over whether cross-border travel policies will permit the leader to attend the event.
Conference Chairman Muddasir Iqbal Butt confirmed that an invitation had been made to Mann but said his participation remained uncertain because of restrictions and policies governing travel between Pakistan and India.
The final decision, he said, would rest with the relevant authorities on both sides.
Butt said the organisers were working with Punjabi language and culture advocates, including Punjab Institute of Language Art and Culture (PILAC) Director General Aslam Shahid, to make the gathering a successful international event.
CM Mann has expressed interest in visiting Lahore.
He referred to the invitation during proceedings of the Indian Punjab Vidhan Sabha. According to sources at PILAC, he wanted to attend the conference but there is uncertainty whether the Indian government would permit him to travel to Pakistan.
Mann also highlighted the cultural and linguistic connections between the two Punjabs.
His remarks have raised expectations among Punjabi cultural circles that the gathering could provide an opportunity to strengthen links between communities divided by the international border.
Preparations for the conference by various organisations are in full swing and invitations to delegates from around the world are being sent.
A visit by the chief minister of Indian Punjab would give the conference significant prominence.
It could also create opportunities for dialogue among writers, academics, artists and cultural organisations. Mann's statement regarding participation in the conference has become a subject of debate among Punjabi scholars and community.
The conference is scheduled for November 27 to 29 at PILAC in Lahore.
The organisers intend to bring together participants from Pakistan and the international Punjabi community to discuss the language's future, literary traditions, cultural identity and issues affecting communities speaking it.

title: Ring Road drivers face steep fines
description: Ring Road drivers face steep fines
content:
Cameras, traffic police, LRRA compound penalties
Lahore Ring Road Authority (LRRA) has increased fines for traffic violations, adding to the financial burden on commuters already grappling with high inflation and penalties imposed by city traffic police and Safe City Authority cameras.
The revised penalties cover offences ranging from driving without a licence and speeding to illegal parking, overloading, using tinted windows and crossing roads on foot.
Several fines have increased substantially, including the penalty for driving without a licence, which has risen tenfold from Rs500 to Rs5,000.
The increase comes as the Ring Road police intensify enforcement against traffic violations, while motorists also face fines under the city traffic police's existing penalty schedule.
The measures have increased the financial consequences of traffic offences in the city.
Under the revised Ring Road penalties, improper overtaking will attract a fine of Rs5,000 for cars and Rs10,000 for vehicles with engine capacities exceeding 2,000cc.
Using the wrong lane will incur a Rs2,000 fine, while driving against the direction of traffic on a one-way section will cost Rs5,000.
The fine for overloading has increased from Rs2,000 to Rs7,000, while the penalty for illegal parking has doubled from Rs1,000 to Rs2,000.
Cars emitting excessive smoke will attract a Rs4,000 fine, compared with Rs5,000 for commercial vehicles.
Drivers caught overspeeding will face fines of Rs5,000 for vehicles with engine capacities of up to 2,000cc and Rs10,000 for larger ones.
Underage driving will incur a Rs10,000 fine.
Other violations carrying penalties include using black-tinted window films or non-standard number plates, both attracting fines of Rs5,000. Motorcycles entering the Ring Road will also incur a Rs5,000 fine.
The revised schedule also increases the penalty for pedestrians crossing the Ring Road from Rs200 to Rs1,000.
Bringing cattle onto the Ring Road will attract a Rs5,000 fine for their owners.
The fine for using a mobile phone while driving or failing to fasten a seat belt has also been increased from Rs500 to Rs3,000.
At the authority's performance review meeting last week, it was highlighted that Lahore Ring Road police had penalised 1,783 unlicensed drivers and 2,088 smoke-emitting vehicles in September. Challans were issued to 6,183 vehicles for overloading, while action was taken against 3,095 vehicles without number plates and 446 with tinted windows.
The police also fined 281 motorcycles for traffic violations and issued challans to 2,793 people for illegal pedestrian crossing. A further 5,322 vehicles were penalised for overspeeding, while 1,447 people were fined for not wearing seatbelts.
Seventy-two cases were registered against drivers for negligence and speeding, while several drivers were arrested and taken into custody.
At the monthly review meeting, Punjab Ring Road Authority Chairperson Safi Ullah Gondal directed the police to intensify action against speeding and motorcycles entering the route.
He also ordered stricter enforcement to prevent pedestrian crossings and accidents and improve road safety.
The city traffic police had already increased fines for a wide range of traffic violations in recent months. Under the revised schedule, overspeeding attracts fines ranging from Rs2,000 for motorcycles to Rs20,000 for cars with engine capacities exceeding 2,000cc and public service vehicles. Driving without a licence carries fines of Rs2,000 for motorcycles, Rs3,000 for three-wheelers and Rs5,000 for cars with engine capacities below 2,000cc. The penalty rises to Rs10,000 for larger cars and Rs15,000 for public service vehicles.
With motorists facing penalties from city traffic police, Safe City Authority cameras and Ring Road police, the increase adds to the financial burden on people using Lahore's roads.
While the higher fines are intended to strengthen enforcement of traffic laws and improve road safety, motorists already facing challans from multiple enforcement systems must contend with the cumulative cost of traffic violations.
