title: Residents raise alarm over  narrowing of Nehr e Khayyam
description: Residents raise alarm over  narrowing of Nehr e Khayyam
content:
Residents of Clifton Block 5, joined by environmentalists, architects, engineers and public representatives, inspected Nehr-e-Khayyam for the third consecutive Sunday, expressing concerns over ongoing construction, newly erected barricades and the waterway's drainage capacity.
During the resident-led site inspection, participants observed and documented the installation of three to four rows of concrete box drains, each measuring three metres, which residents said had narrowed the waterway from its original 120-foot width to approximately 50-60 feet.
Residents demanded the disclosure of project documents, engineering designs, environmental assessments and details of the approved scope of work. They also objected to proposed commercial activities, including shops and a food street, on Nehr-e-Khayyam land.
Climate Action Centre Yasir Hussain said the project raised questions about compliance with legal requirements, including prior information to residents, environmental assessment and disclosure of the project proponent and public-private partnership arrangements. He also questioned the absence of sewage treatment provisions and sought clarification on the engineering design.
Leader of the Opposition in the KMC City Council Advocate Saifuddin warned that sewage mixed with garbage could clog the concrete drainage system, creating serious maintenance and sanitation problems.
Pakistan Maholiyati Tahaffuz Movement representative Ahmad Shabbar questioned the arrangements for sewage disposal beyond the Nehr, warning that without a clear plan, contaminated water could return to the channel during high tide. He also sought details about sludge removal, waste management, potential methane accumulation and the possible heat-island effect associated with concrete covering.
Boat Basin Food Street President Naeem Sajjad raised concerns about potential hazards from enclosing sewage in concrete drains.
A retired civil engineer associated with the Karachi Water and Sewerage Board stressed that the design must account for high tides, downstream water levels and their effects on gravity-driven discharge.
With construction continuing, residents urged the relevant authorities to disclose outstanding information, address engineering and environmental concerns, and ensure meaningful public consultation.

title: DNA mix up prompts second exhumation in honour killing case
description: DNA mix up prompts second exhumation in honour killing case
content:
First samples reportedly belonged to elderly woman after grave was wrongly identified
A court-supervised second exhumation was carried out on Sunday to collect fresh forensic samples from the remains of a 21-year-old woman allegedly murdered in the name of honour in Jamshoro district, after the first attempt failed to establish her identity through DNA testing because the grave had reportedly been wrongly identified.
The exhumation of Zulekhan was conducted at Jiye Shah graveyard under the supervision of Second Civil Judge and Judicial Magistrate Aamir Riaz Rasool Memon. A medical board comprising Additional Police Surgeon Dr Muhammad Adeel Rajput, Dr Madiha Sheikh, Dr Asad Memon and other officials collected samples from the remains for laboratory analysis.
Zulekhan was allegedly drugged and strangled to death on May 22, 2025, in the Syedabad area of Jamshoro district. Following the incident, Kotri DSP Shah Nawaz Jokhio told a press conference that the woman had allegedly been killed by her two brothers, Abdullah and Sanaullah, uncle Muhammad Ibrahim, nephew Saddam and maternal uncle Saifullah. Police had announced the arrest of three suspects, but the accused were subsequently released on bail.
The first exhumation was conducted after the grave was identified by the victim's brother Abdullah and maternal uncle Muhammad Alam Bardi. Fourteen samples were collected, but DNA testing reportedly failed to match the victim, with the samples instead found to belong to an elderly woman.
The victim's mother, Sher Bano, challenged the identification of the grave, prompting the court to order a second exhumation. This time, the grave was identified by the mother herself, and the newly collected samples have been sent for chemical and forensic analysis.
The victim's husband, Nadeem Bardi, has not been included in the case because of a reported mental illness.

title: Sindh lab declares six medicines counterfeit
description: Sindh lab declares six medicines counterfeit
content:
Seven samples fail tests as active ingredients go undetected
The Sindh Drug Testing Laboratory has declared seven samples of six widely used medicines counterfeit after tests failed to detect their required active ingredients, while the pharmaceutical companies named on their packaging denied manufacturing the products.
The medicines include Augmentin 625mg, Velosef 500mg, No-Spa Forte 80mg, Mucon Suspension, Brexin tablets and Lexoberon Liquid, according to laboratory reports issued by Syed Adnan Rizvi, director of the Sindh Drug Testing Laboratory Karachi and provincial government analyst.
The samples were declared counterfeit under the Drugs Act, 1976. The reports detail the test findings, batch numbers and responses from the manufacturers named on the packaging.
The laboratory found no detectable amoxicillin trihydrate or clavulanic acid in the Augmentin 625mg tablet sample. GlaxoSmithKline Pakistan Limited, whose name appeared on the packaging, disowned the product in a letter dated September 24, 2026.
The Velosef 500mg capsule sample also failed testing, with no cefradine detected. GlaxoSmithKline Pakistan Limited denied manufacturing the product in a letter dated September 9, 2026.
Similarly, the No-Spa Forte 80mg tablet sample contained no detectable drotaverine hydrochloride. Hoechst Pakistan Limited, named on the packaging, disowned the product in a letter dated September 7, 2026.
The laboratory also failed to detect oxethazaine, aluminium hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide in the Mucon Suspension sample. Lucky Core Limited Pharmaceuticals denied manufacturing the product in a letter dated September 7, 2026.
In the case of Brexin tablets, testing found no detectable piroxicam beta-cyclodextrin, the medicine's stated active ingredient. GlaxoSmithKline Pakistan Limited disowned the product through a letter dated September 7, 2026.
Meanwhile, two samples of Lexoberon Liquid, from batches numbered 46292 and 43445, failed to show the presence of sodium picosulfate monohydrate.

title: Why are blood ties weakening in Pakistani society
description: Why are blood ties weakening in Pakistani society
content:
From family feuds to property disputes, economic pressures and changing lifestyles are driving relatives apart
Once bound by blood and tradition, Pakistani families are increasingly being torn apart by money, property disputes and changing lifestyles. From fathers disowning sons to brothers becoming bitter rivals, relationships that once offered lifelong support are giving way to silence, resentment and estrangement.
A recent incident in Karachi, involving the alleged suicide of Dr Umar and his family, highlighted the extent to which family ties can deteriorate. Dr Umar's brother, Muhammad Abu Bakr, told police that the two had not been in contact for the past 10 years. Their estrangement was so severe that Abu Bakr did not even know how many children his brother had. He learnt only after the incident, when he arrived in Karachi, that Dr Umar had three daughters.
The father of Dr Umar's wife, Mahwish, also told police and the media that he had been out of contact with his daughter for a considerable period. As a result, he was unaware of the family's deteriorating financial circumstances. He said he had visited his daughter's flat for the first time after the incident.
Announcements and public notices declaring estrangement between close relatives regularly appear in newspapers and on social media. Fathers disown sons, while brothers publicly sever ties with one another, often following prolonged family disputes.
Abdul Jabbar, a Larkana resident, told The Express Tribune he had considered disowning his drug-addicted son but dropped the idea after friends intervened. However, the two have long remained out of contact.
Last April, Pakistan People's Party (PPP) MNA Mir Aijaz Jakhrani publicly severed ties with his half-brother, Azad Jakhrani, days after their father's death. Their relationship had deteriorated following the death of Ejaz's son, Zaid, and later soured further over their father's property.
Social scientists say several factors are contributing to the breakdown of family relationships, including urbanisation, changing lifestyles, financial pressures and disputes over inheritance.
Dr Riaz Ahmed Shaikh, a professor in the Department of Social Sciences at Shaheed Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Institute of Science and Technology (SZABIST), Karachi, told The Express Tribune that rapid urbanisation had largely dismantled the traditional joint-family system.
In rural communities, extended families traditionally lived together and supported one another in times of need. In cities, however, larger families often cannot live under one roof, weakening everyday interaction and mutual support.
Dr Shaikh also pointed to changing marriage patterns. In the past, marriages between cousins often kept extended families closely connected. As marriages increasingly take place outside the immediate family network, he said, relationships with blood relatives may become less close.
Advocate Muhammad Ismail Rajput said rising needs and growing aspirations were also creating friction within families. Financial difficulties can trigger disagreements when relatives are unable to meet one another's needs, while competing ambitions and expectations can widen existing rifts.
Property and other family disputes frequently end up in court, where relatives become opposing parties in lengthy legal battles. Rajput said thousands of cases involving family members were pending before different courts. As disputes drag on, relatives who once shared close bonds can begin to treat one another more like adversaries than family.

title: Picnic turns fatal as truck rams car
description: Picnic turns fatal as truck rams car
content:
One killed, four injured as speeding truck hits car on Superhighway
A 19-year-old man was killed and four others were seriously injured when a speeding truck rammed their car near Jamali Bridge on the Superhighway early Sunday morning. The victims were returning from a picnic at a farmhouse when the accident occurred in front of Mandi House within the jurisdiction of the Site Superhighway police station.
The deceased was identified as Muhammad Sufyan, son of Muhammad Yasir, a resident of Gulshan-e-Iqbal Society in Malir who was undergoing an apprenticeship at Pakistan International Airlines (PIA). The injured were identified as Abdullah, Ahmed, Bilal and Abdul Rehman.
According to the duty officer at the Site Superhighway Industrial Area police station, 10 friends had travelled to a farmhouse for a picnic in two cars. Five of them were travelling in the car that met with the accident while they were returning.
Rescue officials said the crash was apparently caused by overspeeding. A speeding Shahzore truck struck the car from behind, causing the driver to lose control and the vehicle to crash into the footpath. The truck driver abandoned the vehicle and fled the scene after the accident.
Sufyan's body was shifted to Abbasi Shaheed Hospital for medico-legal formalities, while the injured were taken to Dow University Hospital for treatment. Police moved the damaged car and the truck to the police station and launched a further investigation into the incident.
A 28-year-old food delivery rider was also killed after a speeding car hit his motorcycle near the Matriculation Board Office in North Nazimabad in the early hours of Sunday, police said. The police detained four youths travelling in the car and registered a case against the driver, identified as Azaan, according to PS North Nazimabad SHO Adeel Ahmed.
The deceased, Imtiaz, was a resident of Banaras Town in Orangi Town. A friend of Imtaiz alleged that the occupants of the car were under the influence of intoxicants. He also claimed that he was assaulted when he reached the scene.
Imtiaz's brother said the deceased had been working as a food delivery rider for the past six years and was due to get married next year.

title: Five of a family killed in horrific road crash
description: Five of a family killed in horrific road crash
content:
CM directs officials to ensure best medical care for three injured women
Five members of a family, including two five-year-old boys, were killed and three women injured when a passenger coach and a car collided head-on on Tando Adam Jhol Road in Sanghar district in the wee hours of Sunday.
The crash left the car trapped beneath the coach, with the dead and injured pinned inside for hours, while the coach driver fled the scene. The passenger coach was travelling from Karachi to Sanghar when it collided head-on with the car.
The deceased were identified as 48-year-old Mano Kolhi, his 40-year-old wife Neelan, their 30-year-old son Ramoon, his five-year-old son Deval, and five-year-old Kanyo, identified in the police account as Ramoon's nephew.
Three women, Roshni, Heeri, wife of Ramoon, and Gulabi, sustained injuries.
Police and local residents rushed to the scene after receiving information about the crash. The car was cut free from beneath the coach to retrieve the bodies and rescue the injured, who were shifted to the taluka hospital. The injured women were later referred to Hyderabad for further treatment.
The coach driver escaped after the collision. Following the completion of legal formalities, the bodies were handed over to the bereaved family.
According to police, the victims belonged to the village of Bilawal Khoso in the New Saeedabad taluka of Matiari district. The family was returning home after attending a charity feast in the village of Piro Faqir Shoro when tragedy struck.
The arrival of the five bodies in Bilawal Khoso plunged the village into grief, with anguished cries echoing through the bereaved household and a pall of mourning descending on the area.
The family had suffered a similar catastrophe in 2019, when seven young labourers from the same household were killed and several others seriously injured in a collision between a Qingqi rickshaw and a passenger coach near Wanjhari on the National Highway. Some of the survivors were left disabled.
Described as extremely poor and struggling to make ends meet, the family is now facing the burden of arranging the latest victims' last rites. Social and civil society organisations have been appealing on social media for financial assistance to help cover the funeral expenses.
Sindh CM Murad Ali Shah has expressed deep sorrow over the loss of lives, extending condolences to the bereaved families and praying for the speedy recovery of the injured.
He directed the relevant authorities to ensure the provision of the best possible medical treatment to those injured. He also expressed heartfelt sympathy with the families of the deceased.
Urging citizens and drivers to strictly observe traffic laws, the CM stressed the need to avoid overspeeding and reckless driving, saying the protection of human lives should be every citizen's foremost priority.
He called on drivers to operate vehicles carefully and within prescribed speed limits, warning that even a moment of negligence could lead to a fatal accident. Strict compliance with traffic regulations and responsible driving, he said, could help save precious lives.

title: Int l Silk Route Festival opens in capital
description: Int l Silk Route Festival opens in capital
content:
Diplomats, tourism officials gather at PNCA to promote trade and cultural exchange
The International Silk Route Festival commenced at the Pakistan National Council of the Arts (PNCA) on Saturday, bringing together diplomats, government officials, tourism representatives, business entrepreneurs, sponsors, young people, exhibitors and international delegates to celebrate Pakistan's cultural heritage and promote regional cooperation through tourism, trade and cultural exchange.
The festival was organised by Silk Route Enterprises in collaboration with the Pakistan Tourism Development Corporation (PTDC) under the Ministry of Inter-Provincial Coordination, provincial tourism departments and private-sector stakeholders.
The festival was organised by Silk Route Enterprises directors Sadaf Khalid Khan, Mian Hashim Masood and Prince Shehryar Khan to revive the spirit of the ancient Silk Route and strengthen Pakistan's connections with Central Asia, China, South Asia and the wider international community.
The opening ceremony was attended by Sardar Yasir Ilyas Khan, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Tourism, as the chief guest.
Sadaf Khalid Khan and Mian Hashim Masood warmly welcomed the chief guest and distinguished diplomatic representatives, including Uzbekistan Ambassador Alisher Tukhtaev, Sri Lankan High Commissioner Rear Admiral Fred Senevirathne, Portuguese Ambassador Paulo Miguel Guedes Dominguez, Tajikistan Ambassador Sharifzoda Yusuf Toir and Belarus Ambassador Andrei Metelitsa. Representatives of government tourism departments, the private business sector, international delegates from Sri Lanka and Malaysia, and members of the youth community also attended.
In his welcome address, Sardar Yasir Ilyas Khan appreciated the efforts of the Silk Route Enterprises team in organising the international initiative.
He highlighted Pakistan's enormous potential for tourism, trade and investment with countries across the Silk Route region and emphasised the need to translate these opportunities into practical cooperation.
He also proposed establishing a dedicated task force to promote the Silk Route region, stressing the importance of coordinated efforts among government institutions, tourism departments, private-sector stakeholders and international partners to strengthen regional connectivity and develop sustainable tourism and trade opportunities.
Managing Director of the Pakistan Tourism Development Corporation Aftab ur Rehman Rana also highlighted Pakistan's significant potential for tourism, trade and cultural exchange with countries along the historic Silk Route.
He emphasised the importance of promoting Pakistan's diverse tourism attractions, cultural heritage and regional connections to attract international visitors and create new opportunities for cooperation.
The International Silk Route Festival seeks to revive the legacy of the ancient Silk Route, which historically connected civilisations through trade, knowledge, art and cultural interaction. These historic routes linked regions stretching from China and South Asia through Central Asia and the Middle East towards Europe, facilitating the exchange of goods, ideas, traditions and innovations.
Building on this historic legacy, the festival aims to establish a contemporary platform for cultural diplomacy, tourism promotion, business networking, investment opportunities and people-to-people engagement.

title: Bus stand s transfer prompts protest call
description: Bus stand s transfer prompts protest call
content:
Municipal corporation union president arrested, sent to Jhelum jail
Despite the imposition of Section 144, a protest has been announced against the decision to transfer the General Bus Stand in Pirwadhai from the Municipal Corporation to the Regional Transport Authority.
The president of the Municipal Corporation's Collective Bargaining Agent (CBA) union has been arrested under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance and sent to Jhelum jail.
Deputy Commissioner and Municipal Corporation Administrator Nadeem Nasir visited the Rawalpindi Municipal Corporation (RMC) office and convened a meeting of supervisors working under the Suthra Punjab programme.
He said exemplary cleanliness must be ensured in accordance with the chief minister's vision and that there would be no protests, only work. He added that his doors were open to those willing to work.
The secretary of the Regional Transport Authority was appointed administrator of the General Bus Stand in Pirwadhai, which operates under the Municipal Corporation.
In response, CBA union president Haroonur Rashid called for a protest, refusing to accept the decision. He is facing trial in a May 9 case and had been suspended from service, but was continuing to perform his duties as union president while on bail.
However, he was arrested under Section 144 and sent to Jhelum jail. He was also made to vacate his official residence.
Meanwhile, Deputy Commissioner and Municipal Corporation Administrator Nadeem Nasir made a surprise visit to the Municipal Corporation office on Friday and summoned a meeting of Suthra Punjab supervisors. Chief Officer of the Municipal Corporation Faisal Shehzad was also present.
Addressing the meeting, the deputy commissioner said no one should assume that their job was permanent. Those who worked would remain employed. He said he would recruit even 600 new workers if necessary to ensure cleanliness in the city.
"There will be no protests, only work," he said, adding that the supervisors should consider whether a person who could not protect himself could protect them.
He urged the workers to focus on their duties and assured them that their problems would be addressed. He said his office doors would remain open to them from 9:30am to 11:30am.
Whether the issue concerned their children's school fees, medicines or any other difficulty, he said, efforts would be made to resolve it.

title: Exhibit spotlights snow leopard conservation
description: Exhibit spotlights snow leopard conservation
content:
WWF-Pakistan, in collaboration with Serena Hotels, recently marked World Snow Leopard Day with a special exhibition titled 'The Mountains We Share: People, Snow Leopards and Stories of Coexistence', celebrating decades of conservation efforts and the people and partnerships dedicated to protecting one of Pakistan's most elusive and iconic species.
Held at Serena Hotel Islamabad, the event brought together government representatives, diplomats, conservation organisations and other stakeholders to review progress in snow leopard conservation and discuss the challenges facing the species and the mountain communities that share its habitat.
Through photographs, personal accounts and an illustrated timeline, the exhibition traced the evolution of snow leopard conservation in Pakistan, from early field observations and pioneering research to satellite tracking, community-led initiatives and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, to strengthen wildlife protection. It highlighted the growing recognition that safeguarding snow leopards requires more than protecting the species alone. Addressing human-wildlife conflict, supporting local communities, preserving connected habitats and improving protected-area management are essential to ensuring the long-term survival of the apex predator.
The event featured addresses by Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar, WWF International President Dr Adil Najam, WWF-Pakistan Director General Hammad Naqi Khan, and Serena Hotels Corporate Director of Human Resources and Organisational Development Dr Moin Uddin.
The programme also featured perspectives from mountain communities and wildlife photographers, alongside stories written by children imagining the world through the eyes of a snow leopard.
Pakistan is one of only 12 countries that provide a habitat for the snow leopard, making its conservation significant beyond national borders. The exhibition underscored the importance of sustained scientific research, community stewardship and institutional collaboration in protecting the species and the fragile mountain ecosystems on which people and wildlife depend.

title: Hina Javed s family seeks judicial probe
description: Hina Javed s family seeks judicial probe
content:
Alleges key evidence was overlooked in investigation; urges CM to form commission
The family of Hina Javed, who was murdered in a high-profile case in Rawalpindi, has written an open letter to Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, demanding the immediate formation of a judicial commission to ensure a transparent investigation.
The family has urged the chief minister to personally review the complete case file, alleging that investigators shifted their focus towards a domestic worker before key forensic reports were received, while crucial evidence concerning the victim's husband and father-in-law was allegedly overlooked.
In the letter, the family said repeated attempts to contact the chief minister directly had failed. However, it had conveyed its reservations about the procedure adopted by the police investigation committee through various forums and government representatives.
The family claimed that DNA belonging to Hina's husband, Faisal Asghar, and his father was found on her neck. It also alleged that the victim's father-in-law had initially described the incident as a burglary at the house.
According to the letter, forensic reports concerning the mobile phones of Hina and the suspects are still pending, while important messages had also been deleted from the victim's phone. The family alleged that investigators had directed the probe towards the domestic worker before receiving forensic and fingerprint reports.
While also accusing the domestic worker of involvement in the murder, the family demanded a thorough and impartial examination of the roles of Faisal Asghar and the other suspects, along with all evidence available against them.
The letter maintained that determining whether a person was guilty or innocent was ultimately the court's responsibility. However, the family said it had no confidence in the findings and procedures of the police investigation committee, making a judicial commission necessary to ensure a transparent probe.
Addressing the chief minister, the family recalled her commitment to treating violence and injustice against women as a red line and urged her to play an effective role in securing justice for Hina.
Meanwhile, in her second social media statement on the case, Maryam Nawaz said the investigation had not yet been completed and assured the family that no effort would be spared to ensure justice. She also said she would personally meet the victim's family.

title: Private schools get one week to register

content:
Rawalpindi authorities warn of permanent sealing in crackdown
The District Registration Authority for Schools in Rawalpindi has issued red notices to all unregistered private schools across the district, giving them a one-week deadline to complete their registration.
The authorities have warned that all unregistered private schools will be permanently sealed in a grand operation after the deadline expires.
The authority has also approved third-party safety audits of private school buildings and government school buildings and formally constituted a committee for the purpose.
Registration has been approved for 34 new private schools, which have been directed to establish IT and science laboratories and submit the relevant certificates.
The important meeting was chaired by Additional Deputy Commissioner for Social Services Fazail Mudassir. Officials from the education and buildings departments, along with representatives of private school associations, also attended.
The registration process of one school was deferred because its documents were incomplete. The meeting also approved fines for institutions that violated government orders during the summer vacations.
The third-party school building safety audit committee will be headed by the additional commissioner.
Its members will include the chief executive officer of education, the executive engineer of the buildings department and the deputy director of development.
Abrar Ahmed Khan, a member of the District Registration Authority, expressed concern over notices issued by certain tehsil municipal administration officials during safety audits, directing schools to convert their buildings to commercial use.
He called on the relevant authorities to take immediate notice of the matter.
The additional deputy commissioner said no unregistered private school would be allowed to operate in the future. He added that all schools whose buildings were declared unsafe would also be sealed, stressing that the lives of children were their highest priority.
On the other hand, the Strategic Management Unit (SMU) of the Punjab School Education Department has given final approval to paint colours, codes and finishes for buildings being constructed under the provincial development project, "Additional Classrooms, Missing Facilities, Dangerous Buildings and SMC Classrooms", across government schools in the province.

title: Lula says bus cuts hinder voters in Brazil

content:
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva said Sunday that many people had been "barred from voting" after buses were taken out of circulation in Sao Paulo and several other cities.
"We are asking the Supreme Court to extend the electoral process so that those who were effectively barred from voting, due to the dirty tactics of mayors, can still cast their votes," said Lula.

Lula said 40 percent of buses were pulled from service in Sao Paulo, a problem also taking place in several cities in his native northeastern Brazil.
"I've never complained about anything in any election before. Whether I won or lost, I'd just accept it and get ready for the next one. But this time, something abominable is happening," he said.
"No one should give up on voting just because some scoundrel of a business owner or some crooked, criminal mayor tried to stop the people from casting their ballots."
The regional electoral court of the northeastern state of Bahia, where Lula won 65 percent of the vote in the first round, ordered the arrest of the local transport secretary for failing to offer free transport on election day.
Local media reported that 75 buses had been prevented from leaving garages in the city.
"We do, in fact, have transportation difficulties in some locations, which are already being resolved," Kassio Nunes, president of the Superior Electoral Court, told journalists.

title: Pakistan boosts sea LPG imports amid land cuts
description: Pakistan boosts sea LPG imports amid land cuts
content:
Iran supply disruptions push domestic retail prices higher
Pakistan has accelerated liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) imports through the sea route following disruptions to supplies from Iran, with more than 11,600 tonnes of the fuel arriving at Karachi's ports in a week as retail prices soar countrywide.
An LPG carrier, Yellow Stone, carrying 4,000 metric tonnes of gas loaded in Bahrain, berthed at Port Qasim on October 24, marking another addition to the country's seaborne supplies, port authorities said on Sunday.
In a statement, the Port Qasim Authority (PQA) said the vessel's arrival marked the commencement of cargo handling in accordance with applicable procedures, underscoring the port's role in facilitating essential energy imports for domestic and commercial consumers.
The latest consignment follows the arrival of two other vessels within the preceding 72 hours.
The PGC Yiannios, carrying 4,520 tonnes of LPG, berthed at the Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) terminal, while the Alisa 1, carrying 3,083 tonnes, completed its cargo operation.
The shift towards seaborne imports comes after the suspension of LPG bowser movement across the Gabd-Rimdan border crossing between Pakistan and Iran disrupted land-based supplies, contributing to a sharp increase in prices.
In Lahore, consumers reported paying as much as Rs570 per kilogramme, almost double the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority's (Ogra) official rate of Rs279 per kilogramme for October.
Market prices have reportedly reached Rs500 to Rs600 per kilogramme in Punjab and Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, with rates climbing even higher in colder and hilly areas. Consumers said some vendors had stopped selling LPG openly following government action against overpricing but continued supplying it discreetly at inflated rates.
Pakistan's daily LPG consumption is estimated at 4,000 to 4,500 tonnes, against domestic production of around 2,000 to 2,500 tonnes. Demand typically rises to 6,000 to 7,000 tonnes a day during peak winter, when households increasingly depend on the fuel for cooking and heating.
Pakistan LPG Distributors Association Chairman Irfan Khokhar warned that prices could rise further if supply disruptions persisted. He called for immediate imports, stricter action against overcharging and a review of Ogra's pricing mechanism.
Meanwhile, commercial cargo movement has resumed at the Gabd-Rimdan crossing. Mir Naveed Jan Kalmati, president of the Gwadar Chamber of Commerce and Industry, told a private television channel that trade operations had restarted on Saturday morning.
Iranian Ambassador to Pakistan Reza Amiri-Moghaddam also said on Sunday that Iran's borders with neighbouring countries remained open for trade.
Referring to reports that several hundred trucks carrying LPG had crossed the Rimdan-Gabd border but were awaiting clearance, the ambassador said bilateral border trade was an integral part of agreements reached at the highest levels and served the interests of both countries.
With winter approaching and demand expected to rise, additional seaborne consignments could help ease supply pressures. However, the extent of relief for consumers will depend on the continuity of imports, the resumption of cross-border supplies and the enforcement of official prices in local markets.

title: Shadab scripts a miracle as Pakistan stun England
description: Shadab scripts a miracle as Pakistan stun England
content:
Hits 113, shares 89-run last wicket stand with Haris in one-wicket win
Shadab Khan eventually lived up to the expectations as he hit his maiden century to put Pakistan in the final when they conquered England by one wicket in a crucial ODI tri-series clash at the Gaddafi Stadium Lahore on Sunday.
Set to chase 242, Pakistan were reeling at 154-9 in the 34th over and there was no hope of a resurrection.
However, Shadab engineered a stunning knock, hitting unbeaten 113 off 96 balls to steer the hosts to unbelievable victory with 17 balls to spare. Shadab hammered five sixes and 13 fours in his first century of his career.
He dominated an 89-run tenth wicket unbroken stand with Haris Rauf, who remained not out on seven which came off 19 balls.
Jamie Overton was the pick of the bowlers with 3-43 while Gus Atkinson and Liam Dawson claimed two wickets each.
Set to chase 242, Pakistan suffered a lengthy collapse. The hosts kept losing wickets at regular intervals
Green-shirts got off to a shaky start as Gus Atkinson and debutant Henry Crocombe struck early to put them under immediate pressure. Fakhar Zaman departed for ten off 18 balls, caught by Jamie Overton off Atkinson, before Crocombe dismissed Saim Ayub for six, also caught by Overton. Atkinson then removed Babar Azam for ten, bowled, leaving Pakistan struggling at 31-3 inside seven overs.
Stumper Saad Baig briefly revived hopes of a recovery with an aggressive innings of 32 off just 22 balls, striking seven fours. His attacking approach helped Pakistan move forward, but Jamie Overton ended the counterattack by having him caught by Will Jacks to leave Pakistan reeling at 74-4.
Salman Agha and Hasan Nawaz attempted to rebuild the innings through a more cautious partnership. Salman made 26 from 49 deliveries while Hasan scored 15 off 33 balls. Liam Dawson broke through by dismissing Hasan, caught by Harry Brook, before Overton removed Arafat Minhas for one, caught by Joe Root. Pakistan slipped to 103-6, with pressure mounting.
Salman became Dawson's second victim when he was caught by Sam Curran for 26, reducing Pakistan to 122-7. Overton then claimed his third wicket by dismissing Shaheen Afridi as Pakistan fell to 131-8. Will Jacks then removed Razaullah (8) and now there was no such hope left. But Shadab had thought otherwise to gift a sensational win to the hosts.
Earlier, Ben Duckett struck his fifth one-day international century to take England to a seemingly good total.
Duckett scored 105 off 111 balls, including ten fours and two sixes, anchoring England's innings after they lost three wickets for 19 runs inside the first five overs.
Tom Banton fell for four, Joe Root scored five and captain Harry Brook was run out for one as Pakistan made an early breakthrough with the new ball.
Duckett rebuilt the innings alongside Sam Curran, who contributed 42 off 52 deliveries. The pair added 126 runs for the fifth wicket before Curran was dismissed by Shaheen Shah Afridi for 42.
Duckett reached his century off 104 balls, but Pakistan struck regularly in the latter stages to prevent England from building a commanding total.
Shaheen finished with 4-46 from 8.4 overs, also reaching the milestone of 150 ODI wickets. Left-arm spinner Arafat Minhas claimed 2-26, while debutant Razaullah also took two wickets, conceding 38 runs in eight overs.
Razaullah marked his ODI debut with the dismissals of Will Jacks, who scored 13, and Liam Dawson, who made five.
Gus Atkinson provided a late contribution with an unbeaten 36 off 28 balls, including three sixes, but England were dismissed with 20 balls remaining.
The third straight loss put England on the brink of elimination.
Earlier Pakistan opted to field first after they won toss. Pakistan made two changes, bringing in Shadab Khan in place of Faheem Ashraf. Fast bowler Razaullah will make his ODI debut as he has replaced Naseem Shah whose left hand finger has dislocated. But skipper Shaheen Afridi said that he would be fit for the next game against Sri Lanka.
England made one change, bringing in Henry Crocombe in place of Josh Tongue. Henry will make his international debut as a fast bowler. Pakistan have won their previous two matches and they need just one win to qualify for the final.
The 89-run unbeaten tenth wicket partnership between Shadab and Haris is the highest in a successful ODI chase, surpassing Deryck Murray and Andy Roberts' previous record of an unbeaten 64 for West Indies against Pakistan in the 1975 World Cup.
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif congratulated the Pakistan cricket team on their thrilling victory, praising the players' determination and the match-winning partnership between Shadab and Haris.
In a statement, President Zardari lauded Shadab's century and his decisive last-wicket stand with Haris, saying the team had displayed courage, determination and excellent cricket. He also praised the national side's overall performance in the tri-nation series and congratulated Pakistan Cricket Board Chairman Mohsin Naqvi on the team's success.
In a post on X, Prime Minister Shehbaz said every run, wicket and catch reflected the team's grit, discipline and fighting spirit. He described Shadab's century as spectacular and said the partnership with Haris had turned the match around. He also praised the Lahore crowd for filling millions of hearts with pride and joy, and commended Naqvi and his team for their efforts to strengthen Pakistan cricket and promote international cricket on home soil.

title: Riyadh reopens airport amid fresh attacks
description: Riyadh reopens airport amid fresh attacks
content:
Three explosions were heard in Riyadh late on Sunday as Saudi Arabia intercepted missiles and drones targeting its capital and southern regions, while Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis renewed threats against the kingdom's main airport, which partially resumed operations following a deadly attack earlier this month.
The blasts echoed across the Saudi capital after residents received emergency alerts warning of a "hostile aerial threat", an AFP journalist reported. Saudi civil defence also issued alerts for the southern cities of Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran, before announcing that the danger had passed.
The Saudi-led coalition said two drones and a ballistic missile had been launched towards Riyadh, while a cruise missile targeted Khamis Mushait. It later reported intercepting 10 ballistic missiles fired towards southern Saudi Arabia.
Saudi civil defence said shrapnel from the interception of two ballistic missiles over Khamis Mushait and Ahad Rafidah injured two people and damaged residential buildings and vehicles. The attacks came as King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh partially resumed operations at two terminals on Sunday.
The airport had suspended operations on October 10 following an attack claimed by the Houthis that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300. The airport said late on Saturday that Terminal 1 would handle domestic flights, while Terminal 2 would serve international flights operated by national carriers.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree warned that the airport would "never be safe", describing it as a "military target" and urging airlines, airport staff and travellers to stay away. The group also claimed to have attacked the airport and Saudi oil facilities on Saturday.
The Saudi-led coalition said earlier this month that the Houthis had carried out 20 attacks on the airport between October 1 and 11. The renewed fighting has also shattered a United Nations-brokered truce that had largely held since 2022.
The escalation has added to regional instability amid the US-Israeli offensive against Iran, placing Saudi Arabia, a US ally, under increasing pressure. US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that he had ruled out striking Iran that day.

title: PM says poverty must not block education
description: PM says poverty must not block education
content:
Shehbaz launches 500,000 Chromebook distribution Highlights technology's role in modern-day learning Students t
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Sunday launched a nationwide initiative to distribute 500,000 Chromebooks equipped with internet connectivity among talented and deserving students over the next two years, saying financial hardship must not prevent young people from pursuing education and developing their abilities.
Addressing the launch ceremony of the Prime Minister's Youth Chromebook Scheme, Shehbaz said providing modern educational facilities and technology to the country's youth was a collective responsibility and essential to preparing them for an increasingly technology-driven world.
He said the devices would be distributed strictly on merit, with students from mainstream educational institutions and religious seminaries eligible for the programme. The initiative aims to enable beneficiaries to attend classes remotely, access electronic libraries and acquire knowledge beyond the limitations imposed by their circumstances.
"Intelligence and hard work should not be held captive by wealth and poverty," the prime minister said, emphasising that students' abilities and commitment, rather than their financial backgrounds, should determine their eligibility.
The selected students are also being provided with bags and devices to facilitate internet access. According to the prime minister, the connectivity offered through the initiative could benefit an estimated 2.5 million people, including family members of the recipients.
Recalling earlier laptop distribution programmes launched under former prime minister Nawaz Sharif, Shehbaz said 600,000 laptops had been distributed on merit across the country over approximately a decade, covering Punjab, Sindh, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan, Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Kashmir.
The prime minister said the government now intended to distribute 500,000 Chromebooks within two years, accelerating efforts to equip students with the tools required to compete internationally and pursue higher education.
He said the earlier laptop scheme had demonstrated its value during the Covid-19 pandemic, when students relied on technology to continue university classes and learning despite widespread disruption. Many beneficiaries had subsequently secured employment and become doctors, engineers and other professionals, he added.
Shehbaz said access to education should remain a priority for the government, regardless of a student's social or economic background. He described education and ability as lasting assets that could not be taken away by changing financial circumstances.
Highlighting the programme's inclusive approach, the prime minister referred to Syed Shams Raza, a student whose father had been martyred, and Alma Mahak Sabir, a student from a religious seminary who had spoken about her educational ambitions at the ceremony.
He praised Shams for continuing his education despite personal hardships and said the country had many talented young people facing similar challenges. He also commended Mahak for her confidence and determination, addressing concerns that students enrolled in religious seminaries might be excluded from technology-based educational initiatives.
Shehbaz clarified that students from seminaries had also benefited from previous laptop distribution programmes alongside those attending universities and colleges. The new scheme, he said, would follow the same principle, with merit and hard work serving as the criteria for selection.
The prime minister also highlighted the government's efforts to expand access to quality education through the Daanish Schools programme. He said he had recently inaugurated a Daanish School in Islamabad, while another 27 campuses were under construction across the country.
According to Shehbaz, the schools would provide modern educational facilities, including smart boards, electronic libraries, sports grounds, residential accommodation and food facilities, without charging students. He said financial constraints should not stand in the way of children receiving quality education.
He thanked Rashid Minhas, associated with the Tokyo Care Foundation, for supporting the Chromebook initiative, describing the contribution as a reflection of overseas Pakistanis' confidence in the potential of the country's youth.
Education Minister Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui, addressing the ceremony, said Pakistan needed to adapt to changing educational trends and turn its approximately 150 million young people into a productive national asset. He said effective investment in youth was crucial to ensuring the country's demographic advantage translated into progress.
Tokyo Technology Care Foundation Chairman Rashid Minhas said the memorandum signed with the government aimed to empower students to become creators in the digital world and contribute to a national digital transformation.
Prime Minister's Youth Programme Chairman Rana Mashhood Ahmad Khan also praised the initiative, saying the involvement of overseas Pakistanis and renewed international confidence in Pakistan offered opportunities for young people to excel in technology and innovation.
The prime minister distributed Chromebooks among selected students at the ceremony, which was attended by ministers, parliamentarians, educationists, vice chancellors, diplomats and other guests.
The government has previously distributed around 600,000 laptops under the Prime Minister's Youth Laptop Scheme, launched in 2014. The latest initiative comes amid efforts to expand local technology production, including the establishment of a Chromebook assembly line in Pakistan in collaboration with Google and local institutions.

title: 2 servicemen martyred as forces kill 7 terrorists | The Express Tribune
description:
2 servicemen martyred as forces kill
7 terrorists
content:
Security forces killed seven terrorists during two separate intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Dera Ismail Khan district of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) and Qila Saifullah district of Balochistan, while two servicemen were martyred in the line of duty.
According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), security forces conducted an IBO in the Zarkani area of Dera Ismail Khan on Saturday following reports of the presence of Khwarij belonging to Fitna Al Khwarij, a term used for terrorists belonging to the Indian proxy Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
"Owing to meticulous conduct of operation by security forces, six Indian-sponsored Khwarij were sent to hell," the military's media wing said in a statement. However, it added that two servicemen, Naik Ghulam Murtaza and Sepoy Taseer Ahmed, embraced martyrdom.
"During the intense fire exchange, Naik Ghulam Murtaza (age: 36 years, resident of District Gujrat) and Sepoy Taseer Ahmed (age: 30 years, resident of District Talagang), having fought gallantly, paid the ultimate sacrifices and embraced shahadat," the statement said.
Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the slain terrorists, who, according to the ISPR, had been actively involved in numerous attacks against security forces and law enforcement agencies, as well as the killing of innocent civilians.
The ISPR said a sanitisation operation was under way to eliminate any other Indian-sponsored terrorists found in the area. It added that the sacrifices of the soldiers reinforced the military's commitment to safeguarding the country.
"The relentless counter-terrorism campaign under vision 'Azm-e-Istehkam', as approved by the Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan, by security forces and law enforcement agencies will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country."
Separately, Radio Pakistan, citing security sources, reported that security forces killed Adil Shah, alias Darvesh, a commander of Fitna Al Khawarij, during an IBO under Operation 'Radd-ul-Fitna 3' in Qila Saifullah.
The report said the slain commander had been associated with the group since December 2020 and had managed its financial affairs since 2024. He had also been involved in arranging permanent residences for foreign terrorists in Zhob, Sherani and Shaban, the source added.
The commander had been involved in attacks on security forces and kidnappings for ransom since 2022, while 19 first information reports (FIRs) had been registered against him. A bounty of Rs2.5 million had been placed on his head.
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif hailed the security forces for killing the six Indian sponsored terrorists.
They paid tribute to Naik Ghulam Murtaza and Sepoy Taseer Ahmed, who were martyred during the operation.

title: Meghan vowed to keep kids away from her father
description: Meghan vowed to keep kids away from her father
content:
Wrote to him that she knew about allegations against him
Meghan Markle reportedly sent her estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr., a final letter in December 2025, informing him that she knew about allegations against him involving child sexual abuse material and that he would never meet his grandchildren, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet.
According to a report by The Sun, cited by PEOPLE, the Duchess of Sussex sent the letter while her father was recovering in a hospital in the Philippines after undergoing a leg amputation. The letter reportedly marked the final time she intended to contact him, bringing another development to their long-running family estrangement.
Sources cited in the report said Meghan wanted to ensure that her father received and read the letter. Hospital staff reportedly delivered it to him, and he read it several times.
The letter allegedly addressed the accusations that had recently emerged publicly, with Meghan telling her father that she was aware of the allegations and would not allow him to meet her children. The reported communication also stated that she would not contact him again.
The development follows reports that Thomas Markle Jr., Meghan's half-brother, allegedly discovered hundreds or thousands of images depicting child sexual abuse among belongings at his father's former home in Cebu, the Philippines. He reportedly alerted authorities in the Philippines and contacted the FBI.
Thomas Markle Sr., 82, has denied the allegations, describing them as lies. The claims have not been established as fact, and authorities are examining the allegations.
Meghan addressed the situation publicly on October 23, saying she was deeply distressed by the reports and that her decision to keep her father away from her children had been made to protect them.
"I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications' distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them," she said in a statement to PEOPLE.
The Duchess also revealed that she had been made aware of troubling allegations against her father after a letter was sent to the Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection. She said she had been assured that the claims were being investigated.
The Metropolitan Police subsequently confirmed receiving a letter containing allegations of alleged offending outside the United Kingdom in January 2019. The force said it passed the letter to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex but did not share the details with other law enforcement agencies.
Meghan's relationship with her father deteriorated in the lead-up to her 2018 wedding to Prince Harry. Thomas Sr. did not attend the ceremony and has never met Archie, seven, or Lilibet, five.
The reported letter provides further insight into the circumstances surrounding Meghan's decision to maintain the estrangement. However, the allegations against Thomas Sr. remain unproven, and he continues to deny wrongdoing.

title: Video game depicts N Korea s invasion of South
description: Video game depicts N Korea s invasion of South
content:
'Call of Duty', however, is still all the rage in latter
The latest instalment of the "Call of Duty" video game franchise, featuring a full-scale North Korean invasion of South Korea, has topped sales charts in the would-be target, even as real-life border tensions are ratcheting higher.
"Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4", the latest edition of the globally popular franchise is set against a backdrop of tensions between the United States and Russia.
Its Friday release comes on the heels of an explosion inside the heavily fortified Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) that injured three South Korean soldiers, further straining ties on the peninsula.
The game follows several parallel storylines: a squad of young American and South Korean soldiers fighting for survival, a former serviceman driven by revenge, and a power struggle surrounding a new North Korean leader -- a character players can also take on.
The new edition has generated considerable interest in South Korea, where able-bodied men are required to serve between 18 and 21 months in the military, depending on the branch.
The title has topped both the global and South Korean sales charts on Steam, one of the world's largest digital distribution platforms for PC games.
The campaign begins with a surprise invasion of South Korea by North Korean forces, who deploy paratroopers and infiltrate through an underground tunnel to catch South Korean and US troops off guard.
In reality, the US stations about 28,000 troops in South Korea to help deter the nuclear-armed North. Seoul and Pyongyang remain technically at war because the 1950-53 Korean War ended in an armistice rather than a peace treaty.
Reactions among South Korean gamers have been largely positive, with some posting hashtags featuring a Korean slogan meaning "exterminate communism" on social media and others saying they were considering upgrading their computers or buying new consoles to play the title.
"I cried so much playing the game to a point I almost got dehydrated. It reminds me so much of my grandfather, who fought in the Korean War," a Threads user with the handle b_yeol_t said.
Another user, posting under the handle ireozima_zebal, described the experience as "horrifying" because of its implications for a potential conflict on the Korean peninsula.
"This is what would unfold if the North launched an invasion, with the border province of Gangwon overwhelmed within an hour and our defence line pushed back right on the edge of Seoul," the user said.
But the game has also drawn criticism for turning the fraught history between North and South Korea into entertainment.
The title raises the "question of whether it is appropriate... to present the tragedy of the Korean War and the current antagonism between South and North as something to be consumed for entertainment", Kim Sung-jae, chairman of the Kim Dae Jung Peace Center, wrote in the Hankyoreh newspaper last month.
On Saturday, North Korean state media said leader Kim Jong Un had urged his military to become the strongest in the world at a two-day meeting of company commanders in Pyongyang last week.
As of October 2023, Call of Duty has sold over 500 million copies and has 100 million monthly active players across all platforms. The franchise generated $30 billion in revenue by 2022. The series is verified by the Guinness World Records as the best-selling first-person shooter game series. It is the most successful video game franchise created in the United States and the fourth best-selling video game franchise of all time. Other products in the franchise include a line of action figures designed by Plan B Toys, a card game created by Upper Deck Company, Mega Bloks sets by Mega Brands, and a comic book miniseries published by WildStorm Productions, and a feature film in development by Paramount Pictures, set to be released in 2028.
Sledgehammer Games, which were co-developers for Modern Warfare 3, have developed three titles, Advanced Warfare (2014), WWII (2017), and Vanguard (2021). They are the lead developer for Modern Warfare III (2023), the third entry in the Modern Warfare reboot sub-series.

title: Dasti phone case raises SC eyebrows
description: Dasti phone case raises SC eyebrows
content:
The Supreme Court has questioned the registration of multiple criminal cases against PTI MNA Jamshed Ahmed Dasti, with Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi observing that even allegations involving the theft of a Nokia mobile phone had been made against the lawmaker.
"Cases under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) may be understandable, but there is even an allegation of stealing a Nokia mobile phone. In the past, cases of buffalo theft were registered against prominent people. Nokia phones came later," Justice Abbasi remarked during the hearing of Dasti's petition challenging his seven-year sentence in a 2013 fake degree case.
Justice Abbasi criticised the practice of registering multiple cases over the same alleged offence in different parts of the country, observing that the burden ultimately fell on the courts.
"You say the judiciary ranks 136th in the world, but these are your achievements; the judiciary gets the blame," he remarked.
He added that if 100 cases were registered against an individual, it could take a lifetime to get them all resolved. The judge observed that the courts were left helpless and that the public was turning the judicial system into a subject of ridicule.
Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmad Khan, who headed the two-member bench, observed that all members of parliament were respectable in the eyes of the court. However, he questioned the political commitment to judicial independence, saying that politicians tended to remember such principles only after moving into opposition.
"When you move into opposition, you suddenly remember everything, including the independence of the judiciary," Justice Shahzad remarked.
He added that politicians should play their role when they were in power, rather than turning to the courts only when they themselves faced legal action.
During the hearing, Additional Prosecutor General Punjab Tariq Siddiqui informed the court that a report regarding cases registered against Dasti in Punjab had been submitted.
According to the report, 47 cases had been registered against the PTI lawmaker in the province. Of these, 35 had been disposed of, while 12 remained pending.
The bench also questioned Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) officials about their appearance in the proceedings. ECP Director General Law Muhammad Arshad Khan informed the court that the commission was appearing as the complainant in the matter in response to a court notice.
Dasti told the bench that he had waged a struggle against corrupt elements and had also spoken against political party leaders.
Justice Shahzad responded that it appeared Dasti had spent his entire life engaged in this struggle.
Justice Abbasi remarked that Dasti spoke courageously, adding that whether his position was right or wrong was a separate matter.
The Supreme Court directed the inspectors general of police (IGPs) of Sindh, Balochistan, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Islamabad, along with the Attorney General's Office in relation to the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), to submit comprehensive reports within 10 days regarding all pending cases against Dasti.
Justice Abbasi said reports had been sought from all the IGPs and asked who had appeared on behalf of the Islamabad police.
The bench also examined the proceedings relating to the election commission. The ECP's law director informed the court that the National Assembly speaker had referred a matter to the commission, which had subsequently issued a decision. However, the Lahore High Court had suspended the operation of that decision through a stay order.
During the hearing, the Punjab government's counsel argued that, in view of a decision by a two-member bench, the case should be heard by a three-member bench.
Dasti's counsel said he had no objection to the case being heard by either a two-member or a three-member bench.
The SC directed the Punjab government's counsel and other lawyers to come prepared to assist the court on whether the matter should be heard by a two-member or a three-member bench.
The court extended Dasti's interim bail and adjourned until November 4.

title: Muzaffarabad  Murree road accidents kill 14
description: Muzaffarabad  Murree road accidents kill 14
content:
Fourteen people were killed and seven others critically injured in two separate road accidents in the mountainous regions of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) and Murree on Sunday.
In Muzaffarabad, seven people, including a father and his two sons, died when a passenger jeep plunged down a steep mountain slope, while another seven were killed and seven injured after a family van fell into a deep ravine and caught fire in Murree.
The Muzaffarabad accident occurred around noon near Sathra Podemar village, when a jeep travelling from Nakka Shakkar Pattiyan village towards Seri Darra, northeast of the city, went out of control on a landslide-affected stretch of road.
The vehicle had covered barely three kilometres before plunging down the mountainside and rolling over several times, ultimately coming to rest as a wreck.
According to police and administration officials, the jeep fell approximately 1,000 to 1,500 feet below the road, killing all seven occupants at the scene.
"Their bodies were scattered across the accident site," Muzaffarabad Additional Deputy Commissioner Zeeshan Nisar said.
He said local residents retrieved the bodies before being joined by personnel from Rescue 1122. Police later handed over the bodies to the deceased's relatives for burial.
In the separate accident in Murree, seven people were killed and seven others critically injured when a passenger van carrying 14 members of the same family plunged into a deep ravine on Baroha Link Road and caught fire.
The family, comprising men, women and children, was returning after attending a wedding ceremony when the accident occurred. The seven injured sustained serious injuries, and rescue teams were transferring them to Holy Family Hospital in Rawalpindi for treatment.
Their condition was reported to be critical.
The cause of the fire that engulfed the van remained unknown, according to rescue officials.

"The NCCIA has registered cases against the suspects under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA), and further investigations are under way," he said.

title: Lahore faces the return of toxic smog | The Express Tribune
description:
Lahore faces the return 
of toxic smog
content:
Weather and policies briefly cleared the air, but experts warn peak smog season lies ahead
Every year, the government points to improving air quality figures, but in Lahore's smog fortress, the daily struggle to breathe tells another story. A parent's persistent dry cough, a child's wheezing breath, eyes stinging in the haze and mornings shrouded in toxic air have become part of everyday life. As another smog season begins, residents are left wondering how long they must endure air that turns the most basic act of breathing into a health hazard.
Even though Lahore recorded better air quality in September and October this year than in the previous two years, pollution levels remain unhealthy. Punjab EPA and IQAir data show the average AQI was 143 in September and 163 in October 2024, compared with 89 and 182 respectively in 2025. This year, the average stood at 99 in September and around 109 in October so far. Experts attribute the improvement partly to favourable weather and government measures but warn that sustained progress depends on controlling emissions.
Despite the relatively better figures, pollution levels began rising again in the second half of October. According to hourly records available from the Punjab EPA, Lahore's AQI ranged between 229 and 290 from October 17 to 21, reaching 290 on October 21. Elevated pollution levels were also recorded at several monitoring stations on October 22, highlighting the risk of a renewed deterioration in air quality as the season progresses.
Muhammad Aleemul Hassan, director of the Pakistan Meteorological Department's Lahore office, said severe winter cold had shortened from around 75 to 50 days, while day and night temperatures had risen. The department's three-month forecast predicts near-normal rainfall and slightly above-average temperatures, factors that could affect pollution levels in the coming months.
Hassan noted that a relatively favourable western weather system was expected during the last days of October and the first week of November. The system could bring a drop in temperatures and help improve air quality, although the extent of any improvement would depend on the weather conditions and the movement of polluted air.
Founder of the Pakistan Air Quality Initiative Abid Omar said the Punjab government had initiated measures to tackle air pollution in the right direction but stressed that these efforts needed to continue. He said the government had undertaken various initiatives with 30 million US dollars in funding from the World Bank, although it would take time for their results to become apparent.
Omar added that much of the improvement in air quality last year had resulted from natural factors rather than government interventions alone. This, he said, underlined the importance of distinguishing between temporary improvements caused by weather and lasting reductions achieved through effective pollution-control policies.
The Punjab government has introduced measures to curb emissions, including zigzag technology in brick kilns, industrial inspections, vehicle emissions testing, and anti-smog guns. Experts say their effectiveness depends on consistent implementation and measurable reductions in pollution.
A study published in the Pakistan Journal of Science in June 2025 found that PM2.5 levels in Lahore typically remain high from October to February. Falling temperatures, low wind speeds and temperature inversions trap pollutants near the ground, while rainfall can temporarily improve air quality by removing particles from the atmosphere.
Punjab Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb warned that Lahore could again rank as the world's most polluted city, attributing the risk partly to polluted air from neighbouring countries. Experts, however, stress that local emissions from vehicles, industries, and brick kilns must also be addressed.
Despite this year's relative improvement, experts warn that PM2.5 levels remain hazardous. A lower AQI does not necessarily mean safe air, particularly for those exposed to pollution over prolonged periods.

title: ECP proposes rule amendments to curb AI misuse during polls
description: ECP proposes rule amendments to curb AI misuse during polls
content:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) proposed 12 amendments to the 2023 codes of conduct for political parties, media organisations and election observers to curb the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) during elections.
According to sources in the ECP, the draft amendments proposed five changes to the code of conduct for media organisations, five for political parties and candidates, and three for election observers.
The commission has sought public and stakeholder feedback on the proposed amendments by Nov 20, with the measures aimed at regulating AI-generated content, prohibiting deceptive deepfakes and ensuring transparency in election-related communication.
Under the proposed rules for media, outlets would be required to clearly disclose when content generated or modified through AI is broadcast, published or released.
The draft strictly prohibits the use of deepfake technology to create fabricated images, voices or statements of political party leaders, candidates, election officials, members of the judiciary, armed forces personnel and other state officials if the content is false, defamatory or intended to ridicule them.
Media organisations would be permitted to use AI tools for preparing, translating, presenting or analysing election-related content, provided they disclose such use to their audiences and remain responsible for the authenticity and accuracy of the material.
Pemra, the Social Media Protection and Regulatory Authority, and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency would monitor undisclosed or unlabeled AI-generated media content and report violations to the ECP, with appropriate action to be taken in cases of non-compliance.
The proposed amendments also require media houses to promptly remove misleading or undisclosed AI-generated content from their platforms, or correctly relabel it, when directed by a regulatory body or the ECP.

title: PM to visit Russia amid regional crisis
description: PM to visit Russia amid regional crisis
content:
Countries seek fresh momentum in relations
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is expected to undertake an official visit to Russia in the coming weeks for talks with President Vladimir Putin, as Islamabad and Moscow seek to inject fresh momentum into their relationship despite differences over Afghanistan and other regional issues.
Although the government has yet to formally announce the schedule, diplomatic sources indicated that preparations were under way for the prime minister's visit to Moscow.
The planned trip would effectively revive Shehbaz's visit to Russia that was postponed earlier this year because of an extraordinary deterioration in the regional security situation.
Shehbaz had been due to travel to Moscow in early March, with the Kremlin at the time confirming that preparations for his visit were under way. However, Islamabad postponed the trip on March 1, citing the prevailing "regional and internal situation", and said fresh dates would be worked out through mutual consultations.
The decision came as Pakistan was grappling with simultaneous crises on two fronts. Fighting between Pakistan and Afghanistan had sharply escalated, while the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran had triggered a wider regional crisis, forcing Islamabad to focus on the security implications as well as the evacuation of Pakistani nationals from Iran.
The prime minister subsequently chaired a high-level meeting to review the regional and internal security situation, including developments in Afghanistan, the Pakistan-Afghanistan border and Iran.
The revival of the visit is therefore significant. It suggests that both Islamabad and Moscow are keen to resume a high-level engagement that was interrupted by regional events rather than by any bilateral disagreement.
The trip is expected to focus on bilateral economic cooperation, particularly trade, investment and energy, while regional security and Afghanistan are also likely to figure prominently in talks between Shehbaz and Putin.
The proposed visit comes at a time when Pakistan and Russia have stepped up high-level contacts, reflecting a mutual desire to broaden a relationship that for decades remained constrained by Cold War alignments and competing regional priorities.
The latest push was evident earlier this month when Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev travelled to Islamabad and held meetings with Pakistan's civilian and military leadership.
During his meeting with Kolokoltsev, Shehbaz expressed satisfaction over the "positive momentum" in bilateral relations and called for greater cooperation in trade and investment, energy and economic development.
The two countries have in recent years explored cooperation in energy, connectivity, agriculture and trade. However, officials acknowledge that considerable potential remains untapped, with banking and payment mechanisms as well as connectivity among the practical challenges to expanding commercial ties.
