title: Mansoor backs Noor to reach top ten
description: Former World No11 says patience  fitness and experience key to squash star   s rise
content:
Former World No11 says patience, fitness and experience key to squash star’s rise
KARACHI: Pakistan’s former international squash player Mansoor Zaman has said that the rising star Noor Zaman has the talent to become one of the world’s leading players but must improve his patience, fitness and match management to fulfill his potential.
Speaking to The Express Tribune in an exclusive interview from Peshawar, Mansoor praised Noor’s technical ability and physical attributes but said his tendency to rush points and finish games too quickly often resulted in lapses of concentration and costly mistakes.
“Noor is doing well. He is very talented and has good quality, but he lacks patience. He is in a hurry and tries to end the game with speed,” Mansoor said.
“It is the wrong thing in him because, in this way, he loses his focus and concentration and then makes mistakes,” said Mansoor, a former World No11.
Mansoor said Noor had the potential to compete with the world’s best once he learned to control the pace of his game and maintain his composure under pressure.
“He has good quality, he has shots with him and his reach and run are superb, but he lacks a little bit in stamina,” he said.
“If he works on his fitness, then I think he will soon find a place in the top ten.”
Noor reached the quarter-finals of the Silicon Valley Open in Redwood City, California, before losing 3-1 to Egypt’s Mohamed ElShorbagy in the Professional Squash Association Gold tournament.
The Pakistani opened his campaign with a 3-1 victory over Malaysia’s Beng Hee Ming before producing an impressive performance against Egypt’s Karim Gawad, a former world number two, who was ranked world number four while entering into the tournament.
Noor won the opening two games against Gawad 11-9 and 11-7, lost the third 11-9, but recovered to take the fourth 11-6 and secure his place in the last eight.
His run ended against fifth seed ElShorbagy, who recovered after dropping the opening game to win 8-11, 12-10, 11-8, 11-8.
Mansoor described the victory over Gawad as an important milestone, saying it could help Noor improve his ranking and secure more favourable draws in future competitions.
“It was a big win in the US, as it will help improve his ranking and onwards he will get easy draws,” he said. “His second game in the US was against world number four and he upset Karim Gawad. It is a good sign for him,” Mansoor said.
Mansoor was one of the finest squash players of his era. He is also a two-time Asian champion.
Mansoor said experience remained a key difference between Noor and the established players at the top of the rankings, who had competed more frequently against elite opposition.
“He has the quality in his game like a world champion. He needs experience,” he said. “The top ten players are more experienced as they play more matches. Noor has just got the chance and now he plays with top ten players.”
He urged Noor to continue working on his fitness and consistency, adding that sustained effort could help the Pakistani establish himself among the sport’s leading players.
“He needs a little bit of hard work and there is nothing impossible. He can become the world’s top player,” Mansoor said.
Noor Zaman, who was also part of Pakistan's silver-medal winning team in Nagoya Asian Games, is currently World No 34.

Ethan Klein has issued his first public statement after his wife, Hila Klein, accused him of infidelity and announced their separation, asking for privacy as questions emerge over their relationship and shared businesses.
The YouTuber and H3 Podcast co-host addressed the controversy through Instagram Stories on October 23, hours after Hila made her allegations public.
“I know a lot of people are understandably looking for a comment from me, but I ask that you please respect my family’s privacy and do not contact them looking for me or asking for their comments,” Ethan wrote.
Ethan Klein provides an update pic.twitter.com/fcrFxdMcmb
He added that his family members were not involved in the situation and shared the public’s outrage and disappointment.
In a subsequent statement, Ethan said he was working with Hila to urgently remove his ownership and financial interests from their joint ventures, including the H3 Podcast, Teddy Fresh and Teddy Glow.
Hila made her allegations in an Instagram post on October 22.
Hila Klein accuses husband Ethan of having an affair for over 6 months amid details of reported separation
Ethan Klein’s past remarks about men who cheat on their wives resurface amid affair allegations
Ethan Klein’s net worth and $9 million mansion in focus amid wife Hila's affair allegations
Hila Klein’s cheating allegations put her 19-year relationship with Ethan Klein in focus
She claimed Ethan had initially dismissed her concerns before admitting to an affair that she alleged had lasted more than six months.
She also said she was uncertain whether she knew the full extent of the relationship.
Hila confirmed that she was navigating separation and co-parenting their three sons, adding that her immediate priority was caring for herself and her children.
The H3 Podcast crew also responded, stating that its members would no longer work with Ethan or profit from his involvement.
The team expressed support for Hila and described its reaction to the developments as shocked and heartbroken.
Ethan had announced an indefinite hiatus for the H3 Podcast shortly before the allegations became public.
The show's future remains uncertain amid the couple’s separation, the proposed business changes and the crew’s decision.

title: US Justice Dept demands California counties help identify suspected noncitizen voters
description: Warns election officials they could be targets of federal  scrutiny  if they refuse
content:
Warns election officials they could be targets of federal 'scrutiny' if they refuse
Less than two weeks before United States midterm elections, the US Justice Department has warned election officials across California they could be targets of federal "scrutiny" if they refuse to help identify suspected noncitizens on voter rolls and set aside their mail ballots pending citizenship checks.
According to letters dated Friday, local officials were given 48 hours to help determine the citizenship status of individuals on federal government lists. The Justice Department shared with Reuters texts of six of the letters on Saturday, which were signed by Bilal Essayli, first assistant US attorney for the Central District of California.
He warned counties that continuing to process ballots from individuals on the list without verifying citizenship status risked "significant federal scrutiny and legal exposure."
Read: From tech giants to anonymous nonprofits, the biggest donors in US midterms
On Saturday, California's attorney general accused the Justice Department of "politicising and weaponising the law" to attack President Donald Trump's perceived enemies.
Officials who knowingly counted ballots cast by individuals identified by federal agencies as noncitizens risked becoming "aiders and abettors to a federal crime," Essayli wrote.
Each letter includes local statistics drawn from a previously distributed list of 20,000 people who the Justice Department alleges are noncitizens registered to vote.
For those whose "citizenship status cannot be confirmed, we request that you immediately instruct the appropriate elections official to segregate — not cancel — those individuals' vote-by-mail ballots until their citizenship status can be determined," Essayli wrote.
The Justice Department said it identified 1,754 suspected noncitizens registered to vote in Orange County, 1,355 in Riverside County, 1,133 in San Bernardino County, 334 in Ventura County, 180 in Santa Barbara County and 63 in San Luis Obispo County.
Read More: Trump rallies Republicans for midterms
Another letter separately shared by Contra Costa County listed "407 likely aliens" registered.
"This letter came to us 11 days before Election Day with an unenforceable 48-hour deadline," said Dawn Kruger, a spokesperson for Contra Costa County’s Elections Department, adding: "Our office is conducting this election in accordance with federal and state laws and that is what we will continue to do."
Versions of the letters were sent to all 58 California counties, according to the New York Times .
In the run-up to the midterms, the Justice Department has ramped up prosecutions of people accused of illegally voting while not holding US citizenship. The White House has also pushed federal agencies to accelerate their review of at least 47 state voter rolls obtained by the Department of Homeland Security, according to an internal email seen by Reuters .
On October 16, the Justice Department warned Los Angeles County and California election officials they could be liable as abettors of a federal crime if they count mail ballots returned by more than 20,000 people the Trump administration says are probably noncitizens.
Also Read: Trump's approval falls to record low of 31% as midterms near, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
That warning came the day after the Trump administration filed a lawsuit asking a federal judge to block ‌the state from counting mail ballots from those 20,000 people. The Justice Department on Thursday asked the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals to intervene in the case.
On Saturday, California Attorney General Rob Bonta said the Justice Department acted at Trump's direction. "It is once again the United States Department of Justice politicising and weaponising the law to attack its enemies, and it is completely improper," he told MS Now .
California officials have rejected the Justice Department's demand to set aside those ballots, saying the federal government has not provided sufficient information about how it identified the alleged noncitizens.
California Secretary of State Shirley Weber has accused the administration of attempting to unlawfully access protected voter data and purge voter rolls, saying such efforts undermine confidence in elections.

Maaz Sadaqat joins squad as injury cover ahead of matches in Lahore
Pakistan have released left-arm wrist-spinner Sufyan Moqim from their squad, with the nature of the pitches in Lahore influencing the decision, and have added left-handed batsman Maaz Sadaqat as cover for players carrying minor niggles.
Moqim will return to domestic cricket following his release from the national squad, while Sadaqat has been brought in as a precautionary measure to provide additional batting cover.
“Left-arm wrist spinner Sufyan Moqim has been released from the Pakistan Men’s squad, keeping in view the nature of Lahore pitches,” the PCB said on Sunday.
“He will return to play domestic cricket. Left-handed batter Maaz Sadaqat has been added to the squad as cover for players carrying minor niggles,” the Board said.
Pakistan are due to face England today in their third show of the ODI tri-series where spinners don’t have much to offer due to nature of the pitches.
Pakistan have won both their previous matches and if they beat England today they will qualify for the final.
Maaz had a superb T20I series against Sri Lanka recently which hosts won 2-1 at the Pindi Cricket Stadium.

title: North Korea s Kim Jong Un returns from China after war memorial visit  state media says
description: Kim says during his tour that people would  forever remember the glorious years of fighting alongside Chinese people
content:
Kim says during his tour that people would "forever remember the glorious years of fighting alongside Chinese people
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un returned from a surprise one-day trip to the Chinese ‌border city of Dandong, where he visited a historic Korean War memorial, North Korean state media said on Sunday.
Kim visited the city on Saturday and returned by road, crossing a newly opened bridge that connects North Korea to its biggest international backer and trading ​partner. The quick trip symbolised a push by Beijing and Pyongyang to expand trade ties.
North Korean state ​media emphasised the historical weight of the visit, which came a day before the anniversary ⁠of China joining the Korean War on Pyongyang's side. The bilateral relationship is an "unbreakable" bond forged during the 1950-1953 ​conflict between North Korea and the US-backed South, state media said.
The two Koreas are technically still at war after ​the conflict ended in an armistice, rather than a peace treaty.
Kim said during his tour that the North Korean people would "forever remember the glorious years of fighting alongside the Chinese people" and pass down "generational gratitude to the Chinese people who helped our revolution with ​blood", state news agency KCNA reported.
Read: North Korea threatens South with 'most horrible' consequences, announces border countermeasures
Beijing and Pyongyang have been seeking to bolster their economic relationship ahead of a trip ​to the region by US President Donald Trump next month. It also highlights a delicate diplomatic balancing act by Pyongyang, which ‌has also ⁠been deepening military ties with Russia in the past two years.
Guided by Wang Huning, the fourth-highest-ranking official in the Chinese Communist Party, Kim visited Dandong's Memorial Hall of the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea, accompanied by a high-level North Korean delegation that included his sister, Kim Yo Jong, and Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui.
Touring the memorial, ​Kim viewed an archival photograph ​of his grandfather, North ⁠Korean founder Kim Il Sung, and Mao Zedong, founder of the modern Chinese state, footage from North Korea's state-run television KRT showed.
Kim presented a commemorative plaque featuring Kim Il ​Sung as a gift to the museum before holding a formal meeting with ​Wang and inspecting ⁠a bus factory in Dandong.
Kim last visited Beijing in September 2025 for a military parade, and Chinese President Xi Jinping visited North Korea in June.
"Enjoying a bird's-eye view at the middle point of the newly inaugurated bridge, Comrade Kim Jong ⁠Un expressed the ​expectation that the bridge would undoubtedly and correctly fulfill its historic mission ​of linking the two countries and firmly joining the minds of the peoples of the two countries," KCNA reported.

title: 11 shot near Florida A M university in Tallahassee
description: Local police confirm there are injuries from shooting  but have not determined how many
content:
Police count six adults, six juveniles among injured as initial findings show physical altercation preceded shooting
A shooting near a Florida university campus in Tallahassee on Saturday night left 11 people with gunshot wounds and another injured, authorities said.
The shooting took place near Florida Agricultural & Mechanical University's campus on Perry Street, the university said, while police counted six adults and six juveniles among the injured.
"At least three of the shooting victims have sustained serious injuries, while nine others are reported to be in stable condition," the Tallahassee police said in a statement .
Initial findings showed a "physical altercation" preceded the shooting, police said, without elaborating.
Read: Who is the ‘Black Widow’ at the centre of a Florida murder case?
"It is especially heartbreaking to know that children are among those injured," said police chief Lawrence Revell. The youngest of those shot was 11, the NY Post newspaper said, but police did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
An altercation at a homecoming party escalated into gunfire, and a fight between two or three individuals led to shots being fired just before 8pm, the paper added.
"The safety and security of our students, faculty, and staff remain our highest priority," Florida A&M said on X.
Our hearts are with the victims and everyone affected by tonight’s incident on Perry Street. Please avoid the area as Tallahassee police investigate. Read the University’s statement below and follow official University channels for updates. pic.twitter.com/n4yPinLPh9

title: Opposition leader says Netanyahu ‘no longer fit’ to lead Israel | The Express Tribune
description: Gadi Eisenkot criticises proposed use of cryptocurrencies to prepare for potential international banking sanctions
content:
Gadi Eisenkot criticises proposed use of cryptocurrencies to prepare for potential international banking sanctions
Just days before pivotal Israeli elections, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot said on Saturday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is “no longer fit” to lead the country, warning that his economic plan to counter potential international sanctions threatens national security.
On X, the Yashar party leader accused Netanyahu of turning his attention to “dismantling the Israeli economy for generations ahead” after “dismantling Israeli society and weakening the army.”
Eisenkot said Netanyahu’s recent remarks are “conclusive proof that he has lost touch with reality and moved into a world of delusions,” accusing him of proposing preparations to disconnect from the global financial system in response to Israel’s declining international standing.
“This is the madness of a man who is no longer fit to lead the country,” he said.
His comments came one day after Netanyahu said he had requested an economic plan involving alternative payment methods, including cryptocurrencies and blockchain technology, in preparation for possible international economic and banking sanctions.
Netanyahu expressed concern about potential sanctions, including restrictions on the Israeli banking system.
Read: Israel launches major West Bank operation after soldiers killed
Netanyahu did not say Israel would withdraw from the global economic system. The characterization of the proposal as economic isolation formed part of Eisenkot’s criticism.
Netanyahu also warned that US military aid would not last forever, urging Israel to prepare for its possible end and to strengthen military self-reliance.
Eisenkot mocked the proposal as “Bibicoin,” combining Netanyahu’s nickname, Bibi, with his proposed use of alternative payment methods and financial technologies.
He questioned how Israeli technology companies serving foreign clients would receive payments or attract overseas investment if they had to bypass international banking and rely on cryptocurrencies.
He also questioned how international acquisitions of Israeli companies could proceed if the economy moved toward isolation from the global financial system.
He warned that this course could prompt Israeli companies to relocate abroad, cause losses in savings and investments, and encourage citizens to leave the country.
Eisenkot said the consequences could include fewer jobs and reduced resources for healthcare and education, ultimately harming national security.
Read more: 'Apartheid automation': How Israel uses AI to monitor Palestinian land, movement and lives
“This is not an imagined nightmare scenario, but Netanyahu’s plan for Israel if he is reelected” on Tuesday, he said.
“This is a real warning. Israel will not withstand another four years like these.”
Netanyahu’s remarks also drew criticism in Israeli political and economic circles.
Israeli media cited an unnamed senior economic official who said that using cryptocurrencies and alternative financial technologies to circumvent banking sanctions would not achieve the intended goal. The official warned that merely proposing such an approach could damage the economy.
The debate comes amid mounting international pressure on Israel for its war on the Gaza, settlement expansion, and occupier attacks in the occupied West Bank.
The UK and other Western countries have taken measures against individuals and entities linked to Israeli settlements, while concerns have grown in Israel about broader economic and diplomatic pressure.
The exchanges also come ahead of Tuesday’s Knesset elections, in which Netanyahu and Eisenkot are competing to lead the next government.
Also read: Israel’s Katz vows to strike Beirut’s southern suburbs over any rocket or drone fire
In his post, Eisenkot urged Israelis to vote for “a better shared future.”
The former military chief is one of Netanyahu’s leading rivals, with the two sharply divided on security and economic policies, the country’s leadership, and its foreign relations.
Israeli politics also remains deeply divided on responsibility for the failures surrounding the October 2023 attack, the conduct of subsequent wars, military conscription, the economy, and relations with the US and other Western countries.

title: Lens fight back to beat Paris FC
description: Thauvin and Hazard score late goals to seal a 2 1 win
content:
Thauvin and Hazard score late goals to seal a 2-1 win
Paris FC missed the opportunity to go top of Ligue 1 as they went down 2-1 at Lens on Saturday in a matchday heavily impacted by the protests taking place across France.
Florian Thauvin and Thorgan Hazard scored in the final 30 minutes as last season's French Cup winners came from behind to beat Paris FC.
The result condemned PFC to remaining joint on 14 points with five other clubs at the top of the table.
Lens now sit just one point behind them in sixth place.
Luca Koleosho opened the scoring two minutes into first-half stoppage time at the end of a crisp counter-attack.
The 22-year-old picked the ball up on the left flank near the Paris FC area, before driving up the pitch and exchanging a one-two with Lassine Sinayoko and finishing crisply from the edge of the box.
PFC thought they had a numerical advantage to go with their one on the scoreboard early in the second half when Lens defender Jean-Clair Todibo was given his marching orders for a challenge on Ilan Kebbal.
But VAR intervened to find the PFC attacker was offside earlier in the action and Todibo returned to complete Lens' complement.
Thauvin, a 2018 World Cup winner with France, showed his pedigree just after the hour as he drove in on his left foot and fired home from 22 yards.
The 33-year-old combined with Hazard as the Belgian netted the winner for Lens with a left-footed strike inside the box on 83 minutes.
"This isn't anything new. In many matches this season, he's got us out of tricky situations, and again today, he did what only Florian Thauvin can do -- so that's great," Hazard said.
"He's a good leader, a good captain. He carries the team."
It was the sole Ligue 1 match of the day after champions Paris Saint-Germain had their home meeting with Lyon pushed back to Monday.
The postponement of the PSG game on Friday came after a decision was taken earlier in the week to postpone another French top-flight football game, in the south-western city of Toulouse between the home team and Troyes, from Saturday to Sunday.
Games in France's second-tier Ligue 2 have also been moved this weekend on the request of police.
Police deployed resources elsewhere as French authorities braced for another weekend of protests in the capital and across the country after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago.
The trouble broke out on the fringe of nationwide protests over the rising cost of living. Since then, authorities have ordered partial curfews in parts of Paris and other cities to prevent further violence.
Lille visit Monaco, Marseille host Le Havre and Rennes welcome Strasbourg, alongside three other fixtures, in a jam-packed Sunday.
Second-placed PSG then take on league leaders Lyon on Monday, with a winner likely to go outright top.

title: Beier sends Dortmund top of Bundesliga
description: Beier scores in the 80th minute to earn a 1 0 win over Frankfurt
content:
Beier scores in the 80th minute to earn a 1-0 win over Frankfurt
Maximilian Beier scored in the 80th minute to send Borussia Dortmund top of the Bundesliga after a hard-fought 1-0 home win over Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday.
In a game lacking clear chances, Jobe Bellingham came off the bench and had an instant impact, threading a clever pass for fellow substitute Beier to score.
The narrow victory was Dortmund's first in the league since mid-September and took Niko Kovac's side three points clear atop the table.
Bayern Munich can return to the top of the standings with a win at Freiburg on Sunday but will be without coach Vincent Kompany, who is being treated in hospital for a mystery virus after collapsing at training on Friday.
"We've got a great team. Those who aren't playing from the start, they're the finishers. They're the ones who close out the match, who decide things," Kovac said.
"Maxi struck that shot really well. I'm happy for the lad because he's had a tough time lately."
Dortmund had started the season with a run of six straight wins but came into Saturday's game in a mini slump, having won just one of their past four in all competitions.
The best opportunity of the first half fell to Serhou Guirassy with 15 minutes gone. The Guinean was one on one with Noah Atubolu but tried a soft chip, which the goalkeeper palmed away.
Just after the break, Guirassy headed a Joey Veerman corner against the bar.
Beier came on for the ineffective Fabio Silva with 22 minutes remaining. With 10 minutes left, he collected a Bellingham pass and curled in the winner from just inside the box.
Niclas Fuellkrug scored for the sixth straight Bundesliga match as his Werder Bremen side won 3-2 at Mainz.
Fuellkrug, who returned to Bremen on loan from English Championship side West Ham in the summer, converted two penalties inside the opening 25 minutes to notch up a second straight Bundesliga brace.
Ludovit Reis grabbed Bremen's other goal, while Anthony Caci and Lee Jae-sung scored for the hosts.
Fuellkrug now has eight goals this season, half of his total in his final campaign in Bremen in 2022/23, when he won the Bundesliga top-goalscorer award.
The Germany striker scored just three goals during an injury-hit 18-month spell at West Ham and just one in a six-month loan at AC Milan.
Bremen coach praised his in-form striker, telling reporters: "You can tell that he feels comfortable.
"He is our guiding star -- and he's shining brightly right now. He's carrying this team along with him."
RB Leipzig rebounded from their 4-1 thumping away at Real Madrid midweek with a comfortable 4-0 home win over promoted Elversberg.
Romulo scored a double while Tidiam Gomis, who scored Leipzig's only goal at the Bernabeu, and Christoph Baumgartner also got on the scoresheet as the Saxons climbed to fifth.
Without a point away from home, Leipzig have now won their four home games by a collective score of 18-0.
Paderborn's Rayan Philippe scored in the 88th minute against his parent club Hamburg to grab the promoted side a 1-0 victory in what was just their second win of the season.
Augsburg drew 1-1 with Union Berlin as both sides finished with 10 men.
Cologne and Schalke played out a scoreless draw in a match marred by an ugly clash of heads between visiting players Robin Gosens and Soufiane El-Faouzi, who both left the field.

title: Alvarez fires Atletico to win against Deportivo
description: Mikautadze fires Villarreal to a dramatic 2 1 win over Valencia
content:
Mikautadze fires Villarreal to a dramatic 2-1 win over Valencia
Julian Alvarez continued on his road to redemption by scoring the only goal as Atletico Madrid beat Deportivo La Coruna 1-0 on Saturday to close the gap on La Liga leaders Barcelona to two points.
Diego Simeone's side are second, with champions Barca hosting Real Madrid, third, in the Clasico at Camp Nou on Sunday.
Alvarez netted for the second consecutive game, having grabbed his first of the season in Atletico's 1-1 Champions League draw at Stuttgart in midweek.
Atletico supporters hounded Alvarez during his first appearances this season after he tried to force his way out of the club in the summer, but the tension has gradually cooled.
Home fans at the Metropolitano stadium directed a few whistles at the team in general after a slow start, with Deportivo having the best chance of the first half.
Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak saved well from Lorenzo Amatucci, while at the other end Diego Simeone's side lacked spark.
Early in the second half Alvarez found the breakthrough. Alejandro Grimaldo fired in a dangerous low pass towards the far post, where the Argentina international turned it over the line.
Alvarez came close to a second after a slick team move, with Alex Baena slipping him in, but Depor goalkeeper Leo Roman saved the striker's attempted lob with his face.
The former Manchester City striker looked much closer to his best form in this outing after struggling with some fitness problems earlier in the campaign.
Alexander Sorloth lashed narrowly over from a tight angle as Atletico sought to kill off the game, unsuccessfully.
Deportivo might have levelled in stoppage time with Kevin Sanchez volleying well wide from Adama Traore's cross when well placed to trouble Oblak.
The Galicians' best chance came with virtually the last kick of the game, with Oblak saving from Sanchez on his line, when the forward seemed destined to score.
Earlier, Georges Mikautadze snatched a late 2-1 win for Villarreal in a derby clash against Valencia, who had midfielder Harvey Elliott sent off as both sides finished with 10 men.
The Yellow Submarine came from behind to triumph, climbing into mid-table and leaving Javier Aguirre's Los Che 19th, in the relegation zone.
Pepelu sent Valencia ahead from the penalty spot in the first half before American defender Alex Freeman headed the visitors level at Mestalla stadium after 69 minutes.
Inigo Perez's Villarreal had Pape Gueye sent off when the Senegal international hit Jose Gaya in the face with his elbow.
However, English midfielder Elliott, on loan from Liverpool, was soon dismissed for two quick yellow cards for apparent dissent.
Villarreal striker Mikautadze broke through in stoppage time, racing through and finishing with aplomb to claim the three points.

title: Aston Villa end Manchester City   s perfect start
description: Arsenal beat Everton 2 0 to join Guardiola   s side on 21 points
content:
Arsenal beat Everton 2-0 to join Guardiola’s side on 21 points
Manchester City's flawless start to the Premier League season was ended in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa on Saturday that allowed Arsenal to join them at the top of the table with victory over Everton.
Tottenham won at Chelsea for just the second time in 42 visits to Stamford Bridge as Mike Penders's own goal and a Cole Palmer red card cost the Blues in a 2-0 defeat.
Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City's struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons.
Nicolas Jackson struck twice for Unai Emery's men to continue a fine run of form for a new-look Villa side.
Erling Haaland briefly levelled early in the second half, but Maresca was left to rue City not making more of their dominance for large spells of the game.
"We lost because we probably are not being clinical enough in their box," said Maresca.
The Villa side that won the Europa League last season was decimated by high-profile departures during the transfer window.
But Emery has quickly moulded his new squad into shape with Jackson proving his critics from a difficult spell at Chelsea wrong.
The Senegal international pounced on an error by Marc Guehi to fire Villa ahead after just six minutes.
Another of Villa's new signings Zion Suzuki then thwarted City with a string of stunning saves.
Haaland headed in his 13th goal in 10 games this season to equalise.
Villa, though, swiftly responded as Gianluigi Donnarumma failed to keep out Jackson's low shot on the hour mark.
"A fantastic day to share with our supporters in Villa Park," said Emery.
"We felt that this is our fortress and the energy the supporters gave us was really fantastic."
Arsenal took advantage to move alongside City on 21 points from eight games with a routine 2-0 win against Everton.
Shorn of the creative inspiration of Bukayo Saka, who is set for a lengthy spell on the sidelines with a thigh injury, Arsenal had to rely on their set-piece prowess to get the job done.
Ezri Konsa bundled in his first goal for the club after Everton failed to clear a corner to open the scoring on seven minutes.
Fellow centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes doubled the lead for Mikel Arteta's men midway through the second period.
"We had some problems to finish the actions but we scored from a set-piece," said Arteta. "That gave us the confidence and composure to go and dominate the game."
Tottenham climbed out of the bottom three as Chelsea self-imploded at the Bridge.
A game hampered by wild weather conditions exploded into action in the final 15 minutes when, on his first Premier League start, Penders, deputising for the injured Emi Martinez, miscued his attempted punch from a Spurs corner over his own line.
Moments later Palmer was dismissed for a second yellow card after catching former team-mate Conor Gallagher.
Spurs took full advantage as Mathys Tel's low strike also deceived Penders to win for only the second time at their London rivals since 1990.
Fulham also moved out of the relegation zone with a 1-0 win at Coventry thanks to Oscar Bobb's individual effort.
On Sunday the focus turns to Manchester United boss Michael Carrick when his side take on Bournemouth.
A seven-game winless streak has plunged Carrick's future into doubt just months after he was hired on a two-year deal after a successful interim spell in charge at the end of last season.

description:
Protests sweep
Italian cities
content:
Protests against war and rising living costs took place in major Italian cities on Saturday, with some incidents of violence, a week after unrest erupted across the country. Authorities deployed a heavy police presence and many shops closed as a precaution against possible damage. The demonstrations, which followed clashes last weekend in which protesters fought with police, looted shops and vandalised property, were violent in Turin, Rome and Bologna, with clashes between officers and demonstrators. They were largely peaceful in Milan. Reuters witnesses did not observe any shops being looted or property vandalised. After calls for further demonstrations circulated on social media this week, authorities made extensive security arrangements and deployed large numbers of police officers to prevent a repeat of last weekend’s violence. Earlier on Saturday, Italian police said they had detained a person allegedly linked to organising the “October 17 Movement” — last weekend’s protests — and had taken them to police headquarters in Milan for questioning.

title: Ukraine says Starlink back to normal | The Express Tribune
description:
Ukraine says Starlink
back to normal
content:
Ukraine said on Saturday the Starlink satellite system and its military version Starshield were now fully functional after over a week of restrictions that disrupted military operations and intensified tensions with the US. Hours later, Elon Musk, who owns the systems, accused the Ukrainian military of violating Starlink’s terms. “Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week”, he said on X. There were no immediate public comment from Ukrainian officials. Problems with the systems came after US President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel while pressing Kyiv to stop striking Russian oil refineries. Ukrainian officials said the restrictions, which capped operations at speeds of 160 kph (100 mph), hampered the military’s ability to intercept Russian attack drones and forced the cancellation of some operations. “The main thing for today is that Starlink and Starshield have resumed operations at their pre-restriction speeds. The speeds are now at the level we need,” President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on the Telegram app. According to Zelenskiy, the speeds started returning to normal overnight. Ukraine’s defence ministry said on Saturday the connection remained stable at over 400 kph. Ukraine does not rely on the systems for long-range drone operations on Russian territory, including attacks on refineries. But Starlink remains vital for frontline communications, and the deployment of Starshield-enabled medium-range attack drones has helped Ukraine gain the upper hand in several areas of the battlefield this year. The restrictions sparked outrage in Ukraine, particularly as they coincided with disruptions to allied warnings about incoming Russian missile attacks. Kyiv later said it continued to receive US intelligence. Neither Musk nor the US government has acknowledged responsibility for restricting Starlink or Starshield in Ukraine. Both have said publicly that any such decision could only have been taken by the other. Reuters has reported that the order to throttle Starshield came from inside the White House. Previously, US administrations had several times asked SpaceX to turn Starlink on or off in various countries, sources said.

title: NAB scrutinises PTI era uplift projects
description: NAB scrutinises PTI era uplift projects
content:
Former CM, ministers face asset probes as anti-graft body seeks records
The National Accountability Bureau (NAB) has launched a detailed probe into alleged irregularities in development projects, contract awards and the assets of former government officials during the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) administration in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.
According to NAB sources, the bureau has already sought the asset records of former chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur and former ministers Fazal Hakim and Dr Amjad. Parallel inquiries are under way into development schemes and contracts executed during the tenure of then-caretaker or inactive chief minister Sohail Afridi.
Officials said NAB has begun examining expenditure on various development projects, the process of awarding contracts and the quality and cost of construction works carried out under the previous provincial government. The Communication and Works (C&W) Department has been specifically asked to submit complete details of roads constructed during Sohail Afridi's period in office, lists of ongoing and completed schemes, the total number of contracts issued and the identities of the contractors who secured them.
Relevant departments have been directed to provide full documentation covering project approvals, contract allotments and execution of civil works so that any possible irregularities can be assessed. NAB sources confirmed that notices have also been issued to the Revenue Department, the registrar of Defence Housing Authority (DHA), the Peshawar Development Authority (PDA) and other concerned institutions demanding records of properties and assets held by former PTI office-holders.
Once these records are examined, the bureau may issue formal notices calling the relevant leaders for inquiry if warranted by the evidence. In a related track, NAB is reviewing the possibility of action against officers allegedly involved in illegal recruitments and corruption during the PTI government's tenure. Files pertaining to these matters are being collected and analysed.
A NAB spokesperson emphasised that any further steps will be decided strictly on the basis of the records under scrutiny and the strength of available evidence. "No final conclusion has yet been reached regarding the allegations against the leaders or officers concerned," the sources added.
The investigation marks a significant escalation of NAB's focus on Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's previous administration. By targeting both high-value development projects and the personal assets of senior political figures, the accountability body is signalling its intent to examine the full spectrum of governance decisions taken between 2018 and 2023. Provincial departments have been placed under pressure to produce documents promptly, raising expectations that the probe could expand if discrepancies emerge in the paperwork.
Observers note that such inquiries often take months to complete, given the volume of files involved and the need for cross-verification with multiple agencies. For now, NAB has confined itself to the collection and preliminary examination of records. The outcome will depend on whether the material yields concrete evidence of wrongdoing or remains within the realm of administrative review.
As the process continues, the former officials named in the asset requests and the contractors linked to the scrutinised projects remain under the cloud of investigation, pending the bureau's final assessment.

title: Three women shot dead over child custody dispute
description: Three women shot dead over child custody dispute
content:
Suspect allegedly opens fire at in-laws' home in Sheikhupura village
Three women were allegedly shot dead by a man at his in-laws' home in Thattha Ali village along the Sheikhupura-Sargodha Road following a dispute over the custody of his infant daughter, police said on Saturday.
The suspect, identified as Anser Abbas Bhatti, alias Antal Bhatti, allegedly opened fire at the house, killing his elderly mother-in-law, Najma Bibi, his sister-in-law Shamaila Bibi, wife of Subtain Bhatti and Nazia Bibi, wife of his other brother-in-law, Ali Hassan.
After the shooting, the suspect allegedly searched for his wife, Maria Bibi, both at the house and in several homes in the neighbourhood.
However, she escaped because she was away from the house when the incident occurred.
The suspect subsequently fled the village. According to the report, he also fired shots in the streets while escaping, triggering panic among residents.
Several villagers reportedly locked their homes amid fears of further violence.
Police from Sadar Farooqabad took the bodies into custody and shifted them to the District Headquarters Hospital for post-mortem examinations.
Sheikhupura District Police Officer (DPO) Bilal Zafar Sheikh said a team led by DSP Farooqabad Circle Tariq Kiyani had been formed to arrest the suspect.
Police were searching for him, he added.
According to the DPO, Anser Abbas belonged to Gujiana Nau village and married Maria, a resident of Thattha Ali, about two years ago.
The couple had a daughter, but frequent domestic disputes led Maria to leave her husband and move to her parents' home.
A custody case concerning the couple's infant daughter was subsequently filed in the family court and remained pending, the DPO said.
He said the suspect allegedly travelled from Gujiana Nau to his in-laws' home in Thattha Ali on Friday and demanded that the child be handed over to him.
An argument reportedly followed, during which he allegedly opened fire, killing the three women.
Police said efforts were under way to trace and arrest the suspect. The investigation is continuing.
Punjab Inspector General of Police Abdul Kareem has taken notice of the killing of three women in Farooqabad's Thattha Ali village, Sheikhupura, allegedly by a man over a domestic dispute, and sought a report from the regional police officer (RPO), Sheikhupura.
The IGP directed the Sheikhupura district police officer (DPO) to use all available resources to arrest the suspects and ensure they were brought to justice.
According to details, the suspect, identified as Antal Abbas, allegedly became enraged after his wife sought khula (judicial dissolution of marriage) and obtained the child through a court bailiff.

Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has declared frontline polio workers national heroes for their dedication and services.
In her message on World Polio Day, the chief minister reaffirmed her commitment to eradicating the disease from the province.

In an anti-polio campaign, more than 10 million children under the age of five had been administered polio drops in 13 high-risk districts, she said.
Regular anti-polio campaigns are being conducted in districts of Punjab.
Preparations have been completed for a Sub-National Polio Campaign scheduled from November 2 to 8 in selected districts of Punjab, alongside a nationwide campaign.
The chief minister said environmental samples were being continuously tested across the province to monitor and prevent the spread of the virus.
District Health Management Teams, representatives of the World Health Organisation (WHO) and UNICEF and the administration were monitoring the campaign, she added.

He urged the federal government to constitute a JIT under Section 3 of the Pakistan Commissions of Inquiry Act and appealed to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir to intervene in the matter.
He stressed the need to broaden the scope of the investigation to examine all relevant aspects of the incident and determine responsibility.
Meanwhile, parents of the affected children complained that they continued to face serious difficulties in securing medical treatment, financial assistance and justice.
According to the parents, four children from one family have been diagnosed with HIV, but only two are receiving financial assistance from the Auqaf Fund.
They said medical facilities had initially improved but subsequently deteriorated again. Despite the formation of several inquiry committees, the difficulties faced by affected families remained unresolved, while many were still awaiting financial assistance.
The parents complained that even after receiving financial assistance cheques, they were unable to obtain the funds on time.
They said they had repeatedly informed the authorities about their difficulties but were merely advised to remain patient.
"Our children are fighting this disease every day, while our families are struggling to meet medical and other expenses," the parents said.
They demanded uninterrupted, quality medical treatment for their children, transparent and timely disbursement of financial assistance and concrete measures to safeguard their future.
Advocate Tariq Mansoor further alleged that he had been subjected to pressure and received phone calls over his efforts to advocate for the rights of the affected children. However, he vowed to continue his struggle despite these pressures.
He said he had also written letters to the World Health Organization (WHO), UNICEF, the International Labour Organization (ILO) and European organisations, seeking their support for the affected families.
The lawyer appealed to the public to raise their voices for the children and launch a social media campaign under the slogan "Justice for Valika Hospital."
He emphasised that the affected children needed practical relief rather than mere announcements and repeated inquiry committees.
Such relief, he said, must include lifelong medical treatment, uninterrupted access to medicines, financial assistance and a transparent investigation to hold those responsible accountable.

title: Mpox virus claims life of one more child
description: Mpox virus claims life of one more child
content:
Authorities intensify surveillance as death toll rises to 12
One more child has died of mpox in Sindh, raising the province's death toll from the viral disease to 12 this year, as health authorities intensified surveillance, contact tracing and treatment measures following seven new cases reported over the past week.
The total number of confirmed mpox cases in Sindh has reached 98, prompting the provincial health department to direct public and private hospitals to strictly implement infection prevention and control protocols to contain the spread of the virus.
According to a spokesperson for the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital at NIPA, a child undergoing treatment for mpox died at the facility. The patient had been transferred from a private hospital a few days earlier and was receiving medical care. The spokesperson attributed the child's death to mpox.
Dermatologist and Additional Director of the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital, Regal, Dr Abdullah Yahya, said mpox was a contagious viral disease that could spread through close physical contact with an infected person, particularly through direct contact with skin rashes, blisters and lesions.
He explained that the virus could also spread through contaminated clothing, towels, bedding and other personal belongings used by infected individuals.
Early diagnosis, isolation of infected patients and strict adherence to medical guidelines were essential to preventing further transmission, he said.
Dr Yahya said, infants, individuals with weak immune systems and patients suffering from other serious medical conditions were particularly vulnerable to severe illness and complications.

title: Rainy weather drives streetside snack sales
description: Rainy weather drives streetside snack sales
content:
Demand for samosas, pakoras, hot soups and Kashmiri tea rises despite higher prices
The first heavy rainfall of the winter season brought a chill to the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad on Saturday, prompting a surge in demand for traditional winter delicacies, including samosas, pakoras, soups, yakhni and Kashmiri tea.
As temperatures dropped and cold winds swept through the cities, vendors set up stalls and pushcarts across neighbourhoods, commercial centres, wholesale markets, bus stands and the District Courts area. Meanwhile, stalls selling summer favourites such as sugarcane juice, lemonade and traditional lemon drinks have closed, with demand for these beverages declining.
Small and large markets have witnessed increased sales of freshly fried samosas and pakoras, while steaming cups of chicken corn soup, vegetable soup and yakhni have attracted customers seeking warmth during the chilly weather. Tea accompanied by crispy snacks has become a familiar sight, while pink Kashmiri tea garnished with almonds and pistachios has emerged as another popular winter treat.
Residents say enjoying pink tea topped with nuts during cold, rainy evenings has a distinctive appeal. The aroma of freshly fried snacks and hot beverages has filled markets, drawing customers to roadside stalls and pushcarts, which remain busy late into the night.
However, the rising cost of living has pushed prices of these seasonal favourites to record levels this year. In local markets, potato samosas are being sold for Rs60 each or Rs700 per dozen, while chicken samosas cost Rs70 each. Mixed pakoras are available at Rs600 per kilogram. A serving of plain chicken corn soup costs Rs150, rising to Rs200 with egg. Plain yakhni is priced at Rs100, while a serving with egg costs Rs150.
Unfried, ready-to-cook frozen snacks are also available for households. Plain potato samosas cost Rs1,060 per dozen, while chicken samosas are priced at Rs1,200 per dozen.
Iftikharuddin, Hassan Shah and Feroz Khan, who had visited the District Courts to attend hearings in their cases, said the cold, rainy weather had made tea with pakoras and samosas particularly enjoyable. They remarked that tea now felt incomplete without pakoras, particularly during the winter season.
The seasonal trade has also provided a welcome boost to small vendors and pushcart operators, whose businesses benefit from increased footfall as the weather turns colder.

title: Pindi thrift bazaars price out poor
description: Pindi thrift bazaars price out poor
content:
Costlier second-hand items at flea markets attract low, middle-income groups
Even before winter fully sets in, second-hand winter clothing, including shoes, coats and shawls begin flying off the stalls at Landa bazaars across the city.
The second-hand clothing items come cheaper than those available in the open market and also boast a variety of unique designs which are sourced from abroad and leftover export inventories. Clothes also come in from donations made to Western charities which are exported to Pakistan.
However, while prices of second-hand clothing used to be affordable for the poor who could not otherwise purchase warm clothes to protect themselves against the cold, in recent times, the increase in prices of items at Landa bazaars, now rebranded as thrift stores, have effectively iced them out.
With increase in clothing prices across the board, middle low-income families were already looking for cheaper clothing options. However, the social media influencer-powered recasting of second-hand clothes as sustainable and economical alternatives to mass-produced lower quality branded options has heightened demand among higher income groups. So much so that now, even women from affluent households are choosing to buy good-quality pieces from Landa bazaars, getting them dry-cleaned and flaunting them as high-quality or vintage pieces.
This year, prices of second-hand clothing in Landa bazaars has risen sharply once again. Children's sweaters are now priced at Rs500, while children's coats cost between Rs700 and Rs1,000. While a winter clothing set for a child could cost up to Rs5,000 in the regular market.
Women's coats are available for Rs1,000 to Rs2,000, while shoes cost Rs500 to Rs1,500. Men's coats are priced at Rs1,000 to Rs1,500, men's jackets at Rs1,500 to Rs2,500. Good-quality sweaters cost around Rs1,200 to Rs1,500.
Residents Amjad Ali and Faizan said people had to get through four months of winter and could not afford new sweaters from major brands costing Rs5,000 to Rs10,000, coats priced between Rs8,000 and Rs10,000 or even mufflers which cost around Rs1,000.
Stallholders Shakoor Khan and Azmatullah said they no longer received any free bales of clothing, and Landa bazaars had become a fully commercial business since the government imposed taxes of up to 200 per cent, in addition to customs duties and transportation costs from Karachi, which had made the goods more expensive. Nevertheless, the second-hand clothing still remains 40 to 60 per cent cheaper than clothes in the open market, providing some relief to low and middle-income families.
The history of Landa bazaars, the centres for used winter clothing and other goods in Pakistan, is linked to British colonial rule.
During British rule in the subcontinent, a British woman named Linda launched a campaign to help the poor. She collected old, used clothes and shoes from wealthy British households and distributed them among poor local people through a free stall at a designated location.
Over time, other people also began bringing their old clothes and the place gradually developed into a proper marketplace. It became known as the Linda Market after the British woman, and the name later evolved into Landa Bazaar through local pronunciation.
When British officers and their families returned from the subcontinent or discarded old belongings such as overcoats, hats, raincoats and winter suits, considering them useless, local contractors and shopkeepers began purchasing and selling these items at low prices.
Today, clothes donated to charitable organisations in Western countries, including Britain, the United States and Europe, reach Pakistan as part of a global second-hand trade worth billions of dollars.

content:

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un returned home Saturday after a day-long trip to the Chinese border city of Dandong, Beijing's state media reported, though the purpose of the unannounced visit was not immediately clear.

Neither North Korea nor China disclosed Kim's visit in advance. South Korean lawmaker Youn Kun-young said Kim was "understood" to have met Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Saturday.

Xinhua quoted Wang as saying the visit was significant for "consolidating public goodwill towards the friendship (and) deepening political mutual trust and jointly pursuing
greetings and best wishes" to the North Korean leader.
The trip fell near the date both countries use to mark the entry of Chinese troops into the Korean War. Kim attended a memorial ceremony to fallen soldiers and visited an automobile factory, Xinhua said.

Mines, minerals provincial subjects, says G-B CM
Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Advocate Amjad Hussain Azar has maintained that mines and minerals are a provincial subject and should not be treated as the exclusive domain of the federal government, calling for stronger enforcement and monitoring of the region's mineral resources.
He also backed the creation of new provinces wherever consensus exists, saying the Gilgit-Baltistan Assembly had already passed a resolution demanding provincial status for the region.
Speaking to the media in Karachi on Saturday, Azar said his government had completed its first 100 days and begun implementing the Pakistan Peoples Party's (PPP) manifesto.
He highlighted efforts to ensure transparent recruitment and promote livestock, commerce, tourism and border trade, while disclosing that a public-private partnership unit had been established in Gilgit-Baltistan and that the United States had shown interest in investing in the region's energy sector.
On the question of provincial autonomy, Azar argued that the federal government could not handle every matter itself and that provinces should be allowed to discharge their respective responsibilities.
He said the mining and minerals sector particularly required effective enforcement and monitoring.
The chief minister said the Gilgit-Baltistan Assembly had passed a resolution seeking provincial status for the region and that the PPP supported this demand.
He maintained that new provinces should be created wherever there was consensus, while the issue should not be pursued in areas where agreement had yet to emerge.
Azar said his government had started fulfilling its promises and assuming the responsibilities of a democratic political administration. He added that work was underway to improve higher education, healthcare and education in Gilgit-Baltistan.
Commenting on the country's economic difficulties, Azar said industrial activity had stalled and that industries could not operate sustainably on the basis of expensive thermal electricity.
Hydropower, he said, was the cheapest source of electricity and offered considerable potential to support industrial growth.
He said a public-private partnership unit had been established in Gilgit-Baltistan and disclosed that the United States had shown interest in investing in the region's energy sector.
The chief minister also highlighted Gilgit-Baltistan's vast tourism potential, saying the region's economic opportunities should be developed so its people did not remain poor. He stressed the need to harness local resources to improve livelihoods and create better economic prospects.
Azar also pledged to work towards ending load-shedding in Gilgit-Baltistan, asking residents to allow the government some time to address the problem.
He said his government remained in contact with Gilgit-Baltistan residents living in Karachi and was attentive to their concerns.
Taking aim at the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) performance in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), Azar urged people to assess the province's 13 years under PTI-led governments by examining conditions across its different regions.
He alleged that the party had failed to focus on governance and instead remained engaged in confrontations with political parties and state institutions.
He said such an approach was bound to produce adverse consequences, arguing that the PTI had relied on popular slogans and political disputes rather than effective governance.

"We were having negotiations, the cowards (Americans) messed everything up...I still think we should go and conclude it," Pezeshkian said.
Meanwhile, Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis said they launched attacks on Saudi oil facilities and airports on Saturday, and the Saudi-led coalition fighting the group said it downed two missiles, as clashes between the two sides intensified.
On another front of an escalating conflict reignited by the Iran war, Yemen's Saudi-backed government said the Houthis also fired three ballistic missiles at coast guard sites in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden.
Saudi authorities did not comment directly on the Houthi statements, though they reported missile debris falling near the site of one of the purported oil targets. It was not immediately clear if any of the reported attacks had hit their targets in the kingdom or had been intercepted.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, an Aramco facility in Yanbu, the Rabigh oil refinery, crude oil pumping stations and the East-West Pipeline.
He also said the group targeted King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, an airport in Najran and an airbase in Khamis Mushait.
The Saudi-led coalition earlier said it destroyed two ballistic missiles fired by Houthis towards Yanbu and Taif.
Saudi Civil Defense said debris from intercepted missiles had fallen in the Makkah and Medina regions.
It said parts of the intercepted missiles fell in Wadi al-Mughammas in Mecca, while debris also fell in areas in Jeddah, Taif and Rabigh. It was not clear if that was linked to the Houthis' reported targeting of the Rabigh oil refinery.
Shortly after that, Houthis denied that they attacked Mecca and Medina, saying that their operations "target Saudi oil facilities and military bases."
The renewed fighting has shattered a 2022 UN-brokered truce that largely halted cross-border attacks between the Saudi-led coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, and the Houthis, who control the capital Sanaa.
The escalation has opened another front in the US-Israeli war on Iran.
In Yemen, the Interior Ministry of the internationally recognised government said two of the Houthis' missiles had struck a coast guard headquarters, while a third hit a coast guard building in the Tawahi district.
Houthi spokesman Saree said the group's forces had targeted Saudi-backed military gatherings at what he called Al-Nasr camp and a naval base in Aden, saying Saudi officers were overseeing the mobilisation there.
There was no immediate comment from the Saudi-led coalition on that assertion.
Earlier on Saturday, Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense briefly issued alerts warning residents of potential danger in Taif and Yanbu, as well as in the holy city of Mecca and the kingdom's second-largest city, Jeddah.
About 10 minutes later, the agency said the threat had passed.

title: Ex US envoy s vitriol draws bitter rebuke
description: Ex US envoy s vitriol draws bitter rebuke
content:
Govt snubs claims of arming Afghans against Taliban
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on Saturday rejected former US envoy Zalmay Khalilzad's allegations that Pakistan was arming Afghans to fight the Taliban, describing them as baseless and misleading while reiterating its concerns over terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory.
The ministry's response came a day after Khalilzad, who served as the US special representative for Afghanistan during the first Trump administration, claimed on X that there were "many reports" of Pakistan arming Afghans to fight the Taliban in Afghanistan.
He also alleged that Islamabad was recruiting Afghans to fight anti-Pakistan insurgents and predicted that relations between the two countries would deteriorate further.
In a post on X, the ministry's fact-check account said Khalilzad's sweeping assertions recycled speculative narratives and reflected what it described as a personal agenda to support the Afghan Taliban regime. It said his unsubstantiated allegations exposed his "skewed agenda-based views".
The ministry said it was misleading to conflate Pakistan's counterterrorism operations against organisations operating from areas controlled by the Afghan Taliban with allegations that Islamabad was recruiting Afghan nationals or sponsoring armed groups inside Afghanistan.
It maintained that Pakistan's operations were aimed at terrorist organisations threatening its citizens and stressed that the country had made enormous sacrifices in the fight against terrorism and for regional peace and security.
In a separate statement issued on Saturday, the ministry said the Afghan Taliban regime had resorted to diversionary allegations instead of addressing Pakistan's longstanding security concerns.
It said blaming Pakistani security institutions did not absolve Kabul of its responsibility to prevent Afghan territory from being used for attacks against Pakistan.
Citing international assessments, the ministry referred to the United Nations Security Council's Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team's 16th report, S/2025/796, which examined the presence and activities of terrorist groups in Afghanistan.
It also cited the US Lead Inspector General's Operation Enduring Sentinel report to Congress for January-March 2026, which stated that the Afghan Taliban continued to allow the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) to operate from Afghan territory.
According to it, the report linked Taliban support and greater freedom of operation for the group to an increase in attacks against Pakistan and estimated the TTP's strength at 4,000 to 6,000 fighters.
The ministry said repeated attempts by armed terrorists to cross the Pakistan-Afghanistan border, casualties among Afghan nationals and members of terrorist groups during Pakistani counterterrorism operations, and the recovery of foreign-origin weapons from militants warranted serious scrutiny.
It also referred to Pakistani concerns over the alleged facilitation of terrorist groups by Afghan Taliban officials, including in Kandahar, saying such concerns required credible explanations and verifiable action rather than blanket denials.
The statement urged the Afghan Taliban regime to end any tolerance, facilitation or support for terrorist organisations, including the TTP, the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and their affiliates, and ensure that Afghan territory was not used to plan or launch attacks against Pakistan.
It added that Pakistan's security measures were directed against terrorist threats, not the Afghan people, and that peace and stability in the two neighbouring countries were closely linked.
Islamabad, it said, remained open to engagement based on mutual respect, verifiable commitments and concrete action against terrorist sanctuaries, support networks and cross-border infiltration.
Khalilzad, who negotiated the US agreement with the Taliban that paved the way for the withdrawal of NATO forces from Afghanistan, has repeatedly called for Islamabad and Kabul to reach a negotiated settlement, including in January this year.
The former envoy has previously drawn criticism from Pakistan. In November last year, the ministry accused him of creating a false impression about the presence of the Islamic State-Khorasan (IS-K) group in Punjab after he claimed an IS-K commander had been killed in Akhtarabad.
The ministry said the man had died in a robbery-related incident, not a counterterrorism operation, and that there was no evidence linking him to IS-K.

title: Hit Pakistani song  Majboor  gets global audience
description: Hit Pakistani song  Majboor  gets global audience
content:
Belgian DJ 'Lost Frequencies' remixes it for international listeners
A Pakistani pop song that has attracted more than 250 million streams is getting a new international audience through a remix by Belgian DJ and producer Lost Frequencies.
The electronic music artist has officially remixed Majboor, performed by Sheheryar Rehan and Zoha Waseem, bringing his dance music sound to a track that gained popularity across South Asia and beyond.
Released in 2025, Majboor has featured on Spotify, YouTube and Apple Music charts. It also entered Spotify's Global Viral Top 50, attracting listeners in Pakistan, India, Bangladesh and the United Arab Emirates. The collaboration began taking shape when Lost Frequencies started playing his version of the song during live performances. He later shared a clip of one such performance on Instagram, paving the way for an official release.
"There's something timeless about Majboor," Lost Frequencies said. "I loved blending those beautiful melodies with my own sound and bringing it to the dance floor."
Sheheryar, who wrote and composed the original track, said the song's international journey had been difficult to predict.
He said the remix offered a fresh musical perspective while retaining the emotion of the original, adding that it was exciting to see the song reach new audiences around the world.
The original combines Sheheryar's songwriting with Zoha's ghazal-influenced vocals, creating a contemporary Pakistani pop sound. Xulfi, co-founder and chief operating officer of Giraffe Music, which is associated with the project, said music could take stories to places artists might never have imagined.
He pointed to Lost Frequencies performing Majboor in India as an example of how musical collaborations could help Pakistani music reach international audiences.
Lost Frequencies, whose real name is Félix De Laet, became internationally known with Are You With Me, which topped charts in 18 countries and made him the first Belgian artist to reach number one in the UK.
In 2014, Lost Frequencies made a remix of country artist Easton Corbin's "Are You with Me". The song had originally appeared in Corbin's second studio album, All Over the Road, but had not been released as a single. Lost Frequencies remixed the song and uploaded it to SoundCloud. Armada Music A&R, and founder of The Bearded Man label, Marwen Tlili discovered the record and subsequently signed it. The official release was on 27 October 2014. The track topped Belgium's Ultratop chart on 15 November 2014, reaching number two in the Walloon chart as well.
The remix highlights how streaming platforms and live performances can help songs cross geographical and musical boundaries, allowing artists from different markets to connect with new listeners.

title: New film highlights Pakistani women s stellar anti polio role
description: New film highlights Pakistani women s stellar anti polio role
content:
Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy's 'Across Every Doorway' focuses on challenges faced by vaccination workers
A new documentary by Oscar-winning filmmaker Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy will focus on four women working to eradicate polio in Pakistan, highlighting the challenges faced by vaccination workers and scientists protecting children from the disease.
Titled Across Every Doorway, the film was announced by SOC Films on October 24 to mark World Polio Day. It follows women working in Karachi, Rawalpindi, Peshawar and Islamabad, documenting their roles in vaccination campaigns, community outreach and laboratory testing.
The documentary explores how health workers deal with vaccine refusals, misinformation and public mistrust, while trying to ensure that every child receives polio drops.
"Behind every door is a family, a conversation, and a child whose future deserves to be protected," Obaid-Chinoy said, adding that the film aimed to bring attention to the women whose work often goes unseen.
In Karachi, Fouzia Ahmed, an area supervisor with the World Health Organisation's Polio Programme, works with vaccination teams and visits households reluctant to vaccinate their children. The documentary shows how she manages resistance while supporting colleagues who sometimes face verbal abuse and safety concerns.
In Rawalpindi, area coordinator Dr Shumaila Akbar monitors vaccination campaigns and checks whether teams are following required standards. Her work also involves travelling and managing responsibilities in the face of social expectations surrounding women's roles.
The film follows community health worker Laiba Ijaz in Peshawar as she tries to reach children who might otherwise be missed, including newborns and families who have recently moved into the area. Her personal journey, shaped by financial difficulties after her father fell ill, forms another part of the story.
In Islamabad, virology and immunology laboratory scientist Dr Riqba Akhtar tests environmental and human samples for traces of poliovirus. Her work helps authorities monitor the virus and inform responses on the ground.
The documentary also examines how conversations with doctors, religious leaders and local officials can help address concerns about vaccination.
Known for her work in films that highlight the inequality with women, as of 2019, Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy's accolades include two Academy Awards, seven Emmy Awards and a Knight International Journalism Award. In 2012, the Government of Pakistan honoured her with the Hilal-i-Imtiaz, the second-highest civilian honour of the country. She features in listings of the world's most popular personalities and Time named her one of the 100 most influential people in the world in 2012.
She received her bachelor's degree in economics and government from the Smith College and two master's degrees from Stanford University. While at Stanford, she made two award-winning films, and upon returning to Pakistan, she launched her career as a filmmaker with her first film Terror's Children (2002) for The New York Times. She went on to win the Emmy Award for Best Documentary for the war-on-terror Pakistan's Taliban Generation (2009). She gained wider recognition for the documentaries Saving Face (2012) and the biographical A Girl in the River: The Price of Forgiveness (2016). For her work in both of these, she won the Academy Award for Best Short Subject Documentary and five Emmy Awards in different categories. She gained wider recognition for making the musical journey Song of Lahore (2015), and the animated 3 Bahadur film series (20152018). The latter is the country's first-ever computer-animated feature length film.
Her Academy Award win for Saving Face made her the first Pakistani to win an Academy Award, is one of only eleven female directors who have ever won an Oscar for a non-fiction film and is the first female film director to have won two Academy Awards by the age of 37. She is the first non-American to win the Livingston Award for Young Journalists for Reinventing the Taliban (2003). In 2017, Obaid-Chinoy became the first artist to co-chair the World Economic Forum.
Across Every Doorway is scheduled for release in November 2026.
