title: Clayface  leads box office as  You Can See Everything  grows in second weekend
description: Clayface  leads weekend box office with projected  24m opening as  You Can See Everything  expands
content:
'Clayface' leads weekend box office with projected $24m opening as 'You Can See Everything' expands
DC Studios’ Clayface is leading the US box office with a projected $24 million opening weekend, while A24’s You Can See Everything continues to grow following its nationwide expansion.
The body horror film earned $10.4 million on its opening day across 3,458 locations. With a reported production budget of $40 million, its projected domestic debut offers a promising start for Warner Bros. and DC Studios.
The film has received a 76% critics’ score and 93% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes, alongside an A- CinemaScore rating.
The reception could help Clayface maintain its box office performance through Halloween and beyond. Its results also offer potential relief for Warner Bros. following disappointing performances from releases including Digger, Supergirl and Practical Magic 2.
Meanwhile, You Can See Everything , a documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, has expanded from 855 to 2,655 locations in its second weekend. The film is estimated to have grossed $20 million, bringing its domestic total to $45 million.
According to the report, it has become the highest-grossing documentary of the past decade, with further growth expected.
In third place, Fathom and Laika’s animated film Wildwood earned $4.3 million on its opening day from 2,752 locations. It is projected to finish the weekend with between $11 million and $12 million.
However, its reported production budget of more than $100 million makes profitability difficult. The film has a 100% critics’ score and 98% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes, as well as an A CinemaScore.
Paramount and Legendary’s Street Fighter ranks fourth, with an estimated $8.4 million in its second weekend, a 73% decline from its $31 million debut. Its domestic total has reached $46.7 million against an $82 million production budget.
Rounding out the top five is Wicker , a fantasy romantic comedy starring Olivia Colman and Alexander Skarsgård. The film is projected to open with $6 million from 1,471 locations, supported by Rotten Tomatoes scores of 94% from critics and 95% from audiences.

title: Pakistan rejects Afghan Taliban    diversionary allegations  demands action against TTP and BLA
description: Says    blanket denials    fail to address concerns after Mujahid accuses Pakistan of shifting blame for security failures
content:
Says ‘blanket denials’ fail to address concerns after Mujahid accuses Pakistan of shifting blame for security failures
Pakistan on Saturday accused the Afghan Taliban regime of resorting to “diversionary allegations” instead of addressing its “legitimate and longstanding security concerns”, urging Kabul to take verifiable action against terrorist groups, including the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA), operating from Afghan soil.
The statement came a day after Afghan Taliban regime spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid accused Pakistan’s security agencies of blaming Afghanistan for their failure to maintain security at home, allegedly to mislead the public.
Responding to this in a statement posted on X, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting said the Afghan Taliban regime had resorted to “diversionary allegations” instead of addressing Pakistan’s “legitimate and longstanding security concerns”.
Ministry of Information and Broadcasting Islamabad, 24 October 2026 Taking note of the recent statements of the Afghan Taliban Regime where they have once again resorted to diversionary allegations instead of addressing Pakistan’s legitimate and longstanding security concerns.…
“Blaming Pakistan’s security institutions does not absolve the Regime of its responsibility to prevent Afghan territory from being used for terrorism against Pakistan,” the ministry said.
It called on the Afghan Taliban regime to end any tolerance, facilitation or support for terrorist organisations, including the TTP, BLA and their affiliates, and ensure that Afghan territory was not used to plan, prepare or launch attacks against Pakistan.
The ministry said Pakistan’s concerns were not based on conjecture, citing the United Nations Security Council’s Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team’s 16th report and the US Lead Inspector General’s Operation Enduring Sentinel report to Congress for January-March 2026.
According to the ministry, the US report stated that the Afghan Taliban continued to allow the TTP to operate from Afghan territory, with Taliban support and greater freedom for the group contributing to an increase in attacks against Pakistan. It estimated the TTP’s strength at 4,000 to 6,000 fighters.
Read : Pakistan refutes former US envoy's 'unsubstantiated' allegations of arming Afghans to fight Taliban
The ministry said these assessments underscored the seriousness of Pakistan’s concerns about terrorist sanctuaries and support networks operating from Afghan soil.
It also rejected the assertion that Afghanistan lacked either the capacity or the interest to destabilise Pakistan, saying the claim did not address the documented concerns.
Repeated attempts by armed terrorists to infiltrate across the Pakistan-Afghanistan border, the killing of Afghan nationals and members of terrorist groups during Pakistan’s counterterrorism operations, and the recovery of foreign-origin weapons from terrorist elements warranted serious scrutiny, the statement said.
Pakistan had also raised concerns over the alleged facilitation of terrorist groups by Afghan Taliban officials, including officials in Kandahar, it added.
“Such concerns cannot be dismissed through blanket denials; they require credible explanations and verifiable action,” the ministry said.
The statement stressed that Pakistan’s security measures were directed against terrorist threats, not the Afghan people, adding that peace and stability in the two countries were closely linked.
It said the Afghan people stood to gain as much as their Pakistani neighbours from a region free of terrorism.
The ministry said attempts to portray Pakistan’s security concerns and defensive measures as hostility towards Afghanistan would neither deflect attention from the issue nor resolve it.
Pakistan would continue to take all necessary measures to protect its citizens, sovereignty and territorial integrity, it said, adding that Islamabad remained open to responsible engagement based on mutual respect, verifiable commitments and concrete action against terrorist sanctuaries, support networks and cross-border infiltration.
Also Read : Pakistan hits Afghan terror hideouts; 22 killed
“Peace can only prevail in the region if Pakistan’s core concern of terrorism originating from Afghanistan is verifiably addressed by the Afghan Taliban,” the statement said.
On Friday, the Afghan Taliban spokesperson rejected Pakistan’s claims that Afghanistan was allowing its territory to be used for terrorist activities against Pakistan, accusing Pakistani officials of shifting blame for their own security failures onto Kabul.
In a statement posted on X, Afghan Taliban regime spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid said Pakistani military circles and other security agencies blamed Afghanistan when they failed to establish security in their own country, in an attempt to mislead the public.
“We once again strongly reject the repeated accusations directed by Pakistani officials at Afghanistan regarding the destabilisation of security in their country,” he said.
We once again firmly reject the repeated allegations by Pakistani officials accusing Afghanistan of being responsible for insecurity in Pakistan. Unfortunately, whenever Pakistan’s military establishment and other security agencies fail to maintain security within their... 1/5
Mujahid said it was not in Afghanistan’s interest to create insecurity in Pakistan or support acts of instability there. He also claimed that Afghanistan lacked the capabilities and resources to foment or finance insecurity in other countries.
“Insecurity in a neighbouring country directly harms both the region and Afghanistan,” he said, adding that instability in Pakistan was detrimental to Afghanistan in economic, social and humanitarian terms.
The spokesperson accused Pakistani officials of blaming Afghanistan instead of focusing on their own security responsibilities. He also alleged that Pakistan was spending resources on efforts to destabilise Afghanistan.
“This amounts to evading their primary and fundamental responsibilities, undermining regional stability, and wasting economic resources on futile endeavours,” he said.
Mujahid further claimed that the approach had distracted Pakistan’s security forces from their own duties and diverted their attention from the responsibilities they were supposed to fulfil.
Pakistan has repeatedly accused terrorist groups based in Afghanistan of carrying out attacks inside the country and demanded that Kabul take action against them. The Afghan Taliban government has rejected accusations that it allows its territory to be used for attacks against Pakistan.
Islamabad maintains that the terrorist nexus extended beyond the movement of terrorists across the border to their training, arming and operational support.
In 2026 alone, terrorism emanating from Afghan soil claimed the lives of 1,327 Pakistanis and injured another 2,484, according to figures cited by Pakistani authorities.
Officials said that whenever Pakistani forces targeted terrorist hideouts, the Taliban regime instead moved to defend the militants and their sanctuaries rather than dismantling the infrastructure. The issue, Pakistan has argued, was not confined to TTP.
UN assessments have continued to document the presence of several other militant organisations in Afghanistan, including al Qaeda, the East Turkestan Islamic Movement (ETIM) and Islamic State-Khorasan, reinforcing concerns about the broader militant ecosystem operating from Afghan territory.
Pakistani officials say the continued presence of these groups, combined with training facilities, cross-border infiltration and access to sophisticated weapons, demonstrates that Afghanistan remains an important base for terrorist activity affecting Pakistan.
Pakistan's position, according to officials, remains that Kabul must take concrete steps to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries, eliminate training infrastructure, prevent cross-border infiltration and ensure that Afghan territory is not used for attacks against Pakistan.
The government has maintained that the issue was fundamentally one of Pakistan's national security and that continued attacks from Afghan soil cannot be addressed through denials alone.
Pakistan says it expected the Taliban regime to fulfil its commitments by taking verifiable action against terrorist groups operating from its territory rather than defending or denying their presence.

title: Nishat Group and LUXEED sign strategic MoU to bring premium new energy vehicles to Pakistan
description: The collaboration will strengthen Pakistan   s new energy ecosystem through innovative mobility solutions
content:
The collaboration will strengthen Pakistan’s new energy ecosystem through innovative mobility solutions.
Nishat Group , one of Pakistan’s largest and most established business groups, and premium new energy mobility brand LUXEED have signed a strategic cooperation agreement in Wuhu.
Under the agreement, the two sides will combine their strengths and resources to introduce the LUXEED brand in Pakistan, advancing the country’s new energy mobility ecosystem through technology integration and local synergy. Senior representatives of both companies attended the signing ceremony.
Nishat Group is one of the pillars of Pakistan’s private sector, with deep roots in textiles, cement, banking, insurance, power and agriculture.
Over decades, it has built a reputation for refined operations, long-term investment and the ability to move decisively when the market changes. Its portfolio spans the full chain of manufacturing, finance and energy, giving it the resource integration capability and market reach that few groups in the country can match.
That strength is already visible in the automotive sector. Through NexGen Auto, Nishat Group brought OMODA & JAECOO to Pakistan in August 2025, backed by a USD 100 million investment and local assembly in Faisalabad.
The brand recently crossed 15,000 customer deliveries in its first year, supported by Nishat Group’s market strength, focus on customer service, and growing dealership network. NexGen Auto also recently introduced iCAUR to Pakistan, together with Chery Group, as unveiled at PAPS 2026.
The cooperation with LUXEED International marks the next step: a strategic expansion into the premium new energy segment. By bringing advanced technology to Pakistan, Nishat Group aims to support the green transformation of the country’s automotive industry and raise the competitiveness of the local market.
As ideas of luxury evolve around the world, a new generation of pioneering consumers is moving away from symbolic labels and looking instead for genuine driving experiences and intelligent technology.
Based on in-depth research into global user needs, LUXEED has built its brand on three pillars: Intelligence, Luxury and Driving Pleasure, expressed in the proposition “I DRIVE, YOU ENJOY.”
LUXEED is a premium electric vehicle brand created through a partnership between Chery and Huawei. Operating under Huawei’s Harmony Intelligent Mobility Alliance (HIMA), Chery handles vehicle manufacturing and engineering, while Huawei supplies its HarmonyOS smart cockpit, Qiankun ADS driver assistance, and digital drive technology.
On 21st October, LUXEED held its global brand launch event in Wuhu. The event turned it into tangible experiences: driving pleasure from the freedom of driving unleashed, luxury through perceptible safety and comfort, and intelligence that puts people first by letting technology adapt to the user.
LUXEED is supported by Chery Group, which has ranked first in China’s brand passenger-vehicle exports for 23 consecutive years and has cumulative global sales of more than 20 million units.
Its mature manufacturing system, global R&D network and overseas operating experience give the brand a solid base for expansion in major markets around the world. Pakistani customers already know that strength through the OMODA & JAECOO and iCAUR brands that the Nishat Group has introduced over the past 12 months.
Pakistan’s new energy market is growing every month, but customers who want a premium, technology-led alternative have had limited choice.
This Nishat Group and LUXEED partnership aims to change that by building a complete system of products, services and an ecosystem, so that buyers can count on the same standard of availability, after-sales support and trust that they expect from a Nishat Group business.
With technology innovation as its engine and customer needs as its foundation, the partnership opens a new chapter of intelligent and eco-friendly premium mobility for Pakistani consumers and adds momentum to the country’s economic and environmental progress.
Details of LUXEED models, specifications, pricing and the timeline for Pakistan will be announced by Nishat Group at a later stage.

title: Kristen Bell   s daughter takes    sneaky photos    of Dax Shepard raiding cereal cupboard while mum is away
description: Here   s what he didn   t consider  I have a mole on the ground  obviously   she joked of her daughter s secret updates
content:
'Here’s what he didn’t consider: I have a mole on the ground, obviously,' she joked of her daughter's secret updates
Kristen Bell has revealed that her eldest daughter, Lincoln, secretly takes photos of her father, Dax Shepard, when the actress is away for work, giving her a glimpse into the family’s activities at home.
The Nobody Wants This star shared the story during an appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon on Thursday, October 22, explaining that she had been travelling in and out of town for around six weeks while promoting her work.
“As a mom, you get nervous to leave town, but then you realise they’re fine,” Bell told host Jimmy Fallon. She added that she had not received any calls from school about her children being absent and that nobody had returned home needing stitches.
However, Bell revealed that she had a way of finding out what happened while she was away. “Here’s what he didn’t consider: I have a mole on the ground, obviously,” she joked, referring to her eldest daughter’s secret updates.
Bell explained that Lincoln, 13, had been sending her what she called “in-house paparazzi photos” of Shepard. One picture showed the actor and podcast host raiding the cereal cupboard at around 10 p.m., despite the children supposedly being in bed.
“It is 10 p.m., we’re supposed to be in bed, but Dad is in the cereal cupboard, and he’s just like going hog wild,” Bell recalled of the message accompanying the photograph.
Fallon showed the audience one of the pictures, prompting Bell to affectionately praise her daughter. “That’s my girl right there!” she said.
The late-night cereal raid was not the only evidence Bell received about what happened at home during her absences. The actress said she regularly received phone notifications informing her that McDonald’s or Taco Bell had been delivered.
“I usually receive, almost immediately, notifications on my phone,” she explained. “Your McDonald’s has been delivered. Your Taco Bell has been delivered.” She joked that Shepard and their daughters seemed to rely on fast food whenever she was away.
Bell and Shepard married in 2013 and share two daughters, Lincoln, 13, and Delta, 11. The couple have occasionally discussed their parenting experiences publicly, with Shepard previously describing fatherhood as the most transformative experience of his life.
“Nothing compares to being a dad. It is the greatest thing that has ever happened to me,” Shepard said during a panel at South by Southwest in March 2023.
Bell has also recently spoken candidly about the challenges of balancing marriage and parenting. In an interview with Bustle , she pushed back against the idea that her celebrity status makes family life easier.
“It’s hard,” she said. “Do not think because I am on your television that it is easy for me. It’s brutal. I cry weekly.”

title: Jenna Ortega says Disney channel media training made it difficult to set boundaries with fans
description: Ortega was told that whenever someone met her  it was probably the only time they would ever interact with her
content:
Ortega was told that whenever someone met her, it was probably the only time they would ever interact with her
Jenna Ortega has revealed that media training she received as a child star on Disney Channel continues to affect how she approaches interactions with fans, explaining that she is learning to establish healthier boundaries as an adult.
The Wednesday actress, 24, discussed the lasting impact of the training during an appearance on the Happy Sad Confused podcast with host Josh Horowitz. Ortega recalled being taught that every encounter with a fan could be a particularly meaningful moment for that person, leaving her feeling pressure to make herself available.
“When I was young, and I was on Disney Channel, they took us to, like, media training,” Ortega said. She explained that she was told that whenever someone met her, it was probably the only time they would ever interact with her, making the encounter special in their lives.
“No pressure,” she joked, reflecting on the advice.
Ortega said the message had stayed with her over the years and influenced how she responded to people approaching her in public. Although she understands that fans may be excited to meet her, she is trying to give herself more freedom to decide when she feels comfortable interacting with strangers.
“That has never left me,” she said. “And sometimes I try to give myself grace, and I’m trying to have better boundaries.”
The actress explained that she does not always feel safe stopping for photographs, particularly when approached by adult strangers. She acknowledged that she is more comfortable with certain interactions, including those involving children, but said it can be difficult to determine how much access to give people.
Ortega also pointed out that not every encounter is positive. While some fans are kind and considerate, others can be aggressive, unkind or make interactions uncomfortable.
“It is a lot, though,” she said. “And again, it’s sweet. Like, some of the interactions are so sweet, and some of them are a little bit more embarrassing, or aggressive, or mean. And it’s hard to know what the balance is. But I do what I can.”
Ortega began acting professionally at the age of nine and rose to prominence playing Harley Diaz in the Disney Channel sitcom Stuck in the Middle , which ran from 2016 to 2018. She also voiced Princess Isabel in the animated series Elena of Avalor .
Since leaving Disney Channel, Ortega has established herself as a leading figure in horror and thriller projects. Her credits include the Scream franchise, Ti West’s X and Netflix’s Wednesday , in which she plays Wednesday Addams. She also portrayed Astrid Deetz in Beetlejuice Beetlejuice .
The actress has previously spoken about the pressures of growing up in the entertainment industry, including the expectations placed on young performers to maintain a public image and engage with audiences online. In an earlier interview, she described the demands of social media training and the pressure to build a following while promoting Disney projects.
Ortega’s latest comments highlight another aspect of growing up in the public eye: learning to separate the expectations attached to celebrity from her own comfort and personal safety. While she appreciates the support she receives, she is increasingly recognising that she cannot accommodate every request from fans.

title: Police confirm letter about Meghan Markle   s father was not shared with other law enforcement agencies
description: A spokesperson said it was decided to share the letter to the office of Duke and Duchess of Sussex for their awareness
content:
A spokesperson said it was decided to share the letter to the office of Duke and Duchess of Sussex for their awareness
The Metropolitan Police has confirmed that it received a letter containing allegations against Meghan Markle’s estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr, in January 2019, but did not share the details with other law enforcement agencies.
In a statement issued on Saturday, October 24, the London police force said the letter contained claims of alleged offending outside the United Kingdom. It was referred to the force’s Protection Command because of concerns relating to the security of the Duchess of Sussex.
“The letter was reviewed and a decision was made that it should be passed to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex for their awareness,” a Metropolitan Police spokesperson said. “The details of the allegations in the letter were not shared with other law enforcement agencies.”
The force added that it was reviewing how the matter had been handled and considering whether to refer itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC), the police watchdog.
The confirmation comes after Meghan said she had been made aware of troubling allegations concerning her father in 2018, following her wedding to Prince Harry. In a statement to PEOPLE on October 23, the Duchess said a letter had been sent to the Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection, and that she had been assured the allegations were being investigated.
However, the police force’s records place its receipt of the letter in January 2019, several months after the date Meghan recalled.
A representative for Meghan addressed the discrepancy on October 24, saying that, without a diary entry or a contemporaneous record, it was understandable that she might have misremembered the timing by a few months. The representative added that if the police held a time-stamped record confirming the letter was reviewed in 2019, that should be treated as the accurate reference point.
The developments follow reports that Thomas Markle Sr, 82, was facing allegations concerning the possession of child sexual abuse material. His son, Thomas Markle Jr., reportedly alerted authorities after allegedly discovering images among belongings at his father’s former home in Cebu, the Philippines.
Thomas Sr has denied the allegations, describing them as lies. The claims have not been established as fact, and the Metropolitan Police clarified that it is not investigating him.
Meghan said she was deeply distressed by the reports and expressed concern for any children who may have been harmed. She also explained that her decision to keep her children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, away from their grandfather was made to protect them.
“I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them,” she said.
The Duchess has been estranged from her father since the period surrounding her 2018 wedding to Prince Harry. Thomas Sr did not attend the ceremony and has never met Archie or Lilibet.
The Metropolitan Police’s review will examine how the letter was handled in 2019 and whether further scrutiny by the IOPC is necessary. The force has not announced a final decision on whether to refer the matter to the watchdog.

title: Punjab bans permanent police escorts for ministers  MPAs among others
description: Principal Secretary to the Chief Minister Sajid Zafar Dall issued a notification conveying the decision
content:
Principal Secretary to the Chief Minister Sajid Zafar Dall issues notification conveying the decision
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Saturday directed that no permanent police squad be deployed with provincial ministers, members of the provincial assembly and other individuals.
Principal Secretary to the Chief Minister Sajid Zafar Dall issued a notification conveying the decision.
According to the notification, provincial ministers, advisers, special assistants, parliamentary secretaries, chairpersons of standing committees and members of the Punjab Assembly will not be allowed to retain permanent police escorts.
The restriction also applies to government officials and private individuals.
Read: PA seeks answers over CM's aircraft use for private visit
The notification further prohibits the installation of flagstaffs or the display of official flags on government vehicles without prior permission.
The chief minister has made it clear that unauthorised police escorts will not be tolerated under any circumstances.
Earlier in March, the provincial government had also introduced austerity measures amid rising fuel costs, including suspending government-provided fuel for provincial ministers, cutting fuel allowances for government officers’ vehicles by 50% and restricting protocol convoys accompanying ministers and senior officials to one vehicle for essential security purposes.
The use of police personnel for VIP protocol has long drawn ire in Punjab over the diversion of public resources from routine policing. In November 2025, The Express Tribune reported a rise in armed private escorts, commonly known as “dala culture”, amid concerns about weak regulation, unauthorised armed patrols and the use of security as a display of power. Punjab had issued more than 200 new private security company licences in recent years, while taking enforcement action against firms for violations.
Prior to that, authorities had also announced a crackdown on private security firms using police-like uniforms and vehicles after armed guards escorting foreign visitors were involved in a violent road dispute in Lahore.

title: Jordan king orders  iron fist  response to deadly church attack
description: Authorities searched for gunmen who opened fire and killed nine people during a church funeral service
content:
Authorities searched for gunmen who opened fire and killed nine people during a church funeral service
Jordan's King Abdullah ordered security forces on ‌Saturday to respond with an "iron fist" as authorities searched for gunmen who opened fire and killed nine people during a church funeral service.
The assailants fired for several minutes in broad daylight at the church in Karak governorate on Friday, ​and also wounded 40 people in the rare attack on Jordan's Christian minority.
Security ​was stepped up at malls, foreign embassies and other locations across the country, ⁠the US embassy in Amman said.
A priest described how ​he and others ordered people to get to the ground at Saint George's Greek Orthodox church, ​about 120 kilometres southwest of the capital, Amman.
Read More: Pakistan condemns 'heinous terrorist attack' on church in Jordan
"A sense of panic took hold among those present," Theodoros Soueiss told Reuters . "The gunfire was indiscriminate, and you never knew where a bullet might land."
King Abdullah condemned the "despicable terrorist ​act" as he chaired a National Security Council meeting and said there was no room for leniency when ​it comes to the lives of Jordanians, the royal court said.
Such attacks are highly unusual in Jordan, a relatively stable state in the Middle East, though ‌authorities there say they ⁠have foiled several plots in recent years.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack in the kingdom, a major partner with the US in the fight against militant groups.
Officials have said it is too early to determine whether the attackers had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan.
"A massacre, a massacre in every ​sense of the word," ​said Tarek Ammarin ⁠at a hospital where the wounded were being treated. A relative of Ammarin's was injured in the attack.
Christians make up a minority of Jordan's ​population. The country is home to several biblical sites that attract Christian ​pilgrims from ⁠around the world.
Jordan has been among the US allies in the Middle East to be hit by Iranian attacks this year after the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February.
Bahjat al-Rushda, mayor ⁠of ​Shihan village in Karak, joined a long list of officials ​condemning what they called an attack by extremist terrorists.

content:
'I think, for me it’s just the way she just would treat us [on tour and set] with so much care and love,' Dameski said
Lady Gaga’s longtime collaborator Michael Dameski believes the pop superstar will be a wonderful mother, praising the singer for the kindness and care she showed her dancers while working together on her Mayhem Ball world tour.
Dameski, 30, shared his thoughts on Gaga’s new chapter as a parent during an exclusive interview with PEOPLE at the 2026 Industry Dance Awards in Los Angeles on Wednesday, October 21. The Australian dancer performed alongside Gaga on her tour and appeared in the music video for her hit song Abracadabra .
“I think, for me, it’s just the way she just would treat us [on tour and set] with so much care and love,” Dameski said. “I really see [motherhood] for her and I’m really excited for her.”
The dancer also described Gaga as one of the hardest-working people he has ever encountered, explaining that witnessing her dedication to her craft had been an inspiring experience.
“She’s the hardest worker I think I’ve ever encountered in my life,” he said. “I’m so grateful for having that experience because I just don’t think I’ve ever met someone who works as hard.”
Gaga, 40, reportedly welcomed her first child, a daughter, with her fiancé, entrepreneur Michael Polansky, in June. According to documents obtained by PEOPLE, the baby was born on June 9. The couple have not publicly confirmed their daughter’s name or sex.
Sources previously told PEOPLE that becoming a mother had long been important to Gaga and that she was enjoying time away from the public eye with her baby. Polansky has also reportedly been actively involved in caring for their child as the couple adjust to parenthood.
The singer and Polansky became engaged in 2024 after going public with their relationship in 2020. Their partnership also extends to their professional lives, with Polansky collaborating with Gaga on her 2025 album Mayhem and co-producing her subsequent tour.
Gaga has previously spoken about her hopes of becoming a mother. In a 2025 interview with ELLE , she discussed wanting her future children to develop their own identities rather than feel defined by her fame or artistic career.
“I would never actually want to shape it or tell them how to think about me,” she said of how her children might view her artistry. She added that she and Polansky had discussed the importance of allowing their children to become their own people.
Gaga released Mayhem in March 2025 before launching the Mayhem Ball world tour that July. The tour concluded at New York City’s Madison Square Garden in April 2026, shortly before the reported arrival of her daughter.
Dameski’s comments offer a glimpse into the personal qualities that have made an impression on Gaga’s collaborators, as the singer embraces a new chapter away from the demands of touring and public appearances.

title: Saudi missile plant expansion may produce more powerful missiles  study says
description: Experts say the makeup of Saudi Arabia s missile force suggests that the complex relies on Chinese technology
content:
Experts say the makeup of Saudi Arabia's missile force suggests that the complex relies on Chinese technology
Saudi Arabia appears to be expanding its ballistic missile factory to build larger solid-fuel missiles that could fly farther or carry heavier payloads, according to two US researchers who analyzed ​more than a year of commercial satellite images.
More capable missiles could help Saudi Arabia to deter attacks by Iran and make its military more self-reliant, while possibly strengthening its position in a deadly ‌conflict with Yemen's Tehran-backed Houthi fighters.
But they risk fueling a regional missile race and could deepen opposition in the US Congress to a US-Saudi civilian nuclear agreement that has already raised concerns about proliferation.
Satellite company Planet Labs, based in the US, took images of the al-Duwadimi complex about 125 miles (200 km) west of Riyadh between April 2025 and September 2026.
Read: Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed Houthi ballistic missiles fired towards Yanbu, Taif
The two researchers, Sam Lair and Michael Duitsman of the Foreign Policy Research Institute, assessed that those images show a new building that houses casting pits — wells in which a mixture of fuel ingredients is ​poured into missile motor casings and allowed to harden.
The Saudi embassy and Information Ministry did not respond to requests for comment.
The building, flanked by what appear to be walls to protect nearby structures from accidental explosions, is ​at least twice as large as the one believed to house the plant’s existing casting pits, Lair and Duitsman said in their assessment.
The Foreign Policy Research Institute (FPRI) is ⁠a non-partisan research organization in Philadelphia.
A second new building could be used to store fuel ingredients or finished missile components, they said.
The imagery "suggests that Saudi Arabia is expanding the infrastructure at the missile production complex, likely to produce larger missiles ​which could deliver larger payloads or reach longer ranges," they wrote.
Militaries favour solid-fuel missiles because they can be stored for long periods and launched more quickly than liquid-fuel systems.
Lair and Duitsman and experts from the London-based International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) ​and the CNA research and analysis organisation told Reuters that the makeup of Saudi Arabia's missile force suggests that the al-Duwadimi complex relies on Chinese technology .
Lair and Duitsman said that its characteristics are also similar to Chinese missile plants.
Also Read: Makkah pact ratification completed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia: FO
Saudi Arabia secretly acquired about 40 liquid-fuel DF-3 ballistic missiles from China in 1987, according to a 1991 declassified CIA estimate. It displayed two of them for the first time in an April 2014 military parade, according to a YouTube video and photographs of the event.
The FPRI team also recently identified from social media ​videos and photos what they assessed was the wreckage in Yemen of a Saudi-fired Chinese-designed DF-15 missile.
Lair said the kingdom may now be producing the solid-fuel DF-15, and that the expansion of a1-Dumadimi is likely for the production of the ​longer-range DF-21 or a similar missile.
Riyadh is believed to have turned to Beijing because Washington has long restricted exports of longer-range missile systems.
The Chinese embassy and defence ministry did not respond to requests for comment. The CIA declined to comment. The White House did ‌not respond to ⁠a request for comment.
A satellite image shows the solid propellant motor plant in Al Duwadimi, Saudi Arabia, September 18, 2026. Photo: REUTERS
Missiles would alter the balance of power
Sascha Bruchmann, a research fellow at IISS, said longer-range missiles would allow Saudi Arabia to strike Iran without risking its US-supplied F-15 jet fighters against Iranian air defenses.
“You’d want a system to threaten whatever is holy to Tehran ... if you don’t have the political will to send an F-15 with JDAMs over Tehran,” said Bruchmann, referring to US-made satellite-guided bombs. “Iran has a lead because its missiles and drones can strike Saudi wherever it wants. The Saudis could close that capability gap a bit.”
Bruchmann, who reviewed the FPRI analysis at Reuters request, concurred that the expansion of al-Duwadimi could be for producing more powerful solid-fuel missiles.
Janes, the defense intelligence company, also reviewed it and said the ​buildings “may suggest an effort to expand production capability or support ​the development of longer-range missiles.”
Saudi Arabia's apparent pursuit of ⁠more powerful missiles comes as other Gulf powers are also seeking to expand their offensive and defensive arsenals, said Decker Eveleth, a CNA analyst who has been tracking the al-Duwadimi construction with commercial satellite imagery and concurred with the FPRI assessment.
“This is being replicated across the Middle East,” he said. “You see exactly the same thing happening in the UAE. You see ​the exact same thing happening in Turkey. Everybody is doing this now.”
The expansion of al-Duwadimi could have political consequences in the US by stiffening bipartisan congressional opposition to ​a US-Saudi agreement under which the ⁠US would help Riyadh establish uranium enrichment for power generation.
Opponents say that the deal lacks sufficient safeguards to prevent Riyadh from secretly building a nuclear weapon. The kingdom has denied any such plan.
The FPRI assessment said the Planet Labs imagery showed that the expansion at al-Duwadimi began in April 2025 with ground-clearing and digging for the suspected storage building. Work on the suspected casting-pit building began later that month or in early May, it said.
A December 12, 2025, photo showed what researchers assessed were ⁠two deep pits ​inside the building that had no roof yet.

A September 18, 2026, photo shows the roof still partly missing and "heavy-duty blast-diverting walls" on ​either side to prevent accidental explosions from damaging adjacent structures.

title: Unregistered shelter homes leave children beyond effective oversight
description: More than 50 private shelter homes in Punjab remain unregistered
content:
More than 50 private shelter homes in Punjab remain unregistered
For hundreds of orphaned, abandoned and vulnerable children in Punjab, a shelter home is meant to be a place of safety. Yet many of the private institutions housing these children remain outside the government’s full oversight, leaving authorities without a clear and up-to-date picture of how many children are living there, under what conditions, and whether they are safe.
According to the Child Protection and Welfare Bureau (CPWB), only 14 shelter homes have been licensed, while more than 50 remain unregistered. A 2021-22 CPWB mapping study, conducted with UNICEF Pakistan, identified 105 residential care institutions in Punjab—41 government-run and 64 private—with 5,762 children. Four years later, however, the government still lacks updated data on these institutions and the children living in them.
The CPWB said applications from another four to five facilities were under review. Before licensing, officials inspect buildings, staff, facilities and child-care arrangements, followed by periodic inspections.
Private shelter homes provide accommodation, food, education and other basic facilities to children at a time when capacity in government institutions remains limited. However, the lack of effective oversight of unregistered facilities has raised concerns about child protection. In the past, several incidents have also raised questions about the living conditions and treatment of children in unregistered institutions.
The recent killing of 15-year-old orphan Waseem Abbas in Multan has renewed concerns about the protection of children living in institutional care. Waseem, who had been living at an NGO-run orphanage, was allegedly chased and run over by a contractor after being sent to work with him to learn electrical work. Police registered a murder case, while the CPWB rejected the orphanage’s registration application on October 20, citing concerns about arrangements for the protection and supervision of children. The case has raised questions about how children are supervised and safeguarded after leaving the institutions responsible for their care.
In April 2024, 32 children were recovered from an unregistered orphanage in Gajjumata, Lahore. According to the CPWB, the children were living in two small rooms. A case was registered against the head of the institution under the Punjab Destitute and Neglected Children Act, although medical examinations did not confirm sexual abuse.
In September 2025, 18 children were taken into protective custody after a video showing children being subjected to violence at an unregistered institution in Chichawatni surfaced on social media. Police said the children had been physically abused. One caretaker was arrested, while cases were also registered against the institution's administrators.
Child protection experts say the existing system for registering and regularly monitoring private shelter homes needs to be strengthened. Iftikhar Mubarak, head of Search for Justice, said registration with the CPWB could improve the quality of services provided to children as well as the monitoring system.
He suggested that shelter homes should also be required to produce a CPWB registration certificate when registering with the Punjab Charity Commission or renewing their registration annually.
Child rights activist Rashida Qureshi said it was alarming that some institutions did not even have clear legal authority to keep children in their custody. She called for the registration and regular inspection of all shelter homes, along with uniform standards for children's accommodation, food, education and healthcare.
Sahil Legal Aid Coordinator Imtiaz Soomro, advocate, said effective monitoring was necessary to ensure the safety of children in shelter homes, religious seminaries and boarding schools. However, he said it remained unclear which institution was responsible for monitoring these facilities under the existing system.
He called for the CPWB and other child rights institutions to establish an effective and regular monitoring mechanism to prevent the exploitation of children.
According to Soomro, incidents of sexual and physical abuse and other forms of exploitation in shelter homes, seminaries and boarding schools often go unreported. He further added that media access to some of these institutions was also limited, making it difficult for incidents involving children to come to light.
The CPWB said 11 Child Protection Institutes were currently operational in Punjab, while 25 Child Protection Units had been established across the province, of which only six were functional.
With more private than government institutions providing residential care to vulnerable children, the lack of an updated government record raises a fundamental question: if authorities do not know the current number of private shelter homes or the children living in them, how can the safety, rights and welfare of those children be effectively monitored?

title: 2 suspects arrested for robbing former PM Raja Pervaiz Ashraf   s Jhelum residence
description: Two domestic staffers held after goods worth millions go missing despite police deployment
content:
Goods worth millions go missing despite police deployment
Household items worth millions of rupees were allegedly stolen from the residence of former prime minister and Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) MNA Raja Pervaiz Ashraf despite the deployment of police personnel for security, it emerged on Saturday.
Police said two domestic employees were taken into custody in connection with the incident.
The theft was reported at the ex-premier’s residence in Punjab’s Dhok Amb village, in the jurisdiction of Jatli Police Station located in Jhelum district.
Read: Raja Pervez Ashraf says he has lived a 'spotless life' after drug queenpin Pinky allegedly names him
According to the first information report (FIR), the former PM’s personal assistant arrived at the residence and found a domestic staff member absent. Police personnel deployed there informed him that the employee had been missing since the previous night.
A subsequent inspection of the rooms and other parts of the residence revealed that three air conditioners, two doors, three windows, a grass-cutting machine, carpets, three fans, decorative items, crockery and other valuable household belongings were missing.
The ex-PM’s personal assistant lodged a complaint with Jatli police, naming the domestic servant and requesting that another domestic employee also be questioned in connection with the incident.
A Rawalpindi police spokesperson said preliminary investigations had indicated the alleged involvement of both employees in the thefts, after which the two domestic workers were taken into custody. An investigation is being conducted under the supervision of Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Gujar Khan.

title: Quentin Tarantino surprises with 17 minutes of Brad Pitt   s    The Further Mis Adventures of Cliff Booth
description: Director David Fincher  who was also in attendance  helmed the new film from a screenplay written by Tarantino
content:
Director David Fincher, who was also in attendance, helmed the new film from a screenplay written by Tarantino
Quentin Tarantino surprised audiences at AFI Fest by screening the first 17 minutes of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , the upcoming Netflix film starring Brad Pitt as the stuntman introduced in Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood .
The filmmaker made the surprise announcement on Friday, October 23, following a screening of his 2019 film at the TCL Chinese Theatre in Hollywood. During a question-and-answer session moderated by Rotten Tomatoes’ Jacqueline Coley, Tarantino offered the audience a choice between discussing the sequel and watching its opening footage.
“Well, I could talk a little bit about ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,’ or I could show you the first 17 minutes,” Tarantino told the audience.
Director David Fincher, who was also in attendance, helmed the new film from a screenplay written by Tarantino. The project continues the story of Cliff Booth, played by Pitt, eight years after the events of Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood .
The sequel moves the action from 1969 to 1977 Los Angeles, where Cliff has moved beyond his work as a stuntman and become a Hollywood fixer. He takes on difficult situations for people in the entertainment industry, using his unconventional skills to deal with problems that others cannot easily resolve.
The film’s cast also includes Elizabeth Debicki as talent agent Karen Crosby, Scott Caan as television star Charlie Peters, Carla Gugino as Charlie’s wife Toni, and Yahya Abdul-Mateen II as former professional football player turned actor Roderick “Hot Rod” Harrison. Peter Weller also appears in the film.
Tarantino explained that his affection for Cliff was a major reason he wanted to revisit the character. Reflecting on the original film, he recalled a review describing it as the first fictional world he had created that he would want to live in.
“I loved the Cliff Booth character,” Tarantino said. “I loved the way that Brad played him, and there was this aspect of him as sort of like a paperback hero.”
He added that he could imagine Cliff appearing in a series of paperback adventures, with the character becoming involved in different situations and escapades. The new film expands on that idea by placing Cliff in a different era of Hollywood, with a fresh set of characters and criminal entanglements.
Tarantino has handed directing duties to Fincher, who previously worked with Pitt on films including Se7en , Fight Club and The Curious Case of Benjamin Button . Pitt reportedly helped bring Fincher on board for the project.
The screening comes as Tarantino prepares for another major project outside film. During the same appearance, he discussed The Popinjay Cavalier , his upcoming stage play starring Sacha Baron Cohen, which is scheduled to premiere in London's West End next year. Tarantino said rehearsals would begin in November, with previews planned for February.
The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth will receive an IMAX theatrical release on November 25 before arriving on Netflix on December 23. The film marks a continuation of Tarantino’s Hollywood story, with Fincher bringing his own directing approach to the screenplay and Pitt returning to one of his most celebrated recent roles.

title: Pakistan fall after bright start
description: Shaheens surrender two goal lead in historic FIFA Under 15 WC and Festival debut
content:
Shaheens surrender two-goal lead in historic FIFA Under-15 WC and Festival debut
Pakistan suffered a 4-2 defeat against Gambia in their opening match of the FIFA Under-15 World Cup and Festival 2026 in Baku, surrendering an early two-goal advantage after a dramatic second-half comeback by their opponents.
Shaheens made an impressive start, scoring the tournament's opening two goals to put Gambia under pressure.
Ameer Hamza opened the scoring in the fifth minute, collecting the ball on the right near halfway before driving towards the Gambian defence and unleashing a powerful strike past the goalkeeper.
Hamza then helped create Pakistan's second goal, winning a tackle that sent the ball towards Baxi Hamal Khan. Advancing from the left, Baxi produced a superb finish into the top corner to double Pakistan's lead.
Gambia responded before half-time, reducing the deficit and shifting the momentum ahead of the interval.
The African side carried that momentum into the second half, equalising early after the ball slipped past Pakistan goalkeeper Shayan. Gambia continued to press, forcing Pakistan to defend deep as they sought to regain control of the contest.
Pakistan gradually settled and began creating opportunities of their own. Kaleemullah tested the Gambian goalkeeper repeatedly, forcing several saves as the Shaheens attempted to restore their advantage.
However, Gambia struck again on a swift counter-attack, with a player collecting the ball before firing a powerful left-footed effort into the corner to put his side ahead.
The comeback was completed when Gambia added a fourth goal with a curling strike into the top corner, sealing a 4-2 victory after trailing by two goals.
Despite the defeat, Pakistan's opening performance offered encouragement, particularly through the attacking contributions of Hamza and Baxi, whose goals showcased the team's ability to compete on the international stage.

The preview aired on Friday, October 23, during the game between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays
Marvel Studios has released a special preview of Avengers: Doomsday during Game 1 of the 2026 Major League Baseball World Series, bringing together the upcoming superhero film’s characters and several prominent baseball players.
The preview aired on Friday, October 23, during the game between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays. Created specifically for the World Series, the promotional video features MLB stars Bryce Harper, Freddie Freeman, Jacob Misiorowski, Junior Caminero and Randy Arozarena alongside characters from the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
The footage includes a baseball scene set in the world of The Fantastic Four: First Steps , with Pedro Pascal’s Reed Richards, also known as Mister Fantastic, demonstrating his elastic abilities while preparing to throw a ceremonial first pitch. The scene features a retro-inspired setting at Ebbets Field, with Reed wearing a Brooklyn Dodgers cap.
Worlds collide ⚾ An exclusive preview of Marvel's new Avengers movie assembles Bryce Harper, Freddie Freeman, Jacob Misiorowski, Junior Caminero and Randy Arozarena 👀 Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters everywhere December 18 pic.twitter.com/WX1YtKjAKt

The preview also offers glimpses of familiar faces, including Chris Hemsworth’s Thor, Chris Evans’ Steve Rogers, Paul Rudd’s Scott Lang, Shuri and members of the X-Men.
Robert Downey Jr. also appears as Doctor Doom, the central threat in the upcoming film. The preview ends with Doom arriving above the baseball field, prompting Harper to tell the group, “We gotta go. Like, now.”

title: WAPDA dominate National Athletics Championship

content:
Shahbaz wins marathon as Amtul secures two golds
WAPDA strengthened their lead at the Lok Sahaita 54th National Athletics Championship with 16 golds after the third day of the competition at NED University on Friday.
Navy remained second with seven gold medals, followed by the Higher Education Commission (HEC) with six, as the championship entered its final day. The closing ceremony is scheduled for Saturday.
WAPDA collected ten gold medals in the men's events and six in the women's competitions, underlining their dominance across the championship.
Navy's Shahbaz Masih won the men's marathon, completing the 42-kilometre race in two hours, 48 minutes and 48 seconds. Sindh's Raees Khameer finished second in 2:55:26, while Police's Ahmed took bronze in 2:58:23.
HEC's Abu Bakar claimed gold in the decathlon with 5,294 points. Punjab's Abdul Rehman finished second with 5,127 points, narrowly ahead of WAPDA's Shoaib Khan, who scored 5,125.
HEC's Khabeeb won the men's 3,000-metre steeplechase in 9:41.16, while WAPDA's Muhammad Irfan took silver and Police's Mubashir finished third.
In women's events, HEC's Kinza Fatima won the 400-metre hurdles in 1:05.40. WAPDA's Nazia claimed the 800 metres in 2:25.10, ahead of HEC's Nida Karim.
WAPDA also won the mixed 4x400-metre relay in 3:39.10 and the mixed 4x100-metre relay in 44.50 seconds.
Navy's Amtul Rehman added two titles to her tally, winning the women's heptathlon with 3,608 points and the triple jump with a distance of 11.77 metres. The victories took her gold-medal count at the championship to four.
Navy's Abdullah Nawaz won the men's discus throw with a distance of 51.05 metres, while WAPDA's Hazrat Umar claimed the men's 400-metre hurdles in 55.06 seconds.
The championship is being held under the supervision of the Athletics Federation of Pakistan and organised by the Sindh Athletics Association with the support of Lakh Sahaita.

title: Malaysia crowned Johor Cup champions
description: Hosts rally from two goals down to beat Pakistan on penalties
content:
Hosts rally from two goals down to beat Pakistan on penalties
Malaysia staged a remarkable comeback to defeat Pakistan in a penalty shootout and win the Sultan of Johor Cup 2026 after an entertaining final ended 2-2 at the Taman Daya Hockey Stadium.
The hosts held their nerve to triumph 4-3 in the shootout, denying Pakistan the title after recovering from a two-goal deficit in regulation time.
Pakistan appeared firmly in control after penalty-corner specialist Rana Waleed opened the scoring in the 19th minute. Usman Muhammad extended their advantage four minutes later, scoring a field goal to put Pakistan 2-0 ahead and leave Malaysia facing an uphill battle.
However, the hosts responded quickly to reignite their hopes. Adam Asyraf Johari converted a penalty corner in the 25th minute, reducing the deficit to 2-1 and giving Malaysia renewed momentum.
Malaysia continued to push forward after the break, searching for an equaliser against a determined Pakistan defence. Their persistence paid off in the 49th minute when Dheeressh Gunaseelan scored from a penalty corner to bring the hosts level at 2-2.
Neither side could find a decisive goal during the remaining regulation time, forcing the final into a penalty shootout to determine the champions.
Malaysia proved more clinical from the spot, converting four attempts through Johari, Gagandeep Singh, Rahuul Fazrien Muhammad Nazrien and Ashrafeel Iman Mohd Rizal.
Pakistan scored three times, with Ali Hamza converting once and Waleed finding the net twice. Despite Waleed's impressive contribution, Pakistan fell just short as Malaysia sealed a memorable victory on home soil.
The triumph capped a spirited recovery by Malaysia, who overturned an early two-goal deficit to claim the trophy in front of their home supporters.
For Pakistan, the defeat marked their second runners-up finish in the Sultan of Johor Cup. They had also finished second in the 2016 edition.

Four children from the same family were killed, and four others were injured when a van carrying them to a religious school plunged into a deep ravine in Azad Jammu and Kashmir's Neelum Valley on Saturday, police said.
According to Neelum Valley police, the van was travelling from Nagdar, about 20 kilometres from the district headquarters, Athmuqam, when the accident occurred.

The injured were subsequently taken to Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan Hospital in Muzaffarabad for further treatment.

The deceased were identified as 12-year-old Hasnain, 10-year-old Taifoor, 16-year-old Aleen and two-year-old Zareed. The victims included siblings.
Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) Azad Jammu and Kashmir President Shah Ghulam Qadir expressed grief over the loss of the children and extended his condolences to the bereaved families. He also prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured.

title: Moonshot curbs hacking ability in new Kimi model as fears grow over AI powered cyberattacks
description: It removed cyber related data from training  while retaining general coding skills in its AI model
content:
It removed cyber-related data from training, while retaining general coding skills in its AI model
Moonshot ​AI has reduced the cyber-offensive capabilities of its newest model, the Chinese startup said ‌on Saturday, as fears grow that increasingly autonomous AI could turbocharge hacking.
Beijing-based Moonshot announced the curbs while introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, which it describes as its most capable 3-trillion-parameter-class open-weight model. The company plans to publish the model's ​weights — files allowing outside developers to run and modify it on their own systems — by ​November 4.
Moonshot said it removed cyber-related data from the training corpus and reinforcement-learning environments ⁠used to develop the model, while retaining general coding skills.
"We aim not to release open weights ​that would extend the absolute frontier of cyber capability," the company said.
Governments, technology companies and security researchers ​are growing increasingly concerned that AI could make sophisticated hacking easier and cheaper. Models that can write code, operate software tools and complete long, multi-step tasks may help users identify weaknesses in programs and automate parts of cyberattacks.
China proposed ​export controls last week that would ban exports of AI-driven malware-generation and mutation technology and restrict AI-assisted ​vulnerability-discovery tools. The draft measures, which remain open for public comment, cite the risk that such capabilities could be ‌used ⁠against critical infrastructure, defence-industrial and core government systems, or to bypass security protections.
Read More: Bill Gates warns of 20 years of turmoil from artificial intelligence
Moonshot said open-weight models can improve security by helping more organisations inspect and secure their own software, including older systems that receive little attention.
Unlike proprietary, closed-weight AI systems, however, open-weight releases make central oversight more difficult. Once the files ​are widely distributed, the ​original developer has less ⁠ability to restrict access, monitor use or update safeguards than with a hosted service.
K3.1 Pro scored 81.0% on its internal cyber benchmark, compared with 90.5% ​for a similar version without the risk-reduction measures, the company said. The ​test involved finding ⁠and exploiting software vulnerabilities in a controlled environment. Moonshot said the comparison showed that filtering cyber-related data reduced the model's offensive cyber performance, although it still outperformed its predecessor. The results have not been independently verified.
K3.1 ⁠Pro has ​a 1-million-token context window, allowing it to process very large ​amounts of text at once. Moonshot also released a faster version, K3.1 Pro Highspeed, which it said runs at two to ​three times the speed of the standard model.

title: Curtis  Karim reach ABC Cup final
description: Top seed rallies to win five game semi final  Karim prevails over Siow
content:
Top seed rallies to win five-game semi-final; Karim prevails over Siow
England’s Curtis Malik overcame Yassin Shohdy of Egypt 3-2 in a closely contested semi-final of the Venice ABC Open Squash Championship at the DHA Creek Club on Saturday.
Top seed Malik won 12-10 in the opening game before taking the second 11-7. Shohdy fought back strongly, winning the next two games 11-9 and 11-8 to level the match and force a decider.
Malik held his nerve in the fifth game, winning 11-5 to complete a 12-10, 11-7, 9-11, 8-11, 11-5 victory in a match that swung back and forth.
Shohdy's response after falling two games behind threatened to turn the contest around, but Malik regained control in the deciding game to seal his place in the final.
In the other semi-final, second seed Karim El Hammamy of Egypt produced a dominant performance to defeat Yee Xian Siow of Malaysia 3-0.
El Hammamy won 11-9, 11-9, 11-6, maintaining control throughout the contest and avoiding the need for a fourth game.
Karim had qualified for the semi-final after beating Asim Khan of Pakistan 3-1 in the quarter-finals.
Curtis had defeated Ziad Ibrahim of Egypt 3-0 to make it to the semi-finals.
The final between Curtis and Karim will be interesting as both players have done extremely well in the 24-man event in which Pakistani players failed to deliver.
Both Asim and Nasir Iqbal did not live up to the billings.
Meanwhile Egypt's Raneem Elaraby and Amina El Rihany advanced to the final of the women’s section.
Fourth seed Elaraby defeated compatriot Haya Rizk 3-1, recovering from a second-game setback to win 11-3, 4-11, 11-7, 11-4.
Second seed El Rihany also produced a strong performance, overcoming third seed Nour Shahin by the same scoreline. El Rihany won 11-3, 10-12, 11-8, 11-4 to book her place in the title decider.

title: PTI retains Junaid Akbar as K P president  grants authority to Noorul Haq Qadri in his absence
description: Party chairman Barrister Gohar grants Ali Asghar responsibilities in the absence of both
content:
Party chairman Barrister Gohar grants Ali Asghar responsibilities in the absence of both
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Saturday issued a notification stating that the party’s provincial organisation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) would continue to function under the presidency of Junaid Akbar, highlighting no changes to the provincial cabinet or organisational structure until further orders.
The government and opposition failed to reach an agreement, and emergency and governor’s rule were declared on October 11 after talks failed , following a PTI long march towards Islamabad that began on October 4. On the same day, police arrested 59 PTI workers in Swabi and six others in Khyber district, while reports emerged that ousted chief minister Sohail Afridi and Akbar had also been taken into custody. Since then, intraparty rifts reportedly emerged, leading to PTI leaders exchanging barbs online.
According to a notification issued today and shared on X, Senator Noorul Haq Qadri, identified as the party’s senior vice-president in K-P, would preside over meetings of the provincial cabinet in the absence of Junaid.
The notification further assigned PTI K-P General Secretary Ali Asghar the responsibility of chairing meetings in the absence of the senior vice-president. He was also authorised to convene and chair meetings of other tiers of the provincial organisation.

According to the document, Asghar would oversee the organisation’s administration, coordination and supervision across its various tiers and wings to ensure the implementation of party policies, strategies and decisions.
The notification was signed by Barrister Gohar in his capacity as chairman of PTI.
The notification comes amid an internal rift within the PTI, with differences over the party’s leadership and political strategy in K-P spilling into the public domain. On October 21, The Express Tribune reported that former K-P chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur and PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja had exchanged criticism over allegations of internal divisions, the provincial leadership and the handling of the party’s political affairs.
Raja warned of attempts by what he described as “undemocratic decision-makers” to undermine internal consensus, while Gandapur demanded that the party secretary general substantiate his allegations and apologise.
The dispute intensified following a purported audio recording in which Gandapur allegedly blamed Raja’s “mismanagement and flawed planning” for the provincial government’s dismissal and the party’s current predicament. The Express Tribune said it could not independently verify the recording.
Read more: Opposition leaders criticise govt over stalled talks, restrictions on parliamentarians
Gandapur also challenged claims that provincial lawmakers were attempting to decide the party’s leadership and the next chief minister without the approval of PTI founder Imran Khan and the party’s political committee. Raja, meanwhile, maintained that Afridi remained the lawful chief minister and that Akbar continued as provincial party president, with Asghar acting in Akbar’s absence.
Barrister Gohar sought to contain the fallout, telling the media that he had spoken to the leaders involved and urged them to stop issuing statements against one another.
He maintained that the party’s provincial lawmakers remained united and that Afridi continued to be the party’s choice for chief minister. Against this backdrop, the October 24 notification formalises the arrangements for the PTI’s K-P organisation, specifying who will preside over meetings in the absence of senior office-bearers.

title: OpenAI resumes frontier AI training after security overhaul  discloses flaw in widely used software
description: Disclosure highlights concerns over AI agents exploiting software flaws  including in safeguards to control them
content:
Disclosure highlights concerns over AI agents exploiting software flaws, including in safeguards to control them
OpenAI said on Friday it had resumed training of its most advanced AI models after tightening security and barring internet access, and ​disclosed a flaw in a widely used software that it found while ‌testing its defenses.
The disclosure comes amid concerns over the ability of increasingly capable AI agents to identify and exploit software flaws, including in the guardrails meant to contain them.
OpenAI had paused training of its ​most capable models after one of its research models used a configuration error ​to gain limited internet access in September. The company said it contained ⁠the incident and used the pause to strengthen its defenses.
To test them, OpenAI had ​teams of AI agents try to break out of their restricted environments. It said the ​agents found previously unknown flaws, which it had fixed, and training resumed on October 1.
During that exercise, the ChatGPT maker found a flaw in Brotli, a widely used data compression tool.
Read More: Bill Gates warns of 20 years of turmoil from artificial intelligence
The company said attackers ​could exploit the flaw by sending malicious data that lets them run their own ​code on affected systems, including those using popular web software such as Node.js , Bun and Envoy.
OpenAI said the ‌root ⁠cause was fixed in Brotli's source code in February, before it was known to create a security vulnerability, but no new version was released at the time. Brotli has since released updated versions and published a public record of the flaw after OpenAI disclosed ​it.
Separately on Thursday, AI ​safety evaluators METR ⁠and Redwood Research said they found several new vulnerabilities in OpenAI's internal system, including an exploit agents could have used to keep hundreds ​of their actions from being monitored, in a pilot review earlier ​this year.
OpenAI ⁠told the safety organizations it has since patched all vulnerabilities affecting its production safeguards, although METR and Redwood said they had not verified the fixes.
OpenAI has been conducting a broad review of ⁠its AI ​models' activity since the Hugging Face incident in July, ​and has informed more than 100 organizations about incidents of unauthorized activity tied to its AI agents.

title: Pakistan seek tri series final berth
description: Will Jacks backs England to bounce back in must win clash against the hosts
content:
Will Jacks backs England to bounce back in must-win clash against the hosts
Pakistan will look to extend their winning run when they face England in the third match of the ODI tri-series at Gaddafi Stadium Lahore on Sunday.
The match will start at 1pm PST, with victory securing Pakistan a place in the October 31 final.
Pakistan have won both their matches, beating Sri Lanka by 37 runs before defeating England by 87 runs in Rawalpindi.
For England, the match is crucial. Having lost both their opening games, they must beat Pakistan to keep their hopes of reaching the final alive.
Pakistan have twice defended 300-plus totals, but the Green-shirts will need to adapt to a new surface at Gaddafi Stadium, which could offer different from those in Rawalpindi.
England, meanwhile, were stunned by Sri Lanka in a two-wicket defeat the other day after the hosts completed a world-record chase of 430 runs with one ball remaining.
Pakistan’s captain Shaheen Shah Afridi said his team would focus on maintaining its momentum rather than worrying about the opposition's performances.
“We don't bother about the other team, what runs they scored and what their mindset is. Our mindset is that we have to win the match,” Shaheen told a news conference on Saturday.
“We will try to stick to our plans. We will try to carry on our normal discipline, and we have to win the match,” he added.
“If we bowl first, we will try to restrict them to 250, and we are capable of doing so as a bowling unit.”
Shaheen also backed openers Saim Ayub and Fakhar Zaman, stressing their importance to the team's plans.
“If you pick five or six top ODI batters, you will find Saim scoring runs. His benefit to the team is that he is a utility bowler also. You saw against England that he contained the batters when we badly needed it, and he is also a good fielder. We will pray for him to perform,” Shaheen said.
“Fakhar is also one of Pakistan's main players, and his presence in the team is very important,” he added.
The Pakistan captain said the team was working towards settling on its best combination, noting that there had been few changes in the previous matches.
He described Abrar Ahmed as a very good bowler and said the leg-spinner could be included when conditions were expected to favour spin.
Shaheen also highlighted the need for a specialist all-rounder at number eight. He also said that T20I captain Sahibzada Farhan could be considered for future opportunities as Pakistan plan ahead for the World Cup.
“If we feel the need for Sahibzada, as he is the T20 captain, we will give one or two players a chance in future matches and decide about him,” Shaheen said.
England’s all-rounder Will Jacks, meanwhile, remained optimistic about his team's prospects, saying they had an opportunity to revive their campaign.
“I think we have got a good chance to bounce back. We have still got two more games in this series, and we know now we are in a very simple situation: we have to win both matches to give ourselves a chance. We are looking forward to the challenge,” Jacks said.
He also expected Lahore to provide favourable batting conditions, although England would assess the surface after training.
“They have definitely got the ability here to have a wide variety of pitches. We have obviously seen Rawalpindi is a good place for batting in both red-ball and white-ball cricket. I am expecting something similar here in Lahore,” he said.
“We have only just got here, so we will need to have a look tonight, see how the training pitches play and then assess tomorrow.”

title: Alexander brothers    survivors speak out in new documentary ahead of sentencing
description: The Wolves of Real Estate  The Alexander Brothers  features women recounting their experiences with the brothers
content:
'The Wolves of Real Estate: The Alexander Brothers' features women recounting their experiences with the brothers
Survivors of the Alexander brothers’ sexual abuse are sharing their experiences in a new documentary examining the rise and fall of the wealthy real estate siblings, who were convicted of sex trafficking earlier this year.
The Wolves of Real Estate: The Alexander Brothers features women recounting their alleged experiences with Tal, Oren and Alon Alexander, including the difficulty of understanding what happened to them and finding the courage to speak publicly. The three-part documentary premieres on Peacock on Sunday, October 25, just two days before the brothers are scheduled to be sentenced in federal court.
“I didn’t even know what to call what they did to me,” one woman says in a preview of the documentary. Another survivor breaks down in tears while describing her experience.
The documentary explores how the brothers allegedly used their wealth, luxury holidays and glamorous social lives to attract women before drugging and sexually assaulting them. Tal and Oren became prominent figures in the luxury real estate industry, while Alon held an executive role at the family’s security company.
The brothers moved within wealthy social circles in Miami, New York City, the Hamptons and Aspen. Their public image stood in stark contrast to the allegations that eventually led to their arrests in December 2024.
Following a five-week federal trial in Manhattan earlier this year, all three brothers were convicted of charges including sex trafficking and conspiracy to commit sex trafficking. Additional convictions included offences involving minors and sexual abuse. Prosecutors have requested life sentences for the brothers ahead of their October 27 sentencing.
The documentary also examines why it took some women years to come forward and the influence that wealth and power can have on whether survivors feel safe speaking publicly. Some witnesses at the brothers’ trial testified under pseudonyms to protect their identities.
The case gained wider attention after women filed civil lawsuits against Oren and Alon, accusing them of rape and sexual assault. Those cases were followed by further allegations from dozens of women, contributing to the criminal investigation and prosecution.
The Wolves of Real Estate: The Alexander Brothers aims to provide a broader account of the case beyond the courtroom proceedings, drawing on interviews and accounts from people connected to the brothers at different stages of their lives.
The series arrives as the brothers face sentencing following their federal convictions. Prosecutors have argued for life imprisonment, while the documentary revisits the experiences of women whose accounts helped bring the case into the public eye.
All three episodes of The Wolves of Real Estate: The Alexander Brothers will premiere on Peacock on Sunday, October 25.

title: Rybakina to face Fernandez for Ningbo title
description: Kazakh seed secures victory over Diana Shnaider in the semifinal
content:
Kazakh seed secures victory over Diana Shnaider in the semifinal
Top-ranked Elena Rybakina closed in on her fourth WTA title of the year as she beat Diana Shnaider on Saturday to set up a Ningbo Open final against Leylah Fernandez.
Three-time Grand Slam winner Rybakina, the number one seed and defending champion, defeated the 13th-ranked Russian 6-3, 7-5.
Rybakina, who usurped Aryna Sabalenka as world number one in her US Open triumph in September, missed last week's Wuhan Open with a foot injury.
The Moscow-born Kazakh threatened to run away with the first set but struggled to put Shnaider away when serving at 5-3 up.
Rybakina twice double-faulted as she uncharacteristically saw an astounding 10 set points come and go.
The 27-year-old finally clinched the set at the 11th time of asking.
The hard-hitting Shnaider, 22, dug herself out of a hole on her own serve to hold at the start of the second set.
Now in the groove, Rybakina ramped up the pressure to break serve in the seventh game, then held for a 5-3 lead.
Rybakina served for the match at 5-4 but inexplicably crumbled with victory in sight and was broken to love, only to recover and immediately grab the break back.
She served for the match once more at 6-5 and this time made no mistake, sealing the deal on her second match point with a two-handed backhand down the line.
In the other semi-final, Fernandez defeated Marie Bouzkova 6-3, 7-5 as she chases a second title in as many months.
The Canadian world number 30 won her first title of the year in Singapore last month and had too much for the 26th-ranked Bouzkova of the Czech Republic.
After dominating the first set, Fernandez broke early in the second for a 2-0 lead, only for Bouzkova to hit back as both struggled on their serve.
The second set turned into an arm-wrestle before Fernandez prevailed in just under two hours when Bouzkova returned long.
