title: France deploys 70 000 police to try to contain nationwide protests
description: In France s second and third cities  Marseille and Lyon  clashes broke out between hooded youths and police
content:
In France's second and third cities, Marseille and Lyon, clashes broke out between hooded youths and police
Demonstrators took to the streets of France ​on Saturday under the watch of 70,000 police officers, with unrest appearing markedly less severe than a week earlier despite scattered confrontations in several cities.
Tens ‌of thousands of people marched peacefully through the French capital, according to police numbers, denouncing the high cost of living and accusing President Emmanuel Macron of cutting public services while failing to tackle rising inequality.
"Down with the state, the police and the fascists," some of the flag-waving crowds chanted.
Elsewhere, police fired tear gas at people in Clermont-Ferrand, Grenoble, Lille and Nice, where a water cannon was deployed after protesters ​refused orders to pull back.
In France's second and third cities, Marseille and Lyon, clashes broke out between hooded youths and police.
The government deployed 10,000 more police ​and gendarmes than on October 17, when nationwide protests descended into some of the worst unrest in France in years.
"We have to be ⁠ultra, ultra responsive," said Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, who has accused far-left groups and criminal gangs of fomenting violence.
Nunez told reporters that police had arrested 135 people nationwide by ​early afternoon, many following pre-emptive searches that he said had uncovered fireworks, ball bearings and other items that could be used as weapons.
Much of central Paris took ​on the appearance of a city under lockdown, with shopkeepers boarding up storefronts , museums closing their doors and more than 20 metro stations shut.
Business groups urged retailers to remain closed after thousands of shops and businesses were damaged or looted across France last weekend.
"There are hardly any customers, so it's not really worth staying open," said Oskar, manager of a Kiton boutique in Paris.
Several of the capital's best-known cultural institutions, including ​the Louvre, the Musee d'Orsay and the Paris Opera, closed for the day as a precaution, leaving tourists frustrated.
French security forces fanned out across Paris on Saturday ahead of protests that authorities fear could turn violent, ​with Interior Minister Laurent Nunez urging police to be "hyper-reactive" against troublemakers and looters.
Soldiers from an anti-terrorism military unit patrolled the Champs-Élysées avenue while police vans circled the Arc de Triomphe, looking to protect some of the capital's most famous sites from any repeat of the unrest that shook France last week.
Nunez has mobilised 70,000 police nationwide for Saturday's demonstrations, 10,000 more than on October 17, when a wave of vandalism and looting raised questions about the government's ability ​to maintain order.
Anger over living costs and strained public services has drawn students, workers and unions onto the streets in recent weeks, ​but authorities say radical militants and bands of young looters have exploited the protests to sow chaos.
Read: ‘Threat exists’: Paris police warn of possible unrest ahead of protests
Speaking to police in Paris, ⁠Nunez warned officers that they would face attempts to target shops, public institutions and security forces.
"We have to be ultra, ultra responsive. We ​have significant calls for disruption from political groups and quite simply from criminals," he said. "It is going to be a long day."
Many ​shopkeepers in Paris boarded up storefronts, while luxury retailers beefed up security.
Business groups have urged stores to remain closed after thousands of shops and businesses were damaged or looted across France last weekend.
Lidiya Shevchenko, a sales assistant at a Graziella Braccialini store in Paris, said she doubted many customers would venture out to browse luxury boutiques during ​the day.
"I suppose the mood is just as important when it comes to shopping," she said.
Several of Paris' best-known cultural institutions, including the Louvre, ​the Musée d'Orsay and the Opera House, will close for the day to avoid being caught up in any turmoil. More than 20 metro stations were also ‌shut.
The location ⁠of Saturday's main Paris demonstration remained unclear after police sought to move organisers away from the city centre towards the southeastern fringes of the capital.
"The declared route poses serious risks of disturbances to public order, notably because of the high concentration of businesses similar to those targeted during the weekend of October 17-18," the Paris police prefecture said.
Read more: Hitler's historic teahouse goes up in flames in Germany, arson suspected
The last-minute decision angered some on the left.
"Once again, those in power are creating disruption for the ​marches and impossible deadlines for organisations ​to reorganise themselves. These methods are ⁠multiplying across the entire country," hard-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon wrote on X.
Demonstration in Orleans against far right
Authorities have sharply restricted demonstrations across much of France. Marseille reversed an earlier ban and authorised a union march, while ​protests remain restricted in central Lyon. Union rallies will also go ahead in Strasbourg, but bans remain in ​force in several ⁠other cities including Nancy, Metz, Besançon, Belfort, Rouen, Le Havre, Toulon and Limoges.
The first authorised march began mid-morning in Orleans, about 120 km (75 miles) south of Paris, to protest against Marine Le Pen's far-right National Rally, which is holding a congress in the city this weekend.
"We have come to tell the far ⁠right, face ​to face, that we are not afraid," said Bally Bagayoko, the mayor of Saint-Denis and ​a member of the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party.
Tensions were heightened by a shooting west of Paris on Friday in which a gunman suspected of acting out of Islamophobic hatred killed one person and ​wounded four others, including a 12-year-old girl.

title: RJ Mitte accused business manager Lisa Harrison of mishandling his earnings before his death
description: Mitte said he had trusted a manager with tax payments while building his career as a young actor
content:
Mitte said he had trusted a manager with tax payments while building his career as a young actor
The financial allegations surrounding late Breaking Bad actor RJ Mitte have resurfaced following reports identifying the business management company he accused of mishandling his earnings.
Mitte, who played Walter White Jr. on the acclaimed television drama, died on October 12, 2026, aged 34. His representative confirmed that he died by suicide. However, there is no verified evidence that the financial dispute caused his death.
In a November 2025 appearance on The Iced Coffee Hour podcast, Mitte said he had hired a business manager as a teenager to help protect his income. He claimed money intended for tax payments was diverted, leaving him responsible for unpaid taxes and additional charges.
“I’ve paid more in taxes than I got from Breaking Bad ,” he said during the interview, describing the financial consequences of the arrangement.
According to recent reports citing a police complaint, Mitte and his mother raised concerns with authorities in 2015. The reports identify Harrison Business Management, operated by Lisa Harrison, as the company involved. Mitte alleged that money had been taken from funds intended to cover his financial obligations.
The allegations have not resulted in criminal charges against Harrison in connection with Mitte’s claims, according to reporting by The Blast . Her husband, attorney David Brody, has denied wrongdoing, telling the Daily Mail that she had done nothing wrong.
Mitte also claimed during his podcast appearance that other actors had experienced similar problems. He said resolving the financial situation was difficult and described the lengthy process of addressing the resulting tax liabilities.
The renewed attention has prompted discussion about the financial risks young performers can face when entrusting their earnings to professionals. Mitte began acting at a young age and became widely recognised through Breaking Bad , which ran from 2008 to 2013.
Beyond his acting career, he was an advocate for disability rights, drawing on his own experience living with cerebral palsy. His death has prompted tributes from former co-stars and renewed interest in his life and career.

title: Mpox claims another child s life in Sindh  this year s death toll rises to 12
description: The child  a resident of Karachi  died during treatment at the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital in NIPA
content:
The child, a resident of Karachi, died during treatment at the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital in NIPA
Another child died of mpox in Karachi on Saturday, taking the number of deaths caused by the viral infection in Sindh this year to 12, as health authorities reported seven new cases over the past week and intensified surveillance, contact tracing, and treatment measures.
According to Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital spokesperson Rashid Khan, the child, a resident of Karachi, was being treated in the hospital in NIPA for monkeypox and passed away during treatment, further revealed that the patient had been transferred to the facility from a private hospital a few days earlier.
Khan said the total number of mpox cases reported in Sindh has climbed to 98.
The Express Tribune contacted Sindh Institute of Skin Diseases (Regal) Additional Director and consultant dermatologist Dr Abdullah Yahya to learn about the disease.
Read: Sindh reports two more monkeypox cases, tally rises to 98
Dr Yahya cautioned that mpox was a contagious viral disease that could spread through close physical contact with an infected person, including direct contact with skin lesions, blisters and sores.
“The virus could also be transmitted through contaminated clothing, towels, bedding and other personal belongings used by an infected person,” he said, while stressing the need to avoid contact with contaminated items and affected persons.
Dr Yahya also emphasised the importance of early diagnosis, isolating infected individuals and following medical advice to prevent further transmission.
“Mpox can affect both children and adults, although the severity of the illness varies from person to person. Infants, people with weakened immune systems and those suffering from other underlying medical conditions may face a higher risk of severe illness and complications,” the skin doctor outlined.
He also underscored the common symptoms of the virus, saying it includes fever, body aches, swollen lymph nodes, and unusual skin rashes, blisters or sores.
According to Dr Yahya, suspected and confirmed patients should be kept separate under medical supervision, with appropriate infection-prevention measures in place.
Most patients can recover with appropriate medical care and monitoring, he said, adding that immediate medical attention was necessary if severe symptoms developed.
According to figures available with the provincial health department, Karachi has recorded the highest number of mpox cases in Sindh, with 26 infections reported.
Khairpur has reported 22 cases, followed by Sukkur with nine and Hyderabad with five. Ghotki, Kashmore and Shaheed Benazirabad have recorded three cases each.
Read more: HIV crisis at Valika snowballs, toll hits 169
Men account for approximately 73% of reported cases, while women make up the remaining 27%.
Hospital sealed over infection-control concerns
Separately, the Sindh Healthcare Commission has sealed Ibn-e-Hasan Hospital in Malir 15, Karachi, following concerns over infection-prevention arrangements after a laboratory report confirmed mpox in a 20-day-old newborn.
According to information available to The Express Tribune , the infant had undergone circumcision at the hospital.
The case has raised concerns about the implementation of infection-control protocols at healthcare facilities, particularly the sterilisation of medical instruments and the use of proper sterile procedures during treatment.
Health authorities have stepped up efforts to identify and monitor close contacts of infected patients to prevent further spread of the virus.
Patients being treated at government hospitals are being provided with medical care, while public and private healthcare facilities have been directed to follow prescribed infection-prevention measures and use appropriate protective equipment when examining and treating suspected cases.
Health experts have also advised the public to maintain good hygiene, avoid direct contact with the lesions, blisters and sores of suspected or confirmed patients, and refrain from sharing their personal items, particularly towels, clothes, and bedding.

title: SHC orders transfer of thousands of narcotics cases to five special courts in Karachi
description: District judges directed to ensure compliance with the order  submit a report to the SHC member inspection team
content:
District judges directed to ensure compliance with the order, submit a report to the SHC member inspection team
The Sindh High Court (SHC) has directed the transfer of thousands of pending cases registered under the Sindh Control of Narcotic Substances (CNS) Act, 2024, to the five newly constituted special courts in Karachi.
According to an official communication issued by SHC Member Inspection Team-II, Muhammad Jahangir Khan, on the directions of the chief justice, all district and sessions judges in Karachi South, East, West, Central and Malir have been instructed to ensure the transfer of the pending drug cases to the Special Courts constituted under Article 30 (Establishment of Special Court) of the CNS Act.
The letter seen by The Express Tribune outlined that the cases have been transferred to CNS Courts-I, II, IV, V and VI, Karachi in accordance with the territorial jurisdiction. The letter further directed the district judges to ensure compliance with the order and submit a report to Khan.
The development follows changes to the provincial narcotics law after the Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997 was repealed on October 15, 2024, and replaced by the Sindh CNS Act, 2024.
According to authorities, all cases registered under the latest act have been transferred to the new courts, including four cases registered against alleged Cocaine Queen Anmol alias Pinky.
Under the new arrangement, remand proceedings in newly registered cases will also be conducted before the CNS courts. Interim and final charge sheets in both new and pending cases will also be submitted to these courts.
It is worth noting that under the new law, the government can establish narcotics control police stations, check posts and check points to eliminate the menace of drug trafficking. It also provides stricter punishments alongside safeguards, such as video evidence in cases, to protect the rights of citizens.
Article 17, clause 2 of the law states, “The video recording of all raids, seizures, inspections and arrests shall be made by the officer in charge of such operations.”

title: Macklemore calls for  Free Palestine  and condemns ICE at first show since Ed Sheeran tour controversy
description: Macklemore also expressed solidarity with people in Sudan  the Democratic Republic of the Congo  Lebanon and Haiti
content:
Macklemore also expressed solidarity with people in Sudan, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Lebanon and Haiti
Macklemore has reiterated his support for Palestine and condemned US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) during his first concert since being removed from Ed Sheeran’s North American Loop tour over his pro-Palestinian statements.
The rapper performed a 17-song set at Red Rocks Amphitheatre in Colorado on Thursday, October 22. During the show, he addressed the audience with a speech calling for freedom for Palestinians and people affected by conflicts and injustices around the world.
“Being a human being in this moment is not complicated,” Macklemore said. “It is not political. It is human to have a heart, to watch others suffering and to say, ‘Not anymore!’ So I say, free Palestine. I say, free Palestine!”
He continued by expressing solidarity with people in Sudan, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Lebanon and Haiti, as well as those affected by ICE in the United States who are afraid to leave their homes. He concluded his remarks by telling the audience: “The message will always be love.”
The performance marked Macklemore’s return to the stage following the controversy surrounding his removal from Sheeran’s tour last month. The dispute began after the rapper called for a free Palestine during performances at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey in September and performed his 2024 protest song ‘Hind’s Hall’ alongside footage from Gaza.
His remarks prompted criticism from several groups and public figures, while the Israeli-American Council launched a petition calling for him to be removed from the tour. Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft also objected to Macklemore appearing at Sheeran’s scheduled shows at the venue.
Macklemore subsequently announced that he had been dropped from the remaining dates. He said the decision followed discussions with Sheeran, who had told him that Kraft and other stadium owners objected to his presence on the line-up. Sheeran has not publicly provided a detailed account of the decision.
Following the fallout, Macklemore pledged his entire $1 million earnings from the tour to six organisations supporting Palestinians. He also announced a series of benefit concerts across the UK and Europe under the name Free Palestine Tour . The shows subsequently sold out.
In announcing the concerts, Macklemore said they had been organised quickly through community support, with the aim of raising funds and demonstrating solidarity with Palestinians. He also argued that music could be used to support calls for liberation, particularly when artists face pressure over their public statements.
The controversy has continued to draw reactions from musicians and other public figures. Rage Against the Machine guitarist Tom Morello praised Macklemore for standing by his position, while other artists have weighed in on the dispute surrounding his removal from Sheeran’s tour.
Macklemore’s latest performance reinforces his commitment to using his platform to speak about Palestine and other humanitarian issues, despite the professional consequences that followed his earlier remarks.

title: Easy A    director Will Gluck says Amanda Bynes found    Easy A    supporting role tough opposite Emma Stone
description: Gluck recalled that Bynes never auditioned for the 2010 comedy and was professional throughout filming
content:
Gluck recalled that Bynes never auditioned for the 2010 comedy and was professional throughout filming
Easy A director Will Gluck has reflected on Amanda Bynes’ experience making the 2010 teen comedy, suggesting it may have been difficult for the former child star to take a supporting role opposite Emma Stone.
Speaking on the Plus One podcast with Jess Lucero, Gluck said Bynes had already become a major star before joining the film, while Stone was emerging as its lead performer.
“She was a huge star and then she had to play, like, a second banana to Emma,” Gluck said, describing the situation as “kind of tough for her”. He nevertheless praised Bynes’ performance, adding that she was great in the film.
Bynes played Marianne Bryant, a devout Christian student who becomes one of the central figures in the school drama surrounding Stone’s character, Olive Penderghast. The film, released in 2010, became a notable entry in the teen comedy genre and helped strengthen Stone’s career.
Gluck also emphasised that Bynes was professional throughout production. He recalled that she did not audition for the role, explaining that they had met beforehand and spent time getting to know each other.
“She was 100 percent a pro,” he said, adding that he was shocked by the difficulties Bynes experienced after leaving acting. Gluck said people later asked whether he had noticed warning signs while working with her, but he recalled seeing nothing unusual on set.
Easy A ultimately became Bynes’ final film appearance. She stepped away from acting shortly after its release and later spoke publicly about her struggles and the impact of watching her performance in the movie.
In a 2018 interview with Paper magazine, Bynes said she disliked her appearance and acting in the film, describing the experience of watching it as a turning point in her decision to stop acting.
Bynes later focused on her personal well-being and other creative interests. Her experience has continued to draw public attention, while Gluck’s recollections offer a glimpse into her time on the set of the comedy.

title: James Bond casting race narrows as Jacob Elordi reportedly misses final auditions
description: Denis Villeneuve and casting director Nina Gold are overseeing the search for Daniel Craig   s successor
content:
Denis Villeneuve and casting director Nina Gold are overseeing the search for Daniel Craig’s successor
The search for the next James Bond is reportedly entering its final stage, with Callum Turner and Jack Lowden among the actors expected to undergo screen tests as Amazon MGM Studios looks for Daniel Craig’s successor.
According to Variety , the final auditions could begin as early as October 23, although the exact list of actors taking part has not been confirmed. Reports from other entertainment outlets have also named Josh O’Connor as a potential finalist, while the identity of another possible candidate remains unclear.
Jacob Elordi, who had been linked to the role, is reportedly not among those taking part in the latest screen tests. Jack O’Connell, another actor previously discussed as a contender, has also been reported to be out of the running.
Turner, 36, has attracted attention for his performances in Fantastic Beasts and Masters of the Air . He has been linked to the coveted role for months but has not publicly confirmed any involvement in the final casting process.
Lowden, also 36, is known for playing River Cartwright in the spy drama Slow Horses . Speculation intensified after his co-star Gary Oldman appeared to suggest that the casting decision had already been made, although no official announcement has followed.
O’Connor, known for The Crown and Challengers , has also emerged in recent reports about the auditions. However, Amazon MGM Studios has not officially confirmed the reported shortlist or identified its preferred candidate.
The new Bond film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, with Nina Gold overseeing casting and Steven Knight writing the screenplay. The project follows Amazon MGM Studios gaining creative control of the franchise in 2025.
Craig last played the British secret agent in No Time to Die , released in 2021. Since then, speculation about his replacement has included numerous established actors, but the studio has yet to announce its choice.
Although the reported screen tests suggest the selection process is progressing, the final candidates and announcement date remain unconfirmed. The next James Bond casting decision is expected before the end of 2026, according to industry reports.

title: India down New Zealand in T20I thriller
description: Tilak Varma smashes an unbeaten half century as the visitors chased 181
content:
Tilak Varma sizzles with the bat as the visitors chase 181 with a ball to spare
Tilak Varma struck a brutal half-century as India powered to a thrilling four-wicket win over New Zealand in the second T20 on Saturday for a 2-0 series lead.
The tourists scored 68 runs from the last 4.5 overs in Christchurch to clinch victory with a ball to spare, having looked down and out when they were reduced to 70-5 in the 11th over, in pursuit of 181.
Tilak carved 51 not out off 26 balls while Nitish Kumar Reddy struck the winning runs in an unbeaten 26 off 13 to hand India control of the five-match series.
The result matched their four-wicket win in the opening match at the same Hagley Oval venue two days earlier, which was achieved with two balls to spare.
New Zealand's bowling was vastly improved, led by captain Mitchell Santner, who took 4-21 through the middle stages as India's top order failed to match their dynamic batting from game one, when they chased down 225.
Spinner Santner claimed the scalp of dangerous opener Abhishek Sharma for 27 in his first over and Naman Dhir for 31 in his fourth to have the tourists teetering at 112-6.
However, Tilak in particular swung the bat brilliantly over the closing stages, finding the boundary four times in the penultimate over bowled by Nathan Smith.
Opener Sanju Samson, who set up victory on Thursday with a rapid 67, departed cheaply.
That dismissal brought Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to the crease after the 15-year-old batting sensation was called up for his 10th T20, replacing the injured Ishan Kishan.
However, he didn't last long, caught in the infield off Smith for four.
Earlier, Glenn Phillips scored his second straight half-century as New Zealand recovered from 41-3 to post 180-5.
Phillips struck four sixes in his 70 off 43 balls as he put on 116 in a fourth-wicket rearguard with Bevon Jacobs, whose 58 came off 46 balls.
Seamer Arshdeep Singh was India's best bowler, taking 2-33 off four overs.

content:
Says she is closely monitoring the high-profile murder case
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Saturday said that DNA and polygraph test results indicate the alleged involvement of a domestic worker in the murder and sexual assault of Hina Javed, as investigations into the high-profile case remain ongoing.
Responding to a tweet by senior journalist Mubashir Zaidi drawing attention to the case, the chief minister said she was closely monitoring developments in the investigation.
However, she clarified that the investigation into Hina's murder and sexual assault had not yet concluded.
I am keeping a close watch. The DNA test results and polygraph test suggest that the murder and rape were committed by the servant, however the investigation is ongoing. Thank you. https://t.co/kVZ8WwvlNg
Hina, a 45-year-old digital designer, was found dead at her residence in Rawalpindi's Lal Kurti area on August 20. Police arrested her husband, Faisal Asghar Imam, and domestic worker Zeeshan Arshad in connection with the murder.
Earlier, investigators conducted DNA and polygraph examinations of both suspects at the Punjab Forensic Science Agency as part of efforts to establish their possible roles in the crime.

The committee subsequently launched a fresh investigation , examining forensic evidence, visiting the crime scene and reviewing possible shortcomings in the earlier police probe.
Meanwhile, the victim's family has repeatedly expressed dissatisfaction with the investigation and demanded the formation of a judicial commission to ensure an independent and transparent inquiry.
In the latest development, an autopsy report revealed extensive injuries on Hina's body, including a broken neck, a deep wound to the back of her head and multiple signs of violence.
The case has also reached the National Assembly Standing Committee on Interior, which has summoned senior Punjab police officials for a briefing scheduled for October 29.
The investigation remains ongoing, and the allegations against the suspects are subject to judicial determination.

title: Pakistan refutes former US envoy s  unsubstantiated  allegations of arming Afghans to fight Taliban
description: Info ministry says Khalilzad s paddling of such allegations only exposed his  skewed  agenda based views
content:
Info ministry says Khalilzad's paddling of such allegations only exposes his 'skewed, agenda-based views'
The Ministry of Information on Saturday categorically rejected the baseless and misleading allegations by former US envoy to Afghanistan Zalmay Khalilzad of arming former Afghans to fight the Taliban and terrorist groups.
"Pakistan categorically rejects the baseless and misleading allegations by Khalilzad of arming former Afghans to fight the Taliban and their supporter terrorist groups. His sweeping baseless assertions merely recycle speculative narratives as part of his personal agenda to prop terrorism supporting Taliban regime," said the ministry in a statement issued on X.
The statement came in response to a post by former US diplomat Khalilzad on X, in which he claimed that Pakistan was arming Afghans to fight the Taliban in Afghanistan and that the "Pakistani military was recruiting Afghans to fight anti-Pakistan insurgents."
The ministry further said it was misleading to conflate Pakistan's legitimate counterterrorism operations against terrorist organisations operating from inside Afghan Taliban regime-controlled areas threatening Pakistani citizens with allegations of "recruiting Afghan nationals or sponsoring armed groups inside Afghanistan.”
*𝐅𝐚𝐜𝐭 𝐂𝐡𝐞𝐜𝐤 | 𝐌𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 & 𝐁𝐫𝐨𝐚𝐝𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠* ◾️ Pakistan categorically rejects the baseless and misleading allegations by Zalmay Khalilzad of arming former Afghans to fight Taliban and their supporters terrorist groups. His… pic.twitter.com/c5UQfgAgh5
It added that Pakistan remained at the forefront of the fight against terrorism and had made enormous sacrifices to protect regional peace and security.
“Successive UN monitoring reports have documented the continued presence and activities of terrorist organisations, including TTP and Al-Qaeda, inside Afghanistan,” the ministry said.
The ministry stated that Khalilzad’s claims diverted attention from the Afghan Taliban regime’s responsibility to prevent its territory from being used by Indian-sponsored proxies for terrorism against Pakistan.
“Khalilzad paddling of such unsubstantiated allegations only exposes his skewed agenda-based views,” the ministry concluded.
Read : Info ministry calls out Afghan Taliban for deflecting attention from terrorist sanctuaries
Pakistan has repeatedly accused terrorist groups based in Afghanistan of carrying out attacks inside the country and demanded that Kabul take action against them. The Afghan Taliban government has rejected accusations that it allows its territory to be used for attacks against Pakistan.
Islamabad maintains that the terrorist nexus extended beyond the movement of terrorists across the border to their training, arming and operational support.
In 2026 alone, terrorism emanating from Afghan soil claimed the lives of 1,327 Pakistanis and injured another 2,484, according to figures cited by Pakistani authorities.
Officials said that whenever Pakistani forces targeted terrorist hideouts, the Taliban regime instead moved to defend the militants and their sanctuaries rather than dismantling the infrastructure. The issue, Pakistan has argued, was not confined to TTP.
UN assessments have continued to document the presence of several other militant organisations in Afghanistan, including al Qaeda, the East Turkestan Islamic Movement (ETIM) and Islamic State-Khorasan, reinforcing concerns about the broader militant ecosystem operating from Afghan territory.
Also Read : One soldier martyred, 12 terrorists killed as security forces foil infiltration attempt in Kurram: ISPR
Pakistani officials say the continued presence of these groups, combined with training facilities, cross-border infiltration and access to sophisticated weapons, demonstrates that Afghanistan remains an important base for terrorist activity affecting Pakistan.
Pakistan's position, according to officials, remains that Kabul must take concrete steps to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries, eliminate training infrastructure, prevent cross-border infiltration and ensure that Afghan territory is not used for attacks against Pakistan.
The government has maintained that the issue was fundamentally one of Pakistan's national security and that continued attacks from Afghan soil cannot be addressed through denials alone.
Pakistan says it expected the Taliban regime to fulfil its commitments by taking verifiable action against terrorist groups operating from its territory rather than defending or denying their presence.

title: Hitler s historic teahouse goes up in flames in Germany  arson suspected

content:
Police arrest man after fire engulfs Eagle's Nest, but his possible involvement remains unclear
Adolf Hitler's historic teahouse, known as the Eagle's Nest, went up in flames Friday evening in southern Germany, with police suspecting arson and arresting a man, local media reported Saturday.
Emergency services were alerted shortly after 9pm local time (1900GMT), prompting a major firefighting operation, German newspaper BILD reported.
The building, officially known as the Kehlsteinhaus, was already engulfed in flames when firefighters and police arrived, according to police. A police spokesperson told the newspaper that officers suspected arson.
Police said officers responding to the fire encountered a motorcyclist traveling in the opposite direction. The officers alerted firefighters before stopping and arresting the man, according to police.
Read: Hitler's birthplace begins new life as a police station
Authorities have yet to determine whether the arrested man was involved in starting the fire, while the cause of the blaze remains under investigation.
No injuries were reported, and initial findings indicated that nobody was inside the building when the fire broke out.
Firefighters continued battling the blaze late Friday, while the extent of the damage remained unclear.
The Kehlsteinhaus was built in 1937-38 as a representative teahouse for Nazi leader Adolf Hitler at an altitude of 1,834 metres (6,017 feet) above sea level. The building was intended to host foreign dignitaries and serve as a political reception venue away from public view.

Scarlet Rose Stallone says working alongside her father has strengthened their relationship and mutual respect
Sylvester Stallone has openly defended casting his daughter, Scarlet Rose Stallone, in Tulsa King , acknowledging that family connections helped her secure a role in the Paramount+ crime drama.
In an interview with USA Today , the actor addressed criticism over Scarlet’s casting and argued that parents naturally want to give their children opportunities.

Authorities close 24 metro stations in capital as police, trade unions disagree over demonstration route
Paris police remained on alert Saturday over possible unrest in the French capital, with a police spokesperson warning that "the threat exists" following violent incidents last week.
Speaking to French broadcaster BFMTV , Paris Police Prefecture spokesperson Helene Denechere said authorities were taking the threat seriously and closely assessing the security situation ahead of planned demonstrations.
"The threat exists, it is being taken into consideration. Very serious acts were committed on Saturday, of a scale and violence that was underestimated. Today, it is being assessed," Denechere said.

She acknowledged that authorities had underestimated the scale of the mobilisation and the severity of the violence during demonstrations on October 17.
Denechere also said police have seized dangerous objects, including fireworks mortars, during security checks across the Ile-de-France region ahead of the protests.
Paris police and trade unions remained at odds over the route of Saturday's demonstration in the capital.
The police prefecture on Friday banned a previously agreed route between Place de la Bastille and Place de la Nation. Instead, authorities proposed an alternative route between Porte d'Italie and Porte de Vincennes via the Boulevards des Marechaux, according to a police decree.

The decree authorised the demonstration to take place from 1pm local time (1100GMT) to 7pm.

Paris public transport operator RATP said 24 metro stations were ordered closed from 9am Saturday at the request of police, citing security concerns.
Demonstrations were also authorised in eight major French cities, including Lille, Strasbourg, Mulhouse, Grenoble, Marseille, Toulouse and Amiens. In Marseille, law enforcement officers were deployed around the city's Old Port ahead of the demonstration.

title: FIFA Under 15 World Cup and Festival kicks off in Baku
description: Pakistan to face Gambia as 189 nations feature in inaugural tournament
content:
Pakistan to face Gambia as 189 nations feature in inaugural tournament
The inaugural FIFA Under-15 World Cup and Festival kicks off in Baku, Azerbaijan, on Saturday (today), bringing together teams representing 189 member associations for a week-long international youth football competition.
Pakistan will also face Gambia on the opening day as the tournament provides young players from around the world with opportunities to compete internationally and gain experience against teams from different footballing backgrounds.
The tournament runs until October 30, with more than 3,000 players, coaches and officials expected to take part, according to FIFA. Matches will be staged primarily at the purpose-built Hovsan Competition Complex, while the finals will be held at Baku's Crystal Hall.
The competition will use an eight-a-side format, with matches consisting of two 20-minute halves. Players born in 2011 or 2012 are eligible to participate.
Nearly 1,000 matches are scheduled across the tournament, with up to 20 fixtures taking place simultaneously on multiple pitches.
Teams will first compete in a qualification stage before being placed into six performance tiers for the second phase, based on their results. All participating teams will continue playing through to the final day, with winners crowned in each tier. The winner of Tier A will be named FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival champion.
FIFA introduced the competition following a decision by its council in December 2025, aiming to expand access to international football for all 211 member associations, regardless of their size or footballing tradition.
The inaugural edition features boys' teams, while the 2027 tournament is planned to include girls' teams. From 2028, FIFA intends to invite member associations to enter both boys' and girls' U-15 teams in separate competitions.

content:
Writes to relevant departments to nominate representatives from the ISI, IB, Pakistan Rangers (Sindh) and NCCIA
The Sindh government on Saturday constituted a Joint Investigation Team (JIT) to investigate the death of Mir Raza Ali, appointing Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) West Zone Karachi Irfan Ali Baloch as its convener, whose killing was initially treated by police as suicide but was later ruled a murder by the commission.
Raza, a graduate who ran a waffle-making business under the banner Wafflix, went missing from his PECHS residence in the early hours of July 28. Later, his body was found within the jurisdiction of Gulistan-e-Johar Police Station. A post-mortem was conducted at Jinnah Hospital, and the body was buried the same day.
Police initially opined the death to be a suicide. The family contested this, claiming the body bore visible torture marks. The commission recorded that the police surgeon, in early August, pointed out anomalies in the first post-mortem report — the very document police had relied upon for their suicide theory. The body was exhumed on August 8, initial findings were shared on August 8–9, and the final official report, issued around August 31, confirmed the cause of death as "a perforating firearm injury from the back, ruling out suicide".
The JIT would include representatives of the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Intelligence Bureau (IB), Sindh Rangers and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA).
The Sindh Home Department had written to the relevant agencies, seeking the names, designations and contact details of their nominated officers within seven days.
The federal Interior Ministry had also been asked to nominate a senior Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) officer of Grade 20 or above for the JIT. The ISI representative was required to be at least a Grade 18 officer.
Separately, the Sindh government had initiated measures to implement the recommendations of the judicial inquiry commission that examined the circumstances surrounding Raza’s death and identified alleged shortcomings in the police investigation.
Inquiry into 13 police officers and personnel
Additional Inspector General of Police (IGP) counter-terrorism department (CTD) Zulfiqar Ali Larik was appointed head of a one-member committee tasked with reviewing the performance of 13 police officers and personnel named in the judicial inquiry report. DIG West Zone Baloch would assist the committee.
The committee would examine the officials’ conduct, performance and leadership capabilities and submit its findings and recommendations regarding each officer to the Sindh IGP.
The judicial commission recommended further investigation into Inspector Ghaus's role in the case, particularly in connection with the alleged burning of the crime scene.
The committee would also investigate allegations that Station House Officer (SHO) Kamran Qureshi had facilitated the destruction of evidence.
Read: Judicial commission grills doctor over errors in Mir Raza's first post-mortem report, calls it 'criminal negligence'
SHO Ferozabad Adeel Afzal and Sub-Inspector Shabbir Laghari had been recommended for suspension and disciplinary proceedings. SHO Kamran Qureshi and Inspector Ghaus had also been suspended, with disciplinary action initiated against them.
The inquiry committee would examine possible violations of Sections 201, 166(2) and 218 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) in connection with the conduct of police officials.
DIG West Zone Baloch and DIG Special Branch Naeem Ahmed Sheikh would also be part of the inquiry committee.
The Sindh government had decided to communicate the judicial commission’s observations to DIG Amir Farooqi and DIG Farrukh Lanjar.
Arrangements would be made for the training of the investigation team headed by Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Samiullah Somroo, while Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Siraj Lashari and Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Nida Junaid would be asked to explain their conduct.
SSP Zubair Nazir Sheikh and Superintendent of Police (SP) Usman Suduzai would also be informed of the commission’s observations.
However, no further action would be taken against Additional Inspector General of Police (AIG) Karachi Azad Khan.
The commission had recommended acknowledging the performance of Head Muharrar Zeeshan and Police Constable Muhammad Arif and providing them with further training.
The cabinet’s subcommittee had directed the IGP to take action in line with the judicial commission’s recommendations.
Inquiry into health officials and medico-legal procedures
The Sindh government had also decided to initiate an inquiry against Special Secretary Health Shehryar Memon in connection with the implementation of the judicial commission’s recommendations.
A request had been sent to the chief secretary to arrange an inquiry by a senior officer.
The commission had pointed to an alleged lack of leadership and supervision on the part of Health Secretary Tahir Sangi. Its observations would be conveyed to him through the chief secretary.
On the commission’s recommendation, the Sindh Health Department had been directed to formulate rules under the medico-legal framework.
The Sindh Home Department had instructed the health secretary to suspend Dr Osama Sheikh and initiate proceedings against him under the applicable CND rules. Dr Sheikh would also be sent for further training in accordance with the judicial commission’s recommendations.
Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah had approved the recommendations of the cabinet’s subcommittee.
A case that began with a missing young man and a police theory of suicide has exposed what a judicial commission has described as a deeply flawed investigation, compromised evidence and a breakdown of public trust so severe that even the identification of the actual killer may not convince the public.
The single-member Judicial Commission probing the death of 25-year-old Raza has recommended a joint investigation team (JIT), led by DIG Irfan Baloch and comprising senior representatives of the ISI, IB, Pakistan Rangers (Sindh) and the NCCIA, to establish the truth.
Read more: Mir Raza case: Commission says Dr Usama targeted Dr Summaiya with smear campaign
In a scathing assessment, the commission termed the police investigation an "epic failure", warning that the trust deficit between the Sindh police and society had become "nearly unrectifiable" in this case.
Headed by Sindh High Court Judge Justice Omar Sial, the commission submitted its report to the provincial chief minister on October 15, 2026.
The commission concluded that the available medical and physical evidence was incompatible with suicide. "The bullet trajectory, the unusual location of the wound for a self-inflicted injury, the absence of blood, the state of the body, the principles of medical jurisprudence, acid burns and the anesthesia detected in the blood, all clearly excluded suicide as the cause of death. It was a murder," the report stated.
The commission found that the police had failed in their most basic responsibility: establishing the truth. It said the suicide hypothesis rested on a handful of unconfirmed text messages, selectively obtained video footage and a preliminary post-mortem report that did not itself conclude that the death was a suicide.
The report also pointed to contradictions between the first and second reports prepared by Dr Osama Shaikh, further weakening the police position.
Describing the investigation as "a rudderless ship, not aware of its destination", the commission said the possibility of an active cover-up in the initial stages "cannot be conclusively ruled out".
The commission described the change in medical board as a "highly irregular, inexplicable, legally flawed overreach", attributing it to officials at the upper levels of the Sindh Health Secretariat, particularly the secretary and special secretary.
It further observed that the director-general of health services had "looked the other way", despite being aware that he lacked the legal authority to constitute such a board. "The two gentlemen who directed the change in the Board could not give a cogent reason for the abrupt change," the report stated.
With a significant portion of the physical evidence compromised, the commission said the case had reached a critical juncture at which a conventional police investigation was unlikely to restore public confidence.
It warned that even an accurate conclusion or the apprehension of the actual culprit might not be accepted by the public because of the severe breakdown in trust..
The commission also called on the police to acknowledge their operational failures, apologise transparently and initiate formal inquiries against the officers responsible.

title: Israel launches major West Bank operation after soldiers killed
description: Netanyahu orders lockdown in West Bank  says considering extensive IDF operation in Judea and Samaria
content:
Netanyahu orders lockdown in West Bank, says considering extensive IDF operation in Judea and Samaria
Israel's military launched an operation in the occupied West Bank on Friday it said would last several days and include searches and building demolitions, after gunmen killed two soldiers days ahead of Israeli elections in which security has been a key focus.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is locked in a tight race to keep his job in Tuesday's vote, having campaigned on promises to keep Israelis safe, and he and his right-wing allies visited the scene of the attack.
Security forces were searching targets and questioning suspects to "locate and dismantle terrorist infrastructure" in the Hebron area from they said the attackers had emerged, according to a joint statement from the Israeli military and Shin Bet domestic security agency.
Forces were also "demolishing reillegal structus that could pose a security threat at the site of the encounter", they said, adding that "counterterrorism operations" were underway at dozens of locations. The operation "is expected to continue for several days," the statement, released late on Friday, said.
Read: 'Apartheid automation': How Israel uses AI to monitor Palestinian land, movement and lives
Hamas, without claiming responsibility, praised Friday's fatal attack on two Israeli soldiers as a "heroic operation" and called on supporters to carry out more.
A Hebron-based AFP photographer heading to another assignment witnessed the gun battle break out at the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint between the soldiers and two Palestinian men armed with a handgun and an automatic rifle. Israeli forces eventually shot dead the attackers.
Netanyahu credited the soldiers with having "prevented what could have been a major attack", and ordered a lockdown in the West Bank.
Visiting Hebron, the premier said he and Defence Minister Israel Katz were "considering a very extensive IDF operation in Judea and Samaria, such as has not been carried out since" the 1967 war. The first step would see Israeli forces "enter the neighbourhood from which the terrorists came, evacuate the residents, go from house to house, and destroy the terrorist infrastructure," he said.
The military would apply a model previously used in refugee camps in the northern West Bank, he said, the scene of a large-scale operation launched in January 2025 that the United Nations said forcibly displaced thousands.
Israeli rights group B'Tselem called for urgent international pressure to prevent Israel from "plans for collective punishment and acts that could constitute war crimes ".
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres through a spokesman voiced concern over Israeli closures that affect Palestinian livelihoods and called for a halt to violence on all sides.
Far-right Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who also holds a position within the defence ministry, called for a large-scale military offensive in the West Bank "exactly like in Gaza". He said authorities were "sending an unequivocal message to our enemies: if you mess with the Jews, you will pay a very painful price."
National Security Minister and far-right firebrand Itamar Ben Gvir said the Ramallah-based "Palestinian Authority must be dismantled". "It is impossible for there to be an authority within Judea and Samaria that incites murder, calls for murder, and works for murder," he told reporters.
No evidence suggests that the Palestinian Authority - which exercises limited self-rule in parts of the West Bank - was connected to Friday's attack.
Both Ben Gvir and Smotrich are especially vocal champions of Israeli settlements in the West Bank, which have proliferated under Netanyahu's government but are illegal under international law.
Netanyahu vowed to "pursue Hamas" everywhere, adding: "You have no place to hide."
Read More: More than 20 US senators introduce privileged resolution seeking report on West Bank violence
Israel vowed to obliterate the group in the wake of the October 7, 2023 attack that resulted in 1,221 deaths, according to an AFP tally from official Israeli figures.
Gadi Eisenkot, the former army chief who is Netanyahu's top rival in the upcoming vote, said he was praying for soldiers wounded in Friday's shooting.
The operation comes as tensions soar in the West Bank, including over attacks by extremist Israeli settlers against Palestinian olive harvesters .
According to an AFP tally based on data from the Palestinian health ministry, Israeli forces and settlers have killed 1,117 Palestinians in the territory since the start of the Gaza war in October 2023. Israeli figures show at least 51 Israelis have been killed in Palestinian attacks or during Israeli military operations during the same period.

title: Weeks  not days  in Kompany recovery  Bayern
description: Club confirms that their head coach is in stable condition
content:
Club confirms that their head coach is in stable condition
Bayern Munich expect coach Vincent Kompany to miss an extended period as he continues his hospital treatment for a virus after collapsing on the training pitch on Friday.
Speaking at a press conference on Saturday, Bayern sporting director Max Eberl confirmed Kompany was still hospitalised in a "stable" condition.
Kompany's English assistant coach Aaron Danks will replace the 40-year-old for Sunday's Bundesliga match at Freiburg.
Eberl told reporters "examinations were continuing" to determine the nature of the former Manchester City and Belgium captain's condition, with a recovery timeframe yet to be determined.
"Vinnie will be given all the time he needs. We're not starting to put together any timeframes.
"We need to firstly figure out what it is and then we'll discuss calmly what recovery time is to be. We won't be talking about days, but weeks. We need to all be clear on that."
Taking Saturday's press conference in Kompany's absence, Danks said he had spoken with the former centre-back briefly on Friday but only to wish him well.
"I explained to him that we wouldn't be having no football conversations. It was just checking in on his health and making sure he's OK.
"All the football operations are in our hands and we'll work together as a team to keep the club moving forward."
Bayern's second team's game was postponed yesterday after Kompany's collapse but Eberl said the club did not consider trying to postpone Sunday's Bundesliga game.
"I think the greatest joy for Vinnie would be for us to play well tomorrow and, ideally, get a positive result," Eberl said.
"That would probably be one of the best things we could do to help him recover."
Danks confirmed Germany captain Joshua Kimmich, who has been on bereavement leave since Tuesday, would also miss Sunday's game.
Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday's home clash with Arsenal despite missing the pre-match press conference due to the virus.
Speaking after the Arsenal game, Kompany said his body reacted after he tried to push through the illness.
"I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn't listen to my body -- and then at some point my body just said, 'enough is enough!'"
The defending champions sit on top of the Bundesliga table ahead of Sunday's game, one point above Freiburg.
Their next Champions League match is on November 3 in Madrid against Atletico.

title: Marc Marquez wins Australian sprint
description: Victory puts him 10 points clear of fellow Spaniard Martin in the standings
content:
Victory puts him 10 points clear of fellow Spaniard Martin in the standings
Marc Marquez stormed home first from pole in the Australian MotoGP sprint race on Saturday to seize control of the world championship from Jorge Martin who crashed out challenging him for the lead.
The reigning seven-time world champion, who dominated qualifying, had too much power in his Ducati to surge to the chequered flag ahead of his brother Alex in the 13-lap contest.
Victory put him 10 points clear of fellow Spaniard Martin in the standings ahead of the final MotoGP ever around the waterfront Phillip Island circuit on Sunday.
Martin, who started from fourth under dark clouds but with the rain staying away, took the lead on lap three in a ding-dong battle with his rival.
But he lost control on lap eight while challenging for the lead once again to put a massive dent in his championship ambitions.
"It was a tight battle," said Marquez. "Of course, I gave everything. I was aggressive, and he (Martin) was faster than me.
"But just I tried to defend in the best way possible. Both of us we are riding to the limit. Both of us, we deserve the victory because we are pushing a lot.
His brother Alex, who started second, filled an all-Ducati podium with Fabio Di Giannantonio.
Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi, who won the MotoGP last week in Indonesia, was fourth to remain third in the standings, 50 points behind Marquez.
Pedro Acosta (KTM) came fifth and Ai Ogura (Aprilia) sixth.
Marc Marquez held the line to be first at the opening corner with Martin up to second with Johann Zarco third and it stayed that way at the end of lap one.
Martin was pressing hard and he took the lead on lap three as the race became a dogfight between the two championship leaders as they pulled clear of the field.
A big mistake from Martin running wide on lap five opened the door again for Marquez, with the lead changing hands several times as they battled for supremacy.
But Martin pushed too much and sensationally lost control on lap eight, skidding out to end his race.
Phillip Island has been a staple on the calendar since 1997 but the Australian race is moving next year to a street circuit in Adelaide.

title: Dolly Parton   s estate appoints niece Danielle Parton after nephew   s dismissal
description: Danielle Parton is a military veteran  airline pilot and entrepreneur who founded moonshine brand Shine Girl
content:
Danielle Parton is a military veteran, airline pilot and entrepreneur who founded moonshine brand Shine Girl
Dolly Parton’s estate has named her niece Danielle Parton as its official brand ambassador, announcing the appointment weeks after the dismissal of the country legend’s nephew, Bryan Seaver, amid a legal dispute involving alleged threats.
The estate described Danielle, 50, as a commercial airline pilot, military veteran and entrepreneur whose work ethic and independent spirit reflect qualities associated with her famous aunt. The appointment is intended to celebrate Dolly’s legacy and connect with fans around the world.
The announcement came in an Instagram Reel featuring Dolly introducing Danielle to the public. In the video, Danielle reflected on her relationship with her aunt, whom she affectionately called “Aunt Granny”, and the lessons she said she had carried throughout her life.
Danielle explained that her career had taken her into aviation and military service. She served in the National Guard for 20 years before building a career as a pilot. She also established Shine Girl, a moonshine business in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, near Dollywood. The company draws on the Parton family’s history with moonshine while giving the tradition a contemporary identity.
Speaking about her aunt’s legacy, Danielle said losing Dolly had changed her perspective and made her think more deeply about the stories, values and lessons passed down through the family. She said she hoped to honour those principles without attempting to replace her aunt.
“I would never try to speak for Dolly,” Danielle said, explaining that she wanted to share the woman she knew and support the work that brought joy to others.
The appointment follows the September dismissal of Bryan Seaver, the son of Dolly’s sister Cassie Parton, from his position as head of security for the estate.
A lawsuit filed by Dolly’s manager, Danny Nozell, accused Seaver of threatening the estate and people connected to the singer’s legacy. The company managing Dolly’s business interests also obtained a temporary restraining order against him.
Seaver has disputed the allegations, telling ABC News that the order was “spurious and simply a publicity stunt”. The claims remain disputed, and the legal conflict has drawn attention to the management of Dolly’s legacy.

title: Leclerc tops times in practice
description: 29 year old finishes ahead of Mercedes  championship leader Kimi Antonelli
content:
29-year-old finishes ahead of Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli
Charles Leclerc completed a double top for Ferrari on Friday when he led the times ahead of Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli in second practice for this weekend's United States Grand Prix.
The 29-year-old Monegasque father-to-be, who won in Austin two years ago, clocked a best lap in one minute and 35.291 seconds to outpace the 20-year-old Italian by 0.042 seconds with four-time champion Max Verstappen of Red Bull 0.189 seconds adrift in third.
Leclerc, whose wife Alexandra Saint Mieux is expecting their first child, had earlier topped opening practice ahead of Verstappen and drove like a man on a mission throughout the day.
Antonelli could clinch the drivers' title to become Formula One's youngest champion -- and Italy's first since Alberto Ascari for Ferrari in 1953 -- this weekend if he wins and his main rivals are unable to stay within reach of his points total.
Team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton need to finish in the top eight and top four respectively to keep their title hopes alive if Antonelli wins.
Hamilton was fourth for Ferrari, six-tenths off the pace, with Russell fifth ahead of Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and the McLarens of world champion Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Isack Hadjar was ninth in the second Red Bull and Oliver Bearman 10th for Haas.
Verstappen, winner of the last two races, showed he meant business as soon as the pitlane opened for FP2 by accelerating after the two Racing Bulls and, unexpectedly, surging past Lawson at Turn One, much to the New Zealander's surprise.
He swiftly posted a lap in 1:36.581 to go top ahead of Russel, with Antonelli grumbling about his seat 'moving around like crazy', a distraction that required an early stop in the pits.
Three drivers had grid penalties confirmed between the sessions: five places for Racing Bulls' rookie Arvid Lindblad, ten for Alpine's Franco Colapinto and 20 for Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto, all for exceeding the limits on taking new power unit components.
Norris, on hards, then went top briefly before Russell beat his time but then dropped to second as Verstappen took a tow from team-mate Hadjar to clock 1:35.934 and go clear by a tenth.
Given his need to win, Antonelli's absence for repairs was a setback as his rivals, notably Verstappen and Russell, capitalised before he rejoined the fray -- and immediately took third behind them. It was a sign of his pure talent and speed.
By this time, Russell had experienced a curious skirmish with Leclerc which resulted in a black-and-white flag warning him for driving standards. It appeared he had forced the Ferrari driver off track.
After a busy half hour, most switched to soft tyres for some qualifying simulation runs that began with Russell going top before Verstappen and then Leclerc took control, the Ferrari clocking 1:35.291.
To confirm Ferrari's form, Hamilton went third, albeit six-tenths adrift of his team-mate, until demoted a place by the hasty Antonelli grabbing second, just 0.042 off Leclerc's time.

title: Pakistan calls for equitable  non discriminatory civil nuclear cooperation at UN
description: At UN  Pakistan pushes for equitable civil nuclear cooperation  stresses safety and energy security
content:
All countries must retain their inalienable right to utilise nuclear energy for peaceful purposes: Ambassador Raza
Pakistan on Saturday underscored the fundamental importance of equitable, non-discriminatory civil nuclear cooperation to help secure its national energy future at the United Nations.
“Efforts to prevent the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction must not impede international cooperation in the peaceful uses of dual-use technologies, which is vital for the economic development of the Global South,” the remarks were made by Counsellor at Pakistan's Permanent Mission to the UN, Syed Atif Raza, while speaking during the UN General Assembly Plenary discussion on the report of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA).
Raza also highlighted that Pakistan was a party to the principal international instruments of nuclear safety and security.
“All countries must retain their inalienable right to utilise nuclear energy for peaceful purposes, consistent with their respective non-proliferation and international legal obligations,” the Pakistani delegate said.
Read: IAEA mission reviews nuclear security
Pakistan, he said, maintained that compliance or safety issues should be resolved through technical bodies like the IAEA without political bias.
“Outstanding situations must be addressed and resolved through dialogue and diplomacy, in a manner that upholds the non-proliferation regime while ensuring regional and international peace and security,” Raza said.
“Countries should refrain from irresponsible and destabilising rhetoric, actions, and postures that could escalate tensions and increase the risk of conflict.”
Pakistan, he said, operates six nuclear power reactors – all under IAEA safeguards, supplying about 20 per cent of the national energy needs and one-third of low-carbon power generation.
“We support the agency’s work in peaceful applications of nuclear science and technology and look forward to the successful implementation of IAEA’s major initiatives.”
#PakistanAtUNGA At UNGA, Pakistan Calls for Equitable Access to Peaceful Nuclear Technology, Urges Resolution of Outstanding Issues through dialogue and diplomacy - Our Press Release pic.twitter.com/1wUFsHS5vK
At the outset, Rafael Mariano Grossi, the IAEA Director-General, briefed the General Assembly on Syria, Iran and Ukraine, noting that the agency had gained access to previously restricted facilities in Syria after nearly two decades.
“All the nuclear material in Syria is now under monitoring and verification”, he said, describing this as a major step towards Damascus’ reintegration into the international community.
“Discreet diplomacy, perseverance, factual, objective, technical work also pay off”, he added.
On Iran, the IAEA chief said the agency had completed most of the technical preparations needed to verify its nuclear activities, expressing hope that negotiations between Tehran and Washington would produce an agreement.
“There will not be a lasting, stable solution without a diplomatic agreement”, he stressed, adding: “For a diplomatic agreement to happen, we need the verification.”
On Ukraine, he warned of continuing nuclear safety risks at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, where the IAEA has maintained a presence for nearly five years. The agency recently negotiated its eighth localised ceasefire between the Russian Federation and Ukraine, allowing essential repairs to prevent a nuclear accident.
Read More: Repair work begins on Ukrainian nuclear plant's power lines
Grossi also highlighted the Agency’s independent monitoring of treated water discharges from Japan’s Fukushima nuclear power plant. Turning to the peaceful uses of nuclear technology, he stressed the need to expand access to nuclear energy in developing countries and welcomed the World Bank’s decision to finance nuclear projects as a “watershed” moment.

title: Pakistan Railways declares three month emergency amid rising train accidents
description: Officers are also directed to visit the field and supervise train operations on Sundays
content:
Railways recorded more than 55 accidents involving passenger and freight trains since January 1
Pakistan Railways (PR) has imposed an emergency across the department on the instructions of Railways Minister Hanif Abbasi to ensure safe train operations.
According to a statement issued by PR headquarters in Lahore on Saturday, all leave for field officers had been cancelled for three months.
"Officers have also been directed to visit the field and supervise train operations on Sundays. Railway officers have been required to travel by train when visiting other cities for official duties," it said.
The statement further added that chief engineers of the civil and mechanical departments would submit daily reports to the ministry on their respective areas of responsibility, while daily reports had also been sought from the head of safety.
The emergency measures will remain in force until December 31.
“We will provide passengers with the safest possible travel in line with the prime minister’s vision,” Abbasi said.
Railways log over 55 accidents this year
On October 17 , Abbasi visited the Steel and Carriage Shops in Mughalpura, where he inspected production facilities and directed officials to ensure quality standards in the manufacturing of railway components.
During his visit to the Mughalpura Steel Shop, the minister inspected the electric arc furnace and reviewed the spectro laboratory responsible for testing parts manufactured in the furnace.
Railways recorded more than 55 accidents involving passenger and freight trains since January 1, raising concerns over railway safety, maintenance standards and the effectiveness of measures announced to prevent mishaps.
The accidents have reportedly left several people dead and dozens injured, while also causing millions of rupees in damage to railway infrastructure. Repeated incidents have fuelled fear among passengers, some of whom say travelling by train remains a necessity despite the risks.
Passengers have questioned how they can avoid railway travel when it remains an essential mode of transport for them. The frequency of accidents has also raised questions about the implementation of safety measures under the directions of the railways minister.
Read: PR to finally begin ML-1 work this year
Despite the minister's strict instructions, accidents have continued to occur, while railway officials have reportedly continued to provide reassuring assessments of the situation. The recurring incidents have placed the department's safety and maintenance arrangements under scrutiny.
According to railway sources, passenger and freight trains have been involved in more than 55 accidents of varying severity since the beginning of the year. The Yusufwala coal train has reportedly been involved in several accidents.
On August 27, 10 wagons of a freight train derailed near Khanpur. On the same day, the engine and two coaches of the Rawal Express went off the tracks near Kala Gujran.
On September 27, the Yusufwala coal train met with an accident near Khairpur.
Earlier, on September 9, three wagons of a coal-laden freight train derailed at Kotri yard. On September 2, the power van of the Khyber Mail derailed near Sanjani.
Another coal train accident occurred on September 6, when seven wagons went off the tracks. These incidents add to a series of mishaps involving freight operations, with railway sources identifying the Sukkur, Karachi and Multan divisions among the areas where most train accidents have occurred.
On May 24, a shuttle train in Quetta was targeted in an act of sabotage, damaging three coaches. The Rahman Baba Express also suffered a major accident in the Multan division, further highlighting the range of incidents affecting railway operations.

title: Bayern   s Kompany in hospital
description: Coach collapses during a training session with FC Bayern s reserve team
content:
Coach collapses during a training session with FC Bayern's reserve team
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany was taken to hospital by an emergency medical team on Friday after collapsing during training, the club said.
"Vincent Kompany had to seek medical attention on Friday after collapsing during a training session with FC Bayern's reserve team," Bayern said on their website.
"Kompany is undergoing thorough examinations at the hospital and will remain under medical care."
Kompany, the 40-year-old former Manchester City defender, missed training and a press conference on Tuesday ahead of Bayern's Champions League draw against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena.
"I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn't listen to my body -- and then at some point my body just said, 'enough is enough!'" Kompany said after the Arsenal game.
On Friday, Bayern's sporting director Max Eberl said the health of their coach "is our top priority".
"We at FC Bayern will do everything we can to ensure he recovers quickly. Vinnie is receiving all the necessary medical care and support, as well as all the time he needs. His coaching staff, whom we trust completely, will take over his duties."
English assistant coach Aaron Danks took training and handled the press conference ahead of the Arsenal game.
"It affected his legs at times; he was experiencing some pain. It's just a virus. He needs rest," Danks said on Tuesday.
"The most important thing we're encouraging him to do right now is to rest and take as much time as he needs—no matter how long that may be."
Bundesliga leaders Bayern visit Freiburg, who are third in the table, on Saturday.
Their next Champions League match is on November 3 in Madrid against Atletico.
The Spanish club posted their best wishes on social media.
"We wish you a speedy recovery. We hope to see you here in Madrid, on the bench, in a few days," wrote the Spanish club adding a heart emoji.
Kompany, a centre back, started his career with Anderlecht in his native Brussels. He moved to Hamburg and then to Manchester City as one of the club's last signings before the Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008.
He went on to play 360 games for the club, where he was also captain for eight season as the team became the dominant force in English football.
He played 89 times for Belgium and finished his playing career back at Anderlecht in 2019 where he was player-coach in the first of his three seasons in charge
He took over at Burnley in 2022, leading them to a Championship title in 2023 but the club was relegated the next season with their lowest ever points total.
Bayern, who had just endured a trophyless season and had been unable to persuade Thomas Tuchel to stay, sprung a surprise by paying Burnley to sign Kompany as manager in 2024.
He led the club two the Bundesliga title each of his first two seasons and to a German Cup in 2026. After six games, Bayern lead the table this season on goal difference. In 74 Bundesliga games under Kompany, Bayern have won 57 and lost three.

title: Pakistan condemns  heinous terrorist attack  on church in Jordan
description: Reaffirms solidarity with Jordan in fight against terrorism day after at least seven killed  34 injured in attack
content:
Reaffirms solidarity with Jordan in fight against terrorism day after at least seven killed, 34 injured in attack
Pakistan on Saturday strongly condemned "the heinous terrorist attack" at a funeral procession in a church in Jordan's Karak governorate, which resulted in "the loss of several precious lives, with many injured," the Foreign Office (FO) said in a statement.
A day earlier, seven people were killed and 34 injured when gunmen opened fire during a funeral at Hamoud Church in Jordan's Karak governorate, in a rare attack on the country's Christian minority.
"Pakistan extends its heartfelt condolences to the government and the people of the brotherly Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan," the FO said. It particularly extended Pakistan's condolences to the bereaved families, "on the loss of their loved ones."

Rights group says two children killed, three people wounded, four abducted in Houthi attacks in Taiz over 24 hours
A Saudi-led ​coalition fighting Yemen's ‌Houthis said it destroyed two ballistic missiles fired ​by the ​group towards Taif and Yanbu on Saturday, as fighting between the sides continued.
Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence on Saturday briefly issued alerts warning of potential danger in Taif and Yanbu, as well as the holy city of Makkah and its second-largest city Jeddah.
