title: PHC orders police to recover missing child
description: PHC orders police to recover missing child
content:
Chief Justice Atiq Shah refuses further time, summons IGP after five-month delay
The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Friday directed police to recover a child missing from Faqirabad for the past five months and produce him before the court by next Monday.
Chief Justice SM Atiq Shah observed that despite the passage of five months, police had failed to recover the child and no further time could be granted.
During the hearing of a petition seeking the child's recovery, the Chief Justice ordered the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General of Police to appear in person. On the subsequent hearing, Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Peshawar Dr Mian Saeed and the Advocate General appeared in court.
The petitioner told the court that her son had been missing for five months and that a ransom demand had been made through a phone call. Police informed the court that the caller had been traced through call data, but the child was not found in his custody, preventing recovery so far.
The Advocate General suggested the possibility that the child might have run away from home. The Chief Justice rejected the suggestion, stating that the mother had approached the court for her child's recovery and it was the duty of the relevant authorities to find him. "The court is not concerned with how the child is recovered; the authorities must find him," he remarked.
CCPO Peshawar assured the court that every possible effort would be made for the child's early recovery but requested more time. The Chief Justice noted that had the concerned Station House Officer made timely efforts, the child would already have been recovered. He refused any further extension and ordered the child's production in court by next Monday.
The Advocate General also informed the court that contact had been made with the Advocate General of Punjab to seek cooperation in the recovery efforts. The hearing was adjourned until next Monday.

Adviser on Information Samar Haroon Bilour and designated districts' Adviser on Information Mahmood Jan Babar were also present.
Describing the Apex Committee meeting as a significant day in the province's history, the governor said officials had given detailed briefings on security and development matters. The Additional Chief Secretary overseeing the 12 designated districts had also presented the proposed plan.

Regarding problems related to gas and wheat, Kundi said the prime minister had directed the secretary of food to convene a meeting soon. An inquiry had also been initiated into the wheat issue at the Azakhel wheat warehouse.
The governor announced a zero-tolerance policy towards corruption, stressing that officials must fulfil their responsibilities. Those failing to deliver would have to relinquish their positions, he added.
Kundi alleged that the province had fallen behind over the past 13 years but said efforts would now be made to put it firmly on the path of development. He declared that there would be no compromise on maintaining peace and order, describing the fight against terrorism as the government's foremost priority.
He said improved security would attract domestic and foreign investors, generate employment opportunities and strengthen the provincial economy. Public-private partnerships would also be encouraged to accelerate development.
The governor said the province's rights would be pursued with the federal government through reasoned arguments. He had held meetings with leaders of the Awami National Party, Jamaat-e-Islami and Qaumi Watan Party, emphasising that all political parties must unite to secure the province's legitimate rights.

Zendaya will campaign for a best actress Oscar for playing Chani in 'Dune: Part Three', marking a major category shift
Zendaya is set to campaign for the best actress category at the Academy Awards for her role as Chani in Dune: Part Three , marking a change from the supporting actress category in which she was positioned for the franchise’s first two films.
According to multiple sources cited by Variety , the decision reflects Chani’s expanded role in the upcoming instalment, which is directed by Denis Villeneuve and serves as the final chapter of his science-fiction saga. Warner Bros. and representatives for Zendaya declined to comment on the reported campaign.
Dune: Part Three takes place nearly two decades after Paul Atreides, played by Timothée Chalamet, takes control of the Imperium. Paul has become a ruthless emperor and faces the consequences of his rule as old allies return, new threats emerge and a conspiracy develops. Chani is central to the unfolding mystery as the story explores the cost of power and the fate of those close to Paul.
The film also features Jason Momoa, Florence Pugh, Rebecca Ferguson, Anya Taylor-Joy, Robert Pattinson, Javier Bardem, Josh Brolin, Charlotte Rampling and Isaach de Bankolé. Warner Bros. is scheduled to release the film in cinemas and IMAX on December 18.
The reported Oscar campaign comes during a busy year for Zendaya. She is also expected to compete in the lead actress category for The Drama , a romantic dark comedy directed by Kristoffer Borgli and co-starring Robert Pattinson. For Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey , she will seek supporting actress recognition alongside Anne Hathaway, Samantha Morton and Charlize Theron.
Zendaya previously won two Emmy Awards for playing Rue in Euphoria and received a Golden Globe for the role in 2023. She also earned two Golden Globe nominations in 2025 for Challengers , as an actress and producer.
An Oscar nomination would be the actor’s first.

title: Punjab govt to pursue alleged gang rape case after Azerbaijani victim changes stance
description: Victim says earlier statement was made under pressure  seeks closure of alleged gang rape case
content:
Victim says earlier statement was made under pressure, seeks closure of alleged gang-rape case
Punjab Information Minister Azma Bukhari said on Friday that the provincial government would pursue the case involving the alleged gang rape of an Azerbaijani woman despite a video statement circulating on social media in which the victim said she had forgiven the suspect and did not want to pursue the case.
The minister’s statement came after a video of the victim, Diana, who was allegedly raped in Lahore earlier this year, circulated on social media in which she said her statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) had already been recorded before a judicial magistrate.
A video of the victim, apparently recorded on Oct 9, surfaced in which she could be seen saying that a suspect had neither assaulted her nor taken her mobile phone and belongings.
“I gave my earlier statement under pressure, and I do not want to pursue this case,” she said, requesting that the case be closed.
Later, in another video, Diana reiterated her statement, giving a clean chit to the suspect. She said she wanted to appear before the court to record her statement but was told that her life was in danger.
She further claimed that she had been forcibly sent out of Pakistan and was not allowed to express her view. She also said she wanted to forgive the other suspects and did not want to pursue the matter any further.
Speaking to a private television programme, Aaj Shahzaib Khanzada Kay Sath , Bukhari said Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz was particularly concerned about rape cases and would not allow anyone to relax until all the suspects were arrested and due process was followed.
Read : Azeri woman tells court she was 'threatened, sexually assaulted and pushed out of car'
Asked whether the Punjab government would pursue the case since the state could also pursue rape cases, she replied in the affirmative, saying the chief minister had categorically asked her to convey that she believed the state should be the complainant in cases involving crimes against women and children.
“The chief minister, as chief executive, stands with every victim and with the poor and vulnerable. Until and unless these powerful people are made an example of, such crimes cannot be eliminated,” she said.
Bukhari said the chief minister was prepared to approach the chief justice of Pakistan and the chief justice of the Lahore High Court with the information available to her.
“Whether it is a speedy trial, improving the laws or whatever is needed, she is ready to work on that,” she said, adding that CM Maryam would not allow “this hooliganism and culture of bullying” against women, children or vulnerable sections of society in Punjab.
The minister said the woman, the victim in the case, had, for one reason or another, changed her position, and the possibility of money being involved had also arisen.
However, she said the state would pursue the case because a co-suspect had already recorded a statement saying all the suspects were involved with him.
“Even if they retract this statement, it is not possible for them to get away,” she said, adding that the government would not allow anyone to take the law into their own hands.
Earlier today, CM Maryam alleged that the family of a suspect in the case had offered Rs15 million to Rs20m to the victim to withdraw her allegations, while the judge who granted bail to the suspect had also allegedly been bribed.
“It was revealed that the accused’s wealthy family allegedly offered Rs15m to Rs20m to the victim in exchange for withdrawing her allegations, despite her statement already having been recorded under Section 164,” Maryam said in a post on X.
In a recent rape case, it was revealed that the accused’s wealthy family allegedly offered 1.5–2 crore to the victim in exchange for withdrawing her allegations, despite her statement already having been recorded under Section 164. It was further alleged that the judge who…
She further alleged that the judge who granted bail to the accused had also been bribed.
“If these allegations are true, they raise deeply disturbing questions about the integrity of the justice system and the vulnerability of rape survivors to financial pressure and the misuse of power,” she said.
Maryam said she would continue to keep a close eye on such cases to ensure that “no rapist or perpetrator escapes justice simply because he has money, influence, or connections”.
“Justice must never be for sale, and no one should be above the law,” she said.
As the statements surfaced, Lahore police warned against attempts to influence the investigation into the alleged gang rape through videos circulating on social media, saying the woman’s statement under Section 164 of the CrPC had already been recorded before a judicial magistrate.
Lahore Deputy Inspector General (Investigation) Syed Zeeshan Raza said the woman had named three suspects in her judicial statement and that two arrested suspects had also acknowledged the alleged involvement of the third suspect.
He said the video statement appeared to be an attempt to influence the investigation, adding that the third suspect would be included in the investigation and the case would be completed on merit.

The case was registered at Defence C Police Station in September after the woman alleged that three men had sexually assaulted her at an apartment in a private housing society near Raiwind during the night between Sept 25 and 26.
According to the first information report, the woman had arrived in Lahore on a business trip and was allegedly taken to a cafe by two women, where three men joined them. She alleged that she was subsequently taken to an apartment, given an intoxicating drink and sexually assaulted.
The suspects allegedly left her near the airport and took her mobile phones and other belongings.
On Sept 28, the woman recorded her statement before a judicial magistrate at the Cantonment Courts. Police subsequently identified the suspects and pursued the investigation, with several people arrested in connection with the case.
The latest developments have also raised questions about the primary suspect’s legal status. A sessions court had extended his interim pre-arrest bail until Oct 27, but police subsequently arrested him outside the court premises.
His counsel reportedly challenged the arrest, maintaining that it had taken place despite the extension of bail.
The conflicting accounts are likely to remain central to the investigation.

The inquiry committee, headed by Sindh University of Business Administration and Economics (SIBA) Jamshoro Vice Chancellor Professor Dr Arbeela Bhutto, has been directed to submit its findings to the provincial minister within 30 days.
According to notifications issued by the Universities and Boards Department, the inquiry aims to establish the facts, determine responsibility and identify any officials or employees who may have been involved in the alleged irregularities. The suspension will remain in effect until completion of the inquiry and further orders from the competent authority.
The committee also includes Additional Secretary of the Universities and Boards Department Amir Fazal Owaisi and Mehran University of Engineering and Technology Jamshoro Registrar Dr Nasrullah Pirzada.
The committee will examine the Class XII annual examination results for 2026, with particular attention to position holders, candidates among the top 10, and students securing A-1 and A grades in the pre-medical and pre-engineering groups.

title: Sindh job reforms fail to curb merit complaints
description: Sindh job reforms fail to curb merit complaints
content:
Sindh Assembly, Prisons Department turn to private testing firm instead of government-run academic institution
Despite a series of reforms aimed at making government recruitment more transparent, complaints over merit-based hiring continue to dog Sindh's job system.
The government's efforts have struggled to deliver the promised change, largely because key measures have not been fully implemented. Some influential provincial institutions, including the Sindh Assembly and the Prisons Department, have themselves sidestepped the government's recruitment mechanism.
Rather than using the testing service of the government-run Sukkur IBA University, which was engaged by the provincial government to help ensure merit in BPS-5 to BPS-15 recruitment, the two institutions have hired a private testing company to conduct tests for their vacant positions.
It is worth noting that the system for providing government jobs in the province is divided into three categories. Recruitment to BPS-1 to BPS-4 positions is carried out at the district level. For BPS-5 to BPS-15 positions, a digital platform called the Sindh Job Portal was established in 2025.
All departments were directed to receive applications for their vacant positions through the platform, while candidates who secured at least 40 marks through the testing service of Sukkur IBA University were declared eligible for these positions. The third category comprises BPS-16 and above positions, which are filled through the Sindh Public Service Commission (SPSC).
Unfortunately, questions have been raised for some time over the transparency of recruitment in all three categories. Several young people who were declared unsuccessful in the SPSC examination held in 2024 continued their protests for several months. Some of these candidates later succeeded in examinations conducted by the Federal Public Service Commission (FPSC).
The very notion that lower-grade jobs, from BPS-1 to BPS-4, are awarded on merit in the province also appears questionable. This can be gauged from a recently viral video of Provincial Minister for Prisons Haji Ali Hassan Zardari. In the video, when a journalist complains to him that jobs in his department are not being awarded on merit, the minister looks at the journalist in surprise and asks, "What merit is there in BPS-1 to BPS-4 jobs?"
A large proportion of government jobs in the province falls within BPS-5 to BPS-15. This is also why the majority of unemployed young people have traditionally applied for positions in these grades. Consequently, the provincial government has also faced greater pressure over government employment in this category.
For this reason, the Sindh government decided to improve the recruitment system, at least for this category of jobs, by establishing the Sindh Job Portal and engaging the testing service of Sukkur IBA University to ensure merit.
However, some influential departments have not implemented these government measures, citing their autonomous status. The Sindh Assembly and the Prisons Department are among the most prominent examples.
The two institutions used a private testing company to fill their vacant positions instead of engaging the testing service of Sukkur IBA University.
In this regard, The Express Tribune contacted the Secretary of the Provincial Assembly G.M. Umar Farooq to ask why the services of a government university's testing service had not been obtained. However, he did not respond.
The same question was put to Inspector General of Prisons Fida Hussain Mastoi, but he also did not respond.

title: Dark web trail leads to child exploitation ring
description: Dark web trail leads to child exploitation ring
content:
NCCIA probe reveals minors being used to produce pornographic cartoons
What began as an online interaction allegedly drew a 13-year-old girl into the orbit of a suspected dark web network, where children were reportedly assigned tasks and paid to produce pornographic animated content. A timely intervention by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) has now brought the case to light, raising concerns about the online exploitation of minors.
The agency rescued the girl during a crackdown in Rabia City, uncovering what investigators suspect is a wider network involving child exploitation and the production of pornographic cartoons. The probe has also revealed suspected links to individuals in Germany and the United Kingdom, according to NCCIA officials.
Investigators are examining whether children were deliberately targeted, manipulated and paid to carry out tasks as part of the alleged operation. Officials have also launched a probe into the possible use of so-called "red rooms" on the dark web to assign tasks to minors.
Speaking at a press conference, NCCIA Deputy Director Shehzad Akbar said the agency had acted on credible information about the suspected network. The girl's father was informed, and the two devices used by the child were seized with his cooperation.
Akbar rejected suggestions that the initial task assigned to the girl involved killing a cat. He said, however, that the child was allegedly being subjected to psychological manipulation similar to tactics attributed to dark web groups operating internationally. Had the network not been exposed, the situation could have become more serious, he added.
The investigation is continuing to establish the role of suspected local handlers and identify other children who may have been targeted.
According to information shared by the officials, the wider case involves 42 suspects, including 12 juveniles. Investigators are examining evidence that children were allegedly paid to produce pornographic animated content, with some reportedly receiving around $100, described in the information provided as approximately Rs6,000. The agency has seized 19 mobile phones from Pixel Craft, a company reportedly operating for around two years, five phones from Art Office and 17 from Art Design, which reportedly employed 17 people. Officials are investigating the companies' possible links to the suspected network.
Akbar said a man identified as Fudan was allegedly operating the network. Preliminary findings also indicate that the companies provided logos, banners and other digital design services to foreign clients. Investigators are examining whether these businesses were connected to the alleged exploitation activities.
The deputy director said the agency had previously detained a boy in Karachi who was allegedly searching online for ways to take revenge on another person. In a separate case, the NCCIA arrested a suspect identified as Hamza on Thursday over alleged anti-state propaganda. Officials said the allegations were being investigated further.
Akbar said the agency had recovered 39 accounts on WhatsApp, Instagram and other social media platforms over the past 15 days. It had also blocked 95 accounts allegedly linked to financial fraud and taken action against 38 accounts suspected of harassing women through fake identities.
The agency is pursuing cases involving the hacking of social media accounts, online financial fraud and harassment through fabricated identities. It has also received numerous complaints about the hacking of WhatsApp Business accounts.
Investigators are separately examining allegations that individuals have been operating social media accounts under women's names and using fabricated identities to harass others. The NCCIA said investigations into the suspected child exploitation network and other cybercrime cases were under way.

Authorities ban dangerous metal wires, nylon strings
The Lahore district administration has allowed kite-flying across the district, except in designated prohibited areas, from March 12 to 14, 2027, as part of Basant celebrations.
Deputy Commissioner Lahore has issued a formal notification outlining the dates, conditions and safety measures governing the manufacture, sale and use of kites and strings.
Under the notification, the manufacture of kites and strings will be permitted from September 5, 2026, to March 14, 2027.
The purchase, transportation and storage of kite-flying materials will be allowed from February 1, 2027, while their sale will be permitted from February 10 to March 14.
Digital registration has been made mandatory for kite and string manufacturers, traders and shopkeepers.
Only registered shopkeepers will be allowed to sell kite-flying materials, and registered manufacturers and sellers will be required to maintain complete records of their stock and sales.
The notification sets a maximum length of 35 inches and a width of four-and-a-half githas for kites. The dimensions of guddas have been fixed at 34 inches in length and one-and-a-half tawas in width.
The manufacture and use of dangerous strings, metal wires, nylon strings and strings coated with sharp abrasive material have been prohibited.
Manufacturers have been directed to use only materials specifically permitted under the notification.
Compliance with safety measures, including the installation of safety rods on motorcycles, has also been made mandatory.
The district administration and police have been directed to ensure strict enforcement of the prescribed safety conditions during Basant.

title: Olive farming can cut  4b oil import bill
description: Olive farming can cut  4b oil import bill
content:
Experts highlight crop's potential to diversify agriculture
Experts have called for expanding olive cultivation in Pakistan to reduce the country's edible oil import bill, improve food and nutritional security and develop a high-value export industry.
Despite being an agrarian country with fertile land, Pakistan imports edible oil worth around $4 billion annually, experts said at an international workshop titled "Olive: Health Utility, Nutrition Value, and Sustainable Food Systems" at the University of Agriculture Faisalabad (UAF) on Friday.
The workshop was organised by the university's Department of Physics in collaboration with the Olive Culture II Scale-Up project.
It featured Italian experts Dr Alessandro Leone of the University of Bari Aldo Moro and Dr Francesco De Musso of the Olive Culture Scale-Up project at CIHEAM Bari, along with Dr Muhammad Nouman, who is also associated with the project.
Speaking to the foreign delegates, UAF Vice-Chancellor Dr Zulfiqar Ali said Pakistan had launched its National Olive Value Chain Policy in collaboration with Italy, describing the expanding olive sector as a promising development for the country's agriculture.
He said olive cultivation could help strengthen nutritional security, diversify agricultural production and promote sustainable food systems. Strengthening research, improving farming practices and developing technical expertise would enable farmers to realise the crop's economic potential and build more resilient agricultural systems, he added.
Prof Leone said Italy's Puglia region was a major centre of olive cultivation, accounting for around 50% of the country's olive oil production.
Italy was among the world's leading olive oil producers, he said, adding that the sector played a significant role in the regional economy through traditional orchards, newly established plantations and high-density cultivation systems.
He said Pakistan could benefit from international experience in olive farming, particularly modern high-density orchard systems, to improve productivity and explore commercial opportunities.

title: Punjab envisages Water Quality Index
description: Punjab envisages Water Quality Index
content:
15 stations monitor pollution in rivers canals, drains
The Punjab government has set up 15 automated monitoring stations at various locations to monitor water pollution in the province's canals, rivers and other natural water bodies.
The stations track water quality and analyse 14 parameters every hour.
The stations have been installed along rivers and barrages to enable continuous monitoring of water quality. The government is also preparing to introduce a Water Quality Index, similar to the Air Quality Index (AQI), to provide regular assessments of pollution levels in water bodies.
Punjab Environmental Protection Department Environmental Monitoring Centre Head Noor Ahmed said while talking to The Express Tribune that the index would help assess water pollution levels and identify their sources on a scientific basis.
He said monitoring stations had been installed near the Ravi Siphon and the river's confluence with Hudiara drain. Water quality is also being monitored at Head Marala, Khanki and Trimmu on the River Chenab, as well as at Kalabagh on the Indus and other locations.
Data collected from the stations will help authorities track changes in pollution levels at different points along the rivers and assess the extent of contamination over time.
Research is also under way to identify the sources of pollution in Hudiara drain.
Water samples have been collected from 56 locations along the drain, with approximately 1km distance between sampling points.
The official said the samples would be analysed across all seasons to determine the contributions of local industries, urban discharges and polluted water entering from across the border.
The findings are expected to help establish the proportion of pollution attributable to each source.
Preliminary observations indicate that pollution levels are higher in the downstream sections of the rain near Lahore than at closer to the border. However, the precise contribution of different sources will be determined after the completion of the study, the monitoring centre head added.
According to a report, pollution levels in the Ravi remain relatively low between Narowal and Zafarwal and the siphon.
The situation changes after the river enters Lahore, where untreated municipal sewage and contaminated water from around 10 locations enter the it, adversely affecting the water quality.
The finding highlights the need to treat municipal sewage and industrial effluent before discharging it into water bodies.
Meanwhile, specialised water squads have been deployed across the province to monitor industrial discharges and take action against units violating environmental regulations.
The teams are tasked with identifying sources of industrial pollution and enforcing compliance with environmental laws.
In Lahore, work is under way to install at least eight wastewater treatment plants for the city's sewage before its discharge into waterways. The implementation of some projects for the purpose has begun.
The environment department has also deployed anti-smog guns at pollution hotspots on the basis of air pollution readings and ground conditions.
Punjab Environment DG Abdullah Nayyar Sheikh said the department was using a data-driven approach to deploy the guns at locations where pollution levels required immediate attention.
He said field teams were monitoring conditions across the city and ensuring that the machinery was moved to identified pollution hotspots.
He said the action was part of efforts to curb dust and particulate matter during the smog season.
"The deployment of anti-smog guns is being linked with field monitoring so that the available machinery can be utilised where it is most needed," he said.
According to the department, the anti-smog guns are being deployed on a priority basis at locations with elevated PM10 (Particulate Matter 10) levels to suppress dust on roads and surrounding areas for limiting its dispersion.
Operations Member Sajid Bashir said the deployment was not restricted to any location and was being adjusted according to monitoring readings.
He said field teams were continuously assessing different areas and shifting the machinery where required to address pollution hotspots.
The guns were operated on Friday at Quaid-e-Azam Campus, Bahkewal, Muslim Town, Maulana Shaukat Ali Road, Gulberg, Stedex Complex, Doctor Hospital, Main Multan Road, Jail Road in Jinnah Town, Pasco Society and other spots.

The film premiered as the centrepiece selection of the New York Film Festival on October 2 and is scheduled to open in cinemas on December 4.

Pascal also shared a brief line from his upcoming Marvel film Avengers: Doomsday , saying his character would deliver the words, “It’s good to see you again.” He additionally discussed De Noche , his anticipated collaboration with director Todd Haynes, describing the project as personally meaningful.

The case has also reached Parliament’s Standing Committee on Interior, which has included it in the formal agenda of its October 29 meeting and sought a briefing from senior Punjab police officials on the investigation and progress made so far.
The committee has summoned Punjab Inspector General of Police and Crime Control Department (CCD) Additional Inspector General Sohail Zafar Chattha. Rawalpindi Regional Police Officer Babar Sarfraz Alpa and Senior Superintendent of Police (Operations) Malik Tariq Mehboob have also been asked to brief the committee on the case.
The parliamentary committee has invited Hina’s family to attend the October 29 meeting, where they can present their concerns and position on the investigation.
In view of the latest medical findings, the family’s reservations about the investigation and the case’s referral to the parliamentary committee, the October 29 meeting has assumed considerable significance, sources said.
Hina was allegedly killed by her husband in connivance with his father and an employee. A preliminary post-mortem report found a fracture to a neck bone and injuries to Hina's ribs and hip. Samples, including those required for DNA analysis, were sent to a forensic laboratory.
Police said the precise cause of death remained unestablished until the issuance of complete post-mortem and forensic reports.
A special investigation team took Asghar and Arshad to Lahore under tight security on August 25. Their samples were submitted to the Punjab Forensic Science Agency for DNA and polygraph examinations.
Meanwhile, police sources drew attention to old YouTube lectures by Asghar, who reportedly taught corporate communication at several universities. In one lecture, he asked a student why a husband might shoot his wife and discussed hypothetical scenarios involving marital relationships, infidelity and financial motives.
According to police sources, domestic worker Arshad gave three different statements from the time he was taken into custody until the formal investigation. In his first statement, Arshad claimed that Hina was killed according to a plan in collaboration with Asghar.
Read More : Hina Javed murder: Domestic worker confesses to crime, police say
In his second statement , he claimed responsibility for the murder. However, during the formal police investigation, Arshad allegedly recorded a third statement, saying he had been called during a quarrel between the husband and wife.
According to police sources, Arshad also revealed that Hina resisted and tried to run away to save her life, after which both men caught her. During her resistance, she was allegedly strangled.
According to police sources, the investigation into Hina's murder was not limited to her husband and domestic worker, and inquiries were being conducted from various angles. Police were also examining whether domestic worker Arshad killed Hina after she allegedly saw him stealing money or other items from the house.
According to sources, Arshad used to sleep in a portion of the house occupied by Hina and other family members. He had also been accused of stealing Hina's purse, cash and other items from the house.
Police were investigating whether Arshad killed Hina out of fear that his alleged theft would be discovered. However, according to police sources, another question being examined was whether, if only one person was involved in the murder, he could have moved the body alone to the bathroom and hung it from the shower.
On September 1, the investigation team recovered the alleged murder weapon , a screwdriver, from the possession of suspect and employee Arshad during a 10-day inquiry.
The team also recovered the nikahnamas of both wives of the main suspect along with the divorce deed of his first wife, Iram Zaib.
On September 3, Civil Judge Adil Sarwar Sial sent Asghar and Arshad to Adiala Jail on a 14-day judicial remand in the murder case.
Also Read : Hina Javed murder probe expands
The court ordered that the challan be completed within two weeks and both suspects, along with the challan, be produced before the court on September 16.
On September 6, Arshad, who remained in police custody on a 10-day physical remand, was sent on judicial remand.
Sources said the special investigation team had started recording separate statements of police officers, personnel and others.
On September 11, Arshad filed a bail application before an Islamabad sessions court on Thursday, declaring himself innocent.
In his bail petition, the suspect denied involvement in the murder and contended that the allegations levelled against him in the FIR were completely false and that he had nothing to do with the incident.
He said that he was mentally incapable of committing such a serious crime and requested that he be granted bail.
On September 30, the Punjab government constituted a high-powered committee to review the investigation into Hina's murder case.
On October 1, Additional District and Sessions Judge Naseer Ahmed dismissed both bail applications of accused Arshad and extended the judicial remand of both accused until October 14.
On October 10, a high-level investigation team launched a fresh probe into Hina's murder, visiting the crime scene in Lalkurti and reviewing key evidence, including the victim's DNA report.
On October 17, Hina's family expressed complete distrust in both the CCD and the local police and decided to file a private complaint, also described as a judicial FIR, before a local magistrate next week.
On October 19, Arshad's father alleged that his son was forced at gunpoint to restrain the victim and was subsequently tortured in custody to make him confess to the crime.

title: NAZA  and a world in disorder
description: NAZA  and a world in disorder
content:
Cook points to is a world in disorder, propped up by a new form of colonialism
In his pithy but poignant commentary on the documentary film NAZA, British journalist Jonathan Cook identifies a malaise that helped lift Western civilisation to its current strength.
Today's Western privileges were built on a long history of naked, racist colonialism - greed, pillage, slavery and genocide - that we have never truly renounced or forsaken.
NAZA is not just about Israel and Gaza. It is about the evil lurking in us all, says Cook, in a bitter reminder of the conflicts, land grabs and democratic repression taking place across the world.
What Cook points to is a world in disorder, propped up by a new form of colonialism: bigger powers relying on smaller, amenable states to pursue their objectives while practically ignoring the rule of law and human rights.
One wonders if the turmoil following the imposition of Governor's Rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa is also a manifestation of this global disorder and quest for absolute power.
The 48-member Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC), comprising tribal elders from 12 districts for looking after the ex-FATA regions, recalls a proposal discussed in the 1990s to replace the existing FATA administrative arrangement with a tribal advisory council. The crucial difference is that the 2018 merger brought these areas under the provincial system, with courts, police and other civilian institutions. Whether the new council will work within that framework or gradually undermine it by restoring the influence of federally appointed or politically favoured tribal intermediaries.
The composition of the council has already raised doubts about its acceptability. Five nominated members – Shahabuddin Khan of Bajaur, Baz Muhammad Khan of Bannu, Maulana Misbahullah Dawar of North Waziristan, Maulana Saleh Shah of Upper South Waziristan and Malik Jamil of Lower South Waziristan – had refused to join or distanced themselves from the arrangement. Can the council members exercise authority over communities whose members have not elected its representatives?
The concern is that the council could become a buffer between the authorities and the population. Critics also fear that a council dominated by status-quo figures could facilitate a return to the old FATA system in practice, even if the formal structures of provincial government remain in place.
Will the council be able to oppose decisions that conflict with local interests, or will they serve as intermediaries for policies they cannot meaningfully influence? For some tribal elders, participation may carry the risk of alienation from their own communities.
There is also a wider regional dimension. The former FATA lies along the porous and sensitive Pakistan-Afghanistan frontier. Afghan objections to the Durand Line and the presence of militant groups on both sides of the border complicate security and governance. Calls for a return to the previous administrative arrangement have therefore been viewed by some observers in the context of regional political and security calculations. Suspicions have also surfaced whether the system responds to specific demand by the Haqqani network or the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP)?
As for tackling terrorism, the military has for years played a leading role in border security, intelligence-based operations and counterterrorism, alongside the police and the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD). The relevant question is, what will change under the new arrangement? Will it improve coordination among civilian authorities, security agencies and local communities or will the council create another administrative layer without resolving the underlying problems?
Another reality facing Pakistan is that the TTP and the Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP) operate through different organisational structures, although both pose serious security threats, presumably with the same objectives.
Neither the creation of an advisory council nor the appointment of tribal elders can, by itself, dismantle these networks which the authorities claim are foreign proxies.
Residents of Waziristan, Bajaur, Kurram and Khyber have reason to ask why militant violence continues despite the substantial presence of security forces. They also question how some militants appear able to move across the border or travel within the region despite repeated assurances about security arrangements.
Locals in these regions also point to another factor – the American quest for critical minerals. Since these areas possess a number of minerals and rare earth, they fear that the political changes are only meant to extract natural resources with the help of status-quo tribal elders. The former tribal districts contain mineral resources that could generate revenue and employment, but the distribution of benefits has long been contentious. Some residents suspect that the new council could facilitate resource extraction while keeping local communities at a distance from decisions about licences, royalties, ownership and environmental safeguards.
The central issue is therefore not simply whether Governor's Rule is lawful or whether an advisory council can be established. It is whether the new arrangement strengthens representative government or replaces it with indirect control over natural resources of the region. A council that lacks public confidence may become another source of friction rather than a means of stabilisation – unlikely to deliver lasting peace and meet public aspirations.
The people of the former tribal districts have already experienced major changes in their administrative status, repeated security operations and prolonged instability. They need functioning courts, accountable policing, representative local government, security from militant violence and a fair share of the region's resources.
Ultimately, three questions remain unanswered. Will the council strengthen the political and constitutional integration achieved in 2018, or weaken it in practice? Will it help reduce militancy through public cooperation and accountable civilian institutions, or merely add another layer of administration? And will the region's mineral wealth benefit its people, or deepen their distrust of the state? Until the authorities provide clear answers, doubts about the purpose and legitimacy of the new arrangement are likely to persist.

title: Vishwa Guru s game
description: Vishwa Guru s game
content:
Pakistan was expected to shrug, reasoning that ending statehood did not alter the disputed status
On 29 October 2019, as many as 27 Members of the European Parliament, mostly from far-right parties, went on a pilgrimage to Indian-occupied Kashmir. The visit was an optical surgical strike against the unexpected perception of isolation enveloping New Delhi after the 5 August decision to revoke the territory's statehood and bifurcate it.
Unexpected, because every duck was supposed to be in a row. Pakistan was expected to shrug, reasoning that ending statehood did not alter the disputed status. A compliant international media, now influenced by Indian interests, was programmed to ignore it, while the foot traffic of world leaders would normalise the manoeuvre. Instead, Islamabad took a firm stand, pockets of Western media resistance fought back, diplomatic traffic halted, and the matter reached the UN Security Council. Desperate to manage optics, the Modi government flew in these MEPs, staging a global endorsement for domestic consumption.
But were these politicians duped patsies, or was their presence symptomatic of deeper ideological alignment? In 2019 and 2020, the EU DisinfoLab exposed the 'Indian Chronicles', revealing how the Delhi-based Srivastava Group used fake NGOs and resurrected dead experts to manipulate European politicians. Yet Modi's accession had rendered such outfits redundant. Why run a convoluted side hustle when mainstream global media and Indian civil society were already offering what Professor Timothy Snyder calls 'anticipatory obedience'? These far-right MEPs shared the BJP's pathological hostility towards Muslims, both capitalising on the war on terror's Islamophobia. Did a desperate Modi government seek help from ideological twins, then throw a redundant Srivastava Group under the bus to hide the true extent of this collusion?
Almost a year later, the FinCEN Files exposed a vast financial shadow economy, flagging 44 Indian banks for facilitating over 2,000 suspicious transactions. Between 2011 and 2017, they processed over $1 billion in flagged dark capital, much of it vanishing into shell networks. Crucially, that is the period that saw the revival and mainstreaming of the modern far-right, from the American Tea Party to ultra-nationalist European populists. The leaks hinted at a dark symbiosis. The dominant order manages such outbursts by misdirecting attention, so the world forgot the flagged Indian operations.
The symbiosis, one suspects, relies on a multi-phase playbook. The first phase was a massive intelligence and policy blind spot, engineered at the zenith of the Global War on Terror. Intellectuals like Samuel Huntington, platformed by editors like Fareed Zakaria, laid the theoretical timber by framing Islam and China as the world's inherent enemies. India positioned itself as the indispensable natural ally, securing sweeping concessions and elevating its elite into the West's highest echelons. By harvesting Israel's weapons-grade Islamophobia and the West's Sinophobia, India manufactured the blind spot for its domestic, regional and eventually global ambitions.
With international cover secured, the second phase normalised domestic extremism. The elevation of a leadership defined by the Gujarat riots, managed by a political enforcer who had faced tadipar (extirpation or exile) orders, signalled that secular moderation was over. The militant consolidation of the Hindu Right was mainstreamed, immune to Western censure because the West had locked itself into the GWOT blind spot.
The final phase of the Vishwa Guru project is reshaping the global order in India's image. By pitting the West against China and Islam, India makes itself diplomatically inevitable. It also dismantles the West's Enlightenment principles, Christian egalitarianism and human rights sensibilities by financing the rise of the Western far-right. As that far-right rejects egalitarianism, it retreats toward the "golden age" of pre-Christian paganism. India intercepts this retreat, appropriating global paganism under the banner of a shared "Indo-European legacy".
This osmosis is no accident; it realises a century-old blueprint. The project is fundamentally anti-Western and anti-Abrahamic, rejecting democratic equality for a rigid, birth-based order. VD Savarkar, architect of militant Hindutva, subordinated democratic principles to ancient hierarchical codes, declaring the Manusmriti "the scripture which is most worshippable after Vedas... even today it is the fundamental law of Hindus."
This reverence for caste over universal rights was globalised by Savitri Devi, born Maximiani Julia Portas. Disgusted by the egalitarian foundations of Judeo-Christianity, this European fascist relocated to India in 1932, convinced the caste system was the last living remnant of pure Aryan paganism. She left an indelible Nazi mark on the Hindu Right's formative years. In 1939 she met Savarkar, who backed her efforts to weaponise Hindu nationalism. She praised Hinduism because it "never admitted the absurd dogma of equality."
For today's Hindutva establishment, these are active operational directives. Devi's ideological virus remains potent, her texts hosted on platforms run by William Pierce, architect of The Turner Diaries. Backed by a rising economic state's processing power, this hatred of monotheism and equality escalates toward a global Brahmanic order designed to supersede Western democracy.
But what does this mean for Pakistan? The recent Shanghai Cooperation Organisation planning meetings in Islamabad gave a stark answer. In an exclusive PTV News interview during a rare visit, India's National Coordinator for the SCO, Alok Dimri, claimed that the SCO presidency had arrived in "our and the Persian civilisational neighbourhood". This was no gesture of inclusivity. By subsuming Islamabad into an Indian civilisational sphere on state television, New Delhi unveiled its own corollary to the Monroe Doctrine or the One China policy. After last year's May war, when India reacted with bitter tantrums to Pakistan's diplomatic attention, the establishment realised it needed a formalised doctrine of absolute subcontinental dominance.
For over a decade, the Modi government has strung the Pakistani establishment along with promises of a peaceful settlement, while investing in every conceivable Pakistani fault line to weaken the state from within. New Delhi has no genuine intention of making peace.
As the old adage warns: if the horse befriends the grass, what will it eat? To expect peaceful coexistence from a project built on hierarchical conquest is a fatal miscalculation. The diplomatic charm deployed in Islamabad is the anaesthetic for Akhand Bharat, a warning that the Vishwa Guru is no longer just consolidating its borders but executing its endgame.

title: The paradox of Pakistan s political parties
description: The paradox of Pakistan s political parties
content:
Imran Khan built much of PTI's political identity around challenging corruption, injustice and entrenched power
Pakistan's political parties suffer from a peculiar contradiction. The parties that encourage their workers to question authority risk being overwhelmed by internal revolt. Those that demand obedience may look disciplined, but they become helpless when their leadership is removed or pressured. One is noisy but fragmented; the other orderly but overly dependent. Neither has solved the problem of building an institution larger than its leader and this is what makes them vulnerable to implosion.
Imran Khan built much of PTI's political identity around challenging corruption, injustice and entrenched power. He encouraged ordinary supporters to speak against what they considered wrong. That message cultivated political confidence, but political empowerment is not the same as political organisation. Since Khan's imprisonment in 2023, PTI has struggled to translate an intensely committed support base into a coherent chain of democratic decision-making.
Workers accuse leaders of failing to pursue his release effectively; leaders face pressure from competing factions; and social-media commentators increasingly set the terms of internal debate. A public disagreement quickly becomes a test of loyalty. Someone asking for strategy is branded timid; someone urging talks is accused of betrayal. Party workers have every right to question decisions. Digital voices may expose failures that an inner circle would prefer to conceal. The problem begins when accusations replace evidence and online influence substitutes for authority derived from party members.
Who, then, speaks for PTI: elected officeholders, imprisoned leaders, street activists, overseas supporters or the loudest account on X? Without trusted rules, every faction claims to defend the founder while questioning everyone else's legitimacy. The deeper difficulty is the absence of a trusted referee. Where authority depends on personal access to a jailed founder, disagreements cannot be settled through regular procedures. Whoever claims the most authentic interpretation of the founder's wishes acquires influence without carrying the responsibilities of a formally accountable office.
Yet this is only one side of Pakistan's political paradox. In parties dominated by established families or entrenched elites, dissent often has limited influence on leadership succession. Workers may spend decades organising rallies and defending party leaders without gaining a realistic route to the top. Personal allegiance becomes the currency of advancement. Internal elections, where they occur, rarely settle fundamental questions of power. Such parties may display unity, but unity maintained by unequal access to power is not the same as institutional strength.
When pressure comes from outside, organisations with weak internal ownership can prove vulnerable to defections, patronage and negotiations conducted above the heads of ordinary members. This should not erase history. PPP workers and other opposition activists resisted Zia's dictatorship, notably through the Movement for the Restoration of Democracy. Many paid heavily for that resistance. The lesson is not that some parties have brave followers and others do not. It is that bravery cannot permanently substitute for institutions.
Meanwhile, Pakistan's civilmilitary imbalance makes these weaknesses more consequential. Political parties compete fiercely against one another, sometimes accepting interventions against rivals that they would condemn against themselves. The result is a familiar cycle: leaders rise with powerful backing, fall into confrontation, and discover that constitutional principles cannot be defended selectively. The October suspension of PTI's government in K-P, justified by federal authorities on security grounds and rejected by PTI as politically motivated, illustrates how sharply those constitutional disputes can escalate. With the government gone, divisions within the party have further widened rendering democracy weaker.
The tragedy is that Pakistan repeatedly produces powerful political personalities without producing equally powerful political institutions.

title: Protecting the watchdogs
description: Protecting the watchdogs
content:
Pakistani journalists continue to work in one of the world's most dangerous media environments, according to several local and international press-related NGOs and monitoring groups. The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) regularly ranks Pakistan among the deadliest countries for reporters, with dozens killed in the past two decades, but barely any prosecutions or convictions to show. Reporters Without Borders (RSF) similarly documents persistent physical attacks, death threats, harassment and digital surveillance. The Pakistan Press Foundation (PPF) records dozens of cases each year - from beatings and abductions to pressure on media owners to silence critical coverage. These threats are not just dangers for journalists, but also detrimental to all Pakistanis, as the public's right to know is being eroded.
The threats themselves range from non-state armed groups targeting journalists to political and economic pressures - including advertising boycotts, licensing leverage and legal harassment - which have forced newsrooms to self-censor. Digital intimidation, including hacking and online smear campaigns, increasingly follows reporters home. The common thread is impunity, because when attacks go uninvestigated and unpunished, they embolden further violence. CPJ's impunity index has repeatedly highlighted Pakistan's failure to bring the killers of journalists to justice.
Safety requires more than condemnations. The federal and provincial governments should establish independent, adequately funded protection mechanisms that are approved by journalist unions. The police must treat attacks on journalists as attacks on democratic accountability, with transparent investigations and witness protection. The judiciary should also expedite hearings of cases involving violence against journalists.
Journalists are the public's eyes and ears. A free press is not a threat to stability, but rather a precondition for good governance in a democracy.

title: Organ trade crackdown
description: Organ trade crackdown
content:
Underlying this criminal industry is an uncomfortable economic reality
The FIA's recent crackdown on an illegal transplant network in Islamabad is commendable. Five arrests, the seizure of vehicles and the freezing of properties worth Rs87.5 million suggest that the trade is not merely sustained by desperate patients and impoverished donors. It is a lucrative criminal enterprise that relies on intermediaries and medical expertise with access to healthcare facilities.
Of particular concern is the ease with which the suspects circumvented established medical procedures. Forged referral letters and false donor identities were reportedly used to obtain laboratory tests, while transplants were performed inside residential properties without the necessary medical safeguards. How were such arrangements allowed to operate, and why were irregularities in donor verification not detected? These questions must be answered through a thorough investigation rather than another round of arrests that leaves the wider network untouched. Pakistan's transplantation laws expressly prohibit the commercial sale of human organs, yet legislation means little when its enforcement remains inconsistent. Regulatory authorities must establish stricter mechanisms for verifying donor relationships and scrutinising transplant records. Hospitals found to have knowingly facilitated illegal procedures must face serious consequences, while medical professionals involved in the trade should be subjected to criminal prosecution. Following the money is equally important, particularly where illicit proceeds have allegedly been invested in property.
Underlying this criminal industry is an uncomfortable economic reality. Poverty leaves vulnerable individuals susceptible to brokers who offer immediate financial relief in exchange for irreversible medical risks. Meanwhile, patients facing lengthy waits for legitimate transplantation may be driven towards dangerous alternatives. Enforcement must therefore be accompanied by stronger donor protections and improvements in access to lawful transplantation services.

title: An uneasy peace
description: An uneasy peace
content:
American military assets stand depleted in the Middle East
As Americans gear up for the November 3 mid-term polls to elect Representatives and Senators, an uneasy peace prevails in the Middle East. President Trump's wish list for a deal with Iran - under which the Islamic Republic would give up its enriched uranium and provide safe passage for the superpower to exit the volatile region - remains unrealised. Hectic diplomatic efforts by Qatar and Pakistan have yet to bear fruit. Iran remains adamant that the US must exit the region, as the latter stands badly bruised by the losses it incurred in the war.
American military assets stand depleted in the Middle East, with many key military bases heavily degraded by recent conflict. Coupled with this is the reality of Israel being unable to unilaterally defend itself, as its Iron Dome air defence system has been severely overwhelmed. Last but not least is the reluctance of Doha and Riyadh to back any new military adventurism by Washington against Tehran.
This paints a paradoxical security dilemma wherein the Gulf Arab states that once depended on US military muscle are now on their own. On a positive note, a trans-regional security nexus is in the making. The trilateral Makkah Agreement and the recently-signed four-nation Badr Pact - comprising Pakistan, Türkiye, Qatar and Indonesia - are spontaneous responses to this shift. By focusing on joint military production and technical R&D, these nations have emerged as a formidable deterrent force.
Yet, Washington's jingoism and lack of a consistent policy remain a major point of concern. All signs indicate the region is heading back toward a major conflagration. Reports from across the Atlantic that the US wants to nail down Iran as a point-scoring exercise before the midterms are deeply unnerving. The body language and rhetoric emerging from Iran's power corridors is one of defiance, and the IRGC has vowed "surprises" that could prove disastrous for American allies in the region. No such misadventure will bring an end to the war; instead, it would trigger a new geo-economic crisis and leave the region devastated to the core.

title: The only thing moving fast in Karachi is my blood pressure
description: The only thing moving fast in Karachi is my blood pressure
content:
Karachi does not need a traffic police department
Karachi is a beautiful city with one small problem: everything here tests your patience as if patience were a compulsory subject in the CSS examination. You leave home to reach somewhere in thirty minutes and return with a new personality, three emotional problems, and enough anger to write a letter to the United Nations. Actually, scratch that the UN should write a letter to Karachi asking what on earth is happening here.
And if you think the city is testing your patience, wait until you see what it has done to the roads.
For starters, why does every road look as if it has survived a war nobody told us about? One moment you are sitting peacefully in your car, and the next moment your head hits the roof because your tyre has discovered a pothole the size of a swimming pool. Honestly, driving in Karachi has reached a stage where I do not need Google Maps to find my destination. I need a satellite to warn me about the next hole trying to swallow my car.
The potholes, however, are not the only obstacle. The speed breakers then enter the picture. I don't understand why there are so many speed breakers? Is the city trying to stop speeding, or is it trying to stop people from reaching their destinations altogether? Some roads have so many bumps that your car starts feeling like a washing machine on the spin cycle. You leave home with your bones in the correct places and arrive at work wondering whether your spine is still under warranty.
At this point, Karachi does not need a traffic police department. It needs a physiotherapy department at every signal. Yes! Speed breakers here are not speed breakers. They are spine breakers. I have started measuring distance not in kilometres but in the number of times my head hits the roof. Oh, you live ten bumps away from me? Nice, we're practically neighbours.
In fact, I don't even bother asking for directions anymore. I just ask, "How many head injuries away is it?"
The person who invented speed breakers in Karachi deserves an award for "Most Creative Way to Torture the General Public Without Going to Jail". It's brilliant, really. Diabolical, but brilliant.
Then there is this road that gets repaired, dug up, repaired again, and dug up once more. What exactly are we searching for underneath? Gold? Oil? The remains of an ancient civilisation?
Of course, once you finally escape the roads, traffic welcomes you with open arms. Karachi traffic has its own rules and, apparently, nobody has read them. A car wants to go straight, a motorcycle wants to go diagonally, a bus wants to become a train, and a rickshaw believes it has a sab chalta hai licence. Everyone is in a hurry, but somehow nobody is moving. And then come the horns. Why does the person behind you keep honking when you are stuck behind another hundred vehicles? What exactly am I supposed to do? Grow wings? Fly over the car in front of me?
Well, the noise is only half the problem. Some drivers seem determined to attack your eyesight as well. Karachi apparently believes that if your ears have suffered enough, your eyes should not be left out. Yes, these are the people who drive with their high beams on at night. Why? Are you driving a car or landing an aeroplane? I am trying to get home, not apply for a pilot's licence. One look into the rear-view mirror and I can see my ancestors waving goodbye.
So in Karachi, Google Maps should stop saying, "You have arrived." It should say, "Congratulations. You survived."

title: Leslie Bibb joins Camila Mendes in Amazon MGM Studios     Upgraded 2
description: Leslie Bibb joins Camila Mendes in  Upgraded 2   the Prime Video sequel to the 2024 romantic comedy  filming in Italy
content:
Leslie Bibb joins Camila Mendes in 'Upgraded 2', the Prime Video sequel to the 2024 romantic comedy, filming in Italy
Leslie Bibb has joined the cast of Upgraded 2 , the upcoming sequel to the 2024 romantic comedy starring Camila Mendes. The film is being developed by Amazon MGM Studios for worldwide release on Prime Video.
Bibb will star alongside Mendes, who is returning to the franchise as both an actor and producer. Director Becca Gleason is set to helm the sequel, with Luke Roberts and Justin Matthews returning as screenwriters after writing the first instalment.
Leslie Bibb joins the cast of the upcoming sequel to UPGRADED at Prime Video opposite Camila Mendes. pic.twitter.com/hs1gBMN5Go
Plot details for Upgraded 2 remain under wraps. The original film followed Ana, played by Mendes, an ambitious intern at a New York City art auction house who pretended to be the company’s director while pursuing a romance with a wealthy man. As their relationship developed, her deception threatened both her career and her personal life.
Amazon MGM Studios secured worldwide distribution rights to the sequel, which is expected to reach audiences in more than 240 countries and territories through Prime Video. Production is scheduled to begin in Italy in October 2026.
Producers include Mike Karz and Bill Bindley for Gulfstream Pictures, Mendes and Rachel Matthews for Honor Role, Lena Roklin for Luber Roklin Entertainment, and Piers Tempest for Tempo Productions.
Bibb recently appeared in the fifth season of HBO’s Hacks , earning an Emmy nomination for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Comedy Series. She also returned for the second season of Apple TV’s Palm Royale and appeared in the third season of HBO’s The White Lotus .
Her other credits include Iron Man , Iron Man 2 , Confessions of a Shopaholic , Tag and Juror #2 . Bibb is also set to star in HBO’s dark comedy series The Rush Whisperer and Prime Video’s romantic comedy series Escorted , alongside Brett Goldstein and Lesley Manville.
Further casting details and a release date for Upgraded 2 have yet to be announced.

content:
Seven cases detected in a week; health dept steps up contact tracing and surveillance
The Sindh Health Department on Friday reported two more cases of monkeypox, or mpox, taking the provincial tally to 98, as the department stepped up surveillance, contact tracing and patient care following seven new infections in the past week.
It said authorities are tracing and monitoring people who came into contact with infected patients to contain the spread of the virus.
The department also directed public and private healthcare facilities to strictly implement infection prevention and control measures.
Read: Tally hits 95 as two more mpox cases reported in Sindh
Citizens have also been advised to maintain proper hand hygiene and avoid direct contact with rashes, blisters and sores on suspected or confirmed patients. They have been cautioned against sharing personal items used by infected individuals, including towels, clothing and bedding.
People developing unusual rashes or blisters have been urged to seek immediate medical attention and inform their doctors about any contact with a suspected mpox patient.
The health department said mpox was a preventable and treatable public health concern, urging citizens to follow precautionary measures and rely on official sources for verified information rather than spreading unconfirmed reports.
Sindh's mpox outbreak has intensified in recent months, with health authorities reporting a steady rise in infections across the province. Earlier this month, The Express Tribune reported 95 confirmed cases and 11 deaths, highlighting a growing need for stronger surveillance, early diagnosis and contact tracing.
The outbreak has extended beyond imported infections, with cases reported among Karachi residents who had no history of foreign travel . In June, a 26-year-old security guard in Karachi had tested positive, taking the provincial tally to 37 at the time.
Earlier reports also documented infections in Khairpur and Karachi , prompting authorities to establish isolation facilities and strengthen infection-control arrangements in hospitals.
Health experts have warned that delayed diagnosis and stigma can discourage patients from seeking timely medical care, increasing the risk of further transmission. Mpox can spread through close physical contact with an infected person, contact with skin lesions and contaminated personal items.
Symptoms can include fever, body aches, swollen lymph nodes, and unusual skin rashes or blisters.
Authorities have consequently emphasised early testing, isolation of confirmed patients, monitoring of close contacts and strict infection-prevention measures in healthcare facilities.

title: Zardari seeks stronger, mutually beneficial ties with Germany as countries mark 75 years of relations | The Express Tribune
description: Zardari seeks broader cooperation with Germany in meeting with Steinmeier
content:
Zardari seeks broader cooperation with Germany in meeting with counterpart Steinmeier
President Asif Ali Zardari on Friday called for a holistic expansion of bilateral cooperation between Pakistan and Germany to build a robust and constructive partnership, expressing readiness to translate existing ties into a stronger and mutually beneficial relationship through sustained engagement.
The president said this during a meeting with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier in Berlin, according to a statement issued by the President's Office, adding that President Zardari thanked him for the invitation and the warm hospitality extended to him and his delegation.
President Zardari is visiting Germany from October 22 to 24 at the invitation of Steinmeier. During the visit, he is scheduled to meet senior German leaders and business representatives to discuss bilateral relations, particularly the strengthening of economic and trade cooperation.
Zardari said the visit, taking place after 23 years, reflected Pakistan’s commitment to deepening its longstanding cordial and friendly relations with Germany and translating them into a stronger, mutually beneficial partnership through sustained constructive engagement, marking a significant chapter in bilateral ties as the two countries commemorate the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations this year.
1/2 President Zardari Stresses for Holistic Expansion of Bilateral Cooperation towards Robust Constructive Partnership between Pakistan and Germany* President Asif Ali Zardari has stressed on the imperative of realising available potential for expanding existing political,… pic.twitter.com/xM3eSpbSaK
He underscored the need to realise the existing potential for expanding political, economic and defence cooperation, with greater emphasis on trade, emerging technologies, climate resilience, skills development, and people-to-people and cultural exchanges.
President Zardari said Pakistan highly valued Germany as a major European partner and greatly appreciated its support for women’s empowerment, social protection and human development.
He said Pakistan was prepared to expand cooperation beyond traditional areas and pursue innovative, mutually beneficial collaboration in scientific development, healthcare, education, vocational training, technological advancement, trade and investment, agriculture, commerce and industry, and climate resilience.
He emphasised the importance of strengthening cooperation through enhanced government-to-government and business-to-business engagement, as well as interactions among experts.

President Zardari also expressed gratitude to President Steinmeier for Germany’s acknowledgement of Pakistan’s sincere mediation role in the US-Iran conflict.
“Pakistan believes that conflicts should be resolved through sustained dialogue and constructive negotiations to promote regional and global peace and stability,” he said.
President Steinmeier warmly welcomed President Zardari’s visit on the occasion of the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. He also conveyed condolences over the deaths of children in a recent school roof collapse in Peshawar.
The German president expressed hope that Pakistan and Germany would intensify their engagement in business and trade to promote bilateral commercial ties, educational collaboration and technological cooperation.
He also praised Pakistan’s growing diplomatic profile in efforts to resolve regional and global disputes.
President Steinmeier appreciated the Pakistani government for facilitating the verification of 500 Afghans destined to be repatriated to Germany while also acknowledging Pakistan’s humanitarian assistance to millions of Afghans over the past more than four decades.
President Asif Ali Zardari and German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier holding delegation-level talks at the Office of the President on Friday Photo: PID
The two presidents discussed challenges relating to Afghanistan. President Zardari said Pakistan had no conflict with the Afghan people but would not allow terrorists to use Afghan soil to attack Pakistani citizens or violate the country’s sovereignty.
Responding to President Steinmeier’s interest in the Makkah defence pact, President Zardari said the arrangement was aimed at ensuring regional security and providing an alternative to regional conflicts, adding that it was not directed against any specific country.
President Zardari also invited President Steinmeier to visit Pakistan. The German president said he would consider the invitation and look to visit at an appropriate time.
Earlier, President Zardari was accorded a guard of honour at the German Ministry of Defence ahead of his meeting with President Steinmeier and high-level delegation talks.
The German president welcomed his Pakistani counterpart at the formal reception ceremony, where the national anthems of both countries were played, after which the two presidents held a one-on-one meeting followed by delegation-level talks.
The Pakistani delegation included Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, provincial ministers Sharjeel Memon and Jam Khan Shoro, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla and Pakistan’s Ambassador to Germany Salman Sharif.

title: Trump weighs quick end to Iran war against letting conflict  wither
description: Iranian army orders ground forces to maintain highest combat readiness amid tensions with US
content:
Iranian army orders ground forces to maintain highest combat readiness amid tensions with US
President Donald ‌Trump said on Friday the United ‌States could end ⁠the ​war ​with ‌Iran quickly, but questioned whether Washington ​should seek a swift conclusion or ⁠allow the conflict to gradually ‌wind down.
"We could end it very quickly," ⁠Trump ⁠said.
"Do we want ​to finish ‌it off or just want to let it wither?" Speaking to reporters on the ⁠White House South Lawn ⁠as he left on a trip to Florida, Trump said oil is getting out through the Strait ⁠of Hormuz.
Trump on Iran: The question is, do we want to finish it off or let it wither? We are getting everything we want. pic.twitter.com/jNSSsGpEdt
"We are ​getting everything we want,' he said.
The Turkish foreign minister warned on Friday that a new attack on Iran would further spread war and conflict across the region.
“Military intervention in Iran is by no means a solution. No one supports this at the moment,” Hakan Fidan told reporters after an R4+E3 meeting in Istanbul, the first-ever meeting in this format.
The US and Israel are said to have developed plans for renewed strikes against Iran after the American midterm elections.
The war that began in late February has yet to be settled despite a ceasefire and a memorandum of understanding to finalize a peace deal.
Iran’s Army Ground Forces commander Brig Gen Jahanshahi ordered military unit commanders to maintain the highest level of combat readiness, warning that negligence during wartime could have serious consequences, Tasnim News Agency reported on Friday.
“In wartime conditions, any negligence or carelessness can carry heavy costs,” Jahanshahi said, according to Tasnim .
He stressed that maintaining effective operational readiness requires continuous training, accurate assessments of military capabilities, coordination among units and the rapid identification and correction of shortcomings.

The remarks come amid heightened military tensions between Iran and the US following months of hostilities and ongoing disputes over security and maritime navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.
