title: Mourinho must stop Barca machine
description: Portuguese renews one of football s most bitter rivalries on Sunday
content:
Portuguese renews one of football's most bitter rivalries on Sunday
Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho will renew one of football's most bitter rivalries on Sunday when he takes charge of his first Clasico since returning to the club, with La Liga leaders Barcelona awaiting him at Camp Nou.
The Portuguese veteran's first spell at Madrid was defined in large part by his battle to end Barca's dominance under Pep Guardiola, with relations between the Spanish giants slumping to their lowest ebb.
Mourinho managed to break Barca's spell by guiding Real Madrid to the Spanish title in 2012, the crowning achievement of his reign from 2010-13.
Clasicos became increasingly compelling during that period, some would say not for the right reasons, as he and his staff clashed with their Barcelona counterparts both pitch-side and verbally in the media.
The 63-year-old worked as an assistant at Barca under Bobby Robson and Louis van Gaal in the 1990s but was overlooked for Guardiola in 2008 when the Catalans replaced Frank Rijkaard.
Mourinho's frequent battles with Guardiola, Lionel Messi and even with Madrid's own icons like Iker Casillas sometimes overshadowed his sporting achievements.
The most infamous flashpoint was when Mourinho poked then Barca assistant coach Tito Vilanova in the eye in August 2011.
Earlier that year, at the end of the prior season, Madrid and Barca clashed four times in just 18 days, illustrating the intensity of the rivalry.
The first was in La Liga, a 1-1 draw, which helped Barcelona take a step towards retaining the Spanish title as Madrid trailed them.
Mourinho's Madrid beat Barca to win the Copa del Rey in the second, with Cristiano Ronaldo scoring the winner in extra-time.
Then the Catalans got the better of Los Blancos in a Champions League semi-final double header, winning the first leg 2-0 in the Santiago Bernabeu, with Madrid defender Pepe sent off. Mourinho called it a "scandal".
Barcelona held Real Madrid to a 1-1 draw in the second leg to reach the final, which they went on to win.
It was in this period that Guardiola said he could not and would not compete with the "boss" Mourinho in the press room.
Mourinho has hit the ground running in his second spell at Madrid in that regard.
The coach brandished print-outs of incidents after losing the derby clash to try and prove his point that Atletico Madrid deserved two red cards, and refused to attend a press conference after Vinicius Junior was sent off against Villarreal.
Many believe Mourinho employs these tactics as a distraction to take the pressure off his team when they are not performing.
A victory in the Clasico might encourage him to focus on the football, and stopping Hansi Flick's side -- back-to-back Spanish champions -- is one of the main reasons he was rehired by president Florentino Perez.
Flick's Barca have won six of seven Clasicos against Real Madrid since the German arrived, scoring 22 goals and shipping only 11.
Mourinho insists it is impossible for his team to be at the level he wants them to be at after such a short time in charge.
"I've been here for over a hundred days. Obviously, we are not where I want, but there are things we are doing better today than before," said the coach.
Madrid have won their last four matches between La Liga and the Champions League, and after sharing minutes around early in the season, some preferences are emerging.
Although Mourinho said initially he did not see midfielder Federico Valverde as a right-back, where he has been used in the past, he has selected the Uruguayan there in the last two games, ahead of Denzel Dumfries and Trent Alexander-Arnold.
"We created a lot on that side, and Fede had a fantastic match," said Mourinho after the Leipzig win.
In Valverde's place in midfield Mourinho deployed Arda Guler against Sevilla on Sunday and then Bernardo Silva against the German side, with Madrid improving on the ball and retaining more possession.
However, the Clasico poses a different challenge. Mourinho, who deployed defender Pepe in midfield against Barca, may revert to type to try and spoil the hosts' flowing football.

title: NCCIA arrests 4 suspects over child sexual abuse material trafficking in Islamabad
description: NCCIA says suspects lured children aged 6 14 through social media
content:
NCCIA says suspects lured children aged 6-14 through social media
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Friday arrested four alleged members of an international gang involved in child sexual abuse and the production and sale of sexually explicit videos of minors.
Speaking at a press conference in Islamabad, NCCIA Additional Director Muhammad Shoaib Khan said investigators had recovered around 50 to 60 objectionable videos involving children from a mobile phone belonging to a child.
“The subsequent investigation led to the arrest of the four suspects,” he added.
نیشنل سائبر کرائم انویسٹی گیشن ایجنسی (NCCIA) کے سائبر کرائم رپورٹنگ سینٹر اسلام آباد نے بچوں کے استحصال اور آن لائن گرومنگ کے مقدمے میں کارروائی کرتے ہوئے 4 رکنی گینگ کو گرفتار کر لیا۔ درج مقدمے کی تحقیقات کے دوران ملزمان کے قبضے سے مقامی کم عمر بچوں سے متعلق بچوں کے جنسی… pic.twitter.com/FHnTlAIicm
According to Khan, the suspects allegedly befriended children aged between six and 14 through Instagram and other social media platforms, luring them with promises of money before coercing them into recording explicit videos.
Read: Naqvi vows to strengthen NCCIA as cybercrime cases mount in Punjab
The videos were allegedly circulated through WhatsApp groups and sold to buyers internationally, the director said.
Khan also said the agency had previously secured convictions against two Chinese nationals in child sexual abuse material cases.
The arrests come amid an intensified nationwide crackdown by the NCCIA on online child exploitation, blackmail and digital fraud.
On October 10, the NCCIA signed agreements with international artificial intelligence (AI) organisations to strengthen its ability to detect and investigate online offences against children. NCCIA Lahore Additional Director Atif Ameer revealed that AI-assisted analysis had helped identify a suspect in Gujranwala, leading to his arrest.
In a separate operation in Lahore on October 7, the NCCIA arrested 39 people , including a woman, over allegations that an illegal call centre used AI-generated explicit images to blackmail borrowers who had taken digital loans. Investigators alleged that the operation exploited access to borrowers’ mobile phone galleries and contact lists. Forty laptops and 41 mobile phones were seized for forensic examination.
In a separate development, the NCCIA arrested 473 foreign nationals during raids on call centres across the country for their alleged involvement in financial fraud, the NCCIA official said.
Khan stated that the suspects posed as bank representatives in Malaysia, China and India to defraud victims.
The agency also detained 22 suspects in cyber harassment cases over the past week, he said, adding that female officers of the NCCIA had been tasked with the investigation in these cases.
Separately, a Karachi East judicial magistrate remanded a man, Shoaib Nawaz Afridi, to the custody of the NCCIA for three days in a case involving the alleged blackmail of a woman.

title: Injuries in China s Tibet rise to 76 after earthquake  death toll remains at 16
description: President Zardari  Prime Minister Shehbaz express deep grief  sorrow over loss of lives in earthquake
content:
President Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz express deep grief, sorrow over loss of lives in earthquake
The number of people injured in a magnitude 7 earthquake that struck China's southwestern region of Tibet has risen to 76, local government authorities said at a press conference on Friday, while the death toll remained unchanged at 16.
The quake, with an epicentre in Nagqu, a high-altitude city in northern Tibet, a sparsely populated region of China, is the strongest to hit the country since January 2024.
Homes that developed cracks or began leaning during the main earthquake may be at risk of collapse during aftershocks, although communication and power supplies are gradually being restored, local officials said during the press conference.
More than 300 police officers, including traffic and community police personnel, were sent to the epicentre to carry out rescue and emergency relief work, the Nagqu police department said in a separate post on the messaging app WeChat earlier on Friday.
Officers sent to the region checked homes for damage and helped people relocate to safer locations, the Nagqu police also said in the WeChat post.
A video the police posted on Douyin, TikTok's sister app, showed officers packing supplies into a truck in the dark and inspecting a building and rubble with flashlights.
More than 12,000 people have been safely relocated, state media outlet Xinhua reported.
Videos previously released by local official media showed people leaving their homes and seeking shelter outside or in cars parked on the street. One resident reported being awakened by the strong quake and hearing the house squeaking during the tremor.
Read: Hundreds missing after devastating flood hits Nepal-Tibet border, 95 bodies recovered
President Xi Jinping said the tremor caused "significant casualties" and took place at a "high-altitude location" in cold weather.
"(We) must go all-out to carry out search and rescue operations and do our utmost to treat the injured, so as to minimise casualties," Xinhua quoted Xi as saying.
He called for assistance for residents and rescue equipment to be sent to the area promptly.
The epicentre was in a mountainous area about 190 kilometres (120 miles) east-northeast of Nagqu, and 390 kilometres northeast of the regional capital Lhasa, the US Geological Survey said.
It struck at 10:33 pm (1433 GMT) on Thursday at a shallow depth of around 10 kilometres.
Lhawang Dagpo, a local official in the Maru township, the quake's epicentre, said it put cracks in the walls of his office, according to Xinhua.
Power and telecoms services were disrupted in the county seat, the agency said.
Baqing County has mobilised more than 1,600 people to help in the relief operation, CCTV reported.
The municipal fire and rescue brigade has dispatched 25 vehicles and 110 personnel, and the Nagqu Armed Police Detachment sent 225 officers and soldiers and 18 vehicles, CCTV said.
As of 4:30 am on Thursday, relief supplies including 1,000 prefabricated houses, 3,239 tents, four generators and 1,000 flashlights had been delivered, it added.
Earthquakes in China are relatively common.
In January 2025, a quake in Tibet's rural Tingri county killed at least 126 people.
The disaster came little over a year after at least 148 people died in a quake in remote Gansu province in northwest China in December 2023, according to state media.
That quake was China's deadliest since 2014, when more than 600 people perished in the southwestern province of Yunnan.
A massive tremor in 2008 in Sichuan province left about 90,000 people dead or missing, including around thousands of schoolchildren.

title: R 4 foreign ministers  meeting reaffirms solidarity with Saudi Arabia over Houthi attacks
description: R 4 meets with foreign ministers of  Germany  France  UK and Italy  discuss developments in Gulf amid regional tensions
content:
R-4 meets with foreign ministers of Germany, France, UK and Italy, discuss developments in Gulf amid regional tensions
Foreign Minister/DPM Ishaq Dar on Friday met the foreign ministers of Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Egypt during the sixth Regional Four (R-4) Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, and expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia in the wake of recent Houthi attacks on the kingdom.
Diplomatic observers say the R-4 grouping is gradually positioning itself as a stabilising middle-tier platform, bridging Gulf, South Asian and Eastern Mediterranean perspectives, at a time when traditional alliances are being recalibrated in the aftermath of the Iran-US conflict.
The Istanbul meeting comes in the backdrop of increasing Houthi attacks on Saudi oil and civilian infrastructure that have reached an unprecedented scale and several conflicts that are converging around the same strategic fault lines that include regional security, energy supplies, maritime routes and the risk of wider war.
FM Dar is currently in Istanbul to attend the R-4 Foreign Ministers’ meeting.
In a post on X, the FO said that FM Dar participated in the 6th R-4 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Istanbul, alongside Turkiye FM Hakan Fidan, Saudi FM Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud and Egyptian FM Badr Abdelatty.
Read : R-4 forum focuses on regional security concerns
According to the FO statement, the foreign ministers expressed "solidarity with Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed their support for its sovereignty and territorial integrity, further condemning the Houthi attacks targeting the Kingdom and underscoring the importance of respecting state sovereignty".
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 participated in the 6th R4 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Istanbul today, alongside H.E. Hakan Fidan of Türkiye, H.H. Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud of Saudi Arabia, and H.E. Dr. Badr Abdelatty of… pic.twitter.com/PYgO1E3Xbf
FO stated that the ministers reviewed regional developments since their last meeting in New York, with particular focus on the situation in the Middle East and related security challenges/ conflicts.
The statement further noted that the ministers discussed ways to strengthen regional coordination and advance diplomatic efforts to promote lasting peace, security, and stability.
In a separate meeting of R-4 with the foreign ministers of Germany, France, the UK and Italy, developments in the Gulf region amid ongoing US-Iran tensions came under discussion.
In a post on X, FO said that the "meeting provided an opportunity for exchange of views on regional developments in the Gulf region, their social and economic impacts, and the urgent need to foster diplomatic engagement to resolve regional challenges of peace, security, and stability".
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 participated today in the first meeting in Istanbul with the Foreign Ministers of the R4 (Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Egypt), along with their counterparts from France, Germany, Italy and the United… pic.twitter.com/ON3eFokBRA
FO added that FM Dar briefed his counterparts on the diplomatic and mediatory role Pakistan continued to play in de-escalating tensions, preventing resumption of hostilities and promoting peace.
"All Ministers agreed for continued engagement in this format," the statement further noted.
A joint statement issued after the meeting by the FO condemned Houthi strikes on civilians and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and called on the Houthis to stop attacks on the kingdom.
"They expressed their full solidarity with the Government of Yemen and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and called on the Houthi militia to immediately cease all military actions, threats and attacks, and to return to the political process in good faith," the statement noted.
The ministers also condemned in the "strongest terms" the unacceptable escalation by the Houthi militia, which has deepened humanitarian suffering, as well as the continued strikes carried out by the Houthi militia against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, particularly those targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure, and the attacks carried out against commercial shipping in the Red Sea and the Bab Al Mandeb.
🔊 PR No. 3️⃣0️⃣5️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Joint Statement on the R4 Ministerial Meeting (Istanbul, 23 October 2026) 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/FnDl86yDoN
Concerning the military conflict between the US/Israel and Iran as well as around the Strait of Hormuz, the ministers underlined the urgent need to address this conflict only through dialogue and diplomacy as well as to prevent the "targeting of civilians and civilian infrastructure", including vessels.
The ministers also expressed support for the Islamabad MoU and welcomed continued diplomatic efforts to prevent further escalation and reaffirmed their commitment to a lasting negotiated solution.
"The Foreign Ministers of the Republic of Türkiye, Arab Republic of Egypt, Islamic Republic of Pakistan, and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (R4 Group) met today in İstanbul to discuss regional issues of mutual concern, united in their commitment to contribute to diplomatic efforts and guided by the mutual interest to promote peace and stability in the region and beyond, in line with the principles and purposes of the UN Charter," the statement said.
The ministers underscored that the Israeli occupation constitutes the "fundamental source of instability in the region" and beyond, and that Israeli policies create a deep sense of injustice in global public opinion, further calling for the early implementation of the two-state solution in accordance with the relevant UN resolutions.
According to the joint statement, the ministers reiterated their support for the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, including their inalienable right to self-determination and to establish an independent, sovereign, viable, and contiguous State of Palestine on the basis of the 4 June 1967 lines, with East Jerusalem as its capital, in accordance with relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions in order to achieve comprehensive peace in the Middle East.
The ministers also called for an urgent end to the ongoing Israeli violence, as well as attempts to change the legal and historical status of Jerusalem, and to bring an end to further destruction and humanitarian tragedy in Palestine, further condemning all the previous and current settlement activities in the West Bank and Jerusalem, as well as the settler violence against Palestinians while underlining the urgent need for uninterrupted flow of humanitarian aid and reconstruction in Gaza.
"The Ministers underscored the vital importance of freedom of navigation, permanent maritime safety and security, and safeguarding navigational rights and freedoms. They noted that disruption of sea lanes threatens the security and prosperity of all, through blocking global supply chains, flows of energy, fertiliser and food, impacting vulnerable populations in the region and beyond, and thus requires collective efforts by the international community to address these challenges," the FO said.
According to the statement, the ministers also rejected any measures or restrictions that impair lawful navigation and called for the swift and full resumption of safe, secure and unimpeded passage through the Strait of Hormuz.
The joint statement concluded by stating that the ministers agreed to "maintain close consultation and coordination on the afore-mentioned matters".
Dar meets French counterpart on R-4 sidelines
Meanwhile, FM Dar met with France’s Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs, Jean-Noel Barrot, on the sidelines of the R-4 meeting.
In a post on X, the FO stated that the two sides discussed ways to further strengthen Pakistan-France bilateral cooperation, adding that FM Dar underscored the importance of sustained engagement and regular dialogue to advance bilateral cooperation across areas of mutual interest.
FO noted that Dar and Barrot exchanged views on current regional and international developments, including the wider economic and social repercussions of ongoing crises, particularly the impact on energy costs.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 met with France’s Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs, Jean-Noël Barrot @JnBarrot , in Istanbul today. Recalling their recent meeting on the sidelines of the last UNGA, the two sides discussed ways… pic.twitter.com/HSDSaRVomp
"Both sides emphasised the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in addressing regional challenges and promoting peace and international cooperation," the statement added.
It said that FM Barrot appreciated Pakistan’s role and FM Dar's personal efforts in promoting sustained engagement and advancing diplomatic efforts towards regional peace and stability.
"DPM/FM appreciated France’s positive engagement alongside the UK, Germany and Italy with the R4 countries to discuss regional and international developments and support diplomatic efforts towards peace and stability," the FO stated.
Dar meets UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband
Separately, FM Dar met UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband on the sidelines of the R-4 meeting in Istanbul.
The FO said in a post on X that the two sides expressed satisfaction with Pakistan-UK bilateral relations and agreed to further strengthen bilateral cooperation in areas of mutual interest.
"They exchanged views on evolving regional and international developments, underscoring the importance of dialogue, diplomacy and continued engagement," the statement added.

The two sides expressed satisfaction with Pakistan-UK bilateral relations and agreed to further strengthen bilateral cooperation in… pic.twitter.com/11UbSrybzb
FO further noted that Miliband commended Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and stability.
According to the FO, FM Dar appreciated the UK’s constructive engagement with the R-4, alongside Germany, France and Italy, in support of regional peace and stability.
Meeting with Saudi FM Prince Faisal Al Saud
Meanwhile, FM Dar also met with Saudi FM Al Saud on the sidelines of the R-4 ministerial meeting.
In a post on X, the FO stated the two leaders reaffirmed the enduring strength of the fraternal ties between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia and their commitment to further strengthening their strategic partnership through close cooperation across all areas of interest and regular consultations at all levels.

Julianne Moore celebrates son Caleb’s wedding to Kibriyaá Morgan with a heartfelt speech after playing matchmaker
Julianne Moore delivered an emotional speech at her son Caleb Moore Freundlich’s wedding to Kibriyaá Morgan, celebrating the couple’s relationship nearly a decade after helping bring them together.
Caleb, 28, and Morgan, also 28, married in a civil ceremony at Brooklyn Borough Hall on October 8, followed by a larger wedding celebration on October 11 at The Roundhouse in Beacon, New York. The event was attended by approximately 140 guests, according to The New York Times .
Moore, 65, attended the wedding alongside her husband, filmmaker Bart Freundlich, and their daughter, Liv Helen Moore Freundlich. The actress also escorted her son down the aisle before sharing a speech reflecting on the newlyweds’ nine-year relationship.
“They have seen one another through college, Covid, early adulthood, career changes, their first apartment, their second apartment, Ben the cat!” Moore said. “I marvel at their commitment, and I celebrate their love.”
The couple’s love story began after Moore encouraged Caleb to connect with Morgan, whom she had met in 2013 while Morgan was helping recruit prospective students to Chapin School. At the time, Moore’s daughter was considering transferring to the school.
The actress later discovered that Morgan and Caleb were both attending Davidson College and suggested that her son look her up. They met in person in 2016 and initially became close friends before beginning their romantic relationship in February 2017.
Caleb proposed to Morgan in August 2024, with Moore announcing their engagement on Instagram and congratulating the couple.
Following the wedding, Moore shared footage of the newlyweds walking down the aisle, writing that her family loved them. Caleb and Morgan also celebrated their marriage on social media, with Morgan describing the wedding weekend as one she would cherish forever.
During the reception, Moore and her son danced to George Harrison’s song “Give Me Love”, adding another personal moment to the family celebration.

title: Sindh job reforms fail to curb merit complaints
description: Sindh Assembly  Prisons Department turn to private testing firm instead of government run academic institution
content:
Sindh Assembly, Prisons Department turn to private testing firm instead of government-run academic institution
Despite a series of reforms aimed at making government recruitment more transparent, complaints over merit-based hiring continue to dog Sindh’s job system.
The government’s efforts have struggled to deliver the promised change, largely because key measures have not been fully implemented. Some influential provincial institutions, including the Sindh Assembly and the Prisons Department, have themselves sidestepped the government’s recruitment mechanism.
Rather than using the testing service of the government-run Sukkur IBA University, which was engaged by the provincial government to help ensure merit in BPS-5 to BPS-15 recruitment, the two institutions have hired a private testing company to conduct tests for their vacant positions.
It is worth noting that the system for providing government jobs in the province is divided into three categories. Recruitment to BPS-1 to BPS-4 positions is carried out at the district level. For BPS-5 to BPS-15 positions, a digital platform called the Sindh Job Portal was established in 2025.
All departments were directed to receive applications for their vacant positions through the platform, while candidates who secured at least 40 marks through the testing service of Sukkur IBA University were declared eligible for these positions. The third category comprises BPS-16 and above positions, which are filled through the Sindh Public Service Commission (SPSC).
Unfortunately, questions have been raised for some time over the transparency of recruitment in all three categories. Several young people who were declared unsuccessful in the SPSC examination held in 2024 continued their protests for several months. Some of these candidates later succeeded in examinations conducted by the Federal Public Service Commission (FPSC).
The very notion that lower-grade jobs, from BPS-1 to BPS-4, are awarded on merit in the province also appears questionable. This can be gauged from a recently viral video of Provincial Minister for Prisons Haji Ali Hassan Zardari. In the video, when a journalist complains to him that jobs in his department are not being awarded on merit, the minister looks at the journalist in surprise and asks, “What merit is there in BPS-1 to BPS-4 jobs?”
A large proportion of government jobs in the province falls within BPS-5 to BPS-15. This is also why the majority of unemployed young people have traditionally applied for positions in these grades. Consequently, the provincial government has also faced greater pressure over government employment in this category.
For this reason, the Sindh government decided to improve the recruitment system, at least for this category of jobs, by establishing the Sindh Job Portal and engaging the testing service of Sukkur IBA University to ensure merit.
However, some influential departments have not implemented these government measures, citing their autonomous status. The Sindh Assembly and the Prisons Department are among the most prominent examples.
The two institutions used a private testing company to fill their vacant positions instead of engaging the testing service of Sukkur IBA University.
In this regard, The Express Tribune contacted the Secretary of the Provincial Assembly G.M. Umar Farooq to ask why the services of a government university’s testing service had not been obtained. However, he did not respond.
The same question was put to Inspector General of Prisons Fida Hussain Mastoi, but he also did not respond.

Authorities ban dangerous strings, metal wires and nylon strings
The Lahore district administration on Friday allowed kite-flying across the district, except in designated prohibited areas, from March 12 to 14, 2027, as part of Basant celebrations.
The Lahore deputy commissioner issued a formal notification outlining the dates, conditions and safety measures governing the manufacture, sale and use of kites and strings.
Under the notification, the manufacture of kites and strings would be permitted from September 5, 2026, to March 14, 2027.

Only registered shopkeepers would be allowed to sell kite-flying materials, and registered manufacturers and sellers would be required to maintain complete records of their stock and sales.
The notification sets a maximum length of 35 inches and a width of four-and-a-half githas for kites. The dimensions of guddas have been fixed at 34 inches in length and one-and-a-half tawas in width.
The manufacture and use of dangerous strings, metal wires, nylon strings and strings coated with sharp abrasive material had been prohibited.
Manufacturers have been directed to use only materials specifically permitted under the notification.
Compliance with safety measures, including the installation of safety rods on motorcycles, has also been made mandatory.
The district administration and police have been directed to ensure strict enforcement of the prescribed safety conditions during Basant.

'I could never do what I’m being accused of. It’s the worst thing anyone could accuse me of,' Thomas Sr said
Meghan Markle’s father, Thomas Markle Sr., has denied allegations that he possessed child pornography, describing the claims as “a bunch of lies” after reports emerged that his son had alerted authorities to the alleged discovery of the material.
The 82-year-old addressed the allegations in a statement to the Daily Mail on Friday, October 23, following reports that his son, Thomas Markle Jr., had allegedly found a large collection of child sexual abuse material among his father’s belongings.
“I’m shocked, I’m hurt and I’m very upset that my son is making these accusations against me. I could never do what I’m being accused of. It’s the worst thing anyone could accuse me of,” Thomas Sr. said.
“This is bull****. It’s just a bunch of lies. It’s sick. I have no idea why Tom is trying to destroy me with these lies,” he added.
According to reports by The Sun , Thomas Jr. claimed he discovered four large boxes containing computers and other belongings at his father’s former home in Cebu, Philippines. He alleged that the boxes contained hundreds or potentially thousands of images depicting child sexual abuse and said he reported the discovery to authorities.
Thomas Sr. disputed his son’s account, claiming the computers in question had not been in his possession since 2025. He said they had been packed in Mexico and transported to the Philippines by cargo ship, adding that he had repeatedly asked his son to return them.
“I don’t know who had access to the computers,” Thomas Sr. said, maintaining that he had never downloaded such material. He also claimed he had not spoken to his son in months and questioned why the allegations had been made.
The reports prompted renewed attention to Meghan’s estrangement from her father. The Duchess of Sussex issued a statement on October 23 expressing distress over the allegations and revealing that she had been made aware of troubling claims involving her father in 2018, shortly after her wedding to Prince Harry.
Meghan said a letter containing the allegations had been sent to the Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection, and that she had been assured the matter was being investigated. She also explained that keeping her children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, away from their grandfather had been a decision made to protect them.
“I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them,” she said.
Meghan added that her thoughts were with any children who may have been harmed and expressed hope that justice would be served. Thomas Sr. has strongly denied the allegations, which remain allegations and have not been established as fact.
The Metropolitan Police has said it is making internal enquiries to establish whether a letter was passed on in 2018. It has also clarified that it is not currently investigating a man in his 80s residing outside the United Kingdom. Philippine authorities have reportedly begun looking into the allegations.

content:
Diesel will cost Rs393.66 under the daily pricing mechanism
The federal government on Friday increased the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.91 per litre while keeping the price of petrol unchanged till October 26.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, petrol would continue to be sold at Rs377.71 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs393.66 per litre from October 24 to October 26.
The latest revision comes a day after the government decreased the price of petrol by Rs1.60 per litre while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.64 per litre for October 23.
Read : Govt cuts petrol by Rs1.60, increases diesel by 1.64 paisas for Oct 23
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Also Read : Govt mulls $2b LNG import decision
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices rose ​on Friday, with Brent crude touching its highest since late April, after Houthi attacks in Saudi ‌Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East, where UAE authorities also reported an oil spill.
Brent crude futures gained $4.01, or 3.54%, to $117.18 a barrel by 12:21 pm ET (1622 GMT). Brent's session high of $117.38 was the highest since the end of ​April. US West Texas Intermediate crude gained $3.75, or 3.77%, to $103.22.
"The market ​is concerned about these continued Iranian attacks on tankers that we've seen increase over the last week," said Andrew Lipow, president of ‌Lipow ⁠Oil Associates. "While there has been an increase in oil transiting out of the Strait of Hormuz, that could change at any minute."

title: Iran has detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if war resumes  officials say
description: Undersea cables carry 99  of global internet traffic  but under 1  of international bandwidth crosses Hormuz
content:
Undersea cables carry 99% of global internet traffic, but under 1% of international bandwidth crosses Hormuz
Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to target undersea communications cables in the Gulf if the United States and Israel attack Iran again, two senior Iranian security officials ​told Reuters .
Their comments followed warnings by Iranian officials that undersea cables in the region could become targets in any renewed conflict if diplomacy with Washington ‌collapses.
The two Iranian security officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, gave few details and did not say how or where exactly Tehran would carry out such attacks. But one of them said Iran would aim to prevent repairs after any attacks to prolong disruptions to communications, including internet connections.
"If Iran is attacked, there will be no more red lines ... from undersea cables to military bases, including covert ones," one ​of the officials said.
The official warned Washington not to "play with fire" and said Iran had full access to the undersea cables and could easily destroy them.
Yadollah ​Javani, the deputy head of political affairs for Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC), said on Wednesday that Iran could target seven major internet cables beneath ⁠the Strait of Hormuz if Iranian infrastructure came under attack.
Undersea cables carry around 99% of global internet traffic, according to the International Telecommunication Union, a UN agency. But the ​global impact of such attacks by Iran could be limited, as less than 1% of international bandwidth passes through the Strait of Hormuz, said Alan Mauldin, research director at telecommunications ​research firm TeleGeography.
The strait separates Iran and Oman, linking the Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.
Read More: Trump weighs quick end to Iran war against letting conflict 'wither'
The US Department of State and Iran's Foreign Ministry did not respond to Reuters ' requests for comment on the Iranian security officials' remarks. There was no immediate comment from Gulf states.
The plans for possible attacks on undersea cables reflect a conviction in Iran's leadership that a renewed US military ​campaign would have to be met with a stronger response than before.
Top security official Mohsen Rezaei warned this month that US-linked digital infrastructure across the Gulf, including data centres and ​AI facilities, could be targeted in a renewed conflict.
Washington's Gulf allies have invested heavily in such infrastructure and they "should hold Washington, not Tehran, responsible for any damage to undersea cables," the second Iranian ‌security official ⁠said.
Alex Vatanka, director of the Iran programme at the Middle East Institute in Washington, said such threats were intended to deter renewed conflict and put pressure on Washington by making Gulf governments and US companies fear for their investments in the region.
"Tehran wants Gulf states and corporate executives to press [US President Donald] Trump over the risks his policies pose to their investment plans," said Vatanka.
Multiple cable cuts could slow internet services and disrupt financial transactions, e-commerce and cloud computing, analysts said. The impact would depend on how operators rerouted traffic and ​the capacity available on alternative connections, Mauldin said.
Restoring ​connections during wartime could be difficult, ⁠experts said, and higher insurance costs and delays in obtaining permits to enter territorial waters could further complicate repairs.
Also Read: Yemeni army says over 35 Houthi fighters killed or wounded in Taiz
The Red Sea could offer a more significant target than the Strait of Hormuz, particularly if Iran had support from its Houthi allies in Yemen, though Tehran ​has made no public statement indicating it plans to target cables there.
The Red Sea carries data between Europe, East Africa and ​Asia, with capacity routed ⁠through it accounting for about 3% of global international demand and around 10% of traffic travelling between regions, Mauldin said.
Gulf governments have been investing heavily in technology to diversify beyond oil and become global artificial intelligence hubs, deepening ties with US technology firms.
Iranian strikes directly hit two Amazon Web Services facilities in the UAE in March and damaged infrastructure near one of its ⁠facilities in Bahrain. ​The IRGC named US tech companies including Microsoft, Google, Apple and Nvidia as legitimate targets at the ​height of the war in March.
Land-based connections can provide alternative routes for internet traffic, and Gulf states and US technology companies are investing in additional infrastructure to improve resilience.
Microsoft plans to invest more than $400 million in subsea ​and terrestrial connectivity across the Middle East by 2030.

title: Sofia Coppola says it was    embarrassing    to see herself snapping at mother in    Making Marie Antoinette
description: Rather than remove the scene  Sofia chose to preserve it because it reflected the honesty Eleanor wanted
content:
Rather than remove the scene, Sofia chose to preserve it because it reflected the honesty Eleanor wanted
Sofia Coppola has admitted that watching herself snap at her late mother, Eleanor Coppola, in behind-the-scenes footage from Marie Antoinette was embarrassing, but she ultimately decided to keep the candid moments in a new documentary honouring her mother’s vision.
The Oscar-winning filmmaker revisits the making of her 2006 period drama in Making Marie Antoinette , a documentary assembled from around 80 hours of footage Eleanor filmed during the production. The material captures Sofia directing the film, which starred Kirsten Dunst as the French queen, and offers an intimate look at the pressures and creative decisions behind the ambitious project.
One particularly personal scene shows Sofia sitting in her trailer while her mother asks her questions. Tired from the demands of the production and a press junket, the director expresses frustration at having to talk when she wants to prepare for filming.
“I was snapping at my mom. But it’s real,” Sofia said while reflecting on the footage, acknowledging that she would not have wanted the public to see that side of herself.
Rather than remove the scene, Sofia chose to preserve it because it reflected the honesty Eleanor wanted from the documentary. She explained that her mother was interested in showing the reality of filmmaking, including moments that were less flattering or polished.
The project also gave Sofia an opportunity to look back at herself as a younger filmmaker. Marie Antoinette was only her third feature film, and she said the footage reminded her of how much she has grown more comfortable asserting herself over the years.
Eleanor began revisiting the footage with her daughter during the COVID-19 pandemic, when the family was together at their home in Napa Valley. She had long wanted the material to become a documentary, but died in April 2024 before the project could be completed. Sofia subsequently worked with editor Aaron Matthews and other collaborators to bring her mother’s vision to the screen.
The documentary includes Diane Lane reading Eleanor’s journal entries from the period, adding her perspective to the footage. It also captures moments from the production involving Dunst, Jason Schwartzman and other members of the cast and crew.
Beyond the personal exchanges between mother and daughter, the film documents Sofia’s efforts to defend her creative choices on a large production. One recurring theme is her commitment to telling the story from Marie Antoinette’s perspective, even when members of the crew advocated for a greater focus on the male characters.
Sofia said revisiting the material has also given her a deeper appreciation of her mother’s perspective, particularly as she is now a mother herself. Completing the documentary became a way to fulfil Eleanor’s wishes while preserving her work as a documentarian.
Making Marie Antoinette arrives as Sofia’s original film marks its 20th anniversary. Initially met with mixed reviews, the period drama has since developed a devoted following, with renewed attention being paid to its distinctive visuals, costumes and approach to the historical genre.

title: Prince William makes surprise appearance on    The Graham Norton Show    in Royal first
description: The prince joined actors Cate Blanchett and Hannah Waddingham  conservationist Robert Irwin and singer Jorja Smith
content:
The prince joined actors Cate Blanchett and Hannah Waddingham, conservationist Robert Irwin and singer Jorja Smith
Prince William made a surprise appearance on The Graham Norton Show on Friday, October 23, marking a first for a working member of the British royal family on the popular BBC talk show.
The Prince of Wales, 44, joined actors Cate Blanchett and Hannah Waddingham, conservationist Robert Irwin and singer Jorja Smith for a special episode dedicated to the Earthshot Prize, the environmental initiative he founded in 2020. The appearance was recorded ahead of the broadcast, with the studio audience reacting with surprise when William joined the famous red sofa.
During the conversation, William discussed why he established the Earthshot Prize, which recognises and supports solutions to environmental challenges. He explained that years of hearing negative stories about the environment had left him feeling discouraged, inspiring him to create a platform that combined urgency with optimism.
“For many years I was hearing stories about environment issues and one thing that struck me was the negativity and doom which got me down,” William said. “I thought we could do something more powerful and more optimistic and the idea of an awards' ceremony came about and we could talk about urgency and optimism together.”
He added that the initiative aims to highlight people developing practical solutions and help expand their impact around the world. Blanchett, who serves on the Earthshot Prize Council, described the initiative as a “tapestry of solutions”, while Irwin serves as a global ambassador for the project. Waddingham previously hosted the 2023 Earthshot Prize ceremony in Singapore.
William also spoke about his life away from royal duties, revealing that he and his children, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis, enjoy watching The Celebrity Traitors . The prince said his children were particularly enthusiastic about the BBC reality competition.
“I love it, the family love it. Charlotte and Louis are obsessed with it. It's really good telly,” he said.
He also shared his admiration for filmmaker Christopher Nolan, describing himself as a fan of the director’s work. William said he enjoys films that encourage deeper thought, singling out The Dark Knight trilogy for its psychological depth.
When Norton asked about his childhood ambitions, William revealed that he had once dreamed of becoming either a police officer or a DJ, although he admitted he was not particularly good at the latter.
The special episode also featured a musical performance by Smith, who performed her song “Dancing” before joining the other guests for a conversation.
William's appearance comes ahead of the next Earthshot Prize awards ceremony, which will take place in Mumbai, India, in November. The event will bring together environmental innovators and public figures to recognise projects working to protect the planet.
The Earthshot Prize was launched in 2020 with the aim of supporting solutions across five environmental goals, including protecting and restoring nature, cleaning the air, reviving the oceans, building a waste-free world and fixing the climate.
The special edition of The Graham Norton Show aired on BBC One on October 23, offering viewers a rare opportunity to see the future king in a relaxed television interview outside the usual format of royal engagements.

The reality television star made the comments during a recent episode of The Kardashians , while discussing her ideal partner with comedian Nikki Glaser on the set of their upcoming film, The Fifth Wheel .

She then added, “Let me just say this: I am just really, really happy. That is all I will say for now.”

The pair have also reportedly travelled to Japan and Paris, while Kim has been seen supporting Hamilton at Formula One races.
Hamilton, 41, has previously been linked to singer Nicole Scherzinger and actress Sofía Vergara. Kim shares four children, North, Saint, Chicago and Psalm, with her former husband, rapper Kanye West.
A source previously told People that Kim was “very into him”, adding that the couple made time for each other despite their busy careers.

Speaking to The Times , she said she had wanted to heal and work on herself before opening up to romance again.
Her latest comments offer a rare glimpse into her relationship with Hamilton, although she has not directly confirmed that he is the person who fulfils her partner checklist.

title: Baywatch  star David Charvet opens up about depression after quitting Hollywood
description: Baywatch  star David Charvet reveals depression and identity loss after leaving Hollywood to raise his own children
content:
'Baywatch' star David Charvet reveals depression and identity loss after leaving Hollywood to raise his own children
Baywatch star David Charvet has opened up about experiencing depression after stepping away from Hollywood to focus on raising his children.
The 54-year-old actor discussed the emotional challenges of leaving the entertainment industry during the October 22 episode of Fox’s Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test .
Charvet, who shares daughter Rain, 19, and son Shaya, 18, with his ex-wife Brooke Burke, said becoming a father influenced his decision to put his acting career on hold. He explained that his own childhood experiences shaped his determination to remain present in his children’s lives.
The actor revealed that his father left his mother before he was born, leaving him without a close relationship with his dad. He said the experience made him understand the importance of family bonds and motivated him to give his children the love and support he had missed growing up.
Charvet said he was travelling around the world for work when he decided he did not want his children to experience a similar absence. He subsequently stepped away from Hollywood and began rebuilding his life outside the spotlight.
However, the transition was difficult. “It was a very difficult first three years,” Charvet said, explaining that he went through a period of depression and felt he had lost his identity. He added that showing his children love and dedication remained his priority.
The actor is now returning to television through Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test , marking his first TV appearance in approximately 20 years. Charvet said he was motivated to participate partly because his children had never seen him on television and he wanted them to witness him taking on the challenge.
He also revealed that training with his son helped him prepare for the competition, although he found the psychological challenges particularly demanding.
New episodes of Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test air Thursdays at 9pm ET on Fox.

title: Collateral damage feared in K P IBO s if residents fail to move away from terrorists  Sanaullah
description: Says around 70pc of terrorist formations are present in designated districts of K P
content:
Says around 70pc of terrorist formations are present in designated districts of K-P
Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah on Friday warned of possible collateral damage during planned intelligence-based operations in designated districts of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa if residents failed to distance themselves from terrorists or drive them out of their localities.
Speaking on the private television programme Naya Pakistan , Sanaullah said terrorists entered Pakistan from Afghanistan and carried out attacks, alleging that training camps across the border operated with Indian funding and training, while reports also suggested Israeli involvement in such attacks.
“That is why Pakistan’s armed forces have closed the border with Afghanistan. You must also be aware that no trade is taking place through that route,” he said.
Read : PM Shehbaz defends emergency, governor’s rule in K-P, blames PTI for resurgence of terrorism
Praising the security forces for their work, the PML-N leader said they knew the number of terrorists and their current locations.
He said terrorist groups comprised between three and 15 members, adding that around 70 per cent of these groups were present in the areas designated for the operations, for which a separate development committee had also been established.
According to Sanaullah, the terrorists were hiding among the local population and living alongside ordinary citizens rather than operating openly. He said law enforcement agencies were conducting intelligence-based operations in these areas.
The adviser warned that civilians could suffer collateral damage if residents did not remove terrorists from their communities or move away from the areas to allow security forces to carry out operations.
“The people have been told either to drive these elements out of their populated areas or, if they do not want to do so, to move aside themselves so that the operation can proceed. If neither of these options is possible, there is a risk of collateral damage,” he said.
Sanaullah said the armed forces could dismantle and neutralise the terrorist groups within three to five months and criticised inactive K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi for what he described as a lack of cooperation with law enforcement agencies in tackling terrorists and their facilitators.
He alleged that the provincial leadership had previously supported the terrorists and discouraged cooperation with security forces, telling them that operations against the militants would not be allowed.
Also Read : Sanaullah links reversal of K-P governor's rule to PTI support for counterterrorism efforts
However, he said the situation had now changed, and a committee had been established under the chairmanship of a former governor. He expressed confidence that dismantling the terrorist networks in the coming months was an achievable objective.
Asked how future security operations would differ from previous intelligence-based operations (IBOs), given that 7,177 such operations had been conducted over the past six months, Sanaullah said the provincial government and civil administration would be responsible for holding areas after they had been cleared of terrorists.
He said the authorities would ensure that militants could not return to the cleared areas or establish a presence there again.
“Things were different earlier. Many areas were cleared three or four times, but the problem persisted because the responsibilities that should have been fulfilled by the provincial government and civil administration were not carried out. Their attitude was, in fact, the opposite,” he said.
Sanaullah said it would take months, rather than years, to rid the affected areas of terrorism and restore peace.
His remarks came a day after Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a Rs160 billion development package for K-P following a meeting with the Area Development Council, comprising representatives of the tribal districts and tribal elders, at the Governor House in Peshawar.
The prime minister said he had directed the authorities to strengthen the Counter Terrorism Department and make it more effective. He also assured that the federal government would provide all necessary resources to eradicate terrorism.

Louis Partridge to star in and produce 'One Last Summer', a coming-of-age film shot in Tuscany with Mia Jenkins
Enola Holmes star Louis Partridge is set to headline and produce One Last Summer , an independent coming-of-age film that has completed filming in Tuscany, Italy.
Partridge, also known for his role in House of Guinness , will star alongside Mia Jenkins, whose credits include Love Me Love Me and Geek Girl , and Jude Carmichael, who appeared in Dear England at the National Theatre. Additional casting details have not yet been announced.
Written and directed by Misha Citron, the film follows Milo, played by Partridge, who returns to the Tuscan countryside to visit the home of his late, estranged father. He arrives with his best friend Zac, portrayed by Carmichael, before agreeing to a double date with two American travellers.
What begins as an enjoyable encounter gradually takes an unexpected turn, forcing the characters to confront their past experiences, their present identities and the changes they face as they prepare to leave Italy. The story explores youth, attraction, insecurity, grief and the intensity of relationships formed over a short period.
Partridge and Citron have co-founded Pipe Dream Films, the production company behind One Last Summer . Partridge described the project as an opportunity to experience creative collaboration from both sides of the camera, adding that the filmmakers hoped to create something that would appeal to young audiences while retaining a broader emotional connection.
Citron said the film aims to capture the intimacy and emotional intensity of youth, including the uncertainty surrounding attraction, fear and loss.
The project is produced by Jim Parks, known for Steven Soderbergh’s The Christophers , alongside Maya Nurmohamed and Saskia Steinberg of Blue Lobster Productions.
The film marks another project for Partridge as he expands his work beyond acting into production. A release date for One Last Summer has not been announced.

description: Plot details for  Red  White   Royal Wedding  remain under wraps  although the title has fuelled anticipation
content:
Plot details for 'Red, White & Royal Wedding' remain under wraps, although the title has fuelled anticipation
Nicholas Galitzine has described filming Red, White & Royal Wedding as a “nice reset” after completing work on the intense Second World War drama The Mosquito Bowl, reflecting on the contrast between the two projects.
Speaking to Variety, Galitzine discussed moving between the romantic comedy sequel and Peter Berg’s historical war film, which required a physically demanding and immersive approach to depicting the experiences of American servicemen during the Pacific campaign.
In The Mosquito Bowl, Galitzine plays John McLaughry, one of four talented American college football players who abandon their promising sporting careers to enlist in the US Marine Corps after the attack on Pearl Harbor. The film also stars Bill Skarsgård as Bob Bauman, Ray Nicholson as Tony Butkovich and Tom Francis as David Schreiner.
Based on Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Buzz Bissinger’s book The Mosquito Bowl: A Game of Life and Death in World War II, the film follows the young athletes as they confront the brutal realities of war and the bonds formed between men facing extraordinary circumstances.
The production pushed Galitzine beyond his previous experiences as an actor. In an interview with Netflix’s Tudum, he described how the cast performed much of the action themselves, with limited use of stunt doubles. He recalled explosions going off just feet away, trees catching fire and the sounds of war surrounding them during filming.
By contrast, Red, White & Royal Wedding returns Galitzine to the romantic world of Prince Henry, the British royal whose relationship with American politician Alex Claremont-Diaz, played by Taylor Zakhar Perez, became the focus of the 2023 film Red, White & Royal Blue.
The sequel sees both actors reprise their roles, with Jamie Babbit directing a screenplay written by Gemma Burgess, Matthew López and original novel author Casey McQuiston. The returning cast includes Uma Thurman, Sarah Shahi, Rachel Hilson, Ellie Bamber, Clifton Collins Jr. and Stephen Fry, alongside new additions Henry Ashton and Alex Høgh Andersen.
Plot details for Red, White & Royal Wedding remain under wraps, although the title has fuelled anticipation about the next chapter in Henry and Alex’s relationship.
Galitzine has continued to build a diverse filmography, moving between romantic dramas, historical stories and thrillers. His credits include The Idea of You, Mary & George and The Craft: Legacy, while his role in Red, White & Royal Blue helped introduce him to a wider international audience.
The Mosquito Bowl is scheduled to open in select cinemas on October 30 before arriving on Netflix on November 25, 2026. A release date for Red, White & Royal Wedding has not yet been announced.

title: AI discovered bugs may soon trigger fresh disruptions  cyber experts say
description: Government websites in Europe and elsewhere suffered outages from Wednesday after weaknesses were found in PHP
content:
Government websites in Europe and elsewhere suffered outages from Wednesday after weaknesses were found in PHP
Advances in artificial intelligence have uncovered a stream of new software vulnerabilities that are almost ​certain to trigger more disruption along the lines of the outages that percolated across global government websites this week, according to seven cybersecurity professionals who spoke to ‌ Reuters .
AI helped drive a doubling of the number of digital flaws discovered year-on-year, according to research due to be published in the coming days by VulnCheck, a Massachusetts-based threat intelligence firm.
Matthew Prince, the chief executive of the digital infrastructure firm Cloudflare, told Reuters he was aware of “a bunch of additional severe vulnerabilities that are present in other pieces of critical software” and predicted busy months ahead as AI surfaced long-hidden weaknesses in the ​fabric of the internet.
“I think we’re going to have a couple years where every single week it’s going to feel like the sky is falling,” Prince said in an ​interview on Thursday.
Read More: Millions of hacking attempts as companies, governments rush to patch PHP flaws
The outages that spread across government sites in Europe and elsewhere beginning on Wednesday happened after the discovery of weaknesses in PHP, ⁠a venerable programming language that powers a huge swath of the internet. Operators have been rushing to fix their software in anticipation of mass exploitation and, because some felt they could ​not patch before hackers jumped in, a subset simply yanked their sites offline until they could make them safe.
VulnCheck researcher Patrick Garrity said the scramble to fix PHP came during an already busy ​week in cybersecurity. The week also brought disclosures of vulnerabilities PHP alternative Node.js and streaming program Plex, breaches tied to AI gateway LiteLLM and development platform Railway, and the revelation that the Indian certificate authority eMudhra had used an extraordinarily flimsy cryptographic key that potentially put users across the internet at risk.
“If we just saw four or five things like this, this week, I would expect we’re going to see a lot more,” Garrity said. “I ​think there’s going to be a lot more fire drills for anything that’s internet exposed.”
The codebases that run modern programs are sprawling and mistakes, or “bugs,” that open up potential avenues ​for exploitation often crop up in unexpected places.
Previously, finding bugs required a baseline level of skill, and taking advantage of those bugs to build digital lockpicks – called “exploits” – could be expected to take weeks or months ‌of work ⁠by an experienced professional.
That would in the past have provided defenders a little breathing room to fix bugs and gently roll out software updates.
AI has effectively thrown those assumptions out the window . Models can find one bug after another by subjecting codebases to round-the-clock scrutiny, and can turn around exploits in hours. Shane Fry, the chief technology officer of Virginia-based RunSafe Security, said the demonstrated performance of AI models over the past few months had effectively laid to rest any doubts over whether they would change the industry.
“What's fundamentally, and unquestionably, changing is the timescale for not only finding ​vulnerabilities, but how quickly adversaries can weaponise ​them,” Fry said.
Also Read: Microsoft develops AI tool that can diagnose 'sequentially' like a doctor
While all the experts ⁠Reuters spoke to agreed that defenders’ timelines were getting shorter, they were split on whether AI would lead to a hacker free-for-all.
Daniel Stenberg, the lead developer of the file transfer tool curl, argued the vulnerabilities found by AI models tended to be exotic bugs that were difficult for ​rogue actors to take advantage of. Ramy Rahman, a senior principal solutions engineer at cybersecurity company ArmorCode, said “more disclosed vulnerabilities do not ​automatically mean more successful attacks."
There ⁠was tentative evidence of that around the PHP vulnerability that drew worldwide concern this week. Threat intelligence firm Hunt.io said that – like and Cloudflare – it had seen aggressive attempts to take advantage of the bug. But the firm’s head of research, Esteban Borges, said that, as of 2 p.m. Eastern Time on Thursday (1800 GMT), the cybercriminals he tracked to cobble together a working tool ⁠to take ​advantage of it.
Prince, of Cloudflare, told Reuters he had seen anecdotal evidence of compromises linked to the PHP vulnerability.
The ​deluge of AI-driven discoveries might rattle the industry, but would be a net positive in the end, he said, comparing it to slaying the monsters in a haunted house.
The confrontation might be scary, he said, but leaving the monsters to lurk ​quietly behind closed doors was far worse.
“The reality is, we’re going to get a lot of this stuff cleaned up,” he said.

Eddie and Susie plan an ambitious casino project in the Middle East as danger threatens their criminal empire
Robert Carlyle, Elijah Wood and Orlando Bloom are among the new cast members joining The Gentlemen as production begins on the Netflix crime drama’s third season in the UK and Morocco.
The trio will appear alongside Dexter Fletcher, Bruna Marquezine, Ed Speleers, Saffron Burrows and Bugzy Malone, according to Variety . The new additions mark their first collaboration with series creator Guy Ritchie, while Wood and Bloom reunite after starring together in The Lord of the Rings films.
The returning series follows Eddie Horniman, played by Theo James, and Susie Glass, portrayed by Kaya Scodelario, as they build a criminal enterprise after Eddie inherits Halstead Manor.
Ray Winstone will return as crime boss Bobby Glass, alongside Joely Richardson as Lady Sabrina, Vinnie Jones as Geoff, Jasmine Blackborow as Charly, Harry Goodwins as Jack, Benjamin Clementine and Maya Jama.
Daniel Ings, who played Eddie’s older brother Freddy in the first two seasons, was not included in the announced returning cast. Giancarlo Esposito, who appeared as American billionaire Stanley Johnston, was also absent from the list. Their involvement in the new season has not been confirmed by the announcement.
According to the season three synopsis, Eddie and Susie pursue their most ambitious venture yet by planning to build a casino in the Middle East. Their plans face mounting danger, raising questions about whether Eddie’s ambition could threaten their operation.
The third season will consist of eight episodes, each running approximately 60 minutes. Ritchie created the series and is writing the new instalment with Matthew Read. Ritchie and Evan Creevy are directing.
Produced by Moonage Pictures for Netflix and Miramax TV, the series follows its second season, which launched in September. Netflix renewed The Gentlemen for a third season in August, with Ritchie saying the story’s growing ambition and expanding world made another instalment feel inevitable.
The newly announced cast adds several established performers to a series centred on power, family ties and the risks of expanding a criminal empire.

description: The couple welcome baby boy Azmar  sharing his name and a heartfelt prayer with fans
content:
Share his name and a heartfelt prayer with fans
Pakistani showbiz stars Mawra Hocane and Ameer Gilani shared the heartwarming news of welcoming their baby boy, revealing his name in an emotional Instagram post that has touched the hearts of their fans.
The couple took to Instagram to share a beautiful moment from the hospital, where he was seen reciting a prayer for his newborn son. Announcing the little one’s arrival, he introduced him as Azmar, a name that means “lion,” symbolising strength and courage.
In his heartfelt caption, Ameer wrote: “Our son ‘Azmar’ — it means lion. وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ ‘And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be content.’ Alhamdulillah. Syed Azmar Hussain Kamal Gilani, the king of our jungle, our pride, our littlest most precious treasure.”
The touching announcement reflected the couple’s happiness as they stepped into a new chapter of their lives as parents. Gilani’s choice to share a prayer alongside the announcement added a deeply spiritual and emotional touch to the special moment.
Mawra also shared the announcement on her Instagram Story, revealing that the couple had finally decided to share their little secret with the world.
“Our little secret ... is yours. We could fully do with some extra prayers and love,” she wrote, inviting fans and well-wishers to keep their growing family in their prayers.
The announcement quickly became a joyous moment for their admirers, with the couple’s fans celebrating the arrival of their little bundle of joy and sending love and prayers to the new parents.
Many sent their congratulations while others also applauded the couple's simplicity. "No pregnancy announcement, no gender reveal, direct the baby, love ittt", one user wrote.
Hocane and Gilani are among Pakistan’s popular on-screen and off-screen couples. Their relationship attracted considerable attention from fans, particularly because of their natural chemistry in television dramas.
The two actors worked together in the popular drama Sabaat , which brought them together on screen, and later reunited in Neem . Their performances and on-screen pairing won them a dedicated fan following, with viewers often expressing their admiration for their chemistry.
The couple eventually confirmed their real-life romance when they announced their marriage in February 2025. Their wedding celebrations delighted fans, who had long speculated about their relationship.
Mawra, known for her performances in Pakistani television and films, has built a successful career with projects including Sammi , Sabaat , Qissa Meherbano Ka and the Bollywood film Sanam Teri Kasam . Ameer has also established himself as a recognised television actor through dramas such as Sabaat , Neem and Very Filmy .
With the arrival of their son, Syed Azmar Hussain Kamal Gilani, the couple has begun an exciting new chapter beyond their professional achievements. Their heartfelt announcement has offered fans a glimpse into their happiness as they embrace parenthood, with prayers, love and warm wishes pouring in for the family.

title: Asim crashes out of ABC Cup

content:
Egypt’s El Hammamy, England’s Curtis Malik advance to semi-finals of squash event
Pakistan’s last remaining hope Asim Khan suffered a quarter-final defeat at the Venice ABC Cup at DHA Creek Club here on Friday, losing 3-1 to Egypt’s Karim El Hammamy in the men’s singles event.
Asim, one of Pakistan’s experienced campaigners, made a promising start after losing the opening game 11-8. He fought back strongly to win the second set 11-7 and level the match 1-1.
However, El Hammamy regained control in the following games, winning 11-8 and 11-7 to seal victory and book his place in the semi-finals.
The Egyptian capitalised on Asim’s weaknesses in the closing stages while the Pakistani appeared to struggle with fatigue as the match progressed.
Pakistan’s other experienced player Nasir Iqbal had already exited the competition in the first round, leaving Asim as the country’s key representative in the men’s singles quarter-finals.
In another men’s singles quarter-final, top seed Curtis Malik of England defeated Z Ibrahim 3-0 to advance to the semi-finals. Malik dominated the encounter, winning 11-8, 11-8, 11-5.
Egypt’s Yassin Shohdy also progressed after defeating compatriot Salah Eltorgman 3-1. Shohdy lost the second game 11-4 after taking the opener 11-9, but recovered to win the third 11-5 before clinching the fourth 12-10.
In the women’s singles quarter-finals, Egypt’s Habiba Rizk overcame England’s Lucy Turmel 3-2 in a closely contested encounter. Rizk won 11-7, 11-8 and 11-8 in the first, third and deciding games, while Turmel took the second 11-8 and the fourth 11-3.
Egypt’s Rowan Elaraby defeated Hong Kong’s Toby Tse 3-0, winning 11-4, 11-1, 11-8. Nadine Shahin of Egypt beat Japan’s Akari Midorikawa 3-1, while compatriot Amina El Rihany swept South Africa’s Hayley Ward 3-0, winning 11-7, 11-2, 11-9 in the quarter-finals.

content:
The eight-episode series premieres on Friday with viewers able to stream it online through regional streaming services
Hudson Williams is returning to television with Yaga , a mystery thriller inspired by Slavic folklore that sees the Heated Rivalry star take on a new role in a story involving a missing heir, suspicious characters and ancient magic. The eight-episode series premieres on Friday, October 23, with viewers able to stream it online through regional streaming services.
In the United States, Yaga will be available exclusively on AMC+, while Canadian audiences can watch the series on Crave. The show will also be available on Sky and NOW in the UK and Ireland, with BINGE and Foxtel On Demand carrying it in Australia.
The series launches with its first two episodes on October 23, followed by weekly releases on Fridays. The final two episodes are scheduled to arrive together on November 27.
For viewers in the United States, AMC+ offers subscription plans with and without adverts, as well as a seven-day free trial for eligible new subscribers. The service is also available through Prime Video Channels. Availability and trial terms may vary by platform and location.
Yaga follows private investigator Charlie Rapp, played by Noah Reid, who arrives in the coastal town of Whittock to investigate the disappearance of Henry Park, a young heir to a powerful fishing business portrayed by Williams. The investigation brings Rapp into conflict with local detective Carson, played by Clark Backo, and university professor Katherine, portrayed by Carrie-Anne Moss.
Williams plays both Henry Park and his look-alike roommate, Logan Casey, adding another layer of mystery to the story. The series combines a police investigation with supernatural elements, dark humour, complicated relationships and a reimagining of the legendary witch Baba Yaga.
The cast also includes Sheila McCarthy, Megan Follows, Ezra Franky, Patrick Gilmore, Katharine Isabelle and Hiro Kanagawa. Kat Sandler created the television adaptation from her own stage play and serves as its writer and showrunner.

title: Pakistan reach Johar Cup final
description: Green shirts hold Japan to set up Malaysia showdown
content:
Green-shirts hold Japan to set up Malaysia showdown
Pakistan on Friday qualified for the final of the Sultan of Johor Cup hockey tournament despite being held to a 2-2 draw by Japan in their crucial last league game in Ipoh, Malaysia.
Goals from Hamza Fayyaz and Ghulam Mustafa helped Green-shirts recover from a deficit at the Taman Daya Hockey Stadium in Johor Bahru.
Both sides finished the league stage with seven points each and a goal difference of plus eight, but Pakistan advanced to Saturday's final because they scored more goals than Japan, netting 18 compared with their rivals' 16.
Pakistan will face unbeaten hosts Malaysia in the final, having recorded victories over China and Canada before losing narrowly to Malaysia earlier in the tournament.
The Green-shirts defeated China 8-3 and Canada 6-2 before suffering a 3-2 defeat against Malaysia, which left their hopes of reaching the final dependent on the final round of matches.
Pakistan responded to the pressure against Japan, with Fayyaz scoring in the 34th minute and Mustafa adding the second in the 43rd minute to secure the draw they needed.
The result sets up a rematch with Malaysia, who have emerged as the tournament's strongest side after winning all three of their earlier matches.
Malaysia beat Pakistan 3-2 in their previous meeting to maintain their unbeaten record and move closer to the final. The hosts also gained some revenge after losing twice to Pakistan in last month's Junior Asia Cup in Inner Mongolia, China.
Pakistan had an early opportunity in that match when they were awarded a penalty stroke in the 12th minute, but goalkeeper Abid Amsyar Hanif saved Rana Waleed's flick.
Malaysia took the lead through T. Naaveennash Panicker in the 28th minute before Adeel equalised for Pakistan in the 36th minute.
The match turned in Malaysia's favour when Waleed was shown a red card in the 51st minute for striking an opponent with his stick. Mustafa Ghulam received a yellow card three minutes later, further reducing Pakistan's options.
Malaysia took advantage of their numerical superiority as Safwan Salihe restored their lead in the 55th minute before Naaveennash scored again two minutes later.
Despite earning eight penalty corners, Malaysia could not add to their tally.
Pakistan will now have the opportunity to challenge the hosts for the title on Saturday with a tournament victory within reach after their resilient performance against Japan to secure a place in the final.

title: WAPDA dominate National Athletics
