content:
Yasir snares javelin gold as Arshad Nadeem stays away
WAPDA on Friday continued their dominance at the National Athletics Championships on Friday, winning several gold medals here at the NED University of Engineering and Technology.
Pakistan’s No2 javelin thrower and Asian bronze medallist Yasir Sultan, who belongs to WAPDA, claimed gold with a throw of 74.63 metres. Navy's Abdul Qadeer Khan finished second with 67.25 metres, while Higher Education Commission’s (HEC) Muhammad Bilal secured bronze with 66.69 metres.
Olympic champion Arshad Nadeem was not in action on the second day, leaving Yasir to lead the field in the event.
According to sources Arshad was not feeling well and skipped the event.
WAPDA also secured gold in the women's javelin throw through Fatima Hussain, who recorded a distance of 41.76 metres. Punjab's Sania Ijaz took silver with 41.59 metres, while HEC's Khadija Mehreen claimed bronze with 40.43 metres. Mehreen had won the women's shot put title on the opening day.
In the men's pole vault, WAPDA's Hassan cleared 4.10 metres to take gold. Punjab's Abdul Rehman finished second with 3.40 metres, while Navy's Ikram Zahoor took third place with 3.30 metres.
HEC's Khaula Qamar Khan won the women's 400 metres in 58.76 seconds. WAPDA's Rida claimed silver with 59.47 seconds, while HEC's Kinza Sarfraz finished third with 59.59 seconds.
WAPDA continued their success in the men's 400 metres, where Salman Ahmed secured gold with a time of 48.40 seconds. Teammate Zewar Shah took silver with 48.60 seconds, while former national champion Abdul Mueed Baloch of PAF finished third by clocking 48.82 seconds.
Navy's Amtul Rehman won the women's high jump with 1.55 metres. WAPDA's Noreen Fatima took silver with 1.45 metres, while Sindh's Anaya Ahsan secured bronze with 1.40 metres.
Muhammad Azam of WAPDA won the men's 110-metre hurdles in 14.85 seconds, narrowly ahead of HEC's Abu Bakar, who clocked 14.88 seconds. WAPDA's Aks Miran finished third with 15.31 seconds.
In women's 10,000 metres, WAPDA's Maria Bibi claimed gold in 43 minutes and 35 seconds. HEC's Gonash Batool finished second to collect her second medal of the championships, having earlier won silver in the 1,500 metres. WAPDA's Mahnoor Afzal took bronze.

content:
Residents of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town have reported a worsening food crisis since 2022
The White House said on Friday that United States First Lady Melania Trump has secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will begin on October 29.
Residents ‌of the southern Ukrainian town, occupied by Russian forces since February 2022, have reported a deepening food crisis.
"Both nations agreed to temporarily stop all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare ​a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway," a White House statement said.
https://t.co/7SCCBYIYZR pic.twitter.com/E2pZCGriHe
The development ​comes as Melania Trump's husband, President Donald Trump, pressures Ukrainian President Volodymyr ⁠Zelensky to reach an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the war, which ​began when Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022.
Melania Trump has been active in trying to ​get Ukrainian children seized by Russia during the war returned to their families.
"The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster. Oleshky's remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly ​residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food, and clean water," Melania Trump said in ​the statement.
Read More: Russia, Ukraine exchange strikes as US envoy leaves after talks
Melania's focus is ‘to save children,’ Trump
US President Donald Trump said on Friday that first lady Melania Trump’s focus is on saving children, after she announced a Russia-Ukraine agreement for a temporary ceasefire in the southern Ukrainian city of Oleshky.
Asked by reporters as he departed the White House whether the first lady would take part in trilateral peace talks, Trump said: “That is not the worst idea I’ve ever heard.”
“What she wants to do is save children, and that’s her focus. And both sides are cooperating with her, so doing a very good job,” he said.
“Her initiative, and they contacted both sides, and both sides wanted to do it,” he added.
Russia welcomes US first lady Melania Trump’s efforts to coordinate a localized truce for humanitarian purposes in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, in Ukraine’s Kherson region, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said on Friday.
Speaking to reporters, Peskov said military officials were working to coordinate the ceasefire to facilitate the humanitarian operation, adding that “those who wish to leave the town will be able to do so.”
He said the operation requires extensive and complex preparations involving various parties, with Melania Trump playing a coordinating role.
Peskov said the issue was discussed in a recent telephone conversation between Russian President Vladimir Putin and US his counterpart Donald Trump.
The ceasefire will allow non-military teams from both countries to visit residents in their homes and coordinate ‌transportation for ⁠those wishing to evacuate to either Russia or Ukraine, with an unnamed American media organisation accompanying the teams to document the process, the first lady said.
Newsmax, a right-leaning news outlet, said in a report that its cameras would be granted "exclusive access to document the effort".
Oleshky, located across ​the Dnipro River from ​Kherson, has a remaining ⁠population of 1,700 to 2,000 people — primarily elderly residents, along with about 50 children — down from roughly 24,000 before the war, the White House ​said. About 90% of the city flooded after the destruction of the Kakhovka Dam, according to the White House.
The statement said Melania Trump and her representative worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms of the localised ceasefire.
"Residents who wish to evacuate will ⁠receive ​coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate ​some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine,” Melania said.

title: At least seven killed in attack at church in Jordan  state owned outlet says
description: Sources said two gunmen opened fire for at least seven minutes in a church in Karak area
content:
Sources said two gunmen opened fire for at least seven minutes in a church in Karak area
At least seven people were killed and 10 others injured on Friday when gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan's Karak governorate, the state-owned television station Al-Mamlaka reported.
Security forces had deployed at the church and were pursuing the suspects, the station reported.
It said two gunmen got out of a vehicle and opened fire during a funeral procession at the Hamoud church in Karak.
Khaled Burqan, a man who had been attending the funeral, told Al-Mamlaka that dozens of people had been attending the funeral and two men - one carrying a rifle and another carrying a pistol - opened fire on them for several minutes.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack, and Jordanian authorities did not say who was responsible.
Such attacks are extremely rare in Jordan, which is relatively stable but has been increasingly targeted by Iranian attacks this year since the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February.
Christians make up a minority of Jordan's population, though the country is home to several biblical sites that attract Christian pilgrims from around the world.

Following the discussions and submission of the proposed arrangements, police granted permission for the concert to proceed. The organisers also dismissed reports suggesting that the Delhi event had been cancelled, confirming that it would take place as scheduled.

Banks expressed confidence in Fanning’s ability to take on the younger version of the colourful Capitol escort
Elizabeth Banks is confident that Elle Fanning will bring Effie Trinket to life in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , revealing that she knew the actress would excel in the role.
Banks, who portrayed Effie in the original Hunger Games film series, shared her thoughts on Fanning’s casting in an interview with PEOPLE. The actress and filmmaker expressed confidence in Fanning’s ability to take on the younger version of the colourful Capitol escort, a character Banks made popular on screen.
Fanning will portray a younger Effie in the upcoming prequel, which takes place decades before the events of the original The Hunger Games films. The story follows the 50th Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell, and centres on a young Haymitch Abernathy long before he becomes Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark’s mentor.
The casting gives Fanning the opportunity to put her own stamp on Effie, whose distinctive fashion, elaborate wigs and memorable mannerisms made her one of the franchise’s recognisable characters. While Banks played Effie as an eccentric Capitol figure who gradually revealed a more compassionate side, the prequel will explore an earlier chapter in the character’s life.
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is based on Suzanne Collins’ novel of the same name and is directed by Francis Lawrence, who has helmed several films in the franchise. The cast also includes Joseph Zada as young Haymitch Abernathy, Whitney Peak as Lenore Dove Baird, Ralph Fiennes as President Snow, Jesse Plemons as Plutarch Heavensbee and Kieran Culkin as Caesar Flickerman.
The film is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on November 20, 2026, bringing audiences back to Panem for another chapter in the dystopian saga.
With Banks backing Fanning’s casting, the prequel will introduce a fresh interpretation of Effie Trinket while connecting the new story to the character audiences came to know in the original films.

title: Francis Lawrence says    Sunrise on the Reaping    brings back what fans loved about    Hunger Games
description: The film follows Haymitch Abernathy during the 50th Hunger Games  24 years before Katniss   s story
content:
The film follows Haymitch Abernathy during the 50th Hunger Games, 24 years before Katniss’s story
Francis Lawrence has explained why The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping feels like a return to form for the franchise, while promising audiences a fresh take on familiar elements of the dystopian series.
In an interview with GamesRadar+ , Lawrence said reading Suzanne Collins’s novel brought back the excitement he felt when he first joined the franchise to direct The Hunger Games: Catching Fire in 2013. He has since directed every subsequent instalment, including the prequel The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes .
Lawrence said the original novel and its film adaptation, along with Catching Fire , connected strongly with audiences through their protagonists, structure and key sequences. These included the reaping ceremonies, chariot processions, interviews and the deadly arena contests.
However, he explained that later entries explored different storytelling approaches. Mockingjay , the final book in the original series, was divided into two films, while The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes focused on the origins of future antagonist Coriolanus Snow.
By contrast, Sunrise on the Reaping returns to the Games themselves. The story centres on Haymitch Abernathy and the 50th Hunger Games, which take place 24 years before the events involving Katniss Everdeen.
Despite the familiar framework, Lawrence stressed that audiences should not expect a straightforward repetition of earlier films. He praised Collins for finding ways to overturn expectations, even during sequences that appear recognisable at first.
“What's great is that Suzanne upends expectations,” he said, explaining that seemingly familiar moments can develop in unexpected directions. He added that the film combines the elements audiences associate with the franchise with a different approach.
Joseph Zada plays the young Haymitch, while the cast also includes Glenn Close and Ralph Fiennes.
Based on Collins’s 2025 novel of the same name, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on November 20, 2026. The film aims to revisit the series’ central competition while exploring a defining chapter in Haymitch’s past.

title: Makkah pact ratification completed by Pakistan  Saudi Arabia  FO
description: Spokesperson says agreement has 16 articles  no hidden provisions  endorses text presented in the Turkish parliament
content:
Spokesperson says agreement has 16 articles, no hidden provisions; endorses text presented in the Turkish parliament
The Foreign Office confirmed on Friday that Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have completed their ratification processes for the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), while Türkiye is undertaking the requisite legal procedures for the agreement’s ratification.
“Each country follows its own constitutional and legal procedures for the approval and ratification of international agreements,” Foreign Office Spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said during the question and answer session after the weekly press briefing held in Islamabad.
The spokesperson said Pakistan and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia had completed their ratification processes, while Türkiye was pursuing the requisite procedures in accordance with its legal framework.
Asked whether the agreement contained any undisclosed clauses, particularly in view of Pakistan’s separate defence agreement with Saudi Arabia, the spokesperson said the MJDA comprised 16 articles and contained no hidden provisions.
🔊 Transcript of the Weekly Press Briefing by the Spokesperson https://t.co/IBRZCZjJ2R 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/APzZlHao5i
“There are no hidden provisions; the agreement is explicit and clear in its provisions and articles,” Khan stressed, adding that Pakistan endorsed the text released by the Turkish parliament in the media.
He further outlined that matters related to the agreement’s ratification and operationalisation are deliberated through the trilateral Strategic Political and Defence Committee, whose latest meeting was held on October 5.
Emphasising the defensive nature of the MJDA, Khan said it was consistent with the United Nations Charter and aimed at promoting regional peace, security and stability.
In response to a question about an International Crisis Group report warning of the risk of renewed conflict between Pakistan and India amid increased militant activity in Indian-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, the spokesperson said Islamabad wanted all disputes to be resolved peacefully and in accordance with international law.
“From Pakistan’s perspective, war is not a solution to any issue,” the spokesperson said, adding that disputes over Jammu and Kashmir and the Indus Waters Treaty should be addressed through dialogue and adherence to international law.
Read: CDF Munir vows to hit Indian-sponsored terrorist outfits hard ‘wherever they are’
While acknowledging that the issues posed a potential risk of conflict, Khan dispelled chances of another military confrontation with India and reiterated that Pakistan was fully prepared to protect its sovereignty and territorial integrity.
On the possibility of another false-flag operation by India, the spokesperson said it could not be ruled out.
“We are prepared for all eventualities,” Khan cautioned.
The spokesperson also commented on remarks by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio during his visit to India, in which he referred to Pakistan as a nuclear-armed state and spoke about Washington’s interest in maintaining cooperative relations with Islamabad.
The spokesperson said Pakistan enjoyed strong relations with the United States across several domains, including trade, investment and people-to-people contacts.
More than $5 billion worth of Pakistani exports went to the United States, the spokesperson said, describing the country as one of Pakistan’s most important export destinations.
The spokesperson said India often viewed Pakistan’s relations with other countries through a “zero-sum” lens, arguing that New Delhi’s strategic alignment with Washington cannot prevent the United States from maintaining ties with Islamabad.
On the Indus Waters Treaty, the spokesperson urged the international community, including the five permanent members of the UN Security Council, international organisations and bodies working in the water sector, to play a role in upholding international law.
Although the treaty was signed between Pakistan and India, the spokesperson said its implications extended beyond the two countries because allowing an upper-riparian state to misuse treaty provisions or weaponise water could set a precedent elsewhere.
Pakistan would not allow its share of water to be diverted from rivers meant to flow into the country, the spokesperson said, recalling that the National Security Committee had warned that any diversion of Pakistan’s water would be considered an “Act of War”.
The Foreign Office spokesperson also said Pakistan and the Maldives are members of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), which has remained inactive for quite some time now. He assailed India for SAARC’s prolonged inactivity, saying the regional organisation had effectively been held hostage since 2016, when a summit scheduled to take place in Islamabad did not go ahead.
The spokesperson said countries across the region wanted SAARC to be revived to boost regional trade, connectivity, transit and energy links.
He noted that intra-regional trade among members accounted for less than 5% of their overall trade, describing the region as one of the least economically integrated in the world.
“A functional SAARC would benefit all countries in the region rather than just Pakistan.”
Pakistan rejected what it described as “baseless and unwarranted assertions” by India’s Ministry of External Affairs regarding resolutions on Jammu and Kashmir adopted by the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), while expressing grave concern over an eviction notice issued to a historic mosque in New Delhi.
Speaking at the Foreign Office’s weekly press briefing, spokesperson Khan said the resolutions adopted at the 52nd session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers in Baghdad reflected the collective and longstanding position of member states on the Kashmir dispute.
He said the OIC’s position was firmly grounded in relevant United Nations Security Council (UNSC) resolutions and that the organisation had rejected India’s unilateral measures to alter the internationally recognised disputed status of Jammu and Kashmir.
The OIC had also called on the international community, including the UNSC, to take effective measures to implement the relevant resolutions, he stated. “The organisation’s continued principled support is an important reaffirmation that the Jammu and Kashmir dispute remains an internationally recognised dispute,” he added.
Also Read: Security forces kill 10 Indian-sponsored terrorists in Gwadar operations: ISPR
Describing India’s portrayal of the OIC’s collective position as misleading and dismissive of legitimate international concerns, the spokesperson said New Delhi should instead fulfil its international obligations, respect the fundamental rights of the Kashmiri people and create conditions for a peaceful resolution of the dispute in accordance with UNSC resolutions and the wishes of the people of Kashmir.
The ambassador also expressed grave concern over what he described as “yet another” eviction notice issued to a historic mosque in New Delhi. He said the Race Course Mosque was a Waqf property and a heritage site facing the threat of demolition under the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government.
“The measure exemplifies worsening Islamophobia in India,” he said, adding, “Pakistan calls upon the international community to take notice of incidents involving the demolition of places of worship, including those belonging to Muslims, and urges Indian authorities to desist from discriminatory measures.
Foreign Office spokesperson Khan said Pakistan would be willing to engage in talks with Afghanistan if there is a clear understanding that Kabul is ready to curb threats emanating from its soil.
Responding to questions at the weekly press briefing, Khan said Pakistan valued its engagement with Russia on Afghanistan and regional security, but no new initiative was currently on the table to facilitate talks between Islamabad and Kabul.
He noted that Russia had played a positive role through the Moscow Format meetings since 2017.
Khan said Pakistan had consistently pursued diplomacy with Afghanistan since the Taliban returned to power in 2021, engaging bilaterally and through forums involving Qatar, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia, China and Russia. However, these efforts had failed to ease tensions due to what he described as the Taliban’s “intransigence”.
He questioned the value of further dialogue unless the Afghan authorities acknowledged the presence of terrorist outfits on their territory and established a credible mechanism to prevent cross-border attacks. Citing United Nations monitoring reports and assessments by the Special Inspector General for Afghanistan Reconstruction (SIGAR), Khan said more than 20 terrorist organisations were operating in Afghanistan.
He added that Pakistan was not alone in its concerns, with China, Uzbekistan, Iran and other regional countries also worried about threats allegedly emanating from Afghanistan.
Probed about the reports of communication between intelligence officials and Afghanistan’s anti-Taliban leaders and the possibility of a proxy conflict, Khan reiterated Islamabad’s stated preference for a negotiated settlement.
On Field Marshal Asim Munir’s visit to Tehran , accompanied by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, amid renewed threats by the US president to resume hostilities, the spokesperson declined to comment, saying the question could be taken up on another occasion. He was also asked whether Pakistan was in contact with Washington and pursuing diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions.
In his opening statement, however, the FO spokesperson reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to diplomatic engagement, regional coordination and the peaceful resolution of conflicts. He said Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar had held separate telephone conversations with his Egyptian and Iranian counterparts on October 18 to discuss regional developments.
Dar and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi exchanged views on the evolving regional situation and the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers meeting held in Baghdad on October 17 and 18. Dar emphasised the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in addressing regional challenges.
Read more: Iran says it targeted four oil-carrying ships in Arabian Gulf
In a separate conversation, Dar and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty discussed the regional situation and condemned Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, reaffirming solidarity with the Kingdom and support for its sovereignty, territorial integrity and security, the spokesperson said.
The two ministers reviewed cooperation under the Regional Four framework, comprising Pakistan, Egypt, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia, and looked forward to the next meeting to strengthen coordination on regional issues.
He also highlighted Dar’s participation in the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Council of Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 19 and 20.
The spokesperson further outlined Pakistan’s recent diplomatic engagements, including Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu’s state visit from October 20 to 22 at the invitation of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.
During the visit, Muizzu met President Asif Ali Zardari and held talks with the prime minister. The two sides reviewed bilateral relations and agreed to expand cooperation in trade, investment, health, education, tourism, agriculture, defence, maritime security, climate change and people-to-people contacts.
The visit also resulted in the exchange of 20 memoranda of understanding , giving fresh impetus to cooperation across various sectors.
Khan noted that it was the first visit to Pakistan by a Maldivian president in 11 years and coincided with the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries.
Further Reading: Pakistan, Latvia discuss visa service
On the European front, the spokesperson said President Zardari was on an official visit to Germany from October 22 to 24, focusing on strengthening trade, investment and economic cooperation. The visit coincided with the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and Germany.
Pakistan also held bilateral political consultations with Lithuania on October 19 and Latvia on October 21. The discussions covered trade, investment, information technology, digital services, educational cooperation and the mobility of students, professionals and businesspeople.
Khan said Pakistan and the European Union held the 10th round of their bilateral counterterrorism dialogue in Islamabad on October 22. Both sides reviewed regional and global developments affecting the terrorist threat landscape and condemned terrorism in all its forms and manifestations.
“The EU condemned recent terrorist attacks in Pakistan, expressed solidarity with affected civilians and acknowledged Pakistan’s counterterrorism efforts. The discussions also covered violent extremism, terrorist financing, radicalisation and the misuse of cyberspace by terrorist groups,” the spokesperson said.
Both sides expressed concern over the security implications of terrorism emanating from Afghanistan and agreed to hold the next round of dialogue in Brussels in 2027.
The spokesperson said Pakistan, Qatar, Turkiye and Indonesia signed the Badr Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding in Doha on October 21 to strengthen cooperation in defence industries. The agreement covered manufacturing, technical training, research and development, technological innovation and industrial capacity-building.
He also said Pakistan had reaffirmed its commitment to multilateralism and the principles of the UN Charter at a ceremony in Islamabad marking United Nations Day on October 22.
Meanwhile, Dar had arrived in Istanbul to attend a meeting of foreign ministers from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Egypt, the spokesperson added. The Regional Four meeting was to be followed by a gathering involving the same four countries alongside the United Kingdom, France and Germany. According to the spokesperson, it would be the first meeting of the seven countries in this format.
The meetings were expected to provide an opportunity to review regional developments, strengthen diplomatic coordination and explore ways to promote peace, security and stability, he said.
Khan reiterated that Pakistan remained committed to promoting peace and stability through dialogue, strengthening economic and institutional partnerships, and working with international partners to address shared challenges.

title: Bournemouth hammer 10 man Milan
description: Juventus secure a draw against Rennes
content:
Bournemouth pulled off a sensational 3-0 home victory over 10-man AC Milan on Thursday to make it three wins from their opening three games in the Europa League.
Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier converted first-half penalties to put Bournemouth firmly in control against AC Milan, one of Europe's leading clubs.
Milan goalkeeper and skipper Mike Maignan was red carded early on for a foul on Tyler Adams and his side never fully recovered.
Amine Adli scored a sublime 84th free-kick to make it 3-0, the Premier League side having opened their inaugural Europa League campaign with victory at Real Sociedad followed by a 3-0 home win over Sturm Graz last week.
Bournemouth, who became the first English club since Sunderland in 1973/74 to win the first three European fixtures in their history, will now face Sparta Prague and Celta Vigo in November.
Bournemouth's Premier League rivals Crystal Palace rebounded from a 5-0 weekend thrashing by Brighton to claim a 2-2 draw with Beskitas in Istanbul, while Scottish giants Celtic suffered a third successive defeat, going down 2-1 to Celta Vigo.
Bayer Leverkusen, however, also made it three straight wins with a Jonas Hofmann double earning a 2-0 away win at OFI Crete as both Juventus and Sunderland lost ground in Thursday's third matchday.
The once mighty Hungarian side Ferencvaros kept pace with Leverkusen on nine points thumping Portuguese outfit Torreense 4-1, while Belgium's Union Saint-Gilloise won 4-0 against Israeli outfit Hapoel Be'er Sheva.
Saint-Gilloise, Sunderland and Juve all have seven points from three games.
Juventus thought they had come from behind to beat French side Rennes but had their late 'winner' ruled out for a marginal offside.
Zeki Celik put Juve ahead after five minutes only for a poor clearance 10 minutes later allowing Musa Al-Taamari to poke home an equaliser. Jut before the break Boulaye Dia put the visitors ahead.
Juventus made it 2-2 thanks to a handball and a spot-kick transformed by Nick Woltemade before VAR provided the biggest talking point, disallowing Jhon Lucumi's 88th minute strike.

title: Sanaullah says letter sent to Achakzai  urges opposition leader to meet PM Shehbaz
description: Adviser says meeting not matter of ego  stubborness  parties should meet to discuss issues on constitutional positions
content:
Says meeting not matter of ego and stubborness, parties should meet to discuss issues on constitutional positions
Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah on Friday said that a letter had been sent to Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai, entreating the latter to respond and to meet Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to discuss "issues on constitutional positions" amid a breakdown in communication between the government and the opposition following the administrative shakeup in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.
Earlier in the day, Achakzai stated that the premier could come to the opposition's office "and have tea with me or give me an invitation and wherever he wants to have negotiations I will go".
The opposition leader added, "Or I can go to him at the prime minister's house and give him an invitation."
Achakzai also said, "Discussions will not take place like this. The way you have made fun of Maulana Fazlur Rehman, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf and our people of the Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Aain-e-Pakistan."
شہباز شریف میرے آفس آئے چائے پیے اور مجھے دعوت دے جہاں مرضی مزاکرات کر لے، یا میں وزیر اعظم آفس میں چلا جاتا ہوں، اسے دعوت دیتا ہوں مزاکرات کی، جہاں مرضی مزاکرات کر لیں، لیکن مزاکرات اس طرح نہیں ہوں گے مزاق کے ساتھ جس طرح آپ نے تحریک انصاف اور تحریک تحفظ آئین پاکستان کے اکابرین… pic.twitter.com/a6jQva8E6k
Speaking to reporters later on the opposition leader's comments, Sanaullah said that there was "no issue of ego or stubbornness in this", referring to PM Shehbaz meeting Achakzai.
"This type of talk that come here or come there, it doesn't change anything. What is the rationale of this?"
Sanaullah said that when the opposition leader meets PM Shehbaz, they could together discuss the issues which should be discussed constitutionally.
A day earlier , Achakzai said that political dialogue required a meeting with PTI founder Imran Khan. He also recalled that Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman had met the prime minister in connection with the issue.
The opposition had asked the government to ensure that the prime minister personally extended an invitation for negotiations, he said. “Negotiations cannot take place in an atmosphere where the process itself is being mocked,” he said.
Read: Achakzai warns opposition may take to streets
The remarks came as the government and the opposition remain at loggerheads regarding the governance of K-P after President Asif Ali Zardari approved the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province on October 11 on the advice of PM Shehbaz and following approval by the federal cabinet.
The move transferred executive authority from the elected provincial government to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and affected 12 districts under the emergency proclamation. PTI rejected the decision, arguing that it undermined provincial autonomy and the party’s electoral mandate.
Federal ministers accused the provincial government of failing to address terrorism and governance challenges, while PTI considered the possibility of an in-house change or dissolution of the provincial assembly.
On October 12, a petition challenging the imposition of emergency measures and governor’s rule in K-P was filed in the Peshawar High Court by the PTI. The opposition argued that the constitutional requirements had not been fulfilled and that the intervention violated provincial autonomy.

title: AFC backs Infantino   s re election bid
description: FIFA boss sets his sights on another term
content:
FIFA boss sets his sights on another term
The head of Asian football on Friday said the region supported Gianni Infantino's bid for re-election as FIFA president, weeks after stinging criticism over his aborted World Cup selloff plan.
The 56-year-old Swiss was present at a Tokyo meeting of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) when president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa gave his unequivocal backing, in a significant boost to Infantino's prospects of extending his reign.
The AFC in August had joined European body UEFA and CONCACAF, representing federations in North and Central America and the Caribbean, in condemning Infantino over his plan to open FIFA's premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors.
Infantino has faced calls to quit and lost the support of some associations in his bid to be re-elected to a fourth and final term.
"I think that we reaffirm our full commitment, of course, to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as FIFA president," said Sheikh Salman.
"I think you've visited a lot of countries in Asia. I've spoken to a lot of members within this continent.
"I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well. Your support to Gianni is very clear."
Hinting at previous discord, Sheikh Salman told the AFC Extraordinary Congress and Infantino: "Gianni, yes, we had some issues we spoke about in the past.
"But let's not relate the two things together. We need to move forward... football is strongest when we work together."
Infantino, who apologised last week for the failed private investment project, has headed FIFA since 2016 and is running for re-election in March.
In response to the AFC's backing, Infantino said: "We have seen the transformation that Asian football, and as a consequence world football, has gone through in these years.
"It has become truly global. It has become for everyone, and this would not have been possible without a strong, a united, a committed Asia. And for this, I thank you very much."
The deadline for candidates to declare for the election is November 18.
No heavyweight candidate has put themselves forward to run against Infantino so far, despite outspoken condemnation, most notably from Europe.
Many leading European national associations have withdrawn their support for Infantino over controversies including his close relationship with US President Donald Trump.
Two months ago the AFC and Sheikh Salman signalled they could turn on Infantino.
A joint letter with UEFA and CONCACAF declared football "belongs to no individual".
"Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding -- or demanding -- power to be held," they wrote.
"When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned," the confederations said.
Infantino has received the backing of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) while South American governing body CONMEBOL is largely supportive.
The confederations do not vote as blocs and there have been some supportive voices for Infantino from within CONCACAF.
AFC members Kuwait and 2022 World Cup hosts Qatar had previously backed him.
So too did the football federation of Saudi Arabia, which will host the 2034 World Cup

title: Brook looks to revive England s campaign
description: Captain urges his charges to regroup after Sri Lanka s record chase in tri series
content:
Captain urges his charges to regroup after Sri Lanka's record chase in tri-series
England captain Harry Brook has said his team would return to the drawing board and keep their approach simple as they attempt to revive their campaign in the ODI tri-series after Sri Lanka chased down a target of 430 in a dramatic contest on Thursday.
Sri Lanka pulled off the second-highest successful chase in men's one-day international history, reaching 430-8 with one ball to spare at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium after Brook's record-breaking double century had powered England to 429-4.
Brook struck 202, the fastest double century in men's ODI cricket and the first by an England batsman in the format, but his remarkable innings proved insufficient as Sri Lanka produced a stunning response.
Pavan Rathnayake led the chase with 130, sharing century partnerships with Avishka Fernando, who scored 97, and Dasun Shanaka, who also made 97. Janith Liyanage then struck a blistering 61 off 27 balls to take Sri Lanka over the line.
England have now lost both their matches and face the prospect of elimination while unbeaten Pakistan have won both their games. Sri Lanka's victory has strengthened their position in the race for a place in the October 31 final.
Brook said England needed to learn from their mistakes and make the most of their remaining opportunities.
“Yeah, we’ve got to go back to the drawing board a little bit. We know where we’ve gone wrong and, unfortunately, we did not execute well enough with the ball,” Brook said.
“We’ve got a great opportunity in the next couple of games to try and nail down a spot in the final.”
He added that the team needed to keep things simple, back themselves and recover quickly from the disappointment.
England will face Pakistan at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium on Sunday in a crucial match for their hopes of reaching the final.
Brook admitted that the defeat had overshadowed his outstanding individual performance.
“It was a nice innings, but being on the losing side, it has no value whatsoever in my eyes. Its heart-breaking. It’s very disappointing that we haven’t been able to defend 430, but that’s life, that’s cricket,” he said.
The England captain described the match as an incredible contest and praised Sri Lanka for their determination in completing the chase.
“Incredible game of cricket. Both teams were exceptional,” Brook said.
“Sri Lanka just outplayed us, unfortunately. We could not quite hit our straps with the ball and played into their strengths a little bit. Again, they played exceptional cricket to knock off the target. I think, as you said, first time in 20 years is an incredible achievement, so fair play to them.”
England had also suffered an 87-run defeat against Pakistan after a batting collapse, leaving them under pressure to deliver in their remaining fixtures if they are to qualify for the final.

title: Stars reach final after thrilling chase
description: Sadaf  Iram guide Stars past Invincibles in National T20
content:
Sadaf, Iram guide Stars past Invincibles in National T20
Stars secured a place in the National Women’s T20 Tournament final with a seven-wicket victory over Invincibles on Friday, while unbeaten Strikers completed their eighth consecutive win by beating Conquerors by 60 runs.
Sadaf Shamas scored an unbeaten 59 and Iram Javed contributed 47 as Stars chased down a target of 141 in 19.2 overs at Bohranwali Ground, finishing on 144-3 with four balls to spare.
Invincibles had posted 140-6 after Eyman Fatima led their recovery with a 63-ball 85, including 12 fours and three sixes. She shared a 115-run partnership for the third wicket with Syeda Aroob Shah, who scored 29.
Invincibles had made a disastrous start, losing openers Samiya Afsar and captain Gull Feroza with just one run on the board before Eyman steadied the innings.
Diana Baig took two wickets for 17 runs, while Stars captain Tuba Hassan claimed two for 21.
Stars lost Samina Aftab for 19 and Yusra Amir during the chase, but Sadaf and Iram added 76 runs to put their side firmly on course for victory.
Sadaf’s unbeaten innings came off 52 balls and included six fours and two sixes. Iram’s 47 ensured Stars reached the target and finished level on eight points with Invincibles, advancing to the final on net run rate as their opponents slipped to third place.
In the other match at Jawad Club Ground, Strikers maintained their unbeaten record with a comprehensive win over Conquerors.
Player of the match Najiha Alvi struck an unbeaten 63 off 52 balls to help Strikers post 123-6 in their 20 overs. Omaima Sohail added 36, with the pair sharing a 56-run partnership.
Conquerors leg-spinner Ghulam Fatima took four wickets for 14 runs, but her side struggled in reply and were bowled out for 63 in 14.1 overs.
Ravail Farhan top-scored with 22, while Aliya Riaz made 13. Omaima, Neelam Mushtaq, Tania Saeed and Rameen Shamim took two wickets apiece to seal the victory.
Strikers, led by Natalia Parvaiz, will face Tuba Hassan’s Stars in the final on October 26 at Iqbal Stadium in Faisalabad. Strikers have won all eight of their matches in the tournament so far.

content:
Actor says she will change her weight for a role if needed but not compromise her comfort to meet public expectations
Actor and producer Hareem Farooq has spoken out against the criticism she faces over her weight and appearance, saying she refuses to let public opinion dictate how she lives or pursues her career. She also addressed the pressure women face to meet societal beauty standards, how mothers can inadvertently pass those expectations on to their daughters, and the impact of hurtful comments on mental health.
In a recent interview with Aamna Haider Isani, Farooq questioned why she should have to compromise her comfort simply because some people disapproved of her appearance. “Why should I be suffering because there are a few hundred who are like, ‘She doesn’t look good, what is she wearing?’” she said.
The actor made it clear that she was no longer willing to make herself uncomfortable to meet other people’s expectations. “It’s okay. You can get uncomfortable if you want to. I refuse to do that to myself,” she added.
Farooq also spoke about the religious and personal significance she attaches to her body. “This body is given to us by Allah and it’ll be given back to Him. I refuse to abuse my body in order to make a few people comfortable,” she said.
Reflecting on her early years in mainstream media, Farooq said the scrutiny surrounding her weight had been a longstanding issue. When she first entered the industry, she recalled, there were few actresses with broader body types, leaving her particularly exposed to public commentary.
“This hasn’t happened in one day. It was a shock when I initially started in mainstream media. At that time, there weren’t many broad girls in the fraternity. I got a lot of public reactions about how big my weight was, but I had a pretty face,” she said.
She also highlighted what she sees as a contradiction in public reactions to her appearance: while some people criticise her weight, they continue to watch her dramas. “At the same time, people are still watching my dramas, which is the reason why I’m sitting here. Because I do get that love,” she said.
Despite the scrutiny, Farooq said she had never allowed comments about her body to cost her a professional opportunity. “There’s never been an instance where I have let a project go,” she said.
She distinguished between changing her appearance to satisfy public expectations and undergoing a physical transformation for a role, explaining that she remained willing to do the latter when required. “At the end of the day, as an actor, I know there might be a margin where I need to cut down weight for a character or gain. I’ll do that. I’ll even cut my hair short,” she said.
However, Farooq noted that actors had a degree of flexibility when it came to changing their appearance that ordinary people might not enjoy. “But as an actor, I get that pass, and normal women who aren’t actors don’t get that pass,” she added.
Farooq also reflected on how societal expectations surrounding appearance could be passed from one generation of women to the next, with mothers sometimes reinforcing the same standards they had struggled with themselves.
“It’s so interesting that fathers never say much, but mothers do. They just worry about you. Women are the ones who have to listen to everything because they bear the responsibility to make everyone happy,” she said.
She explained that when mothers hear criticism about their daughters’ weight, skin tone or height, they may instinctively try to protect them by encouraging them to change their appearance. However, the emotional consequences of such advice can go unrecognised.
“When someone says to a mother that your daughter is fat, or dark-skinned, or her height is short, she wants to protect her, which is why she tells her to work on herself,” Farooq said.
Recalling the advice young girls sometimes receive, she said she had seen mothers encourage their daughters to try anything that might help them grow taller, including hanging from objects. “I have seen this around. So many things young girls have to face because their mothers also face the same from society,” she said.
Farooq acknowledged that such responses often stem from a desire to shield daughters from judgment, but stressed that the impact of these comments on young girls is frequently overlooked. “I feel the first instinct is to protect the daughter, but the impact of saying that to the daughter isn’t really recognised. We also need to take note of that,” she said.
Although the conversation often centres on women, Farooq emphasised that men also face appearance-based criticism, including comments about their height, skin tone and facial features.
“As much as this conversation is important for women, it’s also for men. Men are also suffering. They’re short, dark, or don’t have nice faces, receiving those kinds of comments,” she said.
Turning to her own experience of changing her weight, Farooq explained that the motivation behind her transformation had eventually become more personal.
“There was a time I realised that it doesn’t matter. When I lost weight, it was for me. Maybe I did take pressure somewhere, but when I started, I realised that I never knew I had this much willpower,” she said.
However, the reaction to her weight loss reinforced her belief that public opinion was difficult to satisfy. “When I started to transform, people were then commenting on how much weight I lost, so the comments will always be there. I can be a size two and a fourteen,” she said.
For Farooq, the experience underscored the importance of developing a healthier relationship with oneself rather than constantly trying to meet shifting expectations. “You have to love yourself. If you don’t love yourself, you can’t love anyone else,” she said.
She also urged people to be more mindful of the language they use, highlighting the connection between hurtful remarks and mental well-being.
“Words are very powerful, and we need to be careful about it,” she said, adding that society had become accustomed to complaining and making negative remarks. “Each person doesn’t have the ability to keep listening to complaints. As a nation, we’re so used to complaining and making bad comments,” she said.
Farooq further reflected on the importance of recognising personal limits, acknowledging that she, too, had regrets about how she had managed her body and responsibilities.
“I also have regrets, such as letting myself get to this point or my body. You have to manage yourself and draw a line. I was going all in with everything I had,” she said.
She recalled reaching a point when she realised that her way of living was no longer sustainable, emphasising the importance of recognising one's limitations. “That time I realised that my life isn’t sustainable,” she said.
Farooq also stressed that making mistakes was part of being human. “You have to realise you’re human, and we all make mistakes,” she said.
Speaking about the practices that help her maintain a more positive outlook, Farooq said she had developed a habit of beginning each day with gratitude, particularly towards her body and what it allowed her to do. “I see myself with gratitude. Before I even get out of bed, when I open my eyes, I have a few rituals I do,” she said.
“The most important, I tell myself I’m grateful for my body and say thank you for the ability to walk and move around. I start my day by thanking my body,” she added, explaining that the practice helped her recognise and challenge moments when she became negative about herself.
Farooq has previously spoken about body image and unrealistic beauty standards. In a 2024 interview , she discussed playing Masooma in the drama Bismil and the pressure on actresses to conform to conventional standards of beauty.
She questioned why different body types should not be represented and celebrated on screen, challenging the assumption that actresses must fit a particular physical ideal.
Alongside her acting career, Farooq has continued to expand her work as a producer. Her latest film, Mango Jutt , pairs her with Faysal Quraishi in a Punjabi-language action comedy blending romance, humour and action.
The film marks her return to the big screen after Heer Maan Ja (2019) and her debut in a Punjabi-language production.

title: Hasan Piker reacts to Hila Klein accusing Ethan of an affair in a five word statement
description: The former    Leftovers    co hosts fell out over political disagreements after working together from 2021 to 2023
content:
The former ‘Leftovers’ co-hosts fell out over political disagreements after working together from 2021 to 2023
Hasan Piker has drawn attention online after posting “JUDGE ME BY MY ENEMIES” following allegations by Hila Klein that her husband, Ethan Klein, had been having an affair. The pointed remark has attracted particular interest because of the long-running public fallout between the two internet personalities.
Hila shared a statement on October 23, 2026, alleging that Ethan had been involved in an affair for more than six months. She said she had repeatedly raised concerns before discovering what she described as a series of lies. These remain claims made publicly by Hila, rather than independently established details.
The reaction has also renewed discussion of Hasan and Ethan’s former working relationship. The pair co-hosted Leftovers , a political commentary podcast that launched in 2021. Their collaboration ended in October 2023 after disagreements surrounding the Israel and Gaza conflict deepened tensions between them. Their differing perspectives and the responses from their respective audiences contributed to a highly publicised split.
The disagreement continued in 2025, when Ethan published a lengthy video criticising Hasan and his political commentary. Hasan and Ethan subsequently engaged in further public exchanges, keeping their dispute in the spotlight.
Against that history, Hasan’s short post has been interpreted by online commenters as a pointed reaction to the latest controversy involving his former co-host. The phrase suggests that a person’s opponents can say something about their own character, making it particularly pointed given the pair’s history.
However, Hasan’s post does not itself establish any details of the allegations, and he has not provided a longer explanation in the material currently available.
The controversy has also prompted a response from the H3 Podcast team. In a statement, staff members said they were shocked and upset by the allegations and would not continue working with Ethan involved or profiting from his participation.
The latest developments have placed the former collaborators back in the same online conversation, years after their podcast ended.

title: Anoushey Ashraf says society questions women who marry later in life
description: TV host discusses scrutiny she faced for marrying at 40 and societal expectations women encounter around marriage
content:
TV host discusses scrutiny she faced for marrying at 40 and societal expectations women encounter around marriage
Television host Anoushey Ashraf has opened up about the public scrutiny she faced for remaining unmarried until her 40s, saying her family always prioritised education and financial stability over societal expectations about marriage.
Appearing in an interview with Vasay Chaudhry, Ashraf discussed the attention surrounding her decision to marry in her 40s and questioned why a woman’s personal choices so often become a subject of public discussion. “When you get married at 40, people ask a lot of questions,” she said, describing the scrutiny faced by women who do not follow society’s expected timeline for marriage.
Ashraf also recalled an encounter with an older woman whose reaction to her years as an unmarried woman left her surprised. “One time an aunty grabbed me and was like, ‘I used to do so many prayers for you,’ and I’m like, ‘What? It’s not that big of a deal,’” she said.
The anecdote reflects a familiar social attitude in Pakistan, where remaining unmarried beyond a certain age can be treated as a cause for concern rather than a personal choice.
Ashraf, however, said she had been building a fulfilling life long before marriage entered the picture. “I was working, earning money, living respectfully, travelling, and I’m educated, and here they were crying,” she said, pointing to the independence and stability she had achieved.
Her remarks challenge the assumption that a woman’s happiness or success is incomplete without a husband. Ashraf’s experience highlights how professional independence, personal growth and the freedom to make one’s own decisions can be sources of fulfilment regardless of marital status.
She also spoke about the double standards women encounter before and after marriage, noting that getting married does not necessarily free them from society’s scrutiny but can bring a new set of expectations.
“When you’re not married, you can do many things and people will judge you. Now after getting married, no matter what I say, somehow in our society it’s expected that I have higher social standards now because I have a man standing next to me,” she explained.
Her observation highlights how a woman’s social standing can become tied to whether she has a husband. Instead of being recognised for her individual identity, achievements and values, she may be judged according to the perceived respectability or status associated with marriage.
Ashraf also credited her mother with shaping her outlook on marriage and independence, recalling advice that placed personal happiness and financial security above social pressure.
“My mother always raised me to believe that if staying happy means staying single, I should. Just make sure you’re financially settled. We have given you everything and raised you well enough to know you can make your own choices,” she said.
The advice placed financial independence and personal happiness at the centre of a woman’s life rather than treating marriage as an obligation. It also reflected her mother’s belief that daughters should be equipped to make their own decisions and define fulfilment on their own terms.
Her mother’s approach, Ashraf suggested, was not about rejecting marriage but ensuring that it remained a choice rather than a necessity. Women should be able to enter relationships because they want to share their lives with someone, not because they fear social judgement or feel that time is running out.
Ashraf remains active as a VJ, television and radio host, actor and producer. She rose to prominence in the early 2000s as one of the pioneering faces of Pakistan’s music television scene and has also spoken publicly about women’s independence, animal welfare and environmental issues.

title: Naqvi vows to strengthen NCCIA as cybercrime cases mount in Punjab
description: Says govt to strengthen agency through additional personnel  resources  offices and dedicated police stations
content:
Says govt to strengthen agency through additional personnel, resources, offices and dedicated police stations
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Friday pledged to strengthen the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), revealing that it had only 61 personnel across Punjab, a province with a population of around 140 million, as investigators struggled with a growing backlog of cases involving online fraud, harassment and blackmail.
Speaking to the media in Lahore, Naqvi said he would raise the agency’s staffing and resource shortages with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, adding that the government was working to improve its capacity to respond to complaints and investigate cybercrime.
“An investigating officer has 3,000 to 4,000 cases. How can they possibly work?” he asked, pointing out that investigators had to attend court hearings, hear complainants, prepare challans and conduct investigations. “If this is the situation in Lahore, the situation in Multan and other areas is much worse,” he remarked, adding that he would take up the issue with the prime minister in the coming days.
The government planned to strengthen the agency by increasing its personnel and resources, opening more offices and establishing dedicated police stations. Plans were also being developed to set up NCCIA police stations across the country, with the arrangements expected to be finalised within 10 to 15 days, he added.
Naqvi stressed that some complaints required an immediate response, particularly cases involving the online harassment and blackmail of women and girls. “There are some sensitive cases in which you cannot wait months, weeks or even days. You have to respond within hours,” he said.
The minister recounted meeting several women who had attempted suicide after facing harassment, describing their experiences as a stark reminder of the urgency of improving the agency’s response.
Read: Islamabad court sentences 2 men to 10 years for blackmailing 12-year-old girl with objectionable photos
He also highlighted delays arising from existing legal procedures.
Under the current law, the NCCIA was required to issue three notices before registering a first information report (FIR), a requirement that could delay action in sensitive cases. “If a girl is facing harassment, and there have been cases in which girls have attempted suicide, we have to respond differently in such cases,” he emphasised.
He urged women and girls to exercise caution when sharing personal photographs and videos online, warning that offenders could use such material to blackmail victims. “I would request mothers, sisters and daughters not to share any personal photographs with anyone,” he said, cautioning that doing so could leave them vulnerable to exploitation.
According to Naqvi, offenders often obtained photographs or videos under false pretences before threatening victims and exploiting them. The government would step up public awareness campaigns to help people recognise such risks and report abuse.
He also stressed the importance of awareness in tackling financial fraud, with scammers impersonating relatives or pretending to be ill to persuade people to transfer money. “Some people ask for money by pretending to be a relative, while others pretend to be ill and ask for money,” he explained.
The amounts involved ranged from Rs10,000 to millions of rupees, he added, pledging that the authorities would work to prevent such fraud and help victims recover their money. “The most important thing is to run awareness campaigns for the public so that these cases can be reduced,” he said.
He further urged people to protect their passwords and other sensitive information, warning that sharing passwords could expose them to financial losses and other forms of online crime.
Read more: AI to be used in online child abuse probes
Turning to enforcement, Naqvi announced that around 600 people had been arrested during operations against call centres over the preceding 10 to 12 days. He praised the NCCIA for conducting operations despite its limited staffing, stressing that its personnel needed greater institutional support to handle the scale of cybercrime complaints.
The government would also work to improve coordination with banks, particularly in cases involving fraudulent transfers. He argued that the NCCIA needed stronger powers and mechanisms to identify accounts receiving money obtained through fraud and freeze them promptly to prevent further losses.
Some powers available to the Federal Investigation Agency, including those relating to bank accounts, were not available to the NCCIA, he added.
The minister also referred to the arrest of a government employee in a harassment-related case, maintaining that the authorities should proceed if the allegations were established. “There is no exemption for a government employee in a harassment case. If it is proven, there should be no leniency, regardless of who the person is,” he said.
He added that the authorities were working to address fake social media accounts and other forms of online abuse through coordination with relevant agencies.
Naqvi also highlighted Pakistan’s cooperation with other countries to investigate cybercrime and apprehend suspects operating across borders. “Every day, discussions are under way with embassies and police liaison officers,” he said, explaining that Pakistan was working with foreign counterparts to arrest suspects involved in cross-border offences.
The cooperation worked both ways, with Pakistani authorities helping foreign partners apprehend suspects while seeking assistance in cases involving offenders operating abroad.
He concluded that the government would continue to strengthen the NCCIA’s staffing, resources and operational capacity while expanding public awareness campaigns to curb online fraud, harassment and blackmail.

title: USEFP opens new gallery space in Islamabad for US exchange alumni artists
description: Debut show by Lahore based Minaa Haroon turns inherited jewellery  accessories into carriers of memory  lineage
content:
Debut show by Lahore-based Minaa Haroon turns inherited jewellery, accessories into carriers of memory, lineage
The United States Educational Foundation in Pakistan (USEFP), and the Pakistan-US Alumni Network on October 22 opened the first ‘Shahkaar Fankaar Alumni Artist Showcase’ in a new gallery space in the USEFP building in Islamabad, a press release by the US embassy said on Friday.
"This gallery space will feature the achievements of US government-sponsored exchange program alumni in the arts," it said. The release added that the first exhibition was a solo show by Lahore-based artist Minaa Haroon, an alumna of a US Department of State exchange program on cultural preservation.
Haroon "showcased artwork utilising inherited jewellery and accessories as carriers of memory, identity, and lineage, starting with her mother’s jewellery," the embassy said, noting that the opening marked "decades of US education and exchange programs and spotlights an alumna whose achievements reflect the mutual partnership between the United States and Pakistan."
Haroon is a visual artist and Assistant Director of Fine Arts at the Lahore Arts Council, the embassy said. It added that in April 2024, the artist traveled to the US as a visiting scholar in the Cultural Preservation Professional Exchange Program run by the US government. “My participation as a visiting scholar in the US deepened my reflection on cultural inheritance," she said.
Haroon added, "Through visits to museums and galleries, I encountered different ways in which histories and traditions are preserved, interpreted, and carried forward.”
The opening included a 3D projection of Haroon’s works on the exterior wall of the USEFP building by Hoola Digital Pvt Ltd, the Islamabad-based company that created the projections on the Pakistan Monument and Lahore Fort to commemorate the 250th birthday of the US on July 4, 2026.
According to the press release, Director of Public Engagement at the US embassy Heidi Smith said that “for decades, educational and cultural exchanges have brought Americans and Pakistanis together as partners in learning, innovation, and creativity."
Read: IT minister formally inaugurates ‘The Innovation Hive’ established by USEFP
She noted that Haroon's work "shows how an exchange experience can sharpen an artist’s vision and strengthen the ties between our two nations."
As per the embassy, Smith stated that as the US celebrates 250 years of independence, "our exchange alumni are helping shape the next chapter of the US-Pakistan relationship.” The director also presented Haroon with a certificate of recognition for her artistic excellence and her achievement as an exchange alumna.
Further, USEFP Executive Director Dr Peter K Moran provided a written statement to commemorate the opening saying, “A cultural and educational exchange program has the power to disrupt our everyday, to reframe our usual signposts, and alter our horizons, not just metaphorically, but physically too." According to the release, Moran added, "How better to consider that kind of transformation and the exchange of ideas, forms and horizons, than in art."
The executive director thanked the US Department of State exchange alumni, "who express their ways of seeing and framing the world, and make us reflect on our own vision.” Asma Rashid Khan, Director of Satrang Gallery and program advisor for the showcase, and Sarah Rajper, the exhibition’s curator, along with representatives from the US Department of State with other guests from Pakistan’s art world, exchange alumni, and members of the diplomatic corps attended the event.
Open to the public through November 20 at the USEFP building in Islamabad, the viewing hours for the showcase are from 10:30am to 5:00pm from Monday through Friday.
Since the USEFP’s founding in 1950, thousands of Pakistanis and Americans have taken part in its educational and research exchanges, with three additional alumni artists to have their work featured in solo exhibitions in the USEFP gallery in 2027.

title: Halloweentown 5    in development at Disney nearly 20 years after last film
description: The new film has no confirmed cast or release date  leaving fans waiting for further details
content:
The new film has no confirmed cast or release date, leaving fans waiting for further details
Disney is developing a fifth Halloweentown film, bringing the beloved fantasy franchise back into consideration nearly two decades after its last instalment.
According to TheWrap , writers Lily Houghton and Ryan Koehn are developing a screenplay for the potential movie for Disney Channel and Disney+. The project remains in its early stages, and details about the plot, director and release schedule have not been announced.
The script will be based on characters created by Paul Bernbaum, who wrote the original Halloweentown , released in 1998. The first film follows teenager Marnie Piper as she discovers that she comes from a family of witches and begins learning about her magical heritage.
Kimberly J Brown played Marnie in the first three films, including Halloweentown II: Kalabar’s Revenge in 2001 and Halloweentown High in 2004. Sara Paxton took over the role in the fourth instalment, Return to Halloweentown , released in 2006.
It remains unclear whether Brown, Paxton or other familiar cast members will return for the potential fifth film. Disney has not announced casting details, and the project has not been confirmed for production.
The franchise has maintained a strong audience over the years. The four existing films have accumulated 160 million hours of viewing globally on Disney+. The original movie also ranked among the platform’s 10 most-watched Halloween films in October 2025.
Houghton’s writing credits include the horror comedy Forbidden Fruits , while Koehn worked on the Gossip Girl reboot and has other screenwriting credits, including Homeschooled .
A fifth film would expand Disney’s collection of Halloween-themed titles, which includes Hocus Pocus and Twitches . However, with the screenplay still in development, it is too early to know whether the story will reunite original characters or introduce a new generation of witches.
All four existing Halloweentown films are currently available on Disney+.

title: Jenna Ortega plans TV break after    Wednesday    ends
description: The actress says a few days without her phone felt freeing and helped her reconnect with everyday life
content:
The actress says a few days without her phone felt freeing and helped her reconnect with everyday life
Jenna Ortega has revealed that she avoids reading reviews, watching her own films and checking box office figures, explaining that she does not want public opinion or commercial performance to dictate how she feels about her work.
In a new cover story for Vogue , the Wednesday star said reading reviews could have a negative effect on her mental state. She also explained that she avoids box office updates, even when her team sends them to her, because she does not want her career to become focused on numbers.
Ortega previously relied on social media to gauge audience reactions to her projects. However, she said she has been using these platforms less frequently, citing the amount of artificial intelligence generated content online and the tendency for people to scrutinise themselves too closely.
The actress also described an unexpected break from technology after her phone stopped working. Rather than immediately getting it repaired, she spent several days without easy access to social media or constant digital communication.
She recalled planning journeys by checking maps on a computer and memorising streets, while arranging specific places and times to meet people. Ortega described the experience as freeing.
Her comments come as she prepares for the release of Klara and the Sun , a film directed by Taika Waititi and adapted from Kazuo Ishiguro’s novel. Despite the film’s reception and box office expectations attracting attention, Ortega said her usual approach means she will not be closely monitoring reviews or financial results.
Ortega has also been thinking about what comes next in her television career. Speaking on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, she reflected on beginning television work as a child, including roles in Jane the Virgin and Disney’s Stuck in the Middle .
The actress currently leads Netflix’s Wednesday , which is heading towards its third season. Ortega said she expects to step away from television for a while once the series concludes, giving herself time to explore different opportunities.
“What I’m meant to do will come and find me,” she said, expressing a desire to leave room for new experiences after years of working on television productions.

title: At least 12 killed as passenger bus collides with van in Balochistan s Uthal
description: Collision near Zero Point left 22 others injured  while rescue teams shifted the wounded to nearby hospitals
content:
Collision near Zero Point left 22 others injured, while rescue teams shifted the wounded to nearby hospitals
At least 12 people were killed and 22 injured when a passenger bus collided with a passenger van near Zero Point in Uthal, Lasbela district of Balochistan, on Friday, police said.
Uthal District Headquarters (DHQ) Hospital Medical Superintendent Dr Awais Wajid said women and children were among the dead and injured, adding that the injured had been shifted to Karachi for further treatment.
According to police, the bus was travelling from Lasbela to Karachi when the two vehicles collided near Uthal Zero Point, resulting in heavy casualties.
Police, rescue teams, district administration officials and local residents rushed to the scene following reports of the accident. The injured were initially shifted to nearby hospitals by ambulance before being referred to Karachi for further treatment.
An investigation had been launched to determine the cause of the collision. Traffic on the national highway was disrupted following the accident, with police working to restore the flow of vehicles.
Meanwhile, arrangements for the treatment of the injured and the handover of the bodies to their families were under way.
Also Read: Four killed in Bolan road accident
Balochistan has witnessed several fatal road accidents in recent months. On October 19, four people , including women and children, were killed when a Mazda truck collided with an Alto car near Darbi in Bolan district.
On October 13, four people were killed and five injured when a passenger van travelling from Quetta to Kalat collided with a truck near Badrang in Mastung district.
Earlier, in July, at least 40 passengers were killed and eight injured when a coach travelling from Quetta to Peshawar plunged into a ravine in the Dana Sar area along the Sherani-Zhob highway.
In January rescue officials said they had recorded more than 24,000 road accidents in Balochistan during 2025, resulting in over 415 deaths and nearly 30,000 injuries. The N-25 National Highway connecting Quetta and Karachi was identified as the province’s most accident-prone route.

title: H3 Podcast crew will no longer work with Ethan Klein after wife Hila   s affair allegations
description: The crew expressed support for Hila and said its members were looking after one another
content:
The crew expressed support for Hila and said its members were looking after one another
The H3 Podcast crew has announced it will no longer work with host Ethan Klein, following allegations from his wife and co-host, Hila Klein, that he had an affair lasting more than six months.
In a joint statement posted on Instagram on October 23, the crew said its members were “shocked, angry, and heartbroken” by the allegations.
They confirmed the decision to end their professional relationship with Ethan was unanimous and said they would not continue working with him “involved or profiting in any way”.
Hila, co-founder of clothing brand Teddy Fresh, shared a three-part Instagram post alleging her husband had been unfaithful.
“I am living in a nightmare I can't wake up from,” she wrote. She said Ethan had admitted to the affair after being caught in a lie, describing the betrayal as immeasurable.
The crew expressed support for Hila and said its members were looking after one another. However, it acknowledged uncertainty about the podcast’s future, stating: “We don't yet know what that means for the future.”

The announcement came less than 12 hours after Ethan said on Instagram Stories on October 22 that the H3 Podcast was going on “indefinite hiatus”.
The show, which began on YouTube in 2016, has not formally announced its closure or plans for a replacement format.
Ethan and Hila Klein married on October 12, 2012 , and share three children — Theodore, 7, Bruce, 4, and Sunny, 2 — together.
Ethan has not publicly responded to the allegations at the time of publication. The claims have not been independently confirmed, and the future of the podcast remains unclear.

title: Amy Winehouse musical in development for London   s West End
description: Producer Catherine Schreiber is attached to the early stage project  with casting reportedly under way
content:
Producer Catherine Schreiber is attached to the early stage project, with casting reportedly under way
A musical celebrating Amy Winehouse’s life and music is in development for London’s West End, with the project reportedly involving her father, Mitch Winehouse.
According to Variety , Tony Award-winning producer Catherine Schreiber, whose credits include Cabaret and Rent , is attached to the production. Casting is reportedly under way, although the project remains in its early stages. Details about the creative team, storyline and potential opening date have not yet been announced.
Mitch Winehouse is also said to be involved, raising the possibility that the musical will feature some of the late singer’s best-known songs. Her record label has been approached for comment, but further official details have not been confirmed.
The development follows years of discussion about bringing Winehouse’s story to the stage. In a 2017 interview, Mitch expressed his support for a musical that would celebrate his daughter’s life and music, saying he wanted audiences to remember her for her talent rather than focus solely on her struggles.
Winehouse died in 2011, aged 27, leaving behind a celebrated catalogue that includes the albums Frank and Back to Black . The latter, released in 2006, helped establish her as one of the defining British singers of her generation.
Interest in her music remains strong. The 20th anniversary of Back to Black was recently marked with a tribute concert at London’s Roundhouse, featuring performances by Jorja Smith, Mark Ronson, Lianne La Havas and Corinne Bailey Rae.
An expanded edition of the album is also scheduled for release on October 23, featuring previously unreleased demos, B-sides and a recording of a 2007 performance at Amsterdam’s Paradiso.
Winehouse’s life has already been explored through screen projects, including Asif Kapadia’s acclaimed 2015 documentary Amy and the 2024 biopic Back to Black , directed by Sam Taylor-Johnson.
If the West End production proceeds, it will add another major project to the singer’s posthumous legacy. However, its final format, casting and production schedule remain unconfirmed.
