title: Aamir Khan gets emotional over years lost to work  regrets missing time with his children
description: Actor says Covid prompted him to rethink his priorities and spend more time with family and close friends
content:
Actor says Covid prompted him to rethink his priorities and spend more time with family and close friends
Bollywood star Aamir Khan became emotional while reflecting on the personal cost of his decades-long career, admitting that his relentless commitment to filmmaking had left him with regrets over time missed with his children and loved ones.
Speaking at the Singapore International Film Festival, where he received the Screen Icon Award, Khan looked back on the choices that shaped his professional journey and acknowledged that his single-minded focus on work had come at the expense of important relationships.
According to Gulf News , Khan said the Covid-19 pandemic had prompted him to reconsider how much of his life he had devoted to his career.
The actor explained that intense dedication to a project could be understandable for a limited period, but maintaining that pace for decades came at a personal cost. As he reflected on his children growing into adults, he said he felt a deep sense of loss.
Khan paused as he struggled to contain his emotions, wiped away tears and apologised to those present before continuing. His remarks drew applause from the audience.
The experience prompted him to reassess his priorities. He said he had made a conscious effort over the past four years to spend more time with his family and close friends.
"It's okay to work like a madman, completely obsessed with what you're doing for one year, two years, five years. But if it goes on for 30 years, I mean, you've lost your relationships. Your kids have grown up; they're adults now. So I felt a deep sense of loss," he said.
Khan was grateful that he had recognised the need for change in his mid-50s rather than waiting until much later in life, when it might have been too late to reconnect with loved ones. "I'm so glad that this thought occurred to me when I was 56 and not when I was 86, when it would really be too late to do anything about it," he added.
The actor also revisited a difficult chapter from the beginning of his career, when the success of his 1988 film Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak led him to take on numerous projects in quick succession.
Khan said he had signed nine films within six months of the film's success. The decision eventually proved overwhelming, with several of the projects failing commercially.
He recalled the emotional toll of that period and how he turned to his then-wife, Reena Dutta, for support as he struggled with mounting professional pressure. "At that time, mentally and emotionally, I felt like I was in quicksand. I was sinking slowly, and the more I struggled to get out, the deeper I was getting," he said.
Following a string of unsuccessful films, Khan said some people dismissed him as a one-film wonder. The experience left him feeling increasingly trapped, as his attempts to recover from the setbacks only added to his distress.
His account highlighted the uncertainty of the film industry, where an early breakthrough does not necessarily guarantee sustained success.
Alongside his reflections on his career and family, Khan shared an update on the proposed sequel to 3 Idiots , the popular 2009 comedy directed by Rajkumar Hirani.
According to Gulf News , Khan confirmed that Hirani was working on the screenplay and said he hoped to hear the final version within the next few weeks. "Raju is working on the script. In fact, hopefully once I'm back in the next couple of weeks, he'll narrate the final version to me. So, fingers crossed," he said.
The original film, which featured Khan alongside R Madhavan, Sharman Joshi and Kareena Kapoor Khan, became one of Hindi cinema's most recognisable comedies. It explored friendship, education and the pressure to meet societal expectations.
However, the sequel's progress remains dependent on the screenplay's development.
Hong Kong filmmaker Peter Chan Ho-sun presented Khan with the Screen Icon Award at the Singapore International Film Festival.
During his remarks, Khan acknowledged the collaborative nature of filmmaking, noting that films were shaped by the contributions of many people rather than the efforts of a single individual.
Khan last attended the festival nine years ago with Secret Superstar . This year's programme also includes a 25th-anniversary screening of Lagaan , the acclaimed 2001 sports drama that marked his debut as a film producer.
His emotional appearance offered a glimpse into the personal struggles behind a career marked by ambitious projects, commercial highs and professional setbacks. Above all, his reflections underscored how professional success can come at a cost when personal relationships are repeatedly placed second to work.

title: Erin Foster  pro Israel creator of  Nobody Wants This  responds to Adam Brody   s support for Palestine
description: Brody  who portrays a Jewish rabbi in the series  expressed support for a  free Palestine  in a recent interview
content:
Brody, who portrays a Jewish rabbi in the series, expressed support for a 'free Palestine' in a recent interview
Erin Foster, creator of Netflix’s Nobody Wants This , has responded to comments by actor Adam Brody expressing support for a free Palestine and describing the situation in Gaza as genocide.
Brody, who portrays a Jewish rabbi in the series, shared his views during an i nterview with GQ . Discussing Israel and Palestine, he said, “Put me down as thinking it’s a genocide. Put me down as wanting a free Palestine.”
Foster, who has publicly expressed support for Israel, addressed the comments in an upcoming episode of the Not Skinny But Not Fat podcast, scheduled to debut on October 27, 2026.
“You know, it’s complicated. I think our work environment, our set is very similar to dinner tables around the world where people are having debate and discussion and disagreeing,” Foster said. “And you know, while I love Adam, I also disagree with him. And that’s okay.”
She also emphasised the importance of Jewish representation in television, explaining that the series was created to celebrate Judaism and her personal experiences within the faith.
“I think that as the creator of the show, all I can say is that I want our Jewish fans to know that I see you and I hear you and I understand how you feel,” she said.
Foster added that the series has always been intended as “a love letter to Judaism”, highlighting what she described as the importance of positive Jewish representation.
“That being said, everyone is entitled to a different opinion than me,” she said, reiterating that viewers should understand the creative intentions behind the programme.
Brody’s comments have also drawn reactions from others associated with the series, prompting further discussion about differing political perspectives within the production.

title: China s first AI film hits cinemas  but ticket sales lag
description: Country s first AI film faces weak presales  testing whether audiences will pay to watch AI made cinema
content:
Country's first AI film faces weak presales, testing whether audiences will pay to watch AI-made cinema
China's first fully AI-generated feature film opens in cinemas on Friday in what promises to be a tough box-office test for the country's booming tech industry as advance ticket sales lag.
More than 10,000 screenings of the sci-fi thriller Sanxingdui: Future Past are scheduled for Friday, according to ticketing platform Maoyan.
Public reception, however, has been less than enthusiastic.
Presale revenue as of Friday morning stood at 80,000 yuan ($11,980), while total box-office takings were forecast to remain below 150,000 yuan, only a fraction of the reported production cost, according to Maoyan.
Ticket prices range from 20 to 90 yuan, bringing the number sold to a few thousand at most.
Jiang Defu, CEO of the production company Bona Film Group, acknowledged the lukewarm reception in a recent interview but said the film was pushing boundaries.
"We are the first to try it, the first to get a theatrical release permit, and the first to be tested by the audience," he told Chinese film industry outlet Yuli. "I think that is not easy at all."
Nearly 100 people took more than two years to make the film, which cost more than 10 million yuan ($1.5 million), Bona said, although all the actors, their voices and the backdrops are AI-generated.
The film touches on the theme of humanity in a future shaped by AI.
But that was not enough to convince Iris Yang, who attended a free preview screening of the film on Thursday for acquaintances of the production team and industry workers.
Yang said she would not have paid for a ticket, given the movie's quality.
"If AI generation can match the theatrical experience of Avatar, I think I would be willing to pay for it," she said, referring to the US franchise known for the quality of its animation.
AI-generated video has gained popularity in the world's second-largest economy. On Douyin, the Chinese equivalent of TikTok, AI-generated short dramas garnered more than 200 billion views in September alone.
But "the audience won't automatically pay for the tickets just because it's an AI-generated film", independent AI director Zhang Jun told AFP .
Online, Chinese social media users also seemed unconvinced by the launch of AI movies in cinemas.
"If it's free to watch on streaming platforms, it could become legendary. But paying to watch? People are not going to accept it at this stage," one user on Weibo commented.
In Hollywood, the rise of AI has sparked concern among film workers about the prospect of job losses.
An AI-generated sci-fi feature called Gods Don't Give Gifts is scheduled for US release on December 4.
And a virtual Hollywood actor called Tilly Norwood, whose interviews have gone viral while fuelling job fears, is also set to star in an upcoming movie called Misaligned .

title: Security forces kill 10 Indian sponsored terrorists in Gwadar operations  ISPR
description: A civilian was killed and several vehicles damaged during attacks near Gabd border crossing and Gwadar city  says ISPR
content:
A civilian was killed and several vehicles damaged during attacks near Gabd border crossing and Gwadar city, says ISPR
Security forces killed 10 terrorists, including a woman, during operations in Gwadar after Indian-sponsored Fitna al-Hindustan terrorists attempted attacks near the Gabd border crossing and in Gwadar city, the military’s media wing said on Friday.
In a statement, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said the attacks took place on Thursday, leaving one civilian dead and several vehicles damaged. The operations concluded without any casualties among security personnel, and order had been restored, it added.
“Security forces foiled the terrorists’ designs and their bid to undermine the writ of the state and spread their misconstrued agenda,” the statement said.
The ISPR said the terrorists had targeted the very people they claimed to represent, seeking to obstruct Balochistan’s development and prosperity.
“The coercion of a Baloch woman into this attack is a crime not only against the state but also against the hurmat of Baloch women,” the statement said, condemning the involvement of a woman in the attack.
Also Read: 3 terrorists killed as security forces foil attack on construction camp in Gwadar: state media
The military’s media wing also criticised the use of women for propaganda, saying the tactic was intended to inflame public sentiment and lend a false sense of legitimacy to the terrorists’ campaign.
“Such tactics are contrary to Baloch and Islamic traditions, which hold women in the highest honour,” the statement said, adding that the people of Balochistan had consistently rejected those who shed blood in their name.
The ISPR said the counterterrorism campaign under the vision of “Azm-e-Istehkam”, approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, would continue.
“Security forces and law enforcement agencies remain resolute in eliminating foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country,” it added.
صدرِ مملکت آصف علی زرداری کا گوادر میں فتنہُ الہندوستان کے دہشت گردوں کے حملے کو ناکام بنانے اور دس دہشت گردوں کو جہنم واصل کرنے پر سیکیورٹی فورسز کو خراجِ تحسین۔ صدرِ مملکت کا دہشت گردی کے واقعے میں ایک شہری کی شہادت پر گہرے دکھ اور افسوس کا اظہار۔ بلوچستان کے امن و استحکام کے…
Meanwhile, President Asif Ali Zardari praised security forces for foiling the terrorist attacks in Gwadar and killing 10 terrorists, while expressing grief over the civilian’s death.
He said attempts to undermine peace and stability in Balochistan would not weaken the people’s resolve to pursue development and prosperity, stressing that peace was essential to safeguarding their rights and interests. He also condemned the exploitation of Baloch women’s dignity for political purposes.
A day earlier, Radio Pakistan reported that security forces had killed three terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan while foiling an attempt to attack an unoccupied construction company camp in Gwadar. Security sources said the forces had also surrounded other suspects.
In a separate operation, security forces were targeting terrorists hiding in a hotel near the Gwadar Highway. The Gwadar general officer commanding was personally leading the operation, according to the report.
Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022, and over the same period, TTP attacks increased more than sevenfold to 838 from 118.
Although K-P has borne the brunt of terrorism, Balochistan has also remained a major target of Indian proxies, which often target civilians and military installations in the province.
Over the past few years, Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist attacks, with militants frequently targeting convoys, abducting security personnel and civilians, and attacking security and civilian installations.
In a similar incident last week, 20 trainee police personnel were abducted by unidentified armed men while travelling between Kalat and Mastung in Balochistan.
Read More : Armed men abduct 20 trainee police personnel travelling from Kalat to Nushki: officials
The abducted personnel belonged to the districts of Kharan, Nushki, Chagai and Washuk in Rakhshan Division. They included eight personnel from Kharan, five from Nushki, four from Chagai and three from Washuk.
The forces continued operations across the provinces against what the state describes as Indian-sponsored terrorists and their proxies. Still, despite these efforts, the groups have continued to target civilian and defence installations.
In one such attack in July this year, at least 30 people, including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. The attackers also abducted several civilians and police personnel after the assault.
In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation , which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

title: French  Japanese authors try to write novel on one day train ride
description: 16 French and Japanese writers collaborate to create a 200 page novel aboard a luxury train in under 24 hours
content:
16 French and Japanese writers collaborate to create a 200-page novel aboard a luxury train in under 24 hours
Sixteen writers -- half French-speaking and half Japanese -- boarded a luxury train in Kyoto on Thursday, faced with the unusual task of collectively writing a novel in under 24 hours.
The authors, who include Muriel Barbery, are taking part in a project by L'ecriture en mouvement -- Writing in Motion -- a French association that promotes literary exchanges.
By the time the Mizukaze -- their striking, bottle-green train in the Art Deco style -- pulls into the western city of Matsue on Friday morning, they hope to have completed a 200-page story.
"It's a completely crazy project: coming together on an iconic train, where 16 voices must form a coherent and meaningful whole," said Barbery, famous in the English-speaking world primarily for her 2006 novel The Elegance of the Hedgehog.
"We were each given the biography of a character -- someone whom all the other characters knew, and who is the reason why they all ended up on the same train," she added.
French novelist Muriel Barbery said each author was given a character's biography to incorporate into the work. PHOTO: AFP
It is the second time Writing in Motion has orchestrated such a project. The first, held in Canada in 2015, also united local writers with French counterparts.
The central theme and overall narrative were discussed before departure, but the plot -- set aboard the Mizukaze itself -- will take shape as the journey unfolds.
The landscape outside, dotted with paddy fields and Japan's distinctive architecture, "will inevitably find its way" into the writing, said French writer Christophe Ono-dit-Biot.
So, too, will the train's spacious cabins, dark wood panelling, plush carpets and wall sconces that recall the opulence of the Orient Express.
French writer Herve Le Tellier (R) described the process as akin to "synchronised swimming". PHOTO: AFP
"It's not like we're making a collection of separate short stories. We're creating a novel, and I'm working to build bridges between the different pieces," said Anne Forrest-Wilson, the founder of Writing in Motion .
Interpreters are on board to help ensure smooth communication.
In the train bar, Toh EnJoe, a master of Japanese science-fiction, sipped a glass of wine as he wrote.
"It would be nice if it all comes together. There's a high chance it won't," he said.
"Everyone is drawing their parts separately, so the key point is how everyone is going to coordinate with each other -- or not."
His own character, he notes, "is unusual... my protagonist is someone who missed the train".
Several of the Japanese authors have won some of their country's most prestigious literary awards, including EnJoe, who took the Akutagawa Prize in 2012.
Others include Hitomi Kanehara, a novelist known for her radical style, and the poet Machi Tawara.
Toh EnJoe, a master of Japanese science-fiction, sipped a glass of wine as he wrote. PHOTO: AFP
The exercise follows the tradition of Oulipo , a movement founded in the 1960s mainly by French-speaking writers seeking new literary forms by imposing constraints on their techniques.
The group's best-known members have included Georges Perec and the Italian novelist Italo Calvino.
"Practicing gymnastics individually is not the same as doing it collectively. What we're doing is a little like synchronised swimming," Oulipo President Herve Le Tellier said.

title: Australia sanctions North Koreans over  fraudulent  IT work  cybercrime
description: The two men are alleged key operators in Pyongyang s cybercriminal activities overseas
content:
The two men are alleged key operators in Pyongyang's cybercriminal activities overseas
Australia said on Friday it had sanctioned two North Korean individuals and companies over the use of "fraudulent" IT workers and cybercrime to earn cash for the isolated nuclear-armed state.
The two men are alleged to be key operators in Pyongyang's cybercriminal activities overseas, estimated by analysts to bring in billions for the country's weapons programme.
"The North Korean entities and individuals sanctioned today facilitate North Korea's use of fraudulent IT workers to raise revenue for the regime's nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programmes," the office of Australia's foreign minister Penny Wong said.
Read: North Korea threatens South with 'most horrible' consequences, announces border countermeasures
North Korea faces a slew of international sanctions over its weapons and nuclear programmes. It stands accused of seeking to skirt those sanctions by employing thousands of IT workers impersonating nationals of other countries to obtain work and income on online platforms and remit the money to government agencies.
North Korea has furiously denied those allegations, deriding them as efforts to "tarnish" its image.
The United States and allies warned in July that North Korean workers were using AI tools to further obscure their true identities.
And last month, New Zealand's cybersecurity agency revealed a North Korean IT worker had used a fake identity to obtain remote work with a company in that country and then threatened to release sensitive information when exposed. The two men sanctioned by Australia on Friday, Yu Pu Ung and Sim Hyon Sop, have already been named by the US government.

In 2024, the US Treasury described the China-based Yu as a "linchpin" of North Korea's illicit money-making activities and warned he was "skilled at employing various schemes to avoid detection". Sim, reportedly a top "shadow banker" for the regime, is wanted by the FBI, with a $5 million reward for information leading to the arrest for his role in helping transfer funds in and out of North Korea.

title: LHC acquits Quran desecration convict  cites lack of proof and mental illness evidence
description: Court sets aside life sentence  ruling that a burnt copy alone could not establish deliberate desecration
content:
Court sets aside life sentence, ruling that a burnt copy alone could not establish deliberate desecration
The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Friday acquitted a man convicted of desecrating the Holy Quran, ruling that the recovery of a burnt copy alone could not establish guilt without proof of a wilful and deliberate act.
Justice Tariq Mehmood Bajwa of the court’s Rawalpindi bench allowed the criminal appeal filed by Shahidur Rehman, setting aside his conviction and life sentence under Section 295-B of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC).
The court held that the prosecution had failed to establish conclusively that the appellant had set fire to the copy. It also found that evidence of his long-standing mental illness could not be disregarded merely because no formal application had been filed under Section 464 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC).
Reiterating a fundamental principle of criminal law, the court observed that even a single reasonable doubt entitled an accused to acquittal as a matter of right.
The case was registered at Sarai Alamgir police station in Gujrat district following an incident allegedly reported on January 27, 2022.
According to the prosecution, the appellant emerged from a street near his residence carrying a burning copy of the Holy Quran and threw it onto the main road as people rushed to extinguish the fire. A major portion of the copy was burnt.
The trial court convicted him under Section 295-B PPC and sentenced him to life imprisonment on December 20, 2025.
Examining the evidence, Justice Bajwa noted that the complainant and another key prosecution witness had admitted during cross-examination that they had not seen the appellant setting fire to the copy.
The court explained that the word “wilfully” in Section 295-B required an intentional, deliberate and conscious act. The mere fact that a copy of the Holy Quran had been damaged by fire was insufficient to establish the offence unless the prosecution proved that the appellant had knowingly and deliberately caused the damage.
Justice Bajwa emphasised that the gravity of an allegation could not substitute for proof, adding that criminal cases had to be decided on evidence rather than emotions or sentiments. The prosecution was required to establish every essential element of the offence beyond reasonable doubt.
Addressing the appellant’s mental condition, the court noted that prosecution witnesses had consistently described him as mentally unwell. The complainant and other private witnesses said he had suffered from mental illness for approximately 13 to 14 years and had remained confined to his house for around 12 years.
The court examined the protection available under Section 84 PPC, which excludes criminal liability where, at the time of an act, a person is, by reason of unsoundness of mind, incapable of understanding the nature of the act or that it is wrong or contrary to law.
The judgment distinguished between mental incapacity at the time of an alleged offence and an accused’s capacity to understand trial proceedings or conduct a defence. It held that the absence of a formal application under Section 464 CrPC did not justify disregarding evidence relevant to the appellant’s mental condition at the time of the alleged offence.
Read more: LHC acquits man in wife's murder case
The court observed that the evidence raised serious and reasonable doubts about the appellant’s mental capacity at the relevant time, bringing the protection under Section 84 PPC into consideration.
It also identified shortcomings in the investigation. The investigating officer had not identified the specific Surah, Para or other portion of the Holy Quran allegedly defiled, while the recovered burnt pieces had not undergone scientific examination or other reliable identification.
The alleged matchbox had not been taken into possession, and no investigation had been conducted to establish the circumstances in which the copy had caught fire, the court noted.
Prosecution witnesses also gave contradictory accounts of the police’s arrival at the scene, the time officers spent there, the recording of their statements and their presence at the police station. These discrepancies further weakened the prosecution’s case, the court observed.
The judgment also noted that the investigating officer had made no meaningful effort to ascertain or address the appellant’s mental condition before sending him to judicial lock-up.
Finding that the prosecution had failed to establish the appellant’s involvement through reliable and consistent evidence, the high court acquitted him by extending the benefit of doubt.

title: New Greece law bans social media for under 15s
description: Bill to take effect January 1  will require age verification  impose harsh penalties if companies fail to comply
content:
Bill to take effect January 1, will require age verification, impose harsh penalties if companies fail to comply
Greece's parliament passed a law Friday banning children under 15 from social media, joining a growing number of countries imposing curbs on young people's use of the apps.
Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis announced plans for the ban in April, taking to TikTok — one of the most popular social networks with young people in Greece — to explain the "difficult but necessary" measure.
After a heated debate in a parliamentary session that started Thursday and stretched into Friday, Mitsotakis's conservative New Democracy party used its majority to pass the bill which no other parties backed, the Ana news agency reported.
The opposition socialist Pasok party abstained after seeking an alternative bill that would have banned social media for under-13s and parental controls for 13- and 14-year-olds. Other left wing and nationalist parties voted against.
Read: EU to ban social media for under 13s, curb access until 15
The bill, set to take effect on January 1, will require age verification on social networks and impose harsh penalties if companies fail to comply.
Australia last year became the first country to introduce such a social media ban for kids, barring under-16s. More than 20 countries have passed similar laws, according to an AFP tally.
Critics say social networks use addictive algorithms to keep kids glued to their screens, and warn excessive scrolling can damage their mental health .
Bans have faced push-back from free-speech advocates, and sceptics question how well they will work.

title: Rebel Wilson wins  359 000 in legal battle over  The Deb  as producers receive just  10
description: The dispute centres on  The Deb   a musical comedy in which Wilson made her directorial debut  starred and produced
content:
The dispute centres on 'The Deb', a musical comedy in which Wilson made her directorial debut, starred and produced
Rebel Wilson has won a second legal victory in the dispute surrounding her directorial debut, The Deb , with an Australian court ordering a production company to pay her business $359,000 in unpaid producer fees while awarding the opposing company just $10 in damages.
The New South Wales Supreme Court dismissed most of the case brought by UK production firm AI Film, which had sought $15 million from the actress, alleging that statements she made on social media and a website targeting producer Amanda Ghost had damaged the film’s commercial prospects.
Justice Elisabeth Peden found that AI Film had not demonstrated a causal link between Wilson’s statements and any financial losses. The court awarded AI Film’s subsidiary, AI Films, $10 in nominal damages for technical breaches of a social media contract. Wilson’s company, Camp Sugar Productions, was awarded $359,000 in unpaid producer fees, along with interest, and the company was ordered to pay Wilson’s legal costs.
The dispute centres on The Deb , a musical comedy in which Wilson made her directorial debut and also starred and served as a producer. The film had a reported budget of $22 million but earned approximately $335,000 at the Australian box office.
AI Film alleged that Wilson had made false and damaging claims about the producers, including accusations of financial misconduct, in an attempt to undermine the film and potentially devalue it. Wilson denied the allegations and countersued, seeking unpaid fees.
During the proceedings, the court examined Wilson’s social media posts accusing the producers of embezzling money and attempting to obstruct the film’s release. Justice Peden found that Wilson had acted maliciously in connection with the creation of a website targeting Ghost. However, the court found that AI Film had failed to establish that the website or the allegedly misleading statements had caused the company financial damage.
The judge also heard evidence that international distributors had expressed concerns about the film, describing it as feeling “small and distinctly Australian” in emails exchanged in October 2025.
Following the ruling, Wilson celebrated the outcome on Instagram, sharing a photograph of herself wearing a graduation gown and holding her University of New South Wales degree.
“This girl never knew how much she was going to need that law degree!!” she wrote.
Wilson added that defending herself had come at “an enormous personal, emotional and financial cost”, but said she was proud to have stood her ground “for myself and for others I was trying to protect”.
The decision marks Wilson’s second court victory connected to The Deb . Earlier in 2026, the Federal Court of Australia ruled in her favour in a separate defamation case brought by the film’s lead actor, Charlotte MacInnes.
MacInnes had alleged that several of Wilson’s social media posts damaged her reputation by suggesting she had withdrawn a complaint about an alleged uncomfortable encounter involving Ghost to advance her career. The court found that Wilson’s posts were not defamatory. MacInnes has lodged an appeal against that decision.
The legal disputes surrounding The Deb have also continued in the United States, where the film’s producers are pursuing separate defamation proceedings against Wilson in California.
A full written judgment explaining the reasons behind the latest ruling is expected to follow. For now, the decision leaves Wilson with a $359,000 award plus interest, while the production company’s successful claims resulted in only nominal damages.

Investors to be offered plots without upfront payment, with govt seeking 15% share of project inventory, says minister
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Friday announced plans to auction large plots in Islamabad for high-rise hotels, shopping malls and residential complexes without charging investors upfront, with the government seeking a share of the projects’ inventory instead of payment for the land.
Speaking at the Saudi-Pak Real Estate Expo in Lahore, Naqvi said the auction would start at 15% of the project’s inventory, with investors free to offer a higher share. The plots would be available in sizes of one, three and six acres, with buildings required to have a minimum height of 600 feet.
“The interesting thing is that it will be free of cost. We will not be asking for any money. We will go for inventory, and we will start the auction at 15% of the inventory. Then it will depend on the investor how much they offer us,” he said.
Naqvi said the government would impose two main conditions on investors: projects would have to be completed within two years of approval, and buildings would have to meet the minimum height requirement.
“We have only two demands: to complete the project within two years from the day of approval,” he said, adding that the approval process would be handled through a one-window operation at the Ministry of Interior. “We can do it within three to four weeks, so the investor does not need to go to any other office,” he stated.
The minister said the government was also prioritising the security of Pakistani and foreign investors.
To address potential concerns and prevent hurdles during project development, it would establish a five-member auction committee comprising representatives of the National Accountability Bureau (NAB), the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC), the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) and the Capital Development Authority (CDA), along with a judge to head the committee, he added.
Naqvi said it had yet to be decided whether the judge would be serving or retired. “All the stakeholders and those who could create hurdles for investors in the future will be part of the committee,” he added.
Naqvi also announced plans for a Manhattan-style city on 1,000 acres of land behind the Prime Minister’s House in Islamabad, featuring residential and commercial complexes surrounding a central park and a lake.
“We are launching a Manhattan-style city in Islamabad, which will have a completely different set of laws, rules and standard operating procedures (SOPs),” he said.
“It will be just like Manhattan, with a Central Park in the middle and a lake, surrounded by residential and commercial complexes,” he added.
The interior minister also announced plans for "Asia’s largest safari park, spanning 450 acres in Islamabad," saying the project would tap the country’s potential for entertainment and recreational facilities.
Citing an example from Punjab, Naqvi said an existing safari park that had been in poor condition was improved within six months through reconstruction and the introduction of additional animals.
He added that the park’s annual auction value had increased from Rs20 million to Rs680 million within a year of the improvements, despite the facility having only half the number of animals initially planned.
“This is the potential we have for entertainment in Pakistan. Our people are eager for entertainment, but we lack facilities, whether in the form of safari parks or other attractions,” he said.
Naqvi further said Islamabad offered significant opportunities for residential and entertainment projects, adding that the government had also taken steps to address concerns over high property prices.
He expressed confidence that the planned developments would attract investors from Saudi Arabia, reiterating that the government would simplify the process through a one-window operation at the Ministry of Interior.
“I can assure you of one thing: it will be a one-window operation. You will not need to visit any other government office. Everything will be handled by the Ministry of Interior,” he said. “We look forward to welcoming all of you to Islamabad, and I can assure you that these projects will change Pakistan,” he added.

content:
Canadian PM says there may be a decision on the issue before year-end
Canadian engineering company AtkinsRealis is in the running to help build Turkiye's third nuclear power plant, Canadian Prime Minister Mark ​Carney said.
NATO allies Canada and Turkey upgraded their relations to a "strategic partnership" ‌during the first bilateral visit by a Canadian prime minister a day earlier as Carney seeks new global trade partners to reduce reliance on the United States.
Landed in Ankara. This is the first bilateral visit to Türkiye by a Canadian Prime Minister, and we’re here to elevate our partnership. Unlocking access to a market of more than 85 million people. Creating new economic opportunities for our workers and businesses. pic.twitter.com/wVs344cLeX
The new partnership signed in Ankara focuses on ​trade and investment, defence, security and energy. It aims to create jobs and ​opportunities for Canadian and Turkish companies to do more business together.
Asked about ⁠talks on Canadian involvement in Turkiye's planned third nuclear power plant - over which Ankara ​has also held talks with South Korea, Russia, China, and Japan - Carney said the decision ​would ultimately be made by the Turkish government, but he believed Canada had better odds now.
"If you would have asked us a year ago how we would have pegged the chances, they would ​have been very low. Now there are good chances. There's real competition, of course," ​Carney told reporters in Istanbul, adding that there may be a decision on the issue before year-end.
Read: Turkiye, US agency sign grant agreement on next-generation nuclear technologies
He ‌said ⁠the strength of Canada's CANDU technology, partnership with some Turkish businesses, including on the construction side, and the ability to build out elements of the supply chain make it "quite a compelling proposition."
Rosatom, Russia's state nuclear energy company, is building Turkiye's first nuclear power station ​at Akkuyu in the ​Mediterranean province of ⁠Mersin under a $20 billion accord from 2010. It said last week that it expected a year-end nuclear start-up at the site.
Turkiye plans to ​build a second nuclear power plant in the Black Sea region ​of Sinop, ⁠with the third planned in the northwestern region of Thrace.
Reuters had reported before Carney's visit that the allies would discuss potential purchases by Turkey of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from Canada, as ⁠well as ​critical minerals. On Thursday, they said they had agreed ​to significantly increase collaboration across the energy sector, including in LNG, civil nuclear energy and renewable energy.

title: French businesses  events to close with more weekend protests expected
description: Macron blames  seditious  ultra left groups for unrest  far left France    Unbowed party denies allegations
content:
Macron blames 'seditious' ultra-left groups for unrest, far-left France ​Unbowed party denies allegations
Businesses, cultural events and museums planned to close at the weekend despite curbs on ​demonstrations as French President Emmanuel Macron seeks to restore order a week after nationwide protests turned violent .
France's main student union, ‌UNEF, has called for rallies on Saturday, while the Yellow Vest movement , an anti-establishment force that emerged in 2018, filed plans this week for a march through central Paris.
Macron was due to meet student representatives later on Friday to discuss their plans, but UNEF said their rallies, which grew from high school protests last month against teacher shortages and ​shabby facilities, would go ahead.
"Macron is trampling upon the freedom to protest in our country, and is spitting on the values of ​the republic he claims to defend," the union said in an emailed statement.
Trade Union leader says curbing protest will not work
France is still reeling from the worst violence in years last weekend, when looting and riots took place on the fringes of nationwide protests , though overnight curfews in parts of Paris and other cities have since passed without major incident.
Macron blamed "seditious" ultra-left groups for the unrest - allegations the prominent far-left France ​Unbowed party denied - and said a day earlier that "illegitimate" protests would be banned in coming days. Demonstrations organised by groups such as trade unions would be allowed to proceed but could be diverted along alternative routes, he said.
Read: Macron rebukes foreign leaders over unrest rhetoric
Marylise Leon, the general secretary of the CFDT, one of the nation's largest trade unions, said the measure would do little to ​restore calm, adding that it would be better for the government to make concrete proposals to address people's anger. "It's counterproductive because there is a lot ​of anger, a lot of anger and a demand to be considered and to be listened to," she told French broadcaster TF1 . "It's not for the president to decide ‌who can ⁠legitimately request to protest."
Workers, students and others are protesting budget cuts and calling for higher wages to help people meet high living costs. The government says it understands their concerns but needs to keep spending in check to contain rising borrowing costs.
Far-right to meet in Orléans with counter-protests planned
All protests planned for Saturday in Marseille and Lyon, France's second- and third-largest cities, have been banned, local authorities said.
Despite the curbs, and what the justice minister said had been 2,700 ​arrests since Saturday, businesses, institutions and ​events were planning to close in ⁠case of more unrest.
The Marseille Chamber of Commerce urged businesses to shut on Saturday, while organisers of Art Basel Paris said the art fair would be shuttered all weekend. The Louvre and the Fondation Louis Vuitton will be ​closed on Saturday.
Orléans, in central France, was bracing for unrest, as the far-right National Rally was scheduled to ​have a party meeting, ⁠with thousands expected to hold demonstrations in opposition.
Read More: 'France is burning', Trump blames immigration for riots
The interior ministry is due to unveil its security plans later on Friday. Macron is expected to hold a meeting on defence and security as well as meeting with student groups on Friday.
Soaring energy costs, pressure on household budgets and concerns over deteriorating public services have fuelled ⁠unrest among ​workers and younger voters, but the French government has little spare cash to address concerns.
The risk ​premium on French government debt over German bonds widened to its highest level in 15 years yesterday, highlighting investor unease. Credit rating agency Moody's is expected to announce a ratings ​action on France late on Friday.

title: Obsession    star Inde Navarrette says Gen Z is tired of product placement in films
description: The horror hit    Obsession    reportedly earned  522m worldwide after being made for less than  1m
content:
The horror hit ‘Obsession’ reportedly earned $522m worldwide after being made for less than $1m
Inde Navarrette has urged Hollywood to reconsider its approach to younger moviegoers, arguing that Gen Z audiences want original films without feeling they are being targeted by advertising and product placement.
The Obsession star shared her views during an appearance on The Kyle Buchanan Show , where she discussed what could encourage younger audiences to keep visiting cinemas. Navarrette said originality and authentic human experiences should remain central to filmmaking, rather than allowing commercial interests to dominate what viewers see on screen.
“Gen Z just wants to go to something that they do not feel like they are being sold,” Navarrette said, pointing to the frequency of advertising and product placement in movies.
She acknowledged that commercial partnerships are a familiar part of modern entertainment, noting that some television commercials have become memorable cultural references. However, she argued that audiences still want films built around compelling stories rather than promotional messaging.
Navarrette also stressed the importance of emotional connection in cinema, saying technological advances have not changed the need for stories that reflect human experiences. She credited Obsession with delivering the kind of originality and emotional impact she believes audiences are seeking.
The horror film became a major box office success, with Variety reporting a worldwide gross of $522 million against a production budget of less than $1 million. Its reported performance across four consecutive weekends also demonstrated the strength of audience word of mouth.
Navarrette’s comments come amid broader discussion about younger generations and theatrical moviegoing. A Fandango study reported by Variety found that 87% of Gen Z respondents and 82% of millennials had seen at least one film in cinemas during a year. The figures compared with 70% for Gen X and 58% for baby boomers.
The study also found that Gen Z and millennial moviegoers averaged around seven cinema visits annually. Both groups showed an appetite for shared theatrical experiences, suggesting that cinemas can still attract younger audiences when films offer something worth experiencing together.
Navarrette’s message to studios is clear: audiences want stories that make them feel something, not films that leave them feeling they have been sold a product.

US firm expresses interest in working to promote progressive business environment, productive economy in Pakistan
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said Pakistan was ready to partner with international consulting firms to strengthen economic growth, stressing the need for "impact and accountability" as the government pursued structural reforms and privatisation, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office (PMO).
“Pakistan is ready to have a productive and meaningful partnership with international consulting firms to strengthen economic growth, while ensuring impact and accountability at their end,” PM Shehbaz said during a meeting with Peter Briggs, managing director of the North American operations of international consulting firm Alvarez & Marsal (A&M), in Islamabad.
The prime minister welcomed Briggs and reiterated Pakistan’s willingness to open its economy to promising international markets and consult globally recognised economic experts, according to the PMO.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif met with Mr. Peter Briggs, the Managing Director, North American Operations of Alvarez & Marsal (A&M), an International Consulting Firm in Islamabad today. The Prime Minister welcomed the Managing Director while reiterating Pakistan's… pic.twitter.com/ggAxUiPrTv
PM Shehbaz said that after successfully achieving the goal of economic and fiscal stability, the government was taking effective measures to introduce deep-rooted structural and economic reforms. These measures aimed to “usher into an era of export-led growth and productive economy,” he said.
He highlighted the government’s focus on improving the performance and efficiency of the domestic manufacturing sector, while also taking measures to attract foreign direct investment (FDI).

The premier also told the delegation that the government was following a “vibrant strategy” to assess the economic viability of state-owned enterprises (SOEs) and subsequently pursue privatisation to support the national economy and economic growth.

Briggs thanked PM Shehbaz for the meeting and extended his gratitude regarding the government’s commitment to attracting FDI and engaging constructively with international economic experts.
He also expressed A&M’s eagerness to establish positive coordination and cooperation with Pakistan to promote a progressive business environment and a productive economy.

title: State counsel completes cross examination in Imaan  Hadi security breach case
description: Court expected to provide Imaan and Hadi with their Section 342 questionnaires tomorrow
content:
Court expected to provide Imaan and Hadi with their Section 342 questionnaires tomorrow
A state-appointed counsel on Friday completed the cross-examination of all prosecution witnesses in a security breach case against lawyers Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha, who are being tried at Adiala Jail over the alleged disruption of an international cricket team’s security route and incitement to public unrest.
The couple is accused of removing barriers along the route. They were indicted in the case on October 7.
Anti-terrorism court (ATC) Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra heard the case inside Adiala Jail, where state counsel Atif Mahmood cross-examined the prosecution witnesses.
The court was expected to provide Imaan and Hadi with their questionnaires under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) at the next hearing on Saturday. A decision could be reserved once the trial proceedings were completed.
Read More: ATC replaces state counsel after Imaan, Hadi object to appointment
The proceedings followed a dispute over the appointment of state counsel. On Thursday, the court replaced Taimoor Janjua with Advocate Atif Mahmood after Imaan and Hadi objected to Janjua’s appointment. Judge Sipra accepted their application challenging the appointment.
During Thursday’s hearing, Hadi alleged that Janjua had told people he received Rs500,000 and completed the cross-examination in a single day. Janjua disputed the criticism, while Judge Sipra expressed displeasure over his conduct in court.
The court had appointed Janjua a day earlier after the defence lawyers failed to cross-examine the prosecution witnesses.
The Islamabad ATC framed charges against Imaan and Hadi on October 7 in a case relating to the alleged removal of security barriers and disruption of a designated route during the visit of an international cricket team.
The court subsequently recorded statements from all seven prosecution witnesses, and the case has reached the cross-examination stage.
The trial was shifted to Adiala Jail amid disputes over the accused’s production in court and defence lawyers’ access to their clients.
Separately, Imaan and Hadi approached the Islamabad High Court (IHC) seeking to suspend the trial, alleging procedural violations in the framing of charges, including that they had not been physically present when indicted and had not received copies of relevant documents.
The IHC heard their appeals on October 19 and said it would issue an order after hearing the respondents.
Imaan and her husband Hadi were rearrested on September 17 , shortly after the Supreme Court granted them bail and suspended their sentences in a separate social-media posts case. They were produced before an Islamabad ATC in connection with a case registered at Kohsar Police Station.
Police sought 30-day physical remand, but ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain rejected the request and sent the couple on judicial remand. The judge noted that although they had been nominated in the FIR as members of an unlawful assembly, no weapon had been attributed to either accused.
Read More: SC suspends trial court order, grants bail to Imaan Mazari, Hadi Ali Chattha
On September 27, the court issued a contempt notice to the Adiala jail superintendent after the authorities failed to facilitate the signing and transmission of the documents and also failed to produce the accused through video link. Two days later, the issue was resolved after Imaan and Hadi signed the required powers of attorney.
On September 29 , the ATC ended the contempt proceedings against the jail authorities and separately confirmed that notices had been issued on the couple’s bail applications, with arguments scheduled before Judge Abul Hasnat.
On October 7, the ATC had framed charges against Imaan and Hadi in the case related to the alleged violation of a designated route and incitement during the arrival of an international cricket team, despite defence objections that legal requirements had not been fulfilled.

title: Carrick under pressure as Brighton eye Liverpool
description: Manchester United risk slipping into the relegation zone
content:
Manchester United risk slipping into the relegation zone
Beset by infighting and off to their worst league start for decades, Manchester United host Bournemouth needing to snap a seven-game winless run to quell talk of another mid-season managerial change.
Michael Carrick's men are 13th in the Premier League and could even drop into the bottom three if results go against them this weekend.
At the other end of the table, Manchester City aim to extend their flawless start to the season at Aston Villa, despite doubts over the club's future in the English top-flight.
Third-placed Brighton are dreaming of an unlikely title challenge but face a stiff examination when they travel to Liverpool.
AFP Sport looks at the pick of the Premier League action this weekend:
The Red Devils sank to new depths during a terrible start to the season in a 4-1 thrashing by Champions League debutants Como in midweek.
Captain Bruno Fernandes took aim at his manager's passive tactics after the match, saying United had to be more "brave".
But Carrick, who apologised to the travelling fans in Italy, hit back at his players for not covering enough ground.
"Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win," said the former United midfielder.
The blunt remarks come just a week after defender Lisandro Martinez criticised the club's board for not investing enough in the transfer market.
United's return of seven points from their opening seven games is their lowest of the Premier League era.
After the departures of Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim in the past two seasons, United are facing another campaign of transition unless Carrick can quickly right the ship.
Only Barcelona have outscored Brighton in Europe's top five leagues this season, with the Seagulls netting 23 times in their seven games.
Brighton have soared through the divisions and into Europe on the back of owner Tony Bloom's expertise in data analytics, but they are yet to win a major trophy in their 125-year history.
Matching Leicester's remarkable title triumph a decade ago still seems unlikely, but Brighton will get a clearer idea of where they stand after visits to Anfield and Manchester City in the next two weekends.
Despite routinely selling their prized assets to wealthier clubs, Brighton's smart recruitment of both players and coaches has ensured they have continued to thrive.
"We can enjoy it, but on the other side it's also very important to stay humble and stay grounded because in football things can change quickly," said 33-year-old manager Fabian Hurzeler.
"We have to have this hunger inside of us to keep going and never be satisfied -- to keep pushing."
Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca is the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club.
Yet it may all count for nothing unless City are successful in their appeal after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.
Maresca's men travel to Aston Villa on Saturday, hoping to improve on a miserable recent record in Birmingham.
City have lost on their past three visits to Villa Park and face a resurgent opponent after an overhaul of Unai Emery's squad in the transfer market.
Villa have won five and drawn one of their past six games in all competitions as new signings Nicolas Jackson, Johan Manzambi and Zion Suzuki have quickly settled in to mitigate the loss of Ollie Watkins, Morgan Rogers and Emi Martinez.
"How we are responding, getting better, is really fantastic," Emery said after Villa beat Viking to make it three wins from three in the Champions League.
"How some individual players are feeling comfortable and getting confidence and getting better rhythm on the field is really as well something (that) makes us happy and confident (in) ourselves."

title: Barcelona eye Clasico statement against Real Madrid
description: Flick s side look to extend their advantage despite defensive injuries
content:
Flick's side look to extend their advantage despite defensive injuries
For weeks La Liga leaders Barcelona have been eagerly awaiting Sunday's Clasico as a chance to stretch the gap between themselves and rivals Real Madrid to a massive nine points.
Some turbulence in the final approach to the clash at Camp Nou has complicated the picture for Hansi Flick's Spanish champions, who suffered their first defeat of the season at Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Tuesday.
By contrast Real Madrid have won four consecutive matches, thrashing RB Leipzig on Wednesday, and starting to look, for the first time since Jose Mourinho's arrival this summer, like a team.
Despite that, the equation remains favourable for Flick. With Raphinha fit again and teenage winger Lamine Yamal enjoying a state of grace, Barcelona will be confident of building on their six-point lead over third-placed Madrid.
A Clasico often proves a fork in the road. Last season Madrid won the first meeting against Barcelona but Vinicius Junior's outraged reaction at being substituted pulled apart the fragile seams of Xabi Alonso's new era.
The Basque coach was ousted little over two months later, and his replacement Alvaro Arbeloa was unable to stop Madrid finishing a second straight season without winning a major trophy, while Barca retained the Spanish title at a canter.
On Sunday Brazil international Vinicius is suspended. Even aside from his underwhelming performances, his absence may help Madrid in terms of providing a clearer path for Mourinho.
"Vinicius's four-match suspension was seen within Real Madrid more as a solution than a problem," wrote Spanish daily AS.
Mourinho has largely deployed all of his team's stars when available, despite the difficulty it poses in terms of a cohesive game plan and finding balance between attack and defence.
Record 140 million euro ($157m) signing Yan Diomande offers more defensively and he is starting to hit his stride going forward, meaning the teenager may be Mourinho's choice against Barca.
An alternative would be to add an extra midfielder to try and disrupt Flick's free-flowing Barcelona, a strategy firmly within Mourinho's wheelhouse, although PSG showed Barca are easier to beat by attacking.
Despite Madrid's improving recent form, Mourinho insisted "confidence doesn't exist" for Clasicos.
"It's not a game like the others... we're losing 24 hours of rest (compared to Barcelona)," Mourinho complained on Wednesday.
Barcelona have their own problems regardless, including several injury concerns in defence. Eric Garcia and Andreas Christensen are sidelined, while Jules Kounde is a doubt. Midfielder Dani Olmo is also out injured.
Furthermore, the Catalan giants shipped four goals against PSG and showed they are no closer to solving their vulnerability at the back, something which has persisted in the Flick era, partially caused by their high defensive line.
"We made too many mistakes, especially in ball possession, easy ball losses," admitted Flick. "This is what we have to analyse...
"We have to understand the mistakes happen because (players) are not fresh. What they had to do the last couple of weeks is unbelievable."
The good news for Barcelona is that they still have the Midas touch -- everything turns to goals. They have scored at least twice in every match this season.
"Our unbeaten run (domestically) is still intact, and we'll do everything we can to keep it that way," Raphinha told TNT Sports.
Barcelona have averaged over four goals a game this season and Raphinha is the league's top scorer, with 12 goals, three more than Kylian Mbappe has scored for Real Madrid, with Yamal third on eight.
Mbappe and Yamal are both hoping they will be crowned the planet's best player on Monday at the Ballon d'Or ceremony, but the bigger prize for their teams would be a Clasico victory.

title: US to host women s Club World Cup in 2028
description: The inaugural tournament features 19 elite sides
content:
The inaugural tournament features 19 elite sides
The United States will host the inaugural women's football Club World Cup in 2028, FIFA announced Thursday.
"The decision was taken in view of its experience in organising FIFA tournaments, the maturity of its infrastructure and services and the level of stakeholder interest in women's football in the country," world football's governing body said.
The US has a proven track record of staging large sporting events, notably co-hosting the men's World Cup earlier this year.
The first-ever women's Club World Cup will be staged from January 5-30, 2028.
It will bring together 19 top-tier clubs from all six continental confederations.
The AFC (Asia), CAF (Africa), CONCACAF (North America) and CONMEBOL (South America) will be represented by three clubs apiece at the competition, one team will fly the flag for the OFC (Oceania) and six of Europe's best sides will represent UEFA.
Seven clubs have already secured their berths at the tournament: Arsenal (England), Club America Femenil (Mexico), Barcelona (Spain), Gotham (United States), Naegohyang (North Korea), Corinthians (Brazil) and Wuhan Jiangda (China).
"These seven clubs, and a dozen more, will come together to show the strength and depth of women's club football to a global audience," said FIFA chief women's football officer Sarai Bareman.
"They will have the opportunity to tell their story, expand their fan base and represent their club on the world stage. They have thoroughly earned this opportunity to be part of history in the United States."
FIFA said the introduction of the tournament marked "a major milestone for the professionalisation and global expansion of the women's club game, giving elite club sides a true world stage to compete on every four years".
Initially slated for 2026, FIFA pushed the inaugural tournament back by two years so it enjoys a clear window following the 2027 women's World Cup and ahead of the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles.

title: Hashimoto sweeps to gymnastics world all around title
description: He finishes 1 799 points clear of China   s Yang Haonan
content:
He finishes 1.799 points clear of China’s Yang Haonan
Japan’s Daiki Hashimoto successfully defended his men’s individual all-around title at the Artistic Gymnastics World Championships in Rotterdam on Thursday ahead of China’s Yang Haonan and Britain's Joe Fraser.
Having already claimed team gold the previous day, the 25-year-old from Narita secured his seventh world title in the Netherlands and his fourth all-around crown in a row.
He took it by a comfortable margin, finishing 1.799pts ahead of Yang. It was the biggest winning margin in a men's all-around at an Olympics or a worlds in 13 years.
Hashimoto is a worthy successor to fellow Japanese, the elegant Kohei Uchimura, who won a record six consecutive world all-around titles between 2009 and 2015.
Initially trailing the unflappable Yang, and despite a modest start on the first two apparatuses (floor exercise and rings), the three-time Olympic champion eventually surged to victory thanks to two outstanding performances on the parallel bars and the horizontal bar.
Reigning Olympic champion Shinnosuke Oka, meanwhile, endured a difficult evening. Two botched landings on vault during the fourth rotation ended his hopes of reaching the podium.
There was even greater disappointment for Russia’s Arsenii Dukhno, who trailed Hashimoto by just one-tenth of a point heading into the final rotation.
A fall on the horizontal bar following a missed grip ended his challenge for gold and even knocked him off the podium altogether, leaving him seventh.
The World Championships continue on Thursday with the women’s individual all-around competition.

title: PSL 12 roadmap sets stage
description: Direct signings open as 2027 tournament expands to six venues
content:
Direct signings open as 2027 tournament expands to six venues
The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Friday opened the direct signing window for the 12th edition of the Pakistan Super League (PSL), with the tournament scheduled to run from March 18 to May 2, 2027.
The PCB said the 46-day competition would feature 44 matches, including 40 league games and four playoff fixtures, across five to six venues, marking an expansion of the country's premier Twenty20 franchise tournament.
Franchises can directly sign one marquee player who did not feature in either of the previous two editions, PSL 10 and PSL 11. The window will remain open until November 23, the board said.
The player auction is scheduled for January 23, 2027, while the tournament's opening match will take place on March 18. The final is set for Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium on May 2.
The PCB said a franchise workshop would be held next week to discuss player-retention deadlines, the pre-auction trading window, auction rules and playing conditions.
The board has also aligned its domestic competition calendar with the PSL pre-season schedule, with the National T20 Gold and National T20 Silver tournaments set to serve as key platforms for identifying talent ahead of the auction.
The initiative is intended to provide standout domestic performers with a pathway into the PSL and potentially the national team, the PCB said.
PCB Chairman Mohsin Naqvi said the upcoming edition would build on the league's momentum and provide greater opportunities for cities across Pakistan to host matches.
“The roadmap we have finalised and are partially announcing today gives every stakeholder, from franchises and players to commercial partners and broadcasters, the certainty to plan at the highest level,” Naqvi said.
PSL Chief Executive Salman Naseer said the expansion to five or six venues would bring the competition closer to fans in more cities.
The direct-signing window marks the start of preparations for franchises as they assemble their squads for the 2027 season, with player signings, trades and retention decisions expected to shape the teams ahead of the January auction.

title: My everyday reality looks very different   Barbara Palvin shares BTS of runway return 6 weeks postpartum
description: Palvin walked the 2026 Victoria   s Secret Fashion Show shortly after giving birth to her daughter with Dylan Sprouse
content:
Palvin walked the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show shortly after giving birth to her daughter with Dylan Sprouse
Barbara Palvin has opened up about her postpartum experience after walking in the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show just six weeks after giving birth to her daughter, Sylvie.
The 33-year-old Hungarian model shared behind-the-scenes photographs on Instagram on October 22, revealing that nursing pads had been sewn into her bra for the runway appearance. She also posted a photograph of herself pumping backstage.
Palvin thanked Victoria’s Secret for supporting her, writing that the brand was “embracing me exactly where I am in my postpartum journey and making me feel so beautiful and confident.”
The model also highlighted the challenges mothers face when returning to work after childbirth, particularly in the United States, where many women return within six to eight weeks without paid maternity leave.
“Mothers deserve more time, more support, and more choices,” Palvin wrote, acknowledging that her return to work was a choice she was fortunate to have.
She also encouraged mothers not to compare their experiences, explaining that life after childbirth can look very different from the polished image presented on the runway.
“What you saw on that runway was me all dolled up, but my everyday postpartum reality looks very different,” she said, adding that finding time for a shower or a peaceful meal can feel like a significant achievement.
Palvin and her husband, actor Dylan Sprouse, welcomed their first child in September. Sprouse attended the fashion show to support his wife, praising her dedication and composure.
Palvin concluded her message by celebrating motherhood and thanking her family and friends for their support, describing the experience as “hard, beautiful, messy, emotional, and so, so worth it.”

title: Microsoft develops AI tool that can diagnose  sequentially  like a doctor
description: Model uses  orchestrator  that employs simulated panel of clinical experts collaborating to solve diagnostic cases
content:
Model uses 'orchestrator' that employs simulated panel of clinical experts collaborating to solve diagnostic cases
Microsoft researchers say an AI tool that diagnoses patients step by step, as doctors do, was more than twice as accurate as general physicians at solving complex medical cases, according to a study published on Thursday in Science .
The model identifies and coordinates the questions that should be asked of a patient, as well as the exams and tests that should be ordered, using an "orchestrator" that organises how AI will tackle a problem by employing a simulated panel of clinical experts collaborating to solve diagnostic cases, according to the report.
Existing medical AI models typically take an all-at-once approach that examines all of a patient's symptoms, lab results and imaging studies to generate a diagnosis.
With the orchestrator coordinating the steps to reaching a diagnosis, the AI model first decides what to ask about the patient’s history and what is significant in the physical exam. Based on what it learns, it decides which tests to order, considers the results, and orders further testing as appropriate. All the while, it is updating its working hypotheses and plans, the research leaders said in an interview.
Read: AI, social media drive self-medication trend
Tasked with diagnosing more than 300 highly unusual and confusing medical dilemmas, the model employing the diagnostic orchestrator was more than twice as accurate at "working up" the patient and determining the diagnosis as general physicians using textbooks and the internet. The tool also outperformed human physicians when presented with scenarios drawn from a major database of emergency room admissions.
Assessments comparing these types of older systems to human doctors usually use multiple-choice questions, the researchers said.
"AI has become very good at getting a 100% pass rate on those,” said Dr Dominic King, the corporate vice president of the health unit at Microsoft AI, whose team is developing the new technology. “But of course, that's not real-world. No patient ever came to see me with a nice summary.”
Read More: Alibaba open-sources AI model detecting cancer, 150 medical conditions
The researchers also found that diagnostic processes cost less when the orchestrator designs the work-ups than when human doctors do. “We're not just measuring the accuracy of the systems. We're also measuring how judiciously and carefully it goes through a diagnostic work-up,” said Harsha Nori, head of AI at Microsoft AI Health.
In a collaboration with Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Centre in Boston, the researchers will next test the tool’s ability to triage patients in emergency department waiting rooms.

title: Ryan Gosling   s band Dead Man   s Bones announces new music after 17 year break

Gosling and Zach Shields' rock duo is making a comeback with new music set to be released later this month
Ryan Gosling and Zach Shields are bringing their rock duo Dead Man’s Bones back after 17 years, with new music scheduled for release on October 27, 2026.
The pair announced their return on the band’s Instagram account on Thursday, October 22, signalling a revival of the project known for its eerie songs about ghosts and monsters.
Dead Man’s Bones released its self-titled debut album in 2009, collaborating with the Silverlake Conservatory Children’s Choir. The upcoming release marks the duo’s first new music since that album.
The band’s announcement video features a haunting voice reciting a poem about ghosts returning to the world, ending with the words, “All of this must change Oct. 27”. A young girl’s voice then announces the release date.
Gosling’s partner, Eva Mendes, had previously hinted at the comeback on social media, writing, “Trying to summon new music from Dead Man’s Bones”. Following the announcement, she added, “He came through on his promise to me.”
Although the band has been inactive for years, Gosling has continued to demonstrate his musical abilities through films including La La Land and Barbie .
His performance of “I’m Just Ken” in Barbie earned him a Grammy nomination, and he performed the song live at the Academy Awards in 2024.
The comeback comes during a busy period for the actor, who is campaigning for an Oscar for Project Hail Mary .
He is also expected to appear in Star Wars: Starfighter , scheduled for release next year, while Marvel’s Ghost Rider is among the projects on the horizon.

title: Rybakina into Ningbo quarter finals
description: World number one progresses after injury forces Kudermetova to retire at 5 0
content:
World number one progresses after injury forces Kudermetova to retire at 5-0
World number one Elena Rybakina reached the quarter-finals of the Ningbo Open on Thursday on her return from injury when opponent Polina Kudermetova retired.
The top seed and defending champion was cruising 5-0 in eastern China when the world number 105 from Uzbekistan called it quits because of injury.
Moscow-born Kazakh Rybakina will face Poland's unseeded Katarzyna Kawa in the last eight.
Rybakina, 27, won the US Open for her third Grand Slam crown in September and usurped Aryna Sabalenka as world number one in New York.
She was then stunned in the second round in Beijing at the start of this month, and pulled out of the Wuhan Open citing a foot injury.
Alexandra Eala crashed out in the Ningbo last 16 as the Philippine history-maker suffered a battling straight-sets defeat to Diana Shnaider.
The Russian world number 13 won 7-5, 6-4 and will face the talented American teenager Iva Jovic in the quarter-finals.
The 21-year-old Eala in August became the first player from the Philippines to win a WTA title and is typically followed by a throng of fans from her country.
But after beating France's Diane Parry in straight sets in the previous round in Ningbo, the world number 20 came up against a far sterner test in Shnaider.
The 22-year-old Russian, who is seeking to win a sixth WTA singles title, used her superior power to take the first set in just over 50 minutes.
The second set was closer as Eala fought for survival.
Shnaider put the Eala serve under severe pressure in the ninth game before breaking for 5-4, then doggedly held to seal victory in one hour and 55 minutes.
The 18-year-old Jovic defeated two-time Grand Slam finalist Jasmine Paolini of Italy 6-4, 6-3.

content:
Board sets October 31 deadline for outstanding dues
A proposal to reduce Pakistani players’ salaries in the Pakistan Super League (PSL) has been rejected by the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), following a virtual meeting with franchise owners on Thursday.
During the meeting, one franchise owner argued that players’ salaries were too high and should be reviewed. However, the board did not approve the proposal.
The PCB also directed stakeholders with outstanding dues to clear all payments by October 31. An official of one defaulting company said the company would meet its obligations.
“We are not going to run away. I will arrange a bank guarantee against my land and submit it to the PCB,” the official said.
A representative of another defaulting franchise said he had no information about the matter and that only the company’s owner could provide details.
The auction for PSL Season 12 is expected to take place on January 23. One franchise owner proposed holding the auction in China.
The board set January 13 as the deadline for player retentions, prompting another franchise owner to suggest that the process be held in December instead. The owner of another team said he would comment only after consulting his cricket operations team.
The PSL 12 final will be held at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium on May 2, while the opening match is scheduled for March 18.
The South Asian Games (SAG) are scheduled to take place in Islamabad, Lahore and Peshawar from April 4 to 11. No PSL matches will be held in these cities during that period.
The tournament schedule will be finalised at the next meeting of the cricket committee.
During the meeting, PCB officials also briefed franchise representatives on the promising talent emerging from school cricket. The board said it wanted to develop young players into future stars and urged franchises to assess their abilities, identify the most talented prospects and nurture them within their teams.
The proposal received a positive response from franchise owners.
