title: From tech giants to anonymous nonprofits  the biggest donors in US midterms
description: Donors have made contributions to both parties  special interest groups such as PACs
content:
Donors have made contributions to both parties, special interest groups such as PACs
The 15 largest contributors in the upcoming United States midterm elections have donated over $1.5 billion, an AFP analysis of Federal Election Commission data shows, as the race shapes up to be the most expensive midterms to date.
The biggest donors, as of October 21, have made contributions to both parties and to special interest groups, such as super political action committees (PACs) lobbying for deregulated AI and cryptocurrency.
World's richest man and Republican ally Elon Musk has donated over $365 million, including $278 million since July 1. According to campaign finance tracker OpenSecrets, this makes him the largest individual contributor in a federal election cycle since unlimited election spending was allowed in 2010.
Read: Trump's approval falls to record low of 31% as midterms near, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
"We're on track to have the most expensive midterm elections in US history", Michael Beckel, director of money in politics reform at bipartisan advocacy organisation Issue One, told AFP .
AFP analysed contributions since November 6, 2024, counting businesses and their leaders, as well as business partners and/or spouses as a single contributor where relevant, based on a New York Times methodology to track campaign finances.
Of the top 15 biggest contributors, five are in tech, particularly in the AI and cryptocurrency sectors. These donors, who tend to favour deregulation in their industries, are "pumping massive sums of money into US elections hoping to elect politicians who will advance their preferred policy positions," Beckel said.
Venture capitalists and business partners Marc Andreessen and Benjamin Horowitz have spent over $113 million so far. They donated $50 million to the pro-AI super PAC Leading the Future and $46.8 million to Fairshake, a cryptocurrency super PAC.
They also donated $12 million to US President Donald Trump's Make America Great Again (MAGA) Inc super PAC.
Read More: Trump government ads draw scrutiny weeks before midterm elections
Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase has donated close to $57 million in total this election cycle, including donations from its CEO and co-founder Brian Armstrong. Ripple Labs, another crypto firm, and its co-founder Chris Larsen have donated over $68 million. The majority of those two companies' contributions were to Fairshake.
The Winklevoss brothers Cameron and Tyler, major figures of the crypto landscape, donated to MAGA Inc and to their own pro-crypto super PAC.
Musk's donations have mostly gone to his Republican-leaning America PAC, as well as to the Republican Senate Leadership Fund super PAC (SLF). The SLF used Musk's $158 million donations in September to support Ken Paxton, the Republican Senate candidate in Texas.
Four anonymous nonprofit groups, known as 501C4 organisations or dark money groups, are amongst the top 15 donors this election cycle. These nonprofits fund campaign finance but are not legally required to publicly disclose their donors.
"Dark money spending has been increasing year over year, and it is a troubling trend because voters should be able to know who is financing the ads that they see", Shanna Ports, Senior Legal Counsel at the Campaign Legal Center, told AFP .
Also Read: Trump’s new AI-powered website says president lost 2020 election
One Nation, a Republican nonprofit group, gave almost $138 million to the SLF. The American Action Network, another Republican dark money group, has contributed over $64 million to the Republican Congressional Leadership Fund, which is the SLF's counterpart for electing Republicans to the House.
Two Democratic nonprofit groups — House Majority Forward and Majority Forward — respectively contributed $95 million to the House Majority PAC and $104 million to the Senate Majority PAC. Both focus on getting Democratic candidates elected to Congress.
Some historic donors have continued giving this election cycle. Billionaire couple Elizabeth and Richard Uihlein donated over $135 million this election cycle to support Republicans. George Soros, a longtime Democratic donor, has contributed at least $102 million. The Israeli American businesswomen and conservative political donor Miriam Adelson gave close to $67 million to various Republican PACs.
Other big donors on the list are billionaire businessman Jeff Yass, who has donated $109 million so far, mostly to Republican groups, as well as hedge fund manager Paul Singer, who donated over $52 million, also to Republican groups.
Billionaire ex-mayor of New York City Michael Bloomberg has spent $52.6 million so far, including around $30 million in contributions made after September 1. His team told the New York Times he will spend $80 million in September and October.

title: US  South Korean officials see little chance of Trump Kim meeting this year
description: Pyongyang shows little interest in diplomacy aimed at containing nuclear program as Trump downplays meeting prospects
content:
Pyongyang shows little interest in diplomacy aimed at containing nuclear program as Trump downplays meeting prospects
United States and South Korean officials see the chances fading of a meeting between President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un this year, according to five people with knowledge of the situation.
Trump, the only US president to have met a North Korean leader, has been eager to jump-start talks with North Korea, but Pyongyang has shown little interest in diplomacy aimed at containing its nuclear program .
The US has received no response from North Korea on holding a Trump-Kim meeting , and there is little time left before a regional summit in China next month where it might occur, said the five people — four of them briefed by senior officials from the US and South Korea, as well as a South Korean official.
North Korean state media has said Pyongyang would put tough conditions on agreeing to a bilateral summit, potentially including sanctions relief, even as Kim's powerful sister has said the two leaders have an "excellent" relationship.
Trump 'open' to talks, nothing scheduled, official says
In August, the Republican president said he planned to meet with Kim later this year and that the North Korean leader had responded to his outreach . South Korea's intelligence agency told lawmakers late last month that there was a 50% chance of Trump and Kim meeting on the sidelines of the November 18-19 summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation group in Shenzhen, China.
But on Monday, Trump, who met Kim three times in his first term, downplayed the prospects of such a meeting happening during the APEC meeting or a regional summit in the Philippines , also in November. "I get along with him very well, and I'm not sure that anybody's asking for a meeting," Trump told reporters at the White House.
Another South Korean official familiar with the matter said Pyongyang has made no move indicating it is preparing for a meeting with Trump. All of the people spoke on the condition of anonymity to relay private conversations.
Read: China, US agree on strategic stability, trade and AI cooperation
South Korea's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Last week, Seoul's ambassador to Washington, Kang Kyung-wha, said no concrete progress had been made toward a Trump-Kim summit.
North Korea's permanent mission to the UN did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
"President Trump in his first term held three historic summits with North Korean Leader Kim Jong Un that stabilised the Korean Peninsula," said a White House official on condition of anonymity. "US policy on North Korea has not changed. President Trump remains open to talking with Kim Jong Un, without any preconditions. No meetings to announce at this time. The leaders will meet at the appropriate time."
Last month, a senior US official told reporters that Trump was "ready" to speak with Kim and that "the ball is very much in North Korea's court.”
Ankit Panda, a senior fellow in the Nuclear Policy Program at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, said there is less than a 10% chance of a meeting between Trump and Kim at the APEC summit. "If Trump wants a meeting with Kim, I think the North Koreans are looking for a costly public signal," Panda said, arguing that a recent US decision to scale back exercises with South Korea had not been sufficient.
Washington has occasionally sought the assistance of China, which has maintained close ties with Kim, in brokering talks with North Korea. But cordial talks between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, set to continue at APEC, have not produced breakthroughs with Pyongyang.
Read More: Trump, Xi wrap up summit with tea and archives tour
The two Koreas remain technically at war under a truce that ended fighting in the 1950-53 Korean War. The US stations about 28,500 troops and military hardware in South ​Korea in combined defence against North Korea, which has pursued nuclear arms and ballistic-missile development. South Korean officials, citing private research group estimates, have said North Korea possesses between 80 and 120 nuclear warheads.
Trump's meetings with Kim in 2018 and 2019, while historic, yielded no concrete results.
"I don't know when they're going to meet," US Ambassador to South Korea Michelle Steel told an event in Seoul organised by the American Chamber of Commerce in Korea on Wednesday. If they could arrange a meeting, she said, it would likely be announced abruptly. "If it happens, then it's going to happen the next day or within a couple of days' notice."

title: Trump accuses Minnesota congresswoman of identity fraud  calls for her resignation
description: Trump accuses Minnesota congresswoman of identity fraud  calls for her resignation
content:
US president claims Ilhan Omar used false name to take office; congresswoman’s office has denied allegation
US President Donald Trump called a day earlier for Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar’s resignation from Congress, accusing her of using a false name when she was sworn into office, an allegation her office has denied.
“Because she used a fake name to be sworn in, I assume she must IMMEDIATELY resign from Congress,” he wrote on his Truth Social platform.
Trump claimed the Minnesota lawmaker’s real name was Ilhan Nur Said Elmi, which shares a surname with her former husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi.
He further claimed that Omar had “openly admitted to FRAUD” and called on House Speaker Mike Johnson to recognise that her congressional seat had been vacated.
Read: Trump administration reopened citizenship probe into Rep Ilhan Omar: report
Omar has made no such admission, and no court has established that she used a fraudulent identity.
Trump’s remarks followed an Oct. 21 Justice Department court filing related to a federal search of Omar’s Washington, DC home that identified her as “Ilhan Nur Said Elmi, a/k/a Ilhan Abdullahi Omar.”
Prosecutors did not explain why they used the alternative name, and the filing did not establish that Omar had committed fraud.
“This is completely false. Ilhan Omar is her real name,” a spokesperson for the congresswoman told Fox News.
Federal agents searched Omar’s home on October 12 as part of an investigation into possible false statements in immigration and citizenship records.
Omar, who became a US citizen in 2000, has denied wrongdoing and accused the Trump administration of using the investigation to intimidate her ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.

title: Antonelli eyes perfect weekend in title bid
description: The Mercedes rookie could become Formula One   s youngest ever champion if rivals George Russell and Lewis Hamilton falter
content:
The Mercedes rookie could become F1's youngest-ever champion if rivals George Russell and Lewis Hamilton falter
Kimi Antonelli admitted on Thursday that he needs to have a ‘perfect weekend’ at the United States Grand Prix to realise his dream of winning a maiden drivers’ world championship.
Mercedes’ 20-year-old Italian could become the youngest champion in F1 history and the first from Italy since Alberto Ascari in 1953 if he wins Sunday’s race and nearest rival and team-mate George Russell fails to finish in the top eight.
He would also need seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari to finish outside the top four.
"If you think about it, it’s crazy,” said a smiling and relaxed Antonelli, speaking to reporters at a news conference at the Circuit of the Americas.
“For me, it needs to be a perfect weekend and the others they need to do a poor result, which is unlikely.
"Of course, anything can happen and it’s crazy to think about it. We had a meeting this morning and we said ‘just have fun’ so we’re in the same mindset that I’ve had all year.
"So, we go one race at a time and I just try to do my best every weekend and then we’ll see.”
Seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, who vacated his seat at Mercedes for Antonelli when he moved to Ferrari, warmly praised him for his talent and his general demeanour.
Asked, as a multiple champion, if he had any advice to give the young Italian who is on the brink of glory, Hamilton smiled and said: “Slow down!”

Raul Fernandez and Jack Miller escape serious injury after separate crashes
World champion Marc Marquez topped the timesheets in an incident-packed first practice at the Australian MotoGP on Friday ahead of Raul Fernandez and Jack Miller who both took nasty tumbles.
The Spanish Ducati rider clocked a last-gasp blistering lap of 1min 27.985sec around the waterfront Phillip Island circuit -- which is hosting its final MotoGP -- in warm but windy conditions.
Championship leader Jorge Martin, who is two points clear of Marquez with five rounds of the season left, came seventh on his Aprilia.
Marco Bezzecchi, who won last week in Indonesia and is third in the standings, was fourth, also on an Aprilia.
Marquez's fastest time put him 0.048 ahead of last year's Australian grand prix winner Fernandez, who skidded off at Turn 7 and barrel-rolled across the gravel mid-way through the session.
Iker Lecuona, standing in for the injured Fermin Aldeguer at Ducati-Gresini, also suffered a fall at the same corner, bouncing off a tyre wall.
Home hero Miller was another to crash out at high-speed, this time at Turn 2, just seconds after setting the fastest time. He gave the thumbs up afterwards to signal he was okay.
Brad Binder, meanwhile, suffered a big engine failure on the main straight, pulling off with white smoke billowing from his KTM.
Phillip Island has been a staple on the calendar since 1997, but the Australian race is moving next year to a street circuit in Adelaide.
The second practice session, from which the top 10 riders go straight into Saturday's second round of qualifying, gets underway at 3:00 pm (0400 GMT).

title: Argentina designates foreign cartels  guerrilla groups as terrorist organisations
description: Milei administration targets Mexico   s Sinaloa Cartel  Colombia   s ELN  FARC dissidents  Ecuador   s Los Tiguerones
content:
Milei administration targets Mexico’s Sinaloa Cartel, Colombia’s ELN, FARC dissidents, Ecuador’s Los Tiguerones
The Argentine government designated five major Latin American transnational criminal and insurgent organisations as terrorist entities a day earlier, issuing an official resolution aimed at crippling their regional operations and financial networks.
The measure, announced by the Office of President Javier Milei, formally places Mexico’s Sinaloa Cartel and La Nueva Familia Michoacana, Colombia’s National Liberation Army (ELN) and FARC-EP dissidents, and Ecuador’s Los Tiguerones onto Argentina's Public Registry of Persons and Entities Linked to Acts of Terrorism and Their Financing (RePET).
According to the executive decree, the national security measure was formulated through joint coordination between Argentina's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Security, Ministry of Justice and the State Intelligence Secretariat (SIDE).
Read: Trump administration designates drug cartels as terrorist organisations
“The operational capacity, regional geographic expansion, and illicit diversification of these groups pose direct threats to the lives, property, and assets of our citizens,” the presidency said in an official statement, citing classified intelligence assessments.
The government outlined specific national security grounds for each designated entity.
The Sinaloa Cartel, from Mexico, was cited as a massive transnational syndicate driving global narcotics smuggling, human trafficking and extortion. The executive order aligns Argentina’s stance with international allies, including the United States, which previously designated the cartel.
Read more: US designates Colombia's largest drug-trafficking gang as terrorists
La Nueva Familia Michoacana, also from Mexico, was highlighted for its expansion into international drug trafficking and illegal mining, as well as its growing influence across South American illicit supply chains.
Los Tiguerones, from Ecuador, was identified as a high-violence cartel responsible for contract killings and maritime drug trafficking. The group splintered from Los Choneros in 2020 alongside Los Chone Killers, an entity Argentina added to the RePET registry in August.
The ELN and FARC-EP dissidents from Colombia were described as far-left guerrilla insurgencies rooted in armed struggle whose regional recruitment, logistics and weapons trafficking networks extend well beyond Colombia’s borders to threaten Argentine stability.
By adding the organisations to the RePET registry, Argentine law enforcement and intelligence agencies gain expanded administrative powers to freeze assets, disrupt cross-border financing and heighten surveillance on suspected operational cells.
The move also enables direct, real-time intelligence sharing between SIDE and international counter-terrorism partners to target the money laundering pipelines fueling regional drug trade.

title: Hamilton sets sights on racing in African grand prix
description: The Ferrari driver hopes to extend his career into his forties to fulfil his ambition of racing on the continent
content:
The Ferrari driver hopes to extend his career into his forties to fulfil his ambition of racing on the continent
Lewis Hamilton on Thursday welcomed Formula One’s decision to return to Africa, but revealed reservations over the choice of Rwanda to host the continent’s first Grand Prix in more than three decades.
The seven-time world champion also said he wanted to stay in F1 racing into his forties to make sure he can fulfil his dream of racing in an African Grand Prix.
Speaking to reporters ahead of this weekend’s United States Grand Prix, the Ferrari driver said he was aware of concerns regarding Rwanda and said they should not be overlooked.
"Of course, I don’t get to choose where we go and, naturally, there’s problems all over the world today,” he said. “I’ve seen many of the stories, but I think we really have to approach it with humility.”
Formula One announced a 10-year agreement to race in Rwanda last week with the race set to join the calendar after a circuit has been built in the early 2030s.
The last time an F1 race was held in Africa was the 33rd South African Grand Prix near Johannesburg in 1993 when Hamilton was just eight years old.
"There’s a lot that we don’t know,” added Hamilton who has called for a return to Africa for many years.
“Growing up in England, they never taught us anything about Africa. It needs to be on the curriculum…
"A lot of the problems they have there are still the results of colonialism and the west intervening, but if you see the people, you see so many designs that are out there today. Top brands come from Africa, and it’s got all the richest resources.
"I really hope, and I still have hopes, that Africa unites. I know there’s many people that don’t want that to happen -- because they would be so powerful if they did, but I’m still hopeful that at some stage they will.
"And, of course, going doesn’t mean that you neglect the things that are happening there.
"So hopefully many people start to educate themselves a little more about what is happening, what has happened for hundreds of years and I hope that does spark the conversation.”
Hamilton, who warmly praised runaway championship leader Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes as he sat alongside him at a news conference, revealed also that he hopes to continue racing into his mid-forties.
"I’m looking forward to racing with him longer. I mean, I’m now forced to have to stay a lot longer because we have a race in Africa -- and that’s been my dream, to be able to race in Africa.”
"So, you’ve got time,” said the 20-year-old Italian. “You’ve got to do at least the first one.”
"Yeah,” replied Hamilton. “I have to keep fighting to try and stay fit if I can. If I can still punch out good results over the next year, we’ll keep it going.”

title: South Africa thump Australia to level Test series
description: Jansen takes five wickets after Bavuma   s 179 helps the hosts seize control of the second Test
content:
Jansen takes five wickets after Bavuma’s 179 helps the hosts seize control of the second Test
South Africa captain Temba Bavuma said his team beat Australia by playing "good old Test cricket" as the hosts levelled the three-match series with a win by an innings and 31 runs at St George's Park on Thursday.
Bavuma was named man of the match for his career-best innings of 179. It provided the foundation for a victory which seemed improbable with the first two days ruined by rain and his team in deep trouble on the third morning after being sent in.
"I think it's just basically to try and stay in the moment," Bavuma said of the way South Africa kept their focus in a match which had major changes of fortune.
"When we were batting it was all about how we can extend it, how we can go another hour. Another hour becomes a session, how we can make sure we keep them on their feet because we know how that does have an effect.
"And then once the opportunity is there (when bowling) we've been calling on ourselves to be a lot more ruthless. We play good old Test cricket, try and wear the opposition down and then take them down when the opportunity presents itself."
Bavuma said he didn't want to get too excited about the win with the final Test starting in five days. "There's still a job at hand with another match still to go," he said.
South Africa were 110-6 on the third morning of the second Test before Bavuma had match-changing partnerships with Marco Jansen (85) and Simon Harmer (82) to enable South Africa to declare on 425-9.
Australia collapsed to 99 all out in their first innings, with tall left-armer Jansen taking 5-33, but provided stern resistance in the follow-on innings before being bowled out for 295.
Rain prevented any play before lunch on Thursday and more rain was threatening when Jansen claimed the final wicket after the final drinks break.
Australian captain Pat Cummins said the fight shown by Travis Head, who scored 121, and Scott Boland, who was sent in as a nightwatchman on the fourth evening and batted until after tea on Thursday was a "blueprint" for the third Test.
"Scotty and Trav played their roles well but it was a long way to come back from. Last week (in winning the first Test in Durban) everyone contributed but today, across the board, not enough of us contributed.
"You've got class bowlers in the opposition. You might need to weather the odd storm but when you do get through it there are some runs out there.
"It's almost a reverse of last week. One side gets ahead and suffocates the other side with a few early wickets."
Cummins said it was a series between the two top Test teams in the world. "The series at one-all, it's similar to where we would have thought it was going to be."

title: Cummins hints at Australia shake up
description: Marnus Labuschagne and Nic Maddinson face scrutiny after Australia   s batting failures in Gqeberha
content:
Marnus Labuschagne and Nic Maddinson face scrutiny after Australia’s batting failures in Gqeberha
Australia captain Pat Cummins admits it is hard to "paper over the cracks" after a thumping second Test defeat to South Africa, with the fate of at least three players hanging in the balance.
The visitors crashed by an innings and 31 runs at St George's Park in Gqeberha on Thursday to leave the three-Test series finely poised at 1-1 heading into the decider at Cape Town next week.
Australia collapsed to 99 all out in their first innings and were then dismissed for 295, with a superb 121 from Travis Head and defiant 40 off 166 balls by nightwatchman Scott Boland the only highlights.
The manner of the heavy loss did not go down well in Australia, with headlines ranging from "horror show" to "shambolic Aussies" and "brutal failures laid bare".
"Clearly need to be a lot better than that if we want to compete," Cummins said.
"I think a loss can sometimes kick you into gear. You can maybe paper over the cracks sometimes in a win. Whereas I think in a loss, it makes you ask questions as a player of yourself."
Heading into the third Test, there are question marks around at least three players, not least the underperforming Marnus Labuschagne who has gone three years without a Test century.
"He's actually doing the hard bit, he's getting to 30," Cummins said of number three Labuschagne.
"I think he's got to find a way to turn those into bigger scores -- 30s aren't going to win you many matches.
"So, again, we'll work on that in the next couple of days. It's one Test match left in the series, we've got to win this."
Recently-recalled opener Nic Maddinson is also on shaky ground after scores of 0, 48, 0 and 8 across the first two Tests, while all-rounder Beau Webster appears vulnerable.
Cameron Green is expected to be available for Cape Town after injury sidelined him from the first two Tests while Josh Inglis is also fit. Cooper Connolly is another option.
Paceman Boland, who came into the side at Gqeberha at the expense of spinner Nathan Lyon, will be hard to drop given his batting exploits and a five-wicket haul in the first innings.
Much will depend on the nature of the Cape Town pitch on whether Australia again opt for four seamers or Lyon is brought back.
Cummins admitted some hard decisions would have to be made.
"That's the challenge. Do you give someone one more game, or do you feel like now is the right time to make a move?" he said.
"Does it feel like someone's just about to turn the corner, and they're going to be away, or does it now feel like the right time for a change-up?"

title: CDF Munir vows to hit Indian sponsored terrorist outfits hard    wherever they are
description: He was briefed on security situation  ongoing counter terrorism operations  border management measures
content:
Affirms that with support of people, Pakistan will surely inflict total defeat to terrorists, their perverted ideology
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir vowed to continue the campaign against “Indian-sponsored terrorist outfits” and “hit them hard wherever they are”, the military's media wing said on Friday.
According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), CDF Munir visited Corps Headquarters in Peshawar. Upon arrival, he was received by the Peshawar Corps Commander.
The army chief was briefed on the prevailing security situation, ongoing counter-terrorism operations, border management measures, and the operational preparedness of formations deployed in the province.
“Field Marshal commended the high morale and professionalism of officers and troops, directing them to continue vigilance and highest standards of operational readiness to effectively counter threats,” the statement said.
ISPR said, “He underscored that we would continue the campaign against Indian-sponsored terrorist outfits to the fullest and hit them hard wherever they are."
“While paying tributes to the sacrifices of the people of Pakistan, including Shuhada and Ghazis of the security forces, CDF Munir affirmed that with the support of the people, Pakistan would surely inflict total defeat to the terrorists and their perverted ideology,” the statement concluded.
Read: PM Shehbaz defends emergency, governor’s rule in K-P, blames PTI for resurgence of terrorism
CDF Munir arrived in Peshawar a day earlier to attend a meeting of the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday. The meeting discussed the security situation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), with the government reiterating its commitment to restoring peace and accelerating development in the province
PM Shehbaz defended the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), saying the measures had been necessitated by the deteriorating security situation, and vowed to restore peace, prosperity and development in the province.
Defending the decision, he maintained that the Constitution and law empowered the government to take the measures implemented in K-P. He thanked the coalition partners for supporting the move, particularly President Zardari and Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) President Nawaz Sharif.
The meeting came amid a resurgence of terrorism in K-P. Security assessments presented to the federal cabinet showed that terrorist incidents in the province had increased by 195 per cent between March 2024 and September 2026, with police and security personnel bearing the brunt of attacks.
On Thursday, four police personnel , including a Counter-Terrorism Department deputy superintendent of police, were martyred in an exchange of fire with armed men in Karak. In a separate incident in Bannu, two civilians were injured in a remote-controlled bomb explosion.

title: Yemeni army says over 35 Houthi fighters killed or wounded in Taiz
description: Saudi Arabia postpones UN global data forum  statistical forum to 2027
content:
Army says its operations targeted Houthi positions; Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted 11 Houthi drones
Yemen’s army said Friday that more than 35 fighters of the Houthi group were killed or wounded in a military operation targeting the group’s positions in southwestern Taiz province.
In a statement, the army’s 35th Armored Brigade said its forces carried out a “swift and targeted operation” against Houthi positions and fortifications along the Aqrouz front in the Al-Misrakh district.
It said the operation targeted positions at Jabal Al-Manara, Kour, Wadi Kour, Al-Maqda, Al-Dabaya and Kahlan, leaving “more than 35 Houthi fighters killed or wounded.”
Read : Death toll from Houthi attack on Yemen training camp rises to 7
The statement did not specify the number of fatalities or injuries.
The operation also disabled a military vehicle equipped with weapons and destroyed Houthi fortifications at the targeted sites, it added.
The Houthis did not immediately comment on the Yemeni army’s account.
Taiz province has witnessed fierce fighting between the Yemeni army and the Houthis for weeks, killing and wounding hundreds on both sides.
Taiz holds strategic importance as a geographic bridge and a vital link between Yemen’s northern provinces.
Control of the province would mean control over supply routes and key transport corridors connecting the interim capital, Aden, with the country’s central and northern provinces.
These developments are part of a military escalation that began in July and is considered the most extensive since the relative calm that followed a truce launched in April 2022.
Since Oct. 5, Yemeni government forces have been conducting Operation Dawn of Yemen, which Presidential Leadership Council Chairman Rashad al-Alimi said aims to regain control of state institutions from the Houthis and recapture the capital Sanaa.
Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthi group said that its air defences intercepted and destroyed 11 drones and a ballistic missile.
The drones were intercepted over Riyadh, Medina, the Eastern Province and the southern region, while the ballistic missile was intercepted as it headed toward Najran in southwestern Saudi Arabia, coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said in statements posted on the X.
In its latest statement on Thursday, the coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed two drones launched toward the southern region.

Earlier, it reported the interception of four drones over Riyadh and Medina, one over Riyadh and four over the Eastern Province.
The statements did not provide details on where the drones were launched from or whether the interceptions caused damage or injuries.
The announcements came a day after Saudi authorities reported that four people had been killed in attacks in the country’s Eastern Province.
Two died from falling debris after air defences thwarted an attempted drone strike on an Aramco oil facility, while two others were killed in an attack targeting King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.
Also Read: Saudi-led coalition intercepts, destroys drone in Riyadh region
The coalition also reported intercepting seven drones Wednesday, including one heading toward the southern region and six over Medina and the Eastern Province.
Separately, Saudi Arabia's General Authority for Statistics has postponed the United Nations Global Data Forum and the Second Saudi Statistical Forum, previously scheduled for November 9 to 12, 2026, in Riyadh, to 2027, the authority said in a statement.
Oil spill from tanker hits Umm Al Quwain coast, beaches shut
An oil spill from a tanker was detected off the coast of Umm Al Quwain, prompting containment operations and environmental assessments, the United Arab Emirates Ministry of Climate Change and Environment said on Friday.
The ministry said all beaches and coastal areas in Umm Al Quwain had been temporarily closed until technical teams completed their assessments and determined the necessary safety and marine protection measures.
The ministry also urged fishermen and other sea users to avoid affected areas and follow official instructions.
The announcement followed reports of a strange odour by residents in some emirates on social media. The ministry said that odours reported by residents in Sharjah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain posed no health risks to them.
Yemen has been engulfed in conflict since the Houthis seized Sanaa and several other provinces in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognized government.
The Houthis control much of northern and western Yemen, while government forces and their allies hold Aden and large parts of the country’s southern and eastern provinces

title: Apple launches into foldable market as iPhone Duo sales begin
description: Apple s estimated delivery dates for the Duo have slipped to late January as demand outpaces supply
content:
Apple's estimated delivery dates for the Duo have slipped to late January as demand outpaces supply
Sales of Apple's first folding phone, the iPhone Duo, began on Friday, with market watchers betting on whether the device can reinvent the small foldables market in the same way the iPhone did for smartphones.
The Duo's reception could prove an early test for new CEO John Ternus, the former hardware chief who unveiled the phone barely a week after taking charge in September.
It could also have large implications for a niche category in which ⁠rivals such as Samsung Electronics and Huawei Technologies have sold premium ​offerings for several years.
Within minutes of pre-orders opening last Friday, Apple's estimated delivery dates for the Duo had slipped to late January as demand outpaced supply. The US company called the response from customers "nothing short of extraordinary."
In Sydney, the first Apple store to sell the phones on Friday, a queue of customers formed outside before opening at 8am local time (2100 GMT).
Simon Krishnan, a 48-year-old engineer, paid A$3,899 ($2,734) for a Duo with 512GB memory.
"This is a bit of a luxury item for me, because it's so expensive, but I just think, you know what? Life's too short," he said.
In China, a soft consumer market combined with memory costs pushing prices higher has led to six straight quarters of declines in smartphone shipments. Apple's market share, however, has rebounded as some phone buyers trade up to premium devices while others seek value at the lower end of the market, putting pressure on mid-range brands.
Read: Apple will have limited iPhone Duo units available in stores on Friday
Liu Wei, a 26-year-old healthcare professional, already has a foldable phone from Xiaomi 1810.HK, but still queued outside a central Shanghai Apple store from 6am to get his hands on Apple's first foldable.
"I've used Apple products for many years, and I have more trust (in the brand), so I bought one on launch day to try it out," he said.
In Hong Kong, May, 38, who declined to give his full name for privacy reasons, secured a 256GB iPhone Duo, which retails for HK$17,499 ($2,231.73), during an online pre‑sale and aimed to resell the handset for a profit of around HK$4,000: “A few meals' worth of money,” he joked.
Early reviews have praised the Duo's design as well as its sturdy and barely visible hinge, a major feat for phones whose prominent creased screen has long been a drawback and potential deterrent for buyers.
But reviewers have said camera compromises, including the absence of a telephoto lens and third-party apps that still need to be reworked for the new display size, could disappoint some buyers. They have also said the Duo in its smaller, folded state is less handy for the litany of quick tasks that most users carry out each day on standard iPhones, with several prominent reviewers recommending against the Duo for many Apple customers.
Read more: Apple Music in Pakistan: Subscription prices, features and how to sign up
"It's been a lot of fun trying the Duo out for a week, but it feels like I've gotten to use an extraordinarily polished prototype — not a finished product that I'd want to buy and carry," longtime Apple commentator John Gruber, author of the blog Daring Fireball, wrote in a review.
Tech commentator Marques Brownlee, popularly known as MKBHD, said in a YouTube review that "if you're just a regular person who doesn't do much more than texting, social media and browsing here and there, then it is probably a no. But if the $2,000 doesn't mean much to you, and you like the idea, after the learning curve and getting used to not having facial identification, it is a really fun phone."
The limited supplies could disappoint Apple fans lining up in front of stores to buy the Duo. Apple told Reuters that walk-in availability would vary by country, with limited stocks in the US, Australia, Canada, Mexico and much of Britain and Europe. In China, France, Hong Kong, India and Japan, units would be available only for customers who had ordered online.
"Foldables have been an established category for years, but adoption has remained relatively limited compared with conventional smartphones. Apple's entry could bring the format to a much broader audience," said Francisco Jeronimo, vice president at market researcher IDC.
IDC expects Apple will take 44% of the foldable value in 2026 on 31% of foldable units. By 2027, it will become the market leader in the category both in value and units shipped, IDC forecasts.
"Apple has made a convincing case for this form factor," Jeronimo said after spending a week with the passport-shaped Duo.
"Now comes the next test: turning excitement into availability, adoption and a lasting new chapter for the smartphone market," Jeronimo said.

title: Tom Skerritt dies at 93   Top Gun  actor   s cause of death and estimated net worth
description: Born in Detroit  Michigan  on August 25  1933  Skerritt served in the United States Air Force before pursuing acting
content:
Born in Detroit, Michigan, on August 25, 1933, Skerritt served in the United States Air Force before pursuing acting
Tom Skerritt, the Emmy Award-winning American actor known for Top Gun , Alien and Picket Fences , has died aged 93.
His family confirmed his death on October 22, 2026, stating that he passed away from natural causes on October 21.
No specific medical condition was identified as contributing to his death.
According to the family’s statement, Skerritt was remembered for his humour, curiosity, generosity and lifelong dedication to storytelling and helping others.
Born in Detroit, Michigan, on August 25, 1933, Skerritt served in the United States Air Force before pursuing acting.
His career spanned more than six decades, with appearances in over 150 film and television productions.
'Alien' and 'Picket Fences' star Tom Skerritt dies at 93
He made his film debut in War Hunt in 1962 and gained wider recognition through MASH (1970).
In 1979, he played Captain Arthur Dallas in Alien , before taking on the role of Commander Mike “Viper” Metcalf in Top Gun (1986), alongside Tom Cruise.
Skerritt also achieved considerable television success as Sheriff Jimmy Brock in the CBS drama Picket Fences , which ran from 1992 to 1996.
His performance earned him the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series in 1993.
According to Celebrity Net Worth, Skerritt’s estimated net worth was $12 million at the time of his death. This figure is an independent estimate, not a verified valuation of his estate.
He is survived by his wife, Julie Tokashiki, five children, five grandchildren and two great-grandchildren. His family has requested privacy following his death.

Brent crude futures are up $1.14, or 1%, at $114.31 a barrel
Oil ​prices rose on Friday, with Brent crude touching a more than five-month high, after Houthi ‌attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East.
Brent crude futures gained $1.14, or 1%, to $114.31 a barrel by 1006 GMT, having earlier reached $114.72 for the highest level since May 4. US West Texas ​Intermediate crude gained $1.65, or 1.7%, to $101.12.
The Brent benchmark is on track for a third consecutive weekly ​gain of about 4%, while WTI is poised to finish 0.3% down on the ⁠week.
Saudi Aramco on Thursday ordered the evacuation of its headquarters in Dhahran on the Gulf near Bahrain, Reuters ​reported, as fighting intensified between the world's largest crude exporter and Yemen-based Houthis.
"The market remains concerned about a ​potential escalation, which, in a worst-case scenario, could trigger renewed supply disruptions," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo, adding that volatile oil flows and elevated freight rates have left the market undersupplied.

Terrorists seized eight mill workers, nine project employees
The Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) in Dera Ismail Khan has registered a formal case against Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) terrorists for the abduction of passengers and workers of a sugar mills along with employees of other projects.

title: PHC halts deputy speaker s eviction  arrest
description: PHC halts deputy speaker s eviction  arrest
content:
Allows her to retain residence, bars arrest pending hearing
The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Thursday suspended a government notice ordering the inactive Deputy Speaker of the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Assembly to vacate her official residence, allowed her to continue living there and directed law-enforcement agencies not to arrest her.
A two-member bench comprising Justice Ijaz Anwar and Justice Faheem Wali issued the written order arising from the previous hearing. Advocate Yasir Khattak appeared on behalf of the petitioner, the inactive Deputy Speaker.
In its detailed order the court noted that the relevant presidential ordinance makes no mention of the offices of Speaker or Deputy Speaker. Similarly, the administrative directive requiring vacation of official residences contains no reference to these constitutional posts. The judges therefore found sufficient ground to stay the eviction process pending further examination of the legal position.
During arguments, counsel for the petitioner contended that the K-P Assembly Speaker and Deputy Speaker Act 2026 confers a clear legal right on the Deputy Speaker to occupy the official residence for the duration of her term. He further argued that law-enforcement agencies are barred from conducting any raid or taking coercive action against the residence while the office-holder remains in position.
Opposing the petition, the Advocate General submitted that an emergency situation empowers the provincial government to reclaim official residences allotted to ministers, advisers and the Deputy Speaker. He also apprised the court that a criminal case under Section 406 of the Pakistan Penal Code has already been registered against the Deputy Speaker on the complaint of the Deputy Commissioner of Chitral.
After hearing both sides, the bench suspended the notice to vacate the residence, expressly authorised the petitioner to remain in occupation and ordered that she should not be arrested. The matter will be taken up again on the next date of hearing.
The ruling provides immediate relief to the inactive Deputy Speaker and places the burden on the provincial authorities to justify the eviction drive in light of the statutory protections available to the holder of the office.

title: K P DCs granted MPO detention powers
description: K P DCs granted MPO detention powers
content:
Move enables three-month preventive detention despite previous PHC ruling
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi has delegated powers of preventive arrest and detention under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance to all Deputy Commissioners across the province, the Home Department announced in an official notification.
Acting on the Governor's directive, the provincial government has transferred authority under Section 3(1) of the West Pakistan Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960, to every Deputy Commissioner in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. The powers allow any person to be placed under preventive detention for up to three months.
Previously, these special powers rested exclusively with the Additional Chief Secretary (Home). The decision to decentralise them follows concerns over the prevailing law-and-order situation and is intended to enable faster, more effective preventive measures at the district level.
Governor Kundi said the step would reduce administrative delays and strengthen coordination between district administrations and law-enforcement agencies. "These powers have been delegated so that timely and effective preventive action can be taken on the ground," he stated.
He stressed that the authority must be exercised strictly in accordance with the Constitution and the law. "I expect every Deputy Commissioner to act responsibly and work in close cooperation with law-enforcement agencies," the Governor added. "Under no circumstances should these powers be misused."
Officials noted that the move places greater operational responsibility on district heads while retaining the requirement for accountability and legal compliance. The notification formalises the transfer of powers province-wide with immediate effect.
It may be recalled that the Peshawar High Court (PHC) in May 2023 declared the deputy commissioner's orders to arrest those accused of involvement in May 9 protests under Maintenance of Public Order (3 MPO) as null and void.
The law of 3 MPO in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) had been challenged in the high court.
A writ petition was filed by Advocate Naeem Ahmed Khattak through the mediation of Advocate Ali Azim Afridi against the powers granted to the district governments under 3 MPO. In the writ petition, the provincial government had been made a party through the chief secretary and the law secretary. It was submitted that the bill is not correct and is unconstitutional.
According to the writ petition, any citizen can be arrested without giving any reason under the law of 3 MPO. Along with this, the administrative officers have the power to issue, execute, punish, and try warrants, it noted.
Although the SC has on various occasions given decisions regarding the separation of the administration from the judiciary, judicial powers have been completely abolished in this regard, Afridi pointed out.
He noted that under MPO, there is no trial and everyone is arrested and thrown in jail without assigning any reason, he had added.
Subsequently, the PHC sought a response from the K-P caretaker government over the arrests of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) workers under MPO.
However, K-P Advocate General Amir Javid objected to the admissibility of the writ petitions, saying that they could not be heard at the time because the provincial cabinet had imposed an emergency in the province.

title: LHC acquits man sentenced to life in murder case
description: LHC acquits man sentenced to life in murder case
content:
Judge finds prosecution evidence insufficient to sustain conviction
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has acquitted a man sentenced to life imprisonment in a murder case, ruling that the prosecution had failed to prove his guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.
The court also dismissed the complainant's plea seeking enhancement of the sentence from life imprisonment to death.
Justice Farooq Haider allowed the criminal appeal filed by Muhammad Asif against his conviction, according to the written judgment.
Asif was accused of shooting and killing Tayyab Raza.
A murder case was registered against him at Shorkot Cantt police station in Jhang district on July 14, 2015.
On March 10, 2021, an additional sessions judge in Shorkot convicted Asif and sentenced him to life imprisonment, along with a fine of Rs100,000.
The complainant subsequently approached the high court, seeking enhancement of the sentence to death.
In its judgment, the LHC identified several weaknesses in the prosecution's case, including a delay in registering the first information report (FIR), which raised doubts about the prosecution's account.
The court also found that the eyewitnesses had failed to provide a satisfactory and legally acceptable explanation for their presence at the crime scene.
It noted that Asif had not been named in the initial FIR and was nominated later.
The judgment observed that medical evidence could establish the nature of the injuries but could not, by itself, identify the assailant.
The evidence relating to the identification of a motorcycle and police records was also found insufficient.
The court further noted that the pistol casings had been sent to the forensic agency after the accused's arrest.
It also held that evidence not put to the accused during the trial could not be used against him to sustain a conviction.
Concluding that the prosecution had failed to establish the charge beyond reasonable doubt, the LHC accepted Asif's appeal and acquitted him.
It also dismissed the complainant's plea for enhancement of the sentence.
In another case, the LHC has suggested an amendment to the Punjab Sentencing Act, 2019, to bring murder cases involving imprisonment for life within its scope, so that courts can exercise structured judicial discretion while determining sentences in light of aggravating and mitigating circumstances.
Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq, while converting the conviction of a man from Section 302(b) to 302(c) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) in a murder case arising from a sudden confrontation between rival groups of boys, observed that the existing law excludes offences carrying the death penalty from its ambit, even where alternative punishments include a fixed term or life imprisonment.
The court recommended that the act be amended to incorporate offences punishable with life imprisonment and empower judges to adjust the minimum period in appropriate cases.
It also suggested that the Sentencing Council envisaged under the law be tasked with framing comprehensive guidelines and a formal sentencing hearing be made mandatory.
Allowing an appeal in part, the court reduced the prison sentence of Mehar Farhan to the period already undergone by him, after finding that the fatal hockey-stick blow had been inflicted during a sudden confrontation without sufficient evidence of premeditation or an intention to kill.
The court, however, maintained the compensation of Rs500,000 payable to the deceased's heirs, along with the consequences of default and the benefit already granted under Section 382-B of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Chairing a meeting attended by the regional and district police officers through video link, the chief minister expressed concern over the law and order situation in Rawalpindi division and directed the police to intensify action against serious crimes, illegal possession of weapons and corruption within the force.
Detailed briefings were given on the law and order situation in every district. The inspector general of police briefed the chief minister on the overall security situation across the province, including a recent incident of the murder of a boy in Multan and other serious crimes.
Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz directed the police to ensure strict enforcement of a ban on camera-equipped glasses and other surveillance devices.
She also ordered preventive action and seizure of illegal weapons.
Expressing dissatisfaction with traffic management, she directed the police to ensure action against speeding. She also ordered an intensified anti-corruption campaign in the police and strict action against personnel involved in it.
The chief minister directed the police to prevent wheat smuggling from all districts, particularly along provincial borders.
She instructed all RPOs to hold weekly meetings to review all categories of crimes and submit performance reports of the relevant DPOs.
She ordered province-wide police patrolling to ensure a visible presence of law enforcement personnel and create a sense of fear of the law among criminals. She also directed police officers to visit the organisers of the Tableeghi Ijtima.
The chief minister praised the police for their performance regarding a proposed sit-in and paid tribute to personnel who had lost their lives while performing duty. She ordered the provision of lifetime salary and financial packages for the families of martyred police officers.
CM Maryam Nawaz directed the police to ensure effective patrolling by the Dolphin Force in Lahore and provide it motorcycles and other necessary facilities.
She said there would be no tolerance for the culture of hooliganism in Punjab and those involved would not be spared. She ordered an intensified crackdown on narcotics and comprehensive measures to identify crime hotspots and dismantle criminal networks.
The chief minister also directed the authorities to continue capacity-building of the riot management force to effectively deal with crowds and maintain law and order.
Officials said the overall crime rate in the province had continued to decline, with significant reductions reported in several districts.

Following a surge in wheat flour prices, broiler chicken meat has also become increasingly expensive in Hyderabad, with its price reaching Rs720 per kilogram after an increase of up to Rs180 over the past few days.
The continuous rise in wheat and flour prices has been followed by a sharp increase in broiler chicken meat prices, putting further pressure on household budgets and making the staple protein increasingly unaffordable for residents.
Consumers said broiler chicken meat was available at around Rs520 per kilogram just a week ago, but its price has now suddenly climbed to Rs720 per kilogram. Chicken breast meat is reportedly being sold for as much as Rs750 per kilogram.
The steep increase has forced many residents to cut back on their purchases. Consumers who previously bought larger quantities are now purchasing smaller amounts out of necessity.
Meanwhile, there appears to be no effective administrative mechanism in place to control broiler chicken meat prices in the city.
Shopkeepers, however, said poultry farm owners were supplying chickens to wholesalers at high rates based on weight, leaving retailers to add their operating costs before selling the meat to consumers.
Meanwhile, the price of farm eggs also varies across the city, with a dozen being sold for between Rs240 and Rs260, adding to the financial burden on households.

description: Witness says no effective measures were taken to save lives despite opportunities to do so
content:
Witness says no effective measures were taken to save lives despite opportunities to do so
A shopkeeper on Thursday alleged that Gul Plaza had no fire safety arrangements or alarm system, telling a judicial magistrate that the circumstances surrounding the deadly blaze raised suspicions of a conspiracy.
The witness, Shahid Paniwala, made the allegations while recording his statement before a judicial magistrate (South) hearing the Gul Plaza fire case. Defence counsel Javed Mir completed his cross-examination of the witness during the proceedings.
The witness alleged that negligence by the market administration had left shopkeepers and customers trapped for hours, adding that no effective measures were taken to save lives despite opportunities to do so.
He maintained that since the fire had originated inside the market, responsibility rested with its administration. The intensity and spread of the blaze, he said, had raised suspicions that it was deliberately set. The incident resulted in loss of lives and substantial financial damage, he added.
The witness told the court that he had sent a letter on January 22 to the deputy inspector general, SSP South and SHO Nabi Bakhsh, seeking registration of a case. When no action was taken, he approached the sessions court. Following court notices, a report was submitted on January 31 stating that the case had already been registered on the evening of January 23.
He also referred to a judicial commission report which, according to him, stated that only two to four of Gul Plaza's 16 entrances were open. The magistrate, however, directed him to focus on his own statement rather than referring to the report.
The witness claimed that the market had neither fire safety arrangements nor fire alarms and that the Gul Plaza traders' union was not registered. He also offered to provide videos to support his allegations, but the court observed that such material was not required for the recording of a statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
He requested that the traders should not be labelled a conspiratorial group unless their testimony was proved false.
During cross-examination, the defence questioned the witness about his mineral water supply business, operated under the name "It's Pure", and the financial losses he claimed to have suffered in the fire.
The witness said his business generated an income of Rs400,000 to Rs500,000 a month, but acknowledged that it was not registered with any department and that he had not submitted laboratory reports to the market administration. He said the administration had never asked him to provide such reports.

content:
Province reports 11 deaths from virus so far this year
Sindh has reported two more cases of monkeypox, or mpox, taking the total caseload recorded in the province this year to 95. The virus has claimed 11 lives so far.
The latest cases involve 21-year-old Salman Ali and 23-year-old Ishrat Fatima, both of whom tested positive for the virus, according to a report by Dow University's provincial public health laboratory.
Both patients are already receiving treatment at the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital, officials said.
The emergence of additional cases has underscored the importance of continued surveillance and preventive measures to contain the spread of the virus.
Of the 95 cases thus far, 71 were men, accounting for 75.27 per cent, while 24 were women. People aged 30 to 39 were the most affected age group, with 26 confirmed cases, while 23 children up to the age of nine also tested positive for mpox.
April recorded the highest number of cases at 31, followed by September with 20, August 17, July seven, October six so far, March five, June four and May two.
Experts said mpox is a viral disease that can spread through close physical or skin-to-skin contact with an infected person, as well as contact with lesions, bodily fluids or contaminated objects. Suspected patients should also limit close contact with others to reduce the risk of transmission, experts said.
Common symptoms include fever, headache, body aches, weakness, swollen lymph nodes and skin rashes or blisters.

title: Govt to form JIT in Mir Raza case
description: Govt to form JIT in Mir Raza case
content:
Home minister says govt to abide by commission's findings and recommendations
Sindh Home Minister Zia-ul-Hasan Lanjar said on Thursday that the government would constitute a Joint Investigation Team (JIT) to probe the Mir Raza case in line with the findings and recommendations of the judicial commission, adding that the team would be formed after approval from the chief minister and the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) would be formally approached in this regard.
Speaking to the media at the Sindh Assembly, the home minister said that the provincial government received a detailed, seven-volume report on the Mir Raza case. A subcommittee of the Sindh Cabinet has reviewed the matter and briefed the chief minister on its findings, he added.
The minister said the judicial commission was constituted on the chief minister's directives and entrusted with an important responsibility by the provincial government. He described Justice Umar Sial as an experienced and senior judge, adding that the government had prepared its recommendations in light of the commission's findings.
Lanjar said the cabinet's subcommittee has prepared a draft of its recommendations, which would be submitted to the chief minister for approval. Once the recommendations were approved, the JIT would be constituted and a letter sent to the FIA.
He added that he would recommend to the chief minister that the JIT complete its investigation and submit a charge sheet before the relevant court.
The home minister further said a separate committee, headed by Zulfiqar Larik, would be formed to inquire into the conduct of police officers in connection with the case.
Referring to the affected family's demand for a JIT, Lanjar said the family had approached the constitutional court seeking its formation, but the petition had been dismissed. He maintained that the provincial government would abide by the judicial commission's findings and recommendations.
He added that he had also conveyed to Justice Umar Sial the government's willingness to assist in the matter, saying the affected family was also agreeable to a JIT investigation.
Earlier, the single-member Judicial Commission probing the death of 25-year-old Mir Raza Ali had recommended a joint investigation team (JIT), led by DIG Irfan Baloch and comprising senior representatives of the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Intelligence Bureau (IB), Pakistan Rangers (Sindh) and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), to establish the truth.
In a scathing assessment, the commission had termed the police investigation an "epic failure", warning that the trust deficit between the Sindh police and society had become "nearly unrectifiable" in this case.
Headed by Sindh High Court Judge Justice Omar Sial, the commission had submitted its report to the provincial chief minister on October 15, 2026.
The commission concluded that the available medical and physical evidence was incompatible with suicide. "The bullet trajectory, the unusual location of the wound for a self-inflicted injury, the absence of blood, the state of the body, the principles of medical jurisprudence, acid burns and the anesthesia detected in the blood, all clearly excluded suicide as the cause of death. It was a murder," the report stated.
The commission found that the police had failed in their most basic responsibility: establishing the truth. It said the suicide hypothesis rested on a handful of unconfirmed text messages, selectively obtained video footage and a preliminary post-mortem report that did not itself conclude that the death was a suicide.
The report also pointed to contradictions between the first and second reports prepared by Dr Osama Shaikh, further weakening the police position.

title: Illegal parking returns to district courts
description: Illegal parking returns to district courts
content:
Ambulances remain stuck in traffic as parking congestion paralyses movement
Despite the construction of an extensive underpass and an overhead bridge around the District Courts, illegal parking has once again taken over the area.
Claims that the underpass and overhead bridge would bring traffic and parking under complete control have failed to materialise.
Parking for thousands of motorcycles and dozens of cars, stretching from the main gate of the District Courts to the old petrol pump, has once again brought traffic movement to a standstill.
Passing through the area has become difficult, particularly during office hours and at closing time. Heavy traffic congestion has become routine during two peak periods, from 8am to 10am and from 1:30pm to 2:30pm.
Long queues of vehicles belonging to the Green Transport bus service and other routes, along with dozens of wagons, Suzuki vans and Bykea motorcycles, have also become a common sight.
At the time of the underpass's construction, it was announced that parking would be completely prohibited in the area and that a large commercial parking plaza would be built in the Jinnah Park area at a cost of Rs1 billion.
However, even after six months, work on the project has not begun. Consequently, the parking of cars and motorcycles has returned to its old location near the main entrance of the District Courts.
The administration has now also awarded an expensive parking contract for roadside parking. The contractor has started charging Rs100 for a motorcycle and Rs200 for a car. Disputes between the contractor and lawyers and litigants over the charges have become a separate problem.
Meanwhile, illegal parking in front of the main entrance of the District Courts has completely paralysed traffic, with ambulances also frequently getting stuck.
Litigants Qaiser Ali, Feroz and Nazakat said there was no parking facility anywhere in the court premises. They said around 25,000 litigants, employees, lawyers and clerks visited the courts daily and questioned where they were supposed to park their motorcycles and cars.
They demanded that the commercial parking plaza, included in the District Courts underpass project, be completed immediately.
Otherwise, they warned, congestion caused by thousands of vehicles and motorcycles would persist on all four sides of the court premises, traffic would remain jammed and the underpass project would also fail to achieve its objectives.
President of the District Bar Association, Malik Tariq Mahmood Sajid Awan, said the issue of parking encroachments had been raised forcefully with the competent authority. He said the association strongly demanded construction of the commercial plaza at Jinnah Park.

title: Chakwal awaits major hospital
description: Chakwal awaits major hospital
content:
Residents of district with population of over 2m face limited beds, shortage of medics
The establishment of a major hospital equipped with modern medical facilities remains a pressing public demand in Chakwal district, which has a population of approximately two million.
A shortage of basic healthcare facilities, limited hospital beds, a lack of specialist doctors and the need to travel to Rawalpindi and other cities for the treatment of complicated illnesses have created serious difficulties for urban and rural residents alike.
The question remains: when will the people of Chakwal have access to quality healthcare in their own district?
Chakwal has a distinctive identity because of its history, tourism, culture and traditions, but healthcare challenges continue to await government attention.
Complaints about inadequate medical facilities in relation to the district's large population have been growing.
Residents say increasing pressure on government hospitals limits the availability of treatment, while the lack of modern medical equipment, specialist doctors and other essential facilities further compounds their difficulties.
Three interchanges of the Islamabad-Lahore Motorway fall within Chakwal district. Consequently, people injured in traffic accidents between the Salt Range and Neela Interchange are taken to the District Headquarters Hospital in Chakwal.
The hospital, with only 200 beds, is considered inadequate for the growing population and such emergencies.
Public demands are growing for a modern, fully equipped hospital with at least 600 beds. Residents say existing healthcare facilities are insufficient to meet the needs of a district with a population of around two million.
They believe a major hospital would not only enable patients to receive treatment locally but also help reduce the burden on hospitals in other cities.
Residents say patients suffering from heart, kidney and liver diseases, cancer and other complicated illnesses often have to be shifted to Rawalpindi or Islamabad for better treatment.
This exposes them to travel difficulties, additional expenses and delays in treatment.
The situation is particularly distressing for poor families travelling from remote villages.
People living in Chakwal city and surrounding rural areas already face financial difficulties because of their limited resources. When a patient has to be transferred to a hospital in a larger city, ambulance charges, travel costs, medicines and other expenses place an additional burden on the family.
Public representatives and residents say a modern district hospital should have emergency services, intensive care units, operation theatres, advanced diagnostic equipment, laboratories, maternal and child healthcare facilities, and specialist doctors in various fields.
Such facilities would reduce the need for patients to travel to other cities for treatment.

title: Dry fruits prices spike with rise in demand
description: Dry fruits prices spike with rise in demand
content:
With the onset of winter, prices of dry fruits, including almonds, cashews, walnuts, pistachios and pine nuts, have surged, while peanuts, soup and yakhni have also become significantly more expensive, putting these seasonal treats beyond the reach of many low-income households.
Fresh peanuts alone have caused concern among consumers this year.
Last year, they cost Rs800 per kilogram, but their price has now crossed Rs1,000 per kilogram. Roasted black chickpeas have reached Rs800 per kilogram.
Although hundreds of soup and yakhni stalls have opened across the city, their rising prices have made even these popular winter refreshments difficult for ordinary residents to afford in neighbourhoods and local markets.
A cup of Kashmiri pink tea now costs up to Rs200.
Egg soup is being sold for Rs200 per cup, while a glass of plain yakhni costs Rs150 and a special serving Rs200.
In the open market, peeled almonds are selling for Rs2,800 to Rs3,400 per kilogram, cashews for Rs3,200 to Rs4,000, pistachios for Rs3,800 to Rs4,500, walnuts for Rs1,000 to Rs1,800, and pine nuts for Rs7,500 to Rs8,000.
Raisins cost Rs1,200 to Rs1,800 per kilogram, while jaggery is selling for Rs800 to Rs1,400 per kilogram. Dried apricots have also doubled in price compared with last year.
In Narnkari Bazaar, raw peanuts are being roasted on the spot and sold to customers. Wholesale trading in peanuts and roasted chickpeas has also picked up in Narnkari Bazaar and Ganjmandi's Nimco Market.
Small soup stalls and carts have appeared in markets and neighbourhoods across the city. They generally open after sunset and continue operating until 1am.
Families have also started visiting soup and yakhni shops in central markets in large numbers.

title: Organ trade network busted
description: Organ trade network busted
content:
Five suspects held, Rs87.5m properties frozen, three vehicles seized
The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has busted an organised gang involved in illegal kidney transplants in the federal capital, arresting five suspects, recovering Rs1 million in cash, freezing properties worth Rs87.5 million and seizing three vehicles. The agency is also considering launching a separate money-laundering investigation.
According to officials, FIA Islamabad Zone Director Shehzad Nadeem Bukhari formed a team under the supervision of Deputy Director Anti-Corruption Mir Faizan following a tip-off. The team, accompanied by officials from the Human Organ Transplantation Authority (HOTA), raided an illegal transplant facility in PWD Society, Islamabad.
The raid revealed that a kidney from donor Ramzan Arshad had allegedly been transplanted illegally into recipient Muhammad Qasim. Three suspects were arrested at the scene, while two others were apprehended later. A court subsequently granted the FIA seven days' physical remand of the suspects.
Investigators found that the recipient had allegedly paid Rs3m for the transplant. Agents had arranged the donor and promised him Rs400,000, of which Rs340,000 was to be paid to the donor and Rs60,000 divided among three agents as commission.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspects had allegedly performed kidney transplants in residential properties without the required medical qualifications or credentials. Essential tissue-typing, cross-matching, PRA, and HLA tests were reportedly arranged illegally through agents at a hospital. As these tests were restricted to close relatives approved by HOTA, the suspects allegedly submitted donor samples under relatives' names using forged referral letters to create the impression of a legally permitted related-donor transplant.
Recipients' dialysis was allegedly arranged through a technician at a hospital in Islamabad. If a patient's condition deteriorated after transplantation, the patient was transferred to another hospital. The network reportedly comprised agents, a doctor, a nurse, an anaesthesia provider, medicine suppliers, laboratory testing personnel and dialysis providers. It allegedly operated in PWD Society, Phase IV of a private housing society and private premises in Peshawar.
Further investigations revealed that the suspects had allegedly purchased valuable properties in Islamabad using proceeds from illegal kidney transplants. One suspect bought a 10-marla house in Media Town for Rs62.5m, while another purchased a five-marla house in Jinnah Garden Phase I for Rs25m
The FIA has frozen both properties after issuing notices under Section 5 of the FIA Act, 1974. Letters have also been sent to banks to obtain the suspects' financial records, while separate money-laundering proceedings against the two individuals are under consideration.
The agency recovered Rs1m in cash during searches and seized three vehicles: one Changan Oshan X7 and two Honda Civic cars. Their transfer and registration have also been frozen through the relevant excise office.
Following the raid, teams from HOTA, the Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority (IHRA) and the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP) inspected the illegal facility and are to submit separate reports.
A case has been registered against the suspects under Sections 9, 10 and 11(a)(ii) of the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 2010, read with Sections 34, 419 and 109 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC). Officials said raids are continuing at various locations to arrest other nominated suspects.

title: Israeli strikes  gunfire kill four in Gaza
description: Israeli strikes  gunfire kill four in Gaza
content:
Medics report deaths in Gaza City, Khan Younis and Jabalia
Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least four Palestinians in separate incidents across the Gaza Strip on Thursday, according to health officials, as attacks continued despite a year-old ceasefire.
In Gaza City, an Israeli strike on a car killed at least one person, medics said, revising an earlier toll of two. Emergency crews were seen spraying water on the burning wreckage as crowds gathered at the scene.
Other strikes killed a Palestinian man riding a motorcycle in the southern city of Khan Younis and another man near the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza. Gunfire killed a woman near the Jabalia refugee camp in the north, medics said.
Israel has intensified strikes against Hamas in recent weeks, accusing Hamas of rearming and launching attacks in violation of the ceasefire. Hamas denies attempting to carry out attacks or rebuild its arsenal and accuses Israel of undermining the agreement.
Israel's military said it had struck Hamas fighters in Khan Younis, Nuseirat and Gaza City but was unaware of the reported incident in Jabalia. The US-brokered ceasefire envisages the eventual reconstruction of Gaza, but progress has stalled amid disagreements over Israeli troop withdrawal.
Gaza health officials say at least 1,500 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began, while Israel says four of its soldiers have died. Palestinian authorities put the overall death toll from Israel's offensive, launched after the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attack at more than 74,000.

title: Russia  Ukraine trade fresh attacks
description: Russia  Ukraine trade fresh attacks
content:
Overnight Russian strikes kill two, Moscow downs hundreds of drones
Russia and Ukraine launched major overnight attacks despite renewed diplomatic efforts to end their war, with strikes killing two people and injuring 30 others in Kyiv and elsewhere and Moscow reporting that its air defences had intercepted most of hundreds of drones targeting the region.
The attacks came hours after US envoy Steve Witkoff held three-hour talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Saint Petersburg on Wednesday. US President Donald Trump described the discussions as the closest the two sides had come to ending the war.
Moscow indicated it was "in principle" ready to resume trilateral negotiations with Ukraine and the United States, potentially in mid-November, after the US midterm elections. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the talks should focus on post-war security.
Air raid sirens sounded throughout the night and into the day in Kyiv, where two people were killed and more than 30 other people wounded, city authorities said. Two women aged 50 and 60 were killed and dozens more people were wounded in an attack on a crowded market in the eastern city of Lozova.
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Russian strikes injured 15 people in the Ukrainian capital, eight of whom required hospitalisation. The attacks also damaged metro infrastructure at the Pivdenny Bridge, restricting traffic between parts of the city.
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said two people were wounded as Russian air defences intercepted barrages involving 630 drones headed towards the region, including 163 approaching the capital. Reports indicated that two people were wounded in the Moscow region.
The latest exchanges followed deadly attacks on Wednesday, when Russian strikes killed at least four people in Ukraine.
