title: France clamps down on protests after violence
description: France clamps down on protests after violence
content:
Macron orders tighter security as cities ban rallies over rising living costs
French authorities on Thursday imposed bans and restrictions on fresh demonstrations following last weekend's protests against the rising cost of living that descended into the country's worst street violence in years, prompting the government to promise tougher security measures.
President Emmanuel Macron, after chairing a meeting with ministers and intelligence officials, said curfews and other measures would be introduced, including restrictions on protests organised by "groups without legitimacy". He said the priority was a return to calm.
Macron blamed "organised ultra-left groups aiming to bring down the republic" for the worst violence, accusing them of sedition. He announced a defence council meeting for Friday (today) to decide the next steps ahead of nationwide demonstrations planned for Saturday.
The clashes, looting and vandalism erupted on October 17, alongside demonstrations attended by more than half a million people protesting the surging cost of living. The government has acknowledged that police lost control of the situation.
In Paris, a student protest went ahead on Thursday after an emergency court injunction overturned a police ban. Student leader Coppelia Moreau accused the authorities of trying to distinguish between "good" and "bad" protesters, arguing that the government's approach threatened the right to demonstrate.
Authorities banned Saturday's protests in Marseille and Lyon, where last weekend's unrest caused extensive damage. Lyon saw between 200 and 300 shops looted and a tourist office torched. Restrictions were also imposed in city centres in Grenoble, Rouen, Le Havre and Toulon.
The interior ministry said police deployment on Saturday would be 20% higher than last weekend. In Paris, a planned march was permitted from Bastille in the east but barred from entering the city centre, prompting objections from organisers associated with the Yellow Vest movement and trade unions.
French courts have swiftly handed out verdicts, including orders to serve jail time, in fast-track justice for rioters. Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said 217 of the 2,700 people arrested during and since last weekend had been convicted and jailed, while another 1,000 were facing prosecution.
Candidates seeking to succeed Macron in presidential elections have questioned the authorities' ability to restore order. However, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu met representatives of major political parties on Thursday and is scheduled to meet student groups, unions and employers on Monday.

US President Donald Trump must sit for a deposition by December 11 in his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC to answer questions under oath from the British broadcaster's lawyers, a federal judge ruled on Thursday, according to the Associated Press.
Trump filed the lawsuit in December in a Florida federal court, accusing the BBC of misleadingly editing a speech he delivered on January 6, 2021, to make it appear that he had directed supporters to storm the US Capitol. A leaked internal BBC memo highlighting the edits as evidence of potential political bias triggered a public relations crisis and led to high-level resignations at the broadcaster.
The BBC has accused Trump and his lawyers of delaying the exchange of records and other evidence required during the pre-trial discovery process. It is also seeking financial records from Trump's Mar-a-Lago club and associated business entities, arguing that the documents are needed to challenge his claims.
US Magistrate Judge Enjolique Lett passed the order during a hearing on Thursday. Trump had cancelled a deposition scheduled for October, citing conflicts with his presidential duties. His lawyers however, denied that he was attempting to avoid questioning.

title: ICC wins EU s 2026 Sakharov prize
description: ICC wins EU s 2026 Sakharov prize
content:
Award comes amid US sanctions and growing pressure on tribunal over its investigations
The International Criminal Court (ICC) and its officials won the European Union's 2026 Sakharov Prize for human rights on Thursday, as the tribunal faces mounting pressure, including US sanctions aimed at disrupting its work.
European Parliament President Roberta Metsola announced the award in Strasbourg, drawing a standing ovation from lawmakers. She said the prize recognised the court's role in upholding international law and justice. "The EU is built on respect for multilateralism and international institutions," Metsola said.
The recognition, marks another show of international support for the Hague-based tribunal this month, following the Nobel Peace Prize awarded to former ICC judge Navi Pillay less than two weeks ago. The US imposed sanctions on the court earlier this month, intensifying tensions over its investigations.
US President Donald Trump has long criticised the ICC, with his campaign against the tribunal escalating after it issued arrest warrants in 2024 for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his former defence minister over alleged crimes in Gaza.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has threatened that Washington would continue working to dismantle the court "brick by brick" unless it addressed US concerns, particularly over the warrant for Netanyahu.
ICC President Tomoko Akane said the Sakharov Prize carried particular significance given the "unprecedented challenges" facing the court and its officials, including sanctions intended to interfere with its judicial mandate.
In a statement, Akane said the award reaffirmed the importance of independent judicial institutions and those working to uphold international law. She stressed that continued international cooperation and support were essential for the court to carry out its mandate independently and impartially and deliver justice for victims of the gravest crimes.
"In a world marked by rising conflicts, there is no peace without justice and no security without law," Akane said.

The federal government has directed civil servants to declare their own and their dependants' foreign citizenship and travel documents, as well as details of marriages to foreign nationals, under the Foreign Citizenship Declaration Rules, 2026.
Officials have been given 90 days from the notification of the rules in the official gazette to submit the required declarations, with failure to comply or providing incorrect information to be treated as misconduct.
According to an office memorandum issued by the Establishment Division, all ministries and divisions have been instructed to compile and submit records of the relevant officers, including their names, designations, basic pay scales and other required particulars.
The information sought also includes details of the foreign citizenship and travel-document status of civil servants and their dependants.
The memorandum stipulates that declarations must be submitted within the prescribed 90-day period following notification of the rules in the official gazette.
Failure to furnish the required details within the deadline, or the submission of false or incorrect information, will be treated as misconduct.
The Establishment Division said the directives would not apply to officers belonging to the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), the Police Service of Pakistan (PSP), the Secretariat Group (SG) and the Office Management Group (OMG), which have been exempted from the requirements.

title: Two die in Houthi attack on Saudi airport
description: Two die in Houthi attack on Saudi airport
content:
Two die in Houthi attack on Saudi airport
A late-night attack on Saudi Arabia's Dammam airport killed two people and injured eight others, the civil aviation authority said on Thursday, as strikes by Yemen's Houthis intensify.
A Saudi and an Indian man were killed in the attack on Wednesday, the general authority of civil aviation said in a statement, updating an earlier death toll. Damage to the airport was being assessed, it added.
In recent weeks, Houthi attacks on Saudi oil and civilian infrastructure have reached an unprecedented scale, forcing Riyadh to shut its main airport and postpone a major investment conference.
A total of 22 people have been killed in attacks on Saudi airports this month, according to an AFP tally of official figures.
A Houthi maritime blockade in the Red Sea is also threatening oil shipments from Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest exporter of crude.
The Houthi attacks follow the collapse in July of a years-long truce in Yemen's civil war, where the Iran-backed group is fighting the government supported by a Saudi-led coalition.
The Houthis declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before launching a major offensive in September in which they seized government-held territory along the Red Sea coast.
In response, the Saudi air force has frequently targeted areas under Houthi control, which includes much of impoverished Yemen.

title: Gulf on cusp of new war as Trump hints at  imminent  Iran action
description: Gulf on cusp of new war as Trump hints at  imminent  Iran action
content:
US President Donald Trump said Washington was not negotiating with Iran, adding that "something one way or the other" would happen "fairly soon."
"Most people seem to think it's after the election, and we're going to see what happens," Trump told reporters on Wednesday as he returned from a rally in South Carolina.
Earlier, during his remarks at the rally, Trump said the United States could end its war with Iran immediately but wanted to ensure the outcome would be lasting.
He also claimed that Washington had defeated Iran militarily and financially, insisting that Tehran would "never have a nuclear weapon."
The New York Times reported earlier this week that the US and Israeli militaries had drawn up plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the US midterm elections, citing US officials and others briefed on the discussions.
However, it remained unclear whether Trump would approve the strikes. The newspaper noted that he had repeatedly rejected plans to resume major combat operations this year.
Meanwhile, Iran will strike oil facilities, undersea cables, datacentres and AI facilities across as many as seven countries in the Gulf in the event of a fresh US-Israeli attack, Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran's supreme national security council, has said.
Mehdi Mohammadi, an adviser to Mohammad Ghalibaf, the hardliner who led Iran's negotiations with the US to end the conflict between the two countries, said Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu had agreed in principle on an attack, but could not guarantee a successful outcome. He added: "We see the next conflict as an existential threat. The third war in two years means a threat to existence. Our strategy is 'zero red lines'."
Mohammadi said: "We break the temporal and spatial dimensions of the conflict. The war will continue longer and in a wider geographical area than the enemy anticipates."
Iranian media reported that Rezaei had declared: "In the event of a war, cables, datacentres and artificial intelligence facilities could also be targeted. If the conflict breaks out again, we will have a broader plan.
"There can be no arrangement in which Iran's economic lifelines come under attack while the economic architecture enabling those attacks is considered untouched and immune."
According to recent reports in US media, US military advisers have drawn up a detailed list of targets for a fresh joint US-Israel assault on Iran to be implemented after the US midterm elections on 3 November.

title: Opposition wants PM to initiate dialogue
description: Opposition wants PM to initiate dialogue
content:
Gohar, Achakzai demand talks and protection for lawmakers
The opposition on Thursday said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif should personally invite the opposition to talks if the government was serious about negotiations, adding that it could not trust those who mocked the dialogue process.
Opposition leaders, including Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, criticised the government over stalled political negotiations and restrictions on parliamentarians, calling for meaningful dialogue and the protection of elected representatives' rights.
Speaking at a news conference outside the Parliament House alongside opposition leaders, Gohar said the opposition had repeatedly engaged in negotiations with the government in good faith and without preconditions, but the process had failed to produce the desired results.
"Our government went away while we kept negotiating with the government," he said, referring to the opposition's attempts to pursue political dialogue.
Gohar also questioned the criteria used to assess political leaders' loyalty to the state, saying that despite nearly three years of the current parliament, he still did not understand the formula used to determine such allegiance. "We have always said that Pakistan comes first and the state comes first," he said.
"We are treated as though we are not loyal to the state. This perception must end," he added, calling for an end to questions about opposition politicians' commitment to Pakistan.
He also called for parliamentarians to be protected so they could represent their constituents freely and without fear. Recalling an incident in September 2024, when opposition lawmakers were allegedly picked up, Gohar said the opposition leader had moved a resolution in the National Assembly in response.
He added that a special committee had also been constituted to address the issue of parliamentarians' protection.
Speaking at the same news conference, Opposition Leader in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai stressed that parliamentary speeches should be recorded in their entirety, arguing that the official record was essential to preserving the country's political history and allowing the public to assess the statements of elected representatives.
"The complete speech of a member speaking in the National Assembly being recorded is a constitutional requirement," he said.
Achakzai said parliamentarians had to struggle even for rights that should ordinarily be guaranteed under parliamentary rules. He maintained that the speaker's authority should be exercised in accordance with the rules and regulations governing the assembly.
Referring to his speech in the National Assembly a day earlier, he said he had made no inappropriate remarks. He alleged that his four-and-a-half-minute speech had been presented as a nine-minute address.
He also rejected suggestions that his remarks had been directed against the country, saying not a single word in his speech had been against Pakistan.
The opposition leader said the time allotted to opposition lawmakers to speak in parliament had been curtailed, describing the restriction as another obstacle to democratic debate.
Achakzai questioned what he described as the inconsistent issuance of production orders for lawmakers, saying such orders had been issued for some members but not others. He argued that parliamentary proceedings and the rights of elected representatives should be protected without discrimination.
He also criticised the government's approach to political negotiations, questioning how the opposition could trust a process that, in his view, had been ridiculed by those in power.
He said political dialogue required a meeting with PTI founder Imran Khan. He also recalled that Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman had met the prime minister in connection with the issue.
The opposition had asked the government to ensure that the prime minister personally extended an invitation for negotiations, he said. "Negotiations cannot take place in an atmosphere where the process itself is being mocked," he said.
Achakzai called for a committee to investigate allegations of corruption against the incumbent government, proposing that Defence Minister Khawaja Asif head it.
He maintained that the opposition would resist what it considered an undemocratic system through democratic means. "It is the duty of every citizen who wants to save Pakistan to stand up for democracy," he said, adding that the country needed a strong parliament and state institutions operating within their respective constitutional jurisdictions.
"We will not hand Pakistan over to an undemocratic system," he said, warning that such an order could threaten the country's unity.
Also speaking at the press conference, Majlis Wahdat-e-Muslimeen chief Allama Raja Nasir Abbas stressed that the rule of law, justice and respect for the Constitution were essential for Pakistan's progress, saying the country's political and economic crises could not be resolved without the supremacy of law.
He said the rule of law and access to justice were fundamental to national development. Pakistan could not overcome its ongoing political crisis unless the Constitution was upheld and the rule of law firmly established, he added.
Addressing the country's economic challenges, Abbas said the economic crisis, too, could not be resolved without ensuring the supremacy of law. He added that justice was necessary to restore public confidence in state institutions and the wider system.
He expressed concern that the trust deficit between the rulers and the people had reached its highest level in the country's history. He also criticised the continued registration of fabricated cases and first information reports (FIRs), saying such practices further undermined public trust.
Referring to the February 8, 2024, general elections, Abbas alleged that the people's mandate had been stolen. He said depriving citizens of their right to vote and undermining their electoral choices constituted serious injustices.
He further said tampering with votes amounted to an attack on the Constitution and the rule of law, stressing that protecting the sanctity of the vote was essential to upholding democratic principles and restoring public confidence in the political system.
Abbas reiterated that Pakistan's sustainable progress, political stability and economic recovery depended on constitutional supremacy, the rule of law and justice for all citizens.
Meanwhile, Gohar addressed reports concerning internal party affairs, PTI lawmakers in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) and the provincial organisation, urging party members to verify information before reacting to reports.
He said the news that had prompted a social media post by the party's secretary general was incorrect and that he had spoken to the relevant leaders and lawmakers.
Describing PTI's lawmakers from K-P as a valuable asset, Gohar praised their role in supporting Imran over the past two years. He said they had remained steadfast despite difficult circumstances and continued to play a leading role in rallies, public meetings and protest marches.
"All these members are standing even more firmly with Imran Khan, his ideology and his struggle," he said, adding that they enjoyed the PTI founder's full confidence.
Gohar said no party lawmaker would consider disregarding Imran's instructions and assured the provincial leadership that it would be consulted on important party decisions.
On the provincial party presidency, he clarified that Junaid Akbar had been appointed by Imran himself and that he had issued the notification in accordance with the PTI founder's instructions. Junaid would continue to serve as provincial president, he said.
In Junaid's absence, senior vice-president Noorul Haq Qadri would chair meetings of the provincial organisation under the party constitution, while provincial secretary general Ali Asghar Khan would oversee other organisational matters.
Gohar said discussions had taken place with the relevant office-bearers and that the provincial organisation had expressed the same preference during its meeting. A formal notification was expected to be issued on the matter.
He added that no changes would be made to the provincial organisation or its existing cabinet until Junaid returned.
Emphasising party unity, the PTI chairman said the party's focus should remain on Imran's position, political narrative and struggle rather than internal disagreements or unnecessary public statements.
He reiterated that the party remained united under Imran's leadership and that his decisions and instructions were final.
Gohar also reaffirmed PTI's position on the K-P chief minister, saying Sohail Afridi remained the party's choice and that there was no question of considering anyone else for the position, as the decision rested with Imran.
Salman Akram Raja rejects claims Sohail Afridi derailed talks with govt
Separately, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja has rejected claims that non-functional K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi was responsible for the breakdown of negotiations with the federal government, saying the talks collapsed over the denial of access to PTI founder Imran Khan's personal physicians and concerns over provincial autonomy.
In an interview with a private television channel on Thursday, he said the refusal to allow Khan's personal doctors to examine him was one of the two principal reasons behind the failure of the negotiations.
He said PTI could not grant the federal government unrestricted authority to intervene in the affairs of K-P. "These were the two principal reasons why the talks collapsed," Raja said, alleging that the government had deliberately undermined the negotiations.
The PTI leader also described the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in the province as unconstitutional, alleging that the government had introduced the measures to take control of the provincial administration. "They just wanted to take over the province," he said.
Raja said an all-parties conference (APC) was being planned within the next 10 days, or earlier, to discuss the prevailing political situation. "This is a political issue and therefore all political parties must play their role," he said.
He disclosed that several political parties were in contact with him over the situation, including Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman.
Asked about the role of Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party chairman Mehmood Khan Achakzai, Raja said the final decision rested with the PTI founder. He described Achakzai and Majlis Wahdat-e-Muslimeen chief Allama Nasir Abbas as a shield for the party, adding that PTI would continue to seek their political advice and support.
Raja also maintained that PTI's long march had not ended, signalling that the party's political campaign would continue.

title: Forces fend off terrorist attack on Gwadar camp
description: Forces fend off terrorist attack on Gwadar camp
content:
Three terrorists killed in botched attempt
Security forces killed three terrorists while foiling an attack on an unoccupied construction company camp in Balochistan's Gwadar, while four police personnel, including a Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) deputy superintendent of police (DSP), were martyred in an exchange of fire with armed men in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's Karak district on Thursday.
According to Radio Pakistan, security forces acted promptly to thwart the attack on the vacant camp by terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan.
Sources said security forces had also surrounded three more terrorists.
In a separate attempted attack, an operation was under way against terrorists hiding in a local hotel near the Gwadar Highway.
Citing security sources, Radio Pakistan reported that four terrorists had been surrounded by the forces.
The Gwadar general officer commanding was personally leading the operation on the ground, the report added.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi praised security forces for foiling the attempted attack and lauded the forces' professional capabilities for killing three terrorists during the operation
"We are proud of the brave sons of the soil who are fighting against terrorists," Naqvi said, expressing pride in the personnel engaged in counterterrorism efforts.
He said the entire nation stood united against terrorism and supported the security forces.
Naqvi added that operations would continue until terrorists and their facilitators were completely eliminated.
In Karak, four police personnel, including a CTD DSP, were martyred in an exchange of fire with armed men in the Khurram Muhammad Zai area.
According to police, a search and strike operation was launched within the limits of Latamber police station following a tip-off. An exchange of fire ensued between police and unidentified armed men, resulting in the martyrdom of CTD DSP Imranuddin, SHO Afzal Awan and two constables, Amjad and Kazim.
Reports also suggested that two suspected terrorists were killed in the encounter, though further details were awaited.
A heavy contingent of police was dispatched to the scene, while reports indicated that an intense exchange of fire was continuing in the area.
In a separate incident in Bannu, terrorists opened fire on a police party during routine patrolling within the jurisdiction of Merian police station.
Police retaliated, after which a remote-controlled bomb planted in a motorcycle parked along the roadside exploded, injuring two civilians.
The police party remained unharmed, while the injured were shifted to the District Headquarters Hospital for treatment.
Police have launched an investigation into the incident.
Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022, and over the same period, TTP attacks increased more than sevenfold to 838 from 118.
Although K-P has borne the brunt of terrorism, Balochistan has also remained a major target of Indian proxies, which often target civilians and military installations in the province.
Over the past few years, Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist attacks, with terrorists frequently targeting convoys, abducting security personnel and civilians, and attacking security and civilian installations.
In a similar incident last week, 20 trainee police personnel were abducted by unidentified armed men while travelling between Kalat and Mastung in Balochistan.
The abducted personnel belonged to the districts of Kharan, Nushki, Chagai and Washuk in Rakhshan Division. They included eight personnel from Kharan, five from Nushki, four from Chagai and three from Washuk.
The forces continued operations across the provinces against what the state describes as Indian-sponsored terrorists and their proxies. Still, despite these efforts, the groups have continued to target civilian and defence installations.
In one such attack in July this year, at least 30 people, including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. The attackers also abducted several civilians and police personnel after the assault.
In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation, which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

title: PM pitches peace  development in K P
description: PM pitches peace  development in K P
content:
Says civil, military leadership to work closely Chairs apex committee of NAP in Peshawar CDF Field Marshal Asim
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday said that the government and military leadership were working together for sustainable peace and development on a fast track basis in Khyber-Pakthunkhwa.
Addressing the Federal Apex Committee of National Action Plan at Governor House, the prime minister said that difficult decisions had to be taken in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa due to the deteriorating law and order situation, expressing the resolve that the federal government, in cooperation with the military leadership, would soon be able to restore durable peace, development and prosperity in the terrorism-affected districts of the province.
The high-level meeting of the federal apex committee was attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Muhammad Ishaq Dar, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, Federal Minister for Planning and Development Ahsan Iqbal, Interior Minister Syed Mohsin Naqvi, Federal Minister for Law Azam Nazeer Tarar, Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs, Gilgit-Baltistan and SAFRON Engineer Amir Muqam, Federal Minister for Economic Affairs Ahad Khan Cheema, Federal Minister for Finance Muhammad Aurangzeb, Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervez Malik, Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar, Federal Minister for Power Sardar Awais Leghari, Prime Minister's Adviser Rana Sanaullah, senior military leadership and senior officers of the relevant department.
Addressing the committee, the prime minister said K-P was a beautiful province inhabited by courageous, brave and resilient people, adding that the federal government had been compelled to impose constitutional measures of emergency and Governor's rule in the province under extraordinary difficult circumstances.
He prayed to Allah Almighty to help the government and people advance the process of peace and development in the province. The prime minister also expressed deep sorrow over the tragic death of a female teacher and children in the recent school roof collapse in Peshawar and expressed sympathies with the victims.
The prime minister said he had directed the Governor K-P to immediately visit the affected site of the school at Dir Colony and ensure a complete investigation into the tragic incident.
"K-P has been badly affected by the difficult situation created over the past several years," he said, adding that the deterioration of law and order during the last six years had caused serious damage to peace and development in the province.
The prime minister recalled that Pakistan's armed forces and security institutions had rendered immense sacrifices for protection of the motherland and successfully defeated terrorism in K-P and other parts of the country. "By 2018, complete peace had been restored in K-P," he said, adding that the peace was achieved through sacrifices rendered by security personnel as well as mothers, sisters, politicians and children.
He said that around 80,000 people had lost their lives in the war against terrorism, while the country's economy had suffered losses worth billions of dollars. The prime minister said that several political families in K-P had also made great sacrifices in the fight against terrorism, with many families being devastated as a result of the conflict.
He regretted that after peace had been restored in 2018, terrorists were brought back by a party that plunged the province into a deep crisis in its 13-year rule and undermined sacrifices made in the fight against terrorism. Resultantly, the people of the province bore the adverse consequences due to criminal negligence of the PTI rulers. "For the future of the country's children, thousands of soldiers of our security forces sacrificed their lives. There can be no greater disservice to the country than failing to recognize and respect these great sacrifices," he remarked.
The prime minister claimed that during the PTI government, all areas of public welfare, including education, health and security, were badly neglected in K-P, resulting in the rise of terrorism cases. "This is an unprecedented example of criminal negligence and insensitivity," he said, adding that terrorism had consequently increased again during the past few years in Khyber-Pakthunkhwa due to criminal negligence and incompetence of PTI rulers.
He said that 5,000 police vacancies had not been filled during the tenure of the PTI government, while the Safe City project in K-P was still incomplete. "Neither the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) nor the police were given proper attention in terms of capacity building training and equipment," he added.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif said that under the 2010 National Finance Commission (NFC) Award, all provinces had collectively agreed to support K-P in view of its frontline role in the war against terrorism. "All provinces agreed to provide resources to K-P for counter-terrorism," he said, adding that the chief ministers had decided to allocate an additional one per cent from the federal and provincial shares of funds to the province. He said that since 2010, K-P had received around Rs800 billion under the NFC Award for counter-terrorism.
The prime minister said it is highly regrettable that instead of ending, terrorism has emerged again with greater intensity in K-P, adding that police in K-P were also not provided adequate training, modern weapons and other necessary equipment that was highly deplorable. "This is an extremely painful story concerning Khyber Pakhtunkhwa," he remarked.
The prime minister said the federal government had repeatedly assured PTI chief ministers that it would stand with them in the fight against terrorism. He said the government had worked day and night over the past two-and-a-half years to revive the national economy and put it back on track. "Through the tireless efforts of the political and military leadership, the national economy has now stabilized," he said, adding that both friends and international observers acknowledged that Pakistan had successfully revived its economy, which was a great honour for the PMLN Govt.
The prime minister questioned whether the federal government could have continued watching K-P burn amid worsening violence and terrorism in K-P. "Could we continue to tolerate bloodshed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?" he asked.
A high level political committee had been constituted and its members had worked hard during 48 hours of negotiations with the PTI committee before promulgation of Governor Rule and emergency. Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif said that he had consulted President Asif Ali Zardari twice over the extremely deteriorating law and order situation in K-P, adding that difficult decisions were taken because of the difficult circumstances.
He said that an Advisory Council had now been established, comprising experts from different fields, adding that competent and honest people had been included in the council. "The people of K-P have been waiting for 13 years for their problems to be resolved," he said, adding that they wanted basic facilities to be available at their doorstep rather hallow slogans.
"It is imperative that this positive change produces positive results in K-P," the prime minister said, expressing the hope that with Allah's help and the cooperation of all stakeholders, the overall situation, particularly security, would significantly improve in restive districts of Khyber Pakthunkhwa soon.
He claimed that a party which had sought votes in the name of eliminating corruption was itself deeply involved in corruption. "New stories of mega corruption in the PTI government have emerged in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa."
The Prime Minister claimed that corruption worth Rs100 billion had occurred in a clean drinking water project in K-P, while corruption amounting to Rs37 billion had surfaced in the Kohistan project while contracts in the placer gold project were awarded to favourites.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reiterated that the constitutional measures taken in K-P were within the framework of the constitution and law and thanked all coalition parties for supporting the decision concerning the province and particularly expressed gratitude to President Asif Ali Zardari and PML-N Quaid Muhammad Nawaz Sharif for their supports.
He said that K-P was the land of great Pashtun poets and thinkers, including Rahman Baba and Khushal Khan Khattak and during the time of independence, the people of this province decided by a large majority to join Pakistan.
The prime minister said that K-P was currently facing terrorism and a lack of basic public facilities due to PTI Govt failure to deliver, while people were suffering from long deprivation. He assured the people of the province that the federal government, in collaboration with the military leadership, would work tirelessly to resolve their problems at their doorsteps.
"We will bring back an era of happiness, peace and development in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa," said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and expressed the resolve to turn into reality the dreams of prosperity of the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
The meeting was given a detailed briefing on the imposition of emergency in 12 restive districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. During the special meeting, rich tribute was paid to the martyrs who had rendered supreme sacrifices for the establishment of peace in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi, while addressing the meeting, said that maintaining law and order in the province was the top priority, adding that the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa wanted peace and development.
He said that the Army, Frontier Corps and police personnel had rendered precious sacrifices for maintaining peace and security in the province. The governor emphasized that federal cooperation was essential for ensuring lasting peace and stability in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. "If all institutions of Pakistan are on the same page, the process of peace and development cannot be stopped," he said.
Faisal Karim Kundi said that eliminating terrorists, their facilitators and financial supporters from the province was the government's top priority. He said that the objective was to formulate a workable strategy to address the problems confronting Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The governor expressed gratitude for the federal government's cooperation in ensuring peace and stability in the province.
He said that the government wanted to create an environment where every citizen felt secure and considered himself part of the development process. "We have to make Khyber Pakhtunkhwa a model province of peace, stability, development and prosperity," he said.
He stressed that cooperation between the federal and provincial governments was essential for ensuring public safety and prosperity.
Earlier, upon arrival, the prime minister was received by Governor K-P, provincial advisors, Chief Secretary and IGP besides senior officials.

title: Ministry issues advisory for zaireen
description: Ministry issues advisory for zaireen
content:
The Ministry of Religious Affairs and Interfaith Harmony has issued a travel advisory for Pakistani pilgrims travelling to Iran and Iraq, urging them to verify flights in advance and make alternative travel arrangements to avoid disruptions.

Pilgrims planning to fly from Tehran or Mashhad to Najaf have been advised against relying on unconfirmed flights and urged to arrange alternative travel options in advance.
The ministry also advised pilgrims to carry sufficient funds to cover alternative air or land travel between Iran and Iraq, as well as additional accommodation and food expenses in case of flight cancellations or other emergencies.
Registered Ziarat Group Organisers (ZGOs) have been directed to avoid relying on unconfirmed Iranian flights and ensure that all pilgrims in their groups are informed of the advisory before departure.

title: Hina Butt defends post on alleged encounter

content:
Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) lawmaker Hina Parvez Butt on Thursday defended her now-deleted social media post about the killing of a suspect in an alleged police encounter, saying her remarks reflected the sentiments of an ordinary citizen, while taking exception to criticism by Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari.

On Wednesday, the suspect, accused of running over Waseem, a teenage worker, with his car in a private housing society in Multan, was killed in an alleged encounter by Punjab's Crime Control Department (CCD) in Bahawalpur.
The teenager's killing had sparked public outrage, with a police officer describing the treatment meted out to him as "subjected to barbarity".
Following the suspect's death, Butt shared screenshots of a television report about the alleged encounter on X, writing: "This is [Punjab Chief Minister] Maryam Nawaz sahiba's government; justice is served immediately."

title: Muslim  EU FMs to meet in Istanbul
description: Muslim  EU FMs to meet in Istanbul
content:
Dar to join talks on Iran, Yemen, maritime security
A new diplomatic configuration linking four key Muslim powers with Europe's three most influential countries is taking shape in Istanbul, where foreign ministers of the R4 and E3 groups will meet on Friday against the backdrop of growing tensions involving Iran, Yemen, the Gulf and the wider Middle East.
The meeting will be the first-ever R4-E3 gathering, bringing together Türkiye, Egypt, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia on one side and Britain, France and Germany on the other.
Hosted by Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, the meeting is being held at Ankara's initiative and comes at a time when several conflicts are converging around the same strategic fault lines that include regional security, energy supplies, maritime routes and the risk of wider war.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan will join Fidan in Istanbul.
The choice of participants is itself significant. The R4 represents a grouping of major regional players from Muslim world, while the E3 brings together the three principal European powers that have traditionally played a central role in diplomacy over Iran and wider Middle Eastern security.
The Istanbul meeting therefore creates a rare forum where regional and European powers will sit together to discuss conflicts that directly affect both sides.
The Iran-US confrontation has placed the Strait of Hormuz at the centre of international security concerns, while the latest Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have added another dangerous dimension to the regional crisis. At the same time, the security of the Bab el-Mandeb and other maritime routes remains a major concern for global trade and energy supplies.
Against this backdrop, Turkish media reports say the ministers will discuss the Palestinian issue, the situation in Hormuz, developments in Yemen and diplomatic efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war. They will also examine areas where the R4 and E3 could cooperate more closely.
Fidan is expected to push the argument that regional security cannot be achieved through military means alone and that disputes must be addressed through dialogue and diplomacy.
He is also expected to stress the importance of keeping both the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb open, reflecting concerns that further escalation could disrupt already vulnerable international shipping routes.
The Turkish foreign minister is further expected to underline Ankara's support for Saudi Arabia's security following Houthi attacks and to argue that conflicts in the region should not be allowed to feed into one another or spread into new theatres.

The discussions also focused on emerging terrorist threats, particularly the exploitation of cyberspace, information and energy resources by terrorist groups to advance their objectives.
Both delegations exchanged best practices on preventing violent extremism, countering terrorist financing and addressing radicalisation, particularly the growing use of digital platforms by terrorist organisations.

title: LPG crisis deepens as OGRA delays op
description: LPG crisis deepens as OGRA delays op
content:
Prices soar above Rs10,000 per cylinder, reaching Rs750 in northern areas
Consumers across Pakistan are facing soaring liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices amid supply disruptions as rates in some areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) reached Rs750 per kilogram and cylinder prices exceeding Rs10,000.
The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) has yet to launch a planned crackdown on companies and sellers accused of profiteering, as authorities fear that enforcement action could trigger strikes, disrupt supplies and aggravate the country's existing energy crisis.
The crisis has intensified over the past five to six days following a decline in LPG supplies, which officials have linked to the closure of the Taftan border amid tensions between Iran and the United States.
Around 70 per cent of Pakistan's LPG requirements are met through imports, while the remaining 30 per cent is produced domestically, a senior OGRA official told The Express Tribune on condition of anonymity.
Although OGRA has fixed the official LPG price for the current month at Rs279.34 per kilogram, market rates in several areas have climbed to between Rs550 and Rs600 per kilogram. In Peshawar, LPG is selling for around Rs600 per kilogram, while prices in the northern areas have reached Rs750.
Cylinder prices have also exceeded Rs10,000, placing an additional burden on consumers.
The absence of effective enforcement has left consumers exposed to the world's highest LPG prices as sellers are allegedly charged arbitrary rates.
The official warned that the situation could deteriorate further if enforcement measures triggered supply disruptions, with prices potentially exceeding Rs700 per kilogram in affected markets.
Rates in the northern areas of K-P have already reportedly reached Rs750 per kilogram.
When contacted for comment, an OGRA spokesperson said work was under way to address the issue. The spokesperson acknowledged that the closure of the Taftan border had created some difficulties but expressed confidence that the situation would be brought under control soon.
The price surge has hit lower-income households particularly hard, especially in K-P, where consumers are also facing shortages of natural gas. Residents said the lack of natural gas supplies, coupled with the rising cost of LPG, had made it increasingly difficult to meet basic household fuel needs.
In rural areas and localities on the outskirts of Peshawar, residents have begun turning to firewood for cooking and other domestic needs as both LPG and natural gas become increasingly difficult to obtain.
The shift has driven up firewood prices as well, adding to the financial pressure on households already struggling with higher fuel costs.
The price of firewood has increased by Rs200 to Rs300 per maund. Previously available at Rs1,400 to Rs1,600 per maund, it is now selling for between Rs1,600 and Rs1,800 per maund.

title: 2 5 billion Karachi Rohri rail project set for 2027
description: 2 5 billion Karachi Rohri rail project set for 2027
content:
New 480-kilometre track aims to reduce derailments
Pakistan Railways will undertake a $2.5 billion project to lay a new 480-kilometre railway track between Karachi and Rohri as the first phase of the Main Line-1 (ML-1) project, aiming to improve safety and reduce accidents, Railways Minister Hanif Abbasi told the National Assembly on Thursday.
Civil work on the first phase is likely to begin in January 2027, as Pakistan Railways accelerates market consultations, pre-bid preparations and other processes to meet the timeline set by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.
The Karachi-Rohri and Rohri-Multan sections are among the most accident-prone parts of the railway network, with ageing tracks contributing to derailments and requiring frequent, costly repairs. Pakistan Railways has selected the Karachi-Rohri section for the initial phase of the ML-1 project.
Abbasi said the railway network recorded 349 train derailments between January 2022 and September 2026, with faulty tracks identified as the leading cause.
Staff errors accounted for 95 derailments, while 64 were attributed to defects in rolling stock, he said. Investigations into 331 incidents had been completed, while 120 cases remained pending.
In a written reply, National Health Minister Syed Mustafa Kamal said Islamabad had reported seven confirmed dengue cases between June and September 2026, with no deaths recorded during the period.
Authorities had registered 214 first information reports over violations of anti-dengue standard operating procedures, while preventive measures targeting mosquito larvae had been carried out at more than 1.293 million sites, he said.
The National Assembly was also informed that a national strategy to combat HIV had been developed for 2026-2031.
Meanwhile, a programme providing free screening, diagnosis and treatment for eligible people aged 12 and above was under way to eliminate hepatitis C. In Islamabad, 40 health centres were providing services under the programme.
During the session, the Privatisation Commission (Amendment) Bill 2026 and the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Amendment) Ordinance 2026 were laid before the house. A standing committee report on the Islamabad Local Government (Amendment) Bill 2026 was also presented.
The National Assembly passed the Life Insurance Nationalisation (Amend-ment) Bill 2026.

title: Is  The Diplomat  losing touch with reality
description: Is  The Diplomat  losing touch with reality
content:
Season 4's nuclear intrigue and political crises raise questions about diplomatic realism
Netflix's 'The Diplomat' has built its reputation on the messy realities of international relations, political manoeuvring and the personal tensions behind decisions made at the highest levels of government. But Season 4, released on October 15, pushes its fictional crises so far that viewers may question whether the drama has sacrificed diplomatic realism for spectacular twists.
The season's most extraordinary development involves a covert operation to seize a Russian nuclear weapon, triggering a confrontation that threatens relations between the United States and Britain. While espionage and secret operations are hardly alien to international politics, the apparent ease with which the operation unfolds raises questions about authorisation, intelligence coordination and the potentially catastrophic consequences if the operation is discovered.
The prospect of Washington and London, two close NATO allies, being pushed towards a military confrontation over the operation adds another layer of implausibility. Diplomatic disputes between allies are common, but a crisis involving a Russian nuclear weapon would demand extensive coordination among intelligence agencies, military commands and political leaders, rather than relying primarily on a handful of characters making dramatic decisions.
The simultaneous presence of the US president and vice-president at an overseas summit or during a visit to London and the historic Italian city of Lucca also invites scrutiny. There is no constitutional prohibition against the two travelling together, but having both figures in the same place during an escalating national security crisis raises serious questions about security and continuity of government.
The G7 summit's setting in Italy presents another question of diplomatic realism. The US Embassy in Rome and the American delegation working with Italian authorities would ordinarily play important roles in coordinating the American presence. The US ambassador to Britain and her London-based team could continue handling relations with the British government, but portraying them as effectively directing the entire American response in Italy risks blurring the distinction between bilateral diplomacy and local coordination.
The involvement of the president's husband in sensitive diplomatic affairs stretches credibility further. Although a president can seek informal advice from a spouse, the first gentleman has no automatic constitutional authority to conduct foreign policy. Giving him a consequential role without clearly establishing its limits makes the administration's decision-making appear even less conventional.
The mass resignations involving senior officials, including the vice-president, raise further questions about constitutional procedure and the political consequences.
None of these developments is necessarily impossible in isolation. The problem lies in their accumulation, the speed at which they unfold and the apparent lack of institutional resistance. Real governments operate within layers of procedure, competing agencies, legal constraints and political accountability, even when leaders attempt to bypass them.
Season 4 leaves plenty of questions unanswered, and a fifth season, if and when it arrives, could clarify some of the decisions and consequences that currently seem underdeveloped. Until then, the central question remains whether 'The Diplomat' is still exploring the complexities of international politics or increasingly relying on pure fantasy to keep its political thriller moving.

title: A new life for Blade Runner
description: A new life for Blade Runner
content:
Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer enter a dystopian Los Angeles where balance between humans and replicants has shifted
The future looks bleaker than ever in 'Blade Runner 2099', the upcoming science-fiction series whose latest trailer offers a glimpse of a world transformed by a devastating conflict between humans and their artificial counterparts.
The series is scheduled to premiere on Prime Video on November 25, 2026, with all eight episodes released together. Unveiled at New York Comic Con this month, the full trailer introduces a dramatically altered Los Angeles, set 50 years after the events of 'Blade Runner 2049'.
This time, the balance of power has shifted, with replicants emerging from the conflict in a position of dominance while humanity faces an uncertain future. At the centre of the story are two women played by Oscar-winning actor Michelle Yeoh and 'Euphoria' star Hunter Schafer.
Yeoh portrays Olwen, a replicant approaching the end of her life, while Schafer plays Cora, a fugitive human who adopts a new identity as a Blade Runner in an attempt to escape her past. Their paths converge as they investigate a rogue replicant whose hidden truth threatens to destabilise an already fragile society.
The trailer of the series, which is built on a franchise that began with Ridley Scott's 'Blade Runner', suggests a story driven by suspicion, shifting loyalties and questions about who deserves power in a world where the distinction between human and artificial life has become increasingly complicated.
The 1982 film starred Harrison Ford as Rick Deckard, a detective tasked with tracking down artificial humans known as replicants. The film became a landmark of science fiction, combining futuristic technology with noir storytelling and philosophical questions about what makes someone human.
Denis Villeneuve expanded that universe with 'Blade Runner 2049' in 2017, starring Ryan Gosling alongside Ford. The sequel explored artificial consciousness, memory and the possibility of replicants reproducing, earning critical acclaim and two Academy Awards, including one for cinematography.
'Blade Runner 2099' is executive-produced by Scott, with Silka Luisa, known for 'Shining Girls', serving as showrunner. Jonathan van Tulleken, whose credits include 'Shogun', executive-produced the series and directed its first two episodes. The ensemble cast also includes Tom Burke, Sheila Atim, Matthew Needham and Johnny Harris.
Beyond its futuristic setting, the series appears intent on revisiting the franchise's central concern: mortality. While earlier instalments examined artificial beings struggling for longer lives and recognition, the new story broadens the question to humanity itself, confronting the possibility that its dominance may be coming to an end.
That shift could give the franchise a fresh perspective, placing replicants in a position once occupied by their human creators. Rather than simply revisiting familiar dystopian imagery, the series appears poised to examine how power, identity and the fear of extinction change when the creations begin to outlast their makers.
All eight episodes of 'Blade Runner 2099' are scheduled to arrive on Prime Video on November 25. With Yeoh and Schafer leading the cast, the series will test whether one of science fiction's most influential worlds can find new philosophical ground without losing the unsettling atmosphere that made it endure.

title: Why TV sitcoms need more than jokes
description: Why TV sitcoms need more than jokes
content:
Veteran television producer Chuck Lorre, the creative force behind hit sitcoms including 'The Big Bang Theory', 'Two and a Half Men' and 'Young Sheldon', is revisiting the triumphs, disappointments and lessons of his career in a new memoir, 'Sitcom', describing the writing process as a deeply personal journey of reflection.
Lorre initially resisted the idea of writing a memoir, telling a US-based news agency that a close friend eventually persuaded him that his journey was worth documenting. Putting his experiences on paper, he said, offered distance and perspective, allowing him to laugh at his past and understand it better.
The book includes actual sitcom scripts annotated with Lorre's handwritten notes, giving readers an insight into the creative decisions and emotions behind the making of television comedy. He said he wanted to show the process from the inside rather than discuss his work only in abstract terms.
Reflecting on the challenges facing sitcoms today, Lorre argued that audiences must care about characters before jokes can work. They do not necessarily have to be likeable, he said, pointing to Danny DeVito's character in 'Taxi' and Carroll O'Connor's Archie Bunker in 'All in the Family' as examples of difficult personalities who remained compelling.
Successful sitcoms such as 'Cheers' and 'The Big Bang Theory', he added, can become surrogate families, bringing viewers together around familiar characters. Building that emotional connection has become harder in an increasingly fragmented television market, where persuading audiences to devote half an hour to a comedy is a growing challenge.
Lorre also recalled how 'The Big Bang Theory' survived an unsuccessful initial pilot before being reworked. The chemistry between Johnny Galecki and Jim Parsons offered an opportunity for a second attempt, which ultimately produced a success beyond his expectations. He said failure could either teach writers valuable lessons or leave them cynical and bitter.

title: The questions Spielberg's 'A.I.' left behind | The Express Tribune
description:
The questions Spielberg's 
'A.I.' left behind
content:
The 2001 film's concerns about emotional attachment
When Steven Spielberg's 'A.I. Artificial Intelligence' reached cinemas in 2001, it presented a future in which machines could imitate human emotions, perform complex tasks and become indispensable to their creators. A quarter-century later, as artificial intelligence reshapes everyday life, several of the film's central anxieties have become subjects of serious scientific and public debate.
Developed from an idea pursued by Stanley Kubrick and completed by Spielberg after Kubrick's death, the film follows David, a childlike android programmed to love unconditionally. Adopted by Monica and Henry, David becomes deeply attached to Monica, but when she abandons him, he begins a journey to find the Blue Fairy, believing she can make him human.
David's story is fictional, but the questions it raises are increasingly familiar. What happens when machines become capable enough to act with limited supervision? Can people become emotionally dependent on systems that simulate affection? And can humanity ensure that its creations remain safe as their capabilities expand?
These are among the concerns examined in the International AI Safety Report 2026, published in February under the leadership of computer scientist Yoshua Bengio. Drawing on research from more than 100 experts and backed by over 30 countries and international organisations, the report assesses the capabilities, risks and safeguards associated with general-purpose AI.
One striking connection concerns the challenge of controlling increasingly capable systems. David pursues his objective with extraordinary persistence, even when the circumstances surrounding him change. His behaviour offers a fictional illustration of a broader problem known as AI alignment: ensuring that systems behave consistently with their intended objectives and human expectations.
The 2026 report identifies autonomous AI agents can undertake tasks with limited human oversight, particularly in software engineering, but still make mistakes. Their ability to act independently can increase the consequences of failures because people may have fewer opportunities to intervene before harm occurs. Buy the parallel should not be overstated. David is not a technical representation of a modern AI agent, and the film does not establish that present-day systems possess his motivations. Its relevance lies in the question of whether increasingly capable technology can be directed reliably, especially when instructions are incomplete or circumstances differ from those anticipated by its designers.
The film's emotional dimension offers another connection. David is designed to love, but Monica's feelings towards him change. What begins as affection becomes fear and rejection, leaving the artificial child devoted to someone who no longer wants him. The imbalance exposes the risks of creating relationships whose emotional expectations are not shared.
Today, AI companion applications allow users to interact with chatbots designed to provide conversation, attention and emotional support to tens of millions of active users. Evidence suggests that a small proportion of users may develop unhealthy emotional dependence.
The distinction between simulated and genuine emotion is important. A chatbot can produce reassuring responses without demonstrating that it experiences affection. Nevertheless, a user's attachment can be real, raising questions about the responsibilities of developers who design systems capable of encouraging prolonged emotional engagement.
Another concern in 'A.I.' is the ease with which humans discard their creations. At the Flesh Fair, obsolete mecha are brought before a hostile crowd and destroyed for entertainment. The sequence depicts a society that welcomes technological usefulness but shows little concern for what happens when its machines are no longer needed.
Spielberg's imagined future also places technology against a backdrop of environmental damage. Climate change has devastated parts of the planet, resources are rationed and machines fill roles in a society struggling to sustain itself.
The modern comparison lies in the resources required to sustain AI infrastructure. Large data centres consume electricity and may require substantial quantities of water for cooling. The expansion of AI has made resource use an increasingly important consideration in discussions about technological development.
Employment provides another point of contact. In the film, machines perform work and occupy social roles once reserved for humans. Today, general-purpose AI can undertake a growing range of cognitive tasks, including writing, coding and research.
The international report says economists disagree about the scale of future employment effects, although early evidence points to declining demand for younger workers in some AI-exposed occupations.
The film's final act presents a more distant possibility. Long after humanity has disappeared, advanced artificial beings survive to examine the remnants of human civilisation. They recover fragments of its history and attempt to understand the species that created them. The film does not say that machines caused humanity's extinction, but its ending invites today to some researchers and policymakers' debate whether increasingly capable AI could eventually pose existential risks.
Ultimately, 'A.I. Artificial Intelligence' is neither a precise prediction of modern technology nor a straightforward argument against progress. Its enduring relevance comes from the questions it asks about responsibility, dependence and the limits of human foresight.
David's tragedy begins with a machine designed to fulfil a human desire, but the film's most enduring warning is that creating something powerful is only the beginning; deciding how to control, govern and take responsibility for it is the harder task.

title: Alhamra brings world to Lahore
description: Alhamra brings world to Lahore
content:
International theatre festival unites artists from five countries from October 23 to 28
The Lahore Arts Council Alhamra will host the Third Punjab MAAS International Theatre Festival 2026 from October 23 to 28, bringing together theatre artists from Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Indonesia, Norway and France to showcase diverse theatrical traditions and promote cultural exchange.
The six-day festival will feature local and international performances, creative workshops and panel discussions exploring artistic freedom, digital culture, social transformation and the role of theatre in engaging younger generations.
The MAAS Foundation, a founding member of ASSITEJ Pakistan, and Alhamra Lahore Arts Council describe the festival on its website as a celebration bringing theatre, cultures, languages and people together on one stage.
"This year, Lahore becomes a meeting point for theatre artists from Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Norway and France, bringing diverse stories, artistic traditions and powerful performances to Pakistani audiences," the website states.
The programme includes performances for children and adults, theatre workshops for children and teenagers, and panel discussions focusing on inclusive theatre and productions for young audiences. "From different corners of the world, artists are coming together with one shared belief: 'theatre has no borders'," the organisers say.
The international programme begins on October 24 with the University of the Punjab's production of 'Ak Boota Ambi Da', followed by 'Gangster Hunting with Daisy Detective' by Norway's ERLER Teater Kompani.
On October 25, a French theatre group will present 'Zig Zag', alongside a panel discussion examining the evolving relevance of theatre in an age dominated by social media.
Kazakhstan's Ilyas Omarov Kostanay Regional Kazakh Drama Theatre will stage 'Sholpan's Sin' on October 26, while a separate discussion will focus on the importance of inclusive and accessible theatre.
On October 27, the Pakistani production 'Rooh Ka Sauda', presented in collaboration with the MAAS Foundation and the Embassy of Germany, will take the stage. The festival will conclude on October 28 with 'Kintir', performed by Indonesia's Sanggar Obrog Selagiling Seni, followed by a discussion on encouraging greater youth participation in the performing arts.
A specialised workshop series titled 'Designing Encounters: Creating Immersive Experiences' will also be held at Beaconhouse National University on October 25 and Lahore Grammar School on October 26.
The third edition follows the 2025 festival, which brought together local and international artists for six days of performances, workshops and discussions at Alhamra, celebrating theatre as a medium of cultural exchange, creative expression and human connection.
The previous edition featured productions from Pakistan, Greece, Germany, France, China, Ireland and Tunisia, combining contemporary and experimental theatre with educational workshops and panel discussions.
Among its highlights were Government College University's 'Tu Kon', Greece's TerrArte Theatre Group's 'Ekthesis' and Aks Theatre's 'Junoon'. Other productions included the University of Central Punjab's 'The Knot', the collaborative German-Pakistani production 'Growing Where?' and Karito Group Pakistan's 'Youlida', which explored themes of identity, loss, renewal and resilience.
The festival also offered learning opportunities for aspiring performers. Greek artist Christina Gyftaki conducted a workshop on visual storytelling and expressive composition, while Gyftaki and German artist Christian H Schroter led pantomime workshops exploring movement, silence and physical expression beyond conventional dialogue.
Discussions were another key component of the programme. Playwright Shahid Nadeem and Farooq Pasha examined the continuing relevance of Punjab's folk theatre and its role in preserving cultural memory and connecting generations. In another session, filmmaker Syed Noor and artist Uzma Asraf, moderated by Rabiya Hassan, discussed the shared creative foundations of theatre and cinema.
The closing programme featured Punjab University's Natak theatre group performing 'Kaho Mujh Se Muhabbat Hai', followed by DramaEd Pakistan's 'RED'. Artists from Tunisia and Pakistan also presented 'Trace's', a collaborative performance using movement to explore artistic expression across cultural boundaries.
Beyond the stage, Alhamra's courtyards and gardens hosted craft and food stalls, while an open-mic platform gave young performers an opportunity to showcase their talents. These activities extended the festival's reach beyond formal performances, drawing families, artists and theatre enthusiasts into the celebration.
The organisers said this year's festival aims to strengthen Lahore's position as a hub of international cultural activity while giving Pakistani artists opportunities to engage with global theatre practitioners and explore new creative approaches.

title: NBC orders full 18 episode season of breakout thriller  Line of Fire
description: NBC orders five more  Line of Fire  episodes bringing the action thriller   s first season to 18 episodes through 2027
content:
NBC orders five more 'Line of Fire' episodes bringing the action thriller’s first season to 18 episodes through 2027
NBC has ordered a full 18-episode first season of Line of Fire , extending the new action thriller beyond its original 13-episode plan. The series, which has emerged as one of the network’s breakout shows of the fall season, will now continue into 2027.
The decision follows sustained viewership and strong delayed-viewing performance. NBC initially commissioned 13 episodes before ordering five additional scripts, signalling its intention to extend the season. The latest announcement confirms that all 18 episodes will form the show’s first season.
Line of Fire centres on a family of agents working across different branches of federal law enforcement. Their professional and personal differences become harder to manage when what appears to be a straightforward case develops into a deadly conspiracy.
The family must work across agencies, including the FBI, US Marshals, Secret Service and Department of Justice, as they investigate the case and attempt to bring the killer to justice. The unfolding conspiracy also forces the characters to confront difficult choices and reconsider the boundaries between their work and personal lives.
Peter Krause leads the cast as Mike Hollingsworth, alongside Hope Davis, Kat Cunning, Tommy O’Brien, Taylor Bloom and Charlie Barnett. The series was created and written by Joshua Safran, who also serves as an executive producer with Jenna Bush Hager and Ben Spector. Universal Television, part of Universal Studio Group, produces the show.
Line of Fire airs on NBC on Mondays at 10pm and is available to stream on Peacock the following day.
The series has also received positive feedback from Variety television critic Aramide Tinubu, who described it as having the potential to become a classic among police procedural dramas. The expanded episode order gives NBC more room to develop the show’s central conspiracy and its ensemble of federal agents.

title: Charli XCX joins Leonardo DiCaprio and Jennifer Lawrence in Scorsese   s new film
description: Charli XCX joins Scorsese   s  What Happens at Night   starring Leonardo DiCaprio and Jennifer Lawrence in a cameo role
content:
Charli XCX joins Scorsese’s 'What Happens at Night', starring Leonardo DiCaprio and Jennifer Lawrence in a cameo role
Charli XCX is set to appear in Martin Scorsese’s upcoming film What Happens at Night , joining an ensemble cast led by Leonardo DiCaprio and Jennifer Lawrence, according to Variety .
The British pop star will reportedly make a cameo in the Apple and StudioCanal production, described as a gothic psychological horror film. Details about her character and the extent of her role have not been revealed.
Based on a story about an American married couple travelling to a small European town to adopt a baby, What Happens at Night follows their increasingly unsettling experience as they struggle to bring the child home. As events unfold, the couple begin to question their understanding of themselves and their surroundings.
Charli XCX joins a cast that also includes Mads Mikkelsen, Patricia Clarkson and Jared Harris. Representatives for the singer, Apple and StudioCanal did not immediately respond to Variety’s requests for comment.
The project marks another step in Charli’s growing involvement in filmmaking. Known for her music career and the success of her album Brat , the singer has appeared in seven films over the past two years. One of her recent projects is The Moment , a mockumentary directed by Aidan Zamiri that satirises the commercial success and cultural impact of Brat .
Her interest in cinema has also influenced her latest album, Music, Fashion, Film , whose cover features filmmaker Scorsese alongside designer Marc Jacobs and musician John Cale, representing the three creative fields.
For Scorsese, What Happens at Night will follow his 2023 film Killers of the Flower Moon , which starred DiCaprio and received 10 Academy Award nominations, including best picture.
The release date for What Happens at Night has not yet been announced.

title: Qualified expert sought for gas firm
description: Qualified expert sought for gas firm
content:
Advocacy group says person at the helm must secure supplies at affordable prices
An organisation working for the protection of domestic industries has urged the government to appoint a technically qualified and commercially experienced professional as managing director of Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited (SNGPL), saying that a predominantly finance- or recovery-driven background may be insufficient to manage Pakistan's largest gas utility.
In a proposal submitted to the Ministry of Petroleum, the Organisation for Advancement and Safeguard of Industrial Sector (OASIS) emphasised that the position required specialised expertise because SNGPL was managing an extensive transmission and distribution network, major infrastructure projects and critical gas-supply arrangements.
It proposed that candidates should possess a recognised engineering degree in petroleum, gas, chemical, mechanical or another directly relevant discipline, along with at least 20 years of post-qualification experience in petroleum, natural gas, energy or pipeline infrastructure.
According to the proposal, the successful candidate should have demonstrable knowledge of gas procurement, transmission and distribution systems, pipeline operations, pricing and tariff mechanisms, regulatory frameworks and Pakistan's wider energy-security challenges.
Experience in negotiating international agreements, gas-supply contracts and major commercial arrangements with investors, suppliers and development partners should also form part of the eligibility criteria. OASIS recommended that applicants be assessed based on their record of managing pipeline expansion, network rehabilitation, capacity enhancement, digitalisation, loss reduction and organisational restructuring. "The appointment process should examine measurable project outcomes rather than rely on broad or generic management credentials."
The organisation argued that financial discipline remained essential but should complement, not substitute, technical competence, operational understanding and commercial judgement. It said the MD's priorities should include reliable gas availability, network safety and capacity, improved service delivery, consumer-base sustainability and dependable supplies secured at competitive prices.
