title: Tally hits 95 as two more monkeypox cases reported in Sindh
description: Province reports 11 deaths from the virus so far this year
content:
Province reports 11 deaths from the virus so far this year
Sindh has reported two more cases of monkeypox, or mpox, taking the total caseload recorded in the province this year to 95. The virus has claimed 11 lives so far.
The latest cases involve 21-year-old Salman Ali and 23-year-old Ishrat Fatima, both of whom tested positive for the virus, according to a report by Dow University’s provincial public health laboratory.
Both patients are already receiving treatment at the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital, officials said.
The emergence of additional cases has underscored the importance of continued surveillance and preventive measures to contain the spread of the virus.
Of the 95 cases thus far, 71 were men, accounting for 75.27 per cent, while 24 were women. People aged 30 to 39 were the most affected age group, with 26 confirmed cases, while 23 children up to the age of nine also tested positive for mpox.
April recorded the highest number of cases at 31, followed by September with 20, August with 17, July with seven, October with six so far, March with five, June with four and May with two.
Experts said mpox is a viral disease that can spread through close physical or skin-to-skin contact with an infected person, as well as contact with lesions, bodily fluids or contaminated objects. Suspected patients should also limit close contact with others to reduce the risk of transmission, experts said.
Common symptoms include fever, headache, body aches, weakness, swollen lymph nodes and skin rashes or blisters. People developing symptoms have been advised to avoid close contact with others and seek immediate medical evaluation and diagnostic testing.
Medical experts advise avoiding close physical contact with infected individuals, maintaining proper hand hygiene and refraining from sharing personal items. People experiencing fever, swollen lymph nodes or unusual skin rashes and blisters should seek immediate medical attention.

title: Chappell Roan brings out Christina Aguilera for surprise duet at Los Angeles concert

content:
Before introducing Aguilera, Roan paid tribute to her, crediting her with helping pave the way for women in pop music
Chappell Roan surprised fans by bringing Christina Aguilera on stage during her Super Graphic Spectacular concert in Los Angeles, where the pop stars performed Aguilera’s hit “Beautiful” and a duet of Roan’s song “Coffee”.
The surprise appearance took place on Wednesday, October 21, at the Shrine Auditorium. Before introducing Aguilera, Roan paid tribute to the singer, crediting her with helping pave the way for women in pop music to express themselves freely through their music and fashion.
“I want to introduce this person [who] honestly paved the way for me and all women in pop to do whatever the f--- they want, sing and wear whatever the f--- they want,” Roan told the audience, adding that she was grateful to Aguilera. “She’s a f---ing legend.”
Aguilera, 45, embraced Roan, 28, as the pair met on stage. The “Dirrty” singer then returned the praise, saying that from the moment she heard Roan’s voice, she knew the younger artist was “a force to be reckoned with”.
Aguilera performed her 2002 hit “Beautiful”, one of the defining songs of her career, before joining Roan for “Coffee”. Aguilera described the latter track as “one of my favourite songs of hers”, making the collaboration a meeting of two generations of pop artists.
The performance formed part of Roan’s two-night Super Graphic Spectacular event, which brings together musicians and other performers for a celebration of pop music and queer culture. The first night also featured Lola Young, Tinashe, Amanda Lepore, Blaine Petrovia and Kyra Jeté.
Roan also performed a version of Olivia Rodrigo’s “Expectations”, following the release of a remix featuring the two singers earlier in the month.
The second night, scheduled for Thursday, October 22, includes performances by Caroline Polachek, MUNA, Alisa Mae, Fantasia Royale Gaga and Sweaty Eddie, with Roan headlining again.
Beyond the performances, the event has a charitable purpose. All proceeds will benefit Roan’s Midwest Princess Project, which supports transgender young people and LGBTQ+ communities by helping fund organisations providing resources and assistance.
Aguilera’s appearance also highlighted the influence she has had on younger performers, including Roan, who has become known for her theatrical style, bold fashion choices and outspoken approach to self-expression. By bringing the veteran pop star on stage, Roan celebrated an artist whose music and public image helped expand expectations of what a female pop performer could be.
The unexpected collaboration quickly became a highlight of the Los Angeles show, bringing together Aguilera’s signature vocals and Roan’s distinctive pop sensibility for a performance that honoured both their music and the influence artists can have across generations.

title: Pakistan  Maldives move to establish direct air links
description: PM Shehbaz says aviation ministry directed to explore direct flights between Pakistan and Maldives
content:
PM Shehbaz says aviation ministry directed to explore direct flights between Pakistan and Maldives
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday said he had directed the Ministry of Aviation to explore ways to establish direct flights between Pakistan and the Maldives, as the two countries agreed to strengthen air connectivity and expand bilateral trade.
Addressing the Maldives-Pakistan Business Forum 2026, which was also attended by Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu, the prime minister expressed hope that the president’s visit would prove a turning point in relations between the two countries.
“Above all, this will be a game-changer in terms of promoting our bilateral trade and investment portfolios,” he said.
Read : Pakistan, Maldives sign 20 MoUs, target $200m trade
Addressing businessmen, entrepreneurs, traders and investors from both countries, PM Shehbaz described the agreement to increase bilateral trade from $13 million to $200 million over the next two years as an opportunity that required concrete action and coordinated efforts.
“My brother President Muizzu, on my request, readily agreed to make a firm understanding to increase our bilateral trade from $13 million to $200 million in the next two years, and now it’s all up to us to make use of this opportunity,” he said.
He urged the business communities of both countries to prepare comprehensive plans to achieve the target through joint efforts and close coordination.
The prime minister said Pakistan would send a delegation to Malé after President Muizzu’s return, comprising experienced exporters, relevant government ministers and officials, to work towards expanding trade ties, adding that both countries would make additional efforts to meet the agreed target.
Highlighting the importance of connectivity, PM Shehbaz said there were currently no direct flights between Pakistan and the Maldives, making the establishment of an air link essential to closer bilateral relations.
“Connectivity is very important. We don’t have direct flights from Malé to Karachi or Islamabad, so this air link is extremely important,” he said.
The prime minister said he had directed the Ministry of Aviation to explore ways to launch flights between the two countries as soon as possible, adding that President Muizzu had also instructed his country’s airline to prepare a plan to start flights to Pakistan.
“I have given instructions to the Civil Aviation Department to work out a plan whereby they can start these air flights between the two countries as early as possible,” said the prime minister.
Emphasising the importance of maritime connectivity, the prime minister said the two countries would find it difficult to achieve their trade targets efficiently without a direct shipping schedule between Karachi or Gwadar and Malé.
He thanked President Muizzu for visiting Pakistan, noting that it was the first visit by a Maldivian leader in 11 years and expressed hope for continued high-level engagement.
“I hope this will be your first visit amongst many in times to come, and I hope you can at least make two visits to Pakistan this year,” he concluded.

title: Sharjeel says PPP was  last party  to support emergency in K P
description: Says Sindh has made significant progress in public transport over the past four to five years
content:
Says Sindh has made significant progress in public transport over the past four to five years
Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon on Monday stated that the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) was the “last party” to support governor’s rule and the imposition of an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), further adding that the party had advocated political dialogue and engagement as the first course of action.
The emergency and governor’s rule were declared on October 11 after negotiations between the government and opposition failed , culminating in a PTI long march towards Islamabad that began on October 4.
“PPP was the last party that was in favour of the governor’s rule. We tried to engage them, not once but ten times, and PPP told the federal government that it wanted to resolve issues through political dialogue, but after multiple attempts, if the K-P chief minister himself had an inclination towards the Taliban and terrorists and was not willing to agree, then the government could not let the people of K-P be left on their own at the mercy of the terrorists”. Memon made these remarks during a visit to the Green Line BRT Operations Command and Control Centre, where he received a briefing on the system’s operations, integration with other transport projects, ridership and overall performance.
Transport Secretary Asad Zamin, TransKarachi CEO Zubair Channa, Yellow Line BRT Project Director Kamal Dayo and Sindh Mass Transit Authority Managing Director Behzad Memon accompanied him.
Memon said it was important to connect the Green Line with other BRT projects. The Red and Yellow lines were also being linked, with plans to connect the Orange Line to the Green Line, the Green Line to the Red Line, and the Yellow Line to the Red Line. The links would make it easier for passengers to transfer between services and reach their destinations.
He added that work was continuing on sections of the Yellow Line, including bridges and other construction, further saying that the Sindh government aimed to complete the projects as soon as possible and establish effective connections between them, creating an integrated and modern transport network in the metropolis.
Memon said that Sindh had made significant progress in public transport over the past four to five years, including electric scooters, Pakistan’s first electric buses and Pink Buses for women.
He said the Green Line had been built before Sindh assumed responsibility for it, but it had not included buses reserved for women. Women faced difficulties when using public transport, he said, and better travel facilities could encourage them to travel and help parents feel satisfied about sending their daughters out for education and work. He said the Sindh government had taken several steps to empower women and improve their access to transport.
Asked about Green Line ridership, Memon said that when the service was under the federal government, it carried around 50,000 passengers a day, further noting that since Sindh took over the transport department had worked to improve its performance and the service now carried around 90,000 passengers daily.
The senior minister said the Sindh government aimed to begin road construction in every district across the province within the next six to eight months to improve travel facilities.

Memon said that in Sindh, the government had worked with the Rangers and other law-enforcement agencies to tackle terrorism in Karachi. When conditions worsened in the riverine areas, the government and relevant agencies also conducted operations against bandits. He said kidnapping-for-ransom incidents in Sindh had since declined significantly.
Recalling Karachi’s past, the senior minister said the city had once seen 30 to 40 people killed each day, frequent strikes, closures of businesses and educational institutions, and industries relocating elsewhere. Memon said cooperation between the government and the establishment had helped restore peace, adding that Karachi no longer faced daily strikes on the same scale, and terrorist incidents had declined.
Memon recalled the bombing at the October 18, 2007 homecoming rally for former prime minister Benazir Bhutto, in which hundreds of PPP supporters were killed or injured, and her assassination in Rawalpindi later that year. He said the party’s position against terrorism had always been clear.
He said Benazir had pledged in her final speeches that Pakistan’s flag would again fly in Swat, where Taliban and extremist groups had expanded their influence.
Memon reiterated that the PPP would not remain silent when citizens were suffering from terrorism, innocent people were being killed, and businesses were operating in fear.
He described the recent visit to China as successful and said the chief minister would brief the provincial cabinet on it, further stating that the visit aimed to identify opportunities to benefit Pakistan, particularly Sindh and its people.
Memon said the Sindh government was working democratically across sectors, including health, education, transport, irrigation and local government, to improve people’s lives.

title: Colombia s Jerusalem embassy move draws ire
description: Colombia s Jerusalem embassy move draws ire
content:
Pakistan and 18 other countries have condemned Colombia's inauguration of its embassy in Jerusalem, saying any move to recognise the city as Israel's capital was "null and void" and had no legal effect, according to a Foreign Office (FO) statement issued on Friday.
According to the FO, the joint statement was issued by the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Algeria, Djibouti, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Malaysia, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Syria, Sudan, Turkiye and Yemen.
In a joint statement, the foreign ministers expressed their "unequivocal rejection" of the move, saying it contravened relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions and undermined international efforts to achieve "a just and lasting peace based on the two-State solution".
The ministers said their position was consistent with relevant UN Security Council and General Assembly resolutions, particularly Security Council Resolutions 476 and 478, adopted in 1980.
The resolutions rejected attempts to change Jerusalem's character or status and called on states to withdraw diplomatic missions from the city, which the statement said was part of the Palestinian territory occupied in 1967.
The ministers called on the Colombian government to "reconsider and reverse this decision", uphold its obligations under international law and refrain from measures that "prejudice the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people".
They reaffirmed the Palestinians' right to "an independent and sovereign Palestinian State with East Jerusalem as its capital".
The condemnation came two days after Colombia opened its embassy in Jerusalem on October 14, becoming the 10th country to establish a diplomatic mission in the city, Reuters reported.

title: LHC declares MDCAT paper retrieval illegal
description: LHC declares MDCAT paper retrieval illegal
content:
Extends stay on expulsion of Afghan medical students
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has declared the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council's (PMDC) decision to collect question papers from candidates after the recent Medical and Dental College Admission Test (MDCAT) illegal and unconstitutional, directing the council to immediately upload the papers to its official application.
Justice Ahsan Raza Kazmi allowed petitions challenging the policy, ruling that collecting question papers from candidates after they had completed the examination was unlawful. The court ordered the PMDC to make the papers available on its official app so that all candidates could access and review them.
The petitions were filed by two candidates, Anabia Tahir and Rehan Shahid. Their counsel, Barrister Imran Afrasiab, argued that candidates should be allowed to retain question papers after completing an examination, adding that this was the established practice worldwide.
He contended that students were entitled to question papers after examinations, including those conducted by schools, colleges and universities, and that examination authorities could not forcibly retrieve them once candidates had been allowed to use them.
Afrasiab said the PMDC had unilaterally introduced the policy this year, requiring candidates to return their question papers along with their answer sheets immediately after the examination. He challenged the move as illegal.
Federal government counsel Malik Zaheer Arshad partially supported the petitioners' position, while the PMDC's lawyer defended the council's decision and urged the court to dismiss the petitions.
After hearing the arguments, the court declared the practice illegal and directed the PMDC to upload the question papers to its official application without delay, enabling candidates to access and study them. The court also ordered immediate implementation of its decision.
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has extended its interim order restraining all medical colleges in Punjab from expelling Afghan students in view of a controversial Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) notification.
Justice Khalid Ishaq on Friday heard petitions filed by more than 30 Afghan students against their expulsion from medical colleges.
During the hearing, the PMDC's counsel sought an adjournment. The court accepted the request, postponed further proceedings, and extended the interim relief granted to the petitioners.
The petitioners submitted that they had secured admission to medical colleges under the Afghan refugees' quota. They maintained that they had gained admission on merit.
In a notification dated September 1, the PMDC ordered medical colleges in Punjab to ask Afghan medical and dental students to complete official formalities for their return to Afghanistan while also suspending future admissions, transfers and migration involving Afghan nationals.
The LHC on September 11 restrained all medical colleges in Punjab from expelling Afghan medical students.

title: SPI stays in double digits on costly fuel
description: SPI stays in double digits on costly fuel
content:
Short-term inflation holds above 11% YoY, driven by energy shock from regional war
Pakistan's short-term inflation remained in double digits at 11.38% year-on-year for the week ended October 15, 2026 as the fallout from the Middle East conflict continued to keep energy prices elevated, according to data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS).
The Sensitive Price Indicator (SPI), which tracks 51 essential items from 50 markets in 17 cities, edged down 0.04% week-on-week. The combined index stood at 372.43 against 372.58 a week earlier and 334.39 in the corresponding week of last year.
The year-on-year reading has stayed above 10% for several consecutive weeks, driven mainly by sharp increases in fuel and related costs linked to the US-Iran war, disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi attacks affecting regional supply routes. Petrol was 49.60% higher than a year earlier, diesel rose 43.98% and LPG jumped 68.95%. Electricity charges for Q1 were up 58.59%.
Among food items, onions recorded the steepest annual increase of 75.19%, followed by wheat flour (35.13%) and chicken (20.77%). Mutton rose 14.90% and beef 12.27%. On the other hand, tomatoes were 63.65% cheaper year-on-year, potatoes fell 39.93%, sugar declined 23.20% and eggs were down 19.83%.
On a weekly basis, prices of 23 items (45.10%) increased, seven items (13.72%) decreased and 21 items (41.18%) remained unchanged. The biggest weekly drops came in tomatoes (23.05%), onions (4.90%), bananas (2.59%) and petrol (0.70%). Sugar and gur also eased slightly.
Weekly gains were led by gram pulse (4.97%), wheat flour (3.36%) and chicken (3.31%). Eggs, mash pulse, masoor pulse, firewood and diesel also registered modest increases.
Across consumption quintiles, the week-on-week decline ranged from 0.01% to 0.06%. The lowest expenditure group (Q1) saw a 0.06% weekly drop and an 8.19% year-on-year rise, while the highest group (Q5) recorded a 12.09% annual increase.
The SPI serves as a key short-term gauge of price pressures faced by households. Elevated energy costs continue to feed into transport, production and food prices, keeping inflationary pressures intact despite the modest weekly easing.

title: Chinese investors see opportunity but local businesses struggle
description: Chinese investors see opportunity but local businesses struggle
content:
Delegation shows interest in setting up Chinese pavilion, electric bus and truck manufacturing
Chinese companies are planning new investments in Pakistan, especially in Punjab's electric vehicle, information technology and tourism sectors, at a time when many Pakistani businesses report weak sales, high costs and an uncertain outlook. The contrast raises a question for the local industry; what do foreign investors, especially Chinese, see that domestic firms either cannot see or cannot act on?
On October 16, a 20-member delegation of the Pakistan-China Business Forum met Punjab's Minister for Industries and Commerce Chaudhry Shafay Hussain. The delegation included officials of Chinese companies working in EVs, IT, tourism and agriculture.
Wei Linzhui, Director of the Forum's Beijing Office, said the group wanted to showcase Chinese products in Punjab. "We want to build a China pavilion on 100 kanals of land," he said, adding that investors would set up assembly and manufacturing plants for electric buses and trucks, and companies were ready to invest in the IT sector. The forum is also studying the possibility of setting up an IT university in Gujrat.
This is not the first delegation that has met the provincial minister. Many such groups have already announced new investments in different sectors, most of which have already materialised. Provincial Minister Hussain said the government would provide the land for the pavilion. He said chip frame manufacturing was about to begin in Punjab for the first time in the country and the Faisalabad plant of Chinese phone maker was in final stages of completion.
Many electric bike plants have been opened in the province over the past year and plot prices in industrial hubs have been reduced. A community centre for foreign investors is being built in the Faisalabad Special Economic Zone (SEZ) and a 50-acre Expo Centre is planned there, with construction due to begin later this year. The minister described China's progress as a "role model" for Pakistan, adding that Chinese investment was promoting technology transfer.
He said Chinese companies had made new investments worth hundreds of thousands of dollars in Punjab over the past two and a half years. The figure is modest compared with earlier Chinese commitments, which suggests the current interest is still at an early stage.
Chinese involvement in Pakistan's economy is not new. The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), launched in 2015, was initially valued at about $46 billion and headline figures later rose to $62 billion. Most completed projects are related to power generation, roads and Gwadar Port. China is one of Pakistan's largest bilateral creditors.
Such investments from China arrive despite security risks. Analysts point to several reasons for continuous capital inflows. Many Chinese manufacturers face crowded home markets and are expanding into Africa, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Latin America, not only in South Asia. Pakistan offers a population of about 240 million and demand for affordable vehicles, phones and electronics. EVs also align with Pakistan's efforts to reduce its oil import bill.
Chinese firms often have access to state-linked financing and established supply chains. Pakistani businesses operate under different conditions. Borrowing costs stayed high for much of the past three years, energy tariffs rose sharply, and taxes and import restrictions have squeezed margins. Pakistani entrepreneurs must also compete with multinationals and Chinese giants that have deeper capital and can absorb losses while building market share. Some foreign firms also benefit from tax and tariff incentives in SEZs.
A Lahore-based businessman, who asked not to be named, said local firms should not be dismissed as risk-averse; the field was actually uneven. "Chinese companies are not investing in Pakistan out of special affection. They invest everywhere, in Africa, Central Asia and Latin America, because their home market is saturated and their government backs expansion abroad," he said. "They arrive with cheap finance, long-term plans and facilities we never get. With the same tax breaks and access to credit, many local firms will invest too and may give a tough time to our neighbouring competitors."
Provincial governments are competing for this capital. Punjab is offering land, lower plot prices and SEZ facilities, while Sindh has also sought Chinese participation, particularly in energy and industries around Karachi.

title: Govt seeks US investment in minerals
description: Govt seeks US investment in minerals
content:
To attract foreign investors, PMIF26 being organised in mid-November
With plans underway to encourage the United States to invest in the mineral-rich Balochistan province, the government is going to organise the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum (PMIF) on November 12-13.
PMIF26 was originally scheduled to be held on April 8-9 in Islamabad but was rescheduled. During the last event, the US and its allies dominated the conference while Chinese participation was not much prominent. Later, a separate event was held for Chinese investors.
So far, no US company is operating in Balochistan but Pakistan is now urging Washington to lead investment in Balochistan's minerals despite security risks. Earlier, a Canadian firm delayed work on the Reko Diq copper and gold mining project due to the beginning of US-Iran war.
The last year's edition of the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum attracted 5,000 delegates from more than 50 countries. The event saw the signing of 16 memoranda of understanding (MoUs) and featured 18 panel discussions. For the upcoming event, Pakistan is desperately looking towards the US to invest in mineral resources in Balochistan.
Export-Import Bank of the US has already approved $1.25 billion in December 2025, which the US embassy said could unlock up to $2 billion in American mining equipment and services exports and support roughly 13,500 jobs in both countries. Reko Diq's first-year shipments, once operational, are projected to generate $2.8 billion in exports.
On September 8, 2025, Pakistan's Frontier Works Organisation and Missouri-based US Strategic Metals (USSM) signed two MoUs focusing on the development and processing of critical minerals, including rare-earth elements, and logistics services. The agreements establish a framework for collaboration in scores of critical minerals essential for defence, aerospace and technology industries.
According to the Prime Minister's Office, the partnership will begin immediately with the export of readily available minerals from Pakistan, including antimony, copper, gold, tungsten and rare-earth elements. This lays the foundation for scaling up towards establishing a USSM's highly flexible poly-metallic refinery in Pakistan.
The refinery will produce intermediate and finished products to meet the rapidly growing demand in the US market. The first phase is envisaged to result in an investment of $500 million in critical minerals. Next steps include forming dedicated teams to explore the full potential of Pakistan's vast resource base, identifying critical minerals for immediate export and building a strong base for long-term partnership in exploration, extraction and processing. Importantly, their cooperation will prioritise sustainability, profitability and environmental responsibility to ensure benefits for the people of both nations.
Pakistan's mineral reserves are estimated at around $8 trillion and spread over 600,000 square kilometres, according to the Institute of Cost and Management Accountants (ICMA). The vast mineral resources highlight the massive economic potential of the mining sector. The sector has historically contributed less than 3% to the gross domestic product (GDP), ICMA said. With strong governance and security, annual mineral exports could rise from about $3 billion to $8 billion and GDP growth could climb from roughly 3% to 6%.
The challenge, however, is to turn the geological potential into bankable projects, exports, jobs and industrial capacity. This requires more than mining and greater focus on exploration, geological data, modern technology, infrastructure, financing, predictable regulation, environmental safeguards and partnerships with international companies. Pakistan's policy direction is increasingly focused on building that ecosystem.
Reko Diq, located in Balochistan's Chagai district, has one of the world's largest undeveloped copper and gold deposits. The project is a joint venture between Barrick Mining, which holds a 50% stake, the Balochistan government with 25% shareholding and three federal state-owned enterprises having 25% interest. In February 2025, Barrick announced completion of the updated feasibility study for the project. Reko Diq will be a major contributor to Pakistan's economy and is also expected to have a transformative impact on Balochistan.
The updated study estimates a 37-year mine life, with total capital investment of $8.83 billion. The project will be developed in two phases, where phase-I requires around $5.6-$6 billion. Production is expected to begin by the end of 2028.
In phase-I, the project will process 45 million tonnes of ore annually, producing about 240,000 tonnes of copper and 297,000 ounces of gold. Phase-II, planned for 2034, will double the processing capacity to 90 million tonnes per year, raising average annual production to 460,000 tonnes of copper and 520,000 ounces of gold for first 10 years.
According to the feasibility study, Reko Diq has probable mineral reserves of around 3 billion tonnes, containing an estimated 15 million tonnes of copper and 26 million ounces of gold. Barrick estimates the project could generate $90 billion in operating cash flow and $70 billion in free cash flow over its mine life. Reko Diq is the largest foreign direct investment (FDI) project in Balochistan.
International lenders have assembled a financing package exceeding $2.6 billion. The Asian Development Bank approved $410 million in August 2025 – $300 million in loans and a $110 million guarantee for Balochistan's equity stake. The International Finance Corporation and World Bank approved a $700 million concessional loan in June 2025.
Global copper demand is forecast to grow 24% to reach 42.7 million tonnes a year by 2035, driven by electrification, according to Wood Mackenzie. The International Energy Agency has said electricity demand from AI-driven data centres will accelerate this further.

title: Govt  MNCs in deadlock over PET bottle ban
description: Govt  MNCs in deadlock over PET bottle ban
content:
Talks remain inconclusive as industry warns of Rs10b revenue loss, cites no legal basis
The government and multinational companies (MNCs) failed to break a gridlock over a sudden ban on the use of recyclable bottles by the food and beverages industry, driven by the authorities' desire to present Islamabad as a plastic-free city at the upcoming Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit.
A meeting this week between Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry, whose subordinate department initiated the action, and representatives of Nestlé, Coca-Cola, PepsiCo and Metro remained inconclusive, according to people privy to the discussions.
The companies were of the view that there was no legal ban on the use of recyclable plastic, and that the existing ban was justified. Their stance has also been supported by the Pakistan Environmental Protection Agency (Pak-EPA), whose director has publicly stated that existing regulations do not ban PET (polyethylene terephthalate) bottles.
Dr Zaigham Abbas, an official of the federal agency, reportedly said there was no legal basis for removing PET bottles from sale. He said the clarification has been conveyed to the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) administration.
However, despite these explanations, including international examples, details of existing recycling practices and the industry's position that no commercially viable substitute is currently available at the required scale, the government continued to emphasise the need to explore alternative packaging solutions, particularly glass bottles, according to industry representatives.
They said the sudden ban on PET bottles would also dent federal tax revenues by at least Rs10 billion, in addition to sending negative signals to international investors about the government itself violating environmental regulations.
Industry representatives said the government appeared determined to pursue its objective of presenting Islamabad as a plastic-free city ahead of the upcoming SCO summit. Despite the industry's explanations regarding the existing legal framework, established recycling practices and the lack of commercially viable alternatives at scale, the government remained focused on finding alternatives to plastic PET bottles, with glass packaging and paper solutions.
The summit is scheduled to take place next month, and the government plans to serve food and drinks in plastic-free material, the industry was told this week. But industry representatives said establishing a glass bottle factory would require significant investment and take at least two years.
The American Business Forum (ABF), the Overseas Investors Chamber of Commerce and Industry (OICCI) and the Collect and Recycle (CoRe) Alliance had also separately raised the issue with federal authorities. But so far there has been no breakthrough.
The ABF requested the withdrawal of the proposed ban on PET bottles and the effective enforcement of the ICT Single-Use Plastics Regulations, 2023, in an appeal to the minister for interior.
Officials said the minister of state for interior acknowledged that existing law contained relevant provisions but emphasised that Pakistan was scheduled to host the SCO summit in approximately 10 months. The government aims to present Islamabad as a plastic-free city during the event.
The minister's view could not be immediately obtained.
Industry representatives said the government was still urging all multinational companies to propose viable alternatives to plastic PET bottles.
They said another meeting will be held next week to discuss the matter in greater detail. They said there were indications the government may not take any negative action on retail until an expert meeting planned for next week.
The minister advised company representatives to prepare their respective cases thoroughly and come equipped with all relevant technical details, supporting evidence and expert input to substantiate their positions.
In an opinion piece published in The Express Tribune, the writer wrote that within days, a campaign against litter had become a campaign against lawful trade. The article stated that Islamabad does have a plastics law. The Single-Use Plastics (Prohibition) Regulations, 2023 were made by the Pak-EPA under the Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997.
They name PET in their definition of plastic, then ban six items: polythene bags, straws, plastic crockery, cutlery, food-service ware and stirrers. PET bottles are not on the list. Instead, from July 2028, beverage bottles must contain at least 50% recycled plastic. The choice was deliberate: PET is to be recycled, not banned.

Federal Minister for Economic Affairs and Pakistan's Governor to the World Bank Group (WBG) Ahad Khan Cheema sought continued WBG financing for the ML-1 railway project and the National Artificial Intelligence and Economic Development Programme during a meeting with WBG President Ajay Banga on the sidelines of the 2026 WBG-IMF Annual Meetings in Bangkok, according to a statement issued on Friday.

title: LSM stalls as steel  fertiliser slump
description: LSM stalls as steel  fertiliser slump
content:
Sequential decline of 4.96% as transport strike hits wearing apparel, auto taxes dampen sales
Large-Scale Manufacturing (LSM) output increased 0.67% in August 2026 compared with August 2025 but declined 4.96% compared with July 2026, according to provisional data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS).
The Quantum Index of Manufacturing (QIM) for August 2026 was estimated at 113.19, against 112.45 in August 2025 and 119.10 in July 2026.
Cumulatively, factory activity posted 1.85% growth during July-August 2026-27 compared with the same period last year, with the QIM reaching 116.14 against 114.03 in July-August 2025-26, pointing to a modest improvement in industrial output over the two-month period.
According to the PBS, production during July-August 2026-27 increased in tobacco, wearing apparel, wood products, coke and petroleum products, rubber products, non-metallic mineral products, fabricated metal, computer, electronics and optical products, electrical equipment, automobiles, other transport equipment and furniture. However, output declined in food, beverages, textiles and leather products.
LSM growth slowed in August due to elevated petroleum prices despite a significant jump in refinery production and continued growth in the automobile sector, AKD Securities Director Research Mohammed Awais Ashraf told The Express Tribune. "Sequential decline in wearing apparel due to transportation strike, and lower automobile sales due to increase in taxes and auto policy uncertainty led to decline on a sequential basis," he said.
Wearing apparel production increased 10.85% in August 2026 compared with August 2025 and registered growth of 16.69% during July-August 2026-27 compared with the corresponding period of the previous year.
Coke and petroleum products recorded an increase of 31.85% in August compared with the same month last year. Production in the sector grew 15.48% during July-August 2026-27.
Automobile production increased 11.66% in August 2026. The sector posted growth of 32.45% during July-August 2026-27 compared with the same period last year.
Cotton yarn production increased 1.46% in August and grew 2.09% during July-August 2026-27. Cotton cloth production recorded an increase of 0.04% in August, while output during the two-month period declined 0.03%.
In contrast, fertiliser production declined 9.00% in August. The sector recorded a decrease of 7.55% during July-August 2026-27. Iron and steel production fell 11.56% in August, and output declined 11.48% during the first two months of the current fiscal year. Cement production decreased 3.52% in August 2026, though the sector recorded growth of 1.26% during July-August 2026-27.
Information technology (IT) exports reached $435 million in September 2026, up 18% year-on-year and 10% month-on-month, the second-highest monthly level on record, just shy of an all-time peak. First-quarter exports for FY27 totalled $1.25 billion, registering growth of around 18% year-on-year.
Adviser to the Finance Minister Khurram Schehzad noted on X that the momentum reflected targeted incentives in the FY27 budget for the export sector, particularly IT, alongside a strengthening digital economy. He said these were supporting exports, non-debt foreign exchange earnings, high-value jobs and Pakistan's integration with global markets.
According to Topline Securities, the monthly figure was a nine-month high, up 19% year-on-year. IT exports during 1QFY27 stood at $1.25 billion, while the trailing 12-month value reached $4.8 billion, reflecting 20% year-on-year growth from $4.0 billion in the corresponding period last year.

title: BoP swings to  4 39b deficit
description: BoP swings to  4 39b deficit
content:
Portfolio investment records $2.93b net inflow against $631m outflow last year
The overall balance of payments (BoP) swung to a deficit of $4.39 billion in September, compared with $118 million in August, as the current account deficit widened to $356 million from $73 million, according to State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) data.
For July-September, the BoP recorded a deficit of $3.12 billion, against a surplus of $274 million in the corresponding period last year. The figures highlight the growing gap between Pakistan's foreign exchange earnings and payments, with the merchandise trade deficit remaining the largest component of the goods and services trade imbalance.
Pakistan's goods trade deficit widened 21.1% to $9.33 billion in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27 as imports grew nearly twice as fast as exports, highlighting mounting pressure on the external account despite a recovery in merchandise exports in September.
Goods imports increased 14.3% to $17.78 billion during July-September, compared with $15.56 billion in the same period last year. Goods exports rose 7.7% to $8.45 billion from $7.85 billion. The widening trade gap contributed to a deterioration in the current account, which recorded a deficit of $874 million during the first quarter, compared with $755 million a year earlier.
Goods exports increased 15.5% year-on-year to $3.02 billion in September, reversing a 1.5% decline recorded in August. However, imports grew faster, rising 22.7% to $6.17 billion from $5.03 billion a year earlier. Consequently, the monthly goods trade deficit widened to $3.16 billion in September from $2.42 billion a year earlier. The contrasting growth rates suggest the recovery in exports has yet to keep pace with the expansion in import payments.
Pakistan's services exports increased 22.8% to $2.72 billion in the first quarter, compared with $2.21 billion a year earlier. Telecommunications, computer and information services remained a major contributor, generating $1.25 billion during July-September, up from $1.06 billion in the same period last year. Other business services exports rose to $622 million from $486 million, while travel services exports increased to $322 million from $157 million. Services imports, however, also increased to $3.55 billion from $3.05 billion. The resulting services trade deficit narrowed slightly to $831 million from $840 million a year earlier.
Workers' remittances rose 14% to $10.88 billion during the first quarter, compared with $9.54 billion in the corresponding period last year, providing an important source of foreign exchange. However, monthly remittances declined to $3.59 billion in September from $3.66 billion in August, a decrease of around 1.9%.
The secondary income balance, which includes remittances and other current transfers, reached $11.61 billion during July-September, compared with $10.06 billion a year earlier. Despite these inflows, the current account remained in deficit as the combined goods, services and primary income balance deteriorated.
Pakistan's primary income deficit widened slightly to $2.32 billion during the first quarter from $2.27 billion a year earlier. Primary income payments reached $2.56 billion, compared with credits of $244 million, reflecting the continued imbalance between income paid abroad and income received from overseas. The primary income account includes cross-border income flows such as investment income and compensation of employees.
Foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows into Pakistan increased to $720 million during the first quarter, up 20% from $600 million in the same period last year. However, monthly FDI inflows slowed to $219 million in September from $322 million in August.
Portfolio investment recorded a net inflow of approximately $2.93 billion into Pakistan during July-September, compared with a net outflow of $631 million a year earlier. The September figure included a $2.87 billion net portfolio inflow, largely reflected in debt securities. Despite these investment flows, the financial account recorded a net outflow of $4.16 billion during the first quarter, compared with $726 million in the corresponding period last year.
The SBP's balance of payments table reported gross foreign exchange reserves, including cash foreign currency holdings and excluding unsettled claims on the Reserve Bank of India, at $22.88 billion in September, compared with $18.49 billion in August. The central bank's reserve-assets measure recorded an increase of $4.38 billion in September, while the overall balance of payments showed a deficit of $4.39 billion.
Furthermore, the Pakistani rupee edged up Rs0.01 against the US dollar on Friday, closing at 276.91 in the inter-bank market, compared with 276.92 on Thursday. Internationally, the dollar was heading for its first weekly decline in five weeks as concerns over artificial intelligence investment and falling US yields lifted the euro from a 17-month low.
Meanwhile, gold prices in Pakistan rose by Rs2,800 per tola on Friday to reach Rs440,636, tracking gains in the international market, according to the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association (APGJSA). The price of 10-gramme gold increased by Rs2,401 to Rs377,774. On Thursday, gold had remained unchanged at Rs437,836 per tola. In the international market, gold gained $28 to reach $4,181 per ounce. Meanwhile, silver prices climbed by Rs108 to a record high of Rs6,256 per tola.

title: Liaquat Ali Khan s legacy recalled at PNCA

content:
Minister calls for preserving national heroes' contributions for future generations
Federal Minister for National Heritage and Culture Aurangzeb Khan Khichi on Friday underscored the need to familiarise younger generations with Pakistan's history and the sacrifices and services of its national heroes, describing this as a key priority of the National Heritage and Culture Division.
He expressed these views while inaugurating a photographic exhibition at the Pakistan National Council of the Arts (PNCA) to mark the 75th death anniversary of Shaheed-e-Millat Liaquat Ali Khan, Pakistan's first Prime Minister and one of the country's prominent founding leaders. Samia Liaquat Ali Khan, his great-granddaughter, attended the event as guest of honour.
The federal minister appreciated the initiative, observing that such exhibitions helped preserve the memory of national leaders and highlight their contributions to Pakistan's history.
He said institutions operating under the National Heritage and Culture Division were organising activities to raise awareness of the lives, services and sacrifices of prominent national figures. He also commended Secretary of the National Heritage and Culture Division Asad Rehman Gilani for promoting such initiatives.
Khichi said exhibitions of this nature reminded the nation of the sacrifices made by its forefathers and provided an opportunity to renew its commitment to following in their footsteps for Pakistan's progress and prosperity.
He added that efforts would be made to invite students and young people from Islamabad and Rawalpindi to visit the exhibition, enabling them to learn more about the country's history, national leaders and the struggle for Pakistan.
Reaffirming the division's commitment to preserving the legacy of national heroes, the minister said their contributions must be passed on to future generations to inspire young people to play their part in national development.
Speaking on the occasion, Samia Liaquat Ali Khan applauded the organisation of the photographic exhibition in memory of Shaheed-e-Millat and thanked the federal minister and the secretary for their efforts.
Recounting her family's memories, she described Liaquat Ali Khan's assassination as the greatest tragedy of her life.

title: Daducha Dam s final stretch faces hurdles
description: Daducha Dam s final stretch faces hurdles
content:
Disputes continue to threaten timely delivery of the long-awaited project
The timely completion of the Daducha Dam project has assumed greater importance amid the growing water shortage in Rawalpindi.
The project has remained delayed despite 24 years having passed, but officials say construction work is now 92 per cent complete.
Construction began in September 2024, and a deadline of Dec 31, 2026, has been set for completion.
However, work on the transmission line, treatment plant, filtration plant and distribution network has yet to begin.
Rawalpindi Commissioner Salman Ghani visited the dam and directed the authorities to complete the remaining work within the stipulated timeframe.
Rawalpindi faces a daily water shortage of 21 million gallons, with demand standing at 72 million gallons per day against a supply of just 51 million gallons.
The Daducha Dam project is designed to supply 35 million gallons of water daily.
Of this, 15 million gallons will be provided to the Water and Sanitation Agency (Wasa), while a formula for distributing the remaining 20 million gallons between the cantonment board and a private housing society has yet to be finalised.
Progress on the treatment plant, filtration plant and supply network will be possible once the water distribution issue is resolved.
These components are estimated to cost a total of Rs36 billion.
The project's initial estimated cost was Rs6.49 billion, which has since increased to approximately Rs15 billion. Political changes, land disputes and court proceedings have contributed to the delays.
The dam will have a water storage capacity of 60,000 acre-feet. It will stand 123 feet high and extend 737 feet in length. According to officials, work on stone pitching, the spillway, retaining wall, bridge and other construction components is under way.
However, completion of the dam alone will not ensure water supply, as the treatment plant and transmission line must also be completed.

content:

The Punjab Development Working Party (PDWP) has approved the third revised PC-I of the Rawalpindi Ring Road project, raising its estimated cost to Rs50.4 billion.

Construction of the Ring Road route under Group-I has been completed, while work on the tolling booth system under Group-II is under way. Construction of the 38.3-kilometre route and four interchanges - GT Road Banth, Chakbeli Khan, Adiala and Chakri - has been completed in the project, which had remained pending for around 15 years.
The PDWP approved the third revised PC-I, worth Rs50.4 billion, at a meeting held in Lahore on October 12 under the chairmanship of the chairman of the Punjab Planning and Development Board.
The project's original PC-I was valued at Rs26.9 billion. The cost subsequently rose to Rs32.9 billion under the first revised PC-I and Rs46.4 billion under the second revised PC-I. The third revised PC-I has now been approved at Rs50.4 billion. Meanwhile, the tolling system under Group-II has been transferred from One Network Company to the Punjab Ring Road Authority (PRRA), which will now be responsible for its operation and maintenance.

title: Hina Javed s family rejects CCD probe
description: Hina Javed s family rejects CCD probe
content:
Accuses sleuths of favouring husband, says DNA findings require further scrutiny
The family of 45-year-old digital designer Hina Javed, who was murdered in the jurisdiction of the Civil Lines police station, has expressed complete distrust in both the Crime Control Department (CCD) and the local police and decided to file a private complaint, also described as a judicial FIR, before a local magistrate next week.
The family has obtained the relevant case record, including the FIR and details of the investigations conducted by the police and the CCD, for submission with the complaint.
The private complaint will name Hina Javed's husband, Faisal Asghar, as the principal accused, while her father-in-law, Asghar, and domestic worker Zeeshan Arshad will also be nominated as key co-accused.
Fahad Javed, the victim's brother and complainant in the case, has described the high-powered committee formed by the Punjab government under the leadership of CCD chief Sohail Zafar Chattha as completely biased.
The family alleged that efforts were being made to divert the investigation and protect Faisal Asghar by declaring him innocent and preparing to submit a challan to the court.
According to the family, DNA findings have linked the husband to three locations or items connected with the case. They said his fingerprints were found on the sheet allegedly used to strangle Hina Javed and on the latch of the room in which she was confined.
The family also questioned why the husband had allegedly remained silent if the domestic worker was committing the murder, and why he had fastened the room's latch.
A summary of the DNA report in the murder case has also revealed findings concerning biological samples collected during the investigation.
According to the summary, male reproductive cells recovered from the victim's body matched the DNA profile of the arrested domestic worker, Zeeshan Arshad. The victim's nail samples also matched his DNA, while samples collected from several objects at the crime scene reportedly contained his DNA as well.
Sources suspected that Hina Javed may have been sexually assaulted after being murdered. The samples of the victim's husband, domestic worker and father-in-law were analysed as part of the investigation.
The summary also stated that DNA attributed to Faisal Asghar was found on a broken lock, the internal latch of the room and a portion of the sheet recovered at Zeeshan Arshad's identification.

title: Ambani s Reliance breaks silence on Musk  says Jio awaits same clearances as Starlink
description: Says it welcomes competition after Musk accuses Ambani of blocking Starlink   s India launch
content:
Says it welcomes competition after Musk accuses Ambani of blocking Starlink’s India launch
Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance said it welcomed competition from Elon Musk's Starlink and that its own satellite services were also ‌awaiting clearance, its first response to ‌accusations that ​Ambani was blocking Starlink's India launch.
Musk, the world's richest man, ​has repeatedly accused the Indian government ‌and Ambani of stalling Starlink's ​years-long efforts to launch in a market of more than a billion internet subscribers. India has denied any bias in its approval process.
The Friday statement, which did not name ⁠Musk, comes days before Reliance Industries' digital unit Jio Platforms seeks a $108 billion valuation in India's ‌largest IPO to date.
Read : Musk steps up attack on Ambani, shares reports on Reliance-linked BJP donations
Jio houses Reliance's telecom arm, which has over 530 million customers and is a potential competitor to Starlink in India's internet market.
"At Reliance, we have never feared competition," the conglomerate said ⁠on Friday, addressing "remarks about Reliance and the Indian market" in ⁠a statement it ​said was intended ‌to "place the facts on record".
Starlink responded on Friday, saying it had worked with Indian regulators and the industry for more than five years and had built dedicated systems, gateways and other infrastructure in the country with the required government approvals.
"Starlink is ready to connect India with high-speed internet," the company said on X.
In a separate post responding to Reliance, Musk said: "Much appreciated".
India’s long wait for satellite internet
Musk's posts on X have ranged from asking whether Ambani was the "real boss" of India to addressing ⁠him as "Prime Minister Ambani" and asking whether he would allow Starlink to compete.
The attacks mark a sharp turn for Musk, who has a warm public rapport with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and come as New Delhi courts foreign investment and negotiates a trade deal with Washington.
Also Read : Influential Hindu group urges India to block Starlink amid Musk-Ambani feud
India has licensed Starlink, Jio's satellite internet arm, and Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb to operate services, but none has the security clearance needed to launch.
Satellite broadband could help ⁠to connect hundreds of millions of Indians who remain offline, mostly ​in rural and remote areas.
Musk has said he would price Starlink affordably in India to take on Jio's low-cost internet plans.
Cheap data is how Jio built its presence in India, and Musk has used the same strategy in markets like Kenya to ​disrupt local telecom players.

title: Museum revives Lyallpur s colonial era history
description: Museum revives Lyallpur s colonial era history
content:
Recreated 1896 office of first colonisation officer Captain Popham Young
The Lyallpur Museum has recreated the office of Captain Popham Young, the first colonisation officer of Tehsil Lyallpur, as part of an initiative to preserve the city's historical heritage and familiarise younger generations with its administrative, social and economic evolution.
The historical corner, established in the museum's first gallery, was inaugurated by Sri Lankan High Commissioner Rear Admiral Fred Senevirathne and Faisalabad Commissioner Imran Hamid Sheikh.
Officers of the divisional and district administrations were also present.The high commissioner and his team were briefed on the renovation and design of the recreated office, which features official items associated with the period, including an old photocopier, calculator and other objects reflecting the administrative environment of the late 19th century.
Senevirathne appreciated the initiative, describing it as an important step towards reviving the pre-partition history of the subcontinent and sensitising future generations to the region's rich historical background.
He also expressed a desire to revisit the museum for a more detailed tour.
On the occasion, the commissioner presented the high commissioner with a model of Faisalabad's historic Clock Tower.
Speaking to the media, Sheikh said the initiative was significant in reconnecting residents with the history, culture and heritage of their city. He said Tehsil Lyallpur was established in 1896, while Lyallpur was granted district status in 1904.
Before becoming a district, the area had been part of Jhang District and had developed as an administrative centre during the British colonial period.
He said Captain Popham Young, the first colonisation and settlement officer, was associated with the early development of Lyallpur, while Sir Ganga Ram also contributed to its urban planning. The original plan included the Clock Tower, eight bazaars and surrounding residential areas.
The commissioner said the recreated office aimed to give visitors an insight into the administrative system of the time. He invited residents to visit the gallery, adding that the setting had been designed to give them a sense of stepping back into 1896. Lyallpur Museum Coordinator Shahnaz Mehmood said four historical maps of the city had previously been displayed in the first gallery.

The EPA has directed its field formations and concerned departments to ensure strict implementation of the ban and take action against those found burning waste in streets, roadsides, vacant plots, markets and other open areas.
Open burning of mixed waste produces thick smoke and fine particulate matter that can significantly worsen air quality and contribute to smog.
EPA Director General Abdullah Nayyar Sheikh stressed the need for a more aggressive and preventive approach to curbing pollution, with authorities required to stop waste burning rather than merely responding after smoke incidents occur.
The department has called for coordinated action by local administrations, municipal authorities and other relevant agencies to ensure timely collection and proper disposal of waste. Officials have also been directed to keep a close watch on areas where open dumping and waste burning are commonly reported.
Authorities are particularly focusing on eliminating avoidable sources of pollution ahead of periods when stagnant atmospheric conditions can trap pollutants over urban areas.
The department urged the public, businesses and local authorities to avoid burning waste and instead use proper waste collection and disposal arrangements.

title: Peshawar mourns school roof collapse victims

content:
UN team visits site as bereaved families seek answers
Peshawar remained gripped by grief for the second consecutive day on Friday following the devastating roof collapse at a school in Dir Colony while political leaders, government officials and other prominent figures continued visiting the site and meeting bereaved families.
A United Nations delegation also visited the affected school to examine its infrastructure and assess the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. The team met relatives of the deceased children during its visit.
The secretary of the Private Schools Regulatory Authority briefed the UN delegation on the incident and provided details about the school and its infrastructure.
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, Federal Minister Amir Muqam, advisers to various departments and other political leaders and government officials also visited the affected families to offer their condolences.
Although inquiry committees have been constituted to investigate the incident, the relevant departments had yet to visit the site to begin their investigations, according to the available information.
The tragedy has left several families devastated, with some losing more than one child in the collapse.
Zakirullah, a father who lost both his sons, Abu Bakr and Muhammad, said his three children, two boys and a girl, had been studying at the school since the beginning of their education.
He said his daughter informed him about the incident. When he reached the school, he found children buried beneath the debris, with rescue workers struggling to reach them.
"The scenes were unbearable, and everyone was distressed," he recalled.
His two sons, both second-grade students, were trapped under the rubble and could not initially be seen. Rescue workers shifted them to a hospital, where both children succumbed to their injuries.
Zakirullah, who serves as deputy khateeb at Peshawar Service Club and originally belongs to Dir, said the loss had left his family shattered.
Other families also recounted heartbreaking accounts of the incident. One child had reportedly been sent home to bring school fee money. By the time the child returned, the roof had collapsed.
According to accounts shared by children, the roof had been shaking when they moved around in the classroom. However, a teacher had reportedly reassured them that there was nothing to fear.
The incident also claimed the lives of three friends, Abdullah, Shayan and Muhammad, according to the account of one bereaved parent.
In another devastating loss, five children belonging to the family of Pir Muhammad also died in the collapse.
As the city continued to mourn the victims, families called for answers about the circumstances that led to the disaster. The planned investigations are expected to establish the cause of the collapse and determine whether any negligence or safety violations contributed to the tragedy.

Antonio Banderas joins Nicolas Cage in 'True Detective' season 5, with HBO's crime drama set in New York
Antonio Banderas has joined Nicolas Cage in season five of HBO's crime anthology series True Detective , adding another major name to the upcoming instalment. Production is scheduled to begin in 2027, with the new season set in Jamaica Bay, New York.
According to Deadline , Banderas will play Rai Garcia, while Cage will star as Henry Logan. Cage's involvement was confirmed at New York Comic-Con last week, following reports in 2025 that he was in talks to join the series.
Issa López, who created and led the fourth season, True Detective: Night Country , is returning as writer, director and showrunner for season five. Although plot details remain under wraps, López has hinted at connections between the upcoming season and the events of Night Country . She previously explained that the new instalment would feature a different story and new characters while retaining some important links to the Alaska-set season.
True Detective has explored different locations and casts throughout its run. The first season starred Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson and was set in Louisiana. Season two moved to California, featuring Colin Farrell, Rachel McAdams and Vince Vaughn, while the third season starred Mahershala Ali and Stephen Dorff in the Ozarks. The fourth season featured Jodie Foster and Kali Reis in Alaska.
HBO's head of drama series, Francesca Orsi, previously praised López's vision for the fifth season, describing its setting as different but equally powerful.
With Banderas and Cage leading the cast, True Detective season five is taking shape ahead of its planned 2027 production.

title: Sindh mulls raising university professors  retirement age to 65

content:
Sindh Chief Secretary Asif Hyder Shah has called for discouraging non-teaching recruitment at public universities to ease their mounting financial burden, as vice chancellors warned that private institutions were poaching experienced faculty with better salary packages.
The concerns were raised at a meeting chaired by Shah with VCs of 32 public universities across the province to review their financial and administrative challenges, academic standards, research activities, infrastructure and student facilities.
The meeting was attended by the chairman of the Sindh Higher Education Commission (SHEC), the secretary of universities and boards, VCs and other relevant officials.
Shah acknowledged the challenges facing public universities and said the provincial government wanted to work with university administrations to find practical solutions. He said the government was providing Rs44.46 billion in grants to Sindh's universities during the current financial year.
Pension liabilities, he said, had emerged as a major challenge for universities, prompting him to call for curtailing unnecessary recruitment, particularly in non-faculty positions, to reduce the financial burden.
The chief secretary said recommendations concerning university syndicates would be placed before the provincial cabinet. He added that the government would consider including people with backgrounds in education and higher education in university syndicates.
He also stressed the need to engage university alumni more effectively in institutional development and encouraged VCs to submit research proposals to the government for possible financial support.
While universities were undertaking research, Shah said, their findings needed proper accreditation and stronger links with industry to translate academic work into practical benefits. He urged institutions to establish closer ties with international universities and promote industry-oriented research.
On the establishment of new campuses, the chief secretary called for comprehensive research and feasibility studies before approving such projects. Universities should assess the potential student population and develop clear policy guidelines and benchmarks to ensure that new campuses were academically justified and financially sustainable, he said.
Shah also called for reducing electricity costs through solarisation and said a solarisation plan would be introduced for universities. He directed institutions to eliminate illegal electricity connections.
The chief secretary further said a summary proposing an increase in the retirement age of university professors from 60 to 65 years would be sent to the provincial cabinet. The government would also approach the federal authorities to address issues falling within their jurisdiction.
During the meeting, VCs highlighted the difficulties of retaining qualified and experienced faculty amid competition from private universities offering higher salaries.
They said the departure of teachers to foreign countries, coupled with the reluctance of some to return or their efforts to seek overseas opportunities again after returning, was disrupting faculty availability and continuity.
The VCs also cited pension liabilities and hefty electricity bills as major contributors to their financial strain, alongside shortages of faculty and other human resource challenges.

School owners and principals have also been directed to immediately notify the relevant directorate if their buildings are found to be dilapidated, damaged, structurally weak or otherwise hazardous. Academic activities in such buildings must be suspended without delay.

title: Hasina s repressive legacy and India conundrum
description: Hasina s repressive legacy and India conundrum
content:
Such postulations, nevertheless, can hardly disguise a bitter reality
Can I respond to this question over lunch in private?
This evasive, though light-veined, response by Dinesh Trivedi, the Indian High Commissioner, represented the catch 22 situation that both India and Bangladesh are trapped in over the issue of ex-PM Sheikh Hasina.
When pressed harder by several locals on Dhaka's request for Hasina's extradition, Trivedi referenced the "well-structured legal process currently underway in New Delhi" to extricate himself from the extremely uncomfortable situation during the recent Bay of Bengal Conversations 2026.
In a typical deflective way, the Indian envoy held the Bangladesh Army responsible for flying Hasina to India with an innocent qualification; as neighbours it was our duty to accept the situation on that day (August 5, 2024).
Such postulations, nevertheless, can hardly disguise a bitter reality; Bangladesh's political spectrum remains deeply divided over the fate of Sheikh Hasina. For many Bangladeshis, she must face justice for the murder and maiming of thousands of opposition activists, students during the July 2024 uprising. For them, Hasina's 15 year rule embodied brute repression and a foreign policy beholden to India at the cost of broader national interest.
Even the International Crimes Tribunal sentenced Hasina to death for crimes against humanity (on 17 November 2025). This verdict came on the back of raging public sentiment over the Hasina era.
Since Sheikh Hasina's 15-year era was marked by enforced disappearances (up to 4000, though figures vary), extrajudicial killings, arbitrary arrests, torture, politically motivated criminal cases and the use of administrative and legal mechanisms to marginalise and silence opposition parties, the younger generation seems unforgiving. The calls for bringing the former PM to justice resonate almost everywhere.
Between 2009 and 2024, the security establishment, intelligence agencies in particular, were used indiscriminately to abuse, harass and punish the political rivals. And hence the popular demand to hold her accountable.
Yet, for India, the former prime minister still counts as a "treasured guest" and hence New Delhi's nearly flat refusal to hand her over.
The issues also exposes limitations of any government in Dhaka; Bangladesh is almost surrounded by Indian territory, with the Bay of Bengal to its south and a short border with Myanmar to its southeast. Its land border with India extends roughly 4,096 kilometres. This makes India an unavoidable neighbour in Bangladesh's security, economic and diplomatic calculations – also called the "tyranny of geography" by Ali Riaz, a Bangladesh-origin Distinguished Professor at the University of Illinois.
Geography – a powerful structural factor – clearly imposes limits to Bangladesh's relations with India. No surprise that a recent speech Prime Minister Tarique Rahman delivered at the Bay of Bengal conference betrayed a deliberate shift towards diplomatic moderation, economic pragmatism and regional engagement. Though Rehman focused mostly on democratic transparency, accountability and indiscriminate rule of law, he did allude to the inevitability of normal relations with all neighbours.
That's why conscious transition from emotional vows of revenge to guarded rational positive messaging is clearly discernible in the government's narratives, possibly in view of the limits that inescapable geography and the Hasina legacy – deeply entrenched loyalists, supporters within civil-military hierarchies – place on the government.
Additionally, 15 years of Hasina's rule changed the institutional, political and economic landscape, and those networks, habits and loyalties cannot disappear with one electoral transition. At the same time, India's unusually close relationship with Hasina created a structural Indian stake in Bangladesh that complicates Rahman's effort to reform the state and redefine foreign policy.
While pursuing democratic ideals, Bangladesh also wants relations based on mutual respect and equality, Rehman underlined. The language of dialogue, partnership and mutual respect a clear signal, amplified also by Andaleeve Rahman, Rehman's information minister.
We are determined to take on the multitude of challenges that are upon our head and hence not interested in bloc politics. We want to stay clear of big power rivalries to be able to focus on internal economic development, improving governance and ensuring stability, the minister explained, in what appeared to be an indirect message to India.
Both the PM and the Information Minister as well as a number of Bangladeshi participants at the Bay of Bengal Conversation appeared to project their country as a pivotal access to maritime trade, regional supply chains and potentially more efficient transport links between India, Nepal, Bhutan and the Bay of Bengal.
Rahman's speech explicitly identified shipping, fisheries, tourism, energy and regional supply chains as areas of opportunity, without detailing the steps being taken to address the public anxiety over the injustice and oppression perpetrated under Hasina. Will he be able to deliver justice without turning accountability into another instrument of political revenge – as is the norm in South Asia and many African countries? This requires investigating disappearances, prosecuting those credibly implicated in abuses, providing redress to victims and ensuring fair trials regardless of political affiliation.
Rehman's predicament also shows that repression and autocratic regimes deeply scar the society, making it difficult for the victims and those at the receiving end to get over it. High-handed politics – rough treatment of the opposition, enforced disappearances, etc – subvert the rule of law to the extent that turns correction an arduous job – a double edged sword.
That is why the critical test that lies ahead for Rahman is whether he will be able to normalise relations with India on the one hand, and whether the pressing circumstances would allow him to break with the methods of the past or reproduce them under a different political leadership wrapped in a self-serving lingo.
