title: Karachi court acquits cocaine queen  Pinky  in two drug cases
description: Prosecution fails to produce sufficient evidence  prompting the court to accept the acquittal pleas
content:
Prosecution fails to produce sufficient evidence, prompting the court to accept the acquittal pleas
A district and sessions court in Karachi on Friday acquitted Anmol alias Pinky in two drug-related cases registered by the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and Gizri police, citing a lack of evidence.
In May, Karachi police arrested Pinky, accusing her of operating one of the city’s most organised narcotics supply networks. She was arrested during a joint operation conducted by city police and a civil agency at an apartment in the Garden area. Investigators claim she ran a sophisticated cocaine processing and delivery operation with links extending beyond Karachi to Lahore, Islamabad and other cities. Police also said cases were registered against Pinky at Gizri Police Station in 2020, 2021 and 2022, and she was a fugitive in the said cases. Later, on August 13, a sessions court acquitted the alleged cocaine queen in three cases.
The judge announced the verdicts on applications filed by Anmol seeking acquittal in cases involving alleged drug offences and facilitation registered with the CTD, as well as a separate drug case registered at Gizri Police Station.
Read: Karachi court acquits drug queenpin 'Pinky' in three cases
A case was registered against Anmol at the CTD police station in 2018. Her brother, Nasir, had already been acquitted in the case.
The cases were heard by the additional district and sessions judge (South), in whose court Anmol appeared via video link. During the hearing, the prosecution failed to produce sufficient evidence against her, prompting the court to accept her acquittal pleas.
In its order, the court directed that Pinky be released if she was not wanted in any other case.
With the latest verdicts, Pinky has now been acquitted in five cases. A total of 22 cases related to alleged drug peddling and other offences have been registered against Pinky at various police stations across Karachi.
Pinky was arrested on May 11, following the death of two prominent personalities allegedly caused by drug overdose. She came under intense public scrutiny, while the police faced criticism, after she was produced before a court with what appeared to be special protocol a day after her arrest.
According to the police, Pinky not only supplied narcotics to affluent neighbourhoods, including DHA and Clifton, but also personally prepared high-grade cocaine and managed deliveries through female riders and online platforms.

During interrogation, she allegedly claimed that “no one in Pakistan makes better cocaine” than her. Police said she sold two categories of cocaine — “White Coke” for Rs25,000 per gram and “Golden Category” cocaine for Rs40,000 per gram.
Pinky further alleged that she was being coerced into naming politicians and members of the entertainment industry.
She claimed that she had been subjected to torture and an investigating officer slapped her during interrogation. "The IO threatened me and asked me to name a former prime minister and actors Muneeb Butt and Syra Yousuf in the case," she had alleged.

title: Scotland fast bowler Wheal retires from cricket
description: Recurring back and knee injuries force the paceman to end his career after four T20 World Cups
content:
Recurring back and knee injuries force the paceman to end his career after four T20 World Cups
Scotland fast bowler Brad Wheal has retired from cricket at the age of 30, citing recurring injuries that have left him unable to cope with the demands of fast bowling.
Wheal made his international debut against Hong Kong in 2016 and went on to play 18 one-day internationals, taking 27 wickets, and 26 Twenty20 internationals, claiming 24 dismissals.
The right-arm paceman featured in four ICC Men’s T20 World Cups, including the 2026 edition in India. He was also part of Scotland teams that recorded memorable victories over Bangladesh in 2021 and the West Indies in 2022.
Wheal, who also represented English county side Hampshire, said the decision to end his career had not been easy but was one he had come to terms with.
“I’ve loved my time at Hampshire and representing Scotland as a professional cricketer, but unfortunately, recurring injuries have forced my hand, and I’ve made the decision to retire from playing cricket,” he said.
“I’ve had four stress fractures in my back and recently had surgery on my knee, and ultimately my body can’t cope with the demands of fast bowling anymore.”
Wheal said representing Scotland had been a source of pride for him and his family, adding that his experiences at international tournaments and friendships with teammates were among the highlights of his career.
“I’m incredibly thankful to all my teammates, coaches and support staff who I’ve worked with over the years,” he said, also thanking Scotland supporters for their backing.
Wheal added that he would continue to follow the national team and support his former teammates from afar.

title: Rogue AI agents broke into Indian firms  live systems  government says
description: AI model providers voluntarily disclose that their agents  exceeded the authorisation of their assigned tasks
content:
AI model providers voluntarily disclose that their agents 'exceeded the authorisation of their assigned tasks'
AI models under test broke into Indian organisations' live systems and read confidential records undetected, India's ​cybersecurity agency said, the country's first such official ‌account after similar incidents of rogue AI behavior worldwide.
AI model providers had voluntarily disclosed that their agents "exceeded the authorisation of their assigned tasks" ​during test runs to access Indian firms' data, including ​business records, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said ⁠late on Thursday.
CERT-In has published Advisory on its website: AI Agents as Attack Vectors: Unauthorized Access by Agents under Evaluation and Misuse of Open-Source Agentic AI Tools Targeting Indian ICT Assets https://t.co/oYv3CSMx6c
It did not name the providers or the ​affected organisations.
The disclosure brings India into a growing global debate ​over how AI companies test models with advanced hacking abilities. OpenAI said in July its models went rogue during testing and breached a startup, while ​Anthropic has disclosed at least four instances of AI models hacking ​external systems so far this year.
OpenAI has also apologised for the hacking of ‌an ⁠Australian government website by its rogue AI agent.
Read: Global financial watchdog calls for more human oversight of agentic AI
None of the affected Indian entities detected the intrusions themselves, and in every case it was the AI companies that flagged the incidents, CERT-In ​said.
In a second ​set of ⁠cases, the government agency's own investigations found attackers deliberately using freely available AI tools to ​probe Indian systems and break in for financial ​gain, with ⁠such tools deployed widely across infrastructure in multiple countries.
Attacks that once took days from first entry to final damage were compressed ⁠to ​a few hours, CERT-In said, and ​victims that failed to fully clean up were attacked again within days, at ​greater depth.

title: Iran ships some LPG  jet fuel despite US blockade  data shows
description: Tehran has been concealing cargoes among    a growing volume of ship to ship transfers by other Gulf producers off Oman
content:
Tehran has been concealing cargoes among ​a growing volume of ship-to-ship transfers by other Gulf producers off Oman
Iran has managed to export some liquefied petroleum gas and jet fuel since July, despite a US naval blockade, shipping intelligence showed, and people involved in security said.
Tehran has in recent weeks been concealing such cargoes among ​a growing volume of ship-to-ship transfers by other Gulf producers off Oman, four people in maritime security who track Gulf oil movements told Reuters .
The Iranian exports and methodology are ‌reported for the first time here. While a fraction of its former energy exports, the cargoes are rare evidence of petroleum products getting through a blockade that has halted Iran's crude exports.
Analysis by US advocacy group United Against Nuclear Iran (UANI), which monitors Iran-related tanker traffic using ship and satellite tracking, shows at least eight gas tankers carrying Iranian LPG have left the Gulf of Oman since mid-July.
Another tanker carrying Iranian jet fuel reached Myanmar in September, additional satellite imagery and analysis by maritime intelligence ​group SynMax show.
The US imposed targeted sanctions in 2023 on Myanmar's jet-fuel industry, citing military airstrikes on civilians that the United Nations says have killed thousands of people. Myanmar's military government has ​repeatedly denied targeting civilians, saying its operations are directed against armed groups.
Read: Oil heads for weekly gain with Mideast supply risks
Six of the eight gas tankers and the jet fuel tanker are under US sanctions for ⁠transporting Iranian petroleum and petrochemical products, a Reuters analysis of the vessels and sanctions imposed on ships by the US Treasury showed.
"What we have seen passing is a handful of tankers carrying Iranian LPG, ​but the overwhelming majority of tankers laden with Iranian products have been redirected by US forces," said Jemima Shelley, senior research analyst with UANI.
Shelley said some Iranian LPG tankers transferred cargoes near the Omani coastal towns ​of Shinas and Sohar, while others waited in the Gulf of Oman before heading past the US blockade, which US Central Command has said sits across the Gulf of Oman near the Iran-Pakistan border.
The total amount of these LPG cargoes was estimated at 4.1 million barrels, Shelley said.
Shelley said the shipments were driven "more by opportunism" than showing a new trend of Iran trying to export its oil and petrochemicals by using smaller ships.
Most of the cargoes sailed to Malaysia's Eastern Outer Port ​Limits to conduct further STS transfers for likely destinations in China, Shelley said, based on UANI's analysis.
The Iranian government did not respond to a request for comment. Myanmar's military-backed government did not respond to a ​request for comment on whether the country had received Iranian jet fuel.
The US military's CENTCOM said its naval blockade, which was first imposed on Iran-related oil exports on April 13, is "ironclad". The blockade was lifted in June ‌after the ⁠US reached a draft understanding with Iran, but it was reimposed on July 14 following the collapse of the agreement.
A US military official told Reuters that the passage of a vessel does not necessarily mean it had evaded the blockade. Every ship was assessed individually, including through a review of its papers, and some vessels could be allowed through for humanitarian reasons, the official added.
Read more: Iran president says conflict in Mideast amounts to 'ecocide'
The official said the appearance of a vessel on US sanctions lists is not the only factor to make it subject to the blockade, adding that US forces are also closely monitoring some ships without taking action against them for operational reasons.
Centcom said in an ​update on October 13 that during the three ​months of the latest blockade, four commercial vessels ⁠had been disabled and 135 ships had been turned around by US forces.
The US military has turned around ships from Asia and also seized some tankers, previous CENTCOM statements said.
Washington has coupled its blockade with a sanctions campaign aimed at severing Iran's remaining financial links and depriving it of revenue. Last week, it imposed ​fresh sanctions on 17 vessels involved in transporting Iranian crude, petrochemicals and petroleum products.
A US Treasury spokesperson questioned shipping data suggesting vessels had evaded the blockade, ​saying ships could spoof their ⁠locations or use false identities when loading.
Such data "should be taken with a grain of salt", the spokesperson said.
The Treasury spokesperson said Operation Economic Outcast, together with the blockade, was "suffocating the Iranian regime".
Torbjorn Soltvedt, principal Middle East analyst at risk intelligence company Verisk Maplecroft, said although there was no sign of Washington easing its blockade, worsening economic conditions in Iran could push Tehran to take greater risks.
"If Iran can move product tankers through, even in small ⁠numbers, jet fuel ​may be a good option. Iran's aviation industry is under increasing pressure from US sanctions, with a growing number of planes ​grounded, and a potential surplus of jet fuel at Iranian refineries," Soltvedt added.
Iranian crude exports fell to zero in September, according to Kpler, the first month without a shipment since the analytics firm began tracking the producer in 2013.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has ​said the blockade prevented most Chinese purchases of Iranian oil and left Iran unable to deliver crude to customers.

title: Major hurricane Trudy keeps strengthening as it nears Mexico s Pacific coast
description: Trudy has the potential to even reach Category 4 or 5 intensity  says hurricane meteorologist
content:
Trudy has the potential to even reach Category 4 or 5 intensity, says hurricane meteorologist
Hurricane Trudy rapidly intensified into a major hurricane on Friday morning, carrying ​maximum sustained winds near 120 mph (195 kph) and ​higher gusts, as it moves closer to Mexico's Pacific ⁠coast.
Additional strengthening is still forecast before Trudy is expected ​to approach the Mexican coast on Saturday as a life-threatening ​major hurricane, the US-based National Hurricane Centre said.
"Trudy has the potential to even reach Category 4 or 5 intensity," said Alex DaSilva, a ​hurricane meteorologist at private forecaster AccuWeather.
Mexico's civil protection agency ​asked residents to start preparations for the storm's arrival by securing doors ‌and ⁠windows, and removing objects that could be thrown around by the strong winds.
Read: Little damage as Hurricane Polo sweeps over Mexico's Pacific coast
The hurricane will strike Mexico's Pacific coast, a region that has already been battered in recent weeks ​by storms ​that left several ⁠dead and caused severe flooding.
Located about 250 miles (400 km) south-southwest of the resort city of Acapulco, ​the storm is expected to produce up to ​12 ⁠inches (30 cm) of rain in the states of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco, increasing the risk of life-threatening flooding and landslides, ⁠according ​to the NHC.
Meanwhile, Tropical Storm Simon ​continues to weaken farther northwest offshore, after dropping heavy rain along the coast earlier ​as a hurricane.

title: Steven Soderbergh steps in to help Matt Reeves finish    The Batman Part II
description: Robert Pattinson returns as Batman  with Scarlett Johansson  Colin Farrell and Sebastian Stan also among the cast
content:
Robert Pattinson returns as Batman, with Scarlett Johansson, Colin Farrell and Sebastian Stan also among the cast
Steven Soderbergh is stepping in to help complete principal photography on The Batman Part II while director Matt Reeves deals with an ongoing family matter, according to a statement confirmed by Variety .
The Oscar winning filmmaker approached Reeves to offer assistance, with DC Studios supporting the arrangement. A studio representative said Soderbergh would work closely with Reeves, the cast and crew to complete the remaining filming while preserving the director’s creative vision.
Soderbergh also praised Reeves’ work on the first The Batman , describing it as carefully constructed and visually distinctive. He said his goal was to help capture footage that would fit seamlessly with the material already filmed, allowing Reeves to finish the highly anticipated sequel.
Reeves clarified the situation in a post on X on October 15, stressing that he was not leaving the project. He expressed gratitude to Soderbergh for helping during a challenging period and thanked supporters for their concern.
Just to be clear, I am not leaving The Batman Part II. I am profoundly grateful to Steven for coming to my aid during this challenging time to help me finish principal photography. Thank you to all for your concern and well wishes. 🦇
Warner Bros and DC Studios had announced a temporary production pause earlier in October, explaining that Reeves needed time to address a family matter. The latest arrangement allows filming to move towards completion with Soderbergh assisting behind the camera.
The sequel has faced several scheduling changes since its announcement at CinemaCon in 2022. Initially scheduled for October 2, 2026, its release was moved to October 1, 2027, before being postponed again to February 2028.
Robert Pattinson is returning as the Caped Crusader. The cast also includes Scarlett Johansson, Colin Farrell, Sebastian Stan, Andy Serkis and Jeffrey Wright.
Soderbergh is known for directing films including Traffic , Erin Brockovich and Ocean’s Eleven . His experience across different genres makes him a notable choice to support the production during its final weeks of principal photography.
Despite the unusual arrangement, Reeves remains involved in the film. The collaboration is intended to help complete filming without replacing his creative leadership, as anticipation continues to build for the next chapter of Pattinson’s Batman story.

title: Sanaullah links reversal of K P governor s rule to PTI support for counterterrorism efforts
description: PM   s adviser urges political consensus on security  saying federal govt remains open to cooperation with opposition
content:
PM’s adviser urges political consensus on security, saying federal govt remains open to cooperation with opposition
Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah on Friday hinted that the federal government could consider foregoing interim governance in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) if the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) agreed to support law enforcement agencies in their fight against terrorism.
A day earlier, a joint session of parliament adopted two separate resolutions ratifying the presidential proclamations imposing a state of emergency and governor’s rule in K-P for two months, amid protests from the opposition. Before that, both houses of parliament had separately approved the emergency in the province by majority vote under Clause 1 of Article 232 of the Constitution, despite objections from opposition lawmakers.
The emergency and governor’s rule were declared on October 11 after negotiations between the government and opposition failed , culminating in a PTI long march towards Islamabad that began on October 4.
Speaking to a private news channel, Sanaullah said the government wanted all political parties to reach a consensus on counterterrorism, arguing that growing security challenges required a unified response from the federal and provincial governments.
He said the government’s primary demand from the opposition was that it stand with Pakistan, its law enforcement agencies and armed forces. The fight against terrorism had cost the country precious lives, including those of military personnel, he added.
Sanaullah maintained that political differences should not undermine ongoing counterterrorism efforts, stressing that the strategy adopted to combat terrorism should not be questioned or made conditional on political demands.
Read More: Opp fails to thwart govt move in K-P
The remarks came amid renewed political engagement following meetings involving Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party chief and Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi.
Responding to questions about why the government was pursuing negotiations despite parliament’s ratification of the emergency measures and governor’s rule, Sanaullah said the administration continued to seek consensus among political parties on matters of national security.
He argued that the evolving security situation demanded cooperation rather than confrontation, adding that the federal and provincial governments needed to adopt a common strategy to counter the threat. “Everyone should stand with Pakistan, its law enforcement agencies, and its armed forces,” he added.
He stressed that the war on terrorism had cost precious lives among law enforcement personnel, including military servicemen, and said it was therefore essential to support them and recognise their courage. “Together we need to win this war [against terrorism],” he said.
Sanaullah attributed the latest wave of terrorism to India’s defeat in Marka-e-Haq, referring to the May 2025 Pakistan-India conflict. He said that India had subsequently launched a covert campaign against Pakistan under what he called “Operation Sindoor 2”.
“They are trying to avenge their defeat in the war,” he said, stating that India was using the Afghan Taliban as proxies in its conflict with Pakistan. “They have housed terrorists in training camps and funded them,” the prime minister’s adviser said.
Sanaullah further alleged that Israel was providing technical training to terrorists in Afghanistan, enabling them to operate drones. “In view of all these precarious circumstances, there is a strong requirement that the central and the provincial governments adopt a unified approach to eliminate the threat,” he said.
He reiterated that the government wanted a collective response to what it described as a challenge to Pakistan’s sovereignty, warning that counterterrorism efforts could not succeed without coordination between the federal and provincial governments.
Addressing contentious issues between the government and opposition, Sanaullah said previous rounds of negotiations had either produced agreements on specific matters or referred unresolved issues to a special committee comprising representatives from both sides.
He said these mechanisms were intended to facilitate dialogue and identify a way forward on outstanding matters.
The prime minister’s adviser also criticised the PTI’s response to legal proceedings against its leaders, arguing that allegations of political victimisation should be addressed through the judicial process.
Also read: Pakistan, others walk out as Israeli president speaks at CICA summit in Azerbaijan
He said cases could be resolved only in accordance with the law and that courts, rather than political parties, were responsible for determining the guilt or innocence of those accused.
Sanaullah contrasted the current government’s engagement with the opposition with the tenure of former prime minister Imran Khan, claiming that the PTI founder had not contacted the then opposition leader during his four years in power.
He said Shehbaz, by comparison, regularly met the opposition leader in parliament and invited him to discuss issues of national importance. He added that Achakzai had declined repeated verbal and written invitations to meet the prime minister.
Commenting on the detention of PTI leaders, including Imran Khan’s sisters, Sanaullah alleged that those detained had been involved in planning or supporting unrest. He cited calls for attacks on the governor’s house and rioting in Islamabad as grounds for the authorities’ actions.
He also accused the PTI’s social media team of operating like a “mafia”, saying that it used artificial intelligence and manipulated images to advance the party’s political agenda. “Therefore, actions taken against them are a necessity bound by concerns regarding law and order,” he said.
According to Sanaullah, those detained could be released if the PTI demonstrated that it would not engage in activities intended to provoke unrest in the future.
Read More: PTI disowns Imran's X account in IHC
The adviser maintained that the government remained open to political engagement but insisted that cooperation on national security, particularly the fight against terrorism, was essential.
Sanaullah said the federal government’s position on K-P and other outstanding political matters should be viewed in the context of the broader security challenges facing the country.
He concluded that the threat posed by foreign-backed terrorist networks required a coordinated national response, with political parties, law enforcement agencies and the armed forces working towards the common objective of eliminating terrorism.

title: Elizabeth Holmes claims she has never lied as documentary reveals shocking details about her life
description: Holmes was convicted of fraud related offences in 2022 and sentenced to more than 11 years in prison
content:
Holmes was convicted of fraud-related offences in 2022 and sentenced to more than 11 years in prison
Elizabeth Holmes has made a startling claim about her honesty in You Can See Everything , a new documentary that offers an intimate look at the disgraced Theranos founder in the weeks before she began her prison sentence, while revealing unexpected details about her relationship with partner Billy Evans.
Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, the nearly three-hour documentary follows Holmes, Evans and their two young children at their California home during the 34 days leading up to Holmes’ imprisonment in May 2023. Filmed largely in secret over three years, the project begins as a portrait of Holmes’ private life before taking increasingly unusual turns that raise questions about trust, image management and the documentary itself.
One of the film’s most striking moments comes when Fielder questions Holmes about her history with Theranos, the blood-testing company she founded, and asks whether she has ever told a lie. “I don’t think so,” Holmes replies. When pressed on whether she has ever told even a small social lie, she eventually acknowledges that she probably has.
The documentary also captures Holmes watching Amanda Seyfried’s portrayal of her in the Hulu series The Dropout for the first time. After Fielder persuades Holmes and Evans to watch the programme, Holmes becomes emotional during a scene featuring Seyfried’s performance and asks for the screen to be turned off.
Seyfried later becomes part of the documentary herself, reprising her Emmy-winning portrayal of Holmes in reenactments, including scenes connected to a phone call Holmes makes from prison. The unusual structure blurs the boundaries between documentary footage, dramatic recreation and the public image of a convicted fraudster.
The filmmakers’ access to Holmes and Evans also takes an unexpected turn when the couple invite them to stay in their guest house. The accommodation initially lacks basic amenities, including mattresses, and the directors later become concerned that surveillance devices may have been planted in their rooms. They arrange for the guest house to be checked for hidden recording devices, with Oppenheim describing the experience as feeling like a conspiracy thriller.
Another major revelation concerns Evans, who allegedly sought a share of the documentary’s profits. According to Fielder’s account in the film, Evans arranged a meeting with the filmmakers and executives from distributor A24 to negotiate a financial stake. The alleged discussion is recreated with actor Christopher Abbott portraying Evans. By the end of the documentary, Evans has reportedly withdrawn the demand and will not receive a share of the profits.
The alleged dispute leads to a tense dinner involving Evans, Seyfried and Fielder. Seyfried is reportedly surprised to learn about the proposed financial arrangement and wants to know whether Holmes was aware of it. During the dinner, Evans also criticises Seyfried’s portrayal of his partner in The Dropout . The discussion grows more heated when they disagree over conservative political commentator Charlie Kirk, whom Evans says he admires.
The conversation ends without resolving whether Holmes knew about the alleged attempt to negotiate a share of the documentary’s earnings. The film leaves that question open rather than establishing her involvement.
Perhaps one of the most consequential revelations comes when Evans discusses Holmes’ social media presence while she is incarcerated. He tells Fielder and Seyfried that he manages her X account and frequently publishes or reposts controversial content without her knowledge or approval. Seyfried appears visibly surprised by the admission.
The documentary’s revelations arrive years after Holmes’ rise and fall in Silicon Valley. She founded Theranos with the promise of revolutionising blood testing, but the company’s technology failed to deliver on its claims. Holmes was convicted of fraud-related offences in 2022 and sentenced to more than 11 years in prison.
You Can See Everything premiered at the Telluride Film Festival before screening at the New York Film Festival. The documentary opened in US cinemas on October 16, 2026, offering audiences a new and unconventional examination of Holmes, her relationship with Evans and the way she presents herself to the world.
Holmes’ attorneys and Evans were contacted for comment about the documentary, according to PEOPLE. The film’s central questions remain unresolved, leaving viewers to consider how much of the couple’s apparent openness reflects genuine transparency and how much may be shaped by their desire to control their public narrative.

title: Smith targets batting depth for World Cup
description: Pakistan   s batting coach stresses adaptability and problem solving across conditions
content:
Pakistan’s batting coach stresses adaptability and problem-solving across conditions
Pakistan’s South African batting coach Michael Smith wants the country's batsmen to develop greater adaptability and depth as the team begins a year-long build-up to the 2027 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.
Pakistan's preparations will include an extensive programme of One-Day International cricket at home and abroad, with the upcoming ODI tri-nation series providing an opportunity to assess batting options and prepare for varying playing conditions.
Smith, a former South African first-class cricketer, said Pakistan's recent Twenty20 International series against Sri Lanka had offered useful preparation, particularly on pitches with additional pace and bounce.
“I think we played really well against Sri Lanka on some wickets that we asked for a little bit of pace and bounce because that's what we are going to be getting in 12 months' time in the World Cup,” Smith told PCB Digital.
He stressed the importance of adapting to different surfaces, noting that teams could encounter contrasting conditions during the tournament.
“In the World Cup you are going to be playing in different places in South Africa and Zimbabwe where you could come across five different pitches in five different games,” he said.
Smith identified problem-solving as a key component of his coaching philosophy, saying batters needed to make sound decisions against different bowling attacks and adjust their approach according to match situations.
“The biggest thing that we talk about is problem solving and being able to have the skillset to play on different wickets against different bowling attacks,” he said.
Pakistan have several experienced options in their squad, including Babar Azam, who has scored 20 ODI centuries, and Fakhar Zaman, the country's only double centurion in the format. Salman Ali Agha has also emerged as a consistent contributor, having scored more than 1,000 ODI runs since the 2023 World Cup.
The squad also includes younger batsmen and wicket-keeping options, while all-rounders Shadab Khan, Faheem Ashraf and Arafat Minhas could strengthen the lower order.
Smith said Pakistan needed sufficient depth across all batting positions rather than relying on a small group of established players.
“We don't want to be a team that relies on two or three players. We want to know who our two or three best players are in every position and hopefully give them enough experience so we can set them up for success,” he said.
The coach added that building a winning mentality would be equally important during the preparation period.
“Winning games from different places is the true hallmark of really good teams,” Smith said.
Pakistan will use the tri-series to evaluate their options while balancing the need to win matches with giving players opportunities to establish themselves ahead of the global tournament.

title: Sylvester Stallone regrets doing his own stunts after nine back operations
description: The    Rocky    star says injuries from his action career have left him feeling he has never fully recovered
content:
The ‘Rocky’ star says injuries from his action career have left him feeling he has never fully recovered
Sylvester Stallone has admitted he has serious regrets about performing his own stunts throughout his action film career, revealing that years of injuries and major surgeries have taken a lasting toll on his health.
In an interview with Fox News Digital , the Rocky star described the physical consequences of his work, saying he had accumulated countless injuries over the years. He recalled undergoing nine back operations and three neck fusions after working on The Expendables , alongside injuries affecting both shoulders and his eyes.
Stallone said the repeated procedures had left him feeling that he was never quite the same again. His comments offer a candid look at the physical cost of maintaining an action hero image over several decades.
The actor also reflected on an accident while filming The Expendables , the 2010 action film he directed and starred in alongside Jason Statham and Mickey Rourke. During a scene involving WWE wrestler Steve Austin, Stallone was tackled and suffered serious injuries, including a fractured neck. He subsequently required spinal procedures and had a metal plate inserted into his neck.
Looking back, Stallone said aspiring performers should allow trained professionals to handle dangerous sequences rather than attempting to prove themselves by doing everything personally.
“Let the pro do it,” he advised, warning that the physical consequences of a stunt can follow an actor long after filming has ended.
He also dismissed the idea that he should feel proud of the damage he sustained, describing his decision to continue performing dangerous stunts as foolish.
Stallone shared similar reflections while discussing his memoir, The Steps , with The New York Times . He said his approach to pushing his body had come at a terrible price and suggested he would make different choices if he could revisit his career.

title: Barcelona face Betis challenge
description: Hansi Flick s irresistible side have scored 43 goals in that spell
content:
Hansi Flick's irresistible side have scored 43 goals in that spell
There is much debate over who should win the Ballon d'Or this year, but if Lamine Yamal's recent form continues over the season, handing out next year's award would be simple.
The teenage winger was at his mesmerising best as Barcelona waltzed to a 4-1 win at Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday, to make it 10 victories from 10 matches this season across all competitions.
Hansi Flick's irresistible side have scored 43 goals in that spell, including seven in the last two games, even without talisman Raphinha.
A sensational dribble from Yamal helped create a goal for Anthony Gordon in Istanbul, and the winger's inviting cross also carved out another for Fermin Lopez.
"I don't know what to call it, it was an almost-rabona dribble," Yamal told Movistar.
"It came off well to set up Gordon, that's the main thing, that it was effective at the end of the day."
Yamal had a moment of luck when the ball bounced off the defender back to him but showed excellent reflexes and speed to keep it in and find the former Newcastle winger.
The 19-year-old was named player of the match and earned lavish praise from his coach after another performance in which his ability to beat defenders and generate danger proved decisive.
"It's amazing to have a player like him on this level. He changed the game for us and this was really good," Barca coach Flick told reporters.
"In the second half he was fantastic, how he dominated the game, the (final ball)... it's unbelievable what he's doing."
Yamal has eight goals and nine assists in 10 games for Barcelona this season.
However, perhaps the most impressive aspect of Barcelona's start has been that their attacking brilliance has not depended on any one player.
Raphinha's absence has given former Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus an opportunity to step in successfully, while Karim Adeyemi has added goals and electric speed when needed to replace Gordon.
In midfield, Flick can call on Gavi and Dani Olmo among others without his side losing its identity, while Dutchman Frenkie de Jong is soon to return from injury.
That depth will become increasingly important as Barcelona enter the most demanding part of their autumn.
Critics have pointed out that they have yet to face one of Europe's elite sides, with Galatasaray away arguably their toughest assignment so far.
That argument will be tested this weekend as Barcelona face Manuel Pellegrini's high-flying Real Betis at La Cartuja.
The Andalusian side are third in La Liga, five points behind Barca and one ahead of Real Madrid.

title: K P raises compensation for martyred police personnel to up to Rs35m
description: Replace residential plots for martyrs families with cash payments after families face location related difficulties
content:
Kundi announces cash payments of up to Rs70m in place of residential plots, increased injury compensation
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Friday announced a revised welfare package for police personnel and their families, increasing compensation for officers martyred in the line of duty to up to Rs35 million and replacing residential plots allotted to bereaved families with cash payments of up to Rs70 million.
Speaking at a media briefing, Kundi said the measures had been finalised over the previous two to three days in consultation with the inspector-general of police and the chief secretary. “We have taken measures for the police over the past two to three days, and today we are putting them into practice,” he said, adding that further steps would follow.
Under the revised compensation package, the families of martyred constables, head constables, assistant sub-inspectors (ASIs), sub-inspectors (SIs) and inspectors would receive Rs17 million, up from Rs11 million.
For the families of martyred deputy superintendents of police (DSPs) and assistant superintendents of police (ASPs), compensation had increased from Rs16 million to Rs25 million.
The families of martyred superintendents of police (SPs), senior superintendents of police (SSPs), assistant inspectors-general and officers in grades 18 and 19 would receive Rs30 million, compared with the previous Rs21 million.
For the families of deputy inspectors-general (DIGs), additional inspectors-general, the inspector-general of police and officers in grade 20 and above, compensation had increased from Rs21 million to Rs35 million.
Kundi said the government had also increased compensation for police personnel who suffered serious injuries or permanent disabilities while on duty. Payments for permanent disability had risen from Rs500,000 to Rs5 million, while compensation for severe injuries had increased from Rs100,000 to Rs1.5 million.
Cash payments to replace residential plots
Kundi said the government had revised the scheme under which residential plots were allotted to the families of martyred police personnel, as some families faced difficulties when plots were allocated far from their hometowns.
“If a family belonged to Dera Ismail Khan, Lakki Marwat or Bannu, it could be allotted a plot in Nowshera or Swat, which created difficulties for the family,” he said.
Under the revised scheme, families would receive cash instead of plots, allowing them to choose their own housing arrangements.
Families of martyred constables and head constables, who were previously entitled to five-marla plots, would receive Rs18 million in cash. Those previously entitled to seven-marla plots would receive Rs25 million, while families entitled to 10-marla plots would receive Rs35 million.
Families of officers of SP and SSP rank and above, who were previously entitled to one-kanal plots, would receive Rs70 million in cash.
Kundi said the payments would allow bereaved families to rent a house or purchase a plot or home in a location of their choice.
Compensation for families of serving police personnel
The governor said the government had introduced a compensation package for close relatives of serving police personnel, including their spouses, children, parents and siblings, who could also face security threats. “Just as our police officers face risks, their families can also be targeted,” he said.
Under the new package, Rs5 million would be paid if a police officer’s spouse or child was killed in a targeted attack. If an officer’s parent, brother or sister was killed in such an attack, the compensation would amount to Rs3 million.
Kundi also announced compensation for police personnel killed while off duty. The families of constables, ASIs and inspectors killed while off duty would receive Rs4 million, while those of DSPs and ASPs would receive Rs5 million. Families of SPs, SSPs and officers in grades 18 and 19 would receive Rs7 million.
Kundi announced special financial assistance of Rs10 million for the weddings of daughters of martyred police personnel. He also said the government planned to establish a fund to support the education of children whose parents had been martyred while serving in the police.
He said he had directed the inspector-general of police to ask the police welfare department to approach educational institutions and banks for contributions through their corporate social responsibility funds.
The proposed fund would cover the children’s education, including studies abroad, and help them become financially independent. The government and police would also seek to help them secure employment, he added.
The governor said police salaries had been increased by more than expected, adding that details of the revised pay package would be announced soon. The aim was to make the provincial police’s salary package more competitive than those offered in other provinces, he added.
Kundi stated that 17,000 posts in the K-P police were vacant. He had directed the inspector-general to expedite recruitment and promotions and fill the vacancies to ensure the force could perform its duties effectively. “We need to fill the vacant posts so that the police can be fully equipped to perform their duties,” he said.
Concluding his remarks, he said the government would continue taking measures to promote peace, development and prosperity in the province.
“The days of differences between the province and the federation are gone. The whole of Pakistan is ours. The federation is not our enemy, and Punjab, Sindh and Balochistan are not our enemies. We have to work together for peace, prosperity and development in the province,” he added.
Earlier this week, Kundi distributed residential plot allotment letters to the families of 54 martyred police personnel at a ceremony at the Governor’s House.
He said the government was preparing a broader welfare package to increase police salaries and compensation for officers killed or injured on duty, alongside financial assistance for housing, education and other needs of bereaved families.
The federal government imposed governor’s rule in K-P on October 11, following President Asif Ali Zardari’s approval of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s advice.
The move transferred executive authority from the provincial government to Governor Kundi, while an emergency was declared in 12 districts under Article 232 of the Constitution.
The federal government cited worsening security concerns and authorised the deployment of the Pakistan Army to assist the civil administration.

title: Southgate does not forsee a return to management
description: The former England coach says his desire to remain involved in football has changed
content:
The former England coach says his desire to remain involved in football has changed
Former England manager Gareth Southgate has said he does not forsee a return to coaching after his "desire to be involved in football" has changed.
Southgate led the Three Lions to two finals of the Euros in 2021 and 2024 but fell agonisingly short of ending England's wait since 1966 to win a major tournament.
The 56-year-old resigned shortly after Euro 2024 and since then has embarked on a range of other experiences rather than seeking a route back into the game.
Southgate has been a visiting lecturer at Harvard Business School in Boston and fronted a documentary where he travelled across the United Kingdom to understand challenges facing young men and boys.
"I don't see a scenario where I do that," Southgate told the Amol Rajan Connection podcast on a possible return to Premier League management.
"Towards the end of my time with England, I stopped enjoying, at the very least for a period, the wins that keep you going.
"By the end, I didn't even enjoy the wins for any longer than a couple of minutes. So, I've hardly watched football."
Southgate added he has not even visited a football stadium since going to see his first club Crystal Palace win the FA Cup final in May 2025.
"I went to the FA Cup final to see my team, Crystal Palace, win their first trophy. I've not been to a football ground since. So my sort of desire to be involved in football has changed."
English football has been rocked in recent weeks by Manchester City's guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League rules.
City have appealed and deny any wrongdoing, plunging the world's most watched league into limbo awaiting a final ruling and decision on any potential sanction.
"My underlying thought is none of this is good for football and there are no winners," said Southgate.
"Because if you're at the Premier League, for a very brief moment you might feel justified that all the flak you've had for this case taking so long, this is why it's taken so long and there's the verdict, and I'm sure there's an element of justification in that.
"Then there's this realisation of how do we deal with all of this because you know the possibility of all the different legal cases that emerge from this, how long this could still take, what's the right sort of punishment, how do you keep the whole game on track?

title: DWTS  Val Chmerkovskiy and Carrie Ann Inaba drama explained  Will Smith Oscar s slap reference and apology
description: The controversy arose when Inaba criticised Chmerkovskiy s wife Jenna Johnson s performance on an episode of  DWTS
content:
The controversy arose when Inaba criticised Chmerkovskiy's wife Jenna Johnson's performance on an episode of 'DWTS'
Val Chmerkovskiy has apologised to Dancing with the Stars judge Carrie Ann Inaba after referencing Will Smith’s infamous Oscars slap in a now-deleted social media post responding to criticism of his wife, Jenna Johnson.
The controversy began following the October 13, 2026 episode of DWTS , when Inaba assessed Johnson and her dance partner, Harry Shum Jr., after their samba to Usher’s “Yeah!” during Super Bowl Night.
Although Inaba said she “loved every minute” of the performance, she criticised the routine for needing “more content” and pointed out an illegal lift.
Johnson questioned the feedback, while Chmerkovskiy subsequently shared a TikTok remark that read, “You almost saw the Fresh Prince enter the ballroom last night.”
The reference was widely interpreted as invoking Smith’s 2022 Oscars confrontation with Chris Rock, when the actor slapped the comedian after a joke about his wife, Jada Pinkett Smith.
Inaba addressed the post on Instagram on October 15, sharing the alleged remark and thanking other outlets “for bringing this to my attention.”
Later that day, Chmerkovskiy issued a public apology through his Instagram Stories, confirming that he had also contacted Inaba privately.
“I have reached out to Carrie Ann to apologize directly and personally, and I also want to apologize publicly as I understand my words affect so many outside of our internal DWTS family,” he wrote.
He added, “I am truly sorry to Carrie Ann, and everyone who I hurt with my careless post. I will do better moving forward.”
The professional dancer acknowledged the impact of his platform and said he needed to think more carefully before posting online.
The dispute has also drawn attention to differing opinions about Inaba’s judging, with some defending Chmerkovskiy’s intended meaning while others criticised the reference to violence.
Chmerkovskiy’s apology follows a tense exchange that has brought the latest DWTS judging controversy into the spotlight.

title: Ben Affleck defends Tom Cruise   s    Digger    and warns against punishing risky films
description: Alejandro G Inarritu film stars Cruise as an oil tycoon confronting a global catastrophe after an Antarctic disaster
content:
Alejandro G Inarritu film stars Cruise as an oil tycoon confronting a global catastrophe after an Antarctic disaster
Ben Affleck has defended Tom Cruise’s Digger amid its disappointing box office performance, warning that celebrating its failure could encourage Hollywood studios to produce increasingly formulaic films.
Speaking on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, Affleck compared the public reaction to the film with school bullying, arguing that some people appeared eager to mock its commercial performance without necessarily watching it.
He described Digger as an ambitious project made by talented filmmakers and said its financial losses should not overshadow the creative risks involved in producing an unconventional film.
“If you punish movies that take risks, guess what you’re going to get? A bunch of s***ty homogenised movies,” Affleck said, according to Variety . He added that filmmakers cannot create something genuinely interesting without taking significant creative chances, even when those decisions risk public criticism.
Directed by Alejandro G Inarritu, Digger stars Cruise as an oil tycoon confronting a potential global catastrophe after an oil rig malfunctions in Antarctica. The incident triggers a chain of events threatening to send ice towards Europe.
The film has divided critics and struggled commercially since its October 2 release. According to figures reported by Variety , it had earned approximately $15m at the domestic box office against a production budget exceeding $160m. Marketing costs were reportedly estimated at another $100m.
The publication also reported that the film could leave Warner Bros facing losses of around $245m, making it one of the studio’s most expensive box office disappointments.
Affleck is not the only prominent figure to defend the project. Anne Hathaway praised the film on Letterboxd, describing it as ambitious and encouraging audiences to see it and form their own opinions. Musician Neil Young and actor Mandy Patinkin also expressed strong support.

title: Mason Crane set to revive England career dreams
description: Leg spinner earns England recall after nine years away from international cricket
content:
Leg-spinner earns England recall after nine years away from international cricket
The 29-year-old Mason Crane has been named in England's squad for the upcoming ODI tri-series in Pakistan, marking a return to the international fold after making three appearances for his country as a 20-year-old in 2017 and early 2018.
His last international outing came in the final Test of England's 2017/18 Ashes tour in Sydney, where he scalped the wicket of Usman Khawaja, who had already made 171 runs, before Australia hammered them 4-0 in the series.
Crane also played two T20Is against South Africa and his only wicket came in the form of Proteas great AB de Villiers.
Speaking to the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast, Crane admitted he had begun to lose hope of another international opportunity before rediscovering his ambition in recent years.
"I didn't really expect it, to be honest," Crane said.
"It was a bit out of the blue. But it's really cool and I'm buzzing.
"I think there was a period a few years ago where I was sort of resigned to the fact it may not come again, where I maybe put a bit too much pressure on myself and wasn't particularly enjoying it.
"But the last couple of years I feel like I've I sort of got that spark back and the ambition that comes with it."
The 29-year-old will now look to make the most of his return, with his improved all-round game helping strengthen his case for international recognition.
Crane has been in good form in the domestic circuit in England, picking up 34 wickets in 14 County Championship matches and a further 15 in 10 Vitality Blast appearances in 2026, helping his case for a recall.
Crane has also been working to develop his craft as a leg-spinner, insisting he wants to be recognised for more than occasional moments of brilliance.
"I don't want to just be a highlights reel bowler, every now and then bowl a really good ball and just live off that," he added.
"I pride myself on trying to play to the situations really, trying to work out how I'm going to get the most out of a wicket and get a particular guy out.
"I've also given myself a bit more freedom, I guess, with the ball now. I try and bowl more variations, but I'm also better at bowling them now.
"It's about sort of adding as many strings to your bow. It's really important."
England begin their tri-series campaign against Pakistan on October 20 in Rawalpindi as the teams to continue their build-up to the upcoming ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup in 2027.

title: Liam Payne remembered as    sensitive  and  wonderful    on second death anniversary
description: The Wanted singer Siva Kaneswaran pays tribute to Payne  2 years after his tragic death in Argentina at the age of 31
content:
The Wanted singer Siva Kaneswaran pays tribute to Payne, 2 years after his tragic death in Argentina at the age of 31
The Wanted singer Siva Kaneswaran has paid tribute to Liam Payne on the second anniversary of the One Direction star’s death, remembering him as a “wonderful”, sensitive and sincere person despite the rivalry between their bands.
Speaking exclusively to the Daily Mirror on October 16, 2026, Kaneswaran reflected on losing Payne, who died in Buenos Aires, Argentina, in October 2024, aged 31.
His death came two years after The Wanted singer Tom Parker died aged 33 following a battle with an inoperable brain tumour.
“Losing Liam felt so recent after losing Tom,” Kaneswaran said, recalling how Payne had supported Parker and attended his funeral before performing at the Inside My Head charity concert at the Royal Albert Hall.
“When Tom passed, Liam messaged online initially and paid his respects, then he came to Tom's funeral. He was such a wonderful person, so honest and sincere.”
Kaneswaran added, “You could tell he was a really sensitive young man. There are no words to describe that feeling of losing someone like Liam. I can only imagine what it was like for the fans. I still send my love to his friends and family and all the fans. His death was a big, big loss.”
The tribute highlights the relationship that developed between the musicians despite the highly publicised rivalry between One Direction and The Wanted during their rise to fame.
Kaneswaran, who now performs with Max George as The Wanted 2.0, said the deaths of Payne and Parker had changed his outlook on life.
“Death teaches you one thing - it teaches you how to live. Go for it and follow what you truly want,” he said.
He added that performing and making music continued to bring him happiness, while emphasising the importance of living in the moment and cherishing relationships.
As fans remember Payne two years after his death, Kaneswaran's words offer a personal reflection on friendship, loss and the lasting impact of a fellow musician.

title: PM reaffirms Pakistan   s support for Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks in meeting with newly appointed envoy
description: PM thanks Saudi leadership for its longstanding economic and financial support to Pakistan
content:
Dar wishes Ambassador Albugamy a successful tenure in Pakistan
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to standing “shoulder to shoulder” with Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its sovereignty, security and territorial integrity, while strongly condemning the recent escalation in Houthi attacks against the kingdom.
“The prime minister reaffirmed that Pakistan stood shoulder to shoulder with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its sovereignty, security and territorial integrity,” the Prime Minister’s Office said in a statement following Shehbaz’s meeting with newly appointed Saudi Ambassador Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy.
The prime minister “strongly condemned the recent escalation in Houthi attacks against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia”, which had resulted in “the loss of precious lives and injuries to scores of innocent people, including Pakistani nationals”, the statement added.
“He underlined that Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had always stood by each other,” it added.
The newly arrived Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, H.E. Dr. Rajeh Tami Albugamy, called on Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif. Welcoming the Ambassador to Pakistan, the Prime Minister congratulated him on assuming his new responsibilities and wished him success in… pic.twitter.com/WZe2TXUuji
PM Shehbaz said the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement and the Makkah Joint Defence Alliance marked “historic milestones” in the countries’ longstanding fraternal relations and reflected their “shared commitment to regional peace and security”.
The prime minister also noted that Pakistan-Saudi Arabia relations had “witnessed remarkable progress in recent years” and reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to “further strengthening existing institutional mechanisms to deepen and broaden bilateral cooperation across various sectors”.
The premier welcomed Albugamy to Pakistan, congratulated him on assuming his new responsibilities and wished him success in his diplomatic assignment.
He also thanked the Saudi leadership for its “longstanding economic and financial support to Pakistan” and assured the ambassador of Pakistan’s full support and cooperation in further strengthening the two countries’ longstanding fraternal ties, the statement said.
The newly arrived Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, H.E. Dr. Rajeh Tami Albugamy called on Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad, today. pic.twitter.com/Vmy1JUfShD
Separately, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar also met Saudi Arabia’s newly appointed Ambassador to Pakistan, Albugamy, in Islamabad, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) said in a post on X.
According to the ministry, Dar “underscored the longstanding fraternal bonds and strategic partnership between Pakistan and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia” and reaffirmed the two countries’ “shared commitment to further strengthen bilateral cooperation for mutual progress and prosperity”.
The newly appointed Saudi ambassador conveyed greetings from the Saudi leadership to Pakistan’s leadership and people, the ministry said.
Dar reciprocated with “warm greetings and best wishes” for Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan bin Abdullah Al Saud, and the people of Saudi Arabia.
The deputy prime minister also wished Ambassador Albugamy a successful tenure in Pakistan, the statement added.
The newly appointed Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Pakistan, H.E. Dr. Rajeh Tami Albugamy, called on Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 in Islamabad today. The DPM/FM underscored the longstanding fraternal bonds and… pic.twitter.com/dCMsROmFUa
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agreed to move immediately towards implementing their collective defence commitments and deploying agreed military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia. The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of the Strategic-Political and Defence Committee of the Makkah Alliance for Defence in Riyadh on October 5.
Under the decision, the committee directed the necessary measures to provide the agreed forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in Saudi Arabia, in accordance with approved arrangements and the national legislation of the three countries. It said the move would enhance “readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats”.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed MJDA, a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
Houthis have repeatedly carried out missile and drone attacks against Saudi Arabia since the Yemen war escalated in 2015, targeting military installations, airports, oil facilities and other critical infrastructure.
Saudi authorities said attacks on October 6 and 7 killed three people and injured 36 others, including a Pakistani national. On October 11, a further strike on Riyadh airport killed at least 12 people and injured more than 300, while a subsequent attack on October 12 killed a Pakistani resident and injured 11 others.
The attacks disrupted airport operations, with flights suspended or cancelled, while the Houthis also claimed an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.
In September 2019 , the group claimed responsibility for drone attacks on Saudi Aramco’s Abqaiq processing facility and Khurais oil field, attacks that temporarily disrupted more than half of Saudi Arabia’s crude production.
The attacks continued in subsequent years, including strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure in March 2022.
More recently, Houthi attacks have again targeted Saudi territory. In September, the group claimed missile and drone strikes on a Saudi military base and other targets, while Saudi authorities reported attacks affecting several cities.
It is worth noting that on September 25 , Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye senior military leadership strongly condemned attacks targeting the holy city of Makkah as they reaffirmed their commitment to the collective defence of the Kingdom under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.
Read: Makkah defence alliance agrees to 'rapid force deployment' in Saudi Arabia: FO
A day after that, Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman reaffirmed continued joint efforts to confront attacks targeting Makkah and civilian and economic facilities in the Kingdom during a meeting with the Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir.
Then, on September 27, Defence Minister Asif also reiterated the resolve to implement the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement amid the rising Houthis attacks on Saudi Arabia and said that both Pakistan and Türkiye would stand with Saudi Arabia practically and diplomatically in case of any aggression.
Asif further stressed that protecting Saudi Arabia fell under divine duty.
"If there wasn't an agreement, if Saudi Arabia had been attacked, especially if the sacred cities of Makkah and Madinah were attacked, then we are bound by an eternal agreement; that is, we will protect the House of God and Madinah," he stated in an interview to a private channel.
He also outlined that the "worldly agreement" referring to the MJDA between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to protect one another, would operate in all circumstances.
Read more: Saudi-led coalition says new attack at Riyadh airport causes fire, day after strike kills 13
Yemen’s civil war reignited in July after a UN-brokered truce collapsed, months into a wider Middle East war. Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government have since claimed hundreds of strikes on Houthi-held territory. The Houthis say the attacks have killed civilians, including women and children. Reuters could not independently verify those claims.
The Saudis entered the Yemen war in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition to try to force the Houthis out of ‌the Yemeni capital ⁠Sanaa. The war became a bloody stalemate, with hundreds of thousands of Yemenis killed by fighting and famine.
A 2022 ceasefire reached by the Saudis and the Houthis unravelled this summer, culminating in a lightning Houthi advance that took the Red Sea chokepoint of Bab el-Mandeb from Saudi-backed government forces.
Significance of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
The MJDA was the latest step in longstanding military and strategic cooperation between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. Signed in Makkah, the pact established a framework for collective deterrence and stipulated that an armed attack on any one of the three countries would be considered an attack on all three, while providing for wider cooperation across defence.
The agreement followed nearly a year of negotiations and came amid heightened instability across the Middle East. Turkiye and Pakistan had sought closer regional security cooperation, while Saudi Arabia had faced growing security concerns as conflicts spread across the region, threatening its territory, energy infrastructure and ambitious economic development plans.
For Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the trilateral pact is built on their Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed in September 2025. That agreement stated that “any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both” and committed the two sides to strengthening defence cooperation and joint deterrence.

title: Pakistan condemns Indian defence minister s remarks threatening military aggression
description: FO warns of forceful response to any attack  urges New Delhi to abandon its belligerent posture and dangerous rhetoric
content:
FO warns of forceful response to any attack, urges New Delhi to abandon its belligerent posture and dangerous rhetoric
Pakistan on Friday rejected and condemned "provocative remarks" by India's defence minister threatening aggression against Pakistan, warning that any military action would be met with a forceful response.
“Restraint and commitment to peace must never be mistaken for weakness. Any aggression will be met with a forceful response,” Foreign Office spokesperson Ambassador Sajjad Haider Khan said during the weekly press briefing.
He said the remarks reflected India's “hegemonistic mindset” and the risks its “belligerent posture” posed to regional peace and stability in South Asia.
Khan reminded India of the consequences of its military aggression in May 2025, saying Pakistan had demonstrated its capability and resolve to defend its sovereignty and territorial integrity and had delivered a befitting response.
“Let there be no ambiguity. Pakistan remains fully prepared to safeguard its sovereignty and territorial integrity against any ill-advised aggression,” he said.
He urged India to draw appropriate lessons from last year's events, abandon its belligerent posture and dangerous rhetoric, and act responsibly to ensure lasting peace in the region.

The FO also strongly condemned the latest Houthi attack targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, reaffirming its support for Saudi Arabia's sovereignty, territorial integrity and security.
Khan said Pakistan remained deeply concerned over continuing attacks against Saudi Arabia and reiterated Islamabad's solidarity with the kingdom. “Pakistan underscores that attacks against civilian populations and critical infrastructure are unacceptable and constitute a grave threat to regional peace and security,” he said.
The spokesperson added that Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Turkiye had issued a joint statement on October 11 under the R4 Group Framework, condemning continuing Houthi attacks, including the strike on King Khalid International Airport.
The four countries reaffirmed their solidarity with Saudi Arabia, supported its measures to protect its territory and population, and called for an immediate and unconditional cessation of the attacks.
On Palestine, Khan said Pakistan had joined the foreign ministers of 18 other countries in condemning Colombia's inauguration of its embassy in Jerusalem, describing the move as contrary to relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions and detrimental to the two-state solution.
In a joint statement issued on Friday, the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Algeria, Djibouti, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Malaysia, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Syria, Sudan and Türkiye rejected the move.
🔊PR No.2️⃣9️⃣0️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Joint Statement by the Foreign Ministers of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, Algeria, Djibouti, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Malaysia, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Syria, Sudan and Türkiye 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/DEkSfSUmsE
Pakistan urges Kabul to act against terrorists
Highlighting Pakistan's counterterrorism efforts, Khan said Dar had addressed an international conference on Pakistan's evolving counterterrorism landscape, the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), cross-border threats and regional security, organised by the Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad on October 12.
According to the spokesperson, Dar reaffirmed Pakistan's resolve to combat terrorism in all its forms and called on Afghan authorities to take “concrete, verifiable and irreversible action against groups operating from Afghan soil” against Pakistan.
He also highlighted the threat posed by “Indian-sponsored terrorist groups operating against Pakistan”, including those originating from Afghan territory.
Khan said the deputy prime minister had outlined counterterrorism measures, including the implementation of the National Action Plan, Operation Azm-e-Istehkam and enhanced intelligence coordination. He also paid tribute to the armed forces and law enforcement agencies for their sacrifices.
Pakistan reiterates stance on Jammu and Kashmir
On Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir, the spokesperson reiterated Pakistan’s position that India’s actions on August 5, 2019, to divide the region into parts were illegal and void.
“We have been saying it repeatedly and cannot alter the fact that Jammu and Kashmir is an internationally recognised disputed territory whose final status has to be determined in accordance with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions and as per the wishes of the Kashmiri people,” he said.
Pakistan condemns forced displacement of Palestinians
Commenting on the continued displacement of Palestinian refugees in the occupied West Bank and reports that displaced residents of the Tulkarm refugee camp would not be allowed to return, Khan stated that Pakistan considered the forced displacement of Palestinians and attempts to prevent their return serious violations of international law.
Read: Israeli occupiers attack olive pickers in central West Bank, torch 3 vehicles
He said such actions undermined the fundamental rights of the Palestinian people and called on the international community, particularly the United Nations Security Council, to intervene to halt unlawful evictions, uphold the right of displaced Palestinians to return and hold the occupying power accountable for its ongoing violations.
The spokesperson reiterated Pakistan’s support for the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination and its call for the establishment of a viable, independent and contiguous Palestinian state based on the pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital.
Pakistan, Oman agree to expand cooperation
Turning to bilateral relations, the spokesperson said Omani Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamoud Al-Busaidy visited Pakistan from October 13 to 14 at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.
The two foreign ministers co-chaired the eighth session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission, reviewing bilateral relations and agreeing to enhance cooperation in trade, investment, energy, maritime connectivity, information technology and workforce mobility, he added.
Khan further said five agreements and memorandums of understanding were signed during the visit, along with a protocol recording the proceedings of the commission's session. The two sides also exchanged views on regional and international developments and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening longstanding ties.
Separately, Dar met Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev on October 14, he said. The meeting reviewed the positive trajectory of Pakistan-Russia relations, with both sides discussing greater cooperation in trade, investment, culture, tourism and people-to-people exchanges.
They also underscored the importance of continued coordination at multilateral forums, including the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, he added.
Dar holds calls with regional counterparts
The spokesperson said Dar held a telephone conversation with Maldivian Foreign Minister Ertugrul Hisham Adem on October 10 to discuss preparations for President Mohamed Muizzu's forthcoming visit to Pakistan.
Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral relations and agreed to remain in close coordination to ensure a substantive and productive visit.
On October 15, Dar held separate telephone conversations with Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan to discuss regional and international developments.
During his conversation with Abdelatty, Dar emphasised the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in addressing regional challenges and reaffirmed Pakistan's support for de-escalation efforts.
His discussion with Fidan covered the situation in Gaza and Palestine, as well as preparations and strategy for the forthcoming Organisation of Islamic Cooperation Council of Foreign Ministers meeting in Iraq.
The spokesperson said both conversations underscored the importance of continued engagement and close coordination to promote peace and stability.
Pakistan, EU discuss legal migration pathways
On Pakistan's engagement with the European Union, the spokesperson said Dar met European Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration Magnus Brunner in Islamabad on October 13.
The two sides reviewed bilateral relations and discussed cooperation on migration and mobility under the Pakistan-EU Strategic Engagement Plan.
Dar highlighted Pakistan's efforts to combat irregular migration, migrant smuggling and human trafficking, stressing that these measures should be accompanied by greater opportunities for legal migration for skilled Pakistani workers and professionals.
Brunner appreciated Pakistan's progress in curbing irregular migration and acknowledged the potential for expanding legal migration pathways, Khan said.
Responding to a question, the spokesperson said Pakistan had made significant progress in curbing irregular migration to Europe, with EU figures recording a decline of around 64 per cent over the past 18 months.
He added that the achievement reflected Pakistan's sustained efforts to strengthen border management, improve institutional capacity, combat human smuggling and human trafficking, and enhance international cooperation.
Khan further said Pakistan had emphasised in its interactions with the EU that migration and mobility was one of the pillars of the Pakistan-EU Strategic Engagement Plan, signed in 2019, and that efforts to curb irregular migration should be complemented by greater opportunities for safe, orderly and legal migration.
“In this spirit, Pakistan and the EU launched the Migration and Mobility Dialogue back in November 2022, and the dialogue is a win-win template, since it affords an opportunity for both sides to take this opportunity forward,” he said. “In Europe, they are short of labour, and in Pakistan we have sufficient labour workforce,” he added
IAEA completes first nuclear security mission in Pakistan
The spokesperson also announced the successful conclusion of the International Atomic Energy Agency's (IAEA) International Physical Protection Advisory Service (IPPAS) mission to Pakistan on October 9 .
The mission reviewed Pakistan's national legal and regulatory framework governing nuclear security. The IAEA team appreciated the country's cooperation, transparency and professionalism during the review.
Khan said the completion of the first-ever IPPAS mission to Pakistan reflected Islamabad's commitment to strengthening nuclear security and promoting international cooperation for the safe, secure and peaceful application of nuclear technology.
Digital reforms to facilitate document attestation
Separately, Dar witnessed the signing of a memorandum of understanding between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Higher Education Commission and the Inter-Boards Coordination Commission to integrate their databases.
The initiative aims to streamline the attestation and verification of educational documents, improve transparency and expand access to digital services for Pakistanis at home and abroad, the spokesperson said.
He added that the initiative would reduce delays and eliminate the need for physical visits, making consular services more accessible and efficient.
Responding to a question about the inquiry into alleged irregularities in attestation services and reports of officials being taken into custody, the spokesperson said the Foreign Office was progressively digitising attestation and apostille services to make them faster, more transparent and more accessible.
He said e-attestation had been launched through the ministry's portal, while the transition towards e-apostille was underway, including online applications, electronic payments, digital verification and e-certifications.
Eligible applicants could also be exempted from physical appearances, subject to prescribed safeguards, a measure that would particularly facilitate overseas Pakistanis. “This is a massive leap forward,” he said, adding that the process was ongoing and had been personally steered by the deputy prime minister and foreign minister.
The spokesperson said the memorandum of understanding signed between the FO and the Higher Education Commission would enable greater integration among stakeholders, replacing manual application and processing procedures with automation.
Regarding the inquiry, he clarified that the committee was constituted from outside the ministry and was continuing its work. “They will be announcing their proceedings once it is completed,” he added.
