title: Jennifer Lawrence   s witty comment puts    The Hunger Games  Sunrise on the Reaping    in spotlight
description: The playful interaction has sparked excitement among fans hoping to see Lawrence return to Panem
content:
The playful interaction has sparked excitement among fans hoping to see Lawrence return to Panem
Jennifer Lawrence has shared a cheeky exchange with the official Hunger Games account after responding to a post connected to the upcoming prequel, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping .
“U guys are great. What are you promoting?” Lawrence wrote in a comment, prompting a playful response from the franchise’s official account: “a movie! think you'd like it!”
Fans quickly noticed the exchange. Its humour came from Lawrence’s history with the franchise, in which she played Katniss Everdeen across four films, beginning with The Hunger Games in 2012.
The upcoming film, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , returns audiences to Panem decades before Katniss’s story. Based on Suzanne Collins’s novel, it follows a young Haymitch Abernathy during the 50th Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell. Joseph Zada plays the younger version of the character, originally portrayed by Woody Harrelson.
The new instalment features a cast that includes Ralph Fiennes, Jesse Plemons, Glenn Close, Elle Fanning, Kieran Culkin, Maya Hawke and Mckenna Grace. Francis Lawrence, who directed several previous films in the series, returns behind the camera, with the screenplay adapted by Billy Ray.
Lawrence’s comment is not, by itself, confirmation that she will appear in the prequel or take part in its promotional campaign. Reports have previously linked her to a possible return as Katniss, alongside Josh Hutcherson as Peeta Mellark, but Lionsgate has not officially confirmed either actor’s involvement in the film.
With the story centred on Haymitch’s experience in the arena, the prequel introduces a younger generation of characters while revisiting the world that made Lawrence a global star. The account's reply has also renewed interest in whether Lawrence might revisit Katniss in a future instalment.
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is scheduled to open in cinemas on November 20, 2026.

title: 2 children among 8 killed in separate road accidents in K P
description: Six die as passenger van overturns in Buner while two children are killed after being run over by a truck in Charsadda
content:
Six die as passenger van overturns in Buner while two children are killed after being run over by a truck in Charsadda
Eight people were killed and eight others injured in two separate road accidents in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa on Friday.
Six people were killed and seven injured when a passenger van overturned in Buner, while two children were killed and another injured after being run over by a truck in Charsadda, Rescue 1122 spokesperson Bilal Ahmad Faizi said.
Rescue 1122 teams reached the accident site in Buner after receiving information and launched relief operations. Five ambulances and 20 rescue personnel took part in the operation, shifting the deceased and injured to hospital, he added.
The cause of the accident was not immediately known.
In the Charsadda incident, three children were run over by a truck near Tarnab Road. Rescue teams responded on the instructions of District Emergency Officer Ghayoor Mushtaq Khan and shifted the children to the District Headquarters Hospital.
The deceased were identified as five-year-old Mubeen, son of Farhadullah, and 11-year-old Saifullah, son of Sher Wali. Fourteen-year-old Yaseen, son of Farhadullah, was injured. According to initial information, Farhadullah and Yaseen belonged to Gulshanabad Khat Korona, while Saifullah was a resident of Kheshgi.
Read: Four killed as passenger van collides with dumper on Swat Motorway
K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi expressed grief over the loss of lives in the passenger van accident in Buner and offered his condolences and sympathies to the families of the six people killed. He also wished the seven injured people a speedy recovery and directed the relevant authorities to ensure they receive the best possible medical treatment.
On October 13, four people, including a woman, were killed and five others injured when a van collided with a truck on the Quetta-Karachi National Highway near Badrang in Mastung district. The van was travelling from Quetta to Kalat when the collision occurred.
Earlier, on August 30, four people were killed and seven injured when a passenger van collided with a dumper near Tunnel No 3 on the Swat Motorway in Lower Dir district. A motorway police spokesperson attributed the crash to the negligence and carelessness of the van driver.
In July, at least 40 people were killed and eight injured when a passenger coach travelling from Quetta to Peshawar plunged into a ravine in the Danasar area of the Sherani-Zhob Highway, near the Balochistan-Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa border. The difficult mountainous terrain complicated rescue efforts.

title: Pakistan  18 countries reject Colombia   s Jerusalem embassy  says move has  no legal effect
description: Joint statement calls on the Colombian government to  reconsider and reverse  this decision
content:
Joint statement calls on Colombian government to 'reconsider and reverse' this decision
Pakistan and 18 other countries have condemned Colombia’s inauguration of its embassy in Jerusalem, saying any move to recognise the city as Israel’s capital was “null and void” and had no legal effect, according to a Foreign Office (FO) statement issued on Friday.
According to the FO, the joint statement was issued by the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Algeria, Djibouti, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Malaysia, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Syria, Sudan, Turkiye and Yemen.
In a joint statement, the foreign ministers expressed their “unequivocal rejection” of the move, saying it contravened relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions and undermined international efforts to achieve “a just and lasting peace based on the two-State solution”.
The ministers said their position was consistent with relevant UN Security Council and General Assembly resolutions, particularly Security Council Resolutions 476 and 478, adopted in 1980.
🔊PR No.2️⃣9️⃣0️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Joint Statement by the Foreign Ministers of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, Algeria, Djibouti, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Malaysia, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Syria, Sudan and Türkiye 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/DEkSfSUmsE
The resolutions rejected attempts to change Jerusalem’s character or status and called on states to withdraw diplomatic missions from the city, which the statement said was part of the Palestinian territory occupied in 1967.
The ministers called on the Colombian government to “reconsider and reverse this decision”, uphold its obligations under international law and refrain from measures that “prejudice the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people”.
They reaffirmed the Palestinians’ right to “an independent and sovereign Palestinian State with East Jerusalem as its capital”.
Read: Colombia quake death toll tops 250
The condemnation came two days after Colombia opened its embassy in Jerusalem on October 14, becoming the 10th country to establish a diplomatic mission in the city, Reuters reported. The move marked a shift in relations with Israel under President Abelardo de la Espriella, who reversed his predecessor’s decision to sever diplomatic ties with Israel.
Former Colombian president Gustavo Petro broke off diplomatic relations with Israel in May 2024 over its military operations in Gaza. Colombia’s embassy opening also coincided with the restoration of a free trade agreement between the two countries.
Most countries maintain their embassies to Israel in Tel Aviv, while Israel regards Jerusalem as its capital and Palestinians seek East Jerusalem as the capital of a future independent state. The city’s status remains one of the most contentious issues in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

title: Constable martyred in terrorists attack on police checkpost in Peshawar
description: Reports that several terrorists were injured during the exchange of fire are being verified
content:
Governor Kundi, provincial police chief express condolences, say martyrs’ sacrifices remain valuable asset
A police constable was martyred when terrorists attacked the Spina Mela police checkpost in Hassan Khel, Peshawar, last night, Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Mian Saeed Ahmad said on Friday.
According to the CCPO, police personnel on duty responded with heavy retaliatory fire, confronting the attackers with courage and determination and forcing them to retreat and flee.
Police said reports that several terrorists were injured during the exchange of fire were being verified. A search operation was launched in the area to trace the fleeing attackers.
Meanwhile, funeral prayers for the martyred constable, Muhammad Jalal, were offered with full state honours at Malik Saad Shaheed Police Lines in Peshawar.
K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, Chief Secretary Dr Muhammad Fakhr Alam Irfan, Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed, Inspector General Frontier Corps North Major General Rao Imran Sartaj, Pakistan Army and Counter-Terrorism Department officials, CCPO Dr Mian Saeed Ahmed, Peshawar Commissioner Captain (retd) Khalid Mahmood, police officers and personnel, and the constable’s family attended the funeral.
Read: Three terrorists killed in joint CTD, police operation in K-P's Tank
A police contingent presented a salute to the martyred constable, while the governor, chief secretary, and police and Pakistan Army officials laid floral wreaths on his coffin and paid tribute to him.
Governor Kundi and the provincial police chief expressed their condolences and sympathies to the bereaved family, saying the sacrifices of police martyrs were a valuable asset to the department.
“The cowardly acts of terrorists cannot demoralise the police,” Governor Kundi said.
He added that the police force would continue its efforts with unwavering resolve to protect the country and its people, maintain law and order, and eliminate terrorism.
K-P has witnessed a series of attacks targeting police personnel in recent months. On October 8, Station House Officer Daud Khan and his gunman, Farhad, were martyred when armed men opened fire on a police patrol near the Karak-Kohat boundary. Earlier, on September 28, three traffic police personnel were killed when unidentified gunmen attacked their vehicle in Tank district.
On September 25, Counter-Terrorism Department Constable Muhammad Afaq was martyred , and three other personnel were injured during an intelligence-based operation against suspected suicide attackers in Peshawar’s Garhi Sherdad area. One of the deadliest recent attacks took place on September 18, when a blast followed by an assault at Kohat Police Lines killed 15 police personnel among 23 people. Eight attackers were killed during the subsequent clearance operation.

title: PKF eyes reforms after Asian Games failure
description: Federation considers greater exposure  Iranian coach and league revival for improvement
content:
Federation considers greater exposure, Iranian coach and league revival for improvement
Pakistan’s disappointing campaign at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya has prompted the country’s kabaddi authorities to consider changes aimed at restoring Pakistan’s standing in a sport in which it was once a major force on the international circuit.
For the first time in the history of the Asian Games, Pakistan returned without a medal in kabaddi. The team failed to reach the semi-finals after suffering a 51-30 defeat by Iran in a crucial group match. However, the biggest setback came against Thailand, a relatively inexperienced opponent, who edged Pakistan 48-45 to severely dent their semi-final hopes.
“Yes, it was unfortunate that we returned without a medal for the first time in four decades,” Pakistan Kabaddi Federation’s (PKF) Secretary General and former national captain Mohammad Sarwar told The Express Tribune.
“We were leading Thailand by 14 points, but we lost the match in the last seven minutes. It was heartbreaking for all of us,” Sarwar said.
He identified a lack of international exposure as one of the main reasons behind Pakistan’s disappointing performance, saying regular competitions against top teams were essential to developing match temperament.
“Our biggest issue is the lack of exposure. Other teams travel to India and keep playing matches, and that makes a significant difference. We do not play against India and rarely travel abroad, except for major events. We need to increase our international exposure because match temperament is crucial ahead of such important competitions,” Sarwar said.
Pakistan had also invited Iran to participate in a joint training camp ahead of the Asian Games, but the plan did not produce the desired results. “The team usually trains in Iran, but the conflict involving Iran and the United States prevented Pakistan from travelling there this time,” Sarwar said.
Pakistan have won seven bronze and two silver medals in kabaddi at previous Asian Games, making their failure to reach the podium a significant setback for the country.
Sarwar acknowledged that Pakistan needed to pay greater attention to mat kabaddi, the format played at the Asian Games, where barring strong India, Iran and South Korea have made considerable progress.
“We need to focus on this format. The problem is that circle-style kabaddi is usually given priority in Pakistan. Iran, for example, focus on Asian-style kabaddi, while their circle-style game is weak,” he said.
“We did not expect to return without a medal because we believed our team was competitive.” The federation is also considering hiring an Iranian coach in an effort to improve the team’s performance in the Asian-style.
“We are now considering hiring an Iranian coach, even though we were the ones who taught them kabaddi. We will see how this experiment works,” Sarwar said.
Pakistan’s next target is the Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games, where the federation hopes to build a stronger squad.
“Our next target is the Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games. We will build a good team and see how the players perform,” Sarwar said.
The 6th Asian Indoor and Martial Games are penciled in for December 11-21 in Riyadh. The federation also plans to revive its domestic league, which it believes could help improve players’ competitiveness and financial security.
“We held the Super Kabaddi League a few years ago and intend to revive it. Such an event is important if we want to keep the sport alive and strengthen players financially,” Sarwar said. Pakistan began their Asian Games campaign convincingly, beating Malaysia 65-22 and Nepal 58-43. However, consecutive defeats against Thailand and Iran ended their hopes of reaching the semi-finals.
India won both the men’s and women’s kabaddi titles, defeating Iran in both finals. The Indian men secured a 40-34 victory, while the women won 37-34.
India’s continued progress has been supported by a high-profile professional league that provides players with regular competition and greater exposure. Pakistani players also featured in the league in the past, but their participation has been suspended in recent years because of strained political and diplomatic relations between the neighbouring countries.

title: Pakistan to chair IMF  World Bank boards in 2027 for first time since 1953
description: Ahad Cheema says Pakistan will work to amplify voice of developing countries  ensure provision of development finance
content:
Ahad Cheema says Pakistan will work to amplify voice of developing countries, ensure provision of development finance
Pakistan will chair the boards of governors of the World Bank Group (WBG) and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in 2027 for the first time since 1953, with Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Khan Cheema nominated to lead both institutions’ boards for the year, the Ministry of Economic Affairs said on Friday.
The announcement was made during the plenary session of the annual meetings of the WBG and the IMF in Bangkok, Thailand.
The ministry said Cheema had been briefed by the WBG’s Corporate Secretariat on the responsibilities of the chairmanship. He also met WBG Vice-President and Corporate Secretary Aradhana Kumar Capoor to discuss institutional support and coordination during Pakistan’s tenure.
Cheema also met outgoing chairman Carlos Carvalho Spalding and congratulated him on successfully completing his term. The two discussed the responsibilities of the chairmanship and priorities for the coming year, the ministry added.
Cheema said Pakistan would work to amplify the voice of developing countries and ensure the effective and predictable provision of development finance.
He said Pakistan remained committed to improving coordination among multilateral development institutions and sought to mobilise private investment to support sustainable and inclusive growth.
Pakistan would work with the WBG, the IMF and member countries to strengthen the multilateral development and financial system, Cheema said.
The annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group are being held in Bangkok, Thailand, with Pakistan’s delegation, led by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, engaging with international lenders, investors and development partners on economic reforms, financing and investment opportunities.
During the meetings, Aurangzeb highlighted Pakistan’s fiscal deficit falling to a 22-year low , three consecutive years of primary surpluses and improved foreign exchange reserves, while reaffirming the government’s commitment to structural reforms and sustainable, export-led growth. Pakistan has also called for reforms to the international financial system to make multilateral institutions more representative and responsive to the needs of developing countries.
Finance and Revenue Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb met World Bank Group President Ajay Banga at a dinner hosted by Thailand’s prime minister on the sidelines of the World Bank Group–IMF Annual Meetings 2026 in Bangkok, Pakistan Television said in a post on X.

title: David Surkamp dies at 73  Pavlov   s Dog frontman s cause of death and net worth
description: The singer  guitarist and songwriter became known for his distinctive vocals and contribution to progressive rock
content:
The singer, guitarist and songwriter became known for his distinctive vocals and contribution to progressive rock
David Surkamp, the lead singer of progressive rock band Pavlov’s Dog, has died aged 73, prompting tributes from fans and fellow musicians.
The news was announced by the band’s violinist and mandolinist, Abbie Steiling, in a social media post.
Surkamp died unexpectedly on October 13. However, neither Steiling nor the band publicly disclosed the cause of death, and no further details about the circumstances have been released.
Following the announcement, Pavlov’s Dog expressed condolences to Surkamp’s children, Saylor and Evan, and the wider family.
The band also invited fans to share memories of the musician through its social media channels.
Born Robert David Surkamp, the American singer, guitarist and songwriter became known for his distinctive vocals and contribution to progressive rock.
Pavlov’s Dog emerged from St Louis in the early 1970s and released its debut album, Pampered Menial , in 1975. The record featured “Julia”, one of the group’s best-known songs.
The band followed with At the Sound of the Bell in 1976 before its original line-up split in 1977.
Surkamp later formed Hi-Fi with Ian Matthews and continued developing his musical career. He reunited with Pavlov’s Dog in 1990 and remained associated with the group through subsequent recordings and performances.
Celebrity finance websites estimate Surkamp’s net worth at approximately $3.48 million in 2026. This figure has not been independently verified.
Surkamp was married to singer and guitarist Sara Surkamp and leaves behind two children. His legacy remains closely connected to Pavlov’s Dog and its enduring contribution to progressive rock.

description: Brighton target another statement win in Sunday s derby against Crystal Palace
content:
Brighton target another statement win in Sunday's derby against Crystal Palace
Manchester United travel to historic rivals Leeds on Sunday with pressure mounting on manager Michael Carrick, while Manchester City aim to extend their perfect Premier League start despite the uncertainty over their future.
Brighton could be one of the big winners should City suffer severe sanctions for breaking financial rules.
The Seagulls riding high, just two points behind second-placed Arsenal, ahead of their grudge match against Crystal Palace.
AFP Sport looks at the pick of the action from the English top-flight this weekend.
United are off to their worst league start in 40 years and were plunged further into chaos by defender Lisandro Martinez's attack on the club's hierarchy over a lack of investment in the squad after Tuesday's 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid.
The Argentine took aim at technical director Jason Wilcox after the Red Devils only added three midfielders during the transfer window.
But Martinez himself has been one of those most culpable for a miserable start to the campaign for his part in goals conceded to Fulham and Tottenham in recent weeks.
United have won just one of their opening six league games and were also dumped out of the League Cup last month by Brighton.
Leeds last beat the Red Devils at Elland Road back in 2002, but did inflict the only home defeat of Carrick's interim spell in charge last season when the sides met in April.
Carrick is increasingly at risk of becoming just the latest manager unable to turn around a sharp decline at Old Trafford since Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013.
But he said the hostile atmosphere that will await his side presents the perfect chance to bounce back.
"What a great game (on) Sunday to prepare for. It's a fantastic game for us, for the club, for the history, for the supporters," said Carrick.
"Everything to do with the game is a great game so we'll be ready for that."
Manchester City sit pretty at the top of the table with six wins from six league games, but that may all count for nothing if they do not successfully overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League rules.
Enzo Maresca's men shut out that distraction to win 3-0 at Liverpool last weekend and rallied impressively in the second half despite losing 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germain in a thrilling Champions League tie on Tuesday.
But the uncertainty over their future has left the entire league in limbo.
City deny any wrongdoing and a case that began eight years ago has at least a few months left to run before the appeal is heard and a potential sanction announced.
"My underlying thought is none of this is good for football and there are no winners," said former England manager Gareth Southgate.
City can stretch their lead at the top to six points when Ipswich visit the Etihad on Saturday, with Arsenal not in action until 24 hours later at Nottingham Forest.
'Ruthless' Brighton eye Champions League
Arsenal's only defeat this season came in a 3-0 trouncing by Brighton, whose remarkable rise could reach new heights this season with many of the other established giants struggling.
Brighton have soared through the divisions and into Europe on the back of owner Tony Bloom's expertise in data analytics.
But they are yet to play Champions League football.
Despite routinely selling their prized assets to wealthier clubs, Brighton's smart recruitment of both players and coaches has allowed them to continue to thrive.
That has also made them a neutral's favourite but manager Fabian Hurzeler wants his side to show their nasty side against rivals Palace on Sunday.
"We want to be ruthless. We want to create this energetic atmosphere where it makes it so hard to come to this place," said Hurzeler. "We have to keep building this together with our fans and not be the nice football club anymore."

title: Billy Joel shares heartbreaking health update on performing and driving after brain disorder diagnosis
description: Joel says he cannot drive or perform for now as he continues to manage normal pressure hydrocephalus diagnosed in 2025
content:
Joel says he cannot drive or perform for now as he continues to manage normal pressure hydrocephalus diagnosed in 2025
Billy Joel has revealed that he cannot currently drive or perform live as he continues to manage normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH), a brain disorder diagnosed in 2025.
The 77-year-old singer shared the update in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter published on October 15, 2026.
“I’m not allowed to drive,” Joel said, explaining that he must undergo further medical tests before doctors determine whether he can return to performing.
He also revealed plans to auction more than 70 motorcycles from his collection because his condition has made riding unsafe.
“I ended up having over a hundred motorcycles, and the truth is you can only ride one at a time,” the “Uptown Girl” singer said. “I’m into my 70s now, and I realized I can’t ride as much as I used to.”
Joel explained that NPH “makes driving a little bit iffy” and that he had decided it was time to pass his motorcycles on to other owners.
The musician also discussed why he cannot currently perform, saying his neurologist had warned him that concerts could place additional strain on his condition.
“Rock and roll is loud, man,” he said, describing the lighting, sound, stress and energy involved in live performances. He added that further tests would help determine whether he could return to the stage.
Joel cancelled his remaining tour dates in May 2025 following his diagnosis and earlier postponements after a fall during a performance.
Last month, he revealed that he had undergone brain surgery involving the implantation of a shunt, which he said improved his memory, balance and overall ability to function.
He continues to attend physical therapy and follow medical advice.
Despite the challenges, Joel offered reassurance to fans, stating, “I’m not going anywhere. I’m here. I’m still here.”

Pakistan on Friday launched a seven-day hockey goalkeeping training camp for 15 junior and senior goalies in Islamabad.
The camp aims to improve goalkeeping standard in the country.
The camp is being held at Naseer Bunda Hockey Stadium under Dutch coach Bob Veldhof, with a specialist goalkeeping coach overseeing sessions focused on modern techniques.
The programme includes morning and evening sessions covering technical skills, physical fitness and mental confidence, Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF) said.
The PHF spokesperson said the camp aims to strengthen national team's defence and prepare goalkeepers for the demands of modern hockey.
Pakistan have been facing defence issues in recent years and a strong goalkeeping department can bring improvement at the back-end.

title: ATP proposes rankings system changes
description: The changes aim to ease scheduling pressure and increase player earnings
content:
The changes aim to ease scheduling pressure and increase player earnings
The ATP unveiled plans to change its ranking system, centre the tour more on its Masters 1000 events and increase bonus payments for players from 2028 on Thursday.
Players take their best results from 19 regular-season tournaments, as well as the eight-man ATP Finals should they qualify, to form their ranking.
The current system allows players to replace up to three of their results from the eight mandatory 1000-level events with better performances from lower-tier competitions.
But the ATP wants to take away that possibility, ensuring points from all Masters tournaments count towards a player's ranking regardless of their results.
"Today, players can replace up to three of their weaker results from ATP Masters 1000 events with better results from ATP 500 or ATP 250 events later in the season," the ATP said in a Q&A posted on its website.
"That can create pressure to add tournaments after an early loss to make up the points.
"The proposals would remove this, so results at the biggest events count in full and players can plan their schedules around them rather than chasing points and risking overplaying."
Top players have regularly complained of burn-out in recent seasons, with several notable absentees from big events, especially later in the year.
World number one Jannik Sinner has not played since winning Wimbledon in July due to a knee injury, while seven-time Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz was also sidelined for large parts of 2026.
"The demands of the season fall hardest on the players who go deepest at the biggest events," the ATP said.
"Many players, including those in the mid-rankings, find it hard to protect time for recovery when the system rewards them for adding one more tournament."
The governing body for the men's tour added it was looking into weighting ranking points more favourably for players who go deep into tournaments.
It is also "reviewing a limit on how many ATP 250 results count towards the rankings of top players".
Several players, including Sinner, protested against perceived low prize money at both this year's French Open and Wimbledon.
The ATP does not organise the Grand Slam tournaments, but it has announced plans for a large increase in bonus payments and pension contributions from the tour.
Players ranked in the world's top 250 would share a year-end rankings bonus worth a total of $25 million, while the bonus pool for top-ranked players available at 1000 events is slated to increase from $21.5 million to $50 million by 2028.
"The proposals would take ATP's annual central investment in the sport through player compensation and support to more than $100 million from 2028," ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi said in an open letter.
The ATP also said it would push ahead with its reforms of the doubles game, despite fierce pushback from doubles specialists.
It is planning to cut down the size of doubles draws, reallocating prize money to the early rounds and qualifying of singles tournaments.

title: Lyon down Palace in Europa League
description: Sunderland snatch a 2 1 stoppage time win over Torreense
content:
Sunderland snatch a 2-1 stoppage-time win over Torreense
French club Lyon held off Crystal Palace 3-2 in the Europa League on Thursday, while Sunderland made a late comeback to break the hearts of Portuguese second-division side Torreense.
Bayer Leverkusen, Juventus, Benfica and Bournemouth all also won to maintain their perfect starts to the league phase.
It was a painful return to his old home for Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage as the UEFA Conference League champions fell to their fourth defeat of the season in all competitions.
"It's a very disappointing return because we lost. I can't take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn't there," Sage told UEFA.com.
"The scoreline may have been close, but there was a big difference in the way the two teams played. We were nowhere near our usual standards in the first half."
Lyon took the lead inside the opening 10 minutes through Corentin Tolisso and Ernest Nuamah then doubled Lyon's advantage two minutes into first-half injury time.
Yeremy Pino halved the deficit for Palace early in the second period, but a close-range flick by Pavel Sulc restored Lyon's two-goal buffer.
Daichi Kamada smashed home a second for Palace with nine minutes remaining but the hosts held out to make it two wins from two to start the league phase.
Bayer Leverkusen followed up their opening 2-0 win with a 4-0 success at Polish side Lech Poznan.
AC Milan cruised to a 4-0 victory at Red Bull Salzburg, courtesy of a hat-trick scored by Italian teenager Alphadjo Cisse.
Club-record signing Goncalo Ramos made it four on 72 minutes before a red card for Filippo Terracciano took some of the sheen off the win for Ruben Amorim's men.
In the Estadio Municipal de Leiria, Portuguese Cup winners Torreense looked set to hold their Premier League opponents to a draw until Noah Sadiki's 93rd-minute strike made it 2-1 for the visitors.
The 15th-placed side in Portugal's second tier stunned Sunderland in the 37th minute as centre-half Volnei Feltes cut past a flimsy challenge and unleashed a piledriver 30 yards from goal, which left Robin Roefs rooted to the spot.
Black Cats boss Regis Le Bris sent on first-team regulars Granit Xhaka and Enzo Le Fee just shy of the hour and the move paid dividends as Jules Ahoka struck shortly afterwards to level the scores.
After a lengthy VAR check decided against awarding Sunderland a late penalty, Torreense must have thought they had done enough to earn a famous point until Sadiki popped up at the death to thrash in the winner.
"Conceding a goal in the last minute is a blow to the chest," Torreense coach Carlos Simoes said. "The players are in the dressing room, devastated."
Fellow Premier League outfit Bournemouth enjoyed a fine home debut in Europe as they eased to a 3-0 win over Sturm Graz, courtesy of goals by Evanilson, Rayan and Alvaro Rodriguez.
Juventus fought from behind to emerge 2-1 victors at Celta Vigo after Newcastle loanee Nick Woltemade made it two from two in Europe to cancel out Hugo Alvarez's opener for the hosts, and Randal Kolo Muani scored an injury-time winner.
Martin O'Neill's Celtic continued their difficult start to the season as they sank to a fourth defeat in their last five outings, outclassed 4-1 at Benfica.

title: Dar orders action against hoarding  overpricing of essential commodities
description: Dar told adequate stocks available to meet domestic demand  with  no shortages anticipated  and prices stabilising
content:
Says adequate stocks available to meet domestic demand, with 'no shortages anticipated' and prices stabilising
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Friday directed the authorities to take "strict action against hoarding, artificial shortages and overpricing of essential commodities," as a government committee reviewed stock position, supply arrangements and prices, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) said.
According to the post on X, MoFA said Dar chaired a meeting of the Cabinet Committee to review the stocks and prices of essential commodities.
The committee reviewed the “stock position, supply arrangements and prices of essential commodities”, the ministry said. Dar was informed that “adequate stocks were available to meet domestic demand”, with “no shortages anticipated” and prices stabilising, it added.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 chaired a meeting of the Cabinet Committee to review the stocks and prices of essential commodities. The Committee reviewed the stock position, supply arrangements and prices of essential commodities.… pic.twitter.com/FA258IZ99O
The deputy prime minister directed all concerned authorities to “monitor supply chains and commodity prices to facilitate domestic consumers”, in line with the prime minister’s directives.
He stressed that “strict action would be taken against hoarding, artificial shortages and overpricing of essential commodities”, the MoFA said.
The meeting was attended by the ministers for National Food Security and Research and Climate Change, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Tariq Bajwa, the commerce secretary and senior representatives of relevant federal and provincial ministries and departments.
Pakistan’s year-on-year consumer price inflation slowed to 10.3 per cent in September from 11.1 per cent in August, but rising electricity and fuel costs continued to put pressure on household budgets. Average inflation during the first quarter of the current fiscal year stood at 10.2 per cent, while monthly inflation increased by 1.3 per cent in September.
Short-term price pressures also persisted. The Sensitive Price Indicator rose 11.97 per cent year-on-year in the week ending October 8, with the price of a 20-kilogramme bag of wheat flour increasing 5.69 per cent in a week to Rs2,851, compared with Rs2,150 a year earlier. Onion prices more than doubled over the same period, while petrol prices rose 47.52 per cent year-on-year.
Pakistan’s wheat and flour markets have faced rising prices and supply disruptions despite a substantial harvest, with concerns over hoarding, weak procurement and restrictions on interprovincial trade. In July, Punjab sought one million tonnes of wheat from federal reserves after failing to procure its planned three million tonnes from farmers, purchasing only 480,000 tonnes. Officials also said the province had been unable to trace about four million tonnes of wheat believed to have been hoarded, raising questions over stock management.
The situation was compounded in K-P by restrictions on wheat and flour supplies from Punjab. K-P requires about 5.2 million tonnes of wheat annually but produces only 1.2 million tonnes locally, leaving it heavily dependent on supplies from other provinces. Flour millers have said the restrictions disrupted deliveries, forced mills to close and drove up prices, with a 20kg flour bag reaching Rs2,700 in January.
Read more: Punjab flour halt drives prices higher
Despite repeated requests by the K-P government to restore supplies, restrictions remained in place in September, pushing prices of fine, special fine and mixed flour up by as much as Rs100 per 20kg bag. The provincial assembly passed a resolution on the issue, while Chief Minister Sohail Afridi sought the prime minister’s intervention.
Flour prices have come under particular pressure in Peshawar, where a 20kg bag of coarse flour reached Rs3,300 in early October, while fine flour of the same weight sold for Rs3,120. An 80kg bag of coarse flour was priced at Rs13,200. The increase came as government-subsidised flour became largely unavailable in the open market, prompting concerns about supply shortages and allegations of artificial price manipulation.
The increase also affected consumers buying bread. Tandoors raised the price of a 50-gramme roti to Rs30, up Rs10, while some markets stopped selling single rotis and offered larger ones instead. The provincial Food Department said it had distributed more than 417,000 bags of flour at official rates during the preceding week and was releasing 3,000 metric tonnes of government wheat from strategic reserves to flour mills daily.
The IMF has also raised its inflation forecast for Pakistan to 9.9 per cent for the current fiscal year, up from its earlier projection of 8.4 per cent, while maintaining its economic growth forecast at 3.5 per cent.

title: Israeli occupiers attack olive pickers in central West Bank, torch 3 vehicles | The Express Tribune
description: Palestinian farmers assaulted in town of Turmus Ayya as attacks intensify during olive harvest season
content:
Palestinian farmers assaulted in town of Turmus Ayya as attacks intensify during olive harvest season
Israeli occupiers on Friday attacked Palestinian olive pickers north of Ramallah in the central occupied West Bank, assaulting farmers and setting three vehicles on fire, local sources said.
The sources told Anadolu that a group of occupiers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives in the town of Turmus Ayya and physically assaulted several farmers.
The occupiers also torched three Palestinian vehicles and attacked the outskirts of the town, the sources added.
On Monday, the Palestinian Colonisation and Wall Resistance Commission said it had documented 136 attacks linked to the olive harvest season carried out by Israeli forces and occupiers since the beginning of October.
According to the commission, the incidents included beatings, expulsions, intimidation, gunfire, tear gas, and arrests.
They also included theft of olives and harvesting equipment and damage to trees, causing losses to farmers and restricting their access to agricultural land.
Read: UN official sounds alarm about Gaza, West Bank year after ceasefire
Attacks by Israeli forces and occupiers against Palestinians and their property across the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, have intensified since the start of Israel’s genocide on Gaza in October 2023.
On Wednesday , a Palestinian woman was killed and two people, including a girl, were injured in an Israeli airstrike targeting a residential building in Gaza City early Wednesday, sources said.
A medical source at Al-Shifa Hospital told Anadolu that the body of Reem Asaad Awad, 33, and two injured people were brought to the hospital following the airstrike on a residential building in the Rimal neighbourhood.
The source said the strike caused extensive destruction to the targeted apartment and neighbouring buildings. A large fire also broke out after the attack and was later extinguished by civil defence crews.
Meanwhile, witnesses said Israeli military vehicles and quadcopter drones opened heavy fire toward Palestinian homes in the Tuffah neighbourhood, northeast of Gaza City, while explosive devices were dropped on Al-Sikka Street in the surrounding area.
Separately, sources said the Israeli army carried out a large-scale demolition operation, blowing up homes within areas where its forces are deployed east of Gaza City.

title: Indian police detain  cockroach  movement founder Dipke ahead of protest
description: Cockroach Janta Party is demanding resignation of India s chief election commissioner over a revision of voter lists
content:
Cockroach Janta Party is demanding resignation of India's chief election commissioner over a revision of voter lists
Police ​detained India's 'cockroach' movement founder Abhijeet Dipke and some supporters on Friday, ahead of a protest called by him in Delhi's central business district, ‌the latest rally to demand the resignation of India's election chief.
The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), opposition groups, and student organisations have held almost daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter lists that critics say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision, but the Election Commission has denied favouring any party ​and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.
Dipke called Friday's protest ​in support of two CJP leaders detained and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at a protest site in ⁠violation of a ban.
Read : India's 'cockroach' movement leaders detained in jail for five days, party and police say
Indian police detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke ahead of a protest demanding the election chief’s resignation, over a voter-list revision that allegedly favoured PM Narendra Modi’s BJP. pic.twitter.com/ceQQbg9a1o
The group and left-wing student organisations had urged supporters to gather at Central Park in New Delhi's busy Connaught Place shopping and food district ​on Friday evening to wave and hoist the national flag.
Police say they warned movement leader against protesting
The live video on CJP's Instagram handle showed Dipke coming out of a ​house and walking towards the street, where police officers stopped him and, after a brief argument, hauled him into a police car and drove away.
"We are detaining you right now," a police officer could be heard telling Dipke.
"I have not broken any law right now ... how can you detain me?" Dipke asked the police officers as he was taken away, the second time in a week that ​he has been detained.
There was no immediate comment from the police on the detention.
🚨 BREAKING NEWS🚨 Delhi Police have detained Abhijeet Dipke as he was heading alone to Central Park to hoist the Tricolour. #coackroachjantaparty #cjp_पार्टी pic.twitter.com/V0jgAyh9Lr
"Abhijeet is detained by Delhi Police," CJP posted on X. "This government is so scared of ​the youth waving national flag."
Student activist Neha Bora , a prominent face of the protests, was also detained as she tried to reach Connaught Place with dozens of supporters, local media reported.
Earlier on Friday, ‌police met Dipke ⁠and warned him against going ahead with the protest. Security was stepped up and the park itself shut by civic authorities.
Senior police officer Sachin Sharma told news agency ANI that Dipke was served a notice that asked him to obey the law, and that he was informed of the implications of any violations.
Television images showed dozens of people arriving at Connaught Place amid heavy security, some of them waving small versions of the national flag.
Small protests were also held in financial capital Mumbai and tech hub Bengaluru, while ​student organisations held a demonstration in the ​eastern city of Patna, with people ⁠waving flags of their organisations and pushing against police barricades.
The cockroach movement has emerged as one of the biggest political challenge s faced by Modi and his BJP in his 12 years in power.
A weeks-long sit-in by its supporters earlier this year ​forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over exam paper leaks.
Read More : Modi's education minister quits as jubilant Indian youth protesters claim victory, end protest
The latest demonstrations erupted after the Indian Express newspaper reported that ​Kumar's two deputies raised concerns ⁠internally about voter list changes, registration procedures and digital systems.
The 130 million names that were removed from voter lists starting last year — equivalent to more than the population of Japan — included 28 million people who had died, 63 million who relocated, and 30 million who could not be traced, according to the Election Commission.
Opposition parties allege the deletions disproportionately affect Muslims ⁠and other minorities, ​who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party, allegations the commission and the BJP reject.
Defence ​Minister Rajnath Singh said the demonstrations were the main opposition Congress party's attempt to "seize power".
Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Friday accused the Congress and its allies of using protests in the national capital to seek a change of government along the lines of Bangladesh and using the energy of young people to spread "anarchy", news agency PTI reported.…
"Instead of channelling the energy of the youth toward nation-building, they are being used as pawns in the politics of anarchy," ​he said at a media briefing on Friday.

title: Saudi organisers say 2027 Asian Cup  on schedule  after attacks
description: Organisers say they will continue monitoring regional developments and security conditions
content:
Organisers say they will continue monitoring regional developments and security conditions
The Asian Cup in January is "on schedule", Saudi Arabian organisers said, after growing fears for the tournament following Houthi attacks on the country.
The continent's top football official said this week that the competition could be postponed to 2028, while stressing there was "no hurry" to make a decision.
The 2027 Asian Cup is supposed to kick off on January 7 in the Saudi cities of Jeddah, Riyadh and Al Khobar.
In a statement late Thursday, the local organising committee said: "Preparations remain on schedule for the tournament.
"This work continues in close coordination with the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and other relevant stakeholders."
Saudi Arabia has in recent days come under sustained attack in a dramatic escalation in the war with the Iran-backed Houthi group.
Several sporting events, including matches in domestic football, have been postponed.
The local organising committee for the Asian Cup, the region's most prestigious football tournament, said it "remains committed to keeping preparations on track and ensuring the necessary resources are in place to deliver a tournament that reflects Saudi Arabia's ambitions and standards as a host.
"At the same time, it will continue to monitor developments relevant to the tournament and ensure the appropriate conditions are in place for its successful delivery."
AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa told reporters on Wednesday they could wait until the end of November to make a final decision.
"We could move back a year to 2028 if we need to," he said.
"But at the moment we are monitoring the situation and everything is on schedule."

K-P governor stated that "in the decisions of the merged districts, the voice, traditions, and aspirations of the local population should be given fundamental importance", further adding that the new representatives should be in accordance with their own will and trust.
On Thursday, under the new administrative system, a series of jirgas were underway in the tribal districts of K-P to select members of the RDC and establish local representation.
For this purpose, jirgas and consultative meetings were held with local elders, scholars, and relevant stakeholders in Bajaur, Kurram, Bara, Khyber, Upper Dir, and Lower Dir to discuss the role of the RDC, local representation, public issues, and development needs.
The district administration and relevant authorities provided assistance in establishing an RDC and resolving public issues through consultation with local elders.
Local elders expressed confidence in the new administrative system and pledged to continue cooperating with government institutions, resolving public issues and working together for lasting peace and stability in the region.
Through this initiative, an attempt was being made to provide effective representation to the local population of the tribal districts by linking local traditions and community consultation with the administrative and development process.
Under the new administrative system, local people were to select councils in 12 districts of K-P, including Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, North Waziristan, South Waziristan Upper, South Waziristan Lower, Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Lakki Marwat and Bannu.
In this regard, jirgas were held a day earlier in Mohmand, Bannu and Waziristan with elders, scholars and local elders, during which the new administrative system, local representation in the RDC, the law and order situation and development needs were discussed.
The selection of RDC representatives in the remaining districts was also expected to be completed over the next two days.

Council members were being selected under the jirga system, taking into account the wishes of the local population, tribal traditions, and mutual consultation.
The purpose of selecting council members through the jirga was to provide representation to local elders and effectively convey the problems, needs, and development priorities of the area to the relevant authorities.
The purpose of the RDC was to identify development projects according to local needs, propose solutions to public problems and improve coordination with relevant administrative agencies.
The new administrative arrangements were introduced after the federal government imposed governor’s rule and emergency measures in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa on October 11.
Following the president’s approval on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, executive authority was transferred from the provincial government to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi. The federal government also formed an 11-member advisory council to oversee provincial administrative affairs and ordered the establishment of the RDC in the 12 designated districts.
The government said the measures were intended to improve security, strengthen governance, and accelerate development in areas affected by terrorism. The RDC is intended to provide a channel for local representation within the new arrangement, allowing communities to communicate their concerns and development priorities to the relevant authorities.

title: Infantino offers apology but  no answers  at FIFA meeting
description: Senior officials demand documents and explanations over the abandoned investment initiative
content:
Senior officials demand documents and explanations over the abandoned investment initiative
FIFA president Gianni Infantino gave "no satisfactory answers" when grilled Thursday during a meeting to discuss his attempts to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, senior members of football's global governing body said, but he did offer an apology for the failed project.
"We asked a great many critical questions, but there were no satisfactory answers from my point of view," said Bernd Neuendorf, the head of the German Football Association (DFB), who is also a member of the FIFA Council.
Neuendorf was speaking after the Council met behind closed doors at the body's Zurich headquarters, where Infantino's FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal was one of the main topics on the agenda.
Infantino has been under severe pressure since his announcement in late July that he wanted to open FIFA's premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors.
That plan was ultimately abandoned in the face of widespread criticism, with a rebellion led by European governing body UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and CONCACAF, which runs the sport in North and Central America and the Caribbean.
"I apologised for the mistakes that we made in relation to the communication and consultation process related to the FIFA Forward Enterprise project," Infantino said in a video published by FIFA.
"But what is important to remember is that it was a proposal, so in no way a done deal, just a proposal, that actually intended to enable FIFA to invest more in our member associations."
However, the FIFA chief reaffirmed that the FFE initiative "has been permanently withdrawn and will not reappear in any form".
Infantino has headed FIFA since 2016 and is running for re-election next March, despite calls for him to stand down in the wake of the FFE plan.
For the moment, no heavyweight candidate has put themselves forward to run against him.
Debbie Hewitt, the chair of the English Football Association who is also a FIFA vice-president, told reporters that Infantino is "not fit to be FIFA president" unless he releases all documents pertaining to the failed sell-off plan and answers key questions.
Hewitt and Neuendorf are among the 36 members of the FIFA Council, along with Infantino.
"We were asked to submit our questions" in relation to the plan which was not put to the FIFA Council before the July announcement, Hewitt said.
"One of the disappointing things was we didn't get answers. We didn't get answers to anything we had specifically requested, for example getting the papers from FFE, and so we asked the question why and why not."
Many leading European national associations have withdrawn their support for Infantino in the upcoming election because of the uproar caused by FFE and other controversies, including his relationship with US president Donald Trump.
Chief among those were Infantino's decision to create a FIFA Peace Prize and award it to Trump at last December's World Cup draw, and the decision to suspend a ban for United States striker Folarin Balogun following a red card during the World Cup after Trump intervened directly by phoning Infantino.
"I speak for myself as a Council member -- from my position nothing has shifted," Hewitt added. "I have no new information that makes me feel any differently to how I felt when I went in, other than we do have a president of FIFA who is apologetic about what has happened, and secondly a promise again that we will get the information that we have requested."
FIFA confirmed its intention to set up a $6.35-billion development fund for the next four years, a plan which is expected to be finalised by the Council at its next meeting in December.
To finance the fund, which would allow money to be distributed to FIFA's 211 federations as well as to the regional confederations, it would draw in part on its financial reserves after a commercially successful 2026 World Cup.
The plan would allow for the payment of $25 million to all 211 member federations.
Infantino may hope the latest plan reinforces his position ahead of the election.
The deadline for submitting candidacies is November 18.

title: Shooter kills four at Oregon elementary school before being shot dead by community member
description: The dead were children aged 5  8 and 11 and one    teacher  7 year old student and a 54 year old teacher were injured
content:
Dead were children aged 5, 8, 11, and one ​teacher; 7-year-old student and a 54-year-old teacher were injured
A 16-year-old shooter opened fire on Thursday at an elementary ‌school in Bend, Oregon, killing four people, including three children, before being killed by an armed member of the community who had pursued the assailant into the school, police said.
The shooter entered Silver Rail Elementary School by firing through locked doors, police said, without offering any details beyond the suspect's age.
The dead were children aged 5, 8 and 11 and one ​teacher. In addition, a 7-year-old student and a 54-year-old teacher were taken to hospital with critical injuries, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz ​told a press conference.
Oregon Governor Tina Kotek, appearing at the same briefing, thanked the community member who "heroically intervened to ⁠stop further loss of life."
"No parent should have to have this kind of day, and no community should have to live through this ​kind of day. And as we learn more about the children and the adults who have been killed or injured, and their families and their ​loved ones, we are going to do a lot of crying, and we are going to cry together, and we're probably going to cry privately," Kotek said.
Krantz said the community member, whom he did not identify, saw the suspect enter the school and pursued him.
Read: K-P orders safety checks at schools
School shootings have become a recurring feature of American life, including high-profile ​attacks such as those at Columbine High School in 1999, Sandy Hook Elementary School in 2012, Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in 2018, and ​Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, in 2022.
Each shooting revives debates over gun laws in a country where gun rights are protected under the Constitution's Second Amendment. ‌Gun rights ⁠advocates have argued for arming teachers as a means of defence.
Krantz said every Bend police officer went through a full day of active shooter training in August.
"Unfortunately, this is something we train for regularly, and we must," Krantz said. "This is going to be a long investigation."
Thursday's shooting took place in Bend, a city of about 100,000 people in rural central Oregon, 175 miles (280 km) southeast of Portland, in the ​Oregon high desert adjacent to the ​Deschutes National Forest.
Silver Rail Elementary School ⁠serves kindergarten through fifth grade, roughly ages 5 to 11, and has about 450 students and 40 staff members, officials said.
Read more: US arrests person in connection to Canada school shooting, officials say
Gun control advocate Gabrielle Giffords, a former congresswoman who survived a mass shooting in 2011, said ​in a statement she was "heartbroken" by the shooting in Bend.
"This cannot continue to be a reality in our ​country. Leaders at ⁠every level must step up and act,” Giffords said.
Emergency responders received a call at 12:59 pm PDT (1259 PKT on Friday) from a person in a vehicle who reported being shot at multiple times by someone with a long gun, Krantz said.
In the minutes afterwards, dozens of calls were received saying the shooter had entered ⁠the school, ​Krantz said. Law enforcement immediately directed the school to go into lockdown, he said.
Officers arrived ​at 1:02 pm (0 and moments later an officer reported the suspect had been shot, Krantz said. Police entered and confirmed the suspect was dead, he said.

title: Thousands march in Argentina to demand implementation of public university funding law
description: Protesters demand implementation of law to secure resources for universities  staff salaries  student scholarships
content:
Protesters demand implementation of law to secure resources for universities, staff salaries, student scholarships
Thousands of students, graduates, teachers and university staff marched to Argentina’s Congress in the capital, Buenos Aires, on Thursday to demand that President Javier Milei’s government implement a law guaranteeing funding for public universities.
“We demand that the government comply with the law once and for all,” said one of the university representatives.
The fifth Federal University March brought together university communities, trade unions, political parties and social organisations. The main demonstration took place outside Congress, where protesters called for increased university funding and salary adjustments.
Protesters demanded the implementation of the University Funding Law to secure resources for universities, staff salaries, and student scholarships.
The demonstration coincided with an opposition effort to debate the repeal of Decree 70/2023, signed by Milei shortly after he took office in December 2023. They failed to secure the quorum needed to open the special session in the Chamber of Deputies, however.
Read: Messi nets brace to win in first match after Argentina exit
The Senate rejected the measure in March 2024, but it remained in force pending action by the lower house. The decree introduced extensive changes to Argentina’s legal and economic framework, including the repeal of a law restricting foreign ownership of rural land.
The protests followed a court ruling ordering the government to implement the University Funding Law and update salaries and scholarships. The government appealed the decision. Authorities deployed security forces around Congress, erecting barriers and restricting traffic. Police used tear gas against protesters, according to local media.
The mobilisation was part of a nationwide day of demonstrations, with university communities and social organisations also gathering in other cities to demand funding for public higher education.

title: Peshawar school roof collapse  Case registered against owners  contractor
description: Case registered under section 322  148 and 149  FIR says substandard material was used in schools construction
content:
Case registered under section 322, 148 and 149; FIR says substandard material was used in schools construction
Police on Friday registered a case against the owners, shareholders, and contractor of the private school in Peshawar’s Dir Colony, where the roofs collapsed, killing 30 children and a female teacher and injuring 52 people, according to the first information report (FIR).
The roof of the three-storey Al-Khair school building in Peshawar’s Dir Colony collapsed during morning classes on Thursday, burying students and teachers beneath the rubble. Rescue teams worked for several hours to recover victims, while the building’s location in a densely populated neighbourhood with narrow streets hampered access to the site.
Police said the school had about 110 enrolled students and that the building’s weak structure and poorly constructed roof were among the factors being investigated. The school owner, Khan Muhammad, was taken into custody.
The case was registered at Agha Mir Jani Shah police station under Section 322, relating to qatl-bis-sabab (death caused without direct intent), and Sections 148 and 149 of the Pakistan Penal Code, police said, adding that efforts were underway to arrest the nominated suspects.
According to the FIR, substandard construction materials were used in the school building, which was in a dilapidated and unsuitable condition. It also stated that complaints had previously been made about the deteriorating condition of the building’s walls and roofs, but the school owners allegedly failed to address concerns raised by children.
The roofs of the nursery classroom on the second floor and rooms on the ground floor collapsed, the FIR stated.
The school land, measuring 16 marlas, is owned by Waheed and Javed. The land was acquired on lease in 2024, after which the school building was constructed.
Following Thursday’s collapse in Peshawar, the provincial government ordered a fact-finding inquiry and directed a structural safety audit of educational institutions across K-P. The Elementary and Secondary Education Department also recommended a province-wide survey of government school buildings to assess their structural condition and classify them according to safety risks.
The incident has renewed concerns over the structural safety of educational buildings in Pakistan, where similar collapses have killed and injured students in recent years.
On June 30, 2026, 14 children were killed when the roof of a private tuition centre collapsed in Lahore’s Kahna area. A teacher and eight other children were also injured. Police said the centre was housed in an ageing building, while the roof of an unfinished second floor reportedly gave way amid concerns over poor construction.
In May, at least four children were killed and 20 people injured when a classroom roof collapsed at a private school in Dera Ghazi Khan, Punjab, while construction work was under way to extend the building.
In September, five people were killed when a wall of a dilapidated government school building collapsed in Karachi’s Orangi Town, although the school was closed at the time.
The repeated incidents have raised questions about building maintenance, construction standards, and the enforcement of safety regulations at educational institutions.

title: Oil heads for weekly gain with Mideast supply risks
description: Brent crude futures fall 71 cents  or 0 67   to  105 21 a barrel
content:
Brent crude futures fall 71 cents, or 0.67%, to $105.21 a barrel
Oil prices eased on Friday ​but were heading for weekly gains on the uncertainty over Middle East supplies and a larger-than-expected crude ‌stocks draw in the United States.
Brent crude futures fell 71 cents, or 0.67%, to $105.21 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down 77 cents, or 0.79%, to $97.20.
WTI settled up more than 3% on Thursday after a big US crude stock ​draw on hurricane production shut-ins.
For this week so far, Brent increased 0.44%, while WTI jumped 5.81%.
"Uncertainty in the ​Middle East and concerns over the sustainability of oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz ⁠has the market pricing in a significant risk premium," ING analysts wrote in a note on Friday.
There needs to be ​some kind of agreement between the US and Iran to provide the market with more confidence that stronger oil flows ​from the region will continue, they added.
Supply jitters also rose as attacks around the Strait of Hormuz have surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it was stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month.
Total Hormuz ​clearance averaged 11.62 million barrels per day over seven days to October 13, about 68% of the 17.15 million ​bpd baseline, according to ship tracking firm Kpler.
"Intensified Iranian attacks drove Gulf crude flows sharply lower," Kpler analysts said in a report on ‌Thursday, ⁠adding that they expected a slower and more uneven Hormuz recovery, without a comprehensive political deal.
Read: Oil prices climb as Iran deploys new tactics to target ships transiting Hormuz
The Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing two guards, while the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen detailed dozens of attacks on Saudi infrastructure in the escalating conflict.
The International Energy Agency agreed on Thursday to release over 20 ​million barrels of diesel to the ​market and any oil ⁠remaining from a record release of emergency reserves pledged in March to boost supply and cool soaring prices.
During the previous trading session, oil prices rose overnight in a sign that "investors ​were dissatisfied with these measures," Haitong Futures said in a note on Friday.
"What would ​really cool the ⁠oil market is an easing of tensions in the Middle East."
The Trump administration is considering lifting sanctions on some so-called shadow fleet vessels that have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in an effort to reduce record-high ⁠global freight ​rates, a US official said on Wednesday.
The discussions come days after US ​President Donald Trump temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel fuel, a move met with criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, European countries and some of ​Trump's fellow Republicans.

title: Iran president says conflict in Mideast amounts to  ecocide
description: US president says he does not foresee deploying ground troops to strike suspected Iranian nuclear site
content:
Trump rules out use of nuclear weapons against Iran
Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian on Friday urged countries to condemn what he called "ecocide" in the Middle East caused by "wars of aggression".
Pezeshkian said the conflicts in Gaza and the wider Middle East had inflicted a significant toll on nature that extended beyond borders and required "international solutions".
"What has occurred in our region as a result of wars of aggression is ecocide, or environmental genocide, and it must be condemned," Pezeshkian told a nature summit in Armenia attended by UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres.
Trump rules out use of nuclear weapons against Iran
US President Donald Trump ruled out using nuclear weapons against Iran, saying Washington did not need them and emphasising that the "mother of all bombs" was non-nuclear.
Asked during an interview on Thursday with Newsmax about reports that his administration was considering using the bomb against Iran, potentially after the US midterm elections, Trump stressed that it was a conventional weapon.
"The mother of all bombs is not nuclear," Trump said, adding: "This is just an extremely large bomb."
He reiterated that the weapon was not nuclear.
"The mother of all bombs is one big bomb, but it's not nuclear," he said.
Trump ruled out using nuclear weapons, saying the US did not need to resort to them.
"No, I wouldn't use nuclear. We don't have to," he said.
Read: Pakistan, Iran to discuss regional peace efforts at OIC moot: IRNA
Trump also raised the possibility of further strikes against Iran's nuclear facilities, including a suspected underground site known as Pickaxe Mountain.
"Now, we're looking at Pickaxe Mountain. We may have to go there," he said.
"We'll take a shot at that one. We'll knock it out fast."
Asked whether such an operation would involve American ground troops, Trump replied: "No, I don't see that. I don't see that."
He said withdrawing before ensuring Iran could not obtain nuclear weapons might require further US military action within a year.
"We want to make it so that they will never have a nuclear weapon," he said.
Trump also predicted that the war would end soon, saying Tehran was negotiating with Washington.
"The Iran war will be over very soon. It's going to end very soon," he said.
Read more: Saudi Arabia accuses Iran of encouraging Houthis as attacks intensify
"One way or the other, it'll end very soon. And oil will go dropping like a rock — and gas prices as well."
Trump claimed Iranian officials had requested a halt to American and Israeli military operations.
"They've asked us to please stop. And we do, because we're negotiating with them," he said.
Asked whether he trusted Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Trump responded: "I don't trust anybody, honestly."
"I don't trust anybody," he said. "In the world of politics, I don't trust anybody."
Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until Iran’s rights are respected: army chief
Chief Commander of the Islamic Republic of Iran Army Major General Amir Hatami highlighted Iran's enemy's miscalculations in the recent war, saying that the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until the rights of the Iranian people were respected, according to IRNA on Friday.
Strait of Hormuz to remain closed until Iran’s rights are respected: Army chief https://t.co/ZpqDYZfEu5 pic.twitter.com/qu0jiSeixi
Speaking in a ceremony at Imam Ali Officers’ University in Tehran on Thursday, Major General Hatami said that the enemy’s miscalculation was the reason for the outbreak of the war, noting that it had assumed Iran was in a weak position and underestimated the capabilities of the country’s Armed Forces.
He added that the Iranian Army and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) responded with full force, launching many strikes against the enemy from the earliest hours of the imposed war.
Ousted US general warned before Iran war of missile defence shortages lasting until 2030: Report
Ousted US Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George warned months before the US-Israeli war against Iran that American missile defence stockpiles were critically low and could take until 2030 to recover, CBS News reported on Thursday.
George raised the warning in late December, two months before the conflict began, according to US officials familiar with his assessment. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth removed him from his post in April as the war was underway.
The general’s assessment, included in the Pentagon’s fiscal 2027 force allocation planning, identified shortages of Terminal High Altitude Area Defence (THAAD) interceptors and Patriot missiles, with supplies expected to remain at strategically low levels until 2030.
The officials reportedly attributed the shortfall to weapons transfers to Ukraine, US military support for Israel, and limited defence industry production capacity.
The war with Iran has further strained supplies, according to the report. A Centre for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) estimate found that US forces entered 2026 with approximately 2,300 Patriot interceptors and used between 1,050 and 1,430 during the conflict.
The country’s prewar THAAD inventory stood at around 355 interceptors, of which an estimated 190 to 290 were expended.
Mark Cancian, a retired Marine colonel and senior adviser at CSIS, told CBS News that these systems would be crucial in a potential conflict with China.
“Air defence — missile defence — that will be huge,” he said, explaining that a major confrontation with Beijing would demand substantial interceptor supplies.
Replenishing the stockpiles remains a lengthy process, the report said. The CSIS estimates that new THAAD interceptor contracts take over four years to fulfil, while Patriot PAC-3 orders take an average of 3 1/2 years.
The Pentagon rejected claims of a shortage. Chief spokesman Sean Parnell told CBS News : “Claims of US munitions shortages are false.”
He added that Washington retains “everything required to strike at the time and place of the President’s choosing.”

title: Three terrorists killed in Swat IBO
description: Three terrorists killed in Swat IBO
content:
Bodies recovered from hideout in Kanju area; weapons, maps and documents seized
Three wanted terrorists belonging to the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) were killed during a joint intelligence-based operation by the Swat Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and district police on Thursday. Two of their companions managed to flee the scene and are being actively searched for.
The Swat Region CTD received confirmed intelligence that several terrorists linked to the group of TTP commander Muzaffar alias Khalid were present in the mountainous stretches of Segram, Lalo Banda and adjoining areas under the jurisdiction of Kanju police station, intending to carry out sabotage activities.
A well-prepared operation was launched. At Sakhadoob within Kanju police station limits, the terrorists opened fire as soon as they spotted the security personnel. In the ensuing exchange, the militants took positions inside a nearby house and continued indiscriminate firing.
Once the shooting stopped, a search of the house yielded the bodies of three terrorists. The two remaining militants had already escaped; efforts to track them down are under way.
From the possession of the killed terrorists, security forces recovered three AK47 Kalashnikov rifles, six magazines and a large quantity of ammunition. A gas cylinder used for cooking and several utensils were also found at the hideout.
During the body search, national identity cards of the three slain militants, a map of Shakardara police station and a diary were recovered.
The deceased have been identified as Abdullah, son of Syed Bashir, resident of Neela Gram, Matta, Swat; Mansoor Ali, son of Abdul Muttalib, also of Neela Gram, Matta, Swat; and Ghufranullah, son of Afzal Khan, resident of Shidala, Shakardara, Swat.
Preliminary information indicates that the three were involved in multiple terrorist incidents this year. These include a firing attack on Afzal Khan Gujjar, firing on the house of Nemat Ali Khan, the targeted killing of Saleemullah alias Sajid of Neela Gram, and several other attacks.

Speaking on the occasion, Governor Kundi emphasised the need for better urban planning, particularly the provision of adequate parking facilities across Peshawar. He directed the relevant departments to identify important development schemes on a priority basis so that funds could be released without delay.
"Peshawar is the provincial capital and it must be developed into a modern city that meets contemporary urban requirements," the Governor said. He stressed that effective execution of development projects was essential for the overall uplift of the city and improvement in the quality of life of its residents.
Governor Kundi also issued specific instructions to the Forest Department, directing it to prepare a comprehensive strategy for obtaining carbon credits. He noted that such a plan would enable the people of the northern districts to benefit from the environmental and economic advantages of carbon trading.
Officials assured the Governor that work on priority projects would be accelerated and that coordination among departments would be strengthened to remove bottlenecks. The meeting concluded with a shared commitment to turn Peshawar into a model provincial capital that balances heritage preservation with modern infrastructure and sustainable urban growth.

title: Tragedy jolts officials out of slumber
