Education Dept forms fact-finding committee; probe ordered into structural failure at Al-Khair school; 93 children shi
The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Department of Elementary and Secondary Education has constituted a fact-finding committee to investigate the collapse of a classroom roof at the private Al-Khair Education System in Dir Colony, Peshawar.
The committee has been directed to submit its report on an urgent basis.
According to an official notification issued by the department, Managing Director of the K-P Private Schools Regulatory Authority (KPPSRA) Javed Iqbal will serve as chairman of the committee. Deputy Secretary (Primary) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Department Muhammad Farooq has been named a member, while the panel itself will nominate its third member.
The committee has been tasked with conducting a thorough inquiry into the incident. It will examine the causes of the roof collapse, assess any possible negligence, identify structural defects in the building's construction, and evaluate other contributing factors. Officials have also instructed the panel to recommend concrete measures aimed at preventing similar tragedies in the future and to submit appropriate recommendations.
The devastating incident at the private school in Dir Colony claimed the lives of 32 students and one female teacher. Dozens of other people were injured when the classroom ceiling gave way.
Education authorities moved swiftly to order the probe amid public concern over safety standards in private educational institutions. The formation of the fact-finding body signals an official effort to establish accountability and address potential systemic shortcomings in school infrastructure oversight across the province.
The committee's findings are expected to provide clarity on whether the collapse resulted from construction flaws, maintenance failures, or other lapses. Its recommendations could influence future regulations governing private schools in K-P.
Meanwhile, Lady Reading Hospital received 61 children from the site. Thirty-one were declared dead; the remaining 30 were treated and discharged. No child remained under treatment by evening. Naseerullah Babar Memorial Hospital admitted 32 children; two of them died. Of those brought to the second hospital, 26 were boys and six were girls.
The emergency wards filled with the continuous wail of ambulance sirens. Medical staff and bystanders stood in tears as injured children were carried in. Distraught parents, some without proper shoes, ran from stretcher to stretcher searching for their sons and daughters. Mothers wept and pleaded with doctors for any information. The hospital activated its full emergency protocol, calling in all on-call staff and establishing a help desk to register victims and guide relatives. The sudden influx of onlookers forced administrators to request additional security to clear the area and allow ambulances to move freely.
According to the final list released by LRH, the dead included 14 girls and several teachers. Most of the children were aged between six and 13. Four children remained unidentified at the time of reporting.

content:

The police registered a murder case against 19 suspects, including four nominated and 15 unidentified men, and launched a search for them. The District Bar Association announced a strike and boycotted court proceedings after the murder case was registered against former secretary Rana Murtaza Hakeem.
According to the FIR registered at Tandlianwala city police station on the complaint of Zafar Iqbal, a resident of Chak 410-GB, Murtaza Hakeem had purchased 200 kanal of land from Rai Faisal, Iftikhar, Imtiaz and others around two years ago to launch a housing society.
He had subsequently sold a portion of the land to Rai Shehzad, who planned to build a marriage hall there.
However, Rai Faisal and others allegedly stopped him, claiming that their payment had not been cleared and they would not allow the construction until the matter was settled.
They allegedly deployed their 24-year-old employee, Muhammad Boota, at the site. Shehzad then contacted Hakeem and asked him to resolve the dispute.
The FIR stated that Hakeem arrived at the site the following day with his brother, Azhar Waseem, Ashfaq, Imran and other armed men in several vehicles.
An argument reportedly broke out, followed by an exchange of gunfire, during which Boota was injured. He died while being taken to a hospital.
Police officers reached the scene after receiving information about the incident. The suspects allegedly fled while firing into the air.
The police handed over the body to the family of the decessed after post-mortem examination and registered the case under sections 302, 148 and 149 of the Pakistan Penal Code. An investigation was under way.
SHO Ahmed Muneel Shah said Hakeem had purchased the land and sold a portion of it to Shehzad, who was Rai Faisal's brother-in-law.
When Shehzad began laying the foundations for a marriage hall, Faisal and others allegedly objected.
Shehzad then called Hakeem and his associates, leading to a confrontation in which Boota was killed in the exchange of fire, the SHO said.
Meanwhile, District Bar Association President Mian Muhammad Tariq and Secretary Chaudhry Kaleemullah Gul condemned the registration of the case against Hakeem, describing the FIR as baseless.

title: Smog threat looms despite rain
description: Smog threat looms despite rain
content:
Downpour brings citizens brief relief from air pollution
After many days of hazy skies and pollution, Lahore welcomed clear weather following rainfall with a refreshing breeze and pleasant temperatures bringing residents relief.
The rainfall in the metropolis and several other parts of Punjab brought relief from air pollution, leaving an improved air quality.
However, the respite may prove temporary, as dry weather is expected to return, raising concerns that pollutants could gradually accumulate again and intensify the seasonal smog threat in the coming days.
The Punjab Environmental Protection Agency's real-time monitoring dashboard recorded Lahore's overall Air Quality Index (AQI) at 71 at 10:00am on Thursday, placing the city in the satisfactory category.
The reading was substantially lower than the 132 recorded at the same hour a day earlier, indicating a marked improvement in the air quality.
The dashboard showed that conditions varied across monitoring stations with Multan Road recording an AQI of 109, while Safari Park reported 41.
The improvement follows a spell of rain and unsettled weather in Lahore and nearby areas. The rain that began overnight helped remove suspended particles from the atmosphere, while accompanying air movement dispersed pollutants that accumulate over urban areas.
Reduced airborne dust and improved visibility made outdoor conditions more comfortable.
The Pakistan Meteorological Department indicated that temperatures across Punjab remained moderate.
The absence of widespread rainfall means that continued improvement in air quality will depend on wind movement and the amount of pollution released into the atmosphere.
With predominantly dry conditions forecast for Lahore from Friday onwards, the immediate cleansing effect of the rain may gradually diminish.
"If emissions continue and winds remain insufficient to disperse pollutants, the city could experience another increase in particulate pollution, particularly during the early morning and nighttime hours," said an EPD official.
Punjab generally experiences its smog season from October through February, when cooler weather conditions, transport emissions, industrial smoke and other pollution sources combine to worsen air quality.
Vehicle exhaust, industrial emissions, smoke from brick kilns, construction dust and the burning of agricultural residue can contribute to the pollution.
When rain temporarily clears the atmosphere, pollution levels can rise again after the weather becomes dry.
Environmental experts regard rainfall as a short-term natural mechanism for reducing airborne particles. The duration of the improvement depends on the intensity of the rain, wind speed, humidity, atmospheric stability and the rate at which fresh emissions enter the air.
In Faisalabad, a spell of early-morning rain brought a respite from lingering heat but also inundated low-lying areas, causing inconvenience to residents, especially pedestrians.
According to a WASA spokesman, Gulfishan Colony recorded the highest precipitation at 26 millimeters, followed by Jail Road with 25mm, Ghulam Muhammad Abad and Dogar Basti 24mm each, Madina Town 22mm and Allama Iqbal Colony 21mm.
Dark clouds began gathering over the city on Wednesday evening but the rain started at around 4:00am and continued until 5:10am, turning several low-lying areas into pools. With additional input from APP

title: Tharis on the move as drought drives livestock exodus
description: Tharis on the move as drought drives livestock exodus
content:
Failed rains, withered crops, soaring food costs deepen hunger, malnutrition
With rain-fed crops failing, natural grazing drying up and fodder running short, drought-hit families in Tharparkar district are once again packing up and migrating with their livestock in search of water and food, as rising food costs and child malnutrition compound the crisis on World Food Day.
Farmers who sowed millet, guar and other rain-dependent crops after initial rainfall this year have watched their hopes fade as subsequent rains failed to arrive on time. Parched fields and withered vegetation have left both families and their animals struggling to survive, forcing livestock owners to abandon their villages for the irrigated barrage areas.
For many, the journey means carrying provisions for more than a week and surviving on dry bread, jaggery and water along the way.
Khemoon Bhel, a livestock owner from Vee Hangorja village in Mithi taluka, is among those heading towards the barrage region. He said he had cultivated 20 acres of land after the initial rains, but the subsequent dry spell destroyed his crops and left his animals without fodder.
Having returned to his village from the barrage areas only two months ago, Bhel is now being forced to migrate again with his livestock. The money he spent on tractor work and purchasing seeds has gone to waste, with little prospect of recovering his investment through the failed harvest.
For rural households across Tharparkar, the consequences extend far beyond lost crops. Their livelihoods depend heavily on seasonal rainfall, limited agricultural production and livestock. When crops fail and grazing grounds dry up, families lose not only their grain harvest but also access to fodder, milk and a crucial source of income.
The crisis is further aggravated by the cost of food. With local wheat production limited, most households depend on market purchases to meet their staple food needs. Failed crops, shrinking livelihood opportunities and rising prices are making it increasingly difficult for poor families to afford adequate meals.
The strain on household food supplies is also raising concerns about malnutrition among children and pregnant women.
A medical study examining 129 children treated for severe acute malnutrition at Mithi Civil Hospital between March and June 2024 found that 117, or 90.7 per cent, were suffering from anaemia. The findings were published in a scientific paper in January 2026.
Rainwater harvesting, drought-resilient crops, reliable fodder and water supplies for livestock, affordable staple foods and targeted assistance for vulnerable families are among the measures needed to strengthen food security. Better nutritional screening and treatment for children and pregnant women must also be prioritised.
The district administration has yet to declare Tharparkar calamity-hit or initiate the process of seeking relief measures from the Sindh government, prompting local social activist and lawyer Qurban Samejo to file a constitutional petition before the Sindh High Court's Mirpurkhas circuit.
Samejo alleged that the district administration had neither conducted the required survey and forwarded it to the provincial government nor shown any apparent intention to do so, despite deteriorating conditions on the ground. He said the court had summoned the National Disaster Management Authority, relevant Sindh govt departments and the deputy commissioner to submit reports in connection with the petition.
Lawyer Ashiq Ali said drought-like conditions recurred in Thar every three to four years, with climate change further intensifying the district's vulnerability.

description:
City's Rs24b garbage 
business fails to deliver
content:
PAC questions failure to turn rubbish into revenue or electricity
Sindh's Public Accounts Committee (PAC) has exposed a four-year delay in implementing the 2021 amendments to the Sindh Solid Waste Management Board Act, with divisional boards yet to be constituted and the institution still operating without the rules required under the amended law. The disclosure came as lawmakers questioned why Karachi's waste management system, despite consuming Rs24 billion annually, had failed to generate revenue from the city's rubbish or produce electricity from it.
At its meeting on Thursday, chaired by Nisar Khuhro, the PAC directed the Local Government Department to establish divisional-level boards under the chairmanship of mayors and frame the necessary rules in accordance with a Sindh cabinet decision.
The proposed boards are to be established in Karachi, Hyderabad, Sukkur, Mirpurkhas, Shaheed Benazirabad and Larkana.
The committee reviewed audit paragraphs concerning the Sindh Solid Waste Management Board's Karachi operations for 2023 and 2024. The audit raised concerns over the failure to generate revenue through waste recycling and the absence of arrangements to produce electricity from discarded waste, depriving the public of a potential source of lower-cost power.
Khuhro asked how much waste the institution collected across Sindh, how much it spent on collection and what revenue it generated from the material.
Managing Director Fawad Ghaffar Soomro told the committee that the board had an annual budget of Rs28 billion, of which Rs24 billion was spent on collecting waste in Karachi alone. The city generated an estimated 10,000 to 12,000 tonnes of waste daily. Three Chinese companies and one Turkish company had been contracted to collect waste in Karachi, Soomro told the committee.
He said door-to-door waste collection had been launched in one Karachi district, following a model used in Larkana. Around 70% of the city's population lived in established residential areas, where waste was collected from high-rise buildings through bins, while trolley-based collection was used in the remaining 30%, largely comprising informal settlements. The board had also entered into an agreement with DHA for waste recycling, he added.

title: Blows to head suspected in elderly couple s murder
description: Blows to head suspected in elderly couple s murder
content:
Couple had planned to sell the house and two adjoining shops before returning to Canada
What began as a grisly disturbing discovery at a North Karachi residence has taken a grim turn, with initial post-mortem findings suggesting that an elderly couple were killed by repeated blows to the head with a hard, blunt object.
The bodies of 70-year-old Muhammad Yameen and his 65-year-old wife, Nafees Akhtar, were found inside their house on Wednesday night, triggering a murder investigation. The initial medical findings have established multiple head injuries on both victims, although the precise circumstances surrounding their deaths remain under investigation.
The couple had recently returned to Pakistan from Canada and were staying at the North Karachi property, which they had allowed relatives to use for a long time. Renovation and maintenance work was underway at the house, adding another dimension to the police probe.
The couple had planned to sell the house and two adjoining shops before returning to Canada, where their two sons and a daughter reside.
Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed said samples had been collected to determine whether the victims had been administered any intoxicating substance or poison. The final findings will be compiled after the chemical analysis report is received.
Investigators from the Sir Syed police station said evidence had been collected from the crime scene. No signs of robbery were found at the house, prompting investigators to examine the possibility of personal enmity as a motive for the killings. Police are reviewing CCTV footage from cameras installed in the surrounding area and tracing labourers who had been working at the couple's house as part of the investigation.

title: Septuagenarian man dies of  rabies
description: Septuagenarian man dies of  rabies
content:
Medical staff initiated emergency treatment and consulted the neuromedicine team
A 70-year-old man died at Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC) after developing symptoms of suspected rabies nearly 20 days after being bitten by a dog, taking the reported rabies-related death toll in Sindh to 39 this year.
Syed Ghulam Rasool, a resident of Baldia Town, had sustained dog bites to his left hand and foot but had not received anti-rabies vaccination following the incident, hospital officials said.
According to hospital records, he was brought to the emergency department at 2:16am on October 14 in critical condition, with severe muscle stiffness and hydrophobia, or fear of water - symptoms associated with rabies.
Medical staff initiated emergency treatment and consulted the neuromedicine team. He was subsequently admitted to the FGO ward on suspicion of rabies encephalitis, a potentially fatal inflammation of the brain caused by the virus. However, he could not survive.
With his death, the number of reported rabies cases in Sindh this year has reached 39, according to the figures provided. These include nine cases at JPMC, 28 at Indus Hospital Karachi and one at Indus Hospital Badin.
Health experts warn that rabies is almost invariably fatal once clinical symptoms appear, but timely medical intervention after exposure can prevent the disease.
According to World Health Organisation guidance, anyone bitten or scratched by a suspected rabid animal should immediately wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical attention without delay. Post-exposure prophylaxis, including anti-rabies vaccination and rabies immunoglobulin when indicated, is essential to prevent the infection from progressing.

title: Sindh seals 34 MoUs at Shanghai moot
description: Sindh seals 34 MoUs at Shanghai moot
content:
CM offers 10-year tax holiday to attract Chinese investment in energy, other sectors
The Sindh government has secured 34 memorandums of understanding (MoUs) with Chinese and Pakistani businesses and government entities at an investment conference in Shanghai, seeking to attract investment in energy, manufacturing, agriculture and emerging technologies.
Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, addressing the media after the second Sindh Investment Conference, said the agreements covered government-to-government (G2G) and business-to-business (B2B) cooperation, with the aim of creating jobs, expanding industry and strengthening economic ties.
The day-long conference, held after a gap of 12 years, attracted around 400 delegates, including investors, business leaders, Chinese companies and financial institutions.
Shah described Sindh as a cost-effective destination for manufacturers and exporters, citing its strategic location, skilled workforce, industrial capacity and access to regional markets.
"Shanghai transformed its economy by promoting investment, and Karachi is poised to scale new heights of development through a similar model," he said.
A major focus was the Dhabeji Special Economic Zone (SEZ), a China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) priority project spanning approximately 1,530 acres in Thatta district. Proposed industrial clusters include automotive manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, electronics, textiles, steel and warehousing.
Shah said investors in special economic zones could benefit from a 10-year income-tax exemption and duty-free imports of capital goods, subject to applicable laws. The Sindh Investment Department has also established a dedicated China Desk and a Single Window Facility Centre to facilitate investors. Each agreement would be assigned a focal person and reviewed at the highest level of the provincial government, he said. "For us, the signing is the beginning of the work, not the end."
Key areas of cooperation include Thar coal utilisation, coal-to-chemicals, renewable energy, electric vehicle manufacturing, charging infrastructure and mineral processing. Sindh's wind-energy potential is estimated at around 50,000 megawatts.
The province is also seeking investment in artificial intelligence, cloud computing and data centres. Under its People's Information Technology Programme, around 1,500 young people are trained annually to meet digital-sector requirements.
The conference highlighted the 435-acre Education City Special Technology Zone, which aims to attract investment in software, financial technology, biotechnology, clean energy and electronics.
Agriculture and food processing offer further opportunities, including rice processing, mango-pulp production, date processing and red-chilli dehydration, supported by modern technology, cold-chain facilities and export logistics.
Shah said Karachi's commercial importance and Sindh's two major seaports offered investors access to domestic and international markets.
Karachi Port handled approximately 53.95 million tonnes of cargo and 2.651 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) of containers in 2024-25, while Port Qasim has an annual handling capacity of around 89 million tonnes. The chief minister cited existing Chinese-backed projects, including Shanghai Electric's 1,320-megawatt Thar Block-I power plant, operational since 2023, and the Port Qasim coal-fired power project.

Education experts and former college principals have called on the Higher Education Department to address the severe shortage of professors and lecturers in colleges across the province by rationalising teaching staff rather than hiring daily-wage college teaching interns.
They have demanded that surplus professors and lecturers be identified and transferred to colleges facing staff shortages.
Retired principals said the rationalisation process in colleges had been planned in 2010 but was not implemented despite all the necessary administrative preparations.
It was subsequently postponed to 2011 and, according to them, the same practice has continued for the past 16 years.
They alleged that despite preparations for rationalisation, the process is repeatedly postponed at the beginning of the academic year on one pretext or another.
As a temporary measure, hundreds of college teaching interns and temporary daily-wage teachers are hired at colleges facing staff shortages. According to the former principals, millions of rupees are being spent every month on their salaries.
Former principals and professors supported the demand for immediate rationalisation, calling all surplus teachers to be transferred to colleges where they are needed.

title: Liaquat s assassination remains unresolved
description: Liaquat s assassination remains unresolved
content:
75 years and three probes later, no one has yet been brought to trial for first premier's killing
The 75th death anniversary of Pakistan's first prime minister, Nawabzada Liaquat Ali Khan, is being observed today, with the mystery surrounding his assassination on Oct 16, 1951, at a public gathering in Rawalpindi's historic Company Bagh, now called Liaquat Bagh, remaining unresolved.
Even after 75 years, it remains unclear who killed or arranged the killing of the country's first prime minister, and why.
Three investigations were conducted into the assassination: a police investigation, a judicial commission inquiry and an investigation by Britain's Scotland Yard. However, none produced a conclusive outcome.
The case was never brought before a court, and a challan was never prepared or submitted. It was eventually shelved at the police station.
Liaquat Ali Khan had arrived at Liaquat Bagh on Oct 16, 1951, to address a large public gathering.
As the meeting began, Syed Akbar Khan, allegedly an Afghan national standing at the front, opened fire with a pistol. Both bullets struck the prime minister, who was rushed to the Military Hospital but succumbed to his injuries.
Police shot and killed the alleged assassin at the scene, leaving key questions surrounding the murder unanswered.
A two-member judicial commission comprising Justice Muhammad Munir and Justice Akhtar Hussain was formed to investigate the assassination. Scotland Yard also conducted an inquiry.
Both investigations attributed the killing to the assassin's personal act, a conclusion that has never been universally accepted.
Aftab Mir, a 95-year-old resident of the adjoining historic Arya Mohalla neighbourhood, recalled witnessing the events as a young man.
He said he was fully conscious of what was happening at the time and had gone to listen to the gathering because his home was nearby. He climbed onto the railing along Murree Road to listen to the speech.
The gathering had barely begun when gunshots rang out, triggering panic and a stampede. People standing on the railings jumped towards the Murree Road side.
He said they subsequently learnt that Liaquat Ali Khan had been killed and the assassin had also died.
Mir recalled that when they entered Liaquat Bagh after the crowd had dispersed, hundreds of shoes and bicycles were scattered around the venue. Many bicycles had been knocked over during the stampede.
He said a truck arrived at night and took away the bicycles and shoes, after which he had no further information about them.
Liaquat Bagh is also where former prime minister Benazir Bhutto was assassinated. The circumstances surrounding the killings of both leaders remain unresolved, with little prospect of the mysteries being solved, the report said.
The giant nameboard at the main gate of the historic Company Bagh, now known as Liaquat Bagh, was brought down by heavy pre-monsoon rain and a storm earlier this year. However, it has not been reinstalled even after four and a half months, reportedly because of a severe financial crisis.
The park, which is around 300 years old, had a signboard installed three years ago at a cost of hundreds of thousands of rupees.

title: 150 mini dams for Potohar
description: 150 mini dams for Potohar
content:
Punjab launches second phase of three-year agriculture transformation plan
The Punjab Agriculture Department has launched the second phase of a project to construct mini dams in the rain-fed Potohar region, offering a 70 per cent subsidy to promote year-round irrigation, horticulture and fish farming under a three-year Agriculture Transformation Plan.
During the first phase, 111 mini dams were completed in the previous fiscal year. Under the second phase, 150 mini dams are planned in the Rawalpindi division by June 30, 2027.
A subsidy of Rs1.75 million is being provided for each mini dam, and billions of rupees have been released for the project.
Under the initiative launched by Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz for the Potohar region, rainwater will be stored in mini dams and used for irrigation.
The project is expected to help prevent soil erosion, reduce damage caused by floods, ensure water availability for cultivable land throughout the year and improve groundwater levels. It is also expected to promote profitable activities such as horticulture and dairy farming.
Farmers have welcomed the initiative. Growers Afzal Ali and Faizan said the project would benefit them by ensuring water supplies for crops and orchards throughout the year.
They added that fish could be raised in the mini dams to provide fish for household consumption, while the water bodies could also encourage the presence of aquatic birds.

title: School bags burden young shoulders
description: School bags burden young shoulders
content:
Parents have expressed serious concern over the burden of heavy school bags on young children, saying the daily weight is affecting their health, comfort and ability to concentrate in class.
Every morning outside schools, parents can be seen helping young children carry bags that appear disproportionately large for their small frames. According to parents, the bags are often overloaded with textbooks, notebooks, water bottles and lunch boxes, making them difficult for children to carry.
Orthopaedic doctor Dr Bilal of Rawalpindi says many young patients are reporting shoulder and back pain linked to heavy school bags.
"We are seeing many young patients complaining of shoulder and back pain due to heavy school bags," he said, adding that excessive weight could affect spinal development, cause muscle strain and lead to poor posture if left unaddressed.
He said a child's school bag should weigh no more than 10 to 15% of their body weight. Carrying excessive weight, he added, could place additional pressure on the spine and shoulders, causing fatigue, headaches and difficulty walking properly.
Dr Bilal said children were still developing physically and prolonged pressure from heavy bags could cause tiredness throughout the day, potentially affecting their concentration and learning
Atiqa, the mother of a seven-year-old Class 2 student, said her daughter's bag is so heavy that she could not lift it properly. "I have to carry it to the school van daily, and in the evening she complains of pain in her shoulders," she said.
She said her daughter leave for school happily but return exhausted and often avoid homework because of fatigue.

Families of two young men who earn their living by selling flowers in the federal capital have approached the Islamabad police chief at his open court, alleging that police illegally detained the men for eight days, extorted Rs0.23 million from their relatives and threatened to implicate them in false cases if they failed to pay an additional Rs1 million.
The inspector general of police (IGP) has directed the assistant superintendent of police (ASP) of Ramna Circle to investigate the allegations.
In a written application submitted at the IGP's open court, Babar Ali and Hakim Ali stated that their brothers, Sher Ali, son of Allah Rakha, and Hashim Ali, son of Allah Ditta, worked at a flower and decoration shop in I-10.
They alleged that around eight to nine days ago, 10 to 12 men in plain clothes picked up their brothers from the shop without any apparent offence and shifted them to Shalimar police station.
According to the application, at around 9pm the same day, police personnel entered their homes in Mirabadi without a court order, violating the sanctity of their homes.
They allegedly took away a motorcycle purchased on instalments from Sher Ali's house and a Vivo mobile phone from Hashim Ali's residence.
The applicants further stated that their brothers had previously been acquitted in a case and no case against them was currently pending before a court.
They alleged that when they went to Shalimar police station to meet their brothers, a police officer demanded a bribe of Rs1 million and threatened to implicate them in serious criminal cases and send them to jail if they failed to pay.
The applicants said they were forced to pay Rs230,000 in cash. Despite the payment, they alleged, further demands were being made and their family members were being threatened with detention.
They claimed their brothers had been kept in illegal confinement for the past eight to nine days and had not been produced before any court.
When contacted by *The Express*, Islamabad police spokesperson Jawad Taqi confirmed that the two complainants had appeared at the IGP's open court on Thursday.

title: Pindi s historic graveyards face neglect
description: Pindi s historic graveyards face neglect
content:
Centuries-old cemeteries preserve city's history, house graves of prominent figures
The 52 historic graveyards of Rawalpindi, a city with an ancient heritage, are not only running out of burial space but also preserving an enduring record of its history.
These cemeteries contain the graves of influential personalities who once wielded considerable power, while their old tombstones offer glimpses into the city's past.
The history of Rawalpindi's graveyards stretches back around 500 years. An old grave dating back to 1650, belonging to Kashmiri prince Abdul Sattar, is located in the Talian Shahaan graveyard near Committee Chowk.
The Eidgah graveyard houses the approximately 200-year-old grave of Sheikh Habibullah, a prominent notable of Amritsar, India.
At Dhoke Ratta graveyard, a grave belonging to a woman, Bakht Bibi, bears the date July 3, 1833. The cemetery is also the final resting place of the mother of film star Sultan Rahi, cricketer Mian Bakhsh and prominent city figure Lala Syed Mir.
The Christian cemetery on Harley Street, commonly known as the Gora Cemetery, contains the grave of the late Bishop of Calcutta, Robert Millman, with a tombstone dating back to 1876. Established in the early 1800s, the historic cemetery has also been visited by Queen Elizabeth and Lady Diana.
The cemetery contains the graves of 357 soldiers who died in the First and Second World Wars. Lady Diana visited the Gora Cemetery during her trip to Pakistan in 1997 for the country's Golden Jubilee celebrations.
The Parsi cemetery on Murree Road is around 180 years old. Meanwhile, the 350-year-old Hindu cremation ground, known as Nishan Ghat, was removed from Pirodhai around 30 years ago.
A new site was subsequently established outside the city, near the medical university.
The modern graveyard at Dhoke Illahi Bakhsh, which is around 169 years old, contains the grave of the wife of a nephew of former Indian prime minister Indira Gandhi who had converted to Islam. It also contains the graves of 11 members of a family who were killed during the Hathora Group incidents in General Ziaul Haq's era.
The history of the Army Cemetery in Westridge spans more than a century. It is the final resting place of former army chiefs and Syed Sharafuddin, father of former president General Pervez Musharraf.
Other graveyards dating back 200 to 300 years include those at Talian Shahaan, Dhoke Ratta, Dhoke Khabba, Dhoke Illahi Bakhsh, Eidgah, Gora Cemetery, Jhanda Chichi, the Army Cemetery, the Air Force Cemetery, Morgah and Shah Pyara.
However, the graveyards are now filled with graves and face numerous problems, including widespread encroachments, a lack of streetlights and bushes growing three to five feet high. Rainwater accumulates at several places, while the overgrowth provides shelter for snakes and mongooses.
Gambling, alcohol consumption and drug sales are reportedly widespread in the graveyards. Drug use and street robberies have also become common. Activities involving fake spiritual healers, rituals and black magic are reportedly taking place at the sites. The graveyards have also become crime hotspots and are contributing to the spread of dengue, residents say.

title: Three dead in Istanbul deluge
description: Three dead in Istanbul deluge
content:
Turkish city sees heaviest rainfall in 80 years
Istanbul was battling on Thursday to recover from flooding caused by what officials described as the heaviest rainfall in at least 80 years, as the toll rose to three dead and five missing.
The rain began lashing Turkiye's largest city in earnest on Wednesday morning and intensified throughout the day, causing chaos and flash flooding, with footage showing cars being dragged away by the fast-flowing waters.
"We are talking here about the highest level of precipitation in Istanbul since records began in 1942," Istanbul governor Davut Gul said.The death toll from the floods rose to three when authorities found a man's body near a park in the Kagithane area on the European side, Gul's office said in a statement.
The storm also claimed the life of a 14-year-old boy who was electrocuted when he stepped into a puddle in the Balat area. He was rushed to hospital but medical personnel were unable to save him, officials said.
Five others were missing, officials said.
In Beykoz, on Istanbul's Asian side, DHA news agency said another man had died after falling into a well while trying to drain the water at a school construction site. There was no immediate official confirmation of his death.
Istanbul municipal teams and firefighters were carrying out cleanup operations at schools, football pitches, garages and other sites on Thursday, pumping water out of flooded areas and clearing mud, an AFP photographer reported.
On Wednesday evening, the governor said schools would be shut across Istanbul until Monday, urging people to stay home "unless absolutely necessary" and advising those living in basement properties "to spend the night on safer, higher floors".
Dramatic footage posted online late Wednesday and collated by DHA showed a line of parked cars in the northern Sariyer district being pushed into the torrent of muddy water, where they were swept away.
Another showed people being hauled from the raging waters to safety through a first-floor window, while elsewhere two people with umbrellas were seen stepping into the shovel of a large mechanical digger, which took them away.
Power and water cuts have also hit areas of the city, notably in Sariyer where shopkeepers could be seen trying to salvage their goods from the mud, an AFP journalist said.

title: India poised to surpass Japan in GDP
description: India poised to surpass Japan in GDP
content:
India is expected to become the world's fourth-largest economy by 2027, overtaking Japan, according to International Monetary Fund (IMF) projections that on Thursday laid out the Asian nations' contrasting trajectories.
The IMF said Japan would remain the fourth-largest country by nominal gross domestic product this year, but in 2027 India is set to take its place, with a GDP reaching $4.52 trillion.
Japan is slated to slip to sixth place that year, falling behind both India and the United Kingdom, the projection showed.
India has shown strong growth in recent years despite global economic headwinds, with the IMF this week raising its forecasts for 2026 growth to hit 7%.
Japan, by contrast, is plagued by an ageing population and other structural problems that have seen the Asian giant's growth stagnate.
The United States is the world's largest economy, followed by China and Germany.

title: Zelensky defies Trump s call for restraint
description: Zelensky defies Trump s call for restraint
content:
Putin vows revenge after Kyiv resumes refinery attacks
Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday that recent Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries had not caused significant damage and vowed that Moscow would respond, Interfax reported.
"They hit here and there. Nothing particularly significant. Nevertheless they are carrying on," Putin said.
His comments came after a major Ukrainian drone attack ignited a fire at an oil refinery in Russia's Ryazan region on Thursday morning, according to the regional governor.
It was the first confirmed Ukrainian attack on a Russian energy facility since US President Donald Trump announced on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an energy ceasefire.
On Wednesday, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said that Ukraine had attacked oil refineries in the Saratov and Ryazan regions, although Ukraine denied any involvement.
Ukraine resumed its attacks on Russia's energy infrastructure on Thursday, after the governor of the Ryazan region in western Russia revealed there had been a strike on a major oil refinery in the territory overnight.
The strike had caused a large fire, but led to no casualties and temporary school closures, according to authorities.
The Ukrainian attacks targeting Russian oil come after Zelensky's fury at US President Trump for signing a 'treacherous' deal with Putin to buy Russian diesel on Friday.
Trump has, in recent days, demanded Zelensky quit as leader and blamed Zelensky for spiralling energy prices.
Zelensky, meanwhile, lambasted Trump over his apparent admiration for Putin, accusing the US president of having an instinctive affinity for autocrats and the super-wealthy.
"He [Trump] speaks about it openly and loudly that he loves such people and he respects such people. Because for him people who can be leaders 20 years, 30 years, 40 years, it means they can be very strong," Zelensky said.
Washington piled pressure on Kyiv to stop striking Putin's refineries, claiming that a moratorium, alongside a US deal with Moscow to buy hundreds of thousands of tonnes of Russian diesel, is necessary to bring down American fuel prices.
Zelensky condemned the US' deal with Russia, arguing it would help Russia prolong its brutal invasion of Ukraine

title: UN reports Afghan detentions
description: UN reports Afghan detentions
content:
The United Nations mission in Afghanistan said on Thursday that Taliban morality police arbitrarily detained hundreds of people and subjected dozens to ill-treatment between July and September, allegations the Taliban rejected.
The UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) said it documented 443 arbitrary arrests and detentions and 97 cases of ill-treatment by morality police during the three-month period.
The incidents were linked to alleged violations of rules on women's hijab, restrictions on beards and hairstyles, compulsory prayer attendance and bans on music, UNAMA said.
When the Taliban returned to power five years ago, amid the withdrawal of the US and its allies, they promised to govern more liberally than they had in the late 1990s and early 2000s.
But those assurances quickly faltered, human rights groups say, with sweeping restrictions on women and girls.
The report also recorded four killings and 14 arbitrary detentions of former Afghan security force members despite a general amnesty announced after the Taliban returned to power in 2021.
Taliban spokesperson Zabiullah Mujahid rejected the findings, saying detentions were lawful and accusing UNAMA of conducting propaganda against the government.

title: Israeli firm used online ads to run vast spy op
description: Israeli firm used online ads to run vast spy op
content:
Israeli digital advertising agency Discover-Tech spied on internet users through a sprawling network of online ads that it used to track targets and help hack their devices, two research groups said on Thursday.
Its services gave Israel's Candiru - a spyware company blacklisted by the US government - as well as other Israeli surveillance firms access to advertising platforms run by Google, Comcast, Russia's Yandex and others, according to separatereports from Canadian cyber watchdog group Citizen Lab and New York advertising security firm Confiant.
The reports show how the online advertising business, long a subject of privacy concerns, can also serve as a channel for sweeping espionage campaigns.
"The way online advertising works today is a systemic security threat," Wolfie Christl, a senior researcher at Citizen Lab, told Reuters. "For states, the private sector, civil society and everyone else alike."
Discover-Tech's online ads - often for ordinary products such as phones or earbuds - reached more than 120,000 websites and 75,000 apps through its various partnerships, Citizen Lab said.
Users who visited sites or used apps with the malicious ads could be identified and tracked by Discover-Tech, which would sometimes also try to extract phone numbers from some smartphone users, the researchers said. Ads only needed to load on a website for the spying to occur.
Some ads would be used to help plant spyware from Candiru on users' devices, both research groups said, though Confiant said that ads it tied to Candiru were a tiny fraction of Discover-Tech's overall volume.

title: Trump blocks military execution livestreaming
description: Trump blocks military execution livestreaming
content:
US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the execution of the Fort Hood gunman would not be livestreamed, but that immediate families of the victims would be able to view it in person.
Nidal Hasan's execution - scheduled for Dec 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 - is set to be the first by a US military firing squad since 1945.
"I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan but, many very good and well-meaning people would rather not watch him die through streaming or through any other visual device," Trump wrote.
"He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed. That said, the execution may be viewed in person by the immediate families of the victims, if they so choose. They deserve to witness JUSTICE!"
Some of Trump's fellow Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance, as well as religious leaders and international observers, had expressed doubts about the Pentagon's plan to livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan.
Recent polls have also shown a majority of Americans opposed livestreaming it.
The United Nations said streaming the execution would amount to "torture," while the president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops said it was a "barbaric promotion of a culture of death," and both Australia and Britain's prime ministers described it as "abhorrent"

title: Opp fails to thwart govt move in K P
description: Opp fails to thwart govt move in K P
content:
Joint sitting endorses emergency, governor's rule
A joint session of parliament on Thursday adopted two separate resolutions ratifying the presidential proclamations imposing a state of emergency and governor's rule for two months in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) amid opposition uproar.
Through the first resolution, the joint sitting approved the proclamation of emergency issued by President Asif Ali Zardari under the second proviso to Article 232(1) of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan. The approval was granted in accordance with Article 232(7) of the Constitution.
In a separate resolution, the parliament approved the proclamation issued by the president under Article 234(1) of the Constitution, in accordance with Article 234(3).
The adoption of the two resolutions formalised Parliament's approval of the presidential proclamations concerning the province of K-P under the relevant constitutional provisions.
During the session, opposition members tore up copies of the resolution to register their dissent.
After the proceedings concluded, the joint sitting of Parliament was adjourned indefinitely.
Parliament can endorse emergency and governor's rule for two months at a time, and for an extension, another joint session of the Parliament would have to be called. Furthermore, the extraordinary governance protocol can be extended for a maximum period of six months as per the Constitution.
Article 234, clause 3 of the Constitution, reads, "A Proclamation issued under this Article shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months, unless before the expiration of that period it has been approved by resolution of the joint sitting and may by like resolution be extended for a further period not exceeding two months at a time; but no such Proclamation shall in any case remain in force for more than six months."
A day earlier, both houses of parliament approved an emergency in K-P by majority vote under Clause 1 of Article 232 of the Constitution, despite opposition lawmakers' objections. First, the National Assembly (NA), then the Senate, debated the matter, with opposition lawmakers strongly opposing the Centre's decision and raising a hue and cry during the proceedings. However, the resolution was passed by a majority vote.
The Centre imposed emergency and governor's rule in K-P on October 11, suspending the PTI-led provincial administration amid a dispute over the province's security situation and counter-terrorism measures. The government has defended the move, citing a deterioration in law and order and an alleged failure by the provincial administration to coordinate counter-terrorism efforts with federal authorities.
Thursday's session was chaired by NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq. Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry initially presented the presidential proclamations concerning the imposition of emergency measures and governor's rule in the province.
The emergency proclamation was laid before the joint sitting under Article 232(7) of the Constitution, while the proclamation imposing governor's rule was presented under Article 234(3).
Opposition lawmakers protested during the proceedings, with several members wearing black armbands.
Chaudhry later moved a motion under Rule 232 of the Parliament (Joint Sitting) Rules, 1973, seeking to suspend certain sub-rules. Opposition members opposed the motion, prompting Speaker Sadiq to put it to a vote by asking lawmakers to stand.
The procedural motion was adopted by 214 votes to 56.
Following its approval, Chaudhry moved two separate resolutions before the joint sitting - one seeking ratification of the presidential proclamation of emergency under Article 232 of the Constitution and the other seeking approval of the proclamation imposing governor's rule under Article 234.
Subsequently, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar initiated debate on the two resolutions. He defended the imposition of emergency in K-P as a "last resort", telling a joint session of parliament that the decision followed a worsening security situation and deliberations by the federal cabinet. Urging lawmakers to approve the proclamations under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, Tarar said the government was prepared to answer questions about the grounds for the move and rejected comparisons with martial law. "This option was exercised as a last resort," he said.
Tarar told the joint sitting that the K-P governor had written a detailed letter to the president and prime minister about conditions in the province, warning that the conflict involving terrorism was intensifying. He said the government had presented figures and other material to explain why it had invoked the constitutional provisions.
According to the minister, the prime minister placed the matter before the federal cabinet after examining the material, allowing for collective consideration of the decision. He said the cabinet debated the matter for two and a half hours before recommending that the prime minister advise the president to exercise his powers under Articles 232 and 234 and impose an emergency in view of the seriousness of the situation.
Tarar also criticised the provincial leadership's priorities, referring to deaths in incidents in Tank and Bajaur. He said families were receiving condolences while injured people were undergoing treatment in hospitals, including assessments over whether their limbs needed to be amputated. "In my view, the chief minister and provincial ministers should be there, rather than at rallies where music is being played and there is an atmosphere of celebration," he said.
The minister said discussions in the apex committee, of which he was a member, had revealed that the counter terrorism department lacked a fully developed institutional structure and adequate resources. He said the overall security situation, the provincial government's conduct and the material examined by the federal government had informed the cabinet's deliberations.
Responding to lawmakers who had likened the emergency to martial law or a repeat of October 12, Tarar argued that the measure had been taken through procedures provided for in the Constitution. "The affairs of the state must be governed by the Constitution of Pakistan," he said. "Whatever is provided for in the Constitution must be carried out in the manner it mandates."
Law minister said he, the interior minister and the information minister, had explained the reasons for the decision during a media interaction on October 11, following the issuance of the proclamation. The government had subsequently presented its explanation in both houses of parliament, he added.
Outlining the parliamentary process, he said the Senate and NA had separately debated and approved the emergency proclamation issued by the president on October 11 under Article 232. He said that the separate consideration by the two houses as an additional safeguard introduced through the 18th Amendment, saying it required both chambers to examine the proclamation within 10 days and decide on its approval through resolutions.
Tarar said consideration by a joint sitting was a further constitutional requirement. He added that a proclamation would cease to remain in force if the joint sitting passed a resolution disapproving it by a majority of its total membership. Turning to Article 234, the minister said it provided a mechanism concerning the exercise of a province's administrative and legislative powers, with the president acting upon his satisfaction that the provision needed to be invoked.
He said a proclamation under that article also had to be placed before a joint sitting of parliament. The two proclamations before lawmakers formed part of the same document, he added. Tarar said the president had summoned the joint session to fulfil these constitutional requirements, following detailed discussions in the National Assembly and Senate.
Tarar described the 1973 Constitution as a consensus document, framed after extensive debate and careful consideration of the country's political circumstances, and said it was held in high regard by the Pakistani people and democratic forces. The minister welcomed questions from lawmakers about the reasons and material underpinning the emergency, saying the government was available to respond to members on both sides of the aisle.
He also said a final effort at negotiations had been made, but declined to discuss the competing political accounts, saying he was addressing the legal aspects of the decision. "I am speaking only from a legal point of view," he said.
Thanking the NA speaker and Senate chairman for allowing detailed debate, Tarar urged lawmakers to examine the proclamations and give reasons for their decision. "The Constitution of Pakistan gives you the authority to decide on this," he said.
Leader of the Opposition in the NA, Mahmood Khan Achakzai, addressing the joint session of Parliament, questioned how terrorists continued to enter Pakistan despite the construction of a 20-foot-high wall along the Afghanistan border, while blaming the country's internal shortcomings and past policies for the prevailing security situation.
"I say this with God as my witness that the circumstances in which our country has become trapped are the result of our own internal shortcomings," he said. Achakzai recalled that the Constitution had been framed with great difficulty following the breakup of Pakistan, which he attributed to personal egos.
"Pakistan was also divided because of our egos," he said. Criticising the imposition of governor's rule in K-P, Achakzai said those in power were also bound by constitutional rules and regulations.
Achakzai also alleged that institutions had mistreated eight members, questioning the conduct of those responsible. Achakzai stressed that political negotiations should be based on parliamentary supremacy and the rights of provinces over their resources.
He said the opposition was prepared for unconditional negotiations within the framework of the Constitution. Achakzai also called for the formation of an alliance of political parties that believed in democracy. He alleged that a plan had been devised to seize the resources of the provinces and warned that the people would resist any such move.
Achakzai called for the rights of Seraiki, Sindhi, Pashtun and Baloch communities over their resources to be recognised.
Turning to terrorism, Achakzai said he would quit politics if terrorism was not eliminated. "If terrorism is not eliminated, I will leave politics," he said.
He also called for an end to the reliance on weapons and the use of force, warning that public anger could lead to a strong reaction. Achakzai also alleged that the opposition's chief minister and members of the provincial assembly had been abducted.
"You are kidnappers. You are terrorists," he said. Referring to restrictions on meetings with the PTI founder Imran Khan, Achakzai questioned the legal basis for preventing access to him. Achakzai also referred to the treatment of the political leader, alleging that those now leading the government had previously forced their own leader to leave Attock Fort.
"For God's sake, have mercy on this country," he added. Achakzai said the opposition would have supported the government if the circumstances had justified such support. He further alleged that police had detained one of his associates at Karachi Company on the 26th, stripped him, and recorded a video with a girl to send to his wife.
Referring to the February 8 elections, Achakzai challenged government lawmakers to swear that they had genuinely won their seats.
He questioned the legitimacy of the election results and asked lawmakers to swear by their family members that they had won the elections.
Gohar urges government to withdraw terrorism allegations against PTI
PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, addressing the joint session of parliament, rejected allegations that his party was supporting terrorism, saying PTI condemned terrorism in all its forms.
Gohar said the government had accused PTI of supporting terrorists, an allegation he categorically rejected. "Decide whether we are supporting terrorists or not," he said, adding that the prime minister had deeply hurt the party through such statements.
He condemned the allegations and warned that they could have repercussions at the international level. "The Pakistan Army is ours. We live and die in Pakistan," he said, accusing the government of putting the federation at stake.
Gohar reiterated that PTI condemned all forms of terrorism and accused the government of removing an entire provincial government out of fear of a single meeting. "If we are supporting terrorism, then hang us," he said, questioning whether the government considered PTI members part of the country.
He warned that future generations would force the government to apologise for its allegations, maintaining that PTI could be accused of many things but could never support terrorism. He urged the government to withdraw the allegations as soon as possible.
The PTI chairman also rejected the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in K-P, as well as the decision to call in the army. "We reject your emergency, governor's rule and the calling in of the army," he said, adding that PTI would work towards building a Pakistan in which those responsible would be held accountable.

title: ECP orders immediate LG polls in Punjab
description: ECP orders immediate LG polls in Punjab
content:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has decided to immediately hold local government elections in Punjab and cantonment areas, directing its officials to immediately submit draft election schedules for approval.
The commission rejected the Punjab government's response as unsatisfactory, turning down its proposal to conduct local government elections in three phases in April 2027.
According to an ECP statement, the decision was taken at a meeting chaired by Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Sikandar Sultan Raja and attended by commission members Nisar Ahmed Durrani, Babar Hassan Bharwana and Justice (retd) Ikramullah Khan, along with the ECP secretary and senior officials.
The meeting was informed that the Punjab government, in its October 14, 2026, response to the commission's October 2 letter and draft election programme, had proposed holding local government elections in three phases in April 2027. It cited dense fog and severe winter conditions in December, followed by the start of Ramazan in February, as reasons for seeking the delay.
The ECP, however, rejected the proposal, stating that consultations with the provincial government under Section 219(3) of the Elections Act had been completed on August 20, 2026.
During those consultations, the provincial government had agreed to hold local government elections between December 15, 2026, and January 15, 2027.
The commission said it had decided to proceed with the elections in Punjab and issue the schedule without further delay in fulfilment of its constitutional and legal responsibilities. It directed its office to immediately submit the draft election programme for approval.
The ECP expressed disappointment over the provincial government's failure to provide lists of officers for appointment as district returning officers, returning officers and assistant returning officers. It directed the government to submit the required lists within a week.
The commission also decided to proceed with local government elections in cantonment areas and directed its office to submit the election programme for approval immediately.
According to the statement, a consultative meeting was held on April 15, 2026, with the additional secretary of the Ministry of Defence and the director general of the Military Lands and Cantonments Department.
During the meeting, the ECP had asked the defence secretary to move a summary to the federal government so that it could formally request the commission to conduct elections in cantonments under Section 19(D) of the Cantonments Act, 1924.
The commission said it had sent several reminder letters to the Ministry of Defence, while the CEC had also written to the prime minister on the matter. However, no satisfactory response had been received.
The ECP said it had decided to proceed with cantonment elections in view of its constitutional and legal obligations, directing its office to immediately place the election programme before the commission for approval.

title: TTAP halts talks over Imran s access
description: TTAP halts talks over Imran s access
content:
Alliance demands family and doctor visits, release of detainees
The Tehreek-e-Tahaffuz Ayeen-e-Pakistan (TTAP) on Thursday suspended all negotiations with the government until Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan is allowed to meet his family and his doctors are granted access to him, saying no talks would take place until information about his health was provided.
The announcement came a day after parliament endorsed an emergency proclamation for Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, deepening the political standoff between the government and opposition despite recent efforts to resolve their differences through dialogue.
"Until a meeting with Imran is arranged and information about his health is provided, there will be no talks with the government," the alliance said in a statement posted on X after a meeting chaired by its chairman, Mahmood Khan Achakzai. It said Achakzai would have exclusive authority to negotiate with the government.
The alliance also demanded the release of Imran's sisters, access to him for his doctors, and the immediate release of K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, provincial assembly speaker Babar Saleem Swati, PTI provincial president Junaid Akbar and all arrested members of the national and provincial assemblies, as well as party leaders.
TTAP condemned the imposition of governor's rule and an emergency in K-P, describing the measures as "an attack on the Constitution and the public mandate". It demanded their immediate withdrawal and said its constituent parties would challenge the decisions in the Peshawar High Court.
The National Assembly and Senate on Wednesday approved the emergency proclamation for K-P by majority vote, following the federal government's decision to impose the measure alongside governor's rule on October 11. The government has defended the move on security grounds, citing deteriorating law and order in the province and the need for greater coordination in counterterrorism efforts.
The alliance also called for the release of human rights lawyer Imaan Mazari, her husband Hadi Chatha, Dr Mahrang Baloch and all political prisoners associated with the Baloch Yakjehti Committee.
It reiterated its opposition to all forms of terrorism, including violence against civilians by the state, attacks by state institutions on political parties and sectarian violence. TTAP expressed support for the National Action Plan but called for the immediate implementation of a joint resolution adopted by a peace jirga in the K-P Assembly instead of introducing new policies.
On Balochistan, the alliance blamed the worsening security situation on what it described as an unrepresentative provincial government and failed federal policies. It called for the province's problems to be resolved through dialogue with its people rather than the use of force.
The statement also expressed concern over the situation in Azad Jammu and Kashmir, alleging that an "artificial system" had been imposed on its people. It condemned what it said was the denial of internet access and basic necessities for five months.
TTAP said restrictions on judicial independence and the media had prompted it to approach international human rights organisations and the United Nations to highlight what it described as human rights violations and breaches of the Constitution in Pakistan.

title: Houthis hit presidential palace in Aden
description: Houthis hit presidential palace in Aden
content:
Saudi-led coalition says missile intercepted in Medina
Yemen's Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing two guards, while the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen detailed dozens of attacks on Saudi infrastructure in the escalating conflict.
The Saudi-led coalition said Thursday that it had intercepted a cruise missile in the Medina region, home to one of Islam's holiest cities.
Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said on X that a "cruise missile has been intercepted and destroyed in the Medina region."
The attack was the first in the current conflict between the Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi Arabia on Aden's al-Maashiq palace, the seat of Yemen's Saudi-backed and internationally recognised government. The conflict is a new theatre in the wider regional war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February.
The government's prime minister and cabinet members were safe following the attack, Yemeni Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said. Witnesses told Reuters they heard loud booms near the palace. Yemen's cabinet said the attack involved missiles and drones, and officials told Reuters that two guards were killed.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the Houthis had bombed what he described as the Saudi military operations headquarters in Aden, as part of the group's declared policy of targeting "Saudi reinforcements wherever they were located".
The Houthi-run news agency SABA said the headquarters was run by Saudi officers and that there were weapons depots there. Reuters could not independently verify the claims.
The renewed fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed forces resumed in Yemen last month, and aid agencies have warned of rapidly worsening conditions.
Last week, government forces launched a campaign to recapture areas controlled by the Houthis, recovering ground near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a global shipping artery.
Residents of Taiz, northwest of Aden, have said they face intensifying bombardment and dwindling supplies as the Houthis tighten their grip on areas around the city, Yemen's third-largest.
War broke out in Yemen in 2014 when the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa, driving the government south. A Saudi-led military intervention the following year led to a bloody stalemate before a 2022 truce that held until this year.
In that phase of the conflict Houthi fighters and allied forces briefly seized al-Maashiq palace during a battle for Aden, before withdrawing.
As Saudi Arabia backs government forces, the Houthis have been firing ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports, ports and oil installations, turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point in the wider war and threatening its ambitious economic plans.
On Thursday, the Saudi-led military coalition said the Houthis had attempted to attack dozens of such sites, highlighting the risk to Saudi civilian infrastructure. The governing council of the UN's International Civil Aviation Organization condemned the recent attacks on civilian airports, aircraft, and aviation infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.
Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki told reporters that the Houthis had launched 20 attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh this month, killing 17 people and wounding 333 others. The airport is one of Saudi Arabia's main international aviation hubs.
The coalition said Houthi attacks on Abha airport in southwestern Saudi Arabia near the Yemeni border had killed three people and wounded 28.
Maliki said the Houthis had acquired advanced military technology with the help of "regional actors," including ballistic missiles, drones and explosive-laden fast boats.
Iran has provided weapons, money and training to the Houthis, although Tehran has officially denied arming them in violation of a UN arms embargo.
Maliki also said the coalition had destroyed 127 weapons storage facilities and launch platforms in Yemen's mountainous areas, calling on the Houthis to immediately halt operations targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure.
Shortly afterwards, the Houthi military spokesperson said Saudi airspace and airports were unsafe, renewing a warning to airlines while excluding airspace over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.
Saudi Arabia's civil defence authority also issued an early-warning alert over a potential threat in the southern province of Najran, before saying the danger had passed.
Later, the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed a drone in the southwestern Saudi Arabian city of Khamis Mushait, and another launched towards the country's southern region.

title: Classroom turns into a death trap
description: Classroom turns into a death trap
content:
35 schoolchildren, two female teachers killed in Peshawar school roof collapse, Owner arrested as investigation
At least 35 children and two female teachers were killed on Thursday when the roof of a school collapsed during morning classes in Peshawar's Dir Colony, police and rescue officials said.
As distraught parents and relatives gathered at the site to search for loved ones, rescue workers spent hours pulling children from the rubble of the privately run Al-Khair School System.
Most of the children killed were under 13 and from low-income families. More than 50 people were injured, including children who suffered injuries ranging from minor wounds to severe trauma, said Arif Khattak, regional director of the Rescue Department.
Rescue 1122 said its teams, ambulances and disaster response vehicles reached the site and launched relief operations. More than eight injured children were initially given first aid and taken to hospital, while the search for others continued. Rescue workers later transported more than 40 injured students and teachers to Lady Reading Hospital (LRH).
A roof on an upper floor collapsed onto classrooms below, bringing down two storeys of the building, a rescue official said.
"The fatalities include 12 girl students and a female teacher," LRH spokesperson Mohammad Asim said.
Three children remained in critical condition with head injuries, while most of those taken to the hospital had been treated and discharged, he added.
The collapse occurred at 8:48am local time, and the rescue operation lasted four to five hours, Khattak said.
"It was a weak building structure," Peshawar police chief Mian Saeed said. "Its roof was overloaded with construction on a weak structure, which caused the collapse."
Saeed said the school's owner, Khan Muhammad, had been arrested and an investigation launched.
Around 110 students were attending classes in three classrooms when the roof collapsed, according to police.
Distraught relatives accused the school administration of ignoring warnings about the building's condition and demanded accountability.
"Make an example of them, a lesson for all, so that no one dares open a school just to make money without providing facilities," said Mohammad Zaman, who lost two nephews in the collapse.
The school was located in a densely populated, low-income neighbourhood of Peshawar.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed sorrow over the tragedy and offered condolences to the victims' families, his office said.
Jawad Ahmad, whose son and daughter attended the school and survived, said he was devastated by the news.
"It felt as if someone had shot me in the chest when I learned that the school building had collapsed," he said.
According to the hospital's latest list, the victims included 12 female students and two female teachers, while the remaining fatalities were boys. The children were aged between six and 13.
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi announced compensation of 1 million rupees for the family of each person killed and 200,000 rupees for each injured person.
Kundi said the investigation would be completed within four days and those responsible would be identified and punished, regardless of the department they belonged to. He said the inquiry would examine the responsibility of everyone involved, from the school owner to the relevant government departments.
A preliminary investigation report prepared by Rescue 1122 and the district administration pointed to alleged serious negligence by the school administration and failures to ensure the building's safety.
According to the report, the roof of the upper floor had deteriorated after rainfall, and students had alerted the school owner to its poor condition. Instead of carrying out proper repairs or ensuring the building was safe, the administration allegedly reinforced the roof temporarily and called students back to school. The roof subsequently collapsed, the report said.
The report, which has been sent to the provincial government, examines the causes of the collapse, the building's structure, the deteriorated roof and the alleged negligence of the school administration.

title: HRCP flags violations of minorities rights
description: HRCP flags violations of minorities rights
content:
The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) said on Thursday that religious minorities continued to face violations of their fundamental rights, including the misuse of blasphemy laws, forced marriages and conversions, hate speech and discrimination, despite recent legislative measures aimed at protecting them.
In its seventh annual report on freedom of religion, titled "Sanctuary Denied: Freedom of Religion or Belief in 2025/26", the HRCP said scores of people accused of blasphemy remained in legal limbo, while alleged perpetrators linked to an "organised entrapment network" had yet to be investigated.
Girls from Christian and Hindu communities continued to face abductions and forced marriages, exacerbated by poverty and inadequate police responses, the report said.
Discriminatory employment practices, controversial changes to school curricula and the marginalisation of minority concerns in mainstream media further undermined the principle of equal citizenship, it added.

title: Sitting CM s arrest  unjustified
description: Sitting CM s arrest  unjustified
content:
Experts question legality of Afridi's protective custody
The placement of a sitting chief minister in protective custody has raised serious questions about democratic norms and constitutional authority, with experts questioning the move against the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) government and calling on the courts to examine its legality.
Former justice Wajihuddin Ahmed said the courts had the power to take cognisance of the matter, while senior journalist Mazhar Abbas questioned the justification for targeting the PTI-led provincial government in the name of counterterrorism.
Questions have also been raised over the constitutional basis of the move, the status of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly and its implications for the upcoming Senate elections.
Senior journalist Mazhar Abbas said the issue was not the rise in terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which has remained a longstanding problem across the country since the September 11 attacks and the ensuing war on terror, but the politicisation of terrorism against the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI).
He alleged that the security situation was being used as a pretext to target the party.
Abbas said all major political parties were signatories to the National Action Plan (NAP), but none had implemented it in letter and spirit while in power.
He questioned why only the PTI-led government in K-P was being targeted. In reality, he said, the entire provincial government and assembly had been held in abeyance along with the chief minister, who continued to hold the office in name only.
Justice (r) Wajihuddin Ahmed said the constitutional court had the power to take cognisance of the protective custody of the K-P chief minister.
Asked whether the law provided for suo motu action in the matter, he said the court still had considerable powers at its disposal and should exercise them to safeguard the spirit of the Constitution.
He said there was no provision in law allowing the arrest of a chief minister, in any form, in such circumstances. Placing both a speaker and a chief minister in custody was unimaginable under any democratic dispensation, he said, adding that the imposition of emergency should be questioned by the courts.
However, Abbas disagreed with Justice (r) Wajihuddin Ahmed's view that the courts could take up the matter, saying that no court would examine it because the judiciary had been brought within the ambit of the government's authority.
He argued that terrorism was not the actual reason for the measures and that, under such regimes, reasons were used merely to satisfy paperwork. Even when terrorism was cited as the justification on paper, he said, history had shown that such measures had never produced positive results.

Justice Najafi, however, observed that the petition concerning the now non-functional chief minister was no longer a live issue, adding that governor's rule and the emergency were separate matters.
