title: Iran s  Midday Meal  takes top prize at Asia s biggest film festival
description: This year s Busan International Film Festival lineup featured 13 contenders
content:
This year's Busan International Film Festival lineup featured 13 contenders
Iranian filmmaker Majid Majidi's Midday Meal took home the top prize at South Korea's Busan film festival on Thursday, claiming along with it automatic eligibility for the Oscars' international feature category.
The Busan International Film Festival (BIFF), Asia's largest, launched its first true competition section only last year. This year's lineup featured 13 contenders -- including a trio of South Korean titles.
A jury led by Chinese filmmaker Zhang Yimou ( Raise the Red Lantern ) chose Majidi's drama about a teacher in a poor Iranian village who is forced to turn to smuggling to keep his school afloat.
"I think it's thanks to the love and energy my mother gave me before she passed away a few months before filming began," Majidi said via an interpreter in accepting the award.
He went on to praise the Iranian people for having "never given up" despite the ongoing conflict with the United States, years of legal sanctions and a lack of access to medicine.
This year's win carries special significance as the US-based Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences in May revamped longstanding rules governing the selection of eligible titles for what was once known as the foreign language Oscar.
Winning one of a group of six film festivals, a list that includes Busan, Cannes, Berlin and others, now grants immediate eligibility.
The category had previously been limited to a single film per country chosen by an Academy-approved selection committee.
The broad list of contenders is then winnowed down to just five nominees.
Busan, long an incubator for Asian film talent, opened its 31st edition with a screening of director Kim Jong-kwan's The Table: Day and Night , an intimate Korean drama.
Oscar-winning actress Michelle Yeoh received this year's Asian Filmmaker of the Year prize, while Hong Kong filmmaker Ann Hui received the Camellia Award for her contributions to empowering women in the industry.
A total of 315 films were screened at this year's festival, with 246 officially selected titles making up its largest lineup since 2019.
The festival drew more than 200,000 visitors, organisers said on Thursday.

The 69th Grammy Awards are scheduled for February 7, 2027, with nominations set to be announced on November 16
Olivia Rodrigo and Olivia Dean are emerging as the leading contenders for nominations in the Album of the Year category at the 2027 Grammy Awards, according to Gold Derby's latest predictions, setting up a potential showdown between two of pop music's most talked-about artists.
Rodrigo's third studio album, You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love, and Dean's The Art of Loving are both generating significant awards-season buzz. The two records have established themselves as strong contenders in a competitive field that also includes Taylor Swift, Rosalía and Noah Kahan.
According to Gold Derby's combined predictions, Rodrigo and Dean are closely matched in their chances of securing Album of the Year nominations. The race remains open, however, with the Recording Academy's official nominations yet to be announced.
Rodrigo's latest album marks another significant chapter in her career. After earning Album of the Year nominations for both Sour and Guts, the singer is seeking recognition for her third studio release, which has further established her reputation for combining emotionally direct songwriting with alternative rock influences and contemporary pop.
Her campaign is also supported by the success of her music throughout the eligibility period. Rodrigo's song "The Cure" has emerged as a major contender in the general-field categories, with the track submitted for Record of the Year and Song of the Year, alongside Best Pop Solo Performance and Best Music Video.
Dean, meanwhile, is building on her breakthrough at the previous Grammy Awards, where she won Best New Artist. Her album The Art of Loving has strengthened her position as one of the year's most prominent pop-soul performers, giving her a potential route into the Grammys' biggest category.
Taylor Swift is another major name expected to feature in the conversation. Her album The Life of a Showgirl has enjoyed considerable commercial attention, although its reception has been more divided than some of her previous releases. Swift's extensive Grammy history could also become a factor as voters weigh the year's strongest projects.

The final nominations will depend on Recording Academy voting rather than early predictions or betting markets. Gold Derby's rankings offer a snapshot of the developing race, but they do not guarantee that any artist will receive a nomination or ultimately win.
The 69th Grammy Awards are scheduled for February 7, 2027, with nominations set to be announced on November 16, 2026. Until then, Rodrigo and Dean remain two of the most closely watched names in the race for one of music's most prestigious honours.

title: Online  witch hunt  sweeps up Asians misidentified as Cornell rape accused
description: Digital sleuths have for years misidentified accused perpetrators of high profile shootings and other crimes
content:
Digital sleuths have for years misidentified accused perpetrators of high-profile shootings and other crimes
Asians who share a name with one of the men accused of raping a US university student have faced a torrent of online abuse.
The alleged 2024 gang rape of a Cornell University student, detailed in a recent lawsuit, has sparked an outpouring of outrage against the seven accused perpetrators. The case has sent internet sleuths scouring digital footprints for clues to track them down.
One of the accused is a Korean man identified by US media as Winston Lee. The problem is that the world is full of people named Winston Lee.
The rage misdirected at people who share that name, some of whom live outside the United States and look nothing like the accused, lays bare the perils of a chaotic internet, where people distrustful of public institutions become digital detectives.
One of those wrongly identified was a Chinese American whose LinkedIn profile identifies him as a New York-based finance professional who graduated from Cornell University in 2020 -- four years before the alleged rape.
One message told him to "go to hell." Others said he deserved to be imprisoned. Death threats poured in.
"You can't hide. Your future is over," said one message he received via LinkedIn.
"You'll get exactly what you deserve...which is prison!! You'll be gang raped there."
Another said that a "black magic" spell had been cast upon him.
In a video on TikTok -- where his bio reads "Not part of Cornell7" -- he said he had hired a lawyer to press charges against a woman who posted his phone number and his parents' address online.
After a deluge of hateful messages, another man misidentified as Winston Lee posted a personal appeal to TikTok detectives.
"I am Indonesian and not the Winston Lee named in the recent Cornell University case," he said.
"Please verify the identity of the person you are looking for before contacting, tagging, or making accusations against someone."
After a similar flood of messages, a Chinese-American student named Winston Lee at the University of Pennsylvania added a disclaimer to his LinkedIn profile: "I do not go to Cornell."
Those appeals did not appear to slow what Reddit discussion boards described as an "online hunt" for the seven accused, drawing many users down internet rabbit holes.
With few verified details about the man actually accused, internet users continued searching aggressively for his whereabouts.
One Reddit post claimed Winston Lee was now serving in the South Korean army.
Another user on X said she had received tips suggesting Lee had been spotted on Cornell University's campus.
People with names like the other six accused also complained about rage spamming and threats.
"These social justice warriors are literally messaging and harassing the wrong" people, said podcast host Brad Polumbo.
"These things should be litigated through the criminal process or through some sort of fair process, not through a social media mob or witch hunt."
A group of former Cornell students, who belonged to the same Chi Phi fraternity as the seven accused but graduated before the alleged incident, also complained of online smear campaigns.
"They are being wrongfully accused on social media of having involvement, are consequently receiving death threats and related hate mail," their attorney Adam Ford wrote in a letter to the university that was obtained by AFP .
"Most of them have had their employers and higher education institutions take adverse actions against them, including being placed on leave."
Digital sleuths have for years misidentified accused perpetrators of high-profile shootings and other crimes, exposing them to abuse.
Such misidentification can further roil an already chaotic information ecosystem and hinder the actual investigation by generating false leads, warned Mike Rothschild, a researcher who studies conspiracy theories.
"The wrongfully accused are often hounded. They sometimes have to go into hiding, or get death threats, or are even violently attacked themselves. And there is no penalty for being wrong on the part of those accusing them," he told AFP .

content:
RJ Mitte was photographed smiling at an Albuquerque airport on October 4, eight days before his death at age 34
RJ Mitte was photographed smiling with a fan at an Albuquerque airport just eight days before his death, in what appears to be one of the final pictures taken of the Breaking Bad actor.
The photograph, taken by Bethany Crass on October 4, shows Mitte wearing a flannel shirt, a T-shirt and a cap while posing with a stuffed Woody doll from Toy Story . He appeared cheerful as he smiled for the camera.

In the days following his death, tributes poured in from friends, family members and former co-stars. Moncada also spoke emotionally about Mitte's struggles in a video shared by TMZ.

title: Is    Whalefall    worth watching  Rotten Tomatoes critics weigh in on survival thriller
description: The film follows a diver with only one hour of oxygen as he desperately searches for a way out
content:
The film follows a diver with only one hour of oxygen as he desperately searches for a way out
Whalefall is receiving a largely positive response from film critics ahead of its nationwide cinema release, although some reviewers have questioned its emotional storytelling and unusual premise.
The survival thriller stars Austin Abrams as Jay Gardner, a deep sea diver searching the Pacific Ocean off California for the remains of his late father, Mitt, played by Josh Brolin. His mission takes a horrifying turn when he is swallowed by an enormous sperm whale, leaving him with only an hour of oxygen to escape alive.
Directed by Brian Duffield, the film is adapted from Daniel Kraus’s 2023 novel of the same name. The cast also includes Elisabeth Shue, Jane Levy, Emily Rudd and John Ortiz.
According to the review figures cited by Forbes on October 14, Whalefall had earned a 79% critics’ score on Rotten Tomatoes from 43 reviews. The score may change as additional reviews are published, and an audience rating was not yet available in the supplied report.
Several critics praised the film for combining claustrophobic survival tension with family drama and gruesome imagery. Liz Shannon Miller of Consequence described it as a cathartic and deeply human experience, while Rocco T Thompson of Slant Magazine praised its grounding in factual possibilities and its emotional climax.
Simon Crooks of Empire also praised the film, calling it frightening, thrilling and distinctive. Other reviewers were less impressed.
Owen Gleiberman of Variety gave the film a negative review, while David Rooney of The Hollywood Reporter criticised its approach to emotional drama. Jacob Oller of AV Club also questioned the balance between grotesque spectacle and flashback driven storytelling.
The divided response suggests Whalefall may appeal most to viewers who enjoy unusual survival stories, body horror and emotionally charged family narratives.
The film is rated PG 13 and is scheduled to open in cinemas nationwide on October 16, 2026, following preview screenings on October 15. Its Rotten Tomatoes score remains subject to change as further reviews arrive.

Two countries also reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral defence at the 16th JCDC meeting
Pakistan and Malaysia on Thursday reaffirmed their resolve to strengthen counter-terrorism cooperation as a joint military exercise between the two countries concluded at the National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC) in Pabbi, Nowshera district.
According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), Exercise Harimau Markhor-IV, the fourth edition of the bilateral counter-terrorism exercise between the two armies, concluded at the NCTC.
“The two-week-long exercise focused on sharing counter-terrorism experiences, refining operational drills and procedures, and enhancing combat skills through exchange of best practices,” the statement said.
Pakistan and Malaysia have concluded joint counterterrorism exercise Harimau Markhore-IV at the National Counter Terrorism Centre in Pabbi. According to ISPR, troops shared operational experience, refined combat drills and exchanged best practices, reinforcing longstanding… pic.twitter.com/yXHIWdfwbF
Read : President calls for stronger Pakistan-Malaysia cooperation in law enforcement, security
It added that the exercise reaffirmed the longstanding military cooperation between the two countries and their shared resolve to strengthen collaboration in the counter-terrorism domain.
Separately, the 16th meeting of the Pakistan-Malaysia Joint Committee on Defence Cooperation (JCDC) was held earlier today, with both sides reaffirming their commitment to strengthen bilateral defence and security cooperation further.
Both sides reviewed progress made since the previous meeting in 2025 and discussed matters of mutual interest, according to a statement.
The meeting was held at the Malaysian Ministry of Defence, where the Pakistani delegation was led by Secretary Defence Lieutenant General (retired) Muhammad Ali, while the Malaysian delegation was headed by Deputy Secretary General (policy) Mohd Yani bin Daud.
During the plenary session, the delegations reviewed progress since the 2025 JCDC meeting in Malaysia, appreciated recent achievements and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral defence and security ties.
Pakistan and Malaysia have longstanding ties dating back to 1957, when Malaysia gained independence on Aug 31. Pakistan was among the earliest countries to recognise Malaysia as a nation and also helped in drafting its constitution. The two countries have since maintained close ties.

Last year, during Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s visit to Malaysia, the two countries agreed to deepen cooperation in defence, trade and emerging technologies, while Kuala Lumpur also agreed to import $200 million worth of meat from Pakistan.
The two countries are also bound by the Malaysia-Pakistan Closer Economic Partnership Agreement, signed in 2007, which promotes trade in goods and services, regulates investment flows and supports cooperation in intellectual property, healthcare, telecommunications, tourism and construction.

title: Justin Baldoni   s former PR firm linked to alleged smear campaign against safety advocate
description: Court evidence cited reportedly connects Hiya Health to TAG PR   s crisis planning
content:
Court evidence cited reportedly connects Hiya Health to TAG PR’s crisis planning
Justin Baldoni’s former crisis public relations firm has been linked to an alleged effort to discredit consumer safety advocate Tamara Rubin, according to a report by The Hollywood Reporter published on October 14, 2026.
Rubin runs Lead Safe Mama, an online resource focused on potential exposure to lead and other harmful substances in consumer products. She says she discovered a website attacking her reputation in October 2024, alongside damaging edits to her Wikipedia page. At the time, she did not know who was responsible.
Rubin believes the attacks were connected to Hiya Health, a children’s vitamin company she had publicly criticised after laboratory findings she reported in September 2024 indicated the presence of lead and other heavy metals in its products. Hiya disputed her findings.
According to The Hollywood Reporter , Hiya emerged as a client of TAG PR in evidence connected to an ongoing defamation lawsuit filed by publicist Stephanie Jones against TAG head Melissa Nathan and other defendants. The evidence reportedly included a staff member’s reference to work on a crisis scenario plan in October 2024.
The report also identified a connection between Hiya executive Benita Litt and Baldoni. Litt, who is married to Hiya’s co-founder and chief executive, had previously served on the board of Baldoni’s now-shuttered nonprofit, BeLove.org, also known as The Wayfarer Foundation.
Baldoni hired TAG PR in August 2024 amid the fallout from his film It Ends With Us and his dispute with Blake Lively. Lively later accused Baldoni, Nathan and other defendants of participating in a smear campaign, allegations that became part of legal proceedings.
Court documents also included an email from a nutritionist recommended by Baldoni to Lively that praised Hiya’s children’s multivitamins.
Neither Baldoni nor Hiya responded to The Hollywood Reporter ’s requests for comment, while Nathan had not returned requests concerning her ongoing legal cases.
The reported connections do not independently establish who was responsible for the alleged attacks against Rubin. The claims remain allegations, and Hiya has disputed Rubin’s product findings.

title: Global financial watchdog calls for more human oversight of agentic AI
description: Says firms should set clear  risk based triggers for when AI agents must seek human approval
content:
Says firms should set clear, risk-based triggers for when AI agents must seek human approval
The Financial Stability Board (FSB), a global standard setter, has called for greater human oversight of agentic AI ​in final guidance for banks and other firms ‌on managing the technology's risks.
The FSB's guidance, published on Thursday, comes as regulators ramp up efforts to contain growing AI risks, including the ​threat of AI-enabled cyber-attacks, Reuters reported this week.
The board has strengthened its recommendations on the use of artificial intelligence agents in the financial sector, calling for more intensive human oversight in higher-risk use cases.
In its final guidance, the FSB said firms should set clear, risk-based triggers for when AI agents must seek human approval.
Read: Israeli firm used online ads to run vast spy operation, researchers say
The group said it had strengthened its recommendations on agentic AI following feedback on draft guidance published in June, growing interest among financial institutions in adopting the technology, and the distinct risks and controls it entails.
The FSB's June draft guidance said AI agents, which can plan and execute tasks with limited human oversight, pose distinct challenges for human oversight.
A series of incidents has raised policymakers' concerns about the potential for AI systems to circumvent safeguards, including an incident in July in which an OpenAI agent escaped a controlled testing environment and hacked AI company Hugging Face.
The FSB also removed a guideline recommending that financial institutions treat AI as “synthetic employees”.
Instead, firms should recognise that “AI agents do not reason like humans and may interpret pre-defined goals in unexpected ways,” the FSB said.

Indian authorities have asked Bollywood actor Imran Khan to leave the country by the end of the ​month, saying he breached immigration laws after joining a ‌protest against the election commission chief, local media reported on Thursday.

A complaint was filed against him at a police station in Mumbai, ​saying Khan had ​breached the ⁠law, and the Foreigners Regional Registration Office, a federal government agency responsible for tracking and ​monitoring foreign nationals in India, sent him a notice ​to ⁠leave based on the complaint, the Indian Express said.
Khan did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Reuters .
A nephew of ⁠actor ​Aamir Khan, and hailing from an ​illustrious film family, Imran acted in several hit Bollywood films from 2008 to ​2015, before suddenly retiring.

title: Pakistan gear up for ODI tri series
description: Sri Lanka also undergo training at the Pindi Stadium  England set to arrive today
content:
Sri Lanka also undergo training at the Pindi Stadium; England set to arrive today
Pakistan on Thursday underwent tough training session at the Pindi Stadium Rawalpindi to fine-tune for the ODI tri-series which will start on Sunday.
Sri Lanka also did training while England were scheduled to arrive on Friday morning, as per the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB).
Pakistan’s players did batting, bowling and fielding practice under the supervision of head coach Mike Hesson who recently led his side to a 2-1 win over Sri Lanka in the T20I series at Rawalpindi.
Pakistan will be led by ace pacer Shaheen Shah Afridi. Star batsman Babar Azam, Fakhar Zaman, Salman Ali Agha, Naseem Shah and Haris Rauf will also be seen in the series.
Pakistan team assembled at Islamabad on Wednesday night for the most important assignment which will help all three sides to prepare for next year’s World Cup to be held in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.
As many as nine players, who recently were also part of the T20I series, will also be seen in action in Pakistan’s team for the tri-series which will be hosted by Pindi and Lahore.
Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson said the team had made progress in ODI cricket over the past six months but would need to maintain that momentum.
“Our one-day side made some good progress in the last six months. We've got to continue that,” Hesson told reporters after Pakistan lost the third T20I to Sri Lanka.
“Certainly, against the Sri Lankan side, who would have got some confidence, and obviously an England side who's currently number one in the world. So, it's going to be a tough tri-series, one we're looking forward to,” Hesson said.
Pakistan fast bowler Naseem Shah, meanwhile, is looking to build on his return to the ODI squad. The paceman claimed three wickets for 36 runs in four overs in Pakistan’s opening T20I against Sri Lanka at Rawalpindi on October 9.
“You change a lot as a human being and as a cricketer as you get matured and you gain experience,” Naseem said.
“You also learn a lot through ups and downs in life. You bowl with express pace when you are young and new in the sport, but now I think that you also need to have some sense in terms of what you are trying to do,” said the pacer.
Pakistan’s recent ODI record offers grounds for optimism. The Green-shirts whitewashed Sri Lanka 3-0 at home in November 2025, then beat South Africa 2-1 in another home series. They lost 2-1 away to Bangladesh in March 2026 before responding with a 2-1 home series victory over Australia in May and June.
England will arrive on the back of three consecutive ODI series victories against Sri Lanka and India at home and Sri Lanka away. Sri Lanka, by contrast, have lost three of their last four series.
The series begins in Rawalpindi before moving to Lahore, where the final will be played on October 31.
Meanwhile Sri Lanka faced a setback with opener Pathum Nissanka ruled out of the tri-series as he awaits medical clearance following a left hamstring injury sustained during the recent tour of England. Lahiru Udara has been named as his replacement.
Lahiru is also in sublime form and had blasted 91 in the first T20I in Pindi on October 9 to single-handedly guide the visitors to 182. However, Pakistan chased that target with seven balls to spare.

title: Pakistan hockey secures private sponsorship
description: Partnership targets youth development and international success
content:
Partnership targets youth development and international success
Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF) and Vital Group on Thursday signed a sponsorship agreement aimed at promoting hockey and encouraging greater youth participation in the sport.
The signing ceremony at Islamabad was attended by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, Prime Minister's Youth Programme Chairman Rana Mashhood Ahmed Khan, PHF President Mohyuddin Ahmad Wani, Vital Group's Mian Asad, national team players and former Olympians.
Ahsan Iqbal said hockey was a symbol of Pakistan's national identity and the country had the potential to regain its lost glory in international hockey.
He said talented young players were being encouraged to help restore Pakistan's golden era in the sport, adding that the national team must once again raise the country's flag on the international stage.
He said that private-sector support would play an important role in developing sports and motivating athletes, stressing that financial security would allow players to focus on their performance rather than worrying about meeting their expenses.
"A player's focus should be on how to score the next goal, not how to meet his expenses," he said.
Ahsan also highlighted the growing importance of science, technology and data in modern sports, saying physical fitness, mental strength, discipline and consistent training were essential for international success.
He offered the national hockey team the use of the National Sports City in Narowal as a permanent training base, saying the facility provided international-standard facilities for 14 sports at one location.
He added the government was taking steps to provide hockey players with modern training facilities and a supportive environment.
PHF chief Mohyuddin Ahmed Wani said the federation would take all possible measures to promote hockey and would work with private sponsors to strengthen the sport.
He added that the agreement with Vital Group was an important step towards advancing hockey in Pakistan and expanding opportunities for young people.
Mashhood said public-private partnerships were essential for sports development and noted that Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif had specifically mentioned a proposed hockey league in his budget speech.
He said the government had restored departmental sports and was providing athletes with opportunities to demonstrate their abilities.
Mashhood also said a large number of Dutch players would be available for the Pakistan Hockey League, expressing confidence in efforts to strengthen the country's hockey structure.
Pakistan, a former powerhouse in international hockey, has been seeking to revive its fortunes through improved training, institutional support and greater investment in the sport.

title: Alli Hoff Kosik   s  People  Please  brings 13 Going on 30  vibes to the Jersey Shore
description: Alli Hoff Kosik unveils  People  Please   a magical novel about people pleasing  fresh starts and summer change
content:
Alli Hoff Kosik unveils 'People, Please', a magical novel about people-pleasing, fresh starts and summer change
Author Alli Hoff Kosik is preparing to release her second novel, People, Please , a contemporary fiction story blending magical realism, relationships and self-discovery against the backdrop of New Jersey's Jersey Shore.
PEOPLE exclusively revealed the cover of the upcoming book, which will be published by Grand Central Publishing on May 18, 2027. The novel follows Kat, whose life takes an unexpected turn when her husband announces he is leaving her because her people-pleasing tendencies have strained their marriage.
Seeking a fresh start, Kat moves to her father's apartment in New Jersey, where she plans to help him prepare for his own wedding. There, she meets Sydney, a single mother and essential oils enthusiast whose unconventional approach to life challenges Kat's established habits.
Set during what the book's synopsis describes as a wild, experimental summer, People, Please explores personal growth and the difficulties of breaking free from the need to satisfy everyone else.
Kosik said the idea allowed her to explore her own experiences with people-pleasing through speculative fiction and magical realism. She cited films such as 13 Going on 30 and Wish Upon a Star as inspirations for the story. The novel is set in Ocean City, a real seaside town in New Jersey that holds personal significance for the author.
The book also underwent a creative transformation. Kosik initially envisioned People, Please as a young adult novel and her debut publication. However, after completing Too Blessed to Stress , she reconsidered the project and developed it for adult readers.
The author said adding essential oils and multi-level marketing to the plot helped the story take shape. She hopes the finished novel will offer readers both an enjoyable summer read and a meaningful exploration of people-pleasing.
People, Please is available for preorder ahead of its May 2027 release.

title: Saturday Night Live    stays silent as Shane Gillis faces criticism over controversial monologue about women
description: Former cast member Ego Nwodim joined the response with a sarcastic post about gym attire
content:
Former cast member Ego Nwodim joined the response with a sarcastic post about gym attire
Shane Gillis has faced criticism after describing women as “wh*res” during his monologue on Saturday Night Live , while the programme and NBC have yet to comment publicly, according to CNN . The remarks sparked online criticism.
The comedian hosted the sketch show last weekend. He joked about women wearing tight shorts to the gym and defended his description, saying there was no other way to put it.
Jessie Leo, a graphic designer who works on Saturday Night Live , criticised the joke in an Instagram post. She questioned how employees could feel comfortable approaching NBC human resources after the company approved the segment and raised concerns about rape culture and victim blaming.
Former cast member Cecily Strong responded with an ironic post about wearing workout clothes. Ego Nwodim also shared a gym outfit photo with a sarcastic reference to the insult. Women online posted pictures of their gym outfits in response to Gillis’ comments.
Actor Dan Levy criticised the comedian in a video, arguing that women wearing short shorts at the gym should not be labelled with a derogatory term and that men who do so are expressing misogyny. He urged men to speak out against attitudes that help excuse or minimise sexual violence.
The controversy has renewed scrutiny of Gillis’ history with Saturday Night Live . He was dismissed from the cast in 2019, days after his hiring was announced, when clips emerged of him using anti Asian and anti gay slurs on a podcast.
The latest backlash has also unfolded amid public discussion of sexual violence following a lawsuit concerning an alleged 2024 gang rape involving a former Cornell University undergraduate. The allegations remain under investigation and should not be treated as established findings.
NBC and Saturday Night Live had not publicly addressed the criticism at the time of CNN ’s report.

title: Sri Lanka s Nissanka ruled out of tri series
description: The right hander sustains injury to his left thigh
content:
The right-hander sustains injury to his left thigh
Sri Lanka opener Pathum Nissanka has been ruled out of the upcoming ODI tri-series against Pakistan and England because of a hamstring injury, dealing a significant blow to the visitors ahead of the tournament.
The right-handed batter sustained an injury to his left thigh during Sri Lanka's recent tour of England, which also forced him to miss the three-match T20 International (T20I) series against Pakistan earlier this month.
Nissanka had been expected to recover in time for the One Day International (ODI) tri-series, but his rehabilitation has not progressed sufficiently for a return to international cricket.
Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) confirmed on Thursday that the opener had not received medical clearance to resume competitive action. The selectors have named Lahiru Udara as his replacement in the 16-member Sri Lanka squad.
Udara is yet to make his ODI debut but has represented Sri Lanka in five Test matches and seven T20 Internationals, including the recently concluded T20I series against Pakistan.
The batter has an established record in List A cricket, scoring 3,017 runs in 102 matches at an average of 32.09. His tally includes three centuries and 21 half-centuries.
The ODI tri-series will begin on October 18, with Sri Lanka facing hosts Pakistan in the opening match at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. England are the third team competing in the tournament.
Sri Lanka will be led by Kusal Mendis, who will also take the wicketkeeping duties, as they prepare for the 50-over competition without one of their key opening batters.

title: PSG  got lucky  to win Man City thriller  says Enrique
description: Defending champions secure a comfortable victory over the Premier League side
content:
Defending champions secure a comfortable victory over the Premier League side
Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique said the European champions rode their luck to beat Manchester City 4-2 and maintain a perfect start to their defence of the Champions League.
The visitors ran riot in the first half of City's first home game since being found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules as they raced into a 3-0 lead.
Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha were on target in a near flawless first 45 minutes by the French champions.
But City roared back after the break as Erling Haaland struck twice, while they also hit the woodwork twice and were denied by a brilliant goalline clearance by Nuno Mendes.
"We could have lost this match if they scored the chances that they created," said Luis Enrique.
"I think it was a very nice match, but the way they play, it's amazing. We like to play these kind of matches."
Maghnes Akliouche briefly restored PSG's three-goal lead in the second half, while Ferran Torres also missed a late penalty for the visitors.
"We try to win every single match. We try to score. We don't stop if we score one or two goals," added Luis Enrique.
"It's very nice to feel that but I have to repeat, today we were lucky because in the second half we could have conceded more goals."
Enzo Maresca had made a perfect start to the daunting challenge of replacing Pep Guardiola as City manager by winning his first eight games in all competitions.
Guardiola, who won 20 trophies in a 10-year spell at City, made his return to the Etihad Stadium in a show of support after City were found guilty on more than 100 charges of financial impropriety between 2009 and 2018.
But he saw his former players fall to their first defeat of the season despite a spirited fightback after being thoroughly outplayed in the first half.
"From tonight we can learn many things," said Maresca. "Even if we concede two goals (in two minutes) against the best team in Europe, we need to continue.
"I try to continue to learn from the players because I just arrived three months ago, but the feeling at the moment is very good."
Victory took PSG top of the Champions League table after two games, while City drop to 17th.

title: Zverev to reach Shanghai semi finals
description: German seed cruises past De Minaur in Shanghai
content:
German seed cruises past De Minaur in Shanghai
Top seed Alexander Zverev took "a huge step up" to dismantle Alex de Minaur 6-4, 6-4 on Thursday and roll into the Shanghai Masters semi-finals.
He will play Alejandro Davidovich Fokina, who advanced when France's Arthur Gea retired injured from their quarter-final after 22 minutes.
Zverev, who will end the year at world number one, was tested by the Australian's speed in the first set but sent down a string of dazzling forehands to convert a break point in the fifth game.
Despite a double-fault the German saved three break points in a row to hold serve and was rewarded in the 10th game, taking the first set with a buttery backhand at the net.
Zverev refused to relent in the second set, setting up another break point in the seventh game to go up 4-3 when De Minaur served into the net.
The 27-year-old Australian clung on for a bit longer but Zverev wasn't sticking around, clinching victory on the first match point.
"Very satisfied with my level... it was a huge step up from the last couple matches."
Zverev needed three sets to win his two previous matches.
France's Gea was in the biggest match of his career when he quit his quarter-final with muscle issues.
The 21-year-old took a medical timeout for work on his lower right side when he was down 1-4 in the first set.
He returned to play but ended the match minutes later.
"I felt this morning, during a warm-up, pain in the psoas," he said, referring to a muscle in the lower back.
He said he received "treatments" and decided to step on court despite being unsure about his fitness.
"I tried from the beginning, but it was not enough to play full and too dangerous for the end of the season.
"I'm really sad, but it's the best choice I could do," said 56th-ranked Gea, who was playing in his first tournament at the prestigious ATP 1000 level.

title: Martinez blames  anger  for dig at Man Utd hierarchy
description: English giants suffer defeat in Spain on Tuesday in the Champions League
content:
English giants suffer defeat in Spain on Tuesday in the Champions League
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez said "anger and frustration" at defeat to Atletico Madrid led to his swipe at the club's board for a lack of investment in the transfer market.
The English giants lost 2-0 in Spain on Tuesday in the Champions League. They are also off to their worst start to a Premier League season for 40 years.
Martinez took aim at technical director Jason Wilcox, saying he "100 percent" expected more investment in the squad during the transfer window after United finished third in the Premier League last season to return to Europe's top competition.
United signed three midfielders -- Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos -- for around £150 million ($198 million), but their spending fell far short of some of their Premier League rivals.
"After the match, I spoke out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted," Martinez posted on social media.
The Argentine international's comments were backed by some fans, but Martinez has been criticised for his own part in United's poor start to the season.
He scored an own goal in a 1-1 draw at bottom-of-the-table Fulham last month and was outmuscled by Dominic Solanke as 10-man Tottenham salvaged a point at Old Trafford last weekend.
"When I talk about wanting more, I'm talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club. To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level.
"These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.
"I believe in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I'm convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment."
The pressure is rising on United boss Michael Carrick just months after he was handed the job on a permanent basis.
Carrick's men travel to historic rivals Leeds on Sunday before another Champions League trip, to Italian side Como, on Wednesday.

Rockstar Games’ new trailer offers a closer look at the story, its protagonists and the music accompanying the game
Rockstar Games has released the official launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto 6, offering a closer look at the story, its protagonists and the music accompanying the highly anticipated title.
The 90-second trailer introduces Jason and Lucia, two characters whose lives take a dangerous turn after a criminal operation goes wrong.
According to Rockstar’s official description, “when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida”.
The description adds that the pair must “rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive”.
The trailer also features original music from French electronic duo Justice, who have composed the game’s original score.
Rockstar has confirmed that a new Justice single, "Flower in a Hurricane", featuring Tame Impala, SZA and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard, will appear on Grand Theft Auto 6: The Album, the game’s official soundtrack.
Rockstar confirmed that the trailer was captured entirely on a PlayStation 5, although it did not specify whether the footage came from the standard console or the PS5 Pro.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is scheduled for release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on November 19, 2026.
It will mark Rockstar’s first major new single-player release since Red Dead Redemption 2 launched in 2018.
In an interview with Bloomberg , studio heads Phil Hooker and Aaron Garbut also suggested that the company’s next game could arrive sooner, citing improvements to development tools, technology and team structure.
Hooker said: “The engine, the tools and the team we’ve built during this project will allow us to do things more quickly.”

title: Inde Navarrette says she studied    Jujutsu Kaisen    and    Demon Slayer    to learn screenwriting
description: The    Obsession    star explored film and TV storytelling during the period between completing the film and its release
content:
The ‘Obsession’ star explored film and TV storytelling during the period between completing the film and its release
Actor Inde Navarrette has revealed how studying anime, including Jujutsu Kaisen and Demon Slayer, helped her understand storytelling and develop her screenwriting skills while waiting for her acting career to progress.
Navarrette, known for playing Nikki Freeman in Obsession , explored film and television storytelling during the period between completing the film and its eventual release.
She also streamed games on Twitch to make ends meet while considering her next career steps.
In an interview with The Hollywood Reporter on October 14, Navarrette explained how comparing anime series helped her understand different narrative techniques.
“I transitioned into studying film and watching movies and asking, ‘Why do I like them?’” she said.
She highlighted the contrasting approaches used in Jujutsu Kaisen and Demon Slayer , particularly their handling of timelines.
“With Jujutsu Kaisen, they play with timelines, right? With Demon Slayer, they don’t, it’s very linear. And what does that mean and how does that affect with storytelling?”
Navarrette said she examined how information revealed early in an episode could become significant much later, using those lessons to inform her own screenwriting.
A self-described nerd and keen gamer, Navarrette is also interested in voice acting.
In an August interview, she identified the Resident Evil franchise as a dream project, explaining: “I love that world, specifically — the Resident Evil world.”
Meanwhile, she is preparing to play Rogue in Marvel Studios’ upcoming X-Men reboot.
Navarrette has stressed her commitment to the character, saying: “I’ve studied that character. I want to do it justice for myself, for [director Jake Schrieier], for what they want to portray and also for what I as a fan want her to be like.”

The actress welcomed twins Aya and Ohm in April 2023 and has spoken openly about becoming a mother later in life
Hilary Swank is expecting her third child with husband Philip Schneider, three years after the couple welcomed twins Aya and Ohm.
The actress, 52, announced the pregnancy in an Instagram video shared on October 14. In the clip, Swank, Schneider and their twins dance in the dark with glow sticks attached to their bodies. In an interview with PEOPLE , Swank discussed motherhood while advocating for California bill AB 1901, which calls for greater transparency around diaper ingredients. She said she was fortunate to spend time with her children.
Swank has reflected on becoming a parent later in life. She said the timing allowed her to be present with her children, while her established acting career gave her flexibility to step in and out of work.
The actress has said she wanted children earlier, but circumstances did not make it possible. She believes she might have been a different parent had she started a family in her twenties or thirties.
Swank has also credited personal growth with helping her approach parenting. She said working on herself helped her recognise patterns she did not want to pass on to her children.
The star, known for Million Dollar Baby and the series Yellowjackets , has said her children remind her to stay present. Her announcement suggests the family is preparing to welcome another baby in December, although she has not shared details about the pregnancy.

title: Tom Cruise stunned NASCAR chief by asking to compete in real ARCA race
description: NASCAR hopes the upcoming film will introduce the sport to a new generation of fans
content:
NASCAR hopes the upcoming film will introduce the sport to a new generation of fans
Tom Cruise reportedly surprised NASCAR chief executive Steve O’Donnell by asking whether he could compete in a real race ahead of the planned Days of Thunder sequel.
O’Donnell revealed the actor’s unusual request during an interview with Front Office Sports , explaining that Cruise was interested in entering a race in the ARCA series, a lower tier of stock car racing connected to NASCAR.
“I was shocked,” O’Donnell said, recalling their conversation. He added that he was unsure whether the idea would become reality, although Cruise wanted the upcoming film to feel as authentic as possible.
Cruise played fictional rookie driver Cole Trickle in the original Days of Thunder , released in 1990. The film helped bring NASCAR racing to a wider audience, and the sport’s leadership hopes the follow up can generate similar interest decades later.
The sequel, announced in August 2026, is expected to star Cruise alongside Anne Hathaway and is reportedly planned for release in 2028. NASCAR is involved in the project, with discussions focusing on how the film can reflect the sport as it operates today.
O’Donnell said Cruise wanted audiences to understand modern racing, including the technology involved in preparing cars, the competition format and the points system. NASCAR hopes these details will help newcomers follow the action and feel more connected to the sport.
Cruise attended the Coke Zero Sugar 400 at Daytona International Speedway in August, where he met drivers and spoke with racing figures. The visit coincided with the announcement of the new film.
The actor has also emphasised that the story should capture the people and community behind the races, alongside the speed and danger associated with the sport.
Although Cruise’s request to enter an actual ARCA event appears unlikely to happen, his reported interest reflects the production’s emphasis on realism. NASCAR is hoping the film will introduce its racing culture to fresh audiences while showing existing fans how the sport has evolved since the original movie.

His credits include Khuda Kay Liye , Waar and Zarrar , with his performances often associated with action-oriented and socially themed cinema. His recent film credits include Bullah and Psycho , both released in 2026.

Zulfiqar began his career in modelling before establishing himself as a television actor. His drama credits include Diyar-e-Dil , Shehr-e-Zaat and Sang-e-Mar Mar , while his film work includes Cake , Sherdil and Huey Tum Ajnabi .

title: Naqvi says govt exhausted efforts to secure K P s cooperation on terrorism
description: DPM Dar cites constitutional articles to defend federal authority  questions PTI s role in return of TTP
content:
DPM Dar cites constitutional articles to defend federal authority, questions PTI's role in return of TTP
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Thursday said the federal government had exhausted all efforts to secure the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) government’s cooperation in combating terrorism and avoiding the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule, maintaining that the decision had been taken reluctantly after months of unsuccessful engagement.
Addressing a joint session of Parliament, Naqvi rejected opposition allegations that the government had used terrorism for political purposes, saying it had repeatedly attempted to bring the provincial administration on board to fight terrorism together.
“We made every effort to bring their government on board so that they could fight shoulder to shoulder with us,” he said.
The interior minister said efforts to secure cooperation from the provincial leadership had begun long before the latest round of political negotiations. Referring to an Apex Committee meeting held in Peshawar in February, Naqvi said he had attended alongside the Peshawar corps commander, while the K-P chief minister had hosted the meeting.
He said considerable difficulties had been encountered in arranging the meeting, which aimed to establish a common position on counter-terrorism. The plan was to agree on a joint approach and issue a press release stating that federal and provincial authorities would work together to combat terrorism, he added.
مجلسِ شوریٰ (پارلیمنٹ) کے مشترکہ اجلاس کے دوران وفاقی وزیر برائے داخلہ و انسدادِ منشیات سینیٹر سید محسن رضا نقوی کا اظہارِ خیال۔ #JointSession pic.twitter.com/J1Fl9MJx46
Naqvi urged lawmakers to obtain and read the press release that was eventually issued, particularly its concluding remarks, to understand what had transpired. He recalled that security personnel had been martyred on the same day and that participants had learned of their deaths during the meeting.
He said the K-P chief minister had been persuaded through a formal request to attend the funeral prayers of the personnel. Naqvi claimed this was the last occasion on which the chief minister had attended the funeral prayers of a security official.
Turning to the government's negotiations with Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), Naqvi acknowledged that members of the party's negotiating committee had expressed a clear commitment to combating terrorism. He singled out PTI leader Asad Qaiser, saying his position during the talks had been so firm that even government representatives had not expressed themselves in similar terms.
Naqvi said all members of the opposition delegation had discussed terrorism and maintained that the fight was for Pakistan, rather than any individual or political party. However, he said he had pointed out to Qaiser a significant difference between the position of the negotiating committee and that of the provincial government.
He further said he had asked Qaiser to consult the provincial leadership because it did not share the views being presented by PTI representatives during the negotiations. According to Naqvi, the opposition delegation subsequently returned after consultations and was given a mandate to discuss the issues raised.
The interior minister said the government had not sought to discredit the opposition's position on terrorism and acknowledged that the negotiating committee had not retreated from its stated commitment.
He also referred to a television interview involving the K-P information minister, saying the interviewer had repeatedly asked him to condemn terrorism. Naqvi said the interviewer had made the request three times and that he was willing to provide the video clip, along with other evidence, if required.
Naqvi maintained that the government had pursued every available channel of communication with the provincial leadership. He said he had personally met the K-P chief minister several times and worked with him to formulate a security plan for five districts.
Also Read: Parliament's joint session takes up resolutions on K-P emergency, governor's rule
Under the proposed arrangement, the police would be strengthened in those districts, while civil armed forces would gradually withdraw over six months, allowing the police to assume responsibility for security operations. The federal government and security forces were prepared to support the provincial police during the transition, he said.
However, Naqvi questioned who had prevented the provincial government from implementing the arrangement, adding that the reasons for its failure were a separate matter. He also said the chief minister had publicly criticised military personnel shortly after security officials had been killed.
Referring to incidents in Bannu and other areas, Naqvi said the chief minister had delivered speeches against the same forces whose personnel had recently lost their lives.
The minister maintained that the federal government had wanted the provincial administration to lead counter-terrorism operations, with the army, Frontier Corps and other security organisations providing assistance. He said the government had not sought to take control of those operations away from the province.
According to Naqvi, the provincial leadership had been unwilling to assume responsibility for leading the operations despite repeated requests. He urged lawmakers to ask participants in the negotiations whether terrorism had been discussed, saying the subject had been addressed at the beginning of the talks.
Naqvi said Qaiser had responded to the government's concerns about terrorism within the first few minutes, after which discussions had moved to other political issues.
He rejected suggestions that the government had misused the terrorism issue, saying efforts to secure provincial cooperation had been under way since before August and September. Engagement had taken place at different levels, including directly with the K-P chief minister, he added.
Naqvi recalled efforts ahead of a planned visit by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in September to arrange a meeting between opposition leaders and the premier.
Read More: PTI leadership goes into hiding
Although the meeting could not take place, he said further efforts followed calls for dialogue by PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, the president and the prime minister. Negotiations subsequently resumed, with government representatives continuing their efforts to reach an understanding.
According to Naqvi, the government waited until late at night for a response on the fourth point of the proposed agreement and made a final telephone call urging the opposition to resolve the outstanding issue.
He maintained that individuals associated with the provincial leadership had created the circumstances that eventually compelled the government to act.
“Do not put this on us,” he said, blaming those involved in provincial decision-making for the failure to reach an agreement. “We did not walk away from the negotiations,” he added.
He appealed to members of both negotiating committees and National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq to confirm that government representatives had remained available throughout the talks.
According to Naqvi, opposition representatives had repeatedly held separate consultations in another room, sometimes lasting one, two or three hours, while government representatives waited. He said the government had neither imposed a deadline on those consultations nor demanded that the opposition immediately announce a decision.
He recalled that government representatives had occasionally asked how much longer the consultations might take but had otherwise continued waiting. He maintained that the government had attended every round of negotiations and remained willing to engage.
Referring to the proposed agreement, Naqvi said nearly all its provisions reflected demands made by the opposition. The only additional line concerned the withdrawal of PTI's long march, which had been included following a suggestion by PPP Senator Sherry Rehman.
He said he had not insisted on including that condition and maintained that the government had otherwise attempted to accommodate the opposition's demands. He rejected suggestions that the government had treated negotiations as a matter of political ego or had been unwilling to maintain contact with PTI.
Read More: Govt defends K-P emergency, alleges PTI-KP govt’s ‘nexus’ with terrorists
Turning to the provincial government's financial concerns, Naqvi said he had personally accompanied the K-P chief minister to meetings with the finance minister on several occasions. He had also taken the chief minister to meet Prime Minister Shehbaz to discuss the province's financial difficulties.
Meetings had also been held with Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, and efforts had been made to address individual issues raised by the provincial government, he added.
Naqvi acknowledged that the government and opposition might hold different political positions but rejected allegations that federal authorities had attempted to exploit the province's difficulties.
He maintained that the government had continued its efforts until the final hour to prevent the imposition of emergency measures. Although it had become apparent during the final 24 hours that negotiations had failed, the government had nevertheless explored alternatives, he said.
According to the minister, one proposal involved the provincial government itself adopting emergency measures in 12 districts affected by terrorism. He claimed provincial representatives had agreed to the proposal in principle, with the aim of ensuring that the federal and provincial governments could jointly confront the security threat.
Naqvi said the chief minister had not accompanied military personnel during any counter-terrorism operation, citing political considerations as the reason. “If the chief minister does not stand with the army because he cannot afford it politically, how can we conduct operations?” he asked.
He stated that the government had been left with no alternative after repeated attempts to secure cooperation had failed. He urged lawmakers to distinguish between political disagreements and the circumstances surrounding the decision.
The minister acknowledged that preventing terrorism was the federal government's responsibility and said it would fulfil that obligation. He maintained that terrorism had to be confronted directly and that the government could not remain in the background while security personnel continued to lose their lives.
He said the fight against terrorism could not be conducted through contradictory policies, with political leaders opposing terrorism at the federal level while adopting a different position at the provincial level. He urged PTI lawmakers to consult their provincial leadership and resolve the differences.
Addressing allegations that PTI had been accused of supporting terrorism, Naqvi said no political party should face such an accusation without justification.
He maintained that the government had not accused PTI as an organisation of carrying out terrorist activities. “We never said PTI was doing this. We have always said that you were not standing with us,” he said.
However, Naqvi said some individuals at the local level were coordinating with terrorist elements. He maintained that any such conduct needed to be addressed while distinguishing it from allegations against a political party as a whole.
The interior minister also referred to the government's earlier engagement with PTI, saying efforts to resolve the party's concerns had continued for an extended period, including during 2025 and before. He added that government representatives had repeatedly held negotiations, some publicly and others privately.
Referring to the opposition's renewed offer of negotiations, Naqvi questioned why PTI representatives were unable to make decisions independently during talks. He suggested that the party's senior leadership did not sufficiently trust its own representatives to negotiate and make binding decisions.
Naqvi said government representatives attended negotiations with a mandate from the president and prime minister and expected the opposition to do the same.
He questioned the usefulness of reaching an understanding with opposition representatives if they subsequently had to return to jail to obtain their leader's approval. The interior minister urged PTI negotiators to come to the table with sufficient authority to make decisions.
He reiterated that the federal government had been prepared to negotiate in the past and remained willing to engage. PM Shehbaz had repeatedly called for political dialogue, Naqvi said, adding that the proposed agreement itself reflected a shared understanding of the need for negotiations.
Referring to the document discussed during the talks, Naqvi said its first provision concerned a meeting between opposition leaders and the prime minister to initiate political dialogue. The second proposed the formation of a political committee to discuss various matters between the government and opposition.
The third provision concerned the protection of legal rights, including medical treatment, meetings and other matters. The proposed arrangements also covered applications concerning the sentences of elderly and ill prisoners, he added.
Another provision concerned the implementation of the National Action Plan in K-P to strengthen the fight against terrorism.
Naqvi said the plan under discussion was National Action Plan II, which he maintained had been approved during PTI's tenure in government. He said political parties had agreed to the framework, which involved revisions to the earlier 20-point National Action Plan.
The minister maintained that the framework had been developed with the participation and agreement of political parties, including PTI. He questioned why a party should abandon a counter-terrorism framework merely because it was no longer in government.
Naqvi reiterated that the federal government had not wanted emergency measures to be imposed in K-P. He said the decision had caused considerable concern within the government and had been taken only after other options had been exhausted.
According to Naqvi, the situation had developed over several months, during which federal authorities had repeatedly attempted to secure cooperation from the provincial administration.
He recalled travelling to Peshawar from Karachi and other cities to attend the funeral prayers of security personnel killed in terrorist attacks. Naqvi said provincial government representatives had often failed to attend those funerals.
He maintained that the positions taken by PTI's parliamentary representatives differed considerably from those of some members of its provincial leadership. According to the minister, those differences had contributed to the failure of negotiations and the circumstances that led to the imposition of emergency measures.
Imran Khan's health and access to medical care
Referring to concerns about the health of PTI founder Imran Khan, Naqvi said the opposition had raised the matter for nearly a year and that the government had attempted to address its concerns.
He referred to PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, saying both had been involved in discussions concerning medical arrangements.
Naqvi questioned whether the government had failed to arrange detailed briefings from doctors for PTI representatives or to address their concerns.
He further said whenever the government received information suggesting a deterioration in the PTI founder's health, medical examinations had been arranged promptly. Even when a minor concern was communicated following a meeting, medical personnel had been sent to conduct examinations that same night, he added.
Naqvi maintained that such efforts had not always been made public because they concerned sensitive medical matters.
Referring to an issue involving the PTI founder's eye, Naqvi said the government had agreed to arrangements concerning his family and medical treatment. He said the government had accepted the requests presented during discussions but claimed that an additional condition had been introduced after the arrangements were finalised.
According to Naqvi, PTI representatives had initially suggested the name of another individual to be included in the hospital arrangements but later changed their position and insisted on attending themselves.
Turning to meetings with the PTI founder, the interior minister said such meetings had taken place in recent weeks and would continue. He maintained that access to the party's founder was not the central obstacle to political dialogue.
Concluding his address, Naqvi responded to remarks by Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai concerning the legitimacy of lawmakers elected through Form 47.
He said he could not swear on behalf of government lawmakers about the legitimacy of their electoral victories. However, he challenged those questioning the election results to swear that they had themselves won the seats they occupied.
Dar says opposition ignored constitutional provisions on K-P emergency
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar defended the federal government’s constitutional authority to address internal disturbances in K-P, saying the opposition had overlooked key provisions of the Constitution while challenging the move to impose emergency measures in the province.
Also speaking during the joint session, Dar said Article 232(1) of the Constitution clearly outlined the procedure for imposing an emergency and argued that its second proviso had been “conveniently ignored” by the opposition.
“Provided further that if the President acts on his own, the Proclamation of Emergency shall be placed before both Houses of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) for approval by each House within ten days,” he read from the Constitution, urging fellow lawmakers not to mislead the House or misquote the law.
Responding to opposition arguments, Dar said they had referred to Article 148(3) while ignoring Article 143, which dealt with inconsistencies between federal and provincial laws.
مجلسِ شوریٰ (پارلیمنٹ) کے مشترکہ اجلاس کے دوران نائب وزیراعظم و وفاقی وزیر خارجہ سینیٹر محمد اسحاق ڈار کا اظہارِ خیال۔ #JointSession pic.twitter.com/U70zV0RkaR
Article 148(3) states: “It shall be the duty of the Federation to protect every Province against external aggression and internal disturbances and to ensure that the Government of every Province is carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.”
Dar also cited Article 149(4), which provides for the federal government to issue directions to a province to prevent “any grave menace to the peace or tranquillity or economic life of Pakistan or any part thereof”.
He subsequently read Article 234, which deals with a situation in which a provincial government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.
Under Article 234(1), if the president, after receiving a report from the governor, is satisfied that such a situation has arisen, the president may assume some or all of the functions of the provincial government or direct the governor to do so on his behalf, subject to the provisions of the article.
Dar said the provision referred to “the satisfaction of the president and not the parliament”.
He also cited Article 234(3), which states that a proclamation issued under the article must be placed before a joint sitting of Parliament and will cease to remain in force after two months unless approved by a resolution of the joint sitting. It may be extended for further periods of up to two months at a time, but cannot remain in force for more than six months.
Turning to the security situation, Dar recalled the rise in terrorism in 2014, when the Army Public School (APS) attack took place, prompting an All Parties Conference (APC) and the formulation of the National Action Plan to combat terrorism.
“This menace of terrorism happened at its peak in 2014, during which APC incident took place. All parties conferences were called and a national action plan was made [to combat terrorism],” he said.
Dar reminded the opposition that PTI founder Imran Khan had participated in those deliberations and that the NAP was subsequently revised during the PTI-led government.
“We paid Rs100 billion annually to wage Zarb-e-Azb against the terrorists, I was the finance minister at the time,” he said, recalling the military operation launched against terrorist groups.
He said the government had initially expected the war to end within a year, but it took four years to eliminate terrorism in the region. According to Dar, the operations resulted in terrorists fleeing to the neighbouring country or dispersing within Pakistan.
He said Operation Raddul Fasaad was subsequently launched to target those who had dispersed across the country. The combined impact of the two operations and the collective resolve of the people had brought terrorist activity to “virtually zero”, he added.
Dar questioned the opposition over the return of the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) to the country, asking lawmakers: “Who were the ones who opened the border and allowed the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan to re-enter the country?”
He further questioned why the PTI-led government had released 100 hardened criminals, arguing that the current security crisis had emerged in the aftermath of those decisions. “Few individuals in that party [PTI] are responsible for this mess,” he said.

title: Salman Khan says no one stopped him from getting married  hints at wanting children
description: Actor says staying single was his own choice and discusses loneliness  fatherhood in conversation with Karan Johar
content:
Actor says staying single was his own choice and discusses loneliness, fatherhood in conversation with Karan Johar
Bollywood star Salman Khan has said his decision to remain unmarried was entirely his own, adding that he had no one else to blame for staying single and was content with how his life had unfolded.
The 60-year-old actor made the remarks during the opening episode of Season 9 of Koffee With Karan , which aired on October 14. Khan appeared as the first guest of the show's final season , hosted by filmmaker Karan Johar. The full episode has yet to be released online.
“Nobody stopped me from getting married; I stopped myself,” Khan said, explaining that remaining unmarried had been his own decision.
The actor added that he could not blame anyone else for his relationship status, saying he was happy with his choice rather than viewing himself as someone who had been denied a partner. However, he suggested that fatherhood could still be part of his future.
“I do want to have children at some point,” he said, describing having children as one of life's most wonderful experiences.
During their conversation, Johar spoke about occasionally feeling lonely without a romantic partner and asked Khan whether he experienced similar feelings. Khan challenged the idea, pointing to Johar's children and mother as sources of companionship. He argued that being without a partner did not necessarily mean someone had to feel lonely.
Khan also expressed happiness over Johar becoming a father, reiterating that children could bring considerable joy to a person's life.
The episode also saw Khan criticise photographers who capture female actors from uncomfortable or inappropriate angles. He distinguished between celebrities who deliberately arrange public appearances for promotional purposes and those who prefer to keep their lives private.
He criticised the practice of photographing actors without regard for their comfort, particularly when such images were circulated on social media. Khan also questioned posts that asked users to identify celebrities from photographs taken from behind, with Johar agreeing that the practice was ridiculous.
Actress Karisma Kapoor later joined Khan and Johar for the show's rapid-fire segment. Khan and Kapoor have appeared together in 13 films. Their chemistry on the programme prompted fans to speculate about a possible romance, with some suggesting that the two should become a real-life couple.
The appearance marked Khan's third visit to the Koffee With Karan couch. He previously appeared on the show alongside his father, screenwriter Salim Khan, and later with his brothers Arbaaz and Sohail Khan.
On the professional front, Khan is next set to appear in director Apoorva Lakhia's Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace .

title: Alexander Skarsg  rd and Olivia Colman made    Wicker    intimate scenes more seductive than expected
description: The practical costume took 18 months to make  with craftsmanship by artists who worked on    The Lord of the Rings
content:
The practical costume took 18 months to make, with craftsmanship by artists who worked on ‘The Lord of the Rings’
Alexander Skarsgård and Olivia Colman brought an unexpected sensuality to the sex scenes in Wicker , according to co-director Eleanor Wilson, who initially imagined the moments primarily as comedy.
In an interview with The Hollywood Reporter , Wilson explained that the scenes were designed to make audiences laugh. However, their tone developed during filming as Skarsgård appeared in his elaborate costume and worked alongside Colman and intimacy coordinator Ita O’Brien.
Wilson said the scenes became surprisingly more sensual than the filmmakers had anticipated once the actors began performing them on set.
The fantasy film follows a lonely fisherwoman who wishes for a husband woven for her. Her creation comes to life, setting off an unusual chain of events in a medieval village. Skarsgård plays the Wicker Husband, while Colman stars opposite him in the darkly comic fairytale.
The directors wanted the husband to look strikingly beautiful, making Skarsgård’s casting central to the character’s design. Wilson explained that the prosthetics needed to preserve the actor’s likeness and allow his facial expressions to remain visible, ensuring his performance was not lost beneath the elaborate construction.
The production favoured practical effects over extensive computer generated imagery. Skarsgård’s costume and prosthetics were created with the help of 3D printing, with the design process taking considerable time.
Speaking to Graham Norton earlier this month, the Swedish actor said the suit took 18 months to make. He praised the craftsmanship and revealed that he particularly liked the prosthetic nipples, which he later presented to the talk show host as a gift.
The costume was reportedly made by artists who had also worked on The Lord of the Rings films.
With its unusual premise, elaborate practical effects and deliberately provocative humour, Wicker has attracted attention ahead of its cinema release. The film is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on October 30, with its creative team aiming to balance absurd comedy with unexpected sensuality.

title: Sahar Hashmi calls out double standards over delayed payments in showbiz
description: Actor shares how artists face criticism for missed deadlines while overdue payments are blamed on accounts processing
content:
Actor shares how artists face criticism for missed deadlines while overdue payments are blamed on accounts processing
Actor Sahar Hashmi has drawn attention to delayed payments in the entertainment industry, highlighting what she sees as a double standard in how professionalism is judged.
Hashmi shared an Instagram Story featuring a post that contrasted the expectations placed on artists to meet deadlines with the delays they may face when waiting for their payments.
"If work is delayed by one day, it is unprofessional. If payment is delayed by 30 days, then there is a delay because of acount processing", the post read.
The post highlighted how even a one-day delay in delivering work can be labelled unprofessional, while payments held up for 30 days are often attributed to the accounts department still processing them.
"Professionalism goes both ways," the post added. She did not name any individuals or production houses in her post.
The message called for accountability on both sides of a professional relationship. While artists are expected to meet deadlines and fulfil their commitments, timely payments are also an essential part of the agreement between performers and production teams.
Delayed remuneration has been a recurring concern for performers and other professionals in the entertainment industry, where timely payments are essential to maintaining trust between artists and production teams.
Hashmi is not the only figure in Pakistan's entertainment industry to speak out about the issue. Filmmaker Mehreen Jabbar and actors Romaisa Khan , Ahmed Ali Butt , Nadia Afgan , Mohammed Ahmed and Haroon Shahid , among others, have also raised concerns about delayed payments.
Hashmi made her acting debut in the television drama Zulm and has since appeared in projects including Ishq Hua , Shadi Card and Mann Mast Malang . She gained further recognition for her performance as Bano in Zanjeerain . She has continued to build her profile through television dramas, including Shaidai .

title: Sally Rooney s books no longer sold in UK over support for banned pro Palestinian group
description: Bestselling author has been a vocal supporter of Palestine Action
content:
Bestselling author has been a vocal supporter of Palestine Action
Irish novelist Sally Rooney's books will no longer be sold in Britain over her plans to use her royalties to support Palestine ​Action, a pro-Palestinian group banned as a terrorist organisation, Rooney and ‌her publisher said on Wednesday.
The bestselling author, known for novels including Normal People and Conversations with Friends , has been a vocal supporter of Palestine Action, including after it was proscribed by ​the British government under terrorism laws last year.
Rooney previously said in ​a witness statement submitted to London's High Court, in support of ⁠a legal challenge over the ban on Palestine Action, that her plans ​could lead to her books being withdrawn from sale in Britain.
Her publisher Faber ​said on Wednesday that it had agreed with Rooney that "we can no longer supply her works in the UK in any format", though it would sell her works elsewhere.
"Current ​legislation in the UK has led to circumstances where Faber cannot pass ​on UK earnings to Sally Rooney for her work," Faber said in a statement. "To sell ‌a ⁠writer's work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher."
Rooney said in a statement: "I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions and I ​am wholly prepared to ​accept the ⁠consequences."
Palestine Action, which had increasingly targeted Israel-linked defence companies, was banned shortly after a June 2025 break-in at the ​Royal Air Force's Brize Norton base.
Last year, Palestine Action's co-founder ​Huda Ammori ⁠challenged the ban and the High Court ruled in her favour in February, before the Court of Appeal overturned that decision in June. The Supreme Court is due ⁠to ​hear an appeal next month.
More than 3,000 people ​have since been arrested for holding signs in support of Palestine Action and its proscription has ​been criticised by civil liberties groups.
