title: Sindh CM assures Chinese investors of security  announces over two dozen MoUs
description: Murad says province has strengthened police security for Chinese nationals and projects through a dedicated unit
content:
Murad says province has strengthened police security for Chinese nationals and projects through a dedicated unit
Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on Thursday assured Chinese investors of the provincial government’s commitment to protecting Chinese nationals and their projects, saying a dedicated security unit had been established within the Sindh police and its capacity was being further strengthened.
Addressing the Sindh Investment and Trade Conference in Shanghai, the chief minister said the provincial government was committed to deploying all necessary resources to ensure the safety of Chinese nationals and investments in Sindh.
“It is our government’s pledge to make sure that all resources are used to ensure the safety of Chinese people and of Chinese projects in Sindh,” he said.
CM Shah also expressed gratitude to the Chinese government for assisting in building the capacity of the provincial police to improve security arrangements.
The chief minister’s remarks came as he invited Chinese business leaders to explore investment opportunities in Sindh, announcing that more than two dozen memorandums of understanding (MoUs) would be signed across key sectors during the conference.
Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah, while delivering a keynote address at the Sindh Investment and Trade Conference in Shanghai, said that Sindh is Pakistan’s gateway to the world. Karachi Port and Port Qasim handle the bulk of Pakistan’s seaborne trade and connect… pic.twitter.com/ocBU8g8YWk
The proposed agreements would cover energy and minerals, electric vehicles and automobile manufacturing, digital transformation, food processing, logistics, warehousing and trade, underscoring the provincial government’s commitment to strengthening economic cooperation with China.
“I’m glad to inform you that today more than two dozen memorandums of agreement will be signed across these sectors,” he said, adding that each agreement would be assigned a dedicated focal person in the Sindh Investment Department and reviewed at the highest level of the provincial government.
“For us, signing is just the beginning of the work and not the end,” he said, emphasising the need to translate investment commitments into tangible economic activity.
CM Shah highlighted Sindh’s strategic location, economic base, natural resources, investment incentives and existing Chinese investments as key reasons for investors to consider the province.
Also Read: China, Pakistan begin first-ever joint army training exercise
He described Karachi as Pakistan’s financial capital and a gateway for seaborne trade, connecting investors to markets across the Middle East, Africa and Central Asia. He also pointed to the presence of the State Bank of Pakistan and the Pakistan Stock Exchange in Karachi, as well as Sindh’s young and increasingly skilled workforce.
“Thar holds about 175 billion tonnes of lignite, one of the largest coal reserves in the world,” the chief minister said, adding that the province’s wind corridor had an estimated potential of around 50,000 megawatts.
He also highlighted Sindh’s agricultural production, including rice, cotton, wheat, sugarcane, fruits and dates.
Outlining the province’s investment framework, CM Shah said special economic zones offered incentives guaranteed by law, including a 10-year income tax exemption and duty-free imports of capital goods. He also noted that Sindh was the first province in Pakistan to enact public-private partnership legislation.
Referring to a regional assessment cited during the conference, he said Sindh had been ranked sixth alongside sovereign countries, highlighting the province’s standing as an investment destination.
The Sindh Investment Department, he added, offered one-window facilitation to investors, from initial enquiries to the commencement of production.
The chief minister cited several Chinese enterprises already operating in the province as evidence of the potential for further cooperation.
He said Shanghai Electric’s Thar Block-I project, featuring a 1,320-megawatt power plant, had been in commercial operation since 2023, supplying electricity to millions of homes using locally sourced coal.
He also mentioned China Machinery Engineering Corporation’s operations at Thar Block-II and China Three Gorges Corporation’s wind farm at Jhimpir.
CM Shah also highlighted the operations of Service Long March Tyres, a Pakistan-China joint venture based in Nooriabad, saying the company had begun exporting to the United States and Brazil.
He pointed to the expansion of Chinese automobile manufacturers in Pakistan, including BYD, Changan, JAC and Dongfeng, describing electric vehicles and automobile manufacturing as sectors in which bilateral cooperation could be expanded.
“BYD sold more than 10,000 vehicles within months of its launch in Pakistan and is now setting up a 25,000 vehicles per day manufacturing facility, which is almost complete. Similarly, Changan Automobiles, Jack Motors and Dongfeng Motors, among others, are doing business in collaboration with local businesses,” the chief minister said.

Other companies he cited included United Energy Group, Pakistan-China Electric, China National Nuclear Corporation and Hutchison Ports.
Looking ahead, CM Shah identified energy and minerals, including coal-to-chemicals and the wider Thar value chain, as major areas for future collaboration. Electric vehicles, automobile manufacturing, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, smart cities, food processing and logistics were also highlighted as sectors with considerable potential.
Concluding his address, CM Shah invited Chinese business leaders to visit Sindh and assess its investment opportunities firsthand, describing deeper economic engagement as a natural extension of the 75-year friendship between Pakistan and China.
Referring to the Chinese philosopher Laozi’s saying that a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step, he said the two countries could take further steps together to build a stronger economic partnership. “Shanghai showed the world what investment can achieve. Sindh invites you to build the next story with us,” he said.
He urged Chinese investors to invest with confidence and grow alongside local businesses, adding that the province was ready to welcome new partnerships. “China and Pakistan have built a friendship that has withstood the test of time. Now let us build businesses that shape the future.”

title: Lanterns    season 2 update reveals what must happen before renewal
description: Peter Safran says an announcement about the HBO series is expected before the end of 2026
content:
Peter Safran says an announcement about the HBO series is expected before the end of 2026
HBO’s Lanterns could return for a second season, but DC Studios is making the quality of its next story a key factor in the renewal decision.
Peter Safran, co-chief of DC Studios, said the series has not yet been renewed. Speaking to Collider , he indicated that an update on its future should arrive before the end of 2026, although he did not provide a specific announcement date.
Safran explained that the creative team must develop a follow up capable of matching the standard established by the first season. He said a second season would depend on whether the writers could produce what the studio considers a worthy successor to the successful opening instalment.
The executive also highlighted the value of bringing the Green Lantern property back into the cultural conversation. Lanterns adapts characters and concepts from DC Comics’ Green Lantern franchise, which centres on an intergalactic police force.
The eight episode series stars Kyle Chandler as Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre as John Stewart. Its first season follows the two Green Lanterns as they investigate a murder mystery on Earth, bringing a grounded crime drama approach to the superhero story.
The season finale aired on October 4 and resolved the central mystery surrounding Hal Jordan’s apparent death. It also revealed the identity of the second Manhunter and explored how Stewart becomes Earth’s sole Green Lantern, setting up developments connected to DC Studios’ forthcoming film Man of Tomorrow .
The show also attracted substantial viewing figures. According to Variety , the seventh episode drew 7 million US viewers during its first three days of availability. Earlier episodes had averaged over 12 million viewers per episode in the United States, with the reported average rising to nearly 19 million when international audiences were included.
Despite that audience interest, a second season is not guaranteed. Safran’s comments suggest the writers’ room must first establish a compelling direction for the story. Fans can expect greater clarity on the series’ future before the year ends, provided the anticipated announcement arrives as indicated.

title: Israeli firm used online ads to run vast spy operation  researchers say
description: Reports show how online advertising business can serve as channel for espionage campaigns
content:
Reports show how online advertising business can serve as channel for espionage campaigns
Israeli digital advertising agency Discover-Tech spied on internet users through a sprawling network of online ads that it used to ​track targets and help hack their devices, two research groups said on Thursday.
Its services gave Israel's Candiru — a spyware company blacklisted by the US government — as well as ‌other Israeli surveillance firms access to advertising platforms run by Google, Comcast, Russia's Yandex and others, according to separate reports from Canadian cyber watchdog group Citizen Lab and New York advertising security firm Confiant.
The reports show how the online advertising business, long a subject of privacy concerns, can also serve as a channel for sweeping espionage campaigns.
"The way online advertising works today is a systemic security threat," Wolfie Cristl, a senior researcher at Citizen Lab, told Reuters . "For states, the private sector, ​civil society and everyone else alike."
Discover-Tech's online ads — often for ordinary products such as phones or earpods — reached more than 120,000 websites and 75,000 apps through its various partnerships, Citizen ​Lab said.
Read: Eight US states sue OpenAI, claiming ChatGPT harms young users
Users who visited sites or used apps with the malicious ads could be identified and tracked by Discover-Tech, which would sometimes also try to ⁠extract phone numbers from some smartphone users, the researchers said. Ads only needed to load on a website for the spying to occur.
Some ads would be used to help plant spyware from Candiru ​on users' devices, both research groups said, though Confiant said that ads it tied to Candiru were a tiny fraction of Discover-Tech's overall volume.
Malicious ads shown in hundreds of sensitive networks
Confiant cofounder Jerome Dangu ​said Discover-Tech was pumping out at least 10 million ads per day all around the world and that data-sharing arrangements — called cookie matching — allowed it to track people even beyond the reach of its advertisements.
"Very likely hundreds of millions of people would have been touched by Discover-Tech," Dangu said.
Discover-Tech, which was founded in 2020, did not return messages left via its contact form. A LinkedIn message and emails sent to its chief executive, Dekel Boni, were not returned.
Reuters ' ​attempts to reach Candiru's owners were not successful. The US Commerce Department blacklisted Candiru in 2021 for allegedly supplying spyware that was used to maliciously target government officials, journalists, activists and academics.
Citizen Lab said ​a powerful form of Candiru spyware delivered through Discover-Tech's ads had been used to compromise 45 Windows devices at the Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera between 2024 and 2025, something it said it was able to confirm because ‌the media ⁠group had shared its network logs with the group. Al Jazeera did not return messages seeking comment.
Dangu of Confiant said that the malicious ads had been shown to users in "hundreds of networks in sensitive categories," including the Pentagon, the International Atomic Energy Agency, and the International Criminal Court. He also said that some regions, like the Palestinian territories, were particularly saturated by the Israeli firm's ads.
"You go to almost any site in Palestine — any site — you find a Discover-Tech ad. It gives them a very complete visibility on the digital activities of an entire country," he said.
Read more: Australia introduces digital safety bill allowing users to switch off social media algorithms
Citizen Lab also said it had similar ​evidence showing the malicious ads were shown to people ​in the United Nations, NATO, the European ⁠Commission, and more than a dozen other national governments. Other networks the ads appeared in included chip-related firms such as Nvidia, SanDisk, Broadcom, and Micron, as well as several media organisations in Mexico, Israel, and Europe that were not identified.
In addition to identifying Candiru and a couple of other surveillance vendors, ​Citizen Lab said it was able to glean some details about where Discover-Tech's users might be based because the firm inadvertently exposed its authentication ​logs to the internet, ⁠showing people logging in from internet protocol addresses in Israel, Europe, and the Gulf.
Discover-Tech is now being frozen out of parts of the online ad market.
Google said in a statement that it had collaborated with Citizen Lab and Confiant's investigation and kicked Discover-Tech off its ad platforms "for systematically violating our policies."
IAB Europe, the European-level association for the digital marketing and advertising ecosystem, said in an email that Discover-Tech had ⁠been suspended from ​its list of globally approved vendors last week after an audit identified policy violations.
Comcast ad tech subsidiary Beeswax removed Discover-Tech ​from its platform "following recent activity," Comcast said in a statement. Yandex did not return Reuters messages seeking comment.
Advertising-driven surveillance is increasingly being seen as a national security threat. Earlier this year, the Pentagon said it had received reports that US forces deployed ​to war zones had been targeted using location data harvested by ad tech firms and data brokers. Branches of the military have since disabled ad tracking on some devices.

title: Netflix   s    Hollywood Arts    faces criticism for blatantly copying    Victorious
description: The 12 episode series introduces a new generation of students at the performing arts school in Los Angeles
content:
The 12 episode series introduces a new generation of students at the performing arts school in Los Angeles
Netflix has returned to the world of Nickelodeon’s Victorious with Hollywood Arts , a 12 episode spinoff starring Daniella Monet as Trina Vega. However, the new series has received a mixed assessment, with Variety critic Aramide Tinubu describing it as a largely unoriginal return to a familiar television formula.
Created by Jake Farrow and Samantha Martin, the comedy follows Trina as she struggles to establish herself as an actress while living in the shadow of her younger sister, Tori Vega, played by Victoria Justice in the original series. With acting opportunities scarce, Trina accepts a substitute teaching position at Hollywood Arts, despite having little experience to qualify her for the role.
The series begins with the retirement of Mr Sikowitz, played again by Eric Lane, prompting principal Helen, portrayed by Yvette Nicole Brown, to bring Trina in as a temporary instructor. Her unconventional teaching methods soon introduce her to a new group of aspiring performers.
Among the students are Qwest, a musician who has misled his parents about receiving a basketball scholarship, and Oscar, the school’s biggest star. Oscar’s sister Emmy works behind the scenes as a stage manager, while classmates Jen and Pepper compete for attention and success.
Tinubu criticises the show’s exaggerated performances, awkward dialogue and resemblance to earlier children’s sitcoms. The review suggests that viewers familiar with Victorious may find little that feels fresh in the new production.
Nevertheless, the critic identifies a promising element in Trina’s character. As a woman in her thirties who remains uncertain about her career and future, she offers a relatable portrayal of adulthood for younger viewers. Her students also face questions about their talents, ambitions and place in the performing arts world.
The review praises the ensemble’s comic timing, physical performances and musical abilities, particularly Emmy Liu Wang’s singing.
Although Hollywood Arts does not break new ground, the series could appeal to preteen audiences seeking a lighthearted school comedy. The show is now streaming on Netflix, offering younger viewers a new entry point into the franchise while bringing back a familiar character for longtime fans.

title: Meghan Markle and Prince Harry reunite for first official joint outing since moving back to the UK
description: The joint appearance comes nearly two months after the Sussexes returned to Britain
content:
The joint appearance comes nearly two months after the Sussexes returned to Britain
Meghan Markle and Prince Harry have made their first official joint public appearance since relocating to the United Kingdom with their two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, visiting Nottingham on October 15, 2026, to support local charities and youth programmes.
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex received a warm welcome from a crowd of around 100 people as they arrived at the Community Recording Studio (CRS), a charity that provides young people with access to music, recording facilities, creative activities and mentoring. Meghan greeted well-wishers, accepted flowers and a balloon, and told one person in the crowd, “It's great to be back.”
The visit held particular significance for the couple, as Nottingham was where they made their first official joint appearance following their engagement announcement in November 2017. Nearly nine years later, their return marks a new chapter as they resume their charitable work in Britain after moving back from California.
During their visit to CRS, Harry reunited with Jah Digga, a musician, poet and youth mentor who attended the organisation as a child. Digga has spoken about how the charity helped him move away from gang involvement. Meanwhile, Meghan joined a confidence-building and bracelet-making workshop with young girls, and the couple observed an acting workshop led by professional actor André Squire.
The Duke and Duchess also planned visits to Epic Partners, an organisation supporting children and families through mentoring, education and sport, and Himmah Hub, a community group working to tackle food poverty. At Himmah Hub, Meghan was expected to reunite with women involved in the Hubb Community Kitchen, which she supported after the 2017 Grenfell Tower fire. She previously collaborated with the women on a charity cookbook.
Harry has longstanding ties to Nottingham's youth initiatives. His involvement with Epic began after a visit to the community in 2013, leading to the Full Effect programme, which combined mentoring, school-based support and creative activities. The initiative received backing from The Royal Foundation, the charitable organisation Harry established with his brother, Prince William, in 2009. Harry and Meghan later separated from the foundation in 2019 to pursue their own charitable work.
The joint appearance comes nearly two months after the Sussexes returned to Britain with Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5, following several years living in Montecito, California. The family has since settled in the Cotswolds, with the children attending school in England.
According to a source close to the couple, their initial priority after the move was establishing a routine and helping their children settle into their new surroundings. Now, with the family adjusting to life in Britain, Harry and Meghan are turning their attention towards their professional and philanthropic commitments.
“After they first arrived in England, their focus was on establishing a routine and getting the kids settled into school,” the source told PEOPLE. “Now, they're both excited to focus more on their work and the projects that matter to them.”
The insider added that the couple are balancing their working lives with family time, explaining that they work during the week while the children are at school and enjoy weekends together.
Meghan's Nottingham appearance also marked her first official engagement since returning to Britain in August. Harry, meanwhile, had already undertaken several solo appearances, including events connected to the Invictus Games.
Their return to Nottingham offers a reminder of how much has changed since their first joint engagement in 2017. No longer working members of the royal family, Harry and Meghan are now pursuing charitable initiatives independently while rebuilding their lives in the country they previously left.
For the couple, the visit represents an opportunity to reconnect with communities and organisations that have played an important role in their charitable work, while beginning a new phase of public engagement in the UK.

title: Australia introduces digital safety bill allowing users to switch off social media algorithms
description: Proposed law to give users greater control over feeds  impose safety obligations on tech companies  introduce fines
content:
Proposed law to give users greater control over feeds, impose safety obligations on tech companies, introduce fines
Australia introduced legislation Thursday requiring social media platforms to let users switch off algorithm-driven recommendations, as part of sweeping measures aimed at strengthening online safety.
The Digital Duty of Care Bill 2026 would require technology companies to proactively prevent online harms rather than respond after they occur.
According to a statement published on Communications Minister Anika Wells’ official website, Australians aged over 16 would be able to choose between algorithmically recommended content as their primary feed or accounts they follow.
The proposed law would establish minimum safety standards for social media platforms, gaming services, applications and artificial intelligence chatbots.
Platforms would also be required to protect users under 18 from harmful content, including material promoting eating disorders, dangerous stunts, criminal behaviour and hostility toward women.
Read: Under new regulations, Turkiye bans children under 15 from social media
The legislation would empower Australia's eSafety Commissioner to remove AI-powered nudification services and reduce response deadlines for cyberbullying and online abuse complaints from 48 to 24 hours.
Companies violating the requirements could face penalties of up to 109.2 million Australian dollars (75 million US dollars).
Professional news content and entertainment media would be exempt from the proposed provisions.
"The Digital Duty of Care is the next step in our world-leading online safety laws," Wells said.
Read more: The surrender to algorithmic control
"It will set basic safety standards for the digital services we use every day, just as we have for food, cars and kids’ toys," she added.
The bill was introduced in the House of Representatives and must pass both houses of Parliament, including the Senate, before becoming law.
The proposal follows Australia's landmark restrictions on social media access for children under 16, part of Canberra's broader efforts to regulate digital platforms.

BBC commissioned two-part documentary about J.K. Rowling’s 'Harry Potter' success amid divisive gender identity views
BBC has commissioned a two-part documentary examining the career and legacy of J.K. Rowling, exploring her rise to fame through Harry Potter and the public debate surrounding her views on gender identity.
Scheduled to premiere next year, the documentary will examine the author’s childhood, the creation of the bestselling fantasy series and her subsequent public interventions. Rowling is not involved in the production.
The first episode will focus on Rowling’s early life and the development of Harry Potter, which brought together millions of young readers and generated a global franchise worth billions.
According to the documentary’s press release, “As the books inspired a generation of outsiders and brought millions of young fans together through the emerging internet, Rowling created a universe with an economic legacy worth billions”.
The second instalment will examine Rowling’s life and public profile after the success of Harry Potter, including her comments on Scottish independence, feminism, free speech and gender identity.
The announcement comes amid continued debate over Rowling’s views on transgender people and their impact on her relationship with some fans and members of the Harry Potter film cast.
The author is also an executive producer on HBO’s upcoming Harry Potter television adaptation, which has faced calls for a boycott from some viewers because of her views. The series is scheduled to launch in December.
Several actors associated with the adaptation have faced criticism over their involvement. John Lithgow, who will portray Albus Dumbledore, previously said he considered leaving the project following backlash over Rowling’s views, but ultimately decided to remain.
Lithgow defended his decision by describing the books as “clearly on the side of the angels, against intolerance and bigotry.”
The BBC’s documentary is expected to examine how Rowling’s public statements have shaped discussions about her work and legacy, alongside the enduring commercial success of the Harry Potter franchise.

title: Egypt  Qatar stress need to halt hostilities against Saudi Arabia
description: Foreign ministers condemn attacks on kingdom  call for diplomatic efforts to contain regional tensions
content:
Foreign ministers condemn attacks on kingdom, call for diplomatic efforts to contain regional tensions
Egypt and Qatar stressed the need to halt all hostilities against Saudi Arabia and expressed solidarity with the kingdom, according to the Egyptian Foreign Ministry on Thursday.
The position was expressed during a phone call late Wednesday between Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and his Qatari counterpart, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, the ministry said in a statement.
The call came as part of “continuous communication and coordination between the two brotherly countries on various issues of common interest,” the statement said.
The two officials discussed bilateral relations and areas of cooperation, including exchanges of high-level visits. They praised the progress in ties and affirmed their commitment to further strengthening them, according to the statement.
On regional developments, the officials discussed the latest situation and agreed on the importance of supporting ongoing efforts and coordinating action to ease tensions and prevent the conflict from spreading.
Read: Saudi-led coalition intercepts and destroys drone in eastern Saudi Arabia
They stressed the need to halt all hostilities against Saudi Arabia, strongly condemned the attacks and expressed solidarity with the kingdom.
The officials also called for activating political and diplomatic channels to resolve the current crisis and strengthen regional security and stability.
The call came amid an ongoing military escalation between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthi group, involving missile and drone attacks on airports and critical infrastructure in the kingdom in recent days.
Since October 5, five Saudi airports have come under attack, leaving 20 people dead and hundreds injured, in addition to material damage and disruptions to air traffic, according to the report.
Meanwhile, the military operation known as Dawn of Yemen has continued. Yemeni Presidential Leadership Council Chairman Rashad al-Alimi said the operation aims to restore state institutions from Houthi control and retake the capital, Sanaa.
Read more: Houthis claim ballistic missile strike on Riyadh airport
The developments in Yemen are part of a military escalation that began in July and is the most extensive since a period of relative calm following a UN-brokered truce that began in April 2022.
Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition supporting Yemen’s internationally recognised government since 2015 against the Houthis, who have controlled Sanaa and several other provinces since 2014.

title: Coe backs Kenya   s 2029 Worlds to fight doping
description: Around 140 Kenyan athletes have been suspended amid efforts to clean up the sport
content:
Around 140 Kenyan athletes have been suspended amid efforts to clean up the sport
Kenya hosting the 2029 World Athletics Championships will help combat the endemic doping problem among its athletes, World Athletics president Sebastian Coe said on a visit to Nairobi on Wednesday.
The east African nation is a global athletics powerhouse, particularly in long-distance and middle-distance running, but has seen a surge in doping cases in recent years.
Around 140 Kenyan athletes have been suspended, including a positive test announced as recently as Tuesday by monitoring body Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU).
"The championships will help us in that quest" for a cleaner Kenyan athletics scene, Coe told AFP on the sidelines of a press conference in Nairobi.
"Is there more work to be done? Yes. Will these championships lend more focus to that? Absolutely," he said.
The AIU is "very clear in their reports to me that progress is being made" in Kenya, he said, adding the country had come a "long way".
Kenya has won the right to host the World Championships in Africa for the first time.
At last year's edition in Tokyo, Kenya finished second overall behind the United States, taking home 11 medals: seven gold, two silver and two bronze.
Marathon world record holder Ruth Chepngetich was handed a three-year ban by the AIU in October 2025 after admitting to doping.
Earlier that year, Benard Kibet, who finished fifth in the 10,000m at the Paris Olympics, was also suspended by the AIU.
In March, Albert Korir, who won the New York Marathon in 2021, was handed a five-year ban after testing positive for a banned performance-enhancing drug.
Athletics is a national sport in Kenya -- where unemployment remains high and well-paid jobs scarce -- and is viewed by many as a way out of poverty.
Coe said that having spoken with Kenya's previous and current leader, integrity in Kenyan athletics is seen as a "key national imperative" and "should be in the best shape possible".
The Briton acknowledged that although Kenyan authorities had improved resources to fight doping, "we'll never be in a perfect world".

title: Bodo sink Dortmund in Champions League
description: Sjovold   s 52nd minute strike proves decisive as the German side suffer their first defeat of the campaign
content:
Sjovold’s 52nd-minute strike proves decisive as the German side suffer their first defeat of the campaign
Fredrik Sjovold's 52nd-minute strike secured a 1-0 victory for Bodo/Glimt over Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Wednesday, extending the Norwegian side's remarkable home record against Europe's elite.
Bodo were a cut above the 2024 Champions League runners-up and took the lead through Sjovold just after the break.
Dortmund improved in the final half hour but were unable to strike back, despite a late chance for Felix Nmecha.
"There's nothing we can complain about, we deserved to lose," Dortmund coach Niko Kovac told DAZN.
"We didn't bring enough passion today -- that's something Bodo did much better. They took the lead and after that we woke up, but by then it was too late."
Dortmund join Manchester City, Inter Milan and Sporting as recent big-name scalps on the artificial turf of Bodo's Aspmyra stadium.
"Each of us needs to ask ourselves what the problem was," Dortmund captain Waldemar Anton said.
"In several areas we were missing our intensity today and without this intensity you won't win a game."
Bodo's run to the round of 16 last season was underpinned by an excellent record at their 8,200-capacity home, officially the smallest venue in this year's competition.
Dortmund arrived in the Arctic Circle on a seven-game unbeaten run but struggled to get a foothold.
The hosts were far more comfortable in the opening half, with Sondre Fet and Ole Blomberg inches away from scoring.
Bodo continued their domination after half-time and broke through when Sjovold turned a low Sondre Auklend cross in at the near post.

Lavrov, Wang meet in Azerbaijan to discuss bilateral ties and international agenda on sidelines of conference
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi discussed bilateral ties and the ongoing wars in Ukraine and Iran during talks on the sidelines of an Asian security meeting.
A statement by the Russian Foreign Ministry late Wednesday that the meeting, held on the sidelines of the 7th summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) in Azerbaijan’s capital Baku, “highly assessed” the development of bilateral ties.
Expressing this assessment particularly in the context of the 25th anniversary of the 2001 Sino-Russian Treaty of Friendship, the statement said Lavrov and Wang coordinated positions on bilateral political dialogue, among other issues.
“An in-depth exchange of views took place regarding cooperation within the CICA framework, and the future development of this platform was discussed,” the statement said, noting that both parties emphasised the importance of bolstering coordination on international platforms.
The statement further said the two sides also discussed relations with the US and the situation surrounding the Ukraine and Iran wars, adding that the talks were held in an atmosphere of “trust and constructive cooperation characteristic of Russian-Chinese relations.”
The 7th CICA summit, hosted by Azerbaijan as the current chair of the intergovernmental forum, will bring together representatives of member states, observer countries, and partner international organisations.
Discussions will focus on regional cooperation, connectivity, digitalisation, and sustainable development under Azerbaijan's chairmanship priorities.

description: He will miss four La Liga fixtures after his dismissal against Villarreal
content:
He will miss four La Liga fixtures after his dismissal against Villarreal
Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior will miss the upcoming Clasico in La Liga against Barcelona after being issued a four-match suspension on Wednesday following his red card for hair-pulling against Villarreal last week.
The Spanish football federation's disciplinary committee confirmed the Brazilian will be banned for several matches including the visit to face league leaders Barca on October 25 for both the red card and his subsequent protests.
The committee said Vinicius had been suspended for two games for "behaving violently... (while) not being in a position to challenge for the ball" and a further two matches for "protests" to the officials.
As well as the Clasico, Vinicius will be unavailable to face Sevilla (October 18), Racing Santander (November 1) and Valencia (November 7) in La Liga.
Despite Vinicius's red card against Villarreal, Jose Mourinho's fourth-place Madrid earned a 1-0 win to stay six points behind Barcelona.
The 26-year-old winger reacted angrily to the decision, made after a VAR review, which also chalked off a goal he had scored in the aftermath of his pull on Nathan Saliba's hair.
Vinicius had to be held back by his team-mates as he remonstrated with referee Isidro Diaz de Mera.
Mourinho, also upset by the officiating, refused to participate in his post-match press conference.
Vinicius apologised to his teammates and Madrid supporters after the match. "I am sorry to the team and the fans," he wrote on social media.
The attacker has endured a difficult start to the campaign, scoring just once in nine appearances, and was dropped to the bench against Villarreal, with his red card occurring around 20 minutes after he was introduced as a substitute.
Madrid's visit to Camp Nou will be Mourinho's first Clasico since returning as coach of Los Blancos this summer.
Thus far Hansi Flick's Barcelona, back-to-back Spanish champions, boast a perfect record of 10 wins from 10 matches this season across all competitions.

content:
The Asian Cup and other events also face uncertainty
FIFA and the Saudi Esports Federation have postponed the FIFAe Finals 2026 scheduled to take place in Jeddah from October 16 to 25, organisers said on Thursday following recent attacks on Saudi Arabia.
A strike on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday killed at least 12 people and wounded more than 300, with Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi movement claiming responsibility for the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade.
"The decision follows an ⁠assessment of recent developments in the region and their impact on the logistical arrangements required to stage the tournament," organisers of the global video game tournament said.
"Further announcements on the FIFAe Finals will be communicated in due course."
Japan and Brazil withdrew their esports teams on Saturday after assessing the situation in the host country.
The security uncertainty has cast a shadow over sporting events in the kingdom.
The Six Kings Slam exhibition tennis tournament was moved from ⁠October to December while golf's Asian Tour said it is monitoring developments ahead of next month's Saudi International in Riyadh.
The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) said it remains open to delaying the Asian Cup until 2028 if necessary. The continental tournament is scheduled ⁠to kick off on January 7 next year across venues in Riyadh, Jeddah and Al Khobar.
The Korea Football Association (KFA) said it was in communication with the AFC.
"We ⁠are closely monitoring the situation in Saudi Arabia and plan to continue discussions regarding overall developments," the KFA said in a statement.
The previous Asian ⁠Cup was delayed by a year after China withdrew as hosts because of COVID-19 restrictions, with Qatar stepping in to stage the tournament in early 2024.

title: Naseem seeks peak form after injury setbacks
description: The pacer returns to the Pakistan team after a seven month absence
content:
The pacer returns to the Pakistan team after a seven-month absence
Now three months shy of his 24th birthday, with 93 international appearances and 155 wickets to his name, Pakistan fast bowler Naseem Shah says maturity and experience have changed his approach to the game.
“You change a lot as a human being and a cricketer as you age, with maturity levels and experience enhancing,” Naseem told PCB Digital.
“You also learn a lot through ups and downs in life. You do bowl express pace when you are young and new in the sport, but now I think that you also need to have some sense in terms of what you are trying to do.”
Naseem made an immediate impact on his return to international cricket on Friday, October 9, taking three wickets in Pakistan's opening T20 international against Sri Lanka at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium.
The right-arm paceman, playing his first international match in seven months, claimed three for 36 from four overs, striking with just his fifth legitimate delivery.
Rawalpindi holds special significance for Naseem. In February 2020, during only his fourth match for Pakistan, he became the youngest bowler to take a Test hat-trick, achieving the feat against Bangladesh at the age of 16 years and 359 days.
Injuries, however, have repeatedly interrupted his progress during a seven-year international career. One of his biggest disappointments was missing the 2023 ICC Cricket World Cup, while a back injury sustained during the 2026 Pakistan Super League ruled him out of the tournament.
Reflecting on the challenges of rehabilitation, Naseem said injuries could force players to start again from scratch.
“You go back to zero whenever you are injured and sometimes it doesn’t even allow you to go for a run, let alone going through the motions of the game,” he said.
“The rehabilitation programme then becomes important. It is also critical how well you understand your body during those times. Being surrounded by a good medical team also helps.”
Naseem's return against Sri Lanka offered encouraging signs. He first induced an edge from visiting captain Kusal Mendis with a 136.9kph delivery, which was caught at third man.
As Sri Lanka looked to accelerate in the closing stages, he uprooted Dunith Wellalage's leg stump with a 141.9kph delivery before dismissing Lahiru Udara two balls later, with the batter caught at long-on attempting to hit a yorker.
Although he went wicketless in the second T20 international, Naseem conceded only nine runs in two powerplay overs, helping set the tone for Sri Lanka's eventual collapse in the chase.
Asked how fast bowlers could succeed in modern white-ball cricket, where high-scoring matches and entertainment often dominate, Naseem stressed the importance of developing a wider range of skills.
“You have to toy with a batter's mindset in modern-day white-ball cricket given the nature of surfaces around the world and the focus on entertainment through run-fests,” he said.
“One ought to become more skilful and developed as a bowler in these times.”
Naseem is also part of Pakistan's squad for the upcoming one-day international tri-series involving England and Sri Lanka. The competition will form part of Pakistan's preparations for the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, where Shaheen Shah Afridi is set to lead the side.
Pakistan begin their World Cup campaign against Afghanistan on October 8, 2027, and Naseem will be eager to secure a place at his first senior ICC World Cup after missing the 2023 tournament.
He has taken 60 wickets in 34 ODIs at an average of 25.91 and a strike rate of 28.3. His two five-wicket hauls came in consecutive matches: 5-33 against the Netherlands in August 2022 and 5-57 against New Zealand in January 2023.
The achievement made him only the sixth Pakistan bowler to take at least two consecutive five-wicket hauls in the format.
Despite his achievements, Naseem believes his best cricket is still ahead of him.
“I feel I'm yet to play my peak cricket. Whatever the cricket I've played so far, especially Test cricket, I think I lacked a few things,” he said.
“My simple goal is to perform so much that there is no need to talk out loud about my goals or performances. When there are fewer injuries and you are bowling with good rhythm, everything falls into place itself.”

Jenner made it clear that she had never felt a desire to pursue relationships with women
Kendall Jenner has offered a rare glimpse into her dating life, joking that being a lesbian would make relationships easier while addressing long-running speculation about her sexuality during a candid conversation with longtime friend Cara Delevingne on The Kardashians.
In the October 15 episode of the reality series, the 30-year-old model spoke to Delevingne backstage at the L’Oréal Paris Fashion Week show about rumours that the pair had previously dated. Jenner explained that speculation about her sexuality had persisted because of their close friendship.
“We should address this,” Jenner said. “It’s because of our love for each other. People think I’m a lesbian to this day.”
Jenner then clarified that she is not a lesbian, with Delevingne confirming that she knew her friend well enough to support the statement. However, Jenner admitted that she sometimes wonders whether dating women would be easier.
“By the way, I wouldn’t be opposed to having some fun with a girl, let me tell you,” she said, before adding, “For the record, I think being a lesbian would be fun and amazing and easier? I don’t know. Men suck.”
Despite the playful remarks, Jenner made it clear that she had never felt a desire to pursue relationships with women. “I have nothing against having sex with Cara. I just have never had a desire to have sex with women,” she explained, joking that she had consumed too much wine and needed to calm down.
Delevingne embraced the conversation, asking Jenner which woman she would choose if she ever decided to have sex with one. Jenner immediately named her friend, explaining that Delevingne was the only woman she knew who would be nice to her.
The discussion took place in September 2025, when the pair were spending time together during Paris Fashion Week. It also addressed speculation that they had once been romantically involved, something Jenner firmly denied.
The model explained that she and Delevingne had been friends for approximately 11 or 12 years. She credited Delevingne with helping her feel safe and welcome when she was establishing herself in the modelling industry.
“I love Cara. She’s my sister, and that never happened,” Jenner said of the dating rumours.
Jenner has previously spoken about the speculation surrounding her sexuality, including in a January 2026 appearance on Owen Thiele’s podcast In My Dreams. The latest comments offer another example of how Jenner is addressing questions about her private life while maintaining the boundaries she has established around her relationships.

title: Law ministry notifies jail trial for Imaan  Hadi
description: Lawyers  witnesses to attend hearing at Adiala amid complaints over meeting conditions  accused   s physical production
content:
Lawyers, witnesses to attend hearing at Adiala amid complaints over meeting conditions, accused’s physical production
An Islamabad anti-terrorism court (ATC) was informed on Thursday that the Ministry of Law had issued a notification directing that the next hearing of the case against lawyer Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, over the removal of barriers be held at Adiala Jail.
Earlier, ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra had directed lawyers and witnesses to appear at Adiala Jail for the next hearing. The case, registered at Aabpara police station, was subsequently adjourned until Friday.
During Thursday’s hearing, Imaan and Hadi appeared before the court via video link, while their lawyers, Eamil Khan Mandokhail and Riasat Ali Azad, appeared in person. Mandokhail submitted an affidavit detailing the difficulties he said he had faced when he visited Adiala Jail on Tuesday to meet his clients.
According to the affidavit, he received a certified copy of the court order at 2:52pm and reached Central Jail Adiala at 3:50pm. He said he presented the order to the deputy superintendent and requested a confidential meeting in accordance with the Pakistan Prison Rules 1978 and the court’s directions.
He said he was made to wait for about an hour before being allowed to meet his clients at 4:45pm. The meeting lasted only 25 minutes and ended at 5:10pm.
Mandokhail said the meeting had taken place in a conference room rather than a separate room, adding that it had been recorded and lacked privacy. He said he had brought copies of case documents to hand over to his clients but was not allowed to take the documents inside or give them to the two accused.
The affidavit further stated that two female constables had remained with Imaan throughout the meeting, the door had been kept open, and male constables had stood outside. Jail officials could hear the entire conversation, Mandokhail said, describing the arrangements as a violation of the court’s order.
Read: Imaan, Hadi boycott proceedings as ATC records witness statements
He added that Imaan and Hadi had repeatedly told the court that they had not been provided with the relevant documents either before or after the charges were framed.
According to the affidavit, the two accused had insisted during the brief meeting that they were not boycotting the trial. Mandokhail said they wanted to appear in person because audio and internet problems during online appearances prevented them from following the proceedings properly and consulting their lawyers.
He further said his clients had instructed him to challenge all court orders.
Separately, Azad argued that the trial could not proceed in the absence of the accused in person. He said police routinely brought accused persons before the court and questioned why Imaan and Hadi had not been produced.
“They are not terrorists; they can even come on a horse-drawn carriage,” Azad said, arguing that there was no reason the two could not be brought to court.
Judge Sipra said he had been issuing directions for four or five days for the accused to be produced. Questioning why the police had not taken similar steps earlier, he said their conduct was regrettable. “I just want to know what the police are doing. They have changed the whole game,” he added.
The judge also asked whether the jail authorities had submitted a report explaining the failure to produce the accused. He directed his court staff to check whether a report had been received and said the senior superintendent of police would be summoned if it had not.
During the proceedings, the judge said the police had filed an application seeking a jail trial, but the matter had not yet been finalised. He declined to comment on the application, saying it was a legal matter.
Superintendent of Police (SP) Pari Gul requested two to three hours to report on progress, while Azad asked the court to adjourn the matter to another date.
Read more: ATC orders jail authorities to facilitate lawyers' meetings with Imaan, Hadi
The judge also questioned the conditions under which the meeting at Adiala Jail had taken place after Mandokhail said separate rooms were available but his meeting had been arranged in a conference room.
When the judge asked what kind of environment the lawyers wanted, Mandokhail reiterated that the arrangements had prevented them from discussing the case properly.
Azad also asked the court to question police officials about how Imaan and Hadi had arrived at the court at 10pm the previous night. Imaan’s mother, Shireen Mazari, urged the court to ask the police why 12 vehicles had been involved when the two were previously produced.
Addressing the accused through the video link, Judge Sipra briefed them on the proceedings. Hadi said they had no objection to either appearing physically before the court or facing a jail trial, provided their lawyers and journalists were also allowed to be present at the jail.
The hearing was subsequently adjourned. The Ministry of Law’s notification provided for the next hearing to be held at Adiala Jail, with lawyers and witnesses directed to attend.
Imaan and her husband Hadi were rearrested on September 17 , shortly after the Supreme Court granted them bail and suspended their sentences in a separate social-media posts case. They were produced before an Islamabad ATC in connection with a case registered at Kohsar Police Station.
Police sought 30-day physical remand, but ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain rejected the request and sent the couple on judicial remand. The judge noted that although they had been nominated in the FIR as members of an unlawful assembly, no weapon had been attributed to either accused.
Read More: SC suspends trial court order, grants bail to Imaan Mazari, Hadi Ali Chattha
On September 27, the court issued a contempt notice to the Adiala jail superintendent after the authorities failed to facilitate the signing and transmission of the documents and also failed to produce the accused through video link. Two days later, the issue was resolved after Imaan and Hadi signed the required powers of attorney.
On September 29 , the ATC ended the contempt proceedings against the jail authorities and separately confirmed that notices had been issued on the couple’s bail applications, with arguments scheduled before Judge Abul Hasnat.
On October 7, the ATC had framed charges against Imaan and Hadi in the case related to the alleged violation of a designated route and incitement during the arrival of an international cricket team, despite defence objections that legal requirements had not been fulfilled.

content:
Gillis faces criticism for his remarks about women’s gym clothes, describing female gymgoers as dressing 'like wh*res'
Kathy Griffin has criticised comedian Shane Gillis following his controversial Saturday Night Live monologue, describing him as a “hack” while defending his right to express himself through comedy.
In an interview with Page Six , published on October 14, Griffin said comedians should retain their freedom of speech, even when audiences disagree with their material.
“I think as a comic I’m always going to fight for the First Amendment and his right to say it and yet I don’t have to like it,” she said. “So, I defend his right to say it, and I also defend everyone else’s right to think less of him.”
Griffin also criticised a wider group of male comedians, arguing that many rely on similar material and outdated jokes about women.
She referenced comedian Joe Rogan while discussing performers who gained popularity through podcasts and social media.
“There are a lot of hacks who are doing very well, and they come from TikTok or the podcast world,” Griffin said.

Gillis attracted criticism after his October 10 SNL monologue included remarks about women’s gym clothing, describing female gymgoers as dressing “like wh*res”.
His comments prompted responses from several public figures, including Schitt’s Creek star Dan Levy, who challenged the remarks as misogynistic.
Griffin also emphasised the importance of comedians adapting their material over time, reflecting on changes in her own approach to comedy.
“I think it’s important that comedians evolve and change with the times,” she explained.
The comedian added that she had previously used language she now regrets, saying, “I want to think that I’m still learning.”
Griffin is currently on tour and was scheduled to appear at The Town Hall on Friday.

title: PSX gains 769 points despite profit taking
description: KSE 100 reclaims 166 000 level amid broad based buying
content:
KSE-100 reclaims 166,000 level amid broad-based buying
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) extended its gains on Thursday, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index rising 769 points, or 0.46%, to close at 166,186, reclaiming the 166,000 level amid broad-based buying.
According to Ali Najib, deputy head of Trading at Arif Habib Limited, the market maintained its upward momentum throughout the session after opening on a positive note. The index touched an intraday high of 166,877, gaining 1,460 points, or 0.88%, before profit-taking in select stocks trimmed some of the gains.
The market's close above 166,000, supported by turnover of Rs23.5 billion, indicated a constructive near-term outlook. However, profit-taking near the session's high suggested that some investors were opting to sell at higher levels, while escalating regional security risks could keep sentiment cautious.
On the geopolitical front, continued Houthi attacks targeting airports and oil facilities in Saudi Arabia heightened regional security concerns, adding to the risks facing investors.
Among individual stocks, Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL), Fauji Fertiliser Company (FFC), Systems Limited (SYS), Hub Power Company (HUBC), Oil and Gas Development Company (OGDC), Meezan Bank (MEBL), Lucky Cement (LUCK), Habib Bank (HBL), Pakistan Petroleum Limited (PPL) and United Bank Limited (UBL) collectively contributed 560 points to the benchmark's gain.
Trading activity remained stable, with 516.4 million shares changing hands and total market turnover reaching Rs23.5 billion. Cnergyico PK Limited (CNERGY) led the volume chart, with 62.8 million shares traded.
Analysts cautioned that profit-taking and heightened geopolitical risks could temper the market's momentum despite the benchmark's recovery above the 166,000 level.

title: White House defends Press Secretary Katie Zacharia amid questions over legal credentials
description: Watchdog group files complaint seeking investigation into whether she presented herself as authorised to practise law
content:
Watchdog group files complaint seeking investigation into whether she presented herself as authorised to practise law
The White House is defending newly appointed Press Secretary Katie Zacharia amid questions over her legal credentials.
US President Donald Trump introduced Zacharia as an attorney when announcing her appointment last week, and she has also described herself as a lawyer.
However, when a reporter asked on Tuesday which state she had passed the bar exam in, Zacharia replied while standing alongside the president: "When I moved to China."
Zacharia does not appear to be registered with the bar in any of the states where she has lived. White House communications director Steven Cheung defended her appointment, describing her as "uniquely qualified and whip smart to help inform the American people."
Addressing questions about her legal credentials, Zacharia said in a statement this week: "I practised international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials."
Read: Karoline Leavitt announces second pregnancy as she continues role as White House press secretary
On Wednesday, watchdog group Campaign for Accountability filed a complaint with the California State Bar, seeking an investigation into whether Zacharia "repeatedly held herself out to the public as entitled to practice law without a licence to do so, conduct California law treats as a crime."
Zacharia, 42, graduated from Pepperdine University’s law school in 2011 but did not pass California’s bar exam, according to The Wall Street Journal. She told The New York Times that the university president had advised her she could call herself a lawyer, but not an attorney. A law degree alone does not authorise someone to practice law in the US.
A person with direct knowledge of the matter told the outlet that Zacharia took the exam around the time she was planning her wedding and preparing to move to China with her future husband.
In China, only Chinese citizens can obtain licenses to practice law, while foreign employees may work at law firms in other roles.

title: TTAP says  there will be no talks  until meeting with Imran  health update
description: Demands release of K P CM Sohail Afridi  Speaker Babar Swati  Junaid Akbar and all arrested PTI lawmakers and leaders
content:
Demands release of Sohail Afridi, Speaker Babar Swati, Junaid Akbar and all arrested PTI lawmakers and leaders
The Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Aain Pakistan (TTAP) on Thursday announced it would suspend all negotiations with the government until Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan was allowed to meet his family and his doctors were granted access to him, declaring that “there will be no talks” until his health information was provided.
The announcement came a day after the National Assembly and Senate endorsed the imposition of an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), deepening the political standoff between the government and opposition despite recent attempts to reach an understanding through dialogue.
“Until a meeting with Imran is arranged and information about his health is provided, there will be no talks with the government,” the alliance said in a statement shared on X after a meeting chaired by its chairman, Mahmood Khan Achakzai. It added that all authority to negotiate with the government would rest exclusively with Achakzai.
اعلامیہ تحریکِ تحفظِ آئینِ پاکستان تحریکِ تحفظِ آئینِ پاکستان کا ایک سربراہی اجلاس برخانہ محمود خان اچکزئی چیئرمین تحریک تحفظ آئین پاکستان منعقد ہوا، اجلاس میں علامہ راجہ ناصر عباس قائدِ حزبِ اختلاف سینیٹ؛ سردار اختر جان مینگل سربراہ بلوچستان نیشنل پارٹی؛ بیرسٹر گوہر خان قائم… pic.twitter.com/Jg2eWKTlal
The alliance also demanded the release of Imran’s sisters and access to him for his doctors, as well as the immediate release of non-functional K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, provincial Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, PTI provincial president Junaid Akbar and all arrested members of the national and provincial assemblies and party leaders.
The statement strongly condemned the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in K-P, describing the measures as “an attack on the Constitution and the public mandate”. It demanded that the decisions be withdrawn immediately, adding that the alliance’s constituent parties would challenge them in the Peshawar High Court.
The National Assembly and Senate on Wednesday approved the emergency proclamation for K-P by majority vote, following the federal government’s decision to impose the measure alongside governor’s rule on October 11. The government has defended the move on security grounds, citing the province’s deteriorating law and order situation and the need for greater coordination in counterterrorism efforts.
The alliance also called for the release of human rights lawyer Imaan Mazari, her husband Hadi Chatha, Dr Mahrang Baloch and all political prisoners associated with the Baloch Yakjehti Committee.
Read: Bilawal offers to approach PM for ending K-P emergency if PTI agrees to political dialogue
It reiterated its opposition to all forms of terrorism, including violence against civilians by the state, attacks by state institutions against political parties and sectarian violence. The alliance expressed support for the National Action Plan but called for the immediate implementation of a joint resolution passed by a peace jirga in the K-P Assembly, rather than the adoption of new policies.
On Balochistan, TTAP blamed the worsening security situation on what it called an unrepresentative provincial government and failed federal policies. It called for the province’s problems to be resolved through dialogue with its people rather than the use of force.
The statement also expressed concern over the situation in Azad Jammu and Kashmir, alleging that an “artificial system” had been imposed on its people and condemning what it said was the deprivation of internet access and basic necessities for five months.
The alliance said restrictions on judicial independence and the media had prompted it to approach international human rights organisations and the United Nations to highlight what it described as human rights violations and breaches of the Constitution in Pakistan.
A day earlier, Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari renewed call for dialogue in the National Assembly.
“Even today, I invite you to come and hold talks with the government and political parties and create conditions in which there will be no need for this emergency in K-P,” Bilawal told the House. He said he would personally ask the prime minister to end the emergency if such conditions were created.
Bilawal also stressed the need for political cooperation to address terrorism, saying an emergency alone could not provide a lasting solution to the province’s security challenges.

title: Ad  la speaks out after her fan removes Rachel Chinouriri s album promo posters in London
description: Ad  la addressed the incident in an Instagram post  urging fans to respect other artists and their promotional efforts
content:
Adéla addressed the incident in an Instagram post, urging fans to respect other artists and their promotional efforts
Adéla has defended British singer-songwriter Rachel Chinouriri after a fan filmed themselves removing promotional posters for her upcoming album, I Think I Spoke Too Soon , in London.
The incident gained attention after a video shared by a since-deleted or suspended X account showed the fan tearing down Chinouriri’s posters to reveal advertising for Adéla’s single “Ain’t in LA”.
The album is scheduled for release on October 16, 2026.
Returning from a brief social media break, Adéla addressed the incident in an Instagram post, urging fans to respect other artists and their promotional efforts.
“Came across this way too late but u guys this is so f**king *ss,” she wrote. “Please don’t do this. Don’t take ppl’s posters down. Promotion costs money, Rachel’s posters cost money, they deserve to be up and seen.”
Adéla also highlighted the challenges faced by Black women in the music industry, adding that it is “alr hard enough to make sure ur art gets out there & is heard… ESPECIALLY as a Black woman.”
ADÉLA reacts to her fans taking down Rachel Chinouriri posters next to her “Baddest B*tches are in London’ promo: “Rachel’s posters cost money, they deserve to be up and seen. It’s alr hard enough to make sure ur art gets out there & is heard…ESPECIALLY as a black woman.” pic.twitter.com/7eFvlY7XlG
Chinouriri had also responded to the video on X, explaining the financial and personal investment behind her album campaign.
“Hey so this isn’t okay,” she wrote, describing the removal of her posters as hurtful after years of work building her career.
Hey so this isn’t okay. It’s tough enough for black artists in pop to get exposure but ripping down a poster I paid a lot of money and put 10 years of hard work convincing people I’m good enough for this marketing…is just quite mean and makes me pretty sad right now :( …… https://t.co/xF4Iqs5Jhw
In a further response shared on her private TikTok account, Chinouriri clarified that fans were entitled to dislike her music but criticised the decision to destroy promotional material she had paid for.
The incident has prompted discussion about fan behaviour, respect between artists and the difficulties independent musicians face when promoting their work.
Both singers have highlighted the importance of allowing artists’ campaigns to reach audiences without interference.

title: Ben Barnes and Aubrey Cleland confirm marriage in heartfelt wedding announcement
description: The couple shared their wedding announcement alongside photos and a message about appreciating their partner
content:
The couple shared their wedding announcement alongside photos and a message about appreciating their partner
Actor Ben Barnes and singer and actress Aubrey Cleland have confirmed their marriage, announcing the news in a joint Instagram post on Wednesday, October 14, 2026.
The couple shared their wedding announcement alongside photos and a heartfelt message about finding a partner who understands and appreciates them. The post began with the words, “We got married!”
Barnes, known for his role in The Institute , reflected on the significance of finding a lasting connection in a world of billions of people.
“In a world of 8 billion people, it is extraordinary to find someone who feels like your person, someone who matches your sense of humour, curiosity and humanity,” he wrote.
The actor also expressed his admiration for his new wife, describing himself as a “proud husband” and praising her qualities.
“I married a woman of such rare grace, kindness and beauty, who somehow makes the world feel both bigger and more like home, who finds wonder, joy and laughter in things that might have passed me by, and who makes the ordinary feel momentous,” he added.
The couple concluded their announcement by writing, “We are so happy and so excited for everything to come,” signing the message “Ben & Aubrey”.
Their post was tagged at Chateau de Lis, a wedding venue in Oregon City, and credited photographer Naba Zabih.
The announcement followed a report from Page Six earlier in the week that the pair had married in Oregon.
Barnes and Cleland were previously spotted together during a London date night in July 2025.
Cleland also appeared as Barnes’ love interest in the music video for his song “Nevermind”, released in December 2024.
Cleland competed on American Idol in 2013 and later pursued acting, appearing in The Pitt and The Sex Lives of College Girls .

title: Jimmy Carter dies at 73  What is the Nashville reporter s cause of death and estimated net worth
description: His reporting brought viewers interviews with celebrated musicians  actors and other entertainment figures
content:
His reporting brought viewers interviews with celebrated musicians, actors and other entertainment figures
Jimmy Carter, a longtime entertainment reporter for WSMV 4 in Nashville, Tennessee, has died at the age of 73, according to family announcements shared on social media.
His death marks the loss of a familiar television journalist known for interviewing prominent figures in music and film.
Carter reportedly died in his sleep, as confirmed by his family.
However, the cause of death has not been disclosed, and no further details about the circumstances have been released. He is survived by three daughters, five grandchildren and two great-grandchildren.
Carter spent much of his professional career covering entertainment for WSMV 4, an NBC affiliate serving Nashville, a city internationally recognised for its country music industry.
His reporting brought viewers interviews with celebrated musicians, actors and other entertainment figures.
Among the country music stars he interviewed were Dolly Parton, Alan Jackson and Garth Brooks. His film industry interviews included Clint Eastwood, Sylvester Stallone and Kevin Costner.
Through his work, Carter became a recognisable presence on local television, covering entertainment events and prominent personalities visiting or living in Tennessee.
Questions have also emerged about Jimmy Carter’s net worth following news of his death. No official financial records or confirmed estimate of his wealth have been made public.
Online reports suggest his net worth could have ranged from $500,000 to $1.5 million, based on estimated salaries for experienced local television journalists and a career spanning several decades.
However, this figure remains speculative and has not been independently verified.
Carter’s longstanding contribution to Nashville’s entertainment coverage remains a defining part of his professional legacy.

title: South Africa name squad for second Australia Test
description: Breetzke replaces Tristan Stubbs
content:
South Africa have named Matthew Breetzke in their 17-man squad for the second Test against Australia, with Kagiso Rabada in contention to return as the hosts seek to level the series.
Breetzke replaces Tristan Stubbs, opening the possibility of South Africa fielding an additional specialist batter when the match begins on October 18 in Gqeberha.
Ryan Rickelton will take over wicketkeeping duties, while left-handed batter Tony de Zorzi was not considered for selection as he continues his recovery from a left hamstring injury.
Rabada missed the opening Test as he recovered from a hamstring injury but is nearing a return to action.
South Africa lost the first Test by 214 runs in Durban and will look to bounce back in the second match, with the third Test scheduled for Cape Town from October 27 to 31.
Squad: Temba Bavuma (c), Marques Ackerman, David Bedingham, Matthew Breetzke, Corbin Bosch, Gerald Coetzee, Simon Harmer, Marco Jansen, Keshav Maharaj, Aiden Markram, Wiaan Mulder, Senuran Muthusamy, Anrich Nortje, Dane Paterson, Kagiso Rabada, Ryan Rickelton, and Kyle Verreynne.

title: Messi s Inter Miami clinch MLS playoff berth
description: First half strikes from De Paul and Berterame seal a 2 0 win over New York City
content:
First-half strikes from De Paul and Berterame seal a 2-0 win over New York City
Lionel Messi set up a Rodrigo De Paul goal and German Berterame snapped his scoring drought as Inter Miami booked their place in the MLS playoffs with a 2-0 win over New York City FC on Wednesday.
Victory gave Cristian 'Kily' Gonzalez his first back-to-back wins since taking over as head coach last month, guaranteeing second-placed Miami at least a place in the wild card round, with five games left to play.
"I'm leaving happy. Obviously, there's a lot to improve, but we're making progress little by little," Gonzalez said. Messi -- who had scored twice on Saturday after returning to his club side from last week's emotional Argentina send-off -- was again a dangerous presence, playing a hand in both first-half goals. In the 20th minute Messi trapped the ball just outside the penalty area and passed it to De Paul, who found Suarez on the byline with a diagonal looping ball.
Suarez rolled it flat across the face of the goal, giving Berterame a simple finish for his first goal since May. De Paul grabbed Miami's second on a quick counter with the final kick of the first half. Berterame brought the ball across the halfway line and was slightly fortunate to find Messi to his right with a mishit pass. Messi drew in three defenders then laid it off with the outside of his left foot to De Paul, who slammed it high to the keeper's right. In a goalless second half, Messi sent a curling effort from just outside the box over the bar. As the game clock hit 90, Messi played a short corner to De Paul, who unleashed a shot from outside the box toward the far top corner. United States national team goalkeeper Matt Freese made a superb diving save, tipping the ball onto the post. New York City, on a dire streak of just one win in their last 11 MLS games, at least had a chance for a consolation deep in stoppage time with a penalty. Ian Fray brought down fellow substitute Talles Magno, who turned sharply away from goal and ran into the defender's trailing leg. But Dayne St. Clair made a brilliant save, flinging himself low and right to palm the ball around the bar. It was Inter Miami's second straight clean sheet, after none in their previous 10. "I really liked how we handled dropping back into defensive shape. We didn't get caught out on the counter and were very aggressive, breaking up plays whenever a sudden transition from them looked likely," said Gonzalez. "Perhaps our ball circulation was a bit too slow at times, but that's just how the game played out."
Even with first-place Nashville out of sight this year in the Eastern Conference, the win consolidated Miami's grip on second, and home-field advantage into the playoffs.

title: Israeli forces shoot  arrest Palestinian man sought since 2017 in West Bank raid
description: Separately  Israeli prison guards shoot Palestinian prisoners with rubber bullets  leaving them severely injured
content:
Separately, Israeli prison guards shoot Palestinian prisoners with rubber bullets, leaving them severely injured
Israeli forces shot and arrested a Palestinian man they had been pursuing since 2017 during a raid in the northern occupied West Bank on Wednesday, a local prisoners' rights official told Anadolu.
Samer Bani Odeh, a man in his 40s, was shot in the hand when Israeli special forces raided his home and those of his brothers in the town of Tammun, southeast of Tubas, said Kamal Bani Odeh, head of the Palestinian Prisoners Club in Tubas.
Earlier Wednesday, Israeli forces detained one of Samer Bani Odeh's brothers in an attempt to pressure him to surrender, releasing him several hours later, the official said.
Bani Odeh previously spent two years in Israeli prisons during the Second Intifada, according to the official.
His family has faced repeated Israeli raids and arrests over the years, including the detention of his wife, son and brothers, he added.
Separately, the Palestinian Red Crescent Society said a 21-year-old Palestinian was hospitalised after being beaten by Israeli forces at the Al-Murabba checkpoint west of Nablus.
Read: Palestinian woman killed, 2 injured in Israeli airstrike in Gaza despite ceasefire
The man, from the nearby village of Tell, had been detained since 7 am before being released hours later, the society said.
Around 9,350 Palestinians, including 350 children and 90 women, are held in Israeli prisons, where human rights groups have reported widespread torture, starvation and medical neglect, contributing to dozens of deaths in custody.
Israeli prison guards shoot Palestinian prisoners with rubber bullets, leaving them severely injured
Israeli prison guards shot Palestinian prisoners with rubber bullets, leaving one requiring the surgical removal of a testicle and another undergoing surgery for a fractured shin, Israel’s Haaretz daily reported Wednesday, citing medical records and testimonies.
The newspaper said Physicians for Human Rights Israel and the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel had documented 21 shooting incidents across five Israeli prisons since October 2023.
Most occurred in late 2025 and the first half of 2026, often at close range and without any preceding unrest, according to the testimonies. The rights groups said the ammunition appeared to consist of rubber or plastic projectiles.
The most severe case involved a prisoner shot in the testicle at Ketziot Prison in southern Israel in June. Medical records from Soroka Hospital showed the organ had been destroyed, requiring its surgical removal.
In testimony to his lawyer, the prisoner said guards had kicked him in the testicles during a strip search a week earlier, leaving him in severe pain. He said he was allowed to see a doctor only two days later.
A week after the beating, members of the Israeli Prison Service’s Masada unit fired rubber bullets into his cell, striking him in the previously injured testicle and behind his right knee, according to his account.
He said guards dragged him about 50 meters while he was bleeding heavily before he eventually received medical attention and was transferred to a hospital.
In another case documented in July, a prisoner at Ketziot underwent surgery for a fractured left shin after being struck by a rubber bullet, according to prison medical records.
A former inmate also told Haaretz he was shot at close range in April and denied adequate medical care for 15 days. He underwent surgery only after his release.

The rights groups said shootings had occurred inside cells, in prison yards and even in areas where inmates waited to meet lawyers.
Ultra-Orthodox Jewish protesters storm building housing Israeli army training program
Dozens of ultra-Orthodox Jewish protesters opposed to military conscription stormed a building housing an Israeli army training program in Bnei Brak, east of Tel Aviv, on Wednesday, Israeli media reported.
Some demonstrators managed to enter the building but apparently did not reach soldiers inside, according to the Israeli news website Ynet.
The building houses Kodkod, a program that trains ultra-Orthodox Jews for software development and cybersecurity roles in the military.
Footage aired by Israeli media showed protesters clashing with police, who said two demonstrators were arrested.
It was the third attempt to storm the building in a week, according to the Israel Hayom newspaper.
Opposition Yisrael Beiteinu party leader Avigdor Lieberman condemned the protesters, describing anyone attempting to storm an army base as a “terrorist” and calling for their arrest and imprisonment.
Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and ultra-Orthodox Shas party leader Aryeh Deri of encouraging draft evasion at the expense of those serving in the military.
Bennett also pledged to redirect 30 billion shekels ($9.68 billion) in state funding from draft evaders to those performing military service following the Oct. 27 elections.
Ultra-Orthodox Jews make up around 14% of Israel’s population of more than 10 million. Many oppose military service in favor of religious study, despite a June 2024 Supreme Court ruling requiring their conscription.
