title: Britain pledges   17m for repairs to Chernobyl nuclear plant damaged by Russia
description: Funding will form part of an international program coordinated by European Bank for Reconstruction and Development
content:
Funding will form part of an international program coordinated by European Bank for Reconstruction and Development
Britain will provide £17 million ($22.4 million) in funding for critical repairs to the Chernobyl nuclear power plant in Ukraine, whose protective shelter and ventilation system were damaged by a Russian drone strike last year, the British government said Thursday.
The funding will form part of an international program coordinated by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) in cooperation with the Ukrainian government and Group of Seven (G7) donors aimed at restoring the facility's nuclear safety functions.
The repairs are intended to restore the protective structure's confinement and ventilation functions and preserve its expected lifespan. Without the work, corrosion could undermine decades of international investment and increase long-term environmental and safety risks, the British government said.
Read: Russian drone hit nuclear-fuel storage facility near Chernobyl, Ukraine says
Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey said Britain's commitment to Ukraine remained firm as Russia's full-scale invasion continued.
“We are curtailing the war chest funding [Russian President Vladimir] Putin so desperately wants and backing the reconstruction of Ukraine, which has suffered at the hands of his barbaric attacks,” Healey said.
Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said Britain would continue working with its allies to strengthen Ukraine's security and increase the cost of Russia's aggression.
“Our message to Putin is clear – we stand shoulder to shoulder with Ukraine and will do so until they prevail,” Miliband said, adding that London was working towards a just and lasting peace.

title: Eight US states sue OpenAI  claiming ChatGPT harms young users
description: Eight US states sue OpenAI  claiming ChatGPT harms young users
content:
​Lawsuits accuse company of violating state consumer protection laws by misleading users about ‌⁠safety of ChatGPT
A bipartisan group of eight states said a day earlier they had ​sued OpenAI in courts across the country over harms they ‌say ChatGPT has caused to their residents, alleging the chatbot has coached its users — including teenagers — to harm themselves or others.
Attorneys general from the states, which include Iowa, ​Kansas and Arizona, filed the lawsuits independently in state courts, claiming ​ChatGPT is designed to be agreeable and engaging to earn ⁠the trust of users. But the chatbot reinforces delusions, encourages dangerous ​behaviour, and assists users in planning violence like mass shootings, the lawsuits ​claim.
Also Read: AI leaders warn UN of security risks as systems grow more powerful
The lawsuits represent the most significant coordinated state action against an artificial intelligence company, adding to a wave of legal challenges OpenAI faces as it prepares for a ​public listing. Florida's attorney general filed the first such state suit in June.
The ​lawsuits accuse the company of violating state consumer protection laws by misleading users about ‌the ⁠safety of ChatGPT. The states also allege that the company created a public nuisance by endangering the health of their residents.
The lawsuits seek orders forcing OpenAI to make changes to how ChatGPT works. Among other things, ​the states want ​the company barred ⁠from developing AI models that can improve themselves unless it can ensure those models are aligned with human ​values.

title: Five terrorists killed in Balochistan s Washuk IBO  ISPR
description: ISPR says cache of weapons  ammunition  explosives was also recovered during the operation
content:
ISPR says cache of weapons, ammunition, explosives was also recovered during the operation
Security forces killed five terrorists belonging to the Indian proxy, Fitna al-Hindustan, during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in the Washuk district of Balochistan, the military’s media wing said on Thursday.
The federal government last year officially designated all terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as Fitna al-Hindustan , accusing India of sponsoring a proxy war through the outfits.
According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the operation was conducted on the night of October 12-13 following reports of the presence of terrorists belonging to what the military described as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan .
“During the conduct of the operation, a terrorist hideout was busted by security forces through swift and decisive action,” ISPR said, adding that five Indian-sponsored terrorists were neutralised.
A cache of weapons, ammunition and explosives was also recovered during the operation, the statement added.
ISPR said sanitisation operations were being conducted to eliminate any other Indian-sponsored terrorists found in the area.
"Relentless counter-terrorism campaign under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision, as approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan, would continue at full pace to wipe out menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country” the statement concluded.
Read: 49 terrorists killed in Balochistan, K-P IBOs
A day earlier , security forces also killed five terrorists and injured four others during an IBO against Fitna al-Hindustan in the same district of Balochistan. During the operation, advanced weapons and ammunition were recovered.
Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terrorist activity over the past three months, with a series of attacks across the country resulting in the martyrdom of security personnel and civilians.
Last week, 12 people were killed and 35 others injured when a blast struck a joint checkpoint near Aman Mela in the Darazinda area of Dera Ismail Khan, with the TTP claiming responsibility for the attack.
On September 19, 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred in a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, the Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
In a separate incident, a captain and a lieutenant were among six security personnel martyred in an exchange of fire in Hangu district, while eight terrorists were killed.
On September 1, six personnel, including two officers, and a customs department official were martyred as security forces thwarted an attempt to breach the Customs House in Balochistan.
In July, at least 30 people , including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. The attackers also abducted several civilians and police personnel after the assault.

title: PSG outgun Manchester City in Champions League thriller
description: Enrique s side moves top of the table with a 4 2 win in Manchester
content:
Enrique's side moves top of the table with a 4-2 win in Manchester
Paris Saint-Germain further soured the mood at the Etihad Stadium as Manchester City's first home game since the guilty verdict on widespread flouting of Premier League financial rules ended in a 4-2 Champions League defeat on Wednesday.
The European champions turned on the style to strike three times inside the opening 35 minutes through Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha.
But City stormed back in the second half as Erling Haaland scored twice either side of Maghnes Akliouche's strike that briefly restored PSG's three-goal cushion.
"When you see a game at this level, two teams trying to play football, that was the kind of game we thought it would be," said PSG boss Luis Enrique.
"They created a huge amount of problems for us today. The team that lost today were perhaps a bit unlucky."
The 10-time English champions face swingeing sanctions unless they can successfully appeal the ruling of an independent commission last month, which found the club guilty on over 100 charges of financial impropriety.
City shrugged off the uncertainty over their future to win 3-0 at Liverpool on Sunday and remain top of the Premier League, but PSG showed why they are the favourites to win this competition for a third consecutive season.
"It has been a bit of a strange game because we conceded two goals in two minutes," said City coach Enzo Maresca.
"Second half we did enough to deserve something more."
Former City manager Pep Guardiola returned to the Etihad for the first time since his departure in May, sat behind the club's embattled chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano in a show of solidarity.
City made passing reference to the guilty verdict with a lengthy pre-match video detailing the club's historic moments of celebration both before and after an Abu Dhabi-backed takeover in 2008 that transformed their fortunes.
Behind one end supporters unravelled a giant banner reading: "I'm City till I die."
Yet the fighting talk in the stands was not matched on the field as City were blown away by a scintillating first 45 minutes from the visitors.
Gianluigi Donnarumma had a point to prove after the Italian goalkeeper was let go by Luis Enrique just months after helping deliver the club's first Champions League title in 2025.
However, it turned out to be a night to forget for the giant Italian.
Donnarumma was caught out at his near post by Doue's effort from outside the box after a lightning counter-attack to open the scoring.
The move for the second goal two minutes later was even more impressive as Doue and Dembele exchanged an elaborate one-two before the latter headed in at the far post.
Achraf Hakimi hit the post before Vitinha rattled in PSG's third from the edge of the box.
Maresca responded with a triple substitution at half-time and managed to salvage some pride, even if the deficit proved too much to overturn.
Antoine Semenyo and Enzo Fernandez missed glaring chances to pull a goal back even before Haaland glanced home a header from Iliman Ndiaye's cross.
Yet, City were hit by a sucker punch when Donnarumma got a hand to Akliouche's effort but the ball looped high into the air and spun back into the net.
Nuno Mendes made a brilliant clearance off his own line and Haaland hit the bar before the Norwegian slotted home his second of the night.
Donnarumma saved a late Ferran Torres penalty to deny the French champions a fifth goal.
But in the battle between two state-backed projects that have reshaped European football, Qatar-owned PSG are the top dogs right now as City face up to a scandal that leaves their litany of trophies over the past 15 years open to question.
PSG go top of the Champions League table after two games with City three points behind in 17th.

description: Saudi led coalition intercepts cruise missile over Madinah region
content:
Saudi-led coalition intercepts cruise missile over Madinah region
Yemen's Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in ‌the southern city ⁠of Aden ​on Thursday, killing ​two security ‌guards, two government officials told Reuters .
Yemen's ​prime minister and cabinet members who were at the Maashiq ⁠presidential palace complex were unharmed, Information Minister Moammar ‌al-Eryani said, adding that the Houthis had fired five missiles at the complex.

The ⁠Houthi-run Saba News ⁠Agency , citing a ​military ‌official, said the group had targeted a military operations headquarters run by Saudi officers at the complex, as well as weapons depots. Reuters could not ⁠independently verify the claims.
The Iran-aligned group's military ⁠spokesperson, Yahya Saree, said the strike on what he described as a Saudi military operations headquarters in Aden was part of the group's declared policy of "targeting Saudi military ⁠build-ups wherever they are."

Three witnesses had ​earlier told Reuters they heard loud booms in the vicinity of the palace.
Saudi-led coalition intercepts cruise missile over Madinah region
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said on Thursday that it intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile over the Madinah region in western Saudi Arabia.
Coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki announced the interception in a brief statement on X.

The statement did not identify who launched the missile or its intended target, and provided no details on possible casualties or damage. It came amid intensified Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes targeting airports and energy facilities.
The coalition accused the Houthis of carrying out a drone attack on the Taibah electricity distribution station in Madinah on September 29.
The attack knocked a transformer out of service but did not disrupt the electricity grid, according to al-Maliki. The facility supplies electricity to the Prophet's Mosque, one of Islam's holiest sites.
Yemen's Houthis said they did not carry out any attack on the Medina region Thursday, shortly after Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted a missile targeting the area of the holy city.

Yemeni army says it repelled Houthi attack on strategic Jabal Han in Taiz
The Yemeni army said on Thursday that its forces repelled an attack by the Houthi group on the strategic Jabal Han mountain west of Taiz city in southwestern Yemen.
In a statement, Colonel Abdul Basit al-Bahr, deputy head of the Moral Guidance Department at the army’s Taiz Military Axis, said army forces thwarted the Houthi attack on Jabal Han, west of Taiz, “after hours of the fiercest clashes and most intense fighting.”
He added that the attack was repelled after the Houthis had “set fire to (…) Jabal Han, the entire western front and residential neighbourhoods with shells and heavy artillery.”
Bahr did not provide details of casualties or material losses.
Separately, Al-Jumhuriya Channel reported that airstrikes destroyed communications network towers belonging to the Houthis in the Bani Bakkari area of Jabal Habashi district in Taiz governorate.
The Houthi group had no immediate comment on the report.
Jabal Han is considered one of the area’s most important strategic positions, overlooking Al-Dhabab road, the only vital route linking Taiz with Lahj governorate and, farther south, the interim capital Aden.
The Houthis have closed most roads leading to government-controlled areas in Taiz governorate, according to Yemeni human rights and humanitarian organisations.
These organisations accuse the group of besieging Taiz city since 2015 and preventing aid convoys from reaching residents and people affected by the war. The Houthis deny the allegations.
Saudi-led coalition intercepts and destroys drone in eastern Saudi Arabia
The Saudi-led coalition said early on Thursday that it intercepted and destroyed a drone over Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province.
Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki announced the interception without providing further details, including the drone’s origin.
Hours earlier, Yemen’s Houthi group claimed to have struck King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh with a ballistic missile, without providing details of casualties or damage.

Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition supporting Yemen’s government against the Houthis since 2015. The group has controlled the capital Sanaa and several provinces since 2014.
Yemen’s Houthis claim missile hit Saudi fighter jet over northern Yemen
Yemen's Houthi group claimed late on Wednesday that it had struck a Saudi fighter jet with a surface-to-air missile over the northern Yemeni province of Saada.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the missile directly hit the aircraft, putting it at risk of crashing. Saree claimed the aircraft was a Saudi Typhoon fighter jet that had taken off from an airbase in Taif, western Saudi Arabia.
Saudi authorities did not immediately comment on the claim. Earlier Wednesday, the Houthis also claimed to have targeted King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh with a ballistic missile.

title: Real Madrid comeback stuns Roma
description: Rudiger s late strike seals a 4 3 win as Mourinho enjoys happy reunion
content:
Rudiger's late strike seals a 4-3 win as Mourinho enjoys happy reunion
Jose Mourinho enjoyed a Roma reunion to remember as Real Madrid completed an astonishing comeback by scoring three late goals to claim a 4-3 away win in the Champions League on Wednesday.
Marten de Roon gave the hosts a deserved opener before Kylian Mbappe struck back on his 100th Champions League appearance to level the scores at the break.
Two Donyell Malen strikes in the space of six minutes early in the second half seemed to take the game away from the 15-time European champions as Roma ran rampant.
But Real scored three goals in the final six minutes, all stemming from corners, to turn the game on its head as Carlos Espi, Endrick and ex-Roma defender Antonio Rudiger struck at a stunned Stadio Olimpico.
Mourinho was a popular figure as he led Roma to the UEFA Conference League title and Europa League final during two-and-a-half years in charge.
The Portuguese was honoured with banners and chants by the home crowd in Roma's first home Champions League match in more than seven years, and the hosts started strongly as Mario Hermoso forced Thibaut Courtois into a flying fingertip save.
Roma took a deserved lead when De Roon swept a shot past Courtois from 25 yards in the 20th minute, and almost doubled it when Malen's powerful shot squirmed under Courtois before being plucked off the line.
However, one costly moment of switching off proved enough to send them back to square one within five minutes of the opener being scored.
Hermoso misjudged an interception to allow Mbappe a clear run at goal and the France striker's deflected shot flew into the roof of the net to level the scores with Real's first meaningful chance of the game.
Mbappe marked his Champions League centurion status, something he is the youngest player to achieve aged 27, with his 72nd tournament goal – one that moved him into the all-time top five ahead of Real legend Raul Gonzalez.
The equaliser appeared to subdue Roma and steady Mourinho's men, who twice threatened a second before the break as Marc Cucurella and Jude Bellingham came close.
But Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini insisted pre-match that Roma would not compromise on their full-throttle style regardless of opposition, and he was true to his word as they came out firing after the break.
Roma quickly re-took the lead when half-time substitute Rodrigo Mora fed the ball to Malen, who finished brilliantly by taking the ball in his stride with his first touch and lifting it over Courtois with his second.
Things got even better for the Italians just six minutes later when Malen raced onto a through ball to power home his second, given following a VAR review after initially being flagged for offside.
Real looked for a response as Mbappe twice tested Pierluigi Gollini, before having his second goal of the night ruled out for offside.
But set-pieces proved to be the key to unlock the Roma defence, as Espi tucked home a close-range rebound from a header to pull one back before Endrick powered home a header from another corner just two minutes later.
The final blow was struck by Rudiger in the 90th minute, the defender getting in front of his marker to guide home a close-range finish and complete an extraordinary turnaround.
The result leaves Real Madrid with six points from their opening two league phase matches, while Roma are on one point.

title: Aaron Paul pays tribute to  Breaking Bad  co star RJ Mitte after his death
description: Aaron Paul has remembered RJ Mitte  sharing tribute to his  Breaking Bad  co star following his death at 34
content:
Aaron Paul has remembered RJ Mitte, sharing tribute to his 'Breaking Bad' co-star following his death at 34
Aaron Paul has paid tribute to his Breaking Bad co-star RJ Mitte following the actor’s death at the age of 34, remembering their final meeting and praising his kindness and strength.
Mitte, best known for playing Walter White Jr in the Emmy-winning series, died on Monday in Brownsville, Texas. A representative confirmed that his cause of death was suicide.
Paul, who portrayed Jesse Pinkman in the series, shared a tribute on social media, describing Mitte as “an inspiration for so many”.
“I am so sorry you were hurting my friend. I wish we knew,” Paul wrote. “You constantly had a smile on your face and you took every single challenge that was given to you with such confidence and grace.”
The actor recalled meeting Mitte when he was “a little boy” and watching him “grow into a beautiful young man” who took on “every challenge head on”.
“The last time we saw each other I kept calling you Superman. You reminded me of him. You reminded me of him because you always led with kindness and strength. It was blinding. You were born into a world with challenges but you never let any of that stand in your way,” Paul wrote.
Mitte was diagnosed with mild cerebral palsy at the age of three. His character, Walter White Jr, shared the condition, although it was portrayed more prominently on screen.
He appeared throughout Breaking Bad’s run from 2008 to 2013. In 2013, Mitte received the SAG-AFTRA Harold Russell Award, named in honour of the first actor with a disability to win an Oscar.
Addressing readers who might be struggling, Paul encouraged them to seek support and connect with others.
“Hold each other up. That’s what this life is all about. Connect with someone you care about and say I love you,” he wrote.
He concluded his tribute, “RJ, I love you my friend. I’m so sorry.”

title: Parliament s joint session endorses K P emergency  governor s rule amid opposition uproar
description: Session is summoned after both houses of parliament approve President Zardari   s proclamation of emergency in K P
content:
Procedural motion passes with 214 votes in favour and 56 against amid opposition protests
A joint session of Parliament on Thursday adopted two separate resolutions ratifying the presidential proclamations imposing a state of emergency and governor's rule for two months in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) amid opposition uproar.
Through the first resolution, the joint sitting approved the proclamation of emergency issued by President Asif Ali Zardari under the second proviso to Article 232(1) of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan. The approval was granted in accordance with Article 232(7) of the Constitution.
In a separate resolution, the parliament approved the proclamation issued by the president under Article 234(1) of the Constitution, in accordance with Article 234(3).
The adoption of the two resolutions formalised Parliament’s approval of the presidential proclamations concerning the province of K-P under the relevant constitutional provisions.
The House adopted the following Resolutions moved by the Minister for Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. Tariq Fazal Chaudhary, during the Joint sitting of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament). 1. “That the Joint Sitting approves under clause (7) of Article 232 of the Constitution of the… pic.twitter.com/xe9xC4XBfN
During the session, opposition members tore up copies of the resolution to register their dissent.
After the proceedings concluded, the joint sitting of Parliament was adjourned indefinitely.
It is worth noting that the Parliament can endorse emergency and governor's rule for two months at a time, and for an extension, another joint session of the Parliament would have to be called. Furthermore, the extraordinary governance protocol can be extended for a maximum period of six months as per the Constitution.
Article 234, clause 3 of the Constitution, reads, "A Proclamation issued under this Article shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months, unless before the expiration of that period it has been approved by resolution of the joint sitting and may by like resolution be extended for a further period not exceeding two months at a time; but no such Proclamation shall in any case remain in force for more than six months."
A day earlier, both houses of parliament approved an emergency in K-P by majority vote under Clause 1 of Article 232 of the Constitution, despite opposition lawmakers' objections. First, the National Assembly (NA), then the Senate, debated the matter, with opposition lawmakers strongly opposing the Centre's decision and raising a hue and cry during the proceedings. However, the resolution was passed by a majority vote.
The Centre imposed emergency and governor's rule in K-P on October 11, suspending the PTI-led provincial administration amid a dispute over the province's security situation and counter-terrorism measures. The government has defended the move, citing a deterioration in law and order and an alleged failure by the provincial administration to coordinate counter-terrorism efforts with federal authorities.
Today's session was chaired by NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq. Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry initially presented the presidential proclamations concerning the imposition of emergency measures and governor's rule in the province.
The emergency proclamation was laid before the joint sitting under Article 232(7) of the Constitution, while the proclamation imposing governor's rule was presented under Article 234(3).
Opposition lawmakers protested during the proceedings, with several members wearing black armbands.
Chaudhry later moved a motion under Rule 232 of the Parliament (Joint Sitting) Rules, 1973, seeking to suspend certain sub-rules. Opposition members opposed the motion, prompting Speaker Sadiq to put it to a vote by asking lawmakers to stand.
The procedural motion was adopted by 214 votes to 56.
Following its approval, Chaudhry moved two separate resolutions before the joint sitting — one seeking ratification of the presidential proclamation of emergency under Article 232 of the Constitution and the other seeking approval of the proclamation imposing governor's rule under Article 234.
Subsequently, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar initiated debate on the two resolutions. He defended the imposition of emergency in K-P as a “last resort”, telling a joint session of parliament that the decision followed a worsening security situation and deliberations by the federal cabinet. Urging lawmakers to approve the proclamations under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, Tarar said the government was prepared to answer questions about the grounds for the move and rejected comparisons with martial law. “This option was exercised as a last resort,” he said.
Tarar told the joint sitting that the K-P governor had written a detailed letter to the president and prime minister about conditions in the province, warning that the conflict involving terrorism was intensifying. He said the government had presented figures and other material to explain why it had invoked the constitutional provisions.
According to the minister, the prime minister placed the matter before the federal cabinet after examining the material, allowing for collective consideration of the decision. He said the cabinet debated the matter for two and a half hours before recommending that the prime minister advise the president to exercise his powers under Articles 232 and 234 and impose an emergency in view of the seriousness of the situation.
Tarar also criticised the provincial leadership’s priorities, referring to deaths in incidents in Tank and Bajaur. He said families were receiving condolences while injured people were undergoing treatment in hospitals, including assessments over whether their limbs needed to be amputated. “In my view, the chief minister and provincial ministers should be there, rather than at rallies where music is being played and there is an atmosphere of celebration,” he said.
The minister said discussions in the apex committee, of which he was a member, had revealed that the counter terrorism department lacked a fully developed institutional structure and adequate resources. He said the overall security situation, the provincial government’s conduct and the material examined by the federal government had informed the cabinet’s deliberations.
Responding to lawmakers who had likened the emergency to martial law or a repeat of October 12, Tarar argued that the measure had been taken through procedures provided for in the Constitution. “The affairs of the state must be governed by the Constitution of Pakistan,” he said. “Whatever is provided for in the Constitution must be carried out in the manner it mandates.”
Law minister said he, the interior minister and the information minister, had explained the reasons for the decision during a media interaction on October 11 , following the issuance of the proclamation. The government had subsequently presented its explanation in both houses of parliament, he added.
Outlining the parliamentary process, he said the Senate and NA had separately debated and approved the emergency proclamation issued by the president on October 11 under Article 232. He said that the separate consideration by the two houses as an additional safeguard introduced through the 18th Amendment, saying it required both chambers to examine the proclamation within 10 days and decide on its approval through resolutions.
Tarar said consideration by a joint sitting was a further constitutional requirement. He added that a proclamation would cease to remain in force if the joint sitting passed a resolution disapproving it by a majority of its total membership. Turning to Article 234, the minister said it provided a mechanism concerning the exercise of a province’s administrative and legislative powers, with the president acting upon his satisfaction that the provision needed to be invoked.
He said a proclamation under that article also had to be placed before a joint sitting of parliament. The two proclamations before lawmakers formed part of the same document, he added. Tarar said the president had summoned the joint session to fulfil these constitutional requirements, following detailed discussions in the National Assembly and Senate.
Tarar described the 1973 Constitution as a consensus document, framed after extensive debate and careful consideration of the country’s political circumstances, and said it was held in high regard by the Pakistani people and democratic forces. The minister welcomed questions from lawmakers about the reasons and material underpinning the emergency, saying the government was available to respond to members on both sides of the aisle.
Read more: Govt defends K-P emergency, alleges PTI-KP govt’s ‘nexus’ with terrorists
He also said a final effort at negotiations had been made, but declined to discuss the competing political accounts, saying he was addressing the legal aspects of the decision. “I am speaking only from a legal point of view,” he said.
Thanking the NA speaker and Senate chairman for allowing detailed debate, Tarar urged lawmakers to examine the proclamations and give reasons for their decision. “The Constitution of Pakistan gives you the authority to decide on this,” he said.
Achakzai blamed country's internal shortcomings, past policies
Leader of the Opposition in the NA, Mahmood Khan Achakzai, addressing the joint session of Parliament, questioned how terrorists continued to enter Pakistan despite the construction of a 20-foot-high wall along the Afghanistan border, while blaming the country's internal shortcomings and past policies for the prevailing security situation.
“I say this with God as my witness that the circumstances in which our country has become trapped are the result of our own internal shortcomings,” he said. Achakzai recalled that the Constitution had been framed with great difficulty following the breakup of Pakistan, which he attributed to personal egos.
“Pakistan was also divided because of our egos,” he said. Criticising the imposition of governor's rule in K-P, Achakzai said those in power were also bound by constitutional rules and regulations.
Achakzai also alleged that institutions had mistreated eight members, questioning the conduct of those responsible. Achakzai stressed that political negotiations should be based on parliamentary supremacy and the rights of provinces over their resources.
He said the opposition was prepared for unconditional negotiations within the framework of the Constitution. Achakzai also called for the formation of an alliance of political parties that believed in democracy. He alleged that a plan had been devised to seize the resources of the provinces and warned that the people would resist any such move.
Achakzai called for the rights of Seraiki, Sindhi, Pashtun and Baloch communities over their resources to be recognised. Turning to terrorism, Achakzai said he would quit politics if terrorism was not eliminated. “If terrorism is not eliminated, I will leave politics,” he said.
He also called for an end to the reliance on weapons and the use of force, warning that public anger could lead to a strong reaction. Achakzai also alleged that the opposition's chief minister and members of the provincial assembly had been abducted.
“You are kidnappers. You are terrorists,” he said. Referring to restrictions on meetings with the PTI founder Imran Khan, Achakzai questioned the legal basis for preventing access to him. Achakzai also referred to the treatment of the political leader, alleging that those now leading the government had previously forced their own leader to leave Attock Fort.
“For God's sake, have mercy on this country,” he added. Achakzai said the opposition would have supported the government if the circumstances had justified such support. He further alleged that police had detained one of his associates at Karachi Company on the 26th, stripped him, and recorded a video with a girl to send to his wife.
Referring to the February 8 elections, Achakzai challenged government lawmakers to swear that they had genuinely won their seats.
He questioned the legitimacy of the election results and asked lawmakers to swear by their family members that they had won the elections.
Gohar urges government to withdraw terrorism allegations against PTI
PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, addressing the joint session of parliament, rejected allegations that his party was supporting terrorism, saying PTI condemned terrorism in all its forms.
Gohar said the government had accused PTI of supporting terrorists, an allegation he categorically rejected. “Decide whether we are supporting terrorists or not,” he said, adding that the prime minister had deeply hurt the party through such statements.
He condemned the allegations and warned that they could have repercussions at the international level. “The Pakistan Army is ours. We live and die in Pakistan,” he said, accusing the government of putting the federation at stake.
Gohar reiterated that PTI condemned all forms of terrorism and accused the government of removing an entire provincial government out of fear of a single meeting. “If we are supporting terrorism, then hang us,” he said, questioning whether the government considered PTI members part of the country.
He warned that future generations would force the government to apologise for its allegations, maintaining that PTI could be accused of many things but could never support terrorism. He urged the government to withdraw the allegations as soon as possible.
The PTI chairman also rejected the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in K-P, as well as the decision to call in the army. “We reject your emergency, governor’s rule and the calling in of the army,” he said, adding that PTI would work towards building a Pakistan in which those responsible would be held accountable.

title: Raza hopes Zimbabwe can shine on home stage at 2027 World Cup
description: The tournament will mark Africa   s return as a Cricket World Cup host after 24 years
content:
The tournament will mark Africa’s return as a Cricket World Cup host after 24 years
Zimbabwe all-rounder Sikandar Raza says the 2027 Cricket World Cup will offer his country a chance to showcase its hospitality and natural beauty as he prepares for a potentially special tournament late in his career.
The 40-year-old hopes the event, co-hosted by Zimbabwe, South Africa and Namibia, will leave visiting supporters with lasting memories when it begins on October 2, 2027.
“From a collective point of view, I do think the world really needs to see what Africa has to offer: the beauty, the crowd, the vibe and everything that we have to offer in Zimbabwe, especially,” Raza said at the launch of a mobile cricket game.
“The world deserves to see it. For people who will find time to travel to Zimbabwe to watch the World Cup, it will be an unforgettable experience.”
The tournament will mark Africa’s return as a Cricket World Cup host after 24 years and offers Raza a chance to play on home soil at a major international event as he approaches the latter stages of his career.
“Every cricketer dreams of having retired or to retire after a World Cup,” he said.
“The fact that I am coming to the end of my career as well, so to have an opportunity to play a home World Cup is certainly a blessing for me from a personal point of view.”
Zimbabwe will play league matches in Harare, Bulawayo and Victoria Falls, where the newly built Mosi-oa-Tunya International Cricket Stadium is expected to provide a distinctive setting for the tournament.
Raza said the experience for travelling fans would extend beyond the cricket, particularly in Victoria Falls, one of the country’s best-known tourist attractions.
“What we expect from Victoria Falls, as much as cricket is important, but I think outside cricket, beautiful sightings, a peaceful sleep because you can hear the falls, a lovely sunset, and some great human beings and a hospitable environment for everyone,” he said.
Despite the prospect of strong home support, Raza was cautious about how much advantage Zimbabwe could gain from familiar surroundings at an International Cricket Council tournament.
The all-rounder also welcomed the proposed Super Seven format, saying it would reward teams that perform consistently.
“I quite like the Super Seven idea. I think the teams that play well deserve to have more games at the World Cup,” he said.
Raza praised Zimbabwe Cricket for arranging additional fixtures outside its Future Tours Programme to give the national team more opportunities to prepare for major competitions.
“When it comes to Zimbabwe and the fixtures, if you look at our FTP, our board has done really well to find fixtures from here and there outside our FTP programme as well,” he said.
“Zimbabwe Cricket has gone up and beyond for their players to play more games to be ready for whichever fixture.”
Zimbabwe hosted Australia in September and have further preparations ahead, including a tri-series involving Bangladesh and Afghanistan, followed by a three-match one-day international series in India in January 2027.
Zimbabwe have been drawn in Group A alongside Afghanistan, Pakistan, Australia, India and a team emerging from Qualifier A. They are scheduled to open their campaign against the qualifying side on October 9.

title: 911 call reveals response after Hayden Panettiere was found unresponsive
description: Newly obtained 911 audio details effort to revive Hayden Panettiere after she was found unresponsive in August
content:
Newly obtained 911 audio details effort to revive Hayden Panettiere after she was found unresponsive in August
Newly obtained 911 audio has revealed the emergency response after actress Hayden Panettiere was found unresponsive in an apartment in Greenville, South Carolina, on August 16.
ABC News obtained the seven-minute recording through a Freedom of Information Act request to Greenville County EMS.
In the call, a person reporting the incident can be heard asking for help as the operator provides instructions for cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR).
"Oh, god, oh, my god -- you do like CPR or something?" the caller said.
The caller explained that they had entered an apartment shared by their brother and his girlfriend after returning from church. They said the woman was unconscious.
"We need to start CPR. I'm going to tell you how to do CPR, OK? We're going to start with ventilation first. I need you to lay her flat on her back and remove anything from under her head," the operator instructed.
The recording captures the operator counting chest compressions as the caller attempts to provide assistance.
According to officials, first responders "initiated advanced cardiac life support measures" after Panettiere was found unresponsive. She was pronounced dead at approximately 2.32 pm.
The audio corresponds to the date and address of the incident, although South Carolina law restricts the release of information through public records requests that identifies individuals by name.
ABC News said the details in the recording align with publicly released information about Panettiere's death.
The Greenville County Coroner's Office ruled her death an accidental overdose involving drugs, including fentanyl.
The Greenville City Police Department is investigating, and the Drug Enforcement Administration has also joined the investigation, according to sources familiar with the case.
A police report obtained by ABC News states that Panettiere's former boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, was at the scene.
Officers also spoke with Hickerson and his brother, Zach, while emergency medical personnel were treating Panettiere. Zach described her as his brother's girlfriend.

title: South Africa look to bounce back in Gqeberha
description: Coach Shukri Conrad hints at changes after the Proteas suffered a 214 run defeat to Australia in Durban
content:
Coach Shukri Conrad hints at changes after the Proteas suffered a 214-run defeat to Australia in Durban
South Africa coach Shukri Conrad has called for greater composure from his batters while resisting knee-jerk changes ahead of the second Test after a heavy opening defeat.
South Africa were thrashed by 214 runs by Australia in the first World Test Championship match in Durban, with Conrad insisting his side must improve without abandoning the approach that brought them success.
“We obviously need to look at how can we improve the side without being knee-jerk in our reactions,” Conrad said ahead of the second Test, which begins on October 18 in Gqeberha.
The hosts made early inroads after electing to bowl but were unable to contain Australia, who recovered from 230-8 to post 390 in their first innings, thanks largely to Matt Renshaw’s superb 190.
South Africa’s batters then struggled to convert promising starts, none reaching 50 as the hosts conceded a 106-run first-innings deficit.
Australia capitalised with another commanding batting display before Josh Hazlewood’s six-wicket haul sealed an emphatic victory.
While Conrad acknowledged Australia’s outstanding fielding and disciplined bowling, he said his own side needed to avoid costly mistakes at crucial moments.
“We need to show composure,” he said. “But the question is always, ‘will it make the boat go faster if we make changes, or will it slow the boat down?’, and we are constantly looking at how we make the boat go faster.”
South Africa will draw on their resilience during their World Test Championship final triumph at Lord’s in June 2025, when they recovered from a first-innings deficit of 74 runs to defeat Australia.
Conrad said the opening defeat should not prompt his team to question the foundations of its success, although he acknowledged that changes remained possible.
“It doesn’t mean you now have to go soul-searching or questioning all the things we have done really well and are doing really well. We just need to get bloody better,” he said.
“We have guys in our squad who deserve a crack. So safe to say that might be an option.”
Fast bowler Kagiso Rabada could be among those considered as he works towards returning from a right hamstring injury sustained during South Africa’s winter training programme.
“Hopefully, Rabada’s Rolls Royce will be purring down the highway again,” Conrad said.
South Africa also missed Rabada and Lungi Ngidi in the opening Test, leaving the hosts looking for ways to strengthen their attack ahead of the next encounter.
Conrad said the batting performance required particular attention, identifying mental errors as a major factor behind the dismissals.
“Dismissals in the batting sit in one of three categories. It’s either technical, tactical or mental,” he said.
“And if we’re brutally honest, a lot of our dismissals sat in the mental. Is that an easier fix than technical and tactical? Probably not.”
He added that facing one of the world’s strongest bowling attacks on a good batting surface had exposed his team’s shortcomings.
“Every time we felt we were just getting ourselves out of the woods, we would let them back in,” Conrad said.
South Africa will look to level the series in Gqeberha before the third and final Test in Cape Town.

title: Nashville reporter Jimmy Carter dies at 73 after decades interviewing music and film stars
description: Nashville entertainment reporter Jimmy Carter  known for interviewing Dolly Parton and Clint Eastwood  died aged 73
content:
Nashville entertainment reporter Jimmy Carter, known for interviewing Dolly Parton and Clint Eastwood, died aged 73
Jimmy Carter, the Nashville entertainment reporter known for interviewing country music stars and Hollywood actors, has died aged 73.
His family confirmed his death, with his granddaughter Kira Sparks saying he passed away in his sleep on Tuesday, October 13.
In a statement shared after his death, Sparks wrote, “We received the news today that my grandfather, Jimmy Carter, passed in his sleep.”
She also paid tribute to his family, adding, “He leaves behind three daughters who loved him deeply, five grandchildren, and two great-grandchildren.”
A medical cause of death had not been publicly announced in reports published on Wednesday, and funeral arrangements had yet to be confirmed.
Carter grew up in Montgomery, Alabama, and developed an interest in radio at a young age before building a career in Nashville.
He became a familiar presence at award ceremonies, red-carpet events and gatherings around Music Row, interviewing performers and actors throughout his career.
He spent a total of 21 years working at WSMV Channel 4. His first stint lasted six years during the 1980s, before he returned to the station for another 15 years between 2003 and 2018.
Beyond television, Carter also contributed to WSM Radio and the nationally syndicated country entertainment programme Crook & Chase.
His interview subjects included Dolly Parton, Alan Jackson, Garth Brooks, Clint Eastwood, Sylvester Stallone and Kevin Costner.
According to WSMV, Carter received several professional honours during his career, including duPont-Columbia and Edward R. Murrow awards.
Following news of his death, WSM Radio paid tribute to the broadcaster and its former colleague.
“Today, we lost a dear friend and a cherished member of the WSM family,” the station said.
It also remembered Carter as a trusted source and gifted broadcaster who built lasting connections with artists, listeners and colleagues.
His career spanned local television, radio and nationally syndicated entertainment programming, establishing him as a recognisable figure in Nashville’s music and entertainment industry.

title: Oil prices retreat as investors weigh supply outlook  Middle East tensions
description: Brent crude futures fall  1 64  or 1 6   to  104 42 a barrel
content:
Brent crude futures fall $1.64, or 1.6%, to $104.42 a barrel
Oil prices fell more than 1% on Thursday ​as investors weighed risks to supply from attacks on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz against US ‌efforts to cut petroleum shipping costs by easing sanctions on vessels.
Brent crude futures fell $1.64, or 1.6%, to $104.42 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down 98 cents, or 1%, to $94.11, reversing gains from the previous session.
WTI rose to a three-week high in the prior ​session after the Houthis attacked Saudi Aramco's headquarters and Iran said it was deploying new tactics to target ships ​in the Strait of Hormuz and keep oil prices high.
A container ship and a dry bulk ⁠carrier both sank near the strait in the past 24 hours after being hit by projectiles in separate incidents, maritime officials said ​on Wednesday.
Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it is stepping up strikes in ​response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month.
With the Iran war having disrupted shipping and driven up freight costs to record highs, the Trump administration is considering easing sanctions on so-called shadow-fleet vessels that have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, ​Iran and Venezuela to help ease prices, a US official said on Wednesday.
Read: Govt seeks 15-year Saudi oil facility
The new talks centre on the United States potentially ​allowing "legal oil" to flow on previously sanctioned vessels, the US official said.
Increased output from Russia and the Middle East has kept a lid on ‌prices. Russia's ⁠crude oil production rose by 65,000 barrels per day in September to 8.43 million bpd but remained down 870,000 bpd year over year, the International Energy Agency said on Wednesday.
The IEA also said crude oil exports from Middle East Gulf producers rose by 4.4 million bpd in September to around 75% of prewar levels.
"While there is little concrete evidence of a near-term peace deal, oil ​continues to find its way to ​buyers through alternative routes ⁠and logistical arrangements," said Phillip Nova's head of market insights, Priyanka Sachdeva, in a client note.
"These workarounds have helped prevent a more severe supply shock, although they come at a higher cost and ​leave global flows vulnerable to further disruption."
In the US, crude oil and distillate inventories fell, ​while gasoline stocks ⁠rose last week, market sources said on Wednesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.
Crude stocks fell by 11.1 million barrels in the week ended October 9, sources said. That was a much bigger draw than analysts polled by Reuters expected.
"Despite the sharp inventory draw, oil prices ⁠barely reacted. ​The failure to rise on bullish news suggests investors are cautious about chasing ​prices higher at current levels," said Haitong Futures in a note on Thursday.
Official numbers from the US Energy Information Administration are due at 12pm, delayed by a day following the Columbus Day holiday on Monday.

title: At least 30 children  teacher killed as school roof collapses in Peshawar
description: PM Shehbaz takes  serious notice  of the situation  CCPO Peshawar says school owner has been taken into custody
content:
PM Shehbaz takes 'serious notice' of the situation, CCPO Peshawar says school owner has been taken into custody
At least 30 children and a female teacher were killed when the roof of a private school collapsed in Peshawar on Thursday, while more than 50 others were injured, hospital authorities confirmed.
Lady Reading Hospital (LRH) spokesperson Muhammad Asim had initially said that 33 bodies were brought to the hospital, which included 32 children and one teacher, while Deputy Medical Superintendent Dr Ibrahim of Naseerullah Babar Memorial Hospital said that the bodies of two children were also brought to the hospital.
Asim said an emergency was declared at LRH, with senior hospital officials present in the trauma ward to oversee the treatment of the injured, some of whom were in critical condition.
According to an earlier list issued by the LRH, a total of 53 patients were brought to the hospital, including 36 men and 12 women. Of these, 17 were discharged after observation, while 33 died. All children were aged 14 or younger.
According to an updated verified list from LRH, a total of 61 patients were brought to the hospital, of which 30 were discharged after observation while 31 casualties were recorded.
Speaking to the media, Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Peshawar, Dr Mian Saeed, said that the school owner had been taken into custody and a case would be registered over the incident.
He said the school’s roof had been poorly constructed and that the building was located in narrow streets, which had made rescue operations difficult, adding that a total of 110 children were enrolled at the school.
CCPO Saeed further told media that the three-storey building was located in the densely populated Dir Colony, where narrow streets were creating difficulties for rescue operations. He said the building fell within the jurisdiction of the relevant local police station and that 30 children had been present in classrooms on the upper floor when the roof collapsed.
He added that the building had several deficiencies and that the roof slab had been constructed using choka - thin, flat clay tiles or custom-tapered bricks.
CCPO Saeed said that the building was in a dangerous condition and posed a risk of further damage, adding that rescue teams were working to move people out immediately and appealed to people to cooperate with the rescue efforts.
Expressing concern over the possibility of further casualties, he said the building appeared to have been overloaded and questioned how much weight the roof slab could bear. He added that the authorities would examine which building regulations had been violated and conduct a proper inquiry into the incident to determine responsibility for the negligence.
In a further development, the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Department of Elementary and Secondary Education constituted a fact-finding committee to investigate the incident, which was directed to submit its report on an urgent basis.
According to an official notification issued by the department, K-P Private Schools Regulatory Authority (KPPSRA) Managing Director Javed Iqbal would serve as chairman of the committee. Elementary and Secondary Education Department, Deputy Secretary (Primary) Muhammad Farooq, was named a member, while the panel itself would nominate its third member.
The committee was tasked with conducting a thorough inquiry into the incident and would examine the causes of the roof collapse, assess any possible negligence, identify structural defects in the building’s construction, and evaluate other contributing factors. Officials also instructed the panel to recommend concrete measures aimed at preventing similar tragedies in the future and to submit appropriate recommendations.
Meanwhile, K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi visited the school affected by the incident and said a school audit had not been conducted due to negligence by the previous government.
"Strict action will be taken against the individual who issued the NOC for this school, and they will be made an example of, so that in the future, no one dares to toy with children's lives or disregard safety requirements. There will be no compromise on the safety of our children".
He underscored that anyone found responsible for negligence would be punished, adding that the investigation would be completed within four days.
“We will not limit ourselves to an inquiry; we are conducting a full investigation,” the governor underscored.
Kundi added that, in the past, such incidents had been followed only by "photo sessions" and announcements of "inquiry committees".
In a statement on his X account, he also stated that he had "directed that a structural safety audit of all government and private educational institutions in the province be conducted and a report submitted within one week".
"I have also instructed the Education Advisor to immediately review the PSRA Act and include a legal provision under which inspection teams can identify unsafe schools and have them shut down. Regrettably, this important safety provision was not included in the Act during the PTI government's tenure. Now, this legal gap will be addressed".

Later in the day, K-P Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed had also visited the school and inspected the site. Speaking to the media, he said he had ordered an investigation into the roof collapse, adding that terrorism charges could also be included in the case against the school owner.
He said the First Information Report would be registered by the state and an inquiry committee had been formed to investigate the incident.

He concluded that the school owner would be given an appropriate punishment.
Rescue 1122 said ambulances and disaster response vehicles were dispatched to the site, where rescue teams launched operations and shifted injured children to hospital. "The rescue operation was underway to search for more people trapped under the debris," Rescue 1122 added.
Following the incident, Pakistan Army personnel also reached the site and joined rescue and relief agencies in efforts to recover children and school staff feared trapped beneath the rubble and transport the injured to hospitals.
President Asif Ali Zardari expressed deep shock and sorrow over the deaths and injuries of children and teachers in a school accident in Peshawar. “This heartbreaking tragedy has left the entire nation in shock,” the president said, according to the statement issued by the President of Pakistan.
He expressed heartfelt condolences and sympathy to the families of those who lost their lives and the bereaved families. “May Allah Almighty grant the deceased a high place in Jannat-ul-Firdous and give the grieving families the courage and patience to bear this irreparable loss,” he said.

title: Villa put six past Fenerbahce in record rout
description: Emery   s side bounce back from a winless run of three home games in all competitions
content:
Emery’s side bounce back from a winless run of three home games in all competitions
Aston Villa recorded their biggest ever European victory as Nicolas Jackson inspired a 6-0 rout of Fenerbahce in the Champions League on Wednesday.
Unai Emery's side won at Villa Park for the first time this season to maintain their 100 percent start in Europe's elite club competition.
Swiss forward Johan Manzambi put Villa in front and Jackson was on target twice before the interval.
Ross Barkley's second-half double and Tammy Abraham's late strike put the seal on a welcome success on home turf for Villa.
Villa Park's North Stand is currently closed for building work as the club increases the stadium's capacity to over 50,000.
Amid suggestions that the reduced crowd and lack of noise was affecting Villa's players, Emery had said there were "no excuses" for failing to win any of their previous three home games.
Languishing in 16th place in the Premier League, Villa responded to Emery's demand for a more intense performance as they extended their unbeaten run to four games in all competitions.
"Overall it was a very good match. There are still things to improve. It was a strong result for us," Emery said.
"Keep going forward. It helps confidence for us. We did some changes to get other players confidence and minutes. What we did today was fantastic. The Champions League is very difficult."
Following a summer of upheaval featuring the sales of star players including Ollie Watkins and Ezri Konsa, the Europa League holders are finally emerging from a turbulent period.
Saluting Jackson's contribution, Emery added: "He has power to get in behind. He can drop and help as well.
"We need him always to be in the box when we're attacking. Jackson is our striker."
Villa captain John McGinn fired narrowly wide and Ibrahim Mbaye tested Ederson with a long-range blast in a frenetic opening.
Villa were rewarded for their early barrage in the 12th minute.
Matteo Guendouzi's wayward header fell to Manzambi, who took a touch before unloading a powerful shot that took a deflection off Milan Skriniar as it whistled past the wrong-footed Ederson.
Manzambi, 21, is the second player to score on his Champions League debut on his birthday.
Jackson's low strike was pushed away by Ederson, but the Senegal striker wasn't to be denied.
After Fenerbahce surrendered possession carelessly in the 31st minute, Boubacar Kamara's pass found Jackson on the edge of the area and he guided a fine finish past Ederson.
Jackson was proving unstoppable and the 25-year-old made it three after 39 minutes.
Taking aim from 18 yards, Jackson's low drive carried too much power for Ederson, who could only parry it into the net.
It was Jackson's fifth goal in eight games since arriving from Chelsea in August.
Villa also scored three times in the first half when they won at Club Brugge in their opening game of the Champions League group phase.
Playing his first match in England for four years following his troubled spell at Manchester United, Fenerbahce forward Mason Greenwood was booed mercilessly by Villa fans.
In between the taunts, they were able to celebrate two more goals in the second half.
Barkley slotted home from the penalty spot after Ismail Yuksek fouled Manzambi.
And Barkley struck again four minutes later, meeting Mbaye's cross with a shot that deflected in off Bartug Elmaz.
Abraham came off the bench to wrap up Villa's record win as he tapped in Alysson's cross in stoppage time.

title: GTA 6 delays linked to production challenges around vast number of smart NPCs
description: Rockstar reportedly delayed GTA 6 to address production challenges involving its large number of NPCs
content:
Rockstar reportedly delayed GTA 6 to address production challenges involving its large number of NPCs
Rockstar Games’ work on a large number of non-playable characters (NPCs) was reportedly one of the reasons behind delays to Grand Theft Auto 6, according to a Bloomberg report detailing the game’s development.
The highly anticipated title has been in development for more than eight years, with Rockstar expanding its workforce and investing in production to create what it aims to be its most ambitious game.
The company reportedly struggled to produce NPCs at the scale required, prompting it to open a new office and recruit developers specifically to work on the characters.
The report also describes difficulties during development, including a period when the team’s creative direction was unclear.
Phil Hooker, one of the game’s three development heads, said, “The pattern is very familiar. You go through a period where things don’t work, but you see snippets.”
By 2022, the project had begun to take shape after years of work. Rockstar also conducted research to help recreate Vice City, visiting Miami, exploring nightclubs, filming aerial footage and accompanying police officers to crime hotspots.
The game has been delayed twice, with the development team reportedly believing the additional time was necessary.
Jennifer Kolbe, Rockstar’s head of publishing, recalled approaching Take-Two Interactive chief executive Strauss Zelnick to request another delay shortly after the first.
“I think he said, ‘You’re kidding. Please tell me you’re kidding,’” Kolbe recalled. She said Zelnick understood the reasoning after they discussed the issues.
Zelnick has described allowing more development time as “a wise investment in time and financial resources” when it helps a game reach its potential.
Rockstar’s workforce also grew significantly during development, increasing from 2,441 employees during the Red Dead Redemption 2 era to 4,711, according to the report.
GTA 6 is now expected to release November 19.

title: FIFA to offer members  6 35 billion development fund windfall
description: The plan is due to be approved at its Council meeting on Thursday in Zurich
content:
The plan is due to be approved at its Council meeting on Thursday in Zurich
Football's world governing body FIFA is planning to set up a $6.35-billion development fund for the next four years, AFP learned Wednesday from a source close to the matter.
The plan is due to be approved at its Council meeting on Thursday in Zurich, where FIFA president Gianni Infantino and the 36 other members of the federation's executive will gather.
To finance this development fund for the 2026–2030 period, which would allow money to be distributed to FIFA's 211 federations as well as to the regional confederations, it would draw in part on its financial reserves after a commercially successful 2026 World Cup.
The plan, first revealed by the Associated Press, would allow for the payment of $25 million to each of its 211 member federations.
This is far more than the $10 million called for by two of Infantino's chief critics, Aleksander Ceferin, the boss of the European confederation UEFA, and Victor Montagliani, the head of CONCACAF, the confederation of North and Central America and the Caribbean.
Thursday's gathering is the first such meeting since April 28, and comes amid a crisis in the governance of world football, following Infantino's announcement this summer of his desire to open FIFA's premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors.
That plan was ultimately abandoned in the face of widespread criticism from the football world, with a rebellion led by UEFA, CONCACAF, and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC).
At the end of September, Infantino launched a consultation process with the federations to reform how the global body operates, announcing that the first proposals could be examined as early as Thursday's Council meeting.
The 56-year-old, who has headed FIFA since 2016, is running for re-election in March 2027.
His opponents have so far failed to agree on a candidate.
Ceferin has chosen to stand for a new term at the helm of UEFA and, according to several media outlets, Montagliani is expected to do the same at CONCACAF.
The deadline for submitting candidacies is November 18.

title: Medvedev beats Tsitsipas to reach Shanghai quarters
description: The Russian fifth seed wins 6 4  7 5 to set up a last eight clash with Tommy Paul
content:
The Russian fifth seed wins 6-4, 7-5 to set up a last-eight clash with Tommy Paul
Daniil Medvedev beat Stefanos Tsitsipas in straight sets to reach the quarter-finals of the Shanghai Masters on Wednesday, setting up a meeting with Tommy Paul.
Medvedev did not face a single break point in defeating the 28-year-old Greek 6-4, 7-5.
"I felt like I was playing very well today," said Medvedev, the fifth seed.
"I put a lot of pressure on him in the first set.
"Second set, different story. Very tight one. I'm happy that I managed... to get some good returns, get some good rhythm," the 30-year-old said.
The Russian broke his opponent's serve to go up 6-5 in the second set and closed things out in one hour and 24 minutes.
The players were meeting in the singles draw for the 16th time on Tour, with 6th-ranked Medvedev improving his head-to-head record to 11 wins.
Medvedev won the Shanghai tournament in 2019.
His next opponent Paul meanwhile beat Zizou Bergs 7-6 (7/5), 6-4.
"I know sometimes it's hard to back up a big win," Paul said of the 39th-ranked Belgian, who upset second-seeded Carlos Alcaraz in the previous round.
Though Paul said Bergs "raised his level" in the second set, narrowing a 0-4 deficit to trail by just one game, it was the American who triumphed in the end.
Rising Spanish star Rafael Jodar earlier beat Botic van de Zandschulp 6-7 (4/7), 6-4, 6-2 to secure his quarter-final spot.
It was not without incident, though, with Jodar handed a code violation in the second set for swearing at a ball boy in Spanish when asking for a towel.
Jodar will play Casper Ruud in the quarter-finals. The Norwegian advanced when fourth-seeded Felix Auger-Aliassime retired injured when down 2-5 in the first set.
Ruud, ranked 24th in the world, said his opponent's trouble appeared to start in the fourth game of the first set.
"It seemed to me that he maybe twisted his knee... it looked like he kind of stumbled a bit with a wrong step," Ruud told reporters.
"From that moment it seemed like he was in a lot of pain," he said.
Auger-Aliassime needed a medical timeout after the fifth game, starting the next game down 1-4 with white strapping around his left knee.

title: Shakhtar make winning start at new Champions League  home
description: The Ukrainian side rallies from behind to beat AEK Athens 3 1 at Chelsea   s Stamford Bridge
content:
The Ukrainian side rallies from behind to beat AEK Athens 3-1 at Chelsea’s Stamford Bridge
Nomadic Ukrainian champions Shakhtar Donetsk celebrated moving into their new Champions League "home" at Stamford Bridge by storming back to beat AEK Athens 3-1 on Wednesday.
Fans of the club turned up in their thousands to support the team, who emerged from the tunnel draped in blue-and-yellow national flags.
The Greek side took the lead in the 28th minute through Lovro Majer but Pedrinho levelled confidently from the penalty spot just six minutes later.
With about 10 minutes of normal time to go, Vinicius Tobias found the net from a tight angle and substitute Gleiker Mendoza made the game safe, smashing home after cutting in from the left.
The result leaves Shakhtar on four points after two games after a draw against PSV Eindhoven in their opening match in the league phase of the Champions League.
Shakhtar, from the east of Ukraine, are using Chelsea's ground as the base for their European fixtures this season, with the Londoners absent from continental competition.
On the eve of the match, the club's chief executive Sergei Palkin spoke of how playing at the home of the two-time European champions would keep the war-torn nation's struggles "visible".
Shakhtar were forced to leave their home ground, the Donbas Arena in Donetsk, after pro-Russia separatists seized control of the city in 2014.
Since then the team has lived an itinerant existence, playing home European matches elsewhere in Ukraine as well in Poland, Germany and Slovenia due to the security situation in their homeland.
London made sense as the next base for the team.
Since the beginning of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the UK has provided refuge to 265,000 Ukrainians, according to the Ukrainian embassy in London.
Fans from the ex-pat population turned out in force on Wednesday, swelling the crowd to 29,000 -- around 11,000 short of capacity.
"I think it's such a blessing to see my team play here," James Upson, a 20-year-old student, whose mother is from Ukraine and father from the UK, told AFP.
"Obviously, it's unfortunate we can't play in our country, but here it's just a beautiful sight for them to come out to the Champions League anthem in such a beautiful, beautiful stadium."
He said playing in London was a way to keep the Ukraine conflict in the public eye, on a day when Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky was in London for talks with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
"We have to keep ourselves relevant, and we do our best to do so," said Upson. "We played in Valencia as the national team recently. You know, we had good outreach there.
"But to have a local club come to the UK and play here in four matches is just such a wonderful sight."
Marta Palas, 17, said many of her classmates do even not realise the war in Ukraine is still going on.
"I'm about to graduate high school and people don't know about the war, at all," she said.
"They think it's not going on anymore, but it does. It's still on, and it does -- it did get harsher, honestly, from back in 2022. It is quite a hard situation right now."
Serzh Dadizha, 22, a Ukrainian student who studies in Britain, told AFP he wanted to help his team from the stands.
"I want to feel like I'm a 12th player, like I belong here, like I make an impact for my team, like I do something. Not just to watch the show."
Snoop, who goes by his nickname, travelled all the way London from his home in Finland to watch his adopted team.
"When I was a teenager and I saw what was happening in Donbas and Donetsk, I just felt like some kind of compassion for them," said the 26-year-old. "So yeah, it comes from deep in the heart."
Shakhtar, UEFA Cup winners in 2009 and Conference League semi-finalists last season, next host Sporting Lisbon, with Fenerbahce and Real Madrid to follow at their new temporary home.

title: West Indies level T20 series in India
description: Hope   s unbeaten 102 and Keemo Paul   s five wicket haul set up a 24 run victory over India
content:
Hope’s unbeaten 102 and Keemo Paul’s five-wicket haul set up a 24-run victory over India
Shai Hope led from the front with an unbeaten 102 to guide the West Indies to a series-levelling 24-run win over India in the fourth T20 international on Wednesday.
West Indies posted 247-3 in Hyderabad, powered by skipper Hope's blistering 50-ball knock and his unbroken 91-run stand with Sherfane Rutherford, who finished on 49 not out.
Keemo Paul then led the bowling charge with figures of 5-41 to bowl out India for 223 as West Indies bounced back to level the five-match series at 2-2, setting up a decider on Sunday in Bengaluru.
"I think all the guys, we back our skills and we feel we could beat any team on our day," said Paul. "So it's just about staying calm and believing in ourselves and I think we're doing that really well."
Hope struck his third T20 international hundred -- the most by any West Indian batter -- and his second of the series.
West Indies started briskly before they lost Jewel Andrew for 21, but Shimron Hetmyer, who hit 33 off 12 balls, gave Hope company in another quick partnership.
Pace bowler Prince Yadav had Hetmyer caught and bowled but West Indies were never short of power as Rovman Powell contributed 24 off 17 balls.
Hope kept up the onslaught in tandem with Rutherford and brought up his century with the final ball of the innings after hitting Nitish Kumar Reddy for successive sixes.
"We were unfortunate we couldn't execute our plans in bowling and that's where we fell a bit short," said India skipper Shreyas Iyer.
In reply, Sanju Samson got India off to a strong start with his 23-ball 56 but the West Indies bowlers struck regular blows to keep India in check.
Medium-pace bowler Paul struck twice in the fifth over to dismiss Samson and then Ishan Kishan in the space of four balls.
Iyer struggled for momentum before he fell to Shamar Springer for 16.
Left-arm spinner Gudakesh Motie also took wickets in one over, removing opener Abhishek Sharma for 29 before Naman Dhir was stumped for a first-ball duck.
With India needing around 14 per over to win the game, Tilak Varma, who hit 43, and Reddy (41) attempted to pull things back in their quickfire partnership worth 70.
Romario Shepherd had Varma caught and then Paul struck thrice in an over, including the wicket of Reddy, to claim his second five-wicket T20 haul and shut down India's chase.
Number 10 Arshdeep Singh retired hurt after getting hit on his shoulder by a Shamar Joseph bouncer and India's innings folded in 19.3 overs.

title: Clavicular accuser drops sexual assault claim from civil lawsuit as criminal case continues
description: Clavicular   s accuser dropped sexual assault claim from civil lawsuit while his Massachusetts criminal case continues
content:
Clavicular’s accuser dropped sexual assault claim from civil lawsuit while his Massachusetts criminal case continues
Aleksandra Vasilevna Mendoza, known online as Alorah Ziva, has removed a sexual assault claim from her civil lawsuit against streamer Clavicular, whose real name is Braden Peters, as his criminal case in Massachusetts continues.
Mendoza’s second amended complaint, filed in Florida on October 8, removes the sexual battery count while retaining five other claims against Peters.
Her attorney, Drew Moss, told NBC News that the decision was made to avoid interfering with the ongoing criminal proceedings.
“Ms. Mendoza does not want her civil case to interfere with that process,” Moss said.
Peters was charged in September with rape, drugging someone for sexual intercourse and procuring liquor for someone under 21.
The charges concern an alleged encounter in May 2025 at his family’s home on Cape Cod. Peters denies the criminal allegations.
Mendoza’s civil lawsuit continues to seek more than $50,000 in damages. The remaining claims are battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, fraudulent misrepresentation, fraudulent concealment, and unauthorised publication of her name and likeness.
The complaint also alleges that Peters administered cosmetic injections during a livestream in November 2025 without legally valid consent.
It includes screenshots of livestream comments warning that Mendoza was 17 at the time of the alleged incident and claims Peters knew her age.
Peters had requested a pause in the civil proceedings on September 29, arguing that responding to the lawsuit could risk self-incrimination in the criminal case.
His lawyers also argued that invoking his Fifth Amendment rights could negatively affect his civil defence.
A hearing on the request to pause the civil case is listed for October 28. Meanwhile, a separate hearing in the criminal proceedings is listed for October 22, after Peters’ scheduled October 14 arraignment was cancelled, according to NBC News.
