title: Pakistan  Iran to discuss regional peace efforts at OIC moot  IRNA
description: Potential deployment of the largest non nuclear bomb in the US arsenal would mark significant escalation in conflict
content:
Trump 'made and broke' promises, US 'must be penalised' for it: Ghalibaf
Pakistan and Iran were expected to hold new consultations on regional peace efforts at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation’s (OIC) Council of Foreign Ministers meeting in Baghdad this weekend, Iranian state news agency IRNA reported on Thursday.
According to IRNA , Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi was scheduled to travel to Iraq on Saturday for the 52nd session of the Islamic foreign ministers’ meeting, taking place on October 17–18, further adding that foreign ministers from Pakistan, Egypt and Turkiye were also expected to attend.
Iran, Pakistan to hold fresh consultations on regional peace efforts during an Islamic foreign ministers’ meeting in Baghdad this weekend, IRNA reports https://t.co/igMOwYiBR0
“Fresh consultations among key regional players— including Tehran and Islamabad— will take place on the sidelines of the Baghdad meeting,” IRNA reported.
Trump 'made and broke' promises, US 'must be penalised' for it: Ghalibaf
The US "must be penalised and made to alter its conduct," Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said in a statement carried by IRNA on Thursday, adding that this must happen so the US "understands that it has to accept the Iranian nation's rightful demands."
Speaker @mb_ghalibaf : Regarding the proposal presented, as we've said before, the US president made promises and then broke them. America must be penalized and made to alter its conduct, so it understands that it has to accept the Iranian nation's rightful demands. pic.twitter.com/vhNwTlbf0N
"Regarding the proposal presented...the US president made promises and then broke them."
Ghalibaf said separately that Iran must combine military action with negotiations to establish lasting deterrence and prevent its enemies from launching further attacks, stressing that agreements alone cannot guarantee the country’s security, according to IRNA on Thursday.
Speaking in an interview late on Wednesday, Ghalibaf questioned whether negotiations with the United States, even if they resulted in a signed agreement containing Washington’s commitments, would prevent future attacks on Iran.
Iran must fight and negotiate to establish lasting deterrence: Speaker @mb_ghalibaf https://t.co/TTg5xeorUk pic.twitter.com/3feYy2UMDn
Ghalibaf also rejected the notion that Iran should rely only on military confrontation and escalating tensions to exhaust its enemies.
US hostility toward Iran was deeply rooted, he said, saying that Washington’s pursuit of domination and its hegemonic mentality only fueled further ambitions rather than prompting it to back down, according to IRNA .
“The solution is to fight and negotiate at the same time to establish lasting deterrence,” Ghalibaf said, outlining the approach needed to protect Iran against future threats.
He said Iran must become sufficiently powerful to convince the United States, as well as regional and international actors, that they cannot achieve their objectives against the country.
“No one should dare to attack us. Anyone who entertains such a foolish idea should look at experience and understand that Iran is powerful and that no one can stand against us or challenge us,” he said.
The parliament speaker emphasised that such deterrence required not only building military strength but also demonstrating that strength convincingly to potential enemies.
“Whenever we achieve a military victory on the battlefield, we must also turn that victory into a political victory, consolidate it and turn it into a document of defeat for the enemy,” he added.
Strait of Hormuz remains closed, requires coordination for passage: Iran
Deputy chief of the Iranian Army for coordination, Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari, said on Thursday that the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed and that any passage through the waterway must be coordinated with Iranian forces, according to IRNA .
Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of a ceremony honouring army nurses, Sayyari said the situation was evident from oil flows and rising gasoline prices in the United States.
Iran: Strait of Hormuz remains closed, requires coordination for passage https://t.co/YO2Q3NaR2r pic.twitter.com/OkvHiLXckc
He said the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) Navy maintained a strong presence west of the Strait of Hormuz, while the Iranian Army operated east of it, extending northward into the Sea of Oman.
If any passage takes place, it must be coordinated; otherwise, people will see in the news what happens, Sayyari said.
Sayyari said the continued efforts by countries to secure gasoline and diesel supplies showed that the strait remained closed.
US military weighs use of ‘mother of all bombs’ in potential future strikes on Iran, CNN says
The US military has developed strike plans that could include using the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast Bomb, also known as the "mother of all bombs", against Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites if President Donald Trump orders renewed combat operations, CNN reported on Thursday citing US officials familiar with the matter.
The potential deployment of the largest non-nuclear bomb in the US arsenal would mark a significant escalation in the conflict, although officials familiar with military planning discussions told CNN that questions remain over its effectiveness in achieving Washington's strategic objectives.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
Trump says Iran war will end ‘very soon,’ predicts oil prices will plunge
US President Donald Trump said late Wednesday that the war with Iran would end “very soon,” predicting that oil prices would fall sharply once the conflict concludes.
"The Iran war will end very soon … Soon, as they want it to end,” Trump told reporters in Montana.
"They'll never have a nuclear weapon, and oil prices will drop like a rock.”
Earlier, addressing a rally in Montana, Trump expressed uncertainty over which Iranian officials the US was negotiating with as Washington sought to end the conflict.
Read: Iran says reviewing US proposals for talks as indirect messages continue
"They don’t have a navy. They don’t have an air force. Their army is decimated. Their leaders are gone.
"I should have probably left their leaders because I don’t know who the hell we’re negotiating with," he said.
The president also described Iran as having previously been a dominant military force in the Middle East, arguing that US military operations had significantly weakened its capabilities.
“Iran was the bully of the Middle East,” he said, adding that the country was no longer as powerful as it had been.
Trump claimed that US strikes had destroyed Iran’s naval fleet and rendered its military aircraft unusable.
He said Iran had 159 ships and asserted that none remained operational, while also claiming that its fighter jets had been destroyed on the country’s runways.
"You know, they were strong. Now they're not so strong ... I said 'we knocked it out,' but they had exactly 159 ships. How many ships are laying at the bottom of the sea? You know, 159. So they had 274 quite good, but not like ours, quite good jet fighters. How many jet fighters are available for use today? Zero! You know where they are? They're all scattered all over the beautiful runways of Iran. They're all scattered in little tiny pieces all over the runways," he added.
Two ships sink near Hormuz after being hit by projectiles amid surge in attacks
A ​container ship and a dry bulk carrier have both sunk near the Strait of Hormuz in the past ‌24 hours after being hit by projectiles in separate incidents, maritime officials said on Wednesday.
Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it is stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month.
The Singapore-flagged GFS Pride, ​a small container vessel with a capacity of 2,824 20-foot equivalent units (TEU), sank while sailing through the strait, according to ​maritime security sources.
"GFS PRIDE sustained damage and a fire on board, and has since sunk. All ⁠21 crew members were safely evacuated. No injuries have been reported," the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) said in a ​statement on Wednesday, adding that the vessel had been sailing through the strait on Tuesday.
In a separate incident, the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged ​Cape Dao sank close to the strait, weeks after being struck by a projectile on September 23, data from UN shipping agency the International Maritime Organisation showed on Wednesday.
Read more: Strait of Hormuz traffic plunges once again amid new wave of Houthi attacks
One crew member was killed, and the rest of the crew evacuated straight after the strike, maritime sources said.
Its UAE-based manager, Peonies Shipmanagement ​FZE, could not be immediately reached for comment.
The GFS Pride and Cape Dao are the second and third vessels to have ​sunk since the US-Iran war began on February 28, according to an analysis of IMO casualty data.
"MPA is deeply concerned about the continued attacks on ‌commercial shipping ⁠in the Strait of Hormuz," the Singapore authority said.
"Such attacks are unprovoked, unjustifiable, and a breach of international law."
GFS Pride's United Arab Emirates-based manager, GFS Ship Management FZE, could not be immediately reached for comment.
"The latest incidents reinforce the continuing threat to commercial shipping transiting the Strait of Hormuz," maritime risk management company MARISKS said on Wednesday.
"The threat is not confined to tankers, with container vessels ​and bulk carriers also sustaining ​serious damage."
A sharp ⁠escalation in threats to commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas trade passed before the war, has heightened concerns ​about security in the waterway.
Tehran has sought to tighten its grip on the waterway since ​US and Israeli ⁠strikes on Iran on February 28, restricting transit in an effort to gain leverage over Washington.
Iran is increasingly deploying new tactics against vessels transiting the strait as it seeks to keep oil prices elevated and influence US midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters .
While Iran and ⁠the US ​have focused their attacks on tankers, cargo and container vessels have also been ​attacked, immobilised or sunk.
The Maltese-flagged container ship Safeen Prestige was hit by a projectile in March and later sank north of the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards ​attacked and seized the container ship MSC Francesca in April.

title: Balochistan Assembly passes two key bills
description: Balochistan Assembly passes two key bills
content:
The Balochistan Assembly on Wednesday approved the Balochistan Water Resources Management Bill and the Balochistan Cadet Colleges (Amendment) Bill while disposing of a calling attention notice regarding the deteriorating law and order situation in Qila Abdullah district.
The House also referred two audit reports received from the Auditor General of Pakistan to the Public Accounts Committee.
The session began 25 minutes late under the chairmanship of Speaker Captain (retd) Abdul Khaliq Achakzai.
Awami National Party parliamentary leader Engineer Zmarak Khan Achakzai drew the attention of the provincial home minister to the worsening security situation in Qila Abdullah. He said the government must provide details of the steps taken so far to address the daily incidents of violence in the district.
Speaking on the notice, Achakzai stressed that it was the responsibility of the state and the government to resolve the people's basic problems. He recalled that opium cultivation once flourished in Qila Abdullah; due to the absence of serious action, the crop had now spread to other parts of the province. Three police officer posts and 200 constable posts remained vacant in the district, he noted, adding that the rigorous recruitment process for the police should have been matched by equally strict measures against narcotics.
Achakzai said the people of Qila Abdullah wanted peace and that restoring order there could bring stability to the entire Pashtun belt. He urged the government to rebuild public trust and take action without discrimination against anyone who took the law into their own hands.
Provincial Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langove informed the House that concrete steps had already been taken. Two new police stations had been established in the district and the strength of police personnel increased.

title: Cops martyred in Bajaur  Bannu attacks
description: Cops martyred in Bajaur  Bannu attacks
content:
Two officers killed and three injured in separate shootings
An officer of the Bajaur police was martyred and two others were injured when unidentified armed men opened fire in the Loi Sum area of Tehsil Khar on Wednesday.
Noorullah of the Bajaur police was on leave and heading home when the attackers opened fire on him, police said. DSP Saeedur Rehman confirmed the incident and said the injured had been shifted to Headquarters Hospital, Khar, for treatment. Police have launched an investigation and a search operation to arrest the perpetrators.
In a separate incident in Bannu, a head constable of the District Security Branch was martyred when unidentified armed men opened fire near Muslim Abad on Circular Road. The assailants fled after the attack.
According to police, the incident occurred within the limits of Cantonment police station. Head Constable Raqeebullah (No 1987), son of Badshah Zargul, resident of Sokari Zabta Khan, was targeted and succumbed to his injuries on the spot. A heavy contingent of police reached the scene and launched a search operation to arrest the suspects. The body was shifted to District Headquarters Hospital, Bannu, for post-mortem and other legal formalities.
Police said the suspects remain at large and the search operation and further investigation are underway.

Speaking at a ceremony held at the Governor's House, where allotment letters for residential plots were handed over to the heirs of 54 police martyrs, the Governor said the revised package was designed to recognise the sacrifices of the force and improve the living standards of serving officers and their families. He also introduced a special financial assistance package for families of serving police personnel whose parents, spouse, children or siblings lose their lives in terrorist incidents.
The Governor extended the net of welfare further by approving financial support for the families of police personnel who die from causes unrelated to terrorism, police encounters or law-and-order duties. A special marriage grant for the daughters of police martyrs was also sanctioned.

title: LHC finds ex judge s plea about pension not maintainable
description: LHC finds ex judge s plea about pension not maintainable
content:
Rules high court beyond Article 199 review
Dismissing a constitutional petition challenging the rejection of a request for pensionary benefits, the LHC has held that a high court, including its committees comprising judges, and decisions endorsed by the chief justice, cannot be subjected to judicial review under Article 199 of the Constitution.
Justice Asim Hafeez observed that Article 199(5) expressly excludes a high court from the entities amenable to the constitutional jurisdiction of judicial review. He held that the court, its judges' committees and the chief justice constituted an integrated institutional whole, and the constitutional jurisdiction could not be invoked against their collective decision.
The Lahore High Court judge observed that what was prohibited directly could not be achieved indirectly through proposed amendments to the petition.
Emphasising the need to preserve institutional collegiality and judicial comity, the court dismissed both the constitutional petition and an application seeking amendment.
The petitioner, Justice (retired) Zafar Iqbal Chaudhry, had sought pensionary benefits, but the request had been considered and disapproved by a committee comprising judges of the high court.
The recommendations were subsequently placed before the chief justice who declined the request. The decision was conveyed to the petitioner through a letter issued by the registrar on May 11, which was challenged before the court.
A law officer opposed the maintainability of the petition by relying on a Supreme Court judgment.
The petitioner's counsel argued that the judgment had subsequently been reviewed by the Supreme Court and, therefore, could no longer serve as a binding precedent.
However, Justice Hafeez observed that the review judgment had neither overturned nor disturbed the reasoning of the judgment. The Supreme Court had set aside the earlier decision to the extent of the review petitioner because of an apparent error concerning Rule 22 of the Peshawar High Court Ministerial Establishment (Appointment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 2020, which provided a specific right of appeal.
The judge noted that the Supreme Court had remanded that matter to the PHC chief justice for placement before judges nominated to decide the appeal in accordance with law. He held that the limited relief granted in the review proceedings did not alter the established legal position concerning the scope of Article 199(5).
Referring to legal principles discussed in a book, Justice Hafeez observed that the article defines which entities are amenable to judicial review, rather than merely operating as a conventional ouster of jurisdiction.
The court rejected the possibility of treating the judges who considered the petitioner's request, or the chief justice who endorsed the decision, as separate individuals outside the protection afforded to a high court under the constitutional provision.

title: ACE concedes jurisdictional limits
description: Says dispute over property inheritance and civil litigation did not warrant criminal proceedings
content:
Says dispute over property inheritance and civil litigation did not warrant criminal proceedings
The Anti-Corruption Establishment (ACE) has acknowledged before the Lahore High Court (LHC) that a dispute over property inheritance and civil litigation did not warrant criminal proceedings by the department, recommending the quashing of an FIR registered over a decades-old dispute after finding no evidence against government officials.
Justice Sardar Ali Akbar Dogar disposed of a constitutional petition filed by Shahid Mahmood in light of a four-page report submitted by an ACE regional director, which described the matter as civil in nature and confirmed that litigation over it was pending before a civil court in Sheikhupura.
During the hearing, the petitioner's counsel, Mian Dawood advocate, argued that the department had registered an FIR over a 76-year-old inheritance dispute that had already been settled by the courts.
He contended that the petitioner's forefathers had won the case before the Supreme Court, but the opponents had initiated fresh proceedings before revenue authorities over a mutation. After losing before the revenue department, they had got an anti-corruption FIR registered, the lawyer alleged.
The counsel argued that the agencies had no authority to initiate criminal proceedings over inheritance, civil or revenue disputes in the absence of a legally sustainable criminal offence.
In its report submitted before the high court, the anti-corruption regional director stated that the matter was civil and that no evidence had been found against the officials concerned.
The department recommended that the FIR under challenge be quashed.
After considering the report, the LHC disposed of the petition.
The LHC acquitted a man sentenced to life imprisonment in a murder case, ruling that an unexplained three-day delay in registering the FIR, contradictions between the complainant's and eyewitnesses' statements, and lapses in preserving evidence had rendered the prosecution's case doubtful.
Justice Farooq Haider allowed the appeal filed by Sufian alias Jaga, set aside the trial court's judgment and ordered his release, according to the written decision.
The court observed that the prosecution had failed to provide a convincing explanation for the delay in registering the case. The incident had taken place on May 13, 2020, but the FIR had been registered at the Sialkot police station on May 16. A man injured in the incident, Rahman Ali, had died on May 19, 2020.
The judgment further noted contradictions between the statements of the complainant and the witnesses regarding the occurrence, raising doubts about the credibility of the prosecution's account.

title: PTI moves court against detention of party workers  | The Express Tribune
description:
PTI moves court against 
detention of party workers
content:
Maintains detention orders under MPO cannot be issued without cabinet approval
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) has challenged the detention orders issued under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance against its leaders and workers in Karachi before the Sindh High Court (SHC).
Insaf Lawyers Forum (ILF) Sindh President Advocate Faisal Mughal, General Secretary Barrister Ali Tahir and Advocate Shujaat Ali Khan have filed petitions challenging the arrests and detention of party leaders and workers.
Speaking to the media at the SHC, Barrister Ali Tahir said two orders issued by Sindh Additional Chief Secretary Iqbal Memon had been challenged. One order contained the names of 15 workers and the other 27, while the petitions collectively sought relief for 43 party workers.
He maintained that detention orders under the MPO could not be issued without the approval of the Sindh Cabinet, citing several SHC judgments on the matter. He said the court had reaffirmed this legal position in February as well. The lawyer argued that the statutory requirements for exercising powers under the MPO must be fulfilled and that detaining party workers merely on the basis of lists was unlawful.
Advocate Shujaat Ali Khan filed the constitutional petition, while Barrister Ali Tahir and ILF Sindh President Advocate Faisal Mughal are pursuing the matter before the court.
Barrister Ali Tahir expressed hope that the high court would review the detention orders and grant relief to the party workers. He alleged that the action had been taken primarily because of their affiliation with PTI, adding that no concrete evidence had been presented to establish their involvement in any criminal activity.
He said the notifications cited concerns over a possible deterioration in the law and order situation and referred to a request from the Sindh inspector general of police. However, he maintained that no substantial evidence had been brought to their attention to show that the detained workers were involved in arson, vandalism or violence. He added that the Constitution guaranteed citizens the right to peaceful protest and that all legal requirements must be met before anyone's liberty could be curtailed.
Barrister Ali Tahir argued that detention under the MPO should be ordered by the competent forum after examining the relevant material and completing the prescribed legal process, rather than being left to the discretion of an individual officer.

The two sides also discussed joint incubation programmes for emerging businesses and pilot projects to modernise industrial operations and traffic management in Karachi.
Agriculture featured prominently in the talks, with both sides exploring cooperation in hybrid rice, high-yield seeds, agricultural machinery and modern farming techniques.
Shah thanked China for providing training to 1,000 Pakistani agricultural graduates at Chinese universities, including Huazhong Agricultural University. He said Hubei's expertise in rice production and seed technology could help boost agricultural productivity and farmers' incomes in Sindh.
The two sides also discussed establishing a joint laboratory for modern and digital agriculture, promoting mechanised farming and improving cold-chain infrastructure to reduce post-harvest losses. Better storage and transportation systems, Shah said, could improve market access for the province's fruits, vegetables, meat, dairy and fisheries products.
The discussions also covered the next phase of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), with Shah welcoming Hubei's participation and calling for greater collaboration in agriculture, skills development and environmentally sustainable projects.

title: OpenAI employee arrested over alleged recording device
description: OpenAI employee arrested over alleged recording device
content:
A Saudi employee of OpenAI has been arrested in the United States for allegedly planting a recording device in the artificial intelligence company's San Francisco office, federal prosecutors and the firm said on Tuesday.
The US Justice Department said Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, an engineer who joined OpenAI in July 2025, was arrested on October 9. He allegedly wrapped a USB device in toilet paper and inserted it into a television in an executive conference room.
OpenAI's security team discovered the device late last month and referred the matter to the FBI. Prosecutors said Alfozan had also used a productivity tool to search for information about office buildings, meeting rooms, calendars and employees' locations.
A second device was reportedly found during a search of an unattended bag belonging to him. Investigators also cited queries about remote audio recording and memory-card encryption on a chatbot account linked to his spouse.
OpenAI said it had no indication that Alfozan had improperly accessed or extracted its AI model weights, source code or customer data. AFP

title: French student protests swell
description: French student protests swell
content:
Tens of thousands of people have rallied across France in support of protesting high school students demanding better conditions, intensifying pressure on President Emmanuel Macron's government amid growing opposition to its cost-cutting budget.
The interior ministry estimated that 161,500 people joined demonstrations nationwide, more than double the 71,500 recorded last Thursday. Unions put the turnout at 480,000. Most rallies were peaceful, but violence erupted at places.
During a Paris march, masked youths set cars alight, threw objects and attempted to erect barricades. Police fired tear gas in Paris and Lyon. Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg joined a demonstration in Saint-Denis, saying "our future is being robbed".
Students have been protesting since last month over teacher shortages, dilapidated school buildings and overcrowded schedules. AFP

title: Starlink curbs hit Ukraine s drone ops
description: Starlink curbs hit Ukraine s drone ops
content:
Ukraine said on Wednesday that Elon Musk's SpaceX had imposed restrictions on its satellite services, disrupting military drone operations as Russian strikes knocked out power for hundreds of thousands of people amid worsening tensions between Kyiv and Washington.
Ukrainian military officials said the restrictions affected military-grade Starlink terminals used in drones for attacks on Russian targets and for intercepting incoming Russian drones. The sudden limitations reportedly disrupted several missions, with Kyiv seeking clarification from SpaceX, the US government and NATO.
Presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov said SpaceX had imposed a speed limit of 160 kilometres per hour on its StarShield military and intelligence service. A Ukrainian defence ministry source told Reuters that some military units reported losing connections at speeds below half that threshold.
The development comes as US President Donald Trump has publicly criticised Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, calling for stopping attacks on Russian oil refineries, suggesting the Ukrainians should replace their wartime leader.
Zelenskiy warned that the decision could cost lives. "It's a big mistake ... this decision will bring a lot of human losses," he said. He said that it was painful that Trump appeared to be taking Russia's side, adding that a president seeking to mediate must remain neutral.
Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski, whose country pays for Ukraine's Starlink subscriptions, criticised Musk over the reported restrictions, questioning whether he was using his products for political purposes.
Meanwhile, Russian missiles and drones struck Ukrainian cities overnight and on Wednesday, damaging 30 energy facilities, according to Zelenskiy. Around 600,000 people were left without electricity, while six people were killed in the western city of Lutsk. In Kyiv, officials reported two deaths and 21 injuries. REUTERS

title: Two ships sink near Hormuz
description: Two ships sink near Hormuz
content:
Two commercial vessels have sunk near the Strait of Hormuz in separate incidents after being hit by projectiles, maritime officials said on Wednesday, raising the number of ships sunk in the globally strategic waterways to three since the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.
The Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride sank on Tuesday while transiting the strait after sustaining damage and catching fire, according to Singapore's Maritime and Port Authority. All 21 crew members were safely evacuated, with no injuries reported.
In a separate incident, the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged dry bulk carrier Cape Dao sank near the strait weeks after being struck by a projectile on September 23, according to data from the International Maritime Organization (IMO). One crew member was killed, while the remaining crew were evacuated.
Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days, as Iran steps up strikes in response to a US blockade of its ports and tighter sanctions introduced last month. REUTERS

description:
Houthi strikes unsettle
Umrah pilgrims
content:
Attacks on airports disrupt travel as visitors to Makkah and Madina face growing anxiety
Umra pilgrims visiting holiest Islamic sites in Saudi Arabia have been caught up in the country's air war with Yemen's Houthis, with missile strikes on airports disrupting travel and raising fears among visitors, even as Makkah and Madina remain outside the targets.
Footage of Saturday's blast at a Riyadh airport departure terminal, which killed 13 people and wounded 300, showed passengers wearing the simple white garments associated with Umra. Saudi media reported that a Bangladeshi Imam leading a group of dozens of pilgrims died and others were wounded.
The Houthis have said they will not attack Makkah or Madina, which attract millions of faithful annually, but pilgrims' worries do not go away. "I feel deeply worried for my family and myself," said Fadi Anwar, a Jordanian living in Makkah. He said repeated phone alerts from authorities had caused anxiety.
Sudanese visitor Al Amin Hassan Mohammed was in Riyadh during Saturday's attack. He said he and his neighbours went outside their homes, worried by the blast. Friends who had planned to fly through Riyadh instead travelled by boat to Sudan from Jeddah after their journey was disrupted.
Many pilgrims travel to Makkah throughout the year for Umra. While international visitors often fly directly to Jeddah or Madina, others pass through Saudi Arabia's other major air hubs. The Houthi strikes have forced Saudi Arabia to ground many flights.
Travel disruption has also affected business visitors, tourists and foreign residents seeking to leave the kingdom. Some travellers are making lengthy road journeys to Bahrain, Qatar or Dubai to catch onward flights.
A senior executive told Reuters that arrangements were being made to transport foreign employees by road to Doha. Several embassies have also used Qatar for travel, while a transport company representative said fares to Doha and Dubai had doubled. REUTERS

title: Trump s new spokesperson stumbles into controversy
description: Trump s new spokesperson stumbles into controversy
content:
Katie Zacharia's legal credentials questioned after shaky maiden briefing
The White House was facing mounting questions on Wednesday over new press secretary Katie Zacharia's legal credentials, after a faltering first day in the job when she gave an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam.
A US watchdog group filed a complaint with the State Bar of California, asking it to investigate whether President Donald Trump's spokeswoman – the public face of the administration – had broken the law by repeatedly presenting herself as a lawyer without a license.
Campaign for Accountability said Zacharia had described herself as a lawyer during television appearances. "The State Bar should investigate whether Ms. Zacharia has misled the public about her credentials," said the group's executive director, Michelle Kuppersmith.
Zacharia, 41, graduated from Pepperdine University's law school in 2011, but obtaining a law degree does not automatically qualify someone to practice law. Trump described Zacharia as "an attorney" when announcing her appointment Friday.
The controversy followed a rocky first appearance as White House press secretary on Tuesday, when Zacharia read extensively from prepared notes during a briefing lasting just 14 minutes. She took only three questions and stumbled over answers, at one point accidentally referring to the president as her husband.
Trump, however, praised Zacharia's debut, telling reporters: "I thought she was very good." Zacharia succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down in August after becoming one of the most prominent public defenders of Trump's second administration. AFP

title: Pope recuperates after lung cancer surgery
description: Pope recuperates after lung cancer surgery
content:
The Pontiff undergoes 90-minute operation at Rome's Gemelli hospital
Pope Leo XIV was recovering in hospital on Wednesday after surgeons removed part of his right lung and tests confirmed the tumour was cancerous, raising uncertainty over the future of his papacy.
The 71-year-old underwent a 90-minute operation at Rome's Gemelli hospital on Tuesday and spent a "calm" night, the Vatican said. Further tests are expected to determine whether the cancer has spread, although the Vatican said it was detected early and remained localised.
"It's a shock for everyone. We're in 'wait-and-see' mode," a Vatican source told AFP. The first American pope, elected in May 2025, is expected to need about a week to recover. All his audiences have been cancelled until October 20.
The diagnosis has unsettled the Catholic Church, with experts questioning how the illness could affect Leo's active leadership and efforts to bridge divisions within the Church. His health has also cast doubt on a planned visit next month to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where he spent two decades as a missionary.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif wished strength, comfort and speedy recovery of Pope Leo XIV in a social media poet. "My heartfelt prayers are with His Holiness Pope Leo XIV following his surgery. On behalf of the people and Government of Pakistan, I wish him strength, comfort and a speedy recovery," the prime minister wrote in a post on X.
He said Pakistan's Catholic community, and the entire nation, joined him in praying for His Holiness' good health. "His steadfast message of compassion, peace and human dignity resonates deeply with people across Pakistan and the world. We pray that he continues his invaluable service to humanity, with renewed strength and conviction," the prime minister added.Agencies

title: PTI moves PHC against emergency
description: PTI moves PHC against emergency
content:
PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan has approached the Peshawar High Court (PHC), challenging the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and seeking the annulment of the presidential proclamation issued on October 11.
National Democratic Movement (NDM) leaders Mohsin Dawar and Bushra Gohar have also separately filed similar petition in the court.
In his petition, filed through Advocate Ali Zaman, Gohar has termed the measures unconstitutional and discriminatory, arguing that terrorism cannot be used as a pretext to curtail the powers of an elected provincial government.
The federal government, K-P government, chief minister Sohail Afridi, provincial assembly speaker and other relevant authorities have been named as respondents.
The PTI chairman contended that terrorism had affected different parts of the country in the past without elected provincial governments being removed on that basis.
He cited the security situation in Balochistan, where terrorist attacks and casualties had been continually reported, arguing that governor's rule had not been imposed there despite the serious law and order challenges.
The petition also referred to the period between 2007 and 2015, when K-P and the former tribal areas experienced a severe wave of militancy, resulting in substantial casualties among civilians and security personnel.
The petitioner argued that the elected provincial government had not been removed through governor's rule during that period and urged the court to examine the constitutional justification and alleged motives behind the current measures.
Gohar maintained that the PTI opposed terrorism and supported action against militant elements and efforts to restore peace.
He rejected allegations that the party's provincial government had failed to take effective action against terrorism or had shown leniency towards militants, claiming such accusations were being used to exert political pressure and weaken the mandate PTI secured in the 2024 general elections.
The petition argued that the party had won a two-thirds majority in the province and that the federal government could not curtail the powers of an elected government because of political differences.
It also questioned the use of the failure of negotiations as a justification for action against PTI, maintaining that the party had not planned any unlawful activity during its long march and that peaceful political protest could not, by itself, justify suspending an elected government.
Invoking Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, the petition asked the court to examine whether the requirements for imposing an emergency and invoking governor's rule had been met.
Article 232 deals with emergency powers in specified circumstances, while Article 234 provides a mechanism for a presidential proclamation where a provincial government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.
Separately, NDM President Mohsin Dawar and Bushra Gohar filed a constitutional petition through Advocate Yousaf Orakzai, challenging the October 11 presidential proclamation as unlawful, unconstitutional and beyond the president's authority.
The president, Federation of Pakistan, K-P governor, Senate, National Assembly, Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Defence have been named as respondents.
The NDM petition states that the proclamation, issued under Articles 232 and 234, transferred the powers of the provincial government to the governor and shifted the provincial assembly's powers to parliament.
It further claims that the chief minister, provincial ministers, advisers and advocate general were removed from their offices as a result.
The petitioners alleged that the proclamation was mala fide and based on an allegedly fabricated report from the governor, arguing that the provincial government had not sent a report concerning the security situation. They maintained that the constitutional procedure for imposing an emergency under Article 232 had not been followed.
The NDM leaders have asked the high court to declare the proclamation unlawful and set it aside. They have also sought interim relief suspending its implementation until the petition is finally decided.

title: Oman praises Pakistan s diplomacy
description: Oman praises Pakistan s diplomacy
content:
Omani Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr Albusaidi called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday and appreciated Pakistan's "sustained diplomatic efforts" for de-escalation and peaceful solutions to regional challenges, a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said.
Albusaidi's meeting with PM Shehbaz was held on the second day of his two-day trip to Pakistan, during which he also attended the eighth session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) and held a meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.
In his meeting with the Omani foreign minister, the prime minister "highlighted that the strong bond of shared faith, geography, history, culture, and centuries of people-to-people exchanges between Pakistan and Oman provided a strong fraternal foundation to the bilateral relationship", the PMO statement said.
The premier underscored that Pakistan considered Oman a brotherly country, an important maritime neighbour and a valuable partner in a critically important region, it added.
"The prime minister expressed satisfaction over the successful convening of the 8th Session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission.
"He hoped that the meeting would provide a strong foundation for further expanding mutually beneficial cooperation and deepening engagement between the two brotherly countries," the statement said.
It further stated that the prime minister "noted with deep satisfaction the unanimity of views between Pakistan and Oman on all regional and global issues".
He appreciated Oman's "principled stance" of dialogue and diplomacy in resolving disputes, the statement said.
For his part, Albusaidi thanked the government of Pakistan for the hospitality extended to him and his delegation and "expressed satisfaction on successful holding of the 8th JMC session", the PMO statement said.
It added that the Omani foreign minister "agreed that it (JMC session) would pave the way for enhanced bilateral collaboration in diverse sectors for mutual benefit".
"The Omani foreign minister also appreciated Pakistan's sustained diplomatic efforts towards de-escalating tensions and advancing peaceful solutions to regional challenges," the statement read.
It added that PM Shehbaz also witnessed the signing of the Protocol of the 8th session of the Pakistan-Oman JMC, as well as agreements and memoranda of understanding for bilateral cooperation between the two sides in the areas of media cooperation, news and information exchange, historical documentation and archives management, communication and information technology and facilitation of diplomatic and official exchanges.
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Wednesday said that Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia were "totally unacceptable".
He made the remarks while addressing a joint press conference alongside Omani Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr Albusaidi, who is currently on an official visit to Pakistan, following the eighth session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC).
At the outset of the news conference, Dar said that the two sides would sign a protocol relating to the commission.
Dar stated that during his discussions with Sayyid Badr, he "conveyed Pakistan's strongest condemnation" of the recent attacks "which resulted in injuries to several individuals, martyrdom of one Pakistani and injuries to five Pakistani nationals."
According to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on X, FM Dar "reaffirmed Pakistan's full solidarity with the leadership and people of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," including Islamabad's "unwavering commitment to the kingdom's sovereignity, territorial integrity and security, in accordance with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement."
The remarks came as Yemen's Houthis vowed to press on with attacks on airports and oil facilities in Saudi ?Arabia and said they struck the headquarters of oil giant Saudi Aramco. The group said it had launched ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco facilities in the eastern city of Dhahran, King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and an Aramco refinery in Riyadh, without saying when.
Saudi Arabia has faced widening Houthi strikes over the past week, including an attack on Riyadh airport on Saturday that killed 13 people.
Dar and his Omani counterpart "also exchanged views on the evolving situation in the Gulf, underscoring the importance of restraint, de-escalation, dialogue and diplomacy." FM Dar highlighted "the need to ensure the safety and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb, given their critical importance to regional and global food and energy security."
According to the statement, Dar reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to "contributing constructively to diplomatic efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability in the region."
Dar, in his meeting with Sayyid Badr, also raised the issue of Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK), saying that it remained "a long-standing unresolved international dispute." The foreign minister "reiterated Pakistan's call for its just and peaceful resolution in accordance with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions."
Discussing "the grave situation in Palestine," the statement noted, FM Dar reiterated Islamabad's "principled and unwavering support" for the Palestinian people "and their inalienable rights." He stated, "We expressed concern over the continued expansion of illegal settlements and efforts to alter the status of Al-Quds Al-Sharif."
Pakistan also highlighted the "urgent need for the unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance to the people of Gaza," reaffirming Islamabad's support for a just and lasting solution in accordance with relevant resolutions of the United Nations.
Regarding regional developments including the situation in Afghanistan and the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT), FM Dar underscored "the imperative of ensuring that Afghan territory is not used to carry out activities against Pakistan."
On the IWT, the statement noted that the foreign minister "emphasised that India's unilateral decision to hold the treaty in abeyance constitutes a material breach of international law." He added that this represented "a dangerous attempt to weaponise shared water resources," and threatened the water, food and energy security of 250 million Pakistanis.
Welcoming "closer engagement between the business communities of the two countries and encouraged greater investment in Special Economic Zones and Free Zones," FM Dar also acknowledged "the valuable contribution of the Pakistani community in Oman."
The contribution "continues to serve as a strong bridge between our two brotherly countries," he said.
He added that both sides "reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in labour mobility, vocational training, and human resource development to create new opportunities for skilled Pakistani professionals and workers."
Dar expressed gratitude to Sayyid Badr and the Omani delegation "for their constructive engagement and valuable contribution to the success of the JMC session."
He concluded with saying that the "Pakistan-Oman friendship remains strong and forward-looking, and we are committed to building an even more prosperous future together."
Earlier, Dar and Sayyid Badr agreed to strengthen bilateral cooperation and intensify diplomatic efforts for regional peace and stability, as the two countries held the eighth session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) in Islamabad after a seven-year gap.
Speaking during a media briefing in Islamabad, FM Dar welcomed the Omani counterpart and his delegation to Pakistan, conveying greetings on behalf of President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to the Sultan of Oman.
The foreign minister said the two countries had maintained frequent interactions and shared longstanding historical and diplomatic ties. Referring to the JMC, he said: "The meeting was taking place after seven years, and both sides had agreed during their restricted meeting to avoid such lengthy gaps in the future."
He said there was considerable scope for enhancing bilateral trade, economic activities and investment opportunities, stressing that regular engagement was essential to achieving progress.
"I promise that in 2027, God will, I will visit your great country for this purpose and we will have the next GMC there," Dar said. The foreign minister said both sides had identified areas of mutual interest and discussed regional and global developments in detail during their restricted meeting.
He said discussions covered the "United States, Iran, the Strait of Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb, Palestine, the situation in Gaza, Jammu and Kashmir and other pressing regional issues."

title: Houthis hit Aramco HQ  vow more attacks
description: Houthis hit Aramco HQ  vow more attacks
content:
Powerful explosions rattle the Saudi capital
Yemen's Houthis said Wednesday they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi Aramco, after Saudi officials reported a strike on a building in an area housing the energy giant's operations centre.
Powerful explosions meanwhile rattled the Saudi capital, as the coalition fighting the Houthis said it had intercepted a missile fired by the Iran-backed group towards Riyadh.
Yahya Saree, Houthi military spokesman, said their forces had conducted "a high-quality military operation targeting Aramco in Dhahran" as well as strikes targeting Riyadh airport and a refinery in the capital.
"This was carried out using a large number of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones," he said, adding that "operations toward Saudi depths will continue in the coming days, targeting Saudi enemy airports and oil facilities".
Earlier, a Saudi energy ministry official said a building belonging to Aramco in Dhahran was struck, resulting in a "limited fire" but "no casualties or fatalities".
Dhahran is home to Aramco's headquarters, a vast complex comprising numerous buildings and residential compounds.
According to two company employees who spoke to AFP on condition of anonymity, a tower in the headquarters was hit overnight.
"Top three floors have gone," said one of the employees.
A second source briefed on the matter confirmed the strike and that the building was hit.
AFP has not been granted access to the site and was not able to independently verify the degree of damage.
Most strikes on Saudi Arabia have targeted infrastructure on the outskirts of the capital, but the barrages appear to be getting closer to the city centre.
In the city's downtown, residents have been seen parking their cars to stop and look up at the sky, an AFP journalist said.
On Tuesday night, the white plumes of air defence missiles could be seen streaking across the sky followed by explosions.
While walking down a major avenue, a witness told AFP he "saw a projectile cutting across the sky" above a mall, saying it left "a yellowish trail of light followed by a trail of smoke. Then, we heard an explosion".
"People were calm; no one was speaking. We were scared and all looking up at the sky," he added, requesting anonymity.
More blasts were heard on Wednesday, AFP journalists in Riyadh reported, as messages were received on phones warning of an "aerial threat" and urging people to take shelter.
The alert was lifted a few minutes later.
The Saudi-led coalition meanwhile struck oil sites across western Yemen, with spokesman Turki Al-Malki saying the attacks targeted facilities used to supply the Houthis' effort to "threaten the kingdom, Yemen, the southern Red Sea and waterways".
An AFP correspondent in Sanaa reported an explosion, while a breaking news alert on the Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah TV channel said "Saudi aggression" targeted an oil firm.
The coalition has supported Yemen's government militarily against the Houthis since 2015 in a long-running civil war that has created a humanitarian crisis.
Many civilians in the Houthi-controlled Yemeni capital, fearing shortages, have rushed to queue in front of fuel stations, an AFP journalist said.
The latest escalation follows a strike on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday that left 13 people dead in the worst attack on the kingdom since 2015.
The Saudi cabinet vowed in a meeting led by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman that it "will not allow its security or freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait to be threatened".
Many countries have issued travel warnings to their citizens in Saudi Arabia, with France telling its nationals on Tuesday to avoid Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam airports.
Traffic in perennially gridlocked Riyadh was noticeably lighter this week as remote learning for all schools and work-from-home orders for some companies took effect, according to AFP journalists.
Saudi Arabia faces a major economic contraction this year, with GDP expected to shrink 3.3 percent, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday, predicting a regional drop over Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
The kingdom was already facing headwinds from Iran's chokehold on Hormuz since the start of the Middle East war in February, when the United States and Israel attacked Iran.
But the restart in July of Yemen's frozen war has further roiled the kingdom and brought the fight to its own soil.
Houthi attacks have also targeted oil tankers in the Red SeaSaudi Arabia's alternative export route.

title: Pakistan  Russia to deepen security ties
description: Pakistan  Russia to deepen security ties
content:
Underscore importance of closer institutional linkages
Pakistan reaffirmed its resolve to deepen longstanding relations with Russia and expand practical cooperation in areas of mutual interest, particularly security, as Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff (COAS) Field Marshal Asim Munir met Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev on Wednesday.
According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the meeting at General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi focused on matters of mutual interest and the regional security environment, with particular emphasis on strengthening bilateral security cooperation.
"They underscored the importance of closer institutional linkages and improved coordination between the security institutions of Pakistan and Russia," the statement outlined further.
CDF Munir reiterated Pakistan's commitment to further strengthening its longstanding ties with Moscow and translating bilateral relations into tangible cooperation in areas of shared interest, particularly in the security domain.
The Russian interior minister, meanwhile, appreciated Pakistan's contributions to regional peace and stability and acknowledged the professionalism and sacrifices of the Pakistan Armed Forces in the fight against terrorism.
CDF Munir's meeting with Minister Kolokoltsev comes amid expanding PakistanRussia engagement on counterterrorism, law enforcement, military training and broader bilateral relations.
Also, Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev highlighted the potential for expanding trade and economic cooperation with Pakistan in a meeting with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said.
According to a statement issued by the PMO, in a meeting with the premier on Wednesday, Kolokoltsev highlighted the "significant potential for expanding bilateral trade and economic cooperation" between the two countries.
He conveyed Russia's desire to further strengthen bilateral ties and expand cooperation in areas of shared interest, while expressing his country's readiness to further enhance bilateral engagement with Pakistan, the statement said.
Meanwhile, Pakistan and Russia agreed to finalise an extradition treaty and pledged to sign a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on cooperation in preventing organised crime and exchanging information.
The understanding was reached during a meeting between Naqvi and Kolokolstev in Islamabad. The meeting was followed by delegation-level talks, the interior ministry said in a statement.
Naqvi, during the meeting, said the proposed MoU on prevention of organised crime would be an important milestone in cooperation between the two countries.
The two sides pledged to enhance mutual cooperation in areas of shared interests as they agreed to finalise an extradition treaty and an agreement on the exchange of criminals.
Both sides resolved to promote cooperation in areas of mutual interest and decided to ensure early implementation of a readmission agreement, according to the statement.
They also agreed to enhance cooperation between the Anti-Narcotics Force and relevant Russian institutions.
It was agreed in the meeting that working groups from the interior ministries of both countries would soon visit each other.
The two sides also discussed sending skilled manpower from Pakistan to Russia and facilitating visa acquisition for tourists and the business community, as per the statement.
They agreed to enhance cooperation for the prevention of cybercrime between the National Police Academy and the Russian Police Academy, the statement said.
Naqvi said easing the visa regime would increase people-to-people contact between the two countries. He also expressed desire to benefit from Russia's experiences in curbing cybercrime.
He further noted that at present, 1,300 Pakistani students were studying in Russia and Pakistan wanted more students to study there.
Russian Interior Minister Kolokolstev, for his part, said joint measures were essential for the prevention of all organised crime, including terrorism, drug smuggling, and illegal migration.
He said Russia had brought a 33 per cent reduction in cybercrime through effective measures.
The meeting was attended by Minister of State Tallal Chaudhry, the Russian ambassador in Pakistan, special and additional secretaries to interior and other senior officials.

title: EU wants more legal migration from Pakistan
description: EU wants more legal migration from Pakistan
content:
Bloc's migration chief terms Pakistan's nearly 50% Schengen visa refusal rate 'too much'
The European Union needs to make legal travel easier for Pakistanis and address obstacles faced by genuine travelers, the bloc's migration chief has said, calling Pakistan's nearly 50% Schengen visa refusal rate "too much" and acknowledging difficulties in securing visa appointments.
Magnus Brunner, the European Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration, told The Express Tribune in an exclusive interview during his first visit to Pakistan that the EU needed to improve legal migration pathways while Pakistan also had to improve the quality of documents submitted with visa applications.
"We have to do a better job there as a European Union," Brunner said, referring to visa access. "The quality of the documents to get a visa [needs to] improve, to be diplomatic, because this has actually led to refusal rates of Schengen visas in Pakistan [of] almost 50%, which is too much. So we have to work on both sides, I think."
During his visit, Brunner held talks with President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and other officials, with migration, legal mobility, border management and human smuggling high on the agenda.
Brunner said cooperation between Pakistan and the EU had helped bring down irregular migration significantly. "The numbers are good, they are going down. We see a decrease of Pakistanis coming illegally to the European Union of more than 50%, which is great news," he said.
Separately, Pakistani officials said during Brunner's visit that irregular migration from Pakistan to Europe had fallen by 64% over the past 18 months.
Brunner said bringing irregular migration under control was important for creating greater political space within Europe for legal migration. "It is so important for the public perception to get the illegal part right in order to give also more room for a serious discussion on legal pathways," he said.
Asked about difficulties faced by Pakistanis in even securing appointments to apply for Schengen visas, Brunner acknowledged the problem. "Sometimes it's a bit frustrating, I suppose, for Pakistanis who want to travel legally to the European Union," he said.
He stressed that visas remained largely the competence of individual EU member states but said the European Commission was trying through its visa strategy to improve coordination and make the process quicker.
Brunner said Europe also needed legal migration because of demographic changes and labour shortages. "The people get older each year, and that's why we need, of course, legal migration for our labour markets," he said.
On the EU's Talent Partnership with Pakistan, Brunner acknowledged that its potential had yet to be fully realised. "We haven't achieved enough, I think," he said, adding that one of the reasons for his visit was to explore how the skills of young Pakistanis could be better matched with the needs of European economies.
He cited Italy as an example of an EU member state offering opportunities to foreign workers but acknowledged that other countries could do more. "There is room for improvement for other member states," he said.
Brunner said the challenge for Europe was to match skills available in countries such as Pakistan with jobs required by European economies. He also praised Pakistan's efforts to develop legal labour pathways with other countries, citing its arrangements with South Korea.
"In general, I think Pakistan does a very good job in strategically looking into legal pathways all over the world, but also towards the European Union," he said. At the same time, the commissioner said Europe had tightened its approach towards irregular migration following years of political pressure over the issue.
He said irregular migration into the EU overall had fallen by around 55% during the past two years following reforms. Brunner identified the routes from Pakistan and Bangladesh through Gulf countries, Egypt and Libya towards Italy and Greece as particularly dangerous.
"What we see at the moment is that the most dangerous route, where a lot of people lose their lives, is from Pakistan, Bangladesh, through the Gulf countries, to Egypt, to Libya, and from Libya to Italy and Greece," he said.
He said Pakistan was playing an important role in the EU's Eastern Corridor Initiative aimed at tackling irregular migration and human smuggling along the route. "A lot of Pakistanis have lost their lives actually, and that's what it's about... to save lives," Brunner said.
The commissioner also said cooperation under the EU-Pakistan readmission agreement was progressing, although there was room for improvement.
"We have a readmission agreement with Pakistan which is going well. The return numbers are at 30%, around about 30%, which is in general okay, but also there, of course, room for improvement," he said.
He said Pakistani authorities had given him a clear commitment that the country would take back its nationals found to be staying illegally in the EU.
Brunner had a direct warning for young Pakistanis considering dangerous irregular routes to Europe. "Don't put your life into the hands of the smugglers and the human traffickers because it's very dangerous. You can lose your life and the probability of getting asylum in the European Union is almost zero," he said.
"Stick to the education, the right skills, and then find the legal ways to the European Union. We are very happy to have you legally, on a legal basis, on a legal pathway."
Turning to security, Brunner said terrorism in Pakistan could have implications well beyond the country and called counterterrorism a shared objective. "We do everything to support Pakistan in the fight against terrorism and also radicalisation," he said. "This is our common goal."
Asked about the safety of Muslim communities in Europe amid concerns over Islamophobia and racism, Brunner pointed to the EU's internal security strategy. "I think we have to do everything to keep the people safe altogether and to avoid a misuse of religion, which then leads to radicalisation and extremism," he said.
Brunner also praised Pakistan's diplomatic efforts to defuse tensions between Iran and the United States, saying Islamabad had demonstrated its importance as an intermediary.
"Pakistan has shown that the role of Pakistan is really important. And to be the middleman between those two, I think, is really important," he said. "I trust totally the Pakistani government. They're doing everything they can to bring peace and this is what we as Europeans, of course, support."

title: Parliament ratifies emergency in K-P | The Express Tribune
description: NA, Senate resolutions endorse president's order; Achakzai urges reversal of governor's rule
content:
NA, Senate resolutions endorse president's order; Achakzai urges reversal of governor's rule
Both houses of parliament on Wednesday approved President Asif Ali Zardari's proclamation of emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa by majority vote, despite opposition lawmakers' objections to the measures.
The NA session began under the chairmanship of Speaker Ayaz Sadiq as Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry presented the resolution before the House. During the proceedings, Chaudhry moved a separate motion seeking the suspension of question hour to allow the House to take up other parliamentary business. Opposition lawmakers opposed the motion, but it was adopted by a majority vote.
The Lower House later debated the emergency measures imposed in the province, with opposition lawmakers strongly opposing the Centre's decision and raising a hue and cry during the proceedings. However, the resolution was passed by a majority vote. The NA session was subsequently adjourned until 11am on Friday.
Following the approval from NA, the Senate session was held under the chairmanship of Chairman Yousaf Raza Gilani. During the proceedings, the Senate also approved a motion moved by Senator Shahadat Awan to defer the question-and-answer session scheduled for the day.
Speaking in the upper house, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said Rules 132 and 133, which govern ordinary resolutions moved by private members, did not apply to a resolution introduced under a constitutional requirement. He added that the seven-day notice requirement was not applicable in this case.
Rejecting objections to the procedure, the law minister also said the government could not deviate from the Constitution or the rules and regulations of the House.
He maintained that members opposing the resolution should participate in the debate and, if they disagreed with it, reject it through a vote.
The minister called for the matter to be put to a vote after discussion so that the opinion of the House could be ascertained. Following this, the Senate approved the imposition of emergency in K-P as the opposition walked out in protest.
Later in the day, the president summoned a joint session of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) tomorrow morning at 11 under Clause 1, Section 54 (Summoning and prorogation of Majlis-e-Shoora) of the Constitution of Pakistan. The notification regarding it was issued by the NA today.
Earlier, while speaking on the NA floor, the law minister had said the K-P government's approach to combating terrorism had become a "threat to national security", as the federal government tabled a resolution in the NA seeking parliamentary approval of the emergency imposed in the province under Article 232 of the Constitution.
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari renewed his call for dialogue with the PTI, saying he would personally request Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to end the emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) if political conditions were created that made the measure unnecessary.
"Even today, I invite you to come and hold talks with the government and political parties and create conditions in which there will be no need for this emergency in K-P. If you create these political conditions. I will personally stand in this House and request the prime minister that the time has come to end this emergency," said Bilawal while addressing the National Assembly (NA).
Bilawal maintained that the federal government had made every possible political effort to engage the opposition before taking the constitutional step, saying that the opposition had every right to speak against the decision and oppose it, but argued that PTI could not deny its own role in creating the political, legal and constitutional circumstances that led to the situation.
The PPP chairman accused PTI of carrying out a "political suicide attack" on its own government in K-P, adding that opposition leaders could blame the federal government or President Asif Ali Zardari for the loss of their provincial government, but maintained that PTI, particularly its provincial leadership, had played a significant role in creating the circumstances.
He said responsible figures within the opposition were aware of these circumstances, even if they were unwilling to acknowledge them publicly. He argued that if the federal government had concluded that K-P was facing war-like conditions and that its internal situation prevented an effective response to terrorism, the provincial government should have provided political, legal or constitutional grounds for rejecting the proposed measure.
The PPP chairman questioned why PTI's provincial leadership had failed to provide any justification that would have allowed President Zardari or the PPP to oppose the decision.
Bilawal said that when the proposal first came before the president and the PPP, their position was that the government should engage PTI and the opposition before resorting to what he described as a "constitutional atom bomb". He said the objective was to address the federal government's objections and allegations that the provincial government was not cooperating in the fight against terrorism, thereby removing any legal, constitutional or political justification for taking the step.
Speaking during the session, Minister Tarar said the Constitution required a presidential proclamation of emergency under Article 232 to be laid before both houses of parliament - the National Assembly and the Senate - for approval within 10 days of its issuance. Responding to criticism that the imposition of emergency had resulted in the removal of an elected provincial government, Tarar said the decision had been taken after extensive deliberations and a thorough assessment of the security situation in K-P.
He said the federal cabinet had held a two-and-a-half-hour discussion before recommending the emergency measures to the prime minister, citing internal disturbances and cross-border incursions as major factors behind the decision.
Meanwhile, Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party (PkMAP) Chairman Mahmood Khan Achakzai described the government as "a terrorist government", alleging that it had been formed through money and coercion with the support of uniformed institutions, and defended non-functional chief minister Sohail Afridi's opposition to what he termed oppression.
Achakzai accused the government of undermining the electoral mandate, alleging that the assemblies had been bought to install a government that did not represent the people's will. He argued that the PTI had been prevented from contesting the elections under its party symbol and that its candidates had subsequently contested using around 200 different symbols.
"Whether PTI founder Imran Khan was good or bad, whatever he was, I don't go to the past; you went to such an extent to compete with him that you even snatched the party's election symbol. You stopped the party from participating in the election," he said.
Questioning whether the government was punishing the entire country for the PTI's electoral success, Achakzai asked, "Are you punishing Pakistan's 240 million people for this?"
He defended Afridi's stance against the government, saying K-P's people had shown courage in opposing what he described as terrorism. He maintained that the Afridi had called on people to resist oppression rather than resort to violence. Achakzai also criticised the authorities over Afridi's treatment, alleging that the Afridi had been arrested and restrained but not brought before the assembly.
"You have done us a great favour, a very great favour! After arresting Afridi and binding his hands and feet, you didn't bring him here. Do it, do this too. What was he doing, Mr Speaker?" he asked.
Achakzai warned that political confrontation over provincial rights could extend beyond K-P, saying people in Balochistan and Punjab could also resist what he described as the forcible denial of their rights.
He expressed regret over the participation of political representatives from Sindh in the current political situation and warned that the province could face governor's rule over disputes concerning water and mineral resources.
"Next, governor's rule will be imposed in Sindh over water, minerals, Canals, and then you will remember what mistake we made," he said.
Referring to the history of East Pakistan, Achakzai recalled that Mujibur Rehman had worked for the Muslim League before being branded a traitor. He said more than 48% of the people of East Pakistan had voted in favour of Pakistan, invoking the episode to criticise what he described as the denial of political representation.
He also criticised what he called the "Throne of Lahore", describing it as cruel, and urged the government to reconsider its approach towards the provinces.
Addressing the NA speaker, Achakzai called for the reversal of the government's decisions and urged lawmakers to restore parliament's position as the centre of political authority. "Mr Speaker, there is still time; reverse it, reverse these decisions. Come, make this house a fountainhead of power, " he said.
Speaking on the floor of the NA, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said 3,900 people had been martyred in K-P over 14 months, in addition to 2,700 over three years, as he criticised the provincial government for prioritising political interests over counterterrorism efforts.
Asif called for a united national response to terrorism, saying the province was bearing the greatest burden of violence and could not effectively confront the threat without political cohesion.
He alleged that the non-functional K-P chief minister was more concerned about retaining power than addressing terrorism.
Asif said the Afridi had remained in office for 13 to 14 months and questioned whom he had taken instructions from, alleging that the individual directing him was now in Afghanistan. Asif also criticised the province's governance, comparing its development over the past 13 years with that of other provinces.
Referring to a Taliban statement condemning an emergency and the deployment of security forces in certain areas, the minister urged the opposition to clarify its political alignments.
"The opponent is the Pakistan state, and the ally is the Taliban whose hands are stained with the blood of our children," he highlighted during his speech in the lower house.
Alluding to a relative of former premier Imran Khan, whom he said was living in the United States, Asif questioned the extent of that individual's influence over the province's affairs, including health-related matters..

title: PKLI performs two more liver transplants
description: PKLI performs two more liver transplants
content:
The Pakistan Kidney and Liver Institute (PKLI) in Rawalpindi has successfully performed two more liver transplants, bringing the total number of successful liver transplants at the institute to four, alongside one kidney transplant.
The latest procedures were carried out on Oct 12 and 13.
In the first case, a father from Bannu donated his liver to his daughter, while in the second, a man from Rawalpindi donated his liver to his wife.
Medical experts say the liver of a donor can regenerate and return to its normal state in approximately three months.
Both procedures were performed under the supervision of Professor Dr Faisal Saud Dar, Dr Ehsanul Haq and Dr Bilal Ahmed.
Before these procedures, two liver transplants and one kidney transplant had also been successfully performed at PKLI Rawalpindi.
PKLI Project Director Dr Zulfiqar Ali Khan said donors for kidney and liver transplants were accepted only on the basis of blood relations.

title: Capital to have 130 union councils
description: Capital to have 130 union councils
content:
Election appellate authority rejects all objections to Islamabad's UC's
The regional election commissioner, acting as the appellate authority for delimitation in Islamabad, has rejected all objections to the boundaries of the federal capital's 130 union councils and their blocks, declaring the delimitation decisions valid.
With the decision, all 130 union councils of Islamabad have been finalised. Under the new Islamabad Local Government Act, the capital will have three municipal town corporations, three mayors and six deputy mayors.
Each of Islamabad's three National Assembly constituencies will have one municipal town corporation, designated Municipal Town Corporation-I, Municipal Town Corporation-II and Municipal Town Corporation-III.
The delimitation appellate authority has issued orders dismissing the objections.
A complete report will be sent to the Election Commission on Wednesday, after which the final notification will be issued.
Meanwhile, the Rawalpindi bench of the Lahore High Court has remanded 27 appeals filed by political parties and candidates against the delimitation of union councils and councillor blocks in Rawalpindi and Murree districts to the District Election Commission, Rawalpindi, for fresh hearings.
The court directed the election authorities to hear all petitioners and issue fresh decisions on the delimitation of union councils and blocks in accordance with the merits of the cases and the relevant territorial boundaries.
The District Election Commission said it had been informed of the court's decision. Notices would be issued to all applicants next week, and their cases would be heard individually before fresh decisions were made.
Under the new Punjab Local Government Act 2026, Rawalpindi city has also been divided into two municipal town corporations, which will have two mayors and four deputy mayors.
Rawalpindi district has been divided into 17 local government entities, including two town corporations, five municipal committees, six tehsil councils and four cantonment boards.
