title: Canada returned elderly couple found dead at Karachi home
description: No sharp edged weapon injuries found on couple dead bodies  police await post mortem findings
content:
No sharp-edged weapon injuries found on couple dead bodies; police await post-mortem findings
The bodies of an elderly couple, who had returned from Canada a few months ago, were found at their house in North Karachi, with the cause of death yet to be ascertained, police said.
According to a statement issued by the District Central police spokesperson, the bodies were found at house R-93 in Sector 11-C of North Karachi, opposite B Amma Park, within the jurisdiction of the Sir Syed police station.
The deceased were identified as 70-year-old Muhammad Yameen, son of Khuda Bakhsh, and his 65-year-old wife, Nafis Akhtar. The couple had returned from Canada some time ago and were living at the house, the police said.
Read : Five members of a family found dead inside home in Karachi's Malir
Their bodies were taken to Abbasi Shaheed Hospital for medico-legal formalities. An initial examination found no marks of injuries caused by a sharp-edged weapon on either body, contrary to earlier reports that the couple had been found with their throats slit, the police spokesperson said.
However, blood had flowed from their noses and ears and dried on the floor. Police suspected that excessive bleeding might have caused their deaths, while the possibility that they had been given a poisonous substance was also being investigated.
Sir Syed Station House Officer (SHO) Irfan Asif said the cause of death could not be immediately established. He added that poisoning was one possibility, but it was too early to reach a conclusion and the post-mortem report would be needed to determine the cause of death.
The incident came to light when a close relative of Yameen visited the couple but received no response from inside the house. The police were subsequently informed.
Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Fareed Khan said the bodies appeared to be more than 18 hours old. Police were obtaining footage from closed-circuit television cameras installed in the area to gather further information about the incident.
Also Read : Mother, three children brutally murdered
Investigators were also told that workers had been visiting the house for repair work. The couple had last been seen outside the house on Tuesday evening, according to information gathered by the police.
The house, a ground-plus-one structure with a shop, had reportedly been owned by the couple for several years. They planned to sell it and return to Canada to join their three children. The house had recently been vacated by a tenant, and repair work was under way. There was little furniture or other household material inside.
Police recovered mobile phones from the house but found no evidence of robbery, the report said.
Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar took notice of the incident and sought details from the senior superintendent of police for District Central.

title: CAA signs  Off Campus  star Ella Bright as her Hollywood career takes off
description: CAA signs Ella Bright  star of Prime Video s  Off Campus   as the actress prepares for her first studio lead in Narcs
content:
CAA signs Ella Bright, star of Prime Video's 'Off Campus', as the actress prepares for her first studio lead in Narcs
Ella Bright, the breakout star of Prime Video's romantic drama Off Campus , has signed with Creative Artists Agency (CAA) as her acting career continues to gain momentum.
According to Deadline , Bright plays Hannah Wells in Off Campus , opposite Belmont Cameli. Based on Elle Kennedy's bestselling book series, the show follows an aspiring songwriter navigating college life and a complicated romance with a star hockey player.
The series attracted 36 million viewers worldwide during its first 12 days, making it Amazon's third most-watched series debut of all time, behind The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power and Fallout .
Alongside her acting work, Bright has performed and recorded several songs for the show's soundtrack. These include "Baby Now That I Found You", featuring Niall Horan, and "Girl That I Am", written by Amy Allen. She has also completed filming the second season of Off Campus .
Bright is set to star opposite Mason Thames in the upcoming coming-of-age comedy Narcs , which will mark her first leading role in a studio film. She has also wrapped filming on Gable , an independent drama inspired by real-life wrestling, featuring Finn Cole and Ben Foster.
Before her recent success, Bright portrayed a young Kate Middleton in Netflix's The Crown and appeared in all seven seasons of the British television series Malory Towers . Her work on the latter earned her nominations at the BAFTA Children's Awards and the Children's & Family Emmy Awards.
Her previous credits also include the comedy Holmes & Watson , starring Will Ferrell and John C. Reilly. Bright made her West End debut in Harry Potter and the Cursed Child in 2017.
Bright continues to be represented by Prime Talent Media, Accelerate in the UK, Derek Kroeger at Myman Greenspan and Viewpoint.

title: China  Pakistan begin first ever joint army training exercise
description: Exercise will focus on joint counter terrorism operations in high altitude areas  skills training in UAV operation
content:
Exercise will focus on joint counter-terrorism operations in high-altitude areas, skills training in UAV operation
China and Pakistan began their first-ever joint army training exercise on Wednesday in northwestern Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, according to Chinese state media .
The opening ceremony of Karakoram 2026 was held at a training base in Korla city, according to the China Military Bugle , the official media account of Beijing's armed forces.
The two sides exchanged counter-terrorism experience, and Pakistani troops observed some Chinese weapons and equipment.
Read : Pakistan, China conduct joint counter-terrorism exercise
China, Pakistan Kick Off First Joint Army Training in Xinjiang The opening ceremony for the first-ever China-Pakistan joint army training exercise "Karakoram 2026" was held at a training base in Korla, Northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, on October 14, 2026.… pic.twitter.com/Bbl9dppHPf
Focusing on joint counter-terrorism operations in high-altitude areas, the exercise would include skills training in UAV operation, on-the-move target search and firing, and long-range sniping, and would cover joint command and live-force exercises.
#GTMilitaryWatch First #China - #Pakistan army joint training features an all-Chinese equipment lineup: Type 11 assault vehicles, Type 08 IFVs and more. An expert said the choice of wheeled vehicles suits the plateau, and the all-Chinese lineup signals deep trust and possible… pic.twitter.com/u6D25kogX5
The training would help the two sides deepen cooperation and strengthen interoperability in counter-terrorism.
According to China Central Television 's military channel, the weapons and equipment in the training were provided by China and included "Type 191 rifles, Type 201 squad machine guns, Type 11 armoured assault vehicles, Type 08 infantry fighting vehicles, as well as artillery, unmanned and anti-unmanned systems".
Pakistan and China enjoy longstanding, time-tested defence cooperation rooted in mutual trust and strategic partnership.
On May 8, joint patrol exercises were conducted between the Khunjerab Security Force and the Chinese military at the Khunjerab Pass border in Hunza.
Read More : Joint patrol held with China at Khunjerab Pass
The purpose of the joint activity was to further strengthen Pakistan-China border security, promote mutual cooperation, and reinforce friendly relations between the two neighbouring countries.
On December 3, 2025, the Pakistan Army and the People's Liberation Army commenced the joint military exercise Warrior-IX, the ninth edition in the series of bilateral counterterrorism exercises conducted annually between the two countries.
The exercise focused on Counter Terrorism operations to enhance interoperability, refine professional skills, and exchange best practices in modern warfare.

title: Houthis claim ballistic missile strike on Riyadh airport
description: Yemeni army claims 1 250 Houthis    neutralised    in  Dawn of Yemen  operation
content:
Yemeni army claims 1,250 Houthis ‘neutralised’ in 'Dawn of Yemen' operation
Yemen’s Houthi group said on Wednesday that it had hit the main airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh with a ballistic missile.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group’s forces struck King Khalid International Airport “with a ballistic missile, scoring a precise and direct hit.”
Saree did not specify when the attack took place or provide details of possible casualties or damage.
تمكنت قواتنا المسلحة بفضل الله وعونه من استهداف مطار خالد الدولي في عاصمة العدو السعودي الرياض بصاروخ باليستي وكانت الإصابة دقيقة ومباشرة. وفي سياق آخر نفذت قواتنا المسلحة عملية استهداف لعدد من تحشيدات العدو السعودي في منطقة رأس العارة والمضاربة بثلاثة صواريخ بالستية وكانت…
The announcement follows 10 attacks on five Saudi airports on October 5-11 that killed 20 people and injured hundreds, while causing property damage and disrupting flights, according to an Anadolu tally based on official statements.
King Khalid International Airport was the most frequently targeted, with five attacks killing 18 people and injuring hundreds. King Fahd International Airport in the eastern city of Dammam sustained two attacks, while the southern airports of Abha, Jazan, and Najran sustained one apiece.
On Sunday, Saudi authorities said an unidentified projectile struck Terminal 4 at King Khalid Airport, triggering a fire that killed a Pakistani resident and injured 11 others.
An earlier attack on Saturday killed 13 people and injured 309, prompting Saudi authorities to suspend airport operations temporarily. The suspension was extended on Monday.
The Saudi Civil Aviation Authority did not identify those responsible for the attacks on the five airports.
However, the Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s government accused the Houthis of carrying out some of them. The group has also claimed responsibility for attacks on sites inside Saudi Arabia, including airports.
Yemeni army claims 1,250 Houthis ‘neutralised’ in 'Dawn of Yemen' operation
Yemeni government forces said on Wednesday that 1,250 Houthi fighters had been “neutralised” during the “Dawn of Yemen” military operation on several fronts.
Yemeni Armed Forces spokesman Majed Abdullah al-Nazili said in a statement that government forces conducted 2,309 “precise and direct” strikes using warplanes, drones, field artillery, rocket launchers and sniper units.
He claimed the operations disrupted Houthi defensive lines, command-and-control centres, frontline positions and supply routes, allowing government forces to advance.
The spokesman said more than 460 military vehicles and other pieces of equipment had also been destroyed or damaged.
Yemen’s armed forces say they carried out 2,309 precision targeting strikes under the “Dawn of Yemen” operation, neutralizing around 1,250 Houthi fighters and destroying or disabling more than 460 of their military vehicles. pic.twitter.com/HaK7ps7QKr
In the southwestern province of Taiz, government forces continued airstrikes and ambush operations targeting Houthi forces and reinforcements, according to the statement.
Al-Nazili urged residents in Houthi-controlled areas to keep their children away from recruitment campaigns and military positions, and reiterated an amnesty by Presidential Leadership Council Chairman Rashad al-Alimi to fighters who lay down their weapons.
He also accused the Houthis of targeting civilian infrastructure and residential neighbourhoods in Taiz.
The Yemeni army also said it captured five Houthi commanders west of Taiz province, including senior commander Akram Amer, who holds the rank of major general.
Yemen's Houthis vow more attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities after Aramco HQ hit
Yemen's Houthis ​vowed on Wednesday to press on with attacks on airports and oil facilities in Saudi ‌Arabia and said they struck the headquarters of oil giant Saudi Aramco, which was hit the day before.
The Iran-aligned group said it had launched ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco facilities in the eastern city of Dhahran, King Khalid International Airport in ​Riyadh and an Aramco refinery in Riyadh, without saying when.
Saudi Arabia has faced widening Houthi strikes over the ​past week, including an attack on Riyadh airport on Saturday that killed 13 people.
Read: Saudi-led coalition says Houthi ballistic missile intercepted over Riyadh
The Houthis ⁠say they have been retaliating for the kingdom's backing of Yemeni government forces in the Yemen war that ​restarted last month, reignited by the US-Iran confrontation in the Gulf.
Saudi-led forces say they intercepted missile
In a broad threat, the ​Houthis urged "international shipping companies", civilians and workers to evacuate airports and oil facilities, which they declared legitimate military targets.
The Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis towards Riyadh on Wednesday, and several loud booms were heard in ​the Saudi capital.
Saudi authorities earlier issued an alert for a possible aerial threat in Riyadh on Wednesday before the ​warning was lifted, a witness said. It wasn't immediately clear what caused the booms and there was no immediate comment from ‌the ⁠authorities on their source.
The escalating conflict has dealt a blow to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's ambitious plans to transform and diversify the Saudi economy and reduce its reliance on oil.
Read more: Saudi-led coalition announces large-scale operation against Houthis in Yemen, says 136 military targets destroyed
The Saudi Energy Ministry said Tuesday's attack on the headquarters of Saudi Aramco had caused a limited fire and no injuries or deaths.
The Dhahran complex hosts ​a major operations centre for ​Aramco, which oversees a ⁠vast network of onshore and offshore oil rigs, pipelines, refineries and export terminals.
A company source told Reuters earlier that a ballistic missile hit the Aramco headquarters complex. The ​source said an office tower in the complex was struck and that its top ​three floors ⁠were damaged.
Riyadh’s international airport has come under attack four times, including Saturday's attack which was the deadliest in Saudi Arabia in a decade. Authorities have closed the airport until October 17, and airlines have cancelled flights to Saudi Arabia.
Fearing the rise of Iranian influence ⁠and ​the prospect of chaos on its borders, Saudi Arabia intervened in ​Yemen's civil war in support of the government in 2015 after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa.
The UN brokered a 2022 truce between the ​warring sides in Yemen that kept a fragile peace until this year.
The coalition said in a statement on Tuesday evening that it attacked the station and other sites in an operation aimed at "neutralising the capabilities of Houthis" to threaten Saudi Arabia, Yemen and international waterways.
The Saudi cabinet, chaired by de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, issued a statement on Tuesday before the strike on Saudi Aramco saying the Houthis would face consequences for ​their repeated attacks on the kingdom.
South Korea condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's civilian, economic facilities
South Korea on Wednesday condemned Houthi attacks on key civilian and economic facilities in Saudi Arabia, including King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Saudi Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran, which resulted in civilian casualties.
"Attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure can never be tolerated, and such attacks must cease immediately," Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said on the US social media company X.
The remarks came amid escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including repeated strikes on airports and energy sites.

title: Fatima Fertilizer becomes first to partner with Punjab s EP CCD on environmental sustainability
description: Joint initiative focuses on climate action  environmental awareness and sustainable development across Punjab
content:
Joint initiative focuses on climate action, environmental awareness and sustainable development across Punjab
Fatima Fertilizer Company Limited and the Environment Protection & Climate Change Department (EP&CCD), Government of Punjab, have established a Joint Collaborative Framework to strengthen collective efforts towards environmental sustainability, climate action and sustainable development across the province. The collaboration reflects a shared commitment to bringing public- and private-sector stakeholders together to support environmental priorities, encourage responsible practices and build greater awareness of the challenges facing Punjab. It will provide a platform for facilitating partnerships, mobilising stakeholder participation and promoting initiatives that contribute to a more sustainable and climate-resilient future. Via this framework, Fatima Fertilizer and EP&CCD aim to encourage meaningful engagement with industry, academia, youth, civil society and other relevant stakeholders. Areas of potential collaboration include environmental awareness, air quality improvement, smog mitigation, water conservation, waste management, biodiversity protection and green innovation. The initiative also aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 13 (Climate Action), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals). By fostering cross-sector collaboration and supporting awareness and engagement around environmental challenges, the framework seeks to contribute to broader sustainability objectives while encouraging collective responsibility for environmental protection. Commenting on the collaboration, Rabel Sadozai, Director Marketing & Sales, Fatima Fertilizer, stated:
Building a sustainable future requires collective commitment, practical action and strong partnerships across sectors. Through our collaboration with EP&CCD, we aim to contribute to greater environmental awareness, encourage responsible practices and bring stakeholders together around shared sustainability priorities.
We believe that meaningful progress on climate action and environmental protection depends on turning awareness into action and working collectively towards a more sustainable future for Punjab.
Speaking at the event, Ms Silwat Saeed, Secretary, Environment Protection and Climate Change Department (EP&CCD), Government of Punjab, quoted:
Fatima Fertilizer is the first company to come forward and join hands with the Environment Protection and Climate Change Department in this collaborative effort towards environmental sustainability. Addressing the challenges of climate change requires strong partnerships between the public and private sectors.
By combining our efforts and expertise, we can strengthen environmental awareness, promote sustainable practices and build greater resilience for Punjab’s future generations.
The Joint Collaborative Framework underscores the importance of cooperation between public institutions and the private sector in addressing environmental challenges and advancing sustainable development. Through this partnership, Fatima Fertilizer and EP&CCD aim to support a more informed, engaged and environmentally conscious society in Punjab.

title: Netflix cuts about 6  of jobs in biggest layoff since 2022
description: Bulk of job cuts will be in Netflix s product  tech  legal and human resources teams
content:
Bulk of job cuts will be in Netflix's product, tech, legal and human-resources teams
Netflix is laying off 6% of its workforce, or roughly 1,000 employees, in its biggest cuts since ​2022, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters , as the streaming pioneer ‌faces tough competition for viewers from legacy rivals and YouTube.
The bulk of the job cuts would be in Netflix's product, tech, legal and human-resources teams, the email Co-CEOs Greg Peters and Ted Sarandos sent to ​employees on Wednesday showed.
"Our mission — to entertain the world — is ambitious, and delivering on ​it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritise our people ⁠and resources," they said in the memo.
Exclusive: Netflix is cutting about 1,000 jobs, its biggest round of layoffs in years as it struggles with slowing growth and customer engagement https://t.co/4kLKUmxN40
"Our business is strong and growing, and we remain ​on track to deliver our full-year forecast."
Netflix shares, down around 25% so far this year, rose ​0.7% on Wednesday. The company had about 16,000 employees at the end of last year.
Read : Netflix faces new round of layoffs amid PR reorganisation, impacting series and film publicity
This year, the streaming giant has faced doubts about its ability to sustain the growth that disrupted the US media industry by putting ​pressure on cable TV businesses.
Engagement, or the amount of time users spend on Netflix, has ​become a key concern for investors as platforms such as YouTube and TikTok attract viewers with free-to-watch, ‌user-generated content ⁠that gives them a cost advantage over Netflix.
A failed pursuit of Warner Bros Discovery's streaming and studio assets earlier this year deepened doubts about Netflix's strategy. Paramount completed its $110-billion Warner Bros acquisition earlier this month to form Skydance.
"They haven't been able to find like another line ​of major revenue," said ​Ross Benes, senior ⁠analyst at eMarketer, adding the company remains reliant on a subscription business that could be approaching a ceiling.
"Eventually, because they've kind of nearing a ​ceiling with that, they'll need another revenue stream to diversify, and that's ​where it's ⁠been more of a struggle."
Netflix has been trying to expand beyond its subscription business by investing in an ad tier, live programming and gaming.

title: Kelly Clarkson   s feud with Brooklyn store explained after claims she got the  Pretty Woman  treatment
description: The singer said she had travelled to the store intending to purchase but felt she was judged by an employee
content:
The singer said she had travelled to the store intending to purchase but felt she was judged by an employee
Kelly Clarkson is at the centre of a growing online controversy after accusing a Brooklyn store of treating her as though she could not afford its merchandise, prompting a public dispute with the business over a rare mechanical bird and the circumstances surrounding her visit.
The controversy began on October 10, when Clarkson took to X to describe her experience at Art of Play, a speciality shop in Brooklyn, New York. The singer said she had travelled to the store intending to purchase several items but felt she was judged by an employee, who allegedly offered to find her something more affordable instead.
“Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a huge sale,” Clarkson wrote, comparing the experience to the treatment Julia Roberts’ character receives in the 1990 romantic comedy Pretty Woman. She also encouraged her followers to visit the store if they wanted to experience similar treatment.
The post quickly gained attention, bringing widespread scrutiny to the small business and prompting a response from its owners.
At the centre of the disagreement is Molly, a singing and dancing mechanical bird that Clarkson said she had asked about purchasing. According to the singer, an employee told her the item cost $15,000 before offering to find something comparable, a remark she interpreted as condescending.
Art of Play initially disputed her account, explaining that Molly was a one-of-a-kind automaton permanently attached to the shop’s wall and used in its magic shows. The owners said the bird was not for sale and expressed surprise at the sudden backlash directed at their business.
Clarkson subsequently challenged that explanation, sharing a photograph of a price tag displaying $15,000 beside a singing bird automaton. She maintained that the employee had told her the bird was available for purchase at that price and accused the store of changing its story after her complaint went viral.
The shop later issued a more detailed clarification, explaining that the original bird was part of its displays but that its creator, Seattle-based artist Bliss Kolb, owned a nearly identical version that could be purchased for $15,000. The owners said they had attempted to explain the distinction to Clarkson and offered to show her another singing bird automaton, priced at approximately $2,000.
According to the store, Clarkson left before viewing the alternative item. The business described the incident as a misunderstanding and said it had reached out to the singer privately in an attempt to resolve the disagreement.
The dispute took another turn when security footage of Clarkson’s visit surfaced online on October 13. Released by journalist Pablo Torre through his podcast, Pablo Torre Finds Out, the footage showed Clarkson entering the shop with her children, browsing merchandise and speaking with an employee near the mechanical bird.
The video also showed Clarkson speaking to another employee before leaving the store. Her visit lasted less than five minutes, according to reports. However, the footage contains no audio, meaning it does not establish precisely what was said during the disputed conversation or whether the employee’s tone matched Clarkson’s description.
Art of Play co-owner Adam Rubin subsequently criticised the impact of Clarkson’s public accusations, saying the store had received negative reviews and that staff members and neighbouring businesses had faced harassment. He described the backlash as a form of social warfare and expressed concern about the safety of his employees.
Rubin also suggested that the situation had escalated because Clarkson used her large social media following to publicly identify the business. He maintained that the store had treated her as it would any other customer and said he would welcome her back without offering preferential treatment.
The controversy has divided social media users. Some have supported Clarkson, arguing that customers should not be made to feel judged when asking about expensive merchandise. Others have questioned whether the interaction justified publicly naming a small business before the two sides had an opportunity to resolve their disagreement privately.
The reference to Pretty Woman has also become central to the debate. In the 1990 film, Roberts plays Vivian Ward, who is treated dismissively by employees at an upscale clothing boutique because of her appearance. The comparison has resonated with audiences familiar with the scene, although the circumstances surrounding Clarkson’s visit remain disputed.
Neither the released footage nor the competing accounts conclusively establishes what happened during the conversation. While Clarkson maintains that she was spoken to condescendingly, Art of Play insists that the disagreement stemmed from confusion over which mechanical bird was available for purchase.
The incident has since developed into a broader discussion about customer service, celebrity influence and the consequences of publicly criticising small businesses. For Art of Play, the sudden attention has brought both increased visibility and a wave of negative reactions, while Clarkson’s supporters continue to debate whether the store’s explanation adequately addresses her complaint.
For now, the disagreement remains unresolved, with the two sides offering different accounts of the same brief shopping trip.

title: Govt hikes petrol by Rs1 2  cuts diesel by 17 paisas for Oct 15
description: Petrol price increases to Rs393 86 per litre  while HSD will cost Rs396 65 under daily price mechanism
content:
Petrol price increases to Rs393.86 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs396.65 under daily price mechanism
The federal government on Wednesday increased the price of petrol by Rs1.2 per litre, while decreasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by 17 paisas per litre for October 15.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs393.86 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs396.65 per litre for Thursday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government decreased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.71 and 3 paisas per litre, respectively, for October 14.
The government has revised the prices of petroleum products for Thursday @Official_PetDiv #RadioPakistan #News https://t.co/bsKRhWfzBM pic.twitter.com/cudBQVtC4Y
Read : Govt cuts petrol by Rs2.71, diesel by 3 paisas for Oct 14
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices steadied on Wednesday after rising on an attack, opens new tab on the ​headquarters of Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company and Iranian comments about new tactics deployed to target ships and keep oil prices ‌high to influence US midterm elections.
Brent crude futures were up 13 cents at $105.56 a barrel by 1325 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude gained $1.25, or 1.33%, to $95.39 for a more than two-week high.
"Attacks on ships crossing the Strait of Hormuz and military strikes between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis are supporting prices as market participants remain concerned ​about lower oil exports from the region," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo, adding that exports have held up so far.

Apple says it has rules in place to ensure new employees do not use confidential ​information from previous employers
An OpenAI employee who left the ChatGPT maker for Apple ​sent more than 100 files about an unreleased product to a personal ‌account and later made a presentation about the unreleased product to senior Apple leadership, a new filing in the lawsuit between OpenAI and Apple alleges.
In the filing in US federal court ​in San Jose, California, OpenAI alleged that the presentation happened months ago and ​that Apple is now making AI products of its own, citing ⁠the release of Apple's HomeView product this week.
"OpenAI is very concerned that its trade ​secret and confidential information is now circulating inside Apple, where Apple engineers can shape ​Apple’s upcoming products based on OpenAI’s confidential and innovative work," OpenAI said in its filing.
Apple said that it has policies and procedures in place to ensure new employees do not use confidential ​information from previous employers and that it has found no evidence to support ​OpenAI's allegations.

The document, filed on Tuesday, is part of an ongoing trade secret dispute filed by Apple ‌earlier ⁠this year in which it alleged employees of the iPhone maker left and took confidential information to OpenAI's hardware division. OpenAI has denied those allegations.
Earlier this week, US District Court Judge Edward Davila granted part of Apple's request to get early access ​to digital files from ​OpenAI in the ⁠suit.
Davila said Apple could gather data from some of its former employees' devices and sit three of them for depositions on ​a sped-up schedule, including the two defendants in the case — ​Chang Liu, ⁠a former senior system electrical engineer, and Tang Yew Tan, a former vice president of product design for iPhone and Apple Watch.
The case is likely to go to trial ⁠in ​October 2027, though OpenAI has said in court ​filings that it could be ready for trial as soon as June 2027.

content:
Jamie Foxx joins 'East of the River' as producer, backing Dennis Latos’ crime thriller about two estranged brothers.
Jamie Foxx has joined the independent crime thriller East of the River as a producer through his Foxxhole Productions banner, alongside Alex Marks, according to Variety .
Directed by Dennis Latos, the film follows two estranged brothers who reunite to confront an underground poker ring that destroyed their family. The cast includes Ben Barnes, Ben Ahlers, Callie Hernandez and Maria Sten, alongside David Zayas, John Bedford Lloyd, Catherine Curtin, Nathan Wallace and Steven Gregory.
Barnes is known for The Chronicles of Narnia franchise and The Punisher , while Ahlers has appeared in The Gilded Age and Little Brother . Hernandez’s credits include The Flight Attendant and Alien: Covenant . Sten is taking on her first film role since starring in the television series Neagley .
Former WWE wrestler James Storm and former NFL running back Dalvin Cook are also part of the cast.
According to Variety , post-production on East of the River has recently wrapped, and global distribution rights are available through CAA Media Finance. However, a release date has not yet been announced.
Elise Finnerty wrote the screenplay based on a story by Jim Tamburino, while Ben Grant served as director of photography.
Foxx and Marks are producing alongside Nicolas Alvo of Ruta 5 Films, Benjamin Wiessner of Vanishing Angle, Latos and Finnerty. Executive producers include David Schuster of Gloves Up Entertainment, Steven Gregory, John Harms, Gerry Ambrose and Foxx’s daughter, Corinne Foxx. The film is presented by Gloves Up Entertainment in association with Echo Bend Productions.
In a joint statement, Foxx, Corinne Foxx and Marks praised Latos’s storytelling, citing his short film Leylak as the work that first drew their attention to the director.
Latos described East of the River as a combination of gritty family drama and crime thriller, exploring the dangerous consequences of being forced into desperate situations.
With post-production complete, the film is seeking a global distributor.

description: Investors pour money into launch providers  manufacturing and other infrastructure ventures
content:
Investors pour money into launch providers, manufacturing and other infrastructure ventures
Space startups attracted a record $20.8 ‌billion in funding in the third quarter, as investors poured money into launch providers, manufacturing and other infrastructure ventures, according to a report by global investment firm Seraphim.
The figure was nearly triple ​the $7.4 billion invested in the second quarter and more than double the ​prior peak. Excluding Blue Origin's $10 billion financing, investment was still at an ⁠all-time high of $10.8 billion, underscoring growing demand across the sector.
The report, released on Wednesday, ​also showed a record 216 deals were completed during the quarter, up from 140 ​in the second quarter.
While SpaceX remains a dominant force in the industry, recent fundraising has been supported by a growing pipeline of commercial orders and government-backed programs, according to Seraphim.
Read: Two Pakistani astronauts train for space mission
"Capital is following ​evidence of commercial and institutional demand, not just residual IPO enthusiasm," said Lucas Bishop, ​vice president at Seraphim Space.
Infrastructure-related businesses accounted for the bulk of the funding activity. Companies involved ‌in ⁠launch and broader space access attracted $16.4 billion across 120 deals, while satellite communications, Earth observation and other space-service companies raised $4 billion.
Defence and sovereign demand are increasingly supporting investment in launch, manufacturing and orbital infrastructure as governments prioritise domestic space capabilities, Bishop said.

The ​quarter's major fundraising rounds ​included $1.37 billion for ⁠Hadrian, $1 billion for Stoke Space and $500 million for K2 Space.
However, the surge in private investment was in contrast with weaker performance ​among listed space companies. Bishop said many publicly traded space firms ​remain loss-making, ⁠while SpaceX's scale and visibility may have drawn investor attention away from smaller listed peers.

North America accounted for about 70% of global funding year-to-date, while China recorded a quarterly ⁠high ​of $3.3 billion across 49 deals.
Seraphim said funding was likely ​to moderate from the third-quarter's exceptional level, but remain above historical norms as more companies enter growth and ​scale-up phases.

description: The film is poised to make a splash on the global festival circuit following backing from international funds
content:
The film is poised to make a splash on the global festival circuit following backing from international funds
Khadim Dai’s compelling documentary Hazara Town has been officially selected for the International Competition at the prestigious International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA). The film, which explores profound themes of displacement, family bonds, and survival, is poised to make a significant splash on the global festival circuit following substantial backing from international funds.
Hazara Town follows a Hazara family twenty years after fleeing Afghanistan, now residing in Pakistan where they face intensifying persecution.
As mounting pressures close in, the family is forced to confront a heart-wrenching dilemma: whether to stay together amidst growing hostility or embark on perilous journeys of migration, risking separation with the knowledge that they may never see one another again.
Directed by Khadim Dai and produced by Ilyas Yourish for Congoo alongside Graeme Isaac and Anke Petersen, the documentary blends intimate family moments with the broader, harrowing realities of persecution and uprooted lives.
Previously developed under the working title Life in the Shadows, the project has received extensive support from major industry entities including the Sundance Documentary Fund, the IDFA Bertha Fund, and the Close Up Initiative.
Festival programmers have highlighted Hazara Town as a standout inclusion in this year's competitive lineup, praising its delicate balance of personal narrative and urgent socio-political commentary.
As the documentary prepares for its upcoming premiere in Amsterdam, it stands out as a poignant and timely meditation on resilience, memory, and the immense human cost of borders and conflict.

title: Sally Rooney books pulled from UK sale following publisher agreement over Palestine Action support

content:
Rooney noted that fulfilling publication contracts in the UK could now constitute a criminal offence
Award-winning Irish author Sally Rooney's books will no longer be sold in the UK after her publisher Faber made the joint decision to withdraw her titles from the market. The move comes as a direct consequence of current UK legislation and Rooney's vocal public support for the direct-action protest group Palestine Action.
Faber explained in an official statement that existing legal frameworks in the UK have created circumstances where the publishing house cannot legally pass on UK earnings to the author for her work.
Describing the situation as unconscionable, the publisher stated that in full agreement with Rooney, they can no longer supply her works in the UK in any format, though they remain proud to continue selling her books in other international territories.
The controversy stems from Rooney's public backing of Palestine Action, which was proscribed as a terrorist organisation by the UK government last year following protests against British arms exports to Israel.
Last August, the Mayo-born author penned an opinion piece in the Irish Times declaring her intention to support the group and channel proceeds from her work towards their cause, noting that the organisation is not prohibited in the Republic of Ireland.
Addressing the withdrawal, Rooney noted that fulfilling publication contracts in the UK could now constitute a serious criminal offence given her stated intentions. Following careful consultation and deliberation alongside her publisher, she acknowledged that she is fully prepared to accept the consequences of her beliefs.
The decision follows her previous absence from the Sky Arts Awards last year, where she won the literature prize for her fourth novel, Intermezzo, but could not safely enter the UK to collect it without facing potential arrest.

content:
Halle Berry disputes Olivier Martinez’s abuse claims, saying a photo taken by their son shows no injuries in court
Halle Berry has denied allegations that she physically abused her 13-year-old son, Maceo, disputing her ex-husband Olivier Martinez’s claim that a photograph supports his accusations.
In a responsive declaration filed on Tuesday, October 13, Berry argued that the photograph, allegedly taken by Maceo on September 26, does not show evidence of the injuries Martinez has described. According to court documents obtained by PEOPLE , Berry said there was no image showing redness, bruising or marks on their son’s neck consistent with the allegations.
“The only photograph Olivier identifies is a photograph of Halle, standing calmly, with hands in her pocket, feet away from Maceo,” the declaration stated.
Martinez, 60, filed for sole custody of their son on October 1, alleging that Berry, also 60, physically abused Maceo during an incident on September 26. He also alleged other instances of abuse in recent years. Berry has denied the accusations and has said she is a victim of domestic violence herself.
In a subsequent filing on October 12, Martinez claimed Maceo took the photograph because he had been “roughed up” before and felt that no one believed him.
Berry also challenged Martinez’s account of her fiancé, Van Hunt, checking Maceo for injuries. She maintained that Hunt had only said he did not observe redness or bruising, rather than conducting a physical examination.
The custody dispute has also raised questions about whether Maceo should testify during upcoming hearings. Martinez argued that their son should be allowed to tell the court about the September incident and express his custody preferences.
Berry, however, alleged that Martinez had “coached and manipulated” their son and objected to his request for the teenager to testify.
Martinez’s lawyer, Patrick Baghdaserians, denied the manipulation allegations, describing Maceo as the primary victim and arguing that he should have the opportunity to testify.
The claims remain disputed as the former couple’s custody proceedings continue.

title: Reese Witherspoon is buying back Hello Sunshine five years after multi million pound sale
description: Hello Sunshine was founded by Witherspoon in 2016 with a dedicated mission to champion female driven stories
content:
Hello Sunshine was founded by Witherspoon in 2016 with a dedicated mission to champion female-driven stories
Reese Witherspoon is making a major power move in Hollywood by buying back her renowned media company, Hello Sunshine, five years after selling a controlling stake in a massive deal. The award-winning actress and producer has teamed up with French media company Mediawan to reacquire the production banner from Candle Media.
Hello Sunshine was originally founded by Witherspoon in 2016 with a dedicated mission to champion female-driven stories, launching acclaimed hits such as Big Little Lies, Little Fires Everywhere, and The Morning Show.
In 2021, the studio was sold to Candle Media, a Blackstone-backed enterprise, in a landmark transaction valued at approximately $900 million. While Witherspoon maintained an ownership stake and a leadership role following that initial sale, this latest agreement marks a complete return of control over her creative empire.
Describing the transition as a homecoming, Witherspoon expressed her enthusiasm for the new chapter alongside Mediawan. She noted that Pierre-Antoine Capton and his teams have built a global independent studio that firmly puts creators first, aligning perfectly with her original vision for the company.
She also took the opportunity to express deep gratitude to her early backers, Peter Chernin and Jesse Jacobs of The Chernin Group, as well as her recent partners at Blackstone and Candle Media for their unwavering support.
Industry insiders note that the buyback agreement was secured for a fraction of the company's previous valuation, falling into the low-to-mid eight-figure range. Following the acquisition, Hello Sunshine co-founder Seth Rodsky will join the leadership team as a director alongside Witherspoon and representatives from Mediawan.
With fresh backing and renewed independence, Witherspoon and her team are poised to steer the production house into a dynamic new era of storytelling.

title: You   re not alone  the truth will come out     Nobel winner Navi Pillay on global support for Palestinians
description: 2026 Nobel Peace Prize winner draws parallels with international action against apartheid in South Africa
content:
2026 Nobel Peace Prize winner draws parallels with international action against apartheid in South Africa
Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navi Pillay said Palestinians seeking justice are not alone, and the truth will emerge, urging the international community to draw lessons from the collective action and economic sanctions that helped end apartheid in her native South Africa.
In an exclusive interview on Wednesday, Pillay, judge at the International Court of Justice and a former UN human rights chief, reflected on her experience fighting apartheid and the importance of international support for Palestinians amid continuing concerns over accountability for violations in the Gaza Strip.
"I imagine I'm correct in saying that even though Palestinians are struggling for their freedom for more than 90 years now, attention by the international community and support by the international community would be of great significance for them," she told Anadolu .
"The message being, you're not alone. That with information and correct information, the truth will come out."
EXCLUSIVE – Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay on Gaza genocide, international law and accountability 🇵🇸 Message to Palestinians: Pillay says international support tells Palestinians that “you’re not alone” and the “truth will come out” ✊ Collective action: Pillay says… pic.twitter.com/sY2g81CTf7
Pillay, 85, who was awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize for her contributions to international justice, chaired a UN commission of inquiry, which concluded last year that Israel committed genocide in Gaza.
Recalling her experience under apartheid, she said South African lawyers fought a lonely struggle with little international attention. "We really had very little relief. And honestly, the rest of the world didn't pay attention to us," she said.
The rights lawyer said a UN commission gathering evidence and presenting its findings internationally would have greatly helped Black South Africans at that time.
Palestine needs same level of economic sanctions, collective action that helped end apartheid
Pillay stressed the importance of identifying the root causes of Palestinian suffering, and reiterated her commission's finding that Israel's unlawful occupation was the root cause of the longstanding conflict.
She criticised governments for increasingly prioritising their political and regional interests over their responsibilities to maintain international peace and justice.
She said the UN Security Council already possessed mechanisms to respond to violations, including peacekeeping operations, investigative commissions, mediation and economic sanctions.
"The principal tool they have is to impose sanctions, economic sanctions against governments that are violating international human rights law, international humanitarian law; they've used this before," she said.
Questioning the international community's response to Gaza, Pillay said: "So, the question that civil society is asking: 'Why are you sitting back and doing nothing in the face of huge violations that we, the people, can see daily? We can see genocide being committed on our television screens'."
"And I am as unhappy as most people that there has been so little action," she added.
Drawing on South Africa's experience, where apartheid ended in 1994, Pillay emphasised the decisive role of international economic pressure.
Read: Navi Pillay: Nobel laureate who led UN inquiry that found genocide in Gaza
"Apartheid came to an end mainly because of the economic sanctions imposed by the Security Council, by the United Nations against the apartheid government," she said.
"I never thought apartheid will end in my lifetime, but it's this collective action by governments, by businesses, and civil society all over the world that brought an end to apartheid."
Pillay said she had been hoping for similar international cooperation in response to the situation in Gaza.
"I've been hopefully looking for and calling for that level of cooperation, that level of condemnation of the huge violations and killings of Palestinians," she said.
Asked whether Israel's growing international isolation and sanctions targeting settlers in the occupied West Bank could help end its impunity, Pillay said such developments could contribute to broader collective action.
"The one thing we cannot accept is doing nothing," she said.
Recalling Nelson Mandela's position that South Africans could not fully enjoy freedom while Palestinians remained oppressed and occupied, she said Palestinians were seeking measures similar to those used against apartheid.
"Palestinians are calling for the kind of action that was taken to end apartheid. They see the value of economic boycotts," she said.
She also referred to protests by Israelis against efforts to weaken the country's Supreme Court, urging governments to respect civilians' right to protest and cooperate with international criminal investigations.
She stressed that international legal principles must be applied consistently, without selectivity or bias, particularly when civilians are suffering.
Pillay emphasised that governments, rather than international organisations alone, bear responsibility for preventing genocide.
"The Genocide Convention is very clear. The duty is on every state to prevent genocide," she said. "That's a purpose; it's not to react to genocide and to punish the alleged perpetrators. The main reason is to prevent, because it's an intolerable crime when a whole group is being destroyed in whole or in part."
About the potential legal responsibility of governments supplying weapons, intelligence or political support despite warnings of serious violations, Pillay said the states themselves established international conventions and treaties.
"They set the standards. Now they must implement them without selection," she said, arguing that governments were failing to apply their own commitments because of political interests.
Pillay recalled that her UN commission had urged the General Assembly to seek an advisory opinion from the International Court of Justice (ICJ) concerning Israel's occupation of Palestinian territory.
She welcomed the court's opinion in 2024, which found Israel's continued presence in the occupied Palestinian territory unlawful, and outlined obligations concerning Palestinian rights.
She, however, acknowledged that legal proceedings offered limited immediate relief to people suffering on the ground.
"I agree; they're not very helpful to relieve their immediate dire situation," she said. "Let's use international law to assert and realise the rights of people who are oppressed everywhere in the world."
On shortcomings of the international system and its eroding credibility, Pillay pointed to the dominance of governments within the UN and the shrinking space for civil society.
"Certainly, the system is very skewed. Who controls the United Nations? It's member states, it's governments," she said, urging UN members to conduct their affairs in closer cooperation with civil society organisations.
Global opposition to US sanctions on ICC a must
Turning to Washington's measures against the International Criminal Court (ICC), Pillay called on governments, including those outside the Rome Statute, to oppose the campaign.
"I would like to see states of the world, the member states, whether they're parties to the Rome Statute or not, to condemn the unlawful measures and sanctions that the United States is imposing on this court," she said.
Also Read: US imposes sweeping sanctions on ICC
"We should say roundly that it's unacceptable, and then we all have the responsibility to help the court to overcome these obstacles."
The former ICC judge expressed confidence that the court's staff would continue their work despite mounting political pressure.
"They're not going to stop doing what they are doing because they are working out of commitment. They believe that it is possible to realise justice for all," she said.
Reflecting on receiving the Nobel, Pillay described the recognition as unexpected and deeply meaningful. "This award was a huge surprise to me, but a wonderful surprise," she said.
She expressed gratitude that the Nobel Committee had recognised different aspects of her decades-long career, from challenging apartheid to advancing international justice.
"You don't win a case all the time. You win some. You lose many, especially under apartheid South Africa," she said.
Pillay described the committee's recognition of her work as a "memorable moment," saying she appreciated its efforts to examine her contributions to international peace and justice.

title: Trump fires ambassador to Greece Guilfoyle after reports of misconduct
description: News reports alleged Guilfoyle sold access    to Trump administration officials in exchange for money  gifts  favours
content:
News reports alleged Guilfoyle sold access ‌to Trump administration officials in exchange for money, gifts, favours
The White House said on Tuesday it ​had asked US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign after a series of news reports raised concerns that she sold access ‌to Trump administration officials in exchange for money, gifts and favours.
US President Donald Trump had said on Monday that he was considering firing Guilfoyle, who was once engaged to his son Donald Trump Jr. On Tuesday, he told reporters: "She was doing a good job, but we didn't like what we were reading."
President Trump says "he didn't like what he read" on Kimberly Guilfoyle resignation: "She wasn't a member of my family; she dated my son a long time ago." pic.twitter.com/Gs6Zz1cK8p
US lawmakers had raised the alarm after a series of stories ​in the Wall Street Journal beginning last month that detailed Guilfoyle's conduct, including claims she threatened to use US influence to undermine the ​Greek government.
Read : Kimberly Guilfoyle chosen by Trump as US Ambassador to Greece
New White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia confirmed Guilfoyle had been asked to resign, telling a briefing: "She has ⁠been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well."
The White House has asked Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign as U.S. ambassador to Greece, after The Wall Street Journal reported that she had solicited $100,000 from a Trump donor in the run-up to her confirmation hearing last year. 🔗 Read more: https://t.co/JzxVmmD2xc pic.twitter.com/Lrpbj0uO5H
In a post on X, Guilfoyle repeated denials of wrongdoing and said her gratitude and ​respect for Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio remained "unwavering".
"While my time as ambassador may be coming to an end, my commitment to President Trump, the ​America First movement, and the country I love will never end," she wrote. "These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity."
Serving as the United States Ambassador to Greece has been the honor of a lifetime. I will forever be grateful to President Donald J. Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio for entrusting me with the extraordinary privilege of representing the greatest country in the history of…
One of the reports published by the Journal described Guilfoyle's close relationship with a lobbyist for a Greek energy company and her promotion of that firm, while another cited audio recordings of ​Guilfoyle bragging about her ties to wealthy Greek businessmen as she sought an invitation to a Davos dinner honouring another of Trump's sons, Eric.
US businessman ​Eric Deters also told the newspaper that Guilfoyle, a former San Francisco prosecutor, had offered access to Trump administration officials for money, at one point asking him to pay ‌her $100,000 credit ⁠card bill. Britain's Daily Mail reported last week that the State Department's internal watchdog was looking into complaints of inappropriate behaviour from staff at the Athens embassy.
Read More : Kimberly Guilfoyle 'still very fond' of Donald Trump Jr. at inauguration event
The Greek government has not commented on the allegations involving her tenure as ambassador.
Neither the State Department nor Washington's embassy in Athens responded to requests for comment.
Greece has been an important NATO ally of the United States, offering key military facilities to safeguard security in the Eastern Mediterranean, and it leads an ​EU maritime mission to protect commercial ​shipping in the Red Sea.
During a ⁠visit to Athens last week, Rubio said Greece and the US were launching new counterterrorism information sharing between their law enforcement agencies.
Guilfoyle's tenure in Athens was high-profile from the start as she appeared on the cover of Vogue ​Greece and attended late-night parties with Greek celebrities.
She aggressively touted American interests, including signing deals for the import of ​US liquefied natural ⁠gas and drilling deals involving companies including Exxon Mobil .
But she also created diplomatic waves. In her first interview with local media after arriving last November, she said China should sell its 67% stake in the port of Piraeus, which has become a cornerstone of Beijing's Belt and Road Initiative. China’s ambassador to Greece, Fang Qiu, responded ⁠by accusing the ​US of having "an outdated and a harmful mentality" and "a hegemonic mindset".
Dimitris Mantzos, foreign affairs spokesperson ​for Greece’s opposition PASOK party, said Guilfoyle’s firing raised serious issues and unanswered questions. Would Greek officials demand an explanation, he said, or "content themselves with watching the country serve as a 'theatre'" for ​outside interests.

title: UK prosecutor tells jury Russell Brand a  sexual predator
description: Brand denies seven rape and assault charges involving six women  with prosecutors alleging manipulative behaviour
content:
Brand denies rape and assault charges involving six women, with prosecutors alleging manipulative behaviour
Comedian Russell Brand was a "sexual predator" who was "ruthless, calculated and manipulative" when targeting women for sex, a British prosecutor told a UK jury Wednesday at the start of his rape and sexual assault trial.
The one-time left-wing personality, 51, who shot to fame as a television and radio presenter, faces seven sexual offence charges involving six women. He denies all the alleged offences.
Prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones said the alleged offences took place between 1999 and 2009, when Brand's career was beginning to flourish.
Addressing the jury, she gave graphic details of accusations by women, saying the youngest was 21 at the time of the alleged offences.
They came forward to police after seeing media coverage about Brand in 2023 and after he was initially charged in 2025, the court heard.
Brand was "not deterred" when some of the women said no, she said, adding his desire for sexual contact was "indiscriminate and voracious".
He used charm and comic talents when he wanted something but would then be "demanding and entitled... childlike in his expectation that his every desire should be met," Karmy-Jones told the jury of eight men and four women.
"He was ruthless, calculated and manipulative, and the prosecution say -- a sexual predator," she added.
The identities of the women will not be revealed during the trial.
Brand, dressed in a dark suit, black-and-white striped shirt and long white tie, arrived for the start of the case at London's Southwark Crown Court in a black Mercedes-Benz van accompanied by his wife Laura.
In each woman's case, Brand responded to police with a prepared statement saying he did not remember the women and any sexual activity was consensual.
Karmy-Jones said Brand's acquaintances recalled him bragging that he wanted to "bed 5,000 women in his lifetime", adding, "you have to tell them what they need to hear".
It was a clear indication of "how manipulative the defendant could be," she said.
Brand has in recent years reinvented himself as a conservative and faith-based guru for millions of social media followers.
He has pleaded not guilty to all seven of the charges -- three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and one charge of indecent assault.
The first woman met Brand when he was performing at a Labour Party conference in Bournemouth in southern England in 1999.
She invited him to her hotel room where he pushed her onto the bed before raping her without using a condom, the prosecutor said.
Brand has denied seven charges of rape and sexual assault against six women between 1999 and 2009. PHOTO: AFP
One woman said Brand in 2001 tried to drag her into a toilet cubicle at MTV's office, but she resisted.
Another woman met Brand at a London bar in 2004 and said he grabbed her breasts and pulled her into a toilet cubicle, orally raping her, after telling her not to be a "spoilsport".
Yet another woman said Brand visited the radio station where she worked in 2004 or 2005, and kissed her "very aggressively" then grabbed her breasts and bottom.
One woman, who was 21 at the time, said she had consensual oral and then vaginal sex with Brand in 2009 at his house but he then forced her into anal sex without her consent "with full force" without a condom, the prosecutor said.
In the final charge, a woman employed by Channel 4 television said she was working with Brand in a record studio in 2009.
Members of his production team told her she must give him a massage and he then pressed his face into her groin.
The trial at London's Southwark Crown Court should last around six weeks but could stretch into December.
The trial is attracting intense media scrutiny, with numerous British outlets launching dedicated podcasts and US channels reporting from outside the court.
Born to working-class parents in Essex in eastern England, Brand launched a successful stand-up comedy career as a teenager.
He became a household name as a television presenter on MTV , Channel 4 and the BBC , also penning newspaper columns and two autobiographies.
He then made a foray into Hollywood, starring in several hit films, and was in a brief but high-profile marriage to US pop star Katy Perry.
Now remarried and living in Florida with his young family, he has gained a new following as an influencer, with six million subscribers on YouTube, 10.1 million on X and 4.9 million on Instagram.

title: Pakistan Hockey League 2027 launched
description: New league aims to attract investment and elevate standard of the national sport
content:
New league aims to attract investment and elevate standard of national sport
Pakistan on Wednesday launched Pakistan Hockey League (PHL) at a ceremony in Islamabad in a bid to revive the country’s national sport.
Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF) said that it is a joint initiative of the federation and Media Cast, designed to bring together international players, Pakistani talent, corporate sponsors and team owners under a professional competition structure.
Rana Mashhood Ahmed Khan, chairman of the Prime Minister's Youth Programme and chief guest at the launch ceremony, reaffirmed the government's commitment to supporting hockey's revival and encouraging investment in the sport.
He welcomed efforts to bring the government, private sector and hockey community together, expressing confidence that the league and other development initiatives would help restore Pakistan's standing in international hockey.
Khan said the government would continue to support initiatives aimed at developing the sport, nurturing young talent and creating new opportunities for Pakistani players.
PHF President Mohyuddin Ahmad Wani said the federation was committed to sustained reforms, investment and institutional development to strengthen the sport's foundations.
He said priorities included improving playing standards, upgrading infrastructure, attracting corporate investment, expanding facilities and providing players with better incentives and opportunities.
Wani stressed that restoring Pakistan hockey would require professional management, long-term planning and stronger partnerships between the government and private sector.
"Our commitment is to bring investment into hockey, improve infrastructure, provide better incentives for our players and create an environment in which Pakistan hockey can once again progress and succeed," he said.
Salman Danish, owner of Media Cast and a partner in the league, said the company would work with the PHF to organise the competition professionally, attract corporate partners and sponsors, and develop a sustainable commercial model for the sport.
Organisers said the league would seek to increase commercial interest in hockey, raise competitive standards and create sustainable investment opportunities. It is also intended to reconnect younger generations with Pakistan's rich hockey history and traditions.
Pakistan, a former powerhouse in international hockey, has struggled to maintain its position among the sport's leading nations. The league's success will depend on attracting investment, establishing a competitive structure and translating commercial interest into long-term development opportunities for players.

title: Jesse Williams reveals the impact of Harry Belafonte   s support on his career
description: Jesse Williams recalls Harry Belafonte s support after losing acting jobs over his activism against racial injustice
content:
Jesse Williams recalls Harry Belafonte's support after losing acting jobs over his activism against racial injustice
Grey’s Anatomy actor Jesse Williams has spoken about the support he received from late civil rights activist Harry Belafonte after facing professional setbacks over his activism against racism and inequality.
In the documentary Following Harry , Williams recalls how Belafonte helped him navigate a difficult period in his life and career. The film, directed by Susanne Rostock, examines the final 12 years of Belafonte’s life and his lasting influence on civil rights activism in the United States.
Williams, who received the BET Humanitarian Award in 2016, became widely recognised for his speech addressing racial inequality and systemic injustice. However, he says the speech also brought backlash, including threats against him and his family.
“I was offered movies and was told I had the role. And then a top-level executive said, ‘No, I don’t like his politics,’” Williams recalls in the documentary.
The actor said he later visited Belafonte at his home after receiving a message from the activist warning him about the potential backlash. Williams described the meeting as a source of comfort during a chaotic time in his life.
He said Belafonte made him feel “held” and that the support meant a great deal to him. Williams added that much of what he has done since has been shaped by that experience.
Belafonte, who died in 2023 at the age of 96, was known for both his entertainment career and his decades of civil rights work. His achievements included the landmark 1956 album Calypso and film roles in Carmen Jones and Spike Lee’s BlacKkKlansman . He also worked alongside prominent civil rights leaders, including Martin Luther King Jr.
Williams continued acting after the controversy, appearing in Grey’s Anatomy until 2025 and taking roles in Only Murders in the Building and The Morning Show . He also earned a Tony Award nomination for his Broadway performance in Take Me Out .

title: Saudi league postpones three matches after Houthi attacks
description: Al Hilal Al Riyadh and Al Ittihad Al Shabab are moved to December 19
content:
Al Hilal-Al Riyadh and Al Ittihad-Al Shabab are moved to December 19
The Saudi Arabian football league (SPL) has postponed three fixtures, including one involving Cristiano Ronaldo's Al Nassr, following the dramatic escalation in the country's war with the Houthis.
The matchweek nine fixtures have been pushed back in the calendar for "logistical considerations, taking into account the mandatory minimum rest period between matches", according to a statement published on Tuesday on the SPL's website.
The meeting between league leaders Al Hilal and Al Riyadh and the match between Al Ittihad and Al Shabab have been postponed to December 19, while the clash between Al Ahli and Ronaldo's Al Nassr has been rescheduled for March 6, 2027.
The SPL added, however, that the other matchweek nine fixtures "will be played according to the previously announced schedule with no changes".
On Monday, Al Nassr's AFC Champions League match against Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana in Riyadh was delayed by an hour after the coalition announced it had intercepted a missile fired by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital.
A violent battle between a Saudi-led coalition and Yemen's Houthis has erupted in recent days, with missile strikes on airports and energy facilities across the kingdom.
The latest round of fighting was triggered by Houthi strikes on Riyadh's international airport at the weekend that left 13 people dead and operations suspended in the worst attack since 2015.

description: Germany   s Anastasiya Kuparev and South Africa   s Wozuko Mdlulwa also secure singles victories
content:
Germany’s Anastasiya Kuparev and South Africa’s Wozuko Mdlulwa also secure singles victories
France’s Astrid Cirotte, Russia’s Ksenia Laskutova and Thailand’s Kamonwan Yodpetch advanced to the second round of the women’s singles at the Junaid Family Foundation World Tennis Women’s Championships in Islamabad.
Cirotte defeated Russia’s Julia Khramtsova 6-3, 6-1, while Laskutova beat Türkiye’s Serife Pelin Sari 6-1, 6-0. Yodpetch overcame Nepal’s Abhilasha Bista 6-1, 6-1 at the Pakistan Tennis Federation (PTF) Tennis Complex.
South Africa’s Wozuko Mdlulwa recovered from a set down to defeat South Korea’s Jeong Moon 3-6, 6-3, 6-0, while Germany’s Anastasiya Kuparev beat Russia’s Lilia Piskun 6-1, 6-0.

title: Michael Jackson   s Super Bowl legacy explored in upcoming documentary    Spectacle
description: The film will feature previously unseen footage of Jackson and his team  alongside the story behind the performance
content:
The film will feature previously unseen footage of Jackson and his team, alongside the story behind the performance
Michael Jackson’s landmark 1993 Super Bowl halftime performance is set to receive a documentary treatment, with Hulu and ESPN announcing a new film exploring how the singer changed the event’s entertainment legacy.
Titled Spectacle: Michael Jackson at the Super Bowl , the documentary is scheduled to premiere in February on Hulu and ESPN, according to Deadline , which reported the announcement on October 13.
The film will revisit Jackson’s appearance at Super Bowl XXVII at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, California, where the global superstar delivered a performance that helped reshape expectations for halftime entertainment.
Jackson opened the show by standing motionless on stage for around two minutes, building anticipation before launching into his set. The performance included songs such as “Billie Jean” and “Black or White”, alongside “We Are the World”, which featured more than 3,000 local children.
The documentary will examine the planning behind the show, Jackson’s preparation with his team and the performance’s lasting impact. It will also include previously unseen footage of the singer and those involved in bringing the production to life.
The performance followed a period when the NFL faced competition for halftime viewers. In 1992, the In Living Color television special reportedly drew millions of viewers away from the Super Bowl broadcast. Jackson’s appearance the following year helped establish the halftime show as a major television attraction in its own right.
According to the report, the 1993 event marked the first time the Super Bowl’s second half attracted a larger audience than the first, highlighting the impact of the musical performance on viewership.
Bao Nguyen will direct and produce the documentary. Skydance Sports is producing the project alongside Optimum Productions and NFL Films. Producers include Jesse Sisgold, Jon Weinbach and Lauren Gaffney for Skydance Sports, John Branca for Optimum Productions, and Amit Dey for Into the Deep End Films.
The documentary will explore how Jackson’s appearance helped establish the modern halftime show as a major pop culture event, with his performance continuing to influence the spectacle surrounding the annual championship game.

title: Hesson expects tough tri series test
description: Pakistan coach says his charges must maintain recent ODI progress
content:
Pakistan coach says his charges must maintain recent ODI progress
After wrapping up their three-match T20I series with a 2-1 victory over Sri Lanka at home, Pakistan face a tougher test in the ODI tri-series, featuring England and Sri Lanka, which will also be held on home soil.
The tri-series will be hosted by Rawalpindi and Lahore from October 18 to 31. The tournament will follow a double round-robin format, with the top two teams advancing to the final on October 31.
The first three matches will be played in Rawalpindi, while the remaining four, including the final, will be held at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium.
Nine players who recently featured in the T20I series against Sri Lanka are also part of Pakistan’s ODI squad. Shaheen Shah Afridi will lead the side, which also includes Babar Azam and Salman Ali Agha.
England are among the world’s leading teams, while Sri Lanka have gained some momentum after beating Pakistan in the third T20I on Tuesday night in Rawalpindi, denying the hosts a series whitewash.
Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson also expects a tough challenge in the tri-series.
He said Pakistan had made considerable progress in ODIs over the past six months and would need to maintain that momentum against two competitive opponents.
“Well, look, a different group of players. You know, some slightly more experience in certain areas. But look, I'm excited,” Hesson told reporters after Pakistan lost the third T20I to Sri Lanka on Tuesday night.
“I mean, our one-day side made some good progress in the last six months. We've got to continue that. And certainly against the Sri Lankan side, who, you know, would have got some confidence tonight, and obviously an England side who's currently number one in the world. So it's going to be a tough tri-series, one we're looking forward to,” Hesson said.
Pakistan have enjoyed some success in ODIs over the past year.
In November 2025, they swept Sri Lanka 3-0 at home and defeated South Africa 2-1 in another home series. In March 2026, Pakistan lost 2-1 to Bangladesh in an away series. They bounced back in May-June 2026, beating Australia 2-1 at home.
England, meanwhile, have won their last three ODI series, against Sri Lanka and India at home and Sri Lanka away.
Sri Lanka have struggled in recent months, losing three of their last four series.
Pakistan’s ODI squad was expected to assemble in Islamabad on Wednesday ahead of the important assignment.
Attention will also be on fast bowler Razaullah and how he performs in the tri-series if given an opportunity. He featured in two T20Is against Sri Lanka but will need to improve his discipline and consistency.
Hesson said the coaching staff would work with the young fast bowler to help him develop his skills.
“I think, you know, when I think of Pakistan cricket, I think of pace and I think of unusual actions,” Hesson said.
“And, you know, he's fresh, and he's raw, but he's got genuine pace. And even Kusal Mendis, who plays pace well, got done for pace on a few occasions.”
“So, look, he will get better with opportunity. And we have to work with him, and, you know, we've got Shaun Tait now, a chance for someone with, obviously a similar action to be able to work with him and, you know, get good at being able to change his lengths and trust when to bowl his bouncer and when to bowl his yorker. But it's exciting. So we'll see some more of him over the next few months, that's for sure.” Hesson said.
Pakistan ODI squad: Shaheen Shah Afridi (captain), Abrar Ahmed, Salman Ali Agha, Arafat Minhas, Babar Azam, Faheem Ashraf, Fakhar Zaman, Muhammad Ghazi Ghori (wk), Haris Rauf, Hasan Nawaz, Naseem Shah, Razaullah, Saad Baig (wk), Saim Ayub, Shadab Khan and Sufiyan Moqim.
