title: Fact check  Saudi Arabia has not busted any assassination plot involving crown prince  alleged royal family member
description: No such incident has occurred  alleged royal family member does not exist
content:
No such incident has occurred, alleged royal family member does not exist
Several users, the majority of whom appear to be pro-Yemeni accounts based on their past posts, have been sharing an image of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and an alleged royal family member on social media platforms X and Facebook since October 12, 2026, claiming that Saudi authorities busted an assassination plot involving them. However, nothing of the sort has occurred.
Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis are at war again. The latest Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia came amid a renewed escalation in the conflict in Yemen. Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s internationally recognised government launched a military campaign to push Houthi forces away from the strategically important Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key maritime route connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.
The Houthis responded with missile and drone attacks targeting Saudi territory, including airports, military installations and oil infrastructure. The renewed fighting has intensified after years of intermittent conflict and a period of relative calm following a truce in 2022.
On October 8, Yemen’s Houthi movement claimed that it had launched a ballistic missile towards King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, saying it had struck its intended target and disrupted air traffic. Saudi Arabia’s Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles, including two heading towards Riyadh and another directed towards Khamis Mushait. Subsequent attacks on Saudi airports have killed civilians.
On Oct 12, a user who appears to share anti-Saudi content based on their past posts shared an image on X, claiming that it shows an alleged assassin and a royal family member of the crown prince.
The caption of the post said: “Attempted coup inside led by Sheikh Mubarak bin Nuwaf Al-Duaisi Al Saud. It appears there are deep and significant disagreements within the ruling family that may lead to the assassination of bin Salman and end his rule.”
Another user shared the same visuals with the following caption: “Urgent! Right now in Saudi Arabia. Saudi intelligence announces the arrest of the owner of His Highness the Amir Mubarak bin Nawaf Al-Duaisi Al Saud and a number of officers and affiliates following an attempt to assassinate His Highness the Amir Mohammed bin Salman. And thus a military coup attempt that was supported by the Houthis has failed.”
The same visuals were shared by another user, accumulating 1m views.
A pro-Yemeni account, based on its past posts, shared the same image with a similar caption, gaining 290,400 views.
The image with a similar claim was further shared by several other users on social media platforms Facebook and X, as can be seen here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , and here ; collectively accumulating 108,300 views.
A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to its high virality and keen public interest in developments related to Saudi Arabia amid the conflict in the Middle East.
A keyword search was conducted to verify whether any credible Saudi or international media outlets had reported any alleged assassination attempt or the involvement of any such royal family member. However, no credible reports confirming the incident were found.
Further keyword searches for “Amir Mubarak bin Nawaf Al-Duaysi Al Saud” in both English and Arabic yielded no results on any such individual in the Saudi royal family.
A reverse image search was subsequently conducted to trace the origin of the face shown in the viral image and led to the account of Iraqi YouTuber Ali Adel , who has no known connection to the Saudi royal family.
The image was then examined using Google Gemini’s SynthID detector, which identified a digital watermark indicating that the image had been generated or edited using Google AI.
A comparison of the circulated portrait and a screenshot of Adel taken from one of his YouTube videos was subsequently conducted using Quantilence, an AI-based facial-similarity analysis tool. The tool found a 93.7 per cent facial similarity between the two images, further supporting the finding that the portrait uses Adel’s picture rather than depicting a member of the Saudi royal family.
The image was also analysed using AI detection tools and Sightengine flagged the image as 73 per cent AI-generated.
Similarly, another AI detection tool, TruthScan, flagged the image as 99pc AI-generated.
Undetectable AI also flagged the image as 99pc AI-generated.
Further keyword searches revealed that the same claim had circulated on social media in March 2026 , without any evidence at that time as well.
The viral claim of Saudi authorities busting an assassination plot involving the crown prince and an alleged royal family member is false .
No such incident has occurred, and the alleged royal family member does not exist.

title: Pakistan  Russia pledge to deepen security cooperation
description: Underscore the importance of closer institutional linkages and improved coordination between the security institutions
content:
Underscore the importance of closer institutional linkages and improved coordination between the security institutions
Pakistan reaffirmed its resolve to deepen longstanding relations with Russia and expand practical cooperation in areas of mutual interest, particularly security, as Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff (COAS) Field Marshal Asim Munir met Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev on Wednesday.
According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the meeting at General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi focused on matters of mutual interest and the regional security environment, with particular emphasis on strengthening bilateral security cooperation.
“They underscored the importance of closer institutional linkages and improved coordination between the security institutions of Pakistan and Russia,” the statement outlined further.
Read: Pakistan, Russia agree to sign MoU to combat organised crime, finalise prisoner transfer agreement
CDF Munir reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening its longstanding ties with Moscow and translating bilateral relations into tangible cooperation in areas of shared interest, particularly in the security domain.
The Russian interior minister, meanwhile, appreciated Pakistan’s contributions to regional peace and stability and acknowledged the professionalism and sacrifices of the Pakistan Armed Forces in the fight against terrorism. CDF Munir’s meeting with Minister Kolokoltsev comes amid expanding Pakistan–Russia engagement on counterterrorism, law enforcement, military training and broader bilateral relations.
In February, Russian President Vladimir Putin reaffirmed Moscow’s readiness to strengthen counterterrorism cooperation with Pakistan following a suicide attack on an Islamabad imambargah that killed at least 31 people. In letters of condolence to President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Putin expressed solidarity with Pakistan and reiterated Russia’s willingness to work with Islamabad in combating terrorism.
Then, in May, Pakistani and Russian officials held the 16th meeting of the Russia-Pakistan Consultative Group on Strategic Stability in Moscow, where they discussed international security, global stability, arms control, disarmament and non-proliferation. The Foreign Office said both sides found their approaches “aligned” on most of the issues discussed and agreed to continue coordination at relevant international forums. The next meeting was scheduled to take place in Islamabad in 2027.
A month after that, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Kolokoltsev, signed agreements to enhance cooperation on illegal immigration, the repatriation of illegally residing citizens and counter-narcotics efforts. Their discussions also highlighted regional security concerns linked to terrorist camps and drug production in Afghanistan. The agreements provided a practical framework for expanding cooperation between the two countries’ interior ministries and law enforcement agencies.
Read more: Russian interior minister arrives in Pakistan on maiden visit
On August 18, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met Russian Ambassador to Pakistan Albert Khorev in Islamabad and welcomed what he described as positive momentum in bilateral relations. Dar stressed the need for continued collaboration in key areas and sustained high-level exchanges to further strengthen ties.
Towards the end of September, the Pakistan Army and Russian Army participated in the ninth edition of their joint military exercise , Druzhba-IX, at Cherat and the National Counter Terrorism Centre in Pabbi. The two-week exercise focused on sharing operational experience, refining counterterrorism drills and procedures, and enhancing interoperability between the forces.
Finally, a couple of days ago, Kolokoltsev arrived in Pakistan on a four-day visit at the invitation of Naqvi, marking the first visit to Pakistan by a Russian interior minister.

title: Regulator expects Man City appeal to be heard by January
description: Premier League giants face more than 100 charges of financial rules
content:
Premier League giants face more than 100 charges of financial rules
The chair of English football's Independent Regulator has said he expects Manchester City's appeal after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules to be heard by January.
City, who have repeatedly maintained they are innocent of the charges, are currently top of the Premier League table with six wins out of six following their 3-0 defeat of Liverpool last weekend.
No sanction has yet been announced, but City could face a heavy points deduction leading to relegation and there is even been speculation they could be stripped of the three Premier League titles they won between 2009 and 2018.
"The Premier League have said that they want to get this resolved within season, and actually, of course, it's not the Premier League, it's an independent commission that's actually going to hear this, made of three retired either judges or lawyers," Independent Football Regulator (IFR) chair David Kogan told Times Radio on Wednesday.
"My understanding is that there is a prescribed process, which is 12 weeks, and so people are assuming this will actually be heard by the middle or the end of January.
"But as I say, it's not our proces, it's that of the Premier League's independent commission. What I don't think we can do is take any judgment until we're quite clear."
Kogan said Tuesday he would resign if there was political interference in any future IFR investigations of City.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham was criticised for his comments saying he would be "really concerned" if City's Abu Dhabi owners left the club following the verdict.
Downing Street subsequently had to backtrack, insisting no one was "above the rules".
Burnham, who was mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 to June 2026, has since published all of his dealings with the City hierarchy.
"We've had absolutely no interference from anybody since we created the regulator a year ago," Kogan said.
"We cannot, when regulating football, be subject to political interference on decisions we make about owners, directors or anything else."
He added: "And I won't actually be prepared to run an organisation which is subject to that degree of interference."
Manchester City manger Enzo Maresca said last week he "completely trusts" the club and believes it will win its appeal.

title: Mia Goth slams Instagram over fake AI selfie following Shia LaBeouf divorce filing
description: Meta said the account was removed for impersonating a public figure after complaints from Goth   s team
content:
Meta said the account was removed for impersonating a public figure after complaints from Goth’s team
Mia Goth’s representatives have criticised Instagram after an AI altered image falsely presented as a selfie of the actress circulated online shortly after news emerged of her divorce filing from Shia LaBeouf.
The image appeared on an account using the name miagoth_ and showed a person resembling Goth wearing a shirt bearing the message “MY EX IS MY BIGGEST FAN”. The post attracted attention from social media users and several news outlets, which initially treated it as a genuine image of the actress.
However, Goth does not have any social media accounts, according to her spokesperson, Christine Tripicchio. Her team filed multiple complaints with Instagram over the account’s repeated publication of images described as counterfeit and manipulated.
In a statement reported by Variety on October 14, Tripicchio questioned how the account had obtained a blue verification badge despite posting content that could mislead users about Goth’s identity.
She said it was “incomprehensible” that Instagram appeared to prioritise the circulation of manipulated images over protecting the integrity of a public figure’s likeness.
A spokesperson for Meta, Instagram’s parent company, confirmed that the account had been removed for impersonating a public figure. The profile had been labelled as a fan account, but its verification badge and reported following of approximately one million users raised concerns about potential confusion.
The incident has renewed discussion about the risks posed by AI generated images and the challenges of distinguishing authentic celebrity posts from manipulated content. Meta permits certain AI generated depictions of real people under its policies, while using labels and other measures to identify some altered material.
Goth’s representatives have not indicated that the actress created or endorsed the image.
The controversy emerged after reports that Goth had filed for divorce from LaBeouf in Los Angeles on October 6, citing irreconcilable differences and listing July 28, 2025, as their separation date.
The couple, who share a daughter, have had a relationship marked by periods of separation and reconciliation.

title: Arafat urges better powerplay batting
description: Pakistan   s all rounder says stronger partnerships can help boost T20 totals
content:
Pakistan’s all-rounder says stronger partnerships can help boost T20 totals
Pakistan’s emerging all-rounder Arafat Minhas has said that Green-shirts need to make better use of the powerplay and build early partnerships to post bigger totals in T20 cricket.
Reflecting on Pakistan’s batting approach, Arafat said the team had failed to capitalise on the opening overs as effectively as in previous matches.
“I think we didn’t capitalise on the powerplay like in previous games. We could have built partnerships early on in the innings; the total would have been 200 or 200 plus if we had a couple of partnerships,” he said.
Sri Lanka on Tuesday denied Pakistan whitewash when the visitors crushed the hosts by eight wickets in a one-sided game in Pindi.
Arafat explained that when he came to the crease, the captain was already settled, and the pair discussed building a partnership. He said Sahibzada Farhan guided him throughout the innings and he tried to give him as much of the strike as possible before taking the initiative himself.
“However, when I got set, I seized the opportunity and charged against the bowlers,” he added.
He also highlighted the growing importance of adapting to changes of pace in modern T20 cricket, saying teams needed to prepare for bowlers who increasingly rely on variations.
“Wherever you play T20 cricket, changes of pace and variations are now becoming common; I think we have to practise accordingly,” he said.
Explaining his bowling approach, Minhas said he focused on maintaining accurate lines and lengths to restrict the flow of runs and create wicket-taking opportunities.
“As a spinner, I tried to bowl in good areas and contain the run flow; that helped me create those wicket-taking chances,” he said.
Minhas also praised the support of the home crowd at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium, where he made his international debut, describing the atmosphere as a major advantage.
“It is always good to play in front of the home crowd. I made my debut at this venue. It is a huge advantage having fans’ support,” he said, adding that he particularly enjoyed playing at the Rawalpindi venue.
He said Pakistan’s 2-1 series victory was a collective effort that had boosted the team’s confidence, while the quality of cricket throughout the series had also been encouraging.
“The way we won the series 2-1, it was a team effort and gave us confidence; the level of cricket was also good,” he said.

Pakistan squash legend Jahangir Khan is optimistic that the country can regain its lost standing in the sport, saying regular international and domestic tournaments help nurture emerging players and improve their competitiveness.

Jahangir said the continued organisation of such events would not only support the sport’s development but also help improve Pakistan’s image internationally.
The participation of established foreign players in tournaments held in Pakistan was also boosting the confidence of local competitors and motivating them to improve their performances, he added.
Jahangir further praised McDonald’s Pakistan for supporting sports, particularly squash, and urged other corporate organisations to contribute to the development of the game.

title: Monfils officially retired from tennis
description: ITIA confirms that the French seed has been on their retired players list since October 5
content:
ITIA confirms that the French seed has been on their retired players list since October 5
Gael Monfils, the last of his generation's French musketeers, has officially retired from tennis, the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) confirmed to AFP on Wednesday.
The 40-year-old had signalled his intention to leave the sport at the end of 2026 but received a wildcard for an ATP 250 event in Lyon and was widely expected to make a farewell appearance at the Paris Masters at Bercy at the start of November.
The ITIA, however, confirmed that Monfils has been on their retired players list since October 5, ruling him out of any tournaments for the next six months.
Under the rules of the body responsible for anti-doping in tennis, players on this list must make themselves available for random doping tests for at least six months before they are allowed to return to competition.
The former world No. 6 played his last official match in early September when he lost to Learner Tien in the second round of the US Open.
His first round win over Adolfo Daniel Vallejo at Flushing Meadow made him just the third man aged 40 or over to win a match at the New York slam in the Open era after Ken Rosewall in 1977 and Jimmy Connors in 1992.
He had earlier reached the semi-finals of the mixed doubles with his wife Elina Svitolina.
Although Monfils, winner of 13 ATP titles, had not yet made any public statement on Wednesday morning, his retirement marks the end of an era for French tennis.
After the retirements of Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, Gilles Simon and Richard Gasquet, "La Monf" is the last of the four "musketeers" of his generation to hang up his racquet.
But unlike his contemporaries, all of whom now hold positions connected to tennis, the current world No. 254 had stated in September his intention to move into the world of finance and become a wealth manager for a Swiss company.
Having turned professional in 2004, the right-hander reached the semi-finals of the French Open in 2008 and US Open in 2016, and also made it to three Masters 1000 finals.
A spectacular player admired admired the world, Monfils produced his final tour de force at the start of the 2025 season.
By winning the Auckland tournament at the age of 38, he became the oldest player to win a title on the main tour since 1977, a record since broken by Novak Djokovic.
He went on to reach the round of 16 at the Australian Open, notably defeating world No. 4 Taylor Fritz along the way.

title: Fact check  Viral K P Home Department notification ordering arrests of PTI workers is fake
description: The purported notification is fake and AI generated
content:
The purported notification is fake and AI-generated
Several people, the majority of whom appear to be Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) supporters based on their past posts, have been sharing an alleged notification on social media platforms since October 13, 2026, from the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Home Department ordering the identification and arrest of PTI workers across the province. However, the notification is AI-generated.
The federal government imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in K-P on October 11 following the president’s approval of the recommendations by the federal cabinet. The measures were approved under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution.
The decision came during an emergency meeting of the federal cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, where he was briefed on the security situation in K-P. Cabinet members reviewed the situation and took note of the “provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”, according to the Prime Minister’s Office.
Read : Govt was left with 'no option' but emergency, governor rule: PM Shehbaz
A couple of hours after the imposition of emergency was announced, K-P Information Minister Shafi Jan, who had been accompanying now-dysfunctional K-P chief minister Sohail Afridi on PTI’s long march, claimed that Afridi had been taken into custody.
Later, PTI issued a statement condemning the “arrest” of Afridi and others, describing it as an act of “political victimisation and an attempt to weaken the province’s elected leadership and democratic institutions”.
Communication and internet services have also been disrupted in the province. Several PTI leaders and workers were also arrested in the lead-up to the imposition of governor’s rule.
On October 13, YouTuber and self-described journalist Measum Abbas shared a post on X containing a purported notification from the K-P Home Department.
The document bore the name and alleged signature of the additional chief secretary of the province’s Home Department. Its subject read: “Arrest of PTI workers – submission of names from your respective areas.”
It directed deputy commissioners across K-P to identify, verify and arrest PTI workers and submit their names, addresses, CNIC numbers and other details within seven days.
Another X account that appeared to support PTI, based on its past posts, shared the same notification with the following caption: “Order to arrest PTI workers, notification issued.”
Another apparent PTI supporter shared the same image with the following caption: “A display of shamelessness and lack of honour. They’ve made an illegitimate grab in the name of counter-terrorism, and instead of targeting the terrorists, these shameless people are demanding names to crack down on PTI.”
Other pro-PTI accounts on X also shared the same notification, as can be seen here , here , here , here , here and here ; collectively gaining 14,000 views.
A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to its virality and keen public interest in the arrest of PTI workers in K-P following up to and after the implementation of governor’s rule.
A keyword search was conducted to verify whether any credible Pakistani or local news outlets had reported on the alleged K-P Home Department notification ordering the arrest of PTI workers across the province, but nothing was found to corroborate it.
While news reports were plenty about PTI supporters being detained and arrested, none mentioned any such order from the K-P Home Department.
A visual and textual examination of the alleged document revealed discrepancies in its letterhead, which names the issuing authority as “Government of Pakistan, Home Department, Province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.”
Whereas the official X account of the Home & Tribal Affairs Department, Government of K-P, shared a notification on April 6, 2023, along with an authentic letter , which identifies the issuing authority as “Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Home & Tribal Affairs Department.”
The viral notification features Pakistan’s national emblem at the top, whereas the authentic notification carries the provincial government’s emblem.
Furthermore, the alleged notification identified Muhammad Iqbal Khan as the additional chief secretary of the Home Department. However, a keyword search yielded an Oct 13, 2026, Dawn news report titled “Massive reshuffle in K-P bureaucracy under governor’s rule”, which said Amjad Ali Khan, the industries secretary, was transferred and posted as the home and tribal affairs secretary.
Other reports by Dawn and The Express Tribune also identified him as the additional chief secretary, instead of any Muhammad Iqbal Khan.
The notification image was subsequently analysed using OpenAI’s tool to detect the SynthID watermark, which identified a SynthID signal, indicating that the image was likely generated or edited using OpenAI tools.
SynthID works by embedding an invisible digital watermark directly into AI-generated media content. Unlike normal metadata, the watermark forms part of the content itself and is designed to remain detectable even after the media is doctored, such as cropping, applying filters or lossy compression.
The image was also analysed using other AI-detection tools. Undetectable AI flagged the visual as 99 per cent doctored, while Fake Image Detector flagged it as 71pc AI-generated.
Meanwhile, Truthscan flagged the image as 99pc AI-generated, and Sightengine labelled it as 72pc doctored.
iVerify also reached out to Express Tribune K-P bureau chief Shahid Hamid, who confirmed that the Home Department had been contacted to verify the alleged notification and that it was found to be fake.
Furthermore, Dawn correspondent Zahid Imdad said that a deputy inspector general of police posted in K-P had also confirmed the notification was fake and that nothing of the sort had been issued.
The official fact-check account of the K-P government also issued a statement on X dated Oct 13, 2026, saying the viral notification was fake.
The statement read, “A fake notification is currently being circulated on social media, falsely claiming that the K-P Home Department has directed the identification and arrest of PTI workers across the province.”
فیکٹ چیک ✅ فیک نیوز الرٹ‼️ سوشل میڈیا پر خیبر پختونخوا کے محکمہ داخلہ کی جانب سے پی ٹی آئی کارکنوں کی شناخت، فہرستوں کی تیاری اور گرفتاریوں سے متعلق ایک جعلی نوٹیفکیشن گردش کر رہا ہے۔ یہ جعلی نوٹیفکیشن عوام میں گمراہ کن تاثر پیدا کرنے کی کوشش ہے۔ نوٹیفکیشن پر درج چیف… pic.twitter.com/tSMPYbx5YB
It continued, “The fabricated notification also bears the fake name of the chief secretary/official signatory, misleading the public and creating a false impression of politically motivated state action. The public is advised to verify official notifications through authentic government channels and refrain from sharing unverified information.”
The claim that a viral notification from the K-P Home Department ordered the identification and arrest of PTI workers across the province is false .
The notification is fake and AI-generated.

title: Selma Blair   s past biting encounters with celebrities resurface after alleged in flight assault
description: In her 2022 memoir  Blair said feeling overwhelmed in social situations sometimes led to impulsive behaviour
content:
In her 2022 memoir, Blair said feeling overwhelmed in social situations sometimes led to impulsive behaviour
Selma Blair’s past encounters with Sienna Miller, Seth MacFarlane and Kate Moss have resurfaced following reports that the actress was arrested after an alleged incident aboard a flight on October 11.
In her 2022 memoir, Mean Baby: A Memoir of Growing Up , Blair described biting the three celebrities during separate social encounters years earlier. She wrote that feeling overwhelmed in public could leave her struggling to respond appropriately in social situations.
According to Page Six , Blair recalled meeting Miller at the Chateau Marmont in 2006 and biting her arm after introducing herself. Blair described the action as playful at first but said she immediately regretted it. She praised Miller for initially responding with laughter rather than shaming her.
Blair also recounted biting MacFarlane on the hand at a Las Vegas gathering in 2004. She wrote that she had felt starstruck after meeting the Family Guy creator and acted impulsively. MacFarlane reportedly exclaimed that the bite hurt, although Blair said it did not break the skin.
Her memoir describes another encounter with supermodel Moss in a London hotel suite after a Marc Jacobs fashion show. Blair recalled biting Moss’s finger while they were taking Polaroid photographs. Moss initially laughed, but reportedly reacted differently when Blair repeated the action.
The stories have attracted renewed attention because of a reported incident involving Blair on a Delta Air Lines flight bound for John F Kennedy International Airport. She was arrested after allegedly biting a flight attendant and assaulting another person on board.
Reports also allege that Blair kicked a Port Authority police officer while being transported by ambulance and later assaulted a nurse at a hospital. The FBI is reportedly investigating the incident.
Blair’s representative said the actress experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct. The representative added that she received immediate medical attention after landing and was in stable condition.
The reported allegations remain distinct from the incidents described in Blair’s memoir, which she published four years earlier.

title: Air India flight diverted after suspected hijack alert  bomb threat  report
description: Flight AI 2030 lands at Jaipur International Airport  all passengers safely disembark  Indian media reports
content:
Flight AI-2030 lands at Jaipur International Airport, all passengers safely disembark, Indian media reports
An Air India flight en route to New Delhi from Frankfurt, Germany, was diverted to India's northwestern Jaipur city on Wednesday following a suspected hijack alert and an alleged bomb threat, according to media reports.
Flight AI-2030 landed safely at Jaipur International Airport at 9.35 am (0405GMT) and was moved to an isolation bay for security checks, while authorities investigate the incident, India Today reported, citing sources.
Initial checks found that the aircraft's operations were normal, the report said.
According to preliminary information, Ahmedabad Air Traffic Control received an emergency signal from the aircraft for a few seconds around 9 am (0330GMT).
The pilot reportedly activated Squawk 7500, an internationally recognised transponder code used to discreetly alert air traffic control to a hijacking or unlawful interference with an aircraft.
Airport management said all passengers aboard the aircraft were safe and being deboarded, adding that the situation was normal.
The emergency landing occurred after a bomb threat, Hindustan Times reported, citing police sources.
The incident follows a separate attempted hijacking on a flydubai flight on September 30, where the hijacker planned to hijack a passenger aircraft bound for Tel Aviv and crash it into a terminal at Israel's Ben Gurion Airport.
Read: UAE attorney general orders investigation into Flydubai flight incident
On Wednesday, FZ1073, carrying 174 passengers from Dubai to Tel Aviv, made an emergency landing at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport in the northwestern Saudi city of Tabuk after an altercation was reported in the cockpit.
Flydubai said “an altercation occurred in the flight deck,” adding that crew members aboard the aircraft secured the plane and diverted it safely to Saudi Arabia.
Airport officials said both the captain and first officer were injured and taken to a hospital following the incident. All passengers and crew were reported safe and accounted for.
Saudi Arabia’s National Transport Safety Centre later said its safety investigation team had begun work on the incident and was coordinating with relevant authorities to determine the circumstances, examine aviation safety aspects and collect related information and evidence.
The airport said the passengers later departed Tabuk aboard an alternative aircraft provided by Flydubai.

The charges relate to an alleged incident on July 27, with a warrant issued in September
Social media personality Bryce Hall has been charged with felony coercion involving domestic violence and misdemeanour domestic battery following an alleged incident in Las Vegas, according to court records reported by TMZ on October 13.
Hall’s representative has denied the allegations, saying the claims are false and that legal action may be taken against those responsible for spreading them.
According to the report, the alleged incident occurred on July 27. Charges were filed on August 28, and a judge issued an arrest warrant on September 10. Hall was arrested in September and subsequently released from custody without posting bail, court records cited by TMZ indicate.
The case involves Hall’s former partner, Maria Palafox, who is known online as Mika Lafuente. A judge reportedly ordered Hall to stay away from the alleged victim. The allegations have not been established in court, and Hall’s representative has publicly disputed them.
“These allegations are false, and we look forward to the facts coming out in court,” the representative told. The statement also said Hall’s team would pursue legal action over what it described as false and defamatory claims.
The arrest report also revisited the couple’s split. Two days before the alleged incident, Hall reportedly posted a video announcing their separation. He described the breakup as difficult and wished Lafuente well.
The legal case marks a serious development for Hall, who built a large online following through social media videos and later pursued boxing and entertainment projects. He has also been associated with influencer boxing events, including appearances connected to the wider scene surrounding Jake Paul.
Details about the allegations remain limited in the publicly reported account. The charges represent accusations, not proof of guilt, and Hall is entitled to contest them through the legal process.
Hall was scheduled to appear in court on October 13. Any further developments, including court decisions or additional statements from either side, could clarify the status of the case.

title: Kelly Clarkson   s interaction with Brooklyn store owner revealed in new security footage
description: Clarkson  44  is seen browsing the shop before examining a mechanical bird automaton known as Molly
content:
Clarkson, 44, is seen browsing the shop before examining a mechanical bird automaton known as Molly
New security footage has emerged showing Kelly Clarkson interacting with employees at a Brooklyn store after the singer accused a staff member of treating her as though she could not afford to shop there.
The footage, obtained by journalist Pablo Torre and shared on his podcast Pablo Torre Finds Out on Tuesday, October 13, captures Clarkson’s visit to Art of Play, a speciality shop in Brooklyn, New York. The clip lasts four minutes and 50 seconds and has no audio, meaning the conversation between the singer and the staff cannot be heard.
Clarkson, 44, is seen browsing the shop before examining a mechanical bird automaton known as Molly. She then speaks briefly with an employee identified by Torre as one of the store’s owners. After their interaction, the employee gestures towards another area of the shop while Clarkson continues looking at other items.
The Stronger singer later walks towards the exit before turning back to address another employee at the front of the store. She appears to gesture animatedly during the exchange before leaving. The footage also shows her taking out her phone as she exits.
The video surfaced days after Clarkson publicly criticised the shop on X on October 10. In her post, she said she had travelled to Brooklyn intending to buy several items but felt she had been judged by a staff member who allegedly assumed she could not afford something she wanted.
“Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a huge sale,” Clarkson wrote, comparing the experience to the treatment Julia Roberts’ character receives in the 1990 romantic comedy Pretty Woman .
The dispute centres on Molly, a singing and dancing bird automaton displayed inside Art of Play. Clarkson appeared interested in purchasing the piece, but the shop’s owners subsequently explained that the bird was permanently attached to the wall and was not for sale.
In a statement shared on Instagram, the store said the artist who created Molly, Bliss Kolb, owned an almost identical automaton in Seattle and was willing to sell that piece for $15,000. The owners also said they offered Clarkson a different mechanical bird for $2,000, but claimed she left before viewing it.
Clarkson pushed back against the store’s explanation, sharing an image of a $15,000 price tag for the bird on her Instagram Stories. The store later said the price had been raised to $15 million following the attention surrounding the incident.
Art of Play co-owner Adam Rubin also said the business had received a wave of hostile messages and threats following Clarkson’s post. The dispute has drawn widespread attention online, with the store defending its employees and Clarkson standing by her account of the interaction.
A source previously told PEOPLE that Clarkson rarely makes private grievances public, adding that the singer was sufficiently upset by the experience to speak out.
The newly released footage offers a visual record of the encounter, but the lack of audio means it does not establish precisely what was said between Clarkson and the employees. The disagreement over how the interaction unfolded remains at the centre of the controversy.

title: President Zardari receives credentials of French  Saudi ambassadors designate
description: Discusses trade  investment and defence cooperation  reaffirming Pakistan   s commitment to stronger bilateral ties
content:
Discusses trade, investment and defence cooperation, reaffirming Pakistan’s commitment to stronger bilateral ties
President Asif Ali Zardari on Wednesday received the credentials of the ambassadors-designate of France and Saudi Arabia at Aiwan-e-Sadr in Islamabad, reaffirming Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening bilateral relations with both countries.
According to a press release issued by the President’s Secretariat, Zardari received the credentials of France’s Jean-Noël Poirier and Saudi Arabia’s Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy. He congratulated both ambassadors on their appointments and wished them success in their diplomatic assignments.
“The president expressed confidence that they would contribute to strengthening Pakistan’s relations with their respective countries and expanding cooperation in areas of mutual interest,” the statement read.
President Receives Credentials from Ambassadors of France and Saudi Arabia President Asif Ali Zardari today received the credentials of the Ambassador-designate of France, Jean-Noël Poirier and the Ambassador-designate of Saudi Arabia, Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy, at Aiwan-e-Sadr,… pic.twitter.com/FCCtDE0Uoh
During his meeting with Poirier, Zardari reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening ties with France, emphasising the importance of multilateralism, regular high-level exchanges and an independent bilateral relationship.
“The President highlighted opportunities to enhance trade, investment, parliamentary exchanges, educational and cultural links, and defence cooperation,” the statement added.
In his meeting with Albugamy, the president underscored the close strategic partnership between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia and reiterated Islamabad’s commitment to the Kingdom’s security and defence.
“He highlighted the importance of the Makkah Alliance for Defence and the institutional mechanisms underpinning bilateral cooperation,” the statement read.
Read More: Information ministry rejects Reuters report on Makkah defence pact as 'speculative'
Zardari also stressed the need to deepen economic ties, appreciated Saudi Arabia’s financial support and assistance with oil supplies, and highlighted the contribution of the Pakistani community in the Kingdom.
The president expressed confidence that relations between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia would reach new heights during the ambassador’s tenure.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed MJDA, a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
Significance of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
The MJDA was the latest step in longstanding military and strategic cooperation between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. Signed in Makkah, the pact established a framework for collective deterrence and stipulated that an armed attack on any one of the three countries would be considered an attack on all three, while providing for wider cooperation across defence.
The agreement followed nearly a year of negotiations and came amid heightened instability across the Middle East. Turkiye and Pakistan had sought closer regional security cooperation, while Saudi Arabia had faced growing security concerns as conflicts spread across the region, threatening its territory, energy infrastructure and ambitious economic development plans.
For Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the trilateral pact is built on their Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed in September 2025. That agreement stated that “any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both” and committed the two sides to strengthening defence cooperation and joint deterrence.

title: Drake Bell slams SAG AFTRA after losing eligibility for health insurance   Do not become an actor
description: The actor   s reported earnings fell short of the  28 933 threshold required for coverage under the plan
content:
The actor’s reported earnings fell short of the $28,933 threshold required for coverage under the plan
Drake Bell has criticised SAG AFTRA after learning that he does not currently qualify for health insurance through the actors’ union health plan.
The Drake & Josh star shared a screenshot of the plan’s eligibility notice on his Instagram Story. The message stated that his reported covered earnings between July 2025 and June 2026 had failed to meet the minimum requirements, or that he had not satisfied other eligibility rules.
According to the report, Bell had earned $17,480.53 towards the required $28,933 threshold, leaving him $11,452.47 short.
Bell responded with a pointed message warning aspiring performers against entering the industry or joining the union. He also tagged SAG AFTRA and its president, actor Sean Astin, questioning whether performers should be responsible for running the organisation.
His criticism comes amid wider concerns about access to health coverage for working actors, whose earnings can fluctuate significantly between projects. Eligibility depends on meeting the plan’s requirements, meaning that even performers with lengthy careers can face difficulties if their qualifying earnings fall short.
Bell is not the only performer to have raised concerns recently. Jack Haven, known for Atypical , and Heather Matarazzo, who appeared in The Princess Diaries , have also spoken publicly about difficulties qualifying for coverage.
Haven previously described the situation as an emergency and said additional work was needed to secure insurance eligibility. The report later noted that Haven obtained enough work to qualify for coverage.
Bell’s career has included acting, music and voice work. He became widely recognised through the Nickelodeon series Drake & Josh , which aired during the 2000s.
In 2024, he also discussed his experience of childhood sexual abuse in the docuseries Quiet on Set: The Dark Side of Kids TV , identifying former dialogue coach Brian Peck as his abuser.
His latest criticism places renewed attention on the financial pressures performers can face when trying to maintain health coverage between jobs. SAG AFTRA’s eligibility rules remain central to the dispute, although Bell’s post does not establish that the union changed its requirements.

title: Ryan Coogler   s    The X Files    officially gets series order at Hulu
description: Jennifer Yale will serve as showrunner  with original creator Chris Carter returning as an executive producer
content:
Jennifer Yale will serve as showrunner, with original creator Chris Carter returning as an executive producer
Ryan Coogler’s new The X-Files series has officially received a series order from Hulu, marking a new chapter for the popular science fiction franchise.
The project will introduce a new pair of FBI agents investigating paranormal cases, with Danielle Deadwyler and Himesh Patel taking the lead roles. Their characters are expected to develop a dynamic reminiscent of the original investigators, Fox Mulder and Dana Scully, whose contrasting beliefs helped define the long running series.
Coogler, known for directing Black Panther and Sinners , wrote and directed the pilot episode and will serve as an executive producer. Jennifer Yale has been appointed showrunner and executive producer, while original The X-Files creator Chris Carter will also return as an executive producer.
The production’s other executive producers include Zinzi Coogler and Sev Ohanian of Proximity Media. Deadwyler and Patel will serve as co executive producers alongside Simone Harris.
In a statement announcing the project, Coogler said he had loved The X-Files for a long time and considered the opportunity to write and direct its pilot a meaningful experience. He added that the creative team wanted to honour what made Carter’s original series resonate with audiences while developing its own approach to the franchise.
Steve Buscemi and Amy Madigan have also been reported as cast members, although details about their characters have not been disclosed.
The original The X-Files ran for 11 seasons and produced 218 episodes, alongside two feature films. The series followed Mulder and Scully as they investigated unexplained phenomena, government conspiracies and cases involving possible extraterrestrial activity.
Coogler has previously discussed combining standalone monster investigations with larger mythology driven stories involving alien colonisation. However, further plot details for the new series have yet to be confirmed.
It remains unclear whether original stars David Duchovny and Gillian Anderson will return as Mulder and Scully. Hulu has not announced an official release date for the new series.

title: Mike Tyson   s Netflix documentary faces criticism over missing accountability
description: The documentary includes a White House interview with Donald Trump but does not address the assault allegations
content:
The documentary includes a White House interview with Donald Trump but does not address the assault allegations
Mike Tyson revisits his troubled past in Netflix’s four part documentary Tyson , but the series has drawn criticism for presenting an incomplete portrait of the former heavyweight champion and his history of controversy.
In a review published by The Guardian on October 14, Andrew Lawrence argues that Tyson’s willingness to discuss painful experiences does not necessarily translate into accountability for his actions. The documentary explores his childhood in Brooklyn, rise to boxing fame, struggles with addiction and complicated relationship with public attention.
Tyson became one of boxing’s most feared figures through his extraordinary knockout power. However, his career was also marked by serious controversies, including his 1992 rape conviction and imprisonment, his turbulent relationship with actor Robin Givens and his disqualification for biting Evander Holyfield’s ear during their 1997 fight.
The documentary revisits several of these episodes, while Tyson offers his own interpretations of events. Lawrence argues that his candidness can be compelling but also unsettling, particularly when he discusses Desiree Washington, who accused him of rape when she was 18. Tyson was convicted in the case and served a prison sentence.
Washington and Givens are notable absences from the series, despite the documentary addressing their connections to Tyson’s past. Their perspectives could have offered viewers additional context about experiences that remain central to his public reputation.
Director Floyd Russ also interviews US President Donald Trump, who previously promoted Tyson’s fights at his Atlantic City casino. According to the review, the conversation focuses on media treatment of Tyson and Trump, without addressing the rape conviction.
The series also explores Tyson’s grief over the death of his trainer Cus D’Amato and the accidental death of his four year old daughter in 2009. These moments reveal the personal tragedies behind his public image.
Tyson, who also serves as a producer, openly acknowledges his fascination with being filmed, describing the camera as a narcotic. For Lawrence, that admission captures the central tension of the documentary: Tyson remains compelling on screen, yet the series leaves questions about responsibility and redemption unresolved.

title: Pakistan  Russia sign MoU to strengthen cooperation against organised crime
description: Finalise agreements on extradition and the transfer of prisoners  too
content:
PM Shehbaz meets Russian interior minister, stresses need to deepen cooperation in areas of mutual interest
Pakistan and Russia on Wednesday signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen cooperation in combatting organised crime during Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev’s visit to Pakistan.
The MoU was signed after Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met Kolokoltsev, who arrived in Pakistan earlier this week on a four-day visit, marking the first instance of a Russian interior minister visiting Pakistan.
According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office, the premier expressed satisfaction over the positive momentum in Pakistan-Russia relations and emphasised the importance of building on it to further strengthen bilateral cooperation.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif received Mr. Vladimir Kolokoltsev, Minister of Internal Affairs of the Russian Federation, who is currently on an official visit to Pakistan. The Prime Minister expressed satisfaction over the positive momentum in Pakistan-Russia relations… pic.twitter.com/IkuFeAaQql
He reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to deepening its friendly relations with the Russian Federation and making effective use of existing bilateral mechanisms to advance mutually beneficial cooperation.
PM Shehbaz also underscored the need to expand cooperation in areas of mutual interest, particularly trade and investment, energy and economic development.
Interior Minister of the Russian Federation Mr. Vladimir Kolokoltsev called on Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad, today. pic.twitter.com/4TaGFVxYcC
The Russian interior minister conveyed Russia’s desire to further strengthen bilateral ties and expand cooperation in areas of shared interest.
While appreciating Pakistan’s support at various multilateral forums, particularly the United Nations, Kolokoltsev highlighted the significant potential for expanding bilateral trade and economic cooperation between Pakistan and Russia.
He expressed Russia’s readiness to work closely with Pakistan to further enhance bilateral engagement.
Later, the prime minister witnessed the signing of the MoU on strengthening cooperation in combating organised crime.
Both countries agreed to sign the MoU earlier today while also deciding to finalise agreements on extradition and the transfer of prisoners.
The decisions were taken during a meeting between Interior Minister Naqvi and Kolokoltsev at the Ministry of Interior in Islamabad, followed by delegation-level talks on areas of mutual interest. The Russian minister arrived in Pakistan on Monday on a maiden four-day visit at the invitation of Naqvi.
According to a statement issued by the interior ministry, during the meeting, both sides agreed to ensure the swift implementation of the readmission agreement and strengthen bilateral cooperation to combat organised crime, cybercrime, drug trafficking and illegal migration.

Furthermore, working groups from the interior ministries of both countries will also visit each other soon to explore further avenues for cooperation," it said.
The statement added that the two countries also agreed to strengthen institutional links between Pakistan’s National Police Academy and its Russian counterpart to promote the exchange of expertise and improve law enforcement capabilities.

Speaking on the occasion, Naqvi described the proposed agreement on preventing organised crime as an important milestone in strengthening cooperation between the two countries.
He added that Pakistan wished to benefit from Russia’s experience in combatting cybercrime.
During the talks, Kolokoltsev informed the meeting that Russia had reduced cybercrime by 33% through effective measures, highlighting the importance of sharing experience and strengthening cooperation in the field.
He also stressed the importance of joint measures to prevent all forms of organised crime, including terrorism, drug smuggling and illegal migration.

The discussions culminated in both sides underscoring the commitment of both countries to expand bilateral engagement through formal agreements, information sharing, institutional coordination and cooperation among law enforcement agencies.

title: FCC dismisses Bushra Bibi s plea for suspension of sentence in   190m case
description: Order says appeal was filed 61 days late  miscellaneous application was submitted seeking condonation of delay
content:
Order says appeal was filed 61 days late, miscellaneous application was submitted seeking condonation of delay
The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) on Wednesday dismissed an appeal filed by Bushra Bibi, wife of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan, seeking suspension of her sentence in the £190 million case, observing that the main appeal should be decided expeditiously rather than undertaking a parallel examination of the matter.
Imran and Bushra remain incarcerated in Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail. They were sentenced on December 20, 2025, to 17 years in prison in the Toshakhana-II case, while in January last year, an Islamabad accountability court sentenced Imran to 14 years and Bushra to seven years in prison in the £190 million case.
A three-page written order, authored by Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan, noted that Bushra had challenged the Islamabad High Court’s (IHC) April 30 decision rejecting her application for suspension of sentence. According to the order, the appeal was filed 61 days late, and a miscellaneous application was submitted seeking condonation of the delay. The court noted that Bushra’s incarceration at Adiala Jail had been cited as the reason for the late filing.
Accepting the explanation, the court condoned the 61-day delay in filing the appeal. The order also referred to arguments presented by Bushra’s counsel Salman Safdar, who cited the former prime minister Nawaz Sharif case in support of his position.
Read: £190m case: IHC orders Imran, Bushra meeting with their lawyers within seven days
The court observed that the main appeal had already been fixed for hearing before the IHC and that the appropriate course was to ensure its expeditious disposal rather than undertake a parallel examination of the merits of sentence suspension. The court held that there were no sufficient grounds to interfere with the IHC’s order at this stage.
“We find no sufficient ground warranting interference with the impugned order at this stage,” the court observed.
The bench also expressed the expectation that the IHC would decide the main appeal expeditiously while providing both sides adequate opportunity to present their arguments. The court further stressed the need to discourage unnecessary adjournments during the proceedings.
Imran and Bushra are facing a £190 million graft case linked to the Al-Qadir Trust, a welfare organisation they established in 2018. The trust, which runs a university outside Islamabad focused on spirituality and Islamic teachings, is accused of being used as a front to receive land worth millions of dollars from a real estate tycoon.
The government claims the donations were in exchange for Imran’s administration using repatriated UK funds to pay fines against the businessman, instead of depositing the money into Pakistan’s treasury.
Imran has denied any wrongdoing, insisting neither he nor his wife gained financially from the trust or related transactions. In his written response to the IHC, he claimed the case is politically motivated, alleging a corruption reference against Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz led to a fabricated case against Bushra Bibi.
Read More: Islamabad court dismisses case against Imran Khan, citing prior acquittal
He challenged the prosecution’s evidence, highlighted inconsistencies in witness statements, and accused the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) of destroying key records related to political leaders.
Imran has argued that amendments to the National Accountability Ordinance (NAO), 1999 protect cabinet decisions from prosecution unless there is proof of personal gain. The IHC has acknowledged the “substance” of this claim and directed the trial court to consider it while deciding the matter.
He subsequently filed a civil miscellaneous application in the IHC seeking a hearing of his appeals against the accountability court verdict, which convicted him and his wife in the £190 million corruption case.

title: Victoria   s Secret faces backlash for snubbing model Romee Strijd ahead of 2026 Fashion Show
description: The model shared her disappointment in a TikTok video after learning she would not feature in the event
content:
The model shared her disappointment in a TikTok video after learning she would not feature in the event
Fans have criticised Victoria’s Secret after Dutch model Romee Strijd revealed she would not be walking in the brand’s 2026 Fashion Show, despite appearing in five consecutive shows previously.
The 31-year-old model shared her disappointment in a TikTok video on Monday, October 12, after learning she would not feature in the event, scheduled to take place in Los Angeles on Sunday, October 18.
“I just hung up the phone. It’s a no, and it’s fine because rejection is part of modeling, and that’s totally fine,” Strijd said.
In a follow-up video, she explained that her frustration stemmed less from the rejection itself than from the way the decision had been communicated.
She said she “doesn’t feel supported by her agency”, IMG Models, and wanted greater clarity about the casting process.
“I don’t feel like I have the straight story. Just be honest, just tell me, and I can go on with my life and let it go, because it’s fine,” she added.
Strijd said the uncertainty had caused significant stress, particularly as she had repeatedly requested updates to help organise plans for her family.
She shares two daughters, Mint, 5, and June, 3, with husband Laurens van Leeuwen.
Strijd’s comments prompted an outpouring of support, with fans questioning the casting decisions and calling for established Victoria’s Secret models to return.
“The show is a joke if they don’t even hire the OGs,” one commenter wrote.
Another fan said, “You ARE the VS angel 🪽”.
Although Strijd wished this year’s production well, she suggested the experience had made her hesitant about pursuing future shows.
Other established models, including Frida Aesen and Lais Ribeiro, were also reportedly left out of the 2026 lineup.

title: ECP issues notices over delay in Islamabad local govt elections
description: Summons interior secretary  Islamabad chief commissioner as ordinance expires without replacement legislation
content:
Summons interior secretary, Islamabad chief commissioner as ordinance expires without replacement legislation
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Wednesday moved to address the delay in Islamabad’s local government elections, summoning the interior secretary and Islamabad chief commissioner for a hearing on October 21 after the ordinance governing the polls expired without the federal government completing the required legislation.
The commission said it would consider whether the elections could proceed under the Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government Act, 2015, and intended to issue the election schedule under the existing law after the hearing.
“The Election Commission has decided to fix this case for a formal hearing before the Commission on October 21, 2026, and to issue notices to the Secretary, Ministry of Interior, and the Chief Commissioner, Islamabad, to assist the Commission,” the ECP said in a statement shared on X.
The ECP said it had completed the delimitation of constituencies and published the final lists on Wednesday, but the expiry of the Islamabad Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, had left the legal framework for holding the elections unresolved.
“The Election Commission intends to issue the election schedule under the old local government law (ICT Local Government Act 2015) after a formal hearing,” the statement read.
The commission said it had initiated the delimitation process on July 21 under the Federal Capital Islamabad (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, and had since completed the exercise.
However, the ordinance expired on September 6 before the federal government could enact the necessary legislation. A parliamentary standing committee had approved the required legislation on September 3, but the legislative process was not completed before the ordinance lapsed.
The ECP said it had sent its feedback on the Islamabad Local Government Rules to the Ministry of Interior on July 20, seeking legislation and publication of the rules in line with its recommendations.
The Ministry of Law and Justice subsequently returned the draft rules to the Ministry of Interior, citing the expiry of the ordinance and the resulting lack of authority to frame rules under it.
The Ministry of Interior had been handling the proposed legislation and local government rules, while the Ministry of Law and Justice reviewed the draft. The ECP had provided recommendations to the interior ministry to facilitate the establishment of the required legal framework.
The commission has now sought the assistance of the interior secretary and Islamabad chief commissioner to determine how the elections can proceed following the ordinance’s expiry.
Article 140-A of the Constitution requires provinces to establish local government systems by law and devolve political, administrative and financial authority to elected representatives. The ECP is responsible for holding local government elections under Article 140-A and Article 219 of the Constitution.
Islamabad’s last local government elections were held in 2015 , and the elected local government’s term expired in February 2021. Fresh polls have since been delayed amid repeated changes to the legal framework.
The ECP had scheduled local government elections in Islamabad, but the process was disrupted in January 2026 when President Asif Ali Zardari promulgated the Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, amending the 2015 law and replacing the Metropolitan Corporation structure with three town corporations.
The changes required fresh delimitation and effectively reset the election process, prompting the ECP to cancel the scheduled polls.
The federal government subsequently pursued amendments to the local government law, while a separate committee led by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal worked on proposals for a new Islamabad government structure. The National Assembly’s Standing Committee on Interior approved the ICT Local Government Bill 2026 on September 3, but the ordinance expired on September 6 before the replacement legislation was enacted.

title: Korra   s voice actress cried over character s portrayal in  Avatar  Seven Havens
description: Janet Varney said Korra   s portrayal in  Avatar  Seven Havens  left her devastated  as fans debate series    storyline
content:
Janet Varney said Korra’s portrayal in 'Avatar: Seven Havens' left her devastated, as fans debate series’ storyline
Janet Varney, the voice actress behind Korra in The Legend of Korra, has shared her emotional reaction to the character’s portrayal in the new animated series Avatar: Seven Havens.
The storyline presents Korra as a figure blamed for a catastrophic event that ended the world, prompting debate among fans of the franchise.
In Seven Havens, Korra is portrayed as a figure who caused a cataclysm rather than protecting the world. Her legacy has created fear of the Avatar, leading the new Avatar twins, Pavi and Nisha, to be kept hidden instead of being celebrated.
Varney described her reaction after watching the series’ pilot, saying she was deeply affected by the way younger characters spoke about Korra.
“I sobbed through this pilot episode. I was shattered. I cannot emphasize it enough. I finished it, and my partner was like, ‘So?’ And I was like, ‘I can’t even tell you what happened. I’m so upset, crying.’”
She also expressed concern for viewers who have supported Korra throughout the franchise.
“And I was like, ‘I’m so worried about all the people that love Korra and already defend Korra.’ And I had to go back and watch with fresh eyes after I had deeply grieved.”
Varney acknowledged that the series’ direction remains uncertain and encouraged fans to remain open to future developments.
“I know we don’t know what will happen, and I want people to keep the faith, but who knows? But just for me, watching children talk about her as if she’s a monster was heartbreaking. I mean, it really hurt. I’m not her, but I know what she means to some people, and it just really hurt.”
The storyline has divided the Avatar community, with some viewers criticising the treatment of Korra’s legacy. However, the series’ mystery leaves open the possibility that further revelations will explain the events surrounding her actions.
Other criticism has focused on the representation of different cultures in Seven Havens , with some fans arguing that the world’s distinct regional identities have been reduced.
The series has only introduced one haven so far, leaving further world-building to be explored as the story progresses.
Seven Havens has reportedly been renewed for four seasons, with its opening episodes beginning to establish the mystery surrounding Korra and the world she left behind.

title: Fans react to Kacey Musgraves Columbus criticism during Dallas concert
description: Kacey Musgraves called Christopher Columbus  loser  during Dallas show  prompting mixed reactions online
content:
Kacey Musgraves called Christopher Columbus 'loser' during Dallas show, prompting mixed reactions online
Kacey Musgraves criticised Christopher Columbus during a concert in Dallas, Texas, after asking the audience about Indigenous Peoples’ Day. Her remarks prompted mixed reactions online, with some viewers supporting the singer and others criticising her for discussing the subject during a performance.
The country singer made the comments at the American Airlines Center during her Middle of Nowhere tour. In footage shared online, Musgraves asked the crowd, “Yeah, that's right, on this day? What day?”
After the audience responded, “Indigenous Peoples' Day!”, she turned her attention to Columbus.
“Obviously [expletive] Columbus,” she said. “Literally the lamest person to probably ever exist. Like for real. What a loser.”
She continued, “What a loser Christopher Columbus, we hate you!”
Some social media users criticised Musgraves for expressing her views during a concert. One commenter argued that Columbus’s legacy was connected to the development of the United States, while another questioned whether the singer had studied the explorer’s history.
Others objected to entertainers discussing political or historical issues during performances. One viewer wrote, “Omg just shut up and sing girl nobody is there to listen to anything other than your songs.”
The comments also drew support from viewers who welcomed Musgraves speaking about Indigenous Peoples’ Day.
Musgraves’s onstage comments came amid a separate public exchange with Kristi Noem. The dispute began after Noem responded to a post by Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico, who had attended Musgraves’s Dallas concert.
Noem wrote that she would choose Ella Langley over Musgraves and Texas politician Ken Paxton over Talarico.
Musgraves responded with a reference to Noem’s account of shooting her dog, Cricket, which attracted criticism after appearing in her 2024 book.
“I don't think you have a dog in this fight but if you did you would have shot it,” Musgraves wrote.
Musgraves is continuing her Middle of Nowhere tour in support of her album of the same name, released on May 1 2026. The North American run is scheduled to conclude with two performances in Seattle on October 26 and 27.

title: PEMRA bars live coverage of blasts  firing and terrorist attacks
description: Regulator directs channels to air only verified information  warns of legal action over violations
content:
Regulator directs channels to air only verified information, warns of legal action over violations
The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) on Wednesday directed satellite television channels to refrain from broadcasting or providing live coverage of explosions, blasts, firing and terrorist attacks, warning that violations would invite legal action.
In a notification issued on October 13, the regulator reiterated its prohibition order dated February 20, 2023, directing news, current affairs and regional-language channels to refrain from broadcasting, rebroadcasting or providing live coverage of such incidents.
“All satellite TV channel licensees are once again hereby directed to refrain from broadcast, re-broadcast and live coverage of any unfortunate/unpleasant incident such as explosion, blast, firing, terrorist attack etc,” the notification read.
“Satellite TV channels must broadcast only such verified information, warranted by the concerned department/law enforcement agency,” it added.
The notification also directed channels to “effectively use time delay mechanism” and ensure the constitution of an independent editorial board in accordance with PEMRA laws, a Supreme Court judgment in suo motu case No 28 of 2018, and an Islamabad High Court order issued on September 5, 2022.
The regulator warned that violations would invite legal action under Sections 29A, 30 and 33 of the PEMRA Ordinance, 2002, as amended.
The notification came just three days after the federal government imposed emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa on October 11, citing a sharp rise in terrorist incidents and violent activities in the province.
The presidential proclamation said attacks on infrastructure, government installations and law-enforcement agencies had increased, posing serious threats to lives and property. It also alleged that the provincial government had failed to address the security situation effectively.
The move followed reports of a worsening security situation in K-P. Terrorist incidents in the province increased by 195 per cent between March 1, 2024, and September 23, 2026, according to security reports presented to the federal cabinet. The reports also said 73 per cent of terrorist attacks recorded in the province during 2026 had targeted police and security personnel.
Balochistan has also experienced a sharp escalation in violence. According to a Centre for Research and Security Studies report, violence-linked fatalities in the province rose from 265 to 829 in the third quarter of 2026. K-P recorded 186 violent incidents during the same period, accounting for 48 per cent of attacks nationwide.

title: Achakzai warns Sindh could be next to face governor   s rule
description: Opposition leader cites disputes over water and minerals  calls for reversal of emergency and governor   s rule in K P
content:
Opposition leader cites disputes over water and minerals, calls for reversal of emergency and governor’s rule in K-P
Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai on Wednesday warned that Sindh could be the next province to face governor’s rule, citing potential disputes over water, mineral resources and canals, as he condemned the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).
Addressing the National Assembly, Achakzai warned that the government’s actions against provinces and their political representatives could deepen political confrontation, urging it to reverse its decisions and restore the elected government in K-P.
“Next governor's rule will be imposed in Sindh over the occupation of water, on the occupation of mines, of the rivers, and then you will remember what mistake we made,” he said.
مجھے دکھ ہوتا ہے کہ میرے سندھی بھائی اس بلا میں شریک ہوئے ہیں۔ اگلا گورنر راج پانی کے قبضے پر، معدنیات کے قبضے پر اور نہروں کے قبضے پر سندھ میں لگے گا، اور پھر آپ کو یاد آئے گا کہ آپ نے کیا غلطی کی۔ pic.twitter.com/1kPE9WSuk0
The opposition leader also criticised members of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) for supporting the government’s measures, saying he was saddened that his “Sindhi brothers” had become part of what he described as a calamity.
Calling for the reversal of emergency and governor’s rule in K-P, the opposition leader urged the government to make parliament the centre of political authority and resolve disputes through democratic means.
“There is still time, reverse it, reverse these decisions. Come, make this house a fountainhead of power. Repent,” he said.
اب بھی وقت ہے، اب بھی وقت ہے مہربانی کریں۔ اب بھی وقت ہے ریورس کر دیں، ان فیصلوں کو ریورس کریں۔ آئیں! ہم قرآن کے گتوں پر لکھ کر دینے کے لیے تیار ہیں، آئیں اس ہاؤس کو طاقت کا سرچشمہ بنائیں۔ آئیں، توبہ کریں! https://t.co/MqFYNBC78j pic.twitter.com/WSiArS68Jn
Achakzai subsequently termed the federal government a “terrorist government”, alleging that it had been formed through money, coercion and the support of uniformed institutions. He said the assemblies had been bought to bring the government into power and challenged lawmakers to swear on the Quran that this had not happened.
یہ حکومت 8 فروری کو زر اور زور کی بنیاد پر، ہمارے وردی پوش اداروں کی سپورٹ سے، 24 کروڑ انسانوں کو دہشت زدہ کر کے قائم کی گئی، یہ ایک دہشت گرد حکومت ہے . قائد حزب اختلاف محمود خان اچکزئی کا قومی اسمبلی سے خطاب جو قومی اسمبلی نے سینسر کر دیا تھا۔ pic.twitter.com/8o9evhLydT
He also criticised the government’s treatment of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan, saying the party had been prevented from contesting the elections under its electoral symbol and its candidates had been forced to contest on 200 different symbols. “Are you punishing Pakistan's 240 million people for this?” he asked.
Achakzai argued that the PTI’s electoral difficulties did not justify the measures taken against the province, urging the government to reconsider its decisions.
آپ نے عمران خان کے مقابلے کے لیے لنگوٹ باندھ کر حملہ کیا، اس پارٹی کا انتخابی نشان چھینا۔ اس پارٹی کو الیکشن میں حصہ لینے سے منع کیا۔ اس کی پارٹی کے کارکنوں نے یہ غلطی کی کہ دو سو انتخابی نشانوں پر الیکشن لڑ کر آپ کے تمام تماشے کو الٹا کر دیا۔ کیا اس کی سزا آپ دے رہے ہیں؟ pic.twitter.com/CKCkOGbNHY
Defending K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, whose government had been suspended following the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule, Achakzai said the provincial leader had urged people to stand against what he described as wrongdoing rather than resorting to violence.
“You talk about evil, the real evil is this government,” he said, adding that Afridi was right to call on people to stand against it. “He did not hurl abuses or throw stones,” Achakzai said, adding that Afridi had only urged people “to rise up against this evil.”
ابھی آپ برائی کی بات کرتے ہیں؛ میرے دوست، اصل برائی یہ حکومت خود ہے۔ اس برائی کو سیدھے راستے پر لانے کے لیے خیبر پختونخوا کا وزیرِ اعلیٰ بالکل ٹھیک تھا۔ نہ وہ گالی دیتا تھا اور نہ ہی پتھر مارتا تھا، وہ صرف یہ کہتا تھا کہ اس برائی کے خلاف اٹھ کھڑے ہو جاؤ۔ pic.twitter.com/fHCww6ATwR
The opposition leader also criticised the authorities over Afridi’s detention , saying he had been arrested and his hands and feet bound, but had not been brought before the National Assembly. “You have done us a great favour, a very great favour! After arresting Afridi and binding his hands and feet, you didn't bring him here,” he said.
آپ نے ایک مہربانی کی، بڑی مہربانی! شیخ مجیب کو گرفتار کر کے آپ لاہور لے آئے۔ آپ نے یہ مہربانی کی کہ ہمارے آفریدی وزیراعلیٰ کو پکڑ کر، ہاتھ پاؤں باندھ کر یہاں نہیں لائے۔ کر دیجیے، کر دیجیے! بسم اللہ، یہ بھی کر دیجیے! کیا کر رہا تھا وہ ؟ pic.twitter.com/38ch43HmCl
Drawing a parallel with the history of East Pakistan, Achakzai recalled that Sheikh Mujibur Rahman had worked for the Muslim League before being branded a traitor.
He said more than 48% of the people of East Pakistan had voted in favour of Pakistan, invoking the episode to criticise the denial of political representation and the use of force against political opponents.
مجیب الرحمٰن مسلم لیگی کارکن تھا، جس کو غدار کہا گیا، وہ سائیکل پر بیٹھ کر مسلم لیگ کے لیے کام کرتا تھا، مشرقی پاکستان کے 48 فیصد سے زیادہ لوگوں نے پاکستان کے حق میں ووٹ دیا۔ آپ نے اپنے اس رویے سے مجبور کیا کہ میری بات مانو گے تو ٹھیک، نہیں مانو گے تو میں یہ کر سکتا ہوں pic.twitter.com/wo6v7qLH20
Achakzai also criticised what he called the “Throne of Lahore”, describing it as cruel and urging the government to reconsider its approach towards the provinces. He said the provinces would resist attempts to deprive them of their rights through force, adding that Balochistan and Punjab would also stand with them.

The developments followed a period of escalating tensions between the federal government and the PTI-led provincial administration, with reports that Afridi and some members of his cabinet had been taken into preventive custody. The party has also sought legal remedies over the measures and raised concerns about Afridi’s whereabouts.
