title: After NA  Senate approves K P emergency resolution by majority vote amid opposition ruckus
description: Governor s rule will be imposed in Sindh next   warns Achakzai  urges reversal of decisions while there s still time
content:
Law minister says K-P situation threatens 'national security'; Achakzai warns next 'governor's rule will be in Sindh'
The National Assembly (NA) and Senate on Wednesday endorsed President Asif Ali Zardari's proclamation of emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), passing resolutions by majority votes despite opposition lawmakers' objections to the imposition of emergency measures in the province.
The developments emerged after the federal government imposed emergency and governor's rule in K-P on October 11, suspending the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led provincial administration amid a dispute over the province's security situation and counter-terrorism measures. The government has defended the move, citing a deterioration in law and order and an alleged failure by the provincial administration to coordinate counter-terrorism efforts with federal authorities.
The NA session began under the chairmanship of Speaker Ayaz Sadiq as Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry presented the resolution before the House. During the proceedings, Chaudhry moved a separate motion seeking the suspension of question hour to allow the House to take up other parliamentary business. Opposition lawmakers opposed the motion, but it was adopted by a majority vote.
The House adopted the following resolution moved by Dr. Tariq Fazal Chaudhary, Minister for Parliamentary Affairs. "The National Assembly approves the Proclamation of Emergency issued by the President on the 11th October, 2026 in the Province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under second… pic.twitter.com/5enkgK6v4w
The Lower House later debated the emergency measures imposed in the province, with opposition lawmakers strongly opposing the Centre's decision and raising a hue and cry during the proceedings. However, the resolution was passed by a majority vote. The NA session was subsequently adjourned until 11am on Friday.
قومی اسمبلی کا اجلاس 16 اکتوبر بروز جمعہ دن 11 بجے تک ملتوی The session of the National Assembly has been adjourned to meet again on Friday, the 16th October, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. #NASession pic.twitter.com/MHo1K3arTB
Following the approval from NA, the Senate session was held under the chairmanship of Chairman Yousaf Raza Gilani. During the proceedings, the Senate also approved a motion moved by Senator Shahadat Awan to defer the question-and-answer session scheduled for the day.
Speaking in the upper house, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said Rules 132 and 133, which govern ordinary resolutions moved by private members, did not apply to a resolution introduced under a constitutional requirement. He added that the seven-day notice requirement was not applicable in this case.
Rejecting objections to the procedure, the law minister also said the government could not deviate from the Constitution or the rules and regulations of the House.
He maintained that members opposing the resolution should participate in the debate and, if they disagreed with it, reject it through a vote.
The minister called for the matter to be put to a vote after discussion so that the opinion of the House could be ascertained. Following this, the Senate approved the imposition of emergency in K-P as the opposition walked out in protest.
Later in the day, the president summoned a joint session of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) tomorrow morning at 11 under Clause 1, Section 54 (Summoning and prorogation of Majlis-e-Shoora) of the Constitution of Pakistan. The notification regarding it was issued by the NA today.
The President of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, Mr. Asif Ali Zardari, has summoned a Joint Sitting of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) on Thursday, the 15th October, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. in the Parliament House. The Joint Sitting has been summoned in exercise of the powers… pic.twitter.com/hkoYWXWMva
In a separate notification issued by the NA Legislation Adviser Muhammad Mushtaq, the secretariat demanded the production of NA Members Sana Ullah Khan Masti Khel and Dawar Khan Kundi for all the upcoming NA sessions. The lawmakers are currently in the custody of Punjab Police.
اراکینِ قومی اسمبلی کا پروڈکشن آرڈر جاری اسپیکر قومی اسمبلی سردار ایاز صادق نے پنجاب پولیس کی تحویل میں موجود اراکینِ قومی اسمبلی کا پروڈکشن آرڈر جاری کر دیا، ترجمان قومی اسمبلی اسپیکر قومی اسمبلی نے اراکین قومی اسمبلی ثناء اللہ خان مستی خیل اور داور خان کنڈی کا پروڈکشن آڈر… pic.twitter.com/Z7uOWc1rby
The adviser further outlined that the MNAs will be handed back to the cops after the commencement of NA sessions.
Earlier, while speaking on the NA floor, the law minister had said the K-P government's approach to combating terrorism had become a "threat to national security", as the federal government tabled a resolution in the NA seeking parliamentary approval of the emergency imposed in the province under Article 232 of the Constitution.
Speaking during the session, Minister Tarar said the Constitution required a presidential proclamation of emergency under Article 232 to be laid before both houses of parliament — the National Assembly and the Senate — for approval within 10 days of its issuance. Responding to criticism that the imposition of emergency had resulted in the removal of an elected provincial government, Tarar said the decision had been taken after extensive deliberations and a thorough assessment of the security situation in K-P.
He said the federal cabinet had held a two-and-a-half-hour discussion before recommending the emergency measures to the prime minister, citing internal disturbances and cross-border incursions as major factors behind the decision.
“The attitude that the K-P provincial government has maintained regarding the war against terror, particularly over the past one year, since the present cabinet took control there, from Oct 15, 2025, to an alarming degree, was becoming a threat to national security,” he remarked.
The law minister emphasised that effective counter-terrorism operations required close coordination between the federal and provincial governments, stressing that a unified response was essential to ensuring Pakistan's security.
قومی اسمبلی کے اجلاس میں وفاقی وزیر برائے قانون و انصاف سینیٹر اعظم نذیر تارڑ کا اظہار خیال۔ #NASession pic.twitter.com/98OxJCrUcS
He said the sharp increase in terrorist activities since 2021 had been driven by several factors, including external, diplomatic and political developments, accusing PTI of pursuing policies that had aggravated the security situation.
Tarar acknowledged the sacrifices made by the armed forces, police personnel and civilians in confronting terrorism, saying their efforts had helped the country make progress despite persistent security challenges. He maintained that political differences should not undermine counter-terrorism efforts, reiterating the importance of cooperation between federal and provincial authorities in addressing threats to national security.
Arguing that the number of terrorist incidents in K-P over the past year was greater than those recorded during the 2021-2024 spell of terrorism, Tarar claimed that non-functional chief minister Sohail Afridi "overlooked the lit fire," as well as the injuries sustained by the Armed Forces, police, security forces, ulema, and innocent civilians.
"Instead of healing the wounds of the injured, placing his hands over the heads of the widows and orphans of the martyred, attending their funerals, visiting hospitals, reassuring the people, Afridi gave priority to his politics," the minister said.
He added, "When the situation is extraordinary, when the situation is severe, the actions should also be extraordinary; it should not be routine work." Tarar said that there were no restrictions on conducting politics, "but when your own public is being martyred, your own youth in the police force and Armed Forces are giving sacrifices, so then you, being the chief executive of the province, is it not the duty of your government that you go and spend time with them, that you conduct daily meetings, morning and evening, bring everyone together, make an action plan, make implementation measures for it?"
The minister said these circumstances were overlooked by Afridi and "it was also declared that there will be an attack on the capital, that it will be conquered."
He added that instead of "resorting to the use of force to handle this, we emphasised discussions and dialogue," expressing his gratitude to Speaker Sadiq, who "took a personal interest" in the matter and "in respect of the decision of the president and prime minister, provided a platform for mediation."
Tarar noted that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam, along with "our friends and ally" the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), "tried their best that matters be handled democratically."
Tarar added that on directions of the president, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari designated Naveed Qamar, Sherry Rehman and Aijaz Jakhrani to partake in the discussions. On the opposition side, the minister noted that PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas led the delegation and "sat for two days with their heads together," Tarar said.
He added that the Constitution and law have set forth a method for proceedings against someone on whom a case was lodged, saying that "if there is anything that can stop this entire process through legal intervention, then that is the court."
"If you want to free an imprisoned person, in most cases, that is in the control of the court."
Achakzai calls govt ‘terrorist’, urges reversal of emergency, governor's rule in K-P
Meanwhile, Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party (PkMAP) Chairman Mahmood Khan Achakzai described the government as “a terrorist government”, alleging that it had been formed through money and coercion with the support of uniformed institutions, and defended non-functional chief minister Sohail Afridi's opposition to what he termed oppression.
Achakzai accused the government of undermining the electoral mandate, alleging that the assemblies had been bought to install a government that did not represent the people's will. He argued that the PTI had been prevented from contesting the elections under its party symbol and that its candidates had subsequently contested using around 200 different symbols.
“Whether PTI founder Imran Khan was good or bad, whatever he was, I don't go to the past; you went to such an extent to compete with him that you even snatched the party's election symbol. You stopped the party from participating in the election,” he said.
Questioning whether the government was punishing the entire country for the PTI's electoral success, Achakzai asked, “Are you punishing Pakistan's 240 million people for this?”
He defended Afridi's stance against the government, saying K-P's people had shown courage in opposing what he described as terrorism. He maintained that the Afridi had called on people to resist oppression rather than resort to violence. Achakzai also criticised the authorities over Afridi's treatment, alleging that the Afridi had been arrested and restrained but not brought before the assembly.
“You have done us a great favour, a very great favour! After arresting Afridi and binding his hands and feet, you didn't bring him here. Do it, do this too. What was he doing, Mr Speaker?” he asked.
Achakzai warned that political confrontation over provincial rights could extend beyond K-P, saying people in Balochistan and Punjab could also resist what he described as the forcible denial of their rights.
He expressed regret over the participation of political representatives from Sindh in the current political situation and warned that the province could face governor's rule over disputes concerning water and mineral resources.
“Next, governor's rule will be imposed in Sindh over water, minerals, Canals, and then you will remember what mistake we made,” he said.
Referring to the history of East Pakistan, Achakzai recalled that Mujibur Rehman had worked for the Muslim League before being branded a traitor. He said more than 48% of the people of East Pakistan had voted in favour of Pakistan, invoking the episode to criticise what he described as the denial of political representation.
He also criticised what he called the “Throne of Lahore”, describing it as cruel, and urged the government to reconsider its approach towards the provinces.
Addressing the NA speaker, Achakzai called for the reversal of the government's decisions and urged lawmakers to restore parliament's position as the centre of political authority.
“Mr Speaker, there is still time; reverse it, reverse these decisions. Come, make this house a fountainhead of power, ” he said.
Achakzai also questioned the integrity of lawmakers supporting the government, saying some would be unable to uphold their positions if asked to swear on the Quran.
He said the government should reconsider its decisions and allow the assembly to serve as a forum for resolving political disputes rather than deepening confrontation between the centre and the provinces.
3,900 martyred in 14 months amid worsening K-P security situation, says Khawaja Asif
Speaking on the floor of the NA, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said 3,900 people had been martyred in K-P over 14 months, in addition to 2,700 over three years, as he criticised the provincial government for prioritising political interests over counterterrorism efforts.
Asif called for a united national response to terrorism, saying the province was bearing the greatest burden of violence and could not effectively confront the threat without political cohesion.
He alleged that the non-functional K-P chief minister was more concerned about retaining power than addressing terrorism.
Asif said the Afridi had remained in office for 13 to 14 months and questioned whom he had taken instructions from, alleging that the individual directing him was now in Afghanistan. Asif also criticised the province’s governance, comparing its development over the past 13 years with that of other provinces.
Referring to a Taliban statement condemning an emergency and the deployment of security forces in certain areas, the minister urged the opposition to clarify its political alignments.
“The opponent is the Pakistan state, and the ally is the Taliban whose hands are stained with the blood of our children,” he highlighted during his speech in the lower house.
Alluding to a relative of former premier Imran Khan, whom he said was living in the United States, Asif questioned the extent of that individual's influence over the province’s affairs, including health-related matters.
"The PTI chairman is a fair-minded person," Asif said, adding that he could personally vouch for him, while questioning whether the party discussed governance shortcomings internally.
He accused PTI of double standards in its dealings with the military establishment, recalling the party’s past ties with former army chief General Qamar Javed Bajwa and former Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) chief General Faiz Hameed. He then urged the opposition to examine its own political history before demanding equal treatment, arguing that the government had not made the release of its leaders, including former prime minister Nawaz Sharif, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, a political issue when they were imprisoned.
“Until this contradiction stays in our brotherhood, the situation of this country will not be good,” he said, calling for political unity amid the security challenges facing the country.
اسپیکر قومی اسمبلی سردار ایاز صادق نے گزشتہ دنوں حکومت اور اپوزیشن کے درمیان مذاکراتی عمل میں شامل حکومت اور اپوزیشن اراکین کے کردار کو سراہا۔ #NASession @AyazSadiq122 pic.twitter.com/2tfygpdsXq
Recalling the PTI government’s tenure, Asif said opposition members had previously sat alongside military officials during meetings in parliament and supported proposals to bring back individuals he described as terrorists, arguing at the time that their return would benefit Pakistan. He also reminisced about what he described as Imran’s repeated praise for General (R) Bajwa and the military-led government, saying he had heard the PTI founder compliment the former army chief extensively in parliament, the media and meetings.
Turning to his own imprisonment, the defence minister recounted the conditions he faced in jail, saying he had been given only one blanket during a period when temperatures were between seven and eight degrees Celsius. He said PM Shehbaz had arranged for an additional blanket to be smuggled into the prison for him, adding that the person who delivered it had been instructed to ensure it was hidden the following morning.
Asif said he had eaten prison food, describing it as adequate, and that a geyser installed in his cell had subsequently been ordered to be removed.
He also recalled Punjab CM Maryam repeatedly soaking a dupatta in water and placing it over her head to cope with the heat in the cells where she and Nawaz were held at Adiala Jail.
“We didn't cry. I think it is a matter of pride that we, for our belief, for our ideology, for our doctrine, we suffered these pains.”
The minister further recalled his imprisonment under former military ruler General (R) Pervez Musharraf, saying he had been kept in a six-by-four-foot cell at Attock Jail with a solid steel door. He said his loyalty to Nawaz Sharif and his political ideology had helped him endure the experience. Asif argued that the government had not obstructed political activities or protests over the imprisonment of its leaders, saying its members had continued to protest and appear in court without turning their leaders’ release into a political crisis.
Yesterday, Senate Opposition Leader Abbas alleged that negotiations with the government were a sham, claiming that the decision on governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa had already been made before the talks concluded. Abbas had maintained that the opposition had demonstrated a willingness to compromise during negotiations but alleged that the government had already decided on its course of action. Meanwhile, the interior minister said the talks collapsed because of CM Afridi and Murad Saeed. He rubbished the claim that the government was not serious about negotiations with the opposition.
During the session, PTI-backed Senator Zafar accused the government of violating the Constitution by arresting the chief minister, speaker and other ministers in K-P.
Events leading up to resolutions in favour of emergency
The issue of emergency and governor’s rule became a major flashpoint between the federal and K-P government after the talks failed.
On September 21, Interior Minister Naqvi said the government was consulting the law ministry on legal options for the province, including emergency and governor’s rule, if the PTI proceeded with its long march. Two days later, Information Minister Atta Tarar ruled out such plans, saying the federal government had no intention of removing the PTI administration.
On the other hand, CM Afridi rejected the warnings and said he would not retreat from his position because of threats of governors' rule or an emergency. He vowed to demonstrate people's power through a long march, scheduling it on September 27. Later, the chief minister rescheduled the march to October 4. Just days before the PTI’s planned long march, the prime minister and the president formed a committee to negotiate with the PTI and other opposition parties over the march, stating concerns over the province’s deteriorating law and order situation.
The government and opposition parties conducted negotiations over two days. Just as the two sides were nearing agreement on most of the issues, a deadlock emerged, bringing the negotiation process to a halt. The government blamed the K-P government, particularly Afridi, for the deadlock and failure of the negotiations, while PTI said the talks broke down over its demand for a meeting with the party’s founder.
In October, CM Afridi began his long march towards Islamabad, further escalating tensions between the two sides, with both sides continuing to trade allegations. As tensions peaked, PM Shehbaz once again entered the fray and extended an olive branch to the PTI, saying the government was prepared to engage with the opposition if the party ended its long march and sit-ins.
The PTI, however, rejected the offer as its march continued towards Islamabad.
On Sunday, October 11, the federal government imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in K-P under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution. The government cited the deteriorating law and order situation and what it called a lack of support from the provincial administration in the fight against terrorism.
In response, the opposition parties took to the floors of the Senate and NA to coerce the government into taking back its decision. PTI Chairman Gohar even filed a petition in the Peshawar High Court, challenging the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in K-P and seeking the restoration of the province’s elected government.

title: Enrique backs Manchester City to keep titles
description: PSG coach says trophies won on the pitch should stand as Pep Guardiola prepares to return to the Etihad
content:
PSG coach says trophies won on the pitch should stand as Pep Guardiola prepares to return to the Etihad
Paris Saint-Germain coach Luis Enrique said Manchester City "deserve" the trophies they won on the pitch and hopes the English side avoid sanction despite being found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules.
City face severe sanctions, including potential relegation from English football's top-flight, after an independent commission found them guilty on over 100 charges between 2009 and 2018.
There has also been speculation that titles won during that period could be stripped.
City have appealed the verdict and deny any wrongdoing.
Former City boss Pep Guardiola, who left the club in May, is set to return to the Etihad for Wednesday's clash against PSG in the Champions League.
Luis Enrique is a close friend and former Barcelona teammate of Guardiola and said what City won on the field should not be taken away from them.
"I think what they've done on the pitch has been incredible over the last few years and I think they certainly deserve to win on the pitch all the trophies that they have won," the PSG boss said in a pre-match press conference.
"I think the trophies that you win on the pitch remains on the pitch and they deserve to win. I hope they can avoid that sanction, that's what I feel."
Enzo Maresca has so far made a flawless start to the daunting task of succeeding Guardiola.
The Italian has won all eight games in all competitions, but Luis Enrique dismissed suggestions Wednesday's match is the chance to lay down an early marker for either side.
"January is when you can really see the team's level," he added. "Five or six months down the line, things are so different. Many teams change.
"But it's an interesting match at this stage, a fun one to watch."

title: Azerbaijan s governing party defends school uniform rules after hijab dispute
description: Azerbaijan s governing party defends school uniform rules after hijab dispute
content:
Azerbaijan's ruling YAP criticised Erdogan's adviser and Turkish AK Party lawmakers for opposing its new rules
Azerbaijan defended a day earlier its decision to introduce school uniform rules that have led to protests over restrictions on Islamic headscarves, and told close ally Turkey to ​stay out of its domestic affairs.
Azerbaijan, whose constitution separates religion from the ‌state and guarantees freedom of religion, is a secular former Soviet republic with a predominantly Muslim population.
The government introduced rules last month that prohibit school pupils from wearing ​clothing that departs from the official school uniform or is incompatible with ⁠the secular character of state education.
The rules do not explicitly mention the hijab, ​but some protests broke out this week after reports that some pupils and teachers wearing ​Islamic headscarves were being denied entry to schools.

The interior ministry said on Monday that 37 people had been detained for disrupting public order while opposing enforcement of the rules.
The governing Yeni Azerbaijan Party (YAP) a day earlier criticised an adviser to Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and lawmakers from Turkey's ruling ​AK Party for speaking out against Azerbaijan's new rules.
The adviser, Oktay Saral, wrote on X on Monday that ‌it ⁠was "unacceptable" to deny the right to an education to Azerbaijani students who wear headscarves.

"A headscarf is not an obstacle; it is a requirement of religious belief," he said. "We expect Azerbaijan to reverse this mistake as soon as possible."
In a statement, YAP condemned Saral's ​comments as "populist and irresponsible" ​and said they risked ⁠harming relations between the close allies, adding that the new rules were based on equality, secularism and the rule of law.
It ​said Turkey was also constitutionally secular and warned Ankara against using ​Azerbaijan's education ⁠policies for political purposes.

It also rejected criticism of Azerbaijan's ​close relations with Israel, saying they were based on international law and mutual interests.

title: Swiatek wins all Polish battle to launch Wuhan campaign
description: She defeats lucky loser Magdalena Frech 6 2  6 1 to record her 40th win of the season
content:
She defeats lucky loser Magdalena Frech 6-2, 6-1 to record her 40th win of the season
Six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek launched her Wuhan Open campaign by triumphing 6-2, 6-1 in an all-Polish battle against lucky loser Magdalena Frech on Wednesday.
Swiatek posted her 40th victory of the season in one hour and 42 minutes and remains on course for a potential quarter-final showdown with top seed and three-time Wuhan winner Aryna Sabalenka.
"We know each other pretty well, so I just wanted to focus on being consistent and playing as good as possible," Swiatek, the seventh seed, said of Frech.
"I know she is running to every ball always and sometimes using the power of the opponent, so I wanted to not play too crazy but play solid and I’m happy that I did that," said Swiatek, who is chasing a qualification spot for the year-end WTA Finals.
Despite the lopsided scoreline the opening set was tight, lasting over an hour and requiring Swiatek to erase a 0-2 deficit and save seven of eight break points before she finally took the lead on her fourth set point.
Upping the pressure with her relentless forehand, Swiatek claimed a 10th game in a row to build a 4-0 advantage in the second set.
The former world number one briefly lost momentum, getting broken by Frech, but recovered to advance to the round of 16, where she awaits one of two lucky losers, Lanlana Tararudee or Ashlyn Krueger.
British world number 170 Sonay Kartal, who missed six months this year with a spinal stress fracture, upset ninth-seeded Belinda Bencic 6-0, 7-5 to book a date with Jasmine Paolini or Nikola Bartunkova.

title: Shakhtar hope London move a reminder of Ukraine conflict
description: Chief executive Sergei Palkin says the club   s Stamford Bridge base helps keep Ukraine   s plight in the international spotlight
content:
Chief executive Sergei Palkin says the club’s Stamford Bridge base helps keep Ukraine’s plight in spotlight
Shakhtar Donetsk dream of one day taking Champions League football back to Ukraine but a temporary home at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge helps keep the war-torn nation's struggles "visible", according to the club's chief executive Sergei Palkin.
The Ukrainian champions entertain AEK Athens on Wednesday before hosting Sporting Lisbon, Fenerbahce and Real Madrid with west London their latest base.
Shakhtar were forced to flee their home city in 2014, just two years after hosting the European Championship, after war broke out in the Donbas region but could still play their European games in western Ukraine.
However, since Russia's invasion in 2022, all European club matches and national team games have taken place abroad due to the security situation.
Poland, Germany and Slovenia have played host to Shakhtar in recent years, but Palkin believes the switch to "the football capital of the world" helps to keep the Ukrainian cause in the spotlight.
"We are representing our country and want to be visible for Ukraine," Palkin told the BBC.
"We need support from the democratic world.
"We cannot fight alone. Part of our role when we play in London and other cities in Europe is to send these messages and remind people what's going on."
Yet the choice of Stamford Bridge has raised eyebrows.
Chelsea enjoyed a golden era of success under Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich between 2003 and 2022 before Britain sanctioned the oligarch for his close ties to the Kremlin and froze his assets.
Abramovich was forced to sell Chelsea as a result but retained the support of many fans who chanted his name following the British government's action.
On the field, Shakhtar have proven remarkably resistent in the face of such upheaval.
They reached the semi-finals of the Conference League last season and the last four of the Europa League in 2020.
Despite the war, the club remain a hothouse for developing Brazilian talent with 14 players among the current squad from the South American nation.
Shakhtar have also maintained a reputation for nurturing up-and-coming young coaches.
Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi and Lyon coach Paulo Fonseca are among those to have taken charge during their period in exile.
Former Turkey and Atletico Madrid midfielder Arda Turan is the latest promising manager making waves at Shakhtar.
"We are looking on the positive side of being (in London) but we are dreaming of the day that we can play in Ukraine again," Turan said on Tuesday.
"My players taught me how to live at war without showing excuses, always going on with the fight.
"I have an excellent group, not just the players but the staff, everyone in Ukraine.
"We are carrying the hopes of people. It's not just for football purposes."

title: Omani FM appreciates Pakistan   s efforts to ease regional tensions in meeting with PM Shehbaz
description: Foreign minister  Omani counterpart agree to strengthen bilateral ties  step up diplomacy for regional peace
content:
Both leaders reaffirm close ties and seek to expand cooperation across multiple sectors
Oman's Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamood Albusaidi appreciated Pakistan’s sustained diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions and advance peaceful solutions to regional challenges during a meeting with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office.
Albusaidi is visiting Pakistan to co-chair the eighth session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) alongside Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.
According to the statement, the prime minister welcomed the Omani foreign minister and highlighted the shared faith, geography, history and culture, as well as centuries of people-to-people exchanges, that provided a strong fraternal foundation for relations between the two countries.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif received today the Foreign Minister of Oman, H.E. Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamood Albusaidi, who is on a visit to Pakistan to co-chair the 8th Session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission along with Deputy Prime… pic.twitter.com/ONHosHAL34
PM Shehbaz said Pakistan considered Oman a brotherly country, an important maritime neighbour and a valuable partner in a critically important region. He also noted with satisfaction the unanimity of views between Pakistan and Oman on regional and global issues.
Expressing satisfaction over the successful convening of the eighth session of the JMC, the premier hoped the meeting would provide a strong foundation for expanding mutually beneficial cooperation and deepening engagement between the two countries, the statement said.
He also appreciated Oman’s principled stance on resolving disputes through dialogue and diplomacy.
According to the PMO, Albusaidi thanked the Pakistani government for the hospitality extended to him and his delegation. He expressed satisfaction over the successful holding of the JMC session and agreed that it would pave the way for enhanced bilateral cooperation across various sectors for mutual benefit.
The Omani foreign minister also appreciated Pakistan’s sustained diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions and advance peaceful solutions to regional challenges.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif witnessed a ceremony of exchange of MoUs between Pakistan and the Sultanate of Oman, in Islamabad, today. pic.twitter.com/XYxgkpXAIq
The statement said the prime minister witnessed the signing of the protocol of the eighth session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission, along with agreements and memorandums of understanding covering cooperation in media, news and information exchange, historical documentation and archives management, communication and information technology, and the facilitation of diplomatic and official exchanges.
Dar condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
Earlier today, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister (FM) Ishaq Dar, in a joint press conference with his Omani counterpart Albusaidi condemned recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, terming them unacceptable, in violation of international law, and a "serious threat to regional peace and security."
FM Dar stated that during his discussions with Albusaidi, he "conveyed Pakistan's strongest condemnation" of the recent attacks "which resulted in injuries to several individuals, martyrdom of one Pakistani and injuries to five Pakistani nationals."
According to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on X, FM Dar "reaffirmed Pakistan's full solidarity with the leadership and people of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," including Islamabad's "unwavering commitment to the kingdom's sovereignity, territorial integrity and security, in accordance with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement ."

Sayyid Badr Bin Hamad Bin Hamood Albusaidi (14 October 2026) 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/LYrDyrJsEQ
The remarks came as Yemen's Houthis ​vowed to press on with attacks on airports and oil facilities in Saudi ‌Arabia and said they struck the headquarters of oil giant Saudi Aramco. The group said it had launched ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco facilities in the eastern city of Dhahran, King Khalid International Airport in ​Riyadh and an Aramco refinery in Riyadh, without saying when.
Saudi Arabia has faced widening Houthi strikes over the ​past week, including an attack on Riyadh airport on Saturday that killed 13 people .
FM Dar and his Omani counterpart "also exchanged views on the evolving situation in the Gulf, underscoring the importance of restraint, de-escalation, dialogue and diplomacy." FM Dar highlighted "the need to ensure the safety and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb, given their critical importance to regional and global food and energy security."
According to the statement, FM Dar reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to "contributing constructively to diplomatic efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability in the region."
Read: FM Dar condemns Houthi attack on Riyadh airport, says Pakistan is in touch with Saudi authorities
FM Dar, in his meeting with Sayyid Badr, also raised the issue of Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK), saying that it remained "a long-standing unresolved international dispute." The foreign minister "reiterated Pakistan's call for its just and peaceful resolution in accordance with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions."
Discussing "the grave situation in Palestine," the statement noted, FM Dar reiterated Islamabad's "principled and unwavering support" for the Palestinian people "and their inalienable rights." He stated, "We expressed concern over the continued expansion of illegal settlements and efforts to alter the status of Al-Quds Al-Sharif."
Pakistan also highlighted the "urgent need for the unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance to the people of Gaza," reaffirming Islamabad's support for a just and lasting solution in accordance with relevant resolutions of the United Nations.
Regarding regional developments including the situation in Afghanistan and the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT), FM Dar underscored "the imperative of ensuring that Afghan territory is not used to carry out activities against Pakistan."
On the IWT, the statement noted that the foreign minister "emphasised that India's unilateral decision to hold the treaty in abeyance constitutes a material breach of international law." He added that this represented "a dangerous attempt to weaponise shared water resources," and threatened the water, food and energy security of 250 million Pakistanis.
Welcoming "closer engagement between the business communities of the two countries and encouraged greater investment in Special Economic Zones and Free Zones," FM Dar also acknowledged "the valuable contribution of the Pakistani community in Oman."
The contribution "continues to serve as a strong bridge between our two brotherly countries," he said.
He added that both sides "reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in labour mobility, vocational training, and human resource development to create new opportunities for skilled Pakistani professionals and workers."
FM Dar expressed gratitude to Sayyid Badr and the Omani delegation "for their constructive engagement and valuable contribution to the success of the JMC session."
He concluded with saying that the "Pakistan-Oman friendship remains strong and forward-looking, and we are committed to building an even more prosperous future together."
FM's agree to strengthen bilateral cooperation, intensify diplomatic efforts
Earlier, FM Dar and Sayyid Badr agreed to strengthen bilateral cooperation and intensify diplomatic efforts for regional peace and stability, as the two countries held the eighth session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) in Islamabad after a seven-year gap.
Speaking during a media briefing in Islamabad, FM Dar welcomed the Omani counterpart and his delegation to Pakistan, conveying greetings on behalf of President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to the Sultan of Oman.
The foreign minister said the two countries had maintained frequent interactions and shared longstanding historical and diplomatic ties. Referring to the JMC, he said: "The meeting was taking place after seven years, and both sides had agreed during their restricted meeting to avoid such lengthy gaps in the future."
He said there was considerable scope for enhancing bilateral trade, economic activities and investment opportunities, stressing that regular engagement was essential to achieving progress.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 held a cordial meeting with H.E. Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamood Al Busaidi @badralbusaidi ahead of the 8th Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial session. The two Ministers reaffirmed the close, fraternal… pic.twitter.com/jpjqXRlqZJ
“I promise that in 2027, God will, inshallah, I will visit your great country for this purpose and we will have the next GMC there,” FM Dar said. The foreign minister said both sides had identified areas of mutual interest and discussed regional and global developments in detail during their restricted meeting.
He said discussions covered the "United States, Iran, the Strait of Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb, Palestine, the situation in Gaza, Jammu and Kashmir and other pressing regional issues."
FM Dar commended Oman’s leadership and its diplomatic efforts to promote regional peace, particularly its role in efforts to secure peace among Muslim countries. He said Pakistan appreciated Oman’s efforts before Islamabad became involved in supporting the same objective. “So, you did a great job and Pakistan commends, and I personally am a great admirer of your efforts,” FM Dar said.
Referring to Pakistan’s relationship with Oman and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), FM Dar said the countries coordinated closely through the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), the United Nations and other multilateral institutions.
He said diplomatic relations between Pakistan and Oman spanned 55 years, while historical ties between the two countries extended back centuries. FM Dar highlighted the longstanding connections between Oman and Pakistan’s Balochistan province, particularly the historical relationship involving Gwadar.
He said the two countries had agreed to work closely for regional peace and address ongoing challenges. Referring to developments involving the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, FM Dar said the two sides had discussed the situation in Bab el-Mandeb and shared similar views on the need to resolve the issues.
He stressed that diplomatic efforts were necessary to address the suffering caused by regional conflicts and instability. “The sufferings are very, very visible. Even in Pakistan, the energy supply chain has been disrupted. The prices have skyrocketed. The common man obviously cannot afford,” he said.
The foreign minister added that the "consequences of the disruption were being felt across the world." FM Dar called for restoring peace and stability in the region, saying Pakistan and Oman could play an important role in achieving that objective.
He also appreciated Oman’s engagement with Pakistan during the Pakistan-India war and other international developments, saying the two countries regularly kept each other informed and maintained close communication.
FM Dar also referred to his previous meeting with the Omani foreign minister in Manila.
Addressing the briefing, the Omani foreign minister expressed appreciation for the warm welcome extended to him and his delegation in Islamabad. He highlighted the historical, cultural and traditional bonds between Oman and Pakistan and reaffirmed his country's commitment to expanding bilateral cooperation across various sectors.
The Omani foreign minister said the eighth session of the JMC provided an important mechanism for strengthening relations and delivering benefits to the people of both countries. He referred to the existing friendship association, business council and political consultations between the two foreign ministers as mechanisms that could drive closer cooperation.
Sayyid Badr said regular meetings would help both countries fulfil the aspirations of their leadership and people. The Omani foreign minister also acknowledged Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting dialogue and diplomacy at a time of heightened regional tensions. “I would like to also acknowledge Pakistan's constructive role in supporting dialogue and diplomacy in our region at a time when tensions can easily escalate,” he said.
Read More: PM Shehbaz seeks stronger Bahrain ties in trade, energy during meeting with FM Al Zayani
He particularly appreciated Pakistan's diplomatic efforts to facilitate engagement between Iran and the United States. “I salute you for all the efforts that you have led in recent months, and we appreciate Pakistan's role that has helped create space for dialogue between Iran and the United States in particular,” he said.
The Omani foreign minister thanked officials from both countries for their extensive preparations ahead of the ministerial meeting.
Turning to economic cooperation, he said both countries were pursuing important economic transformations and had opportunities to expand collaboration in trade, logistics, port connectivity, energy, food security, technology and tourism. He also highlighted the importance of strengthening people-to-people connections.
The minister said the potential for cooperation existed, but both countries needed to remove obstacles and create favourable conditions for businesses and investors.
He encouraged greater interaction between the private sectors, stronger institutional partnerships, increased academic and technological cooperation, and more regular exchanges between the people of Oman and Pakistan.
The Omani foreign minister expressed hope that the JMC would become a more effective platform for delivering meaningful progress for both countries.
Sayyid Badr had arrived in Pakistan on Tuesday for a two-day visit to co-chair the eighth Pakistan-Oman JMC session, upon FM Dar's invitation. In an earlier statement , the Foreign Office had said Sayyid Badr would also pay a courtesy call to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, with the meeting providing an "important platform" to review the "full spectrum of bilateral relations" and strengthen cooperation across various fields.
The Foreign Office had added that the visit reflected the longstanding fraternal relations between Pakistan and Oman and was expected to further deepen mutually beneficial cooperation across multiple sectors.

title: Judge extends White House access for CNN  MS NOW  Politico amid legal fight
description: Rules Trump likely broke law by banning outlets over coverage deemed biased  inaccurate
content:
Rules Trump likely broke law by banning outlets over coverage deemed biased, inaccurate
A federal judge extended access to the White House for CNN , MS NOW and Politico journalists, deciding on Tuesday that President Donald Trump likely broke the law when he tried to ban them , in the latest ruling against him in the press freedom dispute.
United States District Judge Timothy Kelly issued a written decision that elaborated on his September 24 emergency order that reinstated access for the journalists. The news organisations and press freedom groups have accused Trump of unconstitutional retaliation against journalists for coverage he does not like.
Kelly's order last month gave the CNN , MS NOW and Politico journalists access to the White House grounds on a temporary basis. The judge issued a ruling called a preliminary injunction on Tuesday that will remain in effect until he makes a final judgment in the lawsuit brought by the news organisations, unless an appeals court lifts his order.
Read: US networks halt Trump coverage over ban
Kelly wrote that Trump's public remarks made clear that he banned the news outlets because he considered their reporting biased and inaccurate, and not because of national security concerns as government lawyers later asserted in court. "Simply put, that is unlawful viewpoint discrimination," the judge wrote, adding that "no one should read this decision as suggesting that President Trump’s complaints are meritless."
Trump appointed Kelly in 2017 during his first presidential term.
Past presidents have battled with the press, but Trump's campaign against the media has been unprecedented. He has upended decades of tradition by ​denying basic access to many major news organisations, launching personal attacks on journalists for their reporting and elevating media outlets seen as more sympathetic to the administration. He also has filed lawsuits against multiple news outlets.
Trump announced the ban in September on his social ​media platform, saying CNN , Politico , and MS NOW "shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the president of the United States." The Justice Department has emphasised ​Trump's contention that the ban is legally justified on national security grounds.
Read More: CNN defends reporter following personal attacks by Trump, White House
The outlets have said the revocation of their White House passes was unlawful retaliation for their news coverage and accused the Trump administration of manufacturing meritless national security concerns to justify the ban. The outlets said in a lawsuit that the ban violated the US ⁠Constitution's First Amendment protections for freedom of speech and a free press, as well as their rights to due process, meaning fair treatment from the government.
The White House on September 24 reinstated the CNN , MS NOW and Politico journalists after Kelly decided the ban "likely violated their constitutional due process rights," and ordered their access immediately restored.
The judge held a hearing on October 8 to hear arguments by the news outlets and the Justice Department over whether to extend the protection for the journalists against being barred from the White House. The Justice Department defended the bans as fair and justified.
"Here we have the unusual situation where the president himself has said he wants to chill speech. He wants to coerce better coverage," Theodore Boutrous, an attorney for the outlets, told Kelly during the hearing.
Also Read: News outlets ask US court to block Trump White House ban beyond 14-day order
" CNN , MS NOW and Politico engaged in apparently indefensible conduct," Justice Department lawyer Michael Velchik said.
The legal battle is being waged just weeks before the November 3 US midterm elections in which Trump's ‌fellow Republicans ⁠are fighting to retain control of Congress. Trump's job approval ratings are at record lows in opinion polls amid concerns over issues such as inflation and the Iran war .

title: Section 144 imposed in DI Khan for 30 days amid security concerns
description: Restrictions cover display  carrying and possession of weapons  as well as public gatherings  rallies and marches
content:
Restrictions cover display, carrying and possession of weapons, as well as public gatherings, rallies and marches
The Dera Ismail Khan (DIK) district administration imposed Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) for 30 days, banning public gatherings, rallies, processions and pillion riding on motorcycles until November 11, according to an order issued by Deputy Commissioner Hakmatullah, which emerged on Wednesday.
The restrictions also covered the display, carrying and possession of weapons, as well as the erection or use of tents, temporary structures and other obstructions on public roads, highways and other public places where they could impede public movement or traffic.
The order was issued following a request from the district police officer (DPO), DIK, dated October 13, citing the prevailing law and order situation and the likelihood that public gatherings, processions and marches could obstruct the movement of the general public, disrupt traffic and essential services, and disturb public peace and tranquillity.
The deputy commissioner said he was satisfied that sufficient grounds existed to invoke Section 144 CrPC and that immediate preventive measures were necessary to avert danger to human life, public safety and public order.
Under the order, public gatherings, assemblies, processions, rallies and marches likely to disturb public peace and tranquillity were prohibited throughout the territorial jurisdiction of DIK district. Pillion riding on motorcycles was also banned as a preventive measure in view of the prevailing law and order situation.
The order further restricted the display, carrying or possession of weapons in accordance with the relevant legal provisions and applicable restrictions. It also prohibited the erection or use of tents, temporary structures or other obstructions on public roads, highways and other public places where these could impede public movement or traffic.
In addition, the administration banned any other activity likely to obstruct public movement, disrupt traffic or essential services, endanger public safety, or disturb public peace and tranquillity.
The notification stated that the order would take effect immediately and remain in force for 30 days, from October 13 to November 11, 2026, unless withdrawn or modified.
“Any person contravening this order shall be proceeded against under Section 188 of the Pakistan Penal Code,” the notification stated.
Section 144 of the CrPC empowers a district administration to issue preventive orders restricting certain activities when immediate action is necessary to prevent danger to human life, public safety or public order.
DIK has faced a series of deadly attacks in recent weeks. On September 26, a suicide bombing at a joint checkpoint near Aman Mela in Darazinda killed at least 12 people and injured 35 others, with two Rescue 1122 personnel later killed when their ambulance came under fire while transporting victims. The Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) claimed responsibility for the attack.
On October 7, five people, including two Federal Board of Revenue officials, were killed in separate firing incidents in the district.
Against this backdrop of escalating security concerns, an emergency was imposed in DIK and 11 other districts of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa on October 11 under Article 232 of the Constitution, alongside governor’s rule in the province.

title: Atletico down Carrick s struggling Manchester United
description: The Red Devils remain winless in five matches across all competitions
content:
The Red Devils remain winless in five matches across all competitions
Atletico Madrid eased to a 2-0 win over Manchester United in the Champions League on Tuesday to pile pressure on Red Devils coach Michael Carrick.
Pablo Barrios pounced inside the first minute for Diego Simeone's side and after Leny Yoro's 74th minute red card set United back further, Ademola Lookman added another for the hosts in Madrid.
Man United have made their worst domestic start in 40 years and this league phase defeat in the Spanish capital was another blow, with the team now winless in five games across all competitions.
Man United defender Lisandro Martinez said the team's performance was "really poor" and suggested it was also a reflection of how the club is being run.
"It is annoying, disappointing coming here and I am not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here, it's disappointing," he told Amazon Prime.
Carrick handed Carlos Baleba his first start for the club since arriving from Brighton this summer, as well as pushing captain Bruno Fernandes out to the right side.
Atletico were without their skipper Koke, after the death of his mother, while coach Simeone selected Julian Alvarez from the off for the first time this season at the Metropolitano stadium, after he tried to force a departure this summer.
"As well as for the team, it was very important (to win) for Koke and all of his family, it's a very tough day for them, this victory is for them," said Barrios.
"Getting the goal so soon helped us to manage the game later, I'm really happy for the win."
Atletico fans ordered their supporters to "defend what we love" with a banner display before kick-off and the Rojiblancos were ahead after just 50 seconds.
Alex Baena found a way in behind United's defence and cut the ball across for Barrios, with Ayden Heaven unable to keep the midfielder's shot from crossing the line.
Barrios held up six fingers to pay tribute to Koke.
"It was really tough news for everyone and I said if I scored I would do that," added Barrios.
Carrick had said it was important to get off to a fast start, but his team were unable to follow his instructions.
Bryan Mbuemo might have equalised for the visitors, nudging the ball through Cristian Romero's legs but firing just wide.
Alejandro Grimaldo came inches away from extending Atletico's lead with a free-kick which hit the angle between post and crossbar.
The hosts thought they had a second when Johnny Cardoso finished neatly from the edge of the box before half-time but the goal was disallowed after a VAR review showed the ball had struck Marcos Llorente's hand during the build-up.
Alvarez, yet to score this season for Atletico, hit the post early in the second half.
United rallied and Fernandes's lob drifted narrowly wide before the Portuguese playmaker hit the crossbar from the left of the box after a corner routine.
However the three-time European champions suffered a setback when defender Yoro was harshly dismissed after a VAR review for bringing down Canada striker Jonathan David as the last man.
It opened the door for Atletico to grab their second, with David foiled by goalkeeper Senne Lammens but London-born Nigeria international Lookman was on hand to tuck home the rebound after 79 minutes.
Carrick withdrew playmaker Fernandes, looking ahead to the weekend visit to face rivals Leeds in the English top flight, where improvement is badly needed.
"It is very hard to say after a defeat that there is positives. We just have to work hard to keep working and keep trusting in our structure," United midfielder Youri Tielemans told Amazon Prime.
"We have to keep working, keep trusting each other and be together on this."
Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak saved from United substitute Matheus Cunha in the final stages but there was no way back for United.
Simeone's side were able to claim their first points after an opening defeat at Liverpool.

title: Arsenal cruise past Lille into share of Champions League lead
description: Eze and Saka add to Timber s opener as the Gunners secure a 3 0 victory
content:
Eze and Saka add to Timber's opener as the Gunners secure a 3-0 victory
Arsenal blew away Lille with a three-goal blitz in seven second-half minutes for a 3-0 win to extend their perfect start to the Champions League.
Jurrien Timber's deft finish opened the floodgates just after the hour at the Emirates Stadium before Eberechi Eze and Bukayo Saka rounded off the scoring.
Victory takes Arsenal into a share of the lead at the top of the Champions League table alongside Barcelona and Sporting Lisbon.
Mikel Arteta was able to use the wealth of resources at his disposal as he made five changes to the side that beat Leeds 2-1 on Saturday.
But it was Lille boss Davide Ancelotti, son of Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti, who was the happier after a goalless first half.
The visitors even had the ball in the net but Ayase Ueda was flagged offside.
Bruno Guimaraes came closest to breaking the deadlock for Arsenal before the break when he fired wide from close range and then his powerful shot from range was parried by Berke Ozer.
The Gunners quickly went through the gears in the second period once Timber dinked the ball over Ozer from Noni Madueke's pass.
Arteta had left arguably his three most potent attacking weapons on the bench and the introduction of Saka, Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard made an immediate impact.
"The ones that finish the game are extraordinary," said Arteta.
"They increase the intensity, the quality and we suffocate them more and more and more."
Saka's low cross picked out Eze whose deflected shot flew into the top corner to end any doubt over the destiny of the three points.
The England winger then finished off an exquisite team move from Havertz's cut-back for Arsenal's third.
There were further cheers from the home fans when Olivier Giroud came on as a late substitute for Lille on his return to the club where he scored 105 goals in a six-year spell.
But Giroud could not conjure up another Emirates goal as Lille remain without a Champions League point after defeat to Real Betis on matchday one.

title: FBI arrests Saudi OpenAI engineer over covert recording device  DOJ says
description: Accused allegedly hid thumb sized device in company s executive conference room  faces five years in prison
content:
Accused allegedly hid thumb-sized device in company's executive conference room, faces five years in prison
United States federal agents arrested a Saudi national who was an OpenAI engineer and charged him with installing a hidden audio recording device in an executive conference room at the AI company, the Justice Department said on Tuesday.
The case highlights growing security concerns around sensitive AI research as companies and governments compete fiercely for the talent and technology that could confer economic and strategic advantages.
Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, had worked as an engineer at OpenAI since July 2025, the Justice Department said in a statement. An email sent to an address associated with that name did not elicit a response, and it was not immediately clear who his lawyer was.
OpenAI discovered the recording device plugged into a USB port on the back of a television in an executive conference room at one of its San Francisco buildings on September 30, according to the department.
Read: Microsoft president says milk faces more regulation than AI
The thumb-sized device, which had a microphone and could connect to a camera, was concealed in toilet paper, according to an FBI complaint. It was installed on or about September 28, while its stored data was encrypted and inaccessible. Investigators later found a similar customised device in Alfozan's personal bag.
OpenAI said in a post on X that it used its internal AI models to identify the person responsible for planting the device and trace its origins. The company said it had evidence that the employee intended to place additional recording devices in sensitive areas of its offices to secretly record meetings.
We discovered a sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices. We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier. We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re…
"At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated," the company said.
OpenAI referred the matter to the FBI, which is continuing to investigate. The Saudi embassy in the United States did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
"Abdulrahman Alfozan allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer's executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology," FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement.
Alfozan also used an AI productivity agent to seek information about meeting-room calendars and capabilities for about a month through September 16, according to the FBI complaint. He has been a legal permanent resident of the US since September 2020.
If convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison, a $250,000 fine and three years of supervised release.
Read More: AI models may soon self-replicate without access to data centers, Anthropic warns
A LinkedIn profile showed that Alfozan studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the University of California, Berkeley. He previously worked at Meta and Microsoft , it said. Reuters could not independently verify the details mentioned in his LinkedIn profile.
Separately, the information reported that OpenAI was in early talks to acquire Trail of Bits, a startup that identifies and fixes vulnerabilities in open-source software. The talks were ongoing and could fall apart, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter. OpenAI and Trail of Bits did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.
OpenAI said on Friday it fired three researchers after an investigation found they had violated company policies on handling sensitive information. The researchers, Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni, had published a letter detailing the circumstances of their dismissal and arguing that the abrupt firings could create uncertainty among employees and undermine a culture in which researchers could raise safety concerns.

title: Greta Gerwig   s  Narnia  The Magician s Nephew  trailer divides fans ahead of Netflix release
description: Some viewers welcomed Gerwig   s creative approach  as others questioned whether the film captures the spirit of Narnia
content:
Some viewers welcomed Gerwig’s creative approach, as others questioned whether the film captures the spirit of Narnia
Greta Gerwig’s first trailer for Netflix’s Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew has divided fans, with reactions ranging from praise for its visual style to criticism that the adaptation strays too far from CS Lewis’ beloved fantasy series.
Released on October 13, the trailer features psychedelic imagery and Led Zeppelin’s “Stairway to Heaven”, offering a rock-inspired take on the story.
The response across social media platforms, including Reddit and X, has been sharply mixed.
Supporters have welcomed Gerwig’s creative approach, with one viewer calling it “the best trailer I’ve seen in years”.
Another praised its apparent faithfulness to the source material, writing, “Looks to be a very faithful adaptation with a sort of rock opera twist.”
However, other viewers questioned whether the film captures the spirit of Narnia.
One described the trailer as “Visually stunning trailer but nothing really jumped out to me indicating that this is a Narnia movie.”
Criticism has also focused on the visual effects, with some comparing the film’s aesthetic to Marvel productions such as Thor: Love and Thunder and Guardians of the Galaxy .
Others expressed concern that CGI-heavy visuals could overshadow the story’s original appeal.
The adaptation has faced scrutiny even before the trailer’s release, partly because of Gerwig’s involvement and the decision to cast Meryl Streep as the voice of Aslan, the central lion character.
The film features David McKenna, Beatrice Campbell, Emma Mackey, Carey Mulligan, Ciarán Hinds and Daniel Craig, alongside Streep and other cast members.
Netflix plans to release Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew in cinemas and IMAX on February 12, 2027, giving audiences an opportunity to judge the adaptation beyond its first trailer.

Security forces killed five terrorists and injured four others during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) against Fitna al-Hindustan in Washuk district of Balochistan, state media reported on Wednesday, citing security sources.
The federal government last year officially designated all terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as Fitna al-Hindustan , accusing India of sponsoring a proxy war through the outfits.
According to the post on X, sources said security forces continued operations against Fitna al-Hindustan under Operation Radd-ul-Fitna 3 in Balochistan.
"Advanced weapons and ammunition were recovered during the operation, and security forces remained determined to eliminate terrorism from Balochistan," it added.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also paid tribute to the security forces for their successful operation against Fitna al-Hindustan in Balochistan under Operation Radd-ul-Fitna 3 , the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) statement said.

title: Imaan  Hadi boycott proceedings as ATC records witness statements
description: Judge says authorities reported that no special vehicle was available to bring Imaan and Hadi to court
content:
Judge says authorities reported that no special vehicle was available to bring the accused to court
An Islamabad anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Wednesday began recording witness statements in the barricade removal case in the absence of lawyer Imaan Mazari, her husband Hadi Ali Chattha and their counsel after they boycotted the proceedings.
ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Supra heard the case, in which Eemal Khan Mandokhail appeared as counsel for Imaan and Hadi. “We went to Adiala Jail yesterday, but could not meet them,” Mandokhail told the court.
He said the previous day had been designated for Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) lawyers to meet inmates, but roads had been blocked about one-and-a-half kilometres from the jail.
He added that they had requested a meeting in accordance with a court order but had been unable to meet their clients. A court official informed the judge that jail authorities had said the accused would be produced via video link.
Mandokhail requested the court to ensure the physical appearance of Imaan and Hadi.
Judge Supra said reports from the police and jail authorities had been received, adding that they had reported there was no special vehicle available to bring the accused to court that day.
Prosecutor Raja Naveed Hussain Kiyani requested the court to record the witnesses’ statements. The judge said the statements could be recorded that day and the question of cross-examination could be considered afterwards.
Imaan, Hadi and their lawyers subsequently boycotted the proceedings. “We request the court to call us into the courtroom,” Hadi said.
Read: ATC orders jail authorities to facilitate lawyers' meetings with Imaan, Hadi
Former human rights minister Shireen Mazari called for their privacy to be respected, saying that everything was recorded in the room where meetings took place.
Mandokhail said he had received no directions regarding the recording of witness statements. He requested that the lawyers be allowed to meet their clients before the statements were recorded.
“The court has said that all stakeholders must be satisfied,” Hadi said, adding that the accused were the biggest stakeholders and that their participation was a legal right.
When a witness began recording his testimony, the lawyers and Shireen left the courtroom. Imaan and Hadi also left after the lawyers’ departure.
The testimony of a traffic police employee was being recorded in their absence.
Read: ATC orders jail authorities to facilitate lawyers' meetings with Imaan, Hadi
At the previous hearing on October 13, the ATC directed jail authorities to facilitate meetings between Imaan, Hadi and their legal team, after the lawyers said they had been unable to meet the couple at Adiala Jail.
Hadi also raised concerns about the confidentiality of lawyer-client meetings, saying cameras had been installed in the meeting areas, and questioned how they could defend themselves without access to their lawyers.
Imaan and her husband Hadi were rearrested on September 17 , shortly after the Supreme Court granted them bail and suspended their sentences in a separate social-media posts case. They were produced before an Islamabad ATC in connection with a case registered at Kohsar Police Station.
Police sought 30-day physical remand, but ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain rejected the request and sent the couple on judicial remand. The judge noted that although they had been nominated in the FIR as members of an unlawful assembly, no weapon had been attributed to either accused.
Read More: SC suspends trial court order, grants bail to Imaan Mazari, Hadi Ali Chattha
On September 27, the court issued a contempt notice to the Adiala jail superintendent after the authorities failed to facilitate the signing and transmission of the documents and also failed to produce the accused through video link. Two days later, the issue was resolved after Imaan and Hadi signed the required powers of attorney.
On September 29 , the ATC ended the contempt proceedings against the jail authorities and separately confirmed that notices had been issued on the couple’s bail applications, with arguments scheduled before Judge Abul Hasnat.
On October 7, the ATC had framed charges against Imaan and Hadi in the case related to the alleged violation of a designated route and incitement during the arrival of an international cricket team, despite defence objections that legal requirements had not been fulfilled.

title: Trump says major oil  gas  mineral exploration to begin in Greenland
description: Trump says major oil  gas  mineral exploration to begin in Greenland
content:
US president touts Greenland's oil potential while global energy prices remain high more than 7 months into Iran war
US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that plans were underway for major oil, gas and mineral exploration in Greenland, claiming the Arctic island holds vast, easily accessible oil resources amid months of elevated global energy prices.
"Massive Oil, Gas, and Mineral Exploration is getting ready to begin in our new and beautiful Greenland!" Trump wrote on his social media platform Truth Social, as global energy prices remain elevated more than seven months into the war in Iran.
He suggested that some experts believe Greenland has some of the world's largest easily accessible oil reserves, though he provided no details about the estimates or planned exploration activities.
Trump also emphasised Greenland's strategic location, arguing it would play a central role in defending the US and Europe against future attacks.
"Any future attack on the United States will have to come across Greenland, where our Defence will routinely knock down drones, missiles, or any other form of weapon not yet even conceived," he said.
"It gives us time, location, and sightline, like nowhere else in the World!"
The remarks follow a September agreement between Washington, Denmark and Greenland to expand the US military presence on the world's largest island, including additional bases and missile defence capabilities.
Despite Trump's reference to "our new" Greenland, the island remains a self-governing territory within Denmark, with the agreement recognising Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination.
Greenland stopped issuing new oil and gas exploration licenses in 2021 over environmental and climate concerns, although previously granted licenses remain valid.

title: Tresoldi hat trick fires Brugge past Inter Milan
description: The Italian champions remain without a point after two games
content:
The Italian champions remain without a point after two games
Club Brugge and their young forward Nicolo Tresoldi shocked Inter Milan 4–3 in the Champions League on Tuesday.
Tresoldi, a 22-year-old Italian-German forward, scored the first three goals for the Belgian side.
Former Inter goalkeeper Yann Sommer returned to the San Siro in the Brugge goal.
And the Swiss keeper denied Lautaro Martinez after ten minutes with Marcus Thuram firing wide early on.
A Hakan Calhanoglu foul on Carlos Forbs resulted in a penalty which Tresoldi slotted in just before the half hour.
Tresoldi picked up his second after capitalising on a goalkeeping blunder by the Inter keeper just after the hour and reacting faster than the Inter defence for the third with a quarter of an hour to go.
"It was an unbelievable and fantastic night. I dreamt many times of these nights and this was the best dream," said Tresoldi.
Martinez had given his team a lifeline just before the break following a move initiated by Thuram followed by a Federico Dimarco backheel assist.
The Argentine gave the San Siro crowd hope again in the 81st minute by narrowing the score to 3–2, but Romeo Vernant once again exposed Inter's defensive fragility by adding a fourth goal in the 87th minute.
Ange-Yoan Bonny pulled a goal back for the home side after 93 minutes.
Having lost 2-1 to Real Madrid at the Bernabeu in their European opener, the reigning Italian champions and Serie A leaders remain stuck on zero points and will be under immense pressure to win next week at home against Shakhtar Donetsk.
Club Brugge, who were defeated at home by Aston Villa (3–2) on matchday one, will next host French club Lens.

title: Zverev reaches Shanghai Masters quarter finals
description: The German battles past Bublik 7 6  8 6   4 6  7 6  7 1  despite ankle trouble
content:
The German battles past Bublik 7-6 (8/6), 4-6, 7-6 (7/1) despite ankle trouble
Top-seeded Alexander Zverev toughed out two tie-breaks to beat Alexander Bublik 7-6 (8/6), 4-6, 7-6 (7/1) at the Shanghai Masters on Tuesday, winning his first match since being guaranteed the year-end world number one ranking.
The 29-year-old German will play Alex de Minaur in the quarter-finals.
"I had some physical issues so, you know, I was maybe slower," he told the crowd.
"My ankle was acting up unfortunately again," Zverev elaborated in an on-court interview, later adding that his decline started in the second set.
"I'm starting to feel my body more, but happy to be through."
Zverev, the current world number two, was guaranteed the year-end number one spot after third-ranked Carlos Alcaraz lost to Zizou Bergs in Shanghai on Monday.
On Tuesday, Zverev called the honour "special", saying it was a different feeling to winning tournaments, adding he was "looking forward" to the responsibility of owning that status.
Neither player could create much trouble for his opponent in the first set as they traded aces to hold serve.
But Zverev found himself under pressure when he was forced to save a set point before making it into a tie-break.
He kept his composure as Bublik squandered three set points in a row, taking the first set with a commanding forehand at the net.
That momentum was cut short when Bublik broke the German's serve in the fifth game of the second set. Despite a few clutch backhands a sombre-looking Zverev was unable to avoid tumbling into a deciding third.
The players soon found themselves staring down another tie-break, but this time Zverev raced to a 6-1 lead and closed out the match with an ace.
Earlier, 56th-ranked Arthur Gea put on a convincing show to beat Jakub Mensik 7-6 (7/4), 6-4 in their fourth-round encounter.
Mensik, ranked 15th, hit the ground trying to convert a crucial break point in the final minutes of the second set, but Gea got past his opponent with a cross-court backhand and won on his first match point.
"I'm enjoying how I'm playing. I feel I'm improving all the time," said Gea, the lowest-ranked player left in the draw.
Asked if he might recreate last year's "miracle" that saw Valentin Vacherot claim the title as world number 204, Gea said he would "see what happens".
"I don't think it's miracle when you work hard every day, but I hope to do the same," he said.
Two days earlier the 21-year-old Frenchman beat US Open finalist Ben Shelton, the third seed, 7-6 (7/5), 7-6 (7/3) in the third round for the biggest victory of his career.
Gea next faces Alejandro Davidovich Fokina, who reached the quarter-finals after beating Hubert Hurkacz 1-6, 6-3, 7-6 (8/6) in a dramatic tie-break.
Davidovich Fokina, ranked 26th, beat the 2023 Shanghai champion at the third time of asking after blundering a smash and diving to the ground for a point in vain.
