title: Oil prices climb as Iran deploys new tactics to target ships transiting Hormuz
description: Brent crude futures rise 63 cents  or 0 6   to  106 32 a barrel
content:
Brent crude futures rise 63 cents, or 0.6%, to $106.32 a barrel
Oil prices climbed on Wednesday after two vessels were struck ‌in the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian officials told Reuters they were deploying new tactics to target ships, as Tehran seeks to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections.
Brent crude futures rose 63 cents, or 0.6%, to $106.32 a barrel by 0345 GMT, while US West Texas ​Intermediate crude futures gained 66 cents, or 0.7%, to $94.80 a barrel. Both contracts rose more than $1 in earlier trade ​before paring some gains.
The Iranian officials declined to provide details of the new strategy, but one ⁠said that Iran had started using different offensive tactics against vessels it considered in violation of its restrictions about 10 ​days ago, adding that this had led to an increase in attacks on such ships.
A container ship and a tanker were ​hit by unknown projectiles within the Strait of Hormuz, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Tuesday.
"The fact that Iranian officials are openly admitting to undermining US efforts to keep oil prices under control speaks volumes about the real intentions behind the so-called 'peace talks,'" said Priyanka Sachdeva, ​head of market insights at Phillip Nova.
Read: Govt seeks 15-year Saudi oil facility
"Iran is well aware of its geographical importance and the havoc higher oil prices can ​inflict on the global economy, and it may not shy away from using this leverage."
Elsewhere, the Iran-allied Houthis attacked an administrative building belonging to ‌state-owned oil ⁠firm Saudi Aramco in the city of Dhahran, causing a limited fire, Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said on Wednesday.
The group has fired ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia over the past week in retaliation for the kingdom's support of Yemeni government forces. Riyadh's international airport has been hit four times, with a strike on Saturday killing 13 people.
"Supply concerns stemming from conflict between ​the Houthis and Saudi Arabia ​are driving prices higher," said ⁠Hiroyuki Kikukawa, chief strategist at Nissan Securities Investment, a unit of Nissan Securities.
"However, the expectation that increased Russian diesel exports will ease market tightness is likely to limit sharp price movement ​in either direction," Kikukawa said, projecting WTI to trade between $90 and $100 a barrel.
Last month, Saudi ​Arabia raised oil ⁠production despite disruptions to shipments caused by the US-Iran war. That led to a sharp production increase from OPEC+ — the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and partners, including Russia — OPEC said on Tuesday.
In Russia, the government said on Tuesday it did not see any direct ⁠link between ​peace talks with Ukraine and its deal to export diesel to the US.
The comment ​came after Reuters reported that US envoys had told Ukrainian officials on Friday that the deal was part of an attempt to draw Russia back to ​negotiations for a peace settlement.

title: Kelly Clarkson vs Art of Play  Footage revealed as store lists bird for  15m  owner blasts singer for  social warfare

content:
'Kelly Clarkson has put us in danger', co-owner Adam Rubin claimed, criticising the singer for the fallout of her post
Security footage of Kelly Clarkson’s visit to Brooklyn curiosity shop Art of Play has emerged amid a dispute over an animatronic singing bird, with the store’s co-owner claiming the singer’s social media criticism has put staff at risk.
The footage, released by Pablo Torre, host of the investigative podcast Pablo Torre Finds Out , shows a woman identified as Clarkson entering the shop with her children, browsing items and speaking briefly with an employee near the bird, known as Molly.
The visit lasts less than five minutes. The video does not establish precisely what was said during their conversation.
Clarkson previously accused an employee of giving her the “Pretty Woman” treatment when she asked about the bird, which she said carried a $15,000 price tag.
She claimed the employee condescendingly offered to find something comparable. Art of Play disputed her account, stating that Molly was permanently attached to the wall and was not for sale.
According to USA TODAY , co-owner Adam Rubin subsequently listed the bird for $15 million following the controversy.
Kelly Clarkson blasts Brooklyn store for treating her like Julia Roberts from 'Pretty Woman'
Brooklyn store fires back at Kelly Clarkson over ‘Pretty Woman’ shopping complaint
Kelly Clarkson and Brooklyn store’s back-and-forth over $15,000 singing bird drama continues
He said the store had experienced increased sales and foot traffic alongside threatening messages, negative reviews and harassment affecting neighbouring businesses.
“We are afraid for the safety of our shopkeepers. Kelly Clarkson has put us in danger,” Rubin told Inside Edition , describing the fallout as “social warfare”.
Rubin maintained that the shop had treated Clarkson like any other customer during a busy period.
Clarkson, meanwhile, challenged the store’s explanation, insisting that an employee had pointed to the price tag during their exchange.
The dispute has divided online audiences, with some supporting Clarkson’s account and others criticising her decision to publicly identify the small business.
The released footage has added context, but the disagreement over the interaction remains unresolved.

title: PM Shehbaz meets MDA chief  reaffirms security commitment to Saudi Arabia
description: Lt Gen  retd  Mahmood briefs prime minister on strategies to promote defence and strategic cooperation
content:
Lt Gen (retd) Mahmood briefs prime minister on strategies to promote defence and strategic cooperation
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met Lieutenant General (retd) Nauman Mahmood, the first secretary-general of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), on Wednesday to discuss regional security and defence cooperation, reaffirming Pakistan’s unwavering commitment to safeguarding Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).
The statement came amid continued attacks by Yemen’s Houthi group on Saudi Arabia’s civilian and oil infrastructure, which have killed more than a dozen people and injured scores of others, heightening concerns over the widening regional fallout from the US-Iran conflict. The Houthi attacks have targeted key facilities, including airports and oil installations, amid escalating tensions linked to the wider US-Iran conflict.
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed MJDA in August, a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
During the conversation, the prime minister said that Pakistan stood alongside Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its sovereignty, defence and regional security under the agreement.
“The Makkah peace agreement is a historic milestone for peace, unity and stability in the region,” PM Shehbaz said.
The PMO statement said that PM Shehbaz extended his best wishes to Lt Gen (retd) Mahmood on assuming the post of secretary general,
"During the meeting, Lt Gen (retd) Mahmood briefed the prime minister on strategies to promote defence and strategic cooperation under the framework of the MJDA," it added.
وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف سے مکہ ڈیفینس الائینس کے پہلے سیکرٹری جنرل، لیفٹیننٹ جنرل (ر) نعمان محمود کی ملاقات آج اسلام آباد میں ملاقات ہوئی. وزیراعظم نے عہدہ سنبھالنے پر جنرل (ر) نعمان محمود کے لئے نیک خواہشات کا اظہار کیا. گفتگو کرتے ہوئے وزیرِ اعظم نے کہا کہ مکہ امن معاہدہ خطے… pic.twitter.com/C1jjRiKwBs
A day earlier, Lt Gen (retd) Mahmood also held a meeting with President Asif Ali Zardari, alongside Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi. The president expressed confidence that the MJDA, signed by Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia, would strengthen regional peace and stability through defensive cooperation guided by the principles of the UN Charter and international law.
On September 23, the government appointed Lt Gen Mahmood as the first secretary general of the MJDA.
The appointment was the first major institutional development since Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the pact, and his appointment gives Pakistan the responsibility of establishing and leading the alliance's first secretariat during its formative three-year period.
The decision was taken at the inaugural meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee, held under the MJDA, which brought together the foreign and defence ministers and military chiefs of the three countries in Istanbul on August 31.
Under the arrangement agreed in Istanbul, the secretary general would head the alliance's General Secretariat, based in the Saudi capital and tasked with overseeing implementation of the agreement, coordinating joint activities among the three militaries and supporting expanded defence-industrial cooperation.
For Islamabad, the role also provides an opportunity to shape the working structure of the new defence arrangement as Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye move from the political commitment announced in Makkah towards a more organised mechanism for defence coordination.

Judge Carrie Ann Inaba praised the comedian for applying previous feedback, telling him, “You took the note, and you made it work!”

title: Strait of Hormuz traffic plunges once again amid new wave of Houthi attacks
description: Iran says container ship sinks after hitting mine in Strait of Hormuz
content:
Iran says container ship sinks after hitting mine in Strait of Hormuz
Crude oil and petroleum exports from the Middle East sharply dropped over the past week as Yemen's Houthi militias intensified their attacks on commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting regional shipping lanes.
Maritime transit in the region has suffered drastically since the US and Israel’s pre-emptive joint strikes on Iran on February 28, followed by Tehran’s effective closure of the vital waterway and a subsequent American naval blockade.
Attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz reached a new peak this year over the past week.
At least 14 incidents of attacks, attempted strikes, and obstructions were recorded in and around the Strait of Hormuz on October 5-12, while six ships were attacked on Monday alone, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations and global maritime security sources.
Commercial vessel traffic via the strategic chokepoint fell to its lowest since July 22, affecting outward energy flows.
Oil, petroleum, and liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports from the Middle East plummeted in the wake of the war, and while there have been signs of partial recovery, intensifying security risks sparked concerns.
Houthis increased their attacks on Saudi Arabia, threatening transit through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean.
Middle Eastern crude oil, petroleum, and liquid chemical exports — including shipments from the Gulf of Oman and the Red Sea — fell from 21.1 million barrels per day on October 8 to 6.7 million barrels on October 11, 10.4 million barrels on Monday, and 8.3 million barrels on Tuesday, according to Kpler.
The weekly average of 17 million barrels remained below the pre-war volume of around 23.3 million barrels per day.
Only six commercial ships were able to transit the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, while previously 32 ships passed through on October 8, 24 on October 9, 11 on October 10, and 12 on October 11.
Meanwhile, vessel transit through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait also dropped, with 35 vessels passing through on October 8, 39 on October 10, 46 on October 11, and 32 on Monday.
The attempts by the Houthis to establish a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia to seize control of the Bab el-Mandeb corridor added a new volatile dimension to the wider conflict.
Large-scale supply disruptions across both the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait could pressure global energy supplies and market stability even further, analysts say.
Iran says container ship sinks after hitting mine in Strait of Hormuz
The IRGC navy said on Wednesday that a container attempting to "pass through the unauthorised and high-risk route of the Strait of Hormuz struck a naval mine, exploded, and caught fire severely," according to IRNA .
IRGC Navy: A violating container ship that intended to pass through the unauthorized and high-risk route of the Strait of Hormuz struck a naval mine, exploded, and caught fire severely. pic.twitter.com/fiJJM445ay
"This ship, carrying more than 2,500 containers, sank on Wednesday morning in the southern waters of the Strait of Hormuz due to the intensity of the fire."
Trump, Netanyahu weigh new Iran strikes before elections despite White House denial: report
US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu discussed launching a major new operation against Iran ahead of upcoming elections in both countries, the Axios news site reported on Tuesday.
The report, citing two US officials and other sources with knowledge of the matter, said the discussions took place before Trump publicly stated that he would not strike Iran before the US midterms. Netanyahu raised Israeli intelligence suggesting that Iran was working to rebuild its nuclear program, including possibly operating the Pickaxe Mountain site for uranium enrichment, according to one source.
A White House official called it "false" that the two leaders discussed resuming the war, claiming that Trump has ruled out attacks before the midterms in November.
Both militaries remain on alert and are finalising preparations in case Trump changes course, sources said. One US official described Trump's stance as noncommittal, saying he told Netanyahu to prepare without making a commitment.
According to the report, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and the US Central Command leadership are the strongest advocates of renewed strikes, while most advisers favour continued sanctions and economic pressure.
Israeli Army Chief of Staff Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir reportedly told US Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine that fighting within three weeks could force the postponement of Israel's October 27 vote, given likely Iranian missile retaliation.
Qatari mediators are still awaiting Iran's response to the latest US counterproposal, the report added.
Three fishermen injured in drone incident off southern Iran
Three fishermen were injured after a fishing boat was struck in an incident involving an unidentified drone near Sirik in southern Iran’s Hormozgan province, the provincial governor’s office says, according to Reuters, citing Tasnim news agency.
Tasnim cites local sources as saying a fishing boat was hit in what they described as an attack by a US drone, although Iranian authorities have not officially confirmed the circumstances of the incident or who was responsible.
‘They know what will happen’: IRGC says US would never dare to put boots on ground in Iran
Senior commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) says the United States never dares to carry out a land invasion of Iran, according to Press TV .
‘They know what will happen’: IRGC says US never dares put boots on ground in Iran https://t.co/eIoBoc5fj6
Even the most senior officials in Washington know that such a scenario would lead to devastating consequences for the US military, Brigadier General Mohammad Reza Naqdi said.
Naqdi, who serves as a high-profile advisor to the IRGC chief commander, made the comments on Tuesday in response to speculations that the US would deploy troops to Iran months after its joint aerial aggression with Israel against the country failed for good.
Iran shifting tactics to step up attacks on shipping before US vote, officials say
Iran is deploying new tactics to target ships sailing through the Strait of Hormuz as it seeks ​to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters .
Tehran has tried to exert control over the Strait of Hormuz since the US ‌and Israel launched strikes against Iran on February 28. It has restricted passage through the waterway, which carried about a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas trade before the war, in an effort to gain leverage over Washington.
Its threats and attacks have severely curtailed traffic through the strait, driving up oil prices, though some oil has continued to transit.
The two officials declined to provide details of the new strategy, but one said that Iran had started using different offensive tactics against vessels it considered in violation of its ​restrictions about 10 days ago, adding that this had led to an increase in attacks on such ships.
The strategy included a change in the type as well as the pace of attacks, with ​one goal being to influence the outcome of the US vote, they said.
"The aim is to frustrate efforts by the United States and its allies to bring ⁠down global oil prices," one of the two officials said.
Read: Iran will pursue diplomacy to counter sanctions, secure national interests: Iranian FM
The decision to adopt the new strategy had been taken at the highest levels of Iran’s leadership and was fully coordinated across the country’s ruling system, the officials ​said.
A US military official, speaking on condition of anonymity, confirmed that Iran had changed tactics in one significant way: after the US destroyed much of Iran’s radar capabilities, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) had started ​using unarmed spotters in small boats to identify potential targets, including US naval vessels, the official said.
Last week, in a previously unreported incident, the US military determined that Iranian spotters were operating from a dhow, calling in targets to the IRGC, the official said. US forces confronted the vessel, told its occupants to abandon ship and then destroyed it. There were no casualties, the US official said.
Unwilling to risk its remaining fast boats, Iran had been unable to prevent a ramp-up in oil exports through ​the strait, the official said, particularly after US strikes devastated its navy.
The war — and its $3 billion monthly price tag — has become a key issue on the US campaign trail for November's midterm elections, which will decide control of ​Congress.
US President Donald Trump has been weighing next steps against Iran, but has said he will not attack again before the vote.
The US has meanwhile been pressing its own naval blockade of Iranian ports and extending sanctions as it tries to pile economic pressure ‌on Tehran to ⁠reach a deal to end the conflict.
The standoff over Hormuz has left global energy markets exposed to further disruption, with the threat of attacks and high shipping and insurance costs complicating efforts to restore normal traffic.
In recent days, attacks on commercial ships still sailing through the strait have surged to their highest level since the war began, according to independent data.
There have been at least five incidents in the past 48 hours involving tankers and other commercial ships around the Hormuz area, including drone strikes, according to data analysis from maritime security sources and incidents reported to the British navy-affiliated agency United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).
Read more: Iran says reviewing US proposals for talks as indirect messages continue
That approximately mirrored the rate of attacks on October 3-5, ​pointing to a new escalation, according to data from ​the UN shipping agency, the International Maritime Organisation.
"There ⁠is a tempo increase in strikes, which looks deliberate," one maritime security source said.
As part of the new strategy, Tehran will also expand the geographical scope of its operations beyond the Strait of Hormuz to the Gulf of Oman and waters further afield, the officials said.
Analysis by maritime security sources based on ​attacks reported to UKMTO and maritime security companies in the region suggests this may already be happening. They show Iran targeting ships in areas beyond the ​Strait of Hormuz, including waters off ⁠the coast of Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, in recent days.
UKMTO WARNING 171-26 Click here to view the full warning⤵️ https://t.co/dwpZ53A0Wa #MaritimeSecurity #MarSec pic.twitter.com/swko5njXqh
The second Iranian official added that Tehran would not allow Trump to bring down oil prices before the November elections.
"Just when they think they are getting close to the point where prices will fall, we will push them away from it. This is a game of chess,” the second official said.
"Such vessels would be safe nowhere, even outside the Strait of Hormuz."
The Pentagon and Iran's Foreign Ministry did ⁠not immediately respond ​to requests for comment.
Both Iranian officials said Tehran is moving towards a situation in which ​no vessel violating its restrictions would be able to pass through the strait. "It will be complete closure soon," one of the officials said.
In its latest report on Sunday, the US Navy-led Joint Maritime Information Centre (JMIC) said the threat to merchant shipping in the Strait of ​Hormuz remained "severe", the second-highest level.
"IRGC attacks, attempted attacks, and/or harassment activity persisted, including UAV overflight, targeted surveillance of merchant shipping, and occasional VHF hailing," JMIC said.
Trump warns of further action against Iran
US President Donald Trump signalled further action against Iran during a campaign rally on Tuesday in the state of Alaska.
“Wait till you see what we do to Iran. We're going to do a number. We sort of had it. You know we've had it,” Trump told supporters in Wasilla, where he was campaigning for Republican candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
“They’re just waiting. They’re waiting,” he said.
“We’ve had it, but you know it doesn’t matter. The big thing is they were not going to have a nuclear weapon,” he added.
Trump's remarks came after the Axios news site reported Tuesday that he and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu discussed launching a major new operation against Iran ahead of elections in both countries.
The report, citing two US officials and other sources with knowledge of the matter, said the discussions took place before Trump publicly stated that he would not strike Iran before the US midterms.
US rejects Iran’s claim of control over Strait of Hormuz
The US military’s Central Command (CENTCOM) on Tuesday rejected claims by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) that it controls the Strait of Hormuz and would sink any approaching US Navy warships.
"IRGC's navy commander has no navy. American forces and regional partners clearly control the Strait of Hormuz," CENTCOM said on US social media company X.
🚫 CLAIM: The navy commander for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed today that the Strait of Hormuz is under IRGC control and any approaching U.S. Navy warships would be "sunk." ✅ FACT: IRGC's navy commander has no navy. American forces and regional partners… pic.twitter.com/n9dhNsyI8O
It disputed an Iranian navy commander’s remarks that Tehran controls the strategic international chokepoint, declaring that US forces had helped Gulf partners transport more than 19 million barrels of crude oil through the strait on Monday.
The statement came amid heightened tensions between Washington and Tehran about maritime security and control of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical passage for global oil shipments.

title: Balochistan eyes skilled workforce
description: Balochistan eyes skilled workforce
content:
B-TEVTA to train 30,000 youth for overseas jobs
The Balochistan government plans to provide vocational training to 25,000 young people and prepare 30,000 skilled workers for overseas employment by next year, Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti said, stressing the need to align skills development with domestic and international job market demands.
The targets were discussed at a meeting of the Balochistan Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority (B-TEVTA), chaired by the chief minister, which reviewed measures to strengthen technical education and expand employment prospects for young people.
Bugti directed officials to develop a comprehensive plan to help trained youth secure decent jobs and participate in the national and global economies. He said technical training programmes must keep pace with modern technology and the changing needs of employers.
He also called for stricter oversight and accountability to improve the performance of vocational training institutes and ensure that young people receive quality, market-oriented training.
Officials informed the meeting that an online institute registration portal had become operational to improve the registration and monitoring of technical and vocational education centres across the province.
The meeting also examined delays in the implementation of the Chief Minister's Youth Skill Development Programme. It was decided to take action against those responsible for the slow progress and accelerate work to meet the programme's objectives.
The chief minister reiterated his government's commitment to equipping young people with practical skills and connecting them with sustainable employment opportunities in Pakistan and abroad.
He said developing a skilled workforce was essential to expanding economic opportunities, strengthening Balochistan's economy and helping young people achieve financial independence.

title: Kundi seeks K-P police pay raise | The Express Tribune

police pay raise

Governor orders welfare package for family of martyrs
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Tuesday directed the authorities concerned to prepare and submit, at the earliest, a summary containing proposals for an increase in police salaries and an enhanced welfare package for the families of police martyrs.
Chairing a high-level meeting at the Governor House, he reviewed proposals relating to police salaries and welfare measures for the families of martyred and injured police personnel.
The meeting was attended by Adviser to Governor on Home Affairs Kifayatullah Khan, Chief Secretary Dr Muhammad Fakhr-e-Alam Irfan, Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed, Additional Chief Secretary Home Amjad Ali Khan and other senior police officials.
The IGP briefed the meeting on proposals for increasing police salaries, following which the governor instructed that a comprehensive summary be finalized and submitted without delay.
The meeting also reviewed proposals to enhance the 2025 compensation package for police martyrs and injured personnel. Among the recommendations discussed were replacing residential plots with cash financial assistance for the heirs of martyrs, providing financial support for the marriages of daughters of police martyrs, and establishing an endowment fund to meet the educational expenses of their children.
Agreeing with the proposals presented by the IGP, Governor Kundi directed the authorities concerned to expedite the preparation and submission of the summary for further action.
Meanwhile, Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has handed over 10 newly acquired Armoured Personnel Carriers (APCs) to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police on the directions of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to support its ongoing counterterrorism operations.
In a message posted on X, Mohsin Naqvi said the vehicles were transferred in view of the prevailing security situation and the rising number of terrorist incidents in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He said the prime minister had directed the immediate transfer of the vehicles to help the provincial police carry out its operations against terrorism.

title: Police claim situation in Khyber under control
description: Police claim situation in Khyber under control
content:
Deny cops abduction reports; urge people to not pay heed to 'rumours'
The Capital City Police Peshawar has urged the public not to pay heed to what it described as baseless rumours, saying the situation in Bara had been brought under control.
The police also denied reports that any personnel had been abducted and said around 50 people had been arrested for allegedly attempting to create unrest.
The statement said cases would be registered against those involved in damaging public property and disrupting law and order under relevant provisions relating to terrorism and sabotage, with strict legal action to follow.
Meanwhile, clashes erupted in Bara Bazaar on Tuesday during a protest by Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) workers against the imposition of governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, with protesters setting fire to a National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) office and allegedly taking 15 police personnel hostage, according to police.
A protest by the PTI turned violent in Bara Bazaar in Khyber district, with protesters setting fire to a NADRA office, damaging government property and pelting stones at a Rescue 1122 office.
Several people, including two children, were reportedly injured in firing during the protest.
PTI lawmaker Iqbal Afridi said 11 party workers had been injured and one killed. The casualties could not be independently verified.
Khyber District Police Officer Waqar Ahmed said hundreds of PTI workers gathered in Bara Bazaar on Tuesday afternoon to protest against governor's rule. Police used tear gas and fired into the air to disperse the crowd, which temporarily broke up.
About 90 minutes later, hundreds of protesters led by provincial assembly member Abdul Ghani marched from Minar Chowk towards Bara Chowk, chanting slogans against the government. They set fire to traffic signals upon reaching the intersection, according to the account provided by the district police chief.
As tensions escalated, protesters allegedly detained 15 police personnel inside the tehsil municipal office and took away their weapons and uniforms. Ahmed said the personnel remained in captivity at the time of reporting.
Protesters also set fire to the NADRA office and pelted the Rescue office with stones. Police again used tear gas and fired into the air to disperse the crowd. Two PTI workers were injured by tear gas shells during the demonstrations, Ahmed said.
Separately, reports from Bara Bazaar indicated that several people, including two children, had sustained gunshot wounds. Further details about the casualties were not immediately available.
Protests were also held at Bab-e-Khyber in Jamrud, where demonstrators chanted slogans against the government's measures. Further details about the demonstration were not immediately available.
Tensions remained high at several locations in Khyber district following the protests and violence. The status of the police personnel allegedly detained by protesters, the number of injured and the extent of damage to public property remained unclear.

title: Equipment provided to boost wheat production
description: Equipment provided to boost wheat production
content:
Initiative marks six decades of cooperation with Pakistan
The International Maize and Wheat Improvement Centre (CIMMYT) and the government of Pakistan have expanded their cooperation to strengthen wheat research, develop improved varieties and promote food security, with modern laboratory equipment and agricultural machinery being provided to research institutions.
A high-level delegation led by Dr Flavio Breseghello, director of CIMMYT's Global Wheat Program, visited the Wheat Research Institute at the Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI), Faisalabad, where a modern laboratory and working area was inaugurated.
The initiative marks six decades of agricultural cooperation between Pakistan and CIMMYT.
Under the project, modern equipment is being provided to laboratories at five research institutions, while experimental threshing equipment and other research facilities have been allocated to 11 institutions.
The initiative also included three seed cleaner-cum-graders and 10 zero-tillage seed-cum-fertiliser drills.
Punjab Agricultural Research Director General Dr Sajidur Rehman and Wheat Research Institute Chief Scientist Dr Javed Ahmad briefed the delegation on ongoing research and wheat varieties developed through collaboration between Pakistani scientists and CIMMYT.
Dr Sajidur Rehman said the institute's scientists had introduced more than 70 wheat varieties since 1960, including Mexi-Pak, Inqilab, Sehar, Punjab 2011, Faisalabad 2008, Akbar, Galaxy, Dilkash, Bhakkar Star, Fakhr-e-Bhakkar, Nawab, Sunehra and Falak.
An agricultural seminar was also held, bringing together scientists from AARI and progressive farmers to discuss innovation in wheat research and the use of modern machinery at different stages of cultivation, from sowing to harvesting.
Dr Breseghello said CIMMYT had been working with Pakistan since the 1960s to improve wheat yields. The introduction of its germplasm and its crossbreeding with local varieties had contributed to the development of improved wheat varieties and the country's agricultural progress, he added.
He said modern machinery and equipment provided to wheat research centres would strengthen research capacity and support the development of improved varieties, including those better able to withstand climate change.

title: Police failures delay trials  observes LHC
description: Police failures delay trials  observes LHC
content:
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has reprimanded the Punjab Police over incompetence undermining the criminal justice system and adding to the burden on courts.
The court asked how judges could be blamed for delays when police failures to complete investigations, arrest suspects in time and produce witnesses had stalled trials for years.
LHC Chief Justice Aalia Neelum sought an explanation from the provincial police chief over prolonged delays in investigations and failure to produce witnesses, asking how courts could be blamed for delays when police negligence was contributing to a massive backlog of cases.
The CJ was hearing a post-arrest bail petition filed by Muhammad Saim.
The court sought a report by October 19 on pending challans and cases under investigation, along with details of the department's mechanism to address the delay.
"IG sahib, have you examined this case? Your police officers are adding to the burden on courts. The challan remained pending for two years. When were the accused arrested, and why did the police not arrest them earlier?" the chief justice asked the Punjab Police chief who appeared before the court.
The chief justice remarked that police incompetence had damaged the judicial system, raising the question whether the court could be considered slow when judges were working but the police were failing to perform their duties.
"Is my court slow? The judge is working, while the police are protecting the accused. Should I appreciate this?" the chief justice remarked.
The court also asked what mechanism the police had devised to eliminate such delays and directed the inspector general of Punjab Police to submit a report, which would be examined in chamber.
During the hearing, the court was informed that the case involved 11 accused. The chief justice observed that, according to a report, the police had continued arresting new suspects even after witnesses had begun recording their statements, preventing the trial from concluding for six years.
The petitioner submitted that a double-murder case had been registered at Raiwind city police station in 2020, but the police had failed to complete the investigation or bring the trial to a conclusion. He claimed that he had remained in jail for six years and sought release on bail.
The court granted the police time to complete the investigation and produce the witnesses, while seeking a comprehensive report on pending challans and cases under investigation across Punjab.

title: 164k register in Green Credit Programme
description: 164k register in Green Credit Programme
content:
More than 164,000 citizens have registered with the Punjab government's Green Credit Programme, while 14,647 have earned the credits for various environmental initiatives.
Electric vehicles account for over 70 per cent of applications received under the programme, while initiatives related to water conservation, recycling at service stations and plastic waste management have attracted comparatively less interest.
According to programme data, a total of 46,365 registered participants are from Lahore and 114,913 from other districts of the province. Of them, 144,036 are men and 20,656 women.
The programme offers green credits for 38 environmental initiatives covering air pollution reduction, water conservation, land restoration, waste management, awareness and biodiversity.
Green Credit Programme task team leader Dr Muhammad Wajid Ejaz said electric bikes and cars had attracted the greatest interest among participants.
The programme also offers green credits to encourage rickshaw owners to switch to environmentally friendly electric three-wheelers without abandoning their livelihood.
Dr Ejaz said greater public and business participation was needed in water conservation initiatives. Under the programme, participants can receive Rs50,000 for installing rainwater harvesting systems and an additional Rs50,000 for arrangements to make the collected water reusable.
He said measures were also being taken to encourage service stations to treat and reuse wastewater, but progress in this area had remained limited.
Of the about 150 organisations working in plastic recycling, only three have registered with the programme so far.
The data shows that 7,908 participants have earned green credits for initiatives aimed at improving air quality. Another 2,867 have received credits for land improvement, 1,689 for waste management, 1,492 for environmental awareness, 279 for water conservation and efficient use, and 258 for biodiversity conservation.

title: CM cracks the whip on sanitation
description: CM cracks the whip on sanitation
content:
Orders dismissal of underperforming contractors, payment of workers' dues
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has given the relevant authorities a seven-day deadline to implement the Suthra Punjab beat system across the province, ordered the removal of underperforming private sanitation companies and directed officials to ensure payment of outstanding dues to the workers.
Chairing a meeting to review the programme on Tuesday, the chief minister sought a comprehensive micro-plan for cleanliness and a province-wide progress report by next week.
She also directed officials to ensure that the required workforce and machinery were available within a week.
It was decided that companies showing performance below 80 per cent in any tehsil would be issued warnings, while the contracts of those scoring below 50% would be terminated.
CM Maryam Nawaz ordered activation of government-run sanitation operations within a week as an alternative to services provided by non-performing private contractors.
The chief minister stressed that sanitation workers must not suffer because of unpaid dues from contractors.
It was agreed to recover outstanding payments from defaulting contractors and the officials were directed to devise a legal mechanism to ensure timely payment of workers' salaries and arrears.
The CM said workers would not be made to bear the contractors' failure to fulfil their financial obligations.
The chief minister ordered the submission of detailed weekly reports from every tehsil, covering human resources, machinery deployed under the beat system and field monitoring.
The participants were informed that the new system was intended to strengthen monitoring and service delivery.
The CM ordered that rural areas be cleaned at least on alternate days and accumulated garbage be removed without delay. The assistant commissioner and Suthra Punjab programme in-charge in each tehsil will be responsible for failures in cleanliness arrangements.
The system of waste collection and transportation was also reviewed and a proposal considered to introduce a mobile application for Suthra Punjab workers to improve monitoring and performance.
Officials said anti-littering squads were active in every division of Punjab and had conducted about 264,000 visits so far. The squads issued warnings for violations of sanitation standard operating procedures and spread awareness about waste disposal.
The CM reviewed cleanliness reports from various tehsils and praised the Chakwal administration for improvement in the district.

The Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD), in collaboration with the federal and civilian intelligence agencies, has arrested four suspected militants affiliated with two banned organisations in separate operations in the metropolis, and recovered four hand grenades and a pistol from their possession, officials said.

Preliminary investigations suggested that the suspects were allegedly planning to use hand grenades to attack sensitive locations and an office of a law enforcement agency in Karachi.
In a separate operation, the joint team arrested an alleged SRA militant near the Korangi Causeway stream. He was identified as Asif Ali, alias Asif Sindhi, son of Ashiq Ali Chachar. A hand grenade was recovered from his possession.
During preliminary interrogation, the suspect allegedly disclosed that he had conducted reconnaissance of a foreign national, a police deputy superintendent (DSP), a railway track and the residence of a prominent political figure. title: Gul Plaza management involved in fire tragedy

A judicial magistrate south on Tuesday heard the Gul Plaza fire case in which a shopkeeper, Arif, recorded his statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC). He alleged that most of the building's gates were locked, no fire alarm or firefighting system had been installed, and people were unable to find an escape route during the blaze.
During the hearing, Arif told the court that he had reached Gul Plaza around midnight and found flames at the building's 13 ground-floor gates, 12 of which, he claimed, were locked. He said a man was seen clinging to a window on the mezzanine floor and had died.
The witness said the fire spread throughout Gul Plaza within half an hour. He added that a fire had also broken out on the mezzanine floor in 2016, destroying 21 shops, including his office. An inquiry into that incident had found that Tanveer Pasta had not informed the fire brigade, he claimed.
Arif further alleged that although the building had a public-address system, occupants were not alerted. Videos showed people searching for a way out, but their escape routes were blocked, he said, adding that the electricity had also been switched off.
According to the witness, two stairways leading to the roof from the second floor had been blocked, while Tanveer Pasta had established an office in the rooftop area and placed scrap material in front of its entrance.
Arif claimed that around Rs10 million was collected every month in the head of maintenance charges from the building's five floors, in addition to revenue from billboards, mobile phone towers and parking contracts. Despite repeated requests, he said, the accounts had never been audited.
Referring to approximately Rs8 billion in financial assistance distributed by the Sindh government through the Chamber of Commerce, he alleged that applicants had to obtain verification from Tanveer Pasta to receive the funds.

title: Sindh seeks Chinese investment
description: Sindh seeks Chinese investment
content:
CM proposes K-IV pipeline, smart governance, barrage rehabilitation, climate-resilient agriculture
Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah has sought Chinese investment in water infrastructure, smart governance, pharmaceutical manufacturing and climate-resilient agriculture to strengthen the province's urban management, industrial capacity and food security, according to official statements issued by the provincial information department.
During his official visit to China, the chief minister met representatives of HBSZ Company, Huawei, Humanwell Healthcare Group and Qingfa Hesheng Agriculture Development Co Ltd to explore cooperation in the K-IV pipeline, Sukkur Barrage rehabilitation, artificial intelligence, pharmaceutical production and advanced seed technology.
At a meeting with HBSZ in Wuhan, the CM discussed the proposed 100-kilometre K-IV pipeline for Karachi. The company expressed willingness to undertake its construction, while the chief minister directed officials to initiate work at the earliest.
He also reviewed the Sukkur Barrage Improvement Project, being implemented by a joint venture of China Road and Bridge Corporation and HBSZ. Of the barrage's 54 river gates, 44 have been replaced and made functional, while the remaining 10 are ready for transportation to Pakistan. HBSZ is also fabricating 110 canal gates.
"Sukkur Barrage is extremely important to me. It is the economic lifeline of Sindh," Murad said, adding that its rehabilitation after 90 years had significantly improved water flows.
Launched in February 2023, the project is scheduled for completion by June 30, 2027, with financing from the World Bank and the federal and provincial governments. Rehabilitation of Guddu Barrage is also under way.
During visits to Huawei's urban governance facility and the Wuhan Artificial Intelligence Computing Centre, the CM explored technology-based solutions for public services and city management.
Briefed on systems using real-time data analytics and artificial intelligence, he said Karachi, with more than 20 million residents, could benefit from digital solutions for traffic congestion, water management, waste disposal and urban flooding.
He proposed a pilot project in one district focusing on flood early warning and city operations management, with expansion across Karachi later.
The chief minister also proposed cooperation in data centres, technology transfer, professional training and partnerships between Huawei and Sindh's universities.
Officials said the AI computing centre, launched in 2021, had expanded its capacity to 400 petaflops, providing computing resources to researchers, universities and technology companies.
The CM proposed giving Sindh's researchers access to AI training and advanced computing facilities, highlighting plans to develop Karachi Education City as a hub for research and emerging technologies.
The provincial government plans to pursue the Huawei proposals through a memorandum of understanding at the Sindh Investment and Trade Conference in Shanghai later this week.
CM Murad invited Humanwell Healthcare Group, also known as Renfu Pharmaceutical Group, to establish manufacturing facilities in Sindh for domestic and regional markets.
Discussions covered pharmaceutical manufacturing, active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and healthcare innovation. He highlighted investment incentives in special economic zones at Dhabeji, Bin Qasim and Khairpur, along with Port Qasim's connectivity.
Inviting Humanwell to replicate its manufacturing investments in Africa, he said Sindh could become an export base for Pakistan, the Middle East, Africa and Central Asia.
He urged the company to send a technical delegation to Karachi to assess joint ventures in APIs and finished medicines, assuring it of provincial facilitation and assistance with regulatory approvals.
The chief minister also invited Qingfa Hesheng Agriculture Development Co Ltd to collaborate on high-yield, climate-resilient crops, local seed production and agricultural technology.
During talks with Chairman Wang Shicai, he proposed joint research, farmer training and seed-production systems suited to Sindh's agricultural conditions.
The company briefed the delegation on its hybrid seeds, including rice, maize, cotton and rapeseed. Its hybrid rice varieties have reportedly achieved yield increases of 20 to 30 per cent in relevant trials.

title: JPMC incinerator shut despite repair funds
description: JPMC incinerator shut despite repair funds
content:
Disposal of used syringes, needles and other infectious medical waste is a big question
The incinerator used to dispose of medical waste at the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC) has reportedly remained non-functional and fallen into disrepair despite the release of government funds for its maintenance and rehabilitation, raising concerns about the safe disposal of potentially infectious hospital waste.
The Sindh health department has ordered an inquiry into the utilisation of repair funds, payments made and the current condition of the incinerator.
A complaint sent to Sindh Health Minister Dr Azra Fazal Pechuho alleged that the incinerator's building, machinery and internal combustion chamber were in a dilapidated condition. Exposed electrical wires and a faulty control panel could also make operating the machine hazardous, it said.
According to a notification issued by the health department, the inquiry committee will examine the utilisation of maintenance and rehabilitation funds during the financial year 2025-26 and determine whether the payments were justified under the rules. It will also investigate why the incinerator remains non-operational despite the expenditure of public funds. Additional Secretary General of the Sindh Health Department Zahid Junejo will head the committee, while Professor Dr Israr Ahmed Bhutto of Jinnah Sindh Medical University will serve as a member.
The committee has been directed to complete the inquiry and submit its report and recommendations within 15 days.
The complaint also levelled allegations of financial irregularities against Executive Engineer Ghulam Muhammad Wistaro and a divisional accounts officer named Munawar of the Karachi Central Electrical and Mechanical Division. The officials' responses were not available, and the allegations have yet to be independently verified.
The incinerator's continued closure has also raised questions about how used syringes, needles and other potentially infectious medical waste are being disposed of at the hospital, and whether alternative arrangements are in place. The inquiry committee's findings are expected to clarify how the public funds allocated for repairs were spent, why the incinerator could not be made operational and what arrangements have been made for the safe disposal of medical waste.

title: Financial woes drive family to  mass suicide
description: Financial woes drive family to  mass suicide
content:
Police recover 'suicide note' from head of family's pocket
The latest heartbreaking incident in the metropolis, in which an entire family died in an apparent murder-suicide, has once again raised serious concerns about the financial hardships people face amid rising inflation and the growing struggle to make ends meet.
The incident took place in Falak Naz Society, within the jurisdiction of Bin Qasim police station in Malir, where a family of five, including a man, his wife, younger sister and two children, were found dead inside their house.
SSP Malir Dr Abdul Khaliq Pirzada told The Express Tribune that the house was locked from the inside. When police broke open the door, they found the bodies of the head of the family, 30-year-old Shehryar, and his 28-year-old wife, Saba, seated on chairs. The bodies of Shehryar's 20-year-old younger sister, Shumaila, and two children, five-year-old Aizal and three-year-old Arya, were found on bedding spread on the floor in the same room.
The three appeared to be asleep, but foam was coming from their mouths, the SSP said. Shumaila lived with her brother.
Shehryar and Saba had a gunshot wound to the head, and a pistol was found nearby. A handwritten note was recovered from Shehryar's pocket in which he purportedly admitted to taking his own life and those of his family members.
According to the initial investigation, police suspect that Shehryar and his wife first administered poison to the children and Shamaila before shooting themselves.
However, the exact cause of death of all five will be established after post-mortem examinations, SSP Pirzada said.
The note recovered from Shehryar's pocket was stained red with what appeared to be his own blood. In it, he attributed the family's alleged suicide to financial hardship and the indifference of close relatives.
The note read: "The reason we are taking this step is that our relatives started harassing us. They say that we killed our father."
Shehryar's father had died in a traffic accident some time ago.
"We have no source of income. We asked our relatives to give us money, but they humiliated us. Our maternal aunts and paternal uncles blocked us so that we would not ask them for money.
"Sometimes we would seek financial help for groceries, sometimes for milk for the children, and sometimes to refill our gas cylinder. They left us helpless. They would neither meet us nor offer us any assistance.
"Whenever we went to visit them, they threw us out of their homes. They had promised our elders that they would look after us, but they abandoned us. The situation has become unbearable."
According to the note, Shehryar also expressed a final wish saying, "My last wish is that those who treated us this way should be made an example of. But we have no hope in the law. They are all shameless people who only come to funerals to eat biryani. Nobody comes for help."
Police forensic teams collected evidence and fingerprints from the scene.
SSP Pirzada said police were searching for samples of Shehryar's previous handwriting to compare them with the note recovered from his pocket and establish its authenticity.
Police also recovered a white powder from the house, which may have been a form of poison allegedly administered to the children and Shumaila. The substance has been taken into custody for laboratory test.
According to Malir Investigation Police, a relative had arranged for groceries to be delivered to Shehryar's house a day before the incident. Police said Shehryar had reportedly been suffering from severe depression due to financial difficulties, a claim corroborated by some neighbourhood residents.
The bodies were shifted to Jinnah Hospital for post-mortem examinations. Police have launched an investigation keeping the murder and suicide angles in view to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

title: Pakistan Post tightens restrictions on kite deliveries
description: Pakistan Post tightens restrictions on kite deliveries
content:
All offices directed to monitor movement, booking, delivery of kites, prohibited strings
Pakistan Post has directed all relevant offices to strictly monitor shipments and ensure compliance with instructions aimed at preventing the transportation and delivery of kites and prohibited strings ahead of Basant 2027, following directions from the Punjab government.
The decisions were taken at a high-level meeting convened by the provincial government to discuss arrangements for Basant.
Representatives of relevant government departments, law enforcement agencies, Pakistan Post and courier companies attended the meeting.
Participants agreed to prevent the delivery of kites and dangerous strings to protect human lives, strengthen monitoring mechanisms and take immediate action against violations.
In a letter issued by the postmaster general of the Central Punjab Circle, officials were warned of a possible increase in the use of kites and strings during Basant.
They were directed to closely monitor the movement, delivery, storage, sale and distribution of kites and metallic strings.
According to the letter, the transportation of kites and strings through any channel in Punjab is prohibited, including courier services, postal mail and online delivery systems.
All relevant departments and staff have been instructed to take effective measures to prevent attempts to transport prohibited materials.
The meeting specifically emphasised identifying and reporting metallic wires, metal-coated strings and other dangerous or prohibited kite-flying materials.
Upon receiving information about such materials, the relevant individuals, departments, transport operators, courier companies and online delivery services have been directed to immediately inform the nearest police station.
The letter also calls for the creation of dedicated WhatsApp groups to ensure prompt communication and information-sharing among relevant departments, preventing delays in identifying prohibited materials and taking action against those involved.
All relevant staff have been instructed to identify individuals attempting to book or transport kites and strings and immediately report such incidents to the concerned authorities, including the deputy commissioner's office.
Describing the protection of human lives as a shared responsibility, the letter says government departments, law enforcement agencies, transport operators, courier services, online delivery platforms and the public must work together to ensure that unauthorised, dangerous or prohibited kite-flying materials are not circulated, transported or delivered.

title: Kahuta Road project crawls on meagre funding
description: Only around one kilometre of the planned 28 4 kilometre dual carriageway has been completed so far
content:
Only around one kilometre of the planned 28.4-kilometre dual-carriageway has been completed so far
More than three months into the 2026-27 fiscal year, work has yet to formally begin on the Rawalpindi-Kahuta Road project, including the Sihala railway crossing overpass and Kahuta Bypass, despite its inclusion in the federal development budget. Only Rs1 billion has been allocated for the mega infrastructure project this fiscal year, raising concerns that its long-delayed completion will be pushed back by several more years.
The project's total estimated cost was listed at Rs23.845 billion in the 2025-26 budget. However, only around one kilometre of the planned 28.4-kilometre dual-carriageway has been completed so far.
According to details, the Rawalpindi-Kahuta Road is a strategically important route linking the garrison city with two routes to Azad Kashmir. The project includes the construction of a dual-carriageway from Soan to Kahuta, a four-lane overpass at the Sihala railway crossing, the Sihala Bypass and the Kahuta Bypass.
The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) approved the project on July 27, 2023. Despite its approval, progress has remained slow. During the previous fiscal year, only about one kilometre of dual-carriageway was completed between Kahuta and Hothla Stop. A partially developed route for the Kahuta Bypass was also prepared before work was suspended.
The project has again been included in the 2026-27 federal budget under the National Highway Authority's ongoing schemes, with a revised total cost of approximately Rs23.545 billion.
Budget documents estimated expenditure on the project at Rs6.587 billion by June 30, 2026, while Rs16.958 billion was carried forward into the new fiscal year as the remaining cost to be financed. However, the allocation for 2026-27 stands at just Rs1 billion.
The limited funding is expected to prevent the project from being completed this year, extending delays that have already persisted for several years.

title: IHC orders crackdown on illegal shisha caf  s
description: IHC orders crackdown on illegal shisha caf  s
content:
Court seeks affidavits to stop illegal operations; govt's regulations await approval
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday directed the chief commissioner and deputy commissioner of Islamabad to submit affidavits assuring that no illegal shisha cafés are allowed to operate in the federal capital, questioning how such establishments continue to function without the required no-objection certificates (NOCs).
Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar observed that shisha cafés should not operate in Islamabad until the government framed proper rules and regulations, stressing that the absence of a regulatory framework could not be used to justify illegal activities.
Separately, the Inspector General of Islamabad Police has submitted a report to the court detailing enforcement action against shisha cafés, maintaining that allegations of police negligence were contrary to the facts. The report records 89 cases registered between January 1 and September 7, 2026, involving 282 suspects.
Hearing a petition against shisha cafés operating without NOCs, the chief justice questioned whether the government had formulated rules to regulate these establishments. He said the court had previously directed the authorities to allow only cafés operating in accordance with the law, but its order had been misinterpreted.
The chief commissioner, deputy commissioner, IGP, Prosecutor General Manzoor Jhajja, Advocate General Naveed Malik and Deputy Attorney General Arshad Kayani appeared before the court following directions for their immediate attendance.
During the proceedings, the government counsel informed the court that draft rules for shisha cafés had been prepared and forwarded to the government for approval, which was expected soon.
The CJ recalled that the court had earlier been told that closing the cafés would leave many people unemployed. However, he stressed that the authorities needed to establish whether existing establishments were complying with the applicable requirements.
"If we keep granting extensions, young people will continue using shisha," the chief justice observed, adding that children were being introduced to the habit and that such activities could not be allowed to continue indefinitely.
He said the cafés could be temporarily closed until the rules were finalised and a decision taken on their future. If the government failed to formulate the regulations, he added, it should introduce its own standard operating procedures (SOPs).
The Prosecutor General informed the court that the Supreme Court had imposed a ban on shisha cafés in a suo motu case. The petitioner's counsel suggested that keeping the establishments closed for 15 to 20 days would provide sufficient time to finalise the rules. The director of legal affairs at the Islamabad Inspector General's office also argued that the activity should be stopped in the absence of a governing law.
The chief justice questioned why people should be allowed to use shisha even at the top of a mountain, asking why the public should suffer for the sake of one group.

title: UNDP moves to address liquidity crunch
description: UNDP moves to address liquidity crunch
content:
The United Nations Development Programme on Tuesday announced new initiatives to help attract investors and jobs to developing countries, which are being rocked by crises outside their control amid a sharp drop in official development aid.
UNDP Administrator Alexander De Croo said the agency was increasing its cooperation with the World Bank, and forging new ties to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the European Investment Bank, other financial institutions and private investors, to advance the investment and jobs agenda.
Developing countries needed to undertake reforms to improve governance, improve the rule of law and boost domestic revenues, but progress on that front had been slowed by a series of crises since the COVID pandemic, De Croo told Reuters. "The way development is being financed is changing, and that's a good thing, but we need to create some space for those countries to be able to implement those reforms," De Croo added on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok, Thailand. help countries to become investable."

title: Houthis fire barrage of missiles at KSA
description: Houthis fire barrage of missiles at KSA
content:
Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen oil sites
Loud booms were heard on Tuesday night near the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company, the world's largest and the backbone of the kingdom's economy, in Dhahran, six sources told Reuters, amid an escalating war between Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition.
There was no official comment from the company, Saudi Aramco. A source with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters the Aramco headquarters had been struck, though it was unclear if the building had been hit directly or by falling debris.
One source said the Aramco headquarters was on fire. An evacuation order for the building had been issued, four sources said.
The Saudi-led coalition said fragments of a missile that it had intercepted and destroyed in Dhahran had fallen on a residential area without providing further details.
Authorities also reported drones and missiles were intercepted and destroyed in the capital, Riyadh, and the country's southern region.
The Houthis earlier said Saudi Arabia was attacking the Yemeni capital Sanaa and a Saudi-led coalition warned civilians to stay away from an oil depot on the city's outskirts.
Houthi-run Al-Masirah television reported that the Saudi-led coalition had targeted the Yemen Petroleum Company's Sabah central station, a fuel depot on the outskirts of Sanaa.
Saudi Arabia carried out new airstrikes Tuesday on the Houthi rebel-held Yemeni capital of Sanaa, the Houthis said, after the Saudi-led coalition warned civilians to stay away from an oil depot on the city outskirts, part of a rapidly escalating war between the sides.
Witnesses in Sanaa reported hearing explosions, and the Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV channel said "Saudi aggression targets the oil company in Al-Sabaha, west of Sanaa."
Footage posted to social media showed a large oil fire burning in al-Subaha, just outside the capital. Other footage showed the aftermath of several smaller strikes within Sanaa.
The Saudi-led coalition confirmed later Tuesday it had targeted a Yemeni oil company facility in Sanaa and two sites in other provinces, hours after urging civilians to evacuate the area of the strike in the Houthi-held capital.
Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said on X that the facilities, including those in Saada and Dhamar provinces in western Yemen, were used to "supply the war effort" by the Houthis to "threaten the kingdom, Yemen, the southern Red Sea and waterways."
The strikes came as Saudi Arabia was reportedly scrambling to determine how its air defenses failed to intercept a barrage of missiles and drones fired by the Houthis, including an attack on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday that killed at least 13 people and wounded over 300.
The Saudi-led coalition said on Tuesday that it intercepted and destroyed six missiles and drones launched by the Houthi group toward Saudi Arabia.
Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki announced in separate posts on the US social media company X that forces intercepted one missile heading toward Haradh and another toward Dhahran in the eastern kingdom.
Earlier, the coalition said it intercepted and destroyed three drones north of the Saudi capital, Riyadh.
Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense issued a warning earlier Tuesday of "potential danger" in the Eastern Province and Riyadh before announcing minutes later that the danger had passed.

title: Pope Leo diagnosed with cancer
description: Pope Leo diagnosed with cancer
content:
Pope Leo was diagnosed with a common form of lung cancer after doctors removed a lower lobe of his right lung in surgery on Tuesday, the Vatican said in a medical bulletin.
The 71-year-old pontiff has lung adenocarcinoma, with tissue tests conducted during the operation confirming what doctors had suspected from preparatory examinations, the bulletin said.
The pope was admitted to Rome's Gemelli hospital on Tuesday for surgery to remove a growth on his lung that doctors found in a recent health checkup.
The Vatican had said earlier on Tuesday evening that the surgery had been successful before providing a more detailed update from the pope's lead surgeon, Professor Stefano Margaritora, the chief of thoracic surgery at the Gemelli.
"In order to make the procedure curative, the lower lobe of the right lung was removed using a video-assisted technique," said Margaritora's update.
"A rapid intraoperative histological examination confirmed the diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, as had been suspected from the pre-operative tests," it said.

title: Scientists demand AI supervision
description: Scientists demand AI supervision
content:
Call for setting up of body to oversee cyber capable systems
Around 400 scientists, including AI pioneers Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio, on Tuesday called for an international body to oversee containment standards and incident reporting for advanced cyber-capable AI systems.
The proposed body would set industry-wide containment standards and maintain a registry of significant security incidents, which the scientists said should eventually be made public.
In an open letter, the researchers said frontier AI models should initially be air-gapped from external networks and subject to independent oversight, arguing that voluntary industry commitments are not enough.
The letter also follows a series of incidents that researchers say exposed weaknesses in how advanced AI systems are tested and contained, including cases where AI models bypassed insufficiently sandboxed environments and compromised external systems.
The signatories from 34 countries said organisations developing or testing cyber-capable models should immediately adopt high-assurance containment standards while governments work towards a more formal oversight regime.
Policymakers are increasingly debating how advanced AI systems should be supervised. EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen told Reuters on Friday that the bloc's AI Act is sufficient to address risks from rogue AI systems.
On Sunday, the Trump administration lifted its block on US labs giving Britain's AI Security Institute early access to models for safety testing.
Hinton and Bengio shared the 2018 Turing Award with Meta's Yann LeCun, another leading AI researcher.

title: Indian police detain CJP leaders

content:
Calls for election chief to stand down grow
India's "cockroach" youth movement leaders were detained on Tuesday after they jumped barricades to enter a historic Delhi site popular for protests, demanding that the chief election commissioner resign over a revision of voter lists.
Supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and opposition groups have held almost daily protests this month to demand commissioner Gyanesh Kumar stand down over the revisions critics say favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) by removing the names of millions of voters.
The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol, while the BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.
Thousands joined a protest march by opposition groups on Monday, after a clampdown foiled CJP plans for a weekend demonstration, with police detaining thousands of protesters, including CJP leaders.
Delhi Police announced on Monday that the Jantar Mantar open air observatory, in the national capital's central business district, was no longer designated as an official protest site, and said three new venues had been identified.
The CJP said its leaders Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das, and Ajinkya Shinde were among about 20 people who "sneaked" inside the observatory to "reclaim" it and were detained.
A CJP livestream showed about a dozen people jumping a gate and barricades to reach the site, where they waved the Indian flag and chanted slogans before police detained them. Delhi Police did not respond to a request for comment.
The youth movement, which has mobilised protests in recent months against issues ranging from government school infrastructure to jobs, is among the biggest political challenges to Modi and his BJP in his 12 years in power.

title: Reboot  through K P under consideration  says Vawda
description: Reboot  through K P under consideration  says Vawda
content:
'Reboot' through K-P under consideration, says Vawda
Senator Faisal Vawda said on Tuesday that a "reboot or restart" option through Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) was under consideration and declared that the political show of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) was over now.
Addressing a press conference, Vawda said K-P's deteriorating law and order situation had made the imposition of an emergency inevitable. The decision to impose an emergency in the province had been taken in the public interest, he added.
"What you are seeing today, I told you all about this a year ago," he said, adding that K-P had been governed for 13 years by people with a particular mindset. He claimed that 7,500 people, including Army personnel and police officers, had embraced martyrdom, stressing that the province's security situation required decisive action.
"There is no room for failure," he said, adding that Governor Faisal Karim Kundi would be questioned following the establishment of a new setup in K-P. "If they fail, others will come," he said. He predicted that results in the province would begin to become visible within 60 days.
The senator issued a stern warning to those who disrespected Pakistan's flag. "We will destroy the generations of those who do not raise Pakistan's flag. Those who spoke against a martyr will have their tongues ripped out," he said.
Questioning the slogan that Pakistan could not survive without a particular leader, Vawda said the country would endure regardless of individuals. He argued that people could no longer be expected to adopt a leader's slogans and follow blindly.
Vawda said Pakistan's ability to defeat an enemy 10 times its size demonstrated that the country could accomplish anything. He added that the public would judge political leaders by their performance rather than their slogans. He expressed the hope that Governor Kundi would deliver results.
Turning to the PTI, Vawda claimed that members of the party's cabinet had been present with him in Islamabad and were themselves embroiled in disputes over smuggled vehicles. He said several matters would be brought to the attention of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and President Asif Ali Zardari, adding that evidence would be presented only to them.
He stressed that the "reboot or restart" through K-P was being mulled over. Vawda said the nation must recognise Field Marshal Asim Munir's achievements and honour the sacrifices of martyrs. He urged people to openly support the field marshal.

title: Passenger train derails near Multan  seven killed  50 hurt
description: Passenger train derails near Multan  seven killed  50 hurt
content:
Minor girl among dead; railway minister orders probe
A passenger train derailed near Multan on Tuesday morning, resulting in the death of at least seven people including a minor child and injuring over 50 others.
According to officials, Peshawar-bound Rehman Baba Express met the tragedy at Sher Shah Bridge at around 5:15am when a number of its carriages went off the tracks, with some overturning
Soon after the incident, rescue workers and the Pakistan Army teams arrived at the accident site and started shifting the dead and the injured to the hospital.
Rescue sources claimed that at least seven people including three women, two men and a one-and-a-half-year-old girl died as a result of the derailment. They said over fifty people were transferred to hospital for treatment and a few of these injured were in critical condition.
A spokesperson for Multan's Nishtar Hospital said 21 patients were still receiving treatment, while one injured person was in critical condition. The hospital had called in additional staff to ensure medical care for the victims.
The cause of the derailment remained unclear. Some sources claimed that the train was travelling at a high speed when the accident occurred, but this claim could not be independently verified.
A passenger also claimed that the nuts and bolts of coach No 9 of the Rehman Baba Express had been repaired near Rohri. However, the account could not be independently verified, and it was unclear whether the reported repair had any connection with the accident.
Federal Minister for Railways Hanif Abbasi took notice of the incident and directed the authorities to ensure the provision of the best possible medical facilities to the injured.
He expressed solidarity with the families of those killed and said compensation would be paid to the deceased and injured passengers in accordance with the Pakistan Railways insurance policy.
The minister visited the accident site to review the situation and oversee rescue and relief operations. He also constituted a committee to investigate the incident and directed the Federal Government Inspector of Railways to conduct an inquiry into the derailment.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also took notice of the accident and expressed grief over the loss of precious lives. He extended his best wishes for the speedy recovery of the injured and directed the relevant authorities to expedite rescue operations and ensure that all medical facilities were provided.
The accident disrupted train schedules, particularly services travelling from Karachi towards Rawalpindi. Railway officials said some trains were being diverted through an alternative route, while clearing the affected track and completing relief operations could take several more hours.
Railway authorities said train operations had been restored via the Lodhran-Jahanian route.
Rescue operations continued at the accident site as authorities worked to clear the derailed carriages and establish the cause of the tragedy.
