title: Opp calls K P emergency  pre planned
description: Opp calls K P emergency  pre planned
content:
Terms negotiations a sham as decision had already been taken
Senate Leader of Opposition Allama Raja Nasir Abbas on Tuesday alleged that the federal government had long planned to remove the PTI government in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), claiming that negotiations with the opposition had been a "sham" because the decision had already been made.
Speaking in the Senate, Abbas said the opposition had even withdrawn its demand for a meeting with incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan to facilitate an agreement during talks, but the government had refused to budge on its position.
"We had agreed on political issues during the negotiations. The problem arose when security issues were discussed, and you linked political matters with law and order," he said.
The opposition leader asked whether conditions in K-P had deteriorated to the extent that the elected provincial government had to be removed.
He warned that the move could deepen alienation and undermine confidence in democratic processes. He also cautioned that the action could worsen insecurity rather than help restore peace.
Allama Raja Nasir Abbas urged the government to reverse its action, arguing that governor's rule would not establish peace and could harm the country.
PTI Senator Ali Zafar also challenged the legality of the federal action, saying the Constitution did not permit the government to use emergency provisions or Governor's Rule as a political instrument to take control of a province.
He said the opposition supported a collective effort against terrorism but warned against sacrificing constitutional protections in the process. If the government believed provincial officials were involved in terrorism or facilitating militants, it should present evidence before parliament, he added.
Zafar referred to Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, arguing that the provisions could not be invoked at the government's discretion. He called for the decision to be withdrawn and urged the government to return to negotiations.
The opposition subsequently staged a protest in the Senate.
Responding to the criticism, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi maintained that the measures taken in K-P were in accordance with the Constitution and that the federal government had carefully reviewed the legal implications with the PML-N and the PPP.
He offered to constitute a committee to examine the imposition of governor's rule and determine whether any constitutional violation had occurred.
Naqvi disputed the opposition's account of the negotiations, saying talks had initially focused on terrorism and that PTI leader Asad Qaiser had indicated a willingness to cooperate with the government on security matters.
According to him, Qaiser had also taken responsibility for discussing the issue with the K-P government.
Naqvi said the government had continued contacting PTI leaders until shortly before the decision. He recounted discussions involving Gohar Ali Khan and efforts to secure a recorded message from Imran to defuse a protest, claiming that the process had failed after disagreements within the PTI leadership.
Naqvi further alleged that some PTI figures had direct contacts with the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), adding that the government was prepared to provide evidence.
He said around 80% of those involved in terrorism were coming from Afghanistan and insisted that the federal government's sole objective was to eliminate terrorism and bring K-P's youth into that effort.
Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar also defended the decision, saying negotiations had failed at the final stage after the K-P chief minister was consulted and declined to agree to the proposed arrangement.
Dar argued that political reconciliation could not continue indefinitely while the security situation deteriorated. He said K-P had received about Rs800 billion over 13 years to support its fight against terrorism, including funding linked to the National Finance Commission.
He alleged that the province still lacked a forensic lab and questioned the effectiveness of its counterterrorism efforts. He accused the PTI government of failing to contain terrorism, claiming that attacks during the preceding year had exceeded the number recorded over the previous three years.
The deputy prime minister said the federal cabinet had concluded that the time for political reconciliation had passed and that the province's security problems required urgent action.
Separately, PTI Chief Whip Amir Dogar has written to National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq, seeking production orders for nine arrested opposition lawmakers to attend the assembly session.
In his letter, Dogar invoked Rule 108 of the National Assembly's Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business, arguing that no constituency should be deprived of representation in the elected house because its representative was in custody.
The lawmakers named in the request are Haji Imtiaz Ahmed Chaudhry, Jamal Ahsan Khan, Mian Ghaus Muhammad, Sanaullah Khan Masti Khel, Dawar Khan Kundi, Junaid Akbar, Amjad Ali Khan, Fazal Muhammad Khan and Adil Khan Bazai.

title: Panel seeks provincial quotas in promotions
description: Panel seeks provincial quotas in promotions
content:
Panel seeks provincial quotas in promotions
The Senate Committee on Devolution on Tuesday instructed the federal government to apply provincial quota on promotions to higher grades after it emerged that there was only one federal secretary from Balochistan out of 38 divisions.
Headed by PPP's Senator Zamir Hussain Ghumro, the committee also gave two-week time to the federal government to either handover half of oil and gas well heads with provinces or to share their profits to implement the Article 172(3) of the Constitution in letter and spirit.
In case the government fails to provide an acceptable mechanism, the committee threatened to take punitive measures against the Petroleum Division officials.
The committee, which is mandated to implement the 18th Constitutional Amendment, took up the issue of lack of implementation of provincial job quotas in breach of Article 38(g) and denying provinces their rights in oil and gas sectors in breach of Article 172(3).
There is only one federal secretary, who has Balochistan domicile, out of 38 serving in as many divisions, the additional secretary establishment informed the committee.
"There is an insurgency going on in Balochistan and we have only one federal secretary from the province out of 38 divisions", remarked Ghumro.
The chair said that the implementation of the 18th Constitutional Amendment is the counter to the insurgency – a statement that was also fully endorsed by Establishment Division Secretary, Nabeel Awan.
But the establishment secretary was of the view that there was no quota against the promotions, to which the committee did not agree. The federal government is predominately run by bureaucrats, having Punjab domicile and small provinces feel deprived, the chair noted.
The committee instructed that there were three modes of appointments which include initial appointment by departments and FPSC, appointment by transfer and appointment by promotion.
The chairman said that under the Article 38(g) the federal government has to maintain shares of provinces in all modes of appointments. "They have to cure this omission immediately and post secretaries from officers of other province," he added.
Balochistan's quota in the federal service was determined at 4.5% in 1973, which was increased to 6% by former prime minister Imran Khan in 2020, according to the Establishment Division's written reply.
But the details submitted by the Establishment Division revealed that from grades 1-16 there were 31,235 employees having Balochistan domicile, which was equal to 5.2% and falling below the quota. Likewise, in officer category grade 17-22, there were only 1,287 officers from Balochistan, hardly 3.5% of the total employment.
"The Establishment Division's position is clear, whether someone likes it or not, and it is that all the provinces should get their shares in service as per the constitutional requirements," said Awan, who is also working as chairman of the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).
The federal government would soon start a proactive campaign to fill thousands of vacant positions against Balochistan's quota, said Nabeel Awan. But the written reply showed that these positions will be filled against grade 1 to 16 and Balochistan may not get any share against the highest positions, barring promotions on the basis of merit and seniority.
The written reply showed that the Establishment Division has recently submitted a draft summary for approval of the prime minister, which is under process for seeking one-time exemption from the recruitment ban under the austerity measures for filling existing vacant posts in BS 1 to 16 reserved against the Balochistan quota.
But it added that the recruitment under the proposal would remain subject to the applicable rules, qualifications and prescribed merit procedure.
The Article 38(g) of the Constitution requires that provincial shares in federal services, including autonomous bodies and corporations established or under the control of the federal government, be secured and past omissions rectified, Ghumro stressed.
The Establishment Division informed that a special CSS examination in 2023 was approved to fill accumulated unfilled quota vacancies in the eligible provinces, regions and categories and the upper age was relaxed to 35 years.
In June this year, the Establishment Division had informed that 3,384 posts allocated to Balochistan were currently lying vacant.
The Devolution Committee took exception to the violation of Article 172(3). The committee emphasised that Article 172 envisaged equal participation of the Federation and the provinces in matters relating to natural oil and gas and stressed that board compositions should fully reflect this constitutional principle.
It noted that the federal government was not implementing the Constitution. The Petroleum Division has two options, either hand over half of well-heads to the provinces where these are located or share the declared audited profits with the province, the committee chairman said.
"If our instructions are not implemented, we can move against the officers either under NAB law for misuse of authority, under the Contempt of Parliament Act or to invoke Article 6 for subversion of the Constitution, he added.
The Article 172(3) states that the mineral oil and natural gas within a province or its adjacent territorial waters vest jointly or equally in the province and the federal government, subject to the existing arrangement.
The Petroleum Division took a stance that the Article 172(3) does not expressly specify a mechanism for transferring company shares, profits, assets or management rights.
It added that the joint and equal constitutional vesting is fully recognised, existing Article 161 entitlements regarding well-head federal excise duty net proceeds and royalty collected by the federal government remain unaffected.
The Petroleum Division was also of the view that shareholding, dividend distributions and governance of oil and gas sector companies are regulated by the Companies Act 2017 and SOEs Act 2023, petroleum laws and contracts.
The Petroleum Division recommended referring the matter to the Council of Common Interests (CCI) to seek clarification as to how Article 172(3) operates alongside Article 161 and existing laws. The chair said that the SOE Act will not apply to the oil and gas sector companies where there is joint ownership.

title: Failed talks forced K P emergency  says PM
description: Failed talks forced K P emergency  says PM
content:
Failed talks forced K-P emergency, says PM
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Tuesday that the federal government was left with no option but to take constitutional measures to impose an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) after efforts to resolve the deteriorating security situation in the province through dialogue failed.
Shehbaz took lawmakers from his Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and coalition partners - the Balochistan Awami Party (BAP), Istehkam-e-Pakistan Party (IPP), PML-Zia, PML-Q and Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) - into confidence over the imposition of emergency in K-P.
The PML-N parliamentary party and the allied leaders endorsed Sunday's proclamation of emergency and governor's rule in K-P, as the prime minister explained that the decision followed consultations with coalition partners and detailed deliberations in the federal cabinet.
Addressing a meeting of the PML-N parliamentary party, Shehbaz said the government had repeatedly offered negotiations and cooperation to the provincial leadership but had failed to secure a positive response. "It's now or never," he recalled telling the cabinet, explaining the urgency of the situation.
He said the government's priorities were to restore peace, improve law and order and accelerate development in the province. The PML-N parliamentary party endorsed the government's strategy, while a National Assembly resolution concerning the emergency was planned for Wednesday (today).
Separately, the prime minister told a parliamentary delegation comprising representatives of the PML-Q, BAP, IPP and PML-Zia that the federal cabinet had decided to take constitutional measures under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution.
He accused the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led K-P government of failing to take a clear stance against terrorism and act effectively against terrorist groups. He said attacks had intensified, targeting civilians, police and security personnel, while abductions and other incidents had deepened insecurity.
Shehbaz said the federal government had provided more than Rs800 billion to K-P but the provincial government had failed to adequately strengthen its Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) or establish Safe City projects to improve law enforcement and surveillance.
He also criticised the PTI's performance during its 13 years in power in the province, accusing it of failing to deliver adequately on public welfare and protect citizens' lives and property. He said long marches, sit-ins and political protests had taken precedence over counterterrorism efforts.
The prime minister said the federal government intended to focus on education, healthcare, infrastructure and other essential services alongside restoring security. "Peace and stability are essential to sustaining improvements in economic indicators, reducing poverty and creating employment," he said.
Shehbaz said a technocratic advisory council had been established to assist the governor in improving governance, strengthening the economy and tackling terrorism. "The council includes professionals from fields such as health, education and finance," he added.
The allied parties' delegation said the people of K-P had been deprived of adequate development in health, education and infrastructure during the PTI's tenure. It expressed confidence that federal cooperation would help bring the province's development closer to that of other parts of the country.
The prime minister told the delegation that the government aimed to strengthen the police and CTD, expand their capacity and establish Safe City projects as part of its broader response. The delegation expressed support for the proposed measures.
The move also received backing from the MQM-P, whose delegation, led by party convener and Federal Minister for Education Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui, called on the prime minister and expressed support for the government's proposed measures concerning K-P.
During the meeting, Shehbaz briefed the MQM-P leadership on the provincial situation and the government's future course of action. Discussions covered the broader political situation, the security crisis and the potential consequences of the proposed measures.
The MQM-P also urged the prime minister to address what it described as poor law and order and governance in Sindh. Its leaders called for an immediate meeting involving the Sindh chief minister and the party's two federal ministers to discuss problems confronting the province's urban areas.
According to sources, MQM-P leader Dr Farooq Sattar urged the government to devise a strategy to address the tendency to stage protests in Karachi following incidents elsewhere in the country. The government assured the party that its concerns would be addressed and responded positively to its request.
In a related development, PML-N leader Rana Sanaullah told reporters that the government had been compelled to act, adding that K-P needed to demonstrate improved performance. He rejected the possibility of negotiations with those advocating the breakup of Pakistan.
"Terrorists had only one demand: that Balochistan be separated from Pakistan. How can negotiations be held with those who talk about breaking up Pakistan?" he asked, adding that this was also the narrative being advanced by the PTI.
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, meanwhile, said terrorism in K-P had increased by 200% over the past five years. He said Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman had attempted to resolve the situation through negotiations, but the PTI had abandoned dialogue.
Tarar accused the PTI government in K-P of prioritising social media activities over education and institutional development. He said the federal government's measures were intended to restore security, improve governance and accelerate development in the province.

title: Army tests hypersonic Fatah 2 missile
description: Army tests hypersonic Fatah 2 missile
content:
The Pakistan Army on Tuesday conducted a successful test launch of the hypersonic ballistic missile Fatah-2 extended range, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement, adding that the weapon system was equipped with advanced navigation and state-of-the-art avionics.
"It is capable of engaging targets with high precision and defeating the enemy's missile defence systems due to its unique trajectory and manoeuvrability features. Fatah-2 ER, with its extended range, will further enhance the army's reach and capability of engaging deep targets," said the military's media wing.
The launch was witnessed by the commander of the Army Rocket Force Command (Comd ARFC), senior officers from the Pakistan Army and committed scientists and engineers, the ISPR said, adding that the ARFC commander "appreciated the dedication and technical prowess of scientists and engineers."
The statement also noted that President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir, along with service chiefs, congratulated the scientists and engineers on the successful test launch.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi congratulated the nation on the successful test launch, stating that the scientists and engineers of the Pakistan Army had achieved a commendable feat. He added that the test was a significant development in the defence sector.
Last week, an indigenously developed extended version of the Fatah-4 ground-launched cruise missile was successfully test launched. The weapon system was equipped with advanced avionics and state-of-the-art navigational aids and could engage targets at extended ranges with "high precision and lethality," the ISPR had said.
The test also validated additional "technical parameters" of various sub-systems incorporated for improved accuracy and enhanced survivability, it added.

title: PPP Punjab defends governor s rule
description: PPP Punjab defends governor s rule
content:
Says state security outweighs political interests after dialogue failed
The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) has defended the imposition of governor's rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa as necessary to save the country, invoking its old narrative to justify a move it says was constitutionally required.
The party has taken this position multiple times since the formation of the PML-N-led federal government to justify seemingly undemocratic decisions, arguing that the protection of the state, public safety and law and order must take precedence over political interests.
Addressing a press conference and answering media questions at the Peoples Secretariat in Model Town, alongside Syed Hassan Murtaza, General Secretary of PPP Central Punjab, PPP Secretary General Humayun Khan said the party had supported difficult and unpopular constitutional decisions by prioritising the protection of the state and the public over political interests.
He said he had come to Punjab to discuss organisational matters and that, when faced with a choice between saving the country and pursuing politics, the PPP had prioritised Pakistan and its people.
"For us, the country and the people come first; politics comes later," he said.
Employment, business activity and economic stability, he added, were inconceivable without law and order. Instead of making state affairs contingent upon the release of a single individual, he said, the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) should focus on public issues, law and order, and unemployment.
Syed Hassan Murtaza said the PPP had pursued negotiations and dialogue to improve the situation, but circumstances had become increasingly complex because of the lack of a positive response.
The government, in collaboration with security agencies, had tried to normalise the situation and was ultimately compelled to take certain constitutional measures that were not politically palatable.
He said the declaration issued under the president's signature complied with constitutional requirements and that the PPP had exercised its constitutional prerogative with a heavy heart. Prioritising the state's interests over political gains, he said, was essential.
The PPP had stood by the state despite the political costs, he added, praying that Allah Almighty protect Pakistan and its people from all manner of threats.
Murtaza said the imposition of governor's rule was neither a matter of pride nor a source of happiness for the PPP. However, when the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister was unwilling to engage in dialogue, he said, considering alternative constitutional avenues became inevitable to improve the law-and-order situation in the province.
He questioned what measures should be taken to prevent a clash between state institutions when federal and provincial forces confront one another.

content:
Russia interior minister thanks Pakistan for support at int'l fora
President Asif Ali Zardari on Tuesday called for enhanced Pakistan-Russia cooperation in trade, energy, industrial development, regional connectivity and counterterrorism, emphasising the need to translate the goodwill between the two countries' leaderships into tangible benefits for their people.
He expressed these views while talking to Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev, who called on him at Aiwan-e-Sadr.
Welcoming the Russian interior minister to Pakistan, the president said bilateral relations continue to grow independently of geopolitical considerations and relations with third countries.
He stressed the importance of making full use of existing institutional mechanisms to advance cooperation across various sectors.
The president said bilateral trade, which stood at $243.412 million in the financial year 2025, remained below its potential.
He described Russia as an important energy partner and expressed Pakistan's interest in expanding cooperation in the oil and gas sectors.
Emphasising the importance of regional connectivity, President Zardari said Pakistan's geographical position makes it a natural bridge between South, Central and West Asia. He expressed interest in strengthening connectivity through the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC), as well as rail and road links through Central Asia.
He also stressed the need for the early resumption of direct flights and improved cargo connectivity between Pakistan and Russia.
On people-to-people and educational ties, the president appreciated the manifold increase in visas issued by Pakistan to Russian nationals and called for reciprocal visa facilitation for Pakistani businessmen, tourists and students as well.
He also expressed satisfaction over the growing number of Pakistani students pursuing higher education in Russia and highlighted the need to address their visa, residency and immigration-related difficulties.
Discussing regional security, President Zardari expressed deep concern over escalating tensions in the Gulf, particularly attacks on maritime traffic, energy installations and critical infrastructure. He said the conflict posed serious challenges to regional stability, global energy security, trade and supply chains.
He stressed respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states, urged the parties to exercise restraint and honour their commitments under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, and called for resolving differences through dialogue and diplomacy.
He also underlined the importance of safe maritime navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

title: No mercy for marriage refusal murderer  SC
description: No mercy for marriage refusal murderer  SC
content:
Rejects plea to commute death sentence to life sentence
The Supreme Court held that the principle of life expectancy cannot be applied to commute the death sentence of a man convicted of murdering a young woman because she had refused to marry him, declaring that the killing constituted a grave and aggravated offence with no mitigating circumstances.
A three-member bench, led by Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar, dismissed the convict's review petition seeking to convert his death sentence to life imprisonment on the ground that he had spent 14 years in jail.
In a nine-page judgment authored by Justice Kakar, the court said the murder of an innocent woman solely because she declined a marriage proposal was an act that could not be justified by wounded pride, customary practices or claims of honour.
"It is a matter of profound shame to the conscience of any civilised society when a man fails to gain a woman's affection and responds to her refusal with violence instead of acceptance," the judgment said, adding that marriage was a mutual and voluntary covenant requiring the free consent of both parties.
The court observed that patriarchal systems often treated men as having an exclusive right to choose a woman, demand her hand in marriage and assert possession over her, irrespective of her wishes.
It said a woman exercised her fundamental right when she rejected a suitor, but men operating under a patriarchal mindset sometimes perceived such a refusal as an affront to their "honour". This attitude, the judgment noted, could lead to stalking, home invasions, acid attacks and femicide.
The bench said the case provided an opportunity to examine ego-driven customs and violence against women, particularly whether a woman's refusal to marry could constitute a mitigating circumstance in a murder case.
The court rejected that proposition, observing that treating a woman's lawful refusal as "provocation" or a mitigating factor was an absurd argument because no person had the right to deprive another of life merely for declining a marriage proposal.
"Accepting such an argument would constitute judicial endorsement of the notion that a woman's will is subordinate to a man's preference," the judgment stated.
The court emphasised that a woman's consent to marriage could not be treated as irrelevant in a male-dominated society. It said such a mindset was irreconcilable with Islam, which requires a woman's free assent as a prerequisite for a valid nikah.
Every adult, whether male or female, is equally entitled to decide whether, when and with whom to marry, the judgment said. This right is inherent and does not depend on permission or approval from a person's family, tribe or society.
"There is no excuse for such behaviour, regardless of whether it is committed in the name of honour, custom, injured pride, or emotions," the court observed.
The judgment also referred to Pakistan's obligations under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW).
Article 16 of the convention requires states to ensure that women have the same right as men freely to choose a spouse and to enter into marriage only with their free and full consent.

title: Pak wants Israeli withdrawal from Syria
description: Pak wants Israeli withdrawal from Syria
content:
Envoy warns Israeli actions threaten Syria's sovereignty and stability
Pakistan on Tuesday called for Israel's withdrawal from all occupied Syrian territory, with its envoy to the United Nations warning that continued Israeli military actions were "profoundly counterproductive to the prospects for regional peace and stability" and threatened Syria's efforts towards national reconciliation and economic recovery.
Speaking at a UN Security Council briefing on the humanitarian and political situation in Syria, Pakistan's Acting Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Usman Jadoon, said the actions were "flagrant violations of international law and Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity".
"They are also profoundly counterproductive to the prospects for regional peace and stability," Jadoon said, adding that while Syria worked to consolidate peace and recovery, "such violations serve only to create further instability".
Jadoon said the occupied Syrian Golan remained Syrian territory under international law and cited UN Security Council resolutions 338 and 497. He reiterated Pakistan's call for Israel's withdrawal from all occupied Syrian territory and full compliance with the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement.
The Pakistani envoy said it was "deeply regrettable" that continued Israeli military actions threatened to undermine Syria's efforts to achieve national reconciliation and revive its economy.
Jadoon said Pakistan welcomed the Syrian government's efforts towards national reconciliation and the advancement of the country's political transition.
"Today, amid the challenges of recovery and reconstruction, there is a renewed sense of hope in Syria," he said. He added that a country which had witnessed years of conflict was "steadily reclaiming its rightful place in the region and the wider international community".
Jadoon said Syria's renewed diplomatic engagement, restoration of national institutions and gradual revival of economic activity offered "highly encouraging signs of a new chapter in Syria's history".
He said Pakistan welcomed progress in engagement with the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) and hoped that outstanding challenges, including the situation in Suweida, would be addressed through dialogue and peaceful engagement.
"Syria's unity and diversity are mutually reinforcing," he said, stressing the need for "full respect for Syria's unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity".
The Pakistani envoy said Syria's reconstruction and economic revival required sustained international support. He said the lifting of sanctions by the United States and the European Union, alongside expanding investment and economic partnerships with friendly countries, particularly in the region, and European partners, would provide "important impetus to Syria's recovery and development".

title: Poverty reduction  a national priority
description: Poverty reduction  a national priority
content:
Ahsan Iqbal urges investment in education, skills and human development
Planning Ahsan Iqbal on Tuesday stressed that poverty alleviation, human resource development and improved social indicators must remain top national priorities to transform Pakistan into a sustainable and competitive economy.
Addressing an international conference on Pakistan's Vision for Inclusive and Resilient Economic Transformation, Iqbal said it was imperative to ensure that the benefits of development reached every citizen and region, with equitable access to economic opportunities.
He noted that poverty was not merely a lack of income but also limited access to education, healthcare, nutrition and decent employment.
Expressing concern over the rising poverty rate and weak social indicators in Pakistan, he stressed that addressing these fundamental challenges was essential for sustainable national development.
Iqbal observed around 25 million children were out of school in Pakistan, while the rate of child stunting stood at approximately 40 per cent. Without improvements in education, healthcare and nutrition, he said, Pakistan could not compete effectively in the global economy.
He termed early childhood development, quality education and investment in human resources fundamental to future economic growth.
The minister said the government's focus was not limited to assessing poverty levels; rather, its ultimate objective was to lift people out of poverty and enable them to achieve self-sufficiency. He said the government was intensifying and accelerating its efforts while mobilising all relevant stakeholders to achieve this goal.
He said sustainable poverty alleviation required more than financial assistance or the provision of productive assets to deserving families, adding they also needed skills, business capital, access to markets and reliable livelihood opportunities.
He emphasised women's economic empowerment, employment opportunities for young people and the role of universities in promoting the development of local communities.
Iqbal said the government intended to link poverty alleviation initiatives with evidence-based policymaking, measurable outcomes and effective monitoring to ensure stable incomes, savings, improved nutrition and a better quality of life.
Calling for prosperous districts to become partners in the development of underdeveloped areas, the minister stressed promoting self-reliance and mutual support. He pointed out that 11 of Pakistan's 20 poorest districts were located in Balochistan.
He said resources and capabilities must be pooled to extend the benefits of development to every region and reduce regional inequalities.

title: Migration to EU  PM seeks legal pathways

content:
Shehbaz meets with EU commissioner for migration
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday emphasised the need to complement efforts to curb irregular migration with practical opportunities for "safe, orderly and regular migration" during a meeting with European Union (EU) Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration Magnus Brunner.
The meeting focused on strengthening Pakistan-EU cooperation in the areas of migration and mobility, one of the eight pillars of the Pakistan-EU Strategic Engagement Plan 2019, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said in a press release.
Welcoming Commissioner Brunner on his first visit to Pakistan, the prime minister highlighted Pakistan's sustained efforts to curb irregular migration and combat migrant smuggling and human trafficking through legislative reforms, institutional strengthening, effective enforcement, and international cooperation.
The premier underscored the importance Pakistan attached to its partnership with the EU and reaffirmed its commitment to further strengthening cooperation across all pillars of the Pak-EU Strategic Engagement Plan.
He noted that expanding legal pathways for Pakistani skilled workers and professionals would help meet the labour-market needs of European countries while reducing the vulnerability of prospective migrants to smuggling networks.
Brunner appreciated the measures taken and the cooperation extended by the government of Pakistan. He expressed confidence that these efforts would contribute positively to the expansion of legal migration pathways and the promotion of mutually beneficial labour mobility between Pakistan and the EU.
Terming agriculture as the backbone of the national economy, the prime minister noted that the sector has the potential to steer Pakistan's economy on the path of development in a short span of time.
He made the remarks while chairing the first meeting of the National Agriculture and Food Security Council (NAFSC).
The premier observed that the livestock sector also possessed vast potential to increase national exports and the government was taking steps to increase Pakistan's halal meat exports.
He said the federal government would provide all kinds of cooperation to the provinces for agricultural development, adding that providing farmers with low-cost fertilizer, quality seeds, modern machinery and equipment and technical capabilities for the better use of water was a top priority.
The prime minister expressed his satisfaction at the availability of wheat to meet domestic requirements and warned that no leniency would be shown to those hoarding wheat.
He stressed that ensuring a fair price for farmers' crops, especially small and medium-scale farmers, is a priority, adding that it was necessary to determine the correct price of wheat before sowing so that farmers received appropriate compensation for their hard work.
"We want farmers to get the right price for wheat and consumers to avail of affordable wheat. The decision regarding the price of wheat will be made in consultation with the provinces," he said.
During the meeting, the prime minister lauded Punjab chief minister for taking commendable steps such as farmers' development, aquaculture, shrimp farming, and providing direct subsidies to farmers through the Kissan Card.

title: Huma Khawaja s  Tere Rang  celebrates love  life
description: Huma Khawaja s  Tere Rang  celebrates love  life
content:
Singer says Punjabi song draws inspiration from changing seasons
Singer Huma Khawaja has released her new Punjabi song, Tere Rang, a soulful love song that celebrates the colours of life, relationships and festivities. Speaking to The Express Tribune, Khawaja said the song was created in January and released in October, drawing inspiration from changing seasons and the idea of colours returning to life.
"As we say, autumn comes after spring. So we need colours. When colours change, that is how it got the name Tere Rang," she said.
The singer described the track as a simple, accessible and soulful love song that she hopes will connect with listeners from different walks of life. Its colourful theme, she said, makes it suitable for celebrations ranging from weddings and birthdays to Valentine's Day.
With the wedding season approaching in November and December, Khawaja said the song's upbeat rhythm and festive mood were designed to complement occasions centred on happiness, love and togetherness.
"It is a cute song, a soulful song. It is about spreading love. It is an easy song that everyone can understand," she said.
The track features production by Ali Mustafa, who works from his studio in Lahore. Vocal production was handled by Samia Gauhar, a top-six contestant on Pakistan Idol. Roshaan Ashraf, associated with the Mehboob Ashraf Band, contributed to the percussion and mixing, according to the singer.
Alongside the music, Khawaja has used artificial intelligence to create a video that reflects the song's central themes. She said the visuals bring together colours, love and elements of Pakistan's cultural heritage, including traditional kites.
For Khawaja, the title Tere Rang carries a broader meaning beyond its romantic theme. Colours can represent the excitement of celebrations, the diversity of life and the emotions that connect people.

Bob Odenkirk remembers 'Breaking Bad' co-star RJ Mitte after his death at 34, praising his positivity and kindness
Breaking Bad star Bob Odenkirk has paid tribute to his late co-star RJ Mitte following the actor’s death at the age of 34.
In a statement to PEOPLE on October 13, Odenkirk remembered Mitte as a kind person who used his personal experiences to support others. The actor, who portrayed Saul Goodman in the AMC crime drama, praised Mitte for his positivity and willingness to connect with people.
“Whenever I saw him, he was meeting the world with positivity and a strong desire to connect,” Odenkirk said. “This is simply, deeply sad.”
Mitte, best known for playing Walter “Flynn” White Jr., the son of Bryan Cranston’s character, Walter White, throughout all five seasons of Breaking Bad , died on October 12. His representative confirmed the news to PEOPLE and said his death was by suicide.
Beyond his acting career, Mitte was a prominent disability rights advocate. Born with cerebral palsy, he used his public platform to raise awareness about disability representation and inclusion in the entertainment industry.
His representative also highlighted his work as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s, alongside his role as president of The Mitte Foundation.
Odenkirk’s tribute followed emotional messages from other Breaking Bad cast members, including Bryan Cranston and Dean Norris.
Cranston, who played Mitte’s on-screen father, remembered meeting the actor when he was 14 and praised his determination throughout the series. He described Mitte as his “sweet son on Breaking Bad” and expressed sorrow over his death.
Cranston also revealed that he and Mitte had exchanged text messages weeks earlier and had tried to arrange lunch. Reflecting on their relationship, he wrote that he loved the young actor and would miss him.
Norris, who portrayed Hank Schrader, also mourned Mitte, describing him as a sweetheart and remembering how he looked out for him when he was young.
Mitte’s death has prompted tributes from his former co-stars and renewed attention to his contributions to disability awareness and representation on television.

title: Customs rejects under-invoicing claims | The Express Tribune
description:
Customs rejects 
under-invoicing claims
content:
FBR moves to address valuation discrepancy due to data gap
Discrepancies in mirror trade data cannot, in isolation, be treated as conclusive evidence of under-invoicing and require proper reconciliation and verification, Pakistan Customs said on Tuesday, responding to media reports on alleged import fraud and under-invoicing of goods from China.
It said discrepancies in bilateral trade data reported by Pakistan and China to the International Trade Centre (ITC) had been extensively examined. Such comparisons involve data reported by China as exports to Pakistan and by Pakistan as imports from China, and have inherent limitations due to differences in data retrieval, compilation and reporting practices across institutions and countries. A reported discrepancy of 32% in 2023 was reduced to just 0.54% following reconciliation.
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has also taken corrective measures to improve data reporting, in place since July 2026.
Pakistan Customs said the Directorate General of Customs Valuation accords priority to concerns of local manufacturing industries, including textiles, steel, chemicals, tyres, stationery, dyes, plastics, glass, light engineering goods and automotive vendors. Issuance and revision of valuation rulings is an ongoing process, with efforts to ensure dynamic, realistic and sustainable customs values.
The directorate in Karachi has determined fair customs values and issued valuation rulings under Section 25A of the Customs Act, 1969, covering various yarns and fabrics in consultation with industry associations and stakeholders. These are based on internationally recognised price publications, prevailing global market trends and other parameters. The major ruling on polyester filament yarn has been revised in line with international market trends.
Fresh valuation exercises are underway for existing rulings and additional textile products, including mink yarn, raw white core spun blended yarn, cotton yarn and billiard cloth, to be completed within the specified timeframe.

content:
KSE-100 index slips below 165,000; auto sales fall 3% month-on-month
An early rally at the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) fizzled out on Tuesday as investors resorted to profit-taking at higher levels, pulling the benchmark KSE-100 Index below the key psychological level of 165,000 points amid a mixed and volatile session.
The index touched an intraday high of 166,070.48 before falling to a low of 164,773.67, eventually settling at 164,776.44, down 347.97 points, or 0.21%.
The market opened on a positive note following the previous session's sell-off, with the KSE-100 Index rising 558.25 points, or 0.34%, to 165,682.66 in early trading. By midday, it was up 470.14 points, or 0.28%, at 165,594.55, supported by buying in automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, oil and gas exploration companies, and oil marketing companies.
According to KTrade Securities, the KSE-100 opened on a positive note as Brent crude traded below $105 a barrel, lifting early sentiment and pushing the index over 700 points into the green.
However, as the session progressed, profit-taking across the board erased gains despite oil prices hovering near $105 a barrel. Consequently, the index closed at 164,776, down 348 points (-0.21%) day-on-day.
Selling pressure was concentrated in commercial banks, technology, and oil and gas stocks, with UBL, HBL, Lucky Cement and Mari Energies weighing on the index. Fertilisers were the only sector to offer some support.
Going forward, KTrade noted that cautious trading is likely to persist as buyers remain selective, accumulating on dips rather than aggressively chasing prices. A sustained recovery will depend on improved participation and developments on the geopolitical front, particularly their implications for global oil prices and domestic investor sentiment, it added.
Deputy Head of Trading at Arif Habib Limited (AHL) Ali Najib said profit-taking at higher levels curtailed the recovery and pushed the benchmark into negative territory.
On the sectoral front, sales of cars, light commercial vehicles, vans and jeeps fell 3% month-on-month and 12% year-on-year to 15,100 units in September 2026. However, cumulative sales during the first quarter of FY27 rose 19% year-on-year to 50,500 units.
Among index constituents, Fauji Fertiliser Company, Meezan Bank, Fauji Cement, Fatima Fertiliser and AGP collectively contributed 112 points to the index. Pakistan Telecommunication Company, United Bank, Habib Bank, Lucky Cement and Mari Energies exerted downward pressure, collectively erasing 343 points.
Najib said the market was likely to remain volatile amid domestic political uncertainty, with downside risks offset by selective value buying. He advised investors to remain cautious, prioritise fundamentally strong stocks and avoid aggressive positions until sentiment stabilised.
Overall, trading volume increased to 383.7 million shares versus Monday's total of 362.9 million. The value of traded shares stood at Rs13.1 billion. Shares of 500 companies were traded in the ready market. Of these, 223 stocks closed higher, 226 fell and 51 remained unchanged.
LSE Financial Services was the volume leader with trading in 32.3 million shares, losing Rs0.16 to close at Rs1.03. Foreign investors sold shares worth Rs644.2 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

title: Fitch sees developed market debt above  75tr
description: Fitch sees developed market debt above  75tr
content:
IMF warns AI bust could cut global GDP by 1.1%, says prolonged war could halve 2027 growth
Rising government bond yields are making it much harder for major developed economies to stabilise debt burdens, with countries including France, the US and Britain facing growing fiscal challenges, credit rating agency Fitch said on Tuesday.
In a report, Fitch said benchmark 10-year government bond yields in the world's 10 largest developed economies had risen by an average of 81 basis points so far this year. That would contribute to a nearly $4 trillion increase in overall developed-market government debt, taking it above $75 trillion, or $68.5 trillion across the top 10 economies.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Tuesday flagged significant growth and financial stability risks from a potential ending of the AI investment boom, growing debt levels and a prolonged Middle East conflict.
The IMF forecast global growth at 3.1% for 2026, a slight uptick from a 3.0% forecast in July as still-strong AI infrastructure investment offset higher oil prices caused by the war in the Middle East.
The latest World Economic Outlook report, released in Bangkok during the annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank, also predicts 3.4% growth in 2027, but that is based on assumptions that the Strait of Hormuz reopens by March and shipping conditions return to the pre-war situation by October 2027.
A more protracted war that kept oil prices above $130 through the first quarter of 2027 would cut growth next year by half a percentage point, the IMF said.
In another downside scenario, the IMF said that a steep drop in AI investment could lead to a sharp fall in asset prices, ultimately cutting global GDP by 1.1% by 2028, including a 1.8% drop in US output.
It would also lead to reduced trade, IMF chief economist Silvana Tenreyro said. Trade in AI goods grew 29% between 2023 and 2025, more than triple the 8.3% growth rate of global trade over the same period. Without the AI trade, overall growth in trade would have been only 4.6%, she said.
The debt vulnerabilities of many developing economies are a "major barrier" to inclusive growth, said Nigerian Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele, who chairs the Group of 24 developing nations, warning that member governments were increasingly contending with mounting debt burdens.
Oyedele said estimates showed that developing countries were paying $500 billion more for their debt than developed countries, even as they contend with growing deficits.
"France, Germany, the US all need to do fiscal consolidation, but they're moving in the opposite direction," said Josh Lipsky, vice president of international economics at the Atlantic Council.

title: Pakistan crosses  1b in digital subsidies
description: Pakistan crosses  1b in digital subsidies
content:
USF achieves 17,000km of fiberisation, targets 60% of towers for 5G
The Asia-Pacific Telecommunity (APT) Symposium on Digital Transformation and Universal Service Fund (USF) began in Islamabad on Tuesday, with member states set to develop a framework that moves universal service beyond traditional coverage and voice subsidies towards gigabit fibre, satellite networks, smartphone financing and rural artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.
Organised by the Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication (MoITT) and USF Pakistan with the APT Secretariat, the three-day forum brings together ministers, regulators, industry executives and delegates from across the region.
Speaking as chief guest, Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja said about 2.2 billion people worldwide and nearly 48% of the Asia-Pacific population still lack internet access, a figure higher than the global average. She said connectivity was no longer a privilege but a necessity for education, healthcare, disaster management and national security, adding that progress on the National Connectivity Plan is reviewed every 15 days under Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.
Pakistan has crossed $1.054 billion in digital subsidies, with over 17,000 kilometres of optical fibre cable laid. Fibre broadband home passes rose from under three million in 2024 to over five million. Fibreisation of mobile towers increased from 15% to over 19%, against a target of at least 60% for 5G delivery.
The Fixed Satellite Services (FSS) framework is in its final stages. Three new submarine cables have landed in the past two and a half years. According to GSMA, Pakistan recorded the fastest global progress over two years in reducing the gender gap in mobile internet use, from 38% to 8%. Local entrepreneurs are being offered CVAS licences, and fuel subsidies were delivered to over 10 million people through a technology-based system without requiring a smartphone.
APT Secretary General Masanori Kondo said digital exclusion now manifests as a lack of quality and digital readiness, and universal service funds must become outcome-based frameworks.
USF Pakistan Chief Executive Officer Chaudhry Mudassar Naveed said 158 of 185 projects have been completed, using over Rs169 billion in subsidies and benefiting more than 38.4 million people.
The symposium's four pillars are gigabit broadband acceleration, emerging technology integration, sustainable funding and governance, and multi-stakeholder collaboration, based on the Tokyo Statement 2025.
Sessions will cover 5G readiness, open-access fibre, right of way policies, solar-powered green infrastructure, female digital empowerment, rural AI compute readiness, subsea cable resilience and early warning systems. The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority Chairman Hafeezur Rehman was also present.

title: Pakistan seeks global finance overhaul
description: Pakistan seeks global finance overhaul
content:
Aurangzeb, as incoming G-24 chair, pledges stronger voice for global south
Pakistan has called for reform of the international financial architecture to keep pace with fragmentation disrupting trade and investment, climate shocks eroding development gains, restrictive financial conditions and widening financing gaps, as it prepares to take over as chair of the G-24 grouping of developing nations.
Speaking as First Vice-Chair of the G-24 at the Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors' Meeting on the sidelines of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb outlined three priorities for the grouping: restoring development as the central objective of the international financial system, making the Bretton Woods institutions more representative and responsive, and building a development-oriented architecture.
He stressed that reform must ensure timely support for countries undertaking difficult reforms while confronting external shocks beyond their control, and reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment as incoming chair to strengthening the G-24's collective influence so that the Global South's voice translates into concrete outcomes. Appreciating Nigeria's leadership, he underscored cooperation among members and institutional partners to advance a more representative, resilient and development-centred economic order.
At investor roundtables organised by Jefferies International and Barclays, the minister, accompanied by Finance Secretary Imdadullah Bosal and State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) Governor Jameel Ahmad, highlighted improving fiscal and external balances, consecutive primary surpluses, stronger reserves, rating upgrades and renewed access to capital markets. Discussions covered the IMF-supported programme, debt management and financing instruments including Sukuk, further Panda bond issuance and tokenisation, alongside privatisation, tax-base broadening, agricultural income tax, digital enforcement and federal-provincial fiscal coordination.
He pointed to a strong pipeline of initial public offerings (IPOs) and foreign investor interest in electricity distribution companies, as well as airport outsourcing. Responding to questions, the delegation addressed regional geopolitical risks, energy security and liquefied natural gas (LNG) obligations, alongside economic engagement with the United States and Saudi Arabia.
On funding diversification, the minister told Nikkei Asia that Pakistan will continue to "diversify its funding sources," hinting at more yuan-based bonds and possible yen-denominated samurai bonds. He said the recent Panda bond would not be a "one-time issuance" and that Pakistan intends to "keep going back and be a repeat issuer," given China is the "second largest and deepest capital market in the world." Samurai bonds "would make sense" and are "something which we should think through," he said, adding, "We need to do more homework." He said Pakistan does not want to increase the quantum of its external debt.
Pakistan issued its first Panda bond worth 1.75 billion yuan ($261 million) in mid-May as part of a 7.2 billion yuan programme, with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) providing partial guarantees. On a panel on mitigating sovereign risks in market-access countries, the minister outlined fiscal consolidation, lower inflation and rebuilt reserves, with debt management measures to lower financing costs, extend maturities and reduce rollover risks. He said renewed market access supports a strategy to improve the external debt profile without increasing its overall size, and stressed national ownership of taxation, energy, state-owned enterprise and pension reforms.
In a meeting with Saudi Fund for Development (SFD) Chief Executive Officer Sultan Abdulrahman Al-Marshad, discussions covered trade and investment, private-sector engagement, the bilateral investment protection agreement and refinery upgrades. He noted satisfactory progress on SFD-supported projects, discussed a fresh project pipeline and sought continued support within the fund's mandate.
Talks with International Finance Corporation (IFC) Regional Vice President for the Middle East and Central Asia Imad Fakhoury covered small-business financing, entrepreneurship, capital markets, and green and digital bonds. He reaffirmed commitment to Reko Diq and appreciated IFC's financing leadership. Mining infrastructure and value addition, affordable housing, agricultural storage and cold chains, and public-private partnerships in water services and advanced electricity metering were also discussed. On population, the minister stressed the urgency of addressing rapid growth and its implications for health, education and employment, citing Indonesia, Bangladesh and Iran. He outlined a National Population Council led by the prime minister, emphasising women's education, workforce participation and engagement with religious leaders on birth spacing, and pointed to freelancing, IT-enabled services and digital skills as ways to expand youth earnings and exports.
A meeting with Mashreq Bank's senior management covered digital banking, financial inclusion, offshore service operations, digital accounts for overseas Pakistanis and collaboration on tokenisation, blockchain and digital assets within Pakistan's evolving regulatory framework. The minister also said the National Tariff Policy would not be compromised, calling it "not only about the auto industry – it's about industries in general," and referred to a revamped auto policy targeting 30% electric vehicles among new sales by 2030. He noted that ASEAN reduced tariffs in the late 1990s to generate various upsides, adding, "This can very much be a Southeast Asia moment for Pakistan."
Pakistan, an IMF member since 1950, is in its 25th arrangement and owed the fund about $10.5 billion as of Monday. The minister said the programme's structural reform agenda would lead to sustainability, and that Pakistan would graduate once "the rest of the world becomes convinced that we don't need the lender of last resort."

title: PM urged to reject yarn exclusion from EFS
description: PM urged to reject yarn exclusion from EFS
content:
Textile council seeks protection for inputs, says genuine exporters must not be penalised
The Pakistan Textile Council (PTC) has urged Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to reject demands seeking the exclusion of all yarns and fabrics falling under Chapters 52 and 55 of the Pakistan Customs Tariff from the Export Facilitation Scheme (EFS), warning that accepting them would cause serious and lasting harm to the country's value-added exports, according to a statement issued on Tuesday.
Copies of the letter, signed by PTC Chairman Fawad Anwar, have been sent to the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) chairman and the secretary, Ministry of Commerce.
In the letter, the council said it fully supported government action to curb misdeclaration and misuse of the EFS, but noted that associations representing businesses focused on the domestic market are now seeking further exclusions. Raw cotton, cotton yarn and grey cloth were removed from the scheme in 2025 through SRO1359(I)/2025.
PTC pointed out that these demands are contrary to the understanding reached during earlier consultations that no further exclusions would be sought.
"Accepting these demands would cause serious and lasting harm to Pakistan's value-added exports," Chairman Fawad Anwar stated in the letter.
The council highlighted that global textile and apparel demand has moved firmly towards man-made fibres (MMF). According to Textile Exchange's Materials Market Report 2025, synthetic fibres accounted for 69% of global fibre production in 2024, while cotton's share fell to 19%.
MMF-based products account for about 63% of global textile and apparel trade, but only about 12% of Pakistan's textile and apparel exports. Competing countries are expanding rapidly in this segment, with Bangladesh targeting an increase in the MMF share of its apparel exports from about 24% to 40% by 2030.
The letter noted that Pakistan has almost no viscose or lyocell fibre production, while the domestic polyester value chain carries cost and scale disadvantages against Chinese and ASEAN producers. Value-added exporters therefore rely on imported MMF yarns and fabrics, many of which are specified by international buyers, to secure and deliver orders.
PTC warned that the 2025 exclusions already require exporters to pay taxes upfront on those inputs, adding to liquidity pressure and production costs. Excluding all yarns and fabrics under Chapters 52 and 55 would raise input costs and lock up working capital for apparel and made-ups exporters, restrict access to the fibres that drive global apparel demand, discourage investment in new value-added and MMF-based capacity, and weaken buyer confidence in Pakistan as a stable sourcing destination.
On misuse, PTC reiterated its full support for firm action against misdeclaration, under-invoicing and diversion of EFS imports into the domestic market.
The letter stated that FBR and Pakistan Customs have the legal powers, systems and personnel to detect and prosecute such cases, and that recent detections show enforcement is effective.
"The misuse of a few cannot justify penalising genuine exporters or dismantling a scheme that is central to export competitiveness," the chairman added.
PTC requested the prime minister's intervention on three points: EFS should remain available for all legitimate export inputs, with no further exclusions of yarns or fabrics under Chapters 52 and 55; FBR should strengthen enforcement through input-output coefficient audits, reconciliation of EFS imports against export documents, risk-based examination and strict penalties for offenders; and concerns of domestic suppliers should be addressed by restoring zero-rating on local supplies of inputs to EFS users, rather than by taxing imported inputs.
PTC stated that textiles and apparel remain Pakistan's largest export sector and that its growth depends on competitive access to the inputs the world market demands. The council reaffirmed its commitment to working with the government to curb misuse while protecting the genuine exporters who earn foreign exchange for the country.

title: Oil mixed as WTI hits two week high
description: Oil mixed as WTI hits two week high
content:
Gold recovers as investors await US data; rupee appreciates one paisa
Oil prices were mixed on Tuesday as hopes the US-Russia diesel deal could free up more supplies from Moscow offset attacks in Saudi Arabia and Yemen that could result in additional supply disruptions.
Brent futures were down 59 cents, or 0.6%, at $106.06 per barrel at 1659 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures rose 73 cents, or 0.8%, to $94.47.
That put WTI on track to close at its highest since September 24 for a second day in a row. On Monday, Brent closed at its highest since September 15.
Gold prices in Pakistan rose on Tuesday, recovering part of the previous session's losses, as international bullion prices remained largely stable ahead of key US inflation data and remarks from the Federal Reserve (Fed) chair later this week.
The Kremlin said on Tuesday that it did not see any direct link between a deal on exporting Russian diesel to the US and Moscow's own stance on the Ukraine peace talks.
It was commenting on a Reuters source-based story, which reported that US President Donald Trump's envoys had told Ukrainian officials on Friday that the deal to allow Russian diesel exports was part of an attempt to draw Russia back into negotiations over a possible peace settlement in Ukraine. Russia was the world's third-biggest crude oil producer behind the US and Saudi Arabia in 2025, according to US energy data. Sanctions designed to keep Russian energy out of global markets have helped support oil prices since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022.
Meanwhile, in the local market, the price of gold per tola increased by Rs900 to Rs440,836, according to rates released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association (APGJSA). The price of 10-gramme gold also rose by Rs771 to Rs377,945.
On Monday, gold had fallen by Rs2,100 per tola to Rs439,936.
In the international market, spot gold edged down 0.1% to $4,164.70 per ounce by 1526 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery declined 0.1% to $4,188.40 per ounce.
Silver prices in the domestic market remained unchanged at Rs6,532 per tola.
Director of Interactive Commodities Adnan Agar said the international gold market was moving within a narrow range as investors awaited fresh cues to determine its next direction.
Gold traded between a high of $4,200 and a low of $4,150, standing near $4,154 at the time of his assessment, he said. The market remained sluggish, with prices struggling to break out of their prevailing range.
Agar identified the $4,240-$4,280 range as an important resistance zone, suggesting that gold could face difficulty moving higher unless prices crossed these levels. His comments pointed to continued uncertainty over the near-term direction of bullion.
Investors are awaiting US consumer price index (CPI) data due on Wednesday and producer price index (PPI) figures scheduled for Thursday. The releases could offer fresh clues about inflationary pressures and the Fed's future monetary policy.
The US dollar slipped from its highest level since April last year, while the yield on the 10-year US Treasury note fell to its lowest in more than a week.
The rupee appreciated by one paisa against the US dollar, closing at Rs276.96 on Tuesday, compared with Rs276.97 in the previous session.

title: Govt seeks 15 year Saudi oil facility
description: Govt seeks 15 year Saudi oil facility
content:
Aurangzeb raises $1.2b deferred payment facility with SFD chief
Pakistan on Tuesday took up the issue of revival of the $1.2 billion annual oil facility on deferred payments with the Saudi Fund for Development (SFD), as both sides discussed ways to deepen energy cooperation.
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb raised the matter with SFD Chief Executive Officer Sultan Abdulrahman Al-Marshad on the sidelines of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF) annual meetings taking place in Thailand.
The Ministry of Finance released the details of the meeting but did not comment on the oil facility. Adviser to the Finance Minister Khurram Schehzad also did not respond to a question regarding the Saudi response to the Pakistani request. People privy to the discussions said Saudi Arabia was examining the matter.
According to an official handout, Aurangzeb highlighted Pakistan's improving macroeconomic position and renewed access to international capital markets.
"Discussions focused on expanding trade and investment, strengthening private-sector engagement, following up on the bilateral investment protection agreement and exploring opportunities for refinery upgrades," according to the finance ministry.
The official handout noted that both sides recorded satisfactory progress on SFD-supported projects and emphasised the importance of developing a fresh pipeline of projects. "The SFD reaffirmed its continued support to Pakistan within its mandate," it added.
Saudi Arabia has also extended $3 billion short-term debt through the SFD, which the Kingdom further rolled over for three months in July.
Since 2019, Saudi Arabia has been providing oil on one-year deferred payments. The last facility was signed in February 2025, which expired in April. Instead of seeking short-term financing, the government is now seeking a long-term pipeline to lower immediate external financing requirements.
For the fiscal year 2027-28, the IMF has assessed the country's annual gross financing needs at nearly $30 billion, which the government is planning to cut by securing long-term rollovers of the existing external debt.
The interest rate on the previous facility, finalised before the Pak-Saudi Strategic Partnership Agreement, was 6%, according to economic affairs ministry officials. The last agreement was part of Saudi Arabia's broader financial assistance to Pakistan through the SFD, which had provided approximately $6.7 billion for oil derivatives since 2019.
Pakistan is now seeking a $6.7 billion concessional oil financing facility from Saudi Arabia for a period of 15 years, aimed at ensuring energy security amid heightened Middle East conflict that may keep global prices high and put additional stress on the country's foreign exchange reserves.
The country's annual petroleum group import bill surged to $16.8 billion in the last fiscal year – 5.8% higher. There was a 32% increase in crude oil import cost, which jumped to $7.2 billion in the last fiscal year. The trend is continuing in the current fiscal year and the cost of crude oil import further increased 40% during the July-August period of this fiscal year.
In July this year, a spokesperson of the Ministry of Economic Affairs had told The Express Tribune that the matter of the Saudi oil facility on deferred payments was under discussion with Saudi authorities.
Saudi Arabia has emerged as Pakistan's major bilateral lender after China and lately provided $3 billion in short-term deposit through the SFD for helping the country make debt repayment to the United Arab Emirates.
The IMF has not included the Saudi oil facility in its projected inflows for Pakistan for the financial years 2026-27 and 2027-28, according to the third staff-level report. Any such deal between both governments would offset the impact of any addition in the cost of fuel imports, said government officials. The finance minister also met IFC Regional Vice President for the Middle East and Central Asia Imad Fakhoury.
The finance ministry said the discussions focused on strengthening IFC support for private-sector-led growth and jobs, and translating macroeconomic stability into sustainable growth.
The meeting reviewed IFC's expanding portfolio, small-business financing, entrepreneurship, capital markets, and green and digital bonds. The finance minister reaffirmed commitment to Reko Diq and appreciated IFC's financing leadership, it added.
Discussions also covered mining infrastructure and value addition, affordable housing and developer financing, and agricultural development through improved storage, cold chains and electronic warehouse receipt financing.
The finance ministry said both sides explored greater private-sector participation in livestock development and support for pharmaceutical exports through stronger regulatory standards and investment.

Joey Graziadei makes his acting debut with Jamie Chung in 'The Holiday Spark', a Christmas rom-com premiering November
Joey Graziadei is stepping into a leading acting role in The Holiday Spark , a new Christmas romantic comedy starring Jamie Chung, premiering on The Roku Channel on November 2.
The former Bachelor star, 31, plays Dean, a firefighter who teams up with Laura, a children's book illustrator played by Chung, to organise an unforgettable holiday party for his firehouse. As they work together, the pair begin to reconsider their views on romance and the possibility of finding love unexpectedly.
Graziadei previously appeared on The Bachelorette and led season 28 of The Bachelor before winning season 33 of Dancing with the Stars . He also made a cameo appearance on 9-1-1 , playing a version of himself during a fictional fire at the Bachelor mansion.
The Holiday Spark marks his first leading role in a scripted production.
“Getting to be part of a Christmas movie has been such a fun and special experience,” Graziadei told PEOPLE. He added that the cast enjoyed bringing the story to life and expressed hope that audiences would return to the film during future holiday seasons.
An exclusive trailer offers a first look at the developing romance between Dean and Laura. After meeting the firefighter, Laura tells a friend that she experienced “that feeling”. Their connection grows during a date to select a Christmas tree for the firehouse, although Dean's demanding job repeatedly interrupts their time together.
During one dinner date, Dean leaves early after hearing another emergency siren. He later tells a fellow firefighter that he wants to be with Laura for the rest of his life. His friend encourages him to pursue what he wants rather than avoid it.
The trailer concludes with the pair sharing a romantic moment beside a fireplace. Laura compares their connection to a spark, prompting Dean to say he wants to keep it burning before leaning in for a kiss.
Chung, known for her appearance on The Real World: San Diego , joins Graziadei in the festive romantic comedy, which explores love, commitment and second chances.
The Holiday Spark premieres on The Roku Channel on Monday, November 2.

title: Sylvester Stallone jokes he cannot retire as daughter Sophia   s wedding bills approach
description: Sylvester Stallone says he cannot retire because he needs to pay for daughter Sophia Stallone   s upcoming wedding
content:
Sylvester Stallone says he cannot retire because he needs to pay for daughter Sophia Stallone’s upcoming wedding
Sylvester Stallone has joked that he cannot retire from acting because he needs to pay for his daughter Sophia Stallone’s upcoming wedding.
The Rocky and Tulsa King star, 80, made the comment during an appearance on Live with Kelly and Mark on October 13, when co-host Kelly Ripa asked how much he planned to contribute towards Sophia’s wedding expenses.
“Oh, man, it’s almost embarrassing to say — but I can’t retire,” Stallone replied, prompting laughter from the studio audience. He repeated the remark before adding, “I’m serious!”
Sophia, 30, announced her engagement to boyfriend Michael Sheehan on August 28. She shared photographs of the proposal on Instagram, describing her fiancé as her best friend and expressing her excitement about their future together.
During the television appearance, Stallone also praised Sheehan, calling him “a great guy”. The actor revealed that his future son-in-law had asked for his blessing before proposing to Sophia.
“He actually asked for her hand,” Stallone said.
Ripa joked that Sheehan must have been terrified to approach the Hollywood star. Co-host Mark Consuelos also referenced a memorable line from Rocky II , in which Stallone’s character, Rocky Balboa, proposes to Adrian.
Stallone responded with another reference to the film, joking about Rocky’s promise to keep their home tidy. He also praised Sheehan for being confident during the proposal, recalling that he had wished him good luck.
The actor added that his wife, Jennifer Flavin, was present to act as a referee during the interaction.
Stallone and Flavin, who married in 1997, have three daughters together: Sophia, Sistine, 28, and Scarlet, 24. Stallone also has two sons, Seargeoh, 47, and Sage, who died in 2012 at the age of 36, from his first marriage to Sasha Czack.
Sophia’s engagement marks another milestone for the family, with Stallone’s lighthearted remarks highlighting the financial responsibilities that come with planning a wedding.

title: Girls    returns to HBO with Lena Dunham and original cast for five episode revival
description: HBO is reviving Lena Dunham   s  Girls  for five episodes in 2027  bringing back Allison Williams  Jemima Kirke and more
content:
HBO is reviving Lena Dunham’s 'Girls' for five episodes in 2027, bringing back Allison Williams, Jemima Kirke and more
HBO is bringing back Girls for a five-episode limited revival, reuniting Lena Dunham and several original cast members a decade after the comedy series ended.
Dunham will reprise her role as Hannah Horvath alongside Allison Williams as Marnie Michaels, Jemima Kirke as Jessa Johansson, Zosia Mamet as Shoshanna Shapiro and Andrew Rannells as Elijah Krantz. Production on the Girls revival is scheduled to begin in 2027, although HBO has not announced a release date.
The upcoming revival will revisit the characters as they navigate life in their 40s. Story details remain under wraps, but Dunham said she had been waiting for a specific story that would make returning to the series worthwhile.
The creator and star explained that she struggled for years to imagine the characters in the present day before new ideas emerged around her 40th birthday. She will executive produce the revival alongside Judd Apatow, Ilene S. Landress and Michael P. Cohen. Williams, Kirke, Mamet and Rannells will serve as co-executive producers.
Adam Driver, who portrayed Hannah’s on-and-off boyfriend, is not among the announced returning cast members. Jenni Konner, who co-ran the original series with Dunham, is also not involved in the new project.
HBO comedy programming executive Amy Gravitt said the revival would explore the changes in the characters’ lives since audiences last saw them, while revisiting the personalities that made the original series distinctive.
Girls aired from 2012 to 2017 and followed a group of young women navigating relationships, careers and adulthood in New York City. The series became a prominent part of television discussions about millennial life and earned two Emmy Awards, alongside multiple nominations. Dunham and the show also won Golden Globe Awards for the first season.
HBO has released a promotional video announcing the revival, with further casting and story details yet to be revealed.
