title: Doug Mason opens up about Taylor Frankie Paul   s unaired    Bachelorette    season
description: Mason explained that he had initially stayed quiet out of respect for Paul but decided to share his perspective
content:
Mason explained that he had initially stayed quiet out of respect for Paul but decided to share his perspective
Doug Mason, the winner of Taylor Frankie Paul’s unaired season of The Bachelorette , has opened up about their relationship and the behind-the-scenes experiences that ultimately led to their split.
Mason discussed the experience during the October 13 episode of the Bachelor Happy Hour podcast, hosted by Charity Lawson and Rachel Recchia. He explained that he had initially stayed quiet out of respect for Paul and the show, but decided to share his perspective after feeling that she had downplayed their relationship on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives .
Mason said he was initially drawn to Paul because of how kind and generous she appeared during filming. However, as their relationship developed, he began to question whether they had a future together, particularly because he suspected she still had feelings for her former boyfriend, Dakota Mortensen.
According to Mason, Paul told him that she had slept with Mortensen the night before filming began. The revelation left him struggling with comparisons to her former partner, which became a recurring source of tension during the season.
Mason recalled that one group date was particularly difficult because he felt he could not escape comparisons to Mortensen. He said the situation affected the dynamic between him and Paul, despite believing that their connection had been genuine up to that point.
The relationship also involved significant steps towards a future together. Mason met Paul’s children and her ex-husband, Tate Paul, during filming. He recalled an off-camera conversation with Tate, who warned him that being with Paul would change his life and asked whether he was prepared for the challenges involved.
Despite his doubts, Mason eventually proposed to Paul, and she accepted. He explained that his decision came from his romantic feelings and a desire to believe in their relationship, even as he questioned whether they were truly compatible.
Looking back, Mason said he had since gained a clearer understanding of what he wanted from a relationship. “I loved Taylor for who she was during the show, but of course, since then, I've realized what true love is, and that wasn't it,” he said.
Paul previously confirmed on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives that she had become engaged during her season of The Bachelorette . She also discussed what happened after she returned home, including her continued contact with Mortensen.
The season was pulled from ABC’s schedule before its planned premiere in March after a video surfaced showing a 2023 domestic violence incident involving Paul and Mortensen. The unaired season subsequently became a subject of renewed attention as Paul discussed the relationship and its aftermath on her reality series.
Mason’s comments offer a new account of the relationship from the perspective of the man who proposed to Paul during the season. He said he had moved forward from the experience and wanted to explain his side after watching the relationship discussed publicly.

title: Collin Gosselin accuses mom Kate Gosselin of physical abuse in new memoir
description: Sometimes it was a sharp yank to my ear  Sometimes a slap across the face     Collin writes
content:
“Sometimes it was a sharp yank to my ear. Sometimes a slap across the face,” Collin writes
Collin Gosselin has made fresh allegations of physical and emotional abuse against his mother, Kate Gosselin, in his new memoir, In the Shadow of Eight , recounting what he describes as a difficult childhood behind the scenes of the family's reality television series Jon & Kate Plus 8 .
The 22-year-old alleges that his mother treated him differently from his seven siblings, particularly after he began resisting filming the TLC show. In the book, Collin describes incidents in which he claims Kate slapped him across the face and pulled him by the ear, sometimes leaving marks and bruises.
“Sometimes it was a sharp yank to my ear. Sometimes a slap across the face,” Collin writes, describing what he says was a pattern of physical punishment during his childhood.
He also alleges that Kate made him sleep in a locked basement room that had no furniture, where he used an air mattress. According to Collin, surveillance cameras monitored the space, and he sometimes had to bang on the door to be allowed out to use the bathroom.
“Sometimes I wonder, if the house had burned down, would anyone have remembered to come unlock the door?” he writes in the memoir.
Collin further claims that the situation escalated after he attempted to run away from home. He alleges that Kate used zip ties to restrain him before he was sent to the Fairmont Behavioral Health Institute, where he lived away from his family.
In an appearance on On Purpose with Jay Shetty to promote the book, Collin presented what he described as a report from the facility that allegedly documented Kate acknowledging the locked room. The report reportedly quoted her as saying that a psychiatrist had approved the arrangement.
Collin also recalled speaking with child protective services when he was around 12 years old. He said the investigation did not result in a finding of substantiated abuse, describing the determination as “unfounded”.
Kate has previously denied Collin's allegations and maintained that the decisions concerning his care were made to protect him and the rest of the family. In a 2023 statement shared on Instagram, she said Collin had received multiple psychiatric diagnoses and was placed in a facility after outpatient treatment proved insufficient for his needs.
She also alleged that his behaviour had included violent outbursts and said the measures taken at home were recommended by his paediatric psychiatrist and other specialists. Kate described the family situation as complicated and painful, disputing Collin's account of their history.
Her attorney, Richard Puleo, defended her in a 2024 statement, saying he did not believe Kate had intentionally harmed her son. He argued that her actions were intended to protect herself and the family, while acknowledging that people can have different recollections of past events.
Jon & Kate Plus 8 followed Kate and her then-husband, Jon Gosselin, as they raised their twins, Mady and Cara, and sextuplets Alexis, Hannah, Aaden, Collin, Leah and Joel. The couple announced their separation in 2009, and the programme later continued as Kate Plus 8 .
Collin's new memoir revisits his experiences growing up in the public eye and offers his account of the events that led to his estrangement from his mother and several of his siblings. His allegations remain disputed, with Kate maintaining that her decisions were made on medical advice and for the family's safety.

title: Euphoria    creator Sam Levinson joins Amazon MGM Studios in new deal

content:
‘Euphoria’ creator Sam Levinson signs an overall TV deal with Amazon MGM Studios to develop new shows for Prime Video
Sam Levinson, the creator of HBO’s Euphoria , has signed an overall television deal with Amazon MGM Studios to develop and produce new projects for Prime Video and other Amazon MGM platforms.
Under the agreement, Levinson will work alongside his wife and producing partner, Ashley Levinson, through their production company, Tiny Goat Productions. The pair will develop television projects for the studio as part of the deal.
Levinson is best known for creating, directing and executive producing Euphoria , the drama series starring Zendaya that ran for three seasons from 2019 to May 2026. The show also featured Colman Domingo, Jacob Elordi, Sydney Sweeney, Hunter Schafer and Alexa Demie.
During its run, Euphoria received 32 Emmy nominations and won nine awards, including two for Zendaya in the lead actress category for a drama series. Levinson also received a Directors Guild of America Award in 2023 for his work directing the show’s second season.
His other credits include the films Assassination Nation , released in 2018, and Malcolm & Marie , released in 2021. He also created the 2023 HBO drama series The Idol .
Peter Friedlander, head of global television at Amazon MGM Studios, welcomed the partnership in a statement, describing Levinson as an original television creator known for storytelling that connects with audiences worldwide. He said the studio was pleased to welcome both Sam and Ashley Levinson and provide them with a platform to develop new projects.
Levinson also expressed enthusiasm about the agreement, saying he and Ashley appreciated the trust placed in them by Friedlander and his team and looked forward to producing content for audiences around the world.
The deal expands Amazon MGM Studios’ television development slate, bringing the Euphoria creator and his production company into its portfolio. Details about the first projects planned under the agreement have not been announced.

title: Govt cuts petrol by Rs2 71  diesel by 3 paisas for Oct 14
description: Petrol price decreases to Rs392 66 per litre  while HSD will cost Rs396 82 under daily price mechanism
content:
Petrol price decreases to Rs392.66 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs396.82 under daily price mechanism
The federal government on Tuesday decreased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.71 and 3 paisas per litre, respectively, for October 14.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs392.66 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs396.82 per litre for Wednesday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government decreased the price of petrol by Rs2.93 per litre, while increasing the price of HSD by 61 paisas per litre for October 13.
Read : Govt cuts petrol by Rs2.93, increases diesel by 61 paisas for Oct 13
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices ​were mixed on Tuesday as hopes that the US-Russia diesel deal could free up more supplies from Moscow offset attacks in Saudi Arabia ‌and Yemen that could result in additional supply disruptions.
Brent futures were down 59 cents, or 0.6%, at $106.06 per barrel at 12:59 pm EDT (1659 GMT), while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose 73 cents, or 0.8%, to $94.47.
Diesel prices rose to record highs in many parts of the world in recent ‌weeks due ⁠to global supply disruptions linked to Ukraine's attacks on Russian energy infrastructure and Iran's attacks on Middle East energy infrastructure.

title: Ben Affleck calls Justice League reshoots the lowest point of his career
description: Affleck said the negative experience stemmed from a combination of personal struggles and professional tensions
content:
Affleck said the negative experience stemmed from a combination of personal struggles and professional tensions
Ben Affleck has described the reshoots for the 2017 superhero film Justice League as the lowest point of his career, criticising the circumstances surrounding director Zack Snyder’s departure and the studio’s handling of the troubled production.
Speaking on Josh Horowitz’s Happy Sad Confused podcast, the actor reflected on the difficult experience of making the DC film, which originally had Snyder at the helm before Joss Whedon took over during post-production. Affleck said the negative experience stemmed from a combination of personal struggles and professional tensions.
“The truth is that the experience of Justice League , for me, was so, so negative for lots of different reasons,” Affleck said, explaining that the situation showed him how damaging it could be when a studio and its filmmaker were at odds.
Snyder stepped away from the film after the death of his daughter, Autumn Snyder, in 2017. Whedon subsequently oversaw extensive reshoots that changed elements of the film’s story and tone before its theatrical release.
Affleck strongly criticised how Snyder was removed from the project and suggested the family tragedy had been used as an excuse for the decision.
“Boy, that was shitty. Him being taken off that movie, and the reshoots that we did, if you want the low point of my career, it was that,” he said. “Somebody’s death by suicide, that eclipses everything.”
The actor added that the way the situation was handled was among the worst things he had witnessed in the film industry, describing the experience as “so gross”. He also referred to reports about the working environment during the reshoots, mentioning co-stars Ray Fisher and Gal Gadot, while clarifying that much of what he knew about their experiences had reached him second-hand.
Affleck also spoke about his personal circumstances at the time, revealing that he was drinking too much and struggling to stop. He was also going through a difficult period in his personal life, including his divorce. However, he stressed that these struggles coincided with the film’s troubled production rather than directly affecting the movie itself.
“Those things, while painful, were not what impacted that movie,” he explained. “They just happened to be happening at the same time.”
The comments revisit a period that Affleck has criticised previously. In a 2022 interview with Entertainment Weekly , he described his experience making Justice League as a particularly low point, explaining that he had been unhappy with the production and did not find the experience creatively fulfilling.
Despite his criticism of the theatrical film’s production, Affleck expressed happiness that Snyder eventually got to release his own extended version, Zack Snyder’s Justice League , in 2021.
Affleck played Bruce Wayne, also known as Batman, in Justice League , appearing alongside Henry Cavill, Gal Gadot, Jason Momoa, Ezra Miller and Fisher. The film’s production became a major talking point among DC fans, particularly following the release of Snyder’s version, which restored material absent from the 2017 theatrical cut.
His latest remarks offer another reflection on a film that proved professionally difficult for the actor, with Affleck identifying the reshoots and the circumstances surrounding Snyder’s departure as central to his negative experience.

title: How RJ Mitte changed the way we see cerebral palsy through  Breaking Bad
description: I have cerebral palsy but I ve never let it hold me back     Mitte wrote in a 2014 essay for HuffPost
content:
“I have cerebral palsy but I've never let it hold me back,” Mitte wrote in a 2014 essay for HuffPost
RJ Mitte, best known for playing Walter “Flynn” White Jr. in Breaking Bad , helped change perceptions of cerebral palsy through his acting and advocacy, demonstrating that disability does not have to define a person's identity or limit their ambitions.
The actor, who died by suicide on Monday, 12 October, at the age of 34, leaves behind a legacy that extends far beyond his television career. Through his portrayal of Walt Jr. and his work supporting people with disabilities, Mitte helped challenge stereotypes and create greater visibility for disabled performers in the entertainment industry.
“I have cerebral palsy but I've never let it hold me back,” Mitte wrote in a 2014 essay for HuffPost, reflecting on his experiences growing up and learning to stand up to bullies. “It shouldn't define you. I just happen to have CP.”
Those words reflected the approach he brought to Breaking Bad , in which he played the teenage son of Walter White, portrayed by Bryan Cranston. Although both Mitte and his character have cerebral palsy, the condition was not the defining focus of Walt Jr.'s storyline. Instead, the character was shown navigating family relationships, adolescence and the increasingly dangerous consequences of his father's actions.
Emma Livingstone, founder and chief executive of Up, the Adult Cerebral Palsy Movement, told the BBC that the portrayal was powerful precisely because the character's disability was part of his life rather than the entire focus of his story.
“When we see RJ Mitte on TV just playing a role, but who also happens to have CP, I think that's really powerful,” she said.
Mitte was diagnosed with cerebral palsy at the age of three. The NHS describes cerebral palsy as a group of lifelong conditions affecting movement and co-ordination, caused by problems with the developing brain around the time of birth.
He was cast in Breaking Bad at the age of 14, appearing throughout the series' five-season run from 2008 to 2013. The drama became one of television's most acclaimed programmes, and Mitte's performance helped bring a disabled character into millions of homes without reducing his story to his condition.
In a 2016 interview with Channel 4 News, Mitte said Breaking Bad had “pioneered a lot of TV and writers to be more brave”. However, he also stressed that the entertainment industry still had progress to make in representing disabled people.
His influence extended beyond acting. Mitte supported organisations including United Cerebral Palsy and Can Do Canines, and established the Mitte Foundation, which offered community grants in his hometown in Texas.
Susan Sellers, president and chief executive of United Cerebral Palsy, praised his commitment to ensuring that people with cerebral palsy and other disabilities were seen, heard and given opportunities to reach their potential.
Mitte's impact was particularly significant for aspiring disabled actors, many of whom have described how seeing performers like him on screen helped them imagine careers in the industry.
Ruth Madeley, an actress with spina bifida who portrays disability rights advocate Judy Heumann in the film Being Heumann , told the BBC that representation can help people recognise possibilities they might otherwise overlook.
“If you don't see it, you don't think it's possible,” Madeley said, explaining that acting had not even seemed like a career option to her when she was younger. She described Mitte as a powerful example for young disabled people interested in the arts, praising both his talent and his work challenging barriers.
Keron Day, who appeared in Netflix's Sex Education , also credited Mitte's legacy with helping create opportunities for disabled performers. Speaking to the BBC from a television set, Day said that working in the creative industries was itself a tribute to the path Mitte had helped open.
Comedian and screenwriter Laurence Clarke similarly emphasised the importance of seeing disabled people represented on television. While acknowledging that portrayals had improved since Breaking Bad premiered, he said there was still more work to do.
Mitte continued acting after the series ended, appearing in projects including Hannah Montana , Switched at Birth and Standing Up for Sunny . His later work included Talking to Strangers , released earlier in 2026.
Earlier this month, Mitte also reflected on the enduring reputation of Breaking Bad and the difficulty of matching its success. He said that the series had set a high standard for his own career, while expressing interest in the possibility of continuing its story.
Yet Mitte regarded his advocacy as one of the most meaningful outcomes of his success. He explained that the recognition he gained through the series had given him a platform to support people with disabilities and help others make their voices heard.
“The greatest thing that Breaking Bad has given me is to be able to lend my voice to causes that make a meaningful impact, that change people's lives,” he said.
His legacy lies not only in a memorable television performance but also in the opportunities he helped make visible for others. By portraying a character whose life extended beyond disability, and by speaking openly about his own experiences, Mitte contributed to a broader understanding of what disabled people can achieve on screen and beyond it.

‘Off Campus’ star Antonio Cipriano reveals his favourite romance trope and dream role while promoting Fireball vanilla

The actor shared his reading preferences while partnering with Fireball to promote its limited-edition Torch’d Vanilla flavour and romantasy-inspired collectible.

Speaking to PEOPLE , Cipriano revealed that friends-to-lovers is his favourite romance trope. He explained that he enjoys stories in which two people develop a genuine bond before discovering their romantic feelings for each other.
“Finding two people who really genuinely care about each other without the romance first and then for them to find that in each other, I think is really, really beautiful,” the actor said.
Cipriano also explained why he prefers slow-burn romances, particularly when the relationship develops gradually before reaching an emotional conclusion.
He said books should “be a slow burn for a long time until the last 40 pages”, adding that the eventual romantic payoff makes the wait worthwhile.
Discussing his Off Campus character, John Logan, Cipriano praised his work ethic, loyalty and ability to love deeply. He also expressed empathy for Logan because of the pressure he puts on himself.

title: Hundreds queue in Hong Kong to glimpse Van Gogh painting unseen in public for 60 years
description: Van Gogh   s long unseen painting draws Hong Kong crowds ahead of a record breaking  180 million Sotheby   s auction
content:
Van Gogh’s long-unseen painting draws Hong Kong crowds ahead of a record-breaking $180 million Sotheby’s auction
Hundreds of people queued in Hong Kong on Tuesday to view a Vincent van Gogh painting never publicly exhibited in more than six decades, ahead of a Sotheby's ​auction in New York where it is expected to fetch about $180 million.
The November 18 ‌auction will test the strength of the high-end art market, in which collectors have continued to compete for scarce trophy works, undeterred by broader economic uncertainty.
Painted in May 1890, "Châtaigniers en fleurs", or "Chestnut Trees in Blossom", is one ​of the most important works from the Dutch artist's final days in the French ​village of Auvers-sur-Oise, where he died about two months later, aged 37.
The painting ⁠is poised to set a new auction record for a Van Gogh work, said Scott Niichel, ​of Sotheby's modern and contemporary art department in New York.
"This is a moment of extraordinary optimism, ​frenetic energy, enthusiasm, passion, and colour in the artist's body of work," he said.
Paintings from Van Gogh's final Auvers-sur-Oise period, just after his release from a psychiatric asylum in Saint-Remy-de-Provence, rarely come to market and the auction will ​draw the attention of collectors, museums and investors.
"I'd never heard of this painting before, so I ​wanted to see it with my own eyes," said Li Shanshan, a 50-year-old art lover who travelled about ‌2-1/2 hours ⁠from the southern city of Shenzhen to view the artwork.
The painting, which depicts a massive blossoming chestnut tree with a flowering canopy that dominates the composition, will be sold among part of a collection of 12 long-unseen works, including items by Paul Cezanne and Claude Monet.
Five unveiled at Sotheby's ​in London in late ​September included Cezanne's "Arlequin" and ⁠Monet’s "Le Jardin des Tuileries".
After Van Gogh's death in July 1890, "Châtaigniers en fleurs" was passed to his brother Theo, and then to the latter's widow ​Johanna van Gogh-Bonger and their son Vincent Willem.
Subsequently it was owned by ​German publisher ⁠Samuel Fischer, founder of S. Fischer Verlag, before entering the collection of George "Buddy" DeSylva, the American songwriter, film producer and co-founder of Capitol Records.
In 1953, the painting was acquired by collector Harriet Harris-Jonas, whose holdings ⁠were ​considered significant enough that New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art ​organised visits for patrons to view works in her Fifth Avenue apartment.
The painting was acquired by the Blaquier family from ​art dealer Wildenstein in 1975.

title: Adam Brody reveals what his 12 year marriage to Leighton Meester has taught him
description: Brody explained that people can experience different levels of maturity depending on the circumstances
content:
Brody explained that people can experience different levels of maturity depending on the circumstances
Adam Brody has opened up about the lessons he has learnt from his 12-year marriage to Leighton Meester, explaining why humility, compromise and a willingness to adjust are essential to making a relationship last.
The Nobody Wants This star, 46, shared his reflections in an interview with Elle , published on October 8, 2026. Brody, who married Gossip Girl actress Meester, 40, in 2014, discussed how marriage has changed his perspective on relationships and the importance of recognising that neither partner is always right.
Asked about the wisdom he had gained over 12 years of marriage, Brody explained that people can experience different levels of maturity depending on the circumstances.
"That there's a duality in all of us," he told the magazine. "Oftentimes, I feel mature and responsible, and other times, I feel like a little boy still, and I can't believe I'm the age I am."
The actor went on to explain that maintaining a long-term relationship requires people to put aside their pride and consider their partner's needs alongside their own.
"But I think what I've learned is, if you want it to last and you're taking it seriously, there's a certain level of humbling yourself that is required," Brody said.
He added that couples must be prepared to make adjustments without losing their individual identities. "You have to be willing to adjust. Not change the core of who you are, but really factor someone else's wants and desires and needs into the equation."
Brody also acknowledged that accepting the possibility of being wrong is an important part of sharing a life with another person. "You're not always going to be right, and you have to accept that. It's a lot easier to always be right when you're single," he said.
His comments come as the couple continue to keep much of their relationship private, despite both being established Hollywood actors. Brody and Meester first met through mutual industry connections before reconnecting while working on the 2011 film The Oranges . Their relationship became public in 2013, and they married in a private ceremony in Northern California in early 2014.
The couple share two children: daughter Arlo, born in 2015, and a son, born in 2020, whose name they have not publicly disclosed.
Meester has also spoken about what has helped their marriage endure. In an interview with People in January 2026, she said that genuinely liking one another and enjoying each other's company were central to their relationship.
"I think just liking each other, and getting along is a big part of it," she said, adding that a relationship comes down, at its most basic level, to being able to say, "I really like this person."
The actress also emphasised the importance of accepting imperfections and remaining willing to work on oneself. She explained that being with another person means recognising that both partners will have flaws and challenge each other at times.
Brody previously offered his own advice on lasting relationships during an appearance on Today with Hoda and Jenna in September 2024. He said choosing a good partner and listening to them were important elements of a successful marriage, while acknowledging that relationships still require sacrifice and personal growth.
Beyond discussing his marriage, Brody is preparing to return as Noah in the third season of Netflix's romantic comedy series Nobody Wants This , which is scheduled to premiere on 22 October 2026. The series follows Noah, a rabbi, and Joanne, played by Kristen Bell, as they navigate their relationship and the challenges that come with their different backgrounds.
Brody's latest reflections offer a glimpse into the perspective he has gained through more than a decade of marriage, highlighting the importance of humility, flexibility and mutual understanding in a lasting partnership.

title: What is fuelling India s protests over changes to voter lists
description: Critics say the centralised system leaves errors uncorrected  removing millions from voter rolls
content:
Critics say the centralised system leaves errors uncorrected, removing millions from voter rolls
Major protests have convulsed the Indian capital for more than a week as the opposition Congress party and young people, spearheaded by the "Cockroach" movement, demand the resignation of the top election official.
The dispute centres on the removal of 130 million voters from electoral rolls, a move that critics say benefited Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party in recent state ​elections, claims denied by the poll body and his Bharatiya Janata Party.
What is the revision and why it being done?
The exercise, or Special Intensive Revision (SIR), ‌is a house-to-house revision of the voter rolls, launched in the eastern state of Bihar in June 2025 by the Election Commission, to update voter lists and remove duplicate and ineligible voters, before being expanded nationwide. The commission is an independent constitutional body, though its chief was appointed by a government-majority panel, drawing allegations of political bias, which it denies.
In contrast to the past system of voluntary updates to electoral rolls by voters, the ​SIR — the largest such exercise in nearly two decades — has drawn criticism for using centralised software, with limited powers given to local election officials who check if voters ​have died, moved or are ineligible.
Critics say the centralised system denies local officials the chance to correct errors, resulting in discrepancies that have struck ⁠millions from voter rolls or sent many scrambling to locate ancestral documents or launch legal challenges.
The strict paperwork rules, short deadlines and large-scale deletions that characterise the exercise ​have provoked criticism that they could disproportionately exclude poor, migrant, elderly, homeless and nomadic people.
Read More: Indian police detain 'cockroach' movement founder Abhijeet Dipke
Those dropped are hunting for decades-old documents regarding themselves, their parents and even grandparents in some cases, while ​others seek to correct names altered by translation, spelling or data-entry errors.
Many have been asked to show that they or their parents figured on electoral rolls.
Protesters say more than 130 million voters, or a number larger than the population of Japan, have been dropped from draft rolls across 30 states and territories, an assertion disputed by the Election Commission.
Led by its chief, Gyanesh Kumar , the commission panel says its deletions largely cover the dead, ​or those who moved, registered more than once or are otherwise ineligible.
Critics say the effort shifts to citizens the burden of proving they belong on the rolls, and warn that mismatched ​records could complicate efforts to establish citizenship or receive state welfare benefits.
Why is pressure mounting on the election commission?
Pressure grew after the Indian Express newspaper reported that two of Kumar's panel colleagues had raised at ‌least 14 formal ⁠objections over 10 months concerning voter rolls, registration procedures and digital systems.
Differing views are a part of normal deliberations, the panel says. But opposition parties led by Congress and youth groups have protested, calling for Kumar to step down.
Were Eastern state elections a flashpoint?
This year's elections in the state of West Bengal, swept by Modi's BJP in its first such victory there, became a major political issue after millions of voters were excluded or subjected to review, excluding them from voting.
Opposition parties said eligible voters were disenfranchised, which disproportionately affected Muslim voters, benefiting the BJP. The party ​and the poll body denied the accusations.
In May, the ⁠Supreme Court upheld the Election Commission's SIR exercise, saying accurate electoral rolls were essential for free and fair elections, but ruled that the poll panel could not make a final determination on citizenship.
Opposition parties returned to court this week, citing arbitrary voter deletions and other irregularities, while the ​Election Commission on October 1 directed officials to identify omitted voters and ease the path to re-enrolment.
What are the implications for future state elections?
The revision comes ahead ⁠of a series of important state elections beginning in early 2027, including in India's most populous state of Uttar Pradesh, ruled by the BJP. It is unclear if people left off the electoral rolls will be put back in time to vote.
In Bihar, several people are still appealing for their names to be put back on the electoral roll more than one year later.
The "cockroach" youth ​movement, which has mobilised protests in recent months against a range of issues from government school infrastructure to ​jobs for young people, is one of the biggest political challenges to Modi and the BJP in his 12 years in power.
The movement forced the resignation of Modi's education minister in July over an exam leak scandal. The group continues to ​put pressure on Modi's government for economic and social reforms. The group's success has also inspired opposition parties to join forces.

Joe Manganiello suspects Tom Cruise influenced his lost ‘Reacher’ role over their shared ex, Sofía Vergara
Joe Manganiello believes Tom Cruise may have played a role in his missing out on Amazon's Reacher , according to claims in his upcoming memoir, Bloodlines .
The actor's team reportedly suspected Cruise intervened because of his past relationship with Sofía Vergara, Manganiello's former wife.
According to an advance copy of the memoir obtained by the New York Post, Manganiello was initially considered a strong contender for the lead role in the action series. The actor writes that he met Skydance producer Don Granger for approximately 90 minutes to discuss the character of Jack Reacher.
Granger reportedly praised Manganiello's resemblance to the character described in Lee Child's novels, calling him the closest person to Reacher he had encountered. Manganiello also claims that Skydance owner David Ellison and Child were impressed with his performance.
However, the casting process allegedly took a different direction after then-Amazon Studios chief Jen Salke expressed frustration at being excluded from decisions by male producers. Manganiello's team subsequently speculated that Cruise might have opposed his casting because of Vergara.
Cruise reportedly dated Vergara in 2005, years before she married Manganiello in 2015. The couple divorced in 2023. Manganiello has not presented evidence that Cruise influenced the casting decision, and no response from the actor has been reported.
Cruise previously portrayed Jack Reacher in the 2012 film Jack Reacher and its 2016 sequel, Jack Reacher: Never Go Back . Amazon later adapted the book series for television, casting Alan Ritchson in the lead role in September 2020. The series premiered on Prime Video in February 2022 and was renewed for a fifth season in May 2026.
Manganiello's memoir also explores his health struggles and the breakdown of his marriage to Vergara, including his account of how his autoimmune disease affected their relationship.

title: Ustad Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan   s 78th birth anniversary  Remembering the king of qawwali
description: Pakistan remembers Ustad Khan on his 78th birth anniversary  celebrating his voice and global musical legacy
content:
Pakistan remembers Ustad Khan on his 78th birth anniversary, celebrating his voice and global musical legacy
The 78th birth anniversary of legendary Pakistani singer and qawwali maestro Ustad Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan is being marked on Tuesday, October 13, as fans around the world pay tribute to the artist who transformed traditional Sufi music into an international phenomenon.
Born on October 13, 1948, in Faisalabad , Khan became one of Pakistan’s most influential musical figures. His extraordinary vocal range, emotionally charged performances and distinctive singing style earned him recognition far beyond his homeland, making him a celebrated ambassador of Pakistani music.
Khan played a significant role in introducing qawwali, a traditional form of Sufi devotional music, to international audiences. Through his powerful voice and captivating stage performances, he brought a centuries-old musical tradition to listeners from different cultures and backgrounds. He was widely called Shahenshah-e-Qawwali, reflecting his enormous influence on the genre.
His popularity extended across generations, with celebrated performances and songs such as Dam Mast Qalandar , Tumhe Dillagi Bhool Jani Paray Gi and Afreen Afreen continuing to attract music lovers. His ability to combine spiritual expression with emotional intensity helped make his music appealing even to audiences unfamiliar with the languages in which he sang.
Beyond traditional qawwali, Khan demonstrated a willingness to explore new musical styles. His collaborations with internationally renowned artists helped introduce his voice to listeners who might otherwise never have encountered the genre.
He worked with British musician Peter Gabriel on the soundtrack album Passion and collaborated with Canadian musician Michael Brook on the albums Mustt Mustt and Night Song . His vocals also featured in international film soundtracks, including The Last Temptation of Christ , Natural Born Killers and Dead Man Walking .
These projects demonstrated how traditional South Asian devotional music could connect with contemporary musical arrangements without losing its distinctive character. His international collaborations also helped establish qawwali as an important part of the global world-music scene and he was credited with a record-setting output of 125 albums as a qawwali artist
Khan’s achievements brought international attention to Pakistan’s musical heritage. In 1987, he received the Pride of Performance award from the Government of Pakistan in recognition of his contribution to the arts. His album Intoxicated Spirit also received a Grammy nomination in 1997 in the traditional folk category.
His influence continues through musicians who draw inspiration from his vocal techniques, improvisational skills and experimental approach. His nephew, Rahat Fateh Ali Khan, has also helped carry the family’s musical tradition to newer audiences.
Although Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan died in London on August 16, 1997, at the age of 48, his music remains widely celebrated. His recordings continue to introduce new listeners to the emotional depth of qawwali and the spiritual themes at its heart.
As admirers mark his 78th birth anniversary, Khan’s legacy stands as a reminder of music’s ability to transcend borders, languages and generations. Decades after his death, his voice continues to represent an enduring chapter in Pakistan’s cultural history.

title: IMF flags risks to global economy from AI market correction  war and debt
description: IMF warned poorer nations hit by the Iran war energy shock may have to cut spending or restructure debt
content:
IMF warned poorer nations hit by the Iran war energy shock may have to cut spending or restructure debt
The International Monetary Fund on Tuesday flagged significant growth and financial stability risks from a potential end to the AI investment boom, growing debt levels ‌and a prolonged Middle East conflict.
The IMF forecast global growth at 3.1% for 2026, a slight uptick from a 3.0% forecast in July as still-strong AI infrastructure investment offset higher oil prices caused by the war in the Middle East.
The latest World Economic Outlook report, released in Bangkok during the annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank, also predicts 3.4% growth in 2027, but that is based on assumptions that the Strait of Hormuz reopens by March and shipping conditions ​return to the pre-war situation by October 2027.
A more protracted war that kept oil prices above $130 through the first quarter of 2027 would cut growth next year by half a ​percentage point, the IMF said.
In another downside scenario, the IMF said that a steep drop in AI investment could lead to a sharp fall ⁠in asset prices, ultimately cutting global GDP by 1.1% by 2028, including a 1.8% drop in US output.
Also Read: Finance Minister Aurangzeb vows to strengthen collective influence of G-24
"We now have an economy that is standing on one leg, the AI leg," IMF Managing ​Director Kristalina Georgieva told a Bretton Woods Committee event. "What if it wobbles? What if there is disappointment and that leads to potentially a more difficult environment?"
The IMF emphasised similar risks in its separate Global Financial ​Stability Report , warning policymakers needed to avoid "complacency" in guarding against a potential pullback in AI investment and stock valuations.
"If there are questions about the monetisation of AI, the equity investments will deplete in value, the debt may be difficult to service, and the revenue commitments in the future may not materialise," Jason Wu, assistant director of the IMF's Global Markets Analysis Division, told a press conference at the Bangkok meetings.
An ensuing AI market correction would feed back through ​the real economy, dragging down broader asset prices and overall demand through a wealth effect reduction, said Athanasios Vamvakidis, deputy director of the IMF's Monetary and Capital Markets Department.
It would also lead to ​reduced trade, IMF chief economist Silvana Tenreyro said. Trade in AI goods grew 29% between 2023 and 2025, more than triple the 8.3% growth rate of global trade over the same period. Without the AI trade, overall ‌growth in ⁠trade would have been only 4.6%, she said.
The concerns highlighted in Bangkok also include AI-driven cybersecurity risks. They come as banking regulators step up efforts to contain AI-related risks, with Reuters reporting that major US regulators are quizzing banks on their use of advanced AI models and European regulators are pressing banks to boost recovery plans.
But even the steep drop in output seen under the worst-case AI risk scenario was not likely to reduce growth to levels consistent with a global recession, IMF deputy research director Petya Koeva Brooks told Reuters in an interview.
The IMF reports and meeting participants also highlighted ​risks from elevated public debt levels and rising ​bond yields that may be driven higher still ⁠by war-driven inflation pressures, eating up budgets to service debts and sapping growth.
Georgieva warned against complacency in "systemically important" advanced economies that are "negligent about their fiscal position" and failing to rein in debts like developing economies have been forced to do.
Developing countries must cut spending despite war shock
The IMF also warned that while low-income developing countries were dealing with the disproportionate impacts of the Iran war-fuelled energy shock, many had "no choice" but to cut spending or potentially face debt restructuring.
Speaking to AFP on the sidelines of the organisation's Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Brooks said heavily indebted, oil-importing countries were facing the worst of the energy shock, and had difficult choices in helping their citizens through the crisis.
"Unfortunately, after years of the global economy being hit (by) shock after shock, debt levels have increased quite a lot, and at the same time, inflation has become a problem," she said.
"For those countries that are most vulnerable, this is where the consumption basket is heavily weighted towards energy and food, and so indeed it is much much more difficult," she added.
Read More: IMF raises inflation forecast to 9.9%
The debt vulnerabilities of many developing economies are a "major barrier" to ​inclusive growth, said Nigerian Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele, who chairs the Group of 24 developing nations, warning that member governments were increasingly contending with mounting ​debt burdens.
Oyedele said estimates showed ⁠that developing countries were paying $500 billion more for their debt than developed countries, even as they contend with growing deficits.
The IMF this week is urging countries to begin politically painful steps to bring budgets under control. It singled out Britain for praise as the only major advanced economy to have set out clear plans to reduce government borrowing over the coming years, but urged it to stay the course just weeks before the ⁠new UK ​government unveils budget plans.
Few governments are listening to the IMF's calls to shrink borrowing, said Josh Lipsky, vice president of ​international economics at the Atlantic Council, who is attending the Bangkok meetings.
"France, Germany, the US all need to do fiscal consolidation, but they're moving in the opposite direction," Lipsky said. "I'm afraid that it's going to take some kind of crisis to wake ​up and realise that this is what has to be done."

title: Robert Pattinson confirms  The Batman Part II  production pause after Matt Reeves steps away
description: His comments follow a statement from DC Studios confirming that filming on the sequel had been temporarily halted
content:
His comments follow a statement from DC Studios confirming that filming on the sequel had been temporarily halted
Robert Pattinson has confirmed that production on The Batman Part II will pause temporarily following director Matt Reeves’ decision to step away from the project to focus on a family matter.
The actor shared the update while promoting his latest film, Primetime , explaining that the team would take a short break before determining its next steps. “Yeah, we’re pausing for a little bit, and then we’re going to figure it all out,” Pattinson said during an interview with Official Pop Drop.
His comments follow a statement from DC Studios confirming that filming on the highly anticipated sequel had been temporarily halted. The studio said Reeves was taking time to address a family matter and emphasised that he had its full support.
“Production on The Batman Part II has been temporarily paused while Matt Reeves focuses on a family matter,” the statement read. “Matt has the full support of DC Studios and we look forward to continuing the journey soon.”
Reeves directed the 2022 film The Batman , which introduced Pattinson as a younger Bruce Wayne operating in a crime-ridden Gotham City. The film received positive reviews for its darker approach to the superhero and earned more than $770 million worldwide, establishing a separate cinematic interpretation of the DC character.
The sequel has already experienced several delays. Originally scheduled to arrive in October 2025, the film was subsequently pushed back to October 2026 before another postponement moved its release to October 2027. Warner Bros. later rescheduled the film for 18 February 2028.
Filming began in London in June 2026, with Pattinson returning as the Caped Crusader. The cast also includes Andy Serkis as Alfred Pennyworth, Colin Farrell as the Penguin and Jeffrey Wright as James Gordon. New additions include Scarlett Johansson and Sebastian Stan, although details about their characters have largely been kept under wraps.
The sequel is expected to continue Reeves’ grounded interpretation of Gotham, exploring deeper corruption and the consequences of the events depicted in the first film. Reeves co-wrote the screenplay with Mattson Tomlin.
Despite the production pause, neither DC Studios nor Warner Bros. has announced a further change to the film’s release date. The length of the interruption also remains unclear, with Pattinson’s comments indicating that the team will reassess the schedule before resuming work.
For now, fans will have to wait for further updates on the sequel’s production. The studio’s statement and Pattinson’s remarks suggest that the pause is temporary, although the timeline for filming to resume has not been confirmed.

title: Iqra Aziz and Imran Ashraf revive Bhola and Noori nostalgia with heartwarming instagram post
description: Both actors shared nostalgic pictures from their hit drama  exciting fans
content:
Both actors shared nostalgic pictures from their hit drama, exciting fans
Pakistani actors Iqra Aziz and Imran Ashraf sparked nostalgia among drama fans after a recent Instagram Story brought back memories of their much-loved characters, Bhola and Noori, from the acclaimed drama serial Ranjha Ranjha Kardi .
Aziz shared a photograph of herself with Ashraf on her Instagram Story, adding the words “Bhola aur Noori” alongside a star emoji. The picture shows the two actors sitting closely together in a warmly lit indoor setting, dressed in casual black outfits and smiling at the camera. Imran is seated beside Iqra, who leans towards him, creating a relaxed and affectionate moment that instantly recalls their on-screen pairing.
The actress also added Muqaddraan , sung by Rahma Ali and Saania, as the background soundtrack. The emotional music further strengthened the nostalgic feel of the post, reminding fans of the drama's memorable moments and the journey of its central characters.
The post quickly drew attention from viewers who continue to remember Bhola and Noori as one of Pakistani television's most distinctive on-screen duos.
Ashraf followed by posting the same image to his Instagram to write, "Great Iqra Aziz. Bhola and Noori".
Fans expressed their love, with some questioning if there was a new project. Others wrote, "My Bhola and Noori" followed by "My Ranjha Ranjha Kardi heart omg".
First aired in 2018, Ranjha Ranjha Kardi earned widespread appreciation for its compelling storytelling, layered characters and exploration of difficult social realities.
Imran's portrayal of Bhola, a young man with an intellectual disability, stood out for its emotional intensity and unconventional characterisation. Meanwhile, Iqra played Noori, a determined young woman from a disadvantaged background whose ambitions and life circumstances shape her complicated journey.
Their performances helped the drama move beyond a conventional romantic narrative, addressing themes of social class, identity, vulnerability and relationships. The series also encouraged conversations around disability, consent and society's treatment of marginalised individuals.
In 2019, Ashraf highlighted his gratitude towards viewers who embraced Bhola, with the actor acknowledging the affection audiences had shown the character.
Aziz has established herself as one of Pakistan's popular television actresses through performances across comedy, romance and emotionally demanding dramas.
She became particularly well known for playing Jiya in the hit Ramadan serial Suno Chanda , where her comic timing and lively screen presence won over audiences. Her role as Noori in Ranjha Ranjha Kardi showcased another side of her acting, allowing her to portray a more complex character navigating ambition, hardship and difficult personal choices.
Her other notable projects include Choti Si Zindagi , Khamoshi , Qurban and Ranjha Ranjha Kardi , demonstrating her range across different genres.
In an interview with The Express Tribune , Iqra also discussed the sensitive issues raised by Ranjha Ranjha Kardi , including a storyline involving marital rape
Ashraf, on the other hand, has earned recognition for taking on challenging roles that move beyond conventional television heroes. His performance as Bhola remains one of his most talked-about portrayals, earning praise for the emotional depth and individuality he brought to the character.
Before and after the drama, Imran appeared in several notable productions, including Alif Allah Aur Insaan . His willingness to explore unconventional characters has helped establish his reputation as a versatile performer in the Pakistani entertainment industry.
The latest Instagram moment serves as a reminder of the impact the two actors made together. While there is no confirmed announcement of another collaboration, Iqra and Imran's reunion in a photograph has given fans a reason to revisit the story of Bhola and Noori and celebrate a drama that remains memorable in Pakistan's television landscape.

Meghan Markle and Prince Harry will visit Nottingham for their first joint U.K. outing since returning with family
Meghan Markle and Prince Harry are preparing for their first official joint outing in the United Kingdom since returning to Britain with their children in August 2026.
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex will visit Nottingham on Thursday, October 15, as they resume their charitable work and public engagements.
A source close to the couple told PEOPLE that Harry and Meghan initially prioritised helping their children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, adjust to their new surroundings and settle into school.
“Now they’re both excited to focus more on their work and the projects that matter to them,” the source said.
During their Nottingham visit, the couple will meet organisations supporting young people and local communities. Meghan is expected to reunite with women from London's Hubb Community Kitchen, whom she worked with on the 2018 charity cookbook Together: Our Community Cookbook .
The Duke and Duchess will also visit the Community Recording Studio, which supports young people affected by violence, and Epic Partners, an organisation that provides mentoring and sports opportunities.
The visit marks a return to Nottingham, where Harry and Meghan made their first official joint appearance following their engagement announcement in November 2017.
Since returning to Britain, Meghan has gradually resumed public activities while maintaining contact with friends in Montecito, California. She recently met Malala Yousafzai in London and collaborated on a sweatshirt supporting Moms Offering More, a nonprofit that assists mothers and families.
Prince Harry has also continued his charitable engagements, attending the Invictus Spirit Gala Dinner and Awards and the WellChild Awards. He recently returned to the United States to speak at the Clinton Global Initiative meeting.
The couple continue to balance their professional commitments with family life while keeping details of their U.K. residence private. They also retain their home in Montecito, where they settled after stepping back from their roles as working members of the royal family in 2020.
However, their return has not resolved tensions within the royal family. Harry and Prince William remain estranged, with reports indicating that the brothers are not in direct contact.

title: President reaffirms commitment to regional peace under Makkah pact in meeting with MDA chief
description: Says Makkah pact is  purely defensive in nature  not directed against any country
content:
Says Makkah pact is purely defensive in nature, not directed against any country
President Asif Ali Zardari reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to regional peace and stability under the Makkah Defence Alliance (MDA) in a meeting with Lieutenant General (Rtd) Nauman Mahmood on Tuesday in Islamabad.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed Makkah pact, a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
In a post on X, the office of the president stated that Lieutenant General (Rtd) Nauman Mahmood, the first secretary general of the MDA, formerly called the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), called on President Zardari at Aiwan-e-Sadr.
Read : Lt Gen (retd) Nauman Mahmood appointed first secretary general of Makkah pact
"The president expressed confidence that the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed by Pakistan, Türkiye and Saudi Arabia on August 7, 2026, would strengthen regional peace and stability through defensive cooperation guided by the principles of the UN Charter and international law," it added.
President Reaffirms Pakistan’s Commitment to Regional Peace and Defensive Cooperation Under Makkah Accord Lieutenant General (Rtd.) Nauman Mahmood, the first Secretary General pursuant to Makkah Joint Defence Agreement called on President Asif Ali Zardari at Aiwan-e-Sadr today.… pic.twitter.com/9anJjovXdc
The president further underscored that the accord was "purely defensive in nature and not directed against any country, nor it constituted the formation of a new bloc".
The statement emphasised that Pakistan remained committed to the peaceful resolution of conflicts and enhanced regional and multilateral cooperation to address emerging challenges.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi was also present during the meeting.
Lt Gen (retd) Mahmood is a former senior Pakistan Army commander with experience in military operations, intelligence, professional military education and strategic affairs.
He was in the race for the army chief when the government was looking for the successor of General (retired) Qamar Javed Bajwa in November 2022. He was known as one of the most non-controversial army generals with an impeccable career and apolitical approach.
Read More : Ex-army officer to head Makkah pact secretariat
A member of the Baloch Regiment, he was commissioned into the army on September 11, 1987.
During his military career, he served in command and instructional appointments, including assignments with an infantry formation and at the Command and Staff College. As a major general, he commanded an infantry division in North Waziristan.
He also served in the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), including as director general of its Analysis Directorate, where his responsibilities involved assessment of regional and international developments.
After his promotion to lieutenant general, Naumam served at General Headquarters as inspector general for Communications and Information Technology.
He was promoted to lieutenant general in April 2019 and subsequently appointed commander of XI Corps, commonly known as Peshawar Corps, in December that year.
He remained in command of the corps until November 2021, during a period when Afghanistan was undergoing a major political and security transition following the US military withdrawal.
Nauman was then appointed president of the National Defence University (NDU), Islamabad, becoming the institution's 35th president. He served in that position until April 2023, when he retired from the army.
He has attended professional military courses in Pakistan and abroad, including at the Command and Staff College in Egypt, and is a graduate of the NDU.
On September 23, the government appointed Lt Gen Mahmood as the first secretary general of the MJDA.
The appointment was the first major institutional development since Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the pact, and his appointment gives Pakistan the responsibility of establishing and leading the alliance's first secretariat during its formative three-year period.
The decision was taken at the inaugural meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee, held under the MJDA, which brought together the foreign and defence ministers and military chiefs of the three countries in Istanbul on August 31.
Under the arrangement agreed in Istanbul, the secretary general would head the alliance's General Secretariat, based in the Saudi capital and tasked with overseeing implementation of the agreement, coordinating joint activities among the three militaries and supporting expanded defence-industrial cooperation.
For Islamabad, the role also provides an opportunity to shape the working structure of the new defence arrangement as Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye move from the political commitment announced in Makkah towards a more organised mechanism for defence coordination.
Significance of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
The Makkah pact was the latest step in longstanding military and strategic cooperation between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. Signed in Makkah, the pact established a framework for collective deterrence and stipulated that an armed attack on any one of the three countries would be considered an attack on all three, while providing for wider cooperation across defence.
Also Read : Makkah defence alliance agrees to 'rapid force deployment' in Saudi Arabia: FO
The agreement followed nearly a year of negotiations and came amid heightened instability across the Middle East. Turkiye and Pakistan had sought closer regional security cooperation, while Saudi Arabia had faced growing security concerns as conflicts spread across the region, threatening its territory, energy infrastructure and ambitious economic development plans.
For Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the trilateral pact is built on their Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed in September 2025. That agreement stated that “any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both” and committed the two sides to strengthening defence cooperation and joint deterrence.
The three countries already had extensive military links. Pakistan had provided training and technical assistance to Saudi forces for decades, while Islamabad and Ankara had maintained close defence ties through military training, naval cooperation and defence equipment. In 2023, Saudi Arabia agreed to purchase Turkish drones in what Ankara described as its largest defence export contract.
The signing in Makkah, Islam’s holiest city, added symbolic weight to an agreement that brought together three countries with significant military and strategic capabilities. It also came as Pakistan sought to avoid becoming directly involved in the Iran conflict, instead pursuing diplomatic efforts to mediate, while strengthening its broader regional security partnerships.

title: Ethan Hawke leads supernatural horror podcast    Midnight Radio    ahead of Halloween
description: The series features Noah Centineo  Willa Fitzgerald and Vincent D   Onofrio alongside Hawke
content:
The series features Noah Centineo, Willa Fitzgerald and Vincent D’Onofrio alongside Hawke
Ethan Hawke is entering the world of audio horror with Midnight Radio , a supernatural thriller podcast scheduled to launch shortly before Halloween. The actor stars as the host of a late night AM radio programme whose routine broadcast takes a disturbing turn after he receives a mysterious call.
The caller claims to have been involved in a secret United States space mission that disappeared from public knowledge. As the story unfolds in real time, the radio host becomes caught in a web of alleged government cover ups, interdimensional breaches and psychological warfare.
According to the official synopsis, strange signals concealed within radio static gradually reveal themselves, raising questions about the identity and intentions of the voice on the other end of the line.
The first episode is scheduled for release on October 22 through the iHeartRadio app and major podcast platforms. The nine episode series will then release new instalments every Thursday at midnight Pacific Time, or 3am Eastern Time.
The project reunites Hawke with filmmaker Scott Derrickson and screenwriter C Robert Cargill, the creative team associated with horror films Sinister and The Black Phone . Hawke starred in both films.
Derrickson and Cargill created and co wrote the podcast, which is produced by Hawke and his wife Ryan Hawke’s Under the Influence Productions, alongside Crooked Highway and Mickey Schiff, in collaboration with iHeartPodcasts.
The ensemble also includes Noah Centineo, Willa Fitzgerald, Vincent D’Onofrio, Levon Hawke, Austin Pendleton and Hubert Point Du Jour.
Hawke said the team had no previous podcast experience but enjoyed having creative freedom. He also highlighted the intimacy of audio storytelling and its potential to create fear through sound alone.
“There’s an intimacy to the audio only medium that can be really powerful, and in our case, used to a terrifying effect,” Hawke said.
Derrickson described the project as an independently financed labour of love, explaining that the creators wanted to develop a complex narrative without creative restrictions. The collaboration with iHeartPodcasts will bring the series to listeners across multiple platforms.

title: Influential Hindu group urges India to block Starlink amid Musk Ambani feud

content:
The call for ​Starlink's ban came from Swadeshi Jagran Manch, the economic wing of the RSS
An influential Hindu nationalist group close to India's ruling party urged the government on Tuesday to block Elon Musk's Starlink from launching satellite ​internet services in the country, citing national security concerns.
Starlink's four-year wait ‌to launch in India has come under renewed scrutiny after Musk last week accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government and billionaire Mukesh Ambani of stalling its entry to favour Ambani's Reliance Jio.
India's communications ministry ​said last week that security assessments were under way for Starlink and ​rival satellite ventures backed by Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel. It ⁠described suggestions that the approval process was unfair or discriminatory as "baseless and misconceived".
Read: Satellite internet plan in final stage
The call for ​Starlink's ban came from Swadeshi Jagran Manch (SJM), the economic wing of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak ​Sangh (RSS), the Hindu nationalist organisation that is the ideological parent of Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party.
SJM also linked its demand to trade tensions with the US. If Washington imposes high tariffs on ​Indian imports "in the name of national security, then India is certainly within its ​rights to block Starlink based on its genuine national security concerns", national co-convenor Ashwani Mahajan said ‌in a ⁠statement.
Mahajan added that Starlink's technology could make it difficult for authorities to restrict internet services during security emergencies and ensure Indian internet traffic passes through domestic infrastructure.
SJM has influenced Indian policy in recent years, notably pushing for rules to protect small traders ​from US-owned e-commerce firms ​Amazon and Walmart's ⁠Flipkart.
SpaceX, Starlink's parent company, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Market with more than a billion internet users
Starlink is ​seeking to launch in a country with more than a ​billion internet ⁠subscribers. Alongside Starlink, satellite ventures backed by Reliance Jio and Bharti are awaiting final clearances to begin services.
Musk has repeatedly taunted Ambani on X, questioning why Starlink still lacked ⁠a licence ​despite what he said were years of compliance ​with Indian requirements.
"Is Ambani the real boss of India?" he posted last week, as he accused the rival ​billionaire of stalling Starlink's entry.

title: Hazlewood   s six for secure dominant Australia win
description: South Africa crumble for 206 chasing 421 as Australia take 1 0 series lead
content:
South Africa crumble for 206 chasing 421 as Australia take 1-0 series lead
Josh Hazlewood took six wickets as Australia completed a 214-run win over South Africa on the fifth day of the first Test at Kingsmead on Tuesday.
Fast bowler Hazlewood twice broke promising stands and finished with six for 49.
The hosts, set 421 runs to win, were bowled out for 206, in the first Test series between the teams in South Africa since the 2018 sandpaper scandal.
Opening batsman Aiden Markram defied the bowlers for a minute short of six hours, scoring 75 before he was ninth out, caught behind from an inside edge off Mitchell Starc.
The last four wickets fell for five runs in the space of 16 deliveries against the second new ball.
Markram and Wiaan Mulder (29) were largely untroubled as they batted through the first 110 minutes of the day.
But a double bowling change brought two wickets.
Mulder was caught down the legside by wicketkeeper Alex Carey off Hazlewood for 29 after a 139-minute innings during which he faced 110 balls.
Man of the match Matt Renshaw came on to bowl his off-spinners in the next over and with his first ball dismissed Kyle Verreynne for a single when the South African wicketkeeper played a forcing shot against a wide ball and edged a catch to Steve Smith at slip.
It was the continuation of a dream match for Renshaw, who top-scored in both innings with 190 and 82, then took his first Test wicket when he dismissed South African captain Temba Bavuma on Monday.
It was Smith's fifth catch of a match in which he became the world record-holder for most catches by a fielder in Tests.
Smith was back in action after being off the field at the start of South Africa's innings on Monday following a blow on the head while batting.
Marco Jansen made 35 and added 45 with Markram before Hazlewood bowled him in the fourth over with the second new ball. Three balls later Simon Harmer gloved a sharply lifting ball to Carey.
Australia were in trouble at 124 for six on the first day but dominated the rest of the match after Renshaw steered them to a first innings total of 390.
Former Australia captain Smith, who did not field in Monday's late session after ⁠a blow to the head while batting, returned to action on Tuesday.
"Steve Smith has undergone a series of clinical assessments over the past 24 hours in accordance with Cricket Australia's concussion protocols and has been cleared to take the field this morning," a statement said.

Australia 390 and 314-6 declared v South Africa 284 and 206 (A. Markram 75; J. Hazlewood 6-49)

title: Atal  111   Qais  49   rescue Afghanistan
description: Resolute batting denies Bangladesh victory in one off Abu Dhabi Test
content:
Resolute batting denies Bangladesh victory in one-off Abu Dhabi Test
Sediqullah Atal’s resolute 111 and Qais Ahmad’s valuable 49 not out saved Afghanistan from a certain defeat against Bangladesh as the one-off Test between the two nations ended in a draw at the Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abdu Dhabi on Tuesday.
Chasing a stiff target of 479 Bangladesh’s batsmen demonstrated great patience and reached 346-8 till stumps on the fifth and final day.
Atal, playing his third Test, showed top resistance against Bangladeshi bowlers and completed his well-deserved century. He also became the first Afghanistan’s batsman to score a century in the fourth innings.
Atal struck nine fours and three sixes in his solid knock during which he stayed for 514 minutes at the crease before spinner Taijul Islam removing him in the third session to leave Afghans struggling.at 281-7.
However at this stage Qais shouldered the responsibility and went deep until the end to avert a looming defeat. He hit six fours and three sixes in his 80-ball 49 not out.
He was ably backed by Yamin Ahmadzai (19) as the duo added precious 45 runs for the eighth wicket stand.
Ebadot Hossain and Mehidy Hasan Miraz got three wickets each.
Afghanistan started the fifth and final day’s play with 132-3 with Sediqullah Atal batting on 35 and Shahidullah Shahidi on 19.
However just in the third over Shahidi got retired hurt as he walked off the pitch after the ball thudded into his pads after a throw from the fielder. He was seen in deep pain despite administering first aid by the physiotherapist.
Ikram Alikhil then joined Atal and the duo tried their best to consolidate their position. However Bangladesh’s bowlers were bowling extremely well. Ebadot Hossain provided breakthrough to Bangladesh when he had Ikram, held excellently by Litton Das behind the stumps.
The dismissal also helped Das create world Test record. He became the first player in Test cricket to record nine dismissals behind the stumps while scoring a half-century and a century in the same match. He surpassed the previous record held by South Africa’s Denis Lindsay.
In the Johannesburg Test against Australia in 1966, Lindsay scored 50-plus runs in both innings and recorded eight dismissals. By catching Ikram Alikhil, Litton surpassed Lindsay to set a new record.
Ikram struck five fours in his 36 which came off 69 balls. He added 66 runs with Atal in a well-needed stand.
After the break Bangladesh’s spinner Mehidy Hasan Miraz bowled well, taking two quick wickets of Ismat Aslam (4) and Shahidullah Shahidi (36) to leave Afghanistan reeling at 264-6.
Shahidi, who returned to bat after injury, hammered four fours and two sixes in his 36 for which he faced 69 balls.
Qais and Yamin then did well to end Bangladesh’s winning chances.
Bangladesh had scored 346 and 372-7 declared while Afghans were bowled out for 240 in their first innings
