title: Non functional Khyber Pakhtunkhwa CM Sohail Afridi s brother moves PHC over alleged  illegal  detention
description: Seeks immediate recovery  argues that Afridi s alleged abduction violated his fundamental rights
content:
Seeks immediate recovery, argues that Afridi's alleged abduction violated his fundamental rights
The brother of non-functional Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) chief minister Sohail Afridi on Tuesday moved the Peshawar High Court seeking his immediate recovery, arguing that his alleged abduction and continued detention violated his fundamental rights and demanding an independent judicial inquiry into his disappearance.
The petition was filed amid uncertainty over Afridi’s whereabouts following the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in K-P on October 11, which brought the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf-led provincial government to an end and transferred its powers to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi.
Muhammad Aamir, through his counsel Bashir Khan Wazir, alleged that Afridi had been taken away by armed and masked individuals and was being held illegally. The petition asked the court to establish where the former chief minister was being held, who had custody of him, and under what legal authority he was being detained.
“The petitioner and the family members of the abductee are seriously concerned about his safety, physical integrity and continued liberty,” the petition stated, seeking the court’s intervention “to prevent any further harm”.
The federal government said Afridi and some members of his cabinet had been placed in preventive custody, while Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry clarified that Afridi was being held under protective custody and had not been arrested.
In its petition, Aamir’s counsel argued that Afridi’s public office did not diminish his fundamental rights, stating, “His public office does not diminish his fundamental rights; rather, the circumstances of the present incident call for immediate and effective action by the competent authorities to ascertain his whereabouts and ensure his safety.”
The petitioner asked the court to direct the police authorities to trace Afridi and, if he was found in custody within the court’s territorial jurisdiction, produce him before the court so that the legality of his detention could be examined.
According to the petition, Afridi was detained at the Chief Minister’s House in Peshawar at about 2pm on October 11 before being taken away by “certain unknown armed and masked individuals” in the presence of Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Peshawar.
“The precise sequence of events, the identities of the persons involved and the circumstances in which the abductee was taken away require immediate verification through the relevant official record, eyewitness accounts and other available evidence,” it stated.
“The circumstances in which the abductee was taken away from such a sensitive public institution, despite the reported presence of a senior police officer, raise grave and legitimate concerns regarding the security arrangements, the response of the concerned authorities and the safety and liberty of the abductee,” it said.
The petitioner also expressed concern that Afridi may have been taken to an "undisclosed location" and "may be kept against his will", adding that his whereabouts and present condition needed to be “immediately ascertained through lawful means”.
It called for an investigation into the identities of those allegedly involved, the vehicles used to remove Afridi, if any, and the route taken after he was taken away.
The petition said police authorities could obtain relevant information from security personnel, access-control records, CCTV cameras, official duty rosters and other sources.
Read: 'Afridi, some of his cabinet members have been taken into preventive custody,' confirms Talal
It also sought a detailed report from the CCPO on the circumstances of the alleged incident, the people present at the time, the security arrangements in place and the steps taken immediately afterwards.
An objective inquiry into these matters was necessary, the petitioner said, adding that he did not seek “any finding of culpability against any respondent without due investigation and supporting evidence”.
The petition further asked the court to order the preservation of CCTV footage from the relevant entrances and exits, adjoining roads and routes, along with security logs, entry and exit registers, vehicle access records, duty rosters and official communications.
“Any delay in securing such material may prejudice the investigation and frustrate the process of identifying the persons involved,” it said.
The petitioner also sought an independent judicial inquiry and asked the court to direct the police to register a first information report if one had not already been registered, and the facts legally warranted it.
The petition argued that the alleged detention raised questions about the constitutional protections afforded to Afridi, including the right to be dealt with in accordance with law, the right to life and liberty, safeguards against unlawful arrest and detention, and the protection of human dignity.
It cited Articles 4, 9, 10 and 14 of the Constitution and invoked Article 199, under which the High Court can order the production of a person in custody in circumstances covered by the provision. It also referred to Section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, which provides for directions of the nature of habeas corpus within its scope.
“The impugned detention and disappearance of the abductee is wholly illegal, unlawful, without lawful authority and of no legal effect,” the petition stated, arguing that the authorities had not disclosed any lawful basis for holding him.
Read more: PTI rejects emergency, governor's rule in K-P as unconstitutional, vows to continue struggle
“Its immediate purpose is to ascertain the whereabouts and safety of the abductee, secure his production before this Hon’ble Court if he is found in custody, examine the legality of such custody and ensure that his fundamental rights are protected in accordance with law,” it stated.
The petitioner warned that the matter "cannot safely be left to indefinite delay or uncertainty" and that directions for his production and a prompt report were necessary in the interests of justice.
The court was also asked to direct the authorities to submit periodic progress reports until Afridi’s whereabouts and safety had been established.
In its request for interim relief, the petition sought a preliminary report within a time fixed by the court, the production of Afridi if he was found in the custody or control of any person or authority, and immediate steps for his safe recovery if he was being unlawfully detained.
The petition asked the High Court to direct the authorities to identify those involved and take action against anyone found responsible in accordance with the law, while ensuring due process. It also sought any other relief the court considered appropriate in the circumstances.
The petition followed the federal government’s decision to impose emergency and governor’s rule in K-P on October 11 under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution. The government cited the deteriorating law and order situation and what it called a lack of support from the provincial administration in the fight against terrorism.
Reports of Afridi’s detention emerged shortly after the announcement, with provincial Information Minister Shafi Jan saying the non-functional chief minister had been arrested and urging people to gather in Peshawar. However, there was initially no confirmation from the federal government.
On October 12, the minister of state for Interior confirmed that Afridi and some members of his cabinet had been taken into preventive custody. “Yes, I can confirm that the chief minister and some of his cabinet members have been taken into preventive custody,” he told Reuters , adding that those facing cases would be charged and tried, while the others would be released.
A senior police official also confirmed that eight people, including Afridi, PTI MNA Junaid Akbar, and Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, had been detained

title: Sydney Sweeney   s  The Housemaid  tops HBO Max film charts
description: Sydney Sweeney   s  The Housemaid  reached number one on HBO Max   s US film charts after arriving to platform October 9
content:
Sydney Sweeney’s 'The Housemaid' reached number one on HBO Max’s US film charts after arriving to platform October 9
Sydney Sweeney’s psychological thriller The Housemaid has become the most-watched film on HBO Max in the United States, reaching the top of the platform’s movie charts just days after its streaming debut.
Based on Freida McFadden’s 2022 novel, the film arrived on HBO Max on October 9 2026, following its earlier streaming release on Starz in April.
According to viewership tracker FlixPatrol , it reached number one on the US film charts on October 11 and remained in the top position the following day.
Directed by Paul Feig and written by Rebecca Sonnenshine, The Housemaid stars Sweeney as Millie Calloway, a formerly incarcerated woman who takes a live-in housekeeping job with Nina Winchester, played by Amanda Seyfried. Brandon Sklenar plays Nina’s husband, Andrew, as tensions escalate within the household.
Released in cinemas in December 2025, the thriller reportedly earned $400.5 million worldwide against a production budget of $35 million. Its box office performance led Lionsgate to approve a sequel, while its latest streaming success has renewed attention on the franchise.
On HBO Max, The Housemaid overtook Backrooms , directed by Kane Parsons, and Evil Dead Burn, which debuted on the service on October 2.
The film’s continued popularity comes as audiences await the next instalment, currently scheduled for December 2027.
The sequel is expected to draw from McFadden’s follow-up novel, The Housemaid’s Secret, in which Millie works for a different family.

title: Haunted Chocolatier will feature more action than Stardew Valley  creator says
description: ConcernedApe has shared new details about Haunted Chocolatier  describing it as more action focused RPG
content:
ConcernedApe has shared new details about Haunted Chocolatier, describing it as more action-focused RPG
Eric Barone, the creator of Stardew Valley, has shared new details about his upcoming game, Haunted Chocolatier, revealing that it will feature more action and role-playing elements than his previous hit.
In an interview with GQ , Barone described the project as a town-based game with a stronger focus on combat, exploration and character progression.
"It is still what I call a town game, but it’s more of an action RPG," Barone said.
He explained that players can expect to explore locations, collect equipment and become more powerful while facing monsters and bosses.
"The main focus is more about adventuring, finding equipment and getting more powerful. There are monsters, there are boss fights. It's for the people in Stardew Valley that go into the mines. That's what I do, honestly," he added.
While Stardew Valley combines farming, relationships and life simulation with combat in areas such as the mines, Haunted Chocolatier will place greater emphasis on action.
Players will also run a chocolate business and build relationships with the residents of the game’s town.
Barone first announced Haunted Chocolatier in 2021 and has continued developing it largely on his own. The game still has no confirmed release date, and the developer has not yet allowed anyone else to play it.
Earlier this year, Barone acknowledged that he might have announced the project too soon. In an August blog post, he apologised for the lengthy development process but said he did not want to rush the game and risk compromising its quality.
In his latest interview, Barone explained why he was keeping the unfinished project private.
"No one's playing the game until I'm ready to show it," he said. "If you have a turkey in the oven. You're not going to pull it out halfway and have the guests taste it, right? It needs to be done."

title: BBC announces two part J K  Rowling docuseries ahead of new    Harry Potter    television adaptation
description: Rowling will not take part in the project  which will draw on archival material and interviews
content:
Rowling will not take part in the project, which will draw on archival material and interviews
The BBC is developing a two part docuseries about Harry Potter author J.K. Rowling, examining her rise to international fame, cultural influence and increasingly divisive public profile.
Produced by Rogan Scotland, whose credits include Becoming Frida Kahlo , the series will explore Rowling’s life against three decades of social, political and technological change. According to the announcement, it will consider how she became one of Britain’s most polarising public figures.
Rowling rose to prominence after publishing the first Harry Potter book in 1997. The seven book series became a global success, expanding into films, video games, theme parks, television projects and a substantial merchandising business.
The documentary will also examine the controversy surrounding Rowling’s views on transgender rights. Supporters have praised her as a defender of women’s rights, while critics have accused her of opposing transgender equality. Her positions have contributed to divisions between the author and some actors and fans associated with the Harry Potter franchise.
Rowling will not participate in the documentary. Instead, the production will draw on archival material, her writing and interviews with people who have worked with her.
Simon Young, the BBC’s head of commissioning for history, said the 30th anniversary of the first Harry Potter book made this an appropriate moment to examine Rowling’s influence. He highlighted the significance of the fictional character, the publishing and filmmaking phenomenon surrounding the franchise, and the author’s polarising public reputation.
Provisionally titled J.K. Rowling , the series is scheduled to air on BBC Two and BBC Scotland, as well as on the BBC iPlayer streaming service. BBC Studios will handle international distribution.
The announcement arrives ahead of HBO’s planned television adaptation of Harry Potter . The new series is intended to revisit Rowling’s books in a different format, bringing the franchise to another generation of viewers.
The BBC has not provided a specific broadcast date for the documentary in the announcement. Its two episodes are expected to offer a retrospective on Rowling’s literary achievements and the public debates that have shaped her reputation.

title: Raye   s Royal Albert Hall concert ticketing overwhelmed by AI bots with 1 8 million entries for 5000 seats
description: She said that the scale of the activity had prompted her team to reconsider its approach to ticketing
content:
She said that the scale of the activity had prompted her team to reconsider its approach to ticketing
Raye’s upcoming Royal Albert Hall concert has encountered ticketing difficulties after 1.8 million entries were submitted for just 5,000 available seats, with the singer’s team blaming scalpers using AI bots to create fake registrations.
The concert, titled ‘This Symphony May Contain Hope’, is scheduled for October 23, 2026 and will feature an orchestral reworking of her album This Music May Contain Hope.
The ticket sign-up process was reportedly overwhelmed by hundreds of thousands of registrations believed to have been generated by automated systems.
“It is a new world we are living in now,” Raye wrote. “I have never witnessed bots on this scale.”
Rather than proceed with a conventional presale, which could have been exploited by ticket resellers, Raye’s team manually reviewed the registrations to identify genuine fans.
Selected applicants are due to receive presale links and codes by email on Tuesday at 11:45am BST, with sales opening at midday.
Fans who do not receive a code will have another opportunity during the general sale, subject to remaining availability.
“It is so important to me that fans can buy tickets at the face value price,” Raye said. She added that the scale of the activity had “really opened my eyes” and prompted her team to reconsider its approach to ticketing.
“I’m not sure what the future holds for ticketing,” she wrote, signing off, “Lots of love, Raye.”
The demand reflects the appeal of the singer’s orchestral performances.
Raye has previously presented the symphonic format twice at the same venue, with an earlier performance leading to a Grammy-nominated broadcast on BBC and PBS.

title: World Cup ticket demand soars past 15 million
description: Fans from 142 countries fuel unprecedented global interest
content:
Fans from 142 countries fuel unprecedented global interest
The ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup 2027 ticket applications have seen a surge of demand across the globe since the ballot went live 12 days ago.
The ICC said on Tuesday that a total of 15,083,752 ticket applications have been received since with 4,423,417 ballot registrations generated by fans from across 142 countries, highlighting the immense global interest in the 14th edition of the Men’s Cricket World Cup.
The latest numbers show a dramatic acceleration in demand since the ballot opened, with ticket applications soaring from one million last week to over 15 million in less than two weeks.
The global interest in the tournament, which has been introduced with a new format, will see cricket fans become part of the biggest and most ambitious edition in the tournament’s history, hosted in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia.
"The overwhelming demand for tickets is testament to the stature and appeal of the Cricket World Cup, the allure of Africa as a destination and the anticipation for the event generated by the ICC and its partners' promotional activities leading up to the event launch,” ICC Chief Executive Officer Sanjog Gupta said.
“With a year to go, the ICC has planned an exciting runway of 360 degree activations, multi-platform campaigns and content line-ups, which will elevate the fandom associated with the ICC Cricket World Cup 2027."
The ticket ballot will be open for registration until November 21, 2026, exactly a year before the Cricket World Cup final is scheduled to be played in Wanderers, Johannesburg.
The ODI World Cup will be held across three countries including South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia from October 2 to November 21, 2027.

title: Five members of a family found dead inside home in Karachi s Malir
description: Police recover handwritten note citing financial distress and alleged harassment by close relatives as cause
content:
Police recover handwritten note citing financial distress, alleged harassment by close relatives as cause
The bodies of five members of a family, including two children, were found inside a house in Falak Naz Society in Karachi's Malir on Tuesday, with a handwritten note recovered from one of the deceased pointing to financial hardship and alleged harassment by relatives.
The dead were identified as 30-year-old Shehryar, his 28-year-old wife, Saba, their children, five-year-old Aizal and three-year-old Arya, and Shehryar's 20-year-old younger sister Shumaila, who lived with her brother.
Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Malir Dr Abdul Khaliq Pirzada told The Express Tribune that the house was locked from the inside. When police broke open the door, they found Shehryar and Saba seated on chairs, both with gunshot wounds to the head. A pistol was found nearby.
"The bodies of Shumaila and the two children were found on bedding on the floor in the same room. The three appeared to be asleep, but foam was coming from their mouths," SSP Pirzada said.
A handwritten note was recovered from Shehryar’s pocket in which he purportedly admitted to taking his own life and those of his family members. The note, which was stained red with what appeared to be blood, attributed the family’s circumstances to financial hardship and alleged indifference and harassment by close relatives.
According to the initial investigation, police suspected that Shehryar and his wife had administered poison to the children and Shumaila before shooting themselves. The exact cause of death of all five would be established through post-mortem examinations, Pirzada said.
In the note, Shehryar alleged that relatives had harassed the family and accused them of killing his father, who had died in a traffic accident some time earlier.
Read: Mother, three children brutally murdered
“The reason we are taking this step is that our relatives started harassing us. They say that we killed our father,” the note read.
Shehryar also wrote of their financial distress; “We would ask our relatives to give us money, but they humiliated us. Our maternal aunts and paternal uncles blocked us so that we would not ask them for money,” the note said.
He said they had sought help to buy groceries, milk for the children, and refill their gas cylinder, but had been left without assistance.
“If we went to visit them, they would throw us out of their homes. They had promised our elders that they would look after us, but they abandoned us. The situation has become unbearable,” the note read.
Shehryar also called for those he blamed for the family’s circumstances to be held accountable. “My last wish is that those who treated us this way should be made an example of. But we have no hope in the law,” the note said. “They are all shameless people who only come to funerals to eat biryani. Nobody helps anyone.”
Police forensic teams collected evidence and fingerprints from the scene. SSP Pirzada said investigators were looking for samples of Shehryar’s previous handwriting to compare with the note and establish its authenticity.
Police also recovered a white powder from the house. Investigators suspected it could be a form of poison that had allegedly been administered to Shumaila and the children. The substance was taken into custody for laboratory testing.
Read more: Karachi police arrests 3 suspects over young doctor's murder during Teen Talwar robbery
Malir Investigation Police said a relative had arranged for groceries to be delivered to Shehryar’s house a day before the incident. Police also said Shehryar had reportedly been suffering from severe depression because of financial difficulties, a claim they said was supported by some neighbourhood residents.
The bodies were taken to the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre for post-mortem examinations. Police were investigating both the murder and suicide angles to establish the circumstances surrounding the five deaths.
Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar took notice of the recovery of five bodies and directed the SSP Malir to provide complete details of the incident. He ordered a thorough investigation into all aspects of the case, calling for every possible measure to establish the facts and determine the motives behind the incident.
Lanjar also directed police to use all available resources in the investigation, identify those responsible, and ensure action in accordance with the law. He also asked to be kept informed of the investigation and its progress.

title: Oil falls as Russian diesel supply prospects counter Gulf supply risks
description: Brent dropped  1 18  or 1 1   to  105 47 a barrel by 1125 PKT  US WTI down  1 17  or 1 3   at  92 57 a barrel
content:
Brent dropped $1.18, or 1.1%, to $105.47 a barrel by 1125 PKT; US WTI down $1.17, or 1.3%, at $92.57 a barrel
Oil prices fell on Tuesday and were on track for their first ‌decline in nearly a week, as traders assessed supply risks from attacks on Saudi Arabia while weighing the prospect of additional diesel supplies from Russia.
Brent crude futures dropped $1.18, or 1.1%, to $105.47 a barrel by 0625 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude ​futures were down $1.17, or 1.3%, at $92.57 a barrel.
Both benchmarks climbed nearly $2 a barrel in the previous ​session, with Brent settling at its highest since September 15.
US President Donald Trump said Russia ⁠had agreed to supply diesel to global markets, and his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel ​designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its war on Ukraine.
Additional supplies could help alleviate tightness in global fuel markets, ​tempering some of the supply concerns that have supported crude prices recently.
However, "there is considerable scepticism over the Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire, particularly with reports that Russia has hit Ukrainian energy targets since Trump announced it," ING analysts said in a note.
Read: LNG imports to cost over $1b in winter
Lawmakers from both ​parties in the US complained that Trump's agreement with Putin appears to violate US law barring imports of Russian energy ​until Moscow ends its aggression against Ukraine.
Concerns over the vulnerability of Gulf energy infrastructure and shipping lanes remained in focus ‌after Iran-aligned ⁠Houthis struck Riyadh's international airport over the weekend, while tanker attacks were reported near the Strait of Hormuz.
The incidents threatened to derail a recovery in Middle East supplies seen in September, and have reinforced fears of further disruptions along one of the world's most important energy transit routes.
"Fresh diesel supply from Russia and steadier Saudi flows are offering ​some relief, yet the market ​still looks more worried ⁠about the risk of further hits to ships or pipelines in the Gulf than it is reassured by extra barrels," said Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM ​Trade.
"Until we see clearer signs of de-escalation, the path of least resistance still leans ​higher," he ⁠said.

Ministers of OPEC and non-OPEC Participating Countries in the Declaration of Cooperation said shipping and insurance costs have surged to unprecedented levels of over one-third of the commodity value, impeding efficient movement of crude oil and products.
OPEC has revised down its ⁠oil ​demand growth forecast for this year to 400,000 barrels per day ​from 1.4 million bpd at the start of the year, in line with developments throughout the year, Haitham Al Ghais, Secretary General of ​the organisation, said on Monday.

title: 47 Palestinian families face forced displacement amid Israeli blockade
description: Four families flee as armed Israeli occupiers storm their homes  threaten them with death  says Palestinian commission
content:
Four families flee as armed Israeli occupiers storm their homes, threaten them with death, says Palestinian commission
47 Palestinian families face forced displacement from a village in the northern occupied West Bank , where four families have already fled following threats by armed Israeli occupiers , a Palestinian body said Monday.
The Palestinian Colonisation and Wall Resistance Commission said armed occupiers stormed homes in Khirbet Ras al-Ahmar, southeast of Tubas, and threatened residents with death, forcing four families to leave.
The village has been under an Israeli blockade for nearly a month, with access roads closed and restrictions on water and livestock feed supplies, threatening residents' livelihoods, the commission said.
Read: Israeli army fire kills 5 more Palestinians in Gaza, death toll nears 74,400
Restrictions intensified in mid-September when Israeli forces dug a trench across the village's last remaining access road, forcing residents to collect water at night and travel before dawn to avoid detention. The commission also reported that Israeli authorities demolished six water wells, confiscated pumps and repeatedly cut water lines serving the village.
On October 10, Israeli occupiers gave the 47 families until the following evening to leave their homes.
Read More: US Senate blocks measure demanding report on rights violations in West Bank
The commission warned that continued restrictions could force more families to flee and pave the way for the seizure of their land. It cited similar incidents elsewhere in the occupied West Bank, including Jalud near Nablus, where a Palestinian family was forced from its home after months of attacks, and Wadi al-Rakhim near Hebron, where a family of 10 was confined to its home by Israeli restrictions.
The commission called for the reopening of access roads, the restoration of essential supplies and the protection of residents from further attacks.
Since October 2023, the commission has documented 14,742 attacks across 376 Palestinian villages and communities in the occupied West Bank, saying Israeli occupiers have killed 67 Palestinians during that period.

title: Kacey Musgraves blasts Kristi Noem with brutal dig over criticism of singer s association with James Talarico
description: The dispute began after Talarico shared a photograph with Musgraves online  thanking her for having him at the show
content:
The dispute began after Talarico shared a photograph with Musgraves online, thanking her for having him at the show
Kacey Musgraves has responded to Kristi Noem after the former US Homeland Security secretary criticised the country singer for welcoming Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico at her concert in Texas.
The dispute began after Talarico shared a photograph with Musgraves on social media, thanking her for having him at the show.

title: PSX slips 348 points on profit taking
description: Early rally fades despite Brent crude trading below  105 a barrel
content:
Early rally fades despite Brent crude trading below $105 a barrel
An early buying rally failed to hold at the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) on Tuesday as cautious investors shifted to profit-taking, pulling the benchmark KSE-100 Index into the red after it traded higher in the morning amid buying across key sectors.
The index touched an intraday high of 166,070.48 before falling to a low of 164,773.67, eventually settling at 164,776.44, down 347.97 points, or 0.21%.
The market had opened on a positive note, with the KSE-100 Index rising 558.25 points, or 0.34%, to 165,682.66 in early trading. By midday, it was up 470.14 points, or 0.28%, at 165,594.55.
Buying interest during the session was observed in automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, oil and gas exploration companies, and oil marketing companies. However, the initial momentum faded as investors turned cautious and booked profits, wiping out the index's early gains.
According to KTrade Securities, the KSE-100 opened on a positive note as Brent crude traded below $105 a barrel, lifting early sentiment and pushing the index over 700 points into the green. However, as the session progressed, profit-taking across the board erased gains despite oil prices hovering near $105 a barrel. Consequently, the index closed at 164,776, down 348 points (-0.21%) day-on-day.
Selling pressure was concentrated in commercial banks, technology, and oil and gas stocks, with United Bank Limited (UBL), Habib Bank Limited (HBL), Lucky Cement and Mari Energies weighing on the index. Fertilisers were the only sector to offer some support.
Going forward, KTrade noted that cautious trading was likely to persist as buyers remained selective, accumulating on dips rather than aggressively chasing prices. A sustained recovery would depend on improved participation and developments on the geopolitical front, particularly their implications for global oil prices and domestic investor sentiment, it added.
Overall, trading volume increased to 383.7 million shares versus Monday's total of 362.9 million. The value of traded shares stood at Rs13.1 billion.
LSE Financial Services was the volume leader with trading in 32.3 million shares, losing Rs0.16 to close at Rs1.03.

title: Meta challenges UK media regulator over fees  fines
description: Companies that breach safety rules can face fines of up to 10  of qualifying worldwide revenue or  23 7 million
content:
Companies that breach safety rules can face fines of up to 10% of qualifying worldwide revenue or $23.7 million
A UK High Court will hold a hearing Tuesday on a challenge brought by Meta, the tech giant that owns Facebook and Instagram, over fees and potential fines introduced under the country's Online Safety Act.
Meta is challenging Ofcom in the High Court, claiming that the UK media regulator acted unlawfully, specifically regarding their definition of "qualifying worldwide revenue," which is introduced under the act.
The law, which came into force last year, introduced protections against harmful online content, with Ofcom's operating costs for carrying out its online safety work funded by tech firms.
Under regulations introduced in September 2025, the fees are based on a company's qualifying worldwide revenue and apply to firms earning more than £250 million a year.
Meta explicitly argues that Ofcom's calculation methods are disproportionate and unlawful, while Ofcom said it would "robustly defend" its position.
Read: Microsoft president says milk faces more regulation than AI
The BBC reported in May that lawyers acting for Meta argued that the regulations should be reconsidered by the regulator.
Monica Carss-Frisk KC, for the tech giant, has said in court documents that Ofcom's approach is "troubling" and leads to "a handful of companies such as Meta bearing the vast majority of Ofcom's costs, despite the act making clear that it is concerned with a wide range of internet services offered in the UK.”
Under the Online Safety Act, firms found to have breached safety rules can face fines of up to 10% of qualifying worldwide revenue or £18 million ($23.7 million), whichever is greater.
Meanwhile, a senior director at the regulator told a committee in the House of Lords earlier this year that Ofcom was "operating in a highly litigious environment," including facing two actions by Meta and others from "a raft of services" bringing judicial reviews against the body for trying to collect data.
"We absolutely are looking to drive change in the best way we can," Oliver Griffiths, the Ofcom group director for online safety, told peers hearing evidence about the Online Safety Act.

title: Govt has  credible evidence  that PTI was in touch with TTP  says information minister
description: Alleges provincial govt has shown sympathy towards terrorist groups  and will provide evidence  very soon
content:
Alleges provincial govt has shown sympathy towards terrorist groups, and will provide evidence 'very soon'
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Tuesday claimed the federal government had “credible evidence” that Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) had been in contact with the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), saying the government would present details of the alleged links at a later stage.
"The government has credible evidence that PTI was in touch with the TTP. And very soon, we will be giving you evidence about the links that we have been able to uncover between the PTI and the TTP,” said Tarar while addressing a press briefing for foreign correspondents alongside Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar.
Tarar alleged that the provincial government had shown sympathy towards terrorist groups and had failed to provide adequate support to security personnel fighting them.
“How could a government, which is mandated to protect the lives of people and to maintain law and order in a province, be hand in glove with terrorists to promote terrorist activities?” he asked.
The information minister also accused the PTI leadership of promoting a narrative that undermined law enforcement agencies, saying it had the effect of empowering terrorist groups.
He paid tribute to members of the armed forces, police and other law enforcement agencies killed in the fight against terrorism, saying they had made sacrifices despite what he alleged was insufficient support from the provincial government.
Federal Law Minister Azam Nazir Tarar and Federal Information Minister Attaullah Tarar brief foreign media representatives. https://t.co/rvPz6z16ON
Tarar said the government had also observed a sharp rise in attacks targeting police personnel and installations.
He cited figures indicating that 3,774 terrorist incidents had been recorded in 2025 and 2,857 up to September 2026. He also said fatalities had increased from 267 in 2021 to 3,512 in 2025, while the figure for 2026 had reached 2,775 at the time of the briefing.
He further claimed that attacks targeting police had risen by 168 per cent and that 18 police installations had been targeted over the preceding two years. The information minister said the government believed the change in administration would help improve security and strengthen counter-terrorism operations.
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, meanwhile, accused the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led provincial government of failing to tackle terrorism, alleging that its policies had enabled terrorist groups to operate and that there was a disconnect between the provincial administration and federal counter-terrorism efforts.
He also alleged that there was evidence linking PTI with the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), saying the government would present the evidence at a later stage.
The information minister said the federal government’s negotiations with PTI and the K-P government had focused on counter-terrorism rather than political demands.
“We had only one agenda. There was no political agenda,” he said, adding that the provincial government could have continued with its political activities while discussions on security measures proceeded.
“The federal government only wanted that there should be one unified policy with regard to counter-terrorism,” he said.
Tarar argued that "one country cannot have two foreign policies." The minister explained that while the state was making efforts to persuade Afghanistan’s interim government to prevent its territory from being used for attacks inside Pakistan, K-P's government had adopted a different approach towards the Afghan administration and counter-terrorism.
“How can one country have two policies with regard to counter-terrorism?” he asked.
The information minister said the federal government had tried to reach an agreement with the provincial authorities, but the chief minister had rejected it.
He alleged that the provincial administration had failed to support a coordinated counter-terrorism policy and had not taken sufficient measures to strengthen the police and security infrastructure.
“There was a complete breakdown of governance. There was a complete breakdown of law and order in the province,” he said.
Attaullah Tarar questioned how the provincial government had spent the resources it had received through the National Finance Commission, claiming it had been allocated almost Rs800 billion.
“Why was it not spent on creating a new CTD force, a counter-terrorism department?” he asked, referring also to the installation of Safe City cameras, the establishment of forensic laboratories, police equipment and programmes to counter violent extremism.
He said he had visited Kohat following a terrorist incident, met injured people in hospital and visited the homes of those killed. “The on-ground sentiment in K-P, the people want eradication of terrorism by all means,” he said.
The information minister said the people affected by violence wanted to be free of terrorism because it was damaging their lives and livelihoods. “If you look at the governance, there are no education reforms. There are no health reforms. There is no public service delivery,” he said.
Tarar alleged that terrorist groups had been facilitated by a network involving political interests and illegal economic activity, including cross-border smuggling in the mines and minerals, timber, tobacco, gold and precious stones sectors.
Read more: State determined to rid K-P of terrorists, says Kundi at first advisory council meeting after governor's rule
He further alleged that the provincial government had failed to prevent the registration of vehicles and motorcycles, which he said hindered efforts to track their use.
The information minister also accused the provincial government of failing to consistently participate in Apex Committee meetings intended to coordinate counter-terrorism efforts.
The ministers also outlined the proposed administrative structure for the 12 conflict-affected districts under the Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC).
Tarar said the new arrangement would include a chairman, vice-chairman, council members and spokespersons, alongside an additional chief secretary and other senior officials.
He identified Yahya Akhunzada as the administrator and said the structure would include officials responsible for policing, law enforcement, narcotics control, legal affairs, tribal affairs, human rights, budgeting and revenue.
He said the council would maintain regional and tribal balance to ensure that local communities were represented in decisions concerning security and development.
“This new setup has come with new hope and has come with a renewed assurance that first and foremost law and order will be maintained,” he said. “And as a result, development will take place in K-P. And the people of K-P will be able to lead a life of prosperity, which they truly deserve,” he added.
Tarar said the federal government expected the new administration to take a more coordinated approach to counter-terrorism. He also said the government would pursue the alleged links between PTI and the TTP through the relevant process, reiterating that further evidence would be presented.
The law minister said the decision had been taken after consultations, negotiations with the provincial authorities and a review of reports on the deteriorating security situation.
“The Prime Minister thought it appropriate to bring these matters before the federal cabinet,” Azam said, adding that the decision had been taken by consensus, "without any dissent," in order "to save the people living" in K-P.
The law minister said the federal government had initially pursued negotiations with the provincial authorities to establish a coordinated counter-terrorism policy but had failed to secure the desired outcome.
Explaining the legal basis for the decision, Azam said the Constitution provided for federal intervention when internal disturbances became so serious that a provincial government could no longer maintain law and order.
“Pakistan is a federation. So there is a division of powers,” he said, adding that the federal and provincial governments enjoyed constitutional and legal autonomy within their respective domains.
Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar says protective custody provisions are enshrined in the Constitution and that an emergency under Article 232 applies to the entire province. He adds that the National Finance Commission allocated 1% of gross revenues to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa for… pic.twitter.com/UPRNCHawN3
However, he said counter-terrorism efforts required coordination between federal and provincial agencies.
“Whenever internal disturbances go to a certain extent, both the state government and the federal government, they work in harmony. And they work together because it is for the state, it is for the country,” he said.
The law minister said Article 232 of the Constitution dealt with emergency provisions in circumstances where internal disturbances reached a level that a provincial government could not control.
He also referred to Article 234, which provides for the exercise of presidential powers in the event of a failure of constitutional machinery in a province.
“Now, what has happened with the proclamation issued by the president under Article 232 and 234 of the Constitution?” he asked, explaining that the proclamation authorised the federal government to assume responsibility for running provincial affairs or delegate some of those responsibilities to the governor.
“Within the constitutional scheme, the provincial government ceases to hold the office, the chief minister and the ministers and other office bearers, as mentioned in the proclamation,” he said.
Azam said the federal government had exercised these powers after "thorough deliberations" in the cabinet and while examining "all possible avenues and materials."
He added that the measure was not unprecedented, saying constitutional provisions of this nature had been invoked on nine or 10 occasions by elected governments in the past.
The law minister said the proclamation would have to undergo the approval process stipulated in the Constitution, including consideration by both houses of parliament and, in the case of Article 234, placement before a joint sitting.
Responding to a question about the duration of governor’s rule, he said the Constitution provided a maximum period of six months under Article 234. “We should not speculate that nobody knows the exact time,” he said, adding that the government hoped the situation would improve through efforts from Islamabad.
He said Articles 232 and 234 had been invoked together because the government believed the conditions for both provisions existed simultaneously.
Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar says Islamabad will take steps to improve the security situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where casualties continued to rise daily, adding that the PTI-led provincial government had failed to take serious counterterrorism measures. #AzamNazeerTarar … pic.twitter.com/cAuHmitWgP
“There was totally a breakdown of the constitutional machinery. And on the other hand, the internal disturbance was of such a nature that it was beyond the control of the provincial authorities,” he said.
The law minister said the government’s decision had followed a sharp increase in terrorist incidents in K-P. For comparative analysis, he said the government had divided the previous six years into two periods.
“During 2021-2024, in those years, the total recorded terrorist-related incidents in K-P province remained approximately 2,900,” he said. “In 2024-26, this number rose to approximately 8,600. So there is exactly 195 per cent rise,” he added.
Azam said provincial police were under attack, the armed forces deployed there were under attack, and the province had also encountered a surge in attacks against customs officials and religious scholars.
“Innocent persons lost their lives and got severe injuries during these incidents,” he said.
He cited the killing of nine customs officials in a suicide attack, alongside attacks on security forces and civilians, as examples of the deteriorating situation.
“In such graver conditions, if your priorities are to mobilise people for political gains, and your priorities are not to curb the terrorism or to fight against it in a coordinated manner alongside the federal agencies, it’s simply unfortunate,” he said.
The law minister said the federal interior minister and other stakeholders had remained in contact with provincial authorities but had not received the response required to establish an effective joint strategy.
He said the federal government had explored negotiations and political engagement before deciding to invoke the constitutional provisions. “Everything was discussed, and most of the issues were resolved,” he said, adding that the talks ultimately failed to produce a positive outcome.
Read more: PM forms 11-member panel to monitor K-P
Azam alleged that political considerations had taken precedence over national interests in the provincial government’s response. “Maybe their politics was more dear to them compared to the national interest,” he said.
“Providing a peaceful, congenial environment in the provinces should be the top priority of the government,” he said.
Asked why emergency provisions had been invoked in K-P but not in Balochistan, Azam said the federal government had assessed the two provinces differently on the basis of their respective governments’ responses to terrorism.
He said the Balochistan chief minister had been actively engaging with security agencies, visiting areas affected by attacks, supporting rehabilitation work and meeting injured people and bereaved families.
“Your actions speak louder than your words,” he said, arguing that the Balochistan government had demonstrated its resolve to fight terrorism.
The law minister contrasted that approach with what he described as the K-P government’s failure to respond adequately to attacks and support security personnel.
On the question of whether the new arrangement would succeed in eliminating terrorism, Azam said the government was hopeful that the situation would improve, while acknowledging that the precise duration of governor’s rule could not be predicted.
The ministers maintained that the measures had been taken under the Constitution and were intended to restore law and order, improve security coordination and protect residents of K-P.

title: Explainer  What are the ARDC and ADS  and what are their roles and objectives
description: Yahya Akhunzada appointed first administrator of council as federal govt to supervise body representing locals
content:
Yahya Akhunzada appointed first administrator of council as federal govt to supervise body representing locals
The Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC) was set up with the primary purpose of representing the people of the 12 troubled districts, identifying local issues and addressing development needs under the supervision of the federal government, while an Area Development Secretariat (ADS) was also established to run the council.
Bureaucrat Yahya Akhunzada was appointed as the first administrator of the council. The administrator will be an empowered decision-maker, entrusted with full operational and administrative powers to maintain peace in the troubled areas, run development projects and take timely decisions so that peace, security, terrorism and administrative matters can be handled effectively, on time, and in consultation with the council.
Following the imposition of emergency measures and governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) after the federal cabinet approved the recommendation and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif advised President Asif Ali Zardari to invoke Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, Zardari signed the summary, transferring executive authority from the provincial government to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi.
Read: Governor's rule imposed in K-P for fourth time
The federal government then formed an 11-member advisory council to oversee administrative affairs in the province, ordering the immediate establishment of the ADS in the 12 designated districts which include Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Lakki Marwat, Bannu, Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, North Waziristan, Upper South Waziristan, and Lower South Waziristan.
The government also notified that the ADS would operate under the supervision of the ARDC.
Under the supervision of the federal government, and together with the provincial government, the secretariat will make decisions on security, peace, development and administrative matters in the 12 districts, together with the security forces and law enforcement agencies, and in full consultation with the ARDC.
Council members will be nominated on the basis of the population of the relevant areas and districts, along with the tribal representation of the relevant areas and districts. The process is moving ahead rapidly and will be completed in the next few days, after which the federal government will issue an official notification of the appointments. Council members will be appointed for the duration of the imposition of the emergency or for a period determined by the federal government.
The council will elect a chairman and a vice chairman from among its members, who will ensure its leadership, coordination and effective communication. It will meet every 15 days, while the ARDC can summon a meeting at any time if required. Council members will also be part of the District Coordination Committees of the relevant districts, in order to improve communication and harmony between local representatives and administrative institutions.
Further, based on local needs and public demands, the council will identify the projects required for socio-economic development in the 12 designated districts and will submit recommendations to the federal government through the ARDC. Development project priorities will be determined keeping in view local needs, public issues and ground realities, so that resources may be used more effectively.

The council will also review the local law and order situation and propose practicable measures for its improvement, presenting its recommendations regarding the cooperation and facilitation required by law enforcement agencies to eliminate terrorism and prevent illegal activities. The council's role is to increase cooperation among the relevant institutions, address local issues in a timely manner and assist in making security-related measures effective. It will also give recommendations to improve governance, public safety, development activities and the provision of basic public services.
An important aspect of the arrangement is that representatives of the relevant areas will be directly involved in resolving local issues, determining development priorities and identifying public needs. Through the council, the link between public needs and administrative decisions will be strengthened, helping identify issues at the local level, as well ad aiding institutional coordination and improving public services.
The purpose of the ARDC is to make local representation effective, identify development projects according to public needs, provide support for improving law and order, and ensure better governance and the provision of public services.

title: Flick targets win as Barcelona face Galatasaray test
description: The Catalans head to Istanbul without Raphinha
content:
The Catalans head to Istanbul without Raphinha
Barcelona coach Hansi Flick said he would be happy with a single goal victory at Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday as his team face one of the world's 'best atmospheres'.
The Catalan giants have won all nine games they have played this season across all competitions, scoring 39 goals, more than four a game on average.
However the visit to face Turkish champions Galatasaray in Istanbul is the first in a string of tougher fixtures for Barcelona, with Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid also coming up.
The Spanish champions thrashed Feyenoord 5-1 in their league phase opener but will be without Raphinha for the visit to Turkey and one of the game's most intimidating environments.
"First of all, we have to be ready for this atmosphere," Flick told reporters Monday.
"I think this is one of the best atmospheres ever in the world. It's amazing when I hear some situations or the sounds of the stadium, what the fans are doing, it's unbelievable.
"They support their team. You also can see the results against big teams, they are playing like a big team against them, they've improved a lot."
Not since Barcelona's 2-0 win over Athletic Bilbao in La Liga on August 27 have the Catalans been restricted to fewer than three goals.
However Flick said just one would do at Galatasaray's hostile Rams Park stadium, which has sometimes been nicknamed "Hell".
"The only thing we want is to win, this is our goal, this is what we want," said Flick.
"I'm also happy if we win just 1-0, because to see this team, how they play, how they play out (from the back), they like to play football.
"In attack they have fantastic players, so it's not easy to play against Galatasaray, especially at home."

title: Saudi warning system stayed silent before deadly airport attacks
description: Absence during the airport strikes raised questions about Saudi Arabia s vulnerability to    attack
content:
Absence during the airport strikes raised questions about Saudi Arabia's vulnerability to ‌attack
Saudi Arabia stopped issuing public warnings of imminent military attacks days before a series of deadly strikes on Riyadh airport that killed at least 18 people and wounded more than 300.
The government has not said why there were no alerts to the public before the four Riyadh attacks in the past week.
The warnings had served to highlight ​the violence undermining the kingdom's efforts to project an image of calm to its people and the world during its war with Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis.
Their absence during the airport strikes raised questions about Saudi Arabia's vulnerability to ‌attack, and about its ability to protect residents and visitors, four Western and Arab officials in the region and political analysts told Reuters.
It also reflected efforts to maintain a sense of normalcy, they said.
"They (the Saudi government) want to have it both ways: to launch a military operation and at the same time try to give confidence to the population and external stakeholders," said Sultan Alamer, a US-based Saudi academic and Senior Resident Fellow at the Middle East Policy Council think tank.
The Saudi civil defence - a national emergency management, rescue and firefighting agency which operates under the interior ministry and issues early warning alerts - and the Saudi ​government media office did not respond to emailed questions on why no alerts were issued.
Read: Saudi Arabia rejects Israeli bid to join fight against Houthis: Israeli media
Saudi Arabia's approach is also one that some regional analysts said risked backfiring because the absence of warnings has heightened uncertainty in the kingdom.
On Monday, Saudi ​Arabia's civil defence authority issued its first alerts since September 29, warning of potential threats in Riyadh and southern cities.
Reuters was unable to ascertain whether the decision to issue alerts again was a response ⁠to the airport attacks, and the Saudi government did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the matter.
All Gulf countries have been hit by Iranian drones and missiles since the US-Iran war began in February, but their governments have handled public ​warnings differently.
Qatar's interior ministry has issued mobile phone alerts before nearly every attack, including the most recent attacks in July, when residents were warned to stay inside and away from windows.
Bahrain and Kuwait have repeatedly sounded sirens urging people to take shelter.
Saudi Arabia began issuing threat alerts ​to mobile phones and social media accounts via a national early warning system in May. But despite increasing Houthi attacks leading up to last week, the system went silent.
The last alert before last week's attacks was issued on September 29, for the southern province of Najran, according to posts on the civil defence X account.
The civil defence authority has continued to issue warnings about staying out of harm's way during adverse weather, including rain and flooding, and did so as recently as Monday.
It also warned residents not to share images, rumours or information about interceptions and impact sites, including in a post on ​Monday, under government regulations issued in March.
Read more: Saudi-led coalition says Houthi ballistic missile intercepted over Riyadh
Reuters could not determine whether anyone had faced prosecution for sharing such information, and the Saudi government media office did not respond to a request for comment on the matter.
Before last week's airport attacks, officials from an allied Western ​government asked Saudi authorities why the alerts had stopped, two officials with direct knowledge of the matter said.
The response was that the alerts were too disruptive and many citizens had complained they were being woken by them at night, the officials said.
The Saudi government media office and Saudi officials ‌did not respond ⁠to requests for comment on the assertion.
Former US ambassador to Saudi Arabia Michael Ratney said Riyadh was trying to balance public messaging on attacks with efforts to prevent disruption in the kingdom but had ended up adding to a sense of unease about the strikes.
"Their approach to public messaging seems like a corollary to the quandary they are in: They need to respond to the Houthis but don't want that to result in societal disruption and their public messaging is a reflection of that," he said.
"But the lack of alerts of incoming Houthi attacks creates the very nervousness they are trying to avoid."
Ali Shihabi, a Saudi analyst close to the government, said that with or without early warnings, the kingdom would struggle to defend all of its assets because of its size.
"In Saudi Arabia, you have ​too much to protect. It's a huge country with airports, pipelines ​and oil facilities. There is just not enough coverage to ⁠defend everything at once, not enough Patriots (missile defence systems), interceptors and missile batteries to do it all," he said.
"Saudi Arabia has an unlimited need for air defences," he added."
Despite the attacks, Saudi Arabia hosted an international conference on Monday, though major oil bosses dropped out.
Also read: FM Dar condemns Houthi attack on Riyadh airport, says Pakistan is in touch with Saudi authorities
At the World Petroleum Council Energy Congress in Riyadh, Saudi Prince Abdulaziz bin Salaman, a brother of the Saudi crown prince and the kingdom's energy ​minister, struck a defiant tone while acknowledging risks and Saudi Arabia's intent to keep its economic plans on track.He thanked all who had travelled to Riyadh "because you know this country is safe" ​but added: "Our gathering here does not ⁠mean the risk is gone.""We will never forfeit any chance to maintain our commitment and our vision," he said.
Embassies issue their own internal alerts
Despite no public alerts being issued this month until Monday, Riyadh has been attacked about a dozen times, two of the Western officials said.
During that time, Western embassies in the kingdom have been issuing their own internal missile and drone alerts to staff, according to three people familiar with the matter and alerts seen by Reuters.
These internal alerts are compiled from a mixture of US and other Western government intelligence and input from Saudi authorities, ⁠one of those ​people said.
They include alerts sent to staff around the time of two first airport strikes last week, according to the people familiar with the matter.
They said that ​even the embassies had received no internal warning before Saturday's airport strike, without explanation.
Reuters could not determine why no warning came before Saturday's attack, the deadliest of last week's attacks.

title: Gill claims ICC player of the month award
description: Record breaking double century seals September   s top individual honour
content:
Record-breaking double century seals September’s top individual honour
India batsman Shubman Gill has been named the ICC Men's Player of the Month for September 2026, the International Cricket Council (ICC) revealed on Tuesday.
He won the award ahead of fellow nominees Abhishek Sharma of India and Zimbabwe's Sikandar Raza.
Gill scored 333 runs in India's first two ODIs against West Indies, with a century in the opener and an unbeaten double century in the second. India won both matches by eight wickets.
In the first ODI, in Thiruvananthapuram on 27 September, Gill made 110 off 108 balls as India chased down West Indies' 295/7. India reached the target of 296 in 41.4 overs.
Three days later in Guwahati, West Indies made 405/7, their first ODI total above 400. Gill, captaining India, responded with an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls, including 26 fours and eight sixes, and India finished on 406/2 in 43.3 overs with 39 balls to spare. He reached his hundred in 62 balls, the fastest by an Indian captain in ODIs, and his double century in 117 balls, the fastest in ODI history. It is also the highest individual score in a successful ODI chase. Gill and Rohit Sharma (101 off 75 balls) put on 255 for the opening wicket, India's highest partnership on home soil. The chase was the second-highest successful one in ODI history, behind only South Africa's 438/9 against Australia in Johannesburg in 2006.
India went on to win the three-match series 2-1 after West Indies took the third ODI on 3 October.
This is Gill's fifth ICC Men's Player of the Month award, after wins in January 2023, September 2023, February 2025 and July 2025, extending his record as the men's player with the most wins.
The most recent Indian men's winner was Sanju Samson, in March 2026. Indian men have now won the award 17 times across 11 players, including Gill's five victories.
Reacting to the award, Gill said: “It feels fantastic to win my fifth ICC Player of the Month award, and I am grateful to the panel for this honour."
"It was immensely satisfying to score those runs and even more special to be part of successful run chases in front of our home fans, whose support always gives us an extra boost." he added.
The Indian captain also addressed the changing nature of the game and how important it is to adapt to it.
“The pace of ODI cricket has gone up significantly, and you must think on your feet, assess the conditions quickly and adapt to the demands of the pitch," he said.
"With the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup in southern Africa next year, we are determined to keep raising our standards and build a strong, well-rounded team capable of rising to the challenges ahead," he added.
India’s all-rounder Shafali Verma wins ICC Women’s Player of the Month award:
Shafali Verma has been unveiled as the ICC Women's Player of the Month for the month of September 2026.
It is the second time Shafali has won the monthly award, with the 22-year-old first tasting success in November last year when she helped India claim the ICC Women's Cricket World Cup on home soil.
“It is an incredible honour to win the ICC Player of the Month award again," Shafali said.
"It was immensely satisfying to play my part in our victories at the Asia Cup and the Asian Games, and winning this award makes those triumphs even more special."
Shafali said she was already looking forward to India's upcoming white-ball series against Zimbabwe and she had one eye on next year's ICC Champions Trophy event.
“I am excited about the months ahead and determined to keep performing at my best, with the ICC Women’s Champions Trophy in February next year another tournament to look forward to," she added.
"The memory of winning the World Cup is still so fresh and special, and I can’t wait to be back on the field for an ICC tournament on home soil. It promises to be an unforgettable experience!”
The explosive opener's crowning moment comes on the back of India's win at last month's Asia Cup as well as the gold medal triumph at the recently concluded Asian Games in Nagoya.
Shafali scored 360 runs in seven T20Is, averaging a sensational 72 and boasting a strike rate of 184.61. The right-arm off-spinner also contributed six wickets at an average of 13 and an economy rate of 4.33.
The 22-year-old was the leading run-scorer at the Asia Cup in UAE with 236 runs in five innings, including a knock of 64 in the semi-final against Bangladesh and 68 in the final against Sri Lanka, as India secured a record-extending eighth Asia Cup title.
She continued her form at the Asian Games in Japan, scoring 188 runs in three innings. That included an unbeaten 40 against Japan before she produced a maiden T20I century against Bangladesh, smashing 100 off 49 balls in the semi-final.
The opener climbed into the top four on the ICC Women's T20I batting rankings as well.

title: Israeli actions in Syria ‘counterproductive’ to regional peace, Pakistan tells UN | The Express Tribune
description: Ambassador Jadoon says Israel's actions flagrant violations of international law and Syria's sovereignty
content:
Ambassador Jadoon says Israel's actions flagrant violations of international law and Syria's sovereignty
Pakistan on Tuesday called for Israel’s withdrawal from all occupied Syrian territory, with its envoy to the United Nations warning that continued Israeli military actions were “profoundly counterproductive to the prospects for regional peace and stability” and threatened Syria’s efforts towards national reconciliation and economic recovery.
Speaking at a UN Security Council briefing on the humanitarian and political situation in Syria, Pakistan’s Acting Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Usman Jadoon, said the actions were “flagrant violations of international law and Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity”.
“They are also profoundly counterproductive to the prospects for regional peace and stability,” Jadoon said, adding that while Syria worked to consolidate peace and recovery, “such violations serve only to create further instability”.
Statement by Ambassador Usman Jadoon, Acting Permanent Representative of Pakistan to the UN, At the UN Security Council Briefing on the Humanitarian and Political Situation in Syria (12 October 2026) ********** Madam President, We thank Deputy Special Envoy Cordone, and ASG… pic.twitter.com/G2cSBqSSI7
Jadoon said the occupied Syrian Golan remained Syrian territory under international law and cited UN Security Council resolutions 338 and 497. He reiterated Pakistan’s call for Israel’s withdrawal from all occupied Syrian territory and full compliance with the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement.
The Pakistani envoy said it was “deeply regrettable” that continued Israeli military actions threatened to undermine Syria’s efforts to achieve national reconciliation and revive its economy.
Jadoon said Pakistan welcomed the Syrian government’s efforts towards national reconciliation and the advancement of the country’s political transition.
“Today, amid the challenges of recovery and reconstruction, there is a renewed sense of hope in Syria,” he said. He added that a country which had witnessed years of conflict was “steadily reclaiming its rightful place in the region and the wider international community”.
Jadoon said Syria’s renewed diplomatic engagement, restoration of national institutions and gradual revival of economic activity offered “highly encouraging signs of a new chapter in Syria’s history”.
He said Pakistan welcomed progress in engagement with the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) and hoped that outstanding challenges, including the situation in Suweida, would be addressed through dialogue and peaceful engagement.
“Syria’s unity and diversity are mutually reinforcing,” he said, stressing the need for “full respect for Syria’s unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity”.
The Pakistani envoy said Syria’s reconstruction and economic revival required sustained international support.
He said the lifting of sanctions by the United States and the European Union, alongside expanding investment and economic partnerships with friendly countries, particularly in the region, and European partners, would provide “important impetus to Syria’s recovery and development”.
At the same time, Jadoon said, “sustained humanitarian assistance remains essential to address the needs of the Syrian people”.
He said Pakistan shared a sense of optimism about Syria’s future, adding that bilateral ties between the two countries continued to grow. “The leadership of our two countries recently met on the sidelines of the General Assembly High-Level Week, reaffirming our shared commitment to further strengthening bilateral relations,” he said.
Jadoon also warned that the threat posed by Daesh and other terrorist groups, including foreign terrorist fighters, required "sustained vigilance".
He expressed Pakistan’s support for Syria’s efforts to counter terrorism, consolidate security and strengthen national institutions. “We appreciate the constructive and measured engagement of the Syrian leadership in wisely navigating the country’s challenges amidst a complex regional situation,” he said.
Concluding his remarks, Jadoon reaffirmed that “Pakistan will remain a steadfast friend and partner of Syria,” he said, adding that the two countries’ relations, rooted in shared cultural bonds and mutual respect, would continue to deepen.
“The people of Pakistan will continue to stand in solidarity and friendship with their Syrian brothers and sisters,” he said.

title: Karachi court hands journalist Iqrarul Hassan to NCCIA on four day physical remand
description: Case filed under PECA  alleges anti state content on social media with intent to instigate  incite public
content:
Case filed under PECA, alleges anti-state content on social media with intent to instigate, incite public
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Tuesday produced journalist Iqrarul Hassan before the judicial magistrate (East) at Karachi's city court in a case of harming the state and national integrity through the dissemination of anti-state content on his social media platforms, handing him over to the NCCIA on a four-day physical remand.
According to the First Information Report, the case was filed at the NCCIA by Inspector Muhammad Ali Khan under Sections 9, 10, 20, 24, and 26-A of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) 2016.
The FIR stated that Hassan, "through his personal social media accounts on the platforms X, Instagram and Facebook, is intentionally disseminating false, fabricated, anti-state and defamatory content with the object of instigating the general public against the state, its institutions and its functionaries."
During the hearing, the court asked Hassan whether he had been subjected to torture, to which he replied that he had not been beaten. Asked whether he had a lawyer, he said he had not hired one yet.
The NCCIA sought a 14-day physical remand of Hassan, saying he had to be interrogated in connection with the case. The court granted four days instead.
Read: Journalist arrested on 'attempted rape' charges
According to the FIR, Assistant Director Rana Muhammad Faisal Munir will investigate the case without delay. It added that the content of Hassan's social media posts portrayed the state, its institutions and its functionaries "in a false and distorted manner."
It also noted that Hassan "represented lawful measures as controversial with the intent to instigate and incite the general public at large against the state and the lawfully constituted authorities."
The FIR stated further, "The accused instigated a substantial following, including the general public, on the aforesaid platforms," adding that the content that he posted was published and broadcast "in an open, publicly accessible manner, without restriction, so as to reach and influence the public at large throughout Pakistan and abroad."
A day earlier, Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari said that Punjab Police had not arrested Hassan , adding that investigations into the matter were underway and his family would be informed as soon as verified information about his whereabouts became available.
Azma's statement came after Hassan's wife Farah Iqrar told The Express Tribune that a group of unidentified individuals posing as officials of the NCCIA had allegedly taken him away from their residence in Lahore’s Defence C area.
Read More: LHC seeks NCCIA directors' record
According to Farah, between five and seven people, including women, arrived at the house late on Sunday night, during the intervening hours of Sunday and Monday, and demanded that Hassan come outside. She alleged that the individuals threatened to break down the door if he was not handed over. They subsequently entered the house, forcibly took the journalist from a room and took him away.
Farah said she contacted the relevant agency’s office to inquire about her husband’s whereabouts but received no response. She added that an application regarding Hassan’s alleged abduction was submitted to the Defence C police station at around 6am, after which the police issued a diary number.
She further said she later contacted the relevant authorities to register a computerised first information report online but was told that the network was down.
Hours before the reported incident, Hassan had posted a message on X criticising the Pakistan Peoples Party and referring to Nawaz Sharif and President Asif Ali Zardari.

title: Teenager shoots headmaster  teacher at French school
description: Staff member disarms 14 year old suspect as authorities say incident has no link to nationwide students  protest
content:
Staff member disarms 14-year-old suspect as authorities say incident has no link to nationwide students' protest
A 14-year-old boy opened fire with a hunting gun at a middle school in France on Monday, wounding the headmaster and a teacher before being disarmed by a member of staff, local authorities said.
The shooting took place at Joseph-Lakanal middle school in the southern town of Aubagne, near Marseille, where a third person was grazed by gunfire, police said.
Authorities said there did not appear to be a link with high school protests that have rocked France in recent weeks. "The middle school was not affected by the high school students' protest ," police told AFP .
The suspect "came in carrying a bag which was a guitar case. He clearly removed a weapon from this guitar case — a long gun," said Marseille's deputy public prosecutor Audrey Jouaneton. He fired at least four shots, including inside a classroom occupied by teachers and pupils, leaving a mark on a blackboard, she added.
The headmaster, 53, and teacher, 37, were not in critical condition, according to authorities.
Read: French policing under scrutiny as student protest injuries mount
"The suspect, for reasons as yet unknown, fired at the headteacher, who was hit by a shower of pellets in the thighs and lower back," said Jacques Witkowski, prefect of the wider Bouches-du-Rhone region. He then fired at a second teacher, who was hit by buckshot in the thigh before a member of staff disarmed him, he said.
The suspect "is not known for any history of delinquency or radicalisation," Witkowski added.
Sarah, a pupil at the school, told AFP she heard the fire alarm go off during her Spanish lesson and went into the corridor, where she and her classmates "bumped into" the gunman. "He started shooting and said: 'I've only come for the teachers, not for the pupils,'" she said.
An investigation into attempted murder has been opened.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, who visited the scene, said the suspect's parents had been taken into custody. Investigators were "trying to understand how this young person ended up in a position with this gun", Nunez told reporters.
French President Emmanuel Macron on X praised the teaching staff for their quick reaction. "I commend the composure and exemplary response of the teaching staff, which helped to prevent the worst from happening," he said.
Au principal et à l’enseignante blessés ce matin dans un collège à Aubagne, aux élèves et aux parents sous le choc, j’adresse ma pleine solidarité et mon total soutien. Je salue le sang-froid et la réaction exemplaire de l’équipe éducative, qui a permis d’éviter le pire.
Education Minister Edouard Geffray, who also went to the scene on Monday, called for action against such violence. "All this seems to sit within a global social phenomenon," he said. "We have to provide a societal response... Schools can't do everything, schools cannot treat major violence."
There has been a spate of violent incidents at French schools in recent months, prompting bag checks on entry in some establishments.
In February, a 14-year-old stabbed an art teacher in southern France at least three times, leaving the 60-year-old in critical condition. A 14-year-old student in June last year fatally stabbed a teaching assistant in eastern France. In another, a student carried out a stabbing spree in several classrooms in April last year, wounding a girl and three other pupils.
