title: Zverev to become tennis world number one
description: The German secures the year end top ranking after Alcaraz s third round exit in Shanghai
content:
The German secures the year-end top ranking after Alcaraz's third-round exit in Shanghai
Men's tennis confirmed it will crown a new world number one as Germany's Alexander Zverev was ensured the year-end honour on Monday after Carlos Alcaraz lost his third-round match in Shanghai.
The career-first will cap a stellar season for the 29-year-old, the current world number two, after he won the French Open in June and the US Open in September.
The French Open was his first-ever Grand Slam title.
"It's been a fantastic season for me winning in Paris and New York and knowing that I will finish the year on top of the rankings is just a dream come true," Zverev said in a statement shared by the ATP Tour website.
"So much work and effort have been put into achieving this goal, especially after coming back from the ankle injury," Zverev added.
He suffered a career-threatening ankle injury in his French Open semi-final in 2022.
Zverev will be the first German male player to finish his season as top-ranked in the world, and the oldest to lift the trophy, set to be presented in November, for the first time.
Germany's Angelique Kerber and Steffi Graf have both been the year-end number one women's tennis player.
Zverev's achievement comes in a year where the previous two players to hold the top ranking, Italy's Jannik Sinner and Spain's Alcaraz, have skipped months of competition due to injury.
Sinner, the current number one, has not competed since Wimbledon where he beat Zverev in the final. He announced last week his season was over due to a knee injury.
Alcaraz, ranked third, was sidelined for months with a wrist injury from April until the US Open.
Zverev, 6-foot-6 (1.98m), had been destined for the top from a young age, hailing from a tennis family where his mother and father both played the sport to a high level in the former Soviet Union.
But he plays in the shadow of domestic violence allegations made by two former partners, which he has strenuously denied.
The ATP Tour investigated one claim and found insufficient evidence to punish Zverev.
Another led to a 2023 penalty order and fine from a German court which later dropped the case after a settlement was agreed in June of 2024 -- hours before he was due to play in the French Open semi-finals.

title: India youth shift tactics as police clamp down on election protest
description: Protesters undeterred by thousands of reported detentions during demonstrations over the weekend in the capital
content:
Protesters undeterred by thousands of reported detentions during demonstrations over the weekend in the capital
As police and protesters engage in a high-stakes game of cat and mouse, social media-savvy students are turning ingenuity into a form of resistance.
With tens of thousands of security personnel deployed in key parts of the capital to block the main protest site of Jantar Mantar, protesters turned to holding flash demonstrations elsewhere, taking authorities by surprise.
Protesters have been undeterred by thousands of reported detentions during demonstrations over the weekend in the capital. Many have since been released.
Read More: Indian capital braces for second day of protests against poll chief
They are seeking the resignation of the head of India's election commission, accusing it of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling party, which the constitutional body has denied.
Meghnad S., a 36-year-old content creator, is on a mission that resembles a crowd-sourced rescue service.
Armed with little more than smartphones, his group of about 170 volunteers spent the weekend tracking police vehicles.
As soon as volunteers identified where detainees had been taken, information was fed into a digital dashboard matching them with volunteer drivers.
"Once we get to know where the detainees are, we have a WhatsApp group where we ask if any volunteer driver is around, what car they have, if it is stocked with food, water, fuel," Meghnad told AFP .
"Once those checks are done, we try and get a doctor in our network to join the driver on the way, in case the detainees need medical assistance."
Popular student leader Neha Bora became a viral sensation after a case of mistaken identity led to police detaining her lookalike.
The real Bora, 29, managed to slip through the security cordon and make a dash towards central Delhi before eventually being detained.
She later posted a photograph with her doppelganger, joking that the resemblance was "pure coincidence, not strategy".
The tale of the two Nehas. Not strategy, just coincidence. 😂😂 pic.twitter.com/aBA37Obxg3
It was not just Bora; police were also seen struggling to catch up with sprightly young protesters on streets.
"They have big bellies, they can't run," a protester told reporters.
"They pant after running just 50 metres," she said.
In other dramatic scenes, protesters were seen holding on to one another as they were dragged to waiting buses -- only for them to later wriggle out from the driver's seat or the rear window.
AFP also met several demonstrators who wore Batman masks to avoid being identified.

title: Saudi Arabia rejects Israeli bid to join fight against Houthis  Israeli media
description: Israel seeks Riyadh   s approval through US mediation  hoping military cooperation could pave the way for normalization
content:
Israel seeks Riyadh’s approval through US mediation, hoping military cooperation could pave the way for normalization
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has rejected an Israeli push to join the military campaign against Yemen's Houthi group, despite efforts to secure Riyadh's approval through US mediation, the Israeli newspaper Haaretz reported Monday.
The daily, citing an unnamed diplomatic source, said the crown prince was not interested in Israeli military assistance, fearing that cooperation with Israel could provoke a negative reaction among the Saudi public.
Another source familiar with the matter said Israel hoped military cooperation with Saudi Arabia would strengthen bilateral ties and pave the way for a future normalisation agreement.
There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities on the report.
Read: Saudi-led coalition says Houthi ballistic missile intercepted over Riyadh
Saudi Arabia has no diplomatic relations with Israel and has maintained that normalisation depends on resolving the Palestinian issue, including the establishment of a Palestinian state.
The report comes amid escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including repeated strikes on airports that have caused casualties and disrupted flights.
An attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday killed 13 people and injured more than 300 others.
Another attack on the same airport Sunday killed a Pakistani resident and injured 11 others, according to Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation.
Saudi capital's airport to remain shut this week as airlines cancel services
Authorities have extended the closure of Riyadh's international airport until ​Saturday and airlines scrapped flights after continuing attacks by Yemen's Houthis emptied the skies over Saudi Arabia's capital.
Operations at King Khalid International Airport, Saudi ‌Arabia's second-busiest airport after Jeddah, were suspended to "allow for the completion of procedures to ensure the safety and operational readiness of the airport's facilities", the Saudi civil aviation authority said in a statement.
Late on Monday, the Houthis said they had attacked the airport with a ballistic missile, shortly after Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired by the group towards ​Riyadh.
The Houthis also said in a statement that they targeted an airbase in Khamis Mushait in the kingdom's southwest with a drone. There was no ​immediate Saudi confirmation.
A Notice to Airmen issued on Monday showed King Khalid International Airport will stay closed until 0200 PKT on October ⁠17.
The attacks have now raised worries over civil aviation becoming a target in armed conflict, despite Saudi Arabia-backed Yemeni forces having attacked Sanaa airport earlier in the year under the pretext of attacking Iranian planes.
"This level of sustained intense attack on civil aviation is unprecedented," said Mark Zee, founder of OPSGROUP, a membership-based organization that provides aviation safety advice.
"I think this requires us ​to rethink how we view the current risk picture, and tread very carefully," he said.
Air traffic tracker Flightradar24 showed planes avoiding the city on Monday, though jets were ​crossing Saudi airspace and landing at top hub Jeddah on the country's west coast.
Cancellations across all Saudi airports reached 46.4%, aviation analytics firm Cirium said.
Crisis overshadows Saudi business outlook
The disruption has ‌forced airlines ⁠across Europe and Asia to suspend services, while the Federal Aviation Administration advised US carriers on Sunday to exercise caution when flying to or over Saudi Arabia. EU aviation body EASA widened a Saudi airspace warning on Friday, citing missile and drone attacks.
"The impact goes beyond Saudi Arabia to the wider region and to its global connections," said aviation analyst John Strickland.
OPSGROUP advised airlines to avoid the southern aviation corridor over the Middle East altogether, and take a route from Europe to Asia over central Asia.
Read more: FM Dar condemns Houthi attack on Riyadh airport, says Pakistan is in touch with Saudi authorities
That adds "extensive distance" for some ​routes and "closes off options for getting into ​Dubai, Abu Dhabi for most western ⁠carriers," Zee said.
Lufthansa Group has cancelled all flights to Riyadh until October 16, while Air France-KLM has extended a suspension to and from Riyadh until the end of the month.
Etihad Airways said it had cancelled flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam ​due to "regional disruption", adding that all flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh would be cancelled until October 19.
Qatar Airways ​said on Monday it ⁠had temporarily suspended flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam due to the "current situation".
Delta Air Lines said it was delaying planned services from Atlanta to Riyadh, initially due to start on October 23, until March 2027.
The escalation with the Houthis has raised concerns over the broader economic impact. Saudi Arabia's real GDP is projected to contract by 3.6% this year, reflecting ⁠a combination ​of factors including lower oil activity.
The attacks have put events scheduled in Riyadh this month under pressure, including ​the kingdom's flagship investment conference and the WPC Energy Congress, where several top oil executives were dropped from the programme.
Trump criticizes Yemen’s Houthis while offering no specific response
US President Donald Trump criticized Yemen’s Houthi group Monday but did not outline any specific measures that his administration might take in response to its actions.
Speaking to reporters as he departed the White House for Ohio, Trump was asked what he planned to do about the Houthis.
“Well, the Houthis are misbehaving very badly. No good,” he replied.

title: Coventry crush Newcastle to climb out of relegation zone
description: The Sky Blues record their first Premier League home win in 25 years to climb to 14th
content:
The Sky Blues record their first Premier League home win in 25 years to climb to 14th
Coventry earned a slice of Premier League history as they climbed out of the relegation zone with a stylish 4-1 win against Newcastle on Monday.
Frank Lampard's side are the first club in 127 years to secure successive English top-flight victories immediately after losing their opening four games without scoring.
Jack Rudoni's penalty early in the first half put Coventry ahead with their first ever Premier League goal at the CBS Arena, which became their home in 2005.
Guinean forward Sidiki Cherif increased the Sky Blues' lead after the interval.
Sven Botman got one back for Newcastle, but Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni struck late to ensure Coventry jumped from 19th to 14th place.
Lampard's men had taken their first points of the season by beating Nottingham Forest 1-0 before the international break.
And Coventry's first win over Newcastle since 1999 bolstered their bid to avoid relegation in their first season in the Premier League since 2001.
They will look to make it three consecutive wins when they travel to troubled Tottenham on October 19.
"Today we showed a big energy and showed our abilities. Some quality goals went in," Lampard said after Coventry's first top-flight home win for 25 years.
"You have to ride a bit of luck, but we did it. If we don't have that spirit, we haven't got a chance. We need everybody.
"We have to keep our feet on the ground because it's so hard in this league. If you think you have cracked it you haven't."
A win would have taken Newcastle into fourth place, but instead they were beaten for the second time in six league games this season.
Matthias Jaissle's team were punished for squandering a host of chances in the first half.
Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek handed Coventry a needless penalty in the sixth minute when he fumbled the ball and tripped Cherif in a despairing bid to clear the danger.
Joe Willock teed up Harvey Barnes midway through the first half, finding space outside the Coventry area and picking out his Newcastle team-mate for a close-range effort that he flicked narrowly wide.
Newcastle monopolised possession and Jacob Murphy lashed just over from distance before Matias Fernandez-Pardo's shot was cleared off the line by Bobby Thomas.
Having made one goal-line block to deny Fernandez-Pardo, Thomas did it again with another brilliant clearance on the stroke of half-time after the Newcastle forward rounded Carl Rushworth.
Coventry took full advantage of Thomas's heroics to double their lead three minutes after half-time
Making his first Premier League start after joining from Fenerbahce in the summer, Cherif ensured it would be a day for him to remember forever as the 19-year-old smashed a fine finish into the bottom corner from the edge of the area.
Botman reduced the deficit in the 70th minute when the defender lashed a blistering blast past Rushworth from 20 yards.
But Newcastle midfielder Joelinton, making his first appearance of an injury-plagued season, was guilty of the decisive mistake in the 81st minute.
Joelinton's heavy touch on the edge of his own area allowed Simms to pounce with his first touch after coming off the bench as the striker's deflected drive whistled past Hornicek.
Mfuni, on loan from Manchester City, put the seal on Coventry's vibrant display when he blasted home from long-range in the 86th minute.

title: Infantino could pull off  Houdini  act as critics struggle for candidate
description: The 56 year old Swiss has lost the support of many associations in his bid to be re elected
content:
The 56-year-old Swiss has lost the support of many associations in his bid to be re-elected
Gianni Infantino could survive weeks of criticism and secure re-election as FIFA president in the absence of a heavy hitter to challenge him, observers have told AFP.
The 56-year-old Swiss has lost the support of many associations in his bid to be re-elected to a fourth and final term since he launched and then hastily shelved his plan to allow private investment into the World Cup.
Infantino, though, does crucially retain his core support in Africa and South America.
His FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan, which came to light in July just after the hugely successful World Cup, would have created a commercial subsidiary to run FIFA's biggest events, such as the World Cup.
However, with two of his fiercest critics, Aleksander Ceferin and reportedly Victor Montagliani opting to run for re-election as heads of European governing body UEFA and North American grouping CONCACAF respectively, the opposition to Infantino is desperately seeking a viable candidate to challenge him in the election next March.
Candidates have to declare by November 18.
Terrence Burns, who was marketing strategist for two successful World Cup hosting bids, said Infantino was always in the box seat.
"He holds all the cards and always has," he told AFP. "Any prospective challenger at this point feels either performative or strategic to cut deals."
Former International Olympic Committee (IOC) marketing chief Michael Payne said "everyone is surprised" that no serious candidate has come forward to challenge Infantino.
"If he is re-elected, which is looking increasingly likely, it will redefine the term Houdini," Payne told AFP.
Long-time Infantino critic Lise Klaveness, the head of the Norwegian Football Federation (NFF), has impressed many but has ruled out running.
However, even if Klaveness changed her mind she would face a huge challenge in becoming the first woman to run world football and emulate Kirsty Coventry, who last year became the first woman elected as IOC president.
"People within the IOC administration were working towards the goal of Coventry being elected, as (her predecessor) Thomas Bach's wish was for her to be president," a source close to the world of football governance, who asked not to be identified, told AFP.
"Lise faces exactly the opposite. FIFA staff would be working to stop her being elected."
Infantino, though, is not safe yet as the opposition have mounted legal challenges in the US and filed official complaints with FIFA committees.
Klaveness and the Norwegian federation have highlighted three issues, with the common thread being Infantino's friendship with US President Donald Trump.
The venture capital firm of Josh Kushner, the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared, was to be the major investor in FFE.
However, the same source warned "there is no certainty that the complaints will be looked into. Even if they were to consider them they would take their time.
"The fear in the Infantino camp is the Norwegians could take them to CAS (Court of Arbitration for Sport) if dissatisfied with the decision."
Burns, though, believes the greatest risk to Infantino comes from the legal challenges launched by UEFA in the US courts to gain access to the papers pertaining to FFE. FIFA are strongly contesting the case.
"This point is a fly in the ointment," Burns said. "If the FFE was just a case of misguided process and communications strategy, why hide its specifics?
"That lack of transparency is a rock in Infantino's shoe that will not fade away."
Payne believes the lack of support for Infantino from leading football nations such as Spain, France and England could be damaging.
"Running a global sports federation requires unity -- FIFA will be on the brink of civil war, and this is totally new territory for a sports governing body," he said.
Burns though thinks the opposition will reluctantly make peace with Infantino.
He said football's governing bodies would rather avoid division "unless of course there is overwhelming criminal activity to justify it -- which there is not".
The other point that could tip the balance is if there is a "financial upside" for the federations by removing Infantino. On that point, he said, "again, there isn't."
Burns believes in fact that the process is likely to "result in even greater consolidation of power and influence for Infantino when it is all over."

title: Ronaldo on target as Al Nassr win

content:
Al-Nassr overcome an hour-long security delay to beat Neftchi 3-1
Cristiano Ronaldo scored Al-Nassr's second goal as the Saudi Pro League champions overcame an hour-long security delay to beat Uzbekistan's Neftchi 3-1 in the AFC Champions League Elite on Monday.
Kick-off was delayed after Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence issued a safety ‌warning 15 minutes before the scheduled start time in Riyadh, which has been targeted by missiles fired from Yemen-based Houthis in recent days.
Ange Postecoglou's side shook off the interruption to go in front through Angelo in the 33rd minute with a deflected strike before Ronaldo doubled the lead nine minutes later.
The 41-year-old struck after Sadio Mane delivered a looping cross from ⁠the left that Aiman Yahya directed into Ronaldo's path with his chest and the Portuguese forward lashed the ball into the bottom corner with a shot on the turn.
Alisher Odilov pulled one back for Neftchi six minutes into the second half but Ikromjon Alibaev's red card for a foul on Mohamed Simakan in the 65th minute and an own goal by Anvarjon Gofurov 13 minutes later sealed the win for Al-Nassr.
Meanwhile, defending champions Al-Ahli scored twice in the second half to pick up their first win of the new campaign as Marino Pusic's side beat Al-Wasl from ‌the United ⁠Arab Emirates 3-1.
Roger Ibanez put Al-Ahli ahead with a 20th minute header but Pedro Malheiro levelled in the third minute of first-half stoppage time.
Goals from Trincao and Feras Al-Brikan in the 58th and 91st minutes respectively moved Al-Ahli onto four points from their opening two matches.
"We created also in the first half but ⁠in the second half we made our goals and I think that was the difference," said Trincao. "Physically we were a little bit better and that was the key to changing the game."
Houssine Rahimi scored twice as ⁠Al-Ain defeated Air Force Club 4-1 in Basra, while Hossein Goudarzi's 60th minute goal earned Iran's Esteghlal a 2-1 win over Al-Gharafa.
A last minute penalty from Dostonbek Khamdamov salvaged a 1-1 draw for Pakhtakor ⁠against Brendan Rodgers' Al-Qadsiah in Tashkent while Tractor from Iran were held to a 0-0 draw by Qatar's Al-Shamal.

title: Selma Blair arraigned over alleged Delta flight incident as bail set at  20 000
description: Authorities responded to the incident at John F  Kennedy International Airport on Sunday after Delta flight 938 landed
content:
Authorities responded to the incident at John F. Kennedy International Airport on Sunday after Delta flight 938 landed
Actress Selma Blair was arraigned in New York on Monday evening following an alleged altercation aboard a Delta flight from Los Angeles to New York City, with bail set at $20,000 cash, according to ABC News.
The 54-year-old actress faces two counts of second-degree assault under New York law.
The criminal complaint also alleges separate incidents involving a Port Authority police officer and a registered nurse.
Authorities responded to the incident at John F. Kennedy International Airport on Sunday after Delta flight 938 arrived.
According to the complaint, two flight attendants sustained injuries, while Port Authority officer Maria Suarez allegedly suffered facial, neck and chest injuries during Blair’s transport to an ambulance.
A nurse later reported chest pain following an alleged incident during Blair’s medical treatment at Jamaica Hospital.
Blair’s representative told ABC News, "Selma experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct. Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is currently in stable condition."
Delta confirmed that law enforcement met the aircraft upon arrival and said, "Delta has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first."
The FBI and Federal Aviation Administration are investigating the incident. Blair’s next court appearance on the assault charges is scheduled for January 19, 2027.
She has also reportedly received a federal violation notice relating to alleged assaults within US jurisdiction.
The incident recalls a 2016 flight episode for which Blair later apologised, explaining that mixing alcohol with medication had caused her to black out.
She was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2018 and announced in 2021 that her condition was in remission.
The allegations have not been established in court.

title: Alcaraz exits Shanghai Masters in straight sets loss
description: Bergs beat the second seeded Spanish star 7 5  7 6  7 4  in the third round
content:
Bergs beat the second-seeded Spanish star 7-5, 7-6 (7/4) in the third round
Carlos Alcaraz fell to Zizou Bergs in straight sets at the Shanghai Masters on Monday, interrupting the former world number one's in-form return to the professional Tour after being sidelined for months by injury.
The 39th-ranked Belgian beat the second-seeded Spanish star 7-5, 7-6 (7/4) in the third round to land the tournament's biggest upset yet, and will play Tommy Paul next.
"Today wasn't a good match from my side. I didn't feel good," Alcaraz told reporters, crediting Bergs for taking chances and serving big.
"In a few important moments I didn't play my best, and I would say there were a few moments that he was lucky," the 23-year-old said of their two-hour battle.
Alcaraz said he was "disappointed" by a loss riddled with errors, which came a week after he won the Tokyo Open, adding he would return home and hit practice.
"Right now, you know, all the negative thoughts come to my mind and none of the positives, but I think I will take it, you know, the good things," he said.
His loss also ensures current world number two Alexander Zverev, the reigning French Open and US Open champion, will replace Jannik Sinner as world number one by the year's end, with the Italian's season over due to a knee injury.
Zverev, the top seeded player in Shanghai, will face Alexander Bublik in the last 16 on Tuesday.
Alcaraz started with more quality until Bergs broke the Spaniard's serve to go up 3-2 in the first set.
Alcaraz grabbed back that break in the next game but was uncharacteristically off-target, sending a mess of shots into the net.
He double-faulted to hand Bergs a critical break point in the 11th game, and lost the first set when a volley went short.
Alcaraz, currently ranked third in the world, was visibly frustrated during the second set as he vented to his corner following a series of misfired shots that left him with no points in the fourth and eighth games.
He forced a tie-break but could not reach a third set as Bergs closed things out on the first match point.
"It's a little disbelief and not feeling too much," Bergs, 27, said after winning.
"You're just really in the moment, being focused on the points you have to play," he said.
Earlier, Stefanos Tsitsipas came back to beat Taylor Fritz 3-6, 7-5, 6-3 and earn fourth round meeting with Daniil Medvedev, who brushed aside qualifier Dalibor Svrcina 6-2, 6-3.
A wardrobe malfunction delayed victory for the Greek world number 43 when a tennis ball tumbled out of the American's pocket a second time and forced the men to replay a match point.
A tired-looking Fritz, seeded 11th, hung on for a bit longer to save the eighth game but could not stick around beyond that, with Tsitsipas holding serve to win at the fifth time of asking.
"I could have done a few things easier, but I ended up being my biggest enemy," Tsitsipas told the crowd afterwards.
"I turned things around really well towards the end and became friends with myself and played some incredible tennis," he said.
Felix Auger-Aliassime, Casper Ruud and Rafael Jodar also went through to the last 16.
American world number 18 Paul sent off last year's winner Valentin Vacherot 6-4, 6-2 while Botic van de Zandschulp beat eighth-seeded Arthur Fils 7-5, 6-4.

Mitte was widely recognised for playing Walter White Jr. in Vince Gilligan’s Emmy-winning crime drama,
RJ Mitte’s Breaking Bad co-stars, including Bryan Cranston, Aaron Paul and Dean Norris, have paid tribute to the actor following reports of his death at the age of 34.
Mitte died on Monday in Brownsville, Texas, as confirmed by his representatives. No official cause of death was disclosed, although TMZ reported that he died by suicide.
Mitte was widely recognised for playing Walter White Jr., the son of Cranston and Anna Gunn’s characters, in Vince Gilligan’s Emmy-winning crime drama, which ran for five seasons between 2008 and 2013.

Aaron Paul, who portrayed Jesse Pinkman, expressed his grief in a statement shared with The Hollywood Reporter . “I am at a loss. I am heartbroken over this news. RJ, I love you my friend. You will be missed,” he said.
Dean Norris, who played Hank Schrader, also remembered Mitte fondly. “He was a sweetheart of a young man and will be greatly missed,” Norris said.
Cranston concluded his tribute by encouraging anyone experiencing suicidal thoughts to seek support through the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in the United States.

title: Iran will pursue diplomacy to counter sanctions  secure national interests  Iranian FM
description: US Iran war
content:
Tehran finalising response to US views on Iranian proposal: Iranian deputy FM
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that the Foreign Ministry was pursuing diplomatic avenues to safeguard and defend its rights and interests both nationally and internationally, IRNA reported on Tuesday.
He made the remarks during a meeting with representatives of Tehran Province in Parliament on Monday, as part of ongoing consultations between the legislature and the Foreign Ministry on foreign policy and national security issues.
Iran to pursue diplomacy to secure national interests, counter sanctions: FM @araghchi https://t.co/2c0dK9ckXi pic.twitter.com/Is20xFSDr9
During the meeting, the foreign minister outlined the latest regional and international developments and briefed the lawmakers on the ministry’s key measures and initiatives to safeguard Iran’s national interests.
US was unable to rally allies in war against Iran: Iranian parliament deputy speaker
The United States failed to secure its allies’ support in its war against Iran, demonstrating the setbacks facing Washington’s regional strategy and leaving it increasingly isolated, Iranian Parliament Deputy Speaker Hamidreza Haji Babai said to IRNA on Tuesday.
US failed to rally allies in war against Iran: Deputy speaker https://t.co/JEGjfpJkcu pic.twitter.com/4s0m2uQvBc
According to IRNA , Haji Babai said US President Donald Trump’s continued threats reflected desperation, adding that a country confident in its power and ability to act would have no need to resort to threats.
The legislator added that US allies had refused to join Trump’s acts of aggression against Iran, exposing Washington’s difficulties in advancing regional objectives.
According to Haji Babai, US isolation and resistance against aggression ultimately led to the withdrawal of American forces from Iraq, and US troops would eventually leave other regional countries as well.
He urged regional countries to unite against foreign threats, saying recent wars had shown that the United States could not guarantee their security.
Iran cautions against unilateral measures in global economy
Deputy for international relations of the Central Bank of Iran warned that unilateral measures could deepen economic fragmentation, increase risks, and fuel uncertainty in the global economy, according to IRNA on Tuesday.
Iran warns against unilateral measures in global economy https://t.co/1gQpEyRQPN pic.twitter.com/0VYikF9Eji
Speaking at the G24 meeting of central bank governors and finance ministers in Bangkok, Thailand, Abolfazl Kodehi on Tuesday highlighted the need to strengthen economic cooperation, better economic resilience, and reform international institutions to address the consequences of unilateralism.
He said that globalisation created significant opportunities for many economies over the past decades, but progress in developing international institutions and frameworks has slowed in recent years.
Unilateral economic policies undermine global economic cooperation and make the world economy more vulnerable to uncertainty and risks, he added.
The 2026 Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group will take place October 12 to 18 in Bangkok, Thailand.
Tehran finalising response to US views on Iranian proposal: Iranian deputy FM
Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs Kazem Gharibabadi stated that Tehran was finalising its response to the American side’s observations and views regarding the proposal Iran presented in New York while speaking to Al Arabiya on Monday night, according to Press TV .
Iran remains open to all diplomatic processes while remaining fully prepared to defend itself, Gharibabadi said, and added that Iran would convey its final position through mediators after consultations.
Iran ready for diplomacy but fully prepared to defend itself, deputy FM says https://t.co/GVmJe49MLS
“Tehran remains ready for diplomacy, provided that what is raised is realistic,” Gharibabadi said.
He said that Iran’s readiness to defend itself was no less than its readiness to negotiate.
Continued participation in talks, he added, reflects Tehran’s commitment to the diplomatic process. At the same time, the US must return to fulfilling its obligations.
Gharibabadi emphasised that Iran has not violated any of its commitments, while saying that Washington failed to honour its obligations under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding .
“As long as the American side has completely disregarded all of its commitments, Iran cannot be expected to show further flexibility,” he said.
The remarks come as Tehran continues to pursue diplomatic channels while underscoring its sovereign right to self-defence amid ongoing tensions, according to Press TV .
Trump says US may have gone 'too far' in targeting Iranian leaders
US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that the US might have "gone too far" with targeting Iranian leadership as now they "don't know who the hell we're dealing with anymore," according to Clash Report and Al Jazeera .
Trump on Iran: We might have gone too far with the leaders because we don't know who the hell we're dealing with anymore. We're having a hard time figuring out who the hell to deal with, to be honest with you. I think we went too far. We could have stopped at level one. Level… pic.twitter.com/So3NMfViQm
"We're having a hard time figuring out who the hell to deal with, to be honest with you. I think we went too far."
President Trump has suggested the US may have gone too far in targeting Iran’s leadership, saying Washington is struggling to identify officials with whom it can negotiate. 🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/zjeCMhpJCd pic.twitter.com/3Sv2yruNPW
"We could have stopped at level one. Level two and level two and a half was probably going too far," he added.
Trump says he doesn’t believe China and Russia are helping Iran
US President Donald Trump said on Monday that he does not believe China and Russia are helping Iran, arguing that both countries have too much to lose by doing so.
Responding to comments that Beijing and Moscow are assisting Tehran, Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform: “If they are, it’s at a very low level, but I don’t believe they are at all.”
“They have too much to lose, and we would know about it, and know about it very fast!” he added.
His remarks echo a July Truth Social post in which he said that Chinese President Xi Jinping had told him during their meeting in China in May that Beijing would not “under any circumstances” sell weapons to Iran, including through Chinese companies, and that Russian President Vladimir Putin had also told him that he would not sell weapons to Iran.
At the time, Trump warned that if they did get involved, “it would be very bad for them.”
Read: Iran says reviewing US proposals for talks as indirect messages continue
In May, the Trump administration sanctioned several Chinese companies accused of supporting Iran’s military procurement network and providing satellite imagery that allegedly enabled Tehran to target US forces.
Beijing denies the allegations that Chinese entities aided Iran’s military.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28, prompting Tehran to respond with missile and drone attacks in the region and effectively close the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global energy supplies.
A memorandum of understanding signed in June by the US and Iran following Pakistani and Qatari mediation has since stalled amid disagreements, including over navigation in the strait.
Iran following up on missing Iranian pilots in Qatar: government spokesperson
An Iranian government spokesperson said on Tuesday that the Ministry of Defence and Foreign Affairs were following up on the issue of Iranian pilots in Qatar , and the Qatari government "pledged assistance" and announced its "readiness to cooperate in order to clarify their status", according to ISNA .

content:
Assembly okays 12km railway link from Yaro
The Balochistan Assembly on Monday unanimously adopted a resolution seeking the extension of the Jinnah Train Service from Kuchlak to Yaro Railway Station and the construction of a new 12-kilometre railway track from Yaro to Pishin to provide affordable and reliable transport facilities to residents of Pishin division.

Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI) MPA Syed Zafar Agha moved the resolution, stating that the launch of the Jinnah People's Train Service between Quetta and Kuchlak had provided citizens with an affordable and safe travel option.
He said Pishin division was densely populated, with large numbers of students, government and private-sector employees, patients and other residents travelling to Quetta daily for education, employment, medical treatment and business.
However, the lack of convenient and timely transport facilities had created difficulties for commuters, he added.
The resolution urged the provincial government to approach the Ministry of Railways to extend the existing train service from Kuchlak to Yaro Railway Station and take practical steps to lay a 12-kilometre track from Yaro to Pishin. The proposal was approved unanimously.
During the session, Jamaat-i-Islami MPA Hidayatur Rehman Baloch submitted a call-attention notice regarding financial assistance and subsidies for livestock farmers. The notice was disposed of following an assurance from the parliamentary secretary concerned.

title: K P lawyers announce black day  court boycott
description: K P lawyers announce black day  court boycott
content:
Bar bodies oppose emergency and governor's rule
The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Bar Council has announced a province-wide Black Day on October 13 and a complete boycott of court appearances in protest against the imposition of emergency in the province, describing the move as an extraordinary constitutional step that threatens federal structure, parliamentary democracy and provincial autonomy.
In a statement issued from its office, the Bar Council expressed grave reservations over the federal government's actions under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution of Pakistan. It stressed that any such measure must strictly adhere to the conditions, legal requirements and prescribed procedures laid down in the Constitution. Using constitutional powers to dissolve an elected provincial government or render the public mandate ineffective on the basis of political differences, the Council warned, raises serious concerns about the integrity of the federal system and the principle of provincial self-rule.
The Council strongly opposed the federal action, equating it to a direct assault on the province's autonomy. It made clear that the legal fraternity would not remain a silent spectator and would play its full role in the restoration of democracy and the supremacy of the Constitution and the rule of law.
According to the press release, the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Bar Council has decided that lawyers across the province will observe Black Day on October 13 by staying away from courts. The Council has also summoned a meeting of its general body on October 17 in Peshawar. The session will thoroughly review the prevailing situation, chart a future course of action and deliberate on steps needed to restore the democratic system.

title: Khyber rises in protest as PTI march flops in Swabi
description: Khyber rises in protest as PTI march flops in Swabi
content:
Police arrest workers in Swabi as demonstrations against governor's rule spark clashes in Khyber
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's much-hyped long march in Swabi completely failed to materialize on Monday, with not a single worker turning out despite the party leadership's claims.
District leadership remained absent throughout the day as authorities kept all roads open and traffic flowing normally.
In Swabi, business centres operated as usual while police contingents, containers and other machinery remained deployed across the district. Peshawar, the Islamabad Motorway and the GT Road also stayed open with routine traffic movement.
A police crackdown intensified after the imposition of emergency and Governor's rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. District police arrested more than 180 PTI workers, with sources putting the confirmed figure at 169 so far. Arrests were carried out in Shewa Ada, Yar Hussain Razzar, Swabi Khas, Topi, Lahore, Gadoon and other areas. Those detained include several local office-bearers and active workers, among them District Senior Vice President Muhammad Ayaz Taj Abad, Raees Khan and Mustafa Khan. Police sources said the arrests were made over preparations for the long march and fears of disruption to law and order. Each police station has been assigned a target of hundreds of further arrests, and raids continue.
Meanwhile, on the second day of emergency in Khyber tribal district, protests erupted in Jamrud and Bara against the emergency and Governor's rule and in support of former K-P chief minister Sohail Afridi.
District Police Officer Khyber confirmed that 30 protesters were arrested.
In Bara Bazaar, tension persisted throughout the day between police and demonstrators, particularly around Main Khyber Chowk, Qambar Abad Market and the Sur Minar area. Police resorted to baton charges, tear gas and aerial firing to disperse crowds. The heavy use of tear gas created panic, severely disrupted commercial activity and caused distress to local residents, especially women and children living near the affected markets.
In Jamrud, PTI workers gathered at the historic Bab-e-Khyber to protest the emergency measures and voice support for Sohail Afridi. Reports also emerged that police sealed Afridi's hujra in Bara, though no official explanation was provided. Heavy police presence kept the area under tight control.
The dual developments left commercial life, public movement and daily routines disrupted in parts of Khyber while Swabi remained largely calm under a visible security blanket.

title: ATC orders lawyer access to Imaan  Hadi
description: ATC orders lawyer access to Imaan  Hadi
content:
Adjourns further proceedings until October 14
An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Islamabad on Monday directed jail authorities to facilitate meetings between lawyer Imaan Mazari, her husband Hadi Ali Chattha and their legal team, which had been unable to meet them in connection with a case involving the removal of barriers.
ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra issued the directions during the hearing, which was attended by former human rights minister Shireen Mazari and lawyers Riasat Ali Azad and Aimal Khan. During the proceedings, Azad argued that the case could not proceed without allowing the legal team, comprising Azad, Zainab Janjua and Aimal Khan, to meet their clients.
The judge observed that anti-terrorism law required trials to be conducted on a daily basis and asked the prosecution how many witnesses it intended to produce. The prosecutor said there were nine witnesses. The judge subsequently directed the prosecutor to ensure that the accused were given access to their lawyers.
Chattha questioned why he and Imaan were not being brought before the court, arguing that their continued absence undermined the requirements of a fair trial. He said they had been in jail for eight months and questioned how they could defend themselves and proceed with the case under such circumstances.
He also raised concerns about the confidentiality of meetings between lawyers and their clients, pointing out that cameras had been installed in the areas where meetings were held inside the jail. "The court has to decide our fate. Please summon us to court," Chattha said, adding that it was for the court to determine whether he and Imaan were terrorists.
The court adjourned further proceedings until October 14.
Imaan and her husband Chattha were rearrested on September 17, shortly after the Supreme Court granted them bail and suspended their sentences in a separate social-media posts case. They were produced before an Islamabad ATC in connection with a case registered at Kohsar Police Station.
Police sought 30-day physical remand, but ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain rejected the request and sent the couple on judicial remand. The judge noted that although they had been nominated in the FIR as members of an unlawful assembly, no weapon had been attributed to either accused.
On September 27, the court issued a contempt notice to the Adiala jail superintendent after the authorities failed to facilitate the signing and transmission of the documents and also failed to produce the accused through video link. Two days later, the issue was resolved after Imaan and Chattha signed the required powers of attorney.
On September 29, the ATC ended the contempt proceedings against the jail authorities and separately confirmed that notices had been issued on the couple's bail applications, with arguments scheduled before Judge Abul Hasnat.
On October 7, the ATC had framed charges against Imaan and Chattha in the case related to the alleged violation of a designated route and incitement during the arrival of an international cricket team, despite defence objections that legal requirements had not been fulfilled.

title: N Korea fires missiles days after South Korea s hypersonic test
description: N Korea fires missiles days after South Korea s hypersonic test
content:
North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles toward the sea off its east coast on Monday, South Korea's military said, marking Pyongyang's fourth launch in a month and following Seoul's recent test of a hypersonic missile.
The ballistic missiles, whichappeared to be of different types, were fired at around 9:20 a.m. local time (0020 GMT) from near Pyongyang, and one type flew more than 900 km (559 miles), South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said.
Earlier, Japan's coast guard said North Korea had fired two unidentified projectiles, believed to be ballistic missiles, adding that both appeared to have already fallen. The US Pacific Command, in a statement, said it was aware of the two ballistic missiles launched, but the event posed no immediate threat to US personnel, territory or allies.
"We are aware of the missile launches and are consulting closely with our allies and partners," the statement said.
South Korea's National Security Office convened an emergency meeting, where it condemned the missile launches as violations of United Nations Security Council resolutions and urged an immediate stop.
North Korea has been under UN sanctions since 2006, aimed at halting Pyongyang's development of nuclear weapons and ballistic missiles.
The latest launches come as tensions have been rising between the two Koreas in recent weeks amid weapons tests by both countries.
Last week, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung oversaw the country's first test-firing of a hypersonic missile, a rare public showcasing of a missile test by a South Korean president.
Monday's missile launches by North Korea appeared to be "a show of force in response to the successful test launch of our hypersonic missile, as well as an intentional demonstration of missile capabilities," a spokesperson for South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said. Reuters

title: PSX plunges 1 965 points amid political chaos
description: PSX plunges 1 965 points amid political chaos
content:
Stock selling in banks, oil and gas, cement pulls KSE-100 index down
Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) endured a bruising start to the week on Monday as political upheaval in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) and mounting geopolitical anxiety kept investors on edge, driving the benchmark index deep into the red.
The KSE-100 index remained volatile throughout the session and shed 1,964.87 points, or 1.18%, to settle at 165,124.41 at the close of trading. The imposition of governor's rule and emergency measures in parts of K-P, followed by reports of police crackdown, added to political clamour, stoking fears of further unrest. Selling pressure swept through oil marketing companies, automobile assemblers, cement firms, power producers, commercial banks and oil and gas exploration companies, reflecting the broad-based weakness in market sentiment.
In the international market, oil prices eased on expectations of increased Russian supplies after US President Donald Trump said Ukraine and Russia had agreed to halt attacks on each other's energy facilities following a US diesel supply deal with Moscow. However, the relief was tempered by fears of a wider regional conflict after a Houthi attack on Riyadh's international airport, leaving investors wary amid an already unsettled geopolitical landscape.
Talking to The Express Tribune, KTrade Head of Research Fawad Basir attributed the market's weakness to geopolitical uncertainty and heightened tensions in K-P. He said while June 2026 corporate results in the listed space were better than expected, higher commodity prices were keeping inflation elevated despite the base effect, potentially influencing this month's monetary policy decision. At the same time, exchange rate parity and interest rates remained key concerns amid the Middle East crisis and the IMF programme review, Basir added.
In its report, KTrade mentioned that selling pressure was broad-based across commercial banks, oil and gas, cement and technology stocks. Oil and Gas Development Company, Habib Bank, Meezan Bank and Lucky Cement were among the major laggards.
"Going forward, market direction is likely to remain volatile, hinging on geopolitical developments and oil prices, with sustained easing in crude prices and progress in US-Iran engagement potentially supporting equities, while further regional escalation could extend the bearish trend," KTrade forecast.
Arif Habib Limited Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib observed that the market opened on a negative note amid heightened domestic political uncertainty. Value buying at lower levels offered brief support to the benchmark index, but the recovery proved short-lived, with the bourse closing firmly in negative territory. "Going forward, the market is likely to remain volatile amid political uncertainty and cautious investor sentiment. Further downside pressure cannot be ruled out, although value buying at lower levels may provide intermittent support," he said. Najib advised investors to remain selective, prioritise fundamentally strong stocks and avoid aggressive positions until sentiment stabilised.
Topline Securities said that the KSE-100 index came under renewed selling pressure, closing at 165,124, down 1,965 points (-1.18%). The bearish sentiment followed the federal government's decision to impose emergency in K-P, after President Asif Ali Zardari approved the federal cabinet's recommendation on Sunday. The development heightened political uncertainty, prompting investors to adopt a cautious stance amid concerns over the evolving situation.
Overall trading volumes increased to 363 million shares compared with Friday's tally of 309.4 million. The value of shares traded during the day stood at Rs14.5 billion.
In the ready market, shares of 500 companies were traded. Of these, 135 stocks closed higher, 322 fell and 43 remained unchanged.
Treet Corp was the volume leader with trading in 27.3 million shares, gaining Rs0.37 to close at Rs24.09. Foreign investors bought shares worth Rs11.6 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb has accepted the chairmanship of the Governing Council of the Borrowers' Platform on behalf of Pakistan, acknowledging Egypt's leadership and the contributions of member countries and the Secretariat in operationalising the Platform.
He emphasised that the Platform should promote mutual learning and technical cooperation rather than serve as a collective bargaining or crisis-management mechanism. Outlining Pakistan's priorities under the 2026-27 work plan, he highlighted strengthening debt-management practices, sharing reform experiences and exploring innovative development-financing instruments. He stressed that debt should remain an instrument for development rather than a constraint on it.
The minister was participating in a series of meetings and ministerial engagements on the sidelines of the Annual Meetings of the World Bank Group and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in Bangkok, according to a statement issued on Monday. The engagements focused on macroeconomic stabilisation, structural reforms, investment, climate finance and cooperation on debt management. In a meeting with IMF First Deputy Managing Director Dan Katz, the minister discussed Pakistan's stabilisation, progress under the IMF-supported programme and structural reforms. Both sides welcomed the staff-level agreement and acknowledged improvements in fiscal performance, foreign exchange reserves, inflation and external sector stability.
Aurangzeb highlighted improved investor confidence, sovereign credit rating upgrades and renewed access to international capital markets. Discussions also covered the impact of the Middle East conflict on energy prices and inflation. Participating in the 17th V20 Ministerial Dialogue, he appreciated the V20's support in developing Pakistan's Climate Prosperity Plan and referred to Pakistan's inaugural green Panda bond. He cautioned against initiatives remaining unimplemented, citing the Loss and Damage Fund.
He later met United Nations (UN) Under-Secretary-General and Executive Secretary of the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) Armida Salsiah Alisjahbana. He identified climate change and population growth as challenges and sought technical support for disaster preparedness and bankable climate projects.

title: BOI vows close coordination with businessmen
description: BOI vows close coordination with businessmen
content:
Invites investment in steel mills' land and infrastructure
Federal Minister for Board of Investment Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh has said that the government will work closely with the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) to promote investment, facilitate the business community and accelerate industrial growth. The business community must be involved in policymaking, regulatory matters and economic decisions, as industrialists and traders understand ground realities and business challenges.
Speaking at the LCCI, Sheikh said that the business community should not merely be informed about policies but they should be actively involved in their formulation. "Government departments should consult chambers of commerce and industrial representatives before making decisions concerning regulations, business standards and investment, ensuring that policies remain practical and do not create unnecessary obstacles to commercial activities."
The minister said an effective one-window facilitation system was essential to save investors from visiting multiple departments and facing unnecessary delays in obtaining approvals and the BOI and the government were doing a lot in that regard. He assured the business community that the BOI would maintain close coordination with the LCCI to address investment-related issues.
The federal minister described the development of Special Economic Zones (SEZs) as an important step to attract investment. He said allocating land alone was insufficient. Roads, infrastructure and other essential facilities must also be provided to attract investors and encourage the establishment of industries.
Sheikh also highlighted plans to utilise 6,000 acres of Pakistan Steel Mills' land in Karachi as an SEZ. He invited investors to avail themselves of the opportunities, adding that the effective use of large industrial landholdings, supported by adequate infrastructure, could create new opportunities in manufacturing, logistics, industrial investment and exports.
He said local industrial competitiveness, production capacity and export potential should be considered while formulating trade policies. He stressed that investors needed a predictable business environment, clear regulations and consistency in government decisions to make long-term investment plans with confidence.
LCCI President Ali Hussam Asghar said the business community played a vital role in economic growth, employment generation and investment, but actions of government departments and the exercise of discretionary powers were creating difficulties for industrialists and traders. He said that the LCCI did not oppose the implementation of laws and regulations. However, enforcement methods should not unnecessarily disrupt legitimate business activities. Instead of immediately registering FIRs, sealing business premises or taking harsh action over minor or rectifiable violations, authorities should provide businesses with reasonable time and an opportunity to address the shortcomings.
Asghar also stressed the need to review relevant laws, including the Punjab Environmental Protection Agency Act and the Punjab Food Authority Act and consider necessary amendments. He said the LCCI was reviewing relevant legislation and would put forward proposals for consideration at the provincial and national levels. He said the tax system should build confidence among taxpayers, reduce unnecessary disputes and facilitate compliance rather than create avoidable difficulties for businesses.
The LCCI president said that several industries in Lahore had been operating for five to 30 years but were now facing relocation notices from the Lahore Development Authority and other departments. He called for a clear, uniform and transparent industrial relocation policy, with reasonable deadlines and alternative industrial sites.

title: Rupee gains Rs2 since US Iran war
description: Rupee gains Rs2 since US Iran war
content:
Currency on upward trajectory as SBP buys $8.1b but REER crosses 107
Pakistan's rupee has appreciated by around Rs2 against the US dollar since the Middle East war began, maintaining its strength despite rising energy costs, geopolitical uncertainty and higher global yields.
The Pakistani rupee, extending its modest upward trend against the US dollar, gained 0.01% in the inter-bank market on Monday and closed at Rs276.97 per dollar. It was up three paisa from Friday's closing rate of Rs277/$. The currency's gradual upward trajectory reflects a policy approach focused on accumulating foreign exchange, containing domestic demand and maintaining monetary restraint rather than relying on currency depreciation to absorb external shocks.
Pakistan made net foreign exchange purchases of $8.1 billion during fiscal year 2026, absorbing dollar supply in the inter-bank market and limiting the rupee's potential appreciation, according to Tresmark Research.
However, foreign exchange reserves increased by only around $4 billion during the year, as approximately $11 billion went towards external debt servicing and repayments.
Pakistan's external debt payments falling due within 12 months declined from more than $30 billion in June 2025 to around $24 billion by July 2026, following repayments, rollovers and refinancing.
The improved maturity profile, higher reserves and upgraded credit ratings have strengthened the country's external position. However, these gains remain vulnerable to changes in energy prices, global financing conditions and foreign exchange inflows.
The rupee's appreciation comes as Pakistan continues to struggle with weak exports. The real effective exchange rate (REER) has crossed 107, prompting concerns about the currency's competitiveness.
Authorities maintain that the exchange rate alone cannot resolve structural weaknesses in exports. Currency depreciation could also increase the cost of imported energy and other goods, putting additional pressure on inflation.
The authorities remain cautious about recovering import demand and may consider further rate increases if external pressures intensify. Remittances have remained resilient, although slower labour migration to the Middle East could weigh on future inflows. Inflation is projected to ease towards 7% by June 2027. The rupee's sustainability will ultimately depend on stronger exports, stable remittances, manageable energy costs and sufficient external financing.
Meanwhile, gold prices in Pakistan fell on Monday, tracking a decline in the international market, with the per-tola rate dropping Rs2,100 to Rs439,936.
According to the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association, the price of 10-gram gold decreased by Rs1,800 to Rs377,174. On Saturday, gold had gained Rs1,100 to settle at Rs442,036 per tola. In the international market, gold prices fell by $21 to $4,174 per ounce. Silver prices also declined, shedding Rs23 to reach Rs6,532 per tola.
Adnan Agar, Director of Interactive Commodities, said gold was trading between $4,165 and $4,170 an ounce after touching the high of $4,217 and low of $4,155. He said the market remained under pressure, with prices repeatedly failing to sustain gains around $4,200 to $4,230.
"Gold will remain under pressure unless it breaks above the $4,240-$4,280 range," Agar said.
On the downside, he said gold could find support near $4,100. However, the failure to rebound from that level could expose the market to further weakness. He added that gold had remained range bound between $4,050 and $4,240 for nearly a month.
Agar said rising US bond yields were weighing on gold prices. He also cautioned that a renewed conflict between the United States and Iran could put further downward pressure on the metal.

title: LNG imports to cost over  1b in winter
description: LNG imports to cost over  1b in winter
content:
Pakistan needs to buy expensive gas from spot market to meet high demand during cool weather
As winter is approaching, the struggle to keep kitchen stoves burning through cold months is set to carry a staggering price tag of $1 billion, fuelled by high costs of liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports from the open market triggered by the US-Israel-Iran war.
Pakistan's government is set to import 10 LNG cargoes at double the price at which LNG is being imported from Qatar. These cargoes will be purchased from the spot market for deliveries from November 2026 to February 2027 to meet the high demand for gas in the winter season.
During this period, the government will import 12 LNG cargoes from Qatar, whereas 10 LNG consignments will be bought from the spot market. LNG supply from Qatar has been severely disrupted by the Middle East war.
Pakistan State Oil (PSO) and QatarEnergy have a sale-purchase agreement for 15 years covering 2016 to 2031 and the other contract is for 10 years effective from 2021 to 2031. The second LNG contract proved controversial, signed during the tenure of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) government, as the country did not require more LNG, which led to a market glut.
Both sale-purchase agreements had been struck under a government-to-government arrangement. As per these deals, PSO receives 6.75 million tonnes of LNG (108 cargoes) each year. For 2026, however, PSO and QatarEnergy earlier agreed to divert 24 cargoes to other destinations due to low demand in Pakistan.
Sources said that the issue was taken up in a meeting of the energy task force held in the current month. The projected natural gas demand during the upcoming winter season will require LNG imports during the months of November 2026 to February 2027.
Public-sector entities plan to secure approximately half of this requirement under the existing long-term contracts and for planning purposes, the projected supply comprises 12 cargoes from Qatar and no cargo from Eni under long-term contracts, with the remaining 10 cargoes to be procured through spot contracts.
Based on the estimated Brent-linked long-term price and the spot LNG price of $26.30/MMBtu, being the latest spot price quoted in a tender, the estimated import bill of each spot cargo will be $86.3 million.
Between November 2026 and February 2027, total LNG import costs are anticipated to reach $1,292.83 million for the 22 cargoes required to meet seasonal demand. While term agreements with Qatar (11 cargoes valuing at $351.41 million) and Eni (one cargo worth $78.42 million in January) cover $429.83 million of the total, heavy reliance on the spot market – accounting for 10 cargoes costing $863 million – will drive up the overall bill.
Winter requirements will peak in January 2027 with eight cargoes pushing the monthly cost to $437.32 million, followed closely by December 2026 at $369 million, reflecting how spot purchases significantly inflate winter import expenditures.
The estimated import bill for the 12 cargoes under long-term contracts will be $429.83 million, while the estimated import bill for the 10 spot cargoes will be $863 million. Accordingly, the aggregate projected LNG import bill for the four-month period will be approximately $1,292.83 million. These estimates are subject to actual supply availability, contract quantities, applicable contract prices and the prevailing market rate for spot procurement.
Recently, PSO and Qatar have served LNG contract review notices. PSO is seeking the consent of the federal government to review the contract with QatarEnergy, designated by Qatar for LNG supply. Their LNG contracts will expire in 2031.

title: Govt eyes raising  1b from privatisation
description: Govt eyes raising  1b from privatisation
content:
Aurangzeb expects over 4% growth, says country is pursuing $10b US facility
Pakistan's economy is expected to grow by more than 4% this fiscal year despite elevated oil prices, as the government looks to push for the privatisation of five to six entities that could raise upwards of $1 billion, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb told Reuters on Monday.
Pakistan's economy is considered to be highly vulnerable to a prolonged Middle East conflict given its dependence on Gulf energy imports, remittances and financing support from the region, even as it remains reliant on external financing to bolster foreign exchange reserves and meet debt repayments.
The country with a population of 255 million people has been able to procure adequate quantities of fuel, successfully avoiding any shortages, and critical sectors such as agriculture were holding up, Aurangzeb said.
"So I'm still quite clear that we should clock north of 4%," he said in an interview on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Bangkok.
"And on the inflation side, obviously, we are keeping a very close eye because it does have a knock-on impact in terms of the commodity prices."
Following a period of severe economic turmoil exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, the cash-strapped economy has recovered some of its footing, supported by a $7 billion, 37-month IMF loan program known as the Extended Fund Facility signed in 2024 that includes some tough measures such as raising tax revenue on farm income.
The US-Israeli-led war with Iran, now in its eighth month, and the inflation and hardship it has caused, will dominate the agenda and sideline conversations during the meetings that are being held outside Washington for the first time in three years.
Pakistan, which reached a staff-level agreement with the IMF last week potentially unlocking about $1.21 billion in financing under the Extended Fund Facility and a climate programme, is continuing discussions with the United States for a proposed $10 billion exchange stabilisation facility, Aurangzeb said.
But he declined to provide a time frame for the conclusion of negotiations.
"If it comes through, this will be a great help for us," he said, referring to the facility, which is in addition to ongoing talks with the Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM) and the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC).
"If it doesn't come through, this does not, you know, create any problem for us in terms of access to market."
Following the privatisation of flag carrier Pakistan International Airlines last year, Aurangzeb said the government has around another dozen entities in the pipeline, including state-owned power distribution companies and the outsourcing of airport operations.
"I expect about five or six of these to go through during this fiscal year," he said, adding that they could raise more than $1 billion.
Privatisation has been seen as a key test of Pakistan's reform credibility with the IMF, with officials previously underlining that failure to offload loss-making state firms risked renewed pressure on public finances. "We are quite clear that we want the private sector to lead the country," said Aurangzeb. "So our role is to help support, assist any way we can in terms of the ecosystem."

title: IMF raises inflation forecast to 9 9
description: IMF raises inflation forecast to 9 9
content:
Keeps growth unchanged at 3.5%, suggesting it has not agreed to govt projections
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has revised upward Pakistan's inflation forecast to 9.9% but kept economic growth unchanged at 3.5%, suggesting that it has not agreed to the government's projections of relatively low inflation and high economic growth for this fiscal year.
The fresh figures have been released in the World Economic Outlook (WEO) report while the IMF's staff-level report will be made public only after the loan tranches are approved by the executive board tentatively late November. According to the WEO report, which the IMF released on Tuesday on the sidelines of annual meetings, inflation in Pakistan could accelerate to 9.9% in this fiscal year. In April this year, the IMF had projected Pakistan's inflation rate at 8.4% for fiscal year 2026-27, which it also maintained in July's report.
The IMF has not given any Pakistan-specific reasons for the increase in inflation rate but it has also revised upward the inflation projections for the Middle East and Central Asia region due to the ongoing conflict that has impacted energy supply and prices. The rate is higher than the official target of 8.2%. During the recently concluded staff-level talks, the federal government and the central bank had maintained that despite inflationary pressures Pakistan would be able to meet the annual target.
The 9.9% inflation projection means that the IMF might also be seeking higher interest rates to contain the inflationary pressures.
The government has been fully passing on the increase in fuel prices to domestic consumers in addition to charging heavy taxes. It has given Rs2,000 per month compensation to motorcyclists and Rs3,000 to small car owners. But the IMF has objected to the scheme, terming it broad and carrying high cost. The report underlined that global headline inflation rose in August, as energy prices bounced back following the short-lived ceasefire in the Middle East.
According to the IMF report, economic growth in Pakistan may remain at 3.5% in this fiscal year - a forecast that is unchanged compared to the lender's previous projections. During the review talks, Pakistani authorities had tried to convince the IMF that the annual growth target of 4% will be achieved.
In an interview with Reuters, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said that "I am still quite clear that we should clock north of 4%". Pakistan has been following a prolonged phase of economic stabilisation under three different IMF programmes, which according to the World Bank is one of the reasons for higher poverty in the country.
In his detailed memo, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal has recently recommended to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif an eight-point new Growth-Compatible Fiscal Stabilisation Framework for higher growth and development instead of merely saying in polls that we "inherited an economic crisis" and achieved stability.
He wrote to the prime minister last month that Pakistan was increasingly achieving fiscal stabilisation by compressing development expenditure and borrowing more, rather than sufficiently expanding the revenue base and increasing exports.
"The electorate will judge the government on the economy it experiences in 2029: growth, employment, income, investment, exports, inflation, energy costs and economic opportunity," he wrote.
The IMF has also projected a slightly higher current account deficit of 1% of the gross domestic product (GDP), or about $4.4 billion. It is around $450 million more than the IMF's previous projections. The IMF said that in the Middle East and Central Asia, growth is projected to drop to 0.3% in 2026 before rebounding to 6.3% in 2027. Relative to the April projection, this is a downward revision of 2.2 percentage points for 2026 and an upward revision of 1.7 percentage points for 2027, consistent with a longer closure of the Strait of Hormuz, compared with the baseline assumptions in the April report, and a corresponding larger rebound after the Strait reopens, it added.
But the lender said that the global economy was showing resilience, which is reflected in its latest global growth forecast. The new global growth projection remains broadly unchanged from April, despite a more persistent energy market disruption than anticipated. Global activity is projected to grow at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027.
Global headline inflation is projected to rise to 4.7% this year, reflecting primarily higher commodity prices, and to fall back to 4.1% in 2027; the pass-through to core inflation is expected to be limited.
The IMF said that global activity in the first half of 2026 held up better than expected despite the dragging war in the Middle East and continuing strains from trade tensions. The technology cycle has provided a demand impulse, driven by strong investment in artificial intelligence (AI). The interaction of these forces - geopolitics and technology - has produced a split global economy: favourable terms of trade or technology-related exports and investment give some countries a cushion, whereas others face higher import bills and weaker demand.
But it said that resilience was under strain. Without shoring up supply capacity and replenishing policy buffers, the global economy could soon test the limits of resilience. Inventories in energy markets are dwindling and additional geopolitical shocks could still transmit rapidly through prices and supply disruptions, it added.

Three employees of the Maryam Nawaz Health Clinic in Mirali have been dismissed amid an inquiry into alleged salary deductions, the deaths of five newborns and the provision of substandard medicines at the facility.

On October 3, Chief Executive Officer of the District Health Authority Vehari Dr Fahad Waheed, District Coordinator for the Integrated Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child Health programme Dr Syed Ali Raza and Deputy District Health Officer Dr Dur Zainab visited the clinic to conduct an inquiry.

title: Low wind speed aggravates pollution risk
description: Low wind speed aggravates pollution risk
content:
Low wind speeds are causing concerns about the accumulation of air pollutants across Lahore as several localities reported elevated pollution levels on Monday.
Winds forecast to blow at around 3km per hour during afternoon hours can hamper the dispersal of pollutants, increasing the risk of pollution accumulating near the ground with an expected seasonal deterioration in air quality approaching
Punjab Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) data showed Lahore's overall Air Quality Index (AQI) at 126 at 10am, placing it in the moderate category. The reading was substantially higher than the 74 recorded at the same time a day earlier.
Shahdara recorded an AQI of 209, classified as unhealthy, while Multan Road registered 171 and GT Road 169, indicating unhealthy air for sensitive groups.
IQAir's past assessment placed Lahore's annual average fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentration at 88.9 micrograms per cubic metre, about 17.8 times the World Health Organisation's annual guideline.
The.monitoring data shows that several areas remain vulnerable to unhealthy pollution levels even before the peak winter smog period.
Low wind speed can reduce the rate at which pollutants disperse, allowing emissions from traffic, industries, brick kilns and other sources to accumulate. The impact depends on wind direction, atmospheric stability, temperature and volume of emissions.
environment protection teams inspected 85 brick kilns across the province, demolishing four and sealing two others. A case was registered against an operator, while three kilns received notices for violations.
Officials also inspected 24 industrial units, sealing four and imposing fines totalling Rs200,000.
According to a spokesperson, teams checked 17 barbecue and commercial cooking locations and issued smog notices to four. Suction hoods were installed at 13 commercial cooking points to improve compliance with environmental requirements.
However, vehicle exhaust, construction dust, industrial emissions and burning of waste can continue contributing to pollution even when kilns or factories are shut down for violations.

The initiative will initially cover Lahore, Kasur and Sheikhupura, benefiting more than 4.6 million industrial workers and their family members.
The government aims to extend the programme to Gujranwala, Sialkot, Gujrat, Faisalabad, Sargodha, Sahiwal, Multan, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Bahawalpur, Rahim Yar Khan and Rawalpindi by March, according to a statement.
The programme includes 10 mobile hospitals, five clinics, dental and cardiac units, 40 motorcycles and 10 scooters.
The motorcycle and scooter teams will provide basic medical assistance, first aid, essential medicines and health awareness services.
The mobile hospitals will be equipped with outpatient departments, diagnostic facilities, X-ray and ultrasound services, basic laboratories and medical staff, including male and female doctors, radiologists, nurses and technicians.
The mobile clinics will also offer telemedicine facilities, while the dental units will provide examination and treatment.
During her visit to the Nawaz Sharif Social Security Hospital, the CM inspected the mobile hospitals, dental unit, motorcycles and scooters, receiving a briefing on the medicines and equipment.
Officials also briefed her on a mobile rheumatic heart disease screening initiative, which will cover 29,845 factories, industrial establishments and other workplaces in Lahore, Sheikhupura and Kasur.
The mobile units will also be deployed to screen around 54,000 children enrolled in workers' welfare schools across Punjab for heart conditions.
The field operations of all mobile health units will be connected to a digital hub at the Punjab Employees Social Security Institution (PESSI) headquarters to enable real-time monitoring of their routes and activities.
The chief minister said on the occasion that the province's 24 social security hospitals were providing treatment and medicines to over 10 million industrial workers and their families. The mobile health programme would facilitate early diagnosis and treatment, reducing the burden on hospitals, she added.
