title: PERA officials not immune from criminal law
description: PERA officials not immune from criminal law
content:
LHC dismisses petition of employee accused of torture
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has ruled that officials of the Punjab Enforcement and Regulatory Authority (PERA) cannot claim exemption from the ordinary criminal law merely because a special statutory mechanism exists to deal with complaints against them, holding that allegations of criminal offences must be examined under the relevant provisions.
Justice Muhammad Ajmal Zahid dismissed a constitutional petition filed by a PERA official, observing that the applicability of the special procedure under the Punjab Enforcement and Regulation Act, 2024, must be determined according to the nature of the offence rather than the official status of the accused.
The court held that the existence of a special legal framework does not automatically exclude the general criminal law in every case involving a PERA official. It clarified that while offences punishable under the special law must be dealt with through the procedure prescribed therein, allegations independently attracting provisions of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) cannot be excluded from consideration without examining their legal character.
The ruling came on the petition filed by Tauqeer Asif, a PERA official, challenging an order of an ex-officio justice of peace dated August 29. The order had directed the station house officer concerned to record the version of the complainant and proceed in accordance with law if a cognisable offence was made out.
According to the allegations before the court, the complainant claimed that the petitioner, accompanied by eight to 10 unidentified PERA officials, had subjected him to physical torture, forcibly taken him to Ferozwala police station and later shifted him to an undisclosed location, where he had been stripped and tortured.
The complainant also alleged that the officials had recorded a video of the incident, snatched Rs25,200 from his pocket and threatened him with dire consequences if he disclosed the matter.
He relied on a medico-legal certificate issued by a hospital in support of his claim of having suffered injuries.
The petitioner argued that the Punjab Enforcement and Regulation Act provided a special statutory mechanism for dealing with complaints and offences involving PERA officials, making the ordinary procedure for registration of an FIR under Section 154 of the Criminal Procedure Code unavailable.
His counsel relied on an earlier LHC judgment, arguing that Sections 16, 49 and 53 of the act provided the relevant remedies for grievances arising from the conduct of PERA officials.
Rejecting the argument that the earlier ruling barred recourse to ordinary criminal law in every such case, Justice Zahid observed that the judgment had to be understood in the context of the offences and statutory provisions examined in that matter. Its principle could not be extended indiscriminately to every alleged offence committed by a PERA official, irrespective of whether the conduct independently constituted a crime under general criminal law.
The court explained that Section 16 provides a mechanism for representations against specified enforcement actions, Section 49 deals with the procedure relating to offences punishable under the act and Section 53 provides a complaint mechanism against misuse of authority by PERA officials.
These provisions must be given effect in matters falling within their scope, but their existence does not justify treating every allegation of violence or other criminal conduct as exclusively governed by the special law, the judge observed.
The court noted that the complainant's allegations went beyond a grievance against an enforcement measure, such as a fine, confiscation, sealing of premises or removal of an encroachment.

Investigations are under way to identify and arrest the suspects' alleged accomplices, facilitators and financial backers, while further operations are also being conducted, the spokesperson added.

title: Rabies claims another life as boy battles infection | The Express Tribune
description:
Rabies claims another life 
as boy battles infection
content:
Tharparkar man dies at Indus Hospital, taking province-wide death toll to 38
Two months after a dog bite went untreated, a 12-year-old boy from Hyderabad is now battling suspected rabies encephalitis in Karachi, as the deadly disease continues to claim lives across Sindh.
The boy's case comes as a 38-year-old man from Tharparkar succumbed to rabies at Indus Hospital Karachi, despite receiving four doses of the anti-rabies vaccine. His death has pushed the province's toll from the fatal disease to 38 this year.
The two cases underscore the persistent threat posed by dog bites and the critical importance of timely medical care, including proper wound cleaning and appropriate post-exposure treatment.
Of the 38 deaths reported this year, 29 occurred at Indus Hospital Karachi, eight at Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC) and one at Indus Hospital Badin.
According to JPMC's administration, the boy was brought to the emergency department with hydrophobia and irritability. He had been bitten by a dog on his hand and chest around two months ago but had not received the rabies vaccine following the attack.
A neuromedicine team was called in after doctors suspected rabies encephalitis. The boy was administered the first dose of the vaccine in the emergency department and is being admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for further treatment and monitoring, hospital officials said.
JPMC Chief Medical Officer Dr Ammar Danish said the government had launched awareness campaigns and various programmes to prevent rabies, but public awareness remained inadequate.
He said the stray dog population was growing, while dog-bite incidents were also increasing rapidly. Raising public awareness and ensuring compliance with preventive measures were essential to saving lives, he added.
Dr Danish advised citizens to immediately wash dog-bite or scratch wounds thoroughly with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical attention at the nearest hospital without delay.
He stressed that rabies vaccination and, where medically indicated, rabies immunoglobulin were essential to prevent the disease. People should avoid applying chilli, oil or other home remedies to wounds and must seek treatment without waiting for symptoms to appear, he added.
Meanwhile, an Indus Hospital Karachi spokesperson said the deceased, identified as Naimatullah, 38, belonged to Nohriyo village in Diplo tehsil of Tharparkar district.
Naimatullah had been bitten by a dog around two and a half months ago. He received four doses of the rabies vaccine at the Tehsil Headquarters Hospital in Diplo between July 25 and August 8.
He was admitted to Indus Hospital Karachi on October 7 after developing rabies symptoms. An initial medical assessment indicated that the wound had not been properly cleaned, hospital officials said. The patient subsequently died.
According to the spokesperson, more than 15,000 dog-bite patients have been brought to Indus Hospital Karachi this year, while the number of rabies deaths at the facility has reached 29.
One rabies death has also been reported at Indus Hospital Badin this year, while JPMC Karachi has recorded eight fatalities, taking Sindh's overall rabies death toll to 38.

title: Mental health gap leaves communities unsupported
description: Mental health gap leaves communities unsupported
content:
Sindh has no mental health policy for the past five years with specialists serving only 10 districts
For someone battling depression, anxiety, or another mental health disorder, finding help in Sindh can be as difficult as living with the illness itself. Where a person lives can determine whether a specialist is within reach or whether they have to struggle without one.
Mental-health specialists are concentrated in just 10 districts of the province, while the remaining districts have no reported specialist services. With around 140 mental health professionals serving Sindh, access to psychiatric and psychological care remains severely limited outside major urban centres.
The shortage is compounded by the absence of a provincial mental health policy for the past five years. Experts say the lack of a comprehensive policy has also contributed to inadequate data, making it difficult to determine the true scale of mental health disorders or assess services required across the province.
Dr Karim Khawaja, Honorary Chairman of the Sindh Mental Health Authority, said more than 30 per cent of Pakistan's population suffers from depression and other mental and psychological disorders. He said there were around 600 mental health professionals across Pakistan, including 140 in Sindh, but those in Sindh were available in only 10 districts.
"The remaining districts do not have these specialists," he said, highlighting the geographic gap in mental health care. People living outside these districts may have to travel to larger cities for diagnosis and treatment, creating another barrier for families already facing financial difficulties and other social pressures.
The problem is particularly significant as mental health disorders are believed to be increasing across Pakistan. According to experts, the number of people suffering from mental health disorders has increased by around 15 per cent over the past five years, while more than 30 per cent of the population is estimated to suffer from depression and other psychological disorders.
But the absence of reliable provincial data makes it difficult to establish the scale of the problem in Sindh.
Professor Dr Muhammad Iqbal Afridi, Distinguished National & Meritorious Professor (HEC), said one in every three people in Pakistan, compared with one in every five globally, suffered from some form of psychological illness. "Depression is increasingly being reported among men and women, with domestic conflict and other social pressures contributing to psychological problems among women," noted Dr Afridi.
Young people are also facing growing pressures. Professor Afridi said Pakistan's economic situation, unemployment, terrorism and uncertainty about the future were affecting their mental health. He also pointed to increasing exposure to ice and other addictive substances, as well as excessive use of digital platforms.
Professor Wajid Ali Akhunzada, President of the Pakistan Psychiatric Society, said one in every four young people and one in every five children in Pakistan suffered from some form of psychological illness. He confirmed that the country faced a severe shortage of psychiatric specialists and needed greater investment in mental health services.
Experts say Sindh needs a policy framework covering prevention, early diagnosis, treatment, referrals, specialist training, and data collection. Better data could help identify districts with the greatest need and guide the deployment of additional mental-health professionals and facilities.
For many in Sindh, the hardest part of fighting a mental-health disorder may be finding someone qualified to help. Until care reaches beyond major cities, too many people will be left to struggle in silence, with help out of reach when they need it most.

title: Ghost nets  a deadly trap for marine life
description: Ghost nets  a deadly trap for marine life
content:
Two rare olive ridley turtles rescued off Jiwani
Lost at sea, forgotten by fishermen but still killing indiscriminately, discarded fishing nets continue to haunt marine life along the country's coastline.
Two rare olive ridley sea turtles recently fell victim to the underwater menace near Guns, a coastal settlement close to Jiwani in Balochistan. The turtles, trapped in a strong nylon net, were rescued by fishermen who freed them and returned them to the open sea.
The incident has once again drawn attention to the threat posed by so-called ghost nets - abandoned, discarded or accidentally lost fishing gear that continues to ensnare marine creatures long after it has been left behind.
The latest rescue was the 37th reported incident of olive ridley turtles becoming entangled in fishing nets along the coast over the past 15 years, according to Muhammad Moazzam Khan, technical adviser at the World Wide Fund for Nature-Pakistan (WWF-Pakistan).
Thirty-six such incidents had been documented previously, with the number of turtles trapped ranging from one or two to four in a single incident, Khan said.
He explained that the drifting nets involved in the latest incident were not used in Pakistan. However, changing wind patterns carry large numbers of such nets into the region, where they drift across the sea and threaten marine life.
Between October and December, winds shift from east to west, transporting the nets from one area to another and increasing the risk of entanglement along different stretches of the coast, he added.
Fishing nets can become damaged or unusable over time. While some are accidentally lost at sea, others are deliberately discarded by fishermen instead of being stored on boats or brought ashore for proper disposal. Once abandoned, the nets continue to catch marine animals, earning them the name ghost nets.
Marine creatures trapped in the nets often become more entangled as they struggle to escape. Their movement becomes restricted, leaving them vulnerable to injury and death.
Sea turtles face a particularly grave danger because they must periodically surface to breathe. When entangled in a net, they may be unable to reach the water's surface, eventually drowning.
The threat extends beyond turtles to fish, crabs and other marine organisms, including marine mammals. Ghost nets can remain in the sea for long periods, adding to plastic pollution and damaging the marine ecosystem.
Their movement also makes them difficult to track and retrieve. Ocean currents, waves and winds carry the discarded gear across different locations, exposing marine life in multiple coastal areas to the same danger.
Olive ridley turtles are an important component of the marine ecosystem. Compared with some other sea turtle species, they spend relatively more time near the surface, making them especially vulnerable to floating nets.
Khan said olive ridley turtles had not been visiting the Karachi and Balochistan coasts for breeding for a long time. However, their numbers in the Arabian Sea remain higher than those of green sea turtles.

title: Cricket stadium plan faces legal challenge
description: Cricket stadium plan faces legal challenge
content:
IHC issues notices to PCB, CDA; petitioners raise concerns over wildlife and green zones
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Monday issued notices to the federal government, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), the Capital Development Authority (CDA) and other relevant authorities, seeking their responses to an intra-court appeal challenging the dismissal of a petition against plans to construct an international cricket stadium and establish a sports arena in the federal capital.
A division bench comprising Justice Inaam Ameen Minhas and Justice Shah Rukh Arjumand heard the appeal filed by Hamid Nawaz and Muhammad Khurram Javed. The respondents named in the proceedings include the federal government, the PCB, the CDA, the Chief Commissioner of Islamabad, the Ministry of Climate Change and the Chairperson of the Islamabad Wildlife Management Board.
In their appeal, the petitioners argued that the proposed project would involve land in Zone III of Islamabad, including Sector D-12 and the village of Shah Allah Ditta.
They maintained that the project required careful scrutiny of its potential environmental impact, particularly its implications for wildlife, natural landscapes and ecological preservation. They also argued that relevant international legal obligations, including the United Nations Charter, should be taken into consideration.
According to the petitioners, land had initially been allocated in Sector D-12 for the construction of a stadium. The project was subsequently expanded into a proposed Olympic Village incorporating a football ground, a hockey stadium and other sporting facilities.
They contended that the expanded development would require substantially more land than had originally been allocated and could adversely affect natural landscapes, biodiversity, ecosystems and wildlife.
The petitioners further argued that the construction would transform green areas into built-up zones, potentially causing significant environmental damage.
They asked the court to set aside the single bench's order upholding the decision to allocate land for the cricket stadium. They also sought to have the electronic bidding process, procurement procedures and all related arrangements declared unlawful and quashed.
The appeal challenges an earlier decision by a single-member bench of the Islamabad High Court, which dismissed the two petitioners' plea against the proposed construction of a stadium and sports arena in the capital.
The court has sought responses from the respondents. Further proceedings will determine the issues raised in the appeal.

title: Riot force retained amid police pullback
description: Riot force retained amid police pullback
content:
Authorities decide to withdraw additional personnel as security situation improves
Authorities have decided to withdraw additional police personnel deployed in Attock, Mianwali and Rawalpindi in phases following the improvement in the law and order situation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa after the imposition of emergency measures and governor's rule.
However, the specialised Riot Management Force, trained to handle unrest in Islamabad and Rawalpindi, will remain deployed at its current locations until further orders.
More than 29,000 additional police personnel were deployed in Attock, around 22,000 in Islamabad and over 5,000 in Rawalpindi to assist the district police in maintaining law and order and dealing with the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's planned long march and sit-in.
According to sources, senior authorities have issued directives to force commanders and relevant officials to begin the phased withdrawal of personnel from Attock, Mianwali and Rawalpindi as conditions return to normal. The withdrawal schedule and procedure will be finalised in consultation with the regional police officers (RPOs), city police officers (CPOs) and district police officers (DPOs) concerned.
The instructions require strict adherence to the agreed schedule, with personnel to remain deployed at their current locations with all necessary facilities until their withdrawal. Police contingents will be recalled in three phases, and the process is expected to begin on Monday evening.
The removal of containers and temporary barricades installed at various locations also began in phases on Monday.
Before withdrawing the personnel, officials have been directed to complete records of deployed officers, vehicles and other equipment. Senior police commanders have also been instructed to maintain security and operational readiness until the withdrawal process is completed.
Meanwhile, the decision to retain the Anti-Riot Management Force in Rawalpindi and Islamabad reflects the authorities' intention to maintain preparedness for any potential law and order situation.
Officials have also acknowledged the services of police officers and personnel who have performed prolonged and demanding duties during the security operation, stressing that the withdrawal of other contingents must be carried out in a safe, organised and coordinated manner.

title: Key accused arrested in child  rape  case
description: Key accused arrested in child  rape  case
content:
Relative accused of assaulting 8-year-old girl during family wedding visit
Police have arrested the main suspect in a child sexual abuse case involving an eight-year-old girl in the Sadiqabad area of Rawalpindi, while other relatives accused of concealing the alleged offence and threatening the child into silence have yet to be arrested.
According to the complainant, Nauman Ejaz, who belongs to Lahore, he sent his two daughters, aged eight and six, to Rawalpindi on September 23 to attend the wedding of the sister of the nominated suspect, Haider Ali. The girls travelled with their paternal grandmother.
The complainant alleged that, after returning to Lahore, his eight-year-old daughter, a fourth-grade pupil who was also studying the Holy Quran by heart, told her mother that she was experiencing severe pain in her private parts. She alleged that, on the night of September 25, while she was asleep at the house of Haider Ali's maternal grandmother, Parveen Akhtar, the suspect took her to another room and sexually assaulted her.
According to the complaint, the girl said she woke up because of the pain and screamed, but the suspect covered her mouth and threatened to kill her if she told her grandmother or anyone else about the incident.
The family subsequently took the child to a female gynaecologist, who advised them to seek an examination at a government hospital and register a case against those responsible, the complainant said.
He further alleged that the girl had initially told her paternal grandmother, Zahida Parveen, about the incident. The grandmother reportedly informed Parveen Akhtar, who then called the suspect's mother, Uzma, and his maternal aunt, Shaista, and told them what had happened.
The complainant alleged that the relatives attempted to suppress the matter, saying that the family was preparing for a wedding and that disclosing the incident would disrupt the celebrations and damage the child's reputation. He further claimed that the girl and her grandmother were subjected to intimidation and that the child was repeatedly pressured not to tell her parents after returning to Lahore.
The complainant accused other family members of helping to conceal the alleged offence and sought legal action against them. Police registered a case and arrested the main suspect during the investigation. The other relatives nominated in the complaint, including women, have not yet been arrested.

title: Twin cities clear roadblocks
description: Twin cities clear roadblocks
content:
Move brings relief to commuters, transporters and traders
Authorities have accelerated the removal of hundreds of shipping containers and other barricades placed along key roads, entry and exit points, and around sensitive locations in Rawalpindi and Islamabad over the past two to three weeks, following an improvement in the law and order situation.
Containers had been positioned at 26 locations along major routes, including GT Road, the motorway, Margalla Avenue and Airport Road, to deal with potential protests and prevent any deterioration in law and order. The containers are now being removed in phases and returned to the companies concerned.
The move has brought relief to residents, traders and transporters, who had been concerned about possible road closures and disruptions to daily activities.
According to details, the Rawalpindi and Islamabad administrations had deployed hundreds of containers as a precautionary measure after the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) and Jamaat-e-Islami announced protest marches. The containers were placed along roadsides and at adjoining locations rather than directly across roads, allowing authorities to move them onto the carriageways at short notice if protests or security concerns arose.
The containers were positioned at several key locations, including Rawat T-Chowk, GT Road, Mall Road, Peshawar Road, Murree Road, motorway entry and exit points, Margalla Avenue, Airport Road and Faizabad Interchange. While some had remained in place for around two weeks, containers near Faizabad Interchange had been there for nearly three weeks.
Following the improvement in the security situation, containers have been removed from Rawat T-Chowk, Mall Road, Peshawar Road and areas around Murree Road. The process has also begun at Faizabad Interchange, a major traffic hub connecting the twin cities.
Thousands of commuters, government and private-sector employees, students, passengers and freight vehicles use the interchange daily. The complete removal of the containers is expected to further improve traffic flow and facilitate movement between Rawalpindi and Islamabad.
Heavy machinery and transport vehicles are being used to lift and relocate the containers, which are being returned to their respective companies. Traffic is flowing on major roads across the twin cities, with residents travelling to their destinations as usual.
Residents, transporters and business representatives have welcomed the removal of the barricades. They said the prolonged presence of containers along major roads had created uncertainty and raised fears of sudden closures, particularly among people travelling daily between Rawalpindi and Islamabad for work, business and education.
Transporters said the possibility of abrupt road closures had threatened to disrupt passenger services and freight movement.

President Asif Ali Zardari has called for regional cooperation and global initiatives to strengthen disaster risk reduction, stressing the need to shift from disaster response to preparedness.

He said the country had learned that preparedness is essential and that the traditional approach of responding after a disaster strikes is no longer sufficient.
The president said Pakistan was transforming its disaster management system by using artificial intelligence, satellite technology and real-time data to identify emerging threats, issue early warnings and help communities move to safety before disasters struck.
Emphasising the role of local governments and communities, he said local administrations and community volunteers were often the first to respond during emergencies because of their familiarity with local terrain and populations.
He called upon national and international organisations to make disaster preparedness a core component of their work, adding that Pakistan's experience could offer valuable lessons to the international community.

title: FCC rulings binding on all courts  including SC
description: FCC rulings binding on all courts  including SC
content:
Orders IIUI to reconsider female student's PhD extension request
The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has reiterated that its decisions on questions of law are binding on all courts in Pakistan, including the Supreme Court.
The observation came in a 24-page judgment authored by Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi while deciding a petition filed by a female student whose request for an extension to submit her PhD thesis had been rejected by the International Islamic University Islamabad (IIUI).
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) had also dismissed her petition.
A division bench of the FCC led by Justice Rizvi held that Article 189 of the Constitution gives binding effect to the law declared by the court on all other courts, including the Supreme Court, and places a corresponding responsibility on the FCC to maintain consistency and coherence in its own jurisprudence.
"A principle of law enunciated by an earlier bench of this Court should, therefore, ordinarily be followed by a subsequent bench of lesser or co-equal strength," the judgment stated.
It added that a bench should not depart from, overrule or adopt a view inconsistent with an earlier pronouncement merely because it considers another interpretation preferable.
Where a subsequent bench doubts the correctness of an earlier judgment and considers reconsideration necessary, it should record its reasons and request the chief justice to constitute a larger bench for an authoritative determination, the court said.
The judgment also clarified the scope of judicial review in matters involving universities, holding that respect for academic autonomy does not place every decision taken by an educational institution beyond constitutional scrutiny.
The court observed that constitutional courts ordinarily exercise restraint in matters involving academic judgment. However, the principle applies to the nature of the decision rather than merely to the status of the institution making it.
An assessment of a thesis, research work or academic merit, involving specialised expertise, ordinarily warrants judicial deference, the judgment said. Administrative or regulatory decisions, however, stand on a different footing and remain open to judicial review regarding legality, jurisdiction, procedural fairness and compliance with the applicable legal framework.
"Academic autonomy and judicial review are, therefore, not mutually exclusive," the court observed, explaining that academic autonomy protects the substantive domain of academic judgment, while judicial review ensures that public power is exercised within the bounds prescribed by law.
It added that judicial restraint preserves the legitimate sphere of academic autonomy but does not amount to abandoning the constitutional responsibility to ensure the lawful exercise of power.
The FCC also highlighted the constitutional guarantees of equality and the protection of women, observing that circumstances affecting women's educational progression may warrant reasonable accommodation within the applicable legal and policy framework.
Referring to Article 25 of the Constitution, the court noted that equality before the law does not invariably require identical treatment. The constitutional provision also permits special measures for the protection of women and children.
The judgment observed that women pursuing higher education may have to reconcile their academic progress with marriage, relocation arising from matrimonial obligations, pregnancy, health-related concerns, motherhood and childcare responsibilities.
Where such circumstances materially impede the continuity of education, they deserve due consideration within the flexibility available under the governing rules and policies, it said.
The court added that reasonable accommodation in such cases does not constitute a departure from equality but may help remove disadvantages that impede women's educational advancement and their effective participation in professional and public life.
Such consideration assumes greater significance where the accommodation is permissible under the applicable framework and does not adversely affect an accrued or competing right of a third party, the judgment stated, referring also to Article 34 of the Constitution, which calls for the full participation of women in all spheres of national life.
Applying these principles to the petitioner's case, the FCC observed that her request for an extension had not been considered in the manner contemplated by the applicable legal and policy framework, particularly clause 3.12(iv) of the Higher Education Commission's 2023 policy.

title: Afridi  some of his cabinet members in preventive custody
description: Afridi  some of his cabinet members in preventive custody
content:
Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry confirmed on Monday that former Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) chief minister Sohail Afridi and some of his cabinet members had been "taken into preventive custody," following the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in the province.
"Yes, I can confirm that the chief minister (Sohail Afridi) and some of his cabinet members have been taken into preventive custody," Chaudhry told Reuters.
If any of them have any cases to be tried against them, they will be charged and tried but the others will be released, he said, adding that the detentions happened on Sunday.
A day earlier, K-P Information Minister Shafi Jan claimed that Afridi had been arrested and urged people across the province to gather in Peshawar. However, at the time, no government official had confirmed his arrest or detention.
Meanwhile, the Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Police in Peshawar said Afridi remained in police protective custody.
The DIG added that eight senior PTI leaders had been taken into protective custody following the imposition of emergency measures and governor's rule in K-P. Those detained included Afridi, Junaid Akbar and K-P Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, he said.
"Separately, 169 PTI workers were arrested in a crackdown in Swabi. The arrests were carried out in Shewa Adda, Yar Hussain, Razar, Swabi Khas, Topi, Lahor and Gadoon, among other areas of the district," the DIG said.
According to the DIG, those arrested included several local office-bearers and active PTI workers, saying that they were taken into custody over concerns that preparations for the party's long march, which began on October 4, could disrupt law and order.
The DIG added that a heavy police contingent had been deployed across Swabi and that further arrests were expected.

title: PM forms 11 member panel to monitor K P
description: PM forms 11 member panel to monitor K P
content:
FM Ishaq Dar to head monitoring committee
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday constituted an 11-member monitoring committee for Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) to oversee governance, law and order, and day-to-day affairs in the province, according to sources.
Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar has been appointed convener of the committee, which includes Rana Sanaullah, Azam Nazeer Tarar, Ahsan Iqbal, Amir Muqam, Tariq Fazal Chaudhry and Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui, the sources said.
The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), the Balochistan Awami Party (BAP) and the Istehkam-e-Pakistan Party (IPP – the allied parties of the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) at the Centre – will each have one representative on the committee, they added.
On Sunday, the federal government took control of the K-P affairs after imposing an emergency and governor's rule in the province, deploying the army to assist the civil administration, forming an 11-member advisory council and establishing a special administrative structure for 12 districts.
The emergency followed an increasingly strained relationship between the federal government and the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led provincial administration, particularly over counterterrorism policy and engagement with the Afghan Taliban.
The prime minister has summoned a meeting of the parliamentary parties of the PML-N and its coalition partners for Tuesday (today) to take them into confidence over the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in K-P.
According to Express News, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi will brief the participants on the security situation, while Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar will explain the legal aspects of the decisions. Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry will brief them on the agenda for the parliamentary session.
The premier directed the authorities concerned to develop the Daanish IT Park Islamabad into a world-class hub of technology and transform it into a centre of a modern IT ecosystem through effective collaboration between academia and industry.
Chairing a meeting to discuss matters related to the Daanish IT Park Islamabad, he said that the government would continue its efforts to equip Pakistani youth with modern skills in IT, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and FinTech, besides creating new opportunities for IT entrepreneurs.
He instructed the Ministry of Information Technology to conduct a comprehensive case study of the project.
The prime minister directed to operationalise Daanish IT Park in partnership with global technology companies, and carry out a third-party audit of the project.
During the meeting, a briefing was given on the creation of a comprehensive ecosystem aimed at boosting IT exports and promoting investment in the sector.
The prime minister called for increasing the small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) from Rs1.1 trillion to Rs2.2 trillion by 2028, underscoring their potential to drive economic growth and create business opportunities across the country.

title: Shaza calls for global laws to protect children online
description: Shaza calls for global laws to protect children online
content:
Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja on Monday called for global laws to protect children from the harmful effects of the internet.
Addressing the "Safe Scroll: Protecting Our Children Online" event, she said children's interest in information technology was growing worldwide, with even young children achieving major milestones in the field.
Children could not be kept away from information technology, she added.
Shaza Fatima said there was a need to determine the appropriate level of internet access and screen time for children and establish clear limits.
She said several countries, particularly 20 to 25 member states of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), were considering frameworks and laws to regulate children's use of social media and the internet.
Australia, Malaysia and Thailand were among the countries taking steps in this direction.
The minister said governments alone could not verify the age of every child online or fully monitor their activities. Therefore, major technology companies and digital platforms also needed to take responsibility for age verification and content monitoring through artificial intelligence (AI) and other advanced tools.
Highlighting awareness initiatives, she said the Ministry of IT had launched the "Safe Raho" programme in collaboration with Google, focusing on parental controls and family safety.
She said 12,500 students, teachers and parents had received digital safety training in 100 public schools through a joint initiative involving Telenor and the National Cyber Crime Research Centre (NCRC).
She added that progress had also been made in collaboration with Meta to introduce stricter AI-based controls for children's accounts.
Meanwhile, the "Junior Cyber Heroes" initiative, launched in collaboration with PK-CERT and UNICEF, was raising awareness among children about online safety.

title: Gohar to move PHC against K P emergency
description: Gohar to move PHC against K P emergency
content:
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Monday said he would personally challenge the emergency and governor's rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) in the Peshawar High Court on Tuesday (today), as the party vowed to continue its long march.
Speaking at a press conference outside Parliament alongside Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Opposition Leader in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, Gohar said the party would decide at its parliamentary party meeting on Tuesday how to oppose the measures in the provincial assembly.
"We will raise our voices on every forum. Our long march is ongoing, and our protests are continuing. We will not accept this," he said, adding that the demonstrations would continue.
Gohar called October 11 a "black day" in Pakistan's democratic history, saying the people of K-P had rejected emergency measures and governor's rule, and that the provincial chief minister had been kept in custody and claimed that supporters of the party were in jail.
"We demand that the measures taken on October 11 be withdrawn," he said, adding that the party would challenge the decision through all channels. He said he would personally challenge the decisions taken on October 11 in the Peshawar High Court, adding that the party was also pursuing a legal challenge.
The PTI chairman accused the government of showing stubbornness and said the provincial government machinery had been changed abruptly. He said the party had remained in contact with the government until the very last moment, but the situation had deteriorated.
"The federation will be strong only when the provinces are strong," he said.
Gohar urged the government not to divide the public in the fight against terrorism, calling terrorism a "menace for Pakistan". He said Pakistan's future lay in democracy and that the federation would only be strong when its provinces were strong.
The federal government's decision to impose emergency measures and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was challenged in the Peshawar High Court on Monday.
The petitioner prayed the court to declare the move unconstitutional and suspend the governor's rule notification pending a final verdict.
The petition, filed by Advocate Salman, names President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi as respondents.
It contended that the federal action was unconstitutional, illegal and mala fide.
It further argues that the measure violates fundamental rights, provincial autonomy, the democratic mandate and established constitutional principles.
The petitioner has asked the court to declare the measures null and void and suspend the notification imposing governor's rule until the case is decided.
The plea maintains that the federal government's intervention infringes upon the rights of the province and its elected representatives and runs contrary to democratic and constitutional norms.
The federal government announced the imposition of emergency measures and governor's rule in K-P on October 11, citing the deteriorating law and order situation and an increase in terrorist incidents in the province.
The measures were imposed under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution.

Weighs summoning officials over sisters' detention
The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Monday directed jail authorities to provide heart medication to Dr Uzma Khanum, sister of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan, while reserving its decision on a request to summon the deputy commissioner, Lahore CCPO and other officials in person over the detention of Khan's sisters.
Justice Abher Gul Khan heard petitions challenging the detention of Noreen Niazi and Dr Uzma Khanum.
During the hearing, the petitioners' counsel sought the appearance of the relevant officials to explain the detention notifications and requested that the detainees be allowed access to essential medicines, clothes, spectacles, family members and lawyers.
The petitioners' counsel, Rana Mudassar Umar, told the court that the situation would become clear if the concerned officials appeared and explained the detention notifications.
He said the petitioners were not seeking any special facilities in jail but only basic necessities.
Dr Uzma Khanum's husband, Ahad Khan, appeared before the court and submitted that his wife suffered from a heart condition and needed three medicines daily. He requested that the medicines be delivered to her regularly in jail.
Rana Mudassar Umar also requested permission for Noreen Niazi to receive clothes, medicines and her spectacles, describing these as basic necessities and fundamental rights. He further sought permission for the detainees to meet their family members and lawyers in jail.
The counsel requested that the deputy commissioner, Lahore CCPO, SP and other relevant officials be summoned in person to explain the detentions.
After hearing the arguments, the court directed that Dr Uzma Khanum be provided with her medicines and reserved its decision on the request to summon the officials.

title: Malik calls for stronger Saudi energy cooperation
description: Malik calls for stronger Saudi energy cooperation
content:
Petroleum minister reaffirms solidarity with KSA
Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik on Monday said Pakistan stood shoulder to shoulder with Saudi Arabia during its current difficulties, condemning Houthi attacks on Saudi territory and expressing solidarity with the Kingdom.
"Pakistan strongly condemns the terrorist attacks by the Houthi militia on Saudi soil," Malik said, while offering condolences over the loss of precious lives.
He made the remarks while addressing a plenary session titled "Investment and Trade in Sustainable Energy Solutions: Making Energy Clean, Accessible and Affordable" at the 17th International Energy Forum (IEF) Ministerial Meeting in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
According to a statement, Malik attended the meeting at the invitation of Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud. His participation, he said, reflected Pakistan's solidarity with the Kingdom, in line with the instructions of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir.
Addressing the forum, Malik said the global energy sector was entering a new investment cycle in which energy security, affordability and sustainability needed to advance together.
He stressed the need for investment not only in renewable energy but also in hydrocarbons, critical minerals and essential infrastructure, including electricity grids and pipelines.
Referring to the unprecedented global energy supply shock of 2026, the minister said the crisis had extended beyond oil and gas to affect shipping and insurance.
Despite its heavy reliance on imported energy, Pakistan had navigated the crisis without rationing major energy sources, supported by the government's response and cooperation from friendly countries, including Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Kuwait, he said.
Malik also thanked Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman for personally steering energy cooperation with Pakistan.
On the sidelines of the IEF ministerial meeting, Malik met Libyan Minister of Oil and Gas Khalifa Rajab Abdulsadek to discuss ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in the oil and gas sector.
The petroleum minister informed his Libyan counterpart that Pakistan had encouraged its refineries to explore importing Libyan crude oil as part of efforts to diversify supply sources and strengthen energy security.
He said Pakistan aimed to maintain alternative supply options in the event of disruptions to key maritime routes, including the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
Malik also held a detailed breakfast meeting with Qatar's Energy Minister Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi to explore potential cooperation in the liquefied natural gas (LNG) sector.
Separately, Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar met Malik on the sidelines of the forum.

title: 2 army pilots martyred in Quetta crash
description: 2 army pilots martyred in Quetta crash
content:
Two Pakistan Army pilots were martyred on Monday when a Mushshak training aircraft crashed near Nawan Killi in Quetta due to a technical fault, the military's media wing said.
"Both pilots, Major Husnain Shehzad Humayun (Instructor Pilot) and Captain Abdul Samad (Student Pilot) embraced Shahadat in the unfortunate crash," the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement.
It said that the aircraft crashed around midday on 12 October.
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed grief over the martyrdom of the pilots. In separate statements, the president and the prime minister extended their heartfelt condolences and sympathies to the bereaved families and prayed for the elevation of the martyrs' ranks.
The president, in his statement, expressed heartfelt condolences and sympathies to the families of the martyrs.
Shehbaz said the country's brave sons who sacrificed their lives for Pakistan were a source of pride for the nation. He added that the entire nation held their sacrifices in high regard and shared the grief of their families.
The prime minister prayed that Almighty grant the martyrs a place in His mercy and give their families the strength to bear the irreparable loss.
On June 10, a Pakistan Army Aviation Mi-17 helicopter crashed near Muzaffarabad during take-off due to a technical fault, martyring all personnel on board. The military's media wing said a board of inquiry had been ordered to determine the exact cause of the accident.
On September 2, 2025, an Army Aviation Mi-17 helicopter also crashed near Hudor village in Gilgit-Baltistan during a routine training flight after developing a technical fault; five crew members, including two pilots, were martyred, the ISPR said.

title: Dar warns Afghan Taliban of terrorism costs
description: Dar warns Afghan Taliban of terrorism costs
content:
DPM urges Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Monday issued a warning to the Afghan Taliban regime, saying its failure to act against terrorist groups operating from its soil could ultimately have consequences for Afghanistan itself.
Speaking at an international conference on Pakistan's evolving counterterrorism landscape, Dar said Islamabad had exhausted sustained diplomatic efforts to persuade the Taliban authorities to address Pakistan's security concerns but had yet to see results on its central demand.
"What does Pakistan ask? Only one. Please do not allow your soil to be used against any country, particularly Pakistan, for terrorism," Dar said.
He said Pakistan wanted a stable and prosperous Afghanistan and had repeatedly demonstrated that commitment through political engagement, economic cooperation and regional connectivity initiatives.
But, he added, Islamabad could no longer ignore what it regarded as a growing terrorist threat emanating from Afghan territory. "If the Afghan government does not take action against terrorists, one day it will have to face the consequences itself," Dar warned.
His remarks at the Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad (ISSI) conference represented one of Pakistan's clearest public warnings to the Taliban authorities amid a sharp deterioration in relations between the two neighbours.
Dar recalled that he travelled to Kabul in April 2025 after what he described as a four-year stalemate in high-level engagement and held detailed discussions with acting Afghan PM Mullah Mohammad Hassan Akhund, Deputy PM Abdul Ghani Baradar and Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi.
He said Pakistan subsequently followed through on commitments made during those discussions. Further engagement included another visit involving the Uzbek foreign minister and the Pakistan-China-Afghanistan trilateral dialogue in Kabul in August 2025.
"These were the sincere efforts on behalf of Pakistan," Dar said. "But the one ask, we are not seeing a result, unfortunately, so far."
He said Pakistan had also upgraded diplomatic representation and supported plans for greater regional connectivity, including a proposed railway linking Pakistan and Uzbekistan through Afghanistan.
Despite those efforts, Dar said, attacks inside Pakistan continued to be planned, directed and launched from across the border. He said terrorists infiltrated through difficult mountainous terrain, attacked Pakistani soldiers and civilians and then returned to sanctuaries across the border.
"No fence can substitute for real action against these terrorist sanctuaries," he said, referring to Pakistan's investment in fencing and managing its border with Afghanistan.
Dar cited UN monitoring reports concerning the presence of the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) in Afghanistan and its links with Al-Qaeda, warning that the problem was not confined to Pakistan.
"A group that finds safe haven today to attack Pakistan can use the same safe haven tomorrow to threaten others," he said.
The government, he stressed, wanted the Afghan Taliban authorities to take "concrete, verifiable and irreversible" action against the TTP and other terrorist groups and ensure Afghan territory was not used against Pakistan or any other country.
Dar described the TTP as one of the gravest threats to Pakistan's security and said the group had been responsible for attacks on schools, mosques, markets and security installations.
He also accused India of sponsoring terrorist groups targeting Pakistan, including groups operating from Afghan territory. Dar said Pakistan had shared dossiers with the United Nations and international partners documenting what Islamabad described as Indian patronage of such organisations.
The deputy prime minister said more than 90,000 Pakistanis had lost their lives to terrorism while the country had suffered economic losses exceeding $150 billion.
He said Pakistan's sacrifices needed international recognition, but added that recognition alone was insufficient and called for greater international cooperation against terrorist networks.
Dar said Pakistan remained committed to fighting terrorism through the National Action Plan, Azm-e-Istehkam, stronger intelligence coordination and cooperation between the federation and provinces. "Pakistan's sacrifices deserve recognition, but recognition alone is not enough," he said.

title: Balochistan worse off than K P  says Achakzai
description: Balochistan worse off than K P  says Achakzai
content:
Balochistan worse off than K-P, says Achakzai
Criticizing the federal government for imposing emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) amid the PTI's long march, National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai said Balochistan had a stronger case for the imposition of emergency and governor's rule than K-P.
"If governor's rule is imposed in K-P due to the security situation, then the security situation in Balochistan is much worse," Achakzai said. He was addressing a press conference outside Parliament House alongside Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and others.
He claimed that half of Balochistan had become a no-go area for security forces, but no action was being taken against what he described as the exploitation of the province under the incumbent chief minister.
Achakzai's remarks came amid mounting opposition to the federal government's decision to impose emergency and governor's rule in K-P where Imran Khna's PTI had been in power for the last 13 years.
Achakzai, who also heads the opposition alliance Tehreek Tahafuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP), described Governor's Rule as a major assault on democracy and announced that the alliance would launch peaceful protests in every district from Tuesday, including those where emergency had not been imposed.
He said the opposition would continue its political struggle while keeping the door open to negotiations with the government. He also called for permission to meet incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, offering to submit a written undertaking that the delegation would not disclose details of the meeting.
"I am ready for negotiations for a democratic Pakistan," he said, rejecting claims that he was unwilling to meet the government. He added that he was prepared to meet at various places but not at the Prime Minister's House or the National Assembly speaker's office.
Accusing the government of denying the PTI even the space to express its grievances, Achakzai said the opposition had been raising concerns about the Constitution when emergency and governor's rule were imposed in the province.
He said Article 6 of the Constitution provided for action against those who abrogated or subverted the Constitution, and accused the government of using state power against political opponents.
Achakzai maintained that Pakistan could progress only if Parliament was strengthened and the people's right to vote respected. He alleged that the mandate of millions of voters had been undermined and called on opposition parties to mobilise against what he described as an undemocratic system.
Barrister Gohar Ali KHan, meanwhile, described October 11 as a dark day in the country's democratic history and said the people of K-P rejected the imposition of emergency and governor's rule.
He alleged that the provincial chief minister had been kept in custody and that the government had abruptly changed the administrative machinery in the province despite remaining in contact with the opposition until the last moment.
Gohar demanded the withdrawal of the measures announced on October 11, warning against dividing the public in the name of counter-terrorism. He said the PTI would raise its objections at every available forum and that the party's parliamentary group would meet to determine its future course of action.
"Pakistan's future lies in democracy, and the federation will be strong only when the provinces are strong," he said.
Raja Nasir Abbas also argued that Balochistan was facing a more serious situation and questioned why emergency rule had not been imposed there. He urged political forces to unite with the people against terrorism instead of equating political workers with terrorists.
Earlier, the TTAP leadership met at Parliament House to discuss the political situation, the imposition of emergency in K-P and the future course of action, including the proposed long march.
According to opposition sources, Achakzai urged the PTI and allied parties to continue their political struggle through judicial, parliamentary and public platforms. The leadership also discussed approaching courts to challenge the government's measures.
Despite announcing protests, Achakzai reiterated that the opposition remained willing to negotiate, provided it was allowed access to Imran Khan and the government demonstrated a willingness to address its concerns.

title: K P policy to be set in Islamabad  not Kabul  governor
description: K P policy to be set in Islamabad  not Kabul  governor
content:
Kundi co-chairs Apex Committee meeting with Naqvi Says counterterrorism and development top priorities Vows probe i
The federal and the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) governments on Monday pledged coordinated action against terrorism, promising to strengthen the police and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and accelerate development in the province following the imposition of emergency and governor's rule.
The commitment was made at a meeting of the Provincial Apex Committee at the Governor House, co-chaired by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Governor Faisal Karim Kundi. The meeting reviewed the security situation and measures to eradicate terrorism and establish lasting peace.
Speaking a press conference after the meeting, Governor Kundi said addressing problems that had accumulated over the past 13 years was a major challenge. He stressed that decisions concerning the province would henceforth be made in Islamabad, not Kabul.
The forum directed all relevant institutions to take "coordinated, effective and decisive" steps against terrorism, reiterating that intelligence-based operations (IBOs) would continue and all available resources would be utilised to improve law and order.
It decided to strengthen the operational capacity of the police and CTD by providing modern equipment, vehicles, armoured vehicles, weapons and the required manpower. Participants paid tribute to security personnel who had sacrificed their lives in the fight against terrorism and offered Fateha for the martyrs.
The meeting also agreed to prioritise long-standing public issues relating to education, healthcare, living standards and basic amenities, particularly in underdeveloped and affected areas. Public needs, local priorities and suggestions would be incorporated into policymaking.
Naqvi said the federal government would extend full support to the province in combating terrorism and strengthening its law-enforcement agencies. He said the fight against terrorism could be pursued more effectively if the provincial administration took the lead through firm, coordinated and sustained efforts.
He said 10 new armoured vehicles belonging to the Islamabad Police had been handed over to the K-P police on the directives of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. "The vehicles have been provided to strengthen counterterrorism operations in K-P," Naqvi added.
The interior minister said the security situation had deteriorated over the past two and a half years because of an ineffective counterterrorism approach. He added that the federal and provincial governments were now on the same page in their efforts to restore lasting peace.
Separately, Naqvi also chaired a meeting of the Area Development Secretariat (ADS) to review security, development requirements and public grievances in 12 designated districts, including the merged tribal districts, Bannu, Lakki Marwat, Tank and Dera Ismail Khan.
The meeting decided to provide immediate funds to support peace and development, stressing the timely completion of ongoing projects and the transparent and effective use of federal allocations. Participants also discussed measures to reduce unemployment and create job opportunities for young people.
The governor said security would remain the administration's first priority, followed by development. He stressed that the government would pursue practical, results-oriented measures rather than cosmetic steps and called for restoring freedom of movement in terrorism-affected districts.
Kundi later told reporters that a decision had been taken to investigate alleged corruption and irregular recruitment during the ousted Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) government. "Whether someone is small or powerful, anyone found involved in corruption will be arrested, punished and made to return the money."
The governor said the public had rejected the politics of chaos and that no one would now be allowed to engage in vandalism. He alleged that the PTI had supported terrorism, adding, "We have to eliminate terrorism. Now, policy will come from Islamabad, not Afghanistan," he said.
"The people of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa have made immense sacrifices in the fight against terrorism. The people of the province and the security institutions are united in this fight. This is our own war, and we must fight it together," he added.
Governor Kundi said addressing problems that had accumulated during the PTI's 13 years in power in the province was a major challenge, but efforts would be made over the next three months to improve and reform the system.
The governor said the federal cabinet had decided the previous day to establish an advisory council, whose members had all assumed their responsibilities. A security committee meeting had been held the previous day, while the Apex Committee meeting was convened on the first working day.
He made it clear that there would be no compromise on law and order in the province. He said the provincial government stood with the Pakistan Army, police, Frontier Constabulary (FC) and other law-enforcement agencies and would provide them with all necessary resources and facilities.
He said steps would be taken to equip the police with modern weapons and essential equipment. The government would also review proposals to increase the salaries of K-P police personnel and enhance the compensation package for the families of police martyrs.
Kundi said the federal interior minister had handed over 10 armoured personnel carrier (APC) vehicles to the K-P police. He added that pending projects aimed at strengthening the force's operational capacity would be completed soon.

title: PM warns tax dodgers of no concessions
description: PM warns tax dodgers of no concessions
content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday directed the completion and full operationalisation of the production monitoring systems for sales tax purposes across all manufacturing sectors by the end of this year to ensure effective enforcement of tax laws.
Chairing a review meeting on Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) reforms in Islamabad, the prime minister emphasised that production monitoring through cameras under the faceless taxation system was being made more effective, according to a press release issued by the Prime Minister's Office Media Wing.
The prime minister directed the removal of all hurdles in installing automated production monitoring systems. He said businesses that collected taxes from consumers but pocketed the money instead of depositing it into the national exchequer did not deserve any concessions.
"The government will take all necessary measures to realise the country's full tax potential and ensure effective enforcement of tax laws," he said. He appreciated manufacturing businesses that were voluntarily installing production monitoring systems in compliance with government measures.
The meeting was informed that production monitoring systems had been fully installed in the sugar, cement, tobacco, tiles and fertiliser sectors. Installation was under way in the textile, packaged water, packaged juice and packaged milk sectors.
Participants were also informed that procurement of equipment for the steel, poultry and tyre sectors would be completed by October 15, while procurement for the tea, household electronics, leather, paper and board, and oil and ghee sectors would be completed by October 30.
The systems were expected to become fully operational across all these manufacturing sectors by December 31. Participants were also briefed on resistance from some industries to installing monitoring systems in the textile sector.
The prime minister appreciated textile companies that had voluntarily installed the systems. He also commended the audit report on the production monitoring system in the cement sector and directed the Ministry of Information Technology to arrange audits of the systems in other sectors.
A comprehensive review report on the gap between the country's tax potential and actual tax collection was also presented at the meeting. It included an assessment of the additional revenue that could be generated through improved tax compliance and enforcement.
The meeting was informed that government measures had resulted in an additional Rs1.3 trillion in tax collection over the past three years, representing a 40% increase. The additional revenue had been generated through enforcement measures.
The prime minister commended the FBR Transformation Team for preparing a comprehensive assessment of the country's tax potential and identifying gaps between potential revenue and actual collection. At the end of the meeting, he awarded shields to officials involved in preparing the report.
The meeting was attended by Federal Ministers Azam Nazeer Tarar, Dr Musadik Malik, Ahad Khan Cheema and Shaza Fatima Khawaja, Minister of State Bilal Azhar Kayani, Prime Minister's Adviser Haroon Akhtar and other senior officials concerned.

title: French supermarket fridges hacked
description: French supermarket fridges hacked
content:
Hackers raised the temperature of refrigerators and freezers at hundreds of French supermarkets to as high as 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) overnight, causing fires and spoiling food.
The Paris prosecutor's office said on Monday that a "large-scale" attack was "affecting connected refrigerators in several major food retailers across France", leading to food losses and fires.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has instructed France's National Cybersecurity Agency to investigate, a person in his office said.
France was coordinating with European counterparts because other countries could also be affected, the person said, adding that authorities were assessing whether other French companies were at risk.
Felix Aime, a senior cyber threat intelligence analyst at Sekoia Threat Detection and Research, said Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany and Belgium had also been affected.
Carrefour said 80 of its supermarkets were hit, while Monoprix, which operates about 490 stores in France, said 5% of its stores were affected.
Les Mousquetaires, owner of retailer Intermarche, said fridges at around 150 of its stores were heated up to 50 C for six hours overnight. A spokesperson said all affected food had been discarded to eliminate health risks.
Paris resident Geert de Clercq witnessed staff at an Intermarche in central Paris throwing cartfuls of defrosted frozen foods into a giant trash container, with molten ice cream sloshing out of broken tubs on the street.
Cooperative U CEO Dominique Schelcher said his supermarket group had also been targeted.
"Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products and to the food supply of the French people is of extreme gravity and is unprecedented," he wrote on X.
Food retailers E.Leclerc and Auchan did not respond to requests for comment.

title: UK blames IRGC for airbase plot
description: UK blames IRGC for airbase plot
content:
Iran rejects any connection with Fairford incident
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday that a suspected plot targeting the RAF Fairford air base in Britain was "highly likely" to have been coordinated in Iran, and almost certainly directed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
The RAF Fairford base in southwest England, which had been used by US bombers to carry out strikes on Iran, became the focal point for a major security response after five British men were arrested nearby in the early hours of September 27 on suspected terrorism and explosive offences.
US officials have told Reuters that there had been a suspected plot involving Iran to launch a drone attack, and last week US President Donald Trump said a threat linked to Iran had prompted a decision to withdraw the bombers from the base.
"I can confirm our assessment that it is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard," Burnham told parliament.
Iran has rejected any connection with the Fairford incident.
"Tehran has had no involvement in this matter, and if the British government possesses any documents or evidence to support its claims, it should present them," said Iran's Ambassador to Britain, Seyed Ali Mousavi, according to Iran's state news agency IRNA.
Details around the suspected plot remain thin. The five detained men were later released without charge on police bail "under stringent conditions", and two other arrested men, including a British-Iranian national, have also been released.
Detectives have said petrol but no viable explosive had been found in vans seized along with the five men. However, both police and Burnham have pointed towards the involvement of a foreign state.

title: Political uncertainty grips Germany
description: Political uncertainty grips Germany
content:
Germany's labour minister and co-head of the centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) quit unexpectedly on Monday, adding to uncertainty around Chancellor Friedrich Merz's struggling coalition after bruising state election defeats last month.
Baerbel Bas said she was resigning from both positions to deal with grief over her stepdaughter's recent death.
She added that "public attacks against me, unfortunately also from within the ranks of our coalition partner," had made her situation unbearable.
Bas will be replaced as minister by Alexander Schweitzer, former state premier of the western state of Rhineland-Palatinate, and the whole of the SPD leadership will face re-election in a special party conference at the end of the year. While the departure of one minister was not expected to disrupt the overall government, it highlighted the turmoil facing Europe's largest economy.
Merz's coalition has been under growing pressure following state election victories for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) in eastern Germany last month, which it views as the first step towards victory in federal elections due in 2029.

title: India voter list protests escalate
description: India voter list protests escalate
content:
Opp marches to SC, seeks suspension of changes
Thousands of opposition demonstrators marched to India's Supreme Court on Monday and petitioned it against a revision of voter lists that has sparked days of unrest in the Indian capital and challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Opposition parties and supporters of the "cockroach" youth movement have rallied almost daily this month to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the revision that critics say benefits Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
The change, which started last year, led to over 130 million names – more than the population of Japan – being struck from voter lists, including 28 million who died, 63 million who relocated, and 30 million who could not be traced.
Monday's rally wound its way through some 7 km (4 miles) of streets in central Delhi before reaching the Supreme Court, with protesters waving party flags and shouting slogans demanding Kumar quit.
It passed off peacefully amid tight security, after a clampdown foiled plans by the 'Cockroach Janta Party' to mobilise larger crowds over the weekend, when police detained thousands of protesters, including CJP leaders, and locked down central Delhi.
The opposition group's petition is expected to be heard by the Supreme Court on Tuesday.
The petition, whose signatories include opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, seeks an audit of voter deletions, safeguards against deletions without notice, a hearing, and an interim suspension of the revision nationwide.
The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol, while the BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.
Monday's marchers included opposition party members and left-wing student groups. "The fundamental values of this country are being assaulted, institutions are losing their independence ... I am here to protest against this assault," said Anirudh Siyag, a PhD student.
Authorities closed six metro stations for 11 hours and restricted traffic along several stretches.
The BJP said the protests were an attempt by the main opposition party Congress to seize power.
"By discrediting constitutional institutions, spreading chaos and riots on the streets, and attacking people in the name of politics, all it seeks is a return to power," Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan told reporters.
Delhi Police announced that Jantar Mantar in the central business district was no longer designated as an official protest site and said three new venues had been identified.

title: Nobel Prize in Economics goes to US pair
description: Nobel Prize in Economics goes to US pair
content:
Hall, Woodford awarded prize for work on how to stabilise economies
US academics Robert Hall and Michael Woodford won the 2026 Nobel economics prize on Monday for decades of work developing ground-up models currently used by central banks and finance ministries across the world to stabilise economies.
"With them, we are better equipped to deal with shocks in the economy, such as energy crises or sudden changes in how much households consume," John Hassler, Chair of the Committee for the Prize in Economic Sciences, said in a statement.
Woodford and Hall are frequently name-checked by the world's top central banks which, after a 2022 inflation surge in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic, are currently grappling with the energy shock triggered by the Iran war.
One of the laureates' key insights is that economies could only be kept on an even keel by taking into account the millions of decisions made at a micro-level by households and businesses, rather than by using top-down theories of how economies work.
"...Authorities shouldn't view stabilization of the economy as an exercise that is simply conducted by people pulling levers to control the economy independently of what people in the economy understand about this," Columbia University's Woodford, 70, told a news conference.
In contrast to the oil shocks of the 1970s, when central banks struggled to combat sky-high inflation, Woodford said the new framework was useful during the global financial crisis of the late-2000s to bolster traditional tools of monetary policy.
"Making more explicit statements about the likely future path of interest rate policy, as opposed to relying on simply being able to cut interest rates further immediately, that was an important part of the policy response in the years from 2009 onward," he said.
Beyond so-called "forward guidance" on the future path of monetary policy, the work of Woodford - and Hall, 83, at Stanford University - promoted other concepts used today such as the idea of "sticky" inflation when price changes lag changes in demand.
Another is the "output gap", a measure of demand pressure building up in an economy and how efficiently resources are being used - the goal of stabilisation policy being to steer that gap towards zero.
Hall has served as adviser to the US Treasury Department, the Justice Department and the Federal Reserve Board.
His insight in a 1978 paper that household decisions on consumption are a perfect indicator of their expectations was used by Woodford in a model on how consumption is determined.
Woodford also showed that central banks can stimulate or suppress economic activity by adjusting interest rates, rather than just by the amount of money in circulation.
Such concepts remain core to central banking today. Forward guidance became especially important after the 2008 financial crisis, when rates were near zero or even negative and standard monetary policy seemed to be out of ammunition.
Now, however, some are questioning how relevant it is given the amount of uncertainty in the global economy - with new US Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh a notable sceptic.
The economics prize, formally known as the Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel, is the final award to be given out this year and is worth 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million).
First awarded in 1969, it is not one of the original five awards created in the 1895 will of industrialist and dynamite inventor Alfred Nobel, but was established by Sweden's central bank.
The majority of previous laureates have been from the United States. Only three women have ever won, most recently Claudia Goldin in 2023 for work on how gender has affected pay and employment over time in the United States.

title: Selma Blair detained after alleged disturbance on New York flight
description: US actor allegedly kicked a police officer and assaulted a nurse while being taken to hospital
content:
US actor allegedly kicked a police officer and assaulted a nurse while being taken to hospital
US actor Selma Blair was taken into custody Sunday night after allegedly assaulting crew members aboard a domestic flight arriving in New York City, Fox News reported Monday.
The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey told the outlet that it responded to a call about a “physically abusive passenger” aboard a Delta Air Lines flight.
Authorities intervened around 11 pm local time (0300GMT Monday) after the commercial aircraft, which departed from Los Angeles, landed at John F. Kennedy International Airport.
“Suspect was identified as Selma Blair, a 54-year-old woman. She was taken into custody and transported to the hospital for evaluation,” police said.
Two flight attendants sustained injuries during the altercation, with one crew member requiring hospital treatment for medical evaluation, according to authorities.
Blair allegedly kicked a Port Authority police officer in the head while being taken to the hospital and also allegedly assaulted a nurse after arriving at the hospital, celebrity news outlet TMZ reported.
A representative for the performer told TMZ that a sudden health crisis triggered the episode, saying Blair experienced a medical emergency that led to the behavior before receiving medical attention upon arrival.
Blair was diagnosed in 2018 with multiple sclerosis. She has been in remission since 2021 after undergoing chemotherapy and other treatments, but reportedly still suffers from fatigue and other ill effects.
