title: Global smartphone shipments record worst third quarter in 14 years amid memory shortage
description: Samsung led with 23  market share  driven by Galaxy Z Fold8 demand  despite a 3  annual shipment decline
content:
Samsung led with 23% market share, driven by Galaxy Z Fold8 demand, despite a 3% annual shipment decline
Global smartphone shipments fell 20% on-year to their lowest third-quarter level since 2012, as soaring memory chip costs and supply shortages pressured manufacturers ​and pushed up prices, preliminary estimates from Counterpoint Research showed on ​Monday.
Rising prices for memory components as AI infrastructure projects corner ⁠supplies have driven up production costs and prompted manufacturers to raise retail ​prices, cut shipments and prioritise profitability over volumes.
"Consumers are holding on to ​their devices longer than estimated, increasingly considering refurbished devices and prioritizing higher-value devices," said Counterpoint senior analyst Shilpi Jain.
Samsung retained its top position with a 23% market share, helped ​by demand for its Galaxy Z Fold8 series and stable component supplies ​for its mid-range devices. Shipments fell 3% from a year earlier during the quarter.
Read More: Microsoft plans huge deployment of its own AI chips, with an eye on saving costs
Apple's ‌market ⁠share reached 22%, crossing 20% for the first time in a third quarter, despite a year-on-year decline in shipments.
The absence of a base iPhone 18 model resulted in a smaller launch-month channel fill than the full iPhone ​17 lineup a year ​earlier, Counterpoint said.
OPPO ⁠and vivo recorded shipment declines of more than 20%. Xiaomi saw a more than 30% fall, reducing its ​market share to 10% as the company cut exposure ​to lower-priced ⁠devices and some overseas markets to protect margins.
"The outlook for the remainder of 2026 remains challenging," Counterpoint said.
"Production cuts, tighter portfolios, and greater focus on premium ⁠devices ​are likely to continue, while price-sensitive segments face ​further pressure from higher device prices and limited availability of components."

title: Hackers heat French supermarket fridges  sparking fires and spoiling food
description: France ordered a cybersecurity probe and is coordinating with EU partners to assess risks to other companies
content:
France ordered a cybersecurity probe and is coordinating with EU partners to assess risks to other companies
Hackers forced the temperature of fridges ​and freezers in many French supermarket fridges up to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) overnight, causing fires and spoiling food at several hundred ‌stores in a major cyberattack.
The Paris prosecutor's office said a "large-scale" attack was "affecting connected refrigerators in several major food retailers across France", leading to food losses and fires.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has instructed France's National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI) to investigate, a person in his office said.
France was coordinating with European counterparts because other countries could also be affected, the person said, adding that authorities were assessing whether ​other French companies were at risk.
Felix Aime, a senior cyber threat intelligence analyst at Sekoia Threat Detection and Research, said Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany and ​Belgium had also been affected.
Carrefour said 80 of its supermarkets had been hit, while Monoprix said 5% of its stores were affected.
Les ⁠Mousquetaires, owner of retailer Intermarche, said fridges at around 150 of its stores were heated up to 50 degrees Celsius for six hours overnight. A spokesperson said ​all affected food had been discarded to eliminate health risks.
Paris resident Geert de Clercq witnessed staff at an Intermarche in central Paris throwing cartfuls of defrosted frozen foods into ​a giant trash container, with molten ice cream sloshing out of broken tubs on the street.
Cooperative U CEO Dominique Schelcher said his supermarket group had also been targeted.
Read More: Thousands of cyberattacks blocked every month
"Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products and to the food supply of the French people is of extreme gravity and is unprecedented," he wrote on X.
E.Leclerc and Auchan did not respond to requests for ​comment.
There was no immediate estimate of industry-wide losses.
"Retail and wholesale play an essential role in keeping Europe supplied with the goods people rely on every day," said Christel ​Delberghe, director general at European retail association Eurocommerce. "This incident underlines the importance of resilience across the entire supply chain."
Supermarket cold aisles are typically run by control panels ‌that manage ⁠an entire store's fridges and freezers and can be accessed over the internet, which lets maintenance companies adjust them from anywhere.
The source close to Lecornu said ANSSI had identified a vulnerability in software supplied by Danish company Danfoss.
Danfoss said it was "aware of incidents in France affecting a limited number of refrigeration management systems".
The affected units "were running outdated firmware", Danfoss said, adding that it had "long advised customers to keep supported systems updated with the latest firmware and to migrate legacy systems to current-generation solutions".
On August 9, cybersecurity ​firm Claroty's Team82 published research detailing vulnerabilities ​in the Danfoss AK-SM 800A controller. ⁠According to the report, software updates issued by Danfoss addressed issues that could have allowed attackers to bypass authentication controls and execute code on compromised devices.
The attacks resemble disruptions reported at about a dozen US military commissaries in late August that led ​to food losses after fridges were affected.
Dutch retailer Ahold Delhaize, which operates the Netherlands' largest supermarket chain Albert Heijn ​and has major operations ⁠in the US, said it was dealing with a "security issue" on its network and had taken several systems offline as a precaution.
A message on the retailer's smartphone app said it was unable to deliver groceries because of a "cybersecurity incident".
Online orders account for about 10% of Albert Heijn sales. Physical stores remained open, while Dutch news agency ANP reported that ⁠rival retailers had ​seen a surge in delivery orders.
Ahold Delhaize said there was no reason to see a link ​between the incidents in France and its supermarkets.
Ahold is the fourth-largest grocery retailer in the US. Websites for its Stop & Shop, Giant, Hannaford and Food Lion chains displayed notices saying "site temporarily down".
It was unclear whether ​other operations had been affected.

title: Info ministry calls out Afghan Taliban for deflecting attention from terrorist sanctuaries
description: Cites UNSC report which  estimates approximately 6 000 TTP fighters are present in Afghanistan
content:
Cites UNSC report which estimates approximately 6,000 TTP fighters are present in Afghanistan
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MoIB) on Monday called out the Afghan Taliban for resorting to “rhetoric and diversion” to deflect attention from terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory and launching attacks against Pakistan.
In a post on X, the ministry said the Afghan Taliban regime’s spokesperson had once again resorted to rhetoric instead of addressing what it described as a well-documented terrorist threat emanating from Afghanistan.
It added that attempts to shift attention towards Pakistan’s internal affairs could not conceal the Afghan Taliban’s failure to prevent terrorist groups from using Afghan territory to plan and launch attacks against Pakistan.
The Afghan Taliban regime’s spokesperson has once again resorted to rhetoric and diversion instead of addressing the well-documented terrorist threat emanating from Afghan territory. Attempts to shift attention towards Pakistan’s internal affairs cannot conceal the regime’s…
Pakistan has repeatedly accused the Afghan Taliban regime of failing to act against militant sanctuaries despite being provided with information about their locations and activities.
Citing the Sixteenth Report (S/2025/796) of the UN Security Council’s Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team, the ministry said the report estimated that approximately 6,000 Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) fighters were present in Afghanistan and documented Taliban support for the group.
“These findings cannot credibly be dismissed as Pakistani propaganda. The regime must address this documented threat through concrete action rather than denial,” the ministry said.
Also Read : ‘Irrefutable evidence’ links Afghan soil to terror attacks in Pakistan
It also criticised the Afghan Taliban regime’s record on governance and citizens’ rights, saying its attempts to lecture others on these issues rang hollow in light of its continued restrictions on girls’ education and violations of fundamental human rights.
The ministry reiterated that Pakistan remained committed to dialogue, but said meaningful progress required the Afghan Taliban regime to honour its counterterrorism commitments and take verifiable action against terrorist sanctuaries and support networks.
“Pakistan will take all necessary measures, in accordance with international law, to protect its citizens, defend its sovereignty and safeguard its territorial integrity. The responsibility to end the use of Afghan territory for attacks against Pakistan rests squarely with the regime,” it concluded.
Islamabad has rejected Taliban assurances that Afghan territory would not be used against neighbouring countries, arguing that the ground situation and documented militant activity tell a different story.
Pakistan maintains that the terrorist nexus extended beyond the movement of terrorists across the border to their training, arming and operational support.
Security officials estimate that up to 70 per cent of the Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists infiltrating Pakistan were of Afghan origin. They further claim that the Taliban regime had allowed leftover US and NATO weapons to reach terrorist groups, including Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan .
The security establishment also linked the escalation in attacks to the presence of terrorist infrastructure inside Afghanistan.
In 2026 alone, terrorism emanating from Afghan soil claimed the lives of 1,327 Pakistanis and injured another 2,484, according to figures cited by Pakistani authorities.
Read More : Pakistan warns Afghanistan after Kohat attack, says it can eliminate terror threats ‘wherever they are’
Officials said that whenever Pakistani forces targeted terrorist hideouts, the Taliban regime instead moved to defend the militants and their sanctuaries rather than dismantling the infrastructure. The issue, Pakistan has argued, was not confined to TTP.
UN assessments have continued to document the presence of several other militant organisations in Afghanistan, including al Qaeda, the East Turkestan Islamic Movement (ETIM) and Islamic State-Khorasan, reinforcing concerns about the broader militant ecosystem operating from Afghan territory.
Pakistani officials say the continued presence of these groups, combined with training facilities, cross-border infiltration and access to sophisticated weapons, demonstrates that Afghanistan remains an important base for terrorist activity affecting Pakistan.
Pakistan's position, according to officials, remains that Kabul must take concrete steps to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries, eliminate training infrastructure, prevent cross-border infiltration and ensure that Afghan territory is not used for attacks against Pakistan.
The government has maintained that the issue was fundamentally one of Pakistan's national security and that continued attacks from Afghan soil cannot be addressed through denials alone.
Pakistan says it expected the Taliban regime to fulfil its commitments by taking verifiable action against terrorist groups operating from its territory rather than defending or denying their presence.

title: China s  7 5b EU hybrid boom faces new curbs under China EU deal
description: SAIC  BYD and Chery made up over 90  of Chinese hybrid sales in the EU
content:
SAIC, BYD and Chery made up over 90% of Chinese hybrid sales in the EU
China's deal to curb hybrid vehicle exports to the European Union is set to deal a fresh blow to electric vehicle makers that ramped up hybrid ​shipments exempt from the bloc's tariffs on Chinese-made EVs as sales growth slows at home.
Beijing's exports of hybrids to the EU's 27 member states tripled to $7.5 billion ‌in the first half of this year from $2.5 billion a year earlier, according to Chinese customs data. The figure was nearly nine times the $845 million exported in all of 2021.
Since the EU imposed additional tariffs on Chinese-made EVs in 2024, automakers have increasingly turned to plug-in hybrids, which are exempt from the extra duties. Weak charging infrastructure in parts of Europe has also supported demand for plug-in hybrids, which are marketed for their long range and strong ​fuel economy.
SAIC, BYD and Chery accounted for more than 90% of Chinese hybrid sales volume in the EU, while hybrids represented more than half of their European sales, according ​to Jefferies.
"It's making life a bit more difficult for the Chinese, but...that's not going to stop them as it happened to the electric cars," said ⁠Felipe Munoz of Car Industry Analysis.
"Europe is going to a point where they will need to decide whether they're doing what the US is doing or just let the whole industry be ​bought by the Chinese."
Speaking to reporters at the Paris auto show on Monday, Changan president Zhao Fei said he was "not that concerned" by the deal, which he viewed as a preamble to 'Made in ​Europe' local content rules that could be dealt with by setting up production in the region.
"This actually provides opportunities for Chinese companies like Changan to enter the European market," he said, adding that the company is planning to produce its first cars in the region early next year.
Chinese brands captured a record 15% share of Europe's EV market in the second quarter, up from 9.5% in the first quarter of 2024, while Chinese plug-in hybrids accounted for ​more than a quarter of the segment, rising sharply from just 1.7% at the beginning of 2024, according to Schmidt Automotive Research.
While European Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic ​said on Friday the agreement would cut the imports of "several million cars over four years," Brussels and Beijing have yet to disclose how the arrangement will be implemented.
Read More: Scientific expedition warns of accelerated glacier melting in NW China's Xinjiang
China's Commerce Ministry said on Monday that the arrangement would ‌allow continued export ⁠growth and guarantee China a quota no smaller than that granted to any other source of imports.
Renault CEO Francois Provost said on Monday the surge in Chinese hybrid imports was unsustainable for Europe, but added the agreement was preferable to a trade war and underscored the need to manage trade relations "sensibly".
Investors largely viewed the agreement as a de-escalation of trade tensions and a sign that tariffs on Chinese hybrids may be off the table for now. Shares in BYD fell 1.8%, while Chery and SAIC rose 1.4% and 0.5%, respectively.
"Overall, we believe it is a risk-relief rally story...as the implementation rules, ​volume caps, price floors, carve-outs are still pending technical ​negotiation," Citi analysts said.
The rapid growth of ⁠Chinese hybrid sales has increasingly challenged European manufacturers, including Volkswagen, long the region's leading plug-in hybrid seller, said Li Yanwei, an analyst at the China Automobile Dealers Association.
BYD, China's largest hybrid vehicle exporter to Europe, sold more plug-in hybrids than fully electric models in the first eight months of ​the year, with its Seal U SUV its best-selling model, according to data compiled by Li.
Together with Chery, SAIC and Geely, the company has ​narrowed the gap with ⁠Volkswagen, which still commanded a 31.8% share of the EU plug-in hybrid market.
"Let's see if China honours the agreement or finds workarounds, or temporary tariff exemptions," said Michael Dunne, a consultant who closely follows the Chinese automotive industry.
Analysts said the deal could ultimately accelerate Chinese automakers' push to build vehicles in Europe, even if some manufacturers attempt to frontload exports before any quota system takes effect.
"I would expect this to strengthen ⁠the incentive ​for Chinese automakers to manufacture in Europe," said Bill Russo, founder of Shanghai-based consultancy Automobility.
"If access through imports becomes more ​constrained, investing closer to the customer becomes more attractive. But localisation requires capital...smaller players may reconsider their European ambitions."
Jefferies analysts said the deal signalled "tariff risk off, quota risk on," potentially pushing Chinese automakers towards higher-priced models, increasing pressure on German ​premium brands and accelerating plans to build more vehicles in Europe.

title: Govt cuts petrol by Rs2 93  increases diesel by 61 paisas for Oct 13
description: Petrol price decreases to Rs395 37 per litre  while HSD will cost Rs396 85 under daily price mechanism
content:
Petrol price decreases to Rs395.37 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs396.85 under daily price mechanism
The federal government on Monday decreased the price of petrol by Rs2.93 per litre, while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by 61 paisas per litre for October 13.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs395.37 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs396.85 per litre on Tuesday.
The latest revision comes after the government decreased the price of petrol by 66 paisas per litre, while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by 52 paisas per litre from October 10 to October 12.
Read : Govt cuts petrol by 66 paisas, increases diesel by 52 paisas till Oct 12
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
Since daily pricing began on July 21, petrol prices had been raised 35 times and cut 22 times, while diesel had seen 34 increases and 23 reductions, leaving consumers grappling with persistent price volatility.
Read More : Fuel costs keep squeezing household budgets
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices were up 2% at near two-week ​highs on Monday as attacks on Saudi Arabia overshadowed the prospect of increased supplies after US President Donald Trump hailed ‌fresh Russian diesel exports and a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire on energy targets.
Rebounding from earlier losses, Brent crude futures were up $2.04, or 2%, to $106.76 a barrel at 11:07 am EDT (1507 GMT), their highest since September 29. US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $93.69 a barrel, up $1.84, or 2%.
"The sense of some kind of normality of exports from the Strait of Hormuz was shattered last week. Fresh ​attacks by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia added to this and helped to lift prices," said SEB commodities analyst Bjarne Schieldrop.

title: Punjab Police did not arrest journalist Iqrarul Hassan  Azma Bokhari
description: Says his family would be informed as soon as verified information about his whereabouts are available
content:
Says his family would be informed as soon as verified information about his whereabouts are available
Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari said on Monday that Punjab Police had not arrested journalist Iqrarul Hassan, adding that investigations into the matter were underway and his family would be informed as soon as verified information about his whereabouts became available.
In a statement posted on X, Bokhari said the police had not taken Hassan into custody and that the matter was being investigated.
پنجاب پولیس نے اقرار الحسن کو گرفتار نہیں کیا،اس معاملے کی تحقیقات کی جا رہی ہیں، ان کے بارے میں جیسے ہی کوئی مصدقہ اطلاعات موصول ہوں گی ان کے اہل خانہ کو آگاہ کر دیا جائے گا۔
Earlier, journalist Iqrarul Hassan’s wife, Farah Iqrar, told The Express Tribune that a group of unidentified individuals posing as officials of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) had allegedly taken him away from their residence in Lahore’s Defence C area.
According to Farah, between five and seven people, including women, arrived at the house late on Sunday night, during the intervening hours of Sunday and Monday, and demanded that Hassan come outside.
She alleged that the individuals threatened to break down the door if he was not handed over. They subsequently entered the house, forcibly took the journalist from a room and took him away.
Farah said she contacted the relevant agency’s office to inquire about her husband’s whereabouts but received no response. She added that an application regarding Hassan’s alleged abduction was submitted to the Defence C police station at around 6am, after which the police issued a diary number.

title: Amanda Seyfried reveals why she turned down a show with frequent intimate scenes

content:
The actress said her daughter praised her after she declined photo requests while they were together
Amanda Seyfried has revealed that she recently turned down a television project because it involved frequent sex scenes, explaining that she is no longer comfortable with that level of on screen intimacy.
The 40 year old actress discussed the decision during a panel hosted by Alec Baldwin at the Hamptons International Film Festival on October 4. Seyfried reflected on how her attitude towards romantic scenes has changed throughout her career.
“Our jobs are weird,” she said, explaining that actors sometimes have to portray romantic relationships with people they do not have romantic feelings for. She recalled that kissing scenes once felt exciting and uncomplicated, but admitted that her perspective has shifted with age.
“I passed on a show where I would have to have sex all the time because of the sex,” Seyfried said. “Doesn’t matter who it’s with. I don’t wanna do it. I’m uncomfortable with it. I’m not into it right now.”
She added that she might feel differently if the project came along at another time, but currently does not want to deal with being naked alongside a stranger.
Seyfried also discussed how becoming a mother has influenced her ability to establish personal boundaries. She shares daughter Nina, nine, and son Thomas, six, with her estranged husband, Thomas Sadoski.
The actress recalled declining requests for photographs while spending time with her daughter in Manhattan. After one encounter, she asked Nina how she felt about the decision. Her daughter reportedly told her she was proud of her mother for saying no.
Seyfried said the experience made her reflect on the example she sets for her children and the importance of prioritising their needs when they are together.
The actress is currently starring in The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd , directed by Tim Blake Nelson. The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival before screening at the Hamptons International Film Festival. It features Seyfried as a teacher in an abusive relationship who takes a job at a maximum security prison and develops feelings for an inmate played by Scoot McNairy.

title: Sindh   s mental health gap leaves communities unsupported
description: The province has no mental health policy since the past five years with specialists serving only 10 districts
content:
The province has no mental health policy since the past five years with specialists serving only 10 districts
For someone battling depression, anxiety, or another mental health disorder, finding help in Sindh can be as difficult as living with the illness itself. Where a person lives can determine whether a specialist is within reach—or whether they have to struggle without one.
Mental-health specialists are concentrated in just 10 districts of the province, while the remaining districts have no reported specialist services. With around 140 mental health professionals serving Sindh, access to psychiatric and psychological care remains severely limited outside major urban centres.
The shortage is compounded by the absence of a provincial mental health policy for the past five years. Experts say the lack of a comprehensive policy has also contributed to inadequate data, making it difficult to determine the true scale of mental health disorders or assess services required across the province.
Dr Karim Khawaja, Honorary Chairman of the Sindh Mental Health Authority, said more than 30 per cent of Pakistan’s population suffers from depression and other mental and psychological disorders. He said there were around 600 mental health professionals across Pakistan, including 140 in Sindh, but those in Sindh were available in only 10 districts.
“The remaining districts do not have these specialists,” he said, highlighting the geographic gap in mental health care. People living outside these districts may have to travel to larger cities for diagnosis and treatment, creating another barrier for families already facing financial difficulties and other social pressures.
Read More: Brain rot: you are suffering from it too!
The problem is particularly significant as mental health disorders are believed to be increasing across Pakistan. According to experts, the number of people suffering from mental health disorders has increased by around 15 per cent over the past five years, while more than 30 per cent of the population is estimated to suffer from depression and other psychological disorders.
But the absence of reliable provincial data makes it difficult to establish the scale of the problem in Sindh.
Professor Dr Muhammad Iqbal Afridi, Distinguished National & Meritorious Professor (HEC), said one in every three people in Pakistan, compared with one in every five globally, suffered from some form of psychological illness. "Depression is increasingly being reported among men and women, with domestic conflict and other social pressures contributing to psychological problems among women," noted Dr Afridi.
Young people are also facing growing pressures. Professor Afridi said Pakistan’s economic situation, unemployment, terrorism and uncertainty about the future were affecting their mental health. He also pointed to increasing exposure to ice and other addictive substances, as well as excessive use of digital platforms.
Professor Wajid Ali Akhunzada, President of the Pakistan Psychiatric Society, said one in every four young people and one in every five children in Pakistan suffered from some form of psychological illness. He confirmed that the country faced a severe shortage of psychiatric specialists and needed greater investment in mental health services.
Experts say Sindh needs a policy framework covering prevention, early diagnosis, treatment, referrals, specialist training, and data collection. Better data could help identify districts with the greatest need and guide the deployment of additional mental-health professionals and facilities.
For many in Sindh, the hardest part of fighting a mental-health disorder may be finding someone qualified to help. Until care reaches beyond major cities, too many people will be left to struggle in silence, with help out of reach when they need it most.

title: Microsoft plans huge deployment of its own AI chips  with an eye on saving costs
description: Microsoft s Maia 300 is its third generation AI chip  designed for coding and complex tasks
content:
Microsoft's Maia 300 is its third-generation AI chip, designed for coding and complex tasks
Microsoft announced the next generation of its custom AI chip on Monday and said it plans to deploy potentially more than a million of them next year to back its internal AI services.
The Maia 300, ​as the chip is called, is the third generation of the company's custom chips ​designed to handle AI data crunching such as coding and carrying out complex business ⁠tasks on a user's behalf. Its predecessor is already running Microsoft's in-house AI models, as ​well as models from OpenAI delivered on Microsoft's Azure cloud computing service.
The new version comes amid ​a flurry of custom chips from both cloud computing rivals and AI firms such as OpenAI aimed at loosening the hold of Nvidia on the AI computing market.
To construct the chip, Microsoft took a different technical path from Nvidia ​whose AI accelerators use one massive computing chip surrounded by high-bandwidth memory chips.
The central computing processor ​in Microsoft's Maia 300 silicon is composed of "chiplets" — typically specialized chips bonded together — that use 2-nanometer technology from Taiwan Semiconductor ‌Manufacturing ⁠Co for key computing functions.
Read More: Microsoft president says milk faces more regulation than AI
Other chiplets included in the design use cheaper 3-nanometer tech for functions such as moving data off the processor and elsewhere inside the system.
The Maia 300 processors will go into racks that contain 96 chips and use about 167 kilowatts of power, compared with the ​142 kilowatts used by Nvidia's ​most recent GB300 ⁠AI server racks with 72 of its graphics processing units (GPUs).
Microsoft said the Maia 300 chips will get about 40% more useful computing done per ​megawatt than "leading GPU-based systems," though it did not name the systems it ​used for ⁠a comparison.
"It's basically delivering more intelligence for every watt, every dollar, and every byte of memory by optimizing across the entire system," Rani Borkar, president of Azure hardware systems and infrastructure at Microsoft, ⁠told Reuters ​in an interview.
Microsoft said it plans to roll out "multi-gigawatt deployments" ​of the Maia 300 chip starting next year. Microsoft has said it expects to spend more than $175 billion in capital expenditures ​this calendar year.

title: Anne Hathaway   s    Verity    makes major changes to Colleen Hoover   s novel
description: Colleen Hoover approved removing one of Verity and Jeremy   s children  saying it improved the film   s story
content:
Colleen Hoover approved removing one of Verity and Jeremy’s children, saying it improved the film’s story
Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson’s film Verity brings Colleen Hoover’s bestselling thriller to the screen, but the adaptation makes several significant changes to the original novel, from family details to its dramatic ending.
Directed by Michael Showalter, the psychological thriller stars Hathaway as Verity Crawford, Johnson as Lowen Ashleigh and Josh Hartnett as Jeremy Crawford. While the film retains the novel’s central mystery, several storylines have been altered or removed.
One major difference concerns Verity and Jeremy’s children. In the novel, the couple have a son, Crew, and twin daughters, Harper and Chastin, who die in separate incidents. The film removes Chastin, leaving the family with Crew and Harper, whose death occurs before the main story.
Hoover supported the change, telling Variety that removing one child gave the adaptation a different tone and made the story feel less dark and unrealistic within the time available for a film.
Hathaway’s appearance also differs from the source material. Verity is blonde in the novel, whereas the actor keeps her brunette hair in the film. Hathaway said the decision followed discussions with Showalter about how the characters would look together on screen.
Lowen’s sleepwalking, an important element of the book’s portrayal of her psychological state, was filmed but ultimately cut. The adaptation also omits a graphic passage from Verity’s manuscript involving an attempted self induced abortion.
Other additions include a fantasy sequence in which Lowen imagines kissing Verity, a scene that Hathaway and Johnson reportedly suggested. Hathaway also developed a distinctive, deliberately irritating voice for Verity’s narration.
The film expands Verity’s public profile through appearances involving Alex Cooper, Gayle King and Sean Evans, helping establish her celebrity status. Hartnett also suggested personal accessories for Jeremy, including jewellery made by his fictional children, to emphasise his role as a father.
The ending changes significantly, too. The film shows Jeremy confronting Verity with the manuscript and disposing of her body in a lake. In the novel, the couple leave her in bed to make her death appear different.
The changes reflect the filmmakers’ approach to adapting a psychological thriller for the screen.

Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler star as Tubbs and Crockett in 'Miami Vice ’85', now filming for 2028 release
Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler have unveiled their first looks as undercover detectives Ricardo Tubbs and Sonny Crockett in Miami Vice ’85 , the upcoming reboot of the iconic 1980s television series.
Filming has begun on the crime drama, which is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on May 19, 2028.
Jordan plays Tubbs, while Butler takes on the role of Crockett, characters originally portrayed by Philip Michael Thomas and Don Johnson in the television series. The original Miami Vice aired from 1984 to 1989 and followed two police detectives working undercover to tackle crime in Miami, Florida.
Directed by Joseph Kosinski, the film will revisit the style and atmosphere of mid-1980s Miami. According to the project’s description, Miami Vice ’85 will explore the era’s glamour and corruption, drawing inspiration from the original series’ pilot episode and first season.
The reboot aims to revisit the television show’s cultural influence, particularly its impact on fashion and filmmaking. Kosinski previously directed Top Gun: Maverick and F1 , bringing experience with large-scale cinematic productions to the project.
The cast also features Alden Ehrenreich, Whitney Peak, Camila Morrone, Danny Ramirez, John Leguizamo, Andrew Schulz, Edi Gathegi, Walton Goggins, André Holland and Michael Irby.
Dan Gilroy wrote the screenplay, based on characters created by Anthony Yerkovich for the original television series. Eric Warren Singer worked on an earlier draft. Kosinski and Dylan Clark are producing the film, with Universal overseeing the project.
Jordan most recently won the best actor Oscar for Sinners . He is also set to star in and direct The Thomas Crown Affair , opposite Adria Arjona. Butler’s upcoming projects include A24’s Enemies , in which he co-stars with Jeremy Allen White.
With filming now underway, Miami Vice ’85 is bringing two prominent Hollywood stars into the roles that helped define the original crime drama. The film is expected to introduce the franchise to a new generation while revisiting its distinctive 1980s setting.

title: UK PM Burnham says  clear  Russia meddled in Brexit vote
description: The UK leader told the UN last month that London had evidence of Russian meddling in the 2019 election
content:
The UK leader told the UN last month that London had evidence of Russian meddling in the 2019 election
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday it was "clear" Russia had interfered in the UK's bitter 2016 Brexit referendum, renewing claims of meddling by Moscow.
Burnham said he inquired about Russian involvement in the divisive ballot, in which Britons voted by a narrow margin to leave the European Union, when he became prime minister in July.
"I asked the question coming to Downing Street: 'Was there interference in the 2016 referendum from Russia?' And I've had the clear answer that yes, there was," Burnham told the Rest is Politics podcast broadcast on Monday.
A UK parliamentary committee said in 2020 it could not confirm Russian meddling in the Brexit vote but criticised the Conservatives in power at the time for failing to probe possible interference.
Junior foreign minister Stephen Doughty alleged to LBC radio on Monday that Russia "attempted" to interfere in the vote but had "not succeeded".
Burnham also said German Chancellor Friedrich Merz had told him that Germany's far-right opposition party AfD, "is clearly linked to Russia -- funded, I believe".
"There is certainly misinformation, disinformation that is emanating from Russia into German politics," said Burnham.
He said Britain should "help voters in Germany and France understand that some of this politics is instigated via our enemies".
The new UK leader has renewed accusations of Russian interference, telling the gathering of world leaders at the United Nations last month that London had "evidence" Moscow tried to meddle with the 2019 general election.
He also announced a new disinformation centre to combat "hostile state information attacks".
Later on Monday, Burnham was set to address parliament and urge MPs to seek a new deal and closer ties with the European Union, reopening the divisive Brexit debate which has been politically taboo since Britain officially left the EU in 2020.
"Andy Burnham will declare it would be a dereliction of duty to turn our back on the possibility of a new deal with the EU," his office said.
"He will say we must face up to the reality that Brexit has done more harm than good and that the status quo is not good enough for Britain."

title: Andrew Garfield says OpenAI film  Artificial  turns lens on creators of  new world
description: English American actor stars as Sam Altman  exploring AI   s rise  power  ethics and safety through curiosity
content:
English-American actor stars as Sam Altman, exploring AI’s rise, power, ethics and safety through curiosity
Curiosity and fear powered actor Andrew Garfield's performance in Luca Guadagnino's OpenAI movie Artificial , which premiered at the London Film Festival on Sunday.
Garfield plays OpenAI CEO Sam Altman in the film, which unfolds over two decades and chronicles the conception and growth of the artificial intelligence company behind ChatGPT and Altman's dramatic firing and rehiring in 2023.
"I think the reason I was drawn to it was just pure curiosity and fear and really trying to understand as deeply as possible the people who are ushering us into this next phase of the world," said Garfield.
"There's a sense of courage and imagination and resilience these people at the top of these companies must have, the ability to withstand so much criticism and such a microscopic lens on them as people. And it's important that we do that because we need to know who's in power and who's creating our new world," he said.
Garfield, who also starred in 2010's Facebook origin film The Social Network , did not contact or meet with Altman in preparation for the role.
"I don't know Sam and I have a lot of compassion for a person who's my age, almost, and there's a movie being made about him," Garfield said. "It's not him, but it's an idea of what this story is and his part in it."
OpenAI did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. In an interview with Vanity Fair, Altman said he was not expecting an "accurate depiction".
With a screenplay by Emmy-winning Saturday Night Live writer Simon Rich, Artificial stars Russian Oscar-nominee Yura Borisov as OpenAI co-founder and former chief scientist Ilya Sutskever, who left the company after his involvement in Altman's brief ouster. It follows the ethical differences and conflict over AI safety between Altman and Sutskever, who trained under Geoffrey Hinton, known as the "Godfather of AI", portrayed in the film by Mark Rylance.
The film also stars Ike Barinholtz as Tesla CEO Elon Musk. Monica Barbaro plays Mira Murati, OpenAI's former technology chief. It was shot in 2025 and comes at a time of mounting concerns triggered by recent incidents at OpenAI and Anthropic that have sparked fears rogue AI systems may slip beyond human control.
"It's so fascinating making a film like this when the topic is so relevant right now," said Barbaro. "We'd be on set, watching two people argue with each other on Twitter, who we were portraying in this movie. It was really wild to have that experience. It's exciting and it's also really daunting because you want to be truthful, but the truth seems to change every month."

Garfield offered a different recollection when asked about Altman’s comments. Speaking at the film’s London premiere, he said, “I heard him say that and I was like, I would have remembered. I was so aware of looking for him when we were shooting near his house and on those streets. I didn’t see him and I was very, very disappointed that I didn’t.”
Garfield added that filming so close to Altman’s home felt thrilling, exciting and terrifying, but says he never saw him.
The contrasting accounts have drawn attention as Artificial prepares for release. Garfield plays Altman, alongside other figures connected to the company’s history.
Altman has said he does not expect the film to accurately depict his life, although he praised Garfield’s imitation of his walk and mannerisms after seeing the trailer. He also said the trailer’s portrayal of a bunker filled with firearms was fictional.
The production was originally associated with Amazon MGM Studios, but the company dropped the project. Neon later acquired it for distribution. The film is scheduled to open in select US cinemas on December 25, 2026.

title: Hiba Bukhari urges fans to remain respectful amid online disagreements
description: Actor says remarks were upsetting  clarifies her earlier post was meant to understand situation  not fuel hostility
content:
Actor says remarks were upsetting, clarifies her earlier post was meant to understand situation, not fuel hostility
Pakistani actor Hiba Bukhari has urged her fans to treat others with respect after coming across what she described as “really disrespectful” comments on social media.
In an Instagram Story, Bukhari clarified that her intention behind an earlier post was to understand the situation rather than encourage hostility among her followers.
“Okay. So I am posting this after reading comments and some really disrespectful things which I don’t appreciate in any way,” Bukhari wrote.
The actor emphasised that while she valued her fans, she did not want their support to come at the expense of respect for others, particularly her fellow actors.
“I love my fans and I know for a fact my fandom can not disrespect anyone,” she stated. “I respect my co actors and that is exactly what I expect from you all,” she added.
Bukhari also clarified the purpose of her earlier interaction, explaining that she had been seeking an understanding of the situation rather than attempting to fuel disagreements. “The story was to inquire what is happening,” she wrote.
Concluding her message, the actor appealed to her followers to remain considerate towards one another, expressing disappointment at the hurtful remarks she had encountered. “It’s a request to you all please be respectful towards each other! And it’s actually hurtful to see such things. Lots of love from your Hiba Bukhari,” she said.
Bukhari’s message highlights the challenges public figures can face as their fan communities extend beyond television screens into highly active online spaces. While passionate supporters can play an important role in celebrating actors and their work, disagreements between fans can also spill over into personal attacks and hostility.
The actor’s comments come amid continued public interest in her television projects and on-screen pairings. She starred opposite Danish Taimoor in Humrahi , which became a subject of online discussion following its release. title: Australia set South Africa 421 run target
description: Renshaw continues prolific form with another impressive second innings 82
content:
Renshaw continues prolific form with another impressive second innings 82
Matt Renshaw continued his prolific batting form before Australia declared on 314-6 at tea on the fourth day of the first Test on Monday, setting South Africa a daunting victory target of 421.
Australia held a 106-run first-innings lead after Renshaw scored 190, and the 30-year-old Queenslander again dominated the home bowlers at Kingsmead before a controversial caught-and-bowled dismissal by Keshav Maharaj ended his innings.
Renshaw looked disgusted after Maharaj appeared to juggle the catch before claiming it, with a television review confirming the dismissal.
Australia, who resumed on 33 without loss, scored 141 runs in a fast-moving morning session for the loss of four wickets and added another 140 in the afternoon as they sought to give themselves enough time to take the 10 wickets required for victory.
Opener Nic Maddinson, playing his first Test in a decade after scoring a duck in the first innings, struck 48 before being bowled by Anrich Nortje. Beau Webster remained unbeaten on 39, while captain Pat Cummins smashed four sixes in a whirlwind 32 off 12 balls.
Travis Head managed 11 and Marnus Labuschagne scored 37, but Labuschagne's 53-run partnership with Steve Smith, who made 27, helped Australia accelerate.
Smith was struck on the helmet by a Nortje bouncer while batting and underwent a lengthy on-field assessment before continuing his innings. He was later caught on the boundary off spinner Simon Harmer and did not take the field at the start of South Africa's second innings.
An Australian team spokesman said Smith was "undergoing further assessment", with an update expected later on Monday or on Tuesday. A concussion diagnosis could put him in doubt for the second Test in Gqeberha, which starts on Sunday.
South Africa were 60-1 at the time of filing, with Aiden Markram on 22 and David Bedingham unbeaten on 35. Josh Hazlewood dismissed Ryan Rickelton for two.
The hosts need a determined batting performance to avoid defeat and preserve captain Temba Bavuma's unbeaten record in 12 Tests as skipper.
Bad light curtailed play on each of the first three days and was again expected to threaten an early finish on Monday.

title: More than 100 foreign trekkers stranded in flood hit region of Nepal  official says
description: Authorities rescued 321 people after a landslide blocked Nepal s Budhi Gandaki River  causing downstream flooding
content:
Authorities rescued 321 people after a landslide blocked Nepal's Budhi Gandaki River, causing downstream flooding
More than 100 foreign trekkers are stranded at different locations after the flooding of a river in central ​Nepal at the weekend swept away hiking trails and bridges, an ‌official said on Monday.
Authorities rescued 321 people, including 12 foreigners, on Monday after a pre-dawn landslide at the weekend in Gorkha district, about 100 km (62 miles) west of Kathmandu, blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, ​leading to downstream flooding. The army said the rescue operation would continue on ​Tuesday, even as the water level in the river had receded.
The ⁠river is a tributary of the Trishuli River, downstream from another tributary where ​a glacier collapse caused a catastrophic flood in August that killed 1,457 people, with thousands still ​missing .
There were no reports of fatalities in the flood, but five villagers were out of contact after black muddy sludge and debris washed away homes and damaged infrastructure, including three hydroelectric plants, national disaster ​authorities said.
Read More: Nepal urges villagers to evacuate after flood triggered by landslide, 5 missing
Bhuwan Raj Ojha, an official of the Manaslu Conservation Area Project that ​includes a popular trekking route, said there were more than 100 foreign trekkers stranded in different ‌areas ⁠who could not return because part of the trail had been swept away.
"Those hikers who want to return because of the flood need to be rescued. Those who want to continue their trekking can do so from locations that are safe," ​Ojha told Reuters from ​Gorkha.
"There are restaurants ⁠and tea houses along the route. They are safe."
The International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development said the latest flood may ​have been triggered by the failure of a temporary river ​blockage created ⁠by a landslide, according to preliminary accounts from Nepal's authorities reviewed by ICIMOD.
"This event is another reminder of how exposed mountain communities and river corridors remain to sudden, ⁠cascading hazards," ​Pema Gyamtsho, director general of ICIMOD, said.
"While response ​efforts must remain the immediate priority, understanding what triggered this flood will be critical for reducing future ​risks and strengthening resilience."

title: Robert Pattinson says he has had one of the best years of his acting career on how he feels to be one of the A list actors
description: From    Twilight    to    The Batman     Pattinson has built a career spanning blockbusters and independent films
content:
From ‘Twilight’ to ‘The Batman’, Pattinson has built a career spanning blockbusters and independent films
Robert Pattinson is reflecting on a successful period in his acting career, saying that despite his standing in Hollywood, he still approaches the profession like someone looking for the next job.
“You know, I kind of always approach acting like you’re always just trying to get a job the whole time and sometimes you have really good years. And this was just one of the best years I’ve ever had,” Pattinson said in a clip shared online.
The remark offers a glimpse into how the actor views his recent work. Rather than treating his status as an established star as a guarantee of continued opportunities, he described acting as a career in which fortunes can shift and strong periods cannot be taken for granted.
Pattinson became internationally famous as Edward Cullen in the Twilight film series. After the franchise, he took on roles in independent films and collaborations with acclaimed directors, including Good Time , The Lighthouse and Christopher Nolan’s Tenet . Those projects helped move his screen image beyond his early romantic lead role.
He returned to major studio filmmaking with The Batman , playing Bruce Wayne, and appeared in Bong Joon Ho’s science fiction film Mickey 17 . His recent work also includes Primetime , in which he portrays television presenter Chris Hansen in a dramatisation inspired by the making of To Catch a Predator .
The actor has chosen projects that differ in tone and scale, moving between franchise productions and smaller, director led films. That varied filmography has kept audiences interested in what he might do next.
Although Pattinson did not specify what made this year especially rewarding, he clearly regards it as a standout period in his career. His remarks underline a practical outlook: success can be celebrated, but the next job is never guaranteed. He continues to approach success with caution.

title: Pakistan eye clean sweep against Sri Lanka
description: Farhan and Maaz lead hosts    charge as visitors struggle to find form
content:
Farhan and Maaz lead hosts’ charge as visitors struggle to find form
In-form Pakistan will be desperately looking to complete a clean sweep when they face Sri Lanka in the third and final T20I at the Pindi Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi on Tuesday.
Pakistan are in fine form, having won the first two matches convincingly. The hosts defeated the visitors by four wickets in the opening game before inflicting a comprehensive 82-run defeat on them in the second match on Sunday.
Pakistan have shown strength with both bat and ball, and the Green-shirts will be eager to maintain their momentum in the final game under captain Sahibzada Farhan, who has been in sublime touch.
Pakistan’s top order has performed well in both matches.
In the opening game, the middle order was tested, but a few unnecessary dismissals raised eyebrows as the hosts appeared well placed to chase down a target of 183. However, Pakistan completely outclassed Sri Lanka in the second match, restricting them to 133-7 while defending a formidable total of 216.
The 215-3 was Pakistan’s highest total at home and the second highest overall. The Green-shirts had amassed 232-6 against England in Nottingham on July 16, 2021, which is their record score.
Sahibzada Farhan and Maaz Sadaqat have been outstanding with the bat. The pair have built valuable partnerships for the second wicket in both matches and scored back-to-back half-centuries.
Farhan scored 89 and 73, while Maaz smashed 50 and 96, breathing new life into Pakistan’s top order.
Maaz, who also impressed in the Caribbean Premier League (CPL), punished the Sri Lankan bowlers with aggressive stroke-play, making it difficult for them to contain him.
He played his natural game, and the freedom with which he batted reflected the confidence the team management has placed in the young Peshawar batsman.
Fakhar Zaman has been opening alongside Farhan. Although he has made promising starts, he has failed to bat deep into the innings. Known for his ability to score big, Fakhar has been unable to convert his starts into substantial scores. He will need to show greater application, which could further strengthen Pakistan’s batting line-up.
Hasan Nawaz performed well on Sunday, while it remains to be seen how Saim Ayub and Khawaja Nafay fare when given adequate opportunities. Khawaja scored the winning runs in Pakistan’s first T20I victory but has yet to be tested under significant pressure.
In the bowling department, Imran Randhawa has been particularly impressive. He consistently hits the right areas and has looked effective with the new ball. The all-rounder has taken five wickets in two matches, both of which were his T20I debut appearances.
“I bowled according to plan and achieved success,” Imran told reporters after Pakistan’s one-sided victory on Sunday.
Experienced leg-spinner Shadab Khan, however, has been unimpressive so far, raising questions about his role in the team.
Meanwhile, Sri Lanka’s struggles in T20 cricket have continued.
After losing a T20I series 2-1 to the West Indies and suffering a 3-0 whitewash against England on recent away tours, Sri Lanka are now facing the prospect of a third consecutive series defeat.
Their batting has lacked firepower, while their bowling has struggled to contain Pakistan. Poor fielding has also contributed to their below-par performances, with dropped catches proving costly.
In the second match, Sri Lanka dropped Farhan when he was on 12, allowing the Pakistan captain to make the most of the reprieve.
Sri Lanka last toured Pakistan in October 2019 for a three-match T20I series, which they won 3-0.
This time, however, Pakistan appear poised to turn the tables.
Pakistan squad: Sahibzada Farhan (captain), Abdul Samad, Abrar Ahmed, Arafat Minhas, Fakhar Zaman, Hasan Nawaz, Khawaja Nafay (wicket-keeper), Maaz Sadaqat, Mohammad Salman Mirza, Muhammad Imran Randhawa, Naseem Shah, Razaullah, Saim Ayub, Shadab Khan and Sufiyan Moqim.

title: Litton   s century puts Bangladesh in control
description: Das hits 102 as Afghanistan face mammoth 479 run target
content:
Das hits 102 as Afghanistan face mammoth 479-run target
The wicket-keeper batsman Litton Das on Monday struck a splendid century as Bangladesh strengthened their grip on the one-off Test against Afghanistan, setting the hosts a daunting target of 479 runs on the fourth day at the Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abu Dhabi.
Afghanistan reached 132-3 in their second innings at stumps and they still need 347 more runs to win the Test.
Das scored 102 off 117 balls as Bangladesh declared their second innings at 372-7 after resuming the day with their overnight score of 223-6. His seventh Test century featured 14 fours. He stayed for 182 minutes at the crease.
Bangladesh, who had scored 346 in their first innings, secured a 106-run lead after dismissing Afghanistan for 240. Their strong second innings performance left the visitors facing a formidable chase to win the Test.
Das shared a crucial 149-run partnership for the seventh wicket with Mehidy Hasan Miraz, who remained unbeaten on 52. Miraz faced 97 deliveries and struck five fours, helping Bangladesh build a commanding position before the declaration.
Afghanistan fast bowler Mohammad Saleem claimed two wickets for 69 runs, finishing with match figures of 6-151.
Chasing 479 for victory, Afghanistan endured an early setback when Abdul Malik fell for two. He edged a delivery from Ebadot Hossain to wicketkeeper Das, leaving the visitors under immediate pressure.
Shahidullah joined Sediqullah Atal at the crease but could not provide lasting support. He was dismissed for 19 by Hasan Mahmud, with Das completing the catch behind the stumps. Shahidullah's innings came off 19 balls and included four boundaries.
Afghanistan were struggling at 28-2 when the dismissal left them facing an uphill battle to save the match.
Captain Rahmat Shah then joined Atal and helped steady the innings. The pair put together an important 82-run partnership for the third wicket, offering Afghanistan some hope of resisting Bangladesh's attack.
However, Ebadot struck again to remove Rahmat, who scored 51 off 124 balls, including five fours and a six. His departure left Afghanistan at 110-3 and further increased the pressure on the visitors.
Atal and Hashmatullah Shahidi then batted cautiously to take Afghanistan to 132-3 at stumps, keeping their hopes alive heading into the final day.
Sediqullah Atal was batting on 35 and with him at the end was Hashmatullah Shahidi on 19.
Atal struck on six and one four from 126 balls while Shahidi hit two fours and six in his 27-ball unbeaten effort.
Ebadot Hossain got 2-32 while Hasan Mahmud claimed 1-31.
Afghanistan still require 347 runs to reach their target, while Bangladesh need seven wickets to secure victory. With three wickets down and a substantial deficit remaining, the hosts face a difficult task to turn the contest around.
Bangladesh will look to maintain their discipline with the ball on the final day, while Afghanistan must produce a determined batting effort to avoid defeat.

title: Atiqa Odho urges women to prioritise breast health and seek timely medical care
description: Actor encourages families to make breast cancer awareness and regular health checks part of everyday conversations
content:
Actor encourages families to make breast cancer awareness and regular health checks part of everyday conversations
Veteran actor Atiqa Odho has urged women to prioritise their health and encouraged families to support their loved ones in seeking timely medical care, using her social media platform to highlight the importance of breast cancer awareness and early detection.
Sharing a pink-themed awareness poster featuring three women on Instagram, Odho emphasised the importance of self-care, regular health checks and making breast health a part of everyday conversations.
The poster carried the message, “Look after those who matter, by looking out for Breast Cancer,” highlighting the role that awareness and support can play in encouraging women to seek medical advice.
In her caption, the actor wrote, “A little awareness today can make a lifetime of difference.” “Breast cancer is a reminder that caring for the women we love means encouraging them to care for themselves, too,” she added.
Odho stressed the importance of early detection, noting that “regular self-examinations, timely medical consultations, and recommended screenings are important steps towards protecting our health.”
She also urged her followers to break the silence surrounding breast cancer and encouraged women to seek medical advice without fear or embarrassment.
“Let’s break the silence, spread awareness, and remind every woman that her health matters,” she wrote, encouraging women to prioritise their own health as well as that of their loved ones.
Her message comes as Breast Cancer Awareness Month draws attention to the importance of recognising potential symptoms, understanding screening options and seeking medical advice when concerns arise. The annual campaign also provides an opportunity to address the stigma and silence that can prevent women from discussing their health or accessing care.
While being familiar with changes in one's breasts can help women recognise potential warning signs, self-examination does not replace recommended screening or professional medical assessment. Women should consult a qualified healthcare professional if they notice a new lump, changes in breast shape or size, skin dimpling, nipple changes or unusual discharge. Screening recommendations vary according to age, family history and individual risk.
Beyond the medical aspects, Odho's post highlights the role families and communities can play in normalising conversations about breast health. Encouragement from a mother, sister, daughter or friend can help women feel more comfortable discussing concerns and seeking medical attention.
In another Instagram post, the actor highlighted the burden of breast cancer in Pakistan, drawing attention to the need for greater awareness and early detection.
The post also cited a survival rate of 98% with early screening. However, survival rates vary according to the stage at diagnosis, the type of cancer and other individual factors, and the figure should not be interpreted as a universal guarantee.
Concluding her latest message on a note of care and solidarity, Odho wrote, “With love and care, let’s make awareness a habit, not just a moment.”
Her appeal serves as a reminder that breast cancer awareness should extend beyond a designated month. Encouraging open conversations, seeking timely medical advice and following appropriate screening recommendations can help women make informed decisions about their health.
Odho is one of Pakistan’s best-known television and film actors, with a career spanning more than three decades. She made her television debut in Anwar Maqsood’s Sitara Aur Mehrunissa in 1992 and went on to establish herself through dramas including Dasht , Nijaat and Angaar Wadi .

title: Rebel Wilson accused of misleading court in bitter    The Deb    legal battle
description: The dispute centres on allegations involving producer Amanda Ghost and actor Charlotte MacInnes
content:
The dispute centres on allegations involving producer Amanda Ghost and actor Charlotte MacInnes
Rebel Wilson is facing fresh allegations in the ongoing legal dispute surrounding her film The Deb , with producers accusing the actress and director of misleading the court and mishandling evidence.
Lawyers representing producer Amanda Ghost and her fellow producers filed a motion seeking terminating sanctions in their defamation lawsuit against Wilson. The filing alleges that Wilson gave false testimony under oath and manipulated or manufactured evidence during the proceedings.
The producers claim the alleged conduct has undermined their ability to prepare their case and obtain a fair trial. Their legal team also accused Wilson of destroying evidence they consider crucial to the dispute.
Wilson’s lawyer, Allyson Thompson, rejected the allegations, describing the latest filing as another attempt to damage her client’s reputation. Thompson said the case remained heavily contested and that a robust response opposing the motion was being prepared.
The dispute began in 2024, when producers associated with The Deb sued Wilson for defamation after she made allegations concerning the film’s finances and claims involving its star, Charlotte MacInnes.
MacInnes has separately accused Wilson of defamation over statements made online. However, a judge ruled in Wilson’s favour in that case earlier in 2026, according to the report.
The controversy also involves an incident in 2023, when Ghost and MacInnes took a bath together after swimming at Bondi Beach in Sydney. MacInnes said she willingly entered the bath while wearing a bathing suit to warm up after experiencing an adverse reaction to cold seawater. Wilson later suggested online that MacInnes had been uncomfortable during the incident.
Ghost’s legal team has challenged Wilson’s conduct during the current litigation, while Wilson’s representatives maintain that the latest accusations are an attempt to vilify her.
A trial in Los Angeles is scheduled for January 2027. The allegations in the latest filing remain disputed, and the court has not been reported to have made a final determination on the producers’ claims of misconduct.

title: US launches immigration raid of Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar s home
description: Trump has repeatedly insulted Omar  portraying Minnesota s Somali American community as a threat
content:
Trump has repeatedly insulted Omar, portraying Minnesota's Somali American community as a threat
US authorities conducted a predawn Monday raid on the Washington-area home of Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar as part ​of an ongoing investigation, the Justice Department said.
The raid followed a criminal ‌fraud investigation into the Somali-born lawmaker's immigration paperwork, which was filled out by her late father when she was a child, Fox News Digital reported, citing unidentified sources.
"Today in the Washington, D.C. area, Homeland Security Investigations executed ​a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice. This enforcement ​action is part of an ongoing federal investigation," a Department of Justice ⁠spokesperson said in an email.
A representative for Omar did not immediately respond to a ​request for comment.
The raid came a little more than three weeks before the November 3 ​midterm elections, when President Donald Trump's Republicans will be trying to defend their thin majorities in the US Congress.
Omar has been a frequent target of political insults from Trump, who has cast the Somali American community ​as a threat to Minnesota in a burst of anti-Somali and anti-Muslim rhetoric.
Omar, ​an outspoken critic of Trump, has called his focus on her an "unhealthy and creepy obsession."
Last week, Trump called ‌Democratic ⁠candidate for US Senate from Michigan Abdul El-Sayed, who is Muslim, a "RADICAL Extremist" and "Terrorist Sympathizer" while offering support for the Republican candidate, Mike Rogers.
Civil rights advocates have criticized the Republican president's rhetoric towards minorities and immigrants, including when he previously called Somalis "garbage."

Trump in February said ​that Omar and Democratic ​Representative Rashida Tlaib of ⁠Michigan, who is also Muslim, should be "institutionalized" and sent back to "where they came from." Both lawmakers had criticized Trump during his State ​of the Union address as he touted his administration's hard-line immigration ​crackdown and its ⁠immigration enforcement actions.
The progressive lawmaker has repeatedly said she and her family have faced death threats, which she attributes to "hateful political rhetoric" especially from Trump.
Last month, a Minnesota man who squirted ⁠vinegar on ​Omar was sentenced to one year and two months in ​prison after pleading guilty to assaulting a federal official. Anthony James Kazmierczak admitted to attacking Omar because he ​disagreed with her progressive political views.

title: Zara Larsson teams up with Erewhon to support Malala Fund through  21 smoothie
description: Singer supports the nonprofit   s mission to secure 12 years of free  safe and quality education for every girl
content:
Singer supports the nonprofit’s mission to secure 12 years of free, safe and quality education for every girl
Swedish pop star Zara Larsson has partnered with California-based luxury grocery chain Erewhon to launch a limited-edition smoothie supporting the work of the Malala Fund , the nonprofit co-founded by Pakistani Nobel laureate Malala Yousafzai and her father, Ziauddin Yousafzai.
Larsson announced the collaboration on Instagram, sharing a photo dump in partnership with the Los Angeles-based grocery chain.
Named the Midnight Sun Smoothie after Larsson’s album of the same name, the drink draws inspiration from the singer’s musical identity while bringing a girls’ education initiative into the celebrity food collaboration.
“The Midnight Sun Smoothie by Zara Larsson. Inspired by her album, Midnight Sun, this free-spirited blend captures the essence of an eternal summer, layering organic fruits and organic coconut cream into a smoothie reminiscent of a tropical sunset,” Erewhon said in the product description.
According to Erewhon’s product listing , the 20-ounce drink combines coconut milk, dragon fruit punch, blueberries, banana, strawberries, mango and pineapple. Other ingredients include coconut water, carrot juice, colostrum, whey protein, grass-fed collagen, spirulina, lion’s mane and cordyceps.
The collaboration also supports the Malala Fund’s mission to secure every girl’s right to 12 years of free, safe and quality education. “With this smoothie, Erewhon proudly supports Malala Fund — a nonprofit founded by Malala Yousafzai and her father to drive sustainable change toward every girl’s right to 12 years of free, safe, quality education,” the company said.
The limited-edition smoothie launched on October 8 and is available at Erewhon locations across Southern California and at its Manhattan tonic bar in New York. Priced at $21, it is scheduled to remain on sale until November 7. Customers in Manhattan can also order it through Uber Eats and Postmates.
Hydration brand ROAR Organic is also involved in the launch. The brand confirmed its participation and highlighted the collaboration’s connection to girls’ education.
Founded in 2013, the Malala Fund works to advance every girl’s right to 12 years of free, safe and quality education. Through grantmaking and advocacy, the organisation supports efforts to address the barriers that prevent girls from attending and completing school. Its work includes countries such as Pakistan and Afghanistan, where girls continue to face significant obstacles to education.
According to the organisation’s official overview of girls’ education , poverty, gender discrimination, conflict and inadequate educational resources are among the factors that keep girls out of school.
The collaboration offers Larsson’s fans an opportunity to engage with a cause beyond her music while drawing attention to the global struggle for girls’ education. By connecting a pop-culture name with an established education campaign, the partnership brings the issue of girls’ access to schooling into an unexpected setting.

title: Stolen Renoir paintings found behind wall in France  prosecutor
description: In Sept  thieves broke into Cagnes sur Mer and escaped with two works by Renoir  abandoning two others as they fled
content:
In Sept, thieves broke into Cagnes-sur-Mer and escaped with two works by Renoir, abandoning two others as they fled
Two paintings by impressionist master Pierre-Auguste Renoir, stolen from a museum in southern France and later discovered hidden behind a wall, have sustained slight damage, prosecutors said on Monday.
In September, thieves broke into the museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer and escaped with two works by Renoir, abandoning two others as they fled.
The value of all four paintings had been estimated at nine million euros ($10 million).
On Friday, authorities announced that the two outstanding stolen works had been found.
They were a portrait titled "Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano" and a depiction of a woman at a well called "Young Woman at the Well".
Speaking to reporters in Paris, Marseille prosecutor Nicolas Bessone said the paintings were recovered last Thursday during a search of a home in the southern town of Clermont-l'Herault.
The discovery of the stolen works followed the arrest of six people, including a woman, last Wednesday, said Bessone.
"The paintings were hidden behind a solid cinderblock wall. They were completely undetectable," Bessone said.
"It was through interrogation work that investigators were able to get the receiver of the stolen goods to admit that he had indeed taken possession of the paintings."
A 29-year-old man seen as the main suspect was charged at the weekend after DNA evidence linked him to the theft.
The two paintings were "in relatively good condition", although "the two works showed signs of damage," Bessone said, speaking alongside the head of France's national judicial police, Christian Sainte.
The frame of "Young Woman at the Well" was slightly damaged, while "the canvas of 'Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano' had a tear," Bessone said.
The tear was located "on the dress" in the portrait, the prosecutor said, adding that both paintings "will require restoration work".
Culture Minister Catherine Pegard praised "the efficiency and determination of all those who made this outcome possible."
"Their commitment made it possible to recover these works in record time," the culture ministry said.
A spate of heists at French museums -- including at the Louvre -- has highlighted inadequate security in some cases and led to questions about whether criminal gangs see them as soft targets.
Crown jewels valued at around $100 million were stolen in broad daylight from the Louvre in Paris last year.
While the four suspected Louvre robbers were arrested, the jewels they are accused of grabbing in the seven-minute heist have still not been found.

Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir has emphasised Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening defence ties with Brazil, the military’s media wing said on Monday.

title: Alcaraz exits Shanghai Masters  | The Express Tribune
description: Spaniard suffers a shocking defeat to Bergs in the third round
content:
Spaniard suffers a shocking defeat to Bergs in the third round
Carlos Alcaraz fell to Zizou Bergs in straight sets at the Shanghai Masters on Monday, interrupting the former world number one's in-form return to the professional Tour after being sidelined for months by injury.
The 39th-ranked Belgian beat the second-seeded Spanish star 7-5, 7-6 (7/4) in the third round to land the tournament's biggest upset yet, and will play either Tommy Paul or Valentin Vacherot next.
"It's a little disbelief and not feeling too much," Bergs, 27, said afterwards.
"You're just really in the moment, being focused on the points you have to play," he added.
Alcaraz started with more quality until Bergs broke the Spaniard's serve to go up 3-2 in the first set.
The 23-year-old grabbed back that break in the next game but was uncharacteristically off-target, sending a mess of shots into the net.
He double-faulted to hand Bergs a critical break point in the 11th game, and lost the first set when a volley went short.
Alcaraz was visibly frustrated during the second set as he vented to his corner following a series of misfired shots that left him with no points in the fourth and eighth games.
Alcaraz forced a tie-break but could not reach a third set as Bergs closed things out just past the two-hour mark on his first match point.
Earlier, Stefanos Tsitsipas came back to beat Taylor Fritz 3-6, 7-5, 6-3 and earn fourth round meeting with Daniil Medvedev, who brushed aside qualifier Dalibor Svrcina 6-2, 6-3.
A wardrobe malfunction delayed victory for the Greek world number 43 when a tennis ball tumbled out of the American's pocket a second time and forced the men to replay a match point.
A tired-looking Fritz, seeded 11th, hung on for a bit longer to save the eighth game but could not stick around beyond that, with Tsitsipas holding serve to win at the fifth time of asking.
"I could have done a few things easier, but I ended up being my biggest enemy," Tsitsipas told the crowd afterwards.
"I turned things around really well towards the end and became friends with myself and played some incredible tennis," he said.
Felix Auger-Aliassime, Casper Ruud and Rafael Jodar also went through to the last 16.
