title: SSGC dominate National Cycling Championship
description: Army finish second as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa secure third place
content:
Army finish second as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa secure third place
Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) finished at the summit, followed by Pakistan Army and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, as the 10th National Road Cycling Championship concluded at Bahria Town Karachi on Sunday.
SSGC won the championship with 16 medals, including 11 gold, three silver and two bronze. Pakistan Army finished runners-up with nine medals, comprising two gold, four silver and three bronze, while Khyber Pakhtunkhwa secured third place with seven medals, including two silver and five bronze.
Ahmad Shahzad (Balochistan), Mohammad (Sindh) and Muneeb (Punjab) emerged as the leading young riders while Sindh’s Samar, Punjab’s Christina Haroon and Hoorin Yahya from Crank Addicts stole limelight as young female pedallists.
Organised by the Pakistan Cycling Federation (PCF), the three-day championship attracted cyclists from across the country, who competed in men’s, women’s, junior, masters and other categories.
Teams representing SSGC, Pakistan Army, Pakistan Ordnance Factories (POF), Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, Sindh, Balochistan, Islamabad, Gilgit-Baltistan Scouts and other organisations took part in individual time trials, team time trials and road races.
POF won three gold medals, while Balochistan secured one gold to complete the list of gold-medal-winning teams.
The inclusion of masters’ categories for cyclists aged 40-49 and 50 and above was a notable feature of this year’s championship. The event also provided young male and female cyclists with an opportunity to demonstrate their potential and gain valuable competitive experience.
The closing ceremony was held on Sunday, with HabibMetro Bank senior executive Sharifa Haider Ali attending as chief guest and distributing prizes among the outstanding performers.
The PCF also announced plans to explore the possibility of hosting the South Asian Road Cycling Championship at Bahria Town Karachi next year, subject to consultations and approval from the relevant international cycling authorities and other stakeholders.
The proposed event aims to provide Pakistani cyclists with greater exposure to regional competition and promote the country as a venue for international sporting events.
The federation, however, expressed concern over the lack of an annual grant or financial assistance from the Pakistan Sports Board, saying limited resources had made it increasingly difficult to organise national-level competitions.
It said the championship had been staged with support from sponsors and called on government institutions, private-sector companies and sports bodies to provide greater assistance for the development of cycling in Pakistan.

title: Man City silence Liverpool crowd
description: Enzo Maresca   s men seal an emphatic win to extend their lead at the top of the Premier League
content:
Enzo Maresca’s men seal an emphatic win to extend their lead at the top of the Premier League
Manchester City silenced a hostile Liverpool crowd in their first match since being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations but there is a deep sense of uncertainty over what it actually means.
Enzo Maresca's men are top of the table with six wins out of six after their impressive 3-0 win at Anfield on Sunday.
Yet those points could count for nothing unless City are successful in their appeal against the findings of an independent commission that found them guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League rules.
No sanction has yet been decided, but the club could face a severe points deduction leading to relegation, or even expulsion from the English top flight.
There is even speculation that City could be stripped of the three Premier League titles they won between 2009 and 2018, the period to which the charges relate.
The Premier League, which has a huge global reach, faces an appeal process likely to drag on for months, putting a question mark against every City result, and with huge potential implications for other clubs.
"We're sat here not knowing what it means," former Manchester United captain turned pundit Gary Neville told Sky Sports on Sunday.
"City supporters will be delighted (with the win), but I don't think they recognise right now the stain, the stigma and the damage this is going to do to them."
The BBC's chief football writer, Phil McNulty, said the team's impressive win at Anfield had been overshadowed by what was happening off the pitch.
"Every victory, every league table, will come with a metaphorical asterisk until clarity and finality comes," he said. "No one knows when this will be."
Andoni Iraola's Liverpool are ninth in the table, nine points behind leaders City.
But even if Liverpool fail to challenge for the title, the three points lost on Sunday could cost them dearly in the battle for a place in the Champions League.
Potential sanctions against City could also have an impact on the battle for relegation.
"That today, what does it mean going forward?" former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher said on Sky Sports.
"This has to be done before the end of the season. There's no way this can carry on to the end of the season because we're all getting kidded."
The Premier League announced late last month that an independent commission had found that City had arranged "sham" deals to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion) between 2009 and 2018.
Liverpool feel particularly aggrieved, having finished second behind the Manchester club in the Premier League three times in the past 12 years.
City's rivals believe the Abu Dhabi-backed club's spending in the 2009-2018 period built the foundations for a golden era that continues to bear fruit.
The Premier League leaders spent around £460 million ($609 million) in the 2026 summer transfer window -- a new Premier League record for a single window -- as new boss Maresca reshaped the squad following the departure of Pep Guardiola.
One of City's expensive new signings, midfielder Elliot Anderson, admitted the criticism of the club had galvanised the players as they stepped out at Anfield.
"We've got to stick together," said the England midfielder. "I think it really brings us together. It gives you that determination to come out here, everyone is against you, and turn them over, which we did."
Anderson and his teammates will have to get used to their new reality as the whole of English football waits for a definitive decision in a case that has rumbled on for years.
As chants, banners, flags and scarves at Anfield showed, City stand accused of cheating their way to the top -- and opposition fans will not be silenced.

title: Pakistan stands shoulder to shoulder with Saudi Arabia  petroleum minister
description: Ali Pervaiz Malik condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia  holds talks on diversifying energy supplies
content:
Ali Pervaiz Malik condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, holds talks on diversifying energy supplies
Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik on Monday said Pakistan stood shoulder to shoulder with Saudi Arabia during its current difficulties, condemning Houthi attacks on Saudi territory and expressing solidarity with the Kingdom.
“Pakistan strongly condemns the terrorist attacks by the Houthi militia on Saudi soil,” Malik said, while offering condolences over the loss of precious lives.
He made the remarks while addressing a plenary session titled “Investment and Trade in Sustainable Energy Solutions: Making Energy Clean, Accessible and Affordable” at the 17th International Energy Forum (IEF) Ministerial Meeting in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
According to a press release, Malik attended the meeting at the invitation of Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud. His participation, he said, reflected Pakistan’s solidarity with the Kingdom, in line with the instructions of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir.
Highlights of Participation of Pakistan's delegation led by Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik in the International Energy forum (IEF) 2026 in Riyadh pic.twitter.com/RVjHpMd53h
Addressing the forum, Malik said the global energy sector was entering a new investment cycle in which energy security, affordability and sustainability needed to advance together.
He stressed the need for investment not only in renewable energy but also in hydrocarbons, critical minerals and essential infrastructure, including electricity grids and pipelines.
Referring to the unprecedented global energy supply shock of 2026, the minister said the crisis had extended beyond oil and gas to affect shipping and insurance.
Despite its heavy reliance on imported energy, Pakistan had navigated the crisis without rationing major energy sources, supported by the government’s response and cooperation from friendly countries, including Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Kuwait, he said.
Also Read: Govt says petroleum levy non-tax revenue
Malik also thanked Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman for personally steering energy cooperation with Pakistan.
The minister said Pakistan was working to strengthen its long-term energy security through strategic reserves, a world-class bonded reserves scheme, increased domestic energy production and investment in critical infrastructure, including refineries and tank farms.
He also highlighted efforts to develop competitive electricity and gas markets and introduce targeted relief mechanisms.
International investment and trade frameworks, he stressed, needed to balance innovation and sustainability with affordability, equity and access. Pakistan looked forward to working with all IEF member countries to advance shared energy security objectives for future generations, he added.
Pakistan seeks Libyan crude oil supplies
On the sidelines of the IEF ministerial meeting, Malik met Libyan Minister of Oil and Gas Khalifa Rajab Abdulsadek to discuss ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in the oil and gas sector.
The petroleum minister informed his Libyan counterpart that Pakistan had encouraged its refineries to explore importing Libyan crude oil as part of efforts to diversify supply sources and strengthen energy security.
Riyadh: Federal Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik met Libya’s Minister of Oil & Gas, H.E. Khalifa Rajab Abdulsadek, on the sidelines of the IEF Ministerial Meeting to discuss oil and gas cooperation, including Libyan crude oil supplies to Pak and collaboration on refinery upgradation pic.twitter.com/TMGqDCLNpy
He said Pakistan aimed to maintain alternative supply options in the event of disruptions to key maritime routes, including the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
The Libyan minister described Pakistan as an important country for Libya and said he would encourage the country’s national oil company to allocate greater volumes of crude oil to Pakistani companies.
Abdulsadek also said Libya was planning to upgrade its refineries and expressed interest in learning from Pakistan’s experience in refinery upgradation.
Malik also held a detailed breakfast meeting with Qatar’s Energy Minister Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi to explore potential cooperation in the liquefied natural gas (LNG) sector.
Separately, Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar met Malik on the sidelines of the forum and expressed his intention to visit Pakistan next month to receive the Turkish Petroleum Corporation’s (TPAO) seismic vessel, which is expected to begin data acquisition in the Indus Basin.
Riyadh: On the sidelines of IEF, Turkish Energy Minister HE Alparslan Bayraktar called on the Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and stated he was looking forward to visiting Pakistan next month to receive TPAO seismic vessel to start data acquisition in Indus Basin. pic.twitter.com/RHyaZ5M0Ff
Malik also met other global energy leaders, including ministers and heads of energy companies, to discuss cooperation and investment opportunities.
The meetings underscored Pakistan’s focus on international energy cooperation, diversification of supply sources, resilient energy infrastructure and investment in a secure, affordable and sustainable energy future.

title: Andrew Garfield responds to Oscar buzz for Sam Altman film    Artificial
description: The Luca Guadagnino film explores OpenAI   s turbulent five day leadership crisis in 2023
content:
The Luca Guadagnino film explores OpenAI’s turbulent five day leadership crisis in 2023
Andrew Garfield has responded modestly to growing Oscar speculation surrounding his performance as OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman in Artificial , following an enthusiastic reception at the film’s London premiere.
Speaking to Variety on the red carpet at the BFI LONDON FILM FESTIVAL on October 11, Garfield said he was proud of the project but remained focused on making work he believed in rather than awards predictions.
“As I’m getting older, I’m starting to understand that the things outside of ourselves, we just have no control over,” he said. “I feel really, really proud of this film.”
Directed by Luca Guadagnino, Artificial examines the five day period in 2023 when Altman was removed as OpenAI’s chief executive before returning to the role. The film premiered at the NEW YORK FILM FESTIVAL last week and has drawn attention for its portrayal of influential figures in the technology industry.
Garfield, who has received two Oscar nominations, said he felt grateful that audiences would see the film at all, describing the positive response as an unexpected bonus.
Yura Borisov, who portrays OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever, also reacted to the awards discussion with surprise, saying the outcome remained unpredictable. Borisov previously received an Academy Award nomination for his supporting performance in Anora .
The cast also includes Monica Barbaro as former OpenAI chief technology officer Mira Murati, Ike Barinholtz as Elon Musk and Mark Rylance as artificial intelligence expert Geoffrey Hinton.
Garfield said the film felt particularly relevant because its central figures continue to influence public conversations about artificial intelligence. Barbaro similarly noted that AI is being used across industries, making it important to question the motives behind powerful technologies.
The film has also attracted scrutiny after Amazon MGM Studios dropped it in June, shortly after Amazon announced a $50 billion investment in OpenAI. Neon subsequently acquired the film for distribution and began an awards campaign.
Artificial is scheduled to open in US cinemas on December 25, 2026, followed by a UK release on January 22, 2027.

title: Microsoft president says milk faces more regulation than AI
description: Says there should also be a legal requirement    for companies to write  incident reports
content:
Says there should also be a legal requirement ​for companies to write 'incident reports'
Artificial Intelligence needs urgent global regulation with independent evaluators able to vet new developments, the president of Microsoft said, warning that AI currently faces fewer ​safety requirements than milk.
In an interview with the BBC published on ‌Monday, Brad Smith said a set of global safety rules needed to be in place, requiring a "victim" to be informed if their system is breached by a rogue AI agent ​and an "emergency brake" available.
He said there should also be a legal requirement ​for companies to write "incident reports".
"We know how to do this ⁠for other products," Smith said. "We should build on that knowledge and think about ​how to apply it to AI."
Read: AI to be used in online child abuse probes
"Right now, your washing machine is subject to ​more safety rules than AI. Every carton of milk that you see in the grocery store is subject to safety rules and inspection."
Tech companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI have started disclosing rogue ​or undesired behaviour by AI agents as part of a global debate about ​the fast-advancing technology that has included researchers' warnings of an eventual existential threat to humanity.
Some companies ‌have ⁠called for AI development to slow down, but that has sparked a debate as to whether executives have ulterior motives such as setting rules that preserve the lead of their firms, pre-empting a broader government backlash, or simply slowing ​breakneck spending.
Read more: 3 in 5 AI models fail terrorism safety tests: Study
Microsoft's Smith said ​the one country ⁠that was well-placed to lead the way on regulation of AI was Britain, due to the AI Security Institute ​which was launched under former prime minister Rishi Sunak.
Smith said ​officials in ⁠Washington viewed London very differently to how they viewed Brussels, which regulates AI based on the level of risk via its AI Act.
Britain's institute receives pre-deployment access ⁠under voluntary ​agreements with the major AI models, allowing it ​to assess their capabilities and risks.
AI Minister Kanishka Narayan has told Reuters that Britain would consider regulating ​advanced models if the current system proved insufficient.

description: Gaza documentary  NAZA  surpasses  500k in North America box office amid protest over portrayal of Israel   s military
content:
Gaza documentary 'NAZA' surpasses $500k in North America box office amid protest over portrayal of Israel’s military
The Gaza documentary NAZA has surpassed $500,000 in projected North American box office takings despite being released without a traditional distributor, as screenings have drawn protests over its portrayal of Israel’s military operations in Gaza.
Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, who also worked on the 2024 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land , NAZA expanded to 85 locations across 30 North American cities during its second weekend in cinemas.
The film was expected to earn $378,250 over the four-day weekend, averaging $4,450 per screen. Its domestic total was projected to reach $504,074 by Monday, according to figures reported by The Hollywood Reporter.
NAZA premiered at the Venice Film Festival, where it received the special jury prize and a reported standing ovation lasting more than 20 minutes.
The documentary is being released independently in the United States with support from The Guardian and MK2, with further cinema screenings planned in the coming weeks.
The film has also attracted criticism. The Israeli-American Council organised a protest outside a screening at the Laemmle NoHo 7 cinema in North Hollywood on Friday.
The organisation had previously arranged protests during the documentary’s premiere at the New York Film Festival in September.
IAC chief operating officer Aya Shechter said in a statement, “Our message is clear: Wherever lies are told about Israel, we will show up with the truth.”
Earlier this month, the Israeli Defense Force criticised the documentary, describing it as “a distorted, misleading and disingenuous picture of the IDF's target planning and striking process.”
Despite the controversy, NAZA has received a 100 per cent critics’ approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.
In his review for The Hollywood Reporter, Jordan Mintzer described the film as a “sober and thoroughly documented bombshell of an exposé”.

title: Russell Brand   s criminal trial begins in London over rape and sexual assault charges
description: Russell Brand has pleaded not guilty to seven sexual offence charges in the UK  with his trial at Southwark Crown Court expected to last up to two months
content:
Russell Brand has pleaded not guilty to seven sexual offence charges in the UK with his trial at Southwark Crown Court
British comedian and former actor Russell Brand has arrived at Southwark Crown Court in London as his criminal trial begins over seven sexual offence charges. He has pleaded not guilty to all charges.
Brand faces three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault. The charges were brought by the UK’s Crown Prosecution Service in April and December 2025, following a Metropolitan Police investigation.
The first set of charges relates to alleged offences between 1999 and 2005 involving four women. The additional charges concern two further women and relate to alleged incidents in 2009.
Brand arrived at court on Monday wearing a grey suit and sunglasses, accompanied by his wife, Laura Gallacher, whom he married in 2017. The trial is expected to last up to two months, with a jury of 12 set to determine the outcome. Brand remains on bail.
Jury selection is expected to take place at the start of proceedings, with opening statements from the prosecution and defence tentatively scheduled for Wednesday.
Brand rose to prominence in the mid-2000s as a comedian and actor, presenting television programmes including Big Brother’s Big Mouth and appearing in Hollywood films such as Forgetting Sarah Marshall and Get Him to the Greek . In recent years, he has shifted towards podcasting and online content creation.
In September 2023, The Sunday Times , The Times and Channel 4’s Dispatches published allegations of sexual assault, rape and emotional abuse against Brand following a joint investigation. Brand strongly denied the allegations.
The investigation prompted a police inquiry, which ultimately led to the criminal charges. The Crown Prosecution Service said the charges followed a review of evidence gathered by police.
The CPS has also emphasised that criminal proceedings are active and that Brand is entitled to a fair trial. The charges remain allegations, and the jury will determine the case based on the evidence presented in court.

title: Americans Hall and Woodford win Nobel economics prize for work on stabilisation
description: The two developed new macroeconomic models that improved the ability    to implement effective stabilisation policy
content:
The two developed new macroeconomic models that improved the ability ​to implement effective stabilisation policy
US academics Robert Hall and Michael Woodford won the 2026 Nobel economics prize for "for microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic ​stabilisation", the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences said on Monday.
The prestigious ‌award, formally known as the Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel, is the final prize to be given out this year and is worth 12 million Swedish ​crowns ($1.2 million).
The two laureates developed new macroeconomic models that improved our ability ​to implement effective stabilisation policy, enabling well-timed fiscal and monetary policy measures ⁠that can reduce the intensity of damaging swings in the economy.
"The laureates’ work ​has provided us with a stable theoretical foundation for the models that are now ​used by central banks and governments around the world," John Hassler, Chair of the Committee for the Prize in Economic Sciences, said in a statement.
Read: Navi Pillay’s Nobel Peace Prize is a rebuke to Trump
"With them, we are better equipped to deal ​with shocks in the economy, such as energy crises or sudden changes in how ​much households consume."
The economics prize, first awarded in 1969, is not one of the original five ‌awards ⁠created in the 1895 will of industrialist and dynamite inventor Alfred Nobel, but was established by Sweden's central bank.
The majority of previous laureates have been from the United States. Only three women have ever won, most recently Claudia Goldin in 2023 for ​work on how gender ​has affected pay ⁠and employment over time in the United States.
Analysis by the Institute for Scientific Information, part of Clarivate, had picked researchers working ​on monetary policy, the economics of information technology and evolutionary ​economic theory ⁠as possible recipients.
Last year's winners, Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt, won for work on "creative destruction" and how new technology and production methods can boost growth and living ⁠standards.

description: Abduction of Palestinians by Israeli occupiers on rise in occupied West Bank  Officials
content:
Abduction of Palestinians by Israeli occupiers on rise in occupied West Bank: officials
Israeli army fire killed five Palestinians in the Gaza Strip over the past 24 hours, bringing the death toll from Israel’s genocidal war since October 2023 to 74,382, the Health Ministry said Monday.
In its daily statistical report, the ministry said the toll included three new fatalities and two people who died of earlier wounds, while 18 people were injured in attacks over the past day, raising the overall number of injuries to 175,416.
Despite a ceasefire in effect since Oct. 10, 2025, Israel has continued daily attacks in the enclave, killing 1,493 Palestinians and injuring 5,299 others, according to the ministry.
Israel’s war has also caused widespread destruction affecting around 90% of Gaza’s civilian infrastructure, with an international report estimating recovery and reconstruction costs at around $71.4 billion.
The Israeli military claimed it targeted a combatant in the area, without giving further information.
Late on Sunday, an ​Israeli airstrike hit a tent in the ​Mawasi area of Khan Younis in southern ⁠Gaza, killing three people, medics said. The Israeli ​military claimed to Reuters on Monday they struck combatants in ​the area.
Israel, which alleges Hamas has been rearming and launching attacks in violation of a ceasefire, has stepped up ​strikes on the group in recent weeks.
Hamas has ​denied attempting to carry out attacks or rebuild its arsenal, saying that Israel is undermining the Gaza peace deal.
Last year's US-brokered Gaza ceasefire calls for the eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made ​towards implementing ​a deal ⁠to end the conflict that includes terms for Hamas to disarm and Israel ​to withdraw its troops.
Gaza health officials ​have ⁠said at least 1,400 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli fire since the October 2025 ceasefire. Israel ⁠says ​four of its soldiers have ​been killed by militants in Gaza over the same period.
Abduction of Palestinians by Israeli occupiers on the rise in occupied West Bank: Officials
Abductions and arbitrary detention of Palestinians by Israeli occupiers have increased across the occupied West Bank, particularly targeting farmers and rural communities, Palestinian officials and rights groups said Monday.
Read: Israel strikes Gaza on October 7 anniversary, at least two dead: officials
Salah al-Khawaja, director of the Colonisation and Wall Resistance Commission’s office in the central West Bank, told Anadolu that such incidents were often accompanied by abuse and violence.
“Palestinians were being detained at makeshift checkpoints or seized during attacks on farmers and rural and Bedouin communities,” he said.
Amir Daoud, the commission’s documentation official, said the repeated attacks make farmers fear for their lives and freedom when accessing their land and could discourage them from reaching their fields.
“The impact of the attacks extends from the victim to the entire village and becomes a means of intimidating residents and weakening their connection to their land,” Daoud said.
The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said in May 2025 that it had documented around 36 incidents since October 2023 in which Israeli occupiers, some wearing military uniforms, abducted or detained at least 50 Palestinians, including three children.
Palestinian rights group Al-Haq also said in a September 24 report that documented cases showed an “increasing pattern” of abductions and unlawful arbitrary detentions.
In the latest reported incidents, Israeli occupiers abducted seven Palestinians on Saturday, according to the official Voice of Palestine radio.
The outlet said three abductions were reported in Nahalin west of Bethlehem, three in Qaffin north of Tulkarem and a farmer in Beit Imrin near Nablus, adding that their fate was not immediately known.
Daoud accused the Israeli army of protecting occupiers during some incidents, saying the Qaffin attack took place under army protection.
Settlement affairs researcher Jamal Juma said the abductions were part of a “systematic policy” targeting Palestinian presence in Area C, which makes up around 60% of the occupied West Bank and remains under full Israeli control.
Under the 1995 Oslo II Agreement, which was intended as a temporary arrangement, the occupied West Bank was divided into Areas A, B and C.
Area A is under full Palestinian civil and security control, Area B under Palestinian civil and Israeli security control, while Area C remains under full Israeli control and makes up around 60% of the West Bank.
The incidents have drawn particular concern during the olive harvest season, when Palestinian farmers face attacks including beatings, denial of access to fields, theft of crops and damage to trees.

According to the official Colonisation and Wall Resistance Commission, more than 26,000 olive trees were cut down or damaged across the West Bank during the first half of 2026.
The olive harvest season began on Sept. 20 with olives intended for pickling, while harvesting varieties used for olive oil production is scheduled to begin on Oct. 15.
Since Israel began its genocide in Gaza in October 2023, attacks by the Israeli army and occupiers against Palestinians and their property have intensified across the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem.
The attacks include killings and arrests of Palestinians, the demolition of homes and structures, the burning of mosques and vehicles, bulldozing of agricultural land, preventing farmers from reaching their fields, stealing crops, displacement and illegal settlement expansion.
Palestinians warn that Israel is paving the way through such measures for the formal annexation of the West Bank, in a move that would undermine the possibility of establishing a Palestinian state as envisioned in relevant UN resolutions.

description: Achakzai says Balochistan has become no go area for security forces  yet its CM remains your  blue eyed boy
content:
Achakzai says Balochistan has become no-go area for security forces, yet its CM remains your 'blue-eyed boy'
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Monday said he would personally challenge the emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) in the Peshawar High Court tomorrow, as the party vowed to continue its long march.
Speaking at a press conference outside Parliament alongside Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Opposition Leader in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, Gohar said the party would decide at its parliamentary party meeting on Tuesday how to oppose the measures in the provincial assembly.
“We will raise our voices on every forum. Our long march is ongoing, and our protests are continuing. We will not accept this,” he said, adding that the demonstrations would continue.
Gohar called October 11 a “black day” in Pakistan’s democratic history, saying the people of K-P had rejected emergency measures and governor’s rule, and that the provincial chief minister had been kept in custody and claimed that supporters of the party were in jail.
“We demand that the measures taken on October 11 be withdrawn,” he said, adding that the party would challenge the decision through all channels. He said he would personally challenge the decisions taken on October 11 in the Peshawar High Court, adding that the party was also pursuing a legal challenge.
The PTI chairman accused the government of showing stubbornness and said the provincial government machinery had been changed abruptly. He said the party had remained in contact with the government until the very last moment, but the situation had deteriorated.
“The federation will be strong only when the provinces are strong,” he said.
Gohar urged the government not to divide the public in the fight against terrorism, calling terrorism a “menace for Pakistan”. He said Pakistan’s future lay in democracy and that the federation would only be strong when its provinces were strong.
Speaking alongside Gohar, Achakzai said that opposition parties would stage protests across Pakistan against the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency measures in K-P, vowing to continue a peaceful democratic struggle alongside efforts to negotiate with the government.
He said his party would direct opposition groups to protest according to their capacity and announce a democratic movement in every district where emergency measures had not been imposed.
“We will hold peaceful protests,” he said, adding that the opposition was ready for all forms of negotiations to achieve a democratic Pakistan.
Achakzai criticised the decision to impose governor’s rule and emergency measures in K-P, calling it a major attack. He said he had been raising concerns about the Constitution when the measures were imposed and argued that the situation in Balochistan was worse than the circumstances cited to justify governor’s rule in K-P.
“Balochistan’s chief minister is your blue-eyed boy, but you take no action against what is being looted there,” he said, adding that half of Balochistan had become a no-go area for security forces.
The opposition leader also criticised the government over the February 8 elections, alleging that people’s consciences had been bought and sold through money and coercion. He claimed that voters had elected the PTI founder Imran Khan but that the party had been denied its mandate.
Read: ‘Afridi, some of his cabinet members have been taken into preventive custody,’ confirms Talal
“Forty million people’s right to vote has been mocked,” he said, adding that Pakistan would progress only when Parliament was strong.
Achakzai said the Constitution provided for Parliament and the judiciary and stipulated that Parliament would formulate policies, with all institutions required to operate within constitutional limits. He added that Article 6 applied to those who violated the Constitution.
“The current government is the biggest terrorist,” he said, warning that political parties supporting what he called terrorism would become part of history. He also said that the PTI was not even being allowed to grieve over the theft of its mandate.
Achakzai called for permission to meet Imran, saying he was willing to provide a written assurance that he would not disclose anything discussed during the meeting. “This government wants Imran to leave the country, but he is not leaving,” he said.
He also rejected the suggestion that he did not want to meet the prime minister, saying he was willing to meet but would not go to the Prime Minister’s House or the Speaker’s Office. He said the opposition would continue its struggle against the existing system while pursuing negotiations.
Read more: Govt appoints Yahya Akhunzada to K-P administration
On the occasion, Raja Nasir Abbas also rejected the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency measures, saying the country was dealing with “deceivers and liars”. He said the unanimously agreed Constitution was being made controversial and accused the government of equating political workers with terrorists.
“We have to contend with those who violate the Constitution,” Abbas said, calling for unity in the fight against terrorism. “Let us join hands with the people of the province to fight terrorists,” he added.
Questioning the justification for imposing emergency measures in K-P, Abbas said the law and order situation in Balochistan was worse and argued that emergency should be imposed there instead. He warned that the situation could deteriorate further if the public did not stand together, saying matters had already gone too far.
Earlier, a petition challenging the imposition of emergency measures and governor’s rule in K-P was also filed in the PHC.
The petition was filed by Advocate Salman; the petition named President Zardari, PM Shehbaz and K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi as respondents. It argued that the measures were unconstitutional, illegal and mala fide, and violated fundamental rights, provincial autonomy and the democratic mandate.
The petitioner asked the court to declare the imposition of emergency measures and governor’s rule null and void, and sought suspension of the notification imposing governor’s rule until a final decision on the case.
Federal government imposes emergency, governor’s rule
As the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s (PTI) long march entered the end of its first week, the federal government imposed emergency measures and governor’s rule in K-P, escalating tensions between the centre and the province’s opposition-led political leadership.
PTI leaders rejected the imposition, calling the move undemocratic and vowing to challenge it through constitutional forums. Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman also criticised the decision, accusing the federal government of backtracking on its commitments amid negotiations with the PTI over its long march. The Tehreek-e-Tahafuz Aain-e-Pakistan (TTAP), also condemned the measures and vowed to challenge them through the courts, assemblies and public forums.
Initially planning to launch the long march on September 27, Afridi on September 26 rescheduled the protest to take place on October 4 amid extensive security and traffic restrictions and continuing efforts to negotiate with the federal government.
Marathon talks between the government and the opposition on October 2 and 3 failed to find middle ground in an effort to ease tensions ahead of the long march, as both sides pressed competing demands and remained at an impasse. PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja later said that the deadlock in negotiations with the federal government emerged over the issue of the counterterrorism policy in K-P.
Amid prevailing tensions, the breakdown of negotiations, and Afridi proceeding with the march, President Asif Ali Zardari signed off on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s recommendation to impose emergency rule in K-P amid a deteriorating security situation and the provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism.
The proclamation said the provincial government had failed to take adequate measures against terrorism and referred to the governor’s report highlighting a breakdown in the constitutional system.
The chief minister, provincial ministers, advisers, special assistants and advocate general ceased to hold office with immediate effect. The federal government subsequently authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets under Article 245 to protect citizens, property and government installations for the duration of the emergency proclamation.

title: Nicolas Cage says he may not work with Amazon again after refusing AI waiver
description: Nicolas Cage says he is unlikely to work with Amazon again after refusing AI waiver for  Spider Noir
content:
Nicolas Cage says he is unlikely to work with Amazon again after refusing AI waiver for 'Spider-Noir'
Nicolas Cage has said he is unlikely to work with Amazon again after refusing to sign an artificial intelligence waiver for Spider-Noir, the superhero series developed for Prime Video.
Speaking during a panel at New York Comic Con on Saturday, the actor criticised Amazon’s reported approach to artificial intelligence and explained why he declined to give permission for his likeness to be used through the technology.
“Amazon is a very AI-friendly company, to the tune of $50 billion invested in OpenAI,” Cage said. “I am not an AI-friendly actor, so it’s like, connect those dots! I’m not a member of their club. I didn’t sign the waiver to let him use AI on ‘Spider Noir.’ I’m probably not going to be working with that studio again, but that’s okay.”
Amazon cancelled Spider-Noir after one season last month, shortly before the first weekend of the Emmy Awards.
The series received 11 nominations, the most of any Prime Video programme that year, and reportedly accumulated 2.6 billion minutes viewed during its first six weeks.
Cage also discussed his interest in working with emerging filmmakers, particularly directors from Generation Z who have built their careers through online platforms.
“I got to get with these young directors who are Gen Z, and they’re going at it their own way, whether it’s through the YouTube culture or whatever it is,” he said. “They’re doing it from scratch and by hand. I want to get with that.”
The actor also indicated that he intends to pursue further television projects following Spider-Noir, which marked his first leading role in a television series.
During the panel, Cage revealed that his next project would involve HBO’s crime anthology True Detective.
“My agent’s out there somewhere listening,” Cage quipped. “That’s okay that I’m the first to announce that, right?”

title: Bryan Cranston reacts to  Breaking Bad  being named best TV show of 21st century
description: Bryan Cranston reacts to  Breaking Bad  topping  The New York Times    list of best TV shows of 21st century
content:
Bryan Cranston reacts to 'Breaking Bad' topping 'The New York Times’ list of best TV shows of 21st century
Bryan Cranston has reacted to Breaking Bad being named the number one television show of the 21st century by The New York Times , describing the recognition as a source of pride for everyone involved in the series.
The actor, 70, discussed the ranking in an exclusive interview with PEOPLE after the AMC drama topped the newspaper’s list of the 100 Best TV Shows of the 21st Century.
“I’m exceedingly proud of that,” Cranston said.
“That’s something that’s voted on. That’s bestowed upon us as the collective who had something to do with that show,” he added.
Breaking Bad ran for five seasons between January 2008 and September 2013. The series followed Walter White, a high school chemistry teacher who begins manufacturing and selling methamphetamine with his former student Jesse Pinkman, played by Aaron Paul, after receiving a diagnosis of stage-three lung cancer.
The cast also included Anna Gunn, Giancarlo Esposito, Bob Odenkirk, Dean Norris, Betsy Brandt, RJ Mitte and Jonathan Banks.
The show received 16 Emmy Awards during its run. Cranston won Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series four times, while Paul received three awards for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series. Gunn won Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Drama Series twice.
The series also expanded into a wider franchise, with Better Call Saul focusing on Odenkirk’s character and the film El Camino: A Breaking Bad Movie continuing Jesse Pinkman’s story.
The New York Times compiled its ranking using votes from 516 television industry professionals, including actors, writers, showrunners and producers. Only programmes that premiered on or after 1 January 2000 were eligible.
Following Breaking Bad, The Wire ranked second, Mad Men placed third, Succession came fourth and Fleabag completed the top five.

title: Two Pakistan Army pilots martyred after training aircraft crashes near Quetta  ISPR
description: The aircraft crashed near Nawan Killi due to a technical fault  the instructor pilot  student pilot were martyred
content:
Says the aircraft crashed near Nawan Killi due to technical fault
Two Pakistan Army pilots were martyred on Monday when a Mushshak training aircraft crashed near Nawan Killi in Quetta due to a technical fault, the military’s media wing said.
“Both pilots, Major Husnain Shehzad Humayun (Instructor Pilot) and Captain Abdul Samad (Student Pilot) embraced Shahadat in the unfortunate crash,” the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement.
It said that the aircraft crashed around midday on 12 October.
🚨 #ISPR Press Release Mid-day 12 October 2026, a Mushshak training aircraft of Pakistan Army Aviation crashed near Nawan Killi, Quetta, Balochistan, due to a technical fault. Both pilots, Major Husnain Shehzad Humayun (Instructor Pilot) and Captain Abdul Samad (Student Pilot)… pic.twitter.com/aKaWFADRcu
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed grief over the martyrdom of the pilots. In separate statements, the president and the prime minister extended their heartfelt condolences and sympathies to the bereaved families and prayed for the elevation of the martyrs’ ranks.
The president, in his statement, expressed heartfelt condolences and sympathies to the families of the martyrs.
صدرِ مملکت آصف علی زرداری کا کوئٹہ کے قریب پاک فوج کے تربیتی طیارے کے حادثے میں دو پائلٹس کی شہادت پر اظہارِ افسوس۔ صدرِ مملکت کا میجر حسنین شہزاد ہمایوں اور کیپٹن عبدالصمد کی شہادت پر گہرے دکھ اور افسوس کا اظہار۔ صدرِ مملکت کا شہداء کے اہلِ خانہ سے دلی تعزیت اور ہمدردی کا…
PM Shehbaz said the country’s brave sons who sacrificed their lives for Pakistan were a source of pride for the nation. He added that the entire nation held their sacrifices in high regard and shared the grief of their families.
The prime minister prayed that Allah grant the martyrs a place in His mercy and give their families the strength to bear the irreparable loss.
On June 10, a Pakistan Army Aviation Mi-17 helicopter crashed near Muzaffarabad during take-off due to a technical fault, martyring all personnel on board. The military’s media wing said a board of inquiry had been ordered to determine the exact cause of the accident.
On September 2, 2025, an Army Aviation Mi-17 helicopter also crashed near Hudor village in Gilgit-Baltistan during a routine training flight after developing a technical fault; five crew members, including two pilots, were martyred, the ISPR said.

title: Ella Langley defends concert cancellation after security threat in Tulsa
description: Ella Langley defended cancelling her Tulsa concert after reported security threat  saying she would do it again
content:
Ella Langley defended cancelling her Tulsa concert after reported security threat, saying she would do it again
Country singer Ella Langley has defended her decision to cancel her concert in Tulsa, Oklahoma, on October 9 after her team cited a serious security threat involving the safety of fans, venue staff and the artist.
Langley, 27, addressed the cancellation during her performance at the United Supermarkets Arena in Lubbock, Texas, on October 10. Speaking to the audience, she explained that she would not perform if she believed a show could put people at risk.
“When it comes to keeping you safe and making sure that this show is a safe place for us to come and enjoy our music, then it will happen. But the second it feels like it will not, I’m not doing it,” she said.
The singer added, “I would have made yesterday’s decision 10 billion times over — and I’d do it tomorrow, and I’d do it the next day — because, while I’m grateful to get to do what I do, it’s not the most important thing in this life.”
Langley said she had also considered cancelling the following night’s performance but ultimately felt it was safe to proceed.
In her statement announcing the Tulsa cancellation, Langley said the decision was made on the advice of local authorities, the venue and her security team.
She also apologised to fans for the disruption, acknowledging the time, travel, money and planning involved in attending a concert.
The Tulsa show was reportedly cancelled following a false bomb threat. The Tulsa Police Department said officers searched the venue with its K-9 unit, Bomb Team, patrol officers and BOK Center security but found nothing dangerous.
Police added that they had advised Langley’s team that there was “no credible threat to the event”, but the performance was cancelled regardless.
Langley’s team said information about ticket refunds would be provided to concertgoers soon. Police are asking anyone with information about the incident to contact Tulsa Crime Stoppers.

title: Robert Pattinson says    Primetime    is not an indictment of Chris Hansen
description: Screenwriter Ajon Singh says the film raises questions about society   s fascination with public humiliation
content:
Screenwriter Ajon Singh says the film raises questions about society’s fascination with public humiliation
Robert Pattinson has defended the approach taken by his upcoming film Primetime , insisting that the drama is not intended to condemn Chris Hansen, the television presenter known for hosting To Catch a Predator .
The British actor portrays Hansen in the psychological thriller, directed by Lance Oppenheim and written by Ajon Singh. The film explores the making of the controversial reality series, which followed sting operations targeting suspected child predators.
Speaking to the Press Association at a screening during the BFI London Film Festival, Pattinson described the film as a portrait rather than an attack on Hansen’s character.
“It’s a portrait, and it’s not an indictment of Chris as a person at all,” the actor explained, adding that the story aims to capture the atmosphere surrounding the programme and examine wider issues connected to its popularity.
Pattinson said he had been familiar with Hansen and watched the series when he was younger. He was particularly interested in the unusual perspective offered by the screenplay and the way Hansen became a widely recognised public figure.
Singh adapted the script from an article in Esquire magazine documenting the fallout from one of the programme’s sting operations. The series was taken off the air in 2008 following an operation involving Texas assistant district attorney Bill Conradt, who died by suicide after police officers and a camera crew entered his home. The footage was never broadcast.
Singh said the filmmakers did not intend to deliver a moral judgement on vigilante justice or the audience’s interest in public humiliation. Instead, he wanted viewers to consider why programmes exposing suspected offenders attracted such widespread attention.
Hansen has criticised Primetime , arguing that it attempts to demonise him. However, Singh said he appreciated the presenter encouraging people to watch the film and form their own opinions.
Oppenheim, making his narrative feature debut after working primarily in documentaries, said he wanted to recreate the unsettling experience of watching the original series.
The cast also includes Merritt Wever, Skyler Gisondo and Phoebe Bridgers.

title: France s high school students plan fresh protests
description: A govt source told journalists last week that cost for damage caused by demonstrations is  at least 30 million euros
content:
A govt source told journalists last week that cost for damage caused by demonstrations is 'at least 30 million euros'
France's high school students on Monday begin a new stage of their campaign for improved conditions, hoping to maintain the momentum with a fresh wave of demonstrations.
The new protests, scheduled for Tuesday, could be a turning point in the movement, launched in mid-September, which the government hopes is already winding down.
Read More: French high school blockades continue as protests spread to universities
On Friday, the government noted a dramatic drop in the number of blockades and meetings outside the country's lycees, where students most between 15 and 18 complete their high school education. More than 96pc were opening Friday, said the education ministry.
The authorities are all the more keen to see the student protests end given that online activists have called for demonstrations next Saturday to protest the cost of living. For President Emmanuel Macron's administration, that brings back troubling memories of the grassroots Yellow Vest movement.
Their protests, launched in 2018 over a planned fuel tax rise, saw massive demonstrations and clashes between police and protesters that shook the presidency during Macron's first term in office.
The government is still counting the cost of the high school protests. A government source told journalists last week that the cost for damage caused by the demonstrations was "at least 30 million euros".
On Friday, the justice ministry said more than 6,800 people had been detained since the demonstrations started, 86pc of them minors.
Also Read: Student anger spreads across France
After clashes between some protesters and riot police left some students severely injured, sparking criticism of police tactics, the government suspended the use of stun grenades that cost one student his hand.
Police are investigating 18 alleged cases of misconduct within their ranks. Last week, the government came up with concrete proposals to try to address the students' demands.
Education Minister Edouard Geffray announced on Thursday that some 3,000 substitute teachers would be deployed in the coming days to replace absent staff at the 114 worst-affected high schools.

Ces remplaçants ont vocation à être affectés dans les établissements, soit en "soutien quand… pic.twitter.com/zaPlylt0FO
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu a day earlier promised to make changes to the planned budget 2027 to respond to some demands set out in an online platform the government set up to gather students' views.
🔴 🗣 "On a besoin, pour que les choses avancent, que les discussions se passent dans le calme, dans l'esprit de responsabilité, pour qu'elles donnent lieu à des décisions", déclare Emmanuel Macron à propos des mobilisations lycéennes. #canal16 pic.twitter.com/g1awlWfOHg
The student organisations behind the protests are yet to be convinced, however.
The Union of High School students described the initial announcements last week as "crumbs". They are maintaining their demand for an extra 10 million euros to be invested in the country's lycees.
France's 10,000 medical students, however, are beginning to express concern at the effect any continued school blockades could have on exams starting Monday that help determine their eventual speciality.
Read More: High school students in Paris' deprived suburbs spark national protest movement
They do not want to see the students' action disrupt such a crucial stage of their education.
Last Thursday's student demonstrations mobilised tens of thousands of people across France: 71,500 according to interior ministry figures.
France's interior ministry put turnout at roughly 86,000 for Tuesday morning's high school student protests over learning conditions. The figure excludes Paris. pic.twitter.com/ntsNOGh6JM
Nearly 256,000 took part in last Tuesday's day of action. And one poll, carried out by Ipsos-BVA and published on Sunday, said 54pc of respondents backed the high school student protests.
They had the most sympathy for student complaints about the excessive size of classes and the need to renovate the country's crumbling schools.

title: Cartoon Network leak exposes production files from decades of animated shows
description: Reported 200GB Cartoon Network leak includes storyboards  character designs and animation files from classic shows
content:
Reported 200GB Cartoon Network leak includes storyboards, character designs and animation files from classic shows
A reported leak of more than 200GB of Cartoon Network production files has exposed behind-the-scenes animation material from shows spanning several decades, including The Powerpuff Girls and The Amazing World of Gumball.
The files were reportedly shared through a Google Drive folder, which Mashable accessed to independently confirm its contents.
Other affected productions include Foster’s Home for Imaginary Friends, The Looney Tunes Show, Duck Dodgers and Garfield.
The leak appears to have originated from an anonymous X account called “totallynotaburner”. The account also shared a Google Doc linking to files from other animated series, including Teen Titans, Dexter’s Laboratory, Robot Chicken and The Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandy.
Many of the links have since been taken down, with some removed following copyright complaints. Mashable said Warner Bros. and Paramount did not respond to requests for comment before publication.
The leaked material reportedly includes storyboards, pitch documents, character model sheets and digital puppet rigs.
Model sheets provide reference drawings to help animators maintain consistent character designs, while puppet rigs allow characters to be manipulated digitally rather than redrawn for every frame.
Although such files offer insight into professional animation production, their unauthorised distribution raises concerns about the use of artists’ work.
Production materials from older shows can also be difficult to preserve as studios restructure and digital archives become harder to access.
The leak emerged shortly after Skydance, led by David Ellison, completed its reported $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on October 6. The combined company now controls Warner Bros., HBO, DC Studios, CNN, Paramount, CBS News and Cartoon Network.
Some social media users speculated that Paramount’s security could be connected to the leak, but no evidence has established that link. The source of the files and whether they predate the merger remain unclear.

title: Dan Levy blasts  misogynist  Shane Gillis over  SNL  joke about women   s gym clothing
description: The  Schitt s Creek  star condemned Gillis  remarks  arguing that men must challenge misogyny rather than blame women
content:
The 'Schitt's Creek' star condemned Gillis' remarks, arguing that men must challenge misogyny rather than blame women
Shane Gillis has sparked criticism following his latest Saturday Night Live monologue, in which jokes about women’s gym clothing drew an uneven response from the audience.
Comedian Dan Levy subsequently condemned the remarks on Instagram , arguing that men must challenge misogyny rather than blame women for their clothing choices.
During the monologue, Gillis joked about women’s workout attire, saying, “I didn't know women just dressed like wh*res now.”
He also joked about the clothing’s fit and warned that gym-goers should not look at women because they might appear in the background of their TikTok videos.
The remarks prompted criticism, with Levy addressing what he viewed as the underlying attitudes towards women.
“Women wearing short shorts to the gym does not make them wh*res. It makes the men calling them wh*res misogynists. There's a difference there,” Levy said.
He called on men to take greater responsibility for challenging misogynistic behaviour, adding, “Men need to be defending women more. This is not a women's issue. This is an everybody issue.”
Levy also argued that the objectification of women in the media can influence how they are treated in everyday life, stressing that women should not be reduced to objects.
Several jokes in Gillis’ monologue prompted groans rather than laughter. The comedian also joked about his receding hairline and compared his hairstyle to Adolf Hitler’s, receiving limited laughter.
Gillis, 38, was dismissed from SNL in 2019 after resurfaced podcast clips featuring offensive remarks about Asians and anti-gay slurs triggered backlash.
He later built a career in stand-up comedy, podcasting and acting, including starring in Netflix’s Tires .
The exchange has renewed discussion about misogyny, accountability and the boundaries of humour in entertainment.

title: Islamabad court grants five day remand of suspect in Laiba suicide case
description: Police produce suspect Nauman to court with his face covered
content:
Police produce suspect Nauman to court with his face covered
An Islamabad District and Sessions Court on Monday remanded a suspect in police custody for five days in a case involving the reported suicide of a former International Islamic University Islamabad (IIUI) student, Laiba, following an alleged fraud.
Laiba had reportedly committed suicide after her dreams of pursuing higher studies at Harvard University in the United States were squashed when a man posing as an agent defrauded her of over Rs7 million. Her body was found hanging from a tree in Sector G-10 in Islamabad on Friday. Subsequently, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice of the case , directing Islamabad Police and the FIA to initiate investigations.
The suspect, identified as Muhammad Nauman, was produced before Judicial Magistrate Zunaira Zafar, where police sought a 10-day physical remand for further investigation.
The court, however, granted police five days of physical remand and handed the suspect over to investigators. Police brought Nauman to court with his face covered.
The FIA’s Anti-Human Trafficking Circle in Islamabad registered a case against suspects Nauman and Fatima Sarwar under Sections 419 (cheating), 420 (cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property) and 109 (abetment) of the Pakistan Penal Code, read with Sections 18 and 22 of the Emigration Ordinance, 1979.
Read More: Medical student’s body exhumed at Karachi's Kohi Goth Graveyard 15 months after death
Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspects allegedly acted in connivance to deceive Laiba with promises of a US visa and scholarship. They allegedly received a total of Rs9.3 million from the family.
The FIA said the suspects allegedly prepared fake scholarship award letters, university admission offer letters and fee payment receipts to keep the family under the impression that the process was genuine. Of the total amount, Rs2.9m was transferred through Laiba’s personal bank account, while the remaining sum was received in cash, according to the agency.
Laiba's family stated that she had aspired to enrol at Harvard University for further studies and that they had made significant financial sacrifices to secure Laiba’s academic future and fulfil her dream. Laiba’s father sold his plot and pitched in Rs2.1 million from the sale’s proceeds, while her mother sold her gold jewellery.
Read More: Student cleared after driverless car collides with police vehicle at Islamabad’s D-Chowk
According to the family, the suspect who reportedly defrauded them claimed to be an accounts officer at the Islamabad High Court and at other times presented himself as an employee of the superior judiciary or an officer of a sensitive institution. The family claimed that despite the substantial payment, the promises regarding admission and the scholarship given to Laiba were never fulfilled.
Laiba’s maternal uncle, Rana Amjad, stated that the Harvard University admission letter, scholarship letter and other documents provided by the suspect turned out to be fake upon verification.
He said that Laiba suffered severe distress and mental anguish after the alleged fraud came to light. Her family demanded a thorough investigation into the matter, the arrest of all individuals involved in the alleged fraud, and the recovery of the money.

title: UAE adviser Gargash urges need to revive joint ties on Gulf security  defence
description: Turkiye  Pakistan  Egypt  Saudi Arabia condemn attacks on Riyadh airport
content:
Turkiye, Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia condemn attacks on Riyadh airport
UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash stressed on Monday a pressing need to revive joint Gulf action, particularly on aspects of security and defence, saying that targeting Saudi Arabia undermined the security of all Gulf states.
Neglect of collective Gulf security had 'emboldened others' to overreach against regional states, he added.
Turkey, Pakistan, Egypt and Saudi Arabia condemned attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militants on Riyadh's international airport, saying they were a "dangerous escalation that cannot be justified or accepted under any pretext".
One person was killed and nearly a dozen were hurt in a new attack on Riyadh's international airport on Sunday, Saudi authorities reported, a day after a strike claimed by the Houthis that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300.
Read: Pakistani resident killed, dozen injured in new attack on Saudi airport
The group of regional powers - dubbed the R4 - reaffirmed their solidarity and support for Saudi Arabia, including full support for all "legitimate measures and steps" it takes to counter the attacks, deter threats and prevent them from happening again.
"The Group holds the Houthi militia fully accountable for the results of these attacks and any repercussions that come with it that threaten regional and international peace and security, and demands the immediate and unconditional halt of these attacks," they said in a joint statement on Sunday.
NATO member Turkiye and nuclear-armed Pakistan signed a joint defence pact with Saudi Arabia in August, under which an attack on one party constitutes an attack on all. Last week, the countries said they had agreed to implement their collective defence commitments and ensure the "rapid deployment" of forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia amid the Houthi attacks.
On Thursday, Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Turkiye was assessing how it can help Saudi Arabia, but ruled out troop deployment and Turkish participation in offensive operations. A day earlier, officials had told Reuters that Ankara was sending mainly defensive and technical support to Riyadh.
Turkish support for Saudi Arabia has largely been in a bilateral capacity so far, as Turkiye's parliament has not yet officially ratified the joint defence pact. The agreement is expected to be submitted to parliament in the coming days.
Turkiye, which has NATO's second-largest army and a robust defence industry, has provided Saudi Arabia with defence equipment and agreed to join a Saudi-led coalition to ensure navigational safety in the Red Sea.

title: PSX plunges nearly 1 965 points amid domestic political clamour
description: KSE 100 closes at 165 124 as selling grips banks  oil and gas  cement stocks
content:
KSE-100 closes at 165,124 as selling grips banks, oil and gas, cement stocks
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) endured a bruising start to the week on Monday, as political upheaval in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) and mounting geopolitical anxieties kept investors on edge, driving the benchmark index deep into the red. The KSE-100 Index remained volatile throughout the session before shedding 1,964.87 points, or 1.18%, to settle at 165,124.41.
The imposition of governor’s rule and emergency measures in parts of K-P, followed by reports of police crackdown, added to the political clamour, stoking fears of further unrest.
Selling pressure swept across oil marketing companies, automobile assemblers, cement, power, commercial banks and oil and gas exploration companies, reflecting the broad-based weakness in market sentiment.
In the international market, oil prices eased on expectations of increased Russian supplies after United States President Donald Trump said Ukraine and Russia had agreed to halt attacks on each other’s energy facilities following a US diesel-supply deal with Moscow. However, the relief was tempered by fears of a wider regional conflict after a Houthi attack on Riyadh’s international airport, leaving investors wary amid an already unsettled geopolitical landscape.
Talking to The Express Tribune , Fawad Basir, head of research at KTrade, attributed the market’s weakness to geopolitical uncertainty and heightened tensions in K-P. He said while June 2026 corporate results in the listed space were better than expected, higher commodity prices were keeping inflation elevated despite the base effect, potentially influencing this month’s monetary policy decision.
At the same time, exchange rate parity and interest rates remained key concerns amid the Middle East crisis and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) tranche review, Basir added.
In their report, KTrade mentioned that selling pressure was broad-based across commercial banks, oil and gas, cement and technology stocks. Oil and Gas Development Company, Habib Bank, Meezan Bank, and Lucky Cement were among the major laggards.
Going forward, market direction is likely to remain volatile, hinging on geopolitical developments and oil prices, with sustained easing in crude prices and progress in US-Iran engagement potentially supporting equities, while further regional escalation could extend the bearish trend, KTrade forecasted.
Overall, trading volume increased to 362.9 million shares from Friday's close of 309.4 million shares while the value of traded shares stood at Rs14.50 billion. In the ready market, shares of 500 companies were traded, of which 135 stocks closed higher, 322 fell and 43 remained unchanged.
Treet Corporation was the volume leader with trading in 27.4 million shares, gainng Rs0.37 to close at Rs24.09.

title: K P emergency  governor s rule challenged in Peshawar High Court
description: Petitioner asks court to declare the imposition of emergency measures and governor   s rule null and void
content:
Petitioner asks court to declare the imposition of emergency measures and governor’s rule null and void
A petition challenging the imposition of emergency measures and governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) was filed in the Peshawar High Court on Monday, a day after President Asif Ali Zardari approved the federal government’s decision on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.
The petition was filed by Advocate Salman; the petition named President Zardari, PM Shehbaz and K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi as respondents. It argued that the measures were unconstitutional, illegal and mala fide, and violated fundamental rights, provincial autonomy and the democratic mandate.
The petitioner asked the court to declare the imposition of emergency measures and governor’s rule null and void, and sought suspension of the notification imposing governor’s rule until a final decision on the case.
The legal challenge came after the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s long march , led by former chief minister Sohail Afridi, reached its first week on Sunday amid mounting tensions with the federal government. Islamabad imposed emergency measures and governor’s rule in the province, citing the deteriorating security situation and the need to address terrorism.
The move was followed by a reported crackdown on PTI workers and leaders, with Afridi and several prominent party figures reported to have been arrested.
Read: PTI may challenge emergency in court
The federal intervention effectively transferred executive authority from the provincial government to Governor Kundi, while an emergency was declared in 12 districts. The PTI rejected the move, describing it as an attack on the province’s autonomy and the party’s electoral mandate.
The latest imposition marked the fourth spell of governor’s rule in the province. The first occurred in 1975 under the government of then-prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. The province subsequently experienced two further periods of governor’s rule, in 1994 and 1999, amid separate political and constitutional crises.
Under Article 234 of the Constitution, the president can assume or direct the governor to assume some or all functions of a provincial government when the province cannot be governed in accordance with the Constitution. The arrangement can also allow Parliament to exercise the powers of the provincial assembly, subject to constitutional requirements and time limits.
The emergency was separately proclaimed under Article 232 , which concerns emergencies arising from war or internal disturbance. The federal government said the measures were necessary in view of terrorism and security threats in the province. The two measures together shifted the province’s executive administration to the governor and a federal-backed arrangement, while leaving the legal and political validity of the decision open to challenge before the courts.

title: India opposition parties march to Supreme Court against election chief
description: Delhi shuts metro stations  restricts traffic ahead of new protest against election chief
content:
Election Commission data shows 130 million names deleted from electoral rolls
Hundreds of opposition party demonstrators marched to India's Supreme Court on Monday to protest the removal of millions of names from voter ‌lists that has sparked days of unrest in the Indian capital and challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Opposition parties and supporters of the "cockroach" youth movement have taken to the streets almost daily this month to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the revision that critics say benefits Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
The change that started last year led to over ​130 million names – more than the population of Japan – being struck from voter lists, including 28 million who had died, 63 million who ​had relocated, and 30 million who could not be traced.
Police detained thousands of protesters over the weekend, including leaders of the 'Cockroach ⁠Janta Party' (CJP), as supporters of the youth movement sought to march in protest and were stopped by thousands of security personnel who locked down central Delhi.
The ​Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol, while the BJP has accused its rivals of trying to undermine the country's ​democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.
Opposition parties are marching to the Supreme Court to file a petition over the voter list revision after Chief Justice Surya Kant declined their request for a meeting.
Kant said the issues were already before the court and discussing pending cases would violate judicial ethics and propriety, and suggested the opposition file a petition instead.
Hundreds ​of people, including opposition party members and left-wing student groups , marched to the court on Monday, while leaders travelled by bus.
"The fundamental values of this country are ​being assaulted, institutions are losing their independence...I am here to protest against this assault," said Anirudh Siyag, a PhD student who joined the protest.
Authorities closed six metro stations for ‌10 hours ⁠and restricted traffic along over 20 stretches in anticipation of the demonstration.
Hundreds of security personnel in anti-riot gear were also deployed in central Delhi, with key roads barricaded and water cannons on standby.
The BJP said the protests were the main opposition Congress party's attempt to seize power.
"By discrediting constitutional institutions, spreading chaos and riots on the streets, and attacking people in the name of politics, all it seeks is a return to power," Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan ​told reporters.
Delhi Police announced that Jantar Mantar ​in the central business district was ⁠no longer designated as an official protest site and three new venues had been identified, according to an official order seen by Reuters.
CJP supporters had staged a sit-in for weeks earlier this year at Jantar Mantar, a historic observatory ​and a well-known protest site for decades, to force Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to quit over exam paper leaks.
Separately, CJP ​leaders met Delhi Police ⁠to "demand" a date for a peaceful protest, threatening to announce a new protest call if a date is not given within 24 hours.
The youth movement, which has mobilised protests in recent months against issues ranging from government school infrastructure to jobs, is one of the biggest political challenges to Modi and his BJP in his 12 years ⁠in power.
The ​protests erupted after the Indian Express newspaper reported last month that Kumar's two deputies raised ​several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems.
