title: Beware of suspicious elements
description: Cricketers must stay vigilant against corruption and honey traps
content:
Cricketers must stay vigilant against corruption and honey traps
There was still some time before the meeting, so I thought I might as well have some ice cream. I went into a shop and, when I looked at the price list, did what most Pakistanis tend to do: convert the prices from British pounds into Pakistani rupees. Then I asked myself, ‘would you really spend several thousand rupees on ice cream? You wasteful man! Get out of here!’ But I listened to my heart and thought, ‘How often do you get to visit London? Treat yourself!’ After buying the ice cream, I went back outside and continued watching the traffic passing along Edgware Road. Oh, I haven’t told you that this was the day Pakistan lost the Test match at Lord’s. There is a sizeable Arab community in this area, and Pakistani politicians have also lived here. During my stay, I witnessed a few minor ‘live fights’ between groups of young men in the vicinity. For a few moments, I also thought about the security of my mobile phone and laptop, but then reassured myself that this was London, not Karachi. I had gone straight from the stadium to a ceremony, where I received an award. I was having dinner afterwards when I was invited to a meeting. As the conversation began at an Arabic restaurant, a revelation emerged that left me utterly astonished. That very night, a few players were questioned at their hotel, and their mobile phones were also taken away. More details will emerge in due course. It is possible that the players in question did nothing wrong and are entirely innocent. Therefore, it would not be appropriate to say too much at this stage. We will have to wait and see how the ongoing investigation unfolds. However, they should cooperate fully with the authorities. If someone is innocent, nothing can be established against them without evidence. On the other hand, attempting to divert attention elsewhere will bring no benefit, only harm. Such attempts have been made in the past, but they achieved nothing. Pakistan has witnessed several match-fixing cases. Players are well aware of the damage these scandals cause, yet some still make mistakes. Until a few years ago, surrogate advertising was widespread in the country. Gambling companies would make minor changes to their names to promote themselves indirectly. However, when people visited their websites, they would find links to betting services. Several such companies even sponsored Pakistan’s home series. Despite media reports highlighting the issue, nothing was done. The standard excuse was that one company was called ‘Bet’ while another was called ‘Bat’, and that the similarity in the rest of their names was merely a coincidence. The issue gained greater prominence when a player in the Pakistan Super League (PSL) objected to such advertising and placed a sticker over the logo. Interestingly, he had already played all the other matches in the tournament before doing so. The previous season had also featured a team sponsored by a similar company, whose logo appeared on the players’ shirts. People had understood the meaning of surrogate advertising years earlier, yet the practice continued. Initially, one company dominated the market, but several others eventually joined in. When public outcry grew louder, the government finally took action and banned such advertising. The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) complied fully, but the practice continued elsewhere. In the recent past, billboards featuring a former captain promoting a similar company appeared along several roads in Karachi. Perhaps no other issue has damaged Pakistani cricket as much as match-fixing scandals. It is now time to adopt a genuine zero-tolerance policy. A law should be introduced stating that anyone proven guilty of such an offence must never again be allowed to participate in any cricket-related activity. They should not even be permitted to conduct interviews or offer commentary on digital media. They must be kept completely away from cricketers. If someone commits such an offence without considering the interests of the country, why should anyone else worry about their livelihood? After all, they must have earned enough money to live comfortably for the rest of their lives. When such individuals are not dealt with firmly, young players are encouraged to believe that they, too, can get away with wrongdoing. Seeing people who have committed offences in the past roaming around freely and being celebrated as ‘so-and-so bhai’ or ‘such-and-such bhai’ makes young cricketers think they will escape punishment as well. If corrupt individuals are made examples of, just imagine how much good that could do for the game. Even today, players frequently receive offers that may be suspicious. Thanks to the PCB’s guidance, many report these approaches to the authorities, helping protect themselves from trouble. Players, too, need to think carefully: people do not give expensive gifts for no reason. Why would someone abandon their entire business to attend every match played by the Pakistan team? There must be some motive behind it. Could you be getting used? Could someone be discreetly trying to obtain inside information from you? Monitoring and oversight also need to be strengthened. Why would a businessman become friends with a domestic cricketer? Why would he give him gifts or take him everywhere? Think about it. Players should also avoid falling for messages they receive from women on social media. They should not immediately lose their hearts over such attention. Nor should they send suggestive messages on Instagram that might later emerge as viral screenshots. These days, even voices can be altered using artificial intelligence, so players must exercise caution even when speaking on the phone. Several players have fallen victim to honey traps, and they need proper guidance on how to protect themselves against such schemes. Thanks to the PSL, Pakistani cricketers can now earn substantial amounts even if they never represent the national team. They should always remember the lesson they learnt as children: ‘Greed is a terrible curse.’ Keeping this in mind is in everyone’s best interest.

title: Zheng withdraws from Wuhan citing fatigue
description: The Olympic champion prioritises recovery after an intense run of matches following her return from injury
content:
The Olympic champion prioritises recovery after an intense run of matches following her return from injury
Freshly crowned China Open champion Zheng Qinwen withdrew on Monday from her home tournament in Wuhan, citing fatigue and a right shoulder injury.
Zheng became the first Chinese player to clinch the Beijing title on Sunday by defeating reigning Roland Garros champion Mirra Andreeva 7-5, 6-4 in the final.
It was Zheng's first WTA 1000-level triumph and her first title since winning Tokyo two years ago.
"I'm very sorry to share that I will be withdrawing from this year's Wuhan Open," Zheng said in a statement.
"Wuhan is where my tennis dream began, and the Wuhan Open is also where I made my breakthrough at the WTA 1000 level. I have always looked forward to competing in front of my hometown fans.
"Since returning from injury, however, I have played a demanding stretch of tennis over the past month and a half, competing at the US Open, the Billie Jean King Cup, and the China Open.
"My body is feeling very fatigued after this intense run of matches."
An Olympic gold medallist in Paris 2024 and a former world number four, Zheng underwent elbow surgery last year and missed nearly eight months of action, dropping as low as 160 in the rankings this season.
The 24-year-old has enjoyed a resurgence over the past few weeks, however, reaching the US Open quarter-finals before lifting the trophy in Beijing.
She is now ranked back among the world's top-25 but will not pick up any points in Wuhan, which kicks off Monday and ends on Sunday October 18.
Beijing runner-up Andreeva has also withdrawn from Wuhan, citing a change of schedule, as the Russian teenager looks to get some rest ahead of her first singles appearance at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells next month.
Zheng and Andreeva join a growing list of high-profile Wuhan absentees that also includes world number one Elena Rybakina, last year's Wuhan champion Coco Gauff and reigning Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova.

title: Afridi  some of his cabinet members have been taken into preventive custody   confirms Talal
description: Says those with cases will be charged and tried  others will be released
content:
Says those with cases will be charged and tried, others will be released
Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry confirmed on Monday that former Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) chief minister Sohail Afridi and some of his cabinet members had been "taken into preventive custody," following the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in the province.
"Yes, I can confirm that the chief minister (Sohail Afridi) and some of his cabinet members have been taken into preventive custody," Chaudhry told Reuters .
If any of them have any cases to be tried against them, they will be charged and tried but the others will be released, he said, adding that the detentions happened on Sunday.
A day earlier, K-P Information Minister Shafi Jan claimed that Afridi had been arrested and urged people across the province to gather in Peshawar. However, at the time, no government official had confirmed his arrest or detention.
Meanwhile, the Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Police in Peshawar said Afridi remained in police protective custody.
The DIG added that eight senior PTI leaders had been taken into protective custody following the imposition of emergency measures and governor’s rule in K-P. Those detained included Afridi, Junaid Akbar and K-P Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, he said.
Read: Schools, colleges in three K-P districts closed on Monday following emergency imposition
"Separately, 169 PTI workers were arrested in a crackdown in Swabi. The arrests were carried out in Shewa Adda, Yar Hussain, Razar, Swabi Khas, Topi, Lahor and Gadoon, among other areas of the district," the DIG said.
According to the DIG, those arrested included several local office-bearers and active PTI workers, saying that they were taken into custody over concerns that preparations for the party’s long march, which began on October 4, could disrupt law and order.
The DIG added that a heavy police contingent had been deployed across Swabi and that further arrests were expected.
Read More: PTI rejects emergency, governor's rule in K-P as unconstitutional, vows to continue struggle
Initially planning to launch the long march on September 27, Afridi on September 26 rescheduled the protest to take place on October 4 amid extensive security and traffic restrictions and continuing efforts to negotiate with the federal government.
Marathon talks between the government and the opposition on October 2 and 3 failed to find middle ground in an effort to ease tensions ahead of the long march, as both sides pressed competing demands and remained at an impasse. PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja later said that the deadlock in negotiations with the federal government emerged over the issue of the counterterrorism policy in K-P.
Amid prevailing tensions, the breakdown of negotiations, and Afridi proceeding with the march, President Asif Ali Zardari signed off on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's recommendation to impose emergency rule in K-P amid a deteriorating security situation and the provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism.
The proclamation said the provincial government had failed to take adequate measures against terrorism and referred to the governor's report highlighting a breakdown in the constitutional system.
Issued under Articles 232(1) and 234(1), the proclamation declared that the provincial government could not function in accordance with the Constitution under the prevailing circumstances. It empowered the federal government to direct the governor to assume some or all provincial government functions, while the powers of the provincial assembly would be exercised by Parliament or under its authority.
The chief minister, provincial ministers, advisers, special assistants and advocate general ceased to hold office with immediate effect. The federal government subsequently authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets under Article 245 to protect citizens, property and government installations for the duration of the emergency proclamation.
In light of the decision, the federal government took control of K-P's affairs , deploying the army to assist the civil administration, forming an 11-member advisory council and establishing a special administrative structure for 12 districts. Its members are Tariq Mahmood Pasha, Dr Amir Abdullah, Lieutenant General (retd) Nigar Johar, Samar Bilour, Dr Sarfaraz Ali, Aamir Javed, Dr M Irshad, Kifayatullah, Tayyab Qureshi, Usman Saifullah Khan and Asif Rafiq. Sanaullah Advocate was appointed the Provincial Advocate General.

title: Pakistan sees growth above 4   looks to raise more than  1 billion from privatisation
description: FinMin says govt has another dozen entities in pipeline  including state owned DISCOs  outsourcing airport operations
content:
FinMin says govt has another dozen entities in pipeline, including state-owned DISCOs, outsourcing airport operations
Pakistan's economy is ​expected to grow by more than 4% this fiscal year despite elevated oil prices, as the government looks to ‌push for the privatisation of five to six entities that could raise upwards of $1 billion, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb told Reuters on Monday.
Pakistan's economy is considered to be highly vulnerable to a prolonged Middle East conflict given its dependence on Gulf energy imports, remittances and financing support from the region, even as it remains reliant on external financing to bolster foreign exchange reserves and meet debt repayments.
The South Asian country of 255 million people ​has been able to procure adequate quantities of fuel, successfully avoiding any shortages, and critical sectors such as ⁠agriculture were holding up, Aurangzeb said.
"So I'm still quite clear that we should clock north of 4%," he said in an interview ​on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Bangkok.
"And on the inflation side, obviously, we ​are keeping a very close eye because it does have a knock-on impact in terms of the commodity prices."
Following a period of severe economic turmoil exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, the cash-strapped economy has recovered some of its footing, supported by a $7 billion, 37-month IMF loan program known as the Extended Fund Facility ​signed in 2024 that includes some tough measures such as raising tax revenue on farm income.
The US-Israeli-led war with ​Iran, now in its eighth month, and the inflation and hardship it has caused, will dominate the agenda and sideline conversations during the meetings that ‌are being ⁠held outside Washington for the first time in three years.
Pakistan, which reached a staff-level agreement with the IMF last week potentially unlocking about $1.21 billion in financing under the Extended Fund Facility and a climate program, is continuing discussions with the United States for a proposed $10 billion exchange stabilisation facility, Aurangzeb said.
But he declined to provide a time frame for the conclusion of negotiations.
"If it comes through, this will be ​a great help for us," ​he said, referring to the facility, ⁠which is in addition to ongoing talks with the Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM) and the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC).
"If it doesn't come through, this does not, you know, create any problem ​for us in terms of access to market."
Following the privatisation of flag carrier Pakistan ​International Airlines last ⁠year, Aurangzeb said the government has around another dozen entities in the pipeline, including state-owned power distribution companies and the outsourcing of airport operations.
"I expect about five or six of these to go through during this fiscal year," he said, adding that they could raise more than $1 billion.
⁠Privatisation has ​been seen as a key test of Pakistan's reform credibility with the IMF, with ​officials previously underlining that failure to offload loss-making state firms risked renewed pressure on public finances.
"We are quite clear that we want the private sector to lead the country," said Aurangzeb. "So ​our role is to help support, assist in any way we can in terms of the ecosystem."

title: Sadiq questions Saim   s role in Pakistan   s T20I squad
description: Former opener says selection is unfair to middle order batsmen and backs Sajid as a third spin option
content:
Former opener says selection is unfair to middle-order batsmen and backs Sajid as a third spin option
Former Pakistan Test opener Sadiq Mohammad has questioned the selection of Saim Ayub in the T20I squad, saying the all-rounder’s presence in different batting positions is undermining the team’s middle order batsmen.
“It is an injustice to the middle order batsmen to keep playing Saim Ayub,” Sadiq told The Express Tribune.
“The coaches, selection committee and captain are destroying the middle order. How can Saim fit into every batting position simply because he can bowl a few overs of finger spin?” he said.
Sadiq said that if Pakistan needed a third spinner in T20 internationals, off-spinner Sajid Khan would be a better option.
“If we want a third spinner in T20 cricket, we should give chance to our off-spinner Sajid Khan. He can hit the ball hard, extract turn and is an excellent fielder. We used to play Iftikhar Ahmed in a similar role two years ago,” Sadiq said.
Saim has been included in Pakistan’s T20I squad for the ongoing series against Sri Lanka. He has been batting at number five, while the presence of four specialist openers in the squad has raised questions about the balance of the team’s batting combination.
Saim took one wicket for 19 runs in his three overs on Sunday.
Sajid, meanwhile, has so far been restricted largely to Test cricket, a decision that has raised eyebrows. He was also dropped by his Peshawar team from its T20 side, a decision that reportedly angered the off-spinner.
Sadiq believes Sajid could prove an effective addition to Pakistan’s T20I squad, potentially filling the role previously occupied by Iftikhar Ahmed, who was often used as a power-hitter in the death overs.
Sajid, who has played 16 Tests for Pakistan, is a powerful hitter and has demonstrated his ability to clear the boundary when given the opportunity, even in the longer format.
"Team management should focus on developing a young player for the death overs rather than repeatedly relying on tried-and-tested players based on their mediocre past performances,” Sadiq said.
Sadiq also urged seasoned left-handed opener Fakhar Zaman to go deep and don’t throw his wicket after taking a good start.
“Fakhar Zaman must focus on converting his starts into big individual scores instead of getting out after settling in during the powerplay,” Sadiq said.
“He was dismissed in the fifth over in both innings. If this pattern continues, he could be dropped sooner or later, with Saim Ayub potentially replacing him despite not having proved himself. Both openers have been selected to establish themselves and demonstrate their ability to score big, match-winning totals,” Sadiq said.
Sadiq also pointed out that Shadab has also lost his gloss as a bowler.
"Shadab Khan is another player whose bowling has been largely ineffective. He should also be sidelined, with Sajid Khan considered as a replacement for both Saim Ayub and Shadab."
Sadiq congratulated Pakistan team and skipper Sahibazada Farhan for delivering extremely well in both the T20I matches against Sri Lanka.
"Finally, congratulations on winning the T20 series. Sahibzada Farhan has emerged as a potential new T20 captain, having performed well in both matches. Well played," Sadiq signed off.

title: Betis rise back above Real Madrid to third
description: Isco s brace inspires a 5 2 win over Osasuna
content:
Isco's brace inspires a 5-2 win over Osasuna
Veteran playmaker Isco struck twice to help Real Betis climb back into third place in La Liga with a 5-2 win over Osasuna on Sunday.
The Andalucian side moved a point above Real Madrid, fourth, and level with second place Atletico Madrid, trailing leaders Barca by five points.
Manuel Pellegrini's side claimed a sixth league win from eight matches with an exciting display of attacking football at La Cartuja stadium, where they are playing until their Benito Villamarin home is renovated, likely 2028.
Former Real Madrid midfielder Isco, 34, netted from the penalty spot after a foul on Rodrigo Riquelme, and Ez Abde doubled the hosts lead after half-an-hour with a cool finish.
Ante Budimir's own goal gave Betis their third after half-time, before the Croatian striker netted at the correct and Raul Garcia added another to give Osasuna a fighting chance.
Isco capitalised on a loose ball in the box to grab his second and Jose Morante bagged a fifth in stoppage time to close out Betis's big win.
"Football is never truly under control," said Pellegrini after his side almost let their three-goal lead slip.
"As soon as the pace drops, the other team can pull level."
The former Manchester City coach also praised Isco after his brace.
"He has spectacular quality and a maturity as a player that allows him to perform at whatever level he wants to," added Pellegrini.
Elsewhere Valencia, 19th, earned a point in a 2-2 draw at Racing Santander under new coach Javier Aguirre.
Real Sociedad defeated Deportivo La Coruna 3-2 in another entertaining battle.
The Basque side, sixth, eased into a three-goal lead Mario Soriano pulled one back for the visitors in San Sebastian to spark a Depor fight back.
They were given further encouragement when Real Sociedad's Pablo Marin was sent off in the 66th minute for a foul on Nsongo Bil in the box and Yeremay Hernandez netted from the penalty spot.
Both teams finished with 10 men after Lorenzo Amatucci brought down Mikel Oyarzabal as the last man, and Depor could not find an equaliser.
On Saturday Liga leaders Barcelona beat Getafe 3-0 to prolong their perfect start to the season, with eight wins from eight league games.
Hansi Flick's side are followed by second place Atletico Madrid, who snatched a late 2-1 win at Alaves, while Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid scraped a 1-0 victory over Villarreal despite Vinicius Junior's red card for hair-pulling.

title: Man City shrug off uncertain future to beat 10 man Liverpool
description: The Blues cruise to a 3 0 victory at Anfield to maintain their perfect start
content:
The Blues cruise to a 3-0 victory at Anfield to maintain their perfect start
Manchester City shrugged off the threat of swingeing sanctions to beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 in their first game since being found guilty on more than 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules.
Second-half goals from Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki extended City's flawless start under Enzo Maresca after Ryan Gravenberch had been sent off for two yellow cards.
City re-established their three-point lead at the top of the table, but the future of any title challenge rests on the outcome of the club's appeal against widespread financial impropriety.
"We need to learn how to deal with the outside noise, but make our own noise, which is to win games," said Maresca.
"Our fans were singing at the end, so the noise was from us."
An independent commission found City and their Emirati owners arranged "sham" deals to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion) between 2009 and 2018.
No sanction has yet been handed down, but a severe points deduction or even expulsion from the English top flight are on the table unless City overturn the decision.
There has even been speculation there could be retrospective action to strip titles.
"The uncertainty is not good for anyone," said Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola.
The multiple breaches of Premier League laws came during a period in which City won three titles and a clutch of other trophies.
City's rivals believe, however, that the illegal spending during that period also built the foundations for a golden era under former boss Pep Guardiola, who left at the end of last season.
Liverpool were one of the clubs most affected, having finished second to City three times in the past 12 years.
"City have fundamentally cheated to win those leagues," Jamie Gallaghie, a 48-year-old teacher, told AFP.
The visitors arrived under the protection of a police escort with a hostile Anfield welcome expected, but there was no repeat of the violent scenes when their team bus was pelted by bottles ahead of a Champions League clash in 2018.
Liverpool fans lined the streets to greet the City players with chants of "cheats" and "going down", while merchandise stalls were littered with flags and scarves mocking their rivals' financial scandal.
In the iconic Kop end behind one goal a banner read "a generation of supporters cheated."
The battles between Guardiola's City and Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool in recent years became the Premier League's marquee event.
But with the eyes of the world watching, Liverpool failed to rise to the occasion on the field.
New Liverpool boss Iraola's options were blunted without the injured Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo as the Spaniard suffered his first defeat since taking charge of the Reds.
An Abu Dhabi-backed takeover in 2008 transformed City from mid-table mediocrity into the dominant force of the English game.
City's economic might was on full show and helped turn the game as Maresca could introduce Doku off the bench early in the second half.
Within minutes the Belgian winger had been chopped down by Gravenberch, who was shown a harsh second booking, and Liverpool never recovered.
Doku's deflected shot was then smashed home by Haaland to break the deadlock 25 minutes from time, opening the floodgates.
Three minutes later Doku curled a sensational strike into the top corner himself.
Cherki then exchanged a slick one-two with Josko Gvardiol before slotting under Alisson Becker to rub salt in Liverpool wounds.
The defeat leaves Liverpool nine points adrift of the leaders down in ninth.

title: Forest boss Glasner loses on return to Palace
description: The Eagles recover from Ndoye s early strike to claim a 3 1 victory
content:
The Eagles recover from Ndoye's early strike to claim a 3-1 victory
Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner was beaten on his return to Crystal Palace as Daichi Kamada's first Premier League goal inspired the Eagles' 3-1 win on Sunday.
Glasner was back in south London for the first time since leaving Palace at the end of last season.
The 52-year-old Austrian led Palace to a shock FA Cup final triumph over Manchester City in 2025 and masterminded their UEFA Conference League success in May.
Glasner opted to quit Selhurst Park after reported issues with the club's hierarchy over their transfer policy, opening the way for his move to Forest.
He was greeted warmly by Palace fans before kick-off and it looked like being a victorious return for Glasner when Forest's Dan Ndoye opened the scoring in the third minute.
But Forest wasted a host of chances to increase their lead and Japan midfielder Kamada levelled in the 41st minute to end his long wait for a top-flight goal.
Jefferson Lerma nodded Palace in front in first-half stoppage time and Yeremy Pino's 59th-minute goal sent Glasner home empty-handed.
It was a first home league victory for Palace boss Pierre Sage, who was hired from Lens after Glasner's departure.
Glasner joined Forest in the wake of tension between the clubs, sparked by the legal fallout from Palace's demotion to the Conference League before the 2025-26 season, with Forest taking their place in the Europa League.
The Forest boss did not escape with a cheeky send-off from the Palace supporters, who chanted "you're getting sacked in the morning" chant minutes before the final whistle.
Forest sit in 14th place, with Palace climbing above them into 12th.
Hull extended their unbeaten home record since returning to the Premier League with an 2-2 draw against Everton at the MKM Stadium.
Joe Gelhardt opened the scoring for Hull in the 48th minute following an error by Ainsley Maitland-Niles.
Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall equalised seven minutes later, with Thierno Barry putting Everton ahead in the 68th minute.
Hull responded swiftly as substitute Mohamed Belloumi levelled in the 74th minute.
Fifth-placed Everton remain unbeaten in six league games, while ninth-placed Hull have lost just one of their six matches since earning promotion last season.

title: Dizzy  Lazio join Inter at top of Serie A
description: Roma  Juventus and Milan all dropped points in a frustrating weekend for title contenders
content:
Roma, Juventus and Milan all dropped points in a frustrating weekend for title contenders
Lazio moved level on points with Inter Milan at the top of Serie A with a 3-1 win over Monza on Sunday as pursuers Roma, Juventus and AC Milan were all held.
Ten-man Roma could not keep pace as Donyell Malen's red card overshadowed a 0-0 stalemate in Como. They now sit two points behind the leaders in third.
AC Milan were held 1-1 at Sassuolo to leave them four points adrift of the leaders in fifth.
Surprise package Cagliari continued their impressive start to the season by holding Juventus 1-1 to remain fourth, two points above the Turin giants in sixth.
Under Gennaro Gattuso, who has bounced back after his failure at the helm of the Italian national side who missed out on the 2026 World Cup, Lazio continued their strong start to the season.
Still unbeaten, the Roman outfit secured a fifth victory in six matches to pull level on 16 points with Inter, who beat Parma 3–0 at the San Siro on Saturday.
"We can't look at the standings, otherwise we will get dizzy. We have to take it day by day," said Gattuso.
Their run comes despite ongoing fan protests against owner Claudio Lotito that have left Lazio's home matches sparsely attended amid a stadium boycott.
Nuno Tavares gave Lazio a third-minute lead with a spectacular long-range strike and Gustav Isaksen doubled it midway through the first half.
Monza had Lorenzo Lucchesi sent off on 35 minutes for hauling down Tijjani Noslin as he broke through on goal, but the 16th-placed visitors rattled Lazio after the break, pulling a goal back and coming close to equalising before conceding a third goal in the closing stages.
In Sardinia, Juventus required a late equaliser from Randal Kolo Muani to rescue a point after Daniel Maldini's opener as tempers flared between the coaches.
Maldini, son of AC Milan legend Paolo, struck for the fourth game in a row to mark his 25th birthday in style.
Juventus dominated possession but struggled to carve out clear-cut chances against a Cagliari side boasting the best defensive record in the league until Kolo Muani headed home in the 81st minute.
The France international almost completed the comeback four minutes later when he rattled the underside of the bar from close range, but the hosts held on to take a draw before tempers spilled over at full-time as opposing coaches Fabio Pisacane and Luciano Spalletti were shown red cards.
"Nothing happened. I told him they play good football and are good at wasting time," Spalletti explained when asked what led to the fracas.
"(Pisacane) said 'what do you mean wasting time?' And they kicked us both out. It was nothing major, all pretty normal," he added.
Ruben Amorim's Milan maintained their unbeaten start but drew for the third time in their last four league games.
Matteo Gabbia went off injured early on with the breakthrough not coming until the 63rd minute when Luka Modric slipped in Adrien Rabiot to fire home a powerful finish.
Milan's lead lasted just five minutes before substitute Cas Odenthal turned in the equaliser in a crowded box from a corner.
"We deserved to take the lead, but then after the goal we didn't control the game," Amorim said.
"When we had the ball, we lost it really fast. That can happen, but what cannot happen is to concede that goal on the corner."
Roma continued their unbeaten start against Como but could only pick up a point in the first goalless draw of the Serie A season.
The dismissal of league top scorer Malen for a dangerous tackle early in the second half forced Roma to scale back their ambitions after a bright start where Lorenzo Pellegrini hit the post and Paulo Dybala squandered a glorious chance.
Neither team could find the breakthrough in a clash between two sides widely regarded as dark horses for the title.
Bologna picked up their first win of the season by beating Lecce 2-1.

title: Govt can t keep sleeping when it comes to citizens  security   DPM Dar on K P emergency  governor s rule
description: Expresses confidence that the measures would produce results in the coming weeks and months
content:
Says it's not a 'political move', government has paid heavy political price for difficult decisions in the past
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Monday defended the federal government’s decision to impose emergency measures in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), saying it had “no choice” but to act to protect citizens from terrorism.
“When it comes to the safety and security of our nationals, our citizens, wherever they live, any part of Pakistan, I think it is the duty of the federal government,” DPM Dar said at a conference on Pakistan’s evolving counter-terrorism landscape.
The federal government imposed governor’s rule in K-P on Sunday, with President Asif Ali Zardari approving Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s advice under Article 234 of the Constitution. The decision came amid tensions between the Centre and the PTI-led provincial government over the security situation and counter-terrorism efforts. The PTI rejected the move as unconstitutional and vowed to resist it.
He said the government had determined that there was no alternative to the measures it had taken. “It’s not a political move. It is surely against the menace of terrorism which the province has been hit with in the last decade and a half,” he said. “Can we keep sleeping and looking towards another because it's a political move? No, it's not. I can guarantee you.”
DPM Dar said the government had paid a heavy political price for difficult decisions in the past, including economic measures taken when Pakistan was on the brink of default, and that "whatever costs" the government has to pay to save the economy, to protect property and lives of the people, "I think it is never too much."
He expressed confidence that the measures would produce results in the coming weeks and months, saying he hoped peace would return to the province, lives would be protected and radicalisation would end.
DPM Dar also referred to his experience of negotiating with the same political party in 2014, when a sit-in continued in Islamabad for 126 days, saying the government did not consider political differences a reason to avoid engagement. However, he maintained that public safety had to take precedence when the government believed action was necessary.
DPM Dar said Pakistan had paid an enormous human, economic and reputational price for terrorism, with economic losses exceeding $150 billion. “Mind you, Pakistan's total external debt is 130 billion dollars,” he said.
He said terrorism had tarnished Pakistan’s international image and undermined confidence in the country, while the damage to its reputation and the opportunities lost during that period were incalculable.
“Pakistan has borne a dual burden: fighting terrorism, not countering the misperceptions that have too often obscured our sacrifices,” he said.
Recalling attacks on civilians, Dar referred to the children killed at the Army Public School in Peshawar, bombings at mosques, markets and bus stops, passengers taken hostage on a train, and labourers killed because of where they came from. “These are not just statistics. This is the price the Pakistani nation has paid and continues paying,” he said.
He said the government had made counter-terrorism a national priority, renewed national efforts and placed greater emphasis on implementing the National Action Plan. The Federal Apex Committee had brought together civilian and military leadership to review threats and agree on measures to address them, he said.
Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar says Pakistan has been at the forefront of the war against terrorism for over two decades, adding that terrorism has tarnished the country’s global image. #IshaqDar #WarOnTerror #CounterTerrorism #NationalSecurity #PakistanTV pic.twitter.com/YjL0TGZZYp
DPM Dar said the prime minister had approved the Azm-e-Istehkam initiative with the consensus of the provinces and other stakeholders. The initiative brought together military, intelligence, law enforcement and diplomatic efforts to target terrorists and the networks sustaining them while addressing conditions that allowed extremism to take root.
He said the government had also agreed on measures to improve intelligence coordination and strengthen the role of the National Counter Terrorism Authority.
“These efforts require close cooperation between the Federation and the provinces,” he said. “Every institution has a responsibility and the national effort must continue with unity and resolve.”
DPM Dar commended PM Shehbaz for his leadership and sustained attention to counter-terrorism. He also paid tribute to the Chief of Defence Forces and the Chief of Army Staff and Field Marshal Asim Munir, saying the armed forces, working closely with law enforcement agencies, continued operations against terrorists and their facilitators.
“They confront this danger daily, often at the cost of their own lives,” he said.
Efforts to engage with Afghanistan not yielded results
The deputy prime minister highlighted the repeated diplomatic efforts Pakistan had made to secure action against terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory, while seeking stronger economic and regional ties with Afghanistan.
He referred to three visits to Kabul in 2025, including a visit on April 19 after a four-year stalemate in relations, followed by another visit in July with the Uzbek foreign minister.
During the April visit, DPM Dar said he held detailed discussions with Afghanistan’s acting Prime Minister Mullah Mohammad Hassan Akhund, Deputy Prime Minister Abdul Ghani Baradar and Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi.
He said the discussions covered trade, the economy, refugees and political matters, among other issues. Pakistan had subsequently delivered on commitments it had made to Afghanistan, he said.
“What does Pakistan ask? Only one. Please do not allow your soil to be used against any country, particularly Pakistan, for terrorism,” he said.
Pakistan had continued to pursue engagement, upgraded diplomatic representation and worked towards regional connectivity, including a proposed railway linking Pakistan and Uzbekistan through Afghanistan to Central Asia, he said.
Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar says combating terrorism remains the government’s top priority, urging the international community to acknowledge Pakistan’s sacrifices in the fight against terrorism. #IshaqDar #CounterTerrorism #WarOnTerror #GlobalSecurity #PakistanTV pic.twitter.com/CvVeSRHhLR
In August 2025, Dar and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi had visited Kabul for a trilateral dialogue, he added. “These were the sincere efforts on behalf of Pakistan,” Dar said. “But the one ask, we are not seeing a result, unfortunately, so far.”
He said Pakistan wanted Afghanistan to become stable and prosperous and believed in the future of the Afghan people. However, he said, the Afghan Taliban authorities needed to honour their counter-terrorism commitments and ensure Afghan territory was not used to launch attacks, particularly against Pakistan.
“Sadly, as I said, we can no longer ignore the continuing terrorist threat emanating from Afghanistan,” he said.
DPM Dar referred to reports by the United Nations monitoring mechanisms documenting the presence of the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) in Afghanistan and its close links with Al-Qaeda. He said the threat had implications for regional security beyond Pakistan.
“Just imagine, if Pakistan was not fighting this war as a frontline fighter, this terrorism, God knows, would have spread by now to rich parts of the globe,” he said.
He stated that attacks inside Pakistan were planned, directed and launched from across the border, with terrorists infiltrating Pakistan, attacking soldiers and civilians before retreating to their sanctuaries.
Pakistan had invested heavily in border fencing and management at considerable financial and human cost, he said. “But no fence can substitute for real action against these terrorist sanctuaries,” he said.
DPM Dar said Pakistan had raised its concerns directly and repeatedly, shared specific information and sought concrete action against terrorist groups and the sanctuaries from which attacks against Pakistan were launched.
DPM Ishaq Dar addresses the conference on Pakistan’s evolving counterterrorism landscape https://t.co/eVqfDafW2J
He also cited Pakistan’s decision to allow humanitarian aid to pass into Afghanistan despite a border closure following a wave of attacks in October 2025. He said the United Nations had approached Pakistan’s Foreign Office for permission and that the country had allowed 1,000 containers of humanitarian aid to cross the border, a process that took almost a month.
He said the decision demonstrated Pakistan’s commitment to Afghanistan’s development and prosperity.
The minister also recalled his efforts as finance minister to secure approval for the CASA-1000 energy project linking Tajikistan, Afghanistan and Pakistan. The project had been suspended by the World Bank and International Monetary Fund following political changes in Afghanistan, he said, but efforts had since been made to revive it.
He said Pakistan’s willingness to pursue economic cooperation had not diminished despite its security concerns.
DPM Dar also recounted a conversation with Akhund during his July 2025 visit, saying the Afghan leader had thanked Pakistan for delivering on commitments within eight weeks.
“If you do not take appropriate actions against the terrorist groups in Afghanistan, the day will come, if your government is there, they will haunt you as well and you will be facing threats from the same terrorists in Afghanistan,” Dar said he had told him.
DPM Dar described the TTP as one of the greatest threats to Pakistan’s security, saying it had been responsible for some of the worst terrorist attacks in the country’s history, including attacks on schools, mosques, markets and security installations.
He said the group’s victims included civilians as well as members of the security forces.
He also accused the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) of targeting civilians and security personnel while seeking to undermine Pakistan’s economic development.
Among the incidents he cited was the hijacking of the Jaffar Express in March 2025, when more than 400 passengers were taken hostage. He also referred to attacks on passenger buses, targeted killings of civilians in Rojhan, and assaults on security installations and infrastructure critical to Pakistan’s economic development.
Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar lauds Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir’s role in the fight against terrorism. He calls on Afghanistan to take concrete action against terrorist groups operating from its soil. #IshaqDar #AsimMunir #CounterTerrorism … pic.twitter.com/sfxvDfmkVq
DPM Dar said the groups did not operate in isolation and benefited from external support, including networks providing fighters, funding, weapons and training.
“Pakistan has repeatedly called for action against the support and the sanctuaries that enable their attacks,” he said. “A group that finds safe haven today to attack Pakistan can use the same safe haven tomorrow to threaten others.”
He warned that ignoring the TTP and its supporters would not eliminate the threat but would give them time to grow.
He said Pakistan had consistently raised concerns with the international community about what it alleged was Indian support for terrorist organisations operating against Pakistan, including from Afghanistan.
Pakistan had shared information with the United Nations and international partners documenting alleged Indian support for groups including the TTP and other proxies operating from Afghan territory, he added.
DPM Dar referred to former Indian naval officer Kulbhushan Jadhav, who confessed to involvement in terrorist activities, as well as what DPM Dar described as a record of extraterritorial assassinations, including in North America.
He said alleged state sponsorship of terrorism had been documented and argued that the issue went beyond Pakistan’s bilateral disputes with India.
“When a state uses terrorist groups as instruments of policy against a neighbour, it puts the peace of the wider region at complete risk,” he said. “It undermines international law and relations between the states. Such support must be confronted without political considerations or double standards.”
The minister stated that Pakistan was working to strengthen multilateral cooperation against terrorism and had used its position on the United Nations Security Council to advance international action.
He said Pakistan, an elected member of the Security Council for 2025-26, had chaired the 1988 Taliban Sanctions Committee and served as a vice-chair of the Counter-Terrorism Committee.
These responsibilities provided opportunities to advance international cooperation and the implementation of relevant Security Council resolutions, he said.
Pakistan had also chaired the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure during 2025-26 and used the forum to promote regional cooperation, he said.
The deputy prime minister added that bilateral counter-terrorism dialogue, including with the United States, formed another part of Pakistan’s efforts to address shared threats and strengthen practical cooperation.
“Pakistan’s sacrifices deserve recognition, but recognition alone is not enough,” he said.
He called for timely intelligence sharing, access to technology and further capacity-building support for law enforcement agencies. He also urged effective international action against terrorist financing, weapons supplies and the provision of safe havens.
“States must ensure that their territory is not used for terrorism against any other country,” he said.
He also urged Pakistan’s partners to impress upon the Afghan authorities the need to fulfil their commitments. “A threat that endangers the region and the world cannot leave Pakistan to confront alone,” he said.
DPM Dar warned that terrorist groups were adapting their methods, using social media and encrypted platforms to recruit and radicalise people, raising funds through cryptocurrencies and other digital channels, and experimenting with drones and artificial intelligence to spread propaganda.
He said young people were increasingly exposed to extremist propaganda online and that individuals radicalised through digital platforms could carry out attacks without warning.
Modern weaponry was also finding its way into the hands of terrorist groups, making the work of security forces more difficult, he said. “No state or society can combat these challenges alone,” he said. “We need to share technology, intelligence, and experience.”
Above all, he said, governments needed the political resolve to act against terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, without distinction or excuse.
“Those who killed our children in Peshawar claim to act in the name of Islam. They did not,” he said.
DPM Dar referred to the Quranic principle that killing one human being was equivalent to killing all humanity, saying the principle did not distinguish between people on the basis of religion.
“They are criminals, they speak for no faith or religion, and they have no nationality or boundary,” he said, referring to terrorists. “Terrorism must never be equated with any religion, nationality, civilisation, or ethnicity.”
He added that Islamophobia divided communities and provided terrorists with the propaganda they sought. He said the response to terrorism had to remain firm while rejecting attempts to associate terrorism with a particular faith or community.
Counter-terrorism should not suppress self-determination
DPM Dar said counter-terrorism efforts should not be used as a pretext to suppress legitimate struggles for self-determination recognised under the United Nations Charter and relevant Security Council resolutions.
He referred to Palestine and Jammu and Kashmir, as well as the conflict between Thailand and Cambodia, saying that Pakistan had promoted multilateralism and the peaceful settlement of disputes during its Security Council presidency the previous year.
DPM Dar cited Resolution 2788, which he said had been unanimously adopted after 12 years without a similar unanimous resolution on the issue. He said the resolution’s principles had subsequently been referenced in discussions at the United Nations during the Thailand-Cambodia conflict.
“Those who used to call Pakistan, probably because of the terrorism we have been actually fighting, a terrorist or some other state, now they are very happy to call Pakistan a peacemaker state after what we have done in the last few years,” he said.
He also referred to Pakistan’s efforts to mediate between the United States and Iran, saying the two sides had held direct talks for the first time in 47 years with Pakistan’s participation.
The deputy prime minister said an agreement reached on June 18 had subsequently been violated by both sides, but Pakistan had not abandoned its diplomatic efforts. “As late as just days before, in the high week of the UN General Assembly, on the sidelines of New York, we are making all possible efforts,” he said.
He also referred to the growing strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, saying developments affecting these waterways had wider implications for regional and international security.
Concluding his speech, DPM Dar stated that Pakistan had entered into a joint defence agreement signed in Makkah on August 7, with its inaugural meeting held in Istanbul on August 31.
He said Pakistan had the honour of providing the first secretary-general for a three-year term and that the headquarters would be in Riyadh. A working committee was finalising the programme and operational details, he said.
The framework included a Strategic, Political and Defence Committee comprising the foreign ministers, defence ministers and army chiefs of the three participating countries, he said.
“The idea is not any offensive. The idea is totally objective and defensive,” he said. “So it is for self-defence. And it is nothing which is against any international law or charter.”
DPM Dar cited Article 51 of the United Nations Charter, which recognises the right to individual and collective self-defence, and compared the principle with the basis on which NATO was established.
He said the ultimate objective was to promote peace and closer ties in the region, rather than target any other country.
The agreement was also not restricted permanently to the three founding participants, he said, adding that its provisions would allow other countries to join once the framework was fully established, potentially within a year.
DPM Dar said Pakistan’s counter-terrorism policy, diplomatic engagement and defence cooperation were all aimed at improving security while promoting regional stability and peaceful relations.

title: Zverev digs deep to reach Shanghai last 16
description: The German defeats France   s Quentin Halys 6 4  6 7  8 10   6 3 to keep his bid for a maiden world number one ranking on track
content:
The German defeats Quentin Halys 6-4, 6-7 (8/10), 6-3 to keep his bid for a maiden world number one ranking on track
Alexander Zverev was forced to dig deep in beating Quentin Halys in three sets at the Shanghai Masters on Sunday as he closes in on the world number one ranking.
The German top seed belatedly saw off the Frenchman 6-4, 6-7 (8/10), 6-3 to reach the last 16, despite moving a little uncomfortably at the end.
"He plays unbelievably aggressive and serves incredibly," Zverev, himself one of the biggest servers on tour, said of his beaten opponent.
"This year I have been picking my tournaments and places where I want to peak, I did not do that early in my career.
"It paid off, I won two Grand Slams and reached the Wimbledon final."
Zverev cut a frustrated figure at times, barking at his corner even as he clinched the first set against the 48th-ranked Halys in 38 minutes.
The second set was much closer, going with serve and taking them into the tie-break.
Zverev unleashed a delicious backhand down the line to avoid going down 6-4 in the tie-break, but then squandered a match point when he shanked a forehand return.
A second match point came and went, and Halys took full advantage to force a deciding set courtesy of an overhead smash.
The third was poised for another battle, but Zverev broke for 2-0 and behind his reliable serve powered home for victory.
Zverev, the world number two, is an imminent threat to Jannik Sinner's number one ranking.
The US Open and French Open winner has never topped the rankings.
The Italian Sinner is not playing in Shanghai because of injury, opening the door for the 29-year-old Zverev to usurp him.
World number three Carlos Alcaraz is in action on Monday.
The Spaniard faces Belgium's Zizou Bergs in the third round.

title: Zheng crowned China Open champion
description: Olympic champion beats Andreeva 7 5  6 4  to become first home winner
content:
Olympic champion beats Andreeva 7-5, 6-4. to become first home winner
Zheng Qinwen became the first home winner of the China Open on Sunday as she beat Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva 7-5, 6-4.
The former world number four and current Olympic champion was a wildcard entry in Beijing, having struggled with form and fitness after elbow surgery in 2025.
It was the 54th-ranked Zheng's first title in nearly two years.
Zheng, 24, is the first Chinese player to win the tournament since its inception in 2004.
Andreeva, ranked five, was more consistent to start with, but Zheng grabbed back a break and stayed with her 19-year-old opponent as they battled on the baseline.
Zheng saved three set points to level 5-5 and won every single point after that, sending down an ace to grab the lead.
A crowd desperate to see their homegrown talent crowned champion was at times disruptive as cheers erupted before points ended and shouts for Zheng punctuated serves on both sides of the net.
But the players kept their focus, holding serve until Zheng found a way through in the ninth game of the second set, firing brilliantly against the line to break and go up 5-4.
A double-fault threatened to derail an imminent triumph until Zheng, defiant, sent down an ace to win on her first match point.
It is Zheng's first trophy since October 2024 when she beat Sofia Kenin in Tokyo, and her first-ever title at the prestigious WTA 1000 level.
The players' only previous meeting was in the 2024 China Open quarter-finals, where Zheng beat Andreeva in three sets.

title: Kipruto claims Chicago Marathon as Feysa defends women s title
description: The Kenyan clocks a personal best 2 01 09 to finish nearly two minutes clear
content:
The Kenyan clocks a personal-best 2:01:09 to finish nearly two minutes clear
Amos Kipruto of Kenya dominated a world-class field to finally win his first Chicago Marathon while Ethiopia's Hawi Feysa defended her women's title on Sunday.
Kipruto's time of 2:01:09 was a new personal best and vindication for the 34-year-old, who had finished second in Chicago last year and third the previous edition.
This time, Kipruto pulled clear of defending champion and pre-race favorite Jacob Kiplimo at mile 21 and never looked back.
"Today's race was really good for me... I came here 2024, I became position three, 2025 I became position two. And now 2026 it was either win or die for me," said Kipruto.
He finished the 48th Chicago Marathon nearly two minutes clear in ideal sunny but cool conditions, briefly sinking to the floor after he crossed the finish line, before quickly rising with a giant grin.
Kipruto, the 2022 London champion, had set his previous personal best finishing fourth at this year's historic London race, where the mythical two-hour barrier was broken.
But he had the spotlight to himself in Chicago.
"The preparation for me toward the Chicago Marathon 2026 was perfect for me. I improved a lot in training for the previous London Marathon," said Kipruto.
"But I said 'let's go (for) Chicago' and let be what will be. Everything is all about a mindset. It was a tough field, but I set my mind and I said 'let's go.'"
His time makes him the joint-fifth fastest marathon runner of all time.
Uganda's Kiplimo ultimately slipped back to fourth place.
Tadese Takele Bikila of Ethiopia -- the defending Tokyo champion, making his US marathon debut -- took second, while compatriot Milkesa Mengesha came third.
On the women's side, defending champion Feysa also set a new personal best with a blistering 2:13:33.
"I'm elated to have won the second time," said Feysa, via an interpreter.
She was followed by Sharon Lokedi of Kenya, this year's Boston winner, who stayed with Feysa most of the race but finished 34 seconds back.
"It certainly became quite a battle, especially after the pacemaker dropped out around 33k. But around 35k, that's when I became pretty sure I had this in the bag," said Feysa.
Fellow Kenyan Brigid Kosgei, who set a then-world record of 2:14:04 in Chicago in 2019, continued her fine recent form with third place.
The 32-year-old -- a two-time winner in London, Tokyo and Chicago -- won last year's Shanghai Marathon and took this year's Tokyo title.
More than 55,000 runners competed over the 26.2-mile layout winding through the streets of Chicago.
Catherine Debrunner of Switzerland shattered her own women's wheelchair world record with a time of 1:33:16.

title: Abhishek  Arshdeep guide India to T20 win over West Indies
description: The hosts defend a total of 223 to move ahead in the five match series with two games remaining
content:
The hosts defend a total of 223 to move ahead in the five-match series with two games remaining
Abhishek Sharma struck a quick 69 before Arshdeep Singh's three wickets helped India to a 14-run win over the West Indies in the third T20 international on Sunday.
Opener Abhishek's 30-ball assault guided India to 223 all out, a total their bowlers defended by restricting West Indies to 209-7 in Indore, giving them 2-1 lead in the five-match series.
"It was wonderful to see the bowlers being confident," India captain Shreyas Iyer said.
"The clarity was very much visible when I was interacting. They were ready to take up the challenge and that's what we want."
The previous two games had been won by the team batting second, as the West Indies knocked off a target of 250 to level the series on Friday, pulling off the second highest successful chase in T20Is.
Abhishek handed India a quick start as he put on 108 runs with fellow left-hander Ishan Kishan, who made 37, after India were put in to bat.
Sanju Samson fell for just three before India's batters responded with regular boundaries, Abhishek reaching his fifty off 18 balls.
Spinner Roston Chase broke the stand as he removed Kishan and then dismissed Iyer for one in the same over.
Pace bowler Shamar Springer cut short Abhishek's knock, which featured six fours and five sixes, as India began to wobble.
Tilak Varma (28) and Nitish Kumar Reddy (21) kept the score ticking over as wickets continued to fall.
Lower-order contributions from Axar Patel, who hit 20, and Prince Yadav, who made an unbeaten 13 off six balls, boosted the total.
"Probably with the ball, we could've executed a little bit better," said West Indies skipper Shai Hope. "So those little margins would be the deciding factor come the end of the game."
In reply, West Indies Hope, who made an unbeaten 102 in the previous series-levelling win, for five off left-arm quick Arshdeep before Shimron Hetmyer hit the same bowler for a six and three fours in a 19-run over.
Hetmyer made 43 off 26 balls before being dismissed by Naman Dhir and Rovman Powell fell for five as West Indies slipped in their chase.
Dhir struck again to send back opener Kamil Pooran, who hit a 27-ball 42, to reduce the opposition to 105-4 in the 11th over.
Sherfane Rutherford attempted to repeat his heroics for the second game, clubbing 32 off 20 before Arshdeep bowled him in the 18th over to effectively extinguish West Indies' hopes.
The fourth match is on Wednesday in Hyderabad.

title: Verstappen wins Singapore Grand Prix for first time
description: The Dutchman beats Charles Leclerc by 7 335 seconds  with Kimi Antonelli third
content:
The Dutchman beats Charles Leclerc by 7.335 seconds, with Kimi Antonelli third
Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time in his career on Sunday to complete a perfect weekend where he also finished first in the sprint and was on pole for both races.
Red Bull's Verstappen finished 7.335sec ahead of Ferrari's Charles Leclerc with championship leader Kimi Antonelli third for Mercedes after 62 laps under the lights of the Marina Bay Street Circuit.
The four-time world champion had never won or even achieved a pole position in nine previous attempts going back to his debut for Toro Rosso in 2015.
"It has taken a while but I think this race was very good," said a delighted Verstappen, who was celebrating back-to-back wins after triumphing in Malaysia seven days ago, his first victory of 2026.
"We had pace when we needed to have it on the soft tyre and the medium. So of course very happy to win here," the Dutchman added after claiming the top step of the podium on his 250th grand prix start.
"I think the last few races have been really positive for us, we have a lot of motivation in the team to try and deliver even more results.
"Hopefully we can have a bit more fun until the end of the year."
The McLaren pair of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri were fourth and fifth, ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, who dropped from third on the grid to sixth after botching his tyre strategy.
Liam Lawson's RB was seventh, Nico Hulkenberg eighth in the Audi and George Russell, who started from the back of the grid because of engine penalties, came home ninth in his Mercedes.
"It was a very tough race out there, but really happy with a podium in the end," said Antonelli, who increased his championship lead to 102 points over Russell.
Isack Hadjar in the second Red Bull, who started from the pit lane, rounded out the points scorers in 10th.
"We were quite strong at the beginning of the race, then we started degrading," said Leclerc.
"We did a different strategy to Max, I gave it my all and I don't regret anything. I don't think there was much more to do today."
Verstappen was put under immediate pressure from the quick-reacting Leclerc as he launched from pole position at lights out.
The Dutchman had to swoop across to his left to cut off the Ferrari driver and stay ahead into turn one.
Leclerc stuck to the rear of Verstappen through the first few laps as his teammate Hamilton kept Antonelli at bay.
Hamilton was the only one of the front-runners to start on the slower medium tyres and he was the first to pit, taking on fresh soft rubber on lap 19.
Verstappen left it until lap 32 to stop, and once all the top six had pitted, the order was the same as at the start.
Antonelli and Leclerc dived for a second time under a virtual safety car caused by Lance Stroll's Aston Martin breaking down.
But Hamilton bafflingly decided to stay out on much older tyres, despite being called in by his team, an aberration that would cost the seven-time world champion a podium finish.
Leclerc on fresh rubber quickly passed Hamilton for second.
Norris attempted to overtake Hamilton at the start of lap 55 only to lose his place to Antonelli, who then picked off the Ferrari to move up to third.
"I managed to take advantage of the fight with Lando and Lewis, and very happy with that," said Antonelli.
Norris did get past Hamilton, whose tyres were shot, on the next lap followed by Piastri.
"Sorry boys. I let you down today with that strategy," said Hamilton on team radio.
"My call, and I lost us valuable points. I'll try and make up for it in the next one."

title: Australia seize control against Proteas
description: Smith breaks Test catching record as visitors take 106 run lead
content:
Smith breaks Test catching record as visitors take 106-run lead.
Steve Smith broke the Test record for the most career catches by a fielder as Australia played themselves into a strong position on the third day of the first Test against South Africa at Kingsmead on Sunday.
Smith held four catches, taking his total to 223, as South Africa were bowled out for 284 in reply to Australia’s first innings of 390.
Nic Maddinson (17 not out) and Travis Head (10 not out) added 33 runs off just 5.4 overs to stretch Australia’s overall lead to 139 before bad light ended play for the third day in a row.
Maddinson, who laboured to a 33-ball duck in the first innings, hit two fours off Marco Jansen in the first over of the second innings and added a six off Wiaan Mulder before play was called off.
Australia’s bowlers applied relentless pressure on an easy-paced pitch and a succession of South African batsmen contributed to their own dismissals by playing poor shots.
Six Protea batters reached 30 but David Bedingham’s 49 was the top score.
Australian captain Pat Cummins took three for 54 and Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon took two each as Australia’s long-serving bowling quartet combined with customary efficiency.
Smith started the day on 219 catches, one behind Joe Root of England.
He equalled the record when he caught South African captain Temba Bavuma. Standing at slip, he anticipated Bavuma's reverse sweep against off-spinner Nathan Lyon and moved to his right with Bavuma's mistimed shot going straight to him.
Smith, playing in his 126th Test, broke the record when he lunged to his left from second slip to hold a sharp edge from Bedingham off Australian captain Pat Cummins.
Smith thought he had taken another catch when he held a low edge from Wiaan Mulder at slip in the over before lunch. Mulder started walking off the field but the umpires reviewed the incident and decided the ball had not carried.
But Smith was in the action again with a spectacular catch to dismiss Kyle Verreynne, again anticipating well at slip as the South African wicketkeeper made good contact with a reverse sweep which Smith held in an outstretched right hand.
His fourth catch was from an edge to slip by last man Anrich Nortje off the bowling of Beau Webster.
Smith’s career haul of 223 catches exceeds the total of all but 11 specialist wicketkeepers.

title: One terrorist killed in Bannu operation  security sources
description: Say security operations had proved effective in dismantling terrorist networks and restricting their movement
content:
Sources say security operations proved effective in dismantling terrorist networks, restricting their movement
Security forces killed one terrorist during an intelligence-based operation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's (K-P's) Bannu district, security sources said on Monday.
The operation was carried out based on confirmed intelligence, the sources said, adding that security forces were maintaining close surveillance on the movement and presence of Fitna al-Khawarij in the area.
Fitna al - Khawarij is the term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
The operation was part of ongoing security efforts under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision to counter terrorism in the province, according to the sources. They said security operations had proved effective in dismantling terrorist networks and restricting their movement.
Security forces remained committed to eliminating terrorism from K-P, the sources said, adding that operations would continue until the last terrorist was eliminated.
Read: Security forces kill 11 terrorists in separate Balochistan, K-P operations
Earlier this month, 12 people were killed and 35 others injured when a blast struck a joint checkpoint near Aman Mela in the Darazinda area of Dera Ismail Khan, with the TTP claiming responsibility for the attack.
On September 19, 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred in a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, the Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
In a separate incident, a captain and a lieutenant were among six security personnel martyred in an exchange of fire in Hangu district, while eight terrorists were killed.
Read More : Nine policemen martyred, 28 injured in terror attack on police checkpost in K-P's Hangu
According to two security reports presented to the federal cabinet yesterday, terrorist incidents in K-P increased by 195% between March 1, 2024, and September 23, 2026, while drone attacks rose sharply, with the provincial police and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) facing serious shortages of modern weapons, operational equipment and trained personnel.
The reports, prepared by the K-P police and intelligence agencies, were presented by Director General Intelligence Bureau (IB) Fuad Asadullah. According to the reports, the sharp rise in terrorist attacks over the past two years had become a serious security challenge for the province.
They attributed the worsening situation to terrorist elements based in Afghanistan, local facilitators, what they described as the provincial government's flawed policies and its soft approach towards militants, as well as inadequate preparedness and counterterrorism measures at the provincial level.
The reports said 73% of terrorist attacks recorded in K-P during 2026 targeted police and security personnel, underscoring the growing pressure on law enforcement agencies.

title: Iran says reviewing US proposals for talks as indirect messages continue
description: US Iran war  Strait of Hormuz blockade
content:
Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Navy says oil tanker struck mine in Strait of Hormuz
Iran said on Monday that it is reviewing US proposals for negotiations as Tehran and Washington continue to exchange messages through mediators.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei told his weekly press conference that Pakistan and Qatar continue to play a mediating role between Iran and the US.
“The exchange of messages between Iran and the US through mediators continues,” Baghaei said.
“We are reviewing the Americans’ proposals for negotiations. Iran’s preconditions must be observed for any negotiations,” he added.
Iran dismisses US claims of normalcy in Strait of Hormuz, says they don’t match reality https://t.co/h0mRiMzKNK pic.twitter.com/1q2bd4vxPt
Baghaei said Russia also continues to play a “constructive” role regarding Iran’s nuclear file, pointing to Moscow’s involvement in the 2015 nuclear agreement.
He said Iranian and Russian relations are based on mutual trust and that Tehran welcomes supportive efforts by friendly countries, but stressed that, “technically and precisely,” mediation between Iran and the US remains in the hands of countries such as Pakistan and Qatar.
Turning to the Strait of Hormuz, Baghaei said developments there were a direct consequence of US and Israeli attacks on Iran and rejected suggestions that Tehran’s actions were intended to create negotiating leverage.
“What we have seen in the Strait of Hormuz since February 28 was the direct result of the US and the Israeli regime’s attack on Iran,” he said.
“With the current US approach, security will not return,” he added.
Baghaei rejected US assertions that Iran had lost its leverage, saying such claims did not correspond with realities on the ground.
“They can say Iran has lost its leverage, but we are doing our work,” he said, arguing that energy markets were not responding to Washington’s assertions.
Baghaei also expressed “deep concern” over continuing tensions on the Arab Peninsula and said Tehran was ready to facilitate dialogue between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis in Yemen.
“We do not want war and hostilities to continue between two Islamic countries,” he said.
The spokesman said Iran’s consultations with regional countries were continuing and that Tehran had repeatedly offered to help facilitate dialogue and a peaceful settlement.
Strait of Hormuz is part of Iran’s national security: Official
Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs, Kazem Gharibabadi, said the Strait of Hormuz is part of Iran’s national security, and that the country will continue to control the strategic waterway until the United States returns to its commitments, according to IRNA .
Gharibabadi made the remarks at a press conference in Bandar Abbas, the capital of Hormuzgan Province in southern Iran, on Sunday evening.
“The Strait of Hormuz is part of the Islamic Republic of Iran’s national security, and Iran reserves the right to take the necessary measures to protect its national security,” he said, rejecting criticism of Iran’s control of the strategic waterway.
Strait of Hormuz is part of Iran’s national security: Official https://t.co/ArTbzUAM5x pic.twitter.com/SWGY9Uwpob
“These control measures will remain in place until the United States, as the main aggressor, concludes that military action is not the solution and returns to its commitments,” Gharibabadi said, adding that Iran’s declared arrangements were being enforced in the strait.
Under these arrangements, warships are barred from passing through, while commercial vessels may transit after completing the required coordination, he added.
“At present, no vessel can pass through the strait without coordination with the Islamic Republic of Iran. Vessels that attempt to do so without Iran’s coordination will violate the arrangements announced by Iran and face punitive measures by our Armed Forces,” he stressed.
The deputy foreign minister also referred to an understanding reached between Iran and Oman on the passage of vessels through the Strait of Hormuz.
“The United States’ return to its commitments is an essential and integral part of the process, and any subsequent action by the Islamic Republic of Iran will be contingent on it,” he said.
Gharibabadi added Iran had always sought good and constructive relations with all its neighbours.
He reiterated Iran’s position that security in the Persian Gulf region can only be ensured by the countries of the region, not by foreign forces.
“During the 40-day war, everyone saw that the presence of foreign forces, particularly the United States, was the main source of insecurity not only for the region but also for countries hosting US military bases and equipment. This is a lesson that must be learned from these recent developments and acts of military aggression,” he said.
Military approach in Yemen will make region’s situation more complicated: Araghchi
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stressed that insistence on a military approach and ignoring a political solution will make the ongoing regional situation more complex, according to IRNA .
Military approach in Yemen will make region’s situation more complicated: @araghchi https://t.co/seBMGHz7Tu pic.twitter.com/Bn2CSrKwYk
Speaking in a telephone call with his Saudi counterpart Faisal bin Farhan late on Sunday, Araghchi expressed concern over the escalation of tensions.
He said that persisting with a military approach while neglecting a political solution will only exacerbate the current situation.
The existing crises in the region have no military solution, he reiterated.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Navy says oil tanker struck mine in Strait of Hormuz
An oil tanker struck a mine while attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz, triggering an explosion in its engine room, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said Sunday.
The IRGC Navy said in a statement that the supertanker, capable of carrying around 2 million barrels of oil, was attempting to transit the strategic waterway with its navigation system switched off.
The IRGC Navy: A shuttle tanker (the third oil tanker) laden with 750,000 barrels of crude oil tried to transit through a prohibited route, disregarding the IRGC's repeated warnings. As a result, the vessel struck a sea mine, triggering an explosion and a fierce fire. pic.twitter.com/GZYDkHEIBI
The oil tanker is the third vessel to strike naval mines along the prohibited route in the Strait of Hormuz since Saturday, it added.
The statement did not identify the vessel or specify its nationality or flag.
The IRGC Navy renewed its warning that vessels switching off their navigation systems while passing through the waterway would be classified as “hostile vessels.”
The announcement came after the US Central Command (CENTCOM) said in late August that international shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz had been reopened following the removal of Iranian naval mines by US forces.
Read: Iran says US response to its proposal to reopen Hormuz was 'insufficient'
Iran announced on July 12 that it had again closed the strait following the resumption of US attacks on July 8.
Tehran has threatened to target vessels using routes other than those designated by Iranian authorities or attempting to cross the waterway without permission.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28. Tehran responded with missile and drone attacks across the region and effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, while Washington later imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports.
The US and Iran subsequently signed a memorandum of understanding in June concerning freedom of navigation in the strait, but implementation stalled over disagreements related to security in the strategic waterway.
Iran accuses CENTCOM chief of running oil smuggling operations in Strait of Hormuz
A senior Iranian security official accused the head of the US Central Command (CENTCOM) of orchestrating oil-smuggling operations in the Strait of Hormuz with the assistance of the United Arab Emirates military.
Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of Iran, made the claim in an interview over the weekend with Iranian state-run Press TV .
Rezaei said Admiral Brad Cooper was directing the operations using the UAE military, with five or six small boats transferring oil to large tankers.
He said Iranian forces had been striking five or six vessels involved in the operations each night over the past two or three months.
