There was no immediate comment from the US or the UAE on Rezaei’s claims.
Rezaei also rejected US President Donald Trump’s assertion that the Strait of Hormuz was open, insisting that Iran remained in control of the strategic waterway.
“From now on, therefore, we will maintain control over the management of the Strait of Hormuz. It will remain under our management to ensure peace and security in the region. We will not back down on this issue,” he said.
He said maritime traffic through the strait remained far below prewar levels and accused Washington and its regional allies of using smuggling networks to move oil through the waterway.
Rezaei also warned that Iran could target US-linked technology infrastructure in the region if the United States attacks the country again.
“We have not yet included these assets among our targets. But if war breaks out, many of these cables, data centres, artificial intelligence facilities and numerous other sites will be destroyed,” he said.
He put the value of such infrastructure at more than $2 trillion.
The Iranian official said Tehran was also prepared to deploy additional military capabilities in the event of renewed hostilities.
“Today, we are fully prepared to introduce new capabilities if the war starts again,” he said.

Saudi Arabia's foreign minister discussed the latest regional escalation and efforts to address it with his Iranian counterpart on Sunday, according to a Saudi Foreign Ministry statement.

title: HPV drive set to confront endemic vaccine hesitancy
description: HPV drive set to confront endemic vaccine hesitancy
content:
As authorities prepare their first campaign to vaccinate girls aged 9 to 14 against cervical cancer, quiet concerns ov
As Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) prepares to launch its first province-wide vaccination campaign against cervical cancer, health authorities face a challenge that goes beyond arranging doses and vaccination teams - convincing parents to have their daughters vaccinated.
Cervical cancer is primarily caused by persistent infection with the human papillomavirus (HPV), a virus transmitted through sexual contact. Globally, the disease claims more than 350,000 lives annually, while in Pakistan, more than 5,000 new cases and over 3,000 deaths are estimated each year, making vaccination and early detection crucial.
A year after its launch in Punjab and Sindh, the HPV vaccination campaign is now set to reach K-P, where the Health Department plans to vaccinate around 2.9 million girls aged nine to 14 - including 1.6 million school-going and 1.3 million out-of-school girls - between November 2 and November 14.
However, health officials and experts acknowledge that reaching every eligible girl will require more than vaccination teams and vaccine doses. Winning the confidence of parents and communities, addressing misinformation and overcoming vaccine hesitancy will be critical to the success of the campaign.
This is particularly pertinent in K-P where vaccine hesitancy has assumed an endemic status among the local population given the controversial history of the polio campaign and its links to CIA missions. Even today, K-P continues to record a significant number of refusals during polio campaigns, while vaccination workers have also faced security threats in several areas.
Despite these concerns, not all parents are hesitant about the campaign. While some remain wary of the vaccine's safety and possible reactions, others, particularly those who have witnessed the devastating effects of cervical cancer, see vaccination as an important safeguard for their daughters.
Bashir Khan, who lost his wife to cervical cancer, said he intended to have both his daughters vaccinated. "Losing my wife has made me particularly conscious of the importance of prevention. Parents should understand the importance of protecting their children from a disease that can have devastating consequences," urged Khan.
Conversely, Shamaila Bibi, another parent, was concerned about whether vaccination teams would be properly trained and whether the vaccine could cause reactions among girls. "The problem here is that people often become suspicious even about something positive. If, God forbid, something happens to a girl after vaccination, no parent would want to vaccinate their daughter," she said.
Health experts say such concerns need to be addressed through direct communication rather than allowing rumours to fill the information gap. Dr Bawar Shah, president of the Pakistan Paediatric Association's Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa chapter, told The Express Tribune that the HPV vaccine was safe and had been administered in countries around the world.
"Cervical cancer is increasing rapidly in Pakistan and vaccination offers an important means of preventing the disease. If parents have any questions or concerns, they should discuss them with the Health Department's vaccination teams and seek clarification," said Dr Shah.
Asad Zia, Assistant Director of the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) and in-charge of the Social and Behavior Change (SBC) Cell at the Directorate General Health Services (DGHS) K-P, said awareness campaigns were being conducted in schools, mosques and communities to educate parents about cervical cancer and the HPV vaccine.
Zia claimed health teams were also visiting areas where people had concerns about the campaign. In a recent visit to remote Kurram district, officials met religious scholars, community leaders and residents to address their questions and misconceptions about the vaccine.
When combining the entrenched public mistrust around vaccines with the tabooed nature of female reproductive issues, it is not hard to imagine that convincing families to vaccinate their teenage daughters will spark varying levels of backlash among locals.

title: K P experiences fourth spell of governor s rule
description: K P experiences fourth spell of governor s rule
content:
From Bhutto's 1975 crackdown to Musharraf's 1999 takeover
Governor's rule has been imposed in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa for the fourth time in the province's history, transferring executive powers from the provincial government to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, while an emergency has simultaneously been declared in 12 districts under Article 232 of the Constitution.
The latest development marks the suspension of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) government led by Chief Minister Muhammad Sohail Afridi. Under the new arrangement, Governor Kundi will administer the province with the assistance of an interim cabinet.
The province has experienced three previous periods of Governor's rule, each arising from a different political and constitutional crisis.
The first instance occurred in 1975 under the federal government of then-prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. The measure followed the assassination of Hayat Muhammad Khan Sherpao in a bomb blast while he was addressing a gathering at the Department of History at the University of Peshawar. The federal government subsequently banned the National Awami Party (NAP), made arrests and placed the province under Governor's rule.
The second episode came in 1994, when the federal government led by Benazir Bhutto moved against the provincial administration of Muslim League chief minister Pir Sabir Shah. Amid a political confrontation, assembly members reportedly disappeared and a no-confidence motion was brought against Shah. Aftab Ahmad Khan Sherpao subsequently formed the provincial government.
The third period followed the military takeover by then-army chief General Pervez Musharraf in October 1999, which removed the government of prime minister Nawaz Sharif. Muslim League Governor Mian Gul Aurangzeb was replaced by Lieutenant General (retired) Muhammad Shafiq. He was later succeeded by Lieutenant General (retired) Syed Iftikhar Hussain, who administered the province with his own cabinet until the formation of the Muttahida Majlis-e-Amal (MMA) government in late 2002.
The latest arrangement differs from the previous episodes because the imposition of Governor's rule has coincided with an emergency covering 12 districts, reflecting the security-related scope of the current measures.
The affected areas include the eight merged tribal districts: Khyber, Mohmand, Kurram, Orakzai, Bajaur, North Waziristan, South Waziristan Upper and South Waziristan Lower. The four other districts are Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Bannu and Lakki Marwat.
The emergency covers the Bannu and Dera Ismail Khan divisions in their entirety and parts of the Peshawar, Kohat and Malakand divisions. The Hazara and Mardan divisions have been exempted from the emergency measures.
Meanwhile, disruption of internet services has caused widespread confusion across the province, complicating communication and access to information amid the political and administrative changes.

title: Wandering families content on living under open sky
description: Wandering families content on living under open sky
content:
Belongings, skills and memories travel to every temporary shelter
Across the plains of South Punjab, families known as Pakhiwas live in small tents on vacant pieces of land.
They stay in one place for some time before moving elsewhere, carrying their belongings, traditional skills and memories of the places they have visited. For them, life is a journey and a temporary shelter is home.
The word Pakhi means bird in the local language. Like birds that wander from place to place, these families travel in search of work and shelter, with the open sky as their constant companion.
Their way of life differs from that of settled communities, yet they have preserved their traditions, ancestral occupations and cultural identity across generations.
For Pakhiwas families, home is not always a house with walls and a roof.
Sometimes, it is a tent beneath a tree, a patch of open ground or a shelter built from whatever material is available. Their lives remain closely linked to nature, changing seasons and the daily struggle to earn a living.
Saleem Pakhiwas says he has spent his entire life living this way.
"Since I opened my eyes, I have seen our families moving from one place to another and putting up tents wherever we find a suitable place," he says.
Saleem makes different kinds of baskets to earn a living. His work requires patience and skill, and his products serve practical purposes in everyday life.
As factory-made goods become increasingly common, his craft represents a traditional livelihood that continues to survive in the region.
Other community members pursue different occupations.
Some collect wastepaper and scrap to support their families. Their work also helps recover materials for reuse and recycling, although their contribution often goes unnoticed.
Akram Pakhiwas, who has spent much of his life in different parts of Multan, earns money by collecting mango stones.
He gathers them and sells them to farmers and nursery owners who use them to grow mango plants. South Punjab is famous for its mango orchards, and Akram has connected his livelihood with the region's agricultural economy. What many people discard after eating a mango becomes a source of income for him and a useful resource for nursery growers.
His work demonstrates how people with limited resources find opportunities in things others leave
Life in a tent may seem difficult to those accustomed to permanent homes, but Pakhiwas families have learned to adapt.
Akram acknowledges that they lack many facilities available to settled households, yet years of experience have taught them to manage everyday challenges.
Summer heat in Multan can be particularly harsh for people living in temporary shelters.
Akram says families use small solar panels to meet some basic electricity needs, making daily life more manageable.
Winter brings different challenges. Families cover their shelters carefully to protect themselves from cold winds, using material and methods learned over generations. Although their homes are simple, experience helps them adapt to changing weather.
Healthcare remains a concern. Akram says families generally obtain medicines from local hakims.

title: Fuel costs raise food prices
description: Fuel costs raise food prices
content:
Official poultry rates in Lahore surge sharply
Consumers in the metropolis faced mounting pressure from high food prices this week as official poultry rates surged and essential food items continued to sell above government-notified limits, adding to concerns over the rising cost of household essentials amid higher fuel costs.
Despite the availability of official price lists, substantial gaps persisted between the notified and retail rates of vegetables, fruits and poultry. Food purchases take up a growing share of household budgets, while higher fuel costs add to the financial pressure.
The poultry market witnessed a sharp increase, with the official price of live chicken rising by Rs45 to Rs364378 per kilogramme and meat rate jumping by Rs65 to Rs548 per kg.
However, live birds remained largely unavailable for sale across the city, while chicken meat was sold at Rs550600 per kg. Boneless chicken remained more expensive at up to 1,100 per kg, putting further pressure on citizens trying to manage their daily food expenses.
Vegetable prices also remained under pressure, with several essential items selling well above their official rates. Local garlic rose by Rs25 per kg to Rs210220 but retailed at Rs280300 per kilogramme.
Bitter gourd, spinach, capsicum, cauliflower, carrots and peas also recorded substantial retail premiums.
Capsicum was officially priced at Rs229240 per kg but sold for Rs350400, while peas were notified at Rs365380 and retailed at Rs500600.
Fruit prices also remained elevated, with dates selling for Rs8002,400 per kg, black grapes at around Rs800 and various varieties of pomegranates fetching Rs450800 per kg.
The rising cost of food supplies is adding to the difficulties faced by households already dealing with other essential expenses. Higher fuel costs also increase the cost of transporting goods to markets.

title: 95  of Pakistanis have high blood lipid levels  doctors warn
description: 95  of Pakistanis have high blood lipid levels  doctors warn
content:
Experts say changing dietary habits fuel heart disease among youngsters
High blood lipid levels are contributing to the rising incidence of cardiovascular disease in Pakistan, with medical experts warning that unhealthy dietary habits are increasingly putting young people at risk.
Prof Muhammad Nawaz Lashari, secretary general of the Lipid Society of Pakistan and a professor at Dow University of Health Sciences, said on Sunday that a study had found excessively high blood lipid levels in 95% of the population.
Addressing a press conference on October 10, he said heart disease was increasingly being reported among school and university students, partly because of changing dietary patterns and greater consumption of fatty foods and fast food.
Lashari said a digital application was being developed for the first time in Pakistan to raise awareness about cholesterol and explain the difference between good and bad cholesterol. The application will be available in English, Urdu and Sindhi.
The experts said excessive cholesterol and other blood fats could accumulate in arteries, restrict blood flow and increase the risk of heart attacks and strokes. They attributed the growing incidence of cardiovascular disease among younger people partly to a shift away from traditional home-cooked meals towards foods rich in fat.
Cardiologist Prof Muhammad Ishaq, Dr Akram Sultan, Prof Abdul Rashid, Prof Khalida Soomro, Prof Rafiq Memon, Prof Jameel Ahmed, Dr Ghulam Abbas, Dr Shabbir Muhammad and Dr Dil Bahar Ali Asad were also present at the press conference.
The doctors said many people remained unaware of their cholesterol levels, despite the availability of a simple blood test known as a lipid profile. The test measures different types of blood fats, including high-density lipoprotein (HDL), or good cholesterol; low-density lipoprotein (LDL), or bad cholesterol; and triglycerides.
They recommended regular screening, suggesting that people undergo a lipid profile every six months, while emphasising that testing frequency should be guided by individual risk factors and medical advice.
The experts urged the public to adopt balanced diets, exercise regularly and reduce their consumption of fried and fatty foods. They stressed that early identification of risk factors, timely medical assessment and treatment where necessary could help reduce heart attacks, strokes and premature deaths.

title: Rising flu cases trigger Umrah vaccination
description: Rising flu cases trigger Umrah vaccination
content:
Experts urge timely immunisation as respiratory infections rise and virus continues to evolve ahead of the winter seas
Influenza cases are rising in Karachi, with patients reporting high fever, headache, sore throat, chest infections, dry cough, body aches and other flu-related symptoms. Doctors say the number of influenza patients visiting public and private hospitals has increased by around 20 per cent.
Amid the rise in cases, the Sindh government has made influenza vaccination mandatory for Umrah pilgrims travelling through Karachi Airport. Meningitis and polio vaccinations have also been made compulsory, with pilgrims required to present vaccination documentation before departure.
Medical experts say the current flu virus has shown symptoms similar to those associated with Covid-19, although there is disagreement over whether the virus represents a new influenza variant or a modified Covid-19 variant.
Pharmacist Dr Usman Ghani, who is involved in importing vaccines into Pakistan, said influenza viruses have several strains and can change their characteristics every year, requiring vaccines to be updated accordingly.
"Some health experts are describing this year's influenza virus as a modified Covid-19 variant, while some doctors believe it is a new influenza variant that has changed its characteristics," he said.
Ghani believed vaccination remained an important means of protection against influenza, particularly because the virus can spread rapidly from one person to another. He said children and elderly people were among those more vulnerable to infection, particularly when immunity was weak.
He added that the demand for vaccines had increased significantly following the Covid-19 pandemic as public awareness about vaccination improved. However, he warned that some organisations were importing vaccines from unqualified companies, leaving consumers unable to determine whether the products were genuine.
"Customs officials have even intercepted products sold as vaccines that turned out to contain distilled water or normal saline," he said, stressing that vaccines should be imported from reputable manufacturers.
According to Ghani, influenza becomes more prevalent with the onset of colder weather, generally beginning around October. He said vaccines approved by international health authorities generally have a shelf life of one year and that Pakistan now imports around 700,000 influenza vaccine doses annually because of rising demand.
The vaccination requirement has particular significance for people travelling for Hajj and Umrah, where large numbers of people from different countries gather in confined spaces. A family preparing to travel for Umrah said vaccination was necessary to protect pilgrims from infectious diseases.
"Thousands of people from different countries are present during Umrah, so vaccination is important for protecting people's health," the family said.
Under the new requirements, Umrah pilgrims travelling through Karachi Airport must receive influenza, meningitis and polio vaccinations. After vaccination, they are required to upload their receipt to the NADRA website and obtain a vaccination card, which must be presented at the airport.
The rise in influenza cases has also renewed concerns over the quality and availability of vaccines in Pakistan. Experts say vaccination programmes can help reduce the spread and severity of seasonal influenza, but the public should ensure that vaccines are obtained through authorised and reliable sources.
With the flu season approaching and international travel increasing, health experts say vaccination and other preventive measures will remain important in limiting the spread of influenza, particularly among children, elderly people and other vulnerable groups.

title: Women cash in on digital opportunities

content:
Use e-commerce platforms and digital skills to achieve financial independence
Women entrepreneurs in Islamabad and Rawalpindi are turning smartphones and laptops into sustainable businesses, running successful online stores, freelance services and digital brands from home and becoming financially independent.
With growing internet access, digital payment solutions and government training programs like DigiSkills and e-Rozgaar, a new generation of women business owners is emerging, proving that a small online idea can become a big enterprise.
Women are emerging as queens of their own online enterprises, earning handsome incomes and becoming financially independent, often as sole breadwinners for their families.
From home-based bakeries and Instagram clothing stores to freelancing and YouTube channels, they are transforming mobile screens into thriving shops and offices.
Thirty-year-old Aneela Tariq, owner of "Aneela's Bake O'Clock" in G-11, started baking cakes at home during Covid-19 and began taking orders on Instagram. Today she receives 20 to 30 orders daily and earns over Rs200,000 a month.
"I started with one oven and a Facebook page. Now I have three staff members, all women from my neighbourhood. Online business gave me identity and income without leaving my home," she said. She further said many who were once dependent on others are now covering school fees, managing household expenses and supporting their parents.
Similarly, Zara Ahmed, founder of "Zara- Handmade Jewellery" based in Rawalpindi, sells handmade earrings and clutches through Daraz and Instagram to customers across Pakistan and Dubai.
"My shop is online, my customers are online. I don't need a big plaza. I started with Rs10,000 and now my monthly turnover is Rs300,000," she said.
Sumbal Sheikh from I-8, who runs "Modest Wear by Sumbal", an online abaya store, said women feel more comfortable selling online. "Many women cannot go to markets daily due to family responsibilities. Online work allows us to manage both home and business. I manage my store, parcels and payments from my mobile."
Experts say if provided better internet access, digital literacy and safe online payment mechanisms, women-led online businesses can significantly contribute to Pakistan's e-commerce economy.
For these women, the screen is no longer just for scrolling, it is a shop, an office and a path to self-reliance.

title: Doctors urge regular blood pressure checks
description: Doctors urge regular blood pressure checks
content:
Say undiagnosed hypertension can lead to heart attacks, life-threatening complications
Health experts have urged the public to undergo regular blood pressure checks and adopt healthier lifestyles, to avoid serious medical complications.
According to them, hypertension, commonly known as high blood pressure, often develops without noticeable symptoms, making routine monitoring, early diagnosis and timely treatment essential to preventing potentially life-threatening consequences.
Dr Saleem Baig, a cardiologist, said hypertension was a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases and could cause serious damage to the heart and blood vessels if left untreated.
"High blood pressure is often called a silent killer because many people do not experience obvious symptoms until complications develop. Regular screening is essential, even for people who feel healthy, as early diagnosis and appropriate treatment can significantly reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke," the doctor said.
Dr Raheel Saddiq, a medical specialist, said several factors could contribute to hypertension, including excessive salt intake, obesity, physical inactivity, smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, chronic stress, ageing and a family history of the disease.
"An unhealthy lifestyle can increase the risk of high blood pressure, but the condition can often be prevented or better controlled through practical changes, including reducing salt consumption, maintaining a healthy weight, exercising regularly and eating a balanced diet rich in fruits and vegetables," the specialist said.
The doctors emphasized that people should not rely on symptoms alone to determine whether their blood pressure was normal, as the condition could remain undetected for years.
They also stressed the importance of correct measurement techniques to ensure reliable readings and avoid misleading results that could affect clinical decisions. Doctors further advised avoiding exercise, tea, coffee and smoking.
Dr Haroon Khan, a general physician, said treatment should be tailored to each patient's condition and risk factors, adding that lifestyle changes alone might not be sufficient for everyone.
"People diagnosed with hypertension should follow their doctor's advice, take prescribed medicines regularly and monitor their blood pressure as recommended. They should not discontinue medication or change doses on their own simply because their readings have improved," the physician said.
The doctors recommended limiting salt intake, maintaining a healthy body weight, engaging in regular physical activity, avoiding tobacco, managing stress and getting adequate sleep as important measures to prevent and control hypertension.
They also urged people with diabetes, kidney disease, a family history of hypertension or other cardiovascular risk factors to discuss appropriate screening intervals with their healthcare providers. The burden of hypertension in Pakistan remains a major public health concern. The National Health Survey of Pakistan estimated that the condition affects around 18 per cent of adults and 33 per cent of adults above 45 years of age.

title: Unsafe school vans put children at risk
description: Unsafe school vans put children at risk
content:
Overcrowded vehicles and reckless driving endanger children in twin cities
Every morning, private school vans weave through Islamabad and Rawalpindi, carrying children to their classrooms. For parents, the journey is part of the daily routine. But behind the familiar school run, overcrowding, reckless driving and unsafe transport practices are raising concerns about the safety of young passengers.
For Class 6 student Yumna Amin, the risks became apparent when she arrived at school one morning without her schoolbag. The bag had reportedly fallen from the private van somewhere along the route, taking her books, notebooks and homework with it. Neither the driver nor the other passengers noticed its disappearance.
Teacher Fouzia of F-10/2 Model Girls College noticed Yumna without her bag and contacted her mother, asking her to speak to the driver and find out where it had been lost.
Although the belongings could be replaced, the incident raised a troubling question: if a schoolbag could fall from a moving vehicle unnoticed, how closely were the children being monitored?
Yumna also complained about cramped conditions inside school vans, where children often struggle to accommodate their bags, while drivers rushing to complete their routes expose young passengers to additional risks.
For many families, however, private school transport is a necessity. Parents leave for work early, and professional and household commitments make it difficult to manage school pick-and-drop arrangements themselves.
Nayab Ali said repeated encounters with what she described as irresponsible behaviour by school-van drivers had prompted her to arrange transport for her own children. Many parents, she added, could not afford the same option because of work and family commitments.
Another parent, Arsalan Rao, said he had repeatedly witnessed school transport drivers violating traffic rules.
"Countless times, I have seen van drivers flout traffic rules, yet traffic police often appear to do little to check such deplorable behaviour," he said, warning that reckless driving endangered every child inside the vehicle.
Authorities say enforcement is being stepped up. Rawalpindi traffic official Lehar Mirza said action was being taken against operators carrying children beyond designated seating capacity and those allowing schoolbags to hang from the rear or sides of moving vehicles.
She said violators were being warned and fined, while awareness sessions were being conducted in schools to educate students, parents, drivers and administrations about road safety.
Inspector Traffic Rana Ishtiaq Ahmed of the Education Wing of Islamabad Traffic Police said the department had intensified its road-safety campaign around government and private schools. Personnel were deployed near schools, while awareness activities targeted drivers, parents, teachers and school administrations.
He said traffic police encountered between 60 and 80 violators daily, including school transport drivers, with fines ranging from Rs500 to Rs1,500 depending on the offence. Vehicles failing to meet safety requirements could also face action.
Overcrowding remains a major concern, he said, with vehicles designed for around 10 children sometimes carrying 18 to 20. Police were also preparing a crackdown on vans and pick-ups fitted with rear grills or metal frames for hanging schoolbags.

The initiative is intended to provide an efficient, accessible and cost-effective mechanism for settling disputes outside the conventional court system while easing the pressure on courts dealing with a heavy backlog of cases.

title: Trump announces Russia Ukraine  energy ceasefire
description: Trump announces Russia Ukraine  energy ceasefire
content:
Zelenskiy says Trump's post was his first news of the deal
US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to what he described as an "energy ceasefire", hours after Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy had pushed back against US pressure for a unilateral end to strikes on Russian refineries.
In a social media post, Trump said the energy ceasefire would take effect immediately, but did not elaborate further.
In an interview with Axios, Zelenskiy said Trump's post was the first he had heard of the deal, though a senior Ukrainian official told Reuters that Ukraine was ready to agree to such a ceasefire if Russia was.
Trump, whose war in Iran has been blamed for high diesel prices that are weighing on Republicans' prospects at next month's midterm elections, had previously announced an energy ceasefire in Ukraine in mid-September, though neither side ever confirmed such an agreement was reached.
"Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" Trump wrote on Truth Social.
Earlier on Sunday, Zelenskiy had repeated Ukraine's long-standing position that it was willing to halt attacks on Russian refineries but only if Moscow ceased its own strikes on Ukrainian power infrastructure.
Any such deal would need to come with "real guarantees", Zelenskiy said.
"The real cause of the war in Europe is Russia and Russia alone," Zelenskiy said. "It's possible to stop strikes on energy infrastructure as early as today, but Putin does not want to do so."
In a dramatic deterioration in their relations, Trump on Saturday had warned Zelenskiy that he had "better damn well stop" attacking Russian refineries.

title: Cockroach  leaders released as protesters detained in India
description: Cockroach  leaders released as protesters detained in India
content:
Police detained hundreds of protesters in Delhi for a second day on Sunday as sporadic protests broke out demanding India's election chief ?quit, while a court ordered the release of "cockroach" movement founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other senior leaders.
Dipke and the other leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a nationwide youth protest movement, were detained when their plane landed in Delhi on Saturday as the movement planned to gather thousands ?of people at Jantar Mantar in Central Delhi.
The court ordered their release with an undertaking to "maintain public peace", the CJP said in a statement.
The youth movement, which has mobilised protests in recent months against a range of issues from ?government school infrastructure to jobs for young people, is one of the biggest political challenges to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in his 12 years in power.
The protesters are calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a revision of voter lists that critics say disproportionately benefits Modi.
Youth protesters, many of them from students organisations affiliated with India's communist parties, launched sporadic protests on Sunday afternoon in Delhi before police detained them and hauled them away in vehicles.
Small protests by dozens ?of people were also held in the cities of Mumbai, Kolkata, Panaji and Pune, local media reported.
Abhita Ruheja, a protester who was detained on Sunday, said the authorities had turned Delhi into a fortress. "Is this how a democracy works? They have been scrapping rights after rights and this is turning into a dictatorship," she said.
The All India Students' Association alleged in a post on X that those detained in Delhi were assaulted by police inside the vehicles.

title: Pope Leo to be operated in  coming days

content:
Pope Leo XIV on Sunday announced he would be operated "in the coming days" for a lump on his lung, saying it had been located "at a very early stage".
"During recent medical checks, a nodule on my lung was found. It has been detected at a very early stage and is very localised," the 71-year-old said in a weekly address in St Peter's Square.
"The doctors believe it would be right to intervene and so, following their advice, I have decided to have the operation to remove it. The operation is already planned in the coming days," he said.
Following the pope's statement during his Angelus prayers, the Vatican press office said the expected recovery time from the operation would be around one week.
Chicago-born Leo became the first US pope last year following the death of his Argentine predecessor Francis on April 21, 2025 at the age of 88.

title: Djibouti boat wreck leaves 139 dead
description: Djibouti boat wreck leaves 139 dead
content:
Vessel carried 305 migrants most of them Ethiopian
At least 139 migrants died, including 15 children, and 84 went missing when an overcrowded boat sank while heading from Djibouti to Yemen, a UN agency said Sunday.
The vessel was carrying 305 people, most of them Ethiopian, when it capsized north of the Djibouti town of Obock overnight on October 8-9, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said in a statement.
"Survivors told me that the boat started to sink backwards as soon as they got in it," Alexandre Coissac, IOM chief of mission in Djibouti, told AFP.
"This is a devastating loss of life," he said earlier in the statement.
"Our thoughts are with the survivors and the families who have lost loved ones or remain without news of their relatives."
The IOM gave an initial toll of 109 dead and 116 missing, and revised it to 139 dead and 84 missing in a later statement after more bodies were recovered.
Coissac said IOM teams were on the ground alongside Djiboutian authorities to provide emergency aid.
"This tragedy is a stark reminder of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek economic opportunities" by trying to cross the Bab al-Mandeb Strait to Yemen and then reach Gulf countries, he said.
Coissac said he had spoken to one survivor of the wreck who came from the Tigray region of northern Ethiopia, where rebels are battling the federal government in a recent flare-up of violence.
Among the 109 bodies earlier recovered were 52 men, 42 women and 15 children -- nine girls and six boys -- the initial statement said.
Eighty-two people survived the shipwreck, all Ethiopian nationals, according to the updated toll.
"Poverty, insecurity and the growing impacts of climate change drive many to undertake this journey, despite mounting instability across the Middle East," the IOM said.
The IOM said it was assisting 64 survivors at a migrant centre in Obock.
"Djiboutian authorities are continuing search and rescue operations as fears grow for those still missing."
It called it "one of the deadliest shipwrecks recorded" on the route.
IOM spokesman Kennedy Omondi Okoth told AFP this week that 178,000 people had arrived in Djibouti from Ethiopia from January to October this year.
Since September 10, the IOM detected more than 20,000 crossings to Djibouti from Ethiopia, despite a surge in conflict in Yemen.
The country is stricken by fighting between the Saudi-backed government and Tehran-backed Houthi rebels, who have joined in the regional conflict involving the US and its allies against Iran.

title: Four dead as cyclone Isaias drenches southern US
description: Four dead as cyclone Isaias drenches southern US
content:
Four people died in the southeastern United States as post-tropical cyclone Isaias threatened flooding and tornado risks Saturday as it moved northward after making landfall on Florida's Gulf Coast.
Isaias roared ashore late Friday as a Category 2 hurricane near the resort community of Destin, packing sustained winds of 105 miles (165 kilometers) per hour before weakening overnight, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) said.
It was the first hurricane of an Atlantic season tamed by a historic El Nino weather phenomenon, and the first hurricane since 2024 to hit the US mainland.
In Mary Esther, a coastal community near Destin, Matt Howard said he was fortunate the storm weakened ahead of landfall.
Despite losing power and having his neighbor's metal shed crash into his backyard, "overall, we were okay," he told AFP.
"We hunkered down, got in the center of our house, and did all the things you're supposed to do, and luckily came out on the other side," he said.
Officials reported at least four deaths related to the storm, including two from trees falling on homes -- one near Pensacola in Florida and another in Birmingham, Alabama.
AFP reporters saw overturned vehicles, downed trees and power lines, and numerous buildings with damaged roofs.
Streets along the coast were largely deserted after authorities ordered mandatory evacuations ahead of the storm.
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis warned at a briefing Saturday afternoon that threats remained even though the storm had passed.

title: Iran  US response to proposal to reopen Hormuz  insufficient
description: Iran  US response to proposal to reopen Hormuz  insufficient
content:
The United States' response to Iran's seven conditions in a proposal to reopen the strategic Strait of Hormuz was "insufficient", Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, was quoted by state media on Sunday as saying.
Iran presented a proposal during the UN General Assembly under which the Strait of Hormuz waterway could be reopened and normal maritime passage restored within seven days if the conditions were met, to which the US later replied via Qatari intermediaries.
Washington needs to clarify the issues that remain unclear to Tehran, Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, said, adding "we presented seven conditions to the Americans and clearly stated that the Strait of Hormuz would not be opened to them, and no negotiations would take place, until these conditions are met."
The White House did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
Rezaei said Iran is "no longer in the ?process of responding to the Americans".
"In their response, they have accepted some of our conditions, while others remain unclear," he added.
Tehran said late in September that it had received a US response to its latest proposal to resurrect the collapsed ceasefire in the Gulf, days after US President Donald Trump said he had rejected it.
Qatar and other mediators have transmitted messages between Washington and Tehran in an effort to end the conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the conduit for a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas before the war that began at the end of February with US and Israeli attacks on Iran.
Earlier, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that US-Israeli attacks on Iran's oil facilities and refineries have raised serious environmental risks.
"When an attack causes soil contamination, destruction of water resources, and the creation of hazardous materials, its effects can persist far beyond the time and place of the attack," he said, according to Iranian news agency ISNA.

title: PTI march fizzles out after K P emergency  arrests
description: PTI march fizzles out after K P emergency  arrests
content:
Gohar says measures will not resolve province's security issues
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) planned march towards Islamabad was thrown into disarray on Sunday as the federal government's imposition of an emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa effectively stripped the party of its provincial power base, while a sweeping security crackdown disrupted its mobilisation on the ground.
The planned mobilisation was derailed as police arrested 59 PTI workers in Swabi and six others in Khyber district, while reports emerged that ousted chief minister Sohail Afridi and the party's provincial president Junaid Akbar had also been taken into custody.
Police tightened security across the province, suspended mobile phone and PTCL internet services in Swabi and deployed personnel at key intersections and highways as the federal government moved to take control of the provincial administration.
Former chief minister Ali Amin Khan Gandapur said he had been placed under house arrest at his residence in Dera Ismail Khan.
Meanwhile, the PTI condemned the federal intervention as an assault on provincial autonomy and the democratic mandate, insisting that its political struggle and planned long march would continue.
The PTI caravan, led by Afridi, had been expected to reach Swabi on the night of October 11 as part of its mobilisation towards Islamabad. However, following the emergency and governor's rule, the anticipated show of strength failed to materialise in the district, where the party's local leadership remained largely absent and no major demonstration was reported.
Heavy police contingents were deployed at Aman Chowk in Swabi, Topi, Swabi Interchange and Shewa Adda in Razzar tehsil. Containers were also brought to Swabi Interchange, Jehangira Bridge and the bridge over the Indus River on the Peshawar-Islamabad Motorway amid concerns about possible protests and attempts to block traffic.
However, the Peshawar-Islamabad Motorway and the Grand Trunk Road remained open to traffic.
Police sources said raids had been conducted in Shewa Adda and adjoining areas after reports that the PTI caravan was expected to arrive. The action was aimed at detaining party workers, although no arrests had initially been reported.
PTI leaders had reportedly directed workers to assemble at the Razzar Sports Complex to prepare for the march. Some party activists and youth wing members subsequently gathered at Shewa Adda ground and Ismaila Interchange.
However, police dispersed some of the protesters.
The anticipated mobilisation failed to gain momentum. At Aman Chowk, the situation remained normal as traffic flowing and businesses operated as usual.
The picture changed as the crackdown intensified. Police had arrested 59 PTI workers in Swabi by the latest reports as the emergency and governor's rule effectively prevented the planned march from proceeding through the district as anticipated.
The crackdown extended to Khyber district, where police arrested six PTI workers who were protesting against governor's rule outside Bab-e-Khyber. District Police Officer Waqar Ahmed said police moved against the demonstrators, with dozens of PTI supporters participating in the protest before some fled and six were arrested.
The detained workers were shifted to Jamrud police station. The DPO said authorities would not allow anyone to disturb public order.
Afridi, Junaid Akbar reportedly arrested
Political tensions escalated further after the PTI claimed that Afridi and Junaid Akbar had been arrested following the suspension of the provincial government.
A message posted on Akbar's official social media account said the two leaders had been taken into custody. The party also announced their reported arrests in growing political repression.
An official confirmation from the relevant authorities was not available at the time of the initial reports.
Videos circulated on social media showing the container used by Afridi during the march abandoned beside a road in Charsadda, adding to uncertainty over the whereabouts of the former chief minister and the future of the protest.
Meanwhile, police placed Gandapur, another former K-P chief minister and a senior PTI leader, under house arrest at his residence in Dera Ismail Khan, according to police sources.
A heavy police contingent was deployed outside his home, while security arrangements were tightened in the surrounding area.
Gandapur confirmed the development in a social media message, saying it was an extremely regrettable and condemnable act. He said he was not intimidated by the measures and that the PTI's struggle would continue.
The reported detention of Afridi and Akbar, along with Gandapur's house arrest, dealt a further blow to the party's efforts to mobilise supporters after the federal intervention.
In a separate development, Additional Advocate General Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Shah Faisal Ilyas resigned in protest against "the unconstitutional imposition of an emergency" in the province.
Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, PTI chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan condemned the imposition of governor's rule and an emergency, arguing that neither measure would resolve the province's security problems.
He said counterterrorism efforts required a unified strategy developed through political consensus and rejected allegations that the K-P government had failed to cooperate with the federal authorities.
"If the problem of terrorism exists in 12 districts, why has governor's rule been imposed across the province?" he asked.
Gohar said the PTI had consistently condemned terrorism in all its forms and that the country's security and defence remained paramount. However, he argued that the fight against terrorism should not be used to justify political action against his party or undermine an elected provincial government.
The PTI chairman said the party would challenge governor's rule through the courts, provincial and national assemblies, and public forums. He maintained that the struggle for constitutional and democratic rights would continue.
Gohar also called for the release of political prisoners and the restoration of the legal rights of PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan.
He demanded that Khan be transferred to a hospital for treatment, that his family be permitted to meet him, and that they be provided with details of his health and treatment.
He said the PTI had approached the Supreme Court and high courts 19 times seeking relief for its incarcerated founder. After failing to obtain the relief it sought through the courts, the party had announced a long march for August 5 to secure Khan's rights, he added.
Gohar claimed that around 1,500 PTI workers were imprisoned in Punjab. He further alleged that 10 members of the K-P Assembly, including three ministers, and eight members of the National Assembly had also been arrested.
Rejecting the federal government's narrative concerning the party, he said political action against the PTI should not be conflated with efforts to eliminate terrorism.
Gohar further claimed that terrorism had not been discussed during 15 meetings between the PTI and government representatives before October 2. He said the provincial government had increased police capacity, provided security resources and participated in counterterrorism meetings.
He argued that federal interference had weakened the provincial government's authority and that sidelining an elected chief minister was inconsistent with democratic principles. An autonomous province, he maintained, was essential to a strong federation.
PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said the party had consistently called for a mutually agreed strategy to address terrorism, insisting that decisions on security operations should be made in consultation with political parties rather than imposed unilaterally.
Referring to the Parachinar agreement, Raja said the party wanted previously agreed decisions to be implemented rather than additional conditions being introduced.
He cited the February 2026 meeting of the Apex Committee and a resolution adopted at a peace jirga as important foundations for moving forward.
Raja said Afridi had taken a clear position on the issue and that the provincial government could not give the federal government unrestricted authority to undertake whatever measures it considered appropriate.
"We cannot give anyone written permission to do whatever they want and then endorse it," he said.
He stressed that any decision concerning governor's rule or an emergency had to conform to constitutional principles and emerge from political consensus.
According to Raja, negotiations had involved consultations with opposition leaders Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, while Maulana Fazlur Rehman and other political figures had been working to make the dialogue successful.
He claimed that negotiations had been progressing satisfactorily and rejected the imposition of an emergency as a hasty decision. He also cited Senator Kamran Murtaza as saying that the discussions were moving in the right direction.
Raja said the arrest of a provincial assembly speaker was an extraordinary step, arguing that the assembly continued to exist despite the federal intervention.
He said the crackdown would not force the PTI to abandon its principles, maintaining that the party was seeking peace and protection for innocent people.
Raja also reiterated that the announcement of Afridi's long march had not been withdrawn, saying peaceful protest was a fundamental constitutional right.
"We will not throw stones. Through peaceful protest, we have to express our moral position," he said, adding that a large-scale, peaceful demonstration by citizens across the country would convey a strong message.
He said people would decide how to express their displeasure over actions against democracy, while drawing a distinction between political protest and revolutionary action.
Raja Nasir Abbas calls for NAP implementation
Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, chief of Majlis Wahdat-e-Muslimeen (MWM) and opposition leader in the Senate, deplored the treatment meted out to the PTI, saying Pakistan was a federation whose provinces were united under a single Constitution.
He claimed that Imran Khan had secured the majority of public support in the elections and alleged that the ruling establishment feared the public mandate and had persistently targeted the PTI.
Abbas blamed the government for the prevailing insecurity, arguing that the conduct of those in power had caused greater damage than the country's external enemies could inflict.
He called for the implementation of the National Action Plan (NAP), saying the seven days since negotiations began could have been used to make meaningful progress towards a political settlement.
Abbas said his party could not support military operations in which ordinary citizens became victims. Counterterrorism measures, he argued, had to protect civilians and contribute to lasting peace rather than deepen public alienation.
The press conference was held at an imambargah in Islamabad's Barakahu after K-P House, where the alliance would ordinarily have held such briefings, was sealed. The opposition leaders said the move had forced them to seek an alternative venue.
The Tehreek-e-Tahafuz Ayin-e-Pakistan (TTAP) condemned the emergency and governor's rule as unconstitutional and contrary to democratic principles, announcing that it would challenge the decision through the courts, assemblies and public forums.

title: Maulana Fazl  accuses govt of U turn
description: Maulana Fazl  accuses govt of U turn
content:
Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Sunday categorically rejected the federal government's move to impose governor's rule and declare an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), accusing the government of reneging on its commitments despite progress in negotiations over Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) long march.
Speaking to the media at his residence, Fazl said his party would challenge the decision on every available democratic and constitutional platform, including the courts, parliament and the public.
"The JUI will take this matter to the people and to the courts. We will defend democratic rights and protect the rights of the people in parliament," he said, adding that the party categorically rejected the government's decision.
Recounting the sequence of events leading up to the announcement, Fazl said he had arrived in Islamabad on October 7, when PTI leaders approached him and shared information about the situation.
After hearing their account, he conveyed his assessment that the government had left no avenue open for negotiations.
He said both sides had presented their respective positions and that the PTI was advancing through different stages of its long march in K-P. At the JUI chief's urging, he added, the party had postponed its move towards Islamabad.
Fazl said he subsequently received an invitation from the Prime Minister's Office to attend a dinner with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. Having not met the premier for four months, he consulted his associates on whether he should accept the invitation. His colleagues advised him to meet the prime minister in the interest of the country.
According to Fazl, the prime minister insisted during their meeting that the long march should first be called off. The PTI, meanwhile, was demanding a meeting with its founding chairman, Imran Khan, followed by his transfer to a hospital.
Fazl said the dinner meeting involved a detailed discussion of the matter. He told the prime minister that he first needed to speak to the PTI leadership, as K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi was leading the march but had not been in contact with him.
After returning, Fazl said, he reached out to Afridi and other PTI leaders to discuss the situation and explore a way forward.
The JUI-F chief said he contacted the prime minister early on Sunday morning, around the time of the morning prayers, explaining that Sharif usually went to bed early and woke up very early. The prime minister told him that a cabinet meeting was scheduled and that they should speak before it began.
Fazl said Afridi had indicated that the PTI would call off its long march if the government accepted its demands.
He added that Sharif telephoned him at 9pm and said he would place all the matters before the cabinet. However, at 10pm, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar called to inform him that the government was imposing an emergency in the province.
Fazl said he questioned Dar about the rationale for the move. Dar, he recalled, cited the high level of terrorism in K-P.
"I asked him whether there was no terrorism in Balochistan," Fazl said, arguing that the difference lay in the political conduct of the two provincial governments. "The only difference is that the Balochistan government agrees with whatever the federal government says."
Explaining why he had publicly detailed the sequence of events, Fazl said the government had retreated despite having agreed to the proposed course of action.
"Why did the government back out despite accepting the demands? Why did it break its commitment?" he asked.
He also challenged the government's counterterrorism record, arguing that the deterioration of the security situation since the era of former military ruler Pervez Musharraf reflected a failure of policy and strategy.
"If the situation has worsened from Musharraf's time until today, it is their failure - a failure of their strategy," he said. "Tell us what has become of the operations against terrorism that have been under way since 2010."
Citing the situation in Dera Ismail Khan, Fazl alleged that police stations were sometimes left without police personnel at night, with officers staying in houses in nearby neighbourhoods instead of remaining at their posts.
He said the situation was evidence of the security challenges confronting the province.
"If the institutions are fighting a war against terrorism, we, too, are making sacrifices," he said, recalling that he had once had to collect 90 bodies from a single public gathering.
Fazl reiterated that his party would not accept the government's decision, deploring the move as an assault on democracy carried out in its name.
"These are the killers of democracy in the name of democracy," he said.
Questioning whether the proposed intervention was genuinely based on governance and performance, the JUI chief asked why the same standard was not being applied to Balochistan.
"If an emergency is being imposed in K-P based on performance, is the performance of the Balochistan government satisfactory?" he asked.
Condemning the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman on Sunday said saying the measures would not resolve the province's problems and urged the federal government to withdraw them and resume negotiations.
Addressing a public rally against the petroleum levy in Okara, the JI chief said the government should abandon the path of emergency measures and return to the negotiating table.
He argued that when those in power resort to governor's rule and emergencies to govern, it signals that their political authority is nearing its end.
Naeem accused the parties comprising the Pakistan Democratic Movement (PDM) of pursuing an anti-democratic course since the regime change.
He said the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) had a history of imposing governor's rule and refusing to respect the public mandate. He also claimed that the political system "established through Form 47" had failed.
Regarding the petroleum levy, the JI chief accused the government of imposing "economic terrorism" on the public, saying people across the country were demanding an end to the burden.
He argued that the levy imposed on petroleum products had no legitimate connection with their prices and amounted to collecting extortion money and "jagga tax".
He alleged that the government was shifting the burden of its corruption and expenditure onto ordinary citizens, making it increasingly difficult for them to make ends meet.
Naeem claimed that the government was providing relief worth as much as Rs27 billion a month in response to Jamaat-e-Islami's protest movement, while collecting Rs150 billion through the petroleum levy.
He said party workers had staged sit-ins simultaneously in 42 cities, adding that the campaign had given people renewed hope.
The JI chief said the long march had been temporarily paused but maintained that party workers remained prepared to resume it.
He also slammed the government's agreements with independent power producers (IPPs), accusing successive administrations of strengthening the companies through unjust agreements. Under the arrangements, he argued, consumers were made to bear the costs of electricity generation and were also required to pay even when electricity was not produced.
Earlier, Jamaat-e-Islami Central Punjab chief Muhammad Javed Qasuri told the rally that the party's movement was directed against the elite, the petroleum levy and an "oppressive system".
Referring to the difficulties faced by farmers, he cited high fertiliser and diesel prices and accused the Punjab government of harming the agricultural sector.
Jamaat-e-Islami women's wing secretary-general Dr Humaira Tariq said the party was struggling to resolve the problems confronting the public.
Pakistan was rich in resources, she said, but the people's living conditions had failed to improve because of the poor performance of those in power.

title: PM vows no more silence on terrorism
description: PM vows no more silence on terrorism
content:
Shehbaz tells cabinet K-P govt failed to protect citizens
The federal cabinet on Sunday recommended that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif advise the president to invoke Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution to impose an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), citing the deteriorating security situation and the provincial government's detachment from the fight against terrorism.
The cabinet meeting, chaired by the prime minister, reviewed the worsening law and order situation and rising terrorist violence in the province. Members were given a comprehensive briefing on the security crisis before recommending the invocation of the constitutional provisions.
Addressing the meeting, Shehbaz criticised the K-P government for failing to tackle rising terrorism, saying the federal government would no longer remain a silent spectator. He expressed particular concern over the situation in Tank and Dera Ismail Khan, where residents have borne the brunt of terrorist attacks, and condemned the provincial leadership's silence and lack of empathy towards victims.
The prime minister said that, despite two days of negotiations between federal coalition leaders from the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and a Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) delegation, K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had rejected the final consensus draft at the eleventh hour.
"Despite reaching a finalised draft agreement, the K-P chief minister backed out at the eleventh hour," he said, alleging that the move reflected a lack of willingness to pursue peace. He added that calls to cancel upcoming protest marches had been met with defiance.
Shehbaz further accused the provincial leadership of undermining efforts to secure political agreement, while praising coalition leaders Rana Sanaullah, Mohsin Naqvi, Amir Muqam, Syed Naveed Qamar and Sherry Rehman, as well as mediator Maulana Fazlur Rehman, for participating in the two-day negotiations.
Criticising the provincial leadership over its "sinister role" and attempts to "invade Islamabad to reenact past foul play", Shehbaz said: "We will not remain silent in the face of such a situation. The law will take its course; we will not allow such acts."
He accused the provincial leadership of prioritising political obstruction over the safety of its citizens and urged cabinet members to take firm decisions to address the escalating security crisis. "They ruled for 13 years and are now pushing Pakistan to destruction," he said.
The prime minister recalled that all four provinces had voluntarily agreed under the 2010 National Finance Commission (NFC) Award to allocate an additional 1% share of financial resources to K-P. He said the allocation had amounted to roughly Rs800 billion over the years and was intended to strengthen the province's police force against terrorism.
Shehbaz said the funds were meant to bolster Counter-Terrorism Departments (CTDs), fortify police stations, improve intelligence capabilities, recruit personnel and procure modern weapons but neither the police nor the CTD had been meaningfully strengthened, while terrorism continued unchecked.
He criticised the provincial leadership for failing to condemn terrorist attacks or express sympathy for families whose children had been orphaned by violence. "Instead of standing up against terrorists, they are not only silent, but the situation is getting worse every day," he said, adding that the provincial government's alleged detachment from the counter-terrorism campaign amounted to aiding the menace.
Accusing the provincial leadership of plotting to march on Islamabad, the prime minister warned against a repeat of past disorder, disruption and economic damage. He said Pakistan's hard-won macroeconomic stability, reflected in State Bank reserves, controlled inflation and targeted fuel subsidies benefiting more than 50 million citizens, would not be sacrificed to political enmity.
The prime minister also highlighted Pakistan's diplomatic efforts to ease tensions in the Gulf and secure ceasefires, saying Islamabad was working closely with Saudi Arabia and Qatar while engaging with Iran.
He acknowledged the roles of Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in these efforts. Shehbaz condemned regional escalations and threats to key waterways, including the Bab-al-Mandab Strait, as well as drone attacks targeting holy sites.
Later, the advice to promulgate emergency in K-P was sent to the president, which was approved by Zardari, according to the President Secretariat Media Wing. "The President approved and signed the summary upon the Prime Minister's advice under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution of Pakistan," it said.

title: Centre takes K P s reins
description: Centre takes K P s reins
content:
Governor takes helm after president proclaims emergency under Articles 232(1) and 234(1) CM, ministers cease to hol
The federal government took control of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's (K-P) affairs on Sunday after imposing an emergency and governor's rule in the province, deploying the army to assist the civil administration, forming an 11-member advisory council and establishing a special administrative structure for 12 districts.
Meanwhile, roadblocks sealed key areas of Peshawar, public transport was suspended, educational institutions were ordered closed and matriculation examinations postponed, while police arrested dozens of PTI workers in Swabi amid unconfirmed claims that former chief minister Sohail Afridi and provincial party president Junaid Akbar had also been detained.
President Asif Ali Zardari imposed the emergency under Article 232 of the Constitution, citing escalating terrorist attacks, threats to citizens' lives and property, and attacks on government installations, infrastructure and law-enforcement personnel.
The proclamation said the provincial government had failed to take adequate measures against terrorism and referred to the governor's report highlighting a breakdown in the constitutional system.
Issued under Articles 232(1) and 234(1), the proclamation declared that the provincial government could not function in accordance with the Constitution under the prevailing circumstances. It empowered the federal government to direct the governor to assume some or all provincial government functions, while the powers of the provincial assembly would be exercised by Parliament or under its authority.
The chief minister, provincial ministers, advisers, special assistants and advocate general ceased to hold office with immediate effect. The federal government subsequently authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets under Article 245 to protect citizens, property and government installations for the duration of the emergency proclamation.
Under the deployment order, Governor Faisal Karim Kundi will determine the number of troops and resources required. The federal government also constituted an 11-member advisory council to assist the governor in administering the province.
Its members are Tariq Mahmood Pasha, Dr Amir Abdullah, Lieutenant General (retd) Nigar Johar, Samar Bilour, Dr Sarfaraz Ali, Aamir Javed, Dr M Irshad, Kifayatullah, Tayyab Qureshi, Usman Saifullah Khan and Asif Rafiq. Sanaullah Advocate was appointed the provincial advocate general.
The council held its first meeting at the Governor House under Governor Kundi's chairmanship. Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed briefed members on the law and order situation, while the governor acknowledged the challenges facing the administration and called for responsible and timely decisions.
Kundi said corruption would not be tolerated and stressed that the administration would focus on restoring peace, security, stability and development. He said strengthening the police and Counter-Terrorism Department would be a priority, alongside dismantling the wider support systems sustaining terrorism, including facilitation, financing, recruitment, extremist networks, illegal weapons, drugs and unlawful movement.
The governor also called for effective implementation of the National Action Plan (NAP) and other counterterrorism measures. He said the province had paid a heavy price for terrorism, with police personnel, soldiers, Levies personnel, government employees, religious scholars, teachers, traders and ordinary citizens among those killed.
Later, a special security meeting chaired by Kundi reviewed terrorist threats and the overall security situation. The chief secretary, police chief, members of the advisory council, officials dealing with tribal and home affairs, senior police and CTD officers, and intelligence representatives attended. Participants were briefed that conditions across the province remained peaceful and normal following the emergency's imposition.
The meeting pledged to strengthen law enforcement agencies and improve their operational capacity, while the governor said he and his council would remain available to support the police and security forces.
In another administrative move, the federal government ordered the immediate establishment of an Area Development Secretariat (ADS) to oversee law and order, public safety, governance and development in 12 designated districts: Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Lakki Marwat, Bannu, Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, North Waziristan, South Waziristan Upper and South Waziristan.
The ADS will operate under an Area Representative and Development Council headed by the additional chief secretary, who will also serve as administrator for the designated districts. The administrator will exercise powers over administration, security, law enforcement and development, issue directions to civil administration, police and military officials, supervise departments and order the allocation or transfer of funds.
Provincial officers and personnel in the designated districts will fall under the secretariat's administrative and operational control. The new arrangement is intended to coordinate federal departments, the armed forces and provincial institutions in implementing measures concerning security, economic stability, relief and the provision of basic services.
The federal government also appointed Dr Muhammad Fakhr Alam Irfan as K-P chief secretary with immediate effect. The grade-22 Pakistan Administrative Service officer, who belongs to Mardan, previously served as secretary of the Power Division. The services of grade-20 officer Muhammad Yahya Akhunzada were also placed at the disposal of the provincial government.
Security restrictions meanwhile brought much of Peshawar's Cantonment and adjoining areas to a standstill. Containers blocked major roads leading to the Provincial Assembly, Governor House, Khyber Road and other government installations, while markets in Saddar and surrounding commercial areas remained closed or partially open. TransPeshawar suspended Bus Rapid Transit services, and authorities reported the closure of educational institutions in Peshawar district on Monday.
All educational boards across K-P also postponed matriculation examinations scheduled for October 12 until further notice. The examinations had initially been scheduled to begin on October 7 before being deferred to October 12 amid the PTI's long march.
Police began detaining PTI workers in Swabi after the emergency was imposed, with police sources putting the number arrested at 59. PTI claimed that Afridi and Junaid Akbar had also been arrested, but the administration had not confirmed their detention.
The emergency followed an increasingly strained relationship between the federal government and the PTI-led provincial administration, particularly over counterterrorism policy and engagement with the Afghan Taliban. The two sides' differences had contributed to the breakdown of talks on October 3, while PTI maintained that it had been excluded from security decisions affecting the province.

title: Fuel costs keep squeezing household budgets
description: Fuel costs keep squeezing household budgets
content:
Repeated price revisions and rising transport costs strain consumers
Pakistan's fuel prices have swung sharply in 2026, pushing up costs for consumers. By October 10, petrol had surged by Rs145.13 to Rs398.30 per litre, while diesel rose by Rs139.16 to Rs396.24.
Since daily pricing began on July 21, petrol prices have been raised 35 times and cut 22 times, while diesel has seen 34 increases and 23 reductionsleaving consumers grappling with persistent price volatility.
According to available price records, petroleum prices reached a peak on April 3, 2026, when petrol climbed to Rs458.41 per litre and high-speed diesel to Rs520.35. Prices subsequently moved up and down in response to changing market conditions.
Fluctuations in international oil prices, tensions in the Middle East, import costs and changes in the value of the rupee are among the factors influencing domestic petroleum prices.
Government revenue from petroleum levies and other taxes has also remained a significant component of the fuel price structure. Available official figures show that the government collected approximately Rs1.205 trillion in petroleum levy revenue between July 2025 and March 2026. Collections rose to around Rs1.342 trillion between July 2025 and April 2026.
These figures cover different periods within the fiscal year and should not be interpreted as total collections for calendar year 2026.
For the fiscal year 2026-27, the government has set a petroleum levy collection target of approximately Rs1.676 trillion. This is a budget target, not the amount collected so far during the current fiscal year.
The final retail price of petroleum products includes import costs, levies, customs duties, associated expenses and other applicable components. Consequently, a decline in international oil prices does not necessarily translate into equivalent relief for domestic consumers.
Pakistan relies on imports of crude oil and refined petroleum products to meet its energy needs. Available figures for the first two months of fiscal year 2026-27 show that approximately 2.001 million tonnes of crude oil were imported in July and August. The country's overall oil import bill during the period also ran into billions of dollars.
Crude oil imports and imports of finished petrol are separate categories. Therefore, the volume of crude oil imported cannot be treated as the quantity of petrol imported.
Rising petrol and diesel prices directly affect household expenditure. Motorcyclists, private vehicle owners, rickshaw drivers and employees who commute daily have to spend more on fuel. Higher diesel prices can also increase operating costs for buses, trucks, agricultural machinery and freight transport, potentially pushing up the prices of food, construction materials and other essential goods.
According to the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, annual inflation stood at 10.26 per cent in September 2026, while consumer prices rose 1.27 per cent from August. Transport costs increased by 5.75 per cent month-on-month, and urban motor fuel prices surged 10.76 per cent. Electricity price increases added further pressure on household budgets.
Food prices showed mixed trends, with onion prices rising significantly while tomatoes, chicken and eggs became cheaper. However, higher fuel, transport and electricity costs continued to erode consumers' purchasing power.
Economists believe that the government needs to ensure greater transparency in petroleum pricing, review the tax structure, improve public transport and promote alternative energy sources. While temporary fuel price cuts could offer some relief, lasting reductions in household expenses would require lower dependence on imported energy and reduced transport costs.
Despite repeated price revisions since July 21, petrol remained Rs145.13 per litre more expensive than at the start of the year, while diesel had risen by Rs139.16. The continued volatility highlights the financial strain on households and the need for measures to reduce the impact of fuel costs on everyday life.
