title: When poetry lived in landhi
description: Beyond the posh drawing rooms and grand halls  Karachi   s poetry once thrived in its working class neighborhood
content:
Beyond the posh drawing rooms and grand halls, Karachi’s poetry once thrived in its working-class neighborhood
Although much has been written about the decline of the mushaira in Karachi, not much attention has been paid to the working-class neighbourhoods that served as literary powerhouses of the metropolis—and to the lesser-known literary organisations that kept poetry alive there until the very end.
When we lament Karachi's rapid literary or perhaps intellectual decline, especially from the late 1980s onwards, we often speak in generalities and fall prey to familiar phrases such as "the mushaira lost its audience," "the poets grew old," "the city changed," and the like. However, this broad narrative obscures a more textured story that played out in the city's relatively lower-income neighbourhoods, far from the affluent drawing rooms of Gulshan-e-Iqbal, Defence, and Clifton.
Headquartered on the Eastern edge of the city, in Landhi's C-1 area, a densely populated, working-class pocket, Basm-e-Hameed was one of those rare literary organisations that emerged in the 1960s. It did the quiet, unglamorous work of sustaining mushaira culture in a part of the city otherwise known for its acute poverty and socioeconomic deprivation.
Khalid Alig, Himayat Ali Shair, Hassan Hameedi, Zahida Hina, Mubarak Suroor, and other renowned poets at a mushaira
The organisation was named after Hameed Azeemabadi, a well-known Urdu poet, literary figure, and—perhaps unexpectedly—a prominent footballer from Azeemabad, present-day Patna, the capital of Bihar, India. A shagird (student) of Shaad Azeemabadi, a leading pre-Partition Urdu poet from Bihar, Hameed authored several acclaimed poetry collections,including Sarosh-e-Maikada, Meezane-e-Sukhan, Rasikh, and Maikhana-e-Ilham, also known as Deewan-e-Shaad — the last being a poetic compilation of Shaad Azeemabadi's works.
Although Hameed Azeemabadi never migrated to Pakistan himself, his elder sons—Hasan Hameedi, Aziz Hameedi, and Sagheer Hameedi—co-founded Bazm-e-Hameed in the early 1960s. The organisation was dedicated to promoting lesser-known poets and writers from Landhi and Korangi areas, primarily through the mushaira platform — a longstanding tradition of Urdu literary culture in the Indian subcontinent.
Among the co-founders, Hasan Hameedi was the best-known literary figure. A resident of Purana (Old) Sukkur, where he lived in the historic Jinnat Building, near Jinnat Chowk, Hasan was also a prominent political activist with pronounced leftist leanings. He authored several poetry collections, including Masnawi Jurm-e-Aagahi and Sahar Aawaz Deti Hai. Aziz Hameedi and Sagheer Hameedi were both prominent educationists and Urdu poets. The tarhi mushaira tradition
What set this literary organisation apart was its long-standing tradition of hosting the tarhi mushaira, in which poets were required to recite a new ghazal based on a misra-e-tarah—a specific prescribed line. This format demanded both technical mastery and creative improvisation, and it attracted some of the era's finest poets.
Among those who regularly featured in these mushairas were Johar Saeedi, Khalid Alig, Hasan Musanna Nadwi, Saleem Kausar, Kaif Banarasi, Rasa Chughtai, Pirzada Ashique Keranvi, Zahida Hina, Zafar Zaidi, Naqqash Kazmi, Shahid Alvi, Akhtar Saeedi, Rasheed Asar, Aleem Mahshar, Zaigham Hameedi, Ziaul-Hasan Zia, Rashid Hasan Khan, Professor Shadab Ehsani, Dr Aziza Anjum, Mubarak Hussain Saroor, Naeema Sahar, and Syed Muhammad Sohail, among many others.
Although many literary organisations were active in Karachi during the 1960s and 1970s with a similar mission, this particular one stood apart because of its location and the limited resources at its disposal. Most of the poets from the area came from humble backgrounds and worked menial jobs to earn a living. I have witnessed many such poets arriving on foot in the dead of night from far-flung parts of the city simply to recite their ghazals and poems, without the hope of or receiving any honorarium whatsoever.
Mostly held at the community centre adjacent to the Landhi Fire Brigade Station, these literary gatherings began late at night and continued until dawn. For the organisers, working with limited resources, it was a herculean task to accommodate the large number of attendees, and provide them with a decent meal or refreshments. These usually consisted of little more than chai (tea), biscuits, and boiled eggs.
Residents living near the mushaira venue also helped provide accommodation for those arriving from distant parts of the city. This included collecting large numbers of rugs, sheets, pillows, bolsters, and blankets from neighbouring households to accommodate the guests for the night. It was a communal effort in the truest sense — poetry sustained not by institutions or grants, but by neighbours sharing what little they had.
Most importantly, despite the conservative social milieu, women's participation was equally encouraged at these events, with special arrangements made for those observing purdah. In this, the organisation was ahead of its time, creating a space where literary merit mattered more than social convention.
Naeema Sahar, 81, is one of the living poets who regularly attended the mushairas hosted by Bazm-e-Hameed. Recalling those gatherings, she says: “The mushairas were always held on the last Thursday night of every month, an occasion we eagerly awaited and looked forward to attending. What made these gatherings particularly special was that they were organised by four brothers in memory of their late father, Hameed Azeemabadi. With the Hameedi brothers passing away one by one, exclusive mushairas were held in memory of each brother. Following the death of the last scion, Sagheer Hameedi, the organisation itself became a part of history, bringing this remarkable literary tradition to an unfortunate end. There is no doubt that the people behind it, despite limited resources at their disposal, gave generously of their time and energy to keep the literary flame alive.”
Bazm-e-Hameed, like many other literary and cultural organisations in Karachi, did its best to keep the literary flame burning in an area otherwise known for its socioeconomic deprivation and widespread poverty. However, the onset of the 1990s, marked by deteriorating law and order and the rise of armed political groups that held the entire city to ransom for the next three decades, dealt a decisive blow to it, eventually extinguishing its presence from Karachi's literary scene.
The organisation that had once drawn poets on foot from across the city could no longer guarantee their safety. The mushairas that had lasted until dawn fell silent. And with them, a particular kind of Karachi—plural, curious, and deeply literary—faded a little further into memory.
"More than a literary gathering, it was an institution in its own right that, under the patronage of senior poets, nurtured young talent and taught aspiring poets the art and craft of Urdu poetry,” says Dr Pirzada Sharf-e-Alam, Urdu scholar and author of Urdu Ishtihariyat Ki Tareekh and Pichka Hua Aadmi. “Over time, however, the Bazm evolved into a family tradition and a means of nurturing and cultivating a deep love for literature across generations.”
The bittersweet story of the rise and decline of Bazm-e-Hameed is a necessary reminder that literary culture does not have to be confined to the elite enclaves of Karachi, or to a certain socio-economic class. It flourished in community centres and cramped cottages in suburban areas where lower-income classes resided. Literary culture here was nurtured by those who inherited it from their Indian ancestors and sustained by poor creators who worked menial jobs by day, composed ghazals in the evenings, and recited them in the dead of night.
As a new crop of Karachi's literati continues to find its footing amid the host of challenges facing the city, it is worth remembering that the city's cultural heritage is not confined to its so-called literary festivals and intellectual funfairs in the city's posh areas. Its true essence also resides in the cherished memories of literary organisations such as Bazm-e-Hameed, and in the ghazals that were recited until dawn, when the chai ran out, and the blankets were returned to their owners.
Talking about how the organisation represents a rich literary tradition and a remarkable yet largely unrecognised chapter in the literary scene of yore, another Urdu poet, Saiyad Naiyarul Hasan, shared that, “Every year, it brought together poets, both renowned and obscure, and provided them with an opportunity to meet, exchange ideas, and benefit from one another's poetic creations. Although owing to the unfortunate vicissitudes of time, many of these poets remained largely unknown throughout their literary careers, their poetry was nevertheless distinguished by a unique taste and flavour. It was a source of immense pleasure, filled with words that spoke of possibilities and hope—qualities that may not even be found in the poetry of many celebrated poets."
However, the late Urdu poet Pirzada Ashique Keranvi once remarked, “Thanks to those tarhi mushairas of the bazm, countless poets went on to become published poets with diwans of their own.”
Perhaps that is what makes this a story worth remembering. Its legacy was not built on grand halls or generous grants, but on the quiet persistence of people who believed that poetry mattered. In a city whose literary history is often told through its celebrated names and better-known institutions, Bazm-e-Hameed offers another story — of ordinary people, and of ghazals that continued until dawn.
Perhaps there is something to be learned from those long nights too. In an age of screens and solitary scrolling, there is still value in putting the phone away, sitting together and listening — to poetry, to stories, and to one another.

title: Emergency  governor s rule imposed in K P after president signs summary on PM Shehbaz s advice
description: Cabinet is expected to consider imposing an emergency and governor s rule in K P
author_name: Waqas Ahmad, Khalid Mahmood, AAMIR ILAYS RANA
content:
Govt appoints Muhammad Fakhr as chief secretary, Pakistan Army deployed in province to assist the civil administration
The federal government on Sunday imposed emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) after President Asif Ali Zardari signed the summary on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, following the federal cabinet’s approval of the recommendation.
"The president signed the summary following the federal cabinet’s decision, the prime minister’s advice, reports from relevant institutions on the law and order situation, and the failure of negotiations with government delegations," said a statement issued by the President's office.
It further stated that the president signed the advice, approving it under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution of Pakistan.
صدرِ مملکت آصف علی زرداری نے خیبر پختونخوا میں کی سلامتی کی صورتحال پر وزیراعظم کی ایڈوائس پر دستخط کر دیے ہیں۔ آئینِ پاکستان کے آرٹیکلز 232 اور 234 کے تحت صدرِ مملکت نے وزیراعظم کی ایڈوائس منظور کرتے ہوئے دستخط کیے۔ وفاقی کابینہ کے فیصلے، وزیراعظم کی ایڈوائس، متعلقہ اداروں کی…
According to a government gazette notification, President Zardari imposed an emergency in K-P under Articles 232(1) and 234(1) of the Constitution, with the presidential proclamation taking immediate effect,
The proclamation cites an extraordinary increase in terrorist incidents and violent activities in the province as the reason for the emergency, stating that attacks pose serious threats to the lives and property of the public.
According to the proclamation, attacks by terrorists on infrastructure, government installations, and law enforcement agencies have increased. It also claimed that the provincial government has failed to address the threats posed by terrorism and lawlessness effectively.
The proclamation further states that a report by the K-P governor identified a failure of the constitutional system in the province, adding that the situation had moved beyond the control of the provincial government.
It describes the situation as a threat not only to K-P but also to Pakistan’s overall security.
Under the measures outlined in the proclamation, the federal government may direct the K-P governor to assume all or some of the provincial government's powers.
The governor would exercise the powers and perform the duties assigned by the federal government, according to the notification.
The proclamation also provides for the powers of the K-P Assembly to be exercised by Parliament or a body authorised by it.
Under the notification, the K-P chief minister, provincial ministers, advisers, special assistants and advocate general would immediately cease to hold their offices.
The proclamation states that the emergency has taken effect immediately.
The announcement came shortly after the federal cabinet recommended imposing emergency rule in K-P amid the prevailing security situation.
The cabinet, which met under the chairmanship of PM Shehbaz, reviewed the worsening law and order situation in the province and was briefed on the rising threat of terrorism.
In view of the gravity of the situation, the cabinet recommended that the prime minister advise President Zardari to invoke his constitutional powers under Articles 232 and 234 to impose emergency rule in the province.
The advice was then forwarded to the President’s House.
وزیرِ اعظم محمد شہباز شریف کی زیرِ صدارت وفاقی کابینہ کا اجلاس آج اسلام آباد میں منعقد ہوا. وفاقی کابینہ کو خیبر پختونخوا میں امن و امان کی صورتحال اور دھشتگردی کی بگڑتی ہوئی صورتحال پر بریفنگ دی گئی. کابینہ نے خیبر پختونخوا میں امن و امان کی بگڑتی ہوئی صورتحال اور دھشتگردی… pic.twitter.com/EQBySKCItC
Following the imposition of an emergency in the province, the federal government has issued a formal order authorising the deployment of army troops to assist the civil administration.
According to the order, the deployment has been approved under Article 245 of the Constitution for the period covered by the proclamation issued on Oct 11, 2026, under Articles 232 and 234.
The deployment aims to ensure the protection of citizens’ lives and property, as well as government installations, the order said, adding that the army would assist the civil administration in maintaining law and order and protecting citizens in the province.
The K-P governor, in consultation with the General Headquarters’ Directorate of Military Operations, will determine the number of troops and resources to be deployed, according to the order.
The deployment order will be published in the next issue of the Gazette of Pakistan, Part II.
Dr Fakhr Alam Irfan appointed K-P chief secretary
The federal government notified the appointment of Muhammad Yahya Akhunzada to the K-P government, according to an official notification.
A Grade-20 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), Akhunzada was previously serving as an additional secretary at the Prime Minister’s Office.
He has also served as additional political agent for South and North Waziristan, secretary of health, information and education in K-P, and commissioner of Dera Ismail Khan. Akhunzada hails from Charsadda district of K-P.
According to the notification, his services have been placed at the disposal of the K-P government under Section 10 of the Civil Servants Act, 1973. The appointment will remain effective until further orders.
Govt appoints Yahya Akhunzada to K-P administration
The federal government also notified the appointment of Muhammad Yahya Akhunzada to the K-P government, according to an official notification.
A Grade-20 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), Akhunzada was previously serving as an additional secretary at the Prime Minister’s Office.
He has also served as additional political agent for South and North Waziristan, secretary of health, information and education in K-P, and commissioner of Dera Ismail Khan. Akhunzada hails from Charsadda district of K-P.
According to the notification, his services have been placed at the disposal of the K-P government under Section 10 of the Civil Servants Act, 1973. The appointment will remain effective until further orders.
Federal govt appoints new K-P chief secretary
The federal government on Sunday appointed Dr Muhammad Fakhr Alam Irfan as the new chief secretary of K-P.
According to the notification issued today, Irfan, a Grade-22 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), was previously serving as secretary of the Power Division under the Ministry of Energy.
His appointment as K-P chief secretary takes immediate effect and will remain in place until further orders, the notification stated.
The developments followed a meeting between President Zardari and PM Shehbaz at Aiwan-e-Sadr on Saturday, during which they reviewed the country's overall political and security situation, with particular attention to K-P, where the PTI launched its long march on October 4.
According to sources, the president and prime minister reached an understanding on the possibility of imposing governor's rule or an emergency in the province. However, the final decision rests with the federal cabinet, and no formal announcement had been made at the time of reporting.
The Presidency's media wing said the meeting discussed the overall political and security situation and that separate sessions of the National Assembly and Senate had been agreed upon for Oct 13.

title: Iran says US response to its proposal to reopen Hormuz was  insufficient
description: Iranian FM Araghchi said US Israeli attacks on oil facilities and refineries have raised serious environmental risks
content:
Iranian FM Araghchi said US-Israeli attacks on oil facilities and refineries have raised serious environmental risks
The United States' response to Iran's seven conditions in a proposal to reopen the strategic Strait of ​Hormuz was "insufficient", Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, was quoted by ‌state media on Sunday as saying.
Iran presented a proposal during the UN General Assembly under which the Strait of Hormuz waterway could be reopened and ​normal maritime passage restored within seven days if the conditions ​were met, to which the US later replied via ⁠Qatari intermediaries.
Washington needs to clarify the issues that remain unclear to ​Tehran, Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, said, adding "we ​presented seven conditions to the Americans and clearly stated that the Strait of Hormuz would not be opened to them, and no negotiations would take place, ​until these conditions are met."
The White House did not immediately ​respond to a Reuters request for comment.
Rezaei said Iran is "no longer in the ‌process ⁠of responding to the Americans".
"In their response, they have accepted some of our conditions, while others remain unclear," he added.
Tehran said late in September that it had received a US response to its latest ​proposal to resurrect the ​collapsed ceasefire ⁠in the Gulf, days after US President Donald Trump said he had rejected it.
Qatar and other mediators ​have transmitted messages between Washington and Tehran in ​an effort ⁠to end the conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the conduit for a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural ⁠gas before ​the war that began at the ​end of February with US and Israeli attacks on Iran.
Araghchi warns of environmental risks from US-Israeli attacks on oil facilities
Earlier, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that US-Israeli attacks on Iran's oil facilities and refineries have raised serious environmental risks.
عراقچی: حملات اخیر آمریکا و اسرائیل به تأسیسات نفتی، پالایشگاهی انرژی ایران، خطرات جدی زیست‌محیطی ایجاد کرده -وقتی حمله‌ای موجب آلودگی خاک، تخریب منابع آب و ایجاد مواد خطرناک می‌شود، آثار آن می‌تواند بسیار فراتر از زمان و مکان حمله، ادامه پیدا کند https://t.co/mwiGRXTUej pic.twitter.com/pxPRuG7dSt
"When an attack causes soil contamination, destruction of water resources, and the creation of hazardous materials, its effects can persist far beyond the time and place of the attack," he said, according to Iranian news agency ISNA .
"The environment can no longer be considered a silent victim of war. War and conflict not only target people's lives... but also water, soil, air, forests, agricultural lands, energy resources, natural habitats, and biodiversity."
He said that "the destruction of water and soil resources, air pollution, the destruction of vegetation and ecosystems, and the emission of pollutants, wastes, and hazardous materials are among the consequences that can continue for years and even decades after the end of the conflict.
"In recent years, we have witnessed in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran how military attacks, in addition to human casualties and the destruction of vital infrastructure, have left deep and sometimes lasting effects on the environment."
Araghchi added that "No government, institution, or actor should consider itself beyond international responsibilities."
Iran nuclear technology "safe from external disruption: Chief of Iran Atomic Energy Organisation
Iran’s nuclear technology is safe from external disruption and cannot be halted by threats, pressure, or attacks, Mohammad Eslami chief of the Atomic Energy Organisation of Iran (AEOI), said, according to Al Jazeera .
Iran’s nuclear technology is safe from external disruption and cannot be halted by threats, pressure, or attacks, says Mohammad Eslami, chief of the Atomic Energy Organisation of Iran (AEOI). 🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/nBpyoddbxV pic.twitter.com/6eKP6XPIYi
"We will secure our interests either through diplomacy or through combat," he said, according to ISNA .

"The nuclear industry is rooted in Iran and cannot be destroyed by a blow."
National unity can foil enemies’ attempts to weaken Iran: Pezeshkian
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stressed on Sunday that national unity and solidarity were essential to overcoming Iran's current challenges, saying no power could bring Iran to a standstill if its people stand together and reject exclusionary approaches, according to IRNA.
. @drpezeshkian says national unity can foil enemies’ attempts to weaken Iran https://t.co/sPqizvF0AE pic.twitter.com/0EVjMBbzLh
He warned that internal exclusion and self-imposed restrictions could undermine national strength, saying the country can withstand external pressure if it avoids marginalising its own people.
If Iranians did not undermine themselves through self-imposed restrictions or selective exclusion, the enemy cannot defeat them or bring them to their knees, he said, calling for opportunities that enable young people to develop their potential.
US military says it disabled vessel attempting to violate blockade
US Central Command (CENTCOM) stated on X on Sunday that the military disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman on Saturday, after the ship’s crew "ignored repeated warnings" and "attempted to run the ongoing naval blockade against Iran."
U.S. Forces Disable Cargo Vessel Attempting to Violate Blockade TAMPA, Fla. — U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) forces disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman, Oct. 10, after the ship’s crew ignored repeated warnings and attempted to run the ongoing naval blockade… pic.twitter.com/qBKcU6gWqR
A fighter jet disabled the propulsion system of the Panama-flagged M/V Ocean Molica (also called the "Arika Sun”). According to CENTCOM, the vessel was "attempting to transit regional waters after having previously departed an Iranian port."
CENTCOM resumed the blockade against all ships entering or departing Iranian ports on July 14.

According to CENTCOM tallies, it has disabled four commercial vessels and turned around 135 ships so far. CENTCOM further stated that "US forces destroyed 10 tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' multibillion-dollar shadow network over the same period."
'US should be held accountable' over Minab school attack: Gharibabadi
Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi said in an interview with Press TV that Iran would pursue legal cases in domestic and foreign courts over the US-Israeli aggression against Minab's elementary school.
"US should be held accountable" In an exclusive interview with Press TV's @iammoeen14 , Iran's Deputy FM @Gharibabadi says Iran would pursue legal cases in domestic and foreign courts over the US-Israeli aggression against Minab's elementary school. pic.twitter.com/o2aGhpDXI2
"We must hold the aggressors accountable under international law. Those responsible for the Minab atrocity must answer for their actions before international bodies," he said, according to Press TV .
He also criticised international silence regarding aggression against Iran, saying that "Two wars took place, yet the international system did nothing...the US and Israeli regime violated international law and humanitarian law during the 12-day and 40-day wars."
Impossible for Hormuz to reopen without meeting Iran's conditions: Iran National Security Commission spokesperson
Spokesperson of the National Security and Foreign Policy Committee of the parliament said on Sunday that "it is impossible to open the Strait of Hormuz until the conditions announced by Iran are met," according to ISNA .

He also said that "the issue of revising Iran's nuclear doctrine is getting stronger day by day, both among the people and experts and among the authorities."
Iran not to return to previous diplomatic norms, but to never leave diplomacy: Secretary Rezaei
Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Major General Rezaei said that Iran will not leave diplomacy, but would also not return to previous diplomatic norms, according to Press TV.
🔴 Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Maj. Gen. Rezaei to Press TV: 🔺 US military was expelled from Iraq after it suffered defeat against Iran 🔺 Many powers, greater than US, tried to conquer Iran, but ended up in dustbin of history pic.twitter.com/SlTUl4zpU9
He brought up how the US military was "expelled from Iraq after it suffered defeat against Iran," and said that "Over 30million Iranians" have registered to "take up arms to fight US aggression."
Trump says Iran may step up actions before midterm elections, muses about renaming Strait of Hormuz
President Donald Trump said Saturday that Iran may step up its actions ahead of the US’ Nov. 3 midterm elections – now just weeks away – arguing that Tehran believes doing so would hurt the US.
He also claimed that Washington could end the confrontation quickly.
“They'll probably do a little bit extra before the election, thinking it's going to hurt us,” Trump said in remarks in the Southern state of Tennessee, a longtime stronghold of the president’s Republican Party, where Trump travelled to hold a campaign rally.
“But we could end it really quick,” he added, claiming he had shown restraint toward Iran despite what he called the destruction of the Iranian navy.
“They don't know how nice I've been to them,” he said, claiming that 159 Iranian ships have been sunk since late February, the start of the ongoing war.
Read more: IRGC says it struck LPG tanker attempting to cross Strait of Hormuz
Trump also mused about the flashpoint Strait of Hormuz: “We're thinking about renaming it to the Trump Strait.”
Trump previously said the war with Iran might end just after the November 3 midterm congressional elections, in which the ongoing war has emerged as a key issue.
The president is not running in the midterms, but he is campaigning for fellow Republicans, working to help them keep control of one or both houses of Congress.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28, prompting Tehran to respond with missile and drone attacks in the region and effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz.
The war has continued for more than seven months, driving up global energy prices as commercial oil traffic through the strategic waterway has effectively halted.
The US and Iran signed a framework agreement in June after Pakistan and Qatar mediated to halt hostilities and pave the way for negotiations.
Implementation of the deal has since stalled amid disagreements, including on security and navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.
Tanker catches fire after being struck by unknown projectile in Strait of Hormuz: Maritime agency
A tanker caught fire after being struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said Sunday.
The master of the outbound tanker reported that the vessel was struck on its port side by an unknown projectile, causing a fire onboard, said the UKMTO.
UKMTO WARNING 162-26 Click here to view the full product.⤵️ https://t.co/11gMTgb5bT #MaritimeSecurity #MarSec pic.twitter.com/EAS2qaRARq
The crew was reported safe, while the extent of the damage and any environmental effects remain unknown.
Authorities are investigating, and vessels were advised to transit the area with caution.
The incident came hours after Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said late on Saturday that an oil supertanker struck a naval mine and exploded while attempting to leave the Strait of Hormuz through an unauthorised southern route.
The IRGC said the vessel, which it described as capable of carrying around 2 million barrels of oil, had switched off its navigation systems before trying to cross the vital shipping route for global energy and commodity supplies.
It said the tanker struck a mine while trying to exit through the alternative route, triggering an explosion visible from coastal areas.

title: PSBA adopts WWF Green Office Programme to promote sustainable practices | The Express Tribune
description: The initiative aims to incorporate sustainability into the authority’s daily operations
content:
The initiative aims to incorporate sustainability into the authority’s daily operations
The Punjab Sahulat Bazaars Authority (PSBA) is implementing the World Wide Fund for Nature-Pakistan’s (WWF-Pakistan) Green Office Programme to reduce resource consumption and promote environmentally sustainable practices at its headquarters.
Under a memorandum of understanding with WWF-Pakistan, the authority is working towards Green Office certification, which involves measures to conserve energy and water, reduce paper consumption, segregate and recycle waste, and promote responsible purchasing.
The initiative aims to incorporate sustainability into the authority’s daily operations, extending its resource-efficiency efforts beyond its bazaars to its administrative offices.
PSBA Director General Naveed Rafaqat Ahmad has focused on resource efficiency as both an environmental and financial priority, according to the authority’s initiative brief. Under his leadership, solar-powered bazaars reduced electricity bills by around 90 per cent at pilot sites, the brief said.
The authority has aligned the initiative with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif’s vision of a greener province.
The Green Office certification process is intended to assess workplace practices against environmental standards, encouraging more efficient resource use and responsible waste management.
PSBA’s initiative seeks to make sustainability part of routine public-sector operations by translating environmental commitments into measurable changes in how government offices function.

title: Meghan Markle faces criticism over As Ever partnership with Malala Yousafzai
description: Meghan Markle faces criticism over As Ever campaign with Malala Yousafzai  meant to support girls    education
content:
Meghan Markle faces criticism over As Ever campaign with Malala Yousafzai, meant to support girls’ education
Meghan Markle has faced criticism on social media after announcing a partnership between her lifestyle brand, As Ever, and Malala Yousafzai’s charity, the Malala Fund, with some users questioning whether the campaign combines charitable work with product promotion.
The Duchess of Sussex shared a collaborative Instagram post with the Pakistani education activist to mark International Day of the Girl.
The announcement stated that 100% of net proceeds from selected As Ever jams and teas would support the Malala Fund through a partnership involving Archewell Philanthropies.
The post also encouraged followers to shop through the brand’s website, prompting criticism from some users on X.
One commenter wrote: “Meghan Markle uses Nobel Peace Prize winner Malala Yousafzai to promote her As Ever tea and spread, and Malala is totally cool with it?!?!?!”
Another user questioned the photographs accompanying the announcement, claiming: “There you have it. The staged pap shots were to promote #asever”.
However, the source material provides no evidence that the photographs were staged. The announcement was published as a collaborative post featuring both women, and the campaign outlines a charitable purpose.
The Instagram caption included the statement, “When we support the girls of today, we empower the women of tomorrow. Access to education is the key to unlocking this,” highlighting the initiative’s focus on girls’ access to education.
The announcement specifies that 100% of net proceeds will support the charity, rather than promising that all revenue from sales will be donated. It does not disclose an expected fundraising total.

title: Presley Gerber   s ex Isabella Jones breaks silence three weeks after his death
description: Isabella Jones pays tribute to Presley Gerber three weeks after his death at 27  sharing photos and heartfelt word
content:
Isabella Jones pays tribute to Presley Gerber three weeks after his death at 27, sharing photos and heartfelt word
Isabella Jones has paid tribute to Presley Gerber three weeks after the 27-year-old’s death, sharing a series of photographs of her former boyfriend on Instagram.
“My sweet Presley,” Jones wrote in the caption. “I will miss you for the rest of my life.”
Gerber, the son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber, died late last month following an apparent overdose and cardiac arrest, according to reports. He had reportedly been struggling with addiction and mental health issues.
Following his death, a spokesperson for Crawford and Rande Gerber asked for privacy as the family grieved.
“The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time,” the spokesperson said in a statement.
Jones and Gerber reportedly began dating in 2024. Her Instagram tribute comes as those who knew him continue to remember him and reflect on their relationships with him.
Lexi Wood, who dated Gerber in 2022 and later remained connected to him through their friendship, also shared a tribute following his death.
“It’s hard to put into words what it means to lose someone who was such a meaningful part of my life for so many years,” Wood wrote.
She added that friendship had remained central to their relationship through its different stages. Wood also described Gerber as kind, open, loving and courageous, recalling his romantic and thoughtful nature.
Jones and Wood’s tributes offer personal reflections on Gerber’s life and the connections he maintained with people close to him. His death has also brought renewed attention to the family of Crawford and Rande Gerber as they navigate their loss.

title: The Odyssey    overtakes    Avatar  The Way of Water    as Korea   s highest grossing international film
description: As of Oct 11 the epic film had generated KRW 139 2bn   101 5m  surpassing Cameron s  Avatar  KRW 138bn
content:
As of Oct 11 the epic film had generated KRW 139.2bn ($101.5m) surpassing Cameron's 'Avatar' KRW 138bn
Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey has overtaken Avatar: The Way of Water to become South Korea’s highest-grossing international film of all time, earning approximately $101.5 million at the country’s box office.
As of October 11, 2026, the epic film had generated KRW 139.2 billion ($101.5 million) in South Korea, surpassing the KRW 138 billion earned by James Cameron’s Avatar: The Way of Water . The achievement makes The Odyssey the highest-grossing Hollywood release in the country’s box-office history, according to Variety.
Starring Matt Damon as Odysseus, the film has attracted approximately 12 million admissions in South Korea since its release on 5 August. Its performance has continued well beyond its opening weeks, with the film maintaining the number one position for seven consecutive weekends, the longest such run for an international release in the country.
The film’s success has also extended to premium cinema formats. The Odyssey has set records for admissions on IMAX and Dolby Cinema screens in South Korea, with IMAX screenings reportedly selling out continuously through its fifth week in cinemas. Its strong performance in these formats has contributed to its impressive box-office earnings.
The film crossed 10 million admissions in just 33 days, making it the fastest non-franchise international release to reach that milestone in South Korea. It also became the first international film carrying a 15-plus age rating to achieve the feat.
The record-breaking performance marks another significant achievement for Nolan, whose earlier film Interstellar also attracted a substantial audience in South Korea. With The Odyssey , he becomes the first director to have two non-franchise international films surpass 10 million admissions in the country.
The film’s promotional campaign also generated considerable interest. Its Seoul press conference attracted 209 media representatives, while a premiere event hosted by CGV received more than 32,000 applications. Korean celebrities, including BTS member Jungkook and TXT’s Soobin, also recommended the film, helping sustain online discussion around its release.
Despite overtaking Avatar: The Way of Water , The Odyssey has not claimed the overall record for the highest-grossing film in South Korea. Two domestic productions remain ahead of it: The King’s Warden , which has earned approximately $111.7 million, and Extreme Job , which has generated around $101.8 million.
Nevertheless, the achievement places The Odyssey at the top of the international box-office rankings in one of the world's most competitive theatrical markets. Its sustained run demonstrates the continued appeal of large-scale original filmmaking and premium cinema experiences among South Korean audiences.

title: Brazil s Lula accuses Meta of election interference
description: Lula s campaign said Meta  which owns Facebook  WhatsApp and Instagram  had restricted the reach of his content
content:
Lula's campaign said Meta, which owns Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram, had restricted the reach of his content
The campaign of Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva accused tech giant Meta of election interference on Saturday after his social media content was allegedly blocked on the company's platforms.
The leftist leader is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term in the October 25 runoff, where he will face Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro.
In a statement, Lula's campaign reported instances where platforms owned by Meta -- the parent company of Facebook, WhatsApp, and Instagram -- allegedly restricted the distribution of his content.
The campaign claimed that in recent days, Meta "prevented President Lula's profile from promoting Instagram feed posts," while a post from his official account "experienced an interruption in view counts, which affected its reach."
It also said that prior to last Sunday's first round of voting -- in which Flavio Bolsonaro finished first -- the profiles of Lula and other leftist leaders "suddenly disappeared from Instagram's search function."
"The series of technical issues... raises strong suspicions that Meta's actions constitute an attempt to interfere in the Brazilian electoral process to the benefit of Flavio Bolsonaro's candidacy," the statement added.
Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE) on Saturday gave the social media giant 48 hours to clarify whether it reduced the reach of posts by Lula's campaign and to explain the irregularities reported.
Read More: Bill Gates warns cyberattacks most imminent AI threat
Meta was ordered to "report, profile by profile, all the measures applied" to "Lula's official accounts" and to "explain the anomalies in the metrics" of the videos, the TSE said.
Meta's Brazil office denied the charges, calling them "simply false" and "not supported by the facts."
"Many of the technical issues mentioned did not affect only Brazil or specific accounts," Meta told AFP in an email.
"We comply with electoral regulations and are committed to a level playing field regarding the use of our platforms."
Lula's campaign has filed a complaint with the electoral court over the alleged social media blocks.
Following the first round of voting, Lula -- who does not use a mobile phone -- launched a social media push that includes videos of him addressing his online followers.

title: Javier Bardem reveals he wanted his    Skyfall    villain to have sex with James Bond
description: Bardem played Silva  a former MI6 agent turned cyberterrorist who seeks revenge against the intelligence agency
content:
Bardem played Silva, a former MI6 agent turned cyberterrorist who seeks revenge against the intelligence agency
Javier Bardem has revealed that he wanted his Skyfall villain, Raoul Silva, to have a sexual interest in James Bond, explaining that he pitched the idea to director Sam Mendes while developing the character for the 2012 film.
The Oscar-winning actor discussed the decision during a Screen Talk at the BFI London Film Festival on Sunday, 11 October, reflecting on how he helped introduce a homoerotic undertone to one of the most memorable encounters in the James Bond franchise.
Bardem played Silva, a former MI6 agent turned cyberterrorist who seeks revenge against the intelligence agency and its leader, M, played by Judi Dench. His character's confrontation with Daniel Craig's Bond became one of the film's most talked-about scenes because of its suggestive dialogue and physical intimacy.
Recalling his conversations with Mendes, Bardem explained that he wanted to give Silva a more personal motivation beyond his plans to destroy MI6.
“We went through the reading of it and [Mendes] was so open to what I was proposing to do with the sexuality of the character,” Bardem said, according to Variety. “Because I said, ‘Listen, all the villains have done everything to destroy the world, but what about something personal? What about something like, besides destroying the world, he wants to have sex with Bond?’”
The actor said Mendes agreed to discuss the suggestion with the studio before deciding whether to include it in the film. The resulting scene sees Silva approach Bond, who is tied to a chair, and touch his chest and thighs while speaking suggestively.
Bond responds to Silva's advances with the line, “Well, there's a first time for everything,” before adding, “What makes you think this is my first time?” The exchange leaves the nature of Bond's sexual history ambiguous while unsettling Silva's attempts to gain control of the encounter.
Bardem credited Mendes with allowing him to explore the character's sexuality and push the scene further than audiences might have expected from a traditional James Bond film. The actor also suggested that the moment has endured in viewers' memories because it placed the famously confident spy in an unfamiliar situation.
The decision was notable within a franchise traditionally associated with Bond's relationships with women. Rather than explicitly defining either character's sexuality, the scene relied on ambiguity, provocation and psychological tension.
Bardem also recalled initially feeling nervous about accepting the role. He admitted that he was overwhelmed on his first day on set when he realised he was appearing alongside Craig and Dench in a James Bond film, temporarily forgetting his lines.
Released in 2012, Skyfall was directed by Mendes and became one of the most commercially successful entries in the long-running spy franchise. Bardem's performance as Silva earned widespread acclaim, with the character frequently remembered for his unsettling presence and unpredictable behaviour.
The actor's latest comments offer further insight into how the villain was developed and how a creative suggestion helped shape one of the film's defining confrontations.

content:
'The Social Reckoning' has struggled at the North American box office, earning just $5.5m during its opening weekend
The Social Reckoning has struggled at the North American box office, earning just $5.5 million during its opening weekend, while Jessica Chastain’s horror film Other Mommy claimed the top spot with a $27.5 million debut.
According to Variety, the latest box-office figures highlight the contrasting performances of the two new releases, with Other Mommy exceeding expectations and Aaron Sorkin’s follow-up to The Social Network falling short of its projected opening.
Directed by Rob Savage, Other Mommy stars Chastain in dual roles as a mother and a sinister doppelganger haunting her young daughter. The supernatural horror film earned $27.5 million from 3,365 theatres across North America, despite receiving disappointing reviews from critics and audiences.
Produced on a reported budget of $19 million, the film also collected approximately $17.6 million internationally across 50 markets, bringing its worldwide opening to around $45.2 million. Its theatrical performance provides a boost for Universal Pictures and Blumhouse, although its poor audience reception could affect its performance in the coming weeks.
Meanwhile, The Social Reckoning opened with $5.5 million from 2,606 theatres, placing it well behind the horror release. The film is written and directed by Sorkin and serves as a follow-up to his acclaimed 2010 drama The Social Network , which explored the creation of Facebook.
The new film centres on whistleblower Frances Haugen and the controversy surrounding Facebook's internal documents, which exposed concerns about the platform's impact on society. Jeremy Strong stars as Mark Zuckerberg, with Mikey Madison and Jeremy Allen White also appearing in the cast.
The film's opening marks a significant decline compared with The Social Network , which debuted with approximately $22.6 million in North America in 2010. With a reported production budget of around $30 million, The Social Reckoning now faces the challenge of attracting audiences through word of mouth and its subsequent theatrical run.
The film also received a B- CinemaScore from opening-weekend audiences, while critical reception remained mixed. Its performance reflects the difficulties faced by dramas dealing with contemporary political and social issues in attracting a broad theatrical audience.
Elsewhere at the box office, Verity earned approximately $11.5 million in its second weekend, while Resident Evil collected $8.4 million. Heart of the Beast followed with $7.1 million.
Although Other Mommy has secured the weekend's leading position, its reception suggests that a strong opening does not necessarily guarantee sustained box-office success. For The Social Reckoning , the modest debut puts greater pressure on its international release and continued audience interest as it attempts to build momentum beyond its first weekend.

title: Bill Gates warns cyberattacks most imminent AI threat
description: Rejected Trump s view that AI companies can regulate themselves enough to keep the world safe
content:
Rejected Trump's view that AI companies can regulate themselves enough to keep the world safe
Bill Gates on Sunday warned that unregulated artificial intelligence poses a growing threat and predicted an escalation in AI-powered cyberattacks in the coming year.
The Microsoft co-founder said the risk of AI "getting out of control" remained years away and emphasized that the immediate concern was "bad people" using existing systems without safeguards.
"The front that we'll probably see most dramatically in the next year is cyberattacks," Gates said in an interview with ABC News .
"The real danger right now is not the AI's getting out of control. We need to work on that, but that's years away in terms of the big impact that might have," he said.
"It's really bad people using AI, particularly in AI where you can take out all the safeguards," he said, adding that increased restrictions were needed to prevent bad actors using AI for bioterrorism and cyberattacks.
Read More: Anthropic discloses fake tip to police among new rogue AI incidents
"But right now, you're allowed to take all those safeguards out. So when you have bad people, no safeguards, and then the latest models, that's where, over the next year, primarily in the cyber area, we are going to have a lot of negative surprises," he told ABC.
Gates -- who warned in a lengthy August post that the world was dangerously unprepared for the upheaval brought by AI, especially to employment -- is the latest tech magnate to sound the alarm on the threats posed by the new technology.
In his interview Sunday, he dismissed the idea -- advocated by US President Donald Trump -- that self-regulation by AI companies was sufficient to keep the world safe.
"The idea that for the most dangerous technology humans ever invented, that that's the final word, that just the companies themselves are the only check that society has...it's clear we're not doing enough," Gates said.

Frasier star David Hyde Pierce has recalled the enthusiastic audience reaction when his character, Niles Crane, finally kissed Jane Leeves’ Daphne Moon after years of romantic tension on the hit sitcom.
Pierce, 67, discussed the memorable moment during a recent interview with The Guardian , reflecting on how the show’s writers handled one of its most anticipated relationships. The series premiered on NBC in September 1993 and ran for 11 seasons.
Niles, the younger brother of psychiatrist Frasier Crane, developed feelings for Daphne, his father Martin’s live-in physiotherapist, early in the series. However, Daphne remained unaware of his affection for years, allowing their relationship to develop gradually across multiple seasons.
Recalling their first kiss in front of a live studio audience, Pierce said, “I remember very well — speaking of moments that stick with me — when we kissed in front of the live audience. They lost their minds.”
Leeves, 65, also reflected on the long-awaited romantic development, noting that seven seasons of suspense had left viewers eager to see the characters become a couple.
“Seven years is a long time and I think the audience was sort of begging to please bring this to a conclusion,” she told the publication.
Pierce agreed that prolonging the storyline indefinitely could have weakened its impact. He explained that the characters had spent years doubting whether they deserved each other, and eventually the story needed to move forward.
The actor also praised the creative team for knowing when to resolve the romance and how to conclude the sitcom. He said the creators ended the series while the cast and audience still wanted more, allowing them to shape a final season rather than waiting for the network to cancel the show.
The Niles and Daphne romance remains one of Frasier’s most memorable storylines, with their eventual relationship providing a major payoff for viewers who had followed the characters for years.

title: Donald Trump suggests renaming Atlantic or Pacific Ocean  Trump Ocean
description: We need a river  we need an ocean  So  I was thinking of either the Atlantic or the Pacific     Trump said
content:
“We need a river, we need an ocean. So, I was thinking of either the Atlantic or the Pacific,” Trump said
US President Donald Trump has suggested renaming either the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean the “Trump Ocean” or the “Ocean of the Americas” during a rally in Clarksville, Tennessee, on Saturday, 10 October.
Speaking to supporters, Trump said the United States needed an ocean and a major river to rename, following his administration’s previous efforts to change the names of major geographical landmarks. His remarks prompted laughter and applause from the crowd.
“We need a river, we need an ocean. So, I was thinking of either the Atlantic or the Pacific,” Trump said, adding that the names could be “Trump Ocean” or “Ocean of the Americas”.
Trump also reiterated that he did not intend to rename the Hudson River or the Mississippi River. Referring to the Mississippi, he said he had a particular fondness for the state of Mississippi because of his electoral success there.
The comments follow Trump's earlier efforts to change the names of prominent bodies of water. In January 2025, he signed an executive order directing the US government to use “Gulf of America” instead of “Gulf of Mexico” in federal communications and official records.
In August 2026, Trump also announced an executive order renaming Lake Ontario “Lake America”. The move affected the US government's official naming conventions, although the lake's name is not necessarily recognised in the same way by Canada, which shares its shoreline.
Trump first raised the possibility of renaming the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean during an executive order signing ceremony in August. His latest comments revived the suggestion, although he did not announce a formal executive action to rename either ocean during Saturday's rally.
While the US government can determine the names used on its own official maps and records, it cannot compel other countries or international organisations to adopt the same names. Any proposed change to an internationally recognised geographical name would therefore face the challenge of gaining wider acceptance.
The remarks form part of Trump's broader efforts to change the names of geographical landmarks during his presidency. His administration has also restored the name Mount McKinley for North America's tallest mountain, reversing the 2015 federal decision to use Denali, the name long associated with Alaska Native heritage.
For now, the proposed “Trump Ocean” remains a suggestion rather than an announced official name change. Trump has not outlined a formal process or timeline for renaming either the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean.

content:
Jennifer Simard reveals how fibroids led to emergency care and life-saving surgery before her Broadway return
Broadway actress Jennifer Simard has opened up about years of suffering from uterine fibroids, revealing that she underwent a hysterectomy and oophorectomy after experiencing a serious health scare during her run in Death Becomes Her .
The three-time Tony Award nominee told PEOPLE that she underwent surgery on July 6, days after the Broadway musical closed on June 28. During the final months of the production, Simard experienced severe bleeding that required emergency room treatment.
The actress said doctors initially believed she had eight uterine fibroids, but the actual number was nearly twice as high.
“It turns out I had 15,” Simard recalled.
The procedure involved removing her uterus and ovaries. Despite her health struggles, she managed to complete her run in Death Becomes Her , a feat she said required considerable strength.
Simard also addressed criticism she received from theatre fans over her missed performances. Although she tried to avoid online discussions, members of her team informed her about negative comments questioning her absences.
“They didn’t know what I was suffering with — honestly, for years,” she said.
The actress now hopes her experience will encourage audiences to show greater compassion towards performers who miss shows because of health issues.
Simard described the operation as life-saving and said her recovery took approximately six weeks. She credited her surgeon and confirmed that the laparoscopic procedure, performed with robotic assistance, went smoothly without complications.
Following her recovery, Simard returned to Broadway on September 8, joining the cast of Schmigadoon! at the Nederlander Theatre. She took over the role of Mildred Layton from Ana Gasteyer.
The new production reunited Simard with familiar collaborators and brought her back to the theatre where she received her first Tony Award nomination for Disaster! in 2016.
Reflecting on her return, Simard said she loves the discipline and routine of theatre. She also described Schmigadoon! as a refreshing experience that has helped her reconnect with the joy of performing.

title: Water pollution monitoring lacks public transparency
description: Punjab sets up 15 water quality monitoring stations under Rs2 97 billion project
content:
Punjab sets up 15 water quality monitoring stations under Rs2.97 billion project
Punjab has installed 15 modern stations to track pollution in its rivers, canals and drains, with water quality data sent to a central control room every hour. But while the system monitors the province’s waters, the data remains out of public reach.
According to official documents, the project launched by the Environment Protection Department was initially approved at an estimated cost of around Rs600 million. However, following a revision, its total cost was fixed at Rs2.97 billion in November 2024.
The project covers major rivers, canal networks, drains used for wastewater disposal and other important surface water bodies across Punjab. The Ravi, Chenab, Jhelum and Sutlej rivers have been prioritised for monitoring.
Officials said the stations were equipped with instruments to measure different water quality parameters, assess water flow, store data and transmit information to a central system. The data is sent to the Environmental Protection Department’s central control room, allowing changes in water quality and pollution levels to be identified in a timely manner.
Abdullah Nayyar Sheikh, Director of the Punjab Environmental Protection Agency, said the primary objective was to continuously monitor pollution in rivers and other surface water bodies, identify sources of contamination and provide timely information to support the enforcement of environmental laws.
The project was launched under the Punjab Green Development Programme with support from the World Bank. The initial target was to make all 15 monitoring stations operational by May 2025. However, delays led to a subsequent revision of the project timeline.
ohail Naqvi, Director of Water Affairs at WWF-Pakistan, welcomed the installation of monitoring systems in rivers and at other locations across the province.
He said advanced monitoring systems were already being used in developed countries, where sensors provided timely information about water quality and pollution levels. Such data helped policymakers and planners formulate effective policies for treating industrial and other wastewater and controlling pollution.
However, Naqvi proposed that the government provide the public with direct access to all data collected through the monitoring system. He said that, just as smog and air quality levels were made public, water quality data from different locations should also be released.
He suggested that information from locations such as Trimmu Headworks, the BRB Canal and entry and exit points around Lahore should be made publicly available. The data should include water quality, the presence of heavy metals and organic waste, and changes in water conditions following rainfall.
Naqvi believed transparent public access to the information could make the initiative an important step towards water conservation and environmental improvement.
Dr Muhammad Yaseen, Assistant Professor at the University of Punjab’s Centre for Integrated Mountain Research, said installing monitoring systems at the entry and exit points of rivers, drains and canals would enable continuous tracking of changes in water quality.
He said the system would help determine pollution levels at specific locations and establish how water quality changed as it passed through different areas. This would help authorities identify pollution sources, monitor the discharge of contaminated industrial and sewage water, and take effective measures to improve water quality.
Noor Ahmad, Director of Environmental Monitoring System (EMS), said 15 monitoring stations had so far been installed at Siphon on the River Ravi, downstream of Hudiara Drain and at all headworks.
He said data collected by the stations was being checked, while the imported monitoring systems were being adapted to local rivers, drains and headworks to ensure compatibility with local conditions.
Ahmad added that the data would begin appearing on the central dashboard after a third-party declaration.
While the 15 stations mark progress in monitoring water pollution, experts say public access to the data is essential for transparency, accountability and effective action against contamination.

Their appearance comes three weeks after Presley died on September 20 at a rehabilitation facility in Santa Monica
Cindy Crawford and her husband, Rande Gerber, have been photographed holding hands during their first public outing together since the death of their son, Presley Gerber, at the age of 27.
The supermodel, 60, and the businessman, 64, were spotted walking along Zuma Beach in Malibu, California, on Saturday, 10 October. The couple kept a low profile during the outing, wearing casual outfits as they walked side by side.

The Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner has yet to determine the official cause and manner of death, and the investigation remains ongoing.

A source previously told People that Crawford was heartbroken and completely in shock following her son's death. Other sources have described the family's close relationship and their efforts to support Presley through his struggles with mental health and addiction.
Presley had spoken publicly about his experiences with mental health and substance abuse, using social media to discuss his recovery and encourage conversations about issues that people often find difficult to address.

Although the couple have not publicly discussed their son's death in detail, their latest appearance marks their first public outing together since the loss. Netflix has unveiled the first teaser for its 2026 Christmas movie line-up, offering a glimpse at four festive films starring Jared Padalecki, Maddie Ziegler, Fantasia Barrino and several other familiar faces.
The exclusive teaser, released through People on 11 October 2026, previews A Dog’s Perfect Christmas , Guarding Stars , In a Holidaze and Tyler Perry’s The Gospel of Christmas . The four films will arrive on the streaming platform weekly between November and December, bringing a mix of holiday romance, family drama, comedy and gospel music.
The first release, A Dog’s Perfect Christmas , is scheduled to premiere on 4 November. Starring Dennis Quaid, Milo Ventimiglia, Jennifer Tilly and Mary Steenburgen, the film follows a family struggling to stay together during the festive season. A teenager, her grandfather and his loyal basset hound attempt to hold their household together as Christmas approaches. Cathryn Michon directs the film, which is based on a novel by W. Bruce Cameron, the author of A Dog’s Purpose .
Next up is Tyler Perry’s The Gospel of Christmas , arriving on 11 November. Written and directed by Perry, the film centres on a struggling pastor who inherits his family’s church in a troubled New York neighbourhood. As he faces personal doubts, temptation and a dangerous adversary, he must rediscover his faith to save his church, family and community.
The film stars Fantasia Barrino and Tank, alongside gospel music legends including Shirley Caesar, Fred Hammond, the Clark Sisters, Yolanda Adams and CeCe Winans. Its combination of a Christmas story and gospel performances makes it one of the musical highlights of Netflix’s festive slate.
On 18 November, Guarding Stars will bring a romantic storyline to the line-up. The film stars Leighton Meester as a no-nonsense bodyguard assigned to protect a charming action star, played by Padalecki, during the holidays. As the pair navigate secrets and unexpected romantic feelings, their professional relationship becomes increasingly complicated. The film is directed by Elizabeth Allen Rosenbaum and is based on Katherine Center’s novel The Bodyguard .
The final release, In a Holidaze , is scheduled for 2 December. Ziegler stars as a directionless young woman who finds herself trapped in a Christmas time loop after making a major romantic mistake. Forced to relive the holiday at her family’s cabin, she must work out what truly makes her happy. Rob Lowe also stars in the film, which is directed by Tiffany Paulsen and based on the novel by Christina Lauren.
The teaser offers brief glimpses of the films, including romantic moments between Meester and Padalecki, scenes featuring Ziegler and her co-stars, and Barrino alongside gospel performers. It also includes a glimpse of a Corgi riding a Roomba, adding a playful touch to the festive preview.
Netflix is expected to release longer trailers and additional behind-the-scenes details throughout the week, giving viewers a closer look at the upcoming films ahead of their premieres.
Alongside the new titles, the teaser features clips from previous Netflix Christmas favourites, including Falling for Christmas , Family Switch , The Merry Gentlemen , Hot Frosty , Best Christmas Ever! , The Princess Switch 3 and My Secret Santa .
With its 2026 festive line-up, Netflix is bringing together established Hollywood stars, rising performers and celebrated gospel artists across four films designed to appeal to different holiday viewing tastes.

title: Rising flu cases trigger mandatory Umrah vaccination
description: Experts urge timely immunization as respiratory infections rise and virus continues to evolve
content:
Experts urge timely immunization as respiratory infections rise and virus continues to evolve
Influenza cases are rising in Karachi, with patients reporting high fever, headache, sore throat, chest infections, dry cough, body aches and other flu-related symptoms. Doctors say the number of influenza patients visiting public and private hospitals has increased by around 20 per cent.
Amid the rise in cases, the Sindh government has made influenza vaccination mandatory for Umrah pilgrims travelling through Karachi Airport. Meningitis and polio vaccinations have also been made compulsory, with pilgrims required to present vaccination documentation before departure.
Medical experts say the current flu virus has shown symptoms similar to those associated with Covid-19, although there is disagreement over whether the virus represents a new influenza variant or a modified Covid-19 variant.
Pharmacist Dr Usman Ghani, who is involved in importing vaccines into Pakistan, said influenza viruses have several strains and can change their characteristics every year, requiring vaccines to be updated accordingly.
“Some health experts are describing this year’s influenza virus as a modified Covid-19 variant, while some doctors believe it is a new influenza variant that has changed its characteristics,” he said.
Ghani believed vaccination remained an important means of protection against influenza, particularly because the virus can spread rapidly from one person to another. He said children and elderly people were among those more vulnerable to infection, particularly when immunity was weak.
He added that the demand for vaccines had increased significantly following the Covid-19 pandemic as public awareness about vaccination improved. However, he warned that some organisations were importing vaccines from unqualified companies, leaving consumers unable to determine whether the products were genuine.
“Customs officials have even intercepted products sold as vaccines that turned out to contain distilled water or normal saline,” he said, stressing that vaccines should be imported from reputable manufacturers.
According to Ghani, influenza becomes more prevalent with the onset of colder weather, generally beginning around October. He said vaccines approved by international health authorities generally have a shelf life of one year and that Pakistan now imports around 700,000 influenza vaccine doses annually because of rising demand.
The vaccination requirement has particular significance for people travelling for Hajj and Umrah, where large numbers of people from different countries gather in confined spaces. A family preparing to travel for Umrah said vaccination was necessary to protect pilgrims from infectious diseases.
“Thousands of people from different countries are present during Umrah, so vaccination is important for protecting people’s health,” the family said.
Under the new requirements, Umrah pilgrims travelling through Karachi Airport must receive influenza, meningitis and polio vaccinations. After vaccination, they are required to upload their receipt to the NADRA website and obtain a vaccination card, which must be presented at the airport.
The rise in influenza cases has also renewed concerns over the quality and availability of vaccines in Pakistan. Experts say vaccination programmes can help reduce the spread and severity of seasonal influenza, but the public should ensure that vaccines are obtained through authorised and reliable sources.
With the flu season approaching and international travel increasing, health experts say vaccination and other preventive measures will remain important in limiting the spread of influenza, particularly among children, elderly people and other vulnerable groups.

title: PTI long march fizzles out in Swabi following emergency  governor s rule
description: Police deployed at key locations across Swabi to prevent possible protests  restrict movement of PTI s long march
author_name: Ahtesham Khan  , Ahtesham Bashir, MUHAMMAD SHOAIB
content:
Police deployed at key locations across Swabi to prevent possible protests
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s (PTI) long march effectively fizzled out in Swabi on Sunday amid heightened security arrangements following the imposition of an emergency and Governor’s rule in K-P.
Police were deployed at key locations across the district to prevent possible protests and restrict the movement of the long march caravan led by former chief minister Sohail Afridi. Mobile phone networks and PTCL internet services remained suspended across Swabi, causing inconvenience to residents and disrupting routine communications.
Read More : PTI rejects emergency, governor's rule in K-P as unconstitutional, vows to continue struggle
According to sources, the PTI caravan was expected to reach Swabi on the night of October 11. However, the party’s local leadership remained largely absent, and no significant protest activity was reported anywhere in the district on Monday.
Heavy police contingents were stationed at important locations, including Aman Chowk in Swabi, Topi, Swabi Interchange and Shiwa Adda in Razaar tehsil. In view of security concerns, containers were also brought to Swabi Interchange, Jahangira Bridge and the Indus River bridge on the M-1 Motorway.
Despite these arrangements, the Peshawar-Islamabad Motorway and the Grand Trunk Road remained open to traffic.
Police sources said raids were conducted at several locations in Shiwa Adda and adjoining areas following reports of the expected arrival of the long march. The action was aimed at arresting PTI workers, but no arrests were reported.
Sources said PTI leaders had directed party workers to assemble at the Razaar Sports Complex to make arrangements for the march, prompting police to step up security and surveillance.
Some PTI workers and youth wing members gathered at Shiwa Adda ground and Ismaila Interchange in preparation for the march. However, police dispersed some of the workers, and the anticipated mobilisation failed to materialise.
Following the imposition of the emergency, the situation at Aman Chowk remained completely normal, with traffic moving smoothly and businesses operating as usual.
Police said security measures had been put in place to deal with any eventuality. With no major demonstration reported and the party’s local leadership largely absent, the long march showed little sign of proceeding through Swabi as anticipated.
Police vow action against rioters, violence
Meanwhile, K-P Police resolved to deal firmly with protest demonstrations, warning that those involved in rioting, vandalism or disrupting law and order would face the full force of the law.
Authorities made clear that no damage to government installations, buildings or public property would be tolerated during any protest or disturbance. The public had been advised to stay away from illegal gatherings, violent activities or any form of provocation. Failure to do so would result in the strictest legal action.
Police said they would take action against anyone who threatened peace, attacked security forces or buildings, or endangered citizens’ lives and property. Citizens had been urged to remain peaceful, respect the law and avoid being misled by troublemakers.
Special security arrangements were being put in place to protect police stations, government buildings, banks, petrol pumps, commercial centres and major highways. All protest activities and police responses would be video-recorded to support any subsequent legal proceedings.
To ensure an effective response, the police would maintain close coordination with the district administration and other relevant agencies. Officials emphasised that while peaceful expression of views was a right, violence and lawlessness would not be allowed under any circumstances.
Even before the formal imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in K-P, authorities sealed the Cantonment area of Peshawar, bringing commercial activity and traffic to a standstill.
Saddar Bazaar and other commercial centres inside the Cantonment remained closed. Containers were placed at key points to seal all access routes into the area. Roads leading to the Provincial Assembly, Mall Road, Khyber Road and the High Court were also blocked. Containers had been brought into the city overnight and positioned at Firdous Chowk, Assembly Chowk, University Road, Pajagi Road, Kohat Road and other approaches to Saddar.
The sealing of Cantonment roads also forced the closure of markets in Saddar Bazaar. Traffic movement was suspended, leaving residents facing significant difficulties in daily movement.

A heavy police contingent was deployed on routes leading to Saddar to handle any protests against the emergency decision. TransPeshawar suspended the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) service indefinitely due to the situation, keeping all BRT stations closed and causing hardship for citizens dependent on public transport.
