title: FM Dar condemns Houthi attack on Riyadh airport  says Pakistan is in touch with Saudi authorities
description: Says attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are unacceptable  calls for immediate end to hostilities
content:
Calls attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure unacceptable, urges immediate end to hostilities
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Sunday strongly condemned the Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, calling for an immediate cessation of hostilities and reaffirming Pakistan’s commitment to Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty and security under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.
At least 12 people were killed and 309 injured in the attack on the Saudi capital’s international airport, according to Saudi officials, as tensions escalated in the region following recent hostilities.
In a statement on X, FM Dar said Pakistan condemned the attacks in the strongest terms and expressed deep concern over the Houthi assault.
“Attacks targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure are totally unacceptable, violate international law and pose a serious threat to regional peace and security,” he said.
Deeply concerned by the Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which Pakistan condemns in the strongest terms. We pray for the speedy recovery of all those injured, including the six Pakistani nationals. Attacks targeting civilians and civilian…
FM Dar prayed for the speedy recovery of all those injured, including six Pakistani nationals, and stressed that such acts must cease immediately.
He said Pakistan was in contact with the Saudi authorities and closely monitoring the situation.
Read : Saudi-led coalition says new attack at Riyadh airport causes fire, day after strike kills 12
The deputy prime minister also directed the Pakistani Embassy in Riyadh to coordinate with the relevant authorities to provide all possible assistance to the injured Pakistani nationals.
Reaffirming Pakistan’s longstanding commitment to the Kingdom, FM Dar said Islamabad stood in solidarity with Saudi Arabia’s leadership and people.
“Pakistan remains firmly committed to the Kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security in accordance with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement,” he added.
Meanwhile, the Regional Four (R4) on Sunday condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and the recent targeting of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh in a joint statement .
"The States of the R4 Group (The Islamic Republic of Pakistan, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the Arab Republic of Egypt, and the Republic of Türkiye) condemn in the strongest terms the ongoing hostile attacks perpetrated by the Houthi militia against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including the heinous attacks targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, resulting in civilian deaths and injuries, as well as damage to civilian infrastructure and facilities, which constitute a blatant violation of international law," the statement read.
According to the statement, R4 reaffirmed that the Houthi attacks constituted a "flagrant violation" of the Kingdom's sovereignty and territorial integrity, further adding that it posed a direct threat to Saudi Arabia's security, stability, and the safety of civilians, and was a "dangerous escalation" that could not be justified or accepted under any pretext.
🔊PR No.2️⃣8️⃣5️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Joint Statement by the R4 Group 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/oy93JYi2qk
It added that R-4 further "reaffirmed its solidarity with and support for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including its full support for all legitimate measures and steps it takes to counter these attacks, deter the sources of their threats, and prevent their recurrence, in defence of the Kingdom's security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, and in protection of the safety of its citizens and residents, in line with the Charter of the United Nations and international law".
The statement also noted that R-4 held the Houthi militia fully accountable for the results of these attacks and any repercussions that come with them that threatened regional and international peace and security, and demanded the immediate and unconditional halt of these attacks.
In Saturday's attack, the third on Riyadh's airport in a week, the 12 dead included 4 Saudis, 2 Bangladeshis and nationals of the United States, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, Saudi authorities said.
It was the deadliest such attack in the kingdom in more than a decade and comes amid an escalation of fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces.
Saudi Arabia has stepped up its military involvement in Yemen in recent weeks, launching strikes against the Houthis and backing a Yemeni government counteroffensive after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.
Earlier, Yemen’s Houthis warned airlines, travellers and airport workers to stay away from Saudi airports.
Also Read : Yemen's Houthis renew warning over Saudi airports after deadly Riyadh attack
"We renew our warning to all airlines, experts, employees, workers and travellers against using Saudi airports and airspace, as they are vulnerable to attack and have become a theatre of operations for our forces, except the airports in (the holy cities of) Makkah and Madinah."
Yemen's Houthi-run foreign ministry said later on Sunday that further Saudi military action in Yemen would trigger a stronger response, adding that its actions would be guided by the principle of reciprocity.
"Unless the Saudi enemy stops its aggression and interference in Yemen, worse is yet to come, God willing," the ministry said in statements carried by Houthi-run Al Masirah television.
The two previous attacks on King Khalid International Airport this week killed ⁠four and caused heavy damage to a Saudi commercial plane parked on the tarmac. The strikes have exposed vulnerabilities in Saudi defence capabilities as it wages an air campaign against the ​Houthis to support a ground war by the Yemeni government against the group.
President Donald Trump said on Saturday the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the wider war on Iran that the US and Israel launched in February.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemned the attacks on the airport, saying they "demonstrate a blatant disregard for innocent civilian life".
Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government have claimed hundreds of strikes on targets in Houthi-held territory. The Houthis have said these killed ​civilians, including women and children. Reuters could not independently verify those claims.
The Saudis entered the Yemen war in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition to try to force the Houthis out of ‌the Yemeni capital ⁠Sanaa. The war became a bloody stalemate, with hundreds of thousands of Yemenis killed by fighting and famine.
A 2022 ceasefire reached by the Saudis and the Houthis unravelled this summer, culminating in a lightning Houthi advance that took the Red Sea chokepoint of Bab el-Mandeb from Saudi-backed government forces.

title: Samuel L  Jackson never imagined meeting Marvel legend Stan Lee as a child
description: Samuel L  Jackson recalls his friendship with Stan Lee  saying he never imagined meeting the Marvel legend as a child
content:
Samuel L. Jackson recalls his friendship with Stan Lee, saying he never imagined meeting the Marvel legend as a child
Samuel L. Jackson is reflecting on his friendship with late Marvel legend Stan Lee, revealing that meeting the comic book creator was something he never imagined possible while growing up in segregated Tennessee.
The 77-year-old actor spoke to PEOPLE at the Los Angeles premiere of his thriller The Beast on October 6, where he learned that he ranks just behind Lee in cumulative box office revenue across film roles.
Jackson recalled growing up reading Lee’s comic books and seeing his name associated with some of Marvel’s most iconic characters, including Spider-Man, the Hulk, Iron Man, Thor and the X-Men.
“Never occurred to me as a kid growing up in segregated Tennessee, I would meet Stan Lee,” Jackson told PEOPLE. “So when it happens, it’s not even a dream come true. It’s something beyond that.”
The actor, best known for playing Nick Fury in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, described Lee as a “wonderful, charming person” and praised his warmth and generosity.
Lee, who co-created numerous beloved Marvel characters, died on November 12, 2018, at the age of 95. He had worked on approximately 200 films during his career, leaving behind a lasting legacy in the entertainment industry.
Following Lee’s death, Jackson paid tribute to the comic book pioneer on X, thanking him for creating fictional worlds that offered audiences an escape from reality.
The actor praised Lee for inspiring generations of fans through his characters and stories, highlighting the joy and heroism they brought to people around the world.
Jackson has previously spoken about his long-running involvement in the Marvel franchise, saying he values happiness and satisfaction in his acting career over awards recognition. He has portrayed Nick Fury across multiple Marvel projects and remains one of the franchise’s familiar faces.
Meanwhile, Jackson is currently starring in The Beast , a newly released thriller centred on a US president fighting to save his life and the country.

title: Trump says Russia and Ukraine reach energy ceasefire  effective immediately
description: Zelenskiy said Trump s post was his first news of the deal  Ukraine was ready if Russia agreed
content:
Zelenskiy says Trump's post was his first news of the deal; Ukraine was ready if Russia agreed
US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to what he described as an "energy ceasefire", hours after Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy had pushed back against US pressure for a unilateral end to strikes on Russian refineries.
In a social media post, Trump said the energy ceasefire would take effect immediately, but did not elaborate further.
In an interview with Axios, Zelenskiy said Trump's post was the first he had heard of the deal, though a senior Ukrainian official told Reuters that Ukraine was ready to agree to such a ceasefire if Russia was.
Trump, whose war in Iran has been blamed for high diesel prices that are weighing on Republicans' prospects at next month's midterm elections, had previously announced an energy ceasefire in Ukraine in mid-September, though neither side ever confirmed such an agreement was reached.
"Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" Trump wrote on Truth Social.
Earlier on Sunday, Zelenskiy had repeated Ukraine's long-standing position that it was willing to halt attacks on Russian refineries but only if Moscow ceased its own strikes on Ukrainian power infrastructure.
Any such deal would need to come with "real guarantees", Zelenskiy said.
"The real cause of the war in Europe is Russia and Russia alone," Zelenskiy said. "It's possible to stop strikes on energy infrastructure as early as today, but Putin does not want to do so."
In a dramatic deterioration in their relations, Trump on Saturday had warned Zelenskiy that he had "better damn well stop" attacking Russian refineries, and had urged Ukrainians to replace him as their leader via new elections because he had missed several opportunities to strike a deal with Moscow.
Read More: Trump says ‘it’s time for Ukraine to get a new president’ who can ‘make a deal’ with Russia
Appearing on ABC's "This Week" on Sunday, Zelenskiy responded that he would organise elections in Ukraine if Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to a 60-day ceasefire.
Zelenskiy said it was "up to Ukrainians" to choose their leader, but noted that there needed to be an end to the fighting first. Ukrainian law prohibits elections under martial law for security reasons.
"Please tell Putin, give us two months, 60 days of total ceasefire, 60 days, and we will organise elections," Zelenskiy said.
The Ukrainian leader rejected being blamed for energy price rises, adding that "everybody in the world" knew that the war in the Middle East was a bigger factor.
The steep rise in global diesel prices, which followed the outbreak of the Iran war in February, has become a political liability for Trump's Republican Party ahead of the midterms, when opposition Democrats could gain control of one or both houses of Congress.
On Saturday, Zelenskiy had responded angrily to Trump's announcement of a diesel supply deal with Russia, saying it would embolden Moscow's attacks on Ukraine and lead to a greater loss of civilian lives.
I just spoke with @MarkJCarney , @alexstubb , and @SecGenNATO Mark Rutte. We discussed the energy ceasefire announced by President Trump. Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it is important that Russia support it as well. We are awaiting details from the American side. For our…
Analysts said Trump's diesel supply agreement with Moscow was unlikely to lead to sustained lower fuel prices as the volumes involved were too small.
The diesel deal was also criticised by US lawmakers, including one of Trump's fellow Republicans, Representative Don Bacon, who said it was time to apply more sanctions, not lift them.
On the streets of Kyiv, several residents expressed anger at Trump's suggestion that Ukraine should find a new leader willing to make a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"No one has the right to tell us what to do, especially since elections cannot be held during wartime," said Sabina, a 40-year-old primary school teacher. "In my view, it is a betrayal by our partners," she said, describing Trump's remarks.
Zelenskiy said he would continue discussions with European leaders on Sunday, and there were daily conversations around additional air defence packages, including ammunition for combat aircraft that are used to down Russia's jet-powered drones.
On Monday, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha is due to participate in a European Union Foreign Affairs Council meeting that is expected to discuss increasing sanctions pressure on Russia and advancing negotiations on Ukraine’s EU accession.

title: Scientific expedition warns of accelerated glacier melting in NW China s Xinjiang
description: Xinjiang ranks first in China s glacier reserves  with 24 202 glaciers covering 23 629 sq km
content:
Xinjiang ranks first in China's glacier reserves, with 24,202 glaciers covering 23,629 sq km
Scientists with China's Third Xinjiang Scientific Expedition announced on Saturday that they had found more than 24,000 glaciers in the region and warned of accelerating melt there.
Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region in northwest China ranks first in glacier reserves in the country, followed by Xizang Autonomous Region in southwest China. At a press conference in Urumqi, Xinjiang's capital, the expedition team released the latest data, saying Xinjiang is home to 24,202 glaciers, covering 23,629 square km.
The glacier study is part of a five-year expedition, which was launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Science and Technology. The previous two were conducted in the 1950s and 1980s.
The expedition carried out studies on Xinjiang's ecology, land and agriculture, biodiversity and biological resources, mineral, energy and water resources. Forty-six national research institutions joined the work, with over 6,000 person-times of expedition members.
While the two earlier surveys centered on basic, census-based static resource inventory, this mission yields fresh first-hand data on Xinjiang's climate, ecology and resources.
From the 1990s to 2020, Xinjiang has lost 2,167 square km of glacier area, and most parts of this glacier-rich region are experiencing rapid melting, according to the expedition team.
Global warming is the main cause, said expedition member Li Zhongqin, a glacier researcher at the Northwest Institute of Eco-Environment and Resources under the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS).
The region has been warming faster than the global and national averages. The expedition team noted that over the past three decades, Xinjiang's temperature has been rising at a rate of 0.34 degrees Celsius per decade, roughly 1.7 times the global average and 1.13 times the national average.
Read More: Scientists reveal mechanism behind evolution of brain folds regulated by ancient gene
The surface of lakes and wetlands in Xinjiang has grown by roughly one-third, also partly due to glacier melt, Li said.
Glaciers are vital to Xinjiang as the sources of many rivers in this inland region. Faster melting can increase river runoff, but it can also cause ice avalanches and raise the risk of floods and mudslides, Li told Xinhua, adding that glacier collapses are likely to become frequent in this region.
China's Third Xinjiang Scientific Expedition announced on Saturday that they had found more than 24,000 glaciers in the region and warned of accelerated melting. XINHUA
Strengthening of monitoring efforts is necessary to respond to these risks. Li and his colleagues have used remote sensing satellites and drones to track glacier movement and temperature changes.
Another highlight of the expedition was joint cross-border glacier research, including the identification of glaciers in Tajikistan, which neighbors southwestern Xinjiang, and the publication of an atlas of that country's glaciers.
Scientific cooperation between the two countries stems from the common challenge of glacier melt, said Li Zhi, a researcher at the Xinjiang Institute of Ecology and Geography under the CAS. She and her colleagues have launched a UNESCO-recognized project that focuses on assessing glacial changes in Tajikistan, predicting future glacier trends and studying the risks of glacier-related disasters.
Tajikistan has many glaciers, and melt could lead to disastrous events, such as glacial lake outburst floods, which may endanger local residents, she added.
Besides glacier melt, the expedition also focused on other common regional challenges, such as water scarcity and desertification, and carried out joint scientific research with Central Asian countries.

title: Scientists reveal mechanism behind evolution of brain folds regulated by ancient gene
description: Brain wrinkles and grooves support advanced cognition  traditionally thought to result from newly evolved genes
content:
Brain wrinkles and grooves support advanced cognition, traditionally thought to result from newly evolved genes
A group of Chinese scientists has uncovered the mystery behind how an ancient gene regulates the development of brain folds, shedding new light on the evolution of the human brain. The findings were recently published in Nature Genetics.
The human brain is covered with intricate wrinkles and grooves, which constitute one of the important biological foundations for the emergence of advanced human cognitive functions. The traditional view holds that the expansion of the primate cerebral cortex was primarily driven by newly evolved genes.
However, a research team led by Shi Lei, a researcher from the Kunming Institute of Zoology under the Chinese Academy of Sciences, proposed an alternative possibility: certain ancient and highly conserved genes could also play a key role in human brain evolution by reshaping their expression levels through changes in regulatory elements.
The team compared transcriptomic data from different layers of the embryonic cerebral cortex of mice, tree shrews, marmosets, macaques and humans. They found that an ancient gene called "CCNB1IP1" was already expressed in the brain of the tree shrew, a close relative of primates, long before primates emerged but at relatively low expression levels.
Read More: China's AI journey offers insights
The team further discovered that during the following course of evolution, the expression level of this ancient gene showed a clear stepwise increase among tree shrews, marmosets, macaques and humans, reaching its highest level in the human brain.
"The expression level of this ancient gene is closely correlated with the degree of cortical folding," said Shi, who noted that in marmosets, which have smooth brains, the expression level of this gene is similar to that in tree shrews. In macaques, whose brains have folds, the expression level is markedly elevated. In the human brain, this gene is expressed at the highest level.
Moreover, the team identified a key regulatory sequence, CRE1, that drives the elevated expression of CCNB1IP1.
To verify the gene's function, the team constructed a mouse model carrying the gene. The experiment showed that mice, which normally have a smooth cerebral cortex, developed cortical folding structures after the gene knock-in. Meanwhile, the modified mice exhibited enhanced learning and memory abilities in behavioral tests.
The team noted that this study not only provides a new perspective for understanding the evolution of the human brain, but also offers new clues for exploring the causes of neural development disorders.

content:
Tiffani Thiessen shares her thoughts on daughter Harper embracing ’90s fashion, from side parts to retro outfits
Tiffani Thiessen has shared her thoughts on the resurgence of ’90s and Y2K fashion trends, revealing how she feels about seeing her 16-year-old daughter, Harper Renn Smith, embrace styles from her own youth.
The Saved by the Bell star, 52, discussed the return of retro fashion during an interview with PEOPLE for The Sitdown , while promoting her new series Coven Academy . Thiessen shares Harper and 11-year-old son Holt with her husband, actor Brady Smith.
The actress said it was “really, really fun” to see ’90s fashion receive renewed attention, particularly as the trends make their way into her teenage daughter’s wardrobe.
Thiessen also revealed which returning styles she enjoys, including zig-zag hair parts, side parts, tiny sunglasses and blazers paired with crop tops. She welcomed the comeback of the unitard, although she joked that she would probably choose darker colours rather than the bright orange version she wore on Saved by the Bell .
“I kind of dig it,” Thiessen said of the zig-zag hair part, adding that the trend could help bring side parts back into fashion after the popularity of middle parts.
However, not every retro hairstyle has won her approval. The actress said modern feathered bangs were fine, but she would prefer to leave behind the heavily teased hairstyles that relied on excessive hairspray.
Thiessen also recalled wearing suspenders with baggy trousers and white sleeveless tops, linking the look to her Long Beach roots. She added that she had heard overalls were returning to fashion, another trend she frequently wore in the past.
Thiessen rose to fame as Kelly Kapowski on Saved by the Bell , which aired from 1989 to 1993. She later played Valerie Malone on Beverly Hills, 90210 from 1994 to 1998.
The actress currently stars as Miss Graves, the head of the magical Crescent Veil Academy, in Coven Academy , which is available on Disney+, Hulu and Freeform on Demand.

content:
The boat capsized near Djibouti's Obock port town on the night of October 8–9, the IOM said
At least 139 migrants , including 15 children, have died and more than 116 are missing after a boat carrying ​about 305 people capsized while sailing from Djibouti to Yemen, the ‌United Nations International Organisation for Migration said on Sunday.
The boat capsized near Guhere, north of Obock — a port town in Djibouti — during the night of 8–9 October, the IOM said, ​citing survivor accounts.
More than 80 people survived the shipwreck, all Ethiopian nationals, ​the statement said. A spokesperson for the Ethiopian government did not ⁠immediately respond to requests for comment.
Among the 139 bodies recovered after the ​boat capsized, 52 are men, 42 women and 15 children including nine girls and ​six boys, the IOM said.
The death toll from the #Djibouti shipwreck has risen to 139, with 84 people still missing. As search and recovery efforts continue, IOM is providing emergency assistance to survivors. Every life lost is one too many. Read the latest updates here: https://t.co/LJjeAtSer2 pic.twitter.com/VXfiv3TeFA
"Our teams are on the ground alongside local authorities to provide emergency assistance," said IOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti Alexandre Coissac.
"This tragedy is a stark reminder ​of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek ​economic opportunities," Coissac said.

Djiboutian authorities are continuing search and rescue operations, the IOM statement said, ‌adding ⁠that local authorities are also providing medical care to survivors and arranging burials for the deceased.
The Djibouti government could not be immediately reached for comment.
Yemen is experiencing the most serious escalation in fighting between Saudi Arabia-backed government forces and the Iran-backed Houthis ​since a UN-brokered ​truce largely halted ⁠cross-border attacks in 2022. The renewed conflict could reshape control in Yemen, with implications for Red Sea shipping lanes.
IOM described ​the crisis sparked by the fighting as alarming, with displacement ​figures surging ⁠to 200,000 from 76,000 in mid-September, according to data released by the IOM last week.
More than 3,700 people have fled Yemen by sea to Djibouti as of last ⁠week, ​according to the IOM.
Fighting also broke out in ​Ethiopia last month in the biggest escalation of violence since the Tigray war.

title: Governor s rule imposed in K P for fourth time
description: Emergency declared in 12 districts under Article 232  powers shift to Governor Kundi
content:
Emergency declared in 12 districts under Article 232; powers shift to Governor Kundi
Governor’s rule has been imposed in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) for the fourth time, transferring powers once again from the provincial government to the Governor.
The first imposition came in 1975 under the central government of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. An emergency was declared after Hayat Muhammad Khan Sherpao was assassinated in a bomb blast while addressing a gathering at the Department of History of Peshawar University. The National Awami Party (NAP) was banned and arrests were made as the province came under Governor’s rule.
The second instance occurred in 1994 when Benazir Bhutto’s federal government moved against the Muslim League administration of Pir Sabir Shah. Assembly members were made to disappear, a no-confidence motion was brought against Chief Minister Pir Sabir Shah, and Aftab Ahmad Khan Sherpao subsequently formed the government.
The third imposition followed the 1999 counter-coup by then-army chief Pervez Musharraf against the Nawaz Sharif government. Muslim League Governor Mian Gul Aurangzeb was removed and replaced by Lieutenant General (retd) Muhammad Shafiq.
He was later succeeded by Lieutenant General (retd) Syed Iftikhar Hussain, who administered the province with his own cabinet until the formation of the Muttahida Majlis-e-Amal (MMA) government in November-December 2002.
Read More: Emergency, governor's rule imposed in K-P after president signs summary on PM Shehbaz's advice
Now, for the fourth time, the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf government of Sohail Afridi has been suspended and Governor’s rule imposed. Governor Faisal Karim Kundi will run the province with an interim cabinet.
This latest imposition is unique in that emergency has simultaneously been declared in 12 districts of the province under Article 232 of the Constitution of Pakistan. The districts include the eight merged tribal districts (former tribal agencies), Khyber, Mohmand, Kurram, Orakzai, Bajaur, North Waziristan, South Waziristan Upper and South Waziristan Lower, along with the southern districts of Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Bannu and Lakki Marwat.
The emergency applies fully in the Bannu and Dera Ismail Khan divisions and partially in the Peshawar, Kohat and Malakand divisions. The Hazara and Mardan divisions remain exempt.
The disruption of internet services caused widespread confusion across the province.

title: Nepal urges villagers to evacuate after flood triggered by landslide  5 missing
description: Two women and three men were missing  while 49 others  including a foreigner  were rescued
content:
Two women and three men were missing, while 49 others, including a foreigner, were rescued
Nepali authorities urged villagers on Sunday to move to safer places after ​a flood in a river in the central part of the ‌country swept away several houses and infrastructure, but there were no reports of any casualties.
Two women and three men were out of contact, the national disaster authority said. The ​army said a further 49 people, including a foreigner, had been ​rescued. They did not give the person's nationality.
A landslide in Chumnubri ⁠village in Gorkha district, about 100 km (62 miles) west of Kathmandu, blocked ​the Budhi Gandaki River, leading to downstream flooding, authorities said.
The Budhi Gandaki is ​a tributary of the Trishuli River, downstream from another tributary where a glacier collapse caused a catastrophic flood in August that killed 1,457 people, with thousands still missing.
"We have asked ​villagers living along the river banks downstream to evacuate and remain safe," ​said Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, the Gorkha district's most senior bureaucrat.
Read More: Resilience in the age of climate breakdown
The flood swept away about a ‌dozen ⁠houses and two suspension bridges and damaged a hydroelectric project camp, carrying some of the construction equipment away, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said.
The flooded river carrying muddy sludge was rising and had washed away a highway bridge ​connecting Gorkha with the ​neighbouring Dhading district, ⁠said Dharam Raj Uprety, chief of the Authority.
National disaster authorities alerted people living along the river in the Gorkha, ​Tanahun, Chitwan, East Nawalparasi and West Nawalparasi districts about ​the flood.
"Please ⁠help ensure that people in at-risk areas are moved to safe locations in time and assist search and rescue operations as needed," the National Disaster Risk Reduction ⁠and ​Management Authority said in a social media post.
Officials ​said army and police rescue personnel had reached the area and were also monitoring the situation ​from a helicopter.

title: Michael Douglas reveals he smuggled almost 200 pounds of marijuana to pay for college tuition
description: Douglas explained that he bought marijuana in California for  75 per kg and sold it in New York for  500 per kg
content:
Douglas explained that he bought marijuana in California for $75 per kg and sold it in New York for $500 per kg
Michael Douglas has revealed that he smuggled nearly 200 pounds of marijuana from California to New York to pay for his university education after his father, Hollywood legend Kirk Douglas, stopped providing financial support.
The Fatal Attraction star shared the story in his new memoir, One Helluva Ride , recalling how he found an unconventional way to cover his remaining college expenses during the late 1960s and early 1970s.
According to Douglas, his father gave him $10,000 when he turned 21 and told him he would have to support himself financially from then on. However, the actor still had two years of tuition and other university expenses to cover while studying at the University of California, Santa Barbara.
Douglas eventually realised that two Italian leather suitcases gifted to him by his father could provide an opportunity to make money. Each suitcase could hold approximately 22 kilograms of marijuana, allowing him to transport 44 kilograms in a single trip.
In his memoir, Douglas explained that he bought marijuana in California for $75 per kilogram and sold it in New York for $500 per kilogram. He said he carried out the plan twice, transporting a total of 88 kilograms, equivalent to more than 194 pounds.
The two trips reportedly generated approximately $37,400 in profit, a sum worth more than $360,000 today when adjusted for inflation. Douglas recalled travelling with the suitcases without encountering any problems at the airport and selling the marijuana to a contact in New York.
The actor also described how he eventually told his father about the operation after Kirk Douglas began holding up his son's financial independence as an example to his brothers. Michael reminded him of the suitcases he had received as a Christmas present and explained how he had used them.
Reflecting on his actions, Douglas acknowledged that his approach was neither legal nor something he would recommend to others. He wrote that applying for a student loan would have been a more responsible option, although he had not considered it at the time.
The revelation comes as Douglas promotes One Helluva Ride , which explores his life, career, family relationships and experiences during his younger years. The actor has also discussed the story publicly, including during an appearance on Real Time with Bill Maher on 9 October.
During the conversation, Douglas recalled how his father had effectively left him to manage his own finances while he was still studying. He also discussed the experience in the context of working ordinary jobs despite growing up as the son of a major Hollywood star.
Douglas ultimately completed his university education without student loans or outstanding debt, according to his memoir. His account offers a candid look at an unconventional chapter of his life before he established himself as one of Hollywood's most recognisable actors and producers.

title: France   s Cirotte claims Islamabad W15 title
description: Frenchwoman defeats Thailand   s Yodpetch in straight sets
content:
Frenchwoman defeats Thailand’s Yodpetch in straight sets
France’s Astrid Cirotte defeated Thailand’s Kamonwan Yodpetch 7-5, 7-5 in the women’s singles final of the W15 Islamabad – World Tennis Women’s Futures Championship on Sunday, claiming the title at the Pakistan Tennis Federation (PTF) Tennis Complex.
Cirotte, competing in Pakistan for the first time, said she hoped her success would inspire more young women in the country to take up the sport.
“Tennis is my passion, and achieving a prominent position in this sport is my goal,” she told The Express Tribune.
“I am visiting Pakistan for the first time, and I am enjoying playing tennis here. The courts are new, but the arrangements are excellent,” she added.
The Frenchwoman said tennis offered benefits beyond competition, helping players develop physical fitness and mental resilience.
“Tennis is not just a sport; it makes you physically and mentally stronger,” she said. “Pakistani women can bring pride to their country by playing tennis.”
She added that hard work, dedication and access to qualified coaches were key to success.
Top seed Cirotte reached the final after beating Uzbekistan’s Sevil Yuldasheva 6-4, 7-5 in the semi-finals. Yodpetch advanced with a 6-0, 6-4 victory over South Africa’s Wozuko Mdlulwa.
Cirotte also won the women’s doubles title on Saturday, partnering Mexico’s Sabastiani Leon to beat South Korea’s Jeong Moon and Yodpetch 5-7, 6-2, 10-5.
The first leg of the championship featured 30 players from 17 countries, including France, China, Russia, Denmark, Mexico, Uzbekistan, South Africa, the Netherlands, South Korea, Nepal, Japan, Hong Kong, Germany, Thailand, Turkiye, the Czech Republic and Pakistan.
Sponsored by Fatima Group, the tournament offered players an opportunity to earn valuable ranking points and provided international competition for women’s tennis in Pakistan.
The closing ceremony was attended by Fatima Group representative Asam Sharif, the chief guest, and Deputy Inspector General Saleem Marwat, the guest of honour. Other attendees included PTF director Colonel Gul Rehman, Pakistan Women Tennis Association secretary Zaira Ahmed Zaka, former Pakistan number one Sarah Mahboob Khan and ITA secretary Tufail Cheema.
The tournament was supervised by Turkish ITF Bronze Badge referee Abdullah Haluk Turun.
The second leg of the W15 Islamabad championship is scheduled to begin on October 13 at the PTF Tennis Complex.

title: Andrew Garfield recalls emotional  Spider Man  fan encounter in hotel lift
description: Andrew Garfield recalls meeting emotional  Spider Man  fan in Denver hotel lift and reveals his own starstruck moment
content:
Andrew Garfield recalls meeting emotional 'Spider-Man' fan in Denver hotel lift and reveals his own starstruck moment
Andrew Garfield has recalled meeting an emotional Spider-Man fan in a hotel lift in Denver, describing the encounter as a “very, very sweet” moment.
The actor, 43, shared the story during an exclusive interview with PEOPLE while discussing his upcoming film, The Magic Faraway Tree.
Garfield explained that he had stayed at an airport hotel during a layover when he encountered two women attending a conference.
One of them was wearing a Spider-Man T-shirt and appeared surprised when she recognised him.
“And this one young lady — probably in her 20s or 30s — was wearing a Spider-Man T-shirt, and she looked at me like I was some kind of mirage. And she said, 'Is it you? Is it you? … Are you Spider-Man?'”
Garfield responded with a joke about his time playing the superhero. “I was like, 'I once was when I was younger, yes. Twice was, three times was.'”
He said the woman became “a little bit teary-eyed” after realising she was sharing the lift with the actor. The pair went on to have what Garfield described as a “lovely conversation”.
“She was very cool. She was very chill, but she was sweet, very, very sweet,” he recalled.
Garfield added that he heard a “delightful kind of squeal” from the lift after he left, suggesting the encounter had made a lasting impression on the fan.
The actor played Peter Parker in The Amazing Spider-Man (2012) and The Amazing Spider-Man 2 (2014), before returning to the role in Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021), alongside Tom Holland and Tobey Maguire.
During the interview, Garfield also discussed his own experiences of meeting people he admires, naming Woody Harrelson as someone who still leaves him “starstruck”.
Garfield recalled playing basketball with Harrelson and their respective groups of friends, explaining that his excitement affected his performance.
“I was so excited, but I was so overwhelmed and starstruck that I froze and I played really, really badly,” he said.
Garfield described the experience as “brutal”, but called it “a small price to pay” for playing basketball with one of his heroes.

title: Brennan seals third PGA Tour title in Japan
description: The American cards a three under par 68 to edge Bridgeman and Mitchell by one stroke
content:
The American cards a three-under-par 68 to edge Bridgeman and Mitchell by one stroke
Michael Brennan kept his cool to hold off a chasing pack that included two-time major champion Xander Schauffele for victory Sunday at the Baycurrent Classic in Japan.
The 24-year-old claimed his third title on the US PGA Tour and second of the year after emerging from a tight field at Yokohama Country Club.
He carded a three-under-par 68 to finish on 16-under, one stroke clear of fellow Americans Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell.
Brennan, who had four birdies and one bogey in his final round, admitted he was nervous after starting the day in a share of the lead.
"Maybe I didn't have full control over how I felt but I was more calm today than I have been in weeks past when I've been in contention," he said.
"I tried to start the round and treat it as best I could like any other round, and I felt like I did a really good job of that."
Brennan got his debut win at the Bank of Utah Championship a year ago and followed that up with another title at the Wyndham Championship in August.
He said his growing profile would not distract him.
"It's nice to hear that people think highly of my golf game but it's just my golf game that they know about me," said Brennan, who turned pro in 2024.
"Not that I think they're wrong, but it's just golf."
Defending champion Schauffele finished three shots behind Brennan after a final-day four-under-par 67.
The Tokyo Olympics champion from 2021 was in the mix until a double bogey on the final hole ended his challenge.
Schauffele said he had "no regrets on being aggressive trying to get myself in a spot to win".
"I definitely played good enough golf to win this tournament," said the American, whose win last year in Japan was his most recent on the PGA Tour.
"Overall I think I struck it well and hit a lot of quality shots throughout the week, which was a nice thing to see after a downtick year in approach."
Bridgeman pushed Brennan even closer, trailing the leader by one stroke going into the final hole.
Bridgeman was looking for back-to-back titles after winning in his previous outing, the Biltmore Championship in September.
But a missed birdie putt on the 17th cost him, and Brennan held his nerve on the last hole to clinch victory.
"It was nice to know I had two putts on the 18th green," said Brennan.
"But it was a nervous tee shot, that's for sure."
Japan's Hideki Matsuyama finished on nine-under in front of his home fans.
Three-time major winner Jordan Spieth finished on 11-under after a final-day 67.
Spieth was looking for his first win on the tour since April 2022.
Two-time major champion Collin Morikawa, the 2024 champion in Japan, finished on six-under.

title: Bezzecchi wins in Indonesia
description: The Spaniard edges Marquez by two points
content:
The Spaniard edges Marquez by two points
Marco Bezzecchi stormed to victory in Indonesia on Sunday as Jorge Martin was third to retake the lead from Marc Marquez in the MotoGP world championship.
The Italian Bezzecchi, riding an Aprilia, made his move on pole-sitter Raul Fernandez in the final third of a captivating grand prix at a sweltering Mandalika International Circuit.
Spain's Fernandez came home second and compatriot Martin third, also riding Aprilia bikes.
Ducati's reigning seven-time world champion Marquez finished sixth.
That meant Martin retook the lead in the championship from Marquez by two points, with five more race weekends after this.
Bezzecchi is still alive in the championship title hunt in third.
"It's amazing, I'm very, very happy," said Bezzecchi, who sits on 309 points in the standings.
Martin is top with 355, with Marquez on his tail on 353.
"Very happy to be back on the top step of the podium. It was a nice battle with Raul (Fernandez) and I think me and all my team deserve a result like this.
"They have been through tough times with me," said Bezzecchi, who last won a grand prix in May.
Martin, who will head to Australia in a fortnight with the most slender of leads, said he had done all he could.
"I did the maximum," said Martin, who started alongside title rival Marquez on the second row of the grid.
"I did my best. At the start I lost a lot of positions but tried to be calm and was overtaking riders step by step.
He added: "We are still in the fight and still in the lead."
Fernandez, having to improvise to brake after fracturing two fingers in Saturday's sprint, got away cleanly from his first-ever pole.
He and Bezzecchi, who started alongside him on the grid, had clashed and crashed out in the sprint.
The sprint was won by Marquez to grab the championship lead for the first time from compatriot Martin.
After a third of the 27 laps in the grand prix, Fernandez kept the fellow Aprilia of Bezzecchi at bay despite his injury.
Former world champion Martin was running third, with Marquez looming in fifth without ever really threatening.
Fernandez, who had two previous victories, kept his cool under tremendous pressure from Bezzecchi until lap 19, when the Italian made his move to grasp the lead.
Bezzecchi streaked away from there to win by 4.260sec as Fernandez gamely hung on for second.

title: Seixas becomes youngest Giro di Lombardia winner
description: Enric Mas finishes second while Italy   s Giulio Ciccone takes third
content:
Enric Mas finishes second while Italy’s Giulio Ciccone takes third
French prodigy Paul Seixas ended his breakout season as a history-making Monument winner with a "dream" victory at the Giro di Lombardia on Saturday.
At 20 years and 16 days, Seixas became the youngest ever winner of the Classic of the Falling Leaves and the fourth-youngest winner of a Monument.
"It's crazy, I don't think I realise it. Everything went perfect," said a delighted Seixas.
"My team-mates did a great, awesome job. They all pushed more than what they had to do.
"I had amazing legs, I had the feeling today was a great day. I managed to make the difference at the moment I wanted to."
And he added that "it was a dream" to win this race.
Vuelta a Espana champion Enric Mas took second place, 48sec back, with Italian Giulio Ciccone rounding out the podium just over a minute behind the winner.
Seixas launched a devastating attack on the Civiglio climb with around 19km of the 239km one-day classic remaining, and within a kilometre, he had dropped all of his remaining challengers.
Olympic and European champion Remco Evenepoel was the first to flounder, followed shortly by pre-race favourite Isaac Del Toro and then world champion Brandon McNulty.
Evenepoel and McNulty eventually came home in fourth and fifth.
With cycling superstar Tadej Pogacar, the winner of the last five editions of Lombardia, missing due to injury, Seixas took his chance to end an incredible season as a Monument winner.
It was only his third ever Monument -- the five most prestigious one-day classics on the calendar -- having finished seventh at Lombardia last year and second at Liege-Bastogne-Liege in April.
This success completes a remarkable first full season in the professional ranks for Seixas.
He was fourth at the Tour de France -- his debut Grand Tour -- in July, having won the Tour of the Basque Country and La Fleche Wallonne earlier in the year.
He had also impressed in second-placed finishes at Strade Bianche, Liege and the Montreal GP.
But he endured a disappointing world championships last month, cramping up in the final stages and finishing 15th, although a week earlier he had won the time-trial bronze medal behind specialists Evenepoel and Filippo Ganna.
The race started five minutes behind schedule as the riders staged a brief protest to draw attention to safety concerns following a series of incidents involving vehicles on race routes.
With the dominant Pogacar missing, it promised to be a thrilling race.
Inside the final 60km, American Matteo Jorgenson and McNulty led a dangerous counter-attack behind the day's breakaway.
Evenepoel's Red Bull-Bora Hansgrohe team-mate Giulio Pellizzari led the chase and controlled the gap, ensuring the five counter-attackers were brought back 15km later.
With 20km left, the breakaway riders had around 30sec on the peloton, now driven by McNulty's UAE Emirates XRG team-mate Adam Yates.
Seixas then upped the pace and soon passed the remaining breakaway riders, while dropping Evenepoel and Del Toro.
With 2km to go to the top of the Civiglio climb, only Tom Pidcock and Ciccone were able to follow Seixas.
But within another 500 metres, and still 18km to ride, he was alone.
Seixas had around 30sec over Ciccone and Mas over the top with the likes of Evenepoel, Del Toro and McNulty more than a minute adrift.
Pidcock came home sixth, with Spanish veteran Pello Bilbao taking an impressive seventh place in his final race.

title: Govt defends K P emergency  alleges PTI KP govt   s    nexus    with terrorists
description: Federal ministers Azam Nazeer Tarar  Mohsin Naqvi  Attaullah Tarar address a press conference on K P emergency
content:
Federal ministers accuse PTI-led KP govt of failing to cooperate in anti-terror fight
The federal government on Sunday levelled a series of allegations against the PTI-led Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government, accusing it of failing to cooperate in the fight against terrorism and alleging a “nexus” with terrorist groups, as it defended its decision to impose an emergency in the province.
President Asif Ali Zardari signed off on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's recommendation to impose emergency rule in K-P amid a deteriorating security situation and the provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism.
Speaking at a press conference alongside Interior Minister Naqvi, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and other officials, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said President Zardari had declared an emergency under Articles 232(1) and 234(1) of the Constitution.
Azam said Naqvi would explain the circumstances that led to the decision.
Explaining the background to the decision, he said it had not been an easy step and that he had personally remained involved in back-channel contacts to secure cooperation from the provincial government.
“I would certainly like to explain the background. Today has not been an easy day,” Naqvi said, adding that efforts had continued for a month to bring the K-P government on board.
He said he had personally remained in contact with the provincial government during the process, while discussions were also taking place over the planned long march and other matters.
He said all of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s demands, including meetings and medical treatment, were being addressed even before the party’s planned long march. Talks with opposition leaders had also been scheduled before PM Shehbaz visited New York, but no final response had been received from them, he added.
He said the government had decided to form a committee and arrange a meeting on September 15 or 16, but received no response. Despite that, he said, contacts continued.
Naqvi said a meeting had also taken place between the president and the prime minister, during which he suggested bringing the K-P government on board.

He added that a draft was revised four times the following day, but when the matter appeared to have been finalised, the government learned that a new draft had arrived.
Naqvi said the government had made repeated attempts to reach an understanding with Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) leaders, with the final contact taking place at 11.45pm the previous night. “I told them that even at that point, something could still be done, but there was no response,” he said.
He said the government had proposed a paragraph during negotiations but received no reply. He added that Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman had also met the prime minister.
Naqvi said the government had never demanded that PTI call off its planned sit-in, adding that its primary concern had been terrorism. “Our issue was only terrorism,” he said, adding that the government had remained in contact with PTI leaders and had itself initiated contact with the party on previous occasions.
He said the condition to postpone the long march had come from the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), not his ministry. Naqvi said the security situation in K-P had deteriorated significantly.
خیبر پختونخوا کے 12 اضلاع میں حالات انتہائی خراب ہیں، وفاقی وزیر داخلہ محسن نقوی #KPK #ProvincialSitutation #MohsinNaqvi #Security #LawAndOrder pic.twitter.com/EDLSap3b6u
The interior minister said the security situation in 12 districts of the province had deteriorated to the extent that residents could not venture outside their homes after sunset. A senior Election Commission official had been martyred, police personnel were being targeted in repeated attacks, and Customs officials and security forces were also coming under attack, he added.
He also referred to the death of an Election Commission official the previous day, citing it as an indication of the security challenges facing the province. The interior minister said he had held several meetings with K-P chief minister, during which terrorism had been the main subject of discussion.
According to Naqvi, he had asked CM Afridi about plans to strengthen police in affected districts. He said the chief minister had cited a lack of funds, to which he had responded that the federal government would provide the required resources. Naqvi further claimed that provincial representatives had agreed during negotiations that emergency measures should be introduced in certain districts.
He said the government had struggled to secure public support for its position and claimed that provincial representatives had reservations about having photographs of meetings released publicly. Naqvi said he had never asked them to pose for photographs or make them public.
The minister said the federal government could not continue losing security personnel to terrorism while the provincial government failed to take ownership of the fight. “Terrorism cannot be fought alone under any circumstances; it requires a collective effort,” he said.
Naqvi said the federal government and the K-P government had jointly drawn up a plan to strengthen the police in five districts initially, gradually withdraw the Frontier Constabulary and army, and provide all required funds.
However, he said, no progress had been made at the provincial level despite the passage of four months.
“The foreign policy of the federation and a province cannot be different,” he said, adding that the provincial government’s dealings with the Taliban were no secret.
He said terrorist incidents had increased by 195 per cent and fatalities by 113pc over the past year and a half. He also criticised the provincial government for taking credit for the Rs20 billion budget allocated to the police while debating the definition of a terrorist.
Naqvi said the federal government had been left with no alternative but to take the decision to protect the state if security personnel were to continue being killed daily and the provincial government refused to take ownership of the fight against terrorism.
Naqvi described the emergency as a difficult decision taken after repeated attempts to avert the situation. He claimed that 518 police personnel had been killed over the preceding 18 months.
He said the situation could have been different if the provincial government had agreed to the proposals the previous night, adding that the federal government had been compelled to take the measures.
Law minister blames lack of cooperation for K-P emergency
Law Minister Azam said the prime minister had briefed President Zardari on the circumstances outlined by the interior minister. He said the K-P governor had submitted a report to the federal government as part of his constitutional responsibilities.
He said the federal government had decided to impose an emergency in the province under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution after a reported 196 per cent increase in terrorist incidents over the past two to two-and-a-half years.
Addressing the presser, Azam said the federal cabinet had held a detailed meeting lasting more than two hours, during which relevant institutions presented their reports. He said the K-P governor had also conveyed information to the federal government that was “very alarming”.
The minister said the governor had fulfilled his constitutional responsibility under Article 234, which provides for action when a provincial government’s functioning results in a constitutional breakdown and the government’s writ is no longer visible.
پی ٹی آئی نے مذاکرات کے دوران مثبت ردِعمل نہیں دیا، وفاقی وزیر قانون اعظم نذیر تارڑ #PTI #Negotiations #PoliticalTalks pic.twitter.com/Xdjz2GGoLB
He said the provincial government had been prioritising politics instead of addressing the protection of people’s lives and property, the province’s well-being and Pakistan’s interests.
Azam said reports presented to the federal cabinet showed that reported terrorist incidents had increased by 196 per cent over the past two to two-and-a-half years. The frequency of attacks had risen from one incident every two to three days to around three incidents, he added.
He said the number of people martyred or injured, along with damage to installations and vehicles, had also increased significantly.
The minister said one of the conditions was that the provincial government should fight terrorism with commitment alongside the federal government and the armed forces. However, he said, the trend of attacks showed that the armed forces, K-P police and innocent civilians were among the main targets.
“Instead of coming together and proceeding with resolve, there was reluctance,” he said.
Azam said the federal government and the president had acted within the bounds of the Constitution, whose provisions had been incorporated by the framers of the 1973 Constitution to ensure that the federation and its constituent units functioned together.
He referred to Article 149(4), which, he said, empowered the federal government to issue directions to provinces in matters concerning peace and tranquillity and the safety of the country. Failure to implement such directions could also have consequences, he added.
The minister also referred to Article 232, which provides for the imposition of an emergency in circumstances involving internal threats to provincial security or the threat of foreign aggression.
“What is happening on the border with our neighbouring country — the border is on fire — and what is happening internally in the country is not hidden from you,” he said, adding that both conditions had arisen.
He said efforts had continued to resolve the situation, including an attempt on Saturday, but the circumstances remained unchanged.
“Against this background, after detailed discussions, the president, on the advice of the prime minister, exercised his powers under Articles 232 and 234 to impose an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” he said.
Azam explained that Article 232 dealt with the imposition of an emergency, while action under Article 234 was generally referred to as governor’s rule. However, he said, the situation was so grave and exceptional that the requirements of both constitutional provisions had been invoked.
Referring to the first proclamation issued by the president, the minister said it cited a rise in extremist activities and terrorist attacks to an unprecedented level of violent intensity, posing a grave threat to the lives and property of people in K-P.
He added that the proclamation also noted that the effects of the situation were spreading to other parts of the country.
Azam further said the Sydney-based Terrorist-Affected Countries Index had, for the first time, ranked Pakistan as the country most affected by terrorism.
He questioned how the country could attract foreign investment and sustain economic activity amid such security conditions.
“On one side, we talk about running the economy and attracting foreign investment, but who will come in this situation?” he asked.
He said the president had declared the emergency on the prime minister’s advice. Azam also said the provincial government had been rendered inactive under the measures and that the governor had been directed to exercise his constitutional powers.
He said an 11-member advisory committee had been formed and a secretariat established for 12 districts, from where reports would be sent directly to the federal government.
According to Azam, a council had also been established, with the additional chief secretary to oversee its functioning. He added that officials holding relevant positions had been rendered inactive and that the military had been deployed under Article 245 of the Constitution.
Separately, Information Minister Attaullah alleged that the PTI’s links extended to terrorist groups and that the party was not serious about eliminating terrorism.
He claimed that the PTI-led provincial government had a deep nexus with terrorists, pushing the province’s administrative situation to the brink of collapse.
Attaullah said reports from the Intelligence Bureau and law enforcement agencies had described the situation in the province as extremely alarming.
پی ٹی آئی کو شہداء کے خاندانوں سے کچھ سیکھنا چاہیے تھا، وفاقی وزیر اطلاعات عطا اللہ تارڑ #MartyrsFamilies #AttaullahTarar #TributeToMartyrs @TararAttaullah pic.twitter.com/uBtDyhoM0H
He alleged that political parties other than the PTI had faced terrorist attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and claimed that the relationship between terrorists and the PTI had reached the stage of power-sharing.
According to the information minister, terrorists had been given safe access to the province and had also received financial resources.
He said the provincial government had a constitutional responsibility to protect the lives and property of ordinary citizens, questioning whether it was unable or unwilling to discharge that duty.
Attaullah alleged that the same elements responsible for destroying peace in the province, killing civilians and targeting hospitals, mosques, police stations and security personnel had been empowered by the K-P government.
خیبر پختونخوا میں گورنر کی سربراہی میں 11 رکنی ایڈوائزری کونسل قائم، وفاقی وزیر اطلاعات عطا اللہ تارڑ #AdvisoryCouncil #KPK #GovernerKPK #Governance pic.twitter.com/CgxnMl1DD3
He claimed that a formula for sharing authority between terrorists and the PTI-led provincial government had been taking shape, beginning in the southern districts and gradually spreading across the province.
Recalling a visit to a hospital in Kohat, he claimed injured people had asked him to help them get rid of the PTI government, warning that it would destroy them and saying they wanted to fight the terrorists.
The information minister questioned why terrorists had been given a free hand in the province. He said maintaining law and order and ensuring public safety and security were the provincial government’s responsibilities.
He alleged that the PTI government had not only facilitated terrorists but had also made them partners in provincial administration.
دہشت گردوں اور پی ٹی آئی حکومت کے درمیان پاور شیئرنگ تک بات پہنچ چکی تھی، وفاقی وزیر اطلاعات عطا اللہ تارڑ #AttaullahTarar #KPKGovernment #PowerSharing @TararAttaullah pic.twitter.com/ap5IFaAcuW
According to Attaullah, the alleged nexus had resulted in several districts being handed over to terrorists, who continued to target civilians and mosques and bomb hospitals.
He described the Taliban as elements operating on foreign funding and seeking to push Pakistan towards destruction.
“If someone receives foreign funding, kills our citizens, damages their lives and property, and a provincial government sits with them, facilitates them and makes them partners in government affairs, what could be a greater constitutional crisis?” he asked.
The minister said the provincial government’s mandate was to protect citizens and ensure security and law and order, but it had instead introduced a controversial police-related bill that, he alleged, sought to create a pathway for people associated with terrorist groups to join the police force.
He questioned why direct appointments at the deputy superintendent of police (DSP) level were being made, alleging that the objective was to accommodate terrorists and their supporters in the police force.
The province was being gradually pushed towards destruction, he said, claiming that there was incontrovertible evidence to support his allegations.
Questioning the performance of the K-P cabinet, Attaullah said its members might be seen on television talk shows, but the chief minister’s performance in governance needed to be examined.
He questioned how much time the chief minister had devoted to governance and whether he understood the requirements of running a government and improving the province’s prosperity.
Ataullah said the province had now been freed from what he described as the group responsible for its deteriorating situation.
Responding to a question, he said the PTI-led provincial government had been removed through constitutional means. He held the party responsible for the deaths of thousands of people in K-P, alleging that its policies were based on support for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Afghanistan (TTA).
He also alleged that the PTI government’s conduct in K-P reflected aspects of the Taliban’s policies towards women, with women’s rights being violated in the province.

title: Shelton dumped out in Shanghai third round
description: Gea claims the biggest win of his career with a 7 6  7 5   7 6  7 3  victory over Shelton
content:
Gea claims the biggest win of his career with a 7-6 (7/5), 7-6 (7/3) victory over Shelton
World number 56 Arthur Gea stunned Ben Shelton in straight sets in the third round of the Shanghai Masters on Sunday as the US Open finalist became the biggest casualty so far.
The 21-year-old Frenchman beat Shelton 7-6 (7/5), 7-6 (7/3) for the biggest win of his career.
"I got outplayed today," world number four Shelton told reporters.
"My body wasn't ready," he said, playing in Shanghai as his first tournament since the US Open, apart from the Davis Cup last month.
He skipped the Japan Open that ended last week due to fitness concerns.
"That's just the way this tour is sometimes," he said, adding that jet lag had also taken a toll.
Gea will play either Francisco Cerundolo or Jakub Mensik next.
"Amazing, to be honest," he said after his first win over a top-10 player.
He said his game was "all about focus, concentration" and staying "ready for every point".
Gea added that he has been "more confident on court" following a breakout year that saw him clinch his first professional title in July at a 250-level event in Los Cabos.
He stormed to a 5-3 lead in the first set before the 24-year-old American Shelton came back fighting, levelling to 5-5 with a clutch backhand volley at the net.
The two players were neck and neck in the tie-break until Gea sneaked ahead to win the first set point.
Third seed Shelton forced his way into another tie-break in the second set as the match went past two hours, but faltered as a charging Gea clinched victory at his first chance.

title: Henderson brace inspires Chelsea rout
description: The Blues thrash Bournemouth 5 1 as Henderson strikes twice
content:
The Blues thrash Bournemouth 5-1 as Henderson strikes twice
Xabi Alonso praised Jordan Henderson after the Chelsea midfielder rolled back the years with a double in the 5-1 demolition of Bournemouth on Saturday.
Henderson took just 68 seconds to put Chelsea ahead at Stamford Bridge with his first goal for the club.
The 36-year-old set the tone for Chelsea's stroll in the west London sunshine with a precise finish from Cole Palmer's pass.
Henderson turned provider two minutes later as his pass reached Morgan Rogers, whose shot deflected in off Antonio Silva.
It was the second-fastest goal and assist combo in Premier League history.
Joao Pedro struck twice, either side of Evanilson's reply for Bournemouth, before Henderson capped his impressive performance in the 70th minute.
Henderson whipped a superb free-kick past Bournemouth goalkeeper Djordje Petrovic to the delight of Chelsea fans, who urged the hat-trick chasing midfielder to shoot every time he got the ball in the closing stages.
The former Liverpool captain's influential display came in just his second appearance for Chelsea following his close-season arrival on a free transfer.
Alonso had made Henderson one of his top targets to add experience to a largely youthful side following the England international's departure from Brentford at the end of last season.
"We signed him for everything and if he is able to score two beauties like today we are more than happy for him," Alonso said.
"Apart from the goals he has done many good things. He was always involved in the action, giving instructions to the team-mates, he needs to communicate a lot. It was a very good midfield performance."
After failing to win any of their previous three league games -- including a dismal 3-0 loss at Brentford before the international break -- this was a much-needed result for Alonso.
The Spaniard is in his first season in charge but can expect scrutiny if he fails to assemble a cohesive unit from Chelsea's expensively assembled squad.
"Today was a very complete performance, we were in control for most of the game. We had good stability," Alonso said.
"Overall happy with the game, many positives to take for the future and we have to keep going."
The former Real Madrid boss was surprised to see Chelsea strike twice in the first three minutes, adding: "We always try to start the game with good energy, but I have no explanation, no credit to me.
"It has never happened to me to score so many early goals. Let's see if we can keep doing that.
"Maybe I prefer to score the first one in the last minute! It will happen one day."
Alonso's hopes of challenging for Champions League qualification and eventually competing for the Premier League title were boosted on Saturday when England forward Palmer signed a new contract keeping him at the club until 2034.
"Happy for him and very happy for the club as well. I'm sure the fans are happy to have Cole for years," Alonso said.
"We need to push, we need to help him to have success. He is important in what we are building.
"When you are young you want to keep the best ones for years. We believe Cole is going to be a top-class contract for many years. The longer he is here the better."

title: Real Madrid edge Villarreal  Vinicius sent off
description: Diomande s second half strike earns Real Madrid a 1 0 victory over Villarreal
content:
Diomande's second-half strike earns Real Madrid a 1-0 victory over Villarreal
Yan Diomande earned Real Madrid a tight 1-0 victory over Villarreal on Saturday to keep them six points behind La Liga leaders Barcelona, even though winger Vinicius Junior was sent off for hair-pulling.
Brazil international Vinicius, on as a substitute, scored but his goal was disallowed and then he was dismissed after a VAR review showed he pulled the hair of Villarreal's Nathan Saliba.
Jose Mourinho's Madrid battled through the final stages with 10 men but held on to win and go provisionally third.
Champions Barca lead La Liga after a 3-0 win over Getafe, while Atletico Madrid are five points behind in second after they edged Alaves 2-1.
Striker Kylian Mbappe was fit to start the match for Madrid at their Santiago Bernabeu stadium after suffering a knee problem playing for France during the international break.
There were a smattering of whistles for the superstar forward, with some fans believing he has been unprofessional in recent weeks, but also applause from other supporters.
Mbappe, a candidate for the Ballon d'Or trophy later this month, was Madrid's most threatening player in the first half, although he had little competition.
Mourinho started with out-of-form winger Vinicius on the bench, following his trips to Australia and India with Brazil during the international break.
Madrid improved defensively, giving Villarreal few chances of note, but struggled to build much in attack themselves in a drab opening half.
Mbappe struck the post from Alvaro Carreras's lay-off as Madrid pushed Villarreal back early on.
Villarreal soon gained a foothold and restricted Madrid's opportunities, until Mbappe forced a good save from Peter Gulacsi.
There was some more mild whistling for Madrid's display from their fans at half-time, but soon they were able to celebrate summer arrival Diomande's first goal for the club.
The Ivorian winger, Madrid's record 140-million-euro ($157 million) signing, produced a sharp low finish into the far corner after good work from Federico Valverde to play him in.
Vinicius thought he had doubled Madrid's lead after Jude Bellingham charged in down the left and cut the ball back for him.
However the winger's joy turned to anger after referee Isidro Diaz de Mera was called to watch Vinicius's hair pull on Saliba in the build-up by VAR and sent off the Brazilian, voiding his goal.
Madrid's Belgian goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, who had made a couple of smart saves earlier in the half, produced an acrobatic stop to thwart Carlos Romero.
Mbappe was denied again by Hungarian goalkeeper Gulasci as the forward left the Bernabeu frustrated in his hunt for goals, although his team were able to clinch three important points to stay on Barca's trail.

title: Funding crunch threatens Olympic wrestling
description: PWF seeks Rs30 million to prepare three wrestlers for qualification campaign
content:
PWF seeks Rs30 million to prepare three wrestlers for qualification campaign
Pakistan has considerable wrestling talent but a lack of facilities, financial assistance and international exposure has stunted the sport’s growth and hampered the country’s Olympic ambitions.
Pakistan has failed to qualify a wrestler for the Olympics for decades, with limited state patronage and inadequate participation in international competitions undermining its athletes’ chances of improving their rankings and securing qualification.
With the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics approaching, Pakistan Wrestling Federation (PWF) says a lack of resources remains the biggest obstacle to its qualification campaign.
“We have a bunch of wrestlers who can qualify for the Los Angeles Games if the state provides assistance. We will need Rs30 million to prepare our top three wrestlers, including Inayatullah, Abdullah and Mohammad Gulzar,” PWF secretary Mohammad Inam told The Express Tribune.
Inam said that the amount would cover international exposure, including participation in the rankings series, Asian Championships and World Championships, while the federation would try to arrange training through its own resources.
“We are already late in our Olympic qualification mission, as you need to plan for four years from one Olympics to the next,” he added.
Inam said the federation wished to send its leading wrestlers abroad for six months of training ahead of the Nagoya Asian Games but could not do so because of financial constraints.
Pakistan Sports Board (PSB) sponsored only two members of the wrestling squad for the Asian Games, while the federation paid for the remaining three, he said.
“Last year, we were given Rs3 million by the PSB as a grant, while this year we have not been given even a single penny,” Inam said, adding that the wrestlers’ departments had also declined to provide financial support.
The federation is struggling to meet even its administrative expenses, he said, noting that attracting sponsors remained difficult without major international medals.
Despite the challenges, Inam believes Pakistan can still qualify for Los Angeles if financial assistance is provided and preparations begin immediately.
“We are in talks with Kyrgyzstan to explore training opportunities, but we will still need money for the wrestlers’ air tickets and accommodation. The hosts would provide the training facilities,” he said.
No Pakistani wrestler has received an International Olympic Committee (IOC) scholarship for the current cycle, further complicating preparations.
Under the Los Angeles 2028 wrestling qualification system, places will be available through the World Championships, the United World Wrestling (UWW) rankings series, continental championships and Olympic qualification tournaments.
The qualification process is due to begin in February 2027, making timely financial support crucial if Pakistan is to give its leading wrestlers a realistic chance of reaching the Games.
Inam, a former beach wrestling world champion, urged the authorities to support the federation’s plans, warning that continued financial constraints could deprive Pakistan’s wrestlers of a valuable opportunity to compete at the Olympics.
Wrestling has a huge talent and in recent years the country has delivered extremely well especially at the Commonwealth Games.
Pakistan had impressed in the 2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games with multiple medals. However this year’s Glasgow Commonwealth Games did not feature wrestling and Pakistan could only bring one bronze in boxing.
National grapplers need consistent support from the state which is the only source which can put the country’s wrestling on the path of progression.
Wrestlers mostly earn through mud-wrestling and this is also the biggest hurdle and it obstructs their performance when they come to mat-wrestling which needs more speed and agility. But there is no alternative as wrestlers need to earn their livelihood.
There is the biggest need to promote Olympic wrestling and it would be the only way to go ahead in the discipline, otherwise
, it would be too tough to compete with the world’s best.

title: Shane Gillis swears on live  SNL  Dr  Seuss inspired sketch  apologises for slip up
description: Fellow performer Mikey Day improvised a response during the sketch inspired by  Green Eggs and Ham
content:
Fellow performer Mikey Day improvised a response during the sketch inspired by 'Green Eggs and Ham'
Shane Gillis accidentally dropped an F-bomb during a live episode of Saturday Night Live , prompting fellow performer Mikey Day to improvise a response during a sketch inspired by Green Eggs and Ham .
The incident occurred on Saturday night, with Andrew Dismukes playing Sam-I-Am, Day portraying a character refusing to try the food, and Gillis appearing as his son.
While explaining his father’s refusal, Gillis said, “Bro, it’s a nonstarter. He told me, he says he f**king doesn’t—”
Realising his mistake, Gillis quickly stopped and exclaimed, “Jeez!” as the audience reacted. After briefly regaining his composure, he continued: “He said I do not like green eggs and ham.”
Day then incorporated the slip into the sketch, telling Gillis in character, “You said a bad word.”
Shane Gillis accidentally saying the F bomb on SNL. pic.twitter.com/8R5B8Tc5qV
The exchange allowed the performers to acknowledge the mistake without abandoning the scene.
As the sketch ended, Gillis could be heard apologising, adding, “Sorry about earlier.” He also repeated his apology during the show’s goodnights.
The swear word was audible to viewers watching the live East Coast broadcast and on Peacock.
However, it was censored during the West Coast broadcast, which airs on a slight delay.
Accidental swearing has occurred on Saturday Night Live several times over the years.
Past incidents have involved Paul Shaffer in 1980, Charles Rocket in 1981 and Jenny Slate during her debut as a cast member in 2009.
Gillis’ slip also follows an incident on the October 18, 2025 episode, when Sabrina Carpenter reportedly swore twice while performing “Nobody’s Son”.
