title: Taylor Swift   s  The Life of a Showgirl  The Encore  ranks last in 2026 Metacritic album ratings
description: The album received a Metacritic score of 39 out of 100  placing it last among 237 albums released in 2026
content:
The album received a Metacritic score of 39 out of 100, placing it last among 237 albums released in 2026
Taylor Swift’s The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore has received a Metacritic score of 39 out of 100, placing it last among 237 albums released in 2026 that have received scores based on at least seven reviews, according to TV Fandom Lounge.
The four-track release has attracted criticism from several publications, with reviewers questioning its originality and creative direction.
The website also compared its reception with Katy Perry’s 143 , which scored 35 on Metacritic in 2024.
The Telegraph’s reviewer, who described themselves as a Swiftie, offered a critical assessment of the release, writing, “I’m a Swiftie, and even I think these new songs are terrible. The Life of a Showgirl: Encore Edition is just as derivative and flat as the original album.”
The Guardian also questioned Swift’s recurring lyrical themes, suggesting that her songwriting increasingly relies on familiar references and self-reflection.
Taylor Swift’s 'Showgirl: Encore' becomes second-worst-rated pop album of the decade on Metacritic
Meanwhile, The Independent criticised the track “Cleveland!”, describing its writing as “some of her worst writing”.
TV Fandom Lounge argues that Swift’s commercial success may have reduced the pressure to experiment creatively.
The publication also highlighted the multiple editions released for The Life of a Showgirl , estimating that collecting all 38 variants would cost $741.24.
Despite the critical response, the original album achieved a reported 4.002 million album-equivalent units in its first week, demonstrating Swift’s continued commercial reach.
The contrasting figures highlight the difference between critical reception and sales performance. While the Encore has attracted unfavourable reviews, its long-term commercial impact remains to be seen.

title: Keanu Reeves    stop motion Samurai film  Hidari  seeks new partner after US funding talks stall
description: The search began after the US company asked the Japanese studio behind the project to surrender all rights to the film
content:
The search began after the US company asked the Japanese studio behind the project to surrender all rights to the film
Keanu Reeves’ upcoming stop-motion samurai film Hidari is searching for a new financing partner after negotiations with a US company stalled over a proposed deal that would have required the Japanese studio behind the project to surrender all rights to the film.
Producer Matsumoto Noriko revealed the development during a session at the Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM), held alongside the Busan International Film Festival. Japan’s Dwarf Studios, which is developing the project with production partners Whatever and Tecarat, is now exploring alternative ways to finance the film while retaining control over its intellectual property.
According to Matsumoto, the US company had offered to cover the entire production budget in exchange for all rights. Although the offer provided a potential solution to the film’s financing needs, Dwarf wanted to retain 50 per cent of the rights and sought Japanese investment to help cover the remaining costs.
However, the negotiations could not progress after the people Matsumoto had been dealing with lost their jobs amid upheaval in Hollywood. The setback has left the studio looking for another partner willing to support the project without requiring it to relinquish ownership.
Hidari is directed by Kawamura Masashi and features Reeves as a voice actor. The stop-motion samurai project gained international attention after Dwarf produced a pilot short in 2023, financing part of the work through crowdfunding. The short helped bring Reeves on board and opened the door to further international interest.
The film has since been presented at the Annecy Animation Showcase in Cannes and at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival, helping raise its profile among potential international partners.
Questry chief executive Ibe Tomonobu has established a special-purpose company for Hidari , allowing Japanese and overseas investors to participate in financing the production. The arrangement is intended to provide an alternative to relying on a single international financier.
The project also highlights the challenges facing Japanese productions seeking international co-production deals. Matsumoto explained that stop-motion filmmaking can make such arrangements particularly difficult, as production work is not easily divided between countries to meet spending requirements attached to financing agreements.
Despite the stalled US negotiations, Dwarf Studios remains committed to finding collaborators for Hidari . The search for a new partner will be crucial to securing the film’s financing while allowing its creators to preserve control over the project.

title: PTI rejects emergency  governor s rule in K P as unconstitutional  vows to continue struggle
description: PTI chairman says party  strongly condemns  imposition of emergency in province   categorically rejects  the move
content:
Gohar calls it 'serious political mistake', says people will never accept such measures against their rights
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) leaders on Sunday condemned the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), describing the measures as unconstitutional and undemocratic, and vowing to continue their political struggle.
In posts on X, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and other party leaders rejected the measures, arguing that they undermined the province’s mandate, autonomy and democratic rights. They called for political dialogue and the protection of constitutional rights.
Barrister Gohar said the party “strongly condemns” the imposition of emergency in the province and “categorically rejects” the move, describing it as “an extremely concerning and serious political mistake” and an undemocratic step.
“The people will never accept such measures against their rights,” he said.
Gohar said the mandate of the people of K-P was their constitutional and legal right, adding that peace and stability could not be achieved by ignoring that mandate, weakening provincial autonomy or creating a confrontation between the federation and the province.
He said there was no disagreement over the need to eliminate terrorism, but the fight against militancy could not be used to suppress public voices, pursue political objectives or restrict the province’s constitutional powers.
چیئرمین پی ٹی آئی بیرسٹر گوہر خان کا خیبرپختونخوا میں ایمرجنسی کے نفاذ پر ردِعمل: ہم صوبے میں ایمرجنسی کے نفاذ کی شدید الفاظ میں مذمت کرتے ہیں اور اس اقدام کو یکسر مسترد کرتے ہیں۔ یہ ایک انتہائی تشویشناک اور سنگین سیاسی غلطی اور غیر جمہوری اقدام ہے- عوام اپنے حقوق کے خلاف ایسے… pic.twitter.com/DvY1lwWBI3
“Countering terrorism is possible only through national unity and a joint strategy,” he said.
Gohar added that weakening the provinces would not strengthen the federation, arguing that the solution to the country’s problems lay in political wisdom, constitutional supremacy, meaningful negotiations and practical measures rather than force, confrontation and extraordinary steps.
He said the party would raise its voice on every constitutional, legal and democratic forum to protect the public mandate, provincial autonomy and constitutional and democratic rights.
Gohar also urged the federal government to reconsider its decision, saying it could still be reversed within a few days.
He called on the federation to set aside its ego, understand ground realities, accept legitimate demands and respect public sentiments, warning that failure to do so would cause further political and economic damage and set back the democratic process.
“Reconsidering political decisions is not a sign of weakness but an indication of wisdom in the national interest,” he said, adding that otherwise, “there will be significant damage”.
Former federal minister Asad Umar also criticised the measures, saying Prime Minister Shehbaz and President Zardari had not merely signed off on governor’s rule and emergency in K-P but had initiated a process that could dismantle the existing system.
“Everyone is going to be buried in this political grave,” Umar said in his post on X, referring to political parties.
شہباز شریف اور زرداری نے پختون خواہ میں صرف گورنر راج اور ایمرجنسی پر دستخط نہیں کئے، اس نظام کو لپیٹنے کا سفر شروع کیا ہے۔ اس سیاسی قبر میں سب سیاسی جماعتوں کی تدفین ہونے جا رہی ہے۔
PTI K-P president Junaid Akbar said the party’s planned long march would proceed regardless of whether governor’s rule or martial law was imposed.
“Whether they impose governor’s rule or martial law, our long march will take place in every circumstance, God willing,” he said, adding that the participants had reached Swabi.
“Neither pressure can stop us, nor threats weaken our resolve,” Akbar said.
گورنر راج لگائیں یا مارشل لاء، ہمارا لانگ مارچ ان شاء اللہ ہر صورت ہوگا۔ صوابی پہنچے۔ نہ دباؤ ہمیں روک سکتا ہے، نہ دھمکیاں ہمارے عزم کو کمزور کر سکتی ہیں۔ ان شاء اللہ،
PTI leader Ali Muhammad Khan described the implementation of emergency in K-P as a “non-political move” by the federal government, saying it went against the mandate of millions of people in the province and the spirit of the federation.
“The emergency shall be removed as soon as possible, and K-P should be governed by the elected representatives of its people,” he said.
Ali added that all issues should be resolved through political dialogue rather than confrontation.
The implementation of emergency in Pakhtoonkhwa is a non political move by federal government. It’s against the mandate of the millions of people of Pakhtoonkhwa & the spirit of federation. The emergency shall be removed asap & let Pakhtoonkhwa be governed by the elected…
PTI Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram expressed concern over the reported targeting of Junaid Akbar, the party’s K-P president, through coercive legal measures.
In a post on X, Akram said the actions reflected a pattern of political victimisation. He said arresting or harassing elected leadership, particularly amid the current situation involving emergency and governor’s rule, undermined democratic principles and provincial rights.
He condemned the approach and called for adherence to the rule of law and due process, adding that political issues should be resolved through dialogue rather than repression.
The reported targeting of PTI KP President Junaid Akbar through coercive legal measures is deeply concerning and reflects a pattern of political victimisation. Arresting or harassing elected leadership, especially in the current climate of emergency and governor’s rule,…
Former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser also rejected the reported measures, declaring: “Governor’s rule is unacceptable, emergency is unacceptable.”
Qaiser condemned the measures and said he had consistently raised his voice against terrorism. He also questioned the federal government’s policies, which he said had contributed to the current situation.
He called for the implementation of the unanimous resolution adopted by the peace jirga, saying all political parties had agreed to it.
گورنر راج نامنظور، ایمرجنسی نامنظور! گورنر راج اور ایمرجنسی کے اقدامات کی بھرپور مذمت کرتے ہیں۔ ہم نے ہمیشہ دہشت گردی کے خلاف آواز اٹھائی ہے۔ وفاقی حکومت کی پالیسیوں پر سنجیدہ سوالات ہیں، جن کے باعث موجودہ حالات پیدا ہوئے۔ امن جرگے کی متفقہ قرارداد پر عمل درآمد کیا جائے، جس پر…
Qaiser said ignoring people’s fundamental rights and powers in important national matters was unacceptable, urging all political parties to speak up for the protection of K-P’s rights.
“This is a robbery on the constitutional rights of the province, which is unacceptable,” he said, adding that the party would continue its constitutional and democratic struggle.
Meanwhile, K-P Information Minister Shafi Jan claimed that Chief Minister Sohail Afridi has been arrested and called on people across the province to gather in Peshawar.
In a post on X, Jan said people from across K-P should head towards Peshawar, urging residents of Kohat to make their way to the provincial capital as well.
Jan said, “The people will now have to come out." The people of the tribal districts had a major responsibility, urging them to turn out in support of the chief minister, he added.
وزیر اعلی سہیل آفریدی کے گرفتار کر لیا گیا ۔ اب عوام کو نکلنا ھوگا ۔ پورے خیبر پختون خواہ پشاور کے طرف آئے ۔ کوہاٹ پشاور کے طرف رخ کرے ۔ قبائلی اضلاع کے عوام پر باری ذمہ داری عائد ھوتی ھے ۔قبائل اپنے وزیر اعلیٰ کے لیے نکلنا ھوگا ۔جہاں عوام جمع ھوگی وہاں مجھے اپنے درمیان پائینگے۔
“The tribal people must come out for their chief minister,” he said.

title: Jack Doherty faces 6 month social media ban after signing cryptocurrency casino deal without reviewing terms
description: Doherty said he had signed the contract without reading the conditions  initially believing the restriction was a joke
content:
Doherty said he had signed the contract without reading the conditions, initially believing the restriction was a joke
YouTuber Jack Doherty could face a six-month social media blackout after signing a sponsorship agreement with cryptocurrency casino Shuffle.com without fully reviewing its terms.
The controversy emerged on October 20, when Doherty revealed on X that the agreement could prevent him from posting online.
Admitting his mistake, the influencer wrote, “Hey guys, I think I actually f***ed up.”
Doherty said he had signed the contract without carefully reading the conditions and initially believed the restriction was a joke.
He is now working with a lawyer to challenge the agreement, while Shuffle has indicated that it intends to enforce the deal.
The dispute reportedly began after Shuffle's official X account posted an offer on September 28, stating, “at this point we will pay you to shut the f**k up.”
On October 7, Doherty discussed seeking sponsorship opportunities following disappointing performance from a Solana memecoin associated with him.
He wrote that he needed to “get my money up somehow”, prompting Shuffle to describe its earlier offer as “legit”.
Shuffle co-founder Noah Dummett subsequently confirmed the agreement's six-month term, writing, “For everyone asking:- yes it's real- 6 month term” adding that it was "money well spent to get this mf off the internet".

The reported restriction could extend into April 2027, depending on when the term began. However, the complete contract has not been made public, leaving its precise conditions unclear.
The story has prompted widespread online debate, with some users questioning whether the arrangement is genuine or a publicity stunt.
For now, Doherty's return to social media remains uncertain as the legal dispute continues.

title: Hundreds rally outside US Capitol to demand arms embargo against Israel
description: Protesters mark 3 years since the beginning of Gaza genocide  demand sanctions  arms embargo
content:
Protesters mark 3 years since the beginning of Gaza genocide, demand sanctions, arms embargo
Hundreds of pro-Palestinian demonstrators rallied outside the US Capitol on Saturday to demand an end to Israel's genocide in the Gaza Strip as well as a US arms embargo and sanctions on Israel.
Protesters waved Palestinian flags and carried large signs denouncing the genocide in Gaza and Israel's occupation of Palestinian territories. Some signs drew attention to the economic costs of US wars, linking military spending to high prices and low wages at home.
Organised by the Palestinian Youth Movement and other pro-Palestinian groups, the rally and march marked three years since the start of Israel's military offensive in Gaza in October 2023.
Urging renewed pressure on Washington for its military and diplomatic support for Israel, organisers demanded an “absolute arms embargo and sanctions” on Israel.
Nouhad Akkar of the Palestinian Youth Movement told Anadolu that the demonstrators are determined to hold elected officials accountable for US military assistance to Israel.
“We will not let this genocide be normalised,” she said. “We are sending a message to our people in Gaza, to our people in the region, that we will continue to fight for them, not just for an end to the genocide, but until total liberation and return.”
Read: One year after ceasefire, Gaza’s promised ‘day after’ has yet to arrive
Akkar also urged public institutions to divest from weapons manufacturers supplying Israel. She said her group is campaigning for the state retirement system in Virginia, where many Washington federal government workers live, to withdraw more than $394 million in pension investments in such companies.
“We would like to see elected officials take a stand against the investment of this money,” she said.
Isabella Javidan of the National Iranian American Council linked Israel's offensive in Gaza to military operations in Lebanon and Iran, accusing US lawmakers and defense contractors of enabling violence across the region.
“These are not isolated tragedies. They are not separate; they are expressions of the same imperialist project,” she told the crowd.
Javidan said members of Congress have “repeatedly chosen death over diplomacy, military domination over basic human dignity, and the interests of the war industry over the lives of millions.”
She said lawmakers should recognise that decisions on weapons shipments, military funding, and sanctions have consequences for civilians.
Among the demonstrators, Erik W., who requested that only his first name be used, told Anadolu that he opposes politicians invoking the safety of Jewish Americans to justify arming Israel.
“For me personally, as a Jewish American, I feel like there are a lot of people in government who are speaking on my behalf and are justifying arming a genocide,” he said.
Read more: 1,000 days of Gaza genocide: Israel killed 265 journalists including 27 women, wounded nearly 500 others
“I think arming Israel does not combat antisemitism,” he added, arguing that Israel's actions are harming perceptions of Judaism.
His sign read: “No genocide in our name.” He demanded an immediate arms embargo and urged people not to shy away from describing events in Gaza as genocide and ethnic cleansing.
A discussion with Palestinian political figure Mustafa Barghouti and writer Jehad Abusalim was scheduled to follow the march.
The protest rally took place just weeks before Nov. 3 midterm elections for the US Congress, whose lawmakers must vote to approve any military aid to Israel.
The elections are coming amid growing US public disapproval of Israel’s actions, as well as loud calls for an end to Washington's “business as usual” support for Israel.

title: Shane Gillis     SNL  monologue falls flat as jokes about Hitler and women draw few laughs
description: Several jokes  including remarks about women s gym clothing  prompted groans rather than laughter from the audience
content:
Several jokes, including remarks about women's gym clothing, prompted groans rather than laughter from the audience
Shane Gillis received a mixed response to his latest Saturday Night Live monologue, as the comedian returned to host the NBC sketch show for the third time since his controversial departure in 2019.
Gillis, 38, opened his monologue in a black T-shirt and trousers, discussing his weight, experiences at the gym and discomfort while hiking.
Several jokes, including remarks about women's gym clothing, prompted groans rather than laughter from the studio audience.
Gillis also joked about his receding hairline and compared his hairstyle to that of Adolf Hitler, delivering the punchline: "You’re either gay or you’re Hitler, and isn’t that where we’re at as a country?" The joke received limited laughter before the monologue ended.
Gillis has demonstrated his comedic abilities through stand-up specials and other hosting appearances, although his SNL monologues have proved more challenging.
His relationship with the programme began in September 2019, when he was announced as a new cast member alongside Chloe Fineman and Bowen Yang.
Five days later, NBC dismissed him after resurfaced podcast clips showed him mocking Asians and using anti-gay slurs.
Gillis subsequently built a career outside the show through stand-up comedy, podcasting and acting.
He created and starred in the Netflix series Tires and secured a role in the upcoming biopic Madden .
Despite the initial controversy, SNL creator Lorne Michaels later welcomed Gillis back as a host.
His first hosting appearance in 2024 also attracted criticism for its monologue, although sketches such as "CouplaBeers" received a more positive response.
His latest appearance has again highlighted the mixed reception to his comedy on the long-running programme.

title: Indian capital braces for second day of protests against poll chief
description: Cockroach Janta Party founder  other leaders released from detention on condition of  no breach of peace  for one year
content:
Cockroach Janta Party founder, other leaders released from detention on condition of 'no breach of peace' for one year
New Delhi braced for a second day of youth protests demanding the resignation of India's election chief on Sunday, ​as a court ordered the release of "cockroach" movement founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other senior leaders.
Dipke, the founder of ‌the Cockroach Janta Party, and the other leaders were detained when their plane landed in Delhi on Saturday as the movement planned to gather thousands of people at Jantar Mantar in Central Delhi.
They were produced in front of a magistrate early on Sunday.
"Condition - no breach of peace for one year," ​the CJP's legal head Ratna Singh said in a post on X announcing their release.
Activist and social media influencer Dhruv ​Rathee, who was also among those detained, was released past midnight on condition he did not participate ⁠in any further protests, said an interior ministry official who declined to be named.
Police detained more than 2,000 people and locked down ​Delhi's city centre to thwart Saturday's protest, and thousands of police and paramilitary personnel continued to be deployed across the city on Sunday, ​although metro stations reopened and mobile internet services were back up.
Most of those detained on the first day of protests were released late on Saturday night, police said.
Opposition parties and critics of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government criticised what they said was the high-handed use of force against the protesters, while ​a UN body called on authorities to ensure that the right to peaceful assembly was respected and fulfilled.
India's foreign ministry said ​on Sunday the UN's approach was "selective" and its statement constituted "an unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India."
Millions of names removed from electoral roll
The protests ‌are ⁠calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a revision of voter lists that critics say disproportionately benefits Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which has been in power for more than 12 years.
Sporadic protests have been going on across India since the Indian Express newspaper in late September reported Kumar's two deputies raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems.
The Commission says differing views ​are normal in internal deliberations, ​and has denied favouring any ⁠party.
Modi's BJP has accused groups opposed to it of trying to undermine the country's democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.
Read more: Indian opposition protest police action against lawmakers, push for poll chief's resignation
Election Commission data cited by the party shows about 130 million names, more than ​the population of Japan, have been deleted from electoral rolls during the verification exercise, including 63 ​million people who ⁠had relocated and 30 million who could not be traced.
The BJP and the Commission deny allegations of manipulation, although opposition parties say Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party, are disproportionately impacted by the deletions.
The cockroach party, which began as ⁠an online ​satire, rapidly evolved into a pressure group, with street protests against exam paper ​leaks culminating in the resignation of Modi's education minister.
The CJP has called its protests against Kumar "Season 2" on its social media handles and said it would not stop ​until India's election system was reformed.

The "Crank That" hitmaker, whose real name is DeAndre Cortez Way, posted "SOULJA BOY 2028" on Instagram on Saturday, October 10.

"From music to business to technology, I’ve always believed in thinking bigger and challenging what’s possible," he wrote. "Now I’m exploring what it means to bring that same vision to public service. The future starts with a conversation."
It remains unclear whether Soulja Boy intends to launch a formal presidential campaign or is simply considering the possibility.
His post did not outline specific policies or provide details about a potential campaign.
The announcement follows his appearance at the Crypto Ball, held during events surrounding Donald Trump's inauguration in January 2025.
The rapper subsequently addressed criticism of his performance, saying he had been paid well for the appearance.
Soulja Boy's interest in politics has also featured in popular culture.
In 2019, Saturday Night Live parodied his viral interview with The Breakfast Club in a sketch imagining him running for president.
The rapper rose to prominence in 2007 when "Crank That (Soulja Boy)" spent seven non-consecutive weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, establishing him as an early success story in internet-driven music promotion.

title: Govt appoints Yahya Akhunzada to K P administration
description: Grade 20 PAS officer previously served as additional secretary at PM Office
content:
Grade-20 PAS officer previously served as additional secretary at PM Office
The federal government on Sunday notified the appointment of Muhammad Yahya Akhunzada to the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) government, according to an official notification.
A Grade-20 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), Akhunzada was previously serving as an additional secretary at the Prime Minister’s Office.
He has also served as additional political agent for South and North Waziristan, secretary of health, information and education in K-P, and commissioner of Dera Ismail Khan. Akhunzada hails from Charsadda district of K-P.
According to the notification, his services have been placed at the disposal of the K-P government under Section 10 of the Civil Servants Act, 1973. The appointment will remain effective until further orders.
Federal cabinet approves emergency rule in K-P
The federal cabinet on Sunday recommended imposing emergency rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) amid a deteriorating security situation and the provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism.
The cabinet, which met under the chairmanship of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, reviewed the worsening law and order situation in the province and was briefed on the rising threat of terrorism, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).
وزیرِ اعظم محمد شہباز شریف کی زیرِ صدارت وفاقی کابینہ کا اجلاس آج اسلام آباد میں منعقد ہوا. وفاقی کابینہ کو خیبر پختونخوا میں امن و امان کی صورتحال اور دھشتگردی کی بگڑتی ہوئی صورتحال پر بریفنگ دی گئی. کابینہ نے خیبر پختونخوا میں امن و امان کی بگڑتی ہوئی صورتحال اور دھشتگردی… pic.twitter.com/EQBySKCItC
In view of the gravity of the situation, the cabinet recommended that the prime minister advise President Asif Ali Zardari to invoke his constitutional powers under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution to impose emergency rule in the province.
The PMO said the advice had been forwarded to the President’s House.
According to sources, K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi had sent the prime minister a written explanation of the grounds for emergency measures about a week earlier, as part of the legal requirements for the proposed intervention.
The reported advice argues that the province's law and order situation has deteriorated to the point where imposing an emergency has become necessary. Following cabinet approval, the prime minister is expected to send the advice to the president. The emergency would take effect after presidential approval, according to the sources.
The cabinet division is expected to place the relevant summary before the cabinet on Sunday, potentially through circulation. Sources said a notification detailing the imposition of governor's rule and emergency would be issued following the required approvals.
The proposals reportedly include administrative changes across the province, particularly replacing the incumbent chief secretary with a new, stronger administrator to oversee provincial affairs. Other senior officials could also be transferred.
Read: Tarar lambasts PTI, K-P government
Sources have separately indicated that the federal government is considering imposing an emergency in 12 districts, including eight merged tribal districts- Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, Bajaur, Mohmand, North Waziristan, South Waziristan and Lower South Waziristan- as well as Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Bannu and Lakki Marwat. Another proposal under consideration would transfer certain important provincial powers to the federal government.
Naqvi, speaking informally to journalists, suggested that the government believed its options for resolving the standoff had narrowed considerably.
"What scope remains for not imposing an emergency?" he asked, urging journalists to consider how the situation could be resolved.
Naqvi said the government had made extensive efforts to find a solution and those involved could themselves explain the extent of those efforts. "We have no room left now," he said.

In a message shared during the panel, Cretton expressed his enthusiasm for bringing Kishimoto’s characters to the screen.
“What I’ve always loved about Naruto is that he’s the character who might normally get sidelined as a sidekick,” Cretton wrote.

The federal government on Sunday appointed Dr Muhammad Fakhr Alam Irfan as the new chief secretary of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).
According to the notification issued today, Irfan, a Grade-22 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), was previously serving as secretary of the Power Division under the Ministry of Energy.
His appointment as K-P chief secretary takes immediate effect and will remain in place until further orders, the notification stated.
Federal cabinet approves emergency rule in K-P
The federal cabinet on Sunday recommended imposing emergency rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) amid a deteriorating security situation and the provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism.
The cabinet, which met under the chairmanship of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, reviewed the worsening law and order situation in the province and was briefed on the rising threat of terrorism, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

title: China rejects claims yuan is undervalued
description: PBOC says China   s exchange rate reform has progressively strengthened the role of market forces since the 1990s
content:
PBOC says China’s exchange rate reform has progressively strengthened the role of market forces since the 1990s
China has rejected claims that its currency is undervalued, insisting it has neither the need nor the intention to engineer depreciation to gain trade competitiveness, as it defended its exchange rate policy amid growing international scrutiny of global trade imbalances.
In a policy statement released on October 8, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) said the renminbi (RMB), also known as the yuan, operated under a managed floating exchange rate regime based on market supply and demand, with reference to a basket of currencies.
The central bank said China remained committed to allowing market forces to play the decisive role in exchange rate formation, while retaining the ability to counter excessive short-term volatility that could threaten financial stability.
China’s expanding exports, it argued, reflected its industrial competitiveness, comprehensive supply chains, infrastructure, skilled workforce and investment in research and innovation rather than currency depreciation. “China has no need, nor any intention, to seek trade competitive advantage through currency depreciation and will never engage in competitive currency devaluation,” the statement said.
The lengthy policy document comes amid international debate over China’s trade surplus and allegations that an undervalued yuan gives its exporters an unfair advantage. Beijing argued that global economic imbalances stemmed from deeper structural problems, including the international monetary system, fiscal deficits and consumption patterns in major economies.
The PBOC said China’s exchange rate reform had progressively strengthened the role of market forces since the 1990s, with major steps taken in 2005 and subsequent reforms aimed at improving the mechanism for determining the yuan’s value.
It maintained that the central bank did not target a specific exchange rate or intervene to reverse its long-term direction. According to the statement, routine foreign exchange intervention was discontinued after 2017.
However, the PBOC acknowledged that authorities could deploy macroprudential measures to manage sharp short-term movements, particularly sudden depreciation and market behaviour driven by self-reinforcing expectations.
It cited external shocks, including the tariff escalation of April 2025, as circumstances in which such measures could help stabilise expectations. Direct intervention could also be used in extreme situations to prevent excessive market swings, it said.
China also pledged to improve transparency, saying it had reported balance-of-payments and foreign exchange data under the International Monetary Fund’s Special Data Dissemination Standard since 2016 and would provide additional foreign exchange-related data to the IMF from 2027.
According to the PBOC, the yuan has experienced successive cycles of appreciation and depreciation since the 2005 reform, with greater two-way volatility and exchange rate flexibility.
The currency appreciated from 8.27 against the US dollar at the time of the July 2005 reform to approximately 6.7, representing a cumulative gain of about 23%, the statement said. It added that the yuan’s nominal effective exchange rate had risen by more than 50% and its real effective exchange rate by 35% since 2005, citing estimates by the Bank for International Settlements.
Since 2010, the yuan-dollar exchange rate has experienced three appreciation and three depreciation cycles, broadly moving within a range of 6.04 to 7.35.
The PBOC said the yuan had appreciated by approximately 9% against the dollar cumulatively since 2025, despite renewed strength in the US dollar and rising US Treasury yields during 2026. It cautioned, however, that the currency’s future direction remained uncertain because of competing economic, financial and geopolitical pressures.
The central bank challenged the argument that currency depreciation was necessary to sustain China’s export growth, pointing to periods when the yuan strengthened even as China expanded its share of global trade.
Between 2005 and 2008, the yuan appreciated by 21% against the dollar while China’s share of global exports increased by 2.4 percentage points. Similar gains in export share accompanied yuan appreciation between 2010 and 2014 and between 2020 and 2021.
Conversely, the PBOC said, the currency depreciated by 7% in 2016 and more than 8% in 2022, while China’s share of global exports declined by 0.7 percentage points in each period.
It attributed the country’s export performance to the upgrading of its industrial base and growing competitiveness in higher-value products. Trade in high-tech goods grew by an average of 7.9% annually over the past five years, with growth reaching 11.4% in 2025 and accounting for nearly 60% of overall foreign trade growth, according to the statement.
The central bank added that around 30% of China’s trade was settled in yuan and that foreign exchange hedging coverage among businesses stood at approximately 30%, helping exporters manage currency risks.
It also argued that intervention could not sustainably determine exchange rate trends in a global foreign exchange market with average daily turnover approaching $10 trillion in 2025.
The PBOC rejected a direct or linear relationship between exchange rates and current account balances, arguing that currency movements were increasingly influenced by financial flows, monetary policy, geopolitical developments and market expectations.
It pointed to South Korea and Japan in the first half of 2026, when current account surpluses increased but their currencies continued to weaken, largely because of capital flows and other financial factors.
Similarly, it said a current account surplus did not automatically mean a currency was undervalued, citing Japan, Switzerland and Germany as examples of surplus economies whose currencies had depreciated in recent years.
The bank also challenged the use of IMF assessments to establish that the yuan was undervalued, arguing that the fund’s External Balance Assessment was primarily designed to analyse external imbalances rather than provide a definitive measure of an equilibrium exchange rate.
Different models, assumptions and data could produce substantially different results, the PBOC said, adding that assessments of real effective exchange rates should not be confused with judgements about the nominal yuan-dollar exchange rate.
The statement placed responsibility for global economic imbalances on both surplus and deficit economies, arguing that their causes included shifting patterns of industrial production, investment and savings gaps, and the international monetary system’s reliance on a dominant reserve currency.
China said deficit economies needed to strengthen fiscal discipline, domestic savings and industrial competitiveness, while surplus economies should encourage consumption and investment.
Blaming the yuan for manufacturing losses or fiscal weaknesses elsewhere, it argued, diverted attention from domestic structural reforms and risked deepening protectionism.
Beijing also defended its contribution to global economic stability, citing its expansion of global supply following its accession to the World Trade Organisation, its stimulus after the 2008 financial crisis and the role of Chinese supply chains during the pandemic.
China’s current account surplus as a share of gross domestic product fell from a peak of 9.9% in 2007, while consumption’s contribution to economic growth rose from 37% in 2010 to 52% in 2025, the statement said.
Looking ahead, the PBOC said China would use its 15th Five-Year Plan period to expand domestic demand, boost household incomes and consumption, improve the business environment, encourage innovation and pursue further economic opening.
The stated objective, it added, was to help rebalance the global economy while strengthening international economic and financial cooperation.

title: One year after ceasefire  Gaza   s promised    day after    has yet to arrive
description: Promised withdrawal  governance transition  reconstruction remain incomplete as most Palestinians remain displaced
content:
Promised withdrawal, governance transition, reconstruction remain incomplete as most Palestinians remain displaced
One year after the ceasefire took effect in the Gaza Strip, all the Israeli captives have been returned, but much of what the agreement promised the Palestinians remains unrealised.
Israeli attacks have continued, the military withdrawal has stalled and partly reversed, governance arrangements remain incomplete, and large-scale reconstruction has yet to begin.
Most of Gaza’s roughly 2.1 million people remain displaced, many living in tents, damaged buildings, or amid rubble, as Palestinian authorities say the continuing attacks are an extension of Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza, launched on October 8, 2023.
The ceasefire took effect on October 10, 2025, after mediation by Egypt, Qatar, Türkiye, and the US, providing for a phased Israeli withdrawal, expanded aid, new governance arrangements, and reconstruction.
On October 13, 2025, Hamas released the remaining 20 living Israeli captives as Israel freed 1,968 Palestinian detainees, according to the International Committee of the Red Cross.
The transfer of remains continued until January 26, 2026, when the Israeli army announced the recovery of the last body.
But the ceasefire did not bring an end to Israeli attacks in Gaza.
Over the past year, Israeli violations of the agreement have killed more than 1,470 Palestinians and wounded over 5,180, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry.
Read: Israel strikes Gaza on Oct 7 anniversary
Egypt, Qatar, and Türkiye said in August that continued Israeli attacks violated the agreement and were obstructing implementation of its second phase.
Before the ceasefire was declared, the Israeli army controlled about 75% of Gaza.
The agreement initially brought a partial withdrawal to the so-called “yellow line,” leaving around 53% of the enclave under Israeli military deployment, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).
But the pullback stalled and later reversed.
By late June, OCHA said Israeli forces had expanded westward beyond the yellow line, leaving 64.9% of Gaza under direct Israeli control or tighter restrictions.
Read more: Israel expanding Gaza ‘yellow line’ to derail ceasefire talks, says Hamas
By August, the UN said nearly two-thirds of the enclave was inaccessible to Palestinians or subject to severe restrictions.
A 15-point roadmap linked restrictions on the weapons of Hamas and other Palestinian factions to additional Israeli withdrawals, deployment of an international force, transfer of governance, and reconstruction.
Egypt, Qatar, and Türkiye said on August 3 that Hamas and other Palestinian factions had accepted the roadmap, including its provision on weapons.
Later that month, eight countries, including Türkiye, Egypt, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia, said Israel had rejected the roadmap, obstructing implementation of the broader plan.
A technocratic National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, headed by Ali Shaath, was formed in January to oversee civilian affairs during the transitional period.
But the transfer of governing responsibilities remains incomplete, while a planned international stabilisation force has yet to be deployed.
Despite provisions to increase humanitarian aid, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said in September that Kerem Shalom remained the only operational crossing for goods after the Zikim crossing was closed in May.
Israeli restrictions also continued on materials needed for shelter and construction.
The UN, European Union, and World Bank estimate Gaza will need $71.4 billion over 10 years for recovery and reconstruction, including $26.3 billion in the first 18 months.
Their assessment found that 1.9 million Palestinians had been displaced and 371,888 housing units damaged or destroyed.
OCHA said in September that Israeli restrictions were still blocking urgently needed shelter supplies, including thousands of tents and construction materials.
One year after the ceasefire, the issue of the captives is closed. For Gaza’s displaced population, however, the promised transition from war to recovery has yet to arrive.
Since October 2023, more than 74,000 Palestinians have been killed and over 175,000 injured in Israeli attacks on Gaza, while around 90% of the enclave’s infrastructure has been destroyed, according to Palestinian figures.

Clarkson claimed a shop assistant appeared to assume she could not afford the merchandise she wanted to buy
Kelly Clarkson has described an uncomfortable shopping experience at a Brooklyn boutique, claiming a shop assistant appeared to assume she could not afford the merchandise she wanted to buy.
The singer shared her account on social media, prompting reactions from fans.
The 44-year-old former American Idol winner took to X on Saturday, October 10, after travelling to the store, Art of Play, to browse its products.
"Just drove all the way to Brooklyn to check out this store I thought looked really rad and had a few things in mind to buy," Clarkson began.
Just drove all the way to Brooklyn to check out this store I thought looked really rad and had a few things in mind to buy and literally was looked at as if I couldn’t afford it and was told he could find something comparable for me. Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a…
She alleged that an employee looked at her as though she could not afford the items before offering to find something "comparable".
Clarkson responded: "Wow, dude. You're an idiot and just lost a huge sale."
The singer compared the encounter to Pretty Woman , the 1990 romantic comedy starring Julia Roberts.
In the film, Roberts plays Vivian Ward, who faces dismissive treatment at a boutique because of her appearance.
The comparison resonated with Clarkson's followers, with several expressing disbelief at her account. One fan wrote: "You mean to tell me the guy in the store didn't know who Kelly Clarkson is?!"
Another commented: "If I was a salesperson and saw you come in the store, I would roll out 'the red carpet' treatment."
S ome people reportedly left negative reviews on the store's Google listing following the incident.
The episode comes as Clarkson navigates changes in her professional and personal life.
She announced her departure from The Kelly Clarkson Show after seven seasons and has continued appearing as a coach on The Voice .
The singer has previously said she wants to prioritise time with her children following the death of her former husband, Brandon Blackstock, in August 2025.

title: Kipchoge wins first marathon in three years
description: The 41 year old clocks 2 09 10  beating the course record by two seconds
content:
The 41-year-old clocks 2:09:10, beating the course record by two seconds
Two-time Olympic champion Eliud Kipchoge won his first marathon in three years on Sunday when the Kenyan great cruised to victory at Melbourne.
The most-decorated marathoner in history crossed the finish line in 2hrs 9min 10sec, two seconds inside the race record.
It was his first victory over the distance since Berlin in 2023 and part of his "World Tour" to raise funds for causes he believes in.
The 41-year-old former world record-holder announced in 2025 he planned complete marathons on all seven continents, including Antarctica, over two years.
Melbourne was the third stop after South Africa and Brazil.
He broke away inside the last 10 kilometres on a course raced partly on the Australian Formula One track at Albert Park and which finished inside the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground.
"On the course, it was really wonderful, I enjoyed seeing people standing, cheering, and shouting my name," Kipchoge said, looking fresh at the finish.
He would have gone faster, but slowed down inside the MCG waving to fans.
"It was actually different -– running on a beautiful course, but also running on the Formula One track, and above all else, finishing on a cricket ground," he added.
"It makes me proud to run with the younger generation and inspire the running community in Melbourne."
Australian Thomas Do Canto was runner-up in 2:10:35 while New Zealand's Camille French came first in the women's race in 2:28:25.

title: Beyond the veil
description: The irreversible shift in women   s political consciousness across Iran and Pakistan
content:
The irreversible shift in women’s political consciousness across Iran and Pakistan
On a chilly Friday morning last month, in Tehran, the capital of the Islamic Republic of Iran presented a study in stark, jarring dualities. In one quarter of the city, the government staged a massive military show of force, deploying paramilitary troops, anti-aircraft weapons, and strict state rhetoric to demonstrate total ideological conformity. Just streets away, a completely unscripted gathering unfolded: thousands of women and male allies took to the streets for a marathon. What stood out wasn't just the endurance of the runners, but how defiantly the runners flouted the dress code for women in Iran. Dozens of women ran openly without headscarves, their hair flowing freely in the breeze; others wore their veils casually draped over their shoulders. Nobody donned the hijab.
Four years after the groundswell of the “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” (“Woman, Life, Freedom”) movement—ignited by the tragic death of 22-year-old Kurdish woman Jina Mahsa Amini in the custody of the morality police—the Iranian public sphere has undergone an irreversible change. Even amidst heightened geopolitics, military threats, and an unrelenting domestic crackdown marked by widespread detentions and executions, the subversion of state-mandated modesty has become daily practice. Strikingly, this transformation has bled into the state’s own backyard; recent pro-government rallies have seen female attendees openly defying strict hijab regulations without state interference. Caught between strict official policy and a shifting public, some within the Iranian establishment have begun arguing that women who back the government should still be welcomed as loyal supporters of the system—even if they don't fully comply with mandatory hijab rules.
Across the border, however, a strikingly inverse battle over the female body is being waged in Pakistan. There is no mandatory hijab enforcement by the state in Pakistan, yet religious groups and state actors police women's physical presence and voices just as strictly. Every year on March 8, International Women’s Day, major urban centres like Karachi, Lahore, and Islamabad become flashpoints for the Aurat March, a grassroots feminist collective demanding basic civil rights, an end to gender-based violence, economic equity, and bodily self-determination. Yet, almost synchronously, Pakistan’s religious right mobilises counter-demonstrations known as "Haya Marches" or "Hijab Marches", framing feminist demands as a Western-backed threat to traditional Islamic family values.
These two scenes—Iranian women running bareheaded through Tehran and Pakistani marchers clashing over slogans in Islamabad—expose a shared reality: the female body remains the primary battlefield for political control and religious authority. Nowhere is this struggle more visible than in the fight over who gets to occupy public space.
Patriarchal authority has historically treated the female body not as an individual human entity, but as a symbolic canvas for collective honour, national identity, and religious purity. Whenever a state or religious establishment wants to project its moral authority, regulating women is always the first move.
In Iran, the mandatory hijab law, enacted shortly after the 1979 Islamic Revolution, transformed the female body into an explicit symbol of anti-Western resistance and Islamic governance. Removing the veil was seen as a direct act of treason against the state, not a simple choice of clothing or observing one’s faith. In September 2022, Mahsa Amini’s death in police custody—after being arrested for 'improper attire'—unmasked the heavy-handed force needed to maintain state-mandated modesty laws. The chant “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” was born in rebellion and echoed across Kurdistan, Tehran, Baluchistan, and Azerbaijan— unifying precisely because it recognised that state authoritarianism, ethnic marginalisation, and gender oppression are bound together by the same thread. By running bareheaded in a public marathon, Iranian women are not merely engaging in physical exercise; they are performing a radical act of public space reclamation. They are asserting that their presence in the public square is inherent, unconditioned by state approval or religious surveillance.
In Pakistan, where moral policing is decentralised across feudal systems, conservative clergy, and vigilante street politics, the battle manifests differently. The Aurat March, initiated in 2018, was conceived as an inclusive space to address urgent material realities: honour killings, forced marriages, domestic violence, workplace harassment, and legal marginalisation. Among its notable legal victories was contributing to the historic judicial ban on the archaic and dehumanising “virginity test” for female rape survivors in Punjab.
Yet, despite these tangible contributions to justice, conservative and religious circles have directed their fiercest outrage not at the systemic violence inflicted upon women, but at the marchers' assertion of physical sovereignty. Slogans such as “Mera Jism, Meri Marzi” (“My Body, My Choice”) and placards urging society to “Stop being menstrual-phobic” triggered an explosive theological backlash. A former Minister for Religious Affairs went so far as to publicly demand that the Prime Minister rename International Women's Day as "Hijab Day" to counteract what he characterised as an assault on Islamic values. Religious parties mobilised thousands of counter-protesters, filing police complaints alleging blasphemy—a charge carrying severe penalties in Pakistan—and issuing death threats that forced many organisers to deactivate their social media accounts and go into hiding.
This exposes a clear double standard: while conservative leaders rail against Western influence, they routinely use state power and public intimidation to deny women the basic rights granted by both international law and religious tradition.
does a placard asserting ownership over one’s physical person elicit more hostility than the rape, murder, or structural disenfranchisement of women? The answer lies in the deep-seated societal binary of the "Good Muslim Woman" versus the "Bad Muslim Woman".
In mainstream conservative discourse across South Asia and the Middle East, women are allowed to succeed, but only within strict limits —provided it remains neatly compartmentalised within acceptable patriarchal boundaries. A woman advocating for female literacy, building girls' schools, or demanding access to maternal healthcare is often tolerated, if not praised, as a "nurturing mother" or "dutiful daughter" fulfilling her domestic and community duties. This is categorised as benign, acceptable reform.
However, the moment a woman asserts bodily autonomy—claiming total sovereignty over her physical form, her wardrobe, her reproductive choices, her mobility, and her sexuality—she crosses an invisible ideological line. She transitions from a passive subject to be protected into an autonomous agent demanding rights. By declaring “Mera Jism, Meri Marzi,” Pakistani women explicitly reject the notion that their bodies belong to their fathers, husbands, brothers, or the state. They undermine the foundation of a system that expects women to trade their obedience for safety provided by men.
Critics write off bodily autonomy as a Western idea that threatens Islamic values. Traditionalists argue that giving women individual freedom destroys the family and disrupts social order. Because of this, counter-marches like the 'Haya March' centre on defending the family—pushing the idea that a woman's main role is to stay modest, self-sacrificing, and obedient.
Yet this argument deliberately ignores the socio-economic realities of millions of working-class Muslim women for whom modesty laws offer no protection against economic exploitation, domestic violence, or state neglect. By focusing entirely on clothing and public decorum, conservative power structures distract from their own failure to provide safety, economic justice, and basic human dignity to female citizens.
decades, Muslim feminist theologians have argued that the subjugation of women in Muslim-majority societies is not a result of divine revelation, but of centuries of patriarchal interpretation ( fiqh ) that conflated historical Arab cultural norms with eternal divine intent.
Scholars like Fatima Mernissi, Amina Wadud, and Asma Barlas have systematically demonstrated that the Qur'an introduced revolutionary protections for female autonomy in seventh-century Arabia—granting women independent legal status, rights to inheritance, property ownership, marital consent, and financial independence centuries before similar rights were recognised in the West. Mernissi’s historical-critical analysis revealed how certain misogynistic traditions were fabricated or contextually distorted by male political elites in the later centuries to strip women of political power and push them out of the public sphere.
Amina Wadud frames this as a fundamental matter of faith: in Islam, absolute authority belongs to God alone. When a state or family claims ownership over a woman’s body—dictating what she wears or where she goes—it effectively tries to place human control on par with divine authority. Furthermore, Islamic feminist theology directly addresses the question of bodily autonomy. Far from treating the female body as an inherently shameful source of temptation that must be veiled, hidden, and controlled, progressive Islamic jurisprudence emphasises that the body is a divine trust ( amanah ) given directly to the individual. Progressive Islamic thinkers also argue that faith cannot be forced. In this view, a person's body is a trust given directly to them by God, and genuine spirituality requires personal choice. When the state or society coerces a woman to cover herself, pray, or obey male authority, those actions lose their spiritual meaning—because under Islamic principle, faith relies entirely on free will.
When Pakistani feminists demand an end to domestic violence, marital rape, and honour killings, they are building on a legacy that stretches back to the 1980s. During General Zia-ul-Haq’s military dictatorship, groups like the Women’s Action Forum took to the streets to protest state-enforced laws that institutionalised female inequality. Today’s activists—whether marching in Pakistan or running unveiled in Iran—are not rebelling against faith, but against man-made systems of control designed to strip them of basic safety.
A critical challenge in addressing women’s rights in the Muslim world is the trap of dual orientalism. On one side stands Western imperialist discourse, which frequently weaponises the idea of 'rescuing Muslim women' to rationalise military action, reducing complex societies to a simple story of backwardness. On the other side stand domestic religious hardliners who exploit this history, framing any internal call for women's liberation as a treasonous submission to Western culture.
Muslim women are thus caught in a double bind: condemned by Western saviours if they choose to embrace religious practice or attire, and persecuted by indigenous patriarchs if they demand bodily autonomy and civil rights. The Iranian women running in the Tehran marathon and the Pakistani women marching in the streets of Karachi are actively dismantling this false binary. They refuse to allow foreign powers to define their liberation, just as they refuse to allow local clerics to use religion against their fundamental rights.
Their struggle demonstrates that bodily autonomy is not a foreign ideology—it is an innate human necessity.
Suppressing women under the guise of religious purity is a distinctly modern panic, standing in stark contrast to a history where Muslim women actively shaped public and intellectual life. Today’s regimes are not defending tradition; they are trying to enforce a control that even past centuries didn't demand. But while state violence can police behaviour, it cannot erase political consciousness. The old boundaries have collapsed, and no state decree can force women to un-see the rights they have already claimed.
By rooting their struggle for bodily self-determination within broader frameworks of human dignity, social justice, and authentic theological reform, Muslim women are demonstrating that faith and freedom are not mutually exclusive. The future of gender justice in the region will not be dictated by state decrees or religious fatwas, but by the quiet, unrelenting courage of women reclaiming their bodies, their spaces, and their sacred right to live free.

title: One soldier martyred  12 terrorists killed as security forces foil infiltration attempt in Kurram  ISPR
description: ISPR says Afghan Taliban regime has consistently failed to honour its international counter terrorism obligations
content:
ISPR says Afghan Taliban regime has consistently failed to honour its international counter-terrorism obligations
Security forces killed 12 terrorists and Afghan Taliban while thwarting an infiltration attempt along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's Kurram district, with one soldier martyred during the exchange of fire, the military’s media wing said on Sunday.
According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the movement of a group of khawarij trying to approach international border from Afghanistan to Pakistan was detected and effectively engaged by security forces on October 10.
The security forces, maintaining a high state of alertness and vigilance, effectively thwarted the infiltration attempt. The ISPR said that “Afghan Taliban posts also opened fire to support the infiltration attempt by khawarij ”.
“Skilful and precise engagement by vigilant troops resulted in the killing of twelve khawarij and Afghan Taliban,” the statement added.
The ISPR said that Naib Subedar Hidayat Aman, 40, a resident of Ghizer district, was martyred during the intense exchange of fire. It added that he had “fought gallantly, paid the ultimate sacrifice and embraced shahadat”.
Read: Security forces foil infiltration attempt in North Waziristan
The statement further said that the incident along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border once again vindicated Pakistan’s “objective and factual stance” regarding the wilful abject failure of the Afghan Taliban regime to deny the use of Afghan soil to the terrorist organisation, rather facilitate and patronise cross-border terrorism.
“The Afghan Taliban regime has consistently failed to honour its international counter-terrorism obligations,” the ISPR said.
The security forces remained resolute and unwavering in their commitment to defending the country’s frontiers, the statement added.
A sanitisation operation was underway to eliminate any other Indian-sponsored kharji found in the area, the ISPR said. It added that the counter-terrorism campaign under the vision of Azm-e-Istehkam , approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, would continue at full pace.
The campaign, being conducted by the security forces and law enforcement agencies, aimed to eliminate the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism in the country, the statement added.
“These sacrifices of our brave soldiers further reinforce our unwavering commitment to safeguarding our nation and its frontiers at all costs,” the statement concluded.
President Zardari pays tribute to martyr
President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the security forces for foiling the infiltration attempt along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border. He also expressed "profound grief and sorrow over the martyrdom of Naib Subedar Hidayat Aman during the operation."
In a statement posted on X, President Zardari paid rich tribute to the martyr "for laying down his life in defence of the homeland," extending "heartfelt condolences and sympathy" to the bereaved family. The statement also noted that President Zardari prayed "for the elevation of the martyr's ranks and patience for the bereaved family."
صدر مملکت آصف علی زرداری کا صوبہ خیبر پختونخوا کے ضلع کرم میں پاک افغان سرحد پر دہشت گردوں کی دراندازی کی کوشش ناکام بنانے پر سیکیورٹی فورسز کو خراج تحسین۔ صدر مملکت کا دہشت گردوں کی دراندازی کی کوشش کو ناکام بنانے کے دوران نائب صوبیدار ہدایت امان کی شہادت پر گہرے دکھ اور افسوس…
"Naib Subedar Hidayat Aman sacrificed his life for the protection of the country's borders, setting a great example of courage and bravery," the statement said.
It added that President Zardari also paid tribute "to the professional expertise and readiness of security forces for foiling the terrorists' infiltration attempt and sending 12 Khawarij and Afghan Taliban to hell."
"The Afghan government's patronage and support of terrorist elements poses a grave threat to regional peace and security," the president said, adding that if the Afghan Taliban regime "considers Pakistan's patience, caution, and responsible approach as our weakness, then it is their grave folly."
"Pakistan can not only send these infiltrating terrorists to hell but also annihilate their patrons," President Zardari said, adding, "It is better that this gang reviews its policies in its own interest."
Naqvi pays tribute to forces, martyr for 'crushing' enemy's design
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also paid tribute to Naib Subedar Hidayat Aman and the security forces for "crushing the enemy's nefarious designs to dust."
The Ministry of Interior noted that Naqvi paid tribute to the martyr, stating that he "embraced martyrdom while bravely confronting the enemy," and expressing heartfelt condolences and sympathy to the bereaved family.

According to the ministry, Naqvi stated, "I salute the brave soldiers of the security forces," adding that "the nation takes pride in the professional capabilities and courage of the security forces."

title: Messi nets brace to win in first match after Argentina exit
description: Suarez also nets twice as the defending champions secure only their second league win in 11 matches
content:
Suarez also nets twice as the defending champions secure only their second league win in 11 matches
Lionel Messi scored twice to help Inter Miami rout DC United 4-0 on Saturday, taking a victory in his first match since saying farewell to the Argentina national team.
Four nights after scoring in his final match for the Albiceleste in a victory over Benin, the 39-year-old South American superstar struck in the 47th and 60th minutes as defending MLS champion Miami won for only the second time in their past 11 league matches.
A first-half brace by Luis Suarez staked the Herons to the lead as they improved to 13-5 with 10 drawn for 49 points, jumping from third to second in the Eastern Conference
Messi hopes to make Miami the first team to win back-to-back MLS crowns since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2011-12.
Messi, the top point producer in the league with 23 goals plus assists on 13 others, seeks a third consecutive MLS Most Valuable Player award.
Uruguayan striker Suarez scored in the third minute to give Miami the lead, blasting a left-footed shot from the heart of the box into the top left corner.
Suarez struck again in the 39th for his 16th goal of the campaign, assisted like his first of the night by German Berterame.
Messi blasted home a left-footed shot off an assist from Suarez to give Miami a 3-0 lead and evaded three defenders to add another goal 13 minutes later as the pink-clad hosts pulled away to stay.
In other games, Scottish striker Lewis Morgan and American Djordje Mihailovic scored in second-half stoppage time to rally Toronto for a 2-1 home victory over Montreal.
The visitors grabbed the lead in the Canadian clash on a goal by Mexican forward Daniel Rios in the 52nd minute.
Toronto, however, battled back for the equalizer by winger Morgan, obtained last month from San Diego, in the third minute of stoppage time, his first regular-season MLS goal in two years.
Former Montreal standout Mihailovic struck for the decider in the fifth minute of extra time.
"Now I've scored on both sides of this derby," he said. "It feels good."
Toronto snapped a three-game losing streak to pull within a point of an East playoff berth.
At Chicago, Swiss forward Maren Haile-Selassie scored in the 87th minute to give the 10-man Chicago Fire a 2-1 triumph over New York City.
Austrian midfielder Hannes Wolf gave City the lead in the 19th minute and Chicago dropped to 10 men when Ivory coast midfielder Dje D'Avilla received his second yellow card in the 43rd minute.
Swede Anton Saletros equalized for Chicago in the 55th minute, setting the stage for the decider.

title: Renshaw celebrates second Test century after a decade long wait
description: Australia s batsman surpasses his career best with a record ninth wicket stand alongside Nathan Lyon against South Africa
content:
Australia's batsman surpasses his career-best with a record ninth-wicket stand alongside Lyon against South Africa
Australia's Matt Renshaw said his second Test century was a reward for years of hard work and setbacks after he struck a career-best score in the opening ICC World Test Championship contest against South Africa on Saturday.
Renshaw, who scored his maiden Test hundred almost a decade ago, surpassed his previous best of 184 against Pakistan with a marathon innings that also featured a remarkable 134-run partnership for the ninth wicket with Nathan Lyon.
"I always wanted that second one," Renshaw told reporters after the second day's play.
"I had the monkey off the back early with that first one. I think it was like that has come in the last 10 years, all the hard work, all the failures, all the success. This was nice just for me to get."
Promoted to number five for the first time since his recall in 2023, Renshaw adopted a patient approach against South Africa's attack, reaching the close of the first day with only three boundaries from 115 balls.
He brought up his half-century off the second ball of the following morning before weathering the threat of the second new ball to continue Australia's innings.
Renshaw admitted that he had feared another opportunity at the highest level might never come after failing to make the most of his return to the side in 2023.
"I think once (I) took a few years out of the team, had an opportunity in 2023 and didn't take it, you probably think that you're never going to get this opportunity again," he said.
"So when I hit the ball, I was screaming at it, 'go, go, go'. It sort of all just hit me at once."
Lyon's presence at the other end made the occasion even more memorable for Renshaw, who acknowledged the emotion surrounding their partnership.
"You had Nathan at the other end, who was pretty emotional. So to see that, it was pretty special," he added.
The innings also set a new individual Test scoring record at the Durban venue for a batter coming in at number five or lower, eclipsing Sri Lanka's Kusal Perera, who scored an unbeaten 153 in 2019.
Rain interrupted play for the second consecutive day, limiting South Africa's reply as they reached stumps on 27 for one, still trailing Australia by 363 runs.
Josh Hazlewood struck early by dismissing Ryan Rickelton for a three-ball duck, leaving Aiden Markram unbeaten on 15 and David Bedingham on 12 as the hosts sought to steady their innings.

title: New Zealand split ODI squads for India series
description: The Black Caps recall Finn Allen  Lockie Ferguson and Tim Seifert
content:
The Black Caps recall Finn Allen, Lockie Ferguson and Tim Seifert
New Zealand have named Finn Allen, Lockie Ferguson, Rachin Ravindra and Tim Seifert in split squads for their five-match home ODI series against India, starting on November 4.
White-ball captain Mitchell Santner will lead both groups, with seven players joining the squad for the final two matches as the Black Caps assess their depth ahead of the 2027 ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup.
Ravindra, who missed the preceding T20I series against India with a shoulder injury, has been included for the first three ODIs.
Allen and Ferguson return to the ODI setup for the first time since the 2023 World Cup, while Seifert last featured in the format against Pakistan 18 months ago.
New Zealand will also manage workloads with a two-Test series against India to follow. Red-ball players will leave the ODI squad after the third match to prepare for the first Test in Wellington on November 19.
Head coach Rob Walter said the series offered an opportunity to evaluate players ahead of the next World Cup while ensuring adequate preparation for the World Test Championship campaign.
“With the ODI World Cup just one year away it’s important for us to also view these matches as valuable preparation for that event,” Walter said.
“Bringing in seven players for the final ODIs allows us to test our depth and see how those players fare against a world-class side.”
Walter added that the importance of World Test Championship points had prompted the team to release some players early for additional preparation.
Zak Foulkes, Will O’Rourke and Ben Sears were unavailable for selection as they continue their injury rehabilitation.
