title: Arbitration and human rights
description: Arbitration and human rights
content:
Report's treatment of contractual cascading points towards a more intriguing possibility
Human rights and arbitration are often cast as opposing juridical worlds. One evokes public values, vulnerable claimants and state power; the other, contractual consent, private adjudication and commercial disputes. But that contrast obscures the question: when business activity causes human rights harm across borders, should effective remedy depend upon the institutional label of the forum? It should not. What matters is whether the mechanism can deliver legitimate, accessible and effective redress.
The European Law Institute's "Business and Human Rights: Access to Justice and Effective Remedies" Report presents a formidable objection. It calls the Bangladesh Accords and the Hague Rules on Business and Human Rights Arbitration "impressive and welcome", while cautioning that consensual mechanisms depend upon party consent and may be vulnerable to stronger parties without external control. It therefore favours public-facing mechanisms possessing coercive authority. That concern is legitimate. Yet it does not establish arbitration's irrelevance.
Indeed, the Report's treatment of contractual cascading points towards a more intriguing possibility. It proposes contractual mechanisms through which human-rights due-diligence responsibilities can extend through transnational supply chains, coupled with access to courts. If private ordering can carry substantive human rights responsibilities across borders, why should it become irrelevant when the question changes from who bears responsibility to how that responsibility may be contested and enforced? This does not displace courts; it asks that contractual responsibility and access to remedy be considered together.
That proposition encounters a fundamental limit: substantive obligation is not arbitral jurisdiction. An affected worker, community or other rightsholder does not acquire a right to arbitrate merely because two corporations have contracted. A credible model must address consent, standing, participation, applicable law and enforcement. Where appropriate, contractual arrangements may confer defined third-party rights and establish a legally cognisable basis for participation.
The Hague Rules address this problem at the procedural level. Based on the UNCITRAL Arbitration Rules, they adapt procedure to business-and-human-rights disputes. Their framework can accommodate different claimant and respondent configurations, while consent remains its cornerstone. The Rules therefore do not create substantive rights or conjure jurisdiction where none exists; they demonstrate instead that arbitral procedure can be adapted beyond the conventional commercial paradigm.
Nor does the UN Guiding Principles framework reserve effective remedy to courts. It recognises judicial and non-judicial mechanisms and subjects non-state-based mechanisms to criteria including legitimacy, accessibility, predictability, equity, transparency and rights-compatibility. This is not an endorsement of arbitration as such. It is a functional standard against which arbitration must prove its worth.
That scrutiny must remain exacting. Arbitration cannot cure unequal bargaining power by invocation alone. Cost, evidentiary asymmetry, confidentiality, collective claims, third-party participation and enforcement may determine whether a formally available remedy is genuinely accessible. Courts remain indispensable where public coercive authority is required, consent is absent or mandatory law reserves the matter for judicial determination. An arbitration clause must never become a contractual alibi for extinguishing substantive rights or insulating corporate conduct from legitimate public oversight.
But these limitations establish the conditions of legitimate arbitration; they do not establish its irrelevance.
The better conception is neither courts versus arbitration nor private ordering versus public authority, but a plural remedial architecture in which institutional form follows remedial need. Courts possess coercive authority and public legitimacy that certain disputes require. Arbitration, where jurisdiction is validly constituted and safeguards exist, can offer a potentially neutral transnational forum, procedural adaptability and an enforceable determination.
Arbitration is no panacea. But excluding it from the remedial repertoire would be an untenable dogma.

title: Buildings at risk
description: Buildings at risk
content:
Sindh's problem is not an absence of regulations or even awareness of the risks
How many more lives must be lost before the authorities in Sindh begin treating fire safety as a matter of public survival rather than administrative procedure? According to the latest findings of the Provincial Disaster Management Authority, hundreds of buildings remain dangerous while thousands await re-inspection. In Karachi alone, 162 buildings remain non-compliant with fire safety requirements, while 486 buildings across the province have been classified as high-risk. The Gul Plaza tragedy earlier this year should have been sufficient to shake the provincial administration out of its complacency.
Sindh's problem is not an absence of regulations or even awareness of the risks. It is the entrenched culture of negligence that allows unsafe buildings to remain operational while authorities satisfy themselves with issuing notices and conducting inspections. The consequences of such indifference are borne not by the officials responsible for enforcement but by ordinary citizens. That more than 2,200 buildings were still awaiting re-inspection when the latest figures were reported illustrates the unacceptable pace of corrective action. An audit should be the beginning of enforcement, not an achievement in itself. The Sindh government must establish strict deadlines for compliance and ensure that buildings posing an immediate threat are not permitted to operate until essential safety measures have been installed. Building owners who disregard notices must face meaningful penalties, while officials who fail to enforce regulations should be held equally accountable.
There can be little justification for continued inaction when the dangers have already been documented. The provincial administration has enough evidence to determine where intervention is most urgently required. What it now needs is the will to act against violations, regardless of the commercial interests involved. Public safety cannot remain subordinate to bureaucratic convenience or the profits of negligent building owners.

title: Overcrowding in prisons
description: Overcrowding in prisons
content:
Many of those under trial are only there because they can't afford bail
Pakistan's prison system is buckling under a wholly avoidable overpopulation crisis. The latest Annual Prisons Data Report reveals a staggering 110,513 people behind bars, with three out of every four - 82,988 individuals - having never been convicted of a crime. Our jails now hold 41,681 more people than they were designed for, operating at over 160 per cent of authorised capacity.
Many of those under trial are only there because they can't afford bail. The root cause is an over-reliance on pre-trial detention and a broken bail system. People have been languishing for months, often years, awaiting a verdict. The courts have a backlog of over two million cases, and investigators and prosecutors do not help much by working at a snail's pace. And even in cases where bail should easily be available - such as non-violent crimes - structural hurdles, including an overreliance on pre-trial detention, stand in the way. Small-time drug peddlers are an example. Over 28,000 people are imprisoned under drug laws, a 43 per cent increase since 2023. Many of these individuals are not hardened criminals but petty offenders and the socioeconomically vulnerable, who cannot afford private counsel or surety bonds. The National Commission for Human Rights chairperson observed, "People enter prison faster than our justice system can process them."
Building more prisons is an option, but it is a bad one, because it would not address the underlying problem. Instead, the government should encourage bail reform, reduce unnecessarily long sentences and encourage the use of probation and parole. Until then, Pakistan's prisons will remain warehouses for the unconvicted, and like all the warehouses full of sensitive documents that would magically catch fire every year, the buildings are once again at high risk of fire.

title: Talks or turmoil
description: Talks or turmoil
content:
Two rounds of talks last week ended in a stalemate
The PTI's long march has, on its seventh day, swept like a whirlwind across the south of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and is now inching towards Swabi. Its next destination is Islamabad - a move, of course, fraught with consequences. This march aims to build pressure on a federal government which is wary of the opposition's likely storming of the capital. With the twin cities of Islamabad and Rawalpindi already on high alert, barricaded with containers and a heavy deployment of law enforcement agencies, the way forward should be to defuse the situation through dialogue. Yet, the reality on the ground is driven by K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, who has managed to rally his base from the front at a time when his own party is in disarray and lacks a cohesive political strategy.
The million-dollar question is: what's next? The federal government has been mulling Governor's rule in the province but is yet to do so, perhaps because of a lack of consensus with its coalition partners. The PTI, on the other hand, has a single-point agenda: compliance with the August 18 Supreme Court order as a precondition for coming to the negotiation table. The TTAP, however, believes that an instant audience with Imran Khan can help lower the political mercury and stall the march on the capital. That puts the government in a fix, as it has not been able to win over the opposition by providing it with due political space.
The two rounds of talks last week ended in a stalemate. Yet, there is a silver lining, and that is the offer by JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman to convene an All Parties' Conference while recognising the opposition's right to march on the capital as a constitutional prerogative. One step back from either side could certainly pave the way for a leap forward. All that is desired is a set of confidence-building measures, such as enabling opposition leaders to meet with the incarcerated former PM, subsequently leading to the suspension of the protest and kick-starting a dialogue. Confrontation only begets instability - an outcome that must be avoided at all costs.

title: The poor man s burden
description: The poor man s burden
content:
World Bank has voiced the muted outcries of the poor
For decades in general, and the past couple of years in particular, most of the people of Pakistan have struggled in lawlessness, destitution and poverty, with all their calls and agonies unheeded by a government focused on self-preservation and prolonging itself by whatever means possible. The means employed for its sustenance only worsened the poverty, among other issues, so much that people were left with no voice or stake except invoking the divine. For none in the government cared. Nor was the public good within its capacity, mandate or legitimacy. Therefore, the government, in order to conceal the real public plight, arbitrarily reduced the poverty threshold to 8,000 a month. Until then, the government had desperately passed the buck for, or deliberately overlooked and downplayed, the issues of its own making. It turned a deaf ear to the vanishingly few voices for the voiceless poor amid silenced, sold or mortgaged souls.
Yet the specter of poverty began to bother the elite - not for the public good, however. Recently, the World Bank has voiced the muted outcries of the poor, suggesting that Pakistan is home to almost half of the extremely poor population in the MENAAP region's 23 countries, which include the entire Middle East, North Africa and AF-Pak. This isn't news, however. What the World Bank has reported is nothing but a report of a painful lived, yet muzzled, silenced and unheeded reality of years. What, then, is the news? It is, in fact, the government's notice of the report - the government that remained oblivious to all that the people are grinding under.
The attention isn't glad tidings for the people, either. By now, I may sound so pessimistic that I fail to recognise the regime's sudden change of heart. I'm not - you'll acknowledge. The departure from their years-long deliberate oblivion to the poor's agonies is in fact merely gaslighting and dismissing the acute poverty.
The government has taken notice only to reject the World Bank's claim about the poorest. This makes the ultimate act of taking note of the report - however much it is to denounce it - newsworthy. Isn't it? Besides, the act also carries two vitriolic truths: that the poor, with all their agonies and screams for years, mattered little, if at all, to this regime, which in turn points to another established reality - that its legitimacy lies beyond the public.
Ironically, any achievement, however ill-gotten or deceptive, is readily taken credit for by the incumbent setup. The unbroken record of failures and issues - whether deliberate or arising from its illegitimacy, incapacity or both is never its own. That is, the afflictions and agonies of the people are not the issue; their reporting is.
At the $3-a-day poverty line, which amounts to Rs25,000 a month - let alone those living below it or going without any income at all - this illustration suggests how harrowing life can be: flour costs Rs200 per kg, so 40 kg costs Rs8,000. Just imagine families of four to eight members who eat only loaves twice a day and consume two maunds a month. That would be Rs16,000 of the total Rs25,000, and that too without accounting for the uncertainty and inconsistency of earning $3 a day. What about groceries, healthcare, education, nutritious food, transport and funeral and wedding costs, let alone utilities? No one cares. Not at least this regime.
Had the poor had a voice, they would also have protested the report, calling it a gross underestimation of their miseries. They would also have protested the sheer hypocrisy of all those in positions of power, influence or public trust who, instead of voicing the people's grievances, exploit the vulnerabilities of the poor for personal gain, perks and connections. Notwithstanding the report, the World Bank's promises and the IMF's policies owe a great deal to the extreme poverty in the country.
Beyond predation, oppression, electoral fraud and the seeking of aid and begging in their name, the poor are, for the elite, a liability. For the poor, the regime and its patrons are only a burden on them and the country.

title: Trump says US may join Saudi strikes against Houthis in Yemen
description: Trump said the US may join the strikes  adding that Washington would decide quickly after the latest attack
content:
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that Washington may join Saudi strikes against the Houthis in Yemen following an attack on an airport in Riyadh.
Asked by reporters whether he had decided to take part in the strikes, Trump said: “We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack. We will make a decision. We move very quickly.”
"Have you decided whether to join the Saudi strikes on the Houthis?" @POTUS : "We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack, so we'll make a decision. We move very quickly." pic.twitter.com/8aUAneK2xB
His remarks came after King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital temporarily suspended operations on Saturday following an attack that left several people injured, according to the country's civil aviation authority.
The General Authority of Civil Aviation said in a statement that the airport was attacked Saturday afternoon, adding that authorities were still determining the number of people injured.
Read More: Iran's Pezeshkian says regional diplomacy must go beyond meetings, highlights dialogue, cooperation
The US and UK embassies in Saudi Arabia also urged their citizens Saturday to avoid the airport following attacks, warning of security risks and possible travel disruptions.
Saudi authorities said on Friday that three citizens were killed and others injured in two attacks on Thursday targeting facilities at King Khalid International Airport and a Saudi Arabian Airlines aircraft.
Airport operations later resumed, and air traffic returned to normal, according to the aviation authority.
The Houthis have claimed responsibility for several missile and drone attacks on King Khalid International Airport and other Saudi airports in recent days.
Yemen has been engulfed in war since the Houthis seized control of the capital Sanaa and several provinces in September 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government.

title: Pentagon raises US troop death toll in Iran war to 21
description: The updated figures also showed that 865 US service members had been wounded during the operations
content:
The updated figures also showed that 865 US service members had been wounded during the operations.
The Pentagon late on Friday raised the official death toll of US troops linked to military operations against Iran to 21, acknowledging that two additional deaths had not previously been included in its figures.
As of Friday, the Defence Casualty Analysis System listed 21 military deaths connected to the operations, according to The Washington Post .
The newly included deaths involved Major Sorffly Davius, 46, an Army National Guard member who died in Kuwait on March 6, and an unidentified Navy service member who died by suicide in September, the newspaper reported.
The updated figures also showed that 865 US service members had been wounded during the operations.
Separately, the military confirmed the death of another soldier in a training accident that officials said was unrelated to the conflict with Iran.
Sergeant Devin A. Seibel, 26, died in Iraq in May. His death was recorded under Operation Inherent Resolve, the military's long-running campaign against the ISIS (Daesh) terrorist group.
Read More: Israeli Democrats leader says killing of Iran’s Ali Khamenei was a 'mistake'
Two senior Democrats on the House Armed Services Committee welcomed what they described as the Pentagon's "public correction" of the casualty figures on Friday.
"There is no excuse for a mistake of this magnitude," Representative Adam Smith of Washington, the committee's top Democrat, and Representative Chrissy Houlahan of Pennsylvania, the top Democrat on its military personnel subcommittee, said in a joint statement.
They also described the need for congressional intervention to correct the figures as "an embarrassment" for the military.
In a statement to The Washington Post , the Pentagon did not directly address the revised death toll.
Instead, it outlined changes to its casualty reporting system, including the introduction of a "pending adjudication" category for records still under review.
The Pentagon reiterated its commitment to accurate reporting, saying it "continues to maintain a steadfast commitment to the transparent, accurate accounting of all Service member casualties".

title: Ben Affleck says he argues with children while playing Fortnite
description: Ben Affleck says he argues with younger Fortnite players and drew inspiration from game   s skins for  Animals
content:
Ben Affleck says he argues with younger Fortnite players and drew inspiration from game’s skins for 'Animals'
Ben Affleck has revealed that playing first-person shooter games sometimes leads to arguments with younger players, while explaining how Fortnite inspired the costumes in his upcoming Netflix thriller, Animals .
Speaking on the New Heights podcast, Affleck discussed the inspiration behind a character in the film who wears a fuzzy bunny mask.
He explained that his son had been showing an interest in Fortnite skins and describing some of them as “tough”, prompting the actor to draw ideas from the game’s unusual designs.
“I thought these costumes are so kind of random and unusual, that's what I based the costumes on,” said Affleck. “I thought he'd be getting them off games.”
Affleck also spoke about his own gaming habits, revealing that he plays sports titles such as Madden and NBA 2K, alongside first-person shooters.
Although he considers himself a capable player, he acknowledged that younger competitors can quickly outplay him.
“I always play games,” he said. “I play first person shooter games, so I think I'm good, and then 12-year-olds just fk you up. I try to come out and I'm like, ‘Here I come.’ I get killed right away, and then they taunt you, like, ‘You suck. Fk you!’ I end up getting in arguments. ‘F**k you! I don't suck! I'm a grown man!’”
The actor has previously spoken about his interest in gaming, particularly the tactical shooter Valorant. He has attended several Valorant events with his son and has said that he mains KAY/O, one of the game's agents.
Affleck also joined esports organisation Sentinels for a watch party last year, discussing his experience with Valorant during the stream.

title: Hundreds of thousands rally in London to mark 3 years of genocide in Gaza
description: Pro Palestinian protesters waved flags  held signs condemning Israel and chanted slogans calling for a free Palestine
content:
Pro-Palestinian protesters waved flags, held signs condemning Israel and chanted slogans calling for a free Palestine
Pro-Palestinian protesters took to the streets in London on Saturday to mark the third anniversary of the start of Israel’s genocidal attacks on Gaza, demanding that the government impose a total sanctions regime on Israel.
Gathering at Embankment, hundreds of thousands of people marched towards Downing Street, where the prime minister's office is located, to call for an end to the genocide and a full arms embargo on Israel.
Carrying Palestinian flags, the crowd held several signs in solidarity with the Palestinian people. Some read: "Israel targets children", "Free Palestine" and "Stop the genocide".
They also shouted pro-Palestine slogans, including "From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free."
In a post on X, Palestine Solidarity Campaign (PSC) said: "We demand our government sanction the whole state of Israel and implement a full arms embargo."
Now: Tens of thousands on the streets of London for Palestine. We demand our government sanction the whole state of Israel and implement a full arms embargo. #StopArmingIsrael pic.twitter.com/TszfDImgNy
"After three years Israel continues to commit genocide against the Palestinian people in Gaza," it added.
Read More: Nearly 50,000 women, girls killed or severely injured in Gaza since October 2023: UN Women
As of 3:40 pm local time (1440GMT), over 250,000 people were on the streets in support of Palestine, the PSC said.
Since October 2023 , Israeli attacks have killed more than 74,000 Palestinians and wounded over 175,000 in Gaza. About 90% of the territory’s infrastructure has been destroyed.
Despite an October 2025 ceasefire agreement between Israel and the Palestinian group Hamas, Israeli attacks have since killed 1,454 Palestinians and wounded another 5,090, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry.
The Metropolitan Police said that, under the conditions imposed by the force, the crowd must follow a route along Victoria Embankment, Westminster Bridge, York Road, Waterloo Bridge and the Strand, onto Whitehall where a rally will take place.
It added that several arrests had been made so far, including a woman and a man carrying placards they said were "declaring support for the proscribed organisation Palestine Action".
Palestine Action was banned on July 5, 2025, under the Terrorism Act after members of the group entered a Royal Air Force base and spray-painted two aircraft, causing £7 million ($9.2 million) in damage, according to police.
The decision to ban the group has led to thousands of arrests of people accused of supporting it.
A small number of people from a pro-Israeli group also gathered outside New Scotland Yard near the area where pro-Palestine protesters assembled.

title: Erie  Pennsylvania shooter killed 8 people  then himself  police say
description: Gunman opened fire inside and outside a home before dying by suicide  ABC News reported  citing authorities
content:
Police yet to establish motive as eight of nine ​killed in shooting were family members, one was family friend
A 45-year-old man shot and killed eight people in Erie, Pennsylvania, ​including a pregnant woman and two children, then apparently shot himself to ‌death, authorities said on Saturday at a press conference where they revealed details of the previous evening's shooting.
The shooter, who has yet to be identified, died of an apparent self-inflicted wound before officers arrived on ​the scene, said Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah.
"Some scenes stay with you long ​after you leave them. This is one of those tragic scenes," Lorah ⁠said.
Police have yet to establish a motive, Lorah said. He said eight of the nine ​who died in the shooting were family members, and one was a family friend.
Lorah said ​after the shooter entered the home, he came out of the house and shot two women who appeared "distressed" and were pacing back and forth seeking assistance from neighbours.
Police found the suspect on the second floor ​of the home on Perry Street, Lorah said.
Read More: US arrests person in connection to Canada school shooting, officials say
Erie Mayor Daria Devlin said the police ​department "arrived at a horrific scene, faced unimaginable circumstances, and carried out their duties with courage and professionalism."
"They too ‌are ⁠members of this community, and they too will carry the weight of what happened last night," she said.
Earlier, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro said in a statement on X that he had spoken with Mayor Devlin and had offered support following "the tragic mass shooting."
Today we lost one of Pennsylvania’s finest — Philadelphia Police Officer Shane Seiber, who was shot and killed in the line of duty. Lori and I are praying for Officer Seiber’s loved ones and the entire @PhillyPolice family as they grieve the loss of one of their brothers in…
Shapiro has ​long advocated for "common sense ​gun safety," and pushed ⁠the Pennsylvania General Assembly in 2024 to pass gun reforms, including universal background checks and restrictions on ghost guns, which are homemade ​guns that lack serial numbers and cannot be traced. Several of ​Shapiro’s proposals have ⁠stalled in the state legislature.
There have been more than 400 mass shootings in the US in 2026, according to data compiled by Gun Violence Archive, which defines a mass shooting ⁠as one ​in which four or more people are shot, excluding ​the shooter. The last recorded mass shootings in Pennsylvania took place in July in Philadelphia, according to the ​data.

میری اور پورے پارلیمیٹرنیز کی سیکورٹی خیبر پختون خواہ پولیس نے واپس لے لی ۔ اگر مجھے یا کسی پارلیمیٹرین کو نقصان پہنچا تو اس کے ذمہ دار آئی جی خیبر پختون خواہ ھونگے ۔

The guidelines came as the threat of governor's rule looms over the province amid intense friction between the Centre and the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government on the issue of terrorism in the province and the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's long march to Islamabad.
The police issued written operational guidelines for dealing with riots and protests, stating that damage to government installations, buildings and property would not be permitted during any demonstration.
Read : PM Shehbaz, President Zardari discuss overall situation amid intense tensions between Centre, K-P
The guidelines warned that those participating in unlawful gatherings, violent activities or acts of provocation would face strict legal action.
Action would also be taken in accordance with the law against those disrupting public order, attacking security forces or buildings, or endangering the lives and property of citizens, the guidelines stated.
Citizens were urged to remain peaceful, abide by the law and avoid being misled by troublemakers.
According to the guidelines, special arrangements would be made to protect police stations, government buildings, banks, petrol pumps, commercial centres and major roads.
Protests and related activities would also be video-recorded to assist in subsequent legal proceedings.
The guidelines further stated that coordination with district administrations and other relevant institutions would be ensured to deal effectively with protest situations.
The federal government is considering various constitutional options, including the imposition of governor’s rule or an emergency in K-P, in view of the situation in the province. Consultations on the matter were continuing.
Earlier today, President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reviewed the overall political and security situation in the country, with the deteriorating law and order situation in K-P also coming under discussion.

Separately, PM Shehbaz also met Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman to discuss the situation in K-P and other political matters.
Later, K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met President Zardari and briefed him on the overall security situation in the country, particularly the deteriorating law and order situation in K-P.
The federal cabinet meeting has been convened for 9:30am on Sunday, where the situation in K-P and the available constitutional options are expected to be discussed.

title: PM Shehbaz takes notice of gold medallist   s suicide in Islamabad following education funds scam
description: Directs Islamabad police chief and chief commissioner to arrest the consultant accused of defrauding Laiba Ijaz
content:
Directs Islamabad police chief and chief commissioner to arrest the consultant accused of defrauding Laiba Ijaz.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday took notice of the death of Laiba Ijaz, a student at the International Islamic University Islamabad, who was found dead in the capital a day earlier.
Laiba, who had aspired to study at a US university, was found hanging from a tree near a road in Islamabad on Friday, after her family allegedly lost around Rs7 million to a consultant who had promised to secure her admission and a scholarship.
According to her family, they had lost around Rs7 million to a man who allegedly promised to secure her admission to a US university on a scholarship.
According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the premier described the young student’s death as an extremely regrettable incident.
وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف کا اسلام آباد میں انٹرنیشنل اسلامک یونیورسٹی کی طالبہ لائبہ اعجاز کی خود کشی کا نوٹس، وزیرِ اعظم نے کہا کہ نوجوان طالبہ کی خود کشی انتہائی افسوس ناک واقعہ ہے. وزیراعظم نے آئی جی اسلام آباد اور چیف کمشنر کو مرحومہ کے ساتھ فراڈ کرنے والے ملزم کو فوری طور… pic.twitter.com/qqzgkxbClA
“The accused should be arrested forthwith and awarded exemplary punishment in accordance with the law,” the prime minister said, directing the inspector general of Islamabad police and the chief commissioner to take immediate action against the suspect.
Laiba’s funeral prayers were offered on Saturday, with residents of the area mourning her death. Residents described her as an exceptionally talented and studious student.
FIA registers case, arrests main suspect
The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has registered a case against two suspects and arrested the main suspect in the case.
The FIA’s Anti-Human Trafficking Circle in Islamabad took action after the victim’s family approached the agency following her burial. After completing an inquiry, the agency registered a case against suspects Muhammad Nauman and Fatima Sarwar under Sections 419 (cheating), 420 (cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property) and 109 (abetment) of the Pakistan Penal Code, read with Sections 18 and 22 of the Emigration Ordinance, 1979.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspects allegedly acted in connivance to deceive Laiba, the niece of complainant Amjadur Rehman, with promises of a US visa and scholarship. They allegedly received a total of Rs9.3 million from the family.
Read : Islamabad student found dead after allegedly losing Rs7m in education scam
The FIA said the suspects allegedly prepared fake scholarship award letters, university admission offer letters and fee payment receipts to keep the family under the impression that the process was genuine.
Of the total amount, Rs2.9m was transferred through Laiba’s personal bank account, while the remaining sum was received in cash, according to the agency.
Meanwhile, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry visited the bereaved family after taking notice of the incident. They offered their condolences and assured the family that justice would be served.
Following the interior minister’s directions, the FIA launched efforts to arrest the suspects. Raids were being conducted at various locations under the supervision of the FIA Islamabad Zone director, the report said.
The main suspect has been arrested and is being interrogated, according to sources. FIA officials said the investigation would also determine the role of any other individuals who might have been involved in the case.
The FIA Islamabad Zone said it was committed to bringing all those responsible for the alleged fraud against Laiba to justice.
The family alleged that the suspect had lured Laiba with the promise of a scholarship at Harvard and provided her with a forged scholarship letter. They said he had also portrayed himself as her sponsor to obtain money from them.
According to the family, the suspect claimed to be an accounts officer at the Islamabad High Court and at other times presented himself as an employee of the superior judiciary or an officer of a sensitive institution.
The family further alleged that he had promised to secure a government job for Laiba’s brother and taken an additional Rs500,000 for the purpose.
Laiba’s brother had asked their father for money to start a business, but their father had decided to spend his resources on educating his daughter, the family said.
According to Laiba’s brother-in-law, the International Islamic University had offered her a scholarship to study in Saudi Arabia after she secured good marks in her bachelor’s degree.
When Laiba told the suspect about the offer, he allegedly claimed that he could arrange a scholarship for her in the United States instead.
The family said Laiba and her father had communicated with the suspect exclusively through WhatsApp. They also alleged that a woman was involved in the scheme. The suspect had told Laiba that the woman was based in the United States and worked for his company, they added.
The family alleged that the suspect had posed as an agent to facilitate Laiba’s travel abroad but had defrauded them instead. They said a forged admission letter purportedly issued by Harvard University had also been provided.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also visited the family, accompanied by Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry.
وفاقی وزیر داخلہ محسن نقوی اور وزیر مملکت طلال چوہدری کی جی 10 میں متوفیہ طالبہ لائبہ کی رہائش گاہ آمد وفاقی وزیرداخلہ اور وزیر مملکت کی طالبہ لائبہ کے والد اور اہل خانہ سے ملاقات، المناک واقعہ پر گہرے دکھ اور افسوس کا اظہار pic.twitter.com/XzNZvvYN5k
Addressing a press conference later, Naqvi vowed strict action against those involved in the case, saying the authorities would ensure the arrest of the suspects, recover the money taken from victims and bring those responsible to justice.
“We will soon arrest everyone involved in this incident. We will also recover the money and ensure that they are punished,” the interior minister said, adding that the police and the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) were actively pursuing the case.
He described the matter as a test case and said the authorities would take action against individuals involved in fraud and related criminal networks. He also urged the public to give the police sufficient time to apprehend the suspect.
Naqvi said the case would be pursued on a priority basis and pledged to personally oversee its progress.
“The suspect is not part of the gang involved in the case; he is a swindler,” he said, distinguishing the individual under investigation from the wider criminal network.
The minister further stated that PM Shehbaz had directed him to ensure that arrests were made in connection with the case.
Naqvi also discussed the government's efforts to combat human smuggling and trafficking.
He said the European Union had acknowledged a reduction of up to 64% in human smuggling. Referring to his recent visit to Türkiye, he added that the Turkish government had acknowledged a decline in human trafficking linked to illegal gangs, from 70% to 17%.
“We will eliminate these gangs involved in trafficking by the will of Allah,” he said.
The interior minister also highlighted operational challenges facing the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), stating that the department had a staff strength of 61 and received approximately 3,000 complaints daily.
He said recommendations had been forwarded to the prime minister to improve the department's efficiency and strengthen its capacity to handle complaints.
Naqvi added that the government was working to integrate the NCCIA's complaint system with the Pak ID platform to enable authorities to monitor progress in individual cases.
He said further details about the initiative would be announced in the coming days, expressing confidence that the public would soon notice improvements in the system.

title: Flurry of meetings in Islamabad as govt increasingly hints towards governor s rule in K P
description: Governor Kundi meets with Minister Amir Muqam to discuss overall situation in K P  vow to ensure peace
content:
PM Shehbaz, Fazl discuss easing tensions; Naqvi says no room left now; PTI welcomes Fazl's role
Saturday night saw a flurry of meetings in Islamabad to deliberate on the country's overall political and security situation amid intense friction between the Centre and the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government on the issue of terrorism in the province and the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's long march to Islamabad that has led to threats of imposing federal rule.
In a post on X, the Presidency said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Asif Ali Zardari met at the Aiwan-e-Sadr where they "exchanged views on the country's overall political and security situation".
The meeting comprised senior government and PPP leaders, including Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Prime Minister's Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Federal Minister for Interior Mohsin Naqvi, Attorney General Mansoor Usman Awan, Minister for Law and Justice Azam Nazeer Tarar, Senator Sherry Rehman and more.
"It was agreed in the meeting to convene separate sessions of the National Assembly and Senate on Tuesday," the statement said.
صدرِ مملکت آصف علی زرداری سے وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف کی ایوانِ صدر میں ملاقات، ملک کی مجموعی سیاسی اور سیکیورٹی صورتِ حال پر تبادلہ خیال۔ ملاقات میں وزیر اعظم کی معاونت نائب وزیراعظم سینیٹر اسحاق ڈار، وزیراعظم کے مشیر برائے سیاسی امور سینیٹر رانا ثناء الّلہ، وفاقی وزیر داخلہ… pic.twitter.com/r1T1bTXTy4
Questioned about the meeting, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry said on a private television channel’s talk show that a detailed discussion had taken place on the possibility of imposing an emergency, but negotiations were still under way and all options were being considered.
He said the government had exhausted several avenues, including parliamentary engagement and backchannel contacts, before considering the measure, describing an emergency as a last resort for a political government.
“It's definitely not a praiseworthy move and for a political government such a measure is always a last resort,” he said, adding that different levels and options of an emergency as well as other constitutional options had been discussed.
Chaudhry said the government was still assessing the situation, although he saw developments moving towards what he called the “last option”.
He argued that the federal government had offered to accommodate the opposition’s political demands if it agreed to support the centre’s efforts against terrorism under the National Action Plan (NAP), which he said had been developed by the PTI founder.
Recalling the second day of government-opposition negotiations before the proposed long march, he said PM Shehbaz had told the interior minister that the opposition could have its political demands met if it supported the centre in the fight against terrorism.
Chaudhry questioned what options would remain if the government met the opposition’s political demands but the latter did not unequivocally condemn militant groups or support counterterrorism efforts. He also alleged that the proposed long march was targeting national policy in a manner that could incite rebellion against the state.
The minister said the federal government had not drafted a new counterterrorism document and was instead implementing the framework prepared under the PTI government.
Responding to the PTI’s position that all stakeholders should be included in dialogue on counterterrorism, the minister questioned the provincial government’s commitment to tackling militancy. He cited the absence of counterterrorism departments, forensic laboratories and safe-city surveillance cameras, and alleged that provincial leaders had avoided attending the funerals of security personnel killed in terrorist attacks.
He maintained that talks with the K-P government had never completely stopped, including through other political parties.
Meanwhile, Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Engineer Amir Muqam called for the imposition of governor’s rule across K-P, citing what he described as the provincial government’s failure to maintain law and order and establish its writ.
“There is no writ of the government in K-P, nor does it have any [governance] priorities,” he said, alleging that terrorists were operating freely because of inadequate security arrangements and a lack of checkpoints.
“We collect dead bodies every day,” he said, accusing the provincial government of failing to adequately condemn attacks on the armed forces or take decisive action against militants.
Referring to the security situation in Lakki Marwat and Bannu, he said residents were increasingly reluctant to move around, while militant activity and insecurity continued to affect daily life. However, the PTI rally, suggesting support from terror outfits, moved around freely in these no-go areas at night.
“We, too, are citizens of Pakistan who deserve to live in peace,” he said. Muqam argued that if the provincial government was unable to protect citizens and enforce its authority, the federal government should intervene.
He thereby reiterated that governor’s rule should be implemented throughout the province for the sake of people’s well-being and safety.
Speaking on talks between the opposition and the government, the minister said the negotiations with PTI and other members of the opposition had included a proposal for a joint declaration by the K-P chief minister and the interior minister explicitly condemning terrorism, but claimed that Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had backed away from the proposal.
He also alleged that the negotiations had failed because of the chief minister’s reluctance to call out terrorism for what it truly is, while maintaining that the delegation of opposition had been sincere in seeking a resolution of conflict and the dialogue was foiled by the chief minister.
When probed whether the federal government had support of the people of K-P regarding the mulled constitutional measures including emergency imposition, Muqam claimed that 5,000 to 6,000 people had attended a rally he organised in support of peace in the province, despite short notice and an internet shutdown. He interpreted the participation as evidence of public opposition to the provincial government.
The federal government’s deliberations come amid continuing political differences over the province’s security situation, the implementation of the National Action Plan and the role of the provincial administration in countering terrorism. With negotiations reportedly still in progress, an emergency or governor’s rule remains a matter under discussion rather than a confirmed decision.
Later, the president held a meeting with K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, in which they briefed him on the overall security situation in the country, particularly the deteriorating law and order situation in K-P.
The president was informed about security matters in the province and issues related to law and order in the country.
گورنر خیبر پختونخوا فیصل کریم کنڈی اور وفاقی وزیر داخلہ سینیٹر محسن نقوی کی صدرِ مملکت آصف علی زرداری سے ملاقات۔ صدرِ مملکت کو ملک کی مجموعی سیکیورٹی صورتحال، بالخصوص خیبر پختونخوا میں بگڑتی ہوئی امن و امان کی صورتحال پر بریفنگ۔ ملاقات میں خیبر پختونخوا کی سیکیورٹی اور ملک میں… pic.twitter.com/6gftMtjZkr
In a post on X, Kundi said: "KP has sacrificed enough. Protecting lives and defeating terrorism must take precedence over political interests."
Called on @PresOfPakistan Asif Ali Zardari alongside Federal Interior Minister Senator @MohsinnaqviC42 to brief him on the deteriorating security situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the country’s overall law and order. KP has sacrificed enough. Protecting lives and defeating… pic.twitter.com/P2sikowz8t
Speaking to the media elsewhere, Naqvi asked: "Is there really any room left to avoid imposing an emergency? You tell me, how can this matter be averted? Ask them just how much effort I have made to find a solution. They will tell you themselves the extent of the efforts Mohsin Naqvi has made to resolve the issue."
The interior minister reiterated that there was "no room left now".
Amid the friction between the Centre and K-P, Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman has once again jumped into the fray as a possible mediator.
He held a meeting with the premier at the PM House, in which consultations were held on "important national and political matters".
وزیرِ اعظم محمد شہباز شریف اور سربراہ جمیعت علماء اسلام مولانا فضل الرحمن کے درمیان وزیر اعظم ہاؤس میں ملاقات، اہم قومی و سیاسی امور پر مشاورت ہوئی. pic.twitter.com/6rI4uWUadF
The JUI said the meeting took place at PM Shehbaz's invitation and the PTI leadership was taken into confidence as well before leaving for the talks.
وزیر اعظم مولانا فضل الرحمان ملاقات مولانا فضل الرحمان اپنی رہائش گاہ سے وزیراعظم ہاؤس روانہ ہو گئے۔ ترجمان جےیوآئی ملاقات وزیر اعظم کی دعوت پر ہو رہی ہے۔ ترجمان جےیوآئی وفد میں سنیٹر مولانا عطاء الحق درویش۔ مولانا لطف الرحمان ۔ اور سنیٹر کامران مرتضی شامل ہیں۔اسلم غوری…
The meeting came after PM Shehbaz and Fazl earlier discussed ways to ease tensions between the federal and K-P governments during a telephone conversation, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.
“Fazl also spoke to the prime minister about reducing tensions between the federal government and the K-P government,” the statement added.
وزیراعظم شہباز شریف کا مولانا فضل الرحمان سے ٹیلی فونک رابطہ۔ @CMShehbaz pic.twitter.com/BJ90XusJtz
JUI-F spokesperson Aslam Ghauri, in a statement released by the party's media cell, said the two leaders had discussed the current political situation and the ongoing tensions between the federal and K-P governments.
Ghauri added that Fazl remained in regular contact with the PTI leadership and had taken it into confidence as part of efforts to ease political tensions in the country.
ترجمان:جےیوآئی 10 اکتوبر اسلام آباد: وزیراعظم میاں شہباز شریف کا امیر جے یو آئی مولانا فضل الرحمان سے ٹیلی فونک رابطہ وزیراعظم میاں شہباز شریف کی امیر جے یو آئی مولانا فضل الرحمان سے موجودہ سیاسی صورتحال پر گفتگو ہوئی ۔ خیبرپختونخوا حکومت اور وفاق کے درمیان جاری تناؤ ختم کرنے…
Speaking to The Express Tribune , PTI Secretary Information Sheikh Waqas Akram said that the party would welcome a positive and effective role by Fazl in reducing the ongoing political tensions and uncertainty in the country.
Akram stated that his intervention would be “welcomed”, adding that PTI would appreciate his efforts in this regard.
He emphasised that Pakistan needed political wisdom, patience, serious and meaningful initiatives, and dialogue rather than confrontation to address the current political challenges.
Earlier, Muqam and Governor Kundi held a meeting at the Governor House in Peshawar, state-run Radio Pakistan reported.
During the meeting, they discussed the overall law and order situation in K-P, the ongoing long march, and other significant political matters. Expressing their gratitude to the people of K-P, both leaders said that the public has rejected the "politics of chaos".
A joint statement issued after the meeting affirmed that the federal government would take all possible measures to ensure peace and promote public welfare and development in the province.
Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor @fkkundi held a meeting at the Governor House in Peshawar today. During the meeting, they discussed the overall law and order situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa #News #RadioPakistan …
The contact came as the PTI’s long march is scheduled to travel from Charsadda to Mardan on Saturday, amid efforts to revive dialogue between the government and opposition.
Fazl has emerged as a possible intermediary as efforts to revive negotiations continue. PTI K-P President Junaid Akbar said the party had authorised the JUI-F chief to mediate between the government and opposition, while PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan called for unconditional dialogue and urged both sides to find a way forward.
The latest efforts followed two rounds of negotiations between the government and opposition that ended without an agreement. The sides remained divided over PTI’s demand for access to its jailed founder, Imran Khan, and the role of the K-P government in determining counterterrorism policy. PTI said a joint strategy involving the federal and provincial governments was needed, while the government maintained that cooperation from the provincial administration was essential.
Efforts to resume dialogue have continued as the long march advances, with PTI leaders pressing for renewed negotiations while government figures have urged the party to reconsider its protest.
The march began on October 4 after the initial attempts to reach an agreement failed, and its route is subsequently scheduled to take the convoy through Charsadda and Mardan before reaching Swabi. PTI has said it would announce its next course of action after reaching Swabi.
The political standoff has also fuelled speculation about possible emergency measures and changes to K-P’s administrative structure. Reports citing sources have suggested that a proposal to establish a separate administrative arrangement for 12 districts is under consideration.
Sources have said that the federal government is weighing options including governor’s rule and an emergency as tensions with the provincial government deepen.

title: Fatima Fertilizer secures top position at UN GCNP Sustainability Awards 2026
description: Company recognised for its people focused approach and commitment to advancing the sustainable development goals
content:
Company recognised for its people-focused approach and commitment to advancing the sustainable development goals
Fatima Fertilizer Company Limited has been awarded First Position in the Human Rights category at the United Nations Global Compact Network Pakistan (GCNP) Sustainability Awards 2026.
The distinction recognises the organisation’s steadfast commitment to ethical business operations, inclusive practices, and the advancement of social well-being across its workforce, agricultural partners, and broader local communities.
The award marks another milestone in Fatima Fertilizer’s evolving sustainability journey, which was formally anchored in November 2024 when the Company became the first private-sector organisation in Pakistan to formally adopt the UNDP SDG Impact Framework.
Through the framework, Fatima Fertilizer has mapped its activities against 15 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and 49 targets across eight priority impact areas.
The Company’s sustainability approach integrates responsible business practices with its core role in supporting Pakistan’s agriculture sector and contributing to the wellbeing of the communities it serves.
Its initiatives span farmer livelihoods and food security, employee wellbeing, women’s empowerment, education and skills development, environmental stewardship, climate action, resource efficiency, digital inclusion and responsible agricultural practices.
Rabel Sadozai, Director Marketing and Sales, Fatima Fertilizer quoted:
Being recognised in the Human Rights category is a meaningful affirmation of our people-centred approach to sustainability. At Fatima Fertilizer, we remain committed to creating lasting value for our employees, farmers and communities while advancing responsible business practices and contributing to the Sustainable Development Goals.
The recognition also reflects Fatima Fertilizer’s efforts to advance a number of SDGs, including SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being), SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities), and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production).
The UN GCNP Sustainability Awards 2026 recognition adds to Fatima Fertilizer’s growing portfolio of national and international sustainability and impact recognitions and reflects the Company’s continued ambition to integrate sustainability into its business strategy, operations and long-term value creation.

title: Nintendo leaves GTA 6 Switch 2 possibility up to Rockstar Games
description: Nintendo of America president Devon Pritchard says potential GTA 6 Switch 2 release is up to Rockstar and Take Two
content:
Nintendo of America president Devon Pritchard says potential GTA 6 Switch 2 release is up to Rockstar and Take-Two
Nintendo of America president Devon Pritchard has left the possibility of Grand Theft Auto VI coming to Switch 2 to Rockstar Games and publisher Take-Two Interactive, offering no confirmation of a potential port.
Speaking in a recent interview, Pritchard said the decision would be a matter for the companies behind the upcoming game. According to Kotaku , she added that she had nothing to announce.
GTA 6 is not scheduled to arrive on Switch 2 at launch, leaving the Nintendo console out of the game’s initial release plans. However, Pritchard’s comments did not rule out a future version.
Nintendo Life noted that bringing the game to Switch 2 could require considerable optimisation. The publication also pointed to technologies such as DLSS and frame generation, which can improve image quality and performance on supported hardware.
Whether the console can run GTA 6 to a satisfactory standard remains unclear. The game is expected to be a major entertainment release, but neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has announced plans for a Switch 2 version.
Other Rockstar titles are also absent from the console. Grand Theft Auto V and Red Dead Redemption 2 have not received Switch 2 ports, despite releases on other platforms.
The original Red Dead Redemption, however, arrived on Switch 2 in late 2025 with improved visuals and performance.
Fong, a technical director at Virtuous, the studio behind the Nintendo Switch port of L.A. Noire, said the team was interested in adapting Rockstar’s other games for the system.
Switch 2 owners can already play Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy – The Definitive Edition on the console, offering access to earlier entries in the series.
Meanwhile, Nintendo has its own releases scheduled around GTA 6’s planned November launch. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is due on November 5.

title: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections  sets presidential poll for September 2027
description: Doubts cloud Palestinian vote next month  no legislative or presidential elections have been held since 2005 06
content:
Doubts cloud Palestinian vote next month; no legislative or presidential elections have been held since 2005-06
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections due next month until September 11, 2027, and called a presidential poll for the same date, blaming Israel and the security situation in the Palestinian territories for the delay.
Abbas' decree cited "obstacles posed by Israeli measures" and the need to establish suitable political, security and on-the-ground ​conditions for "free, fair and inclusive elections", the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.
The decree called on Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West ​Bank and Gaza to vote.
There had been serious doubts that the Palestinian Authority vote would go ahead next month. ⁠The Palestinians have not held legislative or presidential elections since 2005-06, after which Abbas' rival Hamas, seized control of Gaza, ousting ​his loyalists.
Abbas has ruled by decree since his presidential mandate expired in 2009.
The Palestinian Authority held municipal elections in April in the West Bank ​and in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza, the only city in the enclave to participate. The vote was the first election held in Gaza since 2006.
The decree said Israeli military attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence and movement restrictions in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, along with Israel's continued withholding of Palestinian tax revenues, created ​challenges to preparing for and holding elections this November.
In Gaza , the decree pointed to "exceptional security and humanitarian conditions", the incomplete withdrawal of Israeli forces, the ​lack of progress in reconstruction and the failure to implement arrangements for deploying international stabilisation forces and police.
Read More: Nearly 50,000 women, girls killed or severely injured in Gaza since October 2023: UN Women
Israeli restrictions on access for election commission staff and international ‌observers to ⁠Gaza and East Jerusalem also complicated preparations, the decree said.
There was no immediate Israeli comment on Abbas' announcement, with officials unavailable for comment on Saturday, the Jewish Sabbath. Israel typically bans the Palestinian Authority from holding elections in East Jerusalem, territory it captured in the 1967 war and later annexed in a move most countries do not recognise.
The decision to postpone followed consultations with Palestinian factions and political forces. It also aimed to ​allow time for a comprehensive Palestinian ​national dialogue to strengthen unity ⁠and address challenges facing the electoral process.
Two Palestinian officials told Reuters on Thursday that leaders of Abbas' Fatah movement and rival Hamas had agreed at a meeting in Cairo on ​Wednesday to postpone the elections.
An August poll by the West Bank-based Palestinian Centre for Policy and Survey Research showed declining support ⁠for both Hamas and Fatah, which many Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank blame for their continuing political divisions.
The delay comes just weeks after Abbas reaffirmed the November election timetable in his September 24 address to the UN General Assembly, as he sought to advance internationally backed reforms.
Abbas had committed ⁠in writing ​to French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to hold ​presidential and legislative elections as part of France's recognition of a Palestinian state in September 2025.
France's foreign ministry said on Thursday that holding the elections was essential and it welcomed the ​launch of an EU election observation mission.

Spokesperson says the officer lost his life after unidentified suspects opened fire on him
Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) Director General Shamshad Akhtar was martyred in a terrorist attack in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's Tank district on Saturday after unidentified armed men opened fire on him.
A press release from the ECP spokesperson described the incident as a targeted killing, stating that the officer was an honest, conscientious and dedicated public servant who had no personal enmity with anyone.
According to the statement, the late officer was held in high regard by his colleagues and fellow officers.
“The chief election commissioner, members of the commission, the ECP secretary and other staff express deep grief and sorrow over his death,” the press release stated further.
Extending their condolences to the bereaved family, they said the entire commission stood with them during this difficult time. They also prayed for the deceased’s forgiveness and elevation of his status in the hereafter, and for patience and strength for his family.
The ECP and its employees called on the government to take effective measures to protect all government employees from terrorist attacks.
K-P has faced persistent militant violence in 2026, with the province’s southern districts, including Tank, Bannu, Lakki Marwat and Dera Ismail Khan, emerging as major security hotspots. In May, The Express Tribune reported that provincial police had sought a special federal security package to strengthen police stations, establish new posts and upgrade security infrastructure in the affected districts.
The threat has also become more sophisticated, with militants increasingly deploying drones, thermal imaging and night-vision equipment against police personnel and security installations.
According to The Express Tribune , 156 police personnel were killed in militant attacks across K-P and its tribal districts between January and July 2026. Violence remained concentrated in Hangu, Bannu, Karak, Tank, Lakki Marwat, Dera Ismail Khan, and Khyber, and was reportedly spreading to the mountainous areas of Malakand Division, including Swat.
Tank witnessed several deadly attacks this year.
On July 24, at least 15 security personnel and a government official were martyred in an attack on a joint police and security forces checkpost in the district. Then again, on September 28, three traffic police personnel were martyred when unidentified armed men opened fire on their vehicle in the Wazirabad area of Tank.
The attacks underscore the continuing vulnerability of law-enforcement personnel in the province’s southern districts.

title: New large docodont fossil sheds light on Jurassic mammaliaform diversity
description: Scientists discovered Megacauda sungei  the largest known docodont mammaliaform  with a long  coiled tail
content:
Scientists discovered Megacauda sungei, the largest known docodont mammaliaform, with a long, coiled tail
An international team led by Chinese scientists has discovered a new docodont mammaliaform species, the largest known of its kind, in Jurassic strata dating back about 160 million years, enriching scientific understanding of Jurassic mammaliaform diversity.
The new species has been named Megacauda sungei. Its fossil specimen, discovered in Ningcheng, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, measures roughly 52 centimeters in length and is estimated to have weighed around 2 kilograms, making it the largest known docodont mammaliaform. Its skull is clearly preserved, its trunk is robust, and its most striking feature is an unusually long, coiled tail.
The specimen also retains well-preserved pelvic bones, hind limbs and tail vertebrae, suggesting it was adapted for swimming. Based on its distinctive teeth, researchers believe it could have hunted small animals living in the same environment, with a lifestyle possibly similar to that of the modern platypus.
The study also sheds light on the animal's throat structure. The bones in its throat are similar to those of modern mammals, suggesting that behaviors such as swallowing, lapping and suckling may have already existed in the early ancestors of mammals, long before modern mammal groups appeared.
"Mammaliaforms from the Mesozoic are often imagined as tiny creatures under dinosaur feet, but Megacauda sungei clearly raises the size limit of this group," said Li Yikun, an associate professor at Shenyang Normal University in northeast China.
The study was published online in the journal Nature on October 7.

title: 3 in 5 AI models fail terrorism safety tests  Study
description: UK nonprofit Tech Against Terrorism tested over 130 AI models with hundreds of simulated terrorist attack
content:
UK nonprofit Tech Against Terrorism tested over 130 AI models with hundreds of simulated terrorist attack
Three in five artificial intelligence (AI) models have failed terrorism safety tests, with models stripped of safeguards consistently providing potentially dangerous information, according to research reported by CBC News on Friday.
The study, conducted by the UK-based nonprofit Tech Against Terrorism , evaluated more than 130 AI models using hundreds of requests resembling those a terrorist planning an attack might submit.
Researchers found that models modified through a process known as "abliteration," which removes safety safeguards, failed every test.
Meta's Llama 3.1 8B model scored 97 out of 100 on the organization's safety benchmark before modification, compared with approximately three afterward.
Researchers said the modified model provided detailed responses to requests involving attacks, terrorist financing and radicalization, while its original version refused such requests.
Read More: Anthropic discloses fake tip to police among new rogue AI incidents
Understandably, there's concern about loss of control, existential risk of AI," said Adam Hadley, founder and executive director of Tech Against Terrorism.
"The thing is actually, this has already happened because a lot of these open models have already been broken — it's just no one's noticed yet."
The organization found more than 29,000 repositories advertising uncensored or unprotected AI models on Hugging Face as of late last month.
Hugging Face said it regularly moderates content violating its policies but warned that some recommendations in the report could undermine open research.
Meta said its models undergo safety evaluations and that its policies prohibit harmful or illegal uses.
The report found no evidence of terrorist or extremist groups using the tested models, apart from one extremist chatbot identified by researchers.
Tech Against Terrorism recommended independent safety benchmarks, stronger protections against safeguard removal and restrictions on distributing modified models.
"This idea that we can't have safety and progress, I think, is false," Hadley said.

title: Renshaw   s 190 puts Australia ahead
description: Record breaking knock gives visitors control against South Africa
content:
Record-breaking knock gives visitors control against South Africa
Matt Renshaw struck a superb career-best 190 and helped Australia take control of the first Test against hosts South Africa as they were bowled out for 390 on the second day at Kingsmead on Saturday.
Renshaw and Nathan Lyon (27) shared a record ninth-wicket stand of 134 for Australia against South Africa, the highest partnership ⁠for that wicket in Durban.
Renshaw went to tea with Josh Hazlewood (5 not out), though they have now used up 137 overs and five sessions on their first innings with bad light potentially an issue for the second day in a row.
However, his resilience came to an end when he was caught in the slip by Aiden Markram on the second delivery just after tea. He scored 190.
Australia were in trouble early in Renshaw's innings as they slipped to 124 for six on day one.
But he has flipped the script after putting on 86 for the seventh wicket with skipper Pat Cummins (43) before swinging the test squarely in the favour of the touring side.
His score is the highest by a ⁠number five batter in tests at Kingsmead.
Australia started the second day on 187 for six and frustrated the home side before Wiaan Mulder (4-68) had Cummins caught by Aiden Markram at second slip.
Mitchell Starc (6) followed quickly after being bowled by Mulder, and at that stage it looked as though South Africa would ⁠run through the lower order.
Lyon was circumspect, however, and Renshaw rotated the strike superbly to make sure he had most of the strike and continued to accumulate runs rather than attack the bowling.
Lyon eventually ⁠fell LBW to Marco Jansen (3-63).
Renshaw’s 190 has come off 395 balls, a classic test innings of patience and waiting for the bad ball.
He was struck in the helmet by ⁠speedster Anrich Nortje, but he soon settled again and his second test century came nine years after his first, 185 against Pakistan in 2017.
Renshaw had made single-figure scores in 11 of his previous 13 test innings.

title: Rahmat   s unbeaten 84 keeps Afghanistan afloat

content:
Hosts reach 211-4 after Bangladesh post 346 in first innings
Afghanistan captain Rahmat Shah struck an unbeaten 84 to keep his side in contention after Bangladesh posted 346 in their first innings on the second day of the one-off Test at the Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abu Dhabi on Saturday.
Rahmat displayed patience and composure throughout his 186-ball innings, striking eight fours and a six to guide Afghanistan to 211-4 at stumps. His unbeaten 72-run partnership with wicketkeeper batsman Ikram Alikhil, who remained not out on 26, helped the hosts recover after losing four wickets.
Alikhil faced 91 balls and struck three fours as the pair kept Afghanistan’s hopes of gaining a first-innings lead alive.
After losing two early wickets, Afghanistan needed a substantial partnership to stabilise their innings. Rahmat joined Abdul Malik at the crease, and the duo added 70 runs for the third wicket to revive their side’s hopes.
Bangladesh seamer Ebadot Hossain provided the breakthrough when he dismissed Malik, who edged the ball to wicket-keeper Litton Das, leaving Afghanistan at 134-3.
Malik, who hails from Baghlan, scored his maiden Test half-century before departing for 62 off 120 deliveries. His innings included four fours and a six.
Afghanistan suffered another setback when Hashmatullah Shahidi was stumped by Litton off spinner Mehidy Hasan Miraz for a duck, leaving the visitors struggling at 139-4.
Alikhil then joined Rahmat, and the pair batted resolutely to prevent further damage and steer Afghanistan towards a respectable total.
Earlier, Afghanistan had made a cautious start before Bangladesh struck twice to reduce the visitors to 64-2 in the 21st over.
Hasan Mahmud claimed the first wicket, dismissing Sediqullah Atal, who was caught by Tanzid Hasan for 17 off 31 balls, including three fours.
Shahidullah joined Malik but could not build a substantial partnership, falling for 20 off 44 deliveries after offering a catch to Hasan Mahmud off Ebadot.
Ebadot was Bangladesh’s most successful bowler, finishing with figures of 2-50 in 11 overs. Hasan and Mehidy claimed one wicket apiece.
Earlier in the day, Bangladesh resumed their first innings at the overnight score of 317-8 and were bowled out for 346 in 92.3 overs.
Nayeem Hasan, who was unbeaten on 11 at Friday’s close, remained not out on 35 off 67 balls, hitting four fours. He received valuable support from Taijul Islam, who scored nine, as the pair added 30 runs for the ninth wicket.
For Afghanistan, medium fast bowler Mohammad Saleem led the attack with 4-82 in 23 overs, while his new-ball partner Yamin Ahmadzai claimed 3-79 in 20.3 overs.
With six wickets still in hand, Afghanistan will look to build on Rahmat’s determined innings and narrow the deficit when play resumes.

title: Anthropic discloses fake tip to police among new rogue AI incidents
description: Rogue AI appears to submit bogus tip to authorities despite restrictions on destructive actions
content:
Rogue AI appears to submit bogus tip to authorities despite restrictions on destructive actions
An Anthropic artificial intelligence model submitted a ​false homicide tip to a Philadelphia police website, among a string of incidents the AI company disclosed on Friday detailing ‌Claude models' unsanctioned manipulation of some government websites.
It is the first known instance in which a rogue AI appears to have tried to communicate a bogus tip to authorities, despite instructions not to create accounts or submit anything destructive, while not explicitly barred from submitting forms.
The cases are the latest examples of rogue or undesired behavior by the AI ​models of tech companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI.
They add fuel to national concerns about the fast-advancing technology amid reports of corporate ​network hacks by AI agents, and researchers' warnings of an eventual existential threat to humanity.
Many of the cases Anthropic ⁠revealed involved websites run by federal, state and local agencies. Anthropic said it briefed the White House and notified all the agencies involved, but ​did not disclose who those parties were.
"Super intelligence companies must immediately disclose incidents involving their models and follow with swift, decisive action to remedy any ​and all harm," FTC Director of Public Affairs Joe Gabriel Simonson said on X.
“Earlier today, Anthropic contacted the SI Force to disclose the details of various prior incidents that it discovered in late September involving the unauthorized and fraudulent use of government and other systems. The company informed us that these events occurred in the past,…
This process was "not optional," he said, adding that the Super Intelligence Force would fulfill its responsibility.
The FTC said Anthropic disclosed to the SI Force on Friday its late September discovery of incidents involving what the task force called "unauthorized and fraudulent use of government and ​other systems".
Tip attributed to automated test process
On Friday, Philadelphia police said Anthropic notified them of the spurious tip this week, and attributed the submissions ​to an automated testing process.
"The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the city is unacceptable," they said.
The July 18 tip purported to come from someone ‌who might ⁠have information about the case, police added.
"I may have information regarding this case," Anthropic's model wrote in its submission.
"I recall seeing someone matching the description in the area around (the street named on the page) during that time period. Please contact me if this information is relevant." The brackets featured in Anthropic's statement.
Previous incidents have involved AI agents hacking into vulnerable systems or commandeering unsanctioned platforms to communicate with one another.
Read More: China vows to curb tech bubbles, keep AI risks in check
In September, Anthropic rival OpenAI apologized for ​the hacking of an Australian health ​data portal by a rogue ⁠AI agent, the first known instance of an AI agent exploiting a government website.
In two cases described on Friday, Anthropic’s models obtained for free public data normally only available for a fee. Another instanced revealed an ​obscure flaw that allowed use of a public tool hosted by a university.
Claude models were also able to ​bypass restrictions by ⁠using free services that shorten URLs.
Philadelphia police said the tip "was flagged as spam and was never forwarded to the Real-Time Crime Center for investigative vetting or dissemination."
Knowingly giving false reports to law enforcement authorities is a misdemeanor under Pennsylvania law, which specifies "a person", however.
This includes "information relating to an offense or incident when he ⁠knows he ​has no information relating to such offense or incident."
Police quoted Anthropic as telling them the ​test process was stopped after discovery of the incident. The false tip was submitted through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com concerning an unsolved homicide.
Police said they had no evidence of unauthorized access to their systems ​or compromise of their data.

title: Jessica Chastain   s    Other Mommy    makes five major changes to horror book
description: Josh Malerman   s 2024 novel gives its demon a more unsettling appearance than the film adaptation
content:
Josh Malerman’s 2024 novel gives its demon a more unsettling appearance than the film adaptation
Other Mommy , starring Jessica Chastain, makes several significant changes to Josh Malerman’s 2024 horror novel Incidents Around the House , including a gruesome death scene and a dramatically different ending.
The film follows Bela, played by Arabella Olivia Clark, a young girl who encounters a sinister entity that takes the appearance of her mother, Ursula, portrayed by Chastain. Although the adaptation retains the central threat, it changes key details to heighten the horror on screen.
One major difference is the demon’s appearance. In the film, the entity can convincingly imitate humans, although subtle signs reveal its supernatural nature. In Malerman’s novel, it has more distinctly unsettling features, including an avian appearance, unstable facial features and a foul smell that affects those nearby.
The séance sequence also differs considerably. In the film, Grandma Ruth, played by Karen Allen, organises a séance that summons the entity and ends with members of a ghost hunting group being killed. The book instead features fraudulent spiritualists who quickly admit they cannot help the family.
Another change involves a frightening encounter at a family entertainment restaurant. Bela follows what she believes is a new friend before the entity pulls her into an endless ball pit. The sequence develops into a surreal ordeal involving the sea and the family car. In the novel, the comparable incident takes place at a playground and ends with Bela suffering a serious fall.
The film also adds a particularly graphic death. Family friend Frank, played by Arian Moayed, becomes the target of the entity after Bela suggests her family might be better off without him. The creature kills him in a bloody scene. In the novel, Frank’s death is reported rather than shown in this manner.
The biggest change comes at the conclusion. The film ends with Bela resisting the entity, leaving her family together. The novel takes a far bleaker direction: the demon assumes Grandma Ruth’s appearance, leads Bela’s parents to their deaths and eventually takes control of Bela after she lets it into her heart.
These differences give the adaptation a distinct ending while preserving the story’s central psychological horror.
