title: Aamer calls for better coaching
description: Former Pakistan   s captain says coaching gaps hinder country   s cricket progress
content:
Former Pakistan’s captain says coaching gaps hinder country’s cricket progress
Former Pakistan captain Aamer Sohail has praised the Pakistan Cricket Board’s (PCB) investment in modern facilities at the National Cricket Academy but warned that better coaching standards are needed to translate those improvements into results on the field.
Speaking to former Pakistan captain Salman Butt in Straight Drive with Salman Butt on Saturday, Aamer said the PCB deserved credit for upgrading facilities and providing players with the resources needed for their development.
However, he questioned why Pakistan continued to struggle to achieve consistent results despite the improvements.
“The encouraging thing I saw, facilities that should be provided to the players in the National Academy, which were not available, are now there,” Aamer said.
“Things have been updated, and the facilities have been enhanced. So this is a very encouraging thing that the prerequisites for the development of the player are available in a true sense. PCB should be given full credit for that.”
He added that the next priority should be to build the capacity of the coaching staff, arguing that infrastructure alone could not guarantee success.
“It’s is a big question mark that despite providing facilities to the players results are not produced,” he said.
“I think there is a need for capacity building,” Aamer said.
Aamer, who has served as Pakistan's Test captain, chief selector and National Cricket Academy director, highlighted the evolution of batting in modern cricket, where players are increasingly encouraged to take risks.
He argued that coaches must adapt their methods to the changing demands of the game and provide players with specific technical guidance rather than relying solely on their natural ability.
Aamer cited Pakistan’s batsman Saim Ayub as an example of a talented player whose development, in his view, has not progressed as expected because of inadequate guidance.
“He is highly talented, no doubt. I think when he came you felt that he is the next best for Pakistan cricket, but lost in translation,” Aamer said.
He questioned whether Saim had received sufficient technical advice to refine his batting, pointing to his no-look shots and footwork as areas where coaching intervention could have helped.
Aamer also raised concerns about Pakistan's fast bowlers, particularly those who initially bowl at speeds exceeding 145 kilometres per hour before experiencing a decline in pace.
He attributed the problem partly to bowling mechanics, arguing that the wrist and shoulder must work together to generate and sustain speed.
“When the wrist is locked, you are bowling with just your arm, and after some time their pace drops due to this reason,” he said.
Aamer maintained that improving coaching expertise was essential to addressing such technical shortcomings and ensuring talented players fulfilled their potential.
“You won't get the desired results until you build your coaching staff's capacity,” he said.
The former chief selector also reflected on his own responsibilities in the role, saying he considered it his duty to ensure players were technically equipped and received guidance when struggling.
“As a chief selector, it was my responsibility to look after players that they are technically well equipped. That was my responsibility to guide them if they are struggling. I had to justify,” he said.
Aamer's comments also highlighted the need for a stronger development pathway connecting school and club cricket with the National Cricket Academy and the senior national team.
He stressed that long-term progress would require sustained investment in coaching, fundamentals and player development, alongside improvements in facilities.

title: Original    Hunger Games    stars guide new    Sunrise on the Reaping    cast
description: Jennifer Lawrence   s possible appearance in the prequel remains unconfirmed as its November release approaches
content:
Jennifer Lawrence’s possible appearance in the prequel remains unconfirmed as its November release approaches
The original Hunger Games stars have offered guidance to the new cast of Sunrise on the Reaping , helping the latest actors prepare to enter the popular franchise.
Producer Nina Jacobson and director Francis Lawrence told PEOPLE that several returning franchise veterans reached out to the newcomers ahead of the film’s release on November 20, 2026. The sixth film in the series adapts Suzanne Collins’ fifth Hunger Games novel and follows a young Haymitch Abernathy during the Second Quarter Quell, decades before he becomes a mentor to Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark.
Joseph Zada takes over the role of Haymitch, originally played by Woody Harrelson. Whitney Peak plays Lenore Dove, while Elle Fanning portrays a younger Effie Trinket, the character Elizabeth Banks played in the original films.
Jacobson said the original actors were generous with their advice, noting that many of the younger performers grew up reading Collins’ books and watching the earlier movies. She singled out McKenna Grace, who plays Maysilee Donner, as an especially devoted fan of the series.
Banks also contacted Fanning after her casting, offering support as the actress prepared to portray the distinctive Capitol representative.
Harrelson was informed early that the prequel was in development. Lawrence explained that the filmmakers wanted him to know about the book centred on his character before the news became widely known. He joked that Harrelson was not necessarily the easiest person to trust with a secret.
Other established actors have also expressed enthusiasm about joining the production. Glenn Close’s team reportedly approached the filmmakers about a role, while Maya Hawke was excited to play Wiress, a character connected to the franchise’s earlier story.
Jennifer Lawrence’s possible involvement remains unconfirmed. When asked about the original Katniss actress, Francis Lawrence said he speaks with her fairly often but offered no confirmation of an appearance.
Sunrise on the Reaping also stars Jesse Plemons, Kieran Culkin, Ben Wang and Molly McCann. The film explores Haymitch’s experience in the deadly competition that shaped his life long before Katniss entered the arena.

title: Tarar lambasts PTI and K P govt  says    hours meant for governance spent plotting prisoner   s release
description: Asks K P lawmakers to redirect focus towards development and security issues
content:
Asks K-P lawmakers to redirect focus towards development and security issues
Federal Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Saturday accused the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) government in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) of neglecting governance and prioritising efforts to secure the release of the party’s incarcerated founder over public welfare, development and security.
“The hours that should have been spent on governance have instead been spent plotting to secure the release of a prisoner,” Tarar said at a press conference in Islamabad, attended by Prime Minister’s Coordinator on Information for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Affairs Ikhtiar Wali Khan and K-P MPA Jalal Khan.
Targeting K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, Tarar alleged that the provincial leadership had devoted insufficient time to governance despite more than 13 years of PTI rule in the province.
“If you do the calculations, you will find that Sohail Afridi has devoted virtually zero hours to governance,” Tarar said, alleging that the chief minister’s administration had prioritised political agitation over addressing public grievances.
Tarar said the provincial government should have focused on establishing modern IT centres, building universities and schools, upgrading hospitals and improving public infrastructure across the province, including in Lakki Marwat, Mardan, Nowshera and Swabi.
Read: PTI terms proposed emergency in 12 K-P districts violation of 18th Amendment as long march enters seventh day
Comparing the provincial administration’s performance with that of the federal government, Tarar cited Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s inauguration of an IT park and the federal fuel subsidy scheme as examples of governance and public relief.
وزیر اطلاعات عطاء اللہ تارڑ، وزیراعظم کے کوآرڈینیٹر اختیار ولی خان، رکن اسمبلی خیبر پختونخوا جلال خان کی نیوزکانفرنس pic.twitter.com/v1EZHrVpJp
According to Tarar, the IT park would support start-ups, improve digital skills and contribute to economic growth. He also claimed that 10 million people had benefited from the fuel subsidy scheme through an IT-based registration system. He also said the federal government had incorporated public feedback into the subsidy scheme, including changes to eligibility requirements, arguing that the initiative demonstrated the importance of administrative follow-up and responsiveness to citizens.
He alleged that successive PTI governments had undermined K-P’s standing as a peaceful destination and failed to deliver adequate public services.
Tarar accuses PTI of failing to tackle terrorism
Tarar accused the PTI leadership of adopting a soft approach towards the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), alleging that terrorists had been brought back to areas where security forces had previously restored peace through operations, including Zarb-e-Azb and Radd-ul-Fasaad.
The information minister claimed that the return of militants had contributed to renewed insecurity in parts of the province and accused the provincial leadership of failing to take a sufficiently forceful stand against terrorist groups.
Referring to attacks in Kohat, Hangu and Dera Ismail Khan, Tarar alleged that the provincial government had failed to respond effectively to the security situation.
He also referred to the killing of police personnel and civilians, including a child in an incident at the Aman Mela checkpoint in Dera Ismail Khan, and questioned the provincial leadership’s responsibility for protecting citizens.
Tarar further alleged that the provincial administration had failed to invest adequately in the police and Counter Terrorism Department (CTD). He said the government should have strengthened security infrastructure and installed Safe City surveillance cameras, particularly at entry and exit points in the merged tribal districts.
The minister alleged that funds allocated for development and security had instead been spent on political protests and agitation.
Tarar said the people of KP were suffering from poverty, inadequate healthcare, limited educational opportunities and insecurity, which he attributed to the provincial government’s failure to fulfil its responsibilities.
Speaking after Tarar, Prime Minister’s Coordinator on Information for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Affairs Ikhtiar Wali Khan alleged that the PTI government had failed to deliver on its promises of educational development during more than a decade in power.
Wali claimed that at least 18 of the province’s 34 universities were on the verge of bankruptcy and that many institutions were operating without vice chancellors.
He challenged PTI leaders to substantiate their claims about establishing new universities, alleging that one institution cited by a provincial minister had yet to be built despite claims that students were already attending classes.
Wali said he had been carrying documents relating to the project for four months and challenged the minister concerned to debate the matter publicly.
Turning to the merged tribal districts, Wali alleged that little progress had been made in establishing new schools, colleges and police stations since their integration into K-P.
“Dedicated funds had been promised for the development of the former tribal areas at the time of their merger with the province. However, money transferred during the government of former prime minister Imran Khan had been diverted towards other constituencies and political activities instead of being spent in the designated areas,” Wali maintained.
He also alleged that public funds had been used to finance social media operations, claiming that thousands of social media influencers had received monthly payments. Wali did not present independently verified evidence of the alleged expenditure at the press conference.
The PML-N leader also assailed the province’s healthcare system and said it had deteriorated under successive PTI governments and required extensive reform.
He criticised the role of Dr Nausherwan Burki, whom he identified as Imran Khan’s cousin and an influential figure in the province’s healthcare system.
Wali highlighted that financial interests had influenced the approval of medicines and the inclusion of hospitals in the Sehat Card programme.
He claimed that only 20 to 40 hospitals out of approximately 100 were included on the relevant panel, adding that hospitals had been charged “fees for inclusion” and “monthly commissions linked to their profits”.
The PM’s aide also accused the provincial administration of neglecting the police and CTD, alleging that they had been deprived of essential weapons and resources despite federal funds being allocated for counterterrorism.
During the press conference, he alleged that a provincial forests minister had links to the timber mafia and claimed that certain PTI leaders had accumulated substantial business interests while holding public office.
Wali urged the people of K-P to compare the province’s development record with that of other parts of Pakistan. He said residents deserved comparable standards of healthcare, education, infrastructure and security, adding that shortcomings existed across the country but should not be used to justify a lack of progress in K-P.
PM’s Coordinator on Information for K-P Affairs Wali also accused the PTI of exploiting Pakhtun identity for political gains, alleging that the party’s rule had even damaged the province’s political culture.
“The culture of respect has disappeared and now people respond with slurs and offensive language,” Wali said, adding that the party should stop what he described as playing the “Pakhtun card” and concentrate on improving public services and living standards in the province.
Read more: ‘No way back’: Afridi vows to continue PTI long march as convoy reaches Peshawar
“No one needs their certification to identify as a Pakhtun,” he remarked.
He urged the K-P government to focus on the province’s development rather than political confrontation, calling for the reopening of Malam Jabba and the BRT system. Wali also alleged that a Rs200 billion Peshawar revitalisation project had been lost to corruption.
In strongly worded remarks, Wali alleged that PTI’s agenda was aligned with that of the Pashtun Tahafuz Movement (PTM), the Tehreek-e-Taliban Afghanistan (TTA), the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and other banned organisations.
“These are your military wings,” Wali said, accusing PTI of maintaining links with groups he described as hostile to the state. He did not substantiate the allegation with evidence at the press conference.
Wali called for accountability within PTI and urged the public to question their elected representatives over “persistent corruption”.
He also referred to PTI as “Fitna Khyber Pakhtunkhwa” and vowed to remove terrorism and its facilitators from the province.
Referring to recent allegations by CM Sohail Afridi on abductions of provincial lawmakers, Wali stated that PTI ministers hid on their own and claimed to be abducted by unidentified individuals.
He asked the people to question the PTI leaders as to why they are able to move freely in areas affected by terrorism in Sindh and elsewhere in the country while the rest of the people have been terrorised by these groups.
“Is their DNA the same?” he asked, questioning what he portrayed as differences in the treatment of PTI leaders across regions.
Jalal Khan questions use of counterterrorism funds
K-P MPA Jalal Khan questioned the provincial government’s claims that it lacked resources to combat terrorism, asking why funds were not being used to strengthen the police and other law enforcement agencies.
“They claim they do not have funds to counter terrorism but they have Rs200 billion in funds to beautify Peshawar?” Jalal Khan asked. He also questioned the utilisation of Rs800 billion that he said the province had received from the federal government to combat terrorism.
Jalal Khan asked why the money had not been used to improve the capacity, equipment and operational readiness of the police and other security institutions.
He said he had not received police security clearance for a meeting in Kohat, while PTI leaders were able to move around the area without fear.
Jalal Khan alleged that whenever the provincial government was questioned about governance or security, its leaders redirected the discussion towards the incarcerated PTI founder, whom he referred to as “prisoner 420”.
“We will rescue the province from these people,” he concluded.
Tarar declines to give verdict on governor’s rule
During the question-and-answer session, Tarar was asked whether governor’s rule or an emergency should be imposed in K-P.
He said he could not give a definitive assessment of the matter.
However, Tarar strongly criticised the provincial government’s performance, saying the province had suffered a significant decline under successive PTI administrations.
“K-P has never fared worse than this. Every department has collapsed during the 13 years of their reign,” Tarar said.
The information minister alleged that PTI had prioritised securing the release of its founder over the welfare of the people, arguing that the provincial leadership had failed to address persistent security and development challenges.
Comparing the situation in K-P with that in Balochistan, Tarar said the latter was confronting terrorism collectively, whereas the PTI leadership in K-P remained preoccupied with its political objectives.
He also accused PTI of repeatedly violating court orders and alleged that violence had “always” accompanied the party’s protests.
Towards the end of the press conference, Wali also criticised the Pashtun Tahafuz Movement, alleging that it supported the concept of a greater Pakhtunistan and did not recognise the Pakistan-Afghanistan border, referring to it instead as the Durand Line.
Wali said he did not support the movement because of what he described as its anti-Pakistan approach.

title: Pakistan eye series victory
description: Farhan   s men look to maintain aggressive approach against Sri Lanka
content:
Farhan’s men look to maintain aggressive approach against Sri Lanka
Buoyed by a convincing victory in the first T20I on Friday, Pakistan will look to seal the series when they take on Sri Lanka in the second match of the three-match series at the Pindi Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi on Sunday.
Pakistan made a strong start to the series, beating Sri Lanka by four wickets in the opening match. Several positives emerged from their approach, with aggressive intent standing out as the biggest takeaway. However, the hosts will need to strike a balance between attacking cricket and composure to ensure a more convincing finish.
Losing several wickets in quick succession, while firmly in control of the chase, was an area of concern. With the top order having laid the foundation, Pakistan could have avoided unnecessary dismissals and finished the contest more comfortably.
The hosts will also need to improve their fielding and wicket-keeping if they are to build on their opening success.
Captain Sahibzada Farhan led from the front with an impressive 89 on Friday, delivering the kind of performance Pakistan needed from their new skipper, who has replaced Agha Salman.
Chasing 183, Farhan and Fakhar Zaman provided the hosts with an excellent start before Maaz Sadaqat added further impetus with his powerful hitting to help Pakistan secure the win.
Earlier, debutant pacer Imran Randhawa emerged as one of the standout performers, taking 2-21 in his four overs. He complemented senior fast bowler Naseem Shah, who claimed 3-36, including the prized wicket of Sri Lankan captain Kusal Mendis in the opening over.
Pakistan are likely to field an unchanged side for the second encounter.
Farhan said the team would continue to adopt an aggressive approach in the coming matches.
“Yes we will play with the same mindset. What I had told before the game happened and will build on it,” Farhan said.
“The way me and Fakhar started and then Maaz added to it I think was positive. Maaz is in great form and I have told him that he should benefit of it as such days do not come always,” he said.
The Pakistan captain also praised Randhawa for his performance with the new ball during the powerplay.
“I know that he is very good with the new ball and he has executed his plans quite well,” Farhan said.
Meanwhile, Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis will be looking for a stronger response from his team as they attempt to level the series.
Mendis emphasised the need for his batsman to adopt a more positive approach during the powerplay and capitalise on the fielding restrictions.
“We have to play positive cricket and score more runs in the powerplay,” Mendis said.
“We were 20 to 30 runs short as 200 and plus would have been a good score on this wicket. We did not bowl well in the powerplay and we will have to bowl first six overs tight and then take wickets in the middle to put pressure on the oppositions,” he said.
The Sri Lankan skipper also praised Lahiru Udara, who struck an impressive 91 off 55 balls to help the visitors post a competitive total.
“He batted really well in the middle and I hope he will carry his fine form in the series,” Mendis said.
Udara proved to be one of Sri Lanka’s biggest positives in the opening match. The wicket-keeper batsman registered his maiden T20I half-century in only his fifth appearance in the format, giving his side a much-needed boost with the bat.
Friday’s victory was Pakistan’s 19th in T20Is against Sri Lanka, taking their head-to-head record to 19-13.
Sri Lanka, however, have fond memories of their previous T20I tour of Pakistan, having swept the hosts 3-0 in a three-match series in October 2019.
Pakistan rested on Saturday, while Sri Lanka were scheduled to train at the Pindi Cricket Stadium ahead of Sunday's encounter.
The visitors are in Pakistan not only for the T20I series but also for an upcoming ODI tri-series involving England, followed by a Test series.

Adviser to CM Balochistan says two CTD personnel sustained injuries during the operation
The Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) killed 10 terrorists belonging to Fitna Al-Hindustan during an effective operation in Barkhan district of Balochistan, Adviser to the Chief Minister of Balochistan for Information and Political Affairs Shahid Rind said on Saturday.
The federal government last year officially designated all terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as Fitna al-Hindustan , accusing India of sponsoring a proxy war through the outfits.
During the press briefing, Rind confirmed the incident and said that the CTD initiated the targeted strike in the Rara Sham area after receiving precise, action-oriented intelligence regarding terrorists' movements.
​"A fierce exchange of fire broke out as security teams closed in on the hideout, resulting in the elimination of all ten terrorists. Law enforcement agencies subsequently recovered a large quantity of heavy weaponry, military-grade arms, and live ammunition from the location," he added.
Rind further said that two CTD personnel sustained injuries in the line of duty during the operation and are receiving prompt medical treatment.
​Reaffirming the provincial administration's unwavering stance against violence, Rind stated that security forces, police, and CTD personnel remain firmly united to eradicate terrorist elements completely, adding that such targeted operations will persist until the threat of terrorism is entirely wiped out from Balochistan.

title: Verstappen wins chaotic Singapore sprint
description: Red Bull driver holds off Ferrari s Lewis Hamilton to win by 2 50sec
content:
Red Bull driver holds off Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton to win by 2.50sec
Max Verstappen won a wet and wild Singapore sprint race for Red Bull on Saturday after George Russell crashed his Mercedes when leading at the end of the opening lap.
Verstappen held off Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton to win by 2.50sec with Charles Leclerc third as the McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri touched and spun on the final lap when fourth and fifth.
A heavy shower 10 minutes before the scheduled start meant a delay of 30 minutes.
All cars began on intermediate tyres with some sectors of the Marina Bay Street Circuit much dryer than others as the field embarked on two formation laps behind the safety car.
The eventual standing start saw Russell start on the front row alongside pole-sitter Verstappen, and it was the Englishman who got away better.
His lead was short-lived as he lost control after touching a treacherous white line on the final bend of the opening lap.
He slid sideways into the pit lane wall, bringing out a safety car.
It was another setback in a season of bad luck for Russell, who will start from the back of the grid in Sunday's grand prix because of engine penalties.
"It was a miscalculation," Russell admitted to Sky Sports.
"Came through the corner, had more battery deployment than I thought, pushed me a little bit wider than I hoped and went on to the white line. Silly mistake. Big consequences."
It left Hamilton, who had a brilliant start from sixth on the grid, in second place having leapfrogged Ferrari team-mate Leclerc and the two McLarens.
The big beneficiary of Norris and Piastri's "papaya spat" on the last lap was championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who inherited fourth place in his Mercedes having started seventh on the grid.
Fifth was RB's Liam Lawson, sixth was the Haas of Oliver Bearman, seventh was Audi's Nico Hulkenberg and Norris got going again to limp home in eighth and round out the points scorers.

title: 11 killed  including three children  in overnight Russia Ukraine strikes
description: Search and rescue operations remain ongoing  people may still be trapped under rubble following attack
content:
Search-and-rescue operations remain ongoing, people may still be trapped under rubble following attack
Overnight Russian and Ukrainian strikes killed at least 11 people, including three children, and injured 22 others, officials from both countries said on Saturday.
In Ukraine, a Russian attack on the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia killed 11 people, including three children, regional military administration head Mykhailo Semikin said on Telegram.
He said search-and-rescue operations were ongoing and people could still be trapped under the rubble following the attack.
Ivan Fedorov, co-chair of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Defence Council, said 16 people were injured in the Russian attack on Zaporizhzhia, adding: “The fate of another 12 people remains unknown.”
Separately, Ukraine’s Air Force on Telegram accused Russia of launching 160 drones, with 117 of them shot down or suppressed.
In Russia, a Ukrainian drone attack on the southern Rostov region injured six people, regional Gov. Yury Slyusar said.
Read: Russia hits Ukraine with drones and missiles, killing at least 15
He said several apartment buildings and private houses in Rostov-on-Don were damaged, along with an unoccupied new building in Bataysk and two vessels in Azov. No casualties were initially reported aboard the ships.
Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin said on Telegram that 403 drones headed toward the Moscow region overnight, with a “majority” of them neutralised by air defence forces at long range, adding that 25 drones were destroyed as they approached the Russian capital.
Russia’s Defence Ministry, meanwhile, said its air defences intercepted or destroyed 560 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions, Crimea -- which Moscow annexed in 2014 -- and the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov overnight.
The ministry also said Russian forces struck Ukrainian port infrastructure and vessels allegedly used in the interests of Ukraine’s military, including a cargo ship carrying military-related supplies to the port of Odesa.

title: Schauffele closes in on leaders
description: American moves four shots off the lead in Japan
content:
American moves four shots off the lead in Japan
Double major winner Xander Schauffele moved four shots off the lead in Japan after carding two eagles and a double bogey on "a weird day" at the US PGA Tour's Baycurrent Classic on Saturday.
Defending champion Schauffele heads into Sunday's final day with a shot at retaining his title after carding a 6-under-par 65 to finish the third round 9-under overall.
The American had a roller-coaster front nine in sunny conditions in Yokohama, starting with a bogey before holing two birdies and an eagle on the par-5 fourth.
Schauffele followed that up with a double bogey on the next hole before sinking another eagle on the par-5 sixth, and went on to card four more birdies and another bogey to finish the round.
"It was a weird day," said Schauffele, who won Olympic gold in Tokyo in 2021.
"It was a lot of good, honestly some really bad in there as well.
"But overall, if someone told me I was going to shoot 65, I'd probably take it."
Michael Brennan, Zach Bauchou and Jacob Bridgeman lead the field heading into the final day on 13-under par.
Bridgeman is looking for his third win on the tour this year.
The trio hold a one-stroke lead over a chasing pack that includes Australia's Adam Scott.
Japan's Hideki Matsuyama is eight shots off the lead after a mixed day when he shot a 2-under-par 69.
Matsuyama, the 2021 champion in Japan, started like a freight train, rattling in four birdies and an eagle on the first seven holes.
He ran into serious trouble on the back nine, though, carding five bogeys and only one more birdie to undo much of his good work.
"It was a mix of great golf and the worst golf," said 2021 Masters champion Matsuyama.
"But it wasn't that I played absolutely terribly on the back nine.
"It was little things, so I just need to make some small adjustments to make sure that doesn't happen again tomorrow."
Three-time major winner Jordan Spieth was six shots off the lead after shooting a 3-under-par 68 to finish 7-under overall.
Spieth is looking for his first win on the tour since April 2022.
Collin Morikawa, the 2023 champion in Japan, was on 4-under overall.

title: Wanted terrorist commander killed in Bannu Police Peace Committee operation
description: Separately  Afghan commander of Shamshad group killed in exchange of fire between members of two terrorist factions
content:
Separately, Afghan commander of Shamshad group killed in exchange of fire between members of two terrorist factions
A wanted commander identified as Zainullah alias Salar was reportedly killed during an operation by the Police Peace Committee in the Ghoriwala area of Bannu district on Saturday morning, a committee spokesman said.
Police Peace Committee spokesman Mer Zaman Marwat said the committee had conducted an operation against suspected terrorists in the area, during which Zainullah was killed.
The suspected commander was reportedly a permanent resident of North Waziristan who had been living temporarily in Ghoriwala, according to sources. Details of the cases registered against him, his alleged activities and the circumstances of the operation were not immediately available.
In a separate incident in South Waziristan Lower, an Afghan commander of the Shamshad group was killed in an exchange of fire between members of two terrorist factions.
Deputy Superintendent of Police (SP) Asghar Ali Shah said Afghan commander Barbad Afghani was killed during an exchange of fire between members of the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) Zarmilan group and the Shamshad group in the Khankot area of Toi Khullah tehsil.
According to the police official, around 12 to 16 members of the Shamshad faction had split into two groups late at night. One group was in Sootian Kalay, while the other was stationed in Pani Khel Kalay.
The group returning from a patrol in Sootian Kalay came under fire from its own associates in Pani Khel Kalay, resulting in Barbad Afghani's death, SP Asghar. The circumstances that led to the exchange of fire were not immediately clear, and no further casualties were reported.
Read: DI Khan, Bannu postpone SSC papers amid mobile, internet suspension
In another incident last night, Raghzai Police Station in the Birmal tehsil came under a quadcopter attack late, District Police Officer Shah Hassan confirmed.
No police personnel were injured, and all staff at the station remained safe, officials said. Further details about possible damage and the identity of those responsible were not available.
Meanwhile, Bannu police placed the district on high alert, with patrols and checking operations continuing across the area.
On the directives of District Police Officer Captain (retired) Muhammad Furqan Bilal, police personnel conducted patrols and checks within the jurisdictions of Domel and Township police stations under the supervision of Sadar Sub-Divisional Police Officer Arshad Khan.
The measures were aimed at maintaining law and order, preventing crime, and protecting citizens' lives and property.
The incidents came amid continuing security concerns in Bannu and South Waziristan Lower, with Bannu district witnessing several security incidents this past month.
On September 13, two civilians were injured in a quadcopter attack at Shakir Chowk in the Bakakhel area, according to reports. Then on September 15, police constable Ahmadullah was killed in a firing incident within the jurisdiction of Bannu Cantt police station.

On September 16, two civilians, including a woman, were killed and two others injured in a suspected terrorist quadcopter attack in Bannu's Wazir subdivision. Police, the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD), the Elite Force and members of the Police Peace Committee subsequently conducted a joint operation. Police said a suspected terrorist was killed during the operation, while a search-and-clearance operation was also launched.

title: China  EU agree to explore tariff cuts  ease trade barriers
description: Beijing  Brussels to maintain dialogue on export controls  EVs and market access
content:
Beijing, Brussels to maintain dialogue on export controls, EVs and market access
China and the European Union have agreed to explore reducing tariffs on certain goods, strengthen cooperation on export controls, and address outstanding market access issues as the two sides seek to stabilise bilateral economic and trade relations.
The agreements were reached during the second meeting of the China-EU Trade and Investment Consultation Mechanism, held in Beijing on October 8-9, according to a joint statement released on Friday.
Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao and European Commission Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maroš Šefčovič led the discussions, which both sides described as pragmatic and productive.
The two sides reiterated their commitment to managing trade differences within the framework of World Trade Organisation (WTO) rules and making bilateral economic and trade relations more balanced.
Read: China’s EV lead built on scale, policy and innovation
They agreed to hold the mechanism’s third meeting in March 2027, while maintaining close communication in the interim, including through a ministerial-level video conference in January.
On trade and investment, both sides agreed to continue exploring the possibility of reducing tariffs on certain goods in accordance with WTO rules and strengthen cooperation under the existing trade monitoring mechanism.
EU-CN trade needs real rebalancing. With Minister Wang Wentao we've reached a shared understanding to:⁰🔹halve HEV, PHEV exports⁰🔹improve access to China's market⁰🔹further ease rare earths export licensing. A first step. I welcome the genuine engagement. We reconvene by Jan. pic.twitter.com/SiKiZYLC8N
They also reached an understanding on trade in hybrid vehicles following intensive consultations, while agreeing to continue procedures relating to price commitments and reviews in the EU’s anti-subsidy cases involving Chinese electric vehicles.
Market access for medical devices remained another area of discussion. The EU welcomed measures taken by China to expand imports of European medical devices, including a procurement-matching meeting planned during the ninth China International Import Expo.
China also agreed to accelerate recognition of regionalisation principles for eligible EU member states on the basis of risk assessments. The two sides will exchange disease-control methods and technologies and explore ways to lift restrictions on imports from relevant member states affected by bluetongue disease.
Also Read: European lawmakers criticise von der Leyen remarks linking Türkiye, Russia and China
Further technical discussions will cover computer reservation systems, regulatory frameworks for cosmetics and medicines, and the EU’s Foreign Subsidies Regulation. Both sides will also continue addressing existing and emerging market access concerns.
The European side clarified that the EU’s financing guidance for inverter projects was not directed at any particular country. The issue will be discussed further, according to the statement.
On investment, the two sides agreed to explore opportunities for cooperation aimed at promoting economic development and pursuing future-oriented initiatives.
Export controls featured prominently in the discussions, with both sides stressing the need for stronger dialogue and greater transparency in their respective policies.
China and the EU underscored the importance of improving the predictability and stability of global industrial and supply chains.
China expressed its willingness to continue facilitating approvals for exports of rare earths and permanent magnets to Europe through its “Green Channel” mechanism. The EU, meanwhile, said it would continue working with member states to resolve key licensing cases involving dual-use goods destined for China.
Read more: Rare earths force Trump to be less hostile before Xi summit
Both sides also discussed possible structural measures to facilitate compliant trade in dual-use items, which can have both civilian and military applications.
Under the export control dialogue mechanism, they reached an understanding on providing advance notification before listings, improving transparency in listing and transfer procedures, and supporting the initiation of transfer procedures within their respective legal frameworks.
The two sides also reported progress in addressing systemic intellectual property issues and agreed to continue efforts to improve protection and enforcement, transparency and predictability.
Progress will be monitored through the China-EU Intellectual Property Working Group, with both sides committing to setting phased objectives for resolving outstanding concerns.
On WTO reform, China and the EU agreed to strengthen bilateral communication and cooperation in an open and constructive manner. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to participating in the reform process and discussing relevant issues with a view to achieving substantive progress.

title: PM Shehbaz inaugurates IT Park to drive tech led growth
description: Says building would be handed over to the company offering the best services  will be run by experts not the govt
content:
Hails country's first national technology facility as crucial milestone for Pakistan's rapid economic progress
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif inaugurated the newly renamed Daanish IT Park (National Technology Park) on Saturday, hailing the country's first national technology facility as a crucial milestone for Pakistan's rapid economic progress and prosperity.
Addressing the inaugural ceremony, PM Shehbaz said the government would not be involved in running the Islamabad IT Park, which would be handed over to a company selected through a transparent bidding process and operated by experts and teachers.
“The government of Pakistan will have nothing to do with this. There will be experts and teachers here, and they will run this IT park,” he said while inaugurating the facility, which he renamed the Danish IT Park.
He said local and international companies working in information technology (IT) and artificial intelligence (AI) would be invited to participate in the bidding process, with the building handed over to the company offering the best services under the most favourable terms and conditions.
“I have already told the ministry that bidding should be conducted transparently. Companies working in the fields of IT and AI, whether in Pakistan or abroad, will be invited,” he said.
The prime minister said the facility would equip young people with skills in information technology (IT) and artificial intelligence (AI), helping Pakistan compete with developed economies.

“This IT park will prove to be a milestone for Pakistan’s development and prosperity,” he said, adding that the facility would house incubation centres, innovation hubs, start-ups, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), industrialists, teachers and students.
The prime minister said the park would help train and empower young people, giving them the skills needed to contribute to economic growth. He called it Pakistan’s first IT park built on “highly modern lines”.
“It will equip and empower not thousands but hundreds of thousands of children with skills,” he said, expressing hope that those skills would help Pakistan reach the ranks of developed countries.
PM Shehbaz said he expected similar facilities to spread across the country once the Islamabad park became fully operational.
“When this becomes a fully operational IT park, I am confident that hundreds and thousands of IT parks like this will spread across all four provinces of Pakistan,” he said.
He added that AI and IT could benefit sectors ranging from agriculture and manufacturing to industry and mining, saying they would allow the country to benefit from “modern knowledge”.
The project had suffered “considerable delays”, he said, adding that it was important for the country’s young women and men to benefit from the facility so Pakistan could move forward.
The prime minister said the project’s foundation stone had been laid in 2018 but continued to say, “What happened afterwards is part of history. I will not say anything about it today, because this is not an occasion for political point-scoring,” he said.
The prime minister credited teamwork and the efforts of government officials and ministers for bringing the project to completion, acknowledging Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Khan Cheema, IT Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja and their teams.
The prime minister said he had chaired several meetings and visited the site more than once, stressing that his concern was not simply to complete the project under his government but to ensure young people could benefit from it without further delay.
PM Shehbaz highlighted that the project was about more than “bricks and mortar”, describing it as an ecosystem built around innovation, vocational training and opportunities for entrepreneurs to work alongside IT and AI experts.
He stated that the park would bring together entrepreneurs and technology specialists, acting as a “great catalyst” for people willing to learn new skills and put them into practice.
Read more: Pakistan, Google team up for AI-driven future
PM Shehbaz then went on to announce that the Islamabad IT Park would henceforth be known as the Danish IT Park, linking the initiative to the Danish school system, which provides education to children from disadvantaged backgrounds.
He said the government intended to extend the initiative to other parts of the country, including Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan.
Thousands of children from poor backgrounds had benefited from Danish schools, he said, with graduates going on to become doctors, engineers, scientists and teachers. Some had pursued higher education at universities around the world, while others were serving in hospitals in Pakistan.
The prime minister also referred to plans for Danish universities, expressing hope that the IT park would become a nationwide initiative.
“God willing, this Danish IT Park will become a mighty tree, and millions of children across the country will receive education under its shade,” he said.
PM Shehbaz thanked the officials involved in the project, including Ahsan Iqbal, Ahad Khan Cheema and Shaza Fatima Khawaja, as well as other members of the team. He also acknowledged Abdullah Jan for his contribution.

title: Britney Spears celebrates 25th anniversary of    Britney    with five previously unreleased tracks
description: The anniversary edition arrives November 6 and includes a studio recording of a Pepsi commercial song
content:
The anniversary edition arrives November 6 and includes a studio recording of a Pepsi commercial song
Britney Spears has released “ She’ll Never Be Me ”, a previously unreleased song recorded in 2001 for her third studio album, Britney , giving fans an official look into her musical archives ahead of the record’s 25th anniversary reissue.
The pop star shared the track on October 9, 2026. Spears co wrote the song with her then boyfriend Justin Timberlake, alongside Bradley Daymond and Alex Greggs. Riprock ‘n’ Alex G handled production.
The self assured pop track centres on an ex who has moved on with someone resembling the singer. Its lyrics emphasise Spears’ individuality and suggest that a new partner cannot replace her.
“She’ll Never Be Me” will feature on Britney (25th Anniversary Edition) , scheduled for release on November 6. It is the first of five tracks being made available for the first time as part of the expanded edition.
The additional songs include “Am I a Sinner”, “When I Say So” and “My Big Secret”. The collection will also feature a studio recording of “Right Now (Taste The Victory)”, originally associated with a 2002 Pepsi commercial.
Released in 2001, Britney followed the success of ...Baby One More Time and Oops!... I Did It Again . The album presented a more mature musical image for Spears and included singles such as “Overprotected”, “I’m Not a Girl, Not Yet a Woman” and “I’m a Slave 4 U”.
Spears famously performed the latter song at the 2001 MTV VIDEO MUSIC AWARDS, appearing with a large python during the memorable stage performance.
“She’ll Never Be Me” marks Spears’ first release of previously unheard original material since her 2023 collaboration with will.i.am, “Mind Your Business”. Her most recent charting release was “Hold Me Closer”, her 2022 duet with Elton John.
The anniversary edition offers listeners a chance to hear material recorded during a defining period of Spears’ career, including songs that did not make the original album’s final track listing.

title: Barricade removal case  ATC rejects plea to drop terrorism charges against Imaan  Hadi
description: Lawyers boycott ATC proceedings while the court records the statements of three witnesses
content:
Lawyers boycott ATC proceedings while the court records the statements of three witnesses
An Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) in Islamabad on Saturday rejected a plea to drop terrorism charges against lawyer Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, as the couple and their lawyers boycotted the proceedings in the barricade removal case.
On Wednesday, the ATC had framed charges against Imaan and Chattha in the case related to the alleged violation of a designated route and incitement during the arrival of an international cricket team, despite defence objections that legal requirements had not been fulfilled.
ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Supra heard the case. During today's proceedings, the court dictated an order on the application regarding the accused's absence during the hearing and the request to drop the terrorism sections. It rejected and disposed of Imaan and Chattha's application to remove the terrorism sections without hearing their lawyers and without granting time.
"Proceedings were held here in your absence. We filed the application to drop the terrorism sections on your instructions," Lawyer Zainab Janjua told Chattha. She added, "I now have no further instructions from you, so we are leaving the proceedings of the case."
Judge Supra noted, "An application against the terrorism sections cannot be heard at this stage. I cannot review my order because I do not have the authority."
Janjua meanwhile asked the court to record her objection. "Let the court record my objection that the trial was held in the absence of Imaan and Hadi on video link," she said.
Further, the court rejected a request to adjourn the case due to the absence of lawyer Riasat Ali Azad, who Janjua had said was with the bar president, who was ill.
Judge Supra also exchanged words with Imaan and Chattha, who were presented via video link.
"Sir, we respect you; we have appeared before you," Chattha said. "We have learned from you that a case cannot proceed without a fair trial," he added. "Why are we not being produced before the court?" Chattha asked, further questioning, "We read in the newspaper the other day that the charge has been framed. Where has our right to a fair trial under Article 10 gone?"
Judge Supra stated, "You have challenged the charge. If the charge has not been framed correctly, it will be quashed by the high court." He also asked a prison official, "You were supposed to produce Imaan and Hadi before the court today. Why were they not produced?" The court sought a response.
Read: Islamabad ATC sends Imaan, Hadi on judicial remand after SC orders release on bail
Meanwhile, the court recorded the statements of three prosecution witnesses, including an FIR witness, the Muharrar, and a witness to the personal search.
It summoned the remaining witnesses for Monday and adjourned further hearing of the case until the same day.
Imaan and her husband Chattha were rearrested on September 17 , shortly after the Supreme Court granted them bail and suspended their sentences in a separate social-media posts case. They were produced before an Islamabad Anti-Terrorism Court in connection with a case registered at Kohsar Police Station.
Police sought 30-day physical remand, but ATC Judge Zulqarnain rejected the request and sent the couple on judicial remand. The judge noted that although they had been nominated in the FIR as members of an unlawful assembly, no weapon had been attributed to either accused.

On September 27, the court issued a contempt notice to the Adiala jail superintendent after the authorities failed to facilitate the signing and transmission of the documents and also failed to produce the accused through video link. Two days later, the issue was resolved after Imaan and Chattha signed the required powers of attorney.
On September 29 , the ATC ended the contempt proceedings against the jail authorities and separately confirmed that notices had been issued on the couple’s bail applications, with arguments scheduled before Judge Abul Hasnat.

Gordon Ramsay has sparked playful reactions from fans after sharing a series of beachside photographs showing off his physique on Instagram .

In a recent interview with Fox News Digital, he acknowledged that work often kept him from everyday family moments with his six children, including school runs, dinners and performances. He described time as the most valuable thing he had sacrificed professionally.

title: Musk steps up attack on Ambani  shares reports on Reliance linked BJP donations
description: Says there are many areas of India  as there are in all countries  with no Internet access
content:
Musk's sharp criticism of Ambani comes after persistent delays in launch of Starlink services in India
Elon Musk on Saturday intensified his criticism of industrialist Mukesh Ambani by sharing screenshots of media reports alleging that a Reliance-funded firm helped boost BJP campaigns on social media and that a Reliance-linked company made substantial political donations to the ruling party.
Musk’s post on X featured a 2022 Al Jazeera report headlined "How a Reliance-funded firm boosts BJP's campaigns on Facebook", along with an archived 2024 report by The Indian Express on Qwik Supply. The latter reported that the Reliance-linked firm donated ₹385 crore to the BJP and ₹25 crore to the Shiv Sena through electoral bonds.
The post came amid Musk’s sharp criticism of Ambani over persistent delays in the launch of Starlink satellite broadband services in India.
A few hours before he made the post, Musk addressed Ambani as "Prime Minister Ambani" and urged him to allow Starlink to compete in India.
"Please accept my humble apologies for not realising that you are the real boss of India," Musk wrote, accusing Ambani of seeking to maintain his market dominance.
Read: SpaceX strikes spectrum deal, paving way for Starlink to become major US mobile carrier
"Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?" he added.
Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to…
"There are many areas of India, as there are in all countries, with no Internet access, which denies children the opportunity for education and for small businesses the opportunity to sell their goods to a global market. Starlink would change their lives for the better," he added.
India rejects monopoly claim after Musk accuses Ambani of blocking Starlink launch
India’s telecom minister on Friday said the country does not allow monopolies in any sector, pushing back after Musk suggested billionaire Ambani was using political influence to block Starlink’s launch in the country.
"India does not allow a monopoly in any sector," telecom minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said at a media briefing on Friday, addressing Musk’s remarks.
Musk’s SpaceX unit is seeking entry into a telecom market with more than a billion internet users, currently dominated by the mobile networks of Ambani’s Reliance Jio and Sunil Mittal’s Bharti Airtel.
"Is Ambani the real boss of India?" Musk wrote on X on Thursday, questioning why Starlink still lacked a licence despite what he said were years of compliance with Indian requirements. He provided no evidence against Ambani.

Ambani’s Reliance Jio did not respond to a request for comment on Musk’s remarks.
A four-year wait to launch Starlink’s satellite internet services in India has sparked heated exchanges online over business influence and regulatory delays, with Musk targeting Ambani and the political opposition joining the row.
While Starlink has already secured a licence to operate in India , a commercial launch still requires it to meet security compliance conditions and receive a spectrum assignment.
The government said on Thursday that all three licensed satellite operators, including Starlink, were at broadly the same regulatory stage, calling suggestions of an unfair or discriminatory process "baseless and misconceived".

content:
Pacer battles hamstring and calf muscle injuries
Injured strike bowler Will O'Rourke has been ruled out of the home series against India and will target a return to face Australia, New Zealand Cricket announced on Saturday.
O'Rourke is recovering from hamstring and calf muscle injuries and will not play in the home ODI and Test matches against India as a "precaution", a statement from the national body said.
New Zealand coach Rob Walter hoped his key new ball bowler would be cleared to play in the four-Test series in Australia starting in early December.
"It's obviously disappointing for Will to have to miss such a marquee tour at home against India," Walter said.
"We all agreed it was best for him to take some more time to rehabilitate both injuries and safely build up his bowling loads.
"Our pace bowling resources will be critical over the next few months so we're taking a conservative approach to Will's return to ensure he's fully fit before he takes the field again."
The 25-year-old has impressed in 14 Tests since his 2024 debut, taking 49 wickets at an average just under 25.
He was a hostile performer in New Zealand's 2-1 series win in England in June, taking 10 wickets, but hasn't played since injuring his hamstring in the final Test.
He subsequently suffered a calf injury at a training session in August.
O'Rourke was previously sidelined for seven months with a back stress fracture before returning to the field earlier this year.
New Zealand have been hit by injuries in the lead-up to India's visit which comprises five Twenty20 Internationals starting on October 22, five ODIs and two Tests.
Batsman Mark Chapman and Zak Foulkes were both ruled out of the T20 squad on Saturday.
They were replaced by Josh Clarkson and Blair Tickner.

title: Maaz Sadaqat makes a statement with maiden T20I fifty
description: Young left hander   s aggressive knock against SL reflects Pakistan   s management   s faith in his natural game
content:
Young left-hander’s aggressive knock against SL reflects Pakistan’s management’s faith in his natural game
Pakistan’s young left-handed batsman Maaz Sadaqat may be in the early stages of his international career, having played just six One-Day Internationals and three Twenty20 Internationals, but he has already shown the potential to make an impact at the highest level.
The Peshawar-born batsman delivered an impressive display of power-hitting in the first T20I against Sri Lanka on Friday night, lighting up the Pindi Cricket Stadium with a blistering half-century that laid the foundation for Pakistan’s successful chase.
Maaz smashed 50 off just 29 deliveries, striking three sixes and four fours, as Pakistan chased down the 183-run target with seven balls to spare. His 92-run partnership for the second wicket with captain Sahibzada Farhan, who scored 89, proved decisive in steering the hosts to victory.
Coming in after the dismissal of Fakhar Zaman, who made 21, Maaz immediately put Sri Lanka under pressure. He took on Eshan Malinga, striking two sixes and a four in the same over, which yielded 16 runs and set the tone for his aggressive innings.
The innings was particularly encouraging for a young batsman still finding his feet in international cricket. More importantly, Maaz’s approach reflected the confidence he has gained from the team management, which has encouraged him to trust his instincts and play his natural game.
“It’s easy to bat in the powerplay. I play with positive intent and the way the modern cricket has been shaped. The way our coaches have told us and the way their mindset is so we back that and we are reaping success,” Maaz told a post-match news conference.
The left-hander said he does not allow outside opinions to dictate his approach at the crease, crediting the management for giving him the freedom to express himself.
“I don’t think about that what people would think and say and the second thing is I back my natural game and the way management has given me green signal to play my natural strokes. I follow that,” he said.
For Maaz, the half-century was a personal milestone, but the team’s victory remained the bigger achievement.
“It’s good that we have won the match. It was my first fifty and I am very happy,” said Maaz.
“And the way I have been playing inshaAllah in the next match too I will carry that,”
His confidence will be encouraging for Pakistan as they seek greater consistency and depth in their batting line-up. The emergence of young players capable of scoring quickly could also help address concerns surrounding the middle order.
Maaz believes Pakistan have made progress in that department with Hasan Nawaz and Abdul Samad making their presence felt.
“I think our problem at the middle order has now overcome as Hasan Nawaz is playing so well in that zone and so is Abdul Samad,” he said.
While one innings does not settle every question about a young batsman’s international future, Maaz’s performance offered a glimpse of what he could bring to Pakistan’s T20 setup. His ability to attack from the outset, coupled with the confidence to back his natural game, makes him a player worth watching as his international career develops.
The challenge now is to ensure that such promise translates into consistency. For Pakistan, nurturing emerging talent will require not only technical guidance but also the belief and backing needed to allow young players to perform without the burden of excessive expectations.
Maaz has made a promising start. If the management continues to provide him with the confidence and freedom to play his natural strokes, Pakistan may have found another attacking option capable of adding impetus to its batting line-up.

title: Man City verdict reignites Liverpool rivalry
description: City expect a hostile reception at Anfield
content:
City expect a hostile reception at Anfield
Manchester City will face the full fury of Anfield on Sunday when the Premier League leaders confront old rivals Liverpool in their first game since being found guilty of breaking financial rules.
City can expect a hostile reception from Liverpool fans after an independent commission found they arranged "sham" deals to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion) between 2009 and 2018.
The financial breaches occurred during a period in which City won three Premier League titles and numerous other trophies, with Liverpool struggling to break the Etihad Stadium outfit's silverware monopoly.
City have appealed against the devastating verdict and manager Enzo Maresca was bullish on Friday that they will overturn the original ruling.
But the Premier League season is now stuck in stasis awaiting a ruling on the appeal and any potential sanction.
"I think the worst thing probably is the uncertainty, that no one knows what's going to happen," Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola said on Friday.
A severe points penalty leading to relegation or even expulsion from the English top flight are on the table, while there is also speculation City could be stripped of titles.
"I think they have to be stripped of the titles. Otherwise you send the wrong message to anyone in the future," John Gibbons of Liverpool podcast The Anfield Wrap told AFP.
"There can't be any trust now, certainly not if there's not an admission of guilt. For me, I don't see how Manchester City continue in the league."
Over the past 12 years, Liverpool have finished second to City on three occasions.
Only one of those in 2013/14 came during the period under scrutiny.
But City's rivals believe the wrongdoing in that period built the foundations for a golden era under former boss Pep Guardiola, who stepped down at the end of last season.
Twice Jurgen Klopp's Reds missed out on the title despite amassing over 90 points.
Those title battles turned meetings between City and Liverpool into English football's marquee event and the eyes of the world will be on Anfield again come Sunday.
"It just shows how remarkable that team that Jurgen Klopp built was and what they were up against," added Gibbons.
"They were obviously going against another side who it has been shown weren't playing by the same rules as everyone else."
Even in happier times, City have rarely enjoyed their trips to Anfield.
Last season's 2-1 victory was City's first win there in front of a crowd since 2003, with their other win coming amid Covid-19 restrictions in 2021.
City return to Anfield sitting top of the Premier League after a flawless start to Maresca's reign, featuring seven successive wins in all competitions.
Just months after the charges against the club were first announced in February 2023, City went on to win the treble, clinching the club's first Champions League crown, as well as the Premier League and FA Cup.
The question is whether Maresca's men can tap into that siege mentality once more, rather than wilting under the intense scrutiny.
Liverpool supporters have often created a febrile atmosphere for City's visits since they emerged as title contenders following the takeover by their Abu Dhabi-based owners in 2008.
This weekend's showdown is likely to set a new standard for vitriol directed at City's players and fans.
"It's going to be massively hostile," said Dom Farrell, author of the book "Glory Days for the Waifs and Strays" that chronicled City's rise from the third tier to European champions.
"If they were to win against Liverpool and then beat an off-form Paris Saint-Germain you really get a siege mentality going.
"But there's also a decent chance they get turned over and then it just starts to feel you're in this sort of dead zone waiting for the verdict."

description: Israeli Democrats leader says killing of Iran   s Ali Khamenei was a  mistake
content:
Yair Golan criticizes Netanyahu for pursuing an 'unrealistic goal' of toppling Iran’s government
Yair Golan, head of Israel’s opposition Democratic Party, said that the killing of Iran's former supreme leader Ali Khamenei at the outset of the US-Israeli war on Iran in late February was a "mistake."
“I think, unequivocally, the elimination of Khamenei the father was a mistake,” Golan said during an interview at an event in the city of Rishon LeZion south of Tel Aviv, The Times of Israel reported a day earlier.
“Not because he didn’t deserve to die, only because it doesn’t serve the interests of the State of Israel,” he stated, noting that Khamenei was 86 years old.
The Israeli politician claimed that Ali Khamenei’s succession by his son, Mojtaba Khamenei , had left Iran under the leadership of “more extreme and violent individuals.”

Golan also criticised Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for pursuing an "unrealistic goal" of toppling the Iranian government, saying it had not been achieved.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on Feb. 28, prompting Tehran to respond with missile and drone attacks in the region and effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz .
The war has heightened regional tensions in the Middle East and raised global energy prices as commercial oil traffic through the strait has effectively halted.
Washington and Tehran signed a framework agreement in June following mediation efforts by Pakistan and Qatar to halt hostilities and pave the way for negotiations.

title: French policing under scrutiny as student protest injuries mount
description: French policing under scrutiny as student protest injuries mount
content:
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornudescribed the demonstrations as the most violent in decades.
Fourteen-year-old Eden suffered a broken jaw and multiple smashed teeth when he was struck by a tear gas canister directed towards him at close ​range by a police officer last week during student protests in France , his parents and family lawyer said.
The teenager had been sitting on a wall looking at his phone metres away from the ‌protest in Saint-Ouen-l'Aumône, the lawyer said. An officer approached him and struck him with a baton, prompting Eden to respond with a kick, according to the local prosecutor. A second officer then fired a tear gas grenade with a Cougar launcher, hitting him in the face.
"(The officer) shot him in the mouth and left him lying on the ground, without even calling the emergency services," said lawyer Elsa Marcel. The family, who asked for Eden's second name to be withheld to protect their privacy, has filed a complaint for attempted murder, she said.
A police ​spokesperson said they do not comment on ongoing investigations. According to the prosecutor’s office, the police officer said that he was seeking to protect himself and his colleagues after the student confronted police. The officer was ​placed under formal investigation on charges of assault by a public official resulting in permanent disability or disfigurement on this Tuesday, eight days after the incident.
The case is one of ⁠24 under investigation by the IGPN internal police watchdog linked to the policing of a more-than-two-week-long wave of student unrest over conditions in schools. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has described the demonstrations as the most violent in decades.
Depuis plusieurs jours, l’ultra-violence a frappé à la porte de nos lycées. Des élèves, des personnels éducatifs, des policiers et des gendarmes ont été blessés. Ces violences doivent être condamnées sans condition. Beaucoup de fausses informations ont circulé sur l’action des…
The police response has renewed ​calls for the withdrawal of the use of rubber bullets and grenade launchers, which are not used by police in many other European countries and have been repeatedly criticised in recent years by rights groups, including Amnesty International and UN ​human rights experts, as dangerous and disproportionate.
Also Read: French lawmaker calls on interior minister to resign over police response to student protests
It has also sparked anger among the public and fanned support for a protest movement that is the latest manifestation of deep-seated discontent with President Emmanuel Macron’s government ahead of a 2027 election.
Via interviews and reviews of legal documents, Reuters has documented 28 cases of injuries suffered due to police force, of which 15 are among those under investigation by the IGPN . They involve the use of rubber bullets, stun grenades, tear gas, batons and charges on horseback.
In two cases, a person's eye has been lost or ​injured due to rubber bullets. In another, a 15-year-old in Lens had his hand blown off — likely by a stun grenade, according to interior minister Laurent Nunez, who paused the use of stun grenades pending an investigation into the case.
Read More: Student protests spread across France, Belgium
Nunez said ​on Wednesday in a radio interview that about 200 students had been injured, but that it was very rarely the result of police action. “Our primary role is, of course, to protect high school students,” he said.
Authorities said that 700 police officers have also been ‌injured, schools have ⁠been burned or ransacked, and teachers and members of the public have been attacked. The police have arrested 6,877 people, mostly minors.

New Zealand fast bowler Will O’Rourke has been ruled out of the upcoming home series against India as he continues his rehabilitation from left hamstring and calf injuries, the country’s cricket board said on Saturday.

“It’s obviously disappointing for Will to have to miss such a marquee tour at home against India,” New Zealand coach Rob Walter said in a statement.
Walter said the team management had agreed to give the pacer additional time to recover and gradually rebuild his bowling workload to avoid further setbacks.
New Zealand will take a cautious approach to his return, with their pace-bowling resources expected to be crucial over the coming months.
India’s tour of New Zealand will feature five Twenty20 internationals, five ODIs and two Tests. The opening T20I is scheduled to take place in Christchurch on October 22.

description: Says Norway has been left with  indelible stain  one that will never be forgotten  for not awarding him Nobel
content:
Says Norway has been left with 'indelible stain, one that will never be forgotten' for not awarding him Nobel
United States President Donald Trump said on Saturday that Norway had been left with "an indelible stain, one that will never be forgotten," for not rewarding him with the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, arguing that he had "settled eight wars" and had deserved the honour.
Trump's remarks came a day after the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to South Africa's Navi Pillay , the judge who headed the Rwanda genocide tribunal and who last year presided over a United Nations commission which accused Israel of genocide in Gaza .
In a post on Truth Social, Trump referred to Pillay and said, "I know nothing about this woman, and neither does anyone else! In fact, to the best of my knowledge, no one ever heard of her other than the fact that she, very obviously, hates Israel."
The US president added, "I don’t know what the woman has done," arguing again that he had "settled 8 Wars, with letters being sent from every president and prime minister from the countries that I helped to the Norwegian Nobel Committee."
Trump also stated that he was "about to settle, or win, two more, Iran and Russia/Ukraine ." He said, "They’re both happening at breakneck speed but, forget them, it’s the 8 that I’ve already settled, any one of which, in particular, Pakistan and India , would be far more than necessary to win the Nobel Prize."
The US president added, "In actuality, I should have won 8 Nobel Peace Prizes, not just 1," citing eight "wars" that he had "settled", including between Cambodia and Thailand, Kosovo and Serbia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, Pakistan and India, Israel and Iran, Egypt and Ethiopia, Armenia and Azerbaijan, and Israel and Hamas. "Additionally, I stopped Iran from having a nuclear weapon and blowing up the entire Middle East and, ultimately, far beyond!" Trump said, claiming that he had "saved more lives than anyone in history."
Read: Nobel Peace Prize goes to South African judge despite PM Shehbaz’s hopes for Trump
Referring to last year's Nobel winner , Venezuela's Maria Corina Machado, Trump called her "a truly fine person" and stated that Machado "stated to the Media when she gave me her Nobel Prize of last year, 'Donald Trump settled many Wars, and deserves the Nobel Peace Prize more than any person that has ever received it.'" Trump added, "Based on my record of PEACE, a record like no one else has ever achieved, I agree!"
Further, Trump said he had "got back all of the hostages in Israel, including the final 28, both living and dead, and worked with Hamas to do it — Nobody believed this was possible!" The US president also stated, "I removed the World’s Evil Dictator, Nicolas Maduro , from Venezuela, and am in the process of making Venezuela a rich Democracy."
"Likewise, with Iran, I stopped them from destroying Israel, the Middle East, and Europe," he said. He further stated that he was "also preventing, on a constant basis, a War between South Korea and North Korea, and Japan and North Korea."
Saying that "numerous other hot spots" have not been involved in wars "only because of President Donald J Trump, and the United States of America."
Moving to cite NATO figures, Trump said he was "responsible for having NATO countries increase spending from 2% to 5% of GDP, creating a stronger alliance and defence," which he said was "another thing that everybody said was impossible to do."

He went further to claim that he had also "negotiated the release, and secured the return, of more than 900 political prisoners from multiple countries in Eastern Europe." He added, "I have brought 196 hostages HOME from captivity, from all over the World, and did it without having paid a ransom, unlike Biden and Obama who would pay Billions of Dollars."
Adding to his list of claims, Trump said, "On top of it all, I have created a soon-to-be very prosperous Arctic ."
"Despite all of this, the Nobel Prize was given today to a liberal person who works at the United Nations, who nobody has ever heard of," he stated. The president added, "In all of the Wars that I have settled, I never spoke to the United Nations — they were of no help."
Concluding his post, Trump said that "The United States of America, represented by me, as your President, should have received the Nobel Peace Prize, but didn’t." He further claimed that the award had been "forever discredited by a handful of Radical Ideologues who are Anti-Democracy, and Enemies of Civilisation!"

title: Hope   s century powers West Indies past India to level T20 series
description: Hope  102   and Rutherford  84  enable the visitors chase a record 250 run target with nine balls to spare
content:
Hope (102*) and Rutherford (84) enable the visitors chase a record 250-run target with nine balls to spare
RANCHI, India: Shai ​Hope struck a century as West Indies completed their highest successful chase in T20 internationals, overhauling a target of 250 to beat India by six wickets on Friday in ‌Ranchi and level the five-match series at 1-1.
Chasing a daunting target, West Indies were rocked early when paceman Mayank Yadav removed ‌Kamil Pooran and Shimron Hetmyer ⁠with ​successive deliveries in the opening over and later ​dismissed Rovman Powell for 24. "But ‌when you chase here in ​India, you always give yourself a chance. You always think you're in the game, regardless of what score is on the board," Hope said.
But five ⁠for two was always going to be challenging." Skipper Hope and Sherfane Rutherford turned ‌the match on its head with a blistering 120-run partnership for the fourth wicket. Rutherford survived on 38 when Yadav spilled a straightforward chance at short fine leg and ⁠capitalised on the reprieve, hammering 84 off 37 balls ⁠before falling to ​Kuldeep Yadav. Hope remained ‌unfazed, anchoring the chase while maintaining the required rate, and combined with Romario Shepherd to guide West Indies home with nine balls to spare.
Hope remained unbeaten on 102 from 45 deliveries. "When we got that partnership there, we just got some more impetus in the innings," Hope said. "Then obviously Sherfane came and did what he ⁠did, played really well with the bat, and just gave us that spark that we needed ⁠to get over the line today." This is the second-highest successful run chase in men's T20 international history, surpassed only by South Africa's pursuit of 259 against West Indies in 2023.
Earlier, Samson's 41-ball 82 underpinned India's total after he and Abhishek Sharma raced to 42 in less than four overs for the opening wicket. Chase halted the early surge by dismissing Sharma and ⁠later removed Kishan for 43 and Shivam Dube, while ​Shamar Springer struck with the key wicket of Samson.
India accelerated again at the death through Iyer and Tilak Varma, who put on 83 runs from 32 balls, with Iyer making 40 before falling off the penultimate ​delivery as the hosts finished on 249-5. The teams ‌meet again in the third T20 in Indore on Sunday.
