title: CM Afridi rejects governor   s rule as PTI long march reaches Mardan
description: A special administrative structure  separate from provincial govt s framework  being considered for these districts
content:
Vows to continue long march, urges supporters to reach Swabi for the next phase of the protest
As the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf’s long march reached Mardan on its seventh day, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Saturday rejected the imposition of governor’s rule or an emergency in the province and vowed to continue the march to Islamabad’s D-Chowk.
Addressing participants of the long march at Manga Bazaar in Mardan, Afridi urged people to come out for the release of PTI founder Imran Khan, saying the public was ready to join the protest and Pashtuns were not afraid of guns or bullets.
Read : PM Shehbaz, President Zardari discuss overall situation amid intense tensions between Centre, K-P
“We will not accept governor’s rule or an emergency as an unconstitutional measure,” he said, adding that arrests could not weaken their resolve.
The chief minister thanked party workers for the welcome he received in Mardan and said Section 804 was in force throughout the city.
He called on people from across the country to reach Swabi the following day under the leadership of their parliamentarians, assuring them that they would be welcomed and looked after.
🔴 LIVE | Islamabad Long March for Imran Khan | Sohail Afridi's Massive Rally in Mardan https://t.co/QDuptVVgr4
“Those who love Imran Khan will reach Swabi at all costs,” he said, adding that people would travel by motorcycle, bicycle or even on foot if they had no other means of transport.
Afridi said the turnout would be so large this time that no one would dare open fire. He added that the party would not retreat in the face of what he described as oppressive tactics.
“One thousand brave people are better than 10 million cowards,” he said.
The chief minister said the party’s plan in Swabi would leave its opponents stunned. He stressed that the protest would remain peaceful and urged participants not to allow any conspiracy to succeed.
Meanwhile, PTI K-P spokesperson Shaukat Yousafzai rejected reports that the federal government was considering imposing an emergency in the province, saying such a move would be a major mistake and would not resolve the prevailing crisis.
He said the federal government could not impose an emergency in K-P and urged it to accept the PTI’s demands, adding that there was still time to resolve the matter.
Yousafzai said a meeting between Imran Khan and the party leadership could help resolve all outstanding issues. He also urged the government to take advantage of Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s offer to mediate.
He alleged that talk of an emergency was intended to put pressure on the PTI, adding that the party would not succumb to such pressure.
Pictures Thread - Long March Day 7 #اب_راج_کرےگی_خلق_خدا #صوابی_انٹرچینج_۱۱_اکتوبر pic.twitter.com/0R1jJoEBzT
“The long march will continue until our demands are accepted,” he said, asserting that the government could not impose an emergency in the province despite reports of such a move.
The statement came after reports emerged that the federal government completed preparations to impose an emergency in 12 districts of K-P and transfer administrative and police powers to the centre amid the province's worsening security situation.
The federal government has repeatedly threatened to impose an emergency or governor’s rule in K-P over the worsening security situation , with K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi saying that such a move would be taken if necessary. The PTI has opposed the proposal, with party leaders warning they would resign from the national and provincial assemblies if governor’s rule or an emergency was imposed.
PTI terms proposed emergency violation of 18th Amendment
Earlier on Saturday, PTI criticised the reported federal government plan to impose an emergency in 12 districts of the province, saying the move would violate the 18th Constitutional Amendment.
"I would like to inform you of the emergency and the fact that a separate administrative structure has been set up in the 12 districts. This is a serious violation of the 18th Amendment, and the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) has always taken the credit for the amendment," said Yousafzai in a video statement.Yousafzai further said that the PTI had never obstructed the fight against terrorism and had always supported our institutions.
"However, we do insist that all stakeholders here be taken into confidence before any action is taken,” he added.
Yousafzai said an all-parties conference (APC) had already been held, at which political parties and other stakeholders had agreed on a 15-point declaration that was sent to the federal government.
“By implementing this declaration, the matter can be resolved,” he said.
He predicted that a large number of people would reach Swabi on October 11, arguing that the protest would dispel the government's misconception that people would not turn out.
Rejecting the suggestion that emergency rule or governor's rule could resolve the situation, Yousafzai said the country needed a political solution
"I do not think that the emergency and the governor's rule are the solution to this problem. This is never the solution. Pakistan needs a political resolution and stability, and political stability can never be achieved through the indiscriminate use of force against political parties and political workers,” he added.
Yousafzai urged the government “to abandon its stubbornness and ego, come to the negotiating table and find a solution.”
PTI leader maintained that the party had not made “any illegal or unconstitutional demands,” adding that the party wants the “High Court and Supreme Court decisions to be implemented, the restrictions on meetings with party founder Imran Khan, and him to be transferred to a hospital.”
He also called for hearings in Imran's cases and relief and release for his sisters and wife.
Yousafzai also expressed concern over the arrests of provincial ministers, members of the National Assembly, members of the provincial assembly and political workers in K-P.
He said the arrests were particularly troubling amid the ongoing political crisis and argued that negotiations and seriousness were needed to resolve it.
Responding to PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari's remarks that the PTI should abandon confrontational politics and avoid extremism, Yousafzai asked, “Bilawal Bhutto, is raising your voice for your legitimate rights extremism? Is raising your voice for your leader extremism?”
“The deterioration in the political environment so far is entirely the result of the irresponsible and threatening statements made by federal ministers,” Yousafzai said.
With tensions running high on both sides, he said reconciliation and mediation offered a way forward. “I have heard that Maulana Fazlur Rehman has become active in playing a mediating role. I would welcome this, and the PTI would certainly welcome any mediation,” he said.
“I do not believe that problems will be resolved through the use of force. Everyone should realise the difficult situation and the quagmire the country is in. All the problems we are facing can be resolved through negotiations,” the spokesperson said.
He added, “I hope the government will refrain from taking any undemocratic steps that could push the country further into a dead end."
Centre prepares to impose emergency in 12 districts of K-P
According to sources, a high-level meeting is expected to take place today, with the president, prime minister and senior military officials likely to attend.
"The meeting is expected to review reports from national security institutions, after which various proposals concerning the imposition of an emergency or governor's rule could be considered," sources said.
Under the proposed plan, an emergency would be imposed in 12 districts, comprising eight merged tribal districts and four settled districts.
The eight merged tribal districts were Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, Bajaur, Mohmand, North Waziristan, South Waziristan and Lower Waziristan. The four settled districts were Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Bannu and Lakki Marwat.
The sources said a special administrative structure, separate from the provincial government's existing framework, was being considered for these districts.
The emergency was initially proposed for two months, after which the situation would be reviewed, and the arrangement could be extended, they added.
Read : Bilawal urges PTI to return to political engagement, says governor's rule in K-P would be 'atomic bomb'
Under the proposed structure, a secretariat headed by a Grade 21 secretary would be established, with a Grade 21 police officer also appointed to the secretariat.
"Four to six additional administrative officers would be part of the secretariat, responsible for administration, finance, development and planning, and other matters," the sources said.
The officers would be appointed directly by the federal government, they added.
According to the sources, under the proposed administrative arrangement, the deputy commissioners and district police officers of the relevant districts would report to the secretariat, along with the additional inspector general of police.
The provincial government had also been informed of the proposed decision, they said.
The sources added that the relevant provisions of Articles 232 to 234 of the Constitution could be examined while considering the proposed measures.
These constitutional provisions provided different mechanisms for federal intervention under certain extraordinary circumstances during an emergency, they said.
Read more: K-P emergency proposal not linked to PTI long march: Tariq Fazal
"However, the constitutional procedures and legal implications of imposing an emergency and introducing governor's rule were distinct. The final decision would therefore depend on the applicable constitutional requirements," the sources added.
Meanwhile, K-P Information Minister Shafi Jan said that the long march led by Chief Minister Sohail Afridi was proceeding peacefully and would travel from Charsadda to Mardan.
CM Afridi would address the public and party workers at various locations during the march, while large numbers of people from Charsadda, Mardan and other areas would join the convoy, Jan said, and participants would stay overnight in Mardan.
“The large public participation in the long march has left the federal government rattled,” he said.
Shafi Jan said the continued press conferences by federal ministers were evidence of "their fear and panic."
He alleged that the federal government was deeply afraid of CM Afridi, who had been elected by the province’s 45 million people.
“The federal government, which has stolen the public mandate, should understand that the people have rejected its ministers’ negative narrative,” the information minister said.
Threats of governor's rule, emergency loom
The issue of Governor’s Rule and emergency has become a major point of contention between the federal and K-P government. On September 21, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the government was consulting the law ministry on legal options for the province, including Governor’s Rule , if the PTI proceeded with its long march.
Two days later, however, Information Minister Atta Tarar ruled out any plan to impose Governor’s Rule, saying the federal government had no intention of removing the PTI administration.
Some federal ministers publicly raised the possibility of federal intervention in K-P. Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam said consultations were under way on the "constitutional and legal option" of imposing Governors' Rule.
CM Afridi, however, rejected the warnings and said he would not retreat from his position because of threats of Governors' Rule or an emergency. He also said PTI supporters could take to the streets at short notice if an attempt was made to remove him.
However, amid the speculation, just days before the PTI’s planned long march, the prime minister and the president formed a committee last week to negotiate with the PTI and other opposition parties over the march, while expressing concern over the province’s deteriorating law and order situation.
The government and opposition parties held negotiations over two days, and the talks initially appeared to be bearing fruit. However, just as the two sides were nearing agreement on most of the contentious issues , a deadlock emerged, bringing the negotiation process to a halt.
The government blamed the K-P government , particularly CM Afridi, for the deadlock and failure of the negotiations. The PTI, however, claimed that the talks broke down over its demand for a meeting with the party’s founder, which the government refused to accept.
As the negotiation process collapsed, CM Afridi began his long march towards Islamabad, further escalating tensions between the two sides, with both sides continuing to trade allegations .
As tensions peaked, PM Shehbaz once again entered the fray and extended an olive branch to the PTI, saying the government was prepared to engage with the opposition if the party ended its long march and sit-ins.
The PTI, however, rejected the offer as its march continued towards Islamabad, entering its sixth day on Friday. The convoy moved towards Charsadda, with CM Afridi leading the procession.

description: Coalition says it is providing round-the-clock air support to Yemeni government forces, targeting Houthi ballistic missile network
content:
Saudi-led coalition announces large-scale operation against Houthis in Yemen, says 136 military targets destroyed
Yemeni government forces said Saturday they had thwarted a Houthi attack north of Dhubab Airport near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in southwestern Yemen.
In a statement on X, the Giants Brigades said they also inflicted heavy losses on the Houthis in personnel and equipment, without providing further details.
⚔️ Yemeni government forces say they thwarted Houthi attack north of Dhubab Airport near strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait in southwestern Yemen 📢 Giants Brigades report heavy Houthi losses in personnel and equipment https://t.co/Wa9NL1M3UF pic.twitter.com/V71jEWClbF
The repelling of the attack coincided with the Saudi-led coalition's airstrikes targeting Houthi reinforcements, according to the statement. The Houthis did not immediately comment on the statement.
On Friday night, the Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s internationally recognised government announced that it was conducting a large-scale military operation against Houthi forces, saying it had destroyed 136 military targets in Houthi-controlled areas. On US social media company X, coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said the operation was targeting Houthi fighters and military capabilities. The coalition said it was providing round-the-clock air support to Yemeni government forces as part of the ongoing offensive.

Al-Maliki said coalition forces were also working to dismantle and destroy the Houthis’ ballistic missile network.

The announcement came as Yemeni government forces intensified their offensive under Operation “Dawn of Yemen.”
Riyadh airport resumes normal operations after Houthi attacks: Media
Passenger and air traffic at King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital returned to normal on Friday after two attacks by Yemen’s Houthis killed three Saudi citizens and injured others, Saudi state media reported.
State-run Alekhbariya TV said passenger movement at the airport is “flowing smoothly,” with operational services resumed and air traffic back to normal.

The broadcaster said the rapid restoration of flights reflected the readiness of the airport’s infrastructure and the flexibility of Saudi Arabia’s civil aviation system in dealing with exceptional circumstances and containing their effect, while prioritising the safety of passengers and staff.
It noted that the attack on the airport was not the first this week, with the country facing Houthi attacks targeting civilian airports since Tuesday.
Trump 'not happy' with Houthi attacks on Saudi airports
US President Donald Trump denounced Houthi attacks on two airports in Saudi Arabia that killed three people and injured 36 others.
Asked about the attacks, Trump told reporters at the White House: "Not good. It’s not a good thing. I’m not happy about it."
Trump's comments come after a fresh wave of Houthi cross-border strikes.
Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation said that three citizens were killed and others injured in two attacks on Thursday that targeted facilities at the airport and a Saudi Arabian Airlines aircraft.
It said one attack targeted airport facilities, while the second struck a Saudi Airlines aircraft. The attacks injured a number of citizens and residents of different nationalities, it said.

The injuries ranged from minor to serious, and the wounded were taken to hospitals for treatment. It also reported property damage from the attacks, without specifying the extent.
The agency did not identify the party responsible for the attacks, but the Houthis said on Thursday that they had launched ballistic and cruise missile attacks targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Najran Airport in the south, and an air base in Khamis Mushait in the southwest.

title: Pakistan condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia  calls for immediate halt at UNSC
description: Says such reckless attacks that constitute a grave threat to regional peace and security
content:
Says such reckless attacks that constitute a grave threat to regional peace and security
Pakistan on Saturday condemned continued Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including the targeting of infrastructure in Makkah and Madinah, calling for an immediate end to the strikes and warning that they posed “a grave threat to regional peace and security”.
“The security and sanctity of the Two Holy Mosques must be respected at all times,” Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, said during the UN Security Council's monthly briefing on Yemen.
“We strongly condemn the continued Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, including the outrageous targeting of infrastructure in the Makkah Governorate and on the Taibah power distribution station in Madinah tul Munawwarah,” Ahmad said.
He added that Pakistan also strongly condemned Houthi terrorist attacks targeting King Khalid International Airport and Abha International Airport, which resulted in civilian deaths and injuries.
“We call for an immediate end of such reckless attacks that constitute a grave threat to regional peace and security,” the envoy stated.
Statement by Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, Permanent Representative of Pakistan to the UN, At the UN Security Council Monthly Briefing on Yemen (09 October 2026) *********** Madam President, 1. I would like to thank you in particular for your kind words addressed to me… pic.twitter.com/Ix7lQzOqlz
Quoting Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's statement issued a day earlier, the envoy said that, “Pakistan stands in unwavering solidarity with the leadership and people of brotherly Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.”
“In line with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, and recent decisions taken by its Strategic Political and Defence Committee, our commitment to the Kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security is resolute,” he quoted the prime minister as saying.
“We also fully support Saudi Arabia’s legitimate right to defend its people and protect its cities and vital infrastructure,” Ahmad said, quoting PM Shehbaz.
He said that the Houthi militia must "immediately cease these attacks" and will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with Saudi Arabia in the face of these threats.
At the briefing, the envoy described Yemen's descent into conflict as “deeply alarming”, citing the escalation of hostilities, continued Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, threats to commercial shipping, fighting around Taiz and Bab el-Mandeb, and the deepening humanitarian crisis.
“These developments demand our urgent attention,” he said, setting out four priorities for Pakistan: condemning attacks on Saudi Arabia, supporting Yemen's sovereignty and territorial integrity, backing diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, and protecting civilians.
Pakistan reaffirmed its support for Yemen's “sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity” and its internationally recognised government.
Read: PM Shehbaz condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, calls for immediate halt
Ahmad said the intensifying Houthi offensive along Yemen's western coast and around Bab el-Mandeb underscored the urgency of protecting maritime security.
“Houthis must cease attacks on commercial shipping,” he said. “Freedom of navigation must be upheld in accordance with international law.”
“These vital waterways cannot remain exposed to attacks that endanger seafarers, disrupt trade and compound global economic hardship,” he added.
Ahmad expressed support for UN Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg's efforts, including his recent engagements, and called for greater diplomatic engagement to prevent further escalation.
“All diplomatic channels must be used to contain escalation, maintain communication and facilitate a cessation of hostilities,” he said.
Ahmad added that Pakistan supported Grundberg's mediation role and his call for political strategies to resolve the conflict. “These efforts should restore a credible, inclusive, Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned political process under United Nations auspices,” he said.
At the beginning of his remarks, Ahmad thanked the special envoy and Assistant Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator Mohammad Yahya for their briefings. He also acknowledged the remarks by Inger Ashing.
He thanked the Security Council president for her words addressed to him, saying he believed they also reflected goodwill towards Pakistan. “It has been a great honour representing Pakistan at the United Nations and in the Security Council,” he said.
Ahmad also thanked fellow council members for the opportunity to work with them and praised their commitment to the shared objective of maintaining international peace and security, which he called the council's primary responsibility.
He thanked UN Secretary-General António Guterres, senior officials in the Secretariat, special envoys including Grundberg, special representatives in the field, and thousands of UN peacekeepers deployed on various missions for their contributions.
He also acknowledged the work of colleagues in the Secretariat's Security Council Affairs Division and his own team for their support.
“Together, we have achieved a lot,” Ahmad said, adding that numerous situations and challenges still required the council's collective attention and continued work, with Yemen among them.
Turning to the humanitarian situation, the envoy warned that renewed fighting was worsening conditions for civilians.
He pointed to the offensive around Taiz and an attack by Houthi elements on Aden airport, saying both highlighted the vulnerability of civilian populations and essential infrastructure.
“Civilians must be protected,” he said. “Safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilian infrastructure, and adequate funding for relief operations are indispensable,” Ahmad added.
“Food, fuel and essential commercial supplies must reach all those in need,” he said.
Pakistan also reiterated its call for the “immediate, unconditional and safe release” of detained United Nations, humanitarian and diplomatic personnel.
Concluding his remarks, Ahmad urged the Security Council to respond collectively to the conflict, “The Council must act with unity and purpose to halt Houthi attacks, safeguard regional security, alleviate suffering and restore a credible path towards a political settlement,” he said.
Ahmad reaffirmed Pakistan's support for the Yemeni people and "efforts towards a peaceful, stable and united Yemen, and will continue to make every effort to advance lasting peace and stability in the region."
Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted 3 Houthi ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh, Khamis Mushait
The latest attacks followed a series of Houthi missile and drone strikes targeting Saudi airports and other infrastructure. Saudi authorities said three people were killed and 36 injured, including a Pakistani national, in attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha International Airport on October 6 and 7.
The Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed multiple ballistic missiles launched towards Riyadh and Khamis Mushait in the southwestern Asir region. Coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said two missiles had been fired towards the Saudi capital and another towards Khamis Mushait.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed the group had targeted King Khalid International Airport with a ballistic missile, saying the strike had disrupted air traffic. He also warned workers at Saudi oil facilities and airlines operating in Saudi airspace about locations the group had declared targets for its military operations.
In response, the Saudi-led coalition said it had struck more than 80 Houthi military sites across the Yemeni governorates of Saada, Hodeidah, Jawf and Marib, warning that the attacks on Saudi Arabia “will not go unpunished”.

title: Indian police detain  cockroach  movement founder Abhijeet Dipke
description: Police also detains protesters  locks down Delhi ahead of rally against election chief
content:
Police also detains protesters, locks down Delhi ahead of rally against election chief
Police in the Indian capital ​Delhi detained the founder ‌of the Cockroach Janta Party, Abhijeet Dipke, on Saturday, ​ahead of a protest ​called by the youth ⁠movement demanding the resignation ​of the country’s chief ​election commissioner, the party said.
TV channels reported earlier that police officers ​met Dipke at ​the Delhi airport after he arrived ‌from ⁠the financial capital, Mumbai, and asked him to call off the protest ​as authorities ​had ⁠banned it.
CJP leaders Saurav Das and ​Ashutosh Ranka were also ​detained ⁠from their flight upon landing, the movement said ⁠in ​a statement.
India detains protesters, locks down Delhi ahead of rally against election chief
Police in the Indian ​capital detained scores of protesters on Saturday amid patrols by thousands of security forces, with travel and telecoms links suspended, in a lockdown to stop a ‌youth protest asking the election chief to quit.
The protest by the "Cockroach" youth movement aims to draw thousands of demonstrators against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a revision of voter lists that critics say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party.
Television images showed police in the central business district of New Delhi chasing down a few dozen young protesters, some wearing backpacks, before they were loaded into vehicles and hauled away.
Read: Indian youth leader says protest will go ahead despite detentions
About 200 ​protesters were detained in the area, a police source told Reuters . Those detained outside Delhi included protest supporter Dhruv Rathee, a popular figure on YouTube, a police ​spokesperson said.
With metro stations and markets shut and mobile internet suspended, police boarded buses to check for protesters after stopping them at points of ⁠entry into the city, with cars and other vehicles also subjected to checks, Reuters witnesses said.
Barricades and concrete blocks stopped traffic, while anti-riot vehicles mounted with tear gas guns ​were stationed on key routes, they said.
"Why is the prime minister so scared of the country's youth, the country's people?" Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the self-named 'Cockroach Janta Party' that called the ​protest, asked on Saturday, shortly before leaving for Delhi.
"Why did you need to close all the railways, the metro, the internet has been closed, roads have been closed? ... this is nothing but fear," he told the ANI news agency in the financial capital of Mumbai.
The protesters have said they plan to gather at Jantar Mantar, a protest site designated by authorities in the heart of New Delhi, at 10am.
The protest, touted by the CJP as an effort to "Save Democracy", is planned as the biggest of a series of demonstrations launched last week after the Indian Express ​newspaper said Kumar's deputies had queried and disagreed with him over list revisions that dropped about 130 million voters.
That number exceeds the population of Japan.
Opposition parties have long accused the government of trying ‌to fix voter ⁠lists to its advantage and were quick to resurrect the allegations following the report.
Read more: Indian opposition protest police action against lawmakers, push for poll chief's resignation
Kumar has not commented, but the Election Commission and the BJP have denied the allegations.
The BJP says Modi's popularity and India's economic growth are key reasons for its electoral dominance and accuses opposition parties of misleading the country as they are unable to win elections.
Nonetheless, the near-daily protests by opposition groups pose a new political challenge to Modi, just months after similar demonstrations forced his education minister to quit over exam paper leaks.
They also come months before a series of ​key state elections starting in early 2027, among ​them one in the most populous state ⁠of Uttar Pradesh, ruled by the BJP.
On Friday, Delhi police said they had not given permission for the protest, and violators would face the force of the law.
Their "temporary and precautionary" curbs aimed at regulating people's movement, preventing overcrowding, maintaining public order, and ensuring the safety ​of protesters and others in the affected areas, police said in a statement.
CJP leaders rejected the police decision and said they would ​go ahead with the ⁠protest as it was their fundamental right.
Deletions affected state polls, opposition alleges
The protesters accuse the BJP of using the revision of voter lists to sway election results, in collusion with its appointees in the Election Commission, including Kumar.
Opposition parties say the voter deletions affected the outcome of some recent state elections won by the BJP, and have cast a shadow on the electoral process in ⁠the world's ​largest democracy.
Election Commission data, also cited by the BJP, shows that about 130 million names have been deleted from ​voter lists during the verification exercise, including 63 million who relocated, 30 million who could not be traced, and 28 million dead.
The commission says the count represents voter entries flagged during the draft revision stage, that the exercise is not ​complete yet, and that voters wrongly removed can enroll again.

title: Following Houthi attacks  Europe s aviation safety    body expands Saudi airspace warning
description: Attacks show greater focus on aviation infrastructure than previously  increasing risks to aircraft
content:
Attacks show greater focus on aviation infrastructure than previously, increasing risks to aircraft
The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) widened its Saudi Arabia airspace warning on Friday, after the Houthis attacked two airports.
The regulator said in an update to a conflict zone information, which was first issued last month, that recent attacks have demonstrated the ability and intent of the Houthis to strike targets "deeper inside Saudi territory."
"While the southern and south-western parts of Saudi airspace remain particularly exposed due to their proximity to Houthi-controlled areas in Yemen, recent attacks have demonstrated the ability and intent of the Houthis to strike targets deeper inside Saudi territory, including in the Riyadh, Tabuk, Medina and Yanbu areas,” it said.
It noted that within the broader escalation observed since late September, repeated missile and drone attacks targeted the area of the capital Riyadh, including its airport.
"During this period, attacks also showed a greater focus on aviation infrastructure than previously, increasing risks to aircraft on the ground and during take-off and landing in the affected areas," according to the EASA.
Read: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted 3 Houthi ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh, Khamis Mushait
"These recurrent missile and drone attacks, together with the activation of air-defence systems, create an increased risk of misidentification of civil aircraft, as well as risks associated with missile and drone overflights, interception activity and falling debris," it said.
The advisory came after Yemen's Houthi group recently carried out ballistic missile and drone attacks targeting Riyadh and other areas of Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia’s Civil Aviation Authority said three people were killed and 36 were injured in Houthi attacks on Abha International Airport in the southern city of Abha and the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.

title: Under new regulations  Turkiye bans children under 15 from social media
description: Providers must also offer differentiated services and take necessary measures for users 15 and older
content:
Providers must also offer differentiated services, take necessary measures for users 15 and older
Turkiye has barred social network providers from offering services to minors under the age of 15, according to new Cyber Security Directorate regulations published on Saturday in the Official Gazette.
The regulation said providers "cannot provide services to children who have not reached the age of 15."
Providers must also offer differentiated services and take necessary measures for users 15 and older, according to the regulations, adding that they should consider the minor’s best interests and their physical, mental, psychological, social, and emotional development.
Age verification must prioritise personal data protection, using methods that determine only whether a user meets the age threshold rather than establishing identity, it added.
Read: Making sense of AI on social media
Saying that providers must make the reliability of verification methods, their algorithm structures, and child-focused service policies "clear, auditable and testable for users, parents and the directorate," it stressed that they must create clear, user-friendly parental control tools.
The regulations come under new legislation on social media passed by the Turkish parliament this April.

title: Iran s Pezeshkian says regional diplomacy must go beyond meetings  highlights dialogue  cooperation
description: US president says Russia to supply diesel to US and global markets
content:
Trump says Iran 'failing badly,' keeps military option open
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Saturday said in a post on X that regional diplomacy "shouldn't just be about holding meetings," adding that it "must be a real tool: for crisis management, maintaining dialogue, preventing escalation, and driving practical cooperation."
Regional diplomacy shouldn't just be about holding meetings. It must be a real tool: for crisis management, maintaining dialogue, preventing escalation, and driving practical cooperation.
On Friday, United States President Donald Trump said that Washington may take action against Iran, while asserting that Tehran is "failing badly."
Asked why a US response might be tied to the Nov. 3 midterm elections – about three weeks away – rather than being carried out now, Trump said: "We may. We will see."
"But I think that they’re failing badly. Their country is failing badly. Their military is defeated. They have no navy. They have no air force. They have 300% inflation, and Iran is in very bad shape," he told reporters.
Trump did not elaborate on what steps his administration could take or a timeline for possible action.
Trump says Russia to supply diesel to US and global markets
President Donald Trump said on Friday that Russia had agreed to supply ​diesel to global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices, and his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel that were designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for its ‌war on Ukraine.
Prices for diesel, used for agriculture, heating homes and trucking, are near a record and risk for Trump's fellow Republicans ahead of the November 3 congressional elections that will determine whether they maintain thin control of Congress. Diesel prices fell after the announcement, but analysts said the deal may not be enough to keep them down.
Trump said on social media he had a "highly successful" discussion with President Vladimir Putin in which they agreed that Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel to US and ​global markets, equal to about 2.25 million barrels of fuel. The US exports about 1.5 million barrels of diesel per day.
After the call, an envoy for Putin, Kirill Dmitriev, praised cooperation between Russia and ​the US in a post on X. Dmitriev asked US officials during his visit to Washington last month for licenses to export diesel to the US market to ⁠be granted to all Russian major oil firms, sources familiar with the situation said.
In October 2025, the US imposed sanctions on Russian oil companies over Moscow's war that began in 2022. The diesel exports could provide Moscow with billions of dollars ​in revenues that could help Putin continue the war with Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy criticised the deal, announced while a Ukrainian delegation was in the US to discuss how to seek a resolution of the war, as a "weak ​decision on the part of strong partners."
"Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world. Russia will 'repay' the diesel with further terror and perfidy," he said on X.
The deal was also criticised by US lawmakers, including Trump's fellow Republican, Representative Don Bacon, who said it is time to apply more sanctions that Congress passed recently, not lift the measures.
Read: US voices concern over Houthi escalation, condemns attacks on Saudi Arabia
"Now is the time to use those sanctions to squeeze Putin’s war machine, not reward a dictator by putting more ​money in his hands while he continues targeting and killing Ukrainian civilians," Bacon said on X.
The US Treasury Department issued a license allowing importation of Russian diesel until April 7.
Trump said Russia would supply another ​500,000 tons in November and a further 1 million tons "immediately thereafter." Even more would follow, Trump said, "based on the condition of their diesel refineries," which have been damaged by Ukrainian attacks.
Analysts said the agreement was unlikely to lead ‌to sustained lower ⁠fuel prices. "I cannot overstate how much of a nothing burger this is," Rory Johnston, an oil market researcher and founder of CommodityContext.com, said on X, adding that Russia usually exports much more diesel than volumes in the deal when its refinery fleet is not under attack.
I CANNOT OVERSTATE HOW MUCH OF A NOTHING BURGER THIS IS pic.twitter.com/XaUOkyZqzy
"It's clearly not a fix, but another stream to aid a very tight diesel market," said Jim Mitchell, an analyst at consultancy Wood Mackenzie.
Diesel prices, which are often a big driver of inflation, are up 70% since the US and Israel launched the war with Iran on February 28. The wars in Iran and Ukraine have triggered a severe global fuel supply crunch, pushing average US diesel prices ​to $6.28 a gallon on Thursday, according to the ​AAA motorist group.
Read More: IRGC says it struck LPG tanker attempting to cross Strait of Hormuz
Prices have stayed high despite two recent ⁠moves by Trump to boost supplies of the fuel: pressuring allies to release emergency reserves and expanding access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel, which is normally used for farm equipment.
US diesel futures fell almost 5% following news of the deal and were trading at $4.64 a gallon.
"Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is ​my Greatest Priority," Trump said.

title: Apni Chhat Apna Ghar: Maryam Nawazmakes history with global recognition  | The Express Tribune
description:
Apni Chhat Apna Ghar: Maryam Nawaz
makes history with global recognition
content:
A home is one of the greatest blessings bestowed by Allah Almighty. Its true value is best understood by those who do not have a home of their own. Providing a roof to a homeless, deserving and underprivileged person is also a special blessing from Allah. The opportunity to serve one's people and help them secure a home of their own is not granted to everyone.
The true significance of having one's own home can only be understood through the emotions of a person who has lived without one or has spent years paying rent. Chief Minister of Punjab Maryam Nawaz has turned this dream into a reality for thousands of deserving and homeless families.
Within just one and a half years, Maryam Nawaz has succeeded in providing 214,330 homes to deserving people across Punjab. Of these, 120,753 beneficiaries have already completed their homes, while another 60,464 houses are currently under construction. So far, Rs278.461 billion in interest-free loans have been disbursed under the programme.
The initiative was particularly close to Maryam Nawaz's heart because it was also a dream of former Prime Minister Muhammad Nawaz Sharif: to enable ordinary people to own homes of their own. Maryam Nawaz has transformed that dream into a reality.
These homes are not merely figures on paper; they are a visible reality on the ground. A dedicated website has been developed for the Apni Chhat Apna Ghar programme, providing real-time information on the locations of the houses. The number of completed and ongoing houses, as well as the amount of loans disbursed, is updated on a daily basis.
The greatest evidence of the programme's transparency is the complete absence of political interference. The entire process is online. Applicants seeking interest-free loans submit their complete and accurate information through the website, following which the relevant institution conducts a thorough verification before approving the application.
Citizens are not required to visit government offices or make rounds of departments. They can apply from the comfort of their homes and receive the facility through a transparent digital process.
In the initial days of the programme, many beneficiaries were astonished when their loans were approved without them having to visit a government office. They wondered how such a substantial relief package could reach them while they remained at home. There was simply no comparable precedent in the past for providing such large-scale relief to thousands of people through a completely digital and accessible mechanism.
Today, more than 200,000 homes are being built across Punjab, and the beneficiaries of the programme are expressing their gratitude to Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz.
It is precisely because of the success of this initiative that the United Nations recognised the Apni Chhat Apna Ghar programme with a global award. The award recognises five major programmes from around the world, and the Punjab government's housing initiative secured the top position.
The award ceremony was specially held in Muscat, Oman, where Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz was invited to the stage and presented with the award. The international recognition was a tribute to her vision and the success of the programme.
This is not merely an award for the Government of Punjab; it is a matter of pride for the 140 million people of Punjab. For Pakistan, it is also a moment of great pride that, for the first time, a Pakistani politician and chief minister has received such significant international recognition for a public welfare initiative.

title: Shrinking grounds put grassroots cricket under pressure
description: Shrinking grounds put grassroots cricket under pressure
content:
Loss of neighbourhood playing fields is narrowing opportunities for young cricketers across the city
Lahore's shrinking number of playing fields is squeezing neighbourhood cricket, particularly for young players from low- and middle-income families. As rapid urban development replaces or limits historic grounds such as Minto Park, Baba Ground, Chauburji, Garhi Shahu and Dharampura, children are increasingly turning to streets and other unsafe spaces, weakening the traditional grassroots pathway through which the city's cricket talent emerges.
Minto Park has historically played a particularly important role in Lahore's cricketing culture. Once regarded as one of the city's biggest cricket nurseries, it hosted dozens of club nets. During the tenure of former PCB chairman Gen (retd) Tauqir Zia, around two dozen additional nets were also installed under the Pakistan Cricket Board. Young players from across Lahore would train there under experienced coaches before returning home.
Several players who trained at Minto Park, including Inzamam-ul-Haq, Taufeeq Umar, Nasir Jamshed and Ahmed Shehzad, went on to represent Pakistan at the international level. Over time, however, many of the cricket and other sporting facilities at the park disappeared.
Former ICC Test umpire and Muslim Club president Mian Aslam, along with other figures associated with local cricket, still regard Minto Park as an important part of Lahore's cricketing history. Aslam said the park had produced seven Pakistan cricket team captains, including Inzamam-ul-Haq.
Baba Ground, Chauburji, Garhi Shahu, Dharampura and several other grounds across Lahore have also traditionally served as important centres for local cricket. Youngsters played alongside teams from local clubs, while children from families with limited financial resources could begin playing without having to pay expensive academy fees.
Local cricket officials say pressure on these grounds has increased with the expansion of the city. In some areas, playing fields have been reduced in size, while sporting activity has been restricted or discontinued altogether. Children now increasingly turn to streets, roads, parking areas and small vacant spaces to play cricket, but residents say these are not safe alternatives because of traffic and other urban activity.
Ali Iqbal, President of Township Gymkhana, said several grounds had been taken over by housing societies and that young cricketers also faced difficulties accessing the grounds that remained. "Building new grounds alone is not enough, and existing facilities need to be restored and equipped with basic amenities."
Iqbal said the shortage of net practice facilities was also affecting the development of young players. A cricketer needed regular net practice, coaching and match experience to improve, he said, adding that a lack of suitable grounds near players' homes could disrupt that development.
Azhar Zaidi, a leading figure at another historic cricket centre, P&T Gymkhana Club, said the club had produced internationally recognised players including Abdul Razzaq, Imran Nazir, Mohammad Irfan and Aleem Dar. He believed Lahore's club cricket system had played an important role in developing players who later represented Pakistan at national and international levels. Zaidi said many young players joining the club came from low- and middle-income families and that P&T Gymkhana tried, within its resources, to provide them with facilities so financial difficulties did not prevent them from developing their talent.
Lahore may still have plenty of cricketing talent, but with grounds disappearing, young players are increasingly running out of places to play. For a city that has long produced national stars from its streets, clubs and neighbourhood grounds, preserving these spaces could be key to keeping its cricketing pipeline alive.

Addressing a press conference at the Peshawar Press Club along with other party leaders, Bacha said that in the previous day's cabinet meeting, Asif Ali Zardari and Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, leaders of the country's most popular political party, the PPP, which had provided the forum for those negotiations, were subjected to severe criticism. Bacha accused the chief minister, who launched his long march from areas under terrorist siege and is touring the province from a container, of now convening cabinet meetings solely for criticism. He said the chief minister had targeted those who facilitated talks with the Centre, levelled harsh criticism against the governor, and opposed the meeting in which Governor Faisal Karim Kundi received a briefing from institutions on law and order.
The meeting should have been called a month earlier, Bacha argued, because PTI is not sincere towards K-P. "The situation in the province is extremely precarious. In such circumstances the Constitution allows the governor to play his role, but the PTI chief minister is completely unfamiliar with the Constitution."
He claimed that under the banner of a long march the convoy is now circling different cities of the province under the chief minister's leadership from a container, and "it seems this caravan will also tour Afghanistan." This, he said, is the same terrorism that the PPP has consistently opposed, the terrorism that martyred Benazir Bhutto and eight of the party's MPAs.
The PPP, Bacha said, speaks for the survival of parliament and advises the chief minister to study the Constitution. "In the past 13 years the PTI government in K-P has delivered nothing. It remains absorbed only in Imran Khan's narrative and has no interest in the problems of the people. Today our soldiers and police personnel are sacrificing their lives fighting terrorists for the country's survival, while these people are misleading the youth. On the other hand the public is making sacrifices because of terrorists. Unemployment is widespread in K-P and corruption is at its peak; contracts worth billions of rupees are being awarded to favourites for crores."

Three MNAs, five MPAs missing since Sept 20; party says more than 18 workers also disappeared
Alleged abductions and arrests of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) lawmakers and workers in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa have continued unabated, with the party reporting that three members of the national assembly and five members of the provincial assembly have been taken since 20 September.
PTI leaders say the incidents intensified after the party announced its long march. According to party accounts, the tally now includes the three MNAs and five MPAs plus more than a dozen-and-a-half workers and office-bearers who remain missing.
The sequence of reported events began with an alleged attempt to abduct Provincial Minister for Construction and Communication Shakeel Khan on 20 September. The following day, Provincial Minister for Irrigation Fazal Shakoor Khan was reportedly seized from a motorway toll plaza.
On 22 September, National Assembly member Fazal Khan from Charsadda was said to have been taken from Rashakai. That same night, between 22 and 23 September, Zubair Khan, the National Assembly member from South Waziristan, was allegedly abducted from his residence in Dera Ismail Khan.
Provincial Assembly member Muhammad Riaz from Kolai-Palas was reported missing on 25 September, while Sultan Rom, the MPA from Swat, was taken by unidentified persons the next day. In a separate incident, unidentified assailants attacked the hujra of MPA Abdul Karim Tordher in Swabi with intense gunfire and then abducted his brother Abdul Nasir along with three security guards.
Reports have also emerged of the arrests in Islamabad of MPA Fateh-ul-Mulk Nasir from Chitral and National Assembly member Dawar Kundi from Tank.
Earlier cases cited by the party include the 17 September abduction of Amir Ijaz, regional general secretary of the Insaf Lawyers Forum. PTI has claimed that Dr Nabi Jan of the Insaf Doctors Forum was likewise taken by unidentified persons. In Mardan, the abduction of MPA Abdul Salam Afridi has been reported and a first information report lodged with police.
Party spokesmen describe the pattern as systematic targeting of elected representatives and grassroots workers in the province. They say the operations have created an atmosphere of fear among PTI ranks and disrupted organisational activity ahead of the planned long march.
Official confirmation of the status of each individual remains limited. Some cases have been registered as abductions; others are described by authorities as arrests linked to ongoing investigations. Families and party lawyers continue to press for information on the whereabouts of those still unaccounted for.
As of the latest reports from Peshawar, the series of incidents that began after 20 September has not subsided, leaving three national and five provincial lawmakers either missing or in custody and a larger number of PTI workers untraceable.

title: Seasonal illnesses surge across Quetta
description: Seasonal illnesses surge across Quetta
content:
Cold, dry weather fuels respiratory ailments
A sharp rise in seasonal illnesses has been reported across Quetta following the recent change in weather. Children, women, young people and the elderly are increasingly falling ill with colds, flu, cough, fever, sore throat, body aches and respiratory problems. Patients already suffering from asthma and allergies are also facing greater difficulties.
The sudden drop in temperature combined with dry and cold winds has led to a noticeable increase in health complaints among residents. Outpatient departments (OPDs) at both government and private hospitals in the city are witnessing heavy rush, with large numbers of people seeking treatment daily for weather-related ailments.
Health experts note that viral infections tend to spread more rapidly during seasonal transitions. Cold and dry air further aggravates respiratory conditions, asthma and allergies.
Experts recommend wearing a mask outdoors to protect against dust and cold winds. They also advise drinking lukewarm water, consuming hot beverages, soup and maintaining a balanced diet. If symptoms persist or breathing becomes difficult, people should consult a doctor promptly rather than self-medicating.
Parents have been urged to protect children from cold winds and abrupt temperature changes, while special care is advised for the elderly and those with pre-existing respiratory conditions.

title: Fasten seatbelts for traffic nightmare
description: Fasten seatbelts for traffic nightmare
content:
Over 96km of roads to be excavated for Rs72b project; alternative routes yet to be finalised
The city's already congested roads are set for another major test, with more than 20 main thoroughfares due to be dug up for the K-IV augmentation project. The work, expected to begin in January 2027, will stretch across 96 kilometres of roads and take 22 months to complete.
For a city where roadworks can drag on for months and even a short stretch can become a daily traffic bottleneck, the prospect of excavation across multiple arteries raises questions about how commuters will navigate the disruption. Officials, however, have yet to finalise a plan for alternative routes and traffic management.
The Karachi Water and Sewerage Services Improvement Project (KWSSIP) has confirmed that the roads will be excavated to lay augmentation pipelines. Project Manager Faisal Javed told journalists during a briefing at his office that a strategy was being prepared to maintain traffic flow and minimise inconvenience to commuters.
He said the work would be carried out in phases, with excavation limited to stretches of one to three kilometres at a time rather than opening up the entire city simultaneously. The project team would also be responsible for restoring roads after the pipelines were installed, he added.
The estimated cost of the augmentation project is Rs72 billion, although the amount could increase. According to Javed, the tendering process is under way, and work is expected to begin in January 2027.
The timeline drew questions from journalists, who pointed out that the 2.7-kilometre stretch between Hasan Square and NIPA had taken a year to complete. Asked how the authorities expected to finish work on 96 kilometres of roads in just 22 months, Javed maintained that the augmentation project would meet its deadline.
The project is being funded by two international financial institutions, with the Sindh government contributing 20% of the cost, Javed said. Excavation is also expected to encounter infrastructure belonging to Sui Southern Gas Company and K-Electric. He said a formula had been prepared to cover payments related to the utilities' installations.
Once completed, the augmentation lines are expected to support the supply of an additional 250 million gallons of water per day to Karachi through the K-IV project, drawing water from Keenjhar Lake. The additional supply is intended for areas facing severe shortages or receiving little or no water.
The briefing also covered KWSSIP's broader efforts to improve the city's water supply and sewerage infrastructure. Established by the Sindh government three years ago, the organisation is implementing projects financed through loans from international financial institutions.
Javed said three components had been completed under the first phase at a cost of $100 million. These included work on pipeline No 5 at the Dhabeji pumping station, improvements at the Pipri pumping station and measures to protect pipelines along the Lyari River.
He said the replacement of the 5.5-kilometre pipeline at Dhabeji alone had cost Rs2.5 billion. The organisation's projects are expected to be completed within four and a half years, with $1.4 billion earmarked for improvements to water supply and sewerage infrastructure.
The briefing was the first time in three years that KWSSIP had invited the media to discuss its projects. Journalists said officials were unable to provide satisfactory answers to several questions, while Project Director Ayesha Hameed did not appear before the media.

title: Madhubala beats TB  but fight for recovery continues
description: Madhubala beats TB  but fight for recovery continues
content:
Madhubala has been experiencing severe health problems for several weeks
Beating tuberculosis has not ended Madhubala's battle for survival. The 22-year-old elephant at Safari Park is now free of the disease, but its lingering effects have left her physically weak and in need of several more weeks of intensive treatment and rehabilitation.
Speaking to The Express Tribune at Safari Park, Four Paws chief Dr Amir Khalil said Madhubala's weakened immune system, weight loss and deteriorating physical condition remained major concerns. Her hind legs are particularly weak, while swelling in her limbs and cracks in her toenails have affected her mobility.
The elephant may even require a crane to help her get back on her feet if she falls, Khalil warned, highlighting the seriousness of her condition.
Madhubala has been experiencing severe health problems for several weeks. Although a bacterial infection was initially suspected, Khalil said there was no longer evidence of such an infection. However, her declining weight and lack of strength in her hind legs continue to complicate her recovery.
Khalil said medication alone would not be enough to restore Madhubala's health. Her treatment plan includes nutritional support, physiotherapy and specialised care to rebuild her strength and improve her overall condition.
The elephant will receive multivitamins, minerals and dietary supplements, with particular attention to supporting her liver health. Daily water-based massages and physiotherapy will also be required to improve blood circulation in her leg muscles.
Swimming will form another important part of her rehabilitation, allowing her to move her legs while gradually rebuilding muscle strength.
The condition of Madhubala's legs and toenails remains a particular concern for the veterinary team. Khalil said that treating elephants presents unique challenges, including the difficulty of administering injections, requiring specialised handling and treatment procedures.
Pakistani and foreign specialists are working together to improve Madhubala's condition. According to Khalil, international experts have been providing guidance remotely over the past several weeks.
He said there were encouraging signs of improvement, but it was too early to make definitive predictions about her recovery. For now, the priority was to stabilise her condition and provide the intensive care she needed.
Madhubala's sister, Malika, has also been looking after her and playing an important role in her care, Khalil said.

Lured by promises of jobs in Turkey and Iraq, 21 Pakistanis were allegedly drawn into a human smuggling network that planned to send them to Europe through dangerous, irregular migration routes. The FIA's Anti-Human Trafficking Circle has arrested two suspected agents and taken all 21 people into custody for protection and further inquiry.
The rescued men, including 16 from Balochistan and five from Karachi's Sohrab Goth area, were allegedly being moved through Iran and Iraq before being sent to Turkey, Greece, Cyprus and other destinations via the so-called Dunki routes.
Assistant Director Afroz Kalwar told a press conference that the arrested suspects, identified as Babar Shehzad and Imtiaz Malik, had allegedly been involved in the illicit business for around 20 years, luring Pakistani citizens with promises of taking them abroad.
According to FIA Investigation Officer Masroor Baloch, the victims had been charged Rs500,000 each. Some were brought from central Punjab to Karachi by bus or train and then allegedly transported through Balochistan towards Iran's coastal city of Chabahar, using both land and sea routes.
Baloch said the victims had been promised employment in Turkey and Iraq. Some were allegedly to be taken from Jiwani in Balochistan to Chabahar and then moved through irregular migration routes towards Turkey, Greece and Cyprus.
He added that the investigation had also uncovered allegations that some victims had previously been held for ransom, while disturbing claims had emerged about the possible removal and sale of human organs. These allegations are being examined as part of the ongoing investigation.

title: Axe falls on KU s exam controller amid LLB result scandal
description: Axe falls on KU s exam controller amid LLB result scandal
content:
Inquiry into suspected result manipulation yet to begin
Blank answer scripts carrying passing marks, failed students receiving revised mark sheets and an alleged scrutiny process that bypassed university rules have put the University of Karachi's examination system under scrutiny. The university has now removed its controller of examinations, but a formal inquiry into the alleged manipulation of law college results has yet to begin.
Controller of Examinations Dr Muhammad Yasir Khan has been removed from the post and sent back to his department to resume teaching. Vice Chancellor Dr Waseem Qazi has appointed Dr Ghufran Saeed of the Department of Food Science as his replacement, with an official notification issued to this effect.
The administrative action follows revelations by The Express Tribune about more than 150 law students who were initially declared unsuccessful but were subsequently awarded passing marks through a disputed scrutiny process. The absence of a formal investigation has raised concerns about the preservation of evidence relating to the alleged alteration of results.
According to reports, the newly appointed permanent VC personally obtained and examined examination answer scripts and found that many were blank despite marks having been awarded to the candidates.
The students belonged to the LLB programmes at SM Law College and Islamia College. Express News had obtained and broadcast images of their answer scripts, original and revised mark sheets, and award sheets, documenting discrepancies between the initial results and those issued after scrutiny. The results had reportedly been altered on the recommendation of the dean of the Faculty of Law and with the approval of former acting VC Dr Tufail Ahmed. The dean of law had convened a meeting with the principals of the relevant colleges, which was described in the report as a fictitious scrutiny committee.
The committee met on August 5 under the chairmanship of the dean and decided to re-examine answer scripts for Paper V of LLB Part II. However, university regulations do not permit the re-evaluation of examination answer scripts under the annual system, where scrutiny is limited to recounting marks. On August 6, the then controller of examinations obtained the acting VC's approval for the committee's recommendations. The approval reportedly included the phrase "other related cases", which was subsequently used to extend the decision to students who had failed Pakistan Studies papers as well.Following the approval, the principal of SM Law College asked students to apply for scrutiny on the same day. The then controller of examinations had, however, described the information as incorrect.
Several students who had failed papers in Obligations and Pakistan Studies, including candidates awarded zero or low marks, were allegedly given between 50 and 65 marks after the scrutiny process. The examinations department had initially issued mark sheets declaring them unsuccessful before issuing revised documents showing them as having passed.

content:
Eight-year-old girl allegedly raped during a family wedding visit
Police have registered a case against a man accused of sexually assaulting an eight-year-old girl in the Sadiqabad police jurisdiction, as well as several of his relatives who allegedly attempted to suppress the incident and harassed the child and her family.
According to the complaint filed by the girl's father, Nauman Ijaz, his two daughters, aged eight and six, travelled from Lahore to Rawalpindi with their paternal grandmother on September 23 to attend a relative's wedding.
The father alleged that after returning to Lahore, his eight-year-old daughter told her mother that she had been sexually assaulted on the night of September 25 while sleeping at the house of Parveen Akhtar, the grandmother of the accused, Haider Ali.

When she woke up in pain and screamed, the suspect allegedly covered her mouth with his hand and threatened to kill her if she told anyone about the incident.
The father said the family took the girl to a female gynaecologist, who, after examining her, advised them to seek a medical examination at a government hospital and register a case against the suspect.
The complainant further alleged that the girl had initially told her paternal grandmother about the incident, who informed the suspect's maternal grandmother. However, instead of reporting the matter to the police, the suspect's mother, aunt and other relatives allegedly attempted to hush it up, citing the ongoing wedding celebrations and the risk of bringing embarrassment to the family.
The complaint alleged that the girl, her grandmother and other family members were repeatedly harassed and pressured not to disclose the incident to her parents in Lahore. The father also accused another relative, Ayan Ali, of mentally tormenting the child while she remained in Rawalpindi.
The complainant said the family's approach to the police was delayed because of the alleged pressure exerted by the relatives and road closures linked to Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) protests, which disrupted travel between Lahore and Rawalpindi.

title: Flood survivors left facing lasting damage
description: Flood survivors left facing lasting damage
content:
Families return to damaged homes; property values plunge in various localities
With the deadly monsoon season finally over, social and commercial activities have returned to normal in the flood-hit areas of the twin cities, with families displaced by flooding also returning to their homes, bearing flood scars.
However, the devastation caused by the floods remains clearly visible in the affected low-lying localities, where property prices have reportedly fallen sharply. A large number of residents have put up 'For Sale' boards outside their houses, apparently seeking to leave the vulnerable areas.
Flood-damaged streets remain broken, while many homes are undergoing fresh paintwork after their walls were damaged by floodwater. In several houses, water marks are still clearly visible on walls. Residents are also continuing to dump damaged furniture, clothing, bedding and other household items in the streets.
Residents of some of the worst-hit areas, including Javed Colony, Nadeem Colony, Mohalla Fazalabad and Arya Mohalla, said flooding occurs almost every year. Gul Tasab Khan, Amjad Shah and Maroob Hussain said single-storey houses were completely submerged this year, destroying household belongings.
They complained that no minister, adviser, elected representative, councillor or district administration official visited the affected areas to offer assistance. They also alleged that WASA, the Municipal Corporation, Suthra Punjab Authority, Rescue teams and other relevant agencies failed to undertake proper post-flood cleaning.
The residents said the Health Department had also yet to carry out protective spraying, forcing affected families to dispose of damaged belongings themselves and clean the streets outside their homes.

content:
CCD team reviews forensic evidence, examines possible lapses in earlier investigation
A high-level investigation team, led by Additional Inspector General of Punjab's Crime Control Department (CCD) Sohail Zafar Chattha, has launched a fresh probe into the murder of Hina Javed, visiting the crime scene in Lal Kurti and reviewing key evidence, including the victim's DNA report.
The investigation follows special directives from Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif. The victim's DNA report has been received by the team, which is examining the evidence and previous investigative steps to identify any possible lapses or overlooked clues.
According to sources, Chattha arrived in Rawalpindi with the special team and inspected the apartment where Hina was allegedly tortured and murdered on August 20. Rawalpindi City Police Officer Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera, Investigation SSP Saifullah, other senior police officials and the case's investigation officer were also present.
The team was briefed on the progress of the investigation, evidence collected from the scene, and the alleged roles of the suspects named in the case: Hina's husband, Faisal Asghar; domestic employee Zeeshan; and her father-in-law, Ali Asghar. Sources said the victim's husband and the employee had been arrested.
During the visit, Chattha reportedly raised questions about the post-mortem report, the alleged murder weapon, forensic evidence, telephone records and the investigation into the suspects. The team also reviewed the earlier investigation and began interviewing police officers who had worked on the case to determine whether any evidence had been overlooked or investigative shortcomings had occurred.
Inspector Iftikhar Ahmed of the Homicide Investigation Unit has also been included in the special team to strengthen the investigation.
Later, Chattha and Saifullah met Hina's brother, Fahad Javed, and his lawyer, Shah Khawar, at the Police Lines Headquarters in Rawalpindi. According to sources, the committee shared details of the DNA report with the family, while the victim's brother and lawyer conveyed their concerns about the investigation conducted so far.
Chattha assured the family that the case would be investigated transparently, impartially and strictly on merit, and that no significant evidence would be ignored. He also assured them that the remaining forensic reports would be obtained soon.
According to sources, the challan will be submitted to the court after the outstanding forensic reports are received and the investigation is completed.
Hina was allegedly tortured and murdered at a residence in Lal Kurti on August 20.

UAE authorities have not publicly identified him, although a source familiar with the matter identified him as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national.

Thousands of police were deployed across the Indian capital on Friday, a day before planned protests to demand the election commission chief step down over alleged voter-roll irregularities, the Press Trust of India news agency reported.

Police have not authorised rallies at the site, and ordered restrictions on the metro subway system from Friday evening "in view of proposed protests and the likelihood of unruly mob movement", a police letter to the metro operator said. The CJP has said that its volunteers and supporters were being detained by police ahead of the planned demonstrationallegations police did not respond to. "Delhi police is working like the BJP's private militia," CJP activist Saurav Das said in a post on social media.

title: Hurricane Isaias intensifies rapidly before landfall
description: Hurricane Isaias intensifies rapidly before landfall
content:
Category 3 storm heads towards US Gulf Coast, prompting evacuations
Hurricane Isaias rapidly intensified into a major Category 3 storm on Friday, prompting mandatory evacuations as it headed towards the US Gulf Coast, where forecasters expected it to make landfall in the evening.
Isaias, packing maximum sustained winds of 195 kilometres per hour, was located about 195 miles south of Pensacola, Florida, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) said. Forecasters expected it to strike the western Florida Panhandle at or near major hurricane strength before weakening over land.
The storm is the first hurricane of an Atlantic season subdued by a historically strong El Niño and is expected to be the first to hit the US mainland since Hurricane Milton in 2024. Mandatory evacuation orders were in effect in several Florida counties.
States of emergency had been declared in parts of Alabama, Florida and Georgia. The NHC warned that storm surge combined with high tides could inundate normally dry areas, with water levels potentially reaching nine feet near the Alabama-Florida border.
At least two airports in northwestern Florida were preparing to suspend operations, while oil and gas facilities in the Gulf of Mexico evacuated workers and halted production. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said federal authorities were coordinating with state and local governments.
Isaias strengthened rapidly over record-warm Gulf waters, which scientists say have been heated by fossil fuel-driven climate change. "Sea surface temperatures in the Gulf of Mexico are in record territory because of fossil fuel-driven climate change," Marc Alessi, a climate scientist, told AFP.
He said the hurricane had drawn on the ocean's energy to intensify. El Niño, the warm phase of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation, typically increases wind shear over the Atlantic, making it harder for hurricanes to develop. However, Alessi said some areas remained favourable for storm formation.
The hurricane has also disrupted energy production. US President Donald Trump, scheduled to attend a college football game in Alabama on Saturday, said earlier this week he would "let the hurricane determine" his travel plans.

title: US imposes sweeping sanctions on ICC
description: US imposes sweeping sanctions on ICC
content:
Move threatens court's operations, the Netherlands, Canada, Japan express support for tribunal
The United States imposed sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Friday, threatening its access to financial services and technology, as the tribunal condemned the move as an assault on international law and urged its 125 member states to defend its independence.
The announcement by Washington came hours after former ICC judge Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize, with the award committee citing political attacks on international legal institutions. The sanctions risk deepening tensions between Washington and European allies that strongly support the court.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the measures were intended to prevent the ICC from prosecuting Americans, describing the tribunal as a "rogue court" and accusing it of threatening US interests. He said the US would ban transactions with the institution, cutting off resources and crippling its ability to operate.
The US Treasury announced an initial six-month grace period, alongside exemptions allowing certain transactions involving telecommunications, software, pension payments and detainees. Rubio said the measures had been structured to give the court and its member states time to address Washington's concerns, adding that the sanctions could be adjusted if those demands were not met.
The United States has repeatedly criticised the ICC over arrest warrants issued against Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and an earlier investigation into alleged crimes by US personnel in Afghanistan. The court says that investigation has been deprioritised.
ICC Deputy Prosecutor Nazhat Shameem Khan told Reuters that the sanctions were intended to undermine international rule of law and the work of an independent judicial institution. She said the court's investigations, prosecutions and other activities would continue.
The sanctions extend beyond earlier US measures targeting individual ICC prosecutors and judges, potentially exposing companies providing services to the court to penalties. Such restrictions could disrupt banking, insurance, credit card facilities and technology services, particularly given the institution's reliance on American systems.
ICC officials have already begun preparing for the possibility of wider restrictions, including shifting office computers from Microsoft software to open-source alternatives and making new banking and health insurance arrangements. The measures could also complicate staff payments, overseas investigations, witness protection and the operation of detention facilities.
Canada, Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Japan and Britain jointly expressed support for the tribunal, saying they regretted and strongly disagreed with Washington's announcement.
Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten called the sanctions deeply regrettable but urged dialogue, saying the six-month period before they take effect offered vital space for negotiations. The Netherlands, as host country, has a particular responsibility to protect the court's operations and staff.
Jetten said his government would continue diplomatic efforts to find a solution with Washington and other parties, stressing the ICC's importance to the international legal order.
