title: Outcry grows over plan to livestream US military execution
description: Outcry grows over plan to livestream US military execution
content:
Lawmakers condemn proposal, as UN warns broadcast will breach torture ban
Condemnation intensified on Friday over the Pentagon's plan to livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan, convicted of killing 13 people at a US military base, with the United Nations warning that broadcasting the death would amount to torture.
Hasan's execution is scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he carried out the 2009 shooting. It would be the first US military firing squad execution since 1945. Several lawmakers said they supported the execution but opposed broadcasting it.
"Livestreaming executions is what jihadists do. America is better than that," Republican Representative Austin Scott said. Senator Jack Reed, the top Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee, described the proposed broadcast as "a barbaric spectacle". He warned it could benefit terrorist recruiters.
US President Donald Trump said Hasan "deserves it", calling him a "maniac", but did not comment on the livestream plan. US Vice President JD Vance said he would not watch the execution if it were livestreamed, citing his Christian faith. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has backed making the execution public.
The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights said livestreaming an execution would constitute a public execution and breach the absolute prohibition of torture. Archbishop Paul Coakley, president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops, called the proposal a "barbaric promotion of a culture of death".
Hasan, an army psychiatrist, killed 13 people and wounded 30 others in the shooting; 12 of those killed were soldiers. He was shot and partially paralysed by a civilian police officer responding to the attack. A military jury sentenced Hasan to death in 2013
Hasan conducted his own defence at trial but called no witnesses and did not deny the charges. The court heard that he opposed US military operations in Iraq and Afghanistan and had communicated online with radical cleric Anwar al-Awlaki.
The Amnesty International said public executions had continued in some countries, reporting at least 17 in 2025 in Afghanistan and Iran. The group's Justin Mazzola said broadcasting Hasan's execution would "only compound the cruelty".

title: PM  Fazl discuss political situation
description: PM  Fazl discuss political situation
content:
PTI seeks resumption of talks through NA speaker
Amid the standoff over the PTI's long march and efforts to revive political dialogue, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif spoke to Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Friday.
The prime minister discussed the overall political situation and developments in K-P, particularly the PTI march.
The Maulana also reiterated that political disputes should be resolved through dialogue and mutual understanding rather than confrontation.
According to sources, the prime minister told the religio-political leader that the federal government had made every possible effort to resolve the issues through political means.
Separately, Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said handling the PTI long march was a separate matter for the federal government, while
containing rising terrorism in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa remained a distinct and more pressing challenge. He said the government's foremost priority was to control terrorism.
Speaking to senior journalists at Parliament House, the minister said the government had dealt with PTI marches in the past and had completed preparations to manage the current one. He maintained that all necessary arrangements related to the march were in place.
Chaudhry clarified that any decision to impose an emergency would not be linked to the long march itself. However, he said a lack of cooperation from the provincial government could become a factor in such a situation.
Pakistan could not afford any confrontation and needed stability, he said, stressing that effective action against terrorism in K-P required cooperation between the federal and provincial governments.
The minister said the PTI secretary-general had also spoken about preventing the loss of innocent lives, but personnel of the armed forces, police officers and ordinary citizens continued to be killed in terrorist attacks.
The government was taking steps to prevent such incidents and bring those responsible to justice, he added.
He urged the PTI leadership to cooperate with the federal government in counterterrorism efforts, saying 12 districts of K-P were severely affected by terrorism. These included eight districts in the former tribal areas and four other districts.
The minister also called into question PTI's past policies and its position on negotiations with terrorists. He questioned why the party's leadership felt secure in certain areas where the political activities of other parties were limited, remarks that amounted to political criticism of the PTI.
Regarding the possibility of Fazl playing a role in resolving the political impasse, Chaudhry said the JUI-F chief was a shrewd politician whose political importance was recognised by the government. However, he said Fazl could play an effective role only if the PTI gave him a full mandate to conduct negotiations on its behalf.
Meanwhile, PTI leader Ali Muhammad Khan contacted National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq to discuss the continuation of negotiations, saying a third round of talks was essential and that progress in the dialogue could help improve the situation.
Speaking to the media, Ali Muhammad Khan said the PTI wanted political tensions to ease through negotiations and all political leaders to be present in Islamabad so that the dialogue process could continue.
He said the party wanted to resolve the political tensions without bloodshed and had repeatedly offered the government a path towards negotiations.
According to Ali Muhammad Khan, Sardar Ayaz Sadiq was currently in Lahore. The two would meet once the speaker returned to Islamabad, he said.
Separately, the central core committee of the JUI-F met under the chairmanship of Fazl to review the prevailing political situation in detail, particularly the various aspects of negotiations between the government and the opposition.
Fazl briefed participants on his recent meetings with opposition and government leaders and consulted them on the developments. The participants also held detailed discussions on the course of the negotiations and the broader political situation.

title: FO quashes speculation over Yemen combat role
description: FO quashes speculation over Yemen combat role
content:
Spokesperson says Pakistan's military will defend Saudi Arabia
Pakistani forces, under the Makkah Defense alliance, will not cross into Yemen to launch attacks against the Houthi militia, the Foreign Office said on Friday, seeking to clarify Islamabad's military commitments to Saudi Arabia amid escalating attacks on the kingdom and the operationalisation of a joint defence pact involving Türkiye.
Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider said the Makkah Alliance for Defence was a defensive arrangement intended to protect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of its members, ruling out Pakistani troops crossing the border into Yemen to conduct offensive operations against the Houthis.
"These forces would not cross the border into Yemen to launch attacks against the Houthis," Sajjad told reporters during his weekly briefing. "However, they would, of course, be utilised to defend the country's territory and safeguard its sovereignty."
The clarification came as questions mounted over the scope of Pakistan's military commitments following an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee of the Makkah Alliance in Riyadh on October 5.
The meeting brought together the foreign and defence ministers and military chiefs of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye to discuss the kingdom's security situation and the implementation of collective defence commitments.
The three countries agreed to take practical steps to strengthen military readiness, integration and their collective capacity to respond to threats. Pakistan was represented by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir.
Sajjad said Pakistan already had a substantial number of troops and resources in Saudi Arabia, adding that the alliance's headquarters would assess the threat and determine the scale, timing and location of any additional deployment.
"Pakistan already has a substantial number of forces, as well as resources, in Riyadh," he said, adding that member states would contribute according to operational requirements.
He said Pakistani forces had been stationed in Saudi Arabia in various capacities since 1982, including under logistical arrangements and training missions. Further deployments had taken place following the signing of the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia last year.
The spokesperson, however, declined to discuss operational details, including the possibility of fresh troop deployments. He also rejected reports that Pakistani fighter jets had participated in airstrikes against the Houthis, describing them as speculative reports that had already been refuted by the information minister.
Asked whether a third country could be involved in the attacks against Saudi Arabia, Sajjad said it would be premature to speculate about the identities of those responsible.
The escalation has raised concerns in Islamabad over the safety of approximately 2.5 million Pakistanis living in Saudi Arabia, as well as the potential impact on travel and economic ties. Sajjad said the attacks were a matter of considerable concern for Pakistan, noting that a Pakistani truck driver had also been killed in a drone attack in Yemen.
He reiterated Pakistan's preference for de-escalation and diplomacy while reaffirming its commitment to Saudi Arabia's security.
The spokesperson also defended the alliance against suggestions that Pakistan was entering a new conflict without adequate civilian consultation. He said the arrangement reflected a whole-of-government approach, pointing to the participation of senior cabinet ministers in the Riyadh meeting.
The Makkah agreement, he added, was intended to consolidate the three countries' defensive capabilities and provide a framework for collective action when required.
Turning to Afghanistan, Sajjad said Pakistan's participation in the eighth Moscow Format consultations on October 5 had been constructive, despite the meeting ending without a joint statement for the first time since the process began in 2017.
He said the disagreement centred on language concerning terrorism emanating from Afghan territory, an issue Pakistan considers central to its security concerns.
According to the spokesperson, the Afghan Taliban delegation objected to retaining language on terrorism that had been agreed upon at last year's meeting. Pakistan had maintained that the statement should reflect the threat posed by armed groups operating from Afghanistan, particularly those targeting neighbouring countries.
"For Pakistan, this is a substantive security issue, not merely a matter of wording," Sajjad said.
He added that the absence of a joint statement should not overshadow the importance of regional dialogue. Pakistan would decide whether to attend the next meeting after further consultations, he said, describing any commitment at this stage as premature.
Sajjad rejected allegations by Afghan Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi that Pakistan supported the Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP) or was conducting activities in Afghanistan's Nuristan and Badakhshan provinces.
He instead accused the Taliban authorities of allowing the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and other terrorist organisations to operate from Afghan territory.
Pakistan, he said, had conveyed the locations of these groups through political and security channels, and its military strikes had targeted sites where terrorists were planning attacks against Pakistan.
The spokesperson urged the Afghan authorities to take responsibility for the security problem, saying Islamabad remained willing to develop friendly relations with Kabul if the threat from Afghan territory was addressed.
He also rejected claims that Pakistan's military actions had targeted civilians, maintaining that the strikes were precise and directed at terrorist targets.
Despite the differences, Sajjad said Pakistan remained committed to political dialogue and diplomacy, but stressed that progress would depend on the other side's willingness to address Islamabad's security concerns.
Sajjad also said Pakistan's mediation efforts between the United States and Iran remained relevant, despite the country's parallel defence commitments in the Gulf.
He said the two sides were now communicating directly and discussing proposals that included seven points, with some elements aligned with the Islamabad memorandum of understanding.
The direct engagement, he added, was itself an outcome of Pakistan's mediation efforts.
Islamabad would remain willing to facilitate further talks if requested, Sajjad said, expressing hope that the two countries would reduce tensions and reach a negotiated settlement.
"If Pakistan is needed to play its role again, it would be very appy to do so," he said.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday strongly condemned the repeated terrorist attacks by the Houthi militia against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including the targeting of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha International Airport, resulting in loss of lives and injuries to civilians.
The prime minister, in a post on X, commended the vigilance and professionalism of the Saudi armed forces and the Islamic Military Counter Terrorism Coalition in intercepting multiple ballistic missiles and their tireless efforts to protect innocent lives and safeguard the Kingdom.
"Pakistan stands in unwavering solidarity with the leadership and people of our brotherly Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," he reiterated and said that in line with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, and recent decisions taken by its Strategic Political and Defense Committee, Pakistan's commitment to the Kingdom's sovereignty, territorial integrity and security was resolute.
Prime Minister Shehbaz said that Pakistan also fully supported Saudi Arabia's legitimate right to defend its people and protect its cities and vital infrastructure.
"The Houthi militia must immediately cease these attacks. We will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with Saudi Arabia in the face of these threats," he resolved.

title: Pakistan s oversized provinces face a governance test
description: Pakistan s oversized provinces face a governance test
content:
WEF examines proposals for 16 to more than 30 administrative units, highlighting fiscal and institutional hurdles
The fast-growing populations can outgrow the administrative systems built to govern them, making institutional scale necessary for development, according to a recent World Economic Forum (WEF) analysis examining Pakistan and broader emerging economies.
The analysis highlights that when administrative systems built for smaller societies are asked to serve vastly larger, more urban, and more unequal populations, decision-making becomes too distant from the citizens it is meant to serve. Pakistan illustrates why reform is necessary and what it should look like, with its population projected to potentially reach 265 million by 2030.
The country's administrative maps dictate how governments raise revenue, allocate public funds, plan infrastructure, respond to shocks, and measure performance. When these maps fail to reflect demographic and economic realities, governance challenges intensify.
While consecutive governments have taken major stepssuch as the 18th Constitutional Amendment and the 7th National Finance Commission Award devolving major responsibilities for health and education while increasing the provincial share of federal taxes from 47.5% to 57.5%many decisions remain far from affected communities.
For example, Lahore district has around 13 million people, while Harnai district in Balochistan has just 128,000, forcing policies designed in provincial capitals to serve vastly different realities.
The Planning Commission's District Education Performance Index found that none of the 134 assessed districts reached the "very high" performance category, underlining the distance between policymakers and districts, budgets and outcomes, and authority and accountability.
Other large, diverse countries have repeatedly adjusted their administrative geography as their populations and economies evolved.
Nigeria expanded from a three-region structure to 36 states by 1996; Indonesia grew from 27 provinces to 38 today; and Kenya replaced its eight provinces with 47 elected county governments in 2013 equipped with a formula-based share of national revenue weighted for population and poverty. In Indonesia, Nigeria, and Brazil, average first-tier populations sit around 6 to 8 millionfar below Pakistan's current average of 60 million.
For Pakistan, experts suggest the debate involves distinct governance scenarios, calling for dividing each existing province into four to create 16 first-tier governments, lowering average population per unit from 60 million to roughly 15 million.
It also calls for creating 23 to 25 units based on population balance or geographic coherence, or building on existing civil divisions to form more than 30 units with average populations closer to other large federations.
Fewer, larger units may be easier to legislate and finance, whereas more numerous units bring capitals and political authority closer to citizens but raise transition costs and require stronger administrative capacity.
Furthermore, cautionary examples like Lebanon demonstrate that fragmentation without fiscal and institutional capacitysuch as municipalities too small and financially weak to deliver servicescan be as debilitating as over-centralisation.
The analysis stresses that boundaries, funding, and mandates must move together. Smaller units without predictable transfers, credible taxing powers, and clear service responsibilities simply reproduce centralisation at a lower level.
In 20242025, provincial taxes brought in Rs983 billion, equating to less than 0.9% of GDP. Meanwhile, although agriculture accounts for 24% of value added, agricultural income taxation has historically yielded very little relative to the sector's size, with the International Monetary Fund estimating agriculture's effective tax rate at just 0.3%.
Provincial tax authorities have long struggled with limited administrative capacity, weak enforcement, and inadequate information. Ultimately, the goal is not to multiply administrative units for its own sake, but to align scale, authority, resources, and accountability so that when populations grow faster than institutions, governments can redesign those institutions to bring decisions and resources close enough to the people who live with the consequences.

title: Bilawal calls K P emergency political  atomic bomb
description: Bilawal calls K P emergency political  atomic bomb
content:
PPP chief urges PTI to quit 'politics of extremism', Asks party to resume parliamentary dialogue
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari on Friday urged the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) to abandon its extremist politics and return to parliamentary engagement, warning that imposing governor's rule or an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) would be a "political atomic bomb" with consequences extending beyond the province.
Addressing the inauguration of a 25-acre Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) sports complex in Baldia Town, Bilawal said the PPP had consistently advocated political dialogue instead of extraordinary constitutional measures, which he maintained should be considered only as a last resort.
"Imposing an emergency in K-P is an atomic bomb and will only be considered as the last resort," he said, adding that an emergency could shrink political space for parties across the country.
The PPP chairman accused the PTI of damaging its own political standing through confrontation with other political parties, the federal government, Parliament, the judiciary and the establishment, while neglecting its responsibilities towards the province and its people.
"The PTI is a party that has public supporters, but it keeps disappointing the people because of its decisions and extremist politics," Bilawal said, warning that the party risked losing its provincial government if it continued with its present approach.
He urged the PTI to resume parliamentary proceedings, participate in committees and engage with other political forces, saying political positions could be improved through democratic engagement rather than confrontation.
"You will not disappoint the voter in K-P if you amend your politics, return to parliamentary committees and interact with other political parties. Politics is a day-to-day affair, and you can improve your political position," he said.
The remarks came as the PTI proceeded with its long march demanding the release of its jailed founder and former prime minister Imran Khan, despite warnings from the federal government against gatherings in Islamabad.
Bilawal questioned why K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi appeared unwilling to pursue dialogue, arguing that the provincial leadership was narrowing the space for negotiations and making the possibility of emergency measures increasingly difficult to dismiss.
He said the federal government and the broader political system had been prepared to consider an emergency in the province about a week earlier. Although governor's rule and an emergency were constitutional and legal options, he stressed that the PPP did not want them exercised.
"We do not want that the last option for the PPP of governor's rule or emergency should be exercised, but it seems that the K-P CM is leaving no space for political engagement," he said.
Bilawal also cited the province's security situation, alleging that the provincial government was not cooperating adequately on counterterrorism. "Given the security situation in K-P and the refusal of the provincial government to cooperate in terrorism, how can I legally say that an emergency should not be imposed in the province?" he asked.
He maintained that abandoning confrontation could help the PTI pursue its political objectives and improve the prospects of its leadership, including Imran Khan, who remains imprisoned. "If the PTI renounces the politics of extremism, then they will save their politics, their government and also, sooner or later, their political leadership," Bilawal said.
He said that imprisonment did not necessarily determine a politician's future, citing his father, President Asif Ali Zardari, whom he described as having the record for the longest incarceration. However, he warned that continued confrontation could leave Imran Khan behind bars long enough to surpass that record.
The PPP chairman also called on the PTI to participate in parliamentary efforts to address electoral grievances, pointing out that the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz had agreed after several months to establish a parliamentary committee on electoral reforms.
"If you do not participate then how will we stop rigging in the future?" he asked, suggesting that Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman could play a role in facilitating negotiations.
Bilawal said political stability was necessary to address economic hardship and provide relief to the public, urging political parties to cooperate on fundamental national issues regardless of who held the office of prime minister.
Turning to Karachi's youth, he said some political forces wanted to push young people towards crime, whereas the PPP wanted them to pursue constructive activities, including sports. He expressed hope that the newly inaugurated complex would provide young people with a lasting facility for healthy recreation.

title: S Africa s Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize
description: S Africa s Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize
content:
S Africa's Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize
The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded Friday to South Africa's Navi Pillay, the judge who headed the Rwanda genocide tribunal and who last year presided over a UN commission which accused Israel of genocide in Gaza.
Pillay, currently a judge on the International Court of Justice in a case where Myanmar also stands accused of genocide, has been "instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide are prosecuted," said Jorgen Watne Frydnes, the chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee in Oslo.
"In historic international court cases, she has shown that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence," the committee said.
Pillay's "independence, her expertise and steadfastness have made her one of the most respected international jurists of our time."
She reacted to the news by making a quip about US President Donald Trump's well-documented desire to win the prize himself.
"If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump," the 85-year-old said during a standing ovation captured by Amnesty International Secretary General Agnes Callamard in Nuremberg and posted on the social network X.
Pillay headed the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry (COI), which does not speak on behalf of the world body, and which last year found that genocide was occurring in Gaza.
Pillay told AFP at the time that her team had shared "thousands of pieces of information" with prosecutors at the International Criminal Court.
Israel categorically rejected the report's findings, slamming it as "distorted and false".
The Nobel committee said that while its prize honoured Pillay's career of fighting genocide, it was not taking a stand on whether Israel's actions in Gaza constitute a genocide.
"We are not the court," Frydnes told AFP.
"It's her report, the Commission's report... It will be decided by the International Court of Justice," he said.
Speaking on Friday after her standing ovation, Pillay noted that many had paid tribute to her courage in that report.
"You can imagine how surprised I was. Why would you need courage to speak the truth?"
The UN said her prize was a "testament to the need and to the value of human rights in this world more than ever".
The International Criminal Court meanwhile said her award was of "particular significance" given current attacks on international law.
The Nobel committee echoed that sentiment in its statement, noting that "at a time of existential challengesincluding more wars and conflicts than the world has seen in a long timeinternational law is no longer just a supplement to peace and security."
The prize for Pillay is sure to anger Trump, whose administration has repeatedly attacked international justice institutions.
"This is a clear message to those who are putting pressure on these institutions, to those who are sanctioning the judges and are attacking the institutions. That needs to stop," Frydnes told AFP after the announcement.
Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has made no secret of his desire to win the prize, insisting that he was the most deserving candidate and claiming to have ended up to eight wars.
"They have a reputation for maybe not giving it to people like me .. and I think it would be a great discredit to them," Trump had said on Wednesday.
But his war against Iran, his territorial expansion ambitions as in Greenland, his hard line on migrants, and his attacks on multilateralism and the media have, according to experts in Oslo, disqualified him for the prize.
Last year, the prize went to Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, a choice generally considered palatable to Trump.
Machado even gave him her Nobel gold medal, judging he deserved it after the capture of President Nicolas Madurothough she failed to obtain his political backing in exchange.
The Nobel committee has said it is not swayed by external pressures.
"Of course we have to discuss it, but it's not like that influences the discussions in the room and decisions that come out," the secretary of the committee, Kristian Berg Harpviken, told AFP ahead of the prize announcement.
The prize comes with a gold medal, a diploma and a prize sum of $1.2 million.
The award will be presented at a formal ceremony in Oslo on December 10, the anniversary of the 1896 death of the prizes' creator, Swedish inventor and philanthropist Alfred Nobel.

JUI-F leader Maulana Muhammad Amjad Khan told The Express Tribune that claims Fazlur Rehman had set conditions were absurd, questioning how someone approached to mediate could impose conditions on either side. A mediator's role, he said, was to hear grievances, suggest solutions and communicate limitations.
Amjad said the government wanted the JUI-F to play a mediating role and had approached the party to bring Fazlur Rehman into the process. He declined to confirm or deny reports of mediation but said the government recognised Fazlur Rehman's relevance to resolving the political impasse.
Asked whether Fazlur Rehman or the JUI-F had contacted PTI leadership to inform it of the proposed mediation, Amjad said no such contact had been made. He added that communication between the two sides took place several times a day.
Amjad said Fazlur Rehman wanted the standoff between PTI and the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N)-led government resolved as soon as possible, warning that further political turmoil could damage an already struggling economy.
The government believes Maulana Fazl could help resolve the crisis because of his existing contacts with PTI and the Tehreek Tahaffuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP), Amjad said. He identified challenges on both sides, including the need for approval from the government's "high-ups" and divisions within PTI.
On a proposed all-parties conference (APC), Amjad said the meeting could be held only after the parties reached a broader consensus. If the PML-N wanted to attend, he said, PTI should invite it.
TTAP spokesperson Akhundzada Hussain on Wednesday dismissed reports that Fazlur Rehman was emerging as a mediator, alleging that the government and pro-government media had promoted the narrative.
Speaking to The Express Tribune on Thursday, Hussain said the PTI and TTAP had met Fazlur Rehman to discuss the proposed APC and its agenda, including the outcome of previous engagements. PTI had not asked him to approach the government on its behalf, he said.
Neither Fazlur Rehman nor anyone representing him had communicated any mediation initiative to PTI or TTAP by late Thursday, Hussain added.
PTI leaders Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, Junaid Akbar and Asad Qaiser had also denied being approached by Fazlur Rehman or holding an internal meeting on the matter.

title: Existing subsidy system soon to be replaced
description: Existing subsidy system soon to be replaced
content:
Targeted electricity and gas subsidies to begin in 2027
The federal government has accelerated energy-sector reforms to meet the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) conditions, preparing to phase out the existing electricity and gas slab and cross-subsidy systems and restrict financial assistance to deserving and low-income consumers.
Under the proposed plan, a new electricity subsidy mechanism is scheduled to take effect in January 2027, while the revised system for gas consumers is expected to be introduced on July 1, 2027, according to official sources.
The Power Division has begun work, with the support of the World Bank, on a socioeconomic registry to identify consumers eligible for subsidies.
The registration process is targeted for completion by November, after which the verified data will be linked with the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) records.
The proposed registry will be used to identify eligible households and determine which consumers qualify for electricity and gas subsidies under the new mechanism.
The changes are intended to direct subsidies towards low-income households instead of continuing the existing arrangements, under which tariff structures and cross-subsidies provide financial relief to different categories of consumers.
Sources said the government had planned the changes partly to ease mounting pressure from circular debt in the energy sector. Reforms are also being pursued alongside preparations for the privatisation of power distribution companies.
The distribution companies have filed applications seeking base tariff adjustments, while the government has briefed the IMF on preparations related to their privatisation and broader energy-sector reforms, the sources added.
The proposed shift towards targeted subsidies would make the socioeconomic registry a central tool for determining eligibility for government assistance in electricity and gas bills.

content:

The federal government has sought provincial input on a proposed national framework to reduce poverty, with Federal Minister for Poverty Alleviation Pir Syed Imran Ahmed Shah saying three provinces have responded positively while the fourth is yet to reply.
Speaking at a press conference in Islamabad, the minister said the framework aimed to coordinate federal and provincial efforts and could reduce the cost of poverty alleviation initiatives by 75%.
He said that provinces were not subordinate to the federal government and could not be directly monitored by it.
The minister criticised the World Bank for placing Pakistan in the Middle East and North Africa region rather than South Asia, alleging that the move was intended to malign the country. He also disputed the bank's assessment of poverty in Pakistan.
An international conference titled "From Poverty to Prosperity" will be held in Islamabad on October 13 and 14, bringing together delegates from 12 countries, experts and institutional representatives to develop a roadmap for tackling poverty.
The minister said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif wanted to improve the lives of vulnerable communities under the Uraan Pakistan Initiative. He added that the conference would strengthen collective efforts to reduce poverty through coordinated policies and sustainable interventions.
Pakistan Poverty Alleviation Fund (PPAF) Chief Executive Officer Nader Gul Barech said the organisation was working with partners across 157 districts.
It had established 171,200 community institutions benefiting 2.67 million people, including 63% women, and provided loans worth Rs139.61 billion.
The organisation had extended 3.69 million interest-free loans with a 98% loan repayment rate. Barech said government efforts had previously reduced poverty, but figures in the latest economic survey showed a slight increase. Several factors contributed to the rise, he said.
The minister announced that a poverty graduation programme would be launched in 25 districts over the next two months. He said a comprehensive national framework was needed to improve data-sharing among federal and provincial governments and institutions working on poverty alleviation.
He also said complaints that people were being asked to pay money to obtain microfinance loans would be investigated if reported.
Although progress had been made in improving living standards, the government had yet to achieve its desired poverty reduction targets.
Organised by the PPAF with the Ministry of Poverty Alleviation and Social Safety, the Centre of Excellence for National Cohesion and Outreach, and Paigham-e-Pakistan, the conference will examine social protection, public investment, access to finance and private-sector opportunities. It will also consider how local communities can participate in development to ensure poverty reduction efforts deliver lasting results.

title: No reform should hollow out UN peacekeeping  Pakistan
description: No reform should hollow out UN peacekeeping  Pakistan
content:
Against a backdrop of multiplying global conflicts and severe financial strain, Pakistan warned at the United Nations that any reform must not "hollow out" the bedrock of UN peacekeeping, the world body's flagship activity.
Speaking at the Challenges Annual Forum 2026, themed "Turning the Tide: Building Momentum for Peace Operations in a Demanding World," Ambassador Usman Jadoon, deputy permanent Representative of Pakistan said, while highlighting the severity of the current financial pressures, and urging the international community not let a temporary liquidity crisis dictate the future of peacekeeping.
The essential challenge is not the perceived decline of peacekeeping, but the preservation of the long-established institutional capacity and political trust required for future deployments, he said in the course of the discussion.
As one of the world's largest troop-contributing nations, Pakistan's stance, in this regard, carries heavy institutional weight.
Over the past six decades, the Pakistani envoy said, more than 270,000 Pakistani peacekeepers have served under the UN flag; 183 have made the ultimate sacrifice. Pakistan is also a host country to one of the UN's oldest peacekeeping missions – United Nations Military Observer Group in India and Pakistan (UNMOGIP), which monitors the LoC in disputed Jammu and Kashmir.
"So, our perspective is shaped both by contributing to peacekeeping and by hosting a mission," Ambassador Jadoon pointed out.
Peacekeeping is the Security Council's primary tool for turning resolutions in New York into reality on the ground, he said. Stripping the Council of a credible peacekeeping capacity paralyzes its ability to halt escalation, shield civilians, and safeguard fragile political processes.
"There is a critical need to distinguish financial pressure from political legitimacy," the Pakistani envoy said.

title: Auto import duties face criticism
description: Auto import duties face criticism
content:
Taxes on vehicle tyres, motorcycle parts clash with trade liberalisation drive
A member of the National Tariff Policy Board has opposed a decision to impose up to 31% additional duty on some imports, which the government has decided to slap despite its new pro-trade liberalisation National Tariff Policy discouraging import substitution.
It is a wrong decision to impose additional customs duty on the import of tyres of vehicles and some parts of motorcycles, said Dr Rubina Athar, a member of the Tariff Policy Board, who was part of the National Tariff Policy formulation and one of the strongest proponents of trade liberalisation.
She was responding to a question during a panel discussion on Pakistan's tariff reforms, arranged by the United Kingdom-funded Revenue Mobilisation, Investment and Trade (REMIT) Initiative.
"Every tariff-related proposal should come to the National Tariff Policy Board before going to the cabinet, and as a member of the board I can say this matter has not come to the policy board for a decision before it was sent to the ECC," said Athar.
The finance ministry said on Thursday that the ECC approved the imposition of 11% additional customs duty on import of tyres to protect the local industry. It slapped 11% additional customs duty on the import of parts of motorcycles and 31% if the manufacturers import these parts instead of locally producing them.
The 31% duty is imposed on motorcycle components including licence plate, bracket, side reflector, right and left-side plate, front decorative connection part, foot plate, wheel assembly, windshield, seat, toolbox, centre covers and plates & parts.
But imports of these parts from China will still be taxed at zero duty under the Free Trade Agreement. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's government had approved the National Tariff Policy with an aim to fully liberalise the economy by demolishing trade barriers. It is the first such decision where the government has added more bricks to the wall instead of tearing them down.
The Federal Board of Revenue had moved the summary for the approval of the ECC. When inquired about the motive, beneficiaries of the additional customs duty and the rationale to breach the tariff policy, it did not give a reply.
"It is the Ministry of Industries' proposal developed by the Engineering Development Board," said the FBR spokesman. In its response, the Ministry of Commerce said that the ECC considered the amendment in SRO 693(1)/2006, which pertains to the imposition of additional customs duty on parts being locally manufactured if imported by OEMs in kit form. The commerce ministry said that the list of items to be included in the SRO is to be reviewed bi-annually by the Ministry of Industries & Production.
The "auto sector SROs do not operate under the National Tariff Policy as was held by the Tariff Policy Board in its meeting held on 6th June, 2026, whereby it was decided that the SRO 693 does not fall within the purview of TPB being part of another policy", according to the commerce ministry. The mechanism available under the Auto Policy 2021-26 still exists in the shape of SROs, including SRO 693(1)/2006, and MOC, in principle, supported the amendment, it added.
However, the auto policy lapsed in June this year and there is no new approved auto policy. But the commerce ministry said that these SROs were still in the field. The ministry said that Service Long March locally manufactures these tyres.
The national tariff policy is aimed at opening the economy by ending the import substitution policy, said Rubina Athar. She said that the import substitution policies had made industries inefficient and the consumers did not benefit from it.
Dr Vaqar Ahmed, a senior economist, said that favouritism in the application of tariff policy would kill its purpose, but the auto sector has been explicitly excluded from the purview.
Zafar Mehmood, Chief Executive Officer of Nimir Chemicals, said that lowering the customs duties would not bring efficiency and reduce cost for the consumers, as other duties and taxes were causing more problems. He said that the National Tariff Policy has compromised the cascading principle of protection, which would severely impact many industries.
Member Customs FBR Shakil Shah agreed that import taxes, particularly advance income tax, were creating serious problems for the industries. The FBR withholds advance income tax at the import stage irrespective of whether the industry would make any profit or not, which is unnecessarily blocking the money of industries, said Shah.
"If the earned profits are less than the withheld advance income tax, the importer will never get refunds, and we need to eliminate these withholding taxes at the import stage," said Shah.
Zain ul Abideen, CEO Rubatech, said that the national tariff policy combined with the new energy vehicle policy was a death sentence to the auto industry. Zain said that preferential treatment being given to the NEVs would eliminate internal combustion engine cars.
But Rubina Athar argued that some shock had to be given to the industries to wake them up from inertia. Wajid Bukhari, Secretary General Pakistan Association of Large Steel Producers, said that the tariff policy did not impact the steel industry so far due to reduction in the interest rates and energy cost.

title: Exporters require wider access to credit insurance
description: Exporters require wider access to credit insurance
content:
Jam Kamal asks EXIM Bank to explore cooperation with international export credit agencies
Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan has called for wider access to export credit insurance and financing to help Pakistani exporters enter new markets, manage payment risks and expand their business, with particular attention to small enterprises and first-time exporters.
The minister was speaking during a meeting with Exim Bank CEO Shahbaz H Syed. Khan emphasised that export support should reach emerging businesses and smaller producers seeking to enter international markets. He noted that access to capital, practical guidance and appropriate risk protection could help these enterprises become established exporters.
The minister proposed closer coordination between Exim Bank and Pakistan's trade and investment officers abroad to identify opportunities, facilitate business contacts and support exporters in destination markets. He also encouraged the bank to explore cooperation with international export credit agencies and financial institutions to broaden financing opportunities.
Speaking at the meeting, Shahbaz H Syed explained that Exim Bank's export credit insurance was protecting exporters from specified commercial and political risks associated with overseas transactions. These included buyer default and events that prevented payments or the transfer of funds from destination markets.
The CEO said coverage could extend up to 90% of the insured risk, subject to applicable terms and assessment, with exporters retaining a share of the exposure. He explained that the assessment focused on the overseas buyer's creditworthiness and the destination market's risk profile, allowing new exporters to seek coverage as well.
Syed highlighted the role of commercial banks as potential partners and distribution channels for export credit insurance. He explained that insured export receivables could support access to financing, subject to banks' requirements and the applicable regulatory framework.
Secretary Commerce Jawad Paul, who was present in the meeting, underscored the importance of connecting insurance protection with practical financing arrangements. The discussion considered how cooperation among Exim Bank, commercial banks and other financial institutions could help exporters use insured transactions to obtain working capital and pursue business growth.
The meeting also examined the financing needs of small enterprises, including businesses supplying larger exporters, and the importance of longer-term investment in production capacity alongside short-term working capital support.
Jam Kamal Khan encouraged Exim Bank to participate more actively in trade exhibitions, including FoodAg, where Pakistani exporters and international buyers could receive guidance on insurance and financing options.

FinMin says Dutch expertise, technology can complement Islamabad's development priorities
Federal Minister for Finance Muhammad Aurangzeb met a Dutch business delegation, led by the Founders Carbon Network (FCN) and accompanied by the Netherlands Ambassador Robert-Jan Siegert.
The minister emphasised the importance of strengthening business-to-business linkages, fostering mutual understanding and deepening bilateral economic cooperation. He noted that sustained engagement between the business communities of Pakistan and the Netherlands would help identify commercially viable investment opportunities, develop partnerships and build investor confidence.
Aurangzeb highlighted Pakistan's improving macroeconomic outlook and stressed the need for translating the gains of stabilisation into productive investment, capital formation, export expansion and private-sector-led growth. He emphasised that the next phase of Pakistan's economic development must be increasingly export-oriented, productivity-driven and employment-generating, supported by structural reforms and greater mobilisation of private capital.
Outlining the government's economic priorities, the finance minister underscored the need to consolidate macroeconomic stability and strengthen fiscal and external resilience; transition towards sustainable, inclusive and responsible growth; maintain momentum on implementation-focused structural reforms; shift from aid dependence towards trade and investment; broaden access to finance for SMEs, agriculture, housing and underserved communities; and position Pakistan to benefit from the "New Economy" through digitalisation and emerging technologies.
Referring to the strengthening external position, the minister noted that foreign exchange reserves had reached a historic high of $21.4 billion, providing over three months of import cover. He emphasised that sustaining these gains and building resilience against external shocks remained essential to reinforcing investor confidence and creating a durable foundation for economic growth.
Aurangzeb identified rapid population growth and climate change as two existential challenges facing Pakistan, underscoring their implications for economic sustainability, human development and long-term resilience. He called for addressing these challenges through sustained policy attention and coordinated reforms.
Highlighting opportunities for closer Pakistan-Netherlands economic cooperation, the minister pointed to the potential for Dutch expertise, technology and investment to complement Pakistan's development priorities across key sectors. He identified public-private partnerships as an important avenue for mobilising private capital, leveraging specialised expertise and translating investment interest into commercially viable projects.
Adviser to the prime minister on privatisation, who was present in the meeting, reaffirmed the government's commitment to expanding private-sector participation through privatisation and public-private partnerships. He noted that these initiatives were aimed at improving efficiency, attracting investment and creating greater opportunities for private enterprises across commercial activities.
Members of the Dutch delegation shared their perspectives on Pakistan's business environment and prospects for expanded bilateral cooperation. The discussions highlighted opportunities to strengthen B2B engagement, identify areas of mutual interest and develop commercially viable partnerships between Pakistani and Dutch enterprises.

title: BIT with Sweden to stay in place
description: BIT with Sweden to stay in place
content:
Cabinet gives directive to probe reasons for issuing treaty termination notice
Pakistan has decided to continue the Bilateral Investment Treaty (BIT) with Sweden following intervention of the federal cabinet. Earlier, Pakistan had served a termination notice for BIT, which irritated Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in a recent cabinet meeting.
The cabinet gave directives to probe who had issued the notice and what were the reasons that led to sending the notice to Sweden to revoke the investment treaty.
The cabinet had called for constituting a committee, named "Committee on Bilateral Investment Treaties", to ascertain the reasons and approval processes followed before issuing the notice of termination of BIT signed between Pakistan and Sweden in 1981.
The committee has also been tasked to formulate guidelines to be followed before releasing such notices in the future, if any. It is examining possible outcomes of the termination of BITs with 25 countries under the Bilateral Investment Treaty (BIT) Strategy of Pakistan 2021.
The committee is also required to determine the relevance of BIT Strategy 2021 and Pakistan Model Bilateral Investment Treaty Template 2021 in the contemporary international economic context. It will prepare a draft BIT policy in relation to the evolving global economic context, covering investment protection provisions, most favoured nation (MFN) criteria, fair and equitable treatment standards, and dispute resolution mechanisms.
Meanwhile, Federal Minister for Board of Investment (BOI) Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh held a meeting with Swedish Ambassador Alexandra Berg von Linde to discuss strengthening bilateral economic relations, enhancing investment cooperation and exploring new opportunities for Swedish companies in Pakistan.
The federal minister underscored the longstanding and friendly relations between Pakistan and Sweden and acknowledged Sweden's strengths in education, governance, technology and innovation. He observed that the two countries had considerable potential to expand their economic partnership, particularly by translating their longstanding ties into greater investment, technology transfer and business-to-business collaboration.
Ambassador Linde too highlighted the longstanding connections between the two countries. She noted the presence of an active Pakistani diaspora in Sweden and the growing interest among Pakistani students in pursuing higher education there, providing further avenues for people-to-people contacts and institutional collaboration.
The meeting noted the presence of more than 40 Swedish companies in Pakistan, reflecting an established commercial footprint and significant potential for further engagement. These companies include Ericsson, IKEA, H&M and Tetra Pak, representing areas such as information and communication technology, retail, consumer goods and packaging.
The minister emphasised that Pakistan's large domestic market, young population and strategic location offered considerable opportunities to international investors. Discussing Pakistan's economic outlook, the federal minister recalled his recent visit to New York, where discussions centred on the challenge of translating Pakistan's demographic and economic potential into higher and more sustainable growth. He observed that Pakistan, as the world's fifth-most populous country, needed to expand productive investment, strengthen industrial capacity and increase value-added exports.
Referring to his recent interaction with the ambassador of Vietnam, he underlined the importance of export-oriented growth and the lessons Pakistan could draw from successful exporting economies. The minister stated that Pakistan was actively working to attract international investors and strengthen its position as an investment destination.
He pointed to improvements in key economic indicators, the country's external-sector position and sovereign credit assessments, including those issued by Moody's, as positive developments supporting investor confidence. He added that the government was placing greater emphasis on value-added exports, industrial development and the removal of barriers to investment, with interest emerging from international investors, including Chinese and American companies. He expressed Pakistan's desire to develop similarly strong investment partnerships with Swedish businesses.
The federal minister identified agriculture, mining and minerals, information technology, digital services, engineering, manufacturing and other productive sectors as promising areas for Swedish investment.

title: Remittances cool to  3 6b in Sept
description: Remittances cool to  3 6b in Sept
content:
With $10.9b in Jul-Sept, inflows on course for about $43.5b in FY27
Workers' remittances stood at $3.59 billion in September, down 1.9% from $3.66 billion in August but up 12.7% from $3.18 billion a year earlier, the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) data showed. However, the pace cooled compared to August 2026.
Inflows in July-September reached $10.88 billion, 14% higher than $9.54 billion in the same quarter of FY26. The quarter was running ahead of last year's record pace.
July, August and September all cleared $3.5 billion, at $3.63 billion, $3.66 billion and $3.59 billion, respectively. The monthly average was $3,625 million, above the FY26 full-year average of $3,465 million.
The July-September quarter points to inflows of about $43.5 billion in financial year 2026-27, against $41.6 billion in FY26 and an SBP projection of around $44 billion. "We expect remittances for FY27 to clock in at $44.7 billion," Topline Securities predicted.
In September, the year-on-year growth slowed to 12.7% from 16.5% in August and 12.9% in July. May's $4.25 billion remained the monthly high. Remittances of $3.5 billion a month are now ordinary, not a peak.
Saudi Arabia was the only large corridor to rise from August, sending $899.1 million, up 2.9% month on month and 19.7% from $751 million a year earlier. It remained the largest source.
Inflows from other GCC countries rose 4.7% to $342.1 million. Oman, Qatar and Kuwait all increased. The UAE was almost flat at $748.5 million, down 0.2% from August and up 10.5% year-on-year.
The month's softness sat in Europe, not the Gulf. Remittances from the UK fell 8.6% to $515.1 million. EU countries fell 9.7% to $447.7 million, led by Italy ($152.9 million to $133.5 million) and Greece ($56.8 million to $48.6 million).
Saudi Arabia and the UAE together accounted for 46% of September remittances. With other GCC countries, the Gulf stood at 55%. Inside the UAE, the quarter splits. Inflows from Dubai rose 30.1% to $1.83 billion in the quarter, Abu Dhabi fell 34.5% to $331 million – even it rose in September, from $91.1 million to $104.5 million. Dubai's remittances eased from $634.6 million to $617.5 million in September.
Over the quarter, remittances from the UK rose 19.4% to $1.63 billion, the fastest among the large corridors. Inflows from the US rose 15.5% to $931 million, after a decline in the previous year's comparison. September inflows from the US were $305.9 million, down 0.9% from August and up 13.7% year-on-year.
Australia rose 9.5% in the quarter and Canada 11.7%. The EU was slower, up 9.8% to $1.41 billion. France was the weak spot, down 4.5%. Smaller corridors grew faster: Ireland 24.4%, Japan 42.6%, and South Korea 21.9%.
The UK, EU, US, Canada and Australia accounted for about 40% of September remittances. Experts say the policy question is skilled migration and student-to-worker routes, not only Gulf labour exports.
At a $3.6 billion monthly pace, remittances still do the heavy lifting on the current account. The SBP has already credited sustained inflows for the reserves rebuild and a narrower external gap.
Furthermore, the Pakistani rupee extended its marginal gains against the US dollar in the inter-bank market on Friday, closing at 277.00 after appreciating by Rs0.01. In the previous session on Thursday, the local currency had settled at 277.01 against the greenback.
In international markets, the euro was on course for its fifth consecutive weekly decline on Friday, although selling pressure showed signs of easing. France's stabilising debt market and falling US Treasury yields helped temper the dollar's rally.
Meanwhile, gold prices in Pakistan rose, tracking gains in the international market, with the price of one tola increasing by Rs5,900 to settle at Rs440,936. Globally, gold rose for a second straight session on Friday to a one-week high, as bargain buying emerged after bullion touched a two-month low earlier this week, while traders assessed the likelihood of further US Federal Reserve rate hikes.
According to rates released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association, the 10-gram gold climbed by Rs5,058 to Rs378,031. On Thursday, gold had gained Rs600 per tola to reach Rs435,036.
In the international market, spot gold rose 1.4% to $4,190.49 by 1544 GMT, heading for a weekly gain of about 1.2%. The metal fell to a two-month low on Wednesday as a stronger dollar and rising US Treasury yields weighed on the non-yielding metal, as per Reuters. US gold futures for December delivery also added 1.4%, trading at $4,215.60 per ounce.
Bullion gained due to "bargain hunting at the lows, as a floor has been building in the $4,000 region," said Rhona O'Connell, Head of Market Analysis at Stone X. "It is arguable that a further Fed hike is already priced in but so is the expectation for continued official sector net purchases. Without any Black Swan event, I find it hard to see gold breaking convincingly higher."
The US 10-year Treasury yields were off over two-decade highs hit on Wednesday. Meanwhile, silver prices in the domestic market rose by Rs144 to Rs6,512 per tola.

title: 7 7 magnitude earthquake rattles Panama  damages buildings and halts flights
description: International airport suspends flights  power down across six provinces  ship passage uninterrupted at Panama canal
content:
International airport suspends flights; power down across six provinces; ship passage uninterrupted at Panama canal
A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck southern Panama on Friday, damaging homes, cutting power, halting flights and sending residents into the streets, while triggering more than a dozen aftershocks.
The US Geological Survey said the earthquake struck at a depth of 12.6 km (7.8 miles) and that some casualties were possible.
Television images showed elderly residents in tears in the streets as a series of weaker aftershocks rattled the country.
"We're scared. It's just the two of us old folks here. The house has cracked, and we're afraid it could fall on us," said Ricardo Brown, 74, in Herrera province in southern Panama, where he noted the quake damaged several homes in his area of Las Minas.
A car damaged by falling debris after an earthquake struck near the southern coast of Panama, in Panama City, Panama, October 9, 2026. Photo: Reuters
The Panama Canal, about 126 miles (203 km) from the epicenter, was operating normally.
About 90 vessels, including bulk carriers, tankers and container ships, were waiting at both ends of the key waterway to transit or dock at berths serving storage terminals and trans-shipment services, according to monitoring data from LSEG's Workspace.
USGS estimated economic losses could amount to 1% to 10% of Panama's gross domestic product.
Power was down across six provinces, according to electricity provider Naturgy. The Tocumen International airport, a major regional hub, suspended flights.
Nestor Luque, director of Panama's geosciences institute, said the quake was triggered by the Azuero Sona Fault System that has long contained a build-up of pressure.
"It's a system of active faults that occasionally, due to the accumulation of stress, release this amount of energy," he said. "The seismic signals have traveled throughout the national territory, and that is why it could be felt everywhere."
🇵🇦 Footage of the Centenario Bridge in Panama after a 7.7 earthquake, with traffic still moving across it. And it was a powerful one. The quake struck roughly 200 km from Panama City, but the shaking was still felt in the capital. Despite that, the Panama Canal and this major… https://t.co/GT3jjSMDRm
In Panama City, Luke said he counted 40 seconds of vibrations, though other areas may have felt even longer tremors.
Sabina Rios, who was on the sixth floor of an old US military-era building in Panama City, said the shaking was unusually strong and prolonged.
"The quake felt strong and lasted a long time, the longest I've felt in years," Rios said.
Traffic snarled across Panama City as many offices released employees early, unsure of conditions or potential structural damage to buildings, and the Metro halted service.
Students in uniform poured onto the streets of downtown Panama as schools were let out early across the city. Classes were suspended nationwide.
The quake's epicenter was close to the rural community of La Pitaloza in a sparsely populated area of Herrera, near the Pacific coastline. Shaking was also felt as far as San Jose, the capital of neighboring Costa Rica, according to a Reuters witness.
In Penonome, a city about halfway between the epicenter and Panama City, social media videos verified by Reuters showed a damaged church and nearby collapsed buildings.
primeras imagenes de los daños del terremoto de panama #earthquake #Terremoto #panama #sismo #temblor pic.twitter.com/zpymnIyo9j
Omar Smith, who heads Panama's civil protection agency, told news outlet Telemetro Reporta that impacts had also been reported in Chitre, the capital of Herrera, and along the coast in Los Santos province.
A tsunami threat triggered by the earthquake off Panama has passed, and no further tsunami danger remains, the US Tsunami Warning System said.
People gather in an open area after an earthquake struck near the southern coast of Panama, in Panama City, Panama, October 9, 2026. Photo: Reuters
Panama was due to hold a national evacuation drill on Monday next week to test the country's emergency response capabilities in the event of an earthquake.
Venezuela and Colombia have also suffered major earthquakes in recent months, causing thousands of deaths in total.

title: Islamabad student found dead after allegedly losing Rs7m in education scam
description: Student   s family says it sold plot and jewellery to consultant who allegedly provided forged university documents
content:
Family says it sold plot, jewellery to consultant who allegedly forged university documents
A young student who dreamed of studying at a US university was found hanging from a tree near a road in Islamabad on Saturday, after her family allegedly lost around Rs7 million to a consultant who promised to secure her admission and scholarship, her relatives alleged.
The student had completed her bachelor’s degree from the International Islamic University Islamabad, earning a gold medal, and hoped to continue her studies abroad.
Her family said they sold a plot of land and jewellery to finance the dream, only to discover that the admission letter, scholarship letter and other documents provided by the consultant were all fake.
Read : Medical student dies in suspected suicide
According to an Islamabad police spokesperson, Sharif Ullah, the student’s body was found hanging from a tree near a road in the jurisdiction of the Ramna police station on Friday.
Police said the incident appeared to be a suicide at first, but the actual cause would be established after a post-mortem examination and further investigation.
Her body was shifted to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), where the post-mortem examination was under way.
Speaking to Express News outside the hospital’s mortuary, the student’s maternal uncle, Rana Amjad, said she was an exceptionally capable student who had completed her BS degree with a gold medal and wanted to pursue further education.
He said her father had been supplying milk on a motorcycle in Islamabad for the past 30 years and lived with his family in a rented flat in the capital.
According to Amjad, her niece met a man while visiting a place for an interview. The man claimed he could secure her admission to a university in the United States. After discussing the offer with her father, the family decided to pursue the opportunity despite opposition from her brothers.
Her father sold a plot in a private housing society and paid Rs2.1 million to the consultant, Amjad said.
Also Read : Domestic reasons suspected in Lahore university student’s suicide attempt: police
The consultant later demanded more money, saying it needed to be deposited in the student’s bank account to generate a bank statement required for the application, he added.
Amjad said his brother-in-law (the victim's father) then handed over his wife’s jewellery to the consultant. Instead of depositing the jewellery’s value into the student’s account, the man allegedly deposited it into his own account and gave her a fake bank receipt.
Amjad, a lawyer by profession, said the family approached him only after handing over the money and jewellery, when the consultant’s repeated delays in arranging his niece’s travel to the United States raised their suspicions.
He said he examined the documents provided by the consultant, including an admission letter purportedly issued by Harvard University, a scholarship letter and other university-related papers. He then had them checked through relatives living in the United States.
“We found out that all the documents were fake,” he said.
Amjad said he told his niece that the family had been defrauded, prompting her to break down in tears.

“She told me not to tell her father because he would not be able to bear it,” he said, adding that she remained deeply distressed over what had happened.
The student’s younger brother said she had wanted to continue her education, but the alleged fraud had shattered the family’s hopes.
The police said the circumstances surrounding her death would become clearer after the post-mortem examination and investigation.

title: Documentary on Elon Musk creates ripples in Hollywood
description: Documentary on Elon Musk creates ripples in Hollywood
content:
Trillionaire technology tycoon's former romantic partners share troubling accounts about him in new film releasing Oc
Elon Musk's former romantic partners offer personal accounts of their relationships with the billionaire in Musk, a four hour documentary directed by Alex Gibney that examines his private life, business career and influence on American society.
The film, which screens at the MILL VALLEY FILM FESTIVAL before its nationwide theatrical release on October 16, draws on interviews with people who have known or worked with Musk. According to SFGATE, among its most compelling contributors are Justine Musk, his former wife, and Ashley St Clair, who has publicly said she has a child with him.
Justine, the mother of Musk's first five children, discusses their relationship and describes experiences she says shaped her understanding of emotional manipulation. She also addresses the death of their first child and Musk's treatment of their transgender daughter, Vivian Jenna Wilson.
St Clair, a conservative influencer, shares details of her early communications with Musk, including personal messages displayed in the documentary. The film examines their relationship and her decision to speak publicly. She reportedly declined a $40m nondisclosure agreement, although the circumstances and terms surrounding that reported offer have not been independently established here.
Musk did not participate in the documentary. Gibney instead uses archival footage and an artificial intelligence generated avatar designed to represent the technology executive.
The director spent four years developing the project. It follows Musk's career from early ventures such as Zip2 and X.com to SpaceX, Tesla, Starlink, X and xAI. Contributors include LinkedIn co founder Reid Hoffman, neuroscientist Sam Harris and journalists Kara Swisher and Zoë Schiffer.
The documentary takes a critical view of Musk's business record and political influence, questioning his public image and examining his companies' relationships with government funding and regulation. These assessments represent the film's arguments rather than undisputed findings.
Musk has threatened legal action over the documentary, according to SFGATE, but the publication reported that no defamation lawsuit had been filed at the time of its review.
Elon Musk is chief executive officer (CEO) and largest shareholder of Tesla and SpaceX. Musk has been the wealthiest person in the world since 2025, and became the only trillionaire (in terms of US dollars) in June 2026; as of October 2026, Forbes estimates his net worth to be US$1 trillion.
Born into the wealthy Musk family in Pretoria, South Africa, Musk emigrated in 1989 to Canada; he has Canadian citizenship since his mother was born there. He received bachelor's degrees in 1997 from the University of Pennsylvania before moving to California to pursue business ventures. In 1995, Musk co-founded Zip2, a web software company. Following its sale in 1999, he co-founded X.com, an e-commerce payment system that merged with Confinity in March 2000 to form PayPal, which was acquired by eBay in 2002. Musk also became an American citizen in 2002.
In 2002, Musk founded and became CEO and chief engineer of SpaceX, a space technology company; the company has since led innovations in reusable rockets and commercial spaceflight. Musk joined Tesla as an early investor in 2004 and became its CEO and product architect in 2008; it has since become a leader in electric vehicles. In 2015, Musk co-founded OpenAI to advance artificial intelligence (AI) research, but later left; his growing discontent with the organization's direction and leadership in the AI boom in the 2020s led him to establish xAI, which became a subsidiary of SpaceX in 2026. In 2022, he acquired Twitter, a social networking service, and made significant changes, including rebranding it as X in 2023. His other businesses include Neuralink, a neurotechnology company that he co-founded in 2016, and the Boring Company, a tunneling company that he founded in 2017. In November 2025, Tesla approved a pay package worth $1 trillion for Musk, which he is to receive over 10 years if certain milestones are met, such as achieving a market capitalization of $8.5 trillion. Musk became the first US-dollar trillionaire upon the initial public offering of SpaceX in June 2026, though a SpaceX stock collapse brought him under the threshold by the next month.
Musk was the largest donor in the 2024 U.S. presidential election, where he supported Donald Trump. After Trump was inaugurated in January 2025, Musk served as Senior Advisor to the President and the de facto head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE).
The film presents a sweeping portrait of a figure whose business decisions and public interventions continue to attract intense scrutiny.

title: Hanna Cavinder jokes about Trevor Keegan taking two days to follow her back

content:
Hanna Cavinder reveals the playful DM she sent Trevor Keegan after her boyfriend took two days to follow her back
Hanna Cavinder has revealed how she made the first move with her boyfriend, Minnesota Vikings guard Trevor Keegan, after he took two days to follow her back on Instagram.
The former University of Miami basketball player, 25, shared details of their relationship in the latest episode of PEOPLE’s WAG World , released on October 9. Cavinder recalled sending Keegan, 26, a direct message after her twin sister, Haley Cavinder, encouraged her to reach out to him.
“I sent him a picture with a drink in my hands. I was like, ‘The wind took me here,’” Hanna said, laughing as she described the message.
Haley, who is married to Dallas Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson, helped introduce the pair by sending Hanna Keegan’s Instagram profile and encouraging her to follow him.
However, Keegan did not immediately return the interest online. Hanna joked that he was “like a turtle” because it took him two days to follow her back.
She also recalled asking Haley and Ferguson whether they had spoken to Keegan on her behalf before eventually deciding to message him herself.
Hanna and Keegan began dating in October 2025 but did not publicly confirm their relationship until June 2026. She explained that she wanted to keep their romance private initially, despite social media being a significant part of her life.
The athlete said she discussed her preference with Keegan early in their relationship and felt that going public was the right decision once they became boyfriend and girlfriend.
Haley also praised Keegan, saying he brings out the best in her sister. She described him as funny and someone she would be friends with regardless of his relationship with Hanna.
Hanna, who previously dated Arizona Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck before their April 2025 split, called Keegan her “best friend” and said they had experienced a great deal together in a short time.
The couple continues to share glimpses of their relationship as Hanna balances her public profile with her personal life.

title: Afghans fight back against Bangladesh
description: Saleem takes three wickets after the visitors    flying start in one off Test
content:
Saleem takes three wickets after the visitors’ flying start in one-off Test
Afghanistan fought back after Bangladesh made a flying start to reach 317-8 at stumps in their first innings on the opening day of their one-off Test at the Zayed Cricket Stadium at Abdu Dhabi on Friday. Opener Tanzid Hasan struck a blistering 83 off 71 balls as Bangladesh raced to 134-1 by lunch after electing to bat first. However, Afghanistan tightened their bowling in the middle session, triggering a collapse before the Tigers recovered through Litton Das and Mehidy Hasan Miraz. Bangladesh lost four wickets in the second session to slip to 226-5 at tea, with three of those dismissals coming for just four runs. Shadman Islam made 67 off 111 balls, while Mominul Haque contributed 39 from 70 deliveries. Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto chipped in with 29 off 42 balls before falling to Qais Ahmad, and experienced batter Mushfiqur Rahim was bowled by Yamin Ahmadzai for a seven-ball duck. Tanzid, who hit eight fours and four sixes, had looked set for a second Test century before Ismat Alam induced an edge that was caught by wicketkeeper Ikram Alikhil, ending a 124-run opening partnership. Afghanistan continued to chip away at the Bangladesh batting line-up, but Litton and Miraz steadied the innings with a 62-run partnership for the sixth wicket. Miraz was bowled by Ismat for 24 off 67 balls, bringing an end to the stand, before Litton reached his 21st Test fifty. The wicket-keeper batsman scored 53 off 89 deliveries, including four fours, but fell to Mohammad Saleem. Saleem then bowled Hasan Mahmud for two to claim his third wicket and leave Bangladesh eight down. Nayeem Hasan remained unbeaten on 11, while Taijul Islam was not out on four as the visitors reached 317-8 after 84 overs. Saleem finished with 3-70, while Ismat claimed 2-20 from 12.4 overs. Yamin gave early breakthroughs and he finished the day with 2-62. The contest marks Bangladesh's first-ever Test at a neutral venue, with Afghanistan looking to build on their late recovery when play resumes on Saturday.
