title: Cummins  Renshaw rescue wobbling Australia
description: South Africa pacemen prevail before the visitors    late fight back with the bat
content:
South Africa pacemen prevail before the visitors’ late fight-back with the bat
Pat Cummins and Matt Renshaw mounted a determined late fight-back to guide Australia to 187-6 at stumps on the opening day of the first Test against South Africa at Kingsmead, Durban, on Friday. Australia, who elected to bat first, struggled against a disciplined South African attack before their captain and Renshaw combined to frustrate the hosts in the final session. Renshaw was unbeaten on 46 from 115 deliveries, while Cummins had made 33 not out off 72 balls, lifting Australia from a precarious 124-6 to 187-6 when bad light brought an early end to play after 65.2 overs. The pair added an unbroken 63-run partnership for the seventh wicket, providing Australia with some stability after South Africa had reduced the visitors to six down. Marco Jansen and Wiaan Mulder claimed two wickets each, while Anrich Nortje also took two wickets to keep Australia under pressure throughout the day. Australia's top order endured a difficult morning after Travis Head fell for nine, caught behind off Mulder, before Nic Maddinson was dismissed for a duck by Jansen. Marnus Labuschagne offered resistance with 37 from 58 balls, striking six boundaries, but his dismissal triggered a collapse. He was trapped lbw by Mulder, leaving Australia at 84-3 at lunch. Steven Smith was removed for 25 in the next over, caught by Mulder off Jansen, as Australia lost two wickets without adding to their score. Renshaw then attempted to rebuild the innings alongside Alex Carey, who scored 14 before falling to Nortje in the 42nd over. Beau Webster lasted only two deliveries, hitting a boundary before being caught behind off Nortje, leaving Australia struggling at 124-6. South Africa appeared firmly in control at tea, with Australia having reached 149-6 after 53 overs. However, Cummins and Renshaw resisted the home attack during the final session, denying the bowlers further success. Jansen finished with 2-35 from 16 overs, while Mulder returned figures of 2-31 from 15 overs. Nortje took 2-40 from 13.2 overs. Australia will look to build on the late recovery when play resumes on Saturday, with Renshaw and Cummins aiming to extend their partnership and push the total towards a more competitive score. The five-day showdown is part of the 2026-27 ICC World Test Championship cycle.

content:
Says talks with Putin led to an agreement to increase Russian diesel supplies after a 'successful discussion'
US President Donald Trump said on Friday that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel fuel to American and global markets following talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Trump said on his Truth Social platform that he had concluded a "highly successful discussion" with Putin, resulting in an agreement to increase Russian diesel supplies.
"I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace, another 500,000 Tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 Tons immediately thereafter," Trump said.
He added that another 3m tonnes would be delivered "within a short period", depending on the condition of Russian diesel refineries.
"Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be coming down, in record numbers, and fast!” Trump said.
The president described lower fuel prices as a priority, particularly for American farmers, ranchers and truckers.

Trump also cited what he described as US "total control" of the Strait of Hormuz and reiterated that Iran would not be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon.
US Treasury authorises Russian diesel supplies
Shortly after Trump's announcement, the US Treasury Department said on X that its Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) was "immediately issuing a temporary general licence to allow the supply of Russian diesel to the global market".
Today, at President Trump’s direction, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) is immediately issuing a temporary general license to allow the supply of Russian diesel to the global market.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28 , prompting Tehran to respond with missile and drone attacks across the region and effectively close the Strait of Hormuz.
The conflict has continued for more than seven months, driving up global energy prices as commercial oil traffic through the strategic waterway has effectively halted.
The US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in June following mediation efforts by Pakistan and Qatar to halt hostilities and pave the way for negotiations.
Implementation of the agreement has since stalled amid disagreements, including over security and navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: What s Russia up to
description: What s Russia up to
content:
American CIA and Pakistan's ISI engineered the Soviet Union's defeat through the mujahideen
Messaging out of Moscow points to the unfolding of a new great game, presumably disturbing for Pakistan. Let us see why recent signals, particularly from Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, merit scrutiny and raise critical questions.
Is Russia settling scores by recognising and openly praising its erstwhile rival, the Afghan Taliban? Is Afghanistan turning into a proxy battlefield yet again? Is Foreign Minister Lavrov's telling the world: you may shun the Taliban, but we will not? And is Russia targeting the United States and Pakistan – partners in the anti-Soviet jihad – because the two are now so close that Moscow sees Islamabad as more of a facilitator of Washington's regional agenda than a neutral partner?
In Moscow's view, the American CIA and Pakistan's ISI engineered the Soviet Union's defeat through the mujahideen, forcing its withdrawal in February 1989. The two agencies later joined hands again in the war on terror, against both Al-Qaeda and the Afghan Taliban, before the United States chaotically withdrew from Afghanistan in August 2021.
The Russian foreign minister first urged all participants of the Moscow Format Consultations on October 5 to acknowledge that the Taliban regime "has been successfully governing the country". Lavrov then showered praise on Taliban security forces for their "uncompromising fight against the Islamic State and other terrorist groups on the Afghan soil".
Why would Moscow go out of the way on the ISIS issue? Most probably because it suspects the American CIA of raising Daesh/ISIS, whose cells operate in Russia and Central Asia. Moscow considers these cells as sources of destabilisation of the region.
"Afghan security forces are waging an uncompromising fight against ISIS and other terrorist groups. Hundreds of militants have been eliminated, and a number of high-profile terrorist attacks, including those targeting foreign nationals and diplomatic missions, have been foiled," Lavrov said.
"Let me emphasise that it is in our shared interest to help strengthen Kabul's counterterrorism capabilities by providing material, technical, and expert assistance, as well as by maintaining contacts between security services and military agencies."
In the same breath, the Russian foreign minister warned against any foreign involvement in Afghanistan and its neighbourhood: "The deployment of NATO military infrastructure in Afghanistan and neighbouring countries under any pretext whatsoever is categorically unacceptable presence of this kind carries the risk of destabilisation and heightened tensions and conflict. We have seen no other outcome from this kind of presence over the past several decades," Lavrov said.
Also in his meeting with Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi on the sidelines of the Moscow Format Consultations, Lavrov had extended his country's appreciation for Taliban's counterterrorism efforts.
This repositioning, it seems, has been underway for a few months.
In a July 15 address to a regional meeting on preventing terrorists from securing weapons in Central Asia, the Russian foreign minister had named ISIS in his customary way, as "Wilayat Khorasan", describing it as an Afghanistan-based threat.
"Terrorism remains one of the most daunting challenges to international peace and stability. For the Central Asian region, the main threat is undoubtedly posed by the Islamic State offshoot Wilayat Khorasan (or Khorasan Province), which seeks to use Afghanistan as a launching pad for expansion and subsequent establishment of a caliphate," said Lavrov.
Curiously at a press conference on October 6, Lavrov did not use the term and instead described the Islamic State's Pakistani branch as a "troublemaker that carries out terrorist incursions in Afghanistan and Pakistan".
The change matters because the July framing contradicted Kabul, and Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid had rejected it, saying the group had been contained and no longer had a physical presence in Afghanistan.
But the October 6 framing fits the Taliban's position better, who insist Daesh/ISKP camps are situated in Pakistan and are being used against neighbours including Afghanistan. In Lavrov's words: "Afghanistan and Pakistan are currently engaged in fairly serious confrontation because Islamic State operates an offshoot which it calls its Pakistani branch. It's a troublemaker that carries out terrorist incursions in Afghanistan and Pakistan."
The new framing moves the focus to an alleged Pakistan-linked entity, and it came as Lavrov was praising the Taliban's counterterrorism record and offering to help in the fight.
Is it a coincidence then that Russia has dropped the "Wilayat Khorasan" framing in favour of the Afghan Taliban's characterisation of Daesh/ISIS ?
In just three months, Moscow has shifted its public position on where the Islamic State's regional threat originates, bringing it closer to the account of Taliban-ruled Afghanistan.
India, too, is lapping up yesterday's alleged terrorists as the legitimate rulers of Afghanistan.
At the UN Security Council committee meeting on September 16, India was the only country to praise the Taliban, boasting of its diplomatic, political and humanitarian support to Kabul. Its ambassador did not mention terrorist groups operating in Afghanistan, nor was women's rights or the humanitarian situation raised.
Why would Russia align with Kabul when Pakistan, China, Uzbekistan and the UN consistently accuse the Taliban of sheltering groups ?
Are Moscow and Kabul signaling to the United States and Pakistan that if they back the alleged anti-Kabul groups, Russia can also step in to help fend off that threat?
Is the Russian claim that Pakistan supplied ammunition to Ukraine also be a driver behind Moscow's recalibration? It perhaps now brackets Pakistan with the pro Ukraine alliance led by US-Europe. Why would it otherwise embrace the Taliban for cooperation?
Is this why the Moscow Format meeting ended without any significant outcome?

title: Visa mills to censorship machine
description: Visa mills to censorship machine
content:
Exploiting this fabricated crisis, lobbyists pushed Congress to pass the Immigration Act of 1990
On 8 October, the US Department of Labour halted the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) process for major outsourcing firms, including Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys and Wipro, following remarks by Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling describing their operations as predatory "visa mills". Federal regulators cited systemic wage suppression and lottery manipulation designed to monopolise skilled worker quotas. With an employment-based green card backlog exceeding one million Indians and waits spanning decades, foreign staff remain bound to sponsoring employers with virtually no pathway to citizenship.
It began in 1989, when an unreviewed, highly lobbied National Science Foundation study sparked panic in Washington by forecasting a catastrophic shortfall of 675,000 scientists and engineers. Exploiting this fabricated crisis, lobbyists pushed Congress to pass the Immigration Act of 1990, which birthed the H-1B visa.
Instead of plugging a domestic skills gap, the Act gave Indian IT conglomerates the legal architecture to construct an industrial-scale labour cartel. By flooding the visa lottery to monopolise the pipeline, these outsourcing firms laid the demographic foundation of Silicon Valley's caste-based backend. Caste matters here because the claim of indentured servitude matters, and this demographic onslaught normalises discrimination at home and whitewashes Narendra Modi abroad.
Bear in mind three facts. Technology platforms are the new media. New citizens of Western nations were long expected to leave their prejudices behind, yet caste belied that. And this diaspora has played a critical role in normalising Modi abroad.
Begin with Modi's coverage. When you are accused, as chief executive of a state, of overseeing the mass murder of two thousand humans, mostly from a minority community, including invalids, pregnant women and children, it takes a lot to remove such charges from public memory, media coverage and search engines. Yet that is what happened after 2014. I covered the 2002 Gujarat riots from my desk in Islamabad and can tell you the outrage in the Western media was palpable. So what changed in America to make it forget? Quick answer: these visa mills changed how such things were viewed or tracked. You need to bend the system and keep covering such a massive hole with inane stories, permanently altering your input criteria.
On the surface, this is an immigration scandal. In reality, it is the unmasking of a thirty-year Trojan Horse. By September 2015, Modi had found willing accomplices on the inside. Travelling through Silicon Valley, he dazzled tech giants with the promise of a billion-user "Digital India". A silent quid pro quo was established: market access in exchange for algorithmic compliance.
I saw this firsthand in 2016. As Indian security forces blinded hundreds of protesting Kashmiri civilians with pellet guns, the digital record was systematically sanitised. Image searches for Kashmir were flooded with serene tourist vistas; the carnage was buried. When I wrote columns exposing this algorithmic whitewashing, my own search visibility would dynamically contract, throttled until I stopped, only to squeeze again when I resumed. Bing and Facebook, in those early days, did not do this. Google, whose backend engineering and product teams were heavily populated by the diaspora, did. This was never an external hack by a troll farm in New Delhi. This was internal curation.
Silicon Valley was primed to accommodate this censorship because its workforce had been captured decades earlier. India did not merely export code; it exported a demographic monopoly and an ancient psychological neurosis. In India, caste is the bedrock from which all other prejudices flow. When a tiny Savarna minority, barely 15 to 20 per cent, commands nearly all institutional wealth and cultural prestige, it lives in perpetual existential insecurity. Whatever strengthens the hierarchy, be it Modi's strongman politics or violent suppression at home, becomes entirely kosher.
When Silicon Valley outsourced its technical workforce to this elite, that siege mentality was hardcoded into the global internet. Dalits, protected by constitutional quotas since the 1950s, formed a narrow but courageous pipeline into engineering, over 67 per cent of whom would later report workplace discrimination in American tech firms, according to Equality Labs. The Shudra working-class majority, 60 per cent of India, was missing altogether. Denied quotas at institutions like the IITs until 2008, they missed the H-1B boom. When Shudra engineers reached California in the 2010s, the boardrooms were closed and their visas and green cards were held hostage by the upper-caste managerial monopoly they sought to escape. An engineering class animated by caste anxiety trained algorithms to suppress dissent, erase the Shudra majority and delete political opposition from view.
It matters because technology dictates the cognitive boundaries of the modern world. When its gatekeepers normalise graded inequality, they hack the moral software of Western democracy. If students watch corporate titans and university administrators treat ancient hierarchies with deferential indulgence, they absorb a chilling lesson: that supremacy is merely culture. Once hereditary inequality is normalised, every other supremacist ideology, from white nationalism to the darkest impulses of early 20th-century Europe, looks coherent.
To protect this apparatus offline, a diaspora lobbying pincer was unleashed. The Hindu American Foundation deployed legal intimidation, while the Coalition of Hindus of North America weaponised digital outrage to kill anti-discrimination bills like California's SB 403. The chilling effect paralysed Western politics. Zohran Mamdani, celebrated as a champion of the working class, cancelled an appearance at the Shri Guru Ravidass Temple in Queens, a prominent Dalit Sikh Gurdwara, during his 2025 mayoral campaign. Imagine even our fiercest princes of light cannot step foot inside an egalitarian shrine for fear of offending upper-caste political capital.
Now the Faustian bargain is unravelling. Tech barons believed that capitulating to New Delhi's censorship requests was the price of a lucrative market. Their own operations now risk being overrun by counterfeits propped up by the Modi government and Indian oligarchs. With Washington's suspension of green card processing for the major IT conglomerates, the racket stands named for what it is: visa mills built on indentured labour. The West imported cheap engineers to write code and got a feudal hierarchy that captured its digital public square, sanitised historical atrocities and built a global censorship machine.
The fight on Delhi streets today is as much for your freedoms and survival as for India's.

title: Students rock  Lashkar e Modi  in India
description: Students rock  Lashkar e Modi  in India
content:
India's own estimates show that among Indian graduates under 25, about 40% are unemployed
Narendra Modi has never faced such an awkward political challenge at home in his entire 12 years in power. The country claiming to be Vishwaguru missed the point that no country can become a world leader unless its knowledge base is strong. Modi's own National Education policy promises to spend 6% of the GDP on education, but remains unfulfilled.
What started as a satire in May when Chief Justice of India Surya Kant compared the unemployed youth with 'cockroaches', the Boston-based communications strategist seized the moment, and asked online if all the cockroaches in India were ready to join hands, and if so, what would be the consequences?
Gen Z responded and formed a huge movement which, for the first time, challenged Lashkar-e-Modi's tyranny and fascism being exercised for long. The youth were genuinely angry over unemployment, multiple scandals in examination system, paper leaks and the Modi government's absolute indifference towards their future. According to India's own estimates, among Indian graduates under 25, about 40% are unemployed.
But what actually kickstarted the student movement was the irregularities affecting the country's examination system, about two million affected in the medical entrance exams alone. Other irregularities were seen in the competitive exams. Therefore, the 'cockroaches' called for the resignation of Education Minister Dharmedra Pradhan. Under Modi, the universities have stopped teaching students to question authority, and that would be the most damaging legacy of this regime.
The 'maun' (silent) Modi government has been ignoring the students' call for long. This time they were surprised as thousands of students marched towards the parliament, with political leaders, critics, Bollywood stars and academicians joining in. Pradhan resigned on July 25, 2026. So the "emperor (Modi) had no clothes", as put by writer Arundhati Roy.
The key factor here was a 26-day hunger strike by climate activist Sonam Wangchuk. Police brutality was at its peak during this time. They used batons, tear gas, and even pellet guns, allegedly, that wounded the students. Before that pellet guns were only used by the security forces in IIOJ&K.
The National University of Singapore's Institute of South Asian Studies described it as the first resignation of a Modi cabinet minister brought about by intense public pressure. Carnegie Endowment scholar Milan Vaishnav said the government's familiar strategy for dealing with protests was no longer working: "They were not easily able to undermine the credibility of the protesters."
And now the same 'cockroaches' are back at Jantar Mantar, calling upon Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign, accusing him of complicity with Modi and Co, in deleting millions of voters in anti-BJP pockets, mostly Muslims, to damage the cause of other political parties, and weaken their voter base to win elections. The Election Commission said it was deleting duplicate or ineligible voters but it has not only challenged the credibility of India's electoral system but also exposed its claim of being the world's largest democracy.
And in this democracy, during the protests, women were groped, beaten, humiliated, dragged, mistreated and injured by Delhi police. Women filmed their injuries and put images on social media. AISA president Neha Bora said: "We may have been treated like dogs, animals and insects, but we are citizens and asking questions is our right."
Icing on the cake: Delhi Police ACO Vivek Bhagat, named in alleged sexual harassment of female journalists during these protests, has been promoted to the rank of additional DCP.
Even leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, said: "What's happening in Delhi right now follows a single pattern: silence any woman who dares to ask questions", while asking: "Mr Amit Shah - why are you and your [Delhi] police so afraid of women?"
Modi can tame journalists into 'godi media', defame political opponents and show disregard to international criticism, but he cannot ignore the 'cockroaches' any more. Although they are powerless, but they have started crawling through Modi's safely guarded image of invincibility, and it is becoming harder and harder to hide it.

title: AI and widening wealth gap
description: US President Donald Trump has done nothing to address the crisis
content:
US President Donald Trump has done nothing to address the crisis
The head of the IIMF is the latest global economic leader to identify the threat AI poses to most of the world's population. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva has warned that AI may boost productivity, but it is also "a source of divergence within countries and across countries", with a "very big distribution from the best to the laggers" in adoption. In plain terms, the gains are mostly flowing to those who own the technology, while everyone else competes for scraps. AI advocates may claim it will power us into the future, but in reality, it is becoming an engine of inequality.
The architects of this disparity aren't hiding; they don't even feel the need to pretend they care by giving away some money. Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk became the first person to amass over half a trillion dollars in wealth while his companies pour billions into AI and robotics, yet his lifetime philanthropic donations amount to under 0.1% of his lifetime earnings, mostly to his own 'charity'. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman proposes an "American Equity Fund" to tax large companies and pay citizens a dividend, but he opposes worker control or public ownership of the AI infrastructure generating the wealth. A report earlier this year by the international NGO Oxfam found that the 10 richest billionaires now hold $2.4 trillion - more than the poorest half of humanity combined.
Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump has done nothing to address the crisis. In fact, his administration is actively attacking "woke AI" and banning federal agencies from considering equity in AI development, effectively outlawing the very efforts needed to prevent algorithms from hard-coding today's disparities into tomorrow's economy. His tax policies have handed Silicon Valley titans enormous breaks while cutting access to government-funded medical care for millions of poor people. Billionaire wealth has surged three times faster than the previous five-year average, fueled directly by the AI stock boom. Without global action today, there will be nothing to stop the coming era of an AI aristocracy tomorrow.

title: Making traffickers pay
description: Making traffickers pay
content:
164 individuals were convicted in trafficking and smuggling cases in the region
For too long, human traffickers in Pakistan have operated with a sense of impunity, enriching themselves by exploiting the desperation of those seeking a better life abroad. The 17-year rigorous imprisonment awarded to two traffickers by a Gujranwala court is therefore a welcome demonstration of the consequences that must await such offenders.
The verdict is not without precedent. Courts in Gujranwala have previously awarded 20-year prison terms to traffickers implicated in the 2023 migrant boat tragedy, while several others have received sentences of up to 22 years. According to the FIA, 164 individuals were convicted in trafficking and smuggling cases in the region during the first six months of this year. These convictions are encouraging but the challenge now is to ensure that such judicial firmness becomes a consistent feature of the justice system rather than an exception celebrated after every tragedy. Pakistan has repeatedly witnessed the deaths of its citizens on dangerous migration routes, yet criminal networks continue to flourish. The prospect of substantial profits evidently remains greater than the perceived risk of punishment. This calculation must change. Where the evidence establishes serious offences, courts should impose the maximum penalties justified under the law. However, the severity of punishment means little if justice takes years to arrive. Human trafficking cases demand expedited proceedings, supported by thorough investigations and effective prosecution. The FIA must also pursue the financiers and facilitators who sustain these networks. Arresting individual agents while leaving their wider operations intact will accomplish little.
International cooperation must also form a central part of the effort to dismantle human trafficking networks. Pakistan must strengthen coordination with transit and destination countries to facilitate intelligence-sharing and joint investigations. The state must demonstrate that trafficking is neither a profitable enterprise nor a crime whose consequences can be evaded through influence or procedural delays.

title: Escalation in the air
description: Escalation in the air
content:
President Masoud Pezeshkian, nonetheless, has called for a negotiated solution
The Houthis are taking the conflict in the Mideast to new heights. Their daredevil attack on the Riyadh airport, which led to the killing of three people (including a pilot) and damaged a Saudi airliner, is a step in escalation. Similarly, satellite images show the Kingdom's Abqaiq oil facility on fire, while the East-West oil pipeline is also in limbo. Aviation remains suspended in the Saudi capital, and PIA has also cancelled its flights to Riyadh. This is in addition to the militia's blockade of the Bab el-Mandeb strait, sending shivers down the spine as global supplies remain choked through both the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz. It seems the warfare inside Yemen is taking root as the state military says it has carried out more than 1,729 operations against the Houthis with no signs of the militia being taken out.
President Masoud Pezeshkian, nonetheless, has called for a negotiated solution, provided Washington does not resort to "pressure and threats." However, there is a dichotomy at work, as the military brass of the Islamic Republic seems bent on upping the ante. The claims from the IRGC that it is prepared for a long-drawn war - and that armament production in the last seven months has risen 2.5-fold - are unnerving. This shock and awe on the strategic and economic fronts has led the UN to forecast a further dip in global growth, slumping to 2.6% in 2026 from 2.9% last year. However, there is a silver lining too, as President Trump told a midterm election rally that the US "will not attack Iran" until the November elections.
This comes as an opportunity for the doves to hammer out an amicable solution to the conflict. Pakistan, China, the UN secretary-general, Qatar and Türkiye are on their toes to persuade Iran and the US to return to the Islamabad MoU. Likewise, the return of the USS Abraham Lincoln to its home port after being in Persian waters for 321 days is a sign of a thaw in the making. All that is desired is a toning down of the rhetoric by the warring sides to help confidence-building measures take root.

title: Before she becomes a bride  let her be a girl
description: Pakistan is home to an estimated 19 million child brides
content:
Pakistan is home to an estimated 19 million child brides
On the International Day of the Girl, coming up on October 11 (tomorrow), we are reminded of a simple but often overlooked truth: girls' rights cannot be separated from their right to childhood. This year's theme, "End Child Marriage. Invest in Girls' Rights", asks us to look beyond the progress we celebrate and confront the gaps that still shape millions of girls' lives. It ends with leaving school, being married too young or becoming a mother before the age of 18. We often tell girls they can become whatever they aspire to be, but what about those who are never given the space to aspire at all? Before we ask what a girl can become, we must first ask whether she has been given the freedom to imagine what she could be.
According to UNICEF, around 650 million girls globally are living with the consequences of being married before the age of 18, while Pakistan is home to an estimated 19 million child brides. Child marriage remains one of the most painful manifestations of inequality. In parts of rural and tribal Pakistan, marriage is still treated as the expected destination for a girl as though she is simply born to become someone's wife. Poverty, limited access to education, concerns about girls' safety, social pressure and the belief that investing in a son's future matters more than investing in a daughter's can all push families towards early marriage.
It is a question of rights. When a girl is married before she is ready, society does not change her marital status; it changes the course of her childhood. Her right to education, health, protection, participation and economic opportunity becomes harder to exercise when adulthood is imposed on her.
Education is often one of the first rights a girl is asked to give up. When a household struggles financially, families may compromise on a daughter's education before a son. A girl learns early that her dreams can be treated as an expense while her brother's future is seen as an investment. Social pressures can then push her into early marriage, cutting short her education and limiting opportunities to earn an income. Child marriage can therefore close several doors at once, making it harder for her to escape the very poverty once given as the reason for marrying her off.
However, it can expose serious health risks for adolescent mothers due to early pregnancy. UNICEF-PK data shows that 18.3% of women aged 2024 were married before turning 18, while 3.6% were married before 15. WHO reports that girls under 16 face four times the risk of maternal death compared with women over 20. Child marriage is therefore not only a social and educational issue, but also a public health concern affecting girls and the next generation.
These consequences also connect to the wider gender gap. According to the World Economic Forum's Global Gender Gap Report 2026, Pakistan ranks 143rd out of 145 economies, with 59.5% of its overall gender gap closed. While Pakistan climbed five places from 148th in 2025, it remains among the world's three lowest-ranked countries. Notably, educational parity has reached 91.7%, while economic participation remains at only 36.4%. The contrast is clear: getting girls into education is one part of closing the gender gap, ensuring that education translates into economic independence and decision-making power remains a much larger challenge.
Investing in girls' rights means ensuring access to healthcare, safeguarding their rights and giving them the opportunities to earn, participate and make their own decisions. When we invest in a girl, we are not simply preparing her for a better future, we are giving her the tools to build one on her own terms.
Ending child marriage begins with changing what we have learned to accept as normal for girls. A girl should not have to prove that her education is worth investing in, or that her dreams deserve the same space as her brother's. The goal is not simply to delay marriage, but to give every girl the time, freedom and choice to decide who she wants to become.

title: Carrie    star Samantha Sloyan reveals why her Margaret White differs from past portrayals
description: Sloyan drew inspiration from Piper Laurie   s unsettling performance in the 1976 film
content:
Sloyan drew inspiration from Piper Laurie’s unsettling performance in the 1976 film
Samantha Sloyan has explained how Mike Flanagan’s reimagining of Margaret White in Carrie allowed her to approach Stephen King’s infamous character differently from previous actresses.
The eight episode Prime Video adaptation of King’s debut horror novel presents a new interpretation of Carrie White’s mother, whose treatment of her daughter stems from a desire to protect her, despite the harm she causes. Speaking to Empire , Sloyan said Flanagan fundamentally changed the relationship between Margaret and Carrie, freeing her from feeling bound to earlier portrayals.
Margaret has previously been portrayed memorably by Piper Laurie in the 1976 film adaptation. Sloyan said she appreciated Laurie’s performance, particularly its danger and unpredictability, and wanted to preserve some of that unsettling quality in her own interpretation.
However, the new version places greater emphasis on Margaret’s emotional complexity and misguided intentions. Rather than approaching the character solely as a frightening religious fanatic, Sloyan described her as a mother struggling with the prospect of her daughter growing up and becoming independent.
“We’re starting from a place of a loving mother,” Sloyan told PEOPLE . She explained that Margaret experiences pain as she feels Carrie moving away from her, even though her attempts to protect her daughter are deeply damaging.
The different characterisation reflects Flanagan’s decision to explore the central relationship from a fresh perspective while retaining elements of the psychological horror associated with the story.
Sloyan also benefited from an established working relationship with Flanagan, having collaborated with the filmmaker on six previous projects. According to the actress, he wanted her for Margaret from the beginning and wrote the role specifically for her.
She described the opportunity to work with a writer she admired as an especially rewarding experience, praising his willingness to advocate for the characters and performers he believes in.
With this adaptation, Sloyan aims to honour the unsettling qualities that made earlier versions memorable while presenting a more emotionally layered Margaret. The result offers a different perspective on the troubled mother and her relationship with Carrie, without removing the damage caused by her behaviour.

title: WandaVision    creator Jac Schaeffer takes on Amazon   s new    Stargate    series
description: WandaVision    creator Jac Schaeffer is developing a new    Stargate    sci fi series for Amazon MGM Studios
content:
‘WandaVision’ creator Jac Schaeffer is developing a new ‘Stargate’ sci-fi series for Amazon MGM Studios
Jac Schaeffer, the creator of Marvel’s WandaVision , is developing a new Stargate television series for Amazon MGM Studios, according to Variety. The project is part of Schaeffer’s overall deal with the studio, which was announced earlier this year.
A writers’ room is expected to open in the near future, according to sources familiar with the project. Schaeffer will executive produce the new sci-fi series alongside Joby Harold and Tory Tunnell of Safehouse Pictures. Representatives for Amazon MGM Studios and Schaeffer declined to comment.
The upcoming series marks Amazon’s second attempt to revive the Stargate franchise for television. Martin Gero had previously been reported to be developing a new entry in the science fiction universe, but that project ultimately did not move forward.
Schaeffer brings considerable experience in genre television to the project. She created WandaVision , the first Marvel Cinematic Universe series released on Disney+, starring Elizabeth Olsen and Paul Bettany as Wanda Maximoff and Vision. The series received 23 Primetime Emmy Award nominations and earned widespread critical acclaim following its 2021 debut.
She later created Agatha All Along , a WandaVision spinoff starring Kathryn Hahn as Agatha Harkness. Schaeffer served as the showrunner, writer and executive producer on the series and also directed episodes.
Her earlier writing credits include Disney’s animated featurette Olaf’s Frozen Adventure and the 2019 comedy The Hustle , starring Anne Hathaway and Rebel Wilson.
The Stargate franchise began with the 1994 science fiction film directed by Roland Emmerich and starring James Spader and Kurt Russell. The film inspired Stargate SG-1 , which ran for 10 seasons, followed by Stargate Atlantis , which aired for five seasons from 2004 to 2008.
Further details about the new Stargate series, including its cast, storyline and release date, have not been announced.

Mark Harmon returns as Gibbs and reunites with a longtime friend in a new ‘NCIS: Origins’ clip from Tuesday’s episode
Mark Harmon is returning to the world beyond Alaska as Leroy Jethro Gibbs in the upcoming episode of NCIS: Origins . A new clip from the October 13 instalment shows the longtime agent reuniting with an old friend after spending years living remotely.
In the preview, Gibbs walks along a busy boardwalk while reflecting on the bonds that can draw teammates back to people and places they thought they had left behind. He then arrives at a house and is greeted by Woody, played by Bobby Moynihan. Woody reacts with surprise, telling Gibbs, “My God, you’re still stunning,” before adding, “Well, this can’t be good.”
The reunion follows the third-season premiere, in which Gibbs was shot by a sniper outside his Alaskan home. The attack appears to prompt his return to civilisation. The present-day storyline will see him investigate a mystery connected to his time at Camp Pendleton in the 1990s.
Harmon, who played Gibbs on NCIS for nearly two decades, is appearing as the character in all 10 episodes of NCIS: Origins season three. He previously served as narrator and an executive producer during the prequel’s first two seasons.
The October 13 episode will also feature a storyline set in Gibbs’ past. A younger version of the agent, played by Austin Stowell, and his team will help a younger Woody after he is accused of murdering a rival from a bowling league.
Showrunner David J. North previously said Gibbs would leave Alaska for the first time in six years and hinted at more encounters with people from his past. North has also teased “so many surprises” during the season.
New episodes of NCIS: Origins air Tuesdays at 10 p.m. ET/PT on CBS and stream on Paramount+.

title: Amnesty International says Punjab anti terror law raises concern on  right to fair trial
description: Says amendment  allows for  secret trials  that could  result in human rights violations  misuse of anti terrorism laws
content:
Says amendment allows for 'secret trials' that could result in human rights violations, misuse of anti-terrorism laws
Amnesty International said on Friday that the Punjab Anti-Terrorism (Amendment) Bill, 2026, raised "serious" concerns about the "right to a fair trial", further noting that the amendment allowed for "secret trials" that could result in grave human rights violations.
On August 31, the Punjab Assembly passed the Punjab Anti-Terrorism (Amendment) Bill, 2026 amid protests and a walkout by opposition lawmakers.
In a public statement , Amnesty International noted that the amendment was a "glaring attack on the right to fair trial in Pakistan".
Pakistan: The Anti-Terrorism (Punjab Amendment) Act, 2026, raises serious concerns about the right to a fair trial. In a new public statement, Amnesty International examines the amendment against Pakistan’s obligations under international human rights law and highlights how…
The statement added that the amendment created a mechanism for trials shrouded in "complete secrecy", exceeding permissible exceptions to the "right to a fair trial", which includes a public trial, under international human rights law, further adding that it deepened concerns regarding "past misuse" of anti-terrorism laws that had resulted in grave human rights violations.
Read : LHC seeks arguments on anti-terror bill's legality
The statement also noted that the process and criteria for designating a trial as a “special security case” were highly vague and lacked transparency.
"The text of section 21AAA(5)(b) suggests that the designated authority has full discretion to decide whether a case or a class of cases require extraordinary protection measures and that the chief justice is bound by this decision. Neither the amendment nor the original act offers a definition of what constitutes extraordinary protection," it added.
Amnesty further stated that the amendment allowed a level of secrecy with enormous potential for miscarriage of justice.
"The amendment is applicable to Punjab province, which is Pakistan’s most populous province consisting of 127,333,305 people (50.9% of the total population)37, and if this act is allowed to be implemented it could lead to a knock-on effect in other provinces who could pass similar legislation."
The amendment inserted a new Section 21AAA into the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, creating a “special security case” mechanism for cases in which participants are considered to require extraordinary protection.
Read More : Punjab Assembly passes controversial anti-terror law
A designated authority — an officer of at least BS-20 whose identity would itself remain confidential — can declare a case or a class of cases a special security case. At the authority’s request, the LHC chief justice can assign the case to an Anti-Terrorism Court judge.
The amendment also said that the identities of judges, public prosecutors, defence counsel, police officers, witnesses and other persons involved in such proceedings “shall not be disclosed”.
Judicial orders will use official titles instead of judges’ names, and witnesses would be identified by codes issued by the designated authority.
The proceedings could be held at secure premises or conducted through video links, including from prisons. The amendment also allows the government to adopt other security measures it considers appropriate.

title: Christy Carlson Romano says Mandy Moore made her feel like an outsider at    The Princess Diaries    party
description: Romano says she also missed her chance to audition for the 2001 Disney film because of filming commitments
content:
Romano says she also missed her chance to audition for the 2001 Disney film because of filming commitments
Christy Carlson Romano has recalled an uncomfortable encounter with Mandy Moore at a party celebrating The Princess Diaries in 2000, saying the interaction left her feeling hurt.
During an October 7 appearance on Page Six Radio , the former Disney Channel star described attending the gathering in Malibu while filming the first season of Even Stevens . Romano said her co star Ty Hodges invited her to the event, which she remembered as a wrap party for the Disney film.
Romano explained that she approached Heather Matarazzo, who appeared in The Princess Diaries , because they had previously worked together on an MTV project. However, she said Matarazzo seemed not to remember their earlier meeting.
According to Romano, the situation became more uncomfortable when Moore, who played school bully Lana Thomas in the film, joined the conversation.
“Mandy was next to [Heather] and Mandy kind of did this, like, [laugh],” Romano recalled.
She said the moment upset her and left her unsure how to interpret Moore’s reaction. Romano described her immediate impression by saying, “Mandy’s a mean girl!” She also acknowledged that she had arrived at the party without being an invited guest, explaining, “I did crash that party, man.”
Her account reflects Romano’s recollection of an interaction from more than two decades ago. It does not establish Moore’s intentions, and the supplied report does not include a response from the singer and actress.
The memory also connects to another disappointment Romano has discussed publicly. In a 2021 YouTube video, she revealed that she had been preparing to audition for The Princess Diaries but missed the opportunity because Even Stevens required her to continue filming.
Romano said the audition had felt like a significant career opportunity, particularly because actors could not simply submit recorded auditions at the time.
The actress has recently published her memoir, Once Upon a Trainwreck: The Fall and Rise of a Child Star , which examines her experiences growing up in the entertainment industry.

title: Preparations complete  ball in K P govt s court on emergency imposition  Tariq Fazal
description: Says issue can be resolved if provincial government stands with federal authorities and law enforcement agencies
content:
Sanaullah links K-P governor’s rule to counterterrorism cooperation, not long march
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry on Friday said the federal government had completed its preparations for imposing governor’s rule or an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, adding that it was now up to the provincial government to decide what role it would play in the proposed measures.
Speaking on a private television programme, Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Sath , the minister said the federal government and law enforcement agencies had to eliminate terrorism in K-P at all costs, and it would be better for the provincial government to cooperate and participate in the fight.
“If the provincial government stays away from this effort, the other option would be to impose an emergency and eliminate terrorism and terrorists from the province once and for all,” he said, clarifying that an emergency would be imposed across the entire province, not just in 12 districts.
Read More : PTI warns of quitting assemblies if governor's rule imposed in K-P
Chaudhry categorically stated that the proposed emergency had nothing to do with the PTI’s planned long march.
He said the government had dealt with longer marches towards Islamabad in the past and stopped them, adding that preparations had been completed to prevent the planned march as well.
“We know how to deal with this long march. This long march is neither a threat nor a problem,” he said.
The minister refrained from giving a date for the imposition of an emergency but said the federal government had now concluded, both mentally and practically, that further delay was not possible.
“I cannot give you a day or date, but a final decision has been made that decisive action to eliminate terrorists in K-P is inevitable,” he said.
Asked whether there was still a chance of negotiations, particularly with Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman emerging as a possible mediator, the minister said the door to dialogue was never closed in political affairs.
However, he blamed PTI for a lack of consensus within its own ranks on whether to authorise Maulana Fazl to mediate.
“When I said the ball was in the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government’s court, the option of Maulana Fazlur Rehman was also on the table,” he said.
He added that if the PTI did not authorise Maulana Fazl to mediate or was unwilling to appoint him as an intermediary, it would be difficult to move the dialogue process forward.
Chaudhry said the PTI leadership would have to provide assurances that it would cooperate in the fight against terrorism if it wanted meaningful and effective negotiations.
“That assurance is the foundation of any lasting solution,” he concluded.
Sanaullah links K-P governor’s rule to counterterrorism cooperation
Earlier, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said that the proposed governor’s rule or emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa was related to the matter of counterterrorism cooperation, not the PTI’s planned long march, and could be resolved if the provincial government stood alongside the federal government and law enforcement agencies.
Speaking on a private television programme, Naya Pakistan , Sanaullah said the negotiations appeared to be heading towards a dead end as the PTI did not seem willing to abandon its plan for a long march and accept the offer of talks.
Linking the possibility of governor’s rule or an emergency in K-P to the PTI leadership and provincial government’s commitment to the fight against terrorism, he said the matter could be resolved if PTI leaders and Chief Minister Sohail Afridi declared their support for the federal government and law enforcement agencies in the fight against terrorism.
Read : CM Afridi says PTI to unveil ‘final plan’ in Swabi as long march enters 6th day, heads to Charsadda
He stressed that the proposed imposition of governor’s rule had nothing to do with the long march.
“If they do not make this commitment, then whether they hold the long march all the way to Islamabad or keep it short of Islamabad will make no difference,” he said.
The PML-N leader said that, over the past three or four days, the K-P chief minister had stated that no military operation would be allowed in the province.
Sanaullah said there would be no need to displace people or evacuate valleys, as the proposed measures would involve intelligence-based operations.
“Imposing an emergency certainly does not mean that those districts will be evacuated and people turned into internally displaced persons (IDPs). Rather, intelligence-based operations will be conducted within the territorial jurisdiction,” he said.
During the same program, K-P Law Minister Aftab Alam expressed surprise at what he described as ambiguity in statements by federal ministers on the proposed measures.
“One minister says that if the long march is not called off, an emergency will be imposed, while another says that the government wants to impose an emergency or governor’s rule because the provincial government is not cooperating with the federation on terrorism-related matters,” he said.
Alam said he believed a narrative was being built against the K-P government as part of what he called a “nefarious conspiracy”.
“God forbid, it is being suggested that we are somehow on the side of someone else in these matters. However, our stance is clear: this war is ours even before it is the federation’s,” he said.
Also Read : Govt trying to avoid ‘last option’ but may consider governor’s rule in K-P if no alternative remains: Khawaja Asif
He maintained that the PTI and the K-P government stood with law enforcement agencies in the fight against terrorism, adding that the provincial government had strengthened the police.
“Our mission is very clear, and it is being deliberately made controversial,” he said.
The issue of Governor’s Rule has become a major point of contention between the federal and K-P government. On September 21, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the government was consulting the law ministry on legal options for the province, including Governor’s Rule , if the PTI proceeded with its long march. Two days later, however, Information Minister Atta Tarar ruled out any plan to impose Governor’s Rule, saying the federal government had no intention of removing the PTI administration.
Some federal ministers publicly raised the possibility of federal intervention in K-P. Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam said consultations were under way on the "constitutional and legal option" of imposing Governors' Rule.
Afridi, however, rejected the warnings and said he would not retreat from his position because of threats of Governors' Rule or an emergency. He also said PTI supporters could take to the streets at short notice if an attempt was made to remove him.
However, amid the speculation, just days before the PTI’s planned long march, the prime minister and the president formed a committee last week to negotiate with the PTI and other opposition parties over the march, while expressing concern over the province’s deteriorating law and order situation.
The government and opposition parties held negotiations over two days, and the talks initially appeared to be bearing fruit. However, just as the two sides were nearing agreement on most of the contentious issues , a deadlock emerged, bringing the negotiation process to a halt.
The government blamed the K-P government , particularly Afridi, for the deadlock and failure of the negotiations. The PTI, however, claimed that the talks broke down over its demand for a meeting with the party’s founder, which the government refused to accept.
Read More : Bilawal urges PTI to return to political engagement, says governor's rule in K-P would be 'atomic bomb'
As the negotiation process collapsed, CM Afridi began his long march towards Islamabad, further escalating tensions between the two sides, with both sides continuing to trade allegations .
As tensions peaked, PM Shehbaz once again entered the fray and extended an olive branch to the PTI, saying the government was prepared to engage with the opposition if the party ended its long march and sit-ins.
The PTI, however, rejected the offer as its march continued towards Islamabad, entering its sixth day on Friday. The convoy moved towards Charsadda, with CM Afridi leading the procession.

title: CM Afridi outlines long march plan till Oct 14 as convoy enters Charsadda on 6th day
description: While Salman Akram Raja rules out compromise  predicts a large Punjab turnout for the long march
content:
Announces phased mobilisation plan, urging party workers from across Pakistan to reach Swabi Interchange on Oct 11
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Friday announced the next phase of the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf’s (PTI) long march, calling on people from across the country to reach Swabi Interchange on Oct 11 and outlining plans for the participation of various divisions till Oct 14, as the march entered its sixth day.
In a post on X, Afridi directed parliamentarians, party office-bearers, organisational officials and workers from across Pakistan to arrange transport and ensure their arrival at Swabi Interchange on Oct 11.
“Starting tomorrow, begin getting them there by any means possible. All Pakistanis should also arrive on that same day,” he said.
Under the announced schedule, caravans from Peshawar and Malakand regions, as well as Kohat Division, including Karak, would reach Swabi Interchange on Oct 13. Mr Afridi said he had instructed parliamentarians and the party organisation to ensure workers from these areas joined the gathering.
۱۱ اکتوبر کو پورے پاکستان سے لوگ صوابی انٹرچینج پر آئینگے۔ پورے پاکستان سے پارلیمینٹیرینز اور تنظیمی عہدیدار ورکرز کو صوابی انٹرچینج تک پہنچائے۔ کل سے کسی بھی طریقے سے اُن کا پہنچنا شروع کریں۔ تمام پاکستانی بھی اُسی دن پہنچے۔ ۱۳ اکتوبر کو خیبرپختونخواہ کا پشاور ریجن، ملاکنڈ…
He said caravans from Hazara region, Bannu Division and Dera Ismail Khan Division would arrive on Oct 14, when the party would announce its plan for moving beyond Swabi Interchange.
“Insha’Allah, on Oct 14, we will advance from Swabi onward,” the chief minister said.
Earlier, addressing the participants at Shabqadar Chowk, CM Afridi also criticised the federal government over its security and economic policies, arguing that Pakistan’s progress had been derailed by what he described as a regime-change operation while defending the PTI’s record in government and calling for an end to what he termed political victimisation.
The chief minister said K-P had experienced peace and prosperity during Imran Khan’s tenure as prime minister from 2018 to 2022, adding that the country’s economic indicators had been positive during that period.
“The true leadership works for the welfare and prosperity of the people,” he said, alleging that decisions taken behind closed doors and the regime-change operation had halted Pakistan’s development.
He blamed what he described as foreign conspirators and internal traitors for pushing the country away from the path of progress.
CM Afridi claimed that 14,000 intelligence-based operations and 22 major military operations had been conducted in Pakistan between 2004 and 2026, alleging that the objective of these operations was not to eliminate terrorism but to target the PTI and Imran Khan.
He said people who had been loyal to Pakistan had repeatedly been branded traitors since 1947, citing the cases of Bacha Khan and Fatima Jinnah, the sister of the country's founder, Quaid-e-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah.
He alleged that patriotic citizens were now being accused of terrorism as the truth about those responsible for violence came to light.
“We know, and they also know, who the real terrorists are,” he said.
CM Afridi said residents of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, police personnel and soldiers were making daily sacrifices in the fight against terrorism, adding that his proposals for ending terrorism were not being taken seriously.
He further claimed that the federal government owed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa more than Rs5,000bn and was not providing the province with its due share under the National Finance Commission award.
He accused the federal government of merely pretending to sympathise with the province.
Defending his provincial government’s performance, CM Afridi said K-P police had some of the best weapons and modern equipment in the country and that the force had one of the lowest levels of corruption.
He said the province had received an award for digital governance, while its Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system and provincial assembly had secured top positions in their respective categories.
The chief minister criticised Pakistan’s foreign policy, saying relations with neighbouring countries were not good because of its failures, claiming that trade with neighbouring countries could generate $100 billion in annual business and Rs27,000b in revenue.
He appealed to people from all sections of society to play their role in achieving what he called genuine freedom and sovereignty.
Separately, addressing the workers in Charsadda, CM Afridi said that PTI would announce its "final plan" in Swabi, which would leave its opponents "sleepless".
“This is not a long march; these are the conditions for a revolution,” CM Afridi said while addressing party workers at Shabqadar Chowk in Charsadda, where the PTI long march had entered the district’s limits.
The chief minister said the public response to the march had been overwhelming.
“When the long march entered Peshawar, the streets were filled with people,” he said, expressing appreciation for the enthusiasm displayed by party supporters.

CM Afridi urged workers to sustain their passion and commitment until the march reached Swabi. Reiterating that he would announce the march’s next phase in Swabi, without disclosing further details. He also expressed confidence that the strategy he intended to announce would succeed through public support
“The power of the people would ultimately prevail,” he stressed during the speech.
Addressing concerns over threats against him, Afridi said he was aware of the warnings.
“I know that threats are being made, but you [PTI supporters] must not be afraid,” he told the long march attendees.
The chief minister also criticised the prevailing situation in the country, saying the conditions in interior Sindh, Punjab and K-P were unlike anything he had witnessed before.
CM Afridi addressing PTI Long March in Peshawar on October 9, 2026. Photo: Screengrab
Earlier in the day, addressing party workers at Bakshi Bridge in Peshawar, CM Afridi had said the next course of action regarding the movement would be announced in Charsadda before the march proceeded to Mardan and then Swabi.
He urged workers to maintain their enthusiasm and said there had been no decline in public participation as he travelled from one end of Peshawar to the other.
“I would like to thank the people of Peshawar from the bottom of my heart. I have travelled from one end of Peshawar to the other, but God willing, there has been no decline in the public’s enthusiasm, passion or participation,” he said.
Read: Bilawal urges PTI to return to political engagement, says governor's rule in K-P would be 'atomic bomb'
The chief minister said the party had moved beyond the equivalent of a Test match and was ready for shorter formats, using cricketing terminology to describe the next phase of its campaign.
“We have played a Test match; now we have to play One-Day, T20 and T10,” he said, adding that the party was even prepared to play “Super Sixes” if workers demanded it.
According to PTI’s social media handle, the chief minister will address various gatherings in Charsadda and stay for the night. It also said that CM Afridi is accompanied by the party’s provincial president, parliamentary leadership, and other party leaders.

PTI’s Salman Akram Raja rules out compromise, predicts large Punjab turnout for long march
Separately, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said the party would not enter into any agreement that compromised its principles, vowing that Punjab would participate in the planned long march with a large number of caravans.
Speaking to the media at the Lahore High Court, Raja said the lives of ordinary citizens were paramount for the party, and it would not take part in any action that causes bloodshed of innocent people.
“We are prepared to endure every hardship, but we will not abandon our principles,” he vowed.
Read more: LHC seeks report on facilities provided to Imran’s sisters in jail
Raja outlined that he was discharging multiple responsibilities as the party’s secretary general and was also looking after the cases of PTI founder Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi.
Commenting on the situation in K-P, Raja claimed that the provincial government had ceased to function and allegedly even a deputy commissioner was refusing to comply with orders.
He condemned what he described as a crackdown on PTI workers in Peshawar the previous day, claiming that several party workers had been abducted.
“We will endure this brutality because we stand for the truth,” he said, remarking that fascism had taken over the country and urging those with authority to “exercise restraint and reconsider their actions”.
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) announced its long march towards Islamabad to press for the release of party founder Imran Khan, accelerate hearings in cases against him and his wife Bushra Bibi, address concerns over his medical treatment and seek an end to restrictions on meetings with him.
The party initially planned to launch the march on September 27, but on September 26 CM Afridi rescheduled the protest to take place on October 4, amid extensive security and traffic restrictions and continuing efforts to negotiate with the federal government. He said the postponement was a unanimous decision of the party’s political committee.
On October 4, the long march began from Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat under CM Afridi’s leadership, with participants from Tank, Dera Ismail Khan, South Waziristan, North Waziristan, Bannu and Lakki Marwat joining the procession.
According to the announced schedule, the convoy was to travel through Karak and Kohat before reaching Peshawar, with additional participants joining along the route.
The protest unfolded amid heightened political tensions and a breakdown in negotiations between the government and opposition.
A number of government officials, including Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, accused the K-P government of foiling negotiations, saying the two sides had made substantial progress before reaching an impasse over terrorism-related issues. The PTI, meanwhile, maintained that its demands and concerns required a political, not an armed response.
As the convoy progressed through the province, Afridi called for constitutional supremacy, the rule of law and the protection of fundamental rights.
PTI leaders pledged that the long march would remain peaceful and continue until the party’s demands were addressed. According to the schedule reported by The Express Tribune , the march was due to reach Charsadda on October 9, Mardan on October 10 and Swabi on October 11, with the party expected to decide its next steps after reaching Swabi.

title: Khloe Kardashian fires back at backlash over    The Kardashians    AI scene
description: Khloe Kardashian addresses backlash over The Kardashians    AI scene  telling fans to watch the full season eight intro
content:
Khloe Kardashian addresses backlash over The Kardashians’ AI scene, telling fans to watch the full season eight intro
Khloe Kardashian has responded to criticism of an artificial intelligence sequence featured in the season eight premiere of The Kardashians , urging viewers to watch the clip in full before judging it.
The reality star addressed the backlash in an Instagram post on October 8, sharing a video of the scene and writing, “WATCH UNTIL THE END.” She added that it was “frustrating” to see people commenting after watching only the first few seconds.
The opening sequence features AI versions of Khloe, Kim Kardashian, Kourtney Kardashian, Kylie Jenner, Kendall Jenner and their mother, Kris Jenner. The digitally created family members appear in different locations around the world, including a yacht in the South of France, Japan, an African safari, Versailles and a ski chalet in Switzerland.
The AI versions eventually reunite in Calabasas after Kim receives a message from Kris asking everyone to return for the family’s premiere. Their appearances then begin to change in surreal ways, with Kourtney’s face turning into a thumb with a red nail and Kylie growing a tail.
The real Kardashian-Jenner family then enters the scene and confronts the digital versions. The AI Kris suggests that an artificial version of the show would be easier to film, but the real family insists it cannot be replaced. Kim says they do not need AI when they have their reality, while Khloe presses a “kill switch” to end the sequence.
The Kardashians’ AI scene has received mixed reactions online. Some viewers praised the concept, while others questioned why the family used AI to make a statement about not being replaceable by the technology. One commenter said they remained confused after watching the clip, while another described the sequence as clever.
Khloe has not provided further details about the criticism beyond her Instagram response.

title: Miles Davis love story    Miles   Juliette    begins filming in Paris
description: Damson Idris will play Miles Davis in Miles   Juliette  with Anamaria Vartolomei  as the film gets under way in Paris
content:
Damson Idris will play Miles Davis in Miles & Juliette, with Anamaria Vartolomei, as the film gets under way in Paris
Production has begun in Paris on Miles & Juliette , a new feature from Oscar-nominated filmmaker Bill Pohlad and his River Road Entertainment.
The film stars Damson Idris as jazz legend Miles Davis and Anamaria Vartolomei as French singer and actress Juliette Gréco. A first-look image from the project has been released.
The cast includes J. Alphonse Nicholson as drummer Kenny “Klook” Clarke, Jay Reeves as pianist Tadd Dameron, Grammy-winning musician and producer Terrace Martin as Charlie “Bird” Parker, Denny Love as James Moody, Lodric D. Collins as Max Roach and Hubert Point-Du Jour as John Coltrane.
Written by Pulitzer Prize finalist Zora Howard, Miles & Juliette follows 22-year-old Davis during a transformative trip to Paris in 1949. There, he meets and falls in love with Gréco, who was emerging as a prominent figure on the city’s postwar Left Bank. The story explores the connection between two young artists before they became internationally known, against a backdrop of musical and cultural change.
Pohlad described the project as a story of a brief encounter between two artists that becomes something unexpected. He previously directed Love & Mercy , the biographical drama about Beach Boys frontman Brian Wilson.
Pohlad and Andrew Van Wyk will produce for River Road, alongside Kim Roth and Dan Clifton. Mick Jagger and Victoria Pearman are producing through Jagged Films. France’s Why Not Productions is providing production services.
The creative team includes cinematographer Maryse Alberti, production designer Dan Weil, editor Sabine Hoffman and Grammy-winning musician Robert Glasper, who will compose the score and serve as music producer. Glasper previously produced the Miles Davis tribute album Everything’s Beautiful in 2016.
CAA Media Finance is handling North American rights. Further details, including a release date, have not been announced.

description: Released on October 9   2026   Other Mommy  is projected to earn around  20 million during its opening weekend
content:
Released on October 9, 2026, 'Other Mommy' is projected to earn around $20 million during its opening weekend
Jessica Chastain’s supernatural horror film Other Mommy is heading towards a promising opening weekend at the North American box office, while Aaron Sorkin’s The Social Reckoning is facing more modest expectations.
Released on October 9, 2026, Other Mommy is projected to earn around $20 million during its opening weekend, potentially giving Universal Pictures and Blumhouse a much-needed boost in the horror market. The film, directed by Rob Savage, has benefited from considerable online attention following the viral success of its unsettling trailer.
With a reported production budget of $19 million, the horror film stars Chastain in a dual role as a mother and a sinister supernatural entity that takes her appearance. Based on Josh Malerman’s novel Incidents Around the House , the story follows a young girl who encounters a frightening presence that looks exactly like her mother.
Meanwhile, The Social Reckoning , Sorkin’s follow-up to the 2010 film The Social Network , is expected to have a considerably quieter debut. The film is tracking towards an opening weekend of approximately $7 million to $8 million in North America, falling well short of its predecessor’s performance.
The new film stars Jeremy Strong as Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg, taking over the role previously played by Jesse Eisenberg. Mikey Madison and Jeremy Allen White also feature in the cast. The story centres on whistleblower Frances Haugen, who exposes internal Facebook documents to a journalist, bringing renewed scrutiny to the platform’s impact on society.
Despite the original film’s critical success and cultural influence, The Social Reckoning faces the challenge of attracting audiences more than a decade after its predecessor. Its projected opening reflects a more subdued theatrical outlook for the adult-oriented drama.
The two releases arrive during a quieter period for cinemas, with studios hoping that the contrasting appeal of supernatural horror and technology-focused drama will encourage audiences to return to theatres. While Other Mommy has the advantage of seasonal demand ahead of Halloween, The Social Reckoning will need positive audience reception to build momentum beyond its opening weekend.

title: Sadie Sink in talks to star in A24 film adaptation of  The Guest
description: The novel explores class  power  desire and social manipulation through Alex   s attempts to secure a place for herself
content:
The novel explores class, power, desire and social manipulation through Alex’s attempts to secure a place for herself
Sadie Sink is in talks to star in The Guest , a film adaptation of Emma Cline’s bestselling novel, with Lorene Scafaria reportedly in discussions to direct the project.
According to Variety , A24 and Square Peg are behind the adaptation of Cline’s 2023 novel, which follows Alex, a young woman who is asked to leave the Long Island home of her wealthy older boyfriend during the final days of summer. Determined to return, she attempts to navigate her way through the wealthy communities of the Hamptons while trying to make it back to him.
The novel explores themes of class, power, desire and social manipulation through Alex’s attempts to secure a place for herself in unfamiliar surroundings. Its tense narrative follows her as she moves between people and places, relying on her ability to persuade others that she belongs.
Sink is best known for playing Max Mayfield in Netflix’s Stranger Things . Since the series concluded, she has taken on stage roles, including a Broadway performance in John Proctor Is the Villain and a West End production of Romeo & Juliet opposite Noah Jupe.
Scafaria previously directed Hustlers , the 2019 crime drama starring Jennifer Lopez and Constance Wu, and has worked on television projects including Succession . The potential adaptation would bring Cline’s psychological novel to the screen under the A24 and Square Peg banner.
No further casting details or production timeline have been announced.

title: Andrew Scott worries    Heated Rivalry    fans may avoid sadder LGBTQ  stories like  Elsinore
description: Scott said that audiences may be reluctant to revisit periods when being gay came with significant hardship
content:
Scott said that audiences may be reluctant to revisit periods when being gay came with significant hardship
Andrew Scott has expressed concern that the popularity of joyful LGBTQ+ romances such as Heated Rivalry could lead audiences to overlook films that explore the more painful parts of queer history.
Speaking at the BFI London Film Festival, Scott discussed the importance of telling different kinds of gay stories while promoting his new film Elsinore , in which he portrays actor Ian Charleson, who played Hamlet while battling AIDS before his death in 1990.
“I welcome things like Heartstopper , Heated Rivalry and Red, White & Royal Blue , and all those things that are joyful,” Scott said, according to Screen International . However, he added that the tendency to categorise gay stories in a particular way troubles him, suggesting that audiences may be reluctant to revisit periods when being gay came with significant hardship.
Scott also reflected on Charleson’s experience of revealing his AIDS diagnosis to his theatre colleagues. He praised the support Charleson received from the theatre community at a time when people living with the disease often faced stigma and a lack of understanding.
“The shame does not lie with the gay people,” Scott said, discussing the need to confront how governments and society responded to the AIDS crisis.
The actor’s comments come amid the success of Heated Rivalry , the hockey romance series that has drawn attention for its portrayal of queer love and relationships. Scott welcomed such stories but argued that joyful representation should exist alongside dramas that confront discrimination, loss and historical suffering.
Elsinore explores the life and legacy of Charleson, who took over the role of Hamlet from Daniel Day-Lewis and continued performing while seriously ill. The film is scheduled for a limited US theatrical release on November 20, 2026.
