title: Govt cuts petrol by 66 paisas  increases diesel by 52 paisas till Oct 12
description: Petrol price decreases to Rs398 3 per litre  while HSD will cost Rs396 24 under daily price mechanism
content:
Petrol price decreases to Rs398.3 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs396.24 under daily price mechanism
The federal government on Friday decreased the price of petrol by 66 paisas per litre, while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by 52 paisas per litre till October 12.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs398.3 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs396.24 per litre from October 10 to October 12.
The latest revision comes a day after the government increased the price of petrol and HSD by Rs2.31 and 78 paisas per litre, respectively, for October 9.
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices fell on Friday as Middle East supply ‌concerns eased after President Donald Trump said the US would not attack Iran before midterm elections next month and talked of "productive" talks to end their war that has disrupted global energy markets.
Trump also teased an upcoming, ​undisclosed announcement on diesel and said he was considering suspending the federal gasoline tax.
Brent crude futures slid 52 cents, 0.50% on Friday to $103.76 a barrel by ⁠12:11 am CDT (1811 GMT). US West Texas Intermediate crude futures fell 22 cents or 0.2% to $91.28.
Trump's Iran pledge, along with China's resumption of product exports, was ​moving prices lower, said PVM Oil Associates analyst Tamas Varga.

title: Troye Sivan reveals emotional reason he asked Ian McKellen to narrate  Party  music video
description: Sivan explained that he sent McKellen a video describing their shared history and asking him to narrate the video
content:
Sivan explained that he sent McKellen a video describing their shared history and asking him to narrate the video
Troye Sivan has revealed the personal story behind recruiting Sir Ian McKellen to narrate his music video for Party , explaining that the Lord of the Rings star was someone he once considered coming out to when he was a teenager.
Speaking about the collaboration, Sivan recalled working with McKellen in a production of Samuel Beckett’s Waiting for Godot in 2010, when he was 14 and approaching his 15th birthday. At the time, the Australian singer was preparing to come out as gay and found hope in being surrounded backstage by older queer people who had built successful lives while embracing their identities.
“I think the first person that I come out to in the world might be Sir Ian McKellen,” Sivan recalled thinking at the time. He wanted to ask the actor for advice but could not find the courage to approach him. The experience nevertheless stayed with him, and years later, he decided to reach out to McKellen for the voiceover.
Sivan explained that he sent McKellen a video describing their shared history and asking him to narrate the music video. Just two days later, he received a video message from the actor, dressed in full Gandalf costume, complete with a long beard. McKellen began the message speaking in the booming voice of his Lord of the Rings character before telling Sivan that he would be delighted to take part.
The collaboration became even more memorable when McKellen used the Lord of the Rings production team and recording equipment in New Zealand to record the voiceover. Sivan said he subsequently contacted the production team to obtain the finished audio files.
McKellen is widely recognised for playing Gandalf in Peter Jackson’s The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit film trilogies. Beyond his celebrated acting career, he has also been a prominent advocate for LGBTQ+ rights, having publicly come out as gay in 1988.
The voiceover opens Sivan’s video for “Party”, released in September 2026 as the second single from his fourth studio album, She’s the Best , which arrived on October 9. Directed by Gordon von Steiner, the video features Sivan as a medieval knight and explores partying as a form of freedom and connection.
Sivan has explained that the video was partly inspired by the idea of queer generations passing knowledge and a sense of belonging to one another. By bringing McKellen into the project, he connected a formative memory from his adolescence with an artistic collaboration that celebrates queer culture and the spaces where people can feel free to express themselves.

title: Shrinking grounds put grassroots cricket under pressure
description: Loss of neighbourhood playing fields is narrowing opportunities for young cricketers across the city
content:
Loss of neighbourhood playing fields is narrowing opportunities for young cricketers across the city
Lahore’s shrinking number of playing fields is squeezing neighbourhood cricket, particularly for young players from low- and middle-income families. As rapid urban development replaces or limits historic grounds such as Minto Park, Baba Ground, Chauburji, Garhi Shahu and Dharampura, children are increasingly turning to streets and other unsafe spaces, weakening the traditional grassroots pathway through which the city’s cricket talent emerges.
Minto Park has historically played a particularly important role in Lahore’s cricketing culture. Once regarded as one of the city’s biggest cricket nurseries, it hosted dozens of club nets. During the tenure of former PCB chairman Gen (retd) Tauqir Zia, around two dozen additional nets were also installed under the Pakistan Cricket Board. Young players from across Lahore would train there under experienced coaches before returning home.
Several players who trained at Minto Park, including Inzamam-ul-Haq, Taufeeq Umar, Nasir Jamshed and Ahmed Shehzad, went on to represent Pakistan at the international level. Over time, however, many of the cricket and other sporting facilities at the park disappeared.
Former ICC Test umpire and Muslim Club president Mian Aslam, along with other figures associated with local cricket, still regard Minto Park as an important part of Lahore’s cricketing history. Aslam said the park had produced seven Pakistan cricket team captains, including Inzamam-ul-Haq.
Baba Ground, Chauburji, Garhi Shahu, Dharampura and several other grounds across Lahore have also traditionally served as important centres for local cricket. Youngsters played alongside teams from local clubs, while children from families with limited financial resources could begin playing without having to pay expensive academy fees.
Read More: Lahore's air quality takes a hit
Local cricket officials say pressure on these grounds has increased with the expansion of the city. In some areas, playing fields have been reduced in size, while sporting activity has been restricted or discontinued altogether. Children now increasingly turn to streets, roads, parking areas and small vacant spaces to play cricket, but residents say these are not safe alternatives because of traffic and other urban activity.
Ali Iqbal, President of Township Gymkhana, said several grounds had been taken over by housing societies and that young cricketers also faced difficulties accessing the grounds that remained. "Building new grounds alone is not enough, and existing facilities need to be restored and equipped with basic amenities."
Iqbal said the shortage of net practice facilities was also affecting the development of young players. A cricketer needed regular net practice, coaching and match experience to improve, he said, adding that a lack of suitable grounds near players’ homes could disrupt that development.
Azhar Zaidi, a leading figure at another historic cricket centre, P&T Gymkhana Club, said the club had produced internationally recognised players including Abdul Razzaq, Imran Nazir, Mohammad Irfan and Aleem Dar. He believed Lahore’s club cricket system had played an important role in developing players who later represented Pakistan at national and international levels.
Zaidi said many young players joining the club came from low- and middle-income families and that P&T Gymkhana tried, within its resources, to provide them with facilities so financial difficulties did not prevent them from developing their talent.
Lahore may still have plenty of cricketing talent, but with grounds disappearing, young players are increasingly running out of places to play. For a city that has long produced national stars from its streets, clubs and neighbourhood grounds, preserving these spaces could be key to keeping its cricketing pipeline alive.

content:
Woah Vicky says her mother has been missing for two weeks as Miami police investigate her disappearance and seek tips
Social media personality Woah Vicky says her mother, Carla, has been missing for about two weeks, and Miami police are investigating after a missing-person report was filed.
Vicky shared a missing-person poster featuring a photo of herself and her mother, saying her family has not heard from Carla in approximately two weeks. The poster says Carla recently travelled by bus from Atlanta to Miami to visit her daughter. It describes the family as “urgently seeking information” about Carla’s whereabouts and safety and asks anyone with information to contact police.
Miami police told TMZ that a missing-person report was generated on Thursday night and that officers are investigating.
Vicky has also spoken about a recent arrest connected to an alleged dispute with her mother. She said she was jailed in Florida about two weeks ago and could not contact Carla after being released. Vicky added that her mother’s phone appeared to be switched off.
TMZ reported that Vicky was arrested in Miami on September 25 on a misdemeanor battery charge. Police had responded to a report from a woman who said she had been assaulted by her daughter and needed help retrieving her belongings.
According to the police report obtained by TMZ, the woman said she had been staying with Vicky for five days while visiting and alleged that Vicky assaulted her by placing her hands around her neck. Police reportedly observed bruises on the woman’s arms.
The report also states that Vicky acknowledged an argument but denied assaulting her mother.
Authorities have not publicly disclosed further details about Carla’s whereabouts. Vicky has appealed for information from the public, and TMZ said it had reached out to her for comment but had not received a response at the time of publication.

title: Madhubala beats TB  but fight for recovery continues
description: Four Paws chief says elephant needs weeks of intensive care as weakened legs  weight loss threaten mobility
content:
Four Paws chief says elephant needs weeks of intensive care as weakened legs, weight loss threaten mobility
Beating tuberculosis has not ended Madhubala’s battle for survival. The 22-year-old elephant at Safari Park is now free of the disease, but its lingering effects have left her physically weak and in need of several more weeks of intensive treatment and rehabilitation.
Speaking to The Express Tribune at Safari Park, Four Paws chief Dr Amir Khalil said Madhubala’s weakened immune system, weight loss and deteriorating physical condition remained major concerns. Her hind legs are particularly weak, while swelling in her limbs and cracks in her toenails have affected her mobility.
"The elephant may even require a crane to help her get back on her feet if she falls," Khalil warned, highlighting the seriousness of her condition.
Madhubala has been experiencing severe health problems for several weeks.
Although a bacterial infection was initially suspected, Khalil said there was no longer evidence of such an infection. However, her declining weight and lack of strength in her hind legs continue to complicate her recovery.
Read: Madhubala goes to Safari Park today
Khalil said medication alone would not be enough to restore Madhubala’s health. Her treatment plan includes nutritional support, physiotherapy and specialised care to rebuild her strength and improve her overall condition.
The elephant will receive multivitamins, minerals and dietary supplements, with particular attention to supporting her liver health. Daily water-based massages and physiotherapy will also be required to improve blood circulation in her leg muscles. Swimming will form another important part of her rehabilitation, allowing her to move her legs while gradually rebuilding muscle strength.
The condition of Madhubala’s legs and toenails remains a particular concern for the veterinary team.
Khalil said that treating elephants presents unique challenges, including the difficulty of administering injections, requiring specialised handling and treatment procedures.
"Pakistani and foreign specialists are working together to improve Madhubala’s condition."
According to Khalil, international experts have been providing guidance remotely over the past several weeks. He also said there were encouraging signs of improvement, but it was too early to make definitive predictions about her recovery. For now, the priority was to stabilise her condition and provide the intensive care she needed.
"Madhubala’s sister, Malika, has also been looking after her and playing an important role in her care," Khalil said.
The Four Paws team is focusing on understanding Madhubala’s medical problems and addressing her immediate needs rather than dwelling on mistakes made in the past.
Khalil said decisions about the next stage of treatment would be made once Madhubala regained the strength to stand and move around independently. Her recovery, he added, would require sustained cooperation among all those involved, alongside appropriate medical treatment, rehabilitation, nutrition and specialised care.

title: Farhan  Maaz star in Pakistan   s win over SL
description: The duo share a 92 run stand as hosts chase 183 with seven balls to spare
content:
The duo share a 92-run stand as hosts chase 183 with seven balls to spare
Skipper Sahibzada Farhan (89) led from the front while Maaz Sadaqat (50) smashed his maiden fifty as Pakistan conquered Sri Lanka by four wickets to take 1-0 lead in the three-match T20I series at the Pindi Stadium on Friday night.
The duo shared 92 runs for the second-wicket stand to enable the hosts chase the 183-run target with seven balls to spare after losing six wickets in the process.
Maaz, who brought in his maiden fifty off 28 balls, smacked three fours and four sixes in his gritty knock.
Although Pakistan lost a few quick wickets at this stage but Farhan stood like a rock and brought his team close to victory before losing his wicket.
Farhan, playing his first match as skipper, hammered 54-ball 89, striking four sixes and ten fours.
Khawaja Nafay made Pakistan home with a brisk seven-ball 12 not out, featuring one six.
Eshan Malinga and Maheesh Theekshana got two wickets each.
Set to chase a seemingly stiff target, Fakhar Zaman and skipper Sahibzada Farhan provided a blistering start to the hosts and brought in their team’s fifty in only five overs.
Medium fast bowler Eshan Malinga eventually gave the breakthrough when he had Fakhar who edged it to keeper Udara after hitting a 13-ball 21 which featured four fours.
Maaz Sadaqat then joined Farhan and in the same over the young left-hander hit Eshan for two glorious sixes and a four to leave his mark as the over yielded 16 runs.
Earlier Sri Lanka’s opener Lahiru Udara smashed a blistering 91 off 55 balls to propel the visitors to 182-8 after opting to bat first.
Udara, who hit his maiden fifty, struck 11 fours and a six, anchoring the Sri Lankan innings after Pakistan made early inroads into the visitors' batting line-up.
Sri Lanka had a poor start when Naseem Shah got rid of captain Kusal Mendis for one in the first over. Mohammad Imran Randhawa, who made his debut, then removed Kamil Mishara for six as Sri Lanka slipped to 18-2 in the fourth over.
Udara steadied the innings alongside Kamindu Mendis, who scored 23 off 18 deliveries, including four boundaries. The pair helped Sri Lanka recover before Saim Ayub dismissed Kamindu to leave the visitors at 78-3.
Imran struck again to remove Sahan Arachchige for one, but Udara continued to attack, reaching his fifty off 32 balls.
Dasun Shanaka added momentum with 18 from 15 deliveries, including two sixes, as he shared a useful partnership with Udara to push Sri Lanka beyond 130.
Shanaka fell to Shadab Khan in the 16th over, but Udara kept the scoreboard moving despite wickets falling at the other end.
Naseem returned to dismiss Dunith Wellalage for five before claiming Udara's wicket on the final ball of the 19th over, ending the opener's outstanding innings.
The dismissal came after Udara had survived a Pakistan review earlier in the innings.
Pakistan's bowlers picked up wickets in the closing overs to restrict Sri Lanka's late charge, although the visitors finished with a competitive total in the end.
Naseem led Pakistan attack as he finished with 3-36 in his quota of four overs. Imran Randhawa impressed on debut with 2-21. Leggie Shadab Khan (1-33) and Saim Ayub (1-17) also contributed with one wicket each.
The second match will be held on Sunday at the same venue.

title: Raye   s family had to make sure she was    still alive    during drug and alcohol struggles
description: I was very distant from my family  who are  my rock now     the singer said
content:
“I was very distant from my family, who are, my rock now,” the singer said
RAYE’s family was so concerned about her wellbeing during a difficult period in 2019 that they had to check whether she was still alive as the singer struggled with substance misuse and alcohol, her sister Amma Keen has revealed.
The British singer, whose real name is Rachel Keen, opened up about the experience during an interview with CBS Sunday Morning on September 27. Reflecting on what she described as a “pretty dark year”, RAYE said she had become distant from her family while dealing with a combination of trauma, frustration and substance misuse.
“I was very distant from my family, who are, my rock now,” the singer said, explaining that the experiences had piled up until the year became “just one blurry mess”.
Her sister Amma, who was living with her at the time, recalled the emotional toll of witnessing RAYE’s struggles. “It was pretty traumatic,” she said. “It would be me that had to double-check she was okay and, yeah, she was still alive frankly.” Amma added that she was only 18 at the time and was deeply worried about her sister.
RAYE also acknowledged that there was a period when she was “just not sober at all”. She credited a Bible verse sent by her grandmother with helping her reassess her life, explaining that her grandmother had been unaware of what she was going through because she had hidden her struggles from her family.
The singer has previously spoken about the difficult experiences that influenced her 2023 debut album, My 21st Century Blues . In 2021, she publicly criticised Polydor Records after years of waiting to release her debut album, eventually parting ways with the label and pursuing an independent career with the support of her family.
Reflecting on her changing relationship with alcohol and her creative process in a February 2026 interview with ELLE , RAYE said she had developed greater discipline and embraced abstinence. Although she still occasionally drinks wine, she explained that she no longer uses alcohol to numb or escape her feelings.
The four-time Grammy nominee is now approaching her next album with a different outlook, saying she prefers the more grounded version of herself she has become. Her journey has also brought her closer to her family, whom she now describes as the foundation of trust and safety in her life.

Paramount+ has also released first-look images from the upcoming series, offering an early glimpse at the new addition to the Avatar universe.

title: Nearly 50 000 women  girls killed or severely injured in Gaza since October 2023  UN Women
description: UN Women urged full implementation of the ceasefire  respect for international law and accountability for violations
content:
Urges full implementation of the ceasefire, respect for international law and accountability for violations
Nearly 50,000 women and girls have been killed or severely injured in Gaza since October 2023, equivalent to one in every 21 women and girls in the enclave, UN Women said on Friday.
"More than 38,000 killed and 11,700 left with injuries so severe that they now live with lifelong disabilities," Sofia Calltorp, UN Women's chief of humanitarian action, told reporters in Geneva.
She said most casualties occurred during the first two years of the war, but violence has continued despite the ceasefire agreement entering into effect a year ago, with 277 women and girls killed since October 2025.
Nearly 50,000 women and girls in #Gaza have been killed or severely injured in the past three years. Killings continue despite the ceasefire. @UN_Women calls for full ceasefire implementation, international law upheld and protection #ForAllWomenAndGirls https://t.co/KqPeAOK8RA pic.twitter.com/7NrHyM6qYg
Nearly one million women and girls have been forced from their homes, while almost all remain displaced, many living in tents or among the ruins of their homes, she said.
Read More: Israel strikes Gaza on October 7 anniversary, at least two dead: officials
Calltorp also warned that the number of female-headed households has doubled, with women now heading one in four households in Gaza.
Meanwhile, funding cuts have severely weakened women's organisations, with 13 of 14 surveyed reporting they can no longer meet growing needs.
All surveyed organisations reported increases in gender-based violence, poverty and mental health distress since 2025, while 13 reported rising child marriage.
UN Women called for full implementation of the ceasefire, respect for international law and accountability for violations.
"What we have found is a horrific amount of collective suffering, an immense amount of pain, and a level of resilience and strength that no woman should have to bear," Calltorp said.

Keri Russell has explained why she and longtime partner Matthew Rhys have no plans to get married, revealing that she considers marriage “antiquated” and believes their commitment to each other does not require a wedding.
The Diplomat actress discussed her relationship with Rhys during an appearance on Chelsea Handler’s Dear Chelsea podcast on October 8. Russell, 50, said she had already been married once and did not feel the need to do it again, particularly in a society where marriage is no longer necessary for the same practical reasons it once was.
“I’ve had a big party. I get to dress up all the time,” Russell said, adding that she did not need to change her surname. She also explained her relaxed approach to relationships, saying, “If you want to be here, be here. If you don’t, that’s cool too.”
Handler said she found long-term relationships without marriage appealing because partners were not guaranteed to stay together, prompting Russell to agree that couples still had to make an effort to maintain their relationship.
The actress also pointed out that she and Rhys have a lasting connection through their family. “P.S., we have kids, so that’s forever. To me, it’s antiquated,” she said.
Russell and Rhys, 51, have been romantically linked since late 2013 after meeting again on the set of The Americans , where they played married KGB spies Elizabeth and Philip Jennings. The pair share a son, Sam, 10. Russell also has two children, River, 19, and Willa, 13, from her previous marriage to carpenter Shane Deary.
Russell and Deary married in 2007 and separated in 2013, with their divorce finalised the following year. She and Rhys have continued their relationship for more than a decade while keeping much of their private life away from the spotlight.

title: 26 women  4 children killed in Sudan RSF drone strike  official  witnesses
description: An attack struck Wad al Mahi governorate in Sudan s Blue Nile state  near the Ethiopian border
content:
An attack struck Wad al-Mahi governorate in Sudan's Blue Nile state, near the Ethiopian border
A drone strike launched by Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces killed 26 women and four children on Friday, an official and eyewitnesses told AFP.
The attack occurred in the Wad al-Mahi governorate of Blue Nile state, near Sudan's southeastern border with Ethiopia, according to Wad al-Mahi governor Mahgoub al-Sheikh.
The latest frontline in Sudan's war between the regular army and the RSF is the border region with Ethiopia, where an internal conflict is threatening to escalate into a regional war.
"We buried 26 women and four children," said an eyewitness in a displacement camp in Abu Shendi.
Just outside the camp is an informal gold mine, where women earn a daily wage using chemicals and their bare hands to clear gold nuggets from clumps of earth the men have extracted.
The victims included "young girls who work with their families in refining the gold", another eyewitness said.
Since the war broke out in April 2023, it has killed more than 200,000 people, aid workers estimate, and created the world's largest hunger and displacement crises.

Keri Russell has shared details of her 50th birthday celebration, revealing why she eventually had to leave the party and put herself to bed.

Russell described the celebration as involving “excessive drinking” and admitted that the festivities became challenging because she prefers going to bed early.
Her actual birthday fell on the final day of the trip, when the group enjoyed a celebratory dinner. However, the actress eventually decided she needed to rest.
“I think I’m gonna lay down for a minute,” Russell recalled telling her friends before going upstairs. She added that she vomited before putting herself to bed, while her friends sent her a video of themselves singing “Happy Birthday”.
Despite the eventful celebration, Russell said she was enjoying turning 50. When host Jimmy Fallon asked about entering the new decade, she replied, “It’s good. 50’s good.”
Russell, who has been with Rhys for years, was filming The Diplomat during the birthday trip. The political drama follows Kate Wyler, a US diplomat navigating international crises and complicated personal relationships.

title: Explainer  Why India s tens of millions of voter deletions have led to widespread protests
description: Opposition parties and youth activists demand India s election chief resign amid protests
content:
Opposition parties and youth activists demand India's election chief resign amid protests
India's verification exercise of its nearly one billion voters has sparked protests across the country, with opposition parties alleging the removal of 130 million names from electoral rolls has unfairly benefited Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party.
Opposition parties and the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party are demanding the ouster of Election Commission chief Gyanesh Kumar and have vowed a huge protest in the capital Delhi on Saturday.
Election Commission data cited by Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party shows that about 130 million names, more than the population of Japan, have been deleted from electoral rolls during the verification exercise, including 63 million people who had relocated and 30 million who could not be traced.
The BJP and the commission deny allegations of manipulation, although opposition parties say Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party, are disproportionately impacted by the deletions.
They say the deletions have affected the outcome of some recent state elections that the BJP won, and have cast a shadow on the electoral process in the world's biggest democracy. The BJP says Modi's popularity and India's economic growth are some reasons for its electoral dominance.
Here are some details about the voter verification drive, which has become one of the biggest political controversies of Modi's 12-year tenure ahead of crucial state elections starting early next year.
Supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party youth movement, farmers' groups and opposition parties are set to protest in Delhi on Saturday, demanding the resignation of Kumar. Police say they have not granted permission, and CJP has reported preemptive detentions of some protest leaders.
Sporadic protests have been going on across India since a report by the Indian Express newspaper in late September said Kumar's two deputies raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems.
The commission says differing views are normal in internal deliberations, and has denied favouring any party.
Read More: At UN, Pakistan says India provides 'active support' to Taliban, backs terrorist groups
Modi's BJP has accused groups opposed to it of trying to undermine the country's democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.
At least seven Indian states will hold elections next year, including BJP-ruled Uttar Pradesh, the most populous and considered a bellwether state in national politics. Verification in Uttar Pradesh began in October 2025 and resulted in 13% of names being deleted, according to local media reports.
Voters with their names missing need to prove their credentials before being enrolled, and many have complained about the process.
Verifying a billion voters: The controversy
India started verification of its voter rolls last year ahead of elections in the eastern state of Bihar, ruled by a BJP coalition. The review has now covered the majority of Indian states.
While voter roll revisions are routine, this round became controversial after large numbers of voters in states such as Bihar and West Bengal found their names missing from electoral rolls and were unable to cast ballots. The BJP won power in West Bengal for the first time in May.
Citing Election Commission data, the BJP says that of the 130 million names deleted from voter lists, 28 million are dead, 63 million have relocated, 10 million are duplicates and 30 million could not be traced by officials.
Opposition parties, including Congress, have accused Kumar of bias and alleged that the process benefits the BJP; the Election Commission and the party deny.
The Indian Express story said the two deputies to the election commissioner had expressed concerns to Kumar at least 14 times in 10 months, but those concerns were not taken into consideration. The Election Commission said all its decisions were lawful.
The report prompted opposition leaders and members of the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party, which in July forced the education minister to quit after weeks of protest, to launch nationwide demonstrations.
What happens to voters removed from the rolls?
The Election Commission says names are removed only when a voter has died, is mentioned more than once on the rolls, has moved to another region or is untraceable. Officers are required to record detailed reasons why a voter is deleted.
People whose names do not appear in draft rolls can request inclusion before final voter lists are published and also appeal if such requests are denied. Voters excluded from final rolls can also challenge the decision.
To participate in future elections, excluded voters must succeed in their appeals or apply for fresh registration.
Opposition parties argue that arbitrary deletions and lengthy appeals prevented millions in Bihar and West Bengal from voting and could be used as a weapon in future elections.
The Election Commission has defended itself against allegations of political bias, including at a rare press conference by Kumar last year, when he asked the opposition to submit their allegations under oath.
Kumar has had a difficult relationship with opposition parties since taking over as the election body chief in February 2025. Opposition lawmakers put forward a motion to have him removed earlier this year, but it was rejected by parliament.
A 2023 law passed by Modi's government grants the election commission chief immunity from prosecution for acts done in an official capacity.
Amid the recent backlash, the Election Commission announced revisions to the verification process, including home visits by officials to collect documents and an extension of the deadline for final verification in some states.

Jessica Biel returns to films after nine years with Matchbox the Movie, revealing why her Apple TV comeback amazed her
Jessica Biel has returned to the big screen after more than nine years away from films, admitting that the length of her break came as a surprise.
The 44-year-old actress stars alongside John Cena in Matchbox the Movie , an action-adventure film released on Apple TV on October 9. Speaking to PEOPLE at a press event in New York City, Biel said she had not realised how long it had been since her last film role.
“That’s weird to me,” Biel said. “I didn’t even know it was a return.” She explained that she had continued working creatively but had focused on television projects rather than films. Realising the length of her movie hiatus “kind of blew my mind”, she added.
Biel's recent television credits include The Better Sister in 2025 and Candy in 2022. In Matchbox the Movie , she plays Aimee, an emergency medical technician who enjoys amateur race-car driving.
The film follows a group of childhood friends whose lives change when Sean, played by Cena, returns to their hometown as an undercover CIA agent. The group becomes caught up in an international pursuit to save the world.
Biel said the script, director Sam Hargrave and cast influenced her decision to join the project. She was also drawn to its mix of action, comedy, friendship and romance. The film marks her first on-screen collaboration with Cena, who plays her love interest.
Preparing for the role also required Biel to undergo performance-driving training. She performed driving sequences involving several vehicles, including an ambulance, a Volkswagen van and a 1968 Ford Mustang Fastback.
The actress, who shares two sons with husband Justin Timberlake, said family responsibilities have influenced her choice of acting projects. She added that the timing of her return felt right and helped her regain confidence in her physical abilities.
Matchbox the Movie began streaming on Apple TV on October 9, 2026.

Freeman is best known for playing Dr John Watson in Sherlock , opposite Benedict Cumberbatch, as well as Bilbo Baggins in The Hobbit trilogy. He first gained widespread recognition as Tim Canterbury in the original British version of The Office and has since appeared in several major film and television productions.
Grand: The Autobiography of Gromit promises to explore the character’s life alongside Wallace, including his views on garden gnomes, his adventures and other previously untold stories. The audiobook is scheduled for release on October 22, 2026, with the printed hardback edition due on November 24.

title: US imposes sanctions on ICC hours after former judge wins Nobel Peace Prize
description: UN secretary general warns US move could deal  a serious blow  to efforts to ensure accountability for grave crimes
content:
UN secretary general warns US move could deal 'a serious blow' to efforts to ensure accountability for grave crimes
US President Donald Trump's ​administration imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Friday, hours after one of its former judges won the Nobel Peace Prize , putting Washington on ‌a diplomatic collision course with European allies.
The ICC's deputy prosecutor, Nazhat Shameem Khan, condemned the sanctions and said they would not halt the tribunal's work.
The Trump administration has long been hostile to the court founded in 2002 to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide , and has previously imposed sanctions on its prosecutors and judges. Friday's move would go far further by potentially punishing companies that provide services to the ​court itself.
Read : Trump administration prepares sanctions against International Criminal Court, sources say
"President Trump will never allow the International Criminal Court to prosecute Americans," Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement, first published by Reuters .
"That is ​why, today, the United States is sanctioning the International Criminal Court. We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off its resources and crippling its ability to operate."
Today, the Trump Administration is sanctioning the ICC. This action should encourage our Allies within the Court to work for solutions to end this threat to U.S. sovereignty forever. pic.twitter.com/D86dCqLUaZ
ICC Deputy Prosecutor Khan told Reuters the sanctions "must be condemned".
"The sanctions are intended to undermine the rule of law internationally and the work ​that an independent judicial institution is doing," Khan said. "Our work will continue across all our situations, our investigations and our prosecutions."
US sanctions on the ICC “must be condemned” as they intend to undermine rule of law internationally and will not stop the court’s investigations and prosecutions across all situations, says ICC deputy prosecutor Nazhat Shameem Khan pic.twitter.com/fDaXrcDL88
Washington has denounced the ICC over arrest warrants issued for Israeli officials, including ​Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and a past investigation into actions of US soldiers in Afghanistan, which the ICC has since closed.
The court counts 125 countries as member states, including all EU countries and all members of the NATO alliance apart from the United States and Turkiye. It has received strong public backing in the past from member countries including major US allies, and is based in the Netherlands, an EU and ​NATO member.
Navi Pillay, the South African jurist who won the Nobel Peace Prize earlier on Friday, had served as a judge on the ICC's Appeals Chamber from 2003-2008. The prize committee ​said in its citation that in naming her it had sought to "issue a reminder" at a time when "judges and institutions of international law are under political attack".
Read More : Navi Pillay: Nobel laureate who led UN inquiry that found genocide in Gaza
"An international legal system in which war criminals are ‌held to account ⁠, and the victims of abuse see justice served is a precondition for a peaceful world," the prize committee said.
Rubio said the sanctions had been structured to give the court and its member states an opportunity to address US concerns.
Washington immediately allowed some exemptions. Shortly after the sanctions were announced, the US Treasury issued four general licenses, which would allow some transactions for ICC telecommunications, software and pension payments, and transactions linked to ICC detainees.
US expects allies to 'rein in the court'
US sanctions typically bar all US-based companies from any work with a sanctioned organisation, ​forcing banks to shut accounts, insurers to end ​coverage and software companies to halt ⁠cooperation.
The Trump administration previously imposed targeted sanctions on court officials during his first term, which were rescinded under President Joe Biden. Washington announced new sanctions just days after Trump returned to office in January 2025.
Court officials have been preparing for months for the prospect of sanctions ​on the court itself, shifting office computers from Microsoft software to open-source equivalents and making new arrangements for banking and health insurance.
The court's registrar, ​Osvaldo Zavala Giler, called ⁠earlier this week for the EU to be prepared to use a so-called "blocking mechanism" that lets it shield European countries from the extraterritorial effects of sanctions.
In his statement, Rubio said the United States had delayed its sanctions hoping that the ICC and the countries party to its founding Rome Statute would address US concerns, but they had failed to do so.
The Trump administration imposed sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC), potentially cutting off its banking, insurance and software services. The move comes amid U.S. anger over ICC arrest warrants for Israeli officials, including Netanyahu, and a previous… pic.twitter.com/CJfJMbxbwL
"Either the ICC will ⁠end its ​threats, or we will end the ICC. We expect our allies, many of whom are part of the ​ICC and that rely on American service members for their defence, to rein in the court," Rubio said.
"We have structured this action to provide an opportunity for States Parties to negotiate and present a solution to address our ​concerns. If these efforts do not bear fruit, we will continue to adjust accordingly," Rubio said.
UN chief condemns sanctions against ICC, warns of 'serious blow' to justice
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned US sanctions against the ICC on Friday, warning that the measures could undermine its work and deal "a serious blow" to international efforts to ensure accountability for grave crimes.
"Today's decision marks a serious blow to our collective pursuit of international criminal justice, of which the ICC is a key pillar. Accountability for international crimes and delivery of justice to victims are central to our global commitment to peace, security, human rights and fundamental freedoms," said a statement issued by his spokesperson, Stephane Dujarric.
UN Secretary-General @antonioguterres condemns the announcement of the imposition by the United States of sanctions against the International Criminal Court as an institution. Full statement: https://t.co/4tZzdbfcsz pic.twitter.com/hGVDlEII3y
Guterres was "deeply alarmed" by the expected impact of the sanctions on the court as a whole, particularly its ability to carry out its mandate, the statement said.
The UN chief also reiterated his support for the court's independence and called on countries to uphold their obligations under international law.
US sanctions draw opposition as countries warn of impact on its work
Meanwhile, six European countries, Canada and Japan, expressed regret over the US announcement of sanctions against the ICC, warning that the measures could significantly affect its operations, staff and their families.
In a joint statement, the foreign ministers of Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, the Netherlands and the UK, along with their Canadian and Japanese counterparts, said they "strongly disagree" with Washington's announcement.
"We, the undersigned States Parties to the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court (ICC), reaffirm our continued and unwavering support for the independence, impartiality, and integrity of the ICC," the statement said.
Foreign ministers of Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan, Netherlands and UK issue joint statement on ICC: - We reaffirm our continued and unwavering support for independence, impartiality, and integrity of ICC - We regret and strongly disagree with announcement of… pic.twitter.com/WL1O4gEkjp
The ministers welcomed the court's preparations to respond to potential sanctions, saying the measures would help it continue carrying out its mandate under the Rome Statute.
"Nevertheless, if put into effect, these sanctions will have a significant impact on the Court's work, its dedicated staff and their families," they warned.
The eight countries also pledged to pursue "constructive and inclusive dialogue" with countries that were not parties to the Rome Statute ahead of the Assembly of States Parties scheduled for December.
"We will continue to work together to support the Court's vital work, uphold the rules-based international system, and advance accountability," the statement said.

title: China vows to curb tech bubbles  keep AI risks in check
description: China warned against reckless tech investment as it boosts self reliance amid rivalry with the US
content:
China warned against reckless tech investment as it boosts self-reliance amid rivalry with the US
China will tighten oversight of its drive into advanced technology, seeking to curb investment bubbles while ensuring artificial intelligence remains "safe, reliable and controllable", according to policy guidelines issued on Friday.
As Beijing ramps up support for high-tech manufacturing and strategic industries to boost technological self-sufficiency amid rivalry with the US, the guidelines warned against blind investment and excessive expansion into emerging sectors.
"Developing new productive forces is an inherent requirement and an important focus for promoting high-quality development," Xinhua cited the guidelines, issued by the ruling Communist Party and the cabinet, as saying.
President Xi Jinping introduced the term "new productive forces" in 2023, emphasising scientific research, technological breakthroughs and industrial upgrading across China's manufacturing base.
The guidelines said China would seek breakthroughs in AI theory and core technologies, strengthen the supply of computing power, algorithms and data, and establish national pilot bases for industrial AI applications. They also called for technology monitoring, risk-warning and emergency-response systems to ensure AI remains "safe, reliable and controllable".
Read More: Anthropic bans 'cruel' behaviour against its Claude AI
China will fully implement its "AI Plus" initiative, using AI to upgrade traditional industries and accelerate the rollout of intelligent products, including connected new-energy vehicles, AI-enabled phones and computers, and humanoid robots, the document said.
The guidelines also pledged to strengthen "original and disruptive" innovation in core technologies and to use China's state-led "new nationwide system" to speed the development and deployment of landmark products.
At the same time, officials were told to prioritise the real economy and avoid bubbles, industrial hollowing-out, blind investment and "swarm-like" rushes into high-tech sectors.
China will "strictly prohibit the illegal or improper abuse of policies in the name of developing new productive forces", the guidelines said, adding that officials responsible for major losses caused by blind investment would be held accountable.
The document also called for the healthy and orderly development of the low-altitude economy — businesses built around civilian drones, air taxis, small aircraft and related services — while ensuring safety.

content:
Starlink’s four-year launch delay in India has fuelled online clashes over business influence and regulation
India’s telecom minister said on Friday the country does not allow monopolies in any sector, pushing back after Elon Musk suggested billionaire Mukesh Ambani was using political influence to block Starlink’s launch in the country.
"India does not allow a monopoly in any sector," telecom minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said at a media briefing on Friday, addressing Musk’s remarks.
Musk’s SpaceX unit is seeking entry into a telecom market with more than a billion internet users, currently dominated by the mobile networks of Ambani’s Reliance Jio and Sunil Mittal’s Bharti Airtel.
"Is Ambani the real boss of India?" Musk wrote on X on Thursday, questioning why Starlink still lacked a licence despite what he said were years of compliance with Indian requirements. He provided no evidence against Ambani.
Starlink is licensed in over 165 countries and has spent five years complying with every single law and requirement of the government of India, so why still no license? Is Ambani the real boss of India? https://t.co/KUSgfJRynZ
Ambani’s Reliance Jio did not respond to a request for comment on Musk’s remarks.
A four-year wait to launch Starlink’s satellite internet services in India has sparked heated exchanges online over business influence and regulatory delays, with Musk targeting Ambani and the political opposition joining the row.
While Starlink has already secured a licence to operate in India , a commercial launch still requires it to meet security compliance conditions and receive a spectrum assignment.
The government said on Thursday that all three licensed satellite operators, including Starlink, were at broadly the same regulatory stage, calling suggestions of an unfair or discriminatory process "baseless and misconceived".

Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry Friday said that Pakistan’s future depends on the talent, knowledge and hard work of its youth. #TariqFazalChaudhry #PakistanYouth #YouthEmpowerment pic.twitter.com/Q0LDdwRs15

title: Kardashians face hypocrisy backlash over AI generated    The Kardashians    season 8 intro
description: The opening features digital versions of the family in luxury destinations before their doubles begin to glitch
content:
The opening features digital versions of the family in luxury destinations before their doubles begin to glitch
The Kardashian family has faced criticism over an AI generated opening sequence for season eight of The Kardashians , with viewers questioning the message behind a skit that appears to reject artificial intelligence after using it to create the footage.
The Hulu reality series returned on October 8, 2026, with an elaborate introduction showing digital versions of the family members enjoying luxurious trips around the world. Kris Jenner appears on a yacht in St Tropez, while Kourtney Kardashian and Travis Barker explore Japan. Khloé Kardashian goes on safari in Kenya, Kendall and Kylie Jenner party in Versailles, and Kim Kardashian visits Switzerland.
The sequence becomes increasingly surreal when the digital family reunites in Calabasas. Their appearances begin to glitch, with Khloé developing an oversized eye, Kim experiencing an unusual change to her ear and Kourtney’s face resembling a thumb.
The real family eventually confronts its artificial counterparts. When the digital Kris suggests AI could make filming easier by removing scheduling conflicts and the need for glam, the real Kris rejects the idea that technology could replace them.
Khloé then switches off the digital family, bringing the sequence to a close with the message, “The Kardashians: AI Could Never.”
However, the intended joke did not convince everyone. Some viewers criticised the family for using AI to deliver an apparently anti AI message. Others questioned the environmental cost of generating the video and argued that the point could have been made without using the technology.
Khloé responded to the criticism by sharing the opening on Instagram and urging viewers to watch until the end. She said comments from people who had only watched the first few seconds were frustrating.
The disagreement highlights the challenge of using controversial technology to make a point about its limitations. While the sequence presents AI as something that cannot replace the real family, some viewers felt the production itself undermined that message.

The Alejandro G. Iñárritu satire earned an $8m domestic opening and a C+ CinemaScore
Anne Hathaway has praised Tom Cruise’s latest film, Digger , calling the satirical comedy brilliant despite its disappointing box office debut.
The Verity star shared her reaction on Letterboxd, where she gave the film five stars in what was reported to be her first review on the platform. Hathaway praised the movie’s ambition, humour and unconventional approach, encouraging audiences to experience it before forming their own opinions.
“I loved this brilliant movie. It’s smart and trippy and aggressive and funny and ambitious,” Hathaway wrote . “It’s worth making the time see and decide for yourself what you make of it. For me? 10/10.”
Her enthusiastic response arrives as Digger faces questions about its commercial performance. The film opened in cinemas to an estimated $8m domestic debut and a $20m global start, while receiving a C+ CinemaScore.
According to Deadline , the production could lose around $150m, although the reported figure represents an estimate rather than a confirmed final financial result.
Cruise stars as Digger Rockwell, an ageing oil magnate whose drilling activities trigger an ecological disaster. The film was written and directed by Alejandro G. Iñárritu, known for films including Birdman and The Revenant .
Its ensemble cast includes Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, Sandra Hüller, Michael Stuhlbarg, Jesse Plemons, Emma D’Arcy, Burn Gorman and Sophie Wilde.
Despite the early financial concerns, Cruise has publicly expressed pride in the project. The actor, who also produced the film, thanked the cast and crew for their work and described the experience of making it as unforgettable.
Hathaway’s review adds a prominent celebrity endorsement to the conversation surrounding the release. Her response does not change the film’s box office figures, but it highlights the difference between commercial performance and individual reactions to a movie.
Rather than presenting her rating as a universal verdict, Hathaway encouraged viewers to see Digger and decide what they think for themselves. Her comments offer a positive counterpoint to the scrutiny surrounding the film’s opening results.

content:
Director Alex Gibney spent four years making the film, which opens in cinemas on October 16
Elon Musk’s former romantic partners offer personal accounts of their relationships with the billionaire in Musk , a four hour documentary directed by Alex Gibney that examines his private life, business career and influence on American society.
The film, which screens at the MILL VALLEY FILM FESTIVAL before its nationwide theatrical release on October 16, draws on interviews with people who have known or worked with Musk. According to SFGATE , among its most compelling contributors are Justine Musk, his former wife, and Ashley St Clair, who has publicly said she has a child with him.
Justine, the mother of Musk’s first five children, discusses their relationship and describes experiences she says shaped her understanding of emotional manipulation. She also addresses the death of their first child and Musk’s treatment of their transgender daughter, Vivian Jenna Wilson.
St Clair, a conservative influencer, shares details of her early communications with Musk, including personal messages displayed in the documentary. The film examines their relationship and her decision to speak publicly. She reportedly declined a $40m nondisclosure agreement, although the circumstances and terms surrounding that reported offer have not been independently established here.
Musk did not participate in the documentary. Gibney instead uses archival footage and an artificial intelligence generated avatar designed to represent the technology executive.
The director spent four years developing the project. It follows Musk’s career from early ventures such as Zip2 and X.com to SpaceX, Tesla, Starlink, X and xAI. Contributors include LinkedIn co founder Reid Hoffman, neuroscientist Sam Harris and journalists Kara Swisher and Zoë Schiffer.
The documentary takes a critical view of Musk’s business record and political influence, questioning his public image and examining his companies’ relationships with government funding and regulation. These assessments represent the film’s arguments rather than undisputed findings.
Musk has threatened legal action over the documentary, according to SFGATE , but the publication reported that no defamation lawsuit had been filed at the time of its review.
The film presents a sweeping portrait of a figure whose business decisions and public interventions continue to attract intense scrutiny.

title: Ben Affleck reveals why he was banned from Instagram twice

content:
Ben Affleck reveals he was banned from Instagram twice for impersonating himself and why he avoids social media
Ben Affleck has revealed that he was banned from Instagram twice for impersonating himself, explaining why he no longer uses social media.
In an interview with Variety published on October 7, the 54-year-old actor said he would make a “terrible influencer” and recalled having just six followers on the platform, including his three children and some of their friends.
“I got banned from Instagram twice for impersonating myself,” Affleck said. He added that his account was mainly an excuse to check his children’s social media accounts.
The actor shares three children, Violet, 20, Seraphina, 17, and Samuel, 13, with his ex-wife Jennifer Garner.
Affleck also explained why he prefers to keep his personal life private rather than maintain an active social media presence. He said that, in the past, people could speak and act without everything becoming part of a permanent public record.
Reflecting on his approach to fame, Affleck said he valued having experienced much of his life away from public scrutiny. He also argued that actors should maintain a certain distance from their audiences.
Citing actors Daniel Day-Lewis, Meryl Streep, Viola Davis and Denzel Washington, he explained that seeing details of their everyday lives would not make him appreciate their films more.
Despite his reluctance to embrace social media, Affleck has recently appeared in TikTok videos with his Animals co-star Kerry Washington to promote their upcoming Netflix film.
In one video, Washington asks Affleck to make a TikTok, but he shakes his head and walks away. She later shared another promotional clip featuring a reference to the famous line “How do you like them apples?”
Animals , directed by Affleck and starring Washington, follows a mayoral candidate and his wife who resort to extreme measures to secure their kidnapped son's ransom. The film is scheduled to arrive on Netflix and in select cinemas on October 9, 2026.

title: Fact check  Viral visuals do not show Houthi attack on Riyadh s King Khalid Airport
description: Viral video shows false video and AI generated images
content:
Viral video shows false video and AI generated images
Several people have been sharing visuals on multiple social media platforms since October 8, 2026, allegedly showing the Houthi attack and its aftermath at Riyadh’s King Khalid Airport. However, the visuals are old and AI-generated.
The latest Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia came amid a renewed escalation in the conflict in Yemen. Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s internationally recognised government launched a military campaign to push Houthi forces away from the strategically important Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key maritime route connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.
The Houthis responded with missile and drone attacks targeting Saudi territory, including airports, military installations and oil infrastructure. The renewed fighting has intensified after years of intermittent conflict and a period of relative calm following a truce in 2022.
On Oct 8, Yemen’s Houthi movement claimed that it had launched a ballistic missile towards King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, saying it had struck its intended target and disrupted air traffic. Saudi Arabia’s Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles, including two heading towards Riyadh and another directed towards Khamis Mushait.
Saudi civil defence authorities also reported material damage to a kindergarten and medical clinic complex in Riyadh from falling missile debris. The attacks disrupted air travel, with Air India cancelling flights to and from Riyadh and Lufthansa suspending flights to the Saudi capital, with the authorities confirming three deaths in attacks on the airports in Riyadh and Abha
On Oct 8, an account shared a video on X of an alleged missile strike on a Saudi aeroplane at Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport with the following caption: “Urgent. New video footage of the moment King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh was targeted.”
A pro-Russian account also shared the same video on X, with a similar caption on Oct 9, gaining 3.6m views.
Similarly, another account on X shared the same video the same day with the following caption: “Breaking: New footage has emerged showing the moment King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh was targeted amid a fresh Houthi-claimed ballistic missile attack.”
Subsequently, the same video was also shared by other accounts on X, as can be seen here , here , here , here , here , here , and here , collectively gaining 29,238 views.
Similarly, another video showed the aftermath of the attack with visuals of burnt planes, with several ground crew members wearing bright yellow high-visibility vests.
On Oct 8, a Palestine-based account, based on its about section, shared the video with the following caption:
“A new crazy video emerges from King Khalid Airport in Riyadh, showing several Saudi civilian aircraft burning on the airport grounds following the Yemeni missile strike. What appears in the video indicates that the scale of the Yemeni strike is much larger than previously believed, as the number of destroyed and burning aircraft seems extremely high, and perhaps what remains hidden is even greater. And most importantly, these scenes reveal only a portion of the airport, and it cannot be ruled out that the damage inflicted on other areas that have not yet been filmed is far greater than what we are seeing. Ansar Allah is determined to impose a comprehensive air blockade on Saudi Arabia, and what we are witnessing in terms of targeting airports and civilian aircraft points to the scale of escalation they seek to enforce. Unprecedented madness.”
A pro-Iranian user shared the same video on X with the caption that translates to: “A transport plane caught fire at Riyadh Airport following a new missile strike.”
A pro-Houthi account, based on its profile picture, shared the same video with a similar caption on X, attracting 670,000 views.
Iranian mainstream media outlet Fars News also shared the same video in its news article on Oct 9 with a title which translates to: “Ansarullah’s fatal attack on Saudi airport.”
Another user who claims to be a journalist from the United Kingdom in their bio on X also shared the same video with the title: “Watch: new footage shows several Saudi aircraft struck & damaged by Ansar Allah strike at King Khalid International Airport.
The video with a similar claim was further shared by several other users on social media platforms Facebook , Instagram and X, as can be seen here , here , here , here , here , here , here , and here ; collectively accumulating 67,000 views.
A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to its virality and keen public interest in the ongoing conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, particularly following reports of the latest attack on King Khalid Airport.
A reverse image search yielded a video shared on X on May 29, 2017. The post was captioned, “A ground services vehicle fire next to one of Saudi airline aircraft caused the front section of its A320-model plane to catch fire.”
The post featured the same footage as the viral video.
احتراق معدة للخدمات الارضيّة بجانب احدى طائرات #الخطوط_السعودية تسببت في احتراق مقدمة طائرتها من طراز #A320 pic.twitter.com/83825y37fH
Further investigation led to a news report published by Airkule , a Turkish local digital media outlet, on May 29, 2017, with the headline “Fire in power unit causes panic.”
According to the report, a fire in an external power unit at Jeddah airport caused panic. Although firefighters extinguished the blaze, soot was left on the radar systems of several aircraft. The report contains the same visual as that of the viral video.
A keyword search using relevant terms such as “A320 aircraft”, “Jeddah airport” and “fire” revealed a report published by Saudi news outlet Saudi Gazette on May 30, 2017, titled “Small fire at Jeddah airport.”
According to the report, Civil Defence personnel extinguished a small fire near the nose of a Saudi Arabian Airlines A320 aircraft at Jeddah’s King Abdul Aziz International Airport. The fire reportedly originated in ground service machinery and spread to a nearby parked aircraft. Authorities subsequently ordered an investigation to determine the cause of the incident.
For the second video, a keyword search yielded no media reports from any credible Saudi, international, or Yemeni news outlets covering the airport attack with the same clip.
A visual examination revealed several discrepancies. At the 1-second mark, the explosion erupts instantaneously after the rocket attack without any structural damage to the airport preceding it.
Despite a massive blast occurring between the 2-5 second mark, the airport shuttle bus, stair trucks, and service vehicles close to the plane remain the same, without any damage.
The video was subsequently analysed using AI-detection tools. Isgen AI Video Detector flagged the visual as 100 per cent doctored, while Is Fake AI flagged it as 79pc AI-generated.
The claim that viral visuals show the Houthi attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid Airport in Riyadh is false.
The first video is old from 2017 and shows an incident at Jeddah airport. Meanwhile, the second video is AI-generated.

title: Joe Manganiello challenges Sof  a Vergara   s account of their divorce in new memoir
description: The actor says emergency surgery and years without a clear diagnosis changed his outlook on parenthood
content:
The actor says emergency surgery and years without a clear diagnosis changed his outlook on parenthood
Joe Manganiello has shared his account of the breakdown of his marriage to Sofía Vergara, saying a prolonged health battle changed his decision about becoming a father.
In his forthcoming memoir, Bloodlines , the actor describes experiencing a mysterious illness for seven years and fearing that it could kill him. His account offers a different perspective on the couple’s separation, which they announced in July 2023 before their divorce was finalised in 2024.
Vergara previously cited their differing views on having children as a factor in the relationship ending. Manganiello, however, says the circumstances were more complicated, with his health concerns playing a significant role in his thinking about parenthood.
According to his memoir, the couple explored fertility options, including IVF attempts and the possibility of using an egg donor. Manganiello says he eventually became reluctant to pursue having a child because he feared he might not survive his illness.
The actor explains that he worried about leaving Vergara to raise a child alone, particularly if the child was not biologically hers. His account presents the decision as one shaped by uncertainty about his future rather than simply a disagreement about whether to have children.
Manganiello says his health problems began not long after the couple married in 2015. He describes symptoms including severe abdominal pain, rashes, headaches and extreme fatigue.
In 2016, he underwent emergency surgery that resulted in part of his intestine being removed. However, his medical problems reportedly continued for years without a clear diagnosis, leaving him concerned about what might happen next.
The memoir recounts how living with prolonged illness affected his outlook and placed emotional pressure on the marriage. Manganiello’s comments do not erase Vergara’s previously stated perspective, but provide his explanation of how the couple’s plans for a family changed.
The former couple married in November 2015 and confirmed their separation eight years later. Their divorce was finalised in 2024.
Through Bloodlines , Manganiello revisits the personal fears and difficult decisions that shaped this period of his life.

title: Djokovic crashes out of Shanghai Masters
description: Serbian suffers straight sets defeat to Hubert Hurkacz
content:
Serbian suffers straight-sets defeat to Hubert Hurkacz
Novak Djokovic went down in straight sets to Hubert Hurkacz on Friday, exiting the Shanghai Masters in his first match after memorably winning the China Open this week.
Big-serving Hurkacz, the 2023 champion in Shanghai, won 6-4, 6-3 as the 39-year-old former world number one faltered against an opponent a decade his junior.
"I didn't feel myself on the court," the Serbian veteran said afterwards.
"It's a super-quick surface, completely different from Beijing. If you lose your serve, it's enough to lose a match."
Djokovic was playing three days after winning the title in Beijing, where he has still never lost a match on the professional Tour.
He hunched over and squatted down between points on a cool evening in Shanghai while a lively Hurkacz refused to give much away.
Djokovic was broken in the fourth game of the second set as he double-faulted to give Hurkacz a 3-1 lead.
The Pole held his serve to see out the win and will face either Italy's Lorenzo Musetti or Chinese wildcard Zhou Yi in the third round.
"It's very difficult to return his serve, almost impossible," Djokovic said of his opponent, who sent down 13 aces across the one-hour-and-28-minute match.
"I didn't adjust, and it was a really tough draw for me to play him in the first match-up."
Hurkacz had advanced to the Beijing semi-finals but ended his match early due to a strained muscle.
It was his first-ever victory against Djokovic in nine meetings on the Tour.
"It was a challenging match, always," Hurkacz said.
"I was pleased with how I performed, how I received in important moments."
A gritty Ben Shelton beat Germany's Daniel Altmaier 6-3, 7-6 (8/6) and will play France's Arthur Gea in the third round.
It was a fitting present for the American third seed, who turned 24 on Friday, though he hinted he may go easy on the celebrations, telling an on-court interviewer: "I hate cake."

title: City boss Maresca stands by club
description: Italian hopes that the 10 time English champions will win its appeal
content:
Italian hopes that the 10-time English champions will win its appeal
Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca said Friday he has absolute faith the club will win its appeal after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.
In his first press conference since the bombshell announcement last week, the Italian also rejected any suggestion that City's haul of silverware over the past 15 years was now tainted.
"I completely trust the club," said Maresca, who was appointed manager in June but also previously worked at the Etihad as part of Pep Guardiola's coaching staff.
"I trust the club because I trust the people and this is also the reason why I joined the club... there is not another club in the world where I would like to be."
An independent commission found City had arranged "sham" contracts with a number of their commercial partners to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by over £900 million ($1.2 billion) over a nine-season period, between 2009 and 2018.
The 10-time English champions, who continue to deny any wrongdoing, are appealing against the judgement.
They likely face a severe points penalty that could lead to relegation or even expulsion from the Premier League if they fail to overturn the verdict.
"The reason why I joined this club is because I completely trust 100 percent the owner, the CEO, the sporting director, all the organisation. So I don't have any doubt about that," said Maresca.
"I spoke with the club for sure and we all (have) trust and the right moment to speak about that is when we win this appeal."
Since an Abu Dhabi-backed takeover in 2008, City have become the dominant force in English football.
They have won eight Premier League titles, the Champions League and multiple other trophies over the past 15 years.
Maresca rejected the suggestion that those successes were now tainted.
"Absolutely not," said the former Chelsea boss. "I know the effort from the players, from the club, from the manager in that time that was Pep. So I know exactly the effort that the club put to achieve that kind of target."
Guardiola stepped down at the end of last season after a trophy-laden decade at the Etihad.
City travel to Liverpool on Sunday for their first outing since the guilty verdict, but Guardiola is set to attend their next home game against Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday.
"After 10 years here, he can come at any time he wants," said Maresca. "I think it would be nice for him. It would be nice for the fans, for everyone."
The new head coach has made a flawless start to his reign in charge, winning all five Premier League games so far to top the table.
City are set for a hostile reception when they travel to Anfield, the home of their fierce rivals, but Maresca said his players would stay focused on the match.
"Probably (it) will be even more warm in terms of environment. But the reason why I decided to be manager is for this kind of game," he said.
"I'm not worried at all. Again, the environment is from the players, it's nice. In this moment, we are top of the league, so the players have all the reasons to be happy and excited."

title: Trump envoy kept financial ties to firm behind  15 billion Hormuz bypass oil pipeline plan
description: Iraq and Syria signed agreements with a consortium including Chevron to study reviving a pipeline bypassing Hormuz
content:
Iraq and Syria signed agreements with a consortium including Chevron to study reviving a pipeline bypassing Hormuz
Thomas Barrack, a top US diplomat in the Middle East, advocated for a firm run by his business partner to take part in the development of an oil pipeline from Iraq to Syria, three people said, activities which appear to violate federal ethics rules.
In July, Iraq and Syria signed ​memorandums of understanding with a consortium made up of the company, Californian investment group TI Capital, along with Chevron and Qatar’s UCC Holding, to carry out technical and financial studies in preparation for rehabilitating the pipeline, which would skirt the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint.
Barrack, US ‌presidential special envoy to both Iraq and Syria as well as ambassador to Turkiye, has a longstanding business relationship with TI Capital and its founder Ziad Ghandour. During his 2025 confirmation hearings, he said he had a financial interest entitling him to as much as a fifth of the profits from a real-estate venture near San Francisco, California, managed by TI Capital—with Ghandour as chief executive— and that he intended to retain it; public records show.
During engagements with Syrian and Iraqi officials after the start of the war in Iran, Barrack pressed for Ghandour's firm to be included in the project, according to two of the people who have direct knowledge of the discussions.
On June 16, a month before the consortium agreement was signed, ​Barrack and Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi issued a joint statement that commended Iraq's decision "to advance a memorandum of understanding with TI Capital to rehabilitate the Kirkuk-Baniyas Pipeline". The statement made no mention of Chevron or UCC in connection with the pipeline.
Reuters found no evidence that Barrack stands to ​profit from the pipeline or other projects. His ties to Ghandour would not constitute a criminal conflict of interest unless he stood to directly profit from the pipeline itself, two ethics lawyers told Reuters.
However, Barrack's relationship with Ghandour makes ⁠such advocacy "a serious problem" under the regulation that prohibits officials from participating in matters that call into question their impartiality because of a personal or business relationship, said Richard Painter, a former chief White House ethics lawyer and a professor at the University of Minnesota Law School.
The impartiality rule, which is not a criminal statute, ​can be triggered by the involvement of a business associate in a project, regardless of whether the official has a financial interest of his own.
“The ethical concern is the appearance of a conflict of interest," said Ann Skeet, interim executive director at the Markkula Centre for Applied Ethics at Santa Clara University.
Asked what Barrack would ​have needed to do to comply, Painter said: "Have nothing to do with this pipeline. Completely recuse. Say this is not a matter I participate in."
Don Fox, a former general counsel and acting director of the US Office of Government Ethics, said that promotion of TI Capital by Barrack would additionally violate a regulation prohibiting officials from using their office to endorse any enterprise or for the private gain of people they are affiliated with.
