Barrack has not filed a conflict-of-interest waiver with the US Office of Government Ethics regarding his ties to the company as it participates in the project, according to a Reuters records request. Waivers allow officials with potential conflicts of interest to participate in matters that would otherwise require the employee to be recused.
In a ​signed ethics agreement before his confirmation hearings last year, he committed to recusing himself from matters directly affecting the financial interests of the real-estate venture unless he first obtained such a waiver.
Barrack’s office and Chevron declined to comment. TI Capital, Ghandour and UCC did not respond to requests for comment.
In a July 17 post ​on X, Barrack said the involvement of US companies in Iraq and Syria was “a new paradigm” aimed at bringing clarity and opportunity to the region.
A fourth ethics lawyer said it was up to the State Department to decide whether its employee's financial holdings create a potential conflict of interest.
"Ambassador Barrack has no affiliation with, role in, or financial interest ‌in the Kirkuk-Baniyas pipeline ⁠project," a State Department spokesperson told Reuters , while acknowledging Barrack’s relationship with the TI Capital real-estate venture.
His public comments on the pipeline reflect "long-standing, publicly stated US policy interest in regional energy integration", the spokesperson said, adding that Barrack was certified to be in compliance with ethics rules.
In a financial disclosure filed with the US Office of Government Ethics in March 2025, before assuming his diplomatic roles, Barrack declared an equity stake in ACD-TI Oakley Investment LLC, a venture building a large housing project near San Francisco. The filing did not disclose the size of the stake, but said he was entitled to 20% of the company’s profits when the earnings reach an established minimum.
Read More: Pentagon prepares 3-day intensive Iran strike option as Trump says no attack before midterms: NYT
ACD-TI is managed by TI Capital and headed by Ghandour, California state corporate records show. Reuters was unable to find contact details for a company representative, and did not get a response to questions sent to its postal correspondence address.
The filing said the profit-sharing arrangement was in return for services he provided ​to the company. Barrack also disclosed to the OGE a paid consulting role ​with the venture in 2024. The filing does not say whether or ⁠how much he was paid.
In a separate signed ethics agreement dated March 7, 2025, three weeks before his Senate confirmation hearing, Barrack listed ACD-TI Oakley among assets he would retain rather than sell.
The historic Kirkuk-Baniyas pipeline, which for decades moved Iraqi crude to Syria's Mediterranean coast, faced sporadic shutdowns from the early 1980s and has been out of action since the US invasion of Iraq in 2003. Mothballed plans to revive it received new impetus this year when, under US attack, ​Iran restricted traffic through Hormuz, pushing oil prices higher.
Several people told Reuters in August the pipeline would take at least four years and cost $15 billion to build.
The idea of bringing TI Capital into the regional project was raised by ​Barrack in May at the Milken Institute ⁠Global Conference in Los Angeles, a third person with direct knowledge of the conversation told Reuters. The discussion, they added, took place on the sidelines of the event.
With the US war on Iran raging, Barrack and Ghandour also participated in an invite-only panel at the conference, where they discussed in more general terms the need for new energy supply lines in the Middle East, the person said.
A Milken Institute spokesperson declined to provide details of the panel discussion, saying it was closed to the media.
Barrack has engaged in business with Ghandour since at least 2020, when the two men created a $250 million blank-check SPAC that was dissolved after Barrack was arrested in 2021 on charges of acting as ⁠an unregistered agent of ​the United Arab Emirates. He was acquitted in 2022.
The Iraqi cabinet named TI Capital later in July as part of another consortium with UCC Holding and ConocoPhillips to assess the Akkas gas ​field, one of Iraq's largest undeveloped reserves. On its website, the firm claims involvement in projects at Syria's Tartous port, without providing details. Syria’s port authority did not reply to questions about TI Capital, and Reuters could not verify its role in Tartous. ConocoPhillips did not reply to a request for comment.
A person close to Barrack said the ambassador trusted Ghandour to help implement US President Donald ​Trump’s regional strategy of bringing Iraq and Syria closer to the US. “Ziad is the chosen man. Hand-picked by Barrack,” the person said.
The White House referred Reuters questions to the State Department.

title: Troye Sivan opens up about loneliness  love and his most experimental album yet
description: Sivan s says his album brings together different music styles  including dance  trip hop  shoegaze and orchestral pop
content:
Sivan's says his album brings together different music styles, including dance, trip-hop, shoegaze and orchestral pop
Troye Sivan is opening up about the personal experiences behind his fourth studio album, She’s the Best , describing the project as his most experimental work yet as he explores loneliness, longing and the relationships that have kept him grounded.
In an interview with Vogue , the Australian singer discussed how the album reflects the contrast between the excitement of his career and the solitude he has experienced away from the spotlight. The record follows his 2023 album, Something to Give Each Other , which featured hits including Rush and One of Your Girls .
Sivan explained that his latest project brings together different musical styles, including dance, trip-hop, shoegaze and orchestral pop. Rather than attempting to recreate the sound of his previous record, he wanted the new album to reflect the more complicated emotions he has experienced in recent years.
The singer also spoke about the women who have supported him throughout his life, explaining that their influence became a central theme of the project. The title track celebrates the women and feminine-presenting people who have helped him navigate personal challenges, including trans women, drag queens and the feminine side of his own identity.
The album features appearances from Nicole Kidman and Lily-Rose Depp, with Sivan describing the project as a deeply personal reflection of his life. Kidman appears in the music video for the title track, while Depp contributes to the album’s closing track, which expresses hope for future love.
Sivan also explored the tension between his life as a performer and the loneliness that can follow the excitement of being on stage. Following the success of his 2024 SWEAT tour with Charli XCX, the singer found himself reflecting on how fame can make it more difficult to maintain privacy and build romantic relationships.
The album’s themes extend to his desire for a lasting connection. While tracks such as “Party” capture the energy of nightlife, other songs focus on longing for a future partner and imagining what a more settled life might look like.
Released on October 9, She’s the Best marks Sivan’s first full-length album since Something to Give Each Other . The new record offers a more introspective direction for the singer, balancing the euphoria of pop stardom with the emotional uncertainty that exists beyond the stage.

title: Udara blasts 91 as Sri Lanka post 182
description: Opener powers visitors to imposing total against Pakistan in T20I series opener
content:
Opener powers visitors to imposing total against Pakistan in T20I series opener
Lahiru Udara smashed a blistering 91 off 55 balls to propel Sri Lanka to 182-8 against Pakistan in the first Twenty20 international at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Friday.
Udara struck 11 fours and a six, anchoring the Sri Lankan innings after Pakistan made early inroads into the visitors' batting line-up.
Pakistan, who elected to bowl after losing the toss, dismissed captain Kusal Mendis for one in the first over, with Naseem Shah providing the breakthrough. Mohammad Imran then removed Kamil Mishara for six as Sri Lanka slipped to 18-2 in the fourth over.
Udara steadied the innings alongside Kamindu Mendis, who scored 23 off 18 deliveries, including four boundaries. The pair helped Sri Lanka recover before Saim Ayub dismissed Kamindu to leave the visitors at 78-3.
Imran struck again to remove Sahan Arachchige for one, but Udara continued to attack, reaching his half-century off 32 balls.
Dasun Shanaka added momentum with 18 from 15 deliveries, including two sixes, as he shared a useful partnership with Udara to push Sri Lanka beyond 130.
Shanaka fell to Shadab Khan in the 16th over, but Udara kept the scoreboard moving despite wickets falling at the other end.
Naseem returned to dismiss Dunith Wellalage for five before claiming Udara's wicket on the final ball of the 19th over, ending the opener's outstanding innings at 91.
The dismissal came after Udara had survived a Pakistan review earlier in the innings.
Pakistan's bowlers picked up wickets in the closing overs to restrict Sri Lanka's late charge, although the visitors finished with a competitive total of 182.
Naseem led the Pakistan attack with three wickets for 36 runs from four overs, while Imran impressed on debut with two for 21. Shadab and Ayub claimed one wicket apiece, while Razaullah also took one.
Pakistan, earlier, handed debuts to Razaullah and Imran Randhawa as visitors Sri Lanka opted to bat first in the first T20I of the three-match series at the Pindi Stadium in Rawalpindi.
Both Razaullah and Imran Randhawa made their Test debuts against England at Edgbaston recently and are set to showcase their skills in the shorter format against Sri Lanka at home.
Razaullah is famous for his fast bowling and aggressive batting while Imran is a medium pacer and is also a very good batsman.
Sahibzada Farhan will lead the side for the first time. Farhan has replaced Agha Salman as Pakistan T20 captain.

title: PSX falls over 350 points in dull trading
description: KSE 100 closes at 167 089 points on Friday amid subdued trading activity and mixed sectoral performance
content:
KSE-100 closes at 167,089 points on Friday amid subdued trading activity and mixed sectoral performance
The KSE-100 Index fell over 350 points to close near 167,090 on Friday amid subdued trading activity and mixed sectoral performance, as local political uncertainty and geopolitical risks continued to weigh on investor sentiment.
Market volumes remained low at 110 million shares, while easing oil prices offered some relief after the previous session’s sharp sell-off.
The benchmark index closed at 167,089 points, down 352 points (-0.21% DoD), amid mixed performance and exceptionally dull trading activity. Volumes remained subdued at just 110mn shares, reflecting cautious investor participation ahead of the weekend.
Following yesterday’s sharp selling pressure amid a more than 5% surge in oil prices, sentiment improved slightly overnight after Donald Trump’s comments suggested limited prospects of further escalation before the US midterm elections, said Ahmed Sheraz, Head of Support Trading at KASB KTrade. Brent crude eased from near $106/bbl to around $102-103/bbl before trading between $103-104/bbl during market hours.
However, local political uncertainty and persistent geopolitical risks, particularly tensions involving the Houthis and the Red Sea, continued to weigh on sentiment. Sectoral contributions remained mixed, with commercial banks, cement and technology stocks facing pressure. HBL, UBL, MCB and OGDC were among the major banking stocks under pressure, while CNERGY, KEL, and PIBTL featured among the volume leaders.
Going forward, the market is likely to remain range-bound and volatile, with participation subdued until greater clarity emerges on Pakistan’s political situation and the evolving geopolitical landscape. Oil price movements will remain a key driver of near-term sentiment.

title: Bilawal urges PTI to return to political engagement  says governor s rule in K P would be  atomic bomb
description: Says governor s rule will be the last resort  Kundi calls PTI long march a  circus   warns of consequences
content:
Says governor's rule will be the last resort; Kundi calls PTI long march a 'circus', warns of consequences
Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari on Friday urged the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) to return to political engagement, adding that imposing governor's rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa would be a "political atomic bomb".
“You will not disappoint the voter in K-P if you amend your politics, return to parliamentary committees and interact with other political parties. Politics is a day-to-day affair, and you can improve your political position,” he stated while addressing an inauguration ceremony of a sports complex in Karachi's Baldia Town.
Bilawal underscored that while introducing governor's rule or an emergency in K-P was a "constitutional and legal option" for the PPP, it was tantamount to a “political atomic bomb” and should only be considered as a measure of "last resort".
"It was the PPP that suggested that PTI should be engaged politically and an emergency not be imposed, because we know that if an emergency is imposed in K-P, then the political space for political parties will shrink and that would reduce the space for all political parties in the country. Imposing an emergency in K-P is an atomic bomb and will only be considered as the last resort".
Bilawal stated that for PTI to restore its “lost political standing”, the party must renounce the “politics of extremism” if it was “true to their leader Imran Khan” and engage with other political parties through political means.
Read : PTI warns of quitting assemblies if governor's rule imposed in K-P
پاکستان پیپلزپارٹی کے چیئرمین بلاول بھٹو زرداری نے کراچی کے بلدیہ ٹاؤن میں 25 ایکڑ پر مشتمل کے ایم سی اسپورٹس کمپلکس کا افتتاح کردیا، جہاں نوجوانوں کے لئے ہاکی گراؤنڈ، باسکٹ بال کورٹ، ٹینس کورٹ، ریس ٹریک، فٹ بال گراؤنڈ، کرکٹ گراؤنڈ اور کرکٹ نیٹ پریکٹس کی سہولیات ہیں جبکہ دو… pic.twitter.com/V3dnBHJbP2
“If PTI renounces the politics of extremism, then they will save their politics, their government and also, sooner or later, their political leadership. This is evident in the history of Pakistan”.
Bilawal further noted that if PTI’s politics continued to revolve around extremism, then “Imran shall remain a prisoner and would even break President Zardari’s record of incarceration”.
Responding to a question on negotiations with PTI, the PPP chairman said PTI had harmed itself politically by sabotaging the talks, adding that Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman should play his role in the negotiation process.
“We do not want that the last option for the PPP of governor's rule or emergency should be exercised, but it seems that K-P CM is leaving no space for political engagement and is actively working towards the imposition of governor's rule in the province”.
Bilawal further questioned why K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi wanted to sabotage the political process of dialogue and negotiations, further adding that democratic forces such as the PPP were consequently forced to confront the possibility of an emergency, especially given the external and internal security situation of the country and K-P in particular.
“Given the security situation in K-P and the refusal of the provincial government to cooperate in terrorism, how can I legally say that an emergency should not be imposed in the province? It is because of the role of K-P CM that an emergency is being considered in the province.”
While talking about Gilgit-Baltistan and South Punjab, Bilawal said that his party would follow the will of the people concerning making new provinces and would support any resolution put forward by the elected representatives for this purpose. "However, if you do not have the support of the people, and want to do it forcefully, then you can continue with your efforts by seeking the mandate of the people".
Bilawal says some parties want to turn Karachi youth into criminals
Bilawal further stated that there were "some political forces that want to make the youth of this city into criminals", but asserted that the PPP wanted to see the youth "with pens in their hands, not weapons".
While speaking about the sports complex, Bilawal said that the city's municipal system had inaugurated the complex so the youth were able to engage in positive activities.
"PPP wants to see the youth play, and does not want to see them involved in crime," Bilawal stressed, adding that he was hopeful the youth would take advantage of the sports complex and that it would be taken care of "so the youth here can always be provided this facility".
“میں نے آج کراچی میں کے ایم سی اسپورٹس کمپلیکس کا افتتاح کیا ہے، میں کراچی کے نوجوانوں کو مبارکباد دینا چاہتا ہوں کہ ان کیلئے کے ایم سی نے یہ اسپورٹس کمپلیکس قائم کیا، ہم چاہتے ہیں کہ ہمارے نوجوانوں کو مثبت سرگرمیوں کا موقع ملے، کچھ سیاسی قوتیں شہر کے نوجوانوں کو کرمنل بنانا… pic.twitter.com/Jyl1PtFKif
Bilawal added: "If you review the entire nation, there is only one political party that wants to do positive politics and the rest of the political parties, whether those of this city, want to do the politics of hatred, division, and fighting."
Kundi calls PTI long march a 'circus', warns of consequences if it triggers unrest
Separately, K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi warned the PTI leadership of serious consequences if its long march resulted in unrest, challenging party leaders to lead the protest themselves rather than sending workers to the front.
Addressing a press conference in Peshawar, the governor challenged the PTI leadership to cross Swabi on Friday if it had the courage to do so. Kundi also criticised the K-P government for its confrontational approach towards the federal government, saying a province had to be administered in coordination with the centre.
Dismissing the march, he said: “It is not a long march; it is a circus moving from one city to another.” He added that the PTI’s May 9 protests continued to damage the party’s image and warned that any fresh attempt to create a similar situation would have consequences that future generations would remember. “They say the workers should go into the protest without leaders. Where will you hide? If you dare, the leaders must come first. I know how to deal with you all,” he said.
The governor further said he knew how to defend the Governor House and was prepared to take responsibility for the consequences of the punitive measures he had ordered, whether minor or serious.
“I do not engage in mere rhetoric; I take action,” Kundi said, adding that the PTI should learn from the consequences of its previous confrontations and guide future generations towards democratic politics.
He advised the protesters to study Articles 149 and 131 of the Constitution, as well as Schedule Four, to understand the relevant legal provisions. He also announced that he would convene a meeting to discuss the law and order situation.
Highlighting recent terrorist attacks in K-P, including incidents in Karak and Khyber, Kundi criticised the PTI leadership for its failure to condemn such attacks. “They never condemn these attacks,” he said, adding that the party lacked the courage to challenge terrorist groups.
The governor also criticised the provincial government for failing to provide adequate resources and fair remuneration to the police and Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) personnel deployed on the front lines.
He accused the PTI-led provincial government of seeking control over the police rather than facilitating the force in carrying out its duties. “All they care about is ‘conquering’ Islamabad,” he said, dismissing the party’s long march as “a drama, an act”.
Kundi said he regularly raised the issue of counterterrorism in his communications with the prime minister, president and interior minister, describing the fight against terrorism as his foremost priority.
“Terrorism is our red line; our party and many other parties have lost their leaders in attacks,” he said, adding that preventing terrorist groups from gaining ground in the province was a shared priority. “We will not let terrorists prevail in our province. This is our one-point agenda,” he said.
He further said the K-P government should formulate and present its own security policy if it disagreed with the federal government’s approach, either on the floor of the provincial assembly or at a press conference. “They have never done that,” he said, questioning whether the PTI leadership intended to follow policies dictated by Kabul, Jalalabad and Kandahar.
He accused the party of distancing itself from discussions on counterterrorism and said its approach could not be allowed to undermine peace and stability in the province. “Doesn’t this province deserve peace, progress and wellbeing?” he asked.
The governor said he would provide the federal government with an assessment of the ground situation whenever requested, adding that the security challenges facing the province were evident to all.
He added that he had little hope of progress with the PTI leadership, accusing it of adopting positions that he believed were contrary to the country’s interests.
Kundi further said Parliament was the most appropriate forum for negotiations with the PTI, while questioning the authority of Chief Minister Sohail Afridi in decision-making.
Responding to a question about inviting the PTI for negotiations, Kundi said: “There is no forum bigger than the parliament for debate.” He stated that the leaders of the PPP, PML-N and PTI had participated in previous talks, but the decision-making authority rested with someone who had “probably escaped the country”.
He added that PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari had also reiterated the need for reconciliation and dialogue with the PTI leadership within the constitutional framework. However, he said, some parties were unwilling to pursue that approach, leaving little room for progress.
Kundi questioned the provincial government’s ability to maintain law and order and protect its elected representatives.
“You should know who are kidnapping your people since you are the chief executive of the province. If you cannot protect your lawmakers, how will you protect the province and its people?” he asked.
He said the chief minister should have resigned instead of complaining about the abduction of lawmakers.
Highlighting the province’s administrative challenges, Kundi said doctors, university faculty members, nurses, teachers and employees of tehsil municipal administrations (TMAs) were on strike over various grievances.
He accused the provincial government of focusing on financial gains rather than resolving the problems confronting public-sector employees and government departments.
Kundi further stated that the province needed effective governance and pledged to protect its people and confront terrorism. “We will protect our province and fight against the terrorists on the front line,” he said, adding that his government would teach the provincial administration how to run the province.
Commenting on the possibility of imposing governor’s rule or an emergency in the province, he said the decision rested with the prime minister and the president, who were better placed to determine whether such a measure was necessary.
Background of debate on imposition of governor's rule in K-P
The issue of Governor’s Rule has become a major point of contention between the federal and K-P government. On September 21, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the government was consulting the law ministry on legal options for the province, including Governor’s Rule , if the PTI proceeded with its long march. Two days later, however, Information Minister Atta Tarar ruled out any plan to impose Governor’s Rule, saying the federal government had no intention of removing the PTI administration.
Read More : Govt 'seriously' considering imposing emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa: Tariq Fazal
Some federal ministers publicly raised the possibility of federal intervention in K-P. Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam said consultations were under way on the "constitutional and legal option" of imposing Governors' Rule.
Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar also said if constitutional conditions for such a step or an emergency were met, it could be implemented.
K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi separately warned the provincial government against creating a situation that could force the Centre to impose Governors' Rule.
K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi warned that the PTI would "rebel" if necessary to force a change in the federal government policies that were "harming the province".
Also Read : Afridi threatens revolt to 'force change'
Afridi, however, rejected the warnings and said he would not retreat from his position because of threats of Governors' Rule or an emergency. He also said PTI supporters could take to the streets at short notice if an attempt was made to remove him.
The developments come amid continued tensions following PTI's announcement of an Islamabad march.
Reports have also emerged about the possible disqualification of the chief minister, his replacement, an in-house change, dissolution of the assembly and a no-confidence motion against him under Article 136 of the Constitution.
The no-confidence motion can be submitted to the assembly secretariat with signatures of 20% of the total membership, following which an assembly session is to be convened within three to seven days on a single-point agenda.
The assembly rules lay down the procedure for a no-confidence motion. After the motion is moved in the house, voting is held through a secret ballot, with members expressing their choice in two separate lobbies. If the motion succeeds, the speaker will issue a schedule for the election of a new chief minister.
The Constitution also provides for the governor to require the chief minister to seek a vote of confidence under Article 130(7). If the governor believes the chief minister has lost the confidence of the majority in the house, the chief minister is required to demonstrate his numerical strength in the assembly.

title: Pope Leo approves Tagle as first Asian dean of Catholic cardinals
description: Former Manila archbishop Tagle has been a senior Vatican official since 2020 and was a papal contender in 2025
content:
Former Manila archbishop Tagle has been a senior Vatican official since 2020 and was a papal contender in 2025
Pope Leo approved Filipino Cardinal Luis Tagle's election as the dean of the Catholic ​Church's college of cardinals, the Vatican said on Friday, ‌in the first selection of an Asian cleric to lead the elite group that one day will choose Leo's successor.
A former archbishop ​of Manila, Tagle has served as a senior Vatican ​official since 2020. He was widely seen as a likely ⁠papal candidate in the May 2025 conclave that elected ​Leo to lead the Church after the death of the ​late Pope Francis.
Tagle, 69, replaces Italian Cardinal Giovanni Battista Re, who is 92 and retiring from the role.
Leo, 71, is relatively young for ​a pope, plays sports and is in good health.
Read More: Vatican envoy lauds Pakistan’s 'constructive role' in promoting regional peace, stability
The dean ​of the college of cardinals is considered the "first among equals" among the ‌Church's ⁠highest-ranking clerics and is responsible for taking charge of the secretive conclave process, held in the Sistine Chapel, once a pope dies or resigns.
The dean, elected by his peers and ​approved by ​the pope, serves ⁠a five-year term that can be renewed once, according to Church law. The role has ​mostly been filled by Europeans, but was ​held by ⁠the late Beninese Cardinal Bernardin Gantin from 1993-2002.
Tagle was seen as a close ally of Pope Francis and is known ⁠for an ​infectious smile and is sometimes called ​by his diminutive nickname "Chito". He leads the Vatican's Dicastery for Evangelization, effectively the ​Church's missionary arm.

title: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce   s  5 35m Ohio property neighbours raise objections over 6 foot fence plan
description: The couple s project team defended the renovations  emphasising the importance of privacy and security
content:
The couple's project team defended the renovations, emphasising the importance of privacy and security
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce have reportedly faced objections from neighbours over renovation plans at their newly purchased Ohio property, including fencing and landscaping proposals .
According to the Daily Mail , a planning board in Bratenahl, near Cleveland, approved a 6-foot fence last month despite objections from some nearby residents.
Neighbour Katherine Bolton reportedly described the property purchase as a “tremendous blow” to “the peace and quiet in Bratenahl”.
She also raised concerns about plans to plant 50 evergreen trees near a century-old clay sewer line shared with her property.
“Planting 50 evergreen trees just ten feet from a 100-year-old clay sewer line is virtually guaranteed to cause severe root intrusion, pipe structural failure and catastrophic sewage backups,” Bolton reportedly told the board, according to the Daily Mail .
Bolton also questioned the potential consequences if the property were sold in the future, saying: “This applicant may decide to sell her house next year. What am I going to do when I have 50 evergreen trees on my sewer line, and they're gone?”
Another neighbour reportedly raised concerns about the fence's spear-shaped top, suggesting it could pose a risk to animals.
The couple's project team defended the renovations, emphasising the importance of privacy and security.
Jacob Kutz of Tiny Construction, who is overseeing the work, said: “The house was one of the largest sales in Cuyahoga County, so the homeowner is looking for privacy and security.”
The Daily Mail reported that the board subsequently approved the front landscaping, subject to trees being positioned with sufficient space to grow.
Kelce reportedly purchased the lakefront estate for $5.35 million earlier this year, according to The Wall Street Journal .

title: Mia Goth appears to take subtle dig at ex Shia LaBeouf in Instagram post days after divorce filing
description: Goth filed for divorce in LA on  October 6 after 10 years of marriage  citing  irreconcilable differences
content:
Goth filed for divorce in LA on October 6 after 10 years of marriage, citing 'irreconcilable differences'
Mia Goth has sparked speculation after sharing an Instagram selfie that appeared to reference her estranged husband, Shia LaBeouf, just two days after filing for divorce.
On Thursday, October 8, the 32-year-old actress posted a photo of herself wearing a shirt bearing the words, “My ex is my biggest fan”.
She captioned the image with a lipstick kiss emoji, prompting speculation about whether the post was directed at LaBeouf, 40.
Goth filed for divorce in Los Angeles on Tuesday, October 6, citing “irreconcilable differences”. The legal documents reportedly list July 28, 2025 as their date of separation.
Goth is seeking primary legal and physical custody of the couple’s four-year-old daughter, Isabel. She has also requested that neither party be awarded spousal support.
The filing states that the “exact nature and extent” of their separate and shared assets and debts remain unknown.

title: Mourinho lashes out at  ridiculous  criticism of Mbappe
description: The French captain has come under fire for spending his time recovering from a left knee injury
content:
The French captain has come under fire for spending his time recovering from a left knee injury
Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho slammed criticism of star striker Kylian Mbappe, on Friday labelling the attacks as "ridiculous".
The French captain has come under fire for spending his time recovering from a left knee injury -- which he suffered playing in a Nations League match against Turkey -- in France and Switzerland rather than Madrid.
The 27-year-old was also pictured at the entrance of a Parisian nightclub and photographed on a bicycle when he was in Switzerland.
Some fans claimed it was a deliberate snubbing of Mourinho, who had only days before said that players should avoid skiing or riding bicycles so as to avoid risking injury.
"Are these criticisms over the top? They are ridiculous," said Mourinho at his press conference on the eve of their La Liga home match with Villarreal.
"All the players who were obliged to be present every day for their recovery were here.
"Mbappe came, like the others, to undergo scans in order to be diagnosed.
"He then went to see a specialist in France, because he has history with his knee which we cannot ignore."
Mourinho, whose side already lag six points behind bitter rivals Barcelona in the title race, is never one to shy away from a confrontation and tackled each of the criticisms against Mbappe.
"Problems involving football are not sufficient for you," the 63-year-old Portuguese coach told reporters.
"Therefore you have raised the issue of the discotheque, which in fact was not one, because it was used for a private event for Fashion Week.
"As for the bicycle in Switzerland. It was in a hotel, made up of small houses, which makes them available so guests can ride to the communal areas, and you would have us believe he was competing in the Tour of Switzerland."
Mourinho shrugged off the potential of a hostile reception for Mbappe on Saturday, reiterating that he was "certain" the all-time World Cup record goalscorer had fulfilled "his obligations to Real Madrid".
It is not the first time this season that Mbappe has been subjected to attacks by fans.
The Ultras Sur, a Real Madrid supporters' group linked to the far right and banned from the Santiago Bernabeu, took issue with him last month.
They were furious that prior to a Real Madrid match, Mbappe, alongside Vinicius Junior and fellow Frenchman Ibrahima Konate, partially rolled up t-shirts bearing the words "We are all Ceutans", which was intended to be a message of support for people in the Spanish territory bordering Morocco.
Ceuta, Spain's north African exclave has been grappling with a migration crisis.

description: The Chinese wildcard overpowers seventh ranked Elina Svitolina 6 3  7 6  8 6  to reach the last four
content:
The Chinese wildcard overpowers seventh-ranked Elina Svitolina 6-3, 7-6 (8/6) to reach the last four
Homegrown hero Zheng Qinwen pulled out some of her best tennis to beat Ukraine's Elina Svitolina 6-3, 7-6 (8/6) at the China Open on Friday and storm into the semi-finals.
Zheng, a wildcard entry in Beijing, finally notched her first straight-sets win of this year's tournament having needed more than 10 hours on court to get to the quarter-final.
The world number 54 sent the crowd roaring as she punched winners down the line, though the seventh-ranked Svitolina came back fighting to force a second set tie-break.
Zheng double-faulted on the first point but crawled her way out from a 0-2 deficit and fell on her back victorious after winning her second match point.
"Truthfully, because I really wanted to grab this win, I was really nervous," the 24-year-old told the crowd.
"I played really aggressive in important moments," she said, adding that her opponent "raised her level" in a tight second set.
Svitolina made just 13 unforced errors over the one-hour-and-47-minute match, but was outgunned by 48 winners from the 2024 Olympic champion.
Later on Friday, Poland's Iga Swiatek, the 2023 title winner in Beijing, was due to play Belgium's Elise Mertens for the last semi-final spot.

title: Bilawal  Sanaullah made members of Judicial Commission
description: Both were appointed members of treasury benches in their respective Houses  following approval from CJP Yahya Afridi
content:
Both were appointed members of treasury benches in their respective Houses, following approval from CJP Yahya Afridi
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari and Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) Senator Rana Sanaullah have been appointed members of the Judicial Commission of Pakistan.
According to a notification issued by the commission, Bilawal and Sanaullah were made members after the approval of Chief Justice Yahya Afridi, who is also chairperson of the JCP.
Bilawal, a member of the National Assembly, and Rana Sanaullah, the leader of the house in the Senate, were both made members of the treasury benches in their respective Houses.
"In pursuance of paragraph (vii) of clause 2 of Article 175A of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973," the notification said. It added that Bilawal and Sanaullah were notified as members "on nomination of the leader of the House in the Senate and the leader of the House in the National Assembly."
Yesterday, JCP sources told The Express Tribune that Bilawal was interested in becoming a member of the JCP. The sources had also said that PPP Senator Farooq H Naek and PML-N MNA Sheikh Aftab had resigned as members of the JCP, paving the way for a possible reshuffle in the commission's parliamentary representation.
Read: 'We will fix it': Bilawal says if system has failed, hand Islamabad to Tharparkar
The development came amid reported dissatisfaction within the PPP leadership over the failure to secure the appointment of its preferred candidates as judges of the superior courts.
The JCP was one of three judicial forums, alongside the Supreme Judicial Council (SJC) and the Practice and Procedure Act (PAPA) committee of the Supreme Court, which were reconstituted in view of the 27th Constitutional Amendment.
The JCP is the constitutional body that elevates judges to the superior courts, while the SJC is the forum that hears complaints filed against judges of superior courts in view of alleged misconduct and the PAPA committee of the Supreme Court forms benches and lists cases.

title: Kashmiri filmmaker Arfat Sheikh released from US ICE detention  campaign says
description: Sheikh was detained on September 24th  His work has explored conflict in his native Kashmir
content:
Sheikh was detained on September 24; his work explores conflict in the valley
Award-winning Kashmiri filmmaker Arfat Sheikh was released from US Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention on bond on Thursday after being detained on September 24, ‌according to a statement by a campaign of his friends and relatives to free him.
Sheikh, whose work has explored conflict in his native India-administered Kashmir, was detained by ICE, part of the Department of Homeland Security, while coming off a plane from California at the Washington Dulles International Airport, the campaign said.
It said Sheikh's bond was granted on Tuesday and he was released on Thursday, adding that ⁠the deportation case against him continues.
The campaign said Sheikh, who lived in Alexandria, Virginia, entered the US in 2019 on a student visa to pursue graduate studies in film at Georgia State University and filed for asylum in 2020. The campaign said he had a pending immigration application and was authorized to work and live in the US.
DHS said on Wednesday Sheikh was arrested on September 24. It said Sheikh "legally entered the US on a temporary basis and illegally overstayed his lawful admittance."
A pending application does not confer legal status in the US, DHS said, adding he will receive due process.
President Donald Trump's administration said in August it ‌was ⁠working "to identify and revoke the non-immigrant visas of foreigners who have come to the US claiming to be short-term visitors, but then file for asylum to stay here permanently."
Trump has pursued an immigration crackdown and deportation drive that he says aims to improve domestic security. Rights advocates say the crackdown has violated due process and free speech rights and created an ⁠unsafe environment, particularly for ethnic minorities, who have raised concerns about racial profiling.
Sheikh's first feature film, 2024's "Saffron Kingdom” won Best Feature Film at the Chicago Filmmakers Awards, the LA Film and Documentary Awards, the Melbourne Independent Film Festival and the Wake ⁠Forest Film Festival. Sheikh, who hails from India-administered Kashmir, won the Emerging Filmmaker Activist Award at the Teaneck International Film Festival.
The film explored conflict in Kashmir through the journey of a family from Srinagar in ⁠India-administered Kashmir in the 1990s to Atlanta in 2019.

title: Russell goes fastest in practice for smoggy Singapore GP
description: Leclerc trails the Mercedes driver by 0 198 seconds  with Norris third
content:
Leclerc trails the Mercedes driver by 0.198 seconds, with Norris third
George Russell in a Mercedes topped the timesheets Friday in the only practice session for the Singapore Grand Prix at a Marina Bay Circuit enveloped in smoky haze caused by fires in Indonesia.
Charles Leclerc's Ferrari was second on a dusty surface with the McLaren of Lando Norris third as drivers and teams had just one hour-long session to maximise their set-ups before sprint qualifying later on Friday.
Singapore is featuring a sprint race for the first time and the only practice session took place before sunset, not ideal preparation for the Marina Bay Circuit's night race on Sunday.
Russell will start from the back of the grid for Sunday's race after taking a penalty for using too many engine components, but he can still compete for pole postion in Saturday's sprint race.
The Englishman went round in 1min 32.274sec, 0.198sec ahead of Leclerc as the top five times were all set on the soft compound tyre, with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton fourth and the second McLaren of Oscar Piastri fifth.
Max Verstappen, who won for the first time this season in Malaysia last weekend, was the fastest of the medium-compound runners in sixth, 0.732sec slower than Russell but half a second ahead of the other Mercedes of championship leader Kimi Antonelli.
Isack Hadjar of Red Bull was seventh fastest, followed by Pierre Gasly of Alpine and Liam Lawson in an RB who rounded out the top 10.
Verstappen has never won in Singapore, where extremes of heat and humidity play a part in the most physically attritional race of the season on a circuit notoriously difficult for overtaking.
Drivers can shed up to 3kg (6lb) during the race from sweating alone and the race has been declared a "heat hazard" by organisers.
That means drivers can opt to wear cooling vests because the heat index is predicted to exceed 31C during either the sprint or the race.
The teams also have to contend with the smoggy haze, which saw Singapore's air quality plunge to an "unhealthy" 205 on Friday according to the IQAir tracking website.
Schools were shut in neighbouring Malaysia because of pollution from the wildfires raging in nearby Indonesia.
Readings above 150 are classified as unhealthy, while levels above 300 are considered hazardous.
Motorsport's governing body said the race was not under threat from the haze.
"Air quality levels are being monitored by the relevant local authorities and appropriate contingency measures are in place should conditions worsen," the FIA said in a statement to AFP.
The FIA added that some off-track activities and entertainment could be affected, but "based on the latest information available, air quality and haze are not forecast to represent a threat to track activity or the conduct of the event".

title: Malaysia closes schools in capital  parts of country due to haze
description: Fires in neighbouring Indonesia again plunges local air quality to among the world s worst
content:
Fires in neighbouring Indonesia again plunges local air quality to among the world's worst
Malaysia closed schools in Kuala Lumpur and other parts of the country on Friday, as haze from fires in neighbouring Indonesia again plunged local air quality to among the world's worst.
Toxic smoke from peatland and forest fires has shrouded cities in the region for more than a month, sending respiratory complaints skyrocketing.
The school closures came as Malaysia's leader discussed the choking smoke with his Indonesian counterpart and called for an urgent regional meeting.
Air quality in Kuala Lumpur has been firmly in "unhealthy levels" this week, with a Swiss-based air quality monitor ranking the Malaysian capital among the world's most polluted cities on most days.
Malaysia's Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said she has instructed whole school closures in four states and two federal territories, as well as one partial closure in the central Pahang State. "In the future, we will ensure that any decision to close schools is notified in advance so that parents have sufficient time to prepare," Fadhlina said late on Thursday.
Also Read: Lahore's air quality takes a hit
Malaysia's King Sultan Ibrahim weighed in on the matter on Thursday, saying schools should be closed as air quality readings reached 150 or higher on the Air Pollutant Index (API).
Under Malaysian guidelines, API readings above 100 are classified as unhealthy, above 200 as very unhealthy, above 300 as hazardous, while readings beyond 500 constitute the threshold for declaring a local emergency.
Kuala Lumpur on Friday showed a reading of around 170 API. The city was the second-most polluted globally behind neighbouring Singapore on Friday morning, Swiss-based air monitor IQAir said.
Malaysia's Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Thursday he discussed the fire situation with the Indonesian leader Prabowo Subianto.
"The haze issue is indeed at a worrying level. And I have personally contacted President Prabowo," Anwar said. "And he also agreed to take the necessary steps," Anwar said, without going into specific details.
He said Malaysia has been taking measures to combat the haze, including increasing attempts to trigger rain via cloud seeding.
Read More: Haze not 'a threat' to Singapore F1 race: organisers
Experts said the flames are being fanned by a turbo-charged El Niño weather phenomenon, causing the worst pollution conditions in years.
Anwar said he asked Malaysia's Foreign Minister Mohamad Hasan to contact the 11-nation Association of Southeast Asian Nations' secretariat for an urgent meeting between environmental ministers to discuss the matter. "So these are all the steps we are taking, but we are monitoring and will try the measures that we ought to take next," Anwar said.
Singapore's air quality levels too dipped into the "very unhealthy" range with a reading of 205 on the Air Quality Index, according to the IQAir website.
The AQI converts measurements of pollutants into a single figure indicating air quality and potential health risks.
Readings above 150 are classified as unhealthy, while levels above 300 are considered hazardous.

title: Faysal Quraishi challenges mindset that daughters should endure abusive marriages
description: Actor stresses parents must stand by their daughters when they face abuse
content:
Actor stresses parents must stand by their daughters when they face abuse
Actor Faysal Quraishi has challenged the belief that married daughters should return to their parents’ homes only after their deaths, stressing that parents remain responsible for their daughters’ safety and well-being even after marriage.
Speaking in an interview with Vasay Chaudhry alongside actor Hareem Farooq, Quraishi questioned the mindset that women should endure abuse in their marital homes rather than seek support from their families.
“I mean, you have raised her, so you won’t stay as her back-up? If she is being beaten up there or is being abused, then why do people have such thoughts that she will only return when it’s her funeral?” he said.
“Is she not your daughter?” he asked, emphasising that marriage does not diminish a daughter’s place in her parents’ lives. “If you are alive and well, take that responsibility,” he added.
His remarks highlighted the importance of parents providing a safe space for their daughters, particularly when they face violence or abuse in their marital homes. He challenged the social stigma that can prevent women from seeking refuge with their families when a marriage becomes unsafe.
Quraishi also referred to the drama Muhabbatein Chahatein , featuring Mawra Hocane, recalling a scene in which a father stands up for his daughter. He praised the portrayal for promoting equality between sons and daughters and demonstrating the importance of parental support.
“I liked it so much that we are showing such stuff in dramas that whether daughter or son, they are both equal,” he said.
He further explained that standing by a child could deter wrongdoing by ensuring the child did not feel alone. “When you stand up for your child, the person doing the crime won’t have the ability to,” he said.
Drawing a connection to his upcoming film, Mango Jutt , Quraishi shared a Punjabi dialogue that conveyed a similar sentiment: “ Hun peeche mur ke vekhi, tere peeche main khlota aan ” — meaning, “Now look back, I am standing behind you.” “When you know someone is beside you, even the person in front of you can’t commit a crime,” he added.
The conversation also touched on Quraishi and Farooq’s upcoming Punjabi film, Mango Jutt , and the thinking behind its unusual title. While “mango” might initially seem unexpected in the title of a Punjabi film, Farooq said it carried several associations, including being Pakistan’s national fruit and the king of fruits.
She suggested that combining “Mango” with “Jutt” was intended to make audiences curious about the film and encourage them to discover its story.
Quraishi added, "When you see the name, you think what is this? But that's the biggest thing about film. Mango is the national fruit and we want the character of Murad Jutt to be a national hero."
The title also reflects the film’s intended family appeal. According to Farooq, its light-hearted and unusual nature makes it accessible to audiences of different ages, including children who may find the name amusing.
Quraishi also highlighted the film’s connection to Punjabi culture, saying viewers would see “ apna Punjab ” on screen. The discussion broadened to the role of Punjabi-language entertainment in Pakistan’s film industry.
Farooq said Punjab’s culture and language represented a significant opportunity for the local entertainment business, while Quraishi pointed to the success of The Legend of Maula Jatt as evidence that Punjabi cinema could attract audiences in Pakistan. "It was also proven though Maula Jutt that Punjabi films can work in Pakistan," he said.
Quraishi suggested that bringing Punjabi storytelling to the forefront could help strengthen the domestic film industry and encourage more productions rooted in regional culture and language.
Farooq also spoke positively about working with Quraishi, describing the experience as enjoyable and praising his collaborative approach on set. “I laughed so much on the shoot. Working with Faysal is a pleasure, and I don’t say this because he’s here,” she said.
She noted that Quraishi had a quality she believed was not always found among more senior actors: a willingness to support fellow performers and producers rather than focusing solely on himself. “He supports producers and actors. He doesn’t just want focus on himself. He is somebody who works with everyone, and that made my job very easy,” she added.
Their discussion highlighted the potential of Punjabi films to bring together performers and audiences from different parts of Pakistan while showcasing regional stories on a wider cinematic platform.
Mango Jutt is scheduled to release in cinemas on October 16, 2026.

title: Makkah alliance ground forces will not cross Yemen to attack Houthis  will defend Saudi Arabia  FO
description: Says that security of each country in Makkah pact is an integral part of collective security of the three countries
content:
Security of each country is an integral part of collective security of the three countries, says spokesperson
Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said on Friday that the Makkah defence alliance between Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia was intended to defend the three countries against aggression and the allied forces would not launch attacks inside Yemen.
Addressing a weekly press briefing in Islamabad, the spokesperson said the three countries had agreed to move towards the practical implementation of their collective defence commitments under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), with the three countries approving measures to strengthen military readiness, integration and coordination.
The decision includes measures to provide agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in Saudi Arabia, in accordance with approved arrangements and the national laws of the three countries.
Asked whether allied forces could engage Houthi forces in Yemen, Khan said the alliance was meant to defend the three countries against aggression and would not launch attacks from within Yemeni territory.
“These forces would not cross the border into Yemen to launch attacks against the Houthis,” he said, adding that they would be used to defend Saudi territory and safeguard its sovereignty.
The spokesperson also categorically rejected reports that Pakistani fighter jets had been involved in cross-border operations, describing them as false.
“This is speculative news, which has also been refuted by the minister for information,” he added.
📍Spokesperson's Weekly Press Briefing on 09-10-2026 , at Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Islamabad pic.twitter.com/InEQNnWYxy
“The Committee also decided to move towards the practical implementation of collective defence commitments and approved measures to enhance readiness, military integration and the collective capacity of the three countries to confront these threats,” Khan said.
The meeting brought together the foreign ministers, defence ministers and chiefs of general staff of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye to review regional developments and cooperation under the agreement.
“The Committee reviewed the security situation and threats facing the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, reaffirmed its commitment to collective defence and strongly condemned attempts to target Makkah and Madinah, as well as attacks on cities, civilians as well as on the economic infrastructure,” Khan said.
At a recent meeting of the three countries’ defence cooperation forum, it was decided that appropriate mobilisation would take place as required, he said.
The alliance’s organisation and headquarters would decide the extent of deployment, as well as when and where it would take place. Member countries would make the necessary contributions accordingly, he added.
Responding to questions about the alliance’s military deployments, the spokesperson said that following the signing of the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement (SMDA) between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia last year, there had been further deployments.
“Since 1982, the Pakistan Armed Forces have been present in Saudi Arabia in one capacity or another, sometimes under logistical arrangements and sometimes as part of training missions,” he said.
He added that the three countries had approved measures to strengthen their collective defence capabilities.
“The parties reaffirmed that the security of each country is an integral part of collective security of the three countries and reiterated their determination to defend their security, sovereignty and territorial integrity in accordance with the provisions of the Makkah Agreement,” Khan said.
The move came amid repeated attacks by Yemen’s Houthi movement on Saudi Arabia. Khan said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had strongly condemned the attacks and praised the vigilance of Saudi forces and the coalition in protecting civilian lives.
Pakistan had also condemned a Houthi attack on the Tayeba power distribution station in Medina on October 2, describing it as deeply reprehensible and a grave provocation. Islamabad had stressed the importance of protecting the sanctity of the two holy mosques and the safety of worshippers and pilgrims under all circumstances.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the MJDA, a trilateral security framework intended to strengthen collective deterrence, enhance military cooperation and promote regional stability.
The agreement established a framework for collective defence, under which an armed attack on any one of the three countries would be considered an attack on all three. It built on longstanding military cooperation and followed nearly a year of negotiations amid heightened instability across the Middle East.
The three countries had also reaffirmed their commitment to collective defence at a meeting on September 25, when senior military leadership strongly condemned attacks targeting the holy city of Makkah.
Separately, Khan rejected a statement by Afghanistan’s foreign minister accusing Pakistan of supporting the Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP).
Pakistan categorically rejected the accusation, he said, adding that the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and other terrorist organisations had found safe havens in Kabul and elsewhere in Afghanistan.
He said Pakistan had conveyed the precise locations of these groups to the Afghan authorities at both the political and security levels.
The spokesperson said the military strikes had been highly precise and targeted specific locations where militants were planning and facilitating further attacks against Pakistan. He described the accusations against Pakistan as unfounded.
Khan also rejected allegations concerning Nuristan and said the situation in Afghanistan needed to stabilise.
“The Afghan government must take ownership of the issue and stop facilitating and supporting terrorists who enter Pakistan from Afghanistan and create problems there,” he said.
Reaffirming Islamabad’s long standing stance, the spokesperson said that Pakistan wanted to maintain friendly and good relations with Afghanistan.
UN chief’s visit and Pakistan’s diplomatic engagements
Khan also outlined the visit of United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres to Pakistan from October 6 to 8, saying it had reaffirmed the country’s longstanding partnership with the organisation and provided an opportunity to discuss regional and international developments.
During his talks with Dar on October 6, discussions covered regional and international peace and security, Palestine, Jammu and Kashmir, Afghanistan, terrorism, peacekeeping, sustainable development, climate change and multilateralism.
“The Deputy Prime Minister briefed the Secretary General on Pakistan’s efforts for dialogue and de-escalation, reiterated Pakistan’s position on Jammu and Kashmir, raised concerns over India’s decision to hold the Indus waters treaty in abeyance and highlighted the continued use of Afghan soil for terrorist attacks against Pakistan,” Khan said.
Guterres also met President Asif Ali Zardari, who conferred the Nishan-e-Imtiaz on him in recognition of his international service and contribution to global peace and development.
Also Read: Pakistan committed to 'negotiated and peaceful outcome' between US, Iran: DG ISPR
The UN chief met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi during the visit. He also visited the headquarters of the United Nations Military Observer Group in India and Pakistan (UNMOGIP) and attended a briefing on Pakistan’s disaster preparedness and early warning capabilities at the National Disaster Management Authority.
Khan said Dar had reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to the UN Charter, international law and the peaceful settlement of disputes, while Guterres had stressed the need for stronger multilateral cooperation and a more representative and effective United Nations.
On Pakistan-UK relations, Khan said British Minister of State for the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan Stephen Doughty met FM Dar on October 6. The two sides reviewed bilateral relations and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in trade and investment, education, security and other areas of mutual interest.
“They also exchanged views on regional and international developments and agreed to work towards early operationalisation of the UK-Pakistan bilateral political consultations and dialogue,” he said.
Khan also said FM Dar met Belarusian National Security Adviser Lieutenant General Alexander Volfovich on October 7. The two sides reviewed bilateral relations and expressed satisfaction with the positive momentum in ties, reaffirming their commitment to further cooperation.

Bahrain’s Foreign Minister Dr Abdul Latif bin Rashid Al Zayani visited Pakistan from October 7 to 8 at the invitation of Dar. The two foreign ministers held discussions on bilateral cooperation and regional developments and co-chaired the third session of the Pakistan-Bahrain Joint Ministerial Commission.
“The two sides reviewed the entire spectrum of bilateral relations and discussed ways to further strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, economic, defence and security ties, labour and manpower, cultural exchanges and other areas of mutual interest,” Khan said.
The two sides also exchanged views on regional and international developments and cooperation at multilateral forums.
Khan said Archbishop Paul Richard, Secretary for Relations with States and International Organisations of the Holy See, had arrived in Pakistan on October 8 for a three-day visit. It was the first visit to Pakistan by a secretary for relations with states and international organisations of the Holy See and coincided with the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and the Holy See.
During his meeting with Dar, the two sides discussed interfaith harmony, dialogue and peace, as well as regional and international developments.
Pakistan protests Indian border killings
Khan said Pakistan had lodged a strong protest with India after two Pakistani civilians were killed by Indian Border Security Force personnel in the Bedian sector of Lahore along the international border on October 2.
The Indian charge d’affaires was summoned to the Foreign Office on October 3, and Pakistan rejected what it described as the unprovoked and disproportionate use of lethal force against unarmed civilians.
Islamabad called on India to conduct an immediate, transparent and credible investigation, take appropriate legal and disciplinary action against those responsible and share its findings with Pakistan.
“India was also urged to respect international law, fundamental human rights, relevant bilateral arrangements and established border procedures, exercise maximum restraint and take effective measures to prevent such recurrences in the future,” Khan said.
Khan said four injured Pakistani crew members of the MT Honour 25, along with the remains of three Pakistani nationals, had been repatriated from Addis Ababa to Karachi on October 4. The remaining three crew members returned to Pakistan on October 7.
Pakistan’s missions in Djibouti and Addis Ababa had facilitated their stay and return, he said.
Dar raises Indus Waters Treaty at international symposium
Khan also highlighted Dar’s keynote address, delivered by video link to the International Water Symposium in Vienna on October 6. The event was organised by Pakistan’s embassy in Austria in collaboration with the Diplomatic Academy of Vienna.
The symposium brought together diplomats, academics and experts to discuss water security, transboundary river governance and obligations under international law.
In his address, Dar condemned what Pakistan described as India’s weaponisation of water, reaffirmed Islamabad’s commitment to the Indus Waters Treaty and referred to a Court of Arbitration award, saying the treaty remained in force and its obligations had to be respected.
“He underscored that shared water should remain instruments of peace and cooperation, not coercion, and reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to defending its rights under the treaty,” Khan concluded.

title: Anthropic bans  cruel  behaviour against its Claude AI
description: Policy does not explicitly cite  model welfare   comes amid philosophical debate over machine consciousness
content:
Policy does not explicitly cite 'model welfare', comes amid philosophical debate over machine consciousness
Anthropic on Thursday moved to bar users from treating its Claude AI system with needless cruelty, amid a growing philosophical debate over whether artificial intelligence can be conscious.
The San Francisco-based AI lab updated its usage policy to include "a prohibition on sustained and needless abusive or cruel behaviour toward our models." "Claude's ability to end these interactions will remain the primary enforcement mechanism," the policy states.
The updated policy does not explicitly cite so-called "model welfare," the idea that AI systems might deserve types of protection usually reserved for living things, but Anthropic and its executives have openly entertained the concept.
Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Read: Most US voters say Trump, Congress don't take AI risks seriously, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
Already last year, the company said it was giving Claude the ability to end conversations in rare, extreme cases of "persistently harmful or abusive user interactions."
Then in February, CEO Dario Amodei told The New York Times he was unsure whether AI models could be conscious. "We don't know if the models are conscious...But we're open to the idea that it could be," Amodei said.
Science fiction and popular culture have been fascinated for decades by the boundary between technology and human intelligence, but asking whether AI is conscious may be the wrong question, according to Jackson Stakeman, a general manager at Sparq, an Atlanta-based AI services provider. "Consciousness is a trap. We can't prove it in each other. Debate it for AI and you go in circles," Stakeman told AFP .
"The mirror is a better metaphor. These systems reflect what we put in, at scale. That's reason enough for the policy change" at Anthropic, he added.
Read More: AI's race to transform the world before the money runs out
Some have rejected the idea of machine consciousness outright, including Pope Leo XIV and Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman.
"AIs are not conscious. They do not feel, experience, or suffer," Suleyman wrote in an essay last month. "Granting rights and moral protections to a technological entity, one that looks to be on a path to be seismically more capable and intelligent than us, is a recipe for disaster," he wrote.
In a sermon delivered in Italian on Thursday at St Peter's Basilica in Vatican City, the pope suggested machines lack a soul, saying they merely "compile data" quickly. "The mind must not simply compile data — as an algorithm now does more quickly than we can," the pontiff said.
It must "recall lived experiences, which contain depths of meaning that only the human soul can recognise, and connect more deeply with the goodness of these experiences," the pope said.

title: SpaceX strikes spectrum deal  paving way for Starlink to become major US mobile carrier
description: Says communications authority also approved 15 000 next generation satellites to deliver service
content:
Says communications authority also approved 15,000 next-generation satellites to deliver service
SpaceX announced on Thursday an agreement to acquire nationwide low-band spectrum licenses, advancing plans to turn Starlink Mobile into a major US mobile carrier through a network combining satellite and terrestrial services.
The agreement covers up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band, the company said in a statement . The acquisition remains subject to final Federal Communications Commission (FCC) approval.
SpaceX said the spectrum would address a key technical gap by allowing signals to penetrate obstacles such as walls, helping provide coverage inside buildings. Most existing mobile devices already support the band, it added.
We announced an agreement to acquire a nationwide low-band spectrum license portfolio that will pave the way for @Starlink to become a major mobile carrier in the US. With this new spectrum and our Gen2 constellation, Starlink Mobile can ensure Americans have access to… pic.twitter.com/uVktZ0g3tu
The low-band frequencies would complement Starlink Mobile's global 2 GHz mid-band spectrum, which the company plans to use for high-bandwidth capacity in the US.
Once regulatory approval is secured, SpaceX plans to combine its satellite-to-mobile constellation with terrestrial infrastructure to provide connectivity indoors, outdoors and in areas without cellular coverage.
Also Read: Will SpaceX paint its rocket pink? Investor questions go beyond Moon and Mars ahead of first results
Separately, SpaceX said the FCC this week approved its next-generation Starlink Mobile constellation application, authorising the launch of 15,000 satellites optimised for global operations using 2 GHz spectrum.
The company said its V2 Starlink Mobile satellites would deliver more than 100 times the bandwidth of the current generation, supporting high-speed connections directly to unmodified mobile devices.
The FCC also authorised additional communications bands that would allow the satellites to use Starlink's existing ground gateway network, according to SpaceX.

title: Zverev churns out win in Shanghai Masters opener
description: The German overcomes Wu 6 4  7 6  7 4   while Mannarino claims a three set upset over Cobolli
content:
The German overcomes Wu 6-4, 7-6 (7/4), while Mannarino claims a three-set upset over Cobolli
Top seed Alexander Zverev churned out an opening win over Chinese wildcard Wu Yibing 6-4, 7-6 (7/4) at the Shanghai Masters on Friday to advance into the third round.
A dive left the German grimacing and grabbing his left ankle during the 11th game of the second set, with Wu, ranked 113th in the world, going up 6-5.
But the 29-year-old held serve and forced a tie-break, capitalising on a series of errors to win on his second match point when the home hope fired long.
"Credit to him, he was playing amazing tennis," Zverev told the crowd afterwards.
"He hits every ball as hard as he can," he added in another on-court interview, crediting a reliable serve for his straight-sets win.
Zverev, the world number two, is on track to end the year with the top ranking after Jannik Sinner announced he was ending his 2026 season due to injury.
Zverev next faces Quentin Halys of France, who downed Belgium's Alexander Blockx in three sets. Earlier, third-seeded Ben Shelton beat Germany's Daniel Altmaier 6-3, 7-6 (8/6) and will play France's Arthur Gea in the third round.
"Tough match-up," said the American, who double-faulted five times across the gritty two-hour match. "Happy with the way I finished." It was a fitting birthday present for Shelton, who turned 24 on Friday, though he hinted he may pass on indulging, telling an on-court interviewer: "I hate cake."
Frenchman Adrian Mannarino upset sixth-seeded Flavio Cobolli 6-1, 4-6, 6-3.
Cobolli, the French Open finalist, twice fell to the ground as he failed to convert two break points in the last game.
The Italian, 24, saved a match point with a well-placed volley but could not stay afloat as 38-year-old Mannarino kept him running and forced him into a backhand he could not return. Mannarino, ranked 83rd, will face either Karen Khachanov or Arthur Fery in the next round.
Elsewhere in the draw, Japanese qualifier Rei Sakamoto beat Russia's Andrey Rublev 6-4, 6-4. Sakamoto, the world number 137, will next play ninth-seeded Alex de Minaur, who advanced after his opponent Alex Molcan withdrew before play.
Later on Friday, Serbian veteran Novak Djokovic was due to start his title bid in the second round against Poland's Hubert Hurkacz.

title: Crazy Rich Asians    returns with original stars for eight episode HBO drama
description: Kevin Kwan says fans will finally see his characters explored in greater depth on television
content:
Kevin Kwan says fans will finally see his characters explored in greater depth on television
The world of Crazy Rich Asians is returning to television, with Constance Wu, Henry Golding, Ronny Chieng and Michelle Yeoh reprising their roles in a new HBO drama series based on Kevin Kwan’s bestselling novels.
Wu, Golding and Chieng have joined the project as series regulars, while Yeoh will appear in a recurring role. The series will continue the story introduced in the 2018 film, bringing its original cast back together for a longer exploration of its characters and their relationships.
Adele Lim, who co wrote the original film, will serve as showrunner and executive producer. She described the production as a reunion for the creative team and said the eight episode format would allow the story to explore the characters and their world in greater depth.
Kevin Kwan, author of the novels, also welcomed the project, saying international fans had waited patiently for the next chapter. He expressed excitement about seeing his characters develop through a television adaptation.
The series is based on Kwan’s book trilogy, which began with Crazy Rich Asians in 2013, followed by China Rich Girlfriend in 2015 and Rich People Problems in 2017.
Jon M Chu, who directed the original film, is returning as an executive producer alongside Lim, Kwan, Nina Jacobson and Brad Simpson. The project is co produced by HBO and Warner Bros Television.
Released in 2018, Crazy Rich Asians became a major box office success, earning more than $239m worldwide against a reported production budget of $30m. The romantic comedy also received strong critical reviews and helped bring a predominantly Asian cast to the centre of a major Hollywood studio production.
A feature film sequel had been in development for years but had not moved forward. The television adaptation now offers another route for continuing the story.
No premiere date has been announced in the supplied report. The returning cast and original creative team, however, mark a significant step towards revisiting the popular fictional world.

title: Pakistan committed to  negotiated and peaceful outcome  between US  Iran  DG ISPR
description: Says Pakistan has been  a very honest broker  and has been clear about its position with all its partners  friends
content:
Says Pakistan has been 'a very honest broker' and has been clear about its position with all its partners, friends
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has said that Pakistan would continue to work towards a “negotiated and peaceful outcome” to the conflict between the United States and Iran, stressing that the war should not “expand horizontally or vertically”.
“We want that this conflict should not expand horizontally or vertically,” Chaudhry said in an interview with CNN correspondent Ivan Watson on Wednesday, a clip of which was shared by Pakistan Television on X on Friday.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
Asked whether Pakistan could continue to act as a neutral broker despite its defence commitments to Saudi Arabia under the Makkah Defence Alliance, Chaudhry said Islamabad had demonstrated its impartiality through its responses to attacks on both Iran and Gulf countries.
“I think what Pakistan has been doing is exhibiting that we have been a very honest broker,” he said, adding that Pakistan had been clear about its position with all its partners and friends.
In an interview with CNN, DG ISPR Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry says Pakistani troops have been deployed in Saudi Arabia for decades, adding that Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye have longstanding diplomatic, political and military relations. @OfficialDGISPR … pic.twitter.com/dVcNT74nbX
He said Pakistan had openly condemned attacks on Iran by Israel and the United States, as well as Iranian attacks on Arab and Gulf countries. “We don't mince our words. Why? Because we have a stake in regional peace and stability,” he said. “We tell all that nobody benefits from expanding this war.”
The military spokesperson's remarks came amid continued regional tensions and questions over how Pakistan would balance its mediation efforts with its defence commitments to Saudi Arabia.
On Pakistan's military presence in Saudi Arabia, Chaudhry confirmed that Pakistani forces were already in the Kingdom, “The Pakistani troops have been there for decades, in multiple capacities have been there for decades in Saudi Arabia,” he said, pointing to the longstanding diplomatic, political and military ties between the three countries.
He said the alliance had not emerged in isolation and was built on sustained relations between the countries. “The Makkah Accord, its actualisation and whatever effects it achieves, that will be purely defensive,” Chaudhry said.
He declined to provide details about how or when forces would be deployed under the agreement, “How that will be done, which component will go there, how it will be employed, that's for the operational commanders to decide,” he said, adding that participating countries did not disclose operational details during a military conflict.
Read: Makkah pact: DG ISPR says Pakistani troops present in Saudi Arabia in 'multiple capabilities'
“The objective of this is not to start labelling enemies and friends,” he said. “The objective is the defence of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and their military.” He added that the three countries had significant military, diplomatic and other capabilities, which could discourage potential attacks against any member of the alliance.
In a major development that may have far-reaching implications for the region, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye activated the practical implementation of their collective defence commitments on Monday.
According to a joint statement issued on Monday night, the activation entailed immediate deployment of "the agreed military forces and capabilities to the kingdom in response to security threats".
The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of the Strategic-Political and Defence Committee of the alliance, held in Riyadh to discuss the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia is currently engaged in an active conflict with Houthis, who have been targeting the various strategic and economic assets in the kingdom.
However, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on Tuesday had rejected what it described as “speculative” reporting by Reuters on the pact, saying operational details concerning the implementation of the collective deterrence mechanism were confidential.
The ministry’s statement followed a Reuters report published on October 2, which said Pakistan had deployed between 30,000 and 40,000 troops to Saudi Arabia to help defend the kingdom’s land borders and assist with drone and missile interceptions, citing a Pakistani official. Reuters reported that Islamabad had not decided to send troops into Yemen in a fighting capacity.
