title: Margaret Hamilton  scientist who worked on NASA s Apollo programme  dead at 90
description: Computing pioneer was awarded Presidential Medal of Freedom by Obama  published over 130 papers
content:
Computing pioneer was awarded Presidential Medal of Freedom by Obama, published over 130 papers
American scientist Margaret Hamilton, who led development of the computer system used by NASA's Apollo lunar programme, has died at the age of 90, her former employer said Wednesday.
In a statement, the Massachussetts Institute of Technology called Hamilton, who taught at the prestigious university from 1959 to the mid-1970s, a "computing pioneer" and said she died on September 30.
We’ve lost an icon. Margaret Hamilton, a computer science pioneer best known for her work at MIT leading development of the flight software for the Apollo missions to the moon, has died at 90. Read about her legacy via MIT News: https://t.co/ODkbdIsoHw pic.twitter.com/M2xauYYUkU
"To say Margaret Hamilton was a pioneer — to say she was ahead of her time — would be a dramatic understatement," said Olivier de Weck, the Apollo Programme Professor and interim head of the MIT Department Aeronautics and Astronautics.
"She was a software engineer at a time when that field was in its infancy, and she not only developed advanced code herself but also led a team in using that nascent technology to develop one of the most complex systems humanity had ever achieved," Weck added.
The famed Apollo programme allowed the United States to beat the Soviet Union in the race to become the first humans to land on the Moon.
NASA chief Jared Isaacmen paid tribute on X, calling Hamilton "a pioneer whose work helped make Apollo and humanity's first journeys to the moon possible."
Margaret Hamilton was a pioneer whose work helped make Apollo and humanity’s first journeys to the Moon possible. The best way to honor her legacy is to finally pick up where her generation left off and never stop going. https://t.co/SZ16EX5GcK
Born in Indiana in 1936, Hamilton studied mathematics before moving to Boston, Massachussetts with her husband in 1959. She found employment at MIT, working in meteorology before she joined a lab in 1965 that was seeking people to develop software to "send a man to the Moon."
Hamilton "was hired as the first programmer for the Apollo project at MIT, as well as the first female programmer in the project," the university said. "By 1968, she was assistant director in charge of (Apollo's) Command and Service Module team, and more than 400 people were working on Apollo's software," MIT said.
Hamilton was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by former president Barack Obama in 2016 for her achievements.
Read: Trump signs order to create a US Space Academy
In 2009, Hamilton told MIT News : "There was no second chance. We knew that. We took our work seriously, many of us beginning this journey while still in our 20s."
"Coming up with solutions and new ideas was an adventure. Dedication and commitment were a given. Mutual respect was across the board. Because software was a mystery, a black box, upper management gave us total freedom and trust," Hamilton added. "Looking back, we were the luckiest people in the world; there was no choice but to be pioneers," she said.
Hamilton went on to publish more than 130 papers, and started her own software companies Higher Order Software and Hamilton Technologies.

title: Gul urges smarter  harder training to revive squash
description: Coach says players fear hard training  need more matches to progress
content:
Coach says players fear hard training, need more matches to progress
Pakistan squash coach Faheem Gul believes harder and smarter training can help the country’s players improve their world rankings and compete effectively at a higher level in international circuit. “I think there is a need for harder and smarter training,” Faheem Gul told The Express Tribune in a detailed chat. “People talk about seven to eight hours of training, but things have changed a lot. Everything is scientific now. Even if players manage two hours of harder and smarter training, they can still make progress. The problem is that the boys are afraid of training,” Faheem said. Faheem recently coached Pakistan’s squash team at the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, where the country won one silver and two bronze medals in squash. Pakistan’s top-ranked player Noor Zaman, and Mohammad Ashab Irfan claimed bronze medals in the men’s singles, while the men’s team, featuring Noor, Irfan and Nasir Iqbal, won silver. Faheem was satisfied with the overall performance but felt Pakistan had missed an opportunity to win gold in the team event. “The boys did well, and we could have won the team event final had Noor won his match. He was leading 2-1 but lost the next two games,” Faheem said. Malaysia’s Ameeshenraj defeated Nasir Iqbal 3-1 before Yow Eain Ng secured a hard-fought 3-2 victory over Noor Zaman to clinch the team gold for Malaysia. Faheem had mixed feelings about Nasir’s performance, saying the Pakistani player needed to become more consistent. “Nasir is good, but the problem is that he wins a game and then loses momentum and is unable to maintain it,” Faheem said. “Our boys will need to work harder if they are to improve their rankings,” he added. Faheem said Pakistan had almost no realistic chance of qualifying for the squash events at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. “There is no chance. It has ended. The winner of the men’s singles event at the Asian Games had to qualify,” Faheem said. “Only 16 players will compete in the Olympics and we are out,” he was quick to add. Squash will make its Olympic debut in Los Angeles, with 16 players competing in each of the men’s and women’s events. Under the qualification framework, places are allocated through continental championships, the host nation, world rankings, a universality place and a final qualifying tournament. The Asian Games singles champions secured continental qualification, with Malaysia’s Yow Eain Ng and Sivasangari Subramaniam winning the men’s and women’s titles, respectively, in Nagoya. Pakistan’s chances have almost ended, given the current world rankings of its leading players. Noor Zaman is the country’s highest-ranked player at No 30, followed by Mohammad Ashab Irfan at No 49, Asim Khan at No 77 and Nasir Iqbal at No 95. Even if a Pakistani player secures a place in the final qualifying tournament, he would still need to win through to reach the Olympics. Faheem also stressed the importance of competing more regularly on the international circuit. “Yes, they will need to play eight to ten matches, and I think they have started playing more now,” he said. Looking ahead, Faheem expressed confidence that Pakistan could win gold at the upcoming 3rd Asian Team Squash Championships which will be held in Islamabad from November 3-7. “We are confident of winning gold,” he said. However, he was less optimistic about the standard of women’s squash in Pakistan, saying considerable work remained to bring the players up to international standards. “They have a long way to go. Their standard is not that good,” Faheem said.

title: Polish police arrest multiple teens over  Bloody Friday  school attack threats
description: Social media in Poland is filled with talk of an    online challenge that could be behind the attacks
content:
Social media in Poland is filled with talk of an ​online challenge that could be behind the attacks
Polish police have arrested a string of young people, mainly for making ‌threats related to school attacks, they said on Friday, as authorities sought to calm fears spurred by rumours online of a "Bloody Friday" after two stabbing sprees in as many days.
Social media in Poland has been filled with talk of a ​supposed online challenge that could be behind the attacks, but police on Friday said their ​investigations had found no evidence of this.
The incidents have prompted a nationwide security response, ⁠with police deployed to 10,000 schools and the government warning against the spread of misinformation that officials ​fear could inspire copycat attacks.
Also Read: Nine injured in Polish stabbing spree
"There is a lot of emotionally charged misinformation circulating online — spontaneous reactions born of ​understandable anxiety — but there is no sign of any nationwide 'challenge' taking place," Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski told private broadcaster TVN24 .
"We cannot rule out the possibility that one, two or three individuals might be communicating in a group, hatching a ​plan, or that a copycat could emerge. However, we see no evidence of a threat stemming from ​a group of people coordinating to harm someone today."
Police said they had detained 10 people, mainly ‌for ⁠making threats online, with further arrests being announced as the morning progressed.
These included a 13-year-old from Warsaw who posted a photo of a knife in a class group chat and threatened other students, a 14-year-old in Warsaw detained on school grounds with a knife and firecrackers, and two 15-year-olds from Pruszkow County just ​outside the capital who ​posted a video with ⁠threats to kill.
On Thursday, a 15-year-old former pupil wearing a helmet-mounted camera killed one employee and injured two others at a Polish primary school in Leszczydol-Nowiny, northeast ​of Warsaw. On Wednesday, a 19-year-old wounded 10 people, including himself, at another school ​in Ostroleka, northeastern ⁠Poland.

Several social media accounts posted pictures of a TikTok account which supposedly belonged to Thursday's attacker and featured images taken before the attack. Reuters was unable to find the account, which appeared to have been taken ⁠down.
"Officers from ​the Central Bureau for Combating Cybercrime are aware of the ​content posted on the TikTok account in question," CBZC told Reuters by email, adding that it was cooperating with the platform.

title: Three terrorists killed in joint CTD  police operation in K P s Tank
description: Personnel come under fire on reaching location  exchange continued for some time before a search operation began
content:
Personnel come under fire on reaching location, exchange continued for some time before a search operation began
Three terrorists belonging to the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) Bhittani Group were killed during an intelligence-based operation jointly conducted by the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) and district police in Tank on Friday, according to a CTD statement.
The operation was carried out in the Garah Fakira area along Jandola Road in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), within the jurisdiction of SMA police station, after the CTD received intelligence that terrorists were present in the area and planning a major attack, the statement said.
Security personnel came under fire when they reached the location and returned fire in self-defence and in an attempt to arrest the suspects. The exchange of gunfire continued for some time.
After the firing stopped, a search operation was conducted in the area, during which three bodies were found. Two of the men were identified as Osama, son of Sultan, and Suleman, son of Wali Muhammad, both residents of Faqeer Kallay in Jandola. The identity of the third man was still being established, the statement added.
The CTD said preliminary information suggested that the men had been involved in several terrorist attacks.
According to the statement, the suspects had planted an improvised explosive device (IED) on the roof of a shop near the Meera Alam petrol pump. The device exploded, killing two police personnel and a civilian and injuring seven people.

The men had also planted an IED along the main road in Wana Bazaar and another on the roof of the office of Bilal, the head of a peace committee, the CTD said.
The statement added that Osama was the brother of Shoaib, a terrorist killed during an attack on Bannu Cantonment in 2025. Musa, who was killed in retaliatory fire after attacking police in Wana Bazaar, was also Osama’s cousin.
Security personnel recovered three Kalashnikov rifles, 11 magazines containing ammunition, and a mobile phone during the search operation. K-P Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed and the additional inspector general of the CTD praised the personnel involved in the operation for their professionalism, courage and bravery.
They reaffirmed their commitment to continuing operations against terrorism in the province and protecting the lives and property of the public, the statement concluded.
On September 25, the K-P CTD said it had foiled a major terrorist attack in Peshawar, killing one terrorist during an intelligence-based operation in the Garhi Sherdad area of Warsak Road.
The department said it had received intelligence that three suicide attackers had entered the provincial capital to target a sensitive installation. CTD Constable Muhammad Afaq was martyred, and three other personnel were injured in the exchange of fire, while a search operation was launched to apprehend the two remaining attackers.

title: Wealthy Gen Z collectors spend more on art than older buyers  report shows
description: A survey of 3 100 wealthy buyers across 10 markets finds Gen Z spent significantly more on art than older generations
content:
A survey of 3,100 wealthy buyers across 10 markets finds Gen Z spent significantly more on art than older generations
Wealthy Gen Z collectors spend far more on fine art than purchasers from any other generation, according to a report published on Thursday ​by Art Basel and Swiss bank UBS.
A survey of 3,100 ‌wealthy buyers from across 10 major markets showed individuals from Gen Z - the youngest adult generation - spent more than twice as much on artworks as those from older generations during 2025 and ​the first half of this year.
The study, which defined ​Gen Z as people aged between 20 and 29, showed ⁠the second-biggest spenders were Baby Boomers in the 62 to ​80 age bracket. Millennials (aged 30 to 45) were next, with wealthy Gen ​X respondents (aged 46 to 61) the most frugal in their art spending.
On average, the individual Gen Z collectors polled spent $347,000 on fine art last year, compared to just $79,000 among their ​Gen X counterparts. Some 40% of the Gen Z respondents cited ​the influence of family as their primary route into collecting.
Younger collectors continue to favour traditional categories such as painting and sculpture, Paul Donovan, chief economist at UBS Global Wealth Management, said in the report. “Some aesthetic preferences remain more consistent across generations than is often assumed,” Donovan said.
The survey also found that almost half the respondents gave preference to an artwork’s uniqueness and rarity over owning something admired by experts or collectors.
The respondents were high-net-worth individuals, which the survey defined as people with a net worth, excluding real estate and private business assets, of over $1 million in 2026.
The report also highlighted rising usage of AI tools for research purchases, as the number of collectors using them has increased from 4 per cent in 2024 to 22pc now.

title: Indian youth leader says protest will go ahead despite detentions
description: Police in the capital said the CJP did not have permission for Saturday s protest
content:
Police in the capital say the Cockroach Janata Party did not have permission for Saturday's protest
The leader ​of India's " Cockroach " youth movement said a major planned protest would go ahead in New Delhi on ‌Saturday, despite the detentions of followers he estimated to run into the thousands, calling for the resignation of the top poll official.
The dispute centres on a controversial revision of voting lists that dropped 130 million voters nationwide, spurring demands by the youth movement, opposition ​parties, and their student units for the official, Gyanesh Kumar, to resign.
"I'll be landing in Delhi ​tomorrow and will march to Jantar Mantar, come what may," Abhijeet Dipke, the founder ⁠of the Cockroach Janata Party, said on X on Friday, referring to a designated protest site in ​the capital.
Thousands of youngsters have been detained across country by the BJP Govt ahead of our October 10 protest. This intimidation is not going to work, Modi. The youth of this country are no longer scared of you. I’ll be landing in Delhi tomorrow and will march to Jantar Mantar,…
"The youth of this country are no longer scared of you," he added in the message, addressing ​Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
The world's largest democracy, with at least 960 million eligible voters in 2024, India began the verification effort last year ahead of elections in the eastern state of Bihar and has now covered the majority of states.
Police in the capital said the CJP did not have permission for Saturday's protest and could ​face legal action if protesters violated rules.
Thousands of police and paramilitary forces, including some from sensitive areas such as Indian Illegally Occupied ‌Jammu and Kashmir, ⁠were being brought in to the capital, according to a government document seen by Reuters .
The CJP said police in several states were detaining thousands of its supporters as they headed for Saturday's protest.

Reuters could not immediately verify the claims or videos posted on X.
The opposition Congress, led by Rahul Gandhi, has called for a ​meeting of allies from more ​than a dozen parties ⁠opposed to Modi and the BJP.
The opposition bloc will meet President Droupadi Murmu, a constitutional figurehead, on Friday evening.
Some long-distance trains to ​New Delhi on Saturday were cancelled. Authorities said police had asked for fewer ​metro train services, ⁠with some exits shut, citing the possibility of "unruly" mobs, according to documents seen by Reuters .

Opposition parties and critics say the latest revision, nearly two decades after the last, constitutes mass disenfranchisement to favour the BJP. They want ⁠the exercise scrapped ​and the old voter lists reinstated.
The election commission says the ​numbers represent voter entries flagged during a draft revision, in an exercise still incomplete, while those wrongly removed can enroll again.

title: Katrina Kaif speaks out on social media criticism after post pregnancy trolling
description: Indian actor addresses online scrutiny at a London event  urging people not to let social media shape their self worth
content:
Indian actor addresses online scrutiny at a London event, urging people not to let social media shape their self-worth
Indian actor Katrina Kaif has spoken out against body-shaming and the pressure to meet social media expectations, saying that allowing criticism to dictate her choices could have left her “paralysed with fear”.
Speaking in London at an event marking the UK anniversary of her beauty brand, Kay Beauty, Kaif addressed the scrutiny she has faced over her appearance since becoming a mother.
“We really need to be careful of letting the narrative on social media affect our self-worth and our value,” she said, emphasising that online reactions should not determine how people perceive themselves.
Kaif's remarks came weeks after she and her husband, Vicky Kaushal, attended the Ambani family's Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations in Mumbai in September.
Photographs and videos from the event prompted comments about her weight and appearance following childbirth. Kaif welcomed her son in November 2025.
The criticism also prompted an outpouring of support from fans, who challenged the body-shaming directed at new mothers. Filmmaker Soundarya Rajinikanth was among those who spoke out against judging women for changes to their bodies after pregnancy.
Without directly naming those who had criticised her, Kaif reflected on how trying to satisfy everyone could undermine a person's confidence and ability to make independent decisions.
“Personally for me, if every time that I faced critiques or comments, I let that dictate my actions, I think I would have been paralysed with fear and unable to move ahead in my life or in any sphere of life,” she said.
“There are times where the world is going to celebrate you and other times you have to really be your own biggest cheerleader,” she added.
Kaif also linked her comments to Kay Beauty's tagline, “It's K to be you”, which promotes self-acceptance rather than the pursuit of a fixed ideal.
Acknowledging that confidence can fluctuate, she said people go through periods when they feel at their best and others when they struggle to reach that point.
“There are times when you feel like you’re acing everything in life, and there are other times when you feel like you just can’t get anything right. There are times when you feel like you’re looking and feeling like the best version of yourself, and other times when you’re kind of on a journey to get there,” she continued.
Kaif encouraged people to approach these ups and downs with perspective, saying it was important to “wear it all lightly and not take yourself too seriously also and just have fun with it”.
The debate surrounding Kaif's appearance has also drawn attention to the wider scrutiny women face over their bodies after pregnancy.
On a recent episode of Bigg Boss 20 , host Salman Khan criticised those who comment on women's weight gain after childbirth. Although he did not name Kaif, his remarks were widely interpreted by viewers as a show of support for the actor.
Khan said weight gain after pregnancy was natural and that new mothers should be given time to spend with their families instead of being subjected to commentary about their appearance.
On the professional front, Kaif was last seen alongside Vijay Sethupathi in Sriram Raghavan's 2024 thriller Merry Christmas . Her anticipated projects include the all-female road-trip drama Jee Le Zaraa , while early discussions have also taken place around Chandni Bar 2 .

title: Ben Affleck   s  Animals  gets roasted by critics as Rotten Tomatoes reviews bash Netflix thriller
description: The film is a contemporary reworking of Akira Kurosawa   s 1963 crime drama  High and Low
content:
The film is a contemporary reworking of Akira Kurosawa’s 1963 crime drama 'High and Low'
Ben Affleck’s crime thriller Animals is facing a wave of negative reviews from critics as the Netflix film arrives on Rotten Tomatoes, with several reviewers criticising its writing, storytelling and execution.
Directed by and starring Affleck, the film follows Mark Kimball, a Los Angeles mayoral candidate whose life spirals into crisis after his son is reported kidnapped. As he struggles to raise a $7 million ransom, the situation takes a complicated turn when the kidnappers are revealed to have taken the son of his family’s housekeeper instead.
The film also stars Kerry Washington as Mark’s wife, Abigail, alongside Steven Yeun, Gillian Anderson, Adriana Paz and Luis Gerardo Méndez. The story explores political ambition, privilege, immigration and the moral choices facing a wealthy family caught in a kidnapping crisis.
However, early reviews have been largely critical. The Associated Press described the film as lacking narrative energy and emotional depth, arguing that its potentially compelling themes are undermined by forced melodrama and flat visuals. The review awarded the film two out of four stars.
Vulture was similarly harsh, calling Animals a “catastrophe” and criticising its writing, disjointed storytelling and underdeveloped characters. The review also argued that the film fails to deliver the moral complexity and tension expected from a kidnapping thriller.
RogerEbert.com also delivered a negative assessment, describing the film as Affleck’s worst directorial effort and criticising its handling of political hypocrisy and immigration. The review argued that the story raises important issues without exploring them in a sufficiently compelling way.
Not every critic has dismissed the film. The Financial Times praised Animals as a tightly constructed thriller, awarding it four stars and highlighting the supporting performances, particularly Gillian Anderson’s portrayal of a mysterious crisis fixer.
Animals is directed by Affleck and written by Affleck, Billy Ray and Connor O. McIntyre. The film is a contemporary reworking of Akira Kurosawa’s 1963 crime drama High and Low , relocating the story to Los Angeles and placing its kidnapping plot against the backdrop of a mayoral campaign.
The film is available on Netflix from October 9, 2026, giving viewers the chance to judge the thriller for themselves amid the divided critical response.

title: US voices concern over Houthi escalation  condemns attacks on Saudi Arabia
description: A Saudi led coalition said it had destroyed three missile launch platforms used by the Houthis
content:
Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport killed three Saudis as war escalates
The US strongly condemned Houthi attacks on civilian infrastructure and airports in Saudi Arabia on Friday, calling on Iran to end its support for the Yemeni group.
"The United States is gravely concerned by the continued escalation by the terrorist Houthis," US deputy envoy to the UN Jeff Bartos told a Security Council meeting.
Bartos cited recent Houthi missile strikes on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh as an example of the threat posed by the group.
He accused the Houthis of acting as "instruments" of Tehran, saying their activities undermined regional stability, threatened maritime navigation and “terrorised” civilians.
🔴 BREAKING: US envoy at UN Security Council meeting on Yemen - Houthis must stop their attacks on Yemen and Saudi Arabia; we stand in solidarity with Yemen and Kingdom following Houthi attacks https://t.co/2bLWE9JoS6 pic.twitter.com/8J0ye4EmDi
"We demand that the Houthis cease their attacks against the legitimate governments of Yemen and Saudi Arabia, and we demand that Iran cease all support to the Houthis," Bartos said.
"In the face of the Houthi threat, the United States stands firmly with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the government of Yemen as they defend their sovereignty and work to restore stability," he added.
Bartos reaffirmed Washington's commitment to working with regional and international partners to counter the Houthi threat, protect navigational rights and freedoms, and promote long-term stability across the region.
Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport killed three Saudis as war escalates
Thursday's attacks on Riyadh airport killed three people, Saudi authorities said on Friday, as Yemen's Houthi group stepped up missile strikes on the kingdom and tried to shut down its airspace in an escalating war triggered by the US-Iran conflict.
The strikes, which also injured several people, damaged a Saudia Airlines plane and sent smoke billowing over the airport, led many airlines to cancel flights to the Saudi capital days before it is due to host a major meeting of global oil chiefs.
#Statement Two attacks targeted King Khalid International Airport facilities and a Saudia aircraft. #GACA pic.twitter.com/6YnBN717Cw
Saudi airstrikes hit Houthi targets in the Yemeni capital Sanaa overnight, Houthi officials and affiliated media said, part of an intensifying air war against the Iran-allied group aimed at reversing its recent territorial gains, threats to international shipping, and attacks on the kingdom.
A Saudi-led coalition backing government forces in Yemen said it had destroyed three missile launch platforms used by the Houthis. It warned it would respond firmly to attacks on civilians.
Read: PIA temporarily suspends flight operations to Riyadh, cites Middle East conflict
The Houthis, who have encircled Yemeni government forces in Yemen's third-largest city of Taiz and are trying to defend positions on the Red Sea coast against a Saudi-backed offensive, had already killed three people with strikes on airports in the kingdom earlier this week.
The Saudi civil aviation authority said air traffic at Riyadh airport had returned to normal, and flight-tracking site flightradar24 showed a gradual resumption of flights, including from some Middle Eastern airlines.
Saudia Airlines said one of those killed on Thursday was one of its employees.
Yemen's civil war has rapidly emerged as the fiercest front in a wider regional conflagration triggered by the US and Israeli attack on Iran that started on February 28.
The conflict is critical for global energy markets, with the Houthis firing on shipping in the Red Sea and its southern gateway, the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, further squeezing Gulf oil supplies with Iran partly blocking the Strait of Hormuz.
Last month the Houthis staged a lightning advance down Yemen's Red Sea coast to take full control over the coastline around the strait, prompting Saudi Arabia to re-enter the long-dormant conflict and back a government counteroffensive.
Read more: Information ministry rubbishes 'fake and fabricated' NYT report claiming use of PAF aircraft against Houthis
On Monday, government forces took back territory around the Bab el-Mandeb coastline after intense Saudi airstrikes and fighting continued there.
However, Houthi forces have also managed to cut off a key road connecting Taiz, a city of more than half a million people with a garrison of thousands of pro-government fighters, with advances in mountain districts.
The group has announced repeated rounds of ballistic missile fire at Saudi Arabia, proclaiming it would shut down Saudi airspace and warning workers at oil facilities that it would strike those too.
Saudi Arabia is seeking assistance from Pakistan and Turkey, its partners in a mutual defence pact, to help ward off Houthi attacks, and has pushed for wider help from allies to aid it in reversing the group's gains inside Yemen.
Bab el-Mandeb 'cleared of Houthi remnants,' Saudi envoy to Yemen says
Saudi Ambassador to Yemen, Mohammed Al Jaber, said on Friday that the Bab el-Mandeb Strait has been "cleared" of the Houthi group.
"Blessed Friday, and victory for every Yemeni and Arab. Bab al-Mandeb has been cleared of the remnants of the Houthi terrorist militia," Al Jaber said in a post on US social media company X, without providing further details.
Bab al-Mandab has been cleared of Houthi militia - Saudi ambassador to Yemen, Mohammed Al Jaber pic.twitter.com/N4sFkTw7rb
The Houthis did not immediately comment on the ambassador's statement.
Yemen has been engulfed in conflict since the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa and several provinces in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.
The military escalation that began in July has marked the most extensive fighting in Yemen since the relative calm that followed a UN-brokered truce in 2022.
As clashes intensified in September, the Houthis seized several key areas in Hudaydah and Taiz provinces and advanced as far as Mayyun Island in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. Government forces launched Operation Dawn of Yemen this week to retake Houthi-held territory.

title: Merub Ali questions normalisation of trolling in the name of humour
description: Actor urges audiences to stop watching content they dislike instead of turning criticism into personal mockery
content:
Actor urges audiences to stop watching content they dislike instead of turning criticism into personal mockery
Actor Merub Ali has questioned the growing normalisation of online trolling, challenging the notion that making fun of someone is harmless simply because they appear to be laughing along.
In a recent interview, Ali addressed how people often justify mocking others by arguing that it is acceptable as long as the person on the receiving end can laugh at the situation, too. “We always get away with trolling by saying that if the person we are making fun of is laughing too, then it is fine,” she said.
The actor also reflected on how audiences have developed what she described as “thick skin” in response to online criticism and mockery, expressing sadness over how commonplace trolling has become. “I think all of us have such thick skin now. It is very sad that trolling has become a thing,” Ali said.
She also pointed out that viewers have a simple alternative when they do not enjoy a particular show or piece of content. “It is 2026, if you do not like to watch something, just don’t,” she remarked.
Her comments come amid recurring debates about online behaviour towards Pakistan’s television and entertainment industry. Actors, producers and other public figures are frequently subjected to memes, jokes and criticism on social media, with discussions sometimes extending beyond their work to personal ridicule.
Recent examples include the online reactions to Danish Taimoor’s television projects and Shaheer Kadwani’s drama debut. Taimoor has faced mockery over his performances and on-screen characters, while Kadwani drew attention during his first appearance in a drama, prompting audiences to comment on his performance.
Although public figures can expect their work to invite scrutiny, such reactions also highlight how quickly criticism can turn into personal jokes and online ridicule.
Ali’s remarks raise a broader question about where the line should be drawn between expressing an opinion and making someone the target of persistent online mockery. Her message is straightforward: viewers who do not enjoy a particular show or celebrity can simply choose not to watch, rather than turning their disapproval into trolling.
On the professional front, Ali is currently appearing in the drama Izzat , in which she plays Rutba, a young woman whose seemingly happy romantic relationship takes an unexpected turn when she calls off her wedding.
Ali made her television debut in Sinf-e-Aahan in 2021 and has since appeared in projects including Paristan and Wabaal .

title: South Africa s Navanethem  Navi  Pillay wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
description: Judge defended Mandela  chaired UN inquiry that concluded Israel committed genocide in Gaza
content:
Judge defended Mandela, chaired UN inquiry that concluded Israel committed genocide in Gaza
The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded Friday to South Africa's Navi Pillay, the judge who headed the Rwanda genocide tribunal and who last year presided over a United Nations commission which accused Israel of genocide in Gaza .
Pillay, currently a judge on the International Court of Justice in a case where Myanmar also stands accused of genocide, has been "instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide are prosecuted," said Jorgen Watne Frydnes, the chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee in Oslo.
She reacted to the news by making a quip about United States President Donald Trump's well-documented desire to win the prize himself. "If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump," the 85-year-old said during a standing ovation captured by Amnesty International Secretary General Agnes Callamard in Nuremberg and posted on the social network X.
Amazing moment. Navi Pillay has received the Nobel Peace Prize ! https://t.co/HL3r1PJzLO We are at the Nuremberg Court; I cannot think of a stronger symbol for her Nobel prize. We are all so thrilled! This is her first reactions upon hearing the news: pic.twitter.com/Crbj6XdiyQ
Pillay headed the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry (COI), which does not speak on behalf of the world body, and which last year found that genocide was occurring in Gaza. She told AFP at the time that her team had shared "thousands of pieces of information" with prosecutors at the International Criminal Court.
The UN said the prize for Pillay, 85, was testimony to the "value" of rights "more than ever". The Nobel jury said it was honouring her at a time when "the system of international law is under tremendous pressure and its institutions are under attack."
"At a time of existential challenges -- including more wars and conflicts than the world has seen in a long time -- international law is no longer just a supplement to peace and security. It is an absolute necessity," Frydnes said.
"Navi Pillay's commitment to universal legal principles and her firm moral compass are constants in a long career," the committee said.
In a world ravaged by conflicts and crises, 287 individuals and organisations had been nominated for the ultimate diplomatic and humanitarian accolade this year.
The prize for Pillay is sure to anger Trump, whose administration has repeatedly attacked international justice institutions.
Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has made no secret of his desire to win the prize, insisting that he was the most deserving candidate and claiming to have ended up to eight wars. "They have a reputation for maybe not giving it to people like me .. and I think it would be a great discredit to them," Trump had said on Wednesday .
But his war against Iran , his territorial expansion ambitions as in Greenland , his hard line on migrants , and his attacks on multilateralism and the media have, according to experts in Oslo, disqualified him for the prize.
Last year, the prize went to Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado , a choice generally considered palatable to Trump. Machado even gave him her Nobel gold medal, judging he deserved it after the capture of President Nicolas Maduro -- though she failed to obtain his political backing in exchange.
Read: Nobel prize sum raised to $1.27m for 2026
The reasons given by the Nobel Committee for choosing Peace Prize winners have changed substantially since 1901, shifting from promoting peace to defending human rights in a trend that gained momentum during the Cold War, according to an AFP analysis.
The Nobel committee meanwhile says it is not swayed by external pressures. "Of course we have to discuss it, but it's not like that influences the discussions in the room and decisions that come out," the secretary of the committee, Kristian Berg Harpviken, told AFP ahead of the prize announcement.
The prize comes with a gold medal, a diploma and a prize sum of $1.2 million. The award will be presented at a formal ceremony in Oslo on December 10, the anniversary of the 1896 death of the prizes' creator, Swedish inventor and philanthropist Alfred Nobel. The Peace Prize is the only Nobel awarded in Oslo, with the other disciplines announced in Stockholm.
Earlier this week, the prizes for medicine , physics , chemistry and literature were announced in Stockholm, with the latter going to Canadian poet Anne Carson on Thursday for her modern twists on Greek mythology and antiquity.
The 2026 Nobel season winds up Monday with the economics prize.

title: A divorced daughter is better than a dead daughter     Zoha Tauqeer says
description: Actor challenges gender stereotypes  calls for women   s safety to take priority over societal expectations
content:
Actor challenges gender stereotypes, calls for women’s safety to take priority over societal expectations
Actor Zoha Tauqeer has spoken out against domestic violence, urging women in abusive marriages to prioritise their safety over societal expectations and challenging stereotypes about emotional control.
In a recent Instagram post, Tauqeer questioned the common assumption that women are less able to control their emotions, pointing instead to reports of violent behaviour involving men. She highlighted the contradiction between such incidents and the stereotypes often directed at women.
“People say women can’t control their emotions and somehow everytime I open the news, it's about some guy who lost their temper and did something. This is far beyond men and women,” she said.
Tauqeer stressed that violence should not be viewed solely through the lens of gender, describing it as a wider social problem that demands serious attention.
Screengrab: zohatauqeerofficial/Instagram
The actor also expressed concern over reports of rape and other forms of violence, turning her attention to women who may be living in abusive marriages.
She urged them not to remain in dangerous situations because of family expectations or fear of social judgement, emphasising that personal safety should take precedence over preserving a marriage at any cost.
“The rising cases of rape and violence are deeply disturbing if you’re in a violent marriage. I urge you to leave. A divorced daughter is much better than a dead daughter,” she wrote.
Tauqeer has previously spoken openly about personal struggles, including her father’s death and her mother’s decision to remarry, in an interview with The Express Tribune .
Her latest post adds to the wider conversation about domestic violence, gender stereotypes and the social pressures that can prevent victims from seeking safety. By urging women to leave abusive relationships, Tauqeer challenged the stigma surrounding divorce and underscored the importance of protecting lives over meeting societal expectations.
On the professional front, Tauqeer is known for her roles in drama serials Zabt and Kaisa Yeh Ishq .

title: LHC seeks report on facilities provided to Imran   s sisters in jail
description: Counsel said 19 days had passed  but the required medicines and clothes had not been provided to the women
content:
Counsel says 19 days had passed, but required medicines, clothes had not been provided to her
The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Friday sought reports on the provision of medicines, clothes and other basic necessities to Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan’s sisters Aleema Khan, Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, who were detained under the Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance.
Justice Abher Gul Khan was hearing petitions challenging the sisters’ detention orders, along with miscellaneous applications seeking access to essential items for the detained women.
The applications were filed by Aleema’s son, Shahrez Khan, and Noreen’s daughter, Sakeena Niazi, through their counsel, Rana Mudassar Umar. The counsel asked the court to ensure that the women were provided with medicines, clothes, books, and other necessities.
During the hearing, the counsel said 19 days had passed, but the required medicines and clothes had not been provided to the women. He also informed the court that separate miscellaneous applications had been filed seeking basic necessities for Uzma and Noreen.
Justice Abher questioned the counsel, observing that clothes and medicines had already been provided to the women, but they had subsequently claimed that nothing had been supplied.
The counsel clarified that the items had been provided in compliance with the court’s order. He requested that jail authorities also be directed to allow medicines, clothes, books and other essential items for Uzma and Noreen.
Read: PTI condemns Aleema Khan's arrest as Lahore DC orders 30-day detention
The judge asked the counsel to submit a written list of the required items, observing that only those specifically authorised by the court would be allowed into the jail. The court declined to allow food items, with the judge observing that the request could not be granted.
Justice Abher said reports would be sought on the miscellaneous applications seeking the provision of essential items.
The counsel also requested that the court hear the main petitions challenging the sisters’ detention orders. The judge, however, said the immediate priority was to ensure the delivery of medicines and clothes, adding that the main petitions could be taken up later.
The judge told the counsel that he would have to set aside the miscellaneous applications if he wished to argue the main petitions, asking him to decide how he wanted to proceed.
The court adjourned further proceedings on the petitions challenging the detention of Aleema, Uzma and Noreen until October 12.
The three sisters were detained for 30 days under Section 3 of the MPO, 1960, ahead of the PTI’s planned protest march towards Islamabad. Aleema was detained on September 20, while Dr Uzma and Noreen were taken into custody a day later.
Read more: Sept 27 protest call irrevocable: Gohar
The Lahore administration’s detention orders cited police reports alleging that the women had been involved in the May 9, 2023 protests and road blockades, and had been mobilising party workers. PTI challenged the orders in the LHC, seeking their immediate release.
The high court declined to suspend the detention orders immediately and sought responses from the relevant authorities. In a separate application concerning Aleema’s detention conditions, the Punjab government later told the court that she had been provided with basic facilities and essential items, including clothes, bedding and toiletries. The court disposed of that application after receiving the government’s report.
However, on September 30, Imran’s cousin Qasim Zaman claimed that the three women had gone on a 48-hour hunger strike at Kot Lakhpat Jail, alleging that essential items had not been provided despite the court’s directions. He also said the family was concerned about their access to relatives and lawyers.

title: Minal Khan urges women to put their health first in Pinktober message
description: Actor expresses solidarity with breast cancer patients and survivors  highlighting importance of early detection
content:
Actor expresses solidarity with breast cancer patients and survivors, highlighting importance of early detection
Actor Minal Khan has urged women to prioritise their health and pay attention to changes in their bodies, sharing a heartfelt message for Breast Cancer Awareness Month that emphasised self-care and early medical attention.
The actor shared a selfie on Instagram wearing a shirt featuring a pink ribbon and the word “Fight”, expressing solidarity with women battling breast cancer, survivors and those learning to put their health first. Her post also featured the hashtag #Pinktober, commonly used for breast cancer awareness campaigns held throughout October.
Sharing the message behind the photograph, Khan wrote, “This pink ribbon is for my sisters fighting breast cancer, for the survivors who inspire us, and for all of us learning to put our health first. 💕”
The actor also reflected on how her understanding of self-care had evolved. “I used to think thinking about my own health was selfish. It’s not. It’s self-love,” she wrote.
Khan encouraged her followers to take a moment out of their busy routines to check in with their health. “Take 1 minute today — for you. Check in with your body. If something feels different or wrong, listen to it and please see your doctor,” she added.
Concluding her message, the actor reinforced the importance of making time for personal well-being. “You deserve that minute. We all do. 🎀”
October is observed internationally as Breast Cancer Awareness Month, with pink ribbons serving as a symbol of support for patients, survivors and families affected by the disease. The annual campaign, widely known as Pinktober, aims to raise awareness, encourage early detection and reduce the stigma surrounding breast cancer.
In Pakistan, breast cancer remains a significant public health concern. Estimates cited by health organisations suggest that approximately one in eight women in the country may develop the disease during their lifetime. Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital has also highlighted the substantial number of women diagnosed with breast cancer each year.
Awareness initiatives across the country use October to encourage women to learn about breast health, recognise potential warning signs and seek medical advice without delay. Organisations such as Pink Ribbon Pakistan conduct public awareness campaigns, educational activities and outreach programmes to promote early detection and improve access to information about the disease.
Potential warning signs of breast cancer include a new lump in the breast or armpit, changes in breast size or shape, skin changes and alterations in the nipple. While these symptoms do not necessarily indicate cancer, they should be assessed by a qualified healthcare professional. Becoming familiar with one's body can help identify changes, but self-examination does not replace appropriate medical screening or professional evaluation.

title: Harry Styles reveals how an ex girlfriend helped him overcome public anxiety during One Direction days
description: Fans speculate whether Styles was referring to Taylor Swift  Kendall Jenner  or another one of his famous exes
content:
Fans speculate whether Styles was referring to Taylor Swift, Kendall Jenner, or another one of his famous exes
Harry Styles has credited a former girlfriend with helping him overcome his reluctance to go out in public during his early years with One Direction, explaining how the experience changed his approach to everyday life.
In a joint interview with Thom Yorke published by Rolling Stone on October 8, the Grammy-winning singer recalled feeling restricted while touring with the band and worrying about being seen outside his home.
“When I’d be home, it felt like, ‘Oh, it’s not safe for me to be out,’” Styles said.
The 32-year-old explained that dating someone more outgoing encouraged him to explore London rather than remain indoors.
Recalling her visit to the city, he said, “So we walked everywhere, and it was this realization for me: ‘Oh, it’s fine to be outside.’”
Styles added, “It kind of broke that thing. Now, it’s changed my life in such a big way, because it’s how you stay connected to the world.”
The singer also said walking helps him notice his surroundings and spark his creativity. He explained that being at ground level allows artists to notice details they might miss when travelling by car.
Despite becoming more comfortable in public, Styles remains protective of his private life.
In a separate 2022 interview with Rolling Stone , he explained why photographs with another person should not automatically be interpreted as confirmation of a public relationship.
“I've never talked about my life away from work publicly,” he said, adding that maintaining this boundary had benefited him.
The former One Direction member, now reportedly engaged to Zoë Kravitz, has been linked to several famous women throughout his career, including Taylor Swift, Kendall Jenner, Olivia Wilde and more.
His latest comments offer insight into how personal experiences have influenced his relationship with fame, public spaces and privacy.

Punjab government approves Rs400m for renovation of the iconic venue, with work expected to finish by January 2027
The Punjab government has approved Rs400 million to renovate and upgrade Lahore's National Hockey Stadium and its adjoining practice pitch.
Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF) said on Friday that the funding was approved by the provincial government and Sports Board Punjab following a special request from the federation.
The project includes installing a new astroturf to bring playing facilities in line with international standards, as well as repairing and upgrading the venue's infrastructure and other facilities.
The PHF said that training infrastructure will also be improved to provide players with modern facilities.
It added that the project would be completed by January 2027.
"The initiative aims to strengthen hockey in Pakistan and improve facilities for players."
The stadium has hosted several major international tournaments, including the 1990 Men’s Hockey World Cup and multiple editions of the Champions Trophy in 1978, 1988, 1994, 1998 and 2004. It also hosted a two-match Pakistan and World XI series in January 2018.

title: New Zealand face injury setback

content:
Chapman, Foulkes to miss India series; Clarkson, Tickner replace duo
New Zealand have been dealt an injury setback ahead of their five-match T20I series against India, with Mark Chapman and Zak Foulkes ruled out and replaced by Josh Clarkson and Blair Tickner. Chapman hurt his hamstring while playing in a T20 league in Europe last month and will be sidelined for the entire five-match series with an eye on returning for the ODI series with India. Foulkes is battling a hip flexor complaint and is still yet to have his return to play timeline determined. It paves the way for all-rounder Josh Clarkson and fast bowler Blair Tickner to be included in New Zealand's 16-member squad for the series that commences in Christchurch on October 22. Black Caps coach Rob Walter is looking forward to welcoming the duo into his playing group. "I’m gutted for Mark and Zak and I wish them both a smooth recovery,” Walter said. “We’re fortunate to be able to lean on the expertise of Josh and Blair.” "I know they’re both very excited to be involved in what’s shaping up to be an epic T20 series.” The two teams met in the final of the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup earlier this year, when India registered a comprehensive 96-run triumph.

'I experienced sexual, emotional, financial and physical abuse in that relationship', Harris told Biel in a message
Crystal Harris has urged Jessica Biel to reconsider portraying Hugh Hefner’s wife in Playmates , raising concerns about how the Playboy founder and his world may be depicted in the upcoming film.
Harris shared a screenshot of an Instagram message she sent to Biel following the announcement of her casting. Harris was married to Hefner from 2012 until his death in 2017.
In her message, Harris wrote, “Please reconsider playing Hugh Hefner’s wife if this film intends to romanticize him or the Playboy world. I was actually his wife, and I experienced sexual, emotional, financial and physical abuse in that relationship.”
She also referred to allegations made by other women, urging the filmmakers to consider their experiences before presenting the Playboy world through a nostalgic lens.
“Many other woman have come forward with allegations of rape, coercion, drugging and exploitation as well. There are also deeply troubling concerns involving minors. I hope everyone involved this film takes the time to listen the women who lived it before helping Hollywood turn it back into nostalgia,” Harris wrote.
Playmates marks the directorial debut of Lorraine Nicholson, who drew inspiration from her childhood visits to the Playboy Mansion.
The film stars Lily-Rose Depp and Indiana Elle, with Bill Pullman portraying Hefner.
According to Searchlight Pictures, the story follows 13-year-old Elle and Anna, one of seven hopefuls competing for the title of Playmate of the Month, as they form an unlikely friendship.
Harris’s comments add to the discussion surrounding the film’s portrayal of the Playboy legacy and the experiences of women associated with it.

title: Nobel Peace Prize goes to South African judge despite PM Shehbaz   s hopes for Trump
description: Says Trump deserves award for his intervention in Pakistan India conflict  securing ceasefire
content:
Says Trump deserves award for his intervention in Pakistan-India conflict, securing ceasefire
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday expressed hope that United States President Donald Trump would receive the Nobel Peace Prize in recognition of his "historic role in advancing peace in South Asia," shortly before South African judge Navanethem "Navi" Pillay was announced as the winner.
South African judge Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, 85, won the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday "for her efforts to promote peace and international law", the Norwegian Nobel Committee said.
In a post on X, PM Shehbaz wrote that Trump's “timely intervention helped bring Pakistan and India back from the brink and secure a ceasefire, that is holding till today.”
President Donald Trump played a historic role in advancing peace in South Asia. His timely intervention helped bring Pakistan and India back from the brink and secure a ceasefire, that is holding till today. In recognition of his outstanding contribution, Pakistan had nominated…
PM Shehbaz added that, in view of this, Pakistan had nominated Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize in recognition of his "outstanding contribution," the prime minister said. “We sincerely hope President’s efforts to promote peace and prevent conflict in our region receive due recognition this time,” he added.
Read: Trump says he deserves Nobel Peace Prize but has doubts he will get it
On June 21, 2025, Pakistan announced its decision to recommend Trump for the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, citing his role in helping secure a ceasefire between Pakistan and India. The government said his intervention had helped avert a wider conflict between the two nuclear-armed neighbours.
The ceasefire was announced on May 10, after days of military exchanges, with Trump saying the United States had mediated the agreement. He later claimed that trade pressure had helped bring the two sides to an understanding.
Trump did not win the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize, which was awarded to Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado. In January 2026, Machado presented her medal to Trump during a meeting at the White House, saying the gesture recognised his commitment to the freedom of the Venezuelan people. Trump thanked her, saying she had presented him with the prize for the work he had done.
The Norwegian Nobel Committee subsequently clarified that although a laureate could give away the physical medal, the prize itself remained inseparably linked to the person who had won it.
Read more: Nobel Peace Prize haunted by the 'spectre' of Trump
Trump has repeatedly made public his desire to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.
On October 8, he said he believed he should win it for his involvement in resolving conflicts but acknowledged uncertainty over the committee’s decision.
“They have a reputation for maybe not giving it to people like me,” he told reporters, adding that he had been “very honored” to receive the award indirectly through Machado the previous year. He also argued that his involvement in multiple conflicts merited recognition.

Archbishop Gallagher meets FM Dar as both sides emphasise importance of international efforts for regional peace
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Friday met with Secretary for Relations with States of the Holy See Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher with the latter commending Pakistan’s "constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability through mediation, dialogue and diplomacy".
In a statement on X, the Foreign Office (FO) noted that Archbishop Gallagher was visiting Pakistan to mark the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and the Holy See.
The statement added that FM Dar welcomed Archbishop Gallagher "and acknowledged the Holy See’s role in promoting peace, interfaith harmony and dialogue, and appreciated the valuable contributions of Pakistan’s Catholic community, particularly in education and health".
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 received H.E. Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher, Secretary for Relations with States of the Holy See, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The Archbishop is visiting Pakistan to mark the 75th… pic.twitter.com/i6ekqdcPBz
The foreign minister also appreciated Pope Leo XIV’s "principled calls for peace and a just resolution of the Palestine conflict", reaffirming Pakistan’s "unwavering solidarity with the Palestinian people".
Archbishop Gallagher and FM Dar "expressed deep concern over the continuing humanitarian crisis and emphasised the importance of sustained international efforts to advance peace in the region", the FO said.
It concluded with noting that both sides "reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening Pakistan–Holy See relations and promoting mutual respect, understanding and peaceful coexistence among faiths".

On Wednesday , the FO had announced that Archbishop Gallagher would visit Pakistan from October 8 to 10 on the invitation of FM Ishaq Dar. The visit, the Foreign Office had said, would be the "first-ever visit to Pakistan by a secretary for relations with states and international organisations of the Holy See".
It had added that Archbishop Gallagher would meet FM Dar to discuss matters of mutual interest including interfaith harmony, dialogue and peace, as well as regional and international developments. He is also expected to call on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and interact with members of the Catholic community in Pakistan.
The FO said that the visit marked an important milestone in the longstanding relations between Pakistan and the Holy See and reflected their shared commitment to further strengthening mutual understanding, cooperation and trust, while promoting interfaith harmony and peace.

title: PIA temporarily suspends flight operations to Riyadh amid Houthi attacks on Saudi airports
description: PIA flight PK 753 from Islamabad to Riyadh and flight PK 754 from Riyadh to Islamabad have been cancelled
content:
Authorities say 3 people killed and 36 injured, including a Pakistani, in attacks on King Khalid International Airport
The Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) temporarily suspended its flight operations to Riyadh amid the worsening situation in the Middle East, PIA spokesperson Abdullah Hafiz Khan said on Friday.
The announcement followed a series of Houthi missile and drone strikes targeting Saudi airports and other infrastructure. Saudi authorities said three people were killed and 36 injured, including a Pakistani national, in attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha International Airport on October 6 and 7.
Khan advised passengers to contact PIA’s call centre at 111-786-786 before leaving for the airport to check the latest status of their flights. The airline apologised for the inconvenience caused to passengers by the situation, Khan said.
PIA flight PK-753 from Islamabad to Riyadh and flight PK-754 from Riyadh to Islamabad were also cancelled.
Read: Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport killed three Saudis as war escalates
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said on Thursday it had intercepted and destroyed multiple ballistic missiles launched towards Riyadh and Khamis Mushait in the southwestern Asir region. Coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki said two missiles had been fired towards the Saudi capital and another towards Khamis Mushait.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed the group had targeted King Khalid International Airport with a ballistic missile, saying the strike had disrupted air traffic. He also warned workers at Saudi oil facilities and airlines operating in Saudi airspace about locations the group had declared targets for its military operations.
Yemen's Houthis have carried out missile and drone attacks against Saudi Arabia since the Yemen war escalated in 2015, targeting military installations, airports, oil facilities and other critical infrastructure.
In September 2019 , the group claimed responsibility for drone attacks on Saudi Aramco’s Abqaiq processing facility and Khurais oil field, attacks that temporarily disrupted more than half of Saudi Arabia’s crude production.
The attacks continued in subsequent years, including strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure in March 2022.
Read More: Makkah defence alliance agrees to 'rapid force deployment' in Saudi Arabia: FO
More recently, Houthi attacks again targeted Saudi territory. In September, the group claimed missile and drone strikes on a Saudi military base and other targets, while Saudi authorities reported attacks affecting several cities.
On September 25 , the senior military leadership of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye strongly condemned attacks targeting the holy city of Makkah as they reaffirmed their commitment to the collective defence of the kingdom under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.
Flight operations in Pakistan have faced repeated disruption since the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran on February 28, triggering retaliatory attacks and airspace restrictions across the Middle East. More than 500 flights to and from Pakistani airports were cancelled in the first three days of the conflict, affecting routes to the Gulf and other destinations, while some foreign airlines diverted aircraft to Karachi.
PIA initially suspended flights to the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Doha and Kuwait, while continuing services to Saudi Arabia on revised routes that avoided conflict-hit areas. By March 5, Pakistani and foreign airlines had cancelled 578 flights since the conflict began, with airspace closures also affecting services from Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad and other cities.
Although flights to Gulf destinations began resuming after a ceasefire announced in April, some countries continued to impose partial airspace restrictions . Renewed tensions later brought further disruption, with PIA suspending flights to Fujairah for 48 hours in March and limiting its services to the United Arab Emirates to Al Ain.

title: Wealthy French quit failing state schools squeezed by pensions and austerity
description: School performance has been slipping for years  and the government is struggling to arrest the slide
content:
School performance has been slipping for years, and the government is struggling to arrest the slide
Clemence Remy moved to the French city of Nantes in 2020 and enrolled her two girls in the local state school. The teachers were good, but she grew so exasperated ​by rolling staff strikes that she eventually put them in a private school.
Those concerns about state schools have helped fuel some of France's most violent protests in decades. They began last ‌month at high schools in Paris' poor northern suburbs, where anger over teacher absences and shabby facilities quickly morphed into a nationwide movement against inequality, weak public spending and falling standards.
France's public schools have long been held up as a crucible of the republican ideal, a place where children from rich and poor families alike can receive a top-notch education imbued with the values of "liberty, equality and fraternity".
But performance has been slipping for years, and the government is struggling to arrest the slide as gigantic ​pension outlays and a need to rein in public finances leave little room for manoeuvre.
Those issues have prompted a growing number of wealthier parents to abandon the public sector in favour of private schooling. ​Remy said the strikes at her daughters' school in Nantes, a left-leaning city in western France, were often last-minute, requiring repeated time off work with little ⁠notice.
Read: French lawmaker calls on interior minister to resign over police response to student protests
"School is an institution we should be able to rely on," she said. "In the end, you realise you can't rely on the system."
Standards fall as pensions gobble up shrinking funds
The maths and reading levels of French ​15-year-olds have fallen drastically since 2003, reaching a record low well below the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development average, according to the body's 2025 "PISA" results.
French state secondary schools were unable to staff nearly 10% of ​teaching hours - or almost half a day of teaching per week - in the 2024/25 school year, of which three-quarters is due to the non-replacement of absent teachers.
Between 10% and 20% of French school buildings are "in a significantly deteriorated condition", according to a 2025 report by Banque des Territoires, the investment arm of state-owned lender Caisse des Dépôts.
The government's inability to turn the tide on education is partly explained by a growing pensions bill that sucks resources away from other priorities, experts say.
France's 2027 ​education budget is €64 billion ($72 billion). Teachers' pensions add another 28% to the cost.
Total government spending on pensions, which is due to reach 436 billion euros or 14% of economic output next year, has grown faster than ​all other categories of public expenditure over the last two decades, while spending has slipped for education, according to Reuters calculations based on Eurostat data.
Read more: High school students in Paris' deprived suburbs spark national protest movement
The steady growth in pension spending is due not only to an ageing population, but also ‌to voters' resistance ⁠to increasing the retirement age or reducing what retirees get.
Economist Erwann Tison of the think tank Institut de l’Entreprise said pension spending "cannibalises" the education budget. That means France can only pay early-career teachers below OECD-average salaries that contribute to frustration and strike action.
"France is effectively handing over large subsidies to older French at the expense of everyone else," Nobel-winning economist Paul Krugman wrote on his Substack on Thursday. "Mass national student demonstrations should come as no surprise."
Wealthier families migrate to private schools
The vast majority of French private schools operate according to the "under-contract" model.
Almost entirely Catholic-run, such schools have greater control over staffing and admissions. Their teachers are paid by the state, with ​fees covering non-teaching costs. A larger pool of substitute teachers ​means they are less affected by strikes or ⁠absences.
Over 2 million children, or 17.6% of all pupils, attend one of France's more than 7,500 under-contract schools, according to a 2023 national audit office report.
Although this proportion rose modestly between 2011 and 2021, the percentage of children from wealthier families has grown at the expense of poorer children, the report found. It said ​some families had moved over to avoid local state schools, or had concerns about safety and teacher absences.
Pupils from "very advantaged" families accounted for 40.2% of the ​total in 2021 compared to ⁠just 26.4% in 2000, while over half of pupils at under-contract schools now come from "advantaged or very advantaged" backgrounds, compared with less than a third in state schools.
"Fifty years ago, ambitious families aimed for the public sector," said Louis Chauvel, a sociologist at the University of Luxembourg. "Today, private institutions are often seen as the better route if you want to maximise your kids' chances."
Virginie Durin, the president of Apel, France's main association representing parents of pupils in ⁠Catholic private ​schools, said not all were wealthy, and that many parents made great sacrifices to afford them.
But she acknowledged a growing concentration of ​wealthier students in certain neighbourhoods.
Nantes, where Remy lives, is a stronghold of under-contract schools in France, with 38% of pupils privately educated.
Remy, who pays €191 ($214) a month per child, recognised that private schools were not affordable for everyone, and were at risk of being colonised ​by the wealthy. But she had no regrets.
"I think it provides an environment where at least the children are encouraged to strive and do better."

title: Zelenskiy accuses US of inaction as Russian strikes kill over 70 in two days
description: Says 215 wounded over same period  urges Starlink access to target Moscow s ballistic missile launchers
content:
Says 215 wounded over same period, urges Starlink access to target Moscow's ballistic-missile launchers
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy accused the United States of being unwilling to help Ukraine after a Russian bomb attack on Thursday killed at least 35 people in the east, sending the two-day death toll from Russian strikes to over 70.
Hours after the strike on the embattled city of Kramatorsk tore through two buses, Zelenskiy criticised Washington's effort to pursue economic ties with Russia while also seeking to mediate the more than four-year war.
City authorities reported a new drone attack in the evening that killed two people. That brought to 35 the total death toll in the city.
Local authorities reported that a Russian guided aerial bomb killed two people in a village in southeastern Dnipropetrovsk and one person died in the western city of Ivano-Frankivsk.
Read: Trump tells Ukraine's Zelenskiy to stop hitting Russian diesel
The attacks were launched a day after a mass Russian drone and missile assault killed dozens across Ukraine — 22 of them in a residential building in the central town of Pryluky, around 130 km (80 miles) east of Kyiv.
Speaking in the early evening, Zelenskiy said 78 people were killed and 215 wounded by strikes in the last two days across Ukraine.
Speaking to reporters in Pryluky , the Ukrainian leader urged the US to accede to his requests to expand Ukraine's access to the Starlink satellite service to help it target Russian ballistic-missile launchers.
"Open Starlink for Ukraine. You did open it when you were responding to Iran ... I’ve said quite openly — give it to us, help us defend our skies and dominate there. And then Putin will sit down at the negotiating table," he said in an emotional statement.
Ukraine has in recent months aimed to wrest the battlefield initiative from Russia, whose gains have slowed this year, but is still suffering from Moscow's increasingly brutal air war.
"So where's the truth here, where's the honesty? Where's the stalemate? ... That's called unwillingness," he said, referring to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio 's assertion earlier on Thursday the war is at a stalemate and that the US would keep working toward a settlement.
Read More: Russia is ready for new ideas on Ukraine peace, but with conditions, senior diplomat says
"One cannot, on the one hand, negotiate with the Russians about future economic projects, whilst on the other hand say that we find ourselves in some sort of ... diplomatic stalemate," Zelenskiy added.
Top Russian and US officials, including US Special Envoy Jared Kushner, have held talks about bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream pipelines that delivered Russian gas to Germany before Moscow invaded Ukraine, Reuters reported on Thursday. Ukrainian negotiators will travel to the US on Friday and Saturday for talks, Zelenskiy added, urging US President Donald Trump to increase sanction pressure on Russia.
Zelenskiy told reporters in Kyiv that he expected Kyiv's European partners to join the talks with the US. He also said Ukrainian negotiators would raise the issue of air defences in light of near-constant Russian attacks.
20 people were wounded in the Kramatorsk strike — one of the biggest single attacks of the year by Russia. Moscow has denied targeting civilians, but regularly pounds cities with missiles and drones.
"The Russians are deliberately targeting civilians. For them, a bus full of passengers is an attractive target precisely because a single strike can kill as many people as possible," regional governor Vadym Filashkin said on the Telegram app.
Images posted by officials showed bodies strewn across a street littered with debris and a charred shell of a bus. Some bodies had not been identified yet, Zelenskiy said, adding that the attack would not go unanswered.
Also Read: Russian strikes kill seven in Ukraine
Separately, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said four people were killed and 19 wounded in morning attacks on the Ukrainian capital Kyiv. Water and electricity supplies were subject to interruptions which officials said would take time to put right.
Russia has unleashed relentless drone strikes against Kyiv in recent weeks, targeting warehouses, data centres and renewing its campaign against Ukraine's power grid ahead of winter.
Russian technology and AI company Yandex said it could not yet determine whether equipment at a data centre hit by a Ukrainian drone attack could be restored. Zelenskiy did not refer specifically to the strike on Yandex, but said Ukraine was "mirroring" Russian attacks on data centres.
