title: US to livestream Army firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter  Pentagon says
description: Decision comes amid heightened debate in US over death penalty following botched lethal injection  of Christa Pike
content:
Decision comes amid heightened debate in US over death penalty following botched lethal injection of Christa Pike
The United States will livestream the Army's upcoming firing squad execution of a gunman who killed 13 people at the Fort Hood military base in 2009, the Pentagon said, in what would be an unprecedented broadcast of a US execution.
Nidal Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, is set to become the first person to be executed by firing squad by the US military since 1945. The execution is scheduled for December 3 at the same sprawling Texas base where Hasan opened fire with a laser-sighted handgun in a medical facility.
It comes amid heightened debate in the US over the death penalty following the botched lethal injection of a Tennessee woman last week.
"It will be livestreamed. Details will follow," a Pentagon official told Reuters , speaking on the condition of anonymity.
Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, who championed the push to execute Hasan by firing squad, confirmed plans to livestream the execution in an X post.
Media have sought to televise US executions in the past but have been blocked by the courts. No other country is known to televise or livestream a legal execution, experts said.
Public executions have become exceedingly rare worldwide. Among countries known to conduct them in recent years are Iran and Taliban-run Afghanistan.
Extrajudicial lynchings in the US, often by white mobs targeting Black Americans, were public spectacles well into the 20th century. The last legally sanctioned public execution in the US was conducted in 1936, death penalty experts said. Thousands watched that 1936 hanging of a young Black man who had been convicted of raping a white woman.
Hegseth told the Human Events Daily program that deciding to execute Hasan by firing squad at Fort Hood on a Thursday at 1pm — the approximate time, day of the week and location of the 2009 shooting — was a "no-brainer."
"We'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public. Because people need to understand that ... there's serious consequences for these types of things," Hegseth said. Asked if Hasan had made any final requests, Hegseth said: "Don't care. We'll see him on December 3."
President must approve firing squad execution
A military jury sentenced Hasan to death in August 2013, after finding him guilty of 45 counts of premeditated murder and attempted premeditated murder. The shooting came weeks before Hasan, now 56, was scheduled to be deployed to Afghanistan. He was left partially paralysed and confined to a wheelchair from being shot by police during his arrest.
Under US military law, a US president must approve an execution by firing squad. President Donald Trump did so on Hegseth's recommendation, the Pentagon said on Monday. The White House declined to say whether Trump supported the livestreaming, referring questions to the Pentagon.
The group Death Penalty Action, which opposes capital punishment, said Hasan's execution would be the first military execution since 1961. According to the Death Penalty Information Centre, the 1961 execution was carried out by hanging. The last known executions by US military firing squads were in 1945, the centre reported.
"It would be extremely, extremely strange" to livestream the event, said Eugene Fidell, a lawyer, author and military law expert who lectures at Yale Law School.
While firing squads have a long history in American military law, as far as he knew it would be unprecedented to livestream or televise an execution, Fidell said, adding that Hasan would need to sue in federal court if he wanted to block a public display of his death.
"The Supreme Court has never addressed this question, and it's an interesting question whether the current Supreme Court would put on their originalist hat and say, 'Well, it was OK in 1790, so what the hell?'" Fidell said.
Read More: US judge says he must declare mistrial in Lindsay Clancy trial over killing her children
Jonathan Lurie, an author and historian of military justice, said there are no compelling reasons to make the execution public. "What's the point of it? Who would want to see that?" said Lurie.
At least five states have firing squads on the books, according to the Death Penalty Information Centre. In 2025, South Carolina carried out the first such execution in the US in 15 years.
Death by firing squad is one of several forms of capital punishment the Trump administration recently added to permissible forms of execution for the gravest of federal crimes, along with electrocution and gas asphyxiation. The number of federal execution options was expanded in part because of increasing difficulties in obtaining drugs for lethal injections, which have also sometimes proved challenging to carry out.
Plans by the state of Tennessee to execute a woman for the first time in more than 200 years went awry last week when prison personnel botched attempts to administer a lethal injection, leaving the death-row inmate, Christa Pike, alive but hospitalised .
Her lawyers said on Wednesday she awoke "angry and confused" in a hospital. Pike remains very sick and shackled to her hospital bed, they said.

title: Below  ending explained  Netflix creator addresses Season 2 possibilities
description: Creator Jesse McKeown has explained the finale while the production team has addressed the possibility of a 2nd season
content:
Creator Jesse McKeown has explained the finale while the production team has addressed the possibility of a 2nd season
Netflix’s Below , starring Josh Hartnett, concludes its six-episode run with a revelation about the mysterious sea creature and an ending that raises questions about the future.
Creator Jesse McKeown has explained the finale, while the production team has addressed the possibility of a second season.
The series follows Calvin Penney (Hartnett), a Newfoundland fisherman haunted by his father’s mysterious death.
When a sea creature threatens his community, Calvin joins forces with a visiting marine researcher to protect his family and uncover the truth.
In the finale, the creature is revealed to be a giant squid mother protecting eggs trapped inside an iceberg.
Calvin and his family help move the iceberg into deeper waters, saving the creature from a planned military attack.
The decision also allows Calvin to confront his past and recognise the creature’s determination to protect its family.
The ending reveals more icebergs at sea, suggesting that other creatures could remain undiscovered.
Speaking to TV Insider , McKeown said the final image had been planned from the beginning. He explained that the story was designed to feel complete while leaving questions about climate change and its consequences.
Executive producer Jessica Rhoades told TV Insider that the team had concentrated on delivering the strongest possible six-episode story.
Netflix has not announced plans for a second season. McKeown told Time , “If there’s another story to tell with these characters, great. But that’s not my intention.”
He also clarified that the ending was not simply a conventional cliffhanger, but a question about humanity’s future.
For now, Below remains a complete limited series, with its closing scenes reinforcing its themes of family, environmental change and the uncertain future facing vulnerable communities.

title: New York City man shot in car with child present by ICE agents  mayor says
description: Mamdani demands end to ICE actions in city amid failed talks with Trump on securing wounded man   s release
content:
Mamdani demands end to ICE actions in city amid failed talks with Trump on securing wounded man’s release
United States immigration agents shot and wounded a man on Thursday in his car with a child present in the Marble Hill neighbourhood of New York City, according to the mayor, city police and eyewitnesses.
Federal immigration agents have shot at least 21 people since Republican President Donald Trump returned to office, seven fatally , sparking protests across the US. Critics contend ​that Trump's push to ramp up deportations has led to an increasing number of violent confrontations, and accuse the administration of resisting accountability for the agents involved.
Trump has said many migrants must be deported, blaming them, often in sweeping terms, for financial fraud and violent crimes.
"Early reports indicate agents surrounded (the man) and a 5-year-old child in his car before firing multiple rounds," New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement. "I have been on the phone with President Trump and (Homeland Security) Secretary Mullin, negotiating the release of the man ICE agents shot. Those negotiations were unsuccessful," Mamdani said in a press conference late in the evening.
Read: Supreme Court lets Trump resume deporting migrants to countries not their own
He said he demanded from the Trump administration that ICE stop its enforcement actions in New York City. "These actions are making the city less safe," Mamdani said. "This city wants ICE out. We want ICE out of our city, ICE out of our schools, ICE out of our hospitals, ICE out of our streets, ICE away from our kids."
The mayor said the child in the car is physically unharmed. New York Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said NYPD has located the child with a family member after a wellness check.
The Department of Homeland Security, ICE's parent agency, said in a statement ICE officers were conducting a "targeted enforcement operation" in the Bronx, New York, to arrest a man from the Dominican Republic with a prior criminal conviction. The man identified as 28-year-old, had been arrested twice in New York City in 2023 and 2025, according to NYPD Commissioner Tisch.
Read More: US judge blocks Trump policy of fining migrants up to $1.8 million
"During the incident, an ICE officer discharged his weapon and the criminal illegal alien was injured," DHS said, adding that ICE officers rendered immediate aid. "The individual is alive and at a local hospital."
The shooting occurred at around 4pm ET (2000 GMT), DHS said.
Working at a restaurant near the shooting, Pedro Almarez said he heard shots fired and went outside to see several officers wearing ICE attire at the scene. "There were a lot of ICE officers, three or four cars," Almarez told Reuters by phone. He said NYPD officers arrived about 10 minutes later. He said the man was only removed from his car after an ambulance arrived.
At the shooting scene, where police strung yellow crime-scene tape to cordon off a city block, a woman standing on a balcony overlooking the area told officers they were "taking our children," according to a Reuters witness.

title: Oil falls as Trump comments on Iran talks ease supply concerns
description: Brent crude futures fall  1 37  or 1 3   to  102 91 a barrel
content:
Brent crude futures fall $1.37, or 1.3%, to $102.91 a barrel
Oil prices fell on Friday as Middle East supply concerns eased after US President Donald Trump said it will not attack Iran before US elections next month ​amid productive talks to end their war that has disrupted global energy markets.
Brent crude ‌futures fell $1.37, or 1.3%, to $102.91 a barrel by 0450 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures fell $1.09, or 1.2%, to $90.40.
On a weekly basis, Brent prices are set for weekly gains after settling 4% higher on Thursday, while WTI is ​set for a slight decline.
On Thursday, Trump said Washington was having "productive discussions" with Iran ​and said no attack was planned before the November 3 midterm congressional elections ⁠, after media reports that he was considering an attack before then.
Iran's Tasnim news agency reported the same day ​that Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran is reviewing the US response to its proposal that ​would reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days.
Read: Vance says Iran must cut enrichment to end war
"The prospect of easing tensions still needs to be reinforced by concrete progress in negotiations and improvements in shipping safety through the Strait of Hormuz," said XS.com analyst Linh Tran.
The ​US is still pressuring Iran economically to try to end the war, now in its eighth ​month, imposing sanctions on Thursday targeting individuals, networks and 17 vessels for transporting Iranian crude, oil products and petrochemicals.
Prices ‌have been ⁠volatile this week as threats to shipping in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, which carried shipments equal to about 20% of global oil and fuel before the war, have increased in October.
Read more: Oil rises as Middle East supply concerns persist amid shipping attacks
China, the world's top oil importer, is set to resume refined fuel exports after a brief halt ​during its Golden Week ​holiday, a move that ⁠will help ease tight global diesel, gasoline and jet fuel markets, Reuters reported on Friday, citing sources.
This week, the International Energy Agency agreed to accelerate ​the release of oil stocks and to prioritise diesel supplies under a ​plan launched ⁠in March.
The oil market is also contending with Hurricane Isaias in the Gulf of Mexico. Because of the storm, producers there have shut in about 1.3 million barrels per day, or 62.9%, of current oil ⁠production ​as of Thursday, according to the US Marine Minerals Administration.
"This ​disruption provides additional support for oil prices, but the duration of its impact will depend on post-storm facility inspections and ​the pace of operational recovery," Tran said.

President Zardari, Naqvi laud security forces, reaffirm resolve to eliminate terrorism
Security forces killed seven terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in North Waziristan, Radio Pakistan reported on Friday, citing security sources.
Fitna al - Khawarij is the term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
According to the sources, a large quantity of weapons and ammunition was also recovered from the terrorists.
Seven terrorists of #FitnaAlKhawarij have been killed by security forces during an intelligence-based operation in #NorthWaziristan @OfficialDGISPR #RadioPakistan #News https://t.co/WveZVFPbPl pic.twitter.com/dMPRsE8xeI
President Asif Ali Zardari commended the security forces for their successful operation in North Waziristan, Radio Pakistan reported.
In a statement, he said the conspiracies of terrorists’ foreign sponsors and their local facilitators would be thwarted at all costs. The president said the entire nation stood with its security forces in the war against terrorism.
President @AAliZardari has commended security forces for their successful operation in #NorthWaziristan @PresOfPakistan @OfficialDGISPR #RadioPakistan #News https://t.co/WveZVFODZN pic.twitter.com/ZFgexAGLK4
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi praised the security forces for their successful operation and commended the forces’ resolve and professionalism, saying the nation stood with them in the fight against terrorism.
The terrorists would find no place to hide, adding that indiscriminate operations against terrorists under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision were continuing and would continue, Naqvi added.
Read: Security forces kill nine terrorists in North Waziristan operation: state media
A day earlier, security forces killed nine terrorists, including four key commanders belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij , during an intelligence-based operation in North Waziristan, Radio Pakistan reported, citing security sources. A large quantity of weapons and ammunition was also recovered from the terrorists, the sources added.
The latest operations came amid continued security operations against terrorist groups in the country. Security forces on Wednesday killed 18 terrorists in separate operations in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, according to state media reports citing security sources. Thirteen Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists were killed in North Waziristan, while five Fitna al-Hindustan terrorists were killed in Mastung, Balochistan.
Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terrorist activity over the past three months, with a series of attacks across the country resulting in the martyrdom of security personnel and civilians.
Last week, 12 people were killed and 35 others injured when a blast struck a joint checkpoint near Aman Mela in the Darazinda area of Dera Ismail Khan, with the TTP claiming responsibility for the attack.

On September 19, 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred in a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, the Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
In a separate incident, a captain and a lieutenant were among six security personnel martyred in an exchange of fire in Hangu district, while eight terrorists were killed.
On September 1, six personnel, including two officers, and a customs department official were martyred as security forces thwarted an attempt to breach the Customs House in Balochistan.
In July, at least 30 people , including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. The attackers also abducted several civilians and police personnel after the assault.
In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation , which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

title: Prosecutors in Maradona death trial seek sentences up to 12 years
description: The defendants deny wrongdoing as closing arguments begin in the trial
content:
The defendants deny wrongdoing as closing arguments begin in the trial
Argentine prosecutors argued on Thursday that the "chaotic" medical team treating football legend Diego Maradona at the time of his death should receive prison sentences up to 12 years.
Seven medical professionals have been on trial since April over Maradona's death on November 25, 2020 while convalescing after surgery for a brain clot.
The star of the 1986 World Cup died of heart failure and acute pulmonary edema -- a condition where fluid accumulates in the lungs -- at a rented home in the Buenos Aires suburb of Tigre two weeks after going under the knife.
The larger-than-life star, who had a history of substance abuse, was 60 at the time of his death.
His medical team, including his chief doctor, psychiatrist, psychologist and nurses, are accused of providing grossly inadequate care in the lead-up to his death. They deny the charges.
In his closing arguments, prosecutor Patricio Ferrai said the defendants' "chaotic organization" left the ailing patient "in a helpless situation, abandoning him to his fate."
He accused them of having "breached their duties, performed actions contrary to the art of healing" and having "omitted all the acts they were required to perform."
The defendants are charged with "dolo eventual" -- a legal term meaning that a person is aware that their actions could cause harm but persisted nonetheless.
The highest prison sentence sought by prosecutors was 12 years, for Maradona's personal physician, Leopoldo Luque.
Other sentences ranging from four to 10 years were sought for other medical staff, which include a psychiatrist, nurse and coordinators.
The health workers have argued that Maradona's death could not have been foreseen and that they did their jobs. Each defendant has also downplayed their own individual responsibility for his care.
The case has revolved around whether the doctors' decision to allow Maradona convalesce in a private home, instead of in a hospital, was negligent.
The prosecution has also pointed to the near-total absence of medical equipment, such as a hospital bed, defibrillator or quickly available ambulance as evidence of what they presented as the defendants' dereliction of duty.
Several medical experts testified that Maradona's carers failed to react to key warning signs -- he was suffering from edema, tachycardia and had difficulty breathing -- in the lead-up to his death.
"Diego Armando Maradona's death clearly did not come out of nowhere: the signs of this fatal outcome began to appear long beforehand," assistant prosecutor Cosme Iribarren summarized on Thursday.
The prosecution again showed the court shock images of the former footballer lying dead in bed, his stomach grotesquely swollen.
Maradona's three daughters, who were present in court on Thursday for the start of the summation, covered their faces to avoid seeing the images.
The summation is expected to last around two weeks and the verdict is expected at a later date.
The first trial over Maradona's death was dramatically annulled last year after two-and-a-half months of hearings, following revelations that one of the judges took part in a clandestine documentary about the case.

title: Bordeaux confirmed in sixth tier of French football
description: The French side faces a long road back after losing professional status
content:
The French side faces a long road back after losing professional status
Six-time French champions Bordeaux, who were sanctioned in the summer for financial irregularities, will play the current season in the sixth tier of French football, the Nouvelle-Aquitaine league confirmed on Thursday.
Bordeaux were sanctioned for failing to provide the roughly 10 million euros ($11.6 million) needed for the 2025-2026 financial year as well as 2026-2027 and meet debt payments.
Once one of France's leading football clubs and the team where the country's new head coach Zinedine Zidane made his name, Bordeaux was sold last month for a symbolic one euro to US-based investment group Park Bench who agreed to take on the remaining debt.
Two days after appearing before the oversight commission of the Nouvelle-Aquitaine league, which approved their recovery budget and issued "a positive opinion on their possible participation in Regional 1," the club was unanimously approved to play in the top tier.
"Rebuilding can now begin," said Dominique Delport, the new president chosen by Park Bench, speaking to AFP.
The new owners are due in commercial court on October 20 to ratify the new continuation plan, which now runs over 12 years, with the debt halved from 26 to 13 million euros.
The team is largely amateur although they are permitted five players on professional contracts, one of which will go to former Ligue 1 striker Baptiste Guillaume.
The club has produced many big names of French football including academy products Bixente Lizarazu and Christophe Dugarry who both played alongside Zidane in the 1998 World Cup-winning team.
A decade earlier Alain Giresse and Jean Tigana were part of a celebrated France midfield that won the European championships in 1984.
However, they were relegated to Ligue 2 in 2022 and then placed in judicial restructuring in 2024, which caused them to relinquish their professional status and their highly-rated academy.

title: CAS opens hearing into Senegal AFCON title appeal
description: The appeal follows CAF   s decision to award Morocco a 3 0 victory after Senegal   s walk off protest
content:
The appeal follows CAF’s decision to award Morocco a 3-0 victory after Senegal’s walk-off protest
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on Thursday opened its hearing into Senegal's appeal against being stripped of the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) title in favour of Morocco.
The hearing in Lausanne comes almost 10 months after Pape Gueye's extra-time goal gave Senegal victory over the tournament hosts following a chaotic finish to normal time.
Many Teranga Lions players had walked off the pitch in protest at a late penalty award to Morocco, which was missed by Brahim Diaz once the Senegalese players returned to the pitch almost 20 minutes later.
But in March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) overturned that result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title.
Thursday's opening day of the hearing lasted more than five hours behind closed doors.
"I know that the wait for supporters, as much the Senegalese and Moroccan ones as all African fans, has been very long," CAS general manager Matthieu Reeb told reporters, before adding that the hearing could last "days or even weeks".
The Moroccan delegation did not speak to reporters but Senegal's football federation president Abdoulaye Sow said he hoped that "sports law" would be upheld "for the dignity and honour of Africa".
Following their defeat, Morocco appealed to CAF, who ruled that Senegal had broken rules barring teams from leaving the field of play without the referee's authorisation.
Senegal blasted that decision as the "most blatant administrative robbery in the history of our sport" and even paraded the trophy to their supporters in Paris at the end of March.
According to Thibault Ulrich, a researcher in sports law at Lausanne University, the CAF ruling was "extremely strict" and failed to recognise Congolese referee Jean-Jacques Ndala's decision to allow the match to continue.
The International Football Association Board (IFAB), the guardians of the laws of the game, have a rule which suggests that Ndala's decision to continue the match cannot be overturned, even if he erred in doing so.
CAS's own rules favour respect for a referee's decisions, unless he has been proven to be corrupt or acting in bad faith.
On March 18, the Senegalese government called for an investigation into suspected corruption at CAF.
Two weeks before rendering its decision in favour of Morocco, CAF had fired lawyer Yassin Osman Robleh, from Djibouti, who had been in charge of guaranteeing the integrity of its procedures for the previous six years, without publishing its reasons.

Yemen's Houthis escalated their campaign of strikes against Saudi Arabia on Thursday, trying to shut down the kingdom's ​airspace and oil facilities with missile fire that has killed three people this week and left a plane badly damaged.
#Statement Two attacks targeted King Khalid International Airport facilities and a Saudia aircraft. #GACA pic.twitter.com/6YnBN717Cw
The group said it had struck Riyadh airport and warned workers ‌to stay away from energy plants, which would be targeted.
Shrapnel from an interception or another projectile hit had left the commercial plane belonging to Saudi state carrier Saudia Airlines heavily damaged after catching fire while parked at an airport terminal on Thursday, three people briefed on the matter said.
They said no passengers were believed to have been on the plane at the time but they could not rule out any injuries as a result of the incident. A thick black column of ​smoke and flames were shown rising from Riyadh airport in video verified by Reuters .
Saudi Arabia's government media office, its civil aviation authority and Saudia Airlines did not respond to emailed requests ​for comment.
Lufthansa and Air India said they were suspending flights to Riyadh after Houthi attacks.

Separately, Saudi officials said debris from an intercepted missile had hit a kindergarten and ⁠medical complex in Riyadh.
The Houthis say they are targeting the kingdom over its support for government forces in Yemen's reignited civil war. Saudi Arabia says it is backing an offensive by Yemen's UN-recognised government to ​take back territory from the Houthis.
The conflict, now an overspill of the US-Iran war, has added new chaos to a region already aflame, and threatens to draw other states into gruelling mountain fighting, with Syria now considering deploying ​troops to assist Saudi Arabia.
The kingdom has pushed for support from allied nations, including Turkiye and Pakistan, even if only in a logistical or defensive capacity, as it tries to reverse Houthi gains in southwest Yemen, by the southern entrance to the Red Sea.
Those requests have taken on more urgency since Saudi authorities said on Wednesday that three people had been killed this week in strikes on Riyadh airport and Abha airport in the southwest.
The Houthis have made Saudi airports a focus ​of their strikes, and the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen said it had destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the group towards Riyadh and another towards Khamis Mushayt, home to a major airbase.
According to data ​compiled by aviation analytics company Cirium, almost half of departures from Riyadh airport had been cancelled by 1500 GMT, with 31 more cancellations expected for Friday in all Saudi airports.
Flight tracker FlightRadar24 indicated numerous delayed arrivals and departures at Riyadh's ‌King Khalid ⁠International Airport on Thursday. The airport advised travellers to contact airlines to check the status of flights before trying to travel.
Riyadh is due to host a major meeting of energy policymakers, the WPC Energy Congress, this week.
Several multinational firms based in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD) told staff to work from home after loud booms were heard on Thursday morning, five people familiar with the matter said, including some affected staff.
Read more: Information ministry rubbishes 'fake and fabricated' NYT report claiming use of PAF aircraft against Houthis
The Saudi government did not respond to a request for comment, and KAFD was not immediately available for comment.
Some diplomats said they had received warnings, and some schools in Riyadh told parents there were orders to shelter in ​place, though authorities did not issue a public alert. ​Reuters could not identify the source of ⁠the booms.
Yemen's long-running civil war, which paused with a ceasefire in 2022, has erupted again in recent weeks with the Houthis seizing stretches of the Red Sea coast last month, including along the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Their threats to shipping and attacks on Saudi cities and infrastructure have ​drawn the kingdom back in. This week, Saudi-backed forces launched a counterattack, taking back some areas around the strait.
However, in a war with several front lines, the Houthis ​have made gains of their ⁠own, surrounding Yemen's third-largest city, Taiz, by taking territory along its main mountain road to Aden.
The fighting, which pits the Houthis against a coalition of Saudi-backed forces under the internationally recognised government, has led to a humanitarian crisis in the poorest Arab state, displacing 200,000 people since the conflict resumed.
One US and one Syrian defence official said Syria was carefully considering options for military support, including defensive aid to protect Saudi Arabia from attacks, or an offensive ⁠deployment to help ​take the fight to the Houthis.
In response to a request for comment to the Syrian foreign ministry, a diplomat said Syria ​stood firmly with Saudi Arabia but that its focus was on domestic priorities such as recovery from its own civil war.
NATO-member Turkey said on Wednesday it was sending mainly defensive and technical support to the kingdom to help in the fight against the Houthis. ​A Turkish official said this was expected to take the form of military equipment, intelligence sharing and weapons systems.

title: UEFA president Ceferin to stand for re election in 2027
description: The 58 year old was first elected in 2016
content:
The 58-year-old was first elected in 2016
UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin on Thursday told the 55 member national associations of European football's governing body that he would stand for a final re-election next year.
The announcement reversed the Slovenian's previous decision that he would not seek re-election and came following "unanimous" support from the national associations, UEFA said in a statement.
The 58-year-old was first elected in 2016 to replace Michel Platini, who resigned after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) banned him from football-related activities over a FIFA corruption case.
Ceferin will stand for a final four-year term at UEFA's congress in Kazakhstan next April.
"I want to thank the national associations for their trust," Ceferin said following Thursday's meeting in Berlin.
"We have faced extraordinary challenges over the past years, and we have faced them as one team.
"There is still important work ahead, and I have therefore accepted their request.
"My ambition remains the same: to keep European football united, make our game stronger and leave UEFA ready for the next generation."
In their statement, UEFA said that over the previous months the 55 national associations had "unanimously" asked Ceferin to reconsider his previous intention not to seek re-election.
"The meeting also focused on the future governance and leadership of FIFA," said UEFA, who have led opposition to Gianni Infantino's leadership of world football's governing body.
One of their proposals is that the FIFA president "leads, not manages".

title: Mourinho s Real Madrid playing catch up in Clasico countdown
description: The six point gap leaves Madrid under pressure to deliver results before their visit to Camp Nou
content:
The six-point gap leaves Madrid under pressure to deliver results before their visit to Camp Nou
Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid trail leaders Barcelona by six points as La Liga action resumes this weekend, with Spanish football starting the countdown to the Clasico after the extended international break.
It has not been plain sailing for the Portuguese veteran since he returned to the helm of Los Blancos, with defeats at Real Betis and then rivals Atletico Madrid leaving them fourth after seven games.
"Obviously we want to be first, not second, third, fourth, or fifth. And we want more points than we have. Obviously, obviously," said Mourinho before the international break, before blaming officials for his team's struggles.
Madrid visit Barcelona at Camp Nou on October 25 in Mourinho's first Clasico since returning to the Spanish capital this summer, following his first stint at the helm between 2010-2013.
Before then come four tough matches for Madrid, hosting Villarreal on Saturday and then Sevilla in La Liga, as well as facing Roma and RB Leipzig in the Champions League.
Barcelona also have a tricky lead-in to the Clasico, with league games against Getafe and Betis mixed with away games in the Champions League at Galatasaray and holders Paris Saint-Germain.
Hansi Flick's side have been unstoppable so far, winning every single match with devastating attacking force, netting 31 goals in their seven league games.
Whether Mourinho is capable of reining in Spain's dominant domestic side will become clear in the testing fortnight ahead.
While Madrid have shown some signs of improvement from last season's poor campaign under Xabi Alonso and then Alvaro Arbeloa, they still have a lot further to go to trouble Flick's Barca machine.
Mourinho has a host of issues to manage in the coming weeks, including the form of Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior.
The coach has defended the Brazilian while admitting he is not at his "killer" best, but starting with the Yellow Submarine's visit to the Santiago Bernabeu, Vinicius must prove he is worthy of a starting spot.
Mourinho hooked the Brazilian in the 2-1 defeat by Atletico and Vinicius subsequently failed to score for his national team in games against Australia and India.
There are also concerns around superstar striker Kylian Mbappe.
The French forward has again impressed in front of goal, scoring seven times in La Liga and maintaining the consistency he has shown since joining Madrid. However, he picked up a minor knee injury while on international duty.
Mbappe did not return immediately to Madrid and posted a video of himself riding a bicycle on social media, a few days after Mourinho had said cycling was something he did not want players to do for safety reasons.
Real Madrid fans are often quick to whistle their own players when unhappy, and Mbappe's recent efforts to promote his Ballon d'Or candidacy have drawn criticism from some supporters, particularly amid frustration at the club's failure to win a major trophy in the past two seasons.
Record signing Yan Diomande has yet to bed into the team fully, while the narrow Champions League win over Inter Milan showed Mourinho's side cannot control matches, despite the good result.
The team's run of one clean sheet in eight matches across all competitions also reflects defensive problems, while Mourinho has criticised his team for not capitalising on chances to finish games off and allowing opponents back in.
Mourinho's and Madrid's complaints about refereeing, most recently and explicitly after the derby defeat by Atletico on September 20, can only stave off pressure from the club's own fans for so long.
"If they leave us alone, calmly, and let us compete on equal terms, there's still a long way to go," said the veteran Portuguese coach in the aftermath of that loss.
After three weeks licking their wounds and looking at fixes for the problems that have quickly appeared, Mourinho's Madrid can now start walking that road.

title: PM Shehbaz condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia  calls for immediate halt
description: Reiterates Pakistan   s commitment to the kingdom   s sovereignty  territorial integrity and security
content:
Reiterates Pakistan’s commitment to the kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, security
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday called on Yemen’s Houthi militia to “immediately cease these attacks” on Saudi Arabia, as he condemned the “repeated terrorist attacks” against the kingdom, including the targeting of airports in Riyadh and Abha.
In a post on X, PM Shehbaz said the attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha International Airport had resulted in “loss of lives and injuries to civilians”.
“I strongly condemn the repeated terrorist attacks by the Houthi militia against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” he said.
I strongly condemn the repeated terrorist attacks by the Houthi militia against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including the targeting of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha International Airport, which resulted in loss of lives and injuries to civilians. I…
The prime minister commended the “vigilance and professionalism” of the Saudi armed forces and the coalition for intercepting multiple ballistic missiles, praising their “tireless efforts to protect innocent lives and safeguard the kingdom”.
Reaffirming Pakistan’s support, he said the country stood in “unwavering solidarity with the leadership and people of our brotherly kingdom of Saudi Arabia”.
Referring to the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and recent decisions taken by the Strategic Political and Defence Committee, PM Shehbaz said Pakistan’s commitment to the kingdom’s “sovereignty, territorial integrity and security” was “resolute”.
He also expressed Pakistan’s “full support” for Saudi Arabia’s “legitimate right to defend its people and protect its cities and vital infrastructure”.
“We will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with Saudi Arabia in the face of these threats,” he added.
Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted 3 Houthi ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh, Khamis Mushait
The latest attacks followed a series of Houthi missile and drone strikes targeting Saudi airports and other infrastructure. Saudi authorities said three people were killed and 36 injured, including a Pakistani national, in attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha International Airport on October 6 and 7.
The Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed multiple ballistic missiles launched towards Riyadh and Khamis Mushait in the southwestern Asir region. Coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said two missiles had been fired towards the Saudi capital and another towards Khamis Mushait.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed the group had targeted King Khalid International Airport with a ballistic missile, saying the strike had disrupted air traffic. He also warned workers at Saudi oil facilities and airlines operating in Saudi airspace about locations the group had declared targets for its military operations.
In response, the Saudi-led coalition said it had struck more than 80 Houthi military sites across the Yemeni governorates of Saada, Hodeidah, Jawf and Marib, warning that the attacks on Saudi Arabia “will not go unpunished”.
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye on October 5 agreed to implement their collective defence commitments and ensure the “rapid deployment” of agreed military forces and capabilities to Saudi Arabia amid escalating Houthi attacks on the kingdom. The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee of the Makkah Alliance for Defence in Riyadh.
Read: Information ministry rejects Reuters report on Makkah defence pact as 'speculative'
Under the decision, the committee directed the necessary measures to provide the agreed forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in Saudi Arabia, in accordance with approved arrangements and the national legislation of the three countries. It said the move would enhance “readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats”.
Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry subsequently confirmed that Pakistani troops were present in Saudi Arabia in “multiple capabilities”, while the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting said operational details of the deployment remained confidential.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed MJDA, a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
Houthis have repeatedly carried out missile and drone attacks against Saudi Arabia since the Yemen war escalated in 2015, targeting military installations, airports, oil facilities and other critical infrastructure.
In September 2019 , the group claimed responsibility for drone attacks on Saudi Aramco’s Abqaiq processing facility and Khurais oil field, attacks that temporarily disrupted more than half of Saudi Arabia’s crude production.
The attacks continued in subsequent years, including strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure in March 2022.
More recently, Houthi attacks have again targeted Saudi territory. In September, the group claimed missile and drone strikes on a Saudi military base and other targets, while Saudi authorities reported attacks affecting several cities.
It is worth noting that on September 25 , Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye senior military leadership strongly condemned attacks targeting the holy city of Makkah as they reaffirmed their commitment to the collective defence of the kingdom under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.
Read more: Makkah defence alliance agrees to 'rapid force deployment' in Saudi Arabia: FO
A day after that, Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman reaffirmed continued joint efforts to confront attacks targeting Makkah and civilian and economic facilities in the kingdom during a meeting with the Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir.
Then, on September 27, Defence Minister Asif also reiterated the resolve to implement the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement amid the rising Houthis attacks on Saudi Arabia and said that both Pakistan and Türkiye would stand with Saudi Arabia practically and diplomatically in case of any aggression.
Asif further stressed that protecting Saudi Arabia fell under divine duty.
"If there wasn't an agreement, if Saudi Arabia had been attacked, especially if the sacred cities of Makkah and Madinah were attacked, then we are bound by an eternal agreement; that is, we will protect the House of God and Madinah," he stated in an interview to a private channel.
He also outlined that the "worldly agreement" referring to the MJDA between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to protect one another, would operate in all circumstances.
Significance of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
The MJDA was the latest step in longstanding military and strategic cooperation between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. Signed in Makkah, the pact established a framework for collective deterrence and stipulated that an armed attack on any one of the three countries would be considered an attack on all three, while providing for wider cooperation across defence.
The agreement followed nearly a year of negotiations and came amid heightened instability across the Middle East. Turkiye and Pakistan had sought closer regional security cooperation, while Saudi Arabia had faced growing security concerns as conflicts spread across the region, threatening its territory, energy infrastructure and ambitious economic development plans.
For Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the trilateral pact is built on their Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed in September 2025. That agreement stated that “any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both” and committed the two sides to strengthening defence cooperation and joint deterrence.

title: Manchester City must  stick together  during crisis  says Haaland
description: The Norwegian urges his team mates to focus on football ahead of their Anfield trip
content:
The Norwegian urges his team-mates to focus on football ahead of their Anfield trip
Erling Haaland said Manchester City must "stick together" in uncertain times after being found guilty of over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules.
City face a severe points penalty or even expulsion from the Premier League after an independent commission found they used "sham" commercial contracts to inflate revenue and cut costs by over £900 million ($1.2 billion) between 2009 and 2018.
Haaland did not join City until 2022 but it is the current squad that could bear the burden of any sanction.
Premier League leaders City return to action for the first time since the guilty verdict was revealed at Liverpool on Sunday.
"We have to stay positive, look ahead and try to win football games and try to enjoy the situation and win the game," Haaland told the club's website.
"We have to stick together, and we have to spread the love to each other.
"So yeah, stick together, enjoy the ride and smile."
Haaland signed a contract until 2034 last year, but his future is likely to depend on the severity of any sanction.
The Norwegian has scored 169 goals in 205 games for the club and also shone in spearheading his country's run to the World Cup quarter-finals.
Europe's top teams would be lining up for the 26-year-old should City face dropping out of the Premier League or even a prolonged spell without Champions League football.
"I care a lot about City, I have to say," added Haaland, whose father, Alf-Inge Haaland, also played for the club.
"I care a lot about the fans because I'm a fan myself -- I feel with them as well."
City manager Enzo Maresca echoed Haaland's call for unity.
"Personally, I'm very calm, to be honest," Maresca told City's website.
"The club has been quite clear. We trust completely the club. We understand the noise but the focus for us is just what we can control and we can control just the football side.
"We need to be all together. I said many times the reason why this organisation in the last 15 years was top was because from the owner, the CEO, the sporting director, the manager, players, fans, they are all on the same page. And this is fantastic."
City have made a perfect start to the Premier League season, winning all of their opening five games, with Maresca insisting the mood among his squad is "fantastic" following a lengthy international break.
"The players are excited for the next two games," he said.
"But especially they are excited because in this moment we are top of the league. The players are just focused on that.
"They know what we can control is the football side –- they are not worried at all about different things."
He added: "They know their profession and they know that the noise is there, but they don't care too much about the noise. They are just focused in this moment on how we can beat Liverpool and how, together with the fans, we can try to win in Anfield."

title: IRGC says it struck LPG tanker attempting to cross Strait of Hormuz
description: Aircraft carrier spent record 265 consecutive days at sea  received Presidential Unit Citation from defense chief
author_name: Anadolu Agency, Reuters, Web Desk, AFP
content:
Pentagon prepares 3-day intensive Iran strike option as Trump says no attack before midterms: NYT
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it had struck a tanker attempting to navigate an “illegal route” through the Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran has sought to blockade since the start of the Middle East war, according to AFP .
The Guards said in a statement carried by state news agency IRNA that Iranian forces “have taken control of the administration of the strait”. They added that the LPG (liquefied petroleum gas) carrier NV Sunshine, owned by NatWit, had been struck hours earlier while attempting to transit an “illegal route” south of the Strait of Hormuz.
Pentagon prepares 3-day intensive Iran strike option as Trump says no attack before midterms: NYT
The Pentagon has drawn up plans for an intensive three-day military campaign against Iran, the New York Times reported on Thursday, even as President Donald Trump said Washington will not launch an attack before the November 3 midterm elections.
The US military, acting on Trump's orders, has developed options to strike Iran's missile and drone arsenal, energy facilities and other military sites, The Times reported, citing US officials.
Senior national security officials, led by Vice President JD Vance, discussed the plans at Camp David last Friday, with the options centring on a short, intensive campaign lasting about three days, according to people briefed on the proposal.
The strikes would focus on Iran's missile and drone arsenal, much of which has been rebuilt by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) since the early phase of the war, the newspaper said.
Other potential targets include Iranian energy facilities as well as IRGC command posts and headquarters.
Axios separately reported that the Pentagon ordered the US Central Command (CENTCOM) several days ago to complete preparations for a possible resumption of major combat operations against Iran.
The directive did not set a date for strikes, and Trump had not made a final decision, Axios said, adding that any renewed major combat operations were expected to include large-scale bombing of Iranian energy, infrastructure and nuclear targets.
The military preparations come as Trump said on Thursday that the US would not attack Iran before the November 3 midterm elections, while pointing to ongoing diplomatic efforts.
In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump said Washington and Tehran were having "productive discussions."
The NYT also reported that Trump has repeatedly declined proposals in recent months to resume major combat operations against Iran, despite ordering the Pentagon to prepare new options.
Three US aircraft carriers are expected to be in the Middle East in the coming weeks as part of the major military buildup, according to the newspaper.
Iran's proxies must stop violent acts, EU's von der Leyen says
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Friday that Iran's proxies must stop what she described as reckless and violent acts, following attacks on Riyadh airport which she attributed to the Iran-aligned Houthi movement in Yemen.
The European Union stands in full solidarity with the people of Saudi Arabia and Gulf partners, von der Leyen said, adding that attacks on civilian infrastructure were "unacceptable".
US sanctions 17 vessels linked to Iran’s ‘shadow fleet’
The US Treasury Department on Thursday imposed sanctions on 17 vessels linked to Iran’s “shadow fleet,” stepping up pressure on Tehran’s petroleum exports.
The department said the vessels had transported millions of barrels of Iranian crude oil, petroleum and petrochemical products to South and East Asian markets.
The sanctions also targeted companies involved in the shipping network.
“No enabler of Iranian sanctions evasion is safe from the full force of Treasury’s authorities,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said.
Among the vessels targeted was the Vanuatu-flagged Tina 5, which Treasury said had transported more than 1.5 million barrels of Iranian crude oil in August.
The Comoros-flagged Sogl transported over 2 million barrels of Iranian propane and butane since September 2025, while the Cameroon-flagged Shenzen carried more than 3.5 million barrels of crude since November 2025, according to the department.
The action is part of Operation Economic Outcast, launched on August 24 to restrict Iran’s access to international financial and commercial networks.
Iranian president says peace talks will only succeed without ‘pressure, threats’
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said at a regional summit in Turkmenistan that peace negotiations would only succeed without “pressure and threats”, with the months-long Middle East war locked in a stalemate, AFP reported on Friday.
“Dialogue holds meaning and a chance of success only when based on mutual respect and mutual commitments, and when devoid of pressure and threat,” he said during his speech at the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) summit.
USS Abraham Lincoln returns to San Diego after supporting Iran war
The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier returned Thursday to its home port of San Diego, ending a record-setting 321-day deployment in which it took part in the US-Israeli war against Iran, according to USNI News .
The carrier pulled into Naval Air Station North Island after a deployment that included 265 consecutive days at sea without a port call, a Navy record.
Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth boarded the ship at sea Wednesday and presented the crew with the Presidential Unit Citation, the highest decoration awarded to military units, for its role in Operation Epic Fury.
Hegseth told sailors the strike group had done what “no other carrier strike group has ever done.”
He rejected what he described as attempts to turn the carrier into “a symbol of dysfunction” or of low morale.
Read: Information ministry rubbishes 'fake and fabricated' NYT report claiming use of PAF aircraft against Houthis
The Lincoln, carrying 5,000 sailors and Marines, left San Diego last November for the Pacific. It was redirected to the Middle East after the US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28.
During the summer, media reports described shortages of food and basic supplies, and declining mental health and morale among the crew, including reports that two sailors tried to jump overboard.
Iran says weapons production surged after aggression
Iran's armed forces remain fully equipped and combat-ready against the enemy, with weapons production not only continuing but sharply increasing despite recent aggression, the Defence Ministry spokesman said, according to Press TV .
‘Hands full against the enemy’: Iran says weapons production surged after aggression https://t.co/MIE7nPInMJ
Brigadier General Reza Talaei-Nik, speaking in a special interview on Thursday, declared that “the hands of the armed forces are full” in terms of equipment, weapons, and a continuous, resilient supply chain, stressing that there is no shortage facing the enemy.
He said production in the seven months following the imposed 40-day war of aggression rose 2.5 times compared with the equivalent period before the conflict.
Heavy explosions in Strait of Hormuz as tankers may have hit mines: Iran’s state broadcaster
Several powerful explosions were reported in the southern passage of the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, possibly after oil tankers struck naval mines, Iranian state broadcaster IRIB reported, citing military sources.
The explosions occurred minutes earlier in the southern passage of the strategic waterway, according to the broadcaster
The sources said oil tankers using “unauthorised” routes may have hit mines deployed in the area.
The report did not provide details about the number or identities of the tankers, possible casualties or damage.
The reported explosions come amid heightened tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran has warned vessels against using routes not authorised by Tehran.
Trump says comment that Iran could 'take out' Los Angeles was misinterpreted
US President Donald Trump on Thursday said comments he made that Iran could "take out" California cities had ​been misinterpreted and that he was instead referring ‌to the need for people to tolerate higher gas prices.
Trump made the remarks at a political rally in Nebraska on Monday as ​he spoke about Americans' wartime economic sacrifices.
Read more: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted 3 Houthi ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh, Khamis Mushait
"Remember, with ​the war, it's just artificial, it's a little ⁠bit high, it's a small price to pay," ​he said then. "It's a small price to pay for ​keeping the world safe, for keeping our country safe. They could take out a city. Let 'em take out Los Angeles, ​let 'em take out San Diego. This is a ​very small price to pay, and it's going to be over ‌with ⁠very soon."
California's Democratic leaders and some fellow Republicans quickly rebuked the remarks.
"What I was talking about was that a temporary increase in the price of Gasoline is a ​small price ​to pay ⁠for Iran not having a Nuclear Weapon," Trump said in a Truth Social ​post on Thursday.
"If you want to see a ​big ⁠price, can you imagine what it would be like if they bombed San Diego and/or Los Angeles?" he ⁠continued, ​saying he loved both cities.
Trump has ​shrugged off cost-of-living concerns stemming from the Iran conflict before.

title: Property sale NOC linked to sanitation fee payment
description: Property sale NOC linked to sanitation fee payment
content:
Punjab govt prepares to complete distribution of five million bills across province
The Punjab government has made payment of the sanitation fee mandatory for obtaining a no-objection certificate (NOC) required for the sale of property.
The distribution of the first sanitation bills across the province is under way.
Under the new condition, an NOC will not be issued for property transactions unless the sanitation fee has been paid. The move has reportedly affected property transactions as the government prepares to complete the distribution of around five million bills this month.
The new requirement comes after the government began billing urban property owners under the Suthra Punjab programme this month. The excise, taxation and narcotics control department has been assigned the responsibility for billing and collecting the sanitation fee from around five million residential and commercial properties in urban areas.
Under the mechanism, two bills will be issued during a six-month period towards the annual sanitation fee liability. Property owners will have 60 days from receipt of a bill to make payment, with late payments subject to penalties.
The government expects to collect around Rs40 billion annually through the sanitation fee.
Data integration between the excise department and Suthra Punjab programme has been completed, allowing sanitation fee records to be linked with property data.
The integration has also resulted in the NOC condition being introduced before completion of the province-wide bill distribution.
Previously, payment of property tax was required before the NOC could be issued. The requirement has been extended to include payment of the sanitation fee.

title: Food streets heat up as winter sets in
description: Food streets heat up as winter sets in
content:
Vendors say families, office workers driving evening demand for hot snacks
As the weather turns cooler, Lahore's appetite for hot and spicy treats is also returning, with food stalls and eateries drawing crowds during the evening.
As dusk falls, sizzling jalebis dipped in syrup, freshly fried samosas, moong daal pathoras and pakoras can be found at food points across the city, with their aromas attracting passers-by. For many Lahoris, a cup of hot tea completes the experience.
Lahore's evenings are traditionally associated with food, but the arrival of a slight chill has further increased the flow of customers to eateries.
From Gawalmandi and Fort Road to Gulberg, Johar Town and Township, demand for hot and spicy snacks has risen during the evening hours.
Office workers returning home and students coming back from universities and colleges can be seen enjoying the cooler weather with their favourite foods.
Ayesha Khan, a woman visiting the market for shopping, said she preferred cold foods during summer, but as soon as the weather became cooler, an evening without a hot samosa, tea and jalebi felt incomplete.
University student Hamza Ali said sitting with friends at a food point after classes and having hot samosa chaat or pathoras was one of the best things about the cooler weather.
Sidra Mahmood, who was out shopping, said it was difficult to resist when the aroma of freshly fried jalebis and samosas reached her, although she tried to avoid eating too many fried foods.
Food vendors are also welcoming the seasonal change.
Shopkeeper Muhammad Usman said demand for samosas, pakoras and pathoras increased as temperatures dropped, particularly in the evening. Office workers returning home and families were among the customers visiting food points in large numbers, he added.
Another vendor, Ali Raza, said demand for jalebi and tea also increased with the change in weather. The aroma of freshly prepared jalebi was often enough to attract customers, he said.
However, health experts have advised food lovers to enjoy such treats in moderation.
Dr Ali Rashid of Services Hospital said samosas, pakoras, pathoras and other fried foods could be consumed occasionally and in moderate quantities, but excessive consumption could put a strain on the digestive system.
He said spicy and fatty foods could aggravate acid reflux, heartburn and indigestion in some people. He advised citizens to eat fresh and hygienically prepared food, drink adequate water and avoid lying down immediately after eating.
For Lahore's food lovers, the changing weather has brought a familiar evening ritual back to life steaming cups of tea, crisp samosas and freshly prepared jalebis. With a little moderation, residents can enjoy the flavours of the season without compromising their health.

title: Rare eagle  From stitched eyes to open skies
description: Rare eagle  From stitched eyes to open skies
content:
Rescued bird recovers 90% and is set to return to the wild in December
Its eyes were stitched shut, its flight feathers damaged and its body reduced to a shadow of what it should have been. Rescued from a remote area of Sukkur, a rare white-tailed eagle is now preparing to take to the skies again - nearly 150 years after the species was last reliably recorded in Pakistan.
The eagle, rescued last year in an extremely weak and injured condition, has made a remarkable recovery and is now about 90% healthy. The infection caused by the stitching has cleared completely, while its flight feathers have begun growing back.
If its recovery continues as expected, the bird will be released in the Margalla Hills in December, coinciding with the seasonal movement of migratory birds.
The eagle was discovered by a group of young bird enthusiasts conducting research on migratory birds arriving in Pakistan from colder regions. According to bird-watcher Haroon Yousafzai, the bird was in such poor condition that rescuers immediately moved it to a secure location for treatment and rehabilitation.
Its ordeal, however, had begun long before the rescue. Yousafzai said the eagle had been deliberately confined at a site used to trap other birds of prey. Its eyes had been sewn shut with thread to prevent it from flying, leaving it with severe wounds and infections. Its flight feathers had also been damaged.
Adding to its misery was an inappropriate diet. Instead of its natural food, including ducks and fish, the eagle had been fed chicken entrails and other unsuitable items, leaving its digestive system in poor condition. After the rescue, sustained medical care, proper nutrition and round-the-clock monitoring gradually began to reverse the damage. Its eye infection has now completely healed and its flight feathers are growing back.
The bird's recovery has drawn particular attention because of the rarity of the species in Pakistan.
Yousafzai said available historical references indicate that the white-tailed eagle was last reliably recorded in Pakistan around the 1870s in the Agrowr Valley, an area adjoining Mansehra and Oghi in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. Other references point to possible sightings in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, but these records are considered less reliable.
Sindh Wildlife Deputy Conservator Mumtaz Soomro praised the young rescuers, saying timely reporting and cooperation between citizens and wildlife authorities were crucial to saving rare species.
The Sindh Wildlife Department plans to release the eagle in the Margalla Hills once it has fully recovered. Experts say choosing a suitable natural habitat is essential to ensure the bird has access to food, water and shelter and can resume its natural behaviour. Before release, the eagle will be fitted with a GPS tracking tag.

Barrister Gohar demanded that legal requirements concerning arrested political workers and leaders be fully observed, and that political issues be resolved through negotiations and constitutional, democratic means rather than arrests.

Three MNAs, five MPAs missing since Sept 20; party says more than 18 workers also disappeared
Alleged abductions and arrests of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) lawmakers and workers in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa have continued unabated, with the party reporting that three members of the national assembly and five members of the provincial assembly have been taken since 20 September.
PTI leaders say the incidents intensified after the party announced its long march. According to party accounts, the tally now includes the three MNAs and five MPAs plus more than a dozen-and-a-half workers and office-bearers who remain missing.
The sequence of reported events began with an alleged attempt to abduct Provincial Minister for Construction and Communication Shakeel Khan on 20 September. The following day, Provincial Minister for Irrigation Fazal Shakoor Khan was reportedly seized from a motorway toll plaza.
On 22 September, National Assembly member Fazal Khan from Charsadda was said to have been taken from Rashakai. That same night, between 22 and 23 September, Zubair Khan, the National Assembly member from South Waziristan, was allegedly abducted from his residence in Dera Ismail Khan.
Provincial Assembly member Muhammad Riaz from Kolai-Palas was reported missing on 25 September, while Sultan Rom, the MPA from Swat, was taken by unidentified persons the next day. In a separate incident, unidentified assailants attacked the hujra of MPA Abdul Karim Tordher in Swabi with intense gunfire and then abducted his brother Abdul Nasir along with three security guards.
Reports have also emerged of the arrests in Islamabad of MPA Fateh-ul-Mulk Nasir from Chitral and National Assembly member Dawar Kundi from Tank.
Earlier cases cited by the party include the 17 September abduction of Amir Ijaz, regional general secretary of the Insaf Lawyers Forum. PTI has claimed that Dr Nabi Jan of the Insaf Doctors Forum was likewise taken by unidentified persons. In Mardan, the abduction of MPA Abdul Salam Afridi has been reported and a first information report lodged with police.
Party spokesmen describe the pattern as systematic targeting of elected representatives and grassroots workers in the province. They say the operations have created an atmosphere of fear among PTI ranks and disrupted organisational activity ahead of the planned long march.
Official confirmation of the status of each individual remains limited. Some cases have been registered as abductions; others are described by authorities as arrests linked to ongoing investigations. Families and party lawyers continue to press for information on the whereabouts of those still unaccounted for.
As of the latest reports from Peshawar, the series of incidents that began after 20 September has not subsided, leaving three national and five provincial lawmakers either missing or in custody and a larger number of PTI workers untraceable.

title: Seasonal illnesses surge across Quetta
description: Seasonal illnesses surge across Quetta
content:
Cold, dry weather fuels respiratory ailments
A sharp rise in seasonal illnesses has been reported across Quetta following the recent change in weather. Children, women, young people and the elderly are increasingly falling ill with colds, flu, cough, fever, sore throat, body aches and respiratory problems. Patients already suffering from asthma and allergies are also facing greater difficulties.
The sudden drop in temperature combined with dry and cold winds has led to a noticeable increase in health complaints among residents. Outpatient departments (OPDs) at both government and private hospitals in the city are witnessing heavy rush, with large numbers of people seeking treatment daily for weather-related ailments.
Health experts note that viral infections tend to spread more rapidly during seasonal transitions. Cold and dry air further aggravates respiratory conditions, asthma and allergies.
Experts recommend wearing a mask outdoors to protect against dust and cold winds. They also advise drinking lukewarm water, consuming hot beverages, soup and maintaining a balanced diet. If symptoms persist or breathing becomes difficult, people should consult a doctor promptly rather than self-medicating.
Parents have been urged to protect children from cold winds and abrupt temperature changes, while special care is advised for the elderly and those with pre-existing respiratory conditions.

title: Balakot remembers victims on quake anniversary

content:
Residents say they had received little more than promises and assurances from the authorities
The 21st anniversary of the devastating October 8, 2005 earthquake was observed in Balakot and surrounding areas with solemnity and grief on Thursday, as residents remembered those who lost their lives in the catastrophe.
A sombre atmosphere prevailed across the valley, with people mourning the loss of their loved ones. The main ceremony was held at Government High School Balakot, where an alarm was sounded at exactly 8:52am, the time the earthquake struck, followed by a one-minute silence in memory of the victims.
Muttahida Majlis-e-Amal MPA Munir Hussain Laghmani, District Education Officer Mansehra Zahid Khan, Assistant Commissioner Balakot Hasrat Khan, former tehsil nazim Haji Rustam Khan, teachers, students, members of the business community and a large number of residents attended the ceremony. A collective prayer was also offered for the departed souls.
However, the anniversary once again revived the long-standing grievances of earthquake survivors. Despite 21 years having passed since the disaster, the authorities have failed to present any concrete and practical plan for the allotment of plots in New Balakot City.
As in previous years, residents said they had received little more than promises and assurances from the authorities. Victims from the red-zone areas of Garlat and Balakot returned to their temporary homes once again, carrying their hopes of being settled in New Balakot City and the renewed pain of waiting for another anniversary.

title: Monkeys need space  not snacks
description: Monkeys need space  not snacks
content:
Conservationists urge visitors to stop feeding monkeys in Margallas
The afternoon was calm on the Margalla Hills. A group of hikers had stopped along the trail to catch their breath, enjoy the cool breeze and admire Islamabad stretching beneath them. From the height of the hills, the capital appeared peaceful and distant, its busy roads and buildings softened by the surrounding green landscape.
A monkey emerged from the trees and moved towards the hikers, its eyes fixed on a packet of biscuits. Within seconds, the quiet break turned into laughter, nervous shouts and hurried steps backwards. The hikers pulled their bags closer as the monkey continued its approach without the slightest hesitation.
"Be careful with the biscuits!" one hiker shouted.
The monkey remained completely unfazed. It had spotted the food and appeared to know exactly what it wanted.
"These monkeys know exactly who is carrying food," another hiker joked.
For the hikers, it was an amusing encounter. But for wildlife enthusiasts and officials, scenes like this point to a deeper and increasingly visible problem: wild animals are becoming accustomed to human food.
Across Daman-e-Koh, Trail 3, Trail 5 and other routes through the Margalla Hills, hikers, families, students and fitness enthusiasts regularly share the trails with wildlife. They come for exercise, fresh air, scenic views and a break from the routine of city life.
Yet the boundary between observing wildlife and interfering with it can disappear quickly when visitors begin offering food.
"We come here for the views and the peace, but the monkeys have become part of the experience too," said regular hiker Khalid Malik.
Another hiker summed up the experience with a laugh: "You can forget your water bottle, but never forget to protect your snacks."
Behind the humour is a serious conservation concern.
Mansoor Sherwani, a young nature enthusiast and biodiversity advocate who volunteers with the Islamabad Wildlife Management Board (IWMB) has made public awareness about wildlife feeding an important part of his work. He regularly approaches visitors on the trails, asking them not to feed monkeys or other wild animals.
For Mansoor, the issue is not about a single biscuit, sandwich or piece of fruit. It is about what repeated feeding teaches an animal.
"Wild animals know how to find food in their own habitat," he explained. "When people keep feeding them, they begin to expect food from humans instead of finding it themselves."
He believes visitors often feed wildlife with good intentions. A person sees a monkey approaching and assumes that giving it a piece of bread, fruit or a paratha is an act of kindness.
But, he argues, kindness can have unintended consequences.
One encounter particularly stayed with him.
A family had arrived on the trail carrying freshly prepared desi ghee parathas. The food had not simply been packed for their own picnic. They had brought the parathas from their village specifically to feed the monkeys.
Several monkeys watched from nearby branches as the family prepared to offer them the food.
Mansoor approached the family and explained why feeding wildlife could interfere with the animals' natural behaviour.
Then, hoping humour would make his message easier to remember, he joked: "Why don't you give those parathas to me instead? I hardly ever get to eat desi ghee parathas like these."
The family laughed, but their intention remained serious. They told him that they had brought the special food from their village specifically for the monkeys.
For Mansoor, the encounter revealed how deeply the practice is rooted in public perception.

title: CCTV footage surfaces in girl s death case
description: CCTV footage surfaces in girl s death case
content:
Police add murder charge, launch raids for arrest of victim's relative
CCTV footage showing the last known movements of 15-year-old Maimoona, whose body was found at her maternal uncle's house a day after she went missing, has surfaced, while police have added Section 302 (murder) of the Pakistan Penal Code to the kidnapping case.
The footage shows the girl, dressed in green and white, walking through a street. A man, whom the family has identified as her maternal uncle, is seen stopping her and talking to her for a while. He also appears to hand her something, after which she turns back and the man walks away in another direction.
Police and family members reportedly checked the maternal uncle's house based on suspicions arising from the footage, but found it locked. In the presence of family members and local residents, police broke open the lock and found the girl's body beneath a charpoy inside the house.
The body bore apparent signs of violence. Police took it into custody, collected evidence from the scene and shifted it to a hospital for a post-mortem examination. Officials said the exact cause of death would be determined after the post-mortem report.
According to police, Maimoona's father, Muhammad Faisal, a resident of Dhoke Najju, had reported her missing. He said she left home for a madrassa on October 6 but did not return. A kidnapping case was registered against unidentified persons the same day.
After recovery of the body, police added the murder charge to the case. Raids are being conducted at different locations, including areas in Charsadda and Abbottabad, to arrest the suspected accused.
Rawalpindi CPO Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera took notice of the incident and directed police to arrest those involved. SSP Investigation Saifullah also visited the crime scene.
The girl's mother has appealed to Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz for justice. In a video statement, she alleged that the suspected accused was alone at home when her daughter went missing and that marks of violence were visible on the body after it was recovered.
She further alleged that the suspect initially joined the family in searching for the girl and, when she later went to his house to ask about Maimoona, he did not open the door and said he had not seen her.
The mother said her daughter had been brutally killed and appealed for justice, questioning how other girls could remain safe if her family did not receive justice.
Police said all aspects of the case were being investigated and that the cause of death and motive would become clear from the post-mortem report and investigation. They said anyone found involved would be arrested and proceeded against according to law.
