Russian president says Tehran is making 'real efforts' to resolve conflict
Russian President Vladimir Putin told Iranian counterpart Masoud Pezeshkian on Thursday that Moscow was ready to do everything in its power to help end the war in Iran, as the two leaders met ahead of a summit of former Soviet states in Turkmenistan.
"You know our position. On our part, we are ready to do everything we can to help you resolve this situation," Putin told Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) summit in the Caspian Sea resort of Avaza, Russian news agencies reported.
Putin said Iran was making "real efforts to end the conflict", which he said had broken out "through no fault" of Tehran. "We are ready to do everything that is in our power to contribute to the settlement of this situation," he said, according to Russian state media.
The Iran conflict began after US and Israeli attacks on Iran on February 28. The meeting came as talks between Tehran and Washington appeared to have reached an impasse. Pezeshkian said earlier this week that negotiations with Washington were "meaningless".
Putin also pointed to what he called a "positive evolution" in relations between Russia and Iran. The two countries have strengthened diplomatic and military ties since Russia launched its offensive in Ukraine in February 2022.
Ukraine and Western countries have accused Iran of supplying Russia with Shahed drones and short-range missiles for use in the war. Russia, meanwhile, has been accused of providing targeting data to Iran for strikes on US interests in the Middle East.
Putin and Pezeshkian arrived in Turkmenistan on Thursday for the CIS summit. The two presidents last met on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Kyrgyzstan in September.

title: Trump rules out Iran attack before midterms
description: Trump rules out Iran attack before midterms
content:
President says Washington and Tehran are holding 'productive' talks
US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the United States would not attack Iran before the November 3 midterm elections,
saying Washington and Tehran were engaged in "productive" discussions aimed at ending the six-month-old war.
"We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "We will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd."
Trump's announcement came as the Treasury Department unveiled fresh ?Iran-related sanctions, targeting dozens of ?people, entities and vessels, on its website.
The war began in February when the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran. The conflict has contributed to higher gasoline prices and weighed on Trump's domestic approval ratings, while Republicans seek to preserve their narrow majorities in Congress.
About 60% of Americans, including one in four Republicans, disapprove of Trump's handling of the Iran situation, according to a recent Reuters/Ipsos poll. Voters have identified the cost of living as their top concern, while the conflict has pushed gasoline prices sharply higher.
Trump has repeatedly said he expects oil prices to fall after the elections but has not offered a detailed plan for ending the war. Washington and Tehran have exchanged proposals in recent weeks aimed at ending the conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global shipping route. Trump rejected Iran's latest offer.
Iranian state media reported on Thursday that Tehran would not abandon uranium enrichment or surrender its uranium stockpile. The comments, attributed to the head of Iran's Atomic Energy Organization, came days after US Vice President JD Vance told Reuters that Iran must make "meaningful" reductions in its enrichment capacity.
Meanwhile, Trump used Truth Social to intensify another dispute, this time over terminology surrounding artificial intelligence. Trump said anyone who continues to use the term "Artificial Intelligence" instead of his preferred phrase, "Super Intelligence", would be regarded by the White House as "THE ENEMY".
"The White House considers anyone that uses the term, 'Artificial Intelligence,' as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, 'Super Intelligence,' THE ENEMY!" Trump wrote, without explaining what consequences would follow.
Trump first proposed replacing the term artificial intelligence during a speech before the UN General Assembly last month, saying his preferred expression "sounds much better". In late September, he signed an executive order requiring the term "super intelligence" to be used across the US government.
The requirement does not extend to the private sector, although some companies and technology figures have begun adopting the terminology. Meta, led by Trump ally Mark Zuckerberg, has used the phrase, while Elon Musk has also employed it in posts on X.
The terminology debate comes as Trump continues to promote AI while concerns grow over AI security and opposition to the expansion of data centres in the United States. Trump has also embraced
renaming places, referring to the Gulf of Mexico as the "Gulf of America" and Lake Ontario as "Lake America".

title: Canadian poet Anne Carson wins Nobel Literature Prize
description: Canadian poet Anne Carson wins Nobel Literature Prize
content:
Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson, whose unconventional work blends poetry, prose, dialogue and translation, won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature on Thursday for what the Swedish Academy described as her "bold and inventive oeuvre".
The 76-year-old laureate, born in Toronto and now an Icelandic citizen, was in Iceland when she received the news. Asked how she felt about winning, she told Icelandic broadcaster RUV: "Crazy, I think they're all crazy." She added: "I'll get a sticker on the front of my book."
The prize, awarded by the Swedish Academy, is worth 12 million Swedish kronor ($1.2 million). The academy praised Carson for creating new forms of contemporary literature through a playful dialogue with classical traditions.
Widely recognised for her translations of classical Greek literature, Carson has written across genres, from literary criticism and opera libretti to verse novels. Her 1998 work 'Autobiography of Red', often regarded as her finest achievement, reimagines classical literature to explore love, desire and destruction.
Her 2019 performance piece 'Norma Jeane Baker of Troy' combines the story of Helen of Troy from Euripides' play 'Helen' with the life of Marilyn Monroe, reflecting her distinctive approach to literary traditions.

The Labor Department said it would not accept new or process pending permanent labour certification, or PERM, applications involving Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini.
PERM certification is required for most employment-based green cards and requires employers to demonstrate that hiring a foreign worker would not adversely affect US workers' wages or job opportunities.
"There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused the system more than Microsoft," Vice President JD Vance said. He accused the company of laying off 6,000 American workers last year while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards.

Microsoft said about 80% of the H-1B applications it filed in the last fiscal year were to extend or change the status of existing employees rather than hire new workers. The company also said it pays H-1B employees the same as other workers doing comparable jobs.

title: 1 2b loan accord reached with IMF
description: 1 2b loan accord reached with IMF
content:
Staff-level agreement subject to approval by executive board
Pakistan and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Thursday reached a Staff-Level Agreement (SLA) on the fourth review of the 37-month Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the third review of the 28-month Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF), paving the way for Pakistan to access about $1.2 billion from the Fund's resources.
The staff-level agreement is subject to approval by the IMF Executive Board and upon approval, Pakistan will have access to about $1.0 billion (SDR 760 million) under the EFF and about $210 million (SDR 154 million) under the RSF, bringing total disbursements under the two arrangements to about $5.7 billion.
The International Monetary Fund said that Pakistan should promptly phase out fuel subsidy scheme, as the number of people, who have been adversely affected by a prolonged period of fiscal adjustments, crossed 10 million and so far availed around Rs10 billion in compensations.
The global lender made its first public remarks about the government's scheme to give Rs100 per liter compensation on 20 liters of petrol used by motorcyclists and 30 liters per month by up to 800 cc car owners after the successful conclusion of review talks.
"The fuel support scheme should be phased out promptly, given its high cost and broad targeting," said Iva Petrova, the Mission Chief of the IMF.
Miss Petrova said that any future fuel supportshould oil prices surprise on the upsideshould be limited, time-bound, targeted using established social assistance programmes, and accommodated within the fiscal year 2026-27 budget envelope.
The finance ministry officially did not comment about the actual timing of phasing out the scheme but a senior official commented that there was an understanding that the scheme would continue till the approved Rs75 billion was fully exhausted.
The government had launched the nation-wise scheme on September 18 and approved Rs75 billion allocations for the fuel scheme for a period of three months, at an average of Rs25 billion per month.
According to the government officials, so far over 100 million people have registered themselves for the scheme and 9.7 million of them are motorbike owners. They said that the over Rs10 billion cost has been incurred so far and the actual fiscal impact of the scheme would be known after the end of the first month.
Initially there was a slow start of the scheme but due to constant increase in prices by the government coupled with unbearably high taxes, the number of beneficiaries is growing rapidly. A senior government functionary said that if the international prices remain high the government should think about extending the compensation to high speed diesel instead of ending it under the IMF pressure.
The Express Tribune had reported that the IMF objected to untargeted subsidy and its high cost.
According to an alarming report by the World Bank, 48% of the poor of Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan (MINAAP) region live in Pakistan. It said that the poverty rate in Pakistan increased because of prolonged period of fiscal adjustments and floods.
The IMF said that Pakistan has successfully navigated the impact of the Middle East conflict, and strong policies have helped preserve macroeconomic stability.
Iva said that "nevertheless, risks remain high, particularly from geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices, tighter global financial conditions, and trade disruptions", said the IMF.
Pakistan has accepted the IMF's condition to amend three laws, the National Telecommunication Corporation Act, the National Bank of Pakistan Act and the Pakistan Railways Act before the approval of the loan tranche.
It added that the staff-level agreement is subject to approval by the IMF Executive Board. Upon approval, Pakistan will have access to about $1 billion under the EFF and about $210 million under the RSF, bringing total disbursements under the two arrangements to about $5.7 billion.
Petrova further said that Pakistan remained "committed to increasing health and education spending further to 2.8% of GDP in FY27, closely monitoring implementation, and reallocating resources as needed to meet this objective".
The 2.8% of GDP target is now lower than nearly 3% or Rs4.24 trillion given by the IMF earlier, as the four provinces had allocated less resources in their budgets compared to the target agreed with the IMF.
Iva said that the Pakistani authorities had arrested the long-term decline in health and education spending, raising it from 2.2% of GDP in fiscal year 2023-24 to 2.5% of GDP in FY26.
Finance Secretary Imdad Ullah Bosal said that Pakistan met the fiscal year 2025-26 IMF condition on health and education spending.
It said that the Pakistani authorities remain committed to sound macroeconomic policies, which are critical to safeguarding stability amidst the ongoing shock-prone environment. The authorities' policy priorities include:
The IMF emphasized that the SBP should maintain an appropriate monetary stance and exchange rate flexibility. "The SBP should continue maintaining an appropriately tight policy stance to ensure inflation returns durably to the SBP's target range".
It added that the exchange rate flexibility should continue to serve as an important shock absorber, while further reserve accumulation, gradual liberalization of the foreign exchange regime, and deeper domestic financial markets will strengthen resilience and support private sector development.
The IMF has again stressed that timely tariff adjustments and cost-reducing reforms remain essential to prevent renewed circular debt accumulation while protecting vulnerable consumers. Priorities include improving sector efficiency, advancing private participation in distribution, deepening electricity market competition, maintaining gas sector cost recovery, and reducing unaccounted-for gas losses.

title: Houthis aim to shut KSA s airspace  oil facilities
description: Houthis aim to shut KSA s airspace  oil facilities
content:
Plane damaged at Riyadh airport as Iran-aligned group escalates attacks
Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis escalated their campaign of strikes against Saudi Arabia on Thursday, trying to shut down the kingdom's airspace and oil facilities with missile fire that has killed three people this week and left a plane badly damaged.
The group said it had struck Riyadh airport and warned workers to stay away from energy plants, which would be targeted.
Shrapnel from an interception or another projectile hit had left the commercial plane belonging to Saudi state carrier Saudia Airlines heavily damaged after catching fire while parked at an airport terminal on Thursday, three people briefed on the matter said.
They said no passengers were believed to have been on the plane at the time but they could not rule out any injuries as a result of the incident. A thick black column of smoke and flames were shown rising from Riyadh airport in video verified by Reuters.
Saudi Arabia's government media office, its civil aviation authority and Saudia Airlines did not respond to emailed requests for comment.
Lufthansa and Air India said they were suspending flights to Riyadh after Houthi attacks.
Separately, Saudi officials said debris from an intercepted missile had hit a kindergarten and medical complex in Riyadh.
The Houthis say they are targeting the kingdom over its support for government forces in Yemen's reignited civil war. Saudi Arabia says it is backing an offensive by Yemen's UN-recognised government to take back territory from the Houthis.
The conflict, now an overspill of the US-Iran war, has added new chaos to a region already aflame, and threatens to draw other states into gruelling mountain fighting, with Syria now considering deploying troops to assist Saudi Arabia.
The kingdom has pushed for support from allied nations, including Turkey and Pakistan, even if only in a logistical or defensive capacity, as it tries to reverse Houthi gains in southwest Yemen, by the southern entrance to the Red Sea.
Those requests have taken on more urgency since Saudi authorities said on Wednesday that three people had been killed this week in strikes on Riyadh airport and Abha airport in the southwest.
The Houthis have made Saudi airports a focus of their strikes, and the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen said it had destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the group towards Riyadh and another towards Khamis Mushayt, home to a major airbase.
According to data compiled by aviation analytics company Cirium, almost half of departures from Riyadh airport had been cancelled by 1500 GMT, with 31 more cancellations expected for Friday in all Saudi airports.
Flight tracker FlightRadar24 indicated numerous delayed arrivals and departures at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Thursday. The airport advised travellers to contact airlines to check the status of flights before trying to travel.
Riyadh is due to host a major meeting of energy policy makers, the WPC Energy Congress, this week.
Several multinational firms based in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD) told staff to work from home after loud booms were heard on Thursday morning, five people familiar with the matter said, including some affected staff.
The Saudi government did not respond to a request for comment, and KAFD was not immediately available for comment.
Some diplomats said they had received warnings, and some schools in Riyadh told parents there were orders to shelter in place, though authorities did not issue a public alert. Reuters could not identify the source of the booms.
Yemen's long-running civil war, which paused with a ceasefire in 2022, has erupted again in recent weeks with the Houthis seizing stretches of the Red Sea coast last month, including along the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Their threats to shipping and attacks on Saudi cities and infrastructure have drawn the kingdom back in. This week, Saudi-backed forces launched a counterattack, taking back some areas around the strait.
However, in a war with several front lines, the Houthis have made gains of their own, surrounding Yemen's third-largest city, Taiz, by taking territory along its main mountain road to Aden.
The fighting, which pits the Houthis against a coalition of Saudi-backed forces under the internationally recognised government, has led to a humanitarian crisis in the poorest Arab state, displacing 200,000 people since the conflict resumed.
One US and one Syrian defence official said Syria was carefully considering options for military support, including defensive aid to protect Saudi Arabia from attacks, or an offensive deployment to help take the fight to the Houthis.
In response to a request for comment to the Syrian foreign ministry, a diplomat said Syria stood firmly with Saudi Arabia but that its focus was on domestic priorities such as recovery from its own civil war.
NATO-member Turkey said on Wednesday it was sending mainly defensive and technical support to the kingdom to help in the fight against the Houthis. A Turkish official said this was expected to take the form of military equipment, intelligence sharing and weapons systems.

title: Pakistan denies PAF jets striking Houthis
description: Pakistan denies PAF jets striking Houthis
content:
Ministry describes NYT report as 'fake, fabricated'
Pakistan on Thursday rejected an American media report claiming that Pakistan Air Force (PAF) aircraft were being used against Houthi targets, describing the report as "fake and fabricated" as Islamabad sought to draw a distinction between its emerging military commitments under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and direct participation in offensive operations in Yemen.
The denial came amid growing international scrutiny of Pakistan's role in the Saudi-Houthi conflict following the activation of the trilateral defence pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.
The New York Times, in a report published on October 7 under the headline "Explosions Heard in Riyadh After Saudis Say Houthi Attacks Killed 3 in Kingdom," reported, citing an unnamed senior Pakistani military official, that PAF fighter jets were being used against the Houthis.
The report further suggested, according to accounts of the NYT story, that Pakistan's role could focus on countering Houthi drone and missile threats through air support rather than a ground offensive in Yemen.
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, however, rejected the specific claim regarding the PAF.
"NYT's story attributing employment of PAF aircraft against Houthis is fake and fabricated," the ministry said in a fact-check.
It also urged international media organisations to avoid "speculative reporting" about the employment of Pakistan's military forces under the Makkah agreement.
"Details of any employment, if necessary will be given by concerned authorities," the ministry said.
The clarification is significant because it comes only a day after the Pakistani military itself publicly confirmed that its personnel were already present in Saudi Arabia.
In an interview with CNN, Director General Inter-Services Public Relations Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry confirmed that Pakistani forces were in the Kingdom, saying they had been there "for decades" and operated in "multiple capabilities and domains".
He did not, however, disclose the number of personnel currently deployed in Saudi Arabia, their specific capabilities or whether additional forces could be sent under the Makkah pact. He also did not confirm any Pakistani participation in operations inside Yemen.
The CNN interview has nevertheless added a new dimension to Pakistan's position.
Islamabad has consistently described the Makkah agreement as defensive. But following the emergency meeting of the alliance's Strategic Political and Defence Committee in Riyadh on October 5, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agreed to move towards the rapid deployment of agreed military forces and capabilities in the Kingdom.
The three countries did not announce troop numbers, deployment schedules or the precise nature of the forces involved.
The Pakistani government has also stressed that any military employment would be carried out under agreed arrangements and in accordance with national laws.
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan provided a similar clarification on Thursday, saying Ankara was assessing how it could assist Saudi Arabia, particularly in areas such as air defence.
But he ruled out an offensive Turkish role.
"This is a defence agreement. This is not an offensive agreement," Fidan said at a joint press conference in Ankara. He added that Turkiye would not send troops into another country to launch an attack.
His remarks are likely to reinforce Islamabad's own effort to establish a clear distinction between defending Saudi territory and conducting offensive operations against the Houthis inside Yemen.
The distinction has become increasingly important as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have intensified, including strikes and attempted strikes involving missiles and drones targeting airports and other infrastructure.
For Pakistan, the immediate challenge is therefore to honour the collective-defence commitment without being drawn into a wider war in Yemen.
The Makkah agreement states that an armed attack against one member would be treated as an attack against all three. Yet the pact does not automatically mean that Pakistani forces will participate in offensive operations beyond Saudi territory.

title: Fazl's 'mediation offer' fuels political frenzy | The Express Tribune
description: JUI-F chief offers help break govt-PTI deadlock, Govt team briefs PM on conciliatory role
content:
JUI-F chief offers help break govt-PTI deadlock, Govt team briefs PM on conciliatory role
A possible new channel for ending the political deadlock between the government and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) appeared on Thursday as the government said Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman was willing to help revive dialogue, while opposition leaders made any negotiations conditional on a meeting with PTI founder Imran Khan.
The government's negotiating committee submitted Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif a report on its meeting with the Maulana, conveying that the JUI-F chief was prepared to play a conciliatory role in resolving differences between the government and PTI.
Government sources said Fazl had also signalled that stalled negotiations between the two sides could be resumed.
According to the sources, Fazl advised the government to pursue a settlement through understanding and dialogue instead of moving towards governor's rule or imposing an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
The committee also briefed the prime minister on the conditions Fazl had proposed for taking on a mediatory role and conveyed a special message from him.
A telephone conversation between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Fazlur Rehman is expected soon, sources said. The government delegation that met the JUI-F chief comprised National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq, Prime Minister's Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah and Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry.
However, the reported mediation bid was disputed by Tehreek-e-Tahafuz Aain-e-Pakistan (TTAP) spokesperson Akhundzada Hussain, who said the reports about Fazlur Rehman entering the process as a mediator were "a story spun by the government or pro-government media house".
He also denied any contact with the JUI-F chief beyond a previous meeting with him.
Speaking to The Express Tribune against the backdrop of reports that the meeting between Fazl and the government delegation had agreed to restart the mediation process with PTI through the JUI-F chief, Akhundzada said no such development had been communicated to either PTI or TTAP up to late Thursday.
Reports had also suggested that Fazl had conveyed conditions to the government for entering the process and that PTI had subsequently held an internal meeting to determine its position on the message.
Akhundzada said Barrister Gohar, Junaid Akbar and Asad Qaiser had all denied being approached by Fazlur Rehman or holding an internal meeting on the matter. Barrister Gohar, however, had expressed hope that Fazl could play a positive role in negotiations.
He said PTI and TTAP had met Fazl only to discuss the proposed All Parties Conference (APC) and its agenda.
Meanwhile, PTI MNA Junaid Akbar said the party has kept the door open to Fazl playing a role in breaking the deadlock between the government and opposition.
Speaking on a private news channel on Thursday evening, Akbar said Fazl had been in contact with the PTI leadership and had expressed a desire to help end the stalemate, subject to the party's agreement.
"We are political people, and we understand that the issue can be solved with dialogue," he added, emphasising that "the intention of this should be dialogue" rather than an attempt to trap the PTI.
Meanwhile, National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas held a telephone conversation to discuss the negotiations and the APC.
According to sources, Achakzai contacted Raja Nasir Abbas from Quetta, and the two consulted each other on the strategy for negotiations as well as the proposed APC.
The two opposition leaders agreed to make talks with the government conditional on a meeting with Imran Khan, sources said.
The political developments unfolded as PTI's long march entered another phase in Peshawar, where mobile and cellular internet services had remained suspended across several areas of the provincial capital for two days, disrupting routine life as well as business and office activities.
A post on the PTI's official X account said the convoy had arrived at the toll plaza and shared pictures of hundreds of supporters gathered to welcome the K-P chief minister.
"God-willing, by the time it reaches Swabi, this caravan will become the largest long march in Pakistan's history," the PTI asserted.
Addressing supporters at the toll plaza, Afridi urged them to remain determined in their "struggle for true freedom".
Sources said mobile services were likely to be restored only after the long march moved towards Charsadda.

title: Pakistan  Bahrain push for stronger economic ties
description: Pakistan  Bahrain push for stronger economic ties
content:
Pakistan, Bahrain push for stronger economic ties
Pakistan and Bahrain on Thursday agreed to strengthen bilateral cooperation in multiple areas, including trade, investment, industries, agriculture and food security, higher education, information technology, logistics and maritime affairs, besides committing to finalise the Free Trade Agreement with the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC).
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and Bahraini Foreign Minister Dr Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani on Thursday signed the protocol recording the Minutes of the 3rd Session of the PakistanBahrain Joint Ministerial Commission here at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Both the sides agreed to establish a Joint Working Group on Trade and Investment at the government level as an institutional mechanism for regular consultations, coordination and cooperation on bilateral trade and investment, a DPM's Office news release said.
The minutes record understandings on cooperation in trade and investment, agriculture and food security, oil, gas and minerals, maritime affairs, information technology and telecommunications, health, education and labour, among other areas.
The bilateral ties and cooperation were discussed as Pakistan and Bahrain held the 3rd Joint Ministerial Commission, co-chaired by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and visiting Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani.
Following the ministerial commission's meeting, both leaders told the media at a joint press stakeout that two sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation across a broad spectrum of sectors, including energy, sports, tourism, and business-to-business dealings, besides achieving the target of doubling trade in three years.
Dar said the two countries signed the protocol of the third session of the 3rd Joint Ministerial Commission and committed to holding the 4th ministerial commission's meeting within a year.
He said that the key outcome of the "very comprehensive and productive" meeting was the strengthening of the institutional framework through the operationalisation of several joint working groups for regular engagement and effective implementation of the decisions.
He said both sides welcomed the closer engagement between the business communities of the two countries, and acknowledged the contribution of the Pakistani community in Bahrain, serving as a strong bridge between the two countries.
Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in labour mobility, vocational training and human resource development, with a view to creating new opportunities for skilled Pakistani professionals and workers.
The deputy prime minister told the media that the two sides also exchanged views on the evolving situation in the Gulf and emphasised the importance of restraint, de-escalation, dialogue and diplomacy, besides discussing the need to ensure the safety and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab-ul-Mandeb.
Two sides also stressed the urgent need for unhindered humanitarian assistance to the people of Gaza and reiterated their support for a just and lasting solution in accordance with the relevant UN resolutions.
Discussing the Indus Waters Treaty, Dar highlighted that India's unilateral decision to place the treaty in abeyance constituted a breach of international law and represented a dangerous attempt to weaponise shared water resources and jeopardise the water, food and energy security of Pakistan's 250 million people.
On Afghanistan, Dar underscored the need to ensure that foreign territory is not used against Pakistan.
In his remarks, the Bahraini foreign minister said next week, on 14th of October, both countries would mark 55 years of diplomatic relations, bonds of brotherhood, trust, and solidarity, that have gained fresh momentum with the official visits to Bahrain by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in November 2025 and President Asif Ali Zardari in January 2026.
He appreciated Pakistan's principled positions during ongoing crises, including its support for Security Council resolutions and for its efforts alongside other partners to facilitate dialogue and de-escalation, including by hosting talks between the United States and Iran.
He reaffirmed Bahrain's strong condemnation of the terrorist attacks on Abha International and King Khaled International Airports, and of the Houthi terrorist militia's attacks on civilians and civilian facilities in Saudi Arabia, particularly the assault on Makkah al-Mukarrama and al-Madinah al-Munawwarah.
Foreign Minister Al Zayani said that his visit reaffirmed the strategic nature of bilateral relations, as both sides were determined to work on the outcomes of JMC for the peace, stability, and prosperity of the two countries, the region, and beyond.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday expressed satisfaction over the positive trajectory of bilateral relations and underscored Pakistan's commitment to further strengthening cooperation with Bahrain in diverse fields, including trade, investment, energy, and human resource development.
Foreign Minister Al Zayani conveyed the greetings and good wishes of the leadership of Bahrain to the Prime Minister and reaffirmed Bahrain's commitment to further enhancing bilateral cooperation across mutually beneficial areas.
The prime minister expressed confidence that the 3rd Session of the Pakistan-Bahrain Joint Ministerial Commission would provide further impetus to bilateral cooperation and contribute to deepening the multifaceted relationship between the two countries.
Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of Bahrain Dr. Abdullatif Bin Rashid Al Zayani called on Chief of Army Staff (COAS) and Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir at General Headquarters on Thursday.
During the meeting, matters of mutual interest, regional security situation and bilateral defence and security were discussed, said a news release issued by Inter Services Public Relations (ISPR).
The COAS underscored the longstanding fraternal relations between Pakistan and Bahrain, rooted in shared values and mutual respect.
He reiterated Pakistan's commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation, particularly in the defence and security domains.
The visiting dignitary appreciated the professionalism and operational preparedness of Pakistan Armed Forces, reiterated resolve further enhance bilateral cooperation and acknowledged Pakistan's contributions towards regional peace and stability.
President Asif Ali Zardari on Thursday said Pakistan attaches great importance to its relations with Bahrain and expressed the desire to further strengthen bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade, investment, economic engagement and security.
The president said this during his meeting with the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of Bahrain Dr. Abdullatif bin Rashid Al-Zayani, who called on him at Aiwan-e-Sadr, a Presidency's news release said.

title: Intel reports on postings face scrutiny
description: Intel reports on postings face scrutiny

IHC questions legal status of findings on foreign assignments
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Thursday questioned the legal status of intelligence reports used in the selection of government officials for postings as trade and counsellor officers at Pakistani missions abroad.
A division bench comprising Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro and Justice Umair Majid Malik heard the federal government's intra-court appeal against a single-bench judgment in favour of officials who had challenged their rejection on security clearance grounds.
During the hearing, Justice Soomro questioned whether intelligence reports could be examined in a judicial order.
Additional Attorney General (AAG) Rashid Hafeez submitted that such appointments were at the discretion of the prime minister and the government.
Justice Soomro questioned whether the court could not intervene where the constitutional distribution of powers was concerned. He also asked whether an officer who was not cleared for posting abroad could be considered fit to serve in Pakistan.
The AAG argued that security clearance was mandatory for government officials being posted abroad. He said the officials were currently serving in Pakistan, but their posting abroad involved a security clearance issue.
He submitted that if an official committed an act within Pakistan, it would have an individual impact, whereas any act committed abroad could have implications for the entire country. He maintained that the petitions filed by the officials were not maintainable before the high court.
Representing the affected officials, Advocate Saad Butt argued that the candidates had been shortlisted after tests and interviews by a high-level grade-22 committee. He said they were subsequently trained and even issued diplomatic passports before being rejected on the basis of intelligence reports.
He said the affected officials were senior civil servants holding important positions, had good ACRs and had received awards, adding that there were no allegations, corruption cases or inquiries pending against them.
The AAG argued that service matters of the officials fell under Section 10 of the Civil Servants Act and could be taken before the service tribunal and other relevant forums. He contended that writ petitions in such matters were not maintainable before the high court.
He reiterated that security clearance was necessary for officials being posted abroad.
The court directed counsel for the other affected officials to present their arguments at the next hearing and also said the AAG would be heard.

title: NEPRA raises power tariff by Rs1 11
description: NEPRA raises power tariff by Rs1 11
content:
August FCA to add Rs19b burden for consumers
Electricity consumers have been hit with an increase of Rs1.11 per unit as the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA) on Thursday issued a notification to raise the power tariff for one month under the August fuel cost adjustment (FCA).
According to the notification, the increase will be recovered from consumers across the country, including Karachi, through their October electricity bills.
The August FCA would place an additional burden of Rs19 billion on electricity consumers.
NEPRA has formally notified the increase, which is applicable for one month only under the August FCA.
The higher additional fuel cost in August stemmed from expensive RLNG imports from the spot market, as contracted supplies from Qatar remained under force majeure, besides higher coal imports and lower-than-estimated availability of cheaper hydropower and nuclear generation.
Hydropower was originally targeted to account for about 41 per cent of total power generation, but its share was slightly below 38pc, while the share of nuclear power was estimated at 16.4pc but turned out to be 10pc due to an outage at the Karachi's nuclear power plants.
As a consequence, the share of imported coal-based generation increased to 15.6pc, instead of 7.4pc as originally planned.
Hydropower has no fuel cost, while the average nuclear fuel cost increased to Rs3.15 per unit due to lower utilisation, instead of Rs2.5 per unit. In contrast, the cost of imported coal-based generation came to Rs17 per unit. The cost of local coal-based generation was reported at Rs5.5 per unit.
The cost of RLNG-based generation was reported at Rs45.93 per unit, even higher than the Rs45.25 per unit cost of furnace oil-based power generation, which also includes a petroleum levy of Rs73,000 per tonne.
The FCA is reviewed every month under the tariff regime applicable across the country and is usually applicable to consumers' bills for one month only.

title: PM orders ministries to push digitisation
description: PM orders ministries to push digitisation
content:
Shehbaz stresses national-level central data centre
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday directed all federal ministries to complete, within the stipulated time frame, necessary measures for digitizing relevant data in coordination with provincial governments and the institutions concerned and ensuring its provision to the central data centre.
Chairing a progress review meeting on implementation of Digital Nation Pakistan initiative, the prime minister said that the national-level central data centre under the Digital Nation Pakistan Programme would play a key role in the delivery of government services and provision of facilities to citizens.
He said clearly defined responsibilities of federal ministries, along with the provision of relevant data to the central data centre, would help bring the government system in line with modern requirements.
The prime minister said the Digital Nation Pakistan Programme was essentially aimed at ensuring efficient and convenient services for citizens at the national level.
He observed that making useful data from all sectors and government institutions available at one place could contribute significantly to the country's economic development.
Referring to the fuel subsidy scheme for deserving segments of society, the prime minister said data sharing among institutions had played a key role in its successful implementation.
He said digitization of the performance of ministries and relevant data was important for preventing corruption and institutional mismanagement.
The prime minister appreciated the Ministry of Health for taking commendable steps, in collaboration with provincial governments, towards establishing universal medical records at the national level.
He also appreciated the implementation of QR codes to ensure the availability and verification of quality medicines across the country.
The Ministry of Information Technology briefed the meeting that, with the active cooperation of all relevant ministries, comprehensive measures were being taken for sector-specific digitization.
The meeting was informed that, keeping in view public convenience, the digitization process in basic service sectors, particularly health, agriculture and other ministries, was being completed on a priority basis.
The Ministry of Information Technology, in collaboration with the Ministry of Law, was also taking special and effective measures to make relevant national laws available at one place, which would provide better guidance for future legislation.
The meeting was further informed that, in accordance with the prime minister's directives, work was underway on the digitisation of priority sectors, with special measures being taken to achieve the objectives of digital government services, a digital economy and digital public facilitation.
Different federal ministries briefed the meeting on their public services, performance and progress in providing relevant data to the central data centre.
A special briefing was also given on the provision of data related to the Ministry of National Health Services to the central data centre and the use of digitization for verification of the quality of medicines.

title: Govt contests World Bank poverty report
description: Govt contests World Bank poverty report
content:
WTO names Pakistan among nations gaining from disruptions amid ME conflict
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb's economic adviser Khurram Schehzad has termed misleading a World Bank report suggesting that Pakistan accounts for 48% of the extremely poor population in the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan (MENAAP) region.
According to the report, Pakistan's share of people living on less than $3 a day stands at 48% of the region's extremely poor population, while the country's poverty rate increased by 6.4 percentage points between 2018-19 and 2024-25.
In a post on X titled "Economic Experts' Analysis, World Bank's New Classification and Poverty Numbers," Schehzad said the recent increase in poverty in Pakistan was part of a broader global trend.
He said countries including Lebanon, Argentina, Syria, Iran and Brazil had experienced poverty increases that were "far greater and more severe" than Pakistan's.
Meanwhile, the World Trade Organisation on Thursday sharply raised its global trade growth forecast for 2026 - with merchandise trade riding the AI boom - and concluded that some nations, including Pakistan, were actually benefiting from trade disruptions amid the ongoing Middle East conflict in some ways.
In its Global Trade Outlook Update 2026, the Geneva-based global trade watchdog said its economists had upgraded their forecasts for global merchandise trade volume growth to 3.9 per cent for 2026 and 4.1pc for 2027 - up from previous estimates of 1.9pc and 2.6pc, respectively, projected at the start of the US-Iran conflict in March.
The report said that despite the conflict, the global economy had remained resilient, reflecting a stronger-than-expected surge in AI-related capital investment and increased supplies of fuels and fertilisers from countries outside the Middle East.
While several countries faced fuel transport disruptions because of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the redistribution of traffic was creating opportunities for various other economies, it said.
"For example, Pakistan's exports of sea freight transport services rose by 73pc year-on-year in the first half of 2026, as its transport operators benefited from increased traffic," the WTO said.
Vessel calls at major container terminals in Karachi were still 14pc higher year-on-year in July, it added.

title: Ahsan Bhoon s degree verified  says PBC

content:
The Pakistan Bar Council (PBC) on Thursday declared the degrees of its elected members, including prominent lawyer Ahsan Bhoon, genuine, saying their academic credentials had been verified through the relevant institutions before they were formally notified as members of the lawyers' top regulatory body.
In an official statement, the PBC said the returning officers (ROs) for its 2020 and 2025 elections had obtained verification of the degrees of elected candidates from their respective universities before notifying them as members of the council.
"It is, therefore, clarified that the verification of the degrees of the returned candidates, including that of Bhoon, was undertaken through the relevant universities in accordance with the prescribed procedure," the council said.
The council said the RO for the PBC Election-2020, who was also the Attorney General for Pakistan (AGP), had the degrees of the successful candidates verified by their respective universities soon after the elections. The candidates were subsequently notified as PBC members.
The same process was initiated again following the PBC Election-2025, with the AGP once more serving as the returning officer and starting verification of the elected members' degrees.
"Some members whose degrees were already verified in the last elections, their degrees too were sent again for verification to the relevant universities as well as the Higher Education Commission (HEC)," the council maintained.
The clarification comes amid a growing controversy over the academic qualifications of lawyers.
Earlier, former MNA and retired Capt Muhammad Safdar called for the verification of the degrees of prominent lawyers, including Bhoon, who is considered a close associate of Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar.
The controversy has emerged ahead of the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) elections on Oct 29, adding another point of contention to an increasingly charged contest within the legal community.
Bhoon, a former SCBA president, heads the Independent Group, also known as the Asma Jahangir Group, while Safdar has formed his own Quaid-e-Azam MuhammadAli Jinnah Group.

title: FCC sets key PTI cases for hearing
description: Bushra sentence plea  Afridi election challenge fixed
content:
Bushra sentence plea, Afridi election challenge fixed
As the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) prepares for a long march in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has scheduled two cases involving the party for hearing next week.
The FCC has fixed for Oct 15 a petition by PTI lawmaker Sher Afzal Marwat challenging the election of Sohail Afridi as chief minister of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.
The court also fixed for Oct 14 a petition by the wife of PTI founder Imran Khan, Bushra Bibi, seeking suspension of her sentence in the Al-Qadir Trust case.
Both cases will be heard by a two-member bench headed by Justice Aminuddin Khan, with Justice Ali Baqar Najafi also on the bench.
The timing of the fixation of both cases is significant.
Bushra Bibi's counsel, Salman Safdar, argued in her petition before the FCC that she is entitled to suspension of her sentence as a woman with a serious medical condition, citing the first proviso to Section 497(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC).
The Islamabad High Court had earlier disposed of applications by former prime minister Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi seeking suspension of their sentences without deciding the matter on merit.
Bushra Bibi filed the appeal days after the Supreme Court said on July 24 that it could not hear bail applications in pending National Accountability Bureau (NAB) appeals. As a result, pending criminal appeals were transferred to the newly established FCC.
The FCC is expected to issue notices to the respondents on Oct. 14.
Meanwhile, the FCC will hear Sher Afzal Marwat's petition challenging Sohail Afridi's election as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister on Oct. 15.
The court took up Marwat's petition on Sept 14 and issued notices to all respondents, including the Attorney General for Pakistan. No notice was issued to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa advocate general.
The petition, filed under Article 175(E) of the Constitution, seeks a declaration that resignation letters submitted by Ali Amin Gandapur on Oct. 8 and 11, 2025, were made under the alleged unconstitutional direction of a convicted and disqualified person and therefore lacked legal effect.
The petition alleges that the process to replace Gandapur as K-P CM was initiated on the directives of Imran, whom it describes as convicted and constitutionally disqualified under Articles 62 and 63 of the Constitution.
It argues that a person subject to such a disqualification is legally barred from exercising control over state functionaries or issuing binding political directives.

title: 'Whalefall' director hopes survival tale inspires awe of whales | The Express Tribune
description:
'Whalefall' director 
hopes survival tale inspires awe of whales
content:
Film turns its terrifying premise into a story about survival, grief
Director Brian Duffield hopes his new survival thriller 'Whalefall', in which a teenager is swallowed by a sperm whale, will inspire audiences to feel awe rather than fear towards the giant marine mammals that dominate the film.
Speaking to Reuters at the film's London premiere this week, Duffield described the movie as "the opposite of 'Jaws'", saying whale experts had welcomed the project and hoped it would encourage audiences to learn more about the animals.
Based on Daniel Kraus' 2023 novel, 'Whalefall' follows Jay, played by Austin Abrams, who dives off California's Monastery Beach in search of his late father's remains. During the dive, he is swallowed by a sperm whale and must find a way to survive and escape.
Hollywood actor Josh Brolin, who plays Jay's father, said he hoped the film would have a very different impact from Steven Spielberg's shark blockbuster 'Jaws', which famously helped fuel popular fears of sharks. "I hope people want to go home and hug their families and realise that we have a short time here and might as well utilise it the best we can," Brolin said.
Beyond its survival premise, the film explores grief and the complicated relationship between Jay and his father, themes that Brolin said helped draw him to the project. "I sobbed at the end of the book," he said. "Partially because of the father-son relationship, partially because it's truly a hero story."
To bring the story to life, filmmakers constructed large-scale interiors and exteriors representing the whale, using computer-generated imagery mainly to enhance the environments.
"Everyone who worked on this movie said it was the hardest thing they've ever done," Duffield said, adding that even sitting inside the whale set was an "incredibly dangerous stunt" for Abrams, known for his role in the 'Resident Evil' franchise.
Kraus, who co-wrote the screenplay with Duffield, said the idea originated from a viral video showing kayakers apparently ending up inside a whale's mouth. "Immediately, I had what I felt at the time was the best idea I've ever had," Kraus said. "Could someone really be swallowed by a whale?"
After consulting whale experts, Kraus said he was told that, under the right circumstances, a person could theoretically be swallowed by a sperm whale. Asked whether Jay's fate could actually happen to a human, Duffield joked that "a lot of things have to go very badly for you for it to happen".
"But sperm whales are designed to do one thing and one thing only, which is eat giant squid. And so if you're smaller than a giant squid, you can fit down that throat," he said. "Who knows what happens next?"
'Whalefall' will begin its global theatrical rollout on October 14.

Astana event attracts entries from 125 countries
Kazakhstan hosted the Astana AI Film Festival (AAIFF) for the first time, attracting 8,067 entries from 125 countries and becoming the world's largest international competition for AI-generated films, Qazinform News Agency reports.
The AAIFF also crowned winners, with $450,000 Grand Prize going to Latvian filmmaker Nikolay Shestak for 'The First Honest Day'. Kazakhstan's Myrzakhan Zhumakhan won the Best Character category for his comedy in 'It Was Just a Joke'.

Zhumakhan said he enjoys pranks and humor, which inspired him to create the story. Only 25 films were selected from thousands of submissions to reach the final. They were evaluated by an international jury that included former UNESCO Director-General Audrey Azoulay and investor Balaji Srinivasan.
The festival had a total prize and support fund of $2 million. Half was allocated to awards, while the remaining amount will support promising AI teams and the development of film production in Kazakhstan.
The festival took place in Astana on 13 October 2026. Submissions ran from May 25 to September7. All submissions underwent a curated selection process by an independent international jury, the organisers said on the festival's website.
The AAIFF debut in the Kazakh capital marked a major step for AI-generated cinema, bringing international filmmakers together to showcase their work and compete for substantial prizes. The opening ceremony was attended by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, Qazinform reported. The festival seeks to become more than a film competition. According to AAIFF Co-Founder and Creative Director Aizatulla Hussein, the more important question is what AI can do to cinema itself.

title: A life in grace  grit  and quiet defiance
description: A life in grace  grit  and quiet defiance
content:
Eva Marie Saint, Hollywood's graceful enigma, is no more
She was the graceful blonde who delivered two of the most notable film performances of the 1950s - first as the virtuous Edie Doyle in 'On the Waterfront' with Marlon Brando, then as the seductive spy Eve Kendall in 'North by Northwest' opposite Cary Grant. But Eva Marie Saint's story began long before Hollywood came calling, and it continued long after the cameras stopped rolling.
Born on July 4, 1924, in New Jersey, Saint was a product of the famed Actors Studio, Lee Strasberg's "method acting" school in New York. There, she honed the craft that would carry her through a career spanning more than six decades - and a life defined as much by the roles she turned down as the ones she accepted.
Saint's early career was spent in live television productions during the formative years of the medium - a proving ground that demanded precision, nerve, and the ability to perform without a second take. It was during this period that she appeared in a 1953 production of the play 'The Trip to Bountiful' alongside the great silent film actress Lillian Gish, whom Saint would later call her mentor.
That production brought her to the attention of director Elia Kazan, who picked Saint for 'On the Waterfront' over Elizabeth Montgomery. It was a decision that would change the course of her career.
The uncompromising 1954 drama depicts the struggles of dockworkers on New York's rough waterfront. Brando played former boxer Terry Malloy, who runs afoul of a corrupt union but defies the odds to become a hero with the help of Saint's innocent but strong-willed Catholic girl Edie, who sees more good in him than he sees in himself. Saint was 30 at the time but was playing a schoolgirl.
'On the Waterfront' won eight Academy Awards, including best picture, with Kazan named best director, Brando best actor and Saint best supporting actress - an Oscar in her film debut.
Saint was pregnant when she accepted her Oscar in March 1955. She gingerly walked to the stage, kissed the golden statuette and excitedly told the audience, "I may have the baby right here!" Two days after the ceremony, she gave birth to her first child, Darrell Hayden.
If 'On the Waterfront' made her a star, 'North by Northwest' made her an icon. The 1959 Hitchcock thriller was a suspenseful espionage tale of mistaken identity, with Saint portraying a seductive spy opposite Grant's advertising man Roger Thornhill. Famous sequences include a crop-dusting plane pursuing Grant and a frantic chase involving Grant and Saint climbing the colossal US presidential faces carved into Mount Rushmore.
Hitchcock guided Grant and Saint through witty, suggestive dialogue that skirted the edge of what studios would allow at the time. 'North by Northwest' - like 'On the Waterfront' often considered one of the greatest films ever made - received three Oscar nominations but won none.
Saint worked with a remarkable roster of directors and stars throughout her career. Otto Preminger hired her for 'Exodus' (1960) with Paul Newman. Vincente Minnelli directed her in 'The Sandpiper' (1965) with Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton. John Frankenheimer directed her in both 'All Fall Down' (1962) with Warren Beatty and 'Grand Prix' (1966) with James Garner. And Norman Jewison cast her in the Cold War satire 'The Russians Are Coming, The Russians Are Coming' (1966), an Oscar best picture nominee.
In 1951, Saint married veteran TV director Jeffrey Hayden - a marriage that lasted until his death in 2016. They had two children. She starred in about 20 movies but turned down many roles to devote time to her family, a decision that spoke to her priorities in an industry that rarely rewards such choices.
Later in her career, Saint often returned to television work. She won an Emmy Award in 1990 for her performance in the drama 'People Like Us.' She also took movie roles into her 80s, including 'Because of Winn-Dixie' (2005), 'Winter's Tale' (2014) and 'Superman Returns' (2006), a film in which Brando appeared posthumously using 1970s archive footage.
Saint died of natural causes at her home in Los Angeles at the age of 102, a statement from her spokesperson said. She leaves behind a body of work that spans the golden age of television, the height of Hollywood's studio system, and the modern era - a career defined not by volume, but by the quiet, unmistakable power of her presence.

title: Making sense of AI on social media | The Express Tribune
description:
Making sense of 
AI on social media
content:
TikTok launches global learning hub to help users identify and use AI responsibly
TikTok has announced new measures, including expanded artificial intelligence (AI) literacy resources and enhanced systems to detect AI-generated spam, to help users identify, understand, and responsibly engage with AI-generated content.
The measures came with a closer cooperation with the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA). TikTok said the steps were part of its efforts to promote responsible and transparent use of artificial intelligence on the platform.
The company said it was expanding its AI literacy initiatives through new educational resources and an in-app learning hub. The new TikTok AI Hub is now available globally, including in Pakistan. It provides users with guides and practical information on identifying AI-generated content and using AI responsibly.
The hub appears in search results when users search for AI-related terms on TikTok. It offers educational material on how AI-generated content is created and used. TikTok has also developed a new guide with industry partners, including the National Association for Media Literacy Education (NAMLE) and AI expert Henry Ajder.
The platform will also test enhanced systems to identify accounts that mainly post AI-generated spam. The system will focus on content related to issues that could affect public trust or wellbeing. TikTok is also strengthening its AI transparency efforts by joining the C2PA Steering Committee and supporting wider use of content credentials, the company says.
It said expert organisations participating in its AI literacy programme had generated more than 200 million views since its launch in November 2025.These organisations include NoFiltr and the Raspberry Pi Foundation, which produce content aimed at helping users understand and use AI responsibly. TikTok said it had committed more than $4 million to the programme and planned to continue investing in it.
The platform had long prohibited spam and used technology to detect and remove fake accounts. More than 86 million fake accounts were removed during the first three months of this year, it said. TikTok also said more than three billion videos had been labelled as AI-generated using Content Credentials, creator labelling tools and invisible watermarking technology.
The company said the new measures were part of its broader efforts to promote positive uses of AI while giving users greater control over their experience. TikTok is also developing AI-powered creative tools, including Smart Split and AI Outline. It is testing features such as Manage Topics, which allows users to control how much AI-generated content they see.

The story follows Chinese-American Rachel Chu, played by Wu, and her fiancé Nick Young, played by Golding, as they travel to Singapore to meet his family. Rachel soon discovers that Nick comes from an extraordinarily wealthy family, setting off a series of complicated family and social conflicts.
The Crazy Rich Asians TV series was initially developed for HBO Max before moving to HBO. Warner Bros. Television and HBO are co-producing the project.
Lim said the series will serve as a continuation of the story, allowing the creative team to explore the characters across eight episodes. No premiere date has been announced yet.

title: PSX down despite IMF agreement
description: PSX down despite IMF agreement
content:
KSE-100 index sheds 1,138 points after early rally
Pakistan's benchmark KSE-100 index fell over 1,130 points on Thursday despite the country's staff-level agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), as renewed regional tensions added to selling pressure.
The index initially gained around 900 points and climbed to the intra-day high near 169,500 before reversing course, closing at 167,441.91, down 0.68%. Heavyweights including UBL, Fauji Fertiliser and Systems Limited led the decline, while market turnover also dropped sharply to 365.9 million shares from 586.9 million in the previous session. At the close of trading, the KSE-100 index of the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) fell 1,138.50 points, or 0.68%, and settled at 167,441.91.
Arif Habib Limited (AHL) reported that the KSE-100 opened with early strength, climbing to the intra-day high near 169,500 before selling pressure and resistance pushed it lower. The benchmark closed at 167,441.9, down 1,138.5 points, or 0.68%, with market breadth negative as 76 index constituents fell against only 23 gainers. PSO, LOTCHEM and Abbott contributed the largest positive points, while UBL, Fauji Fertiliser and Systems Limited were the main drags. Regular-market turnover fell to 366 million shares.
The report linked the session's tone to two external developments. Pakistan and the IMF reached a staff-level agreement that could unlock roughly another $1.2 billion under the Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility once the executive board approves it, offering potential relief against inflation and the fiscal effects of the Middle East conflict.
Separately, Houthi strikes on two Saudi airports that killed three people and injured dozens reinforced regional risk, while a government comment that Pakistan may hit its 30% electric-vehicle sales target for 2030 earlier than planned as petrol prices encourage switching received only a brief mention. Technically, Arif Habib observed that the index had turned down from its first resistance zone; a further slide through 165,500 would open the path towards 160,000. The accompanying Bloomberg chart and PSX tables showed the day range of roughly 2,000 points and confirmed the close near the session low, consistent with independent reports of profit-taking after the prior day's modest gain.
Topline's market review noted that the KSE-100 index witnessed a volatile session, initially gaining around 906 points following positive sentiment surrounding Pakistan's staff-level agreement with the IMF. However, the early gains failed to sustain as investors resorted to profit-taking at higher levels, resulting in a 1,138-point (-0.68%) decline to close at 167,442. The index traded in a wide range of 167,450-169,487 during the session.
Index-heavy stocks remained under pressure, with UBL, FFC, SYS, EFERT, and POL emerging as the major detractors, collectively shaving 394 points off the KSE-100 index. Despite the decline in the benchmark, market activity remained modest, Topline said. Overall trading volumes were recorded at 365.9 million shares compared with the previous session's tally of 586.9 million. The value of shares traded during the day was Rs17.7 billion.
Shares of 496 companies were traded. Of these, 130 stocks closed higher, 324 fell, and 42 remained unchanged.
K-Electric was the volume leader with trading in 29.7 million shares, losing Rs0.08 to close at Rs5.96. It was followed by Cnergyico Pk with 21.3 million shares, losing Rs0.34 to close at Rs12.39, and Waves Home Appliances with 16.9 million shares, losing Rs0.08 to close at Rs7.77. Foreign investors sold shares worth Rs245 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

title: Meeting airs concern over rising prices
description: Meeting airs concern over rising prices
content:
Minister gives directives for current and previous fare comparison, probe into high DAP prices
Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal chaired a meeting of the National Price Monitoring Committee (NPMC) on Thursday to review the monthly and weekly inflation situation, wholesale-retail price gaps, prices of essential commodities and implementation of previous decisions.
The minister expressed concern over rising prices of essential commodities, particularly wheat flour, and directed provincial and district administrations to strengthen the monitoring of supplies, market arrivals, hoarding, profiteering and unjustified price increases.
The meeting was informed that the Consumer Price Index (CPI)-based inflation stood at 10.3% year-on-year in September 2026, compared to 11.1% in August, while average inflation during July-September FY2026-27 stood at 10.2%. The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) increased 13.3% year-on-year, while the weekly Sensitive Price Indicator (SPI) for the week ended October 1 recorded an 11.53% year-on-year spike. Major annual increases were recorded in onions, LPG, electricity, diesel, petrol and wheat flour, while chicken, garlic, gram pulse and LPG recorded notable weekly increases.
Ahsan Iqbal directed the concerned authorities to compare current transport fares with fares prevailing after the previous fuel price hike to determine whether the increase in fuel prices had resulted in any disproportionate rise in fares. He also told the Ministry of National Food Security and Research to examine why DAP prices remained high in Pakistan despite a decline in international markets, stressing that the benefit of lower international prices should be reflected in the domestic market.
He emphasised that the inspection and quality assessment report regarding ghee, edible oil and milk products be submitted within one week. If the industry had proposed a third-party validation, he said, its cost should be borne by the industry and not the government.
The minister asked provincial governments to closely monitor wholesale and retail prices and take enforcement action where unjustified gaps existed, particularly in major markets including Lahore and Karachi. He also called for close monitoring of supply chains and distribution costs to prevent disproportionate pass-through of fuel price increases to essential food costs.
Ahsan Iqbal directed authorities to strengthen measures against hoarding, profiteering and overcharging and ensure uninterrupted supplies of essential commodities, particularly wheat flour, onions and other perishables. He told Ogra to take effective measures to reduce the gap between notified and prevailing market prices of LPG cylinders.
The minister stressed that price monitoring should focus not only on statistics but also on identifying the causes of price increases, addressing market distortions and ensuring timely enforcement to protect consumers.

title: Direct shipping service to Europe restored
description: Direct shipping service to Europe restored
content:
Dedicated service will cut transit time, logistics costs for exporters
Federal Minister for Maritime Affairs Muhammad Junaid Anwar Chaudhry on Thursday said that direct shipping connectivity between Karachi and major European ports had been restored, providing relief to exporters facing longer transit times and increased freight costs due to disruptions in international shipping routes.
In a statement, the minister said Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC) had reinstated its Premium Ipak service in response to the demand from exporters for a dedicated and direct European service.
Under the restored service, MSC will make a weekly call at Karachi Gateway Terminal Limited (KGTL), connecting Karachi with key European destinations through Colombo, Felixstowe, Rotterdam, Hamburg, Bremerhaven, Antwerp, Le Havre and London Gateway.
"The restoration of a dedicated European service is an important development for our export-oriented industries, particularly the textile sector, which has been facing increased transit times and logistics costs because of disruptions to international shipping routes," the minister said.
He said textile exporters had recently apprised him of the difficulties caused by changes in shipping routes, particularly those linked to the situation in the Red Sea. "Exporters told me recently that longer vessel journeys were increasing transportation costs and delivery times for shipments to European and US markets. These additional costs and delays have affected the competitiveness of exporters," he said.
The minister stressed that the government was taking up concerns of the export sector with shipping lines and other relevant stakeholders to improve maritime connectivity and facilitate international trade.
"Reliable and predictable shipping connectivity is essential for Pakistan's exporters. Our focus is to ensure that the maritime sector supports trade, reduces logistical bottlenecks and strengthens Pakistan's access to international markets," he remarked.
He welcomed MSC's decision to reinstate the Premium Ipak service, saying the weekly Karachi call would provide exporters with a more direct connection to important European markets. "The restored service will improve connectivity with major European ports and provide exporters with greater options for planning and moving their shipments," he said.
The minister, however, noted that the reinstatement of the service should not be viewed as a resolution of the wider challenges affecting international shipping routes. "Disruptions to established shipping routes continue to have implications for global trade. We will continue working with the shipping industry and exporters to address connectivity and logistics issues and to strengthen Pakistan's position in international trade," he said.
The federal minister lauded efforts of Karachi Port Trust (KPT) Chairman Rear Admiral (Retd) Shahid Ahmed and the management of KGTL for restoring the shipping link between Karachi and European markets.
KPT chairman said measures were underway to further improve the efficiency of the maritime logistics system. He said the restored shipping connection would improve access from Karachi to key European markets and facilitate the country's exporters.

title: Poultry sector needs export strategy
description: Poultry sector needs export strategy
content:
Haroon Akhtar says it must expand global footprint for branded products
Adviser to the Prime Minister for Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan has said that Pakistan's poultry industry is playing an important role in ensuring food security, generating employment and promoting economic growth, while also serving as a vital link connecting rural areas with industry, laboratories and markets.
He said that time had come for the poultry industry to move beyond meeting domestic requirements and establish a stronger presence in international markets, for which a comprehensive export strategy was essential. Addressing the International Poultry Expo (IPEX) 2026 at Expo Centre Lahore on Thursday, Khan said Pakistan needed a poultry industry that could produce more efficiently, provide affordable nutrition to the people and compete effectively in international markets.
He said that despite high production costs, disease challenges, energy-related pressures and uncertainty, the poultry industry had continued to invest and maintain production, reflecting its resilience and national importance.
The adviser said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif, the government was working to translate policies into practical outcomes and productive economic activity. He added that increased investment, industrial expansion and creation of employment opportunities were the true measures of success of government initiatives.
He stressed the need to ensure uninterrupted availability of feed and other essential raw materials for the poultry industry. Decisions relating to the import of soybean and other critical inputs should be made against clear requirements and within defined timelines to provide greater certainty to the industry.
Khan said Pakistan needed to expand access to international markets for processed, packaged and branded halal poultry products. Alongside halal certification, he stressed the importance of disease surveillance, internationally recognised processing standards and comprehensive traceability systems.
He said biosecurity was essential not only for protecting poultry farms but also for safeguarding export opportunities, while an efficient cold-chain system was fundamental to maintaining product quality and protecting the reputation of Pakistani brands.
"Pakistani poultry products should be of a standard that encourages international buyers to choose them repeatedly on the basis of quality and competitive value," he said.
The adviser said that a practical export roadmap would be developed in collaboration with the Pakistan Poultry Association, covering priority markets, required approvals, production capacity and clearly defined responsibilities.
Khan said that modern technology, precision feeding, advanced genetics, early disease detection and digital monitoring could significantly enhance the productivity of Pakistan's poultry industry.
He urged international partners to contribute to technology transfer, training and development of local supply chains in Pakistan. He said that greater opportunities should also be created for young people in biotechnology, engineering, food science, entrepreneurship and other areas connected with the poultry industry.
He said a strong partnership between the government and industry was essential for sustainable growth of the productive sector. Clear priorities, defined responsibilities and an effective follow-up mechanism were necessary for resolving industrial issues and ensuring implementation.
"The government's objective is to create a business environment where entrepreneurs can plan for the next decade rather than remain focused on the next crisis," he said.
The adviser said Pakistani youth must be provided opportunities to build their future in productive sectors, including poultry, while partnerships established at IPEX 2026 should translate into sustainable investment and long-term business opportunities.
He said the decisions being taken today would shape Pakistan's industrial and productive capacity in the years ahead.
Khan said Pakistan's path to development lay through promoting quality, competitive and export-oriented production. Pakistani products, he added, should become a source of national recognition in international markets through their quality and excellence.
