title: New pricing system may halt petrol import
description: New pricing system may halt petrol import
content:
In letter to secretary, industry says importing OMCs may not be able to recover actual costs
The oil industry has cautioned the government that the revised petroleum pricing mechanism may force oil marketing companies (OMCs) to halt the import of petrol.
The Oil Companies Advisory Council (OCAC) – an industry lobby – has proposed that the relevant provision be amended to provide that where Pakistan State Oil (PSO) has no motor spirit (MS) import cargo during the preceding seven working days, the premium, incidentals, customs duty and the applicable exchange rate adjustment of PSO's most recent MS import cargo shall be applied instead of the calendar-year-to-date (CYTD) average.
In a letter addressed to Federal Secretary Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division) Hameed Yaqoob Sheikh, the OCAC drew attention to the revised petroleum pricing mechanism approved by the federal government on August 19, 2026. It highlighted a specific issue in the mechanism for MS import pricing, which could result in importing OMCs being unable to recover their actual procurement costs.
Under the approved mechanism, where PSO has no MS import during the preceding rolling seven working days, the CYTD average of premium, incidentals and customs duty is applied.
OCAC said it believed that the CYTD average was not an appropriate proxy for the prevailing import cost. In the absence of a PSO cargo within the seven-working-day window, the pricing should instead be based on the actual premium, incidentals, customs duty and applicable exchange rate for PSO's most recent MS import cargo.
"This would ensure that the administered price reflects the latest actual procurement cost, rather than a historical average which may be materially different from the replacement cost faced by importing OMCs," it said. "The issue is particularly relevant in the current market, where MS import premiums have increased significantly."
In October 2026, PSO has an approximately 10-day gap between its cargoes scheduled for October 13-15 and October 26-28. During this period, the current mechanism could revert to the CYTD average premium of approximately $13/barrel.
However, PSO's own subsequent cargoes are being procured at premiums of $28.47/barrel for late October and $28.76/barrel for early November. Industry cargoes are similarly being procured at premiums substantially above the CYTD average. Consequently, applying the CYTD average during the intervening period could result in an estimated under-recovery of approximately Rs16-17/litre for the importing OMCs.
OCAC, therefore, proposed that the relevant provision be amended to provide that where PSO had no MS import cargo during the preceding rolling seven working days, the premium, incidentals, customs duty and applicable exchange rate adjustment for PSO's most recent MS import cargo shall be applied instead of the CYTD average.
"This approach is straightforward, transparent and directly linked to an actual market transaction, while avoiding significant under-recovery where current international procurement costs have moved materially away from the historical CYTD average," it said.
Pakistan remains structurally dependent on imported petroleum products, with approximately 70% of MS requirements met through imports. "Ensuring that the pricing mechanism adequately reflects actual import costs is, therefore, important not only for the financial sustainability of importing OMCs but also for maintaining uninterrupted petroleum supplies," the council said.
The matter was discussed with the Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division) and Ogra on October 6, where the OCAC was advised to submit its recommendation to the relevant forum for consideration.
The issue, it said, also needed to be viewed against the industry's existing financial pressures, including Rs66.7 billion in outstanding price differential claim (PDC) recoveries, stagnant OMC margins, rising operating costs and increasing compliance requirements. OCAC requested for a meeting and the secretary's intervention to consider the proposed amendment on an urgent basis.

Pakistan and the United Kingdom discussed ways to further enhance trade and cooperation in priority sectors and deliver concrete outcomes through the next bilateral Trade Dialogue, during a meeting between Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan and British High Commissioner Jane Marriott.

content:
Pakistan's foreign exchange reserves held by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) increased by $15 million during the week ended October 2, 2026, reaching $21.454 billion, according to data released by the central bank on Thursday.
The country's total liquid foreign reserves stood at $26.797 billion, compared with $26.771 billion a week earlier. The increase in SBP-held reserves came despite a $17 million decline in the net foreign reserves held by commercial banks, which stood at $5.344 billion during the week under review.
According to the SBP, the country's total liquid foreign reserves comprised $21.454 billion held by the central bank and $5.344 billion held by commercial banks. Furthermore, the Pakistani rupee extended its marginal gains and closed at 277.01 against the US dollar on Thursday, up Rs0.01 from Wednesday's close at 277.02. Meanwhile, gold prices in Pakistan edged higher on Thursday, recovering modestly after a sharp decline in the previous session, as international bullion prices also gained amid uncertainty over the US Federal Reserve's rate outlook and concerns over elevated US debt levels.
According to rates shared by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association, the price of gold increased by Rs600 per tola to Rs435,036. The price of 10-gram gold rose by Rs515 to Rs372,973. On Wednesday, gold had settled at Rs434,436 per tola, after declining by Rs3,100. In the international market, spot gold rose 0.3% to $4,122.36 per ounce by 12:20 pm EDT (1620 GMT), after touching its lowest level since August 5 on Wednesday, as per Reuters. A stronger US dollar and higher Treasury yields had pressured bullion in the previous session, while investors continued to assess the Federal Reserve's future rate path.
Minutes from the Fed's September meeting showed policymakers were divided over the rationale for a rate hike, adding to uncertainty over the timing of future monetary-policy moves. Market participants currently see a 21% probability of an October rate hike, while the probability of a December hike stands at 88%, according to market pricing.
Adnan Agar, Director at Interactive Commodities, described the market as "completely sluggish", saying gold was struggling to establish a clear direction. He said bullion was trading within a relatively narrow range, with the market unable to determine whether the next major move would be upward or downward. Agar said downside pressure remained possible, but a move below the $4,000 level appeared unlikely unless major economic data or unexpected news triggered fresh selling. He expected a clearer trading range to emerge over the coming days as investors receive fresh economic signals. Meanwhile, silver prices in the domestic market declined by Rs120 per tola to Rs6,368.

title: ECC clears only Rs2b for local polls
description: ECC clears only Rs2b for local polls
content:
Holds back Rs16.5b; sanctions Rs300m for PM Office, staff colony refurbishment
The government on Thursday approved Rs18.5 billion for holding local government elections, mainly in Punjab and Islamabad, but authorised the release of only Rs2 billion despite a request from the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) to release all the funds.
The Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) of the cabinet that approved these funds also sanctioned a Rs300 million grant for refurbishment of the Prime Minister's Office and his staff colony at a time when the government has banned purchases under the austerity policy. In total, the ECC approved nearly Rs57 billion worth of supplementary grants in the fourth month of the current fiscal year.
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb chaired the ECC meeting, which, according to a few participants, was held in haste and insufficient time was spent discussing agenda items, particularly the funds for local government elections.
According to a press statement issued by the finance ministry, on a summary submitted by the ECP, the committee approved a grant of Rs596.2 million for local government by-elections in Sindh and Balochistan, and delimitation activities in Punjab.
It added that the ECC also considered a separate ECP summary regarding the allocation of Rs17.8 billion for the procurement of materials for local government elections in Punjab, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, ICT and Cantonment Boards across Pakistan. The committee approved the immediate release of Rs2 billion through a supplementary grant, according to the finance ministry.
However, the ECP demanded that the entire amount should immediately be released, as it needed roughly Rs12 billion for holding local government elections in Punjab in December.
But the ECC chairman decided to give the money in tranches, although the Constitution says the federal government does not have the right to reduce any demand from the ECP. Finance ministry officials were of the view that the ECC did not reduce the demand, and it only decided to give it in tranches that will not impact the spending.
The ECP was of the view that it needed another Rs4 billion next week to hold local government elections. The ECC approved a supplementary grant of Rs300 million for the Capital Development Authority (CDA) to meet essential repair and maintenance expenditure relating to the Prime Minister's Office and Prime Minister's Staff Colony, according to the finance ministry.
The ministry did not state whether the money has been approved in relaxation of the austerity policy that bans any procurements, other than for development purposes.
The ECC approved the imposition of 11% additional customs duty on import of tyres to protect the local industry. It slapped 11% additional customs duty on the import of parts of motorcycles and 31% if the manufacturers import these parts instead of locally producing them.
The ECC approved a summary submitted by the Finance Division regarding a financing framework developed by the State Bank of Pakistan to facilitate the inclusion of Agency Financial Institutions (AFIs) under the government's existing risk coverage schemes for small enterprises and small farmers through wholesale and agency arrangements. The framework aims to broaden access to finance by leveraging the outreach of eligible microfinance and non-banking financial institutions.
The committee also approved a Finance Division summary for an addendum to the Second Supplemental Trust Deed of the Credit Guarantee Trust Fund (CGTF), expanding its scope to facilitate more effective utilisation of the existing credit guarantee facility to support affordable housing finance.
The ECC approved Rs2 billion for the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (Smeda), on a summary submitted by the Industries and Production Division, to facilitate implementation of Smeda's approved Business Plan as per the vision of the prime minister.
The committee further approved Rs11.3 billion, on a summary submitted by the Industries and Production Division, to meet the immediate funding requirements of Utility Stores Corporation (USC) and facilitate completion of its closure process.
On a summary submitted by the Privatisation Division, the ECC approved Rs8 billion for the Public Private Partnership Authority. The allocation will support the development and implementation of infrastructure projects through public-private partnerships, it added.
The ECC approved Rs10 billion for the Ministry of Railways, to provide budgetary cover for the Thar Coal Rail Connectivity Project, facilitating the utilisation of indigenous Thar coal for power generation and other industrial sectors.
The committee approved Rs150 million in favour of the Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination to meet requirements related to Pakistan's participation in the 31st Session of the Conference of Parties (COP31), scheduled to be held in Antalya, Turkiye.
The ECC also approved Rs934.5 million for the Pakistan Sports Endowment Fund Scheme, 2025, in favour of the Ministry of Inter-Provincial Coordination. The allocation will support operationalisation of the Fund in accordance with its approved framework and contribute to the development of the national sports ecosystem.
On a summary submitted by the Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training, the committee approved Rs1.7 billion for the prime minister's initiative for short-term training of 1,000 agricultural professionals in China. The initiative aims to strengthen expertise in agricultural technology, innovation and research.
The committee also considered a summary submitted by the Ministry of National Food Security and Research regarding adjustment of Passco's outstanding receivables from provincial governments through at-source deductions. The matter was deferred, with directions to bring the proposal back after further consultation with the relevant stakeholders.
The committee approved Rs4 billion for Pakistan Revenue Automation (Pvt) Limited (PRAL), on a summary submitted by the Revenue Division, to support ongoing restructuring and implementation of FBR's Transformation Plan.
The ECC approved a summary submitted by the Ministry of Commerce regarding investment of Export Development Fund (EDF) resources in government securities, in accordance with the approved framework, to ensure productive utilisation of the Fund's resources and sustainable financial management.

'Talk to Me' spinoff I Let You In will bring an immersive horror story to Meta Quest headsets and VR glasses
Meta has unveiled the first look at I Let You In , an immersive horror series set in the universe of the 2023 film Talk to Me .
The six-episode series will be available exclusively on Meta Quest headsets and is designed specifically for the company’s virtual reality platform. It will also be available on Meta’s VR glasses, which are scheduled to launch in spring 2027.
Directed by Craig William Macneill, known for Them and The Terror , I Let You In follows a group of young travellers who head to Ibiza in search of the ultimate party. Their experience takes a darker turn when they become addicted to conjuring spirits, described as a supernatural high with deadly consequences.
Trent Atherton wrote the series, with Darren Brandl serving as showrunner. The cast includes Aubri Ibrag, Charlotte Maggi, Sofia Hublitz, Julio Peña, Raff Law and Charlie Hiscock.
The project was commissioned by Meta and produced by XRTV, an immersive studio founded by Brandl and Jack Davis. The series has completed filming in Spain and is currently in post-production.
The original Talk to Me , directed by Danny and Michael Philippou, premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in 2023. The horror film follows teenagers who discover a mysterious embalmed hand that allows them to communicate with spirits. It became a box office success, earning more than $90 million worldwide.
Causeway Films, which produced Talk to Me , is also involved in the new series alongside XRTV and Meta. The company’s credits include The Babadook and The Nightingale .

Hayden Panettiere’s daughter Kaya appeared in court as Wladimir Klitschko gets temporary guardianship of her estate
Hayden Panettiere’s 11-year-old daughter, Kaya, made a rare court appearance with her father, Wladimir Klitschko, during a hearing concerning the late actress’ estate.
Kaya appeared remotely on Thursday, October 8, briefly speaking with the judge to confirm her identity and that she was with Klitschko. The former professional boxer did not appear on camera during the hearing.
The court ultimately granted Klitschko temporary guardianship of Panettiere’s estate, allowing him to begin probate proceedings. Kaya is the sole beneficiary of her mother’s estate.
Klitschko’s attorney, Diane Y. Park, also discussed additional powers being sought, including the ability to request and authorise law enforcement assistance in recovering property that may have been misappropriated by a non-family member.
The judge said Kaya will not need to attend the next hearing, which is scheduled for December 7.
Klitschko and Panettiere began dating in 2008 and became engaged in 2013. They welcomed Kaya in 2014 before ending their relationship in 2018. Klitschko was subsequently granted full custody of their daughter.
Panettiere died suddenly on August 16 at age 36 after being found unresponsive at a residence in Greenville, South Carolina. She was pronounced dead at the scene, and an investigation into her death remains ongoing.
In September, Klitschko filed a temporary guardianship request on behalf of Kaya, citing concerns that property belonging to Panettiere’s estate could be lost or damaged before an administrator was appointed.
Before her death, Panettiere discussed her relationship with Klitschko and their daughter in her May 2026 memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning , including her decision to give him full custody of Kaya.

title: PTI authorises Fazl to mediate between govt  opposition  says Junaid Akbar
description: PTI K P president says party agreed to Fazl   s request to mediate and resolve political issues through dialogue
content:
PTI K-P president says party agreed to Fazl’s request to mediate and resolve political issues through dialogue
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa President Junaid Akbar on Thursday said the party had authorised Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman to play a mediatory role between the government and opposition amid the ongoing political standoff.
Speaking on a private television programme, Dunya Mehar Bukhari Kay Sath , Akbar said he had spoken to Maulana Fazl about the need for opposition parties to work together for the supremacy of the Constitution and democracy.
He clarified, however, that PTI had not invited the JUI-F chief to join the long march, which, he said, was aimed at securing a meeting with PTI founder Imran Khan, his release and hearings of his cases.
Read : Sharjeel Memon accuses K-P CM of 'sabotaging' talks with govt
“Our own desire is that we move forward by taking all political parties along,” he said.
Akbar said Maulana Fazl himself had requested PTI to delay the long march, telling the party that he would return from Umrah on Oct 7 and play the role of mediator in the matter as he wanted the issues to be resolved through dialogue.
He said PTI had always sought to resolve political issues through negotiations, but when it was not heard and given space, taking to the streets remained a constitutional and legal option.
“Our effort has always been to resolve issues through negotiations, but when we are not heard and are not given space, the only legal and constitutional option left for us is to come out on the streets,” Akbar said.
He said Maulana Fazl had so far not conveyed any offer from the government to PTI. According to Akbar, the only communication so far had been that the government had contacted the JUI-F chief and that Maulana Fazl had subsequently asked PTI whether it wanted him to play a role in the matter.
Akbar confirmed that PTI had authorised the JUI-F chief to mediate between the government and opposition over the recent standoff, saying the party had no objection if the government also wanted him to play that role.
Asked about negotiations with the government, Akbar said the two sides had “almost” reached an understanding, but the issue of terrorism — on which he said there should be consensus — had been made controversial.
Also Read : ‘No way back’: Afridi vows to continue PTI long march as convoy reaches Peshawar
He said discussions had been under way about ending the long march and questioned how the issue of military operations and emergency had entered the talks.
“Our impression is that the government does not want the issues to be resolved through dialogue,” he said.
Meanwhile, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja dismissed speculation that the party would resign from parliament or boycott the assembly session if governor’s rule or an emergency was imposed.
Speaking on a private television programme, Capital Talk , Raja said no decision had so far been taken to resign or boycott the parliamentary session. He said the party would decide after consultation at a meeting of its parliamentary party.
Asked about the meeting with Maulana Fazl, Raja said the discussion had covered issues relating to the country’s recent political situation, but categorically denied that the JUI-F chief was playing any mediatory role.

Raja said the constitutional rights of K-P were “under attack” and that Chief Minister Sohail Afridi was fighting for those rights.
“The long march is a political process and our legal and constitutional right. Why should we back down?” he said.
He said major decisions in the national interest could be taken if PTI leadership was allowed to meet incarcerated former prime minister Imran Khan.
Raja said the PTI founder could not be removed from the country’s political arena and maintained that he must be included in any political dialogue.

title: Doctrine of Periphery and Pakistan
description: Doctrine of Periphery and Pakistan
content:
Balkanisation of Somalia has been another project of foreign entities for decades
Since the 1950s, the Doctrine of the Periphery has been a core component of Israel's foreign policy strategy. David Ben-Gurion conceived this doctrine because Israel was surrounded by hostile Arab states and diplomatically isolated in the Middle East. By building alliances with non-Arab states and ethnic minorities along the region's geographic periphery, Israel aimed to exploit divisions among Arab nations.
The periphery included, Iran under the Shah, Turkey under the Republican Party, Ethiopia under Haile Selassie, the Maronites of Lebanon, and the Kurds in Iraq. Iran and Israel built the Eilat-Ashkelon Oil Pipeline in 1968 for Iranian oil to bypass the Suez Canal; strategic ties were established with Turkey and Ethiopia; and Kurdish autonomy was backed by the West to keep Iraq destabilised. At the same time, Israel established contacts with Sudan's anti-Egypt Umma Party. Israel did not want Sudan to be integrated in Egypt under Nasser's pan-Arab project. Later, Israel developed links with the Anya-Nya insurgency in southern Sudan, providing them small arms so that Sudan would eventually break down into two. Supporting non-Arab peripheral minorities in their conflicts with Arab states would tie down the Arab governments in their own security, and the Israel-Palestine issue would be left on the backburner.
The balkanisation of Somalia has been another project of foreign entities for decades. Different clan-heads were provided weapons and funds so that civil war would never end, and the provinces started declaring independence. Israel just took the next step by recognising the sovereignty of Somaliland last year, also asking for a military base there, in return.
This tide was somewhat turned in the 70s with the Iranian Revolution and the overthrow of Haile Selassie. And at the same time Israel's peace treaties with Egypt and Jordan turned Israel towards the 'Peace for Peace' (Abraham Accords) approach. It has always been clear that Israel does not want peace, with its neighbours, or within its neighbourhood.
Fast forward to 2023's China-brokered Iran-Saudi Reproachment; the start of the Gaza War; and the suspension of the Abraham Accords. Add to that the economic and strategic setbacks faced by the US and the West. And to that, the Pakistan-China duo replacing US-NATO as the net security provider in the Middle East, and the US intimations that all their bases in the region will be dismantled. All this has rattled Israel to the spine, forcing it into a hysteria of assaults, encroachments and wars in the neighborhood.
Though conditions in the region are still quite volatile, further reversal of the Doctrine of the Periphery and isolation of Israel in the region is underway, and Pakistan has a lot to do with this.
Somalia has just received a senior delegation from the PAF for purchase of 24 JF7 aircraft worth $990 million. Pakistan Air Force, Navy and Army will train their Somalian counterparts. Once Mogadishu is enabled, the balkanisation of Somalia could potentially reverse.
Pakistan and Ethiopia have discussed strengthening defence and aviation cooperation, and expanded air connectivity. Pakistan has offered to bridge Ethiopia's longtime issue of being landlocked by developing a Pakistan-Djibouti-Ethiopia maritime framework. This way the CPEC/Gwadar track would become more viable, as Chinese goods meant for Africa would have a next stop at Djibouti. Already Gwadar has been included in the International North-South Transport Corridor at Russia's behest, expanding the network. Pakistan will invest in Djibouti's free zones; construct a rice-distribution hub there; expand air connectivity; and use Djibouti as a distribution platform into East Africa and COMESA markets. China has its only foreign military base in Djibouti, meaning that China would be providing cover for all these projects.
Sudan is purchasing air defence systems from the PAF; 10 Karakorum-8 trainers; over 200 drones; Super Mushshak aircrafts; and potentially JF-17 fighters – all this reportedly worth 1.5 billion.
In late 2025, Pakistan finalised a weapons package worth more than $4 billion with the Libyan National Army associated with Khalifa Haftar. This includes 16 JF-17 combat aircraft; 12 Super Mushshak trainers; land, air and naval equipment; military training; defense-manufacturing cooperation. All this while maintaining diplomatic relations with the Tripoli government too.
Then there is the PEACE cable aka Pakistan and East Africa Connecting Europe. Landing stations at Karachi and Gwadar will connect with those in Djibouti, Kenya, Egypt and France via undersea cables. Pakistan's Karachi-to-Marseille section of this cable was completed and made ready for service in 2022. This means that Pakistan will be entering the MENA region as a net-security provider, as more states after Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Egypt want to enter this umbrella, while also creating economic and telecommunication frameworks with them that go deeper into Africa and even Europe. Last month, EU's Ursula von der Leyen met PM Sharif and reviewed the broader Pak-EU relationship, including trade, GSP+, regional security and diplomatic cooperation. Kaja Kallas, European Commission VP, described Pakistan as a major regional power and important EU partner. Statements thanking Pakistan for facilitating the ceasefire have been issued by several European leaders.
If together Pakistan, Iran and China are able to circumspect the possibility to secure both the Straits of Hormuz and Bab al Mandab and bring them into an inclusive, collective regional security architecture, that would prove to be the key to ushering a coming Asian Century. As for the Doctrine of the Periphery, that will be reversed for good, and Israel will be forced to live an isolated, confined life, detached from its ex-allies.
Pakistan can rightly pride itself on being pivotal to the grand strategies being played out regionally and globally. Pakistan's geopolitical stature does not seem to be limited to its traditional allies any more, it has extended throughout the Islamic world, Africa and Europe. If there is anything that will deter Pakistan's progress in near-future and its preferred entry into the Asian Century, it will be its internal political instability and widespread corruption in its political and economic aristocracy. All the external accolades and credits will prove to be a façade, if set on top of crumbling, shifting foundations. It is time for those in the corridors of power to wake up to a greater, progressive future of the people instead of conniving for vested interests.

title: On the path to self destruct
description: K P Chief Minister knows exactly where it is going to end
content:
K-P Chief Minister knows exactly where it is going to end
In missile warfare, when a weapon goes astray, either losing guidance or suffering a malfunction, a switch activates within it to what is called self-destruct. It explodes the weapon in the air to avoid unnecessary damage to unintended targets on the ground – there is chivalry in technology too. In the, for now, failed talks between the government and the opposition (read: PTI), the missile is in an uncontrolled mode. Not all missiles carry this benevolent self-destruct option; some still go ahead and hit what they can, intended or unintended, but this one is surely on self-destruct. Whatever way you look at it, government or the opposition, unless one or both change their approach to the issues they want resolved, both are on the way to mutual assured destruction (MAD). A common man will be hardly interested as to what fate awaits each, except that the stakes are just too many for him to ignore what may befall.
What is at stake? Once again, another province, another ethnic definition, another governmental attitude towards a people of another region with highly sensitised sub-national identity, and the horrendous possibility of another nightmarish eventuality. We only need to recall 1971. And for those of us around then, the spectre is fearful. We know the mistakes that the powerful made then, agitating and reinforcing the narrative that gave cause to the millions who suffered, and a nation that was broken in bloodshed and tears. Today, the lessons stand out as clear as crystal: the politics was patently self-serving; hunger for exclusive power and control was at its peak; and the failure of politics led to the ultimate clash between armed force and the people. The country and the nation were forsaken at the altar of personal aggrandisement and exclusivity of power.
I don't think the K-P Chief Minister knows exactly where it is going to end. He has rolled the dice. Soon it will pick momentum and roll in directions beyond his control. One wrong slogan, one ill-intended induction of a sentiment, and the mob will attain its own dynamic and purpose quite different from what Sohail Afridi may have ever imagined. Any effort to intervene physically to break the momentum before then will only enhance the process. Governments are powerful, and prone to overuse force. And in so doing, only add fuel to the fire. March 25, 1971 did not just fall into our midst from the sky or land one day from Mars. It took years in the making. Maybe decades. And we let it slip and slide till it was so out of control that we could only contend with force. The trick is to never let the mass develop. No mass, no momentum. However, it remains an impossibility where sentiments easily charge in ethnic colours. What was so easily achieved in Punjab is not possible in K-P for known reasons. Dialogue, then, is the only way out.
And there is an ongoing war in K-P with groups supported by neighbouring adversaries. The military and the law-enforcement agencies already have their hands full. In war, secure lines of interior are critical to success on the battlefront. How can the entire province be in a state of agitation and chaos if the fight at the front must be won? And before the cost of peace in depth becomes beyond reparation, it would be better to trade the smaller loss for a greater gain. The smaller loss was obvious and on the table; somehow, we let it lapse either because of brinksmanship, loss of face, or once again, patent political interests. We let politics overtake national purpose. And this is true for both sides. But the government in charge is principally responsible for doing the right thing. And the right thing is to do the least damage to national cohesion and territorial solidarity, even if it entails a political cost and a loss of face. The more we delay and dither, the higher the cost we pay to retrieve the moment of repair and concurrence. If we fail at it totally, the dissonance and strife will consume us in physical terms, breaking us apart. We have been there, seen it, and suffered. We don't wish to ever repeat it.
Afridi and his PTI are net gainers, in a perverse way, just as the conceivers of Bangladesh were to many – it does not relieve Imran Khan, though, of his instant predicaments. From their perch, as they see more and understand more, they only need to play the waiting game till the government closes all its options and touches the ebb of its ill-considered reaction. If indeed force, whether constitutional, legal or physical, is employed, the natural consequence is an inevitable clash. That will only accrue insecure depth and highly tenuous lines of interior. We have seen it all and know the consequences. When politics fails, mostly for incompetence or ulterior motives, it takes the convenient back seat, pushing the military forward toward the feared clash.
What was on the table for the PTI to gain was lost for fear of being castigated and an incompetent comprehension of the situation or its possible consequences. Imran Khan would have won full medical attention and regular visits from the family and lawyers under jail rules, which could have expanded to even better terms as confidence improved over time between the party and the government. K-P and its government would have saved the day for Pakistan and its own people from going under the hammer of another ill-considered resort to emergency and summary measures, deepening the sociopolitical divide. A better understanding of the operational environment in the province would have found both the security apparatus and the province working hand in hand to carve a more effective strategy to fight terror and its manifestations intending harm to Pakistan.
Their fears around their political legacy instead took over and held them back from a more gainful outcome of the talks, especially when the flip side is greatly more disconcerting and injurious. The PTI leadership at the talks, not in the province alone, failed the moment and missed the bus, once again. Lady luck does not come calling as often. When it does, seizing the moment is what counts. Ruing the day after does not.
Perhaps there is still time as Afridi orbits the province and develops a wake and a momentum that will only gain in strength and intensity. The surest way to stop him is to intervene through an offer that he cannot refuse. What that is will be the test of the leadership in Islamabad and their commitment to prioritising national stakes over personal and political feuds. It is not about who holds greater force, but who saves the nation from distress and disaffection.

title: Brain rot  you are suffering from it too
description: Sudden loss of orientation could be due to many reasons
content:
Sudden loss of orientation could be due to many reasons
Nearly three months ago, I was driving in Islamabad, an area of my routine drive for the last two decades. While driving, for just two seconds, I lost my orientation and could not figure out where and why I was going. Quickly I got my orientation back and I went where I needed to go. This was just a two?second incident but it made me extremely worried. Was it a reflection of some underlying disease or something else? I was hooked on short videos and reels and watched them for hours. Luckily, I had read some research papers on watching short videos and their effects on memory, so right there I decided to stop watching short videos.
Sudden loss of orientation could be due to many reasons, but as a physician I knew that I didn't have those risk factors. It's three months now and there has not been a repeat of that incident. But how was it linked to excessive watching of short videos and reels?
Once I started researching for this article, I also stumbled on the term "Brain Rot". My ignorance is justified because Gen Z is using this term when they have spent hours on compulsive scrolling and this overstimulates their brains and they can't focus and feel mentally drained. When we are watching short videos which are constantly changing topics, our brain starts getting dopamine (chemical that excites us) bursts as rewards, and it expects to have this chemical frequently as a reward. That affects our working memory and attention span. Reading and watching long videos train our brain to develop patience and keep long attention to the subject.
In my case, probably with mental fatigue and after overstimulation of my brain, I was driving on a familiar route and in this situation our brain moves into autopilot mode and a two?second loss of orientation was possible. Strong proof is that once I stopped watching short videos it never happened.
So, let's be clear. Brain Rot is not a medical terminology but a cultural one. By watching short reels and videos your brain cells are not actually dying and rotting but changing how they operate and that is affecting people's work, relationships and health.
In a large review of 71 individual studies covering around a hundred thousand people and published in 2025 by Nguyen, watching excessive short videos and reels was associated with poorer cognition, poor attention, poorer mental health and stress.
In another review by Marlene Ebster, published in June 2026, which reviewed ten years of published data and included more than 40 studies, they also found excessive use (four hours daily) responsible for inattention, impulsivity, reductions in working?memory span, anxiety, depression and stress. Two of these studies also showed neurobiological changes in the brain. There are plenty of new studies coming with the same conclusion. According to Dr Jared Cooney Horvath, Gen Z has lower cognitive scores in more than one hundred years even though it is the longest formally schooled generation as compared to previous generations. He links it to excessive screen use and recommends non?digital activities and argues that it helps people perform better as our brains need physical interaction like paper books or handwriting for better memory results.
It's difficult to stop watching short videos. Like leaving a drug habit, it needs strong commitment of the person and family support. It's not that you have to stop like me completely, you could start by limiting the time for these scrolls. Use your own phone stopwatch to keep you within limits. I switched to longer videos of at least ten minutes or more. I started watching TV programmes and movies again (on TV and not on phone). I restarted reading books and regular exercise.
While the human brain is declining by computer?assisted algorithms used by social media companies, at the same time computer AI is moving into the super?intelligence arena. Already AI is doing some tasks better than humans and our next generation's brains are declining. It's time to talk with your children, discuss the dangers to their mental health and come up with an agreed schedule of scrolling, balanced by other healthy activities like outdoor sports, walks, book reading or any other non?digital hobbies.
Technology is good until it threatens your survival.

title: Toll on Gaza teachers
description: Toll on Gaza teachers
content:
UNICEF estimates that 97.5% of Gaza's schools have been damaged or destroyed
There can be few greater indictments of a state's brutality than the killing of those whose only duty is to educate children. Yet this is precisely the horror that has unfolded in Palestine, where Israel's relentless military campaign has not only claimed countless innocent lives but also devastated an entire education system. According to the Palestinian Education Ministry, at least 800 teachers have been killed, over 3,300 injured and over 170 detained since October 2023. These figures should shame the conscience of a world that has repeatedly watched Israeli atrocities unfold while offering little beyond hollow condemnations.
The sheer scale of devastation is staggering. UNICEF estimates that 97.5% of Gaza's schools have been damaged or destroyed, leaving an entire generation struggling to access education. Classrooms have been reduced to rubble and teachers forced to conduct lessons in makeshift shelters. This represent an intolerable assault on the foundations of Palestinian society. No military objective can justify the wholesale devastation of an education system. Schools and teachers are entitled to protection, and attacks on civilians cannot be legitimised through sweeping claims of military necessity. The destruction inflicted on Gaza has long surpassed anything that can be morally defended as a proportionate response to a security threat. Nor is this assault on education confined to Gaza. Across the occupied West Bank, Palestinian teachers face military checkpoints, restrictions on movement and the threat of violence. Schools remain vulnerable to demolition, while the withholding of Palestinian revenues has deepened the financial hardship facing educators.
The killing of Palestinian teachers demands far more than another resolution or expression of concern. Those responsible for unlawful attacks must face independent investigation and prosecution. Governments must end the supply of weapons used in violations of international humanitarian law, while international institutions must secure protection for educators and urgently support the restoration of Palestinian schools.

title: Poverty emergency
description: Govt s only direct intervention has been expanding the Benazir Income Support Programme  increasing its budget
content:
Govt's only direct intervention has been expanding the Benazir Income Support Programme, increasing its budget
Poverty in Pakistan has been on the rise since the economic turmoil of the past decade began, after decades of steadily declining. The World Bank's latest report confirms the extent of the problem - Pakistan now accounts for 48% of all people in the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan region living below the $3-a-day poverty line. To be Pakistani is almost synonymous with poverty.
Sticking to the numbers, between 2018-19 and 2024-25, poverty in Pakistan rose by 6.4 percentage points at the $3 line and 3.2 percentage points at the $4.20 line, driven by the Covid-19 pandemic, the 2022 floods, high inflation and currency depreciation. The official poverty rate - which is almost universally considered to be an underestimation - has climbed from 21.9% in 2018-19 to 28.9%, with rural poverty reaching 36.2% and Balochistan recording 47%. Good-paying jobs are generally the best way to address poverty, but unemployment has hit a 21-year high of 7.1%, leaving 5.9 million people without work. And alongside inflation, the lack of government controls or investment in social services has seen inequality soar, even for people who are gainfully employed.
The government's only significant direct intervention has been expanding the Benazir Income Support Programme and increasing its budget. It now has Rs716 billion budget for 2025-26 and aims to support between 10 and 12 million families, or about 50 million people. But cash transfers alone cannot reverse structural impoverishment. The World Bank projects GDP per capita growth of just 2.2% this fiscal year - far too low to generate the jobs needed for a population exceeding 250 million. As the State Bank governor has warned, the current growth model simply cannot sustain such a population.
Macroeconomic stabilisation was and remains important, but without a dramatic focus shift that leads to significant investment in human capital, rural development and productive employment, the poverty trend will remain irreversible.

title: New tranche
description: New tranche
content:
Government's austerity drive has proven to be a facade
Pakistan pulled out all the stops to clinch its next $1.2 billion IMF tranche under the combined $7 billion EFF and $1.4 billion RSF frameworks. The breakthrough comes as little surprise; the government has consistently walked the talk by stringently complying with the lender's directives. By prioritising macroeconomic stability, stabilising the energy sector and driving deep structural reforms, Islamabad has successfully kept its economic programme on track. This latest tranche brings cumulative inflows under the programme to $5.7 billion, providing crucial breathing room as the government considers entering a subsequent programme next year.
The staff-level agreement is highly likely to receive approval from the IMF Executive Board, as Pakistan has met all its prior conditions. However, the discussions regarding the Article IV consultation proved delicate, as they directly tie into structural reforms aimed at transitioning the economy toward higher value-added activities. Looking ahead, Islamabad faces the steep challenge of enhancing competition, dismantling regulatory and trade barriers, accelerating privatisation and strengthening governance alongside anti-corruption institutions.
The government's austerity drive has proven to be a facade, failing to provide any meaningful relief for commoners. Instead, the IMF's persistent demands to broaden the tax base and boost revenue have resulted in crushing direct and indirect tax burdens. Regrettably, salaried professionals and middle-income earners have borne the brunt of these policies.
This inequity has fueled widespread public resentment toward the IMF and raised serious questions about the government's wisdom in shielding the elite from their fair share of economic liability. Concurrently, the IMF's pressure to maintain a high petroleum levy to address the power-sector circular debt is stifling domestic industry. By driving production costs to prohibitive levels, these energy mandates threaten to trigger a wave of industrial shutdowns, leaving the country in a dangerous paradox where the very measures meant to stabilise the economy are ultimately suffocating its engines of growth.

title: Resilience in the age of climate breakdown
description: Resilience in the age of climate breakdown
content:
Pakistan needs to use its existing water more intelligently and more fairly
There is a profound irony at the heart of climate change. Countries in the Global South that have contributed relatively little to historical greenhouse-gas emissions are among those most exposed to its consequences. However, one cannot oversimplify this issue. India remains a lower-middle-income country, yet it is among the world's largest polluters in absolute terms because of the scale of its population, industrial activity and energy use. Pakistan, by contrast, has a much smaller ecological footprint, but this is not the result of environmental consciousness. It reflects the relatively smaller scale of its economy, industrial base and consumption.
The World Bank has estimated that climate-related risks, environmental degradation and air pollution could reduce Pakistan's GDP by 1820 per cent by 2050. The problem becomes even starker when viewed through the lens of Sustainable Development Goals. Pakistan remains far from meeting many of its development targets, and climate shocks threaten to reverse hard-won gains. A flood does not merely destroy crops; it can destroy schools, roads, clinics and livelihoods. Climate change therefore acts as a multiplier of existing development failures.
Yet South Asia still fails to cooperate adequately on problems that do not respect borders. Water, in particular, is increasingly viewed through a security lens rather than a shared survival lens. That is especially dangerous between India and Pakistan. The two countries depend on the same river systems, but mutual distrust has hardened into strategic competition. India is trying to turn water into an instrument of pressure and potential coercion. However, the region cannot afford to treat rivers as weapons. Water scarcity on both sides of the nuclearised border will not be solved through brinkmanship.
The same logic applies to air pollution, which also ignores national boundaries. The World Bank has estimated that more than half of air pollution in many major South Asian cities originates outside the locality in which it is measured. Coordinated action across borders is therefore far more effective, and often less costly, than fragmented national responses. Regional cooperation is not a luxury. It is a necessity.
The same principle should apply to climate finance. The creation of the Loss and Damage Fund was an important achievement, but its resources remain tiny relative to the scale of need. Pledges are still far below what developing countries require to cope with present and future shocks. Demanding more loss-and-damage financing is necessary, but it cannot become the main climate strategy. Rebuilding after every disaster is neither economically nor socially sustainable. Developing countries need to adapt, decarbonize and become more resilient before disasters occur.
For Pakistan, that means rethinking how water and development are managed. The country not only needs new storage dams to contend with its water insecurity, but it also needs to use its existing water more intelligently and fairly. That means investing in water recycling, groundwater recharge, improved irrigation, soil management, rainwater harvesting, wetlands restoration, pollution control, and better storage where appropriate.
Pakistan's energy transition offers a broader lesson. Much of the country's recent solar expansion has been driven not by the state, but by households, businesses and the private market, especially the falling cost of solar panels. That shows what is possible when clean energy becomes affordable. But solar alone is not enough. It still requires stronger grids, storage and transmission if it is to serve the broader public interest. The same is true for water: resilience will not come from grand announcements alone, but from the careful management of existing resources, rather than just waiting for India to restore the Indus Water Treaty.

content:
Kylie Kelce says doctors sent her 'weird DMs' after she discussed possibly getting a breast augmentation
Kylie Kelce has revealed that she received unexpected messages from doctors after discussing her interest in getting a breast augmentation on her podcast.
During the October 8 episode of Not Gonna Lie , Kelce said several medical professionals contacted her after she mentioned her plans for a possible breast lift or augmentation. She described the messages as “weird DMs” and said she has since added the doctors to a banned list.
“I’ve said it [on the podcast], and then I got all these weird DMs of people, doctors’ offices, being like, ‘We’ll do it,’” Kelce said while speaking with guest Jen Hamilton.
The media personality previously discussed the possibility of having a breast lift on her podcast in February. Kelce, who has four children with husband Jason Kelce, said she eventually wants to restore her breasts after pregnancy.
Kelce and the former NFL player are parents to daughters Wyatt, Ellie and Bennett, as well as their youngest child, Finn, who was born in March 2025. The couple married in April 2018 after dating for four years.
The Not Gonna Lie host has also spoken openly about changes to her body following pregnancy. In August 2025, she discussed struggling with her postpartum appearance and said it took her until after the birth of her third child to accept that her stomach would not look the same.
Kelce said she eventually learned to appreciate the physical changes associated with motherhood, while acknowledging that accepting a postpartum body was not an immediate process for her.
Her latest comments continue Kelce’s candid discussions about pregnancy, motherhood, body image and cosmetic procedures on her podcast.

title: Jessica Chastain   s    Other Mommy    faces harsh early reviews ahead of release
description: Rob Savage   s horror film is based on Josh Malerman   s novel    Incidents Around the House
content:
Rob Savage’s horror film is based on Josh Malerman’s novel ‘Incidents Around the House’
Early reactions to Jessica Chastain’s horror film Other Mommy have arrived, with several reviewers criticising its jump scares, visual effects and story ahead of its US release.
The Universal and Blumhouse production stars Chastain in a dual role as a mother whose daughter, played by Arabella Olivia Clark, is haunted by a demonic entity. Rob Savage directs it, which is based on Josh Malerman’s novel Incidents Around the House .
The movie is receiving mixed responses from early viewers, including international influencers, awards bloggers and Rotten Tomatoes critics. Several reactions have been negative, with reviewers questioning its screenplay and execution.
The Jam Report gave Other Mommy 1.5 out of 5, describing its finale as unintentionally funny and criticising what it called ineffective jump scares, weak CGI and increasingly confusing storytelling.
Screen Space also awarded the film 1.5 out of 5, citing its pacing, direction and what it considered an unclear message. The review also accused the film of borrowing from Tobe Hooper’s Poltergeist .
The AU Review gave the film 2 out of 5. It praised Savage’s technical ambition and sequences involving perspective and physical space, but argued that the storytelling did not match those strengths.
Other reactions have been kinder. The Matinee Show called the premise creepy and noted some unsettling moments, while Goldwin Reviews awarded the film 4 out of 5 and praised its ambition and thematic depth.
Savage previously said the film contains around 50 jump scares, a detail that has become part of the discussion around its reception.
Despite the early criticism, Other Mommy is expected to perform strongly at the box office. The film is projected to open with around $20m.
Official US critics screenings are taking place shortly before the film opens on Friday, meaning a fuller picture of the critical response is expected as additional reviews arrive.

Swift could perform her ‘Toy Story 5’ song as awards season gains momentum
Taylor Swift is set to perform at the Academy Museum Gala in Los Angeles on October 17, adding a major music appearance to an evening dedicated to celebrating cinema.
The gala, held at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures, serves as a fundraiser supporting the institution’s exhibitions, screenings and educational programmes. Academy Museum director and president Amy Homma confirmed Swift’s appearance, praising the singer songwriter’s global reach and saying the organisation was thrilled to welcome her.
Details of Swift’s performance remain under wraps. However, her appearance comes as her song "I Knew It, I Knew You", from Toy Story 5 , enters the awards conversation. The track could potentially earn Swift her first Oscar nomination, making the gala a notable event ahead of the Academy Awards season.

The Academy Museum Gala will also honour three filmmakers during the event. Charlize Theron is set to receive the Icon Award, Colman Domingo will be presented with the Vantage Award, and filmmaker John Carpenter will receive the Luminary Award.
Presented by Rolex, the gala raises funds for the Academy Museum’s wider mission to celebrate and preserve cinema. Proceeds help support exhibitions, educational opportunities, public screenings and access to the museum.
The event is co chaired by Robert Rodriguez, Steven Spielberg and Kate Capshaw. Its host committee includes numerous figures from Hollywood, including Jessica Alba, Judd Apatow, Leslie Mann, Adrien Brody, Jon M Chu, Kirsten Dunst, Greta Lee, John Legend, Demi Moore and Seth Rogen.

Lorraine Nicholson will make her feature debut as writer and director of the Searchlight film
Jessica Biel has joined the cast of Playmates , a film from Searchlight Pictures that marks Lorraine Nicholson’s feature writing and directorial debut.
Biel will star opposite Lily Rose Depp, Bill Pullman and Indiana Elle in the project. She will play the wife of Hugh Hefner, portrayed by Pullman, who is herself a former Playmate. The character is fictional and is not based on any of Hefner’s real wives.
According to the official logline, the story follows 13 year old Elle, a know it all who considers the Playboy Mansion her second home. She meets Anna, played by Depp, one of seven hopefuls competing to become Playmate of the Month. The pair develop an unlikely friendship as they try to help each other achieve their goals, with Elle seeking a magazine cover and Anna hoping to win over a boy.
Playmates is being written and directed by Nicholson, who is making her debut behind the camera. Alex Orlovsky and Duncan Montgomery will produce through High Frequency Entertainment, while Depp is also attached as a producer alongside her acting role.
Searchlight Pictures is overseeing the film, with Richard Ruiz, the studio’s vice president of production, and creative executive Cornelia Burleigh overseeing the project. They report to heads of production and development DanTram Nguyen and Katie Goodson Thomas.
Biel has worked across film and television throughout her career, with credits including The Illusionist , New Year’s Eve , Valentine’s Day and The A Team . Her television work includes 7th Heaven , Candy and The Sinner .
Her role in The Sinner earned her Emmy and Golden Globe nominations. Biel has developed a producing career through her Iron Ocean banner, which has been involved with projects including Cruel Summer , Limetown , Candy and The Sinner .

title: Three injured  two trailers torched in attacks
description: Three injured  two trailers torched in attacks
content:
Gunmen set trailers on fire in Turbat as grenade wounds three in Gwadar
Armed men opened fire on two trailers parked outside a police station in Nasirabad area of Turbat district and later set the vehicles ablaze, while three people were injured in a separate grenade attack on a mobile phone shop in Gwadar's Jannat Bazaar, police said.
According to police sources, the armed attackers targeted the two trailers in front of the police station in Nasirabad. They opened fire on the vehicles before setting them on fire. The attackers fled the scene after carrying out the assault.
Following the incident, security forces cordoned off the area and launched a search operation to track down the fleeing attackers. Security was also tightened in and around the area as investigations into the incident continued.
Police said the extent of the damage caused to the trailers was being assessed, while investigators were examining the circumstances surrounding the attack and attempting to determine the identity and motive of the assailants.
In a separate incident in Gwadar, three people were injured when unidentified attackers hurled a hand grenade at a mobile phone shop in Jannat Bazaar, police said.
According to police, the grenade was thrown at the shop during the night, injuring three people present inside. The injured were identified as Shaukat, his son Baqir and Zafar. Police said the three victims were residents of Kashmore district in Sindh.
The injured were shifted to a local hospital shortly after the blast, where they were provided medical treatment. Their condition was not immediately disclosed.
Police and security personnel reached the site soon after receiving information about the attack and cordoned off the area. Investigators collected evidence from the scene as part of an inquiry into the incident.
Security was subsequently increased in Jannat Bazaar and surrounding areas to prevent any further untoward incident. Police said the nature of the attack and its possible motives were being investigated from different angles.

Paramount is developing a live-action 'Cyberpunk 2077' movie with producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura and CD Projekt Red
Paramount Pictures is developing a live-action movie based on CD Projekt Red’s popular video game Cyberpunk 2077 , with producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura attached to the project.
The film will be set in the Cyberpunk 2077 universe, although plot details and casting have not yet been announced. CD Projekt Red, the Polish video game developer and owner of the franchise rights, will produce alongside di Bonaventura.
Released in 2020, Cyberpunk 2077 is set in Night City, a futuristic and dystopian metropolis in California. The game follows V, a mercenary who becomes implanted with a cybernetic biochip containing the digital consciousness of legendary rock star and terrorist Johnny Silverhand.
As Silverhand’s consciousness begins to overwrite V’s mind, the two must work together to find a way to separate themselves while confronting Arasaka Corporation, one of the most powerful organisations in Night City.
The video game has become a major commercial success, selling more than 40 million copies worldwide. Its expansion, Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty , has also sold more than 15 million copies.
The Paramount Cyberpunk 2077 movie is part of the studio’s expanding push into video game adaptations. Paramount is also working on a Street Fighter film with Legendary, while a movie based on the Call of Duty franchise is in development with Peter Berg directing and co-writing alongside Taylor Sheridan.
The live-action Cyberpunk 2077 adaptation adds another major video game property to Paramount’s upcoming film slate. Further details about the director, cast, storyline and release date are expected to be announced later.

content:
Crunchyroll has secured international rights to 'The Apothecary Diaries' movie following season 3 premiere
Crunchyroll has secured international distribution rights for The Apothecary Diaries: The Late Lady's Treasure, the first movie in the popular mystery anime series, just days after the premiere of season 3.
The agreement gives Crunchyroll distribution rights across North America and international territories outside Asia, including India.
Crunchyroll and Sony Pictures Entertainment will handle the film’s distribution, although a release date has not yet been announced.
The Apothecary Diaries: The Late Lady's Treasure is an original mystery written by Hyuganatsu, author of The Apothecary Diaries series. Norihiro Naganuma is directing, with Toho Animation Studio producing the animation.
The film follows Maomao, a young woman with an interest in medicines and poisons, who is drawn into a mystery involving a hidden treasure in the City of Water.
Jinshi, an official from the imperial palace, asks Maomao to accompany him to Binan-shu, a southern province ruled by the Bi clan.
Jinshi’s journey begins after the emperor orders him to fulfil the final request of a concubine who died five years earlier. While examining her body, Jinshi discovers that she remains intact and appears unusually well preserved.
In Binan-shu, Maomao encounters new plants and medicines while the city faces unrest as pirates search for treasure left behind by a deceased leader.
Jinshi voices his concern with one line, "I hope nothing happens …" His fears are realised when an event during the concubine’s burial sets off an unpredictable chain of events.
The Apothecary Diaries has sold more than 57 million copies worldwide. Its anime adaptation premiered in October 2023, followed by its second season in January 2025.
The third season began streaming on Crunchyroll on October 2, with the platform also carrying the first two seasons.

title: Critics divided over how scary Mike Flanagan   s  Carrie  really is
description: Critics are divided over how scary Mike Flanagan   s new Stephen King series  Carrie  is on Prime Video
content:
Critics are divided over how scary Mike Flanagan’s new Stephen King series 'Carrie' is on Prime Video
Mike Flanagan’s new Carrie has received mixed reactions from critics, with reviews differing over how effectively the Prime Video adaptation delivers horror and psychological tension.
The eight-episode series stars Summer H. Howell as Carrie White, a sheltered teenager who faces bullying at school while secretly possessing telekinetic powers.
Flanagan, known for The Haunting of Hill House, Midnight Mass and The Fall of the House of Usher, has adapted Stephen King’s 1974 novel Carrie for a modern audience.
Some critics praised the series for its gradual tension. Lauren Sarner of the New York Post described it as "full of mounting tension", although she suggested viewers expecting the "Gothic atmosphere and chills" of Flanagan’s earlier work could be disappointed.
The series also updates Carrie’s bullying for the social media era. Classmates film her humiliation on their phones, while an anonymous Instagram account is used to spread rumours and target students.
Seattle Times critic Dominic Baez said the shower scene, in which Carrie is humiliated after getting her first period, is "just as traumatic" as in the original novel and 1976 film. Variety’s Aramide Tinubu called the adaptation "harrowing and fearless".
Other critics were less convinced by its ability to frighten viewers. The Hollywood Reporter’s Daniel Fienberg described the series as "far less scary than it should be", arguing that Flanagan is stronger at creating horror moods than delivering frights.
Vulture’s Roxana Hadadi similarly argued that "tension doesn't build" throughout the series, while Esquire’s Eric Francisco said "Flanagan's striking scares are largely absent" and argued that the director "peaked with Midnight Mass in that department."
The Guardian’s Lucy Mangan offered another perspective, describing Carrie as "more like a teen drama with extra bite than a straight-up, blood-soaked horror event."

title: McKenna Grace recreates Jennifer Lawrence   s iconic Katniss dress at  Hunger Games  exhibition
description: Grace said that she wanted to pay homage to Katniss while recognising the significance and message behind the dress
content:
Grace said that she wanted to pay homage to Katniss while recognising the significance and message behind the dress
McKenna Grace recreated one of Jennifer Lawrence’s most memorable Hunger Games looks as she paid tribute to Katniss Everdeen at a special franchise exhibition in Paris.
Grace, 20, wore a replica of the gown Lawrence wore as Katniss in The Hunger Games: Catching Fire at the costume exhibition “Elegance Is Authority: The Story, Style and Power of Panem” on October 6. The event was held at the Musée Rodin in Paris.
The A-line gown was designed by Monique Lhuillier, while the original dress worn by Lawrence was created by Tex Saverio in collaboration with The Hunger Games costume designer Trish Summerville. Grace’s replica featured a fitted bodice with delicate beading, a tiered ballgown skirt and silver embellishments extending from the strapless neckline.
She completed the look with feathers in her hair and diamond earrings, while her blonde hair was styled in an updo with a braided headband. Her makeup included white eyeshadow, long lashes, bronzed cheeks and pink-lined lips.
Grace later shared her excitement about recreating the costume on Instagram, describing herself as a “massive fan” of the franchise. She said the opportunity was special and that she wanted to pay homage to Katniss while recognising the significance of the dress.
The actress also showed off the look on TikTok while posing inside the Musée Rodin. Her caption referenced a line from Suzanne Collins’ The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping : “If you let them treat you like an animal, they will, so don’t let them.” Fans quickly praised the tribute, with several referencing Katniss’ iconic nickname, the Mockingjay and the franchise’s famous imagery.
Lawrence originally wore the dress in the 2013 film The Hunger Games: Catching Fire during Katniss’ televised appearance with Caesar Flickerman, played by Stanley Tucci. The character’s wedding dress becomes part of the film’s dramatic transformation when she spins and the gown catches fire, revealing the Mockingjay-inspired look underneath.
Grace’s tribute comes as excitement surrounding The Hunger Games continues to build ahead of the upcoming adaptation of Collins’ Sunrise on the Reaping . Grace has previously spoken about being a longtime fan of the franchise and even revealed that she once created fan edits of Josh Hutcherson, who played Peeta Mellark in the original films.
The actress later worked with Hutcherson on Five Nights at Freddy’s 2 , making her earlier fandom revelation an amusing part of her connection to the franchise.

title: Govt hikes petrol by Rs2 31  high speed diesel by 78 paisas for Oct 9
description: Petrol price increases to Rs398 96 per litre  while HSD will cost Rs395 72 under daily price mechanism
content:
Petrol price increases to Rs398.96 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs395.72 under daily price mechanism
The federal government on Thursday increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.31 and 78 paisas, respectively, for October 9.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs398.96 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs395.72 per litre for Friday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government increased the price of petrol by Rs1.82 per litre, while decreasing the price of HSD by 91 paisas per litre for October 8.
Read : Govt increases petrol by Rs1.82, cuts diesel by 91 paisas for Oct 8
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices jumped more than 5% on Thursday, then pared gains after President Donald Trump said the US will ‌not launch an attack on Iran before midterm congressional elections in November.
Brent crude futures were up $3.48, or 3.5%, at $103.73 a barrel by 12:41 pm ET (1641 GMT). US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained $2.69, or 3.1%, to $91. At their session highs, both contracts were up more than $5 a barrel, with Brent at its highest ​since September 29 on worries about potential imminent US strikes on Iran and a supply loss in the US Gulf ​of Mexico from Hurricane Isaias.
"Further details surrounding the G7's proposed 100 million-barrel SPR release have disappointed the market, as the barrels appear to be drawn from the previously announced ‌400 million-barrel ⁠release that has yet to be fully marketed," Staunovo added.

Nvidia's Huang to receive National Medal of Science from Trump for outstanding contributions to science

The new disclosure of ​the president's investment in one of the world's most ​valuable companies comes as his administration weighs policies ⁠that could shape Nvidia's fortunes, including rules governing exports of ​its advanced chips.

Past recipients have been honored for advances ranging from cancer detection to protecting ​the food supply ​during droughts.
The Nvidia ⁠trades were one of hundreds the president made in August, according to the disclosure signed ​by the president on September 17 and made ​public ⁠on Thursday.
"All investment decisions are made entirely by independent managers," Ingle said. "There are no conflicts of interest.”

title: Elsinore  producer Andrea Occhipinti reveals he lost many friends during AIDS crisis
description: Occhipinti also recalled that his business partner Kermit Smith was HIV positive when they founded Lucky Red in 1987
content:
Occhipinti also recalled that his business partner Kermit Smith was HIV positive when they founded Lucky Red in 1987
Elsinore producer Andrea Occhipinti has revealed that he lost many friends during the AIDS crisis, explaining why Ian Charleson’s story has held such personal significance for him while discussing his 20-year journey to bring the film to the screen.
The Italian producer spoke to Variety following the London Film Festival premiere of Elsinore , which received a standing ovation. The film stars Andrew Scott as Scottish actor Ian Charleson, who was living with AIDS when he took on the role of Hamlet at London’s National Theatre in 1989. Charleson died in 1990 at the age of 40.
Occhipinti first met Charleson in 1984 while working on The Sun Also Rises . He encountered him again in Rome three years later, when Charleson was filming Dario Argento’s Opera . Occhipinti said Charleson, whom he remembered as funny and lively during their first meeting, seemed completely different when they met again and appeared depressed.
Charleson later introduced Occhipinti to his friend Ethan Silverman. After Charleson’s death, Silverman told Occhipinti about the actor’s determination to play Hamlet despite his illness. That conversation eventually convinced Occhipinti that there was a film to be made about Charleson’s final months.
“I lost a lot of friends,” Occhipinti said of the AIDS crisis, recalling that his American business partner Kermit Smith was HIV positive when they co-founded Lucky Red in 1987. Smith died in 2001. “That’s why this story is so important to me,” Occhipinti added.
Occhipinti first raised the possibility of making the film with Silverman in 2005. Fifteen years later, the project began moving forward, with Andrew Scott attached to play Charleson. Scott’s own experience playing Hamlet and his background in both theatre and film made him a natural choice for the role.
The project eventually brought together writer Stephen Beresford and director Simon Stone, with Studiocanal financing the film. For Occhipinti, the long process was ultimately about more than Charleson himself. He described Elsinore as a story about community and the theatre world that protected Charleson while he was seriously ill.
The film portrays Charleson preparing for Hamlet as his health deteriorates, highlighting his determination to continue working despite his AIDS diagnosis. Scott has said the story should also confront the stigma surrounding the crisis rather than place shame on those living with HIV and AIDS.
Olivia Colman co-stars as Dr Margaret Johnson, a doctor who cared for people living with AIDS during the crisis. The film also emphasises the role played by doctors, nurses, friends and families who supported people facing an illness that was surrounded by fear and prejudice.
Elsinore opened the 2026 London Film Festival and is scheduled to receive a US theatrical release through Focus Features on November 20. Studiocanal will release the film in the UK and Ireland on January 29, 2027.
