title: Israel   s Oscar entry  Tell Me Everything  dropped from Swiss festival after boycott campaign
description: Everybody   s Perfect queer film festival cancelled two planned screenings after receiving messages warning of a boycott
content:
Everybody’s Perfect queer film festival cancelled two planned screenings after receiving messages warning of a boycott
Israel’s Oscar entry Tell Me Everything has been removed from a Swiss queer film festival following pressure from pro-Palestinian groups calling for a boycott over the film’s connection to Israel amid the ongoing war in Gaza.
The Geneva-based Everybody’s Perfect queer film festival had selected Moshe Rosenthal’s Tell Me Everything for its 2026 programme, but cancelled two planned screenings after receiving messages warning of a boycott. The pressure came from a collective of groups including Palestine, Filmer C’est Exister, the Student Coordination for Palestine at the University of Geneva, BDS Geneva, CRAQ and Marad.
The decision comes as cultural institutions and artists linked to Israel face increasing pressure from Palestinian solidarity movements seeking to challenge what they describe as the normalisation of Israeli cultural representation while Palestinians face devastating conditions in Gaza. The boycott campaign against Tell Me Everything reflects a wider push to hold cultural institutions accountable for their associations with Israel.
Tell Me Everything , which premiered at Sundance earlier this year, follows 12-year-old Boaz as he discovers a secret about his father during the HIV/AIDS crisis of the 1980s. The film was recently selected as Israel’s submission for the Best International Feature category at the 2027 Academy Awards and reportedly received a record number of nominations at Israel’s Ophir Awards.
After receiving the boycott threat, the festival asked Rosenthal and the film’s producers to clarify their positions on the Israeli government and the war in Palestine. Rosenthal and Green Productions responded that they do not represent the Israeli government and do not finance or produce films supporting its current policies.
The response did not stop the festival from removing the film. Artistic director Sylvie Cachin said the cancellation was intended to avoid controversy immediately before the festival opened, while communications lead Charlotte Spector acknowledged that the boycott threat had created significant pressure.
The cancellation has prompted debate over whether Israeli artists and cultural works should be treated separately from the state, particularly as international calls for boycotts of Israeli institutions and cultural representation continue. Supporters of the campaign argue that cultural platforms can contribute to the normalisation of Israel internationally, and that refusing such platforms is a form of nonviolent pressure in support of Palestinian rights.
The controversy also highlights the role of Palestine-focused cultural organisations in challenging the presence of Israeli films at international festivals. Palestine, Filmer C’est Exister is itself a Geneva-based film festival, while BDS Geneva and student organisers have been involved in broader campaigns supporting Palestinian rights.
Everybody’s Perfect describes itself as a queer film festival committed to human rights, diversity, inclusion and progressive cultural expression. Its stated mission includes defending human rights and using cinema to create spaces for social reflection and representation.
For supporters of the boycott, the removal of Tell Me Everything represents a small but significant example of cultural pressure over Israel’s treatment of Palestinians. The film’s removal does not end the wider debate over Israeli cinema, but it demonstrates how Palestinian solidarity campaigns are increasingly challenging the country’s cultural presence on international platforms.

title: Elizabeth Banks to play Karen Read in Amazon   s new true crime series

content:
Elizabeth Banks will star as Karen Read in Amazon’s eight-episode drama based on the high-profile Massachusetts case
Elizabeth Banks is set to star as Karen Read in an upcoming Amazon drama series inspired by the high-profile Massachusetts case.
The untitled one-hour series has received an eight-episode order from Amazon and is based on the Law&Crime and Audible Original podcast Karen . Justin Noble, who co-created The Sex Lives of College Girls , will serve as writer, showrunner and executive producer.
The series follows Karen Read, whose boyfriend, Boston police officer John O’Keefe, was found dead in the snow during a blizzard. According to the show’s official logline, Read and her legal team maintain that she is innocent and that a conspiracy was responsible for protecting the real assailants.
The drama will explore the case and its impact on the community, while examining society’s growing fascination with true crime and the different perspectives surrounding high-profile legal battles.
Banks will executive produce the series through her Brownstone Productions banner alongside Max Handelman and Krissy Wall. David E. Kelley and Matthew Tinker will also executive produce through David E. Kelley Productions. Audible and Law&Crime executives are among the additional producers, with Warner Bros. Television serving as the studio.
Banks, who grew up in Massachusetts, said the case had divided families, friends and communities in the state. She added that the series will examine questions surrounding the stories people believe and public trust in institutions.
The project marks another major television role for Banks, who recently starred in Prime Video’s The Better Sister . Her other credits include 30 Rock , Mrs. America and the Pitch Perfect and The Hunger Games franchises. She also directed the 2023 horror comedy Cocaine Bear .
Amazon has not yet announced a release date or additional cast members for the Karen Read series.

title: Israel drastically reduces British diplomatic presence in Jerusalem
description: Miliband said Britain did not accept that the Israeli government had  the legal right  to enforce the closure
content:
Britain pledges to continue delivering 'vital services' in Jerusalem
Israel said the British consulate in east Jerusalem ended its functions on Thursday, but seven diplomats would be allowed to remain in a limited capacity, with Britain saying the outpost would continue to offer "vital services".
The move came after Israel ordered the closure of the consulate in September in retaliation after London led Western sanctions over violence by Israeli settlers against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said Thursday's move to downsize the British presence followed dialogue with the British government aimed at avoiding an escalation of tensions between the two countries.
"As I announced, the British consulate in Jerusalem ended its role today," Saar said in a statement, adding that 20 diplomats, including the consul general, were ending their missions and leaving the country.
Saar said the building was the property of the British government and that a "task force of only seven diplomats" would be allowed to operate from the premises, "which ceased to function as a consulate today".
"Their scope of activity will be very limited," Saar said, adding that the two countries had "agreed on the continuation of dialogue between the governments".
Britain pledged to continue delivering "vital services" in Jerusalem, saying the consulate general building would remain open and would "be known as the UK Mission, Jerusalem".
"The UK Mission, Jerusalem is independent, operational and will continue to deliver vital services and our work with the Palestinian people," Foreign Minister Ed Miliband said in a statement.
Miliband said Britain did not accept that the Israeli government had "the legal right" to enforce the closure.
"We will work in the coming months to build back up our presence and we will not take reciprocal action while such discussions are underway and credible," he added.
The Palestinian Authority's foreign affairs ministry denounced the move as "illegal", saying it viewed it as "an attempt to impose Israeli sovereignty over the occupied city" of Jerusalem.
The British consulate was founded nearly 200 years ago and lies in east Jerusalem, part of the historically Palestinian area that Israel captured in 1967.
Israel later annexed east Jerusalem and considers the holy city its undivided capital.
While Israel controls east Jerusalem, most countries, including Britain, do not recognise its sovereignty over the whole city.
The British consulate handles "political, commercial, security and economic interests between the UK and Palestine", according to its website, as well as consular services for British nationals in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza.
Read More: Senior US Embassy official in Jerusalem suppressed diplomatic cables to shield Netanyahu govt: report
An AFP photographer on Thursday saw that the diplomatic emblem and a plaque that adorned the consulate's facade had been removed.
The measure has led Britain to lose a "historic and meaningful presence" in terms of its support for the Palestinians, an Israeli diplomatic source said.
"So yes, they keep the building" and a limited number of diplomats, the source told AFP , but "they have lost a historic and significant footprint".
The source said they thought recent dialogue between the British and Israeli governments would allow a "turning point" in deteriorating relations.
"If until a few weeks ago, until September 8, we were on a path of spiralling down, then I think the page has turned," the source said.
"Dialogue is a path towards returning to ... more constructive relations."
September 8 was the day Saar ordered the consulate to close.
He also said Israel would expel British representatives at a centre monitoring the US-brokered ceasefire plan in Gaza, bar British training for Palestinian Authority forces and ban 12 Britons, mostly members of parliament, from visiting.
Saar on Thursday said those measures had been implemented.
The retaliation came after 12 countries, including Britain, Canada and France, announced they would sanction trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank, following a surge in settler attacks against Palestinians in the occupied territory.

title: Indian opposition protest police action against lawmakers  push for poll chief s resignation
description: The protests present a new political challenge to Modi midway into his third term
content:
The protests present a new political challenge to Modi midway into his third term
Indian opposition groups demonstrated for a third day on Thursday, protesting police ‌action against Congress party leaders and demanding the resignation of the chief election commissioner over a controversial revision of voter lists.
Opposition parties, their student units, and the " Cockroach " youth movement have been holding almost daily demonstrations seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's ​resignation. They have accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of using ​a revision of voter lists to fix them in its favour, in collusion ⁠with its appointees, including Kumar.
Kumar has not commented, but the Election Commission and the BJP have ​denied the allegations.
The protests present a new political challenge to Modi midway into his third term, ​just months after similar demonstrations led by the self-named Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) forced the resignation of his education minister over exam paper leaks.
Read: Modi's education minister quits as jubilant Indian youth protesters claim victory, end protest
Visuals from news agency ANI showed dozens of Congress supporters staging a protest march on Thursday in ​the southern state of Telangana, while the opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal organised a similar demonstration in ​the eastern state of Bihar.
Hundreds of supporters of the CJP youth movement also protested in tech hub Bengaluru, many ‌of ⁠them holding posters that said, "Every name counts, Every vote matters" and "Stop the Murder of Democracy".
"I think voting right is the most basic point of democracy ... People who actually want to vote, who actually care about the future of India, they are just being (denied) voting rights," Khushi Shrivastava, a 22-year-old architecture ​student who attended the ​Bengaluru protest, told Reuters .

On ⁠Wednesday, Congress accused police of using "brute force" to briefly detain party leader Rahul Gandhi, his sister Priyanka Vadra, and other lawmakers as they tried to ​reach the Jantar Mantar protest site in New Delhi.
Delhi Police said the ​allegations were being ⁠used to "defame" the force.
"We are on the ground and, as officers, we also ensure that every kind of legal duty is followed and no illegal, unnecessary actions take place," senior police officer Shrishti Pandey ⁠told ANI .

title: Dozens protest in Tokyo after Marine accused of murder in Okinawa
description: Latest incident fuels concern that US troop presence could undermine vital East Asian security ties
content:
Latest incident fuels concern that US troop presence could undermine vital East Asian security ties
Dozens of protesters lined up in front of Japan's Foreign Ministry on Thursday after a US Marine was accused of killing a woman in the southernmost prefecture ​of Okinawa , many holding signs decrying crimes by US service members.
The case ‌is the latest in a string of incidents stretching back years that have fuelled unease over the large US troop presence on the island chain near Taiwan and ​China, with US officials warning it could undermine ties vital to ​security in East Asia.
Public reaction to Anna Yagi's killing, however, ⁠has been muted compared with the mass demonstrations that followed the rape ​of a 12-year-old Okinawan girl by three US servicemen in 1995.
Lance Corporal Devin ​Jacob Ballard, 20, is suspected of killing Yagi, 39, in a hotel in the Okinawan capital of Naha last weekend and taking her wallet and backpack. Ballard denied the ​allegations, police said.
Leaders of Thursday's protest spoke over loudspeakers about abuses by US ​service members and called on the government to respond, with others in the crowd rattling ‌noisemakers ⁠in assent.
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has called the killing "extremely brutal and heinous", and Tokyo said it had strongly protested to the US and demanded measures to prevent a repeat of such incidents.
Japan hosts the largest overseas contingent of ​US forces globally. ​Most of the ⁠18,000 Japan-based Marines are stationed in Okinawa, which the US held from the end of World War Two until ​1972.
That presence has repeatedly stirred resentment among residents over ​issues such ⁠as noise, aircraft crashes and the conduct of personnel.
The US on Wednesday began a 48-hour pause of military operations and a ban on alcohol while troops ⁠undergo training ​on standards and discipline. Service members have also ​been given a month-long curfew for a "period of reflection".

title: Travis Barker shares recovery update after undergoing surgery
description: Kourtney Kardashian and daughter Alabama Barker supported the drummer during his hospital stay
content:
Kourtney Kardashian and daughter Alabama Barker supported the drummer during his hospital stay
Travis Barker has revealed he underwent surgery after sharing photos from a hospital bed that prompted concern.
The Blink 182 drummer, 50, explained his hospital visit in an Instagram Stories update on October 7. Barker said his arm, hand and fingers had been numb since a show he played the previous month.
He said he underwent a nerve test on Monday after a show and learned that he needed a cubital tunnel release to address the nerve problem. The procedure is used to treat pressure on the ulnar nerve around the elbow, which can cause numbness and weakness in the hand.
Barker said he wanted to deal with the issue so he could continue playing drums for a long time. He offered an optimistic update on his recovery, saying he expected to be back to normal within a few weeks.
His update came one day after Barker shared hospital photos featuring his family. In one image, his daughter Alabama Barker was beside him, while another showed his wife Kourtney Kardashian supporting him at the hospital.
At the time, Barker did not explain why he was there, leaving fans waiting for further information. His later message clarified that the visit was connected to the nerve problem affecting his arm and hand.
Barker has previously faced other medical issues connected to his work and health. In 2023, he revealed that he had injured his ring finger during a rehearsal, dislocating it and tearing ligaments. He subsequently required surgery for the injury.
The procedure marks another setback for the musician, but his comments suggest he remains focused on returning to drumming. Barker has not indicated that the issue will affect any upcoming Blink 182 commitments.
His update reassured fans who had been concerned after seeing him in hospital clothing and preparing for surgery.

title: Andrew Scott says films should keep addressing AIDS crisis and calls out governments
description: Scott praised HIV and AIDS consultant Dr Margaret Johnson for her contribution to treatment
content:
Scott praised HIV and AIDS consultant Dr Margaret Johnson for her contribution to treatment
Andrew Scott has urged filmmakers to keep addressing the AIDS crisis, arguing that stories about darker chapters of LGBTQ history remain important despite the rise of more joyful queer films and television shows.
Speaking after the European premiere of Elsinore at the LONDON FILM FESTIVAL, Scott welcomed shows including Heartstopper and Heated Rivalry . However, he said he was troubled by reluctance to revisit periods when gay people faced discrimination and the AIDS crisis carried stigma.
Scott said that reluctance could come from shame, but stressed that shame should not be placed on gay people. He instead pointed towards governments that ignored the AIDS crisis and prejudice surrounding people living with HIV and AIDS.
“The shame lies with the governments who ignored the AIDS crisis and the stigma that was around people and the innate prejudice that was in society,” Scott said, according to Variety .
Elsinore , directed by Simon Stone and written by Stephen Beresford, centres on Scottish actor Ian Charleson, played by Scott. Charleson was known for Chariots of Fire and for playing Hamlet at the National Theatre.
In 1989, while living with complications from AIDS, Charleson replaced Daniel Day Lewis in the production after the actor left. Charleson received strong reviews for his performance but died seven weeks after bowing out.
Following the premiere, Scott brought real life figures depicted in the film onto the stage, including National Theatre staff members Linda Tolhurst and Ralph Mills, director Sean Mathias and HIV and AIDS consultant Dr Margaret Johnson.
Scott praised Johnson for her contribution to the development of treatment for people living with HIV and AIDS, calling her a “true life hero”.
Elsinore previously premiered at TELLURIDE FILM FESTIVAL and has received early reviews. Backed by Studiocanal, the film is expected during awards season as audiences revisit Charleson’s story today.

title: Senior US Embassy official in Jerusalem suppressed diplomatic cables to shield Netanyahu govt  report
description: David Milstein  a senior US Embassy aide repeatedly blocked assessments meant for top policymakers  an inquiry found
content:
David Milstein, a senior US Embassy aide, repeatedly blocked assessments meant for top policymakers
A top adviser to the US ambassador to Israel had systematically suppressed, delayed and rewritten internal diplomatic cables to shield the government of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from scrutiny by Washington, The New York Times reported on Thursday.
David Milstein, an influential gatekeeper at the US Embassy in Jerusalem since April 2025 and principal aide to US Ambassador Mike Huckabee, repeatedly stymied assessments intended for senior policymakers, according to an investigation based on interviews with more than a dozen US officials and reviews of internal State Department records.
In late March, Israel approved record-breaking occupation expansions across the occupied West Bank. Embassy personnel drafted an alert warning that the move risked violating US President Donald Trump's explicit red line against annexation. Milstein quashed the memorandum, framing the land acquisitions as a domestic matter before sending a revised text claiming the move addressed unspecified humanitarian needs of occupiers.
Read More: Israel strikes Gaza on October 7 anniversary, at least two dead: officials
Milstein similarly altered reporting on surging violence in the occupied West Bank. When Israeli military commanders warned that attacks by occupiers could trigger a widespread Palestinian uprising, he blocked the dispatches suggesting that Israel failed to take action. Instead, an embassy cable authored under his name praised Netanyahu's initiatives and claimed authorities were actively combatting the unrest.
The aide also suppressed a detailed embassy inquiry into the killings of nine Palestinian Americans by Israeli forces and occupiers, effectively thwarting accountability requests from members of the US Congress. Despite findings showing investigations stalled without criminal charges, the mission forwarded an alternative letter claiming active cooperation with Israeli authorities.
Milstein also edited dispatches regarding aid distribution by the US-backed Gaza Humanitarian Foundation to describe the operations as successful, removing diplomatic warnings that the process was "chaotic, deadly," and risked "mass casualty events".
Staff members noted that the interventions caused reporting from the embassy's Palestinian affairs section to drop from several weekly cables to a few per month and prompted some officials to bypass official embassy channels to obtain unfiltered ground intelligence.
"The elements of the story The New York Times is trying to assemble are so lacking in fact that it ranks up with other Times farcical endeavours," said Huckabee. The US State Department said its personnel remain focused on advancing the administration's foreign policy priorities.

25-day event to feature over 1,000 foreign, 500 Pakistani artists; 80% of programmes to be free
For 25 days, Karachi will become a meeting point for artists from across the globe as the World Culture Festival returns with its third edition, bringing more than 1,000 international performers and over 500 Pakistani artists to the city.
According to a statement by the Arts Council President Ahmad Shah on Thursday, the festival, jointly organised by the Arts Council of Pakistan Karachi and the Sindh government, will run from October 29 to November 22.
Artists from around 150 countries are expected to participate in the festival, which organisers say is aimed at using culture as a bridge between people and promoting a message of peace.
“The World Culture Festival has become an important reference point for Pakistan’s cultural identity,” Shah said. He added that the scale of international participation has grown sharply since the festival was launched. While 43 countries participated in its first edition, the second brought artists from 144 countries, according to Shah.
This year, the festival will feature artists from six continents, including the United States, Iran, Iraq, Palestine and countries across Latin America. Two Palestinian theatre groups will also participate, Shah said, adding that several members of the groups had been killed.
Shah said the festival was not simply about staging performances but about using culture as a form of diplomacy. “We decided to use cultural diplomacy to remove misconceptions about Pakistan, Sindh and Karachi,” he said, adding that foreign artists and delegates were being invited so they could experience the country firsthand and take a positive message back home.
Shah further emphasised that the festival will bring together theatre, music, dance, film, folk and other art forms under one platform, where Pakistani artists from Sindh, Punjab, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan, Kashmir and the Seraiki belt will perform alongside international artists.
Fusion performances involving Pakistani and foreign artists will also be staged, while Sindh’s traditional music and instruments, including the algoza and borindo, will receive special attention. A special Mehran Night will showcase Sindh’s cultural heritage, while the Shah Latif Voices Festival will also be launched.
Shah said international artists had shown particular interest in Pakistan’s traditional instruments, adding that the festival would provide opportunities for greater cultural exchange.
According to the statement, Sindh Chief Secretary Syed Asif Haider Shah stressed that the government wanted to expand the cultural activity beyond the Arts Council and turn the surrounding area into an “Art Village”. He said the KMC, town administration, Water Board, deputy commissioner’s office and other institutions were working on the initiative.
"Road improvements, lighting, benches, food facilities and pedestrian pathways were being developed, with the aim of completing the work before winter. The Arts Council, museums and other cultural venues would eventually form part of an integrated cultural environment," he said.
Special teams were also working on security, traffic and arrangements for receiving foreign delegations, while federal ministries were extending their cooperation. Sindh Culture and Tourism Minister Syed Zulfiqar Ali Shah said all relevant provincial departments had been mobilised for the festival, with coordination also under way with the Civil Aviation Authority, ASF, police and other security agencies.
The minister described the festival as an important vehicle for projecting Pakistan’s soft image. “Pakistan was previously associated with the image of terrorism, but cultural festivals are helping present its positive and cultural identity to the world,” he said.
He added that the festival’s broader objective was to promote love, tolerance and peace by bringing people and cultures together. “The fundamental objective is to bring people closer through culture and convey a message of peace,” Shah said.
The minister further said the number of foreign tourists visiting Pakistan’s tourist destinations had increased by around 50% over the past three years, with cultural activities contributing to the trend.
Around 80% of the festival’s programmes will be free, although advance registration will be required, while tickets will be charged for six to eight major mega concerts, offering visitors a mix of accessible cultural events and large-scale entertainment.

title: Amazon launches first Android tablets  raising prices and incorporating Alexa
description: New tablets will cost up to  550  far above Amazon s previous top end Fire HD 10 price of  180
content:
New tablets will cost up to $550, far above Amazon's previous top-end Fire HD 10 price of $180
Amazon on Thursday unveiled a slate of higher-end tablets that for ​the first time feature its Alexa+ voice assistant and run on Google's Android operating system, a bet that consumers will pay ‌more for premium devices after years of focusing on the budget end of the market.
Seattle-based Amazon had been working on the tablets under the code name Kittyhawk , as Reuters reported exclusively last year, to transition away from its more limited homegrown Fire OS operating system software, after years of gripes from consumers and app developers. Fire OS is a “forked” version ​of Android, with modifications to make it work like a unique operating system.
Known as Alexa Tablets, the line features several different versions with ​starting prices from $230 to $500; all are made with aluminum cases, a switch from Fire tablets’ plastic.
The new tablets ⁠will cost as much as $550, a big bump from Amazon’s more recent top-of-the-line Fire HD 10 tablet which cost upwards of $180, though the company often ​discounted them.
The top Alexa tablet, with 128 gigabytes of memory, for $550 compares with an Apple iPad for $450 and Samsung's Galaxy tablet for $550.
Read More: US suspends Microsoft, major IT firms from key green card programme
The product revamp marks a ​new strategy under devices chief Panos Panay to move upscale and away from the inexpensive gadgets Amazon sold at or near cost to hook customers into using Prime Video, Kindle, music apps and the main e-commerce website. That focus on affordability came with compromises, like lower screen quality and battery life, compared with rivals Apple and Samsung and others.
Alexa+, an ​advanced AI-powered version of the Alexa voice assistant, will feature prominently on the devices to help perform actions or answer questions using generative AI. Accessing Alexa+ ​on the tablets will require a Prime membership or Alexa+ subscription, Amazon said.
Amazon is pushing the pricier devices as worldwide tablet sales are falling, down 12% in the second ‌quarter from ⁠the year before to 33.6 million units, according to IDC data. The US market, which has been especially hurt by a shortage of memory chips, saw sales plunge 32% in the second quarter year over year, IDC data showed.
The Seattle company held just 1.9% of the global tablet market in this year’s second quarter, down from 8% a year earlier, according to IDC. Apple is the leader with 34%, followed by Samsung at 17.5%.
The tablet prices do not include ​a one-time fee customers have to pay ​to turn off advertising displayed ⁠on the lockscreen, though the highest-priced Alexa Tablet will not have the ads. It will require a one-time $20 fee to eliminate the ads, up from $15 for Fire OS tablets, a spokesperson said. Such ads help users “discover new content that’s relevant ​to their interests” and the revenue helps underwrite other innovations, the spokesperson said.
With Android, Alexa ​Tablet customers won’t be ⁠limited to the apps offered in the Fire OS app store, disdained by developers who had to make a third version of apps offered in the Google Play and Apple stores. And the built-in Alexa+ voice AI assistant helps to differentiate the tablets from others.
Amazon has spent billions overhauling Alexa to power it with generative ⁠AI and ​make it more capable for connected homes , shopping and accessing third-party services like Uber and Grubhub. ​The service, free with a Prime membership, is unprofitable.
Prior Fire OS tablets will still work, said the spokesperson, but she did not say whether Amazon will continue to maintain the operating system or ​app store. Earlier this year Amazon cut off support for older Kindle models, citing software maintenance costs as a reason.

title: Turkiye s FM Fidan maintains Makkah pact is  defensive  in nature  will not send troops
description: Says Turkiye has  completed preparations to submit the Makkah  defence agreement to parliament for approval
content:
Says Turkiye has completed preparations to submit the Makkah defence agreement to parliament for approval
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Thursday that Turkiye would not send troops to confront Yemen’s Houthis, while stressing that the Makkah defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan was "defensive", not offensive in nature and did not authorise attacks on other countries.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed Makkah pact, a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
Speaking at a joint ​press conference with his Hungarian counterpart Anita Orban in Ankara, Fidan said that the Makkah agreement provided for mutual defence if one of its signatories came under attack, further clarifying that the pact did not authorise Turkiye to deploy troops to another country's territory to carry out an attack.
LIVE: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan holds a joint press conference with Hungarian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Anita Orban in Ankara https://t.co/yKVJhCOQYF
"But this is a defensive agreement. When a country party ​to the pact comes under attack, you stand by it in its defence. This is not an offensive ‌agreement. ⁠Turkiye will not send troops to another country to carry out attacks on its territory," he said.
"Yemen's legitimate government forces are already continuing the battle on the ground, and Saudi Arabia ​is supporting them. But at the same time, we are doing everything we can to help resolve the issue through peace and dialogue," Fidan added.
The Turkish FM underlined that military officials were assessing possible contributions, particularly in air defence, electronic warfare and technical support, further noting that they would determine Saudi Arabia's operational defence needs and what contributions Turkiye and Pakistan could make.
On Wednesday, two officials told Reuters that Turkiye was sending mainly defensive ​and technical support to ​Saudi Arabia to help ⁠its fight with Houthis.
Turkiye officials have said any support provided at this stage would largely be in a bilateral capacity, as ​Turkiye's parliament had not officially ratified the joint defence pact.
Fidan further stated that Turkiye had completed preparations to submit the Makkah defence agreement to parliament for approval. "The necessary work for the agreement to be submitted to parliament has been completed."
Turkish FM Hakan Fidan says Türkiye is assessing defence support for Saudi Arabia, particularly air defence, as the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan moves toward parliamentary approval and institutional implementation pic.twitter.com/rFZ3y2DFCJ
He said he made a final presentation on the matter to Turkiye President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Wednesday and that Turkiye had decided to send the agreement to parliament as soon as possible.
Fidan said Turkiye's participation in the October 5 meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee of the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence in Riyadh was primarily prompted by attacks targeting Saudi Arabia.
He said the extraordinary meeting also addressed several institutional issues, including the structure of the military headquarters, the status of the secretariat and the appointment of a new secretary.
Although the agreement was signed relatively recently, Fidan said institutionalisation and practical steps had advanced rapidly.
“The parties are showing through their determination that they are serious about this and want to see concrete results,” he said.
Fidan said the meeting also discussed possible Turkish contributions to Saudi Arabia's defence against attacks by Yemen's Houthi group.
Turkish FM Fidan: - Türkiye is working on possible technical support for Saudi Arabia against attacks from Yemen - Türkiye is not sending troops to carry out attacks on another country's land - Mecca agreement is a defence pact, not an offensive alliance pic.twitter.com/3s6TAHJcu8
Turkiye, which has NATO's second-largest army and a robust ⁠defence industry, ​has condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, voiced willingness ​to help meet Riyadh's technical military needs, and agreed to join a Saudi-led coalition to ensure navigational safety ​in the Red Sea.
Fidan’s remarks came after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye activated the practical implementation of their collective defence commitments on Monday.
Read : Makkah defence alliance agrees to 'rapid force deployment' in Saudi Arabia: FO
According to a joint statement issued on Monday night, the activation entailed immediate deployment of "the agreed military forces and capabilities to the kingdom in response to security threats".
The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of the Strategic-Political and Defence Committee of the alliance, held in Riyadh to discuss the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia is currently engaged in an active conflict with Houthis, who have been targeting the various strategic and economic assets in the kingdom.
On Wednesday, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said that Pakistani troops were present in Saudi Arabia in "multiple capabilities" amid the kingdom's conflict with Yemen's Houthis and developments related to it.
Read More : Makkah pact: DG ISPR says Pakistani troops present in Saudi Arabia in 'multiple capabilities'
In an interview with CNN, the military spokesperson was questioned about whether Pakistani military personnel were present in the kingdom as part of the Makkah Defence Alliance, to which he said: "I do confirm that the forces of Pakistan are already there ... the Pakistani troops have been there for decades in multiple capabilities."
The DG ISPR reiterated that forces were present in "multiple domains" in the kingdom.
The Makkah pact was the latest step in longstanding military and strategic cooperation between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. Signed in Makkah, the pact established a framework for collective deterrence and stipulated that an armed attack on any one of the three countries would be considered an attack on all three, while providing for wider cooperation across defence.
The agreement followed nearly a year of negotiations and came amid heightened instability across the Middle East. Turkiye and Pakistan had sought closer regional security cooperation, while Saudi Arabia had faced growing security concerns as conflicts spread across the region, threatening its territory, energy infrastructure and ambitious economic development plans.
For Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the trilateral pact is built on their Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed in September 2025. That agreement stated that “any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both” and committed the two sides to strengthening defence cooperation and joint deterrence.

title: Sebastian Stan warns    Avengers  Doomsday    could be heartbreaking for Marvel fans
description: Stan says reuniting with longtime Marvel co stars felt nostalgic during filming
content:
Stan says reuniting with longtime Marvel co stars felt nostalgic during filming
Sebastian Stan has offered fans an ominous glimpse at Avengers: Doomsday , saying he expects the upcoming Marvel film to be “probably heartbreaking” while admitting he has not seen the finished movie yet.
Speaking with Decider while promoting his new film Fjord , Stan said he does not know how Doomsday turned out. “I haven’t seen the movie, and I don’t know how it turned out,” he said. “I’m sure it’s going to be probably heartbreaking, in a lot of ways. We’ll see who makes it to the next level.”
Stan’s comments have sparked speculation among Marvel fans about whether the film could feature character deaths. However, his remarks do not confirm that any particular character will die, and he has not revealed plot details.
The actor, who returns as Bucky Barnes, also reflected on reuniting with his Marvel co stars during production. Stan said he “got a chance to reunite with everyone” and described the experience as “very nostalgic”, recalling the years they have spent working together.
“It’s been a family and it never stops being that way,” Stan said.
Avengers: Doomsday brings together a large group of Marvel characters, with Chris Hemsworth, Anthony Mackie, Vanessa Kirby, Letitia Wright, Paul Rudd, Florence Pugh and others among the cast. Robert Downey Jr is also returning to the franchise, this time as Doctor Doom.
Chris Evans is also set to appear, marking his return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe after his Captain America story appeared to conclude with Avengers: Endgame .
Directed by Anthony and Joe Russo, Doomsday is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on December 18. The film is expected to set up the next major chapter of the MCU, but Stan offers no confirmation about who survives.

title: Taylor Swift leads 2026 Kids    Choice Awards nominations as Alex Warren set to host
description: Swift has earned six nods  followed by Ariana Grande and Sabrina Carpenter with five nominations
content:
Swift has earned six nods, followed by Ariana Grande and Sabrina Carpenter with five nominations
Taylor Swift leads the nominations for the 2026 Kids’ Choice Awards, while Grammy-nominated singer Alex Warren has been announced as the host of this year’s ceremony.
The nominations were revealed on October 8, with Swift earning six nods, followed by Ariana Grande and Sabrina Carpenter with five nominations each. The annual awards ceremony, which celebrates children’s favourite stars, films, television shows, music, gaming and creators, will take place live from Los Angeles on Saturday, November 14.
Swift is nominated across several categories, including Favourite Female Artist, Favourite Song for The Fate of Ophelia , Favourite Music Collaboration for The Life of a Showgirl with Sabrina Carpenter, Favourite Album for The Life of a Showgirl and Favourite Global Music Star for North America.
Grande’s nominations include Favourite Female Artist, Favourite Movie Actress for Wicked: For Good , Favourite Song for “hate that i made you love me”, Favourite Song from a Movie for “For Good” with Cynthia Erivo and Favourite Music Collaboration for “The Life of a Showgirl” with Swift and Carpenter. Carpenter is also nominated for Favourite Female Artist, Favourite Breakout Artist/Group, Favourite Song for “Manchild”, Favourite Music Collaboration and Favourite Album for Man’s Best Friend .
The film categories feature several major releases, including Avatar: Fire and Ash , How to Train Your Dragon , Jurassic World Rebirth , Lilo & Stitch , Moana , Spider-Man: Brand New Day , Superman and Wicked: For Good in the Favourite Movie category.
On television, Wednesday , Stranger Things , Percy Jackson and the Olympians , Abbott Elementary , Ginny & Georgia and XO, Kitty are among the nominated shows. Meanwhile, KPop Demon Hunters , The Super Mario Galaxy Movie , Toy Story 5 and Zootopia 2 feature in the animated categories.
The 2026 ceremony will also introduce three new categories: Watch Party: Kids’ Choice, Favourite On-Screen Duo/Trio and Favourite Clutch Player of the Year. The latter category includes athletes such as Caleb Williams, Eileen Gu, Freddie Freeman, Hilary Knight, Jack Hughes, Jalen Brunson, Nelly Korda and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.
Warren, who earned his Grammy nomination for his breakout hit Ordinary , will take over hosting duties for the ceremony. Musical performances and additional celebrity appearances will be announced at a later date.
Fans can vote across all 36 categories, putting the final results in the hands of the Kids’ Choice Awards audience. The ceremony will air live on CBS and Nickelodeon for the first time, while Paramount+ Premium subscribers in the US will also be able to stream the event live.

title: Mia Goth seeks sole custody of daughter Isabel in divorce filing with Shia LaBeouf
description: Goth is also asking the court to deny spousal support to both parties
content:
Goth is also asking the court to deny spousal support to both parties
Mia Goth has asked a Los Angeles court for sole legal and physical custody of her four year old daughter, Isabel, as part of her divorce proceedings involving Shia LaBeouf.
The actress filed for divorce on October 6, citing irreconcilable differences and listing July 28, 2025, as the date the couple separated. According to court documents obtained by PEOPLE , Goth is requesting sole legal and physical custody while asking that LaBeouf receive visitation with their daughter.
The custody request puts Isabel at the centre of proceedings following their split. It was reported that Isabel has lived with Goth since the separation, while LaBeouf later moved to New Orleans.
Goth and LaBeouf welcomed Isabel in 2022 after reconnecting following years of an on and off relationship. They first met while working on Lars von Trier’s Nymphomaniac: Vol. II in 2012 and held a Las Vegas wedding ceremony in 2016. Officials later said the ceremony was not legally binding.
Goth has previously spoken warmly about her relationship with Isabel. In an October 2025 interview with ELLE , she described motherhood as a "psychedelic experience" and called her daughter "the greatest gift of my life". She also said she hoped to be a steady presence for Isabel and wanted her daughter to always have a home and somewhere to turn.
LaBeouf pleaded guilty in June 2026 to misdemeanor battery charges linked to a February Mardi Gras altercation in New Orleans. He was sentenced to two years of probation and ordered to complete alcohol rehabilitation, sensitivity training and anger management classes.
Goth’s divorce petition does not publicly state a specific reason for her custody request. Her filing also asks that neither party receive spousal support.
The custody matter will form part of the proceedings as Goth seeks to establish legal and physical custody arrangements for Isabel.

title: Which Warner Bros movies will survive Skydance   s big shake up

content:
Skydance’s Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein will oversee Warner Bros’ slate, including Barbie 2 and Batman Part II
Skydance Pictures executives Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein are set to oversee Warner Bros’ upcoming theatrical slate as the studio prepares for a new era following the Paramount-Warner Bros merger.
Among the projects expected to receive close attention is Barbie 2 , which remains a major priority for the new leadership. Warner Bros is hoping Greta Gerwig will return to direct and co-write the sequel with Noah Baumbach, while Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling are expected to reprise their roles.
The new leadership will also assess projects at various stages of production and development. The Warner Bros slate includes major franchises such as Dune: Part Three , Godzilla x Kong: Supernova , The Conjuring: First Communion and The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum .
James Gunn’s Man of Tomorrow , the follow-up to Superman , is also in post-production, while The Batman Part II is in production but currently paused. The sequel is scheduled for release in February 2028.
Other films in production include an untitled Ocean’s prequel starring Bradley Cooper and Robbie, a new Nancy Meyers film featuring Owen Wilson, Jude Law, Kieran Culkin and Erin Doherty, and several animated projects.
Warner Bros is also developing potential franchise titles including Matrix 5 , Gremlins 3 , Constantine 2 , Goonies 2 and a live-action Hot Wheels movie.
Skydance co-CEO David Ellison has said the company remains committed to both franchise films and original storytelling. Meanwhile, Warner Bros and Paramount are expected to operate as separate creative studios while coordinating their release schedules.
The new leadership will ultimately determine which Warner Bros projects move forward as the combined company balances its extensive film pipeline with financial pressures.

title: Verstappen out to settle  unfinished business  at Singapore Grand Prix
description: Red Bull driver eyes his maiden victory at the circuit
content:
Red Bull driver eyes his maiden victory at the circuit
Max Verstappen said Thursday he was determined to settle his "unfinished business" at the Singapore Grand Prix, where he has never won.
The Red Bull driver took his first victory of 2026 at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last weekend, the 72nd time that he has stood on the top step of the podium in a career that has brought him four world titles.
But none of those wins have come in Singapore where a bumpy track, slow corners and high humidity seem to favour other cars.
The Dutchman would love to break his long losing streak at the Marina Bay Circuit.
"I think in the last few years we have always been bad at low speed and over kerbing and bumps," Verstappen told reporters.
"This car is probably more competitive at low speed, but we still struggle on bumps and kerbs. We know that and so, of course, I have unfinished business here."
He finished second last year behind the Mercedes of George Russell and believes he can go one better and complete back-to-back victories in steamy southeast Asia.
"Every year I come back here and I'm trying to win it. I hope we can be a little more competitive this year compared to the last few years."
With a sprint race in Singapore this year, it means there is only one Friday practice session for the drivers and teams to get up to speed.
"It's always hectic, a sprint weekend, to make the right choices," said Verstappen.
"The most important thing is just to find a good balance with the car straight away. That will help a lot for the rest of the weekend."

title: Bangladesh aim to keep progress in WTC
description: They will face Afghanistan in a one off Test
content:
They will face Afghanistan in a one-off Test
Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto targets further improvement in the five-day format as they meet Afghanistan in a one-off Test starting in Abu Dhabi from Friday.
Bangladesh upset Australia by nine wickets at Darwin in August before losing the second Test to draw the two-match series 1-1, an outcome that was seen as a huge step forward for the visitors.
The win lifted Bangladesh to fourth place in the nine-team World Test Championship (WTC) and gives them a good chance to play next year's final.
Although the Test against Afghanistan is not included in the WTC, Shanto said his team was ready for the challenge.
"We had a very good series in Australia but I believe that is past now," Shanto said at Sheikh Zayed Stadium on Thursday.
"This is a new opponent and different conditions so we must progress further."
A win will further boost Bangladesh's confidence as they host the West Indies later this month, tour South Africa in November and host England in February next year.
Afghanistan also hopes to improve their Test record under new captain Rahmat Shah, having won just four of the 13 Tests they have played since gaining Test status in 2017. They have lost eight and drawn one.
When they last met Bangladesh in Dhaka three years ago it resulted in a heavy 546-run defeat. But they won their other Test against Bangladesh by 224 runs in 2019.
Afghanistan will sorely miss their ace spinner Rashid Khan, who was not selected for the Test on medical advice to give his back some rest ahead of important white-ball matches.
Bangladesh will be without their fast-rising pacer Naheed Rana for a second consecutive series as he recovers from a side strain.
The pitch at Zayed Stadium is on the slow side, bringing spinners into the equation early with high temperatures of 40 degrees Celsius (104 Fahrenheit) expected.

title: Farhan hopes Pakistan s new combination takes off in Sri Lanka T20Is
description: He says the Green shirts are ready to embrace the challenge after a shake up of their T20 setup
content:
He says the Green-shirts are ready to embrace the challenge after a shake-up of their T20 setup
Pakistan captain Sahibzada Farhan hopes a new combination without star players Babar Azam and Shaheen Shah Afridi will come good against Sri Lanka in their Twenty20 International series starting in Rawalpindi on Friday.
The three-match series will see Farhan take on the skipper's role after leading a second-string side to silver at the Asian Games in Japan, losing to India in the final last week.
Also missing from the squad are former T20I skipper Salman Agha and wicketkeeper-batter Mohammad Rizwan, part of an exodus aimed at building the side for the 2028 T20I World Cup in Australia and New Zealand.
"I am confident that this new combination is the best and will settle in this series," said Farhan on Thursday.
"I know how to lead the side and I will not take pressure."
Azam's form had dipped in T20Is, and he was also dropped from Pakistan's final match against Sri Lanka at the Twenty20 World Cup in February.
Shaheen is also out of favour for T20Is but will skipper Pakistan's one-day international side in a tri-series with Sri Lanka and England starting in Rawalpindi from October 18.
Sri Lanka are also in a transition phase with star leg-spinner Wanindu Hasaranga and former skipper Charith Asalanka dropped for the tour.
Hasaranga is joint-fifth in the all-time T20I wicket-taking list with 163 in 101 games.
"Unfortunately, Wanindu is still injured, and we will miss him but we have a few other exciting players who I am sure will stand up and perform," said Sri Lankan skipper Kusal Mendis.
"I think everyone knows how to play in Pakistan," said Mendis, who played in the Pakistan Super League (PSL) earlier this year.
"Pakistan also have some new faces but their players are good and we know some of them from the PSL, so I hope our players will do well."
The series will be the ninth bilateral T20I series between Pakistan and Sri Lanka and the 250th international cricket fixture between the two countries.
Pakistan have dominated their head-to-head record in the format, winning 18 of their 30 T20Is against Sri Lanka. The islanders have won 12.
Of the previous eight bilateral T20I series, Pakistan have won four and three have ended level. Sri Lanka's only series victory came in 2019, when they completed a 3-0 sweep in Lahore.
The opening match will be played at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium, with the second and third games scheduled at the same venue on October 11 and 13.

title: US suspends Microsoft  major IT firms from key green card programme
description: US to suspend Cognizant  Infosys  Tata  Wipro  HCL and Capgemini from key green card programme
content:
US to suspend Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini from key green card programme
The US government is suspending Microsoft, Adobe and several large IT firms from a programme that allows skilled foreign workers to gain permanent residency, senior US officials announced on Thursday, citing alleged fraud and an effort to push companies to hire more Americans.
"Our message to Microsoft is: You're a great American company, but you've got to hire great American workers," US Vice President JD Vance said.
Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling added that some of the largest IT firms in the world would also be suspended from the programme, including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini.
"We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labor certification applications involving these companies," Sonderling said.

title: Mike Tyson says he   s grateful for his troubled past despite addiction  prison and personal loss
description: Everything that was quote unquote    negative     turned out to be a positive for me     Tyson said
content:
“Everything that was quote-unquote ‘negative,’ turned out to be a positive for me,” Tyson said
Mike Tyson says he is grateful for the difficult experiences that shaped his life, despite the years he spent battling addiction, facing personal tragedies and serving time in prison.
The former heavyweight boxing champion, now 60, reflected on his turbulent past in an exclusive interview with PEOPLE ahead of the release of TYSON , a four-part Netflix docuseries exploring his career and personal life.
“I just don’t understand why they still want to know about me,” Tyson said, admitting that revisiting parts of his life can be uncomfortable. The documentary looks at everything from his childhood in poverty and numerous arrests to his rise as heavyweight champion and the controversies that followed his success.
Tyson’s life has also been marked by significant personal losses, including the deaths of his mother, trainer Cus D’Amato and his four-year-old daughter. The series also revisits his struggles with cocaine and alcohol addiction, his marriage to Robin Givens, financial problems and the rape conviction that resulted in a two-year prison sentence, which Tyson has always denied.
Despite those experiences, Tyson says he now looks at his past differently. He has been free from alcohol and cocaine for 10 years and said the memories of what happened remain with him, even though he considers the past to be behind him.
“Everything that was quote-unquote ‘negative,’ turned out to be a positive for me,” Tyson said. “I’m very grateful for it all because it made me a better person. Everything bad that happened to me, I’m grateful for.”
Tyson also reflected on the influence of D’Amato, who discovered him after he took a boxing class while in juvenile detention. D’Amato later became his legal guardian and helped Tyson develop both his boxing abilities and confidence.
“He gave me confidence. He gave me character. He made me believe in myself and what I could do,” Tyson said, crediting his former trainer with helping him move away from a life of crime and focus on becoming a champion.
The documentary also revisits some of Tyson’s most infamous moments, including his 1997 fight with Evander Holyfield, when he bit his opponent’s ear twice. Tyson said he remains embarrassed by the incident despite the public fascination with it.
TYSON will explore the highs and lows of Tyson’s life and career, with the four-part series set to begin streaming on Netflix on October 13.

A K-Electric representative, Rabia, also appeared on behalf of Managing Director Syed Muhammad Talha and submitted a sealed envelope, which was taken on record.
Justice Sial thanked and commended Talha for his “prompt and effective” response to the commission’s request.
The commission’s email and WhatsApp accounts have now been deactivated, while the Rs100,000 reward announced earlier has also been withdrawn, the order said.
In his concluding remarks, Justice Sial thanked Sindh Chief Justice Zafar Ahmed Rajput for entrusting him with the responsibility of heading the commission.
He also acknowledged the support extended by Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah and Home Minister Zia Ul Hassan Lanjar, describing their cooperation as unwavering and complete.

title: Living voters branded dead in India s Karnataka electoral purge
description: Expelled BJP MLA Basanagouda Patil Yatnal sought deletion of 1 054 voters in Vijayapura on Aug 31
content:
Expelled BJP MLA Basanagouda Patil Yatnal sought deletion of 1,054 voters in Vijayapura on Aug 31
They were alive, eligible to vote and still living at the addresses listed on their electoral records. Yet, in Karnataka’s ongoing revision of electoral rolls, eight voters were allegedly marked dead and targeted for deletion — six of them Muslim women.
The cases have surfaced in Vijayapura, where expelled BJP MLA Basanagouda Patil Yatnal submitted a list seeking the deletion of 1,054 voters on August 31, barely a week after the draft electoral rolls were published on August 24.
According to activists and the affected voters, the deletion requests were supported by death certificates that matched the voters’ names but carried different details, including the names of parents or spouses and addresses.
Also Read: India detains several in Gen Z voter protests
The victims include Malanbi Jamadar, 57; Mahabubi Peerazade Jahagirdar, 35; and Raziya Mehrunnisa Sheikh, 35, a resident of Ward-22, Langar Bazaar.
Government teacher Allama Bagwan, along with Abdul Razak Bagwan and Mumtaj Mulla, were also among those reportedly listed for deletion.
Activist Irfan Sheikh said the eight voters whose cases had been identified were alive and that the remaining 1,046 names on the list were also being verified.
The controversy has raised fresh questions over the use of bulk applications to remove voters from electoral rolls, particularly in constituencies with sizeable Muslim populations.
The allegations emerged during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, a nationwide exercise being overseen by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Activists claim more than 4,000 bulk Form-7 applications — the form used to request deletion of names from electoral rolls — have been submitted across Karnataka, with a significant number targeting Muslim voters.
In Babaleshwar alone, 1,373 Form-7 applications were reportedly submitted on September 22. Of these, 1,363 applications were allegedly filed by just 10 people.
The developments triggered protests outside the Vijayapura Deputy Commissioner’s office, while affected women and activists later held a press conference organised by Jagrutha Karnataka in Bengaluru.
The women demanded criminal cases against Yatnal, accusing him of attempting to facilitate the wrongful removal of legitimate voters from the electoral rolls.
District Electoral Officer K Anand ordered an inquiry after preliminary scrutiny found that some of the death certificates submitted with the deletion requests appeared to belong to people with the same names as the voters or raised questions about their authenticity.
The findings have intensified concerns over whether electoral safeguards were followed before deletion requests were submitted or processed.
Under electoral procedures, objections seeking deletion of a voter’s name are subject to verification. The use of allegedly mismatched death certificates has therefore become a central issue in the Vijayapura controversy.
Yatnal has defended the electoral revision process and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He has also publicly alleged that "Muslims are the bogus voters”, a claim that has drawn criticism from activists who say the ongoing exercise risks disproportionately disenfranchising Muslim citizens.
The Vijayapura cases have become a flashpoint in the wider debate over the SIR, with activists warning that wrongful deletions could deprive eligible citizens of their constitutional right to vote.
For the affected women, however, the issue is more immediate: they remain alive, but their names were placed on a list that sought to treat them as though they were not.

Joe Rogan renews his Spotify deal, with the podcast host reportedly set to earn $250 million over the new contract
Joe Rogan has renewed his partnership with Spotify through a new multiyear licensing agreement covering his popular podcast, The Joe Rogan Experience .

Jordan Newman, Spotify’s head of content partnerships, said Rogan had built an enduring show that continues to attract a large global audience.
The Joe Rogan Experience remains one of the world’s most popular podcasts. It ranked as the No. 1 most-listened-to podcast on Spotify, YouTube and Apple Podcasts in 2025. The show has 18 million followers on Spotify and has remained the platform’s most-followed podcast since the partnership began in 2020.
Rogan launched The Joe Rogan Experience in December 2009. The podcast has since released more than 2,500 episodes, featuring guests from entertainment, sports, science, business and other fields.
The podcast has also made Rogan a prominent and sometimes controversial figure because of his political commentary and views.

Prince Harry has spoken about experiencing depression after moving to Canada with Meghan Markle and their son Archie in late 2019.
Speaking during a new MasterClass, Harry, 42, described the effect of leaving what he called a stressful environment after stepping down as a senior working royal. His comments were reported by People.
“Being in Canada, away from the stressful environment where presumably my body was just pumped full of adrenaline, within two or three days, I experienced this adrenaline crash, something that I’d never experienced before,” Harry said. “It was as if I needed stress in order to get the adrenaline to make my brain function because I became useless around the house.”

The couple subsequently returned to England in August, with their children expected to attend school locally.

A source told Us Weekly , that Harry was “not as happy” in the United States and that the family was “open to a new chapter”.

title: Information ministry rubbishes  fake and fabricated  NYT report claiming use of PAF aircraft against Houthis
description: Says details of any employment  if necessary  will be given by concerned authorities
content:
Says details of any employment, if necessary, will be given by concerned authorities
The information ministry on Thursday rubbished what it said was a "fake and fabricated" report by The New York Times claiming that Pakistan Air Force (PAF) aircraft had been used against the Houthis amid the group's escalating conflict with Saudi Arabia.
The New York Times report published on October 7 cited an unnamed source as claiming that PAF fighter jets were being deployed against the Houthis amid tensions between the group and Saudi Arabia.
Sharing a screenshot of the NYT report in a post on X, the ministry stated that it was "fake and fabricated".
The ministry added that international media houses were "again asked to avoid speculative reporting with regards to employment of Pakistan's military forces under Makkah Joint Defence Agreement".

It further said that details of any employment, if necessary, would be given by the "concerned authorities".
The statement also came a day after Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said that Pakistani troops were present in Saudi Arabia in "multiple capabilities" amid the kingdom's conflict with Yemen's Houthis and developments related to it.
Read : Makkah pact: DG ISPR says Pakistani troops present in Saudi Arabia in 'multiple capabilities'
In an interview with CNN, the military spokesperson was questioned about whether Pakistani military personnel were present in the kingdom as part of the Makkah Defence Alliance, to which he said: "I do confirm that the forces of Pakistan are already there ... the Pakistani troops have been there for decades in multiple capabilities."
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed Makkah pact, a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
In a major development that may have far-reaching implications for the region, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye activated the practical implementation of their collective defence commitments on Monday.
According to a joint statement issued on Monday night, the activation entailed immediate deployment of "the agreed military forces and capabilities to the kingdom in response to security threats".
The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of the Strategic-Political and Defence Committee of the alliance, held in Riyadh to discuss the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia.
On Tuesday, the information ministry also rejected what it described as “speculative” Reuters reporting on the pact, saying operational details on implementing the collective deterrence mechanism were confidential.
The ministry’s statement followed a Reuters report published on October 2, which said Pakistan had deployed between 30,000 and 40,000 troops to Saudi Arabia to help defend the kingdom’s land borders and assist with drone and missile interceptions, citing a Pakistani official. Reuters reported that Islamabad had not decided to send troops into Yemen in a fighting capacity.
Houthis have repeatedly carried out missile and drone attacks against Saudi Arabia since the Yemen war escalated in 2015, targeting military installations, airports, oil facilities and other critical infrastructure.
In September 2019 , the group claimed responsibility for drone attacks on Saudi Aramco’s Abqaiq processing facility and Khurais oil field, attacks that temporarily disrupted more than half of Saudi Arabia’s crude production.
The attacks continued in subsequent years, including strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure in March 2022.
More recently, Houthi attacks have again targeted Saudi territory. In September, the group claimed missile and drone strikes on a Saudi military base and other targets, while Saudi authorities reported attacks affecting several cities.
It is worth noting that on September 25 , Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye senior military leadership strongly condemned attacks targeting the holy city of Makkah as they reaffirmed their commitment to the collective defence of the Kingdom under the Makkah pact.
Read More: Makkah defence alliance agrees to 'rapid force deployment' in Saudi Arabia: FO
The Makkah pact was the latest step in longstanding military and strategic cooperation between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. Signed in Makkah, the pact established a framework for collective deterrence and stipulated that an armed attack on any one of the three countries would be considered an attack on all three, while providing for wider cooperation across defence.
The agreement followed nearly a year of negotiations and came amid heightened instability across the Middle East. Turkiye and Pakistan had sought closer regional security cooperation, while Saudi Arabia had faced growing security concerns as conflicts spread across the region, threatening its territory, energy infrastructure and ambitious economic development plans.
For Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the trilateral pact is built on their Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed in September 2025. That agreement stated that “any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both” and committed the two sides to strengthening defence cooperation and joint deterrence.

title: Fact check  Viral Instagram posts of Mahira Khan  Sajal Aly supporting Cockroach Janta Party s Oct 10 protest are fake
description: AI generated screenshots falsely show Mahira Khan and Sajal Ali backing CJP   s Oct 10 protest  no such posts exist
content:
AI-generated screenshots falsely show Mahira Khan and Sajal Ali backing CJP’s Oct 10 protest; no such posts exist
Multiple Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) supporters shared Instagram stories on Oct 8, 2026, allegedly showing social media posts from Pakistani actresses Mahira Khan and Sajal Aly expressing their support for the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) Oct 10 protest. However, the visuals are fake.
Thousands of protesters gathered in New Delhi and Mumbai in October 2026, demanding the resignation of India’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations that revisions to electoral rolls had removed millions of voters. The protests began on Oct 2, with demonstrators accusing the Election Commission of India (ECI) of disenfranchising voters to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling BJP. Both the ECI and BJP denied the allegations.
Amid the demonstrations, the Gen Z-led CJP, headed by Abhijeet Dipke, announced plans to hold a major rally in New Delhi at Jantar Mantar on Oct 10, demanding free and fair elections.
On Oct 8, a BJP supporter shared a post on X featuring images allegedly showing Mahira expressing support for the Oct 10 protest at Jantar Mantar through her Instagram stories.
The post was captioned: “Pakistani actress Mahira Khan supports the October 10 protest.”
It also included her alleged Instagram story, followed by the following caption: “Still, people in India are thinking this is a genuine protest. No bro, it’s a regime-change protest against Modi, the BJP and Hindutva. If they succeed, Pakistanis will return to India, and we might see a situation like 2007 again.”
The alleged story reads: “Just heard Abhijeet Dipke and Dhruv Rathee are going to protest against the BJP government on October 10. Full support to this protest. I can’t come because the BJP has banned Pakistani actors from entering India. Hopefully, after this protest, relations between India and Pakistan will improve again.
Another BJP supporter shared the same story with the following caption: “CJP has started receiving support from Pakistan.”
The claim was further shared by several other BJP supporters on X, further amplifying the virality, as can be seen here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , and here ; collectively accumulating 38,000 views.
Similarly, another visual circulating on social media purported to show an Instagram story shared by Sajal Aly, expressing support for protesters in India and suggesting that a change in the country’s government was imminent.
The text in the alleged story read: “Heard someone is getting kicked out of power in the neighbouring country. Well done, youth. Finally, the era of hatred will end. Hopefully, the new people in power will make our relations better, and we can work together again like brothers.”
The Insta story snapshot was shared by a BJP supporter with the following caption: “It’s one vs all now. This is Sajal Aly, who works in Pakistani TV. She thinks the Modi regime is going to be changed. Even she knows that if Modi gets removed, the new people in power will again make Pakistan their best friend. They will allow Pakistanis to come here and work. And then these snakes will silently plan attacks on our civilians. Pakistan, CJP, leftists and America want to defeat just one man. It’ll be proper cinema if Modi Ji wins in 2029 despite all this foreign funding and paid agenda.”
Another BJP supporter shared the same claim on X with the following caption: “Pakistani actress wants regime change in India. Dumb Indians, open your eyes”
The claim was further shared by several other BJP supporters, further amplifying its virality, as can be seen here , here , here , here and here .
A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to its high virality and keen public interest in the CJP protests in India, along with whether the Pakistani actresses had actually supported them or not.
A keyword search was conducted to verify whether any credible Indian or Pakistani media outlets had reported on the alleged Instagram stories, but nothing was found to corroborate them.
Furthermore, no social media posts were found from Pakistani users, fans and media industry personnel commenting on or reacting to any such alleged posts, casting further doubt about their authenticity.
Inspecting Mahira’s official Instagram account showed no such story. Instagram stories automatically disappear after 24 hours, whereas the viral claim had surfaced on Oct 8.
On closer examination of the viral post, the fingers of Abhijeet Dipke appear distorted, a common discrepancy in AI-generated images.
The image was analysed using OpenAI’s tool to detect the SynthID watermark, which identified a SynthID signal, indicating that the image was likely generated or edited using OpenAI tools.
SynthID works by embedding an invisible digital watermark directly into AI-generated media content. Unlike normal metadata, the watermark forms part of the content itself and is designed to remain detectable even after the media is doctored, such as cropping, applying filters or lossy compression.
The photo was subsequently analysed using other AI-detection tools. Sightengine flagged the visual as 99 per cent doctored, while AI or Not flagged it as 76pc AI-generated.
Meanwhile, Decopy flagged the image as 91pc AI-generated and Fake Image Detector labelled it as 78pc doctored.
Similarly, for the claim regarding Sajal, her official Instagram account also carried no such story.
Meanwhile, analysing Sajal’s post using Truthscan flagged the image as 95pc doctored content.
Undetectable AI labelled it as 95pc edited, and Fake Image Detector flagged it as 76pc computer-generated or modified image.
The claim that screenshots of alleged Instagram posts from Mahira Khan and Sajal Ali show them supporting the CJP’s Oct 10 protest against the BJP party is false.
The viral visuals are AI-generated and the actresses have made no such posts.

title: Will  East of Eden  return for season 2  Everything we know about the Netflix show
description: East of Eden  was developed as a limited series  with the seven episode adaptation designed to tell the story in full
content:
'East of Eden' was developed as a limited series, with the seven-episode adaptation designed to tell the story in full
Netflix’s East of Eden has quickly drawn attention following its release, leaving viewers wondering whether Florence Pugh’s acclaimed adaptation of John Steinbeck’s novel could return for a second season.
However, fans should not expect the story to continue beyond its first season. East of Eden was developed as a limited series, with the seven-episode adaptation designed to tell the story of Steinbeck’s 1952 novel in full. Netflix has not announced plans for a second season.
The series was created and written by Zoe Kazan, who reimagined the novel with greater focus on Cathy Ames, played by Pugh. The character is traditionally viewed as the story’s antagonist, but Kazan’s adaptation explores Cathy’s background and motivations in greater depth while examining the choices that shape her life.
Pugh leads the cast alongside Christopher Abbott as Adam Trask and Mike Faist as Charles Trask. The ensemble also includes Hoon Lee as Lee, Tracy Letts as Cyrus Trask, Martha Plimpton as Faye, Ciarán Hinds as Samuel Hamilton, Joseph Zada as Cal Trask and Joe Anders as Aron Trask.
The story follows the Trask family in California during the early 20th century, with Cathy becoming closely connected to brothers Adam and Charles. Her arrival sets off a chain of events involving love, betrayal, family conflict and the recurring struggle between good and evil.
Kazan previously confirmed that the project was intended to be a limited series. In a 2022 interview, she described it as a limited adaptation and said Pugh was her dream choice to play Cathy.
The decision to make the series limited also allowed Kazan to adapt more of Steinbeck’s sprawling story than the 1955 film, which was directed by her grandfather, Elia Kazan, and starred James Dean. The Netflix series focuses primarily on the Trask family, while reducing some of the Hamilton family storyline from the novel.
All seven episodes of East of Eden are now streaming on Netflix. With the complete story contained within the first season and no renewal currently planned, the series is expected to remain a one-season adaptation rather than continue into a second instalment.

title: Bridgerton    prequel about young Lady Violet greenlit at Netflix
