content:
Shonda Rhimes will write, executive produce and co-showrun the spinoff about Violet and Edmund Bridgerton’s romance
Netflix has greenlit an untitled Bridgerton spinoff focusing on the early life of Lady Violet and her romance with Viscount Edmund Bridgerton, according to Deadline .
The limited series will explore the relationship between the future Bridgerton family matriarch and Edmund before the events of the main series, where Violet is played by Ruth Gemmell.
Like Queen Charlotte: A Bridgerton Story , the new prequel will come from Shondaland. Shonda Rhimes will write, executive produce and co-showrun the series alongside Nicholas Nardini, who previously worked with her on Queen Charlotte .
The story is also connected to Julia Quinn’s Violet in Bloom , a short novella that explores Violet and Edmund’s love story.
Tom Verica, who directed and executive produced Queen Charlotte, will return in the same roles, while Betsy Beers will executive produce for Shondaland.
According to Deadline , discussions about another Bridgerton prequel began after the successful launch of Queen Charlotte in May 2023.
The series introduced younger versions of Queen Charlotte, Lady Danbury and Violet, making them potential candidates for future spinoffs.
The new Violet-focused project follows continued expansion of the Bridgerton universe. Seasons 1 and 3 remain among Netflix’s most popular English-language series, while Season 5 is currently in production in London.
The fifth season will focus on Francesca Bridgerton, played by Hannah Dodd, and Michaela Stirling, played by Masali Baduza.
Netflix has also built a dedicated studio for Shondaland productions in the UK.

title: Halle Berry completes court ordered parenting programme amid Olivier Martinez custody battle
description: Berry had completed the    Our Children First    online mediation orientation and parent education programme
content:
Berry had completed the “Our Children First” online mediation orientation and parent education programme
Halle Berry has completed a court-ordered parenting programme amid her ongoing custody dispute with ex-husband Olivier Martinez over their 13-year-old son, Maceo.
According to court documents obtained by TMZ, Berry signed a certificate on Tuesday confirming that she had completed the Los Angeles Superior Court’s “Our Children First” online mediation orientation and parent education programme.
The programme is required for parents involved in custody or visitation disputes in Los Angeles County. Berry’s completion of the course comes as she and Martinez continue their legal battle over arrangements for their son.
Martinez previously accused Berry of physically abusing Maceo during an incident on September 26. He alleged that the actress put her hands around their son’s neck and choked him while he was playing a virtual reality game.
Berry has denied the allegations, saying the incident involved playful roughhousing and insisting that she never put her hands around Maceo’s neck. She has also said she would never hurt their child and described herself as a domestic violence victim and advocate rather than a perpetrator.
A judge previously granted Martinez’s request for a temporary restraining order, while Berry retained final decision-making authority over Maceo’s mental health and education. Her parenting time was temporarily modified as the custody dispute continues.
Berry has also asked the court to restore the 50-50 custody arrangement she previously shared with Martinez. She has accused her ex-husband of interfering with their son’s therapy and education and of contributing to conflict between her and Maceo. Martinez has denied wrongdoing and said his actions are motivated by concern for their son’s welfare.
The former couple had previously participated in co-parenting therapy in 2024 after agreeing to work with a parenting coach to resolve disputes and improve their relationship as co-parents.
The latest filing comes ahead of the former couple’s next court hearing, which is scheduled for October 16. The custody arrangements and allegations remain subject to the ongoing legal proceedings.

title: Diddy prison release reportedly pushed back to March 2028
description: Sean Combs    prison release date has reportedly moved from January 2028 to March 2 2028
content:
Sean Combs’ prison release date has reportedly moved from January 2028 to March 2 2028
Sean “Diddy” Combs’ federal prison release date has reportedly been moved from January 2028 to March 2, 2028, according to Bureau of Prisons records cited by PEOPLE .
Combs, who is serving his sentence at FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey, was previously scheduled for release on January 21, 2028. The Bureau of Prisons did not comment on the reason for the change.
“For privacy, safety, and security reasons, we do not comment on the conditions of confinement for any incarcerated individual, including reasons for a change in release date,” the BOP told PEOPLE on Wednesday, October 7.
The change comes after reports concerning Combs’ conditions in prison. PEOPLE previously reported that he had been placed in solitary confinement following an NBC News report that alleged he had access to contraband items while incarcerated.
PEOPLE confirmed that Combs remains in solitary confinement.
The NBC report alleged that Combs had access to a “jailbroken” tablet, which he reportedly used to watch films and documentaries, including Netflix’s Sean Combs: The Reckoning.
A source also told PEOPLE that Combs had been seen using a mobile phone to view Instagram and sexually explicit photos sent by a former girlfriend.
The report further alleged that Combs received special meals, massages and premium cognac while in prison.
Combs was sentenced to 50 months in federal prison after being convicted on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution. He was acquitted of more serious charges at the conclusion of his federal trial in New York City.
Following sentencing, Combs was transferred to FCI Fort Dix, a low-security federal facility. He had previously been held at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn during his trial.

title: Tom Cruise   s  Digger  projected to lose  250m after  8m opening weekend
description: Tom Cruise   s  Digger  is reportedly projected to lose  250m after earning  8m domestically
content:
Tom Cruise’s 'Digger' is reportedly projected to lose $250m after earning $8m domestically
Tom Cruise’s Digger is reportedly projected to lose $250 million by the end of its theatrical run, including post-theatrical revenue, according to TheWrap .
The climate change satire, directed and written by Alejandro G. Iñárritu, earned $8 million domestically and $21 million worldwide during its opening weekend.
Insiders at Skydance told TheWrap that the film is not expected to exceed $40 million at the global box office.
Previous reports had estimated a loss of around $125 million, but the projected figure has reportedly increased following the film’s opening performance. Warner Bros., which fully financed Digger , declined to comment.
The film’s reported production budget stands between $163 million and $173 million, according to different insiders cited by TheWrap . Its marketing budget was approximately $100 million, much of which was linked to Cruise’s global press tour.
Digger stars Cruise as a wealthy oil magnate whose wells trigger a global environmental catastrophe. The actor underwent a heavy-prosthetic transformation to play the character, who is depicted as a paunchy, balding billionaire living with a dying cat among mounted stuffed animals.
The film received mixed reviews, with reactions ranging from criticism of its confusing elements to praise for its approach to comedy and environmental themes.
Digger was part of a deal between Cruise and Warner Bros. to develop original and franchise films.
The project also marked a collaboration between Cruise and Iñárritu, who is among the directors to have won consecutive Best Director Oscars.

title: Sharjeel Memon accuses K P CM of  sabotaging  talks with govt
description: Blames Afridi s  stubbornness and ego  for the breakdown  while accusing PTI of failing to confront terrorism in K P
content:
Blames Afridi's 'stubbornness and ego' for the breakdown, while accusing PTI of failing to confront terrorism in K-P
Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Memon on Thursday accused Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi of “sabotaging” negotiations between the government and opposition in Islamabad due to his “stubbornness and ego”, saying the talks had been moving towards a solution before they broke down.
His remarks came a day after Afridi accused the PPP of attempting to create “another East Pakistan” during a meeting of the K-P cabinet, alleging that the party had previously placed personal interests ahead of national interests. The chief minister also criticised Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, who belongs to PPP, for chairing a security meeting, calling it “an attack on the Constitution and democracy” and warning that his government would not allow any attempt to undermine Pakistan’s unity.
“The talks that happened in Islamabad were result-oriented. Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) were part of it, and we were going towards a solution,” Memon said at a press conference in Karachi.
He said the K-P chief minister had “sabotaged” the talks due to his “stubbornness and ego”. “I understand that the reason was that, to look good in Imran Khan’s eyes, he was doing all of this,” he added.
“Talks were going well. The drafts of the agreement had almost been prepared. Some channels even reported that the agreement had been signed and that everything had been settled,” Memon said, while responding to a question.
He claimed that Afridi had acted in a manner aimed at protecting his position before the PTI leadership. “Afridi acted to save his own position before the PTI leadership. The consequences of this are being suffered by PTI and the innocent people of K-P,” he said.
Memon further said PPP had wanted political engagement with PTI and was willing to debate the issue of terrorism on any forum. “I am telling them to come to their senses. Even today there are sensible people in PTI; Gohar, their chairman, and Asad Qaiser,” he added, urging them to come forward and give a “shut-up call” to those promoting a confrontational approach.
Also Read: 'End long march, sit-ins and we will talk': PM Shehbaz once again extends olive branch to PTI
He further said political parties should remain within the political process rather than resort to confrontation or violence, urging senior PTI leaders to rein in such voices. “We want political parties to keep doing their work and have space and continue with a political mindset. Not to pick up weapons and do such hooliganism,” he added.
Memon stated that PPP had not responded to Afridi’s earlier statements but would defend its leadership after the K-P chief minister targeted the party. “PPP will not engage with PTI. But if PTI wants to and launches a baseless smear campaign, then PPP will defend its leaders and show PTI the mirror,” he said.
Asked whether the PPP was prepared for the possibility of governor’s rule or an emergency being imposed in K-P, particularly amid the threat of terrorism and the possibility of PTI protests, Memon said the matter should not be viewed as an issue concerning his party alone. “This is not merely a matter for the People’s Party. It is an issue for every Pakistani, especially my Pashtun brothers and sisters,” he said.
Memon compared the situation in K-P with Karachi’s past experience of terrorism and prolonged strikes, saying around 70% of the province was currently facing a similar situation on a daily basis.
He questioned whether restoring peace should not be the provincial government’s foremost priority. “Political disputes, protests and long marches can continue later but the immediate focus should be on protecting the lives of citizens,” he said.
He said K-P was facing a serious security crisis, with members of the armed forces, police and Frontier Corps, as well as civilians and political workers, being targeted and killed. “Your priority should be to sit down and provide peace to the people and secure their lives. Should the priority be sit-ins and long marches?” he asked.
Turning to the security situation in K-P, Memon said five of the province’s seven divisions were “completely in the grip of terrorism”. “Talibanisation’s biggest headquarters has almost been established in K-P, and its targets are innocent, poor Pashtun brothers and sisters,” he said.
He pointed to the threats facing police personnel and the deterioration of the security situation after dark, attributing it to what he described as “the provincial government’s failure”.
Memon also criticised PTI founder Imran Khan’s past position on negotiations with the Taliban, saying Khan had advocated dialogue with the militant group and the opening of Taliban offices.
He recalled the PPP government’s response to terrorism after the 2008 elections, saying hundreds of thousands of people had been displaced and later resettled. “Before the 2008 elections, in Benazir’s last speech in Rawalpindi, what did she say? She said that we would wave the Pakistani flag in Swat,” he said.
“When the PPP government came in 2008, President Zardari carried out a historic crackdown against terrorists. 800,000 people were displaced. They moved to Karachi, and during the PPP’s time they were resettled,” Memon said. “Those who level accusations against PPP do not see that this entire operation against terrorists was carried out by PPP,” he added.
Read More: Afridi calls Kundi's security meeting ‘attack on Constitution’, warns against 'another East Pakistan' situation
The minister also accused the PTI government in K-P of providing official funding to seminaries and networks he said were involved in terrorism.
“You Google it — the K-P government that was PTI’s government gave funding to the madrassas and terrorists,” he claimed. “Through official accounts, the K-P government gave government money to madrassas that were helping terrorism.” “Those networks that were part of terrorism were being officially funded,” he added.
He questioned why terrorists had targeted rallies held by PPP and other political parties but not PTI rallies. “Why was this?” he asked. He linked it to what he described as the party’s support for the Taliban.
“If your narrative is such that those people who are doing terrorism, you support them, become their spokesperson, they will say that they are our spokespersons, so they will not touch you,” he said.
Memon also cited the Bannu jailbreak during the PTI government and the Army Public School attack, accusing PTI of failing to take a strong position against the Taliban. “In the PTI government, the Bannu jailbreak happened. In double-cabin vehicles, terrorists came under the disguise of a rally and procession, carried out a jailbreak and took away terrorists, and PTI remained silent,” he said.
“Where they have their government, where their writ extends, have they ever said a word for the end of terrorism? Did they ever raise their voice for that? Did they ever hold a press conference against the Taliban?” he asked. He added that PPP had itself suffered heavily from terrorism and maintained that political parties should focus on restoring peace.
Memon also warned that the political conduct being displayed by the K-P government was setting a bad precedent and urged PTI to “come to its senses” and adopt a more sensible approach.
“There are serious people within PTI. I have mentioned their chairman, Gohar and Asad Qaiser. These are serious people. They should make the decisions rather than handing decision-making authority to a young man who could lead things towards some unfortunate incident,” Memon said.
Responding to a question about whether the federal government and PPP leadership had ruled out governor’s rule or an emergency in K-P, Memon said his party had consistently sought political space for PTI in the province. “If you yourself are moving into a circle of self-destruction, who can help you?” he asked.
Memon said PPP wanted Pakistan’s political system and parliament to remain strong and wanted all political parties to retain their political space. “I believe PTI is pushing itself into a dead end, which will become a major problem for them,” he concluded.

title: NEPRA allows Rs1 11 per unit fuel adjustment in October billing
description: Regulator says adjustment follows legal amendments allowing tariff changes based on fuel cost variations
content:
Regulator says adjustment follows legal amendments allowing tariff changes based on fuel cost variations
The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA) on Thursday notified electricity consumers of an additional burden of Rs1.11 per unit in October billing due to higher fuel costs, amounting to Rs16 billion for all consumers.
NEPRA notified the positive Fuel Charges Adjustment (FCA) for August 2026 at Rs1.11 per unit, citing an increase in the actual fuel cost of electricity generation compared with the reference fuel charges.
According to the notification , the actual fuel charges component for August stood at Rs8.21 per kilowatt-hour (kWh) against the reference fuel charges component of Rs7.10 per kWh. This resulted in a fuel cost adjustment of Rs1.11 per unit, which will be reflected in the October electricity bills.
The regulator said the adjustment had been made under the provisions of the NEPRA Act, following amendments to the law that empowered the authority to adjust approved tariffs in line with variations in fuel charges.
Read: NEPRA reviews incremental consumption package
The positive FCA will apply to all consumer categories of ex-WAPDA distribution companies (XWDISCOs) and K-Electric, except lifeline consumers, electric vehicle charging stations (EVCS) and prepaid electricity consumers who have opted for prepaid tariffs.
The adjustment will also apply to electricity consumption falling under the Incremental Consumption Package, according to the notification.
NEPRA directed XWDISCOs and K-Electric to incorporate the August FCA in bills issued during October. The adjustment is to be calculated on the basis of units consumed and billed in August and must be shown separately on consumers’ electricity bills.
Notification of NEPRA issued on October 7, 2026
In cases where October bills were issued before the FCA notification, the additional amount may be recovered in the subsequent billing month, NEPRA said.
The regulator also extended the same FCA to K-Electric consumers in line with federal government policy guidelines concerning the application of uniform fuel charge adjustments. It directed the distribution companies and K-Electric to comply with court orders while implementing the adjustment.
K-Electric wins interim relief as SHC suspends NEPRA tariff orders
Separately, the Sindh High Court (SHC) suspended tariff orders issued by the NEPRA Appellate Tribunal as well as related notifications issued by the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA) concerning K-Electric’s (KE) Multi-Year Tariff (MYT) for the period FY2024 to FY2030, a press release issued by KE said on Thursday.
“The petition challenges judgments issued by the NEPRA Appellate Tribunal on September 23, 2026, review determinations made by the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA) on October 20, 2025, as well as subsequent notifications issued by NEPRA and the Ministry of Energy’s Power Division,” it read further. During the case proceedings, the court issued notices to NEPRA and other respondents on appeals filed by KE challenging the tribunal’s tariff decisions and NEPRA notifications, directing the parties to submit their responses by October 15.
KE’s counsel Barrister Ayan Memon argued that while NEPRA had the authority to review tariff matters, it could not determine a new tariff afresh. The counsel contended that NEPRA had exercised its powers on its own to make changes to the tariff, “which was unlawful”.
Memon also said that the review determinations had resulted in a substantial adverse impact on its MYT for the FY2024-FY2030 control period, making the revised tariff “financially unsustainable” for the company.
Meanwhile, The Express Tribune reported that counsel representing NEPRA said the authority holds the statutory mandate to determine K-E’s tariffs. “Tariffs are reviewed every seven years,” the counsel told the court, adding that the tariff for the period from 2024 to 2030 had been determined through different stages.
According to NEPRA, the supply tariff was determined on May 27, 2025, while the generation tariff was determined on October 22, 2024. The distribution and transmission tariffs were determined on May 23, 2025.
After hearing the arguments, the SHC ordered that the interim impugned notifications and orders were suspended.

title: Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
content:
The prize is awarded by the Swedish Academy and is worth 12 million Swedish crowns
Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature "for her ​bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms ‌for contemporary literature," the award-giving body said on Thursday.
The prize is awarded by the Swedish Academy and is worth 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million).
"She was very taken by surprise. We didn't have so much time to speak, and all she had time to tell me was ​that she is for the moment in Iceland, where she's listening to the wind," said Ingrid Carlberg, ​permanent secretary of the Swedish Academy.
BREAKING NEWS The 2026 #NobelPrize in Literature is awarded to the Canadian author Anne Carson, “for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature.” pic.twitter.com/YRvlRghlGG
Carson's work often blends verse, prose, dialogue and translation in ⁠a genre-defying mix. Born in Toronto, she has also held Icelandic citizenship since 2022.
She is widely known for her ​translations of classical Greek literature, which heavily influence her work, which ranges from opera libretti to literary criticism and verse ​novels such as "Autobiography of Red" from 1998.
"Almost all her literary production has centred upon the intersection between the philologist's obsession with words and the poet's desire for new meaning," the Academy said.
This year’s #NobelPrize laureate Anne Carson was born in 1950 in Toronto, Canada. In 1981, she published her doctoral thesis in Classics entitled ‘Odi et Amo Ergo Sum’, and has, throughout her entire career, combined poetry writing with translation work and teaching at various… pic.twitter.com/GDOE6iTAMg
"She has herself identified the etymology of words as the starting point for all her ​work. Her translations from Classical Greek may be regarded as independent works in their own right."
Her style is exemplified ​in "Norma Jeane Baker of Troy" from 2019, a performance piece which mixes the stories of Helen of Troy in Euripides' play "Helen" and ‌Marilyn Monroe.
Also Read: German and US scientists win Nobel medicine prize for work on optogenetics
Carson had been among favourites this year
Carson, 76, had been among the favourites to win this year's prize, according to bookmakers Ladbrokes, and takes a place beside luminaries such as Alexander Solzhenitsyn, Alice Munro and Ernest Hemingway as a recipient of the award, which often divides opinion among book lovers.
Newly awarded #NobelPrize laureate Anne Carson published a series of notable works in the 1990s. Among these is ‘The Glass Essay’ in ‘Glass, Irony, and God’ (1995), which demonstrates the potential of the long poem where genre boundaries are seen to blur. The same decade saw the… pic.twitter.com/AtrzROjJBj
The Academy has been lambasted for ignoring some of the literary titans ​of the last 120 years ​such as Leo Tolstoy, ⁠Virginia Woolf and Jorge Luis Borges, criticised for snubbing US authors – though it gave the prize to singer-songwriter Bob Dylan in 2016 – and accused of being too obscure in its ​choices.
Read More: Belgian-American wins Nobel in Physics
Defenders say the Academy has made popular picks, such as Colombia's Gabriel Garcia Marquez ​in 1982 and ⁠Doris Lessing in 2007, arguing that part of its task is to highlight lesser-known literary traditions and encourage readers to broaden their horizons.
Established in the will of Swedish dynamite inventor and businessman Alfred Nobel, the prizes for achievements in literature, science and ⁠peace ​have been awarded since 1901.
Last year's prize was won by Hungarian writer Laszlo ​Krasznahorkai , dubbed the "master of the apocalypse" by American critic Susan Sontag.

title: China reportedly holds sensitive F 35 fighter jet parts diverted to Hong Kong
description: US has also deployed F 35 fighter jets during conflict with Iran  with one aircraft sustaining damage from enemy fire
content:
US has also deployed F-35 fighter jets during conflict with Iran, with one aircraft sustaining damage from enemy fire
Chinese authorities are reportedly in possession of parts of an F-35 stealth fighter jet after components of the aircraft were "inexplicably diverted to Hong Kong," CNBC reported.
Shipping giant UPS was transporting a cockpit canopy and weapons bay door from Australia to the United States in late May when the shipment was diverted, Bloomberg reported, citing sources.
According to the sources, both components were coated with radar-absorbing material designed to enhance the aircraft’s stealth capabilities. It remained unclear why the shipment was diverted to Hong Kong.
Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles told reporters that Australia was aware of the shipment and was working with the US and Lockheed Martin to determine how Canberra could assist in the investigation, CNN reported.
Marles also said it was his understanding that the missing shipment did not contain sensitive components, according to CNN .
Lockheed Martin, UPS and the Pentagon did not immediately respond to CNBC ’s requests for comment.
The F-35 is a fifth-generation stealth fighter manufactured by Lockheed Martin, with Washington restricting sales of the aircraft to its closest partners and allies.
Also Read: Israel seeks 'compensation' from US following Saudi F-35 deal: Report
Turkiye, for instance, was excluded from the F-35 programme in 2019 after purchasing Russia’s S-400 anti-aircraft system, amid concerns that the Russian system could be used as an intelligence-gathering platform to learn about the aircraft’s capabilities.
China has previously targeted US military data related to the F-35 in espionage cases, according to US prosecutors in 2024.
A $24 billion sale of F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia was approved last week, although some members of Congress have already raised concerns about the technology potentially falling into Chinese hands.
Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi said the US intelligence community had warned that the sale “could put the crown jewels of American military technology within reach of the Chinese Communist Party.”
Countries operating the F-35 include Australia, Belgium and the US, while Japan, Canada and Singapore are among those that have also ordered the aircraft.
The US has also deployed F-35 fighter jets during the conflict with Iran, with one aircraft sustaining damage from enemy fire, according to the Department of Defence .

title: JPMC doctors protest over three months of unpaid salaries
description: Doctors demand immediate payment  warning of wider protests if their outstanding salaries are not released within days
content:
Doctors demand immediate payment, warning of wider protests if their outstanding salaries are not released within days
Young doctors at the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC) staged a protest on Thursday over the non-payment of their salaries for the past three months, blaming the hospital administration and the Sindh government for the delay.
The protesting doctors gathered outside the Outpatient Department (OPD) Complex and chanted slogans against the hospital administration. They said they had continued performing their duties despite not receiving their salaries and criticised the authorities for repeatedly passing responsibility for the delay from one office to another.
“The hospital administration and the government have treated us like a football,” the protesting doctors said, adding that the hospital administration had directed them to approach the Sindh government, while government officials referred them back to the hospital administration.
The delay began after the provincial government changed the procedure for paying house officers in May, replacing the previous system under which hospitals received funds and distributed salaries through bank cheques with direct transfers into doctors’ bank accounts.
Officials said the new system required additional documentation, including copies of doctors’ CNICs and details of previous cheques, to be submitted to the Sindh Accountant General (AG) office. Hospital administrations said the relevant data had been forwarded and that the delay emanated from the AG office.
Also Read: House officers at public hospitals go 100 days without pay
Speaking to The Express Tribune , Sindh Young Doctors Association President Dr Shahid Awan warned that if the outstanding salaries were not released within the next few days, the doctors would broaden their protest and could stage demonstrations outside the hospital’s administration block and on roads.
“We demand the immediate payment of our outstanding salaries,” Awan said, adding that the matter should be resolved without further delay, whether it involved the Sindh government or the AG office.
The doctors also called for an increase in their salaries, claiming that they had not received a raise since 2020.
Earlier, on September 30, the Sindh Health Department had clarified that the delay was not due to administrative negligence on the part of the hospital management. It attributed the delay to the implementation of a new direct-payment policy and the procedures required to open vendor accounts at the AG office.
In a statement issued by the department, it said that under the new federal policy, house officers’ salaries were to be transferred directly into their bank accounts instead of being paid through cheques issued by hospitals.

The department said the new system required additional documentation and data, including the opening of vendor accounts. It maintained that hospital administrations had submitted the required forms, copies of house officers’ identity cards and details of previous cheques to the AG office within the stipulated period.
However, according to the department, the process was subsequently delayed because the AG office required additional documents and data under the new payment mechanism.
The Health Department said the process of opening vendor accounts was in its final stages and that payment of the outstanding salaries of house officers was expected soon. It added that, given the financial difficulties faced by the doctors, “the matter was being treated as a priority”.
The Express Tribune tried to contact the AG office for clarity on the issue but was refused a response.

title: Rabada set for late fitness call ahead of Australia Test
description: The paceman has not played since May
content:
South Africa are likely to give pace spearhead Kagiso Rabada until the last moment to prove his fitness for Friday’s opening Test against Australia.
Rabada has not played competitively since featuring for Gujarat Titans in the Indian Premier League in May and has been recovering from a hamstring injury suffered in training in August.
The 31-year-old was back bowling in the nets on Wednesday ahead of the first Test in Durban, but teammate Simon Harmer said a decision on his availability could come close to the start of the match.
“Everybody wants him to play. The spectators, us in the change room, the Australians,” Harmer said.
“There’ll be a decision made, I’m sure, as close to the game as possible. He’s proved season in, season out that he’s a world-class player and he’s only going to make our team better.”
Rabada was part of the South Africa side that beat Australia in last year’s World Test Championship final at Lord’s, and his absence would be a major blow as the teams meet again.
If he is rested, Anrich Nortje could make his first Test appearance in more than three years. South Africa also have Marco Jansen, Corbin Bosch and Gerald Coetzee among their pace options in the 18-man squad.
Harmer said South Africa would not risk Rabada’s long-term fitness for the opening match of a busy home season.
“I really hope that he does get in for the first Test, but there’s a lot of cricket this summer and I don’t think we want to risk a short-term game for long-term damage,” he said.
South Africa face Bangladesh in November and England in December after the Australia series as they begin their defence of the World Test Championship title.

title: Haze not  a threat  to Singapore F1 race  organisers
description: Officials say contingency measures are in place if conditions worsen  but track activity remains unaffected
content:
Officials say contingency measures are in place if conditions worsen, but track activity remains unaffected
Motorsport's governing body said transboundary haze from Indonesian fires, which pushed air pollution in Singapore into unhealthy levels on Thursday, did not "represent a threat" to this weekend's Formula 1 race in the city-state.
Singapore's air quality again crossed the threshold, making it one of the most polluted cities globally, according to the Swiss-based air monitor IQAir.
"Air quality levels are being monitored by the relevant local authorities, and appropriate contingency measures are in place should conditions worsen," the FIA said in a statement to AFP.
If the haze worsened "and depending on the pollution level, there may be some restrictions on outdoor activity focusing mainly on entertainment activities rather than the Paddock environment and the circuit," the FIA said late on Wednesday.
But "based on the latest information available, air quality and haze are not forecast to represent a threat to track activity or the conduct of the event," it said.
Race organisers too said they were unconcerned about the haze, despite IQAir's website showing Singapore as the world's third most-polluted major city after Kuala Lumpur and Kinshasa, with an Air Quality Index reading of 174.
The AQI converts measurements of pollutants into a single figure indicating air quality and potential health risks.
Readings above 150 are classified as unhealthy, while levels above 300 are considered hazardous.
Singapore's National Environment Agency data showed all five regions in the city-state recorded "unhealthy" levels of air pollution.
Singapore and Malaysia have been surrounded by a milky haze for more than a month as smoke drifted across from uncontrolled fires on Borneo and Sumatra islands.
The possibility of haze is just one of the "many potential issues" that are covered in the overall contingency plan for the race, said Singapore GP in a statement.
"In the event that haze causes visibility, public health or operational issues, Singapore GP would work closely with the relevant agencies to assess the situation before making any collective decisions regarding the event," it said.
An F1 spokesperson told AFP: "There is absolutely no risk to the event and the conditions where the event is taking place are not at any level of concern."
The FIA's F1 race director Rui Marques, however, issued a heat hazard on Thursday, saying that both Saturday's sprint and Sunday's race will be run at times in a heat index greater than 31C.

title: Alcaraz feeling  mentally fresh  ahead of Shanghai return
description: The Spaniard enters the event after claiming his first title since returning from injury
content:
The Spaniard enters the event after claiming his first title since returning from injury
Carlos Alcaraz said he was feeling "mentally fresh" on Thursday ahead of the Shanghai Masters, after the Spanish star won his first title since returning from a months-long injury.
The world number three said his body was still adjusting to playing demanding matches after coming back from a wrist injury that sidelined him from April until the US Open in August.
But he comes into Shanghai having won the Japan Open on Tuesday, beating Jiri Lehecka 7-6 (7/4), 6-4 in the final.
"I'm feeling very good. Physically I'm well, I'm feeling mentally fresh," the 23-year-old told reporters in the Chinese city.
Alcaraz has never gone beyond the quarter-finals in Shanghai, and missed last year's tournament due to fitness issues.
The former world number one has previously criticised the packed tennis schedule, particularly the autumn "Asian swing" that follows the US Open.
"If we see a couple years back, you know, probably this swing or this part of the season, it's never been my best one," Alcaraz said.
But he added that he was "ready to take on the challenge" in Shanghai, where he will kick off his campaign against either Argentina's Juan Manuel Cerundolo or qualifier Nicolas Mejia of Colombia in the second round.
Alcaraz's path to victory has opened up after current world number one Jannik Sinner announced on Tuesday he was ending his 2026 season with a knee injury.
His main rivals in the draw are Germany's Alexander Zverev, the current world number two, and Serbian veteran Novak Djokovic, who claimed his 102nd career title in Beijing on Tuesday.
Djokovic hails Sinner's 'big-picture' thinking
Djokovic, 39, told reporters in Shanghai that Sinner was "smart" to call time on his season to heal.
"He has to think long-term," Djokovic said. "That's smart because, you know, as someone that... always tried to have the big picture in my mind, I really support that."
"It's important that you give yourself more years to your career, so you have more chances to accomplish all of your objectives," added the 24-time Grand Slam champion.
Djokovic is riding the momentum of his Beijing triumph into the prestigious Shanghai event, which he has won a record four times but not since 2018.
"It was a phenomenal week for me, Beijing, the best week of this year, no doubt," the former world number one said.
"I'm trying to... use the confidence and hopefully have another great deep run."
Djokovic will start his tournament against Poland's Hubert Hurkacz in the second round.

title: Bartunkova thrashes Muchova to reach China Open semi finals
description: The world number 34 sweeps Muchova 6 3  6 0 in just 66 minutes
content:
The world number 34 sweeps Muchova 6-3, 6-0 in just 66 minutes
World number 34 Nikola Bartunkova stunned her Czech compatriot Karolina Muchova 6-3, 6-0 at the China Open on Thursday to breeze into the semi-finals.
The 20-year-old sealed the win in just 66 minutes and will play either Mirra Andreeva or Ekaterina Alexandrova in the next round.
Bartunkova won five consecutive games in 19 minutes in the first set as her seventh-seeded opponent struggled to respond.
Muchova saved five set points but it was not enough to hold back Bartunkova, who had already ousted second-seeded Aryna Sabalenka from the tournament in Beijing.
She raced into to another five-game lead in the second set and gave Muchova no chance of a reprieve, forcing her into firing long to seal a win she described as a "dream come true".
"Honestly I don't know. It was (an) unbelievable match," Bartunkova said on court.
"She's a great player and also a great human being.
"It was a really tough match today, but I was just trying to put my best tennis, and I did it."
Andreeva and Alexandrova were due to play each other later on Thursday in an all-Russian affair.

title: Alcaraz  Sinner  Osaka commit to Australian Open  1 Point Slam
description: The one point contest pits 24 pros against 24 amateurs in a sudden death format
content:
The one-point contest pits 24 pros against 24 amateurs in a sudden-death format
The Australian Open will revive its innovative "1 Point Slam" in 2027 with Carlos Alcaraz, Coco Gauff, Naomi Osaka and Jannik Sinner among those agreeing to take part Thursday.
The sudden-death contest was played for the first time at Melbourne Park this year ahead of the opening Grand Slam of the year, pitting 24 professionals alongside 24 amateurs and celebrity wildcards.
Each match consisted of just one point -- win and you advanced, lose and you were out.
Against the odds, amateur Jordan Smith sensationally upset the star-studded field at a packed Rod Laver Arena to collect a Aus$1 million (US$670,000) prize.
"It creates an opportunity for grassroots tennis players to share the spotlight with some of the biggest names in the game," said Tennis Australia's Tom Larner.
"Having stars like Carlos Alcaraz, Coco Gauff, Naomi Osaka and Jannik Sinner locked in to play, alongside everyday Australians ... captures exactly what this event is about, bringing people together through tennis."
The amateur field will again comprise winners of eight state championship rounds played across Australia, along with eight others who come through qualifying.
More than 1.3 million fans attended the 2026 Australian Open, and organisers are planning to increase viewing capacity and seating even further for the 2027 tournament which runs from January 17-31.

title: Andrew Scott earns Oscar buzz for  Elsinore  performance as Ian Charleson
description: Scott plays Charleson during the last months of his life when he was battling AIDS while preparing to play Hamlet
content:
Scott plays Charleson during the last months of his life when he was battling AIDS while preparing to play Hamlet
Andrew Scott is receiving major praise for his performance in Elsinore , with critics suggesting the actor could be a serious contender for an Oscar for his portrayal of Scottish actor Ian Charleson.
The Simon Stone-directed biographical drama premiered at the London Film Festival this week, following its world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival. Scott plays Charleson during the final months of his life, when the actor was secretly battling AIDS while preparing to play Hamlet at London’s National Theatre.
Charleson was best known for playing Eric Liddell in the Oscar-winning 1981 film Chariots of Fire . In 1989, he took over the role of Hamlet from Daniel Day-Lewis at the National Theatre after Day-Lewis left the production. Charleson continued performing while privately dealing with his AIDS diagnosis and died in 1990, aged 40.
Scott’s performance has been met with widespread acclaim. The Standard described it as a “performance of a lifetime”, while The Guardian called Scott “astonishing” and praised the emotional weight of his portrayal.
The film explores Charleson’s determination to continue performing despite his declining health, while also depicting his relationships with friends, colleagues and Dr Margaret Johnson, played by Olivia Colman. The story is set against the AIDS crisis of the late 1980s, when the disease was devastating communities and carried significant stigma.
Scott also served as a producer on Elsinore , helping bring the project to the screen alongside screenwriter Stephen Beresford. The actor was particularly drawn to Charleson’s story, having previously worked with Beresford on Pride , another film centred on real events involving the LGBTQ+ community.
The growing awards attention marks another potential Oscar campaign for Scott after his acclaimed performance in All of Us Strangers , for which he was not nominated. Current coverage surrounding Elsinore has placed him firmly among the early contenders for this year’s Best Actor race.
Elsinore is screening at the London Film Festival, with the film scheduled to receive a wider UK release on January 29.

title: Shamoon Abbasi challenges Shaan on TikTokers in films
description: Questions whether digital creators should be dismissed as short lived stars  urges industry to let the audience decide
content:
Questions whether digital creators should be dismissed as short-lived stars, urges industry to let the audience decide
Shamoon Abbasi has questioned veteran actor Shaan Shahid’s stance on social media personalities entering the film industry, arguing that it is too early to determine whether TikTokers can build lasting careers in cinema.
The comments came after Shaan questioned whether social media fame could translate into a sustainable career in acting and filmmaking. He argued that online popularity could be temporary and that digital creators entering showbiz would need to learn the craft if they wanted to remain relevant in the long term.
Shamoon questioned whether established figures should dismiss newcomers before audiences have had the chance to see what they can bring to the industry.
In a video shared on Instagram, Abbasi addressed Shaan respectfully, making it clear that his comments were directed at the subject of the debate rather than the veteran actor personally.
Referring to Shaan’s argument that TikTokers making films could prevent the industry from progressing, Shamoon questioned how far Pakistani cinema had progressed in the first place.
“Shaan brother gave this statement that if Tik Tokers make films, the film industry won’t go anywhere but please tell us where the industry has even reached?” he said.
He suggested that before dismissing new entrants, established figures should also examine the industry’s existing challenges and shortcomings.
The actor also addressed the controversy surrounding social media personality Rajab Butt’s upcoming film. Abbasi said he had not personally followed Butt on social media, but acknowledged that prominent digital personalities inevitably attract attention online.
According to Abbasi, the attention surrounding Butt’s film could ultimately work in its favour, regardless of whether people were discussing it positively or negatively. He argued that both criticism and support generate publicity, meaning the ongoing debate itself was keeping the project in the public eye.
Shamoon also questioned the assumption that a TikToker entering cinema would necessarily be a short-lived phenomenon.
“But is it decided that a TikToker will come in movies and just be there temporarily? Who is the one to decide what will be permanent for someone in Pakistan’s film industry? I respect Shaan a lot and have worked with him,” he said.
Shamoon broadened the discussion beyond social media personalities, pointing to the structural challenges facing Pakistani cinema and the difficulties filmmakers face when trying to finance their projects.
He recalled that it took around two years for him and other artists involved in filmmaking efforts to secure funding from government institutions. While the process involved significant delays and bureaucracy, Abbasi said the government ultimately provided financial support.
For Abbasi, the issue therefore extends beyond whether TikTokers should be allowed to make films and into the wider question of how Pakistan can create an environment in which filmmakers are able to produce cinema.
His remarks add another perspective to the debate over whether digital fame can translate into success on the big screen and whether newcomers should be assessed before or after audiences have had the opportunity to see their work.

Kusal Mendis will lead the side in the Test format
Sri Lanka's Dhananjaya de Silva stepped down as captain of the Test team on Thursday, ahead of selection for next month's two-match series against Pakistan.
Kusal Mendis takes over from Dhananjaya de Silva as the new Test skipper of Sri Lanka. The decision on his appointment was taken by the Selection Committee at a meeting held today at SLC headquarters.
Kusal has featured for Sri Lanka in 75 Tests, with 4836 runs at an average of 36.36, with 10 hundreds and 23 fifties to his name.
Kusal hasn't captained Sri Lanka in a Test match yet, but has led the senior side in 22 ODIs and three T20Is.

de Silva said he would be available for selection and remain with the team, but was giving up the captaincy with immediate effect.
"It's my genuine opinion that the mantle should go down to the next generation," de Silva said in a letter addressed to the selectors.
Sri Lanka will play two Tests in Pakistan, with the first starting in Rawalpindi on November 9 and the second beginning in Lahore on November 17.
Sri Lanka Cricket said it welcomed de Silva's continued availability as a player and looked forward to his further contributions to the team.
De Silva has played 69 Tests since making his debut against Australia in 2016. He has scored 4,431 runs, taken 43 wickets and conceded 2,348 runs in the longest format of the game.

title: Nana Patekar  Five iconic roles that defined a singular screen career
description: 3 National Film Awards  a Padma Shri marks career across Hindi  Marathi cinema  establishing him as a unique actor
content:
3 National Film Awards, a Padma Shri marks career across Hindi, Marathi cinema, establishing him as a unique actor
The death of Nana Patekar at 75 has prompted a fresh look at a filmography that was as unpredictable as the actor himself. Across almost five decades, Patekar moved effortlessly between crime dramas, social films, psychological thrillers and comedy, creating characters that often felt less like performances and more like people caught on camera.
Patekar died on October 8 after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa, according to Indian media. As tributes poured in, colleagues and admirers repeatedly remembered the intensity, individuality and range he brought to Indian cinema. His career included three National Film Awards and the Padma Shri, while his performances in both Hindi and Marathi cinema made him one of the most distinctive actors of his generation.
His legacy is particularly visible in the characters that audiences continue to remember years after the films were released. From a paranoid Mumbai gangster to a volatile social crusader and, eventually, an outrageously funny don, these five performances trace the evolution of Patekar's screen persona.
Patekar's breakthrough as a major force in Hindi cinema came with Vidhu Vinod Chopra's Parinda , in which he played the terrifying underworld boss Anna.
The film follows two orphaned brothers, Kishen and Karan, in Mumbai. Kishen becomes involved with Anna's criminal organisation, while Karan returns from abroad and becomes drawn into the violent world surrounding his brother.
What made Anna unforgettable was the contradiction at the centre of the character. He could appear almost paternal before abruptly becoming violent. His paranoia surrounding fire became one of the film's defining elements, culminating in the character's death.
Patekar's performance earned him the National Film Award and Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor. According to The Hollywood Reporter India , he was also injured while filming the climactic fire sequence and spent two months recovering in hospital.
Anna established an image that would follow Patekar for years: a performer capable of making menace feel deeply personal rather than theatrical.
2. Krantiveer (1994) — Pratap Narayan Tilak
Five years later, Patekar delivered one of the most celebrated performances of his career in Krantiveer .
He played Pratap Narayan Tilak, a disillusioned man living in a Mumbai chawl who becomes increasingly involved in confronting corruption, communal violence and political apathy. The Hollywood Reporter India describes the character as a disgruntled chawl dweller who transforms into a powerful voice against the failures surrounding him.
The role was dramatically different from Anna. Pratap was loud, angry and openly confrontational, giving Patekar space to deploy the theatricality and force of his stage-trained performance style.
His speeches became central to the film's identity and helped turn Pratap into an enduring example of the "angry man" archetype in 1990s Hindi cinema. The performance won Patekar the National Film Award for Best Actor.
Where Parinda demonstrated Patekar's ability to frighten an audience through restraint, Krantiveer showed that he could command a film through sheer verbal and emotional force.
In Agni Sakshi , Patekar went in a darker direction, playing Vishwanath, the abusive and unpredictable former husband of Manisha Koirala's character.
The thriller centres on a woman whose new marriage is disrupted when her violent former husband suddenly reappears and claims her as his wife. The Hollywood Reporter India describes Vishwanath as a character who moves unsettlingly between apparent tenderness and outright menace.
Patekar's performance relies heavily on that instability. Vishwanath does not behave like a conventional cinematic villain who announces his intentions. Instead, moments of apparent calm can turn threatening without warning.
That unpredictability makes the character particularly disturbing. The performance also demonstrated that Patekar could dominate a psychological thriller without relying on conventional action or physical intimidation.
His work in Agni Sakshi remains among the performances most closely associated with the darker side of his career.
4. Ab Tak Chhappan (2004) — Inspector Sadhu Agashe
By the time Patekar appeared as Inspector Sadhu Agashe in Ab Tak Chhappan , he had already established himself as one of Hindi cinema's most compelling actors of morally complicated men.
Directed by Shimit Amin, the film follows Sadhu Agashe, an encounter specialist in the Mumbai Police who has killed 56 criminals in police encounters. The Hollywood Reporter India notes that the character was loosely inspired by real-life Mumbai police officer Daya Nayak.
The role was strikingly restrained. Rather than the fiery speeches associated with Krantiveer , Patekar played Agashe with a dry, weary manner. Violence is treated almost as routine — a part of the job rather than something deserving of grand cinematic celebration.
That understatement became one of the performance's greatest strengths. Agashe was neither a straightforward hero nor an uncomplicated villain. He operated according to his own sense of justice, making the character as morally uncomfortable as he was compelling.
The role confirmed that Patekar's intensity had matured. He no longer needed to raise his voice to dominate a scene.
Then came Uday Shetty. For an actor whose career had been defined largely by intense dramatic performances, Welcome offered Patekar an opportunity to demonstrate just how effective his comic timing could be.
He played Uday Shetty, a wealthy Mumbai gangster who wants to find a respectable match for his sister while secretly harbouring ambitions connected to the film industry. His partnership with Anil Kapoor's Majnu Bhai became one of the film's major comic attractions.
The Hollywood Reporter India describes Uday as a gangster whose criminal authority repeatedly clashes with his increasingly absurd involvement in his sister's love life and his aspirations in cinema. The role also introduced Patekar to a younger generation of viewers who may have known him primarily as a dramatic actor. Welcome proved that the same intensity that had once made him frightening could, with a slight change of rhythm, make audiences laugh.
These five roles only represent one section of Patekar's career, but together they explain why his death has produced such a strong sense of loss across Indian cinema.
Anna in Parinda made him terrifying. Pratap in Krantiveer gave his anger a political voice. Vishwanath in Agni Sakshi showed his ability to inhabit psychological darkness. Sadhu Agashe demonstrated his command of restrained, morally ambiguous characters. And Uday Shetty revealed the comic performer hiding inside one of Hindi cinema's most intense actors.
That range was central to Patekar's reputation. The Hollywood Reporter India described his career as one distinguished by an "astonishing range", noting his ability to move from gangsters and cops to comic characters without sacrificing the clarity of his performances. His death has therefore brought back more than individual scenes or famous dialogues. It has revived memories of an actor who rarely seemed interested in fitting neatly into the conventions of stardom.

title: Former Test captain Aamir Sohail reviews NCA development work
description: He stresses the need to turn investment in infrastructure into improved performances
content:
He stresses the need to turn investment in infrastructure into improved performances
Former Pakistan Test captain Aamir Sohail visited the National Cricket Academy in Lahore on Thursday to review player development programmes and high-performance initiatives.
Sohail, who made the visit at the invitation of the Pakistan Cricket Board, was briefed by Director High Performance Aqib Javed on age-group pathways for under-15, under-17 and under-19 players and the academy’s structure for identifying and preparing young cricketers.
He also received a briefing on the Athlete Management System, which is used to monitor player development, assess performances and identify areas for improvement.
The former Test batter, who previously served as Director of the National Cricket Academy and chief selector, reviewed upgraded facilities at the academy, including an ongoing project to install a biomechanics laboratory.
Sohail praised the PCB’s investment in player development and said the facilities now provide a stronger foundation for nurturing talent.
“The facilities that should be available to players at the National Cricket Academy are now in place,” Sohail told PCB Digital. “It is very encouraging to see that the prerequisites required for the development of players are now available in the true sense.”
He also commended PCB chairman’s commitment to investing in Pakistan cricket but stressed that infrastructure and resources must translate into improved performances.
“With the chairman providing such encouragement and showing a willingness to invest in the betterment of cricket, it is equally important that this investment translates into performances and results,” he said.
Sohail also called for greater expertise among those working with players and said the new biomechanics laboratory could help cricketers identify technical shortcomings and improve their performances.
The former captain welcomed the new player pathways but urged the PCB to maintain a sustained focus on school and club cricket.
The PCB’s recently launched school cricket tournament was a positive step, he said, but schools should remain engaged with cricket throughout the year to provide young players with regular opportunities to play and progress.
Sohail represented Pakistan in 47 Tests and 156 one-day internationals between 1990 and 2000.

title: India denies Elon Musk s claim Starlink  blocked by oligarchs
description: Two telecom companies signed pacts with SpaceX last year to bring Starlink internet services to country
content:
Two telecom companies signed pacts with SpaceX last year to bring Starlink internet services to country
India on Thursday denied Elon Musk's claim that “certain oligarchs” were blocking Starlink's satellite communication services in the country to maintain their monopoly, terming it baseless.
Without directly naming Musk, India’s Communications Ministry said in a statement that the government has put in place a fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework for all telecommunication services, including satellite communication services.
It said telecom licences have been granted to three global mobile personal communication by Satellite services based on “non-geosynchronous satellite orbit based satellite communications.”
The statement said security assessment “as part of this process is currently under way in respect of all the three licensees,” and “all three entities are at broadly the same regulatory stage.”
“As such, the suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived,” the ministry said.
Starlink, a division of Musk's company SpaceX, has rapidly expanded its global presence, operating in more than 150 countries and territories. The company provides internet connectivity to remote or underserved areas using a constellation of low-Earth-orbit satellites.
Two Indian telecom companies, Bharti Airtel and Reliance Jio, signed pacts with SpaceX last year to bring Starlink internet services to the country.
Musk wrote on his platform X that “unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people.”
Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are … This is a crime against the people of India! https://t.co/t3YONgpcm7
“You can guess who they are … This is a crime against the people of India!,” he said, responding to a post related to Starlink operations in the world's most populous nation.
India has 958 million internet users, with over 70 per cent internet penetration rate.
Last year, Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Musk in Washington, DC, to discuss space, mobility, technology and governance.

title: No way back     Afridi vows to continue PTI long march as convoy reaches Peshawar
description: Imposition of governor s rule or an emergency will not resolve the situation  Gohar
content:
Afridi says no alliance of local or international establishments can defeat the PTI-led movement
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Mohammad Sohail Afridi on Thursday vowed to continue the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) long march, saying there was “no way back” as the party’s convoy reached Peshawar on the fifth consecutive day of its journey.
Addressing participants of the march, Afridi said the political and democratic struggle would continue within the framework of the Constitution and law and thanked the people of Khyber, the southern districts and Peshawar for participating in the march and urged them to maintain their passion and enthusiasm.
“There is no way back. The dream of true freedom will certainly be fulfilled. They will fire bullets, and we will offer our chests,” he said.
The chief minister said the march was a struggle for “true freedom” and claimed that PTI founder Imran Khan had stood by the nation despite all difficulties and had not bowed to pressure.
“This is the youth’s long march. This is not a fixed match; it will be a decisive march,” Afridi said, using cricketing terminology to describe the movement.
“First we will play a Test match, then a T20 and finally a T10,” he added.
He said he would wait for the participants in Swabi and lead the march himself, adding that the convoy would head towards Swabi and “make them lose sleep”.
Afridi also defended the performance of the K-P government, saying those questioning its achievements were “in a state of panic”. He said the provincial government had promoted e-governance in line with modern requirements and received a Digital Governance Award.
He claimed that the provincial assembly had secured the first position worldwide. The chief minister said the K-P government had not used a government aircraft to obtain the awards, drawing a comparison with Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, whom he said had travelled on an official aircraft to attend her daughter’s graduation ceremony.
“The establishment cannot see the performance of the K-P government,” he said.
He accused the PML-N and PPP of pursuing a “particular agenda”, alleging that they were dividing Pakistan, increasing hatred and promoting prejudice while also alleging that President Asif Ali Zardari was conspiring to impose governor’s rule against a government elected by “90 per cent” people of the province.
The chief minister also criticised the Punjab chief minister over what he described as a narrative against the K-P government and the country as a whole. Referring to a state narrative that “Fitna al Hindustan” was involved in terrorism, he contrasted it with the Punjab chief minister’s reported statement that Punjab faced threats from other provinces rather than India.
“So who is the terrorist — me or the one making this narrative?” he asked.
Afridi also accused the authorities of attempting to silence the PTI by shutting down mobile signals.
“Despite the signals being shut down, they are trembling with fear,” he said, adding that had the signals remained active, the authorities would have “lost their senses” after seeing the turnout.
He said Pakistan had always had “two constitutions” — one for the powerful and rich and another for the weak and poor. According to him, a particular mindset had consistently used the Pakhtuns as a “laboratory” for experiments.
“From 2004 until today, 22 major and 14,000 intelligence-based operations have been conducted,” he claimed.
Afridi said 80,000 lives had been sacrificed but affected families had not even been paid Rs400,000. He questioned why K-P was now being portrayed as a threat to other provinces despite the sacrifices made by its people.
“If this statement is a repudiation of the state’s longstanding narrative, then who is the terrorist?” he asked.
He said the mindset that disregarded the people’s mandate experimented on the Pakhtuns first and subsequently divided the country and created hatred among the people.
“We will not fall for anyone’s narrative and will not allow the country to break apart. Our leader is a symbol of national unity,” he said.
The chief minister described Khan’s imprisonment as unjust and said all efforts to make him bow had failed. He said the PTI had presented seven demands and challenged its opponents to prove even one of them illegal.
“Permission was sought for military operations, an emergency and drone attacks, but I clearly refused,” Afridi said.
He claimed that the objective was more to eliminate the PTI than to eliminate terrorism and said peace could be restored within 100 days if his government’s policy was implemented.
“The objective is more to eliminate the PTI than to eliminate terrorism,” he said.
Afridi also praised the performance of Khan’s government, saying the country had witnessed development and prosperity during his three-year tenure.
“Before the regime change, Pakistan’s per capita income was $1,700, and GDP growth was more than 6pc. The most important thing was that there was peace in the country,” he said.
He said Khan would have to be released to put the country back on the path of development. Referring to poverty, he said that according to the World Bank, 48pc of Pakistan’s population was below the poverty line, while rulers continued to hold press conferences claiming that the country was progressing.
“Even if our opponents bring all institutions and national and international establishments together, they cannot defeat us,” the chief minister said.
Afridi said the next course of action would be announced in Charsadda the following day. He said part of the “actual plan” would be revealed in Charsadda, while the final plan would be announced in Swabi.
“What the destination beyond Swabi will be, we will tell you in Swabi itself,” he said.
Earlier, in post on X, PTI said that the “grand caravan” of the long march, under the leadership of CM Afridi, had reached Hayat Toll Plaza in Peshawar.
وزیراعلیٰ خیبرپختونخوا محمد سہیل خان آفریدی کی قیادت میں لانگ مارچ کا عظیم الشان قافلہ حیات ٹول پلازہ، پشاور پہنچ گیا ہے۔ قافلے میں لاکھوں کی تعداد میں عوام اور کارکنان شریک ہیں۔ شرکاء کے ہاتھوں میں پاکستانی پرچم، عمران خان کی تصاویر اور پارٹی پرچم ہیں، جبکہ ہر طرف عمران خان کی… pic.twitter.com/ygmHcMIG0g
“Everyone has a single demand: Ensure true freedom in the country, the supremacy of the Constitution and law, and the provision of justice,” it said.
The statement said the people of Peshawar had “shattered the idols of fear” and were standing firm with their leader Imran Khan and their elected chief minister.
“Insha'Allah, by the time it reaches Swabi, this caravan will become the largest long march in Pakistan's history. This journey will not stop, Insha'Allah!” it said.
Around 8pm, the convoy was passing through Kohat Road in Peshawar.
'Not your way, not my way': Gohar urges middle path
Meanwhile, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan called for renewed political dialogue, saying the party remained willing to pursue a “middle way” to prevent further instability and safeguard the democratic system.
“We sat down for negotiations with complete honesty, sincerity and good faith, without any conditions. We did not want to sit in negotiations in such a situation, when we had not met our leader, but we made the effort to sit down. Something is better than nothing. Not your way, not my way, but a middle way. Should move forward somehow, whatever happened, for the sake of the country, the nation and democracy,” said Gohar during a press conference in Charsadda.
He regretted that the talks had ended abruptly after two days and said there was still time for both the government and opposition to reconsider their positions.
“We remained seated for two days, but abruptly everything ended. It should not have ended. There is still time. Reality is that both the government and opposition vehicles are stuck in the mud. How do we get this vehicle out of the mud and bring it onto the motorway? We are also calling out; they are also calling out, ‘Let us come onto the motorway,' he added.
Gohar said the only way to prevent the system from being derailed was to set aside egos and allow “common sense” to prevail.
He also called for an end to enforced disappearances and raised concern over the imprisonment of Imran Khan, Bushra Bibi and members of the former prime minister’s family.
Referring to reports about Bushra Bibi’s health, Gohar said: “Last night, reports emerged that Bushra Bibi was unwell. We are all very concerned. I have asked that we be informed about her condition. So far, we do not know how she is.”
He urged authorities with information about her health to immediately inform the party.
Turning to speculation over governor’s rule or an emergency in K-P, Gohar said such measures were not a solution to the province’s political and security challenges.
He argued that imposing governor’s rule or an emergency would increase anger, alienation and political tensions among people in the province, which was already facing a serious law-and-order and terrorism challenge.
Gohar said PTI had made preparations to respond politically and legally to any “unforeseen circumstances”, while insisting that the party wanted all sides to avoid unconstitutional measures.
He also questioned the constitutional scope of the K-P governor’s role, arguing that after the 18th Amendment the governor largely performed a ceremonial function and that executive authority rested with the chief minister.
“The governor does not have the authority to issue directions on the law-and-order situation,” Gohar said, adding that all institutions should function within constitutional and legal boundaries.
Gohar strongly rejected suggestions that PTI, its workers or its provincial government had ever supported terrorism.
“I strongly reject the claim that PTI, the party, its workers, supporters or chief minister have ever supported terrorism,” he said.
He called for the implementation of the National Action Plan and urged the government and opposition to develop a single national narrative against terrorism rather than use the issue for political point-scoring.
“If terrorism takes place in K-P, Balochistan or Sindh, it is Pakistan’s terrorism problem. If anyone dies or is martyred, they are ours,” Gohar said.
He criticised government figures who, he said, had compared PTI supporters coming to Islamabad with terrorists, arguing that such rhetoric was inappropriate for political office-holders.
Gohar said counterterrorism policy should be coordinated nationally and discussed through apex committees and broader political consultations.
“If there is terrorism, take action against it. Wherever it is coming from, call meetings and take steps to eliminate it,” he said.
He also called for an all-parties conference involving political parties across the spectrum so that a common position could be developed against terrorism.
“When all political parties and people are with you, there will be one narrative against terrorism. When you take action, no one will oppose it; everyone will support it,” he said.
The PTI chairman also welcomed opposition by Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F), Jamaat-e-Islami and Awami National Party leaders to the possible imposition of governor’s rule or an emergency in K-P.
Gohar said he hoped the JUI-F chief could play a constructive role in breaking the political deadlock.
“The situation is not moving towards improvement. If people do not move away from their rigid positions and these serious matters continue, the ending will not be good,” he said.
He said Jamaat-e-Islami chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman had also offered to play a role and added that all political parties — whether in government, opposition or outside electoral politics — had a stake in democracy, an independent judiciary, free elections and justice.
Meanwhile, PTI has revised the plan for its long march and issued the schedule for the next phase.
According to PTI K-P Secretary General Ali Asghar Khan, CM Afridi would lead the long march in each district as the "convoy is scheduled to arrive in Peshawar from Khyber tonight."
"PTI said the march will reach Charsadda on October 9, Mardan on October 10 and Swabi on October 11, and the party will decide its next course of action after reaching Swabi," he added.
Long March route so far and the schedule for October 8th #عوامی_مزاحمت_کی_للکار pic.twitter.com/EVSPMvRC1l
The march began from Lakki Marwat on October 4 after talks between the PTI and the federal government failed to resolve their differences. The protest had initially been scheduled for September 27 but was postponed to October 4 as the two sides attempted to negotiate. The talks ultimately broke down, with counter-terrorism policy and meetings with party founder Imran Khan emerging as the main points of disagreement between the federal and opposition.
