title: There was only one Nana Patekar   Bollywood mourns legendary actor
description: Akshay Kumar  Kamal Haasan  other actors remember Patekar s intensity  honesty and individuality after his death at 75
content:
Akshay Kumar, Kamal Haasan, other actors remember Patekar's intensity, honesty and individuality after his death at 75
Veteran Indian actor Nana Patekar died on Thursday at the age of 75 after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa, bringing an end to a career that spanned nearly five decades across Hindi and Marathi cinema.
Patekar was found unconscious at his home in Dona Paula and was taken to a private hospital. Doctors attempted to revive him with CPR for around 45 minutes, but he could not be saved.
He was declared dead at around 5:20am, according to hospital sources. His son, Malhar Patekar, confirmed the death to The Indian Express , saying his father had died of natural causes.
The actor's death prompted an immediate wave of tributes from colleagues and fellow performers, many of whom remembered him not only for his unmistakable voice and intensity but also for the individuality he brought to every role.
Really saddened by the news of Nana ji’s passing. He was one of those rare actors who never needed to do too much to make you sit up and watch. That voice, that intensity, that honesty in every performance… he was completely his own. I feel fortunate that we got to work together… pic.twitter.com/4t1X0UAfVG
Actor Akshay Kumar, who worked with Patekar in Welcome and Housefull 5 , said he was “really saddened” by the news.
“He was one of those rare actors who never needed to do too much to make you sit up and watch. That voice, that intensity, that honesty in every performance… he was completely his own. I feel fortunate that we got to work together in Welcome , and then again more recently in Housefull 5 . There are so many memories from those sets that I’ll always hold close," he said.
Kumar continued, "Nana ji was truly one of a kind. It’s hard to believe you’re gone. Thank you for all the memories. You will be missed more than words can say".
Deeply saddened by the passing of a great actor, a remarkable presence and a true stalwart of the craft. His contribution to cinema and his dedication to his craft will always be remembered. May his soul rest in peace. Om Shanti. 🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/B85M39WIte
Manisha Koirala, who shared the screen with Patekar in Khamoshi: The Musical and Agni Sakshi , remembered him as “a remarkable presence and a true stalwart of the craft.”
“His contribution to cinema and his dedication to his craft will always be remembered. May his soul rest in peace.” Koirala wrote in a tribute shared on X.
Actor Urmila Matondkar, who worked with Patekar in Bhoot , said she was “devastated beyond words” and described him as a “great patriarch of Marathi theatre” and an “awesome human being”. “What do you even write about someone who can never be captured in words,” she wrote on X.
Devastated beyond words..just frozen with grief 🙏🏻 Shocking,shattering n extremely saddening 🙏🏻 What do you even write about someone who can never be captured in words.. Great Patriarch of Marathi theatre n awesome human being आमचे नाना 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/YD2kishMGK
Riteish Deshmukh also mourned Patekar, saying he was shocked “beyond words” by the actor's death.
He called him an incomparable performer who could play everything from a larger-than-life hero and terrifying villain to a poker-faced comic character. He also recalled Patekar's generosity, wisdom and the conversations they shared.
आज शब्द थिजले आहेत, काळजावर जणू वीज कोसळली आहे.⁰नाना गेले... या एका वाक्याने मन सुन्न, निःशब्द झाले आहे. तुम्ही अभिनयाचे आकाश होतात, ज्याला तुलनेची सीमा नव्हती.⁰तुमच्या अनोख्या शैलीने रसिकांच्या हृदयात तुम्ही अढळ घर केले. कधी पडद्यावरचा तेजस्वी नायक, कधी अंगावर शहारे आणणारा… pic.twitter.com/tZoOZxgaEk
Several other names from the film industry also expressed grief.
Paresh Rawal described Patekar as “insanely honest and intense”, while Manoj Bajpayee remembered the actor's journey as an inspiration for aspiring performers trying to find their place in Mumbai's film industry.
BHAU . NANA SAHEB . INSANELY HONEST AND INTENSE. LOVE AND RESPECT FOR EVER . AUM SHANTI 🙏
Randeep Hooda recalled first seeing Patekar in Parinda and said he did not feel he was watching an actor but “a real person”. Hooda described him as “honest, fearless and always true to himself”.
When I first saw him in Parinda I didn’t think I was watching an actor. I thought I was watching a real person. When I met him years later, that feeling stayed with me. He was exactly that, a real person who wore his heart on his sleeve and not just a pretentious actor. Saddened… pic.twitter.com/4vYgKZE4G3
Suniel Shetty, meanwhile, remembered Patekar as “fiercely honest” and “a master of your craft”, writing that “there was only one Nana” and that Indian cinema would not be the same without him.
Absolutely shocking!!! They don’t make men like you anymore. So deeply rooted no matter how high you rose. Unapologetically yourself, fiercely honest and a master of your craft. There was only one Nana. There will never be another. Rest in peace Bhau... Cinema won't be the… pic.twitter.com/K7zrh5qIub
Kamal Haasan also paid tribute, calling Patekar “an extraordinary artist and an even greater human being” while highlighting his work beyond cinema, including his support for farmers in Maharashtra.
Heartbreaking news of Nana Patekar Ji’s passing. An extraordinary artist and an even greater human being. The man was a force of nature, and he uplifted the lives of those around him. Beyond the screen, his work helping farmers in Maharashtra and his volunteer service during the… pic.twitter.com/T72ZGr0kGP
Patekar made his film debut with Gaman in 1978 and went on to become one of the most distinctive performers in Indian cinema.
His breakthrough came with films such as Parinda , for which he won the National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor. He subsequently delivered acclaimed performances in Prahaar , Krantiveer , Agni Sakshi , Khamoshi: The Musical , Ab Tak Chhappan , Apaharan , Rajneeti and the Marathi film Natsamrat .
He also demonstrated a lighter side in mainstream entertainers, most notably as the volatile gangster Uday Shetty in Welcome , a performance that introduced his distinctive comic timing to a new generation of audiences.
Over his career, Patekar won three National Film Awards and was awarded the Padma Shri, one of India's highest civilian honours. He worked not only as an actor but also as a director and writer.
He leaves behind a body of work marked by raw emotion, memorable dialogue delivery and an ability to disappear into characters. For generations of Indian film audiences, his performances remain among the most recognisable examples of intensity and authenticity on screen.

title: PSX down over 1 100 points on oil price surge
description: KSE 100 closes at 167 441 points  as Brent crude crosses  104
content:
KSE-100 closes at 167,441 points, as Brent crude crosses $104
The KSE-100 Index fell 1,138 points, or 0.68%, on Thursday as rising international oil prices and heightened geopolitical uncertainty weighed on investor sentiment.
According to a market wrap by KASB KTrade, the benchmark index closed at 167,441 points, with pressure intensifying as Brent crude breached the $104-per-barrel mark and traded near $105, gaining nearly 5% during the day.
Oil prices rose on growing supply concerns amid geopolitical tensions and uncertainty surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.
The decline came despite the successful completion of Pakistan's latest International Monetary Fund (IMF) review, which cleared the way for a potential $1.2 billion tranche release.
Read: Pakistan, IMF reach staff-level agreement on $1.2b loan
Market participation remained weak, with 152 million shares changing hands during the session.
Commercial banks, fertiliser, oil and gas, and technology stocks were among the sectors weighing on the benchmark. UBL, FFC, SYS, EFERT and POL were among the major stocks contributing to the index's decline.
KEL, CNERGY, PIBTL and FCCL emerged as some of the most actively traded stocks by volume.
Ahmed Sheraz, Head of Support Trading at KASB KTrade, said market sentiment was likely to remain cautious until greater clarity emerged over the geopolitical situation and the direction of international oil prices.
He said a sustained moderation in energy prices could provide relief to equities.
The surge in global oil prices remains a key risk for Pakistan's economy and financial markets, given the country's reliance on imported energy and the potential impact of higher oil costs on inflation , the external account and corporate profitability.

title: Nicolas Maduro  wife expected to face new US charges for alleged torture of Americans
description: Nicolas Maduro  wife expected to face new US charges for alleged torture of Americans
content:
US investigators have discussed charging several additional people for their alleged roles in torture of Americans
US prosecutors in New York are expected to bring new charges against Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, for the alleged torture of Americans held in Venezuelan government custody in recent years, media reports said a day earlier.
The new charges relate to the alleged wrongful detention of more than a dozen Americans in Venezuelan prisons during the years Maduro led the country, according to those briefed on the investigation.
Read: Maduro sits in US custody as loyalists call for defiance
CNN reported that US investigators have discussed charging several additional people for their alleged roles in the torture of Americans, potentially expanding the scope of the case beyond the couple.
Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores are expected to face new charges over the alleged torture of Americans held in Venezuelan government custody in recent years, according to multiple people familiar with the investigation. https://t.co/94GTPBK96S pic.twitter.com/Ou42vWXZrq
The charges would add to the criminal case already facing Maduro and Flores in the US. The couple was captured during a US military raid on the presidential palace in Caracas in January. They have pleaded not guilty to charges, including conspiracy to commit narcoterrorism and are being held without bail in New York.
The new investigation focuses on Americans who were detained in Venezuelan prisons and allegedly subjected to torture or other mistreatment while in government custody.
Also Read: Thousands march in Caracas to demand release of Maduro after US-led capture
Sources did not provide details about the identities of the Americans involved or the specific acts of torture being investigated. US authorities continue to pursue cases linked to alleged abuses committed during Maduro's years in power.
Sources did not indicate whether the new allegations would be added to the existing case or brought separately. They also did not provide details about the evidence prosecutors have gathered or identify the additional people who could face charges.
Any new allegations would have to be proven in court, and Maduro, Flores and any other defendants would be entitled to challenge the charges as the legal proceedings continue.

title: Halle s Berry daughter speaks out after mother is accused of abusing 13 year old son by ex Olivier Martinez
description: Martinez has sought sole custody of Maceo after alleging Berry choked him during a September  26 altercation
content:
Martinez has sought sole custody of Maceo after alleging Berry choked him during a September 26 altercation
Halle Berry’s 18-year-old daughter, Nahla Aubry, has spoken out in support of her mother after Olivier Martinez accused the actress of abusing their 13-year-old son, Maceo .
According to Page Six , Nahla described Berry as a “loving and devoted parent” who “can be strict when necessary” in a declaration filed in Los Angeles Superior Court.
Nahla said she had never witnessed Berry physically abuse Maceo. “I have never seen my mom hit, slap, choke, grab, or physically abuse Maceo in any way,” she wrote.
She also stated, “I have never seen my mom place her hands around Maceo’s neck, put him in a chokehold, restrict his breathing, or engage in any conduct remotely resembling the allegations that have been made against her.”
Nahla described Berry as a hands-on mother who “always made time for me and prioritized what was important to me”.
She said Berry attended Maceo’s games, drove him to practices and tournaments and supported his education.
“My mom is a loving and devoted parent. She can be strict when necessary and expects her children to follow rules and be respectful. At the same time, she is warm, supportive and deeply involved in our lives,” Nahla stated. “I never observed anything abusive about her parenting.”
Martinez has sought sole custody of Maceo after alleging Berry choked him during a September 26 altercation.
A judge temporarily granted Martinez primary custody, while Berry was limited to court-ordered visitation.
Berry has denied the allegations through her attorney, Marina Beck, and requested that their previous 50/50 custody arrangement be reinstated.
The next hearing is scheduled for October 16.

title: Iraqi Airways resumes Iran flights after seven month suspension

content:
Restoring routes aims to facilitate passenger travel, expand Iraq’s regional air connections
Iraqi Airways resumed direct flights to Iran on Thursday after a seven-month suspension that began amid the US-Israeli war on Iran in early March, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).
The national carrier said regular daily flights would operate from Najaf International Airport to Tehran, Mashhad and Isfahan.
The resumption followed efforts by Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Transport Minister Wahab al-Hasani after the necessary regulatory and technical requirements were completed, the airline said.
Read: Trump says Iran deal 'isn't really something that I want to do'
It added that restoring the routes aims to facilitate passenger travel and expand Iraq’s regional air connections, particularly for religious, medical and educational purposes.
Iraqi Airways suspended its flights to Iran in early March as a precautionary measure following the outbreak of the US-Israeli war on Iran on Feb. 28. Iraq also closed its airspace as regional military tensions escalated.

The appeal follows a similar request from BTS member V, who previously asked fans to avoid the group's hotels and respect their privacy.

title: El Nino forecast to reach record strength as global heat  weather risks rise  WMO
description: UN says event could be among strongest since at least 1950  will bring higher temperatures  shift rain patterns
content:
UN says event could be among strongest since at least 1950, will bring higher temperatures, shift rain patterns
An ongoing El Nino event is strengthening rapidly and is forecast to push key Pacific sea-surface temperatures to record levels, increasing the risks of extreme heat, drought and flooding around the world, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said Thursday.
In its latest Global Seasonal Climate Update, the UN weather agency said there is a near-100% likelihood that El Nino will persist through February 2027, with the event expected to peak around December.
“El Nino is firmly established and strengthening rapidly," WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo said, warning it will potentially be "one of the strongest since at least 1950."
For October-December, the average sea-surface temperature anomaly in the Nino 3.4 region of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific is forecast to reach about 3.7C (6.7F) above normal, which the WMO said would be "the highest since observations began."
The previous record was 2.6C (4.7F) above normal during the November 2015-January 2016 period.
The WMO said El Nino is likely to bring above-average temperatures across large parts of the globe while significantly shifting rainfall patterns.
Read: Pakistan among countries vulnerable to 'super' El Niño
Wetter-than-normal conditions are forecast in areas including the Greater Horn of Africa, parts of Central and East Asia, northern parts of the Arabian Peninsula, parts of North America and southeastern South America.
Drier-than-normal conditions are expected across the Indian subcontinent, southern Central America, parts of the Caribbean and northwestern South America.
Saulo said El Nino does not create additional planetary heat but releases heat already stored in the ocean, warning that the ocean from which the current event is drawing is “the warmest we've ever measured it.”
The WMO said national meteorological services and regional climate forums are providing regular updates to governments and humanitarian partners to support preparedness and risk management.

title: Zara Larsson faces backlash for workplace joke as internet users call it  straight up harassment
description: Larsson   s comments about firing staff over a  goon face  on the Las Culturistas podcast have prompted criticism online
content:
Larsson’s comments about firing staff over a 'goon face' on the Las Culturistas podcast have prompted criticism online
Zara Larsson has sparked discussion online after joking that she would fire members of her team if they could not make a “goon face” on demand .
The Swedish pop star made the comments during an appearance on the Las Culturistas podcast with Matt Rogers and Bowen Yang.
Explaining the joke, Larsson said, “The people I work with, we have this thing,” adding, “I want everyone around me to be able to do a goon face. To me, it’s like, ‘Are you free; are you carefree? Are you yourself? Can you be silly?’”
Larsson then said, “If I ask someone on the spot to make a goon face, and they’re like, ‘I can’t do this,’ I’m like, ‘You gotta go, you’re fired.’”
The term "goon face" refers to a distinctive, exaggerated facial expression characterized by a slackened jaw, unfocused gaze, and open-mouth posture, typically associated with the internet subculture surrounding "gooning"—a slang term for prolonged, compulsive sexual self-stimulation or edging.
The comments quickly circulated online, with some users questioning whether Larsson was joking or expressing an actual expectation of employees.
One person wrote, “Am I the only one who thinks this is a little weird?” while another questioned how such a requirement could apply to employees.
A third commenter described the remarks as “straight up workplace harassment”, arguing that employees should not be pressured into doing something that was not part of their contracts.
However, the reaction was not universally negative.
One social media user defended Larsson, writing, “She’s so real for this,” and suggesting that being able to embrace a playful moment was part of matching her energy.
The comments had prompted mixed reactions, while the context of Larsson’s remarks appeared to leave some viewers uncertain about how seriously they were intended.

title: PM Shehbaz seeks stronger Bahrain ties in trade, energy during meeting with FM Al Zayani | The Express Tribune
description: Also expresses satisfaction over the 'positive trajectory of bilateral relations'
content:
Also expresses satisfaction over the 'positive trajectory of bilateral relations'
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday called for further strengthening Pakistan-Bahrain cooperation in trade, investment, energy and human resource development, as he reaffirmed Islamabad’s commitment to expanding the two countries’ “longstanding and brotherly relations”.
The prime minister made the remarks during a meeting with Bahraini Foreign Minister Dr Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, who was visiting Pakistan to co-chair the 3rd Session of the Pakistan-Bahrain Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.
According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office on X, Shehbaz expressed satisfaction over the “positive trajectory of bilateral relations” and said Pakistan remained committed to expanding cooperation with Bahrain in key areas.
Welcoming Al Zayani, the prime minister conveyed his best wishes to the Bahraini leadership and people and highlighted the close ties between the two countries, which he said were rooted in shared values, mutual trust and strong people-to-people contacts.
His Excellency Dr. Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, Foreign Minister of the Kingdom of Bahrain, called on Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif during his visit to Pakistan to Co-Chair the 3rd Session of the Pakistan-Bahrain Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC), along with the… pic.twitter.com/swgwH2RJAo
Al Zayani conveyed the greetings and good wishes of the Bahraini leadership to Shehbaz and reaffirmed Manama’s commitment to further enhancing bilateral cooperation in areas of mutual benefit.
The two sides also exchanged views on regional and international developments and stressed the importance of continued consultations and coordination on issues of mutual interest, according to the statement.
Al Zayani appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role and mediation efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability in the region.
Foreign Minister of the Kingdom of Bahrain H.E. Dr. Abdullatif bin Rashid Al-Zayani called on Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad, today. pic.twitter.com/MVRRlzZTnC
Shehbaz expressed confidence that the 3rd Session of the Pakistan-Bahrain JMC would provide fresh impetus to bilateral cooperation and help deepen the “multifaceted relationship” between the two countries.
The meeting was held in a warm and cordial atmosphere, reflecting the close and longstanding fraternal ties between Pakistan and Bahrain, the statement concluded.
Bahrain foreign minister meets CDF Munir at GHQ
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation in the defence and security domains with Bahrain.
He said this in a meeting with FM Al Zayani at the General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi on Thursday, according to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR).
The military’s media wing further said matters of mutual interest, the regional security situation and bilateral defence and security cooperation came under discussion during the meeting.
CDF Asim Munir shakes hand of Bahrain FM Al Zayani at the General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi on Thursday, October 8, 2026.
CDF Munir underscored the longstanding fraternal relations between Pakistan and Bahrain, describing the ties as being rooted in shared values and mutual respect.
The visiting Bahraini dignitary appreciated the professionalism and operational preparedness of the Pakistan Armed Forces, ISPR said.
Al Zayani also reaffirmed Bahrain’s resolve to further enhance bilateral cooperation and acknowledged Pakistan’s contributions towards regional peace and stability.
Later in the day, Bahrain’s FM Dr Abdullatif bin Rashid Al-Zayani called on President Asif Ali Zardari to enhance ties between the two countries.
The president met FM Al-Zayani at Aiwan-e-Sadr in Islamabad, a statement issued by the president’s office on social media said.
The statement further outlined that the two sides held a restricted meeting followed by delegation-level talks during which President Zardari said Pakistan was keen to translate strong bilateral political relations into deeper trade and investment ties.
He identified food security, information technology and digital services, construction, mining, port handling, research and development, tourism and healthcare as key areas offering opportunities for bilateral cooperation.
The president also stressed the importance of greater business-to-business engagement between the two.
President Zardari in a meeting with Bahrain’s FM Dr Abdullatif bin Rashid Al-Zayani on October 8, 2026 at Aiwan-e-Sadr. Photo: President Office
President Zardari appreciated Bahrain’s warm welcome of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding and the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, as well as its recognition of Pakistan’s efforts to promote “regional peace, security and stability”.
He described Pakistan and Bahrain as longstanding defence partners, noting that their cooperation was reflected in joint military exercises, high-level exchanges and institutional ties.
Pakistan, he added, was ready to further expand cooperation with Bahrain in manpower, logistics, training and defence hardware.
According to the official statement, the president also thanked Bahrain for its support and opportunities for the more than 134,000 Pakistanis living in the kingdom and welcomed continued cooperation on issues concerning the Pakistani diaspora.
“Talking about the regional situation, the President said Pakistan remains committed to constructive engagement with all parties to build trust, bridge gaps and promote lasting peace, security and stability in the region,” it highlighted further.
FM Al-Zayani conveyed the greetings of Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa to President Zardari.
Speaking on meetings of the Pakistan-Bahrain JMC, FM Al-Zayani said it had remained highly productive and covered several important areas of bilateral cooperation.
“President’s visit to Bahrain has left a significant and positive impact on bilateral relations,” the statement noted.
On regional developments, Al-Zayani praised Pakistan’s efforts to mediate between warring parties and bring them to the negotiating table. He said Pakistan’s actions had helped save many lives, invoking the Quranic teaching that saving one life is akin to saving all humanity.
The Bahraini minister also congratulated Pakistan on its successful tenure as a non-permanent member of the United Nations Security Council.
President calls for stronger Pakistan-Bahrain trade, investment and security cooperation President Asif Ali Zardari said Pakistan attaches great importance to its relations with Bahrain and expressed the desire to further strengthen bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade,… pic.twitter.com/eNu4oBCgc8
“During the delegation-level meeting, Dr Abdullatif bin Rashid Al-Zayani was accompanied by Ambassador of Bahrain to Pakistan Mohammed Ibrahim Mohammed Abdulqader, Advisor to the Minister of Foreign Affairs for Political Affairs Hamad Ali Al Mannai, Major General Abdulaziz Mayoof Al-Rumaihi, Director-General of Criminal Investigation and Forensic Science, Ministry of Interior, Shaikh Hamad bin Salman Al Khalifa, Assistant Undersecretary for Domestic and Foreign Trade, Ministry of Industry and Commerce, Eng. Mohammed Mirza Al-Oraibi, Assistant Undersecretary for Agriculture Affairs, Ministry of Municipalities Affairs and Agriculture, and Yousif Salahuddin Ibrahim Salahuddin, First Vice Chairman, Bahrain Chamber of Commerce and Industry,” the official statement detailed.
It added that from the Pakistani side, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Senator Sherry Rehman, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla, Member of the National Assembly of Pakistan Syed Naveed Qamar, the Ministry of Economic Affairs secretary and other senior officials attended the meeting.
Pakistan, Bahrain agree to form joint trade group, push GCC free trade deal
Pakistan and Bahrain agreed to establish a joint working group on trade and investment and committed to “finalising” the GCC-Pakistan Free Trade Agreement, Bahrain’s Foreign Minister Dr Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani said on Thursday.
The understanding was reached during the third session of the Pakistan-Bahrain Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC), co-chaired by Al Zayani and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, where the two sides signed agreed minutes covering more than 15 areas of cooperation.
“We agreed to establish a joint working group on trade and investment, to convene the joint working group on energy next month on oil, gas, and minerals, and to take forward cooperation in food security, information technology, law enforcement, media, labour mobility, health, education, culture, and sport,” Al Zayani said during a joint press conference.
Bahrain also said it would use its presidency of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) to speed up the signing or approval of the free trade agreement, while the two countries aimed to double bilateral trade over the next three years.
Al Zayani said the bilateral relationship was “very healthy and strong” and was valued by Bahrain’s King, Crown Prince and Prime Minister and the Bahraini people. “We have to double the trade during the three years,” he said, outlining the economic target agreed by the two sides.
FM Dar said the JMC had been “comprehensive and productive”, with discussions covering agriculture, energy, sports, tourism and business-to-business cooperation.
#Live : Deputy Prime Minister @MIshaqDar50 and Foreign Minister of Bahrain, Dr. Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, are addressing a joint news conference in Islamabad @ForeignOfficePk @bahdiplomatic #News #RadioPakistan https://t.co/WRCr2yBxYj
The two sides also sought to expand cooperation in industrial collaboration, food security, skills development, higher education, information technology, logistics and maritime affairs, while strengthening engagement between their business communities.
Dar highlighted the Pakistani community in Bahrain as a bridge between the two countries and reaffirmed cooperation in labour mobility, vocational training and human-resource development for skilled Pakistani professionals and workers.
“We are on the same page,” Dar said, referring to the close coordination between Pakistan and Bahrain at bilateral and multilateral forums. He said the two countries regularly met on the margins of international meetings and remained in consultation on issues of mutual interest.
The ministers also exchanged views on the ongoing US-Iran crisis and stressed “restraint, de-escalation, dialogue and diplomacy” as the means of addressing regional tensions.
Al Zayani appreciated Pakistan’s “principled positions” during the crisis, including its support for UN Security Council Resolution 2817 and its efforts with international partners to facilitate US-Iran dialogue and de-escalation.
“We appreciate Pakistan’s efforts with partners to facilitate the dialogue between the United States and Iran, including hosting the talks in Islamabad,” Al Zayani said.
Dar reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to playing a constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability.
In the press conference, both ministers stressed the importance of ensuring the safety and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb, given their significance for regional and global food and energy security.
“Bahrain strongly condemns the terrorist attacks on Abha International Airport and King Khaled International Airport, and the Houthi attacks on Saudi civilians and facilities, including the assaults on Mecca and Madina,” he said. “Targeting airports and civilian facilities violates international law and international humanitarian law and threatens civil aviation,” Al Zayani added.
He expressed Bahrain’s “full solidarity” with Saudi Arabia and conveyed condolences to the victims and wishes for the recovery of those injured.
On Palestine, FM Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for Palestinians and their “inalienable rights”, while expressing concern over the expansion of illegal settlements and attempts to alter the status of Al-Quds Al-Sharif.
“We also called for urgent and unhindered humanitarian assistance to Gaza and reiterated our support for a just and lasting solution in accordance with the relevant UN resolutions,” Dar said.
The ministers said they discussed Afghanistan and the Indus Waters Treaty, with Pakistan stressing the need to ensure that foreign territory was not used against it.
FM Dar stated that India’s unilateral decision to place the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance was a “material breach of international law” and a “dangerous attempt to weaponise shared water resources”.
He said the move threatened the water, food and energy security of 250 million Pakistanis.
The Bahraini foreign minister said bilateral ties had gained momentum through recent high-level exchanges, including Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s visit to Bahrain in November 2025 and President Asif Ali Zardari’s visit in January 2026.
Al Zayani noted that October 14 would mark the “55 years” of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and Bahrain.
He also highlighted the King Hamad University for Nursing and Allied Medical Sciences in Islamabad and the role of more than 140,000 Pakistanis living and working in Bahrain in strengthening ties between the two countries.
Al Zayani described the relationship as “very truthful”, saying both sides were frank with each other, understood their respective constraints and respected one another. “Now we are seeking more delivery and more results for the future,” he said.
Dar recalled Al Zayani’s support during the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict and his role in efforts to facilitate US-Iran dialogue. “We meet frequently at multilateral fora, and we are constantly in touch and consult each other on international issues,” Dar said.
He also thanked Bahrain for the welcome and hospitality extended to President Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz during their recent visits.
The two countries also agreed to continue coordination at the United Nations, where both are serving as non-permanent members of the Security Council. Al Zayani said the two sides would continue their coordination and joint efforts in New York and at other international forums.
Dar said the next JMC would be held in Bahrain in 2027, within 365 days of the current session, after the latest meeting had taken place five years after the previous one.
The Bahraini minister was also scheduled to call on President Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz and Field Marshal Asim Munir during his visit.
Al Zayani said the visit had reaffirmed the “strategic nature” of Pakistan-Bahrain relations and the two countries’ determination to translate their agreements into practical outcomes for peace, stability and prosperity.
Earlier in the day, FM Dar held talks with Al Zayani in Islamabad, with the two sides discussing ways to expand cooperation in trade, economic and investment relations, the FO said in a statement on X.
“The two Ministers reviewed Pakistan–Bahrain relations and expressed satisfaction at the positive momentum in high-level engagement between the two countries," the FO said.
They also discussed engagement through multilateral forums and exchanged views on regional and international developments of mutual interest.

Dr. Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, Foreign Minister of the Kingdom of Bahrain, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today. The two Ministers reviewed Pakistan–Bahrain… pic.twitter.com/fB8aNIh9N8
“The two sides also exchanged views on regional and international developments of mutual interest and underscored that dialogue and diplomacy remain the most viable means of addressing challenges and resolving disputes,” the FO said.
Earlier, the FO said Al Zayani was received by FM Dar at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, where the two leaders were scheduled to hold a bilateral meeting and co-chair the third session of the Pakistan-Bahrain Joint Ministerial Commission.
“The two leaders will hold a bilateral meeting and co-chair the third session of the Pakistan-Bahrain Joint Ministerial Commission,” the FO said in the earlier statement.

Al Zayani arrived in Pakistan on Wednesday night for a two-day visit from October 7-8 at the invitation of FM Dar. He was received at the airport by Economic Affairs Division Secretary Muhammad Humair Karim and Additional Secretary (Middle East) Zahid Hussain.

content:
Anne Hathaway’s 'Verity' is projected to fall to second place in its second weekend
Jessica Chastain’s horror thriller Other Mommy is projected to lead Jeremy Strong’s The Social Reckoning at the North American box office this weekend, according to Deadline's projection.
Deadline forecasts Other Mommy will open with $20 million from 3,200 theatres, while The Social Reckoning is expected to debut with $8 million across 2,200 locations.
Box Office Pro has a similar outlook, estimating openings of $17 million to $22 million and $6 million to $10 million, respectively.
Directed by Rob Savage, Other Mommy stars Chastain as Ursula and her doppelganger, who terrorises her eight-year-old daughter, Bela, played by Arabella Olivia Clark.
The film also features Jay Duplass, Karen Allen and Dichen Lachman.
Meanwhile, The Social Reckoning arrives 16 years after The Social Network . Strong plays Facebook co-founder Mark Zuckerberg, with Mikey Madison portraying former Facebook engineer Frances Haugen.
Jeremy Allen White also stars, while Aaron Sorkin wrote and directed the film.
Anne Hathaway’s Verity is projected to fall to second place in its second weekend, with Deadline forecasting $12 million after opening with $32 million domestically.
Also arriving this weekend, Angel and the Badman will open in 2,000 North American locations, while Fathom Entertainment is screening Guillermo del Toro’s Pan’s Labyrinth in more than 1,000 venues to mark its 20th anniversary.

title: Carrie  TV series  Everything to know about Mike Flanagan   s Stephen King adaptation
description: The Prime Video series stars Summer H  Howell as Carrie White who faces the pressures of teenage life in an online era
content:
The Prime Video series stars Summer H. Howell as Carrie White who faces the pressures of teenage life in an online era
Mike Flanagan’s upcoming Carrie TV series for Prime Video will bring Stephen King’s influential story about bullying, adolescence and telekinetic power to a new generation.
King’s 1974 novel has already inspired several screen adaptations, most notably Brian De Palma’s 1976 film starring Sissy Spacek.
The story was also revisited in The Rage: Carrie 2 in 1999, an NBC television adaptation in 2002 and a 2013 feature film directed by Kimberly Peirce and starring Chloé Grace Moretz.
The 2026 Prime Video series stars Summer H. Howell as Carrie White, who faces the pressures of teenage life in an era shaped by social media.
The series will explore contemporary aspects of bullying while giving Flanagan room to expand on the original story.
Flanagan has previously adapted several works by King, and the author has expressed his approval of the upcoming series.
The episodic format could allow the production to explore elements of the 1974 novel in greater detail while adapting its themes for modern audiences.
The story follows Carrie, a socially isolated teenager whose telekinetic abilities become increasingly significant as she endures bullying and difficult experiences at home and school.
With its established source material and Flanagan’s experience adapting King’s work, Carrie offers a new interpretation of a story that has remained part of popular culture for decades.
The 8-episode miniseries adaptation of Carrie is now streaming on Prime Video.

title: Real toll is far higher   Araghchi says Iran has taken out more US aircraft than disclosed in Congress report
description: Iran FM questions CENTCOM   s refusal to allow a sitting senator to inspect military bases
content:
Iran FM questions CENTCOM's refusal to allow a sitting senator to inspect military bases
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Thursday said Iran’s armed forces had destroyed more US military aircraft than cited in the Congressional Research Service (CRS), which he said had previously reported the loss of 42 aircraft.
In a post on X, Araghchi wrote, “In May, the Congressional Research Service admitted that Iran’s Armed Forces had taken out 42 US military aircraft. Now: 81.” The Iranian foreign minister claimed that the actual number was significantly higher. “Real toll is far higher,” he said.
Araghchi also questioned US Central Command’s (CENTCOM) refusal to allow a sitting senator to inspect military bases that it claimed were in good condition. He wrote, “Proof? CENTCOM won’t let a sitting senator inspect bases it claims are fine”. “You can fool all the people some of the time...” he added.
In May, the Congressional Research Service admitted that Iran’s Armed Forces had taken out 42 U.S. military aircraft. Now: 81. Real toll is far higher. Proof? CENTCOM won’t let a sitting Senator inspect bases it claims are fine. You can fool all the people some of the time... pic.twitter.com/eB3fRrJFt4
According to a recent report prepared by the nonpartisan CRS, at least 81 US fixed-wing, rotary-wing, and uncrewed aircraft were lost or damaged during military operations against Iran.
The figures compile operational incidents recorded since Feb. 28 across Pentagon records, US CENTCOM statements, military inspector general findings, and press accounts.
The compilation shows extensive losses across uncrewed platforms, led by 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones and three MQ-1 multi-role craft downed during operations, along with one MQ-4C Triton that crashed in a flight mishap. Manned combat airframes also sustained substantial hits.
Twelve F-15E Strike Eagle fighters were affected, including three destroyed by friendly fire over Kuwait, one downed over Iran, and eight that suffered light damage during an Iranian missile strike on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan before returning to service.
Iranian ground fire damaged an advanced F-35A Lightning II, while two A-10 Thunderbolt II ground-attack jets were lost or heavily damaged. Support fleets suffered major attrition as well.
Read: Iranian president says US deal ‘not out of reach’ in call with Putin
Seven KC-135 Stratotanker refuelling craft were affected, including one fatal crash in Iraq that killed six crew members and five reportedly damaged on the ground in Saudi Arabia.
One E-3 Sentry early warning plane took a direct hit, two MC-130J special operations transports were intentionally destroyed during a rescue mission, and seven military helicopters, including AH-64 Apache and AH-6 Little Bird models, were lost or damaged.
The disclosures arrive amid soaring financial tolls in the Iran war, which began Feb. 28 with coordinated US-Israeli strikes.
A Lead Inspector General report in September estimated total campaign expenses at $33.4 billion through late June, including $3.7 billion in equipment losses, while the Congressional Budget Office projected hardware replacement costs at up to $3.3 billion.
The CRS noted that the number of aircraft may remain subject to revision due to classification, ongoing combat activity, and attribution.

title: At UN  Pakistan says India provides  active support  to Taliban  backs terrorist groups
description: Says India is a serial violator of human rights that has mainstreamed Islamophobia and extremist ideologies
content:
Says India is serial violator of human rights that has mainstreamed Islamophobia and extremist ideologies
Pakistan told the United Nations that India was sponsoring terrorism against it, saying that New Delhi was providing “active support” to the Taliban authorities in Afghanistan and backing the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) through proxies in the country.
In a strongly worded right of reply by the Permanent Mission of Pakistan to the UN on Thursday, Pakistan’s UN mission said India was providing material and logistical support to the Taliban regime under the “garb of humanitarian aid”, while describing the activities of Indian authorities abroad as a “glaring example of Indian state terrorism”.
“Their newfound love for the Taliban regime is no accident,” Counsellor Muhammad Jawad Ajmal said, saying that India was using its support for the Taliban to facilitate attacks against Pakistan.
“We have once again heard the propaganda made by the Indian delegation in a further statement just now,” Ajmal said.
He described India as a “serial violator of human rights” that had “mainstreamed Islamophobia and extremist ideologies”, saying it was engineering demographic changes in the “unlawfully occupied territories of Jammu and Kashmir”.
He said these actions were being carried out in “gross violation of international law and UN Security Council resolutions”, adding that it was unfortunate for India to make what he called “false accusations and foul remarks”.
Right of Reply by Muhammad Jawad Ajmal, Counsellor at Permanent Mission of Pakistan to the UN In Response to Remarks of Indian Representative (October 7, 2026) ******** Thank you Madam Chair, We have once again heard the propaganda made by the Indian delegation in a further… pic.twitter.com/Np9VIbD2Z9
“Pakistan is fully aware of the cost of Indian sponsored terrorism on our territory,” Ajmal said, saying India is aiding and abetting terrorist groups including “the Fitna al Khawarij TTP and the Fitna al Hindustan BLA through active support of proxies inside Afghanistan”.
Ajmal said Pakistan had repeatedly warned the international community about "Indian attempts to sow discord and create mischief" in the region.
“The capture of serving Indian naval commander Kulbhushan Jadhav on Pakistani territory and his confession for acts of sabotage, espionage and multiple terrorist incidents in Pakistan that have resulted in the deaths of scores of civilians, including women and children, is a glaring example of Indian state terrorism,” Ajmal said.
“The Indian footprint of extraterritorial assassinations and killings abroad, which have now become a global feature of their illegal actions,” included an attempt by Nikhil Gupta to kill a Sikh leader in the United States and the killing of Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Canada, Ajmal said.
He said the cases had taken place “at the behest of the Indian government”, describing the allegations as public knowledge. “Let this be known to all, Pakistan will defend its sovereignty, territorial integrity, its people and its security,” Ajmal said.
“And Pakistan will do all that is needed towards this end, while maintaining its steadfast commitment to peaceful settlement of disputes and compliance with international law and the UN Charter.”
Ajmal also rejected India’s references to Operation Sindoor and Pakistan’s military response in May 2025, saying the “entire world bears witness to the ground realities and what we did”.
Pakistan’s Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Usman Jadoon, also addressed a General Assembly debate on measures to eliminate international terrorism.
Jadoon said terrorism was increasing in several parts of the world, with the threat emanating from Afghanistan having become particularly serious. “Terrorism emanating from Afghanistan, in particular, has emerged as a grave threat, besides its incidence in West Africa and the Sahel, and the Middle East.”
Statement by Ambassador Usman Jadoon, Deputy Permanent Representative of Pakistan, On Agenda Item 112: “Measures to Eliminate International Terrorism” (07 October 2026) *** Thank You Chair I congratulate you and other members of the bureau on your election and assure you of my… pic.twitter.com/lU3kAYYN3M
Pakistan had paid a heavy price for its role in the global counter-terrorism campaign since the turn of the century, including more than 100,000 lives and economic losses of more than $150 billion, he said.
He also linked recent attacks in Pakistan to groups he described as “externally-sponsored”, accusing the TTP and BLA and its Majeed Brigade of operating from Afghan soil with India’s support.
“This terrorism has resulted in the grievous loss of more than 4,700 innocent Pakistanis in just the last three years.”
Jadoon said Pakistan had responded to attacks with intelligence-based counter-terrorism operations against terrorist infrastructure and safe havens along its western border.
“These strikes are strictly targeted at TTP and BLA terrorists and are carried out with high precision and accuracy to avoid civilian casualties,” he said, rejecting “any allegations or insinuations to the contrary”.
He called for a broader international response to terrorism, arguing that the global counter-terrorism architecture had not kept pace with the changing nature of the threat.
Pakistan proposed six areas for action, including tackling threats emanating from Afghanistan and holding accountable those providing safe havens or aiding and financing terrorist groups. It also called for greater attention to the conditions conducive to terrorism, in line with the first pillar of the UN Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy (GCTS).
Jadoon said the international community should distinguish between terrorism and what Pakistan described as the “legitimate struggle of peoples against foreign occupation” and their right to self-determination.
He also called for state terrorism to be rejected, referring to Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir and the Occupied Palestinian Territory.
“Occupation and accompanying repression cannot be masked as counter-terrorism,” he said, adding that counter-terrorism measures should not be misused to violate human rights or international law.
Pakistan further called for changes to the UN counter-terrorism architecture, sanctions regimes and listing procedures so they could respond more effectively to current threats and provide what Jadoon described as a “fair, just and comprehensive mechanism”.
He also urged the international community to address terrorists’ use of new technologies for organising, recruitment and financing.
On the proposed Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism (CCIT), Jadoon said Pakistan supported the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation’s position that any consensus-based convention must distinguish terrorism from legitimate struggles for self-determination.
He criticised what Pakistan regarded as an imbalance in existing counter-terrorism policies, saying they had “singled out only the adherents of one religion – Muslims – for affiliation with terrorism and extremism”.
Any definition of terrorism should also account for emerging threats, including violence by far-right extremists, violent nationalist, xenophobic, Islamophobic and anti-Muslim groups, including Hindutva groups, he said.
Jadoon also called for state-sponsored extraterritorial assassinations, disinformation campaigns, the use of terrorist groups as proxies and “hydro terrorism” to be addressed as instruments of state policy.
Turning to India, he said New Delhi is sponsoring terrorism against Pakistan while carrying it out in IIOJK.
“It is most ironic that a country that is actively sponsoring terrorism against Pakistan, besides perpetrating state terrorism in IIOJK, is playing the victim and spreading falsehoods in this Committee yesterday,” he said.
“We have extensively documented India’s involvement in terrorism inside Pakistan and presented irrefutable evidence to the international community.”
Jadoon also referred to India’s military action against Pakistan in May 2025, accusing it of using “false pretexts and baseless allegations” and deliberately targeting civilian areas and infrastructure, including residential buildings and mosques.
He said 54 civilians, including 13 women and 15 children, had been killed.
“Pakistan exercised its right to self-defence and gave a befitting and proportionate response to the aggressor, targeted against military sites and installations only,” Jadoon said.
The response neutralised Indian fighter jets, drones and military targets, while a US-brokered ceasefire subsequently restored calm, he said.
He said India is subsequently increasing its reliance on terrorist proxies. “Following its humbling on the battlefield, India has only intensified the use of its terrorist proxies against Pakistan,” Jadoon said. “These Indian terrorist proxies will meet the same fate as its fighter jets did – in May last year.”
Jadoon also criticised the ninth review of the GCTS, saying Pakistan had hoped it would reflect key OIC concerns but had failed to address them or add value to the text. He said it was unfortunate that consensus had eluded member states and that the resolution had instead been put to a vote on the 20th anniversary of the GCTS.
Pakistan reiterated its proposal for a General Assembly subsidiary body, funded through the regular budget, to oversee balanced implementation of all four pillars of the strategy through a member-state-driven process.
The proposed body would also seek to translate the strategy’s objectives into “concrete outcomes to eliminate the menace of terrorism”.

title: Yemen's Houthis say they attacked Riyadh airport with ballistic missile | The Express Tribune
description: Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis vows retaliation, saying the attacks 'will not go unpunished'
content:
Two missiles were launched towards Riyadh, another in direction of Khamis Mushait, says spokesperson
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said on Thursday that it intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis toward Riyadh and Khamis Mushait.
Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki said on US social media platform X that two missiles were launched towards the Saudi capital, while another in the direction of Khamis Mushait in the southwestern Asir region.
التحالف: اعترضنا ودمرنا صاروخين باليستيين أطلقتهما الميليشيا الحوثية الإرهابية باتجاه الرياض.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree, meanwhile, warned experts, engineers and other workers at Saudi oil facilities against remaining at locations the group considers “targets.”
He said the warning applied both to facilities previously targeted and to other oil sites that could be targeted in future operations.
Saree also renewed the group’s warning to airlines, airport workers and passengers regarding airspace and airports that the Houthis had previously declared subject to their military operations.
The Saudi-led coalition further added that its forces had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired by Yemen’s Houthis towards Khamis Mushait, according to a statement posted on X.
التحالف: اعتراض وتدمير صاروخ باليستي أطلقته الميليشيا الحوثية الإرهابية باتجاه خميس مشيط.
Earlier on Thursday, Saree claimed that the Houthis targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with a ballistic missile, saying the strike disrupted air traffic.
He renewed a warning to international airlines operating in Saudi airspace, while excluding airspace over Makkah and Madinah.
The latest exchanges come amid a sharp escalation in Houthi missile and drone attacks against Saudi airports, military sites and oil infrastructure.
Yemeni government forces launched a new offensive under Operation “Dawn of Yemen” this week with the aim of restoring state institutions and retaking territory held by the Houthis.
According to the Reuters , smoke was seen rising from a stationary aircraft at Riyadh airport, according to a witness and three people briefed on the matter. There was no immediate official confirmation from Saudi authorities on the reported incident.
The aircraft was believed to be empty at the time, the three people briefed on the matter said.
Pakistani among 36 injured, three killed in Houthi attacks on Saudi airports
Three people were killed and 36 injured, including a Pakistani national, in attacks on two Saudi airports, Saudi authorities said late Wednesday, as fighting escalated in Yemen between Houthi and Saudi-backed government forces.
In a statement issued by Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA), the attacks targeted Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport on October 6 and 7.
"One person was killed and eight wounded in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in the ‌Saudi capital Riyadh, and two were killed and 28 wounded in an attack on facilities at Abha airport," it said.
The injured included Saudi citizens as well as a Bangladeshi resident and a Filipino resident, the authority said. At King Khalid International Airport, a Sudanese resident was killed and eight others were injured.
The wounded included five Saudi citizens, two Egyptian residents and one Pakistani resident, with their injuries also ranging from minor to critical.
“All injured individuals were transported to hospital for appropriate medical care. The two attacks also caused some property damage,” GACA said.
The aviation authority said it was coordinating with relevant agencies to assess the damage and verify the safety of the affected facilities.
“GACA is working in coordination with the relevant authorities to assess the damage, verify the safety of the facilities, and take the necessary measures to ensure the safety of passengers and maintain the security and safety of operations within the Kingdom’s civil aviation system,” it added.
#Statement Attacks Target Abha and King Khalid International Airports. #GACA pic.twitter.com/R4nrRlHRsA
A Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis vowed retaliation, saying the attacks "will not go unpunished". In a statement, the coalition said it had attacked more than 80 Houthi military sites across the governorates of Saada, Hodeidah, Jawf and ​Marib.
The Houthis attacked Aden's international airport with ballistic missiles and explosive-laden drones earlier on Wednesday, the country's Transport Ministry said.
Houthi group ​said on ‌Thursday it had attacked King ​Khalid ​International Airport in the ⁠Saudi capital, ​Riyadh, with ​a ballistic missile.
There ⁠was no immediate ​confirmation from ​Saudi ⁠Arabia of the latest ⁠attack ​claim.
Battles in Yemen have focused in recent days on areas around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a shipping route that has become more crucial for energy exports since the conflict between the US and Iran ​restricted trade through the Strait of Hormuz.
This week, Yemeni government forces with Saudi-led coalition air support launched a counteroffensive to recapture strategic territory near the strait and around the town of Mocha that the Houthis had captured in September, ​but it is unclear if their advance will hold.
The fighting, a spillover from the wider US-Iran conflict, has revived a complex 12-year war in Yemen that led to one of the worst humanitarian crises globally and fragmented the Arab world's most impoverished country. The number of people displaced since the latest round of fighting began has risen to more than 200,000, the International Organisation for Migration (IOM) said on Wednesday.
"People are running for their lives and finding nowhere safe to go," said IOM Director General Amy Pope, who called for ​more funding amid rising needs for food and shelter. Both sides allege that hundreds of people have been killed in fighting, without providing details. The UN says three in four families are going hungry in parts of ​Yemen.
The Houthis have repeatedly targeted infrastructure including airports, oil refineries and pipelines in Saudi Arabia, a US ally.
On Wednesday, the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile north of the Saudi capital Riyadh. It said it ‌was tracking ⁠the launch platform over Houthi-controlled Sanaa and would destroy it, but gave no details of casualties or damage.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said in a statement that the group had targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with several drones.
Any Houthi control of the strait could threaten shipping or global oil flows, and Saudi Arabia has been seeking international assistance to repel the Houthis. Turkey is sending mainly defensive and technical support, two officials said on Wednesday, after the NATO member and Pakistan pledged to implement a collective defence commitment under their newly formed alliance.
Syria is carefully considering providing military assistance to ally Saudi Arabia amid the escalating war against the Houthis, a US ​official and a Syrian military official briefed on the ​matter said.
Options being considered include defensive aid to ⁠protect the kingdom from attacks, or deployment of forces in an offensive capacity to help Saudi-backed Yemeni troops fight the Houthis, the officials said.
The US official said Saudi Arabia had requested that Syria deploy forces to fight the Houthis.
In response to a request for comment from the Syrian foreign ministry, a Syrian diplomat said Syria stood ​firmly with Saudi Arabia in the face of Houthi attacks but that the government's primary focus was on domestic priorities such as recovery from the country's civil ​war.
Fighting on the western front ⁠remains concentrated in the Dhubab district overlooking Bab el-Mandeb, with pro-government forces attempting an advance in the strategic hills to the east of that coastal plain, Yemeni military and government sources said.
On Monday, the Yemeni government said it had reached Mocha, which sits at a junction with a supply route to the critical battleground of Taiz, but the claim had been premature, according to Yemeni military officials on the ground and analysts.
The Houthis, who control much of Yemen's north, seized ⁠the capital Sanaa ​in 2014, prompting a military coalition led by Saudi Arabia, fearful of rival Iran's influence in Yemen and chaos on its borders, ​to intervene.
The Saudi-led coalition accuses Iran of arming, training and funding the Houthis. The group, mountain fighters who have emerged as a force of tens of thousands with missiles and drones that threaten the region, denies being part of Iran's Middle East proxy network, and says ​it develops its own weapons. Tehran also rejects the allegations.

title: Trump says he deserves Nobel Peace Prize but has doubts he will get it
description: Says he should get the prize after wading into eight conflicts since taking office    last    January
content:
Says he should get the prize after wading into eight conflicts since taking office ‌last ⁠January
US President Donald Trump, who waged war with Iran and has yet to broker peace in Ukraine, said on ​Wednesday that he should win the Nobel Peace Prize but acknowledged ‌doubt about his chances.
"I don't know what their decision is going to be," Trump said of the 2026 award, which the Norwegian Nobel Committee will announce on Friday. "They have a ​reputation for maybe not giving it to people like me."
Since his ​return to the White House last year, Trump has repeatedly ⁠said he deserves what may be the world's most prestigious award.
"It is about ​that time," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. "But I was very honored ​to receive it indirectly last time by the recipient, who said nobody in history deserves it more than President Trump."
Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado gave her 2025 Nobel Peace ​Prize medal to Trump in January as she sought US support for her efforts ​in Venezuela.
Trump said he should get the prize after wading into eight conflicts since taking office ‌last ⁠January.
Read: Kagan and Soai win 2026 Nobel chemistry prize for single molecular mirror creation
The leaders of Cambodia, Israel and Pakistan have said they nominated Trump, though there is no way of verifying that.
Parties to some conflicts Trump claims to have resolved dispute the US president's diplomatic role, and fighting has flared ​again in some of ​those regions, including ⁠the Democratic Republic of Congo and along the border between Cambodia and Thailand.
A resolution to Russia's war in Ukraine ​has eluded Trump, who promised to end it on the ​first day ⁠of his second White House term. US-Israel strikes on Iran have led to a seven-month simmering conflict that has upended global energy supplies and driven gas ⁠prices up ​before November's midterm elections.
Pope Leo, the International ​Criminal Court, and the special rapporteur for the Palestinian Territories are among the favorites to win this year.

title: Rahm quitting LIV tour over  unacceptable  terms
description: The move comes as LIV seeks new investors and a fresh start after filing for bankruptcy protection
content:
The move comes as LIV seeks new investors and a fresh start after filing for bankruptcy protection
Jon Rahm is quitting LIV Golf due to "unacceptable" terms, the star's lawyer said on Wednesday, dealing a significant blow to the divisive breakaway tour as it attempts to relaunch itself after declaring bankruptcy.
Along with Bryson DeChambeau, double major winner and former world number one Rahm was arguably the most prominent golfer to defect from the PGA Tour and join the free-spending Saudi-backed league.
But LIV filed for bankruptcy protection last month after its deep-pocketed Middle Eastern backers pulled the plug.
The tour is trying to relaunch next year with new investors as "LIV 2.0". Retaining popular stars like Rahm was widely seen as critical to its prospects.
"Mr. Rahm has independently reviewed the proposed terms of LIV 2.0 as the parties have been referring to it, and has determined that those terms are unacceptable as to him, and he will not be participating going forward in LIV 2.0," his lawyer John Beck told a U.S. Bankruptcy Court of New Jersey hearing on Wednesday.
Beck said that "advanced discussions for a consensual separation agreement of Mr. Rahm and LIV" are ongoing, according to a courtroom audio recording verified by AFP.
That agreement is expected to be presented before the court next month, he added.
"If the parties, for whatever reason, are unable to reach a consensual separation agreement, Mr. Rahm intends to press his objection" through legal channels, said Beck.
LIV Golf did not respond to an AFP request for a comment.
Launched in 2022, LIV Golf's emergence led to bitter divisions throughout the sport as several of golf's top names left the PGA Tour after signing big-money deals.
Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) poured an estimated $5 billion into the tour, before abruptly pulling the plug earlier this year.
Documents from bankruptcy filings show that LIV owes between $500 million and $1 billion in estimated liabilities to at least 1,000 creditors, including star players.
Rahm, DeChambeau and fellow golfer Dustin Johnson hold the largest unsecured claims against the tour, totaling more than $5 million each in immediate past-due payments, per the bankruptcy filing.
Still, new lead investor BC Partners Credit has pledged an initial funding commitment of a potential $300 million to help LIV relaunch in 2027.
Tour officials have outlined a shorter schedule and reduced prize money with tournaments across five continents, in locations including Australia, South Africa, Mexico, England, Hong Kong and the US.
Representatives for Rahm did not respond to an AFP request for a comment on the 31-year-old's future plans.
Widespread reports have recently linked several LIV stars with potential returns to the US-based PGA Tour.
The PGA Tour has said that it currently has no plans to offer LIV players a pathway back.
Rahm continues to play on the DP World (European) Tour, though he announced on Tuesday that he would skip the upcoming Spanish Open to attend the birth of his fourth child.

title: Ronaldo hails Messi after Argentina farewell
description: The Portuguese forward says Messi has left a lasting mark on international football
content:
The Portuguese forward says Messi has left a lasting mark on international football
Portugal captain Cristiano Ronaldo set aside one of soccer's great rivalries on Wednesday to pay tribute to Lionel Messi after the Argentine said he already missed representing his country following his emotional international retirement.
Messi, 39, delivered one final masterclass in ‌Argentina's blue and white on Tuesday, scoring once and setting up two goals in a 3-0 friendly win over Benin before more than 85,000 fans at Buenos Aires' Monumental Stadium, where his farewell became a celebration of an extraordinary 21-year international career.
"Yesterday was my last game, and I already miss wearing the blue and white. I know ⁠I'm making the right decision," Messi said in a lengthy Instagram post. "It's been an incredible journey, full of joy and also some sadness, but I know for sure that every step I took was worth it...
"I don't want to forget Diego (Maradona), who put our country where it deserved to be and who, as I always say, I know helped us both by being here with us and also from heaven, with every step we took.
"Thank you to the clubs where I played, for always respecting my feelings and allowing me to dedicate ‌myself to ⁠my country whenever it was time to put on the national team jersey..."
Messi captained Argentina to the 2022 World Cup title and Copa America triumphs in 2021 and 2024, while also helping them win the 2022 Finalissima.
"I am grateful. I love you all very much; I'm going to miss you, ⁠and I will always thank you for having been by our side, by my side," the Inter Miami playmaker added.
Messi and Ronaldo have vied for recognition as the greatest player of their generation throughout their ⁠illustrious careers, with the 41-year-old Portuguese forward among those to respond to the post.
"Leo, after so many years of defending your country, you've made history that will last forever. I ⁠have the utmost respect for what you've accomplished with Argentina. A hug," Ronaldo said.
Ronaldo, meanwhile, is embroiled in a dispute with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus following his abrupt departure from the national team's training camp.

title: Portugal jump into top five of FIFA world rankings
description: Spain remain top ahead of Argentina  France and England in the latest rankings
content:
Spain remain top ahead of Argentina, France and England in the latest rankings
Portugal was the only team that moved up in the top 10 of the updated FIFA/Coca-Cola World Rankings on Wednesday, climbing two spots to No. 5.
Brazil ‌and Morocco each fell one spot in the only other changes within the top 10, after each drew a friendly during the just-concluded international window. Portugal won all four UEFA Nations League matches during this window, beating Norway ⁠twice and Wales and Denmark once each.
Spain, fresh off winning its second World Cup this summer, built on its margin as the top-ranked team after sweeping the first four Nations League matches, beating England 3-2, Croatia twice and the Czech Republic.
Argentina remains No. 2 after beating Benin 3-0 Tuesday night in Lionel Messi's final match for his country, while France and ‌England ⁠round out the top four. Belgium, the Netherlands and Mexico complete the top 10.
The United States remains in the same spot at No. 16 despite a 4-0-0 international window that included victories over ⁠Peru (4-1), Chile (4-2), Mexico (3-0) and Canada (1-0).
Rwanda was the biggest riser in the rankings, jumping nine spots to No. 119 thanks in large part to ⁠beating World Cup darling Cape Verde 2-1 in Africa Cup of Nations qualifying on Sept. 29.
Sierra Leone was the biggest ⁠faller in this update, dropping eight spots to No. 130 after losing both Africa Cup of Nations qualifying matches.
The rankings will next be updated on Nov. 18.

title: Vega declares intention to run against Infantino
description: Former Spurs defender promises a new direction for FIFA governance
content:
Former Spurs defender promises a new direction for FIFA governance.
Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega said on Wednesday he intends to stand in next year's FIFA presidential election against fellow Swiss Gianni Infantino, becoming the first candidate to publicly declare his ambition to challenge the incumbent.
Infantino, who is seeking re-election in ‌March, has faced mounting opposition since his failed attempt in July to bring private investors into a new FIFA commercial entity holding rights linked to competitions including the World Cup.
Vega, 55, represented Switzerland from 1993 to 2001 and enjoyed a club career that included spells with Cagliari, Spurs, Celtic and Watford.
He won the League Cup with Spurs in 1999 before helping Celtic complete ⁠a domestic treble in the 2000-01 season, lifting the Scottish Premier League, Scottish Cup and Scottish League Cup.
"My purpose is straightforward: to serve football and the people who give the game its life," Vega said in his manifesto.
"I am standing to reunite the global football family, deliver genuine and lasting reform, modernise FIFA for the 21st century, restore stability and credibility, and rebuild the trust that our game urgently needs."
Last month, the Swiss Football Association became the latest national body to withdraw its support for Infantino's bid for another term as FIFA president.
The move was another setback for the 56-year-old, with ‌the ⁠football associations of England, Wales, France, Serbia and several other European countries having already withdrawn their endorsements ahead of the election.
European soccer's governing body UEFA has pledged to present a rival candidate before the November deadline.
Infantino last month wrote to FIFA's 211 member associations proposing an independent review of the governing body's decision-making processes.
Vega is ⁠the first candidate to publicly confirm his intention to challenge Infantino. Vega had also explored runs for the FIFA presidency in 2015, 2019 and 2022.
"Football does not belong to presidents, confederations or administrators," Vega added. "Football is greater than ⁠any position, any individual or any institution.
"It is the people's game and belongs to everyone: the players, coaches, referees, supporters, volunteers, clubs, leagues, associations and communities that give football its life...
"The current ⁠leadership has demoralised the game... Weak governance has damaged FIFA's credibility and eroded trust across the global football family. We must stop this conflict from escalating."
Reuters has contacted FIFA to seek comment from the governing body and Infantino.

title: SHO  gunman martyred in armed attack on police in K P s Karak
description: SHO  gunman martyred in armed attack on police in KP s Karak
content:
Police launch search operation to arrest attackers following firing incident in New Karpa area
A station house officer (SHO) and his gunman were martyred when unidentified armed assailants opened fire on a police party in the New Karpa area of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's (K-P) Karak, District Police Officer (DPO) Imran Khan said on Thursday.
According to DPO Khan, the police party from Banda Daud Shah Police Station was on routine patrol near the Karak-Kohat boundary when armed men opened fire.
SHO Daud Khan and his gunman, Farhad, were martyred in the attack, while a passerby was also injured.
Following the incident, DPO Khan reached the scene along with additional police personnel. The area was cordoned off and a search operation was launched to trace and arrest the assailants.
Further investigation into the attack is under way.
The latest incident came amid a series of attacks targeting police personnel in Karak and other districts of K-P.
On September 9, a police constable was martyred and another injured when unidentified armed men opened fire on a police vehicle during a routine patrol in Karak's Shatakai Dam area.
Earlier, on August 31, a police vehicle was targeted with an improvised explosive device (IED) in the Ghol Banda area of Banda Daud Shah, killing its driver and injuring six other personnel.
In another incident on September 28, three traffic police personnel were martyred when unidentified armed assailants attacked their vehicle in the Wazirabad area of Tank district.

title: HBLPSL 12 to return with eight teams
description: The 12th edition will feature from March 18 to May 2  2027
content:
The 12th edition will feature from March 18 to May 2, 2027
The HBL Pakistan Super League will return for its 12th edition from March 18 to May 2, 2027, with all eight franchises set to compete for the title, the Pakistan Cricket Board announced Thursday.
The tournament will retain its expanded eight-team format for a second successive season after a landmark 2026 campaign that featured the league’s first player auction and produced a record crowd for the final.
Peshawar Zalmi claimed the 2026 title by defeating debutants Hyderabad Kingsmen by five wickets at Gaddafi Stadium on May 3, ending a nine-year wait for the championship.
The PSL Governing Council finalised the 2027 window following consultations with franchise owners and representatives at a meeting in London on September 1.
Attention will now turn to squad building, with direct signings, player retentions, the trade window and the player auction among the key milestones ahead of the tournament.
PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi said the league would aim to build on the success of the previous season.
“HBLPSL 11 showed the world what this league is capable of — thrilling moments that had the whole nation transfixed, record crowds, record broadcasts,” Naqvi said.
PSL chief executive Salman Naseer said the league was determined to maintain the momentum generated by the expanded 2026 edition.
“Last season changed what people expect from this league and we intend to meet every one of those expectations in 2027,” Naseer said.
Further details on the schedule, venues, auction and ticketing arrangements will be announced in due course.
