Brent crude futures rise $2.28, or 2.28%, to $102.28 a barrel
Oil prices rose on Thursday on persistent worries about supply from the key Middle East producing ‌region amid an increase in attacks on shipping in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, while the US cut output as a hurricane menaced offshore production.
Brent crude futures rose $2.28, or 2.28%, to $102.28 a barrel by 0427 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures gained $1.66, or 1.88%, to $89.94.
Prices settled lower on Wednesday after the International Energy ​Agency agreed to accelerate the release of oil stocks and to prioritize diesel supplies under a plan launched in March, as governments ​seek to tackle record fuel prices and supply disruptions caused by the Iran war.
However, threats to oil shipping ⁠in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, which carried shipments equal to about 20% of global oil and fuel before the war, ​have increased in October as the US-Israeli conflict with Iran enters its eighth month.
Attacks on tankers sailing through the Strait of Hormuz hit their ​highest last week of any week since the Iran war began as Gulf producers increased exports. The expansion of attacks is occurring as more crude is flowing out of the Gulf but at higher costs and risk to cargoes and crew.
In the latest attack, a tanker north of Qatar was struck by multiple projectiles, causing casualties, ​the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said on Wednesday.
"The frequency of Iranian attacks on ships is now at the highest point since ​the war began, and likely to intensify further," said Saul Kavonic, MST Marquee head of energy.
Read: Oil gains as US storm and Houthi air strikes threaten supply
He noted that "constrained product flows, extreme logistics costs and high likelihood of ‌Iranian ⁠escalation are keeping prices elevated".
ANZ analyst Daniel Hynes said in a note on Thursday the IEA's oil release would likely consist of barrels that were already part of the group's original 400-million-barrel release plan at the start of the Middle East conflict, meaning it does not appear to represent an additional draw on strategic inventories.
"Ultimately, strategic stock releases can augment supply flows temporarily but do not create new production capacity," Hynes said.
Prices are ​also gaining on supply curtailments as ​a hurricane moves toward offshore production ⁠areas in the US, the world's biggest oil producer, causing companies to shut their platforms.
Shell and Chevron said on Wednesday they were curtailing offshore operations in the Gulf as Hurricane Isaias approached.
Overall, US Gulf of ​Mexico oil and gas producers had shut in about 25.08% of current oil production and 16.37% of ​current natural gas production ⁠as of Wednesday because of the storm, according to the Marine Minerals Administration.
Read more: Govt increases petrol by 88 paisas, cuts diesel by Rs1.88 for Oct 6
Inventory data from the US, also the world's biggest oil consumer, were supportive for prices as crude stockpiles fell by a higher-than-expected amount, while diesel inventories declined slightly.
Crude inventories fell by 3.2 million barrels to 424.1 million barrels in the ⁠week ended ​October 2, the Energy Information Administration said on Wednesday, compared with analysts' expectations in ​a Reuters poll for a 1.7 million-barrel decline.
Distillate fuel inventories, including diesel fuel and jet fuel, dropped by 42,000 barrels to 105.14 million barrels, well below their levels reported for ​this time of year in the past five years.

title: Security forces kill nine terrorists in North Waziristan operation  state media
description: PM Shehbaz  Naqvi laud security forces  reaffirm resolve to eliminate terrorism
content:
President Zardari, PM Shehbaz, Naqvi laud security forces, reaffirm resolve to eliminate terrorism
Security forces killed nine terrorists, including four key commanders belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij , during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in North Waziristan, Radio Pakistan reported on Thursday, citing security sources.
Fitna al - Khawarij is the term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
A large quantity of weapons and ammunition was also recovered from the terrorists, the sources added.
Nine Khawarij, including four key terrorist commanders of Fitnah al Khawarij, have been killed by security forces during an intelligence-based operation in North Waziristan @OfficialDGISPR #RadioPakistan #news https://t.co/9YHAwL2r8G pic.twitter.com/6GzZXtQcDW
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif commended the security forces for their successful operation in North Waziristan, Radio Pakistan reported.
In a statement, the president said every conspiracy by foreign-backed terrorists and their local facilitators would be foiled. He said operations against Fitna al-Khawarij under Azm-e-Istehkam would continue until the complete elimination of terrorism.
The prime minister said successful operations by the security forces against Fitna al-Khawarij reflected Pakistan’s unwavering resolve to completely eliminate terrorism.
He said the officers and personnel of the security forces were rendering commendable services towards eliminating terrorism and establishing lasting peace in the country.
He said the government would not allow terrorists to spread unrest in the country or succeed in their sordid designs.
President @AAliZardari and Prime Minister @CMShehbaz have commended security forces for their successful operation in North Waziristan @PresOfPakistan @PakPMO #RadioPakistan #news https://t.co/pTBO0NCcF5 pic.twitter.com/pcvWbwtr6r
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi paid tribute to the security forces for a successful operation against Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists in North Waziristan. “Indiscriminate operations against terrorists under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision are ongoing and will continue,” he said.
The interior minister praised the resolve of the security forces for killing nine Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists, including four commanders. “The fight against terrorism in the country will continue until all elements of Fitna al-Khawarij are completely eliminated,” Naqvi added.
The interior minister commended the professional capabilities of the security forces for their successful operations against Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists. “The entire nation stands with its brave security forces in the fight to eliminate terrorism,” he said.
The latest operations came amid continued security operations against terrorist groups in the country. Security forces on Wednesday killed 18 terrorists in separate operations in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, according to state media reports citing security sources. Thirteen Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists were killed in North Waziristan, while five Fitna al-Hindustan terrorists were killed in Mastung, Balochistan.
Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terrorist activity over the past three months, with a series of attacks across the country resulting in the martyrdom of security personnel and civilians.
Last week, 12 people were killed and 35 others injured when a blast struck a joint checkpoint near Aman Mela in the Darazinda area of Dera Ismail Khan, with the TTP claiming responsibility for the attack.
Read more: Security forces kill 11 terrorists in separate Balochistan, K-P operations
On September 19, 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred in a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, the Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
In a separate incident, a captain and a lieutenant were among six security personnel martyred in an exchange of fire in Hangu district, while eight terrorists were killed.
On September 1, six personnel, including two officers, and a customs department official were martyred as security forces thwarted an attempt to breach the Customs House in Balochistan.
In July, at least 30 people , including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. The attackers also abducted several civilians and police personnel after the assault.
In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation , which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

title: Veteran Bollywood actor Nana Patekar dies at 75
description: He collapsed after suffering a heart attack at his residence in Goa and was immediately rushed to hospital
content:
Indian media says he collapsed after suffering heart attack at his residence and was immediately rushed to hospital
Veteran Bollywood actor and filmmaker Nana Patekar has died at the age of 75 on Thursday, Indian media reported.
According to the Indian media, Patekar collapsed after suffering a heart attack at his residence in Goa and was immediately rushed to hospital.
Doctors attempted to save him for approximately 45 minutes, but he could not be revived. His death was confirmed at 5:20am, the report stated.
Dr Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Oncology Department at Manipal Hospital, said Patekar was brought dead to the hospital and was declared dead at around 5:30am, ANI reported.
Speaking to ANI, Dr Salkar said, "We had tried our best to save him, but he was brought dead. Cardiac massage was given for almost 45 minutes to an hour, but he just could not be saved."
According to the doctor, Patekar had sent a message to a friend at around 2:30am, saying "he was not feeling well". However, the friend did not see the message because it was late at night.
The friend subsequently called Patekar and reached his residence at around 4am, when the actor was sweating and gradually losing consciousness, Dr Salkar said.
#WATCH | Goa: Dr. Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Oncology Department, Manipal Hospital, says, "Nana Patekar was brought dead to the hospital... he was declared dead by 5:30 am. We had tried our best to save him, but he was brought dead. Cardiac massage was given for almost 45… https://t.co/7aX0YP0p4t pic.twitter.com/VesOdsN8Mj
He said that Patekar's caretaker was sent to the hospital to arrange an ambulance. When the emergency response team arrived at the residence, they began administering "cardiac massage" as the actor was completely "unresponsive".
"Patekar was shifted to Manipal Hospital at around 4:20am or 4:30am, where doctors continued efforts to revive him, but he could not be saved," he added.
According to Salkar, a police case had to be registered as the death was treated as a "medico-legal case (MLC)", adding that Patekar's body had been taken to "Goa Medical College for a post-mortem" examination.
He said the actor's family was not present at the hospital, while his friends and a caretaker were accompanying him.
Patekar began his acting career in 1978 with the film Guman and remained associated with the film industry for several decades.
He appeared in several successful films, including Krantiveer, Paranda, Welcome and Ab Tak Chappan. During his career, he received three National Film Awards and was also honoured with the Padma Shri in 2013.
Bollywood actor Anupam Kher paid an emotional tribute to his friend Patekar in a post on X, describing him as “one of the finest actors and human beings in Indian cinema”. Kher recalled learning of Patekar’s death shortly after finishing a performance and said it was difficult to continue meeting people while absorbing the news.
“I will miss you, my friend. Your warmth. Your hugs. Your extraordinary performances,” he wrote, adding that he would remember Patekar through his films and wished he could hug him one more time.

title: UN chief departs after concluding three day official visit to Pakistan
description: The secretary general held extensive engagements with Pakistan s leadership and senior officials during visit
content:
Guterres holds extensive engagements with Pakistan’s leadership and senior officials during visit
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres departed Pakistan on Thursday after a three-day official visit from October 6 to 8, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) said, as Islamabad reaffirmed its “unwavering commitment to multilateralism and the purposes and principles of the UN Charter”.
In a post on X, the MoFA said the visit “also reflected Pakistan’s deep appreciation for the Secretary-General’s visionary leadership and his contributions to international peace and development”.
UN Secretary-General H.E. António Guterres @antonioguterres departed Pakistan following a three-day official visit from 6 to 8 October 2026. The visit reaffirmed Pakistan’s unwavering commitment to multilateralism and the purposes and principles of the UN Charter. It also… pic.twitter.com/2rNaKv5aDC
In a separate statement, the Foreign Office (FO) said UN Secretary-General Guterres held meetings with Pakistan's leadership and senior officials during his official visit to the country from October 6 to 8.
The secretary-general held “extensive engagements with Pakistan's leadership and senior officials”, according to the statement.
On Tuesday, Guterres met Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, who reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to the UN Charter, multilateralism and the peaceful settlement of disputes through “dialogue and diplomacy”.
“The DPM/FM reiterated Pakistan's call for a just and peaceful resolution of the Jammu & Kashmir dispute in accordance with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people,” the statement said.
🔊 PR No. 2️⃣8️⃣2️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ UN Secretary-General Concludes Visit to Pakistan 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/9M8BTB0Spu
Dar also briefed Guterres on India's unilateral decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance. The decision was described by the deputy prime minister as a “blatant violation of international law”, according to the FO.
“The DPM/FM reaffirmed Pakistan's unwavering support for the Palestinian people and their legitimate struggle for self-determination and statehood,” the statement said.
The two sides also discussed regional and international peace and security, including Afghanistan and counter-terrorism, as well as sustainable development, climate change and the future of multilateralism.
Guterres also called on President Asif Ali Zardari on October 6. The meeting was followed by a special investiture ceremony at the Presidency, where Zardari conferred the Nishan-e-Imtiaz on the UN secretary-general in recognition of his “distinguished international service and contribution to global peace and development”.
A day earlier, Guterres called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and exchanged views on “issues of regional and international importance”.
Read: Guterres hails Pakistan’s role in peacekeeping, diplomacy during meetings with PM, CDF Munir
He also held meetings with the Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff, Field Marshal Asim Munir, and the Minister for Interior and Narcotics Control, Mohsin Naqvi.
“In his engagements, the Secretary-General commended Pakistan's longstanding contribution to the United Nations, including its significant role in UN peacekeeping and its efforts to promote dialogue, mediation, and international cooperation,” the FO said.
The UN chief also visited the headquarters of the United Nations Military Observer Group in India and Pakistan (UNMOGIP) in Islamabad. He attended a briefing at the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), where Pakistan's progress in “disaster preparedness and early warning systems” was highlighted.
On Wednesday, Guterres participated as a guest speaker in a special talk at the Foreign Service Academy on “Strengthening Multilateralism in a Changing World: Geopolitics and the Role of the United Nations”.
Read: Russia's Taliban outreach 'driven by US fears'
In his address, Guterres reflected on his longstanding association with Pakistan and highlighted the “generosity, resilience, and solidarity” of the Pakistani people.
The FO said the secretary-general's remarks drew on his two decades of service to the United Nations, including his time as UN High Commissioner for Refugees. “The visit provided an important opportunity to reaffirm Pakistan's longstanding partnership with the United Nations and to exchange views on key regional and international developments,” the FO said.
“It also underscored Pakistan's unwavering support for multilateralism, with the United Nations at its core, and its abiding commitment to the purposes and principles of the UN Charter,” it added.

title: Trump says US will not attack Iran before midterm elections
description: Iran rejects giving up uranium enrichment  handing over enriched stockpile
content:
Iran rejects giving up uranium enrichment, handing over enriched stockpile
US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the US would not attack Iran before the midterm elections because the two sides were engaged in “productive discussions.”
“We will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd,” Trump wrote on his social media platform Truth Social.
Trump said the US and Iran were having “productive discussions,” while maintaining that a blockade of Iran "will remain in full force and effect".
BREAKING: Trump on Iran: We will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd. https://t.co/UOCKMtsKEt
Trump also claimed that oil was flowing through the Strait of Hormuz at “record numbers,” claiming that 22 million barrels had passed through the waterway later on Wednesday and that “not one barrel” came from or was going to Iran.
“Iran will not have a nuclear weapon!” he added.
His comments came amid media reports that the White House asked the Pentagon to develop options for strikes on Iranian targets that could be carried out before the midterm elections.
Iran rejects giving up uranium enrichment, handing over enriched stockpile
Iran would not give up its right to enrich uranium or hand over its enriched uranium stockpile, the country's nuclear chief Mohammad Eslami said on Thursday.
Speaking to reporters, Eslami, head of the Atomic Energy Organisation of Iran, said uranium enrichment was an inseparable part of the nuclear process, according to state broadcaster IRIB .
When asked whether Tehran could abandon uranium enrichment, he said: “Under no circumstances.”
Iran’s nuclear chief says Tehran will not give up its right to uranium enrichment or hand over its uranium stockpile. pic.twitter.com/HQJn6s4TKD
“How can you claim to have a nuclear industry without having the starting point of the process?” he asked.
Eslami said the nuclear industry was a driving force behind scientific and technological development, stressing that Iran would not retreat from its right to technological advancement.
He also ruled out handing over Iran's enriched uranium stockpile, saying: “No, there is no such thing.”
Regarding cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency, Eslami said inspections of nuclear facilities damaged by US-Israeli attacks remained impossible because of continuing security threats.
“The agency itself knows that the facilities have been bombed and that the threat remains active,” he said.
Eslami said Iranian legislation restricted cooperation with the UN nuclear watchdog, particularly over concerns about the safety of nuclear facilities, personnel and researchers.
“As long as security is not established, naturally, their entry is not possible,” he added.
However, Eslami said IAEA inspectors had visited facilities that were not targeted in the attacks and carried out routine inspections under arrangements made by Tehran.
He criticised the agency for failing to acknowledge those inspections and accused it of acting under pressure from the US and Israel to gather information about damaged nuclear facilities.
The remarks came amid continuing disagreements between Tehran and the IAEA over access to nuclear sites damaged in US-Israeli strikes.
Iran's parliament approved legislation in June 2025 suspending cooperation with the IAEA following Israeli and US attacks on the country's nuclear facilities. The legislation made inspections conditional on security guarantees and approval by Iran's Supreme National Security Council.
Iran's Natanz, Fordow and Isfahan nuclear facilities were targeted during the June 2025 conflict, while Natanz was struck again during US-Israeli attacks in March 2026.
In June, the IAEA Board of Governors adopted a resolution calling on Tehran to provide information about its enriched uranium stockpiles and grant inspectors access to verify nuclear material.
The agency had said it remained unable to verify the status and whereabouts of Iran's enriched uranium stockpile because of restricted access to nuclear facilities.
Tehran maintains that its nuclear program is exclusively peaceful and insists that uranium enrichment is its legitimate right under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.
Iran's Pezeshkian says Tehran cannot be easily isolated amid strong ties with neighbours
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Thursday that Iran cannot be easily isolated, pointing to the country’s ties and extensive exchanges with its neighbors.
“They cannot isolate us so easily because we have 15 neighboring countries in the region, and through each of these routes, we can maintain many of our economic, commercial, political and security exchanges,” Pezeshkian told reporters before departing for Turkmenistan, according to Iranian state broadcaster IRIB .
He said opportunities arising from regional engagement could also contribute to developing Iran’s interactions, regulations and trade.
“I hope we can achieve the objectives we have in mind and will pursue through our discussions,” he added.
Strait of Hormuz security depends on Iran’s will and readiness, says navy commander
Iranian Navy Commander Rear Admiral Shahram Irani stressed the strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz, saying its security depended on the will, vigilance and readiness of Iran’s defenders, IRNA reported on Thursday
In a message to Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy Commander Rear Admiral Ali Ozamaei on the occasion of the Day of the IRGC Naval Force, Irani said the sea was an arena of vital interests for Iran and one of the most important manifestations of safeguarding national security and authority.
He said protecting this maritime front required personnel who combined faith and knowledge with courage and readiness and were prepared to respond without delay in moments of danger.
Irani said the IRGC Naval Force had played a pivotal role in protecting Iran’s national interests and securing the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz through years of sustained presence and efforts across the Persian Gulf.
Navy commander: Hormuz security depends on Iran’s will and readiness https://t.co/r6JHigtUQh pic.twitter.com/1VAg56vpSU
He attributed these efforts to the force’s reliance on domestic capabilities and what he described as a spirit of jihad.
The Iranian Navy commander said this responsibility had become even more important during the Ramadan War and the Hormuz Battle, when IRGC forces defended the country’s territory and interests against the aggression by the “American-Zionist enemy”.
He said the operations had once again demonstrated that the security of the strategic waterway rested on the will and readiness of Iran’s defenders.
Iran’s armed forces stronger, more prepared than ever: deputy commander
Iran’s deputy commander-in-chief, Brigadier General Mohammad Hossein Dadras, said the country’s armed forces were stronger and more prepared than ever, PressTV reported on Thursday.
He also highlighted the continued presence and resilience of the Iranian people.
Iran’s armed forces more prepared than ever, says deputy commander-in-chief Brigadier General Mohammad Hossein Dadras says the country’s armed forces are stronger and more prepared than ever. He also highlights the continued presence and resilience of the Iranian people. pic.twitter.com/WTR1jPg43S
Iranian intelligence sets sights on US military bases in Germany, WiWo reports
Iranian intelligence services are targeting US military bases in Germany, including Ramstein and Spangdahlem, amid concerns over potential covert attacks linked to the Iran conflict, German news outlet WirtschaftsWoche reported on Thursday.
Israel warned US and German partners three weeks ago of a potential threat, with concern focused on bases supporting US military operations and logistics linked to the conflict with Iran, the report said, citing several unnamed Western intelligence officials.
The German defence ministry and the US forces in Germany were not immediately available for comment.
Trump says Iran deal 'isn't really something that I want to do'
US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that his special envoy Steve Witkoff is "doing very well" in negotiations with Iran while indicating that a deal is not his preferred outcome.
"He's working on the Iran deal and doing very well. I think the deal isn't really something that I want to do, but they're willing to offer us anything to stop," Trump told supporters at a campaign rally in San Antonio, Texas.
"They will never have a nuclear weapon," he added. Trump described Witkoff as "a great negotiator" who has "done some phenomenal things," citing the ceasefire deal in Gaza.
The president also said he expects the war with Iran to end soon. "That war ends – it's going to be very soon. It's got to be very soon," he said, describing Iran as "a failed nation."
His remarks came as media reports said that the White House has asked the Pentagon to develop options for strikes on Iranian targets that could be carried out before the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
Trump may order new strike on Iran before midterms: reports
The White House has asked the Pentagon to develop options for strikes on Iranian targets that could be carried out before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, according to media reports on Wednesday.
Asked about the reports, a Pentagon official told Anadolu: "The Department's job is to develop and present military options to the president."
The official did not confirm or deny the reports.
The Atlantic reported, citing two administration officials, that the size and targets of any potential strikes—and whether the administration will ultimately proceed— are still being debated. Trump's advisers believe the right moment for new strikes would be after the midterms rather than before, the magazine said.
Read: Vance says Iran must cut enrichment to end war
A White House official told The Atlantic that Trump "has all options available at any time," but did not address questions about the timing of possible strikes.
Separately, Axios reported that the Pentagon instructed US Central Command (CENTCOM) several days ago to conclude preparations for resuming major combat operations in Iran, citing US officials.
The directive did not include a specific date for launching strikes, according to the report.
Attacks on tankers in Hormuz hit highest of any week since start of Iran war, sources say
Attacks on tankers sailing through the Strait of Hormuz hit their highest last week of any week since the ​Iran war began, according to maritime security sources tracking incidents, amid ‌a bigger export push by Gulf producers.
Attacks, attempted attacks, and harassment activity, including drone overflights, surveillance, and hailing using VHF radio by Iran's Revolutionary Guards, have persisted ​in the strait, the US Navy-led Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) said ​in a note on Sunday.
"These actions continue to demonstrate Iran’s ⁠intent to assert presence along key transit lanes and maintain pressure ​on transiting vessels," the JMIC said.
In the week of September 28-October 5, there ​had been at least 12 attacks on oil, liquefied natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas tankers around the Strait of Hormuz, according to data from three maritime security ​sources who analysed incidents based on information received from the area.
Read more: UN chief heads to Islamabad to boost Pakistan-led US-Iran peace talks
That ​was the highest number of attacks in a single week since the US war with ‌Iran ⁠began on February 28, the sources said.
Separate data collated by the UN's shipping agency, the International Maritime Organisation (IMO), showed nine incidents involving vessels in the same week.
The UN body tends to take longer to verify and ​officially record incidents, ​maritime sources say.
The ⁠closest week in terms of comparable incidents was the week of July 13, when there were eight incidents, ​separate IMO data showed.
Gulf oil exporters topped pre-war levels for ​about half ⁠of September, shipping data showed on Monday, though attacks on tankers and logistical constraints cloud the outlook for sustained higher flows.
India's foreign ministry said on ⁠Tuesday that ​12 crew members were injured after an unknown ​projectile struck Panama-flagged oil tanker On Peace while it was passing through the Strait of ​Hormuz.

title: Hasnain  Khalid and Dahani star in President   s Trophy
description: Hasnain Nadeem hits 121 while Khalid Usman and Shahnawaz Dahani deliver five wicket plus hauls on day two
content:
Hasnain Nadeem hits 121 while Khalid Usman and Shahnawaz Dahani deliver five-wicket-plus hauls on day two
Hasnain Nadeem scores century, while Khalid Usman and Shahnawaz Dahani produced impressive bowling performances on the second day of the fifth round of the President’s Trophy Grade-I played across four venues on Wednesday.
At the Abbottabad Cricket Stadium, Ghani resumed their first innings at the overnight score of 67 for seven against PTV and were dismissed for 102. Test fast bowler Haris Rauf took four wickets, while Israr Hussain and Kashif Ali picked up three wickets apiece.
In turn, PTV were led by Taimur’s 97, while Yasir Khan contributed 71. Taimur’s innings included eight fours and five sixes. Mohammad Ammar coming in to bat at number five remained unbeaten on 80 as PTV strengthened their position to reach 324 for four at the close of play.
Right-arm fast bowler Khurram Shahzad took two wickets for Ghani.
At the Imran Khan Stadium in Peshawar, the match between Khan Research Laboratories and State Bank of Pakistan got underway after no play was possible on the opening day due to rain. SBP won the toss and elected to field first.
Mohammad Abbas and Shahid Aziz took three wickets each, while Sirajuddin picked up two as KRL lost eight wickets during the day and were 127 for eight at stumps. Saqib Khan was KRL’s leading run-getter with 35.
At the Shoaib Akhtar Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi, MIT Solutions resumed their first innings at the overnight score of 186 for eight. Hasnain Nadeem unbeaten on 87 overnight went on to score 121 before MIT Solutions were bowled out for 223.
Opening batter Hasnain’s innings included 18 fours and one six.
In turn, OGDCL’s innings were led by Rohail Nazir, who scored a 110-ball 52, hitting seven fours. Khalid Usman grabbed six wickets as MIT Solutions dismissed OGDCL for 193 in 63.4 overs.
After securing a 30-run first-innings lead, MIT Solutions lost one wicket in their second innings and were 29 for one at stumps.
At the Diamond Cricket Ground in Islamabad, Kingsmen Academy resumed at the overnight score of 31 for one and were bowled out for 217. Mohammad Shayan top-scored with 66, while right-arm fast bowler Shahnawaz Dahani grabbed five wickets and Shehzad Gul bagged four.
In turn, SNGPL made a solid start with Test opening batter Azan Awais unbeaten on 53 and former Test captain Shan Masood not out on 45 at stumps. The pair added 81 runs for the third wicket as SNGPL reached 140 for two in 35 overs when stumps were drawn.

title: Pakistan  IMF reach staff level agreement on  1 2b loan
description: Islamabad agrees to promptly phase out fuel subsidy scheme  and enhance governance of the state owned companies
content:
Islamabad agrees to promptly phase out fuel subsidy scheme, and enhance governance of the state-owned companies
Pakistan and the International Monetary Fund have reached a staff-level agreement on $1.2 billion two loan tranches after Islamabad agreed to promptly phase out fuel subsidy scheme, bring improvements in social and health sector spending, and enhance governance of the state-owned companies.
“The IMF team has reached a staff-level agreement with the Pakistani authorities on the fourth review of the 37-month Extended Arrangement under the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the third review of the 28-month arrangement under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF), according to an early morning statement issued by the IMF.
It added that the staff-level agreement is subject to approval by the IMF Executive Board. Upon approval, Pakistan will have access to about $1billion under the EFF and about $210 million under the RSF, bringing total disbursements under the two arrangements to about $5.7 billion.
The IMF team was led by Ms. Iva Petrova and held discussions under the 2026 Article IV consultation and on the fourth review under the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the third review under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF) in Karachi and Islamabad from September 23 to October 7, 2026.
In a statement, Iva Petrova said that “the fuel support scheme should be phased out promptly, given its high cost and broad targeting”. The mission chief added that any future fuel support—should oil prices surprise on the upside—should be limited, time-bound, targeted using established social assistance programmes, and accommodated within the FY27 budget envelope.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had announced the three-month scheme and allocated Rs75 billion to compensate Rs100 per litre on 20 litres monthly consumption by motorcyclists and 30 litres by up to 800 cc car owners. He had met with the Managing Director of the IMF to convince her but could not succeed.
The Express Tribune had reported that the IMF objected to untargeted subsidy and its high cost. The government officials had claimed that despite objections, the scheme would continue for three months.
Petrova further said that Pakistan remained “committed to increasing health and education spending further to 2.8% of GDP in FY27, closely monitoring implementation, and reallocating resources as needed to meet this objective”.
The 2.8% of GDP target is now lower than nearly 3% or Rs4.24 trillion given by the IMF earlier, as the four provinces had allocated less resources in their budgets compared to the target agreed with the IMF.
Iva said that the Pakistani authorities had arrested the long-term decline in health and education spending, raising it from 2.2% of GDP in fiscal year 2023-24 to 2.5% of GDP in FY26.
The Secretary Finance Imdad Ullah Bosal said that Pakistan met the fiscal year 2025-26 IMF condition on health and education spending.
The Mission Chief said that the planned increase in targeted cash-transfer benefits, together with continued improvements in beneficiary coverage and payment systems, will strengthen protection for vulnerable households and support more inclusive growth.
The IMF said that Pakistan has successfully navigated the impact of the Middle East conflict, and strong policies have helped preserve macroeconomic stability.
Real GDP growth reached 4% in the first three quarters of FY26, and although higher energy prices and supply disruptions weakened the momentum somewhat, FY26 growth is estimated at 3.6%.
Headline inflation, after peaking in May, moderated to about 10.3% in September, while core inflation remained contained.
The current account was broadly balanced in FY26, supported by strong remittances, and gross reserves rose to about over $21 billion by end-September, according to the IMF.
“Nevertheless, risks remain high, particularly from geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices, tighter global financial conditions, and trade disruptions”, said the IMF.
It said that the Pakistani authorities remain committed to sound macroeconomic policies, which are critical to safeguarding stability amidst the ongoing shock-prone environment. The authorities’ policy priorities include:
The government has reassured the IMF that it would achieve the primary budget surplus target of 2% of GDP in this fiscal year on the back of tax policy and revenue administration measures, is critical to placing public debt on a durable downward path.
Revenue administration reforms, including improved risk-based audits, digital invoicing, and use of third-party data, will help safeguard the revenue targets. A comprehensive medium-term tax reform strategy should make the system fairer, simpler, and more growth-friendly, while protecting revenues and reducing distortions.
It said that Pakistan was also making progress in strengthening public financial management to improve the efficiency and transparency of the budget process, public investment, procurement, and government cash management. They remain committed to reducing debt rollover risks and servicing costs amid elevated gross financing needs, while advancing the development of the domestic government securities market and diversifying the investor base.
The IMF emphasized that the SBP should maintain an appropriate monetary stance and exchange rate flexibility. “The SBP should continue maintaining an appropriately tight policy stance to ensure inflation returns durably to the SBP’s target range”.
It added that the exchange rate flexibility should continue to serve as an important shock absorber, while further reserve accumulation, gradual liberalization of the foreign exchange regime, and deeper domestic financial markets will strengthen resilience and support private sector development.
The IMF has again stressed that timely tariff adjustments and cost-reducing reforms remain essential to prevent renewed circular debt accumulation while protecting vulnerable consumers. Priorities include improving sector efficiency, advancing private participation in distribution, deepening electricity market competition, maintaining gas sector cost recovery, and reducing unaccounted-for gas losses.
Iva said that the Article IV consultation focused on reforms to support the structural transformation of the economy to higher value-added activities and reduce gaps relative to peer countries in key areas, including by strengthening competition, reducing regulatory and trade barriers, advancing privatization, enhancing SOE governance and transparency, and strengthening governance and anti-corruption institutions.
Together with efforts to introduce a simpler and fairer tax system, allocate greater public resources toward human and capital development, ensure a more cost-efficient energy sector, and deepen financial markets, these reforms are critical to raise productivity, increase labour force participation and job creation, and support private investment and exports.
In a post on X, the Ministry of Finance said IMF Mission Chief Iva Petrova held a “wrap-up session” with Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb at the Q Block of the Pak Secretariat in Islamabad following the conclusion of the fourth review of the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the third review of the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).
At the conclusion of Fourth Review of Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and Third review of Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF), IMF Mission Chief Ms. Iva Petrova held a wrap up session with the Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue, Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb, at the Q… pic.twitter.com/KmIjVYqJsn
The ministry said Finance Secretary Imdad Ullah Bosal and IMF Resident Representative Mahir Binici were also present.

Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly and Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party (PkMAP) Chairman Mahmood Khan Achakzai has said meaningful dialogue between the government and opposition cannot produce tangible results unless direct consultations are held with PTI founder Imran Khan.

On regional developments, he welcomed international diplomatic efforts aimed at resolving issues involving Afghanistan. He said the international community had a responsibility to contribute to lasting peace, stability and economic development in the region.

Afridi calls for supremacy of Constitution, rule of law and protection of fundamental rights
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) long march entered its fourth day on Wednesday, reaching Shalobar in Bara tehsil of Khyber district, the hometown of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, where local elders, tribal leaders and youth accorded a warm welcome to the chief minister and participants of the march.
Addressing the participants at Basee Baba Chowk, Chief Minister Sohail Afridi said Pakistan belonged to all its citizens and stressed that Pakhtuns had always rendered sacrifices for the country and would continue to play their role in safeguarding its security and stability.
He said the PTI would continue its political and democratic struggle for the release of party founder Imran Khan. Despite political differences, he added, the security, unity and stability of Pakistan were a collective responsibility of all citizens.
The chief minister called for ensuring the supremacy of the Constitution and law, independence of the judiciary, freedom of the press and protection of the rights of political workers.
Criticising the government, Afridi alleged that the prevailing political leadership was contributing to division and tension in the country and that constitutional and judicial orders were not being implemented. He said Pakistan did not belong to any particular family or class but to every citizen, whose constitutional rights must be protected by the state and all institutions.
Afridi urged lawyers, judges, journalists, students and young people, as well as members of other sections of society, to play their role in a peaceful and democratic struggle for the protection of the Constitution, law, freedom and fundamental rights.
He said constitutional supremacy and the rule of law were essential foundations for political and social stability in the country.
Giving details of the march's next phase, the chief minister said participants would stay overnight at Shalobar D Road after completion of the fourth day's activities. The caravan would leave for Peshawar the following day as part of its onward journey.

title: Eritrean troops deployed in Ethiopia s Tigray region
description: Eritrean troops deployed in Ethiopia s Tigray region
content:
Eritrean troops have deployed in Ethiopia's northern Tigray region, multiple sources said Wednesday, threatening to turn an internal conflict into a wider regional war.
Fighting broke out between the rebel Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and Ethiopian federal forces on September 23, sparking fears of a return to the devastating 2020-2022 civil war.
Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing the rebels, and the two neighbours severed diplomatic ties last week.
The Ethiopian army has successfully pushed back the Tigrayan rebels with the help of local militias and entered the regional capital of Mekelle at the weekend without a fight as the TPLF abandoned the city.
Multiple sources told AFP that Eritrean troops have crossed the border and were positioned around Adigrat, some 115 kilometres (70 miles) north of Mekelle, and were pushing south.
Eritrea fears landlocked Ethiopia plans to invade to seize direct access to the Red Sea, and analysts say it wants to prevent the war reaching its territory.
"The Eritrean army has entered Tigray in uniform, equipped with heavy weaponry," said Gebreigziabher Beyene, commander of the Tigray Peace Force, a pro-government militia that has fought alongside the Ethiopian army.
"This force is being struck by drones," he said, adding Eritrea was "deliberately deploying its forces so that the fighting takes place inside Tigray rather than spilling into Eritrea".
In a statement on X, Eritrea's information minister, Yemane Meskel, did not deny that troops had crossed the border, but said Ethiopia's government was creating "a fallacious narrative of 'self-defence' to rationalise and camouflage its war of aggression".
In Adigrat, two eyewitnesses told AFP they saw Eritrean soldiers on the streets, heading south in lorries with heavy weaponry.
A local official, speaking to AFP on condition of anonymity, said the troops had been there for days and "the population is very concerned".
Conflict monitor ACLED said Eritrean troops had crossed the border at Zelambesa on Wednesday.
And it said Tigrayan rebel forces were "heavily present" around Wukro, a town along the same road that leads to the regional capital.
"Eritrean forces entered the war in Tigray to halt the Ethiopian government and allied forces from reaching the border and potentially fighting within Eritrea's territory," ACLED said in a briefing note.

title: Bangladesh nuclear plant draws hope   and worry
description: Bangladesh nuclear plant draws hope   and worry
content:
Bangladesh is preparing to switch on its first nuclear power plant, a long-delayed project promising relief from chronic electricity shortages -- even as some fear living beside it.
The 2.4-gigawatt Rooppur nuclear plant, a $13-billion project more than a decade in the making, has transformed the once sleepy nearby village of the same name, bringing Russian workers, new businesses and jobs.
Once fully operational, its two reactors are expected to supply more than 10 percent of electricity demand in the South Asian nation of 170 million people, which has been hit hard by the fuel crisis sparked by the conflict in the Middle East.
For Md Zahedul Hasan, managing director of state-owned Nuclear Power Plant Company Bangladesh, the giant complex represents the culmination of a decades-old ambition to bring nuclear power to the country.
The plant's first reactor is scheduled to be turned on by the end of this year, and the second unit "will be operational within a year", Hasan said at the site on the banks of the Padma River, 150 kilometres (93 miles) west of Dhaka.
Bangladesh's power sector is dominated by fossil fuels, particularly natural gas, with coal, oil and renewables making up the rest.
The project, built with Russian state nuclear corporation Rosatom, has also brought an unlikely Russian enclave to rural Bangladesh.
Thousands of Russian workers have spent years building and installing equipment, with a residential complex, shops and restaurants springing up around them.
Shop signs appear in Bangla, English and Russian, while some restaurants serve borscht soup alongside local dishes.
Alexander Vladimirovich Skvortsov, a Russian installation technician, said he had a choice between working in Turkey or Bangladesh. He chose Rooppur, moving there with his family in 2024.
"When I first saw the construction site at Rooppur, I realized how much work lay ahead on this project... honestly, Rooppur changed me and my life," he told AFP.
The project has also transformed the local economy.
Md Emon Khan, 28, left his garment-factory job in Dhaka and returned to Rooppur, where he now sells vegetables and fruit to workers.
"I can speak a bit of Russian, and they can speak Bangla, too," he said.
Plant officials say stringent safety measures have been followed and lessons from previous nuclear accidents were incorporated into the project.
Standing near a radiation monitoring tower and an alarm post, 15-year-old Mohammad Nafiz said he saw little to fear.
"We are glad that Rooppur is known to the world, and my friends and I hope that we will work at the plant after graduating from engineering schools," he added.
Md Yunus Ali, 80, whose home is a 15-minute walk from the plant, said opposition to building a nuclear facility in the densely populated area dates back decades.
"A few days ago, they ran a compressor test with a big bang... even the children who were asleep woke up in fear," said Ali, a retired paper mill worker.
"I am old now, and I am not afraid for my life... but I have children and grandchildren, and I want safety for them."
The ambition to build a nuclear power plant at Rooppur dates back to the 1960s.
Several attempts came after independence, including approaches to Saudi Arabia and France, and talks with China and South Korea. No deals materialised.
Bangladesh finally signed an agreement with Moscow in 2015, with the Russian state offering a loan covering about 90 percent of the project's original cost.
The project has since faced delays, including disruption from the Covid-19 pandemic and sanctions on Russia after its invasion of Ukraine, which complicated equipment deliveries and payments.
There have also been corruption allegations surrounding the project, including against ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina and members of her family. They have rejected the accusations.
For most Bangladeshis, however, the biggest question is when Rooppur will finally deliver reliable electricity.
Belly Begum, a 55-year-old farmer, struggles to irrigate her land during frequent power cuts.
"I wish the Rooppur nuclear power plant goes into operation soon, and we reap the full benefit," she said.
"I hope we will get electricity for 24 hours without interruption, as the plant is near my house."

content:
Meeting emphasises soil testing and the use of fertilisers according to crop requirements
The wheat cultivation target for Multan division has been set at 1.776 million acres for the 2026-27 season, up from 1.760 million acres last year.
The target was reviewed at a meeting chaired by Multan Division Commissioner Aamir Karim Khan and attended by the deputy commissioners of Multan, Khanewal, Lodhran and Vehari, agriculture officials and representatives of other departments.
District-wise targets have been set at 445,000 acres for Multan, 503,000 acres for Khanewal, 376,000 acres for Lodhran and 452,000 acres for Vehari.
The commissioner directed the authorities to ensure wheat cultivation on all land allotted under the Apna Khet Apna Rozgar programme and called for coordinated strategies at district and tehsil levels to achieve the targets.
He directed the Agriculture Department and district administrations to provide farmers with timely guidance, quality seed, fertilisers, irrigation water and information about modern farming practices. He also ordered strict action against the overpricing of fertilisers and seed, stressing that farmers should receive quality agricultural inputs at officially notified rates.
The meeting emphasised soil testing and the use of fertilisers according to crop requirements.
The commissioner directed officials to educate farmers about soil health and nutrient deficiencies and promote balanced fertiliser use to improve crop productivity.
A detailed briefing was also given on the availability of canal water. The commissioner directed the irrigation department to coordinate with relevant authorities.

title: Plastic ban enforcement in Faisalabad questioned
description: Plastic ban enforcement in Faisalabad questioned
content:
Probe recommends survey of factories producing bags below prescribed 75-micron thickness
A provincial government probe report has questioned the enforcement of Punjab's plastic bag regulations in Faisalabad, observing that action against retailers appears to be continuing while manufacturers, wholesalers, distributors and other major suppliers of prohibited plastic bags remain largely unchecked.
According to the report, clear restrictions have been imposed in Faisalabad under the Punjab government's environmental policy and prescribed regulations concerning the quality and thickness of plastic shopping bags. However, the manufacturing, supply, sale and use of plastic bags thinner than 75 microns continue in the district.
The report said prohibited plastic bags were still being provided at general stores, grocery shops, fruit and vegetable stalls, bakeries, medical stores and other commercial establishments. In some areas, such bags were found openly displayed inside or outside shops, while shopkeepers continued to use them during routine transactions.
It observed that although action had been taken against some retailers and prohibited bags confiscated, effective and sustained action against factories, manufacturing units, wholesale dealers and major suppliers was not evident.
The report said restricting enforcement to retailers would not achieve the government's objective if the primary sources manufacturing and supplying prohibited bags continued to operate.
It recommended a comprehensive survey of factories and manufacturing units producing plastic shopping bags across the district and the preparation of a complete list of such entities.
The report also called for scientific testing of bag thickness and strict legal action against manufacturers found producing bags below the prescribed 75-micron limit.
It recommended effective monitoring of wholesale markets and distribution networks to trace the supply chain.
It further recommended re-inspection of factories and individuals previously subjected to enforcement action to ensure that violations did not resume.

title: Lahore s air quality takes a hit
description: Lahore s average AQI on Wednesday evening stood at 155  readings show significant variation across the city
content:
Lahore's average AQI on Wednesday evening stood at 155; readings show significant variation across the city
The city's air quality has deteriorated to unhealthy levels as authorities move to tighten vehicle inspections and crack down on smoke emission ahead of the annual smog season.
Lahore's average Air Quality Index (AQI) on Wednesday evening stood at 155, placing the city in the "unhealthy for sensitive groups" category, according to live data from the Punjab Environmental Protection Agency's monitoring network.
The readings showed significant variation across the city. Safari Park recorded the highest AQI at 172, followed by Shahdara at 168, Egerton Road 162, DHA Phase 6 at 160 and Wagah Border 159. GT Road recorded 158, Barki Road 157 and Kahna Nau 152, while Multan Road stood at 149 and Punjab University 132.
Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) was a major component of the pollution readings, with concentrations reaching 103.9 microgrammes per cubic metre at Safari Park and 95.6 at Shahdara.
The deterioration comes as Lahore enters the period when air pollution typically intensifies, with vehicle emissions, industrial pollution, brick-kiln smoke, crop-residue burning and construction dust among the sources contributing to poor air quality.
Lahore was among the world's most polluted major cities in the AQI ranking for Wednesday, with a reading of 156 placing it fifth behind Singapore, Kuala Lumpur, Kolkata and Delhi.
The rankings are based on live readings and can change significantly within hours depending on weather conditions, emissions and other factors. IQAir's live ranking placed Lahore among the world's 10 most polluted major cities.
Against this backdrop, the Punjab Provincial Transport Authority decided to begin a crackdown from October 15 on private vehicles without fitness certificates.
The province has around 2.3 million registered private vehicles, while 20 Provincial Vehicle Inspection and Certification System centres have been designated for fitness certification. Of these, 14 are in Lahore, two in Faisalabad and one each in Sargodha, Multan, Sadiqabad and Rahim Yar Khan.
The authority has issued fresh instructions to all centres to remain operational round the clock, seven days a week, in order to cope with the expected demand before enforcement begins.
The centres have been directed to maintain stocks of inspection stickers. Failure to comply with the instructions will be considered a breach of licensing conditions.

title: LHC seeks report on 500 missing girls
description: LHC seeks report on 500 missing girls
content:
CJ stresses need to change police mindset
Lahore High Court (LHC) Chief Justice Aalia Neelum has expressed concern over more than 500 pending cases of abducted girls in Punjab and directed the provincial police chief to submit a detailed report.
The court was hearing a case concerning a 16-year-old missing girl who was produced before the bench after police recovered her following judicial intervention. The case was disposed of after her rescue.
Chief Justice Neelum asked Inspector General of Police Rao Abdul Kareem whether the girl produced before the court was the same whose photograph was on the court record. The IGP confirmed that she was.
The chief justice asked why such a large number of cases remained pending despite committees having been formed to deal with those involving women and children. "If committees had been formed, why is the situation still like this?" the court asked.
It observed that a girl who had been missing for two years had been recovered shortly after the high court took notice of the matter, asking how many other girls had remained missing for long periods.
The court also expressed concern over the police's attitude towards cases involving women, observing that there was a mindset within the department about what a girl involved in a case might be like. "This mindset needs to change," the court observed.
The chief justice remarked that more than 500 missing-girl cases was a very large number and asked officials to consider the suffering of parents whose daughters had disappeared.
Speaking to the media, the IGP.said the police would review all cases involving women and children, including the quality of investigation, outcomes and follow-up.
He said around 3,200 such cases had been recorded up to January 2025, while 500 cases dating from January 1, 2021, remained pending.
He said the police would determine whether missing women had been recovered and whether the cases had been properly concluded.
The IGP said recovery of missing women was essential and stressed the need for continuous capacity-building of investigating officers.
The LHC dismissed a plea to stop an inquiry against officers of the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) over allegations that a British citizen of Pakistani origin and his brother were forced to hand over cash, vehicles and documents during their detention, observing that such incidents could undermine public confidence in state institutions.
Justice Jawad Zafar dismissed the petition filed by Akmal Hussain who had requested the court to restrain the inquiry ordered by the Faisalabad Justice of Peace against FIA Director Saqib Sultan, Inspector Ajmal Hussain and other officials over alleged misuse of authority.
The court held after examining the record and hearing detailed arguments that the inquiry should proceed and observed that the order of the Justice of Peace was justified.
The petitioner British citizen Salman Babar's counsel, Advocate Mian Dawood, told the court that he was of Pakistani origin and ran a vehicles' business in the United Kingdom who had returned to Pakistan after 16 years.

The meeting was told that the province had released 974,982 tonnes of wheat to the market last year. The additional PASSCO and imported stocks are expected to strengthen market supply and help contain price fluctuations.

title: 63 refuse postings  but only 20 face the axe
description: 63 refuse postings  but only 20 face the axe
content:
Sindh Board of Revenue officials allege selective action to clear key posts for favoured officers
Sixty-three officers said no to new postings. Yet, when the axe finally came down, it was aimed at only 20.
The selective move by the Sindh Board of Revenue (SBR) has triggered accusations of double standards, with affected sub-registrars alleging that rules are being selectively enforced to make room for favoured officers at key postings across Karachi and other major cities.
Of the 63 sub-registrars who reportedly declined new postings after promotion, the Board of Revenue has recommended suspension of only 20, according to official sources. The remaining 43 have escaped the proposed action, raising questions about why the same alleged violation has invited different consequences.
Senior Member Board of Revenue Khalid Haider Shah has sent a summary to the provincial chief minister recommending suspension of the 20 officers, sources said.
The move has drawn the ire of the affected officials, who claim that the action amounts to selective enforcement of rules. They argue that if refusing a new posting constituted grounds for disciplinary action, all 63 officers should have been treated alike.
According to sources, however, the rules do not compel an officer to accept a promotion. An official may decline a promotion under the applicable rules and cannot be forced to take it, they said.
The controversy has deepened amid allegations that the exercise is aimed at creating vacancies for newly promoted officers considered close to influential quarters. Sources alleged that several of the 43 officers spared from action have links with influential political figures, including serving and former provincial ministers.
These allegations could not be independently verified.
Sources further alleged that the proposed suspensions were intended to clear key posts in Karachi and other important cities for preferred officers, even before they complete the mandatory six-month training period.
The Board of Revenue has eight approved posts in the relevant cadre, but five are already occupied by officers serving as inspectors, sources said. This leaves only three vacancies to be filled, yet disciplinary action has been recommended against 20 officers, they added.
The affected sub-registrars have reportedly decided to challenge the orders in court, terming the move discriminatory and contrary to the rules.
The senior SBR member was contacted for his version, but no response was received till the filing of this report.

title: Mir Raza commission closes  mystery remains
description: Mir Raza commission closes  mystery remains
content:
Judge presses police on missing CCTV, conflicting medical opinions and handling of key evidence
Fifteen sittings, 49 witnesses and weeks of questioning later, the Judicial Commission probing Mir Raza Ali's death has concluded its proceedings - but several key questions surrounding the case remain unanswered.
The final hearing turned into a searching examination of the police investigation, with the commission questioning the handling of the crime scene, missing CCTV footage, leaked private chats, cryptocurrency transactions and conflicting medical opinions.
Investigating officer (IO) DSP Siraj Lashari told the commission that the probe was continuing to determine whether Mir Raza had committed suicide or had been murdered. "Police could have easily picked up someone and beaten a confession out of them, but we want justice in this case," he said.
Lashari said a super medical board was proposed because of discrepancies between the reports of Dr Usama and Dr Summaiya Syed, adding that the circumstances and evidence contradicted both reports.
Commission head Justice Umar Sial, however, questioned why the opinion of a single doctor appeared to be carrying so much weight when an eight-member medical board had already conducted the post-mortem. "The Sindh government is facing embarrassment because of Dr Usama. One Usama appears to outweigh everyone else," he remarked.
CPLC representative Kashif told the commission that its analysis of call detail records, geofencing and CCTV footage had not produced any concrete conclusion. He said geofencing began on July 28 and 29 and no suspicious activity or unusually frequent contact with a particular number was found.
Mir Raza's internet remained active until 4:25am, while Apple Maps was accessed between 4.10am and 4.20am. Police have approached the NCCIA and Apple for IP-related information.
The CPLC had 46 cameras in Gulistan-e-Jauhar Blocks 1 to 4, but the incident location fell outside their coverage. Mir Raza appeared on only three cameras. The commission also questioned five missing hours of CCTV footage from Masjid Khizra. Kashif attributed the problem to the mosque's outdated surveillance system.
Justice Sial sharply questioned the police over the preservation of the crime scene, noting that dozens of officers had entered the area.
He also questioned the evidentiary value of footage recorded on a mobile phone by SHO Adeel Afzal and noted that a guesthouse DVR had been found in the officer's vehicle. "The crime scene was made a mess," the judge remarked, questioning why no action had been taken against those responsible.
He also asked whether the police's claim that the crime scene unit reached the spot within 15 minutes was accurate, asking: "Is the IG Sindh lying?"
The commission grilled Lashari over Ali Shaz, whose name had surfaced in connection with a voice note.
Justice Sial questioned whether police had adequately investigated Shaz's movements, his departure abroad, his brother's arrival in Karachi and his apparent concern for Mir Raza.
The judge noted that two suspicious vehicles had emerged during the investigation and that Shaz owned similar vehicles.

title: Medical student s body exhumed 15 months after death
description: Medical student s body exhumed 15 months after death
content:
Family suspects foul play, seeks post-mortem; samples sent for chemical examination
The body of 23-year-old medical student Sultan Zafar, who died last year after allegedly falling from a moving vehicle at Sea View, was exhumed on Wednesday, nearly 15 months after his death, following a request by his family.
A nine-member medical board, comprising seven doctors and two mortuary attendants, exhumed Sultan's body at Kohi Goth Graveyard and conducted a post-mortem examination. Samples were collected and sent for chemical examination, while the final post-mortem report will be prepared after the chemical examination results are received.
The exhumation was ordered by a magistrate on an application filed by Sultan's family.
Professor of Radiology Dr Saba Sohail was appointed chairperson of the medical board. The board included Dr Mehreen Fatima of the Department of Forensic Medicine at Dow Medical College, neurosurgeon Dr Imran, Jinnah Hospital Medico-Legal Officer Dr Mumtaz, Police Surgeon's Office administrative in-charge Dr Yasin, Additional Police Surgeon at Abbasi Shaheed Hospital Dr Kamran Sheikh and Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed. Mortuary attendants Shoaib and Anees were also part of the board.
Sultan had gone to Do Darya with friends on July 23, 2025, where he sustained serious injuries in what was initially described as an accident. He remained under treatment at a hospital for about a week before succumbing to his injuries.
His mother, Dr Mehr Afroz, later donated his organs. On July 31, both of Sultan's kidneys were transplanted into two patients undergoing dialysis at the Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation (SIUT), where Dr Mehr works.
According to the family, CT scans and X-rays conducted after the incident, had revealed fractures in different parts of Sultan's body, including a nasal bone fracture. The family said they approached police over the injuries but received no cooperation.
Speaking to the media after the exhumation, Sultan's maternal aunt Mehr Feroz said the family suspected that he had been murdered. She said three girls and four boys were accompanying Sultan when the incident occurred. According to the family, they travelled in two vehicles from Do Darya towards an under-construction building beyond the area.
Sultan's friends had allegedly told the family that he got out of the vehicle while it was travelling at around 20 kilometres per hour and sustained injuries. However, Mehr Feroz said the family had found no evidence at the alleged site to support the account of an accident.
Police registered a case under Section 320 of the Pakistan Penal Code at Sahil police station nearly six months after the incident, on the complaint of Sultan's mother. The family has now sought to establish the circumstances surrounding Sultan's death through the post-mortem examination and subsequent forensic analysis.

title: Filtration plants supply muddy water
description: Filtration plants supply muddy water
content:
Residents complain plants deliver potentially unsafe water due to overdue filter replacement
Water filtration plants installed across various parts of the city are supplying muddy and potentially unsafe drinking water as their filters have remained unchanged for an extended period.
Despite repeated complaints from residents, no effective action has been taken, raising concerns that facilities established to provide clean drinking water are instead becoming potential sources of waterborne diseases.
Filtration plants in Union Council 46, Naya Mohalla, Sadiqabad, Dhoke Ilahi Bakhsh and Dhoke Hasu have received numerous complaints, with residents reporting that the plants are supplying water mixed with soil.
Operators of the filtration plants said their filters had not been replaced for a considerable period because of a lack of funds. They said the failure to replace the filters had affected water quality. They added the tube-wells supplying these plants had experienced a decline in groundwater levels, causing soil to mix with the water.
Sources said the tube-wells installed across Rawalpindi by the Municipal Corporation, WASA and District Council before 2000 had also experienced declining water levels. While groundwater levels had not fallen significantly until 2000, they have dropped by more than 200 feet between 2001 and 2026, according to the sources
As a result, old tube-wells are supplying water mixed with soil, while filtration plants connected to them are also providing water of questionable quality because of declining groundwater levels and overdue filter replacement.
Residents Iftikharuddin, Fayyaz Shah, Farhan Hamid and Fayyaz said they had laboratory-tested the water and found it to be highly harmful. Complaints had also been lodged with the Pak Ab Authority, but no action had been taken.
RAWALPINDI. The Rawalpindi Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA) has formally transferred administrative control of 130 water filtration plants across the city to the Punjab Saaf Pani Authority (PSPA).
The authority, which previously operated under Punjab's Housing Ministry, will now function under the Punjab Local Government Department and will be responsible for the maintenance and upkeep of 130 filtration plants, which are attached to tube wells.
Rawalpindi WASA Managing Director Azizullah Khan confirmed the development and said the agency was currently focusing its attention on the Chahan Dam and Dadhocha Dam water-supply projects
He said WASA was also working to install 15 tube wells along the Expressway after reaching an agreement with the Capital Development Authority (CDA).
Khan further said the Chahan Dam water-supply project was expected to be completed in 2027 and would provide an additional 17 million gallons of water per day.
The Dadhocha Dam water-supply project, which is expected to provide an additional 35 million gallons of water per day to the city and cantonment areas, is scheduled for completion in 2029.

title: 21 years on  quake victims still await promised homes
description: More than 86 000 people were killed  while millions were displaced and thousands suffered permanent disabilities
content:
More than 86,000 people were killed, while millions were displaced and thousands suffered permanent disabilities
The 21st anniversary of the devastating October 8, 2005 earthquake will be observed across the country, particularly in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Azad Jammu and Kashmir, with prayers and remembrance for the victims.
For the people of Balakot, the epicentre of the disaster, the anniversary continues to evoke painful memories and unfulfilled dreams. At 8.52am on October 8, 2005, a magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck the region, turning thriving valleys into scenes of devastation within minutes.
More than 86,000 people were killed, while millions were displaced and thousands suffered permanent disabilities. Balakot, designated a red zone because of the scale of destruction, bore the brunt of the disaster. Thousands of children were killed when school buildings collapsed, while hardly any family remained untouched by the tragedy.
Twenty-one years later, the memories remain vivid for survivors who continue to mourn their loved ones. Every October 8 brings back memories of children, parents and siblings who were buried under the rubble.
Soon after the earthquake, the government announced the construction of the New Balakot City at Bakrial as an alternative settlement for residents of the devastated city. The project was intended to provide earthquake survivors with safe and modern housing.
However, despite the passage of 21 years, the New Balakot City project remains incomplete, leaving many affected families waiting for the promised settlement.
Despite government and international assistance, dozens of schools and basic health facilities in Balakot and surrounding areas also remain incomplete or non-functional.

description: Missing teenage girl found dead at uncle s house
content:
Police launch investigation and search for the missing relative
The body of a 15-year-old girl who went missing while on her way to a madrassa was recovered from her maternal uncle's house in the Pirwadhai area on Wednesday.
Police took the body into custody and shifted it to a hospital for a post-mortem examination. The girl's maternal uncle, identified as Mumraiz, was reportedly missing from the house.
The girl, identified as Maimoona, was reported missing on Tuesday after she left home in Dhoke Najjo for the madrassa but did not return. Police registered a case of abduction and launched a search for her.
Police sources said the girl appeared to have been strangled, but said the exact cause of death would be determined by the post-mortem report. Evidence was collected from the scene and an investigation was under way from multiple angles.
CPO Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera took notice of the incident and directed police to immediately arrest those involved. SSP Investigation Saifullah visited the scene and supervised the investigation.
According to a police spokesperson, officers had been searching for the girl along with her family after the abduction case was registered. Police also examined CCTV footage from the area to trace her movements and identify suspects.
The girl's mother alleged that CCTV footage showed her brother-in-law, Mumraiz, blocking the girl's route on the day she went missing. She said his wife and children were away in their village at the time and that he was alone at home.
According to the mother, Mumraiz had initially joined the family in searching for the girl. She said he later disappeared after telling her husband that he would return within five minutes after collecting money from him.
The mother further alleged that when police broke open the lock of Mumraiz's house, the girl's body was found under a charpoy. She claimed the girl had marks on her hands and neck and a piece of cloth had been placed inside her mouth.

title: Chinese fire  rescue fleet reaches capital

content:
Twenty-one modern fire and rescue vehicles provided by China to upgrade Islamabad's firefighting and emergency response system have arrived in the capital, according to sources.
The vehicles and equipment supplied under Chinese assistance are worth 72.31 million Chinese yuan, equivalent to approximately Rs3 billion, the sources said.
The consignment includes a modern snorkel fire tender capable of carrying out firefighting and rescue operations in high-rise buildings. The new vehicle can reach a height of around 88 metres.

Sources said the last major procurement of modern fire vehicles and equipment for the Capital Development Authority (CDA) Fire Department took place in 2006, with no major purchase of advanced fire and rescue vehicles for nearly two decades.

title: Three killed in Houthi attacks on Saudi airports
description: Three killed in Houthi attacks on Saudi airports
content:
Three people were killed and dozens wounded in attacks on airports in Saudi Arabia, authorities said on Wednesday, as fighting intensified in Yemen between Iran-aligned Houthi forces and Saudi-backed government troops.
One person was killed and eight wounded in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, while two people were killed and 28 wounded in an attack on facilities at Abha airport, Saudi civil aviation authorities said. The attacks occurred on Tuesday and Wednesday.
The attacks came as the Houthis targeted Aden International Airport with ballistic missiles and explosive-laden drones. Yemen's Transport Ministry said one missile landed near the runway minutes before a flight from Cairo was due to arrive.
Fighting has intensified around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a vital shipping route whose importance has grown since conflict between the United States and Iran restricted trade through the Strait of Hormuz. Yemeni government forces, backed by Saudi-led coalition air support, have launched a counteroffensive to retake territory captured by the Houthis in September.
The renewed fighting has displaced more than 200,000 people, the International Organization for Migration said on Wednesday. IOM Director General Amy Pope said people were "running for their lives and finding nowhere safe to go" and called for increased funding for food and shelter.
The Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile north of Riyadh and was tracking its launch platform in Houthi-controlled Sanaa. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had targeted King Khalid airport with several drones.
The Houthis seized Sanaa in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led military intervention. Riyadh accuses Iran of arming and supporting the group, while the Houthis and Tehran reject the allegations. REUTERS

title: Russia s  vile  strikes kill 25 in Ukraine  Zelenskiy
