content:
Russia pounded Ukraine with waves of missiles and drones in one of its most "vile strikes" on Wednesday, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said, killing at least 25 people, including ?children, and damaging industrial facilities and energy infrastructure.
The heaviest death toll was in Pryluky in Ukraine's northern Chernihiv region, where a Russian missile obliterated a five-storey residential building. Zelenskiy said 19 people died in the attack, including five children.
Zelenskiy said 25 people had been killed in the ?strikes throughout the country, with 100 injured. Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi put the death toll at 28. The president noted that the attacks coincided with Russian President Vladimir Putin's birthday.
"This is the kind of birthday present that Putin gave himself: the killing of ?children, the killing of people," Zelenskiy said in his nightly video address.
In earlier online comments, Zelenskiysaid civilians had also been killed in the capital Kyiv and in the central cities of Oleksandria and Kremenchuk during the massive attack.
In total, Russia fired 70 missiles at Ukraine overnight - many of them high-velocity ballistic munitions - and dozens of Shahed attack drones, he said.
"The Russians wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively. This was one of the most vile strikes."
In Pryluky, an excavator and dozens of rescuers with shovels sifted through rubble at the site ?where several sections of the apartment block had collapsed.
Emergency workers used ladders to get to the upper floors of what remained of the building, and brought out 15 survivors as they worked their way down through the rubble. Around 55 people were wounded in the town, regional officials said.
"There's a lot of destruction, especially in the town centre," said Danylo Savenko, deputy mayor of Pryluky, who said he had run to an air raid shelter with his wife as soon as he heard the missiles flying.

title: Israel strikes Gaza on Oct 7 anniversary
description: Israel strikes Gaza on Oct 7 anniversary
content:
Five killed as loud bangs heard across border in Gaza
Israel carried out new strikes in Gaza on Wednesday as it marked the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks by Hamas, with Palestinian officials reporting five people killed.
Loud bangs across the border in Gaza were audible from the site of the Nova music festival just as family members gathered at dawn to mourn the more than 300 revellers killed three years earlier.
In Gaza City, Al-Shifa hospital reported two people killed in an Israeli strike overnight.
Gaza's civil defence identified one of the dead as Mohamed Tamous and said he was a volunteer for the agency, which serves as an emergency rescue service under Hamas.
The Israeli military said it struck and killed "two Hamas militants who had exited Kamal Adwan Hospital in the northern Gaza Strip," adding that one had "planted explosives... in the area of the Yellow Line with the intention of harming IDF troops."
The so-called Yellow Line demarcates the areas under Hamas and Israeli military control in the Gaza Strip.
The military identified one of those killed in the strike as Tamous, whom it said was a sniper in Hamas's military wing while simultaneously working for the civil defence agency.
In the southern city of Khan Yunis, Nasser Hospital said that a 60-year-old man, Hisham Ibrahim Abu Mustafa, was killed in an Israeli strike and that others were injured.
The hospital also reported receiving the body of Ziad Zaarab, who it said was killed in an Israeli airstrike south of Khan Yunis that left several injured.
A strike on a tent in the Al-Buraq camp in the afternoon killed another person, the hospital said.
In the last strike, the Israeli military told AFP it targeted a "military operative", without immediately providing comment on the others.
On the third anniversary of the first day of the war in Gaza, living conditions remain dire in the coastal Palestinian territory, despite a US-brokered ceasefire that came into effect in October 2025.
"After three years of siege, killing and destruction, Israel has turned the Gaza Strip into an uninhabitable place," said Gaza City resident Mahmoud Abu Hasira.
Hundreds of thousands of displaced people still live in tent cities and makeshift shelters that sprawl on beaches or next to piles of rubble from bombed-out residential buildings.
"We once had homes, but now we have lost our loved ones, whose bodies still lie beneath the rubble," said Bassam Nasser, a resident of Beit Hanoun, a now largely destroyed city in Gaza's north, who was displaced in the early days of the war.
Israel says it controls about 60 percent of Gaza, on the territory's outer perimeter including Beit Hanoun, while most of the Palestinian population lives in the remaining Hamas-controlled areas.

title: Duo wins Nobel for chemical asymmetry puzzle
description: Duo wins Nobel for chemical asymmetry puzzle
content:
France's Henri Kagan and Japan's Kenso Soai on Wednesday won the Nobel chemistry prize for solving the mystery of why only one version of some molecules' mirror-image forms appears in nature, a discovery decisive for the development of pharmaceuticals.
The pair were honoured "for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis", the jury said.
Like hands, all amino acids exist as two mirrored variants, but only one of them is found in the proteins in the body's cells.
The other is rarely found in nature, a phenomenon known as "homochirality", the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences explained.
Chemists have long wondered how that process occurs, and the two Nobel laureates' discoveries have "enabled chemists to drive chemical reactions that lead to homochirality", the jury said.
"Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai have provided a solution to a chemical mystery that is over a century old: how homochirality can emerge spontaneously. The chemical reactions they have developed are spectacular," said Heiner Linke, chair of the Nobel Committee for Chemistry.
"Their discoveries have been decisive for chemists who design reactions for the manufacture of pharmaceuticals," the jury said.
Last year, the chemistry prize went to Japan's Susumu Kitagawa, UK-born Richard Robson and American-Jordanian Omar Yaghi for developing a method of designing molecular structures.
The chemistry prize follows the physics prize, which on Tuesday honoured Belgian physicist Francis Halzen for groundbreaking work using Antarctic ice to capture particles originating in the distant cosmos.
On Monday, the medicine prize was awarded to US psychiatrist and neurologist Karl Deisseroth and German scientists Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel.
The literature laureate will be revealed on Thursday, with some pundits suggesting that the Swedish Academy could follow up last year's award to Hungary's Laszlo Krasznahorkai with a prize for a woman writer, possibly from Latin America.
The most keenly anticipated award -- the peace prize -- is due on Friday.
US President Donald Trump lobbied intensively last year to get the prize and the committee is aware he will be watching closely again.
The economics prize wraps up the Nobel season on October 12.
The Nobel consists of a diploma, a gold medal and a 12-million-kronor ($1.2-million) prize sum, which is shared if there is more than one winner in a discipline.
The laureates will receive their prizes at a formal ceremony on December 10, the anniversary of the death in 1896 of scientist Alfred Nobel, who created the prizes in his will. AFP

title: Iranian president says US deal  not out of reach  in call with Putin

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said during a call with his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, that reaching an agreement with the United States was "not out of reach" if Washington adhered to international legal frameworks, according to the Iranian presidency.
The two leaders discussed regional developments, Iran-US negotiations and relations, according to a statement.
Pezeshkian briefed Putin on negotiations between Iran and the US mediated by Pakistan, describing Washington's "double standards and maximalism" as the biggest obstacle to reaching a fair agreement.

"Our red line is Iran's national interests and the rights of the Iranian people," said Pezeshkian, adding that if Washington adhered to international legal frameworks, reaching an agreement would not be out of reach.
The Iranian president also described Gulf countries as Iran's "brothers" and expressed regret about the use of US military bases in those countries for attacks against Iran.
He said Tehran was ready to cooperate with neighbouring countries to achieve regional peace and security without the presence or involvement of powers from outside the region.
Putin reiterated Russia's support for diplomatic efforts to reach a political settlement to the war and said Moscow was ready to keep helping find a diplomatic solution, according to the statement.
He also stressed the need to respect Iran's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and backed Tehran's demands for compensation for damage caused during the war and long-term security guarantees against additional attacks.
The two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to expanding cooperation under the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty and maintaining close coordination in international forums. AGENCIES

title: DG ISPR confirms Pakistani troops in Saudi Arabia
description: DG ISPR confirms Pakistani troops in Saudi Arabia
content:
Tells CNN forces have served in the kingdom for decades
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said on Wednesday that Pakistani troops were present in Saudi Arabia in "multiple capabilities" amid the kingdom's escalating conflict with Yemen's Houthis and developments related to it.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
In an interview with CNN, the military spokesperson was questioned about whether Pakistani military personnel were present in the kingdom as part of the Makkah Defence Alliance, to which he said: "I do confirm that the forces of Pakistan are already there ... the Pakistani troops have been there for decades in multiple capabilities."
He said the Makkah pact was not borne out of a "vacuum". "There is a sustained diplomatic, political, military and people-to-people relationship between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye," he added.
The DG ISPR reiterated that forces were present in "multiple domains" in the kingdom.
In a major development that may have far-reaching implications for the region, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye activated the practical implementation of their collective defence commitments on Monday.
According to a joint statement issued on Monday night, the activation entailed immediate deployment of "the agreed military forces and capabilities to the kingdom in response to security threats".
The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of the Strategic-Political and Defence Committee of the alliance, held in Riyadh to discuss the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia is currently engaged in an active conflict with Houthis, who have been targeting the various strategic and economic assets in the kingdom.
However, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on Tuesday had rejected what it described as "speculative" reporting by Reuters on the pact, saying operational details concerning the implementation of the collective deterrence mechanism were confidential.
The ministry's statement followed a Reuters report published on October 2, which said Pakistan had deployed between 30,000 and 40,000 troops to Saudi Arabia to help defend the kingdom's land borders and assist with drone and missile interceptions, citing a Pakistani official. Reuters reported that Islamabad had not decided to send troops into Yemen in a fighting capacity.

title: Russia s Taliban outreach  driven by US fears
description: Russia s Taliban outreach  driven by US fears
content:
Sources see no shift in Moscow's policy towards Islamabad
Russia's increasingly accommodating posture towards Afghanistan's Taliban regime has fueled speculation that Moscow may be recalibrating its regional policy, particularly after it publicly recognised the Taliban administration as Afghanistan's national government and apparently ignored Kabul's ties with terrorist groups.
But Pakistani and diplomatic sources have dismissed the perception of any major policy shift, arguing that Moscow's softer approach towards the Taliban is primarily driven by its strategic objective of preventing the United States from regaining a foothold in Afghanistan.
The issue came into sharper focus at a Moscow Format meeting held earlier this week, where the Russian foreign minister publicly praised the Taliban administration. What raised eyebrows in diplomatic circles was Moscow's apparent effort to play down the regime's links with terrorist activities, prompting speculation that changing regional dynamics may be pushing Russia closer to Kabul.
Pakistani officials, however, are not overly concerned about the development. A source familiar with the discussions said Russia, as the host of the Moscow Format meeting, had deliberately adopted a conciliatory tone towards the Taliban, but that should not be interpreted as Moscow having abandoned its concerns about the Afghan regime.
The source said Russia was deliberately pursuing a "soft approach" towards the Taliban, driven largely by its assessment that putting excessive pressure on Kabul could push the regime towards Washington. "Russia's main concern is to deny the US a foothold in Afghanistan again and hence they are working with the Taliban regime," the source said.
"The best course is to keep nudging and prodding them," the source said, describing Moscow's strategy as one of engagement rather than confrontation. The source, however, made it clear that there had been no corresponding change in Russia's approach towards Pakistan.
Pakistan and Russia recently concluded their joint military exercises, while Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's visit to Moscow is also being planned, according to the source.
The absence of a joint statement at the latest Moscow Format meeting was also attributed to differences with the Afghan Taliban rather than any Russia-Pakistan divergence. The source said the Russian side was itself unhappy with the failure to issue a joint statement, pointing out that the Taliban had not objected to a similar statement at last year's meeting.
According to the source, Russia sought Pakistan's input on the proposed joint statement, and Islamabad made it clear that it was prepared to stick to the language and position reflected in the previous statement. However, the Taliban did not agree to the proposed text, resulting in the meeting ending without a joint statement.
The development underscored the growing differences between the Taliban regime and its regional interlocutors over how the security situation in Afghanistan should be addressed.
For Moscow, however, maintaining engagement with Kabul appears to remain a strategic calculation rather than an endorsement of all Taliban policies. Pakistan, meanwhile, continues to press the Afghan authorities to take concrete action against terrorist groups operating from Afghan soil, particularly the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

title: Shehbaz vows to stop rising K P terrorism
description: Shehbaz vows to stop rising K P terrorism
content:
PM says govt wants K-P to develop alongside other provinces
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday said rising terrorism in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa must be stopped "at all costs", the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said.
According to the statement issued by the PMO, the prime minister made the remarks during a meeting with Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam in Islamabad.
During the meeting, matters relating to Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), G-B and K-P were discussed during the meeting. "Rising terrorism in K-P must be stopped at all costs," the prime minister said.
He said the government wanted K-P to develop like other parts of the country and appreciated the sacrifices made by the people of the province in the fight against terrorism.
The statement further added that the federal minister briefed the prime minister on ongoing matters and progress in AJK and G-B. The prime minister directed that effective measures continue to ensure the welfare and development of the people of AJK and G-B and the provision of basic facilities.
Shehbaz said the development of AJK and G-B and the prosperity of their people were among the government's priorities.
Terrorism has risen in K-P over the past month, with a series of attacks targeting police, government officials and civilians across the province.
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said the government was trying to avoid imposing governor's rule in K-P, but warned that it could resort to the option if no other way was left.
Speaking to reporters in Islamabad, the minister said that there was nothing impeding the imposition og governor's rule in the province, but the government was trying not to use what he described as the "last option".
"If there is no other way left, then we can use that option," he said.
Asif also criticised the PTI, urging it to "play the role of a political party rather than a terrorist organisation".
"We cannot leave the capital at their mercy so that every two or three months they join hands with the Taliban and march on the capital," he said.
The minister described the Taliban as an "anti-Pakistan power" and said that if the PTI allied with it and attacked the capital, the government had the right and responsibility to protect Islamabad.
Asif also described the PTI's planned long march as an "attack on Islamabad", saying previous attacks on the capital had also been motivated by political parties' efforts to establish their credibility within their own ranks.
He attributed the failure of talks between the government and opposition to internal differences within the PTI.
"Differences within the PTI have intensified," he said, adding that members of the PTI sitting in the National Assembly, its negotiating team and even its allies wanted a solution to the issue that was acceptable to the entire country.
Asked about the PTI's demand for a meeting with Imran Khan before deciding whether to postpone its long march, Asif said he did not know about it.
He instead urged the PTI to look at its record.
Later, in a post on X, Asif accused the K-P government of having "complete collusion" with terrorists and said there were ample examples and evidence of what he called a "facilitator ecosystem", which, he said, could not be tolerated.
Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said that the government would not accept political demands through pressure tactics or attempts to "hold the state hostage", as the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf maintained that its long march would continue and only Imran Khan could decide when to call it off.
"I want to say this clearly today that no demand can be accepted by holding the state hostage or pursuing the path of political instability," Sanaullah said while addressing a press conference in Islamabad.
He urged PTI to set aside what he described as its politics of instability and prioritise the national interest by resolving differences through dialogue.
Sanaullah said the government remained willing to hold talks but warned that political demands could not be accepted through pressure tactics.
"They should renounce political instability and not give priority to their personal political agenda over the national interest. They should sit for talks and resolve these issues through negotiations. However, despite our desire for talks, under no circumstances should they try to hold the state hostage to have their political demands accepted. This tactic will not be allowed," he added.

title: Afridi hits back at Kundi over security meeting
description: Afridi hits back at Kundi over security meeting
content:
K-P CM says governor lacks authority to summon officials
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Wednesday condemned a security meeting chaired by Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, calling it "an attack on the Constitution and democracy" and warning that his government would not allow "any conspiracy to break up Pakistan" to succeed.
He also accused the PPP of trying to create "another East Pakistan", alleging that the party had previously prioritised personal interests over national interests. "We are with Pakistan and will not allow anyone to break up Pakistan under any circumstances. Whatever their intentions, God willing, they will fail," he added.
While addressing a meeting of the provincial cabinet, Afridi said the provincial government had been elected with a two-thirds majority and that the provincial assembly, cabinet and government remained intact.
"The drama staged by the governor yesterday was extremely regrettable and condemnable," he said, adding, "The governor presiding over such a meeting is an attack on the Constitution and democracy."
The dispute over Kundi's role came amid weeks of tension between the federal and provincial governments, with the possibility of governor's rule or an emergency repeatedly raised over the deteriorating security situation and the PTI's planned march.
The row intensified as Kundi expanded his role beyond his constitutional remit, chairing meetings on matters that fall under the provincial government's authority.
Afridi questioned the governor's authority to summon the chief secretary and IGP while an elected provincial government was in place.
"There is a constitutional procedure for removing a chief minister. The vote of no-confidence is the mechanism to do so," he said, adding that he would consult the advocate general on the constitutional status of the meeting and, if necessary, legislation would be introduced through the provincial assembly.
"We will not allow anyone to launch an attack on democracy. The governor has acted unconstitutionally," he affirmed.
Afridi claimed that the governor's activities were aimed at provoking the provincial government and forcing it to respond in a way that could further deteriorate the situation.
Meanwhile, K-P Advocate General Shah Faisal Utmankhel told the meeting that Pakistan operated under a federal parliamentary system in which the Constitution defined the legislative, administrative and financial powers of different institutions.
He said the governor's appointment was governed by Article 101, while Article 103 set out the governor's conditions and powers and Article 104 provided for the speaker to perform the governor's functions when required.
"In a parliamentary form of government and federalism, the governor is a ceremonial head," the advocate general said, adding that executive powers rested with the provincial cabinet and government.
Afridi defended his government's record on policing and counter-terrorism, saying it had worked continuously to strengthen the police, Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and Special Branch since he took oath on October 15, 2025.
"The weapons now with our police are not with any other police force in Pakistan," he said, adding that his government had invested in CTD infrastructure and provided funds to strengthen the Special Branch, which he described as the "eyes" of the provincial government because effective intelligence was key to preventing attacks.
He also praised the police and administration for their sacrifices in the fight against terrorism, saying they had helped take the province from a period marked by ammunition and suicide attacks towards peace.
Afridi also accused the federal government of treating K-P as a "stepchild".
He said the former tribal districts had been merged with K-P administratively in 2018 but had not been fully integrated financially, and that the funds promised at the time of the merger had still not been provided.
He accused the federal government of continuously imposing military operations on K-P since 2024, while people displaced by the government's "wrong policies" had remained without full compensation. "Around Rs100 billion is still outstanding for our people who sacrificed for Pakistan," he added.
Afridi said people whose homes had been destroyed were still waiting for compensation and that tribal families had been allocated only Rs400,000 per household. "Their handbags are worth tens of millions of rupees, while our tribal people, who have always sacrificed for Pakistan, have been allocated only Rs400,000 for their entire household."
Afridi rejected the argument that the K-P government's lack of cooperation was responsible for the continuing security problem, pointing to Balochistan, where he said the provincial government was cooperating with the federal government but peace had still not been established.

title: Sadiq Fazl meet stirs buzz as PTI deadlock lingers
description: Speaker says a political path is being explored  PTI s Gohar calls for unconditional dialogue
content:
Speaker says a political path is being explored, PTI's Gohar calls for unconditional dialogue
With the government-opposition negotiations seemingly stuck in the political mud and the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) threatening to march on the capital, a senior government official on Wednesday made a quiet visit to the residence of JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman.
Officially, it was a courtesy call by National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq to congratulate the veteran politician on performing Umrah. Politically, however, the timing was hard to ignore.
The meeting came a day after opposition leaders descended on Fazl's residence, keeping alive speculation that the JUI-F chief could once again emerge as a bridge between the two warring sides.
Sadiq, who has been involved in efforts to keep political channels open, played down the political dimension of the meeting, describing Fazl as his "brother" and stressing that their relationship went beyond politics to personal and family ties.
"I came to congratulate the Maulana on performing Umrah," Sadiq told reporters after the meeting, adding that the two had met after about a month and a half.
The media talk soon turned towards the heated political situation in the country, with talks between the government and opposition having broken down, while the PTI is embarking on a long march towards the federal capital to press for relief for party founder Imran Khan.
Sadiq said he remained in telephone contact with opposition members. "Important political matters were discussed during the meeting with the JUI-F chief," he said, according to Express News. "Efforts are afoot to find a political way forward for the betterment of Pakistan."
At the meeting, the National Assembly speaker was accompanied by Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry. Sadiq said there was always hope and that a better way forward would emerge.
"A political path is being found for the betterment of Pakistan," he said when asked about the political situation and contacts with the opposition. Asked specifically about backdoor contacts with the opposition, he said he regularly spoke to fellow parliamentarians by telephone.
The meeting came a day after Senate Opposition Leader Raja Nasir Abbas, former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser and other opposition leaders met Fazl at his residence to discuss the prevailing political situation, negotiations with the government and a proposed All-Parties Conference (APC).
Fazl said after Tuesday's meeting that the government had left little room for meaningful political negotiations and called for a joint political agenda through an APC. He maintained that political and democratic forces believed in negotiations, while urging a political approach to the country's problems.
The latest contacts, with both sides visiting Fazl, followed the failure of government-PTI talks last week, which had been facilitated by Sadiq and were aimed at easing tensions ahead of the PTI's October 4 long march. Both sides blamed each other for the failure of the talks.
On Wednesday, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan renewed his call for unconditional negotiations, saying dialogue should continue until a solution was reached. He criticised the post-talks statements, saying that taking disagreements outside the negotiating forum had damaged mutual trust.
"Political issues should be discussed without conditions and negotiations should continue until an agreement is reached," Gohar said. "It was wrong to come out and issue statements after talks ended," the PTI chairman added.
Also on Tuesday, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif told the PTI to "come to its senses, abandon long march and hold talks" with the government. Gohar, however, said the government had made its offer of talks conditional, whereas the PTI was prepared to negotiate unconditionally if an offer was made.
Gohar said the PTI's demands were straightforward and included meetings with Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi. He also warned against resorting to "any unconstitutional situation", including the imposition of governor's rule or an emergency in K-P, stressing that political issues should be resolved through dialogue.
Regarding the PTI march, Gohar said Islamabad belonged to everyone and there was no reason for the procession not to reach the capital. He said it would reach Islamabad according to schedule on October 11 or 12, arguing that the continuation of the march should not be interpreted as weakness.

title: Bilawal may replace Naek as JCP member
description: Bilawal may replace Naek as JCP member
content:
PPP chief interested in joining commission as party seeks greater say in judicial appointments
Two members belonging to the treasury benches in the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) have tendered their resignations, paving the way for a possible reshuffle in the commission's parliamentary representation, with PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari being considered for membership.
PPP Senator Farooq H Naek and PML-N MNA Sheikh Aftab have resigned as members of the JCP, according to sources. JCP sources told The Express Tribune that Bilawal is interested in becoming a member of the commission. He is currently a member of the National Assembly.
Under the proposed arrangement, the PPP is expected to secure representation from the National Assembly, while the PML-N would be given representation from the Senate.
The development comes amid reported dissatisfaction within the PPP leadership over the failure to secure the appointment of its preferred candidates as judges of the superior courts.
Naek, a senior PPP legal figure and the outgoing JCP member, had proposed 33 candidates for appointment to the superior judiciary16 for the Sindh High Court (SHC), 10 for the Lahore High Court (LHC), five for the Balochistan High Court (BHC) and two for the Islamabad High Court (IHC).
The PPP leadership was particularly interested in securing the appointment of two of its nominees to the SHC. However, neither the judicial nor executive members of the commission supported their candidatures.
Similarly, the executive members did not back any of Naek's nominees for the LHC, IHC and BHC.
Facing insufficient support from both judicial and executive members, Naek withdrew several nominations before the relevant meetings commenced, while some of the remaining candidates failed to secure the required majority.
The PPP had also sought a six-month extension in the tenure of judges serving on the SHC's constitutional benches. However, the JCP's judicial members agreed to extend their tenure by only three months.
The non-confirmation of SHC Additional Judge Syed Fiaz-ul-Hassan Shah was also viewed as a setback for the PPP. Last year, the party succeeded in influencing judicial appointments in several high courts, particularly the SHC, Peshawar High Court and LHC.
The subsequent delay by the president in approving the summary for the appointment of judges for several weeks also generated speculation. The summary was eventually approved following what sources described as an understanding with the government.
The possibility of Bilawal's nomination to the JCP has meanwhile triggered a fresh debate among lawyers over the growing political role in judicial appointments.
One section of the legal community believes it would have been preferable for Bilawal to nominate a trusted lawmaker to represent the PPP on the commission rather than join it himself.
They argue that the influence of powerful political circles in judicial appointments cannot be ruled out following the 26th Constitutional Amendment. They also contend that it could put Bilawal in an awkward position if he is required to endorse nominees backed by other political groups during commission meetings.
Barrister Salahuddin Ahmed said the changes made to the JCP under the 26th and 27th constitutional amendments were a clear indication that political considerations would now outweigh legal considerations in judicial appointments.
"Replacing Farooq H Naek with Bilawal Bhutto Zardari shows that political parties no longer wish to even maintain a fig leaf of pretence that candidates for judicial appointments shall be assessed on the merits of their legal credentials as opposed to the strength of their political affiliations," he said.
Rida Hosain, an advocate, said Bilawal had been one of the most vocal champions of the constitutional amendments.
"At the time, he justified them as the completion of the 'unfinished' agenda of the Charter of Democracy, tackling judicial activism, and ensuring provincial representation in the courts. It was clear then, and it is clear as day now, there is nothing representative or democratic about this structure," she said.
Hosain further argued that the amendments had weakened judicial independence and that their consequences had extended to women's rights jurisprudence, which, she said, had also been affected by the executive-appointed Federal Constitutional Court.
"The judicial members have been rendered a minority in the Judicial Commission. Meanwhile, approval by the sitting government and its allies has become decisive in judicial appointments.
"The High Court judges are also subject to a 'performance evaluation' by the JCP. Not only their appointment, but also their survival on the bench depends on government approval," she said.
She added that the amendments had made the judiciary more vulnerable to interference.
"Ultimately, political power has a dominant say over who sits on the bench, who rises within it, and who remains there," Hosain said.

title: Guterres hails Pakistan s role in global peace
description: Guterres hails Pakistan s role in global peace
content:
Outgoing United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Wednesday appreciated Pakistan's longstanding contribution to the UN and international peace and security, particularly its diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue, mediation and de-escalation.
Guterres, who is currently on a three-day visit to Pakistan, called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif at the Prime Minister's House on Wednesday evening. According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office, several matters of international importance came under discussion.
During the meeting, Shehbaz acknowledged the secretary general's contribution to international peace and security during his tenure. He reaffirmed Pakistan's strong commitment to an effective, inclusive and representative UN, particularly at a time when multilateralism faced significant challenges.
The statement said Shehbaz welcomed the secretary general's UN80 Initiative and emphasised that UN reform should remain responsive to the priorities of developing countries while strengthening conflict prevention, peaceful settlement of disputes, peacekeeping and peacebuilding.
The prime minister highlighted Pakistan's diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue and de-escalation, including its mediation role between the United States and Iran. "Dialogue and diplomacy remain the only viable path to resolving disputes and preventing escalation," he said.
He also emphasised the need for a peaceful resolution of the Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK) dispute in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people.
Highlighting the Indus Waters Treaty, which was unilaterally suspended by India following the terrorist attack in Pahalgam, the prime minister called it a binding international agreement. "India's unilateral decision to place it in abeyance has no legal basis," he said.
During the meeting, Shehbaz expressed serious concern over terrorism emanating from Afghanistan and the presence of terrorist groups on Afghan soil.

title: ATC frames charges against Imaan  Chattha
description: ATC frames charges against Imaan  Chattha
content:
Defence objects over missing case documents
An anti-terrorism court in Islamabad on Wednesday framed charges against lawyer Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha in a case related to the alleged violation of a designated route and incitement during the arrival of an international cricket team, despite defence objections that legal requirements had not been fulfilled.
The ATC had fixed October 6 for the indictment of Imaan and her husband, Hadi Chattha. However, the proceedings were deferred a day earlier after they could not be produced before the court due to a power outage at Adiala Jail. The court directed jail authorities to ensure the accused were produced via video link at the next hearing, warning that failure to comply could lead to contempt proceedings against jail officials.
Judge Tahir Abbas Supra on Wednesday presided over the hearing, during which Imaan and Chattha were produced before the court via video link. Chattha objected that he had still not received copies of the case documents and argued that charges could not be framed until all legal requirements had been met.
Lawyer Zainab Janjua also objected, saying neither Imaan nor Chattha had received the copies or been allowed to meet their lawyers. "The court cannot frame charges without fulfilling all legal requirements," Zainab told the court. The court nevertheless framed charges against Imaan and Chattha. "You can challenge this order," Judge Tahir Abbas told Zainab.
The court ordered that Imaan and Chattha be physically produced at the next hearing and summoned prosecution witnesses for October 9. The hearing was adjourned until October 9.
Earlier, Zainab told the court that she had waited outside the jail for two hours but was not allowed to meet her clients despite a court order. She also said copies of the case documents had not been provided to Imaan and Chattha and requested that they be produced before the court.
"I have the jail authorities' reports with me," Judge Tahir Abbas said. Janjua questioned why Imaan and Chattha were not being produced before the court when other prisoners were being brought from Adiala Jail.
Dr Shireen Mazari also appeared before the court along with lawyers Eemal Khan Mandokhail, Zainab and others. Prosecutor Raja Naveed represented the prosecution.
At the previous hearing on Monday, the ATC had adjourned Imaan and Chattha's bail applications until October 13 after the investigating officer failed to appear before the court.
Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain had expressed displeasure over the officer's absence. The DSP later told the court that the investigating officer was in Gilgit-Baltistan and his phone was switched off.
Defence counsel had argued that all sections in the FIR, except the terrorism provision, were bailable and pointed out that the court had previously rejected the prosecution's request for the physical remand of Imaan and Chattha.
Imaan and her husband Chattha were rearrested on September 17, shortly after the Supreme Court granted them bail and suspended their sentences in a separate social-media posts case. They were produced before an Islamabad Anti-Terrorism Court in connection with a case registered at Kohsar Police Station.
Police sought 30-day physical remand, but ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain rejected the request and sent the couple on judicial remand. The judge noted that although they had been nominated in the FIR as members of an unlawful assembly, no weapon had been attributed to either accused.

title: SC bars forced conversion of dissolution pleas into khula
description: SC bars forced conversion of dissolution pleas into khula
content:
Recognises 'shiqaq' as independent ground for dissolution where serious marital rupture persists
The Supreme Court has ruled that a family court cannot convert a woman's plea for dissolution of marriage on statutory grounds into a decree of khula without her clear and voluntary consent, holding that such a conversion can unlawfully deprive her of her right to dower.
A five-member bench held that where reconciliation has failed and a marriage has descended into a serious and continuing rupture, the relationship may instead be dissolved on the ground of shiqaq under Section 2(ix) of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939.
The bench - comprising Justice Shahid Waheed, Justice Naeem Akhter Afghan, Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar, Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim and Justice Miangul Hassan Aurangzebissued the verdict while deciding two cases concerning Zainab Bibi and Iram Naz Begum.
The petitions were converted into appeals and partly allowed.
The court stressed that a marriage could be dissolved by a court, but neither spouse should be deprived of a lawful right or burdened with a stigma without a foundation in law and evidence.
Both women had approached the family courts seeking dissolution on the ground of cruelty, while also claiming maintenance, dower and dowry articles.
The courts found that cruelty had not been proved but, after reconciliation failed, dissolved the marriages through khula and directed the women to return or surrender dower.
The Supreme Court held that this approach was legally unsustainable because neither woman had elected khula as an alternative basis for dissolution.
Referring to Section 2 of the 1939 Act, the court observed that dissolution on statutory grounds, including cruelty, was distinct from khula.
While a statutory dissolution is based on an established matrimonial wrong or other prescribed ground, khula is a separate right of a woman to seek release from the marital bond when continuation of the marriage has become intolerable.
The bench cited earlier judgments, including Khurshid Bibi, Saima Khan and Dr Faryal Maqsood, holding that a suit for dissolution did not by itself constitute a suit for khula and that a court could not convert a statutory claim into khula without the woman's clear and voluntary election.
The court particularly emphasised the financial consequences of the distinction.
Section 5 of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act preserves a woman's right to dower when a marriage is dissolved under the Act. Khula, by contrast, ordinarily carries consequences relating to surrender or return of the benefit received by the wife.
"Failure to establish cruelty does not authorise the court to manufacture an election of khula on behalf of the wife," the judgment stated in substance.
The court, however, declined to simply set aside the dissolution of the marriages. It examined whether another legal ground existed on the evidence already available.
The bench focused on Section 2(ix), which permits dissolution "on any other ground which is recognised as valid for the dissolution of marriages under Muslim law".
It held that shiqaq, meaning serious and continuing discord or rupture between spouses, could fall within this residuary provision where its factual requirements were established and reconciliation had failed.
The court sought the opinion of the Council of Islamic Ideology, which stated that where there was a serious breach between spouses, the parties could no longer live together in accordance with the purposes of marriage, fault could not fairly be attributed exclusively to one spouse and reconciliation had failed, the condition could constitute shiqaq recognised under Muslim law.
The bench stressed, however, that shiqaq could not be equated with every marital disagreement or incompatibility.
It said shiqaq required a genuine, serious and continuing rupture of such a nature that the essential purposes of marriage could no longer realistically be fulfilled, coupled with failure of meaningful reconciliation efforts. The court distinguished shiqaq from cruelty. Cruelty constituted a matrimonial wrong attributable to conduct falling within the statutory parameters of the 1939 Act, whereas shiqaq concerned the condition of the matrimonial relationship itself.

title: Pension seizure for child maintenance allowed
description: Pension seizure for child maintenance allowed
content:
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has ruled that pension protection under the Pensions Act, 1871 cannot be used to frustrate enforcement of a final family court decree awarding maintenance to minor children.
A two-member bench comprising Justice Malik Waqar Haider Awan and Justice Malik Javid Iqbal Wains held that the pension of a retired army official could be proceeded against to enforce a maintenance decree in favour of his children.
The court observed that a child's maintenance claim was fundamentally different from an ordinary monetary debt between a creditor and debtor. A child does not become a "creditor" merely because a family court has passed a maintenance decree in his or her favour.
The ruling came on a constitutional petition filed by Muhammad Latif, who had challenged the family court's refusal to cancel non-bailable warrants issued against him and its decision to proceed with attachment of funds in his pension account. The LHC directed the executing court to proceed expeditiously and, as far as practicable, conclude the execution within 30 days of receiving a certified copy of the judgment.
The case arose from a dispute involving dissolution of marriage, recovery of dowry articles and maintenance for two minor children. In January 2014, a family court in Jaranwala directed the father to pay Rs3,000 per month to each child from the date of institution of the suit until marriage or a lawful change in custody, with an annual 10 per cent increase. A separate decree ordered recovery of dowry articles valued at Rs248,570. The decrees subsequently attained finality. During execution proceedings, the family court issued non-bailable warrants and moved to attach funds in the petitioner's pension account.

title: FM  CNSC stress close security coordination
description: FM  CNSC stress close security coordination
content:
Dar, Raza discuss national security, regional peace
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and Commander National Strategic Command (CNSC) General Syed Aamer Raza agreed on the importance of "close institutional coordination" in advancing Pakistan's national interests and contributing to regional peace and security, the Foreign Office said on Wednesday.
According to an FO statement, General Raza called on Dar at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, where the deputy prime minister congratulated him on his promotion and appointment as CNSC and wished him success in his new responsibilities.
"The two officials discussed matters of national security and General Raza took charge as the first CNSC on July 31, after Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif promoted him to the rank of a four-star general and appointed him as CNSC on July 24, a move completing the restructuring of the country's higher military command initiated under the 27th Constitutional Amendment.
The position was created under the 27th Constitutional Amendment, which rewrote Article 243. The amendment abolished the longstanding office of the Chairman, Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee (CJCSC) and established the posts of Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and CNSC. It also expanded the constitutional powers of the country's senior military leadership and introduced constitutional protections for five-star generals.
Under the amendment, the prime minister appoints the CNSC on the recommendation of the CDF and Chief of Army Staff. The appointment is for a three-year term, while the prime minister is authorised to determine the terms, conditions and rules governing the office.
The amendment also allows the prime minister to reappoint the CNSC for one additional three-year term on the recommendation of the CDF.

title: PM directs faster ML 1 upgrade

content:
Shehbaz seeks better travel facilities for passengers
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday directed the authorities concerned to expedite work on the upgradation of Main Line-1 (ML-1) and implement corporate-style reforms in Pakistan Railways to make it strong and economically self-sufficient.
The prime minister, chairing a review meeting on reforms in Pakistan Railways here, said that ML-1 should be constructed on a commercial basis by utilising the encroached railway land worth billions of rupees.
He appreciated the efforts of the joint teams of the National Accountability Bureau and the Ministry of Railways, under the chairmanship of the NAB Chairman, regarding the identification and retrieval of encroached land belonging to Pakistan Railways.
He said that the upgradation of ML-1 was vital to uplift Pakistan Railways, provide better travel facilities to passengers, and increase freight transport, stressing the need to harness the actual commercial potential existing in railway properties.
The prime minister said that valuable railway land should be used effectively for commercial purposes to support the development of the national economy and railways.
He said that introducing corporate-style reforms in the railways was among the government's priorities to make it strong and economically self-sufficient.
The prime minister approved utilising bank funding through various commercial projects on railway land for the construction of ML-1.
The meeting was informed that the upgradation of the 1,726-kilometre-long ML-1 has been divided into four major sections, comprising Karachi-Rohri, Rohri-Multan, Multan-Lahore, and Lahore-Peshawar sections.
The prime minister directed the relevant authorities to remove obstacles hindering the provision of financial resources to the housing, agriculture, and Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) sectors, saying that the lending system should be made more effective.
Chairing a review meeting regarding access to finance, the prime minister also directed to make the SME Portal operational by the end of November to facilitate the provision of loans to small and medium-sized enterprises.
The SME Portal will enable real-time monitoring of the latest status of loans being provided by banks, as well as business facilities including Letters of Credit (LCs).
The prime minister directed Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal to contact Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) Deputy Emir Liaquat Baloch as the government seeks to advance dialogue with the party.
According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office, Ahsan Iqbal contacted Liaquat Baloch on the prime minister's special instructions and conveyed Shehbaz Sharif's message to the JI leadership.

title: Halle Berry denies abusing son amid custody battle
description: Halle Berry denies abusing son amid custody battle
content:
Actress submits video evidence to counter ex Olivier Martinez
Halle Berry has denied allegations that she physically abused her 13 year old son, Maceo, amid a custody dispute with her former husband Olivier Martinez.
In a declaration filed on October 5 and obtained by PEOPLE, Berry said she has never physically, emotionally or otherwise abused Maceo. The actor also referred to her own history as a victim of domestic violence, stating that she would never hurt their child.
The dispute centres on an incident on September 26, when Maceo was 12. Martinez alleged in a court filing that Berry became angry while their son was playing a virtual reality game and physically restrained him, including placing him in a headlock.
Berry has rejected that account. She told the court she entered Maceo's room to tell him to stop gaming and began recording him. According to her declaration, Maceo noticed the phone, grabbed it and the pair began playfully roughhousing, which she described as something they frequently do.
Berry denied putting her hands around her son's neck, choking him, restricting his breathing or restraining him. She also submitted video evidence and text messages that she said directly contradict Martinez's description of what happened.
Berry said the situation later escalated when Maceo became upset and allegedly pushed her. Her fiancé, Van Hunt, intervened after Maceo pushed her again when she attempted to take his headset.
Martinez filed for sole custody last week, after which he was granted a temporary restraining order modifying the former couple's custody arrangement. Berry has asked the court to restore their 50/50 custody agreement, which was established in August 2023 when their divorce was finalised.
Berry also disputed Martinez's request for primary custody, arguing that he is unable to provide appropriate child centred guidance. She cited concerns involving Maceo's behaviour and his need for professional support.
The former couple has previously disagreed over Maceo's care. Berry sought court ordered co parenting therapy in 2024, but her request was denied.
Halle Berry began her career as a model and beauty contestant, becoming Miss Ohio USA in 1986, finishing as first runner-up at Miss USA 1986, and placing sixth at Miss World 1986. Her early film roles include Boomerang (1992), The Flintstones (1994) and Bulworth (1998). She produced and starred in the television film Introducing Dorothy Dandridge (1999), for which she won a Primetime Emmy Award and a Golden Globe Award.
Berry won the Academy Award for Best Actress for her portrayal of a struggling widow in the romantic drama Monster's Ball (2001). She played Storm in the X-Men film series (20002014), a villain in Swordfish (2001), the Bond girl Jinx in Die Another Day (2002), a psychiatrist in Gothika (2003), and Catwoman in Catwoman (2004). She also appeared in Perfect Stranger (2007), Cloud Atlas (2012) and The Call (2013), Kingsman: The Golden Circle (2017) and John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum (2019).
Berry produced the television film Lackawanna Blues (2005), and subsequently produced several projects in which she also performed, including the film Frankie & Alice (2010) and the CBS science fiction series Extant (20142015). In 2014, Berry launched the production company 606 Films. In 2020, she made her directorial debut with the Netflix drama Bruised. She has been a Revlon spokesmodel since 1996.
The allegations remain disputed, and no finding that Berry abused Maceo has been established.

title: Disney  to stream Super Bowl in 2027
description: Disney  to stream Super Bowl in 2027
content:
Game scheduled to take place on Feb 14 in Inglewood, California
Disney+ will stream Super Bowl LXI in 2027, giving subscribers another way to watch the NFL championship game alongside its traditional broadcast on ESPN and ABC.
The game is scheduled to take place on February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. It will mark the first Super Bowl produced and carried by ESPN, with Joe Buck, Troy Aikman, Lisa Salters and Laura Rutledge among the broadcasters involved in the coverage.
In the US, Disney+ subscribers will have access to the same English-language presentation airing on ESPN and ABC, as well as the Spanish-language broadcast from ESPN Deportes. Disney+ will also make the Super Bowl available in more than 55 international markets, including Latin America, Brazil, the Caribbean, South Africa and Australia and New Zealand.
The streaming move expands Disney+'s role in live sports as the company continues to bring more ESPN programming to the service. Ahead of Super Bowl LXI, Disney+ will stream two Monday Night Football games, beginning with the Dallas Cowboys' game against the Philadelphia Eagles on October 26. A second game will be announced at a later date.
The Super Bowl will also remain available through the ESPN app in the US. ESPN will offer its traditional broadcast, the Spanish-language telecast and the ManningCast featuring Peyton and Eli Manning, alongside additional Super Bowl Sunday programming.
Disney is already preparing for a major Super Bowl presence, with ESPN planning to establish ESPN Beach at Santa Monica Beach ahead of the game. The week-long broadcast hub will begin on February 8 and will include a free fan experience at the Santa Monica Pier.
Super Bowl LXI has also generated record advertising demand. Disney said ABC and ESPN have already sold all commercial inventory for the broadcast, marking the earliest sell-out by a network in Super Bowl history. Fifty-eight brands across 34 categories have secured advertising spots, including nine companies making their Super Bowl debut.
With Disney+ joining ESPN and ABC, Super Bowl LXI will become one of Disney's biggest live-streaming events yet, further expanding the company's push to combine its traditional television networks with its streaming platforms.
The Super Bowl is among the top-ten world's most-watched sporting events and frequently commands the largest audience among all American broadcasts during the year. Its viewership is bested by the UEFA Champions League final, FIFA World Cup, Tour de France, Cricket World Cup, FIFA Women's World Cup, Summer Olympic Games, and the Winter Olympic games as the most watched sporting event worldwide, and the seven most-watched broadcasts in American television history are Super Bowls. Its halftime shows feature top artists, the most recent of which being Bad Bunny. Headlining a Super Bowl is considered one of the highest honors in music. The Super Bowl is also the second-largest event for American food consumption, behind Thanksgiving dinner.

title: Paris Fashion Week showcases climate change inspired dresses
description: Paris Fashion Week showcases climate change inspired dresses
content:
Creative Director Nicolas Ghesquière unveils airy designs to counter rising global temperatures
Louis Vuitton showed fluid jackets and slinky, sheer dresses on Tuesday as womenswear creative director Nicolas Ghesquière said hotter temperatures caused by climate change were changing his approach to developing fabrics and designing clothes.
Light, flowing fabrics were used throughout the spring/summer 2027 collection on simple strappy dresses, loosely fastened jackets and sheer skirts in white or pastel pink and blue.
A black and white check look and dresses covered in an iridescent diamond pattern provided graphic elements in otherwise pared-back, tonal outfits.
Models emerged in between Louis Vuitton-branded cars on a set made to look like a highway, with a tar floor and road markings - decor Ghesquière said was inspired by learning that the stunning Louvre courtyard was for decades used as a parking lot for finance ministry officials, before the ?museum's ?famous glass pyramids were installed.
Jackets featured flowing sleeves with some also extending into a long train trailing behind the model, and trousers were wide and fluid with long slits up the side to let air in. Small, simple handbags came in cream and lemon tones.
Ghesquière told reporters after the show that despite the ?minimalist appearance, "making things extremely light is very complex and the engineering and development of fabric to fight that gravity is also very complex".
Louis Vuitton, the flagship brand of luxury giant LVMH, has struggled with falling sales ?of its famous monogrammed handbags as fewer middle-class shoppers feel they can stretch to high-end purchases. The monogram was used lightly in the collection, featuring only on a couple of handbags and ?a leather bomber jacket.
A crowd of screaming fans outside the show greeted the arrival of K-pop star Felix, while France's first lady Brigitte Macron was among the celebrity guests, along with actors Zendaya, Emma Stone, and Saoirse Ronan.
In addition to ready-to-wear shows, there are men's and haute couture shows; these are held semiannually for the spring/summer and autumn/winter seasons. The haute couture collections are always presented and exhibited before the ready-to-wear collections, with there being a total of a little over 100 collections each season. Also, every year, famous brands like Dior, Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Kenzo, Givenchy, and Céline host their shows in historical places such as the Carrousel du Louvre and the Grand Palais.
In order to participate, the houses must fulfill the criteria that are set in place by the Chambre Syndicale de la Haute Couture, such as a requirement of 35 looks per year that need to include day and evening wear. Only a few houses are able to fulfill this requirement; therefore, this leaves few to participate in haute couture fashion shows. Since there are only a few spots left for those to participate, there are the well-known high-end fashion brands like Chanel and Alexander Mcqueen, but also the lesser-known ones like Maxime Simöens and Eymele Burgaud.
Paris Fashion Week is part of the global "Big 4" fashion weeks, the others being London Fashion Week, Milan Fashion Week and New York Fashion Week. The schedule begins with New York, followed by London, and then Milan and ends in Paris. New York was the first city to hold a "fashion week".
Although the first fashion week was held in New York, the event itself derives from "salon shows" ("défilés de mode" in French, literally "fashion parades") in Paris couture salons.
Before this organized event was recognized in New York City, fashion showings were being held in Paris as early as the 1700s.

title: Pakistani film 'Wakhri' selected for major UK fest | The Express Tribune
description:
Pakistani film 
'Wakhri' selected for major UK fest
content:
Qandeel Baloch-inspired work to be showcased during 'South Asian Film Season'
Pakistani film 'Wakhri', inspired by the tragic story of social media personality Qandeel Baloch, has been selected for Channel 4 and Film4's South Asian Film Season 2026 in the UK, where it will be showcased alongside a selection of contemporary films from across South Asia.
Directed by Iram Parveen Bilal, the film follows Noor Malik, a widowed schoolteacher who becomes an overnight social media sensation after sharing her unfiltered views about life as a woman in modern-day Pakistan.
Although the film draws inspiration from Qandeel Baloch's story, its themes extend beyond one individual or country. 'Wakhri' explores questions surrounding women's voices, social expectations, gender inequality, online identity and the pressures that come with sudden visibility on social media.
This year's South Asian Film Season features nine films from India, Pakistan and Bangladesh. The season has been curated by Indian cinema expert and longtime season consultant Nasreen Munni Kabir. The selected films span drama, thriller and social realism, exploring themes including class, racial, political and gender divides. Speaking to The Express Tribune, 'Wakhri' producer Abid Merchant described the film's inclusion in the season as an important recognition.
"This is a huge validation for us. Wakhri is about a widowed teacher who raises her voice on social media. It is inspired by the tragic story of Qandeel Baloch, but its message is universal," Merchant said. He added that the film's journey from international film festivals to a major UK broadcaster represented an important milestone for the project.

title: World Culture Festival projects our identity
description: World Culture Festival projects our identity
content:
Sindh Minister lauds Karachi event's role in highlighting country's soft power
Sindh's Minister for Culture and Tourism Zulfiqar Ali Shah has said the World Culture Festival has become an important platform for projecting Pakistan's soft image and positive cultural identity to the world.
Speaking at a press conference in Karachi on Wednesday about the third World Culture Festival 2026, Shah said the festival would begin on October 29 and continue until November 22.
He said Pakistan had historically been viewed internationally through the lens of terrorism, but cultural activities were now helping present a different image of the country.
"Artists coming from different parts of the world see Pakistan and its culture up close and return to their countries with a message of peace and positivity," he said.
The provincial minister claimed that the number of foreign tourists visiting Sindh's tourist destinations had increased by around 50% over the past three years. He said he believed the World Culture Festival had also contributed to this positive trend.
Shah said he had been associated with the festival alongside Arts Council President Muhammad Ahmed Shah from the first day to the last over the past three years.
The third edition of the festival will bring artists from around 150 countries to Karachi. More than 1,000 international artists are expected to participate, while over 500 Pakistani artists will also perform at different events.
The minister also highlighted Sindh's cultural heritage, describing it as a land of Sufis with a history spanning 5,000 years.
He said the poetry of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai gave women a central role and highlighted their rights and dignity.
Shah said the Culture Department would continue to support the Arts Council and that efforts would be made to invite PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari to the festival.
'We want to turn the entire area into an Art Village'
Sindh Chief Secretary Syed Haider Shah said the government's vision was to expand cultural activities beyond the Arts Council and transform the surrounding area into an "Art Village".
He said the area already had a museum and space for cultural activities, while the government was working to improve roads, lighting, seating and other public facilities.
The plan, he said, was to improve the area stretching from the Arts Council towards Burns Road for pedestrians and make it more attractive for residents and visitors.
Local communities and civil society were also being involved in the project, he said.
The chief secretary said the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation, town administration, Water Board and deputy commissioner's office were among the institutions working on the initiative.
He said the government hoped to complete the project before winter.

title: Joint efforts needed to accelerate development
description: Joint efforts needed to accelerate development
content:
Governor assures businessmen of conveying proposals, concerns to relevant authorities
Punjab Governor Sardar Saleem Haider Khan has said that closer cooperation, continuous consultation and joint efforts between the government and the business community can further accelerate the pace of economic development. He said the business community was playing an important role in the national economy and the government was committed to working closely with the private sector to promote industry, trade, investment and exports.
He was speaking to a delegation of the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI), led by President Ali Hussam Asghar and comprising SVP Sardar Usman Ghani, VP Chaudhry Khadim Hussain and executive committee members. The governor remarked that Lahore's business community was an important partner in Pakistan's economic development. He said that meaningful progress in industry, trade, investment and employment could be achieved when the government and private sector move forward with mutual trust, consultation and cooperation.
He underscored that the Governor House would remain accessible to the business community and he would convey their proposals and concerns to the relevant federal and provincial authorities so that business activities could be further promoted.
Khan called the development of agriculture sector and the prosperity of farmers vital for economic stability. "Strengthening industry and agriculture will not only contribute to economic stability but also help increase exports and create employment opportunities."
Speaking on the occasion, LCCI President Ali Hussam Asghar stressed that the chamber would continue its positive and constructive engagement with the government and make all-out efforts to promote the industry, trade and the national economy.

title: PSX edges up 120 points amid profit taking
description: PSX edges up 120 points amid profit taking
content:
Morning gains evaporate as cautious sentiment emerges over oil supply risks
Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) struggled to hold on to early gains on Wednesday as a cautious tone emerged in the latter half, but still late recovery helped the benchmark index close marginally higher.
The KSE-100 index opened in positive territory but turned volatile later, when profit-taking erased most of the morning gains. It settled 120.30 points, or 0.07%, higher at 168,580.41 after hitting the intra-day peak of 169,271.99 and the low of 168,065.87.
Market sentiment was influenced by hopes of talks between the government and PTI, although the opposition party had so far described the prime minister's proposal as merely an offer and called for a formal approach to its parliamentary leaders. The prospect of political engagement provided some support, but failed to prevent the market from losing momentum as the session progressed.
The market also tracked global developments, with Brent crude rising above $100 a barrel amid continuing Middle East supply risks and a storm heading towards oil-producing regions in the United States.
According to KASB KTrade equity trader Ahmed Sheraz, the KSE-100 index closed marginally higher by 120 points (+0.07%) in a mixed and cautious session with 244 million shares traded. Sector-wise, oil & gas and fertiliser came under pressure, while technology stocks lent support. Mari Energies, Meezan Bank and Lucky Cement closed negative, whereas UBL, Systems, Pakistan State Oil and PTCL ended in the black. "The muted index performance reflected a lack of clear direction despite healthy market activity," he said.
"Going forward, elevated oil prices are the key overhang, with Brent trading between $101 and $103 a barrel, raising concerns for Pakistan as an oil-importing economy. A prolonged uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz could keep volatility high, while a relatively cooler domestic political environment offers some relief as government-opposition talks seem to be happening again," Sheraz wrote.
Arif Habib Limited (AHL) Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib observed that the PSX witnessed a consolidation session on Wednesday, where the KSE-100 gained 120 points (+0.07%). The market initially carried forward Tuesday's positive momentum, with the benchmark touching the intra-day high of 169,272 (+812 points; +0.48%). However, profit-taking emerged at higher levels, particularly around the 169k mark, eroding most of the earlier gains and resulting in a largely flattish close.
"The session reflected a cautious approach by investors following the recent recovery," he said. UBL, Systems, PSO, PTCL and K-Electric added 301 points to the index, while Mari, Meezan Bank, Lucky Cement, Hub Power and OGDC erased 187 points.
"Going forward, the KSE-100 may sustain its recovery if oil prices remain subdued and Middle East risks ease, though geopolitical uncertainty may keep volatility elevated. 170k remains the key psychological level, with focus on oil prices and institutional flows," Najib added.
Overall trading volumes rose to 586.9 million shares from Tuesday's tally of 432 million,

title: Rising expenses hurt competitiveness
description: Rising expenses hurt competitiveness
content:
Industry seeks meeting with govt officials to review problems, find out practical solutions
Pakistan's hosiery and knitwear export industry is losing its global competitiveness due to rising production costs, delays in refunds and increasing regulatory and compliance expenses. The Pakistan Hosiery Manufacturers and Exporters Association (PHMA) has called for urgent measures to protect the competitiveness of this key export sector and safeguard export orders.
The demand was made by PHMA Central Chairman Zia Alamdar Hussain in a letter addressed to the federal secretary commerce. The letter urged the Ministry of Commerce to immediately convene a consultative meeting between PHMA representatives and officials from the Ministry of Finance, State Bank of Pakistan, Federal Board of Revenue and other relevant government institutions.
The meeting, it said, should review the problems confronting the hosiery and knitwear export sector and formulate practical measures to protect export orders and Pakistan's competitiveness. The letter revealed that the apparel, hosiery and knitwear industry was facing multiple challenges, including a historic increase in production costs, exceptionally high freight charges, load-shedding coupled with high energy tariffs, heavy taxes, liquidity problems, growing competition from regional countries and weak demand in global markets.
These factors were making it increasingly difficult for Pakistani exporters to remain competitive in international markets, secure new orders and retain existing international buyers. The letter said an extraordinary increase in sea freight had further undermined Pakistan's export competitiveness. Freight rates to some key international markets had gone up by 1.5 to 2.5 times, significantly raising the landed cost of Pakistani products.
Exporters either had to absorb the additional cost themselves, further reducing the already limited profit margins, or pass it on to buyers, making Pakistani products more expensive than those from competing countries. The PHMA chairman urged the government to help exporters cope with the exceptional increase in production, energy, freight and other business costs. In this regard, the PHMA proposed a temporary Duty Drawback on Local Taxes and Levies (DLTL) support of 6% to 8% of FOB value on a shipment basis for a limited period.

title: Non compliant traders to face Rs150 000 penalty
description: Non compliant traders to face Rs150 000 penalty
content:
FBR plans to apply old law; only 100 new retailers file returns under fixed tax
As 100 new retailers submitted returns under the fixed tax scheme and paid an average of Rs32,000, the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) decided to move against non-compliant shopkeepers under the old law and planned to serve them first notice with a Rs150,000 penalty.
The Rs150,000 penalty with the notice to file income tax returns on the expiry of the extended deadline will be many times more than the first-month penalty of Rs10,000 under Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's third tax scheme for retailers in the past four years.
The FBR management plans to map 30,000 traders, who should receive the first notice – a target that seems over-ambitious. Government sources told The Express Tribune that after the failure of the new tax scheme, the internal blame game has begun. In a meeting, they said, the FBR administration described the scheme as not implementable. FBR authorities were of the view that no effective punitive measures had been given in the scheme to force traders to become filers. The Rs10,000 penalty in the first month was many times lower than the penalty under the Income Tax Ordinance for not filing income tax returns and the wealth statement, according to them.
The government had offered traders to pay just 1% fixed income tax or a minimum of Rs25,000 in return for exemption from audit and the facility to deal in cash by not installing the digital machines. As of Wednesday, only 100 new traders had joined the scheme and paid Rs3.2 million in income tax as their full and final liability for tax year 2026 that ended in June. The average tax paid by these traders was Rs32,000, which was Rs7,000 higher than the minimum tax required under the scheme. A total of 2,593 new retailers have so far registered under the new scheme but only 100 of them opted to file returns. Overall, the total returns under the scheme were over 1,000 but 99% were already part of the tax system but they contributed very little.
According to the FBR, there were 4.3 million traders in Pakistan and only 600,000 were part of the tax system. The new scheme targeted the remaining 3.7 million shopkeepers. Sources said there were two views within the government to proceed against the non-compliant traders. One view was that the government should adopt a gradual approach where in the first month a penalty of Rs10,000 would be imposed that would increase to Rs25,000 in the second month and Rs50,000 in the third month. The other view was that the state should remain patient and follow the penalty path given in the scheme.
Tax officials said the scheme was voluntary and those who would not join till the expiry of the deadline were exposed to a treatment under the existing law, a top taxman remarked. They said the FBR would send at least 10,000 to 15,000 notices under Section 114(4) of the Income Tax Ordinance instead of under the fixed tax scheme.
Section 114 (4) states that the FBR commissioner may ask a person to file a return within 30 days from the date of service of such notice or such longer or shorter period as may be specified in such notice or as the commissioner may allow. Section 182 (1) states that where any person fails to furnish a return of income as required under Section 114 within the due date, the FBR can impose a minimum penalty of Rs10,000 in case of an individual having 75% or more income from salary; or Rs50,000 in all other cases.
In addition to the Rs50,000 penalty, these traders would also be liable to a Rs100,000 penalty for not filing the wealth statement. Section 182 (1AA) states where any person fails to furnish a wealth statement or wealth reconciliation statement, such person shall pay a penalty of 0.1% of the taxable income per week or Rs100,000, whichever is higher.
The government is now facing another challenge as traders have announced a partial strike on Thursday against the registration of police cases for using plastic bags. Traders' leader Ajmal Baloch maintained that he still supported the fixed tax scheme and the protest was only against the ICT administration. He said someone from within the government was trying to sabotage the scheme by creating hurdles in the way of effective working of the online application designed to file returns.
Baloch said the application either remained non-operational and if it was operational there were technical glitches. He added that the application was not allowing adjustment of withholding tax paid through electricity bills and it was rectified on Wednesday.
