title: Mir Raza commission closes but mystery remains  | The Express Tribune
description: Judge presses police on missing CCTV, conflicting medical opinions and handling of key evidence
content:
Judge presses police on missing CCTV, conflicting medical opinions and handling of key evidence
Fifteen sittings, 49 witnesses and weeks of questioning later, the judicial commission probing Mir Raza’s death concluded its proceedings on Wednesday, but several key questions surrounding the case remained unanswered.
Raza, the 25-year-old entrepreneur, went missing from Karachi’s PECHS area on July 28. His body was found the following day in bushes near a wedding hall in Gulistan-e-Johar.
The final hearing turned into a searching examination of the police investigation, with the commission questioning the handling of the crime scene, missing CCTV footage, leaked private chats, cryptocurrency transactions and conflicting medical opinions.
Investigating officer (IO) Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Siraj Lashari told the commission that the probe was continuing to determine whether Raza had committed suicide or had been murdered. “Police could have easily picked up someone and beaten a confession out of them, but we want justice in this case,” he said.
Read : Judicial commission visits Mir Raza murder site, summons key witness
Lashari said a super medical board was proposed because of discrepancies between the reports of Dr Usama and Dr Summaiya Syed, adding that the circumstances and evidence contradicted both reports.
Commission head Justice Umar Sial, however, questioned why the opinion of a single doctor appeared to be carrying so much weight when an eight-member medical board had already conducted the post-mortem. “The Sindh government is facing embarrassment because of Dr Usama. One Usama appears to outweigh everyone else,” he remarked.
Citizens Police Liaison Committee (CPLC) representative Kashif told the commission that its analysis of call detail records, geofencing and CCTV footage had not produced any concrete conclusion. He said geofencing began on July 28 and 29 and no suspicious activity or unusually frequent contact with a particular number was found.
Raza’s internet remained active until 4:25am, while Apple Maps was accessed between 4:10am and 4:20am. Police approached the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) and Apple for IP-related information.
The CPLC had 46 cameras in Gulistan-e-Jauhar Blocks 1 to 4, but the incident location fell outside their coverage. Raza appeared on only three cameras. The commission also questioned five missing hours of CCTV footage from Masjid Khizra. Kashif attributed the problem to the mosque’s outdated surveillance system.
Justice Sial sharply questioned the police over the preservation of the crime scene, noting that dozens of officers had entered the area.
He also questioned the evidentiary value of footage recorded on a mobile phone by Station House Officer (SHO) Adeel Afzal and noted that a guesthouse DVR had been found in the officer’s vehicle. “The crime scene was made a mess,” the judge remarked, questioning why no action had been taken against those responsible.
درجنوں پولیس افسران شامل ہوئے جس سے کرائم سین کا کباڑا کر دیا گیا، جوڈیشل کمیشن کے سخت ریمارکس مزید پڑھیں : https://t.co/zWtDwjnO3c #MirRazaCase #Karachi #Latestnews #Expressnews pic.twitter.com/SXkK9Q8ij7
He also asked whether the police’s claim that the crime scene unit reached the spot within 15 minutes was accurate, asking: “Is the IG Sindh lying?”
Read More : ‘You botched the case, you’re also suspicious’: Judge grills SSP over Mir Raza probe
The commission grilled Lashari over Ali Shaz, whose name had surfaced in connection with a voice note.
Justice Sial questioned whether police had adequately investigated Shaz’s movements, his departure abroad, his brother’s arrival in Karachi and his apparent concern for Raza. The judge noted that two suspicious vehicles had emerged during the investigation and that Shaz owned similar vehicles.
Lashari said investigators had found no link between Shaz and the incident and that there was no record placing him near the crime scene.
The alleged leak of private conversations between Raza and his fiancée Salwa also came under scrutiny.
Lashari confirmed that police had taken Salwa’s phone and extracted private chats. Justice Sial questioned how the chats later appeared on social media. “If a private chat has been leaked, it is a crime,” the judge said, directing police to identify those responsible and register a case if necessary.
Police also told the commission that transactions worth around Rs90 million had taken place through three cryptocurrency accounts.
Lashari said the NCCIA had been approached for details. Jibran Nasir, counsel for the family, said an examination of bank accounts had identified three individuals and cryptocurrency-related payments had reached Raza’s account.
Lashari said a review of the crypto account showed a shortfall of around Rs30 million, apparently treated by the platform as a loss.
Justice Sial directed police to obtain the platform’s profit-and-loss ledger to establish the actual position.
At the close of proceedings, Justice Sial told Raza’s family that their concerns had proved justified. “No government representative contacted or met us,” he said, adding that the family had not been provided sufficient information. “Had you been kept informed, the situation would have been different,” he said.
Also Read : Mir Raza commission seeks answers from senior police officers
He rejected criticism that the commission had given the case an ethnic colour and defended questioning people associated with a mosque. “We questioned those whom we found suspicious. Saying that someone should not be questioned merely because of a mosque is not right,” he said.
Lashari said the police wanted justice rather than simply arresting someone and forcing a confession. “Whether it is suicide or murder, the investigation is continuing. Whatever the truth is, it will come out,” he said.
According to commission Registrar Abdul Majid, 15 sittings were held, and statements of 49 witnesses were recorded. The commission had concluded its proceedings and would now prepare its report and recommendations. Justice Sial said the report would be placed at the disposal of the chief minister.
The judicial commission was constituted on August 24, while the Sindh cabinet approved an extension of its tenure on October 1.
Police initially treated Raza's death as a possible suicide, but the court ordered a second post-mortem exam to conclusively determine the cause of death after the first post-mortem report failed to give detailed insight into the victim’s demise. The second autopsy conducted after Raza’s exhumation found a firearm entry wound, multiple ante-mortem injuries and signs of internal bleeding, leading investigators to treat the case as murder.
The initial post-mortem had faced several objections, with the Karachi police surgeon identifying 14 deficiencies, including the absence of an X-ray, failure to collect hand swabs for gunshot-residue analysis and the lack of chemical examination of gunpowder marks around the bullet wound.
Also Read: Mir Raza judicial commission’s term extended until October 15
The investigation subsequently came under scrutiny from Raza’s family, who alleged serious lapses in the handling of evidence and CCTV footage and sought the formation of a joint investigation team. The Sindh High Court later rejected the family’s plea for a JIT but directed the relevant authorities to conduct the investigation impartially, fairly and expeditiously.
Police told a Senate committee in September that they had recorded statements from 78 people but had not found evidence linking anyone to Raza’s alleged murder. Investigators nevertheless continued to treat the case as murder, while reviewing medical, chemical, forensic and digital evidence.
The Sindh government had meanwhile established a judicial commission headed by Sindh High Court Justice Umar Sial to examine the circumstances surrounding Raza’s death, the conduct of the investigation and any possible negligence or concealment of evidence by police or other officials.
The judicial commission had so far examined police records, witness statements and the circumstances surrounding Mir Raza Ali’s death, with its proceedings raising discrepancies in witness accounts, the handling of evidence and the initial post-mortem. The commission also questioned senior police and health officials over the investigation, including the handling of CCTV footage, Raza’s phone and smartwatch, and the initial focus on a possible suicide.

title: 81 US aircraft lost or damaged during Iran war  congressional document shows
description: Nonpartisan research office tallies combat casualties  including 45 drones and fighter jets  as operation costs mount
content:
Nonpartisan research office tallies combat casualties, including 45 drones and fighter jets, as operation costs mount
At least 81 US fixed-wing, rotary-wing, and uncrewed aircraft were lost or damaged during military operations against Iran, according to a recent report prepared by the nonpartisan Congressional Research Service.
The figures compile operational incidents recorded since Feb. 28 across Pentagon records, US Central Command (CENTCOM) statements, military inspector general findings, and press accounts.
The compilation shows extensive losses across uncrewed platforms, led by 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones and three MQ-1 multi-role craft downed during operations, along with one MQ-4C Triton that crashed in a flight mishap.
Read: Iranian president says US deal ‘not out of reach’ in call with Putin
Manned combat airframes also sustained substantial hits.
Twelve F-15E Strike Eagle fighters were affected, including three destroyed by friendly fire over Kuwait, one downed over Iran, and eight that suffered light damage during an Iranian missile strike on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan before returning to service.
Iranian ground fire damaged an advanced F-35A Lightning II, while two A-10 Thunderbolt II ground-attack jets were lost or heavily damaged.
Support fleets suffered major attrition as well.
Seven KC-135 Stratotanker refueling craft were affected, including one fatal crash in Iraq that killed six crew members and five reportedly damaged on the ground in Saudi Arabia.
One E-3 Sentry early warning plane took a direct hit, two MC-130J special operations transports were intentionally destroyed during a rescue mission, and seven military helicopters, including AH-64 Apache and AH-6 Little Bird models, were lost or damaged.
The disclosures arrive amid soaring financial tolls in the Iran war, which began Feb. 28 with coordinated US-Israeli strikes.
A Lead Inspector General report in September estimated total campaign expenses at $33.4 billion through late June, including $3.7 billion in equipment losses, while the Congressional Budget Office projected hardware replacement costs at up to $3.3 billion.
The Congressional Research Service noted that the number of aircraft may remain subject to revision due to classification, ongoing combat activity, and attribution.

title: Guterres hails Pakistan   s role in peacekeeping  diplomacy during meetings with PM  CDF Munir
description: Pays tribute to sacrifices  contributions of Pakistan and its Armed Forces in the war against terror
content:
PM Shehbaz tells UN chief dialogue and diplomacy remain the only viable path to resolving disputes
Outgoing United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Wednesday appreciated Pakistan’s longstanding contribution to the UN and international peace and security, particularly its diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue, mediation and de-escalation.
The appreciation came during separate meetings with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir during Guterres’s three-day visit to Pakistan.
According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office, the premier welcomed Guterres at the Prime Minister's House and lauded his principled commitment to the UN Charter, multilateralism, international law, dialogue and the peaceful settlement of disputes.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif welcomed United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who is on an official visit to Pakistan, this evening. The Prime Minister lauded the Secretary-General for his principled commitment to the UN Charter, multilateralism,… pic.twitter.com/iQWtdSgrlK
Acknowledging the secretary general’s contribution to international peace and security during his tenure, the prime minister reaffirmed Pakistan’s strong commitment to an effective, inclusive and representative UN, particularly at a time when multilateralism faced significant challenges.
The statement said PM Shehbaz welcomed the secretary general’s UN80 Initiative and emphasised that UN reform should remain responsive to the priorities of developing countries while strengthening conflict prevention, peaceful settlement of disputes, peacekeeping and peacebuilding.
He also reaffirmed Pakistan’s longstanding commitment to UN peacekeeping and its continued contribution to the maintenance of international peace and security.
The prime minister highlighted Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue and de-escalation, including its mediation role between the United States and Iran.
“Dialogue and diplomacy remain the only viable path to resolving disputes and preventing escalation,” PM Shehbaz stressed, while reiterating Pakistan’s commitment to regional peace and stability.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif welcomed United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres at the Prime Minister' House, today. The Secretary General is on an official visit to Pakistan. pic.twitter.com/hyaw4jqihw
He also emphasised the need for a peaceful resolution of the Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir dispute in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people.
Highlighting the Indus Waters Treaty, which was unilaterally suspended by India following the terrorist attack in Pahalgam, PM Shehbaz called it a binding international agreement. "India’s unilateral decision to place it in abeyance has no legal basis," he said.
During the meeting, the prime minister expressed serious concern over terrorism emanating from Afghanistan and the presence of terrorist groups on Afghan soil.
“A peaceful and stable Afghanistan remains in Pakistan’s interest,” he said, emphasising the need for concrete and verifiable action against such terrorist groups.
Reaffirming Pakistan’s steadfast support for the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination and statehood, the prime minister reiterated Pakistan’s support for implementation of the Gaza Peace Plan and UN Security Council Resolution 2803.
He also underscored the need for greater access to affordable and concessional financing for developing countries to advance development and climate resilience.
Guterres appreciated Pakistan’s longstanding contributions to the UN and to international peace and security, including its significant role in UN peacekeeping and its constructive engagement in the Security Council.
He particularly appreciated Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue, mediation and de-escalation, and welcomed its continued commitment to multilateralism and the purposes and principles of the UN Charter.
Later, the prime minister hosted a dinner in honour of the UN secretary general and his delegation.
Guterres also met CDF Munir and praised Pakistan’s efforts towards the peaceful resolution of regional conflicts during a meeting.
According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), Guterres met CDF Munir at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, where the two exchanged views on “matters of mutual interest, the prevailing regional security environment and the United Nations’ role in promoting international peace and security”.
“Guterres paid tribute to the sacrifices and contributions of Pakistan and its Armed Forces in the war against terror and in UN peacekeeping missions. He also acknowledged Pakistan’s continued commitment to international peace and security, specifically appreciating Pakistan’s efforts towards the peaceful resolution of regional conflicts,” the statement said.
The ISPR further stated that CDF Munir and Guterres exchanged views on regional stability, the Jammu and Kashmir dispute, India's abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty, and terrorism emanating from Afghanistan .
"The CDF Munir reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to international peace and highlighted its contributions to UN peacekeeping missions," the statement said, adding that CDF Munir "also lauded the United Nations’ role under the leadership of Guterres, in advancing peace, stability and humanitarian cooperation".
UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres met Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces, at GHQ, Rawalpindi, ISPR says. Discussions covered regional security, Jammu and Kashmir, India’s abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty and terrorism emanating… pic.twitter.com/Fx6qB0ssqM
The outgoing UN chief stated, “Your efforts helped deliver the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, the subsequent ceasefire, and the framework for future negotiations,” adding that “every Pakistani should be proud of that pivotal role.”
Guterres also said that Islamabad's contribution "has been on full display as a member of the UN Security Council these past two years.” He noted further, “At a time of growing division and mistrust around the world, Pakistan put a spotlight on the value of multilateralism, dialogue, mediation, and diplomacy. Those same values are vital within societies as well.”
Read: Guterres calls for stronger UN, global cooperation
Regarding terrorism, the secretary-general had said in his address alongside FM Dar that Pakistan had “endured immense suffering,” noting that “thousands of people lost their lives” and reaffirming that the UN stood with Islamabad “in confronting this threat of terrorism.”
According to Guterres, “Pakistan faces challenges, as all nations do”; however, he said what always stood out to him “is the resilience of the Pakistani people and their determination to build a better future.”
Prior to the press conference, the secretary-general and FM Dar discussed regional and global issues relating to peace and security. The discussions covered Palestine, Jammu and Kashmir, Afghanistan, counter-terrorism and the future of multilateralism.
FM Dar briefed Guterres on Pakistan’s positions on Jammu and Kashmir and the Indus Waters Treaty while also highlighting Islamabad's diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue and de-escalation, including its facilitation of the Islamabad Talks between the US and Iran.

title: Russia says plague institute worker s death does not risk an epidemic
description: Laboratory worker fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances  prompting authorities to quarantine dozens
content:
Says it properly informed WHO of plague institute worker's death, blasts media coverage
Russia's health regulator said on Wednesday there were no risks of an epidemic breaking out in Siberia after a plague institute worker there died, as the World Health Organization pressed Moscow ​for more information about her cause of death.
Russian authorities say the 28-year-old laboratory worker died last Friday from pneumonia of an as-yet unestablished origin, in a case that has prompted international concern , including ‌from US President Donald Trump. Around 200 people were initially placed in quarantine.
Asked on Wednesday whether the death was caused by a bioweapon, Trump told reporters: "Well, we don't think so. We're going to find out soon enough, but we don't think so."
He said Russia was not saying much about the situation but "they do say they have it very much under control," adding he had set up a call with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"They're sharing (information) a little bit with our people. We expect them to share it a lot ​with our people," said Trump, speaking in the Oval Office.
Global health officials - as well as the world's media - have been particularly alert to pneumonia cases of undetermined cause since the COVID-19 pandemic, which ​began with a cluster of fast-spreading fatal respiratory illness in China.
However, the cause of individual pneumonia cases can often not be determined.
US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention ⁠Director Erica Schwartz said at an event the agency was prepared to monitor and screen travelers although the risk to the US was extremely low .
The WHO initially said it estimated the risk of the Russia case to ​the public as low, based on what had been made known, but told a press conference on Wednesday it could not make a fuller risk assessment due to insufficient information from the Russian authorities.
Rospotrebnadzor, Russia's health watchdog, said ​on Wednesday it was winding down precautionary measures it had put in place after concluding there was no risk of an epidemic and that it had shared its latest information with the WHO.
No cases of plague had been detected among anyone who had come into contact with the deceased worker, Darya Shipilova, it said, and 90% of those placed in quarantine had been released after nearly 5,000 lab tests had failed to detect any dangerous pathogens.
It said Shipilova had been vaccinated and had therefore been "immune to ​the dangerous infections with which she worked". It did not say, however, what had caused the pneumonia which killed her or how she fell ill.
Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the director-general of the WHO in ​Geneva, said on Wednesday his organisation needed more information from Russia to understand what had happened.
"We would like more information to understand which laboratory tests were conducted, which pathogens were evaluated, and if this individual didn't die from plague, then how ‌did she die?" ⁠Maria Van Kerkhove, director of the WHO's department of epidemic and pandemic management, told a virtual press conference.
Tedros said the WHO had offered assistance to Russia and also repeated a request for Russia to verify "media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause".
Kremlin criticises ‘false information’ in media
The Kremlin said Russia had properly informed the WHO about the incident in line with established procedures.
When asked about the WHO's request to respond to reports about a second person in Siberia allegedly falling ill, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov urged caution when it came to using media reports as a reference for what was happening.
"There is a great deal of media coverage, and the vast majority ​of what the media are reporting about this situation ​is false information," said Peskov.
He advised the media and ⁠others to rely on information provided by the health regulator. It did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on Wednesday about the WHO's questions.
Some Western media outlets have reported — citing unnamed "Russian media" — that a second person in Siberia had died, saying they had died of plague.
Reuters was unable ​to find any such stories in Russian media or any evidence that a second person in Siberia had died although some bloggers on social media were ​making — without evidence — such assertions.
After the ⁠press conference, the WHO sent Reuters a link to a story about a potential second case by the Russian media organization starhit.ru, a celebrity gossip outlet, and a follow-up from British newspaper the Daily Mail.
Tedros said it was important to be transparent based on the lessons from COVID, adding, "We don't have any mandate actually to see whether this media is credible or not."
Russia has not formally responded to the reports about a second person dying, Tedros said, adding that he ⁠had heard only ​informally that Russia had denied those reports.
Tedros' call for more information echoed that of US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who has ​also said Moscow needs to share more information about the incident.
Pneumonia, a lung infection, can have a variety of causes including plague as well as other bacterial infections or viral respiratory diseases, such as flu or COVID-19.
No plague cases detected in Siberia, Russia says, and locals play down scare
Russia's health watchdog said on Tuesday that no cases of plague had been detected among anyone who had come ‌into contact with a Siberian plague institute laboratory worker, and locals said their lives had barely been disrupted.
Authorities say the 28-year-old woman died on Friday from pneumonia of an as-yet unestablished origin, in a case that has prompted international concern, including from US President Donald Trump.
Rospotrebnadzor, the watchdog, said in a ​statement that no infectious diseases had been reported among the staff of the same plague research institute in Irkutsk over ​the past 10 days and that extensive testing had found no microorganisms in the deceased woman's body linked ⁠to her work.
"A comprehensive set of anti-epidemic measures was immediately organised and implemented in full in accordance with public health legislation," the ​watchdog said.
"This included identifying the widest possible circle of individuals who had been in contact with the patient and arranging for them to ​be placed under medical observation in hospital with daily laboratory tests."
It said the results had revealed two cases of COVID-19 and two cases of rhinovirus infection, but that no pathogens causing other infectious diseases had been detected.
"None of the contacts showed any changes in their state of health associated with infectious disease," ​it added.
Elena Sofina, deputy head of the Shelekhov district near Irkutsk, where a local hospital was placed under quarantine, said what she called ​a "dangerous diagnosis" had not been confirmed.
She added that 60% of those placed under quarantine as a precaution had already been released. Local media said around ‌200 people ⁠had previously been quarantined.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov expressed appreciation for an offer of help on Monday from Trump, although without making clear if Moscow planned to accept it.
"It's always good when mutual assistance is offered," Peskov told reporters.
Trump on Monday described the situation as a "big problem for Russia". US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday it was incumbent on Moscow to share more information.
The World Health ​Organisation in Geneva said on Tuesday ​that Russia had told it ⁠there were no cases of plague in the city of Irkutsk. Reuters could not immediately establish if this meant they could rule out plague in the lab worker's case.
In the town of Shelekhov, where ​the lab worker is reported to have died in hospital, locals said their lives had barely ​been disrupted, although they ⁠said some people in shops had initially worn surgical face masks as a precaution.
A resident who gave her name only as Anna said the situation was calm and that people had been prepared for restrictions to be introduced, but that life had gone on pretty much as usual.
"Everyone ⁠had face ​masks at home and wore them for no more than 24 hours," she ​told Reuters .
Denis, another resident, said news of the lab worker's death had been widely discussed in the town and that the local hospital had temporarily stopped doing diagnostic tests ​but had since resumed normal business.

title: Samuel L Jackson reveals his next Marvel project but says he has    no idea    what it   s about
description: You   re not gonna be in this movie  You   ll be in the next   Jackson recalled Marvel telling him
content:
“You’re not gonna be in this movie. You’ll be in the next," Jackson recalled Marvel telling him
Samuel L. Jackson has confirmed that Nick Fury will return in an upcoming Avengers film, but the actor admits he has no idea what Marvel has planned for the character.
Jackson revealed the news during a conversation with The Direct at the premiere of his new film The Beast. When asked about his next Marvel appearance, the actor said, “Next movie... [The] movie after this one.”
Asked whether he could tease anything about the project, Jackson said he had “no idea” what it was about, adding that Marvel “hasn’t told me anything” beyond telling him, “You’re not gonna be in this movie. You’ll be in the next.”
Although Jackson did not name the films, the comments indicate that Nick Fury will not appear in Avengers: Doomsday, which is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on December 18, 2026. His next appearance is expected to be in Avengers: Secret Wars, which is set for release on December 17, 2027.
Very little is currently known about Secret Wars. Anthony and Joe Russo are directing the film, which is expected to serve as the second part of the story that begins with Avengers: Doomsday, similar to the relationship between Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame.
Jackson last appeared as Nick Fury in 2023’s The Marvels. He also led Marvel’s Disney+ series Secret Invasion that same year, marking the first time the character headlined a Marvel project.
Jackson has played Fury since the beginning of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, first appearing in the post-credits scene of 2008’s Iron Man. His return in Secret Wars will bring the character back for another major chapter of the MCU.

title: Look up and look around
description: Climate activist Adam McKay talks to Express Tribune about climate films like Don   t Look Up and his hopes for change now
content:
Climate activist McKay talks to Express Tribune about climate films like Don’t Look Up and his hopes for change now
Adam McKay is one of the biggest directors in Hollywood right now. Almost everyone reading this will have seen his movies. Starting as a writer on Saturday Night Live, he went on to direct highly successful films, such as Step Brothers, a successful comedy starring Will Ferrell and John C Reilly; The Big Short, a dark comedy about the Wall Street financial crisis, starring Brad Pitt, Steve Carrell, Christian Bale and Ryan Gosling; Vice, a movie about the former US Vice President Dick Cheney, starring Bale, and most recently he made Don’t Look Up, starring an ensemble cast including Meryl Streep and Leonardo DiCaprio, which tells the story about a scientist trying to warn the world about a meteor heading towards Planet Earth, but no one takes him seriously. The meteor is meant as an analogy for the Climate Crisis.
McKay sat down for an interview with The Express Tribune to talk about his work and the climate crisis, which is the existential crisis that Adam has dedicated his life to.
ET: Could you briefly introduce yourself and give us a background of your work?.
Adam McKay: I'm a writer, director, and producer, originally from Philadelphia. I became climate aware probably about eight, [or] almost 10 years. Since then, we've started a non-for-profit climate studio called Yellow Dot that combats oil company misinformation and a lot of other things.
I started as a comedy writer [for] Saturday Night Live, Upright Citizens Brigade, all of that kind of stuff. But, mostly now I'm a producer, writer, director, and a lot of my time is devoted towards climate activism.
ET: What drew you to focus on the climate crisis being in the show business?
McKay: We were working on a movie we did about Dick Cheney, and we hired a journalist to interview people about him because there's really not one defining book about Dick Cheney. So there are some really good books like The Angler and a few others, but there's not really one that kind of tells his whole story. So we hired a journalist to go interview people.
When he interviewed Christy Todd Whitman, who was head of the EPA at that time, oh my! What an earful he got about how Dick Cheney was instrumental in halting United States action on climate. Then off of that because, like a lot of people, I had seen Inconvenient Truth, I knew that it was a real thing, but I kind of assumed that we'd been working on it. And at that moment, I was like, where are we at with the climate? And right away when I looked into it, I could tell, oh, we haven't done anything.
The numbers I kept seeing were so disturbing that eventually, as my wife can tell you, I started losing sleep. …One of the benefits of having a job where you make movies and TV shows is you can call people. So I kept talking to scientists and climate journalists, looking for someone to tell me that I was wrong, that in fact, we have a lot of time, it's okay. [But] the people I talked to made it worse. So yeah, I started losing real sleep. I couldn't let it go. And that's what led to us making the movie Don't Look Up.
ET: Could you briefly explain the premise of Don't Look Up?
McKay: I thought long and hard about what is the best way to tell the story of climate in action. And, I had dramatic ideas, I had thriller ideas.
But it was a friend of mine, David Sirota [who] just made some joke about the comet hitting the earth, referring to the Chicxulub event that hit the dinosaurs, some 60 million years ago. And he [Sirota] was like, we all know it, and no one cares. And that just clicked. I really felt like, if we could laugh about the horror show that's coming, that would mean that we have enough distance that we can do stuff.
The premise is a comet is going to hit the earth, and scientists discover it and leaders, news media, billionaires, corporations don't really care or just want to profit off of it, which, sadly, is exactly what happened.
ET: Ever since that movie, things in the US have only gotten worse in terms of the climate crisis. Have you had any luck in bringing people along in terms of at least your circles in Hollywood?
McKay: You know, it's both sad and positive, because for the most part, no. I've learned a lot about the mind-altering effects of privilege, money, and ego. But then there have been people, and whenever they step up, it's kind of like a mini miracle. So, there are people that are waking up.
When I made the movie, and in the year or two afterwards, pretty much everyone treated me like I was crazy, I was overreacting. And that's not really the case anymore. Now, all that really matters is who is being active.
And that's the level I wish were higher. But there are people like Hannah Einbinder, Mark Ruffalo, and really good people who are seeing the truth and responding rather than worrying about their career or fallout or their fans reacting negatively. So, yeah, ever since we put that movie out, it's been quite the journey. Even putting the movie out was quite the journey.
ET: Was this before the fires that happened in Los Angeles?
AM: It was before. Anyone who knows how climate warming, rapid climate warming works, knows that windblown fires are one of the major threats.
We had been trying to reach out to the mayor of Los Angeles [to ask] like, what are your plans? We watched in horror as the mayor cut the firefighting budget. At that point, I had spoken to enough elected officials to understand that for the most part, none of them had any clue– [or] any care about what was happening.
When that red flag notice went up, I had done posts on social media saying, hey, I'm not saying it definitely will be a mega disaster, but it's got a very good chance to be one, be prepared. And it was funny because you could see in the responses, people were rolling their eyes like, oh, he's the crazy climate guy. So, people have died, people have lost their homes. You feel a sick, kind of queasy feeling about it. After the fires, they burned down pretty much whole cities.
The news of the fires failed to mention that humans cause fossil fuel warming or are the driving force behind it. Still most people in LA think it was caused by arsonists or power lines. I mean, it's really something to behold, the amount of power these oil companies have over our news media and the information we get is much stronger than I thought entering this arena.
ET: Is there some hope in the US having capacity to do something about climate?
McKay: I really don't know. For anyone not in the US, I would just say this: It is much worse than you think. I mean, corruption has spread everywhere. Elected officials are really glorified spokespeople, not even really leaders. The exceptions to that, I can maybe name 10, 12. They call me when they have to fundraise and I've had dinner with these people. [But] yeah, the US is not going to be the leader in action when it comes to the huge catastrophe we have entered. It's probably going to be China, maybe Spain, possibly France, South Korea, Brazil.
It'll be interesting to see what Pakistan does. Canada, I think they're too biased. The Scandinavian countries get it. Norway is tricky because they're heavy into oil. But I think it's going to be a case where, you know, 30 to 40 countries are going to have to form an international coalition.
The reason I say this [is that] we are out of time. We have crossed the threshold, the 1.5 degree Celsius threshold. And with this El Nino, we're being pushed towards 1.7 degrees Celsius warming, which means we likely will have our first full month at 2 degrees Celsius warming. The reason that is significant is because that officially and completely takes us out of the last almost 12,000 years of stable climate that scientists call the Holocene. The Holocene is what created the four seasons, agriculture, civilisation.
And we're now going back to that pre-history time. During the Younger Dryas period almost all bipedal apes like Neanderthals, Cro-Magnons, Gigantopithecus all died when the Amok or Atlantic Current shut down. And they think only 10,000 Homo sapiens kind of clung to life. God bless them. We are re-entering pre-Holocene conditions. And first and foremost, it's going to be the collapse of agriculture, both plant and livestock.
And that's already happening. Harvests fail around the world from rains, extreme heat, storms, fires. We scientifically, empirically are in it.
I know Pakistan has been devastated by floods.
They're going to make a lot of us feel powerless, confused, and desperate. And the one truth at the centre of these natural disasters is that the big oil companies did this knowingly and the politicians they own knowingly supported it. And the news media that didn't tell us this was happening, knowingly in exchange for money, betrayed life on earth.
And I say that not because it's about revenge or anger, but because unless you understand that, it becomes an act of God or Allah or Yahweh. And this is not an act of God. This is an act of man and greed and knowing destruction.
Once you get that, you realise we can take action. We have never let science loose on this. It's always been half measures, empty pledges.
There is no question that if in the next year or two, we, or the 30, 40, 50 countries that aren't so far gone, release science, like well-funded, high level innovation, research, development, and engineering, like scaling up. I mean, we have like five things we're going to have to do in the next two years to stop the planet from careening into God forbid three degrees, four degrees Celsius. I mean, at those numbers, that's a mass extinction.
I mean, a few people or whales or dolphins or more likely alligators and jellyfish survive, maybe, but it's a mass die-off event, unless we get to work on creating artificial albedo, geoengineering, like it's going to have to be a host of responses. It is really important to remember that human beings did this.
ET: . Part of the reason that it seems we don't get the reaction that we want from the public is that people don't know just how efficiently resources can be mobilised as they were in the second world war in the US.
McKay: It's very true. I think the one big thing is the fact that big capital, the banks, whatever you want to call it, that the big money took over the news. And even though more and more people doubt the news or are cynical, there's independent news outlets that are rising as fast as they can to kind of fill the breach. But we're really in a moment where time is of the essence. The quote I always throw around is Sir David King from England, who's as establishment as they get. He said, we have three to four years to determine the fate of mankind. And he said this in 2021.
Didn't Pakistan have a natural disaster? And was it Musharraf who didn't respond properly? And that was kind of the end of him. I mean, natural disasters have a way like Katrina with George W Bush. That was when Bush really slipped in the polls. He wasn't doing great before that. But the entire reason for organised government, a lot of it is about natural disasters. If we all work together, share resources, we can get through famine, mass destruction, [etc] by supporting each other. So after that I have no idea what's going to happen.
I mean, there is going to be an energy released from the people that we've never seen before. So you can read all these dusty political commentators, but they have no idea the paradigm shift is coming.
McKay: We're producing the second season of a great, hilarious, absurd show called The Chair Company. And if you think, oh, it's weird that he would bring that up while talking about the end of the civilised world, watch the show and then you will see why it fits. And we have a couple of really cool movies in post-production. One is called Hotel, Hotel, Hotel. Another is called Flesh of the Gods. I personally am going out with a TV show and a feature film. The feature film is purely about climate. It's called 2 degrees C. And yet, parts of it are funny, dramatic, thrilling. And it's about the new chapter that, you know, mankind, homo sapiens are now on or in.
Yellow Dot, our climate studio, is about to release a commercial parody that is voiced by Woody Harrelson that I think is pretty funny. And it's about this freakish El Nino that is about to supercharge planetary warming around the globe.
The writer is a climate activist focusing on the mechanics of mobilisation and organisation

title: Existential threats join bubble fears as AI mood sobers at Singapore forums
description: Risk of state  non state actors using AI to build new chemical  biological weapons remains a real possibility
content:
Risk of state, non-state actors using AI to build new chemical, biological weapons remains a real possibility
Existential and financial risks posed by the artificial intelligence (AI) boom were top ​of mind for investors and policymakers at two conferences in Singapore on Wednesday, highlighting a cautious shift in ‌mood around the AI trade.
Concerns that once centred on frothy valuations have broadened into a wide swathe of fears , including autonomous systems slipping out of human control, AI-designed bioweapons and the possibility that massive spending on the technology may never pay off.
"Anyone who tells you I've ​got absolute control over my autonomous agent... obviously doesn't know what he's talking about. So loss of control ​is a real threat," Singaporean Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan said at the Milken Institute Asia ⁠Summit.
"There is a revolution going on in AI, in biotech, and in energy." At #MIGlobal Asia Summit 2026 today, Vivian Balakrishnan, Minister for Foreign Affairs, Singapore spoke about how capital, tech innovation, and trade are reshaping Asia's economic future. Watch all session… pic.twitter.com/ek8rdBcuRb
Last month, the heads of leading US AI labs came together in a rare show of unity to call for slowing the ​technology's development, warning it could soon improve on its own and slip beyond human control.
Read : Bill Gates warns AI is powerful enough to 'cause a billion deaths'
Claude maker Anthropic plans to caution potential ​investors in its IPO that advanced AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity," Reuters reported last week.
Balakrishnan said on Wednesday the risk of state and non-state actors using the technology to build new weapons, "whether it's in chemistry or biology or in weapons of mass destruction, ​is very real."
Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, founder and chairperson of Indian biopharmaceutical firm Biocon, said that while AI was a force ​for good, bad actors could use it to design new viruses or pathogens.
"The real existential threat is bioterrorism," she said at the Forbes ‌Global ⁠CEO Conference, calling for guardrails and governance. "I don't think self-governance is going to work."
Investors' faith in the AI trade has propped up the stock market even as higher energy prices and episodic routs in the bond market have pushed borrowing costs in major economies to multi-decade highs.
But worries over how long the AI rally could last and what it ​means for global markets have persisted.
Read More : AI risk warnings rattle global markets
"If ​the AI narrative is ⁠unwound because of safety issues, regulation or because, as we go through 2027, end users don't see sufficient ROI (return on investment), there could be issues," said Rohit Sipahimalani, chief investment ​officer at Singapore state investor Temasek.
"The biggest risk to the market is the AI ​narrative. Right now, it ⁠seems very strong," Sipahimalani said at the Milken Institute event.
Bridgewater Associates founder Ray Dalio was less sanguine, saying AI was in a "classic bubble" and there was a difference between "how terrific a technology is and how terrific an investment is."
He told the Forbes ⁠event that ​rising rates and changing circumstances had not "yet harmed ​other things," but that there was pressure for interest rates to rise further.
Once higher rates began to bite, the bubble would start to burst, Dalio ​said. "I think we're close to that."

title: Jeremy Allen White wants to play Gene Wilder in upcoming biopic     I need the call
description: It would be an honour  He was a genius  It would be an honour  Yeah  I love him  I   ve always loved him   he said
content:
'It would be an honour. He was a genius. It would be an honour. Yeah, I love him. I’ve always loved him,' he said
Jeremy Allen White has said he would be honoured to play Gene Wilder in an upcoming biopic about the legendary actor, although he revealed that he has not yet been offered the role.
During an appearance on TODAY on October 7, White was asked by Craig Melvin whether he would consider portraying Wilder, with the question coming amid continued comparisons between the two actors because of their physical resemblance.
“Absolutely, it would be my honour,” White said. “ Young Frankenstein is one of my earliest film memories. Blazing Saddles , he’s a genius. It would be an honour. He was a genius. It would be an honour. Yeah, I love him. I’ve always loved him.”
White then made it clear that he is waiting for an official offer, adding, “I need the call.”
TODAY co-host Savannah Guthrie suggested that White might already have secured the part, asking whether he had been cast as Wilder, particularly in connection with the actor’s most famous role as Willy Wonka.
White quickly clarified that he had not been cast. “Do I already have it? No! No, no, no,” he said, before adding, “We’ll see, we’re manifesting it.”
A Gene Wilder biopic is currently in development, with Dito Montiel attached to direct after securing the rights to Wilder’s life story from the actor’s estate. The project was announced in June, although no casting has officially been confirmed.
White’s interest comes after he has taken on several roles based on real people. He portrayed Bruce Springsteen in Springsteen: Deliver Me from Nowhere and plays Wall Street Journal journalist Jeff Horwitz in Aaron Sorkin’s upcoming film The Social Reckoning .
The actor has previously spoken about the pressure involved in portraying real-life figures. While describing his experience playing Springsteen as wonderful, White said it also came with “a tremendous amount of pressure”.
White also admitted that he initially hesitated before taking the role of Horwitz because he did not want to immediately follow one real-life portrayal with another. He ultimately accepted the part after Sorkin approached him about the project.
For now, White’s comments do not confirm that he will play Wilder, but the actor has made his interest clear as the biopic continues to take shape. The Social Reckoning , meanwhile, is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on October 9.

title: Govt increases petrol by Rs1 82  cuts diesel by 91 paisas for Oct 8
description: Petrol price increases to Rs396 65 per litre  while HSD will cost Rs394 94 under daily price mechanism
content:
Petrol price increases to Rs396.65 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs394.94 under daily price mechanism
The federal government on Wednesday increased the price of petrol by Rs1.82 per litre, while decreasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by 91 paisas per litre for October 8.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs396.65 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs394.94 per litre for Thursday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government increased the price of petrol by Rs1.19 per litre, while decreasing the price of HSD by Rs1.91 per litre for October 7.
Read : Govt increases petrol by Rs1.19, cuts diesel by Rs1.91 for Oct 7
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices rose on Wednesday, with Brent ‌futures holding above $100 a barrel on supply concerns as investors weighed a surprise drop in US crude stocks, global war-driven bottlenecks, and a storm heading for US oil-producing regions.
Brent crude futures were up $1.29, or 1.28%, to $101.87 a barrel at 10:52 am ET (1452 GMT). US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude was up 22 ​cents, or 0.25%, to $89.66.
"The release of strategic oil reserves should help contain near-term price spikes by offsetting declines in commercial inventories. However, such releases provide only temporary relief, as they do not eliminate the underlying tightness in ​the global oil market," UBS analysts wrote.

title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard will    most likely    attend Ken Urker   s funeral amid family tensions
description: Blanchard said she has been invited to the funeral by Urker   s family although arrangements have not yet been finalised
content:
Blanchard said she has been invited to the funeral by Urker’s family although arrangements have not yet been finalised
Gypsy-Rose Blanchard says she will “most likely” attend the upcoming funeral of her former fiancé Ken Urker after his family invited her to the service following his death at the age of 34.
Urker, the father of Blanchard’s 21-month-old daughter Aurora, was found dead at his home in Raceland, Louisiana, on October 1, which was also his 34th birthday. The circumstances and official cause of his death remain under investigation.
Speaking to PEOPLE, Blanchard said she has been invited to the funeral by Urker’s family, although arrangements have not yet been finalised.
“As of right now, we don’t have any details. But they will let me know as soon as they form up solidified plans,” Blanchard said.
Blanchard is also planning her own celebration of life for Urker in Louisiana. She said the November memorial will include fireworks as a tribute to a tradition they shared.
“I have this memory of us for a Fourth of July celebration we had bought so many fireworks and we had the best time to shoot them off,” she said, explaining that Urker would “go overboard” when buying fireworks each year.
Blanchard and Aurora have already had the opportunity to say goodbye to Urker during a private family viewing. Blanchard described the experience as extremely difficult and said Aurora called him “Daddy” when she saw him.
“We got to see him one last time for a private viewing for his family. The day before yesterday and it was the hardest thing to do,” she said.
The plans come amid tension between Blanchard and Urker’s sister Autumn, who has publicly criticised Blanchard following her brother’s death.
Autumn has disputed aspects of Blanchard’s account of her relationship with Urker, including reports that the pair were still together shortly before his death. She alleged that they had separated more than a month earlier and rejected claims that they were engaged or planning to have another child.
Autumn also criticised Blanchard over reports that Urker was discovered after failing to respond to a birthday message from her. She described the suggestion as “a slap in the face” and accused Blanchard of lying about the circumstances.
Blanchard and Urker first met while she was incarcerated and became engaged in 2018. Their relationship went through several breakups before they reconciled in 2024. They later welcomed Aurora in December 2024.
Following Urker’s death, Blanchard said she believed he may have died from an overdose, although she stressed that she did not know whether it was intentional. Authorities have not announced a final cause or manner of death, and the investigation remains ongoing.
Blanchard has described Urker as a devoted father and said she intends to make sure their daughter knows who he was beyond the public scrutiny surrounding their relationship. She has also asked for privacy and compassion for their daughter and both families as they grieve.

Urges political parties to forge consensus on national agenda, calls for constitutional appointments to ECP
Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly and Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party (PkMAP) Chairman Mahmood Khan Achakzai said on Wednesday that meaningful dialogue between the government and opposition could not produce tangible results unless direct consultations were held with Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf founder Imran Khan.
Addressing a public gathering at Baz Muhammad Shaheed Ground in Balochistan's Zhob, Achakzai said all major political leadership must be included in the consultative process to make political dialogue effective and result-oriented.
پښتونخوامیپ کے چیئرمین، اپوزیشن لیڈر محمود خان اچکزئی پشتونخوامیپ کے زیر اہتمام شہداء جمہوریت 7 اکتوبر 1983و شہداء وطن 11 اکتوبر 1991 کے برسی کی مناسبت سے ژوب میں منعقد جلسہ عام سے خطاب کررہے ہے pic.twitter.com/Fqw7kmMHlN
“If one side in negotiations consults its leadership, the opposition must also be allowed to consult Imran Khan,” he said, further adding that he would not participate in formal negotiations until such a meeting was held.
Read : PTI: talks deadlocked over Imran access, K-P policy
میں نے ان پر واضح کیا کہ خدا کے لیے میری بات سنیں، عمران خان سے ملاقات کیے بغیر اور ان کی رائے جانے بغیر، اگر آپ یا آپ کے ساتھی اس مارچ کو منسوخ یا ملتوی کرتے ہیں، تو اس سے آپ کی بھی رسوائی ہوگی اور میرے ساتھیوں کی بھی۔ میں ایسے کسی عمل میں آپ کے ساتھ نہیں ہوں۔ pic.twitter.com/w6XFq6UYKp
The PkMAP chairman urged political parties across the political spectrum to develop a common national agenda to tackle the country’s persistent economic and political challenges, adding that political forces needed to rise above partisan interests and work together to address issues confronting the country.
Speaking about constitutional and administrative matters, Achakzai called for fresh appointments to the Election Commission of Pakistan, including the chief election commissioner, in accordance with constitutional procedures as the incumbent officials’ terms expire.

On regional developments, he welcomed international diplomatic efforts aimed at resolving issues involving Afghanistan, further noting that the international community had a responsibility to contribute to lasting peace, stability and economic development in the region.
پشتونخوامیپ کے زیر اہتمام شہداء جمہوریت 7 اکتوبر 1983و شہداء وطن 11 اکتوبر 1991 کے برسی کی مناسبت سے ژوب میں منعقد جلسہ عام کے مناظر ۔ pic.twitter.com/feOa5eyMzA
Achakzai also called for unity among local communities and urged the peaceful resolution of disputes through traditional jirgas, saying dialogue and collective efforts could help maintain peace and harmony.
PkMAP Central Secretary Nawab Muhammad Ayaz Khan Jogezai and Information Secretary Talimand Khan also addressed the gathering. They highlighted regional development, improved governance and the resolution of local administrative issues.

title: Disney  to stream Super Bowl in 2027 alongside ESPN and ABC
description: The game is scheduled to take place on February 14  2027  at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood  California
content:
The game is scheduled to take place on February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California
Disney+ will stream Super Bowl LXI in 2027, giving subscribers another way to watch the NFL championship game alongside its traditional broadcast on ESPN and ABC.
The game is scheduled to take place on February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. It will mark the first Super Bowl produced and carried by ESPN, with Joe Buck, Troy Aikman, Lisa Salters and Laura Rutledge among the broadcasters involved in the coverage.
In the US, Disney+ subscribers will have access to the same English-language presentation airing on ESPN and ABC, as well as the Spanish-language broadcast from ESPN Deportes. Disney+ will also make the Super Bowl available in more than 55 international markets, including Latin America, Brazil, the Caribbean, South Africa and Australia and New Zealand.
The streaming move expands Disney+’s role in live sports as the company continues to bring more ESPN programming to the service. Ahead of Super Bowl LXI, Disney+ will stream two Monday Night Football games, beginning with the Dallas Cowboys’ game against the Philadelphia Eagles on October 26. A second game will be announced at a later date.
The Super Bowl will also remain available through the ESPN app in the US. ESPN will offer its traditional broadcast, the Spanish-language telecast and the ManningCast featuring Peyton and Eli Manning, alongside additional Super Bowl Sunday programming.
Disney is already preparing for a major Super Bowl presence, with ESPN planning to establish ESPN Beach at Santa Monica Beach ahead of the game. The week-long broadcast hub will begin on February 8 and will include a free fan experience at the Santa Monica Pier.
Super Bowl LXI has also generated record advertising demand. Disney said ABC and ESPN have already sold all commercial inventory for the broadcast, marking the earliest sell-out by a network in Super Bowl history. Fifty-eight brands across 34 categories have secured advertising spots, including nine companies making their Super Bowl debut.
With Disney+ joining ESPN and ABC, Super Bowl LXI will become one of Disney’s biggest live-streaming events yet, further expanding the company’s push to combine its traditional television networks with its streaming platforms.

However, Roach maintained that he considers himself the leading fashion expert on Project Runway , apart from editor-in-chief Nina Garcia. He described Banks primarily as a model when asked whether they were on the same level as fashion experts.
While neither star has explicitly confirmed a personal feud, their Season 22 clash has continued to generate discussion among Project Runway viewers. Banks’ latest comments suggest she is not taking the speculation as seriously as fans have.

title: Ben Affleck opens up about  Animals   Matt Damon and being a    tarnished leading man
description: For  Animals   Affleck reunited professionally with Damon behind the scenes through Artists Equity  their company
content:
For 'Animals', Affleck reunited professionally with Damon behind the scenes through Artists Equity, their company
Ben Affleck has opened up about his new film Animals , his long friendship with Matt Damon and why he has embraced being described as a “tarnished leading man”.
Affleck stars in, directs and co-writes Animals , a crime thriller about a Los Angeles mayoral candidate whose son is kidnapped, forcing him and his wife, played by Kerry Washington, into a desperate attempt to secure the ransom.
The film was originally set to reunite Affleck and Damon on screen, with Damon attached to star alongside Jennifer Garner. However, Damon ultimately left the project to work on Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey , with Affleck later taking on the leading role himself. Damon remains involved as a producer.
Affleck said he understood why Damon chose The Odyssey , describing Nolan’s film as the kind of large-scale production that has become increasingly rare.
“The whole David Lean, pack up 300 people and sail around the world and use all these extras and do everything in camera on film is going away,” Affleck said. He added that working on a Christopher Nolan film of that scale was a “once in a lifetime experience”.
Affleck also revealed that he and Damon had spoken about the possibility of their careers reaching a point where opportunities like The Odyssey could become less frequent.
“All the time,” Affleck said when asked whether they had discussed it. He explained that the changing nature of blockbuster filmmaking had made such productions increasingly unusual.
For Animals , Affleck eventually reunited professionally with Damon behind the scenes through Artists Equity, the production company they founded together. The film also became an opportunity for Affleck to explore themes that had become increasingly important to him, particularly morality, marriage and the choices people make when their carefully constructed lives fall apart.
Affleck said the film asks whether people are genuinely moral or primarily motivated by their own interests. The kidnapping at the centre of the story forces his character and Washington’s character to confront what happens when “the mask comes off”.
The actor also addressed his reputation as a “tarnished leading man”, a description he has previously used when discussing the kinds of characters he finds most interesting.
“I think any good actor’s interested in playing” characters who are not simply two-dimensional or completely virtuous, Affleck said. He explained that characters with flaws and complicated histories offer more opportunities to explore human behaviour.
Affleck said he no longer feels resigned to that description, arguing that the imperfections associated with his public image can make his work more interesting.
“I’m not going to try to pretend that everything I do has always been happy and cheerful and perfect,” he said. “It hasn’t.”
Animals is set to arrive in select cinemas and on Netflix on October 9.

description: Details regarding current force levels  specialised capabilities  potential additional deployments remain classified
content:
Says Makkah pact was not borne out of a 'vacuum'
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said on Wednesday that Pakistani troops were present in Saudi Arabia in "multiple capabilities" amid the kingdom's escalating conflict with Yemen's Houthis and developments related to it.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
In an interview with CNN, the military spokesperson was questioned about whether Pakistani military personnel were present in the kingdom as part of the Makkah Defence Alliance, to which he said: "I do confirm that the forces of Pakistan are already there ... the Pakistani troops have been there for decades in multiple capabilities."
He said the Makkah pact was not borne out of a "vacuum". "There is a sustained diplomatic, political, military and people-to-people relationship between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye," he added.
The DG ISPR reiterated that forces were present in "multiple domains" in the kingdom.

Read : Makkah defence alliance agrees to 'rapid force deployment' in Saudi Arabia: FO
In a major development that may have far-reaching implications for the region, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye activated the practical implementation of their collective defence commitments on Monday.
According to a joint statement issued on Monday night, the activation entailed immediate deployment of "the agreed military forces and capabilities to the kingdom in response to security threats".
The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of the Strategic-Political and Defence Committee of the alliance, held in Riyadh to discuss the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia is currently engaged in an active conflict with Houthis, who have been targeting the various strategic and economic assets in the kingdom.
However, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on Tuesday had rejected what it described as “speculative” reporting by Reuters on the pact, saying operational details concerning the implementation of the collective deterrence mechanism were confidential.
The ministry’s statement followed a Reuters report published on October 2, which said Pakistan had deployed between 30,000 and 40,000 troops to Saudi Arabia to help defend the kingdom’s land borders and assist with drone and missile interceptions, citing a Pakistani official. Reuters reported that Islamabad had not decided to send troops into Yemen in a fighting capacity.

Amanda Seyfried got a hilarious fright from her 9-year-old daughter, Nina, who surprised her while wearing a Scream Ghost Face mask.

title: Michael 2  lands  31m California tax credit as sequel moves forward
description: Lionsgate film chief revealed that around 25  to 30  of the sequel had already been shot during the first movie
content:
Lionsgate film chief revealed that around 25% to 30% of the sequel had already been shot during the first movie
Michael 2 , the planned sequel to the blockbuster Michael Jackson biopic, has been awarded $31 million in California tax credits as the project moves closer to production.
The sequel is among the latest productions receiving support through California’s expanded Film and Television Tax Credit Programme. The state has been increasing incentives for major productions in an effort to bring more film-making activity and jobs back to California.
The first Michael , directed by Antoine Fuqua and starring Jackson’s nephew Jaafar Jackson as the King of Pop, became a major box-office success in 2026. The film follows Jackson’s rise from his time with the Jackson 5 through his emergence as one of the world’s biggest music stars.
The original film ends during Jackson’s 1987 Bad tour with the words “His Story Continues”, setting the stage for a second instalment. Lionsgate has previously confirmed that it is developing the sequel, with the studio hoping to begin filming towards the end of 2026 or in early 2027.
The sequel could explore a later period of Jackson’s career, including material surrounding his Dangerous era and other major events that were not covered in the first film. The original production had initially planned to address allegations of child sexual abuse against Jackson, but those elements were removed following a legal dispute involving a settlement agreement with one of his accusers.
Lionsgate film chief Adam Fogelson previously revealed that around 25% to 30% of a second film had already been shot during production on the first movie, including several major musical sequences. That footage could potentially be incorporated into Michael 2 , helping reduce production costs.
The first Michael was made with a production budget of more than $155 million and became one of 2026’s biggest box-office successes. Lionsgate has said it wants the follow-up to be a major, satisfying film for audiences around the world.
The $31 million California tax credit adds further momentum to the sequel as Lionsgate works towards bringing Michael 2 into production. A release date has not yet been confirmed.

title: Govt trying to avoid    last option    but may consider governor   s rule in K P if no alternative remains  Khawaja Asif
description: Says govt is trying to avoid the    last option    but may consider governor   s rule if no alternative remains
content:
Says the PTI should act like a political party and time has come to make some crucial decisions in K-P
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Wednesday said the government was trying to avoid imposing governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, but warned that it could resort to the option if no other way was left.
Speaking to reporters in Islamabad, the minister said that there was nothing impeding the imposition og governor’s rule in the province, but the government was trying not to use what he described as the “last option”.
“If there is no other way left, then we can use that option,” he said.
Read : Afridi calls Kundi's security meeting ‘attack on Constitution’, warns against 'another East Pakistan' situation
Asif also criticised the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), urging it to “play the role of a political party rather than a terrorist organisation”.
“We cannot leave the capital at their mercy so that every two or three months they join hands with the Taliban and march on the capital,” he said.
The minister described the Taliban as an “anti-Pakistan power” and said that if the PTI allied with it and attacked the capital, the government had the right and responsibility to protect Islamabad.
He referred to the PTI leadership’s alleged failure to attend the funerals of people killed in Taliban attacks and its failure to condemn explosions, claiming that these factors indicated, in his view, that the Taliban had a militant component within the K-P government.
Asif also described the PTI’s planned long march as an “attack on Islamabad”, saying previous attacks on the capital had also been motivated by political parties’ efforts to establish their credibility within their own ranks.
He attributed the failure of talks between the government and opposition to internal differences within the PTI.
“Differences within the PTI have intensified,” he said, adding that members of the PTI sitting in the National Assembly, its negotiating team and even its allies wanted a solution to the issue that was acceptable to the entire country.
Asked about the PTI’s demand for a meeting with Imran Khan before deciding whether to postpone its long march, Asif said he did not know about it.
Also Read : Govt will not accept demands by 'holding state hostage', Sanaullah warns PTI
He instead urged the PTI to look at its record.
“Look at your past. When we were imprisoned, what facilities did you provide us? Did you keep us at the Marriott?” he said.
Asif reiterated that the PTI should act as a political party rather than a terrorist organisation.
Later, in a post on X, Asif accused the K-P government of having “complete collusion” with terrorists and said there were ample examples and evidence of what he called a “facilitator ecosystem”, which, he said, could not be tolerated.
He criticised the provincial government for what he described as “complete detachment” from terrorism in the province and “criminal indifference”.
The minister said the PTI provincial government was focused on its “so-called failed political long march” while its alleged facilitators had unleashed a fresh wave of terrorism against the people of K-P.

He referred to the Oct 6 attack in Dera Ismail Khan, saying five people had been killed, including two customs officials.
“Completely numb to this serious matter, the entire provincial cabinet, including the chief minister, is fully engrossed in their political failed long march,” he said.
Asif accused the provincial government of neither condemning the deaths nor offering condolences to the families of the victims, attending their funerals or visiting their homes.
“This is inexcusable by any standard,” he said.
He further criticised the chief minister for allegedly scheduling a late-night meeting to reprimand the inspector general of police and chief secretary for attending the governor’s security meeting.
According to Asif, the chief minister and his cabinet had “completely abandoned” the people of the province to the mercy of terrorists.
He claimed that people in various parts of K-P were protesting against the provincial government.
“This can no longer be tolerated. Enough blood of K-P’s people has been spilt,” he said, alleging that there was “complete collusion” between the provincial government and terrorists.
Read More : PTI long march enters fourth day, heads to Khyber as party rallies behind K-P CM
The minister also contrasted the PTI government’s treatment of the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz leadership with what he described as the PML-N’s conduct while in opposition.
He said Nawaz Sharif, his family and the PML-N leadership had been imprisoned during the PTI’s tenure, but the PML-N had continued to perform its parliamentary role under the Constitution.
“It did not hold the country and institutions hostage. It fought a legal and constitutional battle in the courts and parliament. It did not ally with the Taliban,” he said.
Asif said the time had come to make “crucial decisions”, adding that K-P could no longer be left “at the mercy of incompetent, insensitive rulers and Taliban allies”.
He also warned against putting the unity of the country at risk, saying an entire province could not be “held hostage”.
The issue of Governor’s Rule has become a major point of contention between the federal and K-P government. On September 21, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the government was consulting the law ministry on legal options for the province, including Governor’s Rule , if the PTI proceeded with its long march. Two days later, however, Information Minister Atta Tarar ruled out any plan to impose Governor’s Rule, saying the federal government had no intention of removing the PTI administration.
Some federal ministers publicly raised the possibility of federal intervention in K-P. Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam said consultations were under way on the "constitutional and legal option" of imposing Governors' Rule.
Afridi, however, rejected the warnings and said he would not retreat from his position because of threats of Governors' Rule or an emergency. He also said PTI supporters could take to the streets at short notice if an attempt was made to remove him.
However, amid the speculation, just days before the PTI’s planned long march, the prime minister and the president formed a committee last week to negotiate with the PTI and other opposition parties over the march, while expressing concern over the province’s deteriorating law and order situation.
The government and opposition parties held negotiations over two days, and the talks initially appeared to be bearing fruit. However, just as the two sides were nearing agreement on most of the contentious issues , a deadlock emerged, bringing the negotiation process to a halt.
The government blamed the K-P government , particularly Afridi, for the deadlock and failure of the negotiations. The PTI, however, claimed that the talks broke down over its demand for a meeting with the party’s founder, which the government refused to accept.
As the negotiation process collapsed, CM Afridi began his long march towards Islamabad, further escalating tensions between the two sides, with both sides continuing to trade allegations .
As tensions peaked, PM Shehbaz once again entered the fray and extended an olive branch to the PTI, saying the government was prepared to engage with the opposition if the party ended its long march and sit-ins.
The PTI, however, rejected the offer as its march continued towards Islamabad, entering its fourth day on Wednesday. The convoy moved from Mattani towards Khyber, with Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi leading the procession.
