title: Megyn Kelly attacks Olivia Rodrigo over Cornell 7 support     Shut up and stick to singing
description: I liked you better when you were in front of a microphone singing your weird little depressing songs     Kelly said
content:
“I liked you better when you were in front of a microphone singing your weird little depressing songs,” Kelly said
Megyn Kelly has launched a furious attack on Olivia Rodrigo after the singer spoke out in support of Jane Doe, the former Cornell University student at the centre of a sexual assault lawsuit involving seven former fraternity members.
Rodrigo addressed the case on social media earlier this week, writing: “Shame on Cornell and on every institution who protects rapists and abusers over women. I stand with Jane Doe.” She added that Doe’s bravery “reverberates across the country” and said she deserves answers, consequences and lasting change.
Kelly responded to Rodrigo during an episode of The Megyn Kelly Show , telling the singer that she did not know what she was talking about and should “shut up and stick to singing”.
“I liked you better when you were in front of a microphone singing your weird little depressing songs,” Kelly said. She went on to describe Rodrigo as a “know-nothing moron” and questioned why the singer was commenting on an issue she believed she did not understand.
Kelly also warned Rodrigo that she could scrutinise the singer’s own music and lyrics if she continued speaking publicly about the case. “Sit down and be quiet,” she said, adding that she would start examining “exactly the kind of messaging” Rodrigo was promoting to young women.
Rodrigo’s comments came after Doe filed a lawsuit against Cornell University and seven former members of the Chi Phi fraternity. Doe alleges that she was drugged and sexually assaulted at a fraternity house in October 2024. The men named in the lawsuit have denied wrongdoing, and none has been criminally charged.
Cornell previously conducted an internal investigation into the allegations, resulting in two men being expelled while others received suspensions or lesser disciplinary penalties. The university has since agreed to an independent review of how it handled Doe’s report.
Rodrigo is among a number of celebrities who have publicly expressed support for Doe, following statements from figures including Florence Pugh, Mariska Hargitay, Hudson Williams and Josh Gad.
Kelly has previously criticised other celebrities who spoke about the Cornell case, including Hargitay, while questioning aspects of the allegations and the response to them. Her latest comments have now placed Rodrigo at the centre of the ongoing debate surrounding the case.

title: Medical student   s body exhumed at Karachi s Kohi Goth Graveyard 15 months after death
description: Family suspects foul play  seeks post mortem  samples sent for chemical examination
content:
Family suspects foul play, seeks post-mortem; samples sent for chemical examination
The body of 23-year-old medical student Sultan Zafar, who died last year after allegedly falling from a moving vehicle at Karachi's Sea View, was exhumed on Wednesday, nearly 15 months after his death, following a request by his family.
A nine-member medical board, comprising seven doctors and two mortuary attendants, exhumed the body at Kohi Goth Graveyard and conducted a post-mortem examination. Samples were collected and sent for chemical examination, while the final post-mortem report will be prepared after the chemical examination results are received.
The exhumation was ordered by a magistrate on an application filed by Sultan’s family.
Read : Court grants three-day remand of two suspects in Karachi DHA assault case
Professor of Radiology Dr Saba Sohail was appointed chairperson of the medical board. The board included Dr Mehreen Fatima of the Department of Forensic Medicine at Dow Medical College, neurosurgeon Dr Imran, Jinnah Hospital Medico-Legal Officer Dr Mumtaz, Police Surgeon’s Office administrative in-charge Dr Yasin, Additional Police Surgeon at Abbasi Shaheed Hospital Dr Kamran Sheikh and Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed. Mortuary attendants Shoaib and Anees were also part of the board.
Zafar had gone to Dau Darya with friends on July 23, 2025, where he sustained serious injuries in what was initially described as an accident. He remained under treatment at a hospital for about a week before succumbing to his injuries.
His mother, Dr Mehr Afroz, later donated his organs. On July 31, both of Zafar’s kidneys were transplanted into two patients undergoing dialysis at the Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation (SIUT), where Dr Mehr works as a doctor.
According to the family, CT scans and X-rays conducted after the incident had revealed fractures in different parts of Sultan’s body, including a nasal bone fracture. The family said it approached police over the injuries but received no cooperation.
Speaking to the media after the exhumation, Sultan’s maternal aunt Mehr Feroz said the family suspected that he had been murdered.
Also Read : Two dead, one injured in Do Darya car crash
She said three girls and four boys were accompanying Sultan when the incident occurred. According to the family, they travelled in two vehicles from Dau Darya towards an under-construction building beyond the area.
Sultan’s friends had allegedly told the family that he got out of the vehicle while it was travelling at around 20 kilometres per hour and sustained injuries. However, Mehr Feroz said the family had found no evidence at the alleged site to support the account of an accident.
Police registered a case under Section 320 of the Pakistan Penal Code at Sahil police station nearly six months after the incident, on the complaint of Sultan’s mother. The family has now sought to establish the circumstances surrounding Sultan’s death through the post-mortem examination and subsequent forensic analysis.

title: New month  new binge  Here s what s landing on Netflix this October
description: Florence Pugh  Ben Affleck  Keri Russell headline a packed month of new releases  returning series and documentaries
content:
Florence Pugh, Ben Affleck, Keri Russell headline a packed month of new releases, returning series and documentaries
Netflix is welcoming October with a packed lineup of new films, original series, returning favourites and documentaries, giving subscribers plenty to watch throughout the month.
The streaming giant's October schedule includes Ben Affleck's Animals , a new adaptation of John Steinbeck's East of Eden, the Victorious spin-off Hollywood Arts , and new seasons of popular shows including Nobody Wants This , Lupin and The Diplomat.
The month will also bring a collection of documentaries focusing on comedians and entertainers, including Martin Mull, Norm Macdonald, Maria Bamford and Matthew Perry.
Here are some of the biggest new titles coming to Netflix in October:
One of Netflix's most ambitious October releases is East of Eden , a seven-episode adaptation of John Steinbeck's celebrated novel.
The period drama follows the complicated lives of two brothers and Cathy Ames, a fiercely independent woman whose arrival has lasting consequences for the family.
Florence Pugh stars as Cathy, with Christopher Abbott and Mike Faist also leading the cast. Created by Zoe Kazan, the series explores family, rivalry, love, ambition and the ways personal choices can shape generations.
Steinbeck's novel, first published in 1952, is considered one of the author's defining works and was itself inspired in part by the biblical story of Cain and Abel.
Crazy Rich, Incredibly Broke — October 1
Netflix's October comedy slate begins with Crazy Rich, Incredibly Broke , which centres on the wealthy AlThahabi family.
The family has built its identity around luxury and social status, but its comfortable existence begins to unravel when it discovers that its financial situation is far worse than expected.
Rather than immediately acknowledge their problems, the family attempts to keep up appearances, creating a series of comic situations as they try to protect their reputation.
Netflix's documentary lineup includes Who Is Martin Mull? , a look at the life and career of the late actor, comedian, musician and artist.
Mull built a career that crossed several creative fields, appearing in television and film while also pursuing music and visual art. The documentary explores his unconventional career and features contributions from people who knew and worked with him.
One of October's biggest film releases is Animals, starring Ben Affleck and Kerry Washington.
Affleck plays Mark Kimball, a Los Angeles mayoral candidate whose family is thrown into turmoil when his son is kidnapped. His wife, Abigail, played by Washington, joins him as they attempt to secure their son's release.
The situation forces the couple to make increasingly difficult decisions while confronting secrets within their own lives.
Affleck also directed and co-wrote the thriller. The cast includes Gillian Anderson, Steven Yeun, Adriana Paz and Luis Gerardo Méndez.
The film arrives on Netflix on October 9, giving subscribers one of the month's most prominent new movie releases.
Fans of Nickelodeon's Victorious will recognise a familiar face in Hollywood Arts.
Daniella Monet returns as Trina Vega in the new sitcom, which revisits the performing-arts school from the original series but introduces a new generation of students. Trina is no longer a student herself. After failing to achieve the acting career she had hoped for, she finds herself back at Hollywood Arts as a substitute teacher.
The series also brings back Yvette Nicole Brown as Principal Helen while introducing several new young performers.
Keri Russell returns as diplomat Kate Wyler for the fourth season of Netflix's political thriller The Diplomat .
Kate continues dealing with the fallout from the political and personal upheaval of previous seasons as tensions between the United States and Britain become increasingly complicated.
Her relationship with husband Hal, played by Rufus Sewell, remains another major part of the story as Kate faces new political challenges and threats.
Norm: The Tale of Norm Macdonald — October 16
Comedian Norm Macdonald is the subject of another major Netflix documentary arriving this month.
Norm: The Tale of Norm Macdonald looks at the comedian's career, from his rise in stand-up to his celebrated run on Saturday Night Live and his later work in television and film.
Directed by Judd Apatow, the documentary draws on archival material and personal footage to examine Macdonald's distinctive approach to comedy and his influence on other performers.
Kristen Bell and Adam Brody return as Joanne and Noah in the third season of Nobody Wants This.
After the twists and complications of their relationship in the earlier seasons, the new episodes move the couple into another stage of their romance.
Season 3 explores what happens when Joanne and Noah attempt to build a life together rather than simply trying to figure out whether they should be together.
French crime series Lupin returns with Omar Sy once again playing master thief Assane Diop.
Part 4 takes place four years after the events of the previous chapter. Assane remains in prison and appears ready to accept his situation, but circumstances soon threaten to pull him back into the world of crime and deception.
The series, inspired by the fictional gentleman thief Arsène Lupin, has become one of Netflix's most successful French-language productions since its debut in 2021.
Paralyzed by Hope: The Maria Bamford Story — October 23
Comedian Maria Bamford becomes the focus of Paralyzed by Hope: The Maria Bamford Story .
The documentary explores Bamford's career, family life and experiences with mental health while examining the personal experiences that have influenced her comedy.
The One About Matthew Perry — October 27
Netflix will also look back at the life of Matthew Perry in the three-part documentary series The One About Matthew Perry .
Perry became an international star through his role as Chandler Bing on Friends , but his life away from the sitcom was marked by struggles with addiction and efforts to maintain his career while dealing with his personal challenges.
The documentary draws on interviews, photographs and footage from Perry's life and explores both his fame and the difficulties he faced away from the screen.
While the focus of Netflix's October schedule is on new releases, the platform is also bringing back several older titles that fit the Halloween season.
The Twilight films will return for viewers looking for supernatural romance, while Alfred Hitchcock's classic Psycho offers a more traditional psychological thriller.
The original Friday the 13th will also be available for horror fans, alongside A Haunted House and its sequel for viewers who prefer their Halloween scares mixed with comedy.
Netflix's October lineup offers a mix of major new productions, returning series and documentaries, giving viewers plenty of options throughout the month. From the literary drama of East of Eden and the suspense of Animals to new chapters of The Diplomat , Nobody Wants This and Lupin , the schedule covers a wide range of genres.
Whether audiences are tuning in for a new drama, a returning favourite or a classic Halloween rewatch, October offers a packed selection of titles to explore.

title: Glen Powell avoids politics because he    does not like the discourse    after  The Running Man  flop
description: Over time  I realised that politics divide people     Powell said and added that  its the worst form of conversation
content:
“Over time, I realised that politics divide people,” Powell said and added that "its the worst form of conversation"
Glen Powell has opened up about why he avoids discussing politics publicly, saying he does not like the divisive nature of political discourse and believes his focus should remain elsewhere.
The actor discussed his approach to politics in a new profile, explaining that although he grew up in a family with political connections, current affairs were rarely discussed around the dinner table. His mother, Cyndy Powell, worked in the Reagan administration at the US Treasury Department, but Powell said politics interests him even less now.
“Over time, I realised that politics divide people,” Powell said. “People trying to prove their point—for me, it’s the worst version of a conversation. I genuinely do not like the discourse. It’s not as healthy as it once was.”
Powell said he does not currently see himself engaging in political discussions, although he respects people who choose to speak out about issues they believe in.
“Engaging, then, for him is ‘not presently possible,’” he said. “I applaud people for jumping into those things and fighting for what they believe in. If I were a political person, I would be talking about it. For me, my calling is elsewhere.”
His comments come as Powell reflects on a particularly difficult period in his career, including the demanding production of The Running Man and the film’s disappointing box-office performance.
Powell revealed that he suffered a serious hand injury while filming the Edgar Wright-directed action film after a stunt involving a retractable prop knife went wrong. He ruptured a tendon and later discovered he had developed a septic infection, requiring emergency surgery. Despite doctors warning him about the seriousness of the injury, Powell returned to filming almost immediately.
The actor also addressed the weak ticket sales for The Running Man , pointing to upheaval at Paramount during its merger as one factor behind the film's underwhelming theatrical run. Powell said the studio had laid off its entire marketing department about a month before the film's release.
The film ultimately underperformed despite high expectations, while Powell's next film, the A24 thriller How to Make a Killing , also received limited attention. Looking back, he said the experience taught him that there was no need to rush projects.
The setbacks prompted Powell to reconsider his relentless work schedule and the pressure he had placed on himself. He said he had begun asking whether he should “keep sprinting” and admitted that he had started to feel nihilistic during the period.
Powell has since continued building an increasingly busy slate. He is set to star in Judd Apatow’s The Comeback King and J.J. Abrams’ The Great Beyond , while also continuing his work on Chad Powers .
Despite the setbacks, Powell remains committed to filmmaking and said he believes in the projects he is making. His comments suggest that, rather than entering political debates, he would prefer to put his energy into the work itself and his growing career behind and in front of the camera.

'RHOSLC' star Whitney Rose files for divorce from Justin Rose months after their separation was confirmed in July
Real Housewives of Salt Lake City star Whitney Rose has filed for divorce from her husband, Justin Rose, after 16 years of marriage.
Whitney submitted the divorce filing in the Third District Court of Salt Lake City on October 6, according to records obtained by E! News . The filing includes a proposed parenting plan, while the petition itself has been sealed.
The divorce filing comes around three months after Whitney and Justin’s separation was confirmed in July. The couple share two children, Bobbie, 16, and Brooks, 13.
Their relationship has been featured throughout the first six seasons of RHOSLC , with the couple documenting various challenges in their marriage on the Bravo reality series.
The seventh season has also addressed the strain in their relationship. In the Season 7 trailer, Whitney questioned whether they could continue their marriage.
“I don’t know if you and I can move forward in our marriage,” Whitney told Justin in the trailer, “or it’s over.”
Whitney and Justin had previously marked their 16th wedding anniversary in November 2025. At the time, Whitney reflected on their relationship and described wax as a symbol of the flexibility and warmth needed for a couple to build a life together.
“The wax represents the flexibility and the warmth that a couple needs to mold their lives together over time,” she wrote in an Instagram post.
Justin also reflected on their relationship in a 2022 post, describing the year as one that had “thrown us some curveballs” while celebrating another year with Whitney by his side.
The latest divorce filing now marks a new chapter for the couple following their reported separation earlier this year.

'Diary of a Wimpy Kid Christmas: The Getaway' premieres on Disney+ on December 4
Diary of a Wimpy Kid is returning with a new animated Christmas movie, Diary of a Wimpy Kid Christmas: The Getaway , which is set to premiere on Disney+ on December 4.
The upcoming film is the fifth animated instalment in the popular franchise and adapts Jeff Kinney’s 12th book, The Getaway , which was originally released in November 2017.
The story follows middle schooler Greg Heffley as his family makes a last-minute decision to escape the holiday stress with a trip to an all-inclusive island resort. However, what is supposed to be a relaxing getaway quickly turns into another series of disasters for Greg and his family.
The Heffleys soon discover that their tropical paradise is not quite what they expected, with their holiday plans descending into the kind of chaotic situations that have become a trademark of the franchise.
Kinney wrote and produced the animated film, while Matt Danner returns as director after previously helming Diary of a Wimpy Kid: The Last Straw .
Alongside the film, fans will also get a new movie tie-in cover for the book. The release comes as the Diary of a Wimpy Kid franchise continues to expand its animated adaptations on Disney+.
The new film is not the only upcoming Wimpy Kid release from Kinney. His latest novel, Fight or Flight , is scheduled to hit shelves on October 20 and will become the 21st book in the bestselling series.
In Fight or Flight , Greg finds himself in trouble after a binder containing his notes about the school bullies falls into someone else’s hands. He must then race to recover it before the information exposes him as the person behind the scandal.
Kinney is also scheduled to embark on a US book tour from October 18 through October 30 to promote the new novel.

title: Russell hit with Singapore grid penalty
description: The Mercedes driver faces a major setback in his title bid after exceeding his season power unit allocation
content:
The Mercedes driver faces a major setback in his title bid after exceeding his season power-unit allocation
George Russell's hopes of winning the 2026 world championship hit another road bump on Wednesday when it was announced that because of an engine penalty he would have to start from the back of the grid in this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix.
The Englishman had to retire in the closing laps while running third in the Bahrain GP in Malaysia last weekend, allowing his Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli, who came second, to open up a gap of 84 points at the top of the standings.
Russell will exceed the season allocation of power unit components and be penalised at least 10 places although Mercedes acknowledged that because of the number of parts he needs replacing, he will start Sunday's race from the back of the grid.
"Malaysia was obviously a very difficult weekend for us," said team principal Toto Wolff who at least had the comfort of Antonelli's podium behind race winner Max Verstappen.
"We have spent the days since then working hard to understand why our performance was not where it should have been.
"George has the added challenge of a power unit penalty, which will mean starting from the back of the grid on Sunday, following the engine failure in Malaysia.
"That is particularly frustrating given the way he drove last weekend and the result he deserved to be fighting for. Unfortunately, these things are part of the sport."
Russell, 28, saw himself as one of the main contenders for the world title as early as winter testing in February, but he was quickly beaten on merit – and with a dose of bad luck – by Antonelli.
The Englishman has at times admitted he has lost the championship and at other times said he has regained "confidence", notably after his victory on the Baku street circuit two weeks ago.
In Malaysia, he quipped after his retirement: "Better to laugh about it."
Sunday's Singapore GP, which will be held on a street circuit at night, is preceded on Saturday by the last sprint race of the season, in which Russell will not be penalised.
One crumb of comfort for Russell might be that when Antonelli had to start from the back for a similar reason in Monza, he worked his way through the field to win the Italian Grand Prix.

title: Shakira breaks silence as Gerard Piqu   dispute reaches court again
description: The former couple personally attended proceedings in Barcelona on October 6
content:
The former couple personally attended proceedings in Barcelona on October 6
Shakira and Gerard Piqué have returned to court four years after reaching a custody agreement following their 2022 separation, with the latest proceedings focused on arrangements involving their sons, Milan and Sasha.
Both Shakira and Piqué attended the proceedings at the Ciutat de la Justícia in Barcelona on October 6, according to HELLO! . The former couple appeared in person as the court considered a request concerning how their children travel between Miami and Barcelona.
Representatives for Shakira said the proposed changes would ask Piqué to travel to Miami during shorter holiday periods rather than requiring the boys to make transatlantic journeys for every visit. The singer’s representatives said the aim is to reduce travel and jet lag while allowing the children to maintain their school, social and family routines for longer.
The documents reportedly state that Shakira is not seeking to reduce the amount of time Milan and Sasha spend with their father. Instead, the proposal would change how travel responsibilities are handled between the former couple.
Shakira and Piqué began their relationship in 2010 after meeting during the FIFA World Cup in South Africa. They welcomed Milan in 2013 and Sasha in 2015 before announcing their separation in June 2022.
Months later, they reached a custody agreement that allowed Shakira to relocate with their sons to Miami, while Piqué remained based in Barcelona. The arrangement subsequently became the subject of further attention as the former couple managed their parenting responsibilities across two countries.
The latest proceedings come during a significant year for Shakira professionally. The singer has continued her Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour and recently extended her Madrid residency with a final performance scheduled for October 12.
The Barcelona hearing marks another legal development between the former partners, although the current request concerns travel arrangements rather than a reduction in Piqué’s time with their children. Shakira’s representatives have stressed that the proposed changes are intended to support Milan and Sasha’s wellbeing and daily routines.

title: Arteta signs new deal until 2030
description: The Spaniard extends his Emirates tenure after restoring the Gunners to the top of English football
content:
The Spaniard extends his Emirates tenure after restoring the Gunners to the top of English football
Mikel Arteta vowed "this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together" after signing a new contract with Premier League champions Arsenal until 2030.
The Spaniard's deal had been due to expire at the end of the 2026/27 season but if he sees out his new contract he will have been at the Emirates for more than a decade.
The club said in a statement on Wednesday that the new agreement, which was widely expected, "reflects our shared belief that the progress we've made and last season's success is the beginning of a special period in our history".
Arteta has reportedly been given a substantial pay rise after leading Arsenal to their first Premier League title for 22 years following three successive runners-up finishes.
"It's a privilege to commit my future to the club and to continue to work with exceptional people who want the best for Arsenal," said the 44-year-old.
"This club is unique, its character and the way it makes you feel, and I have a great sense of privilege that our journey together will continue.
"We have already built a special bond and created memories that will last a lifetime, and what is so exciting is that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together."
Arteta, who replaced Unai Emery in December 2019, is now the longest-serving manager in the Premier League following Pep Guardiola's departure from Manchester City.
The former Arsenal captain came under significant pressure early in his managerial reign at the Emirates but has overseen the club's return to the top of English football.
Arteta also led the Gunners to their first Champions League final in two decades last season but they lost to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties.
He has been in charge for 361 matches in all competitions, with his win percentage of just over 62 percent the best of any full-time manager in the club's history.
Arsenal are currently second in the Premier League, three points behind leaders City after a surprise 3-0 defeat to Brighton before the international break.
Club co-chairs Stan and Josh Kroenke said: "It has been an incredible journey so far and we are excited for what lies ahead in this special relationship.
"Last season was an incredible moment in Arsenal's history, a moment in which we created memories that will last a lifetime. We're determined to create many more in the years ahead.
"We share a special bond with Mikel. We are so proud of everything we have achieved since he returned to the club in 2019."
Arsenal return to Premier League action with a home match against Leeds on Saturday.

title: Pedro retires from football
description: He departs with 99 goals in 321 appearances for Barcelona and major honours across Europe
content:
He departs with 99 goals in 321 appearances for Barcelona and major honours across Europe
Spanish World Cup winner and former Barcelona winger Pedro Rodriguez retired from football on Wednesday at the age of 39.
The forward won the 2010 World Cup with Spain as well as three Champions League titles with Barca, two of those in 2009 and 2011 as part of Pep Guardiola's team which dominated that era of the sport.
Pedro also won five La Liga titles with the Catalan giants, was a Premier League winner at Chelsea, before heading to Roma and finally Lazio.
"I feel that the moment has come. The moment to take a step forward and begin a new stage in my life," said Pedro in a post on social media.
"I leave proud of having lived my dream and of all the people who were by my side to make it come true."
Born in Tenerife, Pedro joined Barcelona's youth academy as a teenager and made his first-team debut in 2008.
Under Guardiola, he became a key figure in the side that won an unprecedented six trophies in 2009.
Pedro netted in the 2011 Champions League final win over Manchester United and scored 99 goals for Barcelona in 321 games, playing with Lionel Messi, Andres Iniesta and Xavi Hernandez among other stars.
"Being part of the best Barca side in history was a privilege, we won everything and amazed the world," said Pedro in his farewell video.
As well as lifting Spain's first World Cup trophy Pedro also won the 2012 European Championship with La Roja.
"One day, almost without believing it, I became a world champion and a starter in a World Cup final," said Pedro, who earned 65 caps and scored 17 goals for his country.
Arriving in 2015 at Chelsea, he won the Premier League in 2017, as well as the FA Cup and Europa League in the subsequent two seasons.
Pedro's final club was Lazio, whom he left at the end of last season after more than 200 appearances for the Serie A side.

title: Noel Gallagher and Susan Sarandon back Drumcree residents in signed letter
description: Noel Gallagher and Susan Sarandon join 48 public figures backing Garvaghy Road residents amid the Drumcree standoff
content:
Noel Gallagher and Susan Sarandon join 48 public figures backing Garvaghy Road residents amid the Drumcree standoff
Oasis guitarist Noel Gallagher, Oscar-winning actress Susan Sarandon and Line of Duty star Adrian Dunbar are among 48 public figures who have signed a letter supporting residents involved in the ongoing Drumcree dispute in Northern Ireland.
The letter is addressed to Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant and calls for an “independent international mediator” to help find a lasting solution to the stand-off between residents of Garvaghy Road and the Orange Order in Portadown, County Armagh.
The signatories said the protection and rights of the local community should be central to any resolution. They also called for residents to be protected from processions that take place without their consent and could cause intimidation.
Other prominent names backing the letter include musician Paul Weller, Derry Girls actor Siobhán McSweeney, The Smiths guitarist Johnny Marr, filmmaker Ken Loach, writer Irvine Welsh, Madness frontman Suggs, Kneecap, Imelda May and actor Maxine Peake.
Kevin Rowland, frontman of Dexys Midnight Runners and one of the signatories, said the letter was inspired by the situation on Garvaghy Road and the residents’ response to it.
The dispute has led to 11 days of deadlock after a decision allowed an Orange Order parade along the predominantly nationalist road on September 27. Residents have maintained a presence on the road, while members of the Orange Order have repeatedly attempted to march along the route.
The Orange Order has said its members have a legal right to complete the parade and called on police to implement the relevant determination. It has also said it remains open to dialogue.
The Drumcree dispute dates back to the 1990s and was one of Northern Ireland’s most serious parading conflicts.

title: Australia prepare for first South Africa Test
description: This is the first Test on African soil between both sides since the    Sandpapergate    scandal
content:
This is the first Test on African soil between both sides since the ‘Sandpapergate’ scandal
Australia play their first Test in South Africa since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal when they start a three-match series in Durban on Friday, with the visitors unlikely to face more than a few heckles over the incident that rocked the sport eight years ago.
The tourists’ efforts to roughen up the ball using sandpaper, and aid reverse swing, in Cape Town in March 2018 were caught on camera and led to a major reckoning for the game in Australia, with captain ⁠Steve Smith among those banned for their role in the subterfuge.
South Africa have played Tests in Australia since ‘Sandpapergate’, and Australia have toured South Africa in the interim for limited-overs internationals.
The scandal has attracted little media focus in South Africa over recent weeks in comparison to the attention devoted to the incident in the Australian press.
After dethroning Australia last year in a thrilling World Test Championship final at Lord’s to win a first major title, South Africa are focused on improving their chances of a return to the final at the end of the 2025–27 WTC cycle.
Australia are also in need of a boost after a surprise ⁠home Test defeat by Bangladesh in August and with an Ashes tour to England starting next June.
The pitch at Kingsmead often proves a fickle track but should offer the spinners a chance to play a leading role in a change from South Africa’s usually seamer-friendly surfaces.
It is unusual for South Africa’s chances to be largely entrusted to their ⁠spin attack, but Simon Harmer and Keshav Maharaj wreaked havoc in India last November when they triumphed in their last two Test outings.
Spin was also a key factor for the home side as they beat Australia in the recent ⁠One-Day International series.
South Africa may therefore opt to rest frontline attack bowler Kagiso Rabada from the Test as he continues his comeback from a hamstring injury.
Injury to Australia all-rounder Cameron Green opens up a chance ⁠at number five for Cooper Connolly, or a fairytale return for 34-year-old Nic Maddinson after recovering from cancer.
South Africa’s also has a choice to make over their number three batsman, with coach Shukri Conrad having several options including a potential first cap for 30-year-old Marques Ackerman.

title: Hasan finds confidence through basics
description: Pakistan   s dashing batsman says domestic and local cricket help revive his form
content:
Pakistan’s dashing batsman says domestic and local cricket help revive his form
Pakistan middle-order batsman Hasan Nawaz said on Wednesday that being dropped from the national side forced him to return to basics and helped rebuild his confidence after a difficult spell of form.
The dashing batsman returned to domestic after losing his place in the national team, playing on different grounds across Punjab as he worked on a plan laid out by head coach Mike Hesson and the coaching staff.
Nawaz was subsequently recalled and made his comeback against India, the same opposition against whom he had struggled before being dropped.
Although Pakistan eventually lost the match, Nawaz believes his performance against the world’s top-ranked side has given him renewed confidence.
“When I was dropped from the team, Mike and other coaches gave me a plan, which I worked on,” Nawaz told reporters at the Pindi Cricket Stadium.
“I returned to basics and played with local cricketers on different grounds across Punjab.”
For Hasan, the experience was more than simply a way of regaining form. He believes playing on local pitches against unfamiliar bowlers can provide valuable preparation for international cricket.
“As far as local grounds are concerned, there you get tough pitches and play different bowlers,” he said.
“I think we all should play cricket there, and when you get a good pitch, it becomes easy to perform.”
Hasan’s return against India carried added significance because of how his previous spell had ended.
“I think I was dropped while underperforming against India, and I made a comeback against the same opposition,” he said.
Pakistan were unable to turn Hasan’s return into victory, suffering a narrow defeat after failing to make the most of key moments in the final against India in the Asian Games.
“We couldn’t win the match, which was a sad feeling,” Hasan said.
“It was a close game, we lost it by making some silly mistakes,” Hasan was quick to add.
Despite the disappointment, Hasan believes facing India can provide an important confidence boost, particularly given their current standing in international cricket.
“There is no hiding that they (India ) are the number one team in the world currently, and performing against them gives me a lot of confidence,” he said.
He said he also travelled to Japan after the CPL with a clear motivation to contribute to Pakistan, but admitted the side ultimately allowed the match against India to slip away.
“When I was on my way to Japan after playing the Caribbean Premier League (CPL) I had the motivation to do something for the country,” Hasan said.
India had downed Pakistan in the 20th Asian Games final by 19 runs.
Pakistan were reduced to 192-6 while chasing a stiff target of 212 in Nisshin and had to content with a silver medal.

title: Andrew Garfield   s    Artificial    wins praise from critics ahead of December release
description: Neon acquired worldwide distribution after Amazon MGM Studios dropped film in June
content:
Neon acquired worldwide distribution after Amazon MGM Studios dropped film in June
Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial is receiving strong early reviews following its world premiere at the NEW YORK FILM FESTIVAL, with critics praising the drama about OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and the development of artificial intelligence.
Andrew Garfield stars as Altman in the PG 13 film, which begins in 2003 and traces the origins and development of AI before moving into Altman’s story. The cast also includes Yuri Borisov as OpenAI co founder Ilya Sutskever, Mark Rylance as AI pioneer Geoffrey Hinton, Ike Barinholtz as Elon Musk and Monica Barbaro as Mira Murati.
As of Tuesday, Artificial had earned a 91% critics score on Rotten Tomatoes from reviews counted by the site. The response has been largely positive, although one critic has given the film a negative rating.
Owen Gleiberman of Variety described the film as a brilliant but playful docudrama and praised its exploration of AI, while Zachary Lee of The Wrap called its approach thrilling, creative and provocative. The Daily Beast critic Nick Schager described the film as engrossing, while Deadline critic Pete Hammond highlighted its dark comedy and increasingly frightening tone.
David Rooney of The Hollywood Reporter also praised Guadagnino’s direction, describing the film as one of the filmmaker’s strongest works. Tim Grierson of Screen International offered the only negative review, arguing that Simon Rich’s screenplay does not provide enough insight into the people who developed the technology.
Artificial faced a major change before reaching cinemas. Amazon MGM Studios dropped the project on June 19, saying the film would be better served by another distributor. Neon acquired worldwide distribution rights 11 days later.
Guadagnino directs from Rich’s screenplay, with the film scheduled to open in cinemas on December 25. Its critical reception has drawn attention ahead of its theatrical release, particularly because of its focus on AI and the people behind its development.

title: Lorde calls out Robert Kraft with Free Palestine jacket after Macklemore tour dispute
description: The singer wore hand decorated jacket during Austin City Limits set and tagged a Kraft fan page online
content:
The singer wore hand decorated jacket during Austin City Limits set and tagged a Kraft fan page online
Lorde has appeared to take aim at billionaire Robert Kraft amid the ongoing controversy involving Ed Sheeran and Macklemore, wearing a jacket bearing a prominent "Free Palestine" message during her Austin City Limits performance.
The singer shared a photo of the hand decorated jacket on her Instagram Story on October 5, two days after her Austin City Limits set. The garment featured several handwritten messages, with "FREE PALESTINE!!!!!!" displayed prominently along the bottom.
Lorde also added "@mr.robertkraft" over the image. According to Billboard , the tag appeared to direct users to a fan page for Kraft rather than a verified account belonging to the billionaire.
The post came after Kraft became involved in a dispute surrounding Macklemore's brief stint as an opening act on Sheeran's Loop Tour. Macklemore performed songs featuring pro Palestinian messages during his first two shows on the tour in September, including references to the violence in Gaza.
Kraft, whose Kraft Group owns Gillette Stadium, subsequently pushed for Sheeran to remove Macklemore from the tour. The American rapper's contract with the tour was later terminated by US promoter Messina Touring Group.
Macklemore subsequently donated the $1m he had earned from the short lived tour appearance to Palestinian aid. Sheeran's remaining opening acts, Finneas, Aaron Rowe and Lukas Graham, also left the tour.
Kraft later announced plans to contribute money to humanitarian organisations working in Gaza. He said advocacy for Palestinians should not come at the expense of the Jewish community.
Macklemore is now planning a Free Palestine Tour, with performances expected in Dublin, London and Paris. Proceeds are set to support Palestinian aid.
Lorde has previously expressed support for Palestinians. During her Ultrasound World Tour performance at Madison Square Garden in 2025, she led the crowd in a pro Palestinian chant while performing "Team".
Her latest jacket has therefore placed her among artists publicly responding to the dispute surrounding Macklemore, Sheeran and Kraft.

title: Saoirse Ronan reacts to husband Jack Lowden s speculation for James Bond role
description: Gary Oldman previously said Lowden was reportedly among six actors considered for 007
content:
Gary Oldman previously said Lowden was reportedly among six actors considered for 007
Saoirse Ronan has addressed speculation that her husband, Jack Lowden, could become the next James Bond after Gary Oldman suggested the actor was on a shortlist for the coveted role.
Speaking to the Associated Press on Sunday, Ronan acknowledged Oldman’s comments but stopped short of confirming whether Lowden had been selected to replace Daniel Craig as 007.
"Gary thinks he’s James Bond," Ronan said when asked about the rumours. She then indicated that the speculation has little impact on their daily life, saying she and Lowden are focused on ordinary responsibilities at home.
"We’re kind of getting on with our life, to be honest. We have plenty of other things to be dealing with," Ronan said, adding that walking their dog and making dinner are currently bigger priorities in their household.
Lowden, who stars alongside Oldman in Slow Horses , has been linked to the Bond role for several months. Oldman first fuelled the speculation in September when he told Canada’s The Morning Show that Lowden was rumoured to be on the shortlist and suggested that a decision had already been made.
Oldman later clarified his remarks during a panel at the TORONTO INTERNATIONAL FILM FESTIVAL. He said he had heard that the next Bond had been chosen but did not know which actor had secured the part. He also said he was hoping the role would go to Lowden.
Amazon MGM has not announced its choice for the next Bond. Denis Villeneuve is attached to direct the upcoming film, while Steven Knight is writing the screenplay. Amazon MGM gained full creative control of the Bond character and intellectual property in February 2025.
Lowden is among several actors who have been linked to the role, including Callum Turner, Jacob Elordi, Tom Holland, Aaron Taylor-Johnson and Harris Dickinson.
Ronan’s comments leave the casting speculation unresolved, with no official confirmation from Amazon MGM about who will succeed Craig as James Bond.

title: Emmys leave broadcast television for Prime Video after 31 years of rotating networks
description: The ceremony will remain free to viewers in the US and over 240 countries and territories
content:
The ceremony will remain free to viewers in the US and over 240 countries and territories
The Primetime Emmys are moving from broadcast television to Prime Video under a new six year global agreement beginning in 2027, marking the first time the ceremony will be carried exclusively by a streaming platform.
According to Variety , Prime Video is expected to pay around $15m annually for worldwide rights, although the Television Academy and Amazon have not publicly confirmed the financial terms. The previous rotating arrangement involving ABC, NBC, CBS and Fox paid an estimated $8m to $10m annually for US rights.
The new agreement will end the rotating network arrangement after 31 years. The Emmys have been televised since 1949, with the ceremony moving between the major US broadcast networks under the most recent system.
The 2027 Primetime Emmys will be available free on Prime Video in the US and across more than 240 countries and territories, meaning viewers will not need a paid Prime subscription to access the ceremony.
Television Academy chair Cris Abrego said the organisation wanted greater continuity and investment from a single broadcast partner. Prime Video head Mike Hopkins said the six year term would give both sides time to develop the ceremony and build its audience.
The agreement could also expand to other Emmy events. The Television Academy’s two nights focused on craft and technical categories could potentially become part of the Prime Video relationship, although additional arrangements would be required.
Another major change could follow in 2027, with Abrego saying the Television Academy’s proposed merger with the National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences could happen by the middle of the year. Awards including the Daytime Emmys could eventually be considered for inclusion in the wider Prime Video partnership, although no deal has been reached.
The move follows increasing changes in awards broadcasting. Prime Video already carries the Academy of Country Music Awards, while the SAG Awards moved to Netflix. The Oscars are also scheduled to stream on YouTube beginning in 2029.
For the Emmys, the immediate challenge will be moving an established audience from traditional television to streaming while maintaining the ceremony’s profile. Prime Video plans to promote the event across its service and through wider marketing campaigns ahead of the 2027 ceremony.

title: Skeet Ulrich says Melissa Barrera   s firing ended his planned Scream arc
description: They had their chance at it and didn   t quite get to complete the three film arc   the actor said
content:
"They had their chance at it and didn’t quite get to complete the three-film arc," the actor said
Skeet Ulrich has revealed that he will not complete his planned three-film story arc in the Scream franchise following Melissa Barrera’s firing, saying there is no future for his character Billy Loomis without her.
Ulrich, who played Billy Loomis in the original 1996 Scream , returned to the franchise in Scream 5 and Scream VI . Although Billy was killed in the original film, the character appeared through hallucination sequences involving his daughter, Sam Carpenter, played by Barrera.
“Without Melissa Barrera and Sam Loomis, there’s no Billy Loomis,” Ulrich told Us Weekly . “He was in her head. They had their chance at it and didn’t quite get to complete the three-film arc that they talked to me about.”
Barrera was fired by Scream producer Spyglass Media Group in 2023 after she posted comments about the Israel-Hamas war and expressed support for Palestine. Spyglass said at the time that it had “zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate in any form”. Barrera denied antisemitism and continued to defend her right to speak about issues she cared about.
Her departure led to major changes to Scream 7 . Jenna Ortega subsequently left the project, while director Christopher Landon also departed. The story was reworked around Neve Campbell’s Sidney Prescott and her daughter as they faced a new Ghostface threat.
Ulrich’s comments come shortly after fellow original Scream star Matthew Lillard spoke about his decision to return as Stu Macher for Scream 7 . Lillard said he felt ashamed that he did not consider Barrera’s situation when he agreed to return and described himself as being on the “wrong side of history”.
Barrera has also addressed the possibility of returning to the franchise, saying she loves Scream and enjoyed making the films but would not work with Spyglass again. She said she could potentially consider returning if the franchise were ever moved away from the company and placed in hands she felt better honoured the legacy of director Wes Craven.
Despite the cast upheaval, Scream 7 became the highest-grossing film in the franchise. A ninth instalment, Scream 8 , is now in development with writers Nora and Lilla Zuckerman.

title: Jessica Chastain breaks silence on    The Savant    delay as Apple sets 2027 premiere
description: Apple has scheduled    The Savant    for spring 2027 after postponing its original September 2025 premiere
content:
Apple has scheduled ‘The Savant’ for spring 2027 after postponing its original September 2025 premiere
Jessica Chastain is standing by her decision to publicly criticise Apple for postponing The Savant following the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk in 2025.
In an interview with Porter published Monday, the Oscar winning actor said she felt responsible to the people involved in the series and to the real person who inspired her character. Chastain said she believed she had to speak publicly because she considered the postponement a mistake.
"I really had to go on record that I thought it was a mistake," Chastain said. She added that the experience taught her that it was acceptable to be honest while remaining respectful and grateful for her career.
Chastain also rejected the idea that women should feel obligated to remain silent because they are fortunate to have work. She said people can express gratitude while also being honest about decisions they disagree with.
The Savant stars Chastain as Jodi Goodwin, a veteran, wife and mother who works undercover in online communities where white supremacists gather and sometimes discuss domestic terror attacks. Chastain also serves as an executive producer on the series.
Creator Melissa James Gibson adapted the thriller from journalist Andrea Stanley’s 2019 Cosmopolitan article, "Is It Possible to Stop a Mass Shooting Before It Happens?"
Apple had originally scheduled the series to premiere on September 23, 2025. The company removed it from its schedule days before its planned debut after Kirk was assassinated, later saying it had decided to postpone the series following careful consideration.
Apple confirmed last month that The Savant will finally premiere in spring 2027. The new launch will come about a year and a half after the original date and is scheduled for after the November 2026 midterm elections.
Chastain’s comments keep attention on the long delayed series and the decision surrounding its release, while Apple has not indicated that the postponement was linked to any criticism from the actor.

title: Jeremy Allen White discusses social media   s  frightening  influence ahead of  The Social Reckoning
description: Jeremy Allen White discusses his concerns about social media and Facebook   s influence in  The Social Reckoning
content:
Jeremy Allen White discusses his concerns about social media and Facebook’s influence in 'The Social Reckoning'
Jeremy Allen White has discussed his concerns about social media and the growing influence of technology companies in The Social Reckoning , Aaron Sorkin’s drama about the investigation into Facebook’s practices.
White stars as former Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz, who spearheaded the investigation that led to the 2021 Facebook Files, alongside Mikey Madison as whistleblower Frances Haugen.
The film also stars Jeremy Strong as Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg.
"I've got a lot of fears about, like, what these companies want ultimately," White said in an interview with AFP.
"They want all of our time. They want all our attention. They want all of our engagement. They want the way we communicate to be with their tools," he continued.
White said he considers the continued expansion of social media companies to be concerning.
"The American TV and film star said it's "a frightening concept that we don't know where the ceiling is here. You know, they have billions and trillions of dollars. What else?""
The Social Reckoning serves as a follow-up to Sorkin’s 2010 film The Social Network, which explored Facebook’s origins and Zuckerberg’s creation of the platform.
White recalled joining Facebook while he was in high school, saying "it seemed innocent enough, I guess, at the time." He also remembered seeing friends become concerned about followers and who followed whom.
"Now it's kind of like how we value everything in this world," he said.
White hopes the film encourages audiences to examine their relationships with social media, including its potential effects on mental health and how people receive information.
Madison, who does not use social media, said she shares "a lot of the same sensibilities" and concerns as White.
Wunmi Mosaku, who plays a fictionalised Zuckerberg adviser, also said the film raises questions about regulation, media consumption and the influence of technology companies. The Social Reckoning arrives in cinemas on Friday.

title: Nathan Fielder says he still does not  understand  Elizabeth Holmes documentary
description: Nathan Fielder still trying to understand his experience making Elizabeth Holmes documentary  You Can See Everything
content:
Nathan Fielder still trying to understand his experience making Elizabeth Holmes documentary 'You Can See Everything'
Nathan Fielder says he is still trying to understand his experience making You Can See Everything , the upcoming A24 documentary about Elizabeth Holmes and her partner, Billy Evans.
Fielder and co-director Lance Oppenheim discussed the film during a screening and Q&A at the Academy Museum. The documentary was secretly screened at the Telluride Film Festival before its public release.
"I still am not sure to this day what I experienced," Fielder told the audience. "Maybe it being out there, everyone can help me understand what I went through a little bit. What we all went through."
Oppenheim explained that the project began after he contacted Fielder, having seen his debut feature Some Kind of Heaven. After initially rejecting Oppenheim's ideas, the pair found inspiration during a visit to The Magic Castle.
A performer asked the audience to suggest a name, prompting someone to shout "Elizabeth Holmes!" Oppenheim said he had learned the previous day that Holmes and Evans had approached A24 about making a documentary covering Holmes' final days before beginning her prison sentence.
Fielder and Oppenheim subsequently approached A24 about meeting Holmes. Fielder recalled finding the first meeting difficult to understand.
"It was a really disorienting experience, talking to someone like that, when they seem so sincere," Fielder said.
Much of the documentary was filmed in 2023, before Holmes began her prison sentence. Fielder initially had a smaller on-camera role, but Oppenheim said the cameras eventually turned towards him to help audiences navigate the events surrounding Holmes and Evans.
The filmmakers and a seven-person crew spent around 35 days documenting their lives, with Fielder and Oppenheim staying in the couple's guest house.
The directors said they often disagreed about what they had witnessed, with even members of the crew forming different interpretations of mundane events.
"The first place that we started from was like, 'Can we document this in a way that brings the audience into this experience?'" Oppenheim said.
You Can See Everything is scheduled to release in cinemas on October 16.

title: Sean  Diddy  Combs ordered to pay  478 000 in defamation legal fees
description: Sean  Diddy  Combs has been ordered to pay NBC  478 000 in legal fees after his defamation lawsuit was dismissed
content:
Sean 'Diddy' Combs has been ordered to pay NBC $478,000 in legal fees after his defamation lawsuit was dismissed
Sean 'Diddy' Combs has been ordered to pay $478,000 in legal fees to NBC after a judge dismissed his defamation lawsuit against the US television network.
According to a court order obtained by Billboard , Combs must reimburse NBC for legal costs incurred while defending against his lawsuit over the 2025 documentary The Making of a Bad Boy.
Combs sued NBC in early 2025 seeking $100 million, alleging that the documentary advanced a "false narrative" that he was involved in the deaths of The Notorious B.I.G. and Kim Porter.
Judge Phaedra F. Perry-Bond dismissed the lawsuit in April under New York's anti-SLAPP statute. The judge found that NBC had followed appropriate journalistic standards by making clear that Combs denied the claims featured in the documentary.
The ruling also noted that interviewees who discussed the theories had their own biases against Combs.
New York's anti-SLAPP law allows a successful defendant to recover legal fees incurred while defending certain cases involving First Amendment-protected speech. The judge subsequently ruled that NBC was entitled to reimbursement.
However, the court reduced the amount requested by NBC's legal team. Gibson Dunn originally billed $990,000, but the judge found that the number of hours claimed was "excessive" and reduced the bill by $512,000.
The resulting award means Combs must pay $478,000 to cover NBC's legal expenses connected to the case.

title: Jawed Sheikh  Saba Hamid  other actors join humanitarian mission for Palestinian families in Jordan
description: Mission saw actors distribute food aid to over 500 families  spend time with children receiving medical treatment
content:
Mission saw actors distribute food aid to over 500 families, spend time with children receiving medical treatment
Pakistani actors have shared glimpses of a humanitarian trip to Jordan, where they joined UK-registered charity SKT Welfare in supporting Palestinians displaced from Gaza.
The five-day mission, which took place from September 29 to October 3, brought together actors including Jawed Sheikh, Khaled Anam, Saba Hamid, Shagufta Ejaz, Ally Khan, Kubra Khan, Gohar Rasheed, Ahmed Ali Akbar and Nabeel Zafar.
During the visit, the delegation helped prepare and distribute more than 500 boxes of essential, non-perishable food items to Gazan refugee families, while also spending time with Palestinian patients and their families receiving medical treatment in Jordan.
Sharing photographs and videos from the trip on Instagram, the actors documented their work with SKT Welfare as well as their interactions with families displaced by the conflict.
According to Khaled Anam’s account of the mission, many of the families receiving assistance included children who had been injured during the conflict or were undergoing treatment for serious illnesses, including cancer and heart conditions.
In the caption accompanying his post, he wrote, "Between September 29 and October 3, 2026, the SKT Welfare organised and deployed a team of actors from Pakistan for a moving mission to Jordan to support displaced women and children from Gaza. From packing to personally visiting and delivering essential non perishable food ration boxes to over 500 Gazan refugee families having children either injured during the conflict or with severe medical conditions like cancer, heart problems etc, in hospitals and their temporary abode."
For the delegation, one of the more personal parts of the visit was an afternoon arranged for children undergoing cancer treatment. SKT Welfare hosted the children for games, activities and a hot meal, giving them an opportunity to spend time away from the pressures of treatment and displacement.
In his Instagram post, Anam described the experience as a chance for the group to “listen, comfort, and stand in solidarity” with Palestinians from Gaza.
The organisation also provides longer-term assistance to patients who have travelled to Jordan for medical care. Its support includes accommodation, meals and transportation, helping patients reach hospitals and attend essential medical appointments while they are away from home.
Saba Hamid, Nabeel Zafar and Shagufta Ejaz also shared photographs from the mission on their respective Instagram accounts. Their posts featured moments from the aid work as well as snapshots of the group’s time in Jordan.
The Jordan visit comes as Palestinian patients and their families continue to navigate medical treatment and displacement far from Gaza. Through its work in Jordan, SKT Welfare says it continues to assist people who have been evacuated for medical care, while its wider relief operations extend to communities inside Gaza.
The actors’ posts have since offered followers a closer look at the mission, documenting both the practical aid delivered and the personal connections formed with families and children during the visit.

title: Purple reign  Philippines seeks to keep grip on ube throne
description: Ube   s global boom is straining Philippine farmers  prompting a raw export ban to protect the crop from biopiracy fear
content:
Ube’s global boom is straining Philippine farmers, prompting a raw-export ban to protect the crop from biopiracy fear
The Philippine ube has become a trend-setting sensation from Los Angeles to London to Seoul, with the humble yam's bright purple hue drawing lines outside coffee shops and bakeries and millions of views on social media.
But keeping pace with the international boom has proven tricky for the archipelago nation's overwhelmingly smallholder farmers, with yields declining and some unable to commit to the plant's nine-month growing time.
Fears that biopiracy might take a chunk out of the blossoming market, meanwhile, have prompted the government to announce a ban on the export of the raw form of the yam.
Standing in his ube field south of Manila, farmer-exporter Al Bonifacio told AFP he was in favour of doing whatever it took to protect the crop from any growers overseas trying to cash in on the craze.
The Philippine ube has become a trend-setting sensation from Los Angeles to London to Seoul, with the humble yam's bright purple hue drawing lines outside coffee shops and bakeries and millions of views on social media. PHOTO: AFP
"Purple is so royal and is very pleasing to the eye," the 59-year-old said with a smile during a visit to his one-hectare (2.5-acre) ube farm. "Our greatest fear is, if we are not able to supply ube to the world, someone (else) will step in."
Sold as powder, extract, paste, or frozen puree, ube is easily mixed into coffee, pastries, ice cream, spreads and even make-up.
At a Tokyo gelato shop, ube importer JP Mercado told AFP the Japanese market was expanding rapidly after the craze first hit neighbouring South Korea.
"It's really taken off like wildfire," he said as a batch of powder was slowly stirred into gelato, turning it a bright purple. "I think social media has been hugely impactful," he said, adding his client list ranged from small cafes to luxury hotels.
Ube was a staple of Philippine gardens as long as 5,000 years ago, boiled and eaten by families as a substitute to rice when their provisions ran out.
Beloved for its mildly sweet, nutty flavour and velvety texture, it later evolved into a party food, consumed as a jam or stewed with sticky rice balls in coconut milk.
Demand exploded locally this decade, most memorably during a purple bread mania that swept the archipelago in the darkest days of the Covid-19 pandemic.
Ube halaya topping over sweet ube rice porridge (champorado) is a popular treat in the Philippines. PHOTO: AFP
"I'm super-obsessed with ube," university student Kym Trivino told AFP as she sipped an ube-matcha concoction at one of Manila's largest shopping malls.
Baker Diane Bustos said her company now sells seven types of ube cookies.
"It took over matcha. That's really something that we Filipinos should be really proud of," she said, referring to the bright green tea powder popularised by Gwyneth Paltrow and other celebrities.
But as ube mania grows globally, clouds loom at home.
Bonifacio told AFP the country's small farmers widely lacked the facilities for post-harvest storage and processing, while access to marketing and financing lagged.
Planting to harvest takes at least nine months, too long for most Filipino farmers who preferred the shorter growing period for beans, squash or bittergourd to feed their families, the farmer added.
Bonifacio said he had been forced to scour the rest of the country for raw ube to meet his growing export commitments, a process that can double his costs.
"We have the land, but quality planting materials are not always available," Leonilyn Ladao, a local agriculturist, told AFP .
"Last year's production was just 12,483 tonnes," Jose Zalde Samson, from the country's plant industry bureau, told AFP of the five-year low.
Industry officials blamed typhoons, which hit key ube farming regions. For the first half of 2026, production was up around 17 per cent.
"The government has only started promoting ube in the past two to three years as demand spiked," Samson explained.
"Before the ube craze, it was a niche market," he said, adding it had lagged behind high-value crops like bananas, mangoes and coffee.
Ube-flavored snacks displayed at a convenience store in Seoul © Jung Yeon-je. PHOTO: AFP
With the pressure on, the government is now working on how it can boost supply. "We are looking at how (the growing season) can be shortened to six months," Samson said.
With neighbours like Thailand and Vietnam now getting into the game, the Philippines is acting to protect its crown.
"We don't want to export it to countries that could use Philippine ube varieties to compete with us," Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel said last month while revealing the ban on raw ube exports.
"We've had data that tubers were being (surreptitiously) exported," Samson said, declining to provide further details.
In Tokyo, ube importer Mercado said he backed the Philippine government's move, which he believed would protect the country's cultural heritage. "Ube really is, I would say, very interlocked with the Filipino identity," he said.
Bonifacio the farmer agreed. "(We) are stewards of the ube industry," he said, looking out over his crop. "We have a stake in this. We have to protect it."

title: Pakistan Navy seizes narcotics worth  96m in Arabian Sea  ISPR
description: ISPR says approximately 850kg of Ice  2 000kg of hashish  cannabis recovered from concealed compartments
content:
ISPR says approximately 850kg of Ice, 2,000kg of hashish, cannabis recovered from concealed compartments
Pakistan Navy Ship (PNS) YARMOOK seized a large cache of narcotics worth approximately $96 million during two counter-narcotics operations in the Arabian Sea, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Wednesday.
According to the military's media wing, "PNS YARMOOK, while deployed in the Arabian Sea, conducted two successful counter-narcotics operations at extended ranges from the Pakistani coast."
The statement added that during the operations, two dhows were intercepted and approximately 850kg of Ice and 2,000kg of hashish and cannabis were recovered from concealed compartments inside the vessels.
The statement further said that "the seized narcotics, valued at approximately $96 million," were taken into custody and would subsequently be handed over to the concerned authorities for "further disposal and legal proceedings."
The successful operations reflected the Pakistan Navy’s sustained presence, vigilance, and unwavering commitment to regional maritime security and the fight against illicit trafficking at sea, the statement added.
Operations reflect PN’s sustained presence, vigilance & commitment to regional maritime security & countering illicit trafficking at sea. PN remains steadfast in ensuring a safe, secure & stable maritime environment & preventing use of maritime domain for illicit activities. 2/2 pic.twitter.com/9YnO83FMNe
President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to and congratulated the Pakistan Navy and its officers on two successful counter-narcotics operations conducted by PNS YARMOOK.
President Zardari praised the Pakistan Navy’s sustained vigilance, preparedness and commitment to combating illicit drug trafficking at sea.
“The Pakistan Navy’s role in preventing illegal activities in maritime waters and safeguarding regional maritime security is commendable,” the president said.
On September 26, PNS HUNAIN and YARMOOK seized more than 2,800 kilogrammes of narcotics, valued at approximately $750 million, during a joint counter-narcotics operation in the Arabian Sea.
ISPR said that the ships were conducting a routine patrol when they intercepted a suspicious boat. A boarding operation was subsequently carried out, during which narcotics were recovered from "concealed compartments."
Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf commended the officers and crew for their "professionalism and vigilance". The naval chief also reaffirmed Pakistan Navy's commitment to maritime security and combating illicit trafficking at sea.

The joint intelligence-based operation "thwarted an attempt to smuggle a large cache of contraband items" in the area. The operation was carried out on "actionable intelligence."

Food vendors claim they experienced financial losses, poor planning and difficult working conditions at the event
Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields festival is facing criticism from food vendors who claim they experienced financial losses, poor planning and difficult working conditions at the event.
The inaugural festival took place on August 29 at Great Park in Irvine, California, with performances from Rodrigo, Bikini Kill, Garbage, Chappell Roan and Doechii.
The event raised $10 million for non-profit organisations, with Melinda Gates matching the amount to bring total donations to $20 million.
Ugly Oats Kitchen owner Mary Chacon said the festival presented an “enormous financial risk” for vendors. She claimed organisers charged about $1,400 in fees and took 35% of sales.
Chacon also alleged vendors were told they could face fines if they ran out of food, while some key setup information arrived “until a few hours before” the event.
She said one member of her team suffered heat exhaustion and struggled to find food, while vendors were effectively stranded at their booths.
“We wanted to send her home, but the staff lot was a two-mile walk from our booth. Most of the vendors were essentially stranded at our booths until 1:00AM,” Chacon said.
Another business, Por Suerte Cookies, said it suffered a “financial loss” and “barely sold anything”. The company also said it was “still waiting to be paid”, adding, “After everything we spent to participate, we have still not received what we are owed for the event.”
Rodrigo, Daisy Chain Fields and DLS Events have not publicly responded to the claims.
The festival also received positive critical attention for its charitable goals and all-female line-up, highlighting the contrasting reports surrounding its debut.

description: Kyle MacLachlan says  Fallout  season 3 has about month of filming left and could arrive in May or June 2027
content:
Kyle MacLachlan says 'Fallout' season 3 has about month of filming left and could arrive in May or June 2027
Fallout season 3 is approaching the final stages of filming, with star Kyle MacLachlan suggesting the Prime Video series could return in May or June 2027.
MacLachlan, who plays Hank MacLean in the series, shared the production update while speaking with a fan at a signing for his new memoir. In a video shared on X, the actor said filming still had around a month remaining.
"We're still shooting away. We've got about a month or so to go," MacLachlan said.
He later discussed a potential release window, adding, "(and then) probably come out maybe May or June. Fingers crossed that it's soon."
MacLachlan did not specify a year when discussing the potential release period, but the production timeline would suggest a May or June 2027 premiere if filming concludes around November 2026.
Prime Video has not announced an official release date for Fallout season 3, meaning MacLachlan's comments do not represent a confirmed schedule from the streamer.
The third season will continue the story following the events of Fallout season 2. Prime Video renewed the series for a third season in May 2025, while principal photography reportedly began in July 2026.
MacLachlan is set to return alongside Ella Purnell, Walton Goggins and Aaron Moten. Annabel O'Hagan and Dave Register have also been promoted to series regulars for the upcoming season.
Aaron Paul joined the cast in May 2026, although his role has not yet been revealed. Emily Mortimer, Manny Jacinto and Thomasin McKenzie are also set to appear in recurring roles.
The first two seasons of Fallout are currently available to stream on Prime Video.

title: Former Playstation head defends physical games as  super important
description: Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden says physical games remain important as Sony moves towards digital releases
content:
Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden says physical games remain important as Sony moves towards digital releases
Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden has defended physical games, arguing that players who continue to buy discs remain an important part of the gaming community.
Layden, who previously served as chairman of PlayStation Worldwide Studios and CEO of Sony Interactive Entertainment America, discussed the shift towards digital games on The Expansion Pass podcast.
While acknowledging the convenience of downloading games, he questioned the decision to move away from physical releases.
Layden said he did not know the financial reasoning behind Sony's plans to end physical disc releases, describing the decision as likely a “heavily spreadsheeted decision” based on costs and profits.
“Downloading a game is easier than going across my living room to put a disc in the machine,” he said. “I just press a button on my controller and I don’t have to move.”
However, Layden argued that physical buyers could represent a particularly valuable section of the market, even if they make up a smaller proportion of players.
“Maybe 80% of the people download and 20% don’t, or whatever that breakdown is going to be,” he said. “But that’s a super important 20%.”
He described physical game collectors as “the most faithful of the faithful” and compared gaming's collecting culture with comic book collecting.
“We are an inquisitive, collecting sort of people and we like to show off our stuff,” he said.
Layden's wider concern centres on whether digital purchases represent ownership or access to a digital asset.
“I think this is probably the more insidious aspect to it, is that it changes the conversation from do you own a game or do you have access to a digital asset, right?” he said.
“If you can’t sell a thing, that means you don’t own a thing. And if you don’t own it, then what are you buying?”
Layden said the shift could affect the reputation of companies moving away from physical releases, adding that he hoped the financial reasoning behind the decision justified its potential impact.

title: Louis Vuitton shows slinky dresses and fluid jackets  adapts to warming world
description: Louis Vuitton   s Ghesqui  re unveils airy designs  adapting fabrics and silhouettes to rising temperatures worldwide
content:
Louis Vuitton’s Ghesquière unveils airy designs, adapting fabrics and silhouettes to rising temperatures worldwide
Louis Vuitton showed fluid jackets and slinky, sheer dresses on Tuesday as womenswear creative director Nicolas Ghesquière said hotter temperatures caused by climate change were ​changing his approach to developing fabrics and designing clothes.
Designer Nicolas Ghesquiere appears on the runway of his Spring/Summer 2027 collection show for fashion house Louis Vuitton during Paris Fashion Week in Paris, France, October 6, 2026. PHOTO: Reuters
Light, flowing fabrics were used throughout the spring/summer 2027 collection on simple strappy dresses, ​loosely fastened jackets and sheer skirts in white or pastel pink and blue.
A black and ​white check look and dresses covered in an iridescent diamond pattern provided graphic elements in otherwise pared-back, tonal outfits.
Models emerged in between Louis Vuitton-branded cars on a set made to look like a highway, with ​a tar floor and road markings — decor Ghesquière said was inspired by learning that ​the stunning Louvre courtyard was for decades used as a parking lot for finance ministry officials, before the ‌museum's ⁠famous glass pyramids were installed.
Models present creations by designer Nicolas Ghesquiere as part of his Spring/Summer 2027 collection show for fashion house Louis Vuitton during Paris Fashion Week in Paris, France, October 6, 2026. PHOTO: Reuters
Jackets featured flowing sleeves with some also extending into a long train trailing behind the model, and trousers were wide and fluid with long slits up the side to let air in. Small, simple handbags came in cream and lemon tones.
Ghesquière told ​reporters after the show ​that despite the ⁠minimalist appearance, "making things extremely light is very complex and the engineering and development of fabric to fight that gravity is also very complex".
Models present creations by designer Nicolas Ghesquiere as part of his Spring/Summer 2027 collection show for fashion house Louis Vuitton during Paris Fashion Week in Paris, France, October 6, 2026. PHOTO: Reuters
Louis ​Vuitton, the flagship brand of luxury giant LVMH, has struggled with ​falling sales ⁠of its famous monogrammed handbags as fewer middle-class shoppers feel they can stretch to high-end purchases. The monogram was used lightly in the collection, featuring only on a couple of handbags and ⁠a ​leather bomber jacket.
A crowd of screaming fans outside the ​show greeted the arrival of K-pop star Felix, while France's first lady Brigitte Macron was among the celebrity guests, ​along with actors Zendaya, Emma Stone, and Saoirse Ronan.
