title: PTI long march ends day four in Bara  to resume from Hayatabad
description: Shafi Jan rejects suggestions that Afridi could be removed from office  tells Sanaullah to worry about himself
content:
Jan rejects suggestions that Afridi could be removed from office, tells Sanaullah to worry about himself
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) long march ended in Bara in Khyber district on its fourth day on Wednesday, after the party held large gatherings in Kohat and Khyber, with Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi leading the procession.
The march will resume from the Hayatabad Toll Plaza at 2pm on Thursday, according to the schedule issued by the party.
The procession will travel from Peshawar towards Charsadda, passing through Ring Road, Bhanamari, Kohati, Ganj and Jamil Chowk before heading to Charsadda.
Earlier on Wednesday, the long march caravan departed from Mattani for Khyber, following a change in its route announced a day earlier. The party had said the march would first head towards Khyber before proceeding to Peshawar.
Addressing a crowd on Frontier Road in Mattani, Afridi said that he could bring peace to K-P "in 100 days" with a policy.
“I will give a policy and will bring peace to K-P within 100 days, but your intention is not to bring peace. You are the enemy of Pashtuns, and there is a mindset that considers Pashtuns as cattle. I will not accept the policy that goes against us. I will give you a policy, and you will have to accept it, and that policy will bring peace”.
آؤ ، میں دیتا ہوں پالیسی: ▪️100 دن میں امن۔⁰وزیرِ اعلیٰ سہیل آفریدی۔ ⁰ #100DayPeaceChallenge #سر_بکف_میدان_میں pic.twitter.com/U7d8XA3A0F
“What have you achieved after 14,000 intelligence-based operations and 22 major military operations? You are still saying there is terrorism in K-P,” he remarked. “They say that the provincial government of K-P does not cooperate with us. I ask: the provincial government in Balochistan does cooperate with you, so why is there no peace in Balochistan? This means you have a failed policy,” Afridi stated.
The chief minister said peace could not be achieved until the authorities stopped targeting PTI and focused on combating and eliminating terrorism.
“You want to finish PTI, not terrorism”.
Afridi added that if the provincial government was saying that it could restore peace in K-P within 100 days, the government should engage with it, adding that he was willing to formulate a policy for this purpose.
Earlier, K-P government spokesperson Shafi Jan said Afridi had presented his case directly before the “court of the people” during the march’s stop in Kohat, where he received a large public reception.
“The people of Kohat made it clear through their enthusiastic welcome that the people stand with CM Afridi,” Jan said in a post on X.
Jan’s remarks came in response to Sanaullah’s criticism of the PTI long march and the K-P government. Sanaullah had said the government would not accept political demands through pressure or attempts to “hold the state hostage”, while accusing the PTI of pursuing political instability and opposing intelligence-based counter-terrorism operations in the province.
He said K-P had the “original Form 45 government”, describing it as a government established through the mandate of PTI founder Imran Khan and the people.
“This government, formed through the votes of the people, cannot be removed through any political plan,” he said. Jan also rejected suggestions that Afridi could be removed from office, "You should worry about yourself,” he said.

He added that the government represented the people’s mandate and that any political action against it would be answered through constitutional and democratic means.
According to Jan, Afridi’s demands included a meeting with Imran, access to personal physicians for his treatment, justice for Bushra Bibi and other members of Imran’s family, decisions in cases on merit, and a comprehensive strategy for restoring peace in K-P through consultation with all stakeholders.
He said Afridi had invited all stakeholders in the province to the K-P Assembly for consultations on restoring peace, resulting in a 13-point plan signed by the opposition leader and other opposition leaders.
“The plan has already been sent to the relevant stakeholders,” Jan said.
He further highlighted that Afridi had made a serious effort to develop a joint and practical strategy for lasting peace by taking all political and relevant stakeholders into confidence.
Jan said the long march was continuing peacefully and within the constitutional framework under Afridi’s leadership, adding that the large turnout in Kohat showed that the chief minister had put his position before the public and that people had listened to him directly.
The change in route was announced by CM Afridi on Tuesday as the march reached its third day. Afridi said the PTI had originally planned to head towards Peshawar but would now first proceed towards Khyber before returning to the provincial capital.
Afridi said the route had been changed as part of the PTI's strategy, without giving further details about the reason for the change.
Read: PTI marchers change route, head to Khyber first
The march had reached Kohat on Monday after beginning from Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat on Sunday. Caravans from Tank, Dera Ismail Khan, South Waziristan, North Waziristan, Bannu and Lakki Marwat had joined the procession at the starting point before it moved towards Karak for an overnight stay.
On the second day, the caravan moved from Karak towards Kohat, with participants from Karak joining the procession. Afridi addressed participants in Kohat and announced that the march would resume its journey towards Peshawar from University Chowk on Tuesday.
On the third day, caravans from Kohat, Hangu, Kurram and Orakzai joined the procession. The march was initially scheduled to travel from Kohat towards Peshawar and stay overnight near Mattani.
Under the original schedule announced by Afridi, the caravan was due to depart from Budh Bair in Peshawar on Wednesday, with participants from Khyber district joining the march there. Other Peshawar constituencies were scheduled to join at Kohat Road Bridge and the Motorway Toll Plaza before the procession moved towards the Charsadda interchange.
The march was then scheduled to move from the Charsadda interchange towards Khairabad on October 8, with participants from Charsadda and Mohmand joining the caravan. The next phase of the march was to be announced at Khairabad.

title: WHO warns escalating conflict in Yemen takes  devastating toll
description: Nearly 1 000 people killed  over 4 200 injured  almost 198 000 displaced since latest escalation  WHO chief says
content:
Nearly 1,000 people killed, over 4,200 injured, almost 198,000 displaced since latest escalation, WHO chief says
World Health Organisation chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned of a "devastating toll" in Yemen amid an escalating conflict.
"The escalating conflict in Yemen is taking a devastating toll. Nearly 1000 people have been killed, more than 4200 injured, and almost 198,000 displaced since the latest escalation, amid outbreaks of cholera and measles," Tedros said.
WHO's immediate funding requirement more than tripled from $9 million to $31 million due to growing needs, he said on US social media company X.
"We urgently call on donors to step up. Lives depend on humanitarian and health aid," Tedros added.
Yemen has been engulfed in conflict since the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa and several provinces in September 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.
Clashes between government forces and the Houthis resumed in July, marking the most intense fighting since a period of relative calm following a UN-brokered truce that began in April 2022.
Fighting intensified in September, when the Houthis seized key areas in Al-Hudaydah and Taiz provinces, including the strategic city of Mokha and Mayyun Island overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Yemen’s Houthis claim attacks on Saudi airports, military bases
Yemen’s Houthi group claimed early on Wednesday that it carried out a series of drone and ballistic missile attacks targeting airports and military installations in Saudi Arabia.
In a statement on the US social media platform X, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the forces targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with several drones, claiming the strike was "precise" and disrupted air traffic there.
He also said Houthi forces conducted two operations targeting Abha International Airport and Khamis Mushait Air Base using a combination of ballistic missiles and drones. He claimed the attacks disrupted air traffic at the airport and caused damage to the military base.
In a separate statement, Saree said Houthi forces targeted three military camps — Dagharir in Jizan, Aakifah in Asir and Al-Mawsim in Jizan — with a large number of ballistic missiles and drones.

title: Hira Soomro urges people to rethink how they perceive animals
description: The actress used her Instagram Story to share a message about animal intelligence and emotions
content:
Actor argues animals can understand and experience emotions, urging greater empathy towards them beyond instinct
Hira Soomro has urged her followers to reconsider how they perceive animals, arguing that their ability to think and feel should not be dismissed simply because they process the world differently from humans.
The actor shared an Instagram Story featuring a video of an animal approaching what appeared to be animal hide, with text on the clip reading, “She recognises the skin.” The post prompted Soomro to expand on what she described as the emotional and cognitive abilities of animals.
“For decades we have been treating animals as living being with no brain or feelings but it's not true they too understand and feel. Their thinking might be instinctual but they do have thinking brain and can feel emotions,” she wrote in the Instagram Story.
Screengrab: hirasoomro_official/Instagram
Her message centred on the idea that animals should not be viewed solely through the lens of instinct. While their way of processing the world may differ from that of humans, Soomro argued that this does not mean they are incapable of understanding or experiencing emotions.
The post comes as discussions around animal welfare and the treatment of stray and domestic animals continue to receive attention in Pakistan. Other Pakistani celebrities have previously used social media to speak about the issue. In February, actor Ushna Shah spoke about animal rights, while Nadia Afgan addressed animal cruelty, violence and accountability.
Soomro is best known for her television work, including her role as Maryam in Tere Bin . She has also appeared in dramas including Chupke Chupke , Khuda Aur Mohabbat 3 and Tere Aany Se . She has built her profile through Pakistani television while remaining active on social media outside her acting work. She has also spoken publicly about balancing her career with motherhood.

title: FM Dar  CNSC Aamer Raza stress  close institutional coordination  on national security
description: The two discuss matters of national security and exchanged views on regional and international developments
content:
The two discuss matters of national security and exchanged views on regional and international developments
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and Commander National Strategic Command (CNSC) General Syed Aamer Raza agreed on the importance of "close institutional coordination" in advancing Pakistan’s national interests and contributing to regional peace and security, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Wednesday.
According to an FO statement, General Raza called on Dar at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, where the deputy prime minister congratulated him on his promotion and appointment as CNSC and wished him success in his new responsibilities.
"The two officials discussed matters of national security and exchanged views on regional and international developments. They agreed on the importance of close institutional coordination in advancing Pakistan’s national interests and contributing to regional peace and security,” the statement said.
Commander National Strategic Command General Syed Aamer Raza, NI (M), called on the Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today. The DPM/FM congratulated General Syed Aamer Raza on his promotion and… pic.twitter.com/zcSMmrNXd6
General Raza took charge as the first CNSC on July 31, after Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif promoted him to the rank of a four-star general and appointed him as CNSC on July 24, a move completing the restructuring of the country’s higher military command initiated under the 27th Constitutional Amendment.
The position was created under the 27th Constitutional Amendment , which rewrote Article 243. The amendment abolished the longstanding office of the Chairman, Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee (CJCSC) and established the posts of Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and CNSC. It also expanded the constitutional powers of the country's senior military leadership and introduced constitutional protections for five-star generals.
Read: PM Shehbaz appoints General Aamer Raza as Commander National Strategic Command
Under the amendment , the prime minister appoints the CNSC on the recommendation of the CDF and Chief of Army Staff. The appointment is for a three-year term, while the prime minister is authorised to determine the terms, conditions and rules governing the office.
The amendment also allows the prime minister to reappoint the CNSC for one additional three-year term on the recommendation of the CDF.
It further provides that the appointment, reappointment or extension of the CNSC cannot be challenged before any court, placing such decisions beyond judicial review. The bill also stipulates that the retirement age, service tenure, or removal clauses under the Army Act will not apply to the CNSC, who will continue to serve as a general in the Pakistan Army while performing his duties in the role.

title: Kagan and Soai win 2026 Nobel chemistry prize for single molecular mirror creation
description: The chemistry Nobel followed those for medicine and physics announced on Monday and Tuesday
content:
The chemistry Nobel followed those for medicine and physics announced on Monday and Tuesday
Scientists Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for solving a long-standing riddle of how to form a single ​molecular mirror image, a discovery hugely important for pharmaceutical manufacturing, the award-giving body said on Wednesday.
"This is ‌the most exciting day in my life; I am very glad to share this prize with Professor Henri Kagan," Soai said, speaking by phone to the Nobel Prize press conference, adding he had been out shopping when receiving the news.
BREAKING NEWS The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences has decided to award the 2026 #NobelPrize in Chemistry to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai “for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.” pic.twitter.com/nH090ql1Xc
The chemistry Nobel, always the ​third prize to be awarded during Nobel week, followed those for medicine and physics announced on Monday and Tuesday.
"So this year's ​prize is about foundational chemistry," said Heiner Linke, chair of the Nobel Committee for Chemistry.
Many of ⁠the molecules essential to life exist in two forms that are mirror images of each other, like left and right hands, ​he said. Yet living organisms almost exclusively use only one version, a phenomenon known as "homochirality" – from the Greek word for hand – ​that has puzzled chemists for more than a century.
Thanks to the discoveries that are being recognised by the #NobelPrize in Chemistry 2026, chemists have gained fundamental new tools for use in their daily work but, above all, these discoveries have contributed to solving one of chemistry’s greatest mysteries: how homochirality… pic.twitter.com/ucsky2AxBw
This year's prize was awarded for discoveries that showed how chemical reactions can be driven to favour a single molecular mirror image, work that has been key for chemists who design reactions for the manufacture of pharmaceuticals.
"Many of the drug molecules ​occur in two variants that are each other's non-identical mirror image: one has the therapeutic effect, while the other can cause ​unnecessary and sometimes harmful side effects," the Nobel Foundation said.
Kenso Soai – awarded the 2026 #NobelPrize in Chemistry – designed the first chemical reaction in which only one of the potential mirror images was formed. Other than life itself, no one had ever achieved this feat. The Soai reaction is one of the most spectacular chemical… pic.twitter.com/CQHBqwo1Ut
Prizes established in will of Swedish inventor
Established in the will of Swedish inventor and ‌businessman Alfred ⁠Nobel, the prizes for achievements in science, literature and peace have been awarded since 1901, with a few interruptions mostly due to the world wars.
Nobel, a chemist by trade, amassed huge wealth in the 19th century from inventions primarily tied to warfare, most notably dynamite. The economics prize is a later addition funded by the Swedish central bank.
Also Read: German and US scientists win Nobel medicine prize for work on optogenetics
Sometimes overshadowed by more famous laureates in ​the fields of physics, literature and ​peace, the chemistry awards ⁠have still recognised many influential discoveries such as nuclear fission and genetic sequencing techniques.
Last year's chemistry award went to scientists Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi for the development of so-called metal–organic ​frameworks, molecular constructions that can help tackle challenges such as climate change and lack of fresh ​water.
Read More: Belgian-American wins Nobel in Physics
The laureates will ⁠receive their medals from Sweden's King Carl XVI Gustaf at a ceremony in Stockholm on December 10, the anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death. The awards are followed by a lavish banquet at Stockholm City Hall.
They also share 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million), as well ⁠as the ​fame of winning arguably the world's most prestigious science award.

content:
Bollywood couple shares a heartfelt Instagram post featuring their firstborn’s hand and baby gloves
Kiara Advani and Sidharth Malhotra are set to become parents once again, with the Bollywood couple announcing that they are expecting their second child in a heartfelt Instagram post on Wednesday.
The couple shared a tender image featuring their intertwined hands, their firstborn’s tiny hand and a pair of baby gloves placed in the middle — a subtle yet emotional hint that their family is about to grow once again.
“Blessed once again with the greatest gift of all. Our hearts are so full of love and gratitude,” Advani wrote alongside the picture.
The announcement comes a little over a year after the couple welcomed their first child .
Advani and Malhotra announced the arrival of their baby girl in July 2025, writing at the time, “Our hearts are full and our world forever changed. We are blessed with a Baby Girl.”
The couple later revealed their daughter’s name, Saraayah Malhotra, in November 2025, sharing a photograph of themselves holding her tiny toes.
Their latest announcement also echoes the way they revealed their first pregnancy.
In February 2025, Kiara and Sidharth shared an understated photograph centred around baby mittens to announce that they were expecting their first child.
Now, baby gloves have once again taken centre stage, with fans and Bollywood celebrities flooding the couple’s latest post with congratulatory messages.
Kiara and Sidharth’s love story began before they officially became one of Bollywood’s most-loved couples. The two first met at the wrap-up party of Kiara’s Lust Stories in 2018, according to Kiara’s earlier account, before their relationship blossomed further when they worked together on Shershaah .
Released in 2021, Shershaah saw the pair share the screen as Vikram Batra and Dimple Cheema. While they remained largely private about their relationship, their chemistry on and off screen fuelled years of speculation.
The couple eventually made things official with their wedding on February 7, 2023, at Suryagarh Palace in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan.
The intimate ceremony was attended by close friends and family, with the pair choosing to keep much of their relationship away from the public eye.
Advani was most recently seen in Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups , alongside Yash, while she has also appeared in War 2 with Hrithik Roshan and NTR Jr.
Malhotra, meanwhile, continues to balance commercial and action-oriented projects, with Vvan: Force of the Forest among his recent work.
For now, however, the spotlight is firmly on the couple’s growing family. After moving from Shershaah co-stars to husband and wife, and then becoming parents to Saraayah, Kiara and Sidharth are preparing to welcome another little member into their family.

title: Halle Berry says she has never abused son as ex Olivier Martinez seeks sole custody
description: Berry submitted video evidence and messages she says contradict Martinez   s account of September 26 incident
content:
Berry submitted video evidence and messages she says contradict Martinez’s account of September 26 incident
Halle Berry has denied allegations that she physically abused her 13 year old son, Maceo, amid a custody dispute with her former husband Olivier Martinez.
In a declaration filed on October 5 and obtained by PEOPLE , Berry said she has never physically, emotionally or otherwise abused Maceo. The actor also referred to her own history as a victim of domestic violence, stating that she would never hurt their child.
The dispute centres on an incident on September 26, when Maceo was 12. Martinez alleged in a court filing that Berry became angry while their son was playing a virtual reality game and physically restrained him, including placing him in a headlock.
Berry has rejected that account. She told the court she entered Maceo’s room to tell him to stop gaming and began recording him. According to her declaration, Maceo noticed the phone, grabbed it and the pair began playfully roughhousing, which she described as something they frequently do.
Berry denied putting her hands around her son’s neck, choking him, restricting his breathing or restraining him. She also submitted video evidence and text messages that she said directly contradict Martinez’s description of what happened.
Berry said the situation later escalated when Maceo became upset and allegedly pushed her. Her fiancé, Van Hunt, intervened after Maceo pushed her again when she attempted to take his headset.
Martinez filed for sole custody last week, after which he was granted a temporary restraining order modifying the former couple’s custody arrangement. Berry has asked the court to restore their 50/50 custody agreement, which was established in August 2023 when their divorce was finalised.
Berry also disputed Martinez’s request for primary custody, arguing that he is unable to provide appropriate child centred guidance. She cited concerns involving Maceo’s behaviour and his need for professional support.
The former couple has previously disagreed over Maceo’s care. Berry sought court ordered co parenting therapy in 2024, but her request was denied.

title: Afridi calls Kundi s security meeting    attack on Constitution     warns against  another East Pakistan  situation
description: K P CM calls governor s meeting an attack on Constitution  says will not allow  any conspiracy to break up Pakistan
content:
K-P CM says governor lacked authority to summon officials, while advocate general outlines constitutional limits
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Wednesday condemned a security meeting chaired by Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, calling it “an attack on the Constitution and democracy” and warning that his government would not allow “any conspiracy to break up Pakistan” to succeed.
He also accused the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) of trying to create “another East Pakistan”, alleging that the party had previously prioritised personal interests over national interests. “We are with Pakistan and will not allow anyone to break up Pakistan under any circumstances. Whatever their intentions, God willing, they will fail," he added.
While addressing a meeting of the provincial cabinet, Afridi said the provincial government had been elected with a two-thirds majority and that the provincial assembly, cabinet and government remained intact. “The drama staged by the governor yesterday was extremely regrettable and condemnable,” he said, adding, “The governor presiding over such a meeting is an attack on the Constitution and democracy.”
The dispute over Kundi’s role came amid weeks of tension between the federal and provincial governments, with the possibility of governor’s rule or an emergency repeatedly raised over the deteriorating security situation and the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) planned march. The row intensified as Kundi expanded his role beyond his constitutional remit, chairing meetings on matters that fall under the provincial government’s authority.
وزیراعلیٰ خیبر پختونخوا @SohailAfridiISF صوبائی کابینہ اجلاس سے خطاب پشاور: گورنر کی جانب سے گزشتہ روز کیا جانے والا ڈرامہ انتہائی افسوسناک اور قابل مذمت ہے، وزیراعلیٰ سہیل آفریدی پشاور: خیبرپختونخوا میں عوام کی دو تہائی اکثریت سے منتخب حکومت موجود ہے، صوبائی اسمبلی، کابینہ اور… pic.twitter.com/VBNPkC0Ryv
Afridi questioned the governor’s authority to summon the chief secretary and IGP while an elected provincial government was in place.
“There is a constitutional procedure for removing a chief minister. The vote of no-confidence is the mechanism to do so,” he said, adding that he would consult the advocate general on the constitutional status of the meeting and, if necessary, legislation would be introduced through the provincial assembly.
He further stated that the advocate general of K-P would be consulted on the constitutional status of the meeting held on Tuesday.
He added that there was a constitutional procedure for removing a chief minister and that a vote of no-confidence was the mechanism provided for this purpose. “We will not allow anyone to launch an attack on democracy. The governor has acted unconstitutionally,” he affirmed.
Afridi claimed that the governor’s activities were aimed at provoking the provincial government and forcing it to respond in a way that could further deteriorate the situation.
Meanwhile, K-P Advocate General Shah Faisal Utmankhel told the meeting that Pakistan operated under a federal parliamentary system in which the Constitution defined the legislative, administrative and financial powers of different institutions.
He said the governor’s appointment was governed by Article 101, while Article 103 set out the governor’s conditions and powers and Article 104 provided for the speaker to perform the governor’s functions when required.
“In a parliamentary form of government and federalism, the governor is a ceremonial head,” the advocate general said, adding that executive powers rested with the provincial cabinet and government.
Referring to Article 131, he said the chief minister was required to keep the governor informed about matters relating to provincial administration and legislative proposals the provincial government intended to bring before the assembly. “There is nowhere written that on his own he can call someone, ask them questions or give instructions or directions,” he said.
The advocate general stated that such powers could be exercised under Article 234 when the constitutional machinery of a province failed and governor’s rule was imposed. “At the moment, the provincial government is in the field,” he added.
Afridi defended his government’s record on policing and counter-terrorism, saying it had worked continuously to strengthen the police, Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and Special Branch since he took oath on October 15, 2025.
“The weapons now with our police are not with any other police force in Pakistan,” he said, adding that his government had invested in CTD infrastructure and provided funds to strengthen the Special Branch, which he described as the “eyes” of the provincial government because effective intelligence was key to preventing attacks.
He also praised the police and administration for their sacrifices in the fight against terrorism, saying they had helped take the province from a period marked by ammunition and suicide attacks towards peace.
Afridi also accused the federal government of treating K-P as a “stepchild”.
He said the former tribal districts had been merged with K-P administratively in 2018 but had not been fully integrated financially, and that the funds promised at the time of the merger had still not been provided.
He accused the federal government of continuously imposing military operations on K-P since 2024, while people displaced by the government’s “wrong policies” had remained without full compensation. “Around Rs100 billion is still outstanding for our people who sacrificed for Pakistan,” he added.
Read More: CM Afridi urges PTI workers to join long march as convoy enters Kohat
Afridi said people whose homes had been destroyed were still waiting for compensation and that tribal families had been allocated only Rs400,000 per household. “Their handbags are worth tens of millions of rupees, while our tribal people, who have always sacrificed for Pakistan, have been allocated only Rs400,000 for their entire household.”
He also raised the case of displaced people from North Waziristan staying at the Bakakhel camp, saying they had been promised between Rs370 million and Rs380 million a month but were still not receiving the amount.
He said the provincial government had provided Rs21 billion to displaced people since taking office and had also borne responsibility for losses caused by military operations and drone strikes. “You make decisions there, but you have never thought about their consequences or what the people go through,” he added.
Afridi called on the federal government to increase K-P’s share under the National Finance Commission and clear outstanding compensation, saying the province had sacrificed 80,000 lives. “We have to fight terrorism as well as deal with conditions created by the federal government’s wrong policies,” he said.
He stated that 14,000 intelligence-based operations and 22 major military operations had been conducted over 22 years but peace had still not been restored. “If peace has not been established despite the sacrifice of 80,000 lives over 22 years, it means your policy has failed,” he added.
Afridi rejected the argument that the K-P government’s lack of cooperation was responsible for the continuing security problem, pointing to Balochistan, where he said the provincial government was cooperating with the federal government but peace had still not been established. “The federal government’s policy is neither effective in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa nor in Balochistan,” he added.
Also Read: PTI: talks deadlocked over Imran access, K-P policy
Afridi said a policy shift was necessary and claimed that peace could be restored within 100 days if the approach proposed by K-P’s stakeholders was followed. “We say that we can bring peace in 100 days. God willing, we will bring it and show it in 100 days,” he said.
He also accused the federal government of interfering in the provincial police’s work, saying K-P’s police had been made independent and freed from political interference and should not be turned into a force resembling the Punjab police.
“Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa police have other duties as well. They have to fight terrorism and deal with the conditions created by your wrong policies,” he said. “But you are making them your personal servants and putting them on other tasks. This is wrong.”
Afridi urged the chief secretary and IGP to direct officials under them to act according to the Constitution and law. “If, God forbid, someone gives you unconstitutional orders, do not obey them,” he said, adding, “These are our people, and this will damage our province and our country.”
He further alleged that a series of actions had been taken to provoke the provincial government and force it into making inflammatory statements.
He claimed that provincial minister Fazal Shakoor Khan had been picked up despite being a member of the provincial cabinet, while PTI workers had been injured in Waziristan. “Shakil Khan was fired at directly. When a goon was injured in retaliatory firing, he was declared to be ‘our man’,” Afridi said.
Also Read: Centre lays ground for governor's rule in K-P
“These things are being done to provoke us, so that we give some statement or create some provocation,” he said. “We have to remain peaceful. We have to talk about the Constitution and the law.”
Afridi directly addressed the chief secretary and IGP, saying they should not comply with unconstitutional or illegal orders. “I am a soldier of Imran Khan, and he has trained us throughout our lives not to do anything unconstitutional or illegal, or anything that could harm Pakistan, our province or our people,” he said.
He urged the chief secretary and IGP to direct officials under them to act according to the Constitution and law.
Afridi said police officers in South and North Waziristan had fired at people while acting as someone’s personal servants and called for inquiries against those responsible.
He also ordered an immediate inquiry against the station house officer of Lachi, alleging that the officer had taken money from people at gunpoint. “The Lachi SHO has become a goon rather than a police officer,” he said, calling for the officer to be removed and for officials who carried out wrongful actions not to be spared.

title: Dropping seniors from T20 squad is ridiculous
description: Sadiq Mohammad says Babar should have been included in T20 squad for SL series
content:
Sadiq Mohammad says Babar should have been included in T20 squad for SL series
Former Pakistan Test opener Sadiq Mohammad has criticised the decision to drop senior players including Babar Azam, Shaheen Afridi and Salman Ali Agha from the T20 squad, saying Pakistan should not have made sweeping changes after losing a series or a tournament and should instead give experienced players an opportunity to recover and perform.
Speaking to The Express Tribune, Sadiq said the decision reflected poor thinking by the selectors and coaches and warned that Pakistan's batting problems required greater attention to technique, discipline and shot selection. “Winning and losing are part of the game,” Sadiq told this correspondent.
“It does not mean that if you have lost the previous series or tournament, and you drop all your senior players like Babar, Shaheen, and Salman. That is a ridiculous and immature decision,” Sadiq said.
“I cannot understand the mindset of our selectors and coaches. When you have immature officials, they tend to make decisions like these without thinking about the long-term consequences,” said Sadiq.
He said all other teams have suffered defeats in the past, but they have not responded by changing their captain and dropping their senior players.
“Usually, they make one or two changes and give the team an opportunity to recover and perform.”
“Babar should have been included in the T20 squad. Pakistan needs technically sound batsmen who have the ability to build an innings and either set or chase a difficult target,” he said.
“Pakistan must select batsmen who have good technique, patience, and sound shot selection. It is the batsmen who take the team close to the target and give it the opportunity to win.”
“An established batsman at the crease must also guide the incoming batsmen, particularly the less experienced players, and encourage them to rotate the strike, play according to the situation, and avoid unnecessary risks.” Sadiq backed the decision of giving more opportunities to young pace-sensation Razaullah.
“Keeping Razaullah in both formats is a good decision. A player who is in form should be given a consistent run for at least two or three series,” Sadiq said.
“The biggest problem Pakistan is struggling with is batting. The coaches and selectors need to communicate clearly with the team, especially the top five batsmen. They need to work on their mindset, discipline, shot selection, and understanding of how to win matches,” Sadiq pointed out.
“When playing T20 cricket, especially while chasing a target, the objective should be to stay close to the required run rate. Ideally, you want two of your top batsmen at the crease during the final three overs.”
“They should concentrate on finding boundaries while rotating the strike through singles and twos, aiming for around 8–10 runs per over rather than constantly looking for sixes,” Sadiq explained.
“In modern cricket, batsmen and tail-enders seem more interested in scoring 18 runs in an over than in surviving and playing the last ball of the 20th over with a realistic chance of winning. Top-order batsmen are often responsible for losing matches because of reckless shots,” Sadiq said.
“This is where good coaching, the right mindset, and proper guidance are required, particularly on how to chase a target intelligently and stay close enough to give yourself a wining chance,” Sadiq said.
He said the PCB must seriously consider restructuring and properly scheduling the President’s Trophy and the domestic one-day competition.
“If the PCB establishes a strong and competitive domestic structure in these two formats, the T20 team will also automatically benefit from a stronger pool of technically sound and mentally prepared players,” Sadiq said. However, he said this requires the right people with the right mindset to run the system. “Our top players should also be required to play at least five matches in each domestic competition to be eligible for selection in the Test and ODI teams.
This would ensure that our best players remain connected to domestic cricket while also helping develop a stronger foundation for Pakistan cricket,” Sadiq signed off.
Pakistan are set to face Sri Lanka in a three-match T20I series starting on Friday at the Pindi Stadium in Rawalpindi.

Ironmouse asked for Fortnite’s 'Meow' artwork to be replaced after fans spotted Gemini AI watermark
Ironmouse has asked for artwork used in Fortnite to be replaced after fans spotted a Google Gemini AI watermark on the cover of her track “Meow”.
The artwork, created for “Meow” by Ironmouse, Sleeping Forest and HalaCG, was added to Fortnite last month. Players noticed a Gemini logo in the bottom-right corner of the image on October 2 and brought it to Ironmouse’s attention.
The artwork was subsequently replaced in Fortnite by October 5. The updated version no longer features the Gemini watermark.
After a fan asked on X whether the Club Ironmouse cover art was AI-made, Ironmouse said she was unaware of the watermark and that her team had contacted those responsible for the release.
“Nope i had no idea thanks for bringing it to my attention. my team has contacted the people in charge of this particular release and demanded it to be changed.”

“The artwork was provided to us by the artist and same that was used across all DSPs. Once it was changed by the artist, we also changed it out, same as the other streaming and digital platforms.”
The incident comes as Fortnite faces continued discussion around the use of AI in its artwork and development.
Players previously questioned a poster featuring a nine-toed character in a hammock, while Epic has also released a developer video showing how it experiments with AI during the concept phase.
In June, Fortnite players also called for AI disclaimers on skins after Epic revealed information about how it creates them.

title: Saved by the Bell    actor Dennis Haskins  cause of death revealed after death at 75
description: The actor died on September 27 at Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center in Burbank  California
content:
The actor died on September 27 at Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center in Burbank, California
Dennis Haskins, best known for playing Principal Richard Belding on Saved by the Bell, died from Parkinson’s disease, according to his death certificate obtained by TMZ .
The actor died on September 27 at Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center in Burbank, California, aged 75.
His death certificate also listed irritable bowel syndrome, depression, hypertension and benign prostatic hyperplasia as significant conditions.
Haskins’ death was previously confirmed by a longtime friend and caretaker and reported by WTVC , a news outlet in his hometown of Chattanooga, Tennessee.
His agent, Jay Schachter, also remembered the actor in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter.
“It’s a tragic loss. Everyone loved Mr. Belding, and those of us who got to know Dennis loved him even more. He was a great person, and he loved, I mean absolutely LOVED, his fans,” Schachter said.
“He always had time for them, no matter what. He was my client and dear friend for over 20 years, and I will miss him terribly. I’m heartbroken.”
A Burbank karaoke bar, Dimples, later revealed that Haskins had privately battled Parkinson’s disease for eight years. The establishment said he had chosen not to discuss his health publicly.
“He had been silent about his fight with Parkinson’s, among other health concerns, because he did not want the attention. He did not want to have to tell people,” the venue wrote in an Instagram post.
Haskins’ ex-wife, Sarah Quinones, later confirmed his Parkinson’s diagnosis to TMZ .
His last public appearance was at a Los Angeles Clippers and San Antonio Spurs game in December 2018.

Justin Timberlake has poked fun at his early 2000s beatboxing after a viral video revisited the singer’s habit of adding vocal percussion during *NSYNC performances.
The 45 year old singer responded to an Instagram Reel shared by Hannah Young on October 5. The comment prompted fans to share their own reactions, with some laughing at Timberlake’s response and others defending his beatboxing abilities.
Timberlake’s beatboxing became particularly memorable during *NSYNC’s 2001 song "Pop", released on the group’s album Celebrity . He also incorporated beatboxing into live performances and battles during the tour that followed.
The singer has previously reflected on the period himself. During a 2023 appearance on Hot Ones alongside former *NSYNC members, Timberlake described his beatboxing as "slightly regrettable". Lance Bass offered a different assessment, calling the performance style "iconic".
The latest exchange gives Timberlake an opportunity to revisit the era with humour, while the viral clip has prompted fans to reconsider a performance habit that was once a familiar part of the group’s live shows.

title: GTA 6 age ratings omit gambling despite drugs and graphic violence

content:
GTA 6’s age ratings list drugs and graphic violence but do not include gambling descriptor
GTA 6’s current age ratings indicate that Rockstar Games’ upcoming open-world game will feature drugs, sexual content and graphic violence, but gambling is notably absent from the listed descriptors.
The game’s classifications, as spotted by GTAVice , do not currently include a gambling descriptor despite identifying several other forms of adult content.
This could suggest that playable casino games will not be included in the base game, although the absence of the descriptor does not confirm that all forms of betting have been ruled out.
The ESRB has rated GTA 6 Mature 17+, citing blood and gore, intense violence, mature humour, nudity, strong language, strong sexual content, and drug and alcohol use.
PEGI’s rating similarly does not include a gambling descriptor. This differs from several previous Rockstar titles, including Red Dead Redemption, Red Dead Redemption 2, Red Dead Online and the PS5 version of GTA 5, which carry gambling-related classifications.
The ratings also detail the level of violence players can encounter. A PEGI description published before being removed referred to “detailed decapitation and dismemberment”.
The listing states that animals can be harmed, although they “do not produce the same injury detail that can be generated towards human characters.” Rockstar has previously confirmed more than 170 animals for GTA 6, including some with “legendary” status.
Drug use is also included in the ratings information. The description says players can carry cocaine and consume it directly from their hands, as well as use drugs from their inventory.

Seaver faces allegations involving threats and claims about his work as an arms dealer
Dolly Parton’s nephew, Bryan Seaver, is facing allegations involving threats against people connected to the late singer’s estate, with court filings detailing claims about his conduct.
Seaver, who had worked as Parton’s head of security, was removed from the role after a dispute with her longtime manager, Danny Nozell.
Reports later alleged that Seaver had made threats and attempted to seek money from Parton’s estate.
Court documents filed in Tennessee allege that Seaver’s communications with Nozell “was to cause fear and chaos to extort money for his personal gain.”
The filing also refers to an email Seaver allegedly sent to an entertainment attorney on September 3, in which he claimed to have sold $27 million worth of ammunition to Haitian police.
“I’m literally an international arms dealer and mercenary,” Seaver allegedly said.
The legal filing also accuses Seaver of making a “threat of continuing retaliation” and quotes him as saying, “I am vengeance for my people for the next 50 years. I have no debt. I only own swords and guns.”
Parton’s estate entity, She’s Alive , LLC, claimed Seaver “sought to extract money from SAL and Dolly Parton’s trusts through an obscene, deliberate and escalating campaign of threats.”
Seaver has rejected the temporary restraining order, calling it “Spurious, and simply a publicity stunt,” according to ABC News.
Meanwhile, Parton’s sister Freida defended Seaver, writing , “We all love Bryan, just as we all love each other.”

title: UK minister wraps up Pakistan visit focused on trade  security and education
description: Doughty also meets members of civil society  reaffirms UK   s commitment to human rights and democratic freedoms
content:
Doughty also meets members of civil society, reaffirms UK’s commitment to human rights and democratic freedoms
UK Minister of State for the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan Stephen Doughty concluded his first visit to Pakistan since taking on the role, with discussions focused on economic growth, trade, regional stability, education and migration.
According to the statement issued on Wednesday, during the visit, Doughty met senior Pakistani political leaders to discuss how the UK and Pakistan could strengthen cooperation on shared priorities, including growth and trade, regional security, stability in Afghanistan and counter-terrorism.
“The UK and Pakistan share deep and historic ties, built on the connections between our people, businesses and institutions,” Doughty said.
“My first visit to Pakistan has been focused on strengthening this and our work together across a range of issues that deliver for people in both our countries — from growth and trade to education, security and regional stability,” he said.
The statement further stated that the minister held talks with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, and Minister for Law, Justice and Human Rights Azam Nazeer Tarar to discuss growth, trade, regional security, including stability in Afghanistan, counter-terrorism cooperation and reducing the risk of escalation in the region.
Doughty also joined Pakistani and British education leaders to discuss the next phase of cooperation between universities in both countries, including expanding access to UK qualifications and building links in areas such as STEM, healthcare and technology, it added.
Read: British High Commission celebrates start of Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games
“I have also seen the huge potential for further cooperation on education, including the strong growth in partnerships between British and Pakistani universities, supporting young people to gain the skills they need for the future,” Doughty said.
More than 15,000 Pakistani students studied for UK qualifications in Pakistan through transnational education (TNE) in 2024-25, an increase of 83% over the past decade, the statement added.
Pakistan is now the fourth-largest host country globally for UK transnational education, with UK institutions accounting for around 65% of Pakistan’s TNE market, it added.
On education, the minister took part in discussions with Pakistan’s Higher Education Commission, university leaders and the British Council on the future of transnational education and how to deepen links between institutions in both countries.
The statement further said that the British Council planned to bring a delegation of UK universities to Pakistan next March to explore further links, with an ambition to see more than 100 British universities working in partnership with institutions in Pakistan by the end of the decade.
Doughty also met members of civil society and reaffirmed the UK’s commitment to human rights and democratic freedoms. He met politicians from across Pakistan’s political spectrum to discuss the UK-Pakistan relationship.
The UK and Pakistan share strong people-to-people ties, with around 1.7 million people of Pakistani heritage living in the UK, while trade between the two countries is worth around £5.5 billion each year and growing, the press release concluded.

title: Russia hits Ukraine with drones and missiles  killing at least 15
description: Two people were killed in the capital Kyiv  four in the northern city of Pryluki and two in the central Poltava region
content:
One Russian missile hit an apartment ‌block in the northern city of Pryluky, killing at least nine people
Russia pounded Ukraine with waves of missiles and drones on ​Wednesday, killing at least 15 people and hitting residential buildings, industrial facilities and infrastructure, Ukrainian officials said.
One Russian missile hit an apartment ‌block in the northern city of Pryluky, killing at least nine people, including three children, regional governor Vyacheslav Chaus said.
Dozens of rescuers picked through the rubble at the site where several sections of the five-story building collapsed, Reuters video showed.
Emergency workers used ladders to get to the upper floors of what remained of the building. Around 40 people were wounded, the governor said.
Big jump in reported drone interceptions
President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said six other people were killed in Kyiv, Oleksandria and Kremenchuk during the heavy overnight attack.
"This was one of the most ​vile strikes: 70 missiles in total, many of them ballistic," Zelenskiy said on the Telegram app. "One of the key targets was ⁠our energy infrastructure. The Russians wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively."
Russia's defence ministry said its forces had carried out a "massive strike" on military-industrial facilities in Kyiv and other ​Ukrainian regions, using high-precision land-, sea- and air-launched weapons, as well as drones.
Read: Russian strikes hit Kyiv during Merz's visit
Ukraine's air force said it had downed just over 80% of the 46 jet-powered drones launched ​by Russia — a sharp increase from recent weeks when, on average, air defences took down 50% to 60%.
Since the summer, Russia has used increasing numbers of the new high-velocity drones in round-the-clock attacks on Kyiv and other cities, stretching Ukraine's air defences, which have struggled to cope with their speed.
The air force did not explain the jump in the interception rate and did not immediately ​respond to requests for comment.
Zelenskiy said that the Russian ballistic missiles remained the major challenge for Ukraine, adding that he and his team were "every day looking for ​Patriot (missile interception) systems that can and must protect people's lives".
The US-made Patriot system is the only weapon in Ukraine's arsenal capable of stopping high-velocity ballistic missiles but tight global supplies have been ‌drained by the ⁠war on Iran this year as well as the Ukraine conflict.
Ukraine's energy ministry said that it had started to roll out partial emergency power cuts in five Ukrainian regions due to the attacks.
Russia's defence ministry said its targets included sites where Ukrainian defence company Fire Point manufactures and stores its Flamingo cruise missiles and medium- and long-range drones in Kyiv as well as regions of Kyiv, Chernihiv, Kirovohrad, Dnipropetrovsk, Poltava and Kharkiv.
Last week, Zelenskiy said Ukraine had fired its first domestically made ballistic missile in combat, ​produced by Fire Point.
In an interview with Reuters ​last week, Zelenskiy said he expected ⁠the company to have a longer-range FP-9 missile ready by the autumn. The company has said that weapon will be able to reach Moscow.
Zelenskiy said Ukrainian troops hit four targets in Russia over the past 24 hours, including ​two Russian oil facilities and a training ground in the Perm, Samara, and Astrakhan regions.
In the Reuters interview, Zelenskiy said ​Ukraine would hit Russia's ⁠energy assets in response to Moscow's escalating strikes on civilian infrastructure.
Many Kyiv residents took shelter in the city's deep underground metro stations as warnings of the upcoming attacks were shared by Ukrainian officials and military intelligence.
Read more: Russian strikes batter Ukraine's energy grid
Several loud explosions reverberated through the capital during the night, Reuters witnesses said.
"The metro is better, because we live on the 9th floor of a ⁠high-rise, and ​it's really scary when you're on the 9th floor and missiles are flying at you," Lesia, ​a 49-year-old Kyiv resident, told Reuters.
Ukrainian officials said Russian ballistic missiles targeted Kyiv in addition to the drones.
Overnight air strikes on the southeastern city of Dnipro damaged an industrial facility, transport infrastructure in Zaporizhzhia and ​apartment buildings in Kremenchuk, regional officials said on the Telegram messaging app.

title: PSX edges 120 points higher as profit taking fuels volatility
description: KSE 100 settles at 168 580 as cautious sentiment emerges  oil prices remain above  100 amid Mideast supply risks
content:
KSE-100 settles at 168,580 as cautious sentiment emerges; oil prices remain above $100 amid Mideast supply risks
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) struggled to hold early gains on Wednesday as a cautious tone emerged in the latter part of the session, although a late recovery helped the benchmark close marginally higher. It settled 120.30 points, or 0.07%, higher at 168,580.41.
The benchmark KSE-100 Index opened in positive territory but turned volatile later in the session as profit-taking erased much of its morning gains. During the session, it hit an intraday high of 169,271.99 and a low of 168,065.87.
Market sentiment was influenced by continued hopes of renewed talks between the government and the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), although the opposition party has so far described Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s proposal as a "mere offer" and called for a formal approach to its parliamentary leaders. The prospect of political engagement provided some support but failed to prevent the market from losing momentum as the session progressed.
The market also tracked global oil developments, with crude prices rising and Brent futures holding above $100 a barrel amid continuing Middle East supply risks and a storm heading towards oil-producing regions in the United States. Brent crude futures rose $1.22, or 1.21%, to $101.80 a barrel by 1008 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 46 cents, or 0.51%, to $89.90.
Read: PSX rallies over easing political woes
According to KASB KTrade’s equity trader Ahmed Sheraz, the KSE-100 Index closed marginally higher at 168,580, gaining 120 points (+0.07%0 day-on-day (DoD), in a mixed and cautious session with 244 million shares traded, while overall index contributions remained mixed.
Sector-wise, oil and gas and fertiliser segment remained under pressure, while technology stocks provided support. Among key names, Mari Energies, Meezan Bank and Lucky Cement closed negative whereas UBL, Systems, Pakistan State Oil and PTC finished in the green. The muted index performance reflected a lack of clear direction despite healthy market activity.
Going forward, elevated international oil prices remain the key overhang, with Brent trading between $101-103 barrel per day, raising concerns for Pakistan as an oil-importing economy. The prolonged uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz could keep volatility elevated, while the relatively cooler domestic political environment offers some relief as government-opposition talks may potentially resume.
“Overall, we expect the market to remain choppy and directionless until greater clarity emerges on the geopolitical and oil-price front,” Sheraz wrote.
Overall, trading volume rose to 586.8 million shares from Tuesday’s 432 million, while the value of traded shares stood at Rs22.3 billion. Of the 501 companies traded in the ready market, 272 stocks closed higher, 184 declined and 45 remained unchanged.
K-Electric became the volume leader with trading in 82.7 million shares, gaining Rs0.45 to close at Rs6.04.

title: Kane eyes Ronaldo record after matching England cap mark
description: The 33 year old matches Shilton   s record at Wembley
content:
The 33-year-old matches Shilton’s record at Wembley
Harry Kane refused to rule out catching Cristiano Ronaldo at the top of the international goalscoring charts after netting twice against the Czech Republic to celebrate his record-equalling 125th England cap.
The captain matched Peter Shilton's men's record at Wembley on Tuesday, scoring his 90th and 91st international goals in a 3-0 win -- and has no intention of retiring any time soon.
Ronaldo, 41, tops the global all-time charts with 146 goals for Portugal.
"We'll see how far we can get," said Kane, who is England's record goalscorer. "We're starting with 50-odd goals. It's an awful long way away right now but who knows? I'm in great shape.
"I've said before that some of the players who I've played went into their late 30s and are still at the highest level and even 40s now. It's season by season with me. As long as I feel like I can help the team... I'll be around."
The striker said equalling former goalkeeper Shilton's haul of England caps was "beyond my wildest dreams", 11 years after his debut.
"Amazing, he deserves the stage, he deserves the praise," said England boss Thomas Tuchel, whose team won three of their four Nations League matches during the international break.
Kane, 33, who scored 79 seconds into his debut in 2015, said he had always demanded the highest standards of himself.
"I always had a lot of self-belief," he added. "I was always willing to maybe do more than others and just push myself.... I combined my talent that I had with a lot of hard work and self-belief and a lot of dedication."
And the former Tottenham player, in the running to win the Ballon d'Or in London later this month, said he still had room to improve despite his vast experience.
"I'm coming off the back of my best season ever as a player and I've started this season as good as I did last season," he said.
"I'm in a good place and for me right now, it's just pushing myself and seeing how far I can get."
Kane, who left Spurs as their record goalscorer, has hit new heights since moving to Bayern, breaking a 49-year-old record to become the fastest player to score 100 Bundesliga goals, in his 98th league game.
"I'm not going to stop," he added. "I'm going to keep pushing and see where it takes me. Maybe in 10 years or so, we'll see where that ceiling is at."

title: IMF chief warns global economy faces energy shocks  AI demand
description: IMF chief warns global economy faces energy shocks  AI demand
content:
Global public debt tracks to soon exceed 100pc of GDP, reaching its highest levels since World War II, Georgieva says
The global economy faces dual pressures from a negative energy supply shock and a positive artificial intelligence (AI) demand shock, the head of the International Monetary Fund said on Wednesday.
Kristalina Georgieva delivered a speech in Singapore ahead of the upcoming annual meetings in Thailand, highlighting that the global economy must navigate three major crosscurrents, which are the rapid arrival of AI, persistently high energy prices and record levels of public debt.

She noted that global public debt tracks to soon exceed 100 per cent of the gross domestic product, reaching its highest levels since the end of World War II.
Advanced economies stand out as the worst offenders with some of the highest gross debt loads, Georgieva said.
The managing director pointed out that opposite forces pull the global economy in two different directions. Georgieva warned that oil prices remain around $100 per barrel due to transport costs and other risks.
She emphasised that natural gas supply from the Gulf remains severely impaired because shipping through the Strait of Hormuz f aces threats .

On the technology front, Georgieva stated that AI hardware and related products now account for more than 10pc of world goods trade. She added that AI could eventually deliver up to 0.5pc of extra world growth annually if countries manage it correctly.
Georgieva urged economic policymakers to stop delaying necessary actions and implement credible fiscal consolidation plans. She also advised central banks in various countries to maintain a prudently hawkish bias in their monetary policies because the AI building boom, energy shocks and high public debt fuel inflation.

title: US beat Canada to wrap up four win international break
description: Teenager Justin Ellis scores second goal in 1 0 win over Canada
content:
Teenager Justin Ellis scores second goal in 1-0 win over Canada
Head coach Mauricio Pochettino expressed optimism for the United States's future as a soccer powerhouse after teen Justin Ellis scored the only goal against Canada on Tuesday to cap a flawless international window with four wins from four friendlies.
The 1-0 win lacked the dynamism, fluidity and multiple goals of wins against Mexico, Chile and Peru, but was another vindication for Pochettino's policy of blooding fresh talent in the post-World Cup window.
Nineteen-year-old Ellis, who had scored on debut against Peru, bundled in an Alex Freeman strike midway through the first half, while Luc de Fougerolles came closest for Canada by hitting the crossbar after the break.
Across four games, seven of 12 US goals were scored by teenagers, with debuts for 13 new players as Pochettino eyes the future following a disappointing last-16 exit at this summer's home World Cup.
"For sure, the future with these young talented players, plus the senior players that we have, I think we have a very good mix," said Pochettino, describing a burgeoning US pool of youthful talent as "deep".
"I hope we can guide this group of players to reach our best level, and compete in our best way, trying to be with the big national teams in the future."
Pochettino had made six changes to his starting line-up. Ellis's goal was the only US shot on target, with a high-pressing Canada spending most of the game on the front foot but unable to break through.
"It was a really difficult opponent... We made changes, we kept the level. I think we managed really well, we competed really well," said Pochettino.
The US got off to a slow start, sitting deep and soaking up a barrage of fouls from an evidently motivated Canada team.
The Canadians had the early shots, though efforts from both Tani Oluwaseyi and Jacob Shaffelburg were from range and barely threatened.
A foul on teen Ellis outside the box prompted a bout of shoving between players, and Pochettino grew enraged on the sideline as the referee allowed several physical challenges to go unchecked.
Ellis was left limping badly but was determined to remain on the pitch, and his doggedness paid off.
In the 29th minute, Alex Freeman picked up the ball on the right flank, played a one-two with Malik Tillman, and surged into the box.
He appeared to shoot, but Ellis popped up to steer his wayward effort into the back of the net.
A slightly ill-tempered first-half ended with two yellow cards -- Oluwaseyi and Gio Reyna -- and Alex Freeman blazing a volley way over the crossbar.
Ellis was hooked at half-time for fellow teen Julian Hall, kick-starting a raft of changes from both sides.
Cole Campbell, 20, became the 13th US debutant of the post-World Cup international window.
Canada pushed forward, and their best chance came in the 63rd minute.
Substitute Mathieu Choiniere whipped in a free kick that De Fougerolles smartly volleyed, but his shot was tipped onto the crossbar at point-blank range by Brian Schwake.
Minutes later, Nathan Saliba flashed a cross across the face of goal but nobody was there to gather, and Canada's chances began to dwindle as the game petered out.

title: Three remaining MT Honour 25 crew members arrive in Karachi
description: Rescued sailors received by  Sindh Governor Nehal Hashmi  Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab at  Jinnah International Airport
content:
Rescued sailors received by Sindh Governor Nehal Hashmi, Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab at Jinnah International Airport
The three remaining MT Honour 25 crew members rescued from Somali pirates arrived in Karachi on Wednesday and were received by Sindh Governor Nehal Hashmi and Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab at Jinnah International Airport.
While welcoming the rescued sailors upon their arrival, Wahab said that all necessary measures would be taken to ensure the crew members’ well-being, adding that while it was a "day of happiness" for those families whose loved ones were returning, it was also a day of mourning for those families who lost their loved ones.
Hashmi said that it was a "national responsibility" to bring back the Pakistani crew members, adding that the entire nation should encourage them upon their repatriation.
"The prime minister showed personal interest in this and was updated by the minute on developments".
Earlier in the day, Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said that the remaining three crew members of MT Honour 25 were en route to Karachi from Addis Ababa and would be reunited with their families.
On Sunday , an aircraft carrying four injured crew members and the remains of three MT Honour 25 sailors landed in Karachi's Jinnah International Airport
In a post on X, the foreign minister wrote, “I am pleased to share that the remaining three crew members of MT Honour 25 (Mr Imran Ali, Mr Husain Yousuf and Mr Muhammad Yasin) are en route to safely return home to Karachi from Addis Ababa later today and will be reunited with their families. InshAllah.”
I am pleased to share that the remaining three crew members of MT Honour 25 (Mr Imran Ali, Mr Husain Yousuf and Mr Muhammad Yasin) are enroute to safely return home to Karachi from Addis Ababa later today and will be reunited with their families. InshAllah 🤲🏼 Our Ambassador in…
“Our ambassador in Addis Ababa met the three crew members and ensured that they were provided with all necessary facilities and services during their stay in Addis Ababa,” he added.
He further added that the foreign office and the Government of Pakistan, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, made every effort to secure the safe return of all our crew members. I am grateful to all those who supported these efforts.
“While we welcome the safe return of our people, we remain deeply saddened by the loss of three Pakistani crew members. May Allah grant them eternal peace and give strength to their families,” he added.
Pakistan remains firmly committed to working with international partners to combat piracy and ensure the safety and security of seafarers and maritime routes.
Read: Four Pakistani crew members from hijacked MT Honour 25 to arrive in Karachi tomorrow: Dar
On Sunday, the four injured Pakistani crew members of MT Honour 25, along with the remains of three others killed, were flown aboard Ethiopian Airlines flight ET 694 from Addis Ababa to Karachi on Sunday, the Foreign Office (FO) said.
Pakistan’s Ambassadors to Djibouti and Ethiopia saw off the four injured Pakistani crew members of MT Honour 25, Usman Ghani, Aqeel Khan, Ameen bin Shams and Yasir Khan, along with the mortal remains of Rafi Ullah Khan, Syed Kashif Umer and Mahmood Ahmad Ansari, from Addis Ababa.… pic.twitter.com/t0x4VqNsuK
Sindh Governor Nehal Hashmi welcomed the injured Pakistanis upon their repatriation and attended the funeral prayers of Mahmood Ahmed Ansari and expressed condolences to his family.
Senior government officials such as Sindh Local Government Minister Nasir Hussain Shah, Sindh Labour and Human Resources Minister Saeed Ghani, and MQM-P leader Farooq Sattar also received the injured upon their return to the country.
Two of the injured people were from Karachi, while one was from Sahiwal and one from Peshawar. The two injured individuals from Peshawar and Sahiwal would depart from Karachi for their hometowns later on Sunday.
Rafi Ullah Khan's mortal remains were handed over to the family, and his funeral prayers would be held after Isha prayers.
Read more: FO expresses condolences over deaths of five crew members in Somalia rescue operation
The oil tanker Honour 25, sailing under the Somali flag from Oman to Somalia, was hijacked by pirates on April 21. There were 17 crew members aboard, 10 of them Pakistani nationals. The families of the Pakistani hostages spent months seeking the safe release of their loved ones, staging peaceful protests and repeatedly approaching government authorities.
During their captivity, the pirates initially demanded a ransom of $3 million, which was later reduced to $1.9 million and subsequently to $1 million. All the Pakistani crew members who were killed or injured were from different areas of Karachi.
The pirates came under pressure during a rescue operation and, while retreating from the vessel, opened indiscriminate fire on the abducted crew before fleeing the ship. Five sailors were killed, including three Pakistanis — Second Officer Kashif Umar, Third Engineer Mahmood Ansari and Boiler Rafiullah. The other two deceased crew members were an Indian sailor, Tanveer, and the chief engineer from Myanmar.
Four sailors were injured — Usman, Yasir, Ameen and Vicky from Indonesia — while Hussain Yousuf, Imran Ali and Yaseen remained safe. The two surviving Pakistani crew members later contacted the Ansar Burney Welfare Trust in Karachi using the ship captain’s mobile phone and provided details of the incident.
Puntland police said the Honour 25 had 18,500 barrels of oil on board when it was hijacked. The police had been pursuing three hijacked vessels off the Somali coast and had also rescued another oil tanker, Sibu 1, on Friday. However, 28 of the 41 pirates arrested during that operation later escaped while being transferred to jail, with several Puntland security officials accusing local police of complicity.
The Gulf of Aden and Somalia coasts have seen a resurgence in piracy since April, with at least 15 attacks recorded this year, the highest number since 2013, according to figures from the International Maritime Organisation.

title: SC dismisses Sindh review plea against acquittal in Baldia factory fire case
description: Court also dismisses petition seeking deletion of remarks concerning MQM
content:
Court also dismisses petition seeking deletion of remarks concerning MQM
The Supreme Court (SC) on Wednesday dismissed the review petition filed by the Sindh government against the acquittal of the accused in the Baldia factory fire case.
On July 1, the Sindh government filed a review petition in the SC’s Karachi Registry against the judgment ordering the acquittal and release of the accused in the Baldia factory fire case. The review petition was filed by Sindh Prosecutor General Shabbir Shah. In the petition, the Sindh government requested the SC to reconsider its judgment.
On June 10, the SC acquitted two MQM workers, Rehman Bhola and Zubair Chariya, in the case, setting aside the death sentences awarded to them by a trial court and later upheld by the Sindh High Court (SHC). The court had set aside the judgments of the Anti-Terrorism Court by extending to them the benefit of the doubt.
A three-member bench comprising Justice Malik Shehzad Ahmed Khan, Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi and Justice Shakeel Ahmad heard the review petitions. Additional Prosecutor General Sindh Saleem Akhtar appeared before the court and presented arguments.
The court also dismissed the petition seeking deletion of remarks concerning the MQM.
Read: Sindh govt challenges SC acquittal verdict in Baldia factory fire case
Earlier, the petition filed by the Sindh government raised the legal question of whether Article 188 of the Constitution applies to a judgment that is “contrary to the facts and the law”. The Sindh government argued that the judgment “suffers from the defect of ignoring eyewitness, medical and other evidence”.
The petition also questioned whether, under the Anti-Terrorism Act, the legal heirs of the victims could challenge the acquittal of convicted persons. It further raised objections regarding the application of Articles 4 and 17 of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984.
According to the petition, the judgment also ignored the evidence of injured witnesses and experts regarding the use of chemicals to start the fire.
On September 11, 2012, more than 260 workers were burnt alive in the multi-storey building of the Ali Enterprises garment factory in Baldia Town in what was the worst industrial disaster in the country’s history.
In 2023, the SHC dismissed appeals challenging the death sentences awarded to the two MQM activists after a special Anti-Terrorism Court had upheld the capital punishment handed down to them.
Read more : Chemical used in Baldia factory fire was ‘highly’ inflammable, says researcher
In its 46-page judgment, the SHC said the forensic report clearly showed that the factory fire had not been caused by a short circuit. It further held that evidence and witness statements confirmed that Zubair Chariya had set fire to the factory.
According to the case record, Abdul Rehman was associated with the MQM as a sector in-charge, while Zubair was an active worker of the town municipality. Both were present at the factory when the fire broke out.

title: WADA seeks tough anti doping stance from Kenya
description: More than 140 Kenyan athletes have been suspended for doping since 2017
content:
More than 140 Kenyan athletes have been suspended for doping since 2017
Kenya as future hosts of the World Athletics Championship must strive for zero tolerance for drugs in sport, the World Anti Doping Agency (WADA) boss said on Tuesday.
Despite a long-running doping crisis, Kenya were last month awarded the 2029 World Athletics Championships, the first time the event will be held in Africa.
"Kenya proudly calls itself the Home of Champions. But for that home to remain respected and credible, it must also be clean," WADA chief Witold Banka said at the end of a three-day visit to the east African country.
"That is why Kenya needs a strong culture of clean sport, zero tolerance for doping, and a more determined approach to preventing and fighting doping.
"Kenya is a great sporting nation full of great athletes and you become, the more important area of sport when it comes to organising major sporting events.
"It's a big honour for you but it's a bigger responsibility as well and brings pressure and big requirements from our side as well", Banka added.
Banka said that joint cooperation with Kenyan authorities would help lay the foundations for a cleaner sport.
"WADA or ADAK (Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya) alone cannot achieve its vision if we do not cooperate with those who have the power to go against those who are producing, smuggling and trafficking dangerous steroids to your athletes," he said.
"We've found a common understanding and we are on the same track and there's a clear goal within Kenya for zero tolerance for doping policy and it has to be established immediately with joint actions and a more aggressive approach to those who are destroying the image of the country and the reputation of the athletes."
More than 140 Kenyan athletes, mainly long-distance runners, have been suspended by the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) since 2017.
