title: Spain fight back to beat Croatia
description: Kane adds to record for England
content:
Spain fought back against Croatia to win 2-1 in Split on Tuesday and remain perfect in Nations League Group A3 while Harry Kane continued his hot form as England beat the Czech Republic 3-0 to stay second.
The victory in Split preserved Spain's long unbeaten run and ensured they will finish in the top two in the four-team group and advance to the quarter-finals.
England stayed three points behind Spain with a home win and will advance to the last four if they do not lose their next game at home to Croatia by eight or more goals.
In their previous match, Croatia capitulated 7-0 to England up the Dalmatian coast at Rijeka. Because of a ban brought on by persistent fan racism, that crowd was made up of 6,000 children under the age of 14.
In a very different atmosphere, Croatia gave a spikier performance and took the lead after 17 minutes. Unai Simon dived to save a low drive from Igor Matanovic but only pushed the ball into the air. Ivan Perisic, a former teammate of Kane at Tottenham, nodded the ball home.
While Spain dominated first-half possession, Croatia created the most dangerous chances and Matanovic could have doubled the lead.
Spain's pressure told after 61 minutes, Dani Olmo collected a poor clearance and rolled the ball to substitute Mikel Merino who had space to pick his spot.
Perisic had earned a yellow card for an excited lunge soon after scoring. That turned into a costly sending off when he was booked again after 79 minutes for a push on Marc Cucurella.
With a minute of normal time left, Merino found space in the box to turn and drive home the winner.
"Another game in which it was my turn to score from the bench," Merino told TVE, adding: "I'll go out there with the best possible attitude even while frustrated about not being able to play more... but this team is a family and that always shows."
The win stretched Spain's unbeaten run to 42 games. The one blemish in that run for the European and World Champions was a penalty shootout loss to Portugal after the last Nations League final had ended in a draw.
"There are days like today when the streak can become complicated," said Merino.
England lost their opener at home to Spain, when Kane missed a penalty that would have salvaged a draw, but have since won three games. Their veteran striker scored once away to the Czechs and twice in Croatia.
On Tuesday, as he equalled the England appearance record held by goalkeeper Peter Shilton with a 125th cap, Kane stretched his national scoring record to 91 with another double.
"Perfect night for me personally and also for the team," Kane told ITV on the pitch. "An extremely proud evening."
England were presented with their opener after 27 minutes when Vladimir Coufal, perhaps imagining an attacker behind him, smashed an England cross into his own net.
Kane finished off a quick, clever England attack by wrong-footing the goalkeeper from close range after 40 minutes. He hit the crossbar early in the second half and then headed home a corner after 57 minutes.
"You saw some fantastic football from us tonight," said Kane.
"As a striker you're just licking your lips and waiting for your opportunities."
Kane received praise from team-mate Jude Bellingham.
"He's playing at a level where it's pretty unmatched, when you look across the world," said the Real Madrid star.
"He's scoring goals for fun, he's still dropping in deep and delivering those passes in behind and wide and contributing in so many areas of the pitch."
In League B, Ryan Christie coolly flicked the ball between his legs to score a 31st-minute opener for Scotland at home to Slovenia but Aljosa Matko and Danijel Sturm hit back after half time to give the visitors a 2-1 win.
Leaders Switzerland ensured they will finish in the top two after they beat North Macedonia 3-0 in Lucerne, Fabian Rieder gave the hosts a first-half lead and Johan Manzambi and Dan Ndoye added late goals.

title: US arrests person in connection to Canada school shooting  officials say
description: Suspect accused of advising attacker  sending money  agreeing to live stream mass shooting that killed nine
content:
Suspect accused of advising attacker, sending money, agreeing to live stream mass shooting that killed nine
United States authorities arrested a person in Washington state on Tuesday who they accuse of providing advice and offering to live stream a deadly mass shooting carried out earlier this year in Canada.
James Cody Bryant, 30, was detained on a charge of conspiracy to murder people in a foreign country in connection to the shooting at Tumbler Ridge , according to the Department of Justice. The charge carries a penalty of up to life in prison.
Bryant was in repeated contact with the shooter, Jesse Van Rootselaar, offering technical advice, sending money, including for the shoes to be used during the attack, and agreeing to live stream the event, law enforcement officials said.
"James Cody Bryant had the information and ability to alert law enforcement and even discussed that possibility with the shooter, but he chose not to, and he encouraged and offered assistance to a murderer," Acting US Attorney for the Western District of Washington Neil Floyd told reporters.
Court records did not immediately list an attorney for Bryant.
Nine people, primarily children, were killed in the school shooting in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, in one of Canada's worst mass shootings.
Read: Philippine student live-streamed fatal school shooting before taking own life, official say
Van Rootselaar, 18, who had suffered a series of mental health problems, killed her mother and stepbrother at home before shooting dead a teacher and five young students at her former school in Tumbler Ridge, a settlement of around 2,400 in the Canadian Rockies, according to police. Van Rootselaar, who police said was born a male but began identifying as a woman, then died by suicide.
Bryant, who officials said they understood was also born a man but identified as female, agreed to live stream a feed of the attack and broadcast it "in a way that would maximise notoriety for the shooter," Mike Herrington, FBI Seattle special agent in charge, said.
The live stream on Twitch was shut down after about 20 seconds, officials said.
"Without Bryant's misplaced loyalty and willingness to operate the live stream, we don't ultimately know if the shooter would have gone through with the crime," Herrington said. "We certainly know the shooter was concerned that not enough people would see the live stream without Bryant broadcasting it, and was depending on Bryant to amplify the live stream because the shooter did not have many followers on social media."

title: Karachi to host National Cycling Championship
description: Three day event to feature elite  junior  para cycling and masters riders
content:
Three-day event to feature elite, junior, para-cycling and masters riders
The tenth edition of the National Road Cycling Championship will be held in Karachi from October 9 to 11, bringing together cyclists from across Pakistan to compete in men's, women's, junior, para-cycling and masters categories.
Pakistan Cycling Federation (PCF) said on Wednesday that the championship will begin at 9am on Friday at Bahria Town Karachi, with events continuing over three days. The closing ceremony and prize distribution will take place at 4 pm on October 11.
Cyclists representing Army, Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC), Gilgit-Baltistan Scouts, Gilgit-Baltistan, Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan and Islamabad will take part, along with riders from other institutions and cycling teams.
Kareng Aidak and the Pakistan Cycling Academy are among the other teams which will feature in the event.
The PCF has also introduced an Open Masters category, giving cyclists from Karachi and other parts of the country an opportunity to compete at the national level.
Para-cycling has been included in the championship to provide cyclists with disabilities an opportunity to compete nationally and showcase their abilities.
The federation said accommodation and other arrangements had been made at Bahria Town Karachi for cyclists and officials travelling from different parts of the country.
PCF president Syed Azhar Ali Shah said national-level sporting competitions were important for engaging young people in positive activities and promoting cycling in Pakistan.
"In the present circumstances, continuing sporting activities and providing young athletes with opportunities to demonstrate their abilities at the national level is the need of the hour," Shah said.
He also appealed to media organisations across the country to provide comprehensive coverage of the championship, saying media support would help promote sport, encourage cyclists and highlight the achievements of Pakistani athletes.

title: Rising terrorism in K P must be stopped  at all costs   PM Shehbaz
description: PM says development of AJK  G B and prosperity of their people are among government   s priorities
content:
Says development of AJK, G-B and prosperity of their people are among government's priorities
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday said rising terrorism in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) must be stopped “at all costs”, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said.
According to the statement issued by the PMO, the prime minister made the remarks during a meeting with Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan (G-B) Engineer Amir Muqam in Islamabad.
During the meeting, matters relating to Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), G-B and K-P were discussed during the meeting. “Rising terrorism in K-P must be stopped at all costs,” the prime minister said.
He said the government wanted K-P to develop like other parts of the country and appreciated the sacrifices made by the people of the province in the fight against terrorism.
وزیرِ اعظم محمد شہباز شریف سے وفاقی وزیر امور کشمیر و گلگت بلتستان انجینئر کی آج اسلام آباد میں ملاقات ہوئی. ملاقات میں آزاد جموں و کشمیر، گلگت بلتستان اور خیبر پختونخوا سے متعلق امور پر تبادلہ خیال کیا گیا۔ وزیرِ اعظم نے کہا کہ خیبر پختونخوا میں بڑھتی ہوئی دھشت گردی کو ہر قیمت… pic.twitter.com/SwzomZFzyv
The statement further added that the federal minister briefed the prime minister on ongoing matters and progress in AJK and G-B. The prime minister directed that effective measures continue to ensure the welfare and development of the people of AJK and G-B and the provision of basic facilities.
PM Shehbaz said the development of AJK and G-B and the prosperity of their people were among the government’s priorities.
Read: Five terrorists killed, two wounded in North Waziristan operation: security sources
Terrorism has risen in K-P over the past month, with a series of attacks targeting police, government officials and civilians across the province.
On October 7 , police foiled an attack by Fitna al-Khawarij on the Shadipur police post in Kohat. Four police personnel were injured in the exchange of fire and shifted to hospital, while police continued to pursue the attackers in a search-and-strike operation.
On September 28 , three traffic wardens were martyred, and at least one other was seriously injured when unidentified armed men opened fire on a traffic police vehicle in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's (K-P) Wazirabad area of Tank district, District Police Officer Abdul Samad said.
On September 26 , at least 12 people were killed and 35 others injured when a blast struck a joint checkpoint near Aman Mela in the Darazinda area of Dera Ismail Khan, with the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) claiming responsibility for the attack, police said. Radio Pakistan reported that the blast was extremely powerful after a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device (VBIED) rammed into the checkpost.
On September 18 , at least 21 people, including 15 police personnel and six civilians, were killed in the blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers, according to an initial incident report issued by the DHQ Hospital Kohat medical superintendent and the district health officer.

title: Govt will not accept demands by  holding state hostage   Sanaullah warns PTI
description: Urges return to talks  defends counterterrorism operations and rejects claims of a new operation or IDP influx
content:
Urges return to talks, defends counterterrorism operations and rejects claims of a new operation or IDP influx
Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said on Wednesday that the government would not accept political demands through pressure tactics or attempts to “hold the state hostage”, as the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf maintained that its long march would continue and only Imran Khan could decide when to call it off.
“I want to say this clearly today that no demand can be accepted by holding the state hostage or pursuing the path of political instability,” Sanaullah said while addressing a press conference in Islamabad.
He urged PTI to set aside what he described as its politics of instability and prioritise the national interest by resolving differences through dialogue.
Sanaullah said the government remained willing to hold talks but warned that political demands could not be accepted through pressure tactics.
“They should renounce political instability and not give priority to their personal political agenda over the national interest. They should sit for talks and resolve these issues through negotiations. However, despite our desire for talks, under no circumstances should they try to hold the state hostage to have their political demands accepted. This tactic will not be allowed,” he added.
حکومت کی جانب سے مذاکرات کے دروازے کھلے ہیں، رانا ثناء اللہ #RanaSanaullah #Dialogue #Negotiations #PakistanPolitics pic.twitter.com/qPVL5foXGa
The adviser also accused PTI of introducing a culture of political intolerance, instability and abusive rhetoric into national politics since 2011. “Unfortunately, PTI has remained successful, to some extent, in both of these objectives,” Sanaullah said.
He argued that political tolerance, which he described as once being a hallmark of Pakistani politics, had been replaced by a culture of abusive and below-the-belt political discourse.
Sanaullah said the trend remained visible in traditional and social media and had also affected the atmosphere surrounding the government’s recent negotiations with PTI.
He further accused PTI of pursuing a consistent agenda of political instability since its 2014 protest in Islamabad. “Political instability began in 2014 and now 12 years have passed. PTI, as a political party, has consistently carried forward this agenda,” he said.
Referring to PTI’s 126-day sit-in in Islamabad in 2014, Sanaullah said: “Since then, laying siege to Islamabad has remained one of PTI’s strong points.”
The adviser added that the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) government was using all its resources for its agenda, arguing that over the past two years they had been used generally, over the past two months specifically, and over the past three days particularly.
ایک طرف شہداء کے جنازے پڑے ہیں اور دوسری طرف پی ٹی آئی ڈھول ڈھمکے کے ساتھ اسلام آباد پر چڑھائی کی تیاری کر رہی ہے، رانا ثناء اللہ #RanaSanaullah #PTI #Islamabad #PoliticalTensions pic.twitter.com/FinNSvcU1W
Sanaullah also accused the K-P government of overlooking martyrs, asking whether the martyred Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) officials and police personnel belonged to the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz or were residents of some other province. “They were people of K-P, residents of K-P,” he said.
He further argued that a “big portion” of those martyred in K-P belonged to the province itself, including civilians, armed forces personnel and law-enforcement officials.
The adviser said the day before, “on one side there lay the bodies of the martyrs, and on the other side, the entire provincial government, while beating drums and chanting slogans, was provoking people to come together”. “This is the attitude of the K-P government; this attitude cannot be tolerated in any way,” he added.
He also claimed that “they have not been able to gather more than a few thousand in any area they have gone”. According to Sanaullah, “Giving priority to your personal, political agenda over national interests, no way is permitted constitutionally, lawfully, or in regard to political ethics.”
He said this had been made clear to the K-P government, adding that its response was that governing or working for people’s welfare was not its agenda and that it had a different agenda.
Sanaullah said PTI’s claims regarding the anti-terrorism policy were “an attempt to create confusion”, referring to a press briefing in which PTI leader Salman Akram Raja had said the federal government “had nothing to do” with the policy. “This is completely wrong,” the adviser said, adding that the policy “is already made; it is being implemented”.
Sanaullah said the main point of contention was the intelligence-based operations being conducted in K-P. He added that Pakistan’s armed forces and law-enforcement agencies were risking their lives and “progressing with success and bravery”.
According to Sanaullah, the K-P government was opposed to the operations.
Also Read: Govt has left no room for talks: Fazl
Referring to separate attacks on police personnel and civilians, including attacks on a passport office and a council in Swat, he said the operations were being conducted against the “beasts” responsible for the attacks. “How can the operations be stopped and how can someone object to them?” he asked.
Sanaullah said explanations were also being given that “some new operation is going to start or IDPs will be created”.
He said Field Marshal Asim Munir, while addressing the armed forces, had clarified the matter, while the federal government had also categorically stated that there was no move to create internally displaced persons. “This is just an attempt, for no reason, to spread fear among the people,” he said.
Sanaullah further said the intelligence-based operations would continue.
دہشت گردوں کا پاکستان کی سرزمین سے قلع قمع کیا جائے گا، رانا ثناء اللہ #RanaSanaullah #CounterTerrorism #PakistanSecurity #Terrorism pic.twitter.com/Aa5kv3CnJG
Turning to Afghanistan, the adviser said Pakistan’s only demand was for Kabul to “stop letting your soil be used for terrorism in Pakistan”. “There is not a word beyond this demand,” Sanaullah said.
He added that brotherly countries, including Saudi Arabia, Qatar, China and Turkiye, “have tried their best” and had explained to the Afghan regime that it should ensure its territory was not used for terrorism in Pakistan. “But they have not done so,” he maintained.
He further said the Afghan regime was not ready to give Islamabad a guarantee and that Pakistan’s policy was that if Afghan soil was being used for training camps or activities enabling terrorism in Pakistan, Islamabad had the right to neutralise them. “For this, Pakistan has, with full evidence but on a limited scale, conducted operations and Pakistan keeps this right protected,” he added.
Regarding the anti-terrorism policy, Sanaullah said it was “based on the experiences of the past 40 years” involving Afghanistan, the Taliban, Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan and Tehreek-e-Taliban Afghanistan.
He stated that there was national consensus on the policy. “If there is no consensus, it is on the part of the PTI and only for the reason that it places its personal politics over national interest. There is nothing other than this,” he added.
Read More: Rising terrorism in K-P must be stopped 'at all costs': PM Shehbaz
Discussing the apex committee, Sanaullah questioned K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi about his participation in the forum and asked how many meetings he had conducted over the past 11 months.
“How many times have you sat and objected to this policy or have tried to bring some betterment to it or have suggested some betterment to it?” he asked.
He said the existing policy against terrorism had been successful, adding that if there had been any lack of success, “the reason for it is the provincial government’s absence and instability”.
‘Security forces lack resources and civil presence’
The adviser also said security forces in K-P remained under-resourced and that the required civil administration presence was lacking in cleared areas.
He said under the anti-terrorism policy, the armed forces conducted intelligence-based operations to clear an area and, once it had been cleared, the area “should be held by the civil administration, police, CTD, but they don't exist there”.
Sanaullah said the absence of a sustained civil and police presence meant that areas cleared by the armed forces could return to the same situation months later.
“The armed forces and other law-enforcement agencies, when they clear one area and then move forward, six months later, three months later, it's the same situation,” he added.
Only Imran can call off long march: Shaukat Yousafzai
Earlier in a statement, PTI K-P spokesperson Shaukat Yousafzai rejected threats of governor’s rule in the province, saying the march would not end under pressure and that only jailed PTI founder Imran Khan could decide its fate.
The long march, which is being headed by K-P CM Sohail Afridi, announced a change in the route, saying the march would first head towards Khyber and then proceed to Peshawar. The march is set to begin from the suburban area of Mattani before heading towards Khyber, where the participants would camp for the night.
Yousafzai criticised Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s repeated offers of dialogue, saying the government should move beyond public statements and address the opposition’s demands.
“The prime minister, do not just play the negotiations game in the media. If you have the authority, accept the opposition’s legitimate demands,” he said.
Yousafzai urged the government to respect decisions of the high courts and Supreme Court and reiterated that PTI would not withdraw its demands concerning party leader. “We will not back down from our demands for a meeting with Imran and his transfer to hospital,” he said.
He also called for the release of imprisoned women, including Imran's sisters.
He questioned K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi’s authority to summon the provincial chief secretary and inspector general of police to a meeting. “Kundi has exceeded his authority. After the 18th Amendment, the governor does not even have the authority to crack a walnut,” he said.
The PTI spokesperson defended CM Afridi amid criticism from federal government figures, saying he regretted what he described as negative propaganda against the chief minister.
Turning to the security situation in K-P, Yousafzai said terrorism could not be addressed by undermining the province’s electoral mandate.
He called on the federal government to bring all stakeholders together to formulate a strategy against terrorism. “All problems will be resolved through negotiations,” he added.
Meanwhile, K-P police spokesman Alam Khan said that Police had prepared a security plan from Peshawar to Nowshera amid security concerns, with drone cameras to be used to monitor the long march.
"Security arrangements have been divided into three categories, with three SPs assigned responsibility for security in the city, suburban areas and along Ring Road," he added.
Khan said that around 300 personnel would be deployed along the march and its routes, while the City Patrol Force unit would also remain deployed at Peshawar’s entry and exit points.

title: Ronaldo says Portugal coach broke promises
description: The 41 year old apologises to teammates and supporters while accepting any punishment from the Portuguese federation
content:
The 41-year-old apologises to teammates and supporters while accepting any punishment from the Portuguese federation
Cristiano Ronaldo on Tuesday accused Portugal coach Jorge Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time in Nations League matches, but said he remained available for his country.
In a statement of nearly 2,000 words, the 41-year-old superstar apologised for walking out on the national team and said he would serve a suspension if necessary.
"I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team," Ronaldo said.
Jesus left the forward unused on the bench for a Nations League match against Norway. Before the next game with Denmark, he said Ronaldo would not start and in response the 41-year-old walked out of the national team camp.
"I owe an apology to my national team teammates for having left the camp," wrote Ronaldo.
"Despite the absolute breakdown of trust in the head coach's word... I shouldn't have done it. The responsibility is mine alone."
Ronaldo also apologised to Portugal supporters, but insisted he had been responding to the veteran coach's "broken word".
"I apologise to the Portuguese people once again, but a broken word has, for me, a defining impact," said Ronaldo.
"I felt that, from that moment on, my presence would only harm the group, and I did what I always said I would do if I didn't feel useful: I picked up my bags and left."
Ronaldo said Jesus, who was appointed after Portugal were knocked out of the World Cup Round of 16, had initially presented him with a plan for the international window which included starting the opening and final games at home, but not travelling for the matches in Norway and Denmark.
The Al-Nassr superstar rejected that proposal, saying it would set a poor example for the captain to remain in Portugal while his team-mates travelled.
Ahead of the Norway game, Ronaldo said Jesus unexpectedly asked if he was fit to play 30 minutes. He agreed and warmed up from half-time, but was not brought on.
"The head coach failed to keep his word to me," said Ronaldo, Portugal's most capped player and all-time top goalscorer.
Former Real Madrid and Manchester United forward Ronaldo said he spoke with Jesus after that and agreed with him that the coach would apologise in a news conference ahead of the Denmark game.
However Ronaldo said Jesus's subsequent press conference was completely different from what was agreed in their conversation, with an "aggressiveness" he had never previously experienced from the coach.
"It was the second time he failed to keep his word. I decided to leave the camp without waiting for any further broken promises," wrote Ronaldo.
The striker said he would serve any "suspension that is imposed" on him and accepted he should be punished for his actions.
"The consequence of this act of mine must be assessed and punished by the Portuguese Football Federation," he explained.
"I understand that the punishment should not have mitigating circumstances. I'm not just any player, I'm the team captain, and that is an aggravating factor."
Portugal won all four of their Nations League matches and qualified for the quarter-finals with two games to spare.

title: Nobel Peace Prize haunted by the  spectre  of Trump
description: Committee faces close scrutiny ahead of announcement as US president campaigned for award since return to White House
content:
Committee faces close scrutiny ahead of announcement as US president campaigned for award since return to White House
Donald Trump's chances of winning the Nobel Peace Prize are seen as minimal, but his "spectre" will cast its shadow over Friday's announcement of the winner in Oslo, experts say.
The Norwegian Nobel Committee knows it will be under close scrutiny: since his return to the White House in January 2025, the billionaire Republican has campaigned intensively for the prize and hasn't hidden his disappointment at not winning it yet.
The chances of him getting the nod are however undermined by his war against Iran , his territorial ambitions — sometimes at the expense of allies, as in Greenland — and his attacks on international cooperation institutions and the media .
Even though he has not been lobbying as openly for the Nobel in recent weeks, Trump remains on everyone's minds, with strong chances that the committee's pick will, regardless of who they choose, be interpreted as direct or indirect criticism of the United States president.
Read: German and US scientists win Nobel medicine prize for work on optogenetics
Trump is "the spectre in the room", said the head of the Peace Research Institute in Oslo (PRIO), Haakon Gjerlow. He said the Nobel committee must be asking itself: "Is there any potential for this prize to create harm rather than good in awarding it?", given the reactions that could emerge from the White House.
"There's always a lot of lobbying, and ultimately perhaps also attempts to exert pressure on the committee. So in one sense we're very used to that," the secretary of the committee, Kristian Berg Harpviken, told AFP . "It's not something we don't discuss. Of course we have to discuss it, but it's not like that influences the discussions in the room and decisions that come out," he insisted.
Last year, the prestigious prize went to Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, a choice generally considered palatable to Trump. Machado even gave him her Nobel gold medal, judging he deserved it after the capture of President Nicolas Maduro — though she failed to obtain his political backing in exchange.
Those events could prompt the committee to this year choose a laureate who enjoys broad consensus, such as an individual or organisation working to protect children or humanitarian efforts.
That could include the Save the Children charity and Mykola Kuleba, a Ukrainian children's rights activist campaigning for the return of kids illegally taken to Russia from occupied territories — a cause close to the heart of Trump's wife Melania.
Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms (ERR), a vast network of volunteers risking their lives to help people facing the double threat of war and hunger, could also be a potential laureate.
But the committee may also choose a laureate that could rub Trump the wrong way. That could include the United Nations special rapporteur for the occupied Palestinian territories Francesca Albanese , Pope Leo XIV, press freedoms with an award to the Committee to Protect Journalists, or international justice bodies such as the International Criminal Court (ICC) and the International Court of Justice (ICJ).
Read More: Nobel prize sum raised to $1.27m for 2026
"We live in an age of predators. We have Trump, Putin, Netanyahu," said Nobel historian Asle Sveen. "They don't want to have an international order. They want to have big powers with spheres of influence. And this court stands in the way," he said, referring to the ICC.
A total of 287 individuals and organisations have been nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize, though the names on the list are kept secret for 50 years.
But peace remains elusive in many parts of the world: 65 armed conflicts involving at least one state actor were registered in 2025, the highest number since 1946, according to PRIO.
"At an overall level, it is clear that the world is not developing in the right direction," said Harpviken. "At the same time ... there is no lack of good initiatives. There is no lack of organisations or individuals who do good work," he said.
"A peace prize may make more sense than ever."

title: Israel strikes Gaza on October 7 anniversary  at least two dead  officials
description: Israeli occupiers injure four Palestinians in West Bank as election officials denied entry ahead of November vote
content:
Israeli occupiers injure four Palestinians in West Bank as election officials denied entry ahead of November vote
Israel carried out new strikes in Gaza on Wednesday as it marked the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks by Hamas, with Palestinian officials reporting two dead.
Loud bangs across the border in Gaza were audible from the site of the Nova music festival just as family members gathered at dawn to mourn the more than 300 revelers killed three years earlier.
In Gaza City, Al-Shifa hospital reported two people killed in an Israeli strike overnight. Gaza’s civil defense identified one of the dead as Mohamed Tamous and said he was a volunteer for the agency, which serves as an emergency rescue service under Hamas.
Israeli occupiers injure four Palestinians, besiege family home in West Bank
Meanwhile, Israeli occupiers injured four Palestinians in separate attacks across the occupied West Bank on Tuesday, including a couple whose home was besieged south of Hebron.
Dozens of Israeli occupiers surrounded the home of Yousef Shnaran in Wadi al-Rakhim in the Masafer Yatta area before assaulting him and his wife, leaving both injured, relative Ayman Shnaran told Anadolu . He said the occupiers had earlier erected a tent just metres from the house before gathering there in large numbers.
Israeli soldiers later arrived but did not lift the siege, while ambulances were unable to reach the injured couple, he said. Seven children remained inside the home.
Read: Vandalism to arson: Israeli occupier attacks on mosques in West Bank hit record levels
Elsewhere in the Hebron area, Israeli occupiers attacked Palestinian homes and opened fire in Beit Ummar, according to the official Palestinian news agency Wafa . Israeli forces also raided several homes in the town. No injuries or arrests were reported.
In the northern West Bank, two Palestinian farmers who are brothers were injured after Israeli occupiers attacked olive harvesters from Marda and nearby Jamma’in north of Salfit. Both were taken to a hospital in stable condition, Wafa said.
The occupiers also stole olives collected by the farmers.
Israeli occupiers have carried out more than 14,742 attacks across the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, since October 2023, killing 66 Palestinians, according to the Palestinian Colonisation and Wall Resistance Commission.
Israel denies Palestinian election officials entry to Gaza, East Jerusalem
Separately, a Palestinian source said Israel refused to allow representatives of the Palestinian Central Elections Commission to enter Gaza and occupied East Jerusalem ahead of legislative elections scheduled for late November.
Wafa quoted an unnamed official source as saying the Israeli government had denied the commission entry to oversee the electoral process. No further details were provided.
On July 9, Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas issued a decree setting November 28 as the date for legislative elections in East Jerusalem, the occupied West Bank and Gaza. If held, they would be the first such elections since 2006.
The commission began accepting applications to register electoral lists on September 26, receiving eight applications during the first four days. Registration remains open until October 13.
Read More: Israeli media says attempt to assassinate senior Hamas figure likely failed in Gaza
Palestinian Vice President Hussein al-Sheikh told journalists on August 2 that an alternative arrangement would be pursued if elections could not take place because they were prevented or obstructed in Gaza or any other part of the Palestinian territories. “The alternative plan is to form the Palestinian National Council by consensus, as the Palestine Liberation Organisation is the sole legitimate representative of the Palestinian people,” he said.
About 2.97 million Palestinians are eligible to vote, including approximately 1.59 million in the West Bank, 1.24 million in Gaza and 140,000 holders of Jerusalem identity cards.
The last Palestinian legislative elections were held in 2006, when Hamas won a majority of seats. A political split followed between Hamas and Fatah. Hamas took control of Gaza about a year later, while the Fatah-led Palestinian Authority remained in the West Bank.
The Palestinian Legislative Council has been inactive since 2007. The Supreme Constitutional Court ordered its dissolution in 2018.

A total of 20,748 Palestinian students and 1,058 educational and administrative staff have been killed in the Gaza Strip and occupied West Bank during three years of Israeli genocide, the Palestinian Education Ministry said on Wednesday.
In a statistical report on Israeli violations against the education sector, the ministry said the figures cover students and staff at schools and universities, alongside thousands of injuries and arrests and the destruction or targeting of dozens of educational institutions.
In the Gaza Strip, 19,189 school students and 1,386 university students have been killed, according to the ministry.
Another 28,586 school students and 3,082 university students were injured.

Israeli forces also detained 416 school students and 481 university students.
Seven educational and administrative staff at schools were killed and 26 others were injured, while Israeli forces detained more than 176 teachers and school employees and 21 university staff members.
Since October 2023, more than 74,000 Palestinians have been killed and over 175,000 injured in Gaza by Israel’s genocide, while around 90% of the enclave’s infrastructure has been damaged or destroyed.

title: Destined  Djokovic wins China Open
description: The 39 year old extends his unbeaten Beijing record to 34 matches
content:
The 39-year-old extends his unbeaten Beijing record to 34 matches
Tennis great Novak Djokovic credited his "never-die spirit" for carrying him to the 102nd title of his career as he won the China Open on Tuesday when his opponent Alex de Minaur retired injured from the final.
With the win, the 39-year-old Serbian extended a perfect record to 34 wins in as many matches for his seventh title in Beijing -- his first since 2015.
Djokovic said afterwards that in more than two decades as a professional player, "the grit and the dedication and the kind of never-die spirit that really is always with me" have carried him through.
Tennis is "quite a cruel sport" with players competing in knock-out tournaments year-round, Djokovic told reporters, adding that the stakes and pressure of performing in front of fans made the sport "so demanding and so special".
"You can feel so much weight on your shoulders, but it is what I have been destined to do," he said.
In front of a jam-packed stadium, Djokovic won the first set in the tie-break 7-6 (7/3) and was down a game in the second set when the Australian ended the match early.
"I always want to visualise myself with the trophy, particularly here in Beijing," Djokovic said during the trophy ceremony.
"But I was also quite aware that reality is a little bit different these days," he said, adding that it had been a challenging year with "physical and health issues".
"I was just trying to find the good feeling on the court," he said.
The first set was a physical battle that lasted more than one hour, and both men needed medical timeouts before the second.
De Minaur, the world number nine, won the first game of the second set before retiring due to a left adductor strain.
The 27-year-old had walked back onto the court after his medical timeout with a white wrap around his left thigh.
"I don't feel great," de Minaur told the crowd afterwards.
"I want to say sorry to the amazing fans that came to watch... I didn't want to finish like this."
De Minaur advanced to the final after his opponent Hubert Hurkacz retired injured from their semi-final on Monday, while Djokovic moved through when Daniil Medvedev was disqualified for hitting a fan with a ball.
But Djokovic, a 24-time Grand Slam champion, put on a valiant show to lift the trophy, ousting top seed Alexander Zverev in the quarter-final after defeating home hope Bu Yunchaokete in a demanding three-set match.
It means Djokovic will end the season with at least one title for the 21st consecutive year, and as the oldest man to win a singles final after Ken Rosewall in Hong Kong in 1977 at age 43.
In the women's draw, Karolina Muchova beat former world number one Naomi Osaka on her ninth match point to reach the quarter-finals, triumphant in a tense tie-break.
Muchova, the seventh seed, overcame 50 unforced errors across the two-hour-and-52-minute match to beat Osaka 7-5, 1-6, 7-6 (9/7).
Osaka, who represents Japan, saved eight match points but could not get past Muchova's match-winning volley.
"I was shaking. I'm happy I made the last volley... Naomi could be standing here. It's me, and I'm really grateful for it," the 30-year-old Czech player told the crowd.
She next faces compatriot Nikola Bartunkova.
Earlier, Russia's Mirra Andreeva beat Ukraine's Daria Snigur 6-2, 6-2 to book her quarter-final spot against fellow Russian Ekaterina Alexandrova.
Alexandrova, ranked 28th, upset Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova 6-2, 6-2, ending the Czech player's bid to return to the Beijing final that she reached last year.

title: Islamabad ATC indicts Imaan Mazari  Hadi Ali Chattha in barricade removal case
description: Orders that Imaan and Chattha be physically produced at the next hearing  summons prosecution witnesses for October 9
content:
Orders that Imaan and Chattha be physically produced at the next hearing, summons prosecution witnesses for October 9
An anti-terrorism court in Islamabad on Wednesday framed charges against lawyer Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha in a case related to the alleged violation of a designated route and incitement during the arrival of an international cricket team, despite defence objections that legal requirements had not been fulfilled.
The ATC had fixed October 6 for the indictment of Imaan and her husband, Hadi Chattha. However, the proceedings were deferred a day earlier after they could not be produced before the court due to a power outage at Adiala Jail. The court directed jail authorities to ensure the accused were produced via video link at the next hearing, warning that failure to comply could lead to contempt proceedings against jail officials.
Today, Judge Tahir Abbas Supra presided over the hearing, during which Imaan and Chattha were produced before the court via video link. Chattha objected that he had still not received copies of the case documents and argued that charges could not be framed until all legal requirements had been met.
Lawyer Zainab Janjua also objected, saying neither Imaan nor Chattha had received the copies or been allowed to meet their lawyers. “The court cannot frame charges without fulfilling all legal requirements,” Zainab told the court.
The court nevertheless framed charges against Imaan and Chattha. “You can challenge this order,” Judge Tahir Abbas told Zainab.
The court ordered that Imaan and Chattha be physically produced at the next hearing and summoned prosecution witnesses for October 9. The hearing was adjourned until October 9.
Earlier, Zainab told the court that she had waited outside the jail for two hours but was not allowed to meet her clients despite a court order. She also said copies of the case documents had not been provided to Imaan and Chattha and requested that they be produced before the court.
Read: Islamabad ATC ends contempt proceedings as Imaan, Hadi sign powers of attorney for litigation
“I have the jail authorities’ reports with me,” Judge Tahir Abbas said.
Janjua questioned why Imaan and Chattha were not being produced before the court when other prisoners were being brought from Adiala Jail.
Dr Shireen Mazari also appeared before the court along with lawyers Eemal Khan Mandokhail, Zainab and others. Prosecutor Raja Naveed represented the prosecution.
At the previous hearing on Monday, the ATC had adjourned Imaan and Chattha’s bail applications until October 13 after the investigating officer failed to appear before the court.
Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain had expressed displeasure over the officer’s absence. The DSP later told the court that the investigating officer was in Gilgit-Baltistan and his phone was switched off.
Defence counsel had argued that all sections in the FIR, except the terrorism provision, were bailable and pointed out that the court had previously rejected the prosecution’s request for the physical remand of Imaan and Chattha.
Imaan and her husband Chattha were rearrested on September 17 , shortly after the Supreme Court granted them bail and suspended their sentences in a separate social-media posts case. They were produced before an Islamabad Anti-Terrorism Court in connection with a case registered at Kohsar Police Station.
Police sought 30-day physical remand, but ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain rejected the request and sent the couple on judicial remand. The judge noted that although they had been nominated in the FIR as members of an unlawful assembly, no weapon had been attributed to either accused.

On September 27, the court issued a contempt notice to the Adiala jail superintendent after the authorities failed to facilitate the signing and transmission of the documents and also failed to produce the accused through video link. Two days later, the issue was resolved after Imaan and Chattha signed the required powers of attorney.
On September 29 , the ATC ended the contempt proceedings against the jail authorities and separately confirmed that notices had been issued on the couple’s bail applications, with arguments scheduled before Judge Abul Hasnat.

title: Mandhana named India women s team captain
description: She takes charge after playing a key role in India   s recent Asian Games gold medal campaign
content:
She takes charge after playing a key role in India’s recent Asian Games gold-medal campaign
India's cricket board on Tuesday named Smriti Mandhana as the new captain of the women's team after Harmanpreet Kaur resigned from the job earlier in the day.
The 37-year-old Kaur, who recently led India to an Asian Games gold medal in Japan, had captained the team to their first women's global title at last year's ODI World Cup.
Mandhana, 30, has been the backbone of India's batting in recent years and played a key part in the Asian Games victory, including a stellar 45-ball 79 in the final against Sri Lanka.
"To be given the responsibility of leading India is a very special honour," Mandhana said in a statement by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI).
"Representing India has always meant a great deal to me, and to now have the opportunity to lead the team is something I will value deeply."
Mandhana, a swashbuckling left-handed opener, has played nine Tests, 120 ODIs and 179 T20s for India since her debut in the white-ball format in 2013.
"The BCCI has full confidence in Smriti and I am sure she will approach this role with the same commitment and professionalism that she has shown throughout her career," BCCI president Mithun Manhas said.
Earlier Kaur stepped down from the role through a social media post on Tuesday morning.
"This is not an easy decision," Kaur wrote.
"It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life," she said.
"I have given everything I had to this team and to Indian women's cricket -- my blood, my sweat, my time, and many times, a part of my own game and personal ambitions."
However, Kaur indicated she would continue to play.
"Captaincy ends. The journey continues," she said.
Kaur's role as leader was first questioned after India's second successive group-stage exit from the T20 World Cup in June.
Her leadership also came up for discussion at a review meeting held by the BCCI on Monday, local media reports said.
Kaur led India in five Tests, 51 ODIs and 155 T20Is.

title: Oil gains as US storm and Houthi air strikes threaten supply
description: Brent futures rise  1 05  or 1 04   to  101 63 a barrel
content:
Brent futures rise $1.05, or 1.04%, to $101.63 a barrel
Oil prices ​climbed on Wednesday as the market weighed supply constraints from a storm heading for US oil-producing ‌regions and attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabia against increased supplies of Middle East crude.
Brent futures rose $1.05, or 1.04%, to $101.63 a barrel by 0400 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures rose 80 cents, or 0.89%, to $90.24 a barrel.
US forecasters said on Tuesday ​a storm forming in the Gulf of Mexico would become the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 within two days ​and would likely hit oil and gas producing facilities.
The offshore areas in the Gulf in ⁠the storm's path produce 15% of US crude oil and 5% of the country's natural gas.
KCM Trade chief analyst ​Tim Waterer said the storm was an "unwelcome complication for crude, raising the prospect of production and refining disruptions at a ​time when the market already has enough supply-side headaches".
The storm could affect six refineries. Refineries in US Gulf states account for about 50% of the national capacity of 18.2 million barrels per day (bpd).
US crude oil inventories fell last week, market sources said on Tuesday, citing data ​from the American Petroleum Institute. Crude stocks fell by 2.09 million barrels in the week ended October 2.

"For now, the ​market is likely to remain nervous to any potential supply disruptions," said ING commodity strategists, adding that supply risks from the Middle ‌East ⁠are still very real amid continued attacks on ships.
Supply has been recovering. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline hit 5.8 million barrels a day, the kingdom's energy minister, Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman, said on Tuesday.
Around 12 million barrels per day of crude oil and 2 million bpd of refined products have left the Middle East on tankers in the last 7 to ​10 days, the head of Vitol ​said.
However, Saudi Arabia's airports ⁠in Jazan and Najran were targeted in two attacks on Monday evening, the Saudi aviation authority said, as hostilities between the kingdom and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis escalated.
The attacks occurred as Saudi-backed ​Yemeni government forces pressed a major offensive to retake territory from the Houthis, after ​weeks of rebel ⁠advances, with Riyadh stepping up airstrikes in support of the campaign.
Attacks and refinery outages are "likely to keep the cracks elevated and scarcity will transmit to crude," said Mukesh Sahdev, chief oil analyst at X Analysts in Sydney, referring to the premiums for ⁠refined products ​over crude.
Crude prices would hold near $100 "without any material de-escalation emerging," he ​added.
US-Iran relations are no closer to repair, with US President Donald Trump saying on Tuesday that nobody knew who was running Iran during the eight-month US-Israeli ​war with Iran.

title: Iyer hits ton as India hammer West Indies in T20 opener
description: Iyer   s maiden T20I century powers India to an eight wicket victory in Lucknow
content:
Iyer’s maiden T20I century powers India to an eight-wicket victory in Lucknow
Captain Shreyas Iyer struck his maiden T20 international century to lead India to a convincing eight-wicket win over the West Indies in the opening match on Tuesday.
With India chasing 172 for victory, Iyer hit an unbeaten 102 off 43 balls to steer his team home with 32 balls to spare in Lucknow. India lead the five-match series 1-0.
With eight needed off 36 balls and Iyer on 95, Ishan Kishan handed his captain the strike and the top-order batter reached his ton with a six and then took a single to complete the chase.
"Definitely exultant - that's the word I would use today," said player of the match Iyer.
"I was actually thinking about getting my first century, and it came through. So, you know, I definitely want to say that dreams do come true."
Iyer and the T20 team produced the win after they landed in India on Monday evening with an Asian Games men's T20 gold medal.
While they were in Japan, a completely different India squad, led by Shubman Gill, beat West Indies 2-1 in an ODI series.
Swashbuckling Abhishek Sharma gave the hosts a brisk start in his 10-ball 21 before spinner Roston Chase got the left-hander caught out.
Left-arm spinner Akeal Hosein then struck in his 100th T20 for the West Indies to send back Sanju Samson caught and bowled for 11.
Iyer and the left-handed Kishan, who made 37, then took charge with a string of boundaries and put on an unbeaten stand of 137.
Iyer raised his first half-century off 28 balls after 10 T20 innings and then changed gear for his next set of 50 in 14 balls.
Spinners set up victory with debutant Naman Dhir returning figures of 3-31 to bowl out West Indies for 171.
India elected to field first and despite a quick start by skipper Shai Hope, who made 52 off 37 balls, the spinners struck regular blows.
"I thought we maybe were a little bit too chaotic in the batting," said Hope. "Very aggressive about playing. But yeah, when you're playing in India, you got to put runs on the board."
Sherfane Rutherford top-scored with 56 but bowlers kept India in control.
Kuldeep Yadav and fellow spinner Axar Patel took two wickets each.

title: Messi says Argentina retirement is  saddest day of my career
description: The 39 year old delivers a goal and two assists before addressing supporters at the Monumental
content:
The 39-year-old delivers a goal and two assists before addressing supporters at the Monumental
Lionel Messi described his retirement from international football as the "saddest day of my career" on Tuesday after playing his final game for Argentina in a 3-0 defeat of Benin.
Messi, who scored a goal and provided two assists in the victory at the Monumental Stadium, took to the field after the win to express gratitude to fans and team-mates as he reflected on his 21-year career with Argentina.
Messi, playing in his record-extending 208th international, also provided the assist for the opening goal scored by veteran Nicolas Otamendi, with Nico Paz also scoring.
"It was a huge source of pride for me to defend this jersey for more than 20 years," Messi told the stadium.
"Even in the worst moments we went through and that I had, I never stopped fighting, never stopped being here.
"Not coming anymore is going to be deeply painful. I swear I'd like to play for the rest of my life, because playing for the Argentina national team is the most beautiful thing that can happen to you."
Messi said that returning to the Monumental -- where Argentina played their first game after winning the 2022 World Cup -- was bittersweet.
"Now I'm here on the saddest day of my career, which is the day I have to say goodbye to the national team, goodbye to all of you.
"But now I'll be on that side (with the fans), supporting all the boys, everyone who comes in. Always united," he said.
Messi though said that despite the sadness, he had no regrets about the timing of his international exit, citing the exertions of Argentina's campaign at this year's World Cup, where the South Americans battled through to the final only to lose to Spain.
Messi said the emotional roller coaster of that tournament -- which included a 2-1 defeat of bitter rivals England in the semi-final -- had taken a toll.
"Even though I want to be here all my life, I feel that this is the moment. The last World Cup was too much, everything I had to live through," said Messi.
"We had the dream of fulfilling my dream and the dream of the whole country, of becoming world champions again.
"In the last World Cup we were very close, and the reality is that nothing strange happened, as people say. The match against England took a huge toll on us physically, and emotionally it was very big.
"We arrived with just enough, we fought like we always did with this jersey, with all the teammates I got to be with and share things with, not only them but also those who were around in the time when we managed to win. We were very close."
Messi took the field alongside his three children and received affectionate waves from his wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, and his mother, Celia Cuccittini, who were watching from a VIP box.
Shortly before kick off, a giant Argentina jersey bearing the word "Gracias" (Thank You) above the football superstar's No.10 was laid out on the pitch as the crowd roared their approval.

title: Freddie Jackson dies at 70  Grammy nominated R B singer s cause of death  career and net worth
description: The celebrated American singer known for his romantic ballads and distinctive voice  died days after his 70th birthday
content:
The celebrated American singer known for his romantic ballads and distinctive voice, died days after his 70th birthday
Freddie Jackson, the celebrated American R&B singer known for his romantic ballads and distinctive voice, has died aged 70.
Jackson died on Monday night, October 5, 2026, just days after his birthday.
Jackson’s family has not disclosed his cause of death. His loved ones said fans will have opportunities to pay tribute to the singer, with further details expected to be announced later.
Born Freddie Anthony Jackson on October 2, 1956, in Harlem, New York, Jackson began singing gospel music at White Rock Baptist Church.
He later joined the group Mystic Merlin before launching his solo career.
Jackson released his debut album, Rock Me Tonight , through Capitol Records in 1985.
The album established him as a major R&B performer, with “Rock Me Tonight (For Old Times Sake)” reaching No. 1 on the R&B chart for six weeks. “You Are My Lady” became another defining recording.
His other recognised songs included “Tasty Love”, “Have You Ever Loved Somebody”, “Jam Tonight”, “Do Me Again”, “Nice ’N’ Slow” and “Love Me Down”.
Jackson also received two Grammy Award nominations in 1986.
He continued recording and performing for decades, with My First Love among his later projects, released in 2023.
Jackson’s net worth was not publicly disclosed. However, several celebrity finance websites estimated his fortune at approximately $3 million, based on earnings from music sales, performances, royalties and entertainment work.
Jackson leaves behind a substantial R&B catalogue that helped define romantic soul music during the 1980s and beyond.

Annette Badland, who played Mae, also suggested that her character could potentially return despite her Season 4 death. “You never know. There is a film called It’s a Wonderful Life, where an angel keeps popping back. Maybe Mae can pop back up as a sort of conscience,” Badland told Decider .
Jason Sudeikis has previously indicated that he revived Ted Lasso with another three-season arc in mind.
There is currently no Season 5 release date. If the series is renewed and production proceeds without major delays, new episodes could arrive in late 2027 or between 2028 and 2029.

title: Security forces kill 18 terrorists in K P  Balochistan operations  state media
description: Police foil attack on Shadipur police post in Kohat  four personnel sustain injuries

Police foil attack on Shadipur police post in Kohat, four personnel sustain injuries
Security forces killed 18 terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan in separate operations in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) and Balochistan, state media reported on Wednesday, citing security sources.
The federal government last year officially designated all terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as Fitna al-Hindustan , accusing India of sponsoring a proxy war through the outfits.
Fitna al - Khawarij is the term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
In K-P, security forces killed 13 Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in North Waziristan, Pakistan TV wrote on X, adding that operations against terrorist groups continued under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision.
Security forces killed 13 Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in North Waziristan, as operations against militant groups continue under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision. #Pakistan #NorthWaziristan #AzmEIstehkam #CounterTerrorism #PakistanTV pic.twitter.com/SXpfiBy0Wx
Separately, security forces killed five Fitna al-Hindustan terrorists during an operation in Mastung, Balochistan, Pakistan TV wrote on X, adding that heavy weapons and ammunition were recovered during the operation, while clearance and search operations continued in the area under Operation Radd-ul-Fitna 3 , it added.

President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the security forces for successful operations against terrorists in K-P and Balochistan. The president praised the bravery and professional capabilities of the security forces for killing 13 Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists during an intelligence-based operation in North Waziristan.
He also paid tribute to the security forces for killing five Fitna al-Hindustan terrorists during a successful operation in Mastung. President Zardari said the security forces had reflected the nation’s resolve and courage through effective and decisive operations against terrorists.
He said the operations were a clear demonstration of firm resolve against terrorist elements. The president said conspiracies by the terrorists’ foreign sponsors and their local facilitators would be foiled.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised the officers and personnel of the security forces for a successful operation against Fitna al-Khawarij in North Waziristan, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) on Wednesday.
The prime minister commended the professional capabilities of the security forces for killing 13 Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists during the operation. He said the security forces had effectively targeted Fitna al-Khawarij hideouts in North Waziristan and surrounding areas.
PM Shehbaz said operations against Fitna al-Khawarij would continue until the complete elimination of terrorism and the establishment of lasting peace in the country. He said effective operations against terrorism under Azm-e-Istehkam reflected the state’s unwavering resolve to completely eliminate terrorism.
The prime minister said terrorists seeking to harm the country’s peace and security would not be allowed to succeed in their “nefarious designs”.
Read: Five terrorists killed, two wounded in North Waziristan operation: security sources
Meanwhile, Police foiled an attack by Fitna al-Khawarij on the Shadipur police post in Kohat, District Police Officer (DPO) Rai Mazhar Iqbal said.
According to DPO Iqbal, "Police launched a strong retaliatory operation after the attack, inflicting heavy losses on the terrorists."
Four police personnel were injured in the exchange of fire and were shifted to hospital, hospital authorities said. The injured personnel were in stable condition and out of danger.
“Following the foiling of the attack, police continued to pursue the terrorists as part of a search-and-strike operation,” the DPO said.
He further added that security had been further tightened across Kohat and police remained committed to maintaining peace in the district.
A day earlier, security forces killed 5 terrorists and wounded two others in a successful intelligence-based operation (IBO) also in North Waziristan. According to state media, the security forces successfully targeted terrorists' hideouts in North Waziristan and surrounding areas, and they had been continuously monitoring the movement of Fitna al-Khawarij before carrying out a decisive operation against the group
Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terrorist activity over the past three months, with a series of attacks across the country resulting in the martyrdom of security personnel and civilians.
Last week, 12 people were killed and 35 others injured when a blast struck a joint checkpoint near Aman Mela in the Darazinda area of Dera Ismail Khan, with the TTP claiming responsibility for the attack.

On September 19, 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred in a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, the Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
In a separate incident, a captain and a lieutenant were among six security personnel martyred in an exchange of fire in Hangu district, while eight terrorists were killed.
On September 1, six personnel, including two officers, and a customs department official were martyred as security forces thwarted an attempt to breach the Customs House in Balochistan.
In July, at least 30 people , including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. The attackers also abducted several civilians and police personnel after the assault.
In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation , which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

title: Ted Lasso  finale recap  Richmond faces major changes as season 4 ends

content:
'Ted Lasso' ends the fourth season with changes at Richmond and a possible path towards another season
The Ted Lasso Season 4 finale brings the Greyhounds’ first season to a close while leaving several major characters facing significant changes, leaving the door open for a potential fifth season.
The finale begins with the Richmond family mourning Mae, whose death affects Keeley, Ted and the Lady Greyhounds.
Roy learns that Keeley is pregnant and is offered the head coaching job at Chelsea. He ultimately accepts, although he plans to remain with Richmond until the end of the season.
At the same time, Rebecca discovers that Zelda was behind the attempt to gain control of AFC Richmond. However, Higgins and Rebecca had anticipated the move, while Hugo Riddles switched sides.
Mae's 2% stake is ultimately returned to Rebecca, giving her 51% ownership of the club.
Ted also makes an important decision concerning Henry. After previously avoiding difficult conversations, he finally tells his son the truth about his grandfather's suicide.
The episode then suggests Ted has chosen to remain involved in Henry's life while continuing his work in football.
Rebecca proposes to Matthijs, and he accepts. Beard also makes changes to his appearance and life, while Roy prepares to leave Richmond for Chelsea.
The biggest change comes with Alice Chilton becoming head coach of the AFC Richmond women's team, with Ted and Beard joining her as assistant managers.
The finale does not reveal the result of the Lady Greyhounds' final match. Instead, it ends with 112 days remaining until their next season, leaving plenty of possibilities for a potential Season 5.
