title: Iranian president says US deal    not out of reach    in call with Putin
description: Vance said US remained open to an agreement but would require concrete Iranian nuclear concessions
content:
Iranian official says 'illegal routes' in Strait of Hormuz to soon be blocked
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said during a call with his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, that reaching an agreement with the United States was “not out of reach” if Washington adhered to international legal frameworks, according to the Iranian presidency.
The two leaders discussed regional developments, Iran-US negotiations and relations, according to a statement.
Pezeshkian briefed Putin on negotiations between Iran and the US mediated by Pakistan, describing Washington’s “double standards and maximalism” as the biggest obstacle to reaching a fair agreement.
He said Tehran was prepared to reach a “balanced and fair” agreement that would ensure lasting peace and security in the region.
“Our red line is Iran’s national interests and the rights of the Iranian people,” said Pezeshkian, adding that if Washington adhered to international legal frameworks, reaching an agreement would not be out of reach.
The Iranian president also described Gulf countries as Iran’s “brothers” and expressed regret about the use of US military bases in those countries for attacks against Iran.
He said Tehran was ready to cooperate with neighbouring countries to achieve regional peace and security without the presence or involvement of powers from outside the region.
Putin reiterated Russia’s support for diplomatic efforts to reach a political settlement to the war and said Moscow was ready to keep helping find a diplomatic solution, according to the statement.
He also stressed the need to respect Iran’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and backed Tehran’s demands for compensation for damage caused during the war and long-term security guarantees against additional attacks.
The two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to expanding cooperation under the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty and maintaining close coordination in international forums.
Iranian official says 'illegal routes' in Strait of Hormuz to soon be blocked
Transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz deemed illegal by Iran will soon be closed, an adviser to ​the Revolutionary Guards' Commander told the semi-official Fars News ‌Agency on Wednesday, referring to the southern pathway hugging Oman's coast.
Mohammadreza Naqdi said these "few routes" had been created by blasting and damaging some of the rocky ​passages in the strategic waterway and were used by "small ​boats smuggling oil and transferring it to tankers", challenging the narrative ⁠that Gulf oil exports are regaining pre-war levels.
"The Strait of Hormuz is ​closed, and the armed forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran ​have full control over it. This situation will continue until Iran’s legitimate demands are met,” he added.
A seven-day moving average for crude exports from the ​region was 18.3 million barrels per day on September 30, provisional ​data from Kpler showed, with volumes topping pre-war levels on 14 days in ‌September.
⁠That included Gulf oil sent via Hormuz, the Red Sea, and from terminals and ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman.
The IRGC has consistently denied that seaborne crude flows in the ​strait are rebounding ​thanks to US ⁠Navy help, with another IRGC adviser, Majid Mirahmadi, saying on Thursday that a daily average of ​10 ships transit the waterway against an average of ​125 ⁠before the war, which started on February 28, when the US and Israel killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in a Tehran airstrike.
⁠Despite ​growing oil flows in September, Iranian attacks ​on tankers and logistical constraints have persisted and call into question whether higher flows ​can be sustained durably.
Iran will never give up its right to enrich uranium: senior Iranian official
Earlier, a senior Iranian official told Reuters that Iran would never give up its right to enrich, but details could be discussed later, adding that US ideas about Iran’s nuclear programme were at odds with Iran’s demands.
The official's comments came in response to earlier comments made by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and US Vice President JD Vance.
The official said Vance’s comments on Iran’s nuclear programme were the Americans’ “ideas and requests”.
There have been no negotiations between Iran and the US about Tehran’s nuclear programme, the official said, adding that the US must first meet Tehran’s conditions before the nuclear issue can be discussed.
US' recognition of Iran’s right to enrichment is Tehran’s red line, the official said.
Iran has failed to reach agreement with US on nuclear programme: Rubio
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday that Iran has "failed to take advantage of multiple opportunities" to reach an agreement with the United States on its nuclear programme.
He made the comments during his trip to Greece in a meeting with the Greek foreign minister.
He also said that Iran has “lost complete control” of the Strait of Hormuz, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday, adding that Tehran’s economy was “in total and complete freefall,” AFP reported.
“There’s almost as much oil flowing out now as there was before this conflict began. So they’ve lost complete control of the Straits,” Rubio said.
Earlier, US Vice President JD Vance said in an exclusive interview with Reuters that Iran ​must make a “meaningful” reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the countries’ seven-month war, even as Washington was unsure how ‌Tehran makes decisions in negotiations.
Vance has taken a leading role in negotiating a settlement to the conflict and brokered a provisional peace agreement in June that quickly fell apart. The war has jolted global energy markets and become a political liability for President Donald Trump and fellow Republicans ahead of November midterm elections.
Speaking on Monday after a campaign trip in Alaska, Vance said ​any agreement would require Iran to reduce its nuclear enrichment capacity, rather than offer assurances of future nuclear drawdowns.
"If you don't want a nuclear weapon, then why ​do you need 60% enriched fuel? And if you want to show commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, don't build highly enriched ⁠fuel. That's a very basic threshold issue," Vance said.
Read: Iran warns regional states of ‘different and decisive’ response to future attacks
"I think if they want to show a commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, they would do something meaningful on their ​enrichment capacity."
Iran and the US have exchanged proposals in recent weeks aimed at ending the war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy shipping route. Trump rejected Tehran's ​latest offer and has warned that military operations could intensify after the midterms.
Vance said the US remained open to an agreement but would require concrete Iranian nuclear concessions.
"We're not going to trade words for actions," Vance said.
Complicating matters, Vance said Washington is uncertain who makes decisions in Tehran.
Vance said the US was in talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. But ​it was unclear how much authority they wield within Iran's power structure, he said, after joint US-Israeli strikes at the start of the war killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
"One ​of the things we picked up on is it's not totally clear how their country makes decisions," Vance said. Separately, Trump said on Tuesday his "biggest problem" is no one knows who is running Iran.
Read more: 'Anything could happen': Trump says 'big decision' incoming regarding Iran
Iran's ‌Foreign Ministry ⁠spokesperson said on Sunday that US officials are well aware of who their Iranian counterparts are and how Iran's decision-making system works.
"The problem is actually the opposite: it lies in the contradictory positions and mixed messaging from US officials," Esmaeil Baghaei told a weekly press conference.
Vance told Reuters he has held personal conversations with field commanders to gauge battlefield conditions. He dismissed concerns over critical munitions shortages and added that while Iranian troops are periodically able to strike commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, they are largely unable to prevent energy exports through ​the waterway.
Vance declined to say if he ​was leading peace talks, though he is ⁠frequently cited as the White House's top negotiator.
"We're certainly involved," he said. "Ultimately, the president of the United States is driving things."
The war — and its $3 billion monthly price tag — has become a key issue on the campaign trail. Higher energy prices have put Trump and Republicans on the ​defensive in competitive states that will decide control of Congress.
Iranian FM stresses continuation of dialogue, cooperation with neighbours
Foreign Minister of Iran Abbas Araghchi emphasised that continued dialogue and cooperation with neighbours is the path prioritised by Iran for building a region that is secure and stable, according to state news agency IRNA .
In a message regarding the visit of his Armenian counterpart, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran wrote that on Monday he hosted Ararat Mirzoyan, the Foreign Minister of the Republic of Armenia, in Tehran.
FM @araghchi stresses continuation of dialogue and cooperation with neighbors https://t.co/CK6nqwhNgD pic.twitter.com/HMWz0oJTNe
Araghchi added that during the meeting they reviewed the expanding relations between Tehran and Yerevan, as well as ways to deepen cooperation in the areas of economy, trade, transportation, energy, and other fields of mutual interest.
He said that it was Iran's belief that regional issues should be resolved through the participation and initiatives of the countries within the region, without the interference of extra-regional forces.
He emphasised that continued dialogue and cooperation with neighbours was the path the Islamic Republic of Iran prioritises to build a more secure, stable, and prosperous region.
Iran envoy: US attacks damaged 111 petrochemical, pharmaceutical facilities
Iran’s ambassador to the Netherlands and Representative to the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) has said that US military attacks on Iran’s chemical industries damaged 111 petrochemical and pharmaceutical facilities, disrupting supply chains and affecting the implementation of the Chemical Weapons Convention.
Iran’s Permanent Mission to the OPCW on Tuesday released excerpts from remarks by Hadi Farajvand at the 113th session of the OPCW Executive Council, saying that 60 petrochemical complexes, 44 pharmaceutical factories and seven pharmaceutical facilities in Iran were damaged during the US attacks, according to IRNA .
Iran envoy: US attacks damaged 111 petrochemical, pharmaceutical facilities https://t.co/upDjlprtCY pic.twitter.com/2W5sQlLb2n
Farajvand said the damage inflicted on Iran’s chemical and pharmaceutical industries had disrupted supply chains and affected the implementation of obligations under the Chemical Weapons Convention.
He also stressed that protecting chemical facilities from armed conflicts is essential to preserving the integrity of the Convention, peaceful activities in the field of chemistry and international cooperation.
He added that the deliberate US attacks on the facilities had raised serious concerns regarding several articles of the Chemical Weapons Convention, as well as the object and purpose of the international treaty.
‘Iran’s economy will not break’: Central Bank governor vows resilience against US economic warfare
The Governor of the Central Bank of Iran (CBI), Abdolnaser Hemmati,told the Iranian public that the national economy would not break under the weight of US economic warfare, claiming that Tehran avoided Washington’s primary objective of triggering catastrophic hyperinflation , according to Press TV .
In a televised interview, Hemmati provided an assessment of the country’s economic battlefield, acknowledging the daily pressures felt by citizens while stating that Iran had neutralised the most severe threats engineered by the United States and the Israeli regime.
‘Iran’s economy will not break’: Central Bank governor vows resilience against US economic warfare https://t.co/Meo0iww16X
Hemmati emphasised that while inflation remains a challenge, the CBI has successfully prevented the economic collapse that US planners had anticipated.
"I am not talking about low inflation; I am talking about the fact that heavy, catastrophic inflation was supposed to happen, and this was one of America's primary goals—a goal that Trump and his Treasury Secretary repeat every day," Hemmati stated. "Fortunately, this did not happen, and the Central Bank has a plan and is actively pursuing liquidity control."
"They planned to bring Iran to economic collapse within two weeks, claim victory, and leave. Now, nine months have passed," he said, referring to the ongoing US-Israeli military and economic aggression that began earlier this year.
"Now they come and say that in another two weeks, Iran will collapse economically. Ten days have passed since that claim, and we are on the front lines of the economic war. We will give them the exact same answer: the result they want is the result they will get themselves."

title: Yemen   s Houthis claim attacks on Saudi airports  military bases
description: Spokesman says forces targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh
content:
Spokesman says forces targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh
Yemen’s Houthi group claimed early Wednesday that it carried out a series of drone and ballistic missile attacks targeting airports and military installations in Saudi Arabia.
In a statement on the US social media platform X, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the forces targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with several drones, claiming the strike was "precise" and disrupted air traffic there.
استهدفت قواتنا المسلحة قبل قليل مطار الملك خالد بالرياض بصاروخ باليستي وكانت الإصابة دقيقة بفضل الله وأدت إلى تعطل حركة الملاحة في المطار.
He also said Houthi forces conducted two operations targeting Abha International Airport and Khamis Mushait Air Base using a combination of ballistic missiles and drones. He claimed the attacks disrupted air traffic at the airport and caused damage to the military base.
He added that the armed forces targeted Saudi military supplies, resulting in the "killing and wounding" of Saudi officers.
استهدفت قواتنا المسلحة بصواريخ بالستية إمدادات عسكرية سعودية وصلت إلى معسكر بدر جوار مطار عدن الدولي ونتج عن الاستهدف مصرع وإصابة عدد من الضباط السعوديين. نحذر العدو من استخدام مطار عدن المدني لأي أغراض عسكرية.
In a separate statement, Saree said Houthi forces targeted three military camps — Dagharir in Jizan, Aakifah in Asir and Al-Mawsim in Jizan — with a large number of ballistic missiles and drones.
Separately, the Saudi-led coalition said Wednesday that it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis toward the Riyadh area.

Coalition spokesman Brigaider General Turki al-Maliki said on the US social media platform X that the missile was intercepted north of Riyadh after being launched by the “terrorist Houthi militia.”
Al-Maliki also said that coalition forces had tracked the missile’s launch platform using the coalition’s intelligence systems in the skies over Sanaa, the capital of Yemen.
“We are tracking the launch platform with the Coalition's intelligence system in the skies over Sanaa, and we will destroy it,” he said.\
Yemeni government forces seize key mountain peak in Taiz province
Yemeni government forces said late on Tuesday that they seized a key mountain peak in Taiz province after clashes with the Houthi group.
The Nation’s Shield Forces said on the US social media platform X that their troops captured the highest peak in Jabal Habashi district as part of ongoing military operations in the province.
It provided no further details and there was no immediate comment from the Houthis.
Earlier on Tuesday, the Nation’s Shield Forces launched a large-scale military operation against the Houthis in Taiz’s Al-Wazi’iyah district as part of the broader Operation “Dawn of Yemen.”

title: Quetta to have 2 900 CCTVs
description: Quetta to have 2 900 CCTVs
content:
Integrated security project aims at strengthening policing
The Balochistan government has approved the installation of 2,900 advanced surveillance cameras across Quetta as part of the Quetta Integrated Security Project aimed at strengthening policing and improving the city's security system.
The decision was taken at a high-level security and policing meeting chaired by Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti.
Officials told the meeting that the new surveillance network would be developed under the Quetta Green Digital Corridor. The project is designed to enhance monitoring, strengthen counterterrorism measures and enable security agencies to respond more quickly to emergencies and security incidents.
The government also approved the establishment of additional Quick Response Force (QRF) stations in Quetta to improve the police response to security threats and other emergencies.
The Balochistan Police will undergo further modernization, with officers and personnel to receive advanced training, equipment and other resources to improve their ability to deal with terrorism and emerging security challenges.
Additional Chief Secretary Home and the Inspector General of Balochistan Police briefed the meeting on the province's overall security situation and ongoing policing initiatives.
The meeting was also informed about measures to improve police discipline and accountability. Officials said 871 police personnel had been dismissed over absenteeism and negligence.
In another administrative measure, the services of 1,005 police personnel deployed with various personalities were withdrawn and the personnel were sent back to the police department.
Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti directed the authorities to ensure that police personnel were provided with the training, equipment and support needed to effectively counter terrorism.
"If the police are deployed to fight terrorism, they must also be given full support," Bugti said, reaffirming the provincial government's backing for police and security forces working to maintain peace in Balochistan.
The chief minister also called for tighter control over non-development expenditures and urged officials to redirect available resources towards projects and measures benefiting the public.

title: PTI raises stakes with long march
description: PTI raises stakes with long march
content:
Asad vows to continue protest until demands met
Senior PTI leader Asad Qaiser on Tuesday said the PTI will hold a peaceful long march and continue its protest until its constitutional demands are met, as tensions between the federal government and the party deepen over political rights and governance in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.
Qaiser, a former speaker of the National Assembly and secretary-general of the Tehreek Tahafuz-e-Aain Pakistan, was responding to remarks by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif about the PTI's planned march.
The PTI was not opposed to Pakistan's development and prosperity but wanted to see the country become a developed and progressive state, Qaiser said.
He called on the prime minister to clarify whether the Constitution gives citizens the right to choose their leaders, recalling that former prime minister Nawaz Sharif had campaigned under the slogan "Respect the vote".
Qaiser said the PTI's constitutional rights had been curtailed and alleged that its founder Imran Khan, his wife and sisters were in detention, while more than 2,000 party workers were in jail.
He also accused the federal government of denying Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and its government their constitutional rights, including the province's "due share" under the National Finance Commission (NFC) Award.
He said commitments made to residents of the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA) at the time of their merger with Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa had also not been fulfilled.
Qaiser questioned whether the federal government had met its constitutional responsibilities in the fight against militancy and in addressing worsening law and order in the province.
He said the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government had convened a jirga on the province's security and political situation, attended by representatives of the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N), Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and other parties, which adopted a unanimous resolution.
He questioned whether the federal government would continue to disregard the position expressed by the province's political leadership and other stakeholders.

title: Kenya reports first ever Ebola death
description: Kenya reports first ever Ebola death
content:
Kenya has reported its first-ever Ebola death, the health minister said Tuesday, after a Kenyan man who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) died after returning to the country.
The DRC declared its 17th Ebola outbreak in May. The deadly disease has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the past 50 years.
Kenya has never previously reported a case. Neighbouring Uganda recorded 20 -- almost all people who had travelled from the DRC -- and two deaths, before being declared Ebola-free in August.
The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said a team was heading to Kenya to provide assistance, and its director general Jean Kaseya would also visit in the coming days.
The Kenyan citizen, who has not been named but was referred to as a 40-year-old businessman, fell ill around a month ago and had been treated in the DRC, Health Minister Aden Duale told reporters.
He travelled overland to the Ugandan capital, Kampala, and then flew to Nairobi on October 3.

title: Dozens held for using AI to coerce debtors | The Express Tribune
description:
Dozens held for using 
AI to coerce debtors
content:
NCCIA seizes 40 laptops, 41 mobile phones in raid on illegal call centre
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) has arrested 39 people, including a woman, for allegedly operating an illegal call centre in Lahore, where borrowers who failed to repay digital loans were blackmailed using AI-generated obscene images.
The arrests were made during a raid after investigators obtained search warrants.
According to the investigators, 38 men and a woman were taken into custody, while 40 laptops and 41 mobile phones were seized from the premises. The devices were sealed and will be examined by forensic experts.
The investigators said the call centre was operating several instant loan applications.
Preliminary investigation showed that the loan applications sought access to borrowers' mobile phone galleries and contact lists when installed.
The investigators alleged that recovery agents subsequently used the information to pressure borrowers into repaying loans.
When borrowers failed to repay the loans within the stipulated period, call centre employees used AI tools to manipulate their photographs and create obscene images, they said.
The victims were threatened with distributing the manipulated images among their family members, friends and other contacts unless they made immediate payments.
Borrowers from digital platforms have previously complained of aggressive recovery tactics, excessive charges, access to personal information and harassment.
The Competition Commission of Pakistan warned in 2023 that some digital lending apps sought access to users' contacts and other personal information, while recovery agents had reportedly harassed and abused borrowers and their emergency contacts.
A man had ended his life in Rawalpindi in July 2023 after facing threats and pressure by loan-app recovery agents. The Federal Investigation Agency had arrested several suspects linked to the loan recovery operation.
The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan later introduced additional safeguards for digital nano-lending, including limits on individual and aggregate borrowing, restrictions on the use of borrowers' personal data and requirements for ethical debt collection.
The regulator warned last year that operators of fraudulent lending schemes were increasingly using social media following action against illegal apps.

Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz said thousands of young people in Punjab had received training as per market requirements under a skill development programme. She said 65 per cent of Pakistan's population comprised youth, describing them as a valuable national asset. They are being provided skills development training.

Young people were being provided technical and vocational training in line with modern requirements in various sectors, with millions in Punjab being equipped with skills according to the requirements of the local job market.
Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz said the construction of 200,000 to 250,000 houses under the Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar programme was a game changer in the housing sector. People from other provinces were coming to Punjab in search of better employment opportunities and a brighter future, she added.
The chief minister appreciated the development achieved in fisheries and other sectors in Oman. ul She said Punjab was the backbone of Pakistan's agricultural economy.
Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz said a pilot programme for shrimp farming launched last year to promote aquaculture in Punjab had proved successful.

title: PCB takes control of Niaz Stadium for 20 years
description: PCB takes control of Niaz Stadium for 20 years
content:
Board says PSL matches may not come to Hyderabad until 2030
The historic Niaz Cricket Stadium has been handed back to the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) for the second time in less than two decades, with the board promising to turn the ageing venue into an international-standard facility - although cricket-starved fans may have to wait until 2030 for a Pakistan Super League (PSL) match.
The PCB and Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (HMC) signed a 20-year MoU on Tuesday, placing the stadium under the board's management for redevelopment, upgrading and professional operation.
The agreement was signed at the stadium by PCB Chief Operating Officer Sumair Ahmad Syed and Hyderabad Mayor Kashif Ali Shoro, six months after Hyderabad's Kingsmen made their debut in the 11th edition of the PSL.
Under the agreement, the PCB will pay just Rs10,000 a month in rent and share 20% of net gate-receipt profits with the HMC. The board, however, will retain exclusive commercial rights over ticketing, hospitality, advertising, broadcasting and sponsorships.
The PCB will also bear the entire cost of development and renovation, including work on the pitch, outfield, floodlights, pavilion, media facilities and spectator stands.
Despite the fresh takeover, the return of major cricket to Hyderabad remains some distance away. Syed said the PCB would try to bring PSL matches to Niaz Stadium by 2030, but only after the venue meets International Cricket Council (ICC) standards.
The stadium's existing capacity of around 12,000 spectators will have to be increased to 20,000, while floodlights, and a media gallery will also have to be installed before it can host major international-level events, he said.
Syed said the upgraded stadium would help promote domestic cricket in the region. He also announced plans to establish a regional cricket academy at the venue in January or February next year, with trials planned for Under-16, Under-17 and Under-19 players.
Mayor Shoro said the provincial government and HMC had undertaken renovation work at the stadium in recent years in response to public demand for its restoration. "Citizens also want to see PSL matches at Niaz Stadium at the earliest," he said.
Built in 1961, Niaz Stadium was named after the then commissioner of Hyderabad. It hosted its last One-Day International on January 24, 2008, when Pakistan played Zimbabwe. This is not the first time the PCB has been given control of the venue. In 2007, then Hyderabad Mayor Kunwar Naveed Jamil had handed over the stadium to the board with similar objectives. However, after no significant upgrade was carried out, the Municipal Committee Qasimabad took the facility back from the PCB.

title: Khairpur s last ruler Talpur  laid to rest
description: Khairpur s last ruler Talpur  laid to rest
content:
Thousands attend funeral of Talpur who had signed the state's accession to Pakistan
The last ruler of the formerly princely state of Khairpur in Sindh, who passed away on Monday, was laid to rest at a graveyard in Kot Diji on Tuesday, with tens of thousands of people attending his Namaz-e-Janaza and burial.
Mir Ali Murad Khan Talpur, who signed the accession of Khairpur to Pakistan, breathed his last at the age of 93, having survived death at the age of nine months when a bullet, allegedly fired accidentally from a gun in his father's hands, pierced one of his lungs.
"I never saw my father happy in his entire life," Mehdi Raza Khan Talpur, one of his two sons, said while talking to the media at the funeral. "But now I believe he will be happy because he always considered life an imprisonment of the soul."
Allama Shehansha Naqvi, who led the Namaz-e-Janaza, remarked that an important chapter in the history of Khairpur had closed with his death. "One of his messages was that it is possible for people to remain divinely connected with the Almighty even if they possess a lot of wealth," he said.
Born on June 29, 1933, in Brighton, England, he was named after King George V. Talpur later attended St Bonaventure's High School in Hyderabad and graduated from Aitchison College, Lahore, before leaving for the UK in 1950 to pursue higher studies at Cambridge University.
Talpur was enthroned in July 1947 as Khairpur's ruler while he was still a minor and his father, Faiz Muhammad Khan Talpur, was alive, on the recommendation of George Mountbatten. He signed an accession agreement with the provincial govt, headed by the then CM Mir Ghulam Hussain Khan Talpur, on October 3, 1947. Six days later, on October 9, 1947, Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah signed the accession.
However, his state retained its authority and even its own army. The military powers of the state were handed over to Pakistan following an agreement in February 1949.
Under the deceased prince, Khairpur's status gradually changed from a semi-controlled to a fully administered province until November 10, 1954, when Khairpur's provincial assembly passed a resolution merging itself with Pakistan. Ten days later, Talpur's status as an independent ruler was abolished.
His family resides in Khairpur's Faiz Mahal, a late-18th-century palace built in 1798 by his forefather, Mir Sohrab Khan Talpur.

Witnesses point to suspicious vehicles, alleged surveillance ahead of the killing
Sealed written statements of three senior police officers were submitted before the Judicial Commission probing the murder of Wafflix's owner Mir Raza Ali on Tuesday, while witnesses told the panel that suspicious vehicles appeared to have followed the victim before the killing.
The statements were submitted by Karachi police chief AIG Azad Khan, DIG East Farrukh Lanjar and DIG Amir Farooqi, who headed the second investigation committee constituted to probe the case.
Mir Raza's family had requested that the three officers be summoned and questioned by the commission. However, the panel rejected the request and instead forwarded written questions submitted by the family to the officers. Their responses were subsequently submitted to the commission in sealed form.
During Tuesday's hearing, security guard Muhammad Riaz appeared as a witness and told the commission that he worked at a house near Masjid Khizra in Gulistan-e-Jauhar.
Riaz said that at around 3.24am to 3.28am on July 29, he went to the rooftop to smoke a cigarette when he noticed two vehicles near the area. A driver appeared to be struggling to take one of the vehicles up a slope, he added.
Responding to questions from the commission, Riaz said he had seen one man who abused someone and remarked, "You can't get the vehicle up." He said both vehicles were white and that he had not seen either of them in the area before that night. A motorcycle also passed through the area during the incident, he added.
Mir Raza's counsel, Advocate Jibran Nasir, asked the witness whether police had visited his house. Riaz said he had heard from some boys that police had visited and were making inquiries.
Advocate Nasir told the commission that the registration number of the suspicious vehicle had been provided to police and that it was registered in the name of a man identified as Tariq.
Two journalists, Babar Saleem and Sault Jaferi, also recorded their statements before the commission. Saleem said CCTV footage appeared to show that Mir Raza was being surveilled. He said the vehicle following Mir Raza from Gulistan-e-Jauhar stopped outside the guesthouse.

Sindh has reported 93 confirmed cases of mpox so far this year, with 11 deaths attributed to the viral disease, according to the latest report of the Provincial Disease Surveillance and Response Unit's (PDSRU) laboratory surveillance network.

Hospital officials said the patient had rashes on his hands and feet, raising suspicion of mpox. Samples were collected for further diagnostic and laboratory testing.
Experts said mpox is a viral disease that can spread through close physical or skin-to-skin contact with an infected person, as well as contact with lesions, bodily fluids or contaminated objects. Common symptoms include fever, headache, body aches, weakness, swollen lymph nodes and skin rashes or blisters. People developing symptoms have been advised to avoid close contact with others and seek immediate medical evaluation and diagnostic testing.

title: KU s  fails  become  passes
description: KU s  fails  become  passes
content:
150+ LLB students 'cleared' after scrutiny despite rules; conflicting accounts offered
In the curious arithmetic of university examinations, scores that once spelt failure have apparently been transformed into passes - and in some cases by a wide margin - at the University of Karachi.
An investigation has uncovered what appears to be a controversial exercise in changing the examination results of a large number of LLB students during the brief tenure of KU's recently retired acting vice chancellor, with documents suggesting that answer scripts were re-examined after students had already been declared failed.
Around 150 students of SM Law College and Islamia Law College, who were initially shown as having failed in at least two subjects, were subsequently declared successful following what the report describes as a scrutiny process. Some students who had reportedly secured zero or very low marks in subjects were allegedly awarded marks ranging from 50 to 65.
The matter has raised questions over the legality of the process, particularly because KU rules, according to former vice chancellor Dr Khalid Iraqi, permit recounting under the annual examination system but do not allow rechecking of answer scripts.
Documents obtained by The Express Tribune include copies of examination papers, original and revised mark sheets, award sheets, minutes of the scrutiny committee meeting and approval documents of the acting VC.
According to the documents, a scrutiny committee comprising Dean of the Faculty of Law Barrister Sarfraz Metlo, officials of the two law colleges and the controller of examinations was formed. The committee met on August 5 under the chairmanship of the dean and decided to re-examine answer scripts for Paper 5 of LLB Part II.
The following day, August 6, the controller of examinations obtained approval from Acting VC Dr Tufail Ahmed for the committee's recommendations. The approval reportedly included the phrase "other related cases", after which students who had failed in Pakistan Studies were also brought within the process.
The principal of SM Law College subsequently asked students to apply for scrutiny following the VC's approval.
The development is particularly significant because former permanent VC Dr Khalid Iraqi had earlier stopped a similar request. Speaking to The Express Tribune, Iraqi said a collective application had been submitted by students, whereas the university rules required individual applications for scrutiny.
He said that under the annual examination system, scrutiny involved recounting and did not permit rechecking of answer scripts. He therefore stopped the process.
The latest case, however, has produced sharply conflicting accounts from university officials. Controller of Examinations Dr Yasir denied that any failed students had been passed. "It is incorrect information. No failed student was passed. I have nothing more to say," he said when The Express Tribune approached him for his version.
Dean of the Faculty of Law Barrister Sarfraz Metlo, however, confirmed that the results had been changed, while insisting that the process was lawful. "We obtained approval from the VC and formed a scrutiny committee. The students had been treated unfairly," he said, adding that 89% of the students had been failed by the same teacher.
According to Metlo, the papers were re-examined in the presence of the principals of both colleges and the controller of examinations.
He denied that students with zero marks had been passed, saying only those who had failed by a few marks were cleared. Metlo also maintained that university law allowed answer scripts to be re-examined.
SM Law College Principal Professor Fareed Dayo gave a similar account, saying around 180 students had been failed by a teacher from Islamia College and that the students were taken before the scrutiny committee, which passed those who had been treated unfairly. Islamia Law College Principal Professor Nadeem Advocate, when contacted, distanced himself from the matter. "I know nothing about it. Whatever you want to ask, ask the Dean of Law," he told The Express Tribune.
The episode comes days after Dr Waseem Qazi was appointed VC by the Sindh chief minister, placing the controversy among the early administrative challenges facing the university's new leadership.
The revised results have already enabled the affected students to move ahead with their academic plans and prepare for subsequent examinations, while questions remain over the authority under which their answer scripts were re-examined and their results altered.

title: No death warrants in Punjab for 12 years
description: No death warrants in Punjab for 12 years
content:
As many as 211 convicts remain on death row in Rawalpindi alone
Sessions and special anti-terrorism courts in Rawalpindi district and elsewhere in Punjab have not issued a death warrant for any convict in a murder or terrorism case for the past 12 years, effectively halting executions in the province.
No death-row convict has been hanged in any jail during this period, resulting in the virtual disappearance of work for executioners. Around 90% of jail executioners have reportedly been dismissed, leaving only about 10% on a daily-wage or standby basis, with none holding a permanent post.
Despite the Supreme Court having rejected their final appeals, 31 convicts are currently awaiting execution, while their mercy petitions remain pending before the President. Review petitions have also been filed by about a dozen convicts.
During the past 12 years, only four convicts in three high-profile cases were executed in Punjab. Aqeel alias Dr Usman and Arshad Mehar were hanged at Adiala Jail in 2014 in the GHQ and Pervez Musharraf attack cases.
Mumtaz Qadri, convicted of assassinating former Punjab governor Salman Taseer, was executed at Adiala Jail in 2016. Imran Ali, convicted of abducting, raping and murdering minor Zainab in Kasur, was hanged at Lahore Jail in 2018.
No convict in an ordinary murder or terrorism case has been executed during the period.
Criminal lawyer Shanzeb Khan said executions had effectively remained suspended amid international pressure from human rights organisations, the United Nations and the European Union.
In Rawalpindi Division, 211 convicts are currently on death row, including three women. Appeals against 72 death sentences in murder and terrorism cases are pending before the High Court, while 153 cases are pending before the Supreme Court and 11 before the Federal Shariat Court.
Mercy petitions involving 36 convicts are awaiting decisions by the President, while review petitions against the sentences of 62 convicts have been filed. Some petitions seek relief on the basis of compromise with the victim's family or conversion of the death sentence into life imprisonment.
Officials of the Sessions and Anti-Terrorism Courts said death warrants were issued when a case file was returned after the Supreme Court had rejected an appeal and the President had rejected a mercy petition. They said no such file had been received for the past 12 years.
The prolonged suspension of executions has also affected executioners. Under jail rules, an executioner is a Grade-4 employee, but about 90% have been removed. Only standby executioners remain and are paid Rs2,500 for carrying out an execution.
Members of the family of Tara Masih, the executioner who hanged former prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, continue to work as executioners on a payroll basis.
According to an Assistant Superintendent of Adiala Jail, before an execution, the executioner covers the convict's face and quietly tells him: "I have no desire or interest in your death; I am only performing my duty."

title: Protests in France escalate
description: Protests in France escalate
content:
Police fire teargas at protesters on biggest day of school demonstrations
Police fired tear gas at protesters blockading French high schools on Tuesday as students, teachers and parents took to the streets on the biggest day of action in a wave of demonstrations against understaffed and dilapidated classrooms.
In Marseille and Nantes, protesters held up signs marked with "The state has killed national education" and other messages, in largely peaceful rallies. In Toulouse, parents linked arms at the front of a march through the city.
But in Strasbourg, Lyon and Rennes, the demonstrations at times turned violent, with police firing tear gas and protesters lighting fires in the streets and hurling projectiles.
"There is such a gap between the elites and us," said Hugo Vetzel, a recent high-school graduate in Strasbourg.
The protests began in September in the deprived suburbs of Paris, before spreading nationwide, presenting a major challenge to President Emmanuel Macron's cash-strapped government at a time when it faces strong economic headwinds.
The High School Students Union said more than half of France's high schools were blockaded or would close for the day. Some local education authorities have tried to move classes online.
"We want more money for the national educational system so that high schools are renovated," said Roberta, another recent high-school graduate at a protest outside Paris' prestigious Henri IV school.
Schools were facing a list of problems from water leaks to rat infestations, she added.
The government has responded to the demonstrations with riot police.
Rights groups, students and parent groups have accused authorities of using disproportionate force against minors. The government says the protest movement has been hijacked by outsiders and morphed into urban violence.
France's interior ministry said 6,100 people have been arrested since the protests began, the overwhelming majority of them minors. More than 1,800 people are being prosecuted, including 1,483 minors, the justice ministry said, without specifying the crimes.

Dozens of Indian opposition lawmakers began a march seeking the resignation of the election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists, as hundreds of security personnel kept vigil in the heart of the Indian capital and barricades were thrown up.
Parties opposing Prime Minister Narendra Modi and members of the popular 'cockroach' youth movement launched protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar - appointed by Modi's government - after the Indian Express newspaper reported divisions in the poll body last month.

"The Election Commission is a puppet in the hands of the government. We are fighting to save our democracy," Mallikarjun Kharge, president of the main opposition Congress party, told reporters as the march began.
Hundreds of security personnel, including paramilitaries in fatigues, fanned out in the area, with barricades thrown up and several routes closed. Television showed security personnel, some holding batons, outside the barricaded Election Commission office.
Congress and other parties allege that the revised voter lists benefit Modi and his party. Kumar has not commented on the issue, but the commission and Modi's BJP denied the accusations.
Authorities advised against travel around planned protest areas and shut off some routes.
Tuesday's event is the latest of a series of almost daily demonstrations by student organisations, political parties and the 'cockroach' movement, which began last week.
India's Supreme Court agreed a day earlier to hear legal arguments seeking its intervention in the accusations against the poll body's voter drive and the conduct of its chief.

Former German spy chief August Hanning was detained on Tuesday on suspicion of attempted treason in a case that ranks among Germany's biggest intelligence scandals since the Cold War.

Five years after his seven-year tenure as head of the BND foreign intelligence service ended in 2005, Hanning agreed with a former BND office manager to receive confidential intelligence information in exchange for payment, according to prosecutors.
The office manager, identified as Manfred D. in line with privacy rules, was also arrested on Tuesday, and both were due to appear before a judge at the Federal Court of Justice.

title: Belgian-American wins Nobel in Physics | The Express Tribune
description:
Belgian-American wins
Nobel in Physics
content:
'Neutrino man' credited with opening new era of astronomy
The Belgian-American Francis Halzen won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work creating an Antarctic observatory of ice to detect high-energy neutrinos, elusive subatomic particles that can reveal otherwise inaccessible information about the cosmos.
Halzen, 82, realised that pristine ice at the South Pole could be used to track such neutrinos, sometimes known as "ghost particles" for the way they pass through the Earth without a trace, only interacting with matter extremely rarely.
"The messengers bring information from the cosmos," Eva Olsson, of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, told a press conference. "They open the door to distant galaxies and tell us about the processes of exploding stars."
The interactions registered by the IceCube observatory provide information about how high-energy neutrinos are created and may even reveal previously unknown phenomena, the Academy said.
In 2014, the US-based Smithsonian magazine dubbed Halzen "Neutrino Man" when giving him one of its Ingenuity Awards, acclaiming him for an "amazing experiment (that) heralds the beginning of a new era in astronomy".
It even published a comic illustrating his life: "How One Physicist's Pursuit of the Cosmos Took Off in Antarctica".
The observatory - in effect a telescopethat shows neutrinos instead of light - is set in a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice, which extends to a depth of 2,500 metres below the surface near the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station.

title: Pakistan bears region s biggest poverty burden
description: Pakistan bears region s biggest poverty burden
content:
World Bank says 48% poor in MENAAP region live in Pakistan
The World Bank said on Tuesday that nearly half of the Middle East and North African region's poor people earning less than $3 a day live in Pakistan and poverty in the country increased due to prolonged economic adjustment that weakened real household incomes and employment opportunities.
In its Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan (MENAAP) region report, the Washington-based lender also said that population-growth adjusted real GDP growth in Pakistan would remain at 2.2% in this fiscal year, which is almost at the last year's level.
Overall, the World Bank has projected 3.8% economic growth rate and 8.2% inflation rate in Pakistan during the current fiscal year 2026-27.
The World Bank had separated Pakistan from the South Asia region and clubbed it with the Middle East and North Africa region.
"Pakistan accounts for about 48% of the people in the region living below the $3 per day (about Rs840 daily income) poverty line", according to the report that the lender released on Tuesday evening.
The report stated that the remaining poor people were concentrated in Afghanistan, Syria, and Yemen the three war-affected countries, which together accounted for another 47% of people living below the poverty line of $3 per day income.
The report further stated that most recent estimates showed poverty rates at the $3 per day line approached or exceeded 20% in Djibouti, Pakistan, Syria, and Yemen.
The latest World Bank Group estimates showed that MENAAP accounts for 14% of the world's extreme poor, second only to Sub-Saharan Africa. After declining substantially during the 2000s and 2010s, poverty reduction stalled around 2019 and reversed following the COVID-19 pandemic.
The regional increase in poverty was "driven primarily by a rise in poverty in Pakistan, where the poverty rate rose by 6.4 percentage points at the $3 per day line and 3.2 percentage points at the $4.2 per day line between 2018-19 and 2024-25 following a succession of adverse shocks, including the COVID-19 pandemic, the devastating 2022 floods, a macroeconomic crisis marked by high inflation and currency depreciation, and a prolonged period of economic adjustment that weakened real household incomes and employment opportunities," according to report.
There has been criticism over the prolonged period of economic adjustments under the IMF programmes that improved the fiscal and monetary numbers but contributed to low economic growth with high poverty and high unemployment.
The report showed that compared to 2.1% last year, the real GDP per capita growth could be 2.2% in this fiscal year. It has also projected a current account deficit of 0.8% of the GDP and the budget deficit of 3.5% -the two key indicators that are higher than the previous fiscal but remain within the manageable limits.
The World Bank said that the governments in the region face simultaneous demands to cushion households from higher prices and respond to conflict-related humanitarian needs. Pakistan has introduced targeted fuel and farm assistance, it added.
The World Bank said that the petrol price increases were 40% or higher in Lebanon, Pakistan, the Syrian Arab Republic, and the United Arab Emirates. Diesel prices rose, on average, by more than 80% in Lebanon and nearly 70% in the United Arab Emirates and have exceeded 40% in Pakistan and the West Bank and Gaza since the start of the Middle East conflict.
Oil-importing countriesDjibouti, Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, Pakistan, and Tunisiaremain exposed through economic channels, including rising inflationary pressures from higher oil and other commodity prices, loss of fiscal space, a decline in remittances from the Gulf economies, and increased costs of borrowing, mainly because of higher insurance risk as the conflict persists.
Pakistan's private sector has also not yet adapted to emerging needs of the economy. The World Bank report stated that the share of firms that introduced a new product or service in the past three yearsa measure of product innovationis significantly lower in MENAAP than in peer economies.
In Egypt, just 9% of firms report product innovation and 3% process innovation; in Pakistan, just 3% of firms reported product innovation and 1% process innovation against a lower-middle-income peer average of 23% for product and 14% for process.
The report noted that AI use is more concentrated in a small number of occupations in the rest of the MENAAP economies. Pakistan records the highest absolute conversation count in MENAAP, but usage is concentrated in arts and media (including graphic design, content creation, and translation rather than software, potentially reflecting the country's large presence on international freelance platforms on which these services are in demand.
Across MENAAP since the introduction of ChatGPT, demand for AI remains concentrated in occupations within the technical core. Across the region, the share of job postings requiring any digital skills increased substantially between 2021 and 2025 in almost all countries, with double-digit percentage point gains in Bahrain, Lebanon, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia
Across MENAAP, Internet use is often above what income levels would predict, but uneven broadband penetration and gaps in electricity access still limit the physical foundations for AI adoption.
Eight MENAAP countriesDjibouti, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Oman, Pakistan, Syria, and Yemenfall below the benchmark line, indicating lower mobile broadband subscriptions than income peers, according to the report.

title: UN chief lauds Pakistan s mediation role
description: UN chief lauds Pakistan s mediation role
content:
Guterres praises Islamabad's US-Iran diplomacy, honours Pakistani peacekeepers
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Tuesday praised Pakistan's role in creating conditions for dialogue between the United States and Iran, saying Islamabad's mediation had helped deliver an agreement, ceasefire and framework for future negotiations while reaffirming the UN's support for Pakistan.
Speaking alongside Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar in Islamabad, Guterres said Pakistan's efforts had demonstrated the importance of trusted countries at a time of growing global divisions and mistrust. He said every Pakistani should be proud of the country's pivotal role in promoting diplomacy and de-escalation.
"From Islamabad, I want to send a loud and clear message to all parties: end the conflict, return to diplomacy," Guterres said, urging the restoration of navigational rights and freedoms in accordance with international law. He also stressed that lasting peace in the region required the Palestinian people's right to self-determination.
Dar said Pakistan's facilitation of dialogue between Washington and Tehran reflected its broader commitment to negotiation, mediation and peaceful settlement of disputes. He said Islamabad had sought to promote diplomacy during its current tenure on the UN Security Council and cited its initiative on Resolution 2788 on strengthening multilateralism.
The two leaders also discussed Palestine, Jammu and Kashmir, Afghanistan, counter-terrorism, climate change, peacekeeping and the future of multilateralism. Dar reiterated Pakistan's position on Kashmir and urged implementation of relevant UN Security Council resolutions, while also raising India's decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance.
He urged India to fulfil its obligations under the treaty and stop "weaponising water", while also expressing concern over the continued use of Afghan soil for terrorist attacks against Pakistan. Guterres acknowledged Pakistan's struggle against terrorism, stressing that legitimate security concerns must be addressed within international law, human rights and the rule of law.
Earlier, President Asif Ali Zardari conferred Nishan-e-Imtiaz on Guterres in recognition of his international service, UN leadership and contribution to global peace and development. The award was the first conferred by Pakistan on a UN secretary-general and was presented at a special investiture ceremony at Aiwan-e-Sadr.
During his meeting with the president, Guterres was praised for his principled leadership and support for dialogue, while Zardari reaffirmed Pakistan's backing for Palestinian self-determination and a two-state solution. He also stressed that the Indus Waters Treaty was a binding international agreement that could not be unilaterally suspended.
Zardari said Pakistan remained committed to combating terrorism and expressed concern over terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory. He also highlighted Pakistan's contribution to UN peacekeeping, noting that more than 270,000 Pakistani peacekeepers had served in 48 UN missions around the world.
Guterres paid tribute to Pakistani peacekeepers, saying more than 180 had lost their lives serving international peace. He also praised Pakistan and Denmark for leading Security Council Resolution 2823 on accountability for crimes against UN peacekeepers, describing it as the resolution with the largest number of co-sponsors in Security Council history.
On climate change, Guterres recalled his visit during Pakistan's catastrophic 2022 floods, saying he had witnessed both devastation and the resilience of its people. He said Pakistan was on the front lines of climate change despite contributing only a tiny fraction of global emissions and called on developed countries to provide finance, technology and support.
Guterres also called for reform of the international system, saying the Security Council no longer adequately represented today's world. He pointed to Africa's lack of permanent representation and divisions among the five permanent members, urging a more representative UN and greater access for developing countries to development finance and debt relief.
"I am here to further strengthen our partnership and to reaffirm a simple message: the United Nations stands with the people of Pakistan," Guterres said, thanking Pakistan for its contribution to the world and reaffirming the importance of dialogue, mediation and diplomacy.

title: Two FBR officials killed in DI Khan
description: Two FBR officials killed in DI Khan
content:
Five people, including three government officials, were killed and two others injured in two separate firing incidents in Dera Ismail Khan on Tuesday, with unidentified armed attackers targeting Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) officials and a highway police vehicle.
According to DI Khan District Police Officer Ziauddin Ahmed, four people, including two FBR officials, were killed when unidentified armed motorcyclists opened fire near Bhatti Pump on DI Khan's University Road, within the jurisdiction of University Police Station, at around 11:40am.
According to an FBR statement, three officials of its Enforcement Squad, Sepoy Izharullah, Guard Rahmatullah, and Sepoy Sulaiman were performing duty at the designated point when unidentified armed persons arrived at the location and opened fire upon them.
As a result of the firing, Guard Rahmatullah and Sepoy Sulaiman embraced martyrdom. Sepoy Izharullah returned fire during the incident, following which the assailants fled the scene.
The attackers also took away official arms and ammunition issued to the squad personnel. Rescue 1122 personnel later shifted the bodies of the four victims to the District Headquarters Hospital.
In a separate attack, unidentified armed men targeted a highway police mobile vehicle near Gulistan Chowk on the bypass. The firing left the vehicle's driver, Highway Traffic Police Constable Habib, dead, while mobile incharge Subhan and another constable sustained injuries.
The injured officials and the body of the martyred policeman were shifted to the Trauma Centre for treatment and medico-legal formalities.
Later, the funeral prayers of Constable Habib and FBR officials Rehmatullah and Suleman were offered at the city's Aijaz Shaheed Police Lines with full official honours.
MNA Faisal Amin Khan Gandapur, Division Commissioner Dawar Khan, Station Commander Brigadier Salman Adil Shah, Regional Police Officer Dera Ghulam Mubashir Maken, DPO Ziauddin Ahmed, FBR officials, political and social figures, and senior police and security officials attended the funeral prayers.
A smartly turned-out police contingent presented a guard of honour to the martyrs. The participants laid floral wreaths on the coffins and prayed for the elevation of the martyrs' ranks, forgiveness for the deceased and patience for their bereaved families.
Senior officials also met the families of the victims and expressed their condolences. They assured the bereaved families that the sacrifices of the martyrs were a matter of pride for the state and nation and that their blood would not go in vain.
Later, in a statement, the FBR expressed deep grief over the tragic killing of its two officials
FBR Chairman Rashid Mahmood Langrial expressed his heartfelt condolences to the families of the martyred officials and paid homage to their courage and commitment. He said the sacrifices rendered by FBR personnel in the line of duty will not be forgotten.
"The FBR stands firmly with the families of its martyred officials and all personnel performing their duties in the service of the country," it added.

title: PTI dismisses  mere offer   asks PM to walk the talk
description: PTI dismisses  mere offer   asks PM to walk the talk
content:
Gohar says party has not been given access to Imran for almost a year
The PTI on Tuesday dismissed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's proposal for renewed talks as a "mere offer", while saying that the government could contact leaders of the opposition in the National Assembly and Senate for negotiations if it were sincere.
The statement came amid heightened political tensions in the country as the PTI's long march reached Kohat.
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi is leading the convoy, which began its march towards Islamabad on Sunday to demand the release of party founder Imran Khan and press the government over what PTI describes as broader political and constitutional grievances.
The premier earlier in the day renewed an offer of talks to the PTI, saying the government was prepared to engage with the opposition if the party ended its long march and sit-ins.
Speaking to the media outside Adiala jail after being denied permission for a meeting with Imran, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan dismissed Shehbaz's offer.
"This proposal of dialogue and talks is only at the level of a mere offer and no positive steps are being taken for this purpose by the government," the PTI chairman underlined.
Gohar said that the party had not been granted access for a meeting with Imran since almost a year. "It is a matter of grave concern for us that we have not been able to meet Imran Khan for a year, as our last meeting with him was on October 16 2025".
He questioned if Imran's doctors, family, party workers and his lawyers were not being allowed to meet him, then what steps was the government taking?
"This is inhumane treatment, and we have strongly condemned it.
"We have stood with the state and have raised the slogan of Pakistan with sincerity, but despite this, we have not been provided access to Imran," he stated.
Gohar said Imran and his wife were in jail and even Imran's three sisters, who had nothing to do with politics, had been imprisoned, further enquiring as to why Imran' sisters had been arrested and if so, why they had been put in jail.
"We consider it a crime for Imran's sisters to spend even one day in jail. His sisters are apolitical and have only stood up for their brother."
Gohar further condemned the arrest of Imran's cousin, Qasim Zaman.
"Our MPAs, MNAs and ministers have been picked up, and this practice of picking people and detaining them should now stop forever".
Meanwhile, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja stated that the government could contact Leader of the Opposition in the Senate, Allama Raja Nasir Abbas and Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly, Mahmood Khan Achakzai, for further talks and negotiations.
Speaking to the media outside the Islamabad High Court, Raja underscored that the long march would continue until matters had been adequately "resolved", further adding that a false narrative was being propagated that the long march had been cancelled.
"Imran has given complete authority to Allama Raja Nasir Abbas and Mahmood Khan Achakzai to negotiate on his behalf and make an agreement, and if the government wants to show some flexibility and negotiate, it can contact them," Raja stated.
National Assembly Leader of Opposition Mahmood Khan Achakzai has instructed the opposition to respond positively to any contact from the government.
Achakzai, who also heads an opposition parties alliance TTAP, sent a message to opposition leaders through TTAP spokesperson Akhundzada Hussain Yousafzai, saying that if the government makes contact, it should be given a positive response.
Sources said Achakzai maintained that the first condition for any government contact should be a meeting with PTI's incarcerated founder Imran Khan, adding that the government could demonstrate positive progress by securing the release of his sisters.
According to sources, Achakzai said that if a meeting with the PTI founder did not take place, meeting the prime minister would be meaningless. He said that if access to the founder was not granted, the opposition could consider refusing to meet the prime minister.

title: Offering talks, PM asks PTI to 'come to its senses' | The Express Tribune
description:
Offering talks, PM asks PTI to 'come
to its senses'
content:
PM says dialogue possible if long march is called off Warns agitation could hurt economy, global standing Says g
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday exhorted the opposition Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) to come to its "senses and abandon its agitational politics", warning that it would severely harm the country's economic growth and international standing.
Addressing the groundbreaking ceremony of the Kashmir Chowk Underpass in Islamabad, the prime minister urged the PTI to call off its long march, saying that dialogue could only take place if the party ended its protests.
"I still ask them to come to their senses. End your long marches and sit-ins. Once you end them, we will certainly sit down with you and talk so that Pakistan moves forward with mutual hard work, honesty, and integrity. This is the desire of the nation, the voice of every Pakistani," the prime minister told the ceremony.
Shehbaz said the PTI had again resorted to the politics of sit-ins and long marches despite the government's sincere efforts to engage in meaningful negotiations. He warned that protests would disrupt exports, manufacturing and imports.
He said a joint committee comprising representatives from the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) had held talks with the opposition, but the process stalled after the PTI demanded last-minute changes to the finalised draft.
"Their sole objective was to sabotage the dialogue," he continued. "As a result of the politics of sit-ins and long marches, the primary target will be your economy. If your labourer or your engineer fails to reach the factory, the manufacturing site, or their office on time, whose loss is it? It is the loss of this country."
The prime minister told the audience that the government had successfully restored macroeconomic stability and was striving for growth through collective teamwork, with positive indicators reflected in rising exports, remittances and industrial production.
He cautioned that undermining these hard-won achievements would amount to hostility towards the state. "We will not allow this to happen. The law will take its course. Protecting the lives and property of the people is our responsibility, and we will ensure this by all means," he said.
Earlier, the prime minister performed the groundbreaking of the underpass, which is being constructed at a cost of Rs1.4 billion to ease traffic flow between Islamabad and Rawalpindi. The project features four slip roads. At present, the intersection handles 107,000 vehicles and faces congestion during peak hours.
The ceremony was attended by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry, Chairman of the Capital Development Authority Sohail Ashraf and others.
In his speech, Shehbaz appreciated Naqvi and his team for setting the target of completing the Kashmir Chowk project within a month. As the intersection is known as Kashmir Chowk, Shehbaz said, the milestone would one day reach Srinagar when the Kashmiri people achieved their inalienable right to freedom.
On the occasion, Naqvi said the project was part of the prime minister's vision to transform and beautify Islamabad ahead of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Heads of State and Government Summit in Islamabad next year.
He noted that upon completion of the Kashmir Chowk and Expressway service road projects, travel time between the twin cities would be reduced from the current 30 minutes to just 16 to 18 minutes. He said Minister of State Talal Chaudhry was personally overseeing two key initiatives.
Highlighting environmental and recreational schemes, Naqvi mentioned that F-9 Park was being upgraded along the lines of London's Hyde Park. Additionally, a safari park, projected to be Asia's largest, along with another park matching the size of F-9, would be developed.
"By the time we leave office, we will make Islamabad three times greener than it was," he said. He also announced that the complete digitisation of land records would be finalised by the end of this year. Naqvi said the elected representatives were working tirelessly for the welfare of the people.

'The Social Reckoning' presents unflinching portrayal of Meta CEO
Aaron Sorkin's The Social Reckoning is drawing attention for its unflinching portrayal of Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and its examination of the Facebook Files, with the film receiving its world premiere in New York ahead of its October 9 release.
The Sony Pictures production focuses on Frances Haugen, the former Facebook employee whose 2021 disclosures exposed internal company research and intensified scrutiny of the social media giant. Mikey Madison plays Haugen, while Jeremy Strong portrays Zuckerberg.
According to The Hollywood Reporter, Strong's performance presents Zuckerberg as a highly controlled and unsympathetic figure, marking a sharp departure from Jesse Eisenberg's more youthful interpretation of the Meta founder in The Social Network. The film depicts internal debates over platform policies, engagement and the consequences of decisions made by Facebook executives.
The project also drew attention through an unusual promotional campaign on Instagram. The advertisement states that Zuckerberg will love The Social Reckoning before adding a reference to Instagram's approach to advertising fact checking. The campaign deliberately connects the film's marketing with one of its central themes.
Sorkin's screenplay incorporates material from Haugen's Senate testimony, including concerns she raised about the company's handling of safety and its business priorities. The story also revisits reporting surrounding Facebook's algorithms and the way content that generates strong emotional reactions can spread across its platforms.
The film arrives at a time when Meta continues to face scrutiny over the effects of its services on young users. The company reached a settlement with US state attorneys general in a case concerning allegations related to children and its platforms.

title: Did Homer write  The Odyssey  in a Turkish cave
description: Did Homer write  The Odyssey  in a Turkish cave
content:
Travellers from around the world visit 'Homer's Valley' outside Izmir where author is said to have penned his works
On a Turkish hillside overlooking the olive-covered slopes outside Izmir is a cave known to generations of locals as the place where Homer penned "The Odyssey".
"This place was always called Homer's Valley by the locals. Travellers from all over the world would come and see the cave where Homer is said to have composed his poems," explained Turkish researcher Altan Altin, who has written a book on the subject.
In fact, nobody knows exactly where Homer wrote his epic poems and there is much mythology around the idea of his cave. Today, of course, the debate has become livelier and more immediate thanks to Christopher Nolan's blockbuster film "The Odyssey".
The poet has for a very long time been associated with the Izmir region of Turkey's Aegean coast, which for most of its history was known as ancient Smyrna.
"The Smyrnaeans have the river Meles, with its lovely water, and at its springs is the grotto, where they say Homer composed his poems," wrote the 2nd-century Greek chronicler and geographer Pausanias.
Those words have fuelled a centuries-long debate, one that continues today, about Homer's life and the location of the river where he was thought to have been born in the year 8 BC.
Visiting the cave, which is filled with rocks, is not easy.
Inside, travellers have left Greek scrawled on the walls, although it is not clear how old the writing is.
Although other places, notably the Greek island of Chios, also lay claim to Homer's origins, ancient Smyrna and its hinterland -- where Bornova is located -- are closely associated with the poet.
"For me, there's no doubt, Homer is from Bornova. In any case, he is from Ionia, which includes Smyrna and Chios. He's from these lands," Altin told AFP. Ionia is the name of an ancient Greek region on Turkey's Aegean coast.
To support his thesis, Altin pointed to a 3rd-century BC frieze depicting the deification of Homer, which he says reproduced the Bornova cave with remarkable precision.
"This bas-relief was already known, but no one had ever noticed the identical details to those found in Homer's cave. This is the first time such a detailed geographical description came to light," he said.
Archaeological evidence from the area also suggests a link to Homer.
"The discoveries from the excavations, especially coins bearing Homer's likeness, show us that the inhabitants of ancient Smyrna considered the poet to be one of their own," archaeologist Mehmet Akif Erdem said.
"'The Iliad' and 'The Odyssey' were written in the (ancient Greek) dialects of Ionic and Aeolic, suggesting that ancient Smyrna and Bornova could be among Homer's native lands," he said.
Beyond the academic debate about his origins, Homer is everywhere in Bornova.
At Yesilova Hoyuk, a Neolithic site considered to be the oldest known prehistoric human settlement in Izmir, there is a bust of Homer with the inscription: "I compiled The Iliad and The Odyssey epics on this land. I lived in Bornova."
The town -- which already hosts a book fair dedicated to Homer and has a statue of Trojan War hero Hector in a local park -- is planning to refurbish the cave and open it to visitors to capitalise on the revival of interest in the ancient poet.
"Preserving Homer's legacy is a duty we owe to humanity. He is one of the founding fathers of literature," Bornova Mayor Omer Eski told AFP.
"The stories he tells are about this land. The question is not whether we should claim Homer or not. His story is also ours," he said.
In 2024, municipal officials from President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AKP party proposed renaming Homer's Valley after a Turkish fighter, saying the site should not have a Greek name.
"Erasing Homer's name would be one of the worst things we could do to Bornova," retorted the mayor.

title: Art turns social issues into study of emotion

content:
Karachi exhibition features works by Adeen Habib, Safwan Sabzwari
Art Scene Gallery in Karachi is hosting a two-person exhibition titled In Each Other's Frame, featuring works by artists Adeen Habib and Safwan Sabzwari.
The exhibition brings together two distinct artistic approaches, with colourful and expressive works exploring contemporary social realities. The display has attracted art enthusiasts, with the artists' use of colour, form and visual language drawing attention from visitors.
Speaking to The Express Tribune, Adeen Habib said the response to the exhibition had been encouraging, with visitors from different age groups and backgrounds coming to view the work.
"I am very grateful. The response has been very good," Habib said. She added that the exhibition had attracted university students as well as older visitors, who had shared positive feedback about the artwork.
For Habib, art is also a way of reflecting on society and its contradictions. She said his work often focuses on social themes, including class differences and economic inequality.
"I usually focus on social themes class disparity and economic issues," She said.
Habib said contemporary society often places considerable importance on luxury and material possessions, a subject she tries to explore through his paintings. Rather than presenting these issues in a purely critical manner, she uses colour to introduce a sense of happiness and positivity into his work.
Her paintings therefore bring together two seemingly contrasting ideas the challenges faced by society and the possibility of optimism within it.
The artist said she wanted her work to encourage viewers to think about the society around them and consider how it could be improved.
The exhibition reflects the broader role of artists as observers of their surroundings, using their work to raise questions about social conditions and everyday experiences.
