title: I m difficult  Only for the wrong people
description: I m difficult  Only for the wrong people
content:
A man with strong opinions is often called confident, a woman with the same qualities can become difficult
I have heard this pet name more times than I can count. Difficult. Opinionated. Strong-minded. Too direct. Too much. And honestly, I have started wondering: is "difficult" simply the word patriarchy uses when a woman won't be convenient?
Maybe I am difficult, but only for the wrong people. I have opinions. A lot of them. And no, I do not plan to apologise for that. I write. I analyse. I question. I challenge ideas. I speak about society, women, politics, injustice, culture, education, war, money, family, and the ridiculous things human beings do every day and then rebrand them as normal.
What exactly is the point of being an intellectual if every thought has to be watered down until nobody can possibly disagree with it? I mean if I am going to write about the world, should I first ask the world for permission to have an opinion?
I understand that my conclusions will not be everyone's conclusions. They do not have to be. Disagreement is their right, but speaking is mine.
Whether you sing my praises or sharpen your knives, I will still remain opinionated. Why? Because an opinion is not a criminal conviction. Your right to disagree is absolute. So is mine. That is called conversation. Moreover, there is also a case study placed on women. A man with strong opinions is often called confident, assertive, outspoken or intellectual. A woman with the same qualities can suddenly become "difficult".
Notice how the same trait gets two verdicts.
A woman says, "I disagree." Difficult. A woman says, "I have boundaries." Difficult. A woman says, "That argument makes no sense." Difficult. A woman says, "No, I will not be shushed." Extremely difficult. She said no to something she did not want to do? Lock her up.
At this point, perhaps the dictionary needs a new edition. Besides there is another blind spot to this that people often gloss over. Being a public intellectual, writer or journalist comes with responsibility. When your words travel beyond your living room, your office or your WhatsApp group, you cannot treat ideas like disposable tissues. You have a responsibility to think, to research, to question, and to understand the consequences of what you put into the public conversation.
And no, "responsibility" does not mean I must spend my life tiptoeing around everyone's feelings like a waitress carrying a tray of fragile egos. It does not mean I should soften every sentence until it becomes meaningless, or pad every argument with so many disclaimers that nobody can find the actual point. I can be responsible and still say the thing you do not want to hear. Both can share the same defence.
And what exactly are you expecting me to compromise? My intelligence? My boundaries? My ability to think independently?
And for what? So that I can become easier to deal with? No, thank you.
I am grateful as a journalist that I can write with conviction, raise difficult questions and engage with subjects that matter. Strong women should not have to wait for permission to enter intellectual spaces. They should be given the microphone, the column, the platform, and the freedom to use all four.
And yes, sometimes I will be wrong. That is part of being human. Being an intellectual does not mean possessing a magical certificate declaring, "Congratulations, you are correct about everything." It means being willing to think, learn, question, and defend your position.
But only for people who need me to be quiet.
I'll wear it like armour no sword can pierce.

title: Netflix   s  East of Eden  draws 6 5 million views in just four days
description: East of Eden  reached 6 5 million views in four days on Netflix  topping the streamer   s weekly TV rankings
content:
'East of Eden' reached 6.5 million views in four days on Netflix, topping the streamer’s weekly TV rankings
Netflix’s East of Eden attracted 6.5 million views during its first four days of streaming, making the limited series the most-watched TV title on the platform for the week of Sept. 28 to Oct. 4.
The adaptation of John Steinbeck’s 1952 novel, created by Zoe Kazan and starring Florence Pugh and Christopher Abbott, topped Netflix’s weekly TV rankings following its release. Pugh plays Cathy Ames, while Abbott portrays Adam Trask in the series, which offers a new adaptation of Steinbeck’s classic story.
The Netflix series has also sparked renewed interest in the original novel. Penguin Classics reported a 200% increase in sales after Netflix announced that East of Eden was moving forward.
While East of Eden led Netflix’s TV chart, it was not the streamer’s most-watched title overall during the week. That distinction went to Unabomber , starring Jacob Tremblay, which recorded 24.9 million views in its second week on Netflix.
Two other films also ranked above the top TV titles. The Widower: ’Til Death Do Us Part placed second on the movies chart with 11.6 million views, while Tyler Perry’s Doing Life followed with 9.3 million views.
On the Netflix TV chart, East of Eden was followed by Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story , which recorded 5.7 million views in its third week of streaming.
The strong opening for East of Eden gives Netflix’s Steinbeck adaptation an early boost as audiences continue to discover the new series and revisit the source material.

title: Pakistan gear up for Sri Lanka T20Is
description: Three match series begins Friday in Rawalpindi as new look Pakistan seek to impress
content:
Three-match series begins Friday in Rawalpindi as new-look Pakistan seek to impress
KARACHI: Pakistan’s T20 squad will hold its first training session on Wednesday (today) ahead of the opening game of the three-match T20I series against Sri Lanka at the Pindi Stadium Rawalpindi, on Friday. All players and officials of the hosts assembled in the federal on Tuesday night to kick-start their preparation for the series. Sri Lanka’s travelling contingent was scheduled to be completed on Tuesday as their last five members were due to land in the federal capital. Eight players and five officials of the visiting side arrived in Rawalpindi on Sunday night, while five reached on Monday morning.
Sri Lanka also held their training session on Tuesday in order to fine-tune for the opener after taking a sound rest. The series will mark the start of a busy home season for Pakistan. It will be followed by an ODI tri-series also featuring England and a two-Test series against Sri Lanka, part of the World Test Championship 2025-27 cycle. All three T20Is will be played at Pindi Stadium on October 9, 11 and 13. The matches will begin at 6pm, with the toss scheduled for 5:30pm. The series promises an intriguing contest, with Pakistan holding the upper hand in their head-to-head record. Pakistan have won 18 of their 31 T20Is against Sri Lanka, while Sri Lanka have recorded 13 victories. Sri Lanka, however, have fond memories of their last full-fledged T20I series in Pakistan. In October 2019, they stunned the hosts with a 3-0 clean sweep under Dasun Shanaka, with Sarfaraz Ahmed leading Pakistan. Sri Lanka have struggled in recent bilateral series, losing 2-1 to the West Indies in June before suffering a 3-0 whitewash against England in England last month. Their Asian Games campaign also ended in the semi-finals against India. For Pakistan, the series will be their first T20I assignment since the T20 World Cup, jointly hosted by India and Sri Lanka, earlier this year. They had swept Australia 3-0 in their previous home T20I series before the global tournament. The spotlight will be firmly on new captain Sahibzada Farhan, who has replaced Agha Salman. Farhan recently led Pakistan at the Asian Games in Japan, but his captaincy came under scrutiny after India posted 211 in the final before restricting Pakistan to 192-6. Agha Salman, who has also lost his place in the T20 squad, led Pakistan in 50 T20Is, winning 31 and losing 19. Pakistan exited the T20 World Cup at the group stage under his leadership. The selectors have also introduced two fresh faces in fast bowler Razaullah and all-rounder Muhammad Imran Randhawa, both of whom recently made their Test debuts against England at Edgbaston. Razaullah has attracted attention for his pace bowling and powerful hitting, while Randhawa provides an additional batting option. Khawaja Nafay is set to take over wicket-keeping duties, having previously played as a specialist batsman during the T20 World Cup, where Usman Khan kept wickets. Nafay’s inclusion adds further firepower to a batting line-up featuring Saim Ayub, Hasan Nawaz, Abdul Samad, Fakhar Zaman, Sahibzada Farhan and Maaz Sadaqat. Abdul Samad produced a match-winning innings against Bangladesh in the Asian Games semi-final, while Hasan Nawaz struck 96 in Pakistan’s defeat against India in the final. Former Australian pacer Shaun Tait will act as bowling coach. Tait has replaced Ashley Noffke who has entered into a deal with Holland as their head coach. Noffke was part of Pakistan’s support staff during the Nagoya Asian Games. Pakistan squad: Sahibzada Farhan (captain), Abdul Samad, Abrar Ahmed, Arafat Minhas, Fakhar Zaman, Hasan Nawaz, Muhammad Imran Randhawa, Khawaja Nafay (wicket-keeper), Maaz Sadaqat, Naseem Shah, Razaullah, Saim Ayub, Mohammad Salman Mirza, Shadab Khan and Sufiyan Moqim.

title: PTI warns of quitting assemblies if governor s rule imposed in K P
description: Tariq Fazal Chaudhry claims 36 PTI MNAs will not  submit their resignations if PTI resigns from the National Assembly
content:
Tariq Fazal Chaudhry claims 36 PTI MNAs will not submit their resignations if PTI resigns from the National Assembly
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) President Junaid Akbar Khan warned on Tuesday that the party would "quit" the national and provincial assemblies if governor's rule or an emergency was imposed in K-P.
Political uncertainty has deepened in K-P amid growing tensions between the federal and provincial governments, with the Centre considering governor's rule and emergency as possible options.
In an interview with a private news channel, Akbar said the party had decided it could no longer remain part of the existing system, even if the chief minister was disqualified. “Our people are being disqualified every day, and we will no longer play this game of assemblies."
"PTI will resign from the assemblies if governor’s rule or an emergency is imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa," Akbar stated.
Read : Centre lays ground for governor's rule in K-P
Akbar stated that these threats of imposing governor's rule only amounted to “verbal firing”, further adding that the federal government did not have the “courage to impose it”.
"We want them to impose an emergency so that we can go to the people and such a decision will benefit us because it will make things easier”.
The PTI leader noted that the party was not given the government of K-P as a charity but “we protected our vote” to secure the provincial government.
Akbar stated that PTI had tried to find the political “middle ground”, but it was unfortunate that the government and state institutions “construed our desire for reconciliation as a sign of weakness”.
“We started our protests because we were denied political space, our people were disqualified, PTI speeches were removed from the assembly record and because the courts did not provide us justice”.
"We have to live here, our children have to live here. These people who make these decisions — they won't stay here, their children will be abroad, their properties will be abroad, and they'll end up abroad themselves," he remarked.
ہم نے یہ لانگ مارچ وزیراعظم صاحب کے کہنے پر شروع نہیں کیا کہ وزیراعظم صاحب ہمیں کہیں گے اور ہم ملتوی کریں گے۔ ہم نے مذاکرات کے لیے جتنا بھی ہم سے ہو سکا، ہم نے وقت دیا۔ ہم سڑکوں پر کیوں آ گئے؟ جب ہمیں اسپیس نہیں ملتا، ہمیں پنجاب میں پی ٹی آئی کا جھنڈا نہیں اٹھانے دیا جاتا، ہمیں… pic.twitter.com/bAvzBR2eD5
Akbar underlined that the PTI leadership had no option but to participate in the long march because there was pressure from party workers to secure relief for Imran. "Imran Khan is our priority because we saw peace in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa during his leadership".
ہماری اولین ترجیح ہی عمران خان ہے اور وہ اس لیے ہیں کہ عمران خان ہی کی وجہ سے ہم نے خیبرپختونخوا میں امن دیکھا تھا۔ اس لئے ہم سمجھتے ہے کہ عمران خان ہوگا تو ملک کا فائدہ ہوگا۔ آپ کا والا وفد وزیراعظم سے نہیں پوچھتا تھا، سب کو پتا تھا کہ کس سے پوچھتا تھا۔ pic.twitter.com/9KacnhMUt4
"If we reach Swabi, we might not be able to control the long march," he added.
Meanwhile, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said that PTI had resigned in the past from the provincial and national assemblies only to regret the decision afterwards.
“The people of K-P did not vote for PTI, so that its chief minister is found loafing around in the streets”.
Chaudhry claimed “on the record” that if PTI resigned from the National Assembly, he had information that 36 PTI MNAs would not submit their resignation.
In response to Fazal, Akbar stressed that “whether 36, 56 or 70 PTI MNAs decide not to resign, we want those party workers who cannot uphold Imran’s narrative and stance to leave the party.”
“There is no shortage or dearth of leadership in the party. Three years ago, you might not have heard the name of Sohail Afridi,” Akbar emphasised.
Background of debate on imposition of governor's rule in K-P
The issue of Governor’s Rule has become a major point of contention between the federal and K-P government. On September 21, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the government was consulting the law ministry on legal options for the province, including Governor’s Rule , if the PTI proceeded with its long march. Two days later, however, Information Minister Atta Tarar ruled out any plan to impose Governor’s Rule, saying the federal government had no intention of removing the PTI administration.
Read More : Govt 'seriously' considering imposing emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa: Tariq Fazal
Some federal ministers publicly raised the possibility of federal intervention in K-P. Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam said consultations were under way on the "constitutional and legal option" of imposing Governors' Rule.
Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar also said if constitutional conditions for such a step or an emergency were met, it could be implemented.
K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi separately warned the provincial government against creating a situation that could force the Centre to impose Governors' Rule.
K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi warned that the PTI would "rebel" if necessary to force a change in the federal government policies that were "harming the province".
Read More : Afridi threatens revolt to 'force change'
Afridi, however, rejected the warnings and said he would not retreat from his position because of threats of Governors' Rule or an emergency. He also said PTI supporters could take to the streets at short notice if an attempt was made to remove him.
The developments come amid continued tensions following PTI's announcement of an Islamabad march.
Reports have also emerged about the possible disqualification of the chief minister, his replacement, an in-house change, dissolution of the assembly and a no-confidence motion against him under Article 136 of the Constitution.
The no-confidence motion can be submitted to the assembly secretariat with signatures of 20% of the total membership, following which an assembly session is to be convened within three to seven days on a single-point agenda.
The assembly rules lay down the procedure for a no-confidence motion. After the motion is moved in the house, voting is held through a secret ballot, with members expressing their choice in two separate lobbies. If the motion succeeds, the speaker will issue a schedule for the election of a new chief minister.
The Constitution also provides for the governor to require the chief minister to seek a vote of confidence under Article 130(7). If the governor believes the chief minister has lost the confidence of the majority in the house, the chief minister is required to demonstrate his numerical strength in the assembly.

title: Hayden Panettiere’s ex Wladimir Klitschko seeks help over allegedly sold jewelry | The Express Tribune
description: Wladimir Klitschko alleges Hayden Panettiere’s jewelry was sold to a pawn shop and seeks police help to recover it
content:
Wladimir Klitschko alleges Hayden Panettiere’s jewelry was sold to a pawn shop and seeks police help to recover it
Wladimir Klitschko is seeking law enforcement assistance over property belonging to his late former fiancée, Hayden Panettiere, amid his request for temporary guardianship of her estate.
In a new court filing obtained by PEOPLE , the former professional boxer alleged that a non-family member previously connected to Panettiere sold items belonging to her, which he believes included jewelry, to a pawn shop.
According to the filing, the pawn shop will not release the items without being contacted by law enforcement. Klitschko is asking authorities to investigate and help recover the property, citing the financial interests of his and Panettiere’s 11-year-old daughter, Kaya, whom court documents identify as Panettiere’s sole heir.
Panettiere died on August 16 at age 36 after she was found unresponsive at a residence in Greenville, South Carolina. First responders provided medical assistance at the scene, and an investigation into her death remains ongoing.
Klitschko previously filed a petition seeking temporary guardianship of Panettiere’s estate. He cited concerns that her belongings could be lost, damaged or otherwise dissipated before a permanent representative could be appointed.
In the filing, Klitschko also alleged that Panettiere had previously hired security after concerns that someone had gained unauthorised access to her property. He said the locks were changed and valuables, including designer clothing, were moved.
Klitschko and Panettiere began dating in 2008 and became engaged in 2013. They welcomed Kaya in 2014 before ending their relationship in 2018. Klitschko was granted full custody of their daughter after their split.
Following Panettiere’s death, Klitschko described the loss as a period of “profound shock and grief” for their family.

title: PTI marchers change route  head to Khyber first
description: Afridi says peaceful protest will continue until demands  including access to Imran  are met
content:
Afridi says peaceful protest will continue until demands, including access to Imran, are met
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Tuesday announced a change in the route of the PTI's long march, saying it would first head towards Khyber and then proceed to Peshawar.
“We are playing a Test match; there are still many overs and players left. The change in route is part of the PTI’s strategy,” he said while addressing participants of the protest at University Chowk in Kohat on the third day of the march before departing for the next destination.
CM Afridi also referred to the earlier change in the march’s date from September 27 to October 4, saying the authorities had reacted strongly to the postponement and were now concerned about the duration of the protest.
Read : CM Afridi urges PTI workers to join long march as convoy enters Kohat
He said the march would eventually move towards Islamabad when the PTI decided to do so, declaring: “When we say we are going to Islamabad, no one will be able to stop us.”
"یہ لوگ انتشار پھیلانے کی کوشش کریں گے، آپ کو اشتعال دلائیں گے آپ لوگوں نے پرامن رہنا ہے میں نے ان کی دُم پر پاؤں رکھا ہوا ہے۔ خواجہ آصف جو ایک بزرگ عورت سے سیٹ ہار چکا ہے اگر یہ غیرت مند باپ کا بیٹا ہوتا تو ایک عورت کی سیٹ پر نہ بیٹھا ہوتا مجھے تمہاری غیرت کا بھی پتہ ہے اور… pic.twitter.com/2PsiJ2LSa4
Afridi vowed to continue the PTI long march, saying all constitutional and legal avenues had been exhausted and the party was now compelled to take to the streets to seek justice for founder Imran Khan. He said the era of what he called “fake, imposed and mandate-stealing rulers” was nearing its end.
Thanking the people of Kohat for their enthusiasm and patriotism, he said PTI workers would not be intimidated by anyone. “My young people, your chief minister is not afraid of anyone, and the youth of my Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa are also not afraid of anyone,” he said.
Afridi said the objective was to bring Imran out of prison and make him prime minister again, claiming that the country would witness development and prosperity under his leadership.
He said Pakistan had enjoyed peace between 2018 and 2022, when, according to him, Imran had not compromised the country’s interests.
The chief minister said the seven-point demands of the long march had already been made public on social media and challenged anyone to identify even one demand that was unconstitutional or illegal.
Afridi said demands for Imran’s medical treatment, a meeting with him and his release were in accordance with law and were not unconstitutional. He questioned why courts were not hearing Imran’s cases, claiming that if the cases were heard, the PTI founder would be released within an hour.
یہ عمران خان کی صحت سے کھیل رہے ہیں۔ ہمارا مطالبہ ہے کہ انہیں شفا انٹرنیشنل ہسپتال منتقل کیا جائے اور ذاتی ڈاکٹر و ہمشیرہ کی نگرانی میں علاج ہو۔ سپریم کورٹ نے آرڈرز جاری کیے، مگر پاکستان پر قابض لوگ اور ان کے لائے جعلی حکمران خود کو آئین و قانون سے بالاتر سمجھ کر انہیں نہیں… pic.twitter.com/TqnyDU0ksX
The chief minister alleged that Imran was being kept in prison because he had refused to submit to powerful figures in Pakistan and abroad. He also alleged that restrictions had been placed on the former prime minister’s name and image in the national media because of his popularity.

Afridi further expressed concern over reports about Imran’s health and alleged that his health was being “played with”. He warned that the jail administration, prime minister and other relevant officials would be responsible if any harm came to Imran.
He said courts, assemblies and state institutions operated with taxpayers’ money and argued that people therefore had the right to demand justice. “If the courts do not provide justice, the people will seek justice on the streets,” he said.
"ہم نہتے پرامن لانگ مارچ کررہے ہیں، ہم نے اپنی ڈیمانڈز سوشل میڈیا پر شیئر کی ہیں میں پورے پاکستان کو چیلنج کرتا ہوں اگر سات نکات میں سے ایک بھی ڈیمانڈ غیرآئینی غیرقانونی ثابت کردیں میں اپنا لانگ مارچ آج ہی کینسل کردوں گا ۔ عمران خان کا علاج غیر آئینی نہیں ہے، عمران خان سے… pic.twitter.com/WkOr1sptoJ
He said that since becoming the chief minister, he had repeatedly approached the authorities and requested a meeting with Imran. According to Afridi, he had also contacted the prime minister over the matter but was told that the request would be considered, after which no meeting was arranged.
Afridi stated that the K-P Assembly subsequently passed a resolution seeking his meeting with Imran, while he had also approached the chief justice of Pakistan without receiving a response.

On the security situation in K-P, he underlined that successive military operations and drone strikes over the past 22 years had failed to eliminate terrorism, further claiming his government had a policy that could restore peace in the province within 100 days.

title: Govt increases petrol by Rs1.19, cuts diesel by Rs1.91 for Oct 7 | The Express Tribune
description: Petrol price increases to Rs394.83 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs395.85 under daily price mechanism
content:
Petrol price increases to Rs394.83 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs395.85 under daily price mechanism
The federal government on Tuesday increased the price of petrol by Rs1.19 per litre, while decreasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.91 per litre for October 7.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs394.83 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs395.85 per litre for Wednesday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government increased the price of petrol by 88 paisas per litre, while decreasing the price of HSD by Rs1.88 per litre for October 6.
Read : Govt increases petrol by 88 paisas, cuts diesel by Rs1.88 for Oct 6
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices were steady on Tuesday after recovering earlier losses, as the market weighed increases in Middle Eastern crude exports and a planned ‌Group of Seven release of emergency diesel and crude stockpiles against supply concerns related to attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen.
Brent futures were down 29 cents, or 0.3%, at $100.03 a barrel at 12:33 pm EDT (1633 GMT), while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 16 cents, or 0.2%, to $89.59.
"The price of the global crude benchmark, Brent, is once ​again toiling around $100/barrel, as its reasons for trading much beyond the psychological 3-digit mark are being eroded ... for now the assumption of more crude getting through has ​dampened price fervour," said John Evans, an analyst at oil broker PVM.

title: Skeet Ulrich explains how Melissa Barrera   s exit changed his  Scream  future
description: Skeet Ulrich says Melissa Barrera   s firing stopped his Billy Loomis three film  Scream  arc from being fully completed
content:
Skeet Ulrich says Melissa Barrera’s firing stopped his Billy Loomis three-film 'Scream' arc from being fully completed
Scream star Skeet Ulrich has explained why he will not be able to complete the planned three-film story arc for his character Billy Loomis following Melissa Barrera’s departure from the franchise.
Ulrich played Billy, one of the original Ghostfaces, in the 1996 film. He later returned for Scream and Scream VI , with Billy appearing through hallucinations experienced by his daughter, Sam Carpenter, played by Barrera.
In an interview with Us Weekly, Ulrich said Billy’s storyline was directly connected to Sam and that the planned arc could not continue without Barrera.
“Without Melissa Barrera and Sam Loomis, there’s no Billy Loomis,” Ulrich said. He added that the filmmakers had discussed completing a “three-film arc” with him, but it was ultimately not finished.
Barrera was dismissed from the franchise by Spyglass Media Group ahead of Scream 7 . At the time, the company said it had “zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate in any form.” Barrera had made social media comments concerning Israel and the war in Gaza.
Barrera has since said she would not return to the franchise while Spyglass controls the rights. She said she loved making the Scream films but would only consider returning if the franchise moved to different leadership.
Ulrich’s comments come after fellow original Scream star Matthew Lillard said he felt embarrassed about returning as Stu Macher in Scream 7 following Barrera’s firing.
Despite largely negative reviews, Scream 7 became the highest-grossing film in the franchise. Scream 8 is now in development with writers Nora and Lilla Zuckerman.

title: Tom Cruise defends  Digger  after box office flop     You hope to make a film that can last
description: The I    rritu directed film just earned about  8 million domestically during its first weekend in theaters
content:
The Iñárritu-directed film just earned about $8 million domestically during its first weekend in theaters
Tom Cruise is defending Digger after the film suffered a disappointing opening weekend, saying he does not make movies simply for their opening-weekend performance.
The Alejandro González Iñárritu-directed film earned about $8 million domestically during its first weekend in theatres, despite its reported production budget of $160 million to $180 million. The result marked one of Cruise’s weakest openings in decades.
Cruise had discussed his approach to filmmaking shortly before Digger arrived in cinemas, explaining that he focuses on creating movies that can have a life beyond their initial theatrical release.
“You hope to make a film that can last,” Cruise said, stressing that he does not make films for “opening weekend” alone.
The comments came as Digger struggled to connect with audiences at the box office. The film opened in 3,321 North American theatres and finished behind Verity and several holdover titles, while its international performance also failed to provide the boost that had been expected.
Digger stars Cruise as Digger Rockwell, a wealthy oil tycoon who finds himself facing an environmental catastrophe. The satirical black comedy was directed by Iñárritu, whose previous films include Birdman and The Revenant .
Cruise has nevertheless remained supportive of the project. Following its release, he shared behind-the-scenes photographs from the production and praised the cast and crew for their work, describing the experience of making the film as unforgettable.
The film's opening has put significant pressure on its theatrical prospects. Variety reported that Digger cost considerably more than initially expected, with the budget rising from an original figure of around $125 million to as much as $160 million to $180 million. The studio also spent heavily on marketing.
Despite the poor start, Cruise's comments suggest that he is viewing the film's performance beyond its first weekend. For the actor, Digger represents a departure from the action-driven blockbusters that have dominated much of his recent career, and he remains proud of the finished film.

title: Caleb Flynn sobs as daughters say they will not visit him in prison
description: The daughters were only a few feet away when Caleb fatally shot Ashley and killed her
content:
The daughters were only a few feet away when Caleb fatally shot Ashley and killed her
Former American Idol contestant Caleb Flynn broke down in court as his two daughters’ statements were read during his sentencing for murdering their mother, Ashley Flynn.
Caleb, 40, was sentenced on October 5 to life in prison without parole for killing Ashley, 37, as she slept at their Tipp City, Ohio, home on February 16. His daughters, who were nine and 11 at the time of their mother’s death, delivered emotional statements through family members during the sentencing hearing.
The younger daughter questioned why her father had killed the only mother she had ever known. She described Ashley as the “perfect person” who loved and cared for Caleb, before telling her father that killing her mother had been his choice.
Caleb began crying heavily as the statement was read aloud. His daughter also said she was heartbroken to see members of her family hurting, including her father, but added that he had made the choice to leave his daughters and their mother.
His older daughter also addressed the betrayal she felt following her mother’s death. She wrote that she loved Caleb deeply but was saddened that he could not love anyone but himself. She also referred to his affair with Alleigha Botner, whom prosecutors identified as his mistress.
“You made me feel like an idiot, thinking that I could trust you,” the older daughter wrote. Her statement ended with a devastating declaration that she did not plan to visit Caleb in prison.
The daughters were only a few feet away when Caleb fatally shot Ashley. During the trial, prosecutors also presented evidence that Caleb attempted to influence the girls’ accounts after the killing, telling them that their statements “could be the difference between life and death for him”. The girls nevertheless provided information to investigators.
Prosecutors said Caleb had been having an affair with Botner, a woman the family knew through church, and had exchanged messages with her about Ashley before the murder. His daughters also learned about the affair following their mother’s death.
Ashley’s younger daughter remembered her as her best friend and said she missed her “so, so, so much”. The family had spent the weekend before Ashley’s death celebrating Galentine’s Day together, including an at-home spa day, baking cookies and watching Cinderella .
Caleb was convicted of aggravated murder, felonious assault and multiple counts of tampering with evidence. In addition to the life sentence without parole, he received consecutive sentences connected to firearm specifications and evidence tampering.
During his sentencing, Caleb continued to maintain that he did not kill Ashley, saying through tears that while he had let her down, he was innocent of the murder. His lawyer has previously said that the conviction will be appealed.

Saqib Majeed says Pakistan's Makkah Agreement role reflects global trust and growing importance as a force for peace
Azad Kashmir Minister for Electricity Raja Saqib Majeed on Tuesday said Pakistan’s role in the Makkah Agreement including the deployment of its army personnel in the Holy Mosques reflected growing international confidence in the country and its armed forces.
Speaking to the media here on Tuesday the minister said the development underscored Pakistan’s expanding strategic and diplomatic role while highlighting the professionalism and capabilities of the Pakistan Army under the leadership of Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir.
He said Pakistan was not only a strong military power but also a country committed to peace, stability and a responsible role in the international community.
The minister Saqib said the Pakistan Army’s professional training, discipline, modern defence capabilities and ability to make effective decisions in difficult circumstances had further strengthened Pakistan’s military standing globally.
He said Pakistan’s role under the Makkah Agreement was evidence of the country’s growing importance and the trust placed in it internationally. The army, he added, had demonstrated its capabilities and established Pakistan as a credible force for peace and stability in the region.
The minister said the country’s armed forces were guarantors of national security, sovereignty and national dignity, adding that their sacrifices, professional expertise and military capabilities had earned Pakistan a prominent position among major defence powers.
Saqib termed Pakistan’s role under the Makkah Agreement a matter of pride for the nation and said it would further enhance the country’s diplomatic influence, international credibility and stature, contributing to its political, military and economic stability.
He added that the Makkah Agreement had brought Pakistan, Türkiye and Saudi Arabia closer, describing the relationship among the three countries as akin to that of “three brothers”.

title: Steven Spielberg to oversee  Transformers 8  as Michael Bay eyes return
description: The eighth  Transformers  film does not yet have a release date  with the project still in development
content:
The eighth 'Transformers' film does not yet have a release date, with the project still in development
Steven Spielberg is taking a larger creative role in the Transformers franchise as Paramount Pictures develops the eighth live-action film, with Michael Bay in talks to return as director.
Spielberg will remain an executive producer on the franchise but is also expected to oversee the creative aspects of the new film alongside longtime Transformers producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura. The pair are looking to guide the next chapter in a direction that honours the spirit of the earlier films.
Michael Bay, who directed the first five Transformers films between 2007 and 2017, is in talks to return to the franchise. If a deal is reached, he would direct a script written by Jason Fuchs, whose credits include It: Welcome to Derry .
The new film is expected to be set in the modern day, although plot details and casting have not been revealed. Shia LaBeouf, who starred in the first three films, is not expected to return.
Spielberg was closely involved with the early Transformers films and served as executive producer on the 2007 original and its sequel, Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen . His increased involvement comes as Paramount moves to give the long-running franchise a new direction following the 2023 release of Transformers: Rise of the Beasts .
Bay's potential return would reunite him with the franchise after nearly a decade away. His final Transformers film was 2017's Transformers: The Last Knight , following a run of five films that helped establish the series as one of Hollywood's major blockbuster franchises.
The new project is among the major developments at Paramount following its merger with Skydance. The studio is also developing a Transformers and G.I. Joe crossover, with Jurassic World writer Derek Connolly attached to that project.
The eighth Transformers film does not yet have a release date, with the project still in development.

title: Paul Mescal takes on new role with Irish thriller 'Mary Is Missing' | The Express Tribune
description: Paul Mescal joins Irish thriller 'Mary Is Missing' as executive producer on Oscar-qualifying short film
content:
Paul Mescal joins Irish thriller 'Mary Is Missing' as executive producer on Oscar-qualifying short film
Oscar-nominated actor Paul Mescal has joined Mary Is Missing as an executive producer, supporting the Oscar-qualifying Irish short film directed by Aisling Byrne.
The psychological thriller was produced by Killian Coyle for Run of the Mill and Arcade Film. It was made in Maynooth, the town where Mescal grew up, and developed through a collaborative writers’ room involving artists with intellectual disabilities.
Mary Is Missing follows Mary, a care worker who disappears without a trace from the Yellow Tree Day Service. When Garda Foley arrives to investigate, the people who last saw Mary become key witnesses.
Their accounts, however, begin to conflict and take increasingly fantastical turns. Foley must determine whether the witnesses are telling the truth, protecting Mary, protecting themselves or describing a reality more complicated than it initially appears.
Mescal said he was drawn to the film because of its distinctive storytelling and collaborative creative process. He also highlighted the involvement of artists with intellectual disabilities and said the film’s connection to Maynooth made the project particularly meaningful to him.
Thirteen of the film’s 19 cast members are artists with intellectual disabilities. The story was developed during a 12-week writers’ room hosted by Run of the Mill, with the ensemble contributing ideas about its characters, themes and storytelling.
The film marks Byrne and Coyle’s third Oscar-qualifying short together, following Headspace and Turnaround . Headspace won the Grand Prix Irish Short at the Cork International Film Festival, while Turnaround earned qualifying awards at the Galway Film Fleadh and Foyle Film Festival.
Byrne, Coyle and Arcade Film are also developing Byrne’s debut feature, which was selected among the final 10 projects for Screen Ireland’s Perspectives scheme.

title: Yemeni government forces launch operation against Houthis to seize Al Wazi   iyah in Taiz
description: Yemen government forces recapture strategic areas from Houthis  killing  wounding or capturing dozens of fighters
content:
Yemen government forces recapture strategic areas from Houthis, killing, wounding or capturing dozens of fighters
Yemeni government forces on Tuesday launched a “large-scale” military operation against the Houthis to seize the Al-Wazi’iyah district in the southwestern Taiz province.
The Nation’s Shield Forces said the offensive was launched as part of the broader Dawn of Yemen operations.
It said the operation aims to restore state institutions and end the Houthi “coup”.
The forces later said they had taken control of strategic hilltops overlooking Al-Mansoura as Houthi fighters retreated from the area during the offensive.
Local sources told state-run Aljoumhouriya TV that warplanes struck Houthi reinforcements near the centre of the Al-Wazi’iyah district.
Meanwhile, government forces continued advancing for a second consecutive day on the southern front of the Marib province as part of the Dawn of Yemen operation, Yemen TV reported.
A military source told the Armed Forces Media Centre that government troops drove Houthi forces from large areas and several strategic positions, including the Thamad, Al-Qaima, and Al-Muqaylat mountain ranges, as well as Aqad al-Qaima, Al-Rasid, and surrounding desert areas.
The source said dozens of Houthi fighters were killed, wounded, or captured in the fighting, while government forces destroyed three weapons positions and disabled military vehicles, causing additional casualties among those aboard.
Read More: Saudi Arabia says 3 injured in attacks on 2 airports in country’s south amid escalation with Houthis
Government air defences also downed a Houthi drone during the fighting, the source added.
Operation Dawn of Yemen was launched on Monday. Presidential Leadership Council Chair Rashad al-Alimi said the offensive aims to restore state institutions, retake the capital Sanaa, and end Houthi control.
The operation has since expanded across several fronts. Government forces said they retook the strategic Bab el-Mandeb area and Dhubab district, while Southern Giants Brigades and Nation’s Shield Forces took part in advances along Yemen’s western coast.
The Saudi-led coalition said 100 fighter jets took part in the opening phase of the operation and that 324 “high-value targets” had been destroyed, while providing round-the-clock air support to Yemeni government forces.
On Tuesday, the Yemeni army said around 100 Houthi fighters were killed and 150 others wounded in Monday’s operations across Taiz as part of Dawn of Yemen, while government forces also reported retaking several strategic mountain positions in the province.
Local sources told Aljoumhouriya TV that warplanes struck Houthi reinforcements near the centre of the Al-Wazi’iyah district.
The latest escalation is among the most significant rounds of fighting in Yemen since a UN-brokered truce in April 2022 ushered in a period of relative calm.
Yemen has been engulfed in conflict since the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa and several provinces in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.

title: Trump blames France unrest on  mass migration   Islam
description: France s interior ministry says    6 100 people arrested since protests began in Sept  overwhelming majority are minors
content:
France's interior ministry says ​6,100 people arrested since protests began in Sept, overwhelming majority are minors
US President Donald Trump on Tuesday blamed mass student protests in France on "mass migration" and Islam, pushing his global right-wing narrative ahead of tough midterm elections at home.
French students have blocked the entrances to hundreds of high schools across the country since late September to demand better conditions, in protests that have descended into sporadic clashes with security forces. A quarter of a million demonstrators took to the streets across France on Tuesday.
"What's happening in France is nothing less than out-of-control mass migration. This isn't about schools, this is about Islam wanting to take over a once great country!" Trump said in a post on Truth Social .
Trump: What’s happening in France is nothing less than out of control mass migration. This isn’t about schools, this is about Islam wanting to take over a once great Country! pic.twitter.com/SzfOqAjiDv
Trump and his administration have long blamed European social issues on migration, calling on Europe to shut its borders and echoing far-right parties by warning of what they call civilizational decline. Leading voices in Trump’s Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement have been using the French protests to ram home points about immigration ahead of the US midterm elections next month.
MAGA commentators have repeatedly posted videos of the French unrest, with Trump ally Glenn Beck saying on Monday that the “riots in France are a clear warning to the rest of the West”. Republicans are doubling down on migration and anti-transgender rhetoric amid fears that Trump’s unpopularity and his Iran war risk losing them control of Congress.
Police fired tear gas at protesters today outside French high schools as students, teachers and parents took to the streets on the biggest day of what Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu described as the ​most violent school protests in decades.
The protests, in which a teenager lost a hand on Monday, were the latest manifestation of public anger in a country where the far right ‌and far left are surging ahead of a presidential election in the spring.
The government is under pressure to tame public debt amid weak growth, and has struggled with basic tasks such as passing a budget since President Emmanuel Macron's allies lost their majority in a 2024 parliamentary vote.
Lecornu told lawmakers at least 215 teenagers and 85 school staff had so far been injured in clashes, "the heaviest toll in decades paid by the school system". His office said more than 700 police officers were also hurt.
Read : Teenager's hand blown off as French school protests enter third week
Macron has convened Lecornu and other senior ministers ​at an emergency meeting on Tuesday, broadcaster BFM reported.
In Marseille and Nantes, protesters held up signs reading "The state has killed national education". In Toulouse, parents linked arms at the front of a march through ​the city.
In Strasbourg, Lyon, Rennes and Paris, the demonstrations at times turned violent, with police firing tear gas and protesters lighting fires in the streets and hurling projectiles.
The ⁠Paris police said the clashes there had come about when some 300 people attempted to face off against security forces, adding that the protest was generally unfolding well elsewhere.
Nearly 2,000 high schools across France are closed as student protests over deteriorating school conditions enter their third week. The protests began in lower-income suburbs around Paris before spreading nationwide, with students joining in solidarity. Some parents and teachers… pic.twitter.com/Sc2g9aYfVi
By late afternoon, they said they were still ​clashing with a small contingent of people. Three storefronts had been damaged.
The protests began in September in the deprived suburbs of Paris, before spreading nationwide.
"There is such a gap between the elites and us," said Hugo Vetzel, a ​recent high-school graduate in Strasbourg.
The High School Students Union said more than half of France's high schools were blockaded or would close for the day. Some local education authorities have tried to move classes online.
Students complain about schools facing basic maintenance problems, from water leaks to rat infestations.
🇫🇷 🪧 #France braced on Tuesday for a day of nationwide high-school ​blockades and trade union-led street #protests in support of #students demanding that President Emmanuel #Macron 's cash-strapped government tackle the issue of understaffed and dilapidated schools. pic.twitter.com/974rzEqfem
Rights groups, students and parent groups have accused authorities of using disproportionate force against minors. The government says the protest movement has been hijacked by outsiders and in some places deteriorated into urban violence.
France's interior ministry said ​6,100 people have been arrested since the protests began, the overwhelming majority of them minors. More than 1,800 people are being prosecuted for unspecified crimes, including 1,483 minors, the justice ministry said.
A teenager's hand was blown off ​as high-school protesters clashed with riot police in northern France on Monday. The regional newspaper La Voix du Nord said the 15-year-old lost his hand and part of his lower arm after picking up a police grenade intended to be non-lethal.
"They want to ‌divide the young ⁠people into good and bad protesters," said Omar Slaouti, a high-school teacher in Argenteuil, a northwestern suburb of Paris. "If there were no trash cans on fire, the government would not have stepped back and become aware of the issues at stake."
Six months before an election to replace Macron, his government and far-right leader Marine Le Pen's National Rally party have accused hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) lawmakers and mayors of stoking the unrest. LFI denies the accusation.
"All the young people are in the streets. Everywhere there aren't police, everything is going smoothly," said Jean-Luc Melenchon, LFI's presidential candidate.
🇫🇷 🪧 💥 'Gen Z has risen up': Tens of thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Tuesday, as unions and teachers joined high school students who for days have been demanding better learning conditions in protests punctuated by violent confrontations ➡️… pic.twitter.com/p4Gcpqdqw4
Lecornu has ordered his ministers to tackle the students' leading demands. Those include ensuring absent teachers are ​replaced, reviewing the length of the 8 am to ​6 pm school day and the need for longer ⁠lunch breaks.
The government will also look at repairs needed to ageing school buildings, said Lecornu, who demanded ministers send in their first proposals by the end of October.
Parent Emilie Lhomme said at a protest outside the Helene Boucher school in Paris that the government's words were not enough: "That's all fine and dandy, but that's not what's ​going to change the daily lives of our children," she said.
Finding spare cash to implement educational reforms will be difficult.
The government is under pressure to try ​to narrow a ballooning budget ⁠deficit as investor concerns about France's growing debt, weak growth and reluctance to rein in spending push the cost of borrowing higher. The yield on France's 10-year bonds briefly hit a 24-year high of over 5% last week.
The surge in French borrowing costs has started to spill into the broader euro area, with the sliding euro currency the latest alarm bell for policymakers. Finance Minister Roland Lescure said on Tuesday there was no need for the European Central Bank to step in.
Le ⁠Pen, the far-right ​euro-sceptic populist leading the presidential race ahead of next spring's election, set out plans to slash public spending if elected , seeking to establish ​her fiscal credibility as the bond market crisis deepens.
French spending on education has lagged inflation, and the country's students are trailing their OECD peers in overall performance, data from the PISA 2025 assessment shows.

title: Paramount wraps up mega Warner Bros merger to create Hollywood powerhouse Skydance
description: Deal combines major film  TV and streaming brands including Warner Bros   Paramount   CBS  CNN and HBO Max
content:
Deal combines major film, TV and streaming brands including Warner Bros, Paramount+, CBS, CNN and HBO Max
Paramount Skydance on Tuesday completed its blockbuster $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros Discovery, creating a Hollywood heavyweight called ‌Skydance and handing CEO David Ellison control of one of the world's largest entertainment companies.
The deal brings together the studios behind "Mission: Impossible", "Harry Potter" and DC Studios alongside major television and streaming networks such as CBS , CNN , Paramount+ and HBO Max — forming an expansive entertainment company spanning film, TV and news.
Shares of the combined company ​moved to the New York Stock Exchange from Nasdaq on Tuesday to trade under the ticker "SKYD".
Settlements with a coalition of US ​states and a Hollywood writers union removed the main legal barriers to the merger, one of the largest ⁠in media history. It comes as Hollywood faces declining cable-TV subscriptions, high cost of competing for streaming audiences and persistent pressure from unions ​over jobs and creative workers' rights.
Ellison said last week the Skydance name was chosen to retain the individual identities of Paramount and Warner Bros studios, ​rather than combining them under a new brand.
Read More: Paramount clears final hurdle for Warner takeover
Analysts, however, said the name reinforces the extent of Ellison's control, highlighting how some of Hollywood's most iconic brands now answer to him and how he has a platform to impose his strategy and culture.
In just 16 years, Skydance has gone from an independent studio to the ​centre of one of Hollywood's biggest power plays. Founded in 2010 by the son of Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, it built its reputation ​as a financial backer and producer of Paramount's blockbuster "Top Gun: Maverick".
After merging with Paramount last year, Skydance set its sights on Warner Bros, entering a heated bidding ‌contest with ⁠Netflix while drawing interest from other potential suitors, including Comcast.
Warner Bros shareholders received an additional $41.9 million in "ticking fee", based on the number of days between September-end and the deal-closing, according to a regulatory filing.
Ellison named Mattel's former CEO Ynon Kreiz as Skydance co-CEO to run day-to-day operations and lead the integration, while Ellison oversees creative direction and overall strategy.
The duo faces the task of combining two large companies while delivering $6 ​billion in planned cost savings, a ​big part of which Paramount ⁠said would come from "non-labour sources" — by combining streaming technologies and cloud providers of the two companies. However, the scale of the cuts is expected to affect jobs across Hollywood.
Skydance plans to combine its streaming services, ​including HBO Max and Paramount+ , into a single service and has pledged to release at least 30 films ​each in the first ⁠two years after closing, rising to 32 a year for the following three.
The combined company is also expected to carry about $80 billion in debt, putting pressure on Ellison to grow streaming, preserve cash flow from cable networks and improve theatrical film performance.
Analysts at MoffettNathanson forecast EBITDA of $16 billion for 2028, ⁠rising to $19 ​billion in 2030. The brokerage also predicted about $67 billion in revenue in 2028 for ​the company, growing to roughly $70 billion in 2030.
CNN chief Mark Thompson and CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss will continue in their respective leadership roles.
Ellison's annual base salary will be $5 million, ​with a target annual bonus of $5 million, according to the filing.

title: Digger  director Alejandro Gonz  lez I    rritu admits Tom Cruise film is    not perfect
description: I    rritu said that he is comfortable with viewers having strong reactions to the movie
content:
Iñárritu said that he is comfortable with viewers having strong reactions to the movie
Alejandro González Iñárritu has acknowledged that Digger is “not perfect” while defending the Tom Cruise film’s polarising response from critics and audiences.
The filmmaker told The New York Times that he is comfortable with viewers having strong reactions to the movie, saying he would prefer that to a lukewarm response. “I prefer that to the lukewarm reception,” Iñárritu said.
Iñárritu admitted that “the movie is not perfect” but said he remains committed to taking risks with his filmmaking. He described Digger as an uncommon and provocative film designed to start conversations rather than provide a conventional viewing experience.
“I like taking risks,” the director said, acknowledging that some viewers prefer greater certainty in storytelling. He compared the experience of watching the film to ice cream, saying it is not something that needs to appeal to everyone.
Digger stars Cruise as Digger Rockwell, an eccentric oil baron whose actions contribute to an environmental catastrophe. Iñárritu described the movie as a disaster film in which humanity itself is the disaster, using the story to explore the relationship between people and the natural world.
The film has received a sharply divided response. Digger currently holds a 51 per cent critics’ score on Rotten Tomatoes, while its audience score stands at 71 per cent. On Metacritic, the film has a 46 out of 100 score from critics compared with 66 from users.
That mixed response has also been reflected at the box office. Digger opened with approximately $8 million domestically, marking Cruise’s lowest US opening weekend since 2007’s Lions for Lambs . The film also opened behind Verity , Resident Evil and Heart of the Beast at the domestic box office.
Despite the disappointing opening, Cruise has expressed pride in the film. The actor praised the cast and crew for their dedication and described the experience of making Digger as unforgettable.
For Iñárritu, however, the divided reaction appears to be part of what he wanted from the project. Rather than seeking universal approval, the director has emphasised his preference for films that challenge audiences and encourage them to discuss their ideas and themes.

title: Rosie O'Donnell joins London play about Gisele Pelicot trial | The Express Tribune
description: Rosie O'Donnell and Julie Hesmondhalgh will join a one-off London play based on the Gisele Pelicot trial
content:
Rosie O'Donnell and Julie Hesmondhalgh will join a one-off London play based on the Gisele Pelicot trial
Rosie O'Donnell, Julie Hesmondhalgh, Adjoa Andoh and Tamzin Outhwaite are among the actors and public figures joining The Pelicot Trial , a one-off documentary theatre performance based on the case of Gisele Pelicot.
The four-hour production will be staged by the Young Vic at London's County Hall on November 30. The performance will also be streamed online.
The play is based on documents from the trial, including testimonies and psychiatric reports involving men prosecuted in the case. It focuses on the trial of Dominique Pelicot, who was sentenced to 20 years in prison after being convicted of drugging and raping his then-wife and allowing other men to rape her while she was unconscious.
The case attracted international attention and made Gisele Pelicot a prominent symbol in discussions surrounding sexual assault and survivor rights. Pelicot waived her right to anonymity during the proceedings and said that shame should belong to her abusers rather than her.
Other cast members include Juliet Stevenson, Samuel West, Olivia Williams, Kadiff Kirwan, Rosie Jones, Sharon Duncan-Brewster, Lorraine Ashbourne and Jordan Stephens.
The Pelicot Trial was developed with journalists and feminist organisations in France. The production received its world premiere in Vienna last year before touring cities including Avignon, New York, Lisbon, Milan and Bergen.
The Young Vic described the production as documentary theatre built from written accounts and testimonies from the trial. The theatre said the performance pays tribute to Pelicot and the wider significance of her decision to publicly identify herself as a survivor.
Additional casting for the London performance is expected to be announced in the coming weeks. Tickets will go on general sale on Wednesday.

Fans can buy or rent Marvel sequel now, with 4K UHD, Blu-ray and DVD arriving December 15
Spider-Man: Brand New Day is now available to watch at home, with Sony Pictures releasing the Marvel sequel on digital platforms on October 6. The film can be purchased or rented through major digital retailers, including Prime Video, Apple TV, Fandango and Sony Pictures Core.
Prime Video lists the film at $29.99 to buy and $24.99 to rent. A rental gives viewers 30 days to start watching and 48 hours to finish once playback begins. An Amazon Prime subscription is not required, although viewers need an Amazon account.

Directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, the film continues Peter’s story after Spider-Man: No Way Home . Peter is living in a world where people he once knew no longer remember him, while a new threat emerges and his powers begin to change.
Sony Pictures has also confirmed a physical home release for December 15, when Spider-Man: Brand New Day will arrive on 4K UHD, Blu-ray and DVD. Preorders are already available.
The film has become a major box office success. Sony says it crossed $1bn worldwide within six days and became the biggest domestic box office film in history. Page Six reported a $954m domestic total as of October 6, while current reports place its worldwide earnings above $2.4bn.
For viewers wanting to see Holland’s latest Spider-Man outing without returning to cinemas, the digital release provides the first official paid home viewing option. Trump says Iran could 'take out' Los Angeles or San Diego, drawing rebukes from California Democrats and GOP allies
The White House pushed back on Tuesday after Democrats accused President Donald Trump of suggesting Iran should "take out" the major US cities of Los Angeles and San Diego.
Viral footage showed comments by Trump at a midterm elections rally in Nebraska on Monday, where he said high oil prices from the Iran war were justified by the need to stop Tehran from getting nuclear weapons.
"It's a little bit high. It's a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe," Trump said.
"They can take out a city. Let them take, let them take out Los Angeles, let them take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay, and it's going to be over with very soon."
Democrats — who control the state of California where both Los Angeles and San Diego are located — accused the 80-year-old Republican president of encouraging Iran to hit the two urban centres.
"Donald Trump is now saying our foreign enemies should 'take out' Los Angeles and San Diego. He is deranged and dangerous," California Governor Gavin Newsom said on X.
After sending the National Guard and Marines to occupy California, Donald Trump is now saying our foreign enemies should “take out” Los Angeles and San Diego. He is deranged and dangerous. https://t.co/N4JQfecAYo
"The nuclear annihilation of an American city is no laughing matter," Hakeem Jeffries, the Democratic minority leader in the US House of Representatives, said on X.
The nuclear annihilation of an American city is no laughing matter.
But the White House insisted Trump was talking about the threat posed by Iran, branding it a "media freakout" that was "not rooted in reality".
"He was clearly stating US cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadn't been stopped," White House Communications Director Steven Cheung said on X.

title: Cynthia Erivo called Sunny Hostin over backlash to Cornell sexual assault remarks
description: Hostin revealed that Erivo reached out to her from Paris after seeing a clip of her discussion of the case
content:
Hostin revealed that Erivo reached out to her from Paris after seeing a clip of her discussion of the case
Cynthia Erivo called her friend Sunny Hostin after the The View co-host faced backlash over her comments about the alleged sexual assault case involving a former Cornell University student.
Hostin revealed that Erivo reached out to her from Paris after seeing a clip of her discussion of the case. Erivo, who is currently working on a film about consent and sexual assault, told Hostin that the clip did not reflect the person she knew.
“She called me and said, ‘Sis, I know you and I know your heart and your life's work has been about protecting women and children. But, the clip that I saw doesn't reflect who you are,’” Hostin recalled during an episode of her Behind the Table podcast.
According to Hostin, Erivo also encouraged her to reconsider how she presented her legal analysis of the case. Rather than leading with the law, Erivo suggested that Hostin lead with empathy so audiences could better understand the legal points she was trying to make.
Hostin said the advice resonated with her because both women are “blunt” and have developed a close friendship as members of the same sorority. She explained that Erivo told her she had learned to express her opinions in a way that allowed people to receive the message rather than simply leading with bluntness.
Hostin had faced intense criticism after discussing the case on The View and questioning aspects of the alleged victim’s 2024 statement. As a former federal prosecutor, Hostin focused on New York’s laws concerning consent and voluntary intoxication, arguing that the legal framework made the case difficult to prosecute.
She later clarified her position on the programme, saying she believed the allegations were morally disturbing and that she would have prosecuted the case if it had come to her under the laws in Washington, D.C. Hostin maintained that the issue was New York law rather than a defence of the alleged actions.
Hostin also acknowledged the distinction between the legal and moral questions surrounding the allegations, saying that the morality of what allegedly happened was very different from the legality under the current law. She said Erivo’s advice helped her approach the discussion differently during subsequent appearances.
The Cornell case involves a former student identified in legal filings as Jane Doe, who filed a lawsuit against the university, members of the Chi Phi fraternity and others. Cornell has said its offices investigated and adjudicated the allegations according to university policies, while the fraternity chapter remains barred from campus.

title: Pageant queen Ana Beatriz Ara  jo Ferreira dies at 22 after lightning strike
description: Ferreira was taken to a local hospital after the incident but was later pronounced dead
content:
Ferreira was taken to a local hospital after the incident but was later pronounced dead
Ana Beatriz Araújo Ferreira, a 22-year-old Brazilian pageant queen, has died after being struck by lightning during a mild rainstorm in Almas, Tocantins.
Ferreira died on October 3 after the lightning strike, according to PEOPLE. She had recently been crowned “Queen of the Rodeo” at the ExpoAlmas agricultural fair and was reportedly caring for her niece when she was struck.
According to local authorities cited by PEOPLE, Ferreira was taken to a local hospital after the incident but was later pronounced dead. Her brother, César Augusto, told CNN Brasil that she had been with her niece when the lightning struck, describing the weather at the time as cloudy with only a light drizzle.
Augusto paid tribute to his sister, remembering her as one of the most beautiful people he had known. He said she had been caring for her niece at the time, describing the moment as an example of Ferreira showing love through a simple act of looking after her family.
Ferreira was also a physiotherapy student at Unopar University. She is survived by her five-year-old son, as well as her parents and siblings.
The organisers of ExpoAlmas also mourned Ferreira's death, saying her passing had left a profound loss for her family, friends and the wider community. The Almas Rural Union remembered her for representing the event with joy and affection for local traditions.
A wake and funeral were held on October 5. Local police are investigating the circumstances surrounding Ferreira's death.

O’Brien was a renowned Irish dancer who performed as Saoirse in Lord of the Dance. She became a prominent figure in Irish dance and performed alongside Flatley during her career.
Flatley described O’Brien as “the most loving mother, wife and person” and said their lives “will never be the same without her”. The couple had one son, Michael St James, who was born in 2007.
A representative for Flatley confirmed that O’Brien died peacefully at Beacon Hospital in Dublin after an illness, according to Irish broadcaster RTÉ.
“The Flatley and O’Brien families are devastated by Niamh’s sudden passing and have asked that their privacy be respected as they come to terms with this heartbreaking loss,” the representative said.
The family also thanked the doctors, nurses and staff at Beacon Hospital who cared for O’Brien during the final weeks of her illness.
Following Flatley’s announcement, several Irish entertainment figures and dancers shared tributes to O’Brien.
Irish actress Victoria Smurfit expressed her condolences, while the Gardiner Brothers, fellow Irish dancers, also paid tribute to her. Television and radio presenter Angela Scanlon and Boyzone and Boyzlife star Keith Duffy were among others who sent messages of support to Flatley and his family.

content:
Deal will enable $4.3 billion in new Constellation investment and expand capacity at US nuclear reactors
Google has contracted for 3,590 megawatts of power from Constellation Energy in the US' largest power grid, with new nuclear energy accounting for about ​a quarter of that supply, the companies said on Tuesday.
The deal will enable ‌more than $4.3 billion of new investment by Constellation and involves adding capacity at several of the power company's nuclear reactors in the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic regions, the companies said.
Major tech companies are racing to ​secure massive amounts of electricity supplies to power data centers across the US by ​striking unprecedented deals with the country's power companies.
Over the last two years, ⁠Constellation unveiled an agreement to restart its Three Mile Island reactor in Pennsylvania to ​serve Microsoft data centers, while Google contracted to restart NextEra Energy's nuclear power plant in Iowa.
In ​the latest arrangement, Google entered into a 20-year power purchase agreement for 890 megawatts of electricity from multiple Constellation-owned nuclear power plants, which would be upgraded to produce more electricity from existing reactors.

Electricity from the ​first of the upgraded plants is expected to be delivered in 2028, the companies ​said.
Google also entered into a long-term supply agreement for an additional 2,700 megawatts of power from Constellation in ‌PJM. ⁠That power is not tied to a specific generation source and serves as long-term revenue certainty for Constellation's operating plants, Google said.
Maryland-based Constellation is the largest US nuclear power plant operator and owns a major fleet of natural-gas-fired power plants.
"We’re committed to meeting our growth responsibly ​by actively investing in ​clean, reliable power ⁠that brings new capacity to our nation's grids," said Amanda Peterson Corio, Google's global head of energy and power, in a statement.
The 11 ​nuclear units expected to be upgraded as part of the arrangement ​with Google ⁠are in Illinois, Pennsylvania, and New Jersey, within the footprint of the largest US electric grid - PJM Interconnection.
PJM management has proposed requiring data center customers connected to the 13-state grid to either ⁠bring ​their own power or face being shut off from ​grid power remotely in times of peak demand.
The deal between Google and Constellation is in response to PJM's "bring your ​own power" proposal, the companies said.

title: Alien  phoenix planet  was born from the ashes of a dying star
description: Researchers say the exoplanet formed from material expelled by a dying star and now orbits its white dwarf remnant
content:
Researchers say the exoplanet formed from material expelled by a dying star and now orbits its white dwarf remnant
In ancient mythology, the phoenix was a miraculous bird with a cyclical pattern of life and death, perishing in flames only to rise again from the ashes. Astronomers have now found a world that rightly can be called a phoenix planet.
Researchers said this exoplanet, as planets beyond our solar system are called, appears to have been born from material expelled into space during the death throes of a star a bit bigger than the sun, and now orbits the highly compact stellar remnant that was left behind, called a white dwarf.
It is classified as a second-generation planet, meaning it did not form from the swirling disk of material surrounding a newborn star, as Earth and other first-generation planets did, but rather from the leftovers of a doomed star.
"This is the first example of a planet forming around a white dwarf," said Jamie Williams, a doctoral student in astrophysics at the University of Warwick in England and lead author of the study published this week in the journal Nature Astronomy .
The white dwarf is located about 250 light-years from Earth, near the constellation Cetus. A light-year is the distance light travels in a year, 5.9 trillion miles (9.5 trillion km).
The planet is a gas giant perhaps slightly more massive than Jupiter, our solar system's largest planet. It orbits the white dwarf every 4.4 days at only 4% the distance between Earth and the sun.
It is so close that the blazingly hot white dwarf's extreme ultraviolet radiation is causing the planet's outer atmosphere to evaporate, with a portion then falling into the white dwarf.
The planet's chemical pattern points to its second-generation origin. It is rich in niobium, copper and zinc, the type of elements that certain dying stars cast off when they expand in their death throes, indicating the planet formed from a disk of this expelled material that surrounded the stellar corpse.
"In myths, a phoenix is born again from its own ashes. In the case of this planet, it is born again from the ashes of its dying host star, and therefore the planetary system is reborn. A second-generation planet is defined as one born after its host star dies - in this case after it has become a white dwarf," Williams said.
Read More: Chinese rocket firm, disease research lab to test space pharmaceutical payloads
The researchers used data from the orbiting Hubble, TESS and FUSE telescopes, and hope to use the James Webb Space Telescope to confirm their conclusions.
A small number of potential second-generation planets previously have been identified orbiting pulsars, a rare type of neutron star, another type of stellar remnant.
"White dwarfs are much more common than pulsars, and over 95% of stars in the Milky Way will evolve to become a white dwarf. Therefore, there would be many more second-generation planets around white dwarfs than around pulsars," Williams said.
While the newly discovered planet would be inhospitable for life, another second-generation planet potentially could be habitable.
"If a gas giant formed around a white dwarf, then a rocky planet could form, too. White dwarfs cool predictably over time and as they get cooler, their cooling slows. So if a second-generation rocky planet formed close enough to the white dwarf then it could remain in the habitable zone for billions of years," Williams said.
A second study published in the same journal describes another exotic celestial phenomenon roughly 300 to 500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Taurus.
Researchers used the Zwicky Transient Facility at Palomar Observatory in California to discover a red dwarf star about 8% of the mass of the sun in a tight orbit with a brown dwarf, an object too small to be a star and too big to be a planet.
The brown dwarf is about 30 times the mass of Jupiter and a third of the mass of the star.
These two companions orbit each other every 87 minutes at slightly more than half the distance between Earth and the moon, and the star's gravitational pull appears to be siphoning material from the brown dwarf.
The researchers detected a hot spot on the star's surface where this material appears to be landing.
"This is the first observed example of this phenomenon," said Aaron Householder, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology graduate student in astrophysics and lead author of the study.
"The two objects are so close together that the entire orbit would fit inside the sun," Householder said.

Berry also asks court to compel Martinez to attend court ordered co parenting therapy
Halle Berry has asked a court to restore her previous 50/50 custody arrangement for her 12 year old son Maceo, whom she shares with former husband Olivier Martinez. The actress also wants her previous authority to make tie breaking decisions reinstated and is asking Martinez to attend court ordered therapy sessions.
According to court documents obtained by PEOPLE and published October 5, Berry claimed Maceo sometimes returns from Martinez’s custody periods angry and combative. She alleged that these difficulties can last for several days, particularly after longer periods with his father.
Berry further claimed Martinez has influenced Maceo during disagreements over issues involving school, football and therapy. She alleged that he has also resisted efforts involving Maceo’s psychological and educational needs. These claims remain allegations contained in Berry’s court filing and have not been established as facts.
The filing comes after Martinez requested sole custody and alleged that Berry physically abused their son. Martinez claimed an incident occurred on September 26, when he alleged Berry choked Maceo. Berry’s latest filing does not directly address those abuse allegations.
On October 1, a Los Angeles County judge granted Martinez a temporary restraining order covering himself and Maceo. The order temporarily changed Berry’s visitation schedule while allowing continued contact between mother and son. The judge declined to require sobriety monitoring, citing insufficient information.
Berry and Martinez finalised their divorce in 2023 after filing in 2015. Their agreement provided for joint legal custody, with Berry paying Martinez $8,000 a month in child support. They later agreed to co parenting therapy in 2024, although the sessions became contentious.
The latest filings mark another escalation in the former couple’s long running custody dispute, with both parents presenting conflicting accounts to the court about what they believe is best for Maceo.
