Lucy Hale will lead Roku’s 'Scarlett Holmes', a romantic mystery series following Sherlock Holmes’ descendant in 2027
Lucy Hale is set to star in Roku’s upcoming limited series Scarlett Holmes , a romantic mystery show inspired by the world of Sherlock Holmes. The series is scheduled to debut in 2027.
Hale will play Scarlett Holmes, a modern descendant of the legendary detective who inherits her family’s exceptional powers of observation. However, instead of investigating crimes, Scarlett uses her skills to help people navigate dating, relationships and romantic dilemmas.
According to the series’ logline, Scarlett works alongside her sidekick, Jane Watson, as they help clients deal with mixed signals, secret crushes and complicated love lives. While Scarlett can solve other people’s romantic problems, she struggles to understand her own feelings.
Her personal life becomes even more complicated when she falls for Ollie Moriarity, a charming podcast producer who is secretly planning an exposé on her methods. Scarlett must then face what may be her most difficult mystery yet: her own love life.
Each episode of Scarlett Holmes will draw inspiration from a well-known romantic comedy, combining mystery elements with the conventions of the rom-com genre.
Hale said she is a longtime fan of romantic comedies and was drawn to the series’ blend of mystery, romance and humour. She described Scarlett as smart, curious and complicated while expressing excitement about playing the character.
Best known for playing Aria Montgomery in Pretty Little Liars , Hale has also appeared in romantic comedies and mystery projects including The Hating Game , Which Brings Me to You , Puppy Love , F, Marry, Kill and Ragdoll .
Scarlett Holmes is written by Paris Herbert-Taylor and Katie Wilbert and produced by Jaggi Entertainment. Sophie Tilson and Steve Jaggi executive produce, with Hale also serving as an executive producer.

title: Chris Rock regrets refusing to pay lawyer fees for wrongfully convicted friend   s brother
description: Roger Logan later received millions in settlements after his murder conviction was overturned
content:
Roger Logan later received millions in settlements after his murder conviction was overturned
Chris Rock has opened up about a painful decision from his past, revealing that he refused to pay for a lawyer for Roger Logan, the brother of one of his close friends, who spent 19 years in prison after being wrongfully convicted of murder.
Speaking with The New York Times for its The Interview series, Rock discussed forgiveness, public accusations and his views on people being judged before all the facts are known. He recalled Logan’s case while explaining why he believes people should be careful before assuming someone is guilty.
Rock said Logan’s brother repeatedly asked him to help pay for legal representation, but he declined because he had a personal rule against paying lawyers. He explained that he had been willing to help people with expenses such as mortgages or education, but viewed legal fees differently because they could become open ended.
The comedian acknowledged that the decision continues to trouble him. Rock said he had the financial means to help Logan and remains unsure whether his contribution could have changed the outcome.
Logan was convicted in a Brooklyn murder case and spent 19 years in prison before his conviction was overturned. According to The New York Times , Logan later reached settlements with New York City and New York State totalling millions of dollars over his wrongful conviction.
Rock also recalled being placed in police lineups several times while growing up in Brooklyn. He described the experience as frightening, saying an identification could have serious consequences for a person’s life.
The comedian connected those memories to his broader point about accusations, particularly concerning Black men. He stressed the importance of establishing whether allegations are true before deciding someone is guilty.
Rock is currently promoting Misty Green , his latest directorial project starring Rosalind Eleazar. The film premiered at the TORONTO INTERNATIONAL FILM FESTIVAL in September before screening at the NEW YORK FILM FESTIVAL. It is scheduled for a limited theatrical release on October 9.

title: Francis Halzen wins Nobel Physics Prize for Antarctic  ghost particle  hunt
description: Prize goes to research into neutrinos at Antarctic observatory
content:
Prize goes to research into neutrinos at Antarctic observatory
The Belgian-American Francis Halzen won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work creating an observatory to detect high-energy neutrinos - some of the universe's most elusive subatomic particles - and try to establish how they are made.
Halzen, 82, realised that pristine ice at the South Pole could be used to track such neutrinos, sometimes ‌known as "ghost particles" for the way they pass through the Earth and our bodies without a trace, only interacting with matter extremely rarely.
"The messengers bring information from the cosmos," Eva Olsson, of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, told a press conference. "They open the door to distant galaxies and tell us about the processes of exploding stars."
Halzen hailed for detecting messengers from the cosmos
The interactions registered by the IceCube observatory in Antarctica provide information about how high-energy neutrinos are created and may even reveal previously unknown phenomena, the Academy said.
In 2014, the US-based Smithsonian magazine dubbed Halzen "Neutrino Man" when giving him one of its Ingenuity Awards, acclaiming him for an "amazing experiment (that) heralds the beginning of a new era in astronomy".
It even published a comic illustrating his life: "How One Physicist’s Pursuit ⁠of the Cosmos Took Off in Antarctica".
The particle detector comprises more than 5,000 sensors set in a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice, which extends to a depth of 2,500 metres below the surface near the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station.
Also Read: German and US scientists win Nobel medicine prize for work on optogenetics
The observatory awaits blips from the nearly massless high-energy neutrinos, which unlike other particles do not lose energy or change direction, in the hope of tracing their paths back to exploding stars, gamma-ray bursts, and cataclysmic phenomena involving black holes and neutron stars. It can expect to register about one per day.
Halzen, a professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in the United States, first presented his idea for capturing neutrino traces at the South Pole in 1988, but the project was not completed until 2011.
"I have to emphasise how lucky I was because, when we started this project, everybody realised this was maybe a good idea, but very few thought it would work, including myself," Halzen told the press conference by telephone.
Neutrinos are electrically neutral, undisturbed by any magnetic field, which means that, in contrast to electromagnetic waves such as visible light, the direction from which they arrive points directly back to their source.
The observatory has been able to determine that high-energy neutrinos originate within but also far outside our own galaxy, setting ‌in motion an ⁠interstellar quest to find the objects and processes that create them.
Through the long winter at the South Pole, when bringing anything in or out is difficult as temperatures below -50°C (-58°F) preclude even aircraft landing, a skeleton crew of "winterovers" have to maintain the observatory.
The station, home to many other activities, can house as many as 150 people and has an industrial kitchen, dining room, gym and even a greenhouse. Six days ago it celebrated the sun's return above the horizon aftre six months of night with a six-hole ice-golf tournament.
Halzen said the main fruits of his work were not yet apparent and that it was too early to say exactly what it could reveal about the universe.
"The real excitement is ⁠that I cannot answer that question yet," he said. "This is just an introduction to the science, the astronomy is still to come."
Winners from Einstein to Bohr and the Curies
Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever congratulated Halzen on the recognition of "a life dedicated to unraveling the greatest secrets of the cosmos through its most minuscule manifestations".
The Nobel physics laureate receives an award of 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million).
The Nobel Prizes were established under the will of Swedish inventor and entrepreneur ⁠Alfred Nobel, whose fortune was built in part on the invention of dynamite.
Physics was prominent in Nobel's will and the prize remains one of the discipline's highest distinctions. Over the decades, it has recognised discoveries that have fundamentally reshaped humanity's understanding of the universe.
Among past laureates are some of the most celebrated figures in science, including Albert Einstein, Marie and Pierre Curie, Max Planck and Niels Bohr, whose work helped ⁠establish the foundations of modern physics.
Nobel medals are presented by Sweden's King Carl XVI Gustaf at a ceremony in Stockholm on December 10, the anniversary of Nobel's death, which is followed by a banquet.
The Peace Prize, the only Nobel not presented in Sweden, is awarded separately in Oslo.

title: PTI dismisses PM Shehbaz s  mere offer  for talks  says govt can initiate contact with opposition leadership
description: Barrister Gohar says PTI has not been granted access to Imran for almost a year  decries  inhumane  treatment
content:
Barrister Gohar says PTI has not been granted access to Imran for almost a year, decries 'inhumane' treatment
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) on Tuesday dismissed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's proposal for renewed talks as a "mere offer”, while saying that the government could contact leaders of the opposition in the National Assembly and Senate for negotiations if it were sincere.
The statement came amid heightened political tensions in the country as the PTI's long march reached Kohat. Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi is leading the convoy, which began its march towards Islamabad on Sunday to demand the release of party founder Imran Khan and press the government over what PTI describes as broader political and constitutional grievances. The convoy is currently in Kohat after travelling through Lakki Marwat and Karak, and is expected to depart for Peshawar later today as the party continues its phased mobilisation towards the federal capital.
PM Shehbaz earlier today renewed an offer of talks to the PTI, saying the government was prepared to engage with the opposition if the party ended its long march and sit-ins.
Speaking to the media outside Adiala jail after being denied permission for a meeting with Imran, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan dismissed PM Shehbaz’s offer.
“This proposal of dialogue and talks is only at the level of a mere offer and no positive steps are being taken for this purpose by the government,” the PTI chairman underlined.
چیئرمین پی ٹی آئی بیرسٹر گوہر خان ملاقات کی اجازت نہ ملنے کے بعد اڈیالہ جیل کے باہر میڈیا سے گفتگو- قاسم زمان کی گرفتاری کی مذمت کی pic.twitter.com/Z9PRAatyQ3
Gohar said that the party had not been granted access for a meeting with Imran since almost a year. “It is a matter of grave concern for us that we have not been able to meet Imran Khan for a year, as our last meeting with him was on October 16 2025”.
Read : 'End long march, sit-ins and we will talk': PM Shehbaz once again extends olive branch to PT
Gohar questioned that if Imran’s doctors, family, party workers and his lawyers were not being allowed to meet him, then what steps was the government taking?
“This is inhumane treatment, and we have strongly condemned it.
“We have stood with the state and have raised the slogan of Pakistan with sincerity, but despite this, we have not been provided access to Imran,” he stated.
Gohar said that Imran and his wife were in jail and even Imran’s three sisters, who had nothing to do with politics, had been imprisoned, further enquiring as to why Imran’ sisters had been arrested and if so, why they had been put in jail.
“We consider it a crime for Imran’s sisters to spend even one day in jail. His sisters are apolitical and have only stood up for their brother.”
Gohar further condemned the arrest of Imran’s cousin, Qasim Zaman.
Former PM Imran Khan’s cousin, Qasim Zaman Khan, was illegally arrested earlier today, as he was waiting outside Adiala Jail for a court appointed meeting with arbitrarily detained and incommunicado Imran Khan. Imran Khan’s wife, nephew and three sisters are already under… pic.twitter.com/gIDuiwbLQz
“Our MPAs, MNAs and ministers have been picked up, and this practice of picking people and detaining them should now stop forever”.
Meanwhile, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja stated that the government could contact Leader of the Opposition in the Senate, Allama Raja Nasir Abbas and Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly, Mahmood Khan Achakzai, for further talks and negotiations.
Speaking to the media outside the Islamabad High Court, Raja underscored that the long march would continue until matters had been adequately “resolved”, further adding that a false narrative was being propagated that the long march had been cancelled.
“Imran has given complete authority to Allama Raja Nasir Abbas and Mahmood Khan Achakzai to negotiate on his behalf and make an agreement, and if the government wants to show some flexibility and negotiate, it can contact them,” Raja stated.
The government and PTI began negotiations on Friday in an attempt to defuse tensions over the party’s planned October 4 long march. The government wanted PTI to call off the march, while the opposition sought political consensus on its demands and maintained that the protest would proceed unless its concerns were addressed.
The two sides held a second round of talks on Saturday under National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq. The negotiations continued for several hours, with the parties initially agreeing on a five-point framework that included legal facilities for PTI founder Imran and his wife, an early hearing of pending cases, and meetings with their lawyers and family members.
The talks , however, ran into a deadlock over provisions concerning counter-terrorism operations in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. The negotiations eventually ended without an agreement in the early hours of Sunday, leaving the government and opposition at an impasse and paving the way for PTI to proceed with the first phase of its long march from K-P.
Read more: Naqvi blames K-P CM for talks ‘collapse’, warns Afridi will ‘be responsible’ if anyone dies during march
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the provincial government had backed away from commitments during the final stage of negotiations, including cooperation with the Centre on counter-terrorism measures, operations in the merged districts and implementation of the National Action Plan. PPP leader Sherry Rehman, who was part of the government negotiating team, said the talks collapsed after the K-P government refused to sign a draft that had already been agreed upon by the negotiating teams.
PTI, however, said the main obstacles were access to Imran and disagreement over how counter-terrorism operations should be conducted in K-P. The party said it wanted Imran to be consulted before any decision was taken to call off the long march and sought the involvement of the provincial government and political parties in framing a joint strategy against terrorism.
Raja said the federal government wanted the provincial government to endorse actions and operations initiated by the Centre, while PTI insisted that such measures should be agreed upon through consultation. The party also said the government had declined its demand for immediate access to Imran, which it described as the principal point of deadlock.

title: Pedro Pascal  Dua Lipa  Kristen Wiig and Nicole Kidman lip sync to AD  LA   s  Nicole Kidman    at Chanel
description: The viral lip sync came as the stars attended Chanel   s Spring Summer 2027 presentation at Paris Fashion Week
content:
The viral lip-sync came as the stars attended Chanel’s Spring/Summer 2027 presentation at Paris Fashion Week
Pedro Pascal, Dua Lipa, Kristen Wiig and Nicole Kidman joined forces for a viral moment at Chanel’s Spring/Summer 2027 show in Paris, lip-syncing to Slovak singer ADÉLA’s hit song “Nicole Kidman”.
The four stars were filmed taking part in a video set to the viral track ahead of Chanel’s show on October 5. The clip quickly gained attention online, with a post featuring the video surpassing 1.8 million views on social media.
The video sees the celebrities take turns lip-syncing to different parts of the song, with Pascal appearing in his Chanel look alongside Wiig, Lipa and Kidman. The moment was particularly fitting given that the song itself is a tribute to the Practical Magic and Eyes Wide Shut star.
“Nicole Kidman” has become a major viral hit since ADÉLA released it alongside her debut album PRIMA in September. The track has inspired a wave of TikTok videos and references to Kidman’s film career.
The song reached No. 3 on the Billboard Global 200 chart dated October 3 after recording 32.5 million streams worldwide in one week. It also reached No. 22 on the Billboard Hot 100, while WWD reported that the track had accumulated more than 78 million Spotify streams and 2.5 million TikTok shares.
ADÉLA, whose full name is Adéla Jergová, is a 22-year-old Slovak singer who has quickly gained international attention. Her song “Ain’t in LA” previously made her the first Slovak artist to enter the Billboard Hot 100, while PRIMA debuted at No. 4 on the Billboard 200.
Kidman has also embraced the song and its connection to her career. The track’s music video references several of her films, including Eyes Wide Shut , Moulin Rouge! , Birth and Babygirl , as well as her famous AMC cinema advertisement.
The viral lip-sync came as the stars attended Chanel’s Spring/Summer 2027 presentation at Paris Fashion Week. Kidman, Lipa and Pascal were among the high-profile guests at the Grand Palais for designer Matthieu Blazy’s latest collection.
The Chanel appearance gave ADÉLA’s viral track another high-profile moment, with the song moving from social media trends into one of the biggest celebrity gatherings of Paris Fashion Week.

title: Aaron Sorkin   s    The Social Reckoning    takes sharp aim at Mark Zuckerberg
description: Sony   s promotional campaign uses Instagram to mock Meta   s approach to political advertising
content:
Sony’s promotional campaign uses Instagram to mock Meta’s approach to political advertising
Aaron Sorkin’s The Social Reckoning is drawing attention for its unflinching portrayal of Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and its examination of the Facebook Files, with the film receiving its world premiere in New York ahead of its October 9 release.
The Sony Pictures production focuses on Frances Haugen, the former Facebook employee whose 2021 disclosures exposed internal company research and intensified scrutiny of the social media giant. Mikey Madison plays Haugen, while Jeremy Strong portrays Zuckerberg.
According to The Hollywood Reporter , Strong’s performance presents Zuckerberg as a highly controlled and unsympathetic figure, marking a sharp departure from Jesse Eisenberg’s more youthful interpretation of the Meta founder in The Social Network . The film depicts internal debates over platform policies, engagement and the consequences of decisions made by Facebook executives.
The project also drew attention through an unusual promotional campaign on Instagram. The advertisement states that Zuckerberg will love The Social Reckoning before adding a reference to Instagram’s approach to advertising fact checking. The campaign deliberately connects the film’s marketing with one of its central themes.
Sorkin’s screenplay incorporates material from Haugen’s Senate testimony, including concerns she raised about the company’s handling of safety and its business priorities. The story also revisits reporting surrounding Facebook’s algorithms and the way content that generates strong emotional reactions can spread across its platforms.
The film arrives at a time when Meta continues to face scrutiny over the effects of its services on young users. The company reached a settlement with US state attorneys general in a case concerning allegations related to children and its platforms.
The Social Reckoning follows Sorkin’s earlier work on The Social Network , although the new film shifts its focus from Facebook’s creation to the consequences of its growth and influence.
With Madison portraying Haugen and Strong taking on Zuckerberg, the film places corporate responsibility, social media and technology at the centre of its drama as it reaches cinemas.

title: Stephen Kings    modern    Carrie    adaptation earns strong Rotten Tomatoes score ahead of debut
description: Summer H  Howell leads eight episodes arriving together on Prime Video October 7
content:
Summer H. Howell leads eight episodes arriving together on Prime Video October 7
Mike Flanagan’s new episodic adaptation of Stephen King’s Carrie has earned a positive early response from critics, with Rotten Tomatoes currently listing an 84% Tomatometer score from 70 reviews. The series is scheduled to premiere on Prime Video on October 7, with all eight episodes arriving on the same day.
Summer H. Howell leads the cast as Carrie White, a sheltered teenager entering public high school after the sudden death of her father. Her arrival exposes her to bullying and the pressures of social media, while she also begins discovering increasingly dangerous telekinetic abilities. Samantha Sloyan plays her mother, Margaret White, with Siena Agudong, Alison Thornton, Joel Oulette, Josie Totah, Arthur Conti, Thalia Dudek, Amber Midthunder and Matthew Lillard also among the cast.
The new series comes from Flanagan, who previously adapted King’s work for Doctor Sleep and The Haunting of Hill House . The 2026 production expands the story into an eight episode television format while introducing changes designed to place Carrie’s experiences in a modern setting.
Critics have largely praised the performances and Flanagan’s approach to the material. Rotten Tomatoes’ critics consensus highlights the adaptation’s compassion and ingenuity, while reviews collected by the site have described Howell’s performance as a major strength. Some critics, however, have questioned whether the story benefits from being extended into a television series and argued that the new version is less frightening or distinctive than earlier adaptations.
Carrie has previously been adapted several times, most notably Brian De Palma’s 1976 film starring Sissy Spacek and Piper Laurie. That film remains highly regarded, holding a 94% critics’ score on Rotten Tomatoes.
With the new series approaching its Prime Video debut, its current critics’ score suggests Flanagan’s latest King adaptation has made a strong first impression overall, although audience reactions will provide another measure after release.

title: Andrew Garfield says Sam Altman initially seemed    great    before    Artificial        And then you learn more about a person
description: Garfield spent two to three months studying footage of Altman before filming began
content:
Garfield spent two to three months studying footage of Altman before filming began
Andrew Garfield has opened up about portraying OpenAI CEO Sam Altman in Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial , revealing that his initial impression of the technology executive changed as he researched the role.
Speaking at the world premiere of Artificial at the NEW YORK FILM FESTIVAL on October 5, Garfield recalled watching Altman testify before Congress. At the time, the actor said he viewed him as honest, transparent and willing to discuss regulation around artificial intelligence.
Garfield said his first impression was that Altman seemed “f***ing great”, adding that he appeared charismatic and someone who could be trusted with significant responsibility. He then acknowledged that researching a real person can lead to a more complicated understanding of their public and private image.
The actor spent two to three months watching footage and listening to material involving Altman while preparing for the role. Garfield said he felt a moral responsibility in making the film because developments in artificial intelligence were generating new concerns throughout production.
“I wish we could give it even more teeth in a way,” Garfield said at the premiere, arguing that greater scrutiny is needed around the people being given significant influence and autonomy through technology.
Artificial dramatises the rise of OpenAI and the events surrounding Altman’s controversial removal and subsequent return as CEO. The film also features Yura Borisov as OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever, Cooper Hoffman as Greg Brockman and Ike Barinholtz as Elon Musk.
Altman has not seen the finished film but has previously commented on its portrayal. In an interview with Vanity Fair , he said he understood the filmmakers were attempting to make a good movie, while indicating that he did not expect it to provide an accurate depiction of events.
The film was initially set for release through Amazon MGM before Neon acquired it. Artificial is scheduled to arrive in US cinemas on December 25, with Guadagnino directing from a screenplay by Simon Rich.
Garfield’s performance continues his history of portraying real people, following roles including Eduardo Saverin in The Social Network and Jonathan Larson in Tick, Tick… Boom! .

Ireland wore them in both games commemorating all the victims of the conflict in Gaza, with Israel sporting black armbands on Sunday ⁠in memory of the victims of the October 7 attack that sparked the war.

title: India among seven countries vying for 2036  Olympics  IOC says
description: Hungary  Turkey  South Africa and South Korea complete the list of interested parties
content:
Hungary, Turkey, South Africa and South Korea complete the list of interested parties
Seven countries, including India, Germany and Qatar, are in the running to ‌stage the 2036 Summer Olympics, the International Olympic Committee said on Tuesday.
Hungary, Turkey, South Africa and South Korea complete the list of interested parties, who are in preliminary talks with the IOC, with a shortlist to be drawn up in March next year and some countries progressing to a strategic dialogue phase.
"Wherever the Games take place, one thing must never change: athletes ⁠have to be at the heart of everything we do ," said IOC President Kirsty Coventry. "That is why, for every future host, delivering the best possible experience for the athletes must always be the starting point.”
India, the world's most populous nation, is attempting to land its first Olympics while Qatar, which has bid before with Doha, is campaigning to become the first Muslim-majority nation to host the world's biggest multi-sports event. Qatar staged the 2022 soccer World Cup.
Hungary, which most recently bid for the 2024 Olympics, has never staged the Games while Munich, host of the 1972 Olympics, is ‌Germany's candidate.
Turkey's Istanbul has failed in five previous attempts while South Africa is hoping to become the first African host of the Olympics. South Africa has major event experience, having organised the 2010 soccer World Cup.
South Korea has staged both summer and winter Olympics in Seoul in 1988 and Pyeongchang in 2018.
Preferred hosts will ⁠be named after the dialogue phase in 2028 and a final decision is expected in mid-2029.
Any other interested countries have until October 31 to come forward but new candidates are highly unlikely to emerge with less than ⁠four weeks before the deadline.
Bidding rules changed under Coventry this year, adding the strategic dialogue stage and involving members more throughout the process. It is also very likely that more than one ⁠country will be named as preferred hosts, unlike in past votes where just one bidder was put forward by the IOC executive board.
Los Angeles will stage the 2028 Summer Games and Australia's Brisbane will host them four years later.

title: Andrew Garfield used Stanislavski technique and crowdsourcing to play Sam Altman in Artificial
description: Garfield spent around two to three months watching and listening to footage of Altman  studying interviews
content:
Garfield spent around two to three months watching and listening to footage of Altman, studying interviews
Andrew Garfield spent months studying Sam Altman as he prepared to portray the OpenAI CEO in Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial , using crowdsourcing and the Stanislavski acting technique to understand the tech executive.
Garfield spent around two to three months watching and listening to footage of Altman, studying interviews and other publicly available material as he worked towards the performance. Rather than simply attempting to imitate Altman, the actor focused on understanding his behaviour and finding the character through observation.
The actor also used crowdsourcing as part of his research, seeking out people who had interacted with Altman and could offer insight into what he was like away from public appearances. The approach allowed Garfield to build his portrayal from a wider range of perspectives rather than relying solely on Altman’s media presence.
Garfield’s preparation also drew on the Stanislavski technique, an acting approach centred on creating a believable character through detailed psychological and emotional understanding. His work was particularly focused on capturing Altman’s mannerisms and physicality.
Artificial is directed by Guadagnino and centres on the events surrounding Altman’s dramatic removal as OpenAI CEO in November 2023 and his return to the company days later. Garfield stars alongside Yura Borisov, who plays OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever, while the film also features Ike Barinholtz as Elon Musk.
The film has attracted considerable attention because of its depiction of real events involving one of the most prominent figures in the artificial intelligence industry. Amazon MGM Studios originally backed the project but dropped it after entering into a major partnership with OpenAI. Neon subsequently acquired the film for release.
Artificial is set to premiere at the New York Film Festival before its theatrical release through Neon on December 25.

title: Anne Hathaway apologises for viral  Verity  red carpet moment
description: Anne Hathaway explains why she directed photographers during viral  Verity  red carpet appearance
content:
Anne Hathaway explains why she directed photographers during viral 'Verity' red carpet appearance
Anne Hathaway has addressed her viral red carpet appearance at the premiere of Verity , explaining why she began directing photographers during a chaotic photo call.
The 43-year-old actor discussed the moment during an appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon after footage of her interacting with photographers circulated online.
“I know exactly what you're going to show, it can only be one thing. It's horrifying; it is the stuff of nightmares, Jimmy,” Hathaway said before the clip was shown.
The footage showed Hathaway waving her arms and directing photographers as she posed alongside Verity co-stars Josh Hartnett and Dakota Johnson. She explained that she was attempting to help manage the crowded red carpet.
“It was like mom mode by way of chorus line,” Hathaway said. “I was trying to be helpful. There were so many of us and the photographers were getting upset, and the vibe was changing.”
Hathaway said she quickly regretted the moment after realising that the incident was also being recorded on video.
“I was doing it because I was trying to get them their picture, but when I was done I was like, 'but there's also video!' And I went into a full cringe crouch from inside.”
She subsequently apologised for the incident, saying, “I apologize, everybody. That girl came out to play last night. Actually, she didn't come to play. She came for business.”
Another recording showed Hathaway telling photographers, “OK, everybody ready? We are going to start from the left and then we can make our way that way.”
Johnson could be heard joking during the incident, “I'm going to leave.”
Verity , directed by Michael Showalter, stars Hathaway as crime writer Verity Crawford, who becomes incapacitated after an accident. Johnson plays a struggling writer hired by Verity’s husband to complete her bestselling series.
The film opened at No. 1 at the North American box office with $32.6 million domestically and $30 million internationally.

title: Nasir Adeeb questions society s double standards for men and women in  Dar e Nijaat
description: Veteran writer draws a contrast between how Zamil and Zaryab are judged  forgiven and given a chance to change
content:
Veteran writer draws a contrast between how Zamil and Zaryab are judged, forgiven and given a chance to change
Veteran writer Nasir Adeeb has questioned the double standards society applies to men and women when it comes to mistakes, morality and forgiveness, drawing a parallel with the characters of ongoing drama Dar-e-Nijaat .
Adeeb is one of Pakistan’s established film writers, best known for his work in Punjabi cinema and for writing the classic Maula Jatt . His long career has made him a familiar voice in discussions about Pakistani cinema and society.
In a recent discussion, he argued that men are often given considerably more room to make mistakes, repent and eventually regain their place in society, while women can remain under scrutiny for actions they may not have committed at all.
For Adeeb, the difference is not simply about individual mistakes but about who society believes deserves a second chance.
He pointed to what he sees as a familiar social pattern: a man may make serious personal or moral mistakes, change his behaviour and eventually be accepted as a reformed person. His past, while remembered, does not necessarily define him forever. Women, he argued, are often judged by a different standard.
Adeeb illustrated his point through Dar-e-Nijaat , drawing a contrast between the way the drama’s two leads, Zamil and Zaryab, are treated in relation to their mistakes and perceived transgressions. “It is very big to say a woman has committed a crime but are sins only for women as men are always forgiven,” he said.
For the writer, Zamil represents a man who can make mistakes yet still imagine a future in which society will accept him after he changes his ways. His eventual redemption remains possible because, in Adeeb’s reading, men are more readily given the space to recover from their past.
“He will get that 'nijaat',” Adeeb said, referring to the freedom and social acceptance he believes Zamil can ultimately receive.
Zaryab’s experience, however, raises a different question. “I link this to Dar-e-Nijaat because his Zamil’s character sees that he will be accepted from society — that, yes, I’ll change, won’t drink alcohol — but the girl who was seen even from the window, people will say, ‘Oh, she’s staring at someone.’”
The contrast, in Adeeb’s interpretation, lies at the heart of the drama’s wider conversation about reputation: a man can be forgiven for what he has done, while a woman can be condemned for what people merely believe she might have done.
The discussion comes as Dar-e-Nijaat continues to generate debate around Zamil and Zaryab’s relationship. Zamil’s behaviour has already prompted criticism from viewers, while Nameer Nawaz Khan himself has publicly acknowledged the problematic side of his character.
Adeeb’s comments therefore shift the discussion beyond whether Zamil is simply a good or bad character. His broader question is what happens after the wrongdoing: who gets the opportunity to change, and who is expected to carry the consequences?

title: Durefishan Saleem reveals the ending she wishes Zaryab had in  Dar e Nijaat
description: Actor envisions Zaryab returning to Harvard  building a career  travelling the world and putting herself first
content:
Actor envisions Zaryab returning to Harvard, building a career, travelling the world and putting herself first
Durefishan Saleem may have played Zaryab through one of the most emotionally complicated journeys in Dar-e-Nijaat , but the actor has a very different ending in mind for her character — one where she chooses herself.
Taking to Instagram, Durefishan shared the ending she would have liked to see for Zaryab, imagining a future in which the character returns to Harvard, completes her degree, starts vlogging, travels the world and builds a life around her own ambitions.
“My sister said she low-key wants Zaryab to go back to Harvard, start vlogging, casually flip her hair, get even richer, lean into her girl gang, and travel the world and honestly, in an ideal world, without the dramatic license, I kind of want exactly the same for her,” she wrote in the caption of her Instagram post.
The post comes as Dar-e-Nijaat takes Zaryab from a promising young woman with a place at Harvard to someone whose life becomes increasingly shaped by heartbreak, faith, relationships and the choices of the people around her.
At the heart of the drama is a question of trust — and whether the person someone has trusted for years is necessarily the person who is actually good for them.
Zaryab's relationship with her childhood love, Zamil, is built on familiarity and emotional history, but his choices ultimately force her to confront how little she truly knows about the person she has placed her faith in.
The drama also explores the complicated relationship between religion, morality and personal choice. Zamil's decision to leave Zaryab in favour of a supposedly more religious path becomes part of a wider conversation about whether outward religiosity automatically makes someone a better partner or a better person.
Meanwhile, Zaryab's growing connection with Abu Bakr challenges her own assumptions about what goodness and compatibility look like. That makes Zaryab's eventual decision particularly divisive.
After everything she loses, Zaryab still ends up married, leaving some viewers wondering whether the story could have offered her another form of resolution, while also hoping it still can as the drama continues to air.
Durefishan's Instagram post appears to tap directly into that question.
Her imagined ending does not necessarily reject romance; instead, it gives Zaryab something the drama's storyline arguably leaves viewers wanting — an identity outside the men in her life. A Harvard degree, a career, friends, travel and a life shaped by her own interests could have represented a different kind of happy ending.
One commenter, identifying herself as a Harvard alumna, wrote that the Pakistani women she knew at Ivy League universities were “powerhouses”, while another joked, “Leaving Harvard for a man is a sus move bestie! GO GET THAT DEGREE”.
Actor Danner Mobeen also joined the conversation, writing, “Gurl go back no man is worth it”.
Romaisa Khan, who plays Hamna in the series, added her own enthusiastic endorsement: “Take Hamna with you!”
The reaction reflects a larger debate Dar-e-Nijaat has generated around Zaryab's choices.
Earlier, Durefishan had addressed criticism of the character's journey, arguing that the story was not simply about whether women should or should not heal with another person, but about the different standards society applies to men and women when it comes to mistakes, redemption and moving on.
The discussion has also extended to Zamil's actions. Nameer Khan , who plays the character, previously called out Zamil's behaviour and urged men to be respectful, honest and accountable in relationships.

title: Bangladesh beat Pakistan in U19 Women s T20 tri series
description: Sadia Akter   s unbeaten 33 helps the visitors reach 139 5
content:
Sadia Akter’s unbeaten 33 helps the visitors reach 139-5
Bangladesh U19 Women beat Pakistan U19 Women by 13 runs in the fourth match of the Rivaj Presents the University of Lahore U19 Women’s T20 Tri-nation series at the Iqbal Stadium in Faisalabad on Tuesday.
This was Pakistan’s second defeat in the tournament.
Batting first, Bangladesh U19 Women scored 139 for five in their allotted 20 overs before restricting Pakistan U19 Women to 126 for seven.
Bangladesh were reduced to four for two in the second over before Ochena Jannat Emanta and Nishita Akter Nishi helped steady the innings. Nishita scored 20 off 19 balls, hitting three fours, while Emanta contributed 17 off 18 balls.
Sadia Islam then scored 24 off 21 balls, hitting three fours before the tourists slipped to 88 for five in 13.1 overs.
Sadia Akter and Farjana Easmim Medha added an unbeaten 51 runs for the sixth wicket to take Bangladesh to 139 for five. Sadia remained unbeaten on 33 off 33 balls, including two fours and a six, while Farjana scored an unbeaten 28 off 22 balls with three fours and a six.
For Pakistan, right-arm off-spinner Rozina Akram returned figures of two for 21, while Maham Nazakat took two wickets for 22 runs.
In turn, Pakistan made a strong start as openers Komal Khan and Ravail Farhan added 69 runs. Komal top-scored with 36 off 29 balls, hitting four fours and a six, while Ravail scored 32 off 29 balls with six fours.
The tourists hit back by removing Komal and Ravail in the 10th over before Areesha Ansari was dismissed for one in the following over.
Zoofishan Ayyaz scored 32 off 30 balls and kept Pakistan in the contest, but regular wickets slowed the chase.
Farjana was the pick of the Bangladesh bowlers, taking three wickets for 25 runs in four overs, while Nishita took two for 28.
Bangladesh – the table toppers will take on Sri Lanka in the fifth fixture of the tournament on Thursday, 8 October.

title: Kaisay signs knowledge partnership with Sri Lanka's Marga Institute | The Express Tribune
description: Agreement follows Bangladesh partnership as Pakistani podcast platform eyes Nepal next
content:
Agreement follows Bangladesh partnership as Pakistani podcast platform eyes Nepal next
Pakistani podcast and media platform Kaisay, with Raja Jawad, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Sri Lanka’s Marga Institute, establishing the research organisation as its knowledge partner for Sri Lanka-focused work.
The agreement was signed at the Marga Institute in Colombo on Saturday by Kaisay founder and host Raja Jawad and Amar Gunatilleke, Executive Vice Chairman of the institute, in the presence of representatives from both organisations, according to a press release.
Under the MoU, the two organisations will share research and perspectives on social and development issues, with specific activities to be jointly developed.
“South Asia has more to gain when we listen to one another with curiosity and respect,” Jawad said, adding that Pakistan and Sri Lanka, despite their different experiences, face several common challenges involving livelihoods, education and opportunity.
“Kaisay South Asia aims to bring the people working on those questions into a wider conversation,” he said, describing Marga’s knowledge of Sri Lanka as an important addition to the initiative.
Gunatilleke said research was most useful when it reached people and informed public discussion.
“We welcome the opportunity to share Sri Lankan perspectives with audiences in Pakistan and across the region, while learning from experiences elsewhere,” he said.
Sri Lanka is the second country where Kaisay South Asia has established a knowledge partnership. The platform earlier signed a separate MoU with Research and Policy Integration for Development (RAPID), a Dhaka-based policy research organisation, for its Bangladesh-focused work.
Kaisay said the two partnerships were country-specific, with RAPID working on Bangladesh-related initiatives and Marga supporting its Sri Lanka-focused activities. The platform plans to expand its regional work to Nepal next, with details to be developed separately.
The Marga Institute is an independent, non-profit Centre for Development Studies established in Sri Lanka in 1972. It conducts multidisciplinary research on development and disseminates its work through education and training, publications and civil society engagement.

title: Pamela Anderson could inherit  10m from 12 day marriage
description: Pamela Anderson could inherit  10m from Jon Peters  despite conflicting accounts of their 12 day marriage
content:
Pamela Anderson could inherit $10m from Jon Peters, despite conflicting accounts of their 12-day marriage
Pamela Anderson could inherit $10 million from producer Jon Peters after their 2020 marriage, despite the former couple giving conflicting accounts of whether they were ever legally married.
Anderson and Peters were romantically involved after first meeting at the Playboy Mansion in the 1980s. Peters told The Hollywood Reporter in 2017 that he immediately believed Anderson would become a major star.
The pair later rekindled their relationship after Anderson’s marriage to Rick Salomon ended. They reportedly married in 2020, but their relationship ended after just 12 days.
Peters later said he still had strong feelings for Anderson. In a 2023 interview with Variety , he said, “I will always love Pamela, always in my heart,” before adding, “As a matter of fact, I left her $10 million in my will.”
However, Anderson has disputed the account that the pair were legally married. During an appearance on Awards Chatter, she said, “I never was married to Jon Peters.”
Anderson explained that Peters had contacted her son and offered him $20 million if he could convince her to marry him. She said she subsequently met Peters for lunch, where he had arranged flowers and gathered family members.
“But I never married Jon. It was never a marriage, but we were just laughing about that,” Anderson said.
A source also previously claimed that Anderson and Peters never legally filed the marriage.
Peters has given a different account of their brief relationship. Speaking to Page Six in 2020, he claimed Anderson had asked him to marry her and said, “She had almost $200,000 in bills and no way to pay it so I paid it and this is the thanks I get. There's no fool like an old fool.”
The conflicting accounts leave the legal status of the reported marriage unclear. Peters’ reported $10 million bequest nevertheless remains connected to their short-lived relationship.

title: Mika Singh challenges negative perceptions of Pakistani Muslims
description: Indian singer recalls the warmth he experienced in Pakistan and speaks positively about its people and Sikh heritage
content:
Indian singer recalls the warmth he experienced in Pakistan and speaks positively about its people and Sikh heritage
Indian singer and rapper Mika Singh has questioned why Pakistani Muslims are often viewed negatively by some Indians, while Muslims living in Dubai are generally perceived more positively.
Speaking in a recent interview, Singh discussed his connection with Pakistan and recalled his experiences with Muslims there, including those who helped maintain Sikh gurdwaras.
He questioned why people appeared to make distinctions between Muslims based on where they were from.
“Muslims from anywhere are not bad. I don't know why we only see Muslims from Pakistan as bad, but like Dubai's Muslims," he said. He added: “I still don't get it.”
Singh also stressed that he did not believe Pakistanis were inherently bad, recalling the warmth and hospitality he experienced during his visit to the country.
"The reason I like Pakistan so much is due to an emotional story. Therre is Guru Nanak's Gudwara there. There is Nankana Sahib and Panja Sahib. There are three very big Gudwara's there," he said.
He continued, "Whenever I get the moment, I always speak positively on Pakistan." The rapper also emphasised that, like many others, he had no issue with Pakistani singers performing in India.
"Whenever someone comes, everyone in our industry has so many problems but I have no issues. I have always gotten respect from them," he said.
Singh's comments have prompted discussion online, with some commenters agreeing with his broader point that perceptions of Pakistanis and Pakistani Muslims can be influenced by the long and complicated history between India and Pakistan.
Others pointed to politics and the way India-Pakistan tensions are discussed publicly, arguing that political narratives can shape how ordinary people view communities across the border.
"That's how politicians have played it," one user wrote, while another added, "Politicians spread hate and lies against Pakistan that the British started when they left."
The singer's remarks come amid a wider conversation about Indian and Pakistani artistes, cross-border cultural exchanges and the distinction between individuals and political tensions between the two countries.
By comparing perceptions of Pakistani and Dubai Muslims, Singh appeared to question whether people's views were sometimes shaped more by nationality, history and politics than by their individual experiences with people.

title: Gauff calls out online racism after China Open win
description: The American says she receives an    insane    amount of racist messages following her disputed challenge against Sun
content:
The American says she receives an “insane” amount of racist messages following her disputed challenge against Sun
American tennis star Coco Gauff said Tuesday she faced an "insane" amount of online racist abuse after defeating Chinese teenager Sun Xinran in a match that included a video review.
During Monday's China Open match against 16-year-old Sun Xinran in Beijing, the former US Open champion requested a video review over flickering LED lights, prompting some boos from the crowd.
"Hey everyone, you can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist," Gauff wrote on X. "The amount of racist comments and messages I've received in the last few hours is insane," her post read.
The umpire agreed for the point to be replayed, and 22-year-old Gauff went on to win the match 7-5, 6-1.
Responding on X to a post containing a racial slur that was flagged as potential "hateful content", the Black American player clarified in a separate post that she challenged the point before Sun's return when she noticed the lights flicker a second time.
"I think it's weird I'm getting hate for following the rules," she said, explaining that players are instructed they can challenge points after play has concluded.
"Xinran is an incredible talent and player. I apologised for the situation at the end of the match, and she completely understood," she added.
By Tuesday morning, the hashtag "Gauff apologised to Sun Xinran after the match" had hit 4.5 million views, ranking as the sixth top trend on Chinese social media platform Weibo.
The Women's Tennis Association (WTA) did not immediately respond to AFP.
During a quarter-final match between Alexander Zverev and Novak Djokovic in the men's draw on Sunday, the umpire also agreed to replay a point after Zverev complained about flickering panels.
Gauff, the world No. 4, claimed the Beijing title in 2024. She is due to play Belgium's Elise Mertens in the round of 16 on Wednesday.

title: Alcaraz wins Japan Open
description: He defeats Czech Republic s Jiri Lehecka in straight sets
content:
He defeats Czech Republic's Jiri Lehecka in straight sets
Carlos Alcaraz won his first title since returning from a four-month injury layoff after beating the Czech Republic's Jiri Lehecka 7-6 (7/4), 6-4 in Tuesday's Japan Open final.
Top seed and defending champion Alcaraz was made to work hard by world number 19 Lehecka in Tokyo before going on to lift his first trophy since the Qatar Open in February.
It was Alcaraz's third tournament since coming back from a wrist injury, following a run to the US Open quarter-finals and an appearance at the Laver Cup.
It was the world number three's third title of the year including the Australian Open, and the 27th of his career.
Hours earlier, world number one Jannik Sinner announced that he had brought a premature end to his season due to an ongoing knee injury.
Alcaraz went into the final with a 3-1 career head-to-head record against Lehecka, who was looking to win his first title of the year.
Alcaraz had his service broken immediately by a confident-looking Lehecka, who gave his top-seeded opponent no time to settle.
The Spaniard broke back in a long tussle midway through the first set and followed that up with a brutal display of power tennis in the next game.
Lehecka proved a tough nut to crack though, and Alcaraz needed to pull out a pair of spectacular drop shots to clinch the first set in a tiebreaker.
Lehecka continued to give Alcaraz problems but the defending champion went a break up midway through the second set and made no mistakes to close out the victory.
Alcaraz is scheduled to play in the Shanghai Masters starting Wednesday.
He pulled out of last year's tournament at the last minute after winning in Tokyo, blaming "physical issues" and taking aim at tennis' packed schedule.

title: Shaan Shahid questions whether social media fame can sustain an acting career
description: Veteran actor says viral popularity may fade unless digital creators invest in learning the craft of acting
content:
Veteran actor says viral popularity may fade unless digital creators invest in learning the craft of acting
Actor and filmmaker Shaan Shahid has sparked a debate over the growing presence of TikTokers and social media personalities in television and film after questioning whether online fame can translate into a lasting acting career.
The veteran actor made the remarks during a recent interview, where he was asked about the rise of content creators such as Rajab Butt and other influencers making their way into mainstream entertainment.
A clip from the conversation has since circulated widely on social media, prompting viewers to debate whether internet popularity can sustain a career beyond the digital sphere.
Shaan appeared to distinguish between having a platform and mastering the craft of acting. While he said he could not dictate what content creators should do with their own platforms, he questioned whether social media fame alone was enough to build a lasting career in the entertainment industry.
However, when speaking specifically about the acting industry, Shaan was more sceptical about the longevity of creators who enter television or film without formally developing their skills. “It’s not going to last. The temporary phase will fade away. First you will get a lot of hype,” he said.
He further questioned how quickly audiences move on from television personalities, asking, “Tell me how many names you remember from dramas.”
For Shaan, the issue is not necessarily that TikTokers or other digital creators are entering the industry, but whether they invest in understanding the profession once they get there. “If you don’t learn the art and craft of the job and just get a hit, you will be successful but they’ll understand why it isn’t relevant after one or three years from now,” he said.
His comments have divided social media users. While some agreed that viral popularity does not automatically translate into acting ability or a sustainable career, others took issue with what they viewed as an overly dismissive assessment of digital creators.
Some fans poked fun at Shaan’s remarks, suggesting that no single actor owns the entertainment industry or gets to decide who belongs in it. Others pointed out that the traditional boundaries between television, cinema and digital media have already become increasingly blurred.
“Actors are singing, singers are acting but everyone has problems with TikTokers and YouTubers. All the actors have their YouTube channels and are even going on TikTok as well,” one user wrote.
The debate has also prompted comparisons with creators who have successfully moved beyond social media. Some users argued that there are already examples of YouTubers and TikTokers who have managed to build substantial careers by using their online platforms as a starting point rather than treating them as an endpoint.
At the heart of the discussion is a question that predates TikTok: whether fame and talent are the same thing. Social media can give an emerging performer an audience almost overnight, while traditional acting careers have historically required years of work, training and exposure.
Shaan himself has spent decades in Pakistan’s film industry. His career has included hundreds of films, directing projects and some of the country’s most recognisable action and dramatic roles.
In a 2026 interview about his upcoming film Bullah , he also spoke about how he studied the work of earlier Punjabi cinema stars and watched thousands of films while developing his own screen persona.
The actor has also previously been outspoken about the state of Pakistani cinema. In May 2026 , he spoke about the industry’s reliance on Eid releases and his concerns that local cinema had become disconnected from its wider audience.
His history of speaking bluntly about the entertainment industry has made Shaan a familiar figure in debates over Pakistani cinema. In 2022 , he also drew attention for his comments about language and acting in The Legend of Maula Jatt , another instance in which his views generated discussion among audiences and fellow industry watchers.

title: End of an era as Messi prepares to hang up Argentina boots
description: Some 85 000 fans are expected at the Monumental as the World Cup winner faces Benin in final international appearance
content:
Some 85,000 fans are expected at the Monumental as the World Cup winner faces Benin in final international appearance
Lionel Messi will pull on Argentina's sky blue-and-white jersey for the last time on Tuesday and enjoy an emotional farewell in front of his adoring fans in a stadium with a name to match his legacy: Monumental.
Some 85,000 Argentina fans will be on hand to watch the 39-year-old idol perform his wizardry in a friendly against Benin that brings down the curtain on his 21-year international career.
Millions more will be following the action in South America's largest stadium, Buenos Aires' Estadio Monumental, on TV.
The most-capped player in Argentine history is hanging up his boots two-and-a-half months after losing the World Cup final to Spain.
"I gave it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance," Messi wrote when announcing his international retirement in August.
On Monday, he took part in his last training session with the team at the complex that bears his name in the Buenos Aires suburb of Ezeiza.
"You can't ask for more, that's it," Nahuel Nieva, a retail worker who took the day off work to watch his hero train, told AFP.
Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated.
No effort has been spared for the sendoff of a player considered one of the game's greatest ever.
Several of the teammates with whom he reached football's pinnacle in Qatar, and who will lead the post-Messi team, will play in the game, including defender Cristian "Cuti" Romero, midfielders Alexis Mac Allister and Enzo Fernandez and forwards Julian Alvarez and Lautaro Martinez.
After the game the captain's armband will pass to Romero.
Coach Lionel Scaloni has vowed to try fill the "void" left by his talismanic captain and the signs from the next generation, some of whom weren't even alive when Messi debuted with the team in 2005, are auspicious.
In their first games since the World Cup final last week, minus Messi, Argentina thrashed Bolivia 4-0 in a friendly in Cordoba on Wednesday before running rings around Burkina Faso on Saturday at Monumental stadium.
Franco Mastantuono and Gianluca Prestianni, two of Argentina's brightest new hopes, both scored their first international goals against Burkina Faso in a 7-0 romp.
The results helped lift the gloom of the defeat in the World Cup final when Argentina and a visibly tired Messi were outplayed by Spain and resorted to thuggish tactics which have been punished with bans and fines for a number of players.
Messi is not only Argentina's record appearance-maker but also its leading scorer with 125 goals in 207 games, as well as a record 68 assists.
"La Pulga" (The Flea) won the eternal gratitude of Argentines -- and sealed his place as rightful heir to Diego Maradona -- in 2022 when he ended their 36-year World Cup drought in Qatar.
During his time with the Albiceleste, Argentina were also crowned 2005 World Youth Champions, 2008 under-23 Olympic champions and they won the Copa America in 2021 and 2024. They also won the 2022 Finalissima, a match between the champions of South America and Europe.
But there were tears along the way too, notably after Argentina's defeat by Germany in the 2014 World Cup final in Brazil, their loss to Spain in this year's final and their shock humiliation by Chile in the 2016 Copa America final.
One detail remains unclear, however: who will inherit Messi's coveted number 10 jersey?
"Until Leo's game, we won't give the number 10 to anyone," said Scaloni. "After that, we'll see."

title: Jack Nicholson   s    The Shining    axe heads to auction for up to   50 000
description: Kubrick   s annotated scripts and    2001  A Space Odyssey    prop are also among the auction highlights
content:
Kubrick’s annotated scripts and ‘2001: A Space Odyssey’ prop are also among the auction highlights
An iconic special effects axe used by Jack Nicholson in Stanley Kubrick’s 1980 horror classic The Shining is heading to auction, with a list price of £30,000 to £50,000.
The axe was wielded by Nicholson as Jack Torrance during one of the film’s most recognisable sequences. Torrance hacks through a locked bathroom door while pursuing his wife Wendy, played by Shelley Duvall, before delivering the famous line "Here’s Johnny!" The prop is also associated with the killing of Dick Hallorann, played by Scatman Crothers.
The item is among hundreds of pieces being offered from Kubrick’s personal archive. The auction, organised by Bonhams, is scheduled to take place in London on February 3, 2027, following public exhibitions in New York, Los Angeles, Paris and London.
Several other items from The Shining are included. They include the two sky blue dresses worn by the Grady twins, Alexa and Alexie, during the eerie scene in which they invite Danny Torrance to play with them. A clapperboard from the film is also being offered alongside clapperboards from 2001: A Space Odyssey , Barry Lyndon and Eyes Wide Shut .
The auction’s expected top lot is a model of the cosmic foetus, known as the star child prop, from the final scene of 2001: A Space Odyssey . It is estimated to fetch up to £800,000.
Kubrick’s annotated film scripts are also among the highlights, offering notes, drawings and alternative scenes from productions including The Shining , 2001: A Space Odyssey and Lolita . His personal script from Spartacus , his director’s chair and a chess set are also part of the collection.
The sale offers collectors an opportunity to acquire objects connected to one of cinema’s most influential directors, whose meticulous approach to filmmaking helped make the term "Kubrickian" part of film vocabulary and remains associated with his distinctive style.

title: Norwegian FA files complaints with FIFA committees
description: Filings cover peace prize  Balogun suspension lift and proposed World Cup stake sales
content:
Filings cover peace prize, Balogun suspension lift and proposed World Cup stake sales
The Norwegian Football Association (NFF) has made two parallel filings with two FIFA committees in relation to three recent ⁠issues that have caused significant controversy in the global football community, it said on Tuesday.
The Norwegians have made the filings with the global governing body's committees on ethics and governance, according to a document seen by Reuters.
The filings mark the NFF's most formal challenge yet ⁠to the leadership of FIFA President Gianni Infantino, escalating longstanding tensions over governance and transparency within world soccer's governing body.
"The first filing is a complaint to the FIFA Ethics Committee. It asks the Ethics Committee to examine the conduct of FIFA President ⁠Gianni Infantino and any other individuals identified through ⁠the investigation for potential breaches of FIFA’s Code of Ethics," the NFF said in a statement.
"The second filing is a referral to FIFA’s Governance, Audit and Compliance Committee (“GACC”). It asks whether FIFA’s governance, financial oversight, internal controls and decision-making processes have worked as intended."
The NFF said the filings related to three separate incidents -- the FIFA Peace Prize, the lifting of a suspension ⁠on US forward Folarin Balogun during the World Cup, and the abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) project ⁠that would have allowed investors to purchase minority stakes in FFE which was going to run FIFA tournaments including the World Cup.
"NFF has for several years raised questions about governance, transparency and separation of powers within FIFA. These filings are a natural continuation of NFFs commitment to the governance of international football," the statement said.
"The purpose is to raise these issues formally ⁠with the appropriate bodies, to have them examined, relevant evidence obtained and accountability for the conclusions reached."
The complaint to the Ethics Committee is expected to be evaluated by the body's investigatory chamber, while the GACC is being asked to use its existing oversight powers to review the governance and institutional issues raised by the three matters, the NFF said. Reuters has contacted FIFA for comment.

title: Former German spy chief arrested over alleged buying of classified information
description: It was not immediately    clear whether the analysis on the classified documents reached its intended recipient
content:
It was not immediately ​clear whether the analysis on the classified documents reached its intended recipient
Former German foreign intelligence chief August Hanning was arrested on Tuesday on suspicion of ​paying for access to classified documents and using them ‌to prepare an analysis for a foreign intelligence service, federal prosecutors said.
Prosecutors did not identify the foreign intelligence service, and it was not immediately ​clear whether the analysis reached its intended recipient.
Prosecutors allege ​that five years after his tenure as head of ⁠the BND intelligence service ended in 2005, Hanning agreed with ​a former BND office manager to receive confidential intelligence information in ​exchange for payment.
The office manager, identified as Manfred D. in line with privacy rules, was also arrested on Tuesday.
Prosecutors said D. is suspected of having ​supplied around 2,000 documents over the years, including classified material ​intended solely for internal use within the BND and senior-level intelligence briefings ‌at ⁠the chancellery.

According to prosecutors, Hanning used classified information supplied by D. to prepare an analysis for an officer of a foreign intelligence service and for years shared political information with a representative ​of another foreign ​intelligence service.
According ⁠to information obtained by the SZ newspaper, the case does not involve Russia.
Hanning did not respond ​to a request for comment from Reuters. The ​BND declined ⁠to comment and referred to prosecutors. The chancellery declined to comment.
Police carried out arrests and searches in the states of Bavaria, North ⁠Rhine-Westphalia ​and Berlin on Tuesday, and both ​suspects were due to appear before a judge at the Federal Court of Justice, ​prosecutors added.

content:
This will be their first game since being found guilty of serious breaches
Manchester City face a hostile reception at Liverpool on Sunday in their first game since being found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules, though how much the verdict will affect the leaders remains unclear.
Fan chatrooms have been humming with opinion and invective but that is nothing new when it comes to relations between the old rivals.
The "sham" commercial contract case has hung over the Premier League for years and may rumble on for some time yet after City filed an ⁠appeal.
Just how much it spills over into the stands at Anfield, and grounds beyond that over the course of the season, remains to be seen.
"If they want an understanding of how angry the game is going to be, then Anfield will tell them like you would never believe," former Manchester United captain and England defender Gary Neville declared recently on The Overlap podcast.
"I suspect there may be banners, there will certainly be chanting. There will be a reception like you have never seen for them at Anfield...it will be a brutal day."
Merseyside Police said there would be an appropriate policing operation in place on the day.
Other commentators said that Liverpool ⁠supporters had been calling City cheats since they were charged by the Premier League in February 2023.
"Man City players already know what rival fans will do amid charges fallout," read a headline in the Manchester Evening news, opens new tabon Monday.
"City players won't necessarily be walking into anything new when they resume their club duties this weekend," wrote the paper's chief City reporter.
"It is not going to ⁠be pretty, but it will be a surprise if it catches the players off guard given how used to the abuse they are." City are unbeaten and three points clear of champions Arsenal at the top of the table, five ahead of ⁠third-placed Brighton & Hove Albion.

title: Fact check  Viral video does not show Baloch female activist killed by police  footage is from Afghanistan
description: Viral video does not show Pakistani police killing female activist in Balochistan  footage is from Afghanistan
content:
Viral video is from Afghanistan and shows a woman reportedly killed by her husband in Ghor province
Several people have been sharing a video on social media platform X since Monday, claiming that it shows the body of a female activist in Balochistan killed by police after being detained for three months and subjected to severe torture. However, the video actually shows a woman who was allegedly tortured and killed by her husband in Afghanistan’s Ghor province last month.
A day ago, an X user who appears to be pro-Afghanistan, based on the account’s previous posts, and who frequently shares content critical of Pakistan’s military and political institutions, posted a video showing the body of a woman with the following caption: “Brutal murder of a 32-year-old female activist in Balochistan. Pakistani police have killed a 32-year-old female activist following three months of detention as a result of severe torture.”
The caption further claimed that the woman’s family said that “various parts of her body were burned with hot iron rods before she was killed”.
Today, another X user shared the same video with a similar caption. That post received 35,800 views.
The video was also shared the same day by YouTuber Adil Raja with the following caption: “Gruesome murder of a 32-year-old female activist in Balochistan. Pakistani police allegedly subjected a 32-year-old female activist to severe torture after three months in custody, resulting in her death. Is this Asim Munir's 'hard state'? And is this the work of Mohsin Naqvi's SHO?”
The video was later shared by multiple other X users, as shown here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here, here , and here .
A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to its high virality and significant public interest in instances of custodial killings.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video yielded a news report published by Afghan media outlet 8AM Media , also known as Hasht-e-Subh Daily , on Oct 4, 2026, titled “The gruesome murder of Nuria in Ghor; a woman tortured and killed before her children’s eyes.”
The report said the woman was 32-year-old Nuria, who was killed in Tangi Sarpanak village, Taywara district, Ghor province, Afghanistan. According to sources cited by the outlet, she was severely beaten and allegedly tortured with a heated iron rod by her husband in front of her children.
The report said she died from her injuries and that her husband later confessed to the killing and surrendered to the Taliban. It also stated that the incident had taken place around 14 days before the article was published.
A subsequent keyword search using terms related to the woman’s name, age, location and manner of death found that several other Afghan media outlets had reported on the same incident.
Kabul Times News , in a report published on Oct 4, also identified the victim as 32-year-old Nuria and said she died after being beaten and tortured by her husband in Tangi Sarpanak village.
KabulNow , in an article published on Oct 5, also reported that a 32-year-old woman named Nuria was tortured and killed in Taywara district of Ghor province, allegedly by her husband in front of their four children.
Another report by Exile TV , published on Oct 5, said the incident occurred on September 20, 2026 , following an argument involving Nuria and her mother-in-law. The outlet reported that her husband allegedly assaulted her and burned parts of her body with a heated iron rod before she died from her injuries.
These reports consistently placed the incident in Ghor province, Afghanistan, and identified the alleged perpetrator as the woman’s husband, contradicting the viral claim that the footage showed a female activist killed by Pakistani police in Balochistan.
The claim that a viral video shows the body of an activist killed by the police in Balochistan is false.
The footage is from Afghanistan’s Ghor province and shows the body of a 32-year-old woman who was reported to have been tortured and killed by her husband in September 2026.

title: Kaur steps down as India women   s cricket captain
description: World Cup winning skipper ends decade long leadership tenure but will continue playing for India
content:
World Cup-winning skipper ends decade-long leadership tenure but will continue playing for India
Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down as captain of India’s women’s cricket team across all formats, ending a leadership tenure that included the country’s maiden Women’s Cricket World Cup triumph.
The 37-year-old announced the decision with immediate effect on Tuesday, but said she would continue playing for India. “Today, I step down as captain of the Indian women’s cricket team across all formats,” Kaur said in a statement posted on Instagram.
“This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life.”
Kaur became India’s T20 captain in 2016 and took charge of the ODI and Test teams in 2022 after the retirement of Mithali Raj.
Her biggest achievement came last year when she led India to their first Women’s Cricket World Cup title, with the hosts defeating South Africa in the final on home soil in November.
Kaur became only the third Indian captain after Kapil Dev and Mahendra Singh Dhoni to win a 50-over World Cup. She is also among five Indian captains to have won a World Cup, alongside Rohit Sharma and Suryakumar Yadav, who led India to T20 World Cup titles in 2024 and 2026 respectively.
Her final assignment as captain ended with India winning their second successive Asian Games gold medal this year, following their triumph in 2022.
Kaur captained India in five Tests, 51 ODIs and 155 T20 internationals. She became the first captain in international cricket to lead a team in more than 150 T20Is.
Her tenure also included a silver medal at the 2022 Commonwealth Games, a runners-up finish at the 2020 Women’s T20 World Cup and semi-final appearances at the 2018 and 2023 editions.
“Now, I’m ready to play for the love of the game again. Captaincy ends. The journey continues,” Kaur said.
