description: Judge sets aside lower court findings  says  law does not permit inversion of burdens
content:
Judge sets aside lower court findings, says 'law does not permit inversion of burdens'
The Lahore High Court (LHC) ruled on Tuesday that a deficiency in furnishing precise particulars of alleged fraud could not, by itself, establish an oral gift or relieve its beneficiary of the independent burden of proving the transaction from which title is claimed, particularly when the gift excluded legal heirs from inheritance.
In a detailed judgment, Justice Anwaar Hussain of LHC's Rawalpindi Bench held that a mutation merely recorded an asserted transaction and could not substitute for proof of the underlying gift. A person relying on an oral gift must independently establish its three essential ingredients — declaration by the donor, acceptance by the donee and delivery of possession — through cogent and reliable evidence, the court noted.
It observed that the burden on a person challenging a transaction on grounds of fraud and the burden on a beneficiary claiming an oral gift as the source of title were two distinct burdens. Failure by the challenger to prove one circumstance alleged in support of fraud could not affirmatively establish that the gift was declared, accepted or completed. Similarly, requiring particulars of fraud could not absolve the beneficiary from proving the gift itself.
Justice Hussain noted that this distinction assumed particular importance where the alleged gift had the effect of excluding persons who would otherwise inherit the estate by operation of law.
The judge further held that particulars of fraud could emerge from the circumstances surrounding a disputed transaction, including the donor’s advanced age or serious illness, inability to understand or participate in the transaction, absence before the revenue authority, or absence of declaration or acceptance.
Therefore, what constituted sufficient particulars could not be determined through a rigid or formulaic test and had to be examined in the factual circumstances of each case.
The court particularly took note of donor Muhammad Sharif’s deteriorating health. The petitioners argued that he was elderly, seriously ill, remained under treatment for a considerable period and had become incapable of even speaking during his final days. The respondent had not specifically denied these assertions and instead described the relevant paragraph of the plaint as factual, making the donor’s physical condition an admitted fact.
Further, the court observed that the alleged gift mutation was recorded on February 22, 2011, while Sharif died on April 5, 2011, hardly one-and-a-half months later. Justice Hussain noted that the proximity of death alone could not establish marz-ul-maut (death illness), but when considered alongside the donor's admitted and progressively deteriorating illness, it constituted a circumstance requiring judicial scrutiny.
Read: LHC rejects property claim based on mutation
The judgement also relied on contemporaneous judicial proceedings recorded on March 30, 2011, days before Sharif’s death. The record showed that he was brought to an executing court in an ambulance because of his poor health and was found unable to speak. His feet were swollen and, considering his condition, the executing court released him on humanitarian grounds so he could receive treatment. Sharif died six days later.
Justice Hussain noted that the authenticity of this contemporaneous judicial record was not questioned and no evidence had been produced to dislodge it. The respondent herself also acknowledged during cross-examination that Sharif was brought to court in an ambulance, which, according to the court, materially corroborated the evidence of his serious illness.
The court also found flaws in the defence evidence regarding the donor’s condition. One attesting witness to the disputed mutation was related to the respondent and was therefore an interested witness, while another witness denied that Sharif was brought to court on a stretcher. The court held that these divergent versions, read with the respondent’s own admission regarding the ambulance, undermined the credibility of the defence evidence.
The judge clarified that death illness could not be established merely because a person was ill at the time of a transaction and subsequently died.
Read More: LHC fines petitioner for 'baseless' plea
The court had to examine whether the illness was connected with death, whether its nature created an apprehension of death, whether it incapacitated the person from performing ordinary activities and whether its duration sustained or diminished the apprehension of imminent death.
Applying these principles, the court held that the circumstances in the present case could not legally be brushed aside. The donor’s deteriorating condition was admitted, contemporaneous judicial proceedings showed that he was unable even to speak and was in sufficiently grave condition to be released for treatment, and he died six days later.
These circumstances, the court held, provided a substantial evidentiary basis requiring examination of his capacity and the validity of the alleged gift.
Turning to the alleged oral gift itself, the court observed that the respondent’s written statement did not disclose the date, time or place of the gift, the persons in whose presence the declaration was made, or the manner in which she accepted it. Judge Hussain described these details as the “factual anatomy” of an oral gift and held that a beneficiary could not rely on the resulting mutation while leaving the underlying transaction without a proven factual foundation.
The judge also held that the courts below had committed a legal error by effectively treating the petitioners’ alleged failure to provide precise particulars of fraud as the source of the respondent’s title.
Once the challenge was considered deficient, the alleged gift was virtually allowed to prove itself. “The law does not permit that inversion of burdens,” the judge observed.
Also Read: LHC seeks update on MPO judgment
The court further held that although concurrent findings of lower courts ordinarily commanded respect, they could not claim immunity where material evidence was ignored or misread, or where an erroneous rule regarding the burden of proof was applied. Such an error, the court said, entered the domain of legality and could be corrected in revisional jurisdiction.
The case arose from a dispute over a gift mutation dated February 22, 2011, allegedly executed in favour of Sharif’s wife. Sharif was issueless and died on April 5, 2011. His nephews challenged the mutation, alleging that it was forged and fraudulent and was procured to deprive them of their inheritance, particularly when the donor was suffering from illness. The trial court dismissed their suit in 2015, mainly on the grounds that the particulars of fraud had not been disclosed, and the appellate court upheld the decision in 2016.
The LHC, however, allowed the civil revision, set aside both judgments and decrees of the courts below, and decreed the petitioners’ suit as prayed for.

title: Rabada in contention to play first Australia Test
description: Decision on his participation will be left until the last minute
content:
Decision on his participation will be left until the last minute
South African pace bowler Kagiso Rabada is in contention to play in the first test against Australia, which starts on Friday, but a decision on his participation will be left until the last minute, batting coach Ashwell Prince said on Tuesday.
Rabada suffered a hamstring injury in training in June and there had been doubt over his participation in the series but he played in a two-day intra-squad match in Durban on Sunday and Monday and Prince said he bowled really well.
“He’ll continue to be involved, obviously, in training over the next few days ⁠leading up to the match, but it’s fair to say that he’s obviously not going to be 100% straightaway," Prince said.
“But he is looking good and he will train with the squad for the rest of the weekend and I think we will leave a call to be made as late as possible,” Prince added in a virtual press conference.
When the preliminary squad of 18 players was named for the Australia test series last month, coach Shukri Conrad warned they would take no chances with the 31-year-old Rabada, who has taken ⁠340 test wickets.
"We will give a decision as much time as humanly possible but we also don't want to take a call based on desperation," he told reporters.
Rabada’s inclusion would be a major boost to the hosts given his role as the team's leading quick bowler but the home side ⁠still have plenty of bowling options if they decide not to risk him.
Corbin Bosch, Gerald Coetzee, Marco Jansen, Anrich Nortje and Dane Paterson have all been selected as pace bowlers and spinners Simon ⁠Harmer, Keshav Maharaj and Senuran Muthusamy are in the squad too.
“We're blessed with whatever combination we choose,” said Prince of the possibility of fielding two spinners. “We can take 20 wickets ⁠whether it is seam heavy, or whether it is two spinners. What plan we go with depends on the surface,” he added.
Sunny conditions are expected over the weekend in the seaside city.

title: Gill  Abhishek  Raza shortlisted for ICC Men   s Player of the Month
description: The trio earn recognition for outstanding white ball performances in September
content:
The trio earn recognition for outstanding white-ball performances in September
India’s Shubman Gill and Abhishek Sharma have been nominated alongside Zimbabwe all-rounder Sikandar Raza for the ICC Men’s Player of the Month award for September after standout performances in white-ball cricket.
Gill’s month was the most prolific of the three, highlighted by an unbeaten 223 against the West Indies in Guwahati. The India captain struck 26 fours and eight sixes as India chased down 406 in 43.3 overs, completing the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history.
The 223 not out was also the highest individual score in a successful ODI chase, while Gill reached his century in 62 balls. He had earlier scored 110 in the series opener in Thiruvananthapuram, taking his tally to two centuries in as many matches.
Abhishek returned to his explosive best during India’s T20I series against Afghanistan. The left-hander smashed 82 from 32 balls in the opening match before producing an extraordinary 108 from 45 deliveries in the third game.
His century came from just 30 balls, the fastest T20I hundred by a batter from a Full Member nation, according to the ICC. Abhishek finished the series with 229 runs at an average of 76.33 and was named Player of the Series.
Raza, meanwhile, underlined his value as an all-rounder during Zimbabwe’s ODI series against Australia. He scored 57 in the opening match, followed it with 45 in the second and remained unbeaten on 81 in the final game. He also took two wickets in the final ODI, including the dismissals of Josh Inglis and Oliver Peake.
The three nominees now await the outcome of the ICC award, with Gill’s record-breaking September, Abhishek’s explosive T20 displays and Raza’s consistency with bat and ball providing a compelling contest.
Women’s shortlist The ICC has also shortlisted India’s Shafali Verma and Sree Charani alongside Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu for the Women’s Player of the Month award for September, following a month of standout performances across the Asia Cup and Asian Games.
Verma was the leading run-scorer at the Women’s Asia Cup as India secured a record-extending eighth title. The explosive opener scored 360 runs in seven T20 internationals at an average of 72 and a strike rate of 184.61, while also taking six wickets.
Her form continued at the Asian Games in Japan, where she scored 188 runs in three innings, including a maiden T20I century against Bangladesh. She added 48 in the gold-medal match as India beat Sri Lanka by 147 runs. Athapaththu delivered an all-round performance, scoring 226 runs and taking 14 wickets in seven T20Is. Her highlight was a remarkable 7-5 against Indonesia, including a hat-trick, during the Asia Cup.
Charani was India’s leading wicket-taker, claiming 18 wickets at an average of 4.83. She also reached 817 rating points in the ICC T20I rankings, becoming the highest-rated women’s T20I bowler in history.
The winner will be decided through a vote, with the nominees recognised for their contributions to a memorable month of women’s cricket.

title: Milind leads USA in record chase against UAE
description: The right hander   s unbeaten 116 powers the hosts to achieve 331 run target with seven balls to spare
content:
The right-hander’s unbeaten 116 powers the hosts to achieve 331-run target with seven balls to spare
Experienced batsman Milind Kumar became the USA’s most prolific six-hitter in men’s ODI cricket as he inspired a record-breaking run chase against the United Arab Emirates in the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup League 2 match on Monday. Milind smashed an unbeaten 116 off just 84 balls at Grand Prairie Stadium, including five sixes, as the USA chased down 331 with seven deliveries to spare. The victory marked USA’s highest successful ODI chase, surpassing their previous best of 294-7 against Nepal in Dallas in 2024. Milind’s fifth ODI century also took him past former captain Monank Patel for the most sixes by a USA batter in the format. He and Shubham Ranjane, who finished unbeaten on 57, shared an unbroken 160-run partnership to complete the chase. The result moved USA to League 2 summit as they continue their bid to qualify for next year’s 50-over World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. The USA have already secured a place in the World Cup Qualifier through their strong League 2 campaign and need one more victory from their remaining matches in the current tri-series to guarantee top spot. The top four teams in the Qualifier will secure places at next year’s World Cup, giving the USA a chance to reach the tournament for the first time. The USA face Namibia in Dallas on Wednesday, while UAE meet Namibia on Friday.

title: French lawmaker calls on interior minister to resign over police response to student protests
description: Opposition politicians demand changes to policing strategy after 15 year old loses hand during demonstration
content:
Opposition politicians demand changes to policing strategy after 15-year-old loses hand during demonstration
French lawmaker Gabrielle Cathala called on Interior Minister Laurent Nunez to resign over police intervention against high school students, as criticism mounts over the government’s handling of nationwide student protests.
Cathala, a lawmaker from the left-wing France Unbowed (LFI), addressed Nunez in the National Assembly on Monday, citing students who had been maimed, lost an eye or suffered a broken jaw during the demonstrations.
Referring to Nunez’s announcement that 10 investigations had been launched into incidents during the protests, Cathala said: “Our issue is not opening investigations after these children’s lives have been ruined; our issue is preventing this violence.”
She called for a change in France’s policing doctrine toward de-escalation and said footage showed plainclothes officers breaking windows and police firing various projectiles at students.
“Mr. Minister, you must resign. You have nothing left to do here,” she told Nunez.
Read More: Student protests spread across France, Belgium
Her remarks came amid political outrage after a 15-year-old student lost a hand on Monday when a grenade used by riot police exploded during a demonstration near Auguste-Behal high school in Lens.
Bethune public prosecutor Etienne Thieffry said it had not yet been established whether the teenager picked up the grenade or whether it had been thrown at him. France’s police watchdog has opened an investigation.
Other opposition politicians have also criticised the police response.
LFI coordinator Manuel Bompard accused authorities of choosing to “repress our children rather than listen and engage in dialogue,” while Green politician Marine Tondelier called the failure to instruct police to exercise restraint a “serious political error.”
Socialist politician Olivier Faure urged the government to immediately review its crowd-control strategy.
Meanwhile, a petition launched on the National Assembly’s website calling for a ban on police use of weapons capable of causing serious injuries during high school protests has received more than 10,000 signatures.
Also Read: Teenager's hand blown off as French school protests enter third week
Nunez told broadcaster TF1 on Oct. 2 that he had not instructed law enforcement officers to exercise restraint during the demonstrations, prompting criticism from opposition politicians.

title: Robert Pattinson thriller  Primetime  banned in Malaysia by censorship board
description: Neither Antenna nor GSC provided details  while the censorship board has not publicly explained the ban
content:
Neither Antenna nor GSC provided details, while the censorship board has not publicly explained the ban
Robert Pattinson’s psychological thriller Primetime has been banned in Malaysia by the country’s Film Censorship Board (LPF), according to local distributor Antenna Entertainment.
Antenna announced the decision on October 6, confirming that the A24 film will no longer be released in Malaysian cinemas. The distributor apologised to local moviegoers and thanked them for their support and interest in Primetime .
“We regret to inform you that PRIMETIME will not be released in Malaysia,” Antenna said in a statement posted on X, adding that the film had been banned by the LPF.
Cinema chain Golden Screen Cinemas (GSC) also confirmed that the film’s Malaysian release had been cancelled, although its announcement did not specifically mention the censorship ban. Neither Antenna nor GSC provided details about the grounds for the LPF’s decision, while the censorship board has not publicly explained the ban.
The decision comes after Primetime ’s Malaysian release had already been postponed. Antenna and TGV Cinemas announced on September 19 that the film’s debut would be moved from October 1 to October 8, while teasing an unspecified development for October 2. The nature of that development was never confirmed.
Directed by Lance Oppenheim in his narrative feature debut, Primetime stars Pattinson as a fictionalised television host inspired by Chris Hansen, the presenter of NBC’s controversial reality programme To Catch a Predator . The cast also includes Merritt Wever, Skyler Gisondo and singer-songwriter Phoebe Bridgers.
The screenplay was inspired by a 2007 Esquire investigation into the behind-the-scenes production of To Catch a Predator . Primetime premiered in competition at the Venice International Film Festival on September 5 before opening in North American cinemas on September 25.
With the LPF’s decision, Malaysian audiences will not receive the planned October theatrical release of Pattinson’s latest film, and no new local release date has been announced.

title: Information ministry rejects Reuters report on Makkah defence pact as  speculative
description: Says the operational details are a matter of operational confidentiality  not be made subject of media speculation
content:
Urges against relying on 'highly speculative reports based on non-attributable and unknown sources'
Pakistan’s Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on Tuesday rejected what it described as “speculative” reporting by Reuters on the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, saying operational details concerning the implementation of the collective deterrence mechanism were confidential.
The ministry’s fact-check followed a Reuters report published on October 2 which said Pakistan had deployed between 30,000 and 40,000 troops to Saudi Arabia to help defend the kingdom’s land borders and assist with drone and missile interceptions, citing a Pakistani official. Reuters reported that Islamabad had not decided to send troops into Yemen in a fighting capacity.
In a statement issued today, the ministry reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to the security of Saudi Arabia and the Haramain Sharifain — Islam’s two holiest mosques in Makkah and Madina — describing that commitment as “non-negotiable”.
"Having taken note of speculative reports by Reuters on the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, it is reiterated that Pakistan has already made Pakistan’s commitment to the security of Haramain Sharifain and KSA abundantly clear, which is non-negotiable," said the statement.
𝐅𝐚𝐜𝐭 𝐂𝐡𝐞𝐜𝐤 | 𝐌𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 & 𝐁𝐫𝐨𝐚𝐝𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 ▪️Having taken note of speculative reports by Reuters on Makkah Joint Defense Agreement, it is reiterated that Pakistan has already made Pakistan’s commitment to security of Haramain… pic.twitter.com/8AYC3m7yuL
The ministry urged against relying on “highly speculative reports based on non-attributable and unknown sources”, saying Reuters should instead refer to official statements from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other authorities.
“Queries, if any, may be referred to them instead of coming out with invented numbers and details,” it said.
The ministry's fact-check came a day after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agreed to move immediately towards implementing their collective defence commitments and deploying agreed military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia. The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of the Strategic-Political and Defence Committee of the Makkah Alliance for Defence in Riyadh on October 5.
Under the decision, the committee directed the necessary measures to provide the agreed forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in Saudi Arabia, in accordance with approved arrangements and the national legislation of the three countries. It said the move would enhance “readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats”.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed MJDA, a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
Houthis have repeatedly carried out missile and drone attacks against Saudi Arabia since the Yemen war escalated in 2015, targeting military installations, airports, oil facilities and other critical infrastructure.
In September 2019 , the group claimed responsibility for drone attacks on Saudi Aramco’s Abqaiq processing facility and Khurais oil field, attacks that temporarily disrupted more than half of Saudi Arabia’s crude production.
The attacks continued in subsequent years, including strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure in March 2022.
More recently, Houthi attacks have again targeted Saudi territory. In September, the group claimed missile and drone strikes on a Saudi military base and other targets, while Saudi authorities reported attacks affecting several cities.
It is worth noting that on September 25 , Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye senior military leadership strongly condemned attacks targeting the holy city of Makkah as they reaffirmed their commitment to the collective defence of the Kingdom under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.
Read: Makkah defence alliance agrees to 'rapid force deployment' in Saudi Arabia: FO
A day after that, Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman reaffirmed continued joint efforts to confront attacks targeting Makkah and civilian and economic facilities in the Kingdom during a meeting with the Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir.
Then, on September 27, Defence Minister Asif also reiterated the resolve to implement the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement amid the rising Houthis attacks on Saudi Arabia and said that both Pakistan and Türkiye would stand with Saudi Arabia practically and diplomatically in case of any aggression.
Asif further stressed that protecting Saudi Arabia fell under divine duty.
"If there wasn't an agreement, if Saudi Arabia had been attacked, especially if the sacred cities of Makkah and Madinah were attacked, then we are bound by an eternal agreement; that is, we will protect the House of God and Madinah," he stated in an interview to a private channel.
He also outlined that the "worldly agreement" referring to the MJDA between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to protect one another, would operate in all circumstances.
Significance of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
The MJDA was the latest step in longstanding military and strategic cooperation between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. Signed in Makkah, the pact established a framework for collective deterrence and stipulated that an armed attack on any one of the three countries would be considered an attack on all three, while providing for wider cooperation across defence.
The agreement followed nearly a year of negotiations and came amid heightened instability across the Middle East. Turkiye and Pakistan had sought closer regional security cooperation, while Saudi Arabia had faced growing security concerns as conflicts spread across the region, threatening its territory, energy infrastructure and ambitious economic development plans.
For Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the trilateral pact is built on their Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed in September 2025. That agreement stated that “any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both” and committed the two sides to strengthening defence cooperation and joint deterrence.

title: Amber Heard runs 21K half marathon in San Sebasti  n  shares photos
description: Heard completed her first half marathon in Spain  finishing 21 kilometres in 1 hour and 39 minutes
content:
Heard completed her first half-marathon in Spain, finishing 21 kilometres in 1 hour and 39 minutes
Amber Heard has completed her first half-marathon in Spain, sharing her running achievement with followers alongside photographs from the event.
The 40-year-old actress posted images from the race on Instagram, revealing that she completed the 21-kilometre distance in one hour and 39 minutes.
Heard celebrated the milestone while wearing lilac sportswear that showed off her her defined physique.
"First half marathon, eskerrik asko Donosti!" she wrote, thanking San Sebastián by its Basque name. "21 kilometers in 1:39 min !!"
Images showed Heard smiling among fellow runners, wearing a finisher's medal and running along a wet road as spectators watched from beneath umbrellas.
She also shared a photograph from the finish line with her hands behind her head.
The achievement follows another running milestone earlier this year. In June, Heard took part in a 10K race in Madrid and captioned a photograph, "First race glow."
She also shared a picture with her eldest daughter, Oonagh, writing, "Nothing beats this feeling."
Heard has been living in Spain in recent years and is raising three children. She welcomed twins Agnes and Ocean in 2025, joining daughter Oonagh, whom she introduced publicly in 2021.
Alongside family life, Heard has continued acting.
In summer 2025, she made her professional stage debut in Jeremy O. Harris's Spirit of the People at the Williamstown Theatre Festival in Massachusetts.

title: James Gunn hits back at    Clayface    critics and defends the film   s creative direction
description: The comments come as  Clayface  faces online criticism and reported concerns about its box office prospects
content:
The comments come as 'Clayface' faces online criticism and reported concerns about its box-office prospects
James Gunn has responded to criticism of the upcoming Clayface film, questioning why audiences should only support projects based on familiar properties.
The DC Studios co-chairman addressed the backlash on Threads after a post questioned who wanted a Clayface movie.
Gunn replied, “Who tf asked for Back to the Future? Casablanca? There’s Something About Mary? Pan’s Labyrinth? Fury Road? Weapons? The Matrix?”
He continued, “Although it may seem like it, Hollywood isn’t a place where the only way to make a movie is the public voting on what IP they want to see that they’ve seen countless times before.”
Gunn also defended the creative team behind Clayface , which was developed from an idea by Mike Flanagan, with James Watkins directing and Hossein Amini involved in the screenplay.
“Sometimes someone – in this case initially Mike Flanagan and then James Watkins and Hossein Amini – were inspired by a relatively little known fictional character and crafted what I believe is a very special story around that character,” Gunn wrote.
“I’d take that inspiration a thousand times over some writer trying to make a buck by writing a listless screenplay about a majorly popular character he or she has no passion or feel for,” he added.
The comments come as Clayface faces online criticism and reported concerns about its box-office prospects. Boxoffice Pro projected an opening between $23 million and $33 million.
Starring Tom Rhys Harries as Matt Hagen, Clayface is scheduled to open in cinemas on October 23.

title: MoistCr1TiKaL collaborating with Jagex on RuneScape animated series
description: MoistCr1TiKaL is teaming up with Jagex and Lyrical Animation on animated series based on RuneScape
content:
MoistCr1TiKaL is teaming up with Jagex and Lyrical Animation on animated series based on RuneScape
YouTuber Charlie ‘MoistCr1TiKaL’ White is teaming up with Jagex and Lyrical Animation to develop an animated series based on RuneScape.
White’s Meatier Productions will produce the project alongside Lyrical Animation, bringing the fantasy world of Gielinor to animation.
The announcement was made by Jagex CEO Jon Bellamy at RuneFest in Birmingham, following the Old School RuneScape keynote.
“When we talk about the future of RuneScape, we don’t just mean games,” Bellamy said.
“We see huge potential to bring Gielinor to life in new ways, both for the millions who already know and love it and for a whole new audience. It’s early days, but we’re excited to explore that potential with Charlie and the team at Lyrical Animation, and we wanted our players to be the first to know.”
Development is still in its early stages, with further details expected in 2027. No streaming platform, voice cast or release date has been announced, meaning 2027 is currently the next expected update rather than a confirmed premiere window.
Daniel Dominguez, Creative Director of Lyrical Animation, also welcomed the project.
“Runescape has such a unique storytelling voice, at once laugh-out-loud funny and effortlessly insightful,” Dominguez said. “To be allowed to help bring that to life for its millions of fans alongside our dear friend Charlie again is a dream come true.”
The RuneScape series follows another animation project involving White, Jagex and Lyrical Animation. The companies are also working on an animated adaptation of White’s Godslap graphic novel, which is already in production and targeting a 2028 release. Lyrical Animation is also developing a Bloodborne adaptation with YouTuber Jacksepticeye.

title: End long march  sit ins and we will talk   PM Shehbaz once again extends olive branch to PTI
description: PM says that if the opposition calls off the march then the government is ready to sit and talk
content:
Says will not allow Pakistan's progress to be harmed, 'protecting people's lives is our duty and we will ensure it'
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday renewed an offer of talks to Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), saying the government was prepared to engage with the opposition if the party ended its long march and sit-ins.
“End your long march. If you end it, then we will certainly sit with you and talk. So that Pakistan moves forward with mutual courage, hard work, trust and meditation," PM Shehbaz said at the groundbreaking ceremony for the Kashmir Chowk Underpass in Islamabad.
The statement came amid heightened political tensions in the country as Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s (PTI) long march reached Kohat. Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi is leading the convoy, which began its march towards Islamabad on Sunday to demand the release of party founder Imran Khan and press the government over what PTI describes as broader political and constitutional grievances. The convoy is currently in Kohat after travelling through Lakki Marwat and Karak, and is expected to depart for Peshawar later today as the party continues its phased mobilisation towards the federal capital.
In his speech today, the prime minister said the government had decided to engage in dialogue after consultation and had held two days of talks between its representatives and the opposition in the chamber of National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq.
“There was a lot of discussion, and there was every hope that, God willing, these talks would reach their desired conclusion,” he said. “But unfortunately, that did not happen.”

The prime minister said that at the last moment, "they not only demanded changes to something that had already been prepared, but their only objective was that these talks should somehow not succeed."
“There is no doubt that the first target of this sit-in and long-march politics will be your economy. If your worker or engineer does not reach the factory, manufacturing site or office on time, whose loss is it? It is the loss of the nation and the country,” he said.
PM Shehbaz said the government had spent around a year and a half working to stabilise the economy.
“Pakistan’s economy has been brought back on its feet through collective efforts and teamwork over the last one and a half years. We have achieved macroeconomic stability, and now the time has come for growth and development,” he said.
He pointed to increases in September exports, IT exports, remittances and domestic production. “Today, Pakistan’s standing at the international level has improved, and even our adversaries are being forced to acknowledge it,” the prime minister said.
“Do you want to damage this? Do you want to harm Pakistan’s progress?”

The prime minister said the government would "not allow this to happen." He said that the law would take its course, and protecting the lives and property of the people is our responsibility.
"The lives of the people, the protection of the wealth, this is our responsibility. We will ensure it in every way. I will still tell them not to lose their senses," he said.
He said this was the aim of the government and the voice of every Pakistani.
The prime minister, earlier in his speech, praised Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and his team for planning to complete the Kashmir Chowk Underpass within a month.
Referring to the name of the project, PM Shehbaz expressed hope that the road would eventually extend towards Kashmir and Srinagar. “God willing, this road will one day reach Kashmir, reach Srinagar, and freedom and rights will be achieved,” he said.
The premier said the construction of roads, flyovers and underpasses helped children, students, cyclists, rickshaw drivers, workers and other citizens reach schools, universities, offices, factories and commercial areas on time.
“They work day and night and take the country’s economic and social development forward,” he said. “This entire process, praise be to God, is continuing through collective efforts,” he added.
Earlier, Naqvi said the Kashmir Chowk Underpass was part of preparations to transform Islamabad ahead of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) conference.
“The prime minister’s vision was that before the SCO conference, Islamabad had to be made a different Islamabad,” Naqvi said, noting that less than a year remained before the conference.

“For the conference, the prime minister is doing his meetings, but for us the most important thing is the beautification of Islamabad and the facilities for the delegates who will come,” he said.
Naqvi said that the underpass and the Islamabad Expressway were among the projects being undertaken as part of the plan.
“Once the underpass and the expressway are completed, the journey from Rawalpindi to Islamabad will be 16 to 18 minutes, which used to take around half an hour,” Naqvi said.
He said State Minister for Interior Talal Chaudhry was personally overseeing efforts to make Islamabad plastic-free and cashless.
On the plastic-free initiative, he said legislation had already been passed. "Implementation will be difficult, but I know Chaudhry will succeed,” he said.
"The target for the initiative was December 31," Naqvi said.
He added that Chaudhry was holding daily meetings on the cashless Islamabad project and that the government hoped to begin work on both initiatives before the end of the year.
“We need to take the lead as the federal government so that the rest of the country can follow,” Naqvi said.
Naqvi also outlined plans to expand Islamabad’s green spaces.
“We have started a project to make F-9 Park like Hyde Park,” he said. “We are also building a safari park on 450 acres, which will be the biggest safari park in Asia.”
Another park roughly the size of F-9 Park was also planned, he said.
Naqvi said Islamabad had seen little development work for 20 to 25 years while its population had tripled and that is why fixing the infrastructure was "the most important thing."

He hoped the development undertaken during the government’s tenure would serve Islamabad for decades.
The minister said the government was also working to digitise all land records in Islamabad, with December 31 set as the target.
Turning to the performance of elected representatives, Naqvi said the public would judge them by how they used their time. “The public wants to see whether their elected representatives are spending every minute for them or on negative politics,” he said.
“On one side, there is an elected representative who has not gone to the office and has not held a meeting for a month. On the other side, there is someone who does not give even an hour’s gap and continues working for the public,” he said.

title: Viral game Dressmaker was created to help developer   s wife reconnect with sewing after illness
description: Steam hit Dressmaker began as way for its creator   s wife to reconnect with sewing hobby after medical diagnosis
content:
Steam hit Dressmaker began as way for its creator’s wife to reconnect with sewing hobby after medical diagnosis
Steam hit Dressmaker began as a personal project designed to help co-creator Sabrina Becker reconnect with her hobby of dressmaking after a medical condition disrupted her plans to pursue costume design.
Released on September 21, the cosy crafting game allows players to run a dressmaking business, select fabrics, cut patterns, sew pieces together and decorate finished garments.
Developed by Cozy Lives and published by Free Lives, the game has since attracted attention from players sharing their virtual creations online.
Some players have created dresses inspired by artworks including the Mona Lisa and Vincent van Gogh’s The Starry Night. However, the project initially had a more personal purpose for Becker and her husband and co-creator, Jonathan Hau-Yoon.
Becker had been interested in sewing for years and even wore a dress she had made herself on her first date with Hau-Yoon. She had hoped to pursue costume design professionally, but her diagnosis of hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome affected those plans.
The condition affects connective tissue and can cause unusually flexible or unstable joints, joint pain and severe fatigue, with symptoms varying between individuals.
Hau-Yoon and Becker subsequently developed Dressmaker as a way to recreate the creative process of sewing digitally and allow Becker to continue engaging with her hobby.
Becker has also played an active role in the game's development. She designs and curates dress pieces, helps shape its aesthetics and provides feedback through playtesting, drawing on her experience with dressmaking.
The project began attracting attention before its full release. A TikTok video showing the game’s concept received around half a million views, while its free prototype reached 100,000 downloads within two months.

title: Rockstar researched GTA 6 with police officers and gang members in Florida
description: Rockstar Games developers travelled across Florida with police and gang members while researching GTA 6
content:
Rockstar Games developers travelled across Florida with police and gang members while researching GTA 6
Rockstar Games developers travelled across Florida with police officers and gang members while researching the locations and communities that inspired GTA 6’s fictional state of Leonida.
Rockstar head of development Aaron Garbut discussed the studio’s research process in an interview with Love Magazine ahead of GTA 6’s release.
He explained that development begins with research trips before gradually involving more members of the team.
A small group initially travelled from Miami through surrounding towns and the Florida Keys to Key West, recording locations and discussing how aspects of the region could be translated into the game.
As development progressed, Rockstar’s research became more extensive, with developers spending time with people from different communities across Florida.
“We do go in-depth, we hang with locals and we hear lots of stories and learn as much as we can,” Garbut said. “We travel around with cops and with gang members.”
Garbut said some of the people the team encountered could be “equally scary”, while the developers also heard stories and visited locations that showed them a darker side of the region.
“The people who showed us around were among the nicest we’ve met,” he added, “the stories, the places, the details could be terrifying.”
Rockstar’s research also included aerial trips through Florida. During one journey, members of the team flew low over mangrove inlets in the Everglades before eventually hovering above a stadium during a Beyoncé concert.
“I think we made the local news the next day,” Garbut recalled.
The studio used its research to build what Garbut described as a world that is “believable and varied, with depth”. Developers recorded smaller details that could influence pedestrian conversations, fictional radio shows and advertisements

title: Sebastian Maniscalco   s Comedy Radio drama explained  Comedians raise concerns over reduced exposure and income
description: Maniscalco   s SiriusXM comedy channel has sparked criticism from comedians over the comic line up change
content:
Maniscalco’s SiriusXM comedy channel has sparked criticism from comedians over the comic line-up change
Sebastian Maniscalco’s SiriusXM comedy channel has sparked criticism from comedians who say the rebrand has reduced opportunities and royalty income for lesser-known performers.
Maniscalco partnered with SiriusXM in April to launch Sebastian Maniscalco’s Comedy Radio, a channel described at the time as “a 24/7 comedy destination”.
The service includes podcasts such as The Sebastian Maniscalco Show and We Got Company , alongside stand-up programming curated and headlined by Maniscalco.
The channel replaced SiriusXM’s Raw Comedy, which comedians said had provided regular exposure and income for performers outside the biggest names in stand-up.
On October 5, comedians including Patton Oswalt, Michelle Wolf and Matthew Broussard criticised the programming changes on social media and called for Maniscalco to reconsider the direction of the channel.
According to figures from Stand Up for Standup, the number of comedians on the channel’s “active roster” fell from 812 in April to 275 in September, a reduction of roughly 66%.
The report also stated that approximately 75% of plays are concentrated among the top 50 performers.
Among the comedians now receiving the most plays are Jim Gaffigan, Kevin Hart and Ricky Gervais.
SiriusXM told Vulture , “SiriusXM works together with our creative partners to program the best possible experience for our listeners.”
The company added, “The launch of Sebastian Maniscalco’s Comedy Radio introduced a new creative direction and a regularly evolving programming mix for the channel.”

title: PSX rallies 2 593 points on easing political concerns
description: PM   s call for dialogue with PTI lifts sentiment as broad based buying returns
content:
PM’s call for dialogue with PTI lifts sentiment as broad-based buying returns
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) staged a strong recovery on Tuesday, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index surging 2,592.79 points, or 1.56%, to settle at 168,460.11, as broad-based buying gathered pace amid hopes of reduced domestic political tensions.
Investor sentiment improved after Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called on the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) to abandon its agitational politics and cancel its long march, saying protests would damage economic growth and Pakistan’s international standing. The call for dialogue, conditional on ending the agitation, provided some relief to investors concerned about renewed political uncertainty.
The Index traded between an intraday high of 168,626.18 and a low of 165,651.68, recovering strongly from the session’s early levels as buying emerged across key sectors.
Buying interest was witnessed in automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, oil and gas exploration companies, oil marketing companies, power generation and refineries.
Meanwhile, international oil prices also eased on Tuesday as resilient Middle Eastern crude exports and a G7 emergency stockpile release reduced immediate supply concerns, although security risks in the region continued to cap further declines.
“The decline in international oil prices, along with the government’s indication that it remains open to negotiations with the PTI to end the long march, has helped improve investor sentiment,” AKD Securities Director Research Mohammed Awais Ashraf told the The Express Tribune . The easing of both external and domestic concerns has encouraged fresh buying across key sectors and supported the broader market recovery, he added.
After yesterday’s heavy sell-off and margin-driven liquidation, the market initially remained subdued and consolidated on thin volumes, but improving domestic and global cues triggered broad-based buying and a strong recovery, mentioned Ahmed Sheraz of KASB KTrade in its market wrap.
Buying was visible across commercial banks, Oil &Gas, cement, investment banks and power, with Engro Holdings, UBL, Hub Power, HBL, Oil & Gas Development Company, and Mari Energies closing the session in the green.
Sentiment was further supported by easing oil prices, with Brent falling below $100 to around $98, amid improving Red Sea conditions, G7-backed strategic oil releases and price support from Saudi producers. Additionally, hopes of US-Iran dialogue also reduced geopolitical risk after President Trump indicated Washington was open to direct talks.
On the domestic front, the government’s outreach to the opposition for negotiations added another layer of clarity, helping the market regain confidence. Going forward, the recovery could extend if geopolitical tensions, oil prices and domestic political noise remain contained, although some consolidation after today’s sharp rebound would be healthy, Sheraz predicted.
Trading volume, however, eased to 432 million shares from 441.8 million recorded on Monday, while the value of traded shares stood at Rs20.1 billion. Shares of 496 companies were traded in the ready market, with 314 closing higher, 147 lower and 35 unchanged.
Cnergyico PK remained the volume leader, with 55.1 million shares changing hands. The stock gained Rs0.72 to close at Rs12.93.

title: Four FBR officials  traffic police officer killed in DI Khan firing
description: Two terrorists were killed in an exchange of fire in Bannu  while three people reportedly abducted in Tank
content:
Two terrorists were killed in an exchange of fire in Bannu, while three people reportedly abducted in Tank
Five people, including four Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) officials and a traffic police officer, were killed in separate firing incidents in Dera Ismail Khan (DIK) on Tuesday, District Police Officer (DPO) Ziauddin said.
The firing took place at Bhatti Pump on University Road, within the jurisdiction of University Police Station, at around 11:40am. Rescue 1122 media coordinator said its control room received information about the firing at Bhatti Pump and immediately dispatched emergency teams to the scene.
The rescue teams recovered the bodies of four people killed in the incident and began shifting them to DHQ Hospital, the coordinator said.
"In a separate incident, a highway patrol mobile came under fire at Gulistan Chowk on the DIK bypass, killing its driver and injuring two others," DPO Ziauddin said.
The deceased driver was identified as Habib, and the mobile in-charge, Subhan, and another constable were injured in the attack. The injured and the deceased were being shifted to the trauma centre, police said.
Following the incident. three officials were suspended, with Dera Ismail Khan Regional Police Officer (RPO) Syed Ashfaq Anwar directing them to report to the police lines. The suspended officials were Sub-Inspectors Ghulam Qasim and Ismatullah and FC official Asghar Ali, while charge sheets would also be issued against all three.
Separately in Bannu, two terrorists were killed in an exchange of fire with police in Feroz Fateh Khel, within the jurisdiction of Mandan Police Station. Police identified the two deceased as Sher Ayaz Khan and Adnan, police confirmed. Their bodies were shifted to the District Headquarters Hospital for post-mortem examinations and legal formalities.
Elsewhere, three people working at basic health units (BHUs) under the Aga Khan NGO were reportedly abducted from Grah Mitho in Tank, according to DPO Tank Abdul Samad. The abductees were identified as Saeed Anwar, Safiullah and Syed Basha.
In South Waziristan's Khasokhel, unidentified individuals targeted the main gate of Prime Minister’s committee member Maulana Misbahullah’s house with explosives at around midnight, damaging the gate. No casualties were reported.
In another incident in Upper Kurram, terrorists fired an RPG-7 round at a house in Dal, within the jurisdiction of Agra Police Station, at around 3:30am. The attack damaged the house’s door, but caused no casualties, DPO Kurram Malik Habib.
Meanwhile, mobile phone services began to be restored in Dera Ismail Khan after three days.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed concern over the recent incidents of terrorism in DI Khan and conveyed his condolences over the martyrdom of four Customs officials and one traffic police official. “The recent incidents of terrorism in Dera Ismail Khan are a matter of concern,” he said.
The prime minister expressed deep grief and sorrow over the martyrdom of four Customs officials and one traffic police official in a firing by terrorists. “We stand with the bereaved families in this hour of grief,” he added.
The prime minister said operations by law enforcement agencies against terrorist elements would continue with full force until terrorism was completely eliminated.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, in a statement, strongly condemned the firing incidents targeting officials in DI Khan and expressed grief over the deaths. He extended his condolences to their families, saying the government stood with them in their hour of grief.
Naqvi said Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa was the province worst affected by terrorism and that “such cowardly attacks cannot weaken the nation’s firm resolve to fight terrorism”.

title: PM ordered maximum political space for PTI in return for full counterterror cooperation  Talal
description: We value security  elimination of terrorism  even if opposition gains political mileage   says quoting premier
content:
'We value security, elimination of terrorism, even if opposition gains political mileage,' says quoting premier
Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry said on Tuesday that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed federal ministers to "give as much political space as can be given" to the opposition, ensuring at the same time that the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) government and the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) agreed to fully cooperate on anti-terrorism.
Speaking during a press conference in Islamabad, Chaudhry said that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi went to Lahore late at night to meet the PM Shehbaz and told him that the K-P government and the PTI had come to an agreement on terrorism.
"The prime minister said that the political space, as much as can be given, should be given," Chaudhry said, quoting PM Shehbaz as telling Naqvi, "We value Pakistan's security, the elimination of terrorism; even if the opposition is given political mileage, the political capital for parties comes and goes."
Chaudhry said PM Shehbaz gave the interior minister an example, recalling that when the country was defaulting, "we were presented with extremely difficult measures, due to which our party's political capital [and] popularity was impacted, but Pakistan was saved from defaulting."
According to Chaudhry, PM Shehbaz also said, "If terrorism is finished from Pakistan and some other party is given the political space, I am not hesitant." The prime minister added, the minister said that "as much political space as they can be given, give it to them but in any case, they should agree fully and 100% to cooperate."
Chaudhry said the meeting between Naqvi and PM Shehbaz followed the first day of talks that had left political discussions between the government and opposition moving forward.
On that day, he said, the interior minister put the government's point of view before the opposition, relating to terrorism and the K-P government's cooperation in the National Action Plan.
"The K-P government's "lack of interest over the past few years, and the promises it made regarding the forces, the budget or other reasons from which it backed off, were all placed in front of the opposition," Chaudhry said

As the talks progressed, however, Chaudhry said, the basic structure of the agreement was almost agreed to, which included political points and those regarding terrorism. It was also agreed to hold a second day of talks.
He said the interior minister had called the opposition leaders the night before the talks began and told them to bring one representative from the K-P government, "or else try to ensure that the K-P CM is also present during the talks."

When the talks started, Chaudhry said, the opposition leaders announced with clarity that they retained complete authority and that the K-P government, along with the entire party, had given them authority. "Whatever they discussed, they said, would be verified by the K-P government and the party," Chaudhry stated.
He added that the point about having a representative was insisted upon again but the government was again reassured that the opposition leaders were in constant communication with the K-P government and party.
Further, Chaudhry said that after the first day of talks, some opposition members went to Peshawar, where they met the K-P chief minister, senior leaders and ministers.
"They took assurance once more regarding terrorism, on the points that the interior minister later tweeted on behalf of the federal government," the minister said. After contact that night, he added, "they again assured us that on matters related to terrorism, there was 100% agreement on the points by the federal government and this would be carried forward."
Chaudhry said that when the second day of talks started, agreement had already been reached on terrorism. "If anyone contradicts this, certainly our opposition leaders are in a fix," he said. "If they say the truthful thing, their own people run to bite them."
On the second day, Chaudhry said, the first draft, which contained all the political matters, was disagreed upon. "Their founder's health, their meetings, members' cases, countless things," he said.
"I used to think that a second Charter of Democracy was beginning," Chaudhry said, adding that "a big breakthrough had happened." In the entire agreement, he said, "for us what was a win was that in Pakistan, to end terrorism, we had successfully come to a consensus with PTI, and for us, this win was enough."
Then, Chaudhry said, at the final hour of the talks, the opposition sat in a separate room for some time and continued contact with the K-P chief minister. "Then they came out, they weren't able to meet eyes with us and they wanted permission to leave," he said.
Further, Chaudhry said he had a few questions, noting that the K-P chief minister said they would not allow any plan against Pakhtuns or K-P. "The National Action Plan (NAP) made by their founder was that against the Pakhtuns? Was it against K-P? That they themselves were implementing?" he asked. "Was the NAP 2 not made by your leader?"

He then asked about areas "where one's wedding is not safe, one's death or grief is not safe, where any party or protest or rally, even a coroner's meeting, is conducted under fear and threat that their leader or convoy will be attacked." "Tell me this, after 2015, on record, in 11 years not one of your provincial or national leaders was attacked by the TTP [Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan] or any other party in K-P or anywhere in Pakistan?" Chaudhry questioned. He argued further that in the same period, "there is not one political party whose members have not been martyred or injured or attacked in funerals, wedding houses."
"Journalists, government employees, no civil society member is safe," the minister said.

Chaudhry further said that despite the security conditions in the province, the K-P government "won't allow the use of drones." He added, "If a quadcopter attack is carried out on security forces, drones can come from Afghanistan, terrorists can fly those drones, and they can drop them on our security forces but you want to leave our security forces defenceless so that they can't use drones?"
"You deliberately want our security forces to appear weak, so that they don't use those arms that are the most effective?" he asked.

Simu Liu and Allison Hsu are married after nearly four years together, with the couple tying the knot in France over the weekend of October 3.
The Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings star, 37, and Hsu, 30, married nearly four years after they were first romantically linked in 2022.

Liu proposed with the Eiffel Tower and a candlelit floral display in the background.
Hsu captioned the engagement announcement, “Us forever 💍💍💍🤍🤍🤍”.
Liu later wrote, “From weekends in Paris, day trips to Palm Springs, long nights on set, afternoons vegging on the couch and everything in between, I choose you forever and always.”
Speaking to People in 2023, Liu said, “She’s absolutely changed my life, so I’m very, very grateful to have her.”
He also described their relationship as one in which he felt “challenged and loved and cared for”.
In November 2025, Liu told Entertainment Tonight that he had “gone full creative director” for the proposal.
The couple’s wedding follows months of planning. Liu previously said the process had been “relatively pain-free and joyous”, with “good music” among their priorities.

title: DI Khan  Bannu postpone SSC papers amid mobile  internet suspension
description: Board says the postponed papers will be rescheduled  with a revised timetable to be announced separately
content:
Board says the postponed papers will be rescheduled, with a revised timetable to be announced separately
The Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE) in Bannu and Dera Ismail Khan have postponed the SSC Annual-II examination papers scheduled for October 7, 8, 9, and 10, according to the notifications issued by the boards.
BISE Bannu said the papers were postponed due to the prevailing security situation and the suspension of mobile and internet services, while BISE DI Khan said its SSC Annual-II Examination 2026 would now formally begin on October 12.
According to the notification issued by the BISE Bannu chairman on October 3, mobile and internet services had been suspended within the jurisdiction of BISE Bannu “due to the prevailing security situation in the area”.
The suspension of mobile and internet services was likely to cause “serious inconvenience to the parents, students, teachers and the Board administration”, particularly in the timely receipt and dissemination of roll numbers, duty letters and other examination-related communications, as well as in the dispatch of examination stationery to the respective examination centres, the notification said.
The prevailing circumstances may “adversely affect the smooth and transparent conduct of the scheduled examination,” it further added.
The chairman of BISE Bannu, being the competent authority, postponed the papers of the SSC Annual-II / Oriental Languages Examination, 2026, scheduled to be held on October 7, 8, 9 and 10. The notification said the schedule of all remaining papers would remain unchanged and they would be conducted strictly as per the already notified date sheet.
“The postponed papers shall be rescheduled subsequently, and a revised schedule thereof shall be notified separately by the Board,” it said.
All concerned were directed to take note of the decision and ensure its immediate dissemination among candidates, heads of institutions, supervisory staff and other stakeholders within their respective jurisdictions.
BISE DI Khan reschedules start of SSC Annual-II examinations
The BISE Dera Ismail Khan has postponed papers of the SSC Annual-II Examination 2026 scheduled for October 7, 8, 9 and 10, with the examination now set to formally begin on October 12, according to a press release issued by the board.
The SSC Annual-II Examination 2026, which was scheduled to begin on October 7 under the previously issued date sheet, would now formally commence on October 12, the statement added.
The statement further said that the Class 10 Physics paper scheduled for October 12 will be held at its scheduled time, while examinations will continue until October 27 in accordance with the issued date sheet. The board said papers scheduled for October 7, 8, 9 and 10 had been postponed.
New dates for the postponed papers would be announced later through a separate notification or press release, it added.
The board directed superintendents, deputy superintendents and relevant examination staff at all examination centres to ensure their presence at their respective examination centres and banks on October 9 for “Preparation Day”.
Students were directed to ensure their presence for their respective papers at the scheduled time from October 12 in accordance with the previously issued date sheet. BISE DI Khan also appealed to students, parents, heads of institutions, and examination staff not to pay attention to any unverified information or rumours regarding the examinations and to follow only information issued through the board’s official sources.

Kelker-Kelly died on Saturday, October 3, 2026, although news of his death was not made public until Monday. The cause of death has not been disclosed.
The actor was reportedly found unconscious at his home and emergency responders attempted to revive him but were unsuccessful. There were reportedly no signs of suspicious circumstances.
Some later reports suggested Kelker-Kelly may have experienced chest pain before losing consciousness and that emergency responders were called to a possible cardiac arrest.
However, this has not been confirmed by his family or representatives.
Several celebrity finance websites have estimated Robert Kelker-Kelly’s net worth at around $10 million, although the figure has not been independently confirmed.
His income came primarily from his television career, while he also worked as a professional pilot and flight instructor.
Born on April 18, 1964, in Wichita, Kansas, Kelker-Kelly began his television career in 1987 as Sam Fowler on Another World .
In 1992, he took over the role of Bo Brady on Days of Our Lives , remaining with the series until 1995.
He later appeared on General Hospital as Stavros Cassadine and continued working in television. His daytime career earned him a Soap Opera Digest Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in 1994.
Kelker-Kelly also appeared in productions including Night Sins , Touched by an Angel , Dream for an Insomniac and Rescue 77 .

title: Australian opposition party vows  biggest cut to immigration  in country s history
description: Plans to slash temporary  humanitarian visas  prioritise skilled workers amid growing anti immigration sentiment
content:
Plans to slash temporary, humanitarian visas, prioritise skilled workers amid growing anti-immigration sentiment
Australia's conservative opposition coalition has proposed to slash temporary and humanitarian visas while prioritising skilled workers in what it called the "biggest cut to immigration" in the nation's history.
The Liberal-National Coalition's migration policy would cut temporary visas by 650,000 over four years and bring annual net overseas migration down to 100,000 for two years, around one-third of its current rate.
The sweeping proposal comes amid growing anti-immigration sentiment in Australia due to high living costs and housing shortages.
The Coalition has come under pressure from the far-right, anti-immigration One Nation party, which has outpolled it in recent surveys and pledged to cut temporary migration by 750,000 over three years.
Read: Supreme Court to weigh Trump's mandatory immigration detention policy
"What we are proposing today is the biggest cut to immigration in the history of this country," Opposition Leader Angus Taylor told a press conference on Tuesday. "It will be putting Australia first and it will be putting our national interest first."
"The net overseas migration numbers will be 100,000 year one, 100,000 year two, going to 160,000 in year four. That will take pressure off roads, off schools, off infrastructure, off houses, and that will ensure that our country has the breathing space it needs."
Under the Coalition's plan, humanitarian visa places would be reduced by half to 10,000. It would cut international student enrollment to 240,000 while abolishing Australia's temporary graduate visa programme that allows students to live, study and work in the country after graduation.
The Coalition also pledged to increase temporary skilled visas by 100,000 and to clear a backlog of construction worker visa applications. "We've also seen under Labor a shift away from skilled migration to mass migration. We will reverse that shift," Taylor added.
Read More: Supreme Court lets Trump resume deporting migrants to countries not their own
The plan goes further than the cuts proposed by the centre-left Labor government last month, which aim to bring annual net migration down to 225,000 by 2028.
Migration surged after Australia reopened its borders in ⁠February 2022 ​following nearly two years of COVID-19 closures, driven largely by international students, backpackers and temporary ​workers.
However, numbers have been declining over the past two years. Net overseas migration stood at 306,000 in the year to June 30, 2025.
Australia's next general election is not due until 2028.

title: Saudi Arabia says 3 injured in attacks on 2 airports in country   s south amid escalation with Houthis
description: Yemen and Saudi against Houthis conflict
content:
Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed depot housing 20 ballistic missiles in northwestern Yemen
Saudi Arabia said on Tuesday that three people were injured in attacks that targeted two airports in the country’s south a day earlier, causing material damage.
In a statement, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said attackers targeted facilities at King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Jazan and Najran International Airport.
Emergency teams and relevant authorities responded immediately in accordance with approved procedures, it said.
The attacks left three people with minor injuries, who were taken to hospital for medical treatment, while material damage was also reported.
The aviation authority said it was working with relevant security agencies to assess the damage and take necessary measures to ensure the safety of passengers, employees, and the kingdom’s civil aviation system.
The statement did not identify who carried out the attacks.
Separately, an explosion was heard in the Saudi capital Riyadh, residents told AFP on Tuesday, with the blast echoing in the northern parts of the city.
Yemen’s Houthis, however, said earlier on Monday that they had carried out a series of missile and drone attacks across Saudi Arabia, including against what they described as “sensitive sites” in Jazan and Najran.
The group also claimed attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Abha Airport, an Aramco refinery in Rabigh and military sites.
Saudi Arabia on Monday condemned Houthi attacks targeting civilian and economic facilities across the kingdom, accusing the group of pursuing military escalation.
Jordan, Gulf bloc condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi civilian infrastructure
Jordan and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) on Tuesday condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes targeting two airports in the country’s south.
Jordanian Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi spoke by phone with his Saudi counterpart Prince Faisal bin Farhan and expressed Jordan’s “absolute solidarity” with Saudi Arabia in the face of Houthi attacks, the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
Safadi said Amman supports all measures taken by Riyadh to protect its security, stability, sovereignty and citizens.
He reiterated Jordan’s condemnation of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including attempts to target the Muslim holy cities of Mecca and Medina and continued attacks on civilian and economic facilities.
Safadi also reaffirmed Jordan’s support for Yemen’s internationally recognised government and efforts to resolve the conflict “in a way that restores security and stability and preserves the country’s unity and sovereignty,” the ministry said.
The two ministers also discussed regional developments and efforts to end the ongoing escalation in the region.
Separately, GCC Secretary-General Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi strongly condemned the attacks targeting King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Jazan and Najran International Airport in southern Saudi Arabia.
Albudaiwi said attacks on Houthi airports and civilian facilities represented a “dangerous escalation” and posed a “direct threat” to civilians and air navigation.
He expressed the GCC states’ full support for Saudi Arabia and measures taken by the kingdom to protect its security, stability and territory.
Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed depot housing 20 ballistic missiles in northwestern Yemen
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said early on Tuesday that its forces destroyed a depot housing 20 ballistic missiles at a mountainous site in northwestern Saada province along with a ballistic missile launch site in the capital Sanaa.
Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki announced the strikes in remarks carried by the Saudi Press Agency ( SPA ).
On Monday, the coalition said it carried out a military operation against Houthi targets in Yemen’s western Hodeidah province on the Red Sea coast.
Al-Maliki said the operation destroyed weapons depots, storage sites for explosive-laden boats and naval mines.
Read: Houthis pushed back from Bab el-Mandeb
He also said that coalition forces thwarted preparations for imminent attacks targeting waterways in the southern Red Sea.
Yemen has been mired in conflict since the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa and several provinces in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.
A 2022 UN-brokered truce collapsed in July, and fighting has since escalated.
Houthis claim attacks on Saudi airports, state oil refinery, military sites
Yemen’s Houthi group claimed Monday evening that it had carried out three military operations targeting two airports, an oil facility and military sites across Saudi Arabia.
In a statement on the US social media platform X, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the operations involved a large number of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones.

Saree said the first operation targeted King Khalid International Airport in the capital Riyadh, claiming it hit its target and disrupted air traffic.
The second targeted a refinery of state oil company Aramco in Rabigh, in the Makkah region, he said, claiming the attack caused a fire at the facility.
According to the statement, the third operation targeted Abha Airport, the Khamis Mushait base, and Akfa camp in the southern Asir region, along with what Saree described as other “sensitive sites” in Najran and Jazan in southwestern Saudi Arabia.
Saree claimed the operations were in response to 60 Saudi airstrikes and missile attacks over the preceding 24 hours targeting Sanaa and the Yemeni provinces of Al-Jawf, Taiz, Hajjah, Saada, and Marib.
He put the total number of airstrikes and missile attacks since the escalation began at 1,576.
Saree also warned international airlines using Saudi airspace against continuing their flights, saying it was now within the group’s area of operations, except for the airspace over Makkah and Medina.
There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities on the Houthi claims
US Navy helicopter declares emergency over Red Sea near Saudi Arabia
A US Navy helicopter declared an emergency while flying over the Red Sea near Saudi Arabia on Monday before disappearing from publicly available flight-tracking data.
The Sikorsky MH-60R Seahawk, operating under the call sign VVHR512, declared an emergency at approximately 5:20pm ET (2:20am PKT on Tuesday) while flying near Yanbu, a city on Saudi Arabia's western coast.
The helicopter was shown at an altitude of roughly 475 feet when the emergency was declared. Its displayed altitude subsequently dropped to zero before the aircraft disappeared from the tracking service.
The US Navy had not publicly confirmed the incident or provided information about the helicopter's crew or condition as of Monday evening.
The reason for the emergency was also not immediately known.
Some reports circulating on social media suggested the helicopter may have crashed, but there was no official confirmation of a crash.

title: Punjab imposes Section 144 for 10 days amid security threats
description: Says province faces  serious and imminent threat  from militant terrorist groups and hostile agencies
content:
Says province faces 'serious and imminent threat' from terrorist groups and hostile agencies
The Punjab government imposed Section 144 across the province for 10 days on Tuesday, banning gatherings of five or more people amid what it called a “serious and imminent threat” to public peace and the safety of life and property.
The decision came a day after Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s (PTI) long march reached Kohat. Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi is leading the convoy, which began its march towards Islamabad on Sunday to demand the release of party founder Imran Khan and press the government over what PTI describes as broader political and constitutional grievances. The convoy is currently in Kohat after travelling through Lakki Marwat and Karak, and is expected to depart for Peshawar later today as the party continues its phased mobilisation towards the federal capital.
According to the notification, the restrictions were imposed under Section 144(6) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, through an order issued by the Punjab Home Department.
The order said, “Credible reports from LEAs and IAs indicate a serious and imminent threat to public peace, tranquillity, and the safety of life & property across the province of Punjab by militant/terrorist organisations and Hostile Intelligence Agencies (HIAs).”
It said multiple threat alerts had been received about possible terrorist activities involving suicide bombers, vehicle-borne improvised explosive devices (VBIEDs) and target killings during large public gatherings across Punjab.
Such attacks could be used “to create mayhem, social unrest and disrupt public peace & tranquillity”, the order said.
It said assemblies, rallies, gatherings, sit-ins, processions, demonstrations and jalsas could present “potential targets for such terrorist attacks”, adding that the possibility of an act of terrorism during such activities could not be ruled out.
The order also said there was a “strong apprehension” that certain elements could organise activities, gatherings or demonstrations that might lead to assemblies of people and provide “easy targets for any hostile activity”.
“Such an incident could be a breach of public peace, disturbance of the public order, a security risk for the general public and could result in loss of life, property and critical infrastructure,” it said.
The inspector general of Punjab police, counter-terrorism department, special branch and several divisional and district administrations had requested “immediate preventive measures” to address potential terrorism and hostile activities, the order said.
Under the restrictions, a complete ban was imposed on assemblies, processions and gatherings of five or more people in any public place, street, road, highway, motorway or open space.
Read: CM Afridi urges PTI workers to join long march as convoy enters Kohat
The ban did not apply to marriage ceremonies, funeral prayers, burial gatherings or prayers in mosques, churches and other places of worship.
Official duties of government and semi-government organisations, courts and other events duly permitted by the relevant deputy commissioner were also exempted. The order also prohibited inciting people to participate in unlawful assemblies.
A separate ban was imposed on the carrying, display or brandishing of all kinds of weapons in public places. Personnel of law enforcement, intelligence and security agencies performing official duties were exempted.
The order said the restrictions would remain in force for 10 days from October 6 unless they were modified or withdrawn earlier.
The Punjab government said the measures were intended to enable authorities to “effectively maintain law & order throughout the province”.
The Punjab government had last imposed Section 144 across the province on September 23 for 13 days, until October 5, banning gatherings of five or more people amid security threats. At the time, the provincial government had also sought Pakistan Rangers’ deployment in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali and requested the federal government to downgrade mobile and internet services at selected locations in Rawalpindi and Attock for law and order purposes.
