title: US judge blocks Trump policy of fining migrants up to  1 8 million
description: Over 103 000 fines issued to migrants amounting to  84b since Trump returned to White House last year
content:
Over 103,000 fines issued to migrants amounting to $84b since Trump returned to White House last year
A federal judge on Monday blocked efforts by the Trump administration to impose fines of up to $1.8 million on migrants who fail to leave the United States after receiving final deportation orders.
US District Judge George O'Toole in Boston issued the ruling in a class-action lawsuit filed last year by two of the thousands of migrants who have been assessed civil penalties by the Department of Homeland Security.
He said the administration imposed the fines unlawfully. Halting the penalty-related policies was necessary, O'Toole said, because collecting the fines would likely drive the plaintiffs into insolvency. "The plaintiffs live in an economically precarious position even without the imposition of the government’s exorbitant fines," he wrote.
Read: Supreme Court to weigh Trump's mandatory immigration detention policy
As recently as July, the department said it had issued more than 103,000 fines to migrants amounting to about $84 billion in total since President Donald Trump returned to the White House last year.
While Congress authorised civil penalties under the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996, no administration sought to impose them until Trump's first term.
Starting last year, Trump's second administration began levying fines of $998 per day for migrants who failed to leave the US after a deportation order. Those fines have been imposed retroactively for up to five years, for a maximum penalty of $1.8 million.
In July 2025, DHS and the US Department of Justice implemented a new process they said would streamline the assessment of fines by eliminating a 30-day notice period and shortening the process for challenging penalties.
Read More: Supreme Court lets Trump resume deporting migrants to countries not their own
The plaintiffs, who also included the Immigrant Legal Resource Centre, challenged that policy as well as what they described as a practice by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement , a DHS agency, of issuing fines using boilerplate forms without independently assessing whether someone's failure to depart was "willful" or "voluntary."
O'Toole, an appointee of Democratic President Bill Clinton, sided with the plaintiffs, holding that the fines were unlawful and violated the Administrative Procedure Act because the forms lacked specific allegations explaining why an individual's conduct warranted a penalty.
He also found the administration had failed to comply with rulemaking processes in adopting its streamlined fine-imposition process because it did not provide the public a chance to comment on the policy change first.

Protestors seeking the resignation of the election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists
Police in the Indian capital, New Delhi, detained opposition lawmakers, including Rahul Gandhi and his sister Priyanka, as they tried to breach barricades during a protest demanding the resignation of the country's chief election commissioner on Tuesday, television channels said.
Dozens of Indian opposition lawmakers began a march seeking the resignation of the election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists, as hundreds of security personnel kept vigil in the heart of the Indian capital and barricades were thrown up.
Parties opposing Prime Minister Narendra Modi and members of the popular 'cockroach' youth movement launched protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar — appointed by Modi's government — after the I ndian Express newspaper reported divisions in the poll body last month.
The protests mark a fresh political challenge to Modi, midway into his third term in office and just months after similar protests forced the resignation of his education minister over exam paper leaks.
Read More: India's Modi turns to Instagram to woo young voters after Gen Z protest
The reported differences over the lists and voter registration procedures stoked concern about the commission's neutrality.
Holding a large banner that said "Save Democracy", lawmakers raised slogans against Modi and demanded that Kumar resign as they marched from parliament to the Election Commission of India headquarters in central Delhi.
"The Election Commission is a puppet in the hands of the government. We are fighting to save our democracy," Mallikarjun Kharge, president of the main opposition Congress party, told reporters as the march began.
Hundreds of security personnel, including paramilitaries in fatigues, fanned out in the area, with barricades thrown up and several routes closed.
Television showed security personnel, some holding batons, outside the barricaded Election Commission office.
Congress and other parties allege that the revised voter lists benefit Modi and his party. Kumar has not commented on the issue, but the commission and Modi's BJP denied the accusations.
Authorities advised against travel around planned protest areas and shut off some routes.
Tuesday's event is the latest of a series of almost daily demonstrations by student organisations, political parties and the 'cockroach' movement, which began last week.
India's Supreme Court agreed a day earlier to hear legal arguments seeking its intervention in the accusations against the poll body's voter drive and the conduct of its chief.
If "there are decisions against the law ... We will take care of it," the court said at the hearing, after the petitioners alleged bias by the poll body.

title: Trump orders firing squad for gunman who killed 13 people at Fort Hood  Texas
description: Sentence against former US Army psychiatrist Nidal Hasan would bring first military execution since 1961
content:
Sentence against former US Army psychiatrist Nidal Hasan would bring first military execution since 1961
President Donald Trump has ordered the use of a firing squad to execute the former United States Army psychiatrist who killed 13 people at Fort Hood, Texas, in a 2009 shooting spree the gunman later described as retaliation for US wars in the Muslim world, the Pentagon said on Monday.
Putting former US Army Major Nidal Hasan to death by Army firing squad was approved by Trump at the recommendation of Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said on X.
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has recommended — and President Donald J. Trump has approved — death by U.S. Army firing squad for convicted terrorist Nidal Malik Hasan, the jihadist who opened fire on unarmed American soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009. He killed 13 people and wounded…
Parnell noted that Hasan shouted "Allahu Akbar" — God is greatest in Arabic — during the attack, which killed 12 unarmed active-duty soldiers and a retired serviceman, and wounded 32 others. The Secretary of the Army will set the time and place of the execution, Parnell said, adding, "Judgment day for Hasan has finally come."
Death by firing squad was one of several forms of capital punishment the Trump administration recently added to permissible forms of execution for the gravest of federal crimes, along with electrocution and gas asphyxiation.
The number of federal execution options was expanded in part because of increasing difficulties in obtaining drugs for lethal injections, which have also proved challenging to carry out for other reasons at times.
Plans by the state of Tennessee to execute a woman for the first time in more than 200 years went awry last week when prison personnel botched an attempt to administer a lethal injection, leaving the death-row inmate, Christa Pike, alive but unconscious and hospitalised on life support .
Pike's lawyers had previously urged that the Tennessee Department of Correction to consider an alternative to lethal injection, such as hanging or firing squad, in anticipation of the trouble executioners faced in establishing a sound intravenous line.
A military jury sentenced Hasan to death in August 2013, after finding him guilty of 45 counts of premeditated murder and attempted premeditated murder for opening fire with a laser-sighted handgun in a medical facility at the sprawling central Texas military base. The shooting came weeks before Hasan, now 56, was scheduled to be deployed to Afghanistan. He was left partially paralysed and confined to a wheelchair from being shot by police upon his arrest.
In a statement responding to Trump's decision, the group Death Penalty Action, which opposes capital punishment, said: "There is nothing Donald Trump loves more than the power to kill."
Military executions are rare, and under the Uniform Code of Military Justice a death sentence imposed by court-martial may not be carried out "until approved by the president."
If Hasan is put to death, it would mark the first military execution since 1961, the group said. According to the Death Penalty Information Centre, the 1961 execution was carried out by hanging. The apparent last known execution by a US military firing squad was one carried out "by musketry" in November 1945, the centre reported.
At least five states have firing squads on the books, according to the Death Penalty Information Centre. In 2025, South Carolina carried out the first such execution in the US in 15 years.

title: Oil gains as traders weigh Gulf tensions against strong Mideast exports
description: Brent crude futures rise 27 cents  or 0 3   to  100 59 a barrel
content:
Brent crude futures rise 27 cents, or 0.3%, to $100.59 a barrel
Oil prices made slight gains on Tuesday as security concerns in the Middle East kept ​a geopolitical risk premium in the market, even as resilient regional crude exports and a ‌G7 emergency stockpile release eased supply concerns.
Brent crude futures were up 27 cents, or 0.3%, at $100.59 a barrel at around 0330 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose 30 cents, or 0.3%, to $89.73 a barrel.
"Shipping data shows regional crude ​exports actually exceeded pre-war levels on several days in late September. Alternative routes and logistical ​adjustments have somehow allowed producers to keep barrels moving despite the disruption around Hormuz," ⁠said Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insights at Phillip Nova.
"However, calling this a full normalisation of supply ​doesn't look justified quite yet... There have been renewed attacks on tankers around the Strait of Hormuz, and ​the number of incidents has increased in recent days. This means that while barrels are still moving, the cost, insurance, routing, and security risks of moving them remain elevated."
Gulf oil flows excluding Iran surged to over 81% of pre-war levels in ​September, data showed, led by a recovery in Saudi exports despite attacks on the kingdom's oil infrastructure ​and escalating Iranian attacks on regional shipping, while Iranian exports fell to zero due to a US blockade.
Read: Oil slips as Middle East crude exports rise, G7 to release stocks
Further easing supply ‌concerns, ⁠G7 countries agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from emergency reserves and pledged to refrain from energy export restrictions after pressure from US President Donald Trump.
However, the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen continued to fuel concerns over potential disruptions to supply from the ​region's largest oil exporter ​amid a stalemate in ⁠US-Iran talks.
Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces staged a lightning advance on Monday to retake the coast around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait up to the city of Mocha. In response, ​the Houthis said they had attacked key locations in Saudi Arabia, including ​an Aramco refinery ⁠in Rabigh. The claims could not be immediately verified.
Additionally, other market factors like low oil inventories are keeping market participants reluctant to believe lower prices can be sustained, said Vivek Dhar, analyst at Commonwealth Bank of ⁠Australia.
Gulf-to-Asia shipping rates have also lifted to new record highs, ​underscoring the tightness in the shipping market, highlighting another aspect of the oil supply chain that has little tolerance for disruption, he ​added.

title: Outgoing UN chief lauds Pakistan s mediation role in US Iran conflict
description: Says efforts helped deliver Islamabad MoU  ceasefire  framework for future negotiations
content:
Says efforts helped deliver Islamabad MoU, ceasefire, framework for future negotiations
United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Tuesday commended Pakistan’s leadership “in helping to create the conditions for dialogue between the United States and Iran and mediating the conflict.”
“Your efforts helped deliver the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, the subsequent ceasefire, and the framework for future negotiations,” he said during a joint press conference in Islamabad with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.
Guterres stated that “every Pakistani should be proud of that pivotal role.”
The UN chief added that “from Islamabad, I went to send a loud and clear message to all parties: end the conflict, return to diplomacy.”
“Fully restore navigational rights and freedoms in accordance with international law. And let's not forget, there will never be peace in the region until the right of self-determination of the Palestinian people is fully realised, as Pakistan has long championed,” he added.
Addressing members of the media, Guterres stated that “Pakistan's contribution has been on full display as a member of the UN Security Council these past two years.”
“At a time of growing division and mistrust around the world, Pakistan put a spotlight on the value of multilateralism, dialogue, mediation, and diplomacy. Those same values are vital within societies as well,” he said.
Saying that Pakistan was “one of the world's longstanding and largest contributors to the UN's peacekeeping,” Guterres noted the importance of “inclusive institutions, respect for human rights, and a vibrant civic space”, which he said were “necessary to help strengthen social cohesion, build trust, and enable people to contribute fully to their country's future.”
Read: Meeting of Makkah defence pact in Saudi Arabia next week to focus on Houthi attacks: FM Dar
The secretary general stated that “Pakistani women and men have served with courage and distinction in some of the most difficult and dangerous environments,” adding that “more than 180 brave Pakistani souls gave their lives in the service of peace.”
Guterres also stated that he was “particularly grateful for Pakistan's leadership with Denmark on Security Council Resolution 2823, which strengthens accountability for crimes against UN peacekeepers.” He noted that 153 countries had co-sponsored the resolution, which was the largest number of co-sponsors for a Security Council resolution in UN history.
Further, Guterres said that Pakistan had “endured immense suffering,” noting that “thousands of people lost their lives” and reaffirming that the UN stood with Islamabad “in confronting this threat of terrorism.”
“My message is the same everywhere in the world: addressing terrorism and legitimate security concerns is necessary and indispensable,” he said. According to the UN secretary-general, “the strongest and most effective security is guaranteed under international law, human rights, and the rule of law.”
Discussing climate change, Guterres recalled his last visit to Pakistan during the “catastrophic floods” of 2022. “I will never forget the utter devastation I saw,” he said. He added, however, “I also saw the resilience, determination, and solidarity of the Pakistani people.”
The UN chief noted, “Pakistan is on the front lines of climate chaos, despite contributing only a tiny fraction of global emissions,” he added that Islamabad was “also on the front lines of the response, from Pakistan's leadership in establishing a loss and damage fund to its growing clean energy transition at home.” However, he stated that “leadership from vulnerable developing countries cannot substitute for responsibility from developed countries,” calling for a “drastic reduction of those emissions this decade.”
“The principle of common, differentiated responsibilities must apply, but all countries must do their part,” Guterres urged. He particularly called on developed countries to “respect their commitments, namely those established in COP 29 in Baku, and deliver the finance, technology, and support developing countries need to build resilience and accelerate a just transition.”
Concluding his address, Guterres stated, “Pakistan faces challenges, as all nations do,” noting, however, that what has always stood out to him “is the resilience of the Pakistani people and their determination to build a better future.”
“I am here to further strengthen our partnership and to reaffirm a simple message: the United Nations stands with the people of Pakistan and we thank the Pakistani people for standing up for the world,” he said.
FM Dar, during his address, thanked the UN chief for his “leadership and his principled commitment to multilateralism, international law, dialogue and peaceful resolution of disputes.” According to FM Dar, Guterres had “been a great friend of Pakistan.”
“We will never forget the secretary general's solidarity with the people of Pakistan during the devastating floods of 2022 and his efforts to mobilise international support for recovery and reconstruction,” FM Dar said, extending gratitude on part of the people of Pakistan.
FM Dar added that he had a “very useful and productive bilateral meeting” with Guterres, noting that the two had “an extensive and candid exchange of views covering an entire range of issues of importance to Pakistan and the United Nations vis-a-vis the global current challenges.” These included, according to the foreign minister, international regional peace and security, West Asia, the Middle East and Palestine, South Asia, Jammu and Kashmir, Afghanistan, terrorism, the future of peacekeeping, sustainable development, climate change, and the future of multilateralism.
“We also reviewed the broad spectrum of Pakistan-UN cooperation and our ongoing contribution to the work of the organisation,” FM Dar said.
He noted further that Pakistan was currently an elected member of the Security Council. “During our tenure, we have made, rather we have tried to make significant contributions to international peace and security with particular emphasis on dialogue, diplomacy, and peaceful settlement of disputes,” he said.
He added that Islamabad’s “initiative on Security Council Resolution 2788 on strengthening multilateralism and mechanism for the peaceful settlement of disputes is a reflection of the approach of Pakistan in this regard.”
The foreign minister noted that the “unanimous adoption of that resolution reaffirmed the importance of negotiation, mediation, preventive diplomacy,” extending gratitude to Guterres for his “engagement with the follow-up to the resolution, including the participation and presentation of solid recommendations in the open debate held in July this year.”
According to FM Dar, “Pakistan also values the secretary general's readiness to extend his good offices in situations where dialogue and diplomacy can help reduce tensions and create space for peaceful solutions,” adding that this was “particularly relevant at a time when the international community is confronted with multiple conflicts and crises.”
“Pakistan believes the United Nations must remain at the centre of international efforts to address these challenges and that diplomacy must be given every opportunity to succeed,” FM Dar stated. He highlighted Pakistan’s “proactive and constructive role in promoting dialogue and de-escalation in the Gulf region.” The foreign minister noted Islamabad’s appreciation for Guterres’ “support for Pakistan's mediation efforts and his recognition of the importance of diplomatic engagement.”
“Pakistan's role in facilitating dialogue is consistent with our broader approach at the United Nations, which is to promote cooperation over confrontation, dialogue over conflict, and peaceful settlement over the use of force,” FM Dar said. He also noted Guterres’ initiatives “aimed at strengthening the multilateral system,” citing “The Pact for the Future, adopted by the General Assembly in 2024,” which he said provided “an important framework for renewed international cooperation and for addressing the challenges of our time.”
Discussing the UN’s role in the international community, FM Dar noted, “We believe that efforts to strengthen the organisation must reinforce its ability to deliver on its core mandates while ensuring that the priorities and concerns of developing countries remain central.”
He also noted that at a time of “growing geopolitical tensions, conflicts, humanitarian crises, climate vulnerabilities, and economic pressures, we need stronger, effective, inclusive, and representative multilateralism.”
“Pakistan will continue to work closely with the United Nations and with Member States to advance this objective,” he said.
FM Dar expressed gratitude to Guterres for his “continued attention to issues of particular importance to Pakistan, including regional peace and stability, counter-terrorism, climate vulnerability, and development challenges.” This included, according to the foreign minister, “the UN's consistent position on the Jammu and Kashmir dispute.”
He added that he also briefed Guterres “on India's unilateral move of holding the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance, which is a blatant violation of international law,” highlighting the need “to ensure that India stops weaponising water and fulfils its obligations under the Indus Waters Treaty.”
FM Dar “also highlighted Pakistan's deep concern at the continued use of Afghan soil for carrying out terrorist attacks against Pakistan,” expressing hope that “the Office of the Secretary-General and the international community at large will help address these challenges.”
He concluded by commending Guterres’ “stellar leadership during his tenure and for his contribution to strengthening the United Nations during a particularly challenging period for the international community.”
Earlier in the day, FM Dar met Guterres in Islamabad and discussed regional and global issues relating to peace and security, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) said on Tuesday.
According to the post on X, MoFA said, discussions covered "Palestine, Jammu and Kashmir, Afghanistan, counter-terrorism and the future of multilateralism."
"Dar briefed the UN secretary-general on Pakistan’s positions on Jammu and Kashmir and the Indus Waters Treaty, reaffirming Pakistan’s call for a just and peaceful resolution of the Kashmir dispute in accordance with relevant UN Security Council (UNSC) resolutions," the ministry said.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 met UN Secretary-General António Guterres @antonioguterres in Islamabad. Discussions covered regional and global issues relating to peace and security, including Palestine, Jammu & Kashmir,… pic.twitter.com/c82AecZRef
The statement further said the deputy prime minister highlighted Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue and de-escalation, including its facilitation of the Islamabad Talks between the US and Iran.
FM Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to dialogue and diplomacy as the most effective means of resolving disputes, according to the ministry.
"The UN secretary-general appreciated Pakistan’s longstanding contribution to the UN, as well as its diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue, mediation and de-escalation," the statement said.
FM Dar warmly received Guterres at the MoFA at the start of his official visit to Pakistan, the ministry added.

title: Modric hopes fans back Croatia against Spain
description: The hosts seek redemption after their 7 0 humiliation by England
content:
The hosts seek redemption after their 7-0 humiliation by England
Croatia captain Luka Modric said he hoped the country's fans would support the team despite a hefty defeat by England when they face world champions Spain on Tuesday in the Nations League.
Modric and his team-mates were crushed 7-0 at home by Thomas Tuchel's England on Saturday and the AC Milan midfielder said afterwards he was "ashamed" of the team's performance.
Croatia host Spain in Split in Group A3 seeking to make amends, while La Roja are hoping to seal qualification to the quarter-finals.
"Losing isn't the problem, but the way we lost is," 41-year-old former Real Madrid star Modric told reporters Monday.
"I hope the fans will cheer us on as always and that, after the match, they can judge how we played.
"That's what we need, so we're hoping for a positive reaction because what happened hurts us more than anyone."
The atmosphere should be different. Against England, Croatia were serving a one-match punishment for fan racism and played the game in front of a crowd of 6,000 local children 14 and under, who were exempted from the ban, and a handful of England supporters.
Facing Spain, who won the World Cup for the second time in July and are unbeaten in 41 matches, is a difficult challenge for Slaven Bilic's Croatia.
"Spain is the best team in the world. They're the champions," said Modric.
"I don't know how Spain is going to interpret our defeat... (but) what happened isn't typical for our team, we all know that...
"Against the best team in the world, we have to fix everything, be aggressive, and not give them too much space to find solutions."
Spain beat Croatia 4-1 in Seville earlier in the international break and have three wins from three games going into the match.
Modric said he has not decided for how long he will continue to represent his country.
"We're taking it one game at a time. We'll see if I leave the national team in a year or a month," explained Modric, who earned a 205th cap against England.
"The important thing for me is to be in a place that makes me happy. I'm willing to help at any time, both on and off the field."
Bilic, coaching Croatia for the second spell in his career, said facing the new world champions offered a quick chance of redemption.
"It (the England thrashing) was incredibly tough. We'll never forget it, but when there's a fire, you have to react," said Bilic.
"On one hand we have a very difficult opponent, but it's the best opportunity for us."
Spain coach Luis de la Fuente wrote off Croatia's heavy defeat by England.
"What happened the other day was just an accident in football," said the Spain coach.
"It doesn't reflect the difference in footballing ability between Croatia and England. This result can motivate them."
Teenage winger Lamine Yamal has excelled for Spain in their first three group matches, scoring in each of them, including a brace against Croatia.
"Lamine is in fantastic form. He's a role model and a born competitor," said the Spain coach.
"He's in good shape to play tomorrow's match. But so are other team-mates, who are all in perfect condition."
Spain and Barca midfielder Dani Olmo developed as a youth player at Dinamo Zagreb in Croatia, although he was not used by De la Fuente in their meeting in Seville.
Olmo left Barcelona as a teenager to join Dinamo, before later rejoining the Catalan giants in 2024 from RB Leipzig.
"Everyone has their own story... I took this decision, one of the hardest of my career to date... because of the interest of Dinamo and how much they wanted to help me grow," explained Olmo.
"I trusted in that, I think it was one of the best steps I took in my career, leaving at 16, with my mother, to a new country, using a new language, it was difficult but beautiful."

title: Jeffrey Archer  bestselling British author and former politician  dies aged 86
description: HarperCollins confirmed that the  Kane   Abel  author died  suddenly and peacefully at home  on Monday
content:
HarperCollins confirmed that the 'Kane & Abel' author died 'suddenly and peacefully at home' on Monday
Jeffrey Archer, the bestselling British author and former politician, has died aged 86.
Archer’s publisher HarperCollins confirmed that the Kane & Abel author died “suddenly and peacefully at home” on Monday. No cause of death was disclosed.
Archer sold more than 300 million books during a writing career spanning five decades.
HarperCollins said he was the only author to have achieved No. 1 bestseller status in fiction, short stories and non-fiction.
His novels were adapted for television and film, including Kane & Abel , the 1985 CBS miniseries starring Peter Strauss and Sam Neill.
ITV adapted First Among Equals in 1986, while the BBC adapted Not a Penny More, Not a Penny Less in 1990.
Archer was also a Conservative politician and served as the party’s deputy chairman before becoming a member of the House of Lords.
His political career was disrupted in 2001 when he was imprisoned after being convicted of lying and cheating in a 1987 libel case involving The Daily Star .
“Jeffrey’s career is the stuff of publishing legend,” HarperCollins said in a statement, according to BBC News. The publisher highlighted his extensive bestseller-list record and described him as “the master storyteller”.
Archer’s final book, Adam and Eve , is due to be released this month.
His website also states that Paramount was developing an adaptation of Not a Penny More, Not a Penny Less for its 50th anniversary in 2026.

title: Kane driven by desire for records says Tuchel
description: England captain reaches new heights in Germany after becoming the fastest to 100 Bundesliga goals
content:
England captain reaches new heights in Germany after becoming the fastest to 100 Bundesliga goals
Thomas Tuchel said England captain Harry Kane is driven by a burning desire for milestone moments as the striker prepares to equal his country's appearance record against the Czech Republic.
Kane will draw level with former England goalkeeper Peter Shilton on 125 caps if he plays in Tuesday's Nations League match at Wembley.
It will be the latest landmark in the 33-year-old's remarkable career.
Kane is already well established as England's record goalscorer, taking his tally to 89 with a double in Saturday's 7-0 win in Croatia.
He also became Tottenham's all-time leading scorer with 280 goals before leaving the Premier League club to join Bayern Munich in 2023.
Kane has hit new heights since moving Bayern, breaking a 49-year record in September when he became the fastest player to score 100 Bundesliga goals, in his 98th league game.
England boss Tuchel believes Kane's sustained success has been fuelled by a fierce competitive streak that pushes him to keep chasing more records.
"I think all these number nines in the world, no matter in which league or in youth football, they are built a little bit differently," Tuchel told reporters on Monday.
"They not only do it so that their team wins, but they also do it for themselves, they do it for the records.
"How many can I score, how many can I assist, who is the best scorer in the league, who do I have to overtake, where is the next record?
"You will not find any goalscorer of this calibre who has not these individual goals set up and pushing him to the limit. So that is what drives him. That's how Harry is built."
After failing to land a single trophy with Tottenham, Kane has already won two Bundesliga titles during his time in Munich.
His impressive form in 2026 has made him a contender to win the Ballon d'Or later in October.
"I'm not sure if I have any more words, because I feel like he scores all the time, he plays fantastic and he's in the shortlist for (the) Ballon d'Or," Tuchel said.
"It's just everything he does, he does it on the highest level, and he does it consecutively.
"Since he takes this major role for Bayern Munich, he found a new level, and it's on and off the pitch highest level."
Tuchel will be without Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and Arsenal defender Ezri Konsa against the Czechs after the injured pair withdrew from the squad.
Scott, who made his first England start against Croatia, has a thigh problem that will reportedly rule him out for two months.
"I can understand that Bournemouth are not happy because they lose a key player," Tuchel said.
"But I can just say that from the moment we took the decision (to play him) there was absolutely no risk apparent to me or our physical staff. It's a one-off."
England are second in group A3 of the Nations League on six points, three behind leaders Spain.

Trump appears to say Iran should be allowed to ‘take out’ Los Angeles and San Diego
Tehran warned Bahrain and other regional states against allowing their territory or airspace to be used in attacks on Iran, saying that it will respond if they allow such attacks again, according to Iran's state news agency IRNA on Tuesday.
Ali Karimi Magham, Second Secretary of the Permanent Mission of the Islamic Republic of Iran to the United Nations, made the remarks on Monday before the UN Third Committee, responding to statements by Bahrain’s representative.
He said Bahrain was speaking about human rights while ignoring the circumstances surrounding events.
Iran warns Bahrain, regional states against attacks from their territory https://t.co/zjyKDHMR6h pic.twitter.com/48z7WfHtET
Karimi Magham said Bahrain was not a victim, noting that it had provided its territory, bases and airspace for an illegal US war against Iran. A country that had made its territory available for an unlawful war against its neighbour, he said, could not express surprise at the consequences, according to IRNA .
The Iranian representative stressed that Iran had not initiated the attack but had been attacked, describing Tehran’s response as the exercise of its legitimate inherent right, and he added that Iran would respond if the territory of a country in the region were used to launch an attack against it again.
Iranian army claims accelerated production of advanced missiles, drones
Spokesman for the Iranian Army Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia spoke on the military’s enhanced readiness in an interview with Fars News Agency, signalling a significant leap in the country’s indigenous deterrence capabilities, according to Press TV .
Akraminia confirmed that the domestic production of new military hardware did not cease during the war.
‘Massive stockpile’: Iran Army announces accelerated production of advanced missiles, drones https://t.co/EGOCQ6wOlQ pic.twitter.com/BR4HqzYxeo
"The new defensive and offensive equipment, including missiles and drones, was being produced on a daily basis during the 40-day (Ramadan) war, and today, their production continues with even greater intensity," the Army spokesman stated.
"Currently, a massive stockpile of this equipment is at the disposal of the Iranian Army forces, and the Army is fully prepared in terms of equipment."
He added that the army already deployed some of these new systems in the field, with plans to officially unveil them to the media at the "appropriate time and if necessary.”
Akraminia also emphasised the tactical experience gained by Iranian forces during the recent US-Israeli aggression.
In a separate interview, IRNA reported that Iranian army commander Major General Amir Hatami said that Iran's defence industry played a critical role in supporting combat forces during the recent 12-day and 40-day imposed wars.
Iran’s homegrown defense industry proved its worth in recent wars: Army chief Hatami https://t.co/wsMQTCX4lo pic.twitter.com/zNA2dW2MQC
Hatami made the remarks during a meeting with Mehrdad Akhlaqi, managing director of the Defence Industries Organisation of the Ministry of Defence and Armed Forces Logistics, at the Army headquarters in Tehran on Tuesday.
IRNA reported that Hatami praised the efforts of defence industry specialists during the conflicts, saying that despite enemy attempts to disrupt the production chain for military equipment and weapons, ministry managers and employees kept production lines operating under the most difficult conditions.
Trump appears to say Iran should be allowed to ‘take out’ Los Angeles and San Diego
US President Donald Trump appeared to suggest on Monday that Iran should be allowed to “take out” California’s two largest cities while discussing war-related price increases.
Speaking at a campaign rally in Grand Island, Nebraska, he argued that Americans should accept higher prices as a cost of maintaining national and global security.
“And again, remember, with the war, it’s just artificial,” he said.
“It’s a little bit high. It’s a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe."
Trump then referred to the possibility of an Iranian attack on an American city.
“They can take out a city,” he said. “Let them take out Los Angeles. Let them take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay.”

He said the war was “essentially almost over with” while acknowledging that it could continue for a longer period.
The president also discussed Iran's ability to withstand economic pressure, saying Iranian leaders have described themselves as having a “big threshold for pain.”
“They need it, let me tell you,” he said.
Trump predicted that the conflict would eventually end “one way or the other” before returning to the economic consequences Americans are facing.
"But it's going to end very soon, and it'll end one way or the other," he said, adding that prices are going to come down "very sharply."
California Governor Gavin Newsom criticised Trump's remarks.
"After sending the National Guard and Marines to occupy California, Donald Trump is now saying our foreign enemies should ‘take out’ Los Angeles and San Diego. He is deranged and dangerous," Newsom said on the US social media platform X.

They could also be subject to civil and criminal enforcement penalties should Iran-related transactions cause US financial institutions or other US persons to violate sanctions, the Treasury Department added.

title: France roar back in Nations League as Italy beat Turkey
description: Olise scores twice as France beat Belgium 4 1
content:
Olise scores twice as France beat Belgium 4-1
Michael Olise starred as France stormed back from behind to thrash Belgium 4-1 in the UEFA Nations League on Monday, while Italy continued their resurgence with victory over Turkey.
Dodi Lukebakio's first-half strike had Belgium on track for a first competitive victory over France since 1981, but Zinedine Zidane turned to his star-studded bench and the hosts produced a devastating late surge.
Les Bleus struck four times in the final 13 minutes to keep Zidane's unbeaten record as coach intact as France edged closer to a place in the quarter-finals.
Desire Doue equalised with a low shot from the edge of the box before Olise pulled the ball back for Rayan Cherki to put France ahead as the floodgates opened, with substitutes accounting for all of the hosts' goals.
Olise put the game to bed with a scruffy third goal before he grabbed another in stoppage time to round off a breathtaking turnaround.
"I think we played well at the end. The first half was difficult.. but we kept going and we're happy," Olise told TF1.
The Bayern Munich winger has been France's most influential player in the early stages of Zidane's reign, netting four times in his last three matches despite starting only once.
"It's a team effort. He (Zidane) brings his own ideas and we follow him. We've done well in these four games and we'll keep going," said Olise.
France hold a three-point lead over Italy in Group A1, with Belgium another point behind.
Zidane's team will complete their group campaign with games away to Italy and at home to Turkey next month.
Italy, who are rebuilding under Roberto Mancini, moved up into second place courtesy of a 3-1 win over Turkey in Bologna.
Gianluca Scamacca drilled Italy ahead only for Aral Simsir to level just after the hour. The Azzurri, who thrashed Turkey 4-1 last week in Bursa, secured another win at home with goals from Riccardo Calafiori and Pio Esposito.
"There was fatigue all around, and we struggled a bit. But we did well to score, and then to score again right after they equalised," said Mancini.
The 61-year-old, who led Italy to Euro 2020 glory, is back for a second spell in charge of a nation who have failed to qualify for the last three World Cups.
"We have to keep playing. We're currently in second place, and we'll likely have to fight to secure that spot in Belgium," added Mancini.
Northern Ireland remain top of Group B2 but had to settle for a 0-0 draw against Georgia after Liverpool goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili saved a late Isaac Price penalty in Belfast.
Hungary are a point adrift following a 2-1 win over Ukraine in a match played in Slovakia.
Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres scored for the seventh Nations League game in a row to give Sweden a 1-0 win in Romania. Graham Potter's side sit two points clear in Group B4 of Bosnia and Herzegovina, who beat Poland 1-0.
Former Tottenham winger Marcus Edwards scored a stoppage-time winner as Cyprus edged Latvia 2-1 in Group C2, while leaders Montenegro and Armenia drew 0-0.

title: Five terrorists killed  two wounded in North Waziristan operation  security sources
description: They had been continuously monitoring the movement of terrorists before carrying out operation against group
content:
President Zardari, PM Shehbaz praise security forces, reaffirm resolve to eliminate terrorism
Security forces killed five terrorists and wounded two others in a successful intelligence-based operation (IBO) against Fitna al-Khawarij in North Waziristan, Radio Pakistan reported on Tuesday, citing security sources.
According to the sources, the security forces successfully targeted Fitna al-Khawarij hideouts in North Waziristan and surrounding areas, and they had been continuously monitoring the movement of Fitna al-Khawarij before carrying out a decisive operation against the group, the sources added.
Fitna al - Khawarij is the term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
The security forces remained committed to completely eliminating terrorism and establishing lasting peace under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision, the sources said.
Five Khawarij have been killed and two others have been injured during an intelligence-based operation by security forces in North Waziristan #News #RadioPakistan https://t.co/TEokSd1Ysv
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif commended security forces for conducting a successful operation in North Waziristan, Radio Pakistan reported.
In his statement, the president said the timely and effective operations by the security forces played an important role in foiling the nefarious designs of terrorist elements.
The prime minister said operations against Fitna al-Khawarij would continue until the complete elimination of terrorism. He said the complete eradication of terrorism and sustainable peace under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision were the government’s top priorities.
President @AAliZardari and Prime Minister @CMShehbaz have commended security forces for conducting a successful intelligence-based operation in North Waziristan #News #RadioPakistan https://t.co/TEokSd1Ysv pic.twitter.com/zUflr9qoeC
Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terrorist activity over the past three months, with a series of attacks across the country resulting in the martyrdom of security personnel and civilians.
Last week, 12 people were killed and 35 others injured when a blast struck a joint checkpoint near Aman Mela in the Darazinda area of Dera Ismail Khan, with the TTP claiming responsibility for the attack.
On September 19, 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred in a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. title: Djokovic into China Open final
description: Medvedev out for hitting fan with ball
content:
Novak Djokovic advanced to the China Open final on Monday after Daniil Medvedev was disqualified late in the second set, when a ball that came off the Russian's racquet hit a spectator.
A man sitting in the stands behind Medvedev's side of the court was seen holding his face and escorted from his seat after being hit, as Djokovic was serving for the match with the score at 7-5, 5-3.
Eleventh-ranked Djokovic will play world number nine Alex de Minaur for the title Tuesday in Beijing.
The Australian had advanced over Hubert Hurkacz after the 29-year-old from Poland retired from their semi-final with an adductor muscle strain.
Medvedev's disqualification arose from a moment deep in the match. When he failed to return a point, the ball bounced off the back wall and Medvedev hit it with a backhand up into the stands, with the chair umpire stopping play.
"Terribly sorry to the spectator, first of all," he told reporters afterwards, adding it was "100 percent an accident" and that he wished to apologise to the fan in person.
"The ball was bouncing back, so I tried to, like, just hit it anywhere, so it doesn't go out from the court," he said.
It had been a physical battle before Medvedev's disqualification.
Djokovic was red-faced and hunched over between points, with both players forcing each other through gruelling rallies, until the Serbian took control in the second set.
The 39-year-old put on a dazzling performance and saved 16 break points across the match, diving at the baseline and sprinting to the net.
"I didn't see what happened, to be honest," Djokovic told the crowd after the fan was hit.
"I'm sure that Daniil didn't... do it intentionally. It happened by accident. Sorry for the crowd," he said, adding that it had been a tough contest.
"I know the feeling," Djokovic told reporters later, recounting his own disqualification from the 2020 US Open after accidentally hitting a ball at a line judge.
"It's horrible... but it happens," he said.
Although Djokovic was three points away from winning the match, he said victory wouldn't have come easy and that he got "lucky" in a "very exhausting" battle.
In the women's draw, third-seeded Coco Gauff dispatched Chinese teenager Sun Xinran 7-5, 6-1 to secure a meeting with Belgium's Elise Mertens in the round of 16.
"Today was really just about feeling," said the 22-year-old American, adding that it could be tough to play young players with styles largely unknown.
"I was just trying not to get frustrated out there," Gauff added, with a loud crowd behind the 16-year-old.
Former world number one Iga Swiatek staged a comeback to advance, dominating a must-win tie-break to beat Croatia's Donna Vekic 4-6, 7-6 (7/0), 6-2.
"I was just angry, wanted to change something, because clearly it wasn't working," the 25-year-old from Poland said on court.
"Sometimes if you care a bit less because you're... probably going to lose, it also helps you a bit," she told reporters.
She will face American teenager Iva Jovic for a spot in the quarter-finals.
China's Zheng Qinwen was tested by Marie Bouzkova, enduring her third three-setter of the tournament to beat the Czech player 7-6 (7/3), 4-6, 7-5.
She pulled out some of her most accurate tennis to clinch the last two games and win when 27th-ranked Bouzkova fired long.
"I gave everything," said Zheng, who had already spent more than five hours on court in the first two rounds.
"Truthfully speaking, I felt a lot of pressure today," the 23-year-old told her home crowd, thanking fans for their support.
Zheng, the current world number 54, next plays 118th-ranked Alina Charaeva, who sent out top seed Elena Rybakina in the second round.
Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova also advanced and will face Ekaterina Alexandrova in the last 16, while Ukraine's Elina Svitolina will play American Ann Li.

title: Wheat flour price surge triggers roti crisis
description: Wheat flour price surge triggers roti crisis
content:
20kg bag hits Rs3,300 as supplies dwindle
The price of a 20-kilogram bag of flour has soared to Rs3,300 in Peshawar, triggering a corresponding rise in the cost of roti and sparking public frustration over what many describe as an artificial crisis.
With government-subsidised flour largely unavailable in the open market, commercial rates have climbed sharply. A 20-kg bag of coarse (dana-dar) flour is now selling for Rs3,300, while fine flour of the same weight costs Rs3,120. An 80-kg bag of coarse flour has reached Rs13,200, and 20 kg of chokar is priced at Rs1,480. Traders and residents say these levels mark a record increase in the city.
The surge has prompted significant investment activity. Flour dealers have reportedly earned crores of rupees in profits within just a few days by capitalising on the rapid price rise. At the same time, allegations have surfaced that an artificial shortage is being engineered. In response, law-enforcement agencies have begun monitoring large dealers and warehouses across the city.
The impact has quickly reached the tandoors. Bakers have raised the price of a 50-gram single roti to Rs30, an increase of Rs10. In several key markets, including Khyber Bazaar, Ashraf Road, Karachi Market, Namak Mandi and Government College Chowk, the sale of single rotis has been discontinued. Only double rotis are now available, selling for Rs40 each. Residents also report a continuous reduction in the weight of rotis being sold.
Despite the sharp rise in prices and the shrinking size of bread, the Peshawar administration has remained silent. Citizens have appealed to the government to take action against bakers and sellers who refuse to supply roti according to the official rate list and prescribed weight.
The combination of vanishing official supplies, soaring market rates, dealer profits and reduced roti weights has left ordinary households bearing the brunt of the crisis, with no immediate relief in sight.
Meanwhile, Food Department claimed it distributed a total of 417,168 bags of flour at official rates across the province through 1,611 active flour dealers last week. According to the figures, Peshawar Division received 101,955 bags, Mardan Division 59,389, Malakand Division 120,737, Hazara Division 38,129, Bannu 12,588, Dera Ismail Khan Division 41,688 and Kohat Division 42,682 bags.
The department stated that 3,000 metric tonnes of government wheat from the provincial strategic reserve is being released daily to flour mills. Citizens are receiving 20-kilogramme bags of official flour at Rs 2,520 through selected dealers.
Eight flour mills were fined for violating standard operating procedures. Teams of the Food Safety and Halal Food Authority and the Food Department are regularly monitoring the quality of wheat and flour.

title: Operation theatre stays closed a month after fire
description: Operation theatre stays closed a month after fire
content:
Five-storey Surgical Tower project launched in 2022 remains incomplete
An operating theatre at Sheikh Zayed Medical College and Hospital, damaged in a fire a month ago, has yet to be restored, causing difficulties for patients awaiting surgery, particularly those in the gynaecology ward.
The fire broke out on September 5 following an alleged short circuit in one of the hospital's operating theatres. At the time, a patient inside the theatre was safely moved to another location by hospital staff, while doctors, paramedics and security personnel brought the fire under control. No casualties were reported.
However, the affected operating theatre has not been fully restored, according to hospital sources. Its prolonged closure has reduced the hospital's available surgical capacity and increased the workload on the only fully operational theatre.
Sources said patients from emergency, outpatient and various other wards were having to be accommodated according to the limited available surgical facilities. Women awaiting procedures in the gynaecology ward were facing particular difficulties, while concerns had also been raised about delays in emergency and other surgical cases.
The situation has also highlighted delays in the completion of the hospital's multi-billion-rupee Surgical Tower project, which was launched to expand modern surgical facilities.
Nazik Hussain said his wife, Sidra, had been admitted to the labour room for childbirth, where doctors deemed an immediate operation necessary. However, he alleged that despite continuous efforts for two days, an operating theatre could not be made available.
On the third day, when his wife's condition became critical, the operation was finally performed. According to Nazik Hussain, the patient would not have faced such a serious situation if an operating theatre had been available in time.
Muhammad Saleem said that due to the unavailability of an immediate operating facility in the labour room, he was forced to shift his patient to a private hospital, where the operation was performed.
He said the lack of timely operating theatre facilities for emergency cases at the government hospital was causing serious difficulties for patients and their attendants.
According to available project details, the approximately Rs7 billion Surgical Tower comprises a five-storey building with a basement, 448 beds and around 384,000 square feet of covered area.
The project includes modern operating theatres for complex surgeries, intensive care units, recovery rooms, post-operative wards and a central sterile services department, among other medical facilities.
Completion of the Surgical Tower is expected to significantly increase the hospital's surgical capacity and reduce pressure on existing operating theatres.

title: Faisalabad s 2021 41 master plan remains in limbo
description: Faisalabad s 2021 41 master plan remains in limbo
content:
FDA says housing schemes are being assessed under the 2015 peri-urban plan
Technical circles and town planning experts have expressed concern over the delay in finalising and enforcing the Faisalabad Master Plan 2021-41, saying uncertainty over the city's future development framework is affecting long-term planning.
The master plan, described by experts as a key document for the city's future economic and urban development, was approved by the Faisalabad Development Authority (FDA) Board of Governors on Dec 22, 2022.
Sources said the Lahore High Court later struck down the master plan after finding that the required Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) had not been obtained before its finalisation.
Abdul Ghaffar, a retired WASA director, said private housing schemes had previously been regulated under the Faisalabad Peri-Urban Structure Plan (FPUSP) 2015, which covered around 912 square kilometres, while the new master plan covered a much larger area.
He said the Anti-Corruption Establishment registered a case on July 20, 2023, against Board of Governors Chairman and MPA Mian Waris Aziz and then FDA Director General Zahid Ikram over alleged provision of undue benefits to private housing developers.
According to Ghaffar, the LHC directed the FDA on March 26, 2024, to obtain a fresh EIA report from the Environment Department. The FDA subsequently filed an intra-court appeal, which was dismissed on Sept 15, 2025.
He said that following the dismissal, the FDA had again adopted the 2015 peri-urban structure plan, which had become obsolete after approval of the new master plan in 2022.
He also claimed that areas designated as residential zones under the 2021-41 master plan had now been treated as green zones under the peri-urban plan, while development work by a private housing scheme was continuing in one such area.
Architect Amjad Ali Khan said the FDA had earlier awarded a contract worth Rs50 million for preparation of the master plan, which was subsequently scrapped.
"If the zoning structure changes, the FDA may have to revise the existing master plan or prepare a new one, and either option would require additional funding," he said.
Town planner Nadeem Khursheed said an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) in Pakistan was a statutory decision-support and regulatory instrument for assessing the environmental and related social consequences of proposed development projects.
He said an EIA was intended to identify potential environmental impacts, prescribe mitigation and management measures, facilitate public participation and enable the competent environmental authority to determine whether a project could proceed and under what conditions.
FDA Director General Chaudhry Muhammad Asif said the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report had been sent to the Director General Environment Punjab for vetting and an open public hearing, which was still awaited.
He said that in the absence of the struck-down master plan, the Faisalabad Development Authority (FDA) was bound to approve layout plans for new housing colonies in accordance with the peri-urban structure plan adopted in 2015 by the then City District Government.

title: School carpooling urged to curb smog
description: School carpooling urged to curb smog
content:
Move aimed at reducing morning air pollution ahead of peak season
The Punjab government has advised schools to promote carpooling among students, parents and staff to help prevent smog caused by emissions.
Environment Director General Abdullah Nair Sheikh directed school administrations to facilitate shared transport arrangements for students travelling from the same areas or along common routes.
According to the DG, traffic congestion around schools during morning hours, vehicular emissions and slow-moving traffic contribute to higher levels of particulate pollution.
He said reducing the number of vehicles making unnecessary trips was essential.
He called on school administrations, parents and students to play their role in anti-smog efforts, while stressing that carpooling should not impose any additional financial burden on parents or students.
Recommendations for effective carpooling arrangements have been forwarded to the school education department.
According to the environment protection department's air quality dashboard, winds in Lahore were blowing from the southeast at five kilometres per hour on Monday morning, while the city's Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 170.
During the last 24 hours, 21 industrial units were inspected across Punjab. Four were sealed, two cases were registered and fines totalling Rs300,000 were imposed for environmental violations.
Officials said 70 brick kilns were also inspected and one of them was sealed and a fine of Rs100,000 imposed. In addition, 18 kilogrammes of plastic was confiscated. water was sprinkled over 1,006 kilometres of roads across the province.
Authorities also issued 301 warnings and notices against burning of solid waste, tyres, rubber and plastic.
Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb said anti-smog measures were not being treated as a temporary campaign but as part of a comprehensive effort to bring long-term environmental improvement.
She said providing farmers alternatives to crop-residue burning remained a government priority.
The air quality in the metropolis remained unhealthy, the overall AQI recorded at 193 at 9:00am and rising to 197 by 7:00pm, according to the Environmental Protection Agency's real-time monitoring data.
Wagah Border remained the most polluted area of Lahore in the evening, recording an AQI of 391, classified as very unhealthy.
Multan Road recorded an AQI of 258, while Barki Road recorded 198 at 7:00pm.
According to IQAir's real-time data, Lahore had an AQI of 167 at 8:00pm, with particulate matter ratio PM2.5 recorded at 78 micrograms per cubic metre.
At the time, Lahore ranked 10th in Pakistan in IQAir's real-time city ranking.
On the other hand, authorities cautioned farmers to refrain from burning rice crop stubble after harvesting, as the practice not only affects soil fertility but also has adverse effects on the environment and health.
A spokesperson said burning crop residue increased air pollution and respiratory diseases.
He advised farmers to incorporate the residues into the soil instead of burning them, saying the practice increases organic matter and improves soil fertility for the next crop.

title: 100kg wheat price hits record Rs13 100 in Hyderabad
description: 100kg wheat price hits record Rs13 100 in Hyderabad
content:
Staple food rate surges by Rs600 in just two days
The price of a 100-kilogram bag of wheat in Hyderabad's open market has reached a record Rs13,100, increasing by Rs600 in just two days and raising fears that the price of flour could cross Rs160 per kilogram.
The sharp increase has been attributed by flour millers and flour-chakki owners to the delay in the release of the government wheat quota, with concerns that continued price increases in the open market could push flour prices to Rs170 per kilogram in the coming days.
According to market sources, a 100kg bag of wheat was available for Rs12,500 on Saturday. Its price increased by Rs300 to Rs12,800 on Sunday and rose by another Rs300 on Monday to reach Rs13,100, described by traders as the highest-ever price recorded in the open market.
Flour mills and chakki owners in Hyderabad are currently purchasing wheat from the open market as they have not been receiving wheat under the government quota. The higher cost of wheat has already affected flour prices. Chakki owners are selling flour at around Rs155 per kilogram at wholesale rates, while retailers and general stores are charging approximately Rs160 per kilogram.
According to flour-chakki owners, if wheat prices are not brought under control, flour could reach Rs170 per kilogram in Hyderabad.
The Sindh government has announced a policy for releasing wheat stocks stored in government warehouses, but the official price has yet to be determined. The provincial cabinet had initially announced that the government wheat quota would be released on October 1. However, the decision was later revised, and the release date was moved to October 20.
Flour-chakki owners said the delay has created an opportunity for traders and hoarders to increase wheat prices in the open market. They claimed the price has been rising almost daily, directly affecting consumers.
They also said that the cost of producing one kilogram of flour at a chakki is around Rs35, while the deputy commissioner has approved only Rs24 as the cost component to be included in the price.
Haji Muhammad Memon, president of the Flour Chakki Owners Social Welfare Association, told the Express that an artificial shortage of wheat had been created in Hyderabad's open market. He claimed that even at Rs13,100, wheat was difficult to obtain and warned that hoarders could push prices even higher in the coming days.
Memon urged Sindh Chief Minister to ensure the immediate release of the government wheat quota, warning that continued shortages could lead to a further increase in flour prices across Hyderabad and other parts of interior Sindh.

description: 3 suspects in trader s murder case remanded to police custody
content:
Court granted the request and handed the three suspects over to Tando Yousuf police for another five days
A court has remanded three suspects arrested in the murder case of Hindu trader Naresh Kumar to police custody for another five days.
Tando Yousuf police produced suspects Waqas Mughal, Asad Ali Dhamach and Shoaib Malik before the Ninth Civil Judge and Judicial Magistrate, Hyderabad, after the expiry of their previous remand. The investigating officer also submitted a progress report and requested further physical remand, stating that the investigation was still incomplete.
The court granted the request and handed the three suspects over to Tando Yousuf police for another five days. According to police, the investigation so far suggested that local trader Waqas Malik allegedly planned the murder. Police alleged that Shoaib Malik facilitated a meeting between Malik and alleged contract killer Asad Ali Dhamach, where payment for the killing was reportedly agreed upon. Police further alleged that Shoaib arranged the weapon used in the crime.
Last week, a debt dispute allegedly ended in the killing of a 35-year-old Hindu trader whose bullet-riddled body was found in his abandoned car hours after he went missing. The police claimed that one of his close acquaintances hired a hitman to eliminate him over repayment of millions of rupees.
Naseem Nagar police arrested a suspect in an injured condition along with a weapon following an alleged encounter, while his accomplice managed to escape.
According to police, the encounter took place when officers were conducting checking in the area. An exchange of fire occurred between police and two suspects riding a motorcycle, during which officers arrested one suspect after he was injured. The arrested suspect was identified as Daniyal alias Manna Sheikh.
During preliminary interrogation, he allegedly told police that he and his accomplice were on their way to commit a crime. Police said the suspect's criminal record showed that he had previously been wanted or involved in cases including alleged police encounters, drug offences and kidnapping registered at various police stations in Hyderabad.

title: White eagle takes wing after 150 years
description: White eagle takes wing after 150 years
content:
Rare bird rescued in critical condition to be GPS-tracked after release into Margalla Hills
Nearly a century and a half after it was last recorded here, a rare White-Tailed Eagle has made an extraordinary return to Pakistan - only to be found barely alive, with both eyes sewn shut and its body riddled with injuries.
The European-origin raptor was discovered in October 2025 during research into migratory birds visiting Pakistan from colder regions of the world. Rescued in critical condition, the eagle was found to be suffering from severe eye infections and other injuries, with bird trappers allegedly using it to lure and capture other birds.
Now undergoing rehabilitation in a controlled environment, the rare visitor is being prepared for a second chance at freedom. Once fully recovered, it is expected to be released in the Margalla Hills in December, fitted with a GPS tracker that will allow researchers to follow its movements and migration route.
Speaking to The Express Tribune, Karachi-based bird enthusiast Haroon Yousafzai said the discovery came during research into migratory birds arriving in Pakistan.
According to Yousafzai, the White-Tailed Eagle had migrated to Pakistan from Europe but was in an extremely critical condition when it was rescued. He said both of the bird's eyes had been sewn shut with thread and it was suffering from severe infections and other injuries. The bird's physical condition had significantly reduced its chances of survival, he said. Following its rescue, it was placed in an environment maintained at a controlled temperature, where it has been receiving treatment and rehabilitation.
Yousafzai said the presence of the White-Tailed Eagle in Pakistan had been recorded after almost 150 years.
The bird is expected to be released into the wild in December after making a full recovery. Yousafzai said the Margalla Hills had been selected as the release site to help the eagle return towards its natural habitat.
Before its release, the eagle will be fitted with a GPS tracker. The device will enable researchers to monitor its movements, migration routes and behaviour in the wild.

Three more Pakistani crew members of the oil tanker Honor 25 are scheduled to arrive in Karachi on Wednesday, after spending two days in Ethiopia.

Somali and Puntland security forces retook the vessel last week in a joint operation. During the operation, pirates opened fire on the hostages, killing five crew members, including three Pakistanis, and injuring five others, four of them Pakistanis.
The bodies of the three Pakistani victims and four injured sailors were brought to Karachi on Sunday.
Yousuf and Ali are Karachi residents, while Yasin belongs to Swat.

title: Country s varsities fall short of global top 400
description: Country s varsities fall short of global top 400
content:
KU languishes in 1,601-1,800 band as 56 institutions make THE rankings
Pakistan's universities have once again been left knocking at the door of the global academic elite, with none managing to break into the world's top 400 in the latest Times Higher Education (THE) rankings.
The country's best-performing institution sits somewhere in the 551-600 bracket, while two of its largest public universities - the University of Karachi and the University of the Punjab - languish in the 1,601-1,800 and 1,801-2,000 bands, respectively.
The rankings paint a sobering picture of Pakistan's academic standing: 56 universities secured a place on the global list, but none came close to the top 400. The gap raises uncomfortable questions about research output, academic productivity and the ability of Pakistani universities to compete on the world stage.
THE has released its World University Rankings 2027, with the University of Oxford retaining the top position for an 11th consecutive year. The Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) ranked second, while Princeton University and Stanford University shared third place. The University of Cambridge secured fifth position and Harvard University sixth.
The California Institute of Technology ranked seventh, Imperial College London eighth, while the University of California, Berkeley and Yale University jointly occupied ninth place.
The top 10 was dominated by the United States and United Kingdom, with seven US and three UK universities making the list. Asian universities continued to strengthen their global presence. China's Tsinghua University ranked 11th and Peking University 13th, while China secured 17 places in the top 200.
Japan had five universities in the top 200, including the University of Tokyo at 27th and Kyoto University at joint 62nd. Malaysia's University of Malaya entered the top 200 for the first time, ranking joint 194th.
Among Pakistani universities, Quaid-i-Azam University emerged as the country's highest-ranked institution, placed in the 551-600 band. The National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST) followed in the 601-650 band, while COMSATS University Islamabad was placed in the 651-700 band.
Bahauddin Zakariya University, the University of Agriculture Faisalabad and the University of Lahore were ranked in the 701-800 band.
The 801-1,000 band included Abdul Wali Khan University Mardan, Air University, Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences and Technology, Gomal University, Government College University Faisalabad, Government College University Lahore, International Islamic University Islamabad, Iqra University and others.

title: Missing CCTV puts Raza probe under fresh scrutiny
description: Missing CCTV puts Raza probe under fresh scrutiny
content:
Five-hour footage gap raises question as commission inspects crime scene
Five hours of missing CCTV footage, multiple routes leading to the spot where Mir Raza Ali's body was found and conflicting accounts over a possible power outage have emerged as key questions before the Judicial Commission probing the young businessman's death.
Justice Umar Sial, who heads the commission, visited the suspected crime scene in Gulistan-e-Jauhar on Monday, inspecting the guesthouse, Masjid Khizra, a Karachi Water and Sanitation Corporation office and colony, a nursery and the location where Mir Raza's body was recovered on July 29.
The inspection brought the surveillance trail of the case into sharper focus. The commission was told that a main CCTV camera at Masjid Khizra remained inactive for five hours, from 5pm to 10pm on July 28 - the period surrounding the incident.
Investigators attributed the missing footage to load-shedding, but Mir Raza's family lawyer Jibran Nasir said information obtained from K-Electric showed there had been no power breakdown in the area.
Justice Sial questioned the mosque's muezzin and caretaker about the cameras. When they expressed ignorance about why the cameras had stopped recording, the judge warned them that they could find their names on his list of suspects if they failed to tell the truth.
According to the commission's written order, seven CCTV cameras are installed at Masjid Khizra, two of which face the area where Mir Raza's body was found. The commission has sought a detailed report from K-Electric on any scheduled or unscheduled power outage in the area between 5pm and 10pm on July 28. The power utility has been directed to submit the report in sealed form on October 7.
Nasir alleged that as many as 116 cameras were installed around the area, whereas police had accounted for only 10. He said footage from only one of the mosque's cameras had been provided and five hours of that recording were missing.
The lawyer also questioned the police account of the crime scene, saying there were four routes leading to the location where Mir Raza's body was found. He claimed the family believed the body may have been brought to the site and dumped there.
The commission inspected these routes as well as the rear exit of a guesthouse that had been questioned by Mir Raza's father. Investigators also showed the commission the route Mir Raza allegedly took towards a nursery and the spot where CCTV footage showed him throwing something. The location where a holster and cartridge casing were recovered was also examined.
Justice Sial later said several important CCTV recordings were still unavailable and that he would examine how many of the recordings requested by the commission had actually been supplied. He said between 30 and 35 camera numbers had emerged during the investigation.

title: Five hour fire battle raged at plastic factory
description: Firefighters also faced difficulties in reaching the factory as the roads leading to premises were extremely narrow
content:
Firefighters also faced difficulties in reaching the factory as the roads leading to premises were extremely narrow
Firefighters battled a major blaze at a plastic-bag manufacturing factory in the SITE Area for more than five and a half hours before bringing it under control.
The fire, which broke out around 11.20pm on Sunday, was doused at 5am with the deployment of 12 Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) fire tenders, a snorkel, two water bowsers and a fire truck from Rescue 1122.
Chief Fire Officer Humayun Khan said the blaze was declared a third-degree fire because of its intensity, prompting the mobilisation of firefighting vehicles from across the metropolis.
"The intensity of the fire continued to increase, which is why it was declared a third-degree blaze," Khan told the media. He added that firefighters had to use foam after water alone failed to contain the flames.
The factory, spread over around 2,500 square yards, contained large quantities of plastic granules and plastic rolls used to manufacture Chinese shopping bags. The presence of highly combustible material contributed to the intensity of the blaze.
Firefighters also faced difficulties in reaching the factory as the roads leading to the premises were extremely narrow, according to the chief fire officer.
Seven fire tenders were initially dispatched to the site, but additional vehicles were called in as the blaze intensified. Rescue 1122 teams also participated in the firefighting operation.

title: Govt  MQM P trade barbs over MDCAT merit
description: Govt  MQM P trade barbs over MDCAT merit
content:
Sattar alleges bias against Karachi students; Sharjeel rejects politics over children
The Sindh government and opposition MQM-P traded barbs on Monday over alleged irregularities in the MDCAT examination 2026, with Dr Farooq Sattar accusing the government and IBA Sukkur of compromising merit, while Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon dismissed the allegations as political point-scoring.
Sattar alleged that paper leaks, nepotism and poor arrangements had jeopardised the future of Karachi students and warned that MQM-P would approach the Sindh High Court if their grievances were not addressed.
Speaking at a press conference at the MQM-P headquarters in Bahadurabad, Sattar, accompanied by Deputy Parliamentary Leader Taha Ahmed Khan and other party lawmakers, demanded that the MDCAT question papers and answer keys be made public and an impartial inquiry be launched into the alleged irregularities.
He said the National Testing Service (NTS) had conducted the MDCAT examination from 2009 to 2019 for a fee of Rs1,500 without major complaints, but alleged that the system had deteriorated since examinations began being conducted through IBA Sukkur and Dow University.
Sattar claimed that out of 133,000 candidates across Sindh, around 12,000 were from Karachi but only two examination centres - Dow University's Ojha Campus and NED University - had been designated for them.
He alleged that around 6,000 candidates were accommodated at each centre and many had to leave their homes at around 4am to reach the venues. Students, he claimed, were made to sit in open areas in extreme heat without adequate drinking water, resulting in a large number of candidates fainting.
"Despite charging Rs9,000 as examination fee, IBA Sukkur and the Sindh government are playing with the future of Karachi's students," he alleged.
He warned that if the government failed to address the complaints, MQM-P would join affected students in approaching the SHC to challenge the MDCAT results and provide them with legal assistance.
Responding to the allegations, Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon said the government would not allow politics to be played over the future of children.
Reacting to Sattar's press conference, Sharjeel said the Sindh government did not discriminate between students from Karachi and Thar and rejected what he described as attempts to divide children into "ours and theirs".
He challenged Sattar to produce evidence instead of making allegations regarding irregularities in the MDCAT examination.
Sharjeel also rejected any attempt to link the Red Line BRT construction work with the MDCAT results, saying the two issues had no connection.
He accused the MQM-P of having promoted a culture of weapons, extortion, fear and violence in Karachi for political interests, adding that such politics should no longer be allowed to push the city's youth towards division.
The senior minister said Karachi's young people were now turning towards education and progress and should not be dragged back into old divisions. "If a student from Thar gets higher marks, the focus should be on enabling more children across Sindh to achieve similar success on merit," he added.
