title: No let up in French protests
description: No let up in French protests
content:
Teenager's hand blown off as violence flares
A teenager's hand was blown off as high-school protesters clashed with riot police in northern France on Monday, a local official said, on the eve of a national demonstration by the pupils' union against underfunding, overcrowding and dilapidation.
The regional newspaper La Voix du Nord said the 15-year-old lost his hand and part of his lower arm after picking up a police dispersal grenade that detonated in the town of Lens as the wave of school protests entered its third week.
François-Xavier Lauch, prefect of Pas-de-Calais, declined to comment on the exact circumstances, saying some 200 to 250 protesters had been hurling objects at police.
Six months before an election to replace President Emmanuel Macron, his government and the far-right National Rally, led by presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen, have accused hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) lawmakers and mayors of stoking the protests. The LFI denies the accusation.
Speaking after meeting with students in the northern Paris suburbs, Education Minister Edouard Geffray said participation in the protests had been declining in recent days.
The government would launch a platform for students to express their dissatisfaction and kick off an action plan for particular schools, he said.
Rights groups accuse police of using heavy-handed tactics against minors, including batons, tear gas and flash-ball guns.

title: Ex prince Andrew takes police to court
description: Ex prince Andrew takes police to court
content:
King's younger brother in judicial review of police warrants
King Charles' younger brother, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, is taking the police to court to challenge warrants connected to his arrest on suspicion of misconduct in public office over allegations he sent government documents to Jeffrey Epstein.
Britain's Judicial Office, part of the non-political civil service, said on Monday a hearing would take place on Thursday after the former prince sought to quash the search warrants issued as part of his arrest in February.
The judicial office gave only limited information about the grounds for the callenge to the warrants. Legal experts said even a successful challenge on technical grounds might not halt the wider investigation into the former prince's conduct.
The second son of the late Queen Elizabeth has denied any wrongdoing in relation to Epstein, and said he regrets their friendship. His lawyer did not respond to a request for comment.
He was arrested on suspicion of leaking confidential government documents to the late convicted sex-offender Epstein when the then-prince served as a British special representative for trade, between 2001 and 2011. Police have not charged him and the investigation is ongoing.
The arrest of Mountbatten-Windsor, and the anger over his relationship with Epstein, has left the British royal family facing one of its worst crises in 90 years.
A Palace source said Andrew had been told that money provided from private funds by his brother the king should not be used to fund his legal challenge.
Thames Valley Police, which carried out the arrest, confirmed it was engaged in legal proceedings in relation to warrants it had obtained. The police force declined further comment.

content:
The United States on Monday announced the approval of a $1 billion sale to the United Arab Emirates of up to 10,000 Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System guidance sections for rockets.
"The proposed sale will improve the United Arab Emirates' capability to meet current and future threats by developing and maintaining a strong and ready self-defense capability and improving interoperability with US forces," the US State Department said in a statement.
It "will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a major defense partner," the statement added.
The Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System converts unguided rockets into precision munitions that can be employed for purposes including shooting down drones, thereby avoiding the use of costly missiles to shoot down comparatively cheap aircraft.
The UAE and other US-allied Gulf countries have been hard hit by the Iran war, during which Tehran's forces have repeatedly targeted them with both drones and missiles.

title: US moves bombers out from UK
description: US moves bombers out from UK
content:
Vice President Vance describes move as 'precaution'
US Vice President JD Vance said on Monday that the decision to move B-1 bombers from a British airbase was done out of an abundance of caution after a suspected Iranian plot at the site last week.
The planes had been stationed at RAF Fairford, the preferred European base for US bombers, and had recently been used in US strikes on Iran. Last week, five British men were arrested near the base - which Iran's Revolutionary Guards previously said was a legitimate target - on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts.
"So, what you saw there is the Secretary of War, out of an abundance of caution, trying to protect our guys," Vance said as he left Washington for a trip to Alaska.
"We do feel with some confidence that the Iranians are, you know, they're trying to do what the Iranian state has done for 49 years, which is engaged in acts of terrorism against the United States (and others), so we are being extremely cautious, and that's all I'd say about that."
Earlier, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was no direct link between the sudden removal of the bombers and the suspected Iranian plot. He said the Pentagon is "constantly reallocating resources where they need to be."
A NATO military source had said on Monday: "It is still believed that Iran poses an acute threat to US assets in the UK".
While much about the incident remains unexplained, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said any plot was likely backed by Iran.
Iran has said accusations that it was involved in any plot are baseless, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi wrote on X: "I can confirm Iran's belief that releasing supposed terrorists working for foreign states really says it all. You're barking up the wrong tree."
Rubio said on Monday the US had confidence in the security of all its bases.
Fairford, located 90 miles (145 km) west of London, is one of the most important in Europe for the US, being one of only a few suitable for heavy bombers such as the B-1 aircraft. It has played a key role in previous US campaigns in the Middle East, although its bombers are not stationed there permanently.
During the current conflict, the US had permission to use Fairford only to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz, or so-called defensive strikes. London had refused permission for the US to use British bases for offensive strikes on Iran.
That approach has strained ties between the US and Britain, typically one of Washington's closest allies.
A Pentagon official confirmed on Sunday that all US bombers which had been deployed to Fairford had headed to their home stations in the US.
The Pentagon said the US bomber force remained ready to deliver precision global strike capabilities "anywhere, anytime".

title: Spain goes for snap elections
description: Spain goes for snap elections
content:
Sanchez gambles on housing protests rare boost
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Monday called an early election for November 29, aiming to increase his parliamentary support after lawmakers last week rejected proposals to address a housing crisis that has drawn nationwide protests.
The snap vote is a high-stakes gamble for Sanchez, whose Socialist Party trails in nearly every opinion poll. An electoral defeat would spell the end of one of Europe's last remaining left-leaning governments at a time when the far right is making unprecedented gains across the region.
It reflects a broader malaise across Europe, under pressure from US President Donald Trump on defence spending, cheap Chinese imports, higher borrowing costs, disaffected youth and the biggest surge in support for the far-right since the 1930s.
However, Sanchez, a wily political operator, has proven time and again his ability to surprise those who had long written him off. An election now could see him capitalise on a wave of anger at unaffordable housing in Spain.
"We need to mobilise and win a much larger progressive majority in parliament, one that will allow us to overcome vested interests, deliver new social advances and continue transforming Spain," Sanchez said in a televised address.
Spain's blue-chip index .IBEX was flat after the announcement, while Spanish government bonds were broadly steady.
Alberto Nuñez Feijoo, leader of the opposition People's Party, on Monday pledged to almost double homebuilding in Spain to 200,000 units a year and cut taxes if he gained power.
"Housing has been this government's great failure and must be the next one's success. When a prime minister has been in office for eight years, it is very difficult to blame others for what he has failed to do," Feijoo said at a small business conference.
Sanchez has made a name internationally with progressive stances on issues from Palestinian statehood to defending multilateral institutions and cracking down on "tech oligarchs", even as a series of scandals weakened his position at home.

title: US  German scientists win Nobel medicine prize
description: US  German scientists win Nobel medicine prize
content:
Trio selected for their technique that helps decode mysteries of brain
American Karl Deisseroth and Germans Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine on Monday for developing optogenetics, a technique that uses light to control individual nerve cells in the brain.
The Nobel Assembly of Sweden's Karolinska Institutet said Deisseroth, 54; Hegemann, 71; and Nagel, 73, had been selected for their "discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics".
"This method makes it possible to switch on, or off, the activity of individual nerve cells in a living brain," said Thomas Perlmann, Secretary-General of the Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet.
Anna Wedell, a professor in genetics and a member of the Nobel Committee for Physiology or Medicine, said a new era in neuroscience had opened but it was only the beginning.
"For the first time we can actually start to understand how the brain processes information and how different neurons interact across the brain," she said.
The trio will share a prize sum of 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million). Announcements will follow in the coming days on this year's Nobel physics, chemistry, literature, peace and economics prizes, with the winner or winners of the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to be announced on Friday.
Deisseroth said he was still awake in the early hours when he was called from Stockholm.
"I was not yet asleep, being a night owl, and now I don't think I'll be able to sleep for quite a while," he said.
Hegemann said he was overwhelmed at getting a call from a number he recognized to be in Sweden: "It's unbelievable when you get this message."
Nagel said he was sitting on a terrace "in a nice little village outside Naples" when the call came through.
"I actually thought it would not happen, but some other people always told me this will happen," Nagel said.
Deisseroth was training to become a neurosurgeon when he encountered patients he could not help at a psychiatric clinic. That encounter – witnessing suffering he had no tools to treat – prompted a career-defining question: Why does the brain work so differently in different people?
The answer would come from an unexpected place: an alga, and two German scientists driven by equally simple curiosity.
Hegemann, fascinated by exploration and unknown territory, began investigating in the early 1990s how the alga Chlamydomonas reacts to light in half a millisecond.
He hypothesized that a single protein both captured light and acted as an ion channel, and contacted Nagel to ask him to test it.
"This was a good chance to do something new and exciting," Nagel said of the original call from Hegemann, which resulted in him injecting Chlamydomonas genes into frog eggs and discovering channelrhodopsin-2, a light-sensitive ion channel.
In 2003, Nagel and Hegemann published findings showing the protein could be introduced into human cells to generate electrical impulses using light. Deisseroth showed the technique in rat nerve cells in 2005, and the method was named optogenetics in 2006.
One scientist at Hegemann's Max Planck Institute in Frankfurt in 2007 recalled researchers taping optical fibers salvaged from Christmas decorations to microscopes.
"We didn't really know how it worked, we didn't really have any tools," said Dima Kuzmin, a neurochemist at the time. "And it was massively exciting."
The three laureates' research is now providing insights about brain disorders. Animal models are being used to understand schizophrenia, Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, epilepsy and addiction – conditions that affect millions of people worldwide and have limited treatment options.
Deisseroth used optogenetics to control the movements of mouse whiskers by activating specific nerve cells in the motor cortex. He also used light to wake sleeping mice, confirming that specific nerve cells control wakefulness.
"There are mouse models of dementia, epilepsy, addiction," Wedell said. "By understanding which cells are active in these diseases in mice, we can understand where to look in humans."

The investigation team told the court that the case involved a serious and sensitive offence and that terrorism provisions had been added to the case on the recommendation of a Joint Investigation Team (JIT).

title: Traditional games fade as social media takes over
description: Traditional games fade as social media takes over
content:
Nearly 15 games that once brought free exercise, collective enjoyment disappear
Modern scientific development has pushed nearly 15 traditional games, some around 150 years old, played across Punjab towards extinction.
These free forms of physical exercise have gradually disappeared from streets and neighbourhoods.
These traditional games were once a distinctive feature of Punjab and were played daily in almost every street and neighbourhood. While boys played marbles and Pithu Garam, girls sitting nearby played Kikli, Gitte and Ishtapu.
The traditional games that have disappeared or are fading include wrestling, Malakhara, kabaddi, Gilli Danda, Pithu Garam, Langri Sher, Vanji, skipping rope, playing with small stones, marbles, Bandar Qila, Kikli, Ishtapu, hide-and-seek, Lukan Miti, Chor Sipahi and riding bicycle tyres.
These games were a major source of physical agility, strength and collective enjoyment.
The famous traditional game Gilli Danda involved a small wooden stick called a gilli and a larger stick. It involved aiming and competing to hit and throw the stick over a distance.
In Pithu Garam, pieces of stone were knocked down and then rearranged, while the opposing team tried to hit the players with a ball and get them out.
Khado Khondi was a traditional game similar to hockey and was played in open fields.
Kabaddi and Malakhara (wrestling) served as traditional arenas for demonstrating strength and endurance.
Aankh Micholi and Lukan Miti, traditional children's games, have now disappeared from the streets.
Kikli was a game played by girls. Two girls held each other's hands and moved around in a circle. A popular song was associated with the game: "Kikli Kaler Di, Pag Mere Veer Di, Dupatta Mere Bhai Da, Phatte Munh Jawai Da."
Another game, Hara Samandar, involved several girls standing in a circle with their arms linked, while one girl stood in the middle. The area within the circle was considered the sea. The girls forming the circle asked the girl in the middle how deep the water was. She would say ankle-deep, and they would respond with knee-deep, hand-deep and neck-deep before she would say, "I am drowning," and fall to the ground.
Ishtapu was played by both boys and girls in a small courtyard. A small bounded playing area was marked on the ground using a stone.
Lukan Miti was also played by both genders and required two teams. One team hid while the other searched for them, after a call was made.
Kokla Chhapaaki was another children's game played by both boys and girls. Children sat in a circle while one child carrying a piece of cloth moved around them singing. The game involved a kind of warning that children sitting in the circle should not look behind them. The cloth was dropped behind one of the children. If the child saw the player dropping it, they could catch them and take their place.
The song sung during the game was: "Kokla Chhapaaki Jumerat Aayi Ae, Jehra Agge Pichhe Vekhe, Ohdi Shaamat Aayi Ae."
Children used to run bicycle tyres through streets with sticks. In Langri Sher, a large square or circle was drawn and one boy or girl, acting as the "lame lion", tried to touch the other children inside.

title: Play on Khusrau s legacy charms spectators
description: Play on Khusrau s legacy charms spectators
content:
Presents life, work of historic literary figure of Subcontinent in entertaining format
"Amir Khusrau," the latest stage production by renowned writer and director Asma Butt, who holds the unique distinction of bringing historical figures and the Subcontinent's rich Sufi and literary heritage to life on stage, has captivated the hearts of the audience.
Presented by Dolphin Communications at the Pakistan National Council of the Arts (PNCA), the play received immense acclaim. At the conclusion of the play, the audience gave a standing ovation, applauding at length to honour Asma Butt, writer Arshad Chahal and the entire cast.
In fact, the play "Hazrat Amir Khusrau" managed to sustain the audience's interest throughout its performance as the spectators frequently expressed their appreciation for the artists' superb acting, the dialogue and the overall presentation.
Speaking to the media, director Asma Butt noted that Amir Khusrau was a towering figure in the subcontinent who was celebrated as a great Sufi, poet and musician. A disciple of Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya, he left a profound impact on the literary and cultural traditions of the region through his poetry in Persian and Hindavi. His mystical poetry remains an integral part of the Qawwali and musical tradition to this day.
While thanking the guests, Asma Butt mentioned that during a tour to India, where she was staging a play about Shah Hussain Madho Lal, she had the opportunity to visit the shrine of Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya. Hearing the mystical verses of Hazrat Amir Khusrau there further solidified her resolve to bring his persona and artistry to the stage. She stated that "Amir Khusrau" is the result of a collaborative effort and that she considers it her responsibility to introduce historical and cultural figures to the new generation.
On this occasion, guests and audience members praised Asma Butt's efforts to promote Pakistani culture and lauded the artists' outstanding performances. They remarked that by staging a play on Amir Khusraufollowing productions based on Shah Hussain Madho Lal, Heer Waris Shah, Saif-ul-Malook, and Dulla BhattiAsma Butt has carried forward a unique artistic tradition.
The play was written by Arshad Chahal and directed by Asma Ismail Butt. The cast included Kaleem Khan, Shahid Mughal, Sabir Khan, Shabbir Shah, Imran Rushdi, Neelam Arshad, Javeria, Noor Shararti, Khalil Noor, Faran Bajwa, Liaquat Shah, Noor Jahan, Simran Ali, Alisha Jahangir, Alishba Jahangir, Shazia Adeeb, and other artists. Vendor 'slapped, threatened and detained' during crackdown against plastic bags
An Islamabad police official allegedly subjected a shopkeeper to violence and threats during a crackdown on plastic shopping bags, with a video of the incident going viral on social media and traders demanding action against those responsible.
The incident happened in the Loi Bher police station area during a district administration campaign against plastic shopping bags. According to the affected shopkeeper, the official slapped him after finding several shopping bags at his shop, threatened him with serious consequences and took him to the police station.
The shopkeeper claimed that some of the bags found at his shop were among those permitted by the government.
Despite the video circulating widely on social media, neither the district administration nor the police initially issued an explanation regarding the incident.
All Pakistan Anjuman-e-Tajiran and Traders Action Committee Islamabad president Ajmal Baloch, Traders Action Committee Islamabad secretary Khalid Chaudhry and other market representatives strongly condemned the alleged treatment and demanded that the Interior Minister take notice of the matter.
The traders said a crackdown in the name of enforcing the plastic-bag ban had resulted in the humiliation and arrests of traders over the past three days. They demanded the immediate release of detained traders and an end to what they described as harassment.
Baloch questioned why authorities were not taking action against factories manufacturing illegal shopping bags, arguing that arresting and fining shopkeepers could not resolve the issue.
Chaudhry said the use of alleged self-appointed magistrates against traders was contrary to a High Court ruling. He demanded that the administration act strictly in accordance with the law.
The traders also claimed that bags confiscated from shopkeepers were later returned to markets for sale, while smuggled bags seized by customs authorities were auctioned and subsequently re-entered the market.
They urged the Environmental Protection Agency and district administration to launch a formal campaign promoting cloth bags and provide traders with viable alternatives instead of relying solely on punitive measures.
The traders warned that failure to release detained traders and end their alleged humiliation would lead to a decision on protests and a shutter-down strike.

title: Pakistan  Taliban clash at Moscow talks
description: Pakistan  Taliban clash at Moscow talks
content:
Tensions over cross-border terrorism derail joint statement
Simmering tensions between Pakistan and the Afghan Taliban regime overshadowed a regional conference on Afghanistan in Moscow on Monday, with the two sides trading sharp accusations over terrorism and cross-border attacks and failing to agree on a joint statement.
The breakdown marked a significant setback for the Moscow Format, a Russia-led regional mechanism established in 2017 to build consensus on Afghanistan. It was the first time since the inaugural meeting that participants failed to issue a joint statement.
The eighth meeting brought together senior representatives from Russia, Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Iran, India and Central Asian states to discuss Afghanistan's political, security and economic situation, including counterterrorism and regional connectivity. Belarus and Egypt attended as guests.
But the worsening confrontation between Islamabad and Kabul quickly became the dominant issue.
Pakistan was represented by Special Representative for Afghanistan Ambassador Mohammad Sadiq, while the Taliban delegation was led by Acting Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi.
Addressing the meeting, Sadiq delivered a blunt assessment of the security situation, putting terrorism at the centre of Pakistan's concerns.
"Terrorism remains at the core of Afghanistan's problems, with roots in the nexus between the Taliban Regime and terrorist groups," Sadiq said, according to the transcript of his statement.
He specifically referred to the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan and other terrorist organisations operating from Afghan territory. "Over the last three years alone, more than 4,700 innocent Pakistanis have lost their lives to terrorism emanating from Afghanistan," Sadiq said.
He accused the Taliban regime of being complicit in the problem and defended Pakistan's military operations inside Afghanistan as acts of self-defence.
"The Taliban regime is complicit in this," Sadiq said, describing Pakistan's counterstrikes as "precise, intelligence-based and defensive in nature."
The Pakistani position effectively challenged the narrative Kabul has been presenting to regional countries that the recent escalation is primarily the result of Pakistani action against Afghanistan.
Muttaqi, in his address, took the opposite position, accusing Pakistan of relying on military pressure rather than diplomacy.
He said Kabul wanted its disputes with Islamabad resolved through dialogue and diplomacy and rejected what he described as a policy of accusations, propaganda and military action.
"Our fundamental position is that the existing problems between Afghanistan and Pakistan, whether security, political or economic, can be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy," Muttaqi said.
The Taliban foreign minister also maintained that Afghanistan had the right to defend itself against aggression and insisted that Kabul would formulate its domestic and foreign policies independently rather than under external pressure.
The sharply contrasting positions made agreement on language concerning terrorism virtually impossible.
Russia's special presidential envoy for Afghanistan, Zamir Kabulov, later confirmed that the dispute between the Pakistani and Afghan delegations prevented the participants from adopting the final document.
"When drafting the final joint statement, we encountered one problem - that problem was that our Afghan and Pakistani colleagues didn't see eye to eye. We regret this," Kabulov said.
He explained that the Afghan side objected to the draft because it referred to Afghanistan too frequently in the context of terrorism. Kabulov noted that similar wording had been used in the statement issued after last year's meeting.
Kabulov nevertheless said the failure to issue a statement would not spell the end of the Moscow Format, arguing that the platform could continue to function despite the disagreement.
The failure to forge a regional consensus was accompanied by unusually strong Russian support for the Taliban government. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, who opened the meeting, praised the Taliban's performance since its return to power in 2021 and described it as a "national government".
"The national government led by the Taliban movement came to power and it put under control the territory of the country, and we should recognize that it has been successfully ruling it," Lavrov said.
Lavrov also praised the Taliban for its efforts against Da'ish and other extremist groups and for combating drug trafficking.
He welcomed what he described as the Taliban government's achievements after the withdrawal of US and NATO forces, while reiterating Moscow's opposition to any return of Western military infrastructure to Afghanistan or neighbouring states.
"I'd like to highlight that we have zero tolerance to the deployment of NATO military infrastructure in the territory of Afghanistan and/or in neighboring countries under any pretext whatsoever," Lavrov said.
Russia has already gone further than other major powers in its engagement with Kabul. Moscow formally recognised the Taliban administration in 2025, making it the first country to do so.
The Russian position at the Moscow meeting therefore stood in marked contrast to Pakistan's emphasis on the Taliban's links with terrorist groups operating against Pakistan.
The meeting also highlighted a broader problem for the regional approach to Afghanistan: countries that once broadly agreed on the need for an inclusive, stable and secure Afghanistan are increasingly divided over how to deal with the Taliban regime and, more importantly, how to assess the security threat emanating from Afghan territory.
The collapse of the joint statement in Moscow has therefore exposed not merely a Pakistan-Afghanistan disagreement, but a widening gap among regional powers regarding Afghanistan's future and how to deal with the Taliban regime.

title: ICC unseals warrants against Taliban supremo  top aides
description: ICC unseals warrants against Taliban supremo  top aides
content:
Court accuses supreme leader, CJ, two education ministers of crimes against humanity
The International Criminal Court (ICC) on Monday unsealed arrest warrants for four senior Afghan Taliban officials accused of crimes against humanity through policies targeting women and girls, detailing allegations of gender-based persecution and severe violations of fundamental rights and freedoms.
The ICC had authorised warrants in July 2025 against Taliban Supreme Leader Haibatullah Akhundzada and Supreme Court President Abdul Hakim Haqqani. The warrants against Education Minister Habibullah Agha and Higher Education Minister Neda Mohammad Nadeem were issued in September 2025.
The court said on Monday that Akhundzada and Haqqani had implemented a governmental policy resulting in severe violations of the fundamental rights and freedoms of Afghanistan's civilian population, involving alleged murder, imprisonment, torture, rape and enforced disappearance.
The judges further said the two ministers were accused of implementing policies that barred girls from attending school beyond primary level and excluded women from higher education following the Taliban's return to power in August 2021.
Both Agha and Nadeem were instrumental in implementing the supreme leader's vision for Afghanistan, according to the court. The warrants against the education ministers are also linked to the Taliban's restrictions on women and girls' access to education.
The court said there were "reasonable grounds to believe" that the suspects had committed "the crime against humanity of persecution on gender grounds", targeting "women and girls, and other persons whose gender expression or identity was viewed as inconsistent with the Taliban's policy on gender".
The ICC said women and girls had been specifically targeted by restrictions on their rights to education, freedom of expression and freedom of movement, although the Taliban had imposed strict rules and prohibitions on the wider Afghan population.
The ICC's Pre-Trial Chamber II said it had decided to unseal all four warrants, with redactions, after concluding that publication would not unduly affect ongoing investigations. It said making the warrants public could also "promote cooperation by the international community, including State Parties, in relation to the situation in Afghanistan".
The warrants are likely to increase international pressure on the Taliban government in Afghanistan, where the higher education ban has also contributed to staff shortages in hospitals, as women are no longer able to qualify as doctors.
Afghan women and girls have faced sweeping restrictions on education and public life since the Taliban returned to power. Girls have been barred from secondary education while women have been excluded from universities, leaving Afghan universities as male-only institutions.
Afghans across the country have told AFP journalists about severe mental health problems linked to the education ban, with teenage girls and women largely confined to their homes. Some women and girls have sought to continue their education online, but internet and electricity problems have hampered their efforts.
Women are also increasingly absent from public life and must follow strict dress requirements when leaving home. They are banned from most jobs and a range of public places, including parks, and must be accompanied by a close male relative on long journeys.
According to UN figures cited in the reports, half of Afghan women now leave their homes only once or twice a month, reflecting restrictions on their freedom of movement and participation in public life. Afghanistan remains the only country where girls are banned from secondary education and women are prohibited from attending university, according to UN Women.
The ICC's move comes amid continuing international concern over the Taliban's treatment of women and girls and provides fuller details of allegations that had previously been disclosed only in broad terms when the court confirmed the existence of the warrants last year.

title: Bilawal says Thar could run Islamabad
description: Bilawal says Thar could run Islamabad
content:
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari on Monday turned the argument over the "failure of the existing system" on its head, saying that if Islamabad had indeed failed, its governance should instead be handed over to Tharparkar, which he said had transformed itself through development.
In an indirect reference to the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P)-led campaign for the creation of new administrative units, Bilawal equated the party's agenda with Zionism, saying he could not understand the logic behind the argument.
"I feel very sad to see a party of political orphans which practises politics of hatred, division and Zionism, wants to introduce Zionist politics in Sindh," he said while addressing the inauguration ceremony of the third phase of the Thar coal project in Tharparkar district. "But I want to tell them that they will fail."
While presenting Tharparkar as a model of development for the country's major cities, Bilawal criticised proponents of new provinces for "forcibly" advancing the contentious argument that the existing system had collapsed while presenting smaller provinces as a remedy.
"I want to tell them that though I can't understand this logic, even if, for the sake of argument, I subscribe to it, their logic will mean that if Islamabad has failed, the capital should be handed over to Tharparkar," he told the gathering.
The PPP chairman said Tharparkar had even outshone major cities of Pakistan in terms of the pace of progress. He cited the brilliant performance of students from Tharparkar in the Medical and Dental College Admission Test (MDCAT) 2026 and rejected criticism of the test results.
"It should be a matter of pride for the country that children of a formerly underdeveloped district are excelling in the national exams. People of Pakistan should have rather congratulated them," he said. He also mentioned a student from Tharparkar who topped an examination in China.
"We will ensure that children of Islamabad also excel in exams like children in Tharparkar," he said. He went on to demand that Islamabad's governance be handed over so that his party and "the brilliant people of Tharparkar" could transform the capital. "This is the way forward if we follow your logic."
Bilawal inaugurated the third phase of the Thar coal project. Under the expansion, coal mining will be enhanced to 11.2 million metric tons per annum (MTPA) from the existing 7.6 million MTPA, which was attained in 2022 during the second phase. The first phase, with 3.8 million MTPA, was started in 2019.
Bilawal said that development driven by the Public Private Partnership (PPP) model had become an example worth emulating across the country. He maintained that the development envisioned in the 1973 Constitution and the 18th Constitutional Amendment had materialised in Tharparkar.
He recalled that Thar's coal initially produced 660 megawatts (MW) of electricity, but generation had now more than trebled to around 2,000MW, which he said was 14% of the country's total power generation. He credited Thar with saving $1.6 billion in foreign exchange that would otherwise have to be spent annually on coal imports.
He recalled that detractors of the Thar coal project used to criticise the quality of the coal as being unsuitable for power generation, but now "not only is electricity being produced from coal, but fertiliser and gas production" are also on the cards.
The PPP chief invited the business community to invest in projects under the PPP model in Karachi and other parts of the country to bolster development and generate employment, in addition to securing business benefits.
He said the Sindh government and the Defence Housing Authority (DHA) were going to undertake a mega development project in Karachi under the PPP model. He also expressed interest in establishing a new port at Keti Bunder in Thatta district, inviting investors to come forward for the projects.
During his visit to the district, Bilawal also visited the SECMC coal mine, Thar Foundation's hospital and school, and interacted with the local community. He was accompanied by Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah.

title: Afridi doubles down on  absolutely not
description: Afridi doubles down on  absolutely not
content:
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday doubled down on his "Absolutely Not" stance against the powerful, declaring that he would continue to stand with his people and resist policies that he believes are against the interests of the province and the country.
"I am Imran Khan's team member. I have said 'Absolutely Not' to the powerful, and I will continue to stand by that position," Afridi said while addressing participants of the PTI's long march at Jail Chowk in Karak. The K-P CM kicked off the PTI's much-touted long march from Lakki Marwat a day earlier.
His remarks came as he accused the federal government and the establishment of pursuing policies that were deepening divisions, isolating K-P and treating it as a stepchild.
Afridi said he had been criticised on television and labelled "immature" by an establishment representative for standing with his people.
"If standing with my people is considered immaturity, then I will continue to do so without hesitation. If loving my country is considered immaturity, I will embrace that charge again and again," he said.
The chief minister alleged that terrorism imposed on Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was the result of a deliberate and well-conceived plan, saying Pashtun blood was once again being shed, people were being displaced, businesses destroyed and military operations and drone strikes carried out.
He said innocent civilians, police personnel and soldiers were losing their lives, while his government was being pressured to become complicit in policies it did not support.
Afridi said misguided policies were pushing the country towards division and fuelling prejudice among its people. He alleged that Rs5.3 trillion had been lost to corruption under the federal government's watch and that the figure had been reported by the International Monetary Fund.
"If this is what is being presented as wisdom and patriotism, then I reject such wisdom," he said.
He alleged that those imposed on the country were attempting to compound one flawed policy with another in an effort to isolate Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. Referring to decisions taken behind closed doors, he also criticised what he described as the imposition of a political party on the country.
"As long as we are alive, we will never allow this to happen," he said. Afridi maintained that those who plundered public resources could not claim to be sincere with the country.
Turning to PTI founder Imran Khan, the chief minister said he was the only leader with a nationwide following and capable of steering Pakistan out of its present crisis.
"Imran Khan is the heartbeat of our people, and 90 percent of the people want him," he claimed. "Imran is the only leader capable of restoring the dignity, credibility and standing of state institutions."
Afridi also praised soldiers who had sacrificed their lives for Pakistan, describing their sacrifices as an integral part of the nation's collective struggle and existence.
He claimed that public rejection of the existing system was growing across the country, with people from Khyber to Karachi seeking to reach Islamabad. He said the government would have to address their democratic demands and that national policies must be guided by the public interest.
The chief minister said his government would resist any policy contrary to the interests of the people.
He said Imran Khan was enduring imprisonment with courage and had refused to compromise his position for the sake of power. Had Khan been motivated by a desire to return to office, Afridi said, he could have secured his release by signing a document, but had instead chosen to remain steadfast.
"The struggle for real freedom will continue alongside Imran Khan," he said, adding that Imran and his family were making sacrifices for the future of the people and generations to come.
Referring to the 26th Constitutional Amendment, Afridi alleged that courts now awaited instructions before taking decisions, while Imran Khan continued to await his people.
"The choice is yours: whether to accept subjugation or stand for real freedom; whether to bow before the powerful or stand up for your rights," he said. The chief minister called upon people from across Pakistan to reach Swabi, where he said the next phase of the movement would be announced.
Later, speaking to long-march participants in Lachi tehsil of Kohat, Afridi reiterated his defiant position.
"I am a soldier of Imran Khan. The combined strength of the entire world cannot put a price on me, nor can it intimidate me," he said. He urged participants to conserve their energy, saying the struggle would be prolonged and require endurance and sustained mobilisation.
"We must not exhaust ourselves. Our struggle is a long one. From October 8, the T20 match begins," he said. Afridi announced that the march towards Peshawar would set off from University Chowk at 3pm and called on the people of Kohat to turn out in overwhelming numbers.
"The message must go out clearly: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa belongs to Imran Khan, has belonged to Imran Khan, and will remain with Imran Khan," he said.

title: PTI  talks deadlocked over Imran access  K P policy

content:
Gohar, Raja say govt's inflexibility caused breakdown; party keeps door to negotiations open
PTI leaders Salman Akram Raja and Barrister Gohar Khan said on Monday that negotiations with the government had reached a deadlock because of the ruling side's refusal to meet key party demands, particularly access to incarcerated founder Imran Khan and consultation on counter-terrorism policy in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), but maintained that the door to dialogue remained open.
Addressing separate press conferences in Islamabad and Swat, the two leaders said the government still had time to revive the talks by allowing the PTI leadership and family members to meet Imran Khan.
They rejected the impression that the deadlock was linked to K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, saying the government had shown no flexibility during the negotiations.
Speaking to the media in Islamabad, Raja said the PTI had two major demands, one of which was access to its founder, adding that the party would not take any decision without consulting Imran Khan.
"There was no agreement to include Imran's personal physician, Dr Faisal Sultan, in the panel of people allowed to meet him," Raja said, adding that meetings between Imran, his family and doctors remained important, particularly amid concerns about his health.
"How could the negotiations have succeeded without them?" he asked.
The PTI secretary general said the issue of terrorism in K-P was the other central point of disagreement. He said the party wanted a consensus-based approach to counter-terrorism measures, with all relevant political and tribal stakeholders taken on board.
He referred to a peace jirga that brought together representatives of political parties and tribal elders to discuss the situation in former tribal areas, arguing that decisions affecting the region could not be taken from a distance.
He maintained that the government had not accepted the PTI demand for consultation with all stakeholders, despite discussions during the negotiations that decisions concerning the tribal areas would be taken through consensus.
Raja said the PTI wanted peace and order to be maintained in the country and had not closed the door to negotiations. The party, he added, would continue its political struggle for "love, respect, the rule of law and the Constitution, and peace".
He recalled telling the government during the negotiations that he and his daughters would come out carrying flowers rather than weapons.
"We are not armed people. We still say that distances should not be created from closeness," Raja said, adding that the two sides had come close to resolving their differences before "suddenly that closeness was turned into distance".
In Swat, Gohar said the government still had an opportunity to restart the negotiations by facilitating a meeting between Imran and the PTI leadership. He warned that any attempt to impose governor's rule or emergency in K-P would have serious repercussions for law and order across the country.
Gohar alleged that the federal government was attempting to paralyse the provincial administration despite the PTI securing more than 20 million votes. He claimed that police and administration were not extending the required cooperation to elected provincial representatives.
He further alleged that two provincial ministers, as well as members of the national and provincial assemblies, had been arrested or allegedly abducted, while the federal government was accusing the provincial administration of non-cooperation.
Gohar said the PTI's provincial government was making efforts at its own level to combat terrorism, while accusing the federal government of failing to play its required role. He also claimed that K-P had not received even Rs10 from the Rs10 billion package announced by the government.
He clarified that Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had no role in the deadlock in the negotiations and that the government had demonstrated no flexibility during the talks.
Gohar said the PTI's announced long march towards Islamabad would remain peaceful and that workers would carry Pakistani flags. The party, he added, would continue its struggle through constitutional, democratic and political means.
He also criticised the government over the arrests of Imran's sisters, saying that despite the difficulties faced by the party, the PTI remained prepared for negotiations and a political solution.
The government and PTI had begun negotiations on Friday in an attempt to defuse tensions over the party's planned October 4 long march.
The government wanted the PTI to call off the march, while the opposition sought political consensus on its demands and maintained that the protest would proceed unless its concerns were addressed.
The two sides held a second round of talks on Saturday under National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq. They initially agreed on a five-point framework covering legal facilities for Imran and his wife, early hearings of pending cases, and meetings with lawyers and family members.
According to a report, the talks subsequently stalled over counter-terrorism operations in K-P and access to Imran, ending without an agreement in the early hours of Sunday and paving the way for the PTI to proceed with the first phase of its long march.

title: PM approves plan to boost livestock exports
description: PM approves plan to boost livestock exports
content:
PM approves plan to boost livestock exports
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif Monday approved a plan to boost livestock exports by importing livestock, rearing them in specialised farms and subsequently exporting them.
The development came as the premier chaired a high-level review meeting regarding ongoing reforms in the livestock sector in Islamabad.
He stressed that import of livestock for these specialised farms should be duty-free.
The premier also approved restructuring of the livestock sector along corporate lines and formulating and implementing reforms through private sector experts.
Specialised farms should be established for livestock exports, the prime minister said, adding that high-yield, superior-breed livestock should be imported and reared in these specialized farms for export purposes.
He emphasised that a modern livestock tagging system should be introduced to ensure that the livestock reared in these farms are indeed exported.
The livestock sector should be reorganised on a corporate model to modernize it, he added.
The premier noted that expertise from private sector specialists should be utilised for the purpose.
Livestock accounts for over 60 per cent of the country's agricultural sector, and the sector holds immense export potential, he said adding that a comprehensive plan with specific targets for eradicating Foot-and-Mouth Disease from the country should be formulated and presented within the next two weeks.
The premier stated that international certification of slaughterhouses across the country must be ensured.
Third-party validation must be ensured to guarantee international standards at slaughterhouses, he maintained, adding that the Ministry of National Food Security should work in collaboration with provincial governments to eradicate livestock diseases.
He said efforts should be made to improve the entire value chain to further develop the meat and livestock export industry.
The prime minister directed that targets for meat, livestock, and related exports be determined and presented.
The meeting was given a detailed briefing on the livestock sector, and proposals regarding the future roadmap for the sector's development and the enhancement of exports were presented.
Regarding the overall potential of Pakistan's livestock sector, the meeting was informed that the country possesses approximately 245 million livestock, with a total estimated value of around Rs 5.5 trillion.
The livestock sector contributes 14.97% to the national economy and 63.6% to the agricultural economy, with an annual production of approximately 74.69 million tons of milk and 6.31 million tons of meat.
It was noted that while around 8 million rural families in the country are associated with livestock, the prevalence of small-scale livestock rearing and a fragmented supply chain hinder the full utilization of export potential.
The meeting was informed that there is immense potential to significantly increase Pakistan's meat exports. Meat exports stood at approximately $530 million in the 2025-26 fiscal year, with the bulk of current exports destined for Gulf countries, including the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Qatar.
It was noted that Malaysia, Saudi Arabia, China, and other nations offer significant prospects as new and expanding markets.
The meeting was also briefed on government initiatives to boost livestock and meat exports. These include the national programme for animal disease surveillance, protection, and animal traceability; the establishment of Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD)-free zones and compartments; digital monitoring of vaccinations and diseases; and the development of export-grade farms alongside international health and Halal certification systems.
Furthermore, the meeting was apprised that the government is focusing on promoting feedlot farming, cold chain infrastructure, de-boning, value-added products, and export-related infrastructure, with a target set to further increase meat exports by 2028.
Federal Ministers Rana Tanveer Hussain, Ahsan Iqbal, Dr. Musadik Malik, Ahad Khan Cheema, Muhammad Aurangzeb, and Attaullah Tarar; Prime Minister's Advisor Haroon Akhtar; Minister of State Bilal Azhar Kayani; and other relevant senior officials attended the meeting.

title: Houthis pushed back from Bab el Mandeb
description: Houthis pushed back from Bab el Mandeb
content:
Yemeni troops retake key coastal positions, advance towards Mocha; rebels make gains around Taiz
Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces launched a major counteroffensive on Monday, driving the rebel Houthi fighters from key positions around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and advancing towards Mocha, while the rebels tightened their grip around the strategic city of Taiz.
Government forces reached the outskirts of Mocha late on Monday, with four government sources saying Houthi fighters were retreating towards the highlands. Yemen's Defence Ministry said the city had fallen, although Reuters could not independently verify the extent of the government gains.
The forces had already seized key positions, including an airstrip in Dhubab district at the mouth of the strait, a vital oil route whose seizure by the Houthis last month sent shockwaves through energy markets. The Houthis rejected the government's claims as baseless.
The government said it had launched attacks on several fronts, while Yemen's military spokesman said government forces carried out more than 1,000 strikes against Houthi artillery and rocket-launcher positions, defensive fortifications, supply lines and logistics assets.
Despite the offensive, the Houthis continued to make gains around Taiz, according to government military sources. The group captured sections of a mountain road, leaving government forces in the city increasingly isolated, although one government source denied that the road had been cut.
The Houthis also warned that Saudi airspace was unsafe for civilian flights and would become a theatre of operations for their forces, according to the group's Saba news agency. Saudi Arabia said it had attacked hundreds of targets to provide air cover for government forces around Bab el-Mandeb.
The fighting has placed another major energy route at risk after Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz restricted Gulf energy exports. Control of Bab el-Mandeb could allow the Houthis to disrupt shipping between the Mediterranean and Indian Ocean.
Riyadh is backing the campaign as part of efforts to restore free traffic in the Red Sea and end Houthi attacks on its territory. The Houthis could still attack vessels with drones from positions farther up the coast and inland even if government forces regain the coastal area around the strait, according to the Reuters.
The strategic stakes were underscored by a fresh attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline. An energy-sector source told AFP that pumping was halted after a station east of Riyadh in Khurais was damaged in an attack.
The Houthis had claimed the previous day that they targeted sites belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco, including infrastructure in Khurais. The East-West pipeline runs about 1,200 kilometres between Saudi oilfields in the east and the Yanbu terminal on the Red Sea.
Meanwhile, the renewed fighting has deepened Yemen's humanitarian crisis. The UN migration agency said on Monday that 184,000 people had been displaced since the war resumed, while AFP cited UN figures putting the number at more than 145,000.
Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, has remained a major frontline since the civil war began. Government forces still control the city, but Houthi fighters have long besieged it from the north, east and west, according to AFP.
The conflict resumed after a 2022 ceasefire held for several years. The Houthis seized Sanaa in 2014 and subsequently took control of much of northern Yemen, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene the following year in support of the internationally recognised government.

title: Pakistan  KSA  Turkiye activate Makkah pact
description: Pakistan  KSA  Turkiye activate Makkah pact
content:
Decide immediate deployment of military capabilities Condemn attempted targeting of Makkah and Madina Appoint Na
In a major development that may have far-reaching implications for the region, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Monday activated the practical implementation of their collective defence commitments under the Makkah Alliance for Defence, a collective security arrangement signed in the holy city of Makkah on August 7.
According to a joint-statement issued on Monday night, the activation entails immediate deployment of "the agreed military forces and capabilities to the Kingdom in response to security threats".
The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of the Strategic-Political and Defense Committee of the alliance, held in Riyadh to discuss the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia is currently engaged in an active conflict with Houthis of Yemen who have been targeting the various strategic and economic assets in the Kingdom.
Without naming anyone, the emergency meeting condemned in the strongest terms the attempted targeting of Makkah and Madinah, as well as continuing attacks targeting cities and civilian and economic facilities in Saudi Arabia.
The three countries reaffirmed their unequivocal rejection of any attack or threat against the Kingdom's security and territorial integrity.
Pakistan and Turkiye also commended the vigilance and readiness of the Saudi Armed Forces and praised their professionalism and competence in countering threats and attacks against the Kingdom and safeguarding its security and territorial integrity.
The committee reviewed the outcomes of political and military consultations held ahead of the emergency meeting and approved the recommendations submitted to it.
It reaffirmed that the Makkah Alliance for Defense represented a firm commitment to collective defence and a unified position in confronting threats.
Under the decision, the three countries will immediately move towards practical implementation of their collective defence commitments and take necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities, ensuring their rapid deployment in Saudi Arabia.
The deployment will be carried out in accordance with approved arrangements and the national legislation of the three participating countries, the joint statement said.
These measures aim to enhance military readiness and integration and strengthen the collective capacity of the three countries to confront and counter threats.
The parties affirmed that the security of each member state is an integral part of the collective security of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.
The countries also decided to appoint Pakistan's Lt Gen (retd) Nauman Mahmood as the alliance's first secretary-general for a three-year term. The parties welcomed the appointment and expressed confidence that Lt Gen Nauman would contribute to advancing the alliance and achieving its objectives.
They said translating the Makkah Agreement into practical measures demonstrated the credibility of their commitment to collective defence, strengthened deterrence effectiveness, and reaffirmed their unity and determination to defend their security, sovereignty and territorial integrity.
The decisions were taken in accordance with the provisions of the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defense.
The emergency meeting occurred amid heightened security concerns in Saudi Arabia, with the three countries reiterating their commitment to collective action in protecting the Kingdom and responding to threats against its territory and vital facilities.
The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, formally the Makkah Alliance for Defence, is a defence pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye signed into force on August 7, 2026.
It builds upon the earlier Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed between Pakistan and KSA on September 17, 2025. The pact's ratification was officially announced amidst the US-Israel-Iran war.
The Makkah Alliance for Defence enshrines a collective security arrangement modelled on Article 5 of NATO, with its official announcement stating that "any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all".

title: Ahsan Bhoon s degrees are valid
description: Ahsan Bhoon s degrees are valid
content:
The University of the Punjab verifies LLB and BA degrees of renowned lawyer and bar leader
The University of the Punjab has verified the LLB and BA degrees of renowned lawyer Chaudhry Ahsan Bhoon, according to records available with the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC), as Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz's husband Capt (retd) Muhammad Safdar intensifies his campaign against the government-backed Independent Group and raises questions over its members' professional credentials.
It has transpired from records of the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC) that the University of the Punjab has verified both the LLB and BA degrees of Chaudhry Ahsan Bhoon, who has been publicly questioned by Capt (retd) Muhammad Safdar over his professional credentials.
According to the records, the PBC on December 19, 2025,wrote to the University of the Punjab seeking verification of the academic credentials of some of its members.
Attorney General for Pakistan Mansoor Awan, in his capacity as chairman of the PBC, had directed the verification of the LLB and BA degrees of candidates whose academic records were available with the bar council.
In response, the university administration, through the Controller of Examinations, informed PBC Secretary Gulzar Ahmad on January 21 that the LLB and BA degrees of six PBC members had been verified. A copy of the letter, now available with The Express Tribune, was also sent to the Higher Education Commission (HEC).
The university verified the degrees of six PBC members, including Minister for Law and Justice Azam Nazeer Tarar, Hafeez ur Rehman, Chaudhry Ahsan Bhoon, Tahir Nasrullah, Shafqat Mahmood and Syed Qalbi Hassan.
According to the University of the Punjab's letter, Ahsan Bhoon's roll number in the LLB examination was 828 and his registration number was 81-GCH-8. He secured 321 out of 700 marks, placing him in the second division. The LLB first annual examination of 1985 was held in March 1989.
The university also verified Bhoon's BA degree. The letter states that his roll number was 7563 and registration number 81-GCH-8. He obtained 406 out of 800 marks, securing a second division. The BA second annual examination of 1983 was held in July 1984.
It is learnt that, following a request from the PBC, the university had also verified the LLB degrees of six members, including Ahsan Bhoon, in January 2021.
Meanwhile, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz's husband, Capt (retd) Muhammad Safdar, has publicly questioned the professional credentials of presidential candidate Syed Amjad Shah and PBC leader Ahsan Bhoon.
Safdar has submitted a complaint to the secretary of the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP), seeking an inquiry into Bhoon's "educational certificate, enrollment and professional credentials".
In his complaint, Safdar alleged that information had come to his knowledge raising questions about the authenticity of the law degree on the basis of which Bhoon entered the legal profession. He claimed that the degree could allegedly be "fake, bogus or otherwise incapable of lawful verification".
Safdar urged the commission to call for and independently verify the original record, arguing that the matter could not be ignored as Bhoon was a sitting member of the JCP.
"The Commission considers the persons who may ultimately sit in judgment over the rights, liberties, property, and disputes of the people of Pakistan," Safdar said in his complaint.
The campaign has generated debate within legal circles over Safdar's repeated targeting of Amjad Shah and Bhoon and whether his campaign is being conducted independently or has the backing of the PML-N leadership.
It is learnt that one section of PML-N lawyers is fully backing Captain Safdar.

title: Students going abroad exempted from MDCAT
description: Those seeking to transfer to a Pakistani university in the middle of their studies would have to clear the NEB exam
content:
Those seeking to transfer to a Pakistani university in the middle of their studies would have to clear the NEB exam
Pakistani students planning to study medicine or dentistry abroad will no longer have to pass the Medical and Dental College Admission Test (MDCAT) as the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) has withdrawn the mandatory requirement following months of scrutiny over its legal basis and effectiveness.
The decision was taken at a PMDC meeting held on Sept 14 and formally announced by the council on Monday.
In a notice shared on X, the PMDC said the council "decided to exempt the mandatory requirement of having passed the MDCAT as a prerequisite for Pakistani students seeking admission into foreign medical and dental institutions."
The notice did not give any reason for the policy change.
PMDC President Dr Rizwan Taj said the decision followed a recommendation by a parliamentary committee that students intending to study abroad should not be required to take MDCAT.
However, students pursuing medical or dental education abroad would remain exempt from MDCAT. Those seeking to transfer to a university in Pakistan in the middle of their studies would have to clear the National Examination Board (NEB) assessment.
Students intending to practise in Pakistan after completing their education abroad would also have to pass the registration examination for foreign medical graduates.
The NEB is conducted by the PMDC twice a year for medical graduates who have passed their examinations abroad. The examination is designed to assess the knowledge, clinical skills and professional competence of students who have partially completed medical or dental education overseas and seek transfer to or admission in Pakistan.
In addition, graduates of foreign universities are required to appear in a registration examination to obtain a licence to
begin their house job and practise medicine or dentistry in Pakistan.

title: Defence minister blames PTI for K P security crisis
description: Defence minister blames PTI for K P security crisis
content:
Khawaja Asif accuses PTI of backing TTP talks
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Monday accused the PTI)of pursuing negotiations with the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), saying the party's policy had contributed to the security crisis in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.
In a detailed statement on X, Asif said the issue between the presidency and the K-P government was "not politics but terrorism", while questioning the provincial government's handling of police capacity, counterterrorism infrastructure and security funds.
He said the PTI had exercised political control or influence in K-P for around 13 years and criticised its leadership for advocating negotiations with the TTP.
"Imran Khan has always had a soft corner for TTP, and the party's thinking has been more aligned with the idea of negotiations with terrorists rather than the state's policy of eliminating terrorism," Asif said.
He claimed that after becoming prime minister, Imran had said he knew how to end terrorism in K-P and called for talks with terrorists.
Asif also criticised the role of former ISI chief General Faiz Hameed, alleging that he had been used to advance the talks agenda.
The defence minister blamed the PTI founder for using the state apparatus to pursue talks with the TTP and its allies.
"The full price of this policy has been paid by K-P and Pakistan, yet even today, the same party is talking about negotiations and engagement with TTP and Tehreek-e-Taliban Afghanistan (TTA)."
He reiterated the military's stated policy towards terrorism, saying, "terrorists will be eliminated."
Asif said official K-P data showed that the province had witnessed around 6,200 terrorism incidents and 1,200 deaths over the past two years, including 37 suicide attacks allegedly carried out by Afghan nationals. "Just this year, 14 suicide attacks have already occurred, the majority by Afghan nationals," he added.
He questioned the deployment and capacity of the provincial police, saying the K-P police force had around 125,000 personnel, of whom about 13,000 were deployed on VIP security duties. He said around 17,000 posts remained vacant despite the province's frontline role in counterterrorism.
Asif also criticised the functioning of the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) in the merged districts, claiming that it had only 17 bulletproof vehicles and around 3,300 personnel, most of whom were contract employees. "Only 25 are permanent, while the rest are contract employees," the defence minister said.
He also questioned PTI leaders' engagement with the security situation, asking whether they had personally visited military checkpoints, met families of soldiers martyred in the fight against terrorism, reviewed the functioning of courts and police stations in the merged districts or regularly attended apex committee meetings on security.
Addressing PTI claims that K-P had been denied adequate financial resources by the federal government, Asif said the province had received around Rs8.5 trillion in federal assistance between July 2010 and 2025. "There is no shortage of funds, but corruption and weak governance diminish their impact," the minister said.
According to figures cited by Asif, the amount included Rs5.867 trillion transferred under the Seventh National Finance Commission (NFC) Award between 2010 and 2025.
He said Rs705 billion had been provided under the 1% share of the divisible pool allocated for the war against terrorism. For the merged districts, Rs704 billion had been disbursed since 2019, he added.

title: Election Commission ready for Punjab LG polls
description: Election Commission ready for Punjab LG polls
content:
Legal, administrative snags delay polls in Islamabad, K-P, Quetta, cantonments
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) said on Monday it was ready to hold local government (LG) elections in Punjab
However, the electoral watcheog said legal and administrative complications were continuing to hold up polls in Islamabad, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Quetta and the cantonment boards.
The assessment was made at a special meeting chaired by Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Sikandar Sultan Raja to take stock of preparations for LG elections across the provinces, the federal capital and the cantonments.
The commission reviewed the province-wise progress of the exercise.
According to an ECP statement, preparations in Punjab had reached the stage where the commission was ready to proceed with the elections and had already sent a draft election schedule to the provincial government.
The commission has also sought lists of district returning officers, returning officers and assistant returning officers to facilitate their appointments, and asked the Punjab government to respond to the proposed schedule at the earliest.
In Sindh, the ECP said preparations had also begun for holding local body elections on time, with instructions issued to its relevant office to take all necessary steps.
In Islamabad, delimitation has been completed, but the Islamabad Capital Territory Amendment Ordinance 2026 has lapsed, the meeting was informed.
The ECP said a National Assembly Standing Committee had already approved legislation in line with the ordinance. It therefore decided to approach the federal government for the "immediate completion of legislation".
However, in the event that the legislation was not completed, the commission said it would proceed with the elections under the existing Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government Act 2015.
The ECP was also told that delimitation in all cantonments had been completed and that it was ready to conduct local body polls there.
However, the amended Cantonments Act requires the federal government to make a formal request to the ECP for holding the elections under Section 19-D.
"Despite reminders and a letter from the chief election commissioner to the prime minister, no request had been received," the statement said.
"The ECP decided to write a final letter to the Ministry of Defence, failing which it would take an appropriate decision regarding holding of elections".
In Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, the ECP recalled that delimitation had been completed in 23 districts and was in progress in seven others when the provincial government amended Section 6 of the K-P Local Government Act 2013.
The amendment increased the population threshold for village and neighbourhood councils from 5,000-15,000 to 30,000-40,000.
In Balochistan, the ECP noted that the term of the local government institutions would expire on Feb 8, 2027. However, it said LG elections in Quetta could not be held despite orders of the Federal Constitutional Court.
The commission said it had completed delimitation on May 21, 2026, in compliance with the court's order, but the provincial government subsequently bifurcated Quetta into two districts without providing details of the new boundaries and other required data.

title: Legal input sought on social media ban for teenagers
description: Legal input sought on social media ban for teenagers
content:
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has summoned the Attorney General for Pakistan (AGP) to assist the court in a petition seeking a ban on social media use by children under the age of 16.
Chief Justice Aalia Neelum heard the petition filed by Alia Saleem. The petitioner's counsel presented arguments before the court.
Written responses from the Federal Ministry of Law and Justice and the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) were submitted to the court during the previous hearing.
The petitioner contended that Pakistan currently lacks a legal mechanism for age verification of children under 16 on social media platforms.
The petition also alleged that PEMRA has failed to effectively enforce its code of conduct aimed at preventing inappropriate content in television dramas and advertisements.
Citing measures adopted in countries including Australia, Italy and Brazil, the petitioner urged the court to impose a similar restriction in Pakistan on social media use by children under 16.
The petition seeks a complete ban on the depiction of indecent scenes and alcohol consumption in television dramas and advertisements.
It also calls for the establishment of a mechanism to protect children on social media platforms and seeks amendments to the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) to introduce a mandatory age-verification system for children.
The court has summoned the attorney general to assist it in determining the legal and regulatory aspects of the matter.
The National Commission on the Rights of Child (NCRC) submitted a 17-page response to the Islamabad High Court (IHC), calling for strict age-verification systems and legal protections against online harm.

title: IO s absence in Imaan bail case incenses ATC
description: IO s absence in Imaan bail case incenses ATC
content:
Summons DSP, threatens jail but adjourns case till 13th
The absence of an investigation officer (IO) during hearing of the bail petitions of rights lawyers Imaan Mazari and her husband Hadi Ali Chattha irked an anti-terrorism court (ATC) judge who summoned a DSP and threatened to send him to jail, in case he failed to satisfy the court.
ATC Judge Abual Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain on Monday took up the couple post-arrest bail petitions in a case that includes terrorism charges and violation of Section 144,
When the judge asked the court staff about the investigating officer, he was informed that the investigator had not shown up. Expressing displeasure, the judge directed the staff to summon the DSP. "Verbal statements will not be accepted," he remarked as the court took a short recess.
When DSP Legal Naeem Yousaf appeared before the court, the judge expressed severe displeasure over the investigating officer's absence and asked where the case record was.
When the DSP began speaking in English, the judge told him to speak in Urdu. The DSP said that, according to his information, the investigating officer was out of the city along with the record.
"You should be ashamed," the judge remarked, warning that he could have the DSP stand facing the wall in the courtroom and send him and the SP to jail in uniform for six months if he failed to produce evidence of the investigator's absence from the city.
The judge also directed the security officials to ensure the DSP did not leave the court premises without permission. The DSP sought some time to provide the relevant information. He subsequently produced a WhatsApp printout, claiming that the investigating officer was in Gilgit-Baltistan.
The judge refused to accept the WhatsApp copy and threw it back toward the DSP, directing him to produce the original document before the court.
He again ordered that handcuffs be brought into the courtroom and directed the security in-charge to remain there, saying that if he ordered the DSP's arrest, the DSP should not be allowed to leave. He also instructed the gate security not to let the police officer leave the premises.
Addressing Advocate Riasat Ali Azad, the judge said the judiciary should have a "judicial force" capable of ensuring immediate implementation of court orders. "The same system of 1898 and 1860 is still operating," the judge remarked.
Later, the DSP submitted a report to the court, stating that the investigating officer was indeed in Gilgit-Baltistan and that his phone was switched off. He said it could take 10 to 15 days to establish contact with the officer.
The judge said he would issue a detailed order regarding the absence of the investigating officer.
The lawyers requested that the matter be adjourned until Tuesday (today) but the judge adjourned the hearing until October 13, stating that he would pass an order concerning the investigating officer.

Jack Doherty’s girlfriend allegedly pulled a gun during an argument over their breakup before the influencer was arrested for alleged domestic violence, according to a police report obtained by TMZ .
The incident reportedly occurred in September in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, where police responded to an alleged dispute involving Doherty and his girlfriend. The woman alleged that Doherty threatened to “beat her ass” during the argument and said he could do so because he was bigger than her. She told police that she went upstairs, retrieved a firearm that was on a table and held it at her side while telling Doherty to leave her alone. She also reportedly told officers she would shoot him if he approached her because she was afraid.
The woman acknowledged hitting and scratching Doherty but told police she did so in self-defense.
Doherty gave officers a different account of the altercation. According to the police report, he said his girlfriend had struck him and showed officers security footage from the residence. Police said the footage appeared to show a verbal argument and the woman using her arm to strike and push Doherty away to create distance.
Officers also noted that Doherty had a visible injury on his face. Despite this, he was taken into custody and transported to jail.
Doherty’s arrest came after allegations of domestic violence. The case remains based on the accounts and evidence described in the police report, and the allegations have not been established as facts in court.
