title: ICC provides more details on arrest warrants for two Taliban leaders
description: ICC issued arrest warrants for Taliban leaders Haibatullah Akhundzada and Abdul Hakim Haqqani last year
content:
Court issued arrest warrants for Haibatullah Akhundzada and Abdul Hakim Haqqani last year
The International Criminal Court provided more details on Monday on arrest warrants issued last year for two Taliban leaders, Haibatullah Akhundzada, the group's supreme spiritual leader, and Abdul Hakim Haqqani, who has been chief justice since 2021.
The ICC had already announced the existence of the warrants in July 2025, saying the men were accused of committing the crime against humanity of persecution on gender grounds against girls, women and other people who did not conform with the Taliban's policy on gender, gender identity or expression.
#ICC Pre-Trial Chamber II unseals four warrants of arrest issued in the #Afghanistan situation against Mr Haibatullah Akhundzada, Mr Abdul Hakim Haqqani, Mr Habibullah Agha and Mr Neda Mohammad Nadim⤵️ https://t.co/LKmot06bf6
The precise contents of the warrants had remained sealed. Now the court has given more information about the findings of the judges who issued the warrants.
They found the suspects "implemented a governmental policy that resulted in severe violations of fundamental rights and freedoms of the civilian population of Afghanistan, in connection with conducts of murder, imprisonment, torture, rape and enforced disappearance".
Also Read: Pakistan hits Afghan terror hideouts; 22 killed
While the Taliban have imposed strict rules and prohibitions on the entire Afghan population, they have specifically targeted women and girls by denying them the right to education, freedom of expression and freedom of movement, the judges found.
According to UN figures, half of Afghan women now leave their homes only once or twice a month as Taliban-imposed restrictions curtail their freedom of movement and participation in public life. Afghanistan remains the only country in the world to ban girls from secondary education and women from attending university, said UN Women, which promotes gender equality.
Afghanistan rejects ICC arrest warrants for Taliban ministers
The Taliban government on Monday condemned the International Criminal Court for issuing arrest warrants for two Afghan education ministers, adding it "does not recognise" the court and the ministers did nothing that merits punishment.
"We are bound by the rulings of Islamic Sharia and its courts, not by intelligence entities or so-called courts," Taliban government chief spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid said in a statement. "Afghanistan calls on such entities not to make claims beyond their authority and jurisdiction."

title: Asif blames PTI s TTP policy for worsening K P security
description: Defence minister questions police capacity  counterterrorism funding and PTI   s policy on talks with militants
content:
Defence minister questions police capacity, counterterrorism funding and PTI’s policy on talks with militants
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Monday accused the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) of pursuing negotiations with the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), saying the party’s policy had contributed to the security crisis in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).
In a detailed statement on X, Asif said the issue between the presidency and the K-P government was “not politics but terrorism”, while questioning the provincial government’s handling of police capacity, counterterrorism infrastructure and security funds.
He said the PTI had exercised political control or influence in K-P for around 13 years and criticised its leadership for advocating negotiations with the TTP.
“Imran Khan has always had a soft corner for TTP, and the party's thinking has been more aligned with the idea of negotiations with terrorists rather than the state's policy of eliminating terrorism,” Asif said.
He claimed that after becoming prime minister, Imran had said he knew how to end terrorism in K-P and called for talks with terrorists.
ریاست اور خیبر پختونخوا کا مسئلہ سیاست نہیں بلکہ دہشت گردی ہے۔ کچھ حقائق دیکھنا ضروری ہے - صوبے کا گزشتہ دو سال کا ڈیٹا: تقریباً 6,200 دہشت گردی کے واقعات، 1,200 شہادتیں اور افغان شہریوں کی جانب سے 37 خودکش حملے کیے گئے۔ صرف رواں سال 14 خودکش حملے ہو چکے ہیں، جن میں اکثریت…
Asif also criticised the role of former Inter-Services Intelligence chief General Faiz Hameed, alleging that he had been used to advance the talks agenda.
Hameed was sentenced to 14 years in prison by a military court in December 2025 on charges including violation of state secrets and interfering in politics.
The defence minister blamed the PTI founder for using the state apparatus to pursue talks with the TTP and its allies.
“The full price of this policy has been paid by K-P and Pakistan, yet even today, the same party is talking about negotiations and engagement with TTP and Tehreek-e-Taliban Afghanistan (TTA).”
He reiterated the military’s stated policy towards terrorism, saying, “Terrorists will be eliminated.”
Asif said the state’s current policy was to eliminate terrorists rather than negotiate with them. He also questioned PTI criticism of military operations, asking whether the army was not fighting terrorism and who else was doing so.
“You say this is a war for dollars. Tell us, how many billions of dollars has America provided to Pakistan in the past few years for the war against terrorism and security?” he asked.
The minister also referred to reported drone attacks in Kohat and Peshawar , as well as attacks by the TTA on security posts. He questioned why the military should not use drones for defence when militants were using them.
Asif said official K-P data showed that the province had witnessed around 6,200 terrorism incidents and 1,200 deaths over the past two years, including 37 suicide attacks allegedly carried out by Afghan nationals. “Just this year, 14 suicide attacks have already occurred, the majority by Afghan nationals,” he added.
He questioned the deployment and capacity of the provincial police, saying the K-P police force had around 125,000 personnel, of whom about 13,000 were deployed on VIP security duties. He said around 17,000 posts remained vacant despite the province’s frontline role in counterterrorism.
Asif also criticised the functioning of the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) in the merged districts, claiming that it had only 17 bulletproof vehicles and around 3,300 personnel, most of whom were contract employees. “Only 25 are permanent, while the rest are contract employees,” the defence minister said.
He also questioned PTI leaders’ engagement with the security situation, asking whether they had personally visited military checkpoints, met families of soldiers martyred in the fight against terrorism, reviewed the functioning of courts and police stations in the merged districts or regularly attended apex committee meetings on security.
Also Read: Govt has kept 'all doors of dialogue open' with opposition: parliamentary secretary
He pointed to more than 3,000 pending prosecution cases in K-P and questioned why, despite the large number of cases, no terrorist had been executed or punished in the province.
According to Asif, the state’s policy in areas affected by militancy was based on a “Hold, Build and Transfer” model — first securing an area, then rebuilding infrastructure and institutions, and finally handing control to the civilian administration. He demanded that the PTI leadership explain its policy for ending terrorism.
Asif also alleged that the provincial police had sought Rs42 billion for the reconstruction and fortification of police checkpoints but had received only Rs1.2 billion, or 2.8%, from the K-P government. “Papers claim that Rs42 billion were spent, while in reality, this amount was embezzled,” he stated.
Addressing PTI claims that K-P had been denied adequate financial resources by the federal government, Asif said the province had received around Rs8.5 trillion in federal assistance between July 2010 and 2025. “There is no shortage of funds, but corruption and weak governance diminish their impact,” the minister said.
According to figures cited by Asif, the amount included Rs5.867 trillion transferred under the Seventh National Finance Commission (NFC) Award between 2010 and 2025.
Read More: K-P received Rs34.88tr in federal funds over past five years
He said Rs705 billion had been provided under the 1% share of the divisible pool allocated for the war against terrorism. For the merged districts, Rs704 billion had been disbursed since 2019, he added.
The figures also included around Rs482.78 billion in direct transfers, including royalties and gas development surcharge; Rs481.43 billion spent under the Benazir Income Support Programme in K-P between 2016 and 2025; and Rs117.166 billion in assistance for internally displaced persons.
He added that the province had received Rs46.44 billion under the latest NFC payment issued on December 17, 2025.
فنڈز کی کمی نہیں، مگر کرپشن اور کمزور طرزِ حکمرانی ان کے اثرات کو کم کر دیتے ہیں - ساتواں این ایف سی ایوارڈ (2010 تا 2025):5,867 ارب روپے - دہشت گردی کے خلاف جنگ (قابلِ تقسیم پول کا 1 فیصد):705 ارب روپے - ضم شدہ اضلاع (2019 سے): 704 ارب روپے - براہِ راست منتقلیاں (رائلٹیز، جی…
Provincial Finance Adviser Muzammil Aslam on Monday rejected the impression that the K-P government was neglecting security or failing to allocate adequate resources to the police and other institutions, saying the province had been prioritising spending on law and order since February 2024.
“The current government of K-P has been allocating resources on a priority basis to police, law and order, judiciary, and temporarily displaced persons (TDPs) since February 2024,” he said in a post shared by the K-P government on X.
Aslam said K-P was fighting the war against terrorism alongside the federal government and armed forces, while bearing a “major burden of expenses” related to containing the threat.
He acknowledged that terrorism remained a major issue for the province but highlighted K-P’s performance on conventional crime, saying its police had a better record than Punjab in cases involving robbery, kidnapping, mobile phone theft and vehicle theft.
*مشیر خزانہ خیبرپختونخوا مزمل اسلم کا خیبرپختونخوا کے سیکورٹی بجٹ پر ردعمل* خیبرپختونخوا کی موجودہ حکومت فروری 2024 سے پولیس، لاء اینڈ آرڈر، عدلیہ اور ٹی ڈی پیز پر ترجیحی بنیادوں پر وسائل خرچ کر رہی ہے۔ مزمل اسلم خیبرپختونخوا پولیس کا جرائم ریکارڈ (ڈکیتی، اغواکاری، موبائل و… pic.twitter.com/VbdVBgc4bc
Aslam said the province had been spending beyond its available resources on police infrastructure in the merged districts, arguing that K-P itself was bearing a substantial share of the financial burden of counterterrorism.
The finance adviser said the police budget had increased from Rs121 billion in 2024-25 to Rs173.8 billion in the 2026-27 budget, representing a 43.6% increase.
He said the allocation for purchasing weapons for the police had also risen from Rs3.3 billion to Rs14.5 billion. “The total police budget in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa is 191 billion rupees, the highest budget rate in all of Pakistan,” he added.
Aslam also compared K-P’s spending with that of other provinces, saying the provincial government was allocating substantial resources to the police.
He disputed claims that K-P was not spending sufficiently on the judiciary, saying the province had allocated Rs6 billion for judicial development, compared with Rs5.2 billion in Punjab, Rs2 billion in Sindh and Rs900 million in Balochistan.
He said K-P had been waiting for a “fair share for the merged districts” under the NFC for the past eight years and had been meeting the related expenditure from its own resources.
Aslam said financial assistance for temporarily displaced persons remained a major point of disagreement between the federal and provincial governments.
He claimed that the federal government had stopped making payments for internally displaced persons (IDPs) in 2022 and said the Centre owed K-P Rs54 billion in outstanding TDP payments.
He said the province had received no payment against the outstanding amount and was instead bearing the full cost from its own resources.
The finance adviser said the federal government’s financial obligations towards K-P should be taken into account when assessing the province’s spending on security and other sectors.
Earlier in the day, PTI-backed K-P Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati also responded to concerns raised by the federal government over the security situation in the province, saying the assembly had already initiated a parliamentary process to address the issue.
He said the legislature had convened a “peace jirga” last year, during which all political parties adopted a joint declaration to constitute a “Special Committee on Security”.
“The Committee has already received detailed briefings, in the presence of the parliamentary leaders of all political parties, from the Inspector General of Police, Counter Terrorism Department (CTD), Additional Chief Secretary Home, Home Department, Chief Secretary, and other relevant provincial institutions,” he said.
Swati said federal leaders had also been informed about the parliamentary process.
“Letters were sent to the Hon'ble Prime Minister of Pakistan, the Chairman of the Senate, the Speaker of the National Assembly and the Federal Minister for Interior, informing them that the Assembly was moving towards comprehensive parliamentary recommendations on the security situation,” he said.
He added that only one major stakeholder’s briefing remained — that of the Peshawar Corps Commander. The speaker said he had spoken to the military leader, who had assured him of his participation in a meeting of the special committee, which had yet to take place.
“I am therefore going to summon another meeting of the Special Committee,” he said, adding that he hoped to bring all relevant authorities and institutions to the same table to present their positions on the “critical” matter.
In view of the concerns being expressed by the Federal Government regarding the prevailing law and order situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, it is important to first look at the comprehensive parliamentary process that the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly has already initiated. The… pic.twitter.com/nCeLxbrEfL
Swati said the meeting would discuss all facts that had been heard, observed and emerged during the committee’s proceedings.
He urged relevant institutions to present their “perspectives, facts and responsibilities” at the upcoming meeting, saying this was necessary for the committee to formulate its recommendations.
“These recommendations will then be presented before the Assembly and, after approval, forwarded to both the Provincial and Federal Governments so that responsibilities, policy direction and practical measures are clearly defined.”
The speaker said the people of K-P wanted peace and that all stakeholders needed to play their part in achieving a sustainable solution. He also avoided assigning blame for the deteriorating security situation.
“Our objective is not to assign blame. Our objective is to bring the facts to the table, clearly identify the responsibilities of the relevant institutions, and work collectively towards implementing the National Action Plan and finding a path to lasting peace,” Swati said.
He said maintaining peace was a collective responsibility and assured that the provincial assembly would continue to support efforts to restore peace.

title: Iran s Pezeshkian says negotiation with US  has no meaning
description: US intends to  live by  security pact with Saudi Arabia  Rubio
content:
US intends to 'live by' security pact with Saudi Arabia: Rubio
Iran's ‌President ​Masoud ⁠Pezeshkian said on Monday that negotiations with the ⁠United States ​were meaningless during a ‌meeting ⁠with Armenian ⁠Foreign ​Minister ‌Ararat Mirzoyan in Tehran, according to Reuters .
"Negotiating with an enemy that assassinates, sanctions, pressures, and threatens every day, and breaks its promises, makes no sense, and our nation will not accept such an approach either," Pezeshkian was quoted as saying by Fars News Agency .
‌ 🔴 پزشکیان: با دشمنی که هر روز ترور، تحریم، فشار و تهدید می‌کند و پیمان‌شکن است، مذاکره معنا ندارد و ملت ما نیز چنین رویکردی را نمی‌پذیرد.
US intends to 'live by' security pact with Saudi Arabia: Rubio
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday that the US intended to uphold its bilateral security commitments with Saudi Arabia amid renewed military confrontations involving Houthi forces in Yemen.
"The United States has a defence and security agreement with Saudi Arabia, and we intend to live by it," Rubio told reporters ahead of a European tour including Iceland, Greece, and Portugal, declining to elaborate on operational specifics.
Rubio said that in the face of continuous Houthi attacks, Riyadh had "a right to defend themselves," adding that Yemeni allied forces were trying to recover areas lost during previous clashes.
🔴 US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says Saudi Arabia has the right to defend itself against Houthi attacks 🔴 The US will honor security commitments to Saudi Arabia, Rubio says pic.twitter.com/s6oHEC9fyp
Addressing control around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, Rubio said Saudi and Yemeni troops opposed Houthi domination near the maritime corridor, describing local counter-offensives as an expected development.
The remarks follow Monday’s announcement by Rashad al-Alimi, the chair of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council, of the launch of a military operation to retake the capital Sanaa with the support of the country’s “brothers and friends” and restore state institutions from the Houthis, who have controlled the city since 2014. Yemeni army units reported securing the Dhubab district and strategic positions along the strait.
Washington has so far rejected direct participation in kinetic strikes in support of the campaign, preferring instead to provide intelligence and advisory assistance to Saudi Arabia.
The United States on Monday announced the approval of a $1 billion sale to the United Arab Emirates (UAE) of up to 10,000 Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System guidance sections for rockets.
"The proposed sale will improve the United Arab Emirates' capability to meet current and future threats by developing and maintaining a strong and ready self-defence capability and improving interoperability with US forces," the US State Department said in a statement.
It "will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a major defence partner," the statement added.
@StateDept has authorized a Foreign Military Sale to the Government of the United Arab Emirates for the purchase of Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System-II Guidance Sections at an estimated sale price of $1.041 billion. - https://t.co/spUwYaJjfx
The Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System converts unguided rockets into precision munitions that can be employed for purposes including shooting down drones, thereby avoiding the use of costly missiles to shoot down comparatively cheap aircraft.
The UAE and other US-allied Gulf countries have been hard hit by the Iran war, during which Tehran's forces have repeatedly targeted them with both drones and missiles.
The State Department also announced on Monday the approval of a $400 million sale to Kuwait -- another Gulf state -- of "repair and return services" for Patriot missiles, which have played a key role in countering Iranian attacks in the region.
"Kuwait will use the enhanced capability to strengthen its homeland defence" and "will have no difficulty absorbing these articles and services into its armed forces," the department said in a statement.
Pezeshkian nominates Mehrdad Akhlaqi as Iran's new defence minister
Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian nominated Mehrdad Akhlaqi as the country’s new defence minister, formally submitting his name to Parliament Speaker Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf in a letter, Tehran Times reported on Monday.
According to Tehran Times, Akhlaqi is a senior official at Iran’s Ministry of Defence and had previously served as the chief executive of the Aerospace Industries Organisation.
Defense Minister Nominee Introduced 🔻The president has formally nominated Mehrdad Akhlaqi for the position of Minister of Defense in a letter to Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf, Speaker of the Iranian Parliament. 🔸Akhlaqi is a senior official at the Ministry of Defense and has… pic.twitter.com/WEhPnjPrwi
Iran threatens to target US bases, warships if Washington launches ground invasion
Iran would target all US military bases and American vessels if Washington launches a ground invasion of the country, a senior commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) warned.
Ali Fadavi, head of the advisory group to the IRGC commander-in-chief, made the remarks a day earlier while appearing on an Iranian state television program.
“If the Americans launch a ground attack, then we will target every location related to the Americans, American bases and every vessel related to the Americans,” he said.
Fadavi argued that the US understands military force, saying Americans “understand missiles hitting their warships” and “missiles hitting their bases.”
He also said Iran’s production of military equipment exceeds the rate at which it is being used, claiming the country’s current capabilities have increased significantly compared with the previous two wars.
Turning to the Strait of Hormuz , Fadavi said Iran and Oman should draw up and enforce rules governing the strategic waterway, adding that such rules have already been prepared and are being implemented.
He also warned that American vessels would be vulnerable to Iranian attacks if Washington deployed them to the region.
Read: US threats are an impediment to deal-making: Iranian FM
“The Americans can only create tensions through the air, and certainly an increase in tensions will be to the detriment of the Americans,” he said.
Fadavi also said Iran had “in no way attacked a Muslim country,” arguing that Tehran had instead targeted US military bases located in those countries.
His remarks come amid increased US military activity in the region and heightened tensions between Washington and Tehran.
The US has recently moved additional naval and military assets toward the Middle East, including carrier and amphibious forces, while strengthening air and missile defences at bases and facilities in the region.
Read more: US to respond to Iranian attacks on forces in Middle East: Trump
The deployments come amid continuing military confrontation between Washington and Tehran, with Iran repeatedly warning that US bases and naval assets across the region could be targeted in response to attacks on Iranian territory.
Any further enemy mistake will draw a crushing response: Iranian general
Iran’s Army Commander-in-Chief General Amir Hatami said that despite the casualties of war, its outcome brought honour and pride to the country rather than surrender, according to Press TV .
1/2 General Amir Hatami: Any further enemy mistake will draw a crushing response Iran’s Army Commander-in-Chief General Amir Hatami said that despite the casualties of war, its outcome brought honor and pride to the country rather than surrender. Follow: https://t.co/oa9JV4iSOo pic.twitter.com/2YDEboIfMj
He said that the enemy, after failing on the military front, had turned to sanctions and economic pressure while pursuing measures aimed at creating insecurity and unrest.
Iran will continue documenting war crimes, pursuing international legal action: Deputy FM
Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs, Kazem Gharibabadi, emphasised the need to continue documenting crimes and damages resulting from military aggression by the United States and Israel and reporting them to international organisations, according to IRNA .
Iran to continue documenting war crimes, pursuing international legal action: @Gharibabadi https://t.co/u5XKVVnCBU pic.twitter.com/X2x8ROvsUb
Gharibabadi made the remarks in Tehran on Sunday in a meeting on government agencies’ interaction with regional and international organisations.
He spoke on the importance of participating in international organisations, saying they can use their capacities effectively through planning.
Gharibabadi said government bodies should prepare annual plans for cooperation with international organisations of which they are members. They should review their cooperation and assess whether to continue participating.
The deputy foreign minister said the Foreign Ministry would support and guide government agencies in their dealings with international organisations.
Iran’s oil minister resigns, president appoints replacement
Iranian Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad has resigned, Iran’s state-run Tasnim news agency reported Sunday, citing a presidential official.
Mehdi Tabatabaei, deputy head of communications at the Iranian president’s office, said President Masoud Pezeshkian has accepted Paknejad’s resignation.
Hamid Bovard has been appointed acting oil minister to oversee the ministry’s affairs, Tabatabaei added.
No reason was given for Paknejad’s resignation, which came amid unprecedented US sanctions on Iran, particularly targeting its oil sector.
Bovard previously served as the head of the state-run National Iranian Oil Company and has spent most of his career working in oilfield operations.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Saturday that Iran has no oil shipments remaining at sea and will generate zero oil revenue this week.
On August 25, the US Treasury Department announced the launch of Operation Economic Outcast, a broad campaign aimed at completely isolating Iran from the global financial system.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28. Tehran responded with missile and drone attacks across the region and effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic route for energy supplies. The US military later imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports.
Efforts to end the war have continued since a June framework deal, which seeks to pave the way for a final peace agreement covering navigation through the strategic waterway and Iran’s nuclear program.
Tanker reports multiple explosions near vessel off Yemen: UK maritime agency
A tanker reported multiple explosions near the vessel off Yemen's coast on Sunday, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).
In a warning, UKMTO said the incident occurred 60 nautical miles south of the port city of Mokha.
UKMTO WARNING 151-26 Click here to view the full product. https://t.co/MonDRJHmN4 #MaritimeSecurity #MarSec pic.twitter.com/5U9KaNsnc2
The tanker's company security officer reported seeing multiple explosions in close proximity to the vessel, the agency said.
“The crew are reported as safe and no environmental impact has been reported,” it added.
Authorities are investigating the incident, UKMTO said, advising vessels transiting the area to exercise caution and report any suspicious activity.
The warning did not identify the tanker or indicate what caused the explosions.

title: Makkah defence alliance agrees to  rapid force deployment  in Saudi Arabia  FO
description: Committee appoints Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood  retd  as secretary general for a three year term
content:
Committee appoints Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood (retd) as secretary-general for a three-year term
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Monday agreed to move immediately towards implementing their collective defence commitments and deploying agreed military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia amid continuing security threats facing the Kingdom.
The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of the Strategic-Political and Defence Committee of the Makkah Alliance for Defence in Riyadh, according to a joint statement issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The committee decided to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in Saudi Arabia in accordance with approved arrangements and the national legislation of the three countries.
According to the statement, the move would enhance “readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats”.
🔊PR No.2️⃣7️⃣5️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Joint Statement: Emergency Meeting of the Strategic Political and Defense Committee of the Makkah Alliance for Defence, Riyadh -5 October, 2026 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/ynFYzqILzc
The committee also affirmed that the Makkah Alliance for Defence embodied “a firm commitment to collective defence and a unified position in confronting threats”.
The meeting was convened to address security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia, with the three countries condemning the attempted targeting of Makkah and Madinah and continuing attacks on cities and civilian and economic facilities in the Kingdom.
The parties reaffirmed their “unequivocal rejection of any attack or threat against the Kingdom’s security and territorial integrity”, according to the joint statement.
Pakistan and Turkiye commended the vigilance and readiness of the Saudi Armed Forces, as well as their professionalism and competence in countering threats and attacks facing the Kingdom and safeguarding its security and territorial integrity.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister, Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 , Federal Minister for Defence, Khawaja Muhammad Asif, and the Chief of Army Staff & Chief of Defence Forces, Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir attended the Emergency Meeting of the Strategic Political… pic.twitter.com/mIFjSgcCbH
The committee also reviewed the outcomes of political and military consultations held before the emergency meeting and approved the recommendations submitted to it.
The committee appointed Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood (retd) of Pakistan as the alliance’s first secretary-general for a three-year term.
The three parties welcomed his appointment and expressed confidence in his contribution to advancing the alliance and achieving its objectives.
The three countries also affirmed that “the security of each Party is an integral part of the collective security of the three countries”.
According to the statement, translating the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence into practical measures would demonstrate “the credibility of the commitment to collective defence”, strengthen deterrence and reaffirm the unity and determination of the three countries to defend their security, sovereignty and territorial integrity.
The emergency meeting was held in Riyadh on October 5, 2026.
Earlier in the day, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar arrived in Riyadh on Monday to attend a meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC), the Foreign Office said.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
According to a post on X, “Upon arrival, the DPM/FM was received by Major General Othman Al-Zahrani of the Saudi Armed Forces, Pakistan’s Ambassador to Saudi Arabia Ahmad Farooq, and Mr Haitham, Protocol Officer at the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Riyadh."
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 arrived in Riyadh today to attend the meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC). Upon arrival, the DPM/FM was received by Major General Othman Al-Zahrani of the Saudi Armed… pic.twitter.com/DgXkjD83jA
In an earlier statement, the FO said that FM Dar, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, and Chief of Defence Forces Field and Chief of Army Staff Marshal Asim Munir travelled to Riyadh to attend a meeting of the SPDC established under the MJDA.
According to the FO, the delegation is due to attend the meeting in the Saudi capital on October 5. The meeting will also be attended by the “respective Ministers of Foreign Affairs, Ministers of Defence, as well as Chiefs of General Staff” of Saudi Arabia and Türkiye.
🔊 PR No. 2️⃣7️⃣3️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Curtain Raiser: Meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) under the Makkah Agreement 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/NNFmZmSQoS
Pakistan’s participation in the meeting “signifies Pakistan’s resolve to continue contributing towards regional peace and stability”, the FO said.
The meeting was held under the MJDA and brought together senior political and military officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.
The FO said the three countries would review cooperation under the agreement as well as discuss developments in the region.
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agreed to the emergency SPDC meeting after their foreign ministers met on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on September 24. The ministers discussed implementation of the Makkah agreement and agreed to convene an urgent meeting of the three countries’ military chiefs.
Read: Makkah pact military chiefs condemn attacks on holy city at Riyadh meeting
The military chiefs met in Riyadh the following day, reviewing threats facing Saudi Arabia and discussing intelligence sharing, military coordination and greater integration of defence capabilities.
The meeting came amid a series of attacks on Saudi Arabia attributed by Riyadh to Yemen’s Houthi rebels, including a strike on a power distribution facility in Madinah. Pakistan condemned the attack and reaffirmed its support for Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty and the security of the Two Holy Mosques.
Significance of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
The MJDA was the latest step in longstanding military and strategic cooperation between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. Signed in Makkah, the pact established a framework for collective deterrence and stipulated that an armed attack on any one of the three countries would be considered an attack on all three, while providing for wider cooperation across defence.
The agreement followed nearly a year of negotiations and came amid heightened instability across the Middle East. Turkiye and Pakistan had sought closer regional security cooperation, while Saudi Arabia had faced growing security concerns as conflicts spread across the region, threatening its territory, energy infrastructure and ambitious economic development plans.
For Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the trilateral pact is built on their Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed in September 2025. That agreement stated that “any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both” and committed the two sides to strengthening defence cooperation and joint deterrence.
Read More: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye sign joint defence pact in Makkah
The three countries already had extensive military links. Pakistan had provided training and technical assistance to Saudi forces for decades, while Islamabad and Ankara had maintained close defence ties through military training, naval cooperation and defence equipment. In 2023, Saudi Arabia agreed to purchase Turkish drones in what Ankara described as its largest defence export contract.
Pakistan had also expanded its military and security cooperation with the kingdom, deploying about 8,000 troops, fighter jets, drones and an air-defence system to Saudi Arabia, according to Reuters . Pakistan deploys troops to Saudi air base under defence pact . Islamabad had also been pursuing wider security and economic ties in the Gulf, including negotiations with Kuwait on an expanded cooperation pact linked to energy and investment. Pakistan-Kuwait agree to boost cooperation across key sectors
The signing in Makkah, Islam’s holiest city, added symbolic weight to an agreement that brought together three countries with significant military and strategic capabilities. It also came as Pakistan sought to avoid becoming directly involved in the Iran conflict, instead pursuing diplomatic efforts to mediate, while strengthening its broader regional security partnerships.

description: Rich in prose yet frustratingly opaque  The Hour of the Wolf weaves grief  family legacy  and political ghosts into a complex  uneven narrative
content:
The Hour of the Wolf weaves grief, family legacy, and political ghosts into a complex, uneven narrative
The first disturbing question is: what if, to her, the idea of intimacy is indelibly shaped by her instability? That would spare us from shoehorning Bhutto into the well-worn trope of strong women who should have known better than to get caught in the undertow of the wrong man. title: The Batman Part II  pauses filming as Matt Reeves focuses on family matter
description: The Batman Part II  production pauses as Matt Reeves steps away for a family matter  with 2028 release also unchanged
content:
'The Batman Part II' production pauses as Matt Reeves steps away for a family matter, with 2028 release also unchanged
Production on The Batman Part II has been temporarily paused after director Matt Reeves stepped away to focus on a family matter, Warner Bros. and DC Studios have confirmed.
The upcoming superhero sequel was filming in London when production was halted on Monday. In a statement, the studio said Reeves has its full support and that it looks forward to continuing work on the film.
“Production on The Batman Part II has been temporarily paused while Matt Reeves focuses on a family matter,” Warner Bros. and DC Studios said. “Matt has the full support of DC Studios and we look forward to continuing the journey soon.”
The production pause comes as The Batman Part II remains scheduled for release on February 18, 2028. Sources said it is currently too early to determine whether the temporary stoppage will affect the film’s release date.
Reeves returns as director for the sequel after helming 2022’s The Batman , which starred Robert Pattinson as Bruce Wayne. Pattinson is set to reprise his role as Batman, with Andy Serkis returning as Alfred Pennyworth and Colin Farrell coming back as Oswald Cobblepot, also known as the Penguin.
The sequel has also added several new cast members, including Scarlett Johansson, Sebastian Stan, Brian Tyree Henry, Jayme Lawson, Charles Dance, Gil Perez-Abraham and Sebastian Koch.
The Batman Part II is being developed by Warner Bros. and DC Studios as part of the expanding DC film slate. Reeves is also returning as a writer and producer on the sequel.
Further details about when production will resume have not been announced. The studio has not indicated that Reeves’ temporary absence will lead to any changes to the film’s creative team.

title: Govt increases petrol by 88 paisas  cuts diesel by Rs1 88 for Oct 6
description: Petrol price increases to Rs393 64 per litre  while HSD will cost Rs397 76 under daily price mechanism
content:
Petrol price increases to Rs393.64 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs397.76 under daily price mechanism
The federal government on Monday increased the price of petrol by 88 paisas per litre, while decreasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.88 per litre for October 6.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs393.64 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs397.76 per litre for Tuesday.
The latest revision comes after the government increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.1 and 30 paisas per litre, respectively, from October 3 to October 5.
Read : Govt increases petrol by Rs2.1, diesel by 30 paisas till Oct 5
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices edged lower on Monday after crude exports from the ​Middle East increased and the Group of Seven nations pledged to boost supplies, though selling was limited by ‌ongoing disruption fears linked to the US-Israeli war on Iran .
Brent crude futures were down $1.10, or 1.08%, at $101.15 a barrel by 11:59 am ET (1559 GMT), while US West Texas Intermediate crude was down 89 cents, or 0.98%, at $90.22.
"A truce in the Middle East remains elusive, and ‌renewed hostilities ⁠between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-backed Houthis will ensure that attacks on energy infrastructure and vessels will continue, keeping the geopolitical risk premium at an elevated level," said PVM Oil Associates analyst Tamas Varga.

title: Teenager s hand blown off as French school protests enter third week
description: France says 5 060 arrested in protests  87  minors  more than 1 800 face prosecution
content:
France says 5,060 arrested in protests, 87% minors; more than 1,800 face prosecution
A teenager's hand was blown off as high-school protesters clashed with riot police in northern France on Monday, a ​local official said, on the eve of a national demonstration by the pupils' union against underfunding, overcrowding and dilapidation.
The regional newspaper La Voix du Nord said the 15-year-old ‌lost his hand and part of his lower arm after picking up a police dispersal grenade that detonated in the town of Lens as the wave of school protests entered its third week.
François-Xavier Lauch, prefect of Pas-de-Calais, declined to comment on the exact circumstances, saying some 200 to 250 protesters had been hurling objects at police.
Six months before an election to replace President Emmanuel Macron, his government and the far-right National Rally, led by presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen, ​have accused hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) lawmakers and mayors of stoking the protests. The LFI denies the accusation.
Speaking after meeting with students in the northern Paris suburbs, Education Minister Edouard Geffray ​said participation in the protests had been declining in recent days.
The government would launch a platform for students to express their dissatisfaction and kick off ⁠an action plan for particular schools, he said.
French police accused of excessive force against pupils
Rights groups accuse police of using heavy-handed tactics against minors, including batons, tear gas and flash-ball guns.
Among several investigations into ​police methods, authorities are examining the case of a 16-year-old who suffered an eye injury after police fired rubber bullets into a crowd of protesters, according to his friends. The Interior Ministry did not ​immediately respond to a request for comment on the allegation of using excessive force.
The LFI, headed by presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon, denies encouraging violence and accuses the government of politicising the issue and neglecting pupils' interests.
France's Justice Ministry said 5,060 people have been arrested since the protests began, with 87% of them minors. More than 1,800 people are being prosecuted, including 1,483 minors, the ministry said, without specifying the crimes. It said 790 cases had been dismissed.
The protests ​have put more pressure on a government trying to narrow a budget deficit as investor concerns about state finances grow, briefly pushing the yield on France's 10-year bonds to a 24-year high over 5% ​last week and raising the likely cost of future borrowing.
The protests began in September in Paris, focusing on poor suburbs , before spreading nationwide. The government says they have been hijacked and morphed into urban violence.
"Our priority is to restore ‌order," government ⁠spokesperson Maud Bregeon told CNews television.
Some 400 to 500 high schools were closed or partially closed ahead of Tuesday's nationwide protest.
Read More: Student protests spread across France, Belgium
wo dozen schools have been burned or ransacked, 78 teaching staff have been injured in the demonstrations and at least 190 students have been injured, Geffray said. He said the goal was for classes at affected schools to restart on Wednesday.
"We’re going to keep blocking until the government hears us," said Sami Karen, 18, who was demonstrating outside Charles de Foucauld high school in Paris. "As long as they don’t listen to us, we won’t stop this fight."
Students and police clash in Lille, Toulouse and Paris
On ​Monday, BFMTV showed images of police and students ​clashing in Lille in northern France, tear ⁠gas being used in Toulouse in the southwest, and a fire being lit as people tried to break into a school in central Paris.
Carole Zerbib, head of the vandalised Lycee Vauquelin in Paris, said it had been attacked by a "very determined" group wearing hoods and masks who had tried to break through ​the entrance door and then lit a fire, forcing the school to be evacuated and classes suspended.
"It was very violent and happened very quickly," ​she said, adding that ⁠she did not believe the attackers were from the school.
Since last Monday, 5,000 people, 85% of them teenagers, have been arrested and dozens injured. Teachers and members of the public have been attacked, while damage to property is estimated in the millions of euros.
Bregeon said the government would fast-track a bill on October 27 to make youngsters found to have damaged property, or their parents, financially liable.
Security officials fear that Tuesday's organised protests ⁠in central ​Paris in particular could bring further violence amid concerns that far-left and anarchist groups could try to take them over.
Sophie Binet, ​head of the CGT labour union, told TF1 television on Monday that her members would attend Tuesday's demonstrations to protect the students.
"We've been appalled by what we have seen over the past 10 days and by the unprecedented crackdown that the ​government has organised," she said.

title: Emily Blunt  Benicio Del Toro and Josh Brolin set to return for  Sicario 3

Emily Blunt, Benicio Del Toro and Josh Brolin are returning for 'Sicario 3', with a new director attached
Emily Blunt, Benicio Del Toro and Josh Brolin are set to return for Sicario 3 , with Black Label Media and Thunder Road moving forward on the long-awaited third instalment of the crime thriller franchise.
According to reports, filmmaker Padraic McKinley has been chosen to direct the project, while Oscar-nominated writer Steven Knight is developing the screenplay. Plot details for the new film remain under wraps.
The Sicario franchise was created by Taylor Sheridan and began with Denis Villeneuve’s critically acclaimed 2015 film, which starred Blunt, Del Toro and Brolin. The original movie became a box office and awards-season success, helping establish Villeneuve as one of Hollywood’s leading directors. A follow-up, Sicario: Day of the Soldado , was released in 2018 and featured Del Toro and Brolin reprising their roles.
The popularity of the franchise has continued to grow, and reports suggest the three stars agreed to return after reading the latest draft by Knight. Producers then launched a search for a director before selecting McKinley for the job.
The script is reportedly being refined with input from the cast, with production expected to begin early next year. While Lionsgate distributed the first two films, the new project is expected to be taken to the market, with several studios already said to be interested.
Black Label Media’s Molly Smith, Trent Luckinbill and Thad Luckinbill will produce alongside Thunder Road’s Basil Iwanyk and Erica Lee, while Ed McDonnell also returns as a producer.
Blunt was recently seen in The Devil Wears Prada 2 and has completed work on A Quiet Place Part III . Del Toro earned an Oscar nomination for One Battle After Another , while Brolin will next appear in Whalefall .

title: UK police arrest 12 after anti migrant protest in southern England
description: 149 migrants were rescued in the Channel  prompting a protest in Hampshire marina and subsequent arrests
content:
149 migrants were rescued in the Channel, prompting a protest in Hampshire marina and subsequent arrests
Twelve people were arrested after an anti-migrant protest in the southern English town of Gosport turned violent, with police saying officers were assaulted during clashes.
Eleven men and one woman were arrested on suspicion of offences, including assaulting police officers, affray and racially aggravated public order offences, Hampshire Police said on Monday.
The arrests followed a protest Sunday at a marina in Gosport, Hampshire, after 149 migrants were picked up in a mid-Channel rescue operation by the Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) alongside a French vessel, according to the Home Office.
Some flares were set off and several scuffles between protesters and police took place during the stand-off.
A police cordon was put in place on Haslar Road.
Read More: UK's Green Party votes to declare 'zionism is racism'
However, some protesters stood in front of police vans to prevent them from advancing, chanting "shame on you" and "deport the lot," according to a report by BBC .
Hampshire Police said it deployed officers to "support our partners in the event of an emergency at sea" including the Maritime and Coastguard Agency, the RNLI and Border Security Command.
The force imposed conditions under the Public Order Act and prohibited the wearing of face coverings.
A small number of police officers were treated at the scene for injuries, although no one attending the protest was seriously injured, police said.
Assistant Chief Constable Simon Dodds said: "Violence and criminal damage have no part in peaceful protest."
"Our position on this has been clear that we will investigate thoroughly and take robust action against anyone responsible," he added.
The migrants were later taken by coach to a processing center in Kent.
The incident marked the second known landing of large numbers of migrants this far west along England's south coast in recent years.

title: Three years of genocide  Israel   s traditional Asian allies shift stance on Gaza
description: Netanyahu cut a lonely figure at the UN last month as scores of delegates walked out during his speech
content:
Netanyahu cut a lonely figure at the UN last month as scores of delegates walked out during his speech
After three years of Israel’s genocide in Gaza that has killed tens of thousands, Tel Aviv's relations with its traditional Asian allies have increasingly fractured, deepening its diplomatic isolation.
A recent illustration of that isolation came at the UN General Assembly late last month, where Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cut a lonely figure as scores of delegates walked out of his speech .
The departing delegates included representatives from Asian nations such as Pakistan, Malaysia, Indonesia and Bangladesh.
Here is a look at how Asian countries have responded to Israel and the Gaza war.
Israel has faced strong state-level criticism from its longtime East Asian allies, such as Japan and South Korea.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi opposed US sanctions against International Criminal Court (ICC) President Tomoko Akane, who sought an arrest warrant for Netanyahu over alleged war crimes in Gaza.
Takaichi reaffirmed Tokyo’s consistent support for the ICC during the UN General Assembly, pushing back against pressure from the US, and saying that the country takes the US sanctions against Akane “very seriously.”
Washington sanctioned Akane, the first Japanese national to head the ICC, in August, accusing the court of encroaching on state sovereignty.
Read More: Gaza residents face another winter amid shelter shortages, dwindling aid
With Seoul, tensions began in April after South Korean President Lee Jae Myung shared a video on social media alleging that Israeli soldiers abused a Palestinian child and then threw him off a rooftop.
Lee said it was necessary to determine the authenticity of the video and assess what actions were taken, stressing the seriousness of the allegations.
“Wartime homicide is no different from matters that we take issue with, such as the forced (enslavement of) comfort women, and the massacre of Jewish people,” he said.
The issue of “comfort women” refers to the sexual enslavement of thousands of women and girls, many of them Korean, by the Imperial Japanese Army during World War II.
Israel strongly criticised Lee for posting the video, calling it “unacceptable.”
Israel’s Foreign Ministry claimed that Lee relied on a “fake account” and had revived an incident from 2024 that had already been investigated.
The ministry accused Lee of trivializing the massacre of Jews on the eve of Holocaust Remembrance Day in Israel.
China, which has long supported a two-state solution, continued to reiterate its call.
President Xi Jinping said the two-state solution is the “right direction” for resolving the longstanding Palestine issue.
Sri Lanka, one of the first countries to recognise the State of Palestine, called at the UN General Assembly for the “early” recovery and reconstruction of Gaza, reiterating its support for Palestinians’ “inalienable” rights and a two-state solution.
“Recovery and reconstruction of Gaza must be an early priority,” Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath said in his address.
He added that Colombo supports resolving the Palestine issue in line with the 1967 borders.
Pakistan, a member of the Gaza Peace Board, also reiterated its “unwavering” support for the Palestinian people and the establishment of an independent State of Palestine based on the pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.
Addressing the UN General Assembly, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said that Palestine must also be granted full membership in the UN.
India, for its part, continued to pursue its strategy of maintaining diplomatic and strategic ties with Israel while continuing to express traditional support for a two-state solution and Palestinian statehood.
India under Prime Minister Narendra Modi has significantly deepened its strategic relationship with Israel, including through Modi’s February meeting with Netanyahu, when the two countries elevated their ties to a “Special Strategic Partnership.”
According to Jatin Desai, a Mumbai-based political analyst, India has historically stood with the Palestinian people. He said India’s position was clear even before the establishment of Israel.
Thailand, which has maintained long-standing ties with Israel, continues to cooperate closely with Israel, particularly in agriculture and education.
Every year, around 100,000 Israeli tourists travel to Thailand, and thousands of Thai workers, both skilled and unskilled, are employed in Israel. The country is also a popular destination for Thai students pursuing academic studies.
Bangkok established diplomatic relations with Israel in 1954, while it officially recognized Palestine in 2012.
In January, US President Donald Trump, as chair of the Board of Peace for Gaza , invited Australia, Vietnam and Thailand to join the international body.
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Canberra would consider the offer, though no decision had so far been taken.
“We’ve received correspondence from the president that arrived, I think, last night. That’s something we haven’t had time to consider. We’ll consider all of these approaches respectfully and through our proper processes,” Albanese said after receiving the invitation.
Thailand said it was reviewing the details of the offer.
Vietnam’s Communist Party General Secretary To Lam accepted Trump’s invitation to join the Gaza Peace Council and “affirmed Vietnam’s readiness to participate as a founding member state of the council.”
Read More: Over 800 Palestinian teachers killed by Israel since Gaza war: education ministry
New Zealand, which did not join neighboring Australia and other European nations to recognise the State of Palestine last year, said recognition of Palestinian statehood is “inevitable.”
In his final speech as foreign minister in the incumbent government earlier this month, Winston Peters said his decision in 2025 not to join most other UN member states in recognising Palestine was an example of truly independent foreign policy.
But he said that recognition was a question of when, not if.
The Pacific, a cluster of small island nations, has provided Israel with a bloc of supportive voices in international forums, even as global criticism intensifies and more countries move to recognise Palestine.
Fiji further strengthened ties with Israel in September 2025 by opening a new embassy in Jerusalem. Days earlier, it abstained in a UN vote on a two-state solution. Like many of its neighbors, Fiji does not recognise Palestine.
Papua New Guinea followed a similar path. In September 2023, it also opened an embassy in Jerusalem and has since repeatedly opposed calls for a ceasefire at the UN. The country continues to reject recognition of Palestinian statehood.
Nauru has long been a loyal supporter of Israel. It recognised Jerusalem as Israel’s capital in 2019 and, in September last year, voted against a resolution backing a two-state solution.
Palau and Micronesia have consistently voted in line with Israel at the UN.
Samoa signed a visa-waiver deal in 2019 but took a slightly different line in September last year, when it abstained in the two-state resolution. Still, like most of its neighbors, it has not recognised Palestine.
Other Pacific nations such as Vanuatu, the Marshall Islands, Kiribati, the Solomon Islands, Tuvalu and Tonga maintain diplomatic relations with Israel, regularly support it at UN forums and do not recognise Palestine.
Tonga and Israel signed a visa-waiver agreement in 2010, while Vanuatu and the Marshall Islands have consistently backed Israel in UN votes.

Jack O’Connell and Odessa A’zion will star as flat-Earthers in 'The End of the World as We Know It' from Studiocanal
Jack O’Connell and Odessa A’zion are set to lead The End of the World as We Know It , a new feature from Ross White and Tom Berkeley, the Oscar-winning filmmakers behind An Irish Goodbye .
The film, produced by Studiocanal, Working Title, Parkville Pictures and Film4, will follow two lonely strangers who meet during an unusual pilgrimage to prove that the Earth is flat. O’Connell, a BAFTA winner known for ’71 and Back to Black , will star alongside A’zion, who earned a BAFTA nomination and gained attention for Marty Supreme . The pair will play star-crossed loners brought together by their shared belief in the flat-Earth theory.
Tim Bevan and Eric Fellner will produce for Working Title Films, while Olivier Kaempfer will produce for Parkville Pictures. Studiocanal is fully financing the film, with Film4 co-financing and executive producing. Studiocanal will distribute the movie theatrically across several territories, including the U.K., France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Benelux, Australia and New Zealand, while also handling worldwide sales.
White and Berkeley previously made An Irish Goodbye , which starred Seamus O’Hara and James Martin. The short film became an awards-season success after screening at more than 60 international festivals and won the 2023 Academy Award for Best Live Action Short Film and the BAFTA for Best British Short Film.
O’Connell will next appear in A Quiet Place Part III and Godzilla x Kong: Supernova , while A’zion is set to star in Mother Courage and Fonda .

title: Data of over 10M customers exposed in cyberattacks on Japanese firms
description: Compromised data included customers    names  email addresses  phone numbers and membership numbers
content:
Compromised data included customers’ names, email addresses, phone numbers and membership numbers
Two Japanese companies have reported major data breaches following unauthorised access to their computer systems, potentially exposing information belonging to millions of customers, local media reported Monday.
Monogatari Corp., operator of the Yakiniku King barbecue restaurant chain, said information belonging to more than 10 million customers was leaked after unauthorised access to its reservation and rewards app, according to Kyodo News.
The compromised information included customers’ names, email addresses, phone numbers and membership numbers.
The breach was detected Friday, the company said, adding that it had found no evidence so far that the leaked information had been misused.
Separately, Daiwa Securities Group said data belonging to around 110,000 customers of its brokerage unit may have been compromised following unauthorised access to a contractor-operated server, Kyodo reported.

The intrusion occurred between Friday evening and Saturday morning on a server operated by Scala Communications Inc., which provides Daiwa Securities with an online customer inquiry management service.
Potentially exposed information includes names, email addresses and account numbers.
Including inquiries that contained no personal information, around 220,000 pieces of data may have been affected.
Daiwa said the compromised information could not be used to conduct transactions, including online trades.
The brokerage has also found no evidence so far that the potentially compromised information has been published or circulated online.

title: Honda plans highway test of wireless charging for moving trucks

Honda may begin trials in late 2026, with public demonstrations planned for April 2027
Japanese automaker Honda Motor said on Monday it ​has developed technology that ‌can wirelessly charge electric vehicles, including large trucks, while being driven, ​and plans to test the ​technology on a Japanese highway.
Honda ⁠plans to test the ​technology along with construction firm Taisei ​and road builder Taisei Rotec in the financial year beginning in April ​2027 or later, it ​said in a statement
The system, developed by ‌Honda's ⁠research arm with the two firms, aims to transfer electricity wirelessly from charging units embedded ​in ​roads to ⁠vehicles in motion, which could lead to fewer ​charging stops.
According to technology.com, the technology is being developed by Honda Research and Development and Taisei Rotec. The system is based on magnetic coupling technology designed to transmit power to moving EVs, mainly logistics trucks.
Honda may launch its first trials in late 2026, with public demonstrations planned for April 2027. The website said the system has three components: a DC power supply, a power transmitter embedded in the pavement, and a receiver under the vehicle.
A Honda engineer declined to comment on the cost compared with a conventional high-speed charging network, saying its economic viability would need to be assessed.

content:
Pakistan name squads for T20I series against SL and ODI tri-series, also involving England
KARACHI: Top order batsman Sahibzada Farhan on Monday replaced Agha Salman as Pakistan’s T20I team skipper as the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) announced squad for the home series against Sri Lanka which will begin at the Pindi Stadium in Rawalpindi from Friday.
Agha has also been dropped from the T20I squad. However he has been kept in the ODI squad which was also announced for the tri-series also involving England.
From T20 squad, which represented Pakistan in the T20 World Cup held earlier this year, Agha Salman, Babar Azam, Mohammad Nawaz (who is serving suspension), Usman Tariq, Faheem Ashraf and Shaheen Afridi have been dropped.
Those who have been inserted include Arafat Minhas, fast bowler Imran Randhawa, Maaz Sadaqat, Hasan Nawaz, Naseem Shah and young pace-sensation Razaullah.
Farhan has recently captained Pakistan during the 20 th Asian Games in Japan where the Green-shirts finished with silver medal.
The ODI squad, meanwhile, will be led as usual by Shaheen Afridi. Faheem Ashraf, Fakhar Zaman, Hasan Nawaz, Razaullah and stumper Saad Baig have been included. Those, who have been dropped from the squad which last played a home series against Australia in May this year Include Maaz Sadaqat, Ahmed Daniyal, Abdul Samad, Sahibzada Farhan, Shamyl Hussain amd Rohail Nazir.
Razaullah, who recently made his fantastic Test debut against England, is also set to make his ODI debut.
Fakhar had missed the previous ODI assignment due to fitness issues.
The T20I series will be played at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium, with the opening match scheduled for October 9. The second and third T20Is will be played on October 11 and 13 respectively.
Following the T20I series, Pakistan will feature in a seven-match ODI tri-series alongside England and Sri Lanka. Rawalpindi will host the opening three matches, before the tournament moves to Lahore for the remaining league matches and the final.
Meanwhile a group of Sri Lankan team has already arrived in Islamabad while some players were scheduled to land on Monday and some will arrive on Tuesday.
The T2oI series will be an interesting contest and will be only the second time Sri Lanka will be playing a full-fledged T20I series on Pakistani soil.
Pakistan have the upper hand over Sri Lanka in T20Is, winning 18 of their 31 meetings, while Sri Lanka have secured 13 victories.
In October 2019, Sri Lanka clean-swept Pakistan 3-0 in Pakistan in a three-match T20I series under the captaincy of Dasun Shanaka, with Sarfaraz Ahmed leading Pakistan.
Sri Lanka have struggled in recent series, apart from their Asian Games campaign, where they were beaten by India in the semi-finals.
Sri Lanka lost a three-match series 2-1 to the West Indies in June at the latter’s backyard and were then defeated 3-0 by England in England last month.
This will be Pakistan’s first T20I series since the T20 World Cup, jointly hosted by India and Sri Lanka, at the start of this year.
Pakistan had clean-swept Australia 3-0 in their last home T20I series, which was held shortly before the T20 World Cup.

title: Damon Lindelof confirms    Lanterns    Season 2 is being explored by writers
description: Damon Lindelof says he will not return creatively but writers are already exploring future stories
content:
Damon Lindelof says he will not return creatively but writers are already exploring future stories
Lanterns Season 2 is now in the early stages of development, with writers already exploring ideas for another chapter of the DC Studios series following its Season 1 finale.
Damon Lindelof, who co-created the HBO Max drama with Chris Mundy and Tom King, confirmed that writers are working on ideas for a potential second season during an interview with Collider . However, HBO has not officially renewed the series, meaning development work should not be treated as a formal season order.
The update arrives after the first season concluded with John Stewart, played by Aaron Pierre, accepting Hal Jordan's ring and becoming Earth's newest Green Lantern. Kyle Chandler's Hal was killed during the series, with the creative team deliberately choosing to make his death carry lasting emotional consequences.
Lindelof said the writers working on Season 2 were aware of the importance of preserving the impact of Hal's death. He rejected the idea of reversing the development through a twist such as revealing that Hal was a clone or that his death had somehow been temporary.
At the same time, Lindelof stressed that he does not know what the eventual creative direction for another season would be. He is not expected to lead the next chapter, leaving the writers currently developing ideas with considerable freedom over the show's future.
The potential continuation would follow John's new role as a Green Lantern, after the Season 1 finale established him as Earth's protector. The finale also left several story possibilities open involving Sinestro, the unusual ring John now carries and the wider Green Lantern mythology.
For now, HBO and DC Studios have not announced an official renewal date, episode order or production schedule for Season 2. The current status is therefore early development rather than a confirmed second season.
The development news nevertheless gives fans a clearer indication that the creative team is considering how Lanterns could continue after its first eight episodes.

The World Tennis Women’s Championship 2026 will begin at the PTF Tennis Complex in Islamabad on Tuesday, with players from 17 countries set to compete in the $15,000 event.

“These events will enable local players to compete against international opposition, gain valuable experience, win matches and earn important WTA ranking points,” he said.
Tufail said back-to-back women’s championships in Islamabad would give Pakistani players valuable international exposure while helping them improve their rankings and compete at the professional level..

title: Norway to propose temporary ban on AI glasses in some public places
description: Norway says no total AI glasses ban  private use and filming with consent would still be allowed
content:
Norway says no total AI glasses ban; private use and filming with consent would still be allowed
Norway's government said on Monday it plans to propose a temporary ban on the use of ​AI glasses in selected places, saying it is concerned ‌people could be photographed, filmed or audio-recorded without their knowledge.
The proposal mirrors a broader global backlash against smart glasses equipped with cameras ​over privacy concerns
Ban could apply to places where the public ​regularly gather, such as parks, beaches, museums, shopping ⁠centres and public events, the government said in a ​statement
"I am worried that new, powerful technology is being introduced ​where people risk being photographed, filmed or audio-recorded without knowing it," Digitalisation and Public Governance Minister Torgeir Micaelsen said.
Read More: LISA teams up with Meta for exclusive smart glasses collection
It could also apply ​to schools, playgrounds and youth clubs and to privacy-sensitive ​places such as doctors' offices, swimming pools and gyms with changing rooms
The ‌government ⁠said it was not eyeing a total ban and that private use, and use where others are not at risk of being filmed without consent, would still be allowed
It ​said it ​would examine which ⁠technology the ban would cover, including whether it would apply to glasses with camera ​and audio recording, glasses with camera and ​AI functions ⁠or also other body-worn technology with camera, audio recording and/or AI
The minority government said it would present a bill to ⁠parliament ​as soon as possible, and would ​also set up an expert group to advise on permanent national regulation ​of body-worn technology.

title: New training hub aims to preserve Lahore s heritage through traditional crafts
description: Programme will train young professionals in lime plaster  tile mosaic  fresco painting and Parchin Kari
content:
Programme will train young professionals in lime plaster, tile mosaic, fresco painting and Parchin Kari
A new training programme has been launched to equip young professionals and students with traditional and modern techniques for conserving Lahore’s historic heritage.
The “Heritage Skills Training Hub” will offer lectures and hands-on training at selected historic monuments across the city, with a particular focus on traditional conservation techniques such as lime plaster, glazed tile mosaic, fresco painting and pietra dura, also known locally as Parchin Kari.
The initiative was launched through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed by the Aga Khan Cultural Service-Pakistan (AKCS-P), Collective Research on Mughal (CROM) Lahore and the Commonwealth Heritage Forum (CHF).
The programme will bring together young architects, engineers, art and design graduates, traditional craftsmen and other professionals working in heritage conservation.
Read: Echoes of heritage: Lahore's past and future
According to the organisers, the initiative aims to strengthen local expertise, promote appropriate conservation practices and ensure that the original character and architectural integrity of historic buildings are preserved.
Ongoing conservation projects will also serve as practical training sites, allowing participants to learn and apply conservation techniques while restoration work is under way, the organisers said.
Similar training sessions were held last year at the Royal Kitchens of Lahore Fort, Shahi Hammam and Wazir Khan Mosque, where participants received hands-on instruction in lime plaster, glazed tile mosaic and fresco work.
CROM Lahore President Usman Saeed said the programme would help address the shortage of specialised heritage conservation expertise in Pakistan.
He said CROM Lahore was offering short courses for young professionals by engaging local and international experts to build capacity in the sector.
Read more: Hidden Mughal chambers rediscovered after centuries under Lahore Fort
AKCS-P Chief Executive Officer Tausif Khawaja said conserving historic buildings also required safeguarding the specialised traditional skills associated with their construction and maintenance.
He said the training initiative would enable young professionals to learn these techniques and pass them on to future generations.
The new training cycle will include advanced instruction in glazed tile mosaic, fresco painting and lime work. Pietra dura, or Parchin Kari, will also be introduced, alongside the documentation of traditional conservation techniques.
