title: Russia officials say    situation under control    after plague reports
description: Plague lab worker in Siberia dies  prompting quarantine of dozens and health watchdog chief to visit region
content:
Plague lab worker in Siberia dies, prompting quarantine of dozens and health watchdog chief to visit region
Russian officials on Monday downplayed reports that a laboratory technician in Siberia had died of plague, insisting the situation was under control and that post-mortem tests had not found traces of the disease.
Reports on Friday that a 28-year-old woman named Darya Shipilova, who had been working for the anti-plague institute in Siberia’s Irkutsk region, had died of plague sparked alarm.
The news outlet People of Baikal, citing unnamed sources close to the regional security services, said she may have contracted pneumonic plague from a broken test tube.
Other media reported a possible link between her death and a lab accident at the facility.
But Irkutsk regional governor Igor Kobzev said Monday that a special expert commission inspection in the region had found that “the cause of death was pneumonia of undetermined etiology.”
He said on Telegram that Russia’s consumer and health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor had determined, following tests, that “no microorganisms linked to the young woman’s professional work were found in her biological samples.”
He added that there had been “no new cases of staff from the anti-plague institute seeking medical attention” since the woman’s death.
Kobzev said the sanitary-epidemiological situation in Irkutsk was “stable.”
“The situation remains under our control and that of the experts.”
Asked about the situation on Monday, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters to “rely on Rospotrebnadzor’s official statements rather than ... rumors and speculations.”
Plague is a bacterial disease that can occur in several forms, including pneumonic plague, the most contagious type. Pneumonic plague can be fatal if not treated early, according to the World Health Organisation.
Woman dies of plague in Siberia, dozens under quarantine
Earlier, a laboratory worker at a plague research institute in ​Siberia has fallen ill and died in undisclosed circumstances, prompting authorities to quarantine dozens of ‌people and the head of Russia's health watchdog to fly to the Irkutsk region.
The death has sparked public health fears on social media, but the authorities said on Monday the situation was under control.
Plague is endemic to Siberia, home to the first known prehistoric human outbreak , as the bacterium that causes it, Yersinia pestis, is present among small wild mammals in its vast wilderness and their fleas. It is rare for Russians ⁠to fall ill with plague, however, though cases in other parts of the world - notably Africa - occur ​every year.
Local media named the woman as Darya Shipilova, an employee at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of ​Siberia and the Far East.
BREAKING: 5 hospitals have been closed for quarantines in Siberia due to a possible plague outbreak. The 28-year-old lab technician Darya Shipilova, died yesterday after breaking a test tube with live Yersinia pestis the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute on September 25th while… pic.twitter.com/N6tKLRyAJ5
There were conflicting reports about how and where the laboratory worker, whose age was given as 28, had fallen ill. Still, the authorities said she had died of pneumonia of as-yet unestablished origin.
Read : Kyiv destroyed deadly samples from US-funded biowarfare labs: Russia
Authorities say no new cases ​reported, all contacts traced
Russia's health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, told state media the institute had not found evidence of ​any accidents involving the handling of pathogens after rumours spread on social media that the woman had dropped a test ‌tube containing ⁠live bacteria.
Nevertheless, Anna Popova, the head of Rospotrebnadzor, flew to Siberia for an emergency meeting over the weekend.
An unspecified number of people who had been in contact with the dead woman were quarantined, parts of the hospital in the town of Shelekhov where she died were cordoned off, and an aluminium plant told its ​workers to wear masks.
Read More : WHO asks Ukraine to destroy ‘high-threat pathogens’ to prevent disease spread
Authorities ​urged people to remain ⁠calm and said there was no evidence that the woman's death was linked to her work.
Igor Kobzev, the governor of the Irkutsk region, said in a statement ​that she had died of "pneumonia of unknown aetiology", adding: "Importantly, over the past few ​days, no new ⁠cases of staff from the Anti-Plague Institute seeking medical attention have been identified."
☣️ Russian officials have downplayed reports that a laboratory technician in Siberia had died of plague, insisting the situation was under control and that post-mortem tests had not found traces of the disease. ➡️ https://t.co/kBegPNx3GV pic.twitter.com/DnCbVmhFdl
He said the situation was under control and that all known contacts of the dead woman had been identified, examined and placed under medical supervision.
Plague ⁠comes in ​three forms affecting different parts of the body. Pneumonic plague, ​an infection of the lungs, prompts the patient to cough out infectious airborne droplets.
If identified quickly, it can be treated with antibiotics. But ​if left untreated, it can be fatal in one to six days.

title: Mark Ruffalo warns Trump    I   m gonna Hulk out and you won   t like me when I   m angry    at voting rights rally
description: Ruffalo urged supporters to stay engaged and vote in the November 3 midterm elections
content:
Ruffalo urged supporters to stay engaged and vote in the November 3 midterm elections
Mark Ruffalo delivered a fiery warning to Donald Trump during a voting rights event in New York, telling the president to keep his hands off the vote before joking that he was going to “Hulk out”.
The Avengers star spoke at the Hands Off Our Vote event on Sunday night, where he urged supporters to remain engaged ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. The event also featured Robert De Niro and other speakers focused on voter participation and election protection.
Ruffalo described the election as a major moment and warned that efforts could be made to interfere with voters. He encouraged people to support Free Speech for People, an organisation involved in efforts concerning election security and voting systems.
He then turned his attention directly to Trump, calling on voters to oppose the president's policies and accusing his administration of trying to make people feel intimidated and powerless.
“We’re not going to let ’em,” Ruffalo told the crowd before addressing Trump directly. “Hands off our f***ing vote!”
The actor's comments drew a response from the audience, with someone shouting, “You tell ’em, Hulk!” The reference was to Ruffalo's long running role as Bruce Banner and the Hulk in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
Ruffalo laughed before embracing the comparison, saying, “I’m gonna Hulk out. You won’t like me when I’m angry.” He also told the crowd that he remained involved and was still playing the Hulk.
Ruffalo ended his speech by urging supporters not to be afraid or discouraged. He stressed the importance of standing together, remaining brave and voting.
The appearance comes during an increasingly active period of political campaigning ahead of the midterms. Ruffalo has frequently used his public platform to comment on political and social issues.

title: Judicial commission visits Mir Raza murder site  summons key witness
description: Justice Omar Sial warns investigation team of arrest if witness who first spotted Raza   s body is not produced
content:
Justice Omar Sial warns investigation team of arrest if witness who first spotted Raza’s body is not produced
Justice Omar Sial, head of the judicial commission investigating the Mir Raza Ali's murder case, visited the crime scene and inspected several locations linked to the investigation on Monday.
The commission also inspected a guest house that Mir Raza’s family had identified as suspicious, examining various locations in and around the premises as part of the inquiry. The commission later visited the site where Raza’s body was recovered and summoned employees of a nearby nursery for questioning.
Mir Raza Ali, the 25-year-old entrepreneur, went missing from Karachi’s PECHS area on July 28. His body was found the following day in bushes near a wedding hall in Gulistan-e-Johar. Police initially treated the death as a possible suicide, but a second post-mortem conducted after his exhumation found a firearm entry wound, multiple ante-mortem injuries and signs of internal bleeding, leading investigators to treat the case as murder.
During the visit, police investigators informed Justice Sial that the person who had first spotted the entrepreneur’s body had travelled to Punjab. Expressing anger over the development, the commission chairman directed investigators to bring the individual back. Justice Sial warned that failure to produce the witness could result in the arrest of the entire investigation team.
Raza’s family members and their lawyer accompanied the judicial commission during the crime-scene inspection. At the site, the family briefed the commission on the circumstances and details they had witnessed on the day the body was recovered.
Read More: Mir Raza commission seeks answers from senior police officers
Meanwhile, during Monday’s proceedings, the commission decided that CPLC representative Kashif Iftikhar and Investigating Officer DSP Siraj Lashari would record their statements at 11am on Wednesday, October 7.
The commission also summoned Karachi-based journalists Babar Saleem and Saulat Jaffri for Wednesday’s proceedings and directed them to present their findings before the commission.
In their report, Saleem and Jaffri relied on CCTV footage to trace the movements of certain vehicles at the crime scene following Raza’s death.
The commission is continuing its inquiry into the circumstances surrounding Mir Raza’s death and examining evidence, witness accounts and investigative findings.
In the last hearing of the commission conducted on October 3, the commission sent questionnaires to senior police officers, including AIG Karachi Azad Khan, involved in the investigation, seeking answers to questions raised by the victim’s family. The sealed questionnaires were delivered through the commission’s designated Nazir, Tajammal Lodhi, to AIG Azad Khan, DIG Amir Farooqi, head of the investigation team, and DIG Farukh Lanjhar.
It is worth noting that the Sindh Cabinet on October 1 approved extending the term of the inquiry commission investigating the death of Mir Raza until October 15, allowing Justice Omar Sial to continue the proceedings if more time was required.
The Sindh Home Department on August 24 notified the formation of a judicial commission to probe the death of 25-year-old Mir Raza, with Justice Sial appointed as its head following his nomination by the Sindh High Court (SHC) chief justice through a letter dated the same day. The first hearing of the commission took place on September 1. The commission’s term had expired on September 28, according to a written order issued by the commission.
The 25-year-old owner of dessert brand Wafflix, Mir Raza Ali, went missing from Karachi’s PECHS on July 28, 2026. The next day, his body was found near the bushes alongside a wedding hall in Gulistan-e-Johar.
Police initially treated the death as a possible suicide, but the court ordered a second post-mortem exam to conclusively determine the cause of death after the first post-mortem report failed to give detailed insight into the victim’s demise. The second autopsy conducted after Raza’s exhumation found a firearm entry wound, multiple ante-mortem injuries and signs of internal bleeding, leading investigators to treat the case as murder.
The initial post-mortem had faced several objections, with the Karachi police surgeon identifying 14 deficiencies, including the absence of an X-ray, failure to collect hand swabs for gunshot-residue analysis and the lack of chemical examination of gunpowder marks around the bullet wound.
Also Read: Mir Raza judicial commission’s term extended until October 15
The investigation subsequently came under scrutiny from Raza’s family, who alleged serious lapses in the handling of evidence and CCTV footage and sought the formation of a joint investigation team. The Sindh High Court later rejected the family’s plea for a JIT but directed the relevant authorities to conduct the investigation impartially, fairly and expeditiously.
Police told a Senate committee in September that they had recorded statements from 78 people but had not found evidence linking anyone to Raza’s alleged murder. Investigators nevertheless continued to treat the case as murder, while reviewing medical, chemical, forensic and digital evidence.
The Sindh government had meanwhile established a judicial commission headed by Sindh High Court Justice Umar Sial to examine the circumstances surrounding Raza’s death, the conduct of the investigation and any possible negligence or concealment of evidence by police or other officials.
The judicial commission had so far examined police records, witness statements and the circumstances surrounding Mir Raza Ali’s death, with its proceedings raising discrepancies in witness accounts, the handling of evidence and the initial post-mortem. The commission also questioned senior police and health officials over the investigation, including the handling of CCTV footage, Raza’s phone and smartwatch, and the initial focus on a possible suicide.

title: James Van Der Beek remembered in emotional    Dawson   s Creek    reunion at Heroes Gala
description: Kevin Williamson accepted Barbara Berlanti Hero Award after helping organise benefit for Van Der Beek
content:
Kevin Williamson accepted Barbara Berlanti Hero Award after helping organise benefit for Van Der Beek
James Van Der Beek was remembered by his Dawson’s Creek family during an emotional reunion at the Barbara Berlanti Heroes Gala in Santa Monica on Saturday, October 3.
The event, held at Barker Hangar, saw series creator Kevin Williamson receive the Barbara Berlanti Hero Award. Joshua Jackson and Julie Plec presented the honour, recognising Williamson’s efforts to organise a Dawson’s Creek table read that raised support for Van Der Beek and his family.
Jackson became emotional while recalling the circumstances surrounding the benefit reading. He said Van Der Beek’s health deteriorated shortly before the event and praised Williamson for helping ensure the actor’s children could be surrounded by people celebrating their father.
Williamson also fought back tears as he reflected on his relationship with Van Der Beek, who played Dawson Leery in the series. He described the actor as the soul of the show and remembered watching him grow from a young performer into a husband, father and friend.
The writer also recalled their early working relationship, joking that Van Der Beek began his time on the series as a difficult young actor who regularly questioned scripts. Williamson said their exchanges became part of their relationship over the years.
Van Der Beek died in February at the age of 48 following his battle with colorectal cancer. His family announced his death after he had publicly discussed his diagnosis in 2024.
Mary-Margaret Humes, who played Dawson’s mother, also attended the reunion alongside Jackson. The gathering came several months after Van Der Beek’s death and renewed attention on the long-running bond between members of the cast and creative team.
The gala also honoured The Pitt actor Katherine LaNasa with the Inspirational Hero Award for her advocacy and resilience following her cancer diagnosis. Former NBA player Jason Collins was posthumously honoured with the Memorial Hero Award.
The Barbara Berlanti Heroes Gala raises money for F Cancer, supporting early detection, prevention and psychosocial initiatives.

title: Instagram turns 16 with 3 billion users under shadow of data privacy  mental health concerns
description: India leads with 480m active users  followed by the US  Brazil  Indonesia  Japan  T  rkiye  Mexico  UK and Germany
content:
India leads with 480m active users, followed by the US, Brazil, Indonesia, Japan, Türkiye, Mexico, UK and Germany
Instagram is celebrating its 16th anniversary since the social media giant was launched and emerged as a dominant force in the global digital economy, boasting over 3 billion monthly active users, but escalating scrutiny over data privacy and youth mental health casts dark shadows over the platform’s success.
Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger launched Instagram as a photo-sharing app on October 6, 2010.
The platform was acquired by Meta two years later for around $1 billion, and the social media titan grew even further with the introduction of video sharing and direct messages in 2013 and short-form Reels in 2020.
India has the platform’s largest user base, accounting for 480 million active users, followed by the US, Brazil, Indonesia, Japan, Türkiye, Mexico, the UK, Germany, and Argentina, according to Statista’s October 2025 data.
The platform is overwhelmingly youth-led, with around 34% of its global users aged 25-34, while those aged 18-24 make up 27.6% of the user base.
Instagram gave rise to the modern influencer economy as profiles with large followings are able to leverage their demographic reach on the app.
In-app shopping features released in 2020 established an e-commerce showcase for major brands and independent entrepreneurs.
At the same time, the platform is facing regulatory and legal pushback around the world amid its commercial and social expansion.
The Irish Data Protection Commission (DPC) fined Instagram €405 million ($453.6 million) in 2022 for violating EU regulations protecting the personal data of minors.
Read More: New Mexico wants Meta to pay up to $40 billion in penalties after data privacy trial
Some 41 US states sued Meta the following year over allegedly addictive features of the app that harm children’s mental health. The dispute led to a settlement in August this year.
Yasmin Ibrahim, deputy dean of the business school and digital economy professor at Queen Mary University of London, told Anadolu that Instagram reshaped the relationship between visibility, social interaction, and commerce, allowing users to turn their routines into marketable assets without a high entry cost.
Ibrahim stated that Instagram users often struggle to tell commercial endorsements apart from real social interactions due to the seamless integration of sponsored products, which places social media influencers in an ambiguous position, blurring the line between friend, celebrity, and sales representative.
The platform has also fostered a culture of comparison among its young user base.
Ibrahim said the platform’s visually driven architecture makes users evaluate and compare their bodies, achievements, and unedited realities with the heavily edited and curated lives of internet strangers.
She warned that this environment fuels and exacerbates social anxieties about not being enough, not consuming enough, or not living life to the fullest.
She mentioned that content saturation leads to a situation where users feel attention fatigue but still feel compelled to return due to the fear of missing out, while the platform allows users to consume other people’s experiences and imagine possibilities by seeing the lives of others enhanced by filters and edits.
She added that Instagram integrates ads into social spaces and transforms the social sphere into a source of commercial value.

title: ATC adjourns Imaan  Hadi bail hearing till Oct 13 after IO fails to appear
description: Judge orders separate proceedings over IO   s absence  warns of punitive order
content:
Judge orders separate proceedings over IO’s absence, warns of punitive order
An Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) on Monday adjourned the hearing of bail applications filed by Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha until October 13 in a case registered over terrorism charges and violation of Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), after the investigating officer (IO) failed to appear before the court.
Section 144 of the CrPC states power to issue an order absolute at once in urgent cases of nuisance or apprehended danger.
ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain expressed displeasure over the officer’s absence. “I will issue an order regarding the unavailability of the investigating officer,” the judge said.
The proceedings took an unusual turn when a court official initially told the judge that the IO was “out”. “Out where?” the judge asked before directing officials to summon the DSP in person. “Verbal statements will not be accepted,” the judge observed.
The court briefly adjourned before the DSP appeared with a report. He told the judge that the IO was in Gilgit-Baltistan and that his phone was switched off. He said it could take “10 to 15 days” to establish contact with the officer. “Until we are able to contact him, I cannot give out information,” the DSP added.
The explanation further irked the judge, who expressed displeasure over what he termed incorrect information provided to the court. He also directed security personnel to ensure that the DSP did not leave the premises without permission.
The judge ordered handcuffs to be brought into the courtroom and instructed the security in-charge to arrest the official if he attempted to leave after an order to that effect.

Addressing the legal counsel for the suspects, Judge Zulqarnain said, “There should be a judicial force so that the court can have its orders implemented immediately.”
Referring to the existing judicial system, he remarked that “the system of 1898 and 1860 is still being followed.”
At the onset of the hearing, petitioners’ counsel Riasat Ali Azad argued that all sections incorporated in the first information report (FIR), except the terrorism provision, were bailable. He also reminded the court that the request for physical remand of Imaan and Chattha had previously been rejected.
“This is a bail case, and the sections invoked are bailable,” Azad said, adding that he was prepared to present detailed arguments if required by the court.
Azad later questioned the prosecution’s handling of the case and alleged mala fide intent. “Look how old this FIR is,” he said, accusing the authorities of making “a mockery of the courts”.
Another defence counsel, Zafar Khokhar, questioned the IO’s handling of the case record. “It does not work like this, that the IO takes the case record with him,” he said.
Azad maintained that the court did not necessarily have to wait for the case record to proceed with the bail matter. He also reminded the court that it had already granted time until Monday for the matter to be taken up.
The court subsequently adjourned the hearing until October 13, with the judge indicating that he would issue a detailed order concerning the IO’s absence.
Imaan and her husband Hadi Ali Chattha were rearrested on September 17 , shortly after the Supreme Court granted them bail and suspended their sentences in a separate social-media posts case. They were produced before an Islamabad Anti-Terrorism Court in connection with a case registered at Kohsar Police Station.
Police sought 30-day physical remand, but ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain rejected the request and sent the couple on judicial remand. The judge noted that although they had been nominated in the FIR as members of an unlawful assembly, no weapon had been attributed to either accused.

On September 27, the court issued a contempt notice to the Adiala jail superintendent after the authorities failed to facilitate the signing and transmission of the documents and also failed to produce the accused through video link. Two days later, the issue was resolved after Imaan and Chattha signed the required powers of attorney.
On September 29 , the ATC ended the contempt proceedings against the jail authorities and separately confirmed that notices had been issued on the couple’s bail applications, with arguments scheduled before Judge Abul Hasnat.

title: Harry Potter  actor David Bradley named Birmingham Hospice patron
description: Harry Potter  actor David Bradley has become new patron of Birmingham Hospice after visiting patients and staff
content:
'Harry Potter' actor David Bradley has become new patron of Birmingham Hospice after visiting patients and staff
Harry Potter and Game of Thrones actor David Bradley has been named the new patron of Birmingham Hospice after visiting patients, families, staff and volunteers.
Bradley, who played Hogwarts caretaker Argus Filch in the Harry Potter films, accepted the role following a visit to the hospice's Inpatient Unit and Living Well Centre in Selly Oak. The Living Well Centre supports people living with life-limiting illnesses.
During his visit, Bradley also met members of the Children's Healing and Therapeutic Support (CHATS) team, which provides support to younger family members when someone close to them dies.
Bradley said he was "very honoured" to become the hospice's patron after meeting the people involved in its work.
"I met some wonderful, dedicated people and it has been a salutary experience," he said.
"I've never had such a positive reaction to just being here. I've been all around the place and been shown round by a few of the patients as well as the wonderful staff. It's been a great day."
The actor said he was particularly impressed by the number of people supported by Birmingham Hospice, which provides care to 685 people each day either at the hospice or in their own homes.
"I think if people knew more about these places, how they are run and how dedicated staff are, people would become aware enough to realise we can all help," he added.
Birmingham Hospice chief executive Paul Bytheway said the charity was "incredibly proud" to welcome Bradley as its patron.
The hospice is only partially funded by the government and needs to raise £8m this year to continue operating, according to Bytheway. He said Bradley's support could help the organisation reach more people and raise "vital funds".
Bytheway also said Bradley's visit had been positively received by patients, families and staff. "Many of our patients are going through a very difficult time," he said. "It gave everyone a real lift."

title: Sam Altman recalls seeing Andrew Garfield portray him during    Artificial    shoot near his home
description: Altman says he has never met Garfield beyond their brief exchange during filming near his home
content:
Altman says he has never met Garfield beyond their brief exchange during filming near his home
Sam Altman has recalled the surreal moment he encountered Andrew Garfield while the actor was filming Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial near his home.
In a new interview with Vanity Fair , the OpenAI CEO said he had never met Garfield, who portrays him in the film, but unexpectedly saw the actor while walking to get coffee. Altman said filming notices had appeared around his neighbourhood, although he initially paid little attention to them.
He later encountered a production crew and saw Garfield dressed like him, carrying a similar backpack and reproducing his mannerisms. Altman said the sight left him feeling as though he had entered “some weird glitch of the simulation”.
Altman said he and Garfield exchanged a wave before continuing on their way. He described the experience as particularly strange because Garfield appeared to have captured his distinctive movements. Altman has also seen the film’s trailer and said Garfield had managed to reproduce the way he walks.
Garfield previously said he had not met Altman to prepare for the role. Instead, the actor said he relied on the screenplay, court transcripts, interviews and other research while developing his portrayal.
Artificial dramatises the events surrounding Altman’s removal from OpenAI in November 2023 and his return five days later. Garfield stars as Altman alongside Yura Borisov, who plays OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever.
The film was originally backed by Amazon MGM Studios before the company dropped it following its major investment in OpenAI. Neon subsequently acquired the film and is handling its release.
Artificial is having its world premiere at the 64th NEW YORK FILM FESTIVAL on October 5, with further festival screenings scheduled later in the month.
Altman has said he is not expecting the film to provide a completely accurate depiction of him. He specifically pointed to a trailer sequence showing his character in a bunker with firearms, saying that scene does not reflect reality.
Despite that criticism, Altman said Garfield appeared to have captured his walk accurately, making the brief real-life encounter especially unusual.

title: Avengers  Endgame  returns to No  1 on global box office chart with rerelease
description: Avengers  Endgame  has overtaken  Avatar  to reclaim top spot on all time global box office chart
content:
'Avengers: Endgame' has overtaken 'Avatar' to reclaim top spot on all-time global box office chart
Avengers: Endgame has returned to No. 1 on the all-time global box office chart after its Avengers Endgame: Encore rerelease pushed the 2019 Marvel film past Avatar .
During the second weekend of the Disney rerelease, Avengers: Endgame earned $4.4 million domestically and $14.4 million internationally. The additional $18.8 million brought its worldwide total to $2.9255 billion, narrowly surpassing Avatar's $2.9237 billion.
James Cameron's Avatar originally became the highest-grossing film worldwide after its 2009 release through Twentieth Century Fox. Avengers: Endgame overtook it in 2019 before Avatar reclaimed the record two years later following another rerelease.
The latest Endgame rerelease has also performed strongly at the box office. Its opening weekend generated $86 million worldwide, making it the second-highest-grossing theatrical rerelease globally, behind Titanic 3D's 2012 rerelease.
Avengers: Endgame: Encore also opened at No. 1 domestically with $26 million. Its opening weekend came as films including Heart of the Beast, Primetime and Forgotten Island entered the market.
Directed by Anthony Russo and Joe Russo, Avengers: Endgame follows Marvel's superheroes as they deal with the consequences of Thanos erasing half of the universe's inhabitants.
The film stars Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Mark Ruffalo, Chris Hemsworth, Scarlett Johansson and Jeremy Renner.
The rerelease comes ahead of Avengers: Doomsday, which will also be directed by the Russo brothers. The forthcoming Marvel Studios film is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on December 18, the same day as Warner Bros.' Dune: Part Three.

title: Nick Reiner   s aunt speaks out on her relationship with him ahead of trial
description: Nick Reiner   s aunt Martine Singer says she has had no contact with him since he was jailed over his parents    deaths
content:
Nick Reiner’s aunt Martine Singer says she has had no contact with him since he was jailed over his parents’ deaths
Martine Singer, the aunt of Nick Reiner, has revealed that she has had no contact with her nephew since he was imprisoned following the deaths of his parents, filmmaker Rob Reiner and Michele Singer Reiner.
Speaking to Los Angeles’ ABC7 News in an interview that aired on October 2, Martine said she was continuing to deal with the loss of her sister and brother-in-law.
"I'm functioning," Martine said. "I went back to work in January, as best I could. But it's always there. It's always in my mind and in my heart."
Martine, who runs one of Southern California's biggest children's nonprofit organisations, recalled receiving a call from a relative in December 2025 informing her that Michele had been killed.
"She said, 'Something terrible's happened and you need to go over there.' It was probably the longest car ride of my life," Martine recalled.
Nick, 33, is accused of killing his parents on December 14, 2025. He was arrested near the UCLA campus and has since been held at Los Angeles' Twin Towers Correctional Facility while awaiting trial.
He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of first-degree murder. Prosecutors have confirmed that they will not seek the death penalty.
Asked by ABC7's Marc Brown whether she had anything to say to Nick, Martine paused before responding.
"I appreciate the question. I'm not sure I can answer that," she said.
Martine also spoke about the difficulty of referring to her sister and brother-in-law in the past tense.
"They were a force field, they really were," she said. "They were magnetic. They were charismatic. They were funny and loud and boisterous. The world seems very empty without them."
Nick's brother Jake Reiner previously discussed the family's loss, saying he and his sister Romy were dealing with their parents' deaths while Nick remained in jail.
Nick is next due in court on October 23 for a probate hearing concerning his access to a family trust to help fund his legal expenses.

“Contrary to popular belief, being an influencer is a lot of work,” Rain said. “You have to post every single day without fail or your views are going to drop tremendously.”
She referenced Davidson’s previous relationship with Kim Kardashian, saying, “I thought Pete would know this after dating the most popular influencer in the world, but I guess paying attention to your significant other isn't everyone's priority in a relationship.”

content:
The photo-booth strip shows a younger Dolly and Carl pulling funny faces for the camera
Dolly Parton and her late husband Carl Dean are being remembered through never-before-seen photographs displayed at her new Nashville museum, offering fans a rare glimpse of the famously private couple.
The photo-booth strip shows a younger Dolly and Carl pulling funny faces for the camera.
The images were discovered inside an old military trunk that had belonged to Dean during his time in the National Guard.
Photo: Dolly Parton’s Life of Many Colors Museum
Dolly’s niece, Rebecca Seaver, said her aunt had not seen the photographs since they were taken. Seaver told Vogue , “Dolly had not even seen it since it was taken, so she was absolutely floored when we found it.”
The trunk also contained Dolly’s simple white wedding dress from her 1966 marriage to Carl, along with her veil, the Bible she carried instead of a bouquet and a letter from the pastor who married them.
The items are now part of Dolly’s Life of Many Colors Museum, which opened on September 29 on the third floor of her SongTeller Hotel in downtown Nashville.
Dolly and Carl first met outside Nashville’s Wishy Washy Laundromat in 1964 and married two years later in Ringgold, Georgia. They remained together for almost 60 years.
Discussing their marriage with Barbara Walters, Dolly said, “Well, I need freedom. The man gives me freedom,” adding, “But he has the same freedom.”
Dean died in March 2025 aged 82, while Dolly died in August 2026 aged 80, before the completed museum opened to visitors.

title: Chris Rock says    wokeness    has created a less forgiving world
description: Rock said forgiveness should remain part of advocacy for people who feel marginalised
content:
Rock said forgiveness should remain part of advocacy for people who feel marginalised
Chris Rock has criticised what he calls “wokeness”, arguing that the movement has contributed to a less forgiving society while acknowledging its role in giving marginalised people a voice.
The comedian made the comments during an interview with David Marchese for The New York Times podcast The Interview . The discussion centred on forgiveness, which is also a major theme of Rock’s upcoming film Misty Green .
Rock said he supports advocacy for people who feel marginalised but believes it should be accompanied by forgiveness. He compared the current cultural climate with the Old Testament, saying, “We’re in the Old Testament right now,” while arguing that forgiveness is missing from the approach he was describing.
When Marchese asked about the post George Floyd period, described during the conversation as the “Woke 1.0” era, Rock maintained that helping people who need support is valuable. His criticism, he explained, begins when those ideas become institutionalised.
Rock used the Salem witch trials as an analogy for what he sees as the dangers of institutionalisation. He suggested that once an organisation is created around identifying wrongdoing, there can be pressure to keep producing targets to justify its existence.
The comedian also discussed forgiveness through the lens of friendship. He argued that remaining loyal to someone only when they behave well does not represent genuine friendship, while stressing that forgiveness does not mean accepting abusive behaviour. He said friends can still be reprimanded when they cross a line.
Rock’s comments come as he promotes Misty Green , which he wrote, directed and stars in. The film centres on an ageing actress attempting to revive her career in Hollywood and marks his return to directing following Top Five .
His remarks have prompted discussion online, with reactions ranging from support for his emphasis on forgiveness to criticism of his characterisation of contemporary social justice movements.

title: Andrew Mountbatten Windsor takes legal action against police over search warrants
description: Thames Valley Police says its misconduct investigation remains ongoing as legal proceedings begin
content:
Thames Valley Police says its misconduct investigation remains ongoing as legal proceedings begin
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor is taking legal action against Thames Valley Police in a bid to quash search warrants used in the investigation surrounding his February arrest.
The former Duke of York has sought a judicial review to challenge the lawfulness of warrants issued by a judge at the Central Criminal Court on February 18, 2026. The warrants allowed police to search his residence on the Sandringham Estate and his former home, Royal Lodge in Windsor.
Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested on February 19, his 66th birthday, on suspicion of misconduct in public office. He was interviewed under caution before being released under investigation. The investigation relates to allegations that he shared confidential information with Jeffrey Epstein during his time as the UK's trade envoy. Mountbatten-Windsor has denied wrongdoing connected to Epstein.
The legal challenge does not establish that the police acted unlawfully. The High Court will consider the arguments surrounding the warrants through the judicial review process.
A private hearing is scheduled for Thursday, October 8, at 2pm before Mr Justice Hilliard. The initial hearing will consider an application by Thames Valley Police to restrict access to court documents connected with Mountbatten-Windsor's claim. The Judicial Office confirmed that the hearing will take place in private.
Thames Valley Police has confirmed that its investigation remains ongoing and that the force is involved in legal proceedings concerning warrants previously obtained from the Central Criminal Court. The force has declined to comment further while those proceedings continue.
The case follows renewed scrutiny of Mountbatten-Windsor's longstanding association with Epstein. Mountbatten-Windsor lost his royal titles and honours amid that scrutiny, while the criminal investigation remains separate from the current legal challenge over the search warrants.
The forthcoming hearing is therefore focused on the court documents and proceedings surrounding his judicial review. Any decision on whether the warrants should ultimately be quashed will form part of the wider legal process.

title: Three remaining Pakistani crew members of MT Honour 25 to arrive in Karachi on Oct 7  FO
description: Says crew members expected to leave Addis Ababa for Karachi on the first available Ethiopian Airlines flight on Oct 7
content:
Says crew members expected to leave Addis Ababa for Karachi on first available Ethiopian Airlines flight on Wednesday
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Monday that the three remaining Pakistani crew members of MT Honour 25 had been rescued and flown to Addis Ababa, where they were expected to begin their journey back to Pakistan on October 7.
The development meant that all seven surviving Pakistani crew members rescued from the vessel had now been brought closer to returning home. Four injured crew members — Usman Ghani, Aqeel Khan, Ameen bin Shams and Yasir Khan — had arrived in Karachi on Sunday aboard Ethiopian Airlines flight ET 694 from Addis Ababa.
The same flight also carried the remains of three Pakistani sailors who died in the incident — Rafi Ullah Khan, Syed Kashif Umer and Mahmood Ahmad Ansari. Their remains were handed over to their families after arriving in Karachi.
The three remaining Pakistani crew members of MT Honour 25 (Imran Ali, Muhammad Yasin and Syed Husain Yousuf) have been successfully rescued and flown to Addis Ababa, accompanied by a team from the Embassy of Pakistan in Djibouti. The three crew members will be received in Addis…
The three rescued crew members — Imran Ali, Muhammad Yasin and Syed Husain Yousuf — were accompanied by a team from the Embassy of Pakistan in Djibouti, Dar said in a post on X. "The three crew members will be received in Addis Ababa and, InshaAllah, depart for Pakistan on the first available Ethiopian Airlines flight to Karachi, expected on October 7," he said.
The foreign minister expressed his "deep gratitude" to the Government of Somalia and the European Union Naval Force Operation (EUNAVFOR) Atalanta for helping secure the crew’s release.
Dar said the naval force had been "present in the vicinity of MT Honour 25", thanking it for its "assistance and cooperation" in securing the crew. "Pakistan remains firmly committed to strengthening bilateral and multilateral cooperation to combat maritime piracy and safeguard the security and freedom of international maritime routes," he concluded.
The oil tanker Honour 25, sailing under the Somali flag from Oman to Somalia, was hijacked by pirates on April 21. There were 17 crew members aboard, 10 of them Pakistani nationals. The families of the Pakistani hostages spent months seeking the safe release of their loved ones, staging peaceful protests and repeatedly approaching government authorities.
During their captivity, the pirates initially demanded a ransom of $3 million, which was later reduced to $1.9 million and subsequently to $1 million. All the Pakistani crew members who were killed or injured were from different areas of Karachi.
The pirates came under pressure during a rescue operation and, while retreating from the vessel, opened indiscriminate fire on the abducted crew before fleeing the ship. Five sailors were killed, including three Pakistanis — Second Officer Kashif Umar, Third Engineer Mahmood Ansari and Boiler Rafiullah. The other two deceased crew members were an Indian sailor, Tanveer, and the chief engineer from Myanmar.
Also Read: FO expresses condolences over deaths of five crew members in Somalia rescue operation
Four sailors were injured — Usman, Yasir, Ameen and Vicky from Indonesia — while Hussain Yousuf, Imran Ali and Yaseen remained safe. The two surviving Pakistani crew members later contacted the Ansar Burney Welfare Trust in Karachi using the ship captain’s mobile phone and provided details of the incident.
Puntland police said the Honour 25 had 18,500 barrels of oil on board when it was hijacked. The police had been pursuing three hijacked vessels off the Somali coast and had also rescued another oil tanker, Sibu 1, on Friday. However, 28 of the 41 pirates arrested during that operation later escaped while being transferred to jail, with several Puntland security officials accusing local police of complicity.
The Gulf of Aden and Somalia coasts have seen a resurgence in piracy since April, with at least 15 attacks recorded this year, the highest number since 2013, according to figures from the International Maritime Organisation.

title: Coyote vs  Acme    success raises questions over David Zaslav shelving film
description: Ketchup Entertainment paid  50m for distribution rights after Warner Bros  shelved film
content:
Ketchup Entertainment paid $50m for distribution rights after Warner Bros. shelved film
David Zaslav’s decision to shelve Coyote vs. Acme is facing renewed scrutiny after the completed Looney Tunes film became a box office success following its rescue by independent distributor Ketchup Entertainment.
Three years after Warner Bros. Discovery treated the film as a tax write off, Coyote vs. Acme has reportedly surpassed $100m worldwide. The result has raised questions over whether Warner Bros. could have benefited from releasing the $70m production itself.
Ketchup Entertainment paid $50m for distribution rights and pre sold international territories to help offset that cost. The distributor’s strong theatrical performance therefore represents a significant success, although the financial outcome would have been different for Warner Bros., which would have faced production costs and theatrical marketing expenses.
The film, starring Will Forte and John Cena, opened in late August with $15.9m domestically. Its reported worldwide total includes $59.8m from North America and $42m internationally.
Analysts cited by Variety said the film benefited from positive reviews, strong word of mouth and the familiarity of the Looney Tunes brand. Shawn Robbins of Box Office Theory said its performance reflected both fan support and the quality of the finished movie.
The result also contrasts sharply with The Day the Earth Blew Up: A Looney Tunes Movie , another Looney Tunes production that Warner Bros. Discovery chose to release through another distributor. That 2024 film earned $15.4m worldwide.
Zaslav had previously defended shelving Coyote vs. Acme as part of a shift in Warner Bros.’ theatrical strategy. The decision followed the earlier cancellations of Batgirl and Scoob! Holiday Haunt , which were also removed from release plans for tax purposes.
Industry analysts have argued that the Coyote vs. Acme performance demonstrates the commercial value of established intellectual property, particularly family friendly brands. However, its success alone cannot establish what Warner Bros. would have earned from a studio backed theatrical release.
The film’s performance has nevertheless reopened debate over the financial and strategic reasoning behind its original shelving.

title: Bracewell chooses casual contract as BBL opportunity beckons
description: The 35 year old remains available for the Black Caps while pursuing a Big Bash League opportunity in Australia
content:
The 35-year-old remains available for the Black Caps while pursuing a Big Bash League opportunity in Australia
Experienced all-rounder Michael Bracewell has opted for a casual playing contract with New Zealand, relinquishing his place on the central contract list to pursue an opportunity in Australia’s Big Bash League.
Left-handed batter Nick Kelly has been promoted to a full-time contract for the first time, replacing Bracewell on the list.
Bracewell remains available for New Zealand’s upcoming home white-ball series against India and hopes to add to his 105 international appearances.
“The backing from New Zealand Cricket for me to take this opportunity at this stage of my career means a lot,” Bracewell said.
“As a white-ball only player, this felt like too good of an opportunity to pass up. I’m still very much committed to the Black Caps and can’t wait to be involved in the upcoming India tour and future white-ball series.”
Bracewell is the latest in a growing group of New Zealand players to choose the casual contract option, following Mark Chapman last month.
Finn Allen, Lockie Ferguson, Adam Milne and Tim Seifert have also previously opted for similar arrangements.
New Zealand coach Rob Walter said Kelly had earned his promotion after several strong domestic seasons.
“Nick’s been a standout performer in domestic cricket for several seasons now and it’s testament to his hard work that he’s earned this first contract at this stage of his career,” Walter said.
“Introducing players like Nick to international cricket a bit later certainly has its advantages in terms of the player knowing their game and being able to trust themselves to perform under pressure.”
New Zealand’s centrally contracted players are Tom Blundell, Devon Conway, Jacob Duffy, Matt Fisher, Zak Foulkes, Mitchell Hay, Matt Henry, Kyle Jamieson, Tom Latham, Nick Kelly, Daryl Mitchell, Henry Nicholls, Will O’Rourke, Glenn Phillips, Rachin Ravindra, Mitchell Santner, Ben Sears, Nathan Smith, Blair Tickner and Will Young.

title: Ex prince Andrew seeks to  quash  Epstein search warrants
description: Judiciary confirmed the High Court was to hold a private hearing on Thursday
content:
Judiciary confirmed the High Court was to hold a private hearing on Thursday
Disgraced ex-prince Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has launched a legal challenge over search warrants for his royal homes issued before his February arrest, Britain's judiciary confirmed Monday, in an unprecedented royal move in modern times.
The judiciary confirmed the High Court was to hold a private hearing on Thursday, as King Charles III's brother challenges Thames Valley Police over the searches in Windsor, west of London, and Sandringham, eastern England.
The force arrested Andrew on his 66th birthday on February 19 on suspicion of misconduct in public office related to his links to late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
Andrew was released the same day after hours of police questioning, but remained under investigation. He has denied all wrongdoing in his associations with the American financier.
His shock arrest prompted Charles to issue a statement insisting "the law must take its course".
Read: Palace slammed over alleged attempts to bury former prince Andrew's Epstein scandal
The Daily Telegraph reported the legal challenge late on Sunday. The newspaper noted it was the first time a member of Britain's royal family has challenged the lawfulness of criminal proceedings against them since the trial of Charles I in 1649.
It said his legal team wanted to examine whether the search warrants granted by a judge at London's Old Bailey court -- formally known as the Central Criminal Court -- were lawful. Andrew's legal team did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The judiciary's press office said, "The case concerns an application by Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor for a judicial review to quash search warrants issued by a judge at the Central Criminal Court on 18 February 2026".
Andrew's arrest and the police searches marked a new low for the ex-prince, who was stripped of his royal titles last year and ousted from his Windsor home over his Epstein connections.
The government has even mulled passing a law to remove him from the line of succession.
Read more: Ex-Prince Andrew continues to 'gripe' as royal fallout deepens
Scandal has engulfed the king's younger brother since one of Epstein's accusers, Virginia Giuffre, claimed in her posthumous memoirs that she had been trafficked three times to have sex with Andrew when she was a teenager.
The former prince has repeatedly denied the claims. He settled a US civil lawsuit in 2022 brought by Giuffre while not admitting liability.
The Thames Valley Police probe follows new revelations from documents relating to the American financier released by the United States earlier this year, including emails in which Andrew appeared to share potentially confidential information with him.
In one November 2010 email seen by AFP, Andrew appeared to share with the US financier reports on his visit to several Asian countries.
Epstein had been convicted in the United States in 2008 of procuring a child for prostitution.
At least nine British police forces confirmed they were looking into claims -- some related to Andrew -- stemming from the batch of some three million Epstein files released by the US authorities in January.
However, the Thames Valley investigation appears to be the most advanced.
Its officers, who swooped on the remote Sandringham royal estate in eastern England to detain Andrew, searched his home there and his former Royal Lodge residence in Windsor, west of London.
In response to Andrew's legal challenge, Thames Valley Police said in a statement that its "investigation into misconduct in public office continues".
"We are engaged in legal proceedings in relation to warrants previously obtained," it added.
"As these legal proceedings are currently ongoing, it would be inappropriate for us to comment further."

title: German and US scientists win Nobel medicine prize for work on optogenetics
description: Deisseroth  Hegemann  and Nagel selected for their discoveries concerning light gated ion channels and optogenetics
content:
Deisseroth, Hegemann, and Nagel selected for their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics
American Karl Deisseroth and Germans Peter ​Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine on Monday for their discoveries on light and optogenetics ‌that have helped understand how the brain works.
The Nobel Assembly at Sweden's Karolinska Institute medical university said Deisseroth, 54, Hegemann, 71, and Nagel, 73, were selected for their "discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics."
BREAKING NEWS The 2026 #NobelPrize in Physiology or Medicine has been awarded to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel “for their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics.” pic.twitter.com/pkDDEBWtkz
Optogenetics "makes it possible to switch on, or off, the activity of individual nerve cells in a living brain," said Thomas Perlmann, Secretary-General of the Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet.
"This ​method is now being used in laboratories around the world to reveal the brain’s mysteries," Perlmann said.
In clinical trials, researchers are restoring vision to ​people blinded by a condition called retinitis pigmentosa by inserting a light-sensitive protein in the retina.
Researchers also hope optogenetics could ⁠improve cochlear implants, allowing more precise stimulation of the auditory nerve than current electrical devices.
The Physiology or Medicine Prize traditionally opens the annual Nobel announcements, with awards ​in physics, chemistry, literature, peace and economics to follow over the coming days.
Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel will share a prize sum amounting to 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 ​m).
🏅 The Nobel medicine prize was awarded Monday to US psychiatrist and neurologist Karl Deisseroth and his German colleagues Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for their work in the field of optogenetics. ➡️ https://t.co/706OtUItET pic.twitter.com/TtkNaMPeaW
In the early 1990s, Hegemann investigated how the alga Chlamydomonas reacts to light in half a millisecond. He hypothesised that a single protein captured light and acted as an ion channel. Nagel tested this by injecting Chlamydomonas genes into frog eggs, discovering channelrhodopsin-2—an ion channel that opens when exposed to light.
In 2003, they published that this protein could ​be introduced into human and hamster cells to generate electrical impulses using light. In 2005, Deisseroth at Stanford demonstrated the technique in rat nerve cells, and ​the method was named optogenetics a year later.
Perlmann said he had talked to all three laureates this morning, and that they were surprised and delighted.
"All three said the same thing, ‌that they ⁠thought it was absolutely wonderful to receive the prize with the other two, and they call them my friends. That it's such an honour to receive them together. So that's something they conveyed," Perlmann said.
The five original Nobel Prizes were created under the terms of Swedish inventor and industrialist Alfred Nobel's will and have been awarded since 1901, with only limited interruptions, chiefly during World War One and World War Two.
A sixth award, the economics prize, was established ​in 1968 by Sweden's central bank, ​the Riksbank.
The medicine prize has honoured ⁠some of the most influential scientific discoveries of the past century, including Alexander Fleming's work on penicillin, recognised in 1945, and Karl Landsteiner, who won in 1930 for his discovery of human blood groups.

title: Jeeno overcomes late wobble to win Lotte Championship
description: The Thai star finishes three shots clear of South Korea   s Yoon In a
content:
The Thai star finishes three shots clear of South Korea’s Yoon In-a
Thailand's Jeeno Thitikul bagged her fourth title of the year with a three-shot victory at the LPGA Tour's Lotte Championship in Hawaii on Sunday.
The world number two carded six birdies in a four-under-par 68 to finish on 21 under par at Hoakalei Country Club on Oahu.
South Korea's Yoon In-a was second on 18 under after also finishing with a four-under-par 68.
Thai star Jeeno suffered a scare coming down the stretch with a double-bogey six on the 16th that dropped her to 19 under.
But back-to-back birdies on 17 and 18 restored her cushion and averted the possibility of a play-off.
"I totally have no idea how I did that," Jeeno said of her birdie-birdie finish. "It was a really good battle with In-a. She played incredible on the front nine.
"I knew I had to focus on my game. The 16th was terrible, a terrible hole for me. But I just tell myself that it's two holes left and everything can happen."
Japan's Miyu Yamashita finished in third place on 17 under after her final-round 67, one shot ahead of fourth-placed Auston Kim of the United States.
China's Michelle Zhang and Sweden's Maja Stark shared fifth place on 15 under, six off the lead.

title: Kim Kardashian reveals how many nannies help care for her 4 children
description: Kardashian also discussed co parenting with Kanye West  particularly regarding North   s developing music career
content:
Kardashian also discussed co-parenting with Kanye West, particularly regarding North’s developing music career
Kim Kardashian has revealed that five nannies help care for the four children she shares with ex-husband Kanye West, while she remains closely involved in their daily routines.
According to the Sunday Times’ Style Magazine , Kardashian has one nanny on rotation whenever her children, North, 13, Saint, 10, Chicago, 8, and Psalm, 7, are staying with her.
Despite having additional childcare support, the Skims founder said she takes responsibility for taking her children to and from school and makes time for family dinners each evening.
“I think I am an intermediate-strict parent,” Kardashian said. “I’m extremely patient and loving. I still have a kid sleep in my bed when they want. I read books with the kids every night.”
Kardashian also discussed co-parenting with West, particularly regarding their daughter North’s developing music career.
“That is something that her dad and I have better communication about,” she said. “We make sure we’re aligned and that she’s in projects that we both approve.”
Kardashian and West were married from 2014 to 2022 and have experienced a complicated co-parenting relationship.
Kardashian previously acknowledged feeling “alone” while raising their children despite having significant support.
“People will always jump to the, ‘Oh, but you have the resources to have nannies and to have help,'” she said in a 2024 interview. Kardashian added that she was “basically raising four kids by [herself].”
The reality star has continued balancing motherhood with her business and entertainment career. She founded Skims in 2019 and has also pursued acting and legal studies.
Kardashian is currently working on several projects and is in a relationship with Formula 1 driver Lewis Hamilton. West married Bianca Censori in December 2022.

title: Lahore magistrate grants four day remand extension to two suspects in Azeri woman case
description: Separate court rejects police request for eight day extension  Nimra   s interim bail extended until October 13
content:
Separate court rejects police request for eight-day extension; Nimra’s interim bail extended until October 13
A judicial magistrate in Lahore on Monday rejected the police’s request for an eight-day extension in the physical remand of two suspects arrested in connection with the alleged rape of an Azeri woman, granting investigators four more days to complete their probe.
The developments came against the backdrop of a case registered on the complaint of the Azeri woman under Section 375A (gang rape) of the Pakistan Penal Code against three suspects at Defence C police station in Lahore.
The woman said she had travelled to the city on a business trip, where she was allegedly lured, intoxicated and raped by three unidentified men in a private housing society near Raiwind during the night between September 25 and 26. On Sunday, October 4, she returned to her home country under police escort.
Judicial Magistrate Azhar Mahmood of the Cantonment Courts heard the police request seeking further physical custody of suspects Ali Zain and Mohsin. The suspects were produced before the court after completing their six-day physical remand.
During the hearing, the investigating officer (IO) told the court that a substantial part of the investigation had been completed.
Read More: Azeri woman in alleged Lahore gang-rape case returns home under police escort
The officer said police still needed to recover the suspects’ mobile phones and conduct potency tests, and requested an eight-day extension in their physical remand.
The court, however, rejected the request and granted police four additional days of physical remand.
Meanwhile, proceedings were also held before a district and sessions court in Lahore on the interim bail petition of Nimra, who is accused of facilitating the alleged rape of the Azeri woman.
Additional District and Sessions Judge Rafaqat Ali heard Nimra’s pre-arrest bail petition and extended her interim bail until October 13.
The IO failed to produce the case record before the court. The court therefore granted the investigator additional time to submit the record and adjourned the hearing.
The case was registered at Lahore’s Defence C police station on the complaint of an Azerbaijani woman in her twenties, who alleged that three men molested her after she was taken to an apartment following a dinner outing on the night of September 25.
According to the FIR, the woman, who had come to Pakistan from Baku for business, said two women took her to a café, where three men later joined them. She alleged that the men subsequently took her to an apartment, gave her an intoxicating drink and raped her. She was later allegedly abandoned near Ghazi Interchange, with her mobile phones taken from her.
Police subsequently identified three suspects and recovered a vehicle allegedly used in the incident. Investigators also detained three people for questioning and launched raids to arrest other suspects. Police said the victim underwent a medical examination and that investigators were examining all aspects of the case.
On September 28, the woman recorded her statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before a judicial magistrate. Police told The Express Tribune that federal authorities had been asked to place the three suspects on the Provisional National Identification List after they reportedly left Lahore. One suspect was traced to Sialkot, while police also detained two relatives and a domestic worker of another suspect during the investigation.
Also Read: Lahore court grants three-day physical remand of suspect in foreign woman rape case
In her detailed statement, the woman named Muhammad Ahmed Tanvir, Syed Mohsin Shah and Syed Ali Zain as the men who allegedly assaulted her. She told the court that she had travelled to Lahore after spending five days in Faisalabad and had contacted two women, Nimra and Muskan , whom she planned to meet before travelling to Skardu.
She alleged that she was confined, threatened and sexually assaulted before being placed in a car and pushed out after she said she would report the incident to the police.
The investigation has since moved into the courts. On October 1, a Lahore district court granted police three-day physical remand of Muskan , one of the women allegedly linked to the complainant's movements before the incident. The prosecution sought her custody for investigation, while her defence denied any involvement and said her relationship with the complainant was limited to friendship.
Yesterday, the complainant left Pakistan for Azerbaijan under police escort after initially refusing to return, saying she wanted to pursue the case. Three Lahore police officers accompanied her on the flight to Baku at the request of the Azerbaijani embassy.

content:
Zayn Malik responds to criticism of alleged 'fence sitting' by resharing 2014 'Free Palestine' tweet on Instagram
Zayn Malik has responded to criticism over comments he made about Palestine by resharing a 2014 tweet on his Instagram account.
The former One Direction singer posted a screenshot of the tweet on Sunday with the caption, “This is for any confused individuals.. check the date.”
The post followed criticism of comments Malik made during his concert at Santiago’s Movistar Arena in Chile on October 2 as part of his Konnakol Tour. Malik told the crowd that he saw “a lot of political noise in the press” and said he did not think any life was insignificant.
Zayn Malik responds to the Backlash for people who claimed he does not support Palestine “This is for any confused individuals.. check the date” Free Palestine from 2014 pic.twitter.com/R05Z01QZLy
Some people subsequently characterised Malik as unwilling to take a clear position on Palestine. The reaction also included comparisons with comments made by Ed Sheeran following controversy surrounding Macklemore’s Loop Tour appearances in September.
Malik’s reshared post featured a tweet he originally published in July 2014, during Israel’s offensive in Gaza. The tweet was retweeted around 220,000 times within days and reached his then audience of approximately 13 million followers.
The 2014 post also drew criticism from some Israeli fans, with a few making death threats against Malik, who was 21 at the time. He did not delete the tweet.
The singer has also been linked to Palestinian causes in more recent years. In April, while Malik was recovering in hospital, his cousin Sasha Malik encouraged people to donate to The Palestine Project on his behalf rather than sending flowers.

The two met at a Nashville gathering hosted by mutual friends in 2022 and began dating officially in 2023
Alexis Wilkins, the country singer and political commentator, is engaged to FBI Director Kash Patel after several years together.
Wilkins announced the engagement on X on Sunday, October 4, sharing a photograph of her ring with the caption, “went and got the law involved” alongside a diamond ring and heart emojis. Patel later reshared the post.
Went and got the law involved 💍❤️ @Kash_Patel pic.twitter.com/OjZmOOrVg7
Wilkins, 27, was born in Boston in 1998. Her family spent part of her childhood in England and Switzerland before settling in Fayetteville, Arkansas.
She attended College du Leman in Switzerland before graduating from Belmont University in Nashville in 2020, according to Vanity Fair.
She began writing songs at nine and travelled to Nashville for music-related trips from the age of 14. Wilkins also had minor acting roles, including appearances on Modern Family and the Adam Sandler film Jack and Jill .
Wilkins pursued a country music career in Nashville and released her debut EP, Grit , in April 2023.
Her music includes political themes, with songs such as “Stand” and “Country Back” addressing American culture and political issues.
She has also performed the US national anthem at conservative political events, including gatherings linked to the NRA and Turning Point USA.
Wilkins has worked as a political commentator and consultant for The American Border Story since May 2025 and has served as an NRA board member since June 2025, according to her LinkedIn profile.
Wilkins has said she met Patel at a Nashville gathering hosted by mutual friends in 2022. They began dating officially in 2023, and she was present when Patel was sworn in as FBI director in February 2025.
Patel has described Wilkins as his “partner in life”.

description: They move into the last 16 at China Open
content:
They move into the last 16 at China Open
Former world number one Iga Swiatek staged a comeback to advance to the last 16 at the China Open on Monday, while home hope Zheng Qinwen survived another three-set test in Beijing.
Swiatek overcame frustration to cling on as her opponent served for the set, dominating a must-win tie-break to beat Croatia's Donna Vekic 4-6, 7-6 (7/0), 6-2.
"I was just angry, wanted to change something, because clearly it wasn't working," the 25-year-old from Poland said on court.
"Sometimes if you care a bit less because you're... probably going to lose, it also helps you a bit," she later told reporters.
She will face American teenager Iva Jovic for a spot in the quarter-finals.
China's Zheng was tested by Marie Bouzkova, enduring her third three-setter of the tournament to beat the Czech player 7-6 (7/3), 4-6, 7-5.
Zheng voiced frustration in each set at movement outside the court, including as she tried to salvage the second set on Bouzkova's serve.
But she pulled out some of her most accurate tennis to clinch the last two games and win the match when 27th-ranked Bouzkova fired long.
"I gave everything," said Zheng, who had already spent more than five hours on court in the first two rounds.
"Truthfully speaking, I felt a lot of pressure today," the 23-year-old told her home crowd, thanking fans for their support but commenting on distractions during play.
"Sometimes I'm a bit screaming in Chinese, because I really see you guys are moving, but next match I hope I will be better on this," she said.
Zheng, the current world number 54, next plays 118th-ranked Alina Charaeva, who sent out top seed Elena Rybakina in the second round.
Coco Gauff, the highest-ranked player left in the women's draw, was due to play Chinese 16-year-old Sun Xinran later on Monday.
Alex de Minaur was scheduled to play Hubert Hurkacz for the first spot in the men's final before a blockbuster clash between former world number ones Novak Djokovic and Daniil Medvedev.

Shai Hope struck an unbeaten 162 as West Indies chased down 352 to register their highest successful run chase in men’s ODIs.

title: Govt has kept  all doors of dialogue open  with opposition  parliamentary secretary
description: Says govt s policy has always been clear that  we want to take matters forward through reconciliation
content:
Says govt's policy has always been clear that 'we want to take matters forward through reconciliation'
Parliamentary Secretary for Information and Broadcasting Barrister Danyal Chaudhry said on Monday that the government had kept 'all doors of dialogue open' with the opposition, saying that the government's policy had consistently been to resolve political differences through dialogue and reconciliation.
Addressing a news conference in Islamabad alongside Prime Minister's (PM) Coordinator for Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Affairs Ikhtiar Wali Khan, Chaudhry said the government had engaged the opposition "with full sincerity" during negotiations involving PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, Salman Akram Raja, Aamir Dogar and other opposition leaders.
"The government's policy has always been clear that we want to take matters forward through reconciliation," Danyal said.
He, however, accused the PTI of failing to establish a clear decision-making structure, claiming it remained uncertain who ultimately had the authority to negotiate on behalf of the party.
"To this day, their party has not been able to identify with whom negotiations should be held, when they should be held and whose decision can actually be considered final. Sometimes the sisters take the lead, sometimes the K-P government takes the lead, and sometimes the opposition party takes the lead," he added, accusing PTI leaders of misleading their supporters.
Read More: No breakthrough after marathon PTI-govt talks
Chaudhry said the government had kept "all doors of dialogue open" and claimed that several drafts had effectively been finalised before differences emerged from K-P.
"We engaged them with complete sincerity and kept every possible door to dialogue open. As the interior minister has also explained, despite our engagement with them, the drafts had been finalised, and then a voice came from K-P and dismantled the entire process," he added.
Chaudhry accused the PTI of relying on what he described as politics based on anger and division rather than governance.
"A party whose only narrative is hatred and setting things on fire has nothing else to sell. It has no performance to show," he added.
Turning to the PTI government's record in K-P, he cited the Peshawar Bus Rapid Transit project and the province's tree plantation initiatives.
"In the province, they basically have two things to show. One is the BRT, which was supposed to be built for Rs6 billion and has crossed Rs100 billion, and the other is the trees they were supposed to plant," he said.
یہ آج تک واضح نہیں ہو سکا کہ پی ٹی آئی میں مذاکرات کے لیے حتمی اتھارٹی کون ہے، دانیال چوہدری #DaniyalChaudhary #PTI #PoliticalDialogue #Negotiations pic.twitter.com/bnTzlI9LDn
Chaudhry said the government's priority during the negotiations had been accommodation rather than seeking merely to delay the march, arguing that the central concern remained deteriorating law and order in KP .
He cited figures claiming that around 2,456 terrorism-related incidents had taken place in K-P during 2026, resulting in 472 deaths.
"The people of that province are living through extremely difficult conditions," he said.
He also criticised the provincial leadership for participating in the protest while K-P faced militant violence.
"When the chief minister and ministers are standing on top of vehicles, who is running the province. In the very province where they boast of their power and raise their fists, who are they showing those fists to?" he said.
Chaudhry also accused the PTI of repeatedly changing its political messaging.
"Sometimes it is a Pashtun touch, sometimes a religious touch, sometimes employment, and sometimes the State of Madinah," he said.
Responding to PTI's argument that the provincial government had not been given adequate space to formulate an effective counterterrorism strategy, Chaudhry pointed to the party's prolonged tenure in K-P.
Referring to the PTI government, he said, "They say they were not allowed to formulate a policy against terrorism," he said.
"You have had 13 years. For 13 years you have been sitting there."
Chaudhry said police personnel fighting terrorists in the province were protecting the Pashtun population rather than targeting it.
He sought to contrast K-P's approach with those of the other provinces.
"The line between us and you is this: look at what Sindh is doing, what Punjab is doing and what Balochistan is doing. What are you doing?" he said.
"We have to eliminate terrorism, whatever the cost."

Chaudhry also alleged that PTI's political direction was influenced from across the Afghan border, telling the party: "Your remote control is in Afghanistan."
Speaking at the same news conference, PM Coordinator for K-P said the government had accommodated the opposition's political demands during negotiations but claimed PTI withdrew when a firm counterterrorism framework came under discussion.
Khan had made a similar claim a day earlier, saying the government had accepted the demands brought by PTI negotiators but that the opposition changed its position when asked to support decisive measures against militancy.
He accused the PTI leadership of placing its political campaign above the security situation in the province and questioned why the K-P government had not prioritised what he described as the most serious issue facing its residents.

title: Marsch calls for severe punishment for Manchester City
description: Canada coach says City should face relegation over rule breaches
content:
Canada coach says City should face relegation over rule breaches
Canada coach Jesse Marsch has called for Manchester City to be punished severely over breaches of Premier League financial rules, saying his experience managing against the club left him convinced there were inconsistencies in the way it operated.
City were found guilty of serious breaches ‌of Premier League financial rules over nine seasons from 2009-10 to 2017-18, with the league alleging the club used "sham" commercial contracts to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than 900 million pounds ($1.19 billion).
The club has denied wrongdoing, saying the verdict contained material errors of law, principle and fact, and filed an appeal on Thursday against the independent commission ruling.
Marsch, who managed Leeds United ⁠from 2022 to 2023, said the disparity between the clubs had been apparent to him during his time in England.
"I think Man City should be punished severely. I think they should have to go down, and by the way, everyone knew about it. Everyone knew," Marsch told the Guardian in an interview published on Sunday.
Marsch also pointed to the 2022 summer transfer window, when Leeds sold Raphinha to Barcelona and Kalvin Phillips to City, while both clubs reported making money.
"That summer (2022), us and Man City were the only teams that said we made money. For us, we did make money, because ‌we sold ⁠Raphinha, we sold Kalvin Phillips. We had a lot left over from what we bought," he said.
"At the time, we weren't in a position financially to not save. Our ownership didn't have deep pockets. Whereas when Man City says this, I was literally like, 'Are you kidding me? Is this some kind of joke?'"
The American coach ⁠was also sceptical about City's signing of Erling Haaland from Borussia Dortmund that summer.
"When they said they got Erling Haaland for £52m, it's like: 'Yeah, OK, sure!' So, I knew there were inconsistencies in it, but what can you do? ⁠You just put your arms in the air and go, 'This is football'," Marsch said.
Reuters has contacted Manchester City for comment on Marsch's remarks.
City's appeal will be heard privately by an independent three-member board.
Potential sanctions ⁠include fines, points deductions and other sporting penalties, with relegation or the removal of titles also discussed as possible outcomes. It remains unclear whether any sanctions would be imposed before the appeal is decided.
