title: Portugal move into Nations League knockout stage
description: Ramos strikes late to secure a 2 1 victory over Norway
content:
Ramos strikes late to secure a 2-1 victory over Norway
Portugal became the first team to reach the quarter-finals of the Nations League when they beat Norway 2-1 on Sunday, but Jurgen Klopp's Germany were frustrated by Greece.
The Portuguese showed they did not need Cristiano Ronaldo, who walked out of the camp on Wednesday when coach Jorge Jesus relegated him to the bench.
Goncalo Ramos secured victory in the 86th minute after Joao Cancelo's powerful finish had levelled Kristoffer Ajer's stunning opener from outside the penalty area for World Cup quarter-finalists Norway.
After the game, Jesus said he was prepared to allow 41-year-old Ronaldo to return to the national team -- but that it would have to be the player's decision.
"If he wants to, he'll return to the national team... we can talk before the next call-up, but Cris is the one who's going to decide," Jesus told reporters.
Jurgen Klopp's Germany failed to break down a resolute Greek side in a goalless stalemate in Thessaloniki.
Germany had the ball in the net through Eintracht Frankfurt forward Jonathan Burkardt in the first half but his effort was disallowed.
Klopp's record as new German boss now reads: lost one, won one, drawn one.
The Netherlands beat Serbia 2-1 thanks to Joshua Zirkzee's winner to move top of their Nations League group.
The Manchester United forward was a second-half substitute in Eindhoven and applied the decisive touch with a tap-in from Tijjani Reijnders' cross.
The match also marked Virgil van Dijk's 100th international appearance.
New Netherlands coach Xavi is unbeaten after four games, with two wins and two draws.
Israel's players wore black armbands in their 1-1 draw against Ireland to commemorate the victims of Hamas' October 7, 2023 attack, after Irish players had worn them in the previous match in Hungary to protest the war in Gaza.
The simple black armbands worn by the Israelis were inscribed with the numbers "7.10" to mark the date of the attack.
Just as in last week's first match which Ireland won 3-0, the Irish players again bowed their heads during the Israeli anthem and the teams refused to shake hands before the match in the small Serbian town of Backa Topola.
The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had refused to host Israel on Irish soil for security reasons, following boycott calls.
On Sunday, Troy Parrott put Ireland ahead from the penalty spot after 39 minutes after Dor Peretz fouled Jimmy Dunne.
But Peretz stabbed in an equaliser two minutes after half-time, sending in from close range after a shot deflected off Ireland defender Liam Scales and into his path.
The result complicates Ireland's qualification task as they now lie third in Group 3 of League B behind Austria and Kosovo. Israel are bottom with two points.
Wales lost again, as Rasmus Hojlund slotted in a 75th minute penalty to earn Denmark a 1-0 win in Cardiff.
Welsh goalkeeper Danny Ward had kept the Danes at bay with a string of saves but he conceded the penalty when he fouled Denmark midfielder Gustav Isaksen.

title: Taylor Swift returns to No  1 with    The Life of a Showgirl  The Encore
description: Four new songs helped drive 173 000 equivalent album units in latest chart week
content:
Four new songs helped drive 173,000 equivalent album units in latest chart week
Taylor Swift has returned to No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore , giving the album its 13th nonconsecutive week at the top.
The expanded edition, released September 25, adds four new songs to the original album: “Patient Zero”, “Babylon”, “Pink Clouding” and “Cleveland!”. Swift’s return to the summit follows the album’s previous 12 weeks at No. 1, with its most recent reign ending in January.
According to Billboard and Luminate, the Encore edition generated 173,000 equivalent album units during the latest chart week. Streaming accounted for the overwhelming majority, with 136,000 streaming equivalent album units representing 138.79 million official on demand streams. Traditional album sales contributed 21,000 units, with the expanded edition available digitally rather than through physical copies at the time of the chart tally.
The result marks another major chart achievement for Swift, whose previous record for weeks at No. 1 was set by The Tortured Poets Department . That album spent 17 nonconsecutive weeks at the summit. The Life of a Showgirl now ranks ahead of 1989 and Fearless , which each spent 11 weeks at No. 1.
The Encore release also arrived alongside a high profile music video for “Patient Zero”, featuring Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell. The video premiered during the MTV Video Music Awards.
Swift’s original album was released in October 2025 and became her 15th Billboard 200 No. 1. It opened with 4.002 million equivalent album units in its first week, according to Luminate data reported by Billboard , setting a record for the biggest weekly total in the chart’s history.
The latest chart result extends Showgirl ’s commercial run nearly a year after its initial release and demonstrates the impact of the four newly released tracks on streaming activity. Billboard also reported that Swift’s “Patient Zero” was expected to compete for the No. 1 position on the Hot 100, with the full top 10 due later.

title: Hasan says Test cricket momentum turning for Bangladesh | The Express Tribune
description: They are fourth in the World Test Championship standings
content:
They are fourth in the World Test Championship standings
Fast-rising pace bowler Hasan Mahmud said on Monday Bangladesh's upward trajectory has made a place in the World Test Championship final a realistic dream for his team.
Bangladesh are fourth in the World Test Championship standings after a shock nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin in August, a result that highlighted the strides made by a side long regarded as Test underachievers.
"The momentum is coming towards us, definitely," Hasan, 26, told AFP in an interview in Dhaka.
"The atmosphere is such that Bangladesh can now dominate in Test cricket," said the right-arm bowler, who played a key role by taking 6-55 in Darwin.
"We haven't dominated (in Test cricket). Now is the time."
Hasan said the Darwin victory could be a springboard for bigger achievements for Bangladesh, who have won six of their 13 Tests in the past two years.
Bangladesh have six Tests remaining in the current World Test Championship cycle, including home series against the West Indies and England, as well as a tour of South Africa.
"If we win four matches at home, why shouldn't we play in the World Test Championship final? That's the dream for Bangladesh now," Hasan said.
The paceman, who enjoyed a successful county stint with Kent this year, has been a central figure in Bangladesh's recent rise.
Nicknamed "Mini-McGrath" after the Australian great Glenn McGrath, he believes the perception of Bangladeshi pace bowling is changing as the South Asian country produces a new generation of quicks.
"Since we started playing, the thinking has changed," he said.
"They now realise Bangladesh also has good-quality fast bowlers who can be world-class."
Hasan's aggressive approach was evident during the Australia series, where he focused on building pressure on batsmen.
"I was just doing my job and bowling. I wasn't giving them anything easy to hit. I would attack them with the short ball and keep bowling my way. If they hit me, they hit me," he said.
Bangladesh were unable to clinch the two-Test series, with Australia claiming the second Test in Mackay by an innings and 51 runs.
However, Hasan said he was confident that Bangladesh's "graph will continue to move upward" in the coming days.
"Look at how much we've improved in Test cricket," he said.
"If the fast bowlers stay in good shape and the batsmen remain in form, then we will go to a higher level."

title: No progress in talks sans meeting with Imran  Salman Akram Raja
description: Says PTI stands by CM Afridi  insists decisions on province be made in consultation with all stakeholders
content:
Says PTI stands by CM Afridi, insists decisions on province be made in consultation with all stakeholders
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said on Monday that negotiations with the government had failed over the party’s demand for access to its founder, Imran Khan, saying no progress could be made without meeting him.
“We have two major demands. One is that we should be allowed to meet the PTI founder,” Raja said while addressing a press conference alongside other party leaders, adding that PTI would not make any decision without Imran.
Raja said there had been no agreement to include Imran’s personal physician, Dr Faisal Sultan, in the panel.
“These were important issues. How could the negotiations have succeeded without them?” he said.
He said meetings between Imran and his family and personal physician, along with the issue of terrorism in K-P, remained important to the party. “All parties are concerned about the PTI founder’s health,” Raja said.
Raja said the party wanted peace and order to be maintained in the country and had not closed the door to negotiations, but two rounds of talks had ended without an agreement.
He said the party had also sought a consensus-based approach to addressing terrorism in K-P, where a peace jirga had brought together representatives of political parties and tribal elders to discuss solutions to problems in the tribal areas.
“Decisions cannot be made from a distance. How can the situation there improve in that way?” he said.
He said the government had not accepted PTI’s demand for consultation with all stakeholders, despite discussions during the negotiations that decisions concerning the tribal areas would be taken through consensus.
Read: Afridi-led PTI convoy to head towards Kohat after overnight stay in Karak
PTI stood by K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi’s position, he said, adding that decisions concerning the province should be made after consultation with all stakeholders. “We can all work together to take the country towards stability,” Raja said.
He said that CM Afridi launched the long march after the negotiations failed.
“On the day of the negotiations, I said that my daughters and I would come out, carrying flowers in our hands, not Kalashnikovs, we are not armed people. We still say that distances should not be created from closeness,” he added.
Raja said the two sides had been close to resolving the issues during the negotiations, but "suddenly that closeness was turned into distance."
He said the government committee had refused to provide access to personal physicians and had declined to work on a mutually agreed course of action. “Then what are we supposed to do?” he said.
Raja said PTI would continue to come out for “love, respect, the rule of law and the Constitution, and peace”.
The government and PTI began negotiations on Friday in an attempt to defuse tensions over the party’s planned October 4 long march. The government wanted PTI to call off the march, while the opposition sought political consensus on its demands and maintained that the protest would proceed unless its concerns were addressed.
The two sides held a second round of talks on Saturday under National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq. The negotiations continued for several hours, with the parties initially agreeing on a five-point framework that included legal facilities for PTI founder Imran and his wife, an early hearing of pending cases, and meetings with their lawyers and family members.
The talks, however, ran into a deadlock over provisions concerning counter-terrorism operations in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. The negotiations eventually ended without an agreement in the early hours of Sunday, leaving the government and opposition at an impasse and paving the way for PTI to proceed with the first phase of its long march from K-P.
Read more: Naqvi blames K-P CM for talks ‘collapse’, warns Afridi will ‘be responsible’ if anyone dies during march
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the provincial government had backed away from commitments during the final stage of negotiations, including cooperation with the Centre on counter-terrorism measures, operations in the merged districts and implementation of the National Action Plan. PPP leader Sherry Rehman, who was part of the government negotiating team, said the talks collapsed after the K-P government refused to sign a draft that had already been agreed upon by the negotiating teams.
PTI, however, said the main obstacles were access to Imran and disagreement over how counter-terrorism operations should be conducted in K-P. The party said it wanted Imran to be consulted before any decision was taken to call off the long march and sought the involvement of the provincial government and political parties in framing a joint strategy against terrorism.
Raja said the federal government wanted the provincial government to endorse actions and operations initiated by the Centre, while PTI insisted that such measures should be agreed upon through consultation. The party also said the government had declined its demand for immediate access to Imran, which it described as the principal point of deadlock.

title: Messi readies for final farewell in Argentina send off
description: The superstar closes his international career with 125 goals  68 assists and a World Cup triumph
content:
The superstar closes his international career with 125 goals, 68 assists and a World Cup triumph
Lionel Messi will bring the curtain down on his glittering Argentina career on Tuesday with a farewell friendly against Benin that marks the dawn of a new era for the South American champions.
After more than two decades of service to his country, the 39-year-old superstar will hand over the captain's armband for good as he makes his final appearance in the Albiceleste jersey at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires.
Messi will be joined for his international swansong by 85,000 spectators and several of the teammates with whom he reached the pinnacle of football at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, alongside members of Argentina's emerging generation.
The friendly marks a symbolic passing of the torch for a player whose international legacy includes a World Cup title, two Copa America crowns and the Finalissima.
Messi also bows out as Argentina's record appearance-maker and leading scorer, with 125 goals in 207 games, as well as a record 68 assists.
His farewell comes two and a half months after Argentina's ill-tempered World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey, where Messi exited in tears after making little impression.
"I gave it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance," Messi wrote when announcing his international retirement in August.
Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated.
Members of Argentina's 2022 World Cup-winning squad -- the players who delivered the country's third star -- and their families will join Messi for Tuesday's farewell against Benin, ranked 93rd in the world.
Veterans of that Doha triumph such as Angel Di María, who retired from international football in 2024, will be there to witness the passing of the torch to a new generation charged with extending the Albiceleste's golden era.
Several of the newcomers, including Franco Mastantuono and Leonel Flores, were not even born when "La Pulga" ("The Flea") made his Argentina debut in 2005 for a team whose history had for so long been dominated by Diego Maradona.
"It's going to be an unforgettable day for everyone. Everyone wants to be at this match, and now it's just about enjoying it," Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said.
Argentina's new generation has already shown what it can do without its captain, although nobody is pretending replacing a man regarded by many as the greatest footballer in history will be straightforward.
"Collectively, we will try to fill the void left by Leo," said Scaloni, who is negotiating a contract extension after leaving his future unresolved following the World Cup defeat in July.
Scaloni, who mastered the art of building the right supporting cast around Messi, will also say goodbye on Tuesday to 38-year-old vice-captain Nicolas Otamendi.
Like Messi and Otamendi, midfielders Rodrigo De Paul and Giovani Lo Celso were called up solely for the Benin game, raising the possibility that neither will represent Argentina again.
Those certain to be involved, at least from the bench, include other veterans of the 2022 World Cup who will be the standard-bearers for Argentina after Messi: defender Cristian Romero, midfielders Alexis Mac Allister and Enzo Fernandez, and forwards Julian Alvarez and Lautaro Martinez.
Tenacious centre-back Romero is set to inherit the captain's armband, first worn by Messi at the 2010 World Cup in South Africa.
Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez and Lautaro Martinez are next in the captaincy hierarchy.
They have already begun to rally around Messi's heirs, who showed their appetite for success in Argentina's first game since the World Cup final, against Bolivia in Cordoba on Wednesday.
Argentina swept the Bolivians aside 4-0, with young talents Nico Paz and Jose Manuel Lopez among the scorers.
They followed that victory with a 7-0 rout of Burkina Faso at the Monumental on Saturday, with Mastantuono and Gianluca Prestianni scoring their first international goals.
While Argentina's future is beginning to take shape, one small but symbolically significant question remains: who inherits Messi's number 10 shirt?
"We won't give the number 10 to anyone until Leo's match takes place," Scaloni said. "After that, we'll see."

title: Jangoo gets T20I call up after stunning ODI run
description: Stumper drafted into West Indies squad as cover for injured Jewel Andrew
content:
Stumper drafted into West Indies squad as cover for injured Jewel Andrew
Amir Jangoo has earned a place in the West Indies’ T20I squad for the upcoming five-match series against India after a prolific ODI campaign, with the wicket-keeper batsman called up as cover for Jewel Andrew.
Andrew suffered a finger injury while completing a catch during India’s third ODI against the West Indies on October 3.
The youngster held on to dismiss Naman Dhir at cover off Gudakesh Motie in the 36th over but was struck on the finger in the process. He was taken to hospital for an X-ray and further assessment, with scans confirming there was no fracture.
Andrew did not immediately return to the field and subsequently did not bat during West Indies’ record successful chase in New Chandigarh. He remains under observation by the team’s medical staff and has not yet been ruled out of the T20I series.
Jangoo, meanwhile, enters the T20I setup riding a wave of confidence after an outstanding ODI series against India.
The 29-year-old scored an unbeaten 58 in the opening ODI before producing a spectacular 114 in the second match. He then added 67 in the third to finish the series with 239 runs.
His tally put him third among the leading run-scorers across both teams, behind India captain Shubman Gill and West Indies skipper Shai Hope.
Jangoo has already represented West Indies in seven T20Is since making his international debut in December 2024. He has scored 163 runs in the format at a strike rate of 120.74.
His latest call-up gives the Caribbean side another wicketkeeping option while adding a batter in red-hot form to a squad preparing for a demanding five-match series.
West Indies will open the T20I campaign against India in Lucknow on Tuesday, with the series then moving to Ranchi, Indore, Hyderabad and Bengaluru.

title: Aimal urges Pakistan to build on Asian Games bronze
description: Former captain says historic medal can open doors to foreign volleyball leagues
content:
Former captain says historic medal can open doors to foreign volleyball leagues
Former Pakistan captain and professional volleyballer Aimal Khan has described Pakistan’s Asian Games performance as “phenomenal”, saying the historic bronze medal can provide a major boost to the country’s volleyball.
“It was a phenomenal performance by the Green-shirts in the Asian Games, winning a bronze medal after a long 64 years,” Aimal told The Express Tribune in an interview from his hometown in Swat on Monday.
Pakistan defeated China in the bronze-medal match to secure the historic podium finish. Aimal was particularly impressed by the quality of the opposition.
“We defeated a strong China team in the bronze-medal match and won the medal. This was the same China team that played in the Volleyball Nations League (VNL). It was not a second-string side, but the way our boys outclassed them was superb,” he said.
Aimal, who has extensive experience of playing in foreign leagues and has received offers from clubs in Oman and Jordan, stressed that Pakistan’s recent rise has not happened overnight.
“It’s not a sudden growth. For the last three to four years, our national teams have been delivering, and this is the plus point,” he said.
The former skipper acknowledged that Pakistan faced considerable psychological pressure in the semi-final against Iran, one of Asia’s dominant volleyball nations.
“Obviously, the pressure is there, and psychologically players feel it when they play against a strong Iran team, which rules Asia in volleyball,” said the spiker.
Aimal believes the Asian Games bronze will also enhance the prospects of Pakistan’s players seeking contracts abroad.
“This will do a lot for Pakistan, and more players will get offers from foreign clubs,” he said.
Around a dozen Pakistani players are currently associated with clubs in Asia and Europe. “It’s extremely good that some players will join foreign leagues, but what will the others do when they come home? They should be engaged now. There should be a league, and it is very important if we want to sustain our growth,” he said.
Aimal said Pakistan Volleyball Federation (PVF) was trying to launch a domestic league but stressed that provincial and regional associations must also contribute to the sport’s development.
“The PVF is trying to launch a league, but associations should also play a role in volleyball development. Tell me, which association has established a volleyball academy?” he questioned.
He also urged provincial governments to support their volleyball players.
“Only the federation cannot do everything. Provinces will also have to play a role. If they give some cash prizes to the bronze-medal-winning team, it will encourage them,” Aimal said.
Pakistan’s bronze in the Asian Games was its first volleyball medal in 64 years. The country’s previous medal in the sport had come at the 1962 Asian Games in Jakarta, where Pakistan also won bronze.
Aimal believes the latest achievement should raise expectations for Pakistan at the continental level.
“If we can win a medal in the Asian Games, we can also win a medal in the Asian Championship,” he said.
He also pointed to Pakistan’s impressive quarter-final victory over India as evidence of the team’s growing potential.
“India are a strong side and had spent so many days in Japan after featuring in the Asian Championship, but Pakistan outclassed them in the quarter-final,” Aimal said.
“This is a clear indication that our talent is prolific and that we have the guts to beat even the toughest teams in Asia.”
Aimal also called for Pakistan to arrange a tour of Europe, saying exposure against stronger oppositions would accelerate the players’ development.
“It’s very important to go outside Asia. Even if we play against top European clubs, our boys can learn more. This will also open further floodgates for our players to sign contracts with foreign clubs because we have the potential and are capable of playing in top leagues,” Aimal concluded.

title: We will fix it   Bilawal says if system has failed  hand Islamabad to Tharparkar
description: Says Tharparkar represents the success of Pakistan   s system  the 1973 Constitution and the 18th Amendment
content:
Says Tharparkar represents the success of Pakistan’s system, the 1973 Constitution and the 18th Amendment
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari said on Monday that if the argument that the system had failed was accepted, Islamabad should be handed over to the people of Tharparkar, saying they would fix it as they had transformed their own region.
“An argument is being forcibly pushed in the country that the system has collapsed, so provinces should be created. I do not understand the logic, but if I accept this logic for even one minute, it means that if Islamabad has failed, then hand Islamabad over to the people of Tharparkar. We will fix it,” Bilawal said while addressing a ceremony in Tharparkar at the Thar Coal Phase-III Inauguration.
“We will have the children there topping every exam. We have just seen the condition of their hospitals; we will make their hospitals 100 per cent free and bring them up to international standards,” Bilawal said.
He said the example of Tharparkar represented the success of Pakistan’s system, the 1973 Constitution and the 18th Amendment. “We should tell Islamabad that they should also run things a little like Thar,” Bilawal said.
He said he had witnessed changes in Tharparkar’s infrastructure, health and education sectors. “I can proudly say that the change I have seen with my own eyes here in Thar is not seen in the rest of Pakistan,” he said.
تھر کے بچے آج صرف خواب نہیں دیکھ رہے، بلکہ اپنی محنت اور صلاحیت سے ملک اور دنیا کے امتحانات میں نمایاں کامیابیاں حاصل کر رہے ہیں۔ تھر کے بچے CSS کے امتحانات میں کامیابی حاصل کر رہے ہیں، جبکہ ایک تھر کا طالب علم چین میں بھی امتحان ٹاپ کر چکا ہے۔ یہ کامیابیاں ثابت کرتی ہیں کہ… pic.twitter.com/t3XGtsd9d4
Bilawal said Thar was producing 2,000 megawatts of electricity through public-private partnerships, accounting for 14 per cent of the national grid, and that the electricity was being generated at the lowest cost.
“We were told that there was no need to extract our coal, that Thar coal was useless and that investing in it and extracting it did not make sense. Today, we are saving $1.6 billion in foreign exchange because of Thar coal,” he said.
Read: Bilawal credits PPP for warding off imposition of emergency in K-P
Bilawal also spoke about the performance of children from Thar in examinations. “If our children, the children of Thar, children from a backward area, are topping exams, then this is a matter of pride,” he said.
PPP chairman also accused an "orphaned" political party of practising “politics of hatred” and “politics of division” in Karachi, saying it was trying to introduce “Zionist politics” in Sindh.
“You may have heard of Zionism, Israel’s [policy] in Palestine, but they want to introduce this Zionist politics in Sindh. I want to tell them that they will never succeed,” he said.

“God willing, we will bury their politics of hatred and Thar will continue to develop. The children of Thar will continue to progress,” he said.
He said 94 per cent of employment opportunities in Thar coal were going to people from Sindh, while 60 per cent were going to young people from Tharparkar. “If public-private partnership and devolution have given you a model of development and success, that model should be implemented across the country,” he said.

O'Brien has criticised Davidson while discussing claims about their reported relationship in 2020
Singer Olivia O'Brien has criticised Pete Davidson while discussing claims about their relationship and his dating history with famous women.
In a recent Instagram comment, O'Brien claimed she was dating Davidson in 2020 and said she discovered they were no longer together after seeing reports that he had gone public with a more famous woman.
“I was dating him in 2020 and found out we were no longer together by seeing on Snapchat Daily Mail that he went public with a more famous woman Imaooo. he is an absolute joke of a human being,” O'Brien wrote.

The comments revisit claims that O'Brien and Davidson were romantically involved before his relationship with Phoebe Dynevor became public.

O'Brien subsequently clarified her comments, saying that media reports had taken her interview out of context and that she had never claimed to date Davidson.
“stop trying to start weird drama over me texting someone 2 years ago,” she wrote at the time.

title: Spanish PM calls early election after key housing measures rejected
description: Spanish PM Sanchez gambles on November 29 snap election to end parliament deadlock
content:
Snap vote is a high-stakes gamble for Sanchez whose Socialist Party trails in nearly every opinion poll
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called an early election for November 29 on Monday, in a bid to strengthen his mandate after a fragmented parliament rejected the government's key housing decrees last week amid widespread protests.
The snap vote is a high-stakes gamble for Sanchez, whose Socialist Party trails in nearly every opinion poll. An electoral defeat would spell the end of one of Europe's last few left-leaning governments at a time when the far right is making unprecedented gains across the region as a growing swathe of European voters desert the centre ground.
Read: Spain's PM calls for end to UNSC veto power, criticises US over global conflicts
However, Sanchez, a wily political operator, has proven time and again his ability to surprise those who had long written him off.
"We need to renew people's support," Sanchez said in a televised address. "We need to mobilise and win a much larger progressive majority in parliament, one that will allow us to overcome vested interests, deliver new social advances and continue transforming Spain."
Frente a sus áticos, sus recortes y su servilismo a las élites, nuestro compromiso con la gente: vivienda asequible, servicios públicos y derechos sociales. España tiene que seguir avanzando y, para eso, necesitamos que la ciudadanía amplíe nuestra fuerza en el Parlamento. Toca… pic.twitter.com/7TJYjaceP3
The premier acknowledged having made mistakes and falling short of campaign promises. "I also know that part of that social majority is dissatisfied today," he said, but vowed to fight for Spain to remain "a bastion of openness, social justice and environmental responsibility".
Spain's blue-chip index.IBEX was flat after the announcement, while Spanish government bonds were broadly steady.
The main opposition People's Party (PP) wrote "AT LAST" in a post on X, with its leader, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, set to hold a news conference later on Monday. The conservatives have been calling on Sanchez to dissolve parliament and call early elections for most of the current legislature.
Por fin decidirán los españoles. https://t.co/fNx43AuQLf
Sanchez has stood out globally for taking a strong stance on progressive issues from Palestinian statehood to defending multilateral institutions and cracking down on "tech oligarchs", even as a series of setbacks and scandals weakened his position at home.
Recently, he has been boosted by proposals to tackle a mounting housing crisis that were well received but were struck down by right-wing lawmakers on Friday, leading to massive protests by housing activists across the country.
Polls suggest a coalition led by PP with the support of Vox is the most likely outcome in Spain, ushering a far-right party into central government for the first time since the return of democracy after the death of dictator Francisco Franco.
Still, despite never winning enough votes to form a majority government, Sanchez has cobbled together a series of fragile and seemingly impossible coalitions, including voices from the far-left to the separatist right, to remain in power for three successive terms lasting eight years.
But growing fragmentation among his partners has meant the government has passed little in the way of legislation in its third term and failed to pass a budget since 2023, even as Spain's economy has continued to be one of the best performing in the developed world.
Vox leader Santiago Abascal warned the election result would be unpredictable despite favourable polling for the right. "Surveys said the same thing in 2023, and Sanchez managed to form a majority with all his accomplices," he told TV channel Antena 3 .
Sanchez took office after leading a move to oust centre-right Mariano Rajoy in the wake of major corruption scandals within Rajoy's PP. However, senior members of Sanchez's own Socialists have in the past year faced allegations of graft, dragging down the party's already weak approval rating, which has hovered at around 26-31 per cent throughout his tenure.
Against the odds, he won a second four-year term in office in 2023 despite heavy losses in earlier regional and local elections by negotiating support from a loose alliance of parties in parliament.
That was achieved after promising a highly controversial amnesty for pro-independence Catalan leaders in exchange for their support, a move still bitterly remembered by many voters as a betrayal of Spanish unity.
Sanchez won early plaudits for moves including the exhumation of Franco from a mausoleum the dictator built for himself outside Madrid, and the reform of a labour law that has seen unemployment fall to its lowest level in almost two decades.
He cemented his humanitarian and pro-immigration credentials early by saying in June 2018 that Spain would accept the Aquarius migrant rescue ship and its 629 passengers, after Italy and Malta both refused to let the ship dock in their harbours.
As other European countries have toughened their policies towards foreign arrivals, Sanchez has consistently argued that immigration is essential for sustaining Spanish growth by plugging gaps in key sectors such as construction, agriculture and hospitality and for providing revenue to prop up Spain's strained welfare system.
More recently, his refusal to agree to US-led demands to increase defence spending to 5pc of GDP while pivoting toward China has rattled US President Trump and some European leaders concerned about the threat of the bloc being flooded with Chinese goods.
Sanchez's housing measures provided a rare chance for the Socialist leader to pitch himself as the leader of a mobilised left and distract from the more politically damaging issues of the migrant crisis in Ceuta and corruption scandals, said Lorenzo Bernaldo de Quiros, economist and president of consultancy Freemarket Corporate Intelligence.
"This is a window of opportunity," de Quiros said. "If he does not call elections fast, (those topics) will return to centre stage."

title: Ronaldo can return to Portugal team if he wants  coach Jesus
description: Portugal coach says veteran forward remains welcome despite squad walkout
content:
Portugal coach says veteran forward remains welcome despite squad walkout
Portugal superstar Cristiano Ronaldo can return to the squad if he wishes, despite walking out on his team-mates, said national team coach Jorge Jesus on Sunday.
Jesus said Ronaldo can come back into the fold "if he wants to" after the team beat Norway without the veteran attacker to reach the Nations League quarter-finals.
The dispute began last week when Jesus left 41-year-old Ronaldo on the bench for Portugal's first win over Norway. Ronaldo subsequently walked out on the squad on Wednesday after learning he would not start against Denmark.
"For me, Cris, in the next call-up, if he's playing at Al-Nassr, he'll be a player who can be called up," Jesus told reporters, referring to Ronaldo's Saudi club side. "If he wants to, he'll return to the national team."
The coach said if Ronaldo wishes to speak to him before Portugal's next matches in November, that would happen.
"If he wants to, as we did before this call-up, we talked before the call-up, we can talk before the next call-up," continued Jesus. "But Cris is the one who's going to decide."
Former Real Madrid and Manchester United attacker Ronaldo is Portugal's all-time leading scorer and most-capped player.
Jesus said he had told Ronaldo he needed him in the squad for his first games at the helm after replacing Roberto Martinez following the 2026 World Cup.
"Cristiano should end his time in the national team the way he wants, he's the one who will decide how he wants it," said Jesus.
"That's how we talked, the two of us -- I said, 'I need you'. In my first call-up, I said, 'I need you, I need you to be close to me, playing or not playing, I need you'. And now I'm saying the same thing."
Ronaldo, who made his Portugal debut in 2003 at the age of 18, has said this will "probably" be his final year in football.
The forward has been a fixture of the national team for more than two decades and has played at six World Cups.
In Ronaldo's absence Portugal became the first team to secure a place in the quarter-finals, with two group games still to play.
Ronaldo's long-time rival for the title of the world's best player, Lionel Messi, will play his final match for Argentina in a friendly against Benin in Buenos Aires on Tuesday.

title: Hesson   s Pakistan  Who really holds the captaincy
description: As Hesson   s influence grows  captains appear increasingly powerless  raising questions over authority and accountability
content:
As Hesson’s influence grows, captains appear increasingly powerless, raising questions over authority
It was only a few months ago that the Pakistan cricket team failed to progress beyond the Super Eight stage of the T20 World Cup. A report emerged afterward that placed the entire blame on coach Mike Hesson, alleging that he had effectively taken over the captain’s responsibilities. Salman Ali Agha was merely used as the face of the captaincy, while the actual decisions were being made by the coach.
The selection committee had initially not included Babar Azam in the squad, but Hesson insisted that he be selected. During matches, he reportedly sent messages to the captain, putting unnecessary pressure on him. Decisions such as dropping Fakhar Zaman in the early matches, delaying the introduction of Usman Tariq into the bowling attack in certain games, or removing him despite taking wickets were also attributed to head coach Hesson and bowling coach Ashley Noffke.
At the time, it seemed almost certain that the coach would soon be sent home. But circumstances took a surprising turn. Hesson not only retained his position; after the coaching staff was removed during the England tour, he even took charge in Test cricket.
Aaqib Javed, who apparently did not like him at all, has now become as close to him as a childhood friend. This is Pakistan cricket for you. Just as Pakistan went from the brink of elimination to becoming world champions in the 1992 World Cup, the coach has similarly survived the threat of dismissal and emerged as an “all-in-one” figure.
The team’s performances do not appear extraordinary. Yet according to the statistics presented by the coach, we are supposedly ahead of even Australia. One wonders why, despite these impressive numbers, we still seem to lose so often.
Now Salman Ali Agha’s departure appears certain. After that, a new captain will be appointed. Perhaps it will be Sahibzada Farhan, who led the young squad at the Asian Games.
Despite winning matches in ODIs, Shaheen Afridi does not appear to be under consideration for the T20 captaincy because he is not a ‘yes-man’ and cannot simply be made to accept decisions against his wishes. Similarly, although Shadab Khan is very close to Hesson because of their association with Islamabad United, it does not appear that he will be given the captaincy immediately. Shadab, too, is not the sort of player who simply agrees with everything.
Salman Ali Agha was used, but he neither performed himself nor managed to lead the team to success. Just as we saw Hesson operating as a “non-playing captain” during the Asian Games, it now seems that Sahibzada Farhan may be the person who suits him best.
Pakistan had a golden opportunity to beat India in the Asian Games final, but astonishing decisions regarding the playing XI and bowling shattered that dream. Hesson appeared completely active from outside the boundary, and his instructions seemed to be followed.
There had initially been talk that a deal had been reached with Babar Azam and that he would be given leadership in all three formats. But after what happened on the England tour, he should consider himself fortunate if he even retains the Test captaincy.
Shaheen may now not even be part of the T20 squad. Otherwise, questions could arise about why he was not made captain. Babar will remain in the team because the authorities seem to have a constant fear that without senior batsmen, it may be difficult to survive 20 overs.
It remains to be seen how long Sahibzada will remain captain if he is appointed. If more defeats follow, he too will be removed and another new face brought in. But that is not the solution to the problem.
Whenever Pakistan has won a major tournament, it was not because of a powerful coach but because the captain was strong. Whether it was Imran Khan, Younis Khan or Sarfaraz Ahmed, they had freedom in making their decisions.
The coach did not select the team and then hand the captain a ready-made playing XI. Decisions about who should bowl when and what the batting order should be were made by the captain. The coach did not stand on the boundary giving instructions.
Even now, Pakistan needs an empowered leader. Whether it is Babar, Shaheen, Sahibzada or Shadab, whoever is appointed should be given complete authority rather than being kept under pressure.
When the team loses, the captain receives the greatest criticism. Therefore, he should also have the freedom to make decisions.
Salman Ali Agha was as responsible for the recent defeats as Hesson was. If the captain has been removed, why has the coach been allowed to stay?
Hesson’s contract is remarkable. He reportedly has the authority not only to help form the initial squad but also to select the playing XI. And he makes full use of these powers.
Sometimes his teams are packed with all-rounders, while at other times five openers are played together. Saim Ayub was a perfectly good batsman, but in the attempt to turn him into an all-rounder, he has effectively been ruined. Now he is struggling with both his batting and bowling.
Constant changes to the batting order have also proved disastrous for the team.
At this point, either Hesson should put in writing that he will win the next World Cup, and then let him do whatever he wants, or he should be told: “Brother, stay within your domain.” This is not tennis, where a non-playing captain can work. Cricket does not operate that way.
The PCB should also establish a separate selection committee comprising people different from the team management.
Everyone remembers the damage caused to Lahore Qalandars when Aaqib Javed was given complete authority in the PSL. Then, when Sameen Rana and Atif Rana came to the forefront and Shaheen Afridi took over the captaincy, the team’s fortunes changed.
Aaqib is now conducting the same Lahore Qalandars-style experiments in Pakistan cricket. He should be kept completely away from team affairs. His opinion can certainly be sought, but the PCB should form a separate selection committee for the squad in which neither Aaqib nor Hesson is included.
Then, perhaps, we might actually see some improvement.
The gold medal slipped away from our hands at the Asian Games. Now, a good strategy needs to be devised for the future. If everyone works within their own area of responsibility, perhaps something positive can happen.
Otherwise, Pakistani fans have already become accustomed to enduring defeats. They will probably endure a few more.

title: What is Israel   s    Sufa 53    military project in southern Syria
description: Residents report loss of farmland  grazing areas and disrupted water flows
content:
Residents report loss of farmland, grazing areas and disrupted water flows
Israeli forces restarted excavation work Sunday west of Al-Asha village in Syria's southern Quneitra as part of a project known as the “Sufa Line,” or “Sufa 53,” according to Syria Alikhbaria TV .
Military vehicles and bulldozers were seen digging near the separation line with the occupied Syrian Golan Heights, extending a route that runs through rural communities from northern to southern Quneitra.
For residents, the project has meant the loss of agricultural land, damage to grazing areas and vegetation, and changes to the natural flow of rainwater in a province where many families depend on farming and livestock.
Israel began work on Sufa 53 in mid-2022 near Hadr in northern Quneitra before extending it south through areas near Jubata al-Khashab, Al-Hamidiyah, Qahtaniyah, Bir Ajam and Bariqa toward Al-Asha.
The project includes a military road roughly eight meters wide, deep trenches, earth berms reaching about five meters in height, observation posts and military positions.
Read: Syria condemns Israeli excavation work near occupied Golan Heights
Israel claims that the fortifications are designed to prevent possible attacks by Iran-backed armed groups.
Construction continued after the fall of the Bashar al-Assad government in December 2024 and intensified as Israeli forces expanded their presence in and around the area of separation in southern Syria.
Syrian accounts say Israeli troops have moved between 300 and 1,000 meters into the area in some locations as work on the project expanded.
The impact has been particularly severe on agricultural communities.
Local authorities previously estimated that around 12,000 dunams (1,200 hectares) of land in northern and central Quneitra had been affected by Israeli construction.
In Jubata al-Khashab alone, local officials said around 7,000 dunams (700 hectares) of land had been lost, while another 6,000 dunams (600 hectares) belonging to Al-Hamidiyah and Al-Hurriyah were taken over for the project.
Residents have also reported extensive damage to grazing land, trees and wild vegetation that had provided an important source of income for local families.
Read more: Israeli airstrikes hit Syrian airbase
Quneitra media director Mohammad al-Saeed previously told Anadolu that the project had caused widespread damage across the province, while access to affected areas remained limited.
Mohammad Mazen Maryoud, mayor of Jubata al-Khashab, said the trenches had disrupted rainwater flows and contributed to soil erosion, directly affecting farming and livestock.
Residents also say the construction has come alongside repeated Israeli raids, detentions, checkpoints and restrictions on access to agricultural land.
Syria’s Foreign Ministry on Sunday condemned the renewed work on Sufa 53, describing it as a “flagrant breach” of the 1974 disengagement agreement and a violation of international resolutions.
The ministry warned that continued Israeli incursions and military activity threatened regional security and stability and undermined international law.
Damascus reaffirmed its right to exercise sovereignty over all Syrian territory and urged the international community to uphold Syria’s territorial integrity and act against continued Israeli violations.

title: Former European diplomats  ministers  officials urge EU to act against illegal West Bank settlements
description: Around 500 former officials criticize bloc over its stance  fault Germany  Italy for opposing sanctions against Israel
content:
Around 500 former officials criticize bloc over its stance, fault Germany, Italy for opposing sanctions against Israel
Around 500 former diplomats, ministers and European officials called on Monday on the European Union and its member states to take action against Israel’s illegal settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank, warning that a planned project near Jerusalem could undermine prospects for a two-state solution.
The signatories urged the EU, in an open letter cited by Belga news agency , to take measures against Israel’s planned E1 settlement project, which envisages the construction of more than 1,200 housing units near Jerusalem.
The signatories include former Belgian Prime Minister Yves Leterme, former French Prime Ministers Dominique de Villepin and Alain Juppe, former Swedish Prime Minister Stefan Löfven and former Italian Prime Minister Massimo D’Alema.
They said the project would divide the occupied West Bank into two parts and further isolate occupied East Jerusalem from the rest of the territory.
The letter described a two-state solution as “the only possible outcome that could resolve the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.”
“Despite the far-reaching consequences of the new land annexation, the EU has taken no measures to deter E1,” the signatories said, criticising the bloc for failing to meet its obligations to respond to violations of international law.
Read: UK, France and Canada sanction Israeli West Bank settlements, in support for two-state solution
They also criticised Germany and Italy for opposing sanctions against Israel.
The former officials called on the European Commission to immediately submit legislative proposals to sanction financial institutions and other service providers involved in implementing the E1 project and other settlements considered illegal under international law.
They also urged the EU to prevent all trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories.
Read more: UK prime minister vows not to stand by as 'horrific suffering continues to grow' in Gaza, West Bank
EU leaders are scheduled to discuss a range of issues, including developments in the Middle East, at a summit in Brussels on October 15-16.
Calls to suspend the EU-Israel Association Agreement have persisted amid concerns over Israel’s policies in the occupied Palestinian territories and its attacks in the region.

title: Israel wear black armbands in Ireland stalemate
description: Parrott   s penalty was cancelled out by Peretz as the sides settled for a 1 1 draw
content:
Parrott’s penalty was cancelled out by Peretz as the sides settled for a 1-1 draw
Israel's players wore black armbands in their Nations League draw against Ireland on Sunday to commemorate the victims of Hamas' October 7, 2023 attack, after Irish players wore them to protest the war in Gaza.
The simple black armbands were inscribed with the numbers "7.10" to mark the date of the attack.
Just as in last week's first match in Hungary which Ireland won 3-0, the Irish players again bowed their heads during the Israeli anthem and the teams refused to shake hands before the 1-1 draw, this time played in the small Serbian town of Backa Topola.
The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had refused to host Israel on Irish soil for security reasons, following calls to boycott the matches.
The two matches against Israel have sparked controversy in Ireland, which has long supported the Palestinian cause.
"I'm absolutely delighted this has finished, it has taken a toll on all of us," said Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson.
"I've given so much credit to the players, they have been absolutely amazing in tough times and I wish no national team to go through what we have gone through for the last two weeks."
On Sunday, Troy Parrott put Ireland ahead from the penalty spot on 39 minutes after Dor Peretz fouled Jimmy Dunne.
The Real Betis striker has now scored 10 of the last 13 competitive goals for the Republic.
But Peretz stabbed in an equaliser two minutes after half-time, sending in from close range after a shot deflected off Ireland defender Liam Scales and into his path.
The tension of the match was evident when the two squads clashed as they left the pitch at half-time.
The result complicates Ireland's qualification task as they now lie third in Group 3 of League B behind Austria and Kosovo. Israel are bottom with two points.
"It felt like a friendly .. there were no people watching, no spark in the game," said Hallgrimsson.
"There was I think lesser emotions involved in this game and I think that was the difference.
"We should have done better in the first half and killed the game."
The Israeli Football Association said Sunday that the request to wear black armbands had been approved by European football's governing body UEFA.
The Hamas-led attack was the deadliest in Israeli history and killed 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.
The massive Israeli offensive in response has left most of Gaza in ruins and killed more than 74,200 people, according to Gaza's health ministry, which is under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
Ireland's 2-2 draw against Austria in Dublin on Thursday was twice briefly interrupted by demonstrations in support of the Palestinians.
Israel has been unable to host international matches on its own soil because of security risks since the outbreak of the war in Gaza.
The first match went ahead in Hungary instead, with Ireland beating Israel following a turbulent build-up in which the Irish squad voted to fulfil the fixture after goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu pulled out a day before the game.
On Saturday, Ireland's press conference in Serbia was cut short as Hallgrimsson fielded questions from Israeli journalists, including one about an Omani pilot's attack on a flydubai flight heading for Tel Aviv earlier in the week.
The Icelander sparked a diplomatic row over the games last month by saying: "We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide. We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."
The Israeli association accused him of "stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy".
On Sunday, Hallgrimsson said in hindsight he would have done things differently.
"Today I would think I did a mistake there because my feelings and my opinion should be set aside when I'm spokesman for an organisation and a group," he said in Serbia.

title: Manchester City beat Arsenal to stay top of WSL
description: Hemp   s brace help City fight back for a 4 2 win
content:
Hemp’s brace help City fight back for a 4-2 win
Lauren Hemp scored twice as Manchester City came from behind on two occasions to beat Arsenal 4-2 in the Women's Super League on Sunday, keeping the champions top of the table heading into the international break after a fifth straight ‌win from their opening five matches.
Arsenal went ahead through Lisa Baum in the 43rd minute, but City levelled when Hemp forced the ball home from a tight angle in first-half stoppage time.
Alessia Russo put the Gunners back in front four minutes after the break but again City came back, Kerstin Casparij equalising in the 63rd minute before Hemp put them in front ⁠for the first time nine minutes later.
Striker Bunny Shaw sealed the three points in the 84th minute with her fifth goal of the season to condemn Arsenal, who are without a win since the opening day of the season, to their second straight defeat after losing 1-0 away to Chelsea last week.
The loss leaves Arsenal in 10th spot on five points from five games after a dismal start to the campaign.
Earlier in the afternoon, Sonia Bompastor's Chelsea thumped West Ham United 3-0 to put them into second place, two points behind City. They took the lead thanks to a ‌Melvine ⁠Malard strike and added two late goals through Keira Walsh and Maika Hamano.
London City Lionesses showed that they will be a force to be reckoned with in the title race, Alexia Putellas scoring twice in the first half of a 6-1 thrashing of Tottenham Hotspur, who were left shell-shocked by the pressing of the visitors.
Spurs ⁠had only conceded two goals in the first four outings, but they were hit for six as London City notched their third successive win in impressive fashion to move to third place on 12 points.
Charlton Athletic, who ⁠are still searching for their first point since being promoted, remain bottom of the 14-team table after a 5-1 hammering at the hands of Brighton & Hove Albion, with Kiko Seike scoring twice for ⁠the Seagulls.
Everton's strong start to the season continued with a 2-1 win over Birmingham City that lifts them to fifth spot in the table on nine points, two ahead of cross-town rivals Liverpool, who lost 1-0 to Manchester United on Saturday.

title: Djokovic stuns top seed Zverev at China Open

content:
Serb fights back to defeat Zverev 4-6, 6-4, 6-4
Novak Djokovic rolled back the years to oust Alexander Zverev from the China Open on Sunday, beating the top seed 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 to set up a blockbuster semi-final with Daniil Medvedev.
The 39-year-old Serbian electrified a packed crowd in Beijing, where he extended an astonishing winning streak to 32 matches and is a firm fan favourite.
Djokovic called it one of his best matches of the year, alongside his epic five-set win over Italy's Jannik Sinner to reach the final at the Australian Open.
He told reporters such battles were "evidence to me that I can still beat the best players in the world on the biggest stage".
"Things are a bit different nowadays. It's hard to be consistently playing on the highest level like the youngsters," he said.
He needed to play a mix of shots in "high-risk tennis" against the German, but he said feeling "physically pretty good" on the court after dealing all year with health issues helped him fight back.
Djokovic got off to a poor start, double-faulting twice in the first game to help Zverev, a decade his junior, break serve instantly.
Boos filled the stadium soon afterward when the umpire agreed to replay a point Djokovic had won, after Zverev complained about a flicker in the LED panels during play.
The German saw out the first set from there, but a valiant Djokovic roared back to seal the second with a cross-court winner to break serve and force a decider.
The 24-time Grand Slam champion faced 19 Zverev aces throughout the match but held steady on his own serve to go 5-4 ahead in the final set.
He then broke the world number two to take the set and the match, seemingly defying his recent physical difficulties with victory in a gruelling two hours and 34 minutes.
Djokovic will face Medvedev in the final four after the former world number one dispatched Francisco Cerundolo 7-6 (7/4), 6-3.
Poland's Hubert Hurkacz also advanced to the semi-finals after beating Karen Khachanov, and will play Australia's Alex de Minaur, who survived a gruelling test to beat Andrey Rublev 1-6, 6-2, 6-3.
Aryna Sabalenka was swatted aside in straight sets in the third round, leaving the women's draw without its top two seeds.
Czech player Nikola Bartunkova, 20, sent down four aces to beat the former world number one 6-4, 6-3 in one hour and 35 minutes.
"I focused on myself, to be calm," 34th-ranked Bartunkova said.
"She's a legend... so I'm really happy that I won the match," she said of the four-time Grand Slam champion.
Bartunkova next faces Austria's Sinja Kraus in the round of 16.
A frustrated Sabalenka tossed her racquet at a break down in the fourth game of the second set, and lost on the first match point when she returned into the net.
Top seed Elena Rybakina -- who replaced Sabalenka as world number one weeks ago -- is also out, having lost to Alina Charaeva in the second round.
French Open champion Mirra Andreeva of Russia set up a fourth-round match with Ukraine's Daria Snigur, while Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova breezed past Viktorija Golubic 6-2, 6-1.
Noskova next faces 28th-ranked Russian player Ekaterina Alexandrova.
Naomi Osaka, the 2019 champion, beat Sara Bejlek and will face either Karolina Muchova or Liudmila Samsonova, scheduled to play each other Sunday night.

title: Islamabad ATC orders Imran Khan s production in Judicial Complex attack case
description: Directs that Imran  be brought either physically or through video link
content:
Directs that Imran be brought either physically or through video link
The Islamabad Anti-Terrorism Court on Monday ordered that Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan be produced at the next hearing in the Judicial Complex attack case against him and others.
Judge Tahir Abbas Supra directed that Imran be brought before the court either physically or through video link.
The court also declared former ministers Farrukh Habib, Hammad Azhar, Murad Saeed and Shibli Faraz proclaimed offenders and sought details of their properties. It issued non-bailable arrest warrants for former Punjab Assembly deputy speaker Wasiq Qayyum and PTI MPA Hassan Khan Niazi.
The court adjourned further proceedings in the Judicial Complex case until November 5. The case against the PTI leaders was registered at Ramna Police Station.
The case stemmed from an incident at Islamabad’s Judicial Complex in February 2023, when Imran arrived to appear before the courts in several cases. A large number of PTI supporters had gathered at the complex, where police said they removed security barriers, damaged the entrance and disrupted court proceedings.

Police subsequently registered a case against Imran, PTI leaders and workers under Section 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act and other provisions. The police alleged that an armed crowd had entered the complex and damaged government property, while several people were arrested and weapons were recovered.
The case was separate from Imran’s arrest in May 2023. He was arrested by National Accountability Bureau officials from the premises of the Islamabad High Court on May 9 in the Al-Qadir Trust case, triggering countrywide protests.
Imran and Bushra Bibi remain incarcerated in Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail. They were sentenced on December 20, 2025, to 17 years in prison in the Toshakhana-II case, which pertains to allegations that the couple unlawfully retained a Bulgari jewellery set gifted by the Saudi crown prince during an official visit to Saudi Arabia.
Imran has been in custody since August 2023, serving a sentence in a £190 million corruption case. He also faces pending trials under the Anti-Terrorism Act in connection with protests on May 9, 2023.

title: Lanterns  finale ending explained  What that last choice means for John Stewart
description: The finale reveals who shot Hal Jordan and sets up John Stewart   s future as Green Lantern
content:
The finale reveals who shot Hal Jordan and sets up John Stewart’s future as Green Lantern
The first season of Lanterns has revealed the truth behind Hal Jordan’s death, while leaving John Stewart with a new role in the DC Universe.
The HBO series, starring Aaron Pierre as John Stewart and Kyle Chandler as Hal Jordan, revealed in its October 4 finale that Sheriff Kerry Kane, played by Kelly Macdonald, was responsible for shooting Hal.
Kerry panicked after Hal told her that her son Noah was a Manhunter. Noah later falsely confessed to killing Hal to protect his mother.
The finale also confirmed that Noah is a Manhunter hybrid. Showrunner Chris Mundy explained the character’s conflict between his programming and his human upbringing.
“What’s programming and what’s free will? He was born from a human and he was raised by a human. He was loved and nurtured, but he’s definitely the other, too,” Mundy told EW .
Noah ultimately asks John to kill him because he fears what he could become, but John refuses.
The finale also changes John’s future as Green Lantern. He uses an unauthorised lantern containing yellow energy linked to fear and chooses to operate independently from the Guardians.
“We wanted John to take [the role] on his terms,” Mundy told the LA Times.
Hal remains dead despite suggestions that he could potentially return. Damon Lindelof told TheWrap, “We knew that we didn’t want it to be a fake-out, in order for all of the emotional progression to feel real and earned.”
John is also set to appear in Man of Tomorrow , while HBO has not officially renewed Lanterns for a second season.

Government-PTI standoff weighs on sentiment as falling oil prices fail to calm investors
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) came under intense selling pressure on Monday, with the benchmark KSE-100 index plunging 2,288 points as renewed political tensions at home weighed heavily on investor sentiment, while falling international oil prices failed to provide relief.
The benchmark settled at 165,867.32, down 2,288.17 points, or 1.36%, from the previous close of 168,155.49. The index hit an intraday high of 167,918.37 and a low of 165,764.21, reflecting persistent volatility throughout the session.
The sell-off came amid heightened domestic political anxiety after government- Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) talks collapsed without a breakthrough, with the PTI pressing ahead with its march towards Islamabad. Differences over counterterrorism policy and access to jailed PTI founder Imran Khan remained among the key sticking points, deepening concerns over renewed political confrontation.
Read More: Oil slips as Middle East crude exports rise, G7 to release stocks
The market remained under pressure despite a decline in international oil prices. Crude prices fell as rising Middle East exports and the planned release of oil stocks by G7 nations boosted supply prospects, offsetting concerns over further damage to Gulf oil infrastructure as the US-Israeli war on Iran drags on.
The decline in oil prices, which could ease pressure on Pakistan’s external account and inflation outlook, failed to offset the impact of domestic uncertainty on investor confidence.
According to Arif Habib Limited (AHL), 8 shares rose while 91 fell, with Pakistan Oilfields (+1.16%), Tariq Glass Industries (+0.81%) and Highnoon Laboratories (-0.23%) contributing the most to index gains. Alternatively, UBL (-1.57%), Engro Holdings (-1.77%) and HBL (-2.34%) were the biggest index drags.
Meanwhile, the party of Pakistan's former PM Imran Khan have begun a march towards Islamabad after talks with the government broke down over demands including access to the jailed leader.
Authorities have placed shipping containers and other roadblocks around Islamabad to prevent demonstrators from entering the capital Yemen's government launched a full-scale military campaign to recapture Houthi-held territory after weeks of escalating conflict between the Iran-backed group and Saudi Arabia. With the downside target of 166k reached, the potential for a near-term pullback rises; however, additional downside targets remain viable in the coming weeks, AHL wrote.
Cumulatively, trading volume fell to 441.8 million shares from 493.9 million in the previous session. Shares of 499 companies were traded in the ready market, with 55 stocks closing higher, 409 lower and 35 unchanged. First National Equities was the volume leader, with 50.3 million shares changing hands. Its stock fell Rs0.05 to close at Rs1.17.

title: UN chief heads to Islamabad to boost Pakistan led US Iran peace talks
description: UN Chief heads to Islamabad to boost Pakistan led US Iran peace talks
content:
Secretary-general has consistently praised Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts in the Middle East conflict
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres left New York for Islamabad at night earlier for a four-day trip during which he will discuss Pakistan’s mediatory role in the US conflict with Iran as well as its “constructive role” in supporting negotiations between the two countries, among other matters.
During the visit –at the invitation of the Government of Pakistan — the UN chief will meet with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar as well as senior government officials. He will also meet with President Asif Ali Zardari.
“Over the years, the Secretary-General has seen firsthand how Pakistan has stood by others, having its own people serve under the United Nations flag, and using its diplomacy and mediation to bring parties together when dialogue is most needed,” UN Spokesperson Stephane Dujarric told APP while discussing the UN leader’s visit to Pakistan.
“This spirit is something we have seen time and again over the years, and it is one of Pakistan’s greatest contributions to our shared world,” he added.
The secretary-general has consistently praised Pakistan’s intense diplomatic efforts in the Middle East conflict , which led to the Memorandum of Understanding that established a ceasefire.
Also Read: Pakistan plans fresh diplomatic push
Speaking during his final press conference ahead of the 81st UN General Assembly high-level debate last month, the UN chief strongly advocated for a return to dialogue to bring a peaceful end to the war following the breakdown of the ceasefire.
Guterres is due to step down as the UN secretary-general at the end of this year after serving two five-year terms.
The secretary-general last visited Pakistan in 2022 , when the country’s vast areas were impacted by the devastating Monsoon floods. It was a solidarity visit that made a deep impression on the flood-hit people.
The UN chief will again visit the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), where he will see firsthand the progress Pakistan has made in strengthening its preparedness and resilience since the floods.
In Islamabad, the Secretary-General will also visit the headquarters of the United Nations Military Observer Group in India and Pakistan, otherwise known as UNMOGIP, which monitors the Line of Control (LoC) in the disputed Jammu and Kashmir.
The Secretary-General is expected to be back in New York on this Thursday.

title: US removes B 1 bombers from UK base amid security concerns
description: Redeployment of B 1 bombers follows arrests of 6 suspects in connection with foiled attack on RAF Fairford facility
content:
Redeployment follows arrests of 6 suspects in connection with foiled attack on RAF Fairford facility
The United States removed its B-1 bombers from a UK air base one ​week after several men were arrested there on ‌suspicion of preparing terrorist acts, a Pentagon official said on Sunday.
A dozen B-1 bombers were stationed at RAF Fairford air base, located ​northwest of London. The planes had been used ​for US strikes on Iran.
"While operational security precluded ⁠us from confirming the movement of our assets and ​forces in real-time, we can acknowledge now that all US ​bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have redeployed to their home stations in the United States," a Pentagon spokesman wrote in ​an email.
Read: Men arrested in major incident at UK air base used by US
Britain has "strong indications" that Iran was involved in a suspected ​plot targeting the base, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday. ‌Iran ⁠said accusations linking Tehran to the alleged plan were baseless and summoned the British ambassador in Tehran over the issue.
The Wall Street Journal first reported that the aircraft were ​removed from ​the base ⁠amid security concerns over suspected terror plots against the facility.
The British government had allowed the ​US to use bombers based at Fairford ​to ⁠strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
US President Donald Trump said those involved in the ⁠plot ​had planned "big damage", while US Secretary ​of State Marco Rubio also pointed to the "hands of a foreign actor."
British police were questioning five men last week on Monday on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences after they were detained near an air base that has been used by the United States to strike Iran.
Officers detained the five men in the early hours of Sunday after they received a tip-off that three large white vans had been seen heading to the military airfield of RAF Fairford in the west of England.
US President Donald Trump said the suspects had been looking to do "big damage" and had been under investigation by British and US authorities. However, a local farmer said she had tipped off police after seeing a group of "hooded and masked men" running into the fields.

title: CM Afridi urges PTI workers to join long march as convoy enters Kohat
description: Afridi announces long march will resume its journey towards Peshawar from University Chowk at 3pm on Tuesday
content:
Announces long march will resume its journey towards Peshawar from University Chowk at 3pm on Tuesday
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi urged PTI workers to join the long march as the convoy reached the Lachi tehsil of Kohat on Monday.
CM Afridi, while addressing the long march in Kohat, thanked the people of the city for their “magnificent welcome”, adding that the "people of Kohat will completely change the atmosphere in Kohat tomorrow".
Afridi further announced that the long march would resume its journey towards Peshawar from University Chowk at 3pm on Tuesday.
“I am a soldier of Imran Khan. Even if the whole world comes together, it cannot put a price on me,” Afridi said, adding that the combined power of the world could not frighten him.
میں عمران خان کا سپاہی ہوں پوری دنیا کی دولت اکٹھی ہوجائے مجھے خرید نہیں سکتی پوری دنیا کی طاقت اکٹھی ہوجائے مجھے جھکا نہیں سکتی ۔ آج ہمارا کوہاٹ میں پڑاؤ ہوگا کل ان شاء اللہ تین بجے کوہاٹ سے پشاور کی جانب روانہ ہونگے۔ آپ نے بڑی تعداد میں نکل کر عمران خان اور ان کی فیملی کو ناحق… pic.twitter.com/Avgnr3BhPO
“Our struggle is a long one. We must not tire ourselves out. The T20 match will begin on October 8,” he underlined.
“We have to convey the message that Khyber Pakhtunkhwa belongs to Imran Khan, belonged to Imran Khan and will remain Imran’s Khan's,” he said.
Earlier on Monday, Afridi led the PTI convoy towards Kohat after spending the night in Karak, as the party resumed its long march following the collapse of talks between the government and opposition.
The march began on Sunday from Lakki Marwat after government-opposition talks failed to resolve a dispute over the PTI’s planned protest. The convoy later in the night reached Karak, where CM Afridi addressed participants at Khatam-e-Nabuwwat Chowk on the Bannu-Karak border. Internet services were also suspended in Karak.
Addressing the gathering before moving towards Kohat, CM Afridi thanked the people of Karak for welcoming marchers from across southern K-P and said renewed violence in the province was the result of what he called a deliberate policy failure.
He sharply criticised the country’s counterterrorism policy, saying Pakhtuns were again bearing the cost of what he described as flawed decisions. CM Afridi also responded to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who had described him as “immature” a day earlier.
“An establishment operative sits on television and says that I am immature,” CM Afridi said. “If standing with my people is immaturity, then I will commit this immaturity again and again.”
“If loving the country is immaturity, then I will commit this immaturity again and again,” he added. CM Afridi alleged that the country was being divided because of flawed policies and accused those in power of promoting provincial divisions and prejudice.
“Because of your wrong policies, the country is being divided. Those who have been imposed want to divide Pakistan and create prejudice in the country,” he said. “I am Imran Khan’s player. I have said ‘absolutely not’ to the powerful,” he added.
The chief minister also accused what he called a dominant “mindset” of treating K-P unfairly.
Read: ‘Absolutely not’: CM Afridi rejects ‘closed-room’ decisions on military operations in K-P
CM Afridi also referred to remarks attributed to Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz regarding security threats, arguing that such statements risked deepening divisions between provinces.
“Our democratic demands will have to be accepted. The policy made in Pakistan will have to be in the interest of the people,” he said. Turning to PTI’s political campaign, Afridi reiterated his support for jailed former prime minister Imran Khan and portrayed the march as part of a wider struggle against the existing political system.
“There is only one leader of the whole of Pakistan, and his name is Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi. Imran Khan is the heartbeat of our hearts. Ninety per cent of people want Imran Khan,” he added. CM Afridi claimed only Imran could pull Pakistan out of its current difficulties and restore respect for state institutions.
CM Afridi said he saw growing resentment against the political system across the country and claimed supporters from Khyber to Karachi wanted to join the mobilisation towards Islamabad.
He praised Imran for remaining in prison rather than compromising for political relief.
“We have to fight the battle for true freedom alongside Imran Khan.” He called on supporters from across Pakistan to gather in Swabi, where he said the next phase of PTI’s strategy would be announced.
The march is due to continue towards Peshawar after covering the southern districts. According to the route announced by Afridi, caravans from Kohat, Hangu, Kurram and Orakzai will join the procession on Tuesday before it travels from Kohat towards Peshawar.
The convoy is then scheduled to move through Peshawar, Charsadda and Mohmand before reaching Khairabad on October 8, where the next phase of the march was to be announced.
The march followed a failure by the government and opposition to reach an agreement over the PTI’s protest.
The talks, chaired by National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq, ended on Saturday without a breakthrough. The government wanted the PTI to cancel the march, while the opposition sought assurances that a meeting with jailed PTI founder Imran Khan would be facilitated.
PTI leaders subsequently said the march would proceed as planned. CM Afridi announced that its first phase would begin from Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat on Sunday, with caravans from several southern districts joining the procession.
K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi warned on Sunday that an emergency could be imposed if necessary to “save the province”, as the PTI began its planned long march. He said the president, prime minister and other institutions could consider imposing an emergency if they believed the situation in the province had deteriorated.
Kundi also issued a warning to those taking part in the march, saying, “If an emergency is imposed, I alone will be enough for them.” He claimed PTI workers were currently “hiding and getting themselves arrested”.
CM Afridi, addressing participants of the march at Khatam-e-Nabuwwat Chowk on the Bannu-Karak border, rejected military operations and drone attacks in K-P and said decisions affecting the province should not be made in “closed rooms”.
He said the southern districts had repeatedly been subjected to terrorism and military operations, while also suffering collateral damage from drone attacks. The chief minister also rejected the possibility of governor’s rule or an emergency in the province, saying the PTI founder’s “vision and policy” would prevail in K-P.
