content:
Reggie McFadden, known for 'In Living Color', has died in Tanzania at 57, his sister confirmed
Reggie McFadden, the comedian and actor known for his work on In Living Color , has died at the age of 57.
McFadden’s sister, Bernice McFadden, confirmed his death to The Hollywood Reporter , saying the U.S. State Department notified the family that he had died in Tanzania. McFadden had been living in the country for several years. A cause of death was not disclosed.
Born in Brooklyn, McFadden appeared on In Living Color from 1993 to 1994, playing various characters during his run on the sketch comedy series.
His television credits also included appearances on Martin, Hangin’ With Mr. Cooper, Coach, Moesha, Getting Personal and Curb Your Enthusiasm.
McFadden also worked in film, with credits including Jacob’s Ladder and Little Nicky. Beyond acting, he had a comedy special on Comedy Central and was a regular performer in Las Vegas.
News of McFadden’s death prompted tributes from fellow comedians. Comic Tony Luewellyn wrote on Facebook, “Rest in peace, fellow comedian, Reggie Mcfadden,” before adding, “Another fallen veteran comedy brother!”
McFadden had also pursued business interests in Tanzania. His Facebook page states that he was the owner of a gold mining company and an entertainment production company in the country.
McFadden is survived by family members, including his sister Bernice, who confirmed his death.

Brent crude fell 66 cents, 0.65%, to $101.59 a barrel at 0740 PKT; US WTI at $90.12 a barrel, down 95 ​cents, 1.03%
Oil prices edged lower on Monday as rising ​Middle East crude exports and a release of oil stocks by the Group of Seven ‌nations boosted supplies, offsetting concerns about further damage to Gulf oil infrastructure amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Brent crude futures fell 66 cents, or 0.65%, to $101.59 a barrel at 0240 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $90.12 a barrel, down 95 ​cents, or 1.03%.
Brent gave up most of its gains last week while WTI was 1.6% lower ​after G7 countries agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from ⁠emergency reserves and pledged to refrain from energy export restrictions after pressure from US President Donald Trump.
The ​release will add to Middle Eastern crude exports, which rose above pre-war levels in four of the seven days of ​the final week of September, shipping data showed on Monday, despite attacks on vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz.
"The G7 decision to tap strategic reserves is taking some of the immediate supply anxiety out of the price, while there's a growing view ​that Saudi export volumes are moving back toward pre-war levels, even if those barrels are still moving at ​higher cost and via less efficient routes," said Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade.
"That combination is enough to subdue prices ‌for now ⁠even though the risks of further damage to energy infrastructure around the Gulf region haven't gone away."

description: President Zardari  PM Shehbaz pay tribute to security forces  say campaign will continue until terrorism is eradicated
content:
President Zardari, PM Shehbaz pay tribute to security forces, say campaign will continue until terrorism is eradicated
Security forces killed three terrorists during an Intelligence-Based Operation (IBO) in Dera Ismail Khan, Radio Pakistan reported on Monday, citing security sources.
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif separately paid tribute to the security forces following the operation, which came a day after eight terrorists, including three key commanders, were killed in another IBO in the district.
President Zardari said effective operations by security forces were playing an important role in dismantling terrorist networks and vowed that the designs of militant elements operating with external support would be thwarted.
صدرِ مملکت آصف علی زرداری نے کہا ہے کہ خیبرپختونخوا سے دہشت گردی کے مکمل خاتمے کے لیے سیکیورٹی فورسز کی کارروائیاں قابلِ تحسین ہیں۔ انھوں نے ڈیرہ اسماعیل خان میں آپریشن میں تین خارجی دہشت گردوں کو جہنم واصل کرنے پر سیکیورٹی فورسز کی تعریف کی۔ صدر آصف علی زرداری نے کہا کہ… pic.twitter.com/H5AoBeUZuy
He said operations against Fitna al-Khawarij under the Azm-e-Istehkam framework would continue until terrorism was eliminated, according to remarks carried by state media.
The term Fitna al-Khawarij is used by the state for terrorists affiliated with the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
Read also: Pakistan launches ‘Operation Azm-e-Istehkam’ to eradicate terrorism
PM Shehbaz, meanwhile, said successful operations against Fitna al-Khawarij were dealing a "heavy blow" to terrorist networks.
He said counterterrorism operations would continue until the menace was eradicated, adding that security forces remained determined to purge Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and the rest of the country of terrorism.
وزیراعظم شہباز شریف کا ڈیرہ اسماعیل خان میں 3 خارجی دہشت گردوں کو جہنم واصل کرنے پر سیکیورٹی فورسز کو خراجِ تحسین فتنہ الخوارج کے خلاف کامیاب کارروائیاں دہشت گردوں کے نیٹ ورکس پر کاری ضرب ہیں، وزیراعظم #ShehbazSharif #SecurityForces #CounterTerrorism #Terrorism pic.twitter.com/wsPL1sFaiQ
The prime minister reiterated that the state remained steadfast in its resolve to eliminate Fitna al-Khawarij .
Dera Ismail Khan has witnessed repeated terrorist violence as well as counterterrorism operations in recent months.
On September 26, a suicide bomber targeted a joint Customs, police and Excise checkpoint in the district's Darazinda tehsil, killing 13 people, including two women, a young girl and a Customs inspector. Twenty-six others were reported injured.
Security forces have stepped up intelligence-based operations across K-P amid a resurgence in terrorist activity, particularly in districts bordering or close to Afghanistan.
In September, the military said 21 terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij were killed in multiple engagements across K-P between September 3 and 5, including terrorists attempting to infiltrate across the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.
Islamabad has repeatedly maintained that militant groups, particularly the TTP, operate from sanctuaries inside Afghanistan and has urged the Afghan Taliban authorities to prevent their territory from being used for attacks against Pakistan.

title: US arrests alleged Chinese agent over covert surveillance operation | The Express Tribune
description: FBI arrested Wanying Zhang at Los ​Angeles International Airport a day earlier before her planned departure to China
content:
FBI arrested Wanying Zhang at Los ​Angeles International Airport a day earlier before her planned departure to China
US authorities arrested ‌a California woman a day earlier and accused her of spying on a son of Taiwan's president at the behest of Chinese officials, the FBI said.
The FBI arrested Wanying Zhang, also known as Heather, at Los ​Angeles International Airport a day earlier before her planned departure to China, the agency ​said in a statement. Authorities charged Zhang, 34, of Irvine, California, with ⁠acting as an unregistered foreign agent.
Zhang surveilled a son of Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te, ​the FBI said. The agency did not directly name Zhang's alleged target, but later shared a ​New York Post report identifying him as Lai Ting-yu, a US resident.
Taiwan's presidential office described Zhang's actions as a "typical case of transnational repression" and thanked the US government for protecting Taiwanese citizens.
Read More: China will not tolerate independence for Taiwan, Xi tells island's opposition leader
"Our country expresses ​the strongest condemnation of such barbaric conduct that disregards human rights and the sovereignty of ​nations," spokesperson Karen Kuo said in a statement.
China's foreign ministry did not respond to a request for ‌comment.
The Justice Department said Zhang travelled to Seattle in 2025 at the direction of Chinese officials ​and sent them ​photos, video and license ⁠plate information of the Taiwanese president's son and his family.
Zhang used tradecraft to avoid detection and never notified Washington that she was ​acting for a foreign government, Bill Essayli, the first assistant US attorney ​for the ⁠Central District of California, said in a statement.
It was not immediately clear whether Zhang has a defence attorney. She will appear today in a Los Angeles federal court, Essayli said.
Washington does ⁠not have ​formal diplomatic ties with Taiwan , but the United States ​is the island's most important international backer and weapons supplier.

title: Yemeni govt forces recapture Red Sea port of Mokha  Bab el Mandeb Strait from Houthis
description: Saudi led coalition says 100 fighter jets participated in the  Dawn of Yemen  military operation against Houthis
content:
Saudi-led coalition says 100 fighter jets participated in the 'Dawn of Yemen' military operation against Houthis
Yemeni pro-government forces recaptured Mokha, a Red Sea port city in western Taiz province in southwestern Yemen, from the Houthi group on Monday after “fierce fighting,” Yemen’s state news agency SABA reported.
The Nation’s Shield Forces, Giants Brigades and Tihama Resistance, backed by the Popular Resistance, took control of the city with air support, a military source told the agency.
The Houthis had controlled Mokha since early September, the source said.
Fighting at several positions surrounding the city involved various types of weapons and left Houthi fighters dead and wounded, according to the source.
🔴 Yemen’s armed forces say the Giants Brigades, the National Shield forces and the Tihama Brigades recaptured the port city of Mokha after violent clashes with the Houthis 🔴 The armed forces are pursuing Houthi elements in Mokha and are combing the city and securing it pic.twitter.com/cuuMrxWlDh
Several Houthi fighters were captured, while others fled, the source added, without providing casualty or prisoner figures.
Yemen's army said earlier on Monday that government forces had taken control of the strategic Bab el-Mandeb area from the Houthis as part of the ongoing military operation, “Dawn of Yemen”.
Military spokesman Lt Col Majid Abdullah al-Nuzayli said the pro-government Southern Giants Brigades and Nation’s Shield forces had “successfully taken control of Bab el-Mandeb.”
In a series of statements on X, al-Nuzayli said government forces also took control of Dhubab airport and cut the road between Dhubab and Mokha.
NEW: Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces say they have seized control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. pic.twitter.com/RsOJL1up7t
He said hundreds of Houthi fighters had been surrounded in the Dhubab area and called on them to surrender, adding that some Houthi fighters later fled by boat via the sea.
Earlier in the day, Yemen's armed forces said they had begun a "strategic offensive" in Yemen's capital Sanaa.
The Houthis have held the capital and vast parts of the northwest, where most of the population lives.
The Yemeni army said earlier that government forces had seized the Dhubab district and strategic positions around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait following clashes with the Houthis.
Yemen’s official Saba news agency said forces from the Nation’s Shield and the pro-government Southern Giants Brigades, backed by the Popular Resistance, took control of Dhubab in western Taiz province.
A military source told Saba that the forces launched a large-scale operation with air support targeting Houthi positions and forces across several areas of the district.
The forces advanced and took control of key positions while cutting supply lines and routes leading to Bab el-Mandeb, the source said.
The source said an unspecified number of Houthi fighters were killed or injured in the clashes, while several military vehicles and equipment were destroyed or damaged.
The Southern Giants Brigades separately announced the launch of what they called a “decisive” military operation against the Houthis in the Bab el-Mandeb area.
Saudi-led coalition says 100 fighter jets involved in Yemen operation against Houthis
The Saudi-led coalition said Monday that 100 fighter jets had participated in the ongoing “Dawn of Yemen” military operation against the Houthis.
The coalition said 324 “high-value targets” had been destroyed since the operation began.
In separate statements, it said it was providing round-the-clock air support to Yemeni government forces on the ground and air protection for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, adding that operations against moving targets were continuing.
Yemeni army says 1,747 Houthis ‘neutralised’ in over 1,100 military operations
The Yemeni army said that its forces had “neutralised” 1,747 Houthi members in 1,122 military operations across several fronts in the country.
Military spokesman Majed Abdullah al-Nuzaili said in a statement on US social media platform X that the operations targeted artillery and rocket-launcher positions, defensive fortifications, approach and advance routes, supply lines and means, reinforcements and military buildups, as well as command structures and command-and-control centres belonging to the Houthis.
He said the operations were conducted in Saada, Al-Jawf and Taiz provinces, as well as along Yemen’s western coast.
According to al-Nuzaili, the operations involved warplanes, drones, artillery, missiles, rocket launchers, and snipers.
Read: Houthis claim missile and drone attacks on Saudi Aramco after 50 strikes on Yemen
He said the operations also destroyed or disabled 364 military vehicles and transport and supply assets.
Al-Nuzaili added that government forces would continue their operations to retake state territory and institutions and extend national sovereignty.
Presidential Leadership Council Chairman Rashad al-Alimi on Sunday announced the launch of comprehensive military operations against the Houthis, saying the armed forces, security forces and other military formations had been ordered to retake the territory held by the group.
Yemen has been mired in conflict since the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa and several provinces in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.
Fighting has intensified since July, with a major escalation in September that saw the Houthis take control of the strategic city of Mokha, and advance to Mayyun Island overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The group has also targeted Saudi Arabia, including energy sites.
Saudi-led coalition pledges continued support for Yemeni government against Houthis
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen pledged on Sunday to continue supporting the Yemeni government and armed forces in efforts to restore state institutions and end the Houthi takeover.
In a statement, coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki described Houthi attacks against Yemenis as "flagrant violations that have brought calamity and suffering to the Yemeni people for many years."
He accused the group of imposing internal blockades, forcibly displacing residents, looting resources and diverting them toward the "war effort."
Al-Maliki also accused the Houthis of recruiting children and damaging Yemen's “social fabric.
He said Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including attempts to target Mecca and Medina, warranted continued measures to deter the group.
Al-Maliki also cited attacks on Riyadh, Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan, Najran, Taif and Yanbu.
He cited attempts to target Saudi vessels in the southern Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, describing them as a "threat to regional and international security, freedom of navigation and international trade."
Al-Maliki affirmed Saudi Arabia's "inherent right" to defend its sovereignty, protect its security and take operational measures to deter the Houthis and halt their violations.
Saudi Arabia and the coalition would continue to stand alongside Yemen until state institutions are restored, he said.
He added that the coalition would also continue its support until the Houthi threat to maritime navigation in the southern Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb is ended.
Earlier Sunday, Yemeni Presidential Leadership Council Chairman Rashad al-Alimi announced comprehensive military operations against the Houthis to reclaim the remaining territory under their control.
The Yemeni army also announced the launch of what it called the "battle of liberation" to restore state institutions and end the Houthi takeover.

title: Perishable food items consumers face overcharging
description: Perishable food items consumers face overcharging
content:
Consumers lament ineffectiveness of govt lists
Consumers in Lahore continued to face high food prices this week despite reductions in official rates for several commodities. Shoppers continued to pay premiums in the markets, with significant gaps recorded between notified and retail prices of vegetables and poultry.
The poultry market highlighted the disparity between official price lists and retail rates. Live chicken price increased by Rs25 to Rs333 per kg, while the official price of meat rose by Rs37 to Rs483 per kg. However, chicken meat continued to sell for Rs500570 per kg.
Live birds remained largely unsold across the city.
The vegetable market recorded a predominantly upward trend, with several essential perishables becoming more expensive during the past week.
Sugar-free potatoes remained unchanged at Rs2730 per kg on the official list but sold for Rs5070 per kg.
Tomato rates were reduced by Rs5060 per kg on the official list to Rs160170 per kg, but retailed at Rs220280 per kg.
Official onion rates decreased by Rs15 per kg to Rs170180 per kg, while the vegetable was sold for Rs220260 per kg.
Farm cucumber, brinjal, cabbage and farm spinach prices remained unchanged on the official list, but were sold well above the notified rates.
Consumers criticised the persistent gap between official rates and market prices, saying the government lists had little impact on what shoppers were paying.
"Every week, we hear that prices have been fixed or reduced, but when we go to the market, the prices are completely different. The government needs to ensure that the notified rates are actually enforced," said a Lahore resident, Muhammad Ali.
Another shopper said families were being forced to cut back on everyday food purchases as prices continued to rise.
"Even when the official price of a vegetable is reduced, we do not see the benefit. The shopkeepers charge whatever they want, while our household budgets remain the same," the consumer said.
"There is a price list, but nobody seems to follow it. If the government has fixed the rates, there should be regular checks and action against those charging excessive prices," said a middle-aged housemaker, Naheed.
The continuing difference between notified and retail prices has added to the pressure on household budgets, particularly for consumers purchasing essential food items on a daily basis.

title: Two brothers die in fire at Shakargarh home  | The Express Tribune
description: Two brothers die in fire at Shakargarh home
content:
Two minor brothers died after a fire broke out while they were playing in a room on the rooftop of their house in Qasim Pura Kothe Saraiya, on the outskirts of Shakargarh.
According to police, the children were playing in the room where paddy straw was stored.
Preliminary information suggested that the children may have set the straw alight while playing, causing the fire to spread rapidly.
The flames engulfed the two brothers, who suffered severe burns and died at the scene.
The deceased were identified as four-year-old Waleed and three-year-old Arsalan. Police said the children were too young to understand the dangers associated with playing with fire.
SHO Sadar Shakargarh Umar Hayat Goraya said the incident occurred in the Qasim Pura Kothe Saraiya area.
Family members tried to rescue the children after learning about the fire, but they could not save them.
Police reached the scene after being informed and launched an initial investigation.
DSP Shakargarh Rana Sajjad said all aspects of the incident were being investigated.
He said preliminary findings suggested that the fire appeared to have been accidental, while the exact circumstances would become clear after completion of the investigation.
The deaths left the family devastated, while the area was plunged into mourning.
Residents expressed grief over the deaths of the two brothers and extended condolences to their family.
Police said the investigation was continuing to determine how the fire started and the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

title: 24  of 552 Punjab wildlife rangers women
description: 24  of 552 Punjab wildlife rangers women
content:
Senior minister vows new era of conservation on World Animal Day
The Punjab government has announced a series of measures to strengthen wildlife protection, curb illegal hunting and combat wildlife crimes across the province as World Animal Day was observed on Sunday.
Senior Punjab Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb said Punjab was entering a "new era" of wildlife conservation under the vision of Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, with animal protection being made a government priority. She said Punjab had become the first province in the country to increase the strength of its Wildlife Rangers to 552, including 24 per cent women.
During the past two years, more than 14,000 challans and over 2,000 FIRs had been registered against illegal hunting and wildlife trafficking, while fines and compensation of more than Rs215 million had been recovered.
Aurangzeb said more than 50,000 birds, over 1,000 wild animals and 37 bears had been rescued and rehabilitated during enforcement operations. She added that the total number of rescued birds had crossed 51,000, while 38 bears had also been rescued.
She said field operations and legal action against wildlife crimes had been strengthened across Punjab, with three modern rescue centres, mobile veterinary clinics and the province's first Wildlife Rescue Force established to provide rescue, rehabilitation and treatment facilities.
According to the minister, Pakistan's first modern wildlife hospital had also been established at Safari Zoo. The facility has a CT scan, X-ray, laboratory, operation theatre, anaesthesia rooms and other medical facilities.
Mobile veterinary clinics were providing on-site treatment and emergency medical assistance to wildlife at safari parks, zoos and other facilities, she added.
Aurangzeb said all 108 protected areas in Punjab had been digitised on the chief minister's directions, while 920 GIS maps had also been prepared. The Punjnad Indus River Dolphin Sanctuary had been established for dolphin conservation, and the province's first wildlife census had been completed.
She said amendments to the Wildlife Act and Big Cat Regulation had strengthened legal protection for wildlife, including big cats.
Lahore Zoo, Safari Zoo, Changa Manga and other parks across the province were also being upgraded according to international standards, she added.
"Animals are an essential part of the ecological balance and survival of the planet," Aurangzeb said, adding that their protection was not the sole responsibility of the wildlife department but a collective responsibility of society. She said Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz had made it clear that cruelty against animals would not be tolerated in Punjab. Meanwhile, a three-day painting competition and awareness walk were organised at Lahore Zoo to mark World Animal Day.
Children, young people and participants from different age groups took part in the competition, producing paintings highlighting wildlife, natural habitats and animal conservation.
A participating student, Fatima, said the paintings conveyed messages about the importance of natural habitats, wildlife and compassion for animals.
An awareness walk was also held under the leadership of Lahore Zoo Director Dr Ghulam Rasool, who said the activity aimed to highlight the importance of animals and birds to the ecosystem and the need for collective efforts to protect them.

title: Five roads to be built with private partnership
description: Five roads to be built with private partnership
content:
Handing over management, operations to generate Rs22b for govt
Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Sunday launched five road projects under the Punjab Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Authority, handing their management and operations over to the private sector in a move expected to generate Rs22 billion in revenue for the provincial government.
The chief minister performed digital inauguration of the 80-kilometre Muridke-Narowal, 33km Shakargarh-Narowal, 97km Faisalabad Ring Road, 52km Faisalabad-Sahianwala and 56km Faisalabad-Samundri-Rajaa road projects.
Under the arrangement, electronic toll plazas will be established on the roads. Private contractors will collect tolls, linked with the National Highway Authority (NHA), for seven years and will also be responsible for the maintenance, repair and rehabilitation of the roads.
PPP Authority Vice Chairperson Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb briefed the chief minister on the projects and plans.
The government said the processing time for PPP projects had been reduced from two years to six months.
Four more roads between Bahawalpur and Yazman (42km), Yazman-Ahmedpur East (43km), Raiwind-Changa Manga (28km) and Gajjumata-Kasur (26km) will also be transferred to the public-private mode.
The authority is also processing projects in water and sanitation, tourism, healthcare, education, waste management, transport and sports. These include water and sanitation projects in Chakwal and Kasur, a Time Travel Park in Lahore, an FMD vaccine plant, a parking plaza and multimodal commercial facility at Badami Bagh, and a bridge over the Sutlej at Sahoka Patan.
Partnership projects have also been planned for solid waste management at fruit and vegetable markets through black soldier fly larvae plants, management of 100 sports grounds and allied facilities, and construction of a modern truck terminal in Faisalabad. The projects in pipel8ne include girls' and boys' hostels at Punjab University and 28 other public sector universities, three medical colleges, and 14 hostels for working women across the province. A nursing hostel will also be built at Sahiwal Teaching Hospital, while the operation and development of Fareedia Park in Sahiwal will be undertaken under the framework.
Other proposed projects include hospitals, parks, sports grounds, waste-to-energy schemes, effluent treatment plants in industrial zones, parking plazas, tourism facilities, water supply and recycling as well as the development of a Zarafa Café and food streets.
The chief minister was informed that divisional working parties headed by commissioners would be empowered to approve and implement projects under the mode costing up to Rs500 million.

title: Rising air toxicity causes alarm
description: Rising air toxicity causes alarm
content:
Pre-smog phase indicates risk of deterioration
Punjab's air pollution situation is showing renewed signs of deterioration as the province moves into October with Lahore experiencing repeated unhealthy air episodes and its weekly Air Quality Index (AQI) touching 295, raising concerns that the current pre-smog phase could develop into a severe pollution crisis as temperatures fall.
According to the latest Punjab Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) real-time monitoring data, Lahore's overall AQI stood at 154 at noon on Sunday, placing the city in the "unhealthy for sensitive groups" category.
The reading was lower than the 172 recorded at the same hour a day earlier but remained above the level considered safe for vulnerable residents.
Pollution levels remained uneven across the provincial capital. At noon, Safari Park recorded an AQI of 180, followed by Shahdara at 171, Multan Road 164, Barki Road 160, Punjab University 152 and GT Road 151. DHA Phase 6 recorded 149 while Kahna Nau, Wagha Border and Egerton Road recorded 145, 140 and 133, respectively.
EPA data shows that Lahore's AQI reached a weekly maximum of 295 at 9am on October 3, placing the city at the upper end of the unhealthy category and close to the "very unhealthy" threshold.
The record shows pollution repeatedly crossing 200 during October 13, indicating that high pollution episodes are already occurring before the traditional winter peak.
The situation is not limited to Lahore as provincial assessments have shown unhealthy and very unhealthy air in several cities.
Lahore's position in international pollution rankings has also fluctuated in recent days. On October 3, IQAir data placed it at the top of its live global major city ranking at one point with AQI reported at 204. However, provincial authorities recorded a substantially different local reading.
The latest international snapshot available on October 4 showed Kolkata first, Delhi third and Lahore fifth with IQAir reading of around 157. The global rankings change in hours.
The more important concern is that air pollution is repeatedly reaching unhealthy levels even before the coldest part of the season.
October marks the beginning of the period in which Punjab's air quality can deteriorate rapidly," said a former chairman of Punjab University Geography Department, Dr Munawar Sabir. As temperatures decline, wind movement may weaken and atmospheric inversion can increasingly trap pollutants close to the ground. The combination of vehicle emissions, industrial activity, brick kilns, construction dust, waste burning and agricultural residue burning can therefore produce increasingly persistent pollution episodes, he added.
IQAir has identified dust, vehicle emissions, brick kilns, construction and industrial pollution among important contributors to Lahore's poor air quality. Its recent assessment noted that weak winds can restrict the dispersion of pollutants.
During winter, high humidity, fog and stagnant atmospheric conditions can occur alongside pollution, worsening visibility and increasing the health risk.
A pre-smog crackdown has targeted crop residue and waste burning, vehicle emissions, construction dust and brick kilns.
The EPA has also directed authorities to reduce dust generating practices, including dry sweeping.
The government also recently introduced smart field enforcement, monitoring and digital drone surveillance to identify pollution sources and violations. Authorities said more than Rs300 million in environmental fines had been imposed during the ongoing year, while measures against paddy residue burning had been intensified.
The EPA has deployed night squads and drones to monitor stubble burning and other pollution sources, particularly along motorways. The strategy combines night surveillance, drone monitoring and ground enforcement so that field teams can respond after suspected violations are identified.
The Punjab government is also expanding its air quality monitoring capacity with plans for 26 additional monitoring stations, 20 smoke opacity meters for vehicle emissions and mobile fuel testing laboratories.
If pollution levels rise substantially during the coming weeks, schools may face restrictions on outdoor activities. Authorities may also have to alter business timings.
Children, senior citizens and patients with respiratory or cardiovascular vulnerabilities face greater risks amid unhealthy air.
The evidence indicates that Punjab has entered the pre-smog deterioration phase.

title: Dry taps  filthy streets as Hyd s water crisis deepens
description: Dry taps  filthy streets as Hyd s water crisis deepens
content:
46k malaria cases reported in nine months as sewage piles up
In one part of the city, residents queue up for water tankers. In another, foul-smelling water flows from household taps. And across several neighbourhoods, sewage sits stagnant on roads and streets, turning everyday life into a struggle.
The city's long-running water and sewerage crisis remains unresolved, with large areas still facing drinking water shortages while others complain of receiving contaminated water. The worsening sanitation conditions have also coincided with a sharp rise in malaria cases, with 46,183 infections reported across Hyderabad Division during the first nine months of the year, according to Sindh Health Department figures.
For a city sitting beside the Indus River, the irony is difficult to miss. Residents of several riverside areas say they are being forced to rely on water tankers despite the availability of river water. Affected areas include various units of Latifabad, HDA Kohsar Housing Society Phases I and II, Daman Kohsar, Mujahid Colony, Iqbal Colony, American Quarters and Hali Road.
Residents also complain that ageing water pipelines have remained unrepaired for years, resulting in dirty and foul-smelling water reaching homes. Videos purportedly showing contaminated water flowing from taps in affected areas have repeatedly appeared on social media, but residents say the problem remains unresolved. The sewerage crisis has meanwhile spilled onto the city's busiest thoroughfares. Sewage remained stagnant on Qadamgah Maula Ali Road from Saturday morning until night, disrupting commercial activity and making movement difficult for motorists and pedestrians.

title: Highway carnage claims 11 lives in a day
description: Highway carnage claims 11 lives in a day
content:
5-member family among victims as two cars collide with trucks on National Highway
As effective traffic regulation and safer road conditions remain elusive on highways and roads across much of Sindh, two separate accidents claimed 11 lives in Naushahro Feroze and Shaheed Benazirabad districts on Sunday.
In the deadliest of the two accidents, a truck crushed a car carrying a family travelling from a village in Naushahro Feroze to Hyderabad for medical treatment, killing five people, including a 45-year-old woman, her 26-year-old son and 14-year-old daughter. The victims were identified as Parveen Rajpar, her son Noshad, daughter Salma, Rafique Ahmed Rajpar, 46, and the car's driver, Asif Rajpar, 32.
The force of the collision left the car completely mangled, trapping the bodies inside for nearly two hours. The truck's front section also became lodged in cranes being used at the scene, forcing local traders to arrange additional cranes to cut through the wreckage and retrieve the bodies.
The bodies were taken to the district headquarters hospital for medico-legal formalities before being transported to Ahmed Khan Rajpar village, where the family was buried.
Police said the truck driver and cleaner fled the scene after the crash, while the vehicle was impounded. No FIR had been registered by Sunday evening.
Around 40 kilometres away, another fatal collision occurred on the National Highway near Shahpur Jahania, where six people travelling in a car were killed after it collided head-on with a truck. Police said the car's tyre burst, causing the driver to lose control and crash into the oncoming truck. Dr Khan also urged people to avoid smoking and other forms of tobacco consumption, stressing that tobacco use posed serious health risks and that preventive measures could significantly reduce the likelihood of tobacco-related illnesses.
Dr Yawer Saeed, Assistant Professor of Cardiology, said cardiovascular diseases were increasingly assuming epidemic proportions in Pakistan and across Asia. He noted that heart attacks had also become more common among younger people over approximately the past decade.

title: 40 years on  quota faces fresh challenge
description: 40 years on  quota faces fresh challenge
content:
A system introduced decades ago to bridge Sindh's urban-rural divide is facing renewed scrutiny, with a growing number of educated Sindhi voices now joining the long-standing demand from Urdu-speaking circles for an end to the quota regime in government jobs and educational institutions.
The debate has gained fresh momentum after the latest MDCAT results, in which students from some of Sindh's most underdeveloped districts, including Tharparkar, outperformed candidates from Karachi, Hyderabad and Sukkur. For critics of the quota system, the results have raised a fundamental question: does a policy designed to compensate for rural deprivation still serve the purpose for which it was introduced?
What was once largely framed as an urban-rural or Sindhi-Urdu dispute is consequently taking on a different dimension. A section of educated Sindhi-speaking professionals and academics now argues that improvements in education and healthcare facilities in rural Sindh have narrowed the gap, while the quota system is increasingly reinforcing divisions between the province's communities rather than addressing them.
Abdul Aleem Lashari, a retired bureaucrat who has served in various positions in Sindh, recently wrote on social media that "this is the right time to abolish the quota system". Speaking to The Express Tribune, he said he believed the province no longer needed the quota system.
Serving bureaucrat Nadeem Memon, responding to Lashari's post, observed that a large number of young people in Karachi preferred employment in the private sector and multinational companies over government jobs.
He argued that ending the quota system could encourage urban youth who had stayed away from government employment to return to the competitive examination system.
Prominent Sindhi scholar Naseer Memon, who is based in Islamabad, said the quota system had been in place for around four decades.

title: Clampdown puts brakes on PTI protests
description: Clampdown puts brakes on PTI protests
content:
Over 75 activists, leaders detained as party takes to streets for founder's release
The city saw a day of protest, arrests and confrontation on Sunday as police cracked down on Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) workers attempting to stage demonstrations for the release of party founder Imran Khan, detaining more than 75 leaders and activists across Karachi.
PTI workers attempted to gather at several locations, including Korangi, Empress Market, Sohrab Goth, Ancholi and Banaras, but police were deployed in advance at key points and detained protesters, including women, before taking them to different police stations. The two sides engaged in a cat-and-mouse game at several locations as protesters repeatedly attempted to regroup.
The crackdown also affected access to the Karachi Press Club, with roads around the premises blocked with barricades in anticipation of the protests, causing difficulties for journalists and residents in the area.
PTI Sindh spokesperson Mohammad Ali Baloch claimed that more than 75 party leaders and workers had been arrested across the city, including PTI Women's Wing president Sareena Adnan and District South president Sheeba Altaf Qadri, along with several other women activists.
According to Baloch, protests were held in Korangi, Saddar/Empress Market and several districts of the city under the leadership of PTI Karachi Division president Faheem Khan. Sindh PTI additional general secretary Rizwan Niazi and Sindh Assembly member Owais Chaudhry also participated in the Korangi protest.
PTI leaders strongly condemned the arrests and demanded the immediate release of the detained workers. Faheem Khan accused the Sindh government and police of suppressing the party's democratic and constitutional rights, saying the arrests would not force PTI workers to abandon their peaceful movement.
Baloch also condemned the closure of roads around the Karachi Press Club, describing it as a restriction on freedom of expression and the right to peaceful assembly. He said the party would continue its protests until Imran Khan's release.
The police, however, confirmed that several PTI leaders and workers had been taken into custody and said legal action would be taken against them in accordance with the law.
Despite pockets of tension and the police action, the overall law-and-order situation in Karachi remained under control and routine life continued largely unaffected.

title: Rare brown bears face new threat in Deosai
description: Rare brown bears face new threat in Deosai
content:
Plastic waste found in bear droppings raises concerns over changing feeding patterns
The vast plains, snow-covered mountains, alpine pastures and crystal-clear lakes of Deosai National Park are among Pakistan's most beautiful natural landscapes.
The area is also an important habitat of the Himalayan brown bear. However, increasing tourism, camping, food remains and plastic waste have increased pressure on the sensitive ecosystem.
Located at an altitude of around 4,114 metres above sea level between Skardu and Astore, Deosai is known in the local Balti language as "Ghab-i-Yarsa", meaning "place of summer".
Due to severe cold, the area remains inaccessible for most of the year, while it is also linked to traditional pastures, natural resources and folk traditions of local communities.
Deosai has historically served as an important route between Kashmir and Gilgit. According to the Gilgit-Baltistan Forest and Wildlife Department, the area was declared a national park in 1993 primarily to protect the Himalayan brown bear and its habitat.
The Himalayan brown bear, Ursus arctos isabellinus, is among the prominent wildlife species found in Deosai. Its population in Pakistan has been affected by poaching and habitat loss.
However, the establishment of Deosai National Park and long-term conservation measures have provided the species an opportunity for recovery in the area.
A 2022 survey estimated the presence of around 66 Himalayan brown bears in Deosai and its buffer valleys, with the possible population estimated at between 58 and 77. The survey also highlighted the need for continuous monitoring of the population and improved habitat management.
According to photographer Asif Ashoor, who was present in Deosai, tourist waste discarded at some locations is attracting brown bears towards food remains. He said pieces or remains of plastic shopping bags had also been observed in bear droppings and urine.
These observations do not constitute conclusive evidence that bears are ingesting plastic, but they require scientific investigation. The concern cannot be ignored because a previous study on the diet of Deosai's brown bears had reported evidence of plastic, food packaging and other waste in faecal samples.
The 2022 survey recorded 12 campsites, 66 tents and 173 people inside Deosai, while around 4,834 livestock associated with these camps were grazing there. Another six locations were also providing restaurants, shops and accommodation facilities for tourists.
Clearing Deosai of tourists is not the solution, but regulating tourism under clear environmental principles is essential.

Amid public concerns of overlooking severely dilapidated roads, authorities concerned have transferred development schemes for the reconstruction and improvement of nine roads in Rawalpindi to the Communications and Works (C&W) Department.

Citizens have expressed concern over the allocation of substantial funds for the reconstruction of some roads that remain in relatively good condition, questioning why severely dilapidated roads are being overlooked.
They pointed out that the road from Bostan Road, Scheme III, to Car Chowk had deteriorated badly and required immediate rehabilitation. The road leading to Cadet College in Gulrez has also remained closed for the past year due to a landslide, forcing traffic through alternative streets, which are themselves in poor condition.

title: School outsourcing enters fourth phase
description: School outsourcing enters fourth phase
content:
Educators warn outsourcing could limit access to secondary education
The School Education Department has approved the fourth phase of outsourcing government schools on the special directives of the Punjab government, with both boys' and girls' high schools included in the latest phase.
Sources told The Express Tribune that the provincial government is expected to invite applications from interested parties in October, while it is in the process of finalising the list of schools to be outsourced under Phase 4.
According to sources, 600 high schools will be included in the outsourcing process, in addition to 5,860 primary and middle schools.
Interestingly, senior teachers' union leaders have been taken on board regarding the outsourcing plan. Under the arrangement, these senior union leaders will not be declared surplus and will retire upon completing their service with full pensions and other dues. In return, they are not expected to offer strong resistance to the outsourcing process.
However, several senior teachers' leaders, including Muhammad Shafiq Bhulawalia, Sufi Ramzan Inqalabi, Bashir Warraich, Nawaz Gondal, Chaudhry Zafran Barkat and Raja Amjad Mahmood, have strongly criticised what they described as a soft approach by some teachers' organisations towards outsourcing and the "sale" of government schools.
They said outsourcing high schools would deprive children from low-income families and those of lower-grade government employees of access to secondary education up to matriculation.
The teachers' leaders called for regular recruitment against vacant teaching posts instead of outsourcing schools. They said the recruitment of daily-wage school interns and teachers at Rs40,000 to Rs50,000 a month had pushed the public education system towards collapse.
They claimed that the government planned to outsource or "sell" 50% of government schools by December 31, 2027, and that no teachers would be recruited on a regular basis in future. Instead, teachers would reportedly be hired on daily wages of around Rs50,000 for individual academic sessions.
Meanwhile, a decision has been taken to increase the registration period and fees for private schools, with directions issued to initiate the formal legal process.
Under the proposed decision, all private schools will be registered for four years and the registration fee will be determined according to the school's monthly fee.
Under the proposed new rules and regulations, a school charging a monthly fee of Rs1,500 has been proposed to pay a registration fee of Rs10,000, while schools charging up to Rs2,500 per month will pay Rs20,000 as registration fee.
Similarly, a registration fee of Rs50,000 has been proposed for schools charging up to Rs5,000 per month, while schools charging a monthly fee of Rs10,000 will pay a registration fee of Rs100,000.
Under the proposed rules, schools charging Rs20,000 per month will pay a registration fee of Rs200,000, while a registration fee of Rs1 million has been proposed for schools charging more than Rs20,000 per month.
Upon payment of the said fee, schools will be granted registration for four years. At the time of renewal after the new licence, schools will have to pay 50 per cent of the prescribed registration fee.

title: Women prisoners face healthcare  legal hurdles
description: Women prisoners face healthcare  legal hurdles
content:
Female inmates struggle with physical and mental health, delayed trials, lack of legal aid and basic facilities
For Nazneen*, prison is no longer just a place behind locked doors - it is where seven months of an ordinary family life have quietly disappeared. Facing a drug-related case, she has watched the familiar world of home give way to concrete walls, uncertainty and the daily struggle of raising her child without the life she once knew.
The loss of freedom, she says, is only the beginning. With no normal home environment, limited schooling for her child and no clear idea of what awaits them after release, the uncertainty has become a source of constant psychological distress.
"For women, prison itself becomes a source of psychological pressure," she said, describing a life marked by prolonged mental stress, illness and a lack of basic facilities. More than 50 women prisoners are currently held at Peshawar Central Prison, many caught in a system where legal assistance, healthcare, education and rehabilitation remain difficult to access.
For some, the uncertainty is compounded by serious illness. Peshawar High Court lawyer Mahwish Mohib Kakakhel revealed that an HIV-positive female inmate in her late 30s was currently being held at the prison, raising concerns over her access to medical treatment, hygiene and proper supervision.
"Some women have remained behind bars for years, waiting for trials, bail or other legal remedies. A significant number are facing drug-related and murder cases. The absence of a dedicated rehabilitation centre for women prisoners means there is little structured support for psychological recovery, education, vocational training or preparation for life after release," noted Kakakhel.
Social activist Dr Khurshid Bano, who has worked for around three decades on women's rights, noted that the procedures for meeting women prisoners were complicated and inmates continued to face harassment and vulnerability.
"Women prisoners should not be viewed solely as people serving sentences but as individuals entitled to healthcare, psychological support, education, social rehabilitation and basic human rights," she emphasised.
The concerns facing women prisoners point to a wider problem inside K-P's prison system, where inmates have reported difficulties accessing specialist doctors, diagnostic facilities and timely treatment.
A writ petition before the Peshawar High Court has also raised the reported deaths of two prisoners, Fazal Rehman and Zahir Shah, at Peshawar Central Prison.
Fazal Khan, a prisoner in a drug-related case, said two inmates known to him had suffered from gallbladder and cardiac complications but faced delays in receiving treatment. One prisoner, unable to afford private care, continued taking routine medicines until his condition deteriorated and he died.
Another inmate, who has spent around 12 years behind bars, said a serious back problem eventually forced him to spend around Rs200,000 on a private operation. "If you do not have money, even getting proper treatment can become extremely difficult inside prison," he said.
Lawyer Shabbir Hussain Gigiani, who filed the petition, has sought specialist doctors from nearby government hospitals to hold regular clinics in prisons, along with diagnostic facilities, medicines and dedicated medico-legal wards for prisoners requiring treatment.
On the other hand, prison authorities reject claims of inadequate medical care, saying routine check-ups, medical staff and camps are available, while the government claims it is working on a telemedicine system. But prisoners say survival inside prison should not mean putting life on hold.
Owais Khan, incarcerated at Peshawar Central Prison, hoped that prisons could provide education and vocational training rather than merely confine inmates.
Rights advocates believe K-P needs a comprehensive rehabilitation framework for women covering healthcare, mental health, legal aid, education and support for reintegration after release.
Because for women like Nazneen, the prison walls may eventually open. The harder question is what remains waiting for them and their children - on the other side.

title: Climate change threatens Kalash life
description: Climate change threatens Kalash life
content:
Shorter winters, drying springs, timber dependence put agriculture, centuries-old culture under pressure
In the picturesque Kalash Valley of Lower Chitral in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, a place long celebrated for its unique civilisation, ancient traditions, natural beauty and cultural heritage, climate change, deforestation, erratic rainfall, flash floods, water shortages and declining agricultural yields are confronting local communities with new environmental and economic challenges.
Residents of Bamboret, Rumbur and Birir valleys report marked shifts in weather patterns over recent years. Snowfall has become shorter and lighter in winter, summers hotter, rains more unpredictable and sudden flash floods more frequent. These changes are damaging farmland and crops while also destroying roads, houses, irrigation systems and other basic infrastructure.
Daniel Feroz, a resident and social activist of the Kalash Valley, told The Express Tribune that the effects of climate change have grown more visible over the past decade. Repeated floods, he said, have severely disrupted daily life, agriculture and infrastructure.
"Flash floods damage people's agricultural land and crops, and in several places houses have also been affected," Feroz said. The main road leading into the valley as well as internal link roads are regularly hit, creating difficulties for both residents and tourists.
The impact is not limited to flooding. Natural water sources are under strain, with many springs showing reduced flow.
Agriculture in the Kalash Valley depends heavily on springs and rainfall. According to Feroz, several springs have seen declining water levels and some have dried up completely. Lands that once supported regular crops are now suffering.
Maize and wheat remain the main crops, but water shortages and unreliable rains are cutting yields. Wheat, in particular, relies on timely rainfall; if adequate rain fails at critical stages, production falls, directly affecting household food security and income.
A major environmental stressor is the community's reliance on forests. With no natural gas supply, residents use wood year-round for cooking, heating homes in winter and other household needs. Wood is also central to traditional construction of houses, livestock shelters and other structures.
While permits are sometimes required for timber used in building, the continuous demand for fuelwood keeps pressure on forests high.
Local journalist Sameer said that dependence on wood is a long-standing issue across parts of Chitral. Both construction and domestic fuel needs drive the demand. He noted that some people extract more timber than permitted and that collecting firewood further strains forests. Providing alternative energy sources that take local needs into account is essential for forest conservation, he said.
Livestock rearing adds another layer of pressure. Large numbers of goats are taken into forests and mountain pastures, where they browse young shoots and saplings, hindering natural regeneration.
"On one hand mature trees continue to be cut; on the other, new plants struggle to grow," Feroz said. Over time this can reduce both the area and density of forests.
Yet goats remain deeply embedded in Kalash society and culture. They feature in social and religious rituals, particularly funeral and mourning ceremonies in which large numbers are sacrificed.
Feroz observed that winter snowfall has also altered. In the past, regular snow fell in December, January and other cold months. In recent years the timing, quantity and consistency of snowfall have changed. Reduced winter snow coincides with hotter summers and more unpredictable rains, further disrupting local life.
In mountain regions forests play a critical role in preventing soil erosion, maintaining natural water systems and stabilising slopes. Their decline, combined with intense rains and weakened hillsides, can increase landslides, debris flows into streams and the destructive power of flash floods.
Residents report that monsoon streams now frequently carry large boulders and debris, damaging roads and disrupting irrigation channels. The Forest Department maintains a presence, Feroz said, but the number of field staff and forest guards is small relative to the vast forested areas. Effective monitoring, transparent permit systems and alternative fuel supplies at the local level could ease pressure on the forests.
Social activist Log Rahmat stressed that Kalash culture cannot be separated from its natural surroundings. Traditions, religious rituals, farming, livestock rearing, water sources and forests are deeply interwoven.

title: Ethiopia controls Tigray capital amid Egypt talks
description: Ethiopia controls Tigray capital amid Egypt talks
content:
Ethiopian federal forces were in full control of the Tigray rebels' regional capital, a local journalist said on Sunday, while Ethiopia's regional rivals gathered in Egypt to discuss the risk of a wider war.
The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and federal forces began fighting again on September 23, sparking fears of a return to the devastating civil war of 2020-2022.
The presidents of Egypt, Somalia, Sudan and Eritrea -- all of whom have difficult relations with Ethiopia -- met in the Egyptian coastal city of El-Alamein on Sunday, calling for regional disputes to be settled through "peaceful means", according to an Egyptian presidency statement.
They also stressed "the necessity of respecting the rules of international law, the principles of good neighbourliness, and non-interference in the internal affairs of states" in the Horn of Africa, the statement read.
Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of directly backing the Tigray rebels, with the added support of Sudan and Egypt, which all three countries deny.
In a counter-offensive, Ethiopian forces have pushed deep into rebel-held territory, entering the regional capital, Mekelle, on Saturday without a fight, as TPLF leaders and troops abandoned the city.
On Sunday, federal troops were patrolling Mekelle and manning key institutions, a local journalist told AFP, as communications were restored for the first time in more than a week.
"We have taken control of Mekelle and we are marching forward," a commander with a pro-government militia told AFP.
Businesses and shops remained closed. Owners had moved stock to safer locations ahead of time, fearing looting and vandalism.
"There are no police," one resident told AFP, speaking like others on condition of anonymity because of the uncertainty of the situation.
"Last night, we had to organise ourselves and take care of security."
"The fact that the war is beginning to lower in intensity brings some immediate relief," said Tewodros, another resident who did not want to give his full name.
"But as seems to be spreading across the region, I'm scared it will drag on," he added.
There are growing fears the fighting could spill over the border into Eritrea.
The mini-summit in Alamein -- on the sidelines of an African business forum -- brought together Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki, Somalian President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) head Abdel Fattah al-Burhan.
Before the talks, Sisi called for dialogue to settle cross-border issues, as concerns grew that Ethiopia's escalating violence could spill across borders.
Eritrea, which shares a long border with the Tigray region, is most directly involved in the conflict.
It accuses landlocked Ethiopia of planning to invade and seize access to its coastline. Analysts say it has backed the rebels in Ethiopia to try to keep the conflict away from its border.
The TPLF has long been the dominant force in Tigray, ousting a government-appointed administration this year.
The rebels' leader, Debretsion Gebremichael, has implied that the group would continue guerrilla-style attacks, as it did when Mekelle fell to government forces in 2020 during the last war.
Their insurgent campaign ultimately led to the TPLF retaking the city the following year.
"We operate under a strategy to strike the enemy wherever we choose," said Debretsion.
A joint statement released after Sunday's talks in Egypt expressed the countries' "complete rejection of any unilateral measures" that could harm the existing water use of downstream states.

title: Pro Europe Latvian PM wins Russia dominated poll
description: Pro Europe Latvian PM wins Russia dominated poll
content:
Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' centre-right party emerged as the victor on Sunday from Latvia's parliamentary election, and he will now set about forming a coalition to maintain his pro-European and pro-Ukrainian course.
Populist parties, boosted by support from Latvia's Russian-speaking minority, also had a good night after an election campaign dominated by fears over neighbouring Russia, the cost of living and other social issues.
Kulbergs' United List party won 42 seats in the 100-seat parliament -- an unprecedented result in the former Soviet republic's post-independence history.
After exit polls hinted at the magnitude of his party's victory, Kulbergs said it was a wider margin than he had expected.
"That means people truly want change," he said, which he said meant "economic growth" and a future for the country's children.
Kulbergs, a former manager in the telecoms and automotive sectors, took over as prime minister in May at the head of a centre-right coalition.
He will be forced to change partners after the election, as one of his members failed to clear the five-percent hurdle to get into parliament.
Security remains central to political debate in Latvia, more than four years after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
Latvia, a member of NATO and the European Union since 2004, views Russia as its principal security threat and has significantly increased defence spending in response.
"Because we are the external border of Europe, we must have a strong economy... a strong border region," Kulbergs said.
But rising living costs, low wages, strains on the healthcare system and long-term population decline all featured prominently in campaign debates.
While most parties expected to enter parliament back both high military spending and maintaining aid to Kyiv, the right-wing Sovereign Power party has broken ranks.
It has opposed military aid to Ukraine and further increases to defence spending. It looked set for a third-place finish, with 15 MPs, after focusing on cost of living issues.
Soverign Power has been tarred pro-Russian by its detractors and most major parties have ruled out working with it.
Latvia First, a conservative party run by a property magnate often compared toh US President Donald Trump, came second in the poll and took 17 seats.
Both populist parties benefitted from changes in voting patterns among the Russian-speaking minority, who make up a third of the population.
They had long rallied around Harmony, which was at one time the country's biggest party.
But Harmony was broadly seen as pro-Kremlin and its support collapsed dramatically in the last election, held shortly after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

title: Pakistani sailor recalls long ordeal
description: Pakistani sailor recalls long ordeal
content:
Survivor describes how rescue operation turned vessel into battlefield
For Pakistani sailor Ameen bin Shams, freedom did not come quietly. After five and a half months in the hands of Somali pirates, it arrived in the middle of a night of gunfire, when armed forces closed in on the vessel carrying the hostages and the pirates refused to surrender.
"Every moment we spent in the captivity of Somali pirates felt like years. We lived in constant fear of death, never knowing when the pirates might kill us," said injured Pakistani sailor Ameen bin Shams.
The nightmare he and his fellow crew members had feared eventually unfolded after Somali security forces launched an operation against another vessel anchored some distance from the Honour 25 and managed to free it.
The development sent the pirates aboard the Honour 25 into a panic. They ordered the crew to start the ship's engines and move forward. It was nighttime, and the Somali naval vessel was approximately 10 nautical miles away.
"That night was nothing short of a nightmare. The pirates gathered all of us on the ship's deck in freezing temperatures. We remained there throughout the night without proper clothing or footwear," Ameen said.
At daybreak, the pirates allowed the crew to go below deck. But just as the sailors were preparing to rest, they were ordered back onto the deck. All crew members, except Imran and Hussain Yousuf, were tied to the deck railing.
Imran later informed the Ansar Burney Trust by phone that he and Hussain Yousuf were inside the ship's main engine room while the remaining crew members had been taken back onto the deck by the pirates.
By then, the pursuing Somali naval vessel had reduced the distance to just one nautical mile. Security personnel gave the pirates 30 minutes to surrender the vessel and release the hostages, but they refused.
According to Imran, gunfire then erupted, with bullets penetrating the interior of the vessel. The intense exchange of fire continued for more than two hours.
There were 41 pirates aboard the Honour 25. During their five-and-a-half months in captivity, the crew members had come to know most of the pirates by name, while the pirates also knew the sailors' names.
Imran said a pirate identified as Arab panicked during the operation and opened fire in the section of the vessel where the hostages had been tied.
The security forces eventually gained control of the ship. Five pirates were killed in the operation, while 13 others were injured and arrested.
For the Pakistani crew, however, the rescue came at a devastating cost.
Second Officer Kashif Umar, boiler operator Rafiullah and Third Officer Mahmood Ansari were killed in the shooting. Their bodies, along with four injured Pakistani sailors, were repatriated to Karachi on Sunday via Addis Ababa aboard Ethiopian Airlines flight ET694.
The injured sailors were identified as Aqeel Khan, Amin bin Shams, Yasir Khan and Yaseen. They underwent medical examinations at the Border Health Services facility at Karachi airport before being taken to Aga Khan Hospital, where they are receiving treatment.
Ameen's wife, Ayesha, said her husband had sustained four bullet wounds and had been admitted to the hospital.
At Jinnah Cargo Terminal, a large number of relatives gathered to receive the bodies of the three sailors who had died in captivity. Emotional scenes unfolded as grieving family members consoled one another after months of uncertainty and fear.
Sindh Governor Nihal Hashmi, along with delegations from the Pakistan Peoples Party and Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan, welcomed the injured sailors and offered condolences to the bereaved families.
The governor presented bouquets to the injured sailors and assured them of the government's full support. The PPP delegation included provincial ministers Nasir Shah and Saeed Ghani, along with Waqar Mehdi, while the MQM-P delegation was led by Farooq Sattar.
Speaking to the media, Nasir Shah described the incident as a shared loss and said the three political parties stood with the injured sailors and the families of those who died.
For the families, the long ordeal had not ended with the return of the sailors. It had changed into mourning and questions over what might have been done to bring the hostages home alive.
The father of Rafiullah said the family had surrendered to Allah's will, adding that his son had died bravely and embraced martyrdom. He said that when the ship was hijacked, Rafiullah had told his younger brother to take care of his children.
His father said one of the pirates fired shots into the air while fleeing, causing bullets to ricochet and hit the crew. Rafiullah, he said, was struck in the neck and was not directly targeted during the operation.
The family of Mahmood Ansari also described the conditions endured by the hostages. His son said they had been kept in extremely poor conditions, were not given proper food and were repeatedly forced to drink polluted water.
Muzammil, son of Mahmood Ansari, told the media at the airport that the families had repeatedly appealed for the safe recovery of the hostages but that the government had failed to listen.
"What is the point of offering compensation now?" he questioned.
The bodies of all three deceased crew members have been handed over to their families, who are making arrangements for their funerals.

title: Pakistan s progress linked to education  teachers  says Shehbaz
description: Pakistan s progress linked to education  teachers  says Shehbaz
content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has said Pakistan's progress and prosperity are closely linked to the quality of its education system and the dedication of its teachers.
In a message on World Teachers' Day observed on Oct 5 every year, the premier said, "On the occasion of World Teachers' Day, I extend my heartfelt appreciation and profound respect to teachers in Pakistan and around the world who are entrusted with the sacred responsibility of educating and nurturing our youth: the architects of our future."
The prime minister noted that teachers played an indispensable role in nurturing the individuality of young people, polishing their abilities and expanding their knowledge.
"Through fostering intellectual development, shaping minds and guiding generations, teachers also help define the shared social foundations and values of our societies," he said.
"The dedication, knowledge and commitment of teachers are undoubtedly instrumental in shaping the future of nations," he added.
"They are the cornerstone of every successful education system, fostering a spirit of inquiry among students and equipping them with the confidence and skills needed to thrive in a rapidly changing world."
The premier observed that only an inclusive, future-oriented education system, responsive to the demands of artificial intelligence, climate change, technological advancement and a knowledge-based employment landscape, could ensure a brighter future.
"The emerging challenges of our time require us to equip our students not only with knowledge, but also with critical thinking, creativity, ethical values, adaptability and the capacity for lifelong learning," he said.
"Making our education system merit-based, high-quality and aligned with global standards remains a foremost priority of the government," he added.

title: Asif, Tarar target PTI after talks stall | The Express Tribune
description:
Asif, Tarar target 
PTI after talks stall
content:
Defence minister accuses Imran Khan of bringing terrorism to K-P
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Sunday fired fresh salvoes at the PTI over the failure of government-opposition talks, accusing the party of adopting double standards on terrorism and using calls for consultation as a delaying tactic.
The exchange followed marathon government-opposition talks over PTI's planned long march, which ended in deadlock in the early hours of Sunday. Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had said the PTI-TTAP side wanted counter-terrorism measures in K-P to be agreed jointly by the federal and provincial governments after consultation with political parties and other stakeholders.
The breakdown in negotiations produced competing accounts from the government and opposition over what had prevented an agreement, with the main disagreement centred on counter-terrorism policy in K-P.
Responding to Afridi's post on X, in which the CM Afridi said the talks had failed because the government had not agreed to jointly formulate a counter-terrorism policy for K-P with the provincial government and other political stakeholders, Tarar said PTI's position on consultation had "outlived its life in the past three years".
"PTI's lame old excuse that all parties should have been consulted has outlived its life in the past three years," Tarar said. "Federal government did exactly that but you never responded to our proposals."
He said the K-P government had only recently begun responding to federal calls for a joint mechanism to fight terrorism because it was "politically weak" and accused it of doing so to protect its political standing in the province.
In a post on X, the defence minister questioned PTI leaders who, he said, spoke about innocent victims in the province but did not visit the families of civilians killed in terrorist attacks.
"You talk about the innocent martyrs of your province, but leave aside the military martyrs - you are even refusing to take ownership of the civilian martyrs. Tell us, have you gone to the home of even a single civilian martyr to offer condolences?"
Asif accused PTI founder Imran Khan of bringing terrorism to K-P and supporting the settlement of terrorists in the province, saying the party's speeches in the provincial assembly and its media record were evidence of this.
"This terrorism was brought to K-P by their leader Imran. He was the biggest supporter of settling them in K-P. The record of assembly speeches and the media bears witness to this."
He challenged PTI leaders to debate the issue with him on television.
Asif also accused successive K-P chief ministers of attacking the federal government after PTI lost power at the Centre, while separately referring to the May 9 events.

title: Govt PTI talks failed over K P terror operation clauses
description: Govt PTI talks failed over K P terror operation clauses
content:
Sources reveal that govt had agreed to ensure Imran meetings, early hearing of pending cases
Before their talks broke down on Saturday, the government and the PTI had agreed on a five-point framework. This included providing legal facilities to the jailed party founder Imran Khan and his wife, ensuring an early hearing of pending cases, and allowing the couple meetings with their lawyers and family members.
Sources said the framework was prepared at the residence of PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan before the formal negotiations between the government and opposition committees.
They revealed that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and PML-N leader Talal Chaudhry separately met Gohar, Allama Raja Nasir Abbas and Asad Qaiser at Gohar's residence before the formal talks began.
The meeting reportedly agreed that whatever was settled between the government and opposition would be put in writing. Naqvi also showed Gohar and Raja Nasir Abbas evidence of approvals obtained at the highest level regarding various issues.
Sources said the first point of the proposed framework was a meeting between the prime minister and the two opposition leaders to help resolve political matters.
Under the second point, the government and opposition would form committees to address political issues and implement decisions within a specified timeframe.
The third point dealt with facilities and legal matters concerning Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi. It was agreed that the PTI founder and his wife would be provided all legal and constitutional facilities, allowed access to their lawyers and family members, and treated in accordance with the jail manual.
It was also agreed that all pending cases would be fixed for hearing at the earliest in accordance with the requirements of justice. Sources said the government also agreed to take a sympathetic view of cases involving elderly PTI leaders such as Yasmin Rashid and Shah Mahmood Qureshi.
The fourth and most contentious point concerned the deteriorating security situation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P). The proposed framework called for the provincial and federal governments to work jointly against terrorism, with the K-P government cooperating with the federal government under the National Action Plan.
According to the proposed framework, the constitutional option of imposing an emergency in the three merged districts of K-P could be used to control the movement of terrorists, with an operation against militants conducted under that arrangement.
Sources said if the provincial government opposed a military operation or was unwilling to conduct one, an operation could instead be carried out through the police, with the military providing full assistance to the police against terrorists.
The fifth point said that, if the negotiations succeeded, PTI would withdraw its call for the long march.
Sources said the first draft of the framework was prepared at around 9:30pm, after which Interior Minister Naqvi left to seek the necessary approval. The PPP and PML-N leaders participating in the talks also kept their respective party heads informed about the progress.
However, the draft subsequently ran into difficulties after Gohar sent it to the K-P government, which sought repeated changes to its provisions.
Sources said Allama Raja Nasir Abbas made his approval of the draft conditional on the consent of K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi. At the same time, Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai made a meeting with Imran Khan a precondition for approving the draft.
The PTI committee tried to convince Achakzai and informed him that the government committee was assuring a meeting with Imran Khan by Tuesday. PTI leaders argued that if the government backed away from the promised meeting with Imran, the party could revive its call for the long march.
Sources said the most significant changes, however, were made by Sohail Afridi to the provisions relating to terrorism in K-P. Afridi reportedly sought extensive changes to the clauses dealing with counterterrorism and the proposed role of the federal government and security forces in the province.

title: Date workers toil through rising heat in Sindh
description: Date workers toil through rising heat in Sindh
content:
In blazing temperatures, Muhammad Idrees ladles boiled dates from a vat simmering over an open flame, work that labourers lament is getting hotter each year in Sindh.
Date season arrives in July, when temperatures in the province regularly hit the mid-40 degrees Celsius.
Workers start before sunrise, and split the day into short shifts, but the heat soon catches up with them. Their gruelling routine involves harvesting and boiling fruit picked from palms that line Khairpur district, which produces more than half the country's dates and supports thousands of farmers and seasonal labourers.
Labourers begin work around 2am to avoid the worst of the daytime heat. Idrees, who has worked the date harvest for more than a decade, said the heat has now become "unbearable".
Date labourers are one of many professions in Pakistan that are becoming more difficult and dangerous as temperatures rise.
"It used to be less intense," Idrees told AFP as temperatures hit 42°C. "The heat is much harsher and the days are extremely hot. We fall ill because of it." Multiple workers said they often suffer heatstroke, fainting and fever. "When the heat makes us sick, we go to the doctor for treatment and then return to work," Idrees added.
Pakistan is among the countries globally most vulnerable to climate change despite contributing less than one per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions.
The country has experienced increasingly frequent heatwaves, erratic monsoon rains and devastating floods, including catastrophic 2022 floods that inundated around one-third of the country and displaced millions, hitting Sindh particularly hard.
Workers descend on date farms to begin work around 2am to avoid the worst of the daytime heat and take a break before continuing until the late evening.
Idrees said the physically demanding work earns him around Rs1,200, roughly $4, a day.
"We harvest the dates, load them onto trolleys and bring them here," he said. "They are boiled over the fire and then spread outside in the sun to dry."
Pakistan, the world's fifth-largest date producer, normally earns more than $120 million a year in exports, according to industry estimates. Date farmer Shahnawaz Phulpoto, who owns more than 1,500 palm trees, said that heavy monsoon rains from shifting weather patterns have hampered date crops and caused financial losses.
