title: Minorities  from the Constitution to sanitation work
description: What south asian societies abhor is disproportionately assigned to the marginalised communities
content:
What south asian societies abhor is disproportionately assigned to the marginalised communities
Bigoted education equips us with nothing but a tunnel vision. I had a learned friend having a doctorate in Islamic studies from a renowned university. Once, I discussed with him an article of the Constitution that says, 'Only a Muslim is qualified to become the president or the prime minister of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.' I asked him why not a non-Muslim. As a contrast, I cited the example of APJ Abdul Kalam, a Muslim president of a non-Muslim country, India. He regurgitated what he was finding hard to rein in: "A non-Muslim stands incapacitated to run the affairs of an Islamic country while a Muslim is qualified to head a non-Muslim state."
All the constitutional bindings for minority rights and all the religious dictats ensuring space and respect for minorities stand null and void when we see sanitation workers, who belong to minority communities, working in drains, sewers and gutters. After all, why are only minorities marginalised for the sanitation work? Even if they do such an unsung commendable service, why are they then stigmatised? The derogatory titles for sanitation workers reveal the indoctrination of bigotry to our subconscious level.
It is in South Asia that sanitation work is culturally perceived as dirty and religiously unholy, as this is a region dominated by racialism and religious discrimination. It results in social stigmatisation of the community doing the sanitation work. Hence, what such a society abhors is disproportionately assigned to the marginalised communities - excluded for religious identity - without offering them any professional choice.
In advertisements, sanitation jobs are specified for the minorities, particularly Christians. Though Punjab S&GAD issued a notification in 2015 against the discriminatory government advertisements for the recruitment of sanitation workers, such advertisements are widely published even today. And still recently, the Islamabad High Court, in its judgment of 11 November 2025, banned the use of the tag 'only Christians and Hindus may apply' in job advertisements. The National Commission for Human Rights notes that 80% of non-Muslim religious minorities are employed in grades 1 to 4. The commission labelled it as a form of 'state-led discrimination'.
A draft of the "Prohibition of Manual Scavenging and Protection of Sanitation Workers (ICT) Bill, 2026" exists for Islamabad Capital Territory. Its article 13(1) says: "All sewer cleaning and maintenance operations shall be conducted exclusively through mechanised systems and equipment." But, non-allocation of funds and resources voids all the legislation and its application.
The Hazardous Occupations Rules 1963 under the Factories Act says that work inside sewer pipelines, pits and storage tanks, as well as all scavenging, including hospital waste, are hazardous occupations. The treatment and status meted out to the sanitation workers stand in stark contrast to what Pakistan has pledged under the Sustainable Goals, especially Goal 8 - of improving the working conditions of sanitation workers. Even the targets 8.5 'full employment and decent work with equal pay' and 8.8 'protect labour rights and promote safe working environments' to be met by 2030 are still a distant dream, given the state's blithe disregard towards the working class.
Though Punjab struck down in 2016 the discriminatory policy of employing only non-Muslim minorities for janitorial work, a member from the majority is yet to be seen doing sanitation work anywhere in Punjab. However, the Suthra Punjab project has reduced manual scavenging to a large extent by replacing it with suctional jetting tankers and desludging machines. The imperative is to expand sewer networks, sewage treatment plants and proper desludging systems, so machines can operate effectively.
Nevertheless, in the recent eight months, 26 sanitation workers died across the country: eight in Karachi and 18 in Punjab. Hark, none of them were Muslim. Without any protective gear and provisions for health sustainability, the sanitation workers, being the pillars of urban hygiene, have to risk their lives to ensure the health of city dwellers. Their deaths lay bare the state's apathy that it has normalised the disposability of vulnerable communities.

title: Standing with teachers
description: Standing with teachers
content:
World Teachers' Day arrives this year with a message that deserves to travel beyond ceremonies and expressions of gratitude. The theme 'Standing with teachers' marks six decades since the landmark ILO-UNESCO recommendation that set international standards for teachers' rights, training, recruitment and working conditions.
For Pakistan, the occasion should force policymakers to question how well do we stand with those on whom the future of our children depends? Teachers occupy a peculiar place in our society. Their importance is routinely acknowledged, yet the profession itself is often denied the security and support such importance should command. In many public schools, teachers work in overcrowded classrooms with weak infrastructure and limited opportunities for professional development. Others serve in remote communities where staffing shortages mean that a single teacher can be responsible for an entire primary school. Last month, it was reported that more than 800 teaching posts were vacant in girls' schools in Lower Dir. Punjab, meanwhile, has extended the services of around 45,000 school teacher interns until May next year as it continues to deal with shortages through temporary appointments. Such arrangements may plug immediate gaps, but they cannot become a substitute for a stable recruitment system. This matters because an education system cannot consistently outperform the people who run its classrooms. New curricula and ambitious reform plans are of limited value if teachers are under appreciated or overburdened.
Pakistan must make teaching a profession that capable people want to enter and remain in. Recruitment should be based on need and competence rather than short-term administrative expediency. Training must continue throughout a teacher's career instead of ending with an initial qualification. Teachers also need a meaningful voice in decisions about curriculum and classroom practice. Standing with teachers ultimately means standing with every child whose future begins in their classroom.

title: Fixed tax failure
description: Fixed tax failure
content:
The government's flagship fixed tax scheme for retailers has collapsed at the starting line. Data from the final day for tax filing - September 30 - shows that just four new shopkeepers filed returns under the 1% fixed tax regime, while 787 returns were submitted in total. For comparison, an estimated 3.7 million retailers operate outside the tax net. The self-assessment scheme depended heavily on business owners acting scrupulously, which is laughable for anyone familiar with how price controls are followed in the country. Instead of willingly paying the nominal one per cent tax to fully legalise company revenues, business owners have instead chosen to go the outlaw route and refuse to willingly comply. Meanwhile, the FBR's notoriously weak enforcement capabilities mean that most of the offenders will feel no pain for their blatant tax evasion.
What makes things worse is that the scheme was extraordinarily generous, with many critics initially fearing that it was giving businesses a golden opportunity to whiten black money. Instead, it appears that many Pakistanis prefer their money to be black. The tax scheme offers retailers with annual sales up to Rs200 million a nominal 1% tax on revenue, complete exemption from audits, and no requirement to install point-of-sale systems. In return, traders were asked only to register and file. The government consulted trade bodies, launched a simplified Urdu-language application, and extended the filing deadline by fifteen days. Yet only 2,195 retailers registered in the first two months - a compliance rate of less than 0.06%.
Unfortunately, non-compliance often carries hilariously low penalties between Rs10,000 and Rs50,000 - which would probably not serve as a deterrent for most people. In fact, some analysts claim they are keeping the scheme alive on purpose. Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani, the brainchild of the scheme, has also threatened more punitive measures, including disconnecting utilities and freezing bank balances.

title: Asiad and dismal Pakistan
description: Asiad and dismal Pakistan
content:
The 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, concluded with a familiar regional hierarchy. China once again dominated the field to top the charts with 169 golds out of a total of 341 medals. Closely following were the hosts, Japan, with 83 golds in a total of 269 medals, and South Korea with 39 golds out of an overall tally of 150 medals.
However, the most compelling storyline of the tournament belonged to the subcontinent, highlighting the contrasting trajectories of Pakistan and India. While India enjoyed a historic outing, finishing 4th on the final standings with 21 golds in an 85-medal haul, Pakistan endured a devastating debacle, finishing a dismal 29th among 45 countries and regions. Pakistan's medal tally ultimately stalled at 10, without a single gold earned.
India's high standing was driven by exceptional performances in archery, wrestling and boxing. The Indian contingent put an emphatic stamp on their campaign on the final Saturday by completing "golden doubles" in both hockey and T20 cricket.
For Pakistan, the disappointment cut deep as the Green Shirts collapsed precisely in those disciplines where they were expected to shine i.e. cricket, hockey and javelin throw. Pakistan found themselves on the losing side of cricket and hockey encounters against their arch-rivals. Pakistan's men advanced to the T20 cricket final but fell 19 runs short of the target against India, settling for silver. The national team suffered a heartbreaking, chaotic semi-final loss to India, ultimately settling for bronze after defeating South Korea in the third-place match. In javelin throw, Olympic gold medalist Arshad Nadeem, the nation's best bet for a top-tier podium finish, surprisingly finished fourth.
This poor performance exposed the profound systemic decay, politicisation and sub-par training facilities plaguing sports management in Pakistan. Left even behind nations like Myanmar, Macau and Mongolia, Pakistan's empty gold tally stands as an urgent wake-up call. Without aggressive investment, structured athlete development and accountability, the gap between Pakistan and its thriving regional rivals will only continue to widen.

title: From friendly to  delusional
description: For Pakistan  the question is whether the Taliban leadership can still be relied upon as a partner against the TTP
content:
For Pakistan, the question is whether the Taliban leadership can still be relied upon as a partner against the TTP
Pakistan's relationship with the Afghan Taliban has entered a dangerous new phase. For months, Islamabad has been warning the Taliban regime that it cannot allow Afghan territory to be used by terrorist groups targeting Pakistan. There have been diplomatic contacts, warnings, mediation efforts, and repeated assurances. None of that appears to have worked. Pakistan is now relying increasingly on military force, carrying out strikes deep inside Afghanistan against what it says are terrorist hideouts and infrastructure. But perhaps more significant than the strikes themselves is the language coming out of Islamabad.
The latest Corps Commanders Conference, chaired by Field Marshal Asim Munir on Friday, strongly backed the military's strategy. The statement issued by the ISPR, however, contained a phrase that perhaps best captures how far relations with Kabul have deteriorated. The military leadership referred to the "delusional Taliban leadership" and its main backer, India, as being responsible for the rise in terrorist attacks in Pakistan. The choice of words was significant. The Taliban leadership was once seen by many in Pakistan as a potentially friendly government in Kabul. There was considerable optimism after the Taliban returned to power in August 2021 that Pakistan would finally have a government on its western border that understood its security concerns. That optimism has long disappeared.
At a recent press conference, Pakistan's chief military spokesperson made another significant claim. He said a meeting held in Kandahar on August 26 involved representatives of terrorist groups who were directed to intensify attacks against Pakistan. The revelation comes at a particularly difficult time for Pakistan. September was the deadliest month in 12 years in terms of terrorist attacks and fatalities, according to security data cited by an Islamabad think tank. In the first nine months of this year, terrorist attacks were up 52 per cent compared with the same period last year. That raises a difficult question for Islamabad: is the current strategy actually achieving its objective?
So far, there is little evidence that the pressure has produced the desired result. There are several possible explanations. The Taliban may not have the capacity to control these groups. It may be unwilling to take action against them. Or Kabul may believe that Pakistan's demands go too far. Whatever the reason, the relationship has reached a point where the old formula of engagement, diplomacy and pressure is no longer producing much.
Pakistan has tried almost everything short of a sustained military confrontation. It facilitated talks with the Taliban, maintained direct contacts with its leadership and brought in Qatar and Türkiye to help bridge differences. But all in vain. Now, the question for Pakistan is no longer simply how to persuade the Taliban to act against the TTP. It is whether the Taliban leadership itself can still be relied upon as a partner.
There is, at this stage, no official indication that Pakistan has decided to seek regime change in Afghanistan. But the increasingly hostile rhetoric and stepped-up military action are being closely watched by anti-Taliban forces inside Afghanistan. Some such forces have already increased attacks against the Taliban. That could open another, much more dangerous chapter in Afghanistan's long cycle of conflict. For Pakistan, there are no easy choices. Walking away from military pressure without securing action against the TTP could leave Islamabad facing an even bigger security problem. Continuing to strike inside Afghanistan risks a prolonged confrontation with the Taliban government.
What is becoming increasingly clear is that the Pakistan-Taliban relations are unlikely to return to where they were after the Taliban's return to power in 2021. Pakistan now appears to be moving towards a much harder Afghan policy, one in which military pressure is no longer simply a tool of last resort, but an increasingly central part of its strategy. The question is where this road ultimately leads.

content:
Drew Afualo says wedding planning caused hair loss and eyelid eczema before her August 2026 wedding to Pili Tanuvasa

The 31-year-old influencer married Tanuvasa in Hawaii after nine years together. Speaking to PEOPLE , Afualo said the preparations were stressful, particularly after major changes had to be made just weeks before the ceremony.
“I lost some hair and I developed eczema on my eyelids, but I did win in the end,” Afualo said while discussing the physical toll of wedding planning.
The couple faced a major setback four weeks before their wedding when Afualo said they had to replace both their wedding planner and venue. Despite the last-minute changes, she said the wedding day itself went smoothly without any major problems.
Afualo described the celebration as “wonderful” and said one of the most meaningful aspects was having her favourite people together in one place. She also highlighted the opportunity to employ Indigenous people for the wedding as an important part of the celebration.
With the wedding behind her, Afualo is now settling into married life with Tanuvasa. The influencer described being newlywed as “amazing” and said the relationship feels much the same despite entering a new chapter.
Afualo said she is particularly looking forward to continuing to grow alongside her partner during their first year of marriage.
The couple’s wedding followed a nine-year relationship, with the Hawaii ceremony marking a new stage in their lives together. Afualo has continued to share aspects of her personal life and career with her large online audience.

title: 40 years on  Sindh quota faces fresh challenge
description: MDCAT results rekindle debate as educated Sindhi voices join calls to scrap urban rural divide
content:
MDCAT results rekindle debate as educated Sindhi voices join calls to scrap urban-rural divide
A system introduced decades ago to bridge Sindh’s urban-rural divide is facing renewed scrutiny, with a growing number of educated Sindhi voices now joining the long-standing demand from Urdu-speaking circles for an end to the quota regime in government jobs and educational institutions.
The debate has gained fresh momentum after the latest MDCAT results, in which students from some of Sindh’s most underdeveloped districts, including Tharparkar, outperformed candidates from Karachi, Hyderabad and Sukkur.
For critics of the quota system, the results have raised a fundamental question: does a policy designed to compensate for rural deprivation still serve the purpose for which it was introduced?
What was once largely framed as an urban-rural or Sindhi-Urdu dispute is consequently taking on a different complexion.
A section of educated Sindhi-speaking professionals and academics now argues that improvements in education and healthcare facilities in rural Sindh have narrowed the gap, while the quota system is increasingly reinforcing divisions between the province’s communities rather than addressing them.
Abdul Aleem Lashari, a retired bureaucrat who has served in various positions in Sindh, recently wrote on social media that “this is the right time to abolish the quota system”. Speaking to The Express Tribune , he said he believed the province no longer needed the quota system.
Read More: Panel to probe into Sindh MDCAT complaints
Serving bureaucrat Nadeem Memon, responding to Lashari’s post, observed that a large number of young people in Karachi preferred employment in the private sector and multinational companies over government jobs.
He argued that ending the quota system could encourage urban youth who had stayed away from government employment to return to the competitive examination system.
Prominent Sindhi scholar Naseer Memon, who is based in Islamabad, said the quota system had been in place for around four decades. Although the facilities available in urban and rural areas had not become equal during this period, he said the gap between the two had nevertheless narrowed.
Memon also maintained that the quota system was contributing to divisions between Sindhi- and Urdu-speaking communities in the province. He called for the urban-rural quota to be abolished and replaced with equal, merit-based opportunities for all candidates.
MQM-Pakistan Deputy Parliamentary Leader in the Sindh Assembly Taha Ahmed Khan also backed the call, describing the rural-urban quota as a discriminatory policy from the outset.
He alleged that the Pakistan Peoples Party had used the system to institutionalise a divide between the people of Sindh’s urban and rural areas. “It is time to abolish this discriminatory system and provide equal opportunities to everyone,” Khan said.

title: PTI says access to Imran Khan  K P counterterrorism policy led to talks deadlock
description: Both sides trade blame with competing accounts emerging over what had been agreed and why the process broke down
content:
Both sides trade blame with competing accounts emerging over what had been agreed and why the process broke down
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) on Sunday expressed regret over the failure of negotiations between its joint team with Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Ain Pakistan (TTAP) and government representatives, urging the government to address the reasons for the deadlock and demonstrate its willingness to engage in meaningful dialogue.
In a statement on X, the party said the negotiations concluded without substantive progress despite “serious efforts” to address political stability, restoration of democracy, supremacy of the Constitution and law, access to PTI founder Imran Khan, his health and medical treatment, and the worsening security situation in K-P and other parts of the country.
PRESS RELEASE PTI Responds to Inconclusive Negotiations and Federal Ministers’ Press Conference Party Says Denial of Access to Chairman Imran Khan Remained Central Impediment; Calls for Consensus Based Counterterrorism Strategy and Immediate Attention to Khan’s Medical Care…
PTI said the principal point of deadlock was its demand for immediate access to Khan so that the party leadership could consult him on matters of national and political importance.
It said its negotiating team had conveyed that other demands could be set aside if the government agreed to this single request. However, according to the party, the government declined to make access to Khan part of the proposed agreement.
The party maintained that consultation with political leadership was an essential part of the democratic process, arguing that just as leaders of other political parties remained central to their parties’ policy and decision-making, PTI should also be able to consult its chairman on major political and national issues.
“Restricting such consultation, particularly during a critical period for the country, inevitably limits the scope for meaningful political engagement,” it said.
PTI further stated that the situation in K-P was another major issue discussed during the negotiations.
According to the party, the government side sought the provincial government’s unconditional support for counterterrorism measures and operations undertaken by the federation and relevant authorities, as well as support for emergency measures within 72 hours in the merged districts and adjoining areas.
PTI reiterated its “unequivocal condemnation” of terrorism and stressed that eliminating terrorism, protecting citizens and restoring lasting peace must remain a national priority.
The party paid tribute to officers and personnel of the armed forces, police, security forces and other law-enforcement agencies who had sacrificed their lives in the fight against terrorism, while expressing solidarity with civilians and families affected by terrorist violence.
It said the people of the province had paid an “extraordinary price” over the years through loss of life, destruction of property and businesses, prolonged insecurity and displacement. “Their concerns and experiences must therefore remain central to any future counterterrorism policy,” PTI said.
Also Read : Naqvi blames K-P CM for talks ‘collapse’, warns Afridi will ‘be responsible’ if anyone dies during march
The party maintained that terrorism could not be defeated through force alone or through unilateral measures that could expose civilians to further loss of life, property damage or displacement.
“Past experience must inform future policy,” it said, adding that any effective strategy must combine firm action against terrorism with protection of civilian populations and sensitivity to local realities.
PTI proposed that authorised representatives of the federal and K-P governments meet within 72 hours to develop a “clear, comprehensive and mutually agreed strategy” for peace and counterterrorism.
It further proposed consultations with political parties represented in the K-P Assembly, elected representatives, tribal elders and other relevant stakeholders so that any policy could enjoy public confidence and be implemented effectively.
The party also rejected attempts to characterise the position of Chief Minister Sohail Afridi as political obstinacy, arguing that had access to Khan been facilitated, the chief minister could have consulted the PTI chairman directly on security and counterterrorism policy, potentially helping bridge differences and create greater consensus.
PTI said effective cooperation among the federal government, provincial government and relevant authorities was indispensable for national security. Such cooperation, however, must respect constitutional requirements, the role of the elected provincial government and the legitimate concerns of the people directly affected, it added.
It further said the health and medical treatment of Khan was also raised as a matter of “fundamental importance”.
The negotiating team sought immediate access to him, his transfer to Shifa International Hospital and the constitution of an appropriate medical board with the participation of his personal physician to ensure proper examination, diagnosis and treatment, according to the statement.
Read More : Kundi, Naqvi slam K-P govt over counterterrorism role during talks
PTI said the government had agreed only to restore meetings between Khan and his family members and lawyers from Tuesday, but had not agreed to additional measures concerning his medical assessment and treatment.
The party welcomed the resumption of family and legal meetings but stressed that such access could not substitute for proper medical examination and necessary treatment. “Khan’s health must be addressed with seriousness, transparency and humanitarian consideration,” it said, adding that all medically necessary steps should be taken without delay.
Responding to the subsequent press conference by federal ministers, PTI said the government should refrain from placing responsibility for the inconclusive negotiations entirely on the opposition and instead address the substantive issues that prevented progress.
It called on the government to explain why immediate access to Khan was considered unacceptable, why the requested measures regarding his medical care were not accommodated, and why a broader consultative approach involving the provincial government, political representatives, tribal elders and other stakeholders was not accepted for developing a sustainable security strategy for K-P.
PTI reiterated that it remained prepared to engage in political dialogue, constitutional processes, meaningful consultation and national consensus to address Khan’s health and treatment, restoration of democracy, supremacy of the Constitution and law, political stability, terrorism and other challenges confronting the country.
The party stressed, however, that meaningful negotiations could not succeed through predetermined positions or demands for unconditional endorsement. “Serious dialogue requires flexibility, mutual confidence, consultation and a genuine willingness to translate discussions into practical progress,” it concluded.
Salman Akram Raja says talks broke down over K-P counterterrorism policy
PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja also said that the deadlock in negotiations with the federal government emerged over the issue of counterterrorism policy in K-P.
Speaking to a private news channel on Sunday, he stated that PTI’s negotiating team maintained that any future strategy against terrorism in K-P should not be determined solely by the federal government.
He said that if the federal government wanted administrative measures that could displace people from their homes, the provincial government could not be held responsible for the consequences if it had no meaningful role in policy formulation.
Raja added that as drafts were amended during talks with the government, PTI’s negotiating team realised that the government’s intentions on some issues were broader than initially understood.
He said the drafts were shared with CM Afridi and the PTI negotiating team because the provincial leadership, being directly responsible for running the province, could better assess the consequences of the proposed measures.
حکومت اور پی ٹی آئی/تحریک تحفظ آئین پاکستان مزاکرات کی ناکامی کی بنیادی وجہ حکومتی اصرار تھا کہ خیبر پختونخواہ حکومت وفاق اور اسکے اداروں کے ان تمام اقدام اور آپریشنز کی تائید کرے جو صوبے میں دہشت گردی کے حوالے سے کئے جائیں گے۔ ضم اضلاع اور ان سے متصل علاقوں میں 72 گھنٹوں میں…
Raja underlined that PTI therefore proposed that the federal and provincial governments jointly formulate a strategy, followed by consultations with all political parties, including Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz and Pakistan Peoples Party, as well as tribal elders and other relevant stakeholders.
Raja said the government rejected suggestions of a “roadmap” and a “joint strategy” and instead wanted emergency measures imposed in several districts within 72 hours.
Rejecting claims that the K-P government had already agreed to the proposals, he said there was no fundamental disagreement between Afridi and the PTI negotiating team.
He added that an English draft contained a provision for imposing an emergency within 72 hours, while the same provision had reportedly been removed from the Urdu version. He said that once the government’s intentions became clear, PTI agreed it could not accept the proposal.
Commenting on the Police Act 2026, Raja said the K-P government was willing to review the legislation, adding that the law could be examined within 72 hours alongside legislation in Punjab, Sindh and Balochistan to identify provisions that could be applied in the case of K-P.
He also stated that there was no disagreement over the National Action Plan, which was a “national, consensus-based document”, further noting that the dispute was over its implementation.
He further said that PTI could not support measures such as drone strikes and operations that displaced people from their homes, adding that the party had consistently opposed such actions in the past.
Raja said that if an emergency was imposed in certain districts and the federal government then decided what action to take without consulting the provincial government, there could be no jointly agreed strategy. “In that situation, anything can happen.”
Leaving all other issues and much noise aside, the primary reason for the failure of the talks around 3am this morning between the government team and the PTI-TTAP team was the following: the PTI-TTAP team stood firm on its principled position that anti-terorrism actions in KPK…
He further said PTI could neither endorse such a policy nor take responsibility for its consequences. PTI, he said, had proposed that the federal and provincial governments formulate a mutually agreed strategy within 72 hours and then implement it.
He rejected allegations that PTI and the K-P government’s position was aligned with the interests of militants, calling such claims “extremely unfortunate” and “completely wrong and contrary to facts”.
He added that PTI stood firmly against terrorism and supported “zero tolerance” for terrorist groups, adding that the party wanted to work with the federal government to eliminate terrorism.
On the security situation in K-P, Raja acknowledged that the government’s writ had weakened in some districts and that militant groups wielded significant influence.
However, he said the underlying causes needed to be understood rather than simply blaming the provincial government. PTI lawmakers and ministers, he added, were themselves among those being targeted by militants. “The realities on the ground in K-P cannot be understood while sitting afar in Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi,” he maintained.
Raja said a comprehensive strategy should also take into account ground realities, local communities and tribal traditions, while facilitating dialogue among tribes living on both sides of the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.
He maintained that a sustainable policy against terrorism in K-P required consultation between the federal and provincial governments, political parties and local stakeholders, rather than unilateral measures that could potentially fuel further displacement and instability. “Military operations alone cannot resolve the security crisis in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” he stated.
Raja said PTI had proposed that the two sides “sit together for 72 hours, discuss the matter thoroughly and then move forward with an agreed policy”.
On negotiations concerning Imran Khan, he said the issue of access to Imran’s personal doctors had remained unresolved. “PTI’s position is that Imran should be transferred to a hospital with an international medical board and doctors personally trusted by his family be involved in his treatment”.
He added that the proposed arrangement for access to Imran included a meeting with his family and lawyers on Tuesday, while the question of meetings with other political figures remained unresolved.
Raja identified two issues as fundamental deal-breakers: the proposed counterterrorism policy in K-P and the treatment of Imran’s personal and legal matters.
Responding to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s claim that many of the political issues had been agreed upon, Raja said minor issues could not outweigh the unresolved major ones.
He underlined that the government was effectively asking PTI to abandon its position on counterterrorism and accept the policy the federal government had decided to implement.
Raja said PTI could not set aside what he described as the personal victimisation of Imran and accept the treatment he was receiving in prison. “These two issues were such that they overshadowed everything else,” he added.
He concluded that it was PTI’s responsibility to speak out and that the party would continue its political struggle regardless of the obstacles it faced.
Amir Muqam rejects PTI’s account of failed talks, says key issues had been agreed upon
Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam, while presenting the government’s position on the talks, rejected Raja’s account of the breakdown in negotiations, saying the talks had been conducted in good faith and that most of the issues raised by PTI had been resolved.
Muqam said representatives from both sides held extensive discussions, including a session lasting around 12 hours, with the aim of preventing the dispute from escalating into a confrontation between the federal and K-P governments.
He stated that PTI’s concerns relating to Imran had been addressed, adding that an agreement had been reached that Imran would continue to meet his lawyers and family members in prison and that arrangements concerning his medical treatment would also be discussed.
Muqam said the wording of the draft agreement had been revised following discussions with PTI and that the issue concerning Imran’s meetings had effectively been settled.
He said the remaining disagreement concerned the issue of terrorism and the role of the K-P government in implementing the counterterrorism policy.
Muqam said the federal side had told PTI from the outset that the K-P government’s participation was necessary because the matter directly concerned the province. He added that PTI representatives had sought time to consult the provincial leadership in Peshawar and subsequently returned saying they had obtained full authority to negotiate on its behalf.
Also Read : Asif, Tarar fire fresh salvoes at PTI after talks deadlock
Rejecting the claim that the government had demanded an emergency in several districts within 72 hours, Muqam said the proposal was instead to use the 72 hours to formulate and sign an agreed course of action between the provincial government and the interior ministry.
He underscored that the 72-hour timeframe was intended for the two sides to sit together, settle the outstanding issues and determine how the counterterrorism strategy would be implemented.
He also rejected PTI’s claim that the federal government wanted to impose its policy unilaterally on K-P. He said the National Action Plan was a national policy and could not be treated as a policy applicable only to K-P.
Referring to a resolution passed by the K-P Assembly, Muqam said the resolution itself contained provisions concerning the use of police and the Counter Terrorism Department to combat terrorism and opposition to military operations.
He further questioned PTI’s position, arguing that the party could not simultaneously demand that the military be excluded from operations while also seeking greater authority and resources for the provincial government.
He also criticised what he described as changes made by the K-P government to its own counterterrorism policy and said powers had subsequently been withdrawn from relevant institutions. “This is a national issue,” he said, adding that the government could consider legitimate proposals but could not make every provincial demand part of the agreement at that stage.
On the question of whether it had been decided that an emergency would be imposed in K-P, Muqam indicated that the matter was still part of the ongoing discussions and did not confirm that a final decision to impose emergency measures had been taken.
Asad Qaiser says access to Imran at heart of talks deadlock
PTI leader Asad Qaiser also stated that the deadlock in negotiations with the government centred on the party’s demand for access to PTI founder Imran Khan.
“The root cause of the deadlock was that we were under the impression that first you would provide us access to Imran Khan,” he said, adding that PTI had withdrawn all its other demands and retained only the request for its political leadership to meet Imran.
In a post on X, Qaiser said the government had told PTI that Imran would not be part of the agreement and that his involvement was “not under consideration” at that stage. He stated that PTI should be able to consult Imran on major policy decisions, just as other political parties consult their leadership.
“If the PML-N consults Nawaz Sharif or Shehbaz Sharif on every matter, or the PPP consults Bilawal Bhutto and Asif Zardari, then our leader Imran Khan — who is the most popular leader and is in jail — shouldn’t we consult him on whatever policy is made?” Qaiser asked. “Shouldn’t we take his direction? So that’s our biggest issue,” he said.
ڈیڈلاک کی بنیادی وجہ یہ تھی کہ ہم یہ سمجھ رہے تھے کہ سب سے پہلے آپ ہمیں عمران خان تک ایکسیس دیں۔ اور ہم نے کہا کہ ہم تمام مطالبات واپس کرتے ہیں، ہمارا ایک ہی مطالبہ ہے کہ ہماری پولیٹیکل لیڈرشپ کو عمران خان تک رسائی دی جائے۔ تو انہوں نے کہا کہ ابھی تک وہ ایگریمنٹ میں شامل نہیں… pic.twitter.com/gbRfkCuXqA
Rejecting the suggestion that PTI was seeking to give the issue of terrorism a political dimension, Qaiser said the party had proposed a mechanism for greater coordination between the federal and provincial governments to address militancy.
He said PTI’s proposed text called for “effective, continuous and meaningful consultation” to eliminate terrorism in K-P, protect lives and property and establish lasting peace.
He further stated that the proposal envisaged regular reviews of existing policies and measures, with amendments where necessary, adding that it also called for authorised representatives of the federal and provincial governments to meet within 72 hours and jointly prepare a “clear, comprehensive, feasible and agreed-upon roadmap” for peace and security.
“All responsible leaders and stakeholders of political parties” would also be included in the process so that the resulting policy could secure wider public trust, Qaiser said.
Earlier on Sunday, the party launched the first phase of its long march from Lakki Marwat to Swabi amid a government-opposition deadlock and mounting political tensions, with no plan for a march towards Islamabad announced so far.
The long march, initially scheduled for September 27, was postponed to October 4, but the standoff between the federal and provincial governments remains unresolved.
On Saturday, talks between the government and opposition failed to break the deadlock over the PTI’s long march, with both sides maintaining their positions and pressing competing demands.
The talks, chaired by National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq, followed an initial round on Friday in which the two sides exchanged their positions but failed to reach an agreement.
The government wanted the PTI to take the initiative by cancelling the march, while the opposition wanted the government to first facilitate a meeting with its jailed founder, according to sources familiar with the talks.

title: Houthis claim missile and drone attacks on Saudi Aramco after 50 strikes on Yemen
description: Yemen s Saudi backed government launches major operation to seize territory held by Houthis
content:
Yemen's Saudi-backed government launches major operation to seize territory held by Houthis
The leader of Yemen's Saudi-backed government announced the beginning of a major military operation against the Iran-backed Houthis on Sunday, aimed at seizing the ‌territory under their control.
Regional and western officials had told Reuters earlier this week that Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies were planning to launch an assault on the Houthis, with the Saudis leading aerial combat and Yemeni forces fighting on the ground.
"Today, I announce the start of military operations to retake the remaining territory of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory," Yemeni ​President Rashad al-Alimi said in a televised address.
The Houthis, meanwhile, said they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area ​of Saudi Arabia, claiming the attacks caused major fires, in response to what they said were 50 Saudi-led air and missile strikes on ⁠Yemen in the past 12 hours.
There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia.
'Opportunities for de-escalation exhausted'
Al-Alimi said the decision to launch the counteroffensive came after all opportunities for de-escalation had been ​exhausted, accusing the Houthis of responding to efforts to calm the conflict with further mobilisation and escalation.
"Our position today is to assume the national responsibility of confronting the Houthi militia, after ​all opportunities for de-escalation have been exhausted," he said.
Al-Alimi said he had ordered the armed forces, security forces and all military formations to begin carrying out their assigned tasks under approved plans.
Saudi Arabia entered neighbouring Yemen's civil war in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition in support of the internationally recognised government, which the Houthis had driven out of the capital Sanaa.
Al-Alimi thanked Saudi Arabia for its support, saying the ​kingdom had "stood alongside Yemen in the darkest circumstances," and called on Yemen's regional allies and international partners to support the country, its armed forces and state institutions.
The US is already ​providing intelligence to support Riyadh's operations in Yemen, while some regional and European nations are providing mainly defensive military aid to the kingdom, six people with knowledge of the Saudi preparations told Reuters .
A truce agreed ‌between the ⁠warring parties in 2022 largely held until this year, when the Houthis launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi shipping and oil infrastructure in a spillover from the Iran war.
The Houthis have so far maintained the initiative on the ground, weeks after seizing the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait in a lightning offensive down the coast that saw government forces collapse.
Bab el-Mandeb is the southern exit passage of the Red Sea, a key shipping route between the Mediterranean and Asia that has assumed even more importance this year as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz , ​which has been effectively closed by the ​Iran conflict.
Read More: Araghchi says Tehran serious about diplomatic path, rules out ‘military solution’ to end war
The Houthis already controlled the northwest ⁠of the country, where most of the population live.
In the last 48 hours, the Houthis have also made gains against government and local forces on strategic hilltops near Yemen's Taiz, military sources said, advancing on the last road between the city and Aden on the southern coast, ​where the Saudi-backed Yemeni government is based.
Houthi control over the Taiz-Aden road would lead to an effective siege of the city, Yemen's ​third-largest, inhabited by hundreds of ⁠thousands of civilians and where thousands of government forces are also stationed.
It would also consolidate control of that flat coastal Bab el-Mandeb area by seizing the rugged mountains overlooking them in the western Taiz countryside, according to Mohammed Al-Qadhi, a veteran Yemeni journalist from Taiz now working as a political analyst.
"This will help them protect their back in case of any operation against the coastline, and ⁠make recapturing ​those areas much more difficult," he said.
The city is important not just for its strategic location; Yemeni President Rashad ​al-Alimi is from the region, and a siege of Taiz would amplify an already-dire humanitarian situation in the country.
Three-in-four families in parts of Yemen are going hungry from the impact of the surge in fighting, which has displaced ​tens of thousands of people and disrupted supplies to millions, the World Food Programme said last week.

title: A taste of home in orbit  How China keeps its astronauts well fed
description: China s space kitchen now offers nearly 200 dishes  including dumplings  Kung Pao chicken and fried rice
content:
China's space kitchen now offers nearly 200 dishes, including dumplings, Kung Pao chicken and fried rice
Although called Tiangong, or "Heavenly Palace," China's space station is becoming less distant and more like home, as astronauts bring the comforting tastes into orbit.
The Chinese space kitchen now serves nearly 200 food items. Alongside dumplings and mooncakes, home-style dishes such as Kung Pao chicken, mapo tofu and fried rice have made it onto the station's menu.
Videos showing astronauts savoring freshly cooked meat and cakes in orbit have gone viral. Their smiling faces and bright eyes make the aroma almost leap off the screen.
Yang Liwei, the country's first astronaut, joked at a recent press conference that he was envious. He said astronauts can now use air-frying equipment in space and enjoy baked chicken wings in orbit. During his Shenzhou-5 mission in 2003, which lasted less than one day, his diet was limited to packaged instant food that could not be heated.
Microgravity, cosmic radiation and the enclosed cabin environment impose strict requirements on space diets. Floating particles and droplets may drift into instruments and trigger malfunctions. Since Yuri Gagarin, the first human to travel into space, paste-like food and compressed energy bars had long served as the standard meals for astronauts.
In June 2013, Wang Yaping, together with two fellow male crewmates, carried out the 15-day Shenzhou-10 space mission. People remembered this female astronaut with a ponytail for her space lecture. At the same time, the image of her floating a "zongzi," a leaf-wrapped rice dumpling, by hand also left a deep impression on the public.
Zongzi is traditionally enjoyed during the Dragon Boat Festival, which happened to coincide with the Shenzhou-10 mission that year. To help the astronauts celebrate, this special snack was added to the spaceship pantry.
Eight years later, Wang spent Spring Festival aboard the Tiangong space station during the Shenzhou-13 mission. It is also China's first six-month-long space stay. Scientists customized the cuisine: for instance, they prepared dumplings with seafood fillings because Wang grew up by the sea, and plenty of spicy food for crew member Ye Guangfu, who was born in chili-obsessed Sichuan Province.
At that time, the core module Tianhe had several sections, including those for working, sleeping, dining and exercising. The videos of Shenzhou-13 crew practicing calligraphy and playing Taichi became social media hits.
China completed the construction of its space station in 2022, with one core module and two lab modules forming a 110-square-meter orbital structure. Oxygen can be fully regenerated, and water recovery exceeds 95 percent.
Since then, long-duration spaceflights have become routine, and the Chinese "space home" can host up to six astronauts in orbit at a time.
Space residency is also set to last even longer. One member of the Shenzhou-23 crew, currently aboard the Tiangong, will conduct a one-year in-orbit stay. Moreover, as China pushes further into deep-space exploration, these extended stays will become the norm, which means astronauts' diets will be more important than ever.
Read More: Chinese rocket firm, disease research lab to test space pharmaceutical payloads
Because weightlessness causes bone calcium loss and muscle atrophy, space food must be high in calcium and protein, low in sodium and balanced in dietary fiber. According to the Astronaut Center of China, researchers have developed space food that counteracts oxidative damage, supports immunity, reduces fatigue and regulates the gut microbiome.
But taste is another problem. In microgravity, blood shifts upward, causing nasal congestion and cutting smell sensitivity by at least 30 percent. Since taste is closely tied to smell, astronauts often find food bland. The center's researchers have responded with adding more strong-flavored dishes, with liquid soy sauce and concentrated chili sauce.
New technology has also played a big role in keeping astronauts well-fed.
The astronaut center, in collaboration with private companies, has upgraded the "space kitchen" with a suite of intelligent appliances for drinking water, food reheating and baking. This allows astronauts in orbit to enjoy hot meals within 20 minutes, rather than waiting longer or eating cold food. Liu Weibo, an expert with the center, gave an example of the hot-air baking oven, which is a pioneering Chinese design for space use that can efficiently remove cooking fumes and allow astronauts to enjoy barbecue in orbit.
During a space lecture for Hong Kong and Macao students last month, Shenzhou-23 crew member Li Jiaying, or Lai Ka-ying in Cantonese, showed freshly baked cakes and said they reminded her of egg waffles, a popular snack from her hometown. She is a Hong Kong local.
Space food supplies have also become more diverse and nutritious, including more fruits and vegetables, as well as frozen steak and chicken wings. The next-generation cargo craft Qingzhou, designed for future in-orbit supply delivery, will have greater cold-chain transport capacity.
However, long-term space residency requires reducing dependence on Earth's supplies, said center expert Bian Qiang. "The controlled ecological life-support tests we are conducting are intended to build an ecosystem in space that regenerates water, air and food on site, to reduce extraterrestrial survival's dependence on Earth resupply and ultimately achieve self-sufficiency."
Since the Shenzhou-16 mission in 2023, China has been growing plants in orbit. It has tested more than 20 varieties from 14 plant species, including lettuce, carrots, potatoes and wheat.
The Shenzhou-18 crew in 2024 was tasked with raising fish in an "aquarium" to study how space affects their growth. Scientists said the work may one day allow astronauts to enjoy fish from their own in-orbit harvests.
China is targeting a crewed lunar landing by 2030. Living on the moon will make resupply much more challenging because of the increased distance from Earth.
"We plan to build a Chinese 'lunar vegetable garden' on the moon," Bian said.
From heating, baking to farming, feeding astronauts well in space is not a luxury. It is part of the mission, bringing a taste of home to the universe.

title: When New York turns the movies into a summer ritual
description: From Bryant Park to Pier 17 rooftops  outdoor screenings are turning films and TV finales into shared city experiences
content:
From Bryant Park to Pier 17 rooftops, outdoor screenings are turning films and TV finales into shared city experiences
From Bryant Park to Pier 17 and Manhattan rooftops, New Yorkers are turning movie and television screenings into shared summer rituals, where the setting, the crowd and the stories become part of the experience.
There is something different about watching a movie in New York when the cinema has no walls.
Instead of rows of seats in a dark theatre, there is grass beneath you, people arriving with blankets and snacks, friends trying to find a good spot, couples settling in beside strangers and a city skyline providing a backdrop that no movie theatre could reproduce.
Then the lights go down and, for the next two hours, hundreds of people are watching the same story together.
That simple idea has become one of New York's most enjoyable summer rituals. Across the city, parks, waterfronts and rooftops are transformed into temporary cinemas.
Some screenings are devoted to beloved classics, while others are built around the latest television obsession.
Many of the outdoor events are free and operate on a first-come, first-served basis, while special screenings may require registration or reservations. But what they have in common is the feeling of watching something together.
After experiencing several of these events myself, I have started to think that the movie is sometimes only half of the attraction.
Bryant Park is one of the clearest examples of how this works. Its Movie Nights have become a New York summer tradition, with people arriving well before the film begins to claim a place on the lawn.
The atmosphere starts building long before the opening credits, as people bring blankets, meet friends, bring food and settle in for an evening rather than simply arriving for a two-hour screening.
This year, the summer movie-night special ended with The Truman Show being screened for the second time, as watchers came in the afternoon and waited until after sunset for the film to begin.
Sitting on the lawn in the middle of Manhattan and watching a film that so many people already know by heart made the experience feel strangely new.
The movie itself was familiar, but the setting and the audience changed it. Someone laughs at a line you have heard ten times before, someone reacts to a scene you had forgotten was coming, and people around you quietly comment on moments as they happen. You become part of an audience again.
Perhaps that is one reason these screenings feel particularly appealing now, when so much entertainment is consumed privately and on demand.
Streaming has made it possible to watch almost anything at any time, but it has also made entertainment increasingly solitary. Outdoor cinema brings back the simple pleasure of reacting to a story alongside other people.
The phenomenon is not limited to old movies. Last summer, I experienced the other side of this culture with The Summer I Turned Pretty .
I went to Bryant Park for a special screening of the first two episodes of the show's third and final season. Fans gathered on the lawn with blankets, snacks and friends, and the atmosphere was closer to a concert or fan gathering than an ordinary television screening.
What made the evening particularly memorable was the appearance of the cast. The actors came onto the stage to greet the fans, turning what had already been a large communal viewing experience into a live fan event.
For people who had followed the characters and storylines through the previous seasons, suddenly seeing the cast in front of them added another layer to the experience.
The audience already had theories, favourite characters and strong opinions about what was going to happen next. So when something happened on screen, the reaction travelled across the lawn: laughter, screams, cheers and collective gasps. It was essentially a giant group chat, except everyone was sitting together in the same physical space.
That is where watching television becomes something more than watching television. The audience is no longer simply consuming an episode; it is participating in a shared cultural moment.
The same idea takes on a completely different atmosphere at Pier 17. Brooklyn Bridge Park's Movies With A View brings free outdoor films to the waterfront, where audiences can watch with New York Harbor and the Manhattan skyline behind the screen. The screenings are first-come, first-served, making arriving early part of the ritual.
I first watched Forrest Gump at Pier 17, where the waterfront setting changes the entire feeling of a familiar film. The light changes as the evening progresses, the water moves, buildings begin to glow and the skyline becomes part of the visual experience. Somewhere between the real city and the movie on the screen, the two begin to overlap.
You are not just watching Forrest Gump anymore. You are watching Forrest Gump in New York on a summer night. That distinction sounds small, but it is exactly what makes these events memorable. The location becomes part of the story you remember later, just as much as the film itself.
The Summer I Turned Pretty experience also showed another side of this new entertainment culture.
For the show's finale, I attended a special screening event at the rooftop at 230 Fifth, where the atmosphere was much closer to a nightlife event than a traditional television screening. There was a bar-style rooftop setting, fans gathered around the screening and the feeling that the finale was an occasion rather than simply another episode.
There were even Sephora gift bags with Summer Fridays lip balms as part of the special collab.
That detail might sound incidental, but it says a lot about where entertainment culture is going. The show was not only being watched; it was being experienced, photographed, branded and remembered. The screening itself became content, the rooftop became part of the story, and the gift bag became something to photograph and take home.
The people attending were not just viewers anymore. They were part of a community of fans who could say they were there.
This is where the relationship between entertainment and brands becomes particularly interesting. Streaming platforms and advertisers have realised that audiences do not necessarily want another advertisement telling them to watch something. Increasingly, they want to be invited into the world of the show.
The Summer I Turned Pretty Bryant Park event is a good example. Prime Video partnered with T-Mobile to transform the park into an experience inspired by the show's Cousins Beach setting, with themed installations and fan activities. The event brought the fictional world of the series into a real New York park and gave fans an opportunity to interact with the show beyond simply watching it on a screen.
The brand is no longer simply interrupting the entertainment; it is helping construct an experience around it. A beauty company can appear through gift bags, a telecommunications company can create a fan experience and a streaming platform can transform a television premiere into a physical gathering. The marketing becomes experiential.
And that can be remarkably effective because people are more likely to remember an experience than an advertisement. You may forget seeing a sponsored post online, but you are less likely to forget sitting on a lawn with hundreds of fans, watching a new episode and then seeing the cast walk onto the stage in front of you.
There is a larger cultural reason these evenings work. New York is one of the most densely populated cities in the world, yet it can also be surprisingly isolating. We pass thousands of people every day without knowing anything about them. Outdoor cinema temporarily changes that dynamic because everyone is looking at the same screen, waiting for the same scene and reacting to the same ending.
For a few hours, strangers become a temporary community.
That may be the most interesting thing about the city's outdoor cinema culture. It is not really about replacing the movie theatre; it is about adding something that the theatre, and certainly streaming at home, cannot provide: a sense of occasion, a sense of place and a sense that other people are experiencing the same thing at exactly the same moment.
Perhaps that is why New Yorkers keep coming back, bringing blankets, snacks and friends and waiting for the sun to go down. In a city where everyone is constantly moving, these screenings offer a rare opportunity to stop, sit beside strangers and share a story from beginning to end.
Because sometimes we do not just want to watch the story. We want to have someone beside us when it happens.

title: Absolutely not     CM Afridi rejects    closed room    decisions on military operations in K P
description: Next phase of the long march will also be announced at Khairabad
content:
Vows to reject policies against people’s interests as PTI long march convoy reaches Karak
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Muhammad Sohail Afridi on Sunday rejected military operations and drone attacks in the province, saying the decisions affecting the people of K-P should be made in the province rather than in “closed rooms”.
The march, which started earlier on Sunday, reached Karak late at night, with the convoy led by the CM Afridi entering the district and staying there overnight before proceeding further on Monday.
Addressing participants of the march at Khatam-e-Nabuwwat Chowk on the Bannu-Karak border, Afridi said the struggle was not only for the Pashtuns but for the entire country.
“I salute your morale for waiting 10 to 12 hours in this heat,” he said, describing the march as a Test match that would be turned into a T20 match in two days.
He said PTI founder Imran Khan had said “absolutely not” to America, while he had said the same to “decision-makers in closed rooms”.
“Yesterday evening, Imran Khan’s chief minister, the chief minister of the Pashtuns, has said absolutely not to military operations and drone attacks,” Afridi said adding that the decisions of the people of K-P will be made right here in the province.
He said that “decision-makers in closed rooms have always sold our blood, but now decisions will be made in the fields in line with the people’s aspirations.”
He said the southern region of the province, where “terrorism and operations are constantly imposed”, also suffered collateral damage from drone attacks.
“We keep saying that the policy you’ve enforced for 22 years is fueling terrorism,” he said, adding that peace had been witnessed “only and only” during Khan’s three-and-a-half-year tenure.
Afridi said that after the regime change, when terrorism was “being imposed again twofold”, his party had repeatedly raised its voice but was told that it was lying.
“We will say absolutely not to every policy that is not in the people’s interest,” he said.
The chief minister said he had no guns and possessed only “the power of the people”. He claimed that people in the southern region had rejected every policy that was not in their favour.
He said the entire nation wanted Khan to come out of prison and lead the country.
“Imran Khan is not breaking; his wife and sisters have been thrown in jail, yet he has not bowed,” Afridi said.
He urged participants to come out and deliver the message that they wanted only one leader, Imran Khan.
“Imran Khan is the guarantee of national unity and the youth’s future,” he said, adding that Khan was the only leader who could restore the country’s honour and dignity.
Afridi rejects governor’s rule, emergency
Earlier, addressing participants of the long march at Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat, the chief minister thanked the participants for their enthusiasm and said the party’s negotiating committee had gone to Islamabad to help reduce the political temperature.
He said a “mindset that makes decisions behind closed doors” had been trying to impose another decision on the people of the province. “Here, there is Imran Khan’s government and Imran Khan’s vision and policy will prevail,” Afridi said.
He told the participants that the people had voted for a leader and “his player” was standing firm in the field. “We do not accept any policy that causes harm to the Pashtuns,” he said, adding that only Khan would rule in K-P. “We neither accept governor’s rule nor an emergency,” he added.
Afridi also rejected the possibility of another military operation in the province, saying a mindset imposed for 79 years was trying to impose another policy of operations on the people.
He said the provincial government had given the federal government an “open policy” that could bring peace to the province within 100 days if implemented. “For this, there must be an intention, but their intention is not peace. They intend to eliminate PTI,” he said.
Afridi said the province had been made a “laboratory” by the federal government for 22 years and that operations had been imposed on it.
The chief minister said there had been peace during Khan’s tenure because, in his view, his policy was correct. “After the regime change, terrorism was once again imposed on us,” he said. “They have started this fire and we will put it out.”

fridi urged people to come out, saying Pakistan’s future decisions would be made by its youth.

He reiterated that millions would take to the streets and said that by the time the march reached Swabi, the movement would spread across Pakistan.
Later, the long march caravan reached Khatm-e-Nabuwwat Chowk on the Bannu-Karak border.
Afridi reached Lakki Marwat by helicopter to lead the long march, and in a video shared by PTI on its X account, he was seen disembarking from a helicopter as party workers gathered around to welcome him.
پاکستان تحریک انصاف کا لانگ مارچ، وزیر اعلیٰ خیبرپختونخوا سہیل آفریدی لکی مروت پہنچ گئے، عوام کا شاندار استقبال #سر_بکف_میدان_میں pic.twitter.com/Tc4TDy2UeP
In another update on X, PTI stated that CM Afridi had arrived at the container, adding that the long march had begun in instalments. "Insha'Allah, this struggle against fascism and lawlessness will continue until the rule of the constitution and law is established in this country, and until the release of all political prisoners, including Chairman Imran Khan".
وزیراعلی سہیل آفریدی کنٹینر پر پہنچ گئے، لانگ مارچ بالقسط کا آغاز ،ان شاء اللہ فسطائیت و لاقانونیت کے خلاف یہ جدوجہد تب تک جاری رہے گی جب تک اس ملک میں آئین و قانون کی حکمرانی نہیں ہوتی، چیئرمین عمران خان سمیت تمام سیاسی قیدیوں کی رہائی نہیں ہوتی۔ #سر_بکف_میدان_میں pic.twitter.com/SCEgCu8b8R
According to an earlier statement issued by Afridi, the first phase of the long march would begin today, October 4, at 1pm from Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat, where caravans arriving from different districts would join.
"Caravans from Tank, Dera Ismail Khan, South Waziristan, North Waziristan, Bannu and Lakki Marwat will join the long march at Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat. The participants will stay overnight near Karak," he said.
CM Afridi added that on Monday, October 5, people from Karak would join the long march at noon and then the caravan would depart at 12:30pm and stay overnight near Kohat.
He said that on Tuesday, October 6, caravans from Kohat, Hangu, Kurram and Orakzai would join at noon. The caravan would depart from Kohat towards Peshawar and stay overnight near Matni in Peshawar.
"On Wednesday, October 7, the caravan will depart from Budh Bair in Peshawar at 12:30pm, where people from Khyber district will also join the long march. Caravans from other constituencies of Peshawar will join the march at the Kohat Road bridge and motorway toll plaza, while participants will stay overnight near the Charsadda interchange," he added.
CM Afridi said that on Thursday, October 8, the caravan would depart from the Charsadda interchange at 12:30pm, where caravans from Charsadda and Mohmand would join.
"People from across K-P would gather at Khairabad on October 8 and stay there overnight. The next phase of the long march will also be announced at Khairabad," he added.
انشأللہ آج گنڈی چوک لکی مروت سے ہم لانگ مارچ کا پہلا مرحلہ شروع کریں گے- آج بروز اتوار، 4 اکتوبر، دوپہر ایک بجے گنڈی چوک لکی مروت سے ٹانک، ڈیرہ اسماعیل خان، ساؤتھ وزیرستان، نارتھ وزیرستان، بنوں اور لکی مروت کے اضلاع سے تعلق رکھنے والے غیور پاکستانی لانگ مارچ کا حصہ بنیں گے۔ رات…
Earlier on Sunday, the party launched the first phase of its long march from Lakki Marwat to Swabi amid a government-opposition deadlock and mounting political tensions, with no plan for a march towards Islamabad announced so far.
The long march, initially scheduled for September 27, was postponed to October 4, but the standoff between the federal and provincial governments remains unresolved.
On Saturday, talks between the government and opposition failed to break the deadlock over the PTI’s long march, with both sides maintaining their positions and pressing competing demands.
The talks, chaired by National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq, followed an initial round on Friday in which the two sides exchanged their positions but failed to reach an agreement.
The government wanted the PTI to take the initiative by cancelling the march, while the opposition wanted the government to first facilitate a meeting with its jailed founder, according to sources familiar with the talks.

title: Iran warns regional states of    different and decisive    response to future attacks
description: IRGC warns US  Israel against further escalation
author_name: Reuters, Anadolu Agency, Web Desk, AFP
content:
IRGC warns US, Israel against further escalation
Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesman, Esmaeil Baghaei, on Sunday warned that any future use of regional countries’ territory to attack Tehran would provoke a "different and decisive" response, according to Press TV .
Speaking at a press conference in Tehran, Baghaei said regional countries must reconsider their actions, adding that Iran and the regional countries were “eternal neighbours.”
“If in the future we witness another aggression by America and the Zionist regime and their soil is used to attack Iran, certainly the response will be different,” Baghaei said.
According to Press TV, he called on neighbouring states not to allow parties that have shown no regard for regional security and prosperity to abuse their facilities and territory.
Iran warns US allies in region: Reusing soil for attacks will bring 'different' response https://t.co/6BhXTs7g4f
Baghaei also stated that the Strait of Hormuz was the main focus of Iran’s negotiations to end the war with the US.
"Securing the Strait of Hormuz, or restoring security to this waterway, requires specific steps from the American side,” Baghaei said, as cited by IRNA news agency.
"This issue has been discussed many times, including stopping interference with Iranian commercial shipping, ending sanctions, and other interventionist measures," he added.
Baghaei said the latest US proposal to Iran to end the war was almost identical to previous proposals, adding that Washington continued to focus on the nuclear file.
🔴 Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei says Tehran has clarified its positions via mediators to the US response to its 7-day plan 🔴 Iran says US proposal is similar to previous ones, focuses on nuclear file while Tehran wants to focus on Strait of Hormuz 🔴… pic.twitter.com/Idok8Daq9v
"We will conduct the necessary investigations regarding some details and will also reflect our supplementary points to the other party," he noted.
The spokesman said Iran’s top leadership had not discussed allowing International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors to return to the country.
IRGC warns US, Israel against further escalation
Iran's Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) Deputy Commander Brigadier General Ali Fadavi warned on Sunday that any further US and Israeli escalation against Iran would be disadvantageous, adding that US vessels were “fully exposed” to Iranian attacks and any source used to strike Tehran would be considered a legitimate target, Press TV reported.
Fadavi underlined that Iran had not attacked neighbouring Islamic countries, but only US bases and interests, and claimed the Strait of Hormuz had “unequivocally” remained under Iranian control in recent months.
According to Press TV , Fadavi also warned that Washington would be “foolish” to launch new aggression against Iran, while stating that regional states could stand up to the US if they chose to.
🔴 The Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) Deputy Commander Brigadier General Ali Fadavi: 🔺Any escalation by US, Israel will be disadvantageous to them 🔺US forced ships to use southern route through Strait of Hormuz pic.twitter.com/3WchACXq9m
Araghchi says Tehran serious about diplomatic path, rules out ‘military solution’ to end war
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran is “serious about finding diplomatic solutions, just as we are serious about defending ourselves,” Al Jazeera reported on Sunday.
Araghchi said there was no military solution to his country’s conflict with the United States, as talks aimed at ending the war appeared to have reached an impasse, AFP reported.
“If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force,” Araghchi said at a gathering of foreign ambassadors.
“There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions,” he added.
Iran to increase the range of its missiles, army spokesperson tells Fars
Iran will upgrade the range of its missiles following the war with the US, as American forces are now positioned as much as 1,000 km (621 miles) away from the Iranian coast, Army spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia told Fars news on Sunday.
"During this war, we concluded that we absolutely must increase the range of our missiles, and we have now moved in that direction," he said.
Iran says Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until Islamabad MoU conditions are met: Nournews
The Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until seven Iranian conditions set out in a June interim agreement with the US are met, Nournews reported Iran’s parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said on Sunday, a few days after Tehran received Washington's reply to its diplomatic proposal.
“The Americans, who say something different in the media, have recently put forward proposals through a mediator. But they must understand that the period of dragging out the process and dictating one-sided demands is over," Ghalibaf was quoted as saying.
"The position of the Islamic Republic of Iran is completely clear and firm, and the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened until our seven conditions, based on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, are met."
Iran ready to "both fight and negotiate," says parliament speaker
Iran’s parliament speaker said on Sunday that Tehran is "neither excited nor intimidated" by the US’ actions, stressing that Iran is prepared to "both fight and negotiate."
"We are present in the military battlefield with all our strength and we will face them with new surprises, and we use the tools of diplomacy to establish our superiority in the military field and impose the rights of the Iranian people," Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf told parliament, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency.
Iran army plans volunteer training programme for “national defence”
The Iranian army plans to begin training volunteers under a programme aimed at preparing citizens for “national defence”, Al Jazeera reported, citing the West Asia News Agency (WANA) .
The Iranian army plans to begin training volunteers under a programme that aims to prepare citizens for “national defence,” reports West Asia News Agency (WANA). 🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/HrCht5WdbF pic.twitter.com/szKJzCl5sX
Iran has also opened a military training centre for everyday citizens in Tehran as part of the programme.
Iran has opened a military training centre for everyday citizens in Tehran. 🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/ZeV953aMQq pic.twitter.com/ssN9HQwu9D
Hegseth says Trump has “options” if Iran “play games” over Hormuz
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said Washington’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz remains “ironclad”, warning that President Donald Trump has “options” if Iran continues to “play games” with the vital sea passage, Al Jazeera reported.
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Washington’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz remains “ironclad”, and that Trump has “options” if Iran continues to “play games” with the vital sea passage. 🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/CmkFLpfZqL pic.twitter.com/RICG5zXU6l
US carrier George HW Bush visits Thailand after Middle East deployment
The US aircraft carrier George HW Bush arrived off Thailand's ​resort island of Phuket on Sunday ‌with about 4,800 personnel aboard for a rest-and-recreation break after months of supporting US operations ​in the Middle East.
The Nimitz-class ​carrier had been operating in the ⁠Arabian Sea during the conflict with Iran, ​according to multiple media reports.
The carrier will ​anchor offshore, while crew members are expected to come ashore through Phuket Deep Sea Port ​and spend time on the popular ​southern resort island from October 4 to 9, local ‌media ⁠reported.
The visit follows a five-day port call by the US carrier Abraham Lincoln at Laem Chabang in eastern Thailand last ​month, with ​about ⁠5,000 sailors and Marines aboard.
A local mayor had estimated each ​US service member from the ​Lincoln ⁠could spend up to 3,000 baht ($89) per day during the visit.
Thailand is the United ⁠States' ​only treaty partner in ​mainland Southeast Asia.
Trump says Iran has 'virtually given up' any plans for nuclear weapons
US President Donald Trump suggested on Saturday that Iran has “virtually given up” any plans to develop nuclear weapons, one of his administration’s most frequently stated objectives in the war with Tehran, now in its eighth month.
Trump also claimed oil prices were currently decreasing, long elevated after Israel and the US launched strikes against Iran on Feb. 28.
“Oil is coming down. Oil is right now lower, and it's been lower than it was under the Biden administration, and they did nothing about the fact that Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon,” Trump told reporters as he departed the White House to attend a rally in the state of Ohio.
“By the way, Iran, as you know, has virtually given up any plans of a nuclear weapon,” he added.
Iran has long denied accusations by the US and Israel that it seeks to develop nuclear weapons, a position reiterated by President Masoud Pezeshkian during his visit last month to New York for the UN General Assembly.
Pezeshkian said Tehran is not seeking nuclear weapons because of a religious prohibition, and offered to dilute its enriched uranium stockpiles under international verification.
Iran, however, has maintained that it will not compromise on its peaceful civilian nuclear program or make structural concessions unless the US lifts economic sanctions

title: Andrew Garfield calls Tom Holland and Tobey Maguire friendship    brotherhood
