content:
Andrew Garfield says working with Tom Holland and Tobey Maguire on 'Spider-Man: No Way Home' created 'brotherhood'
Andrew Garfield has described his relationship with fellow Spider-Man actors Tom Holland and Tobey Maguire as a “brotherhood” following their shared appearance in Spider-Man: No Way Home.
Garfield discussed his friendship with Holland and Maguire during the September 29 episode of Good Hang with Amy Poehler, five years after the three actors appeared together as different versions of Spider-Man in the 2021 Marvel film.
“It's a brotherhood now, which is really, really great,” Garfield said. “Doing [the film] where we're all together really cemented some kind of weird brotherhood that was just beautiful.”
Garfield added that he had known Maguire “a little bit before” and described him as his “north star” because Maguire originated the film version of Spider-Man.
“And I loved what Tom's done,” Garfield continued. “And I think that was very healing for all of us to do that together and to feel less alone in that very, very weird singular experience to be a part of this character's legacy that maybe is arguably one of if not the most popular fictional character in the history of like modern fiction.”
Garfield played Peter Parker in The Amazing Spider-Man and its 2014 sequel before returning to the character in No Way Home . Maguire portrayed Spider-Man in Sam Raimi’s trilogy, which began in the early 2000s.
Holland has played Peter Parker across multiple films, including the most recent entry, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which was released in July.

title: Sri Lanka s players arrive in Pakistan ahead of T20I series
description: Kusal Mendis  Dasun Shanaka among eight players to reach Islamabad
content:
Kusal Mendis, Dasun Shanaka among eight players to reach Islamabad
Sri Lanka's first contingent arrived in Islamabad on Sunday ahead of a three-match Twenty20 International Series against Pakistan, with the visitors set to complete their preparations for the opening game on Friday.
The 13-member group included eight players from Sri Lanka's T20 squad and five team management officials. The T20 captain Kusal Mendis, former captain Dasun Shanaka, spinner Maheesh Theekshana and fast bowler Eshan Malinga were among the players who arrived, along with Kamindu Mendis, Lahiru Udara, Chamindu Wickramasinghe and Dunith Wellalage.
Sri Lanka's head coach, two players and two other officials are due to arrive on Monday, while the remaining five members of the T20 squad are expected to reach Islamabad on Tuesday.
The three-match T20 series will be played entirely at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium, with the first match on October 9, the second on October 11 and the third on October 13.
The T20 series is the first part of Sri Lanka's multi-format tour of Pakistan. Pakistan, Sri Lanka and England will then compete in a three-nation ODI series, with Pakistan facing Sri Lanka on October 18 in Rawalpindi, Pakistan playing England on October 20 in Rawalpindi, Sri Lanka meeting England on October 22 in Rawalpindi, Pakistan taking on England on October 25 in Lahore, Pakistan playing Sri Lanka on October 27 in Lahore and Sri Lanka facing England on October 29 in Lahore. The tri-series final is scheduled for October 31 in Lahore.
Sri Lanka will then play a three-day match in Islamabad from November 4 to 6 before facing Pakistan in a two-Test series. The first Test is scheduled for November 9-13 in Rawalpindi and the second for November 17-21 in Lahore. The Test series forms part of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27.
T20 squad: Kusal Mendis (captain), Kamil Mishara, Sineth Jayawardena, Lahiru Udara, Sahan Arachchige, Kamindu Mendis, Dasun Shanaka, Chamindu Wickramasinghe, Dunith Wellalage, Maheesh Theekshana, Vijayakanth Viyaskanth, Dushmantha Chameera, Binura Fernando, Nuwan Thushara, Eshan Malinga.

'The Bachelor' reportedly contacts internet-famous doctor Mike Varshavski as producers seek a new lead for season 30
The Bachelor is reportedly considering internet-famous doctor Mike Varshavski as a potential lead for its upcoming 30th season as the dating reality show looks to return to its earlier format.
Varshavski, known online as Dr. Mike, has reportedly been contacted by producers, according to a source cited by Page Six. The 36-year-old family medicine physician became widely known online for sharing health-related content and was named People’s “Sexiest Doctor Alive” in 2015.
Dr. Mike has built a significant social media following, with about 15.1 million YouTube subscribers and 6 million Instagram followers. His online popularity could make him a recognisable choice for The Bachelor , which is reportedly seeking a lead with an established career and genuine interest in finding a relationship.
The show is preparing for its 30th season, which is expected to premiere in 2027. Producers are reportedly looking for someone “successful” and “charming” who is seriously interested in finding love rather than using the series primarily to build an influencer career.
The reported casting search comes as The Bachelor attempts to revive its audience after years of declining ratings. The franchise has also faced criticism over contestants and leads allegedly joining for increased visibility and career opportunities.
Grant Ellis, the franchise’s most recent Bachelor, was accused by a contestant of “clout chasing”, although such claims were disputed.
The franchise first premiered in 2002 and has since expanded to include The Bachelorette , Bachelor in Paradise and The Golden Bachelor .
A new casting team was reportedly brought in earlier this year as producers sought a fresh direction for the long-running series. Representatives for The Bachelor did not comment on the reported interest in Dr. Mike.

title: Sass Jordan  Canadian rock star and Canadian Idol judge  dies at 63
description: Sass Jordan  the Canadian rock singer and longtime Canadian Idol judge  has died at 63 after four decades in music
content:
Sass Jordan, the Canadian rock singer and longtime Canadian Idol judge, has died at 63 after four decades in music
Sass Jordan, the Canadian rock singer and longtime Canadian Idol judge, has died at 63. The musician died on Thursday, October 2, surrounded by her family.
Jordan’s family announced her death on social media, saying she had “peacefully crossed over to the other side” while surrounded by loved ones. They described her as “an inimitable force of nature” and “an irreplaceable being of light and joy”.
Born in England, Jordan moved to Montreal with her family when she was 3. She began playing guitar as a teenager and was performing with bands in Montreal clubs by the age of 16.
Jordan launched her recording career as a co-lead vocalist on Bündock’s album Mauve before releasing her solo debut, Tell Somebody . The album’s title track reached No. 11 in Canada, while Jordan won the Juno Award for Most Promising Female Vocalist. She later received three additional Juno nominations for Best Female Vocalist.
Over a career spanning more than four decades, Jordan became known for her blues-rock vocals and performed alongside major acts including Aerosmith, The Rolling Stones, AC/DC and Van Halen.
She became a household name in Canada after joining Canadian Idol as a judge in 2003. Jordan remained on the panel throughout all six seasons of the singing competition.
Three months before her death, Jordan cancelled her remaining 2026 performances because of what her team described as a serious medical condition. Her final performance took place at Peterborough Musicfest in July.
Jordan is survived by her husband, Derek Sharp, daughter Stella Jordan-Sharp, stepdaughter Brianne Sharp and brother Daniel Jordan. Her family has asked for privacy while thanking fans for their support.

description: Glastonbury 2027 tickets sold out in 42 minutes  with festival returning to Worthy Farm from June 23 to 27
content:
Glastonbury 2027 tickets sold out in 42 minutes, with festival returning to Worthy Farm from June 23 to 27
Tickets for Glastonbury Festival 2027 sold out in 42 minutes after thousands of people joined the online queue for the event’s return to Worthy Farm in Somerset.
Tickets went on sale at 09:00 BST on Sunday, with the festival scheduled to take place from June 23 to 27 2027 following a fallow year.
Organisers confirmed shortly after 09:40 that tickets had sold out and notified people who remained in the queue.
Glastonbury tickets cost £408 for 2027, including a £5 booking fee, making them the festival’s highest-priced tickets to date. The price represents a £29.50 increase from the 2025 event.
“Thank you to everyone who bought one and we're sorry to those of you who missed out on a morning where demand greatly exceeded supply,” organisers said in an Instagram post.
“There will be a resale of any cancelled or returned tickets in Spring 2027.”
The first ticket sale, covering coach packages, took place on Thursday and sold out in less than 30 minutes.
Headliners for the 2027 festival have not yet been announced. Organiser Emily Eavis previously said the team was “very excited” and that things were “coming together really well”.
Tickets have risen from £185 in 2010 to £408 for the 2027 festival, with the largest increases coming after the pandemic.
Any tickets from Sunday’s sale that are not fully paid for by the early April 2027 deadline will return to the official resale pool. The exact resale date has not been announced.

title: Ethan Hawke recalls bad mouthing  Hamlet  director while unknowingly mic   d up
description: I was very mad at Michael  Almereyda  that day and I was just spitting venom about this guy     Hawke recalled
content:
“I was very mad at Michael [Almereyda] that day and I was just spitting venom about this guy,” Hawke recalled
Ethan Hawke has recalled an awkward moment on the set of Hamlet when he criticised director Michael Almereyda, only to realise that his microphone was still live and the filmmaker had heard everything.
Hawke shared the story on September 28 while moderating a book talk for his former Hamlet co-star Kyle MacLachlan, whose new memoir Fictional Selves was the focus of their conversation. The actors reflected on making the 2000 Shakespeare adaptation, which starred Hawke as Hamlet and MacLachlan as Claudius.
Hawke said the incident happened while they were filming a scene in a car and had to wait for a long period. He admitted that he was particularly angry with Almereyda that day, despite later working with the director several times and considering him a friend.
“I was very mad at Michael [Almereyda] that day and I was just spitting venom about this guy,” Hawke recalled, explaining that he was complaining about the director without realising the microphone was still picking up his comments.
Hawke eventually noticed MacLachlan making a discreet gesture towards Almereyda. When he looked outside, he saw the director wearing headphones and realised what had happened. MacLachlan then explained that the actors had been mic’d up the entire time, meaning Almereyda had heard Hawke’s complaints.
Despite the uncomfortable situation, Hawke said Almereyda “took it in stride”. The incident did not damage their relationship, with Hawke, MacLachlan and Almereyda later reuniting for the 2020 film Tesla .
Looking back on Hamlet , Hawke also described the production fondly, calling it an “incredibly low-budget movie” made by a group of people who were passionate about their work. The film also featured Julia Stiles, Bill Murray, Diane Venora, Liev Schreiber, Sam Shepard and Steve Zahn.
MacLachlan’s memoir Fictional Selves is now available, with the actor reflecting on his career and experiences working on projects including Hamlet .

title: Olivia Rodrigo could match Billie Eilish record with three Album of the Year nominations
description: Olivia Rodrigo could earn her third consecutive Album of the Year nomination at 2027 Grammy Awards
content:
Olivia Rodrigo could earn her third consecutive Album of the Year nomination at 2027 Grammy Awards
Olivia Rodrigo could become the latest woman to have each of her first three studio albums nominated for Grammy Album of the Year if You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love earns a nomination at the 2027 ceremony.
Rodrigo has already received Album of the Year nominations for both of her previous albums. Sour competed for the award at the 2022 Grammys, where it lost to Jon Batiste’s We Are.
Rodrigo nevertheless won three awards that night, including Best New Artist, Best Pop Vocal Album and Best Pop Solo Performance for “Drivers License”.
Her second album, Guts, returned her to the Album of the Year field at the 2024 ceremony, where Taylor Swift’s Midnights won the award.
You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love could extend Rodrigo’s nomination record. The album debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with the largest opening of her career. The 2027 Grammy nominations are due to be announced next month.
If Rodrigo is nominated, she would join a small group of artists whose first three studio albums have all competed for Album of the Year.
Ye, formerly known as Kanye West, achieved the feat with The College Dropout, Late Registration and Graduation, although he did not win the category with any of the three albums.
Billie Eilish also achieved the three-album run with When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?, Happier Than Ever and Hit Me Hard and Soft. Eilish won with her debut album in 2020 and is the only woman to have achieved the run when considering albums she led as an artist.
Lady Gaga's record is less straightforward because The Fame Monster, which followed The Fame, is generally classified as an EP in the United States.
Her first three full-length studio albums were therefore The Fame, Born This Way and Artpop, with Artpop missing out on an Album of the Year nomination.
If nominated and ultimately successful, Rodrigo could become the first artist in this group to win Album of the Year with her third studio album.

Wolf said he was spending time with an "amazing person" and described their connection as "super real".
"I'm happy in this chapter of my life, and I hope it doesn't change anytime soon," Wolf said.

title: Over 800 Palestinian teachers killed by Israel since Gaza war  education ministry
description: Over 3 300 educators injured and more than 170 detained  ministry says ahead of World Teachers    Day
content:
Over 3,300 educators injured and more than 170 detained, ministry says ahead of World Teachers’ Day
Israel has killed more than 800 Palestinian teachers and injured over 3,300 others since the start of its war on the Gaza Strip in October 2023, the Palestinian Education Ministry said Sunday.
In a statement ahead of World Teachers’ Day, observed annually on October 5, the ministry said educators across the occupied Palestinian territories are fighting “a real battle for survival” to protect the right to education amid systematic targeting.
The education sector in Gaza and the West Bank has suffered “comprehensive genocide” since the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, the ministry said.
The ministry said more than 170 teachers remain detained “in harsh conditions.”
It said movement restrictions and harassment at hundreds of checkpoints have compounded educators’ daily suffering, particularly in Masafer Yatta, south of Hebron, the village of al-Mughayyir in the central West Bank, the Jordan Valley and areas classified as Area C.
Under the 1995 Oslo II agreement, intended as an interim arrangement, the West Bank was divided into Areas A, B and C.
Area A is under Palestinian civil and security control, while Area B is under Palestinian civil administration and Israeli security control. Area C, which accounts for about 60% of the West Bank, remains under full Israeli control.
The ministry said abuses against Palestinian teachers have been accompanied by severe financial hardship, undermining their material and psychological stability as Israel withholds Palestinian tax revenues.
Read More: Gaza health officials say Israeli strike kills 5
Known as clearance revenues, the funds are taxes collected by Israel on behalf of the Palestinian Authority on imported goods and transferred under the 1994 Paris Protocol.
Israel began deducting sums from these revenues in 2019 and subsequently halted transfers, worsening the Palestinian Authority’s financial crisis and its ability to pay public employees’ salaries in full.
Clearance revenues account for approximately 56% of total Palestinian public revenues, making their withholding a major obstacle to paying salaries, providing public services and meeting government obligations.
The ministry urged the international community, the UN, and education and human rights organizations to take urgent action to curb violations and provide international protection for students and education personnel.
It also called on unions worldwide to press for the release of detained teachers and withheld financial entitlements to ensure educators can live with dignity.

content:
'Digger' is expected to finish its opening weekend with around $8 million
Tom Cruise’s Digger has suffered a major box office disappointment, opening to around $8 million domestically as Amazon MGM’s Verity claimed the No. 1 spot with a $32 million debut.
Directed by Alejandro G. Iñárritu, Digger opened in 3,321 cinemas and earned $3.4 million on Friday, including previews. The film is expected to finish its opening weekend with around $8 million, making it one of the weakest domestic debuts of Cruise’s career.
Digger reportedly carries a production budget of between $160 million and $180 million, before marketing costs. The film stars Cruise as Digger Rockwell, a powerful oil tycoon facing an ecological disaster, and also features Mark Ruffalo, Michael Fassbender and Jesse Plemons.
The disappointing result comes despite Cruise remaining one of Hollywood’s biggest theatrical stars. The opening is particularly notable because Digger is Cruise’s first collaboration with Oscar-winning filmmaker Iñárritu, whose previous films include Birdman and The Revenant .
Meanwhile, Verity dominated the weekend. The Amazon MGM thriller, adapted from Colleen Hoover’s bestselling novel, earned an estimated $32 million in its opening weekend from 3,510 locations. The film stars Dakota Johnson as Lowen Ashleigh, a writer hired to complete a successful book series after its author, played by Anne Hathaway, becomes incapacitated.
Verity ’s debut gives it a strong start against its reported $40 million production budget, while Digger faces a far steeper challenge because of its much larger costs. The contrasting performances make the weekend a particularly significant one for both films, with Verity emerging as the clear box office winner and Digger facing a major commercial setback.

title: John Steinbeck   s  East of Eden  returns to top of book charts after Netflix adaptation
description: The classic 1952 novel has seen renewed interest as viewers turn to the original source material behind the new series
content:
The classic 1952 novel has seen renewed interest as viewers turn to the original source material behind the new series
John Steinbeck’s East of Eden has returned to the top of the book charts following the release of Netflix’s new limited series adaptation starring Florence Pugh.
The classic 1952 novel has seen renewed interest as viewers turn to the original source material behind the new seven-episode series. Variety reports that East of Eden has become a No. 1 bestseller following the Netflix adaptation’s release.
Steinbeck’s novel is a multigenerational story set in California’s Salinas Valley and follows the intertwined lives of the Trask and Hamilton families. The book explores themes including family, free will, morality and the struggle between good and evil.
Netflix’s adaptation was created by Zoe Kazan, with Jeb Stuart serving as co-showrunner. Florence Pugh stars as Cathy Ames, while Christopher Abbott plays Adam Trask and Mike Faist portrays Charles Trask. Hoon Lee also stars as Lee, the Chinese American cook whose role has been expanded in the series.
The new adaptation covers the story across seven episodes, allowing it to explore considerably more of Steinbeck’s novel than the previous 1955 film version. The series is now streaming on Netflix, giving audiences the opportunity to watch the adaptation before or after reading the original novel.
The renewed popularity of East of Eden highlights the continued impact of classic literature when it is brought to a new generation through major screen adaptations. With the Netflix series drawing attention to Steinbeck’s story, readers are once again turning to the novel that inspired it.

title: DR Congo sentences 27 soldiers to death for  cowardice
description: Trial of at least 112 soldiers from the 21st Simba Battalion began on Sept  15 at Uvira military court
content:
Trial of at least 112 soldiers from the 21st Simba Battalion began on Sept. 15 at Uvira military court
A military court in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo sentenced 27 Congolese soldiers to death for "cowardice," according to a court document.
The soldiers were convicted of withdrawing from the front line during fighting against AFC/M23 rebels.
The trial of at least 112 soldiers from the 21st Simba Battalion began September 15 at the military court in Uvira, South Kivu province.
The soldiers were accused of violating orders and fleeing battles against the rebels in eastern Congo in August.
The court said 54 soldiers were sentenced Friday to five years in prison after being found guilty of violating instructions, while 10 others received six-month sentences.
At least 21 soldiers, including five women, were acquitted due to insufficient evidence.
Read More: Ebola cases top 8,000 in DR Congo amid contact-tracing gaps
The soldiers had been deployed to secure strategic areas overlooking Uvira, according to the prosecution.
In May, a military court in Congo sentenced 58 Congolese soldiers to three years in prison for "violating instructions" when they withdrew from the front line during clashes with AFC/M23 rebels.
The latest trial came amid continued clashes between the AFC/M23 rebel group and government forces in Uvira territory, according to local sources.
The sides have traded accusations of ceasefire violations.
The M23 rebels have been at the center of the conflict in eastern Congo.
The group controls significant territory in eastern Congo, including the provincial capitals of Goma and Bukavu, which it seized in early 2025.
Congo, the UN and Western nations accuse neighboring Rwanda of supporting the M23 rebel group. Kigali denies the accusation.

title: Marjoe Gortner  Oscar winning documentary subject and actor  dies at 82
description: Marjoe Gortner  the former child preacher and actor known for the Oscar winning documentary Marjoe  has died at 82
content:
Marjoe Gortner, the former child preacher and actor known for the Oscar-winning documentary Marjoe, has died at 82
Marjoe Gortner, the former child preacher whose life was chronicled in the Oscar-winning documentary Marjoe , has died at 82.
Gortner died Friday in Santa Fe, New Mexico, his wife, Susan Magestro, confirmed. A memorial notice said he had been living with congestive heart failure for several years.
Born in Long Beach, California, Gortner was raised in an evangelical family and was pushed into preaching from an early age. His parents promoted him as a child evangelist, and he reportedly performed a marriage ceremony at just 4 years old.
His family travelled across the United States as he preached and collected donations. Gortner later said he became disillusioned with the evangelical movement in his 20s and pursued an acting career in New York.
In 1971, filmmakers Howard Smith and Sarah Kernochan followed Gortner during what he described as his final revival tour. The footage became Marjoe , which won the Academy Award for best documentary feature. The film attracted attention at the time and was later difficult to find until Kernochan recovered the rights.
Gortner subsequently pursued acting, appearing in films and television shows throughout the 1970s and 1980s. His notable film credits included Earthquake , Viva Knievel! , Starcrash and Wild Bill .
On television, he appeared in series including Kojak , Police Story , Airwolf , T.J. Hooker , The A-Team and Falcon Crest .
Actor Ian Ziering also remembered Gortner for his charitable work, saying he helped raise millions of dollars through celebrity sporting events and fundraising initiatives.
Gortner is survived by Magestro, his fifth wife.

Bryan's second show at the stadium drew 73,538 fans breaking Ed Sheeran's record of 71,723 set in 2023
Zach Bryan made headlines during both of his sold-out concerts at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, wearing a “Free Palestine” shirt before breaking the venue’s attendance record on the second night.
Bryan performed his first concert at the stadium on Friday, October 2, where he wore a black T-shirt featuring the words “Free Palestine” alongside “An Appeal to Heaven” and a pine tree design. Members of his backing band also wore clothing supporting Palestine, including drummer Nate Head, whose jersey featured the name of Hind Rajab, the five-year-old Palestinian girl killed in Gaza in January 2024.
The performance came weeks after rapper Macklemore was removed from the remaining dates of Ed Sheeran’s tour following a dispute over his pro-Palestinian messaging. Robert Kraft, the owner of Gillette Stadium, had criticised Macklemore’s actions and said they were deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community. Macklemore responded by saying that antisemitism is real but that criticism of Israel and support for Palestine should not be conflated with hatred of Jewish people.
Bryan returned to Gillette Stadium for his second concert on Saturday, October 3. The second show drew 73,538 fans, setting a new attendance record for the venue. The previous record of 71,723 had been set by Sheeran in 2023. Bryan also wore the “Free Palestine” shirt again during the second concert.
The two concerts were part of Bryan’s With Heaven on Tour , which is scheduled to conclude on October 10 at Jordan-Hare Stadium in Auburn, Alabama. The Gillette Stadium shows marked the final two concerts of his tour before its closing performance.
The shows also followed Macklemore’s announcement of his own Free Palestine tour, with proceeds set to support charities aiding Palestinians. Macklemore had previously pledged $1 million from his earnings from Sheeran’s tour to pro-Palestinian charities and asked Kraft to match the donation. "I felt like I needed my time. I wanted to completely heal and just work on myself. I wasn't ready to open up. I really wasn't even thinking about it. The universe works in your favour when you just allow it to."

title: Janhvi Kapoor speaks out against AI deepfake  demands respect for women s consent
description: Indian actor condemns non consensual manipulation of her  Devara  footage and warns of the growing threat of AI abuse
content:
Indian actor condemns non-consensual manipulation of her 'Devara' footage and warns of the growing threat of AI abuse
Indian actor Janhvi Kapoor has condemned an AI-generated deepfake that manipulated footage from her Devara: Part 1 song Chuttamalle , calling the non-consensual use of her image a “deeply violating” act and warning that the issue reflects a broader reality faced by women.
The altered video, which circulated widely online, digitally manipulated footage featuring Kapoor from the 2024 film and presented her in a sexually explicit manner that was not part of the original production. The incident has triggered strong reactions across the Indian film industry, while renewing concerns about the misuse of artificial intelligence to target women.
Breaking her silence on the controversy on Instagram, Kapoor said the issue extends well beyond the particular video involving her. She argued that the misuse of technology reflects a broader problem surrounding the way women’s bodies, choices and boundaries are treated.
"The criminal misuse of technology to objectify women and circulating fictionalised content without consent is deeply violating, bordering on sexual assault. Almost every woman in my industry has faced some version of this. And women everywhere are increasingly being subjected to it," she wrote.
According to Kapoor, consent should not be viewed as complicated or open to interpretation. A woman’s decisions about her body, appearance and personal boundaries remain hers alone, regardless of what she wears or what choices she may have made previously.
She further argued that the growing threat posed by AI-generated abuse comes on top of the physical and social pressures women already face. In her view, technology has created another avenue through which women can be subjected to harassment and violations of their privacy.
"It is about the larger reality of being a woman. The gaze, the judgement, the constant negotiation for safety and the feelings that our boundaries somehow remain open to interpretation. That threat has now expanded into the digital sphere," she said.
Kapoor also called for a wider change in social attitudes, saying responsibility should not rest solely on women or their families to protect themselves from harassment. Instead, she said society must challenge the attitudes that lead people to believe they are entitled to cross another person’s boundaries.
The actor thanked her Devara co-star Jr NTR for speaking out against the manipulated video. NTR had earlier condemned the clip and said he would pursue legal action against those responsible for creating and circulating it.
The controversy has once again highlighted the growing challenges posed by AI deepfakes, particularly when the technology is used to fabricate intimate or degrading material involving people without their knowledge or consent.
Kapoor ended by emphasising the importance of recognising women’s right to control their own images, bodies and boundaries.
"I hope everything unfolding around us right now forces those who participate in any form of harassment to introspect. Is it really too much for a woman to ask to simply be treated and seen as a human being? Her body, her image, her boundaries, her choice".
Her message ultimately centred on a basic principle: women should be treated as people with the right to control their own images, bodies and boundaries.

Jaime King and Austin Sosa have officially divorced less than two years after secretly marrying in April 2025
Jaime King and Austin Sosa have officially divorced less than two years after secretly getting married, according to court documents.
A Los Angeles judge approved the dissolution of their marriage on Friday, restoring both King and Sosa to single status. The former couple did not have any children together.

King previously said she was caught off guard by the divorce filing. The Sin City actress told Page Six that she had been with Sosa the night before the filing became public and believed they were working through their marital difficulties.
The couple had kept their marriage private. Page Six previously reported that King and Sosa secretly married on April 23, 2025, months before King publicly announced their engagement in July that year.
At the time, King’s representative said the actress was entering a “joyful new chapter” with Sosa and was happy about his relationship with her children.

content:
The lawsuit alleges Cornell failed to adequately punish some of the accused students and seven fraternity members
Cornell University will examine the role of fraternities and sororities on campus following an outcry over the school's handling of a student's rape allegations, the Ivy League school's president ​said on Saturday.
A civil lawsuit filed last month by the woman, who alleges ‌she was drugged and raped in 2024 by several members of the Chi Phi fraternity, has sparked outrage and soul-searching at Cornell over its campus culture at the school in Ithaca, New York.
In a video message, Cornell ​University President Michael Kotlikoff said the school would take steps to prevent a ​similar situation in the future. That includes "a serious look at the role of ⁠fraternities and sororities in campus life," Kotlikoff said.
"At their best, these organizations can provide ​students with friendship, belonging, mentorship and a powerful sense of community," he said. "But being part of ​a group can never diminish individual responsibility."
The university will seek input, he said, from students, alumni and others on how to "preserve what is valuable about Greek life while strengthening individual accountability, transparency and a culture in ​which every member understands their responsibility to protect the safety and well-being of others."
The lawsuit ​against Cornell, seven fraternity members and others, alleges that the school failed to adequately punish some of ‌the accused ⁠students.
The accused men have denied all wrongdoing, the New York Times reported.

Read More: Olivia Rodrigo slams Cornell University over handling of fraternity assault case, shows solidarity for victim
Cornell has defended its handling of the matter, saying it launched a comprehensive investigation and barred the Chi Phi fraternity from campus. The school said it imposed a range of disciplinary measures, including expulsions.
But "we must ​do better," Kotlikoff said. "We ​don’t have all the ⁠answers, but we are committed to investigating and finding the answers our community deserves."
He vowed that university officials would "be more transparent" about their ​actions related to the 2024 incident, but he did not detail ​specific initiatives that ⁠the university would take.
"In the coming weeks, we will create additional opportunities for members of our community to ask questions and hear directly from university leadership," he said.
The case has reignited scrutiny ⁠of ​how law enforcement and universities handle sexual assault complaints, with ​students questioning whether processes are enough to protect them. It has also drawn the attention of New York state ​officials, who have appointed a special prosecutor to investigate.

Saudi Arabia is set to cancel next year’s Joy Awards, the star-studded entertainment ceremony held annually in Riyadh, as financial pressures lead to cuts in culture and entertainment spending, according to two people familiar with the matter.
The event, which takes place each January, has become a major fixture on Riyadh’s events calendar, attracting international performers including Katy Perry and Robbie Williams this year. The awards recognise achievements across music, entertainment and sport.
The reported cancellation comes as Saudi Arabia reassesses spending priorities amid financial strain and the wider impact of the Iran war. Industry sources told Reuters that budget cuts had already begun before the conflict, putting pressure on the kingdom’s plans to establish itself as a major destination for tourism and international events under its Vision 2030 programme.
The General Entertainment Authority, which organises the Joy Awards alongside Saudi media conglomerate MBC Group, did not respond to Reuters’ request for comment. MBC Group and the Saudi government’s media office also did not respond.
The Joy Awards are the latest major entertainment event to face cancellation or postponement in Saudi Arabia. The Red Sea Film Festival was postponed until 2027 last month, while organisers also cancelled Soundstorm, the large desert music festival scheduled for December. Soundstorm, which attracted hundreds of thousands of attendees and featured Cardi B as a headliner last year, is expected to return in 2027.
The Red Sea Film Festival was launched in 2021 as part of Saudi Arabia’s efforts to develop its film industry after the kingdom ended its decades-long ban on cinemas. Industry sources said uncertainty surrounding the Iran war had also made it more difficult to secure international stars for events.
The reported changes come alongside wider reductions or delays affecting several major Saudi projects. These include the planned development of The Line at NEOM and a $50 billion cube-shaped structure in Riyadh. Two people familiar with the matter also told Reuters that plans for the NEOM Stadium, one of the projects linked to the 2034 FIFA World Cup, are being quietly shelved.
Mazen Hayek, a Dubai-based media consultant, said the war and its wider economic effects were prompting Gulf states to reconsider their spending priorities. He noted that some major events had been designed not only as entertainment ventures but also as tools for international visibility and influence.
Not all major events are facing cuts. The Future Investment Initiative, a flagship event aimed at driving investment into Saudi Arabia, is still scheduled to take place later this month, according to organisers.
For now, the Joy Awards cancellation has not been officially announced by the organisers. If confirmed, it would mark a significant pause for one of Saudi Arabia’s most prominent entertainment events as the kingdom reassesses spending across its expanding cultural and events sector.

title: Finnish town braces for change from Google data centres
description: Google plans a    13bn investment in Finland  including data centres  its biggest ever European investment
content:
Google plans a €13bn investment in Finland, including data centres, its biggest-ever European investment
In the northern Finnish town of Muhos, 36-year-old farmer Joni Pitkanen is preparing for life with a new neighbour -- just kilometers away, tech giant Google is planning to build new data centres.
The planned data centres are part of an announced 13-billion-euro ($15-billion) investment in Finland over the next two years -- the US tech giant's single biggest investment in Europe.
A few kilometers down the gravel road that passes by Pitkanen's farm, the forest has already been cut down on land acquired by Google, with excavators now clearing the ground and rumbling trucks shuttling back and forth to the construction area located next to major power lines.
"The project is so massive that it's basically hard to really grasp, even though we're right here on the sidelines," Pitkanen said, as a few cows dozed in a meadow in front of the barn.
Google's expansion plans include the Finnish municipalities of Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala as well as Hamina, where it already operates a data centre.
The massive investment prompted US President Donald Trump to urge Google to rethink its plans in a message on his Truth Social network.
Pitkanen said he was so far "fairly positive" about the project, as it will bring "large-scale business activity" and "life" to the rural municipality with a population of only around 8,800 people.
"But of course we are concerned about... how we can prepare for the energy consumption," he added.
In his office in the small village centre, Muhos mayor Kimmo Hinno told AFP that Google's "massive investment" kept him busy these days as "no industry of this type" existed here at present.
"This will completely change the situation for the entire municipality and the Oulu region," he said, adding that he expected "thousands of workers" of different nationalities during the construction period -- who will need both housing and other services.
Read More: OpenAI safety employee quits, says ‘time for trial and error is over’
Outside a grocery store, 60-year-old nurse Aila Heilima said she hoped the investment would "motivate young people to stay" in Muhos for work, instead of moving to bigger towns in search of job opportunities.
But Google's plans have already sparked controversy.
The Finnish Supervisory Agency (LVV) is currently investigating whether company Tuike Finland, which represents Google, had cleared more than 300 hectares of forest in Muhos without a mandatory environmental impact assessment.
"In our view, operations at this construction site should be suspended until it is clarified whether the project is in compliance with the law," Hanna Halmeenpaa, chair of the board of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation, who filed the request with the agency, told AFP at the edge of the deforested area.
"From the satellite images, we've seen that nature sites which should be preserved have also been logged," she added, explaining that the size of the clear-cut area was comparable to 420 football fields.
Google, meanwhile, told AFP in an email that "tree felling activities have been taking place in compliance with Forestry Act requirements" and they "were awaiting further guidance from LVV on this matter."
"We have conducted extensive nature surveys covering the entire area as part of the zoning and Environmental Impact Assessment processes, to ensure high-value nature zones within the sites have been protected during forestry works," said Sondre Ronander, communications manager for Google in Finland.
Finland has seen a spike in data centre investments, with its cool climate and relatively stable and cheap electricity that is mostly produced without fossil fuels thanks to nuclear plants as well as extensive wind and hydro power.
Prime Minister Petteri Orpo's right-wing government has prioritised attracting data centre investments to the Nordic country, which is grappling with record-high unemployment and sluggish economic growth.
But, as dozens of the energy guzzling centres are now under construction and many more planned by companies including Microsoft and TikTok, uncertainty around energy prices, grid capacity and environmental effects have sparked a public debate in Finland.
A citizen's initiative demanding stricter regulation regarding data centre energy use and consequences for the environment gathered more than 50,000 signatures in just three days after it opened, meaning it will have to be reviewed.

title: Alcaraz through to Japan Open semis
description: Spaniard reaches the last four after Shapovalov retires at 7 6  7 3   2 1
content:
Spaniard reaches the last four after Shapovalov retires at 7-6 (7/3), 2-1
Carlos Alcaraz qualified for the semi-finals of the Japan Open on Sunday after an ailing Denis Shapovalov retired to hand the world number three a 7-6 (7/3), 2-1 victory.
His Canadian opponent was forced to withdraw after suffering an injury to his upper right thigh in the first game of the second set.
Defending champion Alcaraz will play fellow Spaniard Jaume Munar for a place in the final after the world number 64 ended the impressive run of 86th-ranked Kyrian Jacquet of France.
The match was hard-fought until Shapovalov's retirement, with Alcaraz troubled by the variety of his game as the world number 46 mixed deep shots with drop shots, and power with spin.
Alcaraz, who saved four set points against Matteo Arnaldi on Saturday, salvaged another here at 5-4 down and went on to seal the tie-break with a passing shot before Shapovalov's injury.
The Australian Open champion is playing only his third event since returning from a months-long wrist injury, having reached the quarter-finals of the US Open last month.
Later on Sunday, Valentin Vacherot upset France's Arthur Fils 7-5, 4-6, 6-4 to set up a semi-final against Jiri Lehecka.
Fils seemed to be making short work of the big-serving world number 18 when he earned two set points at 5-3.
But he then caved in, losing the next four games to hand Vacherot the opener on a superb down-the-line return.
Fils forced a deciding set after an intense battle, pumping his fist and rallying the crowd, but eventually succumbed in a tight two-hour, 20-minute match.
Lehecka, the Czech world number 23, breezed into the semi-finals with a 6-1, 6-1 demolition of Paraguay's Adolfo Daniel Vallejo, wrapping up the win in under an hour.

title: Meryl Streep   s  Narnia  casting sparks backlash over Greta Gerwig   s Aslan
description: Narnia  The Magician   s Nephew  is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on February 12  2027
content:
'Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew' is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on February 12, 2027
Greta Gerwig’s upcoming The Chronicles of Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew is facing controversy over the casting of Meryl Streep as the voice of Aslan, with some conservative Christian commentators objecting to a woman voicing the character.
Aslan is widely regarded as a representation of Jesus Christ in C.S. Lewis’ The Chronicles of Narnia books. The character is depicted as male in the novels, leading some critics to argue that Streep’s casting represents a significant departure from Lewis’ Christian symbolism.
The casting does not necessarily mean that Gerwig’s version of Aslan will be portrayed as female. However, the decision has already prompted criticism online, particularly from conservative Christian commentators who have accused the production of changing or undermining the character’s religious significance.
Seth Udinsky of the Christian Post argued that the casting was part of an attempt to undermine Christian symbols, while other critics have pointed to promotional imagery showing Aslan with rainbow-tinted whiskers.
Gerwig has not directly addressed the gender controversy. Instead, the director has explained that Streep was chosen because she possessed the qualities she wanted for Aslan.
“I wanted someone who was profound but not pretentious, who had gravitas but not morose self-seriousness,” Gerwig said. She also wanted an actor over 70 who could convey both wisdom and a sense of childlike wonder, describing Streep as “one of the greatest actors to ever do it”.
Gerwig is also taking other creative liberties with The Magician’s Nephew. The story, which was originally published in 1955, is being moved from its early 20th-century setting to the 1950s. The filmmaker has also described the film as having a rock-opera sensibility.
David Bowie is reportedly another influence on the film’s visual approach. Aslan has been shown with different-coloured eyes and a bold red stripe across his face, with Gerwig telling Empire that she wanted the film to draw on the idea of Narnia as a world created through music.
The controversy has also prompted some C.S. Lewis scholars and fans to urge audiences to wait before judging the film. Kat Coffin, a Lewis scholar, questioned the casting but said there was a difference between a woman voicing a male character and actually changing the character’s gender.
The family of Lewis’ late wife, Joy Davidman Gresham, has also expressed support for Gerwig’s production. In a statement provided by Netflix, the family praised the filmmaker’s passion for Lewis’ work and said they were pleased to be working with her and the production team. The C.S. Lewis Company similarly said it was moved by how deeply Gerwig had embraced Lewis’ world.
Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on February 12, 2027, before its Netflix release on April 2.

title: Verstappen wins Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia
description: He finishes 2 307 seconds ahead of Kimi Antonelli
content:
He finishes 2.307 seconds ahead of Kimi Antonelli
Four-time world champion Max Verstappen secured his and Red Bull's first win this year with an imperious drive Sunday in chaotic conditions in a storm-delayed Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
Nine years after winning the last F1 race at the Sepang International Circuit, the 29-year-old Dutchman came through a wild afternoon of accidents and incidents for his 72nd victory and first since Abu Dhabi last year.
In a race of shifting tyre strategies, he came home 2.307 seconds ahead of championship leader Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes and seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton who took third after a thrilling recovery drive.
His Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc was fourth, having fallen to last place in the early laps, ahead of Isack Hadjar in the second Red Bull, McLaren's Oscar Piastri and the Racing Bull of Liam Lawson.
Two-time champion Fernando Alonso finished a season-best eighth for Aston Martin ahead of world champion Lando Norris and Racing Bull rookie Arvid Lindblad.
The result extended Antonelli's lead to 84 points ahead of teammate George Russell, who retired after a late power failure under a safety car.
"It is really nice to win after the year we've had and all the progression we've made," said a delighted Verstappen.
"It is super-nice to win here. It was very hectic with a lot of different things, but we made the right call with the inters (intermediate tyres)."
Antonelli congratulated him and added: "It was the maximum we could have done. We struggled, but I am happy to come away with P2."
Hamilton was greeted by a roar from the big crowd.
"I was more than a minute back after we made the wrong call on tyres at the start and everyone was pulling away."
The race had followed a protracted 100-minute delay following a tropical rainstorm, and began with half the field on intermediate tyres.
Both Mercedes promptly swamped Verstappen, Antonelli taking the lead in turn one, followed by Russell.
Hamilton, on soft slicks, had no grip and tumbled down the order from second on the grid as it became clear that the conditions remained treacherous.
It all changed on lap nine when Valtteri Bottas slid off into the gravel and the safety car was deployed, bringing nearly everyone in for dry tyres with Antonelli taking mediums and Verstappen softs.
Hamilton stayed out and upon the resumption Verstappen pounced to sweep round Antonelli and regain a lead he would not relinquish.
Hamilton continued his recovery, slicing through the field and by lap 23 had dispensed with Lawson to take fifth.
He closed up within six seconds of the Frenchman before the pair pitted on lap 31. "This tyre feels terrible," said Hamilton of his new mediums.
A late virtual and then full safety car saw everyone pit for fresh softs.
Russell's retirement enabled Hamilton to get on to the podium when he passed Hadjar in the final four-lap dash to the chequered flag.

title: Industrial robots working in factories surpass 5M worldwide
description: AI advances and supply chains drove factory automation to a record high  with robot stocks exceeding 5m last year
content:
AI advances and supply chains drove factory automation to a record high, with robot stocks exceeding 5m last year
AI integration, supply chain restructuring drive industrial robot installations, with China leading by installing 354,000 new robots accounting for 59% of the world's active robot inventory, followed by US, as Japan falls to 3rd place in 2025
The ever-growing developments in artificial intelligence (AI) and supply chains drove global factory automation adoption to historic highs, with the global active industrial robot inventory surpassing 5 million last year, according to a report.
The International Federation of Robotics said the operational robot stock rose 9% on an annual basis and global installations jumped 11% to more than 600,000 units.
China boasts an overwhelming dominance in the field, expanding annual robot installations by 20% to 354,000 units, making up 59% of the global deployment, while domestic firms secured 55% of the market share in the country.
Japan’s installations fell 19% to 36,219 units, falling from second place to be replaced by the US, which posted a 12% surge to 38,500 robots.
South Korea maintained its fourth position with 30,200 annual robot installations, followed by Germany with an 8% decline to 24,800. India had a 15% surge to 10,500.
Germany’s growth decelerated while accounting for 41% of all EU installations, alongside contractions in Italy, France, and Spain.
The global robot demand is expected to rise in the coming years, with installations climbing to 655,000 units this year and 806,000 by 2029.
Read More: How Chinese robot dancers find their rhythm on American TV show
Persistent labor shortages in advanced economies, supply chain reshoring and AI-focused technologies lowering deployment costs for small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) drove the expansion in robot installations.
At the same time, Türkiye ranked 17th in the global robot market last year, while robot installations declined 9% to 3,194 units, down from its record of 4,429 units in 2023.
Türkiye’s operational stock rose 7% to a record of 30,990 units, ranking 15th worldwide in the robot fleet.
The country’s metal industry remained the top automation buyer among other sectors, as installations rose 8% to 990 units to capture 31% of the market, with 6,774 robots in active duty.
The Turkish auto sector’s robot inventory climbed 3% to 889 units, accounting for 28% of new installations and maintaining 11,017 active units.
Demand weakened in other sectors, with annual robot installations in the electrical/electronics sector, including home appliances and electrical machinery, falling 37% to 136 units, while adoption in the food products, beverages and tobacco products segment saw annual robot installations plummet by 40% to 144 units.
Some 59% of all new robots were deployed for handling operations/machine tending and 16% for welding and soldering, the report showed.
The report added that the robot density remains quite low, with 52 units per 10,000 workers in the manufacturing industry, while the density was better in the auto sector, reaching 374 per 10,000 workers, compared to a rate of 35 units per 10,000 workers in other industries.

title: Ali Azmat reveals his surprisingly minimal  no chemical  personal care routine

content:
Singer says his bathroom has little beyond soap and toothpaste — and reveals he does not use a toothbrush
Rockstar Ali Azmat has given fans an unexpected glimpse into his personal-care habits, revealing a remarkably minimalist routine that includes soap and toothpaste — but not a toothbrush.
Appearing on Tabish Hashmi’s Hasna Mana Hai , Azmat said his bathroom contains very few personal-care products.
“In my bathroom, I just have soap and a toothpaste,” he said. His routine became even more surprising when he revealed that he does not use a toothbrush. “Not even a toothbrush, I use my finger,” he added.
Azmat explained that his approach comes from his personal aversion to what he describes as “chemicals”, a philosophy he said has become more difficult to maintain as his daughters have grown older and developed an interest in beauty and skincare products.
“I personally am against chemicals,” he said, adding, “For me it is a big exam that my daughters, who are now growing up and are 13-14 years old, they are obsessed with products and wanting certain creams.”
He also recalled a shopping trip in Canada, where he joked that his daughters and their mother persuaded him to spend a significant amount on personal-care products. “When I was in Canada they and their mom made me get 1000-2000 money worth of chemicals,” he said
Azmat’s comments appeared to be less a prescribed routine than a reflection of his personal philosophy: keep things simple, avoid unnecessary products and, where possible, stay away from ingredients he is uncomfortable using.
The conversation also taps into the growing contrast between increasingly elaborate beauty routines and the minimalist approach favoured by some public figures.
At a time when bathroom shelves can be packed with cleansers, serums, moisturisers and specialised treatments, Azmat appears content with considerably less.

title: OpenAI safety employee quits  says    time for trial and error is over
description: Robinson said OpenAI releases systems and strengthens safeguards when problems emerge under    iterative deployment
content:
Robinson said OpenAI releases systems and strengthens safeguards when problems emerge under “iterative deployment”
A former OpenAI safety employee who recently resigned has criticised the company’s approach to AI safety, arguing that a fast-paced culture focused on rapid development increases the risk of failures.
Writing in “I Quit OpenAI Because Its Culture Is Broken”, published by The Atlantic on Saturday, David Robinson said AI companies, including OpenAI, were not being “nearly careful enough” and should place greater emphasis on safety expertise and research before developing more capable systems.
“The time for trial and error is over,” Robinson wrote, arguing that advanced AI systems require safeguards more akin to those used in industries such as nuclear power and aviation.
Robinson said OpenAI relies heavily on what it calls “iterative deployment”, releasing systems and strengthening safeguards when problems emerge.
Read More: AI's race to transform the world before the money runs out
The comments add to a debate within the AI industry over whether companies are moving too quickly to develop increasingly powerful systems. OpenAI and rival Anthropic have faced scrutiny after incidents in which safety controls failed or experimental systems behaved unexpectedly.
Robinson, who said he spent three and a half years at OpenAI, helped draft the company’s preparedness framework and oversaw safety reports for 12 frontier-model launches. “As the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the level of care that I believe is needed,” he wrote.
“We’re making sure our models don’t become more capable than we can safely manage and secure, and we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down,” an OpenAI spokesperson said in a statement.
Robinson also warned that AI capabilities were advancing faster than researchers’ understanding of alignment, a field focused on ensuring AI systems act in accordance with human goals and values.

Mobeen announced the release on Instagram through a collaborative post with Mustehsan, sharing a snippet from the music video. “TOUCH - OUT NOW ON ALL PLATFORMS,” the pair wrote, with Mobeen adding that she and Baker had put considerable thought into the track.

The accompanying music video leans into the song’s carefree mood. Mobeen and Mustehsan are seen dancing alongside a piano, spending time around a house and pool, and driving together in a convertible as they take in scenic views.

Mustehsan had also teased the collaboration through a series of artistic videos from the project in the days leading up to its release, leaving followers intrigued by the unexpected pairing.

title: US Supreme Court to kick off term with bid by Big Oil to toss climate suits
description: Exxon  Suncor face Colorado damages claim as nearly 60 state  local govts pursue cases against fossil fuel companies
content:
Exxon, Suncor face Colorado damages claim as nearly 60 state, local govts pursue cases against fossil fuel companies
The United States Supreme Court begins its new nine-month term on Monday with arguments in a major case involving a bid by oil companies ExxonMobil and Suncor Energy to scuttle a lawsuit by officials in Boulder, Colorado, seeking monetary damages for harms caused by climate change.
It is the first of several important cases already teed up for the term, with disputes involving issues such as President Donald Trump's immigration policies and state-level bans on assault-style rifles to be heard in the coming months. The court's 6-3 conservative majority has moved US law dramatically rightward in recent years.
The top US judicial body, as is its custom, opens its term on the first Monday in October.
US-based Exxon and Canada-based Suncor appealed after the Colorado Supreme Court let Boulder's lawsuit accusing them of state law violations proceed. The Trump administration has backed Exxon and Suncor, arguing that federal law precludes Boulder's claims.
Read: Supreme Court lets Trump resume deporting migrants to countries not their own
Boulder's city and county governments have accused the two companies of helping drive climate change and misleading the public about the risks of fossil fuels. Boulder aims to hold the companies liable for past and future costs associated with climate change such as infrastructure repairs, environmental damage, emergency management and harms to public health.
The burning of fossil fuels releases greenhouse gases including carbon dioxide into the atmosphere, trapping heat and raising average global temperatures over time.
Nearly 60 state and local governments have brought similar suits seeking billions of dollars from fossil fuel companies, with more continuing to be filed, Exxon and Suncor told the justices. A ruling by the Supreme Court in favour of the companies could lead to many of those cases being dismissed.
Monday's arguments mark the latest example of energy-sector companies asking the justices to block climate-related liability or limit federal environmental regulation.
Also Read: News outlets ask US court to block Trump White House ban beyond 14-day order
Backers of the oil companies argue that if Boulder's most far-reaching claims are allowed to proceed, it could give states sweeping power over conduct occurring far outside their borders.
Energy companies and trade groups, along with states allied with them, have built a largely winning record before the justices over the past two decades in cases involving climate liability and the reach of federal environmental regulation.
Exxon and Suncor argue, among other things, that Boulder's claims intrude on an area governed by the Clean Air Act.
Justice Samuel Alito has recused himself from participating in the case. Alito owns stock in several oil and gas companies but not Exxon or Suncor, according to his financial disclosure forms.
The Supreme Court's decision is expected by the end of June.

title: First documented cases of Marfan syndrome found in two cat siblings
description: The condition affects around one in 4 000 people and is associated with changes to connective tissues throughout body
content:
The condition affects around one in 4,000 people and is associated with changes to connective tissues throughout body
Scientists have identified the first documented cases of Marfan syndrome in domestic cats after two feline brothers, Gary and Shaggy, were found to have the rare genetic disorder.
The siblings showed signs of the condition from a young age, including unusually long limbs. As they grew older, veterinary examinations also revealed abnormalities affecting their eyes and enlargement of the aorta, the main artery carrying blood away from the heart. These findings led researchers to investigate whether the cats had Marfan syndrome, a connective tissue disorder best known in humans.
The condition affects around one in 4,000 people and is associated with changes to connective tissues throughout the body, including those in the eyes, bones, ligaments, skin and blood vessels. Until the cases of Gary and Shaggy, it had not been documented in cats.
Researchers from Cornell University’s College of Veterinary Medicine and Baker Institute for Animal Health worked with specialists from Ghent University in Belgium, the University of Pennsylvania and the Schwarzman Animal Medical Center in New York City. The team combined detailed veterinary examinations with genetic sequencing to determine the cause of the cats’ symptoms.
The investigation identified changes in the FBN1 gene, which provides instructions for producing fibrillin-1, a protein that is important for healthy connective tissue. Both Gary and Shaggy carried two altered copies of the gene, with one inherited from each parent.
The finding was particularly unusual because, in humans, a single altered copy of FBN1 can cause Marfan syndrome, while inheriting two altered copies is extremely rare. Researchers discovered that the specific variant carried by the cats did not completely stop the gene from functioning. Instead, it disrupted how the gene's instructions were processed while still allowing some normal function.
That partial function may help explain why Gary and Shaggy survived into adulthood despite carrying two altered copies of the gene. The study found that the genetic variant caused exon 22 to be skipped in a large proportion of the gene's transcripts, while a smaller amount of normally processed genetic material was still produced.
The researchers described the discovery as an important step towards improving veterinary diagnosis of the condition. Dr Jacquelyn Evans, the study’s senior author and an assistant professor at Cornell’s Baker Institute for Animal Health, said the findings could help veterinarians recognise similar cases in the future and potentially contribute to the development of genetic tests.
The findings were published in Scientific Reports on September 19 in a study titled A homozygous hypomorphic FBN1 splice region variant in domestic cats with Marfan syndrome. Researchers said the cases also demonstrate how studying naturally occurring genetic disorders in animals can provide comparative insights into conditions that affect humans.

title: Turkish foreign minister to attend Makkah Joint Defence Agreement committee meeting in Riyadh
description: Fidan expected to reaffirm Turkiye s solidarity with Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks
content:
Fidan expected to reaffirm Turkiye's solidarity with Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Monday will attend a meeting in Riyadh of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee established under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, an alliance founded in August with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.
According to Turkish Foreign Ministry sources, Fidan, National Defence Minister Yasar Guler and Chief of General Staff General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu will also attend the committee meeting in the Saudi capital.
At the meeting, Fidan is expected to share Turkiye's views on the institutionalisation of the alliance and steps to be taken in the coming days, as well as assessments of threats to peace and stability in the Middle East.
Fidan is also expected to express Turkiye's views on regional developments concerning the allies' collective security and note that the progress achieved in the alliance's work in the short time since it was founded is valuable from the perspective of establishing lasting stability in the region.
Read: Meeting of Makkah defence pact in Saudi Arabia next week to focus on Houthi attacks: FM Dar
He is expected to reaffirm Turkiye's strong solidarity with and support for Saudi Arabia in the face of recent Houthi attacks and underline that provocative actions targeting holy sites are unacceptable.
Fidan is also expected to highlight the alliance's importance not only in developing a joint and effective response to existing threats but also in preventing regional crises. He is set to stress that resolving disputes in the region through peaceful means remains a priority and that actions that could further escalate tensions should be avoided.
Fidan is also expected to reiterate the importance of ensuring freedom and security of navigation along international trade routes and draw attention to what Ankara describes as Israel's continued targeting of efforts to establish peace and stability in the region.
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, and Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Makkah on August 7.
The agreement reflects Turkiye, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia's commitments to developing regional solutions to regional problems and their shared strategic vision focused on regional security and stability.
It aims to strengthen the security of the three countries through collective deterrence and defence.
Strategic Political and Defence Committee
A Strategic Political and Defence Committee made up of the foreign and defence ministers and chiefs of General Staff of the three countries was established to guide activities under the agreement.
The committee held its first meeting in Istanbul on August 31, hosted by Turkiye.
Foundational decisions were taken at the meeting, and technical work toward institutionalising the alliance was reviewed, including establishing the alliance's secretariat in Riyadh as soon as possible.
Retired Pakistani Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood was nominated to serve as the alliance’s first secretary-general.
Read More: Saudi crown prince says Makkah defence pact with Türkiye, Pakistan aims to bolster regional stability
The foreign ministers of Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia also met in New York on September 24 on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly .
They discussed regional developments, and a joint statement issued afterwards condemned attacks targeting the holy city of Makkah as well as Saudi Arabia's civilian and economic infrastructure.
The chiefs of General Staff of the three countries also met in Riyadh on September 25.

title: Asif  Tarar fire fresh salvoes at PTI after talks deadlock
description: Defence minister accuses Imran Khan of bringing terrorism to K P
content:
Defence minister accuses Imran Khan of bringing terrorism to K-P
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Sunday fired fresh salvoes at the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) over the failure of government-opposition talks, accusing the party of adopting double standards on terrorism and using calls for consultation as a delaying tactic.
The exchange followed marathon government-opposition talks over PTI’s planned long march, which ended in deadlock in the early hours of Sunday. Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had said the PTI-TTAP side wanted counter-terrorism measures in K-P to be agreed jointly by the federal and provincial governments after consultation with political parties and other stakeholders.
The breakdown in negotiations produced competing accounts from the government and opposition over what had prevented an agreement, with the main disagreement centred on counter-terrorism policy in K-P.
Responding to Afridi’s post on X, in which the CM Afridi said the talks had failed because the government had not agreed to jointly formulate a counter-terrorism policy for K-P with the provincial government and other political stakeholders, Tarar said PTI’s position on consultation had “outlived its life in the past three years”.
“PTI’s lame old excuse that all parties should have been consulted has outlived its life in the past three years,” Tarar said. “Federal government did exactly that but you never responded to our proposals.”
He said the K-P government had only recently begun responding to federal calls for a joint mechanism to fight terrorism because it was “politically weak” and accused it of doing so to protect its political standing in the province.

PTI’s lame old excuse that all parties should have been consulted has outlived its life in the past three years, Federal government did exactly that but you never responded to… https://t.co/fdc1HqNbJO
“Double standards and hypocrisy seem to be your policy; when you say that the PTI K-P government has been taking steps to fight terrorism and is serious in this matter,” Tarar said.
“On the contrary, your narrative on terrorism is in favour of terrorists. K-P government's policy only encourages and supports the spread of terrorism in the province,” he added.
Tarar then questioned why the K-P government had not participated in federal Apex Committee meetings or, “Why doesn't the K-P Government hold its own Apex committee meetings to review terrorism like other provinces hold their meetings?”
He also questioned why the chief minister and his cabinet had not condemned the interim Afghan Taliban government over its support for terrorism in Pakistan.
“Has the K-P government ever shown any outright support to the valiant Armed Forces and the police who have laid down thousands of lives fighting terrorism in K-P?” he said.
Tarar also questioned why the provincial government had not fully implemented the National Action Plan (NAP), particularly measures concerning illegal activities, undocumented Afghan nationals and strengthening the capacity of the police and Counter Terrorism Department.
He also challenged PTI leaders to explain their absence from the funerals of security personnel killed in the fight against terrorism and their lack of visits to security and police posts.
He further questioned how often the K-P leadership had visited the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas and "took interest in their governance and development issues?”
Read: PTI begins first phase of long march amid mounting political tensions
“Once the Afghan Taliban regime in support of terrorism in K-P sends drones and tashkeels, why do you keep quiet?” he asked. “How many times have you stood shoulder to shoulder with our valiant FC soldiers standing guard on the Pak-Afghan border against these terrorists?”
“Please give some answers before ranting confusion and useless rhetoric only,” he said. “This is an old strategy of PTI that when under pressure, they start talking of consultations and joint actions but on the ground they do the exact opposite,” he said.
He also blamed the K-P government for the worsening security and economic situation in the province, saying the alleged failure to implement the NAP had allowed terrorism to flourish.
He rejected Afridi’s call for collective consultation and described it as a delaying tactic. “So stop selling this false narrative of collective consultations, jirgas or any other method as this means nothing on the ground other than delaying tactics,” he said.
Tarar ended his post with a warning to the PTI-led provincial government. “This time the State won’t let you embroil and confuse people by your old age rhetoric and verbosity that has already brought KPK to the brink of collapse,” he said. “No More!!!!”
In a post on X, the defence minister questioned PTI leaders who, he said, spoke about innocent victims in the province but did not visit the families of civilians killed in terrorist attacks.
“You talk about the innocent martyrs of your province, but leave aside the military martyrs — you are even refusing to take ownership of the civilian martyrs. Tell us, have you gone to the home of even a single civilian martyr to offer condolences?”
Asif accused PTI founder Imran Khan of bringing terrorism to K-P and supporting the settlement of terrorists in the province, saying the party's speeches in the provincial assembly and its media record were evidence of this.
“This terrorism was brought to K-P by their leader Imran. He was the biggest supporter of settling them in K-P. The record of assembly speeches and the media bears witness to this.”
He challenged PTI leaders to debate the issue with him on television.
Asif also accused successive K-P chief ministers of attacking the federal government after PTI lost power at the Centre, while separately referring to the May 9 events.
“The entire K-P leadership itself loots government resources and also gives a share to terrorists in the form of extortion,” he said.
“You are partners of the terrorists. Your hands are also stained with the blood that is being shed in K-P. The nation will hold you accountable, and so will God.”

Asif also described Islamabad as a symbol of the country's unity and the federation, saying it represented the identity of 250 million Pakistanis.
He said the country's martyrs had sacrificed their lives for Pakistan and praised the resolve of the people and armed forces to confront internal and external threats.
Asif ended his post by expressing confidence in Pakistan's future.
“God willing, Pakistan will always remain alive,” he said.
Earlier, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also accused the K-P government of backing out of security-related commitments during the final phase of negotiations. He said the provincial government had agreed to submit a 72-hour implementation plan covering counter-terrorism measures, the NAP, cooperation with the armed forces and other security issues.
Afridi subsequently maintained that PTI’s seven-point demands were constitutional and legal and said the long march would proceed after the talks failed to produce an agreement.
Conflicting accounts over talks breakdown
PTI leader Salman Akram Raja similarly said the opposition had insisted that counter-terrorism measures be based on an agreement between the two governments and have the “buy-in” of political parties represented in the provincial assembly.
Raja said the PTI-TTAP team had “stood firm on its principled position” that anti-terrorism actions in KP should be agreed between the federal and provincial governments and that policies aimed at fighting terrorism “must have the support of the local population and be based on ground intelligence”.
The government, however, gave a different account of the negotiations. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the KP government had agreed to sign a written agreement and submit an implementation plan within 72 hours covering a series of security measures, but had backed out during the final phase of the talks.
Read more: Deadlock persists as hours-long govt, PTI talks end without breakthrough
Naqvi said the commitments included reconsidering the Police Act 2026, preventing terrorists from operating freely or finding safe havens in the province, condemning the TTP and other terrorist groups, supporting the national policy on Afghan refugees, increasing funding for counter-terrorism operations and police, strengthening cooperation with the armed forces and implementing the NAP.
“Last night, during the final phase of negotiations, the K-P Government backed out of these commitments,” Naqvi said. “Security must not be politicised while the province is at War.”
The opposition disputed that account. Raja said the government team had insisted that actions initiated unilaterally by the federal government would have to be “owned by the provincial government”, which the PTI-TTAP team had rejected.
The disagreement followed two days of negotiations over PTI’s planned long march. The talks, chaired by National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq, had initially focused on the party’s demands, including political dialogue, legal and medical rights for Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi, relief for prisoners and a jointly formulated strategy to address terrorism in KP.
The opposition also maintained that a meeting with Imran Khan was necessary before the march could be called off, with Haleem Adil Sheikh later saying the government had also rejected an alternative request for Senate opposition leader Raja Nasir Abbas to meet the PTI founder.
With neither side willing to concede on the key issues, the negotiations ended in the early hours of Sunday without an agreement. PTI subsequently maintained that the long march would go ahead , with Afridi announcing that it would begin from K-P on Sunday afternoon.
