title: Seventh heaven for England in Nations League rout of Croatia
description: Kane and Saka score twice each in a 7 0 win
content:
Kane and Saka score twice each in a 7-0 win
Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka both struck twice as England ran riot in a 7-0 rout of abject Croatia in the Nations League on Saturday.
Thomas Tuchel's side ripped Croatia to shreds in Rijeka to make it two wins from their first three matches in their Nations League group.
England captain Kane's double extended his record goal tally for his country to 89.
But the Bayern Munich striker was far from the only stand-out performer for England.
Arsenal winger Saka also bagged a brace as England recorded the biggest win of the Tuchel era.
Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham, restored to the starting line-up after Tuesday's 2-0 win against Czech Republic, was on target to cap a vibrant display featuring three assists.
The effervescent Anthony Gordon netted to make it four goals in his last four England matches before Morgan Rogers completed the annihilation.
Chasing a top-two finish to secure a spot in the Nations League quarter-finals in March, England conclude the international break against Czech Republic at Wembley on Tuesday.
That should be a slightly more raucous occasion than this tie, which was played 'behind closed doors' because of crowd trouble involving Croatia fans against France in 2025.
Around 6,000 local school children and 100 England supporters were allowed into the Stadion HNK Rijeka, creating a subdued environment in a country known for its hostile atmospheres.
England's players had taken a dip in the nearby Adriatic Sea earlier in the week, prompting Tuchel to warn the relaxed mood in the camp must not put his team into "holiday mode".
But with the Adriatic shimmering in the sun just yards from the stadium, it was child's play for England as they demolished ageing Croatia to disappoint the youthful crowd.
Tuchel's men took just eight minutes to go ahead with an incisive raid that exposed the talent gap between the side.
Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, making his first start for England, was the catalyst with a composed pass to Bellingham.
Bellingham slipped an equally measured ball in behind the flat-footed Croatia defence and Kane took a deft touch before stroking a clinical finish into the roof of the net from 10 yards.
England had too much pace and poise for Croatia and it was no surprise when Bellingham increased their advantage at the end of flowing 27-pass move in the 21st minute.
Saka's cross was too high for his team-mates, but Gordon adroitly controlled the ball in mid-air and whipped it back into the six-yard box, where Bellingham stretched to poke into the far corner.
Gordon put the result beyond doubt in the 39th minute, diving to meet Jarell Quansah's pin-point cross with an agile header that flashed past Dominik Livakovic from six yards.
Quansah's assist was a timely riposte to the critics who said Tuchel was wrong to select him instead of Trent Alexander-Arnold after the Real Madrid right-back made his first England start in nearly two years against Czech Republic.
England beat Croatia 4-2 in June in their opening World Cup group game, but this was a far more one-sided encounter.
Bellingham was in irrepressible mood, driving into the Croatia area and baffling Luka Modric with a smooth drag-back before crossing low towards Saka, who slotted home from close-range on the stroke of half-time.
England showed no mercy after the interval and Kane netted again in the 53rd minute, sliding in to convert Anderson's cross with ease.
Saka got the sixth from Kane's pass after another woeful error from hapless Croatia in the 68th minute.
Rogers came off the bench to put the seal on England's swaggering display, rounding Livakovic to net from Bellingham's 87th minute pass.

title: Zverev sets up Djokovic quarter final at China Open
description: The German top seed dispatches home wildcard Shang Juncheng 6 0  6 3 in just 55 minutes
content:
The German top seed dispatches home wildcard Shang Juncheng 6-0, 6-3 in just 55 minutes
Big-serving Alexander Zverev trounced home hopeful Shang Juncheng 6-0, 6-3 at the China Open on Saturday to set up a quarter-final clash with Novak Djokovic, while Elena Rybakina was stunned on her opener in Beijing.
The German top seed needed just 55 minutes to brush aside the Chinese wildcard, ranked 250th, firing nine aces along the way.
"Happy with the win," the world's second-ranked player said, adding that his 21-year-old opponent had been "dangerous" and had "nothing to lose".
"Looking forward to the next couple of weeks," Zverev said ahead of his tie with Djokovic -- who has never lost a match in Beijing -- on Sunday.
Zverev's cruise into the next round comes as he trains his sights on the number-one spot currently held by Jannik Sinner.
The Italian won in Beijing last year but is not there this time around. He said on Saturday that he would not play at next week's Shanghai Masters either.
"I think it's no secret that it's a goal, for sure," Zverev told reporters when asked about the battle for No. 1.
"I know what I'm playing for. I know I'm very, very motivated to play at the moment. But again, I have a tough challenge tomorrow, and that's my focus," he said.
Also in the men's draw, third seed Daniil Medvedev eased into the quarter-finals with a 6-4, 6-3 win over Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff to play Argentina's Francisco Cerundolo.
Alex de Minaur, seeded fifth, and Andrey Rublev both needed three sets to advance and will play each other in the last eight.
In the women's draw, world No.1 Elena Rybakina could not regroup and fell to 118th-ranked Alina Charaeva in the second round.
The 27-year-old from Kazakhstan was playing her first match since seizing the top ranking on her US Open win in New York, but Armenia's Charaeva triumphed 3-6, 6-4, 6-3 in a clinical comeback.
"I don't have words," said 24-year-old Charaeva, who is making her Beijing debut.
"She's (an) amazing player, and for me it's kind of just dream come true."
Wind rattled the closed-roof stadium, with both players serving as thunderous claps echoed over the court.
A supportive crowd tried to rally Rybakina back into contention, but seven double-faults ushered the momentum into the hands of her opponent.
"It was a very tough day," Rybakina said afterward, adding that she had trouble with her foot and was feeling the effects of "a lot going on" following her New York win.
She said she would take a week to rest and get her foot fit for the rest of the season.
Charaeva faces Briton Sonay Kartal in the third round.
World No.4 Coco Gauff kept her composure to beat Camila Osorio 7-6 (7/4), 4-6, 6-2, overcoming shaky serving to survive the second round.
She next faces Chinese teenager Sun Xinran, ranked 582, who beat Spain's Cristina Bucsa 6-4, 7-5.
Sixth-seeded Elina Svitolina and former champion Iga Swiatek, seeded eighth, also went through.
Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen rebuked rowdy fans at her home tournament before opponent Anna Kalinskaya retired with injury to give the Chinese player a 6-7 (4/7), 6-4, 3-0 victory.
During a tight first-set tie-break, Zheng -- a beloved figure in her home country -- twice was heard telling spectators to "stop shouting" as she stepped up to serve.
"I thought the first set in particular was really difficult," Zheng told the crowd in an on-court interview after the two-hour-and-22-minute match.
"Indeed, seeing some movement in the audience, my emotions were not very stable," the 23-year-old added.
Chants for Zheng rang through the stadium before most points, and the umpire stepped in to warn people to stop moving around in the stands during play.
But Zheng declared: "It's my problem, it's my problem," and vowed to adjust.
She next faces Czech player Marie Bouzkova in the third round.

title: When geopolitics becomes economics
description: From the Red Sea to the Strait of Hormuz  economic interests are driving a new contest for global influence
content:
From the Red Sea to the Strait of Hormuz, economic interests are driving a new contest for global influence
Currently, the world has 65 active conflicts, which is the highest number post WWII. Out of these nine are interstate and the remaining 57 are intra state. However, the most significant one that affects the whole world is the Iran-US war. Though scaled down in intensity after the Pakistan-brokered ceasefire and the Islamabad MoU, it still impacts the world economy the most.
The recent unprecedented and quick sweep of Houthis capturing the southern coast of Yemen along the Red Sea has added a newer dimension to this imbroglio. To top it all, US President Trump's denial to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s requests to conduct strikes against the Houthis, and the Houthis’ assurances of not attacking the US and Israeli vessels, came as a surprise to all, but more so for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, an old US ally.
Connecting these developments to Somaliland and its recognition by Israel in December 2025, and UAE’s reported intent to establish a military base there make it a complex maze of geo-strategy. Is it a complementary effort by Iran to counter the alternative oil supply route of KSA? Or is it a US-Israel tit-for-tat endeavour to pressurise KSA to join the Abraham Accords? Nonetheless, it implies that the Bab al-Mandeb and Red Sea maritime route can be controlled any time by the Houthis and Somaliland, albeit with external support.
One must acknowledge that Trump has a strategic sense and vision that he is proudly implementing for the US. It was well deduced at the beginning of Iran-US-Israel War, that the whole effort centres around control of oil, critical minerals, the oceanic chokepoints, keeping petro dollars thriving, continuation of Israeli atrocities and expansion in this garb, and to carve a new security architecture in the region built around the Abraham Accords and Make America Great Again (MAGA). A hold on Venezuelan oil, planned efforts to control Latin American and African oil, and the US-Denmark-Greenland accord on Greenland, where melting ice is creating new water ways and, its possession is essential for establishing Golden Dome air defence system by US, as well as denial of access to its natural riches to Russia and China are the means to gain the ends of this strategy.
It’s only apt to emphasise here that all these conflicts are least about religion or ideology. These are primarily part of economic contestation including trade, control of resources, sea and land accesses and war economy. Interestingly, as of now, the largest oil and gas producing, and exporting country is the US. Despite war, Iran earns billions of dollars from oil sales and Russian gas passes through Ukraine and Ukraine gets royalty. The other element of the war economy is who benefits maximum from prolongation of the conflict(s) and restricted oil flows? The chief beneficiaries are oil producing countries, insurance and shipping companies, black market and military industrial complexes. Israel has been intentionally kept out of this phase of the war affording it opportunity to regroup, reequip and rebuild to continue with its expansionist policy and become strong enough to perpetuate as regional might. Systemic genocide of Palestinians, especially children persists in this moral and legal vacuum.
In this whole scenario, the shedding of responsibility by the US to oversee “the rules-based world order” as a super power engenders chaos, anarchy and increasing sense of insecurity. Consequently, the smaller and middle powers are building interest based alliances to secure their interests, and are hedging to join the blocs/camps.
China’s speedy rise through win-win economic cooperation stays the prime focus of Trump’s MAGA strategy, which boils down to imperialist expansion to enhance US sphere of influence, slow down US decline and scuttle Chinese rise. The recent meeting of President Xi and Trump at the White House may not end their contest, but could help keep it non-kinetic for now.
The Iran-US war is likely to continue until both sides lower their truce aims. Iran is not likely to settle for less than royalty for strait of Hormuz, like Suez canal, assured cessations of hostilities, lifting of sanctions and integration into the world economic system. The Houthis may follow the lead to come to terms with Yemen and KSA in somewhat similar manner. The long term solution of the Iran-US, Houthis-Yemen-KSA and Israel’s accesses resides in diplomacy and politics, not in the use of military instruments.
Pakistan’s brokering of ceasefire, making the Islamabad MoU happen, KSA-Pakistan bilateral, and then trilateral joint defence agreement including Türkiye and continued improvement in our relations with all major and middle powers are manifestations of this fact. Pakistan must continue with efforts for longer lasting regional peace by bringing Iran-US back to table and help effect a ceasefire and forge a long-term solution of Yemen-Houthis-KSA issue. At the same time, new-found relevance and friendships are to be translated into B2B and P2P long-term partnerships to construct complex interdependence with edifice in intertwined destinies for longer lasting good relations with all, especially immediate neighbours. China Pakistan time-tested and trusted bond has to be cemented further.
The writer is a (Retired) Major General, former ambassador, a PhD and a freelance contributor

title: Blank promises
description: Marriage registration leaves women   s rights to chance
author_name: RAZZAk ABRO, Wisal Yousafzai, Muhammad Ilyas
content:
Marriage registration leaves women’s rights to chance
A Nikahnama may take minutes to sign, but its fine print can shape a woman’s rights for decades. Yet crucial clauses on haq mehr, property and delegated divorce are often left blank, crossed out or poorly filled — sometimes by Nikah khawans with little formal training in the law they are recording.
The problem is particularly acute in rural and remote areas, where local familiarity often takes precedence over formal qualifications and families sign without fully understanding the Nikahnama’s legal weight. In such a scenario, computerisation can preserve a record, but it cannot make an incomplete or inaccurate entry meaningful.
The weakness becomes particularly significant in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), where incomplete marriage documentation intersects with the continuing problem of child marriage. Lawyers and child rights activists say that when the age and identity of a bride are not properly verified, registration can fail to identify an underage marriage before it takes place.
Peshawar High Court advocate Aisha Khan said the Nikahnama remains one of the most important legal documents for protecting women’s rights, but its effectiveness depends on the accuracy and completeness of the information recorded at the time of marriage.
Khan said K-P uses Form II of the Nikahnama under the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance and Rules, while the province amended the form in 2023 to include additional particulars concerning dower and the Khatm-e-Nabuwat declaration.
However, she noted that the continued use of unofficial Urdu translations alongside the official federal form, which is in English, can create inconsistencies in the recording and understanding of important marriage details. This becomes particularly problematic when couples do not understand the legal terminology used in the contract.
The difficulty is most evident in entries concerning age, identity, dower and property. Khan noted that accurate age and CNIC information was essential for identifying the parties and detecting potential underage marriages, while complete details of haq mehr and property could later determine whether a woman was able to establish her financial claims.
Columns 13 to 16 deal specifically with dower. Column 13 records its amount, Column 14 specifies whether it is prompt or deferred, Column 15 records the amount paid at the time of marriage, while Column 16 covers property given as dower, including its description and valuation.
Columns 17, 18 and 19 deal with special conditions, delegated power of divorce to the wife and restrictions on the husband's right of divorce, while Column 21 concerns an existing wife and permission from the Arbitration Council for another marriage.
Yet these provisions are not always completed with the same care.
Khan explained that the absence of a standardised official Urdu version had created particular difficulties in Columns 13 to 16. In some cases, registrars record only the cash component of dower, while descriptions of immovable property remain vague or incomplete.
Such omissions may appear insignificant when a marriage is taking place but can become critical when a woman later approaches a family court to recover her dower or establish her entitlement to property. The problem, however, extends beyond K-P.
In Sindh, the difference between urban and rural registration practices is also reflected in the qualifications expected of Nikah khawans. Nazir Ahmed, secretary of an urban union council in Karachi, said a Nikah registrar seeking registration with them must have graduated from a major religious seminary.
In rural areas, however, Abdul Sattar Jokhio, a former union council chairman, shared that the approach was different. In villages, everyone knows the local cleric who solemnises marriages. Therefore, the union council does not require the cleric to produce a certificate or qualification from a religious seminary. That disparity raises questions about who is entrusted with completing a document carrying potentially significant legal consequences.
Local lawyer Muhammad Ismail Mayo Rajput said people from urban areas or better-educated families generally consider it important to have the relevant Nikahnama columns completed when arranging their children's marriages. In rural and less-educated families, on the other hand, the provisions were more likely to be left blank. “Filling out most of these columns is particularly in the interests of brides and women, as it can prevent difficulties for them in the future,” he said.
He pointed to delegated divorce as one example. Where the wife has been given that right and the provision has been properly recorded, she can exercise the delegated right rather than having to approach a court for khula in the same way. Completing the dower provisions, he added, was similarly important to protecting a woman's financial rights.
In Punjab, legal expert Abdullah Malik raised similar concerns over the way dower is recorded. "Column 13 concerns haq mehr, a right of every woman, but registrars sometimes write only “Shariah” instead of specifying an amount." He also highlighted the failure to distinguish between mu’ajjal, or prompt dower, and ghair mu’ajjal, or deferred dower, saying this could create additional difficulties for women seeking to recover their entitlement.
Malik said Columns 17, 18 and 19 were also sometimes crossed out, potentially preventing special conditions and delegated divorce rights from being properly recorded. The problem, therefore, is not simply that a few registrars make mistakes. Pakistan lacks a consistently implemented system under which every Nikahnama is completed, explained and verified according to the same standards.
Legal experts and rights activists say standardisation must extend beyond the form itself to the qualifications, training and monitoring of the people authorised to complete it.
In K-P, marriage registrars are required under provincial rules to meet certain eligibility criteria, and marriages are subsequently entered into a computer system using NADRA-linked software. But Khan cautioned that computerisation alone could not guarantee accurate registration.
“If a registrar enters an incorrect age, identity detail or dower amount without verifying the supporting documents,” the digital system simply creates a more efficient record of inaccurate information.
That limitation becomes especially serious in relation to child marriage.
Qamar Naseem, programme manager at an organisation that works to empower women in K-P, said marriage registration should be digitally connected with birth-registration and national identity systems so that age verification becomes an institutional safeguard rather than something dependent on an individual registrar.
“A credible marriage registration system should not depend simply upon an age written by hand on a form,” he said.
For K-P, where girls below the applicable legal age can still face marriage, such verification is critical. A registrar who merely transfers an age supplied by a family onto a form may miss a legal problem that could have been identified through proper documentation.
Naseem also said incomplete or ambiguous Nikahnamas place an avoidable burden on the justice system because family courts may later have to determine what the parties actually intended when the marriage took place.
The lack of awareness among couples further compounds the problem.
Advocate Mehwish Mohib Kakhel said even educated couples sometimes sign the Nikahnama without reading or understanding its contents. “If people read this important document carefully, many issues concerning their rights and obligations can be clarified before marriage,” she said.
She stressed that the Nikahnama should not be treated as a routine formality. Properly completing and explaining it can provide greater protection for women while also helping prevent child marriage by ensuring that the age and identity of both parties were properly documented.
The responsibility, however, cannot rest with families alone. What is needed is a system in which Nikah khawans are properly qualified, regularly trained and held accountable for every entry they make. A standardised Nikahnama, clear language, routine inspection of registers and mandatory verification of age and identity could close some of the gaps that currently undermine marriage registration.
For women, the consequences can extend far beyond the wedding day. A blank dower column can complicate a financial claim; an omitted condition can become difficult to prove; and an unchecked age can allow an underage marriage to pass through a system designed to prevent it. A marriage may be solemnised in minutes, but the words written — or left unwritten — in its Nikahnama can shape the course of a woman's life for years.

title: Yasir Hussain responds to Akif Ilyas s criticism
description: Yasir Hussain responds to Akif Ilyas s criticism
content:
'I respect his opinion', says actor of makeup artist's comments
Pakistani actor and comedian Yasir Hussain has responded to comments made about him by celebrity makeup artist Akif Ilyas, who recently discussed their past association and criticised Hussain's approach to comedy.
Ilyas, who has worked with several leading names in Pakistan's entertainment industry, spoke about Hussain during an appearance on Nadia Khan's show. According to Ilyas, Hussain used to contact him early in his career and ask him to help build his portfolio. He claimed that Hussain later mocked his appearance, style and friendships during a live awards show.
Ilyas also questioned the quality of comedy in Pakistan and said younger comedians could learn from performers such as the late Moin Akhtar, arguing that comedy should not come at the expense of others.
The comments prompted reactions online, with social media users debating Ilyas' remarks and Hussain's response.
Responding to the circulating clip, Hussain acknowledged Ilyas' contribution to his early career and said he had known him for many years.
Hussain said Ilyas had done his first photoshoot and had not charged him for it. He also described Ilyas as a highly talented artist with expertise in both makeup and photography.
"I have mentioned in almost every interview how much he helped me at the beginning of my career," Hussain said, adding that several other senior artists had also supported him during his journey.
Addressing Ilyas' recent comments, Hussain stressed that he respected his right to have his own opinion.
"Whatever he said in that interview may have been influenced by something he heard or experienced, I don't know. But that is his personal opinion, and I respect it," Hussain said.
He ended his response on a conciliatory note, saying: "I love you, Akif bhai."

Gandhara Independent Film Festival's seventh edition is featuring 88 diverse productions in hybrid format
The seventh edition of the Gandhara Independent Film Festival (GIFF) is bringing independent films from Pakistan and around the world to Karachi in a hybrid format, with screenings taking place at the National Academy of Performing Arts (NAPA) alongside an online programme.
The festival, founded by Cirque Films in 2020, is being held from October 2 to 4 at NAPA's Hindu Gymkhana. This year's programme features 88 selected films, including 28 being screened in person and another 60 available online through a streaming platform.
The films selected for the 2026 edition represent 35 countries, including Pakistan, Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, Egypt, France, Indonesia, Iran, Lebanon, Malaysia, Mexico, Nepal, Norway, Poland, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Syria, Taiwan, the United Arab Emirates and the United States.
The in-person programme includes nine Pakistani short films and 19 international short films. The online selection includes seven feature films, 25 international shorts and 28 Pakistani shorts.
For GIFF Festival Producer Beenish Umer, the hybrid format is partly a practical response to the limited availability of venues and resources for independent cinema in Pakistan.
Speaking with The Express Tribune Umer said, "This is the seventh edition of the festival, which is held annually around this time of the year. This year, it is a hybrid festival, with 28 Pakistani and international films being screened at NAPA over three days, from October 2 to 4".
She said the festival would ideally have a longer physical programme, but venue limitations made that difficult.
"There are another 60 films available on OTT platforms. This is mainly because we have limited venues and resources, so we could not book a venue for the entire week," she said.
"Ideally, all the films should be screened at the festival. International festivals often run for a week or even two weeks, but given what we could manage on the ground, three days was what we could do this year."
The festival's organisers say its hybrid model has allowed GIFF to continue expanding its reach beyond a physical venue. Since its launch in 2020, the festival has showcased more than 700 independent films through online, physical and hybrid editions.
This year's selection also reflects the number of filmmakers seeking platforms for independent work in Pakistan.
According to Umer, the festival received around 500 submissions from filmmakers across Pakistan for this year's edition.
"We received around 500 film submissions from different parts of the country from filmmakers who wanted to participate in the festival," she said.
Actor Ayesha Toor, who attended the festival on its opening day, said events such as GIFF were important for creating opportunities to showcase both international and Pakistani independent cinema.
"I feel very good because such events should take place. I don't know where the Pakistani film industry is going, but we can show international films and we can show local independent films,"
She also highlighted the response from audiences at the festival and said she hoped GIFF would contribute to a wider cultural change in Karachi and Pakistan.
"I'm very hopeful that the Gandhara Film Festival will make that difference, will bring the change that we need in the cultural scene in Karachi and in Pakistan," she said.
The final selection includes films from a wide range of countries and filmmaking backgrounds.
Most of the Pakistani films in the programme are in Urdu with English subtitles, while the international selection includes films in 32 foreign languages.
The festival's physical programme is being hosted at NAPA in Karachi, while the online selection allows viewers to access a larger number of films beyond the three-day physical event.
For independent filmmakers, festivals such as GIFF can provide an alternative route to audiences at a time when short films and independent productions often have limited opportunities for theatrical exhibition.

title: Zach Bryan sports  Free Palestine  shirt during performance
description: Zach Bryan sports  Free Palestine  shirt during performance
content:
Singer is scheduled to return for second show on Oct 3
Zach Bryan drew attention to his appearance at Gillette Stadium on Friday, October 2, after taking the stage in a black shirt bearing the words "Free Palestine".
Bryan was performing at the Foxborough, Massachusetts venue as part of his With Heaven On Tour. His clothing choice gained attention because the stadium is owned by the Kraft Group, led by New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, who became involved in the controversy over Macklemore and Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour.
Macklemore made pro Palestinian comments during performances at MetLife Stadium in September, including a call for "Free Palestine" before performing "Hind's Hall". Kraft later confirmed that he had decided Macklemore should not perform at Gillette Stadium during Sheeran's September 25 and 26 concerts.
Kraft said the decision followed Macklemore's recent actions, material shared from the stage and what he described as a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that he said was offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community. Kraft also said the decision was not intended to deny anyone the right to advocate for Palestinians and said Palestinian suffering was real.
Sheeran's Gillette Stadium shows were cancelled because of severe weather linked to a nor'easter, while Macklemore was removed from the remaining US dates of the tour. Sheeran said the decision to remove the rapper was made by the promoter after venues indicated they would not host shows with Macklemore on the bill.
Macklemore later announced the Free Palestine Tour, with dates in Dublin, Paris and London selling out.
Bryan's shirt was notable because his concert took place shortly after the Macklemore and Kraft dispute. Bryan is scheduled to perform a second night at Gillette Stadium on Saturday, October 3.
Neither Bryan nor Kraft announced a connection between the shirt and the dispute. Its meaning remains open to interpretation.
Zach Bryan had released two self-produced studio albums, DeAnn (2019) and Elisabeth (2020), before signing with Warner Records to release his third album and major label debut American Heartbreak (2022), which peaked at number five on the Billboard 200 and was led by the Billboard Hot 100-top ten single "Something in the Orange". His self-titled fourth album (2023) debuted atop the Billboard 200, while its lead single, "I Remember Everything" (featuring Kacey Musgraves), peaked atop the Billboard Hot 100, Hot Country Songs, and Hot Rock & Alternative Songs charts simultaneously, also earning him a Grammy Award for Best Country Duo/Group Performance. His fifth studio album, The Great American Bar Scene (2024), peaked at number two on the Billboard 200, and his sixth, With Heaven on Top (2026), debuted at number one.
Throughout his career, Bryan has won several awards, including an Academy of Country Music Award, a Grammy Award and four Billboard Music Awards. He has sold over 30 million albums and singles, according to the RIAA.
Bryan started uploading his music to YouTube in 2017, with his friends recording him performing using his iPhone. Bryan's first song uploaded to YouTube was the single "God Speed" which ended up being a track on his debut album. Many of the songs Bryan would upload to his YouTube were written and recorded by him while serving in the Navy.

title: FCC draws line on second reviews
description: FCC draws line on second reviews
content:
Court observed that recall of an order may be considered where an independent procedural defect is established
The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has held that a second review petition cannot be filed in the same matter after a final decision on the first review petition, and a request styled as "recall" or "restoration" cannot be used to seek reconsideration of a judicial decision.
The court observed that recall of an order may be considered where an independent procedural defect is established. However, where the relief sought requires reconsideration of the reasoning or outcome of an earlier judicial order, such a request would in substance amount to a second review petition.
Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi gave the order on a Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No. 37/2026 filed by the Managing Director of the Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL). The court upheld the Registrar's objection dated July 3, 2026, and dismissed the appeal.
The court held that under Order 27, Rule 8 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2025, a second review petition cannot be entertained after final disposal of the first review petition. It noted that Order 10, Rule 2 also limits alteration or addition to a judgment pronounced in open court to correction of clerical or arithmetical mistakes or an accidental slip or omission.

title: Long march fears snarl freight traffic
description: Long march fears snarl freight traffic
content:
Truckers halt northbound journeys, leaving cargo stranded in Karachi
The government's decision to keep the PTI's long march out of the capital has led to a pileup of shipping containers in Karachi.
Truckers are refusing to drive north, for fear their vehicles will be seized and the containers used to barricade Islamabad ahead of an Oct 4 long march.
"Right now, going toward Punjab is like committing suicide," said driver Javid ur Rehman, 35, who has halted such journeys, referring to Pakistan's most populous province.
"The police seize the vehicles and snatch the containers, and then we are left distressed."
Steel shipping containers, packed with sand and welded together, have lined the roads into Islamabad for weeks, in preparations against a march, postponed from Sept 27, to demand Khan's release from prison.
"This is not the way to stop protests," said Rana Mohammad Aslam, president of the Karachi Goods Carrier association. Authorities began stopping vehicles around Sept. 5, weeks before the original date for the march, he said.
The interior, information, commerce and finance ministries did not respond to requests for comment. Punjab police and the provincial home department also did not respond. The containers are positioned ready for placement at key entry points into Islamabad.
Transporters battling rising prices say they cannot afford to have trucks seized.
Police requisitioned more than 2,000 vehicles in September ahead of the march, they added, many still loaded with cargo and held for days with little or no compensation.
Their reluctance is leaving containers to pile up at Karachi. The disruption was affecting routes to Islamabad, Rawalpindi, and the cities of Jhelum, Peshawar and Attock, Aslam said.
Some operators had halted journeys beyond Gujranwala, while others took alternative routes.
The bills are mounting for those whose containers have been seized, as daily demurrage charges on one such container alone can run into Rs30,000 to Rs40,000, Aslam said, adding to losses from missed deliveries and idle trucks.
Consumer prices rose 10.26% in September from a year earlier, while the transport price index climbed 27.43%, the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics said on Thursday.
Operators are struggling to pay drivers and maintain their fleets, as international shippers still expect payment regardless of the reason for the delay, Aslam said.
He was holding talks to find a solution, he added, but transporters could stage their own protest if complaints go unanswered.
For Pervaiz Khan, 50, the risk was enough to keep a load of chemicals parked in Karachi. "Right now, my vehicle is loaded but I am not going," said the father of five, adding that he had loaded his cargo of chemicals by night.
"We depart from Sindh, and the moment we enter Punjab, that's when our troubles begin."
Drivers stranded near Islamabad regretted lost days of work or earnings.
"If the roads open, our children's livelihood will open up," said Sagheer Ahmed, 51, who added that his children awaiting him at home relied on his earnings. "If not, we will just keep standing."

title: Pakistan  India trade barbs over IIOJK at UN
description: Pakistan  India trade barbs over IIOJK at UN
content:
Islamabad rejects Delhi's 'internal matter' claim on disputed territory
Pakistan on Saturday rejected India's characterisation of Jammu and Kashmir as an internal matter, telling a United Nations General Assembly committee that the territory's final status remains unresolved and must be determined in accordance with the wishes of the Kashmiri people.
Speaking during the general debate of the Third Committee of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, Pakistan's First Secretary Sarfraz Ahmed Gohar said Islamabad rejected New Delhi's assertion that Jammu and Kashmir was an integral part of India.
"Pakistan categorically rejects India's futile attempts to dismiss the Jammu and Kashmir dispute as a so-called internal matter," Gohar said, according to remarks shared by Pakistan's Permanent Mission to the UN.
He maintained that Kashmir was an internationally recognised disputed territory whose final status had yet to be determined in accordance with the wishes of its people and relevant UN Security Council resolutions.
Gohar accused India of failing to meet what Pakistan considers its international obligations under those resolutions and urged New Delhi to move towards a peaceful settlement of the longstanding dispute.
The Pakistani representative also highlighted human rights violations and discrimination against religious minorities in India, citing Muslims, Christians, Sikhs and other communities.
He said that religion-based violence, hate speech, discrimination and attacks on places of worship had become increasingly prevalent under the government led by India's Bharatiya Janata Party.
Gohar added Pakistan remained committed to dialogue, diplomacy and the peaceful settlement of disputes in accordance with the UN Charter, arguing that such an approach was necessary for peace and stability in South Asia.
The exchange came as the General Assembly's Third Committee began its work for the 81st session.

content:
PML-N leader urges empowered LGs, end to 'traitor' labels
Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) senior leader Khawaja Saad Rafique has blamed those who had "trampled" Pakistan for the country's present state, saying repeated amendments to the Constitution had failed to alter the fundamental reality that the country could not function without constitutional rule.
Speaking at a dialogue on "Good Governance and Rebuilding of a Collapsed System" organised by Leeds University at a local hotel in Lahore on Saturday, Rafique said those responsible included martial law rulers and their political facilitators.
He also held accountable sections of the judiciary for handing down judgments under doctrine of necessity.
He deplored that a "factory of traitors" had been established in the country, questioning how late Sindhi nationalist and politician G M Syed could have been called a traitor without being allowed to speak and instead being subjected to repression.
He said conditions in Balochistan had worsened and questioned how the state could conceal internal repression. He also asked who had prepared the militias in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, saying the whole nation was now paying the price in blood.
Speaking at the conference, former caretaker prime minister Anwaar-ul-Haq Kakar said he did not believe the country's system had completely collapsed, but acknowledged that its delivery mechanism was very weak.
He said governments based on accountability were recognised by the world and that democracy was the system capable of running them.
Kakar said democracy was a form of governance, but political parties had turned themselves into family systems.
Senior lawyer Hamid Khan said no democratic government had been allowed to complete its course in Pakistan and argued that this eventually resulted in the country being split into two.
Former federal minister and senior political leader Muhammad Ali Durrani said Pakistan had never truly experienced governance.
He said maintaining the status quo was no longer an option and urged people to act rather than expect everything to happen without effort.
Durrani warned that the younger generation was slipping away and that if its mindset was not understood, young people would no longer accept the status quo.
He said the public remained excluded from power and resources to such an extent that even a chief minister needed an aircraft.
"Bridging the distance between power and the people is now an urgent need."
He said politicians claimed they had been placed in power by force, through "Form 47 with a rope around their necks", and asked who should be considered responsible.
In his view, the person who forcibly installed someone in power was not the only culprit; the person who accepted the arrangement was also responsible.
Durrani said those operating under a hybrid system should decide for themselves whether that made them liable under Article 6.
He warned that Pakistan would not function unless public problems and authority were handed back to the people.

title: National Savings plans closure of 111 centres
description: National Savings plans closure of 111 centres
content:
Branch network to be reduced from 374 to 263 as govt seeks to cut operating costs
The federal government has declared 111 National Savings centres inefficient and financially unsustainable, proposing their closure or merger with nearby operational centres as part of a plan to rationalise the organisation's branch network.
The National Savings has issued a notification in this regard, under which the number of National Savings centres will be reduced from 374 to 263. According to the notification, an operational expenditure benchmark of Rs2,500 has been fixed for every Rs1 million in deposits at the centres.
The 111 inefficient centres have been directed to prepare practical plans either to reduce their operating costs or increase their business and deposits to improve their performance.
The notification said the affected centres could prepare plans to increase business and deposits to become more financially viable. Another option under consideration is relocating inefficient centres to areas with greater business and investment potential.
In case of relocation, regional directorates will submit business and relocation plans within 15 days. The notification stated that if a centre was closed, details of all employees posted there, along with their residential locations and preferred places for alternative posting, would have to be provided.
The Central Directorate of National Savings is a state-owned savings bank, operating as an attached department under the Finance Division, Ministry of Finance led by a director general.
The National Savings serves as an intermediary that raises funds from individual savers to help finance the government's fiscal deficit through non-bank means.

title: NCRC seeks age verification to protect kids online
description: NCRC seeks age verification to protect kids online
content:
Recommends stronger NCCIA capacity in IHC report
The National Commission on the Rights of Child (NCRC) has recommended an effective age-verification mechanism and a comprehensive regulatory framework to protect children from online grooming, sexual exploitation and harmful content.
The NCRC made the recommendations in a 17-page written response submitted to the Islamabad High Court (IHC) in a case concerning the use of social media by children under the age of 16.
The NCRC endorsed the concerns raised in the petition and emphasised the need for effective legal and regulatory measures to ensure children's online safety.
The commission recommended measures to limit unnecessary online interaction between children and unknown adults, stating that children need greater protection from potential online risks.
It also called for strengthening specialised capabilities to investigate online sexual exploitation of children and recommended enhancing the capacity of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) to handle cases involving technology-facilitated exploitation of children.
The NCRC further proposed developing a specialised mechanism using technology to combat the online exploitation of children.
In its written response, the commission stated that effective legal and regulatory measures are indispensable for protecting children online and that existing legal and institutional arrangements need improvement.
It maintained that online child protection is not merely a matter of policy but requires effective legal and institutional action.
The NCRC also recommended reviewing the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA), 2016 from the perspective of children's rights and proposed amendments where necessary to strengthen safeguards for children using digital platforms.
The commission stressed that the existing legal framework requires further improvement to address emerging online threats to children and provide them with adequate protection.
The recommendations came as the high court considers concerns surrounding the use of social media by children below 16 and the measures required to ensure their safety in the digital environment.
The NCRC said a comprehensive approach is required to protect children from online grooming, sexual exploitation and harmful material while ensuring that relevant institutions have the legal powers, resources and technical capacity to respond effectively.
The petition is being pursued by Jalal Haider and Yahya Farid.
Online grooming is when an adult or malicious actor builds an emotional connection and trust with a child or vulnerable person online to sexually abuse, exploit, blackmail, or radicalise them.

title: LHC seeks update on MPO judgment
description: LHC seeks update on MPO judgment
content:
Petitioner says safeguards against detention are inadequate
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has sought a report on the implementation of a decision previously issued by a larger bench concerning Sections 3 and 16 of the MPO Ordinancea legal provision that allows authorities to detain any citizen to ensure public order.
Justice Farooq Haider heard a constitutional petition filed by Advocate Abdullah Malik challenging the provisions of the MPO ordinance. During the hearing, the court asked what progress had been made on the implementation of the LHC larger bench's judgment
According to a news report, a larger LHC bench on June 19, 2025 referred three reform proposals to the Punjab Law Departmentgreater transparency in detention orders, a right of appeal and deterrent penalties for misuse of the power during detentionafter being told that 4,770 detention orders were issued in 2023 alone
Justice Haider observed that copies of the larger bench's decision had been sent to the chief secretary and the Ministry of Law and asked about the steps taken to implement the ruling.
Advocate Azhar Siddique, appearing in the matter on behalf of the petitioner, submitted that no action had been taken to implement the June 19, 2025 directions.
The petition contended that the MPO law does not provide clear and effective safeguards against deprivation of a person's liberty through preventive detention. It argued that preventive detention cannot be used as a substitute for the criminal justice system.
The petitioner maintained that a citizen's liberty could not be curtailed without evidence and reasonable grounds. The petition also challenged Section 16 of the MPO law, arguing that its broad restrictions on freedom of expression are inconsistent with constitutional guarantees.
It questioned the legal standards governing terms such as "fear or alarm" and activities considered harmful to public order, arguing that such provisions could permit restrictions on fundamental rights without sufficiently clear criteria.

As the fourth quarter kicks off, the stock market is already on pace for a solid year. The benchmark S&P 500 as of Friday had gained nearly 13% in 2026 and sat about 1% below its mid-August record high. Markets face a busy end of 2026, with the start of corporate earnings season and a pivotal Federal Reserve meeting in coming weeks, along with the looming November 3 mid-term elections that will decide control of the US Congress.
"It does tend to be a seasonally strong period, however I think this year investors are facing some headwinds as we go into the fourth quarter," said Tracie McMillion, Head of Global Asset Allocation Strategy at the Wells Fargo Investment Institute.
Since 1945, the S&P 500 averaged an increase of 4.2% in the fourth quarter, with the index posting gains 85% of the time, according to research firm CFRA. That average percentage rise is more than twice that of the other three quarters.
Fourth quarters of mid-term years have generally been even stronger, with an average gain of 6.4%, as stocks "benefit from the lifting of election uncertainty," Sam Stovall, Chief Investment Strategist at CFRA, said in a note. While fourth quarters tend to shine, mid-term years overall historically have been subpar, a trend stocks have defied so far in 2026. The S&P 500 has averaged a 15% dip in mid-term years historically, while the deepest drop so far this year has only been 9%, according to McMillion of the Wells Fargo institute.
The firm is on "high alert" for a pullback between now and election day, she said, for example, if it looks like the Democrats can wrest full control of Congress from President Donald Trump's Republican party. "If we were to see a change in the leadership in the House and the Senate combined, then we think that could have some policy ramifications that could impact the markets," she said, while adding that a pullback could be a buying opportunity.
The most immediate issue for stock investors is the jump in bond yields. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield on Thursday hit 5.34%, its highest level in 24 years. Yields, which rise when bond prices fall, have soared amid expectations for strong economic growth, surging energy costs that are driving up inflation, and increased competition for capital as companies issue debt to fund AI expansions. Higher yields likely already are impeding the market's advance, investors said. They can create more investment competition for equities and pressure stock valuations, while translating into more expensive borrowing costs throughout the economy.
"The interest rate story is the biggest headwind," said Chuck Carlson, Chief Executive Officer at Horizon Investment Services. "You're going to need some relief on that front. I don't necessarily think the market will tank per se, but to get a meaningful rally in the face of that, I think is going to be a struggle for the market."

title: G20 divided over excess capacity
description: G20 divided over excess capacity
content:
Two countries sign statement calling for more cooperation to eliminate goods produced with forced labour
A "handful" o rejected US calls to curb excess industrial capacity and "non-market" policies, the US Trade Representative (USTR) office said on Friday, exposing divisions within the group of major economies.
The US, this year's G20 chair, issued the statement a day after a trade meeting in Milwaukee that revealed that only two countries – Mexico and Argentina – signed on to a US-led statement calling for more work and cooperation to eliminate mgoods produced with forced labour from supply chains.
The rejection from the vast majority of G20 countries follows the Trump administration's imposition of tariffs of 10% or 12.5% on goods from 59 countries and the European Union over allegations that they fail to adequately enforce bans on forced labour.
USTR is also conducting a second Section 301 tariff investigation into 16 trading partners that show signs of excess industrial capacity. The probe is widely expected to lead to new duties in coming months.
The USTR statement did not name countries that objected to the excess-capacity statement. But China had objected to a similar G20 statement denouncing forced labour and non-market economic policies that lead to excessive exports at a finance leaders' meeting a month ago in North Carolina.
"The draft ministerial statement was supported by all but a handful of members, a few of whom firmly rejected creating this pathway towards cooperative action" on excess capacity, the statement said, adding that this "severely disappointed" the US G20 presidency.
China's excess industrial capacity and industrial subsidies have been key themes of the US-led G20 ministerial meetings so far this year. Beijing has rejected claims that its industrial policies have created excess capacity, accusing Western countries of using the issue to justify protectionist measures.
The US said that G20 trade ministers reached consensus on denouncing the weaponisation of food trade, with members agreeing that trade in food or agricultural inputs should not be used as a tool for economic or political coercion.
In that G20 joint statement, the ministers defined the weaponisation of food as measures to "slow, stop, block or direct the flow of food and agricultural inputs" to exert coercive pressure to extract unrelated geopolitical concessions. "We condemn food weaponisation as it poses a significant humanitarian and economic threat," the G20 trade ministers said.
After pressure from US President Donald Trump that included the threat of a US diesel export ban, the Group of Seven countries on Friday agreed to release some 100 million barrels of diesel reserves to try to drive down record-high US diesel prices. The fuel is widely used in agricultural production.
The US led a pressure campaign on the European Union to draw down emergency diesel inventories, with the Trump administration warning that failure to act could lead to a US ban on diesel exports. Such a ban could sharply reduce supplies to Europe, which has become increasingly reliant on US diesel, and potentially inflict high economic costs on the bloc. Trump is seeking to cool surging fuel prices ahead of the November mid-term elections. Trump told reporters at the White House before departing for Alabama that the US would not impose a diesel export ban. He said the plan was never really on the table, even though in the past two weeks he said several times that such a ban was under consideration, and that he supported the idea.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Thursday that he did not seek a joint statement on a fourth discussion topic, reforming the "most favoured nation" system of published, unconditional global tariff rates that underpin the World Trade Organisation. MFN tariffs have defined the global trading system since the end of World War Two.
Greer has argued that the MFN principle has been abused by non-market-oriented economies such as China that have subsidised industries, but it does not allow these countries to be treated differently. The US statement said some G20 members had expressed a willingness to consider changes to MFN, including expanding exceptions to the principle and issuing new legal interpretations to enable greater use of existing exceptions.

title: Women Chamber aims to boost business growth

content:
Approves new board for strengthening institutional oversight, export promotion
The Faisalabad Women Chamber of Commerce and Industry (FWCCI) has approved the establishment of a board of management to strengthen institutional oversight and accelerate its ongoing and planned initiatives for women's empowerment, business development and export promotion.
FPCCI Vice President Qurrat-ul-Ain, speaking as chief guest at the FWCCI Annual General Meeting, said the proposed board would provide an institutional mechanism for expediting the chamber's projects and future initiatives.
She highlighted FWCCI's progress since its establishment in 2017, particularly the launch of Pakistan's first Women Business Incubation Centre in 2021, which was upgraded into a Women Resource Centre in 2023. In 2024, the chamber established the Pakistan Women Export Facilitation Centre (PWEFC) to help women entrepreneurs access international markets and develop export-oriented businesses.
Qurrat-ul-Ain said efforts were also underway to acquire 100 acres of land at the Faisalabad Industrial Estate Development and Management Company (FIEDMC) for a proposed Women Entrepreneurs Enclave. Separately, efforts were being made to secure two acres at FIEDMC for a dedicated building for PWEFC and FWCCI.
She paid tribute to founding president Rubina Amjad for her contribution to establishing and developing the chamber and urged members to support newly elected President Kanwal Saeed and her team. Outgoing President Shahida Aftab presented an overview of the chamber's achievements during her tenure and thanked the executive committee and members for their cooperation.
Taking charge for the 2026-28 term, Kanwal Saeed said her leadership would focus on addressing internal and external challenges, improving communication with members, strengthening trust and participation, and enhancing financial discipline.
She said the FWCCI should demonstrate clear value to its members by highlighting the opportunities, services and benefits that could stem from active participation rather than relying solely on membership contributions. Newly elected Senior Vice President Samia Tahir and Vice President Dr Sania Arshad also addressed the AGM, while Punjab Provincial Ombudsperson Dr Najma Afzal attended as special guest.
Founding president Rubina Amjad congratulated the newly elected office-bearers and executive committee, while outgoing Vice President Maimoona Imran conducted the AGM proceedings, which were attended by a large number of FWCCI members.

The meeting further considered the Maritime Educational Endowment Fund, aimed at supporting the development of maritime education and human resources. title: PSX below 170k on weak sentiment
description: PSX below 170k on weak sentiment
content:
In turbulent week, benchmark KSE-100 index sheds 2,610 points
The KSE-100 index fell 2,610 points, or 1.5%, during the outgoing week at the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) as geopolitical uncertainty, elevated oil prices and the lack of progress on US-Iran negotiations kept investors cautious.
The benchmark index remained under pressure throughout the week, slipping below the key 170,000 level amid subdued participation. Average daily traded volume declined 22% week-on-week to 525 million shares, while traded value fell 17% to Rs18.7 billion.
Investor sentiment was further dented by a widening trade deficit and higher T-bill yields, although September inflation eased to around 10.3% from 11.1% in August.
On a day-on-day basis, Monday, the first trading day, saw mixed activities, when the KSE-100 slid 340 points (-0.20%) to settle at 170,426. Tuesday was a lacklustre day, with the benchmark index sliding 825 points (-0.48%) to close at 169,600 by breaching the key psychological level of 170k after a gap of seven trading sessions.
Geopolitics tempered sentiment around 170k on Wednesday as the KSE-100 gained 369 points (+0.22%) at 169,969, just below the psychological level of 170k, thereby ending Sept'26 below the milestone. On Thursday, the market endured a volatile and predominantly negative session, resulting in a 1,332-point decline (-0.78%) at 168,636. The bourse culminated the trading week with subdued momentum, declining 481 points (-0.29%) to close at 168,155.
Arif Habib Limited (AHL) noted that the KSE-100 closed at 168,155 points, down 1.5% week-on-week (-2,610 points), as geopolitical uncertainty and the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis dampened hopes of successful negotiations. Among major economic data, Pakistan's crude/POL imports surged 21% year-on-year in Aug'26, driven by a 55% increase in crude oil imports. Meanwhile, local crude production increased 7%. In the latest T-bills' auction, the government raised a total of Rs880 billion, with yields rising for all tenors, in the range of 49.5 to 75 basis points. The majority amount was raised in the three-month tenor, amounting to Rs480 billion.
For Sept'26, tax collection by the FBR improved 9% YoY to Rs1,344 billion, which was Rs1 billion above the target of Rs1,343 billion. This took the quarterly collection to Rs3,066 billion, marking an increase of 7% compared to last year and Rs13 billion above the FBR's target. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) for Sept'26 clocked in at 10.3% YoY compared to 11.1% in Aug'26, AHL said.
Pakistan's liquid foreign exchange reserves position as of October 1 stood at $26.8 billion. Of these, the State Bank-held reserves were $21.4 billion, up $38.9 million, translating into an import cover of 3.04 months. The government increased the National Savings profit rates, effective from Oct'26, by 3 to 19 basis points, with the largest increase of 19 basis points for the Defence Saving Certificates.
Overall refinery supplies surged 32% YoY to 1,084k tons in Sept'26, driven by strong growth across MS, HSD and FO. On a MoM basis, the upliftment improved by 12.5%. OMC sales declined 2% YoY in Sept'26 to 1.35 million tons, amid higher fuel prices. On a MoM basis, OMC sales increased 7%. The Pakistani rupee appreciated marginally by 0.03%, closing at Rs277.07/USD. "Going forward, market direction will once again remain contingent on geopolitical developments, and the ongoing talks between government of Pakistan and the IMF," AHL said. Our top picks include OGDC, PPL, FFC, LUCK, MLCF, NBP, PSO, DGKC, ENGROH, AKBL and NPL.
KSE-100 profitability reached an all-time high of Rs2,031 billion ($7.3 billion) in FY26, reflecting an 18% YoY increase. Banks and E&Ps were the major contributors to the overall profitability.

title: Content creators  influencers seek tax concessions
description: Content creators  influencers seek tax concessions
content:
Digital artists call for fairer regime and review to boost economy
Digital artists, content creators and influencers have called on the government to review the taxation regime applicable to their earnings, arguing that a more balanced tax framework could encourage digital entrepreneurship, attract foreign exchange and create opportunities for emerging talent.
They said earnings from social-media platforms depend on several factors beyond views and subscriber numbers, including audience location, advertising demand, platform policies, production costs and the nature of the content. They maintained that taxation based primarily on gross receipts could place a disproportionate burden on creators, particularly those operating with high production costs or irregular income.
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) introduced a withholding-tax regime on revenues received by digital content creators and social-media influencers from platforms including YouTube, Facebook, Instagram and TikTok. Under Section 154B of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, banks and non-banking financial institutions are required to deduct tax when such revenues are credited or received. FBR has described the measure as part of the government's efforts to bring digital income into the formal tax system.
Sher Muhammad, commonly known as Sher Khumber, a Pakistani music-industry entrepreneur and digital music and rights specialist, said taxation should not become a barrier to the growth of the country's content-creation industry, particularly for artists seeking to build audiences and monetise their work through international digital platforms.
He said the emergence of artificial intelligence was already creating new challenges for the revenue streams of Pakistani artists, particularly in the absence of comprehensive digital-rights protection, while additional taxation could further squeeze the earnings of content creators.
These days, technology kills technology so fast that human talent with cultural and aesthetic aspects could generate unique content for digital creators, who could also promote local culture worldwide, Sher Muhammad added. "Pakistani cultural content, including poetry and music, is receiving appreciation worldwide through social-media platforms. However, many talented artists do not have the technical expertise or resources required to optimise the monetisation of their content," he said.
Muhammad urged the authorities to consider a more supportive tax framework that recognises the costs and challenges associated with producing and monetising digital content. He also said that low tax will help Pakistan's artists to establish digital studios to promote their cultural and local music through social media platforms and video-sharing websites.
FBR introduced a new mechanism for taxing income earned from remunerative social media content, setting a minimum revenue benchmark of Rs195 ($0.70) for every 1,000 YouTube video views and allowing taxpayers to claim expenses of up to 30% of total revenue. The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) notified the rules through SRO 642(I)/2026 and SRO 1641(I)/2026, establishing separate procedures for residents and non-residents earning income through social media platforms.
Dr Noman Ahmed Said, CEO of SI Global Solutions, said content creators should contribute to Pakistan's tax base, but the taxation system should recognise their production costs and irregular income patterns. He noted that withholding tax on social-media platform receipts could be substantial for creators operating on thin margins.
He also called for reconsideration of the 30% expense ceiling contained in FBR's special procedure for taxation of remunerative social-media content. FBR's rules provide for expenses of up to 30% of total revenue in the specified calculation of income.
There is no reliable national average for digital content creators in Pakistan, because earnings are heavily skewed and mostly unreported. Most creators earn little or nothing. Those who monetise typically fall in a wide band.
Salaried content-creator roles in Karachi show a median of about Rs60,000 a month, with a common range of Rs30,000-80,000. Independent creators depend more on brand deals than platform ads. In 2026 rate guides, a nano creator (under 10,000 followers) may charge roughly Rs500 to Rs25,000 per post, a micro creator (10,000-100,000) about Rs5,000-150,000, and larger accounts several hundred thousand to over Rs1 million.
YouTube ad income is thin. Local estimates put 100,000 monthly views at about Rs5,000-20,000 and one million views at Rs50,000-200,000 or more, depending on niche and audience location. Mid-tier creators who combine ads, sponsorships and affiliates often report Rs50,000-400,000 a month. A small top-tier earns far more; the typical creator does not.
"Pakistan should recognise documented business costs, simplify compliance and consider targeted relief for emerging creators," he said. He cautioned that an excessive tax burden could affect investment, employment and foreign-exchange earnings from the digital economy. "However, neither the nationwide tax revenue gain nor the potential economic loss can responsibly be quantified without reliable sector data. FBR should consult creators and other stakeholders and publish an impact assessment," Dr Noman said.
The government seeks to expand the formal tax base while Pakistan's digital economy continues to generate income through international platforms. FBR has also established a Lifestyle Monitoring Cell that uses artificial intelligence and social-media intelligence to identify potential discrepancies between publicly observable lifestyles and declared income and assets.

title: PM aide asks industry to create brands
description: PM aide asks industry to create brands
content:
Govt removing regulatory barriers to enable entrepreneurs to focus on investment & production
Prime Minister's Adviser on Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan has said that Pakistan's textile industry is a key pillar of the country's economic identity and "Made in Pakistan" goods have established their place in global markets. "The country must now expand this position further."
He expressed these views while addressing a ceremony organised by the All Pakistan Textile Processing Mills Association. Haroon Akhtar said Pakistan needed to produce more, produce better and sell more to the world, adding that the country's economic direction should be based on production, exports and private-sector-led growth.
He said the foundation of the National Industrial Policy was being laid on production, investment, productivity and exports. The government's role was not to run businesses but to create an environment in which businesses could succeed. The government would remove regulatory barriers and enable entrepreneurs to focus on investment, production and employment, he added.
Haroon Akhtar said steps were being taken to rationalise tariffs and eliminate unnecessary regulations, while a regulatory guillotine was being used to remove redundant laws and regulations affecting businesses. He said entrepreneurs should focus on investment, innovation and exports instead of permits and complicated procedures.
The textile industry would have to compete globally not only through lower costs but also on the basis of quality, technology, design and sustainability, he said. Pakistan also needed to rapidly shift from exporting raw materials towards finished and value-added products. According to him, Pakistan must create its own brands instead of remaining merely a supplier to global brands. "Pakistan has a complete and integrated textile ecosystem. The real challenge is to create greater value from it," he said.
He stressed the need for investment in modern machinery, technology, skilled human resources and research in Pakistan's textile industry. Competitive energy prices, taxes, refunds, financing and trade facilitation were among the major issues facing the industry, he added.
Haroon Akhtar said investment went where there was confidence and investment took place where there was policy continuity. Businesses needed the assurance that the basic principles of policies would not be changed repeatedly.
The government could establish a framework and open the doors to markets, but the industry had to take advantage of these opportunities, he said. Pakistan needed to move towards industrial transformation through cooperation between the government and industry, he added.
Changes in global supply chains were creating not only challenges but also new opportunities for Pakistan. Global buyers now valued quality, sustainability, traceability and speed, in addition to price, he said.
The adviser added that Pakistan's next textile revolution should be based on productivity, technology and value addition. "When Pakistani cotton goes abroad, it should carry with it the value of Pakistani technology, design, manufacturing and brands," he said.
Pakistan needed to focus not merely on increasing the volume of exports but on creating greater value for the country in every product, he added. "More investment, higher productivity, greater value addition and increased exports should be our industrial goals," Haroon Akhtar said.

title: Govt sets bold DISCO sale deadline
description: Govt sets bold DISCO sale deadline
content:
Tells IMF nine electricity distributors will be privatised by Dec 2027
Pakistan has given an ambitious deadline of December next year to sell its nine power distribution companies that are annually bleeding Rs700 billion, but the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has questioned the model that does not completely stop haemorrhaging even after privatisation.
The government has assured the IMF that it would sell these distribution companies by December 2027, except Quetta Electricity Supply Company, which alone caused Rs154 billion losses in fiscal year 2025.
The government plans to retain most of the past liabilities before the sale and would also continue with the highly uneconomical but politically correct policy of maintaining the same electricity price across the country for both privatised and state-owned entities, according to the sources.
The Privatisation Commission this week briefed the IMF about its plan to sell power distribution companies and its engagement with the prospective buyers. According to the Central Monitoring Unit of the finance ministry, the 10 power distribution companies caused Rs299 billion in losses and another Rs551 billion was given in subsidies during fiscal year 2025. This brings total annual bleeding to Rs850 billion.
The IMF was informed that the government would sell nine power distribution companies by the end of next December, with the first batch of three efficient companies to be sold by March next year. The government was earlier planning to sell these three companies by December this year, but its plan is facing at least a three-month delay.
The privatisation of Faisalabad, Gujranwala and Islamabad power distribution companies was at the due diligence stage, which the government now expects to complete in three months.
The IMF was told that Fesco will be sold in January, Gepco in February and Iesco in March next year. When contacted, the spokesman for the Privatisation Commission confirmed that the IMF has been given the first quarter timeframe to privatise the first batch of three power distribution companies.
The government has planned to sell nine of these entities in four different batches by taking advantage of a healthy momentum created by the sale of Pakistan International Airlines.
According to the spokesman, the second batch, comprising Hyderabad and Sukkur power distribution companies, would be privatised between April and June next year. Another four companies, Peshawar, Hazara, Lahore and Multan power distribution companies, are targeted to be sold by December next year, according to the Privatisation Commission.
However, Quetta, which caused Rs112 billion losses and consumed another Rs54 billion in subsidy in the last fiscal year, is not part of the privatisation plan.
According to the approved privatisation structure, the government will separate land as an asset and the liabilities of pensioners from the balance sheets of Faisalabad, Gujranwala and Islamabad power distribution companies. As of June 2025, the total liabilities of the retired employees of just three companies were equal to Rs312 billion, which may further jump due to the splitting of balance sheets based on March 2026 results.
In June last year, the total assets of these companies were Rs1.2 trillion compared to liabilities of Rs1.05 trillion, showing a total net positive equity of Rs145 billion. The assets and liabilities are planned to be parked in a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV).
The sources said that detailed discussions were also held with the IMF about the government's approved transaction structure, which would not end inefficiencies and the pressure on the budget would also remain even after privatisation.
The IMF also questioned the government about any lessons that it learnt from the controversial privatisation of K-Electric – the country's only privatised entity. Despite privatisation, the government has kept Rs163 billion worth of subsidies in this fiscal year's budget for K-E.
In case the final multi-year tariff of Rs32.37 per unit is implemented, the annual subsidy requirement would come down to around Rs120 billion.
The Privatisation Commission informed the IMF that it would continue the policy of uniform tariff post-privatisation of these entities. However, this negates the purpose of privatisation as the consumers of efficient power distribution companies would still be paying the cost of inefficiency in Quetta, Peshawar and Sukkur.
The spokesman for the Privatisation Commission said that the privatisation transactions are "being structured based on a uniform tariff continuing post-privatisation and the investors (have also been) informed about it".
The IMF also inquired about the implications of carving out the liabilities from the balance sheets of the companies that would be sold. The lender was of the view that this model would not help stop the bleeding. But the Privatisation Commission officials took a stance that, on the same model, PIA had been privatised.
The government had parked Rs673 billion in losses in PIA Holding Company, which jumped to Rs817 billion as of June this year.
The spokesman said that it was "not correct" that the IMF has issues with the proposed privatisation structure that may reduce the bleeding for the government, but it doesn't completely stop the building up of losses.

title: Student protest movement out of control  Paris police chief
description: Student protest movement out of control  Paris police chief
content:
The student protest movement that has spread across France is now "out of control", the Paris police chief said on Saturday, urging demonstrators to return to peaceful action and warning that authorities would respond firmly to violence and vandalism.
Riot police clashed with high school students across France on Friday and unions called for teachers to strike as President Emmanuel Macron's government battled to contain increasingly violent protests over classroom conditions and funding.
Since Monday, around 5,000 people, mostly teenagers, have been arrested nationwide and dozens injured.
Agathe Foucault, a spokesperson for the national police, told RTL radio on Saturday that more than 600 police officers had also been injured.
Teachers and members of the public have been attacked, while damage to property is estimated in the tens of millions of euros.
Paris police chief Patrice Faure, in an open letter published on X ahead of planned renewed protests from next Tuesday, said those who had launched the movement no longer controlled it and called on students to abandon school blockades and unrest in favour of peaceful forms of protest.
"It is time to return to peaceful forms of action," Faure wrote, saying parents also had a responsibility to steer their children away from what he described as the influence of "professional rioters" and their supporters.
Student unions have called for a national day of demonstrations on Tuesday.
Security officials fear that an organised protest in central Paris in particular could see further violence amid concerns that far-left anarchist groups could hijack the movement.
