The couple have travelled, worked together and shared numerous adventures during their marriage
YouTube creators PrestonPlayz and BriannaPlayz are expecting their first baby together after more than eight years of marriage.
The couple, whose real names are Preston and Brianna Arsement, confirmed the pregnancy exclusively to People, revealing that they are expecting their first child in March.
Brianna said she is “beyond thrilled” about the next chapter, adding that she and Preston had been married for more than eight years and were grateful for the time they had spent together before starting a family.
The couple have travelled, worked together and shared numerous adventures during their marriage. Brianna said they had recently begun feeling that “there was a piece missing” and both felt ready to grow their family.
Brianna discovered she was pregnant while her parents and several international guests were staying at their home. She took a pregnancy test one morning before work and decided to wait until later that day to tell Preston.
She then prepared a surprise in their closet, placing baby clothes, a Bible verse and the positive pregnancy test together before revealing the news to her husband.
The couple later told their parents through an elaborate surprise. They told both sets of parents that they were filming a toy unboxing video for Brianna’s YouTube channel. After two ordinary toy unboxings, the third box contained their pregnancy announcement and the baby’s first sonogram.
Brianna said their parents were completely caught off guard and that the reactions were particularly meaningful because they had previously told the couple they had been praying for a grandchild.
Preston and Brianna have not yet found out the sex of their baby. Brianna said they hope to eventually turn the reveal into a video, while Preston believes they are having a boy despite also dreaming that they had a baby girl.
The couple have also started discussing potential names. Brianna said they are considering family and biblical names and want something unique without making it difficult to pronounce.
As they prepare to become parents, Brianna said there is some anxiety because the experience is completely new to them, but she is primarily excited about the future.
“I already feel so in love with this baby we haven’t even met yet,” she told People. “I feel incredibly blessed and grateful.”

title: Bilawal credits PPP for warding off imposition of emergency in K P
description: says govt had decided on emergency  governor   s rule in province  seeks political solution to K P security crisis
content:
Says govt had decided on emergency, governor’s rule in province, seeks political solution to K-P security crisis
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said on Saturday that the federal government had decided to impose emergency or governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, but his party had urged it to first seek a political solution to enable all parties to fight terrorism together.
His remarks came a day after the government and opposition held their first formal talks in years, with the two sides agreeing to continue negotiations on Saturday. The ruling coalition had decided to engage the opposition instead of immediately resorting to emergency or governor’s rule in K-P.
Speaking at an event in Karachi, Bilawal said emergency and governor’s rule were constitutional and legal options that could be used when necessary, but political parties should make every effort to resolve the issue through dialogue before resorting to such measures.
“I understand that the federal government had made up its mind and was ready to immediately impose emergency in Pakhtunkhwa and implement governor’s rule,” he said.

He said the PPP believed that before using such “an atomic bomb” and imposing emergency, political parties should make a comprehensive effort to find a political solution that would enable them to fight terrorism “in a better way”.
Bilawal said terrorism should not be treated as a political issue but as a national one, adding that the government and opposition should work together to counter the threat.
“We don’t want terrorism to be seen as a political issue. We want it to be seen as a national issue,” he said. “Whether you are in the opposition or in the government, we want you to fight it together.”
He said the PPP, the federal government and President Asif Ali Zardari had remained in contact over the past few weeks as terrorist attacks continued in K-P and attacks from Afghanistan also increased.
He also referred to what he described as the role of India in the attacks, saying: “Whether these two attacks are of terrorism or of Afghanistan, whatever is happening, the hand of India behind it is also not a hidden thing.”

Bilawal said the PPP wanted political parties to engage with the PTI and persuade it to end its planned long march on Islamabad.
He said the PTI had the right to protest and had achieved a degree of political success through its protest, but it should also recognise the worsening security situation in K-P.
“While you are focusing on your politics, you are focusing on your protest, terrorism is taking place in Pakhtunkhwa every other day,” he said.
The PPP chairman said a formal written agreement should be reached between the PTI and the federal government under which both sides would work together to fight terrorism.
“If there is a political issue, you should keep it away from terrorism and national interests,” he said, adding that political differences should be dealt with separately from the security situation.
Bilawal said the PPP wanted all political parties to reach an “amicable political solution” in the interest of the provinces and people of Pakistan so that the country did not have to resort to emergency measures to fight terrorism.
“Terrorism is the red line of the Pakistan People’s Party,” he said, adding that the party had lost workers and leaders to terrorism.
He warned that continued deterioration in Balochistan and K-P could have consequences beyond the two provinces, particularly for Karachi.
“Karachi is a mini Pakistan. We are connected to every city, every province,” he said. “If Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa gets sick, Karachi gets a cough.”
Bilawal said the PPP considered terrorism a major issue because any deterioration in the security situation in Balochistan and K-P would eventually affect other parts of the country.
Bilawal’s statement came as the second round of negotiations between the government and opposition continued on Saturday, ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf’s (PTI) planned Oct 4 long march on Islamabad.
Ahead of the negotiations, the government was considering imposing governor’s rule in K-P amid the deteriorating security situation. It had also accused the PTI-led provincial government of poor governance, which it said had contributed to a surge in terrorism in the province.
The possibility of imposing governor’s rule in K-P gained attention after several federal ministers said constitutional provisions allowed such measures if required, while accusing the PTI-led provincial government of failing to address security and governance challenges.
PPP chiarman calls for greater federal support for Karachi
Earlier in his address, the PPP chairman spoke at length about issues confronting Karachi, saying the city had been treated unfairly by the federal government despite its contribution to the national economy.
He said Karachi continued to face shortages of water, electricity and gas, despite Sindh being a major gas-producing province.
“Your Constitution says that the first right is theirs, where this resource is produced,” he said, referring to the province’s claim to its share of natural gas.
He also criticised the federal government over the K-IV water project, saying the Centre had failed to fulfil its commitment to contribute 50 per cent of the project’s cost.
Bilawal said the Sindh government, Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab and the public-private partnership model had provided a way forward for the project.
He also criticised delays in the Hyderabad-Sukkur motorway, saying completion of the project would benefit Karachi and Pakistan’s wider economy.
The PPP chairman praised Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, the Karachi mayor and local representatives for working on the city’s water problems.
“We will continue to listen to all their complaints and criticisms. We will continue to do our work,” he said.

Florence Pugh has opened up about a traditional Māori pōwhiri ceremony that welcomed the cast and crew of Netflix’s East of Eden to New Zealand, describing the experience as “so beautiful”.
Pugh discussed the ceremony while appearing on Late Night with Seth Meyers, recalling how the production began its New Zealand shoot with the traditional welcome.

The actress filmed the seven-part adaptation of John Steinbeck’s 1952 novel at several historic locations in Auckland and the Coromandel Peninsula. The production transformed Heritage New Zealand properties into settings representing early 20th-century California, despite the series being set in the Salinas Valley. 
Filming took place at Alberton and Highwic in Auckland, as well as the Thames School of Mines on the Coromandel Peninsula. Around 150 crew members worked across the locations, making East of Eden the largest production Heritage New Zealand had hosted at the sites.
Heritage New Zealand Auckland properties lead Tanya Wilkinson said the organisation was “delighted and honoured” that the three properties had been selected as locations for the series. She also praised the production team’s professionalism.
Pugh stars in the series as Cathy Ames, the complex central character whose story becomes intertwined with the Trask family across generations. The adaptation was written by Zoe Kazan, with Christopher Abbott playing Adam Trask and Mike Faist portraying Charles Trask.
The series takes a fresh approach to Steinbeck’s novel, with Pugh’s portrayal of Cathy placing greater emphasis on the character’s background and humanity. Pugh has previously spoken about the challenge of playing a character traditionally viewed as one of literature’s major villains.

title: Hurriyat delegation meets AJK president  discusses Kashmir situation
description: AJK president says Kashmir s final settlement should reflect Kashmiri aspirations and UN Security Council resolutions
content:
AJK president says Kashmir's final settlement should reflect Kashmiri aspirations and UN Security Council resolutions
A delegation of the All Parties Hurriyat Conference (APHC), led by Convener Ghulam Muhammad Safi, on Saturday called on President Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Dr Muhammad Najib Khan and discussed the latest situation in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK).
The meeting discussed Indian actions in IIOJK, alleged human rights violations, the situation of Hurriyat leaders and activists, and efforts to highlight the Kashmir issue at the international level.
The AJK president said the Jammu and Kashmir dispute was an internationally recognised issue and its final settlement should be in accordance with the aspirations of the Kashmiri people and relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions, a press release issued here said.
He said the Kashmiri people should be given their right to self-determination to decide their future, and appreciated Pakistan’s political, diplomatic and moral support for the Kashmir cause.
Dr Najib Khan said the unilateral actions of August 5, 2019 could not change the disputed status of Jammu and Kashmir or affect the Kashmiri people’s right to self-determination.
He called upon the international community to take notice of the situation in IIOJK and urged the UN human rights bodies and international observers to be given access to the territory for an impartial assessment of the situation.
The president also called for highlighting alleged human rights violations, arrests of political activists and Hurriyat leaders and restrictions on freedom of expression in IIOJK.
He said the United Nations should fulfill its commitments to the Kashmiri people and urged the international community to press India for implementation of relevant UN resolutions.

Ghulam Muhammad Safi and other Hurriyat leaders congratulated Dr Muhammad Najib Khan on his election as President of AJK and conveyed their best wishes to him.
The APHC convener briefed the AJK president on the latest situation in IIOJK and the challenges faced by Hurriyat leaders and activists.
He said the Hurriyat Conference would continue its political and diplomatic efforts to highlight the Kashmir issue at the global level and advocate the right to self-determination of the Kashmiri people.
The delegation included Muhammad Farooq Rehmani, Mehmood Ahmed Saghar, General Secretary Advocate Pervaiz Ahmed Shah, Syed Faiz Naqshbandi, Sheikh Abdul Mateen, Sheikh Muhammad Yaqoob, Chaudhry Shaheen Iqbal and Information Secretary Imtiaz Wani.
The participants resolved that the political leadership of Pakistan and AJK, the Hurriyat Conference and other stakeholders would continue joint efforts to highlight the Kashmir issue internationally and convey the voice of the Kashmiri people to the world.

State law bans realistic AI intimate images of identifiable people not shown that way in original photos
Elon Musk's xAI on Friday persuaded a US federal appeals court to halt Minnesota's first-in-the-nation ban ​on AI-generated fake nude images as the technology and social media company ‌pursues a lawsuit alleging that the law is unconstitutional.
The St. Louis-based 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals in its order put the law on hold for now, granting a request for an ​injunction by xAI. A lower court judge last month had rejected Musk's bid ​for an order stopping the law.
The state's anti-"nudification" law, which took ⁠effect on August 1, prohibits website operators, software developers and others from allowing users ​to create realistic images depicting an intimate body part that is not shown in ​an original photo of an identifiable individual.
xAI alleges the measure restricts free speech protected by the US Constitution.
Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison's office said in a statement on Friday it is disappointed by ​the appeals court ruling and will defend the new state law as xAI's ​appeal moves forward.

"Minnesota's nudification ban outlaws AI technology products from generating sexual images that harm and harass ‌people ⁠in the vilest way possible," Ellison spokesperson John Stiles said.
xAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
US District Judge Donovan Frank ruled last month that xAI had not shown it would suffer irreparable harm while challenging the law and said the ​company had waited too ​long to seek ⁠emergency relief.
In its appeal, xAI disputed the judge's finding that it delayed bringing suit. The company also said its Grok Imagine tool ​includes "rigorous protections" against creating nudified or sexualized images of real ​people.
xAI has ⁠begun suing users whom it alleges are evading Grok’s technological blockers to create sexual images of people without their consent.
Minnesota had urged the appeals court not to block the law. The ⁠state ​has said it adopted the measure this year to ​combat the spread of what it called a "staggering amount (of) child sexual abuse material that AI products like ​Grok Imagine generate."

description: HyPrSpace is among European startups targeting rising launch demand as falling costs spur plans for satellites
content:
HyPrSpace is among European startups targeting rising launch demand as falling costs spur plans for satellites
HyPrSpace has opened its first mass production factory in France, it said on Thursday, targeting 100 rocket ​engines a year as the French space startup gears up for ‌a planned test flight next year.
HyPrSpace is one of several European space startups seeking to capitalise on growing demand and falling costs of space launches, with governments and commercial ​operators worldwide planning to put thousands of satellites into orbit.
The Bordeaux-based ​company says it could cut those costs further with its Orbital ⁠Baguette One hybrid rocket, which has fewer parts than conventional rockets. Hybrid ​engines have usually been less efficient than fully liquid ones, though HyPrSpace said ​in 2024 that one of its tests had reached an average efficiency of 94%.
France's defence ministry said in September a sub-orbital vehicle would fly in 2027 from a military ​site in what would be a first from mainland France. Two more ​ground tests are required before a flight test.
"Our ambition is to change the paradigm and ‌the ⁠cost of access to space," HyPrSpace CEO Nicolas Billecocq, a former Safran engineer, told Reuters .

till, the company remains a small player in an increasingly crowded European space launch market.
HyPrSpace was not selected in the first round of ​a European Space Agency ​launcher challenge tender, ⁠but Billecocq said the company intended to bid again. The startup's funding is split roughly equally between public and ​private sources, including a €21 million ($24 million) round completed in ​2025.
The new ⁠7,000-square-metre factory near Bordeaux can produce about 100 engines a year, enough for 12 of the company's planned orbital launchers.
Rather than competing with heavy-lift rockets that ⁠deploy ​dozens or even hundreds of satellites at once, ​such as SpaceX or Europe's Ariane , HyPrSpace is targeting customers that seek dedicated access to space, Billecocq said.

title: Apple says it will flag AI requests for Mac data after Meta s Muse draws complaints
description: Apple sandboxes apps on iPhones and iPads  but Macs allow full disk access with user permission
content:
Apple sandboxes apps on iPhones and iPads, but Macs allow full disk access with user permission
Apple said on Friday that it plans to change its Mac operating system to make it more obvious when AI agents ask ​to access all of the data on Macs.
Some users have criticized Meta's ‌Muse, an AI agent capable of carrying out complex tasks like canceling unused subscriptions or haggling for better prices. These people claimed the agent accessed what users believed to be private messages.
On ​Apple's iPhones and iPads, no single app can access data inside another ​app by default, a technique called sandboxing. But Apple's Macs are ⁠more flexible, with a "Full Disk Access" option that allows apps such as cloud ​backup services to access all the data on a machine, with a user's permission.
Apple ​on Friday said some developers were using the Full Disk Access feature in ways that could put users at risk.
"Going forward, we will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely ​wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so ​with very explicit user action," Apple wrote in a post.

title: Hudson Williams  cardigan sends Indigenous designer   s business viral
description: The  350 cardigan was designed by Louis  the founder of Section 35 and the Justin Jacob Louis label
content:
The $350 cardigan was designed by Louis, the founder of Section 35 and the Justin Jacob Louis label
Canadian actor Hudson Williams has helped send Indigenous designer Justin Jacob Louis’ small business viral after wearing one of his cardigans at a New York event.
Louis, who was born in Samson Cree Nation, was away from work with his family on National Day for Truth and Reconciliation when he checked his phone and discovered a sudden surge in sales and social media attention.
“There was, like, a whole bunch of sales and the social media was lighting up,” Louis told CBC News. He said he realised that every cardigan had sold out, with around $12,000 in sales generated within an hour.
The Heated Rivalry star wore Louis’ blue-and-black Journey knit cardigan to the launch event of The Irina Foundation. Williams also wore an orange ribbon marking National Day for Truth and Reconciliation.
For Louis, seeing his work worn by a prominent Canadian actor on the day made the moment particularly meaningful. He said there was “intention and genuine interest” behind Williams’ decision to support his work.
The $350 cardigan was designed by Louis, the founder and creative director of Section 35 and the Justin Jacob Louis label. Williams’ team first contacted the designer by email and Instagram about buying the cardigan just days before the event.
Because there was not enough time to ship the piece from Louis’ warehouse, the designer happened to have the right size at his studio in Chilliwack, B.C. Someone from Williams’ team then drove from Vancouver to the studio on Sunday to collect it.
The actor’s appearance wearing the cardigan had an immediate impact on Louis’ independent business. The brand gained hundreds of new followers throughout the day, while the cardigan sold out and other pieces also began attracting sales.
Louis estimates the shop generated around two to three months’ worth of sales in just two days. Although the brand had not planned to restock the cardigan, the sudden demand prompted Louis to open pre-orders.
“For an independent small business, it helps out so much,” Louis said, describing the experience as a whirlwind.
The Journey cardigan also carries a personal meaning for Louis. He said its design came to him in a dream while he was feeling disconnected and homesick while living around 12 hours away from the community where he grew up.
In the dream, Louis was back at his father’s home, walking across a winter pasture beneath the night sky and thinking about where his ancestors were. He said the stars then appeared to turn into eyes and looked directly at him.
For Louis, the experience became a reminder that his ancestors were always with him, regardless of how far from home he might be.
Williams later messaged Louis directly to thank him for the cardigan. The two have remained in touch, and Louis said he would like to work with the actor again.
For now, the designer remains focused on building his labels and continuing to create work rooted in his culture. He encouraged other designers and small businesses to remain intentional and stay true to their values and cultural identity.
Louis said showcasing the talent, beauty and storytelling within Indigenous communities is what sets their work apart, adding that staying connected to those roots is important.

title: How Chinese robot dancers find their rhythm on American TV show
description: At the finale  27 year old Wu performed with Unitree humanoid robots  blending robotics  ink wash art and modern dance
content:
At the finale, 27-year-old Wu performed with Unitree humanoid robots, blending robotics, ink-wash art and modern dance
A jade pendant bearing a small golden Sanxingdui mask rested against dancer Wu Yufei's chest as he stepped onto the stage of the "America's Got Talent" finale. Commissioned by his wife, this piece of home was by his side as he wowed the audience.
At the finale, 27-year-old Wu, from Sichuan Province in southwestern China, shared the stage with humanoid robots made by Unitree, performing in a fusion of robotics, ink-wash aesthetics, and contemporary stage performance.
"Robots are not merely technological achievements, but can also become creative partners on stage and a new medium for artistic expression," said Fang Zhenghua, the Chengdu choreographer who directed the team's performances.
Wu said their experience in the United States has been genuinely heartwarming. He, along with Fang, showcased not only the advances in humanoid robot technology, but also young people's vision of the future relationship between technology and humanity, adding that audiences are incredibly enthusiastic.
At their audition, Wu performed alongside machines that danced and flipped in time with the music. The act received a unanimous yes from all four judges.
By the September 8 quarterfinals, Wu and the robots were performing martial arts alongside human dancers, kicking and flipping across the stage.
Judge Howie Mandel imagined a martial arts version of the film "I, Robot" and predicted it would be "the most viral moment we're going to have this season." Actress Sofia Vergara pressed her Golden Buzzer, sending the team directly to the Sept. 22 final.
For Wu, however, some of the most memorable exchanges happened away from the machines.
This marked his fourth trip to the United States. He had met a number of American dancers on past trips from the East Coast to the West Coast of the country. They made dance videos together on American streets, capturing times when they moved and played music together.
"Dance is a universal language," he said.
When he made it to the finale, some of those friends reached out on social media to wish him luck. He also received encouraging messages from local viewers he had never met.
Read More: Chinese rocket firm, disease research lab to test space pharmaceutical payloads
"Even though we come from different countries and speak different languages, at that moment they were sincerely wishing me well in the competition," Wu said. "That stayed with me. It felt quite warm."
Wu grew up visiting the Sanxingdui Ruins, a site associated with the ancient Shu Kingdom dating back some 3,000 to 4,500 years. He said visiting the site was "like going to a park." During the contest, he brought one of those familiar faces across the Pacific, jokingly calling it a "mysterious force from the East."
For Fang, inspiration also comes from familiar stories and everyday life. Over the years, his team has incorporated elements like Sichuan opera face-changing, the traditional Chinese composition "A Hundred Birds Paying Homage to the Phoenix," and Three Kingdoms stories into the performances.
For the finale, choreographer Fang wanted to share a Chinese aesthetic that overseas audiences might know less well than kung fu. Water sleeves offered one way to do that, with robots becoming partners in expressing an old art form.
Wu's appearance came in a year when American audiences encountered Chinese creativity in several different settings. In July, Chinese artists joined the Hollywood Film Music Orchestra for a "Black Myth: Wukong" concert in Los Angeles, while Lincoln Center expanded its previous Shanghai Day celebration into Chinese Arts Week. September brought Chinese dance dramas, including "Dream of the Red Chamber," to New York.
On the final stage, flowing sleeves and humanoid robots brought something of China to American viewers, and the friendship had also become part of the story that Wu and his performers would take back home.

Hathaway says welcoming her third child has made this career year especially meaningful for her family
Anne Hathaway has reflected on the lessons she has learned throughout her career, saying she has become more relaxed about her work while navigating an exceptionally busy 2026.
Speaking to CBS Mornings co host Gayle King, Hathaway said she had not expected to have five films released in the same year. She admitted she initially worried audiences might find her constant presence "a little bit" too much, but ultimately decided to embrace the opportunity.
Hathaway said she has learned to "chill out" and become "more open to the fun of it" as her career has progressed. She explained that she now values the feelings and connections created through her work, adding that she wishes she had discovered that perspective earlier in life.
Her latest release, Verity , marks her fifth film of 2026. The psychological thriller, adapted from Colleen Hoover’s bestselling novel, stars Hathaway as author Verity Crawford, who is left incapacitated following an accident. Hathaway said collaboration became especially important because her character spends much of the story unable to move.
The actor also discussed her maternity fashion during a year of back to back promotional appearances. Hathaway credited Rihanna with changing the way she viewed dressing during pregnancy.
"When I saw what she was doing with her maternity style, I just realized that I needed to use my imagination and go out there and have more fun," Hathaway said.
Hathaway is expecting her third child with husband Adam Shulman. The couple are currently focused on enjoying their family of four before welcoming their new baby, which Hathaway said will be a major change for their children.
The actor has embraced a range of maternity looks throughout her 2026 film campaigns, including a Prabal Gurung ensemble that showcased her baby bump and a dramatic black gown worn for the Verity premiere.
With Verity completing her five film releases for the year, Hathaway is entering the final stretch of a particularly busy professional and personal chapter.

The rapper performed her 2021 hit "Get Into It (Yuh)" at Little Caesars Arena on October 1 as part of her TOUR MA VIE WORLD TOUR. The incident comes weeks after Macklemore was removed from the US dates of Sheeran’s LOOP TOUR following his pro Palestinian comments during performances at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on September 4 and 5. Macklemore later said he believed the decision followed pressure from venue owners.
Sheeran subsequently said that removing Macklemore was the promoter’s decision rather than his own. He explained that venues on upcoming dates had indicated they would not host shows if Macklemore remained on the bill. Sheeran said he had attempted to help resolve the dispute but that the promoter and venues ultimately made the decision
Several scheduled opening acts later withdrew from the US tour in solidarity with Macklemore, including Finneas, Lukas Graham and Aaron Rowe, while members of Sheeran’s backing band Beoga also stepped away.

For now, Doja’s altered lyric remains the only apparent connection between her Detroit performance and the dispute. title: Tom Cruise   s  Jack Reacher  franchise ended after creator Lee Child exercised contract veto
description: Child said streaming offered the longer format he felt suited Reacher   s stories better
content:
Child said streaming offered the longer format he felt suited Reacher’s stories better
Tom Cruise’s Jack Reacher movie franchise could have continued beyond two films, but author Lee Child has revealed that he personally used a contractual veto to prevent a third instalment.
Speaking exclusively to Collider ahead of the release of his new novel Chain Reaction , Child explained that his original film agreement, signed in 2005, gave him the right to decide whether the series would continue after two movies. He ultimately exercised that right.
"I had a clause in that movie contract that after two movies I had a veto whether we would do any more. I exercised that veto," Child said.
The first Jack Reacher film, directed by Christopher McQuarrie and starring Cruise in the title role, was released in 2012. It was followed by Jack Reacher: Never Go Back in 2016, with the film franchise ending after the second instalment.
Child said the movies nevertheless had a significant impact on the popularity of his books. He recalled that eight older Reacher novels entered the top 10 paperback list shortly after the first film was released.
However, Child also acknowledged that readers had reservations about Cruise playing Reacher because the actor did not physically resemble the imposing character described in the novels. He said he initially viewed the books and films as separate versions, but later recognised that readers felt differently about the adaptation.
By 2017, Child believed television offered a better format for telling Reacher stories. The shift eventually led to Reacher , the Prime Video series starring Alan Ritchson, whose physical appearance more closely matches the character described in the books.
The series has since become an established franchise. Prime Video has renewed Reacher for a fifth season, while a sixth season was confirmed in September 2026.
Cruise’s two Jack Reacher films therefore remain the only theatrical adaptations featuring the actor, while Child’s character continues on television with Ritchson in the lead role.

content:
A judge limited Berry’s visitation with 12-year-old Maceo pending a court hearing later this month
Halle Berry is facing temporary restrictions on her custody of her 12-year-old son Maceo after her ex-husband Olivier Martinez accused her of physically abusing the child. A Los Angeles County judge granted Martinez a temporary restraining order on October 1, limiting Berry’s visitation while the allegations are considered in court.
According to court documents reported by PEOPLE , Martinez alleged that an incident occurred at Berry’s home on September 26. He claimed Berry physically attacked Maceo, put her hands around his neck and choked him. Martinez also alleged that similar physical incidents had occurred previously, claims that have not been established as facts by the court.
The temporary order applies to Martinez and Maceo and requires Berry to stay 100 yards away from Martinez. Her parenting time with Maceo has been restricted to specified daytime visits, including two weekdays and alternating weekends, until the next hearing. The judge also ordered the former couple to participate in confidential mediation over their custody dispute.
Berry has denied the allegations through her attorney, Marina Beck, who described Martinez’s filing as "entirely meritless and deliberately misleading". Beck said Berry is deeply saddened by the situation and remains focused on Maceo’s best interests.
Martinez had requested stronger restrictions, including changes to their existing custody arrangement and monitoring of Berry’s sobriety. However, the judge denied the request for sobriety monitoring, citing insufficient evidence.
Berry and Martinez married in 2013 and welcomed Maceo that same year. They separated in 2015, and their divorce was finalised in 2023 after years of legal disputes. Their previous custody arrangement provided for joint legal custody.
The latest temporary order is not a final determination of the allegations. A further court hearing is scheduled for October 16, when the custody and restraining order issues are expected to be considered again.

title: High school students in Paris  deprived suburbs spark national protest movement
description: As protests raged at more than 1 200 French high schools this week  police responded with tear gas and rubber bullets
content:
As protests raged at more than 1,200 French high schools this week, police responded with tear gas and rubber bullets
Maisa, a 17-year-old in a poor Paris suburb who aspires to be an English teacher, joined tens of thousands of other students and their supporters this week in protests that spread across France over ​dilapidated schools, classroom overcrowding and teacher shortages.
At Lycee Le Corbusier school in Aubervilliers, a suburb north of Paris in the Seine-Saint-Denis department, protesters said schools in poor ‌neighbourhoods like theirs faced the worst conditions.
“Last year I took the high school French exam without a French teacher, and teachers have a huge impact,” Maisa said.
As protests raged at more than 1,200 French high schools this week, police responded with tear gas and rubber bullets in some cases. More than 5,000 people were arrested, and some protesters were seriously hurt with eye injuries, broken teeth and blows to ​the head. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez called it a "climate of unacceptable violence" and called for order.
French students have blocked schools across the country, demanding more teachers, smaller classes and better-equipped schools. Some protests escalated into clashes with police, while teachers, firefighters and other public workers also demonstrated over funding and resources. pic.twitter.com/eOpPqHF87P
Amelia, 15, joined Maisa in the crowd outside the school gates and held a ​sign reading, "Our address should not decide our future". She said she was demonstrating to demand the same rights as students elsewhere in the country.
"The education ⁠authority is not investing enough in the suburbs. It's classist and racist," she said.
Read: French high school blockades continue as protests spread to universities
Ulysse Rabate, a political scientist at Paris 8 University, said the protests show the way that France's marginalised ​urban neighbourhoods are increasingly influencing national politics.
"When there is a collapse of the public service, of public education, those who feel it the most, and the most violently, are those at the bottom," he ​said.
The nationwide demonstrations and blockades, which began last week, have become a political flashpoint at a sensitive moment for the government, which announced a series of deeply unpopular spending cuts in its 2027 budget on Thursday.
The education budget is set to increase by a below-inflation 1.7% to €65.53 billion, excluding teacher pensions.
The education ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Education Minister Edouard Geffray said that education remained a priority and the ​below-inflation budget increase was due to population decline.
The protests started in the Parisian suburbs, where poverty levels are high, then spread to Paris itself and other French towns, including Marseille, Strasbourg, Tours ​and Lille.
French authorities detained 625 people as high school protests over teacher shortages, class sizes, long schedules and poor conditions escalated into clashes with police. The protests, which began around Paris and spread nationwide, affected 356 schools. At least 83 police and…
At Lycee Le Corbusier, classes including maths, humanities, English and sport have been cancelled since the start of the academic year due to a teacher shortage, according to Karima Kara Ali, an elected parent representative.
In ‌Seine-Saint-Denis, two-thirds ⁠of high schools took part in protests on Thursday, the CGT labour union said. Youth, teachers and parents in four towns complained of unsanitary school conditions and chronic staff shortages, including nurses and social workers.
🇫🇷 ⚠️ French high school students lit fires outside schools and faced off with police on Friday as a protest movement that has forced the closure or disrupted education at more than 560 establishments showed no sign of abating ➡️ https://t.co/iIQtqmkIJE pic.twitter.com/hlggNkhldT
Louise Paternoster, a representative for the Seine-Saint-Denis branch of the CGT's education union, said the area does not get adequate resources for its student population and their educational needs.
Two-thirds of schools in the department have unfilled teacher positions, according to a union survey.
"Our students are losing out on study time. Some schools don't have drinking water. We are not equal to other ​departments," she said, blaming shortages on government cuts ​of 3,256 teacher positions nationwide in 2026.
In ⁠Pantin, a town on the northeastern edge of Paris, teacher Dilan Roche joined her students as they protested outside their school this week to support their demands and protect them from the police.
"What they wrote on banners, we wrote in a letter to the local education authority: overcrowded classes, ​no nurses, no social workers — which is problematic for students with learning difficulties, many living in precarity," she said.
While France ranks in the ​middle of OECD countries for ⁠spending on education, the average expenditure per secondary school student has remained little changed over the last decade, standing at €11,660 in 2024 and €11,910 in 2010, according to education ministry data.
The last nationwide high school protest movement on this scale demanding more funding came in the 1990s. That followed the government sharply expanding access to the baccalauréat, the school-leaving exam that typically paves the way to university, without providing schools ⁠with sufficient additional ​resources, said Professor Clemence Cardon-Quint at Paul Valery University, who researches education funding.
The movement won an increase in funding, but ​spending per student later stagnated despite growing demands on schools.
Cardon-Quint said students and teachers have taken on additional responsibilities over the years, including navigating Parcoursup, the university admissions system introduced in 2018 and criticised by some students and teachers as ​opaque and discriminatory.
"In a period of budgetary restraint, it is more difficult to reduce inequalities," said Cardon-Quint.

title: Sindh CM orders report on killing of five in Ratodero
description: Police said five people  including a passerby  were killed when suspects opened fire at a shop on Jacobabad Road
content:
Police said five people, including a passerby, were killed when suspects opened fire at a shop on Jacobabad Road
Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah on Saturday sought a detailed report from Inspector General of Police Javed Alam Odho over the killing of five people in Ratodero of District Larkana in Sindh.
Earlier in the day, police said five people, including a passerby, were killed when armed men riding a motorcycle opened fire at a shop on the Jacobabad Road in Sindh’s Ratodero. Police further said the incident was linked to an old dispute within the Ghangro tribe.
The chief minister directed the IGP to ensure that those involved in the killings were brought to justice and ordered immediate measures to uphold peace in the area.
CM Shah said the loss of human lives in tribal disputes was “highly regrettable” and prayed for the eternal peace of the deceased. He also conveyed condolences to the bereaved families.
Read: Drug addicts target local infrastructure in Karachi
Following the order of the chief minister, IGP Odho asked Larkana DIG Sheeraz Nazeer to report back on the mass murders.
According to a statement issued by his office, IGP Odho directed that the suspects be arrested without delay and that all available resources be utilised to apprehend them.
He also directed that law and order in the area be maintained at all costs and that effective measures be taken to ensure the protection of citizens’ lives and property.
Meanwhile, Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar also took serious notice of the Ratodero firing incident and sought an immediate and detailed report from the DIG Larkana regarding the incident.
On Saturday morning, gunmen on a motorcycle killed five people in Madeji Kacha area of Ratodero and fled the scene undeterred. Following the incident, a heavy contingent of police reached the area and shifted the bodies to a hospital.
According to police, the deceased were identified as Rajab, Bilawal, Riaz, Qurban Ghanghro and a passerby, Abdullah Brohi.
Police also cordoned off the area and launched a search operation to arrest those involved in the mass murder, claiming that the suspects had been identified.
According to an official statement issued by Larkana Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Azhar Khan Mughal, the incident occurred due to an old feud within the Ghangro tribe.
“The enmity between two groups of Ghangro tribe is long-standing, spanning over 5-7 years. During this period, more than 16 persons from both sides have lost their lives in different incidents of murder and counter-murders,” it stated, adding that the feud was ongoing and both sides were harbouring criminals.
According to SSP Mughal, five persons were nominated as accused in the latest firing incident. The four suspects were identified as Ehsan Ghangro, Bachu Korai, Yaseen Dahani, and Safiullah Dahani, while another unidentified person was also nominated as a suspect.
He further said the suspects were taking shelter in hideouts located in the Kacha area, suspecting that they were shielded by the dens of Long Jatoi and Hafeez Kalhoro.
Highlighting police action taken in the case, SSP Mughal said, Larkana police was put on high alert to “prevent any spillover or retaliatory action in Keti of Larkana”.
He further revealed that the district police, alongside Shikarpur police, have kicked off an operation in Madeji Kacha to apprehend the nominated suspects in the mass murder case.

title: Ben Affleck says dating is not a    big priority    as he addresses Shakira setup rumour
description: Affleck says he is focused on his three children and career at this stage of his life
content:
Affleck says he is focused on his three children and career at this stage of his life
Ben Affleck has offered a candid update on his love life, saying dating is not currently a major focus as he concentrates on his children and work.
Speaking to Entertainment Tonight at the Los Angeles premiere of Animals on October 2, the 54 year old actor and filmmaker said his schedule leaves little room for romance.
"I work a lot and I see my kids," Affleck said. "There’s not a lot of room. I’m not running around." He added that dating is "not a big priority in my life" at the moment.
Affleck also addressed recent speculation involving Shakira after The View co host Ana Navarro said she had considered setting the pair up following his split from Jennifer Lopez. Navarro previously said the idea came to her after seeing Matt Damon, Affleck’s longtime friend, at one of Shakira’s concerts.
When asked about the claim, Affleck said he had never heard about the proposed introduction. He also suggested that rumours surrounding his personal life often reach him through other people.
"I often hear rumours," he said, adding that some things are made up. Affleck also said he does not generally get set up on dates.
The actor described himself as "good" and "happy" with where he is in life. He explained that his children are his main priority, followed by his work, which he said he loves.
Affleck shares three children with former wife Jennifer Garner. Their divorce was finalised in 2018. He later rekindled his relationship with Lopez, whom he married in 2022 before their divorce was finalised in January 2025.
Although Affleck is not actively pursuing a relationship, he has not ruled out romance altogether. He said he is open to whatever adventures life may bring but is not trying to chase anything.
His comments come as he promotes Animals , which he directed, co wrote and stars in alongside Kerry Washington. The thriller is scheduled to arrive on Netflix on October 9.

title: Football finally comes home for one Indian fan
description: India host star studded Brazil for the first time in Kolkata
content:
India host star-studded Brazil for the first time in Kolkata
From Diego Maradona's infamous "Hand of God" to Zinedine Zidane's headbutt, Indian football fan Dipak Nandy has witnessed some of the World Cup's defining moments from the stands.
But on Saturday, the 77-year-old will savour a rare sporting occasion from the comfort of his hometown Kolkata, where Brazil take on his home country in their first-ever international friendly.
Nandy, who has travelled far and wide to attend 11 World Cups, will take in this particular match in front of the television.
Aside from the novelty of welcoming the Selecao to town, he has fond memories of Carlo Ancelotti, the Brazil coach whom he watched as a player for Italy.
Nandy's love affair with the game started in 1966, when Indian former footballer and coach Amal Dutta brought video reels of the World Cup back to Kolkata from England.
"I was sitting in one of the screenings and got bitten by the bug -- and promised myself that one day I will go watch the World Cup," he said.
That remained a distant dream until a friend invited him to Mexico, which hosted the tournament in 1986.
"At that time a passport needed four to five months for processing -- but somehow I got it made in 15 days, and I went for my first World Cup," Nandy said.
He has been to every tournament since, including this year's edition co-hosted by the United States, Mexico and Canada.
Among Nandy's cherished memories are the seven matches involving Argentine legend Diego Maradona, whom he described as a once-in-a-lifetime player.
"He played unbelievable football and played a lone hand in making Argentina champions," he told AFP, his eyes glittering.
"There will be none like him. I walk out of the room when people compare Pele and Maradona."
He was in the crowd when Maradona single-handedly defeated England with two goals in 1986 -- one a blatant handball, the other a glorious run from inside his own half.
Other recollections include the 2006 final in Germany, when France captain Zidane was notoriously sent off for headbutting Marco Materazzi of Italy, who went on to win on penalties.
"I will go to every World Cup till I die -- health and money permitting," said Nandy.
"The amount of money I spent on watching football live, I could have built a huge building, but I don't regret it. Rather, I am proud of it."
Nandy has his own theories about why India, the world's most populous nation, fares so poorly in the sport.
They have never qualified for a World Cup and have only made four appearances at the Olympics, finishing fourth out of 11 teams in 1956.
"The countries that have peaked in football have one single culture with good weather," Nandy said, grumbling about the sport's "weak organisation" and the popularity of cricket.
"India have different religions, food and cultures, and hot and humid weather, which doesn't help the cause."

title: Marquez wins Japanese GP sprint
description: He moves seven points behind leader Jorge Martin
content:
He moves seven points behind leader Jorge Martin
Ducati's Marc Marquez won the Japanese Grand Prix sprint on Saturday to shave five points off Aprilia rider Jorge Martin's lead in the MotoGP championship standings.
Marquez made a scorching start ​and held the inside line on the first turn of the ‌opening lap to surge past Martin, who had set a lap record at the Motegi circuit earlier on Saturday to grab pole position.
Reigning champion Marquez maintained his lead and coasted to victory, moving him to ​306 points - seven behind Martin (313), ahead of Sunday's race.
"The target was ​front row in the qualifying. Starting on first or second was ⁠the best place to do a great sprint race," seven-times world champion Marquez ​said.
"We did a small modification for the sprint race, and I felt much better ​on the bike."
Aprilia's Martin finished second, but was demoted to third behind LCR Honda's Diogo Moreira.
The Spaniard had found it hard going towards the end of the sprint as he was put ​under pressure by Tech3's Enea Bastianini, with the thrilling duel leading both riders ​to stray outside the track.
"I tried in the last lap to do everything I could ‌to keep ⁠Enea behind. I achieved that," Martin said.
"I don't know exactly where I touched (the outside), because I was really focused on not doing it. So, big mistake."
Brazilian Moreira earned his first sprint podium. It was also the first sprint podium for ​satellite team LCR since ​2023.
"Today was the ⁠day. We saw the crash and I said, 'OK, today I will try to push to see'. At the end, lap ​by lap, I was feeling more comfortable with the bike," ​the 22-year-old ⁠said.
KTM's Pedro Acosta, fresh off the first MotoGP victory of his career , started in the front row but quickly found himself in the gravel after being involved in a ⁠three-rider ​crash along with Alex Marquez and Fabio Di ​Giannantonio.
Japan's Ai Ogura (Trackhouse) finished fifth, ahead of Martin's Aprilia teammate Marco Bezzecchi, whose outside bid for the ​championship was dealt another blow.

title: US Muslim group urges White House  Congress to demand release of American teen held by Israel
description: Says Trump administration has legal  moral obligation to protect American citizens overseas
content:
Says Trump administration has legal, moral obligation to protect American citizens overseas
The Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) on Friday called on the White House and Congress to demand the release of Abdalkareem Issa Ahmed Safi, an American teenager held in an Israeli prison for nearly four months without charge.
"It should be unacceptable to the White House and Congress for the Israeli government to continue kidnapping Americans and disappearing them into prisons known for torture , all without any criminal charges or other due process," Nihad Awad, CAIR’s national executive director, said in a statement.
"The Trump administration has a legal and moral obligation to protect American citizens overseas, especially from rogue governments funded by American taxpayer dollars," he added.
Awad urged Congress "to exercise its oversight authority and demand that the State Department secure Abdalkareem's swift and safe release."
Read: US Senate blocks measure demanding report on rights violations in West Bank
CAIR and its chapter in the state of Texas said Safi, a United States citizen with roots in Texas, has been "held hostage in an Israeli prison known for torture for almost four months without facing any criminal charges."
According to a statement from the US-based American Muslims for Palestine, Israeli forces this June raided Safi's family home in Jalazone, north of the city of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank , in the middle of the night.
The group said Safi is the third Palestinian American citizen detained by Israeli forces without charge or trial, alongside Sama Safi and Adam Karakrah.
According to a report by US-based independent news outlet Zeteo , Israeli authorities issued an administrative detention order against him days later, based on information withheld from his lawyer and family. The practice allows Israel to hold detainees without charge or trial.
State Department 'tracking the situation'
Asked about the case, a US State Department spokesman told Anadolu that the department is "aware of reports of an American detained in the West Bank."
"The Trump Administration takes its commitment to assist Americans abroad seriously and we are tracking the situation," the spokesman said.

"When Americans are detained abroad, the Department works on their behalf to obtain access to adequate medical care, proper treatment, and regular consular visits," the spokesman added.
The spokesman said the administration "has no higher priority than the safety and security of Americans," but declined to comment further, citing "privacy and other considerations."

title: Verstappen claims first pole of season
description: He clocks 1 minute 35 130 seconds to edge out Ferrari s Lewis Hamilton
content:
He clocks 1 minute 35.130 seconds to edge out Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton
Red Bull's Max ​Verstappen claimed his first pole position of the season at the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia ‌on Saturday, proving he remains the master of Sepang's challenging circuit nine years after his last victory there.
Verstappen clocked 1 minute 35.130 seconds to edge out Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, who snatched second place in the dying moments of qualifying despite struggling with tyre degradation in the brutal Malaysian heat.
Verstappen's ​team mate Isack Hadjar was third fastest but will start eighth due to a five-place grid penalty, with championship leader Kimi ​Antonelli moved up to third for Mercedes alongside Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.
Verstappen was the last driver to win a ⁠Grand Prix in Malaysia in 2017, in what was his second career victory, before the race was taken off the calendar ​after the government said it could not justify the costs.
Nine years and four championships later, the Dutchman became the first driver this ​season to put a car without a Mercedes engine on pole.
"It's fantastic, we've been trying for many Grands Prix to get more, sometimes a bit closer to the others," said Verstappen as he eyes his first win of the season.
"But to finally get it from where we started the ​season, pretty incredible."
Hamilton, who also has one victory in Sepang, struggled with tyre degradation in practice sessions but ​the veteran Briton said they had now found the right setup.
"It's so hot here, I keep saying it. But that's made it a massive challenge ‌for ⁠the tyres, for the car, for the mechanics in the garage," Hamilton said.
"We made so many changes through all these practice sessions because the cars are sliding, these tyres are overheating. It was really, really hard to find a good balance.
"We made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot."
Hadjar sounded frustrated on the team radio despite finishing ​third fastest and later said he ​expected to go second ⁠quickest to limit the grid penalty as much as possible.
"It's a bit unfortunate we take the penalty on a track that fast," Hadjar said. "But you know, from P8, I'm confident we can ​go through the field and come back for a good result."
Mercedes endured a disappointing ​qualifying session despite ⁠bringing an upgrade package to Malaysia. Antonelli had his first Q2 lap deleted for exceeding track limits, prompting a surprised radio exchange.
"Wait, what? Are we sure about the track limits," he asked before recovering to go second-fastest in the session on fresh soft tyres.
However, he ⁠could barely ​squeeze anything more out of the car in Q3, while teammate George ​Russell - second in the championship - could only manage eighth.
McLaren's reigning champion Lando Norris and team mate Oscar Piastri will start on the third row, and Alpine's ​Pierre Gasly and Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto completed the top 10.

title: Connor Storrie   s  April X  receives mixed reviews as  Heated Rivalry  star leads sci fi thriller
description: April X follows Baxter  played by Storrie  as he searches for his missing twin sister April  portrayed by Lilly Krug
content:
April X follows Baxter, played by Storrie, as he searches for his missing twin sister April, portrayed by Lilly Krug
Connor Storrie’s latest film April X has received mixed reviews from critics, with the Heated Rivalry star leading the futuristic sci-fi thriller in his first major film role since the hit series made him a breakout star.
Directed by Michel K. Parandi, April X follows Baxter, played by Storrie, as he searches for his missing twin sister April, portrayed by Lilly Krug, in a bleak futuristic city. The film was shot before Heated Rivalry premiered and Storrie rose to international attention for his role as Ilya Rozanov in the series.
In April X , Baxter and April are twins living on the fringes of a criminal underworld. While Baxter becomes involved in petty crime, April earns money by making wigs and selling recordings of her vivid dreams. Their lives change when Baxter falls into debt with a local crime boss and April suddenly disappears.
The story then moves five years into the future, where Baxter discovers that versions of April appear to have been cloned and used as sex workers. His search for his sister takes him deeper into a disturbing world involving cloning, human trafficking and exploitation.
Variety's review describes Storrie's performance as capable but argues that the actor has limited material to work with. The review also notes that the film draws from familiar science-fiction influences, including Blade Runner , while attempting to establish its own dystopian world.
Storrie nevertheless takes on much of the film's emotional weight, with Baxter's search for his sister driving the story. The actor also provides hard-boiled voiceover narration throughout the thriller as the character attempts to make sense of April's disappearance.
The film has attracted a range of reactions from critics. Rotten Tomatoes currently lists several reviews praising Storrie's performance, including one from the New York Times that describes him as the film's “saviour”, while other critics have criticised the film's writing, world-building and execution.
April X was released in selected US cinemas on October 2, 2026, following its UK and Irish theatrical release. The film also stars Tudor Chirila, Serban Pavlu and other members of its international cast.
For Storrie, the film arrives at a significant point in his career following the success of Heated Rivalry . While April X was made before his television breakthrough, its release gives audiences an early look at the actor in a leading film role as he moves into the next stage of his career.

title: Pakistan rally to hockey bronze

content:
Green-shirts score four unanswered goals after halftime to beat South Korea 5-3
Pakistan clinched the men’s hockey bronze medal with a 5-3 victory over South Korea at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya on Saturday, staging a remarkable comeback after trailing by two goals at halftime.
The Green-shirts had fallen 3-1 behind at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium but produced a four-goal second-half fightback, keeping South Korea scoreless after the interval.
Sufyan Khan opened the scoring by converting a penalty corner in the first quarter, but Lee Gangsan quickly restored parity for South Korea.
The Koreans then took control in the second quarter. Kim YongBok put South Korea ahead before Yang Jihun converted another penalty corner to give his side a 3-1 lead at halftime.
Pakistan returned from the break with greater urgency and began to turn the contest around. Abdul Rehman pulled one back in the third quarter, reducing the deficit to 3-2 while South Korea struggled to create clear chances.
The decisive turnaround came in the final quarter. Waheed Rana scored twice, including a penalty-corner conversion, to put Pakistan ahead. Hannan Shahid then added another goal as the Green-shirts extended their advantage to 5-3.
South Korea were unable to respond in the closing stages, allowing Pakistan to see out the victory and secure the bronze medal.
Pakistan finished with 57 per cent possession and earned nine penalty corners, compared with five for South Korea.

title: From Sukkur to Houston  Riaz Rafi   s Day and Night finds a global audience
description: Riaz Rafi   s journey takes his Pakistani American art to an international airport and new audiences
content:
Riaz Rafi’s journey takes his Pakistani-American art to an international airport and new audiences.
For years, Riaz Rafi has painted the things that cannot always be put into words. Now, one of his paintings is speaking for him in a place where thousands of people pass through every day.
The Pakistani-American artist’s Day and Night has been selected for display at the International Airport of Houston (IAH), where it will remain for two years. For Rafi, the placement is about more than having his work seen in a busy public space. It is also an opportunity to carry a piece of his Pakistani identity into an international setting.
Silver Streets Artists took to Instagram to share the exciting news, writing that the airport will be featuring Rafi's work, which they termed a project that provides "signature energetic abstract brushwork and rich tonal contrast" and "explores the seamless duality of light and shadow, motion and stillness — a fitting theme for travelers journeying across time zones".
They added, "As part of IAH’s one-year public art program, "Day & Night" will welcome millions of international and domestic visitors passing through Houston over the next 12 months".
“As a Pakistani, I am proud that my painting is displayed at an international airport,” Rafi says. “First, it is to be a Pakistani and also that a work is displayed there and the theme, colours and everything.”
The significance of the setting is not lost on him. An airport is a place of constant movement, where people from different countries and cultures briefly share the same space. Rafi sees that as an opportunity for art to communicate something about the country and culture an artist comes from.
He calls it a country’s “soft image” — an idea he says he had discussed previously on a podcast.
“The soft image which is produced of an image of country, they always show how your country is,” he says. “Your art, culture, music, and dance and all is a reflection of that, so it is a good way to show a soft image of Pakistan.”
That idea is particularly relevant to Day and Night , a work created from the perspective of someone who belongs to two worlds. Rafi is Pakistani by origin and American by residence, and the painting reflects that duality.
Rafi says he is normally reluctant to give his paintings titles. He prefers viewers to arrive at their own interpretations and questions. In this case, however, a title was necessary.
“For the title, I am not keen on just making one,” he says. “I want the viewer to look themselves and see how to understand the painting and raise questions but this was an area where I had to give a title.”
The title itself draws on both Pakistani language and American symbolism.
“In Urdu, we have a saying, ‘Kabhi ke raate bari, kabhi ke din bare’ — some days are long, some nights are long,” he explains. “So here our American flag also has two colours, blue and red, so I kept that in mind when making the creation.”
“Because I am a Pakistani-American artist, I wanted to paint from that point of view.”
The painting will now occupy a very different kind of audience from the galleries and exhibitions where Rafi has shown his work over the decades. He expects travellers from different countries and backgrounds to encounter it, even if only for a few moments.
“This will be in display for two years and whoever travels in those years will see and appreciate the work,” he says.
Rafi’s path to that airport wall has hardly been straightforward.
Born and raised in Sukkur, he developed an interest in drawing as a child. His early years in the city became an important foundation for an artistic career that would eventually take him to Lahore, Karachi and, decades later, Houston.
His formal education in art included the National College of Arts in Lahore and the Karachi School of Art. His journey through the Pakistani art world also brought him into the orbit of influential artists and institutions that would shape his development.
One of the most important figures in his development was Ali Imam, the influential Pakistani artist and gallerist. Rafi worked at the Indus Art Gallery in Karachi and has repeatedly credited Imam and that environment with helping shape his artistic sensibility.
“Ali Imam was one of Pakistan’s people who made us how we are,” Rafi says. “In 1970 he opened Pakistan Indus Gallery which was country’s first modern gallery which created awareness of art and brought it to people’s houses.”
“My real growth happened from Indus Art Gallery.”
He also encountered artists and cultural figures including Firdous Haider and Nighat Chaudhry. His interests were never limited to painting. He learned Kathak from Chaudhry, not as a professional dancer but as another way of understanding movement.
“I am not a professional but I used my art and learning of strokes. I wanted to learn rhythm and continuity through that,” he says.
That sense of rhythm can be found in the way Rafi discusses his paintings. His work has moved between figurative art, abstraction, calligraphy and mixed media, with his influences and interests evolving throughout his career.
But perhaps the most remarkable chapter of his life came when he temporarily lost the ability to speak.
A complicated operation left Rafi without his voice for a period of years. Before that, his artistic life had also crossed into television and acting. The experience of suddenly being unable to speak became another unexpected source of material for his work.
Rafi recalls that during a drama shoot in Hyderabad, he suddenly lost his ability to speak and people thought he was a beggar. He began thinking about what it meant for someone to lower himself completely in order to ask another person for something.
“When I felt that, I left that — a man who is begging for something, he has put himself so low to ask for something,” he says.
“That beggar instinct came as a thought process.”
The experience became a subject for his art.
“From there, the subject came to me,” he says. “That subject came to me because those thoughts always come naturally.”
The loss of his voice gave that instinct for visual communication another dimension. The canvas became a place where he could continue expressing ideas when spoken communication was temporarily unavailable.
There is a certain irony in that history now. A man who once lost his voice is seeing a painting of his speak for him to international travellers.
Rafi says he does not approach the canvas with a rigid blueprint. Instead, ideas accumulate through observation — nature, birds, people, cultural events and the everyday environment around him.
“For planning, when you sit at the canvas there is none,” he says. “But naturally because I get inspiration from nature and birds as well as the culture here and meeting people, there is always something going on.”
“Being here, the thought process is going on and whatever culture event there is, something comes on the canvas on its own. Aesthetically, it is a very strong painting.”
His background in journalism has also remained part of the way he approaches painting.
“My painting usually has a generalist approach. I also have a masters in journalism so there is also that approach in my strokes and colours,” he says.
After coming to the United States in 2013, Rafi says he initially travelled around, visiting museums and galleries before deciding that Houston offered the kind of environment in which he could work with greater calm and freedom.
“I came here in 2013. I actually came from an exhibition and after exploring museums and galleries, I felt that here I could work very calmly and with much freedom,” he says.
Houston also gave him a community in which he could continue exhibiting and developing his practice. His studio is part of the city’s large artist community, where he works alongside hundreds of other creatives.
“The background is that my studio is in my medium district where there are around 200 artists, from which I am but I am one of few South Asians,” he says. “Wherever there are group exhibitions, they ask us for work.”
The city’s airport programme has similarly tried to make its terminals a reflection of Houston’s diversity. In its official calls for artists, the City has described airport art as an opportunity to create memorable first impressions for international travellers and to represent the city’s diverse culture, landscape and ideas.
For Rafi, however, the journey from Pakistan to Houston is not simply about geography. It is about the accumulation of experiences that eventually find their way onto a canvas.
His career has taken him from Sukkur to Karachi, from the galleries of Ali Imam to television, from painting to dance, from a period of silence to a renewed visual language, and now to an international airport where his work will be encountered by people from around the world.
Asked about what comes next, Rafi is reluctant to make grand predictions.
“For future, I can’t say but I believe your work speaks volumes and if it is good and powerful, people will appreciate it,” he says.
He says money, status and displays of material success have never been his motivation.
“I am never on money or showing cars or anything,” he says. “Your work speaks volumes.”
For Rafi, the airport selection is therefore another chapter in a career built less around spectacle than persistence. He sees the opportunity as evidence that the work itself can travel beyond identity, geography and background.
“Because things happened here on merit, they didn’t see I’m South Asian or Pakistani,” he says. “They saw my work over many white artists too.”
“I am not such a big artist but for many years I’ve been doing work with dedication and let’s see where future takes me now. It will only bring more success.”
For an artist whose life has repeatedly crossed boundaries — between Sukkur and Karachi, painting and dance, speech and silence, Pakistan and America — Day and Night may be an especially fitting painting to carry his story forward.
At an international airport, people will arrive and depart beneath its colours. Some may know the artist. Others may know nothing about Pakistan, Sukkur, Ali Imam or the years when Rafi could not speak.
They will simply encounter the painting. And, for Rafi, that is enough.

title: Wrestlers Inayat  Gulzar eliminate at Asian Games
description: Inayat loses to Nurkozha of Kazakhstan  Gulzar suffers defeats in both fights
content:
Inayat loses to Nurkozha of Kazakhstan; Gulzar suffers defeats in both fights
Pakistan ended their wrestling journey in the Asian Games on a disappointing note when their remaining two wrestlers also exited without giving any breakthrough.
Former Youth Olympics bronze medallist Inayat Ullah crashed out of the men’s freestyle 74kg competition after suffering a 12-2 defeat against Kazakhstan’s Nurkozha Kaipanov in the round of 16 in Nagoya.
Inayat showed resistance early but the 2024 Tirana World Championship gold medallist Kaipanov steadily took control, winning the opening period 6-2 before completing the bout with another six points in the second. The Kazakh wrestler secured victory by technical superiority, ending Pakistan’s campaign in the weight category.
Meanwhile Muhammad Gulzar suffered a one-sided defeat against Iran’s Amirali Azarpira in the men’s freestyle 97kg round of 16.
Azarpira dominated from the outset, winning the opening period 6-0 before adding four more points in the second to complete a 10-0 victory by technical superiority.
Gulzar struggled to create scoring opportunities throughout the bout. The Iranian wrestler maintained control and sealed his place in the quarter-finals without conceding a single point.
Gulzar was then given a repechage fight where he ended with a heavy defeat against Turkmenistan’s Shatlyk Hemelyayev.
Gulzar struggled to find a way into the contest as Hemelyayev dominated from the opening exchanges. The Turkmen wrestler collected 12 unanswered points to secure a victory by technical superiority, with Gulzar unable to register a point.
“You know we need more exposure for mat- wrestling development,” Pakistan Wrestling Federation’s (PWF) president Arshad Sattar told The Express Tribune on Saturday.
“Our grapplers are product of mud-wrestling which is their key source of income and you know mat-wrestling is something different and this needs a huge push with the massive assistance of the state. If sate backs us so I hope we will start lifting medals even at the Olympics in the next few years,” Arshad said.
Mohammad Abdullah and Noman Zaka were the other wrestlers who also failed to click on Friday.
Meanwhile Pakistan’s key taekwondo fighter Hamzah Omar Saeed bowed out of the men’s +80kg taekwondo competition after losing 2-0 to Thailand’s Jack Mercer at the Asian Games in Nagoya on Saturday.
Mercer won the opening round 4-2 before extending his advantage in the second, winning 7-5 to secure victory on the final score.
Saeed managed two body-punch points and three points from body kicks, while Mercer also landed a head kick worth three points. The Thai fighter maintained control through the contest
With no Gam-jeom penalties recorded for either athlete, Mercer advanced to the quarter-finals.

title: Pakistan whip China to end 64 year medal wait
description: National volleyballers seal historic victory to secure first bronze in Asian Games since 1962
content:
National volleyballers seal historic victory to secure first bronze in Asian Games since 1962
Pakistan secured the men’s volleyball bronze medal with a commanding 3-0 victory over China at the Asian Games in Nagoya on Saturday.
Pakistan controlled the bronze-medal contest from the opening serve at the Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park Gymnasium, winning 25-18, 25-16, 25-18 in a match that lasted one hour and seven minutes.
China struggled to match Pakistan’s attacking efficiency, while Pakistan maintained pressure throughout all three sets. The winners finished with 75 total points compared with China’s 52 and also benefited from 20 Chinese errors.
Pakistan’s attack proved particularly effective. They converted 46 of 72 spike attempts for a 64 per cent success rate, while China managed 27 successful spikes from 70 attempts, a 39 per cent rate.
Pakistan also dominated at the net, producing 13 block points compared with China’s two. Their defence was similarly stronger, with Pakistan recording 13 digs to China’s nine.
China made 13 opponent errors that contributed to Pakistan’s score, while Pakistan committed 20 errors in the contest.
The first set was closely contested in its early stages before Pakistan established control and closed it out 25-18. They carried that momentum into the second set, opening a decisive advantage and winning 25-16.
China attempted to respond in the third, but Pakistan remained composed and completed the straight-sets victory 25-18.
Pakistan had last time won bronze in the 1962 Asian Games held in Indonesia.
Pakistan had lost their semi-finals against Iran.
In the quarters Pakistan had defeated India 3-0.
In the league stage Pakistan had defeated Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan before losing to Japan to finish second in their group.

title: Court detains Turkey football ref chief
description: Ferhat Gundogdu and six others appear before a judge in graft case
content:
Ferhat Gundogdu and six others appear before a judge in graft case
The head of Turkey's football refereeing body and four others were placed in pre-trial detention by a court as part of a graft investigation, state news agency Anadolu said Saturday.
Ferhat Gundogdu, head of the Central Referees Committee (MHK), and six others appeared before a judge on Friday over allegations of manipulation of the referee administration process.
They appeared before a judge at Istanbul's Caglayan courthouse on several charges, including "official document forgery", "breach of trust" and "illegal acquisition of personal data".
The judge remanded five in custody and granted the other two conditional release, Anadolu said.
It was the latest scandal to shake football in Turkey, coming exactly a year after the Turkish Football Federation (TFF) suspended 149 referees on charges of illegal betting.
On Thursday night, police from the illegal betting and sports crime unit also detained Yasin Kol, a referee from Turkey's top-flight Super Lig, as well as an assistant referee, media reports said.
Justice Minister Akin Gurlek has said prosecutors are examining claims about "interference in the processes of referee classification, assignments, scoring and appointments, as well as the exams on rules".
During Tuesday's raids, police searched the VAR room at TFF's headquarters in Istanbul, with observers saying the investigation was likely linked to last year's betting scandal and would have implications for the federation.
"It does seem to be a continuation of 2025, and it looks like it will continue further," sports journalist Ayhan Sensoy told AFP.
Sensoy, who wrote a 2024 book on the issue called "The Gambling Pit", said it was unlikely federation bosses "have any chance of staying in office".
So far, the TFF has not directly addressed the arrests with its top officials due to fly home on Saturday after attending Friday night's Belgium-Turkey UEFA Nations League clash in Liege, which Turkey lost 3-0.
