title: Tennessee execution survivor Christa Pike unconscious on ventilator  lawyers say
description: Governor halts death penalty for rest of 2026  orders review after state s second botched attempt this year
content:
Governor halts death penalty for rest of 2026, orders review after state's second botched attempt this year
Convicted killer Christa Pike was left gravely ill, unconscious and hospitalised on life support after Tennessee's failed attempt to execute her by lethal injection, her lawyers said on Friday, providing the first detailed account of the injuries she suffered.
Hospital staff were working to save Pike's life and clear the drug pentobarbital from her system, her attorneys said in an emergency motion, which seeks a court order for Tennessee's Department of Correction to preserve evidence from Wednesday night's botched execution.
Pike remained in critical condition, intubated and hooked to a mechanical ventilator to breathe, her lawyers said, after two doses of pentobarbital were administered to her intravenously at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville, the state capital.
The bungled attempt to establish intravenous lines also left both her arms "swollen, burned and blistered," the apparent result of the pentobarbital, a highly alkaline and caustic substance, seeping into the tissues under her skin, the court filing said.
The lawyers accused Correction Department officials of shrugging off prior warnings from Pike's doctors that pre-existing medical conditions — small veins and a blood disorder called thrombocytosis — would make placing IV lines especially difficult.
"At no point did any member of the execution team realise that the IV lines were not correctly placed or that the veins had blown and that the pentobarbital was, in whole or in part, entering Ms Pike's body," her lawyers said in a filing in the Chancery Court for Tennessee's 20th Judicial District.
It said witnesses to the execution attempt could hear Pike "crying, whimpering and breathing loudly throughout the procedure."
The filing provided the fullest picture yet of the medical consequences of an attempted execution that Tennessee Governor Bill Lee said followed the state's established protocol.
It was the state's second botched execution this year, prompting Lee to halt any further attempts to carry out the death penalty for the rest of 2026. He also ordered an independent review of what went wrong.
Read: US judge says he must declare mistrial in Lindsay Clancy trial over killing her children
Pike, 50, was convicted three decades ago of first-degree murder for her role in the torture and killing of a 19-year-old vocational school classmate, Colleen Slemmer, at the University of Tennessee campus in Knoxville in 1995, when Pike was 18.
She had been scheduled to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than two centuries, and the only person in the modern era of US capital punishment to be executed in that state for a crime committed by a teenager.
Pike's then-17-year-old boyfriend was tried as an adult and convicted of murder as well, but received a life sentence with eligibility for parole. A third schoolmate who was 18 at the time and acted as a lookout for the two others ended up testifying for the prosecution and received probation.
Lee earlier this week rejected a clemency petition seeking to commute Pike's death penalty to a life prison term without the possibility of parole. The petition argued for leniency, in part, on the basis of her childhood history of severe neglect, sexual abuse that included two rapes, and untreated mental illness.
The clemency petition also cited evidence that Pike's mother drank heavily during pregnancy, contributing to faulty brain development that made it difficult for her to control her impulses.
The US Supreme Court on Wednesday lifted an 11th-hour stay of execution, which was issued earlier in the day by a federal appeals court to give more time to weigh Pike's claim that her childhood trauma was not properly considered in her sentencing.
In their filing on Friday, Pike's lawyers urged the state Chancery Court to order preservation of evidence they said would show that state prison personnel violated her constitutional rights by subjecting her to cruel and unusual punishment.

South African youngster rewrites T20 record book as Titans crush Knights by 124 runs
South Africa’s Lhuan-dre Pretorius smashed the highest individual score in men’s Twenty20 cricket on Saturday, powering the Titans to a 124-run victory over the Knights in the CSA T20 Challenge.
The 20-year-old opener struck an unbeaten 188 from just 79 deliveries, launching 13 sixes and 15 fours as the Titans piled up 267-3 at Mangaung Oval.
Pretorius surpassed the previous record of 175 set by West Indies great Chris Gayle for Royal Challengers Bangalore against Pune Warriors in the 2013 Indian Premier League.
His remarkable innings featured relentless acceleration. Pretorius reached his half-century from 24 balls before needing only another 16 deliveries to bring up his century. He raced to 150 in just 58 balls and finished with a staggering strike rate of 237.97.
The performance was another landmark for a player who has already represented South Africa in 17 T20 internationals, three one-day internationals and two Tests.
With Pretorius setting the platform, the Titans produced an imposing total before their bowlers completed the rout. The Knights were dismissed for 143, leaving the hosts with a comprehensive victory.
Pretorius’s innings not only secured the Titans a commanding win but also placed his name at the top of the men’s T20 individual scoring list, eclipsing a record that had stood for more than a decade.

title: Pakistan summons Indian envoy over killing of two Pakistanis along international border
description: Foreign Office says Pakistan  categorically rejects any attempt to mischaracterise the deceased as  infiltrators
content:
Foreign Office categorically rejects India's attempt to 'mischaracterise' civilians as 'infiltrators'
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) on Saturday summoned the Indian Chargé d’Affaires and lodged a strong protest over the killing of two Pakistani civilians by personnel of the Indian Border Security Force (BSF) in the Bedian Sector along the International Border on Friday.
"The BSF personnel resorted to unprovoked lethal force against unarmed civilians. Such use of force was wholly unjustified and grossly disproportionate, resulting in the tragic loss of two precious lives. Pakistan categorically rejects any attempt to mischaracterise the deceased as 'infiltrators," said a statement issued by MoFA.
The statement came a day after two Pakistani civilians were killed , and another was injured after Indian BSF personnel opened fire near the Pakistan-India international border in Kasur. The incident reportedly occurred when three residents from Ladhar village moved a few steps beyond a border pillar, upon which BSF personnel opened fire on the men without warning.
According to MoFA, the incident amounted to a serious violation of fundamental human rights, including the right to life, and raised concerns over the protection of civilians under international law.
🔊PR No.2️⃣7️⃣2️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Indian Chargé d’Affaires Summoned Over Killing of Two Pakistani Civilians 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/7o9A1UvrLF
It noted that "the Indian side was called upon to conduct an immediate, transparent and credible investigation into the incident, take appropriate disciplinary and legal action against those found responsible, and formally communicate the findings and action taken to the Government of Pakistan."
Further, it added that "India was further urged to ensure respect for fundamental human rights and international law, strictly observe relevant bilateral arrangements and established border procedures, exercise maximum restraint in dealing with such situations, and take effective measures to prevent the recurrence of such incidents."
The civilian killings were reported after Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry uncovered an Indian “false flag operation”. He rejected Indian claims that a former Pakistan Army soldier had been killed as a Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorist in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK), presenting the individual alive before the media and describing the episode as another Indian “false flag operation”.
Civilian casualties and injuries inflicted by Indian forces during 2016-2026
Cross-border firing along the Pakistan-India border has repeatedly resulted in civilian casualties, particularly in villages close to the Working Boundary.
In October 2016, the military’s media wing confirmed that two civilians, including a toddler, were martyred and another seven were injured in firing in the Harpal, Pukhlian and Charwah sectors.
In September 2017 , the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said India had targeted Pakistani civilians with mortars and automatic weapons, resulting in the death of Muhammad Zahoor, a civilian in Dewra village.
The following year saw another major escalation. In May 2018, The Express Tribune reported that four members of the same family — a woman, two daughters and a son — were killed in firing along the Working Boundary near Sialkot, with 10 others reported injured. The report cited the ISPR and the Foreign Office. The death toll climbed to 16 during a wider six-day confrontation.
Read: Pakistan issues 'strong demarche' to US over 'irresponsible' remarks by ambassador in India on IIOJK status
A year later in October, the Foreign Office said a 10-year-old boy was martyred , and 16 civilians were critically injured in firing in the Sharda sector.
In May 2020, three civilians were reported seriously injured in the Nikial sector, while in September, two civilians were reported seriously injured in the Baroh sector. Both reports cited Pakistan's Foreign Office.
In 2021, at least seven people were injured, including two elderly persons and a teenager, in cross-border shooting. The situation changed for the better after Islamabad and New Delhi reaffirmed their ceasefire in February.
Once again in 2023, however, The Express Tribune reported three civilian deaths and one serious injury in two LoC firing incidents.
2024 remained peaceful, a year after a war broke out between the nuclear-armed rivals.

title: Flydubai co pilot attacked pilot with axe  attempted  terrorist attack   UAE says
description: While Emirati authorities have not publicly identified the co pilot  Israeli officials have claimed    he is Omani
content:
While Emirati authorities have not publicly identified the co-pilot, Israeli officials have claimed ​he is Omani
The co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073 , which was bound for Israel, attempted to carry ‌out a "terrorist attack" during the flight, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general said on Saturday, according to the state news agency WAM .
The co-pilot was identified as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national, a source with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters . A second source briefed on the investigation confirmed the co-pilot’s name. UAE authorities did not immediately ​respond to a request to confirm his identity.
While Emirati authorities have not publicly identified the co-pilot, Israeli officials have previously claimed ​he is an Omani national. Oman has not commented on the incident.
"Investigations into the incident involving flydubai flight ⁠FZ1073 found that the co-pilot had attempted to carry out a terrorist attack," WAM quoted UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi as ​saying.
The co-pilot attacked the pilot inside the cockpit with a crash axe and attempted to take control of the aircraft, the prosecutor general said.
A crash ​axe is typically kept in the cockpit for use during emergencies such as crashes.
Investigations are ongoing to determine the circumstances of the incident, the motives and any related connections, as well as to examine physical and digital evidence, he added. The UAE is leading the investigation. Dubai's government owns the airline.
Read: UAE attorney general orders investigation into Flydubai flight incident
The UAE prosecutor ​general's comments were the first by Emirati authorities to describe the incident as an attempted terrorist attack.
Disaster was averted on Wednesday after passengers and ​crew subdued the co-pilot, who had attacked the captain in what Israeli officials said was an apparent attempt to crash the plane carrying more than 170 ‌passengers and ⁠crew.
A reserve flydubai pilot travelling on the flight took control of the aircraft and landed it at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, where the co-pilot was detained by Saudi authorities.
The captain and co-pilot left Saudi Arabia for Abu Dhabi on Thursday morning after receiving medical clearance, the Saudi Interior Ministry said.
Flydubai said the circumstances surrounding the incident were still under investigation and that it was not in a position to comment ​further, a spokesperson said.
A source briefed ​on the investigation told Reuters on ⁠Friday that Israeli officials were expected to question the co-pilot in the UAE. The source declined to say which Israeli agency or authority would take part.
An Israeli government official told Reuters that Israeli investigators would take ​part alongside Emirati authorities in the UAE-led investigation, seeking to determine what happened and examine the suspect's ​motives and background.
Read more: Trump vows to attack Iran 'very hard' if Tehran behind Flydubai flight incident
Israeli Prime ⁠Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Friday that Israel was looking into whether the co-pilot had acted under anyone's direction, warning that anyone involved would pay a "heavy price".
Netanyahu claimed without providing details on Thursday that the co-pilot had undergone "radical Islamist indoctrination" and appeared suicidal. He then stated that a motive had not ⁠yet been ​established. Most of the passengers on board were Israeli nationals.
The aircraft dropped about 16,625 ​feet in just over 30 seconds while flying over Saudi Arabia on its journey from the UAE to Israel, according to flight-tracking data from Flightradar24. The route is popular among ​Israeli travellers.

Islamabad says territory's final status remained unresolved as diplomatic exchange resurfaces at UN
"Pakistan categorically rejects India's futile attempts to dismiss the Jammu and Kashmir dispute as a so-called internal matter," Gohar said, according to remarks shared by Pakistan's Permanent Mission to the UN.

He maintained that Kashmir was an internationally recognised disputed territory whose final status had yet to be determined in accordance with the wishes of its people and relevant UN Security Council resolutions.
Gohar accused India of failing to meet what Pakistan considers its international obligations under those resolutions and urged New Delhi to move towards a peaceful settlement of the longstanding dispute.
The Pakistani representative also highlighted human rights violations and discrimination against religious minorities in India, citing Muslims, Christians, Sikhs and other communities.

Gohar added Pakistan remained committed to dialogue, diplomacy and the peaceful settlement of disputes in accordance with the UN Charter , arguing that such an approach was necessary for peace and stability in South Asia.
The exchange came as the General Assembly's Third Committee began its work for the 81st session. The committee deals with social, humanitarian and cultural matters, including human rights, racial discrimination, refugees and the right of peoples to self-determination.
Kashmir has remained a source of contention between Pakistan and India since the partition of British India in 1947. Both countries control parts of the Himalayan region and claim it in full, with their respective territories separated largely by the Line of Control.

Islamabad reiterated its position ahead of this year's UN General Assembly session, saying in September that the Kashmir dispute remained unresolved and that its final disposition should be determined in accordance with relevant Security Council resolutions and the wishes of the Kashmiri people.
Pakistan's latest remarks mark a continuation of the diplomatic exchange seen during the UNGA high-level week. On September 25, Pakistani Counsellor Saima Saleem also used a right of reply to reject India's position on Kashmir after comments by an Indian delegate.

title: AI s race to transform the world before the money runs out
description: Economists see little evidence yet of productivity gains as spending on AI dwarfs railway  internet sums
content:
Economists see little evidence yet of productivity gains as spending on AI dwarfs railway, internet sums
Never has so much cash flowed into a new technology as is pouring into AI, eclipsing the sums splurged on railways or the internet when those technological revolutions sucked in capital.
Cumulative spending globally on data centres alone could top $30 trillion by 2050, according to a projection by PwC, almost matching the value of outstanding United States Treasuries. It "dwarfs" what was spent in the railroad or dotcom booms, even after adjusting for inflation, PwC said.
Meanwhile, Anthropic, just one of the major firms in the AI race , plans to spend $518 billion in coming years, according to the IPO prospectus seen by Reuters , which is more than 100 times its 2025 revenue.
Read: Trump tells AI bosses to self-regulate
Its backers say AI technology will be more transformational than the advent of steam engines and the industrialisation they powered.
Yet lurking behind the dizzying projections and huge outlays by AI companies, alongside sky-high valuations, lie assumptions about vast broad-based productivity gains and future profits with little evidence so far - or historical precedent - to be sure they can deliver, economists say.
JP Morgan wrote in August that broad-based productivity gains in the US, which leads the AI race, "remain elusive", raising questions about the sustainability of AI valuations.
A Bain and Company study said productivity gains from existing markets would not be enough to justify current outlays and "entirely new markets must emerge to close the funding gap", suggesting those could range from using AI-guided robots to developing new materials for batteries and semiconductors.
US hyperscalers - the companies rolling out infrastructure around the world like Google, Amazon and Microsoft - and others in the AI race needed to find more than $4.2 trillion of new revenue in the next five years to fund the buildout, Bain said.
"The question is whether the applications arrive in time to pay for it," according to the study, published last month.
Few doubt the potential of AI to transform everything from work in an office to research labs, just as past revolutions shrank journey times from days to hours or connected the world at the touch of a keyboard.
Read More: Financing of historic AI buildout raises systemic risks in US, researcher says
What seems more immutable is the maths behind securing a return on investment or the deadlines for repaying loans, leaving economists to work out the implications for the global economy beyond the ups and downs of investment cycles.
"Historical precedent suggests that technology-driven booms often end when infrastructure buildouts cease to deliver sufficient returns," JP Morgan wrote.
Using the example of Nvidia , the US company whose chips are the backbone of the AI revolution, JP Morgan estimated US productivity gains would need to be 3% to 5% annually over the next 10 years to justify its valuation. That would be a substantial increase from the baseline expectation of the US Congressional Budget Office of 1.75% annual productivity growth for that period.
For the US alone - which according to some estimates accounts for about three quarters of the global AI investment total - investment will run as high as about $9 trillion from 2025 to 2032, equivalent to spending 3.2% of US GDP each year, according to Columbia Business School economist Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh.
He estimates the US AI sector would need to generate about $3.55 trillion in annual revenue by 2032 to earn a 10% return on investment. It earns a fraction of that now.
The leveraged structure of much of the debt funding AI infrastructure also means "a relatively modest deterioration in demand, delays, or asset values can therefore produce much larger losses," he wrote in a conference paper, revised in October.
The dizzying numbers have not stopped US AI bosses speaking with an otherworldly zeal about changes afoot.
Anthropic's Dario Amodei has said an AI future could be "a thing of transcendent beauty", while OpenAI's Sam Altman has said "the rate of new wonders being achieved will be immense" as models learn to improve themselves and accelerate breakthroughs.
Jasjeet Sekhon, chief strategy officer at Google DeepMind , told a summit at UC Berkeley in August that this self-teaching, known as recursive self-improvement, was a "key part of the investment thesis", and that it could, if achieved, deliver unprecedented productivity gains.
Recursive self-improvement, while potentially delivering exponential AI advances, has also raised concerns about existential risks to humanity . Yet the pace of change in productivity might still end up lagging the timelines needed by corporate accounts departments.
Diane Coyle, an economist at Britain's Cambridge University, said the productivity impact of past revolutionary technologies had usually taken about 10 to 50 years to feed through.
Anthropic's economics team modeled a range of scenarios for how much extra growth AI would deliver at an annual rate in 2030. Assuming a baseline of 2% in a non-AI environment, it suggested growth of 2.4% in a scenario with modest AI impact, 5.4% in a substantial scenario and 15.4% in an extreme scenario.
Higher growth would mean more jobs lost , it said, without assigning probabilities for any of the outcomes.
Also Read: Bill Gates warns AI is powerful enough to 'cause a billion deaths'
Amodei forecast last year that AI could wipe out half of all entry-level white-collar jobs within five years. For now, however, some researchers say it appears to have been limited to making it harder for those seeking office work to find a job.
Studies in the US and Britain have pointed to a slowdown in early career hiring for white-collar positions performing tasks at which AI is adept, even if overall employment remains strong.
Researchers at Stanford University said in August that employment of workers aged 22 to 25 in AI-exposed industries, such as accountants and paralegals, was 19% lower than for jobs that AI found hard to replicate, like janitors and builders.
Yet even if the promised transformation takes longer than numbers surrounding AI companies imply, real economic benefits should stay - just as trains still ran after the Panic of 1873 that bankrupted railroad barons, while the internet didn't shut down after the 1990s dotcom bubble burst.
"History is our friend in trying to understand this," said Coyle. "As long as one is left with the infrastructure that's needed to support all the productivity effects down the road, that's okay." ​

title: Yemen sees widest escalation in 3 weeks as displacement nears 200 000
description: At least 100 children recruited by Houthi rebels killed in September  according to Human Rights Ministry
content:
At least 100 children recruited by Houthi rebels killed in September, according to Human Rights Ministry
Yemen witnessed its widest military escalation in three weeks in recent hours between government forces and the Houthi group, as the displacement crisis caused by the fighting continued to worsen.
Clashes were concentrated in the southwestern provinces of Taiz and Lahej, marking the most intense escalation since Sept. 10, when the Houthis took control of the strategic city of Mokha, according to Anadolu’s monitoring.
Amid the escalation on the ground, the number of people displaced since military operations intensified in July approached 198,000, according to government data.
The army said on Thursday that it foiled a major Houthi attack on several fronts in Taiz and Lahej, while carrying out airstrikes on the group’s positions and vehicles.
Read: Trump's national security team holds unannounced Camp David talks on Iran war, Yemen: Axios
“The armed forces’ warplanes carried out six airstrikes on positions and vehicles belonging to the Houthi militia,” the army’s Tor Al-Baha military axis said in a statement, noting that forces “thwarted a large-scale Houthi attack on all fronts of the Tor Al-Baha axis and eliminated all its attacking formations.”
The strikes targeted positions “on the Al-Akboush, Al-Ahkoum and Hayfan fronts south of Taiz province,” it added, without providing details.
The Tor Al-Baha axis operates in Taiz and Lahej provinces, according to an Anadolu correspondent.
The Taiz military axis said in a statement that army forces “are engaged in fierce battles in the Bani Bakari area of Jabal Habashi district, the Himyar front in Maqbanah district in western Taiz, and the Al-Aqroud front in the southeast of the province.”
It added that army forces “inflicted casualties and equipment losses on the Houthi militia,” without providing details.
In a separate development, a military source told Anadolu that government forces foiled a Houthi attack on the Sharie area in the Sama’a district, southeast of Taiz.
The source, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the Houthis attacked the area, but resistance forces thwarted the assault, resulting in deaths and injuries on both sides.
Read more: Saudis plan assault on Houthis to break Red Sea chokehold
The attack was the first launched by the Houthis on the district since 2014, according to Anadolu’s monitoring.
Yemen’s Executive Unit for Internally Displaced Persons Camps Management said on Thursday that the number of people displaced by the escalation since July had risen to nearly 198,000.
The government unit said that “waves of forced displacement caused by the continued military escalation, direct shelling and deteriorating security conditions have worsened, posing serious threats to the lives and safety of civilians.”
It said the number of people registered as displaced since the military escalation resumed in July stood at 29,519 families, comprising 197,906 people.
Taiz topped the list of provinces hosting displaced people, with 13,925 families comprising 97,529 people distributed in 15 districts.
Lahej ranked second, hosting 7,179 families with 50,253 people in nine districts, most arriving from conflict areas in Taiz and Al-Hudaydah.
The temporary capital, Aden, received 3,741 families comprising 17,782 people, while Abyan recorded 2,097 families with 14,679 people.
In Al-Hudaydah, 1,471 families comprising 10,297 people were registered in the districts of Hays and Al-Khokha, with indications of secondary displacement toward Aden, according to the statement.
Yemen’s Human Rights Ministry warned Wednesday of the growing presence of children recruited by the Houthis amid the latest military escalation.
The ministry said it documented the deaths of at least 100 children recruited by the Houthis during fighting in September, based on names, information and photographs it was able to obtain following their deaths.
It stressed that the figure does not represent the total number of recruited or killed children, but only a limited number of cases it was able to identify and verify, adding that field information indicated the actual number was much higher.
Also read: Yemeni government forces seize strategic mountain overlooking Bab el-Mandeb: Official
It also said it had documented cases of children being abducted or recruited in several provinces under Houthi control before being transferred to mobilisation camps and deployed to battlefronts, and later returned to their families as bodies.
In a related development, the government filed a complaint with the UN Security Council, warning of “a serious Houthi threat to the safety of civil aviation.”
It came in a letter sent by the government to the council that was published early Thursday by the Foreign Ministry and Expatriates.
The government warned of “a serious threat to the safety and security of international civil aviation over the southern Red Sea, due to the use by the Houthi terrorist militia of Iranian-origin weapons launched from areas under its control in Al-Hudaydah province toward international air routes.”
The government urged the Security Council “to take urgent international action to confront this threat and enforce the arms embargo imposed on the militia.”
It said the weapons “use heat-tracking systems that track heat sources without distinguishing between military and civilian targets.”
It warned that “launching these weapons near international air routes poses a direct and serious threat to civilian aircraft and their passengers, including UN and humanitarian flights operating in Yemen and the region.”
The complaint came one day after military escalation between government forces and the Houthis on several fronts, including Taiz, Lahej, Marib, Al-Jawf and Al-Bayda, alongside the army’s announcement that it carried out hundreds of strikes against the group’s positions and members.
The Houthis, meanwhile, reported dozens of airstrikes and missile attacks on areas under their control.
The escalation coincided on Wednesday with a military meeting in Aden to discuss strengthening readiness and implementing directives from Presidential Leadership Council Chairman Rashad Al-Alimi on general mobilisation.
Saudi Arabia also announced on Wednesday its full support for the government in extending its authority in the country and restoring stability.
The developments are part of the escalation that began in early July and is considered the widest since the relative calm that followed an April 2022 truce.
Fighting intensified in September, leading to the Houthis seizing several vital areas in Al-Hudaydah and Taiz provinces, including Mokha, and eventually Mayyun Island overlooking the international Bab al-Mandeb maritime strait.
Yemen has been mired in conflict since the Houthis seized the national capital, Sanaa, and several provinces in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in 2015 in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government.

title: Trump says US to send one time  90 payment to 20 million seniors enrolled in Medicare
description: US president s latest financial promise comes as Republicans defend narrow majorities ahead of midterms
content:
US president's latest financial promise comes as Republicans defend narrow majorities ahead of midterms
President Donald Trump said the United States government will send a one-time $90 payment to more than 20 million Americans enrolled in Medicare, a health insurance programme for the elderly, to help offset the cost of their monthly medical insurance premiums.
Trump said on social media late on Friday the payments will come from the Medicare Improvement Fund, which he said was given $2 billion by Congress to improve the Medicare fee-for-service programme.
The announcement is the latest in a series of financial promises the Republican leader has made to voters heading into the November midterm elections where control of Congress is at stake.
Read: US Republicans seek voter relief before midterm elections
Trump's Republican Party currently has a narrow majority in both the Senate and the House of Representatives but his approval rating has been low over his handling of the high cost of living for Americans during the US-Israeli war on Iran that has spiked oil and gas prices.
The White House released some details of Trump's plan on its website, saying most eligible seniors will receive the payment in the form of a direct deposit of $90 in early October. Those without direct deposit will receive a check, also sent in early October, to the mailing address they have registered with Medicare, the White House said.
Read More: Trump government ads draw scrutiny weeks before midterm elections
Last month, Trump proposed sending $5,000 checks to all adult citizens if ⁠the Republicans keep control of the House and Senate in the midterms, though analysts, economists and even some Republicans in Congress reacted with skepticism to the plan.
The Trump administration is also separately sending $500 payments to nearly 1 million Americans in a move that strategists say could potentially influence some election races.
The White House says those payments were a refund for what it describes as excessive fees charged to people ‌who purchased health insurance through the Affordable Care Act.

The two sides exchanged views on measures aimed at providing the people of AJK with speedy, effective and accessible justice, along with the importance of strengthening the judicial system and improving the delivery of justice in accordance with constitutional principles.
Justice Khan briefed the president on matters relating to the role of the judiciary in AJK and issues of constitutional significance. Matters concerning public interest and other issues of mutual interest were also discussed.
Both parties stressed the importance of constitutional institutions performing their respective responsibilities while maintaining institutional respect and cooperation in the region. They also covered matters relating to public interest and the broader role of constitutional institutions in ensuring effective governance, protection of rights, and access to justice.

The meeting came shortly after Dr Khan assumed the office of president of AJK. The president, as head of state, and the chief justice of the SC occupy key positions within the constitutional framework of the region.
The meeting concluded with an exchange of good wishes and a commitment to continue working within the constitutional framework for the welfare of the people of AJK.

title: Security forces kill 11 terrorists in separate Balochistan  K P operations
description: Naqvi praises security forces for their successful operations  against terrorists  in Balochistan and K P
content:
Naqvi praises security forces for their successful operations against terrorists in Balochistan and K-P
Security forces killed 11 terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan and Fitna al-Khawarij in separate operations in Balochistan and Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) under Operation Radd-ul-Fitna 3 and the Azm-e-Istehkam vision, state media reported on Saturday.
The federal government last year officially designated all terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as Fitna al-Hindustan , accusing India of sponsoring a proxy war through the outfits.
Fitna al - Khawarij is the term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
According to the sources, six terrorists of Fitna al-Hindustan were killed during an operation in the Gorander area of Mashkel, Balochistan.
The terrorists opened fire on a security check post in Mashkel and attempted to flee, but security forces responded promptly and eliminated all six terrorists, the sources said.
سیکیورٹی فورسز کی آپریشن ردالفتنہ3 کے تحت فتنہ الہندوستان کیخلاف مؤثر کارروائیاں جاری بلوچستان کےعلاقے گورندر،ماشکیل میں سیکیورٹی فورسز کی کارروائی،6دہشت گرد جہنم واصل ، سیکیورٹی ذرائع فتنہ الہندوستان کے دہشت گردوں نے ماشکیل میں سیکیورٹی چیک پوسٹ پر فائرنگ کے بعد فرار ہونے کی… pic.twitter.com/IzLafcgzna
In another intelligence-based operation in South Waziristan, K-P, security forces killed five terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij , the sources said.
The terrorists’ hideouts were also destroyed during the successful operation, while a large quantity of weapons and ammunition was also recovered from the killed terrorists, the sources added.
Security forces remain determined to completely eradicate the menace of terrorism from the country and establish lasting peace under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision, the sources said
Five terrorists of #FitnaAlKhawarij have been killed during an intelligence-based operation in #SouthWaziristan @OfficialDGISPR #RadioPakistan #News https://t.co/T4p281FpCE pic.twitter.com/Oi5Dfav5Fg
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi praised the security forces for their successful operations against terrorists in Balochistan and K-P. He lauded the professional capabilities of the security forces for foiling the nefarious designs of the terrorists.
Naqvi said, “Security forces killed five terrorists in South Waziristan, and six terrorists were also brought to a terrible end in Mashkel, Balochistan."
“The nation is proud of the brave sons of the security forces,” he added.
Naqvi said the entire nation stands shoulder to shoulder with the security forces in the war against terrorism and “With the support of the nation, the menace of terrorism will be completely eliminated,” he added.
Read: 49 terrorists killed in Balochistan, K-P IBOs
Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terrorist activity over the past three months, with a series of attacks across the country resulting in the martyrdom of security personnel and civilians.
Last week, 12 people were killed and 35 others injured when a blast struck a joint checkpoint near Aman Mela in the Darazinda area of Dera Ismail Khan, with the TTP claiming responsibility for the attack.
On September 19, 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred in a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, the Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
In a separate incident, a captain and a lieutenant were among six security personnel martyred in an exchange of fire in Hangu district, while eight terrorists were killed.
On September 1, six personnel, including two officers, and a customs department official were martyred as security forces thwarted an attempt to breach the Customs House in Balochistan.
Read more : Nine policemen martyred, 28 injured in terror attack on police checkpost in K-P's Hangu
In July, at least 30 people , including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. The attackers also abducted several civilians and police personnel after the assault.
In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation , which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

title: Hasan Nawaz   s 96 goes in vain as India beat Pakistan to claim Asian Games gold
description: Abhishek Sharma   s blistering 61 and Tilak Varma   s unbeaten 51 power India past 200 after Pakistan strike back at Korogi Sports Park
content:
Chasing 212, India restrict the Green-shirts to 192-6 to retain the title
India defeated Pakistan by 19 runs in the final of the 2026 Asian Games men's cricket competition on Saturday to claim the gold medal after Pakistan fell short despite a superb unbeaten 96 from Hasan Nawaz.
Chasing 212 for victory at Korogi Sports Park, Pakistan finished on 192-6 after a promising start gave way to a middle-order collapse.
Sahibzada Farhan and Maaz Sadaqat put Pakistan on course with an opening stand of 33 before India's spin attack struck in successive overs.
Washington Sundar dismissed Pakistan captain Farhan for 10 from 11 balls, with the opener hitting one boundary, before Axar Patel removed wicketkeeper-batter Usman Khan for three from six deliveries.
Pakistan were 36-2 after 4.5 overs and Axar struck again soon afterwards, dismissing Maaz for a valuable 23 from 18 balls. The left-hander hit three boundaries as Pakistan slipped to 39-3 after 6.1 overs.
Saim Ayub and Hasan Nawaz then launched Pakistan's recovery, putting together an 87-run fourth-wicket partnership that revived their hopes of chasing down India's imposing total.
Nawaz continued his impressive tournament with another aggressive innings and reached his third T20I half-century.
But India's bowlers regained control when Shivam Dube dismissed Saim for 29 from 22 balls. His innings included two fours and a six.
Pakistan were five down when Sundar claimed his second wicket, removing Abdul Samad for nine from 12 balls, leaving the score at 162-5 after 17.3 overs.
Pakistan required 33 runs from the final over, leaving them with a difficult task, and could manage only 192-6 at the end of their 20 overs.
Nawaz remained unbeaten on a magnificent 96 from 51 balls, striking five fours and seven sixes, but his effort was not enough to deny India the gold medal.
For India, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar and Shivam Dube took two wickets each to restrict Pakistan and secure the 19-run victory.
Earlier, India opted to bat first and made a fast start as openers Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Abhishek Sharma attacked Pakistan's bowlers from the outset.
Saim Ayub provided Pakistan with an early breakthrough when he dismissed Sooryavanshi with the first delivery of the third over, ending a 28-run opening stand. Sooryavanshi scored 15 from nine balls, including two boundaries.
Abhishek continued his aggressive assault, helping India race past 50 in the fourth over before Pakistan struck again.
Ahmed Daniyal removed Sanju Samson for two from four balls, leaving India 51-2 after 3.5 overs.
The left-hander remained undeterred and brought up his 13th T20I half-century in emphatic fashion before Arafat Minhas finally ended his charge.
Abhishek was dismissed for a blistering 61 from just 28 balls, with his innings featuring three fours and seven sixes.
Shreyas Iyer and Ishan Kishan then rebuilt the innings, adding 35 for the fourth wicket as India moved beyond the 100-run mark.
Minhas broke the partnership by dismissing Kishan for 20 from 18 balls, including three boundaries, leaving India 128-4 after 13.1 overs.
Pakistan then claimed the important wicket of India captain Iyer, with Abrar Ahmed removing him for 21 from 24 deliveries. Iyer struck two boundaries.
Shivam Dube provided the next burst of acceleration, hitting two boundaries as India moved beyond 150 in the 17th over.
Tilak Varma then took control of the closing overs, smashing consecutive sixes against Sufiyan Muqeem in the 18th over before continuing his assault.
Daniyal struck with the first delivery of the final over to dismiss Dube for 27 from 15 balls, including two fours and two sixes.
But Varma finished strongly, hitting another six to take India past 200 before completing his half-century with another maximum.
He remained unbeaten on 51 from 22 balls, with three fours and four sixes, as India closed on 211-6.
Daniyal and Minhas claimed two wickets each for Pakistan, while Abrar and Saim took one apiece.

title: Broadcasting rights for Pakistan   s home matches sold for Rs350 million
description: The latest agreement includes 25 matches     five Tests  14 ODIs and six T20Is
content:
The latest agreement includes 25 matches – five Tests, 14 ODIs and six T20Is
The broadcasting rights for Pakistan’s home matches have been sold for Rs350 million, with only bidder state broadcaster emerging as the successful. The reserve price had been set at Rs600 million, while the latest agreement covers 25 matches.
According to details, the PCB had issued a tender a few days ago for the broadcasting rights to its home matches, with a reserve price of Rs600 million. PTV, the sole bidder, has now acquired the rights. At present, three major broadcasters have significant outstanding payments owed to the cricket board. Although they were not barred from participating in the bidding process, they chose not to take part. A company that has acquired most of Pakistan cricket’s rights in the past also showed no interest.
The national team’s recent poor performances, along with limited public interest in the matches against Ireland and Sri Lanka, were among the reasons for the lack of participation in the bidding process. This time, the PCB also did not allow consortiums to participate. A similar restriction has already been imposed in the Pakistan Super League.
The latest agreement includes 25 matches: five Tests, 14 ODIs and six T20Is. Pakistan are scheduled to play three T20Is against Sri Lanka this month, followed by a seven-match triangular ODI series involving England. Two Tests against Sri Lanka are scheduled for next month.
In January 2027, Pakistan are scheduled to play three T20Is against Ireland, followed by another seven-match triangular ODI series involving Zimbabwe. In February, Pakistan are due to play a one-off Test against Ireland. In February and March, New Zealand are scheduled to play two Test matches in Pakistan.
According to some reports, Zimbabwe have declined to tour Pakistan for commercial reasons, meaning the triangular ODI series may not take place. Similarly, the one-off Test against Ireland may also be cancelled. However, the PCB has yet to officially confirm these developments.

title: France held by Italy
description: Olise scores a stunning goal from a free kick to give home side the lead
content:
Olise scores a stunning goal from a free-kick to give home side the lead
Michael Olise scored another superb goal but France were held to a 1-1 draw by Italy on Friday in Zinedine Zidane's first home game since being appointed coach of Les Bleus.
Four days after coming off the bench to score a stunning solo effort to give France a 1-0 win in Belgium, Bayern Munich star Olise again showcased his spectacular talent by smashing a shot in off the crossbar from a free-kick early in the second half.
However, Inter Milan defender Alessandro Bastoni equalised for Italy midway through the second half to prevent Zidane from making it three wins out of three in charge of his country.
France, who had defender Dayot Upamecano sent off late on, lead UEFA Nations League Group A1 with seven points, with Belgium just behind on six points after a 3-0 win over Turkey.
France and Belgium meet on Monday in their last match of this two-week long international window. Italy have four points before hosting Turkey next.
Zidane was the focus of attention as his home debut, before a packed crowd of 77,118 at the Stade de France just outside Paris, came against the same opponents as in his final game as a player.
The now 54-year-old icon and former Ballon d'Or winner never played again after being sent off for an infamous headbutt on Marco Materazzi in the 2006 World Cup final in Berlin, which Italy won on penalties.
It was a first appearance for the former Real Madrid playmaker at France's national stadium since he played in a friendly against Mexico in May 2006, winning his 100th cap in the process.
"It was magnificent. We would have liked to win for our fans tonight but I was obviously really touched and delighted to be back at the Stade de France," he said.
Beyond the spotlight on his past, Zidane is trying to stamp his mark on the France team in this Nations League campaign, with one eye on the next major tournament, Euro 2028.
"I am happy with the performance albeit not with the result. We had chances to score a second goal and we didn't do it. But I am really proud of my players."
He was again without captain Kylian Mbappe here with the Real striker having returned to his club after suffering a knee injury while scoring the winner in Turkey last week.
Olise returned to the starting line-up in one of six changes from the Belgium game, but new faces Jeremy Jacquet, the Liverpool defender, and Como midfielder Lucas Da Cunha again played.
Italy are rebuilding under Roberto Mancini, who has returned for a second spell as coach of a nation who have failed to qualify for the last three World Cups.
They will be the happier of the two teams with the draw in this game, although they had goalkeeper and captain Gianluigi Donnarumma to thank for keeping them in it with a host of saves in the second half.
"I think this was a great performance tonight against one of the best teams in the world, with very positive aspects to it," said Mancini.
"We are on the right road, and we need to keep playing this way."
Moise Kean should actually have given Italy an early lead after a sweeping move, only for his disappointing finish to be saved by Mike Maigan.
Davide Frattesi also came close in the first half while Kean had a goal disallowed for offside, as an Olise cross which landed on the bar was as close as France came.
The hosts turned up the volume after the break and Donnarumma saved from Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Olise before the latter crashed in the opener on 55 minutes when Rayan Cherki laid off a dead ball.
However, Bastoni caught Da Cunha in possession just outside the France box and was left with an easy finish to pull the visitors level.
Donnarumma, formerly of Paris Saint-Germain, then produced more magic to save from Adrien Rabiot and twice from Eduardo Camavinga, before Upamecano walked for a second yellow on 85 minutes.

title: Pakistan envoy to US briefs University of Hartford students on diplomacy  peacebuilding
description: Ambassador Sheikh interacted with the students individually  responding to their comments and questions
content:
Ambassador Sheikh interacted with the students individually, responding to their comments and questions
A delegation of students from the Master of Arts in International Peacebuilding (MAP) programme at the University of Hartford visited the Embassy of Pakistan in Washington, DC, for an interactive discussion on diplomacy, peacebuilding, conflict resolution and Pakistan’s role in advancing regional and international peace.
According to a press release issued by the embassy, the delegation was led by Phoebe Milliken, Director of the Master of Arts in International Peacebuilding programme, and Hina Athar Khan, Assistant Director of the programme. The international student cohort included participants from Albania, Ghana, Indonesia, Lebanon and the United States, with professional backgrounds spanning UN peacekeeping, interfaith harmony, public policy, community-building and nonprofit leadership, the statement added.
Welcoming the delegation, Pakistan’s Ambassador to the United States Rizwan Saeed Sheikh briefed the students on Pakistan’s diplomatic priorities, with particular emphasis on the country’s longstanding commitment to peace, dialogue and conflict resolution.
He also highlighted Pakistan’s continued partnership with the United States across multiple facets and underscored the ascendant significance of further strengthening the eight-decade-long Pakistan-US relationship, the statement added.
“Peace is something that is of interest to us, and that has got to do with our genesis as a nation state carved out of a subcontinent. Owing distinct identity to the religion that signifies peace by its name, we were born with the intent of peace, with the aspiration to peace, and that is what we have strived for both within and without,” Ambassador Sheikh said.
Reflecting on Pakistan’s diplomatic history, the ambassador highlighted the country’s role in facilitating dialogue among major powers and recalled Pakistan’s contribution to the historic rapprochement between the United States and China in the early 1970s.
Read: Kashmir Committee chairman, Pakistan envoy to US call for peaceful resolution of Kashmir dispute
“When we brought the two top economies of today, the US and China, together in 1971, we made a sterling contribution to global peace as evidenced by the last week’s Summit featuring the US and Chinese leadership in Washington,” he said.
The ambassador also discussed Pakistan’s recent mediation efforts between the United States and Iran and the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, emphasising the value of quiet, sustained and effective diplomacy geared to conflict resolution in its pristine form.
He said Pakistan continued to facilitate diplomatic engagement under the Islamabad MoU framework as a trusted and successful mediator.
“Our consistent quest for peace has dictated our diplomatic effort, as evidenced by our role in peace-making, peace-keeping, and peace-building for almost eight decades now. Our urge for peace is an integral part of our national history. In the current role of trying to resolve one of the most consequential crises in modern times, our leadership has approached the matter with both a sense of history as well as a sense of responsibility, being the mediator trusted by the two sides,” Ambassador Sheikh added.
Earlier, Milliken briefed participants on the University of Hartford’s Master of Arts in International Peacebuilding programme and its emphasis on scholarship, dialogue and practical approaches to peacebuilding.
She highlighted that the programme equipped students with practical skills in dialogue, mediation, reconciliation and constructive community engagement alongside their academic studies, the statement stated.
Read more: Pakistan envoy presents credentials to Dominican president, pledges stronger bilateral ties
Against the backdrop of Pakistan’s recent mediation efforts in the US-Iran conflict, the visit provided students an opportunity to gain first-hand insights into the practice of diplomacy, mediation and peacebuilding and to learn more about Pakistan’s approach to conflict resolution.
During the discussion, the students showed keen interest in Pakistan’s diplomatic engagement on the international stage and exchanged views with the ambassador on mediation, peacebuilding and contemporary global challenges.
They also used the opportunity to learn about Pakistan’s geography, politics, economics and diplomacy through the lens of the country’s current role in facilitating constructive dialogue between the United States and Iran, the statement said.

title: War on Iran could end soon  US president
description: US Iran war  Yemen Houthi Saudi conflict
content:
Trump's national security team holds unannounced Camp David talks on Iran war, Yemen: Axios
US President Donald Trump, speaking at a rally in Alabama, said the war on Iran could end soon, while questioning whom Washington could negotiate with in Tehran and insisting Iran must never obtain a nuclear weapon, according to Al Jazeera .
US President Donald Trump, speaking at a rally in Alabama, said the war o Iran could end soon, while questioning whom Washington could negotiate with in Tehran and insisting Iran must never obtain a nuclear weapon. 🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/EktrJfQaND pic.twitter.com/JIDWcujih5
"I don't know who the hell to deal with. There's nobody to deal with. Nobody wants to be president. I say, who do I speak to in Iran? ...Knock knock, nobody home."
Yemeni army carries out 71 operations against Houthi positions in country's southwest
The Yemeni army announced on Saturday that it had carried out 71 operations targeting Houthi positions in Yemen's southwestern province of Taiz.
"Our armed forces carried out 71 precise targeting operations against combat gatherings, military buildups, and reinforcements belonging to the terrorist Houthi militia" in Taiz, army spokesman Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nuzaili said in a statement on US social media company X.
Yemeni forces conducted 71 precision strikes, destroying Houthi vehicles and reinforcements across ten Taiz areas, including "neutralisation of militia members," Yemeni army spokesman Majed Abdullah al-Nuzaili says Follow our live coverage 👇 https://t.co/engl6Ithuv pic.twitter.com/9lLL0cUlJh
Al-Nuzaili said the operations focused on the areas of al-Aqrood, Sama’, al-Ahkum, al-Akboush, Jabal Rasin, Jabal Jardad, Bani Omar, Bani Bakari, al-Kaawash, and al-Athawir.
The operations "resulted in the destruction of a number of hostile transport and support vehicles, the neutralisation of militia members, and the stripping of their formations of the ability to continue fighting," he added, without specifying the number of casualties.
The Houthi group did not comment on the statement.
The developments come amid a military escalation in Taiz Governorate between government forces and the Houthi group.
Iran executes detainee over January protests, judiciary says
Iran has executed a man detained during protests in January for allegedly firing at police, the judiciary said on Saturday.
The judiciary said Siavash Jamshidi Kheirabadi fired at least three shots at police on January 8 and was arrested two days later with a handgun in Shahrekord in southwestern Iran.
It accused him of contacting people online to organise "anti-security" activities and seeking payment for a "mission", without identifying who was purported to be behind it.
The protests erupted on December 28, 2025, over economic hardship and swelled into widespread foreign-aided demonstrations calling for the end of clerical rule in the Islamic Republic.
Iran blamed armed groups and operatives backed by the US and Israel for involvement in the protests and for the violence.
Israeli Heritage Minister Amichai Eliyahu acknowledged during the protests that Israel had operatives inside Iran. He said they aimed to weaken Iran's capabilities, though he denied they were directly working to topple the leadership.
Trump's national security team holds unannounced Camp David talks on Iran war, Yemen: Axios
Trump's senior national security officials gathered on Friday at Camp David for closed-door discussions on the Iran war and the Saudi-Houthi conflict in Yemen, Axios reported.
Citing three American officials, Axios said Vice President JD Vance presided over the undisclosed meeting, which ran for hours. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, special envoy Steve Witkoff, CIA chief John Ratcliffe and Joint Chiefs Chairman General Dan Caine also took part.
One official said issues were settled or discussed at length.
With talks stalled, Trump is weighing a return to large-scale combat operations against Iran. The Pentagon, according to the Wall Street Journal , is preparing to send a third aircraft carrier strike group and additional Marine ships to the Middle East, adding up to 10,000 troops.
Read: Saudis plan assault on Houthis to break Red Sea chokehold
The WSJ , citing US officials, said the forces are expected to arrive by the end of November.
Trump earlier said he could resume strikes on Iran after the midterm elections in early November if no deal is reached.
Meanwhile, Riyadh is urging Washington to join airstrikes on the Houthis, the rebel group fighting government forces in Yemen since 2014, ahead of a planned offensive. Trump has been reluctant, though officials said he could reverse course.
Iraq cleric Ammar al-Hakim urges reopening of airports for Iran flights
Senior Iraqi cleric Ammar al-Hakim calls for the reopening of all airports to flights between Iran and Iraq, expressing solidarity with Iran and its people in facing economic pressure, according to Press TV .
Senior Iraqi cleric Ammar al-Hakim calls for the reopening of all airports to flights between Iran and Iraq, expressing solidarity with Iran and its people in facing economic pressures. Follow: https://t.co/GHI09iAGh2 pic.twitter.com/Iw14Q2g7Cd
Flight delays, cancellations reported at Riyadh airport amid missile attacks
Flights at Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport were disrupted by delays and cancellations, while explosions were reported in Saudi Arabia’s Asir region following reported ballistic missile attacks, according to Iranian state media.
Houthi projectile hits school in Saudi Arabia's Najran: Civil Defence
A projectile launched by Yemen's Houthi group struck a school in Saudi Arabia's southern city of Najran on Friday, causing material damage, the Saudi Press Agency (SPA) reported, citing a Civil Defence spokesman.
The spokesman said that emergency teams responded after a "hostile projectile" launched by the Houthis fell in the area, according to the news agency.
He said the projectile hit a school in Najran, causing material damage.

Standard procedures for such incidents had been carried out, he added.
Earlier, the Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen's internationally recognised government said it intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis toward the southern Saudi city of Khamis Mushait.
Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition supporting Yemen's internationally recognised government against the Houthis since March 2015.
The group has controlled the capital Sanaa and several provinces since September 2014.
Crude oil tanker struck by unknown projectile off Oman, UKMTO says
The master of a crude oil tanker has reported being struck by an unknown projectile 4 nautical miles east of Oman, ⁠the United Kingdom ​Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said early on Saturday.
UKMTO WARNING 149-26 Click here to view the full warning.⤵️ https://t.co/4vjKc1kTda #MaritimeSecurity #MarSec pic.twitter.com/wJUAcPtJBU
UKMTO said all crew were reported safe and no environmental impact was currently reported.
Russia rebukes US call for Iran to abandon ‘inalienable right’ to nuclear program
Russia’s ambassador to the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has dismissed Washington’s call for Iran to abandon its nuclear program, stressing that Tehran has an “inalienable right” to pursue it, according to Press TV .
In a post on X on Friday, Mikhail Ulyanov slammed the US for relying on “wrong assumptions” about nuclear non-proliferation.
Apparently the #US Ambassador doesn’t know that #Iran is not obliged to abandon its nuclear programme. It is Iran’s inalienable right. Unfortunately the position of the Republican administration is based on wrong assumptions of non-proliferation norms and the IAEA activities. https://t.co/65gvETlQWW
“Iran is not obliged to abandon its nuclear program. It is Iran’s inalienable right,” Ulyanov said.
“Unfortunately, the position of the Republican administration is based on wrong assumptions of non-proliferation norms and the IAEA activities,” he said.
Ulyanov was responding to US Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz, who claimed that Iran had “broken the rules” and was enriching uranium to 60% with “no credible civilian purpose.”
Iran has maintained a consistent position regarding its peaceful nuclear program since the unprovoked US-Israeli wars of aggression in June 2025 and early 2026.

title: Makkah alliance calls emergency meeting
description: Makkah alliance calls emergency meeting
content:
Pact members meet in Riyadh next week amid Houthi attacks
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye have agreed to convene an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh next week as the alliance confronts escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and a growing diplomatic push to contain the crisis.
At a news conference, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Friday that the meeting would assess the "ground reality" and discuss the situation facing Saudi Arabia, particularly following attacks on civilian and economic infrastructure and the recent strike on a power facility in Madinah.
The development marks the latest step in the rapid institutionalisation of the three-way defence arrangement signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye on August 7, under which an armed attack against one member is to be treated as an attack against all three.
The emergency SPDC meeting comes less than two weeks after the three foreign ministers met on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on September 24. Dar, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan discussed the implementation of the agreement and agreed to convene an urgent meeting of the three countries' military chiefs.
The military chiefs subsequently met in Riyadh on September 25, reviewing threats facing Saudi Arabia and discussing intelligence sharing, military coordination and greater integration of defence capabilities. They reaffirmed their commitment to collective defence and to translating the Makkah agreement into practical military cooperation.
The alliance's political and military response has gained urgency following a series of attacks attributed by Saudi Arabia to Yemen's Houthis, including an attack on a power distribution station in Madinah.
Pakistan on Friday strongly condemned the attack and reaffirmed its support for Saudi Arabia's sovereignty and the security of the Two Holy Mosques.
The Houthis have denied responsibility for the Madinah attack.
Dar also disclosed a new diplomatic dimension to the crisis, saying Iran was distancing itself from the Houthis and Iraqi armed groups.
According to Dar, he had discussed the issue with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, who suggested that the groups should be engaged politically rather than targeted militarily.
Dar said Araghchi had conveyed that Iran wanted the matter resolved, while Pakistan had made clear that it was now part of a defence agreement and, "as Muslims", would honour its commitments.
The Iranian proposal, however, does not amount to a formal offer at this stage. Dar described it as an exchange of views between the two foreign ministers and said the question of whether political engagement could replace military action would be considered by the SPDC.
The issue is likely to add another layer to Pakistan's already delicate balancing act between its commitments to Saudi Arabia under the new defence pact and its longstanding policy of maintaining dialogue with neighbouring Iran.
Pakistan has repeatedly advocated diplomacy and de-escalation even as it has publicly condemned attacks on Saudi territory. Dar spoke with Araghchi on September 19, with the two ministers discussing regional developments, energy supplies and the safe passage of shipping.
The emergency meeting will also come as the alliance moves towards establishing a permanent institutional structure.
The first SPDC meeting was held in Istanbul on August 31, bringing together the foreign and defence ministers and military chiefs of the three countries. The meeting agreed to establish a permanent secretariat in Saudi Arabia, initially headed by a Pakistani secretary general for three years.
The agreement also envisages defence-industry cooperation, joint technology development and production.
Retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood was subsequently appointed as the first secretary general, with the secretariat to be established in Riyadh.
Dar told reporters that more than six countries had expressed interest in joining the Makkah agreement. However, he indicated that membership would not be considered until the alliance's secretariat and institutional mechanisms were fully operational.
He also stressed that the agreement was defensive in nature and contained no offensive objective, while allowing other countries to join. The document itself, he said, is open to other countries provided they agree to the principles laid down by its three founders.
He added that any decision on membership would be taken jointly by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, and Pakistan could not decide alone.
He said the prime minister also highlighted terrorism emanating from Afghanistan and the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, and credited Field Marshal Asim Munir, Chief of Defence Forces, for his role in the US-Iran mediation process.
Dar said the country had played a full role in strengthening multilateralism during the United Nations Security Council presidency as a resolution Pakistan moved on multilateralism and peaceful settlement of disputes last year, was adopted unanimously for the first time in 12 years, he said.
On the US-Iran talks, he said that Pakistan had brought the two sides to one table for the first time in 47 years, with six sessions over 21 hours. This led to a signing on June 18.
On the energy crisis stemming from Hormuz and Bab-el-Mandeb, he said the prime minister had flagged its impact on supply chains and prices, which had almost doubled in Pakistan. Despite financial constraints and the IMF programme, he said, the government approved a fuel relief scheme, now benefiting millions, for two-wheelers, three-wheelers and small four-wheelers of up to 800cc.
Answering a question about the Middle East, he said conflict was not a solution to anything. Even after the world wars, he noted, the warring countries had to sit down and build institutions.
Replying to a question, Dar said Pakistan's stance on Kashmir was "absolutely clear". The Kashmiri people, he said, must decide their future through a plebiscite under UN Security Council resolutions. India's actions of August 5, 2019, he added, must be reversed and no demographic change should be allowed in occupied Kashmir.
He said after the Pahalgam incident, Pakistan was blamed at once, and India then used the resulting sentiment to take its next steps.
This time, he said, the Foreign Office did not let India's narrative take hold internationally and that Pakistan had offered an independent, neutral investigation without delay. When India claimed strikes at 15 places and the downing of F-16s, Pakistan challenged the claims and asked India to say how many aircraft had fallen. India, he said, lost its own credibility.
On the Indus Waters Treaty, he said India's decision to hold it in abeyance was not accepted by Pakistan. The national security leadership and the civil-military leadership, he said, had resolved not to give up "even a drop" of Pakistan's water, which he described as a trust of 250 million people.
DPM Dar said he attended a meeting of the Arab-Islamic group of eight countries on Gaza, hosted by Egypt. He also attended the regional four-nation meeting of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Egypt, and a UN Security Council briefing on artificial intelligence. He attended OIC Contact Group meetings on Jammu and Kashmir and on Afghanistan, which he said Pakistan had pushed to be held regularly.
