title: Country on edge as Oct 4 long march looms
description: Country on edge as Oct 4 long march looms
author_name: Waqas Ahmad, Usama Iqbal, Rameez Khan
content:
Govt, opposition face off in second round today
The country held its breath on Friday, as the government and the opposition were set to resume talks on Saturday (today) after failing to bridge major differences in a first round aimed at averting a planned Oct. 4 long march by the Pakistan Tehrik-e-Insaf (PTI).
The meeting, chaired by NA Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq in his chamber, included representatives of the government, Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and the opposition.
The negotiations come amid continued tensions following PTI's announcement of an Islamabad march. Although the protest was postponed from September 27 to October 4, the standoff between the federal and provincial governments remains unresolved.
According to the NA spokesperson, detailed discussions were held on the country's political situation, with the government, PPP and opposition apprising each other of their respective positions. Various matters were discussed in detail and with patience, the spokesperson said.
The second round of negotiations will be held at 2pm on Saturday in the speaker's chamber, the spokesperson added. The government and PPP stressed the need to resolve national issues with the opposition through negotiations.
According to the statement, the NA Speaker played a key role in facilitating negotiations between the government, PPP and the opposition.
Federal minister Amir Muqam, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political and Public Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry attended the meeting. Senator Sherry Rehman and NA members Naveed Qamar and Ijaz Hussain Jakhrani also participated.
Opposition leaders including PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, Malik Amir Dogar and former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser, as well as Salman Akram Raja, attended the meeting.
The delegations were welcomed by Speaker Sadiq upon their arrival. "I am only playing the role of a mediator," he said.
Sadiq said his office was "always open" to resolving issues through negotiations and that he had consistently invited the opposition to engage in dialogue. He maintained that negotiations were the only way to resolve differences and issues, adding that positions and offices were temporary.
"Parliament is the only forum where solutions to issues can be found," he said.
In an earlier post on X, the Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan said the opposition side was being led by the leader of the opposition in the Senate, Allama Raja Nasir Abbas.
According to sources, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi opened the talks by raising concerns over the law-and-order situation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, including the performance of the provincial government and Chief Minister Sohail Afridi.
Naqvi blamed the provincial government for the security situation and recent attacks by the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
Senate opposition leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas rejected the government's position, saying the opposition had come to discuss political issues, not terrorism, and that linking the two would not resolve the dispute.
Nasir Abbas also raised the arrests of lawmakers and restrictions on meetings with Pakistan Tehrik-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan. According to sources, he said the PTI leadership could not take major political decisions without consulting Khan.
He said a meeting between Mahmood Khan Achakzai and himself and Khan could help open a path toward resolving the political dispute. Pakistan Peoples Party leader Sherry Rehman asked whether such a meeting would guarantee a resolution.
Nasir Abbas said the opposition would take responsibility and that the situation would improve if a meeting with Khan took place.
The government team, meanwhile, made clear that it would not allow any advance on Islamabad. It said calls for a long march, threats or an attack on Adiala jail were unacceptable, adding that flexibility would be required from the opposition as well.
Tensions rose several times during the talks, according to sources. Rana Sanaullah and Nasir Abbas exchanged heated remarks over judicial matters.
Nasir Abbas voiced concerns over what he described as incomplete implementation of court orders and restrictions on meetings with Khan. Sanaullah responded that the courts were carrying out their functions and that court orders relating to any long march would be enforced.
National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq urged both sides to exercise restraint and seek a way forward through dialogue.
Speaking to the media after the meeting, PPP's Rehman said the party believed in resolving issues through negotiations.
She said that PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari had stated the party's stance on the long march and that the PTI had to call it off "unconditionally".
"They will have to call it off rather than postponing or deferring," she said.
"Both parties have time; we will meet tomorrow. We will try to conclude this by tomorrow," she stated.
Talking about the opposition's reported demand of facilitating a meeting with incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, she said she could not answer the question. However, she said the opposition had asked for time and "we should respect it".
"A political and democratic attitude requires sitting at the negotiation table and resolving the issues through dialogue," she stated.
Meanwhile, the PTI rejected reports that negotiations between the government and the opposition in Islamabad were conditional on the party calling off its planned long march as sources familiar with the meeting said the two issues were discussed on parallel tracks.
The sources expressed frustration over "factually incorrect accounts of the talks", particularly the claim that the government had made cancellation of the protest a condition for continuing the dialogue.
They said the government had asked PTI to call off the protest and had repeated its publicly stated position during the meeting, but maintained that the demand was not presented as a precondition for negotiations.
According to the sources, PTI's position was that the dialogue should address the root causes that had led to the proposed protest. They said the party had conveyed its willingness to work with the government if there was seriousness about addressing those issues, but rejected the imposition of conditions before the dialogue could produce an understanding.
The sources said the government's stance on calling off the protest was already publicly known and had also been voiced during the meeting. However, they stressed that the dialogue and the long march were being pursued on parallel tracks rather than one being made conditional on the other.
They also said participants had agreed to exercise discretion over matters discussed during the Islamabad meeting and that the only position to be formally communicated to the media would be through a joint statement once it had been finalised.
The sources expressed particular frustration over "inaccurate accounts" subsequently given to the media, specifically disputing a version attributed to Pakistan Peoples Party leader Sherry Rehman regarding the status of the long march.
They said the account that PTI had agreed, or had been asked as a condition of dialogue, to call off the protest did not accurately reflect what was discussed during the meeting.
TTAP spokesperson Akhundzada Hussain said the alliance had lodged a protest over a breach of the understanding regarding discretion on the proceedings, specifically over remarks attributed to Sherry Rehman.
He also maintained that the dialogue had not been made conditional on calling off the march.
It was later revealed that Sherry had sought to clarify her position to TTAP leaders, saying she had only reiterated her party's position on the issue and had not made a specific demand during the meeting.
According to the sources, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi led much of the meeting, with his concerns focused primarily on security and administrative affairs in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Asked whether governor's rule was discussed, the sources said it was among the issues raised during the meeting, but maintained that Naqvi's broader focus was on the security situation and administration of the province.
The sources said the government's concerns were repeatedly framed around the failure of the provincial administration to ensure peace, security and tranquillity in K-P.
According to them, the same narrative that had been advanced publicly before the meeting was reflected in the government's position during the talks.
The PTI side, however, rejected that assessment and questioned the government's suggestion that the provincial authorities were protecting or harbouring non-state actors.
The sources said PTI responded to Naqvi by arguing that if a government could not even protect its own ministers in a province it governed, it could hardly be accused of protecting non-state actors.
They said the PTI side maintained that the approach being taken towards K-P was misplaced and did not adequately reflect the situation on the ground.
However, according to the sources, PTI made clear that negotiations could not proceed on the basis of conditions imposed before the dialogue itself had produced an understanding.
The sources also expressed surprise over the PPP's position during the meeting, saying the party appeared to have blindly supported the government's stance while disregarding long-held positions for power politics.
According to the sources, PTI also raised the issue of Imran Khan's sisters with PPP leader Sherry Rehman and asked her to take up his issue as well. The comment was met with silence.

title: 2 Pakistanis killed in BSF firing near Kasur
description: 2 Pakistanis killed in BSF firing near Kasur
content:
2 Pakistanis killed in BSF firing near Kasur
Two unarmed Pakistani civilians were killed and another injured when India's Border Security Force (BSF) opened fire on the three near the international border in Kasur, according to security sources.
The three residents of Ladhar village had moved only a few steps beyond a border pillar when BSF personnel targeted them without warning, the sources said. They added the firing left two civilians dead and another injured. The three men were unarmed at the time of the incident, according to the security sources.
The deceased were identified as Azmat Rasool, son of Attaullah, and Mohsin Jutt, both residents of Jattan Wali Haveli in Ladhar. The security sources said none of the three men had attempted to cross the border fence. Nevertheless, the Indian forces opened fire on them.
The sources also said that Indian media had described the civilians as infiltrators, continuing a pattern of portraying such incidents as false-flag operations. They said the firing on the civilians constituted an open violation of the border agreement and standard operating procedures governing the international border.
The incident comes amid heightened sensitivity along the international border, where established procedures are intended to regulate movement and prevent incidents involving civilians living close to the frontier.

CCC vows decisive force to crush agitation Top brass reaffirms Pakistan's right to self-defence Stresses 'targ
The 277th Corps Commanders' Conference forum underscored the importance of internal stability and resolved that any attempt to cause agitation or create a May 9-like situation, "on any pretext whatsoever, will be dealt with decisive force and rule of law, without hesitation and discrimination", the military's media wing said on Friday.
According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff (COAS) Field Marshal Asim Munir presided over the 277th Corps Commanders' Conference at General Headquarters, Rawalpindi.
The forum reviewed the prevailing security environment and resolved to maintain a high state of readiness, ISPR said.
The statement further added that it affirmed Pakistan's right to self-defence and targeted action against terrorism emanating from Afghanistan, stressing that "only the Taliban delusional leadership, facilitating terrorism on behalf of India, bears responsibility for its consequences".
"The forum appreciated sustained successful intelligence-based counter-terrorism operations by law enforcement agencies, however, emphasised complementing these kinetic efforts with non-kinetic measures, including people-centric governance at grassroot level, strategic engagement with public, dismantling of terror-crime nexus operating under patronage of vested interests and police capacity building, in line with the National Action Plan and Vision Azm-e-Istehkam," ISPR said.
The forum welcomed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, noting its contribution to longstanding strategic and collective defence ties, the statement added.
"It strongly resented Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, expressed solidarity with the Kingdom and affirmed Pakistan's commitment to the security and sanctity of the Haramain Sharifain," ISPR stated.
The forum also reiterated Pakistan's principled position on Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK) and support for resolution of the Kashmir dispute in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people, it added.
"The forum offered fateha for the Shuhada of the Armed Forces, Law Enforcement Agencies and civil society who laid down their lives for the motherland and paid rich tribute to their supreme sacrifices," ISPR said.
According to the statement, in his concluding remarks, CDF Munir commended the formations for their operational preparedness and professionalism. "He directed commanders to continue to strengthen intelligence-based operations and enhance combat capabilities through absorption of modern technology, training and multi-domain integration".
The field marshal expressed confidence that the Armed Forces, with unwavering support of the nation, remain fully prepared to safeguard Pakistan's sovereignty, territorial integrity and national security, the statement concluded.

title: 4 rescued Pak crew members arrive today
description: 4 rescued Pak crew members arrive today
content:
Four of the 10 Pakistani crew members affected by the hijacking of MT Honour 25 off the coast of Somalia will arrive in Karachi on Saturday, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Friday.
"Following sustained efforts by the Foreign Office and our Embassy in Djibouti, four of the ten Pakistani crew members (Mr Yasir Khan, Mr Aqeel Khan, Mr Amin bin Shams and Mr Usman Ghani) affected by the hijacking of MV Honour 25 off the coast of Somalia have been safely retrieved and are scheduled to arrive in Karachi tomorrow, 3 October, InshaAllah," Dar said in a post on X.
He said the mortal remains of three Pakistani crew members who "tragically lost their lives" were being repatriated to Pakistan, with "all necessary legal and other formalities" being fast-tracked.
"The mortal remains of the three Pakistani crew members (Late Rafi Ullah Khan, Late Syed Kashif Umer and Late Mahmood Ahmed Ansari) who tragically lost their lives are being repatriated to Pakistan, with all necessary legal and other formalities being fast-tracked to expedite the process in this regard," he said.
"My heartfelt condolences go to the bereaved families, who are going through a deeply painful time," Dar said. The remaining three Pakistani crew members - Imran Ali, Yasin Muhammad and Syed Yousuf Hussain - "continue to be aboard the vessel", along with the captain. "We are actively coordinating with our friendly countries to facilitate their safe extraction and earliest possible return to Pakistan, inshaAllah," the minister said on X.
The Foreign Office "remains fully seized of the matter" and was "continuously making every effort" to ensure the return of all Pakistani nationals, "including bodies of the deceased at the earliest and will continue extending all possible support to the affected families", he said.
Meanwhile, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday spoke by telephone with Azhan Kashif, son of the Pakistani national Kashif Umar who lost his life in Somalia.
The prime minister expressed heartfelt condolences to Azhan Kashif over the passing of his father, Syed Kashif Umar.
"We fully share in your grief," he said adding, "May Allah Almighty grant him a high place in Paradise and give your family the strength to bear this shock."
He assured the families that the government will bring the mortal remains of his father and the other two deceased Pakistanis back to Pakistan as soon as possible.
Directives were issued to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and all other relevant institutions to maintain direct contact with the families of Kashif Umar and the other two deceased individuals at every stage.
Kashif Umar was among the three Pakistanis who lost their lives during the rescue operation of a hijacked ship in Somalia.
The prime minister announced financial assistance, free education for children, and housing for the families of the three Pakistanis Syed Kashif Umar, Mahmood Ahmed Ansari, and Rafiullah Khan - who lost their lives during the rescue operation off the coast of Somalia.
He announced financial assistance of Rs12.5 million for each of the families of the Pakistani citizens who lost their lives during the rescue operation.
The prime minister announced the provision of free education and healthcare facilities by the government for the children of the deceased Pakistanis.
The Prime Minister further announced that the government will provide a house to each of the affected families.
He stated that the bereaved families would not be left alone during this difficult time and that the government would provide all possible support and assistance.
He directed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Pakistan Embassy to expedite the process of repatriating the bodies to Pakistan while maintaining constant contact with Somali authorities and other relevant stakeholders.
He also instructed that all possible measures be taken to provide the best medical care for the injured Pakistanis and to ensure the safe return of the remaining Pakistani personnel.

description: Four elected unopposed to AJK LA
content:
The Azad Jammu and Kashmir Election Commission (AJK EC) has officially notified four members elected unopposed to the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Council.
According to a notification issued by the commission, the four members were declared elected on the basis of election results received from the respective Returning Officer.
The members are Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz PML-N leader Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas, Chaudhry Muhammad Saeed and Chaudhry Manzoor Ahmed and Pakistan Peoples Party PPP Chaudhry Latif Akbar, Chaudhry Latif Akbar and Chaudhry Manzoor Ahmed belong to Muzaffarabad division , Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas to Bagh division, and Chaudhry Muhammad Saeed to Mirpur division.
The Election Commission formally published the names of the four elected members under Section 18 of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Council (Election) Act, 1976.
Copies of the notification have also been sent to the relevant authorities, the AJK Legislative Assembly Secretariat, Information Department and other concerned institutions.
Members of the Kashmir Council serve a five-year term and receive a monthly salary of Rs180000.
The four seats had fallen vacant following the expiry of the five-year terms of their previous occupants. The AJKEC had initially scheduled polling for October 12, but with four candidates filing nominations for four seats, the members were subsequently declared elected unopposed after the election process was completed.
The AJK Council is a constitutional body established under the Interim Constitution of 1974. It provides an institutional link between the governments of Pakistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir with its composition and functions defined by the constitutional framework.

title: TTAP questions Bukhari s stance on governor s rule
description: TTAP questions Bukhari s stance on governor s rule
content:
TTAP says it suspected that Bukhari had been compelled to change his earlier position under external pressure
The Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Aain Pakistan (TTAP) has conveyed its reservations to the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) leadership over General Secretary Nayyar Hussain Bukhari's alleged abrupt change of position on the possible imposition of governor's rule or an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, according to a TTAP spokesperson.
However, Bukhari denied making any U-turn, maintaining that the issue had never been discussed between him and the TTAP-PTI delegation.
The disagreement comes as political parties continue to debate possible constitutional options for K-P amid heightened tensions between the federal government and the provincial administration.
Meanwhile, TTAP said it suspected that Bukhari had been compelled to change his earlier position under external pressure.
According to the alliance, Bukhari had previously called on all political parties to sit together to break the cycle of political instability and uphold democratic principles, while describing the imposition of governor's rule as unconstitutional. TTAP representatives said his position had been unequivocal.
Talking to The Express Tribune, TTAP spokesperson Akhundzada Hussain said he was surprised by statements attributed to Bukhari on Wednesday suggesting that the PPP would consider the option of imposing governor's rule and that governor's rule could be imposed on the governor's recommendation in case of the failure of the provincial government.
Hussain said the remarks contradicted the position Bukhari had previously taken.
He said TTAP had conveyed its reservations to PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari through another senior party leader and would now prefer to engage directly with the chairman's office.
Asked about PM's Adviser Rana Sanaullah's remarks during a television programme, in which he was asked whether the PML-N would be invited to the proposed All Parties Conference (APC), Hussain said the PML-N would certainly not be invited.
Speaking to The Express Tribune, Bukhari maintained that he had not changed his position on governor's rule or the imposition of an emergency. He said the matter had never been discussed between him and the TTAP and PTI delegation.
He acknowledged saying that the PPP would examine the proposal if and when the government formally placed it before the party, adding that the ultimate decision rested with the president.
"We are allies in the government, so when they move forward and seek our proposal, we will give our suggestions. Without any proposal being placed before us, how can we give our position on the matter?" he said.
Bukhari said the delegation led by PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar had met him solely to extend an invitation to the PPP for the APC. He said he had informed the delegation that he would convey the invitation to the party chairman, who would decide, after consulting CEC members, whether to attend the APC.
Asked about the date of the upcoming Central Executive Committee (CEC) meeting, Bukhari said convening the meeting was the prerogative of the party chairman, who could either seek the opinion of CEC members individually or call a formal meeting. The ultimate decision rested with him, he added.
He further said he had been informed that the APC had been convened by TTAP rather than the PTI.

title: Ethiopia conflict risks wider regional war
description: Ethiopia conflict risks wider regional war
content:
Forces advance on Mekelle as Eritrea severs diplomatic ties
Fighting in northern Ethiopia intensified on Friday as government forces and allied militias advanced towards Tigray's capital Mekelle, while diplomatic ties with Eritrea collapsed and explosions in Addis Ababa fuelled fears of a wider regional conflict.
The pro-government Tigray Peace Forces militia said it had captured Milazat, about 20 kilometres southeast of Mekelle, as federal troops and allied fighters continued making advances in Tigray since fighting erupted last week.
Banks and shops were closed in Mekelle in anticipation of possible fighting, according to residents. A diplo-matic source said senior Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) leaders had already left the city and the con-flict could continue even if federal forces captured it.
The latest fighting marks the biggest escalation since Ethiopia's devastating 2020-22 civil war, when hundreds of thousands were killed. The TPLF has formed an alliance with six other armed groups seeking to overthrow Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government.
Ethiopia on Thursday ordered the closure of its embassy in Eritrea and expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats, accus-ing Asmara of direct and indirect hostility. Eritrea responded by severing all diplomatic ties, further raising concerns that the conflict could spread beyond Ethiopia's borders.
The two countries fought a border war from 1998 to 2000 and restored diplomatic relations in 2018. Their rela-tionship has since deteriorated, including over Ethiopia's demand for access to the Red Sea, with Eritrea say-ing it fears Ethiopia could attempt to seize its Assab port.
Tensions also widened with Egypt after Ethiopia expelled an Egyptian diplomat. Cairo responded by declaring an Ethiopian embassy counsellor persona non grata and ordering him to leave within 48 hours, describing Ethi-opia's move as unfortunate and unjustified.
The dispute comes as Ethiopia accuses Eritrea, Egypt and Sudan of supporting the opposition alliance led by the TPLF. All three countries have denied the accusations, while the African Union Commission urged Ethiopia, Eritrea and Egypt to exercise maximum restraint.
Meanwhile, explosions were heard in Addis Ababa late ON Wednesday, with diplomatic sources telling AFP that small drones were the most likely cause. An opposition-linked source claimed drone strikes had targeted military headquarters and other sites in the capital.

title: India s Gen Z demands poll chief s resignation
description: India s Gen Z demands poll chief s resignation
content:
Cockroach Janta Party and student groups protest over voter-roll revisions
Prime Minister Narendra Modi faced renewed political pressure on Friday as the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and a separate coalition of student and activist groups staged protests demanding the resignation of India's election chief over a disputed voter-roll revision.
The CJP planned a rally in Mumbai, while student and civil society groups gathered at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar – the venue where the students protested for days in July, forcing resignation of the country's education minis-ter. The party said it would expand demonstrations nationwide in the coming days.
Dozens of protesters gathered at the Delhi site on Friday morning, but police bundled some into buses and took them away. Several nearby metro stations remained closed, while security was tightened in the barricaded area with hundreds of police and paramilitary personnel surrounding the protest site.
In Mumbai, hundreds of police officers were seen assembling around the location where protesters were ex-pected to gather later in the afternoon. Authorities in Delhi had warned against unauthorised assemblies as tensions mounted around the demonstrations.
The protests mark the latest escalation in a dispute that has brought unprecedented scrutiny on India's Elec-tion Commission. Protesters allege that voter rolls were manipulated to benefit Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), allegations rejected by both the commission and the government.
Pressure on Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar intensified last month after the Indian Express reported that his two deputies had formally raised concerns at least 14 times over the previous 10 months about voter-list revisions, registration procedures and the commission's digital systems.
The controversy centres on a nationwide voter-verification exercise launched last year. Critics say the process has resulted in millions of eligible voters being removed from electoral rolls, while the Election Commission says it is intended to eliminate duplicate, deceased or otherwise ineligible voters.
Opposition parties led by Congress are also due to begin separate protests on October 6, with Kumar's resig-nation among their demands. The demonstrations add another front to the broader political confrontation over the voter-verification exercise.

title: Russian strikes disrupt Kyiv bridges | The Express Tribune
description:
Russian strikes 
disrupt Kyiv bridges
content:
Russian airstrikes forced the temporary closure of two bridges over the Dnipro River in Kyiv on Friday, disrupt-ing traffic between the two sides of the Ukrainian capital as Moscow stepped up its bombardment of infra-structure ahead of winter.
Long traffic jams formed during the morning after Russian drones struck the Southern Bridge several times on Thursday. Video footage posted online showed residents walking across the bridge, which had been closed to cars and metro trains following the attacks.
Russian drones also struck a school, although pupils were unharmed because they were sheltering at the time, officials said. Traffic on the Southern Bridge and part of the Paton Bridge was halted on Friday morning, while another bridge was partially closed.
Movement across the bridges was restored by around midday, Reuters witnesses said. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said he had convened a city security council meeting to assess the risks, describing the situation in the capital as "very dramatic".
More than a third of Kyiv's three million residents lived on the eastern, or left, bank of the Dnipro before Russia's 2022 invasion, according to city authorities. But only 18% of jobs were located there, with most residents work-ing on the western bank, home to government institutions and companies.
Separately, a Russian drone strike killed one person and injured two others in Kyiv on Friday after a fire broke out on the upper floors of an apartment building, officials said. In Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, two people were killed and 28 wounded in a guided-bomb strike, according to the regional governor.

title: G7 unlocks oil reserves to ease supplies
description: G7 unlocks oil reserves to ease supplies
content:
100m barrels to be released through IEA over four months as leaders reject energy export curbs
G7 countries agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from their reserves over four months, including a substantial diesel release within the first 20 days, as fuel prices surged amid the wars in Iran and Ukraine.
The agreement followed urgent talks among G7 leaders to coordinate action on energy prices, with the United States pressing European countries to release strategic fuel reserves and warning it could restrict diesel exports.
The leaders said the coordinated release would be carried out through the International Energy Agency (IEA) and begin immediately.
They also pledged to refrain from imposing energy export restrictions among G7 members and urged other producers to avoid measures that could worsen
in a joint statement released by French President Emmanuel Macron's office. The announcement came after Macron convened
a G7 leaders' video call following discussions with US President Donald Trump.
Trump said separately European countries had agreed to release a "massive amount" of diesel from their reserves. "The process will begin immediately," he said in a post on Truth Social.
The European Union had earlier rejected the prospect of a US diesel export ban, with European Commission spokeswoman Anna-Kaisa Itkonen saying such a measure would undermine trust in the United States as a reliable partner.
Oil prices fell sharply during Friday's G7 discussions. US West Texas Intermediate crude declined 4% to $89.15 a barrel after falling as much as 5%, while Brent crude dropped 2.6% to $99.63. US diesel prices have risen more than 70% to $6.39 a gallon since the start of the Iran war.

title: Pacific will host fresh climate push
description: Pacific will host fresh climate push
content:
World powers are flying delegates comprising ministers and climate negotiators, to the Pacific to haggle over the fight against global warming, and to see the plight of island nations surrounded by a rising ocean.
The delegates will meet in the Fijian city of Nadi for the October 5-8 talks to chart the course for a major UN-sponsored global climate summit, known as COP31, to be held in November in Turkey's Antalya province.
For Pacific nations, hosting the preliminary talks in their region offers an opportunity to draw the world's atten-tion to life on the frontline of climate change. Pacific leaders are pushing for the world to stick to a target of lim-iting global warming to 1.5C, enhance access to climate finance, and give more attention to the impact on oceans.

title: Student protests spread across France  Belgium
description: Student protests spread across France  Belgium
content:
Hundreds of schools were closed or disrupted across France on Friday as student protests over learning con-ditions entered a new phase, with authorities reporting mass arrests, injuries, property damage and clashes between demonstrators and security forces.
France's Education Minister Edouard Geffray said more than 1,200 high schools had been disrupted or blocked since the mobilisation began, while more than 100 schools suffered severe damage.
Geffray said 65 school staff, including 40 headteachers, had been injured, while 170 students had also suf-fered injuries. Authorities said about 900 protests were reported outside schools on Thursday, when nearly 2,000 people were arrested and more than 300 police officers and gendarmes were injured.
Strasbourg saw some of the sharpest clashes, with protesters moving towards a University of Strasbourg campus. Mortar fireworks were reported, while tear gas was used.
In the Paris region, 55 high schools were affected by violence, clashes or damage by midday. The Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes region estimated damage at 25 million to 30 million.
Meanwhile, student protests continued in Belgium's Liege province, where police made 40 arrests.
police reported clashes, damaged businesses and scooters set on fire.
Students in Belgium said they were protesting education reforms and measures affecting daily life, including higher public transport costs.

title: Govt to abolish 60  vacant accounts posts
description: Govt to abolish 60  vacant accounts posts
content:
CGA is the premier accounting office of the Government of Pakistan
The federal government has decided to abolish 60% of vacant permanent posts in the federal accounts system, with the Controller General of Accounts (CGA) directing relevant officers to initiate the process.
According to directions issued by the CGA, posts that have remained vacant for at least one year have been recommended for abolition in light of a decision taken by the federal cabinet on August 27, 2024. The directions clarify, however, that vacant posts allocated for transfers, postings and promotions will not be abolished. The abolished posts will be deducted from the quota allocated for initial appointments or direct recruitment, according to the instructions.
All Financial Accounting Offices (FAOs) must review or prepare their vacancy rosters according to the decision. The FAOs have also been instructed to process promotion cases accordingly. The communication containing the directions was issued with the CGA's approval.
The CGA is the premier accounting office of the Government of Pakistan. It is entrusted with the task of producing accurate and timely financial statements for the federation.

title: Civil servants told to declare citizenship
description: Civil servants told to declare citizenship
content:
Government sets one-week deadline under new foreign citizenship rules
The government has decided to enforce the Foreign Citizenship Rules 2026, directing civil servants to submit declarations detailing any foreign citizenship held by themselves or their dependants within one week.
The Establishment Division, through an office memorandum, directed civil servants to provide details of foreign citizenship, foreign travel documents and marriages to foreign nationals. The directive applies to officers holding dual nationality and requires them to furnish the relevant information within the stipulated one-week deadline.
The Establishment Division warned that failure to comply with the instructions or submission of incorrect information could result in departmental action against the concerned officer. It said officers who failed to submit the required declaration within the given timeframe would face proceedings under the Civil Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules 2020.
The submission of a false declaration would also be treated as misconduct and could lead to disciplinary proceedings against the civil servant concerned. The move comes as the government begins implementation of the Foreign Citizenship Rules 2026, with officers required to provide complete and accurate information within the prescribed deadline.

title: ECP proposes Dec 14 for Punjab LG polls
description: ECP proposes Dec 14 for Punjab LG polls
content:
Forwards draft election schedule to provincial govt for consultation, feedback
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has proposed December 14, 2026 as the polling date for local government (LG) elections in Punjab and has forwarded the draft election schedule to the provincial government for consultation and feedback.
The last LG elections in the country's most populous province were held in 2015 and the tenure of the last LGs in Punjab had ended in 2021.
According to the proposed schedule, the ECP will initiate the election process by issuing a public notice for the submission of nomination papers on October 23, 2026.
Candidates will be able to file their nomination papers with the returning officers from October 27 to 30, while the list of received nomination papers will be published on October 31.
The scrutiny of nomination papers will be conducted from November 2 to 5, followed by the publication of the list of validly nominated candidates on November 6.
Candidates will be allowed to file appeals against the acceptance or rejection of nomination papers from November 7 to 11. The appellate authorities will decide these appeals between November 12 and 16.
Following the disposal of appeals, a revised list of validly nominated candidates will be published on November 17. The last date for withdrawal of candidature has been set for November 18, while the revised list following withdrawals will be published on November 19.
The final list of candidates along with their allotted electoral symbols is scheduled to be published on November 20, 2026.
Under the draft programme, polling for the local government elections has been proposed for December 14, 2026, while returning officers are scheduled to announce the results on December 17.
This development follows a consultation meeting held on August 20 between the ECP and the Punjab government's cabinet committee regarding the proposed polling date.
During the meeting, the provincial government proposed holding LG elections between December 15, 2026 and January 15, 2027, a proposal with which the ECP agreed.
The ECP has sent the draft programme to the Punjab chief secretary to obtain suggestions and feedback before issuing the final election schedule.
The draft programme has been prepared for elections to the general seats of Union Councils in Punjab.
The ECP has clarified that the schedule is currently a draft proposal and the final election programme will be issued after completing the consultation process with the Punjab government.
Punjab has not held a full province-wide LG election since 2015, despite subsequent attempts to establish new LG systems and conduct delimitation.

title: Houthi attack on Madina  grave provocation
description: Houthi attack on Madina  grave provocation
content:
Pakistan on Friday strongly condemned an attack by the Houthi militia on the Taibah power distribution station in Madina on September 29, saying the "reprehensible attack" on civilian infrastructure supplying electricity to the Holy Prophet's (PBUH) Mosque was a "grave provocation," the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) said on Friday.
In a post on X, MoFA said the attack was a matter of "deep concern and anguish" for millions of Muslims worldwide.
"The sanctity of the Two Holy Mosques and the safety of worshippers and pilgrims must be respected under all circumstances," the ministry added. Pakistan called for an immediate and unconditional end to reckless actions, saying they also constituted a grave threat to regional peace and security, it added.
The statement further added that the Pakistan reaffirmed its "unwavering solidarity" with the brotherly Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and expressed its full support for the kingdom's sovereignty, territorial integrity and security.
"We stand firmly with Saudi Arabia in its efforts to safeguard the Two Holy Mosques, protect its people and ensure the safety of pilgrims," the ministry said.
The statement said Pakistan had been and would continue to make all efforts to achieve lasting peace and stability in the region.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Thursday that the group had attacked a power distribution station in Madina earlier in the week, putting one transformer out of service but without affecting the electricity network.
The coalition said an investigation and examination of drone wreckage had confirmed Houthi involvement in planning and carrying out Tuesday's attack. Coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said the attack had targeted the Taibah electricity distribution station at 5:11am local time on Tuesday.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said the export of an additional 70,000 metric tons of Pakistani rice to Malaysia would prove to be a significant step for the national economy besides ensuring the prosperity of farmers.
He said enhancing access to global markets for Pakistani agricultural products was the government's top priority. "We will continue our journey toward the goal of export-led economic growth through sustained hard work," he said in a statement.

title: ISPR laid out charge sheet against K P govt
description: ISPR laid out charge sheet against K P govt
content:
Asif accuses provincial govt of 'confusing' terrorism narrative
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Friday said Director General Inter-Services Public Relations (DG ISPR) Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry had effectively read out a "charge sheet" against the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government during his press conference a day earlier, accusing the provincial administration of failing to play its due role in the fight against terrorism.
In a series of posts on X, Asif said political activity could not be used to shield those involved in facilitating terrorism, and questioned why the K-P government was not doing more to combat militancy and strengthen the province's police capacity.
"You cannot hide behind politics while being involved in facilitating terrorism; the DG ISPR has made this clear in unequivocal terms," Asif said.
"We are fighting terrorism, why don't you come forward? Are you cowards or are you in league with terrorists? You create confusion in the terrorism narrative, why don't you build the capacity of the police?"
Asif said the DG ISPR had effectively presented a charge sheet against the K-P government and delivered a clear message that the existing approach would no longer be accepted.
"The most important thing for us is that if there is a state, there is politics; if there is a state, there is democracy; and if there is a state, you and I exist," the federal minister said.
In another post, Asif said he had watched and listened carefully to the DG ISPR's press conference and that, alongside highlighting several important issues, the military spokesperson had also underscored the K-P government's detachment and deliberate indifference towards the fight against terrorism.
Asif questioned what the DG ISPR meant by saying that the terrorism narrative was being confused.
He said the entire nation knew that Fitna al-Khawarij and its supporters, including the TTA regime, were operating against the Pakistani state. In contrast, he said, the PTI advocated engagement with the Afghan regime because Afghans were "our brothers" and called for negotiations and maintaining relations with Kabul.
According to Asif, such an approach confused Pakistan's ongoing fight against terrorism.
He said the state had designated the TTP as Fitna al-Khawarij, but K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and his party had not, to date, used that designation for the group. "What else can be understood from this?" Asif asked.

content:

title: Woman drowns after Jhelum water surge

content:
A 55-year-old Kashmiri woman drowned in the River Jhelum after a sudden surge in the flow, following release of water from India's Uri Dam, the State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA) said on Friday.
The incident occurred at Kucha Syedan, between ChinarI and Hattian Bala, where the widow, Rehmat Bibi, was collecting firewood along the riverbank when she was swept away by the strong current. ChinarI police, Rescue 1122 and local residents launched a joint search operation after the woman went missing.
Her body was recovered from the River Jhelum near Muzaffarabad after several hours of searching. According to SDMA senior official Khushal Mughal, the sudden rise in the river's water level was caused by India releasing water from the Uri Dam without prior warning. The SDMA said additional water was released into the River Jhelum in the morning but the flow was stopped again in the evening, causing the river's water level to fall sharply.
"At this time of year, the river normally remains between 12 and 15 feet. However, following the release from Uri Dam, the flow rose to more than 18.5 feet during the day. After the release was stopped in the evening, the level dropped to 8.5 feet," the official stated.
The administration and rescue agencies have advised residents to avoid the River Jhelum, streams and rainwater channels, particularly when there is a sudden increase in water flow.

title: FCC questions impartiality of ex CJP
description: FCC questions impartiality of ex CJP
content:
Says Supreme Court observations about Monal owner were unsupported by record
The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has raised questions over the impartiality of former chief justice Qazi Faez Isa in the Monal restaurant case, observing that certain remarks made by the Supreme Court bench led by him were based on matters that did not form part of the judicial record.
The observations came in a 44-page detailed judgment issued by a three-judge FCC bench headed by Justice Hasan Azhar Rizvi, after the court overturned the Supreme Court's 2024 decision ordering the demolition of Monal restaurant at Pir Sohawa.
An SC bench led by Isa had dismissed a review petition filed by the owner of Monal restaurant against the demolition order and made certain observations concerning the restaurant's owner.
In July, the FCC, through a short order, allowed appeals filed by the Capital Development Authority (CDA) and the Metropolitan Corporation Islamabad (MCI), effectively overturning the SC's 2024 ruling and permitting the Monal restaurant to remain.
In its detailed judgment, the FCC expressed concern over the manner in which the SC proceedings had been conducted, particularly observations concerning the alleged personal relationships, private affairs and political associations of the parties.
"As the then apex court of the country, the Supreme Court was expected to determine the controversy solely on the basis of the pleadings, the evidence available on the record, and the law on the subject," the judgment stated.
"The judicial findings and observations must emanate from the record before the Court and not from matters resting in the personal knowledge or information of the bench hearing the case."
The FCC observed that references to the alleged personal relationships, private affairs and political associations of the parties did not appear to have been established through admissible evidence forming part of the record.
"The incorporation of such matters into judicial reasoning is liable to create a perception that the controversy has not been adjudicated with complete detachment from unnecessary considerations," it said.
The court emphasised that public confidence in the administration of justice rested on the assurance that every litigant would be judged exclusively on the basis of law and evidence placed before the court.
It observed that where a bench possessed personal knowledge of disputed facts or circumstances relating to a party, or where such knowledge could give rise to a reasonable apprehension of unfairness, judicial propriety required the judge to decline to hear the matter.
"It is beyond cavil that judges of the superior judiciary possess the discretion to recuse themselves in appropriate cases so as to preserve both the appearance and the reality of impartial justice."
The FCC noted that despite recording observations founded upon matters stated to be within their personal knowledge or information, the Supreme Court bench proceeded to adjudicate the controversy.
"The observations of the learned bench, reproduced above, suggest that the manner in which the proceedings were conducted may have given rise to a reasonable apprehension concerning impartiality," it said.
The court held that, in the circumstances, the proceedings might not be regarded as having fully satisfied the requirements of a fair trial.
"The constitutional guarantee of a fair trial under Article 10-A necessarily includes the right to a proper hearing before a competent, independent, and unbiased forum," the judgment said.
The FCC further observed that the SC bench ought not to have heard the case, keeping in view the high traditions of the institution and the established principle that justice should not only be done but should also manifestly be seen to be done.
"The legitimacy of the judicial process depends not merely upon actual impartiality but equally upon maintaining public confidence that justice has been administered fairly, objectively, and without predisposition," the court said.
"For these reasons, the aforesaid observations are legally unsustainable, as they are unsupported by the record and bear no discernible nexus to the determination of the legal issues involved in the case."

title: Newborn abducted from Peshawar hospital

content:
Police trace burqa-clad woman in CCTV footage
A case of an allegedly missing newborn from the Gynecology Department of Lady Reading Hospital (LRH) Peshawar has come to light, with the affected family accusing hospital staff while the administration has described the woman who took the newborn as someone known to the family who visited the labor room with their consent.
According to the affected family, after the child's birth, women were asked to leave the hospital's labor room; however, when they re-entered sometime later, the newborn was not there. The affected father, Hishmat Ali, has demanded the recovery of the child and action against those responsible.
According to Hishmat Ali, his wife gave birth at LRH the previous day. At the time of the birth, hospital staff removed the women of their household from the gynecology room. Later, when the women went back into the gynecology room, the newborn was not present. He stated that a report of the incident was lodged at the police post established in the hospital, but police have not yet registered an FIR.
The affected father said that a nurse in the gynecology ward instead accused the family of making the child disappear, to which he raised the question of why parents would make their own newborn disappear. Hishmat Ali demanded that the child be recovered immediately and handed over to the family, and that a transparent investigation into the incident be conducted.
Meanwhile, a significant development has emerged in the case, as police have obtained CCTV footage from various cameras at LRH. According to police, the footage allegedly shows a burqa-clad woman fleeing the hospital with the newborn.
Police said the alleged female abductor left the labor room with the child at approximately 11 pm and escaped from the hospital through the Bolton Block gate.
Police said the women of the affected family identified the alleged woman after viewing the CCTV footage.
According to police officials, efforts are underway to arrest the alleged female abductor and recover the newborn, while further evidence is also being collected.
Meanwhile, LRH spokesman Muhammad Asim said the matter is being inquired into and police are also looking into the incident. According to the spokesman, the hospital's CCTV footage has been provided to police, with the help of which the woman allegedly carrying the child is being traced.
LRH spokesman Muhammad Asim also said that the affected family has not yet registered an FIR of the incident.
He stated that the said woman had been coming and going in the labor room with the consent of the affected parents, and the parents had also told the staff that the woman was with them and should be allowed to come and go.

title: Illegal blasting blamed for 34 miner deaths
description: Illegal blasting blamed for 34 miner deaths
content:
Quetta disaster inquiry finds safety violations, underage labour and management negligence
The official investigation into the tragic coal mine disaster that claimed 34 lives two months ago in Sur Range on the outskirts of Quetta has finally been made public.
The report by the Chief Minister Inspection Team (CMIT) and other agencies squarely blames the use of illegal explosives, systematic violation of safety laws and the criminal negligence of the mine management for the deaths.
According to the inquiry findings, physical evidence at the site, including drill holes in hard rock, confirms that the accident was caused by underground blasting. The Sardar Muhammad Usman Khan Jogezai Coal Company, which operates Mine No1, held no licence whatsoever to store or use explosives, nor did it employ any trained blasting expert.
Investigators found clear breaches of Regulations 97 and 99 of the Coal Mines Regulations 1926. The mine owner, manager and mine sardar were fully aware that explosives were being used underground yet failed to inform the relevant authorities, an omission the report describes as criminal failure of the administration.
The report also exposes serious violations of Sections 26-A and 26-B of the Mines Act 1923, which prohibit the employment of anyone under the age of 17 in mines. Identity documents of the deceased reveal that six of the victims were under 18 years of age; two of them were younger than 17. The underage miners identified are Ziaullah (16 years three months), Rahmat Ali (16 years four months), Abu Sufyan (17 years two months), Shabirullah (17 years three months), Abu Zar (17 years three months) and Muteeur Rahman (17 years seven months).
Despite extracting coal valued at more than two billion rupees from the mine over the past three years, the company denied workers basic facilities. Miners lacked clean drinking water, proper housing and registration with the Employees' Old-Age Benefits Institution (EOBI).
Even more damning is the revelation that serious safety deficiencies had already been flagged before the disaster. Inspectors had noted a critical shortage of timber supports and the presence of dangerous levels of coal dust, yet the owners completely ignored these warnings.
Of the 34 workers who perished, 33 belonged to District Shangla in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa; the majority came from a single village. The tragedy tore through one family particularly hard: three brothers and their uncle were among the dead.
The findings paint a stark picture of systemic failure, illegal practices, exploitation of child labour, neglect of basic safety measures and a complete disregard for the lives of the men who risked everything underground. The report is expected to form the basis for further legal and administrative action against those responsible.

title: Call to protect capital s shrinking green cover
description: Call to protect capital s shrinking green cover
content:
Govt urged to make sustainability, climate resilience central to revised Master Plan
Citizens, urban planners, researchers and civil society representatives on Friday called for urgent measures to protect Islamabad's shrinking green spaces, tree cover and ecological systems, warning that rapid population growth and development were threatening the capital's environmental balance and liveability.
The participants urged authorities to place sustainability, biodiversity and climate resilience at the centre of the revised Master Plan of Islamabad.
The call was made at a citizens' dialogue titled "Reclaiming Green Islamabad", organised by the Institute of Urbanism (IoU), bringing together policymakers, government officials, urban planners, researchers, journalists and civil society representatives to discuss concerns over the loss of natural spaces in the capital.
Often described as Pakistan's "Green Capital", Islamabad's population has risen from just over 100,000 in the early 1960s to an estimated 2.4 million in 2023. Data presented at the dialogue showed that the city lost around 1,622 hectares of tree cover between 2020 and 2022.
Chairperson of the IoU Board of Directors Tariq Banuri said the loss of green cover was not merely an environmental issue but also a matter of social equity, as pollution, extreme heat and declining tree cover affected residents differently according to their ability to cope with environmental pressures.
"Greening isn't just about nature, it's about us, and especially about fairness," he said, stressing that environmental protection should be a core consideration in every future development decision.
He called for restoring lost green cover, naturally managing rainwater and drainage, and protecting ecological corridors linking parks, trees and waterways across the city.
IoU Executive Director Dr Ejaz Ahmad said urban development and environmental protection should not be viewed as competing objectives, emphasising the need for government, communities and technical experts to work together from the planning stage.
"Urban development and environmental protection are too often treated as opposing forces; in reality, they don't have to be," he said.
Participants expressed concern over recent tree removals and gaps in monitoring, protecting and restoring Islamabad's natural assets. They proposed practical measures, including training students and young volunteers as community organisers and securing formal government support for community-led plantation and conservation initiatives.
They stressed that the ongoing revision of Islamabad's Master Plan provided an important opportunity to embed environmental sustainability, liveability, biodiversity and climate resilience into the capital's future development rather than addressing ecological damage after it occurs.
The participants emphasised that Islamabad's green spaces should be treated as public assets essential to the quality of life of all residents. They called for coordinated action to preserve the natural systems supporting the capital for present and future generations.

"Therefore, the actual number of dengue patients in Rawalpindi cannot be determined. We only share data from government hospitals," officials said.
According to the department, 1,400 teams have so far inspected 5.17 million houses during the ongoing dengue season, detecting larvae at 176,144 houses. Teams also inspected 1.79 million open spaces and plots, finding larvae at 24,709 locations.
Authorities have registered 2,798 cases of violations involving the presence of dengue larvae and failure to implement prescribed standard operating procedures. A total of 686 units have been sealed, while 2,331 challans were issued and fines amounting to Rs3.156 million imposed.
The Health Department has declared the period until November 15 as the peak and most critical phase of the dengue season. According to officials, dengue larvae would gradually die off as rainfall decreased and colder weather intensified thereafter.

title: Urdu edition of prison diary launched
description: Urdu edition of prison diary launched
content:
Poetic work of Vietnam founder Ho Chi Minh unveiled at diplomat-studded ceremony
The Pakistan Academy of Letters (PAL), under the National Heritage & Culture Division, recently organised a ceremony to launch the Urdu translation of Prison Diary, the poetic work of the renowned Vietnamese revolutionary leader, poet and founder of modern Vietnam, Ho Chi Minh.
Prison Diary is regarded as one of the significant literary works of the twentieth century. The book is lauded for giving poetic expression to imprisonment, loneliness, and human suffering, while also highlighting freedom, hope, courage and unwavering determination. The Urdu translation has been rendered by Kausar Khanum, while Najma Saqib is credited for its revision.
The ceremony was held at the Sheikh Ayaz Conference Hall, PAL, Islamabad. It was attended by diplomatic representatives of various ASEAN countries, along with writers, intellectuals and literary figures.
Ambassador of Thailand Rong Vudh Virabutr, High Commissioner of Malaysia Dato' Muhammad Azhar Mazlan, High Commissioner of Brunei Darussalam Colonel (retd) Pengiran Haji Kamal Bashah Pengiran Haji Ahmad, Ambassador of Cuba Damian Cordero Torres, Chargé d'Affaires of Indonesia Rahmat Hindiarta and Chargé d'Affaires of Myanmar Maung Maung Thon were among the distinguished guests.
PAL Chairperson Dr Najiba Arif welcomed the distinguished guests and diplomatic representatives and said that Prison Diary is not merely an account of a revolutionary leader, but also a poetic expression of human freedom, hope, courage and determination. She said that the Urdu translation of the book had been undertaken under the Memorandum of Understanding signed between PAL and Vietnam, and that it represents an important milestone in promoting literary and cultural cooperation between the two countries. She also expressed her resolve to further strengthen literary ties with ASEAN countries. At the end of her address, Dr Najiba Arif led a Fatiha for the renowned writer, poet, and intellectual Haleem Qureshi, who passed away during a ceremony at PAL the previous day, and paid tribute to his valuable literary services.
In addition, Munir Fayyaz and former Ambassador Salahuddin Chaudhry spoke about various aspects of Prison Diary, Ho Chi Minh's personality, poetry and struggle, and presented selected verses from the book.

description: Inflation pushes daily wagers onto pavements
content:

The number of labourers and daily wagers sleeping rough on pavements and roadsides in Rawalpindi has risen sharply amid growing poverty, inflation and declining purchasing power.
Many workers take shelter beneath the Metrobus track or under shop awnings during rain at night or in the early hours. At daybreak, they queue outside selected hotels and food points offering free bread and breakfast.
The number of people spending nights outdoors has particularly increased along Murree Road, from Mareer Chowk to Faizabad, including Chandni Chowk, Rehmanabad, Liaquat Bagh Chowk and the benches inside Liaquat Bagh.
Similar scenes are witnessed around General Bus Stand Pirwadhai, the lawns of the three allied hospitals, Ganjmandi Bazaar, Pirwadhai Jamia Masjid Road, Banni Chowk, Iqbal Road, Moti Bazaar, Bohar Bazaar, Narnkari Bazaar, Hamilton Road, Tyre Bazaar, Naya Mohalla, the inner Sarafa Bazaar, Chhota Bazaar Saddar, Girja Road, Dhoke Syedan Road, Bara Bazaar, Ratta Qadim, Lakri Pul and Pohri Pul.
Most of these workers have arrived from various cities of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and remote areas of northern Punjab in search of employment. During the day, they earn through loading and unloading, working with goods transporters and other daily-wage jobs, while at night they sleep on pavements, carts, roadside platforms and even parked vehicles.
Several charitable hotel owners provide free meals at designated points in Raja Bazaar, Jamia Masjid Road and Bara Bazaar. Workers often arrive an hour before meals and sit in queues on the ground. Destitute women from poor families also arrive with their children to receive free food.
Labourers sleeping beneath the Metrobus track in Ganjmandi, Chandni Chowk and Rehmanabad said they generally earned between Rs700 and Rs1,000 a day, while on some days their income was even lower. Occasionally, they managed to earn up to Rs1,500.
They said they had travelled to Rawalpindi from Peshawar, Nowshera, Buner, Mardan, Kohat, Waziristan, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rojhan Jamali, Layyah and Jhang in search of work
Labourers Muhammad Maskeen, Allah Rakha, Faisal Mahmood and Chan Waiz said their meagre incomes prevented them from staying in small hotels or inns. Some inns, they said, charged around Rs200 for an overnight stay from 10pm to 6am or 7am, an amount they could not afford every night.
"We cannot afford even a small room or an inn every night, so we sleep on pavements, roadsides or beneath the Metrobus track," they said.
Many labourers have also started spending nights in hospital lawns and corridors, claiming to be relatives of patients. They also receive meals from philanthropists who visit hospitals to distribute free food.
Chan Waiz, who has worked in Ganjmandi for five years, said he earned between Rs1,000 and Rs1,200 a day and sometimes managed to make Rs1,500.

title: LHC rejects property claim based on mutation
description: LHC rejects property claim based on mutation
content:
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has upheld concurrent judgments recognising the inheritance claim of a grandson of a deceased landowner, ruling that a revenue mutation alone cannot establish ownership where the underlying gift transaction is disputed and that an alleged divorce must be proved through credible and legally admissible evidence.
Justice Hassan Nawaz Makhdoom dismissed a civil revision petition challenging judgments of the Civil Judge, Sargodha, and the Additional District Judge, Sargodha, which had recognised the inheritance rights of the plaintiff's family branch.
The court held that the alleged gift of 346 kanals of land to the deceased landowner's son had not been established through independent and satisfactory evidence, while the alleged divorce of the plaintiff's grandmother decades before the landowner's death also remained unproved.
The dispute concerned the estate of Dost Muhammad, who died on December 24, 1969. He had two wives, Sahib Khatoon and Jannat Khatoon. Sahib Khatoon was the mother of Salah Khatoon, while Jannat Khatoon was the mother of Malik Ali Akbar.
The plaintiff, Malik Janbaz Khan, claimed inheritance through his maternal grandmother, Salah Khatoon, while the petitioners were the successors of Ali Akbar.
The central issue was whether Sahib Khatoon's branch had lawfully been excluded from inheritance on the basis of an alleged divorce and a gift of property said to have been made by Dost Muhammad in favour of his son.
Janbaz had instituted the suit in 1999, challenging several revenue mutations through which, according to his claim, his family branch had been deprived of its lawful share in the estate. He sought a declaration that the disputed entries were illegal and ineffective against his inheritance rights.
The defendants maintained that Dost Muhammad had gifted 346 kanals of land in Chak No. 29/N.B., Sargodha, to Ali Akbar through Mutation No. 204 dated February 6, 1962, and that the property therefore did not form part of the deceased's estate when he died.
They also contended that Sahib Khatoon had been divorced in 1921 and was consequently not entitled to inherit from Dost Muhammad.
Rejecting the challenge to the lower courts' findings, Justice Makhdoom observed that a mutation was essentially a fiscal entry maintained for revenue purposes and did not, by itself, create, confer or extinguish title to property.
The court noted that the defendants had failed to produce any witness to the original gift transaction or independent evidence establishing that the gift had actually been made.

title: Progress hinges on continuity  Maryam
description: Progress hinges on continuity  Maryam
content:
She says good governance and performance were essential to tackling internal security threats
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has said governments that perform well should be allowed to complete their five-year terms, arguing that the lack of policy continuity in Pakistan remains a major hurdle to development.
Addressing a delegation of the National Command Authority Senior Officers Leadership Course here on Thursday, she said Pakistan's "excellent image and new face" had emerged before the world during its recent war with India, adding that the army and other security institutions were rendering valuable services for the country's defence.
The chief minister said good governance and performance were essential to tackling internal security threats. "We are Pakistanis first, regardless of whether we belong to Punjab, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan or Gilgit," she said, stressing the need for continuity in national policies.
She said Punjab's governance standards had improved because the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz had remained in government in the province for longer periods. While claiming that terrorism had been brought under control in Punjab, she acknowledged that the threat had not disappeared and said the provincial government remained prepared for possible attacks.
The chief minister said the province had previously had around 70 "no-go areas", but no such area now. "I am responsible for the safety of 140 million people, so I had to take decisions that had not been taken before," she said.
She said the government had strengthened the security infrastructure, particularly in border areas, by establishing fortified check posts and providing weapons and night-vision cameras. She also highlighted round-the-clock surveillance to detect terrorist activities.
The chief minister said the Punjab government had established separate groups for administration and law and order and that special attention was being given to crimes against women and children.

title: PUBG task led British national to rob Lahore bank
description: PUBG task led British national to rob Lahore bank
content:
Police recover vehicle allegedly used in South Cantt bank robbery
Police claimed to have arrested a British national allegedly involved in the robbery of a bank in Lahore's South Cantt area and recovered Rs426,000, two pistols and a 12-bore rifle from his possession, officials said on Friday.
The suspect, identified as Subhan Ali, was arrested after investigators traced his movements through Safe City cameras, according to Lahore Deputy Inspector General of Police (Operations) Faisal Kamran.
Police said Ali allegedly robbed the bank of Rs726,000 and took two weapons belonging to security guards during the incident. The recovered cash was stated by police to be part of the amount allegedly taken from the bank.
The suspect was arrested from a house where police said he had gone after the robbery. A white Honda Civic RS Turbo allegedly used in the incident was also recovered. According to police, its registration number had been concealed with black paint.
Speaking at a press conference at Police Lines Qila Gujjar Singh, DIG Faisal said the suspect entered the bank at around 9:19am and remained there for approximately nine minutes before leaving.
Police said the suspect had planned to flee to Islamabad after the robbery and had rented a vehicle for the purpose, paying its owner Rs300,000.
According to the DIG, Ali arrived in Pakistan from Britain on September 16 following a dispute with his parents. He had previously visited Pakistan in April. Police said he had spent six years working as a taxi driver in Scotland.
During questioning, Ali allegedly told investigators that he had been looking for money after spending around £1,200 he had brought from Britain.
Police said he had already identified the bank near Ghazi Road as a potential target because of its location and the availability of parking near his home.
Police also alleged that the suspect had purchased a pistol from Sialkot for Rs45,000 in April and obtained ammunition from the Thokar area for Rs20,000. Investigators are examining the alleged supply of illegal weapons and seeking to identify anyone who may have facilitated their purchase.
A police account of the investigation also linked the alleged robbery to the online game PUBG.
According to police sources, Ali allegedly followed a robbery-related task or instructions in the game, including wearing clothing and a mask similar to those described in the game.
Police further claimed that after the robbery, the suspect returned to his under-construction house, placed the stolen money on a table and resumed playing the game. Investigators said he also changed the vehicle's registration plates before continuing to play.
According to the police account, officers tracking his movements through Safe City cameras eventually reached the house, where they found him with a pistol, the allegedly stolen cash and a briefcase.
Police said the suspect had no previous criminal record.
South Cantt police have registered a case and seized the alleged weapons, vehicle, cash and other material as part of the investigation.

title: Release of answer keys, results of MDCAT 'vague' | The Express Tribune
description:
Release of answer keys, 
results of MDCAT 'vague'
content:
PMDC had refrained varsities from releasing question papers
Important facts have emerged regarding the decision to release the answer keys and results of the Medical and Dental College Admission Test (MDCAT) in Sindh without making the question paper available to candidates.
Although Sukkur IBA University apparently did not release the MDCAT question paper, it has now emerged that the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC), through a notification issued on September 10, had barred all universities conducting the test from releasing the question paper.
The notification, issued 10 days before the examination, directed the participating universities to collect the question papers from candidates immediately after the test and ensure that no candidate retained a copy. It stated that withholding the question paper from candidates was necessary to ensure a better examination process.
The notification was issued by the PMDC's Registration Office, Examination Department, and copies were also sent to the health secretaries of all four provinces.
More than 33,000 candidates appeared in the MDCAT in Sindh on September 20, including over 9,000 from Karachi. However, the non-release of the question paper after the examination created uncertainty, with a large number of candidates claiming that the publication of answer keys alone did not allow them to verify whether their responses had been marked correctly.
When contacted by The Express Tribune, Sukkur IBA Vice Chancellor Dr Asif Sheikh said the university had released the question paper last year but could not do so this year without PMDC's permission. He added that the university would release the paper if the council granted approval, even now.
Meanwhile, PMDC President Dr Rizwan Taj disclosed that the notification barring the release of question papers had been issued on the recommendation of the vice chancellors of the universities conducting the test.
According to Dr Taj, the vice chancellors had advised against releasing the question paper.
The MDCAT consisted of 180 multiple-choice questions, and candidates were provided with carbon copies of their Optical Mark Recognition (OMR) answer sheets. However, the question papers were collected from them immediately after the examination.
Only the answer key was uploaded on the night of September 20, while the question paper remained unavailable. Some candidates alleged that certain answers in the English and Logical Reasoning sections of the published key appeared to be incorrect. They maintained that releasing the question paper would have enabled them to verify the answers and identify any discrepancies.
Responding to these concerns, the Sukkur IBA vice chancellor said the university had reviewed the answer keys several times and was confident of their accuracy. However, he reiterated that the university was bound by the PMDC's instructions regarding the release of the question paper.

title: TDS surge at Kotri Barrage raises water quality concerns
description: TDS surge at Kotri Barrage raises water quality concerns
content:
TDS levels at the Kotri Barrage upstream point increased by 280 milligrams per litre in a single day
A sharp rise in total dissolved solids (TDS) in the Indus River at Kotri Barrage has raised concerns over deteriorating raw water quality, prompting irrigation authorities to seek urgent measures to prevent further contamination.
TDS levels at the Kotri Barrage upstream point increased by 280 milligrams per litre in a single day, reaching 940mg/litre on October 1, according to water tests cited by the Kotri Barrage Division. The level is close to the World Health Organization's guideline value of 1,000mg/litre for TDS in drinking water.
The Executive Engineer of Kotri Barrage Division, Jamshoro, Zafarullah Soomro, wrote an emergency letter on Thursday to the Superintending Engineer, Baghar Circle, Hyderabad, drawing attention to the deteriorating quality of raw water in the Indus at Kotri Barrage.
The letter said daily water-analysis reports provided by the executive engineer of the Hyderabad Water and Sewerage Corporation's Water Supply Treatment Division showed that TDS levels had been rising steadily. The September 30 report recorded TDS at 660mg/litre.
A separate water sample collected by the assistant executive engineer of the Weir Sub-Division, Jamshoro, from the upstream side of the right-bank division wall at Kotri Barrage was tested on October 1 at the Institute of Environmental Engineering and Management, Mehran University of Engineering and Technology, Jamshoro.
