title: The country s system is about to be reset   Naqvi says move will bring improvement in affairs
description: Interior minister says move won t be possible without the support of the business community
content:
Interior minister calls for export-led growth, urges shift towards ‘Made in Pakistan’
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said on Friday that the "country's system was about to be reset" and that this move would improve the state of affairs in Pakistan.
Naqvi’s latest remarks come amid an ongoing debate over the creation of new provinces and restructuring of the country’s administrative setup, after he said earlier this year that the governance system had collapsed and was no longer capable of addressing the country’s challenges
Addressing a ceremony of the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry to congratulate its newly elected office-bearers, Naqvi stated that Pakistan should learn from the "experience and systems" of developed countries.
Also Read : Naqvi vows not to back down from demand for new provinces, says decision must reflect public will
"I will not delve into the details right now, but I have been trying, and while we have achieved many things, I can tell you that the system of this country is going to be reset. For this reset to take place, we need the business community's support. When the system is reset, I remain hopeful that many things will improve," he remarked.
He said the solution to the country’s economic problems was to increase exports by any means possible, adding that whether the target was $170 billion or $9 billion, “every dollar is important” to him.
“Wherever you need me, I am available to you 24 hours a day. As long as I am sitting in this seat, I am here for you,” he told members of the chamber.
He said that over the past three to four months, he had frequently travelled to Iran for mediation efforts aimed at resolving the conflict between Tehran and Washington, which had engulfed the region since Feb 28, when the United States and Israel attacked Iran.
Naqvi said those who had not visited Iran might assume that the country, having been at war and under sanctions for 30 to 40 years, would be devastated, but those who travelled with him were surprised by the level of self-reliance there.
“They have a construction industry, an automobile industry — name anything and they manufacture it in their own country,” he said.
He urged the members to consider shifting towards “Made in Pakistan”, saying that if the goods currently imported from abroad were produced domestically, it would be highly beneficial for the country.
“If Iranians can manufacture and do everything themselves, why can’t we?” the minister asked.
While acknowledging that the country would continue to rely on oil imports, he said Pakistan also imported other goods worth more than $40 billion annually and that this bill could be reduced to $20 billion.
“This is also very easy to do. If we set targets of $10 billion and $5 billion and start working towards them, God willing, we can make significant progress in three to four years,” he said.
He suggested that the chamber should, alongside increasing exports, also prepare a “Made in Pakistan” proposal for Islamabad so that work could be undertaken on both fronts.
Read : Governance system has collapsed: Naqvi
The current debate over new provinces began on July 30, when Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi called for additional administrative units or provinces as part of a broader overhaul of the country’s governance system. Naqvi argued that meaningful structural reforms were needed to improve governance, deliver justice and create opportunities for young people.
A day later, his proposal appeared to receive support from Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, who said an administrative reset, if required, should be undertaken to ensure good governance
The proposal quickly became politically sensitive in Sindh, where the PPP strongly opposed any move to divide the province. Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah rejected Naqvi’s assessment that the governance system had collapsed and called the proposal outdated, warning that no bloodshed would be allowed over the creation of new provinces.
The debate widened in August when Muttahida Qaumi Movement–Pakistan (MQM-P) backed the creation of new provinces and called for a national dialogue with political parties. The party argued that Pakistan’s growing population, poor governance and concentration of political power made greater administrative devolution necessary. The move put the party, which is part of the federal coalition but sits in opposition in Sindh, at odds with the PPP’s position on the province.
The PPP, meanwhile, maintained that administrative reform and the division of Sindh were separate questions. Sindh minister Nasir Hussain Shah said the provincial government was willing to discuss measures to improve governance and devolve power, but rejected linking those reforms to the creation of a new province.
The dispute reached the Sindh Assembly at the beginning of September. On September 3, the house unanimously passed a resolution rejecting any proposal to divide Sindh or alter its territorial limits. The resolution described Sindh as a “historic, civilisational and constitutional entity” and declared that “Sindh is one and shall remain one”.
Read More : PTI's Barrister Gohar warns against dividing provinces without broad public consensus
Naqvi, however, showed no sign of backing away. On September 5, he said he would continue to support new provinces regardless of whether he remained in office, arguing that the ultimate decision should belong to the people rather than politicians or governments. He said the public should first be told the “pros and cons” of creating new administrative units before being allowed to decide.
That position has since raised another question over how public opinion could be formally established. A constitutional debate emerged over whether a referendum could be used to gauge support for new provinces. Article 48(6) allows a matter of national importance to be put to a referendum following approval by a joint sitting of Parliament, although a referendum itself would not create a new province; any change to provincial boundaries would still have to follow the constitutional process.
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan warned on September 7 that dividing Sindh or any other province without the consent of its people and representatives would weaken the federation. He called for a commission and extensive deliberations before the issue was taken to parliament.
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, while accepting that Sindh had the right to take its own position, also said a final decision would have to emerge through consensus. Asif separately suggested that Islamabad could be used as a starting point for any future administrative restructuring, while Prime Minister’s Adviser Rana Sanaullah said the question of new provinces should be taken up at the relevant forums and resolved through consensus among political parties.

title: AJKEC officially notifies four unopposed AJK Council members
description: Three members backed by PML N and the fourth by PPP
content:
Three members backed by PML-N and the fourth by PPP
The Azad Jammu and Kashmir Election Commission (AJKEC) on Friday officially notified four members elected “unopposed” to the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Council.
According to a notification issued by the commission, the four members were declared elected on the basis of poll results received from the respective returning officers.
The elected members have been identified as Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) leaders Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas, Chaudhry Muhammad Saeed and Chaudhry Manzoor Ahmed alongside Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) leader Chaudhry Latif Akbar.
Read: AJKEC orders re-polling at 23 polling stations
Chaudhry Latif Akbar and Chaudhry Manzoor Ahmed represent Muzaffarabad division, Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas represents Bagh division, and Chaudhry Muhammad Saeed represents Mirpur division, respectively.
The AJKEC formally published the names of the four elected members under Section 18 of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Council (Election) Act, 1976.
Copies of the notification have also been sent to the relevant authorities, the AJK Legislative Assembly Secretariat, Information Department and other concerned institutions.
Read more: PML-N's Najeeb Naqi takes oath as 23rd president of AJK
It is worth noting that members of the Kashmir Council serve a five-year term and receive a monthly salary of Rs180,000. Its four seats had fallen vacant following the expiry of the five-year terms of their previous occupants.
The AJKEC had initially scheduled polling for October 12, but with four candidates filing nominations for the vacant seats, the members were declared “elected unopposed” following the completion of the poll process.
The AJK Council is a constitutional body established under the AJK Interim Constitution Act of 1974. It provides an institutional link between the governments of Pakistan and AJK, with its composition and functions defined by the constitutional framework.

title: PM announces Rs12 5m  assistance for families of Pakistanis killed in Somalia hostage situation
description: Announces govt will  also provide one house per family to families of those martyred during the recovery operation
content:
Announces govt will also provide one house per family to kin of those martyred during the recovery operation
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday announced financial assistance of Rs12.5 million rupees per household, free education for children and residential accommodation for the families of the three Pakistanis who were killed during the recovery operation off the coast of Somalia in a hostage situation.
The Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said in a post on X that PM Shehbaz announced that the government would also provide healthcare facilities to the children of Syed Kashi Umar, Mahmood Ahmad Ansari and Rafiullah Khan. Additionally, it would also provide one house per family to these individuals' families for residential purposes.
"The prime minister said that the bereaved families will not be left alone in this difficult time, and the government will provide all possible support and assistance," the PMO said.
Prime Minister @CMShehbaz has announced financial assistance, free education for the children, and residence for the families of three Pakistanis, who lost their lives during the rescue operation off the coast of Somalia @PakPMO #News #RadioPakistan https://t.co/nBLG0TbCEn
The statement said that PM Shehbaz had a telephonic conversation with Umar's Azhaan Kashi, in which he extended his condolences on the death.
Read : Somali pirates kill three Pakistanis during rescue operation
وزیر اعظم محمد شہباز شریف کی صومالیہ میں جاں بحق ہونے والے پاکستانی کاشف عمر کے بیٹے اذہان کاشف سے ٹیلیفون پر گفتگو ہوئی. وزیر اعظم نے سید کاشف عمر کے انتقال پر انکے بیٹے اذہان کاشف سے دلی تعزیت کا اظہار کیا. وزیرِ اعظم نے کہا کہ ہم اپ کے غم میں برابر کے شریک ہیں۔ اللہ…
"The prime minister said that we share equally in your grief. May Allah Almighty grant Syed Kashi Umar a high station in paradise and give your family the strength to bear this shock. The prime minister assured that the government will bring the bodies of Syed Kashi Umar and the other two martyred Pakistanis back to Pakistan as soon as possible," the PMO stated.
It added that the premier directed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and all other relevant institutions to remain in direct contact with the families of the deceased at every stage.
Read More : Pakistan in contact with Somalia over recovery of saved, slain crew of MT Honour 25: FO
He also directed the Foreign Office and the Pakistan embassy to expedite the process of transferring the bodies to Pakistan while maintaining continuous contact with Somali authorities and other relevant parties.
"The prime minister also instructed that all possible measures be taken to provide the best medical facilities to the injured Pakistanis and to ensure the safe return of the other Pakistani crew members".
The oil tanker Honour 25, sailing under the Somali flag from Oman to Somalia, was hijacked by pirates on April 21. There were 17 crew members aboard, 10 of whom were Pakistani nationals. The families of the Pakistani hostages had continuously appealed to the government for the safe release of their loved ones.
During their captivity, the pirates initially demanded a ransom of $3 million for their release. The demand was later reduced to $1.9 million and subsequently to $1 million.
According to the surviving crew members, the governments of Somalia and the semi-autonomous region of Puntland in northeastern Somalia launched a joint operation to free the hostages from the pirates. An exchange of fire took place between Somali security forces and the pirates during the operation.
Pakistani sailors Hussain Yousuf and Imran Ali, who survived the attack, contacted the Ansar Burney Welfare Trust office in Karachi using the ship captain’s mobile phone and provided details of the incident.
The Pakistani crew members said that when the pirates came under pressure and began retreating, they opened indiscriminate fire on the abducted crew members before fleeing the vessel.
Three Pakistani sailors were among the five crew members killed , and four sailors were injured, according to survivors and the Ansar Burney Welfare Trust.
All the Pakistani crew members who were killed or injured were from different areas of Karachi. Their families had spent months seeking the safe release of their loved ones, staging peaceful protests and repeatedly approaching government authorities.

Jennifer Lawrence is reuniting with 'No Hard Feelings' director Gene Stupnitsky for Apple rom-com One Month Mark
Jennifer Lawrence is set to reunite with No Hard Feelings director Gene Stupnitsky for the upcoming romantic comedy One Month Mark , which is being developed by Apple Original Films and Chernin Entertainment.
Stupnitsky is in final negotiations to direct the film, according to Deadline. Lawrence is attached to star and produce through her production company, Excellent Cadaver. Sophie Fleur de Bruijn wrote the screenplay.
The contemporary romantic comedy centres on two people with contrasting relationship histories. The film’s logline describes a woman who has never stayed in a relationship for more than a month and a man who has never gone longer than a month without being in one.
Apple Studios will produce the project, with Chernin Entertainment’s David Ready and Peter Chernin serving as producers. Lawrence will produce alongside her Excellent Cadaver producing partner Justine Ciarrocchi. De Bruijn and Brady Fujikawa are executive producers.
One Month Mark attracted significant interest after Chernin Entertainment acquired the spec script following a competitive auction. The project reportedly drew interest from more than 40 producers, including major production companies, independent financiers and genre-focused labels.
Lawrence and Stupnitsky previously worked together on the 2023 romantic comedy No Hard Feelings , which starred Lawrence alongside Andrew Barth Feldman. According to Deadline, Lawrence pushed to reunite with Stupnitsky for the new project following their previous collaboration.
Stupnitsky previously directed the 2019 comedy Good Boys and co-created the Emmy-nominated series Jury Duty . His writing credits include Bad Teacher , while his recent producing work includes the Sony comedy Narcs .
The filmmakers are now expected to begin searching for Lawrence’s co-star for One Month Mark , with further casting details yet to be announced.

title: Govt increases petrol by Rs2 1  diesel by 30 paisas till Oct 5
description: Petrol price increases to Rs392 76 per litre  while HSD will cost Rs399 64 under daily price mechanism
content:
Petrol price increases to Rs392.76 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs399.64 under daily price mechanism
The federal government on Friday increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.1 and 30 paisas per litre, respectively, till October 5.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs392.76 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs399.64 per litre from October 3 to October 5.
The latest revision comes a day after the government increased the price of petrol by Rs3.26 per litre, while decreasing the price of HSD by Rs1.01 per litre for October 2.
Read : Govt increases petrol by Rs3.26, cuts diesel by Rs1.01 for Oct 2
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices fell $2 after European leaders agreed ​on Friday to a request by US President Donald Trump to release diesel from their reserves to lower ‌prices and reduce the need to import fuel from America.
Brent was down $1.80, or 1.76%, at $100.50 a barrel at 10:49 am CDT (1649 GMT). West Texas Intermediate dropped $2.02, or 2.18%, to $90.85 a barrel.
European Union countries agreed to a French ​proposal to release additional diesel stockpiles, a source familiar with details of the discussion told Reuters .
"Europe is feeling pretty vulnerable," said Phil Flynn, senior ​analyst with the Price Futures Group. "Europe would be one of the areas to suffer the most if we put an export ban on ​diesel."

Bartlett Sher, known for directing To Kill a Mockingbird and South Pacific , will direct the Broadway production. The creative team also includes choreographer Mandy Moore, scenic designer Derek McLane and costume designer Jennifer Moeller.

title: Saudis plan assault on Houthis to break Red Sea chokehold
description: The operation  expected to be launched in the coming weeks  will be led by Yemeni forces on the ground
content:
The operation, expected to be launched in the coming weeks, will be led by Yemeni forces on the ground
Saudi Arabia is planning an offensive against the Houthis in Yemen, with options being considered, including a coastal push to secure the Red Sea shipping route or an assault on multiple fronts, regional and Western officials told Reuters .
The operation, expected to be launched in the coming weeks, will be led by Yemeni forces on the ground, which are overseen by Riyadh, and supported by Saudi air strikes, according to six people with knowledge of the preparations.
While the US is already providing ​intelligence to support Riyadh's operations in Yemen, and some regional and European nations are providing mainly defensive military aid to the kingdom, the Saudi allies aren't expected to play a direct role in combat operations, said the people ‌who requested anonymity to discuss security matters.
Saudi Arabia entered neighboring Yemen's civil war in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition in support of the internationally recognised government, which the Houthis had driven out of the capital Sanaa. A truce agreed between the warring parties in 2022 largely held until this year, when the Houthis launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi shipping and oil infrastructure in a spillover from the Iran war.
Read: Meeting of Makkah defence pact in Saudi Arabia next week to focus on Houthi attacks: FM Dar
A key objective of the planned Saudi offensive, which hasn't been previously reported, is aimed at reversing the rapid gains made by the Houthis last month when they advanced down the coast and seized control of the ​Bab el-Mandeb strait, according to people with knowledge of the plans who include Gulf and Yemeni officials and Western diplomats.
The Saudis are considering two possible options for the assault, the Gulf and Yemeni officials said: Either a narrowly focused attack on ​the area around Bab el-Mandeb or a broader offensive that also includes other synchronised attacks on multiple fronts around Yemen, in the governorates of Al-Bayda, Marib, Taiz and Al-Jawf.
More than 100,000 Yemeni troops could ⁠be mobilized in the offensive, depending on the scale, the officials all said.
Spokespeople for the Saudi and Yemeni governments, the Houthi group and the US military didn't immediately respond to requests for comment about the Saudi plans.
Bab el-Mandeb is the southern exit passage of the Red ​Sea, a key shipping route between the Mediterranean and Asia that's assumed even more importance this year as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, which has been effectively closed by the Iran conflict.
Riyadh has concluded it cannot enter new Yemeni peace negotiations with the Houthis while they remain in control of Bab el-Mandeb, giving them significant global leverage, the Western diplomats and Gulf official said.
Read more: Explainer: Why is the Bab el-Mandeb Strait so important?
The six people with knowledge of the Saudi preparations couldn't give a precise timing for the launch of the offensive, with their estimates ranging from within a week to after the US midterm elections in early November.
Michael Ratney, a former US ambassador to Saudi Arabia, said he expected an offensive to be narrowly focused and certainly more modest in scope than the Saudi-led operation in 2015 that sought to rout the militants.
"As much as they want to vanquish the Houthis completely, they also need to get back to ​status quo ante before Houthis controlled territory along Bab el-Mandeb," he added. "Ideally, it would be a fairly limited operation to retake coastal areas and get back to normal maritime traffic."
The Houthis have become Iran's most formidable ally in the Middle East since Israel's degradation of Hezbollah in ​Lebanon over the past three years.
A Saudi-directed offensive against the group would mark a new flashpoint in a region engulfed by conflict since the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023, and the subsequent US-Israeli war on Iran.
Washington, Saudi Arabia's most powerful ally, is providing military ‌advisers and intelligence⁠, including targeting information, to support Saudi air operations in Yemen, according to one of the Western diplomats.
However, the extent of support may be limited. Reuters has previously reported that US President Donald Trump rebuffed requests by the de facto Saudi ruler Mohammed bin Salman for direct military support such as air strikes.
One of the kingdom's key concerns in launching a new ⁠offensive in Yemen is how to protect its oil facilities and other infrastructure from Houthi drone and missile attacks, according to regional officials who said Riyadh has asked several allies for help with defensive systems.
France, meanwhile, has announced it will send defensive systems and troops to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Red Sea port city of Yanbu.
Any ground operation inside Yemen will rely on the disparate coalition of Yemeni fighting factions that Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates armed and trained at earlier stages of the civil war when the conflict ground to a bloody stalemate.
"Many anti-Houthi forces are still not organised or prepared for the kind of sustained offensive required to push back a disciplined Houthi military force. And they are being tested right now, ⁠as the Houthis apply ​pressure across several fronts at once," said Yemen analyst Mohammed Albasha.
Yemeni forces were further fractured last winter when southern fighters backed by the UAE tried to take ​territory in the east and announce secession plans, leading to their defeat by Saudi-backed fighters after a series of clashes.
Ali Shihabi, a Saudi political analyst close to government thinking, cautioned that the outcome of any offensive by the Saudis against the Houthis would depend on how ground forces perform.
"The priority so far has been to defend the positions on ​the ground and stabilize the front, but certainly they will be going on the offensive," he said. "Success greatly depends on the quality of the performance of the local forces."

title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard shares never before seen photos of Ken Urker and daughter after his death
description: Blanchard described him as an  amazing father  and said he would remain her  soulmate  and  red string
content:
Blanchard described him as an 'amazing father' and said he would remain her 'soulmate' and 'red string'
Gypsy Rose Blanchard has shared never-before-seen photos and videos of her late fiancé Ken Urker and their daughter, Aurora Raina, following his death.
Blanchard posted the emotional Instagram carousel on Friday, October 2, remembering Urker as her “greatest love story”. The first photo showed Urker smiling at a restaurant, while another clip featured the couple telling each other they loved one another as they played with Snapchat filters.
She also shared a video of Urker spending time with their daughter Aurora, whom they welcomed in December 2024. In the clip, the family of three could be seen sitting together on a sofa while using a cat Snapchat filter.
Other memories showed Blanchard and Urker joking together, including one video in which they recreated the famous spaghetti scene from Disney’s Lady and the Tramp . Alongside the carousel, Blanchard wrote that Urker would “always be my greatest love story” and would be “remembered and loved forever”.
Blanchard also addressed Urker’s death in a lengthy statement shared on her Instagram Stories. She described him as an “amazing father” and said he would remain her “soulmate” and “red string”, referring to a connection she believes cannot be broken by time, distance or death.
She also claimed that Urker had endured significant public scrutiny and cyberbullying before his death. Blanchard said she believed the pressure and harassment had a profound impact on him, while stressing that their daughter would grow up knowing how deeply her father loved her.
Urker was found dead at a home in Louisiana on October 1, his 34th birthday. Blanchard has said she believes he died from an overdose, although she told People that she did not know whether it was intentional. Officials have not yet confirmed his cause of death, and an investigation remains ongoing.
Blanchard and Urker first connected in 2017 while she was serving a prison sentence for her role in the 2015 killing of her mother, Clauddine “Dee Dee” Blanchard. They became engaged in 2018 before separating in 2019.
After Blanchard was released from prison in December 2023 and later divorced Ryan Anderson, she and Urker rekindled their relationship. They went on to welcome Aurora in December 2024, with Urker becoming the child’s father.

title: NY governor vows to close intoxication rape loophole at Cornell University
description: New York AG Letitia James named special prosecutor to probe alleged Cornell gang rape after charges were dropped
content:
New York AG Letitia James named special prosecutor to probe alleged Cornell gang rape after charges were dropped
New York's Governor Kathy Hochul vowed on Friday to close a legal loophole allowing offenders to avoid rape charges if their victims were willingly intoxicated, as in the case of an alleged gang rape at Cornell University.
"It should not matter whether they chose to use drugs or alcohol. Voluntary intoxication is not a licence for sexual assault or gang rape. Period," Hochul told reporters. "I support closing this loophole, and will work with the New York State Legislature to accomplish this."
New York Attorney General Letitia James has been appointed special prosecutor to investigate an alleged gang rape at Cornell University, the state's governor announced, following an outcry over prosecutors' decision not to file charges two years ago.
The investigation was reopened on Monday after the alleged victim filed a civil lawsuit, fueling allegations that the elite college failed to properly hold the men accountable.
Read More: Hudson Williams speaks out over Cornell sexual assault case, calls for arrests
The alleged victim said in her lawsuit that in 2024 she was drugged with ketamine, assaulted and raped by seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity, a social club for male students.
"The young woman at the centre of this case deserves to know that every fact will be examined and justice pursued," Hochul added in a post on X.
Choosing to have a drink is not consent, and it’s never a license for sexual assault. New York law should reflect that. I support closing the voluntary intoxication loophole and will work with the Legislature to get it done.
James, a Democrat who has clashed repeatedly with US President Donald Trump, said on X that she was "ready to lead a process guided by the facts and the law".
Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said this week that he planned to file criminal charges against the seven men.
He said his office declined to prosecute in 2024 because the victim's testimony did not establish a lack of consent.
Following the allegations, Cornell closed the fraternity and temporarily suspended the students alleged to be involved, several of whom were later expelled.

title: Niall Horan s  This Town  becomes bigger than any One Direction single
description: Harry Styles     Sign of the Times  and Zayn   s  Pillowtalk  have both also reached five times platinum status
content:
Harry Styles’ 'Sign of the Times' and Zayn’s 'Pillowtalk' have both also reached five-times platinum status
Niall Horan’s first solo single, This Town, has officially become bigger than any One Direction single in the US after earning a new five-times platinum certification.
The song reached the milestone on September 29, exactly 10 years after its release and Horan’s solo debut. The Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) certification means This Town has accumulated five million equivalent units in the US.
The new certification also puts Horan alongside two of his former One Direction bandmates. Harry Styles’ Sign of the Times and Zayn’s Pillowtalk have both also reached five-times platinum status, making the three songs the most highly certified debut solo singles from members of the group in the US.
This Town peaked at No. 20 on the Billboard Hot 100, while Pillowtalk reached No. 1 and Sign of the Times peaked at No. 4. The RIAA certifications are based on combined sales and streaming units rather than chart position.
Horan’s achievement is particularly notable when compared with One Direction’s own catalogue. The group’s highest-certified single in the US is currently What Makes You Beautiful, which is four-times platinum. As a result, This Town now holds a higher RIAA certification than any single released by the group.
However, This Town is not the most highly certified solo song by a former One Direction member. Styles’ Watermelon Sugar has reached seven-times platinum, while As It Was has been certified six-times platinum in the US. Both therefore remain above Horan’s latest milestone.
The other former members have yet to match the five-times platinum mark with their debut solo singles. Liam Payne’s Strip That Down is currently three-times platinum, while Louis Tomlinson’s Just Hold On, recorded with Steve Aoki, is certified gold.
Released on September 29, 2016, This Town marked the beginning of Horan’s solo career while One Direction was on hiatus. Ten years later, the track has reached a certification milestone that surpasses the US certification of every One Direction single.

title: 'Spring Awakening' revival extends Off-Broadway run into spring 2027 | The Express Tribune
description: 'The Spring Awakening' revival has extended its Off-Broadway run at Studio Seaview through April 4, 2027
content:
'The Spring Awakening' revival has extended its Off-Broadway run at Studio Seaview through April 4, 2027
The Off-Broadway revival of Spring Awakening will now run into spring 2027 following what producers described as “unprecedented demand” for the musical.
The revival, created by Steven Sater and the late Duncan Sheik, has extended its run at Studio Seaview through April 4, 2027. The production was previously scheduled to close on Feb. 14.
Previews for the Spring Awakening revival will begin on Nov. 27, with opening night set for Dec. 17. Danya Taymor directs the new production.
In a statement, Seaview CEO said the response to Taymor’s production had been strong and highlighted the lasting impact of Sheik and Sater’s work. The extension allows the current cast and creative team to continue the production for several additional weeks.
Based on Frank Wedekind’s 1891 play, Spring Awakening follows a group of German teenagers in the late 19th century as they navigate sexuality, identity and adulthood while living under strict social expectations.
The musical originally premiered on Broadway in 2006, with a cast that included Jonathan Groff, Lea Michele and John Gallagher Jr. The production ran until 2009 at the Eugene O’Neill Theatre and won eight Tony Awards, including Best Musical.
Sheik, who died on Sept. 17 at age 56, received two Tony Awards for Spring Awakening , winning Best Original Score and Best Orchestrations. He was also known for his 1990s hit song “Barely Breathing,” which spent 55 weeks on the Billboard Hot 100 between 1996 and 1997.
The musical previously received another revival in 2015 through Deaf West Theatre, directed by Michael Arden.
The latest Spring Awakening revival marks another return for the acclaimed musical, with its extended Off-Broadway engagement now continuing through April 2027.

title: Bilawal hails govt opposition talks  hopes for unconditional end to long march
description: Says terrorism poses existential threat  hopes talks allow nation to unite against the menace
content:
Says terrorism poses existential threat, hopes talks allow nation to unite against the menace
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Friday welcomed the government’s decision to engage the opposition to find political solutions, saying he hoped the talks would lead to an unconditional end to the long march and allow the country to unite against terrorism.
His remarks came as the first round of talks between the government and opposition concluded on Friday, with the two sides agreeing to meet again at 2pm on Saturday in the National Assembly (NA) speaker’s chamber.
“I’m pleased that the government has accepted the PPP’s suggestion to jointly engage politically with the opposition in an effort to find political solutions to political problems,” he wrote in a post on X.
I’m pleased that the government has accepted the PPP’s suggestion to jointly engage politically with the opposition in an effort to find political solutions to political problems. The challenge of terrorism has become an existential threat to Pakistan, particularly given the…
Bilawal said the challenge of terrorism had become an existential threat to Pakistan, particularly given the active support he said such groups received from neighbouring countries.
“I hope these talks conclude with the opposition unconditionally calling off its long march, allowing us to come together as a nation to combat the menace of terrorism and address the threats emanating from neighbouring countries,” he said.
Bilawal added that the PPP had been, and would always remain, committed to combating terrorism through all constitutional means.
Read : TTAP accuses Sherry of breaching talks code as PPP leader calls for end to long march
The talks came after weeks of escalating tensions between the federal government and the PTI-led Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government over the party’s planned October 4 march on Islamabad. PTI had initially announced the protest for September 27 but later postponed it to October 4, while the Centre had increasingly discussed constitutional options, including governor’s rule and emergency , citing the deteriorating security situation in the province.
The government and PPP subsequently formed a six-member committee to engage the PTI, with the opposition also signalling willingness to negotiate but insisting on dialogue without preconditions. Barrister Gohar confirmed that the two sides would meet at Speaker Ayaz Sadiq’s office, while maintaining that the long march would proceed unless the party’s concerns were addressed.
The prospect of federal intervention in K-P had become a major point of contention, with federal ministers citing the province’s security situation, while PTI leaders rejected governor’s rule or emergency and called for political engagement instead. K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi also said the October 4 protest would remain peaceful and rejected warnings of federal intervention.

title: Ben Affleck reveals how his late mother and teacher shaped his life
description: Ben Affleck reflects on his late mother and drama teacher  crediting both with shaping his life and career
content:
Ben Affleck reflects on his late mother and drama teacher, crediting both with shaping his life and career
Ben Affleck is reflecting on the educators who influenced his life, including his late mother, Chris Anne Affleck, and his former high school drama teacher, Gerry Speca.
Speaking to PEOPLE at the world premiere of his new film Animals in Los Angeles on Oct. 1, Affleck praised his mother, who spent 35 years teaching in the Cambridge public school system.
“My mom was an extraordinary teacher and an extraordinary woman,” Affleck said, adding that she made many students’ lives better, as she did his own.
Chris Anne Affleck died on June 2 at age 83 after being diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in December 2025. She retired from teaching in 2008.
Affleck also credited Speca with shaping his values and professional approach. The actor said his former teacher taught him to take his work seriously, respect others, collaborate and understand that there is no “star system” in life.
According to Affleck, Speca’s drama class also gave students space to be vulnerable while encouraging them to take responsibility for their work. He described Speca as a “one-in-a-million teacher” and said he could not overstate his gratitude for the educator’s influence.
The actor said Speca’s approach has continued to shape his professional life and that he directly applied what he learned in the drama classroom while making Animals .
“I used on this film” Affleck said of Speca’s approach to building drama, adding that he hoped his former teacher would like the finished movie.
Animals , which Affleck co-wrote and directed, stars him as Los Angeles mayoral candidate Mark Kimball and Kerry Washington as his wife. The film follows the couple after a threat disrupts their carefully constructed lives.
Animals is scheduled to premiere on Netflix on Oct. 9.

Amazon MGM is projecting an opening weekend between $27 million and $30 million
Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson's Verity has opened ahead of Tom Cruise's Digger at the domestic box office, earning $4.5 million from Thursday preview screenings.
The psychological thriller, based on Colleen Hoover's bestselling novel, is expected to open in around 3,500 cinemas across North America. Amazon MGM is projecting an opening weekend between $27 million and $30 million, while industry estimates have placed the film's debut in a wider range of $24 million to $40 million.
Verity follows Lowen Ashleigh, played by Johnson, a writer hired to complete a successful book series after its author, Verity Crawford, portrayed by Hathaway, is left incapacitated following an accident. Josh Hartnett also stars in the Michael Showalter-directed thriller.
Meanwhile, Digger has taken in $1.2 million from Thursday previews. The Warner Bros. film, directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu and starring Cruise, is opening in roughly 3,300 cinemas.
Cruise plays Digger Rockwell, an oil tycoon whose business practices contribute to an environmental catastrophe. The satirical film also features Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, Sandra Hüller, Michael Stuhlbarg and Jesse Plemons.
Warner Bros. is currently projecting a $12 million to $15 million opening weekend for Digger, after earlier forecasts were significantly higher. Box Office Theory has estimated an even lower range of $7.5 million to $12.5 million.
The two films arrive in cinemas as the domestic box office enters October, with Verity targeting audiences familiar with Hoover's bestselling fiction while Digger marks Cruise's return to an original film and his first collaboration with Iñárritu.
Verity and Digger are both now playing in cinemas, with their full opening-weekend grosses expected to provide a clearer picture of their theatrical performances.

content:
Rehman says country is battling terrorism and the situation is worsening
The Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Ain Pakistan (TTAP) on Friday accused a member of the government negotiating team, PPP Vice President Sherry Rehman, of violating the agreement reached for the talks, saying the opposition had not agreed to postpone its long march unconditionally.
The first round of talks between the government and opposition concluded earlier today, with the two sides scheduled to meet again at 2pm on Saturday in the National Assembly (NA) speaker’s chamber.
Both sides remained tight-lipped about the proceedings, with no details emerging about the negotiations. However, TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Yousafzai accused Rehman of breaching the understanding reached between the two sides to keep details of the talks confidential.
Read More : Govt, opposition conclude first round of talks ahead of PTI’s Oct 4 march
“We strongly condemn her statement. A senior parliamentarian like her should not have acted irresponsibly,” he told Express News .
Yousafzai said the opposition alliance had presented its demands to the government delegation, which had also conveyed its concerns to the opposition.
“We have sought time to consult on the matter,” he said.
He said he could not share details of the negotiations as both sides had agreed that the proceedings would not be made public.
Yousafzai said the details of the talks with the government delegation had been shared with opposition leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai during a meeting, which also discussed the future course of action.
Earlier, Rehman said the PPP’s position was that the PTI would have to end its long march unconditionally.
“Not postpone it, not suspend it, not put it on hold — it has to be ended because this is no way,” she said, adding that there had been no reduction in violence during the long march.

“A critical situation is unfolding in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. Our people are being martyred, policemen and soldiers are being martyred,” she said.
“The PPP has always maintained that terrorism is our red line. Mohtarma [Benazir Bhutto’s] martyrdom is before you, so this is a red line for us,” the PPP leader said, adding that the party did not hold long marches for an individual in any case.
Asked about the discussions and demands during the negotiations, Rehman said she did not want to discuss them to avoid a trust deficit that already existed.
“We have told each other that we will give time to the discussions taking place at this stage. They will come back tomorrow, and whatever the final position is, we will present it to you through your medium,” she said.
She said the government and opposition sides would try to conclude the process by Saturday.
Clarifying her comments later in an interview on Naya Pakistan , she said: "My position was that there should be no outside talk on the details of the negotiations because of the existing trust deficit. There was a joint understanding that we should wait until tomorrow before divulging any specific details. If there are questions posed on talk shows, then the general stated party position can be used to answer such questions. It should be said that negotiations will conclude tomorrow”.
Sherry emphasised that she had not made the statement that PTI had asked for more “time” for the ongoing negotiations, further adding that on the long march it was PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s stated position that democratic methods should be used to resolve issues through “political and constitutional means”, especially given the prevailing instability in the country, with an uptick in terrorism and militancy.
“Zardari and Bilawal both wish to resolve issues under a political framework so that political tensions do not rise further,” she underlined.

title: Over 11 400 Israeli occupiers storm Al Aqsa during Jewish holiday season
description: The governorate said Israeli ministers  rabbis and officials were increasingly conducting public religious rituals
content:
Incursions continued on Friday, with further entries expected on Saturday
A total of 11,409 Israeli occupiers stormed Al-Aqsa Mosque in occupied East Jerusalem during the Jewish holiday season between September 12 and October 1, Palestinian authorities said on Friday.
In a statement, the Jerusalem Governorate said the figure covered incursions from the start of the holiday season through Thursday.
It said 593 occupiers entered the mosque compound on September 13 after it was closed to incursions the previous day, a Saturday.
Another 1,678 occupiers entered on September 20 and 21, including 992 on the first day and 686 on the second, according to the statement.
The governorate said 9,138 occupiers entered the compound during the first five days of Sukkot from September 27 to October 1 .
It said incursions continued on Friday, with further entries expected on Saturday.
Read More: Hamas marks Al-Aqsa Intifada anniversary, urges Arab and Muslim support for Palestinians
The governorate said the incursions were accompanied by increasingly public and widespread religious rituals involving Israeli ministers, rabbis, officials and political figures.
Those taking part included far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir , Zehut party leader Moshe Feiglin and Rabbi Yehuda Glick, according to the statement.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also participated in religious rituals at the Al-Buraq Wall, the governorate said.
Practices inside the Al-Aqsa compound included public and collective prayers, prostration, chanting, dancing, singing, clapping and blowing a horn, according to the statement.
Participants also carried prayer books and sheets and wore religious clothing and shirts bearing images and slogans associated with what they call the “Temple”, it said.
Under the historic and legal status quo, Al-Aqsa Mosque is administered by the Jerusalem Islamic Waqf, which is affiliated with Jordan’s Ministry of Awqaf, and is a place of worship exclusively for Muslims.
Since 2003, Israeli police have allowed occupiers to enter the compound through the Mughrabi Gate under police protection, despite repeated Palestinian and Jordanian calls to halt the incursions.

title: Ted Lasso  honours Anthony Head with emotional tribute

content:
The ninth episode of the current season concluded with a title card reading "In memory of Anthony Head"
Ted Lasso has paid tribute to Anthony Head months after the acclaimed actor's death, honouring his contribution to the Apple TV+ series during an emotional penultimate episode.
The ninth episode of the current season concluded with a title card reading "In memory of Anthony Head", marking the actor's legacy on the hit comedy series. Head played wealthy businessman Rupert Mannion, the former owner of AFC Richmond and a central figure in the show's earlier seasons.
The tribute comes after Rupert's name was reintroduced into the storyline in the latest episode, despite Head's character not appearing in the current season.
Head died in June at the age of 72 after developing complications from pneumonia. His death came several months after the death of his long-term partner, Sarah Fisher, who died in December 2025 after being diagnosed with thyroid cancer.
Head's acting career spanned more than four decades and included some of television's most recognisable roles. He was best known internationally for playing Rupert Giles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, while his other credits included King Uther in Merlin and the Prime Minister in Little Britain.
The actor also had strong ties to Bath, where he lived with Fisher at Tilley Farm, her 90-acre animal sanctuary in Farmborough. Fisher was an animal welfare advocate who cared for rescued horses, ponies and donkeys at the sanctuary.
Fisher was also a long-standing patron of Holly Hedge Animal Sanctuary in North Somerset and supported several other animal charities, including Battersea Cats and Dogs Home.
Following her death, a Battersea spokesperson praised Fisher's contribution to the organisation, saying she had fostered dogs, used her expertise in canine behaviour to train staff and volunteers and contributed in numerous ways to animal welfare.
The latest Ted Lasso tribute adds to the recognition of Head's career following his death, while also acknowledging the lasting impact of his portrayal of Rupert Mannion on the Apple TV+ series.

title: Europe agrees to release diesel stocks Trump says
description: G7 to release 100m barrels of diesel and crude over four months  while urging others to avoid energy export curbs
content:
G7 to release 100m barrels of diesel and crude over four months, while urging others to avoid energy export curbs
European countries ​have agreed to release diesel stocks, US President Donald Trump said on Friday, after the White House pressured governments to do so, in a bid ‌to cool surging fuel prices linked to the Iran war.
"Europe has just agreed to release a massive amount of their heavily stocked Diesel Oil. The process will begin immediately," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social.
Trump's statement followed talks on Friday among EU governments, who discussed a proposal by France for European countries to release 50 million barrels of diesel, and for International Energy Agency members to release 50 million ​barrels of crude oil, three sources familiar with the discussions told Reuters.
Under the proposal discussed by European governments on Friday morning, Europe would release part of the ​diesel volumes in a 20-day period, responding to Trump's demand for a rapid release of fuel stocks, two of the sources said.
G7 say to release '100 mn barrels' of diesel and crude
G7 countries agreed Friday to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil from their reserves over four months, leaders said, agreeing to "refrain from export restrictions on energy" and urging others to do the same.
The announcement came after G7 leaders held talks to coordinate action on fuel prices, after the United States upped pressure on Europe to release its strategic reserves by threatening a diesel export ban.
The seven countries agreed to "a coordinated release through the IEA of 100 million barrels to begin immediately over four months, including a frontloaded substantial diesel release within the first 20 days," they said in a joint statement released by French President Emmanuel Macron's office.
Read More: Oil falls about 3% on talks over diesel, crude stock releases
The leaders also said that there would be no ban on diesel exports between them.
"We reaffirm our commitment to refrain from export restrictions on energy and energy products between G7 countries and call on all producers to refrain from imposing bans that could exacerbate market tensions," the leaders said.
"Our citizens' concerns about energy prices remain a top priority," they added.
"We will monitor developments closely and stand ready to adjust measures as needed."
Macron had convened a video call of G7 leaders -- a group comprising also Britain, Japan, Canada, Germany and Italy -- to discuss joint action after he spoke with Donald Trump.
US diesel futures extended their price losses on Friday after reports of the stock release discussions, and were down more than 4% ​to $4.4491 a gallon. Benchmark European diesel futures fell by over $100 a metric ton, LSEG data showed.
The discussions underscore growing pressure on Europe as Trump considers a potential ban on US diesel exports to help lower domestic fuel prices ahead of November 3 midterm elections.
In weighing its response, the EU needs to balance the need to ease soaring fuel costs against preserving emergency reserves to safeguard against uncertain supply from ​Gulf producers due to disruptions caused by the Iran war.
France's finance and energy ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
French President Macron spoke with Trump overnight, emphasising ​the need to work together to combat rising fuel prices and ensure the global availability of refined products, the Elysee Palace said on Friday. France currently holds the presidency of the G7.
Reuters reported on ‌Thursday that ⁠the Trump administration had told Germany and France to draw down emergency diesel inventories or face a potential US diesel export ban, according to three people close to the discussions.
The US had demanded large European countries including France and Germany release 100 million barrels of diesel within a 20-day window, two of the sources told Reuters on Friday.
Global diesel supply has been hit by the US war with Iran and a Russian ban on exports after Ukraine damaged many of its refineries. Chinese refiners have also suspended October fuel exports to bolster domestic stocks, sources said.
The ​proposed 50-million-barrel release equates to approximately 17% ​of the EU's total emergency stocks of ⁠diesel and gasoil, Eurostat data current as of May 2025 showed.
It reflects around 3% of the bloc's annual consumption of the fuel, Eurostat data show.
Europe used to mainly rely on Russian and Middle Eastern diesel imports but has increasingly relied on imports from the United States ​in recent years.
"Having been caught dragging their feet on promised strategic stock releases earlier this year and now jarred by possible US ​export restrictions, European countries ⁠will likely release more diesel and possibly crude from their stocks," said Bob McNally, president of Rapidan Energy Group.
"European strategic stock releases are a necessary, if not sufficient, condition to prevent US export restrictions, which would still remain on the table given acute political anxiety in the White House about high pump prices."
In the call on Friday, EU countries discussed making a condition for any ⁠agreement on diesel ​stock releases a US commitment to not impose a unilateral diesel export ban, one of the sources said.
The ​32-member IEA agreed in March to a coordinated release of 400 million barrels of strategic oil reserves, in response to the Iran war, the largest such release in history.
IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said this week that members ​had released about two-thirds of those volumes.

title: Apple Music finally arrives in Pakistan after 11 years

content:
Users can now access Apple’s music streaming service through local Apple accounts, with plans starting at Rs379
Apple Music is finally available in Pakistan, more than a decade after Apple first launched its music streaming service.
Subscriptions start at Rs379 per month for the Individual plan and Rs649 for the Family plan, with new users eligible for a one-month free trial.
Pakistan was among four countries added to Apple Music’s availability this week, alongside Albania, Brunei and Burkina Faso.
According to Apple Insider , the expansion was spotted through Apple’s Media Services availability information on September 30.
Apple Music first launched in June 2015, initially rolling out across more than 100 countries. Pakistan, however, remained off the list for the next 11 years, leaving users unable to officially subscribe through a Pakistan-based Apple account.
That has now changed, with Pakistani users gaining official access to Apple’s catalogue of songs, albums and playlists, as well as features including personalised recommendations, offline downloads and, where supported, lossless and Dolby Atmos audio.
For Apple users, the biggest change is that Apple Music is now officially integrated into the local Apple ecosystem. Subscribers can access the service through the Music app on compatible devices without relying on a different regional account.
The arrival also brings Pakistan in line with several other Asian and Middle Eastern markets where Apple Music has been available for years, including India, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Indonesia and Japan.
While the launch does not mean all of Apple’s services are now available in Pakistan, Apple Music marks a notable addition to the company’s offerings in the country.

title: New Mexico wants Meta to pay up to  40 billion in penalties after data privacy trial
description: Meta and New Mexico clashed over penalties  with Meta saying the state s demands exceed conduct proven at trial
content:
Meta and New Mexico clashed over penalties, with Meta saying the state's demands exceed conduct proven at trial
The state of New Mexico asked a judge on Thursday to order Meta Platforms to pay between $35 billion ​and $40 billion in penalties after a jury found the company had misled consumers about the privacy of their data on Facebook in ‌a case that came out of the Cambridge Analytica scandal.
Attorneys for New Mexico made the request at a hearing in a lawsuit brought following revelations that the British political consulting firm, which worked on Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, harvested personal data from as many as 87 million Facebook users through a third-party app without their consent.
The jury returned its verdict ​on September 25. Judge Francis Mathew, who oversaw the trial in Santa Fe, will decide how much Meta must pay in financial penalties.
Attorneys ​for Meta and New Mexico clashed at the hearing over how much was appropriate to order, with Meta arguing that the penalties ⁠the state was seeking don't match the conduct the state focused its case on at trial.
"Well, when the parties go to trial, they roll the ​dice," said Mathew. "They have to accept the consequences of their decision to go to trial, do they not?"
The lawsuit, filed in 2021, accused ​Meta of lying to Facebook users in the state about who had access to their data, how the company handles hate speech and misinformation posted on the platform and other internal policies. The company knew that third parties had broad access to users' personal data, and it tolerated hate speech or other harmful content when it benefited the company's bottom ​line, the state said.
Jurors examined 29 statements made by the company and its leadership on those issues and found 26 of them misleading. They said the ​company had committed more than 43 million violations of New Mexico’s consumer protection laws, based on the number of Facebook users or New Mexico residents who were the audience ‌for each ⁠misleading statement.
Attorneys for Meta had argued at trial that the statements were cherry-picked snippets, and the company had repeatedly acknowledged its handling of misinformation or privacy issues was not perfect.
State law allows the judge to decide how much to fine Meta per violation, up to $5,000.
At the hearing on Thursday, Randi McGinn, a lawyer for New Mexico, said applying the full $5,000 penalty to the number of violations would create too large of a penalty under the US Constitution’s protections on ​due process.
But the judge should order a ​significant payment that will impact ⁠the company, McGinn said.
"This court should speak to Meta in the only language it understands, which is money, and the value of its stock price," McGinn said. She said $35 billion to $40 billion, which represents about 20% of the possible penalties that ​could be awarded under state law from the verdict, would impact the stock price while complying with Meta's ​right to due process ⁠under the Constitution.
At the hearing on Thursday, Matt Nicholson, a lawyer for Meta, called the state's request an "astronomical penalty that would obviously violate a host of constitutional provisions."
In court filings, Meta urged Mathew to cap the penalties at $3.45 billion. The jury may have said it found Meta’s statements misleading, but the evidence shows that Meta ⁠does not sell ​user data and New Mexico did not prove that any consumer had actually been misled, ​the company said in court filings.
The judge said he expected to issue a ruling later this month.
The case is State of New Mexico, et. al., v. Meta Platforms, Inc., case number D-101-CV-2021-00132 in the ​First Judicial District Court of New Mexico.

title: Pakistan must raise fitness levels after Vietnam defeat
description: Head coach says fatigue and defensive lapses cost Shaheens as Vietnam fight back for 4 2 win
content:
Head coach says fatigue and defensive lapses cost Shaheens as Vietnam fight back for 4-2 win
Pakistan head coach Nolberto Solano said fitness and a loss of defensive shape proved decisive as his side suffered a 4-2 defeat by Vietnam to finish bottom of Division I Group B in their maiden FIFA ASEAN Cup campaign on Friday.
Pakistan took a deserved lead through Mohibullah Afridi in the 31st minute after dominating much of the opening half at Jakarta's Gelora Bung Karno Stadium.
But Vietnam responded strongly after the interval, scoring three times before Pakistan pulled one back through veteran Kaleemullah Khan in the 88th minute. Hoang Minh Williams then sealed the victory with Vietnam's fourth goal in the closing moments.
Solano said Pakistan's inability to maintain the intensity of their first-half performance was a major factor in the defeat.
"Honestly, it will be very important for us, a great experience for everyone, and of course disappointed with the result," Solano told reporters after the match.
"We started very well in the first half of the game. We know our issues, we know our problems and unfortunately, fitness at this kind of level is different."
Pakistan, ranked 99 places below Vietnam, had impressed before the break, pressing effectively and restricting their opponents while creating several opportunities.
Mohibullah capitalised on a defensive error to put the Shaheens ahead, but Vietnam levelled through Long Hai Nguyen five minutes after half-time before Duc Hoang Nguyen completed the turnaround in the 57th minute.
Bac Dinh Nguyen extended Vietnam's lead in the 80th minute, before Kaleemullah gave Pakistan hope with a late finish. Williams, however, ended those hopes shortly afterwards.
Solano said his side's pressing became less effective as fatigue set in.
"In general, what I saw today in the second half, we were not able to build the same pressure as we did in the first half," he said.
"As all good teams press together, we had a line in the back that was a bit tired. That is why we dropped deeper and deeper."
Despite the defeat, Solano said Pakistan had benefited from playing against stronger opposition and expressed hope for more international opportunities.
"Apart from that, we participated in the tournament; we did quite well. It was a great experience," he said.
"Hopefully, we get these kinds of games in the future."
Pakistan opened their campaign with a 4-0 defeat by Thailand before recovering from two goals down to draw 2-2 with the Philippines.
The defeat by Vietnam left Pakistan with one point from three matches, while Vietnam finished second behind Thailand.
Solano said the team would now turn its attention to preparations for its next assignment in Bangladesh next month.
"Now we need to prepare in Bangladesh next month," he said.

Piccioli was named to lead Balenciaga in May last year as his predecessor, Demna, moved to Gucci
Balenciaga creative director Pierpaolo Piccioli showed colourful tailoring and minimalist sneakers in his Summer 2027 collection at Paris Fashion Week on Thursday, a year on from his debut for the brand he ‌is seeking to breathe new life into.
Piccioli was named to lead Balenciaga in May last year as his predecessor, Demna, moved to Gucci, part of an attempt by the brands' parent company Kering to reverse a sharp decline in sales across the group.
Previously at Valentino, Piccioli is also tasked with reigniting ⁠interest in the brand's womenswear after Balenciaga became more skewed towards men, and his designs have injected colour into the brand after Demna's black leather-dominated era.
In a bright white set inside the Tennis Club de Paris, models in bomber jackets with cinched waists and high collars marched past front-row guests including American actor Sarah Pidgeon, K-pop star Juyeon, Anna Wintour and Kering chairman Francois-Henri Pinault.
Jackets in bright pink and cobalt blue created colour blocks against wide white trousers and ripped jeans, and the ‌collection ⁠featured flowing gowns in orange and powder pink.
In his show notes, Piccioli highlighted "lightness and softness", as well as wearability – a key aspect of every luxury brand's new designs as they try to win back customers who have been turned off by price hikes since the ⁠pandemic.
"In a focus on how garments move and feel, a priority is inherently afforded to comfort and ease – as if in your own skin," Piccioli wrote.
Footwear was flat and minimalist, with ⁠soft thong sandals and the slipper-like Lounge Sneaker a departure from the chunky oversized sneakers of Demna's era. Large, supple handbags in bright shades of green, orange ⁠and blue had no visible logos.
More daring outfits included a white lace dress with ostrich-feather skirt paired with black combat boots, and a bright orange dress covered in strings of organza flowers.

title: Chinese rocket firm  disease research lab to test space pharmaceutical payloads
description: First payloads will fly aboard reusable Lihong 2  testing drug crystallisation and space pharma equipment
content:
First payloads will fly aboard reusable Lihong-2, testing drug crystallization and space pharma equipment
China's commercial rocket company CAS Space announced that it joined hands with the Guangzhou Laboratory to carry out collaborative research and development on space pharmaceutical payloads, with a plan of a suborbital flight validation by a reusable spacecraft in 2027.
The first group of payloads is planned to fly aboard the company's Lihong-2, a reusable launch vehicle. It will conduct protein and small-molecule drug crystallization experiments as well as early technical validation of space pharmaceutical equipment, the company said.
Based in Guangzhou, the laboratory is dedicated to studying respiratory diseases and their prevention and control. Under the collaboration, the lab will raise scientific questions around drug crystallisation and handle experimental design, sample management, ground control and result analysis.
According to Xu Qiang, a lead researcher at the lab, modern medicine has substantial demand for higher-quality structural data, more stable drug crystal forms, disease models that more closely resemble the human body and more efficient screening tools. The space environment may provide new ways to address some of these challenges.
Read More : Chinese hackers impersonated ex-US official to steal emails from AI experts
he microgravity environment of space can help some proteins form higher-quality crystals and offers new experimental conditions for crystal form screening and particle control of small-molecule drugs. Cells under such conditions also more readily form 3D aggregates that can be used to study disease mechanisms and drug responses, Xu noted.
The company said the Lihong series spacecraft are designed for space medicine research, biomedical experiments, manufacturing and space tourism. In January this year, the company's Lihong-1 rocket completed its suborbital flight test mission in northwest China.
"The near space at altitudes of 100 km to 200 km is an ideal experimental environment for microgravity research like space manufacturing and biomedicine," said Fan Na, vice president of CAS Space.
The company has established a joint space medicine lab with a hospital based on this concept. "It can bring data back quickly, accelerating new drug development," Fan added.
Space pharmaceuticals are an emerging sector within the space economy, alongside space breeding, space materials processing, satellite internet and space tourism.
A World Economic Forum report says the space economy is expected to grow from 630 billion U.S. dollars in 2023 to 1.8 trillion U.S. dollars by 2035. Goldman Sachs and other institutions predict the space economy will grow to several trillion dollars over the next 20 years.

title: Supermodel Naomi Campbell wins appeal against charity trustee ban
description: Model wins appeal against a five year trustee ban after a tribunal found fund misuse was hidden from her
content:
Model wins appeal against a five-year trustee ban after a tribunal found fund misuse was hidden from her
Supermodel Naomi Campbell won her appeal on Thursday against a five-year ban from being a charity trustee, with a London tribunal ruling ​that the misuse of funds at the charity she founded had been ‌concealed from her.
Campbell, one of fashion's most recognisable faces, founded Fashion for Relief in 2005, aiming to raise funds for humanitarian causes by staging runway shows.
But it was removed from the Charity ​Commission's register in 2024 and Campbell banned as a trustee shortly afterward following ​complaints of mismanagement and misconduct.
The Charity Commission found widespread financial mismanagement, ⁠including money raised for good causes having been spent on spa treatments, cigarettes and ​room service when Campbell was staying at a five-star hotel near Cannes in southern ​France in May 2018.
A lawyer acting as a trustee for the charity also received around £290,000 ($382,771) in unauthorised payments for apparent consultancy fees.
Campbell, however, said she had no knowledge that charity funds were spent ​on her expenses and was deceived by another trustee about the unauthorised payments.
Her appeal ​was allowed by the First-Tier Tribunal, which said in its ruling that there was "serious misconduct and ‌mismanagement" ⁠at Fashion for Relief, but that the unauthorised payments and misuse of funds were concealed from Campbell.
The tribunal also found that Campbell "was not responsible for the inappropriate use of the charity's resources or any unjustified expenditure" during her 2018 hotel stay.
Campbell "did share ultimate ​responsibility for the charity's ​failure to keep ⁠proper minutes and file its accounts on time", the tribunal added, but ruled that did not mean she was unfit to ​be a charity trustee.
"I'm so grateful to the tribunal and the ​judges for ⁠taking the time to hear my side, look at the evidence and see the truth of what happened," Campbell said in a statement.
The Charity Commission said it was considering ⁠if the ​ruling had "any wider implications for our work."
"Because of ​our regulatory interventions to protect Fashion for Relief's funds, other charities received almost £250,000 owed to them," a Charity ​Commission spokesperson said.

Two civilians were killed, and another was injured after Indian Border Security Force (BSF) personnel opened fire near the Pakistan-India international border in Kasur, state media reported on Friday, citing security sources.
Pakistan TV said in a post on X that the incident reportedly occurred when three residents from Ladhar village moved a few steps beyond a border pillar. Security sources claimed that the BSF personnel opened fire on the men without a warning.
The deceased were identified as Azmat Rasool and Mohsin Jutt, both residents of Jattan Wali Haveli in Ladhar, the sources said, adding that the third man was also injured in the shooting.
According to the sources, all three men were unarmed and had not attempted to cross the border fence.

The security sources further emphasised that the firing constituted a violation of the arrangements and standard operating procedures governing the international border.
Civilian casualties and injuries inflicted by Indian forces during 2016-2026
Cross-border firing along the Pakistan-India border has repeatedly resulted in civilian casualties, particularly in villages close to the Working Boundary.
In October 2016, the military’s media wing confirmed that two civilians, including a toddler, were martyred and another seven were injured in firing in the Harpal, Pukhlian and Charwah sectors.
Then again, in September 2017 , ISPR said India targeted civilians with mortars and automatic weapons, resulting in the death of Muhammad Zahoor, a civilian in Dewra village.
The following year saw another major escalation. In May 2018, The Express Tribune reported that four members of the same family — a woman, two daughters and a son — were killed in firing along the Working Boundary near Sialkot, with 10 others reported injured. The report cited ISPR and the Foreign Office. The death toll climbed to 16 during a wider six-day confrontation.
A year later in October, the Foreign Office said a 10-year-old boy was martyred , and 16 civilians were critically injured in firing in the Sharda sector.
In May 2020, three civilians were reported seriously injured in the Nikial sector, while in September, two civilians were reported seriously injured in the Baroh sector. Both reports cited Pakistan's Foreign Office.
In 2021, at least seven people were injured, including two elderly persons and a teen, in cross-border shooting. The situation changed for the better after the two sides reaffirmed their ceasefire in February.
Once again in 2023, The Express Tribune reported three civilian deaths and one serious injury in two LoC firing incidents.

“As of right now, detectives have not found any evidence of foul play, but they're still investigating and have not ruled out anything yet,” Matherne said.
The Lafourche Parish Sheriff’s Office responded to an emergency call at a home in Raceland, where officers found Urker dead and began a death investigation.
Blanchard later addressed Urker’s death, saying she believed he died from an overdose after an unknown substance was allegedly found at the scene.
She also said Urker did not have drug issues and described him as a responsible person who was intentional about being a father and partner.
Following his death, his sister, Autumn, addressed the circumstances during a TikTok livestream. She confirmed that his passing was “not of natural causes,” but according to her, law enforcement suspected no foul play.
Urker and Blanchard had previously been engaged while Blanchard was serving a prison sentence for her role in conspiring to kill her mother, Dee Dee Blanchard.
The pair later separated before reconnecting following Blanchard’s split from Ryan Anderson.
Urker and Blanchard welcomed their daughter, Aurora Raina Urker, in December 2024.
According to TMZ , Urker’s autopsy was scheduled for later on October 2.
The results could provide further information as authorities continue investigating the circumstances surrounding his death.
