title: OpenAI dismisses 3 researchers over alleged mishandling of sensitive information
description: The company said researchers mishandled sensitive material  breaching rules and undermining trust in its work
content:
The company said researchers mishandled sensitive material, breaching rules and undermining trust in its work
OpenAI has dismissed three researchers after an internal investigation concluded that they mishandled sensitive company information, the ChatGPT developer told news outlets.
“We have parted ways with three individuals” for violating information-access and handling policies, an OpenAI spokesperson said.
The company said the researchers dealt with sensitive material outside its established procedures, violating internal rules and undermining the trust required for its work.
The Wall Street Journal, which first reported the dismissals late Thursday, identified the researchers as Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak, and Mikita Balesni. It said the alleged misconduct included sharing confidential information with an external AI-safety organization that was helping analyze OpenAI’s models.
Neither the outside organization nor the material allegedly shared was identified publicly. OpenAI has not confirmed the names reported by the newspaper.
The dismissals come amid heightened scrutiny of OpenAI’s safety procedures, as well as questions about the safety of AI for the industry as a whole, following several incidents in which experimental AI agents acted outside their intended boundaries during training or evaluation.
In July, OpenAI agents escaped a restricted testing environment and gained access to the internet before breaching systems operated by the open-source development platform Hugging Face.
The agents exploited previously unknown vulnerabilities, established unauthorized communication channels, and shared information across separate evaluations. OpenAI described the episode as a “warning shot” demonstrating that highly capable agents could circumvent technical controls and take potentially dangerous actions without human direction.
Read More: Chinese hackers impersonated ex-US official to steal emails from AI experts
Company channel for reporting 'misalignment'
A subsequent company review found other instances in which its models affected external websites and services. OpenAI said it had notified third parties whose security controls may have been bypassed or whose services were affected, while stressing that notification did not necessarily mean private data had been accessed or a system fully compromised.
The company also acknowledged that in June, its experimental models accessed Australian government websites without authorization during internal testing. One model obtained non-public access to a Services Australia system and retrieved internal files, credentials and aggregate statistics, although OpenAI said no individual medical records were accessed.
OpenAI has since tightened network restrictions, expanded monitoring, and temporarily paused some training and evaluation involving tool use for its most capable models.
The company has also introduced a framework for publicly reporting examples of model “misalignment,” including unauthorized actions, efforts to evade oversight and communication between agents outside approved channels.
OpenAI has said the industry has not yet solved alignment and monitoring well enough to continue expanding the most advanced AI systems at maximum speed indefinitely.

title: Nadia Hussain  Nadia Afgan speak out against victim blaming  sexual violence
description: Actors question why women face intense scrutiny while men accused of sexual violence can face a different standard
content:
Actors question why women face intense scrutiny while men accused of sexual violence can face a different standard
Nadia Hussain and Nadia Afgan have spoken out against victim blaming and what they described as unequal standards in the way society responds to sexual violence and allegations of abuse.
The two actors shared separate posts on Instagram, highlighting what they see as a tendency to scrutinise victims and question their behaviour while those accused of wrongdoing may face comparatively less scrutiny.
Nadia Hussain shared a message addressing the different ways society can treat victims and people accused of wrongdoing. Her post questioned why certain women are subjected to harsh social judgement while the actions of men connected to the same situations can receive comparatively less scrutiny.
She also stressed the importance of accountability in cases of sexual violence, arguing that responsibility should not be shifted towards victims or those who speak out.
"We live in a world where sex workers are judged but not their clients, single mothers are judged but not absent fathers, rape victims are judged but not the rapists and the ones who speak out are judged instead of the ones covering it up,” Hussain wrote.
Nadia Afgan also addressed victim blaming, focusing on what she described as contrasting standards when allegations involve women and men.
In her Instagram statement, Afgan argued that women can face damaging assumptions and character judgements without substantial evidence, while allegations of sexual violence involving men may be met with demands for extensive proof before people are willing to believe them.
She wrote, "Men will believe a woman is a hoe with zero evidence, but need a documentary, 12 witnesses, DNA, CCTV, and God’s signature to believe a man is a rapist”.
Afgan’s post added another perspective to the discussion, drawing attention to the role that credibility, gender stereotypes and social attitudes can play when allegations of sexual misconduct are discussed publicly.
Earlier this week, actor Ayesha Omar challenged the idea that feminism is synonymous with hatred of men, using a series of Instagram posts to highlight cases of violence against women in Pakistan, India and the United States.
“Why does the word feminism bother men so much?” Omar wrote in her caption, accompanying a quote attributed to Nadia Carly that read: “Feminism doesn’t hate men. It hates abusers, sexists, misogynists, rapists, pedophiles, and deadbeats. And good men aren’t bothered by that because they hate them too.”
Omar followed the post with a series of Instagram stories highlighting recent cases of violence against women from around the world and drawing attention to the circumstances surrounding each incident.
Last month, television host Anoushey Ashraf spoke candidly about the exhausting judgement Muslim women can face over the simplest aspects of their lives.
She shared a photo dump on Instagram, opening with a direct message: “Hello, fellow Muslim liberal girl. Can we talk about some of the things that exhaust me?” In her caption, she wrote, “Currently (90% of the time) being audited by both sides. Surely I can’t be the only one going through this?”
The post featured glimpses of her outfits alongside the questions and criticism she said she encountered — from whether she ate halal and why she kept dogs to whether she prayed. The central message was clear: “Too Muslim for some. Not Muslim enough for others.”
“Having to prove my Muslimness to the very Muslim Muslims and my lack thereof to the non-Muslims. Having to explain my faith to some and my outfits to others. A skirt? Radical for some. Regular praying? Radical for others,” she wrote.

Actor Hina Chaudhary has given her followers a glimpse into a difficult period in her life, revealing that she recently underwent a tough surgery and is now taking time to focus on her recovery.

title: Wang wins Asian Games tennis gold and Olympic berth
description: The 25 year old breeze past her compatriot 6 2  6 1 in 66 minutes in Nagoya
content:
The 25-year-old breeze past her compatriot 6-2, 6-1 in 66 minutes in Nagoya
China's Wang Xiyu, fresh from conquering top seed Alexandra Eala, toppled Zhang Shuai to win Asian Games women's tennis singles gold on Friday -- and a ticket to the Los Angeles Olympics.
The 25-year-old Wang breezed past her compatriot 6-2, 6-1 in 66 minutes at the Higashiyama Park Tennis Center in Nagoya.
Tennis is one of seven sports at the Games where the winners receive an Olympic qualification place.
Wang paid tribute to the 37-year-old Zhang, who has won multiple Grand Slam doubles titles and has now added a second Asian Games singles silver medal to the one she won in 2018 in Jakarta.
The veteran Zhang also bagged a team tennis gold in Guangzhou in 2010, when Wang would have been just nine years old.
"She is someone I really respect. Everything that she's been through is also a form of encouragement to me," said Wang.
"Still, on the court, the biggest form of respect I can show is by bringing my best to play her."
The one-sided match was a contrast to the battle Wang had with Philippines star Eala 24 hours earlier, when the Chinese world number 85 came through 3-6, 6-3, 6-2 after two hours and 34 minutes of intense action.
"This is what sport, what elite competition, is like. Your actions speak for you," added Wang.
"It's when you experience success through the trials that you know what it was all for. Keep trying."
She then revealed her tennis skills were way ahead of her culinary efforts, but said it was important never to give up.
"I tried to make a dish of stir-fried cauliflower and it all became burnt," Wang said.
"There's some difficulty in that dish, it's so easy to get it wrong. I'll keep trying."
The men's singles gold medal match on Saturday will see Hong Kong's world number 100 Coleman Wong take on China's 111th-ranked Wu Yibing.

title: Meeting of Makkah defence pact in Saudi Arabia next week to focus on Houthi attacks  FM Dar
description: FM Dar says  at least six countries  have expressed interest in joining the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
content:
FM Dar says 'at least six countries' have expressed interest in joining the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Friday that an emergency meeting of the strategic political and defence committee under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA) between Pakistan, Türkiye and Saudi Arabia would be held next week in Riyadh to discuss the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed MJDA, a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
In a press briefing, FM Dar highlighted Pakistan’s extensive diplomatic engagements during the high-level week of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA). He also underlined that the platform provided an opportunity for Pakistan's delegation to engage global leaders, participate in international forums and conduct bilateral diplomacy from September 21 to 25.
"The full meeting of the Strategic Political Defence Committee will soon be held in Riyadh, and the current ground realities, particularly the situation in Saudi Arabia, will be examined under the Makkah Accord," FM Dar stated.

"Whatever course of action is decided will be shared with the public when the meeting is finalised, and it will also be shared with you when the meeting is attended," he further added.
🔴LIVE: Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister's Media Briefing 02-10-2026 https://t.co/z7XlzXIplc
In response to a question, FM Dar underlined that at "least six countries" had expressed interest in joining the MJDA while stating that he would not provide further details.
While responding to another question, FM Dar stated that the strategic political defence committee would meet again after “the end of October or beginning of November”, when its work was expected to be completed.
Dar said that Pakistan had condemned the attack on a power plant in Medina, further adding that it was "not acceptable", and stated that he had held detailed discussions with Iran over the Houthi attacks and reminded Tehran of Pakistan’s obligations under the trilateral agreement. Iran, he added, denied having any links “both with the Houthis and the Iraqi militia.”
While providing details of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s address to the UNGA, FM Dar said that the premier reiterated Pakistan’s "longstanding position" on Palestine and presented Pakistan's stance on Jammu and Kashmir, particularly in the context of the 2025 conflict with India and the issue of cross-border terrorism.
FM Dar noted that the PM underlined that Pakistan had played a "crucial role" in bringing the US and Iran to the negotiating table after 47 years, with talks held in Istanbul on April 10 and 11. The negotiations comprised six sessions spread over 21 hours, followed by an agreement signed on June 18.
According to FM Dar, the PM also highlighted the impact of developments around the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, particularly their effect on fuel prices, further noting that the government had approved domestic relief measures despite financial constraints and the IMF programme. "Despite all the financial constraints and the IMF programme, the relief that we could provide was approved by the Prime Minister".
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 briefed the media on Pakistan’s extensive diplomatic engagements during the High-Level Week of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly, held in New York from 21 to 25 September… pic.twitter.com/PNINL5ZzAf
FM Dar added that PM Shehbaz also briefed the international community about the "losses suffered" by Pakistan due to terrorism emanating from Afghanistan, in addition to highlighting Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts concerning the US-Iran conflict and developments involving Saudi Arabia.
Describing the PM’s UNGA address as a comprehensive presentation of Pakistan’s diplomatic stance, FM Dar emphasised that it received repeated rounds of applause during the session. "I believe it was a very successful speech. Those who watched it live would have seen that I probably have not seen a speech by a head of state in which there was applause so many times".
FM Dar also stated that Pakistan had completed its two-year term as an elected member of the UN Security Council on September 30, adding that Pakistan held the council’s presidency during the period. "Pakistan played its role over the past two years in promoting multilateralism. I believe the international recognition of this role was reflected in the fact that, after 12 years, the resolution we presented on multilateralism and the peaceful settlement of disputes was unanimously adopted by the UN Security Council."
PM's bilateral meetings, invitation to UN secretary general
FM Dar stated that the premier held several high-level bilateral meetings during the UNGA week, including with the UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who accepted Pakistan’s invitation to visit the country before the end of his tenure on December 31. "We have invited him to Pakistan, and the UN secretary general has accepted”.
According to the foreign minister, the premier met the prime minister of Kuwait, the president of Kenya, the chairman of the presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the president of Iran, the president of Syria, the prime minister of Bangladesh, Tarique Rahman and the prime minister of Lebanon.
"A Pakistani delegation led by the Prime Minister held meetings with the presidents of both the European Commission and the European Council. A detailed meeting was also held with the Managing Director of the IMF," he added.
Dar further stated that he represented Pakistan at meetings of the OIC contact groups on Jammu and Kashmir and Afghanistan, and also participated in consultations involving Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Egypt under the MJDA. "On 25 September in Riyadh, under the Makkah Accord, there was a meeting of the three permanent strategic political defence committees".

FM Dar informed that the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye met in New York on September 24, followed by a meeting of the three countries’ army chiefs in Riyadh on September 25.
Dar noted that Pakistan, as chair of the SCO Council of Foreign Ministers, would host its meeting in November. "We are the chairman of the SCO Council of Foreign Ministers. The SCO Council of Foreign Ministers meeting will therefore be held in Pakistan in November".
At a high-level meeting on the Middle East’s two-state solution chaired by French President Emmanuel Macron, FM Dar reiterated Pakistan’s support for a Palestinian state based on the pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital. "Pakistan’s position is that the solution in the Middle East is a two-state solution and that a Palestinian state should be established based on the pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital".

title: Manchester City launch appeal against explosive financial ruling
description: The club says the ruling contains    material errors    and vows to pursue the case through due process
content:
The club says the ruling contains “material errors” and vows to pursue the case through due process
Manchester City confirmed Friday they had launched an appeal against a damning judgement that found the club guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules.
An independent commission delivered its findings on the Abu Dhabi-backed club earlier this week and City had until Friday to appeal.
The Premier League leaders announced shortly before midday (1000 GMT) they had done so.
No sanction has yet been decided upon but City could face substantial points deductions, a fine or even expulsion from the top division.
The 10-time English champions, who continue to deny any wrongdoing, said Friday they had lodged a "comprehensive appeal" the previous evening.
"The club's firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe," City said in a statement.
"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.
"We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete."
Earlier on Friday, the English Football Association broke its silence on the case, saying that the commission's decision "has significant implications for the integrity of the game".
"We are carefully considering the decision and its implications and will take action where appropriate," the national governing body said in a statement.
It has been widely reported that City will claim that key sponsorship deals were funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club's owners, as part of their appeal.
State-owned bodies are not banned from sponsoring clubs under Premier League rules.
The commission found City had arranged "sham" commercial deals with a number of its sponsors that were part of a "disguised funding scheme".
It said those companies were only required to pay a portion of the relevant sponsorship fees, with the remainder funded by club owners Abu Dhabi United Group.
Private investment company ADUG, owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan, bought City in 2008 and has transformed the club from also-rans into a dominant force.
Sheikh Mansour is also vice-president, deputy prime minister and chairman of the Presidential Court of the United Arab Emirates.
The commission said the deals artificially inflated revenues and reduced costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion) between 2009 and 2018, a period in which they won three Premier League titles and other silverware.
It found the club had concealed the true state of its finances, saying City were "significantly in breach of both the Premier League's and UEFA's spending limits".
Downing Street said on Thursday that the super-club was not "above the rules" following criticism of British Prime Minister Andy Burnham over the case.
"As the prime minister made clear, the initial judgement is serious and there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules," a spokesperson said.
Burnham, the former mayor of Greater Manchester, told the BBC on Wednesday that he did not want to see the club's Emirati owners walk away as a result of the case.
City could face relegation given the sheer scale of the case and there is even speculation that they could be stripped of their titles.
The club could also face a flood of compensation claims from rivals.
UAE airline Etihad Airways, City's main sponsor, said earlier this week that it was considering legal action against the Premier League.
"Etihad categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements," an Etihad spokesperson said in a statement.

title: Vietnam overwhelm Pakistan in ASEAN Cup
description: Shaheens finish bottom with a solitary point from three matches after 4 2 loss to Vietnam
content:
Shaheens finish bottom with a solitary point from three matches after 4-2 loss to Vietnam
Pakistan's maiden FIFA ASEAN Cup campaign ended with a 4-2 defeat at the hands of Vietnam on Friday, despite a strong first-half display that saw the low-ranked side take the lead at Jakarta's Gelora Bung Karno Stadium.
Nolberto Solano's Pakistan side, ranked 99 places below Vietnam, went into the match needing victory to keep their hopes of reaching the semi-finals alive.
They made an encouraging start and controlled much of the opening half before taking the lead through Mohibullah Afridi in the 31st minute.
Pakistan had already threatened several times, with Ali Akbar Khan seeing an early effort blocked after combining with Abdul Samad Shahzad, while Shayek Dost headed wide in the fifth minute.
Vietnam gradually settled into the contest and forced Pakistan goalkeeper Yousuf Butt into action with a deflected effort, but Pakistan continued to create openings through Ali Akbar and Abdul Samad.
Their pressure finally paid off when Mohibullah dispossessed a Vietnam centre-back, advanced towards goal and calmly placed the ball underneath goalkeeper Patrik Giang Le.
Vietnam responded after the break and turned the game around within seven minutes.
Long Hai Nguyen equalised in the 50th minute after receiving a through ball on the left, cutting inside and firing past Yousuf.
Duc Hoang Nguyen then completed the turnaround seven minutes later, striking a cutback first time to put Vietnam 2-1 ahead.
Pakistan attempted to respond, with Abdul Samad Shahzad seeing another effort blocked, while Umar Nawaz headed over from a cross.
Vietnam extended their advantage in the 80th minute when Bac Dinh Nguyen raced onto a long ball and fired into the net.
Pakistan refused to surrender and reduced the deficit two minutes from full time. Ali Akbar's shot travelled through a crowded penalty area before veteran Kaleemullah Khan supplied the decisive touch to make it 3-2.
But any hopes of a late equaliser were ended when Bac Dinh set up Hoang Minh Williams for Vietnam's fourth goal.
The result saw Vietnam finish second in Division I Group B behind Thailand, with the Philippines third and Pakistan fourth.
Pakistan finished their first FIFA competition with one point, having earlier fought back from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 with the Philippines after suffering a 4-0 defeat by Thailand in their opening match.

title: Aurangzeb reviews economic reforms  trade and investment with World Bank  UK envoy
description: Meetings focus on growth  jobs  fiscal management  investment  trade and private sector development
content:
Meetings focus on growth, jobs, fiscal management, investment, trade and private-sector development
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on Friday stressed the need to move from designing economic reforms to their effective implementation, with a focus on practical measures that could deliver measurable improvements in economic activity, investment, jobs and the overall business environment, according to the Ministry of Finance.
Aurangzeb made the remarks during a meeting with a World Bank (WB) delegation led by Country Director Bolormaa Amgaabazar, where the two sides reviewed progress under the ongoing economic reform partnership and discussed implementation priorities covering growth, jobs, fiscal management, revenue mobilisation, capital-market development, trade and investment, and institutional reforms, the finance ministry said in a post on X.
According to the ministry, the meeting discussed the proposed WB growth and jobs operation, including measures to improve the investment climate, reduce regulatory and business constraints, expand access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and develop export-finance products for the Export-Import (EXIM) Bank of Pakistan.
The ministry said the WB had proposed reforms to strengthen the Prime Minister’s Access to Finance initiative, including a unified insolvency framework, factoring legislation and regulations aimed at facilitating SME financing, expanding commercial lending and increasing private-sector participation.
Finance Minister, World Bank Review Progress on Economic Reform Partnership, Discuss Implementation Priorities Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue, Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb, held a meeting with a World Bank delegation led by Ms. Bolormaa Amgaabazar, Country Director, to… pic.twitter.com/8Mx23vInWi
Sectoral reforms in pharmaceuticals, medical products and agriculture also came under discussion, according to the ministry.
The proposed measures included improvements in seed registration, deregulation of selected commodities and stronger international accreditations to help Pakistani businesses participate in international procurement and access global markets, the ministry said.
The two sides also reviewed measures to improve skills development and labour-market alignment, including reforms to the national vocational qualifications framework, greater international recognition of skills and formal overseas migration pathways supported by digital platforms, according to the ministry.
On trade, the meeting reviewed implementation of the National Tariff Policy and analytical support for tariff reforms, including work on the automotive sector and future tariff changes. The discussions focused on competitiveness, productivity, investment, exports and integration into global value chains, the ministry said.
Fiscal and revenue reforms were another key area of discussion.
According to the ministry, the meeting reviewed the WB’s technical assistance for strengthening tax-policy capacity, including the Medium-Term Revenue Strategy and revenue-policy modelling, alongside GST harmonisation, federal-provincial coordination and improved data sharing.

Progress on agricultural income tax reforms was also discussed, including implementation of amended provincial laws and rules and the development of digital systems for registration, filing and payment, the ministry said. The meeting stressed the need to improve compliance and strengthen federal-provincial data sharing.
The ministry said provincial property-tax reforms were also discussed, including efforts to improve and harmonise property-valuation approaches, strengthen digital systems and progressively move towards more market-based valuation frameworks.
The development of domestic capital markets was discussed in the context of WB Group support for a roadmap through the Capital Markets Development Council, according to the ministry. The proposed measures seek to deepen domestic capital markets, broaden financing options and strengthen the ecosystem for investment and capital formation.
The ministry said the meeting also covered public-sector efficiency and the government’s rightsising agenda, with WB technical assistance focused on improving institutional effectiveness and the efficiency of public resources.
Aurangzeb highlighted the importance of strengthening debt-management capacity and domestic bond markets, according to the ministry. Discussions covered ongoing technical cooperation on financial instruments for managing market risks, domestic bond-market development and improving investor-relations capacity.
The WB also briefed the minister on its analytical work on Pakistan’s sovereign credit profile and its pathway towards rating improvement, the ministry said.

In response, Aurangzeb said the government would work to strengthen the quantitative and qualitative drivers of sovereign ratings, including fiscal and debt sustainability, external buffers, sustainable growth, institutional effectiveness and continued structural reforms.
He also stressed the importance of continued engagement with relevant stakeholders to support further improvement in Pakistan’s sovereign credit standing, according to the ministry.
The delegation also discussed governance and institutional effectiveness, with emphasis on practical and measurable reforms to improve governance, regulatory quality, transparency, accountability and the broader business environment, the ministry said.
The WB delegation included Operations Manager Lasse Melgaard, IFC Division Director Simon Andrews, Economist Anna Godfriedovna Okutu Twum, Senior Public Sector Specialist Irum Touqeer, IFC Country Officer Sahar Etezaz, Practice Manager Shabih Ali Mohib, Lead Economist Tobias Akhtar Haque, Senior Economist Rafay Khan and Operations Analyst Omar Riaz.
The meeting was also attended by the secretary and senior officials of the Finance Division, according to the ministry.
Later in the day, British High Commissioner to Pakistan Jane Marriott called on Aurangzeb to discuss Pakistan’s economic reform priorities and opportunities for deeper bilateral trade and investment cooperation, according to a separate post by the Ministry of Finance on X.
It stated that Aurangzeb appreciated the UK’s continued support for Pakistan’s reform efforts through technical assistance, expertise and knowledge sharing. “Pakistan has moved from stabilisation towards sustainable, inclusive and responsible growth, with greater emphasis on productivity, investment, exports and employment,” he said.
Marriott, who was accompanied by Development Director Sam Waldock and Senior Economist Louie Dane, said the UK remained interested in supporting Pakistan’s economic transformation through technical assistance aimed at strengthening the institutional and policy framework for investment, trade and private-sector development, the ministry said.
She also welcomed Pakistan’s recent issuance of a $3 billion dual-tranche sovereign Eurobond, describing it as significant for investor confidence and access to international capital markets, according to the ministry.
Aurangzeb outlined the government’s six priorities: bringing permanence to macroeconomic stability; moving from stabilisation to sustainable, inclusive and responsible growth; staying the course on structural reforms; moving from aid to trade and investment; expanding access to finance; and positioning Pakistan for the New Economy, the ministry said.

Ms. Jane Marriott CMG OBE, British High Commissioner to Pakistan, called on Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue, Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb, to discuss Pakistan’s… pic.twitter.com/oRXGoRyAEm
The discussions covered fiscal management, tax administration, digitalisation, expenditure efficiency, trade and investment promotion, public investment and public-private partnerships (PPPs), according to the ministry.
Aurangzeb emphasised the importance of coordination among institutions to ensure consistency in implementation and create a more predictable environment for businesses and investors, the ministry said.
The ministry further said the discussion covered regulatory reforms and measures to improve the investment environment, including investor facilitation and aftercare, effective investment-promotion mechanisms and the efficiency of key regulatory institutions.
Aurangzeb also highlighted the government’s ongoing efforts to improve the business environment and facilitate domestic and foreign investment, according to the ministry.
The two sides discussed PPPs as a means of mobilising private capital for development projects. Aurangzeb underscored the need for stronger project preparation, commercially sound structures and greater institutional capacity to support PPP transactions, the ministry said. “The British side expressed interest in supporting these efforts through relevant technical expertise, including at the provincial level,” it added.

According to the ministry, Aurangzeb also outlined progress in macroeconomic stability, capital markets and the government’s privatisation efforts, saying the reforms were intended to create greater space for domestic and international investment and move the economy towards investment-led and export-oriented growth.
The meeting also explored ways to strengthen bilateral trade and investment and encourage greater participation by British businesses in Pakistan, it said.
Marriott highlighted the potential role of UK companies and diaspora networks in supporting private-sector development, particularly the growth and internationalisation of SMEs, according to the ministry.
Opportunities in the aviation sector were also discussed, including potential international financing and investment.
“The British side highlighted the potential role of international financing partners,” the ministry said, adding that Aurangzeb said relevant technical and commercial considerations would guide the process.
According to the ministry, Aurangzeb also briefed the British delegation on Pakistan’s external financing strategy, including efforts to strengthen access to international capital markets, improve the quality and sustainability of financing, reduce refinancing pressures and secure longer-term and more competitive sources of capital.
The meeting concluded with both sides reaffirming their commitment to continued Pakistan-UK cooperation on economic reforms, institutional strengthening, trade and investment, with a focus on sustainable growth and expanding opportunities for private-sector engagement, the statement concluded.

title: Bangladesh down Pakistan in U19 Women   s tri series opener
description: Nishita Akter shines with 23 runs and two wickets as Bangladesh defend 117 8 to restrict Green shirts to 87 6
content:
Nishita Akter shines with 23 runs and two wickets as Bangladesh defend 117-8 to restrict Green-shirts to 87-6
Bangladesh opened their account in the Rivaj Presents the University of Lahore U19 Women’s T20 Tri-nation series with a 30-run win over hosts Pakistan, defending their total of 117-8 as Iqbal Stadium Faisalabad became host to an international women’s fixture for the first time on Friday.
Pakistan will take the field against on Saturday against Sri Lanka with the first ball set to be bowled at 11am at the same venue.
Player of the match Nishita Akter Nishi starred for Bangladesh with both bat and ball as she followed her 23-run effort at no.3 with a clinical four-over spell taking two for 16. Pakistan were restricted to 87-6 in 20 overs in their pursuit of the target as Komal Khan top-scored with 29 off 39 striking three fours.
Komal had stitched a 21-run opening stand with Ravail Farhan, who got off the blocks quickly hitting four boundaries before falling for 17 off 12 – pinned leg-before by left-arm spinner Afrin Mim.
Pakistan lost their way losing five for 37 as Bangladesh bowlers applied pressure from both ends with both mainstays of hosts’ batting Zoofishan Ayyaz (12, 15b, 2x4s) and Aqsa Habib (9, 14b) falling to the right-arm off-spin of Nishita Akter.
Debutant Pakeeza Shabbir could only contribute six runs batting at no.3 following her impressive run of form in U19 domestic T20 tournament, while pinch hitter Shahar Bano was also kept quiet by Bangladesh as she struggled to hit a boundary in her 18-ball stay at the crease.
Apart from Nishita and Afrin’s strikes, Farjana Easmim Medha and Oddrita Nowshin picked up one wicket each as all the six bowlers employed by Bangladesh conceded less than six an over.
Earlier, Bangladesh opted to bat first after winning the coin toss and were kept in check by Pakistan bowlers who claimed first four wickets for 47 runs in 9.4 overs. At this juncture, Sadia Akter walked in and scored a valuable 34 not out off 25 balls hitting one four and two sixes and was supported by Sraboni Shill who hit two fours in her 11-ball 12.
Nishita was the fifth Bangladesh batter to fall after scoring 23 off 33 with the help of a solitary boundary, while no.4 Sadia Aslam scored 12 off 11 balls striking two fours. Sadia Akter added 19 runs for the ninth wicket with Oddrita (6 not out, 2b).
For Pakistan, left-arm pacer Mahnoor Zeb picked up three wickets for 24 runs in her four overs, off-spinner Rozina Akram dismissed two batters, left-arm pacer Shahar Bano and local left-arm spinner Maham Nazakat dismissed one batter each.

title: Leclerc tops second practice
description: The 28 year old clocks a best lap of one minute and 37 528 seconds
content:
The 28-year-old clocks a best lap of one minute and 37.528 seconds
Charles Leclerc topped the times for Ferrari ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar to hand a timely boost to team boss Fred Vasseur in Friday's second free practice of this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The 28-year-old Monegasque driver, who had spoken out in support of Vasseur on Thursday, clocked a best lap of one minute and 37.528 seconds to outpace Hadjar by 0.099 seconds in an uneventful session run in sweltering conditions. World champion Lando Norris of McLaren recovered from a disappointing 12th place in the opening run to take third ahead of four-time champion Max Verstappen in the second Red Bull, seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton in the second Ferrari, and Oscar Piastri in the second McLaren. The two heavily upgraded Mercedes of George Russell -- who won in Baku last Sunday -- and championship leader Kimi Antonelli were seventh and eighth, ahead of Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Pierre Gasly of Alpine. Vasseur has been at the centre of speculation since former Red Bull boss Christian Horner described Ferrari as a "dream job" in a recent interview. The session ended under a Virtual Safety Car deployment after Gabriel Bortoleto’s Audi stopped on the track with a transmission failure, the only incident as the drivers intensified their efforts on a dusty, low-grip surface in F1's first visit to Malaysia since 2017. It was clear by the frequent slithering and sliding that tyre degradation was a factor and will be in Sunday's race, when Verstappen will seek to repeat his victory of nine years ago which came just 24 hours after his 20th birthday. After a busy interval during which team bosses Flavio Briatore and Vasseur were involved in a news conference, the second session began with Esteban Ocon, due to leave Haas at the end of the year, leading out from the pit lane. It was a rapid departure as the teams sought maximum track action before what seemed to be an impending rainstorm. The track temperature was 60 degrees Celsius. As he did in the opening run, Verstappen was soon topping the times with 1:37.785 on mediums ahead of Russell and Leclerc, whose Ferrari boss had called for team unity in the face of speculation about his future. "Honestly, the big issue we have today is the stability and serenity in the team," said Vasseur. "It is a focus that we need to have -- and not this kind of question all day." In reaction to comments by Hamilton on Thursday urging Ferrari to review their structure, Vasseur added: "It would be a huge mistake to start (and) to not be unified... "We had a good beginning of the season, for sure. It's not enough. We want to get more; we want to win more. We want to win the championship."

title: Saudi Arabia says Houthis attempted to target Makkah  Madinah 3 times over 9 years  report
description: Latest incidents occur twice in September 2026  alongside earlier alleged attack in 2017
content:
Latest incidents occur twice in September 2026, alongside earlier alleged attack in 2017
Saudi Arabia has reported three Houthi attempts to target the holy cities of Makkah and Madinah over the past nine years, including two incidents in September, drawing condemnation from Arab and Muslim countries.
The Yemeni group has denied some of the accusations.
According to an Anadolu review of official Saudi statements, the latest alleged attacks targeted Madinah and an area south of Makkah, while the first reported attempt occurred in July 2017.
Makkah and Madinah are home to Islam’s holiest sites, the Grand Mosque and the Kaaba in Makkah and the Prophet’s Mosque in Madinah.
Saudi Arabia has led a coalition supporting Yemen’s internationally recognised government against the Houthis since March 2015. The Yemeni group has controlled the capital Sanaa and several provinces since September 2014.
Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia intensified in September after the group announced what it called a “ maritime blockade ” on the kingdom in July and later claimed ballistic missile and drone attacks on Saudi sites and vessels.
On Thursday, the Saudi-led coalition said a drone attack it attributed to the Houthis had targeted a power station in Madinah .
Coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki said the attack occurred early Tuesday and knocked a transformer out of service without affecting the electricity grid. Maliki accused the Houthis of targeting civilian infrastructure providing electricity services to the Prophet’s Mosque, describing the incident as an “extension of this extremist militia’s approach in attempts to target the Two Holy Mosques.”
“Investigation findings, operational data and examination of debris from the drone used in the attack proved the Houthi militia’s involvement in planning and carrying out this act,” he said. The coalition would continue taking measures to deter the Houthis and protect the Two Holy Mosques and pilgrims in Makkah and Madinah, he added.
Read: Pakistan calls Houthi attack on Madinah power station ‘grave provocation’
On September 16, Maliki said Saudi air defences intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone south of Makkah before it entered the city’s restricted airspace. Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Ministry said at the time that it was the second alleged Houthi attempt to target Makkah after an earlier incident in July 2017.
Saudi King Salman bin Abdulaziz condemned the Houthi militia’s attempt to again target Makkah, saying the incident had drawn international condemnation because violating the sanctity of holy sites provoked the feelings of Muslims around the world.
Abdul Mohsen al-Qasim, an imam at the Prophet’s Mosque, also said during a Friday sermon that attacking Makkah and Madinah was “a grave offense before God.”
On July 27, 2017, the Saudi-led coalition announced that it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis toward Makkah over Taif province, around 69 kilometres (43 miles) from the holy city, without causing damage.
Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Ministry accused the Houthis at the time of violating the sanctity of Makkah in “a desperate attempt to disrupt the Hajj season.”
The Houthis did not immediately deny the latest accusation involving Madinah. The group, however, swiftly rejected the Saudi accusation concerning the September 16 incident near Makkah.
Houthi leader Abdul-Malik al-Houthi and Hizam al-Assad, a member of the group’s political bureau, denied the allegation. The Houthis also rejected the July 2017 accusation, saying their missile forces had targeted only the Taif military base, and had not targeted Makkah.
Read More: Saudi Arabia reports fresh Houthi attacks, issues warning for Makkah
In September, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said on United States social media company X that any attack targeting Makkah should be condemned, but described reports of an intercepted drone over the city as “merely a claim” that could not serve as a basis for accusing any party.
Saudi announcements concerning the alleged attempts to target Makkah in July 2017 and September 2026 prompted condemnation from a number of Arab and Muslim countries and organisations.
According to an Anadolu review, statements condemning the Houthis were issued by Turkiye, Qatar, Egypt, Yemen, Jordan, Morocco, Palestine, Syria, Bahrain, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Sudan, the United Arab Emirates and Somalia.
The Gulf Cooperation Council, Arab League and Organisation of Islamic Cooperation also issued condemnations, with several statements warning that attacks involving Makkah would offend Muslims around the world.

title: Lady Gaga apologises after Haus Labs faces backlash over bronzer shade range
description: Lady Gaga apologised to Golloria after Haus Labs faced backlash over range of its upcoming Sun Dipped Bronzing Veil
content:
Lady Gaga apologised to Golloria after Haus Labs faced backlash over range of its upcoming Sun Dipped Bronzing Veil
Lady Gaga has apologised to beauty creator Golloria after her cosmetics brand Haus Labs faced backlash over the shade range of its upcoming Sun Dipped Bronzing Veil.
Golloria, who is known for highlighting a lack of inclusivity in beauty products, criticised Haus Labs in May after testing three of the darkest shades of the unreleased bronzer. The product was initially scheduled to launch with six shades, which the creator argued did not adequately cater to deeper skin tones.
Haus Labs subsequently asked Golloria to remove her post because the product was still under embargo. Gaga has now acknowledged that the way the company handled both the criticism and the planned shade range was wrong.
In a statement shared through Haus Labs, Gaga said the company wanted to "take full responsibility for our mistakes" and admitted that choosing to launch the bronzer with only six shades was "the wrong decision".
The singer also addressed the request for Golloria to remove her post, describing the response as "unkind" and saying it was not how a creator or customer should be treated.
Following the backlash, Haus Labs paused the launch of Sun Dipped Bronzing Veil and returned to product development. The brand has now expanded the planned range from six shades to 11.
Gaga directly apologised to Golloria and the wider community, saying the creator was "100% right" and promising to personally ensure that the same situation does not happen again.
"Thanks to her powerful voice, we decided to pause the launch and go back to the lab to ensure we had a truly inclusive shade range from day one," Gaga said in the statement.
The expanded Sun Dipped Bronzing Veil will launch with 11 shades, with Haus Labs saying the new options were developed to cater to a wider range of skin tones.
Golloria has previously praised Haus Labs for its complexion products, making her criticism of the bronzer particularly notable. Her feedback has also contributed to wider conversations about shade representation within the beauty industry.
The new launch date for Sun Dipped Bronzing Veil has not yet been announced.

title: Nepal plans to drain four glacial lakes after deadly floods
description: 50 million project to be funded by Green Climate Fund  UNDP  government  could take up to six years to complete
content:
$50 million project to be funded by Green Climate Fund, UNDP, government, could take up to six years to complete
Nepal will kick off a high-stakes effort this fiscal year to drain four glacial lakes perched high in the mountains, as it scrambles to reduce flood risks, officials said, after a recent disaster that killed more than 1,400 .
Rescuers are still searching for more than 5,000 people missing in the border region with China after August's glacier collapse unleashed landslides and a flash flood that tore through valleys.
"Our aim is to lower the risk of the lakes breaching their natural dams and reduce the risk of downstream floods," said Subash Tuladhar, an expert with a government research centre tasked with overseeing the new project.
Canals will drain water into nearby rivers in a regulated way, he said, adding that workers faced health risks as a result of the lengthy periods of high-altitude work required, in addition to the dangers of sudden flooding.
Read: Floods, landslides kill 56 in India and 14 in Nepal
Design work and detailed studies targeting the central and eastern lakes of Thulagi, Lower Barun, Lumding Tsho and Hongu II, will begin in the fiscal year that runs until mid-July 2027, authorities said.
The lakes, at heights ranging from 4,050 m to 5,483 m (13,280 ft to 18,000 ft), rank among Nepal's most potentially dangerous, the United Nations Development Programme and the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) said in a 2020 report.
Nepal had the skills and experience required for the $50-million project to be funded by the Green Climate Fund, the UNDP and the government, added Tuladhar, of Nepal's Centre for Hydrology and Water Resources Research.
The work of draining "through gated structures" will start after a detailed study, and could take up to six years to complete, said Sanjeeb Baral, the Centre's executive director. It will encompass installation of sensors, a flood forecasting and warning system, and efforts to build downstream resilience and prepare communities for the risks.
In similar previous efforts, Nepal lowered by 3 m (10 ft) the level of the central Himalayan glacial lake of Tsho Rolpa by in 2000 and that of Imja in the vicinity of Mount Everest, the world's tallest peak, 10 years ago.
Nepal's disaster served as a warning to the world , Prime Minister Balendra Shah, 36, told the United Nations in an impassioned speech last month that blamed climate change despite his country's negligible emissions.
Retreating glaciers, unstable mountain slopes and increasingly unpredictable rivers showed Nepal was paying a heavy price, he added.
Nepal, which has reported about 26 Glacial Lake Outburst Flood events in the past four decades, loses more than 300 lives and property worth millions of dollars to extreme climate events annually on average.
Read More: Nepal turns to drones to deliver flood relief
The latest floods devastated a dozen hydroelectric plants , roads, bridges, farms and settlements. Cash-strapped Nepal would need nearly $5 billion for early recovery, officials have said.
Climate scientists say as temperatures rise glaciers in the Himalayas retreat, leaving behind ​unstable glacial lakes held back by little more than loose rock and ​ice, above valleys home to millions.
Lowering the lakes by 3 m (10 ft) would significantly reduce the threat, said Samjwal Ratna Bajracharya, a retired ICIMOD expert on glaciers, glacial lakes and outburst floods. "They are growing fast, are high up in the Himalayas and could cause outbursts any time, due to earthquakes, avalanches , climatic conditions and unplanned human-induced activity," he told Reuters .

title: Iran knock Pakistan out of title contention
description: Green shirts suffer straight sets defeat in Asian Games volleyball semis
content:
Green-shirts suffer straight-sets defeat in Asian Games volleyball semis
Pakistan’s hopes of reaching the Asian Games men’s volleyball final ended after they suffered a straight-sets defeat against Iran in the semi-finals in Okazaki, Japan, on Friday.
Iran proved too strong for the Green-shirts, completing a commanding 3-0 victory with scores of 25-13, 25-15 and 25-11 at the Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park Gymnasium.
Pakistan struggled to find their rhythm from the outset as Iran dominated the opening set 25-13 before maintaining their grip on the contest with a 25-15 win in the second.
There was no turnaround for Pakistan in the third set as well, with Iran racing away to a 25-11 victory to wrap up the match in exactly one hour and seal their place in the final.
Iran enjoyed a clear advantage in attack, recording a 64 per cent success rate on spikes compared with Pakistan’s 34 per cent. The Iranians also dominated at the net, registering a 32 per cent success rate in blocks against Pakistan’s four per cent.
Iran finished with 75 total points, while Pakistan managed 39.
Usman Faryad Ali was Pakistan’s leading scorer with 11 points, all of them coming from spikes. Murad Khan followed with nine points, including eight from spikes and one block.
Afaq Khan contributed three points, while Jabran and Musawer Khan scored two apiece. Hamid Yazman and Murad Jehan added one point each.
Iran also held the edge from the service line, recording four service points compared with Pakistan’s two.
Pakistan the other day floored India 3-0 to reach the semi-finals.
Pakistan will now meet in the bronze medal match on Saturday with the winners of the second semi-final between Japan and China which is scheduled on Friday.

title: Any attempt to create  May 9 like situation  will be dealt with decisive force  military top brass warns
description: Forum appreciates sustained successful intelligence based counter terrorism operations by law enforcement agencies
content:
Corps Commanders' forum reviews prevailing security environment, resolves to maintain a high state of readiness
The 277th Corps Commanders’ Conference forum underscored the importance of internal stability and resolved that any attempt to cause agitation or create a May 9-like situation, “on any pretext whatsoever, will be dealt with decisive force and rule of law, without hesitation and discrimination”, the military’s media wing said on Friday.
According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff (COAS) Field Marshal Asim Munir presided over the 277th Corps Commanders’ Conference at General Headquarters, Rawalpindi.
The forum reviewed the prevailing security environment and resolved to maintain a high state of readiness, ISPR said.
The statement further added that it affirmed Pakistan’s right to self-defence and targeted action against terrorism emanating from Afghanistan, stressing that “only the Taliban delusional leadership, facilitating terrorism on behalf of India, bears responsibility for its consequences”.
"The forum appreciated sustained successful intelligence-based counter-terrorism operations by law enforcement agencies, however, emphasised complementing these kinetic efforts with non-kinetic measures, including people-centric governance at grassroot level, strategic engagement with public, dismantling of terror-crime nexus operating under patronage of vested interests and police capacity building, in line with the National Action Plan and Vision Azm-e-Istehkam ," ISPR said.
The forum welcomed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, noting its contribution to longstanding strategic and collective defence ties, the statement added.
Read: 'Dead' SSG man 'resurrects' to expose India's lie
"It strongly resented Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, expressed solidarity with the Kingdom and affirmed Pakistan’s commitment to the security and sanctity of the Haramain Sharifain," ISPR stated.
The forum also reiterated Pakistan’s principled position on Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK) and support for resolution of the Kashmir dispute in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people, it added.
"The forum offered fateha for the Shuhada of the Armed Forces, Law Enforcement Agencies and civil society who laid down their lives for the motherland and paid rich tribute to their supreme sacrifices," ISPR said.
According to the statement, in his concluding remarks, CDF Munir commended the formations for their operational preparedness and professionalism. "He directed commanders to continue to strengthen intelligence-based operations and enhance combat capabilities through absorption of modern technology, training and multi-domain integration".
The field marshal expressed confidence that the Armed Forces, with unwavering support of the nation, remain fully prepared to safeguard Pakistan’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and national security, the statement concluded.

With Pakistan needing a victory in the second match to keep their gold-medal hopes alive.
Noor Zaman at one stage was leading 2-1. However, Yow Eain NG fought back strongly and lifted the fourth and fifth sets 11-4, 11-5 to seal much-needed victory for his side.

Court unanimously allows Joint List, United Arab List to compete in vote; majority also clears Ofer Cassif to run
Israel’s Supreme Court on Friday overturned a Central Elections Committee decision barring two Arab electoral lists from running in the October 27 Knesset (parliament) election.
The ruling came after the court heard appeals Thursday from the Joint List, led by Yusuf Jabareen, the United Arab List, led by Mansour Abbas, and Joint List lawmaker Ofer Cassif.
Israel’s Channel 12 said the court ruled by a majority that Cassif was eligible to run.

“In addition, the judges unanimously decided to allow both the United Arab List and the Joint List to participate in the election,” the channel reported.

The ruling by Israel’s highest judicial body clears the way for both Arab lists to contest the election.
Separately, Sami Abu Shehadeh, a candidate on the Joint List and leader of the National Democratic Assembly party, announced Thursday evening that he was withdrawing his candidacy after the Supreme Court advised him to do so as a majority of judges favoured disqualifying him.
Arab citizens make up around 20% of Israel’s population of 10 million, while opinion polls project Arab lawmakers to win between 12 and 14 seats in the 120-member Knesset.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud party, far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir’s Jewish Power party, and other right-wing groups had submitted requests to disqualify the Arab lists to the Central Elections Committee, which approved them in September.

title: US looks to expand use of canoe sized drones to deter migrant crossings
description: Pentagon considers adding up to 50 solar powered boats for Rio Grande  Gulf of Mexico patrols
content:
Pentagon considers adding up to 50 solar-powered boats for Rio Grande, Gulf of Mexico patrols
The Pentagon may expand its use of autonomous surveillance boats on the Rio Grande and in the Gulf of Mexico after the canoe-sized vessels helped authorities detect and deter illegal border crossings and narcotics trafficking during a pilot program that began in January, a United States official said.
The unmanned surface vessels, built by San Diego-based startup Seasats, patrol the river for long periods without crews and are part of a growing push by the military and law enforcement agencies to use relatively inexpensive, autonomous systems for surveillance and security missions.
The border mission also highlights how a new generation of venture-backed defence startups is positioned to win business once dominated by traditional contractors, as the Pentagon looks for faster, cheaper ways to deploy emerging technologies that can operate around-the-clock.
Defence officials are studying whether the boats, which draw power from solar panels, could be deployed more widely as part of broader efforts to monitor remote stretches of the Rio Grande. Aside from Seasats, companies named Saronic, Saildrone and Splash provide similar marine drones.
Read: US immigration officers instructed to halt arrests of non-criminal immigrants: report
Defence officials want to increase the robotic fleet from its current test group of 10 vessels by as many as 50 to relieve the strain on Coast Guard cutters and crewed aircraft patrolling the border with Mexico as part of President Donald Trump's crackdown on illegal immigration .
Maritime drones are "cost-effective solutions to interdict and put people in these areas that narco traffickers are now moving towards," said M Roosevelt Ditlevson, assistant secretary of defence for Homeland Defence and Americas Security Affairs.
Small drones and other unmanned platforms have proliferated across the US military in recent years after their repeated successes in the war in Ukraine .
Seasats' 11-foot, 340-pound Lightfish is a low-profile autonomous vessel that costs roughly $240,000 and can be launched from a boat ramp or the back of a pickup truck. The drone can operate for months at a time in rough seas.
The vessels carry sensors — including electro-optical, infrared and sonar sensors — that feed real-time tracking data directly into military software networks, including Palantir Technologies' Maven Smart System and Anduril Industries' Fortress platform, alerting Customs and Border Protection and Coast Guard units.
The Pentagon said that in an average month, the Lightfish drones have assisted in 452 detections, 350 apprehensions and 100 turnbacks, which refer to when a group of people abort a border crossing attempt after realising they have been discovered. They "see that the vessel is waiting there for them, and they know that they've basically been found out," Ditlevson said.
The drone maker gained international attention in July when Reuters reported that a commercial Lightfish vessel operating inside the Philippines' exclusive economic zone navigated close enough to a Chinese People's Liberation Army Navy guided-missile destroyer to capture detailed close-up video, demonstrating how low-cost autonomous craft can monitor multibillion-dollar military assets.
Read More: Judge strikes down Trump's 75-country immigrant visa ban
With continued success, Ditlevson said Lightfish orders could rise by 50 boats and potentially also operate in the Gulf of Mexico, forming a radar fence between Texas and Key West. But Ditlevson said use will expand in increments, exploring different technologies.
"We're agnostic to the vendor. We want the best technology," he told Reuters in an interview.
Seasats Chief Executive Mike Flanigan said uncrewed systems provide persistent coverage that traditional, fuel-heavy assets cannot match. "A plane or a ship might go really far really fast, but if you say, 'I want to keep that Boeing 737 over a patch of ocean for a day,' it just can't do it," Flanigan said.
"The boat doesn't cover nearly as much territory as fast, but it can stay there for months at a time, which is the key differentiator for these security and monitoring applications."
As tighter border security and targeted military operations have reduced drug smuggling routes, cartels have increasingly pushed into coastal waterways and near-coastal regions. The expanded drone use in the Gulf of Mexico is a precursor to testing the vessels in the harsher seas of the Pacific Ocean near San Diego.

title: Students and police clash as France struggles to quell school protests
description: Unrest over classroom conditions  funding hits Macron s government six months before presidential election
content:
Unrest over classroom conditions, funding hits Macron's government six months before presidential election
Riot police clashed with high school students in cities across France on Friday, as President Emmanuel Macron's government battled to contain increasingly violent protests over classroom conditions and funding.
Tear gas clouded the streets in the eastern city of Strasbourg, fireworks were aimed at police lines in Marseille in the south and rubbish bins set ablaze in Rennes in the west. In Paris, where there were also skirmishes, students waved placards reading "We have a future to build, not to endure".
Six months before next year's presidential election, opinion polls consistently show the deep unpopularity of Macron and his centre-right-leaning government. Planned budget cuts, which exacerbate the funding crisis in education, have fuelled the discontent.
Minister says parents should pay reparations
The protests erupted in the Paris region last week but have turned increasingly violent as they spread nationwide .
Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin told RTL radio that police had arrested 2,000 people, most of them teenagers, since the protests began. He said that parents of those inflicting damage to property should be made to pay reparations.
400 high schools — roughly one in 10 — were closed on Friday due to the unrest and Education Minister Edouard Geffray urged parents to dissuade their children from protesting in the streets. "In the streets, the children are in danger," Geffray told BFM TV .
Read: French high school blockades continue as protests spread to universities
Several students in the Paris region whom Reuters spoke to outside high schools earlier in the week said they were staying away from the protests on Friday due to the escalating violence.
Darmanin said the student protest movement had been hijacked by "outsiders".
Education to get below-inflation budget increase
Students blockading their high schools have voiced anger over overcrowding in classrooms, regular shortages of teachers and dilapidated buildings, blaming years of underinvestment.
"We are 35 per class, we don’t have enough chairs in classrooms, the one hour lunch break (is too short) for everyone to get food,” 15-year-old Kesia told Reuters in the Paris suburb of Pantin before running off as the police used tear gas.
Read More: India's Cockroach Janta Party, student groups to protest, demand poll chief's resignation
Under the draft 2027 budget presented by the government on Thursday, the education budget is set to increase by a below-inflation 1.7% to €65.53 billion, excluding teacher pensions.
Education is traditionally the largest budget item, but that changes next year with debt servicing costs expected to reach €74.5 billion, according to the draft bill.
Intelligence agencies told a crisis meeting on Thursday that the protest movement had been initiated by politicians from the hard-left France Unbowed party (LFI). Senior LFI lawmakers rebutted the allegations and accused the government of politicising the protests ahead of the election to replace Macron.
Students and rights groups have accused the police of using heavy-handed tactics against minors, including the use of batons, tear gas and non-lethal flash-ball guns.
Amnesty International cautioned against the excessive use of police force. "Students must be protected, not beaten with batons," the advocacy group said on social media platform X.

The interior ministry on Friday said that they had opened three investigations into police violence against protesters.
In a sign the protests may spread beyond French borders, some high school students in the city of Liège, in Belgium, began protesting on Thursday. A city hall spokesperson said high schools were closed on Friday.

title: Mo Naqvi   s    Hanging By a Wire  selected as Pakistan s entry for Oscars international feature race
description: The selection marks the first time Pakistan has chosen a documentary for the Best International Feature Film category
content:
The selection marks the first time Pakistan has chosen a documentary for the Best International Feature Film category
Pakistan has selected Mo Naqvi’s documentary thriller Hanging By a Wire as its official entry for the Best International Feature Film category at the 99th Academy Awards, announced Deadline .
The selection marks the first time Pakistan has chosen a documentary for the category.
The film recounts the August 2023 cable car emergency in Battagram, northern Pakistan, when six schoolchildren and two adults were stranded around 900 feet above the ground after a cable snapped.
Directed by Naqvi and written and produced by Naqvi and Bilal Sami, the film combines eyewitness footage, survivor testimony and cinematic reconstructions featuring people involved in the rescue.
“I’m honored that Hanging by a Wire has been selected to represent Pakistan in the International Feature Film category at the 99th Academy Awards, and grateful to the Pakistan Academy Selection Committee,” Naqvi told Deadline.
“It’s a straight-up disaster film, except it really happened, and you’re watching real footage of it unfolding live,” he added. “The community on the ground filmed it themselves and trusted me with that footage, so in a real sense they co-authored this film with me.”
Naqvi also described the film as a story about resilience and resourcefulness during the rescue effort.
Sana Zahra Jafri, deputy chairperson of the Pakistan Academy Selection Committee, said, “The selection marks a historic milestone for Pakistani documentary filmmaking and brings an extraordinary story from northern Pakistan to the International Feature Film Oscar race.”
The documentary premiered in the World Cinema Documentary competition at the Sundance Film Festival and has since screened at Tribeca, Seattle and Sydney film festivals.
Hanging By a Wire is produced by EverWonder Studio, Universal Pictures Content Group, Mindhouse Productions and 64th Street Media.

Asthmatic actor reassures fans she was doing well while explaining her recent social media absence
Saba Qamar has explained her recent absence from social media, reassuring fans that she is doing well while revealing that Lahore’s air quality has been making it difficult for her to breathe.
The actor recently reshared a heartfelt message from a fan who expressed gratitude for her presence and wished her well despite her being less active online. The fan also highlighted how Qamar continues to inspire her followers to stay strong and never give up.
Responding to the message, Qamar thanked her fans for their love and concern while opening up about the breathing difficulties she has been experiencing.
“My dearest fans, thank you so much for all your love, care, and concern. Since I’m asthmatic, the air quality in Lahore has been making it a little difficult for me to breathe properly. Otherwise, I’m absolutely fine, Alhamdulillah,” she wrote.
Qamar added that she would continue to stay connected with her followers through social media whenever she felt better. “I’d still be connected with you through my stories and will keep posting whenever I feel a little better,” she said.
The actor also expressed her gratitude for the continued support and affection from her fans. “Thank you for always being there and sending me so much love. Love you all!” she added.
Her response came after a fan shared a heartfelt post addressed to the actor, saying they missed seeing Qamar’s stories.
The fan noted that, after everything the actor had been through during the year, she had become less active on social media, but her absence was still deeply felt by those who regularly followed her.
While Qamar may have been quieter online, she has remained busy professionally. The actor has taken on several prominent roles in some of the year’s major dramas, including Muamma , Pamaal , and Case No 9 .
Known for taking on unconventional and challenging characters, Qamar has explored a range of socially relevant themes through her work.
Her performances have included portrayals of women dealing with sexual harassment, as well as characters navigating the narcissistic and toxic dynamics that can exist within marriages.
Just this past month, the actor had been wowing fans with photographs from her trip to London, giving followers glimpses of her time in the city.

title: Ben Affleck says he used AI  for lots of things  in  Animals
description: Affleck said he views AI as  another form of computing  and a technological advancement
content:
Affleck said he views AI as "another form of computing" and a technological advancement
Ben Affleck has revealed that he used artificial intelligence "for lots of things" while making his upcoming Netflix thriller Animals, although the actor and director is keeping details of its use under wraps.
Speaking at Bloomberg’s annual Screentime summit, Affleck explained that he was hesitant to reveal exactly where AI had been used in the film because filmmakers are ultimately trying to preserve the illusion of reality for audiences.
The actor said the technology was used in Animals in what he considers an ethical way, stressing that the film remains "a very human movie". He also compared the use of AI in filmmaking to previous technological developments that have changed the industry.
Affleck said he views AI as "another form of computing" and a technological advancement that fits into the long history of new tools being adopted by film and television productions.
His comments come after Netflix acquired InterPositive, the AI company Affleck founded, earlier this year. The company developed tools designed to assist filmmakers during post-production, including work involving editing, visual corrections, background replacements and lighting, rather than generating performances or replacing artists.
Affleck has previously described InterPositive’s technology as being designed to keep creative decisions in the hands of filmmakers. The company's tools were developed around smaller datasets and filmmaking-specific models, with restrictions intended to preserve creative control.
Animals marks Affleck’s latest project as a director, writer and actor. He plays a Los Angeles mayoral candidate whose son is kidnapped, forcing him to make increasingly difficult choices as he attempts to secure his release.
The thriller also stars Kerry Washington, Steven Yeun and Gillian Anderson. Affleck co-wrote the screenplay with Connor O. McIntyre and Billy Ray.
Animals will be released in select cinemas and begin streaming on Netflix on October 9, 2026.

title: Four Pakistani crew members from hijacked MT Honour 25 to arrive in Karachi tomorrow  Dar
description: Three crew members died in the hijacking  while three others remain aboard the vessel with the captain
content:
Three crew members died in the hijacking, while three others remain aboard the vessel with the captain
Four of the 10 Pakistani crew members affected by the hijacking of MT Honour 25 off the coast of Somalia will arrive in Karachi on Saturday, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Friday.
“Following sustained efforts by the Foreign Office and our Embassy in Djibouti, four of the ten Pakistani crew members (Mr Yasir Khan, Mr Aqeel Khan, Mr Amin bin Shams and Mr Usman Ghani) affected by the hijacking of MV Honour 25 off the coast of Somalia have been safely retrieved and are scheduled to arrive in Karachi tomorrow, 3 October, InshaAllah,” Dar said in a post on X.
He said the mortal remains of three Pakistani crew members who “tragically lost their lives” were being repatriated to Pakistan, with “all necessary legal and other formalities” being fast-tracked.
“The mortal remains of the three Pakistani crew members (Late Rafi Ullah Khan, Late Syed Kashif Umer and Late Mahmood Ahmed Ansari) who tragically lost their lives are being repatriated to Pakistan, with all necessary legal and other formalities being fast-tracked to expedite the process in this regard,” he said.
Following sustained efforts by the Foreign Office and our Embassy in Djibouti, four of the ten Pakistani crew members (Mr Yasir Khan, Mr Aqeel Khan, Mr Amin bin Shams and Mr Usman Ghani) affected by the hijacking of MV Honour 25 off the coast of Somalia have been safely retrieved…
“My heartfelt condolences go to the bereaved families, who are going through a deeply painful time,” Dar said. The remaining three Pakistani crew members — Imran Ali, Yasin Muhammad and Syed Yousuf Hussain — “continue to be aboard the vessel”, along with the captain. “We are actively coordinating with our friendly countries to facilitate their safe extraction and earliest possible return to Pakistan, inshaAllah,” the minister said on X.
The Foreign Office, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, “remains fully seized of the matter” and was “continuously making every effort” to ensure the return of all Pakistani nationals, "including bodies of the deceased at the earliest and will continue extending all possible support to the affected families,” he said.
The oil tanker Honour 25, sailing under the Somali flag from Oman to Somalia, was hijacked by pirates on April 21. There were 17 crew members aboard, 10 of them Pakistani nationals. The families of the Pakistani hostages spent months seeking the safe release of their loved ones, staging peaceful protests and repeatedly approaching government authorities.
During their captivity, the pirates initially demanded a ransom of $3 million, which was later reduced to $1.9 million and subsequently to $1 million. All the Pakistani crew members who were killed or injured were from different areas of Karachi.
Also Read: FO expresses condolences over deaths of five crew members in Somalia rescue operation
The pirates came under pressure during a rescue operation and, while retreating from the vessel, opened indiscriminate fire on the abducted crew before fleeing the ship. Five sailors were killed, including three Pakistanis — Second Officer Kashif Umar, Third Engineer Mahmood Ansari and Boiler Rafiullah. The other two deceased crew members were an Indian sailor, Tanveer, and the chief engineer from Myanmar.
Four sailors were injured — Usman, Yasir, Ameen and Vicky from Indonesia — while Hussain Yousuf, Imran Ali and Yaseen remained safe. The two surviving Pakistani crew members later contacted the Ansar Burney Welfare Trust in Karachi using the ship captain’s mobile phone and provided details of the incident.
Puntland police said the Honour 25 had 18,500 barrels of oil on board when it was hijacked. The police had been pursuing three hijacked vessels off the Somali coast and had also rescued another oil tanker, Sibu 1, on Friday. However, 28 of the 41 pirates arrested during that operation later escaped while being transferred to jail, with several Puntland security officials accusing local police of complicity.
The Gulf of Aden and Somalia coasts have seen a resurgence in piracy since April, with at least 15 attacks recorded this year, the highest number since 2013, according to figures from the International Maritime Organisation.
