title: Lahore back on top of global pollution rankings
description: The city recorded an air quality index of 167 on IQAir   s  placing it ahead of Dhaka at 164 and Cairo at 158
content:
The city recorded an air quality index of 167 on IQAir’s, placing it ahead of Dhaka at 164 and Cairo at 158
Lahore once again ranked as the world’s most polluted major city on Friday morning as its air quality slipped into the “unhealthy” category, prompting Punjab authorities to intensify anti-smog operations across the provincial capital's pollution hotspots.
The city recorded an air quality index of 167 on IQAir’s live global ranking earlier in the day, placing it ahead of Dhaka at 164 and Cairo at 158. Provincial authorities later put Lahore’s Air Quality Index (AQI) at 236, saying weak wind movement and lower temperatures had contributed to the accumulation of pollutants.
Officials said winds were blowing from the southeast, with speeds expected to remain between five and six kilometres per hour from 8am until noon before increasing to eight to 10 kilometres per hour between 1pm and 2pm. The expected increase in wind speed could help disperse pollutants and improve air quality later in the day, they said.
The AQI reached 500 on Multan Road at 6am, according to the Punjab Environment Protection Agency’s (EPA) official real-time air quality monitoring dashboard.
At the same time, the AQI was recorded at 345 at Punjab University, 292 in Shahdara and 227 in Gulberg III. However, by 8am, the situation had changed significantly, with the AQI at Punjab University rising to 385, the highest among the monitored areas, while the reading on Multan Road dropped to 91.
IQAir’s rankings are updated hourly, meaning a city’s position and AQI can change significantly during the course of a day. Lahore’s ranking had consequently shifted from the top position recorded earlier in the morning as atmospheric conditions changed.
Figure shows the top-ranked polluted cities according to IQAir. PHOTO: SCREENGRAB/IQAir
The deterioration triggered an emergency response in high-AQI parts of Lahore on the directives of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, according to the provincial government.
Smog guns remained operational in pollution hotspots, while water bowsers and sprayers were deployed to suppress road dust.
Officials said water sprinkling operations were underway along the Ring Road service line in the Hando area, GT Road near UET and Shalimar Town, as well as Burki, DHA and Multan Road.
Drone squads, night squads and the government’s “Hawk Eye” field teams were also conducting round-the-clock monitoring of pollution sources, authorities said, with enforcement teams directed to take immediate action against violations.
The provincial government also reported a series of enforcement actions across Punjab during the previous 24 hours.
Read: Air pollution in Lahore, Punjab cities reaches ‘hazardous’ category
According to official figures, environmental teams inspected 319 industrial units, sealing 15 facilities and registering one first information report over alleged violations of environmental regulations. Fines totalling Rs1.65 million were imposed.
Authorities also inspected 421 brick kilns, demolished five and sealed eight, while five FIRs were registered. Officials said penalties worth Rs1.5 million were imposed for violations as part of the province’s smog-control action plan.
A separate crackdown on substandard plastic resulted in inspections at 267 locations, with authorities confiscating 1,248 kilogrammes of plastic. Six locations were sealed, and fines of Rs117,000 were imposed.
Commercial cooking operations have also come under scrutiny as authorities seek to curb smoke emissions. Officials said 249 barbecue and commercial cooking sites were inspected. Suction hoods had been installed at 88 locations, while 28 establishments were sealed.
With the harvesting season underway, the government also intensified efforts to prevent farmers from burning crop residue, a practice associated with seasonal deterioration in air quality across the region.
Officials said paddy had so far been mechanically harvested across 724,900 acres out of Punjab’s total 6.33 million acres under the crop, representing around 11.5% of the area.
The government said 437,445 notices had been issued to farmers as part of efforts to discourage crop-residue burning.
According to official data, 1,259 Kubota machines had harvested 310,196 acres while 187 balers had covered another 94,124 acres.
The provincial administration said that around 10,000 Super Seeders were now being used by farmers to manage crop residue without setting it on fire and to encourage more environmentally sustainable farming practices.
Read more: Lahore tops world pollution rankings
Senior Provincial Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb warned farmers against burning crop residue and urged residents to avoid activities that contribute to smog. She said enforcement, monitoring, and preventive operations were being carried out simultaneously because weak winds had made it more difficult for pollutants to disperse.
“Farmers must not set crop residue on fire, and citizens should refrain from every activity that causes smog; otherwise the law will come into action,” she said, according to the official statement.
She added that no one would be allowed to pollute the environment.
Air pollution has emerged as a persistent environmental and public health challenge in Lahore, particularly during the cooler months when stagnant atmospheric conditions can trap emissions closer to the ground.
Industrial emissions, vehicular pollution, crop-residue burning, and weak air movement are among the factors frequently associated with Lahore’s recurring smog episodes.

title: Rick Ross attorney seeks expedited release during Miami Beach arrest hearing
description: The 50 year old rapper faces one felony count of battery by strangulation and one misdemeanor count of battery
content:
The 50-year-old rapper faces one felony count of battery by strangulation and one misdemeanor count of battery
Rapper Rick Ross was arrested early Thursday after voluntarily surrendering to Miami Beach police over domestic violence-related charges.
The 50-year-old rapper, whose real name is William Leonard Roberts II, faces one felony count of battery by strangulation and one misdemeanor count of battery.
The allegations relate to an incident at his Star Island mansion in Miami Beach in August.
According to the arrest affidavit and court records cited by Hypefresh, the alleged victim accused Ross of striking and slapping her during an argument and restricting her breathing.
Ross’s legal team has denied the allegations, describing them as “false” and “wrongful”. Ross has pleaded not guilty and maintains his innocence.
During a remote arraignment before Judge Mindy Glazer, Ross’s attorney, Bradley Horenstein, reportedly requested expedited release, citing his client’s celebrity status and safety concerns while in custody.
When Horenstein explained the request, Glazer responded, “What does that mean?” She later told Ross, “Hi, Mr. Roberts. I have no idea who you are, except somebody here in the court who’s going to be treated fairly just like everybody else here.”
Court records cited by Hypefresh show that bond was set at $5,000 for the felony charge and $1,000 for the misdemeanor charge. Ross posted the combined $6,000 bond and was released the same day.
A stay-away order involving the alleged victim was also issued. Ross’s full arraignment is scheduled for October 22, 2026.
The case remains ongoing, and the allegations have not been proven in court.

She added, “The cruelty directed toward him was something no human being should have to endure.”

The couple first connected in 2017 while Blanchard was in prison, became engaged, later separated, and eventually reunited in April 2024 following her split from Ryan Anderson.
Remembering Urker, Blanchard said, “He will forever be my soulmate and my red string, a connection that time, distance, and even death can never erase.”
She added, “Above all, Ken loved our daughter, Aurora.” Blanchard also asked for “privacy and compassion” for their daughter and both families as they grieve his death.

title: Wrestlers Noman Zaka  Abdullah crash out of Asian Games
description: Seasoned taekwondo fighter Shahzaib Khan also stumbles at first hurdle
content:
Seasoned taekwondo fighter Shahzaib Khan also stumbles at first hurdle
Pakistan’s promising wrestlers Noman Zaka and Mohammad Abdullah failed to give breakthrough and were exited in the freestyle wrestling competitions of the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya on Friday.
Abdullah lost his first bout. However Noman was able to take a solid start by beating a Cambodian wrestler in his 86kg first fight and qualified for the quarter-finals. However he tasted defeat there at the hands of one of the leading Japanese wrestlers. He was given a repechage fight but he also lost that against a high-profile Kazakh wrestler.
As per details Noman took a fantastic start when he advanced to the quarter-finals after defeating Cambodia’s Vuthy Heng.
Noman dominated the round-of-16 bout at the Nagoya City Inae Sports Center, racing to a 10-4 lead before securing victory by fall.
The Pakistani wrestler had established an 8-4 advantage in the opening period before adding two more points and sealing the contest to book his place in the last eight.
However in the quarters Zaka failed and was beaten 10-0 by Japan’s Hayato Ishiguro.
Ishiguro, the 2025 Zagreb World Championship silver medallist, dominated the contest, racing to a ten-point advantage without conceding a point.
The Japanese wrestler was declared the winner by technical superiority, ending Noman’s run in the competition.
Zaka then saw his campaign ended after losing 10-0 to Kazakhstan’s Azamat Dauletbekov in the repechage. Azmat is two-time world bronze medallist and three-time Asian champion.
Dauletbekov dominated the contest, scoring five two-point moves to build a 10-0 advantage.
The Kazakh wrestler was declared the winner by technical superiority, ending Noman’s hopes of reaching the bronze medal contest.
Meanwhile Muhammad Abdullah suffered a 13-2 defeat against North Korea’s Kim Kwang Jin in the men’s freestyle 65kg wrestling qualification round.
Kim dominated the contest, building a commanding lead through a series of two-point moves.
Abdullah managed to score two points but could not halt his opponent’s charge.
Kim was eventually declared the winner by technical superiority with points scored by his opponent, sealing a 4-1 classification victory and advancing to the round of 16.
Pakistan’s top taekwondo fighter Shahzaib Khan also exited in the first round.
He was beaten by Vietnam’s Nguyen Hong Trong 2-1 in the -58kg event.
Shahzaib made a bright start to the contest at the Toyohashi Gymnasium, edging Nguyen 12-11 in a closely fought opening round.
The Vietnamese fighter, however, responded strongly in the second round, shutting out Shahzaib 8-0 to level the contest and force a decisive third round.
Nguyen maintained his momentum in the final round and secured a 13-0 victory to seal the contest 2-1.
Shahzaib struggled to find a way through his opponent’s defence after an impressive opening round, while Nguyen capitalised on his opportunities to take control of the bout.
“It is a disappointing result,” Pakistan Taekwondo Federation’s (PTF) chairman Col Mohammad Wasim told The Express Tribune.
“It’s a question mark why he was outclassed after winning the first round. It’s a failure on the part of the fighter and coach Karami who could not handle him in the right way,” Wasim said.
“After winning the first round 12-11, going pointless in the next two rounds means he has been outclassed,” Wasim said.
Shahzaib had won bronze in the President’s Cup in Lahore, an event which had Asian Games like standard.

title: Manchester City Women scrape draw with Real Madrid
description: Khadija Shaw cancels out Linda Caicedo   s opener in a 1 1 draw
content:
Khadija Shaw cancels out Linda Caicedo’s opener in a 1-1 draw
Manchester City were saved by the rules as they drew 1-1 at home to Real Madrid in the Women's Champions League on Thursday.
In the final minute, Silvia Cristobal fired what appeared to be a Real winner but referee Silvia Gasperotti disallowed the goal because she had collided with City's Beth Mead in the build-up.
Elsewhere, Inter Milan's draw in Vienna left reigning champions Barcelona, who thrashed Roma on Wednesday, as the only team with six points after two rounds.
In the first senior match for a Manchester City team since the release of a report into the men's team that found the club guilty of over 100 charges of breaches of Premier League financial rules, the women hosted Real in the relative anonymity of the club's training ground.
Linda Caicedo gave the visitors the lead after 29 minutes.
After the break, City, the reigning English champions, were more aggressive. They were rewarded for their pressing after 51 minutes when Khadija Shaw drove the ball home.
City's late escape left both teams with two draws and just inside the top 12 places.
"We tried the second half much better than we started the first half," Shaw told Disney+. "Disappointed that we didn't win the game but definitely fight to the end and that's good."
The day after Paris FC played their first Women's Champions League home game at Stade Jean Bouin, across the road from Paris Saint-Germain's Parc des Princes, PSG's women's team entertained Leuven 20 kilometres away at the club's suburban training centre.
Rasheedat Ajibade put the hosts ahead from close range after nine minutes against the Belgians.
Naomie Feller then scored two of her own in the 51st and 63rd minutes before Sakina Karchaoui and Vitoria Yaya completed the rout.
In the early games, Modesta Uka scored Austria Vienna's first goal in the Women's Champions League but Inter Milan captain Ivana Andres levelled in the fourth minute of added time to earn a 1-1 draw.
In a match between two teams that had lost in the opening round, HB Koge crushed visiting Swiss team Servette 5-1 in Denmark.

title: Virtual taekwondo makes Asian Games debut
description: VR headsets and motion sensors transformed traditional kicks into a contact free battle
content:
VR headsets and motion sensors transformed traditional kicks into a contact-free battle
Taekwondo dates back more than 2,000 years, but on Friday at the Asian Games the Korean martial art stepped into a not-so-brave future where nobody gets hurt: virtual taekwondo.
At a gymnasium about a 90-minute drive from the main Games host city of Nagoya, a modest number of spectators watched with a mix of fascination and bewilderment.
Taekwondo officials have billed it as "real-world martial arts meets cutting-edge virtual technology".
Competitors wear a VR headset and motion tracking technology allows their movements to control their in-game avatars.
They have "nodes" on their back, thighs and shins to pick up each bodily action.
Rounds are typically 60 seconds each and matches are a best of three rounds, the two combatants standing within their own play area a few metres apart.
The goal is to aim real-life kicks to the virtual body and head of their opponent to deplete their computerised health bar.
The opponent is physically there, standing on an opposing side, but there is never any real-life contact.
Darren Yap won bronze -- to go with another bronze in the traditional format.
"It was fun playing out there. I had zero expectations," said the Singaporean.
Asked what he could see through the VR headset, he said: "You can see your health bar, your opponent's character, your limbs.
"It's a fun way to do sparring and it's a fun way to do taekwondo without the contact."
Officials say virtual taekwondo is just as athletically demanding as the real thing, but safer.
Governing body World Taekwondo "proudly endorses" it, calling it "groundbreaking".
Sceptics say it is just another type of gaming.
The first world championships were in 2024 in Singapore, but on Friday it arrived at a bigger stage.
One of the differences to the real-life sport is that men and women compete in a mixed category. There are also no weight classes.
"It allows more people to participate in the sport, and I think it's cool that women are able to beat men," said Yap, 22, after losing his semi-final to Vietnam's woman athlete Chau Ngoc Tuyet Sang.
Singapore has become the early home of the sport. Virtual taekwondo appeared at the inaugural Olympic Esports Week in the city-state in 2023.
Silver medallist Chau, who also competes in the real-life format, had mixed feelings about no gender or weight separation.
"One advantage is that you don't have to worry about the difference in weight," the 21-year-old said.
"But one disadvantage is that men and women can have differences in physical strength, and men may tend to be stronger.
"That could also mean that some of the movements are faster than those performed by women."

title: Developing countries hit by overlapping crises  UNDP chief warns
description: Rising energy costs  super El Nino mount pressure on developing nations ahead of IMF World Bank meetings
content:
Rising energy costs, super El Nino mount pressure on developing nations ahead of IMF-World Bank meetings
Rising energy costs, a super El Nino and soaring borrowing costs are increasing pressure on developing countries, with conditions nearing those of the pandemic when the G20 suspended debt payments for the poorest nations, the United Nations Development Programme said on Friday.
Global policymakers are expected to discuss the huge challenges facing developing countries at the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in the Thai capital Bangkok from October 12 to 18, UNDP Administrator Alexander De Croo told reporters. He warned events could trigger a "domino effect with many, many countries being pushed into financial distress," but stopped short of calling for a new round of debt relief.
The IMF-World Bank meetings will bring together top financial officials from around the world for talks on the global economy, AI, climate change and other challenges, as government borrowing costs hit their highest in several decades on heightened concerns about inflation as the Iran war drives up energy prices.
At the same time, the strongest El Nino weather effect since 1950 is expected to trigger more floods in some regions and droughts in others, plunging an expected 49 million more people into food insecurity by the end of 2027.
Read: Six big takeaways from a turbulent week of UN diplomacy
De Croo said UNDP surveys conducted since the start of the war showed it had morphed from a regional conflict to "a crisis which has an impact on approximately 100 countries."
Many governments have taken steps to shield their citizens from the surge in oil prices but their fiscal coffers are now running low and their debt levels are rising, with no real relief in sight, he said, adding that countries should focus on measures to help the most vulnerable.
While some countries were diversifying their energy sources and adapting their food systems, those efforts would take time, leaving them in a "really tough, tough spot" for now, he said.
UNDP Chief Economist George Gray Molina said a major shift was seen in September, as some governments began to allow higher energy prices to flow through to citizens, and started rolling back subsidies, tax relief and other steps that had kept food and energy prices largely in check since the war began.
"That means that they're not able to contain fiscally and financially that burden," he said. "We think that this is a significant issue that needs to be discussed." Even middle-income countries had rapidly depleted their fiscal buffers as they raced to mitigate rising energy prices, he said.
Read More: UN chief calls for AI curbs and end to wars in his last assembly address
Molina said bond market and oil price developments over the next 60 days would be crucial. Higher prices had already contributed to protests and social unrest in 10 countries in September, UNDP said.
And many countries expect conditions to deteriorate.
22 of 26 nations surveyed by UNDP rated the crisis as a high or medium priority; 13 said it came on top of an existing economic or fiscal crisis, and all 26 judged that the worst was still to come.

title: Govt  opposition conclude first round of talks ahead of PTI   s Oct 4 march
description: Negotiating committees to meet again at 2pm on Saturday
author_name: Waqas Ahmad, Naeem Asghar, Khalid Mehmood
content:
Second round of negotiations will be held at 2pm on Saturday in NA speaker’s chamber
The first round of talks between the government and opposition concluded on Friday, with the two sides set to meet again at 2pm on Saturday in the National Assembly (NA) speaker’s chamber, according to the NA Secretariat. The meeting, chaired by NA Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq, included representatives of the government, Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and the opposition.
The negotiations come amid continued tensions following PTI’s announcement of an Islamabad march. Although the protest was postponed from September 27 to October 4 , the standoff between the federal and provincial governments remains unresolved.
According to the NA spokesperson, detailed discussions were held on the country’s political situation, with the government, PPP and opposition apprising each other of their respective positions. Various matters were discussed in detail and with patience, the spokesperson said.
The second round of negotiations will be held at 2pm on Saturday in the speaker’s chamber, the spokesperson added. The government and PPP stressed the need to resolve national issues with the opposition through negotiations.
According to the statement, the NA Speaker played a key role in facilitating negotiations between the government, PPP and the opposition.
Federal minister Amir Muqam, Advisor to the Prime Minister on Political and Public Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry attended the meeting. Senator Sherry Rehman and NA members Naveed Qamar and Ijaz Hussain Jakhrani also participated.
Opposition leaders PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, Malik Amir Dogar and former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser, as well as Salman Akram Raja, attended the meeting.
The round of talks resumed after the Friday prayers as the PTI delegation returned to the speaker’s office. Special prayers for the success of the negotiations were also offered at Parliament after Friday prayers.
حکومتی وفد اور اپوزیشن کے درمیان مذاکرات سپیکر چیمبر میں جاری pic.twitter.com/qX6JZNawqD
The negotiations later went into another break as members of the government and PTI committees held separate consultations. The government delegation remained in the conference room while the PTI delegation moved to the meeting room, with both negotiating committees holding consultations over the situation.
The government committee also deliberated on PTI’s demands. The PTI delegation subsequently returned to the conference room and negotiations between the two sides resumed.
چیئرمین پی ٹی آئی بیرسٹر گوہر خان کی حکومتی وفد کے ساتھ مذاکرات کے بعد پارلیمنٹ میں غیر رسمی گفتگو۔ pic.twitter.com/Ay6ufT2Ez0
Talking to the media after the talks, Barrister Gohar Khan said the first round of negotiations had been completed, with both sides apprising each other of their respective positions.
“Our talks were held in a very good atmosphere and the second round will be held tomorrow at 2pm,” he said, expressing hope that the process would produce better results.
چیئرمین پی ٹی آئی بیرسٹر گوہر خان کی حکومتی وفد کے ساتھ مذاکرات کے بعد پارلیمنٹ میں غیر رسمی گفتگو۔ pic.twitter.com/Ay6ufT2Ez0
TTAP leader and Leader of the Opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas also spoke about the proceedings, saying discussions had been held on the opposition’s long march as well as its demands.
“We discussed the long march and our demands. They also conveyed their concerns to us, so it was decided that we would meet again tomorrow,” he said.
He said the important thing was that the dialogue process would continue on Saturday, where the sides would decide on the future course of action.
Another member of the opposition team, Asad Qaiser, said there had been no breakthrough during the meeting and that both sides had presented their respective positions.
Asked whether the opposition was postponing the long march scheduled for Oct 4, Qaiser categorically denied it.
“We have only presented our position so far, and we need to consult further on the matter,” he said.
Sanaullah hopes talks end political deadlock
Meanwhile, Advisor to Prime Minister Rana Sanaullah said that the first round of talks between the government and opposition had been held in a cordial atmosphere, with both sides agreeing not to make statements to the media that could affect the next round of discussions.
“In the first session of the dialogue, we put forth our demands regarding how the government expects PTI to govern Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, and assist the federal government with special regard to the ongoing war against terrorism in the province,” Sanaullah said while speaking to private television programme Naya Pakistan.
Regarding the PTI’s planned long march on Oct 4, Sanaullah said the government had reiterated that it expected the party to adopt a political discourse to voice its grievances rather than resort to violence.
Outlining the discussions, Sanaullah said PTI leaders had raised their reservations about ongoing cases and other grievances while also highlighting matters concerning meetings with PTI founder Imran Khan and his treatment.
He said the federal government had directly communicated with the K-P government on matters of importance that required a detailed response from the provincial administration.
Asked about the government’s priority during the discussions, Sanaullah said, “Security remained at the top” of the agenda.
“They are bound by the Constitution and law to assist the government in security-related matters,” he said, adding that proceeding with the long march would be a “violation”.
Speaking about the imposition of governor’s rule or an emergency, Sanaullah said the Constitution provided for such measures if a provincial government ceased to cooperate with the federal government.
The PML-N leader said Articles 232 and 234 defined the powers granted by the Constitution in this regard, but described it as “definitely a despicable move”.
He said the government did not care who the chief minister was as long as the person remained committed to the responsibilities attached to the office.
Responding to a question about whether the government would concede to PTI demands, Sanaullah said the issues raised by the party were based on political struggle, but it could not undermine the sovereignty of the country to have its demands met.
He expressed hope that the dialogue with TTAP and PTI would end the deadlock and pave the way for a resolution of the conflict.
Yousufzai rejects rumours of long march postponement
During the same programme, TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Yousafzai dismissed rumours about the postponement of the long march, saying the opposition had neither given the government any guarantee nor any assurance that the march would be called off.
“Many proposals were placed on the table. We have said that when we meet again tomorrow at 2pm, we will present our views on these matters,” he said.
He said the opposition had not moved “an inch” from its demands, describing them as its political and democratic right, while expressing optimism about a positive outcome from the negotiations.
Strongly condemning attempts to link the long march with the issue of terrorism, Yousafzai said: “We all love Pakistan. After 70 years, we should not be issuing certificates of patriotism to one another or declaring each other traitors.”
Asked why TTAP chief Mahmood Khan Achakzai had not attended the meeting, the spokesperson said Achakzai had provided his input for Friday’s meeting and might attend the next phase of the negotiations if the need arose.
Ahead of the negotiations, Barrister Gohar said whether the party’s planned long march went ahead would depend on the government’s attitude. He said PTI was going into negotiations with the government in good faith and had set no preconditions for the talks.
Gohar said the party would first listen to the government before presenting its own position. He said governor’s rule or an emergency was not a solution to the long march, adding that a minister had said on Friday that governor’s rule could be imposed even without the march.
اپوزیشن وفد کی قائد حزبِ اختلاف سینیٹ علامہ راجہ ناصر عباس کی سربراہی میں حکومتی مذاکراتی کمیٹی سے مذاکرات جاری۔ pic.twitter.com/T1qWhxcgml
Gohar said whether the long march took place would depend on the government’s attitude. He thanked Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) for accepting an invitation to the All Parties Conference (APC).
Gohar said free elections, inflation and the people’s right to govern were among their demands, adding that the party was seeking justice every day. He said PTI had not received justice from either Parliament or the judiciary.
چیئرمین پی ٹی آئی بیرسٹر گوہر خان کی وفد کے ہمراہ جماعت اسلامی کو آل پارٹیز کانفرنس (APC) میں شرکت کی دعوت دینے کے بعد میڈیا سے گفتگو۔ pic.twitter.com/k8nihx0Eee
The PTI chairman said the party had previously cooperated in the fight against terrorism and would continue to do so. He also said the federal government had never formally written to the provincial government to inform it about any issue.
Speaking to the media before the government-opposition negotiations began, Talal urged political parties not to create problems for the country by acting according to the wishes of any one party. He expressed hope that opposition parties would withdraw their call for a long march, saying the problems faced by ordinary Pakistanis, rather than those of political parties, should come to the fore.
Talal urged political parties not to create problems for the country by being driven by a single desire. “May Allah make it so that the opposition parties withdraw the call for the long march and the problems of ordinary Pakistanis should come to the fore, not those of political parties,” he added.
Separately, Sanaullah said matters concerning the courts had to be decided by the courts, while political matters could be resolved through dialogue. He said the two sides could discuss whatever issues they wanted at the negotiating table and that the government would respond in accordance with political principles and the law.
Sanaullah said it was not appropriate to suggest that one could write to the prime minister but could not meet him, adding that such thinking harmed political tolerance.
The government’s joint negotiating committee held an informal meeting before the talks, with members discussing legal aspects of the negotiations and other issues expected to be raised with PTI.
The talks followed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s decision to engage the opposition, with the government and the PPP forming a joint negotiation committee. The move came as PTI prepared for its October 4 long march .
Ahead of the formal talks, PTI and other opposition leaders met JI Chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman at the residence of JI leader Mian Muhammad Aslam.
The meeting was attended by Barrister Gohar, Abbas, Qaiser and Mustafa Nawaz Khokhar, while the JI chief was accompanied by JI leaders Liaqat Baloch, Mian Muhammad Aslam and Nasrullah Randhawa. The leaders discussed the prevailing political situation, the proposed all-parties conference and the October 4 long march.
اسلام آباد: قائدِ حزبِ اختلاف سینیٹ سینیٹر علامہ راجہ ناصر عباس جعفری کی سربراہی میں تحریک تحفظ آئین پاکستان اور پاکستان تحریکِ انصاف کے قائدین پر مشتمل وفد نے امیر جماعتِ اسلامی پاکستان حافظ نعیم الرحمن سے ملاقات کی۔ ملاقات کے دوران ملک کی مجموعی سیاسی صورتحال، جمہوری عمل،… pic.twitter.com/6QarZn5ElD
Speaking to the media after the meeting, Abbas said the All Parties Conference’s (APC) agenda was to find a way out of the country’s crisis and expressed hope that all political parties would join efforts to address the situation.
Hafiz Naeem said JI had accepted the invitation to attend the APC and would support consensus on a national agenda covering peace, law and order and the economy. “Pakistan belongs to no one party or institution,” he said, calling for an end to bloodshed.
The JI chief opposed governor’s rule or emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) and any move to suspend the Constitution. He called for meaningful negotiations between the government and PTI and said concerns over PTI founder Imran’s health should be addressed.
Read: Govt, allies strike conciliatory note as PTI firms up march plan
Hafiz Naeem also called for the implementation of Supreme Court decisions in letter and spirit and demanded the release of women arrested in connection with the protests, including Imran’s sisters. He also called for there to be no obstacles to bail for PTI leaders.
Barrister Gohar said the opposition had approached JI as a united political front and would enter talks with the government without preconditions. “We will meet the government with complete sincerity,” Gohar said.
He said the final decision on the long march and its next steps would depend on the government’s attitude. Gohar also said the K-P government had not received its due NFC funds despite increasing the capacity of its police force.
Also before the talks, Tariq said the prime minister had invited the opposition to negotiations and that the government’s doors remained open for dialogue. He said the government would enter the talks with positive expectations and that dialogue was preferable to confrontation.
He urged the opposition to adopt a political approach and avoid an “onslaught” on Islamabad, while calling on the K-P government to play its role in countering terrorism.
Talal said the government had never hesitated to hold talks and that ego had never come in the way of negotiations. “Both the PML-N and PPP have always tried to resolve issues through dialogue,” he said, expressing hope that the opposition would not miss the opportunity for negotiations.
The talks came after weeks of escalating tensions between the federal government and the PTI-led K-P government over the party’s planned October 4 march on Islamabad. PTI had initially announced the protest for September 27 but later postponed it to October 4, while the Centre had increasingly discussed constitutional options, including governor’s rule and emergency , citing the deteriorating security situation in the province.
The government and PPP subsequently formed a six-member committee to engage the PTI, with the opposition also signalling willingness to negotiate but insisting on dialogue without preconditions. Barrister Gohar confirmed that the two sides would meet at Speaker Ayaz Sadiq’s office, while maintaining that the long march would proceed unless the party’s concerns were addressed.
The prospect of federal intervention in K-P had become a major point of contention, with federal ministers citing the province’s security situation, while PTI leaders rejected governor’s rule or emergency and called for political engagement instead. K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi also said the October 4 protest would remain peaceful and rejected warnings of federal intervention.

title: Supreme Court to weigh Trump s mandatory immigration detention policy
description: Justices take up administration s appeal of ruling against policy as migrants  advocacy groups take to courts
content:
Justices take up administration's appeal of ruling against policy as migrants, advocacy groups take to courts
The United States Supreme Court agreed on Thursday to hear a dispute over a policy by President Donald Trump's administration that subjects millions of immigrants who entered the US illegally to mandatory detention during their deportation proceedings.
In this latest legal battle over Trump's hardline immigration agenda to reach the top US judicial body, the justices face an issue that has divided lower courts as numerous lawsuits by migrants and advocacy groups challenging the policy have played out. The policy is one of a number of measures his administration has taken in its pursuit of Trump's goal of mass deportation.
The justices took up the administration's appeal of a ruling against the policy by the New York-based 2nd US Circuit Court of Appeals in a case involving a Brazilian national. The Supreme Court will hear the case in its new term that begins on Monday.
The US Department of Homeland Security in July 2025 issued new guidance to federal immigration officials announcing that immigrants in the US illegally are subject to mandatory detention without a bond hearing for the duration of their deportation proceedings, which can take months or even years to conclude.
The guidance represented a departure from a nearly three-decade-old interpretation of federal law that immigrants already living in the US could be released on bond while they pursue their cases in immigration court.
Read: Supreme Court lets Trump resume deporting migrants to countries not their own
The Republican president has enforced a sweeping crackdown on immigration — among his top priorities — since returning to office last year. The Supreme Court, which has a 6-3 conservative majority, has allowed a number of Trump's hardline immigration policies to go into effect.
The administration's detention policy produced an avalanche of lawsuits from immigrants seeking to be released. Immigrants have filed more than 73,000 such cases in federal court so far this year, about a quarter of all civil lawsuits brought in federal court.
A Reuters analysis in February found that hundreds of judges around the country had ruled more than 4,400 times that Trump's administration had detained such immigrants unlawfully.
The 2nd Circuit decision arose from a legal challenge brought by Ricardo Aparecido Barbosa da Cunha, who entered the US illegally around 2004 or 2005 and has remained since then. He was arrested by immigration officers in September 2025 while driving to work in Norwood, Massachusetts, and initially was denied a bond hearing under the disputed policy. He was subsequently released on bond at a later stage of his case, according to court papers.
Michael KT Tan, deputy director of the ACLU's Immigrants' Rights Project and a lawyer for Barbosa da Cunha, said his legal team looks forward to making their case to the Supreme Court. "The courts have repeatedly and resoundingly rejected the Trump administration's radical misinterpretation of the law. Try as it might, the government cannot twist the law to detain immigrants for months or even years on end without a bond hearing," Tan said.
"Not only is it cruel and inhumane; it is unlawful."
Read More: US Supreme Court hands a win to Trump over mail-in ballot restrictions
Bucking a long-standing interpretation of immigration law, the Department of Homeland Security last year took the position that non-citizens already residing in the US, and not just people ​arriving at the border, ⁠qualify as "applicants for admission" subject to mandatory detention.
Under federal immigration law, "applicants for admission" to the US are subject to mandatory detention while their cases proceed ​in immigration courts and are ineligible for bond hearings.
A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson welcomed the court's decision to hear the case. "Under President Trump, the Department of Homeland Security finally implemented the law as Congress intended it to," the spokesperson said, faulting the actions of former President Joe Biden. "This implementation put the nail in the coffin for Biden's catch-and-release policies."
Most federal appellate courts to review the Trump administration's policy have ruled against it. Decisions against the policy by the 2nd Circuit and Cincinnati-based 6th US Circuit Court of Appeals prompted the administration to appeal to the Supreme Court.
Also Read: News outlets ask US court to block Trump White House ban beyond 14-day order
In the 2nd Circuit ruling, US Circuit Judge Joseph Bianco, a Trump appointee, wrote that the administration's "newfound interpretation" of federal law was an implausible basis for implementing what he described as "the broadest mass detention-without-bond mandate in our nation's history for millions of noncitizens."
The Supreme Court already is set to hear arguments in another major immigration-related case during its upcoming term.
The court on Tuesday let the administration resume, for now, swiftly deporting migrants to countries other than their own without offering them the chance to show the harms they may face. The justices scheduled arguments in that case for December.

title: OpenAI agents obscured hacking activity targeting government websites  security firm
description: OpenAI agents obscured hacking activity targeting government websites  Security firm
content:
Asymmetric Security finds data collection from 55 websites, including US government agencies
OpenAI’s artificial intelligence (AI) agents obscured hacking activity targeting government websites, according to findings by digital forensics firm Asymmetric Security a day earlier.
The investigation found that the agents pulled data from 55 websites belonging to government agencies, businesses and nonprofits, including the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the International Energy Agency and the Mayo Clinic.
Asymmetric said the agents erased records or made them inaccessible, limiting the ability of outside auditors and researchers to scrutinise their actions.
Read: OpenAI agents accessed information from US govt sites, company says
The agents also created temporary email inboxes and private accounts on Urlquery, a website malware-scanning service, to download data.
Researchers said these tactics prevented outside auditors from tracing what information was collected from websites including Australia’s health statistics agency and pharmaceutical benefits scheme.
“It’s possible that the agents were deliberately using these tools to cover their tracks,” Asymmetric Security co-founder Pippa Thompson said, according to a report by the Financial Times .
However, the firm could not establish whether the actions were deliberate or resulted from agents going awry under constraints imposed during a test exercise, according to the report.
The findings follow reports that OpenAI models breached Australian public health service websites in June, accessing public and nonpublic files.
Asymmetric co-founder Zainab Ali Majid warned that limited transparency and the gap between the breaches and their disclosure could hinder a thorough investigation.
Read more: AI leaders warn UN of security risks as systems grow more powerful
“We’re reviewing misaligned model activity and notifying organisations when we identify potential impacts to their systems,” OpenAI told the FT .
The company said most activity detected involved “routine research tasks,” including accessing publicly available web content.
The SEC said no private information was accessed, while the CDC, International Energy Agency and Mayo Clinic did not respond to the newspaper’s requests for comment.

title: Israeli passenger says he knew what to do on flydubai plane after watching TV show
description: After arriving from Saudi Arabia at Israel s Ben Gurion Airport  Hayun described how drama onboard unfolded
content:
After arriving from Saudi Arabia at Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, Hayun described how drama onboard unfolded
A passenger who helped save a flight carrying ​more than 170 people to Tel Aviv from crashing says he knew how to stabilise a ‌nose-diving aircraft after watching an aircrash TV show.
Yaniv Hayun, 50, is being hailed in Israel as a hero after he and three other Israeli passengers managed to subdue the co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073, who had stabbed its captain, before pulling up the jet's steering ​control to right it.
A second air crew aboard helped land the plane safely in Saudi Arabia.
Hayun's brother-in-law ​Asaf Chen told Reuters that Hayun was travelling with his wife and two daughters and ⁠that he owns a sewage pumping company.
After arriving from Saudi Arabia at Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, Hayun described how ​the drama onboard unfolded.
"We knew there was an attack because a woman screamed 'stabbing' and the plane shook," he said. "At that ​moment I ran to the cockpit and the plane dived."
He told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who met him at the airport, that the stabbed pilot probably managed to open the cockpit door before collapsing.
Read: Pilot on Tel Aviv-bound flight tried to crash plane
"One (pilot) was down and one was on the controls, and another ​person came in with me. I grabbed the assailant and put him in a chokehold, and pulled him out," ​he told Netanyahu, in a video of their meeting distributed by Netanyahu's office.
He and a few other people subdued the co-pilot, and ‌then ⁠he returned to pull up the unmanned steering control of the plane, Hayun said, his shirt still blood-stained from the fight.
Asked how he knew what to do in the moments before another pilot aboard, whom other passengers identified as a British man called James, took control, Hayun said: "I watch Air Crash Investigation, Mr Prime Minister."
Tzvika Manes, ​an Israeli bank executive and ​one of the passengers ⁠who helped hold the co-pilot down, said they used airline earphones to tie him up.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog said on Thursday that he was nominating Hayun for the Presidential Award ​for Civilian Heroism, along with Manes, and Manes' wife Tali — who was the first to ​alert the ⁠passengers of the violence in the cockpit — and Shota Musaev, a doctor who treated the wounded captain. Musaev helped incapacitate the co-pilot with another passenger, Asaf Rajuan, who was also nominated.
"I'm not a hero," Rajuan said at the airport. "It's something you ⁠do without ​thinking, running to save your daughter's life, your family's life, your wife, ​and all the staff and people on the plane. You don't think, you just act."

title: Security forces kill seven terrorists in North Waziristan IBO  state media
description: President Zardari  PM Shehbaz  Naqvi laud security forces  reaffirm resolve to eliminate terrorism
content:
President Zardari, PM Shehbaz, Naqvi laud security forces, reaffirm resolve to eliminate terrorism
Security forces killed seven terrorists during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in North Waziristan's Eidak area, state-run Radio Pakistan reported on Friday, citing security sources.
Sources said security forces pursued the terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij with determination and combat skills and destroyed their hideouts.
Fitna al - Khawarij is the term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
7 Khawarij have been killed by security forces during an intelligence based operation in #Eidak area of #NorthWaziristan @OfficialDGISPR #RadioPakistan #News https://t.co/K52oFA6XBR pic.twitter.com/e4UPlxaugu
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif have praised the security forces for a successful IBO against Fitna al-Khawarij in the Eidak area of North Waziristan, Radio Pakistan reported.
In a statement, President Zardari said the efforts of the security forces under Azm-e-Istehkam to completely eliminate terrorism and establish lasting peace were commendable.
Prime Minister Shehbaz, in his message, said systematic operations against terrorists reflected the professional expertise of the security forces and the nation’s resolve. He further added that the entire nation was proud of its brave armed forces.
He said the outstanding performance of officers and personnel of the security forces and law enforcement agencies guaranteed the country’s peace and security.
The prime minister said the entire nation stood shoulder to shoulder with the security forces to foil the nefarious designs of Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists. Vigorous operations against all terrorist elements would continue until their complete elimination, he added.
President @AAliZardari and Prime Minister @CMShehbaz have appreciated security forces for a successful intelligence-based operation against #FitnaAlKhawarij in the #Eidak area of #NorthWaziristan @PresOfPakistan @PakPMO @OfficialDGISPR #RadioPakistan #News … pic.twitter.com/lPhtxzPfAt
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi paid tribute to the security forces for a successful operation against terrorists in the Eidak area of North Waziristan. “The brave sons of the soil who sent seven Indian-sponsored terrorists to hell are the nation’s heroes,” Naqvi added.
The interior minister praised the professional capabilities of the security forces for foiling the terrorists’ nefarious designs. “The brave personnel of the security forces are a source of pride for the entire nation,” Naqvi said.
He added that the security forces’ successes in the fight against terrorism were commendable.
Read : Nine policemen martyred, 28 injured in terror attack on police checkpost in K-P's Hangu
On September 29, Security forces continued operations against terrorists in K-P and Balochistan, killing seven terrorists in separate IBOs, security sources said.
Five terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij were killed during an IBO in the Bara area of Khyber district in K-P. A large quantity of weapons and ammunition was recovered from the slain terrorists.
In Balochistan's Chagai district, security forces killed two terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan – a term used for Indian proxy terrorists from the banned Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and affiliates - during an operation in the Nok Kacha area, the sources said.
They added that the terrorists had set an empty water tanker on fire before attempting to flee the area. However, security forces responded promptly and killed both terrorists.
The slain terrorists were also involved in arson attacks at various locations along the N-40 highway.
Read more: 49 terrorists killed in Balochistan, K-P IBOs
Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terrorist activity over the past three months, with a series of attacks across the country resulting in the martyrdom of security personnel and civilians.
Last week, 12 people were killed and 35 others injured when a blast struck a joint checkpoint near Aman Mela in the Darazinda area of Dera Ismail Khan, with the TTP claiming responsibility for the attack.
On September 19, 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred in a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, the Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
In a separate incident, a captain and a lieutenant were among six security personnel martyred in an exchange of fire in Hangu district, while eight terrorists were killed.
On September 1, six personnel, including two officers, and a customs department official were martyred as security forces thwarted an attempt to breach the Customs House in Balochistan.
Read more : Nine policemen martyred, 28 injured in terror attack on police checkpost in K-P's Hangu
In July, at least 30 people , including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. The attackers also abducted several civilians and police personnel after the assault.
In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation , which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

title: India s Cockroach Janta Party  student groups to protest  demand poll chief s resignation
description: Election chief s deputies  raise concerns at least 14 times over 10 months about voter list revisions  digital systems
content:
Election chief's deputies raise concerns at least 14 times over 10 months about voter-list revisions, digital systems
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will face renewed pressure on Friday as the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party and a separate coalition of student and activist groups stage fresh protests, demanding the resignation of the elections commission chief over a controversial voter roll revision.
The CJP will rally in Mumbai and plans to expand demonstrations nationwide in the coming days, while student and civil society groups will gather at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar.
The protests mark the latest escalation in a dispute that has put unprecedented scrutiny on India's Election Commission, long regarded as one of the country's most trusted institutions.
The protesters' main allegation is that the commission manipulated voter rolls in ways that favour Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The commission and the government have denied the allegations.
Read: India's Gen Z cockroach party resists lure of election after rattling Modi
Pressure on Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar intensified last month after the Indian Express newspaper reported the election chief's two deputies had formally raised concerns at least 14 times over the past 10 months over voter-list revisions, registration procedures and the commission's digital systems.
The Election Commission has said differing views are a normal part of internal deliberations and that all its actions were lawful.
"We have been asking and demanding for a change but nothing of that is going to happen, if our only tool that is left to change anything in our society 'the right to vote' is taken away from us," Saurav Das, CJP's convenor, told Indian news agency ANI on Thursday.
"We will only end the protest after Gyanesh Kumar resigns."
Read More: 'The fear killed her': How an exam scandal in India sparked a student uprising
The controversy centres on a nationwide voter-verification exercise launched last year that critics say has led to millions of eligible voters being removed from electoral rolls. The commission says the exercise is intended to remove duplicate, deceased or ineligible voters and ensure the accuracy of electoral rolls.
Opposition parties led by the Congress party are also set to begin protests demanding Kumar's resignation on October 6.
The CJP, a youth movement that emerged earlier this year from online frustration over unemployment and leaked examination papers, has become an unexpected political force.
Led by Abhijeet Dipke, the party gained national prominence after spearheading mass protests over exam-paper leaks that led to the resignation of India's education minister , one of Modi's most significant political setbacks in recent years.

title: US sends additional Patriot batteries to protect Saudi  Qatari energy sites  report
description: US sends additional Patriot batteries to protect Saudi  Qatari energy sites  Report
content:
Deployments aim to reassure allies amid possible resumption of major US combat operations against Iran.
The US military has deployed two additional Patriot missile batteries to protect energy facilities in Saudi Arabia and Qatar amid preparations for possible renewed military operations against Iran, the Axios news site reported a day earlier, citing two US officials and a regional source.
One battery was sent to Saudi Arabia last month to protect a key oil facility, while another was deployed to Qatar to defend a natural gas facility, according to the report.
The deployments were intended to reassure both countries that Washington would protect their critical energy infrastructure if US President Donald Trump resumes major combat operations against Iran . Trump said yesterday that he was considering renewing a bombing campaign in the coming weeks.
“Now I have to make a decision: either Iran signs the deal, or it won't exist any longer,” he said.
Read: Iran seeks deal with US, not war: Pezeshkian
Axios reported that Saudi and Qatari leaders urged Trump in early August against launching a major attack that would include strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure , fearing retaliation against their oil and gas facilities.
US officials said those appeals were a key factor in his decision to pursue economic pressure instead.
The report said Washington would need Saudi permission to use the kingdom’s airspace for renewed major combat operations, but Riyadh would be unlikely to agree without assurances that its oil facilities were protected. US Central Command spokesman Capt. Tim Hawkins declined to comment.
Meanwhile, the US is sending additional warships, fighter jets and troops to the Middle East, Axios reported.
A US official said the USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier and its strike group left San Diego on Sunday and were expected to reach the region around mid-November.
Officials have yet to determine whether the carrier will replace an existing deployment or increase the US presence to three carrier strike groups.
The Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group, carrying thousands of Marines from the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit, also departed for the region Monday and is expected to arrive by the end of November, the report said.

Brent falls $2.83, or 2.77%, to $99.48 a barrel
Oil ​prices fell about 3%, and European gasoil futures dropped over 5% on Friday after reports ‌of talks on additional diesel and crude stock releases, easing concerns over tight global energy supplies.
Brent fell $2.83, or 2.77%, to $99.48 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate dropped $3.35, or 3.61%, to $89.52 a barrel.
Both benchmark contracts were poised for a weekly decline, ​with Brent down about 4.7% so far for the week and WTI lower by around 3.1%.
European ​gasoil futures, a benchmark for diesel prices, fell more than 5% to $1,377 a metric ⁠ton.
"The whole energy complex trades lower, led by gasoil and ULSD, as EU countries discuss releasing fuel and ​crude stockpiles to ease acute market tightness and help avert a potential US diesel export ban," Ole Hansen, ​head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank, said.
European Union countries on Friday discussed a French proposal to release additional diesel stockpiles, in response to US pressure on European nations to unleash more supplies in an attempt to reduce surging fuel prices, ​a source familiar with details of the discussion told Reuters on Friday.
In a call on Friday, EU countries' ​governments discussed a French proposal for European countries to release 50 million barrels of diesel, and for International Energy Agency ‌members to ⁠release 50 million barrels of crude oil, the source said.
Read: Govt increases petrol by Rs3.26, cuts diesel by Rs1.01 for Oct 2
"This highlights that the main stress in the energy market is no longer crude availability, with Middle East flows recovering, but rather refined product supply, constrained by reduced refinery capacity and output across the Middle East and Russia," Hansen said.
Prices settled higher in the previous ​session after Reuters reported that ​Chinese refiners suspended oil product ⁠exports for October as Beijing looked to preserve domestic stocks.
Meanwhile, the Wall Street Journal reported that the US was sending a third aircraft carrier and up to ​10,000 more troops to the Middle East as President Donald Trump weighed resuming strikes ​on Iran ⁠after the US midterm elections.
"The gradual recovery in oil flows through the Middle East Gulf (including pipeline bypass) has picked up pace of late," Barclays said in a note.
However, the bank said physical market fundamentals remained strong, with inventories ⁠continuing to ​draw and prompt cargoes commanding steep premiums over forward prices.
The bank ​raised its fourth-quarter Brent forecast by $20 a barrel to $115 and lifted its 2026 forecast to $100 a barrel.

title: WTA reduces 2027 schedule for world s top 50
description: The measure comes in response to recurring criticism about tennis  overloaded schedule
content:
The measure comes in response to recurring criticism about tennis' overloaded schedule
The WTA announced Thursday that it has reduced the number of tournaments that top-ranked players are required to play in 2027.
The measure comes in response to recurring criticism about tennis' overloaded schedule.
Under the current system, the world's top 50-ranked players are obligated to play the four Grand Slam tournaments, 10 WTA 1000 events and six 500 events each year.
In 2027, they will be required to play only four WTA 500 tournaments instead of six, the women's tour announced in a statement released Thursday.
In addition, they will be able to substitute points earned at a WTA 1000 tournament with those earned at a WTA 500 or WTA 250 tournament.
In other words, a player who chooses not to compete in a mandatory WTA 1000 event could still include the points earned at a less prestigious tournament in her ranking -- whereas she currently risks earning zero points.
The WTA will assess the impact of these measures to decide whether or not to extend them into 2028.
In January, the ATP announced a similar measure, reducing the number of mandatory 500-level tournaments for the world's top 30 players from five to four, starting this season.
The WTA press release issued Thursday also announced that, for the first time, the prize money for "combined" WTA 1000 tournaments will be identical to that of the corresponding men's ATP events.
While the WTA and Masters 1000 tournaments in Indian Wells, Miami and Madrid already offered equal prize money, this was not yet the case for the tournaments in Rome, Canada and Cincinnati.

title: Chinese judoka accused of biting as home hope wins Asian Games gold
description: Maeda goes on to claim  70kg gold after Tang Jing   s quarter final disqualification
content:
Maeda goes on to claim -70kg gold after Tang Jing’s quarter-final disqualification
Japanese judo officials said they had never seen anything like it after eventual champion Rin Maeda appeared to be bitten by her Chinese opponent at the Asian Games.
Maeda was awarded victory in the quarter-final bout in Nagoya when Tang Jing was disqualified just over a minute into the contest.
Tang appeared to bite Maeda just above the wrist while the pair were clinched on the ground, with Maeda showing the referee visible teeth marks after getting up from the mat.
Judges reviewed the footage and Tang was disqualified.
Japan women's judo coach Maki Tsukada told sports website The Digest that it was a first for her in her long career in the sport.
"At tournaments like the Asian Games there have been incidents in the past where someone gets punched in the face or their eye swells up," she said following Thursday's incident in their -70kg class bout.
"I regret that we hadn't anticipated that something like this might happen."
Tsukada said the bite marks were visible despite Maeda wearing protective tape on that part of her arm.
"It was to the point where we thought she might actually start bleeding, but it didn't go as far as needing disinfection or anything like that," said Tsukada.
"Still, the teeth marks were clearly and firmly there."
Maeda went on to win gold, beating Kazakhstan's Azhar Askhat in the final.
"I entered this tournament with a strong determination to win gold," said the 21-year-old.
"Preparing for a multi-sport event like this was a unique experience, but I was able to prepare properly each day and deliver my best performance."

title: Zidane faces Italy in France homecoming
description: Les Bleus arrive on home soil after narrow wins over Turkey and Belgium
content:
Les Bleus arrive on home soil after narrow wins over Turkey and Belgium
New France coach Zinedine Zidane insisted Thursday he has no regrets about his infamous headbutt on Marco Materazzi in the 2006 World Cup final as he prepares to come up against Italy again in his first home game in charge.
"The images will always be there to remind me of what happened in 2006, because they are always being shown," Zidane smiled when asked about the incident which led to him being sent off in extra time in what was his last ever match as a player.
"Fortunately that is not the only thing I did and there were other nicer things, so I try to think more about the positives," Zidane said at a press conference at the Stade de France, where Les Bleus host the Italians in the UEFA Nations League on Friday.
"I don't have regrets because it was part of my career," he continued, adding that he had not spoken to Materazzi since that night in Berlin, in a final which Italy won on penalties.
"In 2006 I didn't know I was going to become a coach. I thought that was the end so it was really difficult for me.
"I am not proud of what happened. I have said it over and over again, but it is part of my career -- you can't only do wonderful things."
Zidane, 54, was appointed France coach in late July, succeeding his former international teammate Didier Deschamps, who stepped down after 14 years in charge following the World Cup in North America.
The former Real Madrid coach's first two matches in charge have come away from home, with Les Bleus winning 1-0 in Turkey and by the same scoreline in Belgium in the Nations League.
Friday's match, in front of what will be a sell-out crowd of close to 80,000 at the national stadium to the north of Paris, will therefore be a homecoming for the coach, who remains an icon in France.
"It is going to be really emotional," said Zidane, whose last appearance at the Stade de France came as a player in a friendly against Mexico in 2006.
France are without captain Kylian Mbappe, who returned to his club Real Madrid after suffering a knee injury while scoring the winning goal in Turkey last week.
Earlier, France forward Ousmane Dembele insisted there was no tension between him and Mbappe after comments made by both players in the media about the Ballon d'Or.
Dembele, of Paris Saint-Germain, won last year's Ballon d'Or and is nominated again this year, while Mbappe is one of the leading contenders to succeed his compatriot.
"There is no issue. We have talked about it. We sit next to each other at the dinner table," Dembele told reporters, dismissing the matter as a "social media squabble".
Mbappe said in an interview last month with France Football magazine that Dembele "was always seen as a talented player, while I was always seen as the chosen one".
A few days later Dembele replied to those comments, saying: "I have never been the chosen one, but I have worked hard, and last year I was rewarded for a fantastic year with Paris Saint-Germain. This year we will see."

title: Pakistan calls Houthi attack on Madinah power station    grave provocation
description: FO says sanctity of Two Holy Mosques  safety of worshippers and pilgrims must be respected under all circumstances
content:
FO says sanctity of Two Holy Mosques, safety of worshippers, pilgrims must be respected under all circumstances
Pakistan on Friday strongly condemned an attack by the Houthi militia on the Taibah power distribution station in Madinah on September 29, saying the "reprehensible attack" on civilian infrastructure supplying electricity to the Holy Prophet's (PBUH) Mosque was a “grave provocation,” the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) said on Friday.
In a post on X, MoFA said the attack was a matter of “deep concern and anguish” for millions of Muslims worldwide.
“The sanctity of the Two Holy Mosques and the safety of worshippers and pilgrims must be respected under all circumstances,” the ministry added. Pakistan called for an immediate and unconditional end to reckless actions, saying they also constituted a grave threat to regional peace and security, it added.

The statement further added that the Pakistan reaffirmed its “unwavering solidarity” with the brotherly Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and expressed its full support for the kingdom's sovereignty, territorial integrity and security.
“We stand firmly with Saudi Arabia in its efforts to safeguard the Two Holy Mosques, protect its people and ensure the safety of pilgrims,” the ministry said.
The statement said Pakistan had been and would continue to make all efforts to achieve lasting peace and stability in the region.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Thursday that the group had attacked a power distribution station in Madinah earlier in the week, putting one transformer out of service but without affecting the electricity network.
The coalition said an investigation and examination of drone wreckage had confirmed Houthi involvement in planning and carrying out Tuesday's attack. Coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said the attack had targeted the Taibah electricity distribution station at 5:11am local time on Tuesday.
He said the facility supplied electricity to the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah.
An operational review and examination of debris from the drone had established Houthi involvement in planning and carrying out what Al-Maliki called a “cowardly terrorist act”.
The attack had knocked one transformer out of service but had not affected the electricity grid, he added.
A Houthi military source, quoted by the Houthi-run Saba news agency, denied the accusation, calling it a “lie” and saying it was intended to cover up what he described as Saudi Arabia's failure to substantiate its earlier accusation that the Houthis had targeted Makkah.

The coalition described that incident as the second Houthi attempt to target Makkah since 2017, while the Houthis denied targeting Makkah or any other Islamic holy site.
The coalition said the Madinah attack was part of what it described as repeated Houthi attempts to target the Two Holy Mosques and “provoke” Muslims worldwide.
It said it would continue taking measures to protect the holy sites and pilgrims.
The latest escalation had been the most serious fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned Houthis since a UN-brokered truce had largely halted cross-border attacks in 2022.
Hostilities had resumed this year after the Houthis declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in July and began attacking Saudi territory and shipping, while Houthi forces had also made major territorial gains along Yemen's Red Sea coast.
Saudi Arabia had responded with airstrikes in Yemen and backed government forces fighting to push back the Houthis.

title: Qatar  ready  if 2030 Asian Games moved back
description: Organisers await clarity from the OCA and IOC over the proposed date shift
content:
Organisers await clarity from the OCA and IOC over the proposed date shift
Doha Asian Games organisers "are ready" if the continent's premier sporting event is moved back a year to 2031 in a major shake-up to the calendar, a top official said Thursday.
The Games, currently ongoing in Japan, are typically held every four years and on even years.
Doha is the next host and according to the current cycle, the Qatari capital would stage the Games in 2030.
However, reports in April said that the executive board of the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) had approved the idea of reshaping the calendar so that future Games double up as qualifying and preparation for the Olympics.
That would mean the Doha Games taking place in 2031, months before the 2032 Brisbane Olympics.
"We are working closely with the OCA. For us, it's 2030," Ahmad Abdulla Al-Buenain, chief executive of the Doha 2030 Asian Games organising committee, told AFP in current host Nagoya.
"But if it needs to be changed either one year earlier or postponed year for some specific reason, we need to make sure as the LOC (local organising committee) that we are ready, that the venues are ready, all the operation plans are going on."
He said that any change will be "between the OCA and the IOC", referring to the International Olympic Committee.
"Yes, LOC as a host country needs to be engaged. But again, it's not a solo decision.
"We need to work closely in the upcoming days to make sure that everyone is satisfied about the date, about the duration, and when it will be, where it will be located and when."
The Aichi-Nagoya Games have faced accusations of organisational failures, especially with athlete accommodation and transport.
Qatar, which in the past 20 years has staged a growing number of major sports events, culminating in the men's 2022 FIFA World Cup, already has all the venues in place.
Doha also staged the Asian Games in 2006.
"Qatar is ready. Whenever it comes to Qatar, Qatar is ready," said Al-Buenain.
One of the major challenges for Japanese organisers has been the ballooning number of participants.
More than 17,000 athletes and officials -- more than the Olympics -- descended on Aichi-Nagoya.
Some teams said there was a shortage of beds.
Al-Buenain said it was "too early to discuss numbers".
But he told reporters: "There is no limit up to this point."

title: Portugal edge Denmark in Ronaldo s absence
description: Vitinha and Felix strike late to beat Denmark 4 2
content:
Vitinha and Felix strike late to beat Denmark 4-2
Portugal put the controversy surrounding Cristiano Ronaldo's departure to one side as they edged Denmark 4-2 in the UEFA Nations League on Thursday.
Joao Felix made the win safe late in the second half after the hosts had twice fought back to level.
With the pre-match build-up dominated by five-time Ballon d'Or winner Ronaldo's sudden departure from the team's training camp on Wednesday, coach Jorge Jesus said before kick-off that he just wanted his side "to focus on the match".
His team showed no signs of being distracted by the furore caused by the 41-year-old's walk-out after Jesus announced Ronaldo would not start the match against Denmark.
"A victory of the highest quality; this Portugal team scored four goals and put in a performance which, in my opinion, was of a very high standard," Jesus told his post-match press conference.
"I still think exactly the same way: there are players with status. That much is crystal clear.
"But I'll say it again: the rules are the same for everyone. That's a method I've followed throughout my coaching career and I'll continue to follow."
Ronaldo, Portugal's record goalscorer, had already spent all of Sunday's 2-1 Nations League win in Norway on the bench, having captained the side in the 1-0 home victory over Wales last Thursday.
"Following the national team coach's press conference, and after having a conversation with the Portuguese Football Federation president, I decided to leave the national team's training camp," Ronaldo wrote on Instagram on Wednesday.
"In due course, I will tell the truth to all the Portuguese people about my reasons for leaving the national team, to which I have always been dedicated."
On the pitch, Joao Cancelo opened the scoring for Portugal inside 13 minutes, before Mikkel Damsgaard curled in a leveller 10 minutes later.
Goncalo Ramos repaid Jesus's faith in starting him again up front by restoring his country's lead two minutes later with a cute near-post finish.
Rasmus Hojlund equalised for Denmark early in the second period, but Paris Saint-Germain lynchpin Vitinha nodded the visitors back in front in the 57th minute.
Substitute Felix then tucked home at the end of a swift counter-attack with three minutes remaining to give new boss Jesus a third win from his first three matches.
"This is more important than anything else that has happened," Jesus added, before looking ahead to a home game against Norway on Sunday. "So that is what I want to focus on: the match, the next match."

title: Klopp averts crisis with first win as Germany boss
description: Florian Wirtz and Tom Bischof score in 2 0 win over Serbia
content:
Florian Wirtz and Tom Bischof score in 2-0 win over Serbia
Jurgen Klopp celebrated his first win as Germany manager on Thursday as his side eased to a 2-0 win against Serbia in the third fixture of their UEFA Nations League campaign.
Liverpool's Florian Wirtz and Bayern Munich's Tom Bischof both found the net as a youthful Germany made short work of a lacklustre Serbia team in Munich.
It was a win that lifted the pressure on the new national team boss, after he began his tenure with a 1-1 draw against the Netherlands and a shock 1-0 defeat to Greece last weekend.
Another loss, or a draw, would have made Klopp the first Germany coach in history not to win any of his first three games in charge.
Instead, victory marked a cautious sense of optimism for the four-time world champions, as they look to return to the international elite under Klopp.
"The mix of football and attitude was top level today. I told the boys that this has to be our benchmark," Klopp told public broadcaster ZDF.
"Jurgen is a coach that pulls people along with him. We saw that today and I hope it continues into the future," said Bischof.
Having nominated a bumper squad of 44 players for his first round of games, Klopp fielded an entirely new starting eleven against Serbia, including three debutants.
Bayern Munich goalkeeper Jonas Urbig, Freiburg forward Derry Scherhant and Brentford midfielder Vitaly Janelt all made their national team debuts, while Celtic's Mika Baur became the 1,000th player ever to represent Germany when he came on as a 77th minute substitute.
The young team showed a marked improvement on the turgid performance against Greece last Sunday, albeit against underwhelming opposition.
Aleksandar Pavlovic, Serge Gnabry and Bischof all had chances in the first half hour, while Serbia mustered only one dangerous counter-attack through Filip Kostic.
The hosts finally broke through shortly before half-time thanks to some elegant footwork from Wirtz.
Wirtz danced through a maze of legs in the box and hit the post, before an unmarked Bischof smashed the ball in on the rebound.
The game continued in the same vein after the break, as Germany continued to pin Serbia back into their own final third.
Juventus' Nick Woltemade should have doubled the lead on 59 minutes but skied the ball high over the bar from a metre in front of goal.
Wirtz spared his team-mate's blushes a moment later, making space for himself in the box with a brilliant first touch and slotting the ball into the bottom corner.
Klopp reserved special praise for the Liverpool player, who has faced criticism in England for his club form recently.
"The rhythm has to be: easy, easy, easy, Flo, Flo, Flo, Wirtz, Wirtz, Wirtz," said the Germany coach. "A performance like that helps us, but it also helps him.
"If he was out of form, we wouldn't just let him play anyway. But he's in form and he showed that in training and today."
The second goal put the win beyond doubt, prompting a Mexican wave to roll around the Munich arena.
