title: Ireland game interrupted twice by Gaza protests
description: Austria twice take the lead before Ireland secure a 2 2 draw
content:
Austria twice take the lead before Ireland secure a 2-2 draw
The Nations League football match between Ireland and Austria in Dublin on Thursday was twice briefly interrupted by demonstrations in support of Palestine.
In the 19th minute, spectators threw tennis balls covered in Palestinian flag stickers onto the field.
The players left the pitch for a few minutes before the match resumed.
In the 35th minute, a man ran onto the pitch waving a Palestinian flag, briefly interrupting the match again.
Ireland's Icelandic coach Heimir Hallgrimsson said afterwards that "you are never happy with this (protests), but understand it and respect it".
The incidents follow the controversy surrounding Sunday's Nations League match between Ireland and Israel.
After lengthy discussions about a boycott, in protest against the war in Gaza, the Irish players finally decided to play the match, which took place in Hungary in a virtually empty stadium.
The Irish players, who won 3–0, wore black armbands, and the captains of both teams did not shake hands or exchange pennants before kick-off.
The return leg is scheduled for Sunday, once again on neutral ground in Serbia, as the Irish Football Association deemed organising the match at home too sensitive.
On Thursday evening, around 200 protesters gathered outside the Dublin Arena as part of a campaign called "Stop the Game".
"I strongly object to these two games against Israel going ahead, because basically it is sports-washing a genocide, sports are political. And it's happened many, many a time where people have boycotted events," said Joanne Doyle, a 56-year-old primary school teacher.
She was one of around 200 protesting outside the stadium in Dublin.
"Ireland should not be playing ball with genocide. We've already played one game against genocidal Israel and crossed the Palestinian picket line." said Mark Coomey, a 26-year-old engineer.
Ireland, alongside Spain and Norway, recognised a Palestinian state in 2024 and has repeatedly criticised Israel over the Gaza conflict.

title: Pakistan  India  Australia in same World Cup group
description: Green shirts open their Group A campaign against India in Johannesburg on October 10
content:
Green-shirts open their Group A campaign against India in Johannesburg on October 10
India will meet defending champions Australia and bitter rivals Pakistan in their first two matches at the 2027 Cricket World Cup, the International Cricket Council (ICC) announced on Thursday.
The India-Australia match, a repeat of the 2023 final, will be in Cape Town on October 7 and the India-Pakistan clash will take place in Johannesburg three days later.
The tournament, hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, will start on October 2 and the final will be played on November 21.
The group match between India and Pakistan will be played at the Wanderers Stadium, the tournament's biggest venue and tickets are almost certain to be in high demand.
Zimbabwe, Afghanistan and a qualifier will be the other teams in Group A.
Zimbabwe will play all of their group matches at home, with two matches in Bulawayo, two in Harare and the last fixture in the group against India at Victoria Falls.
South Africa will play their first match in Group B against New Zealand in Cape Town on October 9, a day after England play the opening match in the group against Bangladesh in Windhoek, Namibia.
England will meet two of their main rivals in the group in Gqeberha. They will play South Africa on October 16 and New Zealand on October 23.
Also in Group B will be Sri Lanka and a qualifier.
Star India batsman Virat Kohli, 37, said in a televised interview at the launch in Cape Town that it would be his last World Cup.
He said that the intensity of a World Cup was like nothing else in cricket.
"To maintain that intensity for 10 games takes a lot out of you in foreign conditions. It's the last World Cup I am going to play for India and my motivation is to leave everything out there," said Kohli.
Australian captain Pat Cummins said of the opening match: "Anytime you play India, you feel there are a billion people watching.
"It's going to be great. I still get called up all the time about that 2023 final and they'll be up for revenge."
After a preliminary round to eliminate two of the three lowest-ranked teams, 12 teams will be split into two groups for round-robin matches before the top three in each group, and the best fourth-placed team, qualify for a Super Seven phase, followed by semi-finals and the final.
Because of political tensions between the two countries, India and Pakistan have only played each other in ICC events since Pakistan toured India for three one-day internationals and two Twenty20 internationals in December 2012.
The rivalry is intense despite India having won all eight matches against Pakistan in Cricket World Cups and eight out of nine in T20 World Cups.

US suffered 'humiliating defeat' against Iran: IRGC commander
Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on the World Day for the Prevention of Violence that the day was an opportunity to recall a "bitter reality" of US and Israeli aggression against Iran.
"When the United States and the Israeli regime target the security and lives of nations through military aggression, the slaughter of civilians, and the destruction of infrastructure, we confront the most blatant form of state violence."

He added that "silence" from other nations when confronted with these crimes amounted to "complicity in violence."
US suffered 'humiliating defeat' against Iran: IRGC commander
The commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Quds Force said the United States, despite its vast resources and equipment, has been expelled from Iraq and has suffered a humiliating defeat against Iran, according to Press TV .
Brigadier General Esmail Qaani made the remarks on Thursday night at the “Nasr Qarib” ceremony in Tehran, held to mark the second anniversary of the martyrdom of the leaders of the Lebanese Resistance, Press TV reported.

“This year’s anniversary is being observed at a time when the US, despite possessing vast resources and equipment, has been expelled from Iraq, and the Iraqi people are celebrating this victory, thanks to the resistance of the Iraqi nation and the heroes of the Resistance Front,” he said.
Qaani said the Americans had imagined they could force Iran to surrender within four days, or two weeks at most, “but they encountered a reality vastly different from their calculations.”
He added that remaining traces of US presence in the region must also be removed, and that signs of this process are already visible.
He went on to say that Washington was downplaying the significance of its exit from Iraq in the eyes of world public opinion by raising peripheral issues, such as aircraft flights.
Yemen carried out 20 strikes on Houthi targets in Taiz province, spokesperson says
The military spokesperson for Yemen's internationally recognised government said on Friday that warplanes carried out 20 strikes over ​the past three hours targeting Houthi movements, personnel, vehicles and ‌military equipment in Taiz province.
The strikes come amid the most serious escalation between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned Houthis since a UN-brokered truce largely halted cross-border attacks ​in 2022.
Unchallenged occupation of southwestern Yemen's Taiz would give the ​Houthis full control over the country's north, a tighter grip ⁠on the Red Sea coast and easier access to the south ​and the southern port city of Aden, seat of the government.
The renewed ​conflict has already displaced tens of thousands of people and could reshape control in Yemen, with implications for Red Sea shipping lanes and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
US Energy Department engineer arrested over alleged support for Houthis
A US Energy Department electrical engineer has been arrested for allegedly supporting Yemen’s Houthis by purchasing materials for homemade explosives and drones and traveling to Yemen, US local media reported on Friday.
“Ashton Hamed Ellaboudy, 51, of Richland, Washington, was arrested Thursday and is due to make his first court appearance Friday,” CBS News reported, citing the Justice Department.
Ellaboudy sought to help the Houthis enhance their communications capabilities and traveled to Yemen last September, CBS News cited the FBI as saying.
“Ellaboudy used a passport issued to him when he was working at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to make his way to Oman, then bordering Yemen,” CBS News quoted the Justice Department as saying.
Ellaboudy faces charges under a US law criminalizing the provision of material support to organizations designated as foreign terrorist organizations, a designation that applies to the Houthis.
If convicted, he could face up to 20 years in prison, according to the Justice Department.
Japanese, Qatari premiers discuss US-Iran war at meeting in Tokyo
The Japanese and Qatari prime ministers on Friday discussed the conflict between the US and Iran during a meeting in Tokyo, according to an official statement.
“I expressed strong concern over the ongoing military tensions surrounding Iran and the significant disruption to the rules-based maritime order,” Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on US social media company X after meeting with Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani.

During the war, in addition to US strikes on Iran, Tehran has also launched attacks on US military bases and energy facilities in Gulf states such as Qatar.
Takaichi conveyed her “deep respect for the important role Qatar is playing as a mediator, and stated my wish to closely collaborate with Qatar toward the early stabilisation of the situation.”
Al Thani spoke on the “current status” of the US-Iran talks, said Takaichi.
Takaichi told Al Thani that Japan “is currently formulating a comprehensive cooperation plan aimed at enhancing the economic and energy resilience of the Gulf countries, including Qatar.”
On bilateral ties, the two sides discussed economic partnership with “a desire to strengthen cooperation not only in traditional energy fields but also in various areas including investment and artificial intelligence.”
“We will continue to closely collaborate with Qatar to strengthen the ‘strategic partnership’ between our two countries,” said Takaichi.
Al Thani, who is also Qatar's foreign minister, also met with his Japanese counterpart Toshimitsu Motegi, according to Japan's Foreign Ministry.
Motegi expressed "strong concern" over the prolonged impasse between the US and Iran, saying that the more than six-month disruption of free and safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz has had a "significant impact on the global economy."
US sends additional Patriot batteries to protect Saudi, Qatari energy sites: Axios
The US military has deployed two additional Patriot missile batteries to protect energy facilities in Saudi Arabia and Qatar amid preparations for possible renewed military operations against Iran, the Axios news site reported on Thursday, citing two US officials and a regional source.
One battery was sent to Saudi Arabia last month to protect a key oil facility, while another was deployed to Qatar to defend a natural gas facility, according to the report.
The deployments were intended to reassure both countries that Washington would protect their critical energy infrastructure if US President Donald Trump resumes major combat operations against Iran.
Trump said on Thursday that he was considering renewing a bombing campaign in the coming weeks.
“Now I have to make a decision: either Iran signs the deal, or it won't exist any longer,” he said.

Axios reported that Saudi and Qatari leaders urged Trump in early August against launching a major attack that would include strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure, fearing retaliation against their oil and gas facilities.
US officials said those appeals were a key factor in his decision to pursue economic pressure instead.
The report said Washington would need Saudi permission to use the kingdom’s airspace for renewed major combat operations, but Riyadh would be unlikely to agree without assurances that its oil facilities were protected.
US Central Command spokesman Captain Tim Hawkins declined to comment.
Meanwhile, the US is sending additional warships, fighter jets and troops to the Middle East, Axios reported.
A US official said the USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier and its strike group left San Diego on Sunday and were expected to reach the region around mid-November.
Officials have yet to determine whether the carrier will replace an existing deployment or increase the US presence to three carrier strike groups.
The Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group, carrying thousands of Marines from the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit, also departed for the region Monday and is expected to arrive by the end of November, the report said.
Houthis say Saudi Arabia launches strikes on Sanaa, 3 Yemeni provinces
The Yemeni Houthi group said Thursday that Saudi Arabia carried out airstrikes on the capital Sanaa and the provinces of Saada, Taiz and Amran.
The Houthi-run SABA news agency said warplanes allegedly belonging to Saudi Arabia targeted Sanaa and several locations across the three provinces.
The report provided no details on the sites targeted, casualties or damage.
Separately, Yemen’s military said 27 airstrikes targeted Houthi positions and gathering points in the southwestern province of Taiz.
Military spokesman Colonel Majid Abdullah al-Nuzaili said the strikes targeted a missile depot, command and control centres, supply and weapons sites, concentrations of Houthi fighters and military vehicles.
He said the strikes destroyed dozens of military vehicles and other assets and killed or wounded a number of Houthi fighters.
Brigadier General Turki al-Maliki, spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition, earlier said on US social media platform X that air defences intercepted and destroyed drones and ballistic missiles launched toward the Saudi cities of Khamis Mushait and Jazan.
Al-Maliki also said the Houthis had targeted the Taiba power station in Saudi Arabia’s Medina with a drone two days earlier.
US ambassador to UN accuses Iran of violating nuclear obligations
The US ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz on Friday accused Iran of violating its nuclear obligations by not abandoning its nuclear program.
"Iran broke the rules. They refused to abandon their nuclear ambitions. They are enriching uranium to 60%, which has no credible civilian purpose," he said.

Iran urges Iraq to lift flight restrictions, restore normal air travel
Iran on Thursday called for restrictions on flights between Iran and Iraq to be lifted and for normal air travel between the two countries to resume.
In a statement, the Iranian Foreign Ministry said Tehran, while respecting Iraq’s national sovereignty, called for “appropriate decisions” to lift the restrictions and restore normal operations by airlines of both countries.
The ministry accused the US of using sanctions and “economic terrorism” to disrupt Iran’s trade and air links with other countries.
It said restrictions on Iran-Iraq air travel run counter to the interests of both countries and have caused serious difficulties for hundreds of thousands of passengers, including pilgrims, patients, students and businesspeople.
The ministry said ties between Iran and Iraq are rooted in deep historical, religious, cultural and people-to-people connections, adding that transportation links should be managed through an “independent, responsible and forward-looking approach” based on their common interests.
Türkiye condemns Houthi attack on civilian infrastructure serving Prophet’s Mosque in Saudi Arabia
Türkiye on Thursday strongly condemned an attack by Yemen’s Houthi group on civilian infrastructure serving the Prophet’s Mosque in Saudi Arabia.
“We strongly condemn the Houthis’ attack on civilian infrastructure serving the Prophet’s Mosque in Medina,” the Turkish Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
“These provocative attacks, which threaten Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty and security and target the sacred values of the Islamic world, must end immediately and unconditionally,” it added.
The ministry also reiterated Türkiye’s support for Saudi Arabia and urged restraint amid regional tensions.
“We reiterate our strong support for Saudi Arabia and emphasise the need to avoid steps that would further escalate tensions in the region,” it said.
OIC, Arab states condemn drone attack on Saudi Arabia's Medina power station
The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and several Arab countries on Thursday condemned a drone attack on a power station in Medina, Saudi Arabia, that the Saudi-led coalition attributed to the Houthis.
The statements from the organisation, the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain followed a Saudi announcement that the Taiba electricity distribution station, which provides power to the Prophet's Mosque, had been targeted.
The organization's General Secretariat said it "strongly condemned and denounced" the attack.
It described the targeting of vital infrastructure and facilities in Medina as "a dangerous escalation and a blatant violation of the sanctity of holy sites," as well as international and humanitarian laws and norms.
The organisation affirmed its full solidarity with Saudi Arabia in measures taken to protect its territory, security and stability, defend Islamic holy sites and safeguard citizens and residents.
The UAE Foreign Ministry said the drone attack constituted "a flagrant violation of the sovereignty of Saudi Arabia and a threat to its security and stability."
It reiterated Abu Dhabi's full solidarity with the kingdom and support for measures aimed at safeguarding its security and stability.
Jordan also condemned the attack, saying it represented a "blatant violation" of Saudi sovereignty and threatened the kingdom's security, stability and territorial integrity.
It also described the attack as a violation of international law and the UN Charter.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Fuad Majali affirmed Jordan's "absolute solidarity" with Saudi Arabia and its support for measures taken to protect the kingdom, its institutions, citizens and residents.
Kuwait said the targeting of an electrical facility serving the Prophet's Mosque was part of what it described as repeated hostile attacks against civilian infrastructure.
"Such attacks constituted a violation of Saudi sovereignty, international law and international humanitarian law, while also provoking the feelings of Muslims worldwide and threatening the sanctity of Islamic holy sites," the Foreign Ministry said.
Kuwait reaffirmed its full solidarity with Saudi Arabia, saying the kingdom's security was inseparable from the security of Kuwait and other Gulf Cooperation Council states.
Bahrain condemned "continued attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis against Saudi Arabia."
Manama said it supports Saudi Arabia in measures taken to defend its sovereignty and security under its right to self-defence.
Bahrain also called on the UN Security Council to take a firm position against repeated Houthi attacks and ensure the implementation of relevant resolutions, including Resolution 2216 of 2015 and Resolution 2817 of 2026.
Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted 2 ballistic missiles, 4 drones over southern Saudi Arabia
The Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s government said on Thursday evening that it intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles and four drones over southern Saudi Arabia.
In a statement, the coalition said the two ballistic missiles were intercepted and destroyed over the cities of Khamis Mushait and Jazan.
Four drones were also intercepted and destroyed over Khamis Mushait, it added.
The coalition said its forces would continue “taking and implementing operational measures to deter the Houthi militia.”
It provided no further details about casualties or damage caused.

A tanker was struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, causing a fire aboard the vessel, the UK Maritime Trade Operations said.

"Several oil tankers have been hit in the Strait of Hormuz in recent days, three of the latest of which are owned or leased by entities in the UAE," a statement carried by IRNA read.

title: Bugti vows quality healthcare across Balochistan
description: Bugti vows quality healthcare across Balochistan
content:

Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti on Thursday said providing quality healthcare to the people was among the government's top priorities, as reforms in the health sector were beginning to show positive results.
He said improvements in medical facilities at government hospitals had encouraged ordinary citizens and members of the provincial assembly to seek treatment at public-sector facilities.
Bugti, accompanied by National Party chief Dr Abdul Malik Baloch, visited Civil Sandeman Provincial Hospital to inquire after the health of MPA and former provincial health minister Mir Rahmat Saleh Baloch, who had undergone a successful angioplasty at the hospital's cardiology department.
The chief minister also consulted doctors about Baloch's condition.
Expressing satisfaction with the treatment, Mir Rahmat Saleh Baloch said the availability of quality healthcare at the hospital was saving people the hardship and additional expense of travelling to other cities for treatment.
In a post on X, Bugti said the primary objective of the ongoing health-sector reforms was to reduce the need for residents to travel outside the province for medical treatment.
He said practical measures were being taken to introduce modern medical facilities and improve treatment standards at government hospitals.
The chief minister said the government was working to equip major hospitals with specialised medical centres and facilities capable of treating complex ailments locally.
He added that efforts were underway to restore public confidence in government hospitals and ensure citizens had access to timely and quality medical treatment within the province.
Bugti said improving the health sector was an ongoing process and the government was utilising available resources to enhance medical equipment, diagnostic facilities, emergency services and treatment capabilities for various diseases.
He said the successful angioplasty of Mir Rahmat Saleh Baloch and his satisfaction with the treatment reflected the progress being made under the health-sector reforms.

PTI's parliamentary party leader in the National Assembly Shahid Khattak and Information Minister Shafi Jan said Chief Minister Afridi would lead the march. Former chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur is also expected to join the procession.
The march is being organised to press for the acceleration of hearings in cases against PTI founder Imran Khan, his treatment at Shifa International Hospital and an end to restrictions on meetings with him.
The chief minister is expected to issue the detailed schedule of the march on Friday (today) and brief members of the provincial assembly, party office-bearers and affiliated organisations.

title: Afridi launches Rs2 6b livestock health plan
description: Afridi launches Rs2 6b livestock health plan
content:
145 mobile clinics, 27 labs to expand vet services
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Thursday inaugurated a Rs2.6 billion livestock health programme aimed at improving animal healthcare and supporting the livelihoods of livestock farmers.
The plan, titled "Ehsaas-e-Bezaban Sehat Gaari", includes 145 mobile veterinary clinics and 27 mobile laboratory testing units, along with the deployment of 202 veterinary doctors and assistants.
According to a brief given by the livestock department, the mobile clinics will provide vaccination, diagnostic, treatment and emergency veterinary services at the tehsil level, expanding access to essential veterinary care for livestock farmers in remote and underserved areas.
The briefing stated that the mobile veterinary network will be integrated with a central digital dashboard to strengthen service monitoring, oversight and operational management.
Mobile milk-quality testing laboratories will also support systematic monitoring of milk quality and provide on-site testing facilities for the detection of adulteration and harmful contaminants.
Speaking at the inauguration, the chief minister noted that "Ehsaas-e-Bezaban Sehat Gaari" was not merely a mobile veterinary service but rather represented a commitment, a sense of responsibility and a vision for the welfare of livestock and the communities that depend on them.
"No farmer should be deprived of quality veterinary services because of geographical distance or location," Afridi said.
He stressed that protecting livestock from disease, inadequate care and limited access to veterinary services was a collective responsibility, adding that the programme was designed not only to provide treatment but also to strengthen disease prevention and improve livestock productivity.
"Livestock represents an important source of income, nutrition and financial security for millions of families across the province, the chief minister said, adding that modern, quality and timely veterinary services were being brought closer to livestock farmers so that they would not have to travel long distances for the treatment and care of their animals.

title: Faisalabad air quality deteriorates ahead of smog season
description: Faisalabad air quality deteriorates ahead of smog season
content:
Nearly 60% of daily OPD patients at Allied Hospital report respiratory complaints
Heavy dust and industrial emissions have already begun affecting several areas along Faisalabad's Sargodha Road ahead of the November smog season.
Areas around Samana Bridge, Madina University, Bawa Chak Drain, Dawood Mills Stop and Yousaf Bus Stop and adjoining localities have been enveloped in dust and smoke from nearby industrial units, according to residents and environmentalists.
Private environmentalist and entrepreneur Sultan Ali Khan said the current Air Quality Index (AQI) in Faisalabad was around 132 to 160, categorised as unhealthy to unhealthy for sensitive groups, according to the Punjab AQI Dashboard and IQAir.
He said pollution levels could rise further during peak traffic hours and periods of low wind.
Khan advised children, older people and those with heart or respiratory conditions to avoid prolonged outdoor exertion during periods of high pollution. He also suggested that people spending extended periods outdoors consider wearing masks and keep windows closed when pollution levels were high.
Abdul Ghaffar, a retired WASA director and former resident of Gulshan-e-Madina Colony, recalled that residents had long faced the impact of soot and smoke in the area.
"Whenever we went to the nearby mosque, especially for Fajr prayers, our clothes would often become covered in soot. The smoke would mix with it and make them almost black," he said.
He said clothes washed and hung outside overnight could also become covered in a white layer before turning black, while floors inside homes were also affected by soot.
He said the pollution had become one of the reasons his family eventually shifted from the locality to FDA City, around four miles away.
Dr Naveed Ahmed, a physician at Allied Hospital, expressed concern over the reported increase in respiratory illnesses associated with deteriorating air quality.
He said industrial pollutants were contributing to respiratory, lung, kidney and ear, nose and throat (ENT) problems.
According to Dr Ahmed, between 5,000 and 6,000 patients visit the hospital's outpatient department daily, with nearly 60% reporting respiratory complaints.
Meanwhile, Environment Protection Department (EPD) Deputy Director Tahir Abbas Sayyal said several industrial and power-related units had been identified as "red zones" and action had been taken against those found violating environmental regulations.
He said the department had conducted inspections of roadside and power-related units and identified violations. The details of the inspections and violations would be shared, he added.
Sayyal said the department had also held a pre-consultative session with industrial units, advising them against using substandard fuel and directing them to adopt required pollution-control measures and keep their control systems operational.
The units were also instructed to provide the Environmental Protection Agency access to their CCTV systems so that compliance could be monitored when required, he said.
"We have taken proper action against them, and we have the relevant files and records," Sayyal said, adding that seven-day notices had been issued to units found with deficiencies.
Explaining the procedure, Sayyal said the notices informed units about deficiencies in their systems and directed them to rectify them. They were also asked to address any other environmental violations arising from their operations.
"If they fail to comply, we proceed towards imposing fines, registration of cases and FIRs, and ultimately demolition where legally applicable," he said.

A dispute over food and the fixing of a water pipe allegedly escalated into violence.
According to the FIR, Usman and his associates allegedly attacked Ashraf and Falak Sher with a sharp-edged improvised weapon made from a steel mug. Both prisoners sustained serious injuries and were initially taken to the jail hospital before being shifted to Lahore General Hospital.

title: Pink salt value addition financing launched
description: Pink salt value addition financing launched
content:
110-acre pink salt processing unit in Quaidabad has been established as a specialised industrial cluster
A Pink Salt Value Addition Financing Scheme was launched on Thursday by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif who distributed cheques among 10 businesspersons who secured interest-free loans under the initiative.
The chief minister stressed the need to introduce value-added pink salt products to international markets.
According to Mines and Minerals Minister Sher Ali Gorchani and Secretary Parvez Butt, the scheme carries an allocation of Rs5 billion in interest-free loans, with individual businesses eligible for financing of up to Rs50 million. The Punjab government will bear Rs1.456 billion in interest costs under the scheme.
A 110-acre pink salt processing unit in Quaidabad has been established as a specialised industrial cluster.
The Pink Salt Mineral Processing Zone in Quaidabad is planned to house 200 value-addition units and create employment opportunities for more than 10,000 people, while contributing to an increase in exports.
A model retail outlet has been established to promote pink salt branding, packaging, marketing and processing. Officials said value addition, branding and development of pink salt products could help increase annual exports by up to $300 million.
The chief minister said Pakistan should export branded pink salt rather than merely raw material.
"Pink salt is Pakistan's uniqueness," she said, adding that the country's salt and labour were being used while other countries reaped the benefits.
She said pink salt was a national mineral asset and urged the development of value-added products for international markets. The government, she added, would support young entrepreneurs and startups under the financing scheme and facilitate their access to global markets.
"Pakistan's pink salt is like gold hidden in the mountains," she said.
The chief minister said that in the past, contracts had allegedly been awarded to benefit political individuals, causing losses to the national exchequer. She said the resources of Punjab, including "placer gold" flowing through its five rivers, should benefit the people of the province.
Meanwhile, European Parliament Member Mary Fatima Khan Holch met Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz and discussed the promotion of agriculture, IT and technology, as well as trade matters.
The CM said on the occasion that the European Union was Pakistan's second-largest trading partner.
Mary Fatima Holch appreciated the public welfare projects being implemented in Punjab and the Minority Card initiative and other measures taken for the welfare of minorities.

title: Litterbugs face hefty fines in Punjab
description: Litterbugs face hefty fines in Punjab
content:
Govt starts billing urban property owners for sanitation services
The provincial government on Thursday began billing urban property owners for sanitation services under the Suthra Punjab programme, while authorities in Lahore announced a crackdown on littering with fines of up to Rs500,000 for serious violations.
The Punjab Excise, Taxation and Narcotics Control Department will issue sanitation fee bills to owners of around five million residential and commercial properties in urban areas across the province. The government expects to collect around Rs40 billion annually through the new system.
According to officials, property owners will receive bills covering six months of sanitation fees and have 60 days to make payment. Late payments will be subject to penalties.
The government has assigned responsibility for billing and collection to the excise department. Data integration between the department and the Suthra Punjab programme has been completed, with bills to be printed using Urban Unit data and sent to the relevant regions.
Inspectors in the respective excise circles will be responsible for delivering the bills. The distribution of bills in urban areas is scheduled to begin on Friday.
The excise department will collect the sanitation fee alongside property tax under the new mechanism. Earlier government-approved rates included monthly charges ranging from Rs300 for residential properties measuring up to five marla to Rs5,000 for those exceeding 40 marla, while commercial units are subject to charges ranging from Rs500 to Rs3,000, depending on their size.
Meanwhile, authorities in Lahore have announced a crackdown on littering, with the Lahore Waste Management Company (LWMC) and Punjab Safe Cities Authority (PSCA) set to jointly monitor violations.
The first phase will target 10 major markets in the city. According to LWMC Chief Executive Officer Sheryar Khan, PSCA cameras will be used to identify people found littering, after which LWMC field staff will reach the location and take action.
Field staff will be able to show shopkeepers video evidence of the violation and impose fines ranging from Rs5,000 to Rs50,000, according to the CEO.
Those found polluting the environment or burning waste could face fines of up to Rs500,000.
The initial list of major markets includes Mall Road, Jail Road, Ferozepur Road, Gulberg Main Boulevard and Liberty Chowk, among others.
Khan said the enforcement would be expanded after the initial 10 to other markets, commercial centres and people found throwing waste from vehicles.
Earlier, Suthra Punjab authorities in Lahore had introduced an e-challan system against littering. Under the applicable laws, littering in public places can attract fines ranging from Rs1,000 to Rs10,000, while failure to keep the area outside a house, shop or factory clean can result in fines ranging from Rs1,000 to Rs50,000. Burning waste can attract a fine of up to Rs500,000 and imprisonment for up to two years.

title: 59 women lured with  jobs   stripped of phones
description: 59 women lured with  jobs   stripped of phones
content:
Police arrest two suspects, including female coordinator
A job interview that promised Rs2,000 a day ended with an unexpected exit - 59 women who had arrived at a farmhouse in Gadap hoping to land work were left without their mobile phones after the alleged event organiser disappeared with them.
The women had been lured from different parts of Karachi with promises of a 25-day assignment at a private housing society, complete with daily wages, food and transport. Instead, they found themselves at a farmhouse where the "boss" they had been told would interview them never showed up.
After lunch, the women were asked to hand over their phones on the pretext that ringing devices could disturb the expected meeting with the boss. The phones were collected in a bag - and the man who collected them allegedly walked out with the haul.
Gadap City police registered a case and arrested two suspects, including a female coordinator, while raids were being conducted for the alleged organiser and recovery of the phones.
According to a spokesperson for SSP Malir District, the women had been promised work at an event titled "Activities" at a private housing society along the Superhighway. They were allegedly told that builders and housing society officials would interview them at the farmhouse before the assignment began.
The spokesperson said the farmhouse had been booked by a man identified as Waqas, while a woman named Nargis was allegedly coordinating the participants. Sahil Salman was identified as the event organiser.
The women were picked up from different parts of the metropolis in two buses and brought to the farmhouse at around 1pm on Wednesday. After lunch, Salman allegedly collected their phones before leaving the premises. Nargis also reportedly left around the same time.
The women alerted police, who reached the farmhouse and recorded their statements. An FIR was registered at Gadap City police station on the complaint of Khushnuma Zaib under Sections 379, 420 and 34 of the Pakistan Penal Code.
Police arrested Waqas, who had booked the farmhouse, and Nargis, the alleged coordinator. Raids were under way to arrest Salman and recover the phones.
Farmhouse manager Ashar Ansari said in a video statement that the premises had been booked for an event involving around 50 to 55 women. He said Waqas had made the booking but did not come to the farmhouse, while a man identified as "Asif or Salman" arrived with a woman. Ansari said that when he later contacted the organiser about payment, he was told that he was on his way. Shortly afterwards, the caretaker informed him that the man had collected the women's phones and fled.

Towns in the metropolis have been asked to explain where billions of rupees collected from gas companies and other institutions for road cutting have gone, after officials failed to provide the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of the Sindh Assembly with a consolidated account of the funds and their utilisation.
The PAC, chaired by Nisar Ahmed Khuhro, directed the Local Government Department to develop a mechanism for monitoring development works carried out by all Karachi towns and submit town-wise details of road-cutting funds and their expenditure.
The issue came up during a PAC meeting on Thursday attended by Local Government Department officials and town municipal commissioners. The committee was reviewing audit paras concerning Jinnah Town Municipal Corporation.
Jinnah Town officials told the committee that the town had received Rs800 million in road-cutting charges, while development works worth Rs300 million had been tendered through National Invitation to Tender (NIT).
Khuhro sought a list of the development schemes included in the Rs300 million NIT and directed officials to provide details of funds received by every Karachi town from Sui Southern Gas Company and other institutions for road cutting, along with their utilisation.
Local government officials admitted that different towns had received varying amounts over different periods but could not provide the PAC with details of the funds received or how they had been spent.
The committee subsequently sought complete town-wise records of billions of rupees received from SSGC and other institutions for road cutting and their utilisation.

title: Mir Raza commission gets extension until Oct 15
description: Mir Raza commission gets extension until Oct 15
content:
Cabinet approves wheat release from Oct 20, 200-bed hospital in North Karachi
The Sindh cabinet on Thursday extended the tenure of the Judicial Commission probing the death of Mir Raza Ali until October 15, giving the panel additional time to complete its proceedings and finalise its findings.
The decision was taken at a meeting chaired by Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, which also approved wheat release to flour mills from October 20, a 200-bed mother and child hospital in North Karachi and several judicial appointments.
The cabinet was told that the commission, headed by Justice Umar Sial, had recorded statements from several witnesses but needed more time to complete its inquiry. It was also authorised to continue proceedings beyond October 15 if required.
The cabinet discussed rising flour prices, with Food Minister Makhdoom Mehboob Zaman saying wheat in Karachi was selling at around Rs12,500 per 100kg bag.
Chief Secretary Asif Hyder Shah directed that government wheat be released to licensed flour mills and chakkis through a regulated mechanism. The release is proposed to begin on October 20. Sindh has more than 9.19 million 100kg bags, including old and newly procured stocks, confiscated wheat, PASSCO supplies and imports expected by month-end.
The cabinet considered a proposal to ban migratory bird hunting in Sindh after a wildlife survey recorded 143,460 birds across six divisions, compared with 140,866 last year.
A ministerial subcommittee was formed to examine the environmental impact, enforcement and international practices before making recommendations. It comprises Dr Azra Fazal Pechuho, Syed Sardar Shah, Zulfiqar Ali Shah and Rajvir Singh Sodha.
The cabinet approved converting the Sindh Government Children's Hospital in North Karachi into a 200-bed mother and child hospital under the Sindh Institute of Child Health and Neonatology. It will provide free maternal, newborn and paediatric care in Central District.
Chhinnesar Dispensary and Maternity Home was also approved for upgrading and round-the-clock operation by the Indus Hospital and Health Network, serving more than 122,000 people.
The cabinet approved amendments facilitating Phase III expansion of the Thar Block-II mining project, increasing annual capacity from 7.6 million to 11.2 million tonnes. The energy secretary was authorised to sign the revised agreements.
The cabinet approved the Sindh Government Lands Management Act 2026, replacing the 1912 law, and fixed Larkana University's affiliation jurisdiction for Larkana and Qambar Shahdadkot districts.
It also approved appointments for vacant anti-terrorism and narcotics courts, new boards for law colleges affiliated with the University of Sindh and Karachi University, and the purchase of 87 vehicles for district judiciary officers and newly appointed Sindh High Court judges.
The cabinet further endorsed Rs1 billion for Phase I of the STAR WASH programme through the Sindh People's Housing for Flood Affectees to improve water, sanitation and hygiene facilities in rural Sindh.

What was meant to be a link in the city's long-delayed Red Line network came crashing down on Thursday when an under-construction bridge structure collapsed near Bait-ul-Mukarram Mosque on University Road, killing a security guard deployed at the site.
The heavy concrete and steel structure gave way in Gulshan-e-Iqbal, burying the guard beneath the rubble and triggering a frantic rescue operation involving Rescue 1122, Edhi, Chhipa, police, Rangers and other emergency services.
Rescuers eventually pulled the man's body from beneath the debris and shifted it to JPMC, while initial fears that other workers could also be trapped prompted a technical search of the rubble. No evidence of anyone else being trapped was found, according to Rescue 1122.
The identity of the deceased guard could not immediately be ascertained, while Aziz Bhatti police were working to identify him with the help of a search device.
Rescue 1122 officials said there were initial fears that more workers could be trapped beneath the collapsed structure. However, the debris was subsequently examined using technical equipment and no evidence of more people being trapped was found.

The spokesperson referred to the recent inauguration of a portion of the project, alleging that it had been presented with considerable fanfare despite the project still being under construction. title: Pregnant mother found dead

content:
Family alleges ex-husband was pursuing victim despite divorce
A missing woman's trail ended in a patch of bushes near Jinnah Gate on Steel Mills Road, where police found the bullet-riddled body of 27-year-old Kashaf Kamal - a mother of one and six-month pregnant - two days after her family said she was taken away by her former husband.

According to the family, Kashaf, the fourth of seven siblings and a resident of Azimpura, Shah Faisal Colony, had contracted a love marriage with Yasir Durrani four years ago. However, Durrani divorced her barely two months later under pressure from his family, despite Kashaf being pregnant at the time
The family alleged that Durrani continued meeting Kashaf after the divorce and would also stay with her. They said he had visited their house two days before her body was found and took Kashaf with him, claiming that she was upset with him and that he wanted to reconcile with her.
They said Durrani usually visited their house on a motorcycle but arrived in a car that day. On Wednesday, he allegedly called the family and said Kashaf had gone somewhere, later claiming that she had gone to meet a friend named Fatima.
According to the family, Durrani returned to their house that night and stayed for about an hour, repeatedly saying that Kashaf had gone missing. Her younger sister subsequently posted a WhatsApp status seeking information about her.
The following day, the family received a call informing them that a woman's body had been found. They went to the Edhi morgue, where they identified the body as Kashaf's.

title: K 4 project  City braces for three years of traffic chaos
description: K 4 project  City braces for three years of traffic chaos
content:
94km network to cut through Karachi's busiest arteries
Karachi's water crisis could soon come with a fresh cost: a prolonged traffic nightmare, as the long-delayed K-IV project prepares to dig up some of the city's busiest roads to install 94 kilometres of water transmission lines - potentially leaving millions of commuters battling disruption for years.
The roads identified for the K-IV augmentation works include major stretches from Northern Bypass to Gulbai, including Abul Hasan Isphahani Road, the route from Maskan Chowrangi to Gulshan Chowrangi, Hasan Square to Liaquatabad and Nazimabad to Gulbai - arteries that already experience severe congestion, particularly during evening peak hours.
The main concern is not a temporary closure lasting a few weeks or months. The augmentation works are expected to continue for years, while no comprehensive alternative traffic plan has so far been prepared, according to sources familiar with the project.
The development comes as the K-IV project, originally conceived more than a decade ago at an estimated cost of Rs25 billion, has ballooned to around Rs224 billion, while the transmission network required to actually bring the additional water into Karachi is still awaiting execution.
Federal Minister for Planning Ahsan Iqbal has set December 2026 as the deadline for completion of K-IV. However, senior Water and Sewerage Corporation officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, told The Express Tribune that at the current pace the project was unlikely to be completed before January 2029, with further delays possible.
The city currently requires around 1.2 billion gallons of water a day, against a supply of approximately 650 million gallons, leaving a massive shortfall. The K-IV project is intended to provide an additional 260 million gallons per day. Even after its completion, however, the city would still face a daily shortfall estimated at 300-400 million gallons.
The critical augmentation network comprises three major lines - R-1, R-2 and R-3, stretching 26km, 40km and 28km respectively, for a combined length of 94km.
The lines, ranging from 72 to 96 inches in diameter, are the key infrastructure required to distribute the additional water into the city.
The R-2 line will run from Northern Bypass towards Toll Plaza, Super Highway, Janjal Goth, Sohrab Goth, Abul Hasan Isphahani Road, Disco Bakery, Gulshan Chowrangi, Rab Medical Centre, Sir Syed University and Nipa Chowrangi, where it will connect with the existing augmentation line. From Hasan Square, the network will continue towards Gharibabad, Liaquatabad, Nazimabad, Habib Bank Chowrangi and ultimately Gulbai. The routes include some of Karachi's most heavily used roads, raising fears of serious traffic disruption once excavation begins.
Sources said the three lines were estimated to cost around Rs80b, with 80% of the financing expected through loans from two international financial institutions and the remaining 20% to be provided by the Sindh govt. Another Rs124 billion is expected to be spent on transmission lines, pumping stations, filtration plants and related works. The K-IV augmentation work between Nipa Chowrangi and Hasan Square began in November 2025, covering just 2.7km. Almost 10 months later, around 70% of the work has reportedly been completed, with another two months or more potentially required.
Sources said this was only the initial stage of the augmentation project, while work on the much larger R-1, R-2 and R-3 network had yet to begin and contracts had not been finalised. The question now facing the city is how long the 94km network will take if just 2.7km has required almost a year.
A senior Water Corporation official confirmed that the lines required for distributing the additional water had yet to be started and that their contract had also not been awarded. At the current pace, the official said, K-IV could take until 2029 to become operational.
The planned excavation has also raised questions about coordination among government departments. KMC is currently carrying out resurfacing work on parts of Abul Hasan Isphahani Road, around Disco Bakery and Maskan, even though the same roads are expected to be excavated once the K-IV augmentation work begins.
Meanwhile, when The Express Tribune team visited Hasan Square-Nipa Chowrangi site to cover the ongoing K-IV augmentation work, personnel present there stopped the team from filming. The staff were asked who had ordered them to prevent media coverage but did not provide an answer.

content:
Wajid Ali, Syed Zameer Shah and Abdul Wahab to receive international recognition
Haripur has earned another major distinction as its calligraphers recently secured all three top positions in the seventh International Islamic Calligraphy Competition held in Houston, United States, under the title "Love of Muhammad (PBUH)".
A total of 1,200 calligraphy artworks from 50 countries were submitted in the international competition, but talented calligraphers from Haripur demonstrated their exceptional skills by securing the first, second and third positions. According to the results, Wajid Ali of Haripur secured first position in the calligraphy painting category presented in the online competition, while second position was also won by Haripur's renowned calligrapher Syed Zameer Shah, who is serving as a DM at Government High School Shadi Hattar.
Third position was secured by Abdul Wahab, also from Haripur.
All three talented calligraphers are students of renowned master and presidential award-winning calligrapher Ustad Ilahi Bakhsh Matee, who also belongs to Haripur and runs an academy while mentoring children in the field to promote the art.
Ustad Ilahi Bakhsh Matee is counted among Pakistan's prominent calligraphers. He also has the distinction of writing the largest Kalma Tayyaba at the National Assembly building, while another major honour associated with his calligraphy is that his work is also present at Masjid-e-Nabawi (PBUH).
In recognition of his valuable services to the art of calligraphy, he has also been awarded the Sitara-i-Imtiaz. Under the training and guidance of the great master, the young calligraphers from Haripur demonstrated their abilities at the international level and secured all three positions.
Ustad Abdul Razzaq and Ustad Rashid Aziz also played an important role in their guidance and efforts.
The international Islamic calligraphy competition is held every year during the blessed month of Rabi-ul-Awwal. Earlier, Zameer Shah had also won a position in the international competition, while securing all three top positions for Haripur this time is an extraordinary and historic achievement.
Wajid Ali, who secured the first position and belongs to Haripur city, will travel to the United States to receive his award and cash prize. The achievement of the three talented calligraphers from Haripur is not merely a victory in a competition, but also a beautiful global recognition of Haripur's talent, art and love for the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
The honour is a source of pride for Haripur, the fruit of the teachers' hard work and a proud moment for Pakistan.
Several prominent personalities also congratulated renowned calligraphers Wajid Ali, Syed Zameer Shah and Abdul Wahab, their teachers and families on the remarkable international achievement.

title: Textures of Emotions  subverts feminine stereotypes
description: Textures of Emotions  subverts feminine stereotypes
content:
The exhibit features 27 works exploring womanhood through varying colours and textures
"Textures of Emotions," a solo exhibition by artist Mobina Zuberi, opens today at Gallery 6, Islamabad. The exhibition brings together 27 recent and selected works from two distinct yet interconnected strands of the artist's practice: her evocative paintings of women and her abstract compositions.
Mobina Zuberi's artistic journey spans several decades, beginning in the 1970s and evolving through a wide range of subjects, styles and approaches. Over the past decade, two particular bodies of work have occupied a significant place in her practice. Although her figurative paintings of women and her abstractions appear markedly different at first glance, both emerge from the artist's sensitivity to mood, expression, form and visual atmosphere. In both, Mobina is less concerned with describing the external world than with capturing something more elusivethe emotional quality of a moment.
The women in Mobina's paintings do not conform to familiar ideals of feminine beauty or to established archetypes. They are neither glamorous figures nor fairy-tale princesses, mythological characters, fertility symbols or folkloric heroines. Nor do they derive from the imagery of the traditional Mughal miniature. Instead, Mobina presents women in seemingly ordinary yet psychologically charged moments. Her figures appear absorbed in their own worlds, often caught in moments of introspection, stillness or quiet anticipation.
There is no deliberate grotesqueness or theatrical distortion in these works; neither does Mobina rely on overt nudity or exaggerated eroticism. Yet many of her figures possess a quiet sensuality and an alluring presence. Their appeal lies not in conventional physical perfection but in the suggestion of an inner life. They seem to exist somewhere between the personal and the universal, inviting the viewer to wonder about the thought, memory, desire or experience that may lie beyond the painted surface.
Her abstract paintings follow a different visual vocabulary, yet they too are deeply concerned with atmosphere and feeling. Here, the human figure disappears, and emotion is communicated through the relationships between shape, colour, space, texture and movement. Balance and spatial depth are carefully orchestrated to create compositions that engage the viewer beyond the immediately visible.

title: Punjab begins garbage tax recovery

content:
New system takes effect from July 1, 2026; household fee ranges from Rs300 to Rs5k
The Punjab government's Local Government and Community Development Department has formally notified the collection of sanitation fees from residential and commercial areas under the Suthra Punjab Programme.
According to the notification, responsibility for collecting the sanitation fee has been formally assigned to the Excise, Taxation and Narcotics Control Department, Punjab, with the new system taking effect from July 1, 2026.
The Excise Department will issue consolidated waste bills covering July, August and September to all consumers during October. The bills are to be recovered by 31 October, while an online payment facility will also be made available by October 15.
According to the notification, monthly sanitation fees for domestic consumers in urban areas have been fixed according to property size. Households up to five marlas will pay Rs300 per month, those measuring five to 10 marlas Rs500, 10 to 20 marlas Rs1,000, 20 to 40 marlas Rs2,000, and properties exceeding 40 marlas Rs5,000 per month.
For commercial premises in urban areas, the monthly fee has been fixed according to the size of the business. Small businesses will pay Rs500, medium-sized businesses Rs1,000 and large businesses Rs3,000 per month.

Residents say workshops, scrap dealers burn waste material to extract oil
Despite restrictions imposed by the district administration and the Environmental Protection and Climate Change Department, workshops, scrap dealers and old-tyre shops along Nullah Leh have stepped up the burning of tyres, plastic and other waste to extract oil and recover recyclable materials.

Citizens Waqar Shah, Fayyaz Akbar and Nadeem Akhtar said the burning of tyres, plastic and waste was prohibited and that the smog season had already begun. They called on the Environmental Protection Department to immediately halt the practice.
They said brick kilns, factories and smoke-emitting vehicles were further contributing to air pollution in Rawalpindi, while the city's air quality index had also crossed 100.
The residents said the government had already imposed a complete ban on burning old tyres to extract black oil and demanded action against those burning tyres and waste plastic.
They added that burning unusable tyres, plastic and scrap along Nullah Leh had become routine, while the remains were subsequently dumped into the nullah instead of being properly disposed of.
The residents said the practice was not only damaging the environment but also increasing the risk of respiratory illnesses among people living near the nullah. They also called for the waste and burnt tyre residue dumped along Nullah Leh to be removed immediately, warning that the material could block the watercourse and worsen flooding during heavy rains. Bloc says work on migrant return hubs 'progressing well'
Work to set up migrant return hubs outside the European Union is progressing "very well", Denmark said Thursday as the bloc's home affairs ministers met in Luxembourg to discuss further ways to boost deportations.
Denmark -- along with Austria, Greece, Germany and the Netherlands -- has been exploring options to set up such migrant centres.
"When it comes to return hubs it's progressing very well," Danish interior minister Morten Bodskov told reporters, arriving at the EU meeting after holding talks with colleagues from the other four nations working on the issue.
"We are moving in the right direction," he said without providing further details.
Germany's Alexander Dobrindt said there were "preliminary" talks but declined to say which countries were involved. More work was needed to make sure any agreement would withstand possible lawsuits, he said.
"These agreements are meant to be sustainable in the long term," he said, adding that he was nevertheless hopeful that a first deal could be sealed by the end of the year.
The Luxembourg talks come with anti-immigration parties riding high across the bloc, as evidenced by far-right gains in Germany last month.
EU ministers gave final approval to tougher new migration rules allowing for the creation of return hubs and granting authorities much broader detention powers.
The regulation is to enter into force in the coming weeks, the EU said.
The meeting agenda included discussion on using "enhanced cooperation" with "priority" non-EU countries for returns of people with no right to stay in the bloc.

title: Syria  Hezbollah held secret talks in Turkey
description: Syria  Hezbollah held secret talks in Turkey
content:
Longtime foes met in September, sources say
Representatives of the Syrian government and Lebanese militant group Hezbollah have held face-to-face talks in Turkey to try to calm tensions between them, according to six sources briefed on the first known meeting between the longtime foes.
The Syrian officials and the Iran-aligned group met secretly at least once last month, the sources - who include two Syrian officials, a US official and a senior Lebanese security source close to Hezbollah - told Reuters.
Hezbollah for years dispatched fighters to Syria to defend former President Bashar al-Assad's government during the country's civil war.
After Assad was ousted in late 2024 in a lightning rebel offensive, tensions rose between Syria's new government and Hezbollah - with Damascus accusing the group of transferring arms through Syria, and the United States encouraging Syria's military to send forces into Lebanon to fight Hezbollah.
The six sources said Hezbollah representatives and Syrian intelligence and foreign ministry officials had taken part in the meeting last month at the invitation of Turkish security and intelligence agencies in an effort to de-escalate.
All the sources spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the meeting.
Syria's foreign ministry, Turkey's foreign and defense ministries and the US State Department did not immediately respond to Reuters' questions about the meeting. Hezbollah's media office declined to comment.
After publication, the Syrian government's English-language account on X denied such a meeting had taken place, saying "these claims are false."
The meeting focused on resolving points of tension between the two parties and went well, according to the US official, the Syrian officials and the Lebanese source.

title: Houthis attacked power station in Medina
description: Houthis attacked power station in Medina
content:
Saudi-led coalition says attack part of attempts to target Two Holy Mosques
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Thursday the terrorist group had attacked a power distribution station in the holy city of Medina this week, putting one transformer out of service but without affecting the electricity network.
The coalition said an investigation and examination of drone wreckage confirmed Houthi involvement in planning and carrying out Tuesday's attack. It said the station supplies electricity to the Prophet's Mosque, one of Islam's holiest sites.
A Houthi military source, quoted by the Houthi-run Saba news agency, denied the accusation, calling it a "lie" and saying it was intended to cover up what he described as Saudi Arabia's failure to substantiate its earlier accusation that the Houthis targeted the Muslim holy city of Mecca.
Saudi Arabia said two weeks ago it had intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone south of Mecca before it entered restricted airspace over the city. The coalition described that incident as the second Houthi attempt to target Mecca since 2017, while the Houthis denied targeting Mecca or any other Islamic holy site.
The coalition said the Medina attack was part of what it described as repeated Houthi attempts to target the Two Holy Mosques and "provoke" Muslims worldwide. It said it would continue taking measures to protect the holy sites and pilgrims.
The latest escalation is the most serious fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned Houthis since a UN-brokered truce largely halted cross-border attacks in 2022. Hostilities resumed this year after the Houthis declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in July and began attacking Saudi territory and shipping, while Houthi forces also made major territorial gains along Yemen's Red Sea coast.
Saudi Arabia has responded with airstrikes in Yemen and backed government forces fighting to push back the Houthis.

content:

President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday the world was living through a dangerous moment and warned the West not to escalate a standoff over Ukraine by threatening the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, which Moscow has made clear it would defend with nuclear weapons if necessary.
Locked in a war in Ukraine which he said Russia had no choice but to launch in order to safeguard its own security, Putin said Russia had no plans to attack any European country and wanted to coexist peacefully.

"If it comes to a direct attack on the Russian Federation – in this case, we are referring to Kaliningrad, and perhaps other territories as well – the question of the Russian Federation deploying all the weapons at our country's disposal will, of course, inevitably and immediately be on the agenda," Putin told the Valdai Forum of international Russia experts in Moscow.

"And we will have to make use of our competitive advantages in this struggle. Yes, of course, France and Britain are nuclear powers – we understand that perfectly well and are fully aware of it," he said. "But no one else possesses the kind of weapons that Russia has today. title: FCC puts CJ in charge of bench formation
description: Rules also provide that a larger bench shall comprise as many judges as the chief justice may determine by order
content:
Rules also provide that a larger bench shall comprise as many judges as the chief justice may determine by order
Unlike the Supreme Court, the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) will have no three-judge seniority committee to oversee the constitution of benches as its newly notified practice and procedure rules vest the authority in the chief justice.
The Federal Constitutional Court (Practice and Procedure Rules) 2026, now notified and available on the court's website, designate the chief justice as the 'master of roster', giving him discretion to constitute benches for hearing cases before the newly established constitutional court.
Under the newly notified rules, notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, every cause, matter or appeal, including an appeal arising out of a judgment passed by a division bench of a high court, shall be heard and disposed of by a bench consisting of not less than two judges, to be nominated by the chief justice.
"If the Judges hearing any cause, petition or appeal are equally divided in opinion, the matter shall, at the discretion of the Chief Justice, be placed for hearing and disposal either before another Judge in Chamber or before a larger Bench to be nominated by the Chief Justice."
The rules further state that the chief justice may, at any stage, if deemed appropriate, constitute a larger bench to hear any cause, petition, or appeal, having regard to the importance, complexity, or public significance of the questions involved.
The rules also provide that a larger bench shall comprise as many judges as the chief justice may determine by order.
Taken together, the provisions make clear that the 'master of roster' system has been retained in the FCC, leaving the chief justice with discretionary powers over the constitution of benches.
Since the restoration of the judiciary in March 2009, Supreme Court chief justices have faced considerable criticism over the formation of what were described as 'like-minded' benches.
During former chief justice Umar Ata Bandial's tenure, the PDM government led by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif enacted the Supreme Court Practice and Procedure Act 2023, under which a three-member committee headed by the chief justice was tasked with constituting benches.
A full court headed by former chief justice Qazi Faez Isa subsequently upheld the SC Practice and Procedure Act 2023.
A majority of judges, including incumbent FCC Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan and Justice Hasan Azhar Rizvi, had strongly supported the three-judge committee for constituting benches.
Even following the 26th Constitutional Amendment, the three-judge committee was retained for the formation of constitutional benches.
The committee remains in place in the Supreme Court.
Following the 27th Constitutional Amendment, jurisdiction relating to the enforcement of fundamental rights and the interpretation of laws and the Constitution was assigned to the newly established FCC.
Lawyers therefore argue that, with these significant responsibilities now vested in the FCC, there is a need for checks on the chief justice's discretionary powers in order to ensure greater transparency within the institution.
"Once you have torn the heart out of an independent court; the replacement you prop up must function with precision and efficiency. It must be a disciplined unit, akin to a military camp. Any democracy within can only lead to weakness," says lawyer Abdul Moiz Jaferii.
Jaferii believes that the chief must have complete control. And so we are back again to the master of the roster. Unacceptable when the chief was heading an independent court. Completely necessary when you have the FCC", he adds.
FCC judges are already facing what some lawyers call a "battle of perception", particularly because they were appointed by the federal government, which is expected to be the primary litigant before the court in several politically sensitive matters.
It has also been witnessed that the FCC has entertained some important cases against PTI.
For instance, it has sought the record of the case related to Imran Khan's health from the Supreme Court. The FCC also issued notices to respondents on a petition against the de-seating of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi.
The court has also sought a reply from the K-P chief minister over his statement regarding the formation of the Imran Khan 'Rahae Force'.
Likewise, the FCC restrained the Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) Peshawar from entertaining a K-P government petition seeking withdrawal of cases against PTI leaders, including K-P CM Afridi.
Interestingly, the government has allocated Rs6.048 billion for the FCC in the 2026-27 budget. Despite the passage of ten months, seven judicial seats in the FCC are still vacant.
More than 23,000 cases are pending in the country's apex court.

title: US death row inmate survives execution
description: US death row inmate survives execution
content:
Christa Pike, convicted of murdering a schoolmate three decades ago, survived Tennessee's effort to execute her by means of lethal injection late on Wednesday, prison officials said, foiling the state's first attempt to put a woman to death in two centuries.
Pike's condition following the ordeal was not immediately known, and it was not clear what legal avenues her lawyers or the state might pursue next after she was taken for medical treatment from the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville.
The Tennessee Department of Correction defended its handling of the high-profile execution, which had been opposed by her lawyers and human rights experts due to Pike's age at the time of the crime, her history as the victim of childhood sexual abuse, and untreated mental illness.
"The Tennessee Department of Correction followed every step of the state's lawful, established execution protocol approved by the Attorney General's Office," the agency said in a statement.
"The lethal injection chemical in the protocol has consistently been effective, and the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out this evening. Christa Pike has been transported to an off-site medical facility," the statement concluded.
Pike's lawyers filed a federal court motion during the process seeking to halt her execution, citing witnesses' accounts that "executioners had injected both syringes of lethal injection chemicals and Pike is still alive and snoring," NBC News reported.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee, who denied Pike's clemency petition on Monday, issued a statement after the botched execution, suspending all executions this year and calling for a "comprehensive, third-party review" of Pike's execution attempt, according to the Nashville Tennessean.
The failed execution is the second in Tennessee this year, after prison officials in May aborted attempts to execute a man convicted of murders after failing to find a suitable vein for his lethal injection.
The botched attempt on Wednesday came hours after the US Supreme Court lifted an 11th-hour lower-court stay of the execution, clearing the way for Pike, 50, to be put to death for her role in the 1995 torture and beating death of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in Knoxville.
Pike was 18 in January 1995 when she, 17-year-old boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp and a third companion lured Slemmer, a classmate at their Knoxville Job Corps vocational center, into a wooded area where they tortured and killed her.
The grisly nature of the slaying, which involved the perpetrators carving the shape of a pentagram in the victim's chest and taking a chunk of her skull as a souvenir of the carnage, drew intense media coverage at the time.
Pike and Shipp confessed to the killing, and both were convicted of first-degree murder.
Journalists who witnessed the attempted execution described snoring, loud exhales, gasps, and complaints from Pike about discomfort in her arm. At times, the curtain was closed, and journalists could only hear sounds.
Clergy were called into the chamber twice, they said, before an ambulance was seen arriving at the prison and then leaving.
Aside from being the first woman the state of Tennessee has tried to execute in more than 200 years, Pike was also poised to became the only person in the modern era of US capital punishment to be executed in Tennessee for a crime committed as a teenager.
