title: Dead  SSG man  resurrects  to expose India s lie
description: Dead  SSG man  resurrects  to expose India s lie
content:
DG ISPR rejects Indian military claims; Asif says reports falsely declared him dead
Director General Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry on Thursday rejected Indian claims that a former Pakistan Army soldier had been killed as a Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorist in the Indian Illegally-Occupied Kashmir (IIOJK), presenting the individual alive before the media and describing the episode as another Indian "false flag operation".
"So-called terrorist incident, another false flag that has been staged by the Indian military. I will take you step by step through the details," Chaudhry said during a press briefing.
He said that he was there to talk about a claim made by the Indian military of an anti-terror operation conducted on Sept 29 inside IIOJK.
The military spokesperson said that the false flag started on the night of Sept 29, when the corps of the Indian military in IIOJK made a social media post saying that "based on specific intelligence input, a joint search operation was launched by the Indian army, Jammu Kashmir police and CRPF Srinagar in the general area Korag, Yousmarg. Vigilant troops observed suspicious activity, and upon being challenged, terrorists opened fire, prompting a fierce exchange of gunfire during which one terrorist was neutralised".
Chaudhry said that after seven hours, the Indian military gave an update yesterday morning, saying that a "body of a Pakistan-based LeT terrorist was recovered in a search operation", further claiming that he had been identified as Mohammad Asif alias Hashim Moosa.
The news conference came after Indian media claimed that Asif, also known as Hashim Moosa, was killed in an operation in IIOJK and had previously served in the Pakistan Army. According to the reports that emerged in Indian media, Asif was born on March 7, 1980, joined the Pakistan Army in 2000 under service number PA-3106947 and retired with the rank of Havildar. Indian media further claimed that he was inducted into the Special Services Group (SSG) in 2005 and served with the 4 Commando "Yalgar" Battalion.
The reports alleged that Asif was deployed in Balochistan from 2006, where he took part in around 10 operations against Baloch insurgents and was credited with 13 "personal kills". They also claimed that he served on former president Pervez Musharraf's VVIP security team between 2006 and 2009.
The DG ISPR stated that the Indian newspaper ANI reported further details about "Asif", including his joining date, his service number, details of his retirement, his photo, and further claimed that he was a former Hawaldar of the SSG branch of the Pakistan military. "A very interesting story is getting cooked, and you have a face as well. You might recall the false flags of Uri, Pahalgam and Pulwama."
He further stated that the Indian government then claimed through the Home Affairs and Press Information Bureau that the Indian Army had neutralised a LeT "commander", who was later identified as "Musa aka Asif Fauji", through an intelligence-led operation.
"According to the Indian government, this was a serious blow to the LeT ecosystem, and Asif had been operating in Jammu and Kashmir since 2022 and was involved in sensational attacks. Asif was neutralised after six months of a sustained operation," he added.
The military spokesperson said that the "so-called credible Indian media" jumped onto the bandwagon, repeating the claims of the Indian government of killing a Pakistani SSG officer during an Indian military operation.
"Now that the Indian military has claimed that Musa is an ex-Hawaldar of the SSG, the question becomes: where is Musa?" he remarked before presenting Asif to the audience.
"Here is that superman gentleman; you can see this superman. Please tell us about your activities. I would request my dear friend Hawaldar Asif to tell something about himself".
Asif stated that he had been receiving calls since yesterday from Indian numbers inquiring about him, further adding that he had seen social media commentary about his "killing" in an Indian military operation. "I was sitting at home when I heard these false reports from the Indian media. This is a heinous allegation from the Indian media, and my presence here shows that I am alive".
"I was inducted in 2000 in the Pakistan Army and joined the SSG in 2005 and served for 18 years and retired from service in 2023," Asif stated.
"What was the need for this drama from India? There are six reasons for this, and it is important to understand why Indians keep on repeating this drama. It is a very shameful and embarrassing thing that no self-respecting nation does," DG ISPR stated.
Chaudhry said that the first reason for these repeated Indian accusations was to "cover its own track of terrorism", adding that India was the biggest terrorist state in the world and its involvement in terrorism in the region went back decades through funding and sponsorship of terror outfits.
"They think that every problem can be rectified and addressed through terrorism. They are terrorising Muslims, Sikhs, Kashmiris, Dalits, tribals and Christians inside India. Such a country that lives and breathes in terrorism is afraid that its dark face will be exposed. What better way to cover your tracks than to call everyone else a terrorist? That is why you see these false, concocted stories coming out of India. This list of false flag events goes back decades, and they have been feeding these lies to their own people and to the world at large," he remarked.
The DG ISPR further stated: "We need to understand that this habit of false flag operations has further encouraged India to even go for transnational killings; you must have seen how they are doing targeted killings far beyond their borders, and the world has seen that. You then need to cover your tracks because they see their own face in the mirror. They are proud of their terrorism."
DG Chaudhry noted that those guilty of perpetrating terrorism internationally could easily concoct stories to accuse Pakistan.
"A normal human cannot comprehend the basis for this drama," he said, assailing the new false flag operation by India. He said such concocted stories appealed to the Indians to create relevance for Indian oppression in IIOJK.
"IIOJK is the biggest garrison in the world, for every 10th Kashmiri, there is a soldier or security official deployed by the Indian Army," he highlighted, adding that nearly a million guard IIOJK.
"Hawaldar Asif does not have to go across the border to instigate Kashmiris," he said, explaining that Indian oppression of Kashmiris and refuting their right to self-determination caused the reaction of Kashmiris that India tries to pin on Pakistan.
"If you wish for a fight, engage with us like you did in Marka-e-Haq and let us teach you a lesson," DG Chaudhry warned.
He lamented that India was obsessed with Pakistan, built lies surrounding it and came up with theatrics matching Bollywood.
The DG ISPR said if the Indians wished to pursue a fresh conflict, "they are most welcome, but this time we will not leave them so easily.
"This time the cost that Pakistan will inflict on their strategic folly will be very, very severe."
Talking about the Makkah agreement, he said the matter of troop deployment to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia was a "confidential matter".
He noted that the operationalisation of the defensive actions under the Makkah alliance was a matter of "operational necessity and confidentiality", adding that it was not a matter for media discourse. "There should be complete clarity that Pakistan's commitment to Saudi Arabia security and sanctity is absolute".
While answering a question on cross-border terrorism emanating from Afghanistan, the DG ISPR noted that as per the Constitution, the army worked under the federal government and therefore it was the task of the federal government to coordinate with the provincial government, further adding that there would be no compromise on "Pakistan's territorial integrity and sovereignty" and everything necessary would be done to secure it.
Responding to another question on India's standing in the world, he stated that "the Indian façade is very well exposed to the whole world. You are hearing from the Canadian prime minister and the US secretary of state talking about Indian terrorism. The façade of Shining India has been exposed."
Answering a question on operations against the Afghan Taliban, DG Chaudhry noted that the Afghan Taliban had made their choice of "abetting and sponsoring terrorism".
He further asked representatives of international media outlets to probe the Afghan government on why there were Afghans involved in acts of terrorism inside Pakistan and what Afghanistan was doing about it, further adding that Pakistan has nothing against the people of Afghanistan.
"The problem is with the Afghan Taliban regime that has forced itself on the country; it is non-inclusive, non-representative, unelected, and because it's a forced regime, such regimes need insecurity and oppression to thrive. For that, they have gathered the whole alphabetic soup of terrorist organisations from ISKP to ETIM. Pakistan, as the frontline state, is fighting these groups."
When asked a question on the PTI's planned long march, he stated that the "army has nothing to do with politics and we will not answer anything related to politics. Politics is for the political parties and the government".
He suggested adhering to the devised National Action Plan for the elimination of terrorism.
"State supersedes politics; the state supersedes democracy too," the DG ISPR emphasised.

title: Pakistan hits Afghan terror hideouts  22 killed
description: Pakistan hits Afghan terror hideouts  22 killed
content:
Warns patience wearing thin, keeps diplomacy open
Pakistan on Thursday carried out fresh aerial and drone strikes against terrorist hideouts inside Afghanistan, killing 22 terrorists, as Islamabad warned that its patience over attacks emanating from Afghan territory was wearing thin and that military action would continue alongside diplomatic efforts.
The latest strikes were conducted under Operation Ghazab-lil-Haq against what Pakistan described as hideouts and safe havens of Fitna al-Khwarij, Fitna al-Hindustan and their affiliates at two locations in Afghanistan.
According to the Ministry of Information, the targets were selected on the basis of credible intelligence and included terrorist camps and hideouts. Large quantities of weapons and ammunition stored at the sites were also destroyed.
"Maximum precautions were taken and it was ensured that no collateral damage occurs," the ministry said.
The strikes came as the Foreign Office said Afghanistan under the Taliban regime continued to provide safe haven to terrorist organisations blamed for attacks inside Pakistan.
Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan told his weekly briefing that more than 36 terrorist organisations were present in Afghanistan and said Islamabad remained "highly concerned" about the situation.
"We would like to have peace and stability in the region, and we also respect the sovereignty of countries. But taking care of the security and safety of Pakistanis also falls on the shoulders of the Government of Pakistan. So, we will take appropriate action," he said.
Sajjad, however, stressed that Pakistan had not abandoned diplomacy and said the two sides remained in contact through different channels.
He said Islamabad was still prepared for "friendly and cooperative relations" with Kabul but insisted that such relations could only be built on trust, mutual understanding and respect for each other's sovereignty.
"Pakistan's readiness to engage in dialogue should not be considered a sign of weakness," he said, adding that the infiltration and activities of terrorist organisations operating from Afghanistan had to stop.
The latest strikes further underline the sharp deterioration in Pakistan-Afghanistan ties. Islamabad has repeatedly accused the Taliban regime of allowing the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and other groups to operate from Afghan territory, while Kabul has rejected the allegations.
The escalation has come amid a surge in terrorist violence inside Pakistan. An Islamabad based think tank recorded 60 attacks during September 18-24 alone, double the previous week, with 73 people killed and 132 injured.
Pakistan welcomes Indian participation in SCO
Despite the tensions with Afghanistan and continuing friction with India, Islamabad on Thursday struck a notably conciliatory tone on Indian participation in the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.
The Indian national coordinator, Ambassador Alok Dimri, attended the first meeting of the SCO Council of National Coordinators in Islamabad from September 28 to 30, the first senior Indian official to visit Pakistan in more than two years, according to the Foreign Office.
Asked about the Indian official's interaction with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, including his positive comments about his visit, Sajjad described the participation as a welcome development.
"His presence here reflected the commonality of views as well as objectives of the entire region with regard to peace, development, connectivity, trade, and transit," the spokesperson said.
He stressed that the SCO was a multilateral platform and that Pakistan hoped Indian participation would continue throughout its chairmanship.
"This is just the beginning, and we hope that Indian participation will continue in the coming months and throughout the year," he said.
The three-day SCO meeting reviewed Pakistan's priorities for its 2026-27 chairmanship and preparations for upcoming meetings and events. The organisation's programme includes an SCO Hockey Tournament in Islamabad from November 20 to December 2.
Pakistan has sought to use its SCO chairmanship to promote connectivity, economic cooperation, innovation and people-to-people contacts, despite the strained relationship with India.
Meanwhile, the spokesperson said Pakistan remained committed to applicable international sanctions regimes while stressing its "enduring and multifaceted strategic partnership" with the United States.
At the same time, he said Pakistan, as a mediator between Iran and the US, believed dialogue and diplomacy remained the only viable route to resolving their differences.
Pakistan has repeatedly said the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding provides the framework for resolving the US-Iran dispute. The Foreign Office has previously described the agreement as the foundation for subsequent diplomatic efforts between the two sides.

title: Govt  allies strike conciliatory note as PTI firms up march plan

content:
Six-member govt-PPP team to meet PTI today, Achakzai rejects talks at Speaker's Chamber
The government and PPP on Thursday formed a six-member delegation to hold talks with the PTI on Friday (today) as the political temperature rises over the party's planned Oct 4 protest march as the opposition demanded dialogue without conditions and the federal government kept the option of governor's rule or emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on the table.
The decision was taken at a meeting between President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif at Aiwan-e-Sadr, where the two leaders reviewed the country's political and security situation and expressed concern over the situation in K-P.
They also stressed the need to strengthen the national resolve against terrorism and ensure effective coordination among relevant institutions for peace and stability.
PTI Chairperson Barrister Gohar Khan separately confirmed that government and opposition representatives would meet at noon on Friday in the office of National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq.
"PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan received a message from the government yesterday for a meeting, which he has accepted in light of the decisions made in today's opposition meeting. God willing, a meeting will take place between the opposition and government delegations in the office of National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq tomorrow at 12pm," a post on Gohar's X account said.
According to the PPP statement, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Adviser to the PM on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, PPP Senator Sherry Rehman and PPP MNAs Naveed Qamar and Aijaz Jakhrani will represent the government and PPP at the meeting.
From the opposition, Tehreek-e-Tahaffuz Ayeen-e-Pakistan (TTAP) spokesperson Akhundzada Yousafzai confirmed his participation, along with Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas and former senator Mustafa Nawaz Khokhar.
However, National Assembly Opposition Leader and TTAP Chairman Mahmood Khan Achakzai ruled out attending any meeting in the Speaker's Chamber.
The opposition alliance's decision followed a meeting with PTI leaders in the Senate opposition leader's chamber. According to a TTAP statement, the participants discussed the overall political situation, the PTI's planned protest march and other constitutional and parliamentary matters.
The proposed meeting between the government and opposition is being seen as a possible avenue for easing the political crisis, with the Oct 4 march having become the latest major point of confrontation between the PTI and the Centre.
The PTI remains determined to proceed with the march, while federal ministers have warned that the Centre may have no option but to impose governor's rule or emergency in K-P, citing the province's security situation and the PTI's protest call.
The opposition has warned the government of dire consequences if either measure is imposed. The TTAP, headed by Achakzai and also comprising the PTI, has announced that it will join the protest.
'Anywhere but not at PM Office, speaker's chamber'
Following the TTAP-PTI meeting, Achakzai said he was unwilling to hold talks at the Prime Minister's House, the Prime Minister's Office or the Speaker's Chamber.
"The prime minister is illegitimate. The mandate of millions of Pakistanis Harsh words are rising to my lips; that is why I am silent.
"I am ready to sit anywhere in Pakistan, under any tree. I am ready to visit the house of any party [leader]. But I will not go to the speaker house [sic], the Prime Minister's House or the prime minister's chamber," he said while speaking to the media at Parliament House after the opposition leaders' meeting, standing alongside Gohar.
Achakzai was responding to a question about PM's Adviser Rana Sanaullah's invitation to him and PTI Chairperson Barrister Gohar to sit with the prime minister for talks. The reporter asked why the meeting was not taking place.
In a video clip shared by TTAP, Achakzai also said a meeting with the prime minister would take place after a meeting with jailed former premier and PTI founder Imran Khan.
PM Shehbaz had extended an invitation to the NA opposition leader to sit together for consultations on issues of national importance and those related to the PTI before leaving for the US. Earlier, the premier had also invited Achakzai on Sept 11 for mandatory consultations on the appointment of a new chief election commissioner.
Gohar told the media that PTI leaders had held a three-hour meeting with Abbas and Achakzai, during which they exchanged detailed views on the problems facing the country and the prevailing situation, particularly in K-P and preparations for the march.
He condemned the "state oppression and tyranny" inflicted on the PTI and its supporters, as well as the detention and treatment of Imran's sisters in jail.
The PTI chairman claimed that attempts had been made to suppress his party "whenever we raise our voice for our rights and for justice in the country".
Gohar also stressed that the party had "always stood with the state and the country", including during the May 2025 conflict with India.
The leaders also discussed reports of a possible imposition of emergency, Gohar said, warning: "The federation becomes strong when the provinces are strong and autonomous, and when the people's mandate is respected. You will put the federation at risk if you take any action in a province that goes against the will of its people."
He reiterated that the PTI's march would remain peaceful, saying, "This is our country; for us, Pakistan comes first, the state of Pakistan and its peace and security."
Gohar said the way to avoid a long march was not through governor's rule or a state of emergency, but by engaging with protesters, listening to the reasons behind their presence on the streets and addressing their concerns.
"We went to the Supreme Court 19 times, but were not heard. We went to the high court 25 times but its orders were not implemented. A special committee was formed in Parliament, but a meeting was never called Even today, the same concerns persist," he said.
Despite these grievances, Gohar stressed that the PTI remained ready for negotiations and had already made its demands clear.
PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja also maintained that protesting was a constitutional and legal right and that the party would not retreat from its planned protest.
"The leader of the long march is Sohail Afridi; Imran Khan has appointed him. We will support him in every possible way," he added.
'Opposition ready for dialogue but without conditions'
Speaking to the media alongside Achakzai and Gohar after the meeting in his chamber, Senate Opposition Leader Abbas called for reconciliation and dialogue to resolve the political crisis, saying the opposition was prepared for talks but without preconditions.
He also stressed that the PTI protest would remain peaceful even if met with violence, and cautioned against the creation of a "false narrative" around the demonstration.
"I have said before as well that when we leave from there, there will be no weapons in our hands," he said. "We know the value of human life."
Abbas called for reconciliation and dialogue to improve the country's situation.
"We are fully prepared to hold dialogue and correct the situation, but this will be without any conditions. If anyone thinks that they will hold a dagger of conditions at our necks, then, such a thing will never be accepted," he said.
Regarding the planned protest, Abbas said the PTI had "decided to adopt a democratic approach by staging peaceful protests and a long march".
He said the government should have "assured the protesters of the protection of their lives and property, provided them with facilities, and, while recognising the right to peaceful protest, designated the routes".
"But, on the contrary, what did the government do? Even before the protests began, containers were placed to seal Islamabad, roads were dug up and nails were hammered into the routes," he said, claiming that this was the behaviour of "scared people".
Abbas stressed that the Constitution guaranteed the rights of Pakistani citizens and that peaceful protests, sit-ins and long marches were part of democratic politics.
He also criticised the reported arrests of PTI members under the Maintenance of Public Order law, calling it a completely "illegal practice".
On Imran, Abbas said, "The only personality who can take Pakistan out of the current crisis is Imran Khan, whom the people trust."
"He will go to Balochistan, where Akhtar Mengal and other leaders will be with him. He will sit with the people and talk to them and convince them. What you cannot do through the force of bullets can be done through dialogue because the people trust him," he added.
Earlier in the day, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said the federal government and PTI had been engaged in "off-the-record talks" over the party's planned Oct 4 protest.
Sanaullah made the remarks while appearing on a private news channel's show.
He said the decision on the proposed march rested with PTI's senior leadership, "with whom off-the-record consultation is ongoing".
"So let us see, even if they do not postpone it, we have arrangements in place to stop them," Sanaullah warned.
He likened the PTI march to a "provincial government attacking the capital", apparently referring to the PTI-led government in K-P.
"If a political party or a private organisation stages a protest, [ ] but for a government to attack [ ] it cannot be tolerated under any circumstances," he held.
"The law will be enacted in full force, and they (PTI) will be barred from entering Islamabad," he added.
Asked about governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Sanaullah said on Thursday that the option was "on the table".
He said the federal government was also consulting its coalition partners over imposing governor's rule in K-P. The final decision, he added, rested with the federal government and the Senate, and the measure would require Parliament's approval before taking effect.
Sanaullah alleged that the K-P chief minister had not been performing his duties as the province's chief executive.
"For the past two months, he has not done anything, nothing about development or counter-terrorism efforts or for the welfare of people [ ] in fact, all he has done is talk about marching to Islamabad and toppling the federal government.
"They want to take ladders to Islamabad to secure the release of a certain someone," he added.
Sanaullah reiterated that if a province is "engaged in such illegal and unconstitutional activities, then the Centre has the right to declare emergency or governor rule and assume power".

title: Taylor Swift s  Opalite  theory gets a reality check
description: Taylor Swift s  Opalite  theory gets a reality check
content:
Graham Norton laughs off speculation that Swift engineered his guest lineup
Talk-show host Graham Norton has poured cold water on one of the more elaborate theories circulating among Taylor Swift's famously detail-focused fans, after his show sofa appeared in the pop star's 'Opalite' music video.
Norton addressed the speculation at the Royal Television Society conference in London, where he appeared with broadcaster Tina Daheley and discussed the unexpected appearance of his familiar sofa in Swift's video. Norton said seeing the sofa was "really odd" and "made my dreams come true", but he was clearly amused by the theories that followed.
The speculation centred on Swift's appearance on 'The Graham Norton Show' last October, when she was joined on the sofa by Domhnall Gleeson, Greta Lee, Jodie Turner-Smith, Cillian Murphy and Lewis Capaldi. All five later appeared in the 'Opalite' music video, prompting some Swifties to construct a theory that Swift had filmed the video first and then arranged for the same group to appear on Norton's programme.
"The Swifties, they love a conspiracy theory," Norton said, according to Variety. "So there were Swifties who thought we'd filmed the music video first and then orchestrated to get all the people on the sofa."
Daheley offered a much simpler explanation, saying the idea for the video was "literally an idea she came up with while she was on the show". Norton acknowledged that possibility, although he admitted the footage made the theory look surprisingly plausible.
"Yeah, yeah. I don't know, but certainly when you watch the clips, there is a moment when it looks like she's having the idea," he said. He added that it was "kind of amazing to have the show get that kind of recognition".
Gleeson, who features prominently in the video, had previously said during the recording that the concept for 'Opalite' "crash-landed into my imagination" while Swift was on the show.
Released in February, 'Opalite' features Swift and Gleeson as two unlucky singles who eventually find their way to each other after taking part in a dance contest.
The appearance of Norton's sofa and the reunion of the programme's guests gave fans plenty of material for speculation, but Norton's comments suggest there was no elaborate plot behind the coincidence.
The theory arrives as Swift continues to enjoy a high-profile run of recognition. At the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards, she won the award for Best Direction for 'Opalite'. Swift also took home the night's biggest prize, Video of the Year, for 'The Fate of Ophelia', from her 2025 album 'Life of a Showgirl'.
During her acceptance speech, Swift dedicated the award to country music icon Dolly Parton, who died on August 25 at the age of 80 following a brief battle with cancer. Calling Parton "the ultimate showgirl", Swift praised her storytelling and the grace, joy, love and gratitude with which she handled her career.
For Swift, then, the latest chapter combines fan theories, unexpected television connections and another major awards moment - proof that even a talk-show sofa can become part of the Swift universe.

title: Black Doves  return with new dangers
description: Black Doves  return with new dangers
content:
Neve Campbell, Ambika Mod join Keira Knightley and Ben Whishaw in Season 2 of Netflix's darkly comic spy thriller
Netflix's darkly comic spy thriller 'Black Doves' is set to return for a second season on November 5, bringing back Keira Knightley and Ben Whishaw as the unlikely pair at the centre of a dangerous web of espionage, betrayal and revenge.
The new season picks up after the events of the first, leaving Helen and Sam alive but compromised, with unfinished business threatening to pull them deeper into the shadowy world of the Black Doves. Helen continues to pass her nation's secrets to the covert organisation while navigating the increasingly complicated political life of her husband, Wallace, who is preparing to become prime minister.
The stakes rise further when Mrs Reed, Helen's enigmatic handler, becomes caught in a ruthless attempt to undermine her position within the Black Doves. Helen is once again reunited with her closest friend, Sam, a former high-end triggerman whose fortunes have fallen sharply and who now spends his days drinking in Soho bars and taking low-paying jobs.
Together, Helen and Sam set out to uncover the truth as loyalties become weapons and trust begins to fracture. Their investigation takes them back to people and conflicts from their pasts, forcing both to confront difficult decisions and painful sacrifices while trying to protect those they love.
Knightley returns as Helen, with Whishaw reprising his role as Sam. Sarah Lancashire is back as Mrs Reed, while Andrew Buchan returns as Wallace. Kathryn Hunter, Ella Lily Hyland, Gabrielle Creevy, Agnes O'Casey and Molly Chesworth also reprise their respective roles from the first season.
The returning cast will be joined by several new faces. Ambika Mod, known for 'One Day', plays Laila, an acerbic and anarchic Black Doves agent sent to assist Helen. Babou Ceesay plays Mr Conteh, a Black Doves executive whose motives appear questionable, while Sam Riley portrays Patrick, an emissary from a mysterious organisation who offers Sam a possible lifeline.
Neve Campbell joins the cast as Cecile Mason, alongside Sylvia Hoeks as Katia Chernov, Goran Kostic as Alexi Chernov and Samuel Barnett as Jerry.
Joe Barton returns as writer, creator and executive producer, with Julian Farino and Kieron Hawkes directing. Barton said he was excited to return to the world of the series and to bring together its returning cast with new performers.
The second season promises the same combination of espionage, dark humour and personal danger that defined its predecessor, with Helen and Sam drawn further into the organisation they serve and the consequences of their increasingly perilous choices.
'Black Doves' Season 2 will premiere on Netflix on November 5, while the first season remains available to stream on the platform.

title: Is Tilly Norwood really an actor? | The Express Tribune
description:
Is Tilly Norwood 
really an actor?
content:
Joseph Gordon-Levitt challenges the idea of AI performers as Hollywood wrestles with technology and creativity
Actor Joseph Gordon-Levitt has dismissed the idea that AI-generated performer Tilly Norwood should be considered an actor, arguing that artificial intelligence can produce convincing outputs but cannot replace the human creativity behind a performance.
The actor, who also serves as a UN Global Advocate for Human-centric Digital Governance, addressed the debate in a video posted on Instagram, describing Norwood as a "piece of software that's being branded as an actress".
Gordon-Levitt said AI was not a person but an algorithm capable of recombining material created by humans, including films, songs, writing and other content available online. For him, that distinction makes Norwood fundamentally different from a human performer.
He compared the AI creation with an animated character such as Donald Duck, noting that audiences do not credit the fictional character itself with a performance. Instead, recognition goes to the writers, animators, artists and voice actors involved in creating it.
Norwood's creator, Eline Van der Velden, has previously described the creation as "a work of art" rather than an artist. Her earlier suggestion that she wanted Tilly to become the next Scarlett Johansson or Natalie Portman, however, drew criticism from actors including Melissa Barrera and Mara Wilson.
The debate intensified after Norwood appeared for an "audition" on CNN. According to reports, the team behind the AI character spent hours working to produce a single scene, underscoring the technology's current limitations.
Norwood has yet to appear in a released film but is attached to the upcoming comedy-drama 'Misaligned', described as a hybrid production bringing conventional filmmakers together with AI specialists.
The disagreement reflects a wider Hollywood argument over AI, with performers and writers concerned about its impact on jobs, pay and creative ownership.
Yet the industry is far from unanimous in rejecting the technology. Ben Affleck, discussing his upcoming Netflix film 'Animals', said AI was used "for lots of things" during production, describing it as another technological development in filmmaking.

title: Paramount clears final hurdle for Warner takeover
description: Paramount clears final hurdle for Warner takeover
content:
Court-approved settlement opens way for a $110b Hollywood deal
Paramount's $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery cleared its final major legal hurdle on Wednesday after a US judge approved a settlement with 12 states, paving the way for one of the biggest media mergers in Hollywood history and bringing two major entertainment empires under one roof.
US District Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin approved the September 21 agreement between Paramount and a California-led coalition of states that had sued to block the transaction on antitrust grounds. The states had argued that combining the companies could reduce competition in film and television and give the enlarged company greater power over prices and consumer choice.
The settlement imposes a series of commitments on Paramount for five years, including requirements covering film production, theatrical releases, cable negotiations and the editorial independence of news organisations. The judge described the agreement as a reasonable legal and factual resolution, rejecting arguments from opponents who wanted stronger conditions.
The deal will bring together two of Hollywood's remaining major film studios, Paramount Pictures and Warner Bros., while also combining streaming platforms Paramount+ and HBO Max and television and news assets including CBS and CNN. The enlarged company will also inherit vast libraries of films and television programmes, ranging from 'Top Gun' to 'Harry Potter'.
Under the settlement, the combined company must release at least 30 films annually in US cinemas during the first two years and 32 films annually during the following three years. It must also spend an additional $300 million a year on US film production, amounting to $1.5 billion over five years. Failure to meet the release commitments could ultimately trigger the sale of Miramax.
Paramount will also establish a $47.5 million fund over five years to support training and career development for workers displaced by the merger. The company has previously said it expects to pursue about $6 billion in savings through the combination, including reductions in overlapping operations, raising concerns among industry workers about potential job losses.
The settlement also addresses the company's television operations. Paramount will be required to negotiate separately with cable providers over basic channels belonging to Paramount and Warner Bros. for five years. The provision is intended to prevent the enlarged company from using its expanded portfolio to gain greater leverage in negotiations.
Perhaps the most closely watched condition concerns news. Paramount has agreed to establish a News Editorial Independence Board to oversee operations at CBS News and CNN. The five-member board is to consist of active or retired journalists with at least 10 years of experience, with members appointed by the combined company's board.
The question of CNN's independence has carried particular political sensitivity because Paramount is controlled by David Ellison, whose father, Oracle founder Larry Ellison, is a major backer of the transaction. The Trump administration's relationship with CNN has also drawn attention after the White House barred CNN, Politico and MS NOW from access, a decision the outlets successfully challenged in court.
The Paramount-Warner deal itself has received scrutiny from across the political and entertainment spectrum. Twelve states initially sought to stop the acquisition, while the Writers Guild of America separately challenged it, arguing that greater consolidation could harm writers and the wider industry. The WGA ultimately settled its case, while maintaining that it believed the merger could damage writers.
Opponents of the settlement had urged the court to impose stronger safeguards or reject the agreement altogether. Some critics argued that the conditions did not go far enough to address the concentration of power created by the merger. The judge, however, said such demands did not establish legal grounds for rejecting a negotiated settlement.
Paramount has said the transaction is expected to close on October 6. The company also announced a significant change to its leadership structure, naming Mattel chief executive Ynon Kreiz as co-CEO alongside David Ellison once the acquisition is completed. Kreiz will join Paramount on October 5 and oversee day-to-day operations and integration of the combined businesses.
Kreiz brings experience in expanding entertainment businesses beyond their traditional boundaries. During his tenure at Mattel, he helped develop the company's intellectual property into films, television and digital games, most notably through the global success of 'Barbie'. His appointment gives Ellison a partner with experience in managing large-scale operations as Paramount prepares to integrate Warner Bros. Discovery.
The transaction is expected to reshape an industry already undergoing rapid change as traditional studios struggle with streaming economics, shifting cinema audiences and rising production costs. For Paramount, the acquisition offers a much larger catalogue, stronger streaming assets and a broader international footprint; for Hollywood, it marks another significant concentration of power among a shrinking number of major media companies.
With the court's approval now secured, the months of legal uncertainty surrounding the takeover are effectively over. What follows will be the far more complicated task of combining studios, streaming platforms, television networks and newsrooms while meeting the conditions imposed by the settlement - and proving that the newly created media giant can deliver on its promises.

title: A pause from the spotlight
description: A pause from the spotlight
content:
Ahad Raza Mir plans to step away from showbiz next year
Actor Ahad Raza Mir has surprised fans by announcing plans to take a break from showbiz in 2027, saying he intends to step away from professional commitments, spend time with his family and disappear from social media during the planned hiatus.
A video from the actor's recent live session has been circulating on social media, in which he spoke about his decision and said he wanted to inform fans well in advance about his absence. "I am taking off next year. I thought to inform you guys in time so that you all should just be ready and prepared about my decision."
Mir told his followers that he planned to completely withdraw from his professional life during the break, including stepping away from Instagram. "I am going on a break, disappearing completely, spending time with my family, and Instagram will be off," he said, describing his decision as "sort of a semi-retirement."
The announcement has generated considerable discussion among fans, with social media users speculating about the reasons behind his planned hiatus. Some suggested he could be preparing for marriage, while others viewed it simply as a much-needed break after a busy period of work.
Mir has not confirmed any of the speculation and has offered no further details about the reasons for his decision. His comments, however, indicate that the break is intended to be temporary rather than a permanent departure from acting.
The actor has appeared in popular dramas including 'Yakeen Ka Safar', 'Ahd-e-Wafa', 'Yeh Dil Mera', 'Mere Humsafar' and 'Hum Tum'. He also starred in the 2018 film 'Parwaaz Hai Junoon' and portrayed Hamlet in the theatre production 'Hamlet: A Ghost Story' in Calgary, Canada, in 2019.
Mir also appeared in Netflix's 'Resident Evil' last year. More recently, he played Haroon Malik in Green TV's 'Ek Mohabbat Aur' and is currently working on 'Kaif-e-Firaq' alongside Yumna Zaidi.

title: Making a business out of joy
description: Making a business out of joy
content:
Young entrepreneurs turn weddings, birthdays and family gatherings into creative opportunities
From grand wedding ceremonies and glittering bridal showers to lively birthdays and intimate farewells, the desire to celebrate in style is fuelling a new race among young entrepreneurs to turn every occasion into a memorable event.
Event management, once largely associated with a handful of established and expensive companies, is increasingly attracting young men and women who are entering the field with creative ideas, flexible packages and services designed for different budgets.
Event managers say the growing appetite for professionally organised gatherings has changed the way people approach celebrations. Customers are no longer interested only in booking a hall; many now want complete arrangements covering decor, lighting, catering, photography, seating and entertainment.
"People want their events to look different and memorable. Even a small gathering is now planned with attention to decoration, theme and presentation," an event manager told APP.
The wedding season remains one of the busiest periods for the industry, with banquets, marquees, hotels and restaurants witnessing increased activity as families prepare for wedding ceremonies, receptions, mehndi functions and related gatherings.
Hotel owners say demand is no longer confined to weddings. "Bookings now come for birthdays, bridal showers, baby showers, farewell parties, corporate dinners and other family gatherings as well," said hotel manager Bilal Abbasi.
He said customers were increasingly interested in personalised arrangements, particularly decor and seating plans that could give even a modest event a distinctive appearance.
The changing trend has created opportunities for young entrepreneurs who can enter the business without the large investments traditionally required by established event companies. Many now operate through social media, using digital platforms to showcase their work and reach potential clients.
Event planner Sana Ahmed said digital platforms had changed the way people searched for event services. "Clients can now explore different ideas online, compare designs and discuss packages before making a decision," she said.
"This has created opportunities for smaller businesses as well," Ahmed said, adding that growing competition was also making professionally arranged celebrations accessible to families with different spending capacities.
Young entrepreneurs are responding with economical packages ranging from basic decoration to photography. The availability of smaller packages is also encouraging families to consider cafes, restaurants and compact event spaces for gatherings previously held mainly at home.
The expanding industry is benefiting a wider network of service providers. Decorators, florists, photographers, caterers, makeup artists, musicians, sound technicians and furniture rental businesses are all finding opportunities through the growing number of celebrations.
As competition grows, event managers are also under pressure to offer something distinctive. Customers increasingly arrive with photographs and videos of elaborate celebrations seen on social media and ask planners to create similar settings within limited budgets.
Irsalan, an event manager in Islamabad, said celebrations could be tailored to different budgets, with décor packages starting from around Rs100,000 and going up to Rs500,000 or more, depending on the scale, design and requirements of the function.
He said hall, food and lighting charges varied according to the number of guests and services selected. For clients seeking a traditional atmosphere, organisers also arrange Qawwali and Sufi music programmes, adding a cultural and vibrant touch to weddings and other celebrations.
For many young entrepreneurs, the business is more than simply arranging parties. It offers an opportunity to turn creativity, design, photography, hospitality and digital marketing skills into a profession. As cities enter another busy season of weddings and celebrations, colourful lights will continue to illuminate venues while young entrepreneurs work behind the scenes to transform ordinary spaces into memorable settings.

title: When machines learn music  musicians pay the price
description: When machines learn music  musicians pay the price
content:
Artists fear shrinking work as artificial intelligence takes on instruments, production and mastering
Artificial intelligence has quietly redrawn the boundaries of creativity, entering fields once considered the preserve of human talent and imagination. From writing and photography to graphic design, video production and music, tasks requiring years of skill can now be completed within minutes.
For Pakistan's musicians, however, the transformation is more than a technological shift. Work that once required live instrumentalists, studio time and teams of professionals is increasingly being done through AI, often at a fraction of the cost, threatening livelihoods built over years.
Renowned flutist Salman Adil says AI has already produced 'Pasoori' in the voice of Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, despite the legendary singer never having performed the song. Musicians once believed instruments such as the tabla, flute and sitar would be difficult for AI to reproduce, but that assumption has changed.
Instead of physically playing an instrument, Salman explains, AI learns from existing music and uses those elements to create something new. For musicians whose income depends entirely on recording work, that development is increasingly becoming a source of concern.
Salman recalls a regular client who used to pay him Rs5,000 to Rs10,000 for each flute track but eventually stopped hiring him. When he asked why, the client said they had shifted to AI, where a subscription costing around Rs5,000 provided music, including flute parts, for several songs.
Renowned tabla artist Qamar Babar describes a similar experience. "We are people who play live music and live instruments, but because of AI our opportunities have become very limited," he says, recalling a time when musicians were regularly called for recording sessions.
"Where a live musician was needed before, people now try to get the work done through AI," Babar says. He believes the entire recording chain has been affected, even though he acknowledges that artificial intelligence has made many musical tasks easier.
For live musicians, he says, the change has been deeply damaging. "We are genuinely worried about where things will go and how much work will remain for people like us. Right now it is difficult to understand how our work will move forward with AI."
Music producer and composer Jibran Rafiq explains why AI has gained such rapid acceptance. Most singers in Pakistan do not have large production budgets, he says, making a cheaper and faster alternative particularly attractive.
Previously, producing a song meant hiring musicians, booking a studio and paying a producer and other professionals. In Saraiki music, for instance, a basic production costs around Rs25,000 to Rs30,000, although Jibran says its distinct style has not yet been fully replicated by AI.
For musicians, the decline in recording opportunities is already apparent. "Some musicians used to record two to four songs in a day. Now that has come down to two, three or four songs a week," Jibran says, adding that the reduction directly affects their income.
Studios, too, are feeling the impact as people who once paid separately for mixing and proper mastering increasingly turn to AI-based mastering. Jibran says many singers do not fully know what good mastering sounds like and therefore accept whatever AI produces.
He warns that the immediate savings could eventually affect artists' creative skills, musicians' livelihoods and the wider music market. Yet he and Salman both see signs that listeners may eventually seek human musicians again as the novelty of AI-generated music begins to fade.
Jibran says much of the AI-produced music began to sound alike, causing people to become bored. Platforms are also responding to AI-generated content in different ways. "This was a trend that came very fast, but now its graph is coming down," he says.
Salman believes AI cannot reproduce the experience of live music, where people sit together and develop a deep and soulful connection with what is being performed. He recently heard an AI-generated qawwali that he found highly artificial and far removed from the original.
In another case, a client who had used AI for a flute part eventually sent it to Salman and asked him to replay it with a human feel. Matching the machine's precision was difficult, he says, but the client preferred the human performance.
The shift has created another burden for musicians: proving that their work is genuinely theirs. Music director Akash Sonu visited Salman's studio to film a flute recording so he could show his own client that the part had been performed by a human rather than generated by AI.
Salman believes artists may increasingly have to prove that their work is authentic. For musicians who depend entirely on recording opportunities, the question is no longer simply whether AI can make music, but whether the market will continue to value the human skill behind it.
He sums up the dilemma in a single line: "AI is killing skill, but there is no substitute for the human vibe." Until that human quality is valued again in the market, musicians whose livelihoods depend on recording work remain uncertain about what comes next.

title: Saudi Arabia denies reports of suicide bomber at Grand Mosque in Makkah
description: Saudi led coalition says Houthis attacked Madinah power distribution station supplying electricity to Prophet s Mosque
content:
Saudi-led coalition says Houthis attacked Madinah power distribution station supplying electricity to Prophet's Mosque
Saudi authorities on Friday denied reports of a suicide bomber at the Grand Mosque in Makkah, saying a man was arrested for harassing passersby and causing panic.
“Security authorities in the holy capital arrested a person for harassing passersby and spreading fear and panic among them, and he was dealt with immediately,” authorities said in a statement on the US social media platform X.
الجهات الأمنية في العاصمة المقدسة تقبض على شخص لمضايقته المارة وإثارة الهلع والفزع بينهم، وتم التعامل معه في حينه بشكل فوري. pic.twitter.com/cNNGjLghk8
“The security authorities confirm that there is no truth to the claims being circulated regarding the incident,” the statement said. The statement provided no further details about the suspect.
Earlier claims circulating on social media alleged that a suspected suicide bomber wearing an explosive vest had approached the Kaaba, a cube-shaped stone building located at the centre of the Grand Mosque that serves as Islam's holiest sanctuary, before being apprehended by security personnel.
Houthis attack Madina power distribution system, Saudi-led coalition says
On Thursday, the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said that the group had attacked a power distribution station in Madinah which supplies electricity to the Prophet's Mosque, one of Islam's holiest sites.
The coalition said the attack put one transformer out of service but did not affect the power network. A Houthi military source, quoted by the Houthi-run Saba News Agency , denied the coalition report.
The Houthis later reported Saudi strikes on the Yemeni capital Sanaa and other parts of Yemen, with no immediate Saudi confirmation of the strikes.
A spokesperson for Yemen's armed forces, which are aligned with the internationally recognised government, said coalition forces had attacked what it described as "high-value targets" in the capital Sanaa, without providing further details.
The recent escalation is the most serious fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis since a United Nations-brokered truce largely halted cross-border attacks in 2022. Hostilities resumed this year after the Houthis declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in July and began attacking Saudi territory and shipping, while Houthi forces also made major territorial gains along Yemen's Red Sea coast.
Read: Saudi Arabia reports fresh Houthi attacks, issues warning for Makkah
Saudi Arabia has responded with air strikes in Yemen and backed government forces fighting to repel the Houthis.
The Saudi-led coalition said an investigation and examination of drone wreckage confirmed Houthi involvement in planning and carrying out Tuesday's attack on the Madinah power station. A Houthi military source said the coalition claim was a "lie" intended to cover up what he described as Saudi Arabia's failure to substantiate its earlier accusation that the Houthis targeted the Muslim holy city of Makkah, said the Saba News Agency .
Saudi Arabia said two weeks ago it had intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone south of Makkah before it entered restricted airspace over the city. The coalition described the incident as the second Houthi attempt to target Makkah since 2017, while the Houthis denied targeting Makkah or any other Islamic holy site.
The coalition said the Madinah attack was part of what it described as repeated Houthi attempts to target the Two Holy Mosques and "provoke" Muslims worldwide. It said it would continue taking measures to protect the holy sites and pilgrims.
The coalition also said it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis toward the southern Saudi city of Khamis Mushait. It gave no immediate details on any damage or casualties.
Local officials said early on Friday that the Houthis had also targeted the headquarters of the Saudi-led coalition forces command in Aden with several ballistic missiles and drones. There was no immediate comment from the coalition or the Houthis.

title: Range extended EVs can save  1b
description: Range extended EVs can save  1b
content:
150,000 REEVs will displace 1.2b litres of petrol over 5 years
Pakistan could save more than $1 billion in gross fuel imports by adding 30,000 range-extended electric vehicles (REEVs) annually for five years, according to industry analysts. The scenario envisages a fleet reaching 150,000 vehicles, cumulatively displacing 1.2 billion litres of petrol and avoiding around 2.7 million tonnes of operational carbon emissions compared with similar petrol vehicles. Outcomes would depend on mileage, charging sources and electric operation.
The broader economic case is supported by the "Future on Wheels", a December 2024 policy viewpoint published by the Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE), authored by Dr Usman Qadir, Mohammad Shaaf Najib and Saddam Hussein.
"With petroleum imports consuming 30% of Pakistan's total import bill, the transition to EVs is a macroeconomic imperative. Accelerating EV adoption directly mitigates this fiscal vulnerability, shielding the current account balance from volatile foreign exchange drains caused by global oil shocks," stated the quotation attributed to Qadir and Najib.
Industry insiders say REEVs offer a practical transition while Pakistan's charging network develops. An electric motor drives the wheels, while an onboard fuel-powered generator supplies electricity when the battery requires support. Modern models can cover roughly 150-180 kilometres on battery power in suitable conditions. Home charging can therefore meet many daily travel needs, while the generator provides additional range for longer journeys.

title: PSX loses 1 332 points amid selling pressure

content:
Oil surge, inflation and US-Iran uncertainty impact market outlook
Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) reversed early gains on Thursday as rising oil prices and inflationary concerns weighed on investor sentiment, while uncertainty about any breakthrough in US-Iran diplomatic efforts added to the cautious mood.
The benchmark KSE-100 Index fell 1,332.47 points, or 0.78%, to settle at 168,636.85. During the session, it touched the intra-day high of 170,688.38 and low of 168,567.79. Meanwhile, crude prices rose around 2% after China suspended oil product exports, tightening global fuel markets already facing supply constraints, whereas investors continued to assess diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war.
On the domestic front, Pakistan's inflation slowed to 10.26% in September from 11.1% in August, primarily led by lower food prices, but remained above the State Bank's medium-term target range. The market had opened on a positive note, with the KSE-100 reaching 170,270.16, up 300.84 points, or 0.18%, at 10:15 am before losing ground.
Muhammad Awais Ashraf of AKD Securities assessed that easing inflationary pressures amid a strong external account position, along with a reduction in domestic political noise, would strengthen investor confidence. Any positive development on the US-Iran war will serve as a key trigger, while the normalisation of trade flows from GCC will reduce the severity of the ongoing crisis. "We advise investors to focus on banks, E&P, fertiliser, textile, OMCs, technology, steel and automobile sectors. Within these, E&Ps and OMCs are positioned to benefit from resolution of the gas-sector circular debt," Ashraf wrote.
"Investor sentiment remained subdued as participants adopted a cautious approach amid heightened geopolitical tensions, which also led to a sharp rise in crude oil prices," JS Global analyst Nawaz Ali commented. Meanwhile, the fragile domestic political situation further weighed on market sentiment and kept investors on the sidelines. "Going forward, trading activity is expected to remain subdued in the absence of fresh market triggers. However, any positive development on the US-Iran front can help improve investor sentiment and provide some relief to the market," Ali mentioned.
KTrade Securities wrote in its market wrap that the index reversed early gains amid sustained selling pressure, shedding 1,332 points (-0.8%). Among key contributors, Kohinoor Textile, Services, Attock Refinery and Ibrahim Fibres provided support, while Pakistan Petroleum, Hub Power, OGDC and Fauji Fertiliser weighed on the index.
Arif Habib Limited (AHL) observed that 14 shares rose while 86 fell with Kohinoor Textile (+1.02%), Services (+0.26%) and Attock Refinery (+0.21%) contributing the most to the index gains. PPL (-2.45%), UBL (-0.81%) and Hubco (-1.22%) were the biggest drags
In a major report, the headline inflation for September 2026 arrived at 10.3% year-on-year, which marked an increase from 5.8% in September 2025. On a month-on-month basis, the inflation increased by 1.3% in September. As a result, the average inflation for 1QFY27 jumped to 10.21% from 4.30% in the same period of last year
Also, Pakistan's government was in discussions with counterparts in Iran, seeking a safe passage for two October shipments of Qatari LNG through the Strait of Hormuz. "The bias remains to the downside with 166k clearly in sight," AHL predicted.
Cumulatively, trading volumes stood at 548.4 million shares, down from 591.2 million on Wednesday. In the ready market, 121 companies advanced, 323 declined and 48 remained unchanged. Kohinoor Spinning was the volume leader with trading in 93.8 million shares, rising Rs0.11 to close at Rs5.84.

title: Govt decides to map non-compliant shops | The Express Tribune
description:
Govt decides to map 
non-compliant shops
content:
Will take punitive action against traders not applying for fixed tax scheme
The government on Thursday announced that it would immediately start mapping non-compliant shops for taking punitive action against traders, who stayed away from a fixed tax scheme that required only 1% tax payment in return for immunity from audit and liberty to deal in cash.
The decision was taken during a review meeting on implementation of the scheme, a day after it emerged that until the statutory deadline only four new traders joined the scheme.
"The meeting decided that FBR officers, together with trader representatives, will begin mapping markets and shops across the country from Friday (today)," said a statement issued by the Ministry of Finance.
Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani chaired the meeting. Going after the traders will be the most difficult part of the scheme as the PML-N has traditionally been soft towards the trading class, which has a 19% share in the economy but less than 1% contribution to taxes.
FBR Member Strategic Transformation Dr Hamid Ateeq Sarwar said on Wednesday that the government was targeting to bring 500,000 to 1 million traders into the tax net out of the 3.7 million who are outside the system.
Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) Chairman Rashid Mahmood Langrial said that the government was worried that the response to the tax scheme remained below expectations, with 787 tax returns filed under the new scheme, of which only four were new filers. The government has already given a 15-day extension for filing returns to all taxpayers. It has estimated at least Rs50 billion will be generated from the scheme and has added the amount to this fiscal year's budget.
The FBR chairman said this week that if the scheme remained successful, the collection should be over Rs100 billion but if it failed, there would be negligible payments.
The state finance minister directed the FBR that its officers, working with trader representatives, should map markets and every individual shop. He said that the shopkeepers must be briefed on the easy tax scheme during the mapping and the FBR officers must visit markets according to a daily schedule.
The government also admitted that there were technical issues in the tax returns specifically designed for the traders. The meeting was briefed that the technical issue in the "other income" column of the tax return, flagged on traders' identification and complaint, had been resolved, according to a statement.
Addressing the meeting, Bilal Azhar Kayani said the shopkeepers had been given a scheme of their own choice, so there was now no justification for not filing the tax returns. He said penalties had been fixed with the consent and consultation of shopkeepers and urged them to avail themselves of the 15-day extension. After the deadline, a shopkeeper will pay a penalty of Rs10,000 in the first month, Rs25,000 in the second month and Rs50,000 in the third month.
Trade leaders Ajmal Baloch, Kashif Chaudhry and tax consultant Habib Fakhruddin were also present in the meeting. Dr Hamid Ateeq Sarwar, Member Inland Revenue Operations Zubair Bilal, senior FBR officials, and chief commissioners and commissioners from across the country attended via video link.
Kayani remained hopeful that the scheme would pick up momentum once the FBR started chasing the traders. If the traders did not opt for the scheme and even the fines proved insufficient, then strong enforcement measures would have to be taken, he said, adding that the FBR would now go to the field to make the traders aware of the new scheme. Overall, the FBR received 5.7 million tax returns compared to the total of 8.5 million returns filed in the last tax year. There was a 32% reduction. There were 19 million registered taxpayers with the FBR but only 5.7 million, or 30% of them, chose to file returns.

title: Energy keeps CPI in double digits
description: Energy keeps CPI in double digits
content:
Expensive power, fuel offsets positive impact of decrease in food prices
Inflation in Pakistan slowed down to 10.3% in September but it remained higher than the official forecast due to increasing prices of electricity and fuel, which offset the positive impact of a significant slowdown in prices of food commodities.
According to the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS), the energy-group prices further increased compared to a year ago. This kept the overall annual inflation rate at 10.3%, which was slightly higher than the official projection of the Planning Commission.
The commission's assumption had been used to project a 7% to 8% average inflation during the current fiscal year despite the Middle East conflict. However, the monthly inflation marginally inched up to 1.3% due to a constant increase in fuel prices, which was the highest rate since April this year.
Pakistan on Tuesday informed the International Monetary Fund (IMF) that despite price pressure from the Middle East war, the inflation rate would remain below the official target of 8.2%. The government's assessment is based on the assumption that if the situation normalises until October 2026 and the average Brent crude price stabilises at $80 per barrel in the current fiscal year, the inflation will remain at 7.5%.
If the oil price remains at around $100 per barrel till December, the projected inflation may increase to 8.2% for the fiscal year. The government has set the inflation target for this fiscal year at 8.2% but it said that due to an anticipated moderation in global crude oil prices, improved agricultural output, exchange rate stability, effective administrative measures and a favourable base effect during the second half, the inflation is projected to stay within the 7% to 8% range, with the most likely outcome being around 7.5%.
Its assessment was that price pressures would remain elevated till December but thereafter, they were expected to moderate gradually over the course of the year, reflecting improving domestic supply conditions and a relatively favourable external outlook.
According to the PBS, the inflation went down both in urban and rural areas, standing in the range of 10.1% in urban areas and 10.5% in rural areas. Food inflation significantly slowed down from 12.1% to 8.1% in urban areas while it went down to 7.7% in rural areas. However, the energy group saw a northbound trend in both urban and rural areas. The pace accelerated to 11.5% in urban areas and 13.1% in rural areas.
During the ongoing review talks, the IMF has urged Pakistan to adjust both exchange rate and interest rate policies to tame inflation and keep the current account deficit under check. However, the federal and central bank authorities were of the view that the policies were appropriate in the given macroeconomic environment. Last month, the central bank kept its policy rate unchanged at 11.5% with a seven to three majority vote.
Core inflation, excluding food and energy prices, slowed down both in urban and rural areas, ranging from 8.1% to 8.6%, much below the policy rate. But the cost of housing, water, electricity, gas and fuel remained the main concern in addition to transportation charges, according to the official bulletin.
PBS reported that petrol price was 39% higher in September compared with a year ago. Within one month, there was an 11% increase in the price of petrol, which was a steep rise given the overall high price. The per-litre petrol was at Rs389.4 for Thursday and the price was Rs400 in case of high-speed diesel that was keeping transport charges high.
The cost of transport services went up by 30% last month over a year ago, according to the PBS. The data-collecting agency stated that electricity prices were higher by 33% in September over a year ago and within one month there was a 15% surge. The high cost of electricity is already driving consumers away from the national power grid.
Motor vehicle taxes jumped by 39% over a year ago, contributing to increase in expenses. PBS said that onion prices were 125% higher in September on a yearly basis, followed by a 41% increase in wheat prices.
Owing to serious management issues, the government is already in the process of importing 765,000 tonnes of wheat. Wheat flour prices were higher by 32% compared to a year ago. But prices of potatoes, chicken, eggs and sugar were lower in the range of 30% to 20% last month.

title: Effective devolution key to Sindh s betterment
description: Effective devolution key to Sindh s betterment
content:
Local bodies of entire country need fiscal, administrative powers to improve governance
Effective devolution of political, administrative and financial powers to the lowest appropriate tier of the government is essential for improving governance and achieving sustainable economic growth, speakers at a discussion said on Thursday.
Speaking at a session titled "Devolution: The Way Forward for Improving Governance in Sindh" organised by the IBA's Centre for Excellence in Journalism, panelists debated whether Pakistan's governance problems could be addressed through the creation of new provinces or by strengthening existing provincial and local governments.
Former federal finance minister Miftah Ismail said the creation of new provinces could not by itself guarantee better governance, arguing "the focus should instead be on empowering citizens and governments at the appropriate level." He said no country could develop and prosper without improving public living standards and education, while stressing that political and administrative reforms had to translate into better services for ordinary citizens.
Ismail argued that the devolution of responsibilities without corresponding financial powers would remain incomplete. He questioned the logic of National Finance Commission (NFC) arrangements if provinces themselves did not establish effective Provincial Finance Commissions (PFCs) to transfer resources to local governments. "Provinces will not do devolution as nobody leaves power," he said and added that new provinces would also provide no guarantee of better governance if elections were not fair and institutions were not functioning effectively.
Former federal secretary M Younus Dagha said administrative units needed greater authority and pointed to the historical link between stronger local governments and improvements in social indicators. He said "unfortunately" devolution had repeatedly advanced under military governments, while elected provincial governments had generally been reluctant to surrender authority to lower tiers.
Dagha highlighted the contrast between Karachi and other parts of Sindh, saying that areas on the right bank of the Indus continue to face flooding and administrative problems while provincial authorities remain heavily occupied with Karachi. If local governments were empowered, he argued, they would be able to respond directly to the problems of their own areas rather than waiting for decisions from provincial authorities.
He also raised the issue of Karachi's fiscal resources, claiming that changes involving the distribution of Octroi and Zila Tax (OZT) had deprived the city of substantial revenues. Research on Sindh's local-government finances has similarly identified OZT as historically one of the most important own-source revenues for municipal councils, particularly Karachi.
Dagha said all three tiers of the government - federal, provincial and local - should operate within clearly defined jurisdictions while maintaining institutional coordination. He further argued that provinces should be allowed greater control over the energy system to support local industries, but said the principle should extend across the distribution system so that electricity and other services could respond to local economic needs.
Economist Kaiser Bengali said Pakistan's decentralisation debate remained constrained by a "fear factor" among political actors and provinces. He said the 18th Constitutional Amendment and the 7th NFC Award were attempts to correct the imbalance of powers between the federation and provinces. The 7th NFC Award increased the provincial share in the divisible tax pool from 47.5% to 57.5% from 2011-12 and introduced criteria beyond population for distribution among provinces.
Bengali argued that the fiscal system should provide stronger incentives for provinces to improve living standards, education and revenue generation rather than relying predominantly on population-based transfers. He also stressed the principle of subsidiarity, under which each function should be performed by the relevant level of government capable of delivering it effectively.
IBA faculty member Dr Nausheen Wasi said the debate over creating new provinces was emerging from quarters that, in her view, were indifferent to the broader public interest. She argued that the fundamental question was whether the state wanted to serve citizens or concentrate power among a few actors. Wasi also linked the debate over administrative restructuring with wider international environment and discussions around mineral resources and corporate farming.

SBP's forex holdings jump $39m; gold falls Rs3,000 per tola
Pakistan's total liquid foreign reserves stood at $26.8 billion as of September 25, 2026, according to data released by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP).
During the week, the SBP's foreign reserves increased by $39 million to reach $21.4 billion. Meanwhile, the net foreign reserves held by commercial banks were recorded at $5.3 billion, contributing to the country's cumulative liquid reserves position.
Furthermore, the Pakistani rupee closed slightly higher at 277.10 against the US dollar, registering a marginal gain of Rs0.01 compared to the previous session's close at 277.11. Internationally, the greenback held near a two-month high, bolstered by rising US Treasury yields amid ongoing global inflation concerns linked to the Middle East conflict.
Meanwhile, gold prices in Pakistan fell on Thursday, tracking the impact of a recent decline in international bullion prices, with the precious metal losing Rs3,000 per tola during the day. According to rates shared by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association, the gold price per tola settled at Rs438,636, compared with Rs441,636 on Wednesday.
The price of 10-gram gold declined by Rs2,572 to Rs376,059. On Wednesday, gold had gained Rs4,300 per tola in the local market. In the international market, spot gold was largely steady on Thursday as pressure from a stronger US dollar and elevated US Treasury yields was offset by softer-than-expected US inflation data, which reduced expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in October. Spot gold edged up 0.1% to $4,159.11 per ounce by 11:17 am EDT (1517 GMT), while US gold futures for December delivery rose 0.1% to $4,189.30, as per Reuters. Despite Thursday's modest recovery, gold prices declined more than 6% in September. Meanwhile, silver prices in the local market fell Rs50 per tola to Rs6,528.
Gold has remained above the $4,000-an-ounce level despite elevated US Treasury yields. The resilience reflects continued demand for the precious metal, although its traditional relationship with rates and the US dollar has weakened in recent years.
Gold, which does not generate any yield, typically comes under pressure when real yields rise because higher-yielding assets become more attractive. Historically, the rates and movements in the US dollar were among the major factors influencing bullion prices.
