title: Fact check  Viral video does not show Dubai Tel Aviv Flydubai flight at time of attempted hijacking
description: Viral video falsely linked to Flydubai hijacking is from Dubai  with 2022 audio added
content:
Viral video falsely linked to Flydubai hijacking is from Dubai, with 2022 audio added
Multiple news outlets and people shared a video across social media platforms on Wednesday allegedly showing an Israel-bound Flydubai flight during a hijacking attempt. However, the clip is from Dubai and the audio is spliced in from a different, older video.
Two pilots were wounded after they fought on board the plane they were flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv, and which was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia on Sept 30. The flydubai plane landed in Tabuk at 9:45am and its “captain and copilot were found to have injuries and were transported to hospital”, a statement from the company operating the airport said.
Several Israeli media outlets reported that a fight had broken out between the plane’s pilots, reportedly causing a distress signal to be activated. Israeli media also reported that two other pilots were flying on the plane as passengers, and that they had taken over the controls to carry out the emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
On Wednesday, the Pakistan Daily posted a video showing a Flydubai plane on Instagram with the following caption: “Dramatic footage reportedly captured by a passenger from the window of a Flydubai aircraft has emerged following an incident on board. The Dubai–Tel Aviv flight was diverted to Saudi Arabia and landed safely after a reported confrontation in the cockpit.”
Sada News Agency posted the same clip with the following caption: “A video circulating on Israeli platforms shows the moment a plane descended more than 14,000 feet in one minute. Security sources do not rule out that the incident was security-related. - Translated by Sada News. Zamir cancels his visit to the United States after the security alert level is raised. Israel retracts its initial account and speaks of an attempted “terrorist” attack using the plane, which one pilot was prevented from carrying out by being stabbed and subdued by the other pilot with the help of passengers.”
A local Arab media outlet, Sham TV , shared the same video on Facebook with the following caption: “A viral video of screams and panic inside the ‘Fly Dubai’ plane heading to ‘Tel Aviv’, which was carrying around 150 Israelis.”
A media outlet, Upuknews , shared the same video with the following caption: “Terrifying Footage Emerges From Flydubai Flight Incident. A passenger reportedly captured dramatic footage from the window of the Flydubai aircraft during the incident. The Dubai–Tel Aviv flight was diverted to Saudi Arabia and landed safely following the reported cockpit confrontation.”
Another X user shared the same clip with the following caption: “Watch: Terrifying footage of the incident, recorded from a passenger window aboard the aircraft flydubai- Yedioth Ahronot News.”
Another user shared the same video with a similar caption, gaining 383,000 views.
The same video was posted by another account with the following caption: “Footage from inside the cabin shows the aircraft’s dramatic dive: passengers can be heard screaming as the plane rapidly loses altitude. According to reports, shortly afterwards passengers intervened in the cockpit incident, brought the situation under control and helped stabilise the aircraft before its emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.”
Several other users also shared the clip across YouTube and X, as can be seen here , here , here , and here ; collectively accumulating 74,300 views.
A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to its high virality and keen public interest in the hijacking incident.
The video was analysed to determine the location where the footage was recorded.
The aircraft can be seen flying in the direction of Terminal 2, towards Dubai International Airport for landing, as can be seen in the snapshot of Google Maps.
The Flydubai plane can be seen flying over a water channel in the viral clip. A comparison with satellite imagery on Google Maps showed that the waterway is an inlet channel located in Dubai, separating the Dubai islands from the mainland.
Additional visuals from the viral video were also compared with aerial imagery of Dubai on Google Maps. Several identifiable geographical features and locations in the viral clip matched Dubai's landscape, indicating the visuals were filmed while flying over Dubai.
However, checking news articles from mainstream international media outlets such as BBC , France 24 , CNN , and Gulf News showed that Flydubai flight FZ1073 was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv.
The flight was subsequently diverted to Tabuk Airport in Saudi Arabia, while Saudi authorities reportedly detained the alleged attacker.
A screenshot of the flight route from the flight-tracking service Flightradar also corroborated the same.
In contrast to the claims in the viral captions that alleged the video showed the moment of descent or when the altercation aboard the plane occurred, Flightradar said that the flight was along the Saudi-Jordan border when the series of incidents occurred.
As can be seen in the flight path, there was no nearby body of water at the time the incident occurred, in contrast to the water seen in the viral video.
Furthermore, the audio in the video was traced to a Facebook post shared on September 30, 2022, with different visuals.
The same audio starts at the 15-second mark. The post was captioned: “This plane hit some bad turbulence over the Andes.”
The video shows passengers screaming out of fear due to turbulence in the flight. A user in the comments section mentioned his experience on the same flight, mentioning that it was from the United States to Amsterdam.
The claim that a viral video shows the Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv at the moment an attempted hijacking occurred is false.
The video is from Dubai and edited with audio of a different incident from 2022, whereas the hijacking occurred over Saudi/Jordanian airspace.

title: Pete Davidson recalls    cooking ketamine    and reaching breaking point before entering rehab
description: Davidson said a call from his mother helped prompt him to seek treatment in 2023
content:
Davidson said a call from his mother helped prompt him to seek treatment in 2023
Pete Davidson has opened up about his past drug addiction, describing the extent of his substance use before entering rehab and explaining how he reached a turning point in 2023.
In a new interview with Variety , published September 30, Davidson said he was using several substances during the most difficult period of his addiction. He recalled using ketamine, LSD, psilocybin mushrooms, nitrous oxide, cannabis and pills, adding that he had reached a point where he was preparing his own ketamine.
Davidson said the situation became frightening because he no longer felt high while taking drugs and instead experienced that sensation when he was sober. He described that realisation as a sign that his substance use had become a serious problem.
The comedian said he reached what he considered a low point in summer 2023, following the release of Bupkis , the autobiographical comedy series in which he played a version of himself. He had also left Saturday Night Live the previous year, a change he said removed a structure that had been part of his life.
Davidson eventually sought treatment after an emotional FaceTime conversation with his mother, Amy. He said she told him her greatest fear was seeing news that something had happened to him. Davidson said he reached a point where he could no longer put her through that fear.
Although he had attended rehab previously, Davidson said his approach was different this time because he wanted to become sober for himself rather than for another person or a career obligation.
The 32-year-old also discussed his life after addiction. He said he has been free from hard drugs for two or three years and has not used cannabis for about a year. He said he currently drinks around four beers a year.
Davidson credited his daughter Scottie with helping reinforce his commitment to sobriety. He said becoming a father changed his priorities and gave him a stronger reason to focus on his life outside the pressures of fame.

title: Obsession    submitted for Golden Globes musical or comedy categories despite its horror roots
description: Focus Features had previously planned an extensive awards campaign for Inde Navarrette and Curry Barker
content:
Focus Features had previously planned an extensive awards campaign for Inde Navarrette and Curry Barker
Curry Barker's Obsession is entering the Golden Globes awards race in the musical or comedy categories, marking a notable campaign decision for Focus Features as the horror film heads into awards season.
The Hollywood Reporter reported on September 30 that Focus Features and its fellow stakeholders have submitted Obsession for consideration as a musical or comedy rather than as a drama. The decision follows months of speculation over where the genre crossing film would be positioned at the Golden Globes.
Starring Inde Navarrette and Michael Johnston, Obsession centres on Bear, a young man who uses a mysterious wish object in an attempt to make his crush, Nikki, fall in love with him. His wish produces increasingly disturbing consequences, giving the film its combination of horror, psychological tension and dark humour.
The musical or comedy submission places Obsession alongside a number of films that have previously crossed conventional genre boundaries at the Golden Globes. Industry insiders cited films including Get Out , The Banshees of Inisherin , Triangle of Sadness , Poor Things , The Substance and Bugonia as precedents for genre-blurring films competing in the category.
The campaign could also affect Navarrette's awards-season positioning. Variety reported earlier in September that Focus Features planned to campaign for Navarrette in the best actress category at the Academy Awards, alongside a broad Oscar campaign for the film.
The Golden Globes submission comes after Obsession became a major commercial success. The film was made on a reported $750,000 production budget and has earned more than $500m worldwide, according to industry reports.
Focus Features will now await the Golden Globes' consideration process, while the film continues its broader awards campaign. The submission does not guarantee a nomination, as category entries remain subject to the Golden Globes' eligibility and voting process.
For Navarrette and Barker, the decision adds another chapter to an unusually strong awards campaign for a horror release that has attracted both commercial attention and recognition for its performances and filmmaking.

title: Anne Hathaway chooses Knicks championship over another Oscar

Hathaway received a signed OG Anunoby jersey and baby gifts from the Knicks
Anne Hathaway has made her priorities clear when it comes to the New York Knicks, choosing another championship for the team over winning a second Oscar during an appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon .
The actress appeared on the September 30 episode to promote her upcoming erotic thriller Verity , but the conversation soon turned to her long-standing support for the Knicks. Host Jimmy Fallon revisited the running joke that Hathaway had become a good-luck charm for the team following the release of The Devil Wears Prada 2 .
The film, which premiered on May 1, includes a scene in which Hathaway's character interacts with Knicks star Karl-Anthony Towns at a Hamptons gathering. The Knicks then went on a 13-game winning streak, prompting playful online speculation that Hathaway had somehow influenced the team's fortunes.
During the episode, Fallon presented Hathaway with a Knicks jersey signed by OG Anunoby. The actress has previously spoken about her admiration for Anunoby after he nearly collided with her and her son while chasing a ball into the stands during a November 2024 Knicks game.
The team also sent Hathaway a basket of gifts for her baby, along with a card signed by Anunoby. Hathaway appeared particularly delighted by the jersey, putting it on during the segment.
Fallon later challenged Hathaway with a game called "Best Thing Ever", in which she had to choose between two things she valued. One choice asked whether she would prefer to win another Oscar or see the Knicks win another NBA championship.
Hathaway hesitated before selecting another Knicks championship. She then acknowledged how strongly she was reacting to the decision, describing the choice as an intense experience for her.
Hathaway previously won the Academy Award for supporting actress for her performance in Les Misérables in 2013. Her latest appearance comes as she continues promoting Verity , while The Odyssey is also among her upcoming major film projects.

title: Bono reveals Ed Sheeran wanted to keep politics out of U2 collaboration
description: The song was written from the perspective of a soldier in Ukraine amid the war with Russia
content:
The song was written from the perspective of a soldier in Ukraine amid the war with Russia
Bono has revealed that Ed Sheeran wanted to keep politics separate from music when the pair collaborated with U2 on ‘Yours Eternally’ earlier this year.
The comments come amid renewed discussion around Sheeran’s position on political issues after Macklemore was dropped as a support act from his Loop Tour following his calls for a “free Palestine” on stage.
According to Macklemore, Robert Kraft told Sheeran that he had “rallied some of the other stadium owners” and gave him an “ultimatum” over the rapper’s involvement. Sheeran later stated, “I am not complicit”.
Sheeran’s band and other support acts, including Aaron Rowe and Finneas, subsequently withdrew from the tour in support of Palestinian solidarity.
During a performance in Philadelphia, Sheeran acknowledged “making mistakes” while maintaining that his shows were about “humanity, not politics”.
In an interview with Rolling Stone UK, Bono urged people not to personalise the controversy, saying, “I would say with Ed and Macklemore that we shouldn’t personalise this, what’s going on.”
Bono also recalled Sheeran asking during their collaboration, “You’re not going to get me into politics, are you?”
The song was written from the perspective of a soldier in Ukraine amid the war with Russia.
Bono said he explained the song’s inspiration, but Sheeran responded, “Yeah, but I just want to keep my thing free.”
Bono added, “You can’t be pushing people around,” while drummer Larry Mullen Jr. said “artists [can] choose whether they want to be involved, and they are entitled to choose whether they want to be involved or not… And it’s not our job to criticise that, no matter how we feel.”

title: David Byrne reflects on    Talking Heads    enduring legacy as all four members reunite
description: David Byrne reflects on    Talking Heads    enduring appeal as the band   s four members reunite for a SiriusXM event
content:
David Byrne reflects on ‘Talking Heads’ enduring appeal as the band’s four members reunite for a SiriusXM event
David Byrne has reflected on the enduring legacy of Talking Heads, admitting that he finds it “surprising” that the band’s music has continued to connect with new generations.
Byrne reunited with Tina Weymouth, Chris Frantz and Jerry Harrison for a rare conversation hosted by Este Haim at SiriusXM’s New York studios on September 28. The event was held to launch Talking Heads Radio , a temporary SiriusXM channel celebrating more than 50 years of the band’s music. The full conversation airs on October 1 at 12pm ET.
During the discussion, the band members looked back at their creative process and the way their approach evolved across their early records. Harrison explained that each album brought a different process, with the group deliberately seeking new challenges rather than repeating what they had done before.
Byrne, meanwhile, said he generally tries not to look back too much, although he remains proud of what Talking Heads accomplished.
“I’m very proud of everything we did,” he said, before acknowledging the continued relevance of their music. “It’s kind of surprising how this stuff has kind of stood the test of time, that it keeps finding a new audience.”
Frantz also reflected on what he believed made Talking Heads distinctive, pointing to the chemistry between the four members and their collaborative approach to songwriting and performance.
The reunion comes after the group appeared together publicly in 2023 for a Q&A at the Toronto International Film Festival celebrating the 40th anniversary of Stop Making Sense . The band has not announced a live reunion performance.
Talking Heads Radio will feature the band’s songs, deep cuts, stories and guest DJ sets, and will be available on SiriusXM’s car service through October 22 and the SiriusXM app through October 31.

title: Joe Jonas opens up about breakouts and learning to slow down his skincare routine
description: Jonas said he experienced breakouts after filming a movie and struggled to understand what was causing them
content:
Jonas said he experienced breakouts after filming a movie and struggled to understand what was causing them
Joe Jonas has opened up about dealing with breakouts and how the experience changed the way he approaches skincare.
Speaking exclusively to PEOPLE, the Jonas Brothers singer, 37, said he once believed his skin was fine as long as he washed his face at night. Over the past few years, however, he has learned more about how his skin reacts to different products and why a more considered routine works better for him.
Jonas said he experienced significant breakouts after filming a movie and initially struggled to understand what was causing them. He eventually realised that he may have been using certain products too quickly or in excessive amounts.
“I started breaking out quite a bit. I couldn’t figure it out,” Jonas said. “There [were] little things that I think that I probably used too much of or too fast, so I’m trying to slow down.”
The singer has also been open about men's skincare and beauty routines over the years. In 2022, he discussed his approach to cosmetic treatments and said he did not believe men should shy away from talking about skincare or ageing.
“We’re all getting older and part of that is being comfortable [in our skin],” Jonas previously said. He also revealed at the time that he had used the cosmetic injectable Xeomin for his frown lines and the scar between his eyebrows.
Jonas' skincare routine is also something he shares with his brothers. He joked that borrowing each other's products can cause disagreements between him, Nick and Kevin Jonas, although the siblings have found other ways to spend time together while touring.
The Jonas Brothers are currently on their Burning Up Tour All Over Again, which is scheduled to conclude in New Jersey in December. Jonas said that after performances, the brothers often spend time together in hotel rooms, watching sports and catching up.
The singer said they have also been making an effort to support each other's individual interests, whether that means playing golf, visiting a coffee shop or looking at art. For Jonas, the focus is ultimately on finding “balance” while working alongside his brothers.
Jonas is also currently the face of Kenneth Cole's new Inspire fragrance campaign, adding another beauty and grooming project to his growing focus on personal care.

title: Why did Conan O   Brien leave Late Night  Comedian explains his decision
description: Conan O   Brien explains why he chose to leave late night television before reaching 30 years in the industry
content:
Conan O’Brien explains why he chose to leave late night television before reaching 30 years in the industry
Conan O’Brien has revealed that he chose to step away from late night television before he could reach the 30-year mark, saying he could see the industry changing around him.
Speaking at Bloomberg’s Screentime in Los Angeles on September 30, O’Brien reflected on his decision to end Conan , his TBS late-night show, in 2021. The comedian said he had spent around 28 years working in late night across NBC and Turner when he began considering his exit.
“I knew I wanted to wrap up my late night gig soon,” O’Brien said, explaining that some people had suggested he stay until he reached 30 years. However, he felt the direction of the industry was becoming increasingly clear.
“I’ve loved it, but you can kind of see which way things [are] going,” he recalled thinking.
O’Brien then offered a characteristically humorous explanation for his decision, saying he wanted to leave before anyone else could make the decision for him.
“And so, in true sort of Irish tradition, I wanted to leave the party before I was asked to leave,” he said.
The comedian also discussed the changing economics of late night television, noting that the format had evolved considerably since its early days. He compared the rise of late night programming to networks discovering unused space in an attic, eventually turning those hours into profitable programming.
According to O’Brien, the growth of cable television, followed by streaming and the internet, fundamentally changed the business. He pointed to the sheer volume of online video content as a new form of competition for traditional late-night programmes.
Despite those changes, O’Brien said he is now more comfortable with his work in podcasting, where he has a smaller team and feels everyone has a crucial role.

title: Off Campus  season 2  Cast  story and everything we know so far
description: Season 2 will shift its romantic focus to Dean Di Laurentis and Allie Hayes  played by Stephen Kalyn and Mika Abdalla
content:
Season 2 will shift its romantic focus to Dean Di Laurentis and Allie Hayes, played by Stephen Kalyn and Mika Abdalla
Off Campus Season 2 is moving ahead at Prime Video, with the hit college hockey romance series returning with a new central couple while keeping its original leads part of the story.
Based on Elle Kennedy’s bestselling Off-Campus book series, the Prime Video adaptation premiered in May 2026 and quickly became one of the streamer’s biggest new series. The first season drew 36 million viewers globally in its first 12 days, according to Prime Video, helping secure its continuation.
Season 2 will shift its main romantic focus to Dean Di Laurentis and Allie Hayes, played by Stephen Kalyn and Mika Abdalla. Their relationship began to take shape during the first season, and their story will become the primary romance when the series returns.
Belmont Cameli and Ella Bright will also return as Garrett Graham and Hannah Wells. While their romance will no longer drive the season, creator Louisa Levy has confirmed that the couple will remain an important part of the ensemble. Antonio Cipriano will return as John Logan, while Jalen Thomas Brooks is back as John Tucker.
The new season will also introduce India Fowler as Grace Ivers, Logan’s eventual love interest from Kennedy’s books. Fowler’s casting has already sparked interest among fans, particularly because Logan and Grace’s relationship is central to The Mistake, the second book in the original series.
Cipriano has teased that viewers will see the beginnings of Logan and Grace’s relationship during Season 2, even though Dean and Allie remain the main couple. The actor has also mentioned a memorable water tower scene from the books that he hopes makes it into the adaptation.
Shay Rudolph has also joined the cast as Summer Di Laurentis, Dean’s sister. Her arrival could help expand the television series into Kennedy’s wider Briar University universe, which includes the Briar U spin-off books.
Plot details remain largely under wraps, but the season is expected to build on Dean and Allie’s relationship while continuing the stories of the Briar hockey players. The decision to make Dean and Allie the central couple means the show is moving from the first book, The Deal, to the third book, The Score, rather than following the novels in their original order.
Filming is already underway. Cameli revealed in June that production had progressed through the first two episodes, with the second season consisting of eight episodes. A release date has not yet been announced by Prime Video.
Season 2 is also expected to continue the show's emphasis on music, although Levy has indicated there will be fewer live musical performances than in the first season. The series will instead continue using songs and its original score to shape key moments.
With Dean and Allie taking centre stage, Logan and Grace beginning their story and Garrett and Hannah remaining part of the ensemble, Off Campus Season 2 is set to expand the Briar University world while introducing another chapter of Kennedy’s hockey romance universe.

Oil surge, inflation and uncertainty over US-Iran situation cloud market outlook
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) reversed its early gains on Thursday as rising oil prices and persistent inflation concerns weighed on investor sentiment, while uncertainty over renewed US-Iran diplomatic efforts added to the cautious mood.
The benchmark KSE-100 Index fell 1,332.47 points, or 0.78%, to settle at 168,636.85. The index touched an intraday high of 170,688.38 and a low of 168,567.79.
Meanwhile, oil prices rose around 2% during the session after China suspended oil product exports, tightening global fuel markets already facing supply constraints, while investors continued to assess diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war.
On the domestic front, Pakistan’s inflation slowed to 10.26% in September from 11.1% in August primarily led by food prices, but remained above the State Bank’s medium-term target range.
The market had opened on a positive note, with the KSE-100 reaching 170,270.16, up 300.84 points, or 0.18%, at 10:15am, before losing ground as the session progressed.

Muhammad Awais Ashraf of AKD Securities assessed that easing inflationary pressures amid strong external account position, along with a reduction in domestic political noise would strengthen investor confidence.

Spokesperson says Pakistan deeply saddened by the loss of five crew members of the hijacked vessel
Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said on Thursday that Pakistan was in close contact with Somali authorities to facilitate the repatriation of saved and slain crew members of the sea-borne vessel MT Honour 25.
“Three of those killed were Pakistani nationals — Rafiullah Khan, Syed Kashif Umar and Mahmood Ahmed Ansari — while four crew members, including three Pakistanis, were injured and were receiving medical treatment,” Khan said while speaking at the weekly media briefing
The spokesperson said Pakistan was “deeply saddened” by the loss of five crew members during the recovery operation of the sea-borne vessel.
“The government remains in close contact with the Somali authorities and other stakeholders to facilitate medical care for the injured, repatriation of the mortal remains and safe return of the surviving Pakistani crew members [of the MT Honour 25].”

The spokesperson also said Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister (FM) Ishaq Dar had held a series of bilateral and multilateral engagements in New York during the high-level week of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly from Sept 21 to 25.
"Details of FM Dar’s engagements would be shared by the deputy premier himself at a press briefing scheduled for Friday," he said.
Giving an update on Pakistan’s chairmanship of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s Council of Heads of State for 2026-27, Khan said the first meeting of the SCO Council of National Coordinators had been held in Islamabad from Sept 28 to 30.
He further stated that National coordinators from SCO member states reviewed activities and initiatives under Pakistan’s chairmanship, discussed preparations for upcoming meetings and exchanged views on strengthening coordination and practical cooperation.

The discussions were held in line with Pakistan’s theme for its SCO chairmanship: “Turning Vision into Action: Connectivity, Innovation and Shared Prosperity.”
The visiting delegations also visited the Pakistan National Council of the Arts and Naseer Bunda Hockey Stadium, where they were briefed on Pakistan’s cultural heritage and preparations for the SCO Hockey Tournament scheduled for Nov 20 to Dec 2, Khan highlighted during the press conference.
He also said that on Sept 30, the national coordinators called on FM Dar, who highlighted Pakistan’s priorities for its SCO chairmanship and its commitment to working with member states to advance the organisation’s objectives.
The spokesperson said FM Dar had also held meetings and telephone conversations with several foreign officials over the past two weeks.
"On Sept 18, the foreign minister met Turkish Ambassador to Pakistan Irfan Naziroglu, with discussions focusing on the evolving regional situation and progress under bilateral mechanisms," he said.
Khan added that FM Dar also met British High Commissioner Jane Marriott to discuss Pakistan-UK relations, understandings reached during the recent visit of the foreign minister to Britain, and ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation.
"On Sept 19, FM Dar spoke by telephone with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. The two discussed the regional situation, with FM Dar stressing the importance of uninterrupted energy supplies and the safe and expeditious passage of ships," said the spokesperson.
He also underscored the importance of dialogue and diplomacy as the main pillars for regional stability and peace.
According to Khan, the same day, FM Dar spoke with Malaysian Foreign Minister Dato’ Seri Mohamad Hasan, with the two discussing bilateral relations, particularly the expansion of trade and economic cooperation.

title: Mir Raza judicial commission   s term extended until October 15
description: Cabinet decides that Justice Umar Sial could continue inquiry beyond extended deadline if further time is required
content:
Cabinet decides that Justice Umar Sial could continue inquiry beyond extended deadline if further time is required
The Sindh Cabinet on Thursday approved extending the term of the inquiry commission investigating the death of Mir Raza Ali until October 15, allowing Justice Omar Sial to continue the proceedings if more time was required.
The Sindh Home Department on August 24 notified the formation of a judicial commission to probe the death of 25-year-old Mir Raza Ali, with Justice Sial appointed as its head following his nomination by the Sindh High Court (SHC) chief justice through a letter dated the same day. The first hearing of the commission took place on September 1.
The decision was taken at a cabinet meeting chaired by Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah at the CM House. The cabinet was briefed that the commission had conducted extensive proceedings and recorded statements from dozens of witnesses as part of its investigation.
The commission required additional time to complete its inquiry and finalise its findings and recommendations, the meeting was told. The cabinet subsequently approved extending the commission’s term until October 15.
KARACHI (October 1, 2026): Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah presides over a cabinet meeting at CM House. pic.twitter.com/eBWicHn8PO
It also decided that Justice Sial could continue the inquiry beyond the extended deadline if further time was required.
The commission’s term had expired on September 28, according to a written order issued by the commission. The commission had requested the Sindh government to extend its tenure until October 15.
The provincial government’s focal person, Javed Ahmed Abro, had informed the commission that the summary seeking an extension had been approved by the chief minister and forwarded to the Sindh Cabinet for a decision.
The commission had subsequently adjourned its proceedings until October 2, pending the cabinet’s decision.
The written order had stated that if the cabinet did not approve an extension, no further witnesses would be summoned and the commission would prepare and submit its report based on the statements recorded so far.
If the tenure was extended, fresh notices would be issued to witnesses, the order had added.
During an earlier hearing, Investigation Officer Siraj Lashari and a representative of the Citizens-Police Liaison Committee (CPLC) had appeared before the commission to record their statements. However, their statements had not been recorded because the commission’s term had expired.
Mir Raza Ali, the 25-year-old owner of dessert brand Wafflix, went missing from Karachi’s PECHS area on July 28, 2026. His body was found the following day in bushes near a wedding hall in Gulistan-e-Johar. Police initially treated the death as a possible suicide, but a second post-mortem conducted after his exhumation found a firearm entry wound, multiple ante-mortem injuries and signs of internal bleeding, leading investigators to treat the case as murder.
The initial post-mortem had faced several objections, with the Karachi police surgeon identifying 14 deficiencies, including the absence of an X-ray, failure to collect hand swabs for gunshot-residue analysis and the lack of chemical examination of gunpowder marks around the bullet wound.
The investigation subsequently came under scrutiny from Raza’s family, who alleged serious lapses in the handling of evidence and CCTV footage and sought the formation of a joint investigation team. The Sindh High Court later rejected the family’s plea for a JIT but directed the relevant authorities to conduct the investigation impartially, fairly and expeditiously.
Read More: Mir Raza commission rejects family's plea to summon top cops
Police told a Senate committee in September that they had recorded statements from 78 people but had not found evidence linking anyone to Raza’s alleged murder. Investigators nevertheless continued to treat the case as murder, while reviewing medical, chemical, forensic and digital evidence.
The Sindh government had meanwhile established a judicial commission headed by Sindh High Court Justice Umar Sial to examine the circumstances surrounding Raza’s death, the conduct of the investigation and any possible negligence or concealment of evidence by police or other officials.
The judicial commission had so far examined police records, witness statements and the circumstances surrounding Mir Raza Ali’s death, with its proceedings raising discrepancies in witness accounts, the handling of evidence and the initial post-mortem. The commission also questioned senior police and health officials over the investigation, including the handling of CCTV footage, Raza’s phone and smartwatch, and the initial focus on a possible suicide.

title: Mushahid Hussain calls for regional strategy to tackle terrorism emanating from Afghan soil
description: Says Pakistan  Afghanistan can no longer afford further conflict  confrontation and instability the region
content:
Says Pakistan, Afghanistan can no longer afford further conflict, confrontation and instability the region
Former senator Mushahid Hussain Sayed called for a multi-pronged regional diplomatic approach to tackle terrorism emanating from Afghan soil, saying the issue was not merely bilateral between Pakistan and Afghanistan but a wider regional security challenge requiring a collective response from Afghanistan’s neighbours.
He made the remarks during his keynote concluding session at the two-day “International Conference on Afghan Predicament and Trajectory to Peace”, organised by the International Parliamentarians Congress (IPC) in Islamabad.
Sayed said Pakistan and Afghanistan could no longer afford further conflict, confrontation and instability in the region.
He described the conference as a productive, “first-of-its-kind” initiative focusing on Afghanistan’s relations with Pakistan and other neighbours to explore possible ways forward.
Sayed noted that Senator Sitara Ayaz, Secretary General of the IPC and host of the conference, had accompanied him twice to participate in a Track 1.5 Dialogue in Istanbul with Afghan counterparts, organised with the facilitation of Turkish friends.
“Both sides, including the Afghan side, accepted that the core issue dividing Pakistan and Afghanistan is the issue of terrorism emanating from Afghan soil, which is destabilising not only Pakistan but other neighbours of Afghanistan as well,” he said.
Sayed said the central conclusion of the Islamabad conference reflected the vision and philosophy of Allama Muhammad Iqbal, who, in his poems 100 years ago, linked peace in Afghanistan with peace in the region and Asia, while instability in Afghanistan inevitably produced instability and volatility across the region.
“Peace, security and stability are indivisible and inextricably intertwined with the region, especially Pakistan and Afghanistan,” he observed.
The former senator emphasised that despite differences with the regime in Kabul, Pakistan’s relationship with the people of Afghanistan should remain paramount.
Referring to the declaration adopted at the dialogue, he said a people-centric approach should ensure that links involving businessmen, traders, medical tourism and students from Afghanistan were not undermined.
Sayed recalled that Pakistan had been a generous host to Afghan refugees for four decades, hosting the largest number of refugees for the longest duration, adding that the historical and people-to-people bonds, particularly trade and education, between the two countries should not be allowed to suffer because of political differences.
He also referred to recent remarks by Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi describing Pakistan and Afghanistan as “inseparable brothers,” saying a similar sentiment had been conveyed by Turkish interlocutors during the Istanbul dialogue.
Sayed said there were indications of a possible opening from Kabul.
Referring to Pakistani journalists who had recently returned from Kabul, he said they had informed him about a meeting with Afghan Interior Minister Sirajuddin Haqqani.
“According to these journalists, there is a glimmer of hope from the regime in Kabul. The regime is keen to find some way forward. They recognise the problem of terrorism and want to establish some mechanism with Pakistan to take this issue forward through dialogue and resolve it,” he said.
Sayed stressed that Afghanistan’s security situation had implications extending well beyond Pakistan.
“This is not simply an issue between Pakistan and Afghanistan. It is a regional security issue,” he said, noting that terrorism and violent extremism emanating from Afghanistan would impact Pakistan, Iran, China, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Russia, as there were Kabul-based militant groups targeting these countries as well.
He pointed to the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) and its Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) as an existing institutional mechanism that could contribute to addressing regional security challenges emanating from Afghanistan.
Sayed also referred to a proposal from Russian Professor Vladimir Sotnikov for a Peace Board comprising Russia and all six neighbours of Afghanistan to work out a collective counter-terrorism strategy against terrorism emanating from Afghanistan.
He cautioned against allowing the region to become embroiled in another cycle of conflict, especially after what he described as the failed wars of aggression by India against Pakistan and by the US and Israel against Iran.
Sayed argued that Pakistan and the wider region had been affected by geopolitical competition since 9/11 and urged regional countries to learn from the consequences of the post-9/11 period.
Referring to the US intervention in Afghanistan, he said that, according to a Brown University research study, the United States had spent approximately $2.2 trillion in Afghanistan between October 7, 2001, and August 15, 2021 — a cost of $100 million a day for 20 years — while leaving behind large quantities of weapons and ammunition worth more than $7 billion, which he said were being used against Pakistan by Afghan-based terrorists.
He said the experience demonstrated the need for regional countries to avoid becoming trapped in another prolonged conflict.
The former senator maintained that the peoples of Pakistan, Afghanistan and Iran were all victims of geopolitics and that it was now time for Afghanistan to be part of the solution rather than remaining part of the problem.
Sayed called for Pakistan, Iran, China, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Russia to collectively explore practical mechanisms for addressing the Afghan security challenge.
He said sustainable peace in Afghanistan was also essential for Pakistan’s vision of emerging as a hub of regional connectivity.
Sayed said Pakistan was seeking to expand regional linkages through trade, economy, energy, ports, pipelines, roads and railways, connecting Pakistan with Central Asia, Iran, Turkiye and Afghanistan.
He also highlighted the role of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) in Pakistan’s broader regional connectivity vision.
“The main stumbling block is the situation in Afghanistan,” he said, stressing that peace and stability in Afghanistan were prerequisites for unlocking the full potential of regional economic connectivity.
He appreciated the organisers and participants for holding what he described as a frank and democratic discussion on Afghanistan.
Sayed particularly congratulated Senator Sitara Ayaz for facilitating the initiative and said Parliament and parliamentarians should increasingly use their institutional and political space to contribute to resolving challenges affecting Pakistan and the wider region.
According to the statement, the two-day dialogue brought together Pakistani and foreign parliamentarians, diplomats, academics and experts to deliberate on Afghanistan’s security situation, Pakistan-Afghanistan relations, regional stability, connectivity, reconciliation and possible pathways towards peace.
Delegates from China, Russia, Tajikistan, Pakistan and Afghanistan’s diaspora participated in the conference, which was well attended.

title: Hundreds of prisoners freed in UK as early release scheme takes effect | The Express Tribune
description: Offenders serving sentences of up to 19 months eligible for release after third of their term
content:
Offenders serving sentences of up to 19 months eligible for release after third of their term
Hundreds of eligible offenders are set to leave prisons in England and Wales as the government’s early-release scheme took effect Thursday.
The scheme was introduced after the prison system came close to running out of capacity in the summer of 2024, with fewer than 100 spaces remaining.
Under the new rules, eligible offenders serving sentences of up to 19 months can be released after serving a third of their term.
The government has faced criticism over the plan, with the main opposition Conservative Party warning that dangerous criminals could be released under the early-release scheme.
Read: UK rapper gets 12-year jail term for hit-and-run killing
“I think what would make the public less safe is if we had no prison capacity in which to put people who are arrested, suspected of crimes, today,” Treasury minister James Murray told Sky News.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s office said last month that more than 3,200 prison places had already been built under the current government, with 14,000 expected by 2031 under the largest prison expansion since the Victorian era.
As of March, more than 70,000 people had been released under the early-release scheme introduced in 2024.

title: Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike survives execution attempt
description: Following the botched attempt  Christa Pike was transported to an off site medical facility
content:
Following the botched attempt, Christa Pike was transported to an off-site medical facility
Christa Pike, convicted of murdering a schoolmate three decades ago, survived Tennessee's effort to execute her by means of lethal ​injection late on Wednesday, prison officials said, foiling the state's first attempt to put a woman to death in two centuries.
Pike's condition following the ordeal was ‌not immediately known, and it was not clear what legal avenues her lawyers or the state might pursue next after she was taken for medical treatment from the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville.
The Tennessee Department of Correction defended its handling of the high-profile execution, which had been opposed by her lawyers and human rights experts due to Pike's age at the time of the crime, her history as the victim of ​childhood sexual abuse, and untreated mental illness.
"The Tennessee Department of Correction followed every step of the state’s lawful, established execution protocol approved by the Attorney General’s Office," the ​agency said in a statement.
"The lethal injection chemical in the protocol has consistently been effective, and the protocol does not allow for additional procedures ⁠beyond what was carried out this evening. Christa Pike has been transported to an off-site medical facility," the statement concluded.
Pike's lawyers filed a federal court motion during the process seeking ​to halt her execution, citing witnesses' accounts that "executioners had injected both syringes of lethal injection chemicals and Pike is still alive and snoring," NBC News reported.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee, who denied Pike's ​clemency petition on Monday, issued a statement after the botched execution, suspending all executions this year and calling for a "comprehensive, third-party review" of Pike's execution attempt, according to the Nashville Tennessean.
The failed execution is the second in Tennessee this year, after prison officials in May aborted attempts to execute a man convicted of murders after failing to find a suitable vein for his lethal injection.
The botched attempt on Wednesday came hours after the ​US Supreme Court lifted an 11th-hour lower-court stay of the execution, clearing the way for Pike, 50, to be put to death for her role in the 1995 torture and beating ​death of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in Knoxville.
Pike was 18 in January 1995 when she, 17-year-old boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp and a third companion lured Slemmer, a classmate at their Knoxville Job Corps vocational center, into a ‌wooded area where ⁠they tortured and killed her.
The grisly nature of the slaying, which involved the perpetrators carving the shape of a pentagram in the victim's chest and taking a chunk of her skull as a souvenir of the carnage, drew intense media coverage at the time.
Pike and Shipp confessed to the killing, and both were convicted of first-degree murder.
Slemmer's mother, May Martinez, has spoken out in support of the execution.
Journalists who witnessed the attempted execution described snoring, loud exhales, gasps, and complaints from Pike about discomfort in her arm. At times, the curtain was closed, and ​journalists could only hear sounds.
Clergy were called into ​the chamber twice, they said, before an ⁠ambulance was seen arriving at the prison and then leaving.
Aside from being the first woman the state of Tennessee has tried to execute in more than 200 years, Pike was also poised to became the only person in the modern era of US capital punishment to be ​executed in Tennessee for a crime committed as a teenager.
In a 226-page petition asking the governor to commute Pike's death penalty to ​a life sentence without the ⁠possibility of parole, her lawyers earlier this week documented her history as the childhood victim of violence, neglect and sexual abuse, including two rapes at ages 11 and 17. They also cited diagnoses she received in prison for bipolar disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder.
Moreover, her lawyers pointed to evidence that Pike's mother drank heavily during pregnancy, contributing to faulty brain development that made it difficult for their ⁠client to control ​her impulses as a young person.
Pike was also convicted in August 2001 of attempted first-degree murder in an ​assault on another inmate, according to the Correction Department.
Executions of female prison inmates are exceedingly rare in the US, with women accounting for just 18 of the 1,683 people put to death since the Supreme Court allowed capital punishment to ​resume in 1976, according to the Death Penalty Information Center. Before Wednesday, Tennessee had executed 17 people.

title: French high school blockades continue as protests spread to universities
description: At least 27 high schools in Paris experience disruptions  while a large garbage fire was lit near gate of high school
content:
At least 27 high schools in Paris experience disruptions, while a large garbage fire was lit near gate of high school
French high school students continued to block their schools on Thursday as protests demanding better learning conditions spread to several universities across the country, according to broadcaster BFMTV.
At least 27 high schools in Paris experienced disruptions, while a large garbage fire was lit near the gate of a high school in the Seine-Saint-Denis department.
In Nice, students from three high schools were also called on to gather outside that same school.
Several hundred high school students came together in Lyon where the mobilization was reported to be unprecedented, with former students also included. Although the actions remained peaceful, police officers were positioned nearby.
In the Rhone department, 27 schools were also affected by the disruptions. Mortar fireworks were reported near several high schools in Lyon, while the prefecture also reported a fire on the facade of another school.
Barricades were also erected, and fires were lit in Lille as well.
Read: Student anger spreads across France
Alongside high schools, more than 15 universities were also blocked across the country. The movement reportedly spread to the main campuses of the University of Strasbourg, Aix-Marseille University, the University of Poitiers and Paul-Valery University.
At least 625 people were arrested Wednesday as blockades continued, with authorities reporting an increase in violence and dozens of injuries.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the arrests came during actions to blockade high schools, describing an "extension of the movement" and an "increase in violence" around some establishments.
At least 32 students or education staff members were injured in the mobilization, while 83 members of the internal security forces were also injured.

title: India end Pakistan   s title hopes with 4 3 win
description: Harmanpreet Singh scores twice as India hold off late Green shirts fightback in Asian Games hockey semis
content:
Harmanpreet Singh scores twice as India hold off late Green-shirts fightback in Asian Games hockey semis
India on Thursday defeated Pakistan 4-3 in a tense men’s hockey semi-final of the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya. Harmanpreet Singh converted two penalty corners as India built a 2-0 lead in the first quarter at Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium.
Pakistan responded in the second quarter through Abu Mahmood, cutting the deficit to 2-1 before halftime.
India restored their two-goal cushion in the third quarter when Sukhjeet Singh found the net, but Pakistan refused to go quietly. Ammad Butt scored in the 38th minute and Hannan Shahid levelled the contest in the 45th.
Waheed Rana then put Pakistan ahead in the 49th minute, completing a remarkable turnaround.
India, however, had the final say. Abhishek scored in the 60th minute to make it 4-3 and send India through.
India dominated possession at 54 percent and earned seven penalty corners, the same number as Pakistan. Both sides had two video referrals, while India received one green card and Pakistan one yellow.
Harmanpreet was the match's most prominent set-piece threat, scoring twice from eight attempts, while Abhishek converted his only shot on target. Sukhjeet also scored from his sole attempt.
India will now await the winner of the other semifinal between Malaysia and South Korea, scheduled for later on Wednesday.

title: Mark Ruffalo speaks out after Paramount Warner Bros merger approval
description: This merger will stifle creativity  weaken free speech  and cost people their jobs     Ruffalo wrote in a statement
content:
“This merger will stifle creativity, weaken free speech, and cost people their jobs,” Ruffalo wrote in a statement
Mark Ruffalo has spoken out against the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger after a US judge approved the deal, saying the agreement could affect creativity, free speech and jobs across the entertainment industry.
“This merger will stifle creativity, weaken free speech, and cost people their jobs,” Ruffalo wrote in a statement posted to Threads on Wednesday. He called the decision “an incredibly disappointing outcome” and said the movement opposing the merger would continue.
Ruffalo has been one of the most vocal Hollywood figures opposing Paramount Skydance’s proposed $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. He previously urged California Attorney General Rob Bonta and other state attorneys general not to settle an antitrust case that sought to challenge the deal.
The actor also spoke against the merger during a Senate hearing in April, arguing that greater consolidation could have consequences for film, television and news media. At the time, he pointed to potential job losses and questioned whether promises from the companies would protect workers and production.
The merger received a major legal green light on Wednesday when US District Court Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín approved a settlement involving Paramount and a coalition of 12 states led by California. The agreement includes requirements for the combined company to release at least 30 films annually in US cinemas for five years and invest an additional $300 million each year in domestic production.
The settlement also requires Paramount to negotiate certain basic cable agreements separately for the companies’ networks and establishes a board of journalists to oversee CBS News and CNN. The deal is expected to close in early October.
Ruffalo has previously faced criticism from Paramount over comments he made while opposing the merger. The company accused him of invoking antisemitic tropes in comments concerning the Ellison family and Oracle’s business ties to Israel. Ruffalo rejected the accusation, saying his criticism was directed at corporate and political actions rather than Jewish people.
George Clooney has also publicly defended Ruffalo’s right to criticise the deal. Speaking at the Venice Film Festival last month, Clooney said he was concerned about large companies consolidating and the potential effect on employment in Hollywood.
With the court approval clearing a major obstacle to the acquisition, Ruffalo’s latest comments signal that opposition to the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger will continue even as the companies move towards closing the deal.

title: Iran hails    expulsion    of US from Iraq  says it marks beginning of broader regional withdrawal
description: IRGC says US should leave the region and let its countries    peoples manage their own security
content:
IRGC says US should leave the region and let its countries’ peoples manage their own security
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Thursday hailed the “expulsion” of the US from Iraq, saying the move marks the beginning of a broader US withdrawal from the region.
In a statement marking the completion of the US withdrawal from Iraq, the IRGC said the development was “the herald of West Asia’s liberation from the yoke of the Great Satan’s domination.”
The IRGC said the US departure from Iraq was the result of the “will of the Iraqi people,” as well as "resistance and action by the Iraqi government," describing it as a “historic victory.”
It called on Washington to leave the region and “leave the management of security to the peoples of its countries.”
The statement said the US presence in Iraq “lasted for two decades” and was a “first step toward the full expulsion of American forces” from the region.
Read: US forces exit Iraq after two decades, leaving opening for Iran
On Wednesday, the US Defence Department said the US and its coalition partners “formally concluded Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq,” while the “orderly departure” of coalition forces and equipment from Erbil Air Base marked the conclusion of the military mission.
Pentagon chief spokesman Sean Parnell said the 12-year campaign “defeated ISIS as an organised military threat in Iraq and across the region.”
Baghdad and Washington agreed in September 2024 to end the coalition’s military mission in Iraq under a timetable extending through the end of September 2026, with a transition to bilateral security relations between Iraq and member states.
The coalition was formed under US leadership in 2014 after ISIS (Daesh) seized large areas of Iraq and Syria, providing Iraqi forces with air, intelligence and training support during operations against the group.
Iraq announced in December 2017 that it had regained full control of territory seized by ISIS.
American forces first invaded Iraq in 2003 to remove Saddam Hussein, and withdrew at the end of 2011.

title: Julianne Moore to receive lifetime achievement award at Rome Film Festival
description: Moore will attend the Italian premiere of    The Debut     her second film with Eisenberg
content:
Moore will attend the Italian premiere of ‘The Debut’, her second film with Eisenberg
Julianne Moore is set to receive a lifetime achievement award at the Rome Film Festival, where she will attend the Italian premiere of Jesse Eisenberg's The Debut .
The honour was announced by Salvatore Nastasi, president of Fondazione Cinema per Roma, which oversees the festival. Eisenberg, who directed and wrote The Debut , will present the award to Moore during the event.
The ceremony will form part of the festival's programme, which runs from October 13 to 25. The official Rome Film Festival programme lists The Debut as a 2026 US production directed by Eisenberg, with Moore, Paul Giamatti, Halle Bailey and Eisenberg among its cast.
In The Debut , Moore plays Mona Friedman, a middle aged New Jersey housewife who takes a small role in a community theatre production. Her involvement with the production grows increasingly intense as she becomes deeply committed to her character and clashes with the show's demanding director, played by Giamatti. The film has been presented as a comedy drama with musical elements.
The film marks Moore's second collaboration with Eisenberg after his 2022 directorial debut, When You Finish Saving the World . The Debut is Eisenberg's third feature as a director.
Moore's performance has already attracted attention during the film's festival run. The Debut screened in the official selection at the San Sebastián Film Festival, where Moore appeared alongside Eisenberg and other members of the cast.
The actress has previously received numerous major film honours, including the Academy Award for best actress for Still Alice . She has also received Oscar nominations for Boogie Nights , The End of the Affair , The Hours and Far from Heaven .
The Rome Film Festival award adds another career honour for Moore as The Debut continues its international festival screenings ahead of its wider release. The film is also scheduled for screenings at the New York Film Festival and other 2026 festivals.

title: UAE attorney general orders investigation into Flydubai flight incident
description: UAE attorney general orders investigation into Flydubai flight incident
content:
Investigation concerns FZ1073 flight bound for Tel Aviv that was diverted and landed safely in Saudi Arabia
UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi on Thursday ordered the formation of a team to investigate an incident involving a Flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv a day earlier.
The UAE’s official WAM news agency said Al Shamsi ordered the formation of an investigation team comprising specialised public prosecutors.
The team will investigate the incident involving Flydubai flight FZ1073, which was travelling from Dubai International Airport to Tel Aviv before being diverted and landing safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, WAM reported.
Al Shamsi directed the team to gather information and evidence and establish the facts, circumstances and motives surrounding the incident, including determining whether it was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose or involved prior planning or direction, according to WAM .
UAE judicial authorities have jurisdiction to investigate the incident under applicable legislation because the aircraft is registered in the UAE and flies under its flag, WAM reported.
Accordingly, UAE law applies to crimes committed aboard the aircraft even when they occur outside the country’s territory, it added.
On Wednesday, FZ1073, carrying 174 passengers from Dubai to Tel Aviv, made an emergency landing at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport in the northwestern Saudi city of Tabuk after an altercation was reported in the cockpit.
Flydubai said “an altercation occurred in the flight deck,” adding that crew members aboard the aircraft secured the plane and diverted it safely to Saudi Arabia.
Airport officials said both the captain and first officer were injured and taken to a hospital following the incident. All passengers and crew were reported safe and accounted for.
Saudi Arabia’s National Transport Safety Centre later said its safety investigation team had begun work on the incident and was coordinating with relevant authorities to determine the circumstances, examine aviation safety aspects and collect related information and evidence.
The airport said the passengers later departed Tabuk aboard an alternative aircraft provided by Flydubai.

title: Twitch faces criticism after CEO reveals that platform uses AI to check streamers for brand compatibility
description: The AI system reviews stream transcripts to assess whether content fits advertiser requirements  prompting criticism
content:
The AI system reviews stream transcripts to assess whether content fits advertiser requirements, prompting criticism
Twitch is facing criticism after CEO Dan Clancy revealed that the platform uses artificial intelligence to transcribe livestreams and assess whether content is suitable for particular advertisers.
Clancy discussed the system during the 75th episode of the Snarketing Podcast , in a video shared by reporter Zach Bussey on September 29.
Clancy explained that Twitch requires creators to classify their content according to established criteria, with those labels showing “over 99% consistency”.
CEO Dan Clancy says Twitch now uses AI to identify streamers that may not match a brand, since it now transcribes all streams for brand safety. It won't show ads on channels or content the AI believes don't match what the advertiser is trying to achieve. pic.twitter.com/aGGq9fDb7U
Advertisers can then specify the type of content they want their campaigns to appear alongside.
Twitch’s AI transcription system adds another layer by reviewing stream transcripts and identifying material that may not suit a specific brand.
Clancy said the technology can identify when “something is happening that may not match a brand”.
The disclosure prompted criticism from some Twitch users, who questioned whether AI should play a role in determining which creators are suitable for advertising.
“So now AI decides which voices are safe for ads,” an X user wrote.
Another user questioned why certain creators had not been affected, while one wrote, “But you still don't ban the people that need to be banned.”
Clancy said Twitch has invested significantly in ensuring advertisers appear alongside creators and content that meet their requirements.
“So, that's something that we've had to invest a lot in to make sure that for a brand, their content is appearing next to creators and content that fits what they're trying to achieve,” he said.
Twitch reportedly did not provide further details about the specific words, topics or behaviours that can trigger the AI-based brand suitability review.

title: K P Junior Squash Championship 2026 concludes
description: Maliha Shah  Danish Sikandar and Atif Ali Naz Crowned Champions  Qamar Zaman Graces Closing Ceremony
content:
Maliha Shah, Danish Sikandar and Atif Ali Naz Crowned Champions; Qamar Zaman Graces Closing Ceremony
The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Junior Squash Championship 2026 concluded in Peshawar Sports Complex with Maliha Shah claiming the girls’ Under-15 title, Danish Sikandar winning the boys’ Under-15 crown and Atif Ali Naz emerging champion in the boys’ Under-11 category.
Squash legend Qamar Zaman was the chief guest at the closing ceremony and distributed prizes among the players. He was accompanied by Buraq Builders Chief Executive Ali Haider Babakhel, Provincial Squash Association Secretary Finance Wazir Muhammad, senior squash coach and chief organiser Munawar Zaman, and squash coach Muhammad Waseem. In the boys’ Under-11 final, PAF’s Atif Ali Naz defeated Anas Rafai 11-9, 11-9, 12-10 to clinch the title.
In the boys’ Under-15 final, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa’s Danish Sikandar overcame PAF’s Ayan Mahboob 11-6, 11-4, 11-7 to win the championship. In the girls’ Under-15 final, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa’s Maliha Shah beat her provincial teammate Parkha Ahmad 1a1-5, 6-11, 11-9, 11-9 to secure the title.
Addressing the ceremony, Qamar Zaman said the provincial squash association has always focused on junior players.
Alongside senior events, junior competitions are organised regularly to identify new talent at the grassroots level and provide them opportunities to progress. He added that the championship offered young squash players of the province an excellent platform to showcase their skills and compete in a provincial-level competitive environment.
On the occasion, Buraq Builders CEO Ali Haider Babakhel said Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa has always produced great squash players who have brought glory to Pakistan at the international level. He announced that more squash events would be organised in future in collaboration with the provincial squash association to give young players greater opportunities to display their talent.

title: Bashir fires Pakistan to shooting bronze at Asian Games
description: Olympian also becomes the first Pakistan s male shooter to win a medal at this stage
content:
Olympian also becomes the first Pakistan's male shooter to win a medal at this stage
Ghulam Mustafa Bashir won bronze medal in the men’s 25 metres rapid-fire pistol at the Asian Games in Nagoya on Wednesday, producing a strong performance in a tense eight-man final.
Bashir finished third with a score of 22, securing Pakistan a place on the podium at the Aichi Prefecture General Shooting Gallery.
This is the first medal from Bashir in his Asian Games career and the second for Pakistan in the continental event history. Kishmala Talat had won bronze in the previous Asian Games in Hangzhou.
South Korea’s Lee Gunhyeok claimed the gold medal after scoring 32, edging China’s Su Lianbofan in the shoot-off. Su also finished on 32 but took silver after the tie-break.
Vietnam’s Pham Quang Huy finished fourth with 20 points, while Indonesia’s Suteja Dewa Putu Yadi placed fifth on 18.
South Korea’s Yoon Seoyeong was sixth with 12, followed by India’s Anish on 11 and Kazakhstan’s Nikita Chiryukin on seven.
Bashir had entered the final after finishing sixth in the second stage also on Thursday with 578 points, including 19 inner tens.
He was among the eight shooters who advanced from the qualifying round.
Lee’s victory also saw him equal the Asian record of 32 in the final, while the competition featured several of Asia’s leading rapid-fire pistol shooters. Bashir had finished eighth in the first stage on Wednesday.

Clover Boys dispute has escalated after private DMs were shared online amid claims of unanswered messages

The messages showed Reggie asking to meet Cenat and speak to him “as a brother”.
He later attempted to contact Cenat on September 25, asking him to answer an important phone call and describing the situation as “like cry for help”.
The screenshots do not establish why Cenat did not respond to the later messages or whether circumstances prevented him from doing so.
Reggie also made other claims concerning members of the Clover Boys circle, including allegations about Cenat’s relationships with other creators.
According to reports, no evidence supporting some of those allegations had been made public, while Cenat had not directly addressed them.
The controversy also involved streamer RaKai after Reggie made an allegation concerning his childhood. RaKai rejected the claim, stating that he had never been “touched in any way growing up”.

title: PM Shehbaz says private sector must lead Pakistan’s economic growth | The Express Tribune
description: Says sectors subsidised since 1960s failed to boost exports; prices rose, while quality, import substitution suffered
content:
Says sectors subsidised since 1960s failed to boost exports; prices rose, while quality, import substitution suffered
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday questioned the performance of industries that have received subsidies for decades without delivering a significant increase in exports, urging the private sector to take the lead in driving economic growth.
Addressing a gong-ringing ceremony for the listing of Naya Nazimabad Apartments REIT at the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX), the prime minister said incentives provided to the construction industry in the budget were beginning to produce results, with growth also being witnessed in Karachi’s construction sector.
He said several industrial sectors had received subsidies since the 1960s but had failed to deliver a significant increase in exports. “Instead, the prices of goods increased, quality and productivity were affected, while import substitution could not be achieved,” he said.
“This is a bitter reality that cannot be corrected without moving forward,” he said, urging exporters to play an effective role in achieving export-led sustainable economic growth.
PM Shehbaz said he had held meetings with prominent bankers during his recent visits to the United States and the United Kingdom, adding that they had appreciated the government’s reform efforts.
He said the International Monetary Fund (IMF) chief had told him that “this is a new Pakistan”, to which he replied: “This is not a new Pakistan, it is a new team.”
“We have to show export-based growth in our economy,” he said.
The prime minister said the budget had provided tax breaks worth Rs2.3 trillion and congratulated the Naya Nazimabad and Lahore projects. “In this entire scenario, there is no parallel to the efforts of the Chief of Defence Forces and the Chief of Army Staff, Field Marshal Asim Munir,” he said.
Read: Response to fixed tax unsatisfactory
He also thanked the chairman of the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) for recovering land worth trillions of rupees and said Pakistan had achieved major successes in the issuance of Eurobonds.
The State Bank’s foreign exchange reserves had reached $21.4 billion, while remittances were showing significant growth, he said.
The government had also provided tax incentives to support industrial development, while the PSX had made significant progress, he said, adding that further reforms were needed in light of developments in other markets in the region.
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, addressing the same ceremony, said economic growth would reach 4 per cent in 2027, compared with 3.7 per cent recorded last year.
The finance minister said the government could raise the growth rate to 6 per cent in the short term through a consumption-led growth model, but doing so would disrupt the balance of payments and push the economy back into a boom-and-bust cycle.
Instead, the government was pursuing an export-led sustainable economic growth model, under which the economy would achieve 4 per cent growth this year, he said.
The finance minister said the number of tax filers had increased by 45 per cent to more than 5.7 million this year, compared with 3.9 million last year. The government was also working on reforms and tax-related issues to increase activity in the capital market, he said.
Aurangzeb said Rs60 billion had been released under the Prime Minister’s Apna Ghar Programme, while the banking industry had approved Rs340 billion under the scheme.
“The real issue is no longer the issuance of loans. The banking industry has taken the step; now the supply side has to take the step,” he said. He added that Arif Habib and the Association of Builders and Developers (ABAD) had to play their role in this regard, while real estate investment trusts (REITs) would act as a bridge.
Read more: No more war impact, govt tells IMF
The finance minister recalled that he had first visited the PSX on March 29, 2024, when the KSE-100 Index stood at 67,000 points, compared with 170,000 points at the time of his address.
“The factors behind the 100 Index are important,” he said. He said 11 initial public offerings (IPOs) had taken place this year, the highest number recorded in the past 20 years.
Investor participation had more than doubled over the past two and a half years, while Gen Z and millennials had accounted for 85 per cent of stock market participation over the preceding 12 months, he said.
Aurangzeb said fiscal stability was a fundamental requirement for economic growth and that, for the first time, investors from Türkiye had shown interest in the privatisation of distribution companies.
“Questions are raised about foreign direct investment, but these matters require time,” he said.
The finance minister stated that the economy had contracted three years earlier and stressed that the government’s role was to provide the private sector with a conducive business environment. “The private sector has to lead,” he said.
“Questions are asked whether this is the government’s job? This is absolutely the government’s job, and we will continue to do it,” he said.
He said the government’s first priority was to make macroeconomic stability sustainable and end the boom-and-bust cycle. “Instead of achieving growth through the injection of liquidity, we have to focus on sustainable growth because once the economy enters a downturn, it is extremely difficult to revive it,” he said.
The finance minister said the achievement of tax targets also needed to be highlighted rather than focusing only on instances when targets were lowered.
“We now have to step into the new economy,” he said. “The new economy is not just crypto; it has other implications as well. We can lead this global service,” he added.
The minister concluded that the government was seeking to expand the bond market to the retail market, while the Capital Markets Development Council was preparing recommendations to present to the prime minister.
Naya Nazimabad Chairman Arif Habib, also at the same event, said 12 new REIT companies would be listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) in the near future, while four REIT companies were currently listed.
He said REIT companies were required to obtain a listing on the PSX within three years of registration. He was speaking at the gong ceremony marking the listing of the Naya Nazimabad Apartment REIT at the Pakistan Stock Exchange on Thursday.
Habib said several economic indicators were at record highs, including remittances and the State Bank of Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves. “There is a need to celebrate this positive change in the economy,” he said.
He thanked the prime minister for attending the celebration despite travelling a long distance. “The purpose of this ceremony is to celebrate Pakistan’s achievements,” he said.
“Looking at the numbers, it seems Pakistan is not being marketed properly,” Habib said, adding that the issuance of Eurobonds reflected international confidence in the country.
He said Pakistan was still being valued at a discount compared with the rest of the world, while its dividend yield of 5.4 per cent was the best in the region. Companies were earning good profits despite high taxes, he added.
Pakistan’s credit rating had improved according to Moody’s and Fitch, he said. “We have succeeded in keeping the current account balanced and there has been a record increase in remittances,” he added.
The Federal Board of Revenue had achieved its target in the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, while $14 billion had come into Pakistan through Roshan Digital Accounts, of which $8 billion had been utilised in Pakistan, Habib said.
“This indicates that Pakistan is emerging. We need to market Pakistan,” he said.
He said the Pakistan Stock Exchange had delivered a 58 per cent return over the past three years and Pakistan was trading at a 35 per cent discount to frontier markets. “In terms of dividend yield, the Pakistan Stock Exchange is leading the region at 5.4 per cent,” he added.
Habib said company profits had increased despite high tax rates.
He said Dubai had been well known for attracting capital outflows related to construction. Naya Nazimabad had been Pakistan’s best-performing project over the past 10 years, he claimed.
“Over the past 10 years, Dubai’s return was 4 per cent while Pakistan’s was 17 per cent. Over the past three years, Pakistan has outperformed Dubai,” he said.
He said his organisation had been promoting REITs since 2015 and had registered 16 REITs worth $630 million. “REITs have contributed to growth in employment, the construction sector, allied industries and tax collection,” Habib said.
He said the prime minister’s Apna Ghar programme was successfully achieving its targets. Land owned by port authorities and Pakistan Railways could also be utilised for REITs, he added.
