title: Security guard killed as under construction bridge structure collapses in Gulshan e Iqbal
description: Bridge structure was part of the Bus Rapid Transit  BRT  project
content:
Bridge structure was part of the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) project
An under-construction bridge structure on Thursday that was part of the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) project collapsed near Bait-ul-Mukarram Mosque in Karachi’s Gulshan-e-Iqbal area, killing a security guard.
The deceased was deployed at the construction site. His identity has yet to be ascertained. The body was shifted to a hospital for medico-legal formalities.
The rescue operation was completed and rescue teams subsequently left the site.
The road from Civic Centre towards NIPA has been temporarily closed to traffic due to debris from the collapsed structure and repair work at the site.
The Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) has begun work on a section of the BRT Red Line project. After the contractor for Lot 2- from Mosamiyat to Hasan Square- was stopped from working and their office was sealed, this portion of the project was handed over to FWO, who deployed machinery and staff at the site.
In the first phase, the FWO will repair the roads connected to the BRT project that are currently in the use as alternative routes for traffic. The organisation has also placed banners and panaflex signs along the Mosamiyat to Hasan Square section, apologising to the public for the inconvenience caused by the construction work.
While FWO is carrying out construction, drug addicts are reportedly damaging the project in broad daylight. Carrying bags on their shoulders, these individuals appear to be waste pickers, but in reality, they are cutting and stealing iron and wiring used in the project.
In the past, security guards were deployed to prevent such thefts, and it is expected that FWO would devise an effective strategy to curb these incidents.
The Red Line project, one of the largest development schemes in Karachi's history, had turned into a major hardship for commuters. A team from The Express Tribune visited the stretch from Numaish Chowrangi to Mosamiyat and observed active construction work for the first time in over four and a half years.
Heavy machinery and a large workforce were seen operating simultaneously at multiple points. At New MA Jinnah Road, construction activity was visible with machinery and labour working side by side. Near New Town police station, road leveling was underway using heavy equipment, while workers were engaged in clearing debris.
Cement barriers that were previously scattered across different points, causing traffic disruption, were also being removed and repositioned, improving traffic flow. Similar activity was observed near Bait-ul-Mukarram Mosque, Mazaar-e-Quaid vicinity, and at Nipa Chowrangi, where drainage work was underway. Other sections of the route also showed visible construction progress.
The 24-kilometre-long Red Line project on University Road began in 2022 and was originally scheduled for completion in 2024. However, it faced repeated delays, negligence, and mismanagement, leaving the project stalled for years.
Speaking to The Express Tribune , citizens expressed hope that with work restarting, the project would now be completed within the promised timeframe.
University Road project to be completed within two months
Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon said on Sunday , while speaking to the media, that work on University Road was nearing completion, announcing that the entire project would be completed within two months. “Now we can say University Road has been built.”
Sharjeel announced while inaugurating the Mosamiyat Flyover, a key component of the Red Line BRT project. Sindh Minister Saeed Ghani and Karachi Deputy Mayor Salman Abdullah Murad were also present at the inauguration.
Memon said work on University Road had reached the final stages and that the difficulties faced by commuters had largely been overcome. He said the Sindh government was working round the clock for Karachi’s development, with different departments engaged in infrastructure and other development projects across the city.
“Those who say that no work is being done in Karachi, I want to tell them that work is taking place,” he said. The senior minister said Karachi’s size brought challenges on an equally large scale, but maintained that the city was also home to the country’s best healthcare system.
On the Red Line project, Sharjeel said the Mosamiyat Flyover was an important part of the corridor and would soon be available for public use after the necessary formalities. Work on stations and other components of the BRT was also progressing, he added.
He acknowledged the delay in the project and apologised to the residents, saying several issues had contributed to the delays. Despite increases in the cost of the dollar, cement and petrol, he said, work had continued.

title: Jim Carrey marries longtime partner Min Ah in private ceremony in Los Angeles
description: The 64 year old actor and Ah  who were first photographed together in 2022  have kept their relationship private
content:
The 64-year-old actor and Ah, who were first photographed together in 2022, have kept their relationship private
Jim Carrey has married his girlfriend Min Ah in a private ceremony in Los Angeles, according to the actor’s representative.
The 64-year-old Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind star and Ah have kept much of their relationship away from the public eye, although they were first photographed together in 2022.
The couple made their public debut at the César Awards in Paris on February 26, where Carrey was accompanied by his adult daughter, Jane, and Ah’s teenage son, Jackson.
During his honorary award speech, Carrey thanked Ah in French.
“Thank you to my wonderful family, my daughter Jane, and my grandson Jackson. I love you now and forever,” Carrey said through translation. “Thank you to my sublime companion, Min Ah,” he added in French. “I love you, Min Ah.”
Carrey has previously been married twice.
He married Melissa Womer in 1987, and they share daughter Jane, before divorcing in 1995.
He married his Dumb and Dumber co-star Lauren Holly in 1996, but the marriage ended the following year.
The actor has also previously dated Jenny McCarthy, Renée Zellweger, Linda Ronstadt and January Jones.
Carrey had previously suggested that he did not expect to marry again.
In a 2014 interview with Howard Stern , he said, “I just don’t see it as necessary, at this point.”
His marriage to Ah marks a change from that earlier position.

title: Trump will not win this year s Nobel Peace Prize  but he may influence who does  say experts
description: Trump will not win this year s Nobel Peace Prize  but he may influence who does  say experts
content:
This year, the five-strong body will be mindful of ​picking someone who can withstand pressure from Trump.
US President Donald Trump will not win ​this year's Nobel Peace Prize as he wages war with Iran , but his influence will still be felt by the awarding body ‌that picks the laureate, according to experts.
Last year's award, to Venezuela's Maria Corina Machado, was unique in the prize's 125-year history, coming amid repeated lobbying by Trump to get the award. Weeks later, Machado gave her gold Nobel medal to Trump, in a bid to win support for her efforts for a democratic Venezuela.
This year, the five-strong body will be mindful of ​picking someone who can withstand pressure from Trump, according to Haakon Gjerloew, acting director of the Peace Research Institute Oslo.
"I think last ​year's events around the Nobel Peace Prize, Maria Corina Machado giving it to Trump afterwards, will affect some of ⁠the considerations that they make," he told Reuters .
"One worry the committee might have is whether awarding it to someone could put them under pressure from ​Donald Trump ... I think the committee will consider whether the award does more harm than good."
That could mean an award to Pope Leo, the International Criminal Court, the International ​Court of Justice or Francesca Albanese, the UN special rapporteur on the Occupied Palestinian Territories, experts say. The announcement is on October 9.

title: Pakistan down Hong Kong to move into men   s team squash final
description: Noor Zaman  Ashab Irfan and Nasir Iqbal combine to seal a 2 1 semi final win after Pakistan recover from early setback
content:
Noor Zaman, Ashab Irfan and Nasir Iqbal combine to seal a 2-1 semi-final win after Pakistan recover from early setback
Pakistan fought back from an early defeat to beat Hong Kong 2-1 on Thursday and reach the men’s squash team event final at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya.
Noor Zaman, Pakistan’s top-ranked player, suffered a setback in the opening match against Kwan Tsz Lau, losing 3-1 after taking the first game 12-10.
Kwan responded strongly to win the next three games 11-3, 11-6 and 11-5, putting Hong Kong within one victory of the final.
Ashab Irfan restored parity for Pakistan with a straight games victory over Henry Chi Hin Leung. Irfan controlled the contest to win 11-5, 13-11, 11-7 and level the tie at 1-1.
The decisive match went the way of experienced Pakistan campaigner Nasir Iqbal, who produced a composed performance against Nam Cheuk Lai.
Iqbal lost a closely fought opening game 12-10 but recovered immediately, taking the next three 11-3, 11-9 and 14-12 to complete a 3-1 victory and send Pakistan into the final.
The result extended Pakistan’s run after they defeated South Korea 2-0 in Wednesday’s quarter-final. Pakistan will play the winners of the second semi-final between India and Malaysia in Friday’s final.
The victory underlined Pakistan’s depth in the team competition, with Irfan and Iqbal responding decisively after Zaman’s defeat had left their side facing elimination.
For Pakistan, the final will provide another opportunity to challenge for a team gold medal, with the trio now one victory away from the title.
Hong Kong, meanwhile, were unable to capitalise on their early advantage as Pakistan won both remaining matches under pressure to complete the comeback.

title: SHC seeks cabinet record over enforcement of UN rules on used vehicle imports
description: The bench directs that details of the meeting be provided within four weeks
content:
The bench directs that details of the meeting be provided within four weeks
Sindh High Court’s (SHC) Constitutional Bench has sought details of a federal cabinet meeting within four weeks while hearing a petition challenging the alleged failure to enforce United Nations regulations on imported used vehicles.
The petition, filed by a local automobile manufacturer, names the federal ministries of Industries and Production and Commerce, the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), the Engineering Development Board (EDB) and other relevant authorities as respondents.
During the hearing, the federal government’s counsel informed the court that the cabinet had already held a meeting on the matter. The bench directed the lawyer to submit details of the meeting within four weeks. The petitioner’s counsel argued that the import of used vehicles was subject to compliance with prescribed safety, environmental and quality standards, including applicable United Nations regulations.
The counsel said the EDB had issued a notification in 2025 introducing a two-stage inspection mechanism covering 62 UN regulations. The system required pre-shipment inspection and independent third-party inspection after vehicles arrived in Pakistan.
However, the petitioner alleged that registered inspection agencies were checking only general requirements rather than verifying compliance with all 62 regulations based on vehicles’ actual condition. The petition further maintained that documents accompanying imported used vehicles did not establish their compliance with prescribed safety standards at the time of import. Referring to the FBR, the counsel said the tax authority had also highlighted ambiguities in pre- and post-shipment inspection requirements in March 2026.
The petitioner argued that local automobile manufacturers were required to comply continuously with the 62 UN regulations, while an equivalent mechanism for imported used vehicles was not being effectively enforced. The petition seeks mandatory inspections before shipment and after arrival, before customs clearance, to ensure imported vehicles meet applicable standards.

Pete Davidson has spoken out in defence of his former fiancée Ariana Grande, while also reflecting on his past relationship with Kim Kardashian and the ongoing public interest in his dating history.

“She’ll be OK,” the 32-year-old said. “But I think it’s f**ked up.”
Despite their brief relationship and engagement in 2018, Davidson said there is no animosity between the former couple. “I think Ariana’s f**kin’ cool and immensely talented and an awesome girl,” he said. “We’re not texting or whatever, but we’re cool.”
Davidson also discussed the attention surrounding his dating history, which has included several high-profile relationships.
“It’s been over a decade,” he said, arguing that his professional work and relevance are often overlooked because of the focus on his personal life.

title: Trump says co pilot in Flydubai incident may have been a  terrorist  or  whack job
description: US president also recounts Netanyahu   s explanation of how plumber knows what to do in emergency
content:
US president also recounts Netanyahu’s explanation of how plumber knows what to do in emergency
US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that he spoke at length with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu about an incident aboard a Flydubai passenger aircraft, adding that the co-pilot may have been either a terrorist or an individual acting irrationally.
“I think it’s an incredible story,” he told reporters at the White House when asked about the incident.
Trump said Netanyahu had briefed him on the events aboard the flight, which was traveling from Dubai to Tel Aviv.
“I did speak to Bibi Netanyahu at length about this event,” he said. “And it seems as though the co-pilot was perhaps a terrorist, or perhaps a whack-job, and he stabbed the pilot.”
Trump then recounted the account he had received from Netanyahu involving an Israeli plumber who he said had no experience flying an aircraft but intervened after hearing a disturbance in the cockpit.
According to Trump’s account, the plumber realised something was wrong after hearing screaming and seeing what was happening in the flight deck.
“Having never flown a plane, he took the stick, lifted it up, and leveled out the plane before it crashed,” he said.
Trump acknowledged that he could not independently confirm the details of the account.
Read: Two pilots wounded after fight on Israel-bound flight forces emergency landing
“Now this is the story that I heard. I don’t know if it’s true, but that’s the story that I got from BB,” he said, referring to Netanyahu.
Trump also recounted Netanyahu’s explanation for how the plumber knew what to do in an emergency.
“When asked why he did that, he said, ‘He watches that show Air Disasters,’” Trump said.
Trump described the television program as “the craziest show” and said Netanyahu told him the passenger watched it frequently and learned from the program “sort of how to fly.”
The comments came after reports of a confrontation between the pilots of a passenger aircraft operating from Dubai to Tel Aviv. According to the reports, the incident triggered a hijacking code before the aircraft ultimately landed in Saudi Arabia.
Flydubai has said the circumstances and motives behind the altercation remain unknown and are the subject of a formal investigation.

title: Fury  Joshua kick off  battle of Britain  in good spirits
description: The British rivals trade friendly jokes and praise ahead of their December 11 showdown in Cardiff
content:
The British rivals trade friendly jokes and praise ahead of their December 11 showdown in Cardiff
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua were all smiles as they kicked off the countdown to their much-anticipated heavyweight showdown at a pre-fight press conference in London.
The British two-time world champions will finally lock horns in Cardiff on December 11 after years of false starts and barbs at each other.
Those expecting fireworks as the two shared a stage in front of a crowd of 1,000 fans were left disappointed as both showed respect for their adversary's career.
Fury invited Joshua to join him for a "pint of Guinness" once they had finished in the ring, while the 2012 Olympic gold medallist ended a face-to-face exchange by tickling Fury in the midriff.
The vacant WBA super heavyweight title is expected to be on the line and Fury hit back at criticism that the pair are only coming together well past their peak.
"People say this fight is too late," said the self-styled "Gypsy King".
"It's the icing on the cake for two great careers when we throw down in front of 80,000 people. May the best man win."
The fight appeared destined for Saudi Arabia or the United States during the early stages of negotiations but Joshua believes the chance to face off on British soil will "inspire a generation".
"I'm really grateful for this opportunity and bringing it to Great Britain because I know people in pubs have had proper fights about who will win and family members have fallen out," he said.
"We'll inspire this generation and the next generation. It was people from this country supporting us. I'm fulfilling my destiny before I depart this world."
Fury has won 36 of his 39 fights and held the WBC, WBO and IBF heavyweight belts during his colourful career, with his only defeats coming against Oleksandr Usyk in world title bouts in 2024.
Joshua has 30 wins from 34 fights, holding the WBO and IBF titles at various stages before a pair of losses to Usyk in 2021 and 2022.

title: From textile engineering to cockpit hero  Indian pilot wins praise after flydubai drama
description: Pilot says when I get out of cockpit or aircraft  I don t want other guy to    know that    I m a pilot
content:
Pilot says when I get out of cockpit or aircraft, I don't want other guy to ⁠know that ​I'm a pilot
For Indian ​pilot Smit Machchhar, hailed as a hero for averting a crash of a flydubai jet bound for Israel, aviation was never ‌part of his childhood dreams.
Machchhar had his sights set on the family's textile business until the aviation bug bit at the age of 19, which scared his mother.
Now, even after thousands of hours of flying, Machchhar's love of aviation is something he keeps in the cockpit, reluctant to discuss with those on the ground.
"Captain Smit ​Machchhar is a HERO," Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on X. "In the face of the gravest danger and despite being ​seriously injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others."
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin ⁠Netanyahu called him a "true hero".
Machchhar is recovering in a hospital in Saudi Arabia's Tabuk, where his flight was diverted on Wednesday after the co-pilot reportedly ​stabbed him mid-air in an attempt to crash the plane carrying 174 people, according to Israeli officials.
The Mumbai native was covered in blood on the cockpit ​floor when he managed to activate the release to open the cockpit door, according to Israeli officials. This allowed passengers and crew to overpower the co-pilot, while two flydubai pilots travelling as passengers helped land the aircraft.
The veteran Boeing 737 captain, who has logged nearly 9,750 flying hours over a career spanning about 15 years, arrived in ​aviation relatively late.
Read: Pilot on Tel Aviv-bound flight tried to crash plane
"Unlike a lot of other aviators right now, aviation was not a childhood dream," Machchhar said in an interview in 2025 on ​a YouTube channel hosted by Zalak Mehta. "It came along much later in my life."
Machchhar, seen in the interview and in social media pictures with a neatly trimmed ‌beard, worked ⁠with Indian commercial airline SpiceJet for more than a decade before joining flydubai in 2022, his LinkedIn profile says.
Once out of aircraft, don't talk aviation
After school, he enrolled in a textile engineering course with the aim of continuing the family's business before pursuing management studies at Mumbai's Welingkar Institute of Management.
It was there, at an aviation seminar, that he discovered flying when he was about 19 years old.
"That's where the aviation bug ... really ​found me," he said, adding that ​his mother was initially scared ⁠of the career choice.
Machchhar later trained in New Zealand before joining SpiceJet, where he rose through the ranks to become a line training captain responsible for mentoring younger pilots. He spent 11 years with SpiceJet and ​the past four years with flydubai.
In his career, he recalled having to divert flights for medical emergencies ​and delay departures over ⁠seemingly minor technical issues.
"Delay is not my problem. As long as you're walking out of the aircraft is what I want," he said.
He has also spoken about keeping aviation separate from his personal life.
"When I get out of the cockpit or the aircraft, I don't want the other guy to ⁠know that ​I'm a pilot," he said. "I don't want to discuss aviation. When I wear the uniform, ​then no nonsense and just do your job, finish the job. When you walk out of the cockpit, that's it. Stop thinking about that. Someone else needs you now. ​The kids are there. They want to play with you."

title: Swiss FA withdraws support for FIFA chief Infantino
description: Infantino remains the only declared candidate ahead of the November 18 nomination deadline
content:
Infantino remains the only declared candidate ahead of the November 18 nomination deadline
The Swiss Football Association (SFV) announced Wednesday it was withdrawing its support for beleaguered incumbent Gianni Infantino in next year's FIFA presidential election.
Several leading European national associations have pulled their support for Infantino, after he caused uproar in July with proposals to create a commercial subsidiary to run FIFA's biggest events, such as the World Cup and Club World Cup.
The SFV's decision carries weight as Infantino is Swiss, and both FIFA and European football's governing body UEFA are based in Switzerland.
The SFV said its executive board met on Friday and "decided to withdraw the support it had declared in June 2026 for Gianni Infantino's candidacy for a further term as FIFA president".
Infantino's plan would have allowed private investors to acquire stakes in a company created under the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) initiative. The backlash that followed led to the proposals being quickly shelved.
The SFV said events in recent months raised fundamental questions over leadership, governance, transparency and decision-making processes with world football's governing body.
It cited Infantino's FFE plans and the lifting of red-carded United States forward Folarin Balogun's one-match suspension during this year's World Cup, following a phone call to Infantino from US President Donald Trump.
SFV president Peter Knabel said that Swiss football's governing body expected FIFA's leadership to uphold the highest standards of transparency, accountability and institutional responsibility.
He said Infantino's proposals last week for "a consultation" with national federations to reform FIFA's governance sent an important signal, and could contribute to improving the situation.
However, "key questions regarding the background, responsibilities and decision-making processes remain unanswered", said Knabel.
"As these have not been convincingly clarified, we cannot justify continuing to support Gianni Infantino's candidacy."
UEFA -- the regional federation that represents World Cup holders Spain and football powerhouses such as France, England and Germany -- is leading the opposition to Infantino, calling openly for his removal.
The SFV, a UEFA member, insisted its decision did not signal a move away from constructive cooperation within FIFA and the global football community.
As the association for the country where FIFA and UEFA are based, "the SFV is aware of its special responsibility and will continue to champion transparency, credible and reliable structure, rules-based decision-making processes", it said.
It called for a strong and united global football community characterised by integrity.
Infantino retains the support of 2034 World Cup hosts Saudi Arabia, while African football's governing body CAF and South America's CONMEBOL are also supportive.
Candidate nominations for next March's FIFA election must be submitted by November 18. Infantino is the only candidate so far.

title: PM Shehbaz to consult president  ministers over K P political  security situation
description: Federal government has been considering different constitutional  legal options
content:
Centre considering different constitutional and legal options, including imposition of governor's rule and emergency
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is expected to consult President Asif Ali Zardari and senior ministers on Thursday over the political and security situation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), with constitutional options including governor’s rule and emergency measures remaining under discussion amid heightened tensions between the Centre and the provincial government.
Sources said today’s consultations would focus on developments in K-P and the constitutional and legal options available to the federal government.
According to the sources, PM Shehbaz had summoned Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Kashmir Affairs Minister Amir Muqam to the Prime Minister’s House, where they would discuss the province’s political and security affairs in detail.
A meeting between the prime minister and president is also expected at the President’s House later on Thursday, sources said.
PM Shehbaz is expected to brief the president on the situation in K-P and discuss possible constitutional measures, including governor’s rule and an emergency.
Read: Govt 'seriously' considering imposing emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa: Tariq Fazal
The developments emerged amid continued tensions following PTI's announcement of an Islamabad march. Although the protest was postponed from September 27 to October 4, the standoff between the federal and provincial governments remains unresolved.
Reports have also emerged about the possible disqualification of the chief minister, his replacement, an in-house change, dissolution of the assembly, and a no-confidence motion against him under Article 136 of the Constitution.
The no-confidence motion can be submitted to the assembly secretariat with signatures of 20% of the total membership, following which an assembly session is to be convened within three to seven days on a single-point agenda.
The assembly rules lay down the procedure for a no-confidence motion. After the motion is moved in the house, voting is held through a secret ballot, with members expressing their choice in two separate lobbies. If the motion succeeds, the Speaker will issue a schedule for the election of a new chief minister.
Also Read: Centre lays ground for governor's rule in K-P
The Constitution also provides for the governor to require the chief minister to seek a vote of confidence under Article 130(7). If the governor believes the chief minister has lost the confidence of the majority in the house, the chief minister is required to demonstrate his numerical strength in the assembly.
The political confrontation between the PTI-led K-P government and the federal government has unfolded against one of the province’s deadliest recent spells of violence. At least 21 people, including 15 police personnel, were killed in the September 18 Kohat Police Lines attack, which was followed days later by an IED attack on a security convoy in K-P that killed six soldiers .
On September 25, a CTD operation in Peshawar foiled an attempted attack by three suicide bombers , although a police constable was killed. The following day, 12 people were killed and 35 injured in a blast at a joint checkpoint in Dera Ismail Khan, with the TTP claiming responsibility.

title: Six terrorists killed in Balochistan s Kachhi  state media
description: Terrorists were targeted using quadcopters  large quantity of weapons and ammunition was recovered from those killed
content:
Terrorists were targeted using quadcopters, large quantity of weapons and ammunition was recovered from those killed
Six terrorists were killed in an Intelligence-Based Operation (IBO) in the Sanni area of Kachhi district, Balochistan, state-run Radio Pakistan reported on Thursday, citing security sources.
The operation was carried out under Operation Radd-ul-Fitna 3 against Fitna al-Hindustan , according to the sources.
The federal government last year officially designated all terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as Fitna al-Hindustan , accusing India of sponsoring a proxy war through the outfits.
The terrorists were successfully targeted using quadcopters, while a large quantity of weapons and ammunition was recovered from those killed, Radio Pakistan said. A clearance operation was underway in the area to eliminate any remaining terrorists.
Sources said that security forces remained committed to eliminating terrorism across the country under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision.
Six terrorists have been killed in an intelligence-based operation by security forces in #Sanni area of #Kachhi district, #Balochistan @OfficialDGISPR #RadioPakistan #News https://t.co/4X7WOxwuSw pic.twitter.com/Vhz4FWGQ5g
Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terrorist activity over the past three months, with a series of attacks across the country resulting in the martyrdom of security personnel and civilians.
On September 28, security forces killed two terrorists belonging to the banned Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in the Nokcha area of Balochistan. The sources said the two men had set an empty water bowser on fire before attempting to flee, prompting security forces to launch a chase that ended in an exchange of fire. They were also accused of involvement in arson attacks at different locations along the N-40 Quetta-Taftan highway.
The incident followed a major security operation along the N-40 highway on August 31, during which 11 terrorists were killed after armed men allegedly set up an illegal checkpoint in Chagai district to disrupt traffic and extort commuters.
On September 19, 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred in a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, the Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
Read : Nine policemen martyred, 28 injured in terror attack on police checkpost in K-P's Hangu
In a separate incident, a captain and a lieutenant were among six security personnel martyred in an exchange of fire in Hangu district, while eight terrorists were killed.
On September 1, six personnel, including two officers, and a customs department official were martyred as security forces thwarted an attempt to breach the Customs House in Balochistan.
In July, at least 30 people , including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. The attackers also abducted several civilians and police personnel after the assault.
In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation , which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

title: Man City scandal risks damage to Premier League s booming brand
description: The club could face possible points deductions  title stripping or even expulsion
content:
The club could face possible points deductions, title stripping or even expulsion
The Premier League has won a lengthy legal battle with Manchester City over financial impropriety, but the consequences could leave lasting damage for a league that has long since become the envy of world football.
City face severe sanctions after being found guilty of over 100 charges between 2009 and 2018, with an independent commission exposing "sham" contracts to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion).
A hefty points deduction resulting in relegation, stripped titles and even expulsion from the English top flight have been mooted as potential sanctions.
But the damage may not be limited to City alone with an entire era of the Premier League now under a cloud.
A takeover in 2008 by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan, the vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, transformed City's fortunes, but also the face of the Premier League.
The club's first top-flight league title for 44 years was one of the most iconic moments in Premier League history when Sergio Aguero netted the winner against QPR in the 94th minute to deny Manchester United the title.
Some of City's rivals have been quick to revel in their downfall.
"Another Premier League medal to be added to the cabinet," posted former Manchester United defender Rio Ferdinand, who was part of the United team that finished second to City in the 2011/12 season.
Yet there could be more lingering collective consequences for a league that has become accustomed to flexing its financial muscle to hoover up the best talent from around the globe.
Italy's Serie A once enjoyed that status in the 1990s.
Although it had lost some of its lustre by the time the Calciopoli scandal came about in 2006, Italian football has arguably never fully recovered in the two decades since.
That case surrounded club officials influencing which referees would officiate their games and led to Juventus being stripped of two titles and relegated to Serie B.
The question is now whether fans will be turned away from the Premier League after feeling cheated over what they have witnessed over the past 18 years.
In total City have won eight titles in the last 15 seasons.
They rewrote the record books, becoming the first side to ever achieve 100 points and win the English top flight for four consecutive years.
All of those achievements are now labelled with an asterisk.
"If I was a player, I'd be 100 percent sticking those medals in the bin. Of course you would, it's cheating," said former Manchester United captain Roy Keane.
Despite the Premier League's spending power, English clubs have still struggled to keep the world's biggest superstars away from Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain.
City's demise could also see the Premier League lose its marquee player in Erling Haaland.
"The Premier League is Britain's greatest soft power cultural asset," Simon Chadwick, professor of Afro-Eurasian sport, told AFP. "What happens when people start to question, 'what have I been watching all these years?'"
By contrast, the Premier League has argued the City case is proof of strong governance.
The league pursued and persisted with an investigation which began in 2018 despite City's best attempts to frustrate the process.
"This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history," said the league's chief executive Richard Masters.
"It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition.
"It is paramount that the league remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously."

title: China s Mu first woman to win eSports Games gold
description: She helps beat Japan in the survival game    Identity V    to win gold
content:
She helps beat Japan in the survival game ‘Identity V’ to win gold
Mu Xinyue called it "the happiest moment of my life" after she became the first woman to win an Asian Games gold medal in eSports.
The 20-year-old played a pivotal role as China beat hosts Japan to win the final of horror survival game "Identity V" in Nagoya.
"When the national anthem was played and the gold medal was around my neck, I was so excited and happy," Xinhua news agency quoted her as saying.
"I think this may be the happiest moment of my life."
Mu is the only woman in China's 23-strong eSports squad at the Games.
Competitive gaming remains dominated by men.
At Asia's biggest sporting spectacular there are 534 eSports competitors.
Just 14 of them, or less than three percent, are women.
For South Korea, another gaming heavyweight, Park So-yeon became the first woman to represent their national team when she competed in Nagoya.
Following her landmark gold medal on Wednesday, Mu said the only thing that mattered was ability.
"As the first female player to win the gold medal I don't think gender is something that should define us or be used as a benchmark," she said.
"I think that whether you're a man or a woman, everyone needs to have enough ability to compete at this level.
"I think every player who makes it here has earned their place through their own ability."
Competitive gaming made its full debut at the Asian Games in Hangzhou three years ago.

title: West Indies pile up record 405 7 in second ODI against India
description: Campbell  Hope and Jangoo hit centuries
content:
Opener John Campbell hit 101 to lay the foundations for West Indies' highest-ever one-day international total of 405-7 against India in their second match on Wednesday.
Skipper Shai Hope (104) and Amir Jangoo (114) also struck centuries to boost the total as West Indies look to bounce back in the three-match series, led by India 1-0, in Guwahati.
Invited to bat first, West Indies lost Keacy Carter for nine before Campbell and Hope put on 110 runs to set the tone for the batting domination.
West Indies' previous ODI best was 389 against England in 2019, but they ended up losing the match.
Campbell reached his second ODI hundred but in the next over fell to pace bowler Gurnoor Brar after the opener hit nine fours and five sixes in 68-ball knock.
Hope and left-handed Jangoo put on 182 runs for the third wicket as the pair hammered the opposition attack with regular boundaries on a batting-friendly pitch.
Hope, a wicketkeeper-batter, raised his 20th ODI ton to go past West Indies legend Brian Lara's 19 hundreds.
Chris Gayle has the most ODI centuries for West Indies with 25 tons.
Jangoo reached his second ODI hundred off 70 balls, leaping up and punching the air in delight.
West Indies lost three quick wickets including Hope, Sherfane Rutherford -- out for a first-ball duck -- and then Jangoo, dismissed by Ravindra Jadeja.
Left-arm wrist spinner Kuldeep Yadav struck twice to reach 200 ODI wickets before Roston Chase with his unbeaten 29 took West Indies past 400.
India will need a record chase, one surpassing their ODI best of 362 against Australia in Jaipur in 2013.

title: Djokovic grinds out opening round win at China Open
description: The Serbian battles through a tight second set to beat Borges 6 3  7 6  7 2  in his Beijing return
content:
The Serbian battles through a tight second set to beat Borges 6-3, 7-6 (7/2) in his Beijing return
Novak Djokovic held his nerve during a tense tie-break to beat Nuno Borges 6-3, 7-6 (7/2) at the China Open on Wednesday and extend his extraordinary unbeaten streak in Beijing.
The 39-year-old Serbian was struggling physically but pushed through the second-set decider for his first win at any event since Wimbledon in July.
The former world number one is set to meet wildcard Bu Yunchaokete of China in the second round.
Fans packed the stands in Beijing to watch Djokovic, a firm favourite in China who has never lost in Beijing in 30 matches -- although this was his first match at the event since 2015.
He delighted the crowd with an ace to end the first game and saved two break points after a pair of double-faults to win the first set.
Djokovic has had health issues in recent months and struggled to pick up points at the start of the second set, using his racquet to stretch his back between games and needing a medical timeout as a trainer worked on his right shoulder.
But he forced a path to victory in one hour and 50 minutes, clinching it when Borges, the world number 49 from Portugal, returned into the net.
It preserved Djokovic's winning streak in Beijing, where he has won six titles.
Earlier, Karen Khachanov swept aside second seed Felix Auger-Aliassime 6-3, 6-3 in their first-round meeting.
Khachanov, the world number 26, won three straight games, taking the first set in 31 minutes.
The 30-year-old then kept his cool to break Auger-Aliassime on the first match point, wrapping things up in one hour and 11 minutes.
He faces either Arthur Rinderknech of France or qualifier Alex Molcan of Slovakia in the round of 16.
Khachanov brushed off suggestions he had Auger-Aliassime's card marked following his second statement win over the Canadian world number five in a matter of weeks.
"It was a tough match," the Russian, who triumphed at the US Open, said.
"When you approach this match you are thinking it's a completely new match, completely different. In China, in Beijing. Different court, different balls.
"You just focus again from zero. You know that what you did well... and you just try to keep the momentum going. There is not much secret about it."

title: Ronaldo leaves Portugal training camp after coach says he is dropped
description: The veteran forward said he would reveal his reasons for the departure at a later date
content:
The veteran forward said he would reveal his reasons for the departure at a later date
Portugal captain Cristiano Ronaldo announced on Wednesday that he had left the team's training camp in Denmark after coach Jorge Jesus told reporters that the striker would be dropped for their next match.
Ronaldo had been due to train with his team-mates at the Parken stadium in Copenhagen on Wednesday but left abruptly after Jesus's press conference.
The veteran coach had said that Ronaldo, who spent the entire match on the bench against Norway on Sunday, would not start Thursday's Nations League clash away to Denmark either.
"Following the national team coach's press conference, and after having a conversation with the Portuguese Football Federation president, I decided to leave the national team's training camp," Ronaldo wrote on Instagram.
"In due course, I will tell the truth to all the Portuguese people about my reasons for leaving the national team, to which I have always been dedicated.
"Now is time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my team-mates, without exception."
Jesus had insisted earlier that there was no rift between him and Ronaldo, although the 72-year-old did acknowledge that his captain had been disappointed to remain on the bench in the side's Nations League win over Norway.
The news sparked a wave of memes on social media and furious backlash from Ronaldo's sister, Elma Aveiro.
"They don't deserve to have the best of anything," she said about the Portuguese people on Instagram.
"We are envious, scornful, and ignorant, and we deserve to return to the mediocrity that defined us in the pre-CR7 era of football."
Following the 2-1 victory in Oslo, Ronaldo went straight to the changing rooms without joining his team-mates in acknowledging the Portuguese supporters in the stands.
"There was no incident whatsoever," Jesus told reporters.
"Any player –- and I was a player myself... when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don't get on... no one is happy about that," Jesus said on Wednesday.
The Portuguese coach added that he had told Ronaldo before the match that he would not be in the starting line-up, but that he might bring him on towards the end of the game.
"Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It's nothing to make a fuss about," Jesus insisted.
The former Benfica boss also explained that Ronaldo had not refused to train on Tuesday, as some Portuguese media outlets had suggested, but that he had had to do individual exercises for physical "mobility" and "strengthening".
Jesus had said that the five-time Ballon d'Or winner would train as normal on Wednesday, however, despite arriving at the stadium in the team bus, Ronaldo did not join his team-mates on the pitch in Copenhagen.
Portuguese media shared a video of him leaving the Parken stadium alongside two members of the backroom staff just after Jesus's press conference.
They also said that Ronaldo's private jet was heading to Copenhagen.
Following Ronaldo's social media post, the Portuguese federation released a statement confirming that the former Real Madrid, Manchester United and Juventus player had left the squad's training camp.
"Preparation for the two matches against Denmark and Norway... continue as planned with the 24 remaining squad members," the federation said.
"The entire delegation remains totally focussed on the national team's next fixtures and on achieving the established objectives."
Jesus had said earlier that for the Denmark match he again intended to start AC Milan striker Goncalo Ramos, who scored the winner against the Norwegians.
"If everything goes according to plan, it will be Goncalo who plays," he said, before adding regarding Ronaldo: "If I need him, he'll come on. If I don't need him, he won't."
At 41, Ronaldo announced this summer that this season would "probably (be) my last year in football".
He is Portugal's leading goalscorer and most capped player, with 146 goals in 234 appearances.

title: Marsh hails improvements after Australia win final one day international
description: Carey   s 74 helps Australia beat South Africa by 45 runs after posting 322 9
content:
Carey’s 74 helps Australia beat South Africa by 45 runs after posting 322-9
Australian captain Mitchell Marsh hailed the improvement shown by his team after they were convincing winners of the third and final one-day international against South Africa in Potchefstroom on Wednesday.
Australia won by 45 runs according to the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method after South Africa's reply to Australia's 322 for nine was ended by rain after 28 overs.
South Africa, who won the first two matches to clinch the series, were struggling on 145 for four at the stoppage, well short of the required rate.
"I thought the batting in particular showed some real improvement, especially from a few of our young guys," said Marsh. "It was a disappointing series but nice to finish with a win."
Marsh said there were encouraging signs looking ahead to the 2027 Cricket World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.
"It's gradual improvement. We have some guys that haven't a lot of experience at this level and in particular playing in South Africa against a team that plays very well at home."
Marsh said he was sorry the match had not gone the distance which seemed a fair comment because Ryan Rickelton, on 71 not out, was the last remaining specialist batsman after Tony de Zorzi injured a hamstring while fielding and was ruled out of the rest of the match.
South Africa, having already won the series, rested key players in captain Temba Bavuma, batsman David Miller and bowlers Marco Jansen and Keshav Maharaj.
Australian Test captain Pat Cummins returned for his first one-day international since November 2024.
Marsh and Travis Head again gave Australia a fast start after stand-in captain Aiden Markram won the toss and sent them in, putting on 78 for the first wicket off 53 balls.
Unlike in the first two matches, there were solid contributions down the Australian batting order, anchored by Alex Carey’s 74 off 88 balls.
Australia's bowlers kept the pressure on South Africa. Xavier Bartlett was excellent with the new ball, dismissing Quinton de Kock and Markram inside the ten-over powerplay.
Leg-spinner Adam Zampa found his best form after being expensive in the first two matches, taking two for 33 in six overs, while Cummins built up lively pace. Although he did not take a wicket he conceded only 17 runs in five overs.
Bavuma said in accepting the series trophy that South Africa had "definitely made strides" during the series. He said the decision to rest leading players was a combination of providing opportunities to other players and prioritising a three-match Test series which starts in Durban on October 9.
Australia 322-9 in 50 overs (M. Marsh 56, O. Peake 48, A. Carey 74, M. Renshaw 30; G. Coetzee 2-61, L. Williams 2-48, C. Bosch 4-60) v South Africa 145-4 in 28 overs (R. Rickelton 71 not out; X. Bartlett 2-25, A. Zampa 2-33).
Result: Australia won by 45 runs (DLS method).
Series: South Africa won the three-match series 2-1.

title: Oil prices rise 2  as China suspends fuel exports
description: Chinese refiners suspend exports of oil products to regions beyond Hong Kong and Macau until further notice
content:
Chinese refiners suspend exports of oil products to regions beyond Hong Kong and Macau until further notice
Oil ‌prices rose around 2% on Thursday after China suspended oil product exports, potentially tightening fuel markets already coping with supply shortages globally, while investors continued to assess renewed diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war.
The new front-month December Brent crude futures contract traded at $100.09 per barrel at ​0829 GMT, up 2.1%, or $2.06, from Wednesday's close. The November contract expired on Wednesday, settling at $103.50 per ​barrel, marking a monthly gain of around 14% in September for the front-month contract.
US West Texas ⁠Intermediate crude was up $2.06, or 2.28%, to $92.48 a barrel.
Prices were volatile on Thursday, having slipped more than 1% in ​early trading, before rebounding.
Chinese refiners have suspended exports of oil products to regions beyond Hong Kong and Macau until further ​notice, four people briefed on the matter said on Thursday, a move that will further crimp war-constrained fuel markets.
"The Chinese export ban suggests concerns about domestic product availability," UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo said, adding that it remains to be seen whether the measures will support higher ​crude imports after recent drawdowns in Chinese crude and fuel stocks.
Read: Oil gains after Trump denies he is willing to ease sanctions on Iran
Global diesel supplies have tightened as a result of falling ​refining capacity due to attacks linked to the Middle East and Ukraine wars, raising pressure on governments to intervene to shield consumers.
The ‌Trump administration ⁠has told Germany and France to draw down emergency diesel inventories to help ease global fuel prices or face a potential US diesel export ban, three people close to the discussions said.
European diesel refinery profit margins were trading at around $80.05 per barrel at 0829 GMT, down around 4% from the previous session. The margin hit an all-time high of $95 per ​barrel on September 23.
Investors continued ​to watch diplomacy efforts and ⁠oil exports in the Middle East.
Saudi Arabia resumed oil tanker loadings from Yanbu, Reuters reported on Tuesday, after earlier restarting operations on its East-West Pipeline.
Iran said on Wednesday it had received a ​US response to its latest proposal to resurrect the collapsed ceasefire in the Gulf.
However, ​US President Donald Trump ⁠denied reports by Axios and CNN citing US officials as saying he was willing to give Iran sanctions relief and release frozen Iranian funds in return for "concrete" steps by Tehran on its nuclear programme.
Goldman Sachs estimates Gulf oil exports, including "dark exports" involving ⁠ships operating ​with their location transponders turned off, have recovered to 23.3 million barrels ​per day over the last week, in line with their 2025 average, as exports doubled in September, it said in a note on Tuesday.

title: PSL 12 likely to start on March 19  2027

content:
PCB settles on dates for next season as the marquee event once again overlaps with the IPL
The 12th edition of the Pakistan Super League is expected to begin on March 19, with the final scheduled for May 2. The dates have been tentatively agreed upon, with an official announcement expected after the franchises are taken into confidence.
According to details, the league’s broadcaster had pushed for a January start, arguing that an earlier window would help secure sponsorships. Franchise owners, however, preferred an April window. The PCB has now decided to tentatively hold PSL 12 from March 19 to May 2, with the final dates to be confirmed after consultations with the franchises.
Ramadan is expected to begin on February 8 next year, meaning the league will be staged after eid. However, PSL 12 will once again overlap with the Indian Premier League (IPL), which is scheduled to run from March 10 to May 15.
A similar clash has occurred in recent years, but it has not had a significant impact on the PSL. Pakistani fans have continued to prioritise their domestic league, while television ratings have remained largely unaffected. Officials are hopeful the trend will continue this time.
Several prominent overseas players, who do not participate in the IPL, could also join the PSL. The date for the player auction has yet to be finalised, but some franchises have already begun contacting foreign stars.
According to sources, several high-profile players could make their PSL debuts next season. While preparations are currently moving slowly, the process is expected to gather pace once the dates are officially announced.
The venues and other logistical details will also be finalised in the coming weeks.

title: Pakistan  India set for Asian Games cricket final
description: Abdul Samad   s blistering 30 and Ishan Kishan   s 80 help Pakistan and India seal contrasting semi final wins
content:
Abdul Samad’s blistering 30 and Ishan Kishan’s 80 help Pakistan and India seal contrasting semi-final wins
Pakistan and India set up a blockbuster Asian Games men’s cricket final on Thursday after contrasting semi-final victories over Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.
Abdul Samad smashed an unbeaten 30 off 15 balls as Pakistan recovered from early trouble to beat Bangladesh by six wickets and reach the Asian Games men’s cricket final on Thursday.
Chasing 112 in a 13-over semi-final at Korogi Sports Park, Pakistan slipped to 53-4 before Samad and Hasan Nawaz combined for an unbeaten 59-run fifth-wicket stand.
Hasan finished 27 not out off 22 balls, with two fours and two sixes, as Pakistan reached 112-4 in 11.3 overs.
Samad provided the decisive burst in the 10th over, taking 22 runs from five deliveries against Mustafizur Rahman.
After Hasan took a single from the first ball, Samad launched Mustafizur over long-on for six before hitting four successive boundaries.
The 23-run over reduced Pakistan’s target to 13 from 18 balls and effectively settled the contest.
Earlier, Pakistan lost captain Sahibzada Farhan for one before Maaz Sadaqat, Saim Ayub and Usman Khan also departed.
Saim made 21 off 12 balls, including two sixes, while debutant Maaz contributed 15 off seven.
Bangladesh, asked to bat first, posted 111-7 from their 13 overs, with Towhid Hridoy top-scoring with 42 off 25 balls, including four sixes and two fours.
Saif Hassan added 19, but Pakistan’s spinners kept Bangladesh from building sustained momentum.
Sufyan Moqim took 3-26 and Arafat Minhas claimed 2-23, while Saim returned figures of 1-3 from his two overs.
Defending champions India then booked their place in the final with a 124-run thrashing of Sri Lanka.
India posted 169-7 after Ishan Kishan struck an unbeaten 80 off 46 balls and 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi added 38 from 21.
Sri Lanka were bowled out for 45 in 9.5 overs, with Jasprit Bumrah, Axar Patel and Abhishek Sharma taking two wickets apiece.
Pakistan and India will meet for the gold medal on Saturday at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin.
The men’s cricket quarter-finals had been washed out by rain, with Pakistan and India advancing based on their higher rankings.
Pakistan 112-4 (11.3 ov) beat Bangladesh 111-7 by six wickets.
India 169-7 (20 ov) beat Sri Lanka 45 all out by 124 runs

title: Pakistan demolish India to storm into volleyball semis
description: Murad Khan plays a key role in Green shirts  inspiring triumph
content:
Murad Khan plays a key role in Green-shirts' inspiring triumph
Pakistan swept arch-rivals India 3-0 on Thursday to reach the semi-finals of the Asian Games men’s volleyball competition and end their opponents’ unbeaten run.
Pakistan won 25-19, 25-23, 25-18 at Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park Gymnasium to beat India at the Asian Games for the second successive edition.
Murad Khan led the way with a match-high 22 points, while Usman Faryad Ali added nine and Mohammad Hamad eight.
Pakistan, ranked 39th in the world compared with India’s 49th, had beaten Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan in the pool stage before losing to hosts Japan to finish runners-up in Pool A.
India entered the quarter-final unbeaten after straight-set wins over Vietnam and Hong Kong and a five-set victory over Qatar.
Pakistan set the pace from the outset, taking the opening set 25-19 in 23 minutes as India struggled to contain their attack.
The second set proved more closely fought. India opened a 16-13 lead before Pakistan fought back to level at 16-16.
India again moved three points clear at 19-16, but Pakistan responded with another three-point run to draw level before taking control.
Pakistan reached set point at 24-22. India saved one, but Pakistan converted the next opportunity to take the set 25-23 after 34 minutes.
Pakistan then dominated the third set, opening a 14-9 lead before extending it to 17-10.
India saved two match points at 24-16, but Pakistan closed out the match on their third opportunity, winning the set 25-18 in 25 minutes.
The victory keeps Pakistan’s medal hopes alive as they advance to the semi-finals.

title: Pakistan carried out  well planned  calibrated  air strikes on terrorist hideouts in Afghanistan  info ministry
description: Ministry says targets were destroyed with precision and initial reports suggest the killing of 22 terrorists
content:
Ministry says airstrikes killed 22 terrorists, destroyed large quantities of arms and ammunition stored at hideouts
Pakistan carried out “well-planned and calibrated aerial strikes” against terrorist hideouts and safe havens in Afghanistan, with "initial reports suggesting 22 terrorists" had been killed, the Information Ministry said on Thursday.
"In continuation of Operation Ghazab lil Haq and Pakistan’s resolve to eliminate terrorists, their networks and supporters, well-planned and calibrated aerial strikes against the hideouts and safe havens of terrorist organisations of Fitna al Khawarij and Fitna al Hindustan have been conducted, killing multiple terrorists", the ministry said in a post on X.
The federal government last year officially designated all terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as Fitna al-Hindustan , accusing India of sponsoring a proxy war through the outfits. Fitna al-Khawarij is the state-designated term for the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
Operation Ghazab Lil Haq was launched in February following renewed clashes along the Pakistan–Afghanistan border, after Afghan Taliban forces fired on multiple locations, prompting swift military retaliation by Pakistan.
The ministry further added that, based on credible intelligence, selective targeting of terrorist camps and hideouts at two locations belonging to Fitna al Khawarij , Fitna al Hindustan and their affiliates has been carried out in Afghanistan with precision and accuracy.
“Targets were destroyed with precision and initial reports suggest the killing of twenty-two terrorists,” the ministry said, adding that large quantities of weapons and ammunition stored at the hideouts had also been destroyed.
*1st October, 2026;* In continuation of operation Ghazab lil Haq and Pakistan’s resolve to eliminate terrorists, their networks and supporters, well planned and calibrated aerial strikes against the hideouts and safe havens of terrorists organisations of Fitna al Khwarij and…
The ministry said Pakistan had always strived to maintain peace and stability in the region. However, the safety and security of its citizens remained its foremost priority.
"It was a matter of grave concern that Afghanistan continued to remain a hub of terrorism. The threat to Pakistan emanated from Afghanistan. In this context, our action precisely targeted the terrorist hubs," the ministry added.
The ministry said, "Maximum precautions were taken, and it was ensured that no collateral damage occurred."
"Our relentless Counter Terrorism campaign, Ghazab lil Haq, under the vision “ Azm e Istehkam ” by the security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan, will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country," the ministry concluded.
Read: Prospects for Pak-Afghan ties reset appear bleak
In another post, the ministry said precise aerial and drone strikes had comprehensively destroyed terrorist hideouts and camps belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan at two locations in areas under the control of the Afghan Taliban regime.
Update-Ghazab lil Haq Islamabad, 01 October, 2026 Through precise aerial and drone strikes, as reflected in the attached clip, terrorist hideout and camps belonging to Fitna al Khwarij and Fitna al Hindustan at two locations in areas under the control of the Afghan Taliban… pic.twitter.com/W6GO512OXM
It said large quantities of weapons and ammunition stockpiled at the hideouts and camps were also destroyed in “calibrated and precisely targeted aerial strikes”.
The latest strikes came amid a sharp escalation in tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan after 23 people, including 15 police personnel , were martyred in the blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
A day later, a captain and a lieutenant were among six martyred during an exchange of fire in Hangu district. Following a series of deadly attacks in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), on September 21, Pakistan carried out “calibrated” air strikes against terrorist hideouts near the Afghan border and conducted intelligence-based ground operations that killed a total of 37 terrorists.
On September 23, Pakistan's air defence systems shot down eight drones after they entered Pakistani airspace from Afghanistan. Four were brought down near the Torkham border and four in mountainous areas near Kohat.
Two days later, Pakistan carried out “precision” aerial and drone strikes against 10 locations in Afghanistan used for launching and storing drones.
Pakistan has repeatedly raised concerns on international forums over terrorist attacks being launched from Afghan soil.
United Nations Security Council report also formally implicated the banned Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and terrorist entities operating from Afghanistan , highlighting tactical collaboration and shared operational logistics between the groups.
Member-state reporting confirmed that BLA terrorists were trained alongside TTP members at facilities in Afghanistan, according to the report, which also described growing operational links among various terrorist groups operating across the border.
This was not the first time a UN report pointed to the threat posed by terrorist groups operating from Afghanistan. In 2023, a UN report also revealed that the TTP had established a new base in K-P in mid-2023, shedding light on close ties between the TTP and the Afghan Taliban, as well as between the TTP and anti-Pakistani groups and Al Qaeda.

title: Inflation pushes Peshawar families into debt
description: Overall prices of essential goods and services have risen by 35 to 40 per cent
content:
Overall prices of essential goods and services have risen by 35 to 40 per cent
Soaring inflation has pushed nearly nine out of 10 low-income households in Peshawar into debt, with most families now unable to repay the loans they took just to cover daily expenses, according to a new survey released on Wednesday.
Dr Muhammad Iqbal Khalil, chairman of the Institute of Regional Studies (IRS), presented the findings at the Peshawar Press Club. The study drew on responses from 462 households, focus-group discussions and consultations with stakeholders across the city.
While inflation is a nationwide problem, Peshawar's poorer neighbourhoods have been hit especially hard. Overall prices of essential goods and services have risen by 35 to 40 per cent. In low-income areas, 48.7 per cent of households described themselves as extremely affected.
Although 67.3 per cent of families reported some increase in income, expenses have risen far faster. Electricity, gas and fuel bills jumped for 93 per cent of households, while 86.4 per cent saw food costs climb. Many families have been forced to switch to cheaper, lower-quality food items. Healthcare has become another major burden: 79.4 per cent said they can no longer afford medical treatment.

title: Doctors escalate strike after LRH assault
description: Doctors escalate strike after LRH assault
content:
Incident prompts boycott amid salary standoff
The Neutral Doctors Community has intensified its ongoing strike by announcing a full boycott of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa hospitals, declaring that doctors will now leave their workplaces and return home for their own safety following a violent incident at Lady Reading Hospital.
Speaking at a press conference at the Peshawar Press Club on Wednesday, Community Chairman Dr Adnan Afridi said the organisation had been observing a pen-down strike for the past 24 days to press for a 30 per cent increase in basic salaries. The latest decision came after security personnel allegedly assaulted peaceful protesting doctors at LRH the previous day.
"Yesterday's attack by security guards acting on the administration's orders has proved that doctors are no longer safe even inside their own hospitals," Dr Afridi said. Accompanied by colleagues from LRH, Hayatabad Medical Complex, Khyber Teaching Hospital and other facilities across the province, he announced that doctors would now combine the pen-down strike with a complete withdrawal from hospital wards.
Under the new plan, only one doctor will remain on duty in each ward while emergency services will continue to be covered so that patients are not left without critical care. "We are not abandoning patients," Dr Afridi stressed. "Emergency cover will be maintained, but the rest of the medical staff will return home to protect themselves."
The doctors' leader accused the provincial health department of deliberately stalling negotiations. He said officials repeatedly summoned the community for talks only to ask them to wait or form yet another committee, thereby wasting time while the core demand remained unmet.
"Our committee already exists," Dr Afridi said. "The 30 per cent salary increase is our fundamental right, yet the K-P government continues to ignore it. Until this demand is fulfilled, the protest will continue."
He issued a stern warning that any attempt to harass doctors in their homes would be met with firm resistance. "If anyone tries to intimidate doctors who are staying at home, they will be dealt with by our own hands," he declared.
Dr Afridi further alleged that the health secretary and other senior officials had been deceiving the doctors under the guise of dialogue. From now on, the community would negotiate exclusively with the Chief Minister and no one else.
"We will not hold talks with any other official," he said. "Our protest will remain in force until the government grants the 30 per cent raise in basic salaries."
The Neutral Doctors Community's decision marks a significant escalation in the month-long standoff that has already disrupted routine services in major public hospitals across the province. Health authorities have yet to issue an official response to the latest announcement.

title: PA body approves Christain Marriage Bill
description: PA body approves Christain Marriage Bill
content:
Proposed legislation replaces 1872 law with new framework for marriage registration
The Punjab Assembly's Standing Committee on Human Rights and Minority Affairs has approved the proposed Christian Marriage Bill 2026, which seeks to replace the Christian Marriage Act of 1872 with a new legal framework governing Christian marriages in the province.
The bill, introduced as a private member's bill by MPA Falbous Christopher, proposes raising the minimum marriage age for Christian men and women to 18 years.
Under the existing law, the minimum age is 16 for boys and 13 for girls.
The proposed legislation would also require both the bride and groom to be Christian for a marriage to be solemnised under the law.
Under the existing framework, only one party is required to be Christian.
A key provision seeks to make registration of Christian marriages with Union Councils and the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) mandatory.
The proposed framework also provides procedures for issuing marriage certificates and maintaining official records.
The bill proposes allowing Christian marriages to be solemnised in all churches registered with the Punjab government according to Christian rites.
It also seeks to remove restrictions on the day and time of marriage ceremonies, including the existing restriction on ceremonies after 6pm.
Under the proposed law, pastors who have received religious education and are affiliated with churches registered with the Punjab government would be authorised to solemnise Christian marriages. Government-appointed Marriage Registrars would also have a role under the proposed framework.
The proposed legislation defines marriage as a union between a man and a woman, replacing the existing law's reference to marriage between "two persons or parties".
It also lays down procedures for giving notice of an intended marriage, issuing certificates and maintaining marriage records.
Couples would be required to submit prescribed notices containing personal, residential and identification details, along with information about the proposed marriage.
The bill further provides for public display of marriage notices and, where applicable, publication of banns for three consecutive weeks by licensed Christian ministers.
At least one of the intending spouses would be required to declare that there was no lawful impediment to the marriage and that consent had not been obtained through force or coercion.
The proposed procedure also provides for a waiting period before a marriage certificate can be issued.
Where a Marriage Registrar is involved, the proposed law provides for maintaining a Marriage Notice Book that would be open to public inspection.
A person aggrieved by a registrar's refusal to issue a certificate could approach the court under the proposed procedure.
Marriage ministers and registrars would also be required to maintain official records, with certificates and entries signed by the parties, the solemnising official and witnesses. Copies of certificates would be forwarded to the relevant registrar and local government office within the prescribed period.
The bill was first submitted to the Punjab Assembly committee in April as a private member's bill.
It has subsequently undergone consultations and clause-by-clause discussions involving assembly members, church representatives, legal experts and other stakeholders.

title: Lahore skies set for 10 day Basant
description: Lahore skies set for 10 day Basant
content:
Punjab CM approves rescheduling of festival
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has rescheduled Basant 2027 in Lahore, extending the festival to 10 days from January 29 to February 7, with a break on February 5 to observe Kashmir Day.
The revised schedule replaces the three-day festival earlier announced for March 12 to 14, 2027.
The chief minister had announced the March dates in August, but approved the revised schedule at a meeting on Wednesday.
She directed authorities to organise the 10-day festival as a gift for the people of Lahore to mark the arrival of the new year.
She said the extended celebrations would help promote Punjab's cultural heritage and Lahore's traditional identity.
"The 10-day Basant celebrations will help promote Punjab's cultural colours and Lahore's ancient historical tradition across the world," she said.
The chief minister directed the relevant departments to make arrangements well in advance and ensure stronger measures for public safety and convenience than those adopted during the previous festival.
She appealed to citizens to celebrate responsibly and stressed that strict adherence to safety regulations would be essential for the success of the extended festivities.
The revised schedule comes as the provincial and district administrations continue preparations for Basant 2027 under a framework regulating kite flying, manufacturing, sale and transportation along with string.
The Lahore district administration had earlier announced that kite flying would be permitted only during designated festival dates and that chemical-coated, metallic and sharp strings would remain prohibited.
Registration of kite manufacturers began on September 5, with licences to be issued only to manufacturers meeting the prescribed legal requirements.
Assistant commissioners have been directed to verify manufacturers' credentials and inspect their premises.
Lahore Deputy Commissioner Captain (retd) Muhammad Ali Ijaz has also directed the administration to ensure strict monitoring of kite-making material and said only approved sizes and cotton string would be permitted.
The district administration has launched the Basant 2027 registration process through a portal, with manufacturers and other stakeholders required to complete the prescribed registration and approval process.
The government has also announced stringent penalties for violations of the kite-flying regulations, including restrictions on the manufacture, transportation and use of prohibited string.
The latest decision follows the revival of Basant in Lahore earlier this year after a prolonged ban. The festival was held from February 6 to 8 under restrictions aimed at preventing accidents and ensuring public safety.
For the 2027 festival, authorities have been directed to improve safety arrangements and public facilitation, particularly at rooftops and other locations where kite flying will be permitted.
The government has also been preparing cultural and beautification activities for the festival, including decorations along major roads, parks and green belts, as well as cultural displays and events showcasing Lahore's heritage.
The Walled City is also being considered for cultural activities featuring traditional Basant colours, food stalls offering local cuisine and live performances by musicians and artistes.
The government has said the preparations are aimed at reviving Lahore's cultural vibrancy while ensuring a safe environment for citizens.

title: Gender violence extends beyond physical abuse | The Express Tribune

beyond physical abuse
content:
Unreported cases remain a major challenge, experts claim
Gender-based violence does not begin and end with physical assault; it can also involve psychological harm, damage to reputation and property, and violations of personal boundaries, experts said on Wednesday.
Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed said the nature and severity of violence determined its legal status, with some offences falling within the category of cognisable crimes. She said domestic violence should not be confined to incidents occurring inside a home, as violence involving close family relationships could fall within its scope regardless of where it took place.
She was speaking at a seminar titled "Growing Gender-Based Violence in Pakistan: Legal Gaps, Barriers to Implementation, Challenges and the Way Forward", organised by the Centre of Excellence for Women's Studies, University of Karachi, in collaboration with UN Women and the university's Office of Research, Innovation and Commercialisation (ORIC), at the Chinese Teachers' Memorial Auditorium.
Dr Summaiya stressed the importance of accurate medico-legal documentation in cases involving violence and injuries, saying medical examinations and evidence had to be recorded in accordance with legal requirements to ensure their admissibility in court.
"Medico-legal reports, medical evidence, police action and the criminal justice system are interconnected," she said, adding that proper documentation could play a crucial role in ensuring justice. She cautioned against interpreting overall violence statistics and domestic violence figures in the same way. While men could account for a higher number of deaths resulting from violence overall, she said the pattern was different in cases of domestic and family violence.
Many cases involving violence against women and children, child abuse and sexual exploitation never reached authorities, meaning official figures did not reflect the full scale of the problem, Dr Summaiya said.

title: Umrah visas  Australia dreams and a Rs7 5m deal

FIA intercepts three passengers allegedly planning illegal journey via Bahrain and Palau
Three Pakistanis hoping to turn an Umrah trip into a clandestine journey to Australia have been stopped at Karachi airport, exposing a suspected new "dunki" route through Bahrain and the tiny Pacific island nation of Palau.
The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) immigration officials intercepted the trio at Jinnah International Airport after their behaviour raised suspicion during immigration clearance. A closer look at their travel documents and mobile phones revealed a trail extending well beyond Saudi Arabia.
The passengers, travelling on Umrah visas, also carried Bahrain and Republic of Palau visas. Investigators said their alleged plan was to spend a few days in Saudi Arabia, travel onwards to Bahrain and Palau, secure temporary residence permits there and eventually attempt to reach Australia through an illegal migration route.
During questioning, the trio, identified as Nadeem Iqbal and Shehzad Ali, from Hafizabad, and Samar Shehzad from Sargodha, allegedly disclosed that they planned to stay in Saudi Arabia for around three days before travelling to Bahrain and then Palau.
They told investigators that an agent, identified as Naeem Murshid of Multan, had arranged their visas and travel for Rs2.5 million per person.
The agent had promised to arrange temporary residence permits (TRPs) for them after a stay of around three months in Palau, according to the trio. They would then attempt to reach Australia through an illegal migration route.
The FIA said documentary evidence, mobile phone data and the passengers' statements indicated that the Umrah journey was being used as a cover for an illegal migration attempt.
The three offloaded passengers were handed over to the FIA Anti-Human Trafficking Circle for further investigation and legal action. The agency said the case had also brought to light a suspected new route for illegal migration to Australia through Bahrain and Palau under the guise of Umrah travel.
