46k-student varsity gets yet another temporary head as permanent appointment remains stuck
Pakistan's largest public-sector university by enrolment, the University of Karachi, is once again set to be run on an interim basis, with its acting head leaving for a 20-day foreign trip just as admissions and entry tests for the 2027 academic session get under way.
Pharmacy Dean Prof Dr Haris Shoaib has been assigned charge of the university's day-to-day affairs as NED University Vice Chancellor Dr Muhammad Tufail Ahmed, who has also been given charge of Karachi University, leaves for academic visits to the United States, Canada and Sri Lanka.
Sources in the Karachi University Registrar's Office said the NOC for Dr Tufail's foreign visits had been issued. At NED University, Pro Vice Chancellor Dr Noman Ahmed has been given temporary charge during his absence.
Dr Tufail was handed additional charge of Karachi University in the last week of July. Sources said his latest foreign visit would be his second overseas academic trip in roughly two months, leaving the 46,000-student university once again without a full-time or acting vice chancellor.
The development comes as the Sindh government has yet to appoint a permanent vice chancellor for the university. Sources said a summary containing three candidates for the permanent post had already reached the Chief Minister's House, but no further progress had been made.
The leadership vacuum comes at a particularly crucial time for the university. Admissions for the 2027 academic session have already begun, with thousands of candidates scheduled to appear in entry tests for various disciplines on October 11. Open-merit admissions are also due to begin the same day.
With Dr Tufail abroad, routine administrative affairs will effectively be handled by a senior dean rather than a vice chancellor during this important phase of the admissions cycle.
Entry tests are among the university's major annual academic events, typically requiring senior leadership to oversee arrangements and proceedings, making the absence of a vice chancellor particularly notable at a time when thousands of prospective students are expected to participate.

title: Divorce  khula cases swamp family courts
description: Divorce  khula cases swamp family courts
content:
Courts receive 10,103 cases, including divorce and khula, in first nine months of 2026
Family courts across the district have witnessed a surge in cases involving family disputes, divorce, khula, maintenance, dowry articles, dower and child custody, breaking previous records.
Christian women have also started approaching courts for maintenance and khula after changes making the Christian family divorce system easier.
During the nine months from January 1 to September 30, 2026, a total of 10,103 family dispute cases were filed in family courts across the district.
These included cases involving divorce, children's maintenance, personal maintenance, return of dowry articles, payment of dower and child custody.
During the same period, 1,246 women were granted divorce decrees, while 220 children taken away from their mothers were recovered and handed back to them. Orders were issued in 11,247 cases for husbands to make immediate temporary payments towards children's maintenance, while 71 women who had left their homes or in-laws' houses and were staying with their parents were ordered to return and settle their homes.
As many as 146 husbands were ordered to return dowry articles and pay dower.
The basic reasons cited for family disputes and khula and divorce cases include Facebook, social media, TikTok, Instagram, chat applications and Messenger, with couples engaging in conversations and exchanging messages throughout the night.
Following changes in Christian family law, Christian women have also approached family courts for divorce this year. Previously, Christian women could not directly obtain divorce, but after the permission was granted, 103 Christian women have so far approached family courts for divorce, maintenance and child custody.
This year, 301 women left their homes for love marriages. With the increase in divorce cases, there has also been a record rise in the number of family meetings between children and parents separated from them.
According to the report, 70 per cent of new marriages that were described as incompatible and outside the family system, including love marriages or marriages resulting from social media friendships, failed.
Due to the increase in family cases, family courts at the district courts in Rawalpindi and all tehsil courts remain crowded daily with women and young children. At present, a total of 16,941 new and old family cases are pending before family courts across the district.
Family cases lawyer Madam Zeb Fayyaz Advocate said the family system should be revived for marriages and a family reconciliation council system should be established at the union council level. She suggested that retired judges be appointed as chairmen and local mosque imams and professors as members of the reconciliation councils.
She said children up to matriculation should not be given complete autonomy through mobile phones and their mobile activities should be monitored. She said mobile phones were a necessity today but children should not be allowed to use them freely until late at night.
Former District and Sessions Judge Shaukat Ali Sajid said social media had brought improvements and employment opportunities but had also created such problems. He said there was an urgent need for a mechanism to keep children away from social media.
He said that in love marriages, family members often prefer divorce over reconciliation over minor issues, which was not appropriate. He said both sets of parents had to play a role in making a marriage work, otherwise the deterioration would have serious effects in the future, or the family marriage system should be implemented.

title: Iraqis jubilant after last US soldiers depart
description: Iraqis jubilant after last US soldiers depart
content:
US withdrawal ends two decades of war but raises fears of militia influence
Iraqis celebrated the departure of US forces on Wednesday after more than two decades of war, but the end of the US-led coalition mission also revived fears that Iran-backed militias could gain influence or Islamic State could exploit a potential security vacuum.
The withdrawal of the final US troops, mainly from an airbase in the semi-autonomous Kurdish region of Erbil, formally ended the US-led coalition's military mission in Iraq, bringing an end to America's longest major military engagement of the 21st century.
Iraqi troops paraded through the streets of Baghdad and the holy city of Najaf to mark the departure. In Baghdad, residents expressed relief at the end of the foreign military presence, while warning that armed groups operating outside government control should now hand over their weapons.
"The withdrawal fills our hearts with joy," said Baghdad resident Ahmed Salah, 70. But he urged powerful militias to surrender their weapons and allow the government to take responsibility for protecting the country.
The United States invaded Iraq in 2003 to topple Saddam Hussein, unleashing years of violence and instability. American forces withdrew in 2011 but returned less than three years later after Islamic State fighters seized large parts of the country and imposed brutal rule.
More than 4,500 US troops were killed in Iraq, while the Iraq Body Count project estimates that more than 200,000 Iraqi civilians died during the conflict. The pullout was agreed in 2024 under President Joe Biden and completed by President Donald Trump's administration.
Trump hailed the withdrawal as a "victory" for both the United States and Iraq, saying they had defeated Islamic State and that it was time for American forces to return home. "I had a choice to stay or to leave, and felt, without question, that it was time for America to go home!" Trump said on his Truth Social platform.
Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi said the end of the international coalition mission did not mean the end of Iraq's fight against terrorism. Instead, he described the withdrawal as the beginning of a phase in which Iraq would assume full responsibility for its security and stability.
Hundreds of supporters of Iran-backed Iraqi militias gathered in Baghdad to celebrate the withdrawal, chanting "Death to America" and carrying portraits of Iran's slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, his son Mojtaba and General Qassem Soleimani.

Andersson abandoned her attempt on Monday after failing to unite the three other parties in her left-wing bloc.

title: Russian strikes batter Ukraine s energy grid
description: Russian strikes batter Ukraine s energy grid
content:
Seven killed as Kyiv warns of worst attacks on power sites in months
Russia launched a major overnight air assault on Ukraine's energy infrastructure on Wednesday, killing seven people and damaging power facilities around Kyiv and other regions in what Ukrainian officials described as the heaviest combined strike on the energy grid in months.
The attack came after days of intensifying drone barrages against the capital, fuelling fears that Moscow is preparing another winter campaign aimed at disrupting electricity and heating supplies as temperatures fall and Ukraine faces shortages of air defences.
Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said that Russia had escalated to "massive strikes on energy infrastructure", adding that there had barely been a day without attacks on energy facilities since summer.
President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Kyiv and the surrounding area were the main targets in an assault involving nearly 190 drones and ballistic missiles. Ukraine's air force said it had shot down five missiles and 155 drones.
A child was among the seven people killed across Ukraine, Zelenskiy said, while critical infrastructure was struck in five regions and damage was reported in five others. The strikes damaged a key power plant and other energy facilities. The overnight assault triggered an air-raid alert lasting more than 12 hours.
Ukrainian authorities have been strengthening protective facilities, diversifying power generation and checking backup systems at critical sites ahead of the expected winter campaign. However, human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets warned of a critical shortage of urban shelters.
In neighbouring Moldova, a drone crossed into the country's airspace and exploded near Hirbovet. Romania and Poland scrambled military jets, while flights at two Polish airports were temporarily suspended.

title: EU return back on Britain s agenda
description: EU return back on Britain s agenda
content:
PM Burnham says govt will assess full membership and closer economic ties
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has reopened the divisive debate over Britain's future relationship with the European Union, saying rejoining the bloc should be considered alongside other options, including closer economic ties.
Speaking to the BBC on Wednesday, Burnham, who became prime minister in July after replacing Keir Starmer, said Brexit had "done more harm than good" and argued that Britain needed to settle its long-term relationship with its European partners.
Burnham said the government could consider remaining outside the EU, joining its customs union or single market, or "go all the way" and seek to rejoin the 27-member bloc. He added the options would first have to be assessed for what was "doable" and their respective advantages and disadvantages.
The remarks mark a significant departure from Starmer's 2024 election commitments, which ruled out rejoining the EU, returning to the single market or customs union, and restoring freedom of movement. Burnham, however, said any decision on a future referendum was not imminent.
The prime minister stressed that his government was developing a 10-year plan. However, when asked whether an in-out referendum could feature in a future election manifesto, he replied: "Things are possible."
French President Emmanuel Macron welcomed the prospect of Britain returning to the EU but warned that membership could not involve choosing only those parts of the bloc that suited Britain.
The European Commission said it was up to London to determine how it wanted to develop relations with the bloc, while adding that Brussels remained open to the options Britain might propose.
The issue is expected to feature prominently ahead of a UK-EU summit planned for November. Burnham has said he will use the meeting to outline different options for Britain's future relationship with Europe.

The Foreign Office on Wednesday expressed condolences over the deaths of five crew members, including three Pakistanis, during an operation by the Somali maritime police to recover the hijacked vessel MT Honour 25 near Bandar Beyla.
The Foreign Office spokesperson said in a statement that the government was making every possible effort to ensure the transportation of the bodies of the deceased Pakistanis to the country and arrange medical treatment for the three injured Pakistani nationals.
The spokesperson confirmed that three Pakistani nationals Rafi Ullah Khan, Syed Kashif Umer and Mahmood Ahmed Ansari were among the casualties during the operation. He added that a Pakistani team at the Embassy in Djibouti is proceeding to Bandar Beyla to assist the Pakistani nationals.
"The Government and people of Pakistan extend their deepest condolences to the bereaved families. We share their grief at this painful time and pray for strength, patience and comfort for the families, and for the departed souls to rest in peace," the spokesperson said.
"Every possible effort is being made to ensure proper medical care for the injured, facilitate the transportation of the mortal remains of the deceased, and ensure the safe return of the surviving Pakistani crew members," the statement added.
"The Government of Pakistan, through its Mission and relevant authorities, remains in close contact with the Somali authorities and other concerned stakeholders," the spokesperson said.
The Palau-flagged Honour 25 oil tanker, with a 17-member crew, including 10 Pakistanis, was seized on April 21 around 30 nautical miles off Puntland's coast while sailing from Oman to Somalia. The tanker had 18,500 barrels of oil on board when it was hijacked.
Somalia's Puntland Maritime Police Force said in a post on X on Tuesday that it had "carried out a maritime operation off the coast of Dharin-baar, Bandar Beyla District", rescuing the MT Honour 25 oil tanker. content:
PM reaffirms Pakistan-China ties as nations mark 75 years
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to further strengthening its all-weather strategic cooperative partnership with China, describing the enduring bilateral friendship as a bond built on mutual trust, unwavering support and deep affinity between their peoples.
Addressing a reception hosted to mark the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China, the prime minister stated that this year Pakistan and China were celebrating the 75th anniversary of the establishment of their diplomatic relations.
The prime minister extended felicitations to President Xi Jinping and the Chinese people on the occasion and said that the celebration of China's Founding Day was always close to the hearts of Pakistani people.
He said China's historic transformation and its growing contribution to global peace, stability and development continued to inspire countries around the world, particularly Pakistan.
He also expressed Pakistan's full endorsement of President Xi Jinping's Global Development Initiative, Global Security Initiative, Global Civilization Initiative and Global Governance Initiative, describing them as foundational pillars of a shared future for mankind.
The prime minister said the Pakistan-China relationship had grown over seven-and-a-half decades into a special bond based on mutual trust, mutual support and close ties between the two peoples.
"Pakistan takes immense pride in our All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership with China," he said, adding that the countries' "iron-clad friendship" had stood the test of time. He said the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) was a powerful expression of the enduring friendship and shared commitment to a more prosperous future for the two countries.
The prime minister said Pakistan and China were now transitioning towards the next phase, CPEC 2.0, with enhanced focus on industrialization, special economic zones, information technology and artificial intelligence, agriculture, and mines and minerals.
He particularly highlighted progress in agricultural cooperation, saying the first group of 1,000 Pakistani agriculture graduates had completed their training in China, while another 1,000 were ready to follow.
He described the initiative as a valuable investment in the skills and future of Pakistani youth. Prime Minister Shehbaz said Pakistan-China relations were the "anchor" of Pakistan's foreign policy and had been nurtured by successive generations of leaders.
Recalling his meeting with President Xi Jinping in Beijing in May, he said their warm and productive discussions had reaffirmed the enduring friendship between the two countries.
He said Pakistan remained fully committed to implementing the important consensus reached between the leadership of the two countries for the mutual benefit of their peoples.
He reiterated Pakistan's resolve to continue moving forward hand-in-hand with China towards building an ever-closer Pakistan-China Community with a Shared Future in the New Era.
Speaking on the occasion, Chinese Ambassador to Pakistan Jiang Zaidong described China and Pakistan as "all-weather strategic cooperative partners and ironclad brothers" and welcomed the growing resilience and vitality of Pakistan's economy under Prime Minister Shehbaz's leadership.
He said this year marked the 75th anniversary of China-Pakistan diplomatic relations, adding that the journey of the past 75 years had demonstrated that the two countries were friends who had been supporting each other through thick and thin.
The ambassador also highlighted the expansion of practical economic cooperation, saying bilateral trade reached $16.44 billion from January to July, up 13.4 per cent year-on-year.
He said bilateral agricultural trade stood at around $830 million during January-August, an increase of 45 per cent year-on-year, while China continued to rank first in terms of investment in Pakistan, accounting for 60.7 per cent of total foreign investment attracted by Pakistan, including Hong Kong.
Ambassador Jiang said China was ready to work with Pakistan to further deepen bilateral cooperation, particularly in industry, agriculture and mining, and to advance the high-quality development of CPEC 2.0 and an upgraded version of the China-Pakistan Free Trade Agreement.
He also outlined plans for cooperation in livelihood projects, including the construction of 100 clean water stations, upgrading of 1,000 smart classrooms and distribution of 100,000 school kits in Balochistan.
He said China would further strengthen cooperation with Pakistan in health, education, climate change and other fields, alongside expanded exchanges among universities, think tanks, youth and women.
The ambassador further said China would deepen defence, security and counter-terrorism cooperation with Pakistan, while maintaining close international coordination and jointly safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of Global South countries.

title: Pilot on Tel Aviv bound flight tried to crash plane
description: Pilot on Tel Aviv bound flight tried to crash plane
content:
Pilot on Tel Aviv-bound flight tried to crash plane
Passengers on a flydubai flight reached Israel safely on Wednesday after customers and crew foiled a co-pilot's attempt to crash the aircraft, Israeli officials said, in a struggle that began when he stabbed the pilot and sent the jet plunging nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds.
Passengers and crew entered the cockpit, overpowered the co-pilot and enabled a second pair of flydubai pilots who were aboard the flight to land the jet safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, Israeli officials said.
More than 10 hours later, the passengers arrived at Tel Aviv's Ben Gurion Airport aboard a flydubai replacement aircraft, with several describing the episode as a miracle and recounting a frantic struggle to prevent a catastrophe.
Israeli officials said the attacker's motive aboard flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv remained under investigation. Israel and the United Arab Emirates, which includes Dubai, signed the Abraham Accords normalizing relations in 2020.
The incident sharpened concerns about global aviation security in a region scarred by years of conflict, prompting Israel to tighten checks on pilots flying into the country.
"I just can say that it was a miracle. It was awful, crazy, and we thank God that we survived it, we didn't think we will make it but thank God we are in Israel. We are back home. And we are happy to see everyone here," passenger Lital Shachaf said.
Israel's ambulance service said a 51-year-old man was taken to an Israeli hospital to be treated for injuries to his upper body. The man was in a "mild condition," it said.
Describing the event as "a serious security incident," Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Saudi authorities would interrogate the co-pilot.
Flydubai said in a statement that the underlying reasons for the event remained unknown and warned against "premature speculation." An Israeli official identified the co-pilot as an Omani national. There was no immediate comment from Oman.
Israeli officials applauded the passengers, who they credited with avoiding a much more serious disaster. Netanyahu said there were 174 people on board the flight from Dubai, most of them Israeli nationals.
A Netanyahu spokesperson told Reuters that the wounded captain, identified by the Israeli leader's office as Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, was covered with blood on the floor when he managed to click the release to open the cockpit door. Passengers who entered found the co-pilot bashing at the plane's control panel, the spokesperson said. "This is something you do without thinking, just running to save your daughter's life, your family's life," said Asaf Rajuan, one of the passengers who helped restrain the attacker. He spoke with a forehead still bloodied from the struggle.
Netanyahu's office released a video showing the prime minister at Ben Gurion Airport giving a hug to another passenger, Yaniv Hayun, who his office said "broke into" the cockpit. "I see you and I see a lion – a big hero," Netanyahu told the man, who was still wearing the blood-stained shirt he had on during the flight.
Flydubai operates daily return flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv, a route that is popular among Israeli nationals. The flight path normally uses airspace over Saudi Arabia and Jordan.
It is not the first time a flight between Israel and the UAE has landed in Saudi Arabia. A flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv made an emergency landing in Riyadh in September 2025 due to a medical incident, Israeli media reported at the time.
Saudi Arabia's Tabuk airport, where the plane landed, said both pilots had been hospitalised after sustaining injuries.
The incident heightened security fears in Israel weeks before Israelis vote in the first election since the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attacks, with Israel's security figuring prominently in the campaigning.
Responding to the incident on X, far-right security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir wrote, "Terrorism is a devil with whom no agreement must be reached".
Israeli media published conflicting reports on the incident, with some outlets reporting that a pilot had tried to crash the passenger plane in an alleged suicide attempt. Some Israeli media outlets initially identified the pilots as Omani and Emirati nationals, while others said they were Russian and Ukrainian.
"Every pilot that is going to be flying into Israel, we are going to know the pilots' identities, know who they are, and do some type of security check," Doron Spielman, a Netanyahu spokesperson, told Reuters.
Netanyahu met on Sunday with UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan during a rare visit to the Gulf country. Israel and the UAE have forged close security, military and economic ties since establishing diplomatic ties.
Israel provided the UAE earlier this year with Iron Dome air-defence systems and Israeli personnel to operate them, helping defend against Iranian attacks launched after Israel and the US began strikes on Iran.
The UAE government had yet to comment on the flydubai incident, while the Dubai state-owned airline said an "altercation" occurred in the cockpit and the flight subsequently diverted to Tabuk, where it landed safely. The UAE's aviation regulator, the GCAA, said the flight "experienced a security incident that was brought under control".

Asif says all available military capabilities stand ready
Pakistan will use "whatever means are available" to defend Saudi Arabia against Yemen-based Houthi aggressors, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has said, reiterating that any enemy of Saudi Arabia is an enemy of Pakistan.
Speaking to reporters during a visit to Rome, Asif declined to say whether Pakistani forces had already participated in airstrikes in Yemen, but said Pakistan's military capabilities would be available to Saudi Arabia under the new mutual defence pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.
"I'm not going into detail, but obviously when I say that we are bound by this arrangement to defend Saudi Arabia, that means whatever means are available at our disposal, they'll be available to Saudi Arabia also. I think that's a categoric statement," he said.

The Houthis had recently captured the strategic port city of Mokha and several Red Sea islands, extending their reach towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, according to the report. The waterway carries about 12% of global trade.
Describing the Houthis as aggressors, the defence minister said Pakistan's commitment to Saudi Arabia was unambiguous. "Any enemy of Saudi Arabia is enemy of Pakistan. That should be very clear," Asif said.
About the Makkah defence pact, the minister said the new alliance was still taking shape, with the three countries establishing a secretariat and developing its framework. Asif said that other countries had also expressed interest in joining the alliance, but there were currently no plans for its immediate expansion.

title: Islamabad  New Delhi strike cordial SCO note
description: Islamabad  New Delhi strike cordial SCO note
content:
India's SCO envoy warmly greets Ishaq Dar, cordial moment follows fresh UNGA tensions
Despite a fresh exchange of sharp rhetoric between Pakistan and India at the United Nations General Assembly, the two sides appeared to set aside their differences during a multilateral engagement in Islamabad, as India's national coordinator for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) warmly greeted the Pakistan's foreign minister with public handshake.
Alok Dimri, India's SCO National Coordinator and an Additional Secretary at the Ministry of External Affairs, was among the national coordinators attending the first meeting of the SCO Council of National Coordinators under Pakistan's chairmanship of the organisation.
The three-day meeting concluded in Islamabad on Wednesday with the participating national coordinators calling on Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
A video released by the Foreign Office showed Dimri warmly greeted Dar with a handshake. The Indian official was subsequently seen standing between Dar and Pakistan's National Coordinator for the SCO Dr Muhammad Faisal, in what was a strikingly cordial visual given the state of bilateral relations.
The interaction assumed added significance because India and Pakistan had only recently traded barbs at the UN General Assembly in New York.
Indian Foreign Minister S Jaishankar had accused Pakistan of being a "serial practitioner of terrorism" while responding to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's address to the UNGA. Islamabad, meanwhile, strongly rejected India's allegations and defended Pakistan's position on the Kashmir dispute and the 2025 military confrontation between the two nuclear-armed neighbours.
Yet the tone in Islamabad was markedly different.
Speaking to Pakistan Television during his visit, Dimri described his first trip to Pakistan positively and said he was happy to be in Islamabad. He also expressed a desire to visit Lahore, Faisalabad and Sialkot.
"I got to visit Pakistan for the first time. I am happy to visit Islamabad," Dimri said, according to footage released by the Foreign Office.
He said Lahore had been designated an SCO cultural city and suggested that there would be opportunities for the Indian delegation to participate in cultural activities during Pakistan's year-long chairmanship.
Dimri also spoke positively about the SCO's broader agenda, highlighting connectivity, trade, transit and regional prosperity.
His visit marks an important Indian participation in an SCO meeting hosted by Pakistan. While India has maintained that bilateral engagement with Pakistan requires a conducive environment, New Delhi has continued to participate in multilateral SCO processes.
The Islamabad meeting was among the first such senior-level Indian engagements in Pakistan since bilateral ties deteriorated sharply.
Pakistan assumed the SCO's rotating chairmanship for 2026-27 on September 1 and has chosen "Turning Vision into Action: Connectivity, Innovation and Shared Prosperity" as the theme of its presidency.
The national coordinators reviewed the programme of activities planned under Pakistan's chairmanship and discussed preparations for forthcoming SCO meetings and events.
The delegations also visited the Pakistan National Council of the Arts and the Naseer Bunda Hockey Stadium, where they were briefed about preparations for an SCO hockey tournament scheduled for November 20 to December 2.
The significance of the Islamabad meeting, however, goes beyond the routine business of the organisation.
Pakistan is due to host the SCO Council of Heads of State summit in August 2027, bringing the question of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's participation into focus.
India has not yet announced whether Modi will travel to Islamabad.
The Indian government has previously said that a decision on his participation and the level of representation would be taken at the appropriate time.
For now, the presence of India's senior SCO official in Islamabad and the unusually cordial public interaction with Pakistan's foreign minister offers a reminder that even amid intense bilateral tensions, the two countries continue to engage within multilateral forums.
Whether that institutional engagement eventually creates space for a higher-level political interaction remains an open question. For Pakistan, the SCO summit in 2027 could provide precisely such a moment, with all eyes likely to be on whether Modi chooses to travel to Islamabad.

title: Clemency must follow law
description: Clemency must follow law
content:
FCC rules executive remission cannot override statutory limits
The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has ruled that executive clemency and remission must operate within the framework prescribed by law, holding that the objectives of punishment, public protection and the authority of judicial sentences must remain paramount.
"Judicial sympathy cannot be permitted to override statutory commands," said a judgment authored by Justice Rozi Khan Barrech. Justice Barrech was leading a division bench which heard an appeal filed by Suba Khan, who was sentenced to life imprisonment in 2015.
The convict subsequently obtained general and special remissions from the executive authorities on several occasions. The case concerned the legality of the remissions granted to him and the preparation and issuance of his nominal rolls.
Nominal rolls are issued by the prison department, which functions under the supervision of the Inspector General of Prisons and the administrative control of the provincial home department under the relevant laws.
According to the nominal roll submitted in the case, Suba Khan had undergone nine years, four months and 19 days of imprisonment, while he had been credited with 15 years, seven months and 18 days of ordinary and special remission.
On the basis of that calculation, the nominal roll showed that he was required to undergo only a further five months and 23 days of imprisonment. The Balochistan High Court (BHC) declared all the remissions granted to him illegal. Suba Khan subsequently approached the FCC against the BHC judgment.
In the FCC verdict said judicial sympathy cannot be permitted to override statutory commands particularly where a sentence is related to a heinous offence and the legislature has deliberately prescribed safeguards to ensure that life imprisonment retained its substantive penal content.
"To hold otherwise would not only undermine the integrity of the sentencing process but would also erode public confidence in the fair and lawful administration of criminal justice," the judgment said.
The FCC held that the excess remission granted to the petitioner could not lawfully reduce his imprisonment below the minimum period prescribed under Rules 140 and 217(ii) of the Pakistan Prison Rules, 1978.
"Hence, the remissions granted to the petitioner in excess does not meet the minimum threshold of fifteen years of imprisonment as provided in Rule 140 and 217(ii) of the Rules 1978," the judgment said.
The court observed that the gravity of an offence and the culpability of an offender had to be considered alongside the statutory remission scheme, which represented the legislature's calibrated balance between encouraging good conduct in prison and preserving the integrity of punishment imposed by a court.
It said that when remissions were granted beyond statutory limits, or calculated in a manner that effectively nullified the minimum period of imprisonment prescribed for life convicts, the penal consequences determined by the sentencing court were substantially diluted.
"Such an outcome undermines the deterrent and retributive purposes of criminal punishment, diminishes public confidence in the administration of criminal justice, and frustrates the legislative intent underlying Rule 217 of Rules 1978 and other enabling rules," the court said.
The FCC further held that the remissions granted to Suba Khan had defeated the legislative intent behind the relevant prison rules.
"A remission granted or computed in derogation of the express provisions of the Prison Rules cannot confer an enforceable legal right, nor can this Court lend its imprimatur to an administrative action that travels beyond the authority conferred by law," the judgment said.
The court also examined comparative jurisprudence and international standards concerning executive clemency and prison remission. It observed that these authorities affirmed that remission must remain within the legal framework established by the legislature, while reform and rehabilitation of prisoners should be encouraged without compromising statutory limits.
The judgment also referred to the Nelson Mandela Rules, the United Nations Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners.

title: New checks target offloadings
description: New checks target offloadings
content:
Govt begins pre-immigration scrutiny at airports
Government authorities have begun pre-immigration scrutiny of passengers travelling abroad to prevent them from being offloaded at airports and suffering financial and legal difficulties.
According to official sources, the FIA, passport authorities and Protector of Emigrants staff have been mobilised at international airports across the country, including Lahore, to check passengers' travel documents before their departure.
The move follows a request by the Overseas Employment Association for the authorities to examine passengers' documents and visas before they reach the immigration counter.
Under the new arrangement, passengers travelling abroad for employment, tourism, Umrah or religious pilgrimage will undergo pre-immigration clearance by FIA immigration officials before being allowed to proceed with their international journey.
Officials said the measures were introduced following incidents involving some Pakistani passengers travelling to countries including Azerbaijan and Bahrain who subsequently disappeared, travelled illegally or were deported.
The pre-immigration process aims to prevent illegal travel and protect passengers from financial and legal complications, FIA officials said. They said passengers whose documents were incomplete or who failed to provide satisfactory answers to questions raised by immigration officials could previously face offloading at the airport at the time of departure.
Under the new mechanism, such issues would be identified and addressed before passengers reach the final stage of immigration clearance. The authorities are particularly focusing on the validity and completeness of travel documents, visas and other papers required for entry into the destination.
Officials said the initiative would also help prevent passengers from becoming victims of fraudulent or improper travel arrangements, particularly in cases involving overseas employment.
They said passengers who are offloaded after reaching the airport often suffer substantial financial losses because their air tickets and visa fees may become non-refundable. According to officials, such incidents had caused losses running into hundreds of millions of rupees to Pakistani travellers.
On September 18, the Islamabad High Court (IHC) allowed a citizen, who had been placed on a travel restriction list and offloaded at the airport, to travel abroad, while questioning the FIA's authority to take such measures under its internal standard operating procedures (SOPs).
Justice Inaam Ameen Minhas, while hearing a petition filed by the off-loaded citizen, expressed displeasure with FIA officials and directed the agency's additional director to submit a response explaining the legal basis for offloading passengers and placing their names on travel restriction lists.

title: TTAP irked by PPP leader s  U turn
description: TTAP irked by PPP leader s  U turn
content:
Bukhari says he has not changed his position on governor's rule
The Tehreek-e-Tahaffuz-e-Aain Pakistan (TTAP) has conveyed its reservations to Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) leaders over General Secretary Nayyar Hussain Bukhari's alleged abrupt change in position on the possible imposition of governor's rule or an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, a TTAP spokesperson said.
However, Bukhari denied making any U-turn on the matter, maintaining that the issue never came up for discussion between the two sides during their meeting.
TTAP, on the other hand, claimed that it suspected the PPP general secretary had been compelled to change his earlier position under external pressure.
According to the alliance, Bukhari had called for all political parties to sit together to break the perpetual cycle of political instability and ensure that democratic principles were upheld, while describing the imposition of governor's rule as unconstitutional. He had been unequivocal in his position, TTAP representatives claimed.
Talking to The Express Tribune, Akhundzada Hussain said he was surprised to see statements attributed to Bukhari on Wednesday, suggesting that his party would consider the option of imposing governor's rule, and governor's rule could be imposed on the governor's recommendation in case of failure of the provincial government, which, he said, contradicted the position Bukhari had previously taken.
He said TTAP had conveyed its reservations to PPP Chairman Bilawal through another senior party leader and would prefer to engage directly with the chairman's office from now onwards.
Asked about PM's Adviser Rana Sanaullah's remarks during a television programme, in which he was asked whether the PML-N would be invited to the proposed APC, Hussain said the PML-N would certainly not be invited.

"We are allies in the government, so when they move forward and seek our proposal, we will give our suggestions. Without any proposal being placed before us, how can we give our position on the matter?" he said.
Bukhari said the delegation led by PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar had met him solely to extend an invitation to the PPP for the APC. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry on Wednesday said that the federal government was "seriously considering" imposing emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.
Chaudhry, while speaking to the media at the Parliament House, again referred to the security situation in K-P and said the federal government was "seriously considering" the imposition of emergency in the province.
"The provincial government's lack of interest or success in controlling it (terrorism) is the reason for which the imposition of emergency under Article 232 is being discussed," he said, expressing confidence that the PPP - an ally of the ruling PML-N in the Centre - would also cooperate in this regard.
Meanwhile, Information Minister Atta Tarar said the PTI had become "politically weak" and questioned whether Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had the political strength to launch a long march.
Talking to the media in Islamabad, the minister said the provincial government's "failure of governance" was evident, accusing it of failing to curb terrorism in the province.
He said the federal government provided funds every year under the National Finance Commission (NFC) to combat terrorism, yet major attacks had occurred in Kohat and Dera Ismail Khan.
"The provincial government should abandon politics and go where people are being killed," Tarar said, stressing that ending terrorism should take priority over political activities.
He said the question of imposing governor's rule in K-P was premature, adding that the situation in the province had deteriorated across sectors, including health and education.
Tarar said he had visited Kohat, Charsadda and Peshawar and witnessed the province's "governance failures". Recalling his visit to the home of slain Constable Faheemullah, he said, "Bodies are falling in K-P. Politics will continue, but people must first be protected from terrorism."
The minister alleged that the Afghan government was supporting terrorism and said Pakistan had given a strong response and would continue to do so.
Meanwhile, sources said no meeting had been held under Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to discuss the imposition of governor's rule or an emergency in K-P.
According to the sources, the prime minister would make a decision on the province's political situation after consulting the senior leadership.
The clarification came amid speculation over possible measures in K-P, including the imposition of emergency or governor's rule.
The prime minister recently returned to Pakistan after completing a 13-day visit to the United States and the United Kingdom, during which he represented Pakistan at the United Nations General Assembly and held meetings with world leaders and business figures. PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Wednesday said the party's planned October 4 long march would remain a peaceful and political activity, urging the government to avoid imposing measures such as governor rule or emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.

title: E filing rules ease property cases overseas
description: E filing rules ease property cases overseas
content:
Overseas Pakistanis can file, attend hearings remotely
The government has issued the E-Filing Rules 2026 for property-related cases involving overseas Pakistanis, introducing an online system for filing property-related petitions, submitting documents and accessing court proceedings.
Under the new rules, overseas Pakistanis can file applications and submit relevant documents electronically before designated special courts without needing to appear physically for every procedural step.
The rules also provide for hearings through video link, allowing overseas litigants to participate in court proceedings remotely. Electronic notices will be served to overseas Pakistanis, and various judicial facilities will also be available through the online system.
Court judgments and decrees will be uploaded on the designated online portal, enabling litigants to access them electronically. The rules also prescribe a mechanism for preserving electronic evidence and maintaining court records in digital form.
The rules allow paper filing in specified circumstances where electronic filing is not possible. An alternative filing mechanism is prescribed for disruptions in the online system, ensuring litigants are not deprived of access to the courts due to a system malfunction.
The new framework is aimed at facilitating overseas Pakistanis involved in property disputes by reducing the need for physical visits to Pakistan and providing them greater access to judicial proceedings through digital means.

title: Sindh records country s biggest rainfall deficit
description: Sindh records country s biggest rainfall deficit
content:
Province gets 51% less rain; Karachi faces 92% shortfall
Sindh remained Pakistan's driest province during this year's monsoon season, receiving 50.8% less rainfall than normal. Karachi recorded an exceptional 92% deficit in rainfall from July to September, according to data released by the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD).
The PMD data showed that Pakistan received a total of 120.5 millimetres of rainfall between July 1 and September 30, which was 19.3% below the normal level for the period.
Sindh received only 71.1mm of rainfall during the three-month monsoon period, 50.8% below normal, making it the province with the lowest rainfall during the season. Karachi experienced an even more pronounced shortfall, with rainfall during the monsoon season remaining 92% below normal.
Balochistan also recorded significantly below-normal rainfall, with a deficit of 33.7%, followed by Azad Jammu and Kashmir with 18.4%, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa with 16.3% and Punjab with 3.8% less rainfall than normal.
Gilgit-Baltistan was the only region in the country to receive above-normal rainfall during the monsoon season. The region recorded rainfall 4.6% above its normal level.
According to the PMD, the formation and effects of the El Nino climate pattern were major meteorological factors contributing to this year's below-normal monsoon rainfall. The department had earlier indicated that the development of El Nino could weaken monsoon activity over South Asia.
El Nino causes changes in global and regional weather systems, which can influence the intensity and distribution of monsoon rainfall across South Asia. The PMD said that monsoon rainfall was also significantly below normal in Pakistan's neighbouring countries this year.
The rainfall deficit has implications for water availability, agriculture and weather patterns across the country, particularly in Sindh, where the shortfall was most pronounced.
Moreover after many years, Pakistan is bracing for a water shortage of around 25 per cent during the Rabi season starting this week, raising concerns about food security next year as wheat is the season's main crop.

title: Photo exhibition depicts Sindh s post flood plight
description: Photo exhibition depicts Sindh s post flood plight
content:
'The Too-Young Monsoon Wives' highlights province's travails
A photography exhibition documenting the impact of climate change, catastrophic flooding, poverty and child marriage in Sindh opened in Karachi on Tuesday, bringing into focus the stories of young girls whose lives were shaped by environmental disasters.
Titled "The Too-Young Monsoon Wives," the exhibition features the work of French photographer Isabeau de Rouffignac, who travelled to Sindh following the devastating floods and photographed communities dealing with the aftermath of the disaster.
The three-day exhibition is being presented by Alliance Française de Karachi in collaboration with the French Embassy in Pakistan and Avari Towers.
Rouffignac's photographs explore the social consequences of flooding beyond the immediate destruction caused by rising waters. Among the stories she documented were those of families who married their daughters at a very young age in the aftermath of the floods.
The exhibition combines photographs with short texts that provide context about the girls and their experiences, highlighting the link between poverty, climate-related disasters and child marriage.
Speaking at the opening, Director of Alliance Française de Karachi Emmanuel Breurec said the photographer had travelled to Sindh during the catastrophic floods and documented their consequences.
"The French photographer Isabeau de Rouffignac is presenting this exhibition with Alliance Française. She came to Pakistan, to Sindh, during the catastrophic floods and took pictures of the consequences that happened there after the floods. She found that one of the consequences was that families had to marry their daughters too early. So, it is their story, actually. You can see the pictures and a little text about those girls being married at a very early age."
Breurec said Rouffignac could not attend the opening in person but had sent a video message for the event.

title: 'Michael' becomes first-ever biopic to pass $1b worldwide | The Express Tribune
description:
'Michael' becomes first-ever 
biopic to pass $1b worldwide
content:
Film on late pop icon Michael Jackson is now among the biggest releases of 2026
Michael, the Michael Jackson biopic starring his nephew Jaafar Jackson, has completed its worldwide theatrical run with approximately $1.029bn at the global box office, according to Box Office Mojo. The final total stands at $1,028,706,645, including $372,303,388 from the United States and Canada and $656,403,257 from international markets.
The result places Michael among the biggest releases of 2026 and makes it the highest grossing biopic recorded at the worldwide box office. The film previously became the first biopic to cross the $1bn milestone in July, surpassing Oppenheimer and Bohemian Rhapsody in the process.
Directed by Antoine Fuqua, Michael stars Jaafar Jackson as his late uncle and follows the singer's early life, his rise with the Jackson 5 and his development into one of the most recognised performers in music history. Colman Domingo plays Joseph Jackson, while Nia Long portrays Katherine Jackson.
The film opened internationally in April, with Box Office Mojo recording a domestic opening of $97.2m. Its worldwide performance was driven particularly strongly by international markets, which accounted for about 63.8% of the final gross.
The billion dollar milestone was confirmed by Lionsgate and Universal in July, when the studios announced that the film had passed $1bn worldwide. At that stage, Michael had already become Lionsgate's first release to reach the figure.
The final tally gives the film a substantial theatrical run despite the discussion surrounding its portrayal of Jackson's life. Its commercial performance also places Jaafar Jackson's first major screen role at the centre of one of 2026's biggest box office stories.
With the theatrical run now complete, Michael leaves behind a billion dollar worldwide total and a new benchmark for biographical films.
Development began in November 2019, when it was reported that Graham King had secured the rights to produce a film about Jackson, with Logan attached to write. Lionsgate announced the film in February 2022. In January 2023, Fuqua was announced as the director, and Jaafar was cast as Michael. Further casting took place from January to April 2024.
After delays caused by the 2023 SAG-AFTRA strike, principal photography took place between January and May 2024. After a clause was discovered in a legal settlement, references to the 1993 child sexual abuse allegations against Michael were removed, the third act was revised, and reshoots took place in June 2025, bringing the production budget to $155200 million.
Michael premiered at the Uber Eats Music Hall in Berlin on April 10, 2026, and was released on April 22 in the UK by Universal Pictures and on April 24 in the US by Lionsgate. It received generally negative reviews from critics, who praised Jaafar's performance but criticized the story as "sanitized". It grossed $1.029 billion worldwide, making it the highest-grossing biographical film, the first biographical film to reach $1 billion, the highest-grossing Lionsgate film and the fourth-highest-grossing film of 2026. A sequel is in development.
On the review aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, 38% of 307 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 4.9/10.
The website's consensus reads: "While Jaafar Jackson's smooth moves bring the King of Pop to uncanny life, this musical biopic mostly plays like a 'greatest hits' album that could've benefitted from including liner notes to give actual insight into the icon." Metacritic, which uses a weighted average, assigned the film a score of 39 out of 100, based on 51 critics, indicating "generally unfavorable" reviews. Audiences polled by CinemaScore gave the film an average grade of "A?" on an A+ to F scale, while those surveyed by PostTrak gave it a 90% positive score, with 84% saying they would definitely recommend it.
Owen Gleiberman of Variety called Michael a "surprisingly effective middle-of-the-road biopic". He praised Jaafar's performance, writing that he "nails the look, the voice, the electrostatic moves - and the mix of delicacy and steel that made Michael who he was".
Pete Hammond of Deadline Hollywood wrote: "You are bound to leave this one dancing. And what is wrong with that?" Abhimanyu Mathur of the Hindustan Times gave Michael four out of five, describing it as a "fun, soulful" film that "hits all the right notes" and praising Jaafar, but noted pacing and structural problems, including a lack of focus on Michael's brothers.
Writing for Prothom Alo, the University of Chittagong professor Moshreka Aditi Haq praised Jaafar Jackson's performance, the depiction of Michael Jackson's childhood and artistic development, and its exploration of themes of freedom, rebellion, and creativity.

Sia and Bernad were married for less than three years. Sia's attorney, Laura Wasser, filed divorce documents in March 2025.
The catalogue sale comes as the former couple continue to navigate financial and custody matters following their separation. Sia has also agreed to pay Bernad $42,500 per month in child support, according to the report.
The $180 million music catalogue deal highlights the significant financial value of Sia's songwriting catalogue, which includes some of the most recognisable pop songs of the past decade. The transaction gives Pophouse a 50% stake in the rights covered by the agreement while providing Sia with a substantial payout.

Attackers remain unidentified as bus carrying workers comes under fire in Homs province
A shooting attack on a bus in central Syria on Wednesday killed seven people and left four others wounded, state media reported.
The perpetrators of the shooting in Homs province have not yet been identified, the official news agency Sana added.
A security source who requested anonymity had initially given AFP a preliminary toll of five dead.
Among the bus passengers were "engineers and workers from a private company" and an employee of the Syrian Electricity Company, who is among the victims, the security source said.
Syrian authorities have been facing major security challenges since the fall of Bashar al-Assad's regime at the end of 2024, with Damascus and its outskirts hit by several attacks.
Shortly before the bus attack, state media reported an explosion at a gas pipeline near one of the country's main power plants, close to Damascus, two days after the sabotage of another pipeline in eastern Syria.
On August 22, a bomb attack on a bus carrying members of the Syrian internal security forces near Damascus injured several people.
In early August, a bus explosion in Jaramana, a town near Damascus where Christian and Druze communities live, left 14 people wounded.
In July, two explosions occurred near a hotel where French President Emmanuel Macron was staying during an official visit, although he was not there at the time.
Those blasts killed one person and wounded 36. The authorities later announced the arrest of those responsible, saying they belonged to the Islamic State group.

Lili Reinhart and Tom Bateman reunite to narrate Quinn’s immersive audio romance 'Olympus U', a Hades retelling
Lili Reinhart and Tom Bateman are teaming up again for Olympus U , a three-episode immersive audio romance for Quinn, following their work together on Prime Video’s The Love Hypothesis .
The actors will narrate the Quinn Original, written by Kate Goldbeck, which offers a modern retelling of the Greek myth of Hades and Persephone. Fake dating. Hades x Persephone. And a mind-reading bond. Welcome to Olympus U. ⚡️🏛️ pic.twitter.com/eKdercnnHY

Olympus U is the third Quinn Original duet production, following Ember & Ice , featuring Heated Rivalry stars Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie, and Rent Free , starring Off Campus actors Mika Abdalla and Stephen Kalyn.

Sindh Engro Coal Mining Company (SECMC), Pakistan's largest open-pit lignite coal mining company, began operations at Thar Block-II in 2019, and developed the project in phases to support the country's growing energy requirements and reduce reliance on imported fuels.
Now, the third phase of the mine's expansion is set to commence on October 5, further increasing the mine's capacity and expanding the use of indigenous coal. The phase-III expansion will increase the mine's annual production capacity from 7.6 million tonnes to 11.2 million tonnes.

Additionally, sentiment was supported by steps being taken to strengthen the domestic financial and energy framework, with the Ministry of Finance unveiling a strategic action plan for the local currency bond market and the government considering direct LNG import by power plants and private companies. According to Arif Habib Limited (AHL) Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib, the PSX experienced a positive trading session, where the benchmark KSE-100 index gained 369 points (+0.22%) to close at 169,969, just below the key psychological level of 170k, thereby ending September 2026 below the milestone.

title: AI boom lifts Asia Pacific equity deals
description: AI boom lifts Asia Pacific equity deals
content:
Fundraising surges 53% to $327b, set to challenge 2021 record
Asia-Pacific companies are poised to challenge their 2021 record for share and convertible bond fundraising this year, as an AI boom drives investment in chips, data centres and power systems.
Companies in Asia-Pacific raised $327.1 billion through equity deals this year, up 53% from a year earlier, LSEG data showed. The record annual high was $557.6 billion in 2021, when issuers had raised $399.7 billion by the end of September. Asia-Pacific companies raised $327.1 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 53% year-on-year, as follow-ons and convertibles outpaced IPOs.
"At year-end, we expect issuance to exceed 2021, which was the historical high, underscoring the scale of the capital-raising cycle we are seeing around AI," said James Wang, Head of Asia Ex-Japan Equity Capital Markets at Goldman Sachs. "AI will continue to drive market volumes over the next one to two years."
The region needs $230.6 billion in the final quarter to beat the 2021 record. That would be a quarterly record, but bankers expect more share sales and convertible bond issues. The known pipeline includes Australian AI infrastructure firm Firmus, Singaporean data centre operator DayOne and Chinese flash memory chipmaker Yangtze Memory Technologies Co that could raise about $5 billion each.
Dealogic data showed Asia-Pacific IPOs and new listings due to price by year-end could raise $10.4 billion, including Mynt's $1.3 billion Philippine IPO and Samsung Biologics' $2.2 billion South Korean rights issue. Reliance Jio Platforms, Reliance Industries' digital arm, has won approval for a Mumbai IPO that could raise about $3.8 billion. Deloitte China expects three to four more Hong Kong mega-listings of at least HK$10 billion ($1.3 billion) each.
Companies are raising funds for AI chips, data centres and power. High-technology firms raised $125.8 billion, or 38% of the total, over three times a year earlier, LSEG data showed. Third-quarter deals showed appetite. South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix raised $26.5 billion in a Nasdaq share sale, while Chinese optical-networking equipment maker Zhongji Innolight raised $7.8 billion in Hong Kong.
But the rush of deals is also making investors more selective, bankers said. "We're seeing some signs" of investor caution after the heavy supply of deals, though the market remains open and companies can still raise funds if terms are more reasonable than two or three months ago, said Kenneth Chow, Asia-Pacific Head of ECM origination and Products at Citigroup.

title: Apparel industry pledges to ramp up exports
description: Apparel industry pledges to ramp up exports
content:
New PRGMEA leadership to focus on GSP+, US tariffs and green compliance
The Pakistan Readymade Garments Manufacturers & Exporters Association (PRGMEA) has elected Sohail Afzal Sheikh as its central chairman for the 2026-28 term. The new leadership has pledged to strengthen apparel exports at a time when the industry is dealing with new tariffs, high energy costs and tighter buyer requirements.
Aamir Lakhani has been elected senior vice chairman and Ansar Aziz Puri vice chairman. "The industry is entering a period of significant transformation, with sustainability, digitalisation, traceability, changing trade policies and evolving buyer requirements becoming increasingly important for global competitiveness," said Sohail Afzal.
He said Pakistan's apparel industry must prepare for new requirements such as the European Union's Digital Product Passport and wider sustainability and supply-chain rules. He stressed the need to invest in energy efficiency, renewable energy, resource efficiency, decarbonisation and digital systems to keep and expand access to international markets.
Sheikh also called for protecting GSP+ market access, addressing the impact of US tariffs and diversifying export markets. He said the government should improve the ease of doing business through competitive energy tariffs, timely refunds and rebates, simpler regulations, better access to finance and efficient trade facilitation.
The new team takes over as Pakistan's textile sector shows a modest growth. Textile and clothing exports rose 5.55% to $3.4 billion in July-August 2026-27 from $3.2 billion in the same period of last year, according to the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics data.
Readymade garments did better than most categories, with exports rising 13.59% in the first two months of the current fiscal year to $827 million.
The annual numbers show how little growth the sector managed to achieve last year. Textile exports in the previous fiscal year were up only 0.26% at $17.93 billion, while readymade garment exports rose 3.87% to $4.29 billion.
Sheikh added that the association would continue its international engagement, including through sending a delegation to COP31 in Antalya, Turkiye. It will present Pakistan's apparel industry views on climate action, textile decarbonisation and sustainable global supply chains.
The new leadership said it would focus on export growth, policy advocacy, market access, sustainability, digital transformation and cooperation between the industry and government.

title: No more war impact  govt tells IMF
description: No more war impact  govt tells IMF
content:
Lender urges adjustments in Pakistan's exchange rate, interest policies
Pakistan has apprised the International Monetary Fund (IMF) that the Middle East conflict will no longer impact its economic outlook, with inflation projected to slow down to 7.5% and the external sector remaining stable, but the global lender has urged it to adjust exchange and interest rate policies.
The federal government further informed the IMF that exports would hit $34 billion and foreign remittances would increase to $45.5 billion in the current fiscal year – better than the budget targets with no adverse impact on imports. It said that this would keep the external sector in a stable situation with the current account deficit remaining between $2.5 billion and $3 billion but significantly lower than the budget target of $3.6 billion.
In a briefing on the economic outlook for the current fiscal year, the federal government predicted a stable exchange rate instead of any devaluation and an easing of inflation in the second half of the year, Pakistani authorities told The Express Tribune.
They said that the central bank in separate meetings also predicted a slowing inflation rate, stable exchange rate and a stable external account. The central bank is said to have informed the IMF that its policy rate at 11.5% was already appropriately tight to tame inflation.
The IMF's detailed response to the government and the central bank's macroeconomic forecast is expected in the next few days. But sources said that the global lender again urged the authorities to implement a market-based exchange rate regime and also appropriately tighten the monetary policy to tame inflation.
The sources said that neither the central bank nor the federal government saw any immediate need for adjustments in the exchange rate and interest rate policies.
They said that the IMF was informed that lower reliance on food imports would generate foreign exchange savings, strengthen the external position and reduce reliance on external financing. The lender was further briefed that the exchange rate would remain stable.
The federal government's assessment was that a key factor in its forecast of slowing inflation was the exchange rate stability. The lender was told that during the first quarter of the current fiscal year, the exchange rate remained around Rs278 to a dollar, stronger than the budget assumption of Rs286 per dollar. Supported by a sustainable current account position and historic high foreign exchange reserves, the exchange rate is expected to remain broadly stable and is likely to limit imported inflation, according to the federal government's assessment.
The IMF was informed that if the situation normalised until October 2026 and the average Brent crude price stabilised at $80 per barrel in the current fiscal year, the projected inflation would remain at 7.5%. If the oil price remains at around $100 per barrel till December, the projected inflation may increase to 8.2% for the fiscal year. The government has set the inflation target for this fiscal year at 8.2%, but it said that due to an anticipated moderation in global crude oil prices, improved agricultural output, exchange rate stability, effective administrative measures and a favourable base effect during the second half, the inflation is projected to remain within the 7% to 8% range, with the most likely outcome being around 7.5%.
Its assessment of taming inflation was that price pressures would remain elevated till December, but thereafter, they were expected to moderate gradually over the course of the year, reflecting improving domestic supply conditions and a relatively favourable external outlook. Pakistani authorities were of the view that, supported by resilient remittance inflows, improving export performance and strong reserve buffers, the external sector was expected to remain stable in the current fiscal year. They informed the IMF that the current account deficit was now projected at around $2.5 billion to $3 billion, equivalent to 0.5-0.6% of GDP. The annual target is $3.6 billion.
Federal authorities have projected exports to peak at $34 billion, compared to the $32.5 billion budget target. They are of the view that an increasing trend in global rice prices is expected to support higher export earnings by at least an additional $300 million.
The fund has been apprised that imports of goods are projected at $69-70 billion, which is in line with the annual target and will not have any adverse impact. During the first two months of this fiscal year, the import bill of petroleum crude increased by 40.5%, while petroleum products declined by 26%. Similarly, LPG imports rose by 47%, while LNG declined by 28.6%.
The federal authorities were of the view that the food import bill was expected to remain contained due to higher domestic production of both food and oilseed crops, particularly canola, sunflower and rapeseed. Likewise, remittances are projected to hit $45.5 billion in this fiscal year, which is better than the annual target and will have a positive impact on the external account. Remittances grew by 14.7% during the first two months of this fiscal year.
The IMF was told that despite the Middle East conflict, the government would achieve its annual growth target of 4%. The government's assessment was that the ongoing conflict won't further dent growth, as it had already set a lower target compared to the initial projection of 5% growth in the current fiscal year. But it said that the changing global conditions, particularly the Middle East conflict, higher oil prices, supply disruptions and renewed inflationary pressures, have created downside risks.

OPEC+ oil-producing countries are likely to keep their oil production targets steady for November when they meet on Sunday, two sources with knowledge of the matter said.
The online meeting of seven core OPEC+ members – Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman – comes as Gulf members are boosting exports that have been disrupted for months by the US-Iran war, although most are still pumping well below their output targets. OPEC+ comprises the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies including Russia. The group has been raising its output targets for most of the year but kept them steady for October.
In September, it completed the phased rollback of a 1.65-million-barrel-per-day supply cut first agreed in 2023.
OPEC data showed the seven core OPEC+ producers produced 25 million barrels per day in August, up 630,000 bpd from July.

title: Overlap in auto environmental standards flagged
description: Overlap in auto environmental standards flagged
content:
Science & technology ministry identifies duplication of PSQCA functions
The Ministry of Science and Technology has sought to withdraw a decision regarding the adoption of environmental, safety and quality standards for imported vehicles.
The ministry has proposed that the Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) revisit its earlier decision, dated September 24, 2025, and modify it to the extent of formulating environmental, safety and quality standards, testing and certification requirements, as it led to duplication of functions with the mandate entrusted to the Pakistan Standards and Quality Control Authority (PSQCA) under the Rules of Business 1973 and the PSQCA Act 1996.
It wanted the ECC to direct the Ministry of Commerce to amend its notification regarding Clause 11 of SRO 61(1)/2026 dated January 15, 2026 by deleting some phrases. It also asked for directing the Ministry of Commerce to amend Clause (xvi) of SRO 1895 dated September 30, 2025 and delete the text that was creating duplication of functions of the PSQCA.
It further requested that the Ministry of Industries and Production be directed to withdraw its notification EDB/Auto/Import/WP-29/2025, dated September 30, 2025, regarding the adoption of environmental, safety and quality standards for imported vehicles.
It emphasised that the Ministry of Commerce should withdraw the decisions made in the meeting held on March 16, 2026 regarding the requirement for the PSQCA to obtain a no-objection certificate from the Engineering Development Board (EDB) for the registration of automobile pre-shipment inspection (PSI) agencies. The PSQCA, as per Section 8 (xxiii), is empowered to register the inspection agencies. SRO 2443, dated December 16, 2025, also empowers the PSQCA for the same.
The Ministry of Science and Technology requested the ECC for approval of the proposals to avoid the overlapping of functions and encroachment on the mandate of the Ministry of S&T/PSQCA.
During the ensuing discussion, it was informed by the Ministry of Industries that a committee had already been constituted under the minister of climate change to deliberate on the matter in detail, following which the agenda was deferred till the finalisation of recommendations of the committee. The forum gave the directive that relevant ministries be requested for their views, before sending any proposal to the ECC.
The ECC considered a summary submitted by the Ministry of Science and Technology titled "Review/ Revisit of ECC Decision in Case No 172/22/2025 Dated 24.09.2025 Regarding Automobile Standards & Regulations" and deferred the agenda.
The S&T ministry briefed the ECC that the PSQCA was a statutory body working under the administrative control of the Ministry of Science and Technology (MoS&T) and that as per the PSQCA Act 1996, the national standards body was mandated to formulate, adopt and notify standards (including automobile standards), undertake conformity assessment activities, register inspection bodies and monitor the quality of products.
The ministry said that, as per Serial No 36 of Schedule-I of the Rules of Business 1973 pertaining to the Science & Technology Division, sub-rule 12, 30, 31 & 32 specifically mentioned the formulation of standards as the sole mandate of the PSQCA.
It pointed out that the Ministry of Industries had submitted the draft Motor Vehicles Industry Development Act (MVIDA) 2025 for review and comments. The S&T ministry, in its earlier office memorandum dated July 18, 2025, inadvertently issued a no-objection to the Ministry of Industries regarding the MVIDA Act. However, the same was subsequently withdrawn vide a letter sent on April 16, 2026, being inconsistent with the prevailing legal framework and statutory mandates of the EDB/Ministry of Industries.
The S&T ministry informed the ECC that in pursuance of its legal mandate, the PSQCA had already undertaken comprehensive initiatives for the development and adoption of automobile standards, including those for buses, cars, tractors, etc. Recently, the ministry has obtained approval of the federal cabinet for the standards of public services vehicles (buses), formulated/adopted by the PSQCA as per directives of the prime minister.
The ministry added that while the draft Motor Vehicle Industries Development Act was pending for discussion, the Ministry of Commerce sent a summary to the ECC dated September 24, 2025 titled "Removal of Quantitative Restriction on Commercial Import of Used Vehicles", upon which the following proposals were approved by the ECC and subsequently ratified by the federal cabinet.

title: Iqbal calls for creating CAREC knowledge hub
description: Iqbal calls for creating CAREC knowledge hub
content:
Region must move from infrastructure to information sharing to tackle challenges
Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal on Wednesday proposed transforming the Carec Institute into a trusted regional knowledge clearing house to turn the experience of member countries into practical solutions for shared economic and development challenges.
Addressing the Governing Council meeting of the Carec Institute in Ulaanbaatar, he said that after 25 years of building roads, railways, energy links and trade corridors, the next phase of regional cooperation must focus not only on moving goods and energy but also on sharing knowledge and expertise across borders.
He proposed a living Carec knowledge platform and expert directory bringing together regional data, policy tools, project evaluations and practical experiences, enabling policymakers to quickly identify what had worked elsewhere and adapt successful approaches to their own challenges.
The minister also called for establishing a Carec peer exchange facility to connect officials facing similar challenges, particularly in trade facilitation, digital customs, logistics, renewable energy, disaster response, agriculture and skills development.
He stressed that the institute's work should be demand-driven, closely linked to policy decisions and measured by practical impact.
Ahsan Iqbal underscored stronger regional cooperation in coordinated border management, interoperable digital trade systems and shared climate-risk information, saying that common challenges required coordinated regional responses.
As Pakistan prepares to assume the Carec chairmanship in 2027, he said Islamabad would place knowledge exchange at the centre of its agenda and work with Carec member countries, the institute and the Asian Development Bank on economic corridors, trade facilitation, digital connectivity and climate resilience.
He offered Pakistan's experience with the Pakistan Single Window as an early case for regional peer exchange and said the country would encourage its universities and research institutions to join the Carec regional knowledge network.
