title: If reset is needed for good governance  then it should happen  DG ISPR
description: Military spokesperson says Pakistan  not a hard state  while briefing on on Balochistan security situation
content:
Good governance is key to security and stability of Pakistan, says military spokesperson
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry on Friday said an administrative reset, if required, should be undertaken to ensure good governance, stressing that any such change must be carried out through constitutional and legal means and in accordance with the will of the people.
He addressed a press conference, where he primarily spoke about Balochistan and AJK and briefed the media on the overall security situation in the country.
"The will of the people of Pakistan is superior. If good governance requires an administrative reset, then it has to be done through constitutional methods, legal procedures and political representatives,” he said.
On Thursday, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said that Pakistan's existing governance system had collapsed and was no longer capable of addressing the country's challenges, calling for administrative reforms, including the creation of new administrative units, echoing the demand put forward by several political parties to create more provinces for better governance.
Responding to a question on whether he agreed with the remarks that the governance system in Balochistan had failed, the DG ISPR said he would not comment on the minister's statement.
However, he stated that good governance was essential for Pakistan's security and stability. "As a primary stakeholder in security, we would like to say that good governance is the key to security and stability. Without that, your issues cannot be solved," he said.
The DG ISPR referred to the National Action Plan (NAP), saying it reflected a consensus among political parties over the past 12 years. "There is a National Action Plan that is an agreed consensus, which has 14 points, on which all political parties over the last 12 years have had consensus, whether they are in power or not," he said.
"The first point is related to kinetics, but the other 13 — creating narratives, choking terror financing, tackling the illegal spectrum, including narcotics and smuggling, capacity building, repatriation of refugees and many other measures — all depend on good governance. So yes, good governance is quintessential for Pakistan."
Asked how such governance could be achieved, the DG ISPR said the issue should be debated by political parties and those in government. "How to get that good governance is for the politicians and the political parties," he said.
"But if you ask us, yes, there has to be a serious discussion because these issues are not being solved, which means something needs to be done," he added.
The military spokesperson said Pakistan's population had increased significantly since the 1972 census and governance structures should be reviewed accordingly.
"I think it was the 1972 census that recorded a population of 65 million. Today we are around 250 million. If your population has increased almost fivefold, we have to see whether this is serving good governance," he said.
The DG ISPR said the debate should be led by elected representatives. "That debate has to be essentially done by those in power, by politicians and those who are responsible for this for the people of Pakistan," he said.
"The answer lies in the will of the people of Pakistan. The will of the people of Pakistan is supreme."
"If good governance requires an administrative reset, then let that happen. If good governance requires changes, then let that happen, but it has to be done through constitutional and legal methods, and as per the will of the people," he said.
Constitution, law only way forward in AJK: DG ISPR
Responding to a question on protests in AJK and the way forward, the DG ISPR said the will of the people would be reflected through the political process.
"The will of the people will be decided by the politicians, and we believe that our respected politicians also desire good governance and administration. Stagnation is not the solution to anything. Even still water begins to stink after a while," he said.
"The state acted with generosity by offering them the opportunity to participate in the election process as per the Constitution. But they have instead opted for violence. But do remember that only the state has the monopoly on violence and we cannot allow a mob to have its way."
He said the state had responded "very wisely and prudently" and remained restrained despite what he described as an agenda surrounding the 12 seats.
The DG ISPR also referred to a recent social media post, saying it criticised historical Kashmiri leaders and those who had fought against Hari Singh.
"They talk about throwing out this occupying force from Kashmir. Which occupying army are they talking about?", he said, adding that such statements reflected the agenda of those behind the campaign.
He also accused the protestors on social media networks of spreading disinformation, saying it's acting like an ecosystem, where they spread lies and disinformation about people being killed.
The DG ISPR said the matter was being handled by the AJK government, police and civilian armed forces, adding that the electoral process would continue.
"The army has nothing to do with this matter; it's a matter for the AJK government, the brave and valiant police and the civilian armed forces. Nothing can change the concept of Kashmir Banega Pakistan, and there will be no compromise on that. The electoral process will continue and assemblies will form."
He said the Constitution and the rule of law would determine the outcome.
"The answer is in the Constitution and the rule of law. But nobody can be given a free pass on coercion and use of violence. Everyone will be held accountable for their actions according to the law and constitution."
Kashmir was, is and will remain Pakistan's jugular vein: DG ISPR
The DG ISPR said Kashmir remained central to Pakistan's position and reiterated Islamabad's longstanding stance that the dispute should be resolved in accordance with United Nations Security Council resolutions and the right to self-determination of the Kashmiri people.
"Kashmir was, is and will remain the jugular vein of Pakistan. There is only one voice that comes from Pakistan: Kashmir Banega Pakistan and the voice from Kashmir is that we are Pakistanis," he said.
He said nothing could alter that position because Pakistan had adopted a legal, principled and constitutional path, describing Kashmir as the unfinished agenda of Partition.
"We all have clarity that once the question is posed to both sides of Kashmir, they will choose Pakistan. Our religion and culture are the same, and the people of Occupied Kashmir have seen the brutal, ugly side of the Indian army. Who leaves the graves of their forefathers? This happened because of the brutality of the Indian side," he added.
Referring to Indian policies in occupied Kashmir, the DG ISPR said attempts to influence the people through financial incentives or legal measures had failed, and despite all this, they had not been able to change the passion of the people of Occupied Kashmir for Pakistan.
He further said that in 2019 and 2025 Pakistan had "settled our scores with the Indian army", adding that subsequent efforts had focused on creating unrest inside Pakistan.
"Then they came up with another option: to start unrest within Pakistan. This time around, they have cloaked their attempt using the language of rights, without mentioning the obligations that come with it."
He said Kashmir was Pakistan's "favourite and most favoured child" in terms of resource allocation, arguing that the debate over rights was being used to pursue a different agenda.
Earlier, DG ISPR said Pakistan was "not a hard state", as he outlined the country's security situation and said security forces had killed an average of 10 terrorists every day so far this year.
Addressing a live press conference focused on Balochistan, the military spokesperson said the briefing would examine three questions: "What is the problem? What is happening? What is being done?"
"We will focus on Balochistan because there is a perception that the condition in Balochistan is very bad," he said.
The DG ISPR said the first issue was not specific to Balochistan but related to Pakistan's overall security environment. "Are we a hard state? Unfortunately not," he said.
Explaining the term, he said a hard state did not mean "a military-run state or an armed forces-dominated state."
"When we say a hard state, it means a state in which the law is equal for all, all issues are dealt with through the law, there is no elitism and everyone is equal before the law," he said.
The DG ISPR then spoke about what he described as "obligations versus rights."
"We are all talking about our rights. We are taking up grievances, taking up arms and raising slogans based on rights. But before these rights, we have some obligations," he said.
Citing Article 5 of the Constitution, he said: "Loyalty to the state is the basic duty of every citizen. Obedience to the Constitution and the law is the obligation of every citizen."
"The law is clear that we all have a basic responsibility. We need to be loyal to the state. Then you can talk about your rights. We first have to speak about our obligations," he added.
Referring to Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir's address at the National Workshop on Balochistan, the DG ISPR said the army chief had also stressed the importance of obligations.
"Asim Munir, at the National Workshop on Balochistan, said, "Yes, we talk about rights, but why don't we talk about obligations? What are they?" he said.
The DG ISPR said every citizen's "first and last identity" should be Pakistani.
"Isn't it every citizen's obligation that our first and last identity is Pakistani, not that we talk about our provincial identity? Because our identity is that we are citizens of the state," he said.
"Our obligation is that we must acknowledge the fundamental and central position of the State of Pakistan," he added.
Turning to the security situation, the military spokesperson said security forces had conducted 40,348 intelligence-based operations (IBOs) across the country so far this year, with the majority taking place in Balochistan.
"Nearly 194 intelligence-based operations are being conducted every day," he said.
The DG ISPR said 3,145 terrorist incidents had been recorded during the period, while security forces had killed 2,084 terrorists, averaging about 10 terrorists being killed every day.
He said 819 people had embraced martyrdom this year, including 303 personnel from the Pakistan Army, 194 law enforcement agencies and 322 civilians.
The DG ISPR said there had been 28 suicide bombing incidents this year, adding that the majority of the suicide bombers were Afghan nationals.
"The majority of them are Afghans. The Afghan national involved in the Tank attack was also an Afghan. Afghan nationals and people associated with their security forces are among the terrorists killed and captured," he said.
Comparing the figures with previous years, he said security forces had killed 2,597 terrorists during the whole of 2025, while 2,084 had already been killed so far in 2026.
"If you look at 2023, our martyr ratio was higher, and we were killing fewer terrorists. In 2024, the tide started turning. By 2025, for each martyr we were taking out two terrorists," he said.
Responding to a question about the rise in terrorist incidents, the DG ISPR said: "You must ask why incidents are increasing. It has to do with the agenda of terrorists affiliated with the Taliban and with the clarity that Pakistan has. These terrorists have come to understand that there is no room for appeasement now."
"Once they know that the state is very clearly telling them, 'Submit in front of the state, otherwise we are here, we are standing here and fighting,' it changes the dynamic," he said.
The DG ISPR added that the increase in incidents was also linked to more proactive intelligence-based operations.
"Once we get more proactive and engage, once we are doing more effective intelligence-based operations, there will be engagement and incidents increase," he said.
Security, governance and development measures in Balochistan
The DG ISPR further said the state was pursuing a multi-pronged strategy in Balochistan, combining security operations, border management, action against smuggling, capacity building and socio-economic development.
He said intelligence-based "kinetic" operations were continuing daily under Operation Shaban, while aerial capabilities were playing an important role because of Balochistan's terrain. "Kinetic operations are happening every day," he said.
The military spokesperson also referred to Operation Ghazab Lil Haq, saying security forces had an obligation to protect the lives, property and honour of the people. "We have an obligation to protect the honour, property and lives of our people, and people who support this terrorism will pay a price for this," he said.
The DG ISPR said strengthening border management with Afghanistan was another key element of the state's strategy. Referring to the repatriation of undocumented Afghan nationals, he said around 2.6 million people had returned to Afghanistan, including approximately 600,000 this year.
"The first thing is to harden the state. We are doing that. If you want to come, get a visa, go on record and do it. There is no free pass along the border," he said.
The DG ISPR said authorities were also targeting the "terror-crime nexus" in Balochistan. He said 2,019 operations had been carried out against the "illegal spectrum", including smuggling, while goods worth Rs24.4 billion had been recovered this year.
He said narcotics worth Rs18 billion and proceeds linked to human smuggling worth Rs4.6 billion had also been recovered, while drug eradication operations were continuing.
Referring to fuel smuggling, the military spokesperson said a permit system introduced in 1959 for border districts had expanded into nationwide smuggling over time as road connectivity improved.
According to the DG ISPR, fuel smuggling had reached around 20.5 million litres per day before authorities moved to curb it. "There is no tax on this. Most of the money goes to a few elites, a few politicians and a few terrorists," he said, adding that the Balochistan government and the Frontier Corps had brought the trade under control.
The DG ISPR said efforts were also under way to strengthen the capacity of security and law enforcement agencies. He said a separate Frontier Corps headquarters was being established for Chagai and the Mineral Corridor, while specialised police training schools were also being developed.
He added that technical capabilities, including aerial surveillance, cyber security and intelligence, were also being enhanced. "They may have Indian cyber and technology, but our kids aren't less than anyone," he said.
The military spokesperson said development and direct engagement with the people formed another pillar of the state's strategy. "We need to empower the common person, not the elites," he said.
He said projects funded through the federal and provincial Public Sector Development Programme included Mangi Dam, the extension of the Pat Feeder Canal, the N-25 highway and the construction of 100 dams, of which 52 had been completed.
According to the DG ISPR, 119 socio-economic projects had been completed in Balochistan, while 12 major road infrastructure projects were underway to improve connectivity.
He added that around 10,800 students received IT training every year, while 60 new education facilities and two new health facilities were being established each month. He also cited the Green Balochistan Initiative, saying it was providing loans to poor farmers.
The DG ISPR said the government was also engaging directly with the public through open forums. He stated that 703 open forums had been held, with the Army, the chief minister, politicians and other state institutions conducting around 144 public engagements each day.
According to the DG ISPR, issues raised during these engagements were recorded and 51% had been resolved. "That is why we say we have to engage directly with the people. We don't need these elites to speak for them," he said.
'Elitism', external actors and propaganda
DG ISPR said "elitism and sardarism", a desire to maintain the status quo, external actors and propaganda were among the factors behind the security situation in Balochistan.
The military spokesperson said these were the "fundamental" issues specific to Balochistan. "This is the fundamental thing, specific to Balochistan," he said.
The DG ISPR said "elitism and sardarism and the desire to maintain the status quo" were among the root causes. "We have to get to the root cause today. This is the part of society that thinks it has no obligation but only rights — the elites, part of them," he said.
"They think that this status quo must be maintained, a status quo where a normal citizen should not study, should not progress, should do nothing, so he can be my slave, be my driver, walk around like my guard because I'm special."
The DG ISPR said they were "prime movers of terrorism." "They are afraid that times are changing. The more afraid they are, the more anxious they become, the more kinetic they get," he said.
The military spokesperson also spoke about what he described as a "desire for appeasement."
"They think, 'We will do terrorism and then talk. Talk with us. Appease us as you used to.' We don't want to talk to you. We will talk to the real people of Balochistan. You are not a stakeholder," he said.
The DG ISPR said some people believed the Balochistan Levies were "our personal army." "They have a habit that this Levies force is our personal army. Half of the guy's salary is mine, the other half will be my personal guard," he said. He added that the Levies force was being turned into a police force.
The DG ISPR also said some people were accustomed to, "in the name of trade", carrying out smuggling. "They are used to, in the name of trade, doing smuggling, bringing narcotics and diesel and selling it at six times the price," he said.
"If you try to stop them, then they will do terrorism and raise slogans that Balochistan is out of our hands. They say, 'Open my permits. Give me my share from the Rs1,000 billion budget.'"
The military spokesperson also referred to what he described as an "external power play."
"They know that Balochistan is blessed not only with vibrant human resources but also natural resources. Allah has given it all blessings. They know the potential of this," he said.
"They get physically involved with these terrorists and they find ready partners in these sardars. They want the same slaves and private jails. They want to see the system they saw during their grandfathers' time."
Referring to Afghanistan, the DG ISPR said: "It's not Afghanistan, it's the Afghan Taliban regime." "Their business is terrorism, and through terrorism they sustain their economy and diplomacy," he said. He also said there was "no difference" between " Fitna al Hindustan " and " Khawarij ."
Turning to what he described as propaganda, the DG ISPR said it had four "verticals": "the sense of deprivation, lack of representation, the missing persons narrative, and terrorism propaganda."
Addressing what he described as the "sense of deprivation," the DG ISPR cited development projects and budget allocations in Balochistan.
He said Gwadar had three universities, four colleges, the Pak-China Hospital, five child dispensaries, an international airport, a seaport, an expressway, industrial free zones, tax-free zones and a cricket stadium. "In all of Pakistan, tell me another city with a population of 300,000 that has all this," he said.
The DG ISPR said Turbat, with a population of around 500,000, had two universities, colleges, an international airport and road connectivity. "Tell me another city of such a population with all this," he said. He added that Balochistan had 13 major hospitals and 650 dispensaries.
The DG ISPR also referred to the province's per capita budget allocation. "Look at the budget per capita. Per capita is Rs75,000-plus, more than any other province. What deprivation is rooted in?" he said.
He said development projects were being targeted. "That's why they kill labourers, attack roads. Whoever wants to work in schools or teach, we will kill them, so that the sardars' army stays ready," he said.
Speaking about political representation, the DG ISPR said the same families continued to dominate electoral politics. "Take out the lists of the assemblies. The same families, the same parties. They win, then their father or brother wins. If they win, it's democracy; if not, then it's rigging. What representation is this?" he said.
Addressing the issue of missing persons, the military spokesperson referred to the Commission of Inquiry on Enforced Disappearances. "They say thousands have been picked up. The government made a commission so that if there is someone missing, there would be a name," he said.
The DG ISPR said the commission had received a total of 10,901 cases since the early 2010s.
"More than 9,000 cases have been disposed of. Of those, around 5,000 people have gone back home, others are in custody, 308 were found to have died, and around 2,400 were found not to be cases of missing persons," he said. He added that around 2,700 cases remained pending.
The DG ISPR said there were more pending cases in Sindh than in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. He also said some people included in lists of missing persons had later been killed while carrying out terrorist activities.
"Some are in Turbat, do terrorism, are killed and then are included in the missing persons list," he added.
Turning to what he described as terrorism propaganda, the DG ISPR said attacks were sometimes filmed to generate content. "A guy attacking a police station is being filmed because we have to give content to show that there is a problem in Balochistan, so people can say, 'Look, this has happened,'" he said.
Attacks on civilians and online propaganda
The DG ISPR said Balochistan's geography and terrain posed significant challenges for security forces.
He said population figures did not always reflect the number of people physically present in the province, as many residents counted in the census were working elsewhere.
Referring to the deployment of the Frontier Corps (FC), the military spokesperson said some people questioned the force's presence without taking into account the distances and terrain.
"There is a narrative that the FC frontage is a minimum of 40 kilometres, while the distance from one post to another can be between 15 and 30 kilometres. Look at the terrain," he said.
Turning to the security situation, the DG ISPR said " Fitna al Hindustan ", " Khawarij ", the RSS, India and the Afghan Taliban were working together.
"What is happening? This Hindustan and Khawarij , and the people sitting in the RSS, India and the Afghan Taliban, they are together. We are hunting them and seeking them, and they are now going for soft targets," he said.
The DG ISPR said the attacks included 178 civilians targeted, 55 kidnappings, 24 attacks on infrastructure, 60 incidents in which property was set on fire, 47 incidents involving damage to property and robbery, and 105 attacks on police and Levies personnel.
The military spokesperson said people across Balochistan, including those in rural areas, were increasingly speaking out against terrorism. "Baloch people are speaking loudly against this terrorism," he said.
The DG ISPR said terrorist groups were exploiting young women through what he described as "honey traps", blackmail and coercion. "They honey-trap daughters, abuse them, make their videos and blackmail them," he said, referring to an account shared by a father from Balochistan.
"The way they are exploiting the daughters of Balochistan shows how merciless and lowly they are. They honey-trap them, mentally trap them and make them commit acts of terrorism," he said.
The military spokesperson said terrorist groups could inflict harm but would not succeed. "When there is this passion, they cannot succeed, but they can hurt. We will give that hurt back tenfold, and so will their sponsors," he said.
Turning to what he described as online propaganda, the DG ISPR said more than 300 Indian websites and over 1,000 social media accounts were involved in disseminating content related to Balochistan. "Most of the propaganda comes from Indian-run accounts," he said.
Describing what he said was the pattern of online dissemination, the DG ISPR said an incident was first "seeded" on Telegram before being framed by initiators, amplified by other accounts, carried by mainstream media channels and eventually picked up by international media.
"First they seed it on Telegram. An incident or event is seeded, then framing is done by initiators, then given to amplifiers, followed by mass amplification through mainstream media channels, and then it is picked up by international media. Then you pick it up and run it as reality," he said.
The DG ISPR also referred to online activity on July 16, saying the "entire Indian social media ecosystem", including political accounts and Baloch Yakjehti Committee-linked accounts, was involved in disseminating content related to Balochistan.
Responding to another question regarding the UAE's alleged involvement in violence in Balochistan, the DG ISPR rejected speculation about strained ties between Islamabad and Abu Dhabi, describing the two countries as close allies.
"Pakistan and UAE are two brotherly and closely bonded countries, and we share deep ties. This speculation in social media about there being problems between Pakistan and UAE, 99 percent of this illogical discussion takes place outside the country. These rumours are spread by those who do not wish Pakistan to have brotherly relations with the Gulf countries."
He said the UAE was currently operating in a challenging regional security environment and any changes in its policies were linked to its national security requirements.
"You have to understand that the UAE is in an environment of military conflict right now and because of that, it is undergoing certain changes, and these changes in rules are important to its national security. It is therefore unacceptable to concoct false stories on social media on differences between these two brotherly countries."
He said Pakistan and the UAE shared deep, historical ties and that their relations were at the political, strategic and, most importantly, people-to-people levels, adding that any attempts at propaganda in this regard would not succeed.
DG ISPR calls Fazl's remarks on martyrs 'deplorable'
Asked about JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman's remarks regarding martyrs, the DG ISPR described the comments as "deplorable" and "difficult to understand".
"Martyrs are the backbone of Pakistan's armed forces... Behind the philosophy of martyrdom stand the Army, the Navy, the Air Force and your police. So, if someone talks about this so lightly, so easily and so loosely, then I would say it is beyond understanding," he said.
He also condemned the JUI-F chief's comments on the martyrs of the Kargil War.
"You speak about their martyrdom in a way that India is trying to promote as its narrative."
The military spokesperson said members of the armed forces sacrificed the most precious thing they possessed — their right to life — for the protection of the nation, adding that such sacrifice began long before a soldier embraced martyrdom.
"You have just seen it in Balochistan. When our officer or soldier goes out on an intelligence-based operation, when he goes out for an operation against these terrorists and Khwarij, when that young policeman or FC soldier stands alone at a checkpoint on a mountain where there is no one for miles, and he knows that 'I am a target of these terrorists, these Indian proxies,' yet he performs his duty there, he has already become ready to sacrifice his life, his right to life, his future and the future of his children. Do you think he is doing it for some pay? Would you do it? That is why it is difficult to understand why someone would say such things. It is not like that," he said.
He urged political leaders to avoid creating confusion among the public. "We should create awareness among our nation. We do not need to confuse them further."

Harry Styles’ debut solo single Sign of the Times has returned to a major career milestone, with the 2017 hit spending a full year on the UK’s Official Singles Chart.
The song has now accumulated 52 weeks on the chart, although its run has not been consecutive. Originally released in April 2017, Sign of the Times debuted at No. 1 before eventually leaving the chart. It returned years later following its appearance in the 2026 film Project Hail Mary and has remained on the ranking since April.
The renewed success has also seen Sign of the Times climb to No. 19 on this week’s Official Singles Chart, its highest position since June 2017. The track has also reached No. 47 on the Official Streaming Chart.
The resurgence comes as Styles continues his Together, Together Tour and promotes his fourth studio album, Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally. The singer initially planned a smaller run of shows in 2026 but expanded the tour following strong demand. The tour is expected to include at least 107 dates once its 2027 leg is completed.
Sign of the Times has also been performing strongly internationally. Earlier in September, the song climbed to a new peak of No. 41 on the Billboard Global 200 and held its No. 37 peak on the Billboard Global Excl. U.S. chart.
The song’s renewed chart performance adds another milestone to Styles’ solo career. His catalogue has continued to find an audience alongside his latest release, with Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally. also maintaining a presence on the UK charts. The album sits at No. 34 on the latest Official Albums Chart and No. 26 on the Official Albums Streaming Chart.
Styles released Sign of the Times shortly after One Direction went on hiatus, making it his first major release as a solo artist. Nearly a decade later, the song is once again gaining momentum on charts in the UK and around the world.

title: Sophia Bush reveals secret wedding to Ashlyn Harris in new memoir
description: Sophia Bush and Ashlyn Harris reveal they secretly married in an intimate upstate New York ceremony in 2025
content:
Sophia Bush and Ashlyn Harris reveal they secretly married in an intimate upstate New York ceremony in 2025
Sophia Bush and former professional soccer player Ashlyn Harris have revealed that they secretly married in an intimate ceremony in upstate New York in summer 2025.
Bush, 44, shared details of the private wedding in her upcoming memoir, And I Will Tell You Mine: Notes from a Life in Progress , which is set to be released on October 27. The couple also discussed their marriage with Vogue on September 30.
Harris, 40, and Bush were joined by Harris’ children, Sloane and Ocean, for the low-key celebration. According to the couple, the family picked flowers from the property and later roasted marshmallows together.
Bush explained that keeping the wedding private allowed them to avoid the pressure often associated with public celebrations. Harris similarly recalled that the children were able to enjoy the day without feeling overwhelmed.
Following the ceremony, Bush and Harris travelled around the country to tell their family and close friends about their marriage in person. Bush said she eventually felt ready to make their relationship public after becoming tired of describing Harris as her “partner”.
“You’re my wife,” Bush recalled telling Harris, describing the moment as meaningful.
Bush and Harris were first linked in October 2023, and Bush publicly confirmed their relationship in a 2024 Glamour cover story. Before marrying Harris, Bush was married to Chad Michael Murray from 2005 to 2006 and Grant Hughes from 2022 to 2024.
In her memoir, Bush also reflects on her decision to embrace marriage again and finding inspiration in Harris’ grandparents’ long-lasting relationship.
Harris said the couple’s decision to share their relationship publicly was also connected to the importance of LGBTQ+ visibility, particularly for young people who may not feel represented.

title: Ben Affleck opens up about discovering his mom   s letters after her death
description: After his mother   s death  Affleck discovered letters she had written to her parents when she was a young woman
content:
After his mother’s death, Affleck discovered letters she had written to her parents when she was a young woman
Ben Affleck has opened up about discovering letters his late mother wrote when she was young, revealing how reading them changed the way he viewed his childhood and her life.
The actor discussed the discovery during the premiere episode of Kerry Washington’s new podcast, Street You Grew Up On, which launched on Wednesday, September 30. Affleck, 54, spoke about losing both of his parents earlier this year and how their deaths prompted him to reflect on his upbringing.
“My parents just died, both of them,” Affleck told Washington, explaining that his father, Timothy Affleck, died in April, while his mother, Chris Anne Affleck, died in June at 83 after being diagnosed with pancreatic cancer.
After his mother’s death, Affleck discovered letters she had written to her parents when she was a young woman. The letters offered him a glimpse into a side of his mother that he had never known personally, before she became a parent to him and his brother Casey Affleck.
The letters described Chris as a young woman “full of life and ambition and dreams”. She had considered becoming a social worker or teacher, lived in California and travelled to Mississippi to participate in protests. Affleck said it was fascinating to realise that his mother had lived a complete life before he was born.
For Affleck, the discovery gave him a deeper appreciation for the sacrifices his mother made for her children. He said the experience made him recognise that she had “her own whole life for 30 years” before becoming his mother.
Chris eventually worked as a public school teacher, teaching fifth and sixth grades. Affleck recalled that she worked long hours, often staying at school until the late afternoon before returning home and taking care of her family.
Looking back, Affleck acknowledged that he did not fully understand how much his mother was doing for him and Casey when he was a child. He said it was only later in life that he began to recognise the extent of her work and commitment to raising her sons.
“She was, I mean, gorgeous and smart and thoughtful and passionate,” Affleck said, reflecting on his mother. “I just thought this woman's amazing and she could do anything.”
Affleck’s conversation with Washington comes as the two actors prepare for the release of their new film Animals, which premieres on Netflix on October 9.
Street You Grew Up On will continue with weekly episodes featuring guests including Dwayne Johnson, Demi Lovato, Colin Kaepernick and Chelsea Handler.

content:
Petrol price decreases to Rs387.40 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs400.35
The federal government on Wednesday decreased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by 14 paisas and Rs1.89 per litre, respectively, for October 1.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs387.40 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs400.35 per litre for Thursday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government decreased the price of petrol and HSD by Rs1.49 and Rs2.73 per litre, respectively, for September 30.
Read : Govt decreases petrol by Rs1.49, diesel by Rs2.73 for Sept 30
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
Earlier this month, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices ‌rose on Wednesday and were on track for significant monthly gains on stalled US-Iran peace talks and tightening US fuel markets.
The Brent November futures contract, which expires on Wednesday, was up $1.12, or 1%, at $103.71 a barrel at 10:50 am EDT. The more active December contract was up $2.65, or 2.8%, at $98.81. US West Texas Intermediate crude was ​up $1.98, or 2.2%, at $91.98.
Qatar said on Tuesday it hopes that shuttle diplomacy between Tehran and Washington can ⁠lead to a breakthrough.
Goldman Sachs estimates Gulf oil exports have recovered to 23.3 million barrels per day over the last week, in line with their 2025 average, as exports doubled in September, it said in a note on Tuesday.
"Recovering crude flows should temper supply-driven ‌price pressures, ⁠although persistent product shortages and elevated freight costs are likely to keep the broader energy market tight," analysts at Japanese bank MUFG said.

Says Pakistan and China are entering a new phase of cooperation under CPEC 2.0
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday hailed China's “extremely important” role in promoting global peace, stability and development and reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening its all-weather strategic cooperative partnership with Beijing.
Addressing a ceremony marking the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People’s Republic of China, the prime minister said it was a pleasure for him to attend the National Day event and extended his “heartfelt congratulations” to Chinese President Xi Jinping and the people of China.
He described the occasion as a day to pay tribute to the perseverance, unity and indomitable spirit of the Chinese nation.

“China has an extremely important role in global peace, stability and development,” he said.
Under the “far-sighted leadership” of President Xi, China had made unprecedented progress in human development, science, technology and innovation, the prime minister said.
He said 2026 held “special significance” in the shared journey of Pakistan and China, as the two countries were celebrating the 75th anniversary of the establishment of their diplomatic relations.

The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), he said, was a manifestation of the two countries’ longstanding friendship and their shared commitment to a more prosperous and developed future for their people.
“We are now entering the next phase of CPEC, CPEC 2.0,” he said.

The new phase would focus particularly on industrialisation, special economic zones, information technology and artificial intelligence, agriculture, mining and minerals, he added.

“Another group of 1,000 people is ready to go to China,” he said, describing the programme as a valuable investment in the capabilities and future of Pakistan’s youth.
PM Shehbaz said Pakistan-China relations were a cornerstone of the country’s foreign policy.
Recalling his conversation with President Xi in May, he said that it had represented a strong reaffirmation of the countries’ longstanding friendship.

“A sincere friend living in a distant land makes a distant land close,” the prime minister said while quoting a Chinese saying, adding that the words best reflected the friendship and closeness between the two countries.
Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zaidong also addressed the ceremony, describing China and Pakistan as “all-weather strategic cooperative partners”.
He said Pakistan was playing an increasingly important role internationally because of its principled position, broad global vision and high level of diplomatic insight.

title: Punjab Assembly   s Standing Committee gives nods to Christian Marriage Bill 2026
description: Upcoming law makes the registration of marriages with the UC and NADRA mandatory
content:
Upcoming law makes the registration of marriages with the UC and NADRA mandatory
The Punjab Assembly's Standing Committee on Human Rights and Minorities Affairs on Wednesday unanimously approved the Christian Marriage Bill 2026, proposing to repeal the century-old Christian Marriage Act 1872 and introduce a modern legal framework governing marriages among the Christian community.
The bill was earlier presented in the Punjab Assembly on April 27, but drew widespread criticism from Christian religious leaders and legal experts, who argued that wider reforms covering divorce, annulment, inheritance, child custody, and separation were also needed, along with proper consultation with the Church during the drafting process.
The meeting, chaired by Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz MPA Raheela Khadim Hussain, evaluated the bill moved by MPA Philebos Christopher.
Christopher told the committee that the proposed legislation was meant to consolidate and modernise the existing legal framework for Christian marriages, strengthen protection of consent and ensure greater legal clarity in matters relating to matrimonial law.
He said a key proposal in the bill was to fix the minimum marriageable age at 18 years for both men and women in the Christian community.
Read: Christian marriage bill faces opposition
According to the MPA, the minimum age for a Christian marriage is 16 years for a boy and 13 years for a girl under the existing law.
“The proposed law would also require both parties to a Christian marriage to identify as Christians,” he highlighted during the meeting.
As per details outlined by the minority lawmaker, the bill proposes a formal procedure for marriage, including written notice before the marriage and a public announcement of the intended marriage. It further seeks to make the registration of Christian marriages with the Union Council and the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) mandatory.
He lamented that registration of Christian marriages with the Union Council and NADRA was not possible under the existing law.
Under the proposed legislation that is now up for approval of the Punjab Assembly, marriages would be allowed to take place in all churches registered with the government of Punjab, according to Christian rites and procedures. It also proposes authorising religiously educated pastors of government-registered churches to solemnise Christian marriages.
“Designated pastors or marriage registrars appointed by the government would also be empowered to conduct marriages,” Christopher explained further.
“A Christian marriage would have to be solemnised in the presence of at least two witnesses, while a formal record of marriages would be maintained through marriage registers and prescribed forms.”
He also emphasised that unlike the existing legal framework, the proposed law would impose no restriction on the day or time for holding a marriage ceremony.

title: Saudi crown prince says Makkah defence pact with T  rkiye  Pakistan aims to bolster regional stability
description: Says attacks targeting GCC countries demonstrate that Gulf security and stability are   indivisible
content:
Says attacks targeting GCC countries demonstrate that Gulf security and stability are 'indivisible'
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) on Wednesday said that the Makkah defence pact with Türkiye and Pakistan aimed to bolster regional stability and shield the region from tensions and conflicts.
Signed by Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia on August 7, the pact is based on the principles of shared responsibility and regional ownership amid growing regional and global instability. The agreement aims to promote security, peace, stability and prosperity while strengthening collective deterrence.
MBS made the remarks while delivering the annual royal address on behalf of King Salman bin Abdulaziz during the opening of the third year of the ninth session of Saudi Arabia’s Shura Council.
Read : Makkah pact military chiefs condemn attacks on holy city at Riyadh meeting
“To strengthen regional stability, shield it from the repercussions of tensions and conflicts, and coordinate efforts, the Makkah Defence Alliance was established between the kingdom, Türkiye and Pakistan,” the crown prince said.
#BREAKING : Crown Prince: As part of our efforts to strengthen regional stability and shield the region from tensions and conflicts, the Makkah Defense Alliance was established between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan to enhance security and stability in the region. pic.twitter.com/mrV6ijuqdR
He said attacks targeting Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries demonstrated that Gulf security and stability were “indivisible”.
MBS said Saudi Arabia was working with fellow GCC countries to safeguard them.
The crown prince said the kingdom was making every possible effort to de-escalate tensions without compromising its security.
“We will not hesitate to respond firmly to any threat or attack aimed at undermining our security,” he said.
Read More : Saudi Arabia warns escalating Middle East threats risk global trade, energy security
MBS also said the establishment of a “multinational defensive maritime coalition” was aimed at strengthening maritime security and protecting common interests in international waterways.
He rejected the use of international waterways as a tool for political or economic pressure.
Mohammed bin Salman: As part of our contribution to strengthening regional stability, shielding the region from the consequences of tensions and conflicts, and coordinating efforts, the Makkah Defense Alliance was established between the Kingdom, the Republic of Türkiye and the… pic.twitter.com/20c9HHmEhj
The crown prince also warned that “the world today is facing an energy crisis open to all possibilities.”
He also condemned Israel’s “brutal attacks” against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip and its “repeated violations” of Al-Aqsa Mosque.
MBS further called on the international community and the Board of Peace to play their roles in reaching a lasting political solution in Palestine.
The Makkah pact is the latest step in longstanding military and strategic cooperation between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. Signed in Makkah, the pact established a framework for collective deterrence and stipulated that an armed attack on any one of the three countries would be considered an attack on all three, while providing for wider cooperation across defence.
Also Read: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye sign joint defence pact in Makkah
The agreement followed nearly a year of negotiations and came amid heightened instability across the Middle East. Turkiye and Pakistan had sought closer regional security cooperation, while Saudi Arabia had faced growing security concerns as conflicts spread across the region, threatening its territory, energy infrastructure and ambitious economic development plans.
For Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the trilateral pact is built on their Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed in September 2025. That agreement stated that “any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both” and committed the two sides to strengthening defence cooperation and joint deterrence.
The three countries already had extensive military links. Pakistan had provided training and technical assistance to Saudi forces for decades, while Islamabad and Ankara had maintained close defence ties through military training, naval cooperation and defence equipment. In 2023, Saudi Arabia agreed to purchase Turkish drones in what Ankara described as its largest defence export contract.
Pakistan had also expanded its military and security cooperation with the kingdom, deploying about 8,000 troops, fighter jets, drones and an air-defence system to Saudi Arabia, according to Reuters . Islamabad had also been pursuing wider security and economic ties in the Gulf, including negotiations with Kuwait on an expanded cooperation pact linked to energy and investment.
The signing in Makkah, Islam’s holiest city, added symbolic weight to an agreement that brought together three countries with significant military and strategic capabilities. It also came as Pakistan sought to avoid becoming directly involved in the Iran conflict, instead pursuing diplomatic efforts to mediate, while strengthening its broader regional security partnerships.

Pete Davidson discusses leaving 'SNL', sobriety, fatherhood and his upcoming films in a new Variety interview
Pete Davidson has opened up about leaving Saturday Night Live , his past relationships, sobriety and fatherhood while discussing his next chapter in a new Variety interview.
The 32-year-old comedian and actor left SNL in 2022 after eight seasons. Davidson said he had wanted to leave earlier but ultimately followed advice from creator Lorne Michaels to give himself time to find his place on the show.
Davidson also reflected on his highly publicised relationships with celebrities including Ariana Grande and Kim Kardashian. He said the media attention surrounding his dating life has often overshadowed his acting and comedy work.
The actor revealed that he reached a low point in 2023 after the release of his autobiographical Peacock series Bupkis . He said he was using several drugs at the time before entering rehab and stepping away from the series. Davidson now says he is sober and has stopped using drugs.
Fatherhood has also changed his outlook. Davidson and his former partner Elsie Hewitt welcomed their daughter, Scottie, and he said becoming a father shifted his priorities away from public opinion and career pressures.
Davidson is preparing for the release of How to Rob a Bank , in which he plays a war veteran involved in bank robberies. The film, directed by David Leitch, is scheduled to hit theatres on November 13.
He is also set to star in Tommy Karate , a crime film based on real-life mob hitman Thomas Pitera. Davidson wrote the screenplay during rehab and is expected to play the lead role.
Despite removing most of his tattoos, Davidson said he plans to keep a tattoo of Hillary Clinton, describing her as a close friend.

title: Govt defends purchase of 45 bulletproof vehicles for SCO summit
description: Cabinet division rejects  sceptical and unwarranted  criticism in the press and on social media
content:
Cabinet division rejects 'sceptical and unwarranted' criticism in the press and on social media
The federal government on Wednesday defended its procurement of 45 bulletproof vehicles for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s (SCO) Council of Heads of State (CHS) Summit scheduled during August-September 2027 in Islamabad, saying the vehicles were essential to meet security requirements for the high-profile international gathering.
A day earlier, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif approved the procurement of 45 against the demanded 65 bulletproof vehicles for the security of SCO leaders, according to the cabinet division, which also claimed the move was endorsed by the deputy PM and the ministries of foreign affairs and interior. The approval sparked outcry on social media.
The Cabinet Division, in a statement shared by Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on X, rejected what it described as “sceptical and unwarranted” criticism in the press and on social media over the purchase.
Pakistan is currently chairing the SCO Council of Heads of State, and the government said the upcoming summit would be among the country’s most significant international events.
GOVERNMENT OF PAKISTAN CABINET SECRETARIAT CABINET DIVISION PRESS RELEASE Purchase of Bulletproof Vehicles for SCO’s CHS Summit, Islamabad 2027 Certain sceptical and unwarranted comments have appeared in the press and social media on the purchase of 45 bulletproof vehicles by…
“The summit, scheduled to be held in Islamabad during August-September 2027, will be the most high-profile gathering, second only to the 1973 OIC Summit. This will give Pakistan an opportunity to further raise its stature and honour amongst the comity of nations,” the press release stated.
According to the statement, the summit would bring together heads of state and government as well as senior representatives of international organisations, making secure and reliable transport arrangements a critical requirement.
The government said security considerations were particularly important given Pakistan’s prevailing security environment and what it described as threats from hostile external elements.
“At present, the latest model bulletproof vehicles available with the Cabinet Division are a few 2016 models, which are far below the standards required for the summit,” the statement said.
Read: Relaxation from ban on new vehicles sought
The decision to procure 45 bulletproof vehicles was considered at several forums, according to the Cabinet Division, which said the number had been determined on the basis of the “bare minimum requirement”.
The government clarified that the bulletproof vehicles would only form part of the overall transport arrangements for the summit. Around 300 other non-bulletproof vehicles would be rented for logistical requirements, it added.
The Cabinet Division said the summit represented an important opportunity for Pakistan to enhance its international standing and showcase its capacity to host major diplomatic events.
Describing the SCO summit as a prestigious international gathering, the government said its significance should not be “underestimated, trivialised or politicised”.
It also urged citizens to view the hosting of the summit as an honour for Pakistan and support efforts to organise the event according to international standards.
The SCO, which includes major regional countries, holds its Council of Heads of State meeting annually to discuss cooperation and key regional and international issues.
Yesterday, the Cabinet Division told the meeting that in compliance with the premier’s directive, 15 BMW 760i xDrive (VR9) bulletproof sedans, costing Rs3billion, would be procured in addition to the 30 bulletproof Mercedes-Benz Maybach S680 Guard (VR10) sedans, for which the Economic Coordination Committee had already approved a supplementary grant of Rs6.60 billion.

title: Seth MacFarlane   s  Ted  animated series sets December Peacock debut
description: Ted  The Animated Series  will premiere on Peacock December 17  reuniting Seth MacFarlane with the original cast
content:
'Ted: The Animated Series' will premiere on Peacock December 17, reuniting Seth MacFarlane with the original cast
Peacock has announced the premiere date for Ted: The Animated Series , with the animated comedy set to debut on December 17, 2026.
The upcoming Ted series comes from creator Seth MacFarlane, who returns as the voice of the foul-mouthed teddy bear. The animated show will also reunite MacFarlane with original Ted movie stars Mark Wahlberg, Amanda Seyfried and Jessica Barth, who will reprise their respective roles.
The Ted: The Animated Series premiere will feature eight episodes, while additional episodes are scheduled to arrive on Peacock in 2027.
The series is set 12 years after the events of Ted 2 . It follows Ted and his longtime friend John as they navigate adulthood, marriage, parenting and their everyday lives. The two characters are now neighbours, each with families and jobs, while continuing to encourage one another’s questionable decisions.
MacFarlane voices Ted, while Wahlberg returns as John. Seyfried voices John’s wife, Sam, and Barth reprises her role as Ted’s wife, Tami-Lynn. The animated series also introduces new characters, with Kyle Mooney playing Apollo and Liz Richman voicing Ruth.
Ted: The Animated Series is created by MacFarlane, Paul Corrigan and Brad Walsh, who also serve as executive producers. Corrigan and Walsh are the series’ co-showrunners.
The animation is being produced by Rough Draft Studios, with Universal Television and production companies Fuzzy Door and MRC involved in the series.
The new Peacock series expands the Ted franchise into animation after the two live-action films, Ted and Ted 2 , which starred MacFarlane alongside Wahlberg. The first look for the animated series has also been released ahead of its December premiere.

title: South African designer Laduma Ngxokolo makes Paris Fashion Week debut with MaXhosa Africa
description: Ngxokolo became the first South African brand to stage a full runway show on the Paris Fashion Week calendar
content:
Ngxokolo became the first South African brand to stage a full runway show on the Paris Fashion Week calendar
South African designer Laduma Ngxokolo has made his Paris Fashion Week debut with MaXhosa Africa, marking a major milestone for the South African luxury fashion brand as it looks to expand its international presence.
Ngxokolo presented MaXhosa Africa’s Spring-Summer 2027 collection on September 28, becoming the first South African brand to stage a full runway show on the official Paris Fashion Week calendar. The show took place at the residence of the South African ambassador to France and featured 54 looks celebrating African unity, culture and craftsmanship.
The collection featured MaXhosa’s distinctive knitwear and geometric patterns inspired by Xhosa beadwork, alongside designs incorporating the names of African countries and imagery of the continent. Kenyan artist Cyrus Kabiru contributed eyewear made from recycled materials, while South African musician Sjava performed during the show.
Ngxokolo, who founded MaXhosa Africa in 2010, said he had spent 16 years working towards a place on the international fashion stage. The brand produces its knitwear at factories in Johannesburg and East London, using locally sourced wool, as part of its wider effort to demonstrate the potential of South Africa’s textile and manufacturing industries.
The Paris debut also comes as MaXhosa Africa looks beyond its established market and towards further luxury expansion. Ngxokolo has identified cities including Dubai, Paris, London and New York as important markets for the brand, while the company is also in discussions with a new financial partner.
The designer has previously spoken about building a luxury label that challenges perceptions of African-made fashion. MaXhosa Africa has attracted international attention over the years, with figures including Beyoncé and Michelle Obama among those associated with the brand.
The Paris Fashion Week appearance gives MaXhosa Africa access to one of the industry's most prominent international platforms at a time when Ngxokolo is seeking to grow the label beyond its existing audience. He has said the company wants to develop a fashion language capable of reaching markets from Canada to Brazil while retaining its African identity.
Ngxokolo also highlighted the wider representation of African designers in global fashion, saying the continent remains underrepresented on major international platforms. His Paris debut therefore represents both a new chapter for MaXhosa Africa and a significant moment for South African fashion on the global runway.

title: Tom Cruise   s new movie Digger faces major box office pressure
description: Tom Cruise   s Digger faces box office pressure as Warner Bros  prepares for the film   s October 2 release
content:
Tom Cruise’s Digger faces box office pressure as Warner Bros. prepares for the film’s October 2 release
Tom Cruise’s upcoming film Digger is facing a challenging box office outlook as Warner Bros. prepares for the release of the star-led comedy on October 2.
Directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu, Digger is an R-rated original comedy starring Cruise as a powerful oil tycoon whose company becomes linked to an environmental disaster. The film is among Warner Bros.’ major releases for the fall and arrives during a difficult year for the studio.
The movie is currently projected to open with between $12 million and $15 million in North America, according to the report. Earlier estimates had placed its opening between $18 million and $20 million.
The film was initially approved with a reported budget of $125 million, although four sources cited in the report said production costs increased to between $160 million and $180 million. Warner Bros. disputed those figures. The studio also disputed estimates that put the movie’s global theatrical break-even point at roughly $350 million, saying it is closer to $300 million.
Digger marks Cruise’s first original film since 2017’s American Made . The actor remains closely associated with major action franchises, including Mission: Impossible , while Top Gun: Maverick became a major box office success in 2022.
However, Cruise’s two most recent Mission: Impossible films saw lower box office returns than earlier entries in the franchise. For Digger , the actor has taken part in an extensive promotional campaign, including appearances on the New Heights podcast and a GQ cover story.
The film could also benefit from Iñárritu’s previous success with films including The Revenant and Birdman . Meanwhile, Warner Bros. is looking ahead to December’s Dune: Part III as another major release.

title: Pakistani human rights lawyer Jalila Haider receives Right Livelihood award
description: Jalila receives Swedish award in recognition of her work to  challenge ethnic  state and patriarchal persecution
content:
Receives Swedish award in recognition of her work to 'challenge ethnic, state and patriarchal persecution'
Human rights lawyer and activist Jalila Haider on Wednesday received the 2026 Right Livelihood Award, which has also been dubbed the “Alternative Nobel Prize”.
The Right Livelihood Award was established in 1980, when Swedish-German stamp collector Jakob von Uexkull sold part of his collection to fund it, after the foundation behind the Nobel Prizes refused to create new awards in the fields of environmental protection and international development.
According to a press release from the Sweden-based Right Livelihood Foundation, Jalila received the award “for breaking barriers, as the first female lawyer from her Hazara community, to challenge ethnic, state and patriarchal persecution, guided by the conviction that no human being is illegal”.
Read : The travails of the Hazara community
The press release noted that the award goes to "women and women-led organisations confronting the world’s most entrenched power structures: authoritarian rule, patriarchal violence, and unchecked AI development".
The 2026 @RightLivelihood Award goes to women and women-led organisations challenging entrenched power structures: 🏆 Jalila Haider @Advjalila 🏆 Rural Women's Assembly @womensassembly 🏆 Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association @GYLA_CSO 🏆 Timnit Gebru @timnitGebru pic.twitter.com/4v29s5Y5au
The foundation's website noted that Jalila was a Hazara human rights lawyer and activist protecting Pakistan’s most vulnerable communities against state repression, patriarchal norms and ethnic violence, adding that in 2018, she led a seven-day hunger strike against the targeted killing of Hazaras that forced the army chief to negotiate directly with Hazara women, resulting in a sustained decrease in attacks against the community.
Right Livelihood Foundation said that Jalila was a founding member of the Women’s Democratic Front (WDF) and helped pioneer Balochistan’s first Women’s March, a street mobilisation that sparked discussions on feminism across the deeply patriarchal region, further adding that her organisation “We the Humans” had also helped over 400 widows of terrorism victims gain financial independence.
Read More : Feminism in the context of digital media
🧵 She's the first female Hazara lawyer in her community's history — and for over a decade she's defended the people her country tries hardest to erase. Meet @Advjalila , a 2026 @RightLivelihood Laureate from Pakistan. pic.twitter.com/dfDrVuvUBw
It added that by "combining legal work with street activism and community empowerment", Jalila had "secured justice for thousands targeted or ignored by those in power, specifically ethnic, gender and religious minorities, as well as refugees", further noting that her law firm had also helped restore freedom of movement for more than 600 political activists and human rights defenders.
According to the press release, "for over 45 years, the Right Livelihood Award has honoured and supported courageous people leading the way to a just, peaceful and sustainable world for all".
A prominent US artificial intelligence researcher and two women-led rights groups were also recognised.
The jury said in a statement it had chosen US artificial intelligence researcher Timnit Gebru “for challenging concentrated power in artificial intelligence and pioneering digital technology rooted in justice, lived experience and human agency”.
Gebru is known for her work examining how biases influence AI, and in 2017, Gebru co-founded Black in AI.
The foundation also gave the nod to the Rural Women’s Assembly — a grassroots movement of more than 178,000 small-scale farmers across 11 Southern African nations.
The Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association, which the jury described as “Georgia’s oldest and most prominent human rights organisation”, was also honoured.

title: Pakistan bound to defend Saudi Arabia with    whatever means    at disposal  Khawaja Asif
description: Asif says any enemy of Saudi Arabia is an enemy of Pakistan
content:
Defence minister says any enemy of Saudi Arabia is an enemy of Pakistan
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Wednesday said Pakistan was bound by its agreement with Saudi Arabia to come to the kingdom’s defence against any threat, stressing that all available means at Islamabad’s disposal would also be made available to Riyadh.
The remarks come amid continued regional tensions and underline Islamabad’s stated commitment to Saudi Arabia’s security under its bilateral defence arrangements.
“We are bound by this arrangement to defend Saudi Arabia, that means whatever means that are available at our disposal, they’ll be available to Saudi Arabia also,” the defence minister said in an interview with Al Jazeera .
Speaking about the Houthis, Asif said there was “absolutely no doubt” in Pakistan’s position that the group was committing aggression against Saudi Arabia.
“We are there to help Saudi Arabia in any conflict, whether it is coming from Houthis or a country or any other outfit which threatens Saudi Arabia’s security. We will be there to defend them,” he said.
Pakistan’s Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif says Islamabad will make “whatever means” available to Saudi Arabia under a new mutual defence pact if Riyadh faces threats from the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen. pic.twitter.com/Qvb9GXTgbT
The defence minister described the Houthis as enemies of Saudi Arabia.
“Any enemy of Saudi Arabia is an enemy of Pakistan,” Asif added, stressing that the position should be “very clear”.
On Iran’s relationship with the Houthis, the defence minister said Tehran did not accept the group as its proxy. He explained that some proxies go rogue.
Asif said proxy groups could, over time, develop agendas and capabilities of their own, citing the broader phenomenon of armed groups becoming independent of those who initially supported them.
Read: Pakistan reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia
“Some country, A, B or C, they launch a proxy and then [the] proxy has its own way of multiplying and then becoming a rogue sort of entity,” he outlined.
The Houthis have repeatedly carried out missile and drone attacks against Saudi Arabia since the Yemen war escalated in 2015. Their targets included Saudi military installations, airports, oil facilities and other critical infrastructure.
In September 2019 , the group claimed responsibility for drone attacks on Saudi Aramco’s Abqaiq processing facility and Khurais oil field, attacks that temporarily disrupted more than half of Saudi Arabia’s crude production.
The attacks continued in subsequent years, including strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure in March 2022.
More recently, Houthi attacks have again targeted Saudi territory. In September, the group claimed missile and drone strikes on a Saudi military base and other targets, while Saudi authorities reported attacks affecting several cities.
It is worth noting that on September 25 , Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye senior military leadership strongly condemned attacks targeting the holy city of Makkah as they reaffirmed their commitment to the collective defence of the Kingdom under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.
A day after that, Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman reaffirmed continued joint efforts to confront attacks targeting Makkah and civilian and economic facilities in the Kingdom during a meeting with the Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir.
Then, on September 27, Defence Minister Asif also reiterated the resolve to implement the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement amid the rising Houthis attacks on Saudi Arabia and said that both Pakistan and Türkiye would stand with Saudi Arabia practically and diplomatically in case of any aggression.
Asif further stressed that protecting Saudi Arabia fell under divine duty.
"If there wasn't an agreement, if Saudi Arabia had been attacked, especially if the sacred cities of Makkah and Madinah were attacked, then we are bound by an eternal agreement; that is, we will protect the House of God and Madinah," he stated in an interview to a private channel.
He also outlined that the "worldly agreement" referring to the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye to protect one another, would operate in all circumstances.

title: Model Sadia Khan mourns loss of her cousin  remembers her as an elder sister
description: Shares emotional tribute on Instagram after her cousin died following a battle with liver cancer
content:
Shares emotional tribute on Instagram after her cousin died following a battle with liver cancer
Model Sadia Khan mourned the death of her cousin, remembering her as more than family — an elder sister and a “beautiful soul” who held a special place in her heart.
Khan shared the news in an emotional post on Instagram, revealing that her cousin had been battling liver cancer and died after facing the illness with strength.
“Today, I lost someone who was not just my cousin, but an elder sister and a beautiful soul who held such a special place in my heart,” she wrote.
Remembering her cousin, Khan said she had spent years giving love, helping others and being there for the people around her. She also reflected on the strength her cousin had shown while battling cancer.
Khan revealed that she was on a plane when she learned of her cousin’s death, making the moment even more difficult.
“I am on a plane right now, and my heart feels so heavy. I feel helpless that I had to leave, but I pray Allah knows my heart, my intentions, and that I did everything I could for her,” she wrote.
Among the memories Khan said she would carry with her were the final duas her cousin gave her while holding her hand.
“The precious duas she gave me while holding my hand are something I will carry with me for the rest of my life. Those moments are everything to me,” she shared.
Khan also spoke about the bond her cousin shared with her late mother, finding comfort in the thought that the two women, who had been close in life, were now reunited.
“She was also very close to my mother, and somehow, through all this pain, I find comfort in knowing that today she is with my mother again,” Khan wrote. “Two souls who loved each other in this life, reunited in the next.”
Khan acknowledged that she does not usually share deeply personal experiences publicly, but asked her followers to remember her cousin in their duas.
“I don’t usually share things this personal, but today I ask you all to please remember my beloved cousin in your duas,” she wrote.
Despite the grief, Khan said she was grateful that she had been able to be there for her cousin, hold her hand and do whatever she could for her.
She ended the tribute with a message of love and remembrance: “Until we meet again. You were loved, you are loved, and you will never be forgotten.”
Sadia Khan is a Pakistani actress and model who began her career in the fashion industry before making her television debut. She gained widespread recognition for playing Imaan in the popular drama series Khuda Aur Muhabbat and has since appeared in several projects, including Laa , Shayad , Maryam Periera and Abdullah: The Final Witness .

title: Verity    review  Dakota Johnson and Anne Hathaway face criticism in Colleen Hoover adaptation
description: Michael Showalter directs the Amazon MGM adaptation of Colleen Hoover   s bestselling 2018 novel
content:
Michael Showalter directs the Amazon MGM adaptation of Colleen Hoover’s bestselling 2018 novel
Verity , the Colleen Hoover adaptation starring Dakota Johnson, Anne Hathaway and Josh Hartnett, has received a sharply critical review from Variety , with critic Guy Lodge describing the film as an ineffective erotic thriller that struggles to build tension.
Directed by Michael Showalter, the film follows Lowen Ashleigh, played by Johnson, a struggling writer hired to complete a bestselling thriller series after its author, Verity Crawford, portrayed by Hathaway, is left unable to communicate following a car accident. Lowen moves into Verity’s home with her husband Jeremy, played by Hartnett, and discovers a disturbing manuscript that appears to reveal secrets about the family.
Lodge’s review argues that the adaptation fails to generate the suspense or erotic charge expected from its premise. The critic also takes issue with the performances, writing that the three leading actors appear disengaged from material that repeatedly pushes towards melodrama.
The review particularly criticises the film’s pacing, describing a story that takes considerable time to reach its major dramatic turns. Its twists and competing versions of events are also portrayed as overly complicated, with the review suggesting that the mystery loses its impact because the film repeatedly signals its own attempts at ambiguity.
Johnson plays Lowen as she becomes increasingly involved with the Crawford family, while Hathaway portrays Verity through both her present condition and a written account of her past. The story draws on themes of authorship, marriage, family tragedy and the uncertain boundary between truth and fiction.
Showalter previously directed Hathaway in The Idea of You , but that Verity is considerably less suited to his comic strengths. The review also points to the production design and score as polished elements that fail to compensate for what it considers weaknesses in the screenplay and direction.

title: We are Pakistanis first  then Kashmiris     says AJK chief justice
description: Praises Pakistan   s judicial and legal fraternity for an important role in strengthening Kashmir   s judicial system
content:
Praises Pakistan’s judicial and legal fraternity for an important role in strengthening Kashmir’s judicial system
Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Supreme Court Chief Justice Raja Saeed Akram Khan on Wednesday said the bond between Pakistan and Kashmir was indelible and the people identify themselves as Pakistanis first.
Addressing a reception hosted in his honour at the Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan, Justice Khan said, “We are Pakistanis first and then Kashmiris.” He added that the slogan of Syed Ali Gilani, “We are Pakistanis, Pakistan is ours”, reflected the sentiment of every Kashmiri.
Speaking on the occasion, Justice Khan said, “Standing before my own bar as chief justice of Azad Kashmir after 18 years is an extremely emotional and honourable moment for me."
Talking about his approach towards judicial reforms, he said he has centred on improving the judicial system through the introduction of institutional reforms since he assumed office as the chief justice.
Justice Khan attributed the disposal of cases from 2025-26 before the AJK Supreme Court to the collective efforts of the entire judicial team.
Read: PML-N's Naqi takes oath as AJK president
He also praised Pakistan’s judicial and legal fraternity for what he described as an important role in the establishment and strengthening of Kashmir’s judicial system.
“Longstanding and strong ties have existed between the legal communities and judiciaries of Pakistan and Azad Kashmir,” he highlighted further.
The AJK chief justice also said bar associations and lawyers across Pakistan always extended respect and affection to the people and judiciary of AJK.
The chief justice acknowledged the support extended by bar associations in Gujrat, Sialkot, Narowal, Karachi and the High Court Bar, among others, saying they had consistently shown respect and affection towards him.
He said lawyers from the Supreme Court and high courts of Pakistan should be given opportunities to appear before the superior courts of AJK to further strengthen professional links between the two legal communities.
Justice Khan stressed that judges and lawyers had complementary roles in the administration of justice, with lawyers assisting judges through legal arguments and guidance.
“Cooperation between the judiciary and lawyers is indispensable for the delivery of justice,” he stressed.
He added that efforts were also underway to organise a similar gathering in Mirpur to further strengthen ties between the bar associations and legal communities of Pakistan and Kashmir.
The AJK top judge noted that people from Azad Kashmir were serving Pakistan in the armed forces, bureaucracy, judiciary, legal profession and other fields.
