title: Govt  seriously  considering imposing emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa  Tariq Fazal
description: Imposing emergency under Article 232  of the Constitution is  being considered because of the security situation in K P
content:
Says move being considered because of the security situation in K-P
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said on Wednesday that the federal government was "seriously" considering the imposition of an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) in response to the worsening security situation in the province.
Political uncertainty has deepened in K-P amid growing tensions between the federal and provincial governments, with the Centre considering governor's rule and emergency as possible options.
Speaking to journalists at Parliament House, Chaudhry stated that the imposition of an emergency was being considered in K-P because of “increasing terrorism" and the provincial government’s lack of "interest" and failure to control the security situation. "The possibility of imposing an emergency under Article 232 of the Constitution is being discussed".
Read : Centre lays ground for governor's rule in K-P
While talking about consultations with the Pakistan Peoples Party on the imposition of emergency in K-P, Chaudhry said the National Assembly speaker would chair a meeting where matters related to legislation would also be discussed.

Views or actions expressed by subjects do not imply endorsement by Express News . Shared in the public interest in compliance with community… pic.twitter.com/DxU2AuuwPB
He added that the federal government could take the PPP into confidence if it decided to proceed with the emergency. “Pakistan Peoples Party has always fought the war against terrorism with full commitment.”
The issue of Governor’s Rule has become a major point of contention between the federal and K-P government. On September 21, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the government was consulting the law ministry on legal options for the province, including Governor’s Rule , if the PTI proceeded with the march. Two days later, however, Information Minister Atta Tarar ruled out any plan to impose Governor’s Rule, saying the federal government had no intention of removing the PTI administration.
On Monday, some federal ministers publicly raised the possibility of federal intervention in K-P. Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam said consultations were under way on the "constitutional and legal option" of imposing Governors' Rule.
Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar also said if constitutional conditions for such a step or an emergency were met, it could be implemented.
K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi separately warned the provincial government against creating a situation that could force the Centre to impose Governors' Rule.
Earlier today, K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi warned that the PTI would "rebel" if necessary to force a change in the federal government policies that were "harming the province".
Read More : Afridi threatens revolt to 'force change'
Afridi, however, rejected the warnings and said he would not retreat from his position because of threats of Governors' Rule or an emergency. He also said PTI supporters could take to the streets at short notice if an attempt was made to remove him.
The developments come amid continued tensions following PTI's announcement of an Islamabad march. Although the protest was postponed from September 27 to October 4, the standoff between the federal and provincial governments remains unresolved.
Reports have also emerged about the possible disqualification of the chief minister, his replacement, an in-house change, dissolution of the assembly and a no-confidence motion against him under Article 136 of the Constitution.
The no-confidence motion can be submitted to the assembly secretariat with signatures of 20% of the total membership, following which an assembly session is to be convened within three to seven days on a single-point agenda.
The assembly rules lay down the procedure for a no-confidence motion. After the motion is moved in the house, voting is held through a secret ballot, with members expressing their choice in two separate lobbies. If the motion succeeds, the speaker will issue a schedule for the election of a new chief minister.
The Constitution also provides for the governor to require the chief minister to seek a vote of confidence under Article 130(7). If the governor believes the chief minister has lost the confidence of the majority in the house, the chief minister is required to demonstrate his numerical strength in the assembly.

title: Macklemore   s Dublin  Free Palestine  tour date sells out within minutes
description: Several fans are saying they were high in the queue when sales opened but were unable to secure tickets
content:
Several fans are saying they were high in the queue when sales opened but were unable to secure tickets
Macklemore’s Dublin date on his Free Palestine Tour has completely sold out, with fans reporting that tickets for the October concert disappeared within minutes of going on sale.
The rapper is scheduled to perform at Dublin’s 3Arena on October 26 as part of the newly announced tour, which comes weeks after he was removed from the remaining US dates of Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour following his public support for Palestine. Fans on social media reported that tickets for the Dublin show sold out within five minutes after going on sale at 10am.
The Dublin concert was announced last week alongside dates in Paris and London. Macklemore is due to perform at Paris’ Accor Arena on October 29 before heading to London’s OVO Arena Wembley on October 30.
The rapid sell-out prompted some fans to express frustration online, with several saying they were high in the queue when sales opened but were unable to secure tickets. Two presales had taken place earlier in the week, including one for fans who signed up through Macklemore’s website and another through the Three+ app.
The new tour follows Macklemore’s departure from Sheeran’s US tour after he used performances at two venues to advocate for Palestinians. Sheeran later said that the decision to remove Macklemore was made by the tour promoter after venues hosting upcoming shows indicated they would not allow the rapper to perform.
Several artists subsequently withdrew from Sheeran’s remaining US dates in solidarity with Macklemore, including Irish acts Aaron Rowe and Beoga, as well as Finneas and Danish band Lukas Graham.
Macklemore has said that the Free Palestine Tour will use its proceeds to support organisations working with Palestinians. The Dublin concert's listed beneficiaries include Anera, Gaza Soup Kitchen, HEAL Palestine, Medical Aid for Palestinians, the Palestine Children’s Relief Fund, Jewish Voice for Peace and UNRWA USA.
The rapper previously announced that he would donate $1 million in net earnings from his Sheeran tour appearances to organisations supporting Palestinians.
With the Dublin show now sold out, Macklemore’s new tour has generated significant demand ahead of its first announced European dates. Further shows and additional artists are expected to be announced as the tour develops.

content:
The Antoine Fuqua directed film stars Michael Jackson’s nephew Jaafar Jackson in his acting debut
Michael , the Michael Jackson biopic starring his nephew Jaafar Jackson, has completed its worldwide theatrical run with approximately $1.029bn at the global box office, according to Box Office Mojo . The final total stands at $1,028,706,645, including $372,303,388 from the United States and Canada and $656,403,257 from international markets.
The result places Michael among the biggest releases of 2026 and makes it the highest grossing biopic recorded at the worldwide box office. The film previously became the first biopic to cross the $1bn milestone in July, surpassing Oppenheimer and Bohemian Rhapsody in the process.
Directed by Antoine Fuqua, Michael stars Jaafar Jackson as his late uncle and follows the singer's early life, his rise with the Jackson 5 and his development into one of the most recognised performers in music history. Colman Domingo plays Joseph Jackson, while Nia Long portrays Katherine Jackson.
The film opened internationally in April, with Box Office Mojo recording a domestic opening of $97.2m. Its worldwide performance was driven particularly strongly by international markets, which accounted for about 63.8% of the final gross.
The billion dollar milestone was confirmed by Lionsgate and Universal in July, when the studios announced that the film had passed $1bn worldwide. At that stage, Michael had already become Lionsgate's first release to reach the figure.
The final tally gives the film a substantial theatrical run despite the discussion surrounding its portrayal of Jackson's life. Its commercial performance also places Jaafar Jackson's first major screen role at the centre of one of 2026's biggest box office stories.
With the theatrical run now complete, Michael leaves behind a billion dollar worldwide total and a new benchmark for biographical films.

title: Electric scooter battery fire destroys university bus in Faisalabad
description: The blaze gutted a parked university bus and seven other electric scooters
content:
Rescue 1122 contains blaze after a scooter caught fire while charging at GCWUF, with no casualties reported
A fire broke out in the parking area of Government College Women University Faisalabad on Wednesday after the battery of an electric scooter reportedly exploded while charging, destroying a parked university bus and seven other electric scooters.
Rescue 1122 teams brought the blaze under control, and no injuries or casualties were reported.
According to Faisalabad Rescue 1122 spokesperson Faisal Anwar, the university’s fire safety system was activated during the incident, alerting security officials on duty. “The support staff evacuated the area,” he said, adding that Rescue 1122 teams reached the scene and contained the fire.
The incident, however, raised questions about the safety of charging electric scooters on university premises, particularly the location of charging points and the proximity of vehicles and other combustible assets.
The university’s communication officer, Dr Ammara Javed, said the prompt response helped prevent casualties. “It is fortunate that no casualty occurred due to the speedy response of the university administration. However, the complete destruction of a university bus and some other scooters is a matter of concern. University students and staff remained safe in this unfortunate incident,” she said.
The cause of the fire had not been established, and it was too early to assign responsibility. Battery fires can result from several factors, including physical damage, manufacturing defects, electrical faults, incompatible chargers, overheating or problems with battery management systems.
Research published in the Fire Safety Journal in 2026 highlighted the risks associated with thermal runaway in lithium-ion batteries, a process that can cause rapid heat generation, gas release and ignition, with burning particles potentially being projected beyond the battery itself.
The incident also comes as Punjab expands its electric mobility infrastructure. Under the provincial government’s electric mobility policy, efforts are under way to develop charging infrastructure, while the Higher Education Department and Energy Department have been working on solarisation and electric vehicle charging facilities at 355 colleges, including 179 women’s colleges.
The growing use of electric vehicles on campuses makes the establishment of clear and uniform charging and fire-safety protocols increasingly important.
Safety measures generally include using compatible, manufacturer-approved chargers; avoiding the use of damaged, swollen or modified batteries; keeping charging points away from heat sources and combustible materials; and ensuring that charging areas can be monitored.
A recent academic study on electric mopeds in Lahore also identified battery damage, overcharging and exposure to heat among potential fire risks.
A technical inquiry into the Faisalabad incident could determine whether the battery, charger or electrical connection malfunctioned and whether the scooter was being charged at a designated facility. It could also examine the separation between charging areas and parked buses, the availability of appropriate firefighting equipment, staff training and access for emergency responders.
While the absence of casualties was a positive outcome, the incident highlighted the need for fire safety to keep pace with the growing use of electric scooters and other battery-powered vehicles on educational campuses.

title: David Fincher set to leave Netflix deal after years with streaming giant
description: Netflix relationship with David Fincher is set to end when his current deal expires next year
content:
Netflix relationship with David Fincher is set to end when his current deal expires next year
David Fincher is set to end his long term overall deal with Netflix after choosing not to renew his agreement with the streaming company, according to a report by Bloomberg . His current deal is due to expire next year, marking a significant change after years of collaboration between the filmmaker and the streamer.
Fincher is not understood to be moving to a rival studio as part of the decision. According to people familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg , the director does not currently feel a need to maintain a large overall agreement with any company. His representative declined to comment.
The filmmaker has maintained a close relationship with Netflix since directing and executive producing House of Cards , the service's landmark political drama. He later produced the crime series Mindhunter and the animated anthology Love, Death & Robots for the platform.
His Netflix film work has included Mank and The Killer , with his latest project, The Further Mis Adventures of Cliff Booth , still set for release through the streamer. Netflix has confirmed that the film, starring Brad Pitt as Cliff Booth, will receive a two week IMAX run beginning November 25 before arriving on Netflix on December 23.
The decision comes during a period when several established Netflix partners have moved their overall arrangements elsewhere. Shawn Levy recently agreed to a new television deal with Disney after his Netflix tenure, while the Duffer brothers moved their deal to Paramount. Variety reported that Levy will begin developing and producing projects for Disney in October 2027.
Fincher's departure from an overall arrangement does not necessarily mean the end of his work with Netflix. The filmmaker could still make future projects for the company, leaving the possibility of further collaboration open even after his current agreement expires.

title: Sylvester Stallone reflects on steroid use and his dramatic    Rocky III    transformation

content:
Stallone said a heart valve replacement became a turning point in how he approached his physical training
Sylvester Stallone has reflected on the extreme physical preparation behind his role in Rocky III , discussing his past steroid use and the demanding routine he followed to change his physique for the film.
Speaking with journalist Tracy Smith at New York’s 92NY, Stallone discussed his new memoir, Steps , and recalled the lengths he went to while developing Rocky Balboa for the third instalment of the franchise.
Stallone said he wanted Rocky to appear significantly different after achieving fame and success. He described the character as becoming increasingly vain and protected before eventually being confronted by Clubber Lang, played by Mr T.
To support that storyline, Stallone said he undertook a major physical transformation. He recalled reducing his body fat dramatically while following an extremely restrictive diet that included tuna and large amounts of coffee. He also acknowledged using steroids during the process.
The actor later discussed the broader expectations surrounding action stars and superhero characters. Stallone argued that performers portraying physically enhanced characters often undergo substantial preparation to create an appearance that differs from an ordinary physique.
His comments come as he looks back on the physical toll associated with his decades of action roles. Stallone previously told The New York Times that he used steroids while making Rocky III and has spoken about the effects he believes the drug had on his body.
During his conversation with Smith, Stallone also recalled a significant health event that changed his approach to physical training. He said his wife, Jennifer Flavin Stallone, urged him to seek medical attention after noticing that he appeared unwell. Stallone subsequently underwent heart valve replacement surgery.
He described the experience as a wake up call and said he believes his wife’s intervention helped save his life.
The discussion was part of the first live instalment of a new series featuring CBS Sunday Morning at 92NY. The programme brings figures from arts, politics and culture before a live audience for extended conversations.
Stallone’s appearance also forms part of the promotion for Steps , his memoir about his life and career, including the creation and enduring legacy of Rocky , which marked its 50th anniversary in 2026.

title: Aaron Sorkin says    The Social Reckoning    reshoots were not driven by trailer backlash
description: Sony gave Sorkin three additional shooting days after he suggested changes to two scenes
content:
Sony gave Sorkin three additional shooting days after he suggested changes to two scenes
Aaron Sorkin has addressed the reshoots for The Social Reckoning , saying the additional filming had nothing to do with reactions to the film’s trailer.
In an interview with Vanity Fair , the writer and director explained that the reshoots took place after Sony Pictures chairman and CEO Tom Rothman offered him an opportunity to revisit the film. Sorkin said he believed there were two scenes where additional work could improve the movie, prompting Rothman to approve three days of shooting.
Sorkin described the process as an effort to improve a film he already liked rather than repair a production that had gone wrong. He distinguished the work from reshoots that studios undertake when a project has serious problems.
The Social Reckoning is Sorkin’s follow up to his 2010 film The Social Network . The new movie focuses on Facebook whistleblower Frances Haugen and journalist Jeff Horwitz, whose reporting contributed to public scrutiny of the company and its handling of internal research. Mikey Madison plays Haugen, while Jeremy Allen White portrays Horwitz. Jeremy Strong plays Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg.
The film also addresses political division and the January 6 attack on the US Capitol. Sorkin has explained that Donald Trump is not named in the film, saying he wanted the story to focus on Facebook’s role in the spread of divisiveness and extremism rather than present the subject through a specific partisan framing.
Sorkin also discussed the production’s limited test screenings. Because the studio wanted to maintain secrecy around the project, he said screenings were conducted with small groups of Sony employees rather than a broad public testing audience. He acknowledged that this was not a representative polling sample.
Legal scrutiny was another part of the production process. According to Vanity Fair , Sony brought in an outside law firm to review the film, with Sorkin discussing changes made to certain dialogue and fictionalised elements during that process.
The Social Reckoning is scheduled to open in cinemas on October 9, with Sony Pictures currently listing the film as an upcoming theatrical release.

title: FO expresses condolences over deaths of five crew members in Somalia rescue operation
description: Says govt making  every possible effort  to bring bodies of three deceased Pakistani nationals home
content:
Says govt making 'every possible effort' to bring bodies of three deceased Pakistani nationals home
The Foreign Office (FO) on Wednesday expressed condolences over the deaths of five crew members, including three Pakistani nationals, during the operation to recover the hijacked vessel MT Honour 25 off the coast of Somalia.
According to a post on X, the FO said the government was making efforts to arrange medical treatment for the three injured Pakistani nationals and ensure that the bodies of the deceased nationals were transported to Pakistan.
The three deceased Pakistani nationals were identified as Rafi Ullah Khan, Syed Kashif Umer, and Mahmood Ahmed Ansari.
"The Government and people of Pakistan extend their deepest condolences to the bereaved families," the FO said. It added, "We share their grief at this painful time and pray for strength, patience, and comfort for the families, and for the departed souls to rest in peace."
The statement noted that four other crew members were injured during the incident, of which three were Pakistani nationals. "The injured have been taken to a nearby hospital and are receiving medical care."
🔊 PR No. 2️⃣6️⃣9️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Pakistan Expresses Condolences over Loss of lives during Recovery of MT Honour 25 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/J2JwnYDSpb
The Foreign Office also stated that the surviving crew members of the vessel had been brought safely ashore at Bandar Beyla. "Pakistan's team at the embassy in Djibouti is proceeding to Bandar Beyla to assist the Pakistani nationals," it said.
The statement further stated that the government, "through its Mission and relevant authorities, remains in close contact with the Somali authorities and other concerned stakeholders."
"Every possible effort is being made to ensure proper medical care for the injured, facilitate the transportation of the mortal remains of the deceased; and ensure the safe return of the surviving Pakistani crew members," it concluded.
The oil tanker Honour 25, sailing under the Somali flag from Oman to Somalia, was hijacked by pirates on April 21. There were 17 crew members aboard, 10 of whom were Pakistani nationals. The families of the Pakistani hostages have continuously appealed to the government for the safe release of their loved ones.
During their captivity, the pirates initially demanded a ransom of $3 million for their release. The demand was later reduced to $1.9 million and subsequently to $1 million. Other than the Pakistani nationals who lost their lives, the deceased also included an Indian crew member, Tanveer, and a chief engineer from Myanmar.
The pirates came under pressure during the operation and, while retreating from the vessel, opened indiscriminate fire on the kidnapped crew before fleeing the ship. The injured sailors were identified as Usman, Yasir, Ameen and Vicky, who hailed from Indonesia. Crewmembers Hussain Yousuf, Imran Ali and Yaseen remained safe.
Read: DPM Dar directs intensified diplomatic efforts for safe, early release of 10 Pakistani hostages
Two surviving Pakistani crewmembers told a human rights lawyer that Somali pirates had killed five kidnapped sailors, including three Pakistanis, and injured four others aboard the MT Honour 25 while fleeing the maritime police.
Pakistani sailors Hussain Yousuf and Imran Ali, who survived the incident, contacted the Ansar Burney Welfare Trust office in Karachi, using the ship captain's mobile phone, and provided details of the incident, according to the trust.
Somalia’s Puntland Maritime Police Force said they had rescued another oil tanker, days after a rescue operation ended with pirates escaping in suspicious circumstances. They added that the Honour 25 had 18,500 barrels of oil on board when it was hijacked.
The Gulf of Aden and Somalia coasts have seen a resurgence in piracy since April, according to figures from the International Maritime Organisation, with at least 15 attacks this year, the highest since 2013.

title: Macklemore   s decade old    Can   t Hold Us    becomes a major hit again
description: The 2011 track  recorded with Ryan Lewis and Ray Dalton  climbed from No  146 to No  100 on the Billboard Global 200
content:
The 2011 track, recorded with Ryan Lewis and Ray Dalton, climbed from No. 146 to No. 100 on the Billboard Global 200
Macklemore’s decade-old smash Can’t Hold Us is experiencing a major resurgence, reaching new career highs on two global Billboard charts amid renewed attention surrounding the rapper.
The 2011 track, recorded with Ryan Lewis and Ray Dalton, climbed from No. 146 to No. 100 on the Billboard Global 200 this week. It also jumped from No. 121 to No. 80 on the Billboard Global Excl. U.S. chart, giving Macklemore his highest-ever positions on both rankings.
The renewed success comes more than a decade after Can’t Hold Us became one of Macklemore and Lewis’ biggest hits. The song was released as a single from their 2012 album The Heist and eventually topped the Billboard Hot 100, becoming the duo’s second No. 1 after Thrift Shop.
Macklemore’s recent chart resurgence follows the controversy surrounding his removal from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour. The rapper was dropped from the tour after making pro-Palestinian comments while performing at MetLife Stadium, with Sheeran later saying the decision was made by the tour promoter after venues objected to Macklemore remaining on the bill.
The renewed attention has also brought Macklemore’s political track Hind’s Hall back into the charts. The song has re-entered Billboard’s Digital Song Sales chart at No. 10 after selling nearly 1,600 downloads in the US, according to Luminate.
Hind’s Hall was originally released in 2024 and was inspired by pro-Palestinian student demonstrations at Columbia University. It previously peaked at No. 7 on the Digital Song Sales chart, making its latest return its second appearance in the top 10.
With Can’t Hold Us now reaching new global chart peaks more than a decade after its release, Macklemore is seeing renewed interest in both his earlier catalogue and more recent music.

Khloé Kardashian recalls travelling to Tennessee to spend time with Dolly Parton for her 2025 podcast
Khloé Kardashian has reflected on the time she spent with Dolly Parton while recalling the country music star’s appearance on her Khloé in Wonder Land podcast in 2025.
Kardashian said she felt “blessed and fortunate” to have spent time with Parton, who appeared on the podcast in July 2025. The reality star travelled to Tennessee to record the episode.
“I think I was one of her last podcasts that she did,” Kardashian told People. “I flew to Tennessee. I got to be with her. I feel so blessed and fortunate that it happened. I can't believe how lucky I am.”
Kardashian also recalled Parton’s approach to her public image, saying she was “sort of like a caricature of herself”.
“She loved it and leaned into it and made no apologies for it,” Kardashian said.
The Good American founder said she related to Parton’s willingness to embrace the public persona she had created for herself, drawing a comparison with her own family’s experience in the public eye.
“She’s in on the joke, and I always think me and my family are also in on the joke,” Kardashian explained. “So I really relate to that type of mentality. I really respect that she just did what she loved to do, and it was harmless, and it was for her. And everyone respected it.”
“That’s how we should all treat others, everyone,” she added.
Parton died aged 80 on August 25, according to the supplied information. Her nephew Bryan Seaver announced her death in an Instagram video, while her team later confirmed that she had experienced a brief, private battle with cancer.

title: Karan Johar announces final season of  Koffee With Karan
description: Filmmaker looks back on the show   s 22 year journey and says he is ready to turn his focus back to films
content:
Filmmaker looks back on the show’s 22-year journey and says he is ready to turn his focus back to films
Karan Johar has revealed that the upcoming season of Koffee With Karan will be his last, bringing an end to a defining chapter of his career while hinting at more time for filmmaking. In an emotional Instagram video, the filmmaker looked back on the origins of the celebrity talk show, which began with an idea he once shared with his late father in 2004.
“This is more of an emotional message than a professional announcement,” Johar said. “I know this show gave me so much. I reached a point in my life where I realised that all good things have to come to an end. With a kind of heavy heart, I have to say that this will be my very last season of Koffee With Karan .”
Johar recalled telling his father in June 2004 that he wanted to host a talk show featuring two celebrities in an informal and candid conversation.
“I think it was June 2004 where I told my dad that I really want to host a talk show and I want to get two celebrities or stars and just have an informal, candid chat with them,” he shared.
His father, however, questioned the idea. “And he looked at me and said Karan, you will invite your friends and chat with them. You do that every day so who will pay you for that?”
Johar's father died that same month, on June 26. “He passed away that month itself, actually. On the 26th of June,” Johar said.
Just weeks later, Johar began filming the show that would go on to become one of Indian television’s most recognisable celebrity formats. “The very first day I shot for it was August 16th, 2004 and I’m here now, 8 seasons later, 22 years later, 161 episodes later.”
Looking back at the people who have appeared on the famous couch, Johar said the show had witnessed friendships, romances, marriages and fallouts over the years.
“A lot happened. I called lovers, I called friends, I called families. I called lovers who then went on to become ex-lovers. Some of them even got married. I nearly put an end to careers of national icons,” he added.
Johar also acknowledged some of the controversies and labels that have followed him throughout his career. “I am living with the word ‘nepotism’ even today” and “‘Conjecture’ because a kind of national word,” he said.
The filmmaker then pointed to an irony he had noticed in public conversations around him: people often asked about the next season of his talk show rather than his next film.
“So much happened. And everywhere I go, fortunately or unfortunately I am always asked when is the next season of Koffee with Karan , I wonder why they don’t ask me when my next feature film is,” he said.
For Johar, however, the decision appears to be less about the criticism surrounding the programme and more about bringing its long-running journey to a natural close.
He also appeared to anticipate the reaction the announcement could generate online, acknowledging that the show had attracted its share of criticism alongside its popularity.
“There will be trolls, there will be comments, there will be posts. And I’m ready to take that on. But within all of that and beneath all of that, I know that there is still abundant love for this cup of Koffee. So join me in my last season of Koffee with Karan and have that one last cup of Koffee with me. Cheers!”
The announcement marks a significant moment for Johar. Over the years, the show became known for its informal celebrity conversations, rapid-fire rounds and candid revelations, while comments and exchanges on the programme frequently became talking points beyond the show itself.
Johar currently has two back-to-back films expected to enter production in 2027. For now, however, he is inviting audiences to join him for one final cup of Koffee .

GTA 6 will feature more than 170 animal species, including Rare, Discoverable and Legendary creatures
GTA 6 will feature more than 170 animal species across Leonida, including rare, discoverable and Legendary creatures, according to Game Informer.
The latest issue of Game Informer has revealed new details about Rockstar Games’ upcoming open-world title, including its wildlife and the activities available to players.
GTA 6 is set in Leonida, a fictional state inspired by Florida, and its animal ecosystem will span urban, rural, aquatic and wetland environments.
According to the magazine, the game will include more than 60 types of birds and over 30 land mammals, alongside reptiles and fish. Wildlife will include feral cats, monkeys, whales, turtles and jellyfish.
“Florida has a diverse animal ecosystem that we wanted to faithfully include across the different biomes in Leonida – urban and rural environs, aquatic life both inland and ocean, and the wetland habitats like the swamps and Everglades,” Rockstar vice president of dynamic art Michael Kane explained.
Some animals will fall into Rare, Discoverable and Legendary categories. Rockstar has not revealed which creatures will belong to these categories.
The wildlife will also feature different visual characteristics, including iridescence, bioluminescence and translucency. Animals will have different feather types, while hair and fur systems will affect pelts and coats.
Players will be able to study animals and visit a zoo, adding wildlife-related activities to the game.
Other activities revealed by Game Informer include base jumping, billiards, gym sessions, kayaking, mini golf, scuba diving, street and off-road racing, air boating and jet skiing.
Jason and Lucia will be able to take part in these activities when they are not carrying out robberies, with some activities also contributing to their relationship.
The scale of GTA 6’s wildlife follows the emphasis placed on animals in Red Dead Redemption 2. Rockstar is scheduled to release GTA 6 on November 19, 2026.

title: Norway parliament probes Epstein links to politicians  diplomats
description: 11 current  former foreign ministers  development ministers face committee questioning with findings due early 2028
content:
11 current, former foreign ministers, development ministers face committee questioning with findings due early 2028
Norway's parliament began public hearings on Wednesday over ties between late United States sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and Norwegian diplomats and politicians in a scandal that has shaken the nation's elite.
US President Donald Trump's Department of Justice in January released millions of Epstein-related documents , revealing connections to politicians, royals and the ultra-rich around the world.
Norway, home of the Nobel Peace Prize and often a fulcrum of international diplomacy, has seen major fallout, triggering parliamentary inquiries and police investigations.
The government must explain what it is doing to restore trust in the foreign service, said Jonas Andersen Sayed, the leader of the hearing at parliament's Committee on Scrutiny and Constitutional Affairs. "There are many people who have demonstrated very poor judgement," Andersen Sayed told Reuters of those who had friendships with Epstein.
Read: Epstein claimed Trump insider role to advise Ambani
The committee has summoned 11 current and former foreign ministers and development ministers, including Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere, who was foreign minister from 2005 to 2012. Stoere reiterated that he had never had any relation to Epstein and said that problems were due to a few individuals not a systemic problem with the foreign ministry.
Issues identified had either been addressed or were being addressed, he said, citing for instance updated rules over conflicts of interest for decision-makers. "Updated and comprehensive rules are necessary, but even the best system provides no complete guarantee against errors being made, whether intentional or unintentional," Stoere said. "No system involving people can guarantee against the misuse of trust."
However, as far as he was aware, Epstein had exercised no influence on Norway's foreign policy, development aid policy "or any other choices we had taken", Stoere added.
Boerge Brende, a former foreign minister also due to testify, resigned from the position of president and CEO of the World Economic Forum after revelations of his friendly relations with Epstein. Brende has said he was unaware of Epstein's past and criminal activities before first meeting him in 2018.
Erik Solheim, a former international development minister, welcomed the probe but said it should not send a signal to diplomats to play it safe in future, particularly when talking to parties involved in wars.
Oslo regularly talks to groups that others boycott, such as Hamas or the Muslim Brotherhood. "We must take care of our peace diplomacy, do more of it," Solheim told the committee.
Though not appearing before parliament, a number of other prominent Norwegians with ties to Epstein, including former premier Thorbjoern Jagland, former minister Terje Roed-Larsen and ex-diplomat Mona Juul, are under police investigation on corruption accusations.
Read More: Melania Trump denies any ties to Epstein
Roed-Larsen has apologised for his close relation to Epstein, which included a personal loan from the financier, and in 2020 stepped down as CEO of the New York-based International Peace Institute, a think tank.
Furthermore, Queen Mette-Marit, wife of King Haakon, has apologised for her friendship with Epstein, but is also not subject to the hearing.
In parallel, parliament has appointed an external commission of academics and legal experts to probe "matters and issues brought to light" by the files, with an aim of "improving the integrity and transparency of Norwegian authorities."
The rare investigative commission, covering more than 30 years of Norwegian diplomatic history, is due to deliver its findings in early 2028.

title: Lahore to host 10 day Basant festival from Jan 29 to Feb 7
description: Maryam Nawaz approves extended celebrations  with a one day break for Kashmir Day and stricter safety measures planned
content:
Maryam Nawaz approves extended celebrations, with a one-day break for Kashmir Day and stricter safety measures planned
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Wednesday approved and rescheduled a 10-day Basant festival in Lahore, with celebrations set to take place from January 29 to February 7 2027. According to an official announcement, celebrations will be suspended for one day on February 5 to commemorate Kashmir Day.
The decision comes after the revival of Basant in Lahore earlier this year, when the traditional spring festival was held from February 6 to 8 after the provincial government lifted the 2007 ban on kite flying through an ordinance .
وزیراعلی مریم نواز شریف کا زندہ دلان لاہور کے لئے بڑی خوش خبری کا اعلان لاہور میں 10 دن بسنت منائی جائے گی، وزیراعلی مریم نواز شریف نے منظوری دے دی 25 سال کے تعطل کے بعد رواں سال فروری میں 6 سے 8 فروری تک لاہور میں بسنت منائی گئی تھی وزیراعلی مریم نواز شریف نے نئے سال 2027…
The chief minister directed the authorities to organise the expanded festival to mark the arrival of 2027 and promote Punjab's cultural heritage. "The 10-day Basant celebrations will help promote Punjab's cultural colours and Lahore's ancient historical tradition across the world," Maryam said.
She also directed the authorities to put in place stronger safety and public facilitation measures than those adopted during the previous festival. She appealed to the public to demonstrate responsibility and vigilance during the celebrations to help ensure the protection of human life.
The emphasis on safety comes after the three-day festival earlier this year resulted in 17 deaths and 160 injuries, according to official Home Department records . However, sources told The Express Tribune that the actual death toll was higher, at 21.
Kite flying and manufacturing were first banned in Punjab in 2005 after more than 25 people were killed. The ban was intermittently relaxed in 2006 and 2007 but was reimposed in 2007 following a rise in fatalities.
By 2024, more than 2,020 people had lost their lives in kite-flying-related incidents, according to available records. More than 90% of the deaths were caused by chemical-coated kite strings that cut victims' throats or faces.

Federal Bureau of Prisons records reportedly show Combs' release date is currently January 21, 2028.

Pakistan is set to take a major step towards revival and transformation of its national game with the formal launch of the Pakistan Hockey League (PHL) in Islamabad on October 14, 2026. PHL is the latest initiative from Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF) in its efforts to improve and modernise hockey infrastructure in Pakistan. The PHF press release said on Wednesday that the federation awarded the rights to Mediacast after a competitive bidding process earlier this year. “Now the PHF and Mediacast are set to launch the inaugural season of PHL in 2027. The PHF said the PHL will also provide an opportunity for Pakistani hockey professionals to work alongside experienced international experts and build expertise that can eventually benefit the entire national hockey structure. “A professionally managed league will create multiple new commercial opportunities through team ownership and partnerships, broadcasting and digital content, merchandising, advertising, hospitality, ticketing and grassroots programmes,” the release added. “The challenge before us is to ensure that the sport’s rich history becomes the foundation of a modern and sustainable future, rather than merely a source of nostalgia.”

title: Ayesha Omar challenges misconceptions about feminism  highlights violence against women
description: Actor shares cases from Pakistan  India and US while calling for greater accountability around violence against women
content:
Actor shares cases from Pakistan, India and US while calling for greater accountability around violence against women
Actor and activist Ayesha Omar has challenged the idea that feminism is synonymous with hatred of men, using a series of Instagram posts to highlight cases of violence against women in Pakistan, India and the United States.
“Why does the word feminism bother men so much?” Omar wrote in her caption, accompanying a quote attributed to Nadia Carly that read: “Feminism doesn’t hate men. It hates abusers, sexists, misogynists, rapists, pedophiles, and deadbeats. And good men aren’t bothered by that because they hate them too.”
Omar followed the post with a series of Instagram stories highlighting recent cases of violence against women from around the world and drawing attention to the circumstances surrounding each incident.
Her first post emphasised the need for men to hold their friends accountable for how they treat women, before turning to individual cases.
Among those she shared was the alleged assault of a pregnant woman in Gujranwala after her family reportedly learned through an ultrasound that she was expecting another daughter.
Omar also shared coverage of protests in New Delhi following the alleged gang rape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park near Kalkaji Temple. Students from Lady Shri Ram College and other Delhi University institutions took to the streets on September 23, demanding greater safety for women and accountability from authorities.
She ended the series by drawing attention to the case now being referred to as the “Cornell Seven” in the United States.
The case centres on allegations made by a former Cornell University student, identified in court filings as Jane Doe, who said she was sexually assaulted by seven students at the Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024.
The renewed investigation has also prompted wider scrutiny of how Cornell University and local authorities handled the allegations when they were first reported.
For Omar, the subject is part of a longer-running public conversation. She has repeatedly spoken about gender equality, feminism and harassment, including her own experiences within Pakistan’s entertainment industry.
In a 2022 interview , Omar described herself as a feminist and said she believed feminism meant equal opportunities for men and women. She also spoke about the objectification of women in the media industry, arguing that women were often judged more harshly than men. She further said feminism was misunderstood as western propaganda.
More recently, in June 2026 , Omar joined actor Aliya Ali in speaking about women’s safety at an event in London. She called on men to take greater responsibility for creating safer environments for women and urged them to speak up about women’s safety.
Her latest Instagram posts continue that conversation, linking a debate over the meaning of feminism with cases of alleged violence against women across three countries.
For Omar, the message remains centred on accountability — particularly the responsibility of men to challenge harmful behaviour among their peers rather than treating feminism itself as an attack on men.

title: Two pilots wounded after fight on Israel bound flight forces emergency landing
description: Boeing 737 plane then again transmitted the initial general emergency signal before later landing at Tabuk
content:
Boeing 737 plane then again transmitted the initial general emergency signal before later landing at Tabuk
Two pilots were wounded after reportedly fighting on board a plane bound for Israel, forcing it to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday.
The flight bound for Israel from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) diverted to Saudi Arabia after transmitting emergency signals following a fight between the pilots, an Israeli official said.
Flydubai Flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv diverted over Jordanian airspace ​towards Saudi Arabia, transmitting a general emergency signal and then another emergency signal that indicated possible unlawful interference several minutes ​later, according to flight-tracking website Flightradar24.
The Boeing 737 plane, which Israeli media said had around 150 Israeli ⁠passengers on board, then again transmitted the initial general emergency signal before later landing at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, the ​website said.
According to Anadolu , the flight was carrying 174 passengers.
The aircraft's data appeared to show that it had suddenly and rapidly descended by nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 ​seconds before the first emergency signal, Flightradar24 said.
Read: Israeli settlers attack West Bank village, blocking family's return home
The emergency signals triggered a major security response in Israel, which has no official diplomatic relations with Saudi Arabia, where the plane landed. The incident highlighted the potential risks on a route that has become popular among Israeli nationals since the UAE and Israel ​normalised ties 6 years ago.
Around 90 minutes after takeoff, while entering Jordanian airspace, the aircraft transmitted code “7700,” the international code for a general emergency, the Israeli newspaper Ynet said.
It subsequently transmitted code “7500,” which is used to indicate unlawful interference with an aircraft, including a possible hijacking.
Passengers overcame co-pilot who tried to crash flight, Netanyahu says
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the co-pilot tried to crash the plane after stabbing the pilot, but passengers restrained him while another pilot safely landed the plane in Saudi Arabia.
Describing the event ​as "a highly severe security incident," Netanyahu said Saudi authorities would interrogate ⁠the co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073 from the UAE to Israel.
The alleged ​assailant, who an Israeli official identified as an Omani national, was arrested after the ​plane landed, Netanyahu said.
"All passengers are out of harm's way," Netanyahu, who described the passengers as being almost all Israeli, said in a video statement released by his office.
The Israeli leader quoted a ​passenger as saying that passengers, along with a member of the crew, broke into ​the cockpit after the aircraft "entered a tailspin and began to dive" and found the co-pilot "trying to ‌sabotage ⁠the plane's systems."
"They saved many lives. They prevented a heavy disaster," he said.
Doron Spielman, a spokesperson for the Israeli prime minister's office, told Reuters the incident was not believed to ​have been a hijacking, describing it as a "different incident".
An airline spokesperson said the flydubai flight experienced an "incident" en route to Tel Aviv and diverted to ‌Tabuk, where ⁠it landed safely. All passengers were safe and accounted for, the spokesperson said, without providing any further details.
An Israeli official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, told Reuters the pilots had transmitted the emergency signals after getting into a physical altercation with each other.
It was not immediately clear if either pilot had intentionally transmitted the signals.
Yasmin Abu Kasis said her daughter Miriam, who was among the passengers ​on the flight, had told her ​that she had heard screaming ⁠and that a man holding a knife had forced one of the pilots onto the floor, and that there was blood everywhere.
Israeli Channel 12 later said the incident appeared not to be security-related and that authorities were checking whether the distress signal had been activated accidentally because of an argument between the pilot and co-pilot.
The broadcaster said the flight crew consisted of a Russian pilot and a Ukrainian co-pilot.
Read more: Israeli occupiers storm Al-Aqsa Mosque in East Jerusalem as Palestinian shops forced to close for ‘Jewish prayers’
Israeli media published a photo purportedly taken from inside the plane, which ​appeared to show a passenger's blood-soaked shirt. Reuters could not immediately verify the image.
In a statement, ​the Israeli prime ⁠minister's office said the situation was "under control" and that all measures were being taken to bring the Israeli passengers back to Israel.
Flydubai operates daily return flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv, a route that is popular among Israeli nationals. The flight path normally uses airspace over Saudi ⁠Arabia and ​Jordan.
Flydubai later informed Israeli authorities that a replacement aircraft would be dispatched from Dubai to Saudi Arabia to bring back the Israeli passengers who had been on the flight, Ynet reported.
The Israel Airports Authority, meanwhile, denied reports that the country’s airspace had been closed during the incident.
Senior officials in Israel’s aviation industry said suspicion of a security incident on the Flydubai flight had not yet been ruled out, Ynet reported.
An initial assessment cited by officials claimed that one of the pilots allegedly "attempted to cause a crash," while the other pilot managed to thwart the attempt with the help of Israeli passengers.
Meanwhile, Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz claimed that an incident involving an Israel-bound Flydubai flight was an "attempted terrorist attack."

title: Florence Pugh says Tom Holland helped make her    Spider Man    return happen
description: Pugh recalled Holland publicly naming her as an actor he wanted alongside him in a future film
content:
Pugh recalled Holland publicly naming her as an actor he wanted alongside him in a future film
Florence Pugh has credited Tom Holland with helping bring her Marvel character Yelena Belova into Spider Man: Brand New Day , recalling how a comment from the actor helped spark excitement around the pairing.
Speaking on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon , Pugh said the opportunity grew from Holland publicly expressing his interest in working with her. She recalled that after Black Widow was released in 2021, Holland was asked at a red carpet event who he would like to appear alongside in a future film.
According to Pugh, Holland named her and specifically referenced her role as Yelena.
“This all happened because of Tom,” Pugh said, explaining that his comment helped fans become excited about the possibility of the two actors appearing together in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
Pugh first played Yelena in Black Widow , where the character was introduced as Natasha Romanoff’s younger sister. She later reprised the role in Thunderbolts , before appearing alongside Holland in Spider Man: Brand New Day .
The latest film, starring Holland as Peter Parker, was released in cinemas on July 31, 2026. Pugh’s return as Yelena adds another established Marvel character to the film’s cast.
Spider Man: Brand New Day has also become a major box office success. The film has surpassed $936m at the North American box office, overtaking Star Wars: The Force Awakens to become the highest grossing domestic release of all time, according to Variety . Its worldwide total has reached approximately $2.45bn.
Pugh celebrated the film’s performance during her television appearance, congratulating Holland on its success.
The actress is continuing her work across several major projects. She is also set to return as Princess Irulan in Denis Villeneuve’s Dune: Part Three . She is scheduled to reprise Yelena in Avengers: Doomsday , which is also due to feature Holland’s fellow Marvel stars.
Pugh’s comments offer a look at how an offhand public remark from Holland eventually became part of her journey with Yelena, connecting her character to one of Marvel’s biggest franchises

title: Gohar urges federal govt to avoid governor   s rule in K P  vows peaceful Oct 4 protest
description: PTI chairman says only release of Imran  Bushra can pave way for resolving political problems
content:
PTI chairman says only release of Imran, Bushra can pave way for resolving political problems
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Wednesday said the party’s planned October 4 long march would remain a peaceful and political activity, urging the government to avoid imposing measures such as governor rule or emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).
Speaking to the media at Parliament House, Barrister Gohar said, "The response to the long march should not be the imposition of governor rule but rather political engagement with PTI founder Imran Khan." “Our effort is that the long march remains peaceful and completely political. Neither should governor rule be imposed nor should an emergency be enforced,” he added.
چیئرمین پی ٹی آئی بیرسٹر گوہر خان کی پارلیمنٹ ہاؤس میں میڈیا سے گفتگو ہماری کوشش ہے لانگ مارچ پُرامن اور مکمل سیاسی انداز میں ہو، نہ گورنر راج لگے اور نہ ایمرجنسی نافذ ہو، لانگ مارچ کا جواب گورنر راج نہیں بلکہ خان صاحب سے ملاقاتیں کرائیں، انصاف کریں خان صاحب اور بشری بی بی کی… pic.twitter.com/FP2Hze6QUf
He further stated that arranging meetings with Imran and ensuring justice would help resolve the ongoing political issues. “Only the release of Imran and Bushra Bibi can pave the way for resolving political problems,” Barrister Gohar said, adding that the October 4 long march would proceed as planned.
Clarifying the party’s position regarding K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, the PTI chairman said the long march was limited to Islamabad and that Afridi had the support of the PTI founder and the entire party. “It is Imran’s province, Imran’s mandate prevails, and Imran’s directions are followed. Nothing will happen based on anyone else’s wishes,” he said.
In a post on X, K-P Information Minister Shafi Jan said the long march would commence from southern K-P on October 4 and would be led by CM Afridi.
لانگ مارچ 4 اکتوبر کو جنوبی خیبر پختون خواہ سے شروع گا ۔ سی ایم آفریدی لیڈ کرینگے ۔
The possibility of imposing governor’s rule in K-P gained attention after several federal ministers said constitutional provisions allowed such measures if required, while accusing the PTI-led provincial government of failing to address security and governance challenges.
Federal officials said the situation in the province had reached a stage where constitutional options, including governor’s rule or emergency, could be considered.
The debate intensified amid growing tensions between the Centre and the PTI-led provincial government, particularly ahead of the party’s planned October 4 march towards Islamabad.
Federal ministers cited law and order concerns, while PTI leaders opposed any move to impose governor’s rule and maintained that political dialogue was the way forward.
K-P CM 'not happy' with PTI's long march preparations
CM Afridi expressed displeasure over the lack of interest among some PTI members in preparations for the party’s planned long march to Islamabad, according to party sources.
He made the remarks while chairing a meeting of PTI’s parliamentary party at the Chief Minister’s House in Peshawar, while some lawmakers did not attend the meeting in person and joined through Zoom.
Addressing participants, Afridi criticised what he viewed as insufficient commitment to preparations for the march.
“We also have Mir Jafars and Mir Sadiqs within our ranks,” Afridi said.
According to the sources, the chief minister reiterated that PTI would depart from Peshawar for Islamabad on October 4, saying that “We are not going to conquer Islamabad, and the federal government is blocking our way.”
Referring to allegations that protesters could carry sticks or slingshots, Afridi said: “We will go with two hands and two feet.”
Later, CM Afridi said in a post on X, “You should prepare; I am ready.”
میری تیاری مکمل ہے۔ کیا آپ تیار ہیں؟ انشاءاللہ 4 اکتوبر۔ pic.twitter.com/Y7wFhAENsM
Meanwhile, PTI K-P President Junaid Akbar directed lawmakers and party leaders currently outside the country to return to Pakistan.
Akbar said MPAs, MNAs, and party leaders who were not in Pakistan on October 4 would have no connection with PTI and told them they could form another party if they wished.
The PTI had initially announced its long march to Islamabad for September 27 , with the party saying it had exhausted other constitutional and legal avenues and was mobilising supporters across the country.
As the date approached, the Islamabad High Court directed federal and provincial authorities to prevent the use of state resources for the protest and ordered that roads could not be blocked by political parties or public office holders. The federal government subsequently stepped up security preparations and warned the PTI against disrupting traffic and economic activity.
The issue of governor’s rule in K-P also became a major point of contention. On September 21, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the government was consulting the Law Ministry on legal options for the province, including Governor’s Rule , if the PTI proceeded with the march. Two days later, however, Information Minister Atta Tarar ruled out any plan to impose Governor’s Rule, saying the federal government had no intention of removing the PTI administration.
The federal government has repeatedly urged PTI not to proceed with its planned march, warning that Islamabad could not be shut down and that any disruption to law and order would not be allowed.
Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry called for dialogue and said a route that could be opened through talks could not be opened through a march. K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also urged the provincial government to abandon the protest , saying the “ground reality” was not in its favour.

title: Aashir Wajahat s  Sadqay  crosses 100 million streams on Spotify
description: Milestone gives the singer renewed confidence after he opened up about his fears before releasing the 2024 hit
content:
Milestone gives the singer renewed confidence after he opened up about his fears before releasing the 2024 hit
Singer and actor Aashir Wajahat is celebrating a major milestone in his music career as Sadqay crosses 100 million streams on Spotify — a figure that has given new meaning to the insecurities he felt before releasing the song.
Wajahat took to Instagram to mark the achievement with a series of photographs capturing the people and memories connected to the song’s journey. Among them were pictures with his brother and fellow artist Nayel Wajahat and singer Nehaal Naseem, his collaborators on Sadqay .
The carousel also featured a childhood photograph of Aashir and Nayel dressed as Superman and Batman. The throwback offered a glimpse of the brothers long before they began making music together, adding a nostalgic touch to a milestone centred on one of their biggest collaborations.
Reflecting on the song’s journey, Aashir opened up about the uncertainty he felt before releasing it. “100 million streams on Spotify. I remember having my insecurities and fears before releasing this track,” he wrote, admitting that he did not know “how it would perform or if people would connect with it.”
The response to Sadqay eventually gave him the reassurance he needed. Wajahat said the song taught him that “when a piece of art comes straight from the heart with the purest of intentions it will make its way to the hearts of everyone it finds”.
Released in 2024 , Sadqay brought together Aashir, Nayel and Nehaal Naseem. The collaboration became one of the standout releases in Aashir’s growing music catalogue and has now crossed the 100 million-stream mark on Spotify.
The singer used the occasion to thank the listeners who helped take the track to the milestone. “Thank you to everyone for tuning in and giving strength to a young scared artist like me to continue what I love. Love to everyone involved in this project who made it possible,” he wrote.
For Wajahat, however, the significance of Sadqay appears to extend beyond the streaming figure. The song has also changed how he sees himself as an artist. “I feel more confident about my craft than I’ve ever felt,” he wrote. He ended his message with a declaration of intent: “I’m locked in.”
The sentiment marks a clear contrast with the uncertainty he described before the song’s release. What began with fears over whether listeners would connect with the track has since become a milestone that has strengthened his confidence in his work.
Wajahat has grown up in Pakistan’s entertainment industry. The son of filmmaker Wajahat Rauf and producer Shazia Wajahat, he began his career at a young age before establishing himself across acting and music.
His acting credits include films such as Karachi Se Lahore , Lahore Se Aagey and Chhalawa , as well as television projects including Pinjra .
Over the years, music has become an increasingly important part of his career, with releases including Naazni , Distant , Dheema Dheema and Tumse Main Mila , among others.
His collaboration with Nayel and Nehaal on Sadqay has proved particularly significant, with the song becoming a defining release in his musical journey.
In 2026, he appeared in the drama Kafeel , where he played Subuk alongside Sanam Saeed and Emmad Irfani. He later reunited with Kafeel co-star Areeka Haq for the music video of his single Beqadra , bringing their on-screen pairing into another project.
His recent work has continued along a dual path, with acting on screen alongside a steadily expanding catalogue of music.

title: Russia issues nuclear warning to NATO as tensions rise in the Baltic
description: Russian embassies in European countries issued statements in the past three days accusing NATO of escalating tensions
content:
Russian embassies in European countries issued statements in the past three days accusing NATO of escalating tensions
Russia has warned NATO it would be ready to resort to nuclear weapons if the Western alliance attempted to cut off Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave that borders the Baltic Sea.
In a document sent to NATO and seen by Reuters , Moscow accused the alliance of a "dangerous and reckless course" that entailed "high risks of the outbreak of a direct armed conflict".
The document said this included the possibility "of Russian strikes against decision-making centres in the alliance's member states right from the outset of the conflict".
"Russia will be ready to use the entire arsenal of forces and capabilities at its disposal, including nuclear weapons, to defend its territory should NATO countries undertake any attempt aimed at isolating the Kaliningrad Region from the rest of the country," said the text, classed as a "non-paper" — diplomatic jargon for an informal document.
In addition to the private warning, Russian embassies in at least three European countries have issued statements in the past three days accusing NATO of escalating tensions through military exercises and planning scenarios involving Kaliningrad. Russia also rejected Western allegations that it poses a threat to Europe.
Read: EU foreign policy chief claims Russia planning 'more sabotage acts' against Europe
The statements said Russia had no intention of attacking NATO countries but warned that any aggression against Kaliningrad — a heavily militarised Russian territory that is sandwiched between Poland and Lithuania — would be met with the strongest possible response.
The warnings highlight a sharp rise in tension between Russia and European countries, which accuse Moscow of stepping up a "hybrid war" on the continent through acts including sabotage and arson.
Russia denies that and rejects repeated statements by Western politicians that it is gearing up for a possible military attack on a NATO country.
NATO denounces 'irresponsible nuclear rhetoric'
NATO spokesperson Allison Hart confirmed Russia had sent a non-paper to the alliance but did not disclose its contents.
"We have sent a response, noting that NATO is a defensive Alliance and none of our activities or exercises pose a risk to any part of Russia. We strongly denounce the threat of force, including any irresponsible nuclear rhetoric. We call on Russia to end its unprovoked war in Ukraine," she said.
Read more: Is NATO ready to fight? The Ukraine war is raising doubts among military analysts
A senior European defence official said: "(This is the) first time since (the) Cold War that Russia is threatening us like this. So this is serious."
A NATO diplomat said: "I would say that the Russian letter is only another Russian attempt to intimidate Europeans, and that the response by NATO is firm and responsible. (It) reaffirms that we will not be dissuaded from supporting Ukraine."
Kremlin says Kaliningrad nuclear warnings meant as reminder to European "hotheads"
The Kremlin said on Wednesday that Russia issued nuclear warnings to NATO over the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad to remind "hotheads" in Europe of the provisions of its existing policy.
Asked to comment, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said: "It is only natural that our diplomats are trying to remind hotheads in Europe of our policy documents on this matter."

title: American Idol  alum Caleb Flynn found guilty of murdering wife
description: Flynn was convicted on Tuesday of aggravated murder  felonious assault and tampering with evidence
content:
Flynn was convicted on Tuesday of aggravated murder, felonious assault and tampering with evidence
Former American Idol contestant Caleb Flynn has been found guilty of murdering his wife, Ashley Flynn, in Ohio.
Flynn, who appeared on American Idol in 2013 and made it to Hollywood Week, was convicted on Tuesday of aggravated murder, felonious assault and tampering with evidence. The jury also found that he used a firearm during the offences.
Prosecutors alleged that Flynn shot Ashley twice in the back of the head while she was asleep at their home in Tipp City, Ohio, on February 16. He then allegedly staged the scene to make it appear that an intruder had broken into the house and called 911, claiming someone else was responsible for his wife's death. The firearm used in the shooting has not been recovered.
The case also centred on Flynn's affair with Alleigha Botner. During the trial, Botner testified about messages Flynn had sent her in which he allegedly discussed wanting Ashley dead. Prosecutors also presented a message Flynn allegedly sent Botner the night before the killing that read, “I choose you. I’m free. Actions will come tomorrow.”
Flynn's defence acknowledged the affair but argued that his infidelity did not prove that he killed his wife. His lawyers maintained that Flynn was elsewhere in the house when Ashley was shot and argued that investigators had not produced direct evidence showing that he fired the weapon.
Flynn did not testify during the trial. Jurors deliberated for approximately two hours before returning guilty verdicts. He became emotional as the verdicts were read in court.
Flynn had previously spoken warmly about Ashley during his American Idol appearance, describing her as someone who encouraged him to pursue his musical ambitions. At the time, he said he loved his wife “more than anything”.
Ashley was a schoolteacher, volleyball coach, mother of two daughters and church volunteer. Her family said in a statement following the verdict that they were grateful to those who helped bring the case to this point.
Flynn is scheduled to be sentenced on October 5 and faces life in prison without the possibility of parole. His defence team has indicated that it plans to appeal the verdict.

Lil Wayne appears to confirm his engagement to 23-year-old Madi Cannon after previously denying reports
Lil Wayne appears to have confirmed his engagement to 23-year-old Madi Cannon days after celebrating his 44th birthday.
The rapper shared the announcement while celebrating fellow Hot Boy B.G.’s engagement to longtime girlfriend Brooke Jones during a Cash Money-No Limit Records arena tour stop in New Orleans.
In a FaceTime call with B.G., Wayne congratulated his fellow rapper before turning the camera towards Cannon.
“I’m marrying this one,” he told B.G. “This is Madison.”
Cannon, who was standing behind Wayne, responded, “Congratulations.” Wayne then put his arm around her and appeared to confirm their relationship status, saying, “This is my fiancée. And congratulations. Let us know what color we’re wearing. I’m the best man you hear me? Love you b-tch.”
B.G. later acknowledged Wayne’s message of support in an Instagram post, writing, “My lil Brodie gave me his blessings @liltunechi.”
The apparent engagement comes after Wayne previously denied that he was engaged to Cannon. During a July livestream, the rapper addressed reports about their relationship and said they had separated.

So, we decided to part. Sucks.”
Wayne was previously married to Antonia “Toya” Johnson. They welcomed their daughter, Reginae Carter, in 1998 and married in 2004 before divorcing in 2006.
The rapper is also the father of three other children: Dwyane, Kameron and Neal. He is set to receive a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in the near future.

title: Chris Brown offered  9 5m option instead of new trial over housekeeper   s injuries
description: Housekeeper Maria Avila must choose between accepting reduced damages or returning to court
content:
Housekeeper Maria Avila must choose between accepting reduced damages or returning to court
Chris Brown could face a new trial focused on damages after a Los Angeles County judge ruled that a $12.9m jury award to his former housekeeper was excessive.
Judge Huey P Cotton issued the ruling on September 29 following the June trial involving Maria Avila, who was attacked by Brown’s Caucasian shepherd while working at his Tarzana home in 2020. The judge gave Avila a choice between accepting a reduced damages award of $9.5m or proceeding with a new trial limited to the amount of compensation she should receive.
The ruling did not overturn the original finding that Brown was liable for the incident. Brown had acknowledged some responsibility while arguing that Avila had been warned not to go outside alone because of the dog.
Avila described serious injuries from the attack, including facial disfigurement, scarring, vision problems and nerve damage. Judge Cotton said she should receive compensation for emotional distress and persistent pain, but found there was insufficient evidence to support the extent of permanent nerve damage reflected in the jury’s award.
The judge also rejected Brown’s argument that the trial had been unfair because jurors heard a reference to his past assault of Rihanna. The separate $855,000 award granted to Avila’s sister, who was also working at Brown’s home during the incident, remains intact.
Avila’s lawyer had not publicly confirmed which option she would choose at the time of the ruling. Brown’s legal team has previously taken steps to challenge the verdict.
The case has also affected Brown’s touring income. A judge previously allowed Avila to pursue a portion of his earnings from his co headlining R&B tour with Usher towards the judgment.
The latest order leaves the damages dispute unresolved while the original liability finding remains in place.
