title: Albert makes history as US beat Chile
description: The 17 year old becomes the youngest US scorer in a 4 2 win over Chile
content:
The 17-year-old becomes the youngest US scorer in a 4-2 win over Chile
Mathis Albert became the youngest-ever US goal-scorer and fellow teen Julian Hall netted in back-to-back games as Mauricio Pochettino's side beat Chile 4-2 in a friendly international Tuesday at St Louis.
Hall created Sebastian Berhalter's opener with a clever dummy, then became the youngest US player to score in his first two appearances before defensive stalwart Chris Richards slammed in a header.
Albert, 17 years and four months old, slammed in a fourth in stoppage time, surpassing Christian Pulisic to become the team's youngest-ever goalscorer.
Diego Ulloa and Maximiliano Gutierrez had briefly put Chile ahead with goals either side of half-time.
A night that began with an emotional pre-game send-off ceremony to World Cup captain Tim Ream, who confirmed his international retirement, proved to be another full of promise for Pochettino's reinvigorated roster.
Fresh from thumping Peru 4-1 at the weekend, when 11 players had made their debuts, Pochettino sent out the youngest line-up yet of his two-year tenure, with an average age of 23 years and 25 days.
Gio Reyna was the only player retained from Saturday's win, with Antonee Robinson captaining for the first time. After scoring on debut, Hall squandered the first decent chance of the game. Played through one-on-one by Berhalter, the 18-year old rounded Chile's goalkeeper, but blasted his shot wastefully over.
Chile grew dangerous on the break. England-born Chile winger Ben Brereton Diaz lashed the crossbar with a fizzing effort, and Dario Osorio rattled the left post with a curling shot.
But the US struck on their own counter-attack. Sergino Dest rolled a sideways pass across penalty spot. Hall made a brilliant dummy, letting it through his feet to Berhalter, who slammed into the bottom-left corner.
In first-half stoppage time, Chile equalized. Another dangerous Osorio corner was parried twice by Brady, his second punch sending the ball back goalward. An almighty goalmouth scramble followed before Ulloa bundled it in.
The game had barely resumed when Chile struck again. Gutierrez won an aerial duel on the halfway line, sprinted toward goal, cut inside, and curled a beautiful finish into the bottom corner.
But barely two minutes later, Hall got his goal, leaping to steer a glancing header from Reyna's lifted cross into the net for 2-2.
Pochettino rang five changes soon after the hour mark, bringing on several more experienced players from the recent World Cup campaign.
Among them was Richards, who quickly slammed home a powerful header from Berhalter's pinpoint outswinging corner.
Deep in stoppage time, Albert's shot rocketed into the crossbar and down across the line -- a goal that was confirmed by the referee moments later, and surpassed Pulisic's 2016 goal against Bolivia in the team history books.
Tempers boiled over as both squads and coaching staff flooded onto the pitch for a bout of shoving and shouting before and the final whistle.

title: Spain brush aside Croatia in Nations League
description: Yamal scores twice as La Roja make it two wins from two with a 4 1 victory
content:
Yamal scores twice as La Roja make it two wins from two with a 4-1 victory
Lamine Yamal netted a brace as world champions Spain continued their winning start to the UEFA Nations League with a 4-1 success in Seville against Croatia on Tuesday, while Harry Kane scored as England won in the Czech Republic.
The match at the Estadio Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan was Spain's first home outing since lifting the World Cup in New York in July.
La Roja captain Rodri was handed the trophy by 2010 winner and Sevilla legend Jesus Navas, before presenting it to the ecstatic crowd.
"We were very excited to bring the trophy here," Yamal said. "To be able to win the game and bring it home is great."
Spain's supporters did not have long to wait before their side provided further excitement in Andalusia as Yamal fired them into the lead inside 75 seconds.
Dion Beljo nodded in Ivan Perisic's cross to briefly level the scores shortly before the half-hour, but Atletico defender Marc Pubill popped up at the other end three minutes later to head in a Yamal centre and restore the hosts' lead.
After also scoring early in Spain's 3-2 win at Wembley against England last week to kickstart their Nations League campaign, Yamal brought his tally in the 2026/27 edition of the tournament to three as he put Spain two clear of Croatia in the 63rd minute with a precise finish at Dominik Livakovic's near post.
"Lamine is keen to keep developing and show the world the sort of footballer he is," Luis de la Fuente said of the 19-year-old star.
"We've enjoyed his magic in the service of the team. In the future, he'll be much more recognised for what he does and for his contribution to the team's play," the coach added of Yamal, who is among the frontrunners for the Ballon d'Or.
Nico Williams then put gloss on the result for Spain with a crisp step-over and finish with one minute remaining on the clock. With two wins from two, Spain lead Group A3 on six points, while Croatia sit third on three points, behind second-placed England on goal difference.
In Prague, Thomas Tuchel's England got their first win of the group with a 2-0 victory over 10-man Czech Republic thanks to second-half goals from Anthony Gordon and Kane. The home team kept England at bay in the first half at the Fortuna Arena despite being a man down after Pavel Sulc was sent off for a high challenge on Elliot Anderson in the 23rd minute.
"We played very professional, second half we stepped up... Deserved victory," Tuchel told ITV. "Strange to get an early red card, not the best for the team and spectators. It's an awkward one but we kept going, got a win and that's what counts."
Barcelona winger Gordon broke the deadlock shortly after the break with a header from a cross served by Trent Alexander Arnold, who made his first England start in almost two years. It was Gordon's third goal in three games for England, including one against Argentina in the World Cup semi-final defeat and another against Spain.
Kane, who also scored against Spain, gave England breathing space in the 69th minute, smashing the ball past Czech 'keeper Matej Kovar after it fell to him inside the box. England will travel to Rijeka to take on Croatia on Saturday, while Spain welcome the Czechs to Oviedo.
"The next match is important for us against a direct opponent and we want to win," Tuchel said to the BBC. Elsewhere, Scotland paid for an early red card at Hampden Park against Switzerland as the visitors ran out 3-0 winners in Group B1.
Slovenia sit second in that pool after downing North Macedonia 2-0 in Ljubljana.

title: Asian Games crowds in spotlight
description: Japan   s 2 0 win over South Korea attracts 998 spectators at a 50 000 seat stadium
content:
Japan’s 2-0 win over South Korea attracts 998 spectators at a 50,000-seat stadium
Under 1,000 spectators watched Asian Games hosts Japan beat South Korea in the semi-finals of the women's football at a 50,000-capacity stadium, highlighting the struggle to generate interest in some events.
It came hours after organisers in Aichi-Nagoya said Tuesday that more than one million tickets had been sold for the continent's biggest sporting spectacular.
Japanese organisers have been on the defensive over attendances ever since the opening ceremony on September 19 took place in front of thousands of empty seats.
Officials said on that occasion that the threat of a typhoon had put people off, and heavy rain fell from Sunday until Tuesday this week.
While some competitions have played out to healthy crowds, others have struggled to attract fans.
Tuesday's first women's football semi-final at the stadium in Shizuoka, a venue for the 2002 FIFA World Cup, saw North Korea beat China 2-0 in front of an official attendance of 564.
With rain falling steadily, 998 people then saw the hosts defeat South Korea by the same scoreline. Japan and North Korea will meet for gold on Friday at the same stadium.
Speaking on Saturday, local Games organisers admitted they were "not satisfied" with ticket sales after the men's and women's 100m, the blue riband athletics events, took place in front of rows of empty seats.
"We will keep aiming for full stadiums, keep selling tickets and work to make sure people who have secured seats actually come," said Satoshi Murate, secretary-general of the Games organising committee in response to a question from AFP.
In a press release late Tuesday organisers said the overall ticket sales rate was expected to be more than 70 percent.
AFP has contacted the local organising committee for comment.

President Zardari, PM Shehbaz commend the security forces for the operation
Security forces killed three terrorists in an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Mir Ali, North Waziristan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), Radio Pakistan reported on Wednesday.
According to sources, a large quantity of arms and ammunition was also recovered from the terrorists. The sources also added that security forces precisely destroyed the hideouts of Fitna al-Khawarij in Mir Ali and surrounding areas.
Fitna al - Khawarij is the term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
They also foiled an attempt by the terrorists to intercept a truck carrying rations near Mir Ali Bazaar, the sources added.
3 terrorists have been killed by security forces in an intelligence based operation in #MirAli , North Waziristan @OfficialDGISPR #RadioPakistan #News https://t.co/R8N6cqJ5br pic.twitter.com/RnFgFDmIse
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif commended security forces for their successful operation in Mir Ali, North Waziristan.
In separate statements, they said the professionalism and courage of the security forces in the war against terrorism were a source of pride.
The president said operations against terrorism would continue to ensure peace in the country and protect the lives and property of the people. He also said the nefarious designs of terrorist elements operating with foreign support would be foiled at all costs.
The prime minister said operations by security forces would continue until terrorism is completely eradicated from the country. He also added that eliminating the menace of terrorism from Pakistan was the government’s top priority.
The entire nation stood shoulder to shoulder with the security forces, he added.
President @AAliZardari and PM @CMShehbaz have commended security forces for their successful operation in #MirAli , North Waziristan @PresOfPakistan @PakPMO @OfficialDGISPR #RadioPakistan #News https://t.co/6th3QIkCrg pic.twitter.com/4ltdPOBFHM
A day earlier, Security forces continued operations against terrorists in K-P and Balochistan, killing seven terrorists in separate IBOs, security sources said.
Five terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij were killed during an IBO in the Bara area of Khyber district in K-P. A large quantity of weapons and ammunition was recovered from the slain terrorists.
In Balochistan's Chagai district, security forces killed two terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan – a term used for Indian proxy terrorists from the banned Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and affiliates - during an operation in the Nok Kacha area, the sources said.
They added that the terrorists had set an empty water tanker on fire before attempting to flee the area. However, security forces responded promptly and killed both terrorists.
The slain terrorists were also involved in arson attacks at various locations along the N-40 highway.
Read: 49 terrorists killed in Balochistan, K-P IBOs
Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terrorist activity over the past three months, with a series of attacks across the country resulting in the martyrdom of security personnel and civilians.
Last week, 12 people were killed and 35 others injured when a blast struck a joint checkpoint near Aman Mela in the Darazinda area of Dera Ismail Khan, with the TTP claiming responsibility for the attack.
On September 19, 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred in a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, the Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
In a separate incident, a captain and a lieutenant were among six security personnel martyred in an exchange of fire in Hangu district, while eight terrorists were killed.
On September 1, six personnel, including two officers, and a customs department official were martyred as security forces thwarted an attempt to breach the Customs House in Balochistan.

In July, at least 30 people , including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. The attackers also abducted several civilians and police personnel after the assault.
In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation , which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

title: Oil gains after Trump denies he is willing to ease sanctions on Iran
description: Brent futures for November contract  which expires today  rise 71 cents  or 0 69   to  103 30 a barrel
content:
Brent futures for November contract, which expires today, rise 71 cents, or 0.69%, to $103.30 a barrel
Oil prices rose on Wednesday after US President Donald Trump denied he would be willing to ‌ease sanctions on Iran while Qatar pushed for peace talks, after falling in the previous session on a recovery in crude supply from the Middle East.
The Brent futures November contract, which is expiring on Wednesday, rose 71 cents, or 0.69%, to $103.30 a barrel. The ​more active December contract rose 35 cents to $96.51. US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 43 cents, or 0.48%, ​to $89.81.
Brent is headed for a monthly gain of around 14%, its biggest climb since July, ⁠while WTI is on track for a 4% rise after having breached $106 for the first time since May.
The spread between ​the two benchmarks this month also expanded to its widest in four months as traders watched potential plans by the US ​to restrict diesel exports, which could create an oversupply in the domestic market and lead US refiners to process less crude.
US President Donald Trump is considering allowing sales of red-dyed diesel, instead of an export ban, to offer some price relief to consumers as the November midterm elections ​loom.
Read: Govt decreases petrol by Rs1.49, diesel by Rs2.73 for Sept 30
"Continued uncertainty over sanctions relief and negotiations is keeping a geopolitical risk premium embedded in prices," said Sugandha Sachdeva, founder ​of SS WealthStreet, a New Delhi-based research firm.
"Improving supplies could cap further gains, but renewed disruption or an escalation in tensions could ‌trigger another ⁠rally," she added.
Qatar said on Tuesday it hopes that shuttle diplomacy between Iran and the US can lead to a breakthrough.
However, Trump denied an Axios report that cited US officials as saying he was willing to give Iran sanctions relief and release frozen Iranian funds in return for "concrete" steps by Tehran on its nuclear programme.
On Tuesday, Saudi Arabia resumed oil tanker loadings from ​its Red Sea port of ​Yanbu after restarting operations on ⁠the East-West Pipeline.
Crude oil exports from Middle East producers have rebounded in September to 16.328 million barrels per day, the highest since the US-Israeli war with Iran started in late February.
"With ​flows through the Saudi East-West pipeline restored, regional exports are now just 11% below pre-war ​levels — a remarkable ⁠recovery for a region still at war," J.P. Morgan research said in a note.
Read more: Oil prices rise for second session on continued Middle East supply concern
Over the past five days, the 10-day average for total oil exports has held at 20.5 million barrels per day, or 89% of 2025 levels, J.P. Morgan estimated.
In the ⁠US, crude ​oil and gasoline inventories rose, while distillate stocks fell last week, market sources ​said on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.
Official inventory data from the US Energy Information Administration is due at 10:30 am. EDT. ​Analysts polled by Reuters expect crude and product inventories to have fallen.

President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that the US had “virtually total control” of the Strait of Hormuz, while claiming that oil shipments through the strategically important waterway had surged to historic levels in recent days.
"We have virtually total control of the Hormuz Strait,” Trump said during a Hispanic heritage month celebration. “In fact, in the last three days, more oil has come out of the Hormuz Strait than at any time in the history of the Hormuz.”
Trump on Iran: We have almost total control of the Strait of Hormuz. pic.twitter.com/DytfH3ReUS
The president reiterated that Iran's military had been “totally wiped out,” and said the war would soon be won.
"We're going to have that war won very quickly, one way or the other," he said.
Pezeshkian links sustainable Gulf security to regional responsibility
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian underscored the importance of the Strait of Hormuz to regional and global security and economy, noting that a responsible approach based on preserving stability and the interests of regional countries, IRNA reported on Wednesday.
According to the Iranian news agency, Pezeshkian said that sustainable security in the Persian Gulf and its waterways depended on cooperation and responsibility among regional countries, in remarks on the occasion of World Maritime Day.
Further, the Iranian president "described the sea for Iran as more than an expanse of water, calling it a divine blessing and part of the country’s history, identity and life, as well as one of its most important resources for the present and future," IRNA said.
President @drpezeshkian : Sustainable Persian Gulf security depends on regional responsibility https://t.co/j7lm3eLSUR pic.twitter.com/iwnhz8ooyT
He added, according to the news agency, that security and development could not be separated and that "maritime security, ports and transport routes provide the conditions for trade and economic activity, while economic development strengthens the country’s national capabilities."
IRNA noted that, according to Pezeshkian, "Iran is seriously pursuing its responsibility to maintain security and stability in regional waterways and ensure the security of maritime shipping and trade, relying on the capabilities and experience of naval forces and all those involved in maritime affairs."
Separately, Iran's Deputy Chief of the Army for Coordination, Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari, noted that the sea was "a key pillar of national power, a driver of trade and the economy, and vital to energy security and the continuity of supply chains," IRNA reported.
The Iranian news agency noted that, according to Sayyari, the United States-Israeli war imposed over the past year demonstrated the importance of Iran’s maritime capacity.
Iran Army commander highlights maritime sector’s role in economic resilience https://t.co/2vLyEcT51p pic.twitter.com/QOlU7NvSEv
Iran says recognising its rights could pave way for ending conflict
The spokesperson of Iran's Defence Ministry General Talaei-Nik said Tehran seeks peace while defending its rights, security, and interests.
According to Press TV , the spokesperson added that recognising Iran’s legitimate rights would pave the way for ending the ongoing conflict.

Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi received US feedback via Qatari mediators in Doha on Tuesday on a seven-day plan aimed at building trust between Washington and Tehran, with sequencing the main sticking point, an official, who was not Iranian but was briefed on the talks, told Reuters .
Araghchi is expected to discuss the US response in Tehran on Wednesday, the official said.
Iran last week presented a seven-day proposal under which Araghchi said the Strait of Hormuz could be reopened and normal maritime passage restored if the necessary conditions were met. US President Donald Trump subsequently rejected the proposal, prompting further Qatari mediation.
The Qatari mediators conveyed the feedback they had received from Washington on Monday, meeting Araghchi and his team on their way back from the United States, the official said.
The document being circulated outlines a seven-day period of trust-building aimed at returning the two sides to an enhanced version of the memorandum of understanding agreed in June, including concrete steps on Iran's nuclear programme, the official said, without further elaboration.
The disagreement centres on the sequencing of the steps rather than the components of the plan, the official added.
Qatar has been shuttling messages between Washington and Tehran in an effort to end the conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The June memorandum of understanding led to a brief ceasefire and included provisions on the strait and Iran's nuclear programme.
On Wednesday, Al Jazeera reported that Tehran received a proposal from the US as diplomatic efforts to “break the deadlock” over the US-Israeli war on Iran continue, according to government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani.

China calls on US, Iran to return to Islamabad MoU, dialogue
China on Wednesday reminded the US and Iran to return to the framework of the Islamabad memorandum of understanding (MoU) and resume dialogue.
Reiterating support for ending disputes through political and diplomatic means, Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said Beijing hopes that Iran and the United States “will choose peace, recommit themselves to the Islamabad memorandum of understanding, and resume dialogue and negotiations as soon as possible.”
“Since day one of the conflict, China has been making active efforts to promote the end of the fighting and talks for peace,” he said, adding that Beijing will uphold a series of initiatives and propositions put forward by Chinese President Xi Jinping for peace and stability in the Middle East.
China will “continue working for restoring peace and tranquillity in the Middle East and Gulf region at an early date,” he added.
Iran has always emphasised ending the conflict and establishing peace
Ministry of Defence and Armed Forces Logistics spokesperson, Brigadier General Reza Talaei‑Nik, said on Wednesday that Iran has "always emphasised ending the conflict and establishing peace", while also considering the defence of the country's "rights, security, and interests as its responsibility," according to IRNA ​​​​​​.

"If the opposing side accepts Iran's conditions and legitimate rights, the path to ending the conflict will be available," he said.
Yemen army says it carried out 414 attacks on Houthi targets in 24 hours
Yemen’s army said late on Tuesday it carried out 414 attacks on Houthi targets across multiple fronts over the past 24 hours.
Military spokesman Majed al-Nuzaili said the operations targeted Houthi reinforcements and military capabilities, according to a statement carried by the official Saba news agency.
He said the attacks inflicted losses on Houthi fighters and military equipment, without providing figures.
There was no immediate comment from the Houthis on the army’s claims.
On Monday, the Defence Ministry said government forces had carried out 356 operations against Houthi targets across 10 fronts, killing or wounding 476 members of the group.
Yemen has been mired in conflict since the Houthis seized Sanaa and several provinces in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in 2015 in support of Yemen’s internationally recognised government.

Iran warns of fallout from Israel’s presence in region after Netanyahu’s UAE visit
Iran warned on Tuesday of the consequences of Israel’s presence in the region following Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s visit to the United Arab Emirates.
The Foreign Ministry condemned the visit, saying it came at a “sensitive time” amid Israeli attacks on Iran and genocide in Palestine and Lebanon.
It said Israel’s presence in the region was creating a “dangerous situation” and urged regional countries to remain alert to threats to collective peace and security.

title: Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson reveal  Verity  scenes they improvised
description: Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson reveal how they improvised scenes and recreated  Verity   s  memorable headboard bite
content:
Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson reveal how they improvised scenes and recreated 'Verity’s' memorable headboard bite
Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson have shared behind-the-scenes details from Verity , including an improvised scene, the film’s headboard bite and its ambiguous ending.
The film, adapted from Colleen Hoover’s 2018 novel, follows struggling writer Lowen Ashleigh (Johnson), who is hired by Jeremy Crawford (Josh Hartnett) to complete the final book in his wife Verity Crawford’s (Hathaway) bestselling series after an accident leaves Verity in a vegetative state.
Lowen later discovers a hidden manuscript that makes her question what happened to Verity and whether the author was responsible for a serious crime.
Director Michael Showalter revealed that Johnson and Hathaway improvised a scene that develops from an embrace between Lowen and Jeremy.
Showalter said the moment evolved into a more intimate sequence involving Verity, describing it as “grief that then turns erotic”.
Johnson later discussed filming the scene with Hathaway and Hartnett, saying, “It was very technical, but obviously incredibly enjoyable. I got to make out with the two of them for a few hours!”
She also told Extra TV, “I would kiss Annie for the rest of my life. Every day. If you need me, I'm there.”
Another detail carried over from Hoover’s novel is Verity biting a headboard. Hathaway said the sequence required extensive preparation, including stunt rehearsals and multiple versions of the headboard.
“We had like stunt rehearsals. We had to test so many things,” Hathaway said. “There are certain things that, like, Verity could be, maybe Verity could be a brunette, but we can't mess up the headboard bite.”
Hathaway also improvised a waltz into bed during another scene, which ultimately remained in the film.
Meanwhile, several sleepwalking scenes involving Lowen were cut. Johnson said, “It's just not necessarily that interesting to watch someone sleepwalk.”
Hartnett also highlighted the film’s ambiguous ending, saying it could encourage audiences to debate its meaning after watching the film.

Chad Lowe and Kim Painter’s daughter Fiona has died at 13, with her family remembering her as 'the light of our lives'
Chad Lowe and producer Kim Painter’s daughter, Fiona Hepler Lowe, has died at the age of 13, with her family remembering her as “a loving young girl who was smart, creative, and loved to dance”.
In a statement shared with PEOPLE on September 29, the family said they were “deeply heartbroken” by Fiona’s death and described her as being deeply loved by her parents and sisters.
“We are deeply heartbroken by the loss of our beloved Fiona,” the family said.
“She was adored by her sisters and she was deeply loved by her parents,” they added. “In fact, she was the light of our lives.”
The family asked for privacy while also including information about the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in their statement.
“Her passing is devastating for our entire family and we ask for prayers and privacy at this time. If you or someone you know is struggling with mental health, please reach out to the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline by calling or texting 988.”
Chad, 58, and Kim, 52, welcomed Fiona on November 16, 2012. She was the second of their three daughters. Their eldest daughter, Mabel Painter, is 17, while their youngest, Nixie Barbara, is 10.
In 2025, Chad shared a post marking Fiona becoming a teenager. Alongside a photograph of his daughter, he wrote, “Celebrating Fiona officially becoming a teen today!!” He added, “Keep dancing through life FiBear! Love you soooo much!! ❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️”
Fiona’s death follows a difficult period for the family after their Pacific Palisades home was destroyed in the 2025 fires.
In February 2025, Chad shared that the family had returned to see the remains of the home where his three daughters had grown up.
“Almost a month after we evacuated our girls finally got to go back to see what’s left of their home,” he wrote. “The way they’ve handled this whole devastating experience is nothing short of remarkable. title: Balochistan leads olive tree plantation drive
description: Balochistan leads olive tree plantation drive
content:
Punjab ranks second with 2,235,962 olive plants over 17,000 acres across 31 districts
Pakistan has planted 7.637 million olive trees across 60,456 acres in 131 districts as part of efforts to promote olive cultivation on a commercial scale.
According to documents available with Wealth Pakistan, olive plantations have spread across Balochistan, Punjab, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Sindh, Islamabad Capital Territory and Gilgit-Baltistan.
Balochistan leads the national plantation drive with 3,199,393 olive plants over 24,620 acres in 31 districts, giving it the largest plantation base among the regions covered by the data.
Punjab ranks second with 2,235,962 olive plants over 17,000 acres across 31 districts. Its plantation base has been developed through different initiatives, including PIDSA, PSDP, Olive Valley and private plantation.
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa has 1,656,499 olive plants over 14,690 acres across 32 districts. Its plantation base includes contributions from PIDSA, PSDP, the 5 Million Olive initiative and private plantation.
The data also show 205,929 olive plants over 1,542 acres in AJK, 129,384 plants over 939 acres in Sindh, 117,958 plants over 976 acres in ICT and 92,296 plants over 690 acres in Gilgit-Baltistan.
Of the total plantation recorded during 2012-26, the PSDP component accounted for the largest share, with 5,029,010 plants over 37,854 acres.
Other contributions included 580,158 plants under PIDSA, 1,320,116 under the Olive Valley initiative, 590,000 under the 5 Million Olive programme, 80,637 under Olives Expansion and 37,500 through private plantation.
The document identifies Pakistan's potential olive-growing area at approximately four million hectares and also points to the presence of millions of wild olive plants.
Alongside plantation expansion, 51 olive oil extraction units have been installed across the country, providing processing capacity for the growing sector.
Of these, 23 extraction units are located in Balochistan, 16 in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, nine in Punjab, two in Islamabad and one in Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
The document also lists supporting infrastructure for the olive sector, including three value-addition laboratories, six fruit-processing units, five weather stations, five nursery tunnels and four national reference laboratories at Islamabad, Chakwal, Tarnab and Quetta.
The figures show that Pakistan's olive development programme has expanded beyond plantation to include processing, laboratory, nursery and other supporting facilities as part of the broader effort to promote olive cultivation on a commercial scale.

title: PHC summons AGP over NFC Award
description: PHC summons AGP over NFC Award
content:
Petition challenges failure to issue new award
The Peshawar High Court on Tuesday summoned the Attorney General for Pakistan for the next hearing and sought a response from the National Finance Commission (NFC) on a petition challenging the failure to issue a new NFC Award.
The petition was filed by former Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa minister Taimur Saleem Jhagra. The court adjourned the hearing until Nov. 11, 2026.
The case was heard by a two-member bench comprising Justice Ijaz Anwar and Justice Kamran Hayat Miankhel. Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Advocate General Shah Faisal Utmankhel, the petitioner's counsel Ali Gohar Durrani and Assistant Attorney General Bilal Ahmed Durrani appeared before the court.
Durrani told the court that the merger of the Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA) with Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa had significantly increased the province's population, making a revision of the NFC Award necessary.
He said the 2017 and 2023 censuses had been completed and that the province's population had increased substantially. Under the Constitution, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa should therefore receive a share in a new NFC Award based on its population, he argued.
Durrani said poverty, unemployment and the number of out-of-school children had also increased following the merger of FATA, making a new NFC Award necessary to support development and meet the needs of the newly merged districts.
The court asked why Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa had not received a new share when the petitioner's party was in power at the federal level.
Durrani replied that successive federal governments had failed to give FATA its due share.
He further said no new NFC Award had been issued since 2010, despite a constitutional requirement for a new award every five years.
Advocate General Utmankhel told the court that no new NFC Award had been issued since the last award in 2010.
He said the federal government had submitted a report stating that Rs27 billion had been released for FATA.
The court asked whether FATA had its own budget before the merger, to which Durrani replied that it had.
Utmankhel said the merger was intended to ensure an equitable distribution of funds and development in the region.

CM inaugurates Pink Bus Service for women
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi expressed displeasure on Tuesday over what he described as a lack of interest among some PTI members in preparations for the party's planned long march on Islamabad, according to party sources.
Afridi made the remarks while chairing a meeting of PTI's parliamentary party at the Chief Minister's House in Peshawar, while some lawmakers did not attend the meeting in person and joined through Zoom.
Addressing participants, Afridi criticised what he viewed as insufficient commitment to preparations for the march. "We also have Mir Jafars and Mir Sadiqs within our ranks."
Meanwhile, the chief minister formally inaugurated new hybrid buses, the Pink Bus Service for women, solarisation of the Chamkani Depot, and the newly established Mall of Hayatabad Depot as part of measures to expand and improve Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) services in the province.
Addressing the inauguration ceremony held at the Mall of Hayatabad Depot, Chief Minister Muhammad Sohail Afridi said he had promised Pink Buses for women across the province and that the buses were now on the roads.
He announced that women travelling on Pink Buses would be charged a fare 25 percent lower than that applicable on other buses.
Appreciating the women drivers of the Pink Bus Service, the Chief Minister said they were role models for other women. He said those who described the people of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa as terrorists should see today that the province believed in empowering women and was taking practical measures in this regard.
Afridi said Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa was a Pakhtun society where respect for women and elders, compassion towards children and patriotism were deeply rooted in their blood and social fabric.
Condemning the inappropriate treatment of women by imposed governments, the Chief Minister said no one could even conceive of violating the sanctity of homes and women in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. "We do not violate the sanctity of the chadar and four walls like the mandate thieves. Rather, we provide protection to them," he said.
A detailed briefing was given at the ceremony on the new hybrid buses, Pink Bus Service, solarisation of the Chamkani Depot, establishment of the Mall of Hayatabad Depot and key features of the projects.
Participants were informed that the BRT service was providing daily transportation facilities to around 250,000 commuters, approximately 30 percent of whom were women.
The BRT system was also reducing carbon dioxide emissions by around 30,000 tonnes annually. It was further stated that the continued expansion of the BRT system was evidence of the success of the project. With the addition of 52 new buses, the total BRT fleet had increased to 296 buses.
The new buses would facilitate the opening of additional routes and help reduce passenger pressure on existing routes.
The Pink Bus Service had also been introduced to address the specific transportation needs of women passengers.
In the first phase, five Pink Buses would operate on selected routes during peak hours. The number of Pink Buses and their routes would be gradually expanded.
The procurement and construction process for 50 additional buses and a new depot, at a cost of Rs6.2 billion, was also under way. Additionally, another 50 buses had also been included in the current Annual Development Programme at a cost of Rs5 billion.

Chief minister announces that senior citizens, persons with disabilities will be allowed to travel free of charge
Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti and Federal Minister for Railways Hanif Abbasi on Tuesday inaugurated the Jinnah Peoples Metro Train Service in Quetta, with the provincial government announcing free travel for senior citizens and persons with disabilities.
The inauguration ceremony was attended by Parliamentary Secretary for Transport Mir Liaquat Ali Lehri, provincial ministers, members of the Balochistan Assembly, Pakistan Railways Chairman, Chief Secretary Balochistan Shakil Qadir Khan, senior government officials and representatives of political parties.
Speaking at the ceremony, Bugti said the service was the first metro train service of its kind in Balochistan and was intended to provide citizens with safe, comfortable and affordable transportation.

The chief minister announced that senior citizens and persons with disabilities would be allowed to travel free of charge, while fares for other passengers would remain subsidised and affordable.
Bugti said the provincial government planned to expand the service to two trains, allowing trains to operate from both directions in the future.
He said work had already begun on the development of the railway track towards the Bostan Industrial Estate. The government was also considering extending the service towards Pishin, Bostan and Mastung, he added.
According to the chief minister, the initial proposal was to import engines and coaches from China at an estimated cost of Rs50 billion to Rs60 billion, with the project expected to take three to four years to complete.
However, following a proposal by Federal Minister Hanif Abbasi, the government decided to have new engines and coaches manufactured through Pakistan Railways.
Bugti said the decision helped save time and resources while making use of the capacity of the national railway institution.

title: UN to hold fourth informal poll of secretary general candidates
description: UN to hold fourth informal poll of secretary general candidates
content:
The UN Security Council met Tuesday to gauge for a fourth time support for a packed field of contenders to lead the world organization, fresh from making their pitch to world leaders who will decide their fate.
After the first three rounds of informal straw polls, Rebeca Grynspan of Costa Rica held a narrow lead over the other six candidates vying to follow Secretary-General Antonio Guterres.
Several of the candidates are known to have met with world leaders during the UN's signature diplomatic event at New York headquarters last week.
Rumors have persisted that a compromise candidate could be parachuted into the process at the behest of the powerful five veto-wielding Security Council members -- Britain, China, France, Russia and the United States.
Guyanese ex-foreign minister Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett narrowly led the second round of the secret process to pick the next UN chief.
Other candidates include Argentina's Rafael Grossi, the current head of the UN nuclear watchdog, Macky Sall of Senegal, Ecuador's Ivonne A-Baki, Ecuador's Maria Fernanda Espinosa and Uganda's Olara Otunnu.
The outgoing secretary-general, Antonio Guterres of Portugal, ends his second five-year term on December 31, 2026.
Even if a candidate earns the required nine votes from the 15 available in the Security Council, they must also avoid a veto by the five major powers, which are deeply divided.
Once a candidate clears those bars, their name will go to the General Assembly of all UN members for confirmation.
The Security Council straw poll was devised in the early 1980s in an attempt to break a deadlock between two candidates shut down by vetoes.
The informal mechanism has persisted, in various forms, despite criticism from countries opposed to the opaque process.
Each of the 15 Security Council members must anonymously assign each candidate one of three labels: "encourage," "discourage," or "no opinion."
But after an unspecified number of votes, the ballots of the Council's five permanent members will have a different color, making it possible to identify potential vetoes, without knowing which country blackballed any given candidate.
It is tradition that the UN's top job should rotate between different regions.
Under that premise, the role should go to a candidate from Latin America this time. There are many candidates from the region, though Sall and Otunnu hail from Africa. AFP

title: Far right Romanian politician detained in fraud probe
description: Far right Romanian politician detained in fraud probe
content:
Romanian police on Tuesday arrested far-right politician Calin Georgescu, a former presidential candidate, after a court ordered his 30-day detention in a one-million-euro ($1.13 million) fraud investigation.
The 64-year-old -- who is already standing trial for fomenting violence following the 2024 presidential election -- is accused of setting up an organised criminal organisation to scam victims.
The Bucharest Court of Appeal ruled Georgescu could be held in pre-trial detention for a month, overturning a lower court decision to free him.
Local media showed video images of police escorting Georgescu from his residence, with handcuffs on his wrists.
Dozens of supporters gathered outside the Bucharest building to where police took him, local television reported.
Supporters had also greeted him at court for the appeal hearing earlier in the day.
Georgescu is accused of setting up a criminal organisation which defrauded a victim of more than 1.1 million euros after falsely promising them business loans from foreign financial institutions.
He has claimed innocence and alleged the investigations are "politically motivated".
Several other far-right politicians have voiced support for Georgescu, vowing to stand by him "through all the attacks he faces".
A previously little-known politician, Georgescu won most ballots in the first round of voting for the presidential election in November 2024. AFP

content:
The UK government said on Tuesday that national museums would remain free for foreign visitors, after previously floating the idea of charging tourists an entry fee to buoy the cash-strapped sector.
Access to permanent collections at national museums such as London's British Museum and National Gallery has been free for the millions of tourists who visit every year since 2001, unlike at many European and international counterparts.
The government announced in March it would explore the idea of charging foreign visitors to boost funding.
The government believes the "impacts and benefits of charging would not be felt equally across the sector and therefore will not introduce charges for overseas visitors", the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport said.

title: Little damage as Hurricane Polo sweeps over Mexico s Pacific coast
description: Little damage as Hurricane Polo sweeps over Mexico s Pacific coast
content:
Mexico's Pacific coast survived the onslaught of Hurricane Polo relatively unscathed, with AFP reporters reporting fallen trees and partially flooded streets but no serious injuries.
Polo made landfall on Monday in the south of Baja California peninsula as a Category 3 hurricane packing winds of up to 175 kilometers (110 miles) per hour, according to the US National Hurricane Center (NHC).
It is the latest in a busy storm season turbo-charged by the El Nino weather phenomenon which has caused unprecedented warming in the equatorial Pacific.
Its passage left the small town of Puerto San Carlos, a fishing and whale watching destination, without power.
Some streets were partially flooded but all the houses remained standing.
"The passage of the hurricane in Baja California Sur has left us with rain, but no loss of life," the state's governor Victor Castro said in a video call with President Claudia Sheinbaum's office.
"It barely brought any rain, it was mostly wind," Victor Garcia, a resident of Puerto San Carlos, told AFP as he gathered up branches that had fallen on his house.
Polo hit just south of Las Barrancas, a fishing village a two-hour drive north of Puerto San Carlos, the NHC said.
It weakened as it moved inland over Sonora state.
"We will assess the material losses today," Castro said.
Baja California Sur is one of the Mexican states most exposed to the annual hurricane season.
This year's season is shaping up as more severe than usual, as a Super El Nino wreaks devastation across Central America, in the form of historic droughts and flooding.
Meteorologists also issued Polo-related warnings of heavy rain and flooding in parts of 10 US states including Arizona, New Mexico, Texas and Colorado. Several of the states are experiencing drought.
In addition to Polo, meteorologists are monitoring Rachel, a tropical storm also brewing in the Pacific off Mexico that is expected to run parallel to the coast and is forecast to strengthen into a hurricane mid-week. AFP

title: Punjab puts drones on 30 day timeout
description: Written permission for agricultural and research purposes may be granted by the committees
content:
Written permission for agricultural and research purposes may be granted by the committees
The Punjab Home Department has imposed a 30-day ban on outdoor drone flights across the province under Section 144 due to security concerns.
According to a spokesperson, limited use of small drones will be allowed for coverage of events held inside halls and marquees, with organisers responsible for their safe operation. Intelligence and law enforcement agencies have been exempted from the ban.
The department has established district "Safe Drone Usage Committees" to regulate the use of the equipment.
Written permission for agricultural and research purposes may be granted by the committees.

EPA plans round-the-clock inspections of industrial units during pre-smog crackdown
As the smog season approaches in November, a verification survey has found that 1,085 of the 1,087 industrial boiler units operating within municipal limits of Faisalabad have been equipped with emission control systems (ECS), according to officials.
The survey was conducted to verify claims by the Environment Protection Department (EPD) regarding the installation and functioning of emission control systems in industrial units.
Sources in the divisional administration said the EPD had claimed that ECS equipment had been installed in all industrial units. However, the then commissioner expressed reservations about the data and constituted a committee to verify the claims.
A third-party assessment was also conducted to evaluate the systems installed at industrial units.
According to the survey, 1,087 boiler units were identified within municipal limits. Of these, two were gas-fired, while 1,085 had emission control and monitoring infrastructure installed.
The survey was conducted in coordination with the Industries and Local Government departments and was signed off by the respective district officials, sources said.
An additional commissioner said the emission control systems were installed during the tenure of former Deputy Director Environment Faisalabad Usman Azhar and had contributed to controlling smog levels last year.
He said continued effective functioning of the systems could help keep the situation under control, but stressed that regular maintenance was essential for their effectiveness.
Azhar said that when he assumed charge as Deputy Director Environment Faisalabad, only around 10 to 20 per cent of industrial units had ECS installed. He said achieving the reported compliance level was the result of field surveys and enforcement carried out under the directions of the divisional administration.
Environmental expert Abdul Rabb of the University of Agriculture Faisalabad said an emission control system comprised hardware, sensors and computer controls designed to capture, treat or reduce harmful pollutants before they were released into the atmosphere.
He said the EPA Faisalabad was conducting a pre-smog crackdown and proposed round-the-clock inspections of textile units, paper and board mills and other factories to check smoke emissions and ensure that ECS were functional.
He said surveillance teams had also expanded inspections to commercial kitchens and barbecue restaurants, where proper emission control systems were required, while joint vehicular emission testing was being conducted with City Traffic Police.
He said the administration's pre-smog action plan included a seven-point framework, including live CCTV monitoring of industrial emissions linked to the Punjab Clean Air Watch.
He stressed that regular monitoring and maintenance of emission control systems would be necessary to sustain compliance and help control air pollution during the upcoming smog season.

Two contrasting pictures of Sindh's dog-bite crisis emerged at a rabies awareness seminar at Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre on Tuesday, with a PPP lawmaker warning of an emergency while a provincial minister claimed the situation was improving.
Speaking at the seminar, PPP MNA Sharmila Faruqui said more than 200,000 dog-bite cases had been reported across Sindh this year, describing the figure as an alarming situation requiring immediate action. She said more than 40,000 cases had been reported in Karachi alone.

Sharmila said every dog-bite victim represented a person and a family, with children and daily-wage workers among those frequently affected. She stressed the need for immediate awareness and timely treatment following a bite.
"Rabies is preventable," she said, adding that post-exposure treatment must be administered before symptoms appear because once clinical symptoms develop, rabies is almost always fatal. Sharmila also urged parents to prevent children from approaching or provoking animals, warning that even a minor scratch should not be ignored.
Nasir Shah, meanwhile, said the Sindh government was taking measures to control the stray-dog population, including a sterilisation programme that was being further organised and strengthened.
He said a meeting involving senior officials, including the chief guest, secretary and health minister, had also been held to discuss the dog-bite problem.
The seminar was attended by JPMC Executive Director Dr Khalid Sher, Emergency Department head Dr Suleman and other medical experts.
The government has also recently initiated coordinated planning with local bodies for the sterilisation, vaccination and tagging of stray dogs, while directives have been issued to ensure the availability of anti-rabies vaccines at dog-bite treatment centres across Karachi.

title: Healthy  Pakistanis turn out to be walking heart risks
description: Healthy  Pakistanis turn out to be walking heart risks
content:
National study flags high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity among adults who considered themselves healthy
A nationwide health study has found a strikingly high burden of heart-disease risk among Pakistanis who considered themselves healthy, with nearly half showing high blood pressure, around one-third diabetes, 70 per cent elevated cholesterol and up to 80 per cent obesity - raising fresh concerns over cardiovascular disease striking at increasingly younger ages.
The preliminary findings of the Pak Sehat Study were presented at a seminar held at the University of Karachi's Faculty of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences in connection with World Heart Day. The event was organised in collaboration with the Pakistan Cardiac Society and PharmEvo.
Tabba Heart Director Dr Bashir Hanif said the study had screened around 2,000 people aged 30 to 65 from across Pakistan, with participants selected in proportion to the population of each province.
All participants considered themselves healthy, but their medical histories, physical examinations, blood tests and diagnostic assessments - including CT angiography and ultrasound - revealed multiple previously unidentified risk factors for cardiovascular disease.
The preliminary results showed that around 45 per cent of participants had high blood pressure, 35 per cent had diabetes and nearly 70 per cent had elevated cholesterol levels. Between 72 and 80 per cent were found to be obese.
Dr Hanif said obesity was closely linked with high blood pressure, diabetes and elevated cholesterol, all of which could subsequently increase the risk of heart attacks, strokes and other cardiovascular diseases. He said South Asians tended to develop heart disease at a younger age and that heart attacks were now being reported even among people under 30.
The study, he said, was examining premature narrowing of coronary arteries and associated risk factors among young and middle-aged Pakistanis to determine why cardiovascular disease was emerging at relatively young ages in the country.
Blood samples from all participants have been preserved for genetic analysis, while dietary, environmental and lifestyle factors will also be studied to identify possible causes of premature heart disease.
Participants will be followed for the next 10 years, with their medical histories, physical examinations and blood tests repeated at different stages. CT angiography will also be repeated after five and 10 years.
NICVD Director of Cardiac Imaging Prof Dr Saba Bhatti said a national registry was also screening apparently healthy pregnant women at antenatal clinics across the country through echocardiography.
She said two research reports based on the registry had found that about four out of every 100 women screened had previously undiagnosed heart or heart-valve disease.

Political pressure and mounting interference in administrative affairs have allegedly prompted Benazir Bhutto Shaheed University Lyari Vice Chancellor Prof Dr Hussain Mehdi to quit, with his resignation exposing a widening dispute over the reinstatement of dismissed employees and the running of the university.
Dr Mehdi has sent his resignation to Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah, the university's controlling authority, but said he would continue performing his duties until the resignation is formally accepted.
The resignation follows a growing dispute at the university that reportedly began during a Syndicate meeting over the case of a dismissed employee and has since escalated into protests, allegations and demands for the removal of the registrar.
According to university sources, the controversy erupted during a heated exchange between PPP leader and Sindh MPA Yousuf Baloch and Associate Professor Dr Ibrahim Noorani over the case of a dismissed employee. A group of university employees has since been protesting for three days against the registrar and demanding his removal, alleging that he is affiliated with a political party.
In a video statement, Noorani, the associate professor in the Department of Public Administration and a Syndicate member, accused Baloch of bringing Tanveer Soomro, whom he described as a "ghost employee" dismissed by the university, into the Syndicate meeting and attempting to secure the reinstatement of employees removed over alleged misconduct and corruption.
Following Noorani's roughly 12-minute video statement, the university administration issued him a show-cause notice over his allegations against the MPA. Dr Mehdi confirmed his resignation and said disciplinary action had been taken against more than 15 employees on various charges. He said some had been accused of consuming drugs on the university premises, while others were classified as ghost employees or were accused of being absent from duty. He added that the Chief Minister's House had directed the university to take action in some cases.
In his resignation, the vice chancellor said the university had made "significant progress" over the past 18 months in financial management, faculty development, academic activities, infrastructure and institutional development.
However, he said, a group of employees apparently motivated by political considerations had been creating unrest and exerting sustained pressure on the administration through protests and demands.
The situation, he said, had reached a point where pressure was being exerted for the registrar's resignation, describing it as a serious concern for the institution. Dr Mehdi maintained that administrative appointments and decisions should be made by competent legal authorities in accordance with applicable laws and rules. If such decisions were instead dictated by employee pressure, he warned, the authority of the university's statutory bodies would be weakened and an inappropriate precedent would be set for future administration.
He said the continuing pressure and disruption had significantly affected the functioning of the university administration and made it increasingly difficult for him to discharge his responsibilities effectively as vice chancellor.

title: Cops bide time as long march stalls
description: Cops bide time as long march stalls
content:
Personnel play marbles with slingshot stones and bathe in Soan river as they await protestors
Police personnel deployed on long march duty in Attock and nearby districts turn to playing marbles with slingshot stones and bathe in the River Soan to pass time as they await protestors.
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's much anticipated long march, which was first announced for September 27, but later postponed to October 3, has left police personnel hanging as they survive on limited resources.
Several cops reported a lack of inadequate facilities, including shortage of drinking water, provision of stale food and limited washrooms. Police officers said they had become forced to use open fields and the space beneath the Attock Bridge as washrooms, which has damaged the nearby radish and carrots crops and polluted the area. The Soan River has also been repurposed as a place to bathe and was up.
In informal chats with media representatives, police officers have said that they still have a couple of days during which they have to come up with ways to kill time. They shared that they had been using the stones provided with their slingshots to play marbles. Football, cricket and volleyball have also become favourite pastimes. They reported that during the ten days they had been assigned to duty, they were not allowed to go home and were keeping in contact with family through video calls.
Many of the police personnel have arrived from far-off districts such as Dera Ghazi Khan, Bahawalpur, Multan, Khanewal, Jhang, Faisalabad, Jahanian and Layyah.
Without proper facilities and lack of any medical services, many officers have reportedly fallen sick. Police officials have been suffering from ailments caused by the changing weather, such as colds, fevers and diarrhoea.
Meanwhile, in Attock and surrounding areas, where containers have not yet been removed, locals have devised shortcuts to reach their homes, offices or shops by choosing to crawl from underneath the containers to cross the road. Many of them are willing to crawl up to 10 to 12 feet flat on their stomach to get to the other side.
RR to open for traffic soon after long march
RAWALPINDI. The district administration has decided to open the Ring Road for traffic as soon as the tolling system becomes operational, without waiting for a major political or formal inauguration, after the opening ceremony was delayed nine times.
The Ring Road will be opened for general traffic in the first 10 days of October soon after the issue of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) long march is resolved.
The road will be opened within 24 hours of completion of the tolling system, while the inauguration ceremony will be held at any time later. Carpeting of the 38-kilometre Ring Road has been completed, while its estimated cost has crossed the alarming mark of Rs55 billion and continues to rise rapidly. According to the district administration, more than 98 per cent of the basic construction work (main carriageway) has been completed.
The main track of the project is fully ready and carpeted. However, work on the toll plaza infrastructure, lighting and finishing is nearing completion.
Due to continuous delays, an increase in material prices and escalation charges, the total cost of the project has now reached Rs55 billion. The project was initially estimated at around Rs22.8 billion, which later increased to Rs46.6 billion and has now reached Rs55 billion with some components of Phase-II and other expenses.

An Israeli airstrike killed the head of Hamas' armed wing in north Gaza on Tuesday, officials on both sides said, with the group describing him as a leader of the October 7, 2023, attack that precipitated thewar in the Palestinian enclave.

Israel, which says Hamas has been rearming and launching attacks in violation of an October ceasefire, has stepped up strikes on the group in recent weeks.
The Israeli military says it has killed at least 20 Hamas figures this month, including some it identified as senior commanders, people who took part in the October 7, 2023, attacks or those who held Israeli hostages.
Hamas has denied trying to carry out attacks or rebuild its arsenal and accuses Israel of undermining the Gaza peace deal.
Also on Tuesday, Palestinians in the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza buried the newly recovered remains of 41 people killed ina series of Israeli strikes on homes in the area in a single day three weeks into the war nearly three years ago.

title: Burnham sets out vision to tackle UK s woes
description: Burnham sets out vision to tackle UK s woes
content:
PM asks for patience in speech focused on long term policy
Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged on Tuesday to revive Britain by tackling its deepest problems such as social care, housing and utilities - issues, he conceded, would take time to fix in what he described as an "honest" speech to the nation.
In an emotional address to his Labour Party in which he imagined the country his father, who died this month, would have wanted to see, Burnham set out a long-term vision, promising greater public control of utilities, reform of the so-called pensions triple lock and the construction of more social housing.
Yet, the former Greater Manchester mayor, 56, said he could only start setting out the groundwork for
resolving those priorities, constrained in the near term by stretched public finances and the previous government's tax pledges.
Any results would only come after the next national election, due by mid-2029, and some in the next 10 years. For the time being, he asked the party at its annual conference in the northwestern English city of Liverpool to keep the faith.
Walking on the stage to "All Together Now" by Liverpool band The Farm, Burnham said he had ignored his first instinct to give "the usual tub-thumping conference speech", instead deciding to offer "a more serious prospectus for Britain than people have been offered in a generation".
It was a pitch decidedly aimed at the long term - aware of not only the lack of public money available to his new government but also the need to placate the bond markets, which have sent Britain's borrowing costs to high levels.
His team said Burnham's speech and plan came from the heart, the culmination of his upbringing, his years spent at the centre of British politics in Westminster

title: Yemen conflict reshapes Saudi UAE ties
description: Yemen conflict reshapes Saudi UAE ties
content:
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman met United Arab Emirates Vice President and Deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Riyadh on Tuesday, the Saudi Press Agency reported.
According to Arab News, the two dignitaries discussed "bilateral relations and developments in the region", adding that the they also reviewed relations between Saudi Arabia and the UAE.
Earlier in the day, Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman received Al Nahyan, Saudi state media reported, as Saudi Arabia faces increasing pressure from the Houthis, who have fired salvos of missiles and drones at the kingdom.
The UAE withdrew from Yemen earlier this year after Saudi Arabia accused it of backing a military operation by Yemeni separatists that it said posed a national security threat to the kingdom.
UAE state news agency WAM said Sheikh Mansour would travel to the kingdom in a "fraternal visit" upon the extended invitation, without providing further details.
Saudi Arabia has been trying to rally international support to confront the Houthis, but it was not immediately clear if that request extended to the UAE.
The Houthis, who have controlled Yemen's capital since 2014, seized the country's Red Sea coast this month in a lightning advance that routed forces of an internationally recognised Yemeni government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia and based in the south.
Saudi Arabia has launched hundreds of strikes in recent days on the fighters' positions in the highlands, according to the Houthis. But the air power advantage has so far done little to slow the advance of the fighters as Saudi-backed government forces have melted away.
Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia on Tuesday denied reports that representatives from the Kingdom attended a meeting between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al-Nahyan in Abu Dhabi at the weekend.
Israeli journalist Dror Balazada on Monday posted on social media that Saudi representatives joined an expanded meeting after Netanyahu met Sheikh Mohamed, with discussions reportedly focusing on security cooperation, Iran, the Houthis and regional defense systems.
A Saudi source told Arab News that there was no truth to the reports circulating about the presence of a Saudi representative at the meeting.

title: Developing nations call for bigger say in shaping AI future
description: Developing nations call for bigger say in shaping AI future
content:
Developing nations are demanding a greater role in shaping the rules governing artificial intelligence, warning that a technology poised to transform economies could instead deepen global inequalities if its development and regulation remain concentrated in wealthy countries.
The debate at last week's UN festival of diplomacy in New York highlighted mounting concern among leaders from Africa, Asia and Latin America around the increasingly powerful technology after several safety breaches, and as top researchers have warned it could destroy humanity.
"Developing countries cannot be reduced to the role of mere users of technologies designed elsewhere, nor should be the mere recipients of standards and norms that they did not adequately participate in shaping," said Foreign Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
"We must ensure that technological transformations of the 21st century do not reproduce the economic imbalances of previous decades," Wagner said.
She made the remarks at a Security Council session dedicated to AI that featured top executives of leading labs, including Sam Altman from OpenAI and Dario Amodei from Anthropic, who urged governments to work together to manage the technology.
Underscoring the surge in interest in the subject, Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman of Bangladesh, who chaired the UN debate this year, said that, "four years ago, AI was raised in this hall by only five delegations – this year, 128 delegations addressed it."

Like other websites using AI-powered chatbots, users type in queries and converse with the system online. "We're making it dramatically easier, faster, and more convenient to get what you need exactly when you need it," Trump said at a launch event for the platform in Washington, attended by top government officials.
"It's a restoration of America's founding promise and it's a reinvention of your government for the 21st century and beyond," he said.
The president also signed an executive order directing all government agencies to integrate their websites with America.gov.
The launch of the new US government platform comes the same day that Trump is to meet with an array of top tech executives to discuss the AI sector's rapid development.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday met senior executives of leading global financial institutions in London, inviting them to expand their operations and investment in Pakistan as the government seeks to build investor confidence and attract capital.
During meetings with executive of Barclays, JP Morgan, Citi, BlackRock and Rothschild & Co, the prime minister highlighted the government's macroeconomic stabilisation measures and ongoing reforms, while discussing opportunities in capital markets, banking and investment.
At a meeting with a JP Morgan delegation led by its EMEA Co-CEO Matthieu Wiltz, Shehbaz discussed cooperation in capital markets, trade finance and investment banking and invited the firm to expand its footprint in Pakistan. During his meeting with BlackRock executives, Shehbaz invited increased investment in Pakistani equities and fixed-income instruments under the firm's frontier markets strategy. Both sides stressed the importance of policy consistency in strengthening investor confidence.
The Prime Minister's Office said the executives of the financial institutions expressed confidence in Pakistan's economic reform momentum and reaffirmed their commitment to deepening engagement with the country's financial sector.
Earlier, Shehbaz became the first Pakistani prime minister to open the trading session at the London Stock Exchange, where he also formally inaugurated Pakistan's $3 billion dual-tranche sovereign Eurobond raised earlier this month.
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and Adviser to the Prime Minister on Privatisation Muhammad Ali accompanied the prime minister in the meetings.
Separately, Aurangzeb met Standard Chartered CEO Bill Winters and discussed Pakistan's structural reforms, macroeconomic developments and potential collaboration in tokenisation, international Sukuk and other financing opportunities.
The meeting also covered potential capital market transactions linked to the government's privatisation programme and efforts to broaden investor outreach across Europe, the Middle East and Asia.

title: Afridi threatens revolt to  force change
description: Afridi threatens revolt to  force change
content:
K-P CM rejects intervention warnings, vows Oct 4 march will remain peaceful
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi has warned that the PTI will "rebel" if necessary to force a change in the federal government policies that are "harming the province".
He has also warned the government against resorting to "any kind of adventurism" during the PTI's October 4 long march, claiming that such attempts will be counterproductive and harm the government.
The CM expressed these views on Tuesday during the inauguration of new hybrid buses in Peshawar and a press conference.
On Monday, some federal ministers publicly raised the possibility of federal intervention in K-P. Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam said consultations were under way on the "constitutional and legal option" of imposing Governors' Rule.
Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar also said if constitutional conditions for such a step or an emergency were met, it could be implemented.
K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi separately warned the provincial government against creating a situation that could force the Centre to impose Governors' Rule.
Afridi, however, rejected the warnings and said he would not retreat from his position because of threats of Governors' Rule or an emergency. He also said PTI supporters could take to the streets at short notice if an attempt was made to remove him.
Addressing the inauguration ceremony, he said decisions concerning the province could not be taken behind closed doors. He said those making such decisions would be brought to the table and policies would be changed, particularly those that he believed were contributing to bloodshed in K-P.
"If needed, we will rebel," Afridi said, adding that he would not accept policies that caused further suffering to the K-P people. He also reiterated his call for the October 4 march, saying it would take place "come what may" and describing it as potentially the biggest long march in Pakistan's history.
In a message to PTI workers posted on X, Afridi urged them to come out for the march at all costs.
Addressing a press conference at the CM House, Afridi said the federal government had failed to demonstrate performance in any area and that even those who had brought the present government to power had realised that an incompetent government had been imposed on the people.
Comparing the performance of the former PTI government at the Centre with that of the incumbent government, he said Pakistan's GDP growth rate had stood at 6.1% during Imran Khan's tenure but had fallen to 2.3% under the present government due to its incompetence.
Afridi claimed that such a large number of people would come out on October 4 that the authorities would not be able to handle the situation. He warned that any attempt at an "adventure" would draw a public response.
He said K-P was the only province where the government had come to power through the strength of the people and not on anyone's "crutches".
He criticised television commentators whom he described as "cartoons", saying that they were telling the people that they were "insects". He said there was intense anger among the people of K-P and that the "cartoon network" was creating hatred among the public.
"Two clowns and cartoons of the federal government have been placed on television with two objectives: to divert public attention from the October 4 Long March and to distract people from the government's corruption," he said.
Afridi alleged that the PML-N was planning to create unrest in the country.
He called upon the people to come unarmed on October 4 and exercise their right to peaceful protest.
The CM said anyone found carrying an object capable of causing harm would be apprehended and handed over to the police. Such a person, he said, would not be considered part of their movement and would instead be associated with the PML-N or those who had brought them to power.
"The October 4 long march will take place under all circumstances and will remain peaceful. The people will exercise their democratic right to peaceful protest and no provocation or act involving damage or harm will be permitted," he said.
Meanwhile, the chief minister also expressed anger over a letter reportedly written by PTI provincial information secretary Shaukat Yousafzai seeking postponement of the October 4 march.
According to sources, the letter caused displeasure among members of the parliamentary party. When Yousafzai attempted to explain his position, the meeting reportedly ended.
Afridi said the letter had not reached him. He added that had it reached him, he would have torn it up and thrown it into the wastepaper basket.

These included Rs1.3246 billion for Chashma Nuclear Power Plant (C2), Rs528.1 million for Tavanir Iran, Rs183.8 million for Punjab Thermal Power Private and Rs159 million for Thar Coal Block-I Power Generation Company.

title: US forces leave Iraq after two decades
description: US forces leave Iraq after two decades
content:
US forces are set to leave their remaining bases in Iraq by Wednesday (today), ending a more than two-decade military presence and raising concerns among Iraqi security officials that the withdrawal could expand Iran's influence while creating space for Islamic State to regroup.
The pullout, agreed in 2024 under then-President Joe Biden and carried out by the Trump administration, is being hailed as a victory by Iran and its allied armed groups, which have long opposed the US military presence in Iraq.
US forces invaded Iraq in 2003 to topple Saddam Hussein and withdrew in 2011, but returned in 2014 to support Iraqi forces in defeating Islamic State. About 4,500 US personnel died during the Iraq war and subsequent operations.
Iraq has maintained close political and military ties with both Washington and Tehran, while Iranian-backed groups have repeatedly attacked US bases. The United States killed Iranian commander Qasem Soleimani in a 2020 strike near Baghdad airport.
Iraqi security analysts and officials said the departure could allow Iran-backed militias to gain greater influence over security and political decision-making. Sunni tribal leaders also warned that Iraq could face a security vacuum, although the withdrawal remains broadly popular among Iraqis.
Security officials in Baghdad and the semi-autonomous Kurdistan region also warned that Islamic State could exploit reduced US intelligence, logistical support and drone capabilities. Kurdish commander Sirwan Barzani said sleeper-cell activity had increased after the planned withdrawal was announced.
Italian forces also completed their withdrawal from Iraq on Tuesday, ending a 12-year military presence. Italy had participated in the US-led Operation Inherent Resolve against Islamic State and NATO's advisory mission in Iraq. Two Italian Carabinieri officers will remain under the EU's EUAM Iraq mission.
Meanwhile, Iraqi Airways is preparing to resume flights to Iran next month after Baghdad secured a one-month exemption from US sanctions. The services will initially operate from the holy city of Najaf, subject to regulatory and technical requirements.
