title: Pakistan urges UNSC to press India over IWT
description: Pakistan urges UNSC to press India over IWT
content:
250 million lives, Indus Basin at stake, Dar tells UN chief
Pakistan has again approached the United Nations, urging the Security Council to call on India to fully implement the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) and comply with the awards of the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA).
Islamabad warned that any attempt to stop, divert, restrict, manipulate or otherwise interfere with the flow of waters legally belonging to Pakistan under the treaty could have far-reaching humanitarian, economic and security consequences.
The appeal was made in a second letter written by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar to UN Secretary-General António Guterres, highlighting the August 31 PCA ruling that found the IWT remains in force and binding on both countries.
The PCA has also issued an order on interim measures concerning construction works at the Ratle Hydro-Electric Plant pending the neutral expert's determination of whether the project's design complies with the treaty.
"The Security Council is urged to take cognizance of this fragile and deteriorating situation in the region and call upon India to fully implement the Treaty and the Awards of the Permanent Court of Arbitration; refrain from any action that may stop, divert, restrict, manipulate or otherwise interfere with the flow of waters lawfully belonging to Pakistan under the Treaty; abandon any project or measure inconsistent with the Treaty; resume without delay all Treaty-mandated cooperation, communication, notification, consultation and data sharing and comply, in good faith, with its obligations under international law, including international humanitarian and human rights law," the letter reads.
This is Dar's second letter to the UN on the issue, following his first communication sent on June 17. In the latest letter, he highlighted the August 31 ruling of the PCA, which held that neither party could justify the suspension or termination of the treaty and affirmed that the IWT remains fully in force and binding on both countries.
The letter also referred to the court's separate order on interim measures sought by Pakistan concerning construction work at the Ratle Hydro-Electric Plant (RHEP), pending the neutral expert's determination of whether the project's design complies with the treaty.
The court unanimously prohibited India from completing the dam wall and power intake structure beyond specified levels until 90 days after the neutral expert issues his final decision, which is expected in July 2027.
Pakistan told the UN that the issue was existential for the country, stressing that the Indus Basin sustains the lives and livelihoods of nearly 250 million people and is central to its agriculture, food security, economy and environmental sustainability.
"Any attempt to politicise water flows or subject them to unilateral control carries consequences far beyond a bilateral legal disagreement. It risks creating humanitarian, economic and security repercussions across an already fragile region."
The letter also warned that India's refusal to accept the binding character of the treaty and the decisions of its duly constituted dispute-settlement mechanisms would also establish a deeply troubling precedent.
The letter said that if a state were permitted to disregard solemn treaty obligations on political grounds, the credibility of transboundary water agreements elsewhere, as well as the wider international law-based order, would be seriously weakened.
The letter stated that Pakistan had exercised restraint and responsibility since India's so-called "abeyance" and remained committed to dialogue, lawful conduct and the peaceful resolution of disputes, including the core dispute over Jammu and Kashmir.
However, it said Pakistan could not accept the normalisation of conduct that endangered its water and food security, economic stability, and the survival and dignity of its people.
"In this connection, the National Security Committee of Pakistan has already underscored that any attempt to stop or divert the flow of water lawfully belonging to Pakistan under the Treaty would be regarded as an act of war."
Pakistan told the UN that India's ongoing destabilising steps, particularly its overall positioning regarding the status of the treaty, alongside continuing treaty violations and the construction of illegal projects, including diversion canals, merited immediate attention and effective action by the Security Council.
It said the council should act to fulfil its mandate and primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security and for preventing the deterioration of a grave situation.
Dar further stressed that the international community must make clear that treaties cannot be arbitrarily suspended, and that shared water resources cannot be weaponised.
He further said that the global community must also make it clear that conduct threatening the lives, livelihoods, and food security of millions of people is incompatible with the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations and international law, including international humanitarian and human rights law, and obligations to implement binding awards cannot be conveniently escaped.
At the end, Pakistan requested that the letter be circulated as an official document of the Security Council under the agenda item "India-Pakistan Question".

title: Three Pakistani sailors killed in Somali ship rescue operation
description: Three Pakistani sailors killed in Somali ship rescue operation
content:
Pirates open fire on 17 hostages while fleeing Four Pakistanis among those surviving ordeal
Somali pirates killed five kidnapped sailors, including three Pakistanis, and injured four others aboard a hijacked ship while fleeing the maritime police, two surviving Pakistani crewmembers told a human rights lawyer on Tuesday.
Somalia's Puntland Maritime Police Force said in a post on X that it had "carried out a maritime operation off the coast of Dharin-baar, Bandar Beyla District", rescuing the MT Honour 25 oil tanker, which was hijacked by pirates near Somali waters on April 21.
Pakistani sailors Hussain Yousuf and Imran Ali, who survived the incident, contacted the Ansar Burney Welfare Trust office in Karachi, using the ship captain's mobile phone, and provided details of the incident, according to the trust.
The pirates came under pressure during the operation and, while retreating from the vessel, opened indiscriminate fire on the kidnapped crew before fleeing the ship, the trust official quoted the two crewmembers as saying.
"The survivors said the governments of Somalia and the semi-autonomous Puntland region in northeastern Somalia launched a joint operation on Tuesday to free the Honour 25 from the pirates, triggering an exchange of fire," the official added.
Speaking to The Express Tribune, Ansar Burney Trust Director Advocate Quratul Ain said the location where the crew members were killed and injured was at a considerable distance from the shore. She said the incident occurred during the operation to free them.
While fleeing, the pirates also damaged the vessel's helm system, rendering it inoperable, Quratul Ain said. "A Somali naval vessel, which was used in the operation, is now towing the damaged ship towards the shore. The process is expected to take at least two days."
The deceased Pakistani sailors were identified as Second Officer Kashif Umar, Third Engineer Mahmood Ansari and Boiler Rafiullah. The two other deceased sailors were an Indian crew member, Tanveer, and the chief engineer from Myanmar. All the deceased Pakistani sailors hailed from Karachi.
The injured sailors were identified as Usman, Yasir, Ameen and Vicky, who is from Indonesia. Hussain Yousuf, Imran Ali and Yaseen remained safe, according to the trust. Quratul Ain said the government of Pakistan and the Ministry of Human Rights had been informed about the incident.
The Palau-flagged Honour 25 oil tanker, with a 17-member crew, including 10 Pakistanis, was seized in April around 30 nautical miles off Puntland's coast while sailing from Oman to Somalia. It was later held off Puntland, a semi-autonomous region in northeastern Somalia.
The families of the hostages spent months seeking the safe release of their loved ones, staging peaceful protests and repeatedly approaching government authorities. Pakistani authorities maintained that diplomatic efforts were under way to secure the hostages' release.
The pirates had initially demanded a $3 million ransom for the crew's release and later reduced the demand to $1 million. During their captivity, the crew members said they faced severe shortages of food, medicines and drinking water, surviving largely on boiled rice and, at one point, were forced to drink contaminated water.
Somali piracy has seen a resurgence, with at least 15 attacks since April, the highest number since 2013. The Puntland police have faced criticism for failing to act against a new pirate network that has been highly active in the region this year.
Puntland police said they had rescued another oil tanker, days after a rescue operation ended with pirates escaping in suspicious circumstances. They added that the Honour 25 had 18,500 barrels of oil on board when it was hijacked.
The police have been chasing three hijacked vessels off the Somali coast in recent days and rescued one of the other oil tankers, Sibu 1, on Friday. However, 28 of the 41 pirates arrested in the operation later escaped while being transferred to jail, with several Puntland security officials accusing local police of complicity.

title: Harassment at checkpoints draws flak
description: Harassment at checkpoints draws flak
content:
Senate panel urges security without compromising citizens' rights
A Senate panel on Tuesday raised serious concerns over the alleged harassment of citizens travelling between provinces at security check posts, calling for stricter oversight of police conduct and urging authorities to ensure that security measures did not come at the expense of citizens' rights and local traditions.
Members of the Senate Standing Committee on Inter-Provincial Coordination (IPC), particularly Senators Rubina Khalid and Aimal Wali Khan, highlighted difficulties faced by travellers over CNIC and domicile checks, while concerns were also raised over searches in tribal areas, including the handling of women's privacy and purdah.
The committee was told that heightened security checks were being carried out in response to continuing daily threat alerts. However, members stressed that police personnel must improve their behaviour and conduct at checkpoints.
The committee also discussed delays and restrictions affecting the movement of essential commodities, particularly wheat, amid concerns over road blockades and the placement of containers.
Officials from the police and food departments briefed the panel on security arrangements, border checkpoints and grain supplies, while the committee called for closer coordination among the federating units to facilitate the movement of people and goods.
The regional police officer (RPO) Rawalpindi reported that 31 cross-border check posts are currently operational in the province, with personnel deployed across 15 critical security locations/check posts.
Although only three incidents have been reported since January, he added that continuous daily threat alerts necessitate strict checking at all security posts.
While these heightened security measures cause temporary disruption and inconvenience to citizens, they remain essential for maintaining overall public safety and national security.
Senator Hidayatullah and other committee members noted that while the public understands the security compulsions, police personnel must improve their behaviour and conduct at checkpoints.
They acknowledged that police performance was under severe strain due to a heavy workload, fatigue and a critical shortage of resources.
Senator Wali highlighted regional disparities, pointing out that Punjab remains relatively secure in terms of law and order compared to other regions where conditions are worse.
Additionally, Senator Wali raised serious concerns regarding searches in tribal areas, emphasising that local cultural norms surrounding women's privacy, specifically in relation to purdah and burqa searches, must be handled with the utmost respect to prevent public distress.

title: PPP refers TTAP APC invitation to Bilawal

content:
Opp delegation seeks PPP participation in all-party confab
The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) on Tuesday said it would refer an invitation from the Tehreek-e-Tahaffuz-e-Ain Pakistan (TTAP) to attend an upcoming All Parties Conference (APC) to party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari after a meeting between the two sides at the party's Islamabad secretariat.
A TTAP delegation, comprising representatives of opposition parties, visited the PPP Central Secretariat and met PPP Parliamentarians Secretary General Syed Nayyar Hussain Bukhari, formally inviting the party to participate in the conference.
Welcoming the delegation, Bukhari said the invitation would be conveyed to Bilawal and that the TTAP would subsequently be informed of the PPP chairman's stance on participating in the conference.
The PPP leader said the party considered continued consultation and engagement among political parties on constitutional and democratic matters important.
The opposition delegation included Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan, Senator Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, Senator Zeeshan Khanzada and TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Yousafzai.
During the meeting, the delegation briefed the PPP leadership on the objectives and agenda of the proposed APC. The two sides also exchanged views on the prevailing political situation, supremacy of the Constitution, strengthening democratic institutions and maintaining contacts among political parties.
Speaking to the media after the meeting, Gohar anticipated a positive response from the PPP leadership.
"We are waiting for the response of PPP (regarding the invitation)," he said, adding that both parties agreed that the role of political parties was extremely important in maintaining democracy.
"Democracy is strengthened when the voice of the people is heard, and the mandate awarded by them is respected," he said.
Gohar called for building consensus among parties on various issues affecting the country's political environment, including an independent judiciary and election commission.
The meeting came as the opposition alliance sought to broaden political consultations ahead of its APC by reaching out to other parties and seeking their participation in the conference. The Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) has agreed to attend the opposition's moot.
The PTI, a key member of the TTAP, is also planning a long march on Oct 4, which was initially scheduled for Sept 27, as the party seeks to form a joint opposition alliance against the government.
Earlier in the day, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi expressed displeasure over what he described as a lack of interest among some PTI members in preparations for the party's planned long march to Islamabad, according to party sources.
Afridi made the remarks while chairing a meeting of PTI's parliamentary party at the Chief Minister's House in Peshawar, while some lawmakers did not attend the meeting in person and joined through Zoom.
Two days ago, the opposition alliance downplayed its differences with the PTI as insignificant and vowed to support the party.
"Our differences are over unilateral decisions by the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa chief minister regarding the movement. But we will not withdraw our support for the march and will participate whenever it is held," a source within the TTAP told The Express Tribune.

title: Heart disease rising among young people
description: Heart disease rising among young people
content:
NICVD expert warns smoking, obesity and inactivity are raising heart risks
Heart disease is increasingly affecting younger Pakistanis, with smoking, physical inactivity, obesity and other modifiable risk factors pushing cardiovascular problems into age groups once considered relatively low-risk, a senior cardiologist has warned.
Speaking during a World Heart Day webinar hosted by The Express Tribune, Dr Fawad Farooq, professor of Interventional Cardiology at the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (NICVD), said prevention must begin before symptoms appear because treatment alone cannot undo the damage caused by cardiovascular disease.
"Treatment alone is not enough," Farooq said, adding that diabetes, hypertension, obesity, inactivity and smoking can combine to significantly increase cardiovascular risk.
He said doctors in Pakistan are increasingly seeing serious cardiac problems among people in their 20s, 30s and 40s. Lifestyle patterns beginning in childhoodincluding reduced physical activity, poor diet, excessive screen time and early weight gainare contributing to this shift.
Farooq expressed particular concern over smoking among younger people, saying some begin as early as 12 to 14. Unlike several other risk factors that develop gradually, smoking can also contribute to sudden cardiac events by increasing the tendency of blood to clot, he said.
Explaining smoking-related harm, Farooq distinguished between tobacco, nicotine and combustion. When a cigarette burns, he said, it produces smoke containing thousands of harmful chemicals that enter the body through the lungs and can damage blood vessels and other organs.
Nicotine, meanwhile, is not risk-free and is addictive, which can lead to dependence. Farooq said this dependence is often what brings smokers back to cigarettes even after they understand the risks associated with combustible cigarettes and the harms caused by smoke.
Farooq said complete cessation remains the preferred option, but acknowledged that long-term smokers may struggle to quit because of this dependence.
For those unable to stop immediately, he said harm-reduction approaches may form part of a structured quitting strategy under medical guidance.
Smoke-free alternatives are also available that can reduce exposure to the harmful by-products of combustion, which he identified as a major source of smoking-related harm.
He referred to nicotine gums, patches, heated tobacco and other non-combustible methods as options intended to reduce exposure to smoke and combustion while dependence is gradually managed. He stressed that such approaches are not for non-smokers and should ultimately support quitting.
Farooq also urged people to monitor blood pressure, blood sugar and cholesterol, remain physically active, maintain a healthy weight and avoid tobacco. "Try to keep your heart healthy while you are in health before developing disease," he said.

Judge Sipra directed the jail superintendent to formulate rules governing the process for signing such documents.
"If this is happening with lawyers, one can only imagine what happens to ordinary litigants seeking to sign power of attorney documents," the judge remarked.
Advocate Zainab informed the court that the Islamabad High Court had already formulated SOPs in this regard. She urged jail authorities not to turn procedural requirements into a form of punishment.
Judge Sipra observed that, in the past, people had been required to obtain signatures on power of attorney documents either at the court lock-up or inside prison vans.
"The first step towards accessing justice begins with the signing of a power of attorney," the judge remarked.
Following the signing of the documents, the court consigned Mazari and Chattha's application to the record.
Furthermore, ATC Judge Sipra ordered the indictment of the two suspects, Imaan and Chattha, on October 6 in the case registered against them at the Kohsar Police Station, involving accusations of an altercation with police. During the case proceedings, Imaan and Chattha appeared before the court via video link, while their lawyers, Riasat Ali Azad and Zainab Janjua, represented them.
Separately, the ATC also issued notices on the bail applications filed by Imaan and Chattha and directed them to present arguments on October 5. ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain presided over the bail hearing.

title: Muslim world needs tech renaissance  Saqib
description: Muslim world needs tech renaissance  Saqib
content:
PVARA chief urges creation of new knowledge
The Muslim world's next technological renaissance should be built on producing knowledge, developing capabilities and solving human problems rather than simply adopting new technologies, Minister of State and Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA) Chairman Bilal Bin Saqib said on Tuesday.
He expressed these views in a keynote conversation on "The Future of Blockchain and Islamic Finance" at the Harvard Islamic Finance Conference.
Proposing "Golden Age 2.0", he stressed that the intellectual legacy of the Islamic Golden Age should inform contemporary efforts in research, enterprise and technological development.
"We honour the past through what we create, not only through what we celebrate," he said. "A new golden age is not a return to the past. It is a return to producing knowledge, building capability and solving human problems."
"The rulebook is a beginning. The public experience is the test," he said. "The question is not simply whether a technology works, but whether people can use it with clear rights, understandable risks and somewhere to turn when things go wrong."
For the Islamic finance audience, the discussion examined how regulatory oversight and Shariah expertise can inform product development while retaining their distinct responsibilities.
Addressing students and young professionals, he discussed practical avenues for collaboration across Muslim societies, including joint research, multidisciplinary teams and supervised testing of financial technologies. He framed shared endeavour around measurable contributions rather than technology adoption alone.
"A shared past gives us connection. Shared work gives us direction," he said. "Let unity be something a young researcher can experience, not only something a speaker can describe."

title: Pak vows response to Afghan attempts to disrupt peace
description: Pak vows response to Afghan attempts to disrupt peace
content:
Tarar says Taliban must move out of 'terrorist mindset'
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said on Tuesday that Pakistan's desire for peace should not be misconstrued as weakness, warning that Islamabad would respond to any attempt to disrupt peace in the country.
"Any attempt from Afghanistan to disrupt peace in Pakistan, these attempts to destabilise Pakistan have been responded to and shall be responded to," said Tarar while addressing a seminar titled "Afghan Predicament and the Trajectory to Peace" in Islamabad.
Tarar said Pakistan and Afghanistan were neighbours and would remain neighbours, with links and connections between the two countries.
"Pakistan believes in peace, Pakistan has always believed in peace," Tarar said, adding that Pakistan believed in peaceful coexistence.
He said Pakistan had made various attempts to ensure negotiations were held, as every problem could be resolved through negotiations and talks, saying various high-level delegations had travelled from Pakistan to Afghanistan to find a solution and ensure peaceful coexistence between the two countries.
"The Afghan interim government needs to move out of its militant mindset into a mindset of a statesman or a state," he said, adding that, currently, the problems that existed were due to this "militant mindset".
Tarar said Afghanistan had "great potential" for trade linkages and that peace could create an environment in which trade routes could be established from Central Asia through Afghanistan to Pakistan.
He said such routes could allow the landlocked Central Asian states to route their goods towards warm waters, adding that "the only problem that exists is violent extremism and militancy".
The minister said there were still safe havens of terrorists and members of internationally proscribed organisations in Afghanistan, adding that Pakistan had sought through talks to highlight the issue and stressed that peace had to be achieved through a viable and sustainable model and dialogue.
Tarar also referred to Afghanistan's youthful population and said a large number of women were excluded from the workforce because of a mindset that did not allow certain members of the population to contribute to economic progress. He said fundamental rights were denied to certain segments of Afghan society based on what he described as a "self-created ideology of Islam".
"This brand of Islam which is trying to be imposed is not the true ideology of Islam," Tarar said, adding that peaceful coexistence required accepting and acknowledging the principle of "live and let live".
Tarar said Pakistan had continued to engage in dialogue and negotiations and had tried to convey that "only peace can lead to prosperity".

title: Unabomber  tops Netflix s chart after just one day
description: Unabomber  tops Netflix s chart after just one day
content:
Crime thriller also reaches No. 1 in several individual markets
Netflix crime thriller Unabomber has reached No. 1 on the streaming service's worldwide movie chart just one day after its release.
The film, starring Russell Crowe and Jacob Tremblay, arrived on Netflix on September 25 and had already claimed the top position globally by the following day, according to FlixPatrol.
Unabomber has also reached No. 1 in several individual markets, including the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Canada, Germany and Italy. The film currently ranks ahead of Best of the Best, A Minecraft Movie, The Whisper Man and Black Adam on the worldwide chart. ScreenRant described the early performance as making Unabomber the "most-watched movie in the world", based on its position across Netflix's global rankings.
Directed by Janus Metz, the crime thriller follows Ted Kaczynski, beginning with his time as a young Harvard student before moving into the investigation that eventually led to his arrest.
Tremblay portrays the younger Kaczynski, while Crowe plays Harvard professor Henry Murray. The film explores the psychological experiments Kaczynski participated in during his time at Harvard before shifting to the investigation surrounding his crimes.
Shailene Woodley, Annabelle Wallis, Alexander Ludwig, Steven Ogg and Marc Menchaca also appear in the cast.
Unabomber's performance comes despite negative reception on Rotten Tomatoes from both critics and audiences. Its position on Netflix's worldwide chart indicates that the film has attracted viewers despite its reception.
On the review aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, 19% of 32 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 4.9/10. Metacritic, which uses a weighted average, assigned the film a score of 46 out of 100, based on 16 critics, indicating "mixed or average" reviews.

title: Zaain Ul Abideen releases new   Chue Chue  version
description: Zaain Ul Abideen releases new   Chue Chue  version
content:
Singer says song's release partly prompted by recent Indian offer
Pakistani singer and songwriter Zaain Ul Abideen has released a new version of his 2009 debut hit Chue Chue, saying he wanted to protect the song's identity and legacy after it was allegedly copied by other artists.
The singer told The Express Tribune that the release of Chue Chue 2.0 was prompted partly by a recent offer from India to remake and release the song with an Indian singer.
According to Zaain, he was contacted around 15 days ago by people in India who wanted to acquire the track and market a new version.
"They said they wanted to release this song," Zaain said.
He said he was told that the song would have to be performed by an Indian singer because a Pakistani vocalist could not be used in India.
Zaain said he turned down the offer despite being offered a substantial amount of money.
"I told them I can't do this because it is my identity and it is my legacy," he said.
The singer explained that allowing another artist to perform and promote the song could eventually distance it from the person who originally recorded it.
"If someone else had sung it, obviously they would have marketed it with his name. But then my name would have been lost somewhere," he said.
Chue Chue was released in 2009 and became Zain's breakthrough song. It was released under Sony Music Entertainment and earned him a nomination for Best Singer of the Year at the 2010 Lux Style Awards.
The song later became part of a separate controversy. In 2024, Zaain accused Pakistani artists Bayaan, Hasan Raheem and Rovali of copying the melody of Chue Chue in their track Maand. The artists' work and the dispute have since drawn attention to questions surrounding musical originality and attribution.
Zaain said the controversy was one of the reasons he felt the song should be reclaimed through a new release.
He said he did not want the melody to be copied again or for the song to become associated primarily with other performers.
"That's why I released Chue Chue 2.0 immediately," he said.
For Zaain, the new version is therefore not simply an attempt to revisit an old hit, but a way of reaffirming his connection with a song that has remained an important part of his musical career.
The singer said financial considerations were secondary to preserving that connection.
"Money is not important for me," he said, adding that the song represented his identity and musical legacy.
With Chue Chue 2.0, Zaain is seeking to retain ownership of its identity and association with its original performer.

content:
Artist's achievement marks another feather in her cap after being named Spotify's EQUAL Pakistan Ambassador for thir
Pakistani rapper, dancer and choreographer Daniya Kanwal was featured on a Times Square billboard in New York, marking another milestone in her growing music career.
Kanwal, who was named the EQUAL Pakistan Ambassador for the third quarter of 2026 by Spotify, has emerged as one of the newer voices in Pakistan's hip hop scene, combining rap with South Asian influences and lyrics centred on identity, womanhood and the experiences of young women.
Her featured track, Mic Check, is part of her debut seven-track album Kanwal, released earlier this year. According to Spotify data, her listeners and streams have increased by more than 3,470 per cent and 6,920 per cent respectively over the past year.
Before turning to music, Kanwal made her mark as a hip hop dancer and breaker under the name B-Girl Destiny. In 2022, she became Pakistan's first female national champion at the inaugural international breaking championship held in the country.
Earlier this year, she also featured on the HBL PSL 11 anthem Khelenge Beat Pe alongside Atif Aslam, the Sabri Sisters and Aima Baig. She was also among the song's lyricists. The track is currently her most-streamed song, followed by Bin Ranjha, Jihadi Aurat and Meri Jaan.
Kanwal's music has also found an audience outside Pakistan. The United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia and the United Arab Emirates are among the countries where her songs are being streamed, while around 70 per cent of her listeners are aged between 18 and 34.
Speaking about the recognition, Kanwal said she was drawn to EQUAL because it created space for women to discuss subjects that are often avoided.
"I love what EQUAL represents because it feels like a girls' night where every conversation is allowed, from freedom and our bodies to shame, desire, ambition and everything we're usually told not to talk about," she said.
She added that women should not have to choose between being "soft or powerful, vulnerable or angry, feminine or unapologetic".
Daniya Kanwal's artistry is rooted in cyphers, movement and lived experience. With a foundation in hip-hop dance, she has developed a style that is raw, fearless and unapologetically authentic.
Although she has been releasing her own music for just over a year, Daniya had already established herself as a performer through music videos and live stage performances. One of her early appearances was in Owais Wahab's 2020 music video 'Adhoora'. In 2025, she gained widespread recognition as a contestant on 'Tamasha Season 4', marking her first major breakthrough in the public eye. Later that year, she made a powerful impact on the music scene with her breakout single, 'Jihadi Aurat'.
Known for seamlessly blending rap with choreography and dynamic stage performance, Daniya views hip-hop as a way of life rooted in authenticity. Her writing is sharp, witty and socially observant, often challenging conventions and confronting uncomfortable realities. Bold, provocative and uncompromising, she brings that same energy to her music, performances and storytelling.

Her career began in hip hop dance before she moved further into music. Performing as B-Girl Destiny, she became Pakistan's first female national champion at the country's inaugural international breaking championship in 2022.
She also featured on the HBL PSL 11 anthem "Khelenge Beat Pe" alongside Atif Aslam, the Sabri Sisters and Aima Baig, and was among the song's lyricists. The track has become her most-streamed song, followed by "Bin Ranjha", "Jihadi Aurat" and "Meri Jaan".
A significant portion of Kanwal's Spotify audience is between the ages of 18 and 34, while her music has also attracted listeners outside Pakistan. The United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia and the United Arab Emirates are among the countries where she has recorded substantial streams.

housing loan limit

The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) has proposed raising the maximum limit for microfinance and housing loans to Rs5 million as part of proposed amendments aimed at expanding access to finance.
According to a notification released by the SECP, the proposed amendments have been issued for consultation with stakeholders. Under the proposals, the annual income threshold for borrowers seeking microfinance loans will be increased from Rs1.2 million to Rs1.5 million.
The commission has also proposed revisions in turnover thresholds for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). For small businesses, it called for raising the maximum annual turnover threshold to Rs400 million from Rs30 million, while the limit for medium-sized enterprises could be increased to Rs2 billion from Rs800 million.
The SECP said the proposed SME thresholds were aligned with recent changes introduced by the State Bank of Pakistan.
The commission has invited stakeholders and other interested parties to submit comments and suggestions for the proposed amendments.

title: Power sector may be allowed LNG import
description: Power sector may be allowed LNG import
content:
Govt mulls policy changes to allocate idle capacity of LNG terminals to power plants
As the country faces electricity outages due to shortage of gas, the government is looking towards the power sector for liquefied natural gas (LNG) import by utilising the idle capacity of LNG terminals.
The government is set to amend the policy that will allocate the unutilised capacity of LNG terminals to power plants for the import of gas for their own use.
So far, Pakistan LNG Limited (PLL) has maintained its monopoly over LNG terminals and the allocation of their unutilised capacity, though it has never been able to utilise the full capacity of these terminals.
For a long time, gas consumers have been paying millions of dollars in capacity charges to LNG terminals but PLL did not allow the private sector to utilise the idle capacity.
Now, the country is facing power outages due to the scarcity of gas following a marked slowdown in LNG supplies through the Strait of Horumuz, a vital shipping lane disrupted by the US-Iran war. PLL has arranged a few spot LNG cargoes at record high prices as Qatar could not ship the contracted consignments.
"Instead of a short-term rolling basis (three months), the relevant state entities (SSGC for the first terminal and PLL for the second terminal) be allowed to auction the operationally possible unutilised capacity for a specified period and quota, to be determined by the concerned regulator, considering the downstream demand and plan for LNG imports," the Petroleum Division said in its proposal submitted to the Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) for approval.
Consumers had been paying over $0.2 million per day in capacity charges to LNG terminals but there were no supplies from the state-owned entities. Since the inception, these terminals have been operating on the model of independent power plants (IPPs), whose capacity was under a contract with the government.
LNG terminals were available but government entities were unable to arrange gas imports. Even before the US-Iran war, Pakistan signed a deal with Qatar for diverting 24 LNG cargoes to other destinations during the ongoing year owing to low gas demand in the country. However, LNG demand emerged after the breakout of US-Iran war but cargo supplies were suspended by Qatar.
At present, Pakistan has two LNG terminals. The government has entered into a contract for the regasification capacity of 630 mmcfd with peak capacity at 690 mmcfd on a reasonable endeavour basis, as and when required, at terminal-2, which has daily delivery capacity of 630 mmcfd.

title: Gold drops despite global rebound
description: Gold drops despite global rebound
content:
Falls Rs800/tola as Fed rate hike bets persist; rupee inches up
Gold prices in Pakistan fell for a second consecutive session on Tuesday, with the local market reflecting the impact of a sharp decline in international bullion prices a day earlier.
The price of 24-karat gold fell by Rs800 per tola to Rs437,336, according to rates released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association. The price of 10-gram gold declined by Rs686 to Rs374,945.
On Monday, gold had suffered a much sharper decline of Rs12,800 per tola, closing at Rs438,136, as international bullion prices plunged amid rising US Treasury yields and expectations of tighter monetary policy by the Federal Reserve.
Tuesday's decline in Pakistan came despite a recovery in international gold prices. Spot gold rose around 1% to $4,155.73 per ounce, rebounding from a more than seven-week low of $4,110.55 recorded in the previous session. US gold futures gained 0.5% to $4,189.60.
However, gold remained below its 100-day moving average, while a stronger US dollar and elevated Treasury yields continued to weigh on the non-yielding asset. The 10-year US Treasury yield also remained at elevated levels, adding to pressure on bullion.
Adnan Agar, Director at Interactive Commodities, said the international gold market remained in a "danger zone" after its recent decline.
He said gold traded between the low of $4,117 and the high of $4,175 on Tuesday and was around $4,147 during the session. According to Agar, the market could test the $4,050-$4,000 range if selling pressure persists.
He added that a move above $4,280 could indicate that the market had established a low. Agar said upcoming US economic data would be crucial for determining the next direction of bullion prices.
Markets are particularly focused on US inflation data due on Wednesday and the monthly employment report scheduled for Friday. The data could influence expectations for the Federal Reserve's rate path.
According to market pricing cited by Reuters, investors were assigning around a 68% probability to a 25-basis-point Fed rate hike in October. Higher rates and Treasury yields generally increase the opportunity cost of holding gold, while a stronger dollar can make bullion more expensive for holders of other currencies.
Meanwhile, silver prices in Pakistan also declined on Tuesday, falling Rs20 per tola to Rs6,558. In the inter-bank market, the Pakistani rupee gained Rs0.03 against the US dollar, closing at 277.12 compared with 277.15 in the previous session.

title: Pakistan proposes next generation economic corridors

content:
Sees CAREC Corridors 5 and 6 as opportunity to connect Central Asia with Arabian Sea
Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal has called for transforming Carec transport routes into next-generation economic corridors by integrating infrastructure, logistics, digital connectivity, energy cooperation and climate resilience.
Participating in a session of the 25th Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (Carec) Ministerial Conference in Ulaanbaatar, the minister said Pakistan viewed Carec Corridors 5 and 6 as an opportunity to connect Central Asia with the Arabian Sea and generate economic activity along the routes.
"The question is no longer simply, 'Can a truck travel this route?' It is, 'Can a business use this route reliably, competitively and profitably?'" he said. Iqbal stressed the need to establish logistics and production hubs along strategic locations, saying cold storage, packaging, warehousing and light manufacturing could transform transit traffic into exports, jobs and value for communities along the corridors.
The minister also called for building a digital corridor across the Carec region, noting that Pakistan Single Window provided a foundation for phased digital integration with regional partners. "A consignment's documents should be checked before it reaches the border," he said.
The minister called for treating borders as a shared service, with compatible operating hours, advance electronic information, coordinated procedures and fewer repeated checks. He also emphasised the need to measure border delays, delivery times, local employment, SME participation and opportunities for women and youth.
"Regional cooperation succeeds when a trader can predict the journey, a farmer can reach a distant market without losing the harvest, and communities along the corridor share in its prosperity. That is how we move from connectivity to competitiveness," Iqbal said.
Earlier, addressing the opening session of the 25th Carec Ministerial Conference under the theme "25 Years of Partnership, Shaping the Future Together," the planning minister said Pakistan looked forward to assuming the Carec chairmanship in 2027 and hosting the 26th Ministerial Conference.

title: IMF pushes targeted subsidies
description: IMF pushes targeted subsidies
content:
Asks to channel fuel relief via BISP; raises circular debt, SOE reform issues
The mission chief of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Iva Petrova, on Tuesday urged Pakistan to give only targeted subsidies through the national social safety net programme to deal with the aftermath of the Middle East conflict.
Petrova also pointed out the continuous missing of quarterly and annual targets of spending on education and health, which in the last fiscal year remained Rs370 billion below the target of nearly Rs3.5 trillion. She sought clarity on how the government plans to address the issue of statistical discrepancy of Rs853 billion in the books of federal and provincial governments.
The issues being raised during a kick-off meeting often become the basis for discussions for the staff-level agreement in addition to progress on performance criteria and structural benchmarks agreed between both sides.
The remarks about fuel subsidy were made during a symbolic kick-off meeting between Pakistan and the IMF, which was held this time on the seventh day of talks. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, who has been abroad for many days, virtually attended the meeting.
The finance ministry did not release an official statement after the meeting, except for releasing a caption of pictures, stating that Muhammad Aurangzeb held a kick-off meeting with the IMF mission, led by Iva Petrova. It added that the IMF mission is in Islamabad for the fourth review of the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the third review of the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).
Government sources said the IMF mission took up the untargeted fuel compensation scheme, which the government has announced to partly offset the impact of unbearably high fuel prices, pushed up by both global prices and higher government taxes.
The government is currently charging a tax of Rs110 on per litre of petrol and Rs101 on diesel; therefore, there is no subsidy on any fuel.
A senior government official said the IMF did not oppose the scheme but said any such scheme should be implemented through an established mechanism, like the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP).
Both the IMF country head and the finance ministry spokesman did not respond to requests for comments till the filing of the story.
Sources said the finance minister responded to the observations made by the IMF mission chief, but no further details were available.
During last week's meeting with IMF MD Kristalina Georgieva, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly session, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif apprised her of the fuel compensation scheme.
After the meeting, the PM told The Express Tribune that he sensitised Georgieva to where the poor man would go due to high price pressure.
According to IT Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja, till last Friday, around 6 million citizens had been registered under the scheme and over 6.2 million fuel relief tokens were generated, of which 4.8 million had been successfully redeemed.
The government has removed the five-litre limit for motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqi following public feedback. Amid volatility in global oil markets resulting from tensions in the Middle East, the fuel relief scheme was aimed at providing direct and targeted relief to citizens most affected by rising fuel costs, according to the Pakistani authorities.
Sources said the IMF mission chief also raised the issue of slow progress on resolving the gas and power-sector circular debt problem.
Unlike the power sector where large subsidies are budgeted by the government to address tariff differential, the gas sector has inherently operated under a cross-subsidy mechanism to protect the vulnerable segment in the residential sector, which has led to inflated tariffs for other consumer categories in order to meet the revenue requirements of gas utilities.
The absence of budgeted subsidies has limited the ability of gas companies to lower tariffs for industry, commercial and residential consumers. The practice of revision of consumer gas prices in line with Ogra bi-annual determination of revenue requirements was consistent and strictly followed until financial year 2013; thereafter, this practice was neither followed nor was any provision of tariff differential subsidy against inadequate price revision ever made in the annual budget.
On a similar analogy, tariff differential in ring-fenced RLNG sale also arose starting FY 2018-19 when the government as a policy decided to divert RLNG to the residential sector for meeting winter gas demand without any firm mechanism for recovery of the cost of RLNG sold at indigenous gas tariff, an official of the Petroleum Division said.
As of March this year, the gas-sector circular debt had peaked at Rs3.6 trillion, including Rs1.8 trillion of principal outstanding amount. This principal amount was inclusive of Rs216 billion in tax refunds, which ideally should not be part of circular debt payments.
Sources said during the kick-off meeting, the IMF mission chief also raised concerns over slow progress on reforms in state-owned enterprises. She urged the government to fast-track these reforms, including amendments to the SOE laws.
The government's performance on structural reforms remains dismally slow and its focus has largely remained on delivering fiscal and monetary targets.
Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said last week that the IMF programme should be more than just fiscal numbers and it should focus on jobs and development.

title: PSX falls below 170k over regional conflict
description: PSX falls below 170k over regional conflict
content:
KSE-100 index erases gains, decreases 825 points amid IMF review
Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) came under renewed selling pressure on Tuesday, with the benchmark KSE-100 index shedding 825.22 points, or 0.48%, as concerns over prolonged Middle East tensions and elevated oil prices weighed on investor sentiment.
The index started off on a strong note, climbing 324.35 points, or 0.19%, to 170,749.97 by 9:38 am, but reversed course later and remained in the red by the close of trading. It touched the intra-day high of 170,944.35 and low of 169,538.23 before settling at 169,600.41.
Earlier, resilience was observed in auto assemblers, cement firms, commercial banks, fertiliser manufacturers, oil and gas exploration and oil marketing companies, but broad-based selling erased gains. Global developments remained a key drag as diplomatic efforts to resolve the US-Iran conflict continued without a breakthrough. Also, oil prices stood higher as geopolitical uncertainty clouded the outlook for Middle Eastern supplies.
The domestic economic backdrop remained in focus as well after Pakistan and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) formally kicked off talks for the fourth review of the $7 billion Extended Fund Facility and third review of the Resilience and Sustainability Facility. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb held the opening meeting with the visiting IMF mission in the backdrop of a challenging external environment.
JS Global analyst Mubashir Anis Naviwala observed that selling pressure persisted at the PSX, where the benchmark KSE-100 index shed 825 points. The market stayed under pressure throughout the session and late selling pushed it to the intra-day low of 169,538. Commercial banks, oil & gas, fertiliser and cement stocks were among the major laggards while chemical and tobacco stocks posted modest gains, he said.
According to Arif Habib Limited (AHL) Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib, the PSX experienced another mixed trading session as the KSE-100 index slid 825 points to settle at 169,600, breaching the key psychological level of 170k after a gap of seven trading sessions.
Market sentiment remained weak in the backdrop of rising international oil prices due to US-Iran tensions and supply disruption risks in the Strait of Hormuz, which directly impacted Pakistan through increased energy import costs and external economic pressure.
Moreover, finance ministry officials were engaged in key review discussions with the IMF to stabilise the economy. On the corporate front, Air Link Communication reported FY26 net profit of Rs6,226 million, up 31% YoY, propelled by strong gross margins and tax reversals including a Q4 profit jump of 36% YoY to Rs2,579 million. Despite skipping Q4 payout, the company paid total FY26 dividend of Rs2 per share.
UBL, Fauji Fertiliser, Pakistan Petroleum, HBL, Mari Energies, Engro Holdings, PSO, Systems Ltd, Pakistan Services and Bank Alfalah collectively erased 556 points from the index. Najib expects market sentiment to remain volatile, with selective buying if geopolitical tensions ease.
Cumulatively, trading volumes rose to 568 million shares compared with Monday's tally of 421 million. The value of traded shares stood at Rs20.8 billion.
Of the 496 companies traded in the ready market, 154 closed higher, 305 fell and 37 stood unchanged. Cnergyico was the volume leader with trading in 56.5 million shares, losing Rs0.23 to close at Rs13.09. title: Food safety concerns hamper exports
description: Food safety concerns hamper exports
content:
Experts to discuss food security, agri-investment amid climate change
The Agri-Connections Conference and Expo will highlight that food security is no longer a national and regional priority alone but it is the problem for every Pakistani household as farmers are dealing with climate perils at a frequency not seen before.
This was stated by Kazim Saeed, CEO Pakistan Agricultural Coalition, while talking to the media on Tuesday.
"The Agri-Connections Conference and Expo will be held at Lahore Expo Center from October 1-2 and its theme is 'food security and agri-investment in the era of climate change'," said Kazim.
He added that Pakistan's exports were a fraction of what they could be partly because of food safety concerns as "we will hear from the FAO at this conference while the IFC will brief on how the transition from a government-administered to a deregulated wheat sector needs the private sector to be engaged".
The CEO stated that the conference would put a spotlight on the livestock sector, which launched a few IPOs in recent years, and would present the ecosystem developing to support the rise in shrimp farming.
Kazim further said that the companies exporting olive oil and chilled meat with international partnerships would give presentations at the conference while the SECP would co-host an agri-investors' roundtable with the Pakistan Agricultural Coalition at the event.
"We work closely with farmers, policymakers, regulators and Pakistan's development partners. Our efforts stretch from the largest business groups and global reinsurers taking interest in Pakistan to the agri-start-ups that seek investor capital to serve farmers," said Kazim.
He pointed out that the federal government was developing an ecosystem for farmers' access to finance, which included credit for purchasing quality inputs, collateral-based lending to farmers, financing for agribusiness and crop insurance.
He said that the State Bank was working with the Zarkheze framework for farm credit and the SECP for crop insurance while the government of Punjab was massively expanding credit to small farmers, tweaking its wheat deregulation framework and making strides in farm mechanisation. "The government of Sindh is developing a legal framework for farmers to congregate for greater market power. These initiatives cannot succeed without the engagement of the many layers of Pakistan's private businesses."

title: IMF asks for SOE law changes before board meeting
description: IMF asks for SOE law changes before board meeting
content:
Voices concern over delay in amendments to half a dozen laws
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has expressed concern over continuous delay in amending half a dozen laws of state-owned enterprises (SOEs), particularly the lack of an effective governance model for the Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda), and has asked Pakistan to amend these laws before board meeting.
During ongoing talks on the fourth review, the IMF mission evaluated progress on amending the National Accountability Ordinance to make the appointment process for the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) chairman transparent and rule-based, Pakistani authorities negotiating with the IMF told The Express Tribune.
The IMF aired concern over the delay in amendments after Pakistan missed the fourth deadline to bring 9 to 10 laws of SOEs in conformity with the main SOE law. During each staff-level review, the government failed to meet the deadline and every time it sought a fresh date, the latest one was August 2026.
Government sources said the IMF had now asked the authorities to align the laws with the SOE Act before mid-November. Subject to the successful conclusion of talks, the IMF board could meet in November to approve the next loan tranche of $1 billion under the Extended Fund Facility. However, the government has ignored such deadlines in the past. The IMF has already disbursed $4.2 billion out of the $7 billion package due to progress on fiscal and monetary matters.
According to the last staff-level report, Pakistani authorities had sent amendments to six laws for parliament's approval in January 2026. The report added that the government now needed to make progress on the remaining three SOEs with dedicated laws.
Last week, Secretary Finance Imdad Ullah Bosal told the National Assembly Standing Committee on Finance that the laws of Port Qasim Authority, Gwadar Port Authority, Karachi Port Trust, State Life Insurance Corporation, National Telecommunication Corporation and Pakistan Railways would be amended. Special Secretary Finance Qumar Abbasi also said that out of nine, three laws had already been passed and the rest were at various stages of approval.
This week, the IMF reviewed the status of amendments in the National Bank of Pakistan law and the governance and financial structure of Wapda. During the third review, Pakistan had requested the IMF that Wadpa should be exempted from the list of entities whose laws were required to be amended due to its strategic and essential work nature.
Pakistani authorities had assured the lender that they would take appropriate measures to improve the governance and financial model of Wapda. But the government on Tuesday could not report progress and another meeting was expected to take place with the IMF.
Finance ministry spokesman did not respond to a question regarding discussion with the IMF about Wapda. But sources said Wapda was a sticking point and the government would have to address the concerns.
Pakistani authorities gave an update on amendments to the NAB law to ensure that the appointment process for the chairman was transparent and it was not just limited to bureaucrats, generals and judges.
According to the IMF condition, to enhance independence and transparency of NAB, Pakistan will submit amendments to the NAB Ordinance to parliament by January next year. The IMF is of the view that the transparency in appointment process is important to increase public credibility of the anti-corruption agency.
The IMF got an update on identifying 10 public-sector entities, which faced a high risk of corruption. It was told that NAB was finalising the methodology and picked 10 out of 30 high-risk entities.
Pakistan is also required to develop a methodology for corruption risk assessment to guide the development of an action plan by NAB to mitigate corruption risks in government agencies by the end of October. The methodological alignment as a preliminary step to the corruption risk assessment is critical to ensure its comprehensiveness and effective use of all relevant information sources.
The IMF expressed concern over delay in amendments to the Sovereign Wealth Act. The extended deadline was March 2026. It wanted to ensure that the SWF-owned SOEs remained under the same high-quality governance structures and accountability standards as all other SOEs, including by amending Section 50 of the SWF Act to explicitly establish that the SWF-owned SOEs were subject to the SOE Act and SOE Policy and any necessary additional amendments to regulate and operationalise the SWF's SOE ownership functions with SWF being owner with appropriate oversight systems.
The government has already proposed these amendments and the matter is now with the Senate Standing Committee on Finance. The current law empowers the SWF to retain 50% of dividends of the companies but it has now been proposed that the income will first go to the government and it will then decide about any further distribution.

title: Faster phones  worse video on 4G
description: Faster phones  worse video on 4G
content:
Data speed hits 18.9 Mbps, premium phones reach 31.3 Mbps
Pakistani smartphone users are facing a growing paradox: faster network speeds, but worse video playback. Despite minor improvements in raw download performance across the country, video streaming quality has taken a hit nationwide, revealing a widening gap between connection speed and real-world usability.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority's Opensignal benchmarking report puts national 4G download speed at 18.9 Mbps, up from 18.6 Mbps in the first quarter. High-end phones averaged 31.3 Mbps.
Upload speed slipped from 5.81 Mbps to 5.32 Mbps. The video score, which measures how a stream actually looks and whether it stalls, fell from 44.97 to 37.53 out of 100.
In other words, the typical 4G connection got a fraction faster and a lot worse to watch. Games experience moved the other way, from 40.93 to 43.85. Users spent 93.67% of connected time on 4G, almost unchanged from 94.21% in the previous quarter.
The figures come from crowdsourced quality-of-experience data collected over 90 days in the second quarter of 2026. Opensignal scores everyday use, indoor and outdoor, peak and off-peak, rather than a controlled drive test. The report covers national averages and 20 cities. It is not a league table of licence compliance.
No operator escaped the video drop. Jazz's national video score went from 47.00 to 41.51. Zong's went from 47.06 to 41.66. Ufone fell from 42.33 to 36.64. Telenor dropped from 34.84 to 30.3.
Download speeds barely moved for the two leaders. Jazz was at 17.62 Mbps in the first quarter and 17.61 Mbps in the second. Zong was at 18.62 Mbps, then 18.55 Mbps. Telenor improved from 6.66 Mbps to 7.5 Mbps and Ufone from 12.36 Mbps to 12.82 Mbps, both from a lower base.
A file can finish downloading while a live stream still buffers. Video is how news, classrooms, shops and ads reach a phone. A seven-point fall with flat speeds points to congestion, uneven capacity at busy hours, or how traffic is handled, not a blank space on the coverage map.
The device in the pocket still matters. National 4G download on all devices was 18.9 Mbps. High-end phones averaged 31.3 Mbps, up from 30.2 Mbps in the first quarter. That gap of about 12 Mbps is built into the same networks.
On national 4G, Zong led download at 18.55 Mbps, upload at 7.81 Mbps and time-on-network at 96.59%. Its video score of 41.66 was a shade ahead of Jazz. Games were 47.28, second to Ufone.
Jazz was second on download at 17.61 Mbps and upload at 6.26 Mbps. Time-on-network was 93.33%. Games were its weakest national metric at 40.15, the lowest of the four.
Ufone did not win on speed. It won on games, at 50.08 nationally. Download was 12.82 Mbps, upload 4.42 Mbps, video 36.64, time-on-network 92.16%, the lowest availability of the four.
Telenor, although merged with Ufone but still mentioned separately by the report, finished last on download, upload, video and games. Download of 7.5 Mbps was less than half of Zong's. Upload was 2.82 Mbps. Video was 30.3. Games were 37.88. Time-on-network, at 92.58%, was close to the pack. The problem was quality when connected, not only whether a signal was there.
City rankings do not follow national table
Jazz took download in Islamabad at 20.86 Mbps, with the strongest large-city video score in the report at 50.22. It also led Rawalpindi, Peshawar, Faisalabad, Sukkur, Hyderabad and Swabi. Quetta was a standout: Jazz download of 22.41 Mbps is one of the highest city prints in the file.
Zong led Lahore at 21.26 Mbps, with video of 48.89, games of 53.56 and time-on-network of 98.18%. It also led Multan at 21.6 Mbps, Karachi at 18.27 Mbps, Gujranwala, Sialkot, Chakwal, Khairpur and Gwadar. In the three northern cities where SCO is also measured, Mirpur, Skardu and Muzaffarabad, Zong led download in each.
Karachi splits the spoils. Zong was fastest. Jazz had the best video, at 47.18. Ufone had the best games, at 56.03. Telenor's 12.19 Mbps was its least-bad large-city download and still last of the four.
Ufone's games lead holds in most printed cities, including Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Peshawar, Quetta and Hyderabad. Its coverage is thinner in places. Time-on-network was 87.97% in Hyderabad, 85.4% in Khairpur and 48.67% in Skardu.
Telenor's weakest city print is Gwadar: 3.87 Mbps download, 1.27 Mbps upload, video of 13.75 and time-on-network of 59.18%. Swabi, Abbottabad, Peshawar and Islamabad were also in the mid-single-digit download range.

title: Supreme Court lets Trump resume deporting migrants to countries not their own
description: Rights groups say 25 000 migrants are sent to 29    third countries    where they have no ties
content:
Rights groups say 25,000 migrants are sent to 29 ‘third countries’ where they have no ties
The US Supreme Court on Tuesday let President Donald Trump 's administration resume deporting ​migrants to countries other than their own without offering them the chance to show the harms they may face, bolstering a tool his administration has used for rapid ‌expulsions as part of his immigration crackdown.
The court granted the Justice Department's emergency request to put on hold Boston-based US District Judge Brian Murphy's ruling that the Department of Homeland Security's policy to remove migrants to so-called third countries is unlawful. The court also agreed to hear arguments in the dispute in December, with a formal ruling on the policy to follow.
The court has a 6-3 conservative majority. Its three liberal justices dissented from the decision to let the ​deportations immediately resume pending the outcome of the litigation.
Read : Temporary US migrants told to leave or stay legally
Murphy's ruling came in a class-action lawsuit filed by immigrant rights groups on behalf of migrants seeking to prevent the US ​government from sending them to third countries without notice and a chance to assert the harms they could face.
More than 25,000 migrants have been deported ⁠to 29 countries under the policy implemented last year, according to a tally by human rights groups, with the vast majority going to Mexico.
The policy is one of several measures the administration ​has taken in its pursuit of Trump's goal of mass deportation. The Republican president has enforced a sweeping crackdown on immigration — among his top priorities — since returning to office last year.
The administration has carried ​out third-country deportations to politically unstable South Sudan, which the US State Department urges Americans to avoid due to the risks of crime, kidnapping and armed conflict, as well as Uganda , Equatorial Guinea , Liberia , the Central African Republic , and other nations.
Department of Homeland Security General Counsel James Percival welcomed the court's decision.
"A bad day for criminal illegals and open-borders activists alike," Percival wrote on social media.
Also Read : US judge blocks Trump administration from stripping immigrants of work permits
Trina Realmuto, a lawyer for the plaintiffs at the National Immigration Litigation Alliance, said the court has "allowed ​the administration to resume sending people to third countries where they face persecution or torture. That is a devastating result for people who may be put on a plane before they ever have ​notice or an opportunity to raise a fear claim."
In February, Murphy ruled that the policy violates immigration law procedures and due process protections under the US Constitution's Fifth Amendment. Due process generally requires the government to provide notice ‌and an ⁠opportunity for a hearing before taking certain adverse actions.
The Supreme Court, which has allowed several of Trump's hardline immigration policies, previously sided with the administration in the legal challenge, suspending a preliminary order that Murphy issued earlier in the case halting the removals. In another win for the administration, the Supreme Court subsequently lifted limits the judge had imposed to protect a group of men from being sent to South Sudan .
The case began in 2025 after the Department of Homeland Security moved to step up deportations of migrants who cannot be returned to any country listed on their deportation orders.
The policy provided that migrants ​could be swiftly removed without notice to third ​countries that have provided credible diplomatic assurance ⁠that they will not persecute or torture the individuals. For countries that have not provided such assurance, deportees would be notified of their destination, and US authorities would assess the likelihood of persecution or torture only if the individual raises such fear on their own.
In its emergency filing to the Supreme Court, ​the Justice Department said third-country deportations are "an essential tool to remove certain aliens, including some of the worst criminal aliens."
But both Murphy and critics ​of the administration said ⁠the policy is also targeting migrants who had been granted legal protection from being sent back to their home countries.
The policy has resulted in deportees being unlawfully transferred by third countries back to their home countries from which the US had already granted them protection, while others have been beaten, sexually assaulted, detained, or have disappeared, the plaintiffs said in a court filing.
The administration is ignoring "the significant harm resulting from deporting thousands of ⁠longtime US ​residents, many with no criminal history, to third countries without regard to the persecution or torture they face there," the plaintiffs ​said.
The Boston-based 1st US Circuit Court of Appeals upheld most of the judge's ruling on September 18.
The case has been hotly contested since it began, and included findings by Murphy that the administration "repeatedly violated, or attempted to violate" his orders. Murphy ​in 2025 found that the administration had violated another order he issued requiring additional steps before attempting to send a group of migrants to South Sudan.

title: Will Reeve shares fertility journey with wife Amanda after cancer diagnosis
description: Will Reeve reveals he and wife Amanda banked sperm after his testicular cancer diagnosis before starting IVF
content:
Will Reeve reveals he and wife Amanda banked sperm after his testicular cancer diagnosis before starting IVF
Will Reeve has opened up about his testicular cancer diagnosis, revealing that he and his wife, Amanda Dubin Reeve, went to a sperm bank shortly after learning he would need surgery.
The ABC News correspondent, 34, discussed his cancer journey during a September 29 appearance on Good Morning America . In an exclusive interview with PEOPLE , Reeve revealed that he and Amanda wanted to preserve the possibility of having children together.
“Out of an abundance of caution, we went right to the sperm bank, like, the day after [the diagnosis],” Reeve said.
Reeve was diagnosed with testicular cancer in April after Amanda encouraged him to seek medical attention for a painful lump he had initially dismissed. An ultrasound led to the diagnosis, and doctors advised him to undergo an orchiectomy, a procedure to remove the affected testicle.
Before the surgery, Reeve was advised to bank sperm as a precaution. He said he and Amanda “do want to start a family” and wanted to preserve their options despite an orchiectomy not necessarily preventing natural conception.
Following the surgery, tests showed that 95% of the cancer was embryonal carcinoma, an aggressive form of the disease. Reeve subsequently underwent a six-hour procedure to remove dozens of abdominal lymph nodes, three of which tested positive for testicular cancer. He also completed two rounds of chemotherapy.
Reeve said he was declared cancer-free on September 8. He and Amanda are now proceeding with in vitro fertilisation, which he described as medically necessary.
“The great joy is that we are going to be able to have children, our own children,” Reeve said.

Curry Barker’s horror-comedy 'Anything But Ghost' has set a May 7, 2027 release date from Focus Features
Curry Barker’s upcoming horror-comedy Anything But Ghosts has secured a May 7, 2027 release date from Focus Features and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster.
Focus Features holds worldwide rights to the film, while Universal Pictures International will oversee its international distribution. Barker directs Anything But Ghosts and co-wrote the screenplay with Cooper Tomlinson, his collaborator from the 2026 horror film Obsession .

Anything But Ghosts is produced by Roy Lee, Steven Schneider, Jason Blum, Adam Hendricks and Greg Gilreath. Daniel Bekerman, Barker, Tomlinson and Ben Ross are among the executive producers.
The project follows Barker’s feature directorial debut, Obsession , which became a notable box office success after its release in 2026. The supernatural horror film reportedly earned $519 million worldwide against a production budget of less than $1 million.
Obsession follows Bear, a lonely young man who uses a mysterious toy called a One Wish Willow to make his crush, Nikki, fall in love with him. The wish has disastrous consequences for Bear, Nikki and their friends.
Barker’s next project will continue his work in the horror genre while adding a comedic element. With its May 2027 release date confirmed, Anything But Ghosts is set to arrive in cinemas from Focus Features and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster.

Separate probes target the revelations and corruption allegations involving former ambassador Mona Juul and others
Eleven current and former Norwegian ministers are set to face parliamentary questioning for two days beginning Wednesday about foreign ministry practices brought under scrutiny by revelations concerning Jeffrey Epstein, the VG newspaper reported on Tuesday.
The hearings will examine what officials knew about concerns of the Foreign Ministry, including grants to the International Peace Institute (IPI), a think tank formerly headed by Terje Rod-Larsen, who had close contact with the late convicted sex offender.
Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, who served as foreign minister from 2005 to 2012, is among those expected to appear before parliament’s control committee.
Committee chair Per-Willy Amundsen described the information made public so far as “disturbing,” but cautioned that two days of hearings would be insufficient to establish a full account of the matters under review.
A separate commission is investigating the revelations and is due to report in January 2028. Norway’s economic crime authority, Okokrim, is also investigating specific corruption allegations involving former ambassador Mona Juul, Rod-Larsen and former Prime Minister Thorbjorn Jagland.
Former Foreign Minister Borge Brende is also expected to face questions about his roles at the World Economic Forum and his contact with Epstein. Committee member Lars Haltbrekken said he would ask whether Brende’s ties to the forum had influenced his work as foreign minister.
The ministry agreed to support the forum in 2015, during Brende’s tenure. It subsequently received funding from Norway’s development aid budget, according to figures cited by VG.
