title: Iranian lawmaker says US will  inevitably  leave region  Israel s  days are numbered
description: Trump claims Iran war  one of the most important things we ve done
content:
Trump claims Iran war 'one of the most important things we've done'
The head of the Iranian parliament's national security and foreign policy commission, Ebrahim Azizi, said on Tuesday that the United States would inevitably leave the Middle East and that Israel's "days were numbered", according to Al Jazeera .
“The US will inevitably leave this region, and the Zionist regime’s (Israel) days are numbered,” Azizi stated on X.
The Iranian lawmaker further underlined that Iran and its neighbours would ultimately remain in the region after the US and Israel were gone. "Ultimately, it is we and our neighbours who remain here, face to face. That day will be a day of regret.”
The U.S. will inevitably leave this region, and the Zionist regime’s days are numbered. Ultimately, it is we and our neighbors who remain here, face to face. That day will be a day of regret.
Trump claims Iran war 'one of the most important things we've done'
US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that the Iran war would be considered one of the most important things his administration had done under his presidency.
“I think in the years to come, they’ll be writing … the history of our country, and they’ll say that it was one of the most important things that we did,” Trump said. “That is, actually one of the most important things that we’ve done under my administration.”
Trump on Iran: In the years to come, they will be writing the history of our country, and they will say the Iran war is one of the most important things that we did. pic.twitter.com/pYRwVHzP59
Addressing an event in Washington, Trump reiterated that Iran would not possess a nuclear weapon and that oil prices would fall, claiming that the war with Iran would be over “very, very soon”.
“Iran will not have a nuclear weapon, and they’re failing very badly. It’ll be over with very, very soon … and oil prices are going to be tumbling down, just like they were before I had to make that little excursion to the Islamic Republic of Iran,” Trump stated.
US issues new sanctions over Iran military procurement networks
The US Treasury Department on Tuesday sanctioned 10 individuals and entities in multiple jurisdictions that it said procured weapons and weapons components for Iran's Ministry of Defence and Armed Forces Logistics (MODAFL).
"Treasury will not tolerate any support to the regime and will continue to identify, expose, and isolate Iran's enablers," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said.
The department said MODAFL was responsible for weapons research, production and acquisition for Iran's armed forces and oversees organisations developing Iran's ballistic missiles and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs).
🔴 BREAKING: The US has sanctioned 10 individuals and entities that allegedly procured weapons and weapons components for Iran’s Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics, the US Treasury Department’s website shows. pic.twitter.com/yL7WGHTLRe
Among those designated was Seyyed Asghar Alizadeh Tabatabai, whom Treasury described as a MODAFL representative in Beijing who "coordinates the procurement of finished weapons systems and dual-use components in China on Iran's behalf."
‘Iranian order’ prevails in Strait of Hormuz, says Iranian army spokesperson
Iranian army spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia said on Tuesday that an “Iranian order” prevailed in the Strait of Hormuz, according to state news agency IRNA .
Akraminia said Iran’s adversaries aimed to "weaken and overthrow" the Islamic Republic, while another strategic objective was to advance plans for a “Greater Israel” in the region, IRNA stated.
Army spokesperson says ‘Iranian order’ prevails in Strait of Hormuz https://t.co/4bKADYtWyT pic.twitter.com/zpgfrdTT8L
IRGC warns US with use of 'new weapons' if attacks resume
Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi, spokesperson for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), warned on Tuesday that Iran would bring “new weapons” to the battlefield if the conflict with the US “takes on a different form”.
“The enemies certainly have other scenarios as well; we are not unaware of those scenarios and have prepared ourselves,” he said in a press conference, according to Fars news agency.
"We are incessantly designing new weapons, upgrading the existing ones, and continuing our mass production of weaponry to be able to defend ourselves. We employ technologies from around the world to manufacture arms capable of defending our country and our people," he remarked.
سخنگوی سپاه: اگر درگیری‌ها شکل دیگری پیدا کند، ما هم سلاح‌های جدیدی را به میدان خواهیم آورد. دشمنان حتما سناریوهای دیگری هم دارند؛ ما از آن سناریوها بی‌اطلاع نیستیم و خودمان را آماده کرده‌ایم. pic.twitter.com/KvBTb99YrF
The IRGC spokesperson also called US President Donald Trump a "big liar", accusing him of concealing the truth from Americans about Iran's nuclear programme and the effectiveness of Iran's blockade of energy supplies from the Gulf.
Among his reasons for waging war on Iran, Trump has cited the need to ensure that it will never be able to build a nuclear weapon.
BREAKING: Iran's Revolutionary Guard calls President Trump a 'big liar'; says US should leave the Middle East 🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/UrMYWUL8h3 pic.twitter.com/nv6Bq3Luku
"The enemy (US) knows that Iran is not after nuclear weapons," Mohebbi said. "Their issue with Iran is not its nuclear programme but rather its vastness, which they want to destroy."
He also challenged US assertions that Iran had lost most of its leverage over the Strait of Hormuz, in part because the US military had been able to protect some of the tankers bringing oil out of the Gulf.
"The fact that the Americans might manage, at great expense, considerable trouble, and high risk to sneak a small vessel through the Strait of Hormuz under cover of darkness to export, say, 100 or 200 barrels of oil does not mean the Strait is open," Mohebbi said.
According to Kpler data, September saw a recovery of oil exports via the Strait of Hormuz, which are set to hit almost 10 million barrels per day, about half the pre-war volume.
Mohebbi further said that the IRGC had prepared a detailed letter to the American people to explain Iran’s positions, according to IRNA .
Letter to American people goes beyond media propaganda: IRGC spokesperson https://t.co/B3KyX0A2nn pic.twitter.com/7X3ce6sk3U
Mohebbi added that the IRGC could have opted for short and immediate media content, such as social media posts, but instead chose to address the American people in a "detailed and logical manner."
He added that the letter seeks to help Americans better understand Iran’s views and positions, adding that while Iran faces limitations in accessing media outlets inside the United States, the country has hundreds of television and radio networks.
In separate comments carried by IRNA , he said that US bases "not only fail to provide security, but are themselves a source of insecurity" in a message addressed to Iran's neighbours.
IRGC Spokesperson: In a message to neighbors, I believe that the governments and nations of the region have come to realize that US Bases not only fail to provide security, but are themselves a source of insecurity. pic.twitter.com/G4oDMaBdVu
"By pouring trillions of dollars into the region and stationing extensive military infrastructure and weaponry there, the United States claimed to be safeguarding regional security. In reality, these bases not only failed to do so, but they also turned into a source of instability," he said.
"These bases couldn't even defend themselves; most are damaged, unusable, and not worth rebuilding for the US."
Vance blames Iranian leadership for failure of Islamabad MoU
US Vice President JD Vance on Tuesday blamed Iranian leaders for the breakdown of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, saying they “screwed up” by deciding to target commercial ships in regional waters, Al Jazeera reported.
In an interview with journalist Vince Coglianese, Vance said, “I think the Iranians recognise that they screwed up, that they signed a deal with us, we had a ceasefire, we had energy prices that had come down and we had the possibility … that if the Iranians behaved, they would get a lot out of a better relationship with the United States".
NEW... @VP @JDVance on who's actually in charge in Iran, and on whether the supreme leader is *even alive*... VINCE: "I saw the Iranian president was on with @BretBaier last week and Bret asked him like 15 different ways: Are you in charge? Is the IRGC calling the shots? Like,… pic.twitter.com/VbZdvN6eIP
“There is a universe where we can strike a deal with Iran, but that requires the Iranians to behave,” he remarked.
“But what happened? They didn’t behave. They started shooting at commercial shipping,” he added.
JD Vance on Iran: I think the Iranians recognize that they've screwed up. They didn't behave. A lot of officials within the Iranian system think it was stupid for the hardliners to start shooting at ships again, but they did. pic.twitter.com/vzhcHiXtHv
Vance also said that evidence suggested that Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei was still alive, although Washington was unsure of this, according to Al Jazeera .
“We think that he’s alive. We don’t know, of course,” Vance said, adding, “I’ve never seen him. I haven’t seen him on camera recently. The best evidence we have suggests that he is alive.”
JD Vance on Mojtaba Khamenei: We think that Mojtaba Khamenei is alive. I don’t know, of course. I’ve never seen him. But the best evidence that we have suggests that he is alive. pic.twitter.com/0e2s2n93nJ
When asked who was in charge in Iran, Vance said, “It’s a very confused system”.
🔴 US Vice President JD Vance said there is still scope for a deal with Iran if its leaders honour their commitments to Washington, while describing Tehran’s political decision-making system as “very confused” https://t.co/AOsFt1UYIR
“I could give you an answer. It would be at best a guess because you have a number of different constituencies. You have the hardliners, you have the conservatives, you have the moderates, you have the clerics and all of these people are involved in the decision-making process,” he added.
“And then of course you have the new supreme leader, who is very detached,” added Vance. “He’s not involved day-to-day; he’s not going on American Sunday shows and talking about these negotiations.”
Qatar working to overcome obstacles between US and Iran, says foreign ministry
Qatar's foreign ministry said on Tuesday that Qatar was still "working to overcome obstacles between the US and Iran," according to Arab News .
“Qatar’s mediation efforts are ongoing, and we are currently relaying messages between the American and Iranian sides,” Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed Al-Ansari told a press conference in Doha.
🔴 Qatari Foreign Ministry: We are working to overcome obstacles between the US and Iran https://t.co/Il7QsmLt9i 🔴 Qatari Foreign Ministry: We continue to play a mediator role to build common ground between Iran and the US pic.twitter.com/kRtgnbeN6K
Asked about the possibility of a large-scale US military attack on Iran, Ansari said: “We are concerned about any escalation in the region and are working to find a peaceful solution.”
The ministry's comments come as Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi departed New York on Tuesday after stating that Qatari mediators will present the US with new ideas discussed with Tehran on how to meet Iran’s conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz on Monday.
Vessel struck by 'unknown projectile' in Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says
The UK Maritime Trade Operations Centre (UKMTO) reported earlier in the day that it had received a third-party report that a vessel was struck "by a suspected unknown projectile" in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday evening.
UKMTO added that the reported attack resulted in a fire, which has since been extinguished.
UKMTO WARNING 143-26 Click here to view the full product.⤵️ https://t.co/WDfvjzsytF #MaritimeSecurity #MarSec pic.twitter.com/lwjw10eHUo
"Crew are safe, there has been no reported environmental impact or damage assessment," UKMTO said.
It also advised vessels to "transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO, while authorities investigate."
If Iran's security not guaranteed, 'no infrastructure in region will remain safe,' warns Ghalibaf
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf said on Tuesday that if Iran's "security is not guaranteed, no infrastructure will remain safe."
Speaker @mb_ghalibaf : "Let both the United States and all other nations understand, as we have said before, that in a region where we cannot sell our oil, no one will sell theirs. And if our security is not guaranteed, no infrastructure will remain safe." pic.twitter.com/rmnQarut6B
In comments carried by IRNA on X, Ghalibaf also addressed the US and "all other nations" that "in a region where we cannot sell our oil, no one will sell theirs," referring to Iran's efforts to exercise control over the Strait of Hormuz.
According to IRNA , while addressing an open session of the Parliament on Tuesday, Ghalibaf said US leaders should understand that Iran would not be intimidated by threats.
. @mb_ghalibaf : Any threat against Iran will draw swift, regret-inducing response https://t.co/JqieyY9Osa pic.twitter.com/hliQsyJO0e
“The leaders of the White House should know that the great and history-making nation of Iran will never retreat in the face of sabre-rattling and rhetoric or an air or trade blockade, and the response of the Islamic Republic of Iran to any threat or adventurism will be harshly regret-inducing and swift,” he said.
Ghalibaf said US attempts to impose a maritime blockade, close air corridors, and exert pressure on Iran’s trade routes would fail through economic planning and military responses similar to those employed during Iraq’s war against Iran in the 1980s.
“If the enemy’s American decision-making apparatus fails to understand this fundamental truth, it will continue to be caught in the cycle of receiving heavy slaps from the Iranian nation,” he said.
Ghalibaf also criticised “light-headed” remarks by US President Donald Trump at the United Nations General Assembly, saying such statements showed Washington has not changed its behaviour toward Iran.
United States is hiding the true casualties of wars on Iran, says Iranian commander
Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari, deputy chief of the Iranian Army for Coordination, says that the United States is hiding the true casualties of wars on Iran, Press TV reported.
Kremlin says it does not want Iran to quit nuclear non-proliferation treaty
Russia does not want Iran to quit the nuclear non-proliferation treaty and counts on it remaining a party to the agreement, the Kremlin said on Tuesday.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov was responding to comments from Iranian officials about Tehran's possible withdrawal from the treaty, which commits Tehran not to develop or acquire nuclear weapons.
Russia and Iran have close ties under a strategic cooperation treaty between the two countries.
Araghchi rules out compromise on Iran's nuclear programme
Araghchi rejected claims that Tehran has compromised on its nuclear programme, saying Iran’s position on the issue remains unchanged, Iranian state media IRIB reported on Tuesday.
Separately, the IRGC said that Tehran will never seek nuclear weapons, and urged the American people to question why the force has been designated a “terrorist” organisation, according to Al Jazeera .
US aviation sanctions raise international law concerns: Iranian scholar
An Iranian academic said on Tuesday that secondary sanctions targeting Iran’s aviation sector may violate principles of international law and undermine nations’ obligations under international agreements, according to IRNA .
Shahram Zarneshan, an international law scholar at Allameh Tabataba’i University, said aviation ties between countries were expanding, with many governed by the 1994 Chicago Convention on International Civil Aviation and related agreements.
Iranian scholar says US aviation sanctions raise international law concerns https://t.co/I44fFlseW7 pic.twitter.com/kOszogpfIP
“Under this legal framework, states enjoy specific freedoms of air navigation and can expand their aviation ties. Therefore, imposing restrictions or prohibitions on such ties may raise legal concerns if they violate states’ international obligations under relevant agreements,” he said.
Zarneshan said countries that have air transport and transit agreements with Iran may also incur international responsibility if sanctions prevented them from fulfilling their commitments.
He stressed that the implications of aviation sanctions should be assessed not only in political and economic terms, but also in light of their impact on flight safety and passengers’ rights.
The remarks come as Washington has intensified sanctions against Iran’s civil aviation sector .
On September 8, the US Treasury Department announced sanctions targeting 36 entities and individuals linked to Iran’s aviation industry, including foreign companies and intermediaries.
Iranian diplomat rejects Canadian FM’s allegations at United Nations
Iranian representative to the United Nations General Assembly Nasser Asadi rejected allegations by Canada’s foreign minister, saying that Western countries spread disinformation to shield Israel from accountability for its crimes, as reported by IRNA .
Iranian diplomat rejects Canadian FM’s allegations at UN https://t.co/GkJKIltkSO pic.twitter.com/nf20MVcsV0
He made the remarks on Monday in response to the Canadian foreign minister’s speech at the UNGA, in which she described Iran as the main threat to regional peace and security.
According to IRNA , Asadi said the real insult to international law was whitewashing Israel’s crimes through disinformation, diverting public attention, demonising a country and labelling it the so-called “main threat to peace and security.”
He described Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s characterisation of the genocide in Gaza as the “biggest lie of the century” during his address to the UN General Assembly last week .
He said that neither Netanyahu’s remarks nor those of Canada’s foreign minister could erase documented facts, invalidate court findings and rulings, whitewash crimes witnessed by the world, or change Israel’s status as the “main threat to peace and security.”
According to IRNA , Asadi further said that no fabrication or falsehood could absolve Canada or other Western countries, particularly the United States, of their international responsibilities.
He said that these countries would be unable to escape the individual responsibility of their officials for involvement in crimes committed by Israel in West Asia.
Iran says Qatar to present US with new ideas aimed at reopening Strait of Hormuz
Qatari mediators will present the US with new ideas discussed with Tehran on how to meet Iran’s conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, Araghchi said late on Monday, adding a final response from Washington could come on Tuesday.
Speaking to Iranian reporters in New York, Araghchi said he met again with Qatari mediators and discussed possible ways to facilitate implementation of Tehran’s conditions.
Qatari mediators will present the US with new ideas discussed with Tehran on how to meet Iran’s conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says, adding that a final response from Washington could come Tuesday https://t.co/2On9DqE6YF pic.twitter.com/zDKH01O2Uu
“They had ideas, and we discussed how a way could be found to meet Iran’s conditions and how those conditions could be fulfilled,” he said, according to the official IRNA news agency.
The ideas will now be raised with the US side, after which Washington’s final response will be relayed to Tehran, Araghchi said.
Read: Trump says US officials ​talked with mediators, will win Iran war 'very soon'
“I hope this will happen by tomorrow,” he added.
He said exchanges through Qatari and Pakistani mediators had remained open but had become more serious following Iran’s latest proposal.
According to IRNA , the US response would be conveyed to Tehran via Qatar.
FM @araghchi : US response to Iran’s proposals to be conveyed through Qatar https://t.co/7oPKrPX7Am pic.twitter.com/7VyBWnchas
“There are conditions, and they have been emphasised by the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, and these conditions must be implemented for the Strait of Hormuz to be opened,” he said.
According to IRNA , the foreign minister said Iran’s seven-point plan has been conveyed to the United States through the Qatari mediator, adding that Tehran is waiting for an official response through the intermediaries.
“Our mission was to inform the American side of these conditions and also to inform all other countries and the international community, so that it would be clear that Iran has a plan in this regard,” Araghchi said, describing the conditions as “completely fair and logical.”
He added that if the US claims it is seeking an agreement or a peaceful solution, “we have presented this solution.”
Araghchi said Tehran had also used its meetings in New York to convey to Washington and the international community the conditions it says must be met for the Strait of Hormuz to reopen.
Later, IRNA reported that Araghchi has left New York for Tehran after concluding his diplomatic engagements and consultations.
On the last day of his presence in New York, he met with António Guterres, the UN Secretary-General, and discussed the most important regional and international developments, according to IRNA .
Iran’s FM @araghchi leaves New York After intensive diplomatic consultations https://t.co/JzyhDw3XqQ pic.twitter.com/oTKjoH80MX
Regional developments and issues related to the war and the current situation in the Middle East were among the focal points of this meeting.
Araghchi outlined the consequences of the US and Israeli military attacks against Iran, stressing that the United Nations and its member states should not remain indifferent to violations of the UN Charter by the United States and should condemn its unlawful interventionist actions and threats.
The Iranian foreign minister also referred to the US and Israeli attacks during the negotiations and the continuation of the aggressive actions, emphasising Iran’s determination to defend its national sovereignty and territorial integrity.
Repeating 'baseless claims' do not alter reality: Iranian deputy FM
Iran’s deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Tuesday that "baseless claims" over the Persian Gulf islands of Abu Musa, Greater Tunb and Lesser Tunb do not change the fact that they are Iranian territory.
تکرار ادعاهای بی‌اساس درباره جزایر ایرانی، حتی از تریبون مجمع عمومی، واقعیت را تغییر نمیدهد. ابوموسی، تنب بزرگ و تنب کوچک، بخش جدایی‌ناپذیر از قلمرو ایران‌اند. مقامات اماراتی باید به جای تکرار ادعاهای واهی، به الزامات حسن همجواری و واقعیت های تاریخی و حقوقی منطقه پایبند باشند.
"Emirati officials should, instead of repeating unfounded claims, adhere to the requirements of good neighbourliness and the historical and legal realities of the region."
US, Iran separately talk with mediators in latest bid to end war
US and Iranian officials spoke separately with mediators on Monday as part ‌of a renewed effort to end seven months of war, according to officials of both countries.
Any further talks are expected to focus on an amended version of a seven-day proposal that Iran presented last week on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, ​an official briefed on the negotiations told Reuters .
The war began in late February with US and Israeli ​attacks on Iran, killing thousands of people over seven months and shocking global markets ⁠as vital waterways for oil remained choked. The US and Iran have twice previously agreed to ceasefires in ​mediated peace talks, in April and June. Those agreements quickly unravelled.
Read more: Iran Guards claim seizure of US underwater drone in Hormuz, US denies
Araghchi, who remained in New ​York after attending the General Assembly, said Iran expected to receive the US response to its latest ceasefire proposals and its conditions for restoring passage of maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, according to state news agency IRNA.
"If the Americans claim ​they are seeking an agreement or a peaceful solution, we have presented that solution," Araghchi said.
US officials separately ​spoke with mediators on Monday, US President Donald Trump told reporters at the White House, without giving further details.
Iran's seven-day plan envisages an end to all hostilities in Iran and Lebanon, the unfreezing of billions of dollars' worth of Iranian assets, an end to sanctions on Iranian oil and the lifting of the US blockade on Iranian ports.
Iran would then allow the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital conduit for ​oil tankers, and the two ​sides would also resume ⁠talks on Iran's nuclear program and Trump's wish to seize or eliminate its highly enriched uranium.
Trump said on Saturday he had rejected Iran's proposal, saying Iran wanted a swift ​agreement because of the crippling economic pressure it is under. However, he also told ​Axios on ⁠Sunday that he expected US negotiators to engage in further talks this week.
Also read: At UNGA, Iran's president vows 'no surrender to US'
Araghchi said on Sunday that mediators had not formally conveyed a US rejection, and that Iran was awaiting Washington's definitive position before deciding its next steps.
"Our conditions are ⁠clear, and ​any move toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent on ​these conditions being met," he said on Sunday, adding that only a negotiated solution could resolve the impasse.
US to grant sanctions waiver for flights between Iran and Iraq's Najaf, source says
US President Donald Trump's administration was set ​to grant a limited waiver to its Iran sanctions program on Monday to allow for flights carrying ‌Shi'ite Muslim religious pilgrims between Iran and Iraq, a person with direct knowledge of the matter said.
The source, who is involved in the deliberations, said the US Treasury Department waiver would allow Iraqi Airways to fly back and forth between Iran and the ​Shi'ite holy city of Najaf in Iraq for one month, with a more permanent waiver potentially following.
Iraq halted ​flights to and from Iran on Friday, in line with US sanctions.
The source said the ⁠move aimed to ease pressure on the Iraqi government of Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, who has sought to deepen ​ties with Washington while also balancing a strong relationship with Iraq's influential neighbour, Iran.
Trump's effort to impose a ​crippling economic blockade on Iran is forcing regional governments to scale back ties with Iran, creating potential backlash against those states, particularly those that balance their ties with both Washington and Tehran.
Zaidi's office over the weekend said that Iraq was seeking an exemption ​for travel between Iran and Iraq for medical treatment, education and pilgrimage.
An Iraqi official said the Iraqi government was ​in talks with the US about the Najaf exemption and expected flights between Iran and Najaf to resume within 48 hours.
The ‌US ⁠State Department referred questions to the Treasury Department, which did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
In recent days, countries including Turkey, the UAE and Iraq have cancelled direct flights with Iran as a result of US pressure. In response, Iranian officials have threatened to halt regional air travel if Iran's air links continued to ​be cut.
With religious ​pilgrims travelling between Iran and ⁠Iraq each year to visit key shrine cities, Iraq is perhaps in the most sensitive position.
Najaf, a centre for religious study, draws millions of pilgrims a year to ​the shrine of Imam Ali, the first Shi'ite leader, and the world’s largest ​and oldest ⁠active Islamic cemetery.
The source said that barring flights between the two countries could cause severe backlash against Iraq's government by uniting Shi'ites who follow Iran's supreme leader and those who follow Iraq's Grand Ayatollah Ali al-Sistani, undermining US efforts to ⁠reduce Iranian ​influence in Iraq.
Zaidi has offered safeguards for the flights, including rigorous screening and information sharing, and ensuring the flights are not used to transfer weapons, sanctioned individuals, or illicit money, the ​source said.
Trump denies offering Iran sanctions relief, release of frozen assets
President Donald Trump denied an Axios report stating that he offered Iran sanctions relief and the release of frozen funds, according to a post he made on his Truth Social account.
“ Axios just released a story that ‘Trump’ offered sanctions relief and frozen funds to Iran. This is untrue. I offered them NOTHING!,” Trump said.
"They should withdraw this fake story, IMMEDIATELY!"

title: Netanyahu asks UAE president to deny report on October 7 warning during secret visit  report
description: UAE s state news agency confirms Netanyahu s visit to Abu Dhabi  says both leaders discussed bilateral relations
content:
UAE's state news agency confirms Netanyahu's visit to Abu Dhabi, says both leaders discussed bilateral relations
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu asked United Arab Emirates (UAE) President Mohamed bin Zayed during a secret meeting on Sunday to deny a report that he had warned Netanyahu of an imminent Hamas attack before October 7, 2023, Israeli newspaper Haaretz said on Monday, Anadolu Agency reported .
Netanyahu asked bin Zayed to deny reports about their phone conversation and details surrounding the events before October 7 that “could embarrass him,” Haaretz said, citing unspecified sources.
Netanyahu asked UAE leader to deny Haaretz Oct. 7 warning report in secret visit https://t.co/5n7BavDi6l
The Israeli premier also asked the Emirati president for what one source described as “moral support,” the newspaper reported.
Netanyahu held an hour-long meeting with bin Zayed, according to two people briefed on the trip.
According to UAE’s state news agency WAM , bin Zayed received Netanyahu, who visited the UAE on Sunday. "During the meeting, the two leaders discussed bilateral relations between the UAE and Israel and ways to strengthen and further develop them".
🚨🇦🇪🇮🇱After 24 hours the Emirati state news agency confirms Netanyahu's visit to Abu Dhabi: "UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan received Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who visited the United Arab Emirates on Sunday. During the meeting, the two leaders… https://t.co/f6lZYJYpj1
Israeli public broadcaster KAN reported that Netanyahu travelled on a private plane owned by an unnamed Israeli businessman and used by senior Israeli figures for international trips.
The broadcaster said it departed Ben Gurion Airport in the afternoon and landed in Abu Dhabi at 3:10 pm (1110GMT). It took off for Israel at 7:10 pm (1510GMT), four hours later, and landed shortly after 10pm (1900GMT).
KAN said Netanyahu had also used the aircraft for a trip to Abu Dhabi during the war with Iran.
The visit comes after Haaretz this month reported that Sheikh Mohamed ​had warned Netanyahu a week and a half before October 7, 2023, ​that Hamas was planning a major operation against Israel. Haaretz had reported that the warning was not passed to Israeli intelligence agencies or the military.
Netanyahu, ​who denied the report and threatened legal action against the newspaper, is facing a tough reelection campaign. Opposition leaders have accused the prime minister of bearing responsibility for security failures that preceded Hamas' October 7 attack .
Read : Netanyahu warned by UAE president before October 7 events, failed to brief security chiefs: Haaretz
On Friday, the New York Times also reported that Netanyahu had received a confidential warning from the UAE president before the Hamas attack but had not passed it on to Israel’s security chiefs.
The UAE declined to comment on the ​ Haaretz report but said it and Israel maintained "open and direct ​lines of communication" since establishing diplomatic relations in 2020. A UAE source previously told Reuters ‌that ⁠the UAE discusses security matters with countries through the "relevant entities," but not "at the level of national leaders".
بيان صادر من وزارة الخارجية بشأن تقارير إعلامية Statement by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Response to Media Reporting pic.twitter.com/9S4Zavjjzc
Earlier this year, the UAE denied that Sheikh Mohamed met with Netanyahu after the Israeli prime minister's office said in May that Netanyahu ​had "secretly visited" the Gulf ​country and met ⁠with the president.
A source familiar with the meeting said at the time that Netanyahu and Sheikh Mohammed met in ​Al-Ain, an oasis city in Abu Dhabi along the country's ​border with ⁠Oman, on March 26.
Read More : Israeli newspaper rejects Netanyahu’s demands, vows to reveal truth in court after lawsuit threat
Since coming under attack during the Iran war , the UAE has strengthened its relationships with the United States and Israel, with which it opened ties ⁠as ​a result of the 2020 Abraham Accords. The ​relationship with Israel gives the UAE a lever for regional influence and a unique channel to Washington.

title: Game of Thrones movie Aegon   s Conquest  sets 2029 release date
description: Game of Thrones  Aegon   s Conquest  has set a June 6  2029 release date  bringing Westeros to cinemas
content:
'Game of Thrones: Aegon’s Conquest' has set a June 6, 2029 release date, bringing Westeros to cinemas
The first Game of Thrones movie, Aegon’s Conquest , has set a June 6, 2029 release date, bringing the world of Westeros to the big screen for the first time.
Owen Harris, who is also involved with HBO’s upcoming series A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms , will direct the film. Beau Willimon has written the screenplay for the upcoming Game of Thrones movie.
Plot details for Aegon’s Conquest remain limited, but the story is expected to focus on Aegon I Targaryen and his conquest of Westeros, which took place centuries before the events of the original Game of Thrones series.
Aegon I, the founder of the Targaryen dynasty, has not previously appeared on screen. Casting details for the character and other roles have not yet been announced.
The Targaryen family has remained a major part of HBO’s expansion of the Game of Thrones universe. The dynasty was central to House of the Dragon , which explores events involving the Targaryen family roughly 200 years before Game of Thrones .
The original Game of Thrones series, based on George R.R. Martin’s fantasy novels, ran for eight seasons from 2011 to 2019. The series received widespread recognition during its run, including multiple Emmy Awards.
Meanwhile, HBO is continuing to expand the franchise on television. House of the Dragon is set to return for a fourth season, while A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms has also been renewed for a second season.
With Aegon’s Conquest , the Game of Thrones franchise is set to extend its story from television to the cinema in 2029.

title: Anthropic s  518b AI buildout hinges largely on deals that cannot be canceled  filing shows
description: Anthropic says 80  of its compute commitments are non cancelable as AI demand outpaces supply
content:
Anthropic says 80% of its compute commitments are non-cancelable as AI demand outpaces supply
Anthropic said it expects to spend at least $518 billion over a decade building AI infrastructure with ​six partners, according to a confidential IPO prospectus seen by Reuters — a plan that ranks among the largest AI buildout commitments ‌on record.
The AI lab said in the prospectus that about 80% of that sum is non-cancelable or requires payment regardless of usage. Anthropic is telling investors the commitments are necessary because access to computing power is becoming the key constraint on AI development, as future demand for advanced AI systems is likely to exceed available supply ​and will be "limited principally by the availability of compute."
The company said it plans to spend at least $111.1 billion with Alphabet's Google, $110 billion ​with Amazon and $31.4 billion with Microsoft under long-term infrastructure service obligations over the next seven to 10 years "regardless of ⁠usage."
Anthropic is separately carrying about $161.2 billion of Broadcom -related equipment lease obligations that are largely non-cancelable, according to the prospectus. Anthropic filed for an ​IPO confidentially with the Securities and Exchange Commission in June but its paperwork has not been publicly disclosed.
Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request ​for comment about the filing.
he company said it committed to pay Google between April 2026 and July 2033 and Amazon between May 2026 and April 2036.
"If our actual spend falls short, we must pay Google the difference," the company said, adding that similar terms apply to its Amazon agreement.
It added its commitment with Microsoft of $31.4 billion ​between November 2026 and May 2033 "is non-cancelable except in the event of Microsoft's uncured material breach."
Read More: China's AI agents can lie and scheme - just like their US rivals
Anthropic also said the lease arrangements with Broadcom are ​non-cancelable by either party except in the case of a default.
The company also disclosed agreements with Elon Musk's xAI that could result in ‌up to $84.5 ⁠billion of spending for Nvidia-based computing capacity through 2029 that are largely cancelable with a 90-day notice.
The filing also showed a deepening relationship with Advanced Micro Devices which committed to buying up to $5 billion of Anthropic stock and to supply AI computing capacity expected to exceed $20 billion.
The overall figure is comparable in scale to OpenAI's Stargate project, a $500 billion AI infrastructure plan whose costs are expected to be shared among OpenAI, SoftBank, Oracle and ​MGX.
Anthropic said it ​is increasingly building its own AI ⁠infrastructure, shifting from a cloud-only model toward dedicated data centers and directly leased chips.
It flagged a key risk in its dependence on Amazon, Google and Microsoft, which provide computing infrastructure and distribution while also developing rival ​AI models.
The company said the three tech giants occupy multiple roles at once as investors, customers, cloud providers, ​distributors and competitors, ⁠creating incentives that "may not be fully aligned" with Anthropic's interests.
"If the compute we have access to from third parties is curtailed, repriced, or terminated ... our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected," it said.

title: Production house behind Heated Rivalry launches The Irina Foundation to aid mental health  LGBTQIA2
description: The initiative is dedicated to inclusivity  accessibility  and mental well being through sports and creative arts
content:
The initiative is dedicated to inclusivity, accessibility, and mental well-being through sports and creative arts
Toronto-based production company Accent Aigu Entertainment (AAE), the producer behind the acclaimed series Heated Rivalry, has announced the official launch of The Irina Foundation. Established as a private, independent fund, the initiative is dedicated to championing inclusivity, accessibility, and mental well-being through sports and creative arts, placing a particular emphasis on supporting LGBTQIA2+ and underserved communities.
By funding organisations that establish inclusive and safe spaces, The Irina Foundation aims to assist individuals in building meaningful human connections while fostering stronger, more resilient communities globally. The non-profit initiative expands on AAE’s existing philanthropic endeavours established over the past year, formalising its commitment to social impact.
The new foundation takes its inspiration from fictional lore, deriving its name directly from the charitable organisation created by characters Shane Hollander and Ilya Rozanov in Rachel Reid’s widely popular Game Changer book series.
Prominent global brands have already committed early backing to the project. Fashion brand Kate Spade New York has stepped forward as the inaugural donor for The Irina Foundation, with men's grooming brand Harry’s also joining as an early supporter to help drive its social mission.

title: British premier says  Brexit has done more harm than good
description: Burnham said Britain must decide its future EU ties to secure a clear path into the rest of the century
content:
Burnham said Britain must decide its future EU ties to secure a clear path into the rest of the century
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Tuesday he will “lay out to the country” different options for the UK’s long-term relationship with the EU, arguing that Brexit “has done more harm than good.”
Speaking at the annual Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, Burnham said Britain could not have “the clear path we need into the rest of this century” without deciding on its future relationship with the EU, which he described as “still our largest market.”
The UK left the EU in 2020, four years after a referrendum in which about 52% of voters chose to leave.
The prime minister said he would use the opportunity around the summit to set out the choices available to Britain.
“And there are different options, and I will see if we can find consensus around one, which will give us clarity about our position and the future of the continent that we live in,” he said.
Burnham also announced that Labour's next manifesto would contain a commitment to change the UK's electoral system.
He said he was creating a “new national commission on electoral reform” and invited all political parties to take part in its work.
“In past years, you have voted twice to support electoral reform. I hear you, I agree with you,” Burnham said.
“We will contest the next election with a manifesto commitment to change the electoral system so that everyone's vote counts and everyone's voice is heard,” he added.
Burnham promised to put Britain "on a new path" and unveiling policies on water, housing, energy and education.
"When we pull as one, there is nothing we can't do," he said. “Today, we draw a line on a decade of division. We stop doom scrolling on posts running Britain down. And we put the country on a new path.”
He acknowledged he "may pay a political price" for his announcements but said “someone has to go through the pain barrier and rip the plaster off.”
‘Water is a symbol of what has gone wrong with Britain’
Burnham said Environment Secretary Angela Eagle would introduce a "strengthened Water Bill" including the repeal of “Margaret Thatcher's ideological ban on public ownership of water companies.”
Read More: British PM vows not to stand by as 'horrific suffering continues to grow' in Gaza, West Bank
"Water is a symbol of what has gone wrong with Britain," he said, criticising sewage dumping, high prices and problems with infrastructure.
He, however, did not announce plans to nationalize any individual water companies.
Burnham said the government could introduce legislation making it easier to reclaim homes from negligent landlords.
He also pledged to bring down energy prices and asked the energy secretary to speed up efforts to decouple green energy prices from gas prices.
On education, he promised to “rebuild a system of comprehensive education in this country with parity between academic and technical.”
Burnham criticised the political direction taken since the 1980s, saying: “Homes, water, energy, transport, care, healthcare - broken up and sold off.”
"The British right talk about taking back control. Never let them forget, they are the ones that gave it away in the first place," he said.
Burnham said his economic strategy would involve nationalisation and devolution, arguing that greater control over essential services could help create conditions for business growth.
He confirmed that the government would stick to its fiscal rules “to get borrowing and debt down.”
The premier said the party would maintain its 2024 general election manifesto commitment not to make changes in the current period, while changes could be considered if Labour remains in power beyond the 2029 election.

title: Lauren Cohan lands leading role in new romantic comedy  Both Sides Now
description: Lauren Cohan and Jake Epstein lead Eric Stoltz   s new romantic comedy  Both Sides Now   now filming in Ontario
content:
Lauren Cohan and Jake Epstein lead Eric Stoltz’s new romantic comedy 'Both Sides Now', now filming in Ontario
Lauren Cohan and Jake Epstein are set to lead the cast of Both Sides Now , an independent romantic comedy directed by actor and filmmaker Eric Stoltz.
Cohan, known for The Walking Dead , and Epstein, who appeared in Degrassi: The Next Generation , will headline the ensemble cast of the upcoming romantic comedy. The film is currently in production in Muskoka, Ontario.
Both Sides Now follows a group of lifelong friends approaching 40 who return to the Jewish summer camp where they grew up to celebrate the upcoming wedding of Eddie, played by Epstein.
The reunion takes an unexpected turn when Eddie’s best friend Lloyd, portrayed by Erich Bergen, invites Eddie’s first love and former camp sweetheart Erin, played by Cohan, to the bachelor weekend. The gathering forces the friends to confront unresolved relationships, old feelings and questions about the paths they chose in life.
Stoltz is directing the film from a screenplay by Hailey Lustig and composer Robbie Roth. The story draws inspiration from the writers’ own long friendship and shared experiences growing up at summer camp.
The cast also includes Bergen, Justin Chatwin and Brian Norris. The romantic comedy will feature six original songs written by Roth and performed by members of the cast.
Both Sides Now marks the feature-film debut of Three Birds Landing Productions, which is independently financing the project. Lustig, Carrie Mudd and Erin Berry are producing the film in association with Peacock Alley Entertainment.
Production began on September 19 and is scheduled to continue through October 20. No release date has been announced for Both Sides Now .

title: Trump   s new AI powered website says president lost 2020 election
description: America gov is designed to provide information about the US government using answers generated from government sources
content:
America.gov is designed to provide information about the US government using answers generated from government sources
The Trump administration’s newly launched AI-powered government website, America.gov, initially gave answers that contradicted several public claims made by President Donald Trump, including his repeated statements about the 2020 presidential election.
Launched on September 29, the website is designed to provide Americans with information about government services using artificial intelligence. The platform says its answers are sourced from official government information and brings together information from thousands of federal websites.
When asked who won the 2020 presidential election, the website initially stated that Joe Biden won and that official federal sources did not show widespread fraud had changed the outcome. The answer also acknowledged that isolated election crimes had occurred and been prosecuted.
Trump lost the 2020 election to Biden and has continued to claim that the result was stolen through widespread fraud. However, repeated audits, recounts and court proceedings did not establish widespread fraud that changed the result. The Trump administration itself described the 2020 election as secure at the time.
The AI website subsequently changed how it handled the question. When asked again about the 2020 election, it responded that it could not answer “political questions”. The same response reportedly appeared when users asked about Trump’s impeachments and felony convictions.
America.gov also initially provided answers that conflicted with other statements from Trump. Asked about a possible 2028 presidential campaign, the site cited the 22nd Amendment’s two-term limit and noted that Trump had already been elected in 2016 and 2024. It also identified the Pentagon as the headquarters of the Department of Defense, despite Trump’s efforts to promote the name “Department of War”.
The launch comes as the administration promotes artificial intelligence as a central part of its technology agenda. America.gov is intended to eventually allow users to complete government-related tasks, with additional functions expected to be introduced as the platform develops.

title: Tom Cruise says he isn   t slowing down his acting career at 64
description: Cruise says there is always    another mountain    and    a new adventure    ahead
content:
Cruise says there is always “another mountain” and “a new adventure” ahead
Tom Cruise has no plans to slow down his acting career as he approaches another major milestone, saying there is always “another mountain” and “a new adventure” ahead.
The 64-year-old actor spoke to PEOPLE at the Los Angeles premiere of his upcoming film Digger on September 28, reflecting on his decades in Hollywood and the collaborators who have shaped his approach to filmmaking.
Cruise recalled working with Paul Newman on Martin Scorsese’s 1986 film The Color of Money, noting that Newman was also 64 when they made the movie. He said his experiences with Newman and other filmmakers have influenced how he views art, life and cinema.
The Top Gun star also discussed his work with director Michael Mann on Collateral and his desire to continue exploring different genres rather than limiting himself to action films. Cruise said he has spent his career “absorbing humanity” and wants to reflect that through cinema.
Looking ahead, Cruise has several projects on the horizon, including a new Days of Thunder film with Anne Hathaway, which is scheduled for 2028. He is also currently promoting Digger, directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu.
“I feel it to be a great privilege,” Cruise said of his career and collaborations. He later added that there is “always another mountain” and “always a new adventure” for him.
Digger, which also stars Riz Ahmed, Sandra Hüller, John Goodman and Jesse Plemons, is scheduled to arrive in cinemas and IMAX on October 2.

title: Morocco s king appoints first woman prime minister following election
description: Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri was appointed the premier after her party came out on top in    Sept 23 election
content:
Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri was appointed the premier after her party came out on top in ‌Sept 23 election
King Mohammed VI appointed Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri on ​Tuesday as Morocco's first woman prime minister after her liberal-centrist party came out on top in ‌a September 23 parliamentary election, the royal palace said.
The king asked El Mansouri to form a new government, the palace said in a statement.
El Mansouri’s Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) was created in 2008 by an adviser to the king and has since positioned itself as ​a counterweight to the Islamist Justice and Development Party (PJD) by advocating social modernisation and secular-leaning views.
Morocco is a ​constitutional monarchy where the king retains sweeping powers over foreign policy, defence and other key ⁠portfolios.
Also Read: Israeli settlers attack West Bank village, blocking family's return home
Under Morocco's constitution, the king appoints the head of government from the political party that wins the largest ​number of seats in the House of Representatives.
PAM, which was the second-largest member in the outgoing coalition, moved up to ​the top spot, bolstered by the recruitment of Fouzi Lekjaa, Morocco's football federation chief and two-time government budget manager, who joined weeks before the vote.
El Mansouri, a lawyer who was housing minister in the outgoing government and Marrakech mayor, will lead talks to form ​a coalition government and submit a list of cabinet members for the king's approval.
The incoming government will ​oversee the last stages of a $20-billion push to get ready for the 2030 World Cup, which Morocco will co-host with Portugal and ‌Spain.
It ⁠will also implement economic policies aimed at addressing widespread youth discontent, an issue highlighted by a mass border rush on the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in July and deadly Gen-Z-led protests last year.
Read more: Spain defends Ceuta sovereignty
PAM won 97 seats, followed by its partners in the outgoing government, the liberal-centrist National Rally of Independents (RNI) with 66 seats, and the conservative nationalist Istiqlal with 65.
During the campaign, ​PAM had ruled out staying ​in a coalition with ⁠the RNI — the two had traded blame over policy shortcomings including a failure to halt rises in food prices.But El Mansouri said on Thursday she would have no "red lines" ​when it came to negotiations. "We have turned the page," she said.
Abdelilah Benkirane, former prime minister ​and leader of ⁠the PJD, which won 54 seats, said the party would stay in opposition.
Three leftist parties took smaller shares of the seats.
Turnout, closely watched as an indicator of trust in elected institutions, fell to about 38% from around 50% in the previous ⁠elections five ​years ago, when the moderate Islamist PJD was dealt a crushing ​defeat after a decade in power.
In recent years, King Mohammed VI has appointed a female adviser, and Morocco has had women in senior institutional ​roles. The outgoing government had four women ministers.

title: News outlets ask US court to block Trump White House ban beyond 14 day order
description: Major news groups ask court to block Trump s White House media ban and restore press credentials
content:
Major news groups ask court to block Trump's White House media ban and restore press credentials
Major news organisations asked on Tuesday a federal court to block US President Donald Trump’s White House media ban beyond an initial 14-day order, demanding full restoration of press credentials while litigation proceeds.
“This Court should issue a preliminary injunction enjoining Defendants… from taking any action to enforce the White House ban,” CNN, MS NOW and Politico said in a joint legal memorandum filed Monday in the US District Court for the District of Columbia. The outlets requested an order requiring administration officials to give their journalists the “same access” to the White House and the president that they had before Sept. 18.
The filing argued that the exclusion constitutes unlawful First Amendment retaliation over critical reporting and violates the Fifth Amendment’s due process clause by revoking hard passes without advance notice, hearings or objective criteria.
Read More: White House defies court order on media access
Attorneys also alleged that administration officials delayed compliance with earlier court directives and continued to impose inconsistent restrictions, including barring CNN from an Air Force One flight to Knoxville and limiting coverage of a state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping .
The motion follows a 14-day temporary restraining order issued September 24 by US District Judge Timothy Kelly, who found that the outlets were likely to succeed on their due process claim. The court also questioned the administration’s national security justification for the restrictions.
Trump announced the ban on Sept. 18, accusing the news organisations of spreading “fake news” and citing years of negative coverage.
The plaintiffs warned that the administration intends to reinstate the ban when the restraining order expires October 8, urging the court to intervene to prevent “irreparable harm” to press freedom.

title: Lindsay Clancy speaks in court for first time since mistrial in children   s deaths
description: Clancy is charged with the January 2023 deaths of her three children  Cora  5  Dawson  3  and Callan  8 months
content:
Clancy is charged with the January 2023 deaths of her three children, Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months
Lindsay Clancy spoke in court for the first time since her murder trial ended in a mistrial as she appeared for a status conference in Massachusetts on September 29.
Clancy, 36, appeared at Plymouth Superior Court, where Judge William Sullivan greeted her at the beginning of the hearing. She responded, “Good morning,” marking her first remarks in court since the five-week trial ended without a verdict.
Clancy is charged with the January 2023 deaths of her three children, Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months. She has pleaded not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility, with her defence arguing that she was experiencing postpartum psychosis at the time.
Prosecutors alleged during the trial that Clancy deliberately killed her children and understood that her actions were wrong. The defence, meanwhile, argued that her mental state meant she should not be held criminally responsible.
The trial ended on September 4 after jurors deliberated for seven days without reaching a unanimous verdict. The jury was reportedly split 11-1, resulting in Judge Sullivan declaring a mistrial.
Clancy's attorney Kevin Reddington has since filed a motion arguing that she should not face a second trial because of double jeopardy protections. He also asked the judge on Tuesday to issue a required finding of not guilty, arguing that prosecutors did not present sufficient evidence to establish criminal responsibility.
During Tuesday's hearing, Reddington also challenged the evidence presented against Clancy and argued that police had not properly investigated the case. Prosecutors disputed the defence's claims, saying there was extensive evidence in the case. Judge Sullivan took the request for a finding of not guilty under advisement.
Prosecutors have not yet formally announced whether they will retry Clancy or what charges they would pursue. The two sides discussed a possible retrial date during Tuesday's hearing, but agreed to wait for rulings on several pending motions. A further hearing has been scheduled for November 2.
Clancy remains in custody at a state psychiatric hospital and is on suicide watch. She became paralysed from the waist down after jumping from a second-storey window following the children's deaths.

title: PM Shehbaz underscores Pakistan   s potential for high yield foreign investment
description: Makes history as the first Pakistani premier to open the London Stock Exchange session
content:
Makes history as first Pakistani premier to open London Stock Exchange session
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday said Pakistan offered significant opportunities for high-yield, secure and mutually beneficial foreign investment as the government continued efforts to strengthen the economy during his address at the London Stock Exchange (LSE) headquarters in Paternoster Square.
PM Shehbaz became the first Pakistani premier to open a trading session at the LSE, where he also formally inaugurated Pakistan’s $3 billion dual-tranche sovereign Eurobond.
“We have strengthened our macroeconomic indicators, which are very promising and augur very well for the future,” he said.
The ceremony was attended by LSE Group Chief Executive Officer David Schwimmer, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, Adviser on Privatisation Mohammad Ali, Pakistan High Commissioner Tipu Usman, members of the Pakistani delegation and British officials.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif, today, became the first prime minister from Pakistan to open the London Stock Exchange trading session and formally inaugurated Pakistan’s landmark US$3 billion dual-tranche sovereign Eurobond. During his address at the LSE headquarters in… pic.twitter.com/yvm6hdA2Uh
The premier said the $3 billion dual-tranche sovereign Eurobond reflected the efforts undertaken by the finance ministry and other government institutions to stabilise the economy.
He attributed the transaction to structural reforms, digitalisation of the economy and measures aimed at putting the country’s finances back on track.
The issuance, described as Pakistan’s largest international bond transaction, attracted nearly $6 billion in global investor demand — almost twice the amount raised — from a geographically diverse institutional investor base.
Read: Pakistan, IMF formally begin talks on EFF, climate programme reviews
The transaction is the first issuance under Pakistan’s renewed Global Medium-Term Note (GMTN) Programme and follows the country’s inaugural Panda Bond and successive sovereign credit-rating upgrades.
It forms part of the government’s debt-management strategy aimed at diversifying funding sources, extending maturities and reducing refinancing risks.
Referring to the government’s privatisation programme, PM Shehbaz cited Pakistan International Airlines and First Women Bank and said the government was moving towards divesting several other state-owned enterprises.
Mr. David Schwimmer, CEO of the London Stock Exchange, presenting a memento commemorating Pakistan’s US$ 3 billion dual-tranche sovereign Eurobond listing at the London Stock Exchange to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, today. pic.twitter.com/ksxlHbD3zz
He said such entities should be operated by the private sector and identified privatisation as an area where Pakistan and the United Kingdom could enhance cooperation.
The premier also referred to the Gulf crisis and its impact on emerging economies, saying Pakistan’s economic trajectory could have been stronger had the crisis not erupted.
“Like other emerging economies, we are negotiating this challenge while also playing an important role as a peacemaker, mediating between the United States and Iran. I hope that we will continue in this direction,” he said.
Read more: Trump claims Iran war 'one of the most important things we've done'
PM Shehbaz said changing geopolitical conditions had prompted investors to reassess the relative safety of different markets, adding that Pakistan needed to draw lessons from the evolving situation.
Addressing Schwimmer, the prime minister sought the LSE chief executive’s guidance on increasing Pakistan’s engagement with international financial markets beyond sovereign borrowing and attracting greater investment into the country.
Shehbaz said opening the LSE session was a significant moment for Pakistan and represented a step towards rebuilding the country’s relationship with the London Stock Exchange.
He also invited Schwimmer to visit Pakistan.
The prime minister also praised Aurangzeb, other economic ministers, government secretaries and officials for their role in efforts to strengthen the economy.
PM Shehbaz meets global finance giants in London
Later, PM Shehbaz met with senior executives of Barclays, JP Morgan, Citi, BlackRock and Rothschild & Co in London, where he sought a greater role for global banks in Pakistan’s financial sector and urged leading financial institutions to invest in the country during a series of meetings, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office.
“The engagements underscored growing international financial sector interest in Pakistan’s economic reform trajectory and improving investment climate,” the statement said.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif held a series of meetings today with senior executives from leading global financial institutions — Barclays, J.P. Morgan, Citi, BlackRock and Rothschild & Co — during his visit to the United Kingdom. The engagements underscored growing… pic.twitter.com/ttTmbB67X3
The prime minister met Mohammad Kamal Syed, Head of Private Bank and Wealth Management UK at Barclays, and welcomed the bank’s interest in Pakistan, according to the statement.
He briefed Syed on the government’s macroeconomic stabilisation measures and encouraged Barclays to explore opportunities in Pakistan’s financial sector, it added.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif meets a delegation of Barclays in London, today. pic.twitter.com/0QhqpKDoWC
PM Shehbaz also met a high-level JP Morgan delegation led by Matthieu Wiltz, Co-CEO for EMEA, where they discussed deepening the partnership across capital markets, trade finance and investment banking, the statement said.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif held a meeting with the delegation of J P Morgan headed by co-CEO of EMEA, Mr. Mathieu Wiltz, in London. pic.twitter.com/Oz2mI2SZUi
The prime minister invited the firm to expand its footprint in Pakistan. At the same time, the delegation reaffirmed its interest in sovereign debt capital markets and corporate banking opportunities, according to the statement.
The premier also met a group of senior Citi officials led by David Livingstone, Chief Client Officer.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif held a meeting with the senior leadership of Citi group in London, today. pic.twitter.com/Sfkwf4Rkrt
According to the statement, Shehbaz commended the bank’s long-standing presence in Pakistan and encouraged an expansion of its corporate and institutional banking services in the country.
In his meeting with a BlackRock delegation comprising Gordon Fraser and Sam Vecht, Co-Heads of Emerging Markets and Frontiers, and Emily Fletcher, Portfolio Manager and Research Analyst, the prime minister invited increased allocations to Pakistani equities and fixed income within the firm’s frontier markets strategy, the statement said.
Both sides also emphasised the importance of sustained policy consistency in building investor confidence, it added.
During his meeting with Rothschild & Co, represented by Lord Mark Sedwill, Chair of Geostrategic Advisory, and Majid Ishaq, Head of UK Investment Banking, discussions centred on Pakistan’s geo-economic priorities and potential advisory collaboration on capital markets and investment strategy, according to the statement.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif met delegation of Rothschild & Co. headed by Lord Mark Sedwill, Chair of Geostrategic Advisory in London, today. pic.twitter.com/k744BxlnhG
“Across all engagements, the visiting executives expressed confidence in Pakistan’s economic reform momentum and reaffirmed their institutions’ commitment to deepening engagement with the country’s financial sector,” the statement said.
The meetings “reflect the growing traction” of Pakistan’s economic reform programme among leading global financial institutions and mark a significant step in the government’s broader effort to strengthen international investor confidence and attract sustained capital flows into the country, it added.

title: Ali Hazelwood announces  The Love Hypothesis  sequel and new film adaptation

Ali Hazelwood announces 'The Two-Body Problem' sequel, while MRC develops its film adaptation for Amazon MGM Studios
Author Ali Hazelwood is continuing the story of Olive Smith and Adam Carlsen with a new sequel to The Love Hypothesis , while a film adaptation of the follow-up is also in development.
Hazelwood announced Tuesday that The Two-Body Problem , a sequel to her 2021 romance novel, will be published on February 2, 2027. The book will revisit the relationship between Olive and Adam several years after the events of the original story.
In a social media announcement, Hazelwood said the recent The Love Hypothesis movie and its cast helped her reconnect with the characters. She described returning to Adam and Olive as an enjoyable experience while acknowledging that some readers may prefer to keep their own interpretations of the original story.
Hazelwood also revealed that MRC is developing a film adaptation of The Two-Body Problem for Amazon MGM Studios. She noted that the project is still in development and that further details have not yet been announced.
The news comes shortly after the release of The Love Hypothesis film on Prime Video. Directed by Claire Scanlon, the adaptation stars Lili Reinhart as Olive Smith and Tom Bateman as Adam Carlsen.
The original novel follows Olive, a Stanford Ph.D. candidate, who enters a fake relationship with the intimidating scientist Adam after trying to convince her friend that she has moved on from a romantic interest.
Published in 2021, The Love Hypothesis became a New York Times bestseller and gained a large following through BookTok. Hazelwood’s books have sold more than 10 million copies worldwide, with several titles also in development for screen adaptations.
The Two-Body Problem is scheduled to arrive in bookstores on February 2, 2027.

title: Israeli settlers attack West Bank village  blocking family s return home
description: Israel says strike killed Hamas commander Al Beik in Gaza  who Hamas said helped lead October 7 attack
content:
Israel says strike killed Hamas commander Al-Beik in Gaza, who Hamas said helped lead October 7 attack
More than 100 Israeli settlers have attacked a village in ​the occupied West Bank, preventing a Palestinian family from returning home and clashing with troops, ‌witnesses said.
Two houses belonging to the Tubasi family in Jalud village were seized by settlers weeks ago, amid a surge of settler violence and land seizures that have drawn international condemnation.
The family had been staying elsewhere in the village, north of the city ​of Ramallah in the Palestinian territory, until Israel's military agreed to escort them back late on ​Monday night and protect them from the settlers.
Around ten minutes after they reached the ⁠homes, a group of over 100 settlers descended, witnesses said. The settlers set the homes on fire, blocked ​access roads, and hurled rocks toward Israeli officers, three of whom were injured, the Israeli military said in ​a statement.
A house belonging to Palestinians Mahmod Tubasi, 60, and his wife Aedah, 51, damaged in what they say was an Israeli settler attack in Jalud in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, September 29, 2026. REUTERS
"Due to the violence, the mission to return the family to their homes was not completed," the military said. Troops had the Palestinians go up to the roof when the settlers broke in but then evacuated them as the clashes intensified, ​witnesses said.
The incident highlights the Israeli military's failure to rein in settlers emboldened by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's ​far-right government, which has overseen an expansion of settlements and settler outposts in the West Bank.
In a statement, Netanyahu said ‌he ⁠strongly condemns the violence and called on law enforcement to prosecute them. Israeli and Palestinian rights groups say settler perpetrators are rarely punished for violence.
Wael Tubasi, who owns one of the two homes, told Reuters on Tuesday that the homes "were damaged beyond description".
"They damaged everything — the doors, the tiles were removed, the stairs were removed. ​They smashed the bathrooms, doors ​and windows. They left ⁠nothing, everything was broken," he said.
Reuters journalists reached the homes on Tuesday afternoon. Inside, the walls were black, stained with tar and residue from tyres the settlers had ​brought in and set ablaze.
Around half a dozen Israeli soldiers were patrolling the ​area. The Tubasi ⁠family was not present.
The military said its forces had arrested two settlers and launched an investigation.
lsewhere in the West Bank on Tuesday, settlers set fire to cars in the village of Al Mughayyir and spraypainted the word "revenge" on ⁠the outside ​of an apartment building.
Moussa Mohammed Hamdan, a village resident, said ​of the settlers: "Wherever they see cars, livestock or olive trees, they destroy them — anything that can hurt us. But God willing, we will ​remain patient."
An Israeli airstrike killed the head of Hamas' armed wing in north Gaza on Tuesday, officials on both sides said, with the militant group describing him as a leader of the October 7, 2023, attack that precipitated the war in the Palestinian enclave .
Israel's government said its military had targeted and killed Izz al-Din Al-Beik, who they said was involved in planning attacks and recruiting. Hamas confirmed his death.
Medics said the Israeli strike hit an apartment building in Gaza City's Nasr neighbourhood around dawn. A second person died from wounds after the attack, health officials said.
Later on Tuesday, two separate airstrikes in Jabalia refugee camp, one near a medical clinic and the other at a tent encampment housing displaced families, killed at least three people, medics said.
Palestinians react as they carry the bodies during the funeral of Al-Qassam Brigades Commander Izz al-Din al-Baik and his bodyguard, who were killed in an Israeli airstrike that targeted an apartment, according to medics, in Gaza City, September 29, 2026. REUTERS
The Israeli military reported two strikes that targeted militants in Jabalia.
Israel, which says Hamas has been rearming and launching attacks in violation of an October ceasefire, has stepped up strikes on the group in recent weeks.
The Israeli military says it has killed at least 20 Hamas figures this month, including some it identified as senior commanders, people who took part in the October 7, 2023, attacks or those who held Israeli hostages.
Hamas has denied trying to carry out attacks or rebuild its arsenal and accuses Israel of undermining the Gaza peace deal.
Also on Tuesday, Palestinians in the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza buried the newly recovered remains of 41 people killed in a series of Israeli strikes on homes in the area in a single day three weeks into the war nearly three years ago.
Hundreds of relatives and friends gathered in an open space to pay respect as the remains were placed in white shrouds adorned with Palestinian flags.
"There are mixed feelings between relief, sadness, and pain. But thank God, the fire in my heart has eased a little, because my husband now has a grave that my orphaned children and I can visit," said Areej Farajallah, who lost her husband.
The bodies were the latest of around 800 that have been recovered by excavation teams moving from site to site in the enclave during the ceasefire.
"With minimal equipment, their remains were recovered after hours of work, retrieving what was left of bones, some skulls, and hair with which it is extremely difficult for us to identify them," said Rami Al-Ayedi, of Gaza's Civil Defence Service.
Palestinian authorities estimate more than 8,000 bodies remain buried in wreckage.
The recovered remains of 112 people from the same clan were laid to rest in the largest mass burial so far last month.
Last year's US-brokered ceasefire calls for eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made as negotiators have failed to agree terms for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops.
Israeli airstrikes have continued. At least 1,400 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since the ceasefire, according to the territory's health officials, while Israel says four soldiers have been killed.
Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Israel's assault on Gaza, launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel in October 2023.

content:
Renée Zellweger has been dismissed from a $10 million lawsuit involving boyfriend Ant Anstead and a house guest
Renée Zellweger has been dismissed from a $10 million lawsuit involving her boyfriend, Ant Anstead, after a woman who alleged she was injured at his Laguna Beach rental home dropped the actress from the case.
According to court documents, Tracey Belland dismissed Zellweger as a defendant in the lawsuit. The dismissal was made with prejudice, meaning the claims against the Oscar-winning actress cannot be filed again.
The legal dispute stems from an alleged 2024 incident at a home Anstead was renting in Laguna Beach, California. Belland claimed she was injured after stepping on a thin rug that covered a hole in the property. She alleged that she stumbled and fell, resulting in a knee injury.
Zellweger was initially named alongside Anstead in the lawsuit, which sought $10 million in damages. However, sources previously cited in the case said the actress had no involvement with the rental property, was not listed on the lease and maintained a separate home nearby.
The dismissal means Zellweger is no longer a defendant in the legal battle, while the case against Anstead remains ongoing.
Anstead has previously denied allegations that he was legally responsible for Belland’s reported injuries.
Zellweger and Anstead have been in a relationship for several years and have occasionally been photographed together at public events. The actress, known for films including Bridget Jones’s Diary and Judy , has largely kept her personal life private.
The latest development removes Zellweger from the lawsuit but does not resolve the claims against Anstead. The legal proceedings involving the television personality and Belland are continuing.

Gabriel Tierney, Auliʻi Cravalho, Peter Berry, Chaneil Kular, Devin Craig and Aidan Shaw have joined the series
Netflix has expanded the cast of Icebreaker, its upcoming college hockey romance drama based on Hannah Grace’s bestselling novel of the same name.
Gabriel Tierney, Auliʻi Cravalho, professional athlete Peter Berry, Chaneil Kular, Devin Craig and Aidan Shaw have joined the series as regular cast members. They join previously announced leads Daisy Jelley and Connor Simos.
Icebreaker follows Anastasia Allen (Jelley), a transfer student determined to reach the Olympics, and Nate Hawkins (Simos), a campus hockey star pursuing a career in the NHL. When an accident forces their teams to share a rink, their rivalry begins to develop into an intense romance.
Tierney, known for Rivals and Enola Holmes 2, will play Aaron, while Cravalho, who voiced the title character in Moana, will portray Lola. Berry will play Robbie, Kular will appear as JJ, Craig will portray Henry and Shaw will play Russ.
The series is based on the first book in Grace’s Maple Hills trilogy. Icebreaker spent 70 weeks on the New York Times bestseller list after its original publication in November 2022 and wider release in 2023. The novel has sold nearly five million copies worldwide, while the three-book Maple Hills series has surpassed 7.5 million copies in global sales.
Jade Halley Bartlett, whose credits include Road House, Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness and Miller’s Girl, created Icebreaker and serves as an executive producer. Amanda Lasher is the series’ showrunner, writer and executive producer.
Grace also executive produces alongside Alex Cooper, Matt Kaplan and Mina Lefevre for Cooper’s Unwell Productions.
