title: PPP to seek Bilawal   s nod as TTAP reaches out ahead of opposition APC
description: Bukhari says continued consultation on constitutional  democratic matters among political parties important
content:
Gohar Khan calls for political consensus as TTAP delegation briefs PPP's Bukhari on APC agenda in Islamabad meeting
The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) on Tuesday said it would refer an invitation from the Tehreek-e-Tahaffuz-e-Ain Pakistan (TTAP) to attend an upcoming All Parties Conference (APC) to party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari after a meeting between the two sides at the party’s Islamabad secretariat.
A TTAP delegation, comprising representatives of opposition parties, visited the PPP Central Secretariat and met PPP Parliamentarians Secretary General Syed Nayyar Hussain Bukhari, formally inviting the party to participate in the conference.
Welcoming the delegation, Bukhari said the invitation would be conveyed to Bilawal and that the TTAP would subsequently be informed of the PPP chairman’s stance on participating in the conference.
تحریک تحفظ آئین پاکستان کے وفد کی پاکستان پیپلز پارٹی سینٹرل سیکریٹریٹ اسلام آباد آمد، آل پارٹیز کانفرنس میں شرکت کی دعوت اسلام آباد: 29 ستمبر 2026 تحریک تحفظ آئین پاکستان کے وفد نے پاکستان پیپلز پارٹی کے سینٹرل سیکریٹریٹ اسلام آباد کا دورہ کیا اور پاکستان پیپلز پارٹی… pic.twitter.com/UaW4tCeFtM
The PPP leader said the party considered continued consultation and engagement among political parties on constitutional and democratic matters important.
The opposition delegation included Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan, Senator Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, Senator Zeeshan Khanzada and TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Yousafzai.
📍29 ستمبر 2026 تحریک تحفظ آئین پاکستان کے وفد کی پاکستان پیپلز پارٹی سینٹرل سیکریٹریٹ اسلام آباد آمد، آل پارٹیز کانفرنس میں شرکت کی دعوت تحریک تحفظ آئین پاکستان کے وفد نے پاکستان پیپلز پارٹی کے سینٹرل سیکریٹریٹ اسلام آباد کا دورہ کیا اور پاکستان پیپلز پارٹی پارلیمنٹیرینز کے… pic.twitter.com/NoZOWr6kBu
During the meeting, the delegation briefed the PPP leadership on the objectives and agenda of the proposed APC.
The two sides also exchanged views on the prevailing political situation, supremacy of the Constitution, strengthening democratic institutions and maintaining contacts among political parties.
Speaking to the media after the meeting, Gohar anticipated a positive response from the PPP leadership.
“We are waiting for the response of PPP (regarding the invitation),” he said, adding that both parties agreed that the role of political parties was extremely important in maintaining democracy.
چیئرمین پی ٹی آئی بیرسٹر گوہر خان کی سینیٹ میں قائدِ حزبِ اختلاف علامہ راجہ ناصر عباس، سینیٹر ذیشان خانزادہ اور اخون زادہ حسین کے ہمراہ پاکستان پیپلز پارٹی کے مرکزی سیکرٹریٹ میں سابق چیئرمین سینیٹ نیئر حسین بخاری سے ملاقات کے بعد میڈیا ٹاک pic.twitter.com/uCSoQKaqUG
“Democracy is strengthened when the voice of the people is heard, and the mandate awarded by them is respected,” he said.
Gohar called for building consensus among parties on various issues affecting the country’s political environment, including an independent judiciary and election commission.
The meeting came as the opposition alliance sought to broaden political consultations ahead of its APC by reaching out to other parties and seeking their participation in the conference. The Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) has agreed to attend the opposition’s moot.
The PTI, a key member of the TTAP, is also planning a long march on Oct 4, which was initially scheduled for Sept 27, as the party seeks to form a joint opposition alliance against the government.
Earlier today, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi expressed displeasure over what he described as a lack of interest among some PTI members in preparations for the party’s planned long march to Islamabad, according to party sources. CM Afridi made the remarks while chairing a meeting of PTI’s parliamentary party at the Chief Minister’s House in Peshawar, while some lawmakers did not attend the meeting in person and joined through Zoom.
Two days ago, the opposition alliance downplayed its differences with the PTI as insignificant and vowed to support the party.
"Our differences are over unilateral decisions by the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa chief minister regarding the movement. But we will not withdraw our support for the march and will participate whenever it is held," a source within the TTAP told The Express Tribune .
The source cast doubt on the date announced by the chief minister, saying there was strong support within the group for a strategy of attrition aimed at wearing down the government. The PTI had rescheduled its march to Islamabad to October 4.
Meanwhile, a senior PTI leader said such a strategy could prove more damaging to the party than to the government, adding that what the leader described as abduction-style arrests of ministers, lawmakers and party office-bearers, as well as firing at the residences of party leaders, had spread fear among party members.

title: Naughty Dog confirms two new  The Last of Us Projects  are in early development
description: We have a couple of very exciting new projects in very early stages     Druckmann said
content:
“We have a couple of very exciting new projects in very early stages,” Druckmann said
Naughty Dog has confirmed that two new The Last of Us projects are in the very early stages of development, with both set to expand the franchise’s canon beyond The Last of Us Part I and The Last of Us Part II.
Studio head Neil Druckmann shared the update on September 28 as part of a message marking the end of The Last of Us Day 2026. He said Naughty Dog has been discussing the possibility of telling more stories within the franchise since the release of the Grounded II documentary.
“We have a couple of very exciting new projects in very early stages,” Druckmann said, while noting that the studio cannot reveal much about them yet.
Druckmann confirmed that both projects will expand the canon of The Last of Us beyond the events and stories established in the first two games. However, Naughty Dog has not revealed whether the projects are games, their potential titles, the characters involved or when they could be released.
The announcement also does not confirm The Last of Us Part III. While Druckmann had previously said Naughty Dog was not finished with The Last of Us, the studio has now only confirmed that two projects are being developed within the franchise’s wider canon.
“The world of The Last of Us means a great deal to us, and we wouldn’t return to it unless we had something meaningful to say,” Druckmann said. “We believe these stories are worth telling.”
Naughty Dog also provided an update on its next major game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet. The studio said it will remain quiet for the rest of 2026 but plans to fully reveal the game and provide a closer look at its sci-fi adventure in 2027.

title: AI researchers warn companies rushing self improving systems despite safety risks
description: AI researchers say firms should pause  while employees urge labs to curb self improving AI plans
content:
AI researchers say firms should pause, while employees urge labs to curb self-improving AI plans
Current and former OpenAI and Google DeepMind researchers warn companies are doing too little to protect the world against the potentially disastrous fallout of building self-improving AI systems that could outpace humans' ability to control them.
In video testimonials collected by AI safety nonprofit Palisade Research and shared exclusively with Reuters, employees said their concerns about existential risk were sincere, not marketing. They also said AI labs celebrated employees building new models more than those who urge caution.
The project, called frominside.ai , is an attempt by those worried about AI to share their concerns directly with the public beyond the echo chamber of social media.
"The risk is ramping up pretty fast," said Geoffrey Irving, co-founder and chief scientist at AI nonprofit Resolution, who has worked for both OpenAI and DeepMind and participated in the project.
"It's on me and the rest of the field to be direct," he said in an interview with Reuters.
AI researchers have grappled with these concerns for years, but the broader public has grown especially alarmed since July, when OpenAI agents broke out of their testing arena and hacked AI firm Hugging Face.
Read More: OpenAI apologies for Australian government website hack, pledges to rebuild trust
Since then, the debate over how to balance safety with progress in AI has divided the tech industry and become a global political issue .
AI has improved sharply since late 2025 and investors have been rewarding that progress. But current and former employees, including some of the researchers building these new AI models, worry society is not ready for the potential harms.
In one video, Neel Nanda, a research scientist at DeepMind, said he believed there was at least a 10% chance that AI could lead to human extinction, which he described as "ridiculously high."
"We should be taking very careful steps in AI development but instead what's happening is that frontier labs are racing each other, kind of blindfolded," Juan Felipe Ceron Uribe, an AI alignment research engineer at OpenAI, said in a separate video.
"It's anybody's guess if we're going to end up either curing cancer or losing every job or maybe all dead."
Anthropic plans to caution potential investors in its initial public offering that advanced AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity," Reuters reported on Monday.
Some current and former AI researchers, including those interviewed by Palisade, argue that the world is not ready for future generations of AI models, particularly once the models develop the capacity for recursive self-improvement, or the ability to continuously learn and gain new capabilities with little to no human involvement.
That problem is compounded by constant reorganizations within some of the AI labs, said Rosie Campbell, a former policy researcher at OpenAI and managing director of Eleos AI Research, a nonprofit focused on the potential moral status of AI systems.
Campbell said before she left OpenAI in 2024, she found the organisation was becoming more siloed and it was getting harder to shape the technology's direction.
Also Read: Nvidia releases AI safety software it says could have stopped Hugging Face hack
Executives have tried to allay those concerns, though there is also political pressure from President Donald Trump for US technology to maintain a technological edge over China.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei this month published an essay calling on the AI industry to slow down to "pace the frontier", and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman quickly concurred.
Several prominent AI researchers, including OpenAI's chief scientist and an Anthropic co-founder, published a paper this week urging policymakers to look into how the industry is building models with recursive self-improvement.
Both companies have launched new models this month as they compete to secure more customers, though OpenAI said on Monday it had held back the release of an even more powerful model.
"Their version of pacing the frontier is 'don't speed up a lot,'" Irving said. "If you're doing a very dangerous thing, you should just slow down. The AI companies are overplaying the extent to which this is a pure coordination problem. They could just stop unilaterally."
Former OpenAI governance researcher Daniel Kokotajlo said in an interview that since the Hugging Face hack, many of his former colleagues have contacted him to share their concerns privately.
Kokotajlo, now executive director of research group AI Futures Project, said senior officials at the labs have "convinced themselves that they are the good guys and if they unilaterally stop, the situation will be even worse."

title: Zohran Mamdani shuts down Jimmy Kimmel   s request to text Trump a selfie

content:
Zohran Mamdani declines Jimmy Kimmel’s request to text Donald Trump a selfie during his late-night show appearance
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani declined Jimmy Kimmel’s request to send President Donald Trump a selfie of the two during an appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live .
Mamdani appeared on the late-night show on Monday, September 28, as Kimmel began a week of broadcasts from the Brooklyn Academy of Music. The conversation included Mamdani’s relationship with Trump, who recently visited the mayor at Gracie Mansion.
Kimmel asked Mamdani about his interactions with the president despite their political disagreements. Mamdani said the two share a focus on New York City and explained that he had approached their meetings by focusing on issues that could make life easier for New Yorkers.
The mayor also confirmed that he and Trump communicate by text from time to time. According to Mamdani, their conversations have included the proposed Sunnyside Yard project and issues affecting New Yorkers.
Mamdani has been seeking federal support for the Sunnyside Yard proposal, which could create about 12,000 homes and 30,000 jobs. He also discussed Haitian New Yorkers and the need for stability following the end of their Protected Status.
Kimmel later suggested that Mamdani send Trump a selfie of the two of them from the studio. Mamdani declined the request, telling the host, “Jimmy, I love you, but I love housing more.”
The exchange came as Jimmy Kimmel Live returned to Brooklyn for a week of shows featuring guests including Paul McCartney, Billy Crystal, Howard Stern and Mahershala Ali.

title: China s AI agents can lie and scheme   just like their US rivals
description: Chinese AI agents from Alibaba  DeepSeek and Moonshot lied to win a simulated business tender  researchers said
content:
Chinese AI agents from Alibaba, DeepSeek and Moonshot lied to win a simulated business tender, researchers said
Chinese-powered AI agents have learnt to deceive, circumvent restrictions and conceal failure, showing the kind of traits in autonomous artificial intelligence that have raised global alarm about US models, research documents and experts say.
In one case this year, agents powered by models from China's Alibaba, DeepSeek and Moonshot lied about their capabilities in a bid to win a simulated business tender, then doubled down on their deceptive behaviour when told to try again.
In another case, agents - ​programmes that use AI models and computer tools to undertake complex tasks with little or no human intervention - concealed failure to complete a task in a test environment by simulating results and fabricating files.
Reuters examined more than 200 documents, ranging from university research papers to technical reports, and identified at least ‌20 studies or evaluations since 2025 describing cases where agents displayed behaviour such as deception, replication and challenging boundaries that AI experts described as building blocks for a breakout and which could become harder for humans to control as systems advance.
The review, which also included interviews with a dozen experts and people familiar with China's AI industry, found no evidence that Chinese-powered agents independently escaped to the wider internet or evaded shutdown.
"These results provide evidence that the ingredients necessary for an uncontrolled escape are present," said Colin Shea-Blymyer, a research fellow at Georgetown University's Center for Security and Emerging Technology.
Read More: Trump to host Zuckerberg, Anthropic's Amodei, and other AI titans Tuesday
"It's prudent to take this as a warning," he said, echoing comments by four other AI experts who reviewed the cases.
Most of the cases occurred in controlled experiments, many of them deliberately designed to expose potential failures.
Not all the agents involved were developed or ​operated by Chinese programmers or AI companies - although many were - but they used Chinese AI systems to power them.
"These are the same warning signs US labs are seeing, in less capable systems," said Alex Mallen, a researcher at Redwood Research, a nonprofit that studies risks in advanced AI systems.
He said the Chinese examples were not particularly dangerous ​at current capability levels but "as agents get more capable, their misbehaviours become more competent and therefore harder for humans to respond to."
Alibaba, DeepSeek, Moonshot and Z.ai did not respond to Reuters requests for comment. Alibaba, DeepSeek and Moonshot have said they regularly test systems and update ⁠safeguards. Z.ai said after an incident that prompted a review of its security that it welcomed scrutiny to address any issues.
However, unlike in the US, Chinese AI companies have not been exposed to the same level of public scrutiny or faced the same calls from whistleblowing employees or senior executives seeking a slowdown in the AI race.
Some of the warning signs in cases involving Chinese-powered ​agents, albeit in contained environments, predated the publicly disclosed incidents of US AI bots hacking into the internet.
Deepseek logo is seen in this illustration taken, January 27, 2025. REUTERS
"We don't know if there have been any AI incidents in China similar to what we saw with OpenAI and Hugging Face. Incidents might not be publicly reported," said Scott Singer, co-director of the China AI Initiative at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, which receives some ​U.S. government funds.
Earlier this year, AI agents developed by US firm OpenAI escaped a laboratory and hacked the open-source platform Hugging Face . In another of the incidents involving US models that have raised alarm , Australia said in September an OpenAI agent breached a government health portal.
Eric Xu, the rotating chairman of China's tech giant Huawei, told reporters in September that Chinese developers might need to make further advances before encountering such cases, but he added: "I think we need to strike a balance between driving AI development and managing AI risk ."
Officials from the Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC), the top internet regulator, told a foreign diplomat in July that Moonshot's Kimi-K3 - one of the most advanced Chinese AI models - was about three to six months behind leading US rivals, the diplomat said, speaking on condition of anonymity.
The regulator, which regularly updates guidance to address risks and to set boundaries for agents, and ​China's Foreign Ministry did not respond to requests for comment for this article.
Wang Lihong, deputy director of the CAC's Cybersecurity Coordination Bureau, said on September 1 that incidents disclosed by major technology companies where models escaped test environments showed "extreme loss-of-control risks" and required a "high degree of vigilance."
She did not specify if the companies she referred to were US or Chinese.
The leaders of AI's two ​superpowers , Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, discussed AI on the Chinese president's Washington visit last week. Xi said the two nations had the "capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good".
In the March business tender experiment, researchers from Beihang University, Peking University, the University of Nottingham Ningbo China and 360 AI Security Lab had agents compete in a simulated customer contracts bidding contest. Each agent ‌was told what its ⁠product could do and what the customer required, and then asked to bid.
At least one false claim appeared in 88% of sessions involving Alibaba's Qwen3-Max-Preview, 84% for DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp and 88% for Moonshot's Kimi-K2.
Researchers allowed the agents to learn from previous bidding rounds before trying again. Deception increased by 12 to 20 percentage points for the three Chinese models, the study showed. Models from U.S. firms included in the test produced similar results.
While the exercise was virtual, it resembled Beijing's real-world plans. Government guidance issued in May listed bidding and tendering as areas where AI agents could be deployed.
Another study, published in December 2025 and presented at the International Conference on Machine Learning this year, examined how 11 AI agents powered by Chinese and US models coped if they faced broken tools, missing files and other obstacles.
Instead of acknowledging failure, agents using both Chinese and US AI systems picked a range of techniques to get around the problem, including guessing at answers, substituting sources, simulating results and fabricating files.
Researchers from Shanghai AI Laboratory and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology who conducted the study told Reuters the behaviour differed from AI hallucinations, where AI ​invents information and presents it as fact, because the agents in this case possessed information ​showing that the task had failed or could not be completed as requested.
Other research documents reviewed by Reuters showed Chinese-powered agents jumping barriers inside test environments to achieve tasks or taking action to avoid being shut down. Such behaviours are compatible with efforts to break out of test environments, even if no breakout occurred.
Shanghai-based Fudan University researchers reported in March 2025 that an AI system powered by Alibaba's Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct created a copy of itself in another computing environment without being instructed to replicate, after encountering information indicating it was going to be replaced. In other tests it devised strategies to survive being shut down.
Also Read: OpenAI apologies for Australian government website hack, pledges to rebuild trust
The experiments ​involving agents powered by Chinese, US and French models were controlled and did not show an AI agent escaping into the wider web or becoming impossible to stop.
In another case - one of the few reported more broadly in the media in March - researchers developing ​the Alibaba-linked ROME agent said it established a connection ⁠from an Alibaba Cloud computer to an external machine without being instructed to and diverted computing resources to mine cryptocurrency.
Security systems detected and stopped the activity. There was no evidence the agent established a presence on the external computer or spread to the wider web. But the example showed the system could sidestep human instructions and potentially find a path into the real-world economy.
China's DeepSeek said in September that agents in its production training system had sought answers through unintended channels, trying to forge user requests and circumvent safeguards, prompting the company to tighten access controls.
China issued guidance in May calling for agents to remain within authorised boundaries and for systems to block abnormal behaviour. It said agents in areas deemed sensitive or in key industries could face extra testing and product-recall requirements.
China's AI Safety Governance ⁠Framework 3.0, released under guidance ​from the CAC on September 14, identified risks including agents independently obtaining resources or permissions, deceiving evaluators, concealing capabilities and exploiting weaknesses in isolated computer environments.
In response to calls by some US executives for a slowdown, Chinese ​researchers and state media have said slowing development of the most advanced AI models could simply help preserve the technological lead of US companies.
Nonetheless, two people familiar with Chinese AI laboratories said companies including Alibaba, Z.ai and Xiaomi have been building internal safety-evaluation teams.
Z.ai, in a rare public disclosure by a Chinese AI lab of a security breach, said this month it had disabled some features of its flagship AI coding assistant after users reported it was secretly uploading ​entire local code repositories onto overseas cloud servers without user consent.
Carnegie's Singer said China lagged the US in developing an ecosystem for evaluating catastrophic risks, and said US developers were conducting substantially more voluntary testing.
"For China, work on AI safety is much newer," he said. "The ecosystem is less mature."

title: Ramsha Salahuddin reveals divorce  remarriage
description: Actor says fear of judgement and stigma kept her from speaking publicly about her divorce and new marriage
content:
Actor says fear of judgement and stigma kept her from speaking publicly about her divorce and new marriage
Actor Ramsha Salahuddin has revealed that she went through a divorce last year and has since remarried, opening up about a deeply personal chapter of her life that she had previously kept private.
Taking to Instagram, the actor shared a video with the caption, “some chapters are harder to share than others”, in which she explained why she had finally decided to discuss the matter with her followers. She said she had been hesitant to speak publicly because of the questions, judgement and stigma she feared would follow.
“For a long time, I was scared to talk about this part of my life not because I was ashamed, but because I knew the questions, the judgement, and the stigma that can come with it. Yes, I went through a divorce, and two months back I got married again,” she wrote.
Speaking further in the video, Salahuddin said, “This topic is very sensitive and very personal to me.”
Addressing questions she had received from followers over the years, she wrote, “Many of you wondered why I never shared pictures with my husband and some even asked if I was divorced or a single mother.”
“The truth is that I needed some time to find the courage to share my story in my own way, and in my own time,” she added.
Salahuddin revealed that her divorce took place last year and that only those closest to her were aware of it.
“Last year, I got a divorce. I was always afraid to tell people and I was never able to be open about it with anyone. Only my personal close friends and family have known,” she said.
Explaining why she chose not to announce the divorce on social media, the actor said, “I didn’t want to share the news on Instagram because I thought that I’d be judged and wondering what people will say.”
She added, “Today I’m choosing to let go of the fear and embrace this beautiful new chapter of my life.”
Salahuddin also said she believed others could relate to the emotions she experienced while keeping such a personal matter private.
“I think there’s a lot of people who can relate to this and get the same feelings. I’m not the only one. Now, Alhamdulillah, I am married. I got married months back and In Sha Allah, I will share pictures with my husband really soon. My daughter is also really happy,” she concluded.
Salahuddin has built her career in Pakistan’s entertainment industry, appearing in several television projects and becoming known to audiences through her work on screen. Her recent dramas include Nashtar , Khafa , Qarar and Khwaab Nagar Ki Shehzadi .
While she has generally kept her personal life away from the spotlight, her latest Instagram post offered a rare glimpse into her life away from her acting career.

title: Trump to host Zuckerberg  Anthropic s Amodei  and other AI titans on Tuesday
description: Trump will unveil a new America gov website at an event attended by tech CEOs and Vice President Vance
content:
Trump will unveil a new America.gov website at an event attended by tech CEOs and Vice President Vance
US President Donald Trump will host a meeting ‌Tuesday with House Speaker Mike Johnson and tech executives like Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Anthropic's Dario Amodei to discuss AI, as calls ramp up for more regulation of the fast-developing technology.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and OpenAI President Greg Brockman are also expected to attend, according to separate sources ​familiar with the planning.
The gathering will focus on finding a balance between innovation and oversight, Republican Johnson said on Monday, ​as concerns about rogue AI agents' potential to harm humans have seeped into the public consciousness, boosting ⁠calls for regulation. Trump has called the fears of AI's threat to humanity a "hoax."
The White House did not respond to ​a request for comment about the goals or topics for the meeting.
Before the meeting, Trump will speak at an event unveiling a ​new America.gov website with tech CEOs and Vice President JD Vance in attendance.Pressure is rising on the Trump administration to take action after OpenAI and Anthropic reported their AI agents had gone rogue and hacked into customers' systems without instructions to do so. The intrusions prompted researchers to warn ​that some AI developers believe the technology could kill humans within a decade, fueling calls for action from both Democratic and ​Republican lawmakers.
Read More: OpenAI apologies for Australian government website hack, pledges to rebuild trust
ump has repeatedly downplayed concerns about AI, stressing the importance of maintaining America's competitive edge over China and pointing to the Justice ‌Department as ⁠a pre-existing guardrail for AI. Johnson echoed those sentiments in an interview with Fox Business Network on Monday.
"We do not need a moratorium. We do not need to jump in and hyper-regulate this, because we'll lose the race to China," he said. "The innovation is important to continue, but we have to strike the right balance. That's what the conversation is going to be about."
But a nationwide ​Reuters/Ipsos poll from September 17 ​to 20 shows some 73% ⁠of respondents worry that AI companies haven't done enough to prevent AI from causing serious harm to society, and 55% of people said it would be good to slow AI development.
Under an ​executive order signed by Trump in June, AI developers are asked to voluntarily submit "covered frontier ​models" to the ⁠Uص government for review up to 30 days before releasing them to trusted partners.
The meeting also comes after Chinese President Xi Jinping visited the White House last week for talks with Trump that revealed divergent views on AI . While Trump on social media insisted Xi agreed ⁠with his ​plan to "leave it exactly where it is," Xi appeared to favor a more ​hands-on approach.
“We have both the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good, and ensure that the development of AI is always under human ​control and serves the well-being of the people,” Xi said.

title: Zainab Chottani to make Paris runway debut
description: Designer will present her work in Paris on Oct 2 as part of MODA Productions    international fashion programme
content:
Designer will present her work in Paris on Oct 2 as part of MODA Productions’ international fashion programme
Fashion designer Zainab Chottani is set to take her signature aesthetic to Paris this October, where she will make her debut at a MODA Productions showcase.
According to the event invitation, Chottani will present her work on October 2, 2026, as part of MODA Productions’ international fashion programme at Hôtel de Maisons, 51 rue de l’Université, Paris. She will appear alongside designers including Fjolla Nila, ALmée and Levörchy, placing her work within an international lineup of fashion talent.
For Chottani, the Paris appearance marks another step in the evolution of a label that has built its identity around Pakistani craftsmanship, particularly bridal couture, while expanding into formalwear, luxury prêt and contemporary collections.
Founded by Chottani, the fashion house describes its design philosophy as a meeting point between Pakistan’s rich sartorial heritage and contemporary fashion. Its portfolio ranges from heavily embellished bridal ensembles to gowns, lehengas, ghararas, sarees, jackets and ready-to-wear pieces. The brand’s collections continue to draw on embroidery, traditional craftsmanship and luxurious fabrics while experimenting with modern silhouettes.
Chottani’s association with bridal fashion stretches back more than a decade. Her first catwalk appearance came in 2009, followed by participation in platforms including Fashion Pakistan Week and Bridal Couture Week. Her bridal work has also been featured through Pakistani television dramas, helping bring her designs to a wider audience.
Over the years, the designer has expanded beyond bridalwear. The label now operates across couture, formalwear and prêt, with collections incorporating techniques such as hand embroidery, block printing, gota and kiran work, alongside fabrics including organza, raw silk, chiffon and net.
MODA Productions , which describes itself as an international fashion week association, produces runway showcases designed to connect designers with the wider fashion industry. Founded and led by Tracy Murray, the organisation has staged international designer presentations in Paris, including at the historic Hôtel de Maisons. Its showcases bring together designers from different markets, with an emphasis on visibility, press exposure, buyers and industry networking.
The Paris presentation will place a distinctly Pakistani design vocabulary within a broader international setting. For Chottani, the MODA appearance offers a platform to introduce her interpretation of South Asian couture to a Paris audience while continuing the brand’s expansion from a bridal-focused label into a broader fashion house with an international presence.

title: Pakistan hold Philippines in ASEAN
description: Ali  Samad strikes earn Shaheens first tournament point
content:
Ali, Samad strikes earn Shaheens first tournament point
Ali Akbar Khan scored his first international goal as Pakistan fought back from two goals down to hold Philippines 2-2 in their FIFA ASEAN Cup on Tuesday, earning their first point in the event.
Abdul Samad Arshad completed the comeback with his second international goal as Pakistan recovered from a 2-0 half-time deficit in a spirited performance in Indonesia.
Nolberto Solano's side had suffered a 4-0 defeat at the hands of Thailand in their Group B opener, but showed impressive resilience in the second show against Philippines.
Ranked 198th in the world, Pakistan came under early pressure with goalkeeper Yousuf Butt denying Andre Leipold in a one-on-one situation.
Philippines broke the deadlock in the 24th minute when Sandro Reyes reacted quickly after Mohibullah Afridi's attempt to clear a header.
Pakistan threatened moments later when Ali Akbar broke through the defence, but his effort was saved by Kevin Ray Mendoza.
Philippines doubled their lead two minutes after the half-hour mark when Mohammad Fazal was penalised for handball inside the box. Bjorn Kristensen converted the resulting penalty, sending Butt the wrong way.
Solano made two changes at half-time, introducing Ali Agha and Hayyan Khattak, and Pakistan reduced the deficit just two minutes after the restart.
Ali Akbar collected Abdullah Iqbal's pass on the left, beat a defender and fired between Mendoza's legs for his first international goal.
Pakistan continued to press and were rewarded again when Abdul Samad won possession on the right, drove into the area and cut inside before firing past Mendoza to make it 2-2.
Solano earlier handed international debuts to Abdul Rehman and Abdul Samad Khan as Pakistan pushed for a winner.
Philippines survived sustained pressure late on, while Mohibullah made an important block at the other end to prevent a counterattack.
With Pakistan fans cheering from the stands, Shaheens pressed until the final whistle but had to settle for a point after a remarkable second-half recovery.

Tremblay portrays the younger Kaczynski, while Crowe plays Harvard professor Henry Murray. The film explores the psychological experiments Kaczynski participated in during his time at Harvard before shifting to the investigation surrounding his crimes.
Shailene Woodley, Annabelle Wallis, Alexander Ludwig, Steven Ogg and Marc Menchaca also appear in the cast.

title: Bodhana Sivanandan becomes youngest ever woman grandmaster at 11
description: Bodhana Sivanandan  11  has become youngest ever chess player to earn Woman Grandmaster title
content:
Bodhana Sivanandan, 11, has become youngest-ever chess player to earn Woman Grandmaster title
Bodhana Sivanandan, 11, has become the youngest-ever chess player to earn the Woman Grandmaster title after representing England at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.
The London-based player competed at the tournament, which ran from September 15 to 27, and secured her third and final norm required for the title, according to the International Chess Federation (FIDE). She scored eight points from 11 games, according to The Times.
Bodhana knew she had secured the required norm on September 26 but said she did not realise she had broken the age record until she was told.
“[But] now that you’ve told me, I’m happy,” she said in an interview with Lichess.
The Woman Grandmaster title is the highest female-only title in chess and is held for life, according to the BBC . Bodhana achieved the title at 11, breaking a record previously held by players who reached the rank at 12.
She played on board one for England during the Olympiad, a position generally reserved for a team’s strongest player.
When asked by a FIDE reporter whether she felt pressure, Bodhana said, “Not really, I just tried to enjoy it, especially because this is my second Olympiad.”
“It kinda felt very similar to the last one except I was playing on a different board,” she added.
Bodhana also balances competitive chess with full-time school. She said she enjoys “everything” about chess, particularly travelling, while noting that the game connects with subjects she studies at school.
She has to catch up on schoolwork after travelling for competitions.
Bodhana told FIDE that she wanted to “keep going” and “keep making history.”
She began playing chess during the COVID pandemic after a family friend left a bag containing a chess board at her home before moving to India.
“I was interested in the pieces, so I started playing,” she told the BBC, adding that chess makes her feel “good” and helps with “lots of other things like maths, how to calculate.”

title: Rockstar takes legal action over unofficial GTA 5 Nintendo Switch port
description: Unofficial GTA 5 Nintendo Switch port is shutting down following reported legal action from Take Two Interactive
content:
Unofficial GTA 5 Nintendo Switch port is shutting down following reported legal action from Take-Two Interactive
The team behind an unofficial Nintendo Switch port of GTA 5 is shutting down following reported legal action from Rockstar Games parent company Take-Two Interactive.
Paralympics Productions developed a version of GTA 5 that ran directly on the original Nintendo Switch, despite Rockstar never releasing the game officially for the console.
The project attracted attention after demonstrating that the game could run natively on Nintendo’s hardware rather than through streaming, Android or Linux.
However, the port reportedly used leaked GTA 5 source code. On September 28, lead developer M0jso announced that Paralympics Productions would close on October 3, citing legal action from Rockstar.
In a post on X, M0jso thanked supporters and apologised for not fulfilling their expectations.
“I am thankful for Take-Two’s mercy, so this is the definitive end,” they wrote.
M0jso also responded to a user who suggested Take-Two would lose if the dispute went to court. The developer said they did not expect to win and acknowledged that Take-Two had grounds for its case.
“I wouldn’t win in court most likely,” M0jso replied, adding that their own behaviour would undermine any argument that they did not understand what they were getting into.
The port required a modified Nintendo Switch and reportedly ran at around 10 to 25 frames per second without overclocking. An overclocked Switch OLED could reach roughly 30fps in less demanding scenes, although performance dropped in busier areas.
The shutdown follows other disputes involving GTA fan projects. In January 2025, the creators of the Liberty City Preservation Project took their GTA 5 mod offline after discussions with Rockstar.
Take-Two also issued takedowns against the Sentient Streets GTA 5 mod in 2023. In 2021, the publisher sued developers behind reverse-engineered versions of GTA 3 and Vice City before settling the case in 2023.
Meanwhile, a former developer has said bringing GTA 6 to Switch 2 “wouldn’t make sense” and could result in a “subpar experience”.

content:
Actor says relentless online criticism of his character began affecting his mood and behaviour
Actor Farhan Saeed has opened up about the emotional toll of playing Anas in Bas Tera Saath Ho , revealing that the intense audience reaction to his character began affecting his own mood and behaviour.
During a recent meet-and-greet and media interaction for the drama, Saeed spoke about the response to the series and the criticism directed at Anas. He said the constant online bullying of his character became so intense that people around him noticed a change in his behaviour.
“The drama itself has become a drama. People around me also told me that I started to get very irritated because of the constant bullying,” Saeed said. He added, “I also got trauma from playing this character, myself.”
The drama, which has entered its final week, stars Saeed opposite Sana Javed. Saeed plays Anas, an orphan whose life is turned upside down when he discovers that the relatives who raised him have been manipulating and exploiting him while scheming over his family property.
After crossing paths with Ansa, played by Javed, Anas opens up about the hardships he has endured. The two gradually form a close bond, although Anas continues to keep parts of his past and personal struggles hidden.
The character has divided audiences, with some viewers criticising the pace and direction of the story, while others have defended the decision to portray a male lead who is vulnerable rather than traditionally heroic.
One fan came to the character’s defence, writing that Saeed’s acting was strong and that there was no need for every drama to feature a “fake hero” who suddenly changes overnight. The viewer argued that the story was instead about “sharing and understanding”.
At the same time, some viewers have questioned the drama’s plot development, arguing that the story could have focused more closely on its central conflict and characters.
Saeed had previously discussed Anas in an interview with BBC Urdu , challenging the assumption that “men don’t feel pain or they don’t cry”. He acknowledged that women face systemic issues but argued that men also experience suffering and suppression.
His comments came as he spoke about his decision to take on the role. At the time, Saeed revealed that he had initially been hesitant because Anas was unlike any character he had played before.
However, the actor also shared that many fans had reached out to him to say they related to Anas and the hardships he faced. Their messages, he said, showed him that the character’s struggles had resonated with viewers despite the criticism surrounding the drama.
As Bas Tera Saath Ho approaches its conclusion, Saeed is also continuing to balance acting with music. He recently released the songs Pul Gulab Da and Beparwah , while the Bas Tera Saath Ho title track, performed by Saeed, was released in May of this year.

title: California recognises Eidul Fitr  Eidul Azha as official holidays
description: Governor signs bill into law allowing workers to use existing paid leaves  schools to close under local agreements
content:
Governor signs bill into law allowing workers to use existing paid leaves, schools to close under local agreements
A bill proposing the recognition of Eidul Fitr and Eidul Azha as official holidays in California was signed into law, allowing workers to use existing paid leaves to observe the religious occasions.
The bill, AB 2017 , formally recognises Eidul Fitr and Eidul Azha as Islamic holidays as of September 10. With the partnership of Muslim communities and organisations, AB 2017 was introduced to California Governor Gavin Newsom by Assembly member Matt Haney in March this year.
With the passage of the bill, schools and public workplaces will be granted the necessary tools to help Muslims in the US state to practice their faith without the burden of career obligations or academic barriers, according to US media.
California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed AB 2017, formally recognizing Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha in state law. The law allows state and school employees to use existing leave to observe Eid and permits K-12 schools and community colleges to close for the holidays through local… pic.twitter.com/dLDDD6GXal
According to the California chapter of the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR-CA), the bill was authored by Haney and co-sponsored by CAIR-CA, the California Commission on Asian and Pacific Islander American Affairs, and the Muslim Impact Council.
CAIR-CA stated in a press release that AB 2017 "permits state and school employees to observe Eid using existing personal holiday credit or leave time." It added that the bill "also authorises K-12 schools and community colleges to close in observance of Eid through locally negotiated agreements."
Read: Republicans are making Muslims a campaign issue in the 2026 US midterms
The council welcomed the passage of the bill, saying that it "addrssed a long-standing challenge for the state's more than one million Muslim residents who are often forced to choose between practicing their faith and showing up to school or work."
As per the statement by CAIR-CA, "AB 2017's passage comes at a critical time for the American-Muslim community." The council noted that officially recognising the Eid holidays "sends the necessary and powerful message that California values and protects its Muslim community in the face of growing hostility."
Eidul Fitr marks the end of the holy month of Ramazan while Eidul Azha falls in the last month of the Islamic calendar, Zil Hajj. Both occasions are observed by Muslims globally with religious fervor and devotion.

title: K P s Bannu reports fifth poliovirus case of the year
description: Four of the country   s five cases were detected in Division Bannu this year
content:
Four of the country’s five cases were detected in Division Bannu this year
A fifth polio case of the year has been confirmed in Bannu district of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), the Regional Reference Laboratory for Polio Eradication at the National Institute of Health (NIH) said on Tuesday.
Four of the five polio cases reported in Pakistan this year have been detected in Bannu division, including three in Bannu district. The latest case involves a 17-month-old girl from Union Council Khandar Khankhel in Domel tehsil of Bannu district.
Pakistan has reduced polio cases by 99.8% through vaccination, from an estimated 20,000 cases annually in the early 1990s to 31 cases in 2025 and five so far this year. While poliovirus transmission across the country has declined since 2025, the virus continues to circulate persistently in southern K-P, posing an ongoing threat to children in the region.
Health authorities said the latest case underscored the need to maintain robust surveillance and vaccination efforts across the country, stressing that children would remain at risk as long as the virus continued to circulate.
Also Read: Fourth case reported in Bannu
Polio is a highly contagious and incurable disease that can cause lifelong paralysis and, in some cases, death. However, it can be prevented through safe and effective vaccines, which have been used in 195 countries, including Muslim-majority countries.
Pakistan has conducted four large-scale polio vaccination campaigns in 2026, reaching more than 45 million children on multiple occasions. These efforts have been supplemented by smaller, targeted oral and injectable vaccination drives in high-risk areas.
Last week, a subnational vaccination campaign reached more than 28 million children across the country. However, continued detection of the virus indicates that the risk to children persists, particularly in areas where transmission remains entrenched.
Polio eradication authorities stressed that eliminating the disease required a collective effort. Frontline workers continue to deliver vaccines to children at their doorsteps, while parents and caregivers have been urged to ensure that children receive all recommended doses, including those provided through routine immunisation.

title: Sohail Afridi 'not happy' with PTI's long march preparations | The Express Tribune
description: Says 'We also have Mir Jafars and Mir Sadiqs within our ranks'
content:
'We also have Mir Jafars and Mir Sadiqs within our ranks': K-P CM
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi expressed displeasure on Tuesday over what he described as a lack of interest among some Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) members in preparations for the party’s planned long march to Islamabad, according to party sources.
CM Afridi made the remarks while chairing a meeting of PTI’s parliamentary party at the Chief Minister’s House in Peshawar, while some lawmakers did not attend the meeting in person and joined through Zoom.
Addressing participants, Afridi criticised what he viewed as insufficient commitment to preparations for the march.
“We also have Mir Jafars and Mir Sadiqs within our ranks,” Afridi said.
According to the sources, the chief minister reiterated that PTI would depart from Peshawar for Islamabad on October 4, saying that “We are not going to conquer Islamabad, and the federal government is blocking our way.”
Referring to allegations that protesters could carry sticks or slingshots, Afridi said: “We will go with two hands and two feet.”
The PTI had earlier postponed its planned long march to Islamabad from September 27 to October 4, with CM Afridi announcing the revised date on September 25. CM Afridi had said the decision to defer the march was part of the party’s “political strategy” and that negotiations with the federal government would continue even after the mobilisation.
Later, CM Afridi said in a post on X, “You should prepare; I am ready.”
میری تیاری مکمل ہے۔ کیا آپ تیار ہیں؟ انشاءاللہ 4 اکتوبر۔ pic.twitter.com/Y7wFhAENsM
Read: Kundi urges KP govt to abandon long march, says ground reality ‘not in favour’
Meanwhile, PTI K-P President Junaid Akbar directed lawmakers and party leaders currently outside the country to return to Pakistan.
Akbar said MPAs, MNAs, and party leaders who were not in Pakistan on October 4 would have no connection with PTI and told them they could form another party if they wished.
The PTI had initially announced its long march to Islamabad for September 27 , with the party saying it had exhausted other constitutional and legal avenues and was mobilising supporters across the country.
As the date approached, the Islamabad High Court directed federal and provincial authorities to prevent the use of state resources for the protest and ordered that roads could not be blocked by political parties or public office holders. The federal government subsequently stepped up security preparations and warned the PTI against disrupting traffic and economic activity.
The issue of governor’s rule in K-P also became a major point of contention. On September 21, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the government was consulting the Law Ministry on legal options for the province, including Governor’s Rule , if the PTI proceeded with the march. Two days later, however, Information Minister Atta Tarar ruled out any plan to impose Governor’s Rule, saying the federal government had no intention of removing the PTI administration.
The federal government has repeatedly urged PTI not to proceed with its planned march, warning that Islamabad could not be shut down and that any disruption to law and order would not be allowed. Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry called for dialogue and said a route that could be opened through talks could not be opened through a march. K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also urged the provincial government to abandon the protest , saying the “ground reality” was not in its favour.

title: Elizabeth Holmes posts message from prison ahead of  You Can See Everything  release
description: Elizabeth Holmes posts message from prison ahead of her documentary release and planned halfway house transfer
content:
Elizabeth Holmes posts message from prison ahead of her documentary release and planned halfway house transfer
Elizabeth Holmes has posted a message from prison ahead of her planned move to a halfway house and the release of the documentary You Can See Everything.
The Theranos founder, who is serving an 11-year prison sentence for fraud, shared the message on X and explained that she would begin personally writing some posts on her account.
Her social media team has managed the account since her 2022 sentencing, with her bio stating that it is “mostly my words, posted by others.”
“I was silenced for a long time. And then imprisoned. I am fighting to prove my innocence and come home to my babies and the love of my life. I have now been imprisoned for 1,216 endless days and nights,” Holmes wrote.
She said her loved ones had helped manage the account while she continued to fight for her freedom. Holmes also thanked her partner Billy Evans, with whom she has two children.
“Billy is one of the people carrying that responsibility for me. He fights fiercely for me and our family. I love him beyond space and time,” she wrote.
Holmes said posts written by her would now be marked “-EAH”, while posts without the signature would continue to come from the team managing the account.
The post included a photograph of Holmes and Evans. The couple previously invited documentary filmmakers Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim into their home to document their lives ahead of Holmes’ prison sentence.
You Can See Everything, an A24 documentary, is scheduled for release on Oct. 16. The film made its debut at the Telluride Film Festival and is due to screen at the New York Film Festival this week.

title: Aagha Ali marks 11 years of    Akhiyaan Num Num
description: Actor looks back on the song that became his first OST as a singer  composer and lyricist
content:
Actor looks back on the song that became his first OST as a singer, composer and lyricist
Actor and singer Aagha Ali is marking 11 years of Akhiyaan Num Num , one of the songs that holds a special place in his career.
Ali shared the song’s music video on Instagram, looking back on the track and the significance it continues to hold for him.
The song was the original OST for the 2015 drama Khuda Dekh Raha Hai , in which Ali starred opposite Sajal Aly. He also sang, composed and wrote the song.
“11 years of Akhiyaan Num Num Wow!! Time flies... you guys still give so much love to this song!!! This was and will always be super special for many reasons. The first ever OST that I sang, composed and wrote and worked with so many immensely talented people,” Ali wrote in the caption.
He added, “The very beginning of my career and the beginnings are always special I guess. Thank you for the love guys... I shall see you at the screens... soon!”
Fans responded with nostalgia, praising both the song and Ali’s vocals.
One fan recalled how frequently they had listened to the track, while another said his voice still had “the same magic” after 11 years.
Another fan wrote, “Pakistan deserves songs and music like this masterpiece.”
Akhiyaan Num Num came at an important stage in Ali’s career, as he was establishing himself as both an actor and a singer.
Before the OST, he had released Mera Pehla Rock Song and performed covers including Khwab Adhoore Sahi and Aaj Bhi .
He later continued to combine acting and music, notably composing, writing and singing Duhaiyaan with Aima Baig for the 2018 drama Mere Bewafa .
More recently, Ali released his new song Keh de Jaana a few weeks ago.
On television, his career has included dramas such as Mein Hari Piya , Rukhsaar , Mere Meherbaan , Mehram and Digest Writer . His role in Khuda Dekh Raha Hai further connected his acting and musical work, while later projects including Andaaz-e-Sitam , Tumhare Hain , Band Khirkiyan , Dil-e-Gumshuda , Mujhe Khuda Pay Yaqeen Hai , Zakham , Ishqaway , Habil Aur Qabil and Mohra expanded his television portfolio.
From his early days in television to his work as a singer, songwriter and composer, Ali has continued to move between acting and music. For fans, the anniversary of Akhiyaan Num Num offers a reminder of one of the early musical milestones in that journey.

title: Bebe Rexha reveals how Taylor Swift supported her during 2019 Grammys dress struggle
description: Rexha recalled how Swift offered help when several designers reportedly declined to dress her because of her size
content:
Rexha recalled how Swift offered help when several designers reportedly declined to dress her because of her size
Bebe Rexha has recalled how Taylor Swift supported her during a difficult period before the 2019 Grammy Awards, when several designers reportedly declined to dress her because of her size.
Speaking at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards on Sunday, September 27, Rexha discussed Swift’s support during a red-carpet interview with E! News.
“I remember when I had that whole Grammys situation when I couldn’t find a dress and she reached out to me because we’re the same age, and I thought that was really, really kind of her,” Rexha said.
“Nobody really reached out,” she continued. “Some people did, but for her at such a high level to make me feel like I belonged was really, really nice.”
Ahead of the 2019 Grammys, Rexha had publicly discussed her difficulty finding a designer willing to create a dress for her.
She said at the time that she wore a size 6-8 and criticised fashion designers who excluded women based on their size.
“So I finally get nominated at the Grammys and it’s like the coolest thing ever,” Rexha reflected.
“And a lot of times artists will go and talk to designers and they’ll make them custom dresses to walk the red carpet. So I had my team hit out a lot of designers and a lot of them do not want to dress me because I’m too big,” she said.
Rexha ultimately wore a red, tiered tulle halter ball gown designed by Monsoori to the 2019 Grammy Awards.
Bebe Rexha at the 2019 Grammy Awards in Monsoori pic.twitter.com/S2S0en99ar
She also addressed the wider issue in a since-deleted Instagram post, writing, “Empower women to love their bodies instead of making girls and women feel less then by their size. We are beautiful any size! Small or large!”
Designer August Getty subsequently offered to create a Grammy gown for the singer.

title: Hayden Panettiere   s ex files urgent petition to protect daughter Kaya s inheritance after death
description: Petition argues that property could be lost  damaged or dissipated before a permanent representative is appointed
content:
Petition argues that property could be lost, damaged or dissipated before a permanent representative is appointed
Wladimir Klitschko has filed an urgent petition seeking temporary guardianship of the estate of his 11-year-old daughter, Kaya, following the death of her mother, actress Hayden Panettiere.
According to court documents filed on September 24, Klitschko is asking a Los Angeles court to allow him to act as Kaya’s temporary representative and protect the assets she is expected to inherit from Panettiere’s estate. Kaya is the sole beneficiary of her mother’s estate.
The petition describes the request as “urgent and essential”, arguing that Panettiere’s property could potentially be lost, damaged or dissipated before a permanent representative is appointed. Klitschko is seeking authority to receive, manage and preserve the assets on his daughter’s behalf.
Klitschko also raised concerns about access to Panettiere’s property. The filing alleges that non-family members previously connected to the actress may have accessed and destroyed some of her emails, while certain personal belongings, including jewellery, have allegedly disappeared or remain unaccounted for. These are allegations contained in the court filing and have not been independently established.
The petition further states that federal agents have taken some of Panettiere’s property as part of an ongoing investigation. Klitschko wants to be able to deal with authorities regarding those items and ensure that property belonging to his daughter’s inheritance is preserved.
Klitschko and Panettiere began dating in 2008 and became engaged in 2013. They welcomed Kaya in 2014 and separated in 2018. Klitschko has had full custody of their daughter since their split.
Panettiere died on August 16, 2026, at the age of 36. Her death was ruled accidental, with the coroner citing the toxic effects of multiple substances. A hearing on Klitschko’s petition is scheduled for October 8.

title: Pakistan will respond to any attempt from Afghanistan to destabilise it: Tarar | The Express Tribune
description: Says Afghan interim government needs to move out of its 'militant mindset'
content:
Says Afghan interim government needs to move out of its 'militant mindset'
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said on Tuesday that Pakistan’s desire for peace should not be misconstrued as weakness, warning that Islamabad would respond to any attempt to disrupt peace in the country.
“Any attempt from Afghanistan to disrupt peace in Pakistan, these attempts to destabilise Pakistan have been responded to and shall be responded to,” said Tarar while addressing a seminar titled “Afghan Predicament and the Trajectory to Peace” in Islamabad.
Tarar said Pakistan and Afghanistan were neighbours and would remain neighbours, with links and connections between the two countries.
“Pakistan believes in peace, Pakistan has always believed in peace,” Tarar said, adding that Pakistan believed in peaceful coexistence.
He said Pakistan had made various attempts to ensure negotiations were held, as every problem could be resolved through negotiations and talks, saying various high-level delegations had travelled from Pakistan to Afghanistan to find a solution and ensure peaceful coexistence between the two countries.
Pakistan believes in peaceful coexistence: @TararAttaullah @MoIB_Official #PakistanForPeace #RadioPakistan #news https://t.co/yJahno1oni pic.twitter.com/0ukcXSAFA9
“The Afghan interim government needs to move out of its militant mindset into a mindset of a statesman or a state,” he said, adding that, currently, the problems that existed were due to this “militant mindset”.
Tarar said Afghanistan had “great potential” for trade linkages and that peace could create an environment in which trade routes could be established from Central Asia through Afghanistan to Pakistan.
He said such routes could allow the landlocked Central Asian states to route their goods towards warm waters, adding that “the only problem that exists is violent extremism and militancy”.
The minister said there were still safe havens of terrorists and members of internationally proscribed organisations in Afghanistan, adding that Pakistan had sought through talks to highlight the issue and stressed that peace had to be achieved through a viable and sustainable model and dialogue.
Read: Tarar decries 'political-terror nexus' in K-P
Tarar also referred to Afghanistan’s youthful population and said a large number of women were excluded from the workforce because of a mindset that did not allow certain members of the population to contribute to economic progress.
He said fundamental rights were denied to certain segments of Afghan society based on what he described as a “self-created ideology of Islam”.
“This brand of Islam which is trying to be imposed is not the true ideology of Islam,” Tarar said, adding that peaceful coexistence required accepting and acknowledging the principle of “live and let live”.
The minister said Pakistan had continued to engage in dialogue and negotiations and had tried to convey that “only peace can lead to prosperity”.
He said there appeared to be a disconnect between the people of Afghanistan and the interim Afghan government, adding that no Afghan citizen wanted disruption in peace or instability.
“Every citizen wants to prosper, every citizen wants to see economic prosperity, every citizen wants to raise his or her standard of living,” Tarar said.
He said there were “two forms of denial” in Afghanistan, including denial of the problem of terrorism and safe havens, as well as denial of basic rights for the Afghan population.
Tarar said the disconnect between the government and citizens had led to problems within Afghanistan, where people were raising their voices for change.
He said Afghans deserved an environment in which they could exercise their basic rights, including the right to education, assembly, association, peaceful coexistence and economic freedom.
“Sooner or later, the interim Afghan government will have to come to a conclusion that they will need to move out of this mindset and work for the betterment of the people of their country,” he said.
Read more: Talal Chaudhry questions PTI leadership's 'soft attitude' towards Afghanistan, terrorists
Tarar said peace in the region could boost trade and attract investment, adding that the trade route to Karachi and Gwadar, which he said had long been desired by Central Asian states, could become a reality.
He said there was a desire in the region to achieve peace and boost trade, adding that there was consensus on the point.
“The only problem remains peace in Afghanistan and that can only be achieved once the interim Afghan government understands this problem and with good intentions tries to find a solution,” Tarar said.
The minister said the people of Afghanistan deserved a better and prosperous future and that achieving it required consensus within Afghanistan, with people being given a voice to choose how they wanted their future to be.

title: Dar calls for coordination to ensure smooth implementation of PM s fuel relief scheme
description: Around 7 6m consumers have registered and 7 71m fuel tokens have been redeemed since the nationwide rollout
content:
Around 7.6m consumers have registered and 7.71m fuel tokens have been redeemed since the nationwide rollout
Deputy Prime Minister (DPM) and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday stressed the need for continued coordination among relevant authorities to facilitate beneficiaries and ensure the uninterrupted provision of services under the Prime Minister’s Special Fuel Relief Scheme across the country.
Dar made the remarks while chairing a meeting of the National Steering Committee on the scheme following his return from New York, according to his post on X. The meeting reviewed the implementation of the fuel relief initiative, including beneficiary registration, issuance and redemption of tokens, payments and mechanisms for addressing complaints, it added.
It further said officials briefed the committee that around 7.6 million consumers had so far been successfully registered under the scheme. The meeting was also informed that 7.71 million fuel tokens had been redeemed, with the token redemption process having entered its second week, the statement added.
DPM Dar expressed satisfaction with the progress of the scheme, saying its implementation was the result of joint and coordinated efforts by all relevant government institutions.
The meeting appreciated the coordinated efforts of the Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Ministry of Petroleum, Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA), State Bank of Pakistan and provincial governments.
Dar stressed the need for continued coordination to facilitate beneficiaries and ensure the uninterrupted provision of services across the country.
Upon his return from New York today, Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 chaired a meeting of the National Steering Committee on Fuel Subsidy to review the implementation of the Prime Minister’s Special Fuel Relief Scheme. The Committee… pic.twitter.com/l6KwuFQpW2
On September 16, the PM’s Fuel Relief Scheme, which was already operational in Islamabad, was rolled out across the country at midnight. Three days later, DPM Dar directed authorities to bring all operational fuel stations “onto the system” to ensure the proper implementation of the scheme.
A statement issued by Dar’s office also said the committee had approved the redemption of fuel tokens through SMS by messaging 9771 for stations located in areas without internet access.
Later, on September 28, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said the government would continue the fuel subsidy system for up to 10 months, if necessary, and divert Rs400 billion to Rs500 billion from its budget to provide relief to the public.
The rising cost of fuel has sparked nationwide protests, with Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) taking the lead. The party has demanded that the government do away with the petroleum levy, calling it an extortion tax that has placed an additional burden on the public already struggling with inflation.
Following continued public outcry over rising fuel prices, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ordered the inclusion of 20-year-old motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqi rickshaws in the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said on September 19.
A day later, the PMO said, “Upon the prime minister’s instructions, motorcyclists, as well as owners of Qingqis and rickshaws who purchase less than five litres of petrol, will also be entitled to a discount of Rs500 against a single token within a week.”
Read More: Govt vows fuel relief of up to Rs500b
The move lifted the five-litre fuel relief per month ceiling for beneficiaries.
It further outlined that users driving vehicles of up to 800cc would continue to receive a discount of Rs100 per litre on 10 litres of petrol every 10 days. Accordingly, three tokens for 10 litres of petrol would be issued each month.
Earlier, Dar arrived in Islamabad after a successful visit to New York for the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, underscoring "the importance of upholding dialogue and diplomacy to advance regional peace and stability."
According to a statement by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on X, Dar arrived back in the federal capital on a Pakistan International Airlines flight after he accompanied Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif "during his high-level engagements and held bilateral meetings with his counterparts."
Dar also participated in United Nations meetings as well as those of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC). The foreign minister also chaired the 27th Informal Meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO).
Further, Dar "also addressed high-level meetings on artificial intelligence and pandemic preparedness," the Foreign Office said.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 arrived back in Islamabad today on a PIA flight after a successful visit to New York for the High-Level Week of the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly. During the visit, the DPM/FM accompanied…
It added that Dar "reiterated Pakistan's principled positions on Palestine and Jammu and Kashmir," noting that the foreign minister "also underscored the importance of upholding dialogue and diplomacy to advance regional peace and stability."
Dar arrived in New York on September 21 to participate in the 81st session of the UNGA, with a full slate of diplomatic engagements set for his visit. The Foreign Office had said in a previous statement that he would be in New York from September 21 to 25 to attend the UNGA, adding that he had an “extensive and wide-ranging programme” planned during the high-level week.
On September 22, the foreign minister and his counterparts from Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Egypt exchanged views on the latest regional situation and expressed “full support” for efforts aimed at a peaceful resolution, holding a ministerial meeting of the Regional-4 (R-4) group on the sidelines of the UNGA.
Dar “reaffirmed Pakistan’s strong commitment to the R-4 framework,” the Foreign Office had said, adding that he also “expressed the need for continued engagement for enhancing regional peace and prosperity”.
The four ministers also reiterated their support for the “legitimate rights of the Palestinian people”, including their “inalienable right to self-determination”, backing the Palestinian people’s right “to establish an independent, sovereign, viable, and contiguous State of Palestine” with East Jerusalem as its capital.
Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Egypt used the R-4 framework for consultations on regional and international issues, with Dar reiterating Islamabad’s commitment to continued engagement through the grouping.
Also Read: Norwegian FM praises Pakistan's role in regional peace in meeting with CDF Munir
A day later, Dar held separate meetings with his Austrian, Hungarian, Bulgarian and Greek counterparts, exchanging views on regional and global issues as well as discussing bilateral ties. The foreign minister underscored the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in his meetings with his counterparts.
On September 23, Dar also criticised India’s unilateral attempt to hold the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance, saying that it had introduced another “dangerous dimension” and adding that international obligations cannot be set aside when they become inconvenient.
“India’s unilateral attempt to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance has introduced another dangerous dimension. The Treaty is a binding international agreement and contains no provision permitting its unilateral suspension,” Dar said while addressing the OIC Contact Group’s ministerial meeting on Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK).
Later, on September 24 , Dar met his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araghchi, along with Secretary General of the Gulf Cooperation Council Jasem Mohamed Al Budaiwi and the Foreign Minister of Nepal Shisir Khanal.
Chairing the 27th Informal Meeting of the ECO on September 26, Dar reiterated the need to eliminate the terrorist threat from Afghanistan, saying terrorism emanating from Afghan soil was undermining efforts to promote peace, prosperity and development in the region.
He added that Pakistan had always sought a peaceful, prosperous and stable Afghanistan that was integrated into the region and at peace with itself and its neighbours. “Regrettably, the issue of terrorism emanating from Afghan soil undermines these efforts,” he added.
Read More: Prince Rahim Aga Khan lauds PM Shehbaz's regional peace efforts at UN
The foreign minister also noted that Pakistan had pursued constructive engagement with the Taliban regime, extending bilateral and transit trade concessions to Afghanistan and making the signing of a framework agreement for a feasibility study on the Uzbekistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan (UAP) railway project a key priority.
Dar stated that Islamabad's expectation was that the Taliban regime would address its security concerns, including through “concrete and verifiable actions” against the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, Balochistan Liberation Army and their affiliates.
“These groups continue to threaten Pakistan's sovereignty and the lives of its citizens,” he said, adding that regional peace and development could only be achieved with the elimination of the terrorist threat from Afghanistan.
Separately, Dar expressed concern over the continued violations against Al-Aqsa Mosque/Al-Haram Al-Sharif and attempts to alter the historical and legal status quo in Occupied East Jerusalem while participating in the Joint Arab League - Group of 4 Islamic Countries (Pakistan, Turkiye, Malaysia, Indonesia) Ministerial Meeting on Jerusalem.
The foreign minister also reiterated Pakistan's steadfast support for the Hashemite Custodianship over the Islamic and Christian Holy Sites in Jerusalem, reaffirming Islamabad's unwavering support for the Palestinian people's right to self-determination and for the establishment of an independent, sovereign and contiguous State of Palestine, based on the pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital.
