title: New UN secretary general should be competent  impartial  upright  China
description: Seven candidates remain in race for UN chief  with the successful candidate set to take office in 2027
content:
Seven candidates remain in race for UN chief, with the successful candidate set to take office in 2027
China said on Monday that the next UN secretary-general should be “competent, impartial and upright” and uphold the UN Charter.
“The election of the UN secretary-general bears on the reform and development of the UN and the vital interests of member states,” Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told reporters in Beijing .
He was responding to questions about the ongoing selection process and whether Beijing could say which candidate it was supporting.
Guo was also asked about media reports that Beijing was weighing whether to support Rebeca Grynspan, Costa Rican economist who heads UN Trade and Development, or Carolyn Rodrigues Birkett, Guyana’s ambassador to the UN.
The process to select the next UN chief is underway, with the successful candidate set to take office on Jan. 1, 2027. Seven candidates remain in the race.
Read More: Six big takeaways from a turbulent week of UN diplomacy
“China supports this election of the new secretary general, in accordance with the provisions of the UN Charter, one (who) observes the UN Charter, abides by the UN Charter, has outstanding competence, is impartial, and upright (and) fulfils responsibility with dedication,” said Guo.
He said China “will work with all relevant parties to participate in the secretary-general election process in a responsible manner”.

Olara Otunnu, Rafael Grossi, Macky Sall, Maria Fernanda Espinosa and Ivonne A-Baki are also in the race.

title: Trump and Xi s  stalemate  summit was a glitzy gift to China
description: US  China agree to lower tariffs on  60 billion of non sensitive goods  delay wider trade deal to 2027
content:
US, China agree to lower tariffs on $60 billion of non-sensitive goods, delay wider trade deal to 2027
President Donald Trump hoped his pomp-filled summit with Xi Jinping in Washington last week would showcase the strength of his personal relationship with the Chinese ​leader.
Instead, the limited outcomes showed just how far apart Washington and Beijing remain on key issues, and reinforced a view among analysts that Xi sees little reason to grant ‌Trump major political victories ahead of November's midterm elections.
"The US-China relationship has settled into a managed stalemate," said Craig Singleton, senior director for China at US-based think tank, the Foundation for Defence of Democracies.
"The elaborate pageantry matters precisely because there is still relatively little substantive progress to showcase."
Both sides said they reached consensus on lowering tariffs on a $60 billion batch of non-sensitive goods, but they set no timeline for adoption. At the same time, a deadline for a broader trade accord ​was pushed into next year.
The absence of a Chinese CEO delegation accompanying Xi also highlighted the challenges of overcoming US suspicion of Chinese investment, casting doubt on the viability of a ​two-way investment scheme the leaders unveiled at a Beijing summit in May, analysts said.
"The Trump-Xi summit created a positive political atmosphere but did nothing to ⁠narrow differences, or reduce mutual suspicions," said Drew Thompson, a senior fellow at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies in Singapore.
White House officials had tempered expectations before the summit, pointing ​out that the leaders would also meet at international forums in Shenzhen and Miami before year end.
But while the uneventful meeting capped off a diplomatic week that exposed the limits of Trump's powers, Joe Mazur, geopolitics ​analyst at Beijing-based consultancy Trivium, said it served as a "PR win" for China.
From the outset, Trump went out of his way to fete Xi — the leader of a country he has previously said is "killing America" with unfair trade practices.
He broke protocol to greet him at the airport, the first time a US president has done so for a world leader in 11 years.
Later, addressing a coterie of top government officials and tech magnates assembled for a lavish state ​banquet in his honour, Trump said they "had never gotten along better".
"The extraordinary courtesy the Americans extended to Xi Jinping met and far exceeded China's expectations," said Shen Weizhong, a former Chinese foreign ministry official ​and vice president of Beijing-based think tank Global Governance Institution.
"The Chinese do not feel that a visit necessarily has to result in a specific number of agreements, or in tariff reductions or other such outcomes ... The mere fact ‌that they meet, ⁠nod to one another and shake hands speaks volumes."
Xi is also in no rush to make concessions, analysts say.
Read More: China, US agree tariff cuts on $60 billion of goods including agriculture, household items
China's dominance in production of rare earths, minerals critical for sectors from tech to autos and defence, gives it a powerful source of leverage, while its trade with the world has surged despite Trump's tariff threats.
Trump did not come away completely empty-handed, however.
China has proposed cutting tariffs on a range of US agricultural goods, from corn to dairy, a commerce ministry list showed on Monday. In return, the US will reduce levies on Chinese imports such as toys, fireworks and Christmas ornaments.
That will be welcome news for American ​farmers, who form one of Trump's key voting blocs, ​ahead of midterm elections that look challenging ⁠for his Republican party.
But commodity analysts were also quick to add that soybeans, one of the US' largest exports, did not feature on China's list, leaving those purchases potentially hostage to any deterioration in ties.
China also gave little indication it is willing to help Trump end the war in Iran ​that has dragged the US president's approval rating to the lowest in his political career.
Shortly after Xi's departure, Chinese Vice President Han Zheng pushed back ​against the US on ⁠Iran and its threats against Cuba at a UN General Assembly meeting in New York.
The Chinese leader also did not shy away from pressing Trump on thornier topics such as US support for Taiwan, the democratically ruled island claimed by Beijing.
Trump avoided the subject in his public comments, in stark contrast to the May summit, at which he called a pending $14-billion package of arms sales to Taiwan a "negotiating chip" with Beijing.
Washington has cast the busy ⁠summit schedule with ​Xi as important to keeping ties on even keel between the world's two biggest economies.
But frequent interactions of the leaders ​also buy Beijing time on unwanted US actions such as the arms sales to Taiwan, said Jeremy Chan, a senior analyst at political risk consultancy Eurasia Group.
"That's a major strategic win for the Chinese and a major loss for Taiwan and a lot ​of US allies and partners in the region," said Chan, a former US diplomat in China.

title: Six terrorists killed in separate K-P, Balochistan operations: security sources | The Express Tribune
description: Interior Minister Naqvi praises security forces for the successful operation against terrorists in Dera Ismail Khan
content:
Interior Minister Naqvi praises security forces for the successful operation against terrorists in Dera Ismail Khan
Security forces killed six terrorists in two separate operations in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, state media reported on Monday, citing security sources.
According to the sources, four terrorists belonging to the Indian-backed proxy group “ Fitna al-Khawarij ” were killed during an intelligence-based operation in K-P’s Dera Ismail Khan district.
The sources said security forces closely monitored the terrorists’ movements before targeting them during the operation, while a large cache of weapons and ammunition, along with Afghan currency, was also recovered.
The operation was carried out under the government’s Azm-e-Istehkam counterterrorism framework.
Security officials said counterterrorism operations would continue as part of efforts to dismantle terrorist networks and establish lasting peace in the country.
Security forces have killed four terrorists during an intelligence-based operation in Dera Ismail Khan @OfficialDGISPR @PakistanFauj #RadioPakistan #News https://t.co/FeTW9cwmjC pic.twitter.com/8FihcLvV5D
In a separate operation in Balochistan’s Nokcha area, security forces killed two terrorists belonging to the banned Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) during a chase after an empty water bowser was set on fire, according to security sources.
The sources said the two men torched the vehicle before attempting to flee. Security forces launched an immediate chase, and both were killed during an ensuing exchange of fire.
The sources identified the two men as BLA members and said they had previously been involved in arson attacks at different locations along the N-40 Quetta-Taftan highway.
The incident came less than a month after a major security operation along the N-40 highway on August 31.
Read More: 49 terrorists killed in Balochistan, K-P IBOs
Security sources said at the time that 11 terrorists were killed after armed men set up what they described as an illegal checkpoint on the N-40 Quetta-Taftan highway in Chagai district in an attempt to disrupt traffic and extort commuters.
The sources said investigators were examining possible links between previous incidents along the N-40 highway and the latest case, particularly attacks involving the torching of vehicles.
Security has been tightened in Nokcha following the latest incident. Security sources said operations against sabotage and terrorist activity were continuing in the area, while investigations were also underway into the latest incident and the alleged involvement of those killed in similar attacks.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi praised the security forces for the successful operation against terrorists in Dera Ismail Khan.
“The security forces have foiled the nefarious designs of Indian-sponsored terrorists. Under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision, indiscriminate operations against terrorists in K-P are continuing and will continue,” he added.
Naqvi said that the entire nation stood with the security forces in the fight to eliminate the menace of terrorism.
Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terrorist activity over the past three months, with a series of attacks across the country resulting in the martyrdom of security personnel and civilians.
Last week, 12 people were killed and 35 others injured when a blast struck a joint checkpoint near Aman Mela in the Darazinda area of Dera Ismail Khan, with the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) claiming responsibility for the attack.
On September 19, 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred in a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, the Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
Also Read : Nine policemen martyred, 28 injured in terror attack on police checkpost in K-P's Hangu
In a separate incident, a captain and a lieutenant were among six security personnel martyred in an exchange of fire in Hangu district, while eight terrorists were killed.
On September 1, six personnel, including two officers, and a customs department official were martyred as security forces thwarted an attempt to breach the Customs House in Balochistan.
In July, at least 30 people , including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. The attackers also abducted several civilians and police personnel after the assault.
In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation , which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

title: Arshad falters again as Sri Lanka   s Pathirage strikes gold
description: Olympic champion settles for fourth as Pathirage seals Asian Games title
content:
Olympic champion settles for fourth as Pathirage seals Asian Games title
Pakistan’s Olympic champion Arshad Nadeem endured another disappointing outing on Monday, finishing fourth in the men’s javelin at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya, while Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage produced a late surge to claim gold.
Arshad, who won Olympic gold in Paris with a record 92.97 metre throw, struggled to find his rhythm throughout the competition. He opened with 76.69 metres, fouled his second attempt and managed 80.29 metres on his third before fouling each of his final three throws.
Sri Lanka’s Pathirage left his best until last, launching the javelin 88.55 metres with his sixth and final attempt to secure the gold medal.
He had also occupied the summit position with 88.33m which he managed in his fourth attempt.
India’s Yashvir Singh took silver with a personal-best 85.72 metres, while compatriot Rohit Yadav claimed bronze with 84.35 metres.
The result adds to a difficult period for Arshad, whose performances have dipped since his landmark Olympic triumph in Paris. He has also struggled at recent major competitions, including the Glasgow Commonwealth Games and the World Ultimate Championship in Hungary.
Pathirage, meanwhile, continued an impressive run of form. The Sri Lankan has now collected three major gold medals in recent months, having also triumphed at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games and the World Ultimate Championship. He previously won a Diamond League title.
His personal best of 92.62 metres is just 35 centimetres short of Arshad’s Olympic record.
Pakistan’s Yasir Sultan also failed to reach the final eight after managing a best throw of 73.50 metres. His series read X, 73.50 and 73.47.
Yasir, who recorded a personal best of 79.93 metres at the 2023 Asian Championships in Bangkok, has struggled to reproduce that form at major competitions in recent years.
Japan’s Yuta Sakiyama retired hurt during his fourth attempt.
India’s Olympic and world champion Neeraj Chopra did not compete in Nagoya because of injury.

title: Armani unveils shimmering collection in pursuit of  evolution
description: Giorgio Armani   s  Evolution  blends signature tailoring with shimmer as the brand adapts after founder   s death
content:
Giorgio Armani’s 'Evolution' blends signature tailoring with shimmer as the brand adapts after founder’s death
Giorgio Armani presented a womenswear collection on Sunday that combined its trademark tailoring with shimmering fabrics, ​as the Italian luxury group navigates a transition period ‌a year after the death of its founder.
Titled "Evolution", the new collection by Silvana Armani – the late designer's niece – featured a palette ​of ivory, black and gold and showcased eighties-inspired sharp-shoulder ​jackets with knee-length trousers, bold geometries and body-skimming ⁠evening gowns.
Models present creations from Giorgio Armani Spring/Summer 2027 womenswear collection during Milan Fashion Week, in Milan, Italy, September 27, 2026. Photo: Reuters
"Style is a way of being, rather than ​an immutable code: the ability to change while remaining true ​to oneself," the group said in notes to accompany its runway show at Teatro Armani, one of the group's headquarters buildings in ​Milan.
Noting that "identity can evolve", it added that the butterflies featured ​on brooches and necklaces symbolised metamorphosis.
Speaking to reporters after the show, Silvana ‌Armani ⁠reaffirmed she was committed to continuity with the brand's aesthetic while allowing room for an "evolution", pointing to the introduction of cotton as an example of change.
The Italian fashion house ​is entering ​a pivotal period as ⁠the clock starts ticking on plans to sell an initial 15% stake to outside ​investors.
Designer Silvana Armani appears during Giorgio Armani Spring/Summer 2027 womenswear collection presentation as part of the Milan Fashion Week, in Milan, Italy, September 27, 2026. Photo: Reuters
CEO Giuseppe Marsocci said the group was open ​to multiple ⁠investors in the share sale, adding that no decision had been made.
Earlier this month, the group named Dario Vitale creative director ⁠of ​Emporio Armani and Giorgio Armani accessories, ​marking the first time someone from outside the Armani family has taken ​on that role.

title: PTI calls for justice as Imran   s sisters remain in detention denied of  fundamental rights
description: Salman Akram Raja seeks justification for the cruel treatment being meted out to the PTI founder s sisters
content:
Salman Akram Raja seeks justification for the cruel treatment being meted out to the PTI founder's sisters
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf Secretary General Salman Akram Raja on Monday questioned the detention of party founder Imran Khan’s sisters, saying they were being deprived of fundamental rights without any specific charges and urged courts to order their immediate release.
Imran's three sisters were detained under Section 3 (Power to arrest and detain suspected persons) of the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance 1960 in Lahore ahead of the party’s planned September 27 march towards Islamabad. Aleema was taken into custody on September 20 , while Uzma and Noreen were detained a day later. Authorities issued 30-day detention orders, citing concerns related to public order. On September 21, PTI challenged the detentions in the Lahore High Court (LHC).
Talking to the media outside the LHC today, Raja said Aleema had been in custody for nine days and questioned the legal basis of her detention. He said the arrests were made “based on an apprehension”.
“What is the justification for the cruel treatment being meted out to Imran's sisters?” Raja asked, adding that detentions under the MPO were based on apprehensions rather than formal charges.
The PTI leader further argued that restricting access to family members and lawyers, as well as food and medicines, did not have any justification under the Constitution and law.
Read: LHC declines stay on Imran sisters' detention
Speaking to the media, Raja further stated that excessive force was used during the arrests, claiming that more than 100 police officials entered the residence and broke doors during the arrests.
He asserted that such actions crossed “all limits of brutality and authoritarianism”.
“We have repeatedly presented these incidents before the court. Despite this, nine days have passed. Even if they are released afterwards, would that still be called justice?”
Raja said the party had approached the courts and urged them to order immediate relief.
The party earlier expressed "grave concern over the rumours and news circulating regarding the well-being" of Imran's sisters.
It said that since their arrest, they had not been granted access to their family members and lawyers.
"This situation is not only extremely alarming but also raises serious questions regarding their fundamental rights. PTI demands that without any further delay, access to the prison be granted to their family and lawyers, their medical needs be fulfilled, and all concerns regarding their health and safety be addressed."
پریس ریلیز: پاکستان تحریک انصاف نے کوٹ لکھپت جیل لاہور میں قید عمران خان کی بہنوں کی خیریت کے حوالے سے گردش کرنے والی افواہوں اور خبروں پر شدید تشویش کا اظہار کیا ہے۔ پی ٹی آئی کا کہنا ہے کہ عمران خان کی بہنوں کو گرفتاری کے بعد سے ان کے اہلِ خانہ اور وکلا تک رسائی نہیں دی جا…
The order passed on September 20 stated that the Lahore police chief forwarded a request based on reports submitted by the Civil Lines Division superintendent of police and the in-charge District Intelligence Branch that claimed that Aleema and Ameer (her driver) had been involved in the May 9 protests and road blockades which motivated workers to damage public and government property. The police and intelligence reports further stated that the two were again mobilising workers through social media and public meetings, potentially creating a law and order situation.
The reports also accused them of raising what the order described as “objectionable slogans” against the government and institutions in an attempt to provoke or incite members of the public. Multiple cases, including FIR No. 96/23 registered at Race Course Police Station, were cited in support of the request for detention.
The matter was later placed before the District Intelligence Committee at a meeting held on September 20, chaired by Lahore Deputy Commissioner Muhammad Ali Ijaz.

According to the order, the committee discussed the matter and endorsed the evidence provided by the police department before unanimously recommending detention of both individuals to maintain the law and order situation in the city.
Similarly, Uzma and Noreen were detained for 30 days under the same law, a day after their sister Aleema Khan was detained.
The Lahore deputy commissioner’s orders cited police reports alleging that the two women’s activities were “prejudicial to the public safety and maintenance of public order” and linked them to the May 9, 2023 protests and road blockades. The orders also said multiple cases had been registered against them.

title: Taylor Swift makes VMAs history and dedicates award to Dolly Parton
description: Swift took home three awards  bringing her career total to an unmatched 33  previously    tied with Beyonce at 30
content:
Swift took home three awards, bringing her career total to an unmatched 33; previously ‌tied with Beyonce at 30
Taylor Swift's showgirl-inspired The Fate of Ophelia claimed the most prestigious trophy at MTV's annual Video Music Awards on Sunday, and the singer dedicated the honour to the late country music legend Dolly ​Parton.
Swift took home three awards at this year's VMAs, bringing her career total to an unmatched 33. She had previously ‌been tied with Beyonce at 30 awards apiece.
Ophelia , the first single off the record-breaking 2025 The Life of a Showgirl album, was named video of the year.
As she held her latest Moon Person trophy, Swift praised Parton as "the ultimate showgirl" who told stories that were "so vivid and so rich." "I think that we were all very lucky ​to share this planet with Dolly Parton for a time," Swift said.
Parton, an award-winning country singer, songwriter and businesswoman, died in August ​at the age of 80.
Earlier in the ceremony, Swift was awarded the inaugural MTV VMA Artist Director Honors. ⁠The 36-year-old has written and directed 18 videos of her roughly 60 videos during her career.
The most recent, for her new single Patient Zero , ​debuted during the ceremony. The video starred Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell as a couple in an unhealthy relationship.
"The main reason I love ​writing and directing music videos so much is because you, the fans, make it so much, so much fun," Swift said. "You actually care about what we're making."
She also won best direction for her Opalite video.
The VMAs were broadcast live on CBS and MTV and streamed on Paramount+ and hosted by Snoop Dogg. Winners in the top categories ​were selected by fan votes.
Pop music legend Madonna led this year's field of winners with seven awards including artist of the year and ​best dance video for Confessions II -- The Film . She recalled her 1984 performance of Like a Virgin at the first VMAs, which she said was considered too provocative ‌for cable ⁠television at the time.
"I think most of you were probably not yet born," the 68-year-old told the crowd before explaining that she had to quickly recover during that performance from a shoe mishap.
"I dove onto the stage to try and make myself look cute and sexy," she said. "My butt cheek was hanging out. In those days, butt cheeks were not hanging out ... my manager told me my career was over."
Speaking about ​the Confessions II album, Madonna said she ​spent the past 18 months "finding ⁠myself, believing in myself and really making the music I wanted to make." "To me, that really is the definition of being an artist," she said.
Madonna kicked off the show with a high-energy performance of two of ​her recent collaborations. Sabrina Carpenter joined her for Bring Your Love - a song later named best collaboration - and ​Charli XCX took ⁠the stage for Danceteria Afterhours surrounded by dancers on a set that looked like a club restroom.
In a more quiet moment, Kacey Musgraves paid tribute to Parton by singing the enduring song I Will Always Love You .
Lisa, a member of the group Blackpink, won the VMA for best pop video for her ⁠solo effort Dream .
​Sporting a black outfit with large white fringe sleeves, she spoke through tears as ​she thanked her fans, known as Lillies. "I wouldn't be here without you guys," she said. "Thank you so much for your love and support."
English singer and songwriter Sienna Spiro, who ​combines pop, jazz and soul music, was named best new artist.

title: Buttler to miss England ODI series in Pakistan
description: He is ruled out after suffering a hamstring injury against Sri Lanka last week
content:
He is ruled out after suffering a hamstring injury against Sri Lanka last week
Wicketkeeper-batsman Jos Buttler will miss England's one-day international series in Pakistan after suffering a hamstring injury.
Buttler was forced to retire hurt during a one-day international against Sri Lanka at Headingley last week before returning to bat in pain later in the match.
The 36-year-old sat out England's 223-run win over Sri Lanka at the Oval on Sunday and will not be fit in time for the tri-series against Pakistan and Sri Lanka in October.
Buttler this month became the first England batsman to score 10,000 runs in international white-ball cricket, including both 50-over ODIs and T20 matches.
"Jos won't be in Pakistan," said England limited-overs coach Brendon McCullum.
"We know he's an incredible athlete, we know he's supremely fit and an ultra professional, so he'll do everything he can to get back as soon as possible but it's hard to judge how long that will be.
"It's disappointing not to have Jos but it will be good for us to see where we're at."
England are due to play two matches against Pakistan and two against Sri Lanka before a potential final appearance.
Buttler's injury is likely to give Jordan Cox another chance to impress as England's wicketkeeper-batsman.
Cox scored 76 from 52 balls against Sri Lanka at the Oval on his return to England's ODI side for the first time since 2024.

title: Pakistan look to bounce back in ASEAN Cup
description: Green shirts are in a must win situation following a 4 0 drubbing at the hands of Thailand
content:
Green-shirts are in a must-win situation following a 4-0 drubbing at the hands of Thailand
Pakistan must regroup quickly when they face the Philippines in their second Group B match at the FIFA ASEAN Cup on Tuesday, after a 4-0 defeat by Thailand in their historic opening game.
Nolberto Solano's side showed defensive discipline early on against Thailand, but were eventually undone by a better-ranked opponent. Teerasak Poeiphimai scored a hat-trick, and Jude-Bell Soonsup added the other goal.
For 30 minutes, Pakistan held firm. Mohibullah made an important interception, Ali Raza produced a timely sliding tackle, and goalkeeper Yousuf Butt made a fine save. But the resistance broke when Poeiphimai reacted quickest to a rebound, and captain Abdullah Iqbal's misplaced pass led to a second goal soon after.
Changes at half-time brought greater attacking intent. Shayek Dost, Hayyan Khattak and Alamgir Ghazi came on, and full-backs Mohammad Fazal and Haris Ali Zeb pushed forward. Abdul Samad Arshad went close with a shot that flashed just wide, but Thailand struck again on the hour and Poeiphimai completed his treble late on.
Pakistan goalkeeper Yousuf Butt, who lives in Denmark, believes there are positives to take from the game.
"This is another level; they are about 100 ranks forward," he said. "We were not feeling pressure, but there is a difference in quality as you can see, they were converting half chances."
He added: "The only thing I'm satisfied with is that we were not being outplayed. We are not satisfied with a 4-0 loss, and we have to be better at phase two, phase three, and more."
Pakistan's focus now turns to sharpening their finishing and their defensive concentration. "We have to capitalise on those small margins, like the ones they were scoring from," said Butt. "We have to be more active on all parts of the field."
The goalkeeper also has reason to feel at home. Pakistan have played the Philippines in the Philippines before, and Butt played football there last year.
"It is going to be familiar," he said. "Insha Allah, I hope we can put in a very good performance and take those steps to take our football to the next level."
With qualification hopes at stake, Pakistan will hope the lessons of Saturday can be turned into something tangible against the Philippines.

title: Emmy Rossum says  Shameless  nudity led to  preconceived notions  in dating life
description: Emmy Rossum says nude scenes on  Shameless  led some dates to form  preconceived notions  about her
content:
Emmy Rossum says nude scenes on 'Shameless' led some dates to form 'preconceived notions' about her
Emmy Rossum has opened up about how nude scenes in Shameless affected her dating life, saying some men formed “preconceived notions” about her based on her character, Fiona Gallagher.
Rossum discussed the experience with Maria Sharapova during the Sept. 16 episode of Pretty Tough. The actress starred as Fiona for nine seasons of the Showtime series, which premiered in 2011 when she was 24.
“It got quite tricky because of the nudity on the show,” Rossum said. “All of the guys that I would go out with had preconceived notions of who I was or how I was sexually.”
Rossum described the experience as “bizarre” and recalled one date with a man who had political ambitions.
According to Rossum, he was concerned about whether dating an actress known for appearing nude on Shameless could affect his future political career.
“He was like, 'I really want to be president someday.' And I was like, 'Wow, that's like a great goal,'” she recalled. “He's like, 'But I feel like running for office dating someone who's been like exposed in the way that you have, do you think that would be tricky for me?' And I was like, 'This is an insane conversation to have.'”
Rossum also reflected on navigating her identity as a young actress while dealing with perceptions created by her work.
“You're trying to figure out who you are,” she said. “You're coming into your own as an artist. And there's also all these preconceived notions about you that are out there that are associated with [you] because your body is your art, right? And and people can get confused.”
Rossum is now married to Mr. Robot creator Sam Esmail. The couple married in 2017 and share a five-year-old daughter and three-year-old son.
Rossum said she and Esmail share similar values, including putting family first. “We're so like-minded,” she told Sharapova. “We're so family first. We're so work second.”

title: Mir Raza judicial commission proceedings adjourned till Oct 2 upon term expiry

content:
Sindh govt to decide on its proposed extension on October 1
The judicial commission probing the murder of Mir Raza adjourned its proceedings until October 2 as its existing term expired and the Sindh government is yet to decide on a proposed extension.
The Sindh Home Department on August 24 notified the formation of a judicial commission to probe the death of 25-year-old Mir Raza Ali, with Justice Omar Sial appointed as its head following his nomination by the Sindh High Court (SHC) chief justice through a letter dated the same day. The first hearing of the commission took place on September 1.
A written order issued by the commission, headed by Justice Sial, said its term had expired on Monday.
The commission had requested the Sindh government to extend its tenure until October 15.

In response, the provincial government’s focal person Javed Ahmed Abro informed the commission that the summary seeking an extension had been approved by the chief minister and was forwarded to the Sindh Cabinet for a decision.
The commission was also told that the cabinet is expected to meet on October 1.
“It will be therefore appropriate to adjourn today’s (September 28) proceedings to October 2, 2026 at 10am,” the written order seen by The Express Tribune stated.
The order further outlined that if the Sindh Cabinet did not approve an extension, no further witnesses would be summoned and the commission would prepare and submit its report “shortly thereafter” on the basis of statements recorded so far.
If the tenure is extended, fresh notices will be issued to witnesses, the order added.
The commission will also send questionnaires to three senior police officers as part of the proceedings.
It is worth noting that during Monday’s hearing of the judicial commission, Investigation Officer DSP Siraj Lashari and a representative of the Citizens-Police Liaison Committee (CPLC) appeared before the commission to record their statements. However, neither of their statements was recorded as the commission’s term had expired on September 24.
Two days earlier, the commission had rejected a request by Raza's family to summon senior police officers in person, directing them instead to submit their questions in writing. A day before that, on September 25, Advocate Jibran Nasir, counsel for the family of Mir Raza, alleged that police had failed to properly investigate the case and were instead attempting to establish the death as a suicide .

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle face 'blackmail' accusation as their UK security arrangements remain under review
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have faced a “blackmail” accusation from royal biographer Angela Levin as their security arrangements remain under review following their return to the UK.
Speaking to TalkTV , Levin criticised the couple’s continued efforts to secure state-funded protection and suggested they could use their children and a potential departure from Britain as leverage.

Their current arrangements are being reviewed by the Royal and VIP Executive Committee (RAVEC), while Meghan is also having her security assessed by her own Risk Management Board.

A friend of Harry’s reportedly said, “If he doesn’t get [security], then I believe he will go back to Montecito for good, and that could be as soon as half-term.”
Security concerns have also reportedly affected the couple’s children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet. Their spokesperson said their move to another school followed discussions with the family’s security team about “the practicalities of their current arrangements”.
The couple have also reportedly questioned their decision to return to the UK amid tensions with other members of the royal family.

title: French far right wins 15 Senate seats  enough to form group for 1st time
description: 3 die as boat capsizes during English Channel crossing off France
content:
3 die as boat capsizes during English Channel crossing off France
France’s far-right National Rally (RN) and its ally, Union of the Right for the Republic (UDR), won 15 seats in Sunday’s Senate elections, giving them enough lawmakers to form a group in the upper house for the first time, Franceinfo reported on Monday.
RN leader Marine Le Pen called the result a “historic victory.” The gains followed advances by the alliance in municipal elections and came less than seven months before France’s presidential election.
The RN-UDR alliance won nine seats in the Mediterranean region, including seven in Provence-Alpes-Cote d’Azur, according to Franceinfo . RN lawmaker Sebastien Chenu said the result “completes our presence in all French institutions.”
Under Senate rules, a political group must have at least 10 members. Forming one gives parties more speaking time and resources, as well as a greater role in parliamentary work.
Read: Far-right win leaves Germany's Merz shaken as AfD plots path to power
The right, centre and Socialist Party are expected to remain the Senate’s three largest forces. The conservative Republicans could lose about seven seats, according to a partial count cited by Franceinfo , with affiliations and some overseas results still pending.
The election also brought left-wing France Unbowed (LFI) into the Senate for the first time, with Gabriel Amard winning a seat in the Rhone department. The party has also claimed a second senator, Marc Pere in Haute-Garonne, though his party affiliation remains disputed.
3 die as boat capsizes during English Channel crossing off France
Three people died on Monday when a boat attempting to cross the English Channel to Britain capsized off the French coast, local authorities said.
The boat capsized off Wissant in France's Pas-de-Calais region, the prefecture said, according to French broadcaster BFMTV .
Authorities said they were still assessing the casualties and warned that the death toll could change. The prefecture was expected to provide further details at a news briefing later Monday.

title: Israeli occupiers storm Al Aqsa Mosque in East Jerusalem as Palestinian shops forced to close for    Jewish prayers
description: Dozens of Palestinian shopkeepers ordered to close their businesses to allow Jewish prayers during Sukkot
content:
Dozens of Palestinian shopkeepers ordered to close their businesses to allow Jewish prayers during Sukkot
Scores of Israeli occupiers stormed Al-Aqsa Mosque in occupied East Jerusalem on Monday, as Israeli authorities forced Palestinian businesses in the Old City to close to allow Jewish prayers during the Sukkot holiday.
Videos posted by occupiers on social media showed scores storming the flashpoint site and performing Talmudic rituals, prayers and singing. The rituals were concentrated in the eastern part of the mosque compound.
On Sunday, more than 1,500 Israeli occupiers, including National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, forced their way into the Al-Aqsa Mosque to celebrate Sukkot under police protection, according to the Islamic Waqf Department in Jerusalem and Palestinian media.
The incursion triggered widespread condemnation, with Palestinian presidential spokesman Nabil Abu Rudeineh describing it as “playing with fire and a dangerous provocation to the feelings of Muslims around the world.” He also warned of a “religious war” that Israel was seeking to ignite in the region.
Al-Aqsa Mosque is the world's third-holiest site for Muslims. Jews call the area Temple Mount, claiming it was the site of two Jewish temples in ancient times.
Read: Around 100 Israeli occupiers storm Al-Aqsa Mosque compound, perform Talmudic rituals
The flashpoint site has seen an increase in occupier incursions since the start of the Jewish holidays, accompanied by Talmudic rituals and prayers inside its courtyards under heavy protection from Israeli police and forces.
The Jewish holiday period began with Rosh Hashanah on September 12-13, followed by Yom Kippur on September 21-22. Sukkot runs from Sept. 26 to October 2, followed by Simchat Torah on October 3.
Monday’s intrusion came as Israeli authorities forced dozens of Palestinian shopkeepers to close their businesses and residents to remain inside their homes in the Cotton Merchants Market, which leads to Al-Aqsa Mosque, to allow Jewish prayers during Sukkot.
“Dozens of Palestinian owners of shops, cafes and restaurants in the Cotton Merchants Market in Jerusalem’s Old City were forced to close them during the Jewish Sukkot holiday to make way for Jewish prayers in the market,” the Association for Civil Rights in Israel said in a statement.
The authorities also ordered around 200 Palestinians living along the prayer route not to leave their homes while the prayers were being held, the association said.
Traders said this was the first time they had been ordered to close their businesses throughout the holiday period, with previous closures limited to certain hours.
The Cotton Merchants Market lies on a route leading to Al-Aqsa Mosque and contains 56 shops, cafes and restaurants, according to the association.
Israeli police informed traders of the closure by phone last week before officers later visited the businesses and told owners directly that they had to close during most days of the holiday, it said.
Read more: Far-right Israeli minister storms Al-Aqsa Mosque under police protection
Police did not provide a written order or instructions regarding the closures, telling traders only that the measure was intended to allow Jewish prayers to be held in the market, according to the association.
“The situation did not involve a security event that would justify restrictions of such severity for consecutive days,” it said, adding that police could instead alter the prayer route, shorten prayer hours or deploy forces to protect traders and their businesses.
“It is unacceptable for dozens of Palestinian traders to be forced to close their businesses throughout the holiday period and for hundreds of residents to be told to remain in their homes to hold Jewish prayers in the Old City,” said Tal Hassin, an attorney with the association.
“The police are turning things upside down: Instead of protecting residents, ensuring the continuation of their daily lives and protecting their property, they are making them pay the price,” she added. “These instructions must be cancelled immediately and the businesses allowed to open.”
Palestinians regard East Jerusalem, where Al-Aqsa is located, as the capital of a future Palestinian state, based on international resolutions that do not recognise Israel’s occupation of the city in 1967 or its annexation in 1980.

“I personally wanted to sing ‘Last Christmas’ because I actually flipping love that song so much!” she said. “But it just wasn't the time of year.”

“To be the first single from my sophomore album,” she said. “You always feel the pressure with a sophomore album. All artists... but I just feel really grateful and just proud as well ’cause I love that song.”

title: Trump asked Xi whether China would buy US weapons  reveals envoy to Beijing
description: China says it is    dedicated to safeguarding world peace and stability
content:
China says it is ‘dedicated to safeguarding world peace and stability’
US President Donald Trump asked Chinese President Xi Jinping whether Beijing would be interested in buying American weapons, Washington’s envoy to China has revealed.
“President Trump continues to say, hey, we sell arms to other people around the world. He (US president) actually asked President Xi, would he like to buy some at one point,” US Ambassador to China David Perdue told Fox News on Sunday.
Trump hosted Xi for a high-stakes summit at the White House on Thursday. The two leaders met Friday again for a private tea session and reviewed pictorial and text archives in Washington before Xi flew home, concluding his three-day state visit to the US.
Describing Xi’s state visit to the US as “successful,” Beijing on Monday said it is “dedicated to world peace.”
Read: China, US agree tariff cuts on $60 billion of goods including agriculture, household items
“China has built its military based on its own needs and is dedicated to safeguarding world peace and stability,” Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told reporters in Beijing.
Perdue made the remarks while defending Washington’s continued arms sales to Taiwan.
“President Trump continues to say, ‘Hey, we sell arms to other people around the world,’” Perdue said.
A US State Department official subsequently told the South China Morning Post that US law prohibits arms sales to China and that Washington has “no offer or plan” to sell weapons to Beijing.
Perdue said Washington’s Taiwan policy had not changed, citing the one-China policy, Taiwan Relations Act, three US-China communiques and Six Assurances.
“We don’t support independence and we don’t support coercion,” he said, adding that Trump had approved an $11 billion arms package for Taiwan and authorized 50% more arms transfers than any US president since 1979.
Read more: China, US agree on strategic stability, trade and AI cooperation
The US has previously sold weapons to China. During closer US-China strategic cooperation against the Soviet Union in the 1980s, Washington supplied Beijing with military equipment, including AN/TPQ-37 counter-artillery radars and Mark-46 torpedoes.
US government-to-government arms sales were subsequently halted, with no new Foreign Military Sales agreements opened after 1990, according to the US Government Accountability Office.
Beijing considers Taiwan part of China and has repeatedly opposed US arms sales to the island.

content:
Swift directed the video, while Oscar-winning cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki worked on the production
Taylor Swift premiered her “Patient Zero” music video at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards, giving fans plenty of details to examine for references to her past work and possible clues about what could come next.
The video stars Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell alongside Swift, who narrates the couple’s story and its connection to her own experiences.
Swift directed the video, while Oscar-winning cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki worked on the production.
The video opens with Johnson visiting a grave before Swift appears alongside her.
Throughout the story, Swift repeatedly appears in Johnson’s life with her husband, played by Farrell. The two women are presented as mirrors of each other, with similar clothing and Johnson applying red lipstick associated with Swift.
The ending reveals that Farrell’s character was married to Swift, an heiress, and poisoned her for her money.
He is apparently repeating the same plan with Johnson’s character, while Swift appears as a ghost attempting to warn her. Johnson eventually places a rose at Swift’s grave, which reads, “Beloved wife and daughter, gone too soon.”
Several scenes contain references to Swift’s previous work.
The cemetery has been compared with the setting of “Look What You Made Me Do”, which premiered at the VMAs in 2017.
The video also features a dinner-table argument resembling the “Tolerate It” staging from Swift’s Eras Tour.
Celebrity cameos include Cara Delevingne and Los Angeles Rams player Matthew Stafford.
Fans have also interpreted clues including “saccharide” and “North or South” as possible references to Farrell and Johnson.
The video’s dark visual style has also led fans to compare it with Swift’s Tortured Poets era rather than the brighter aesthetic associated with The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore .
The music video became available immediately after the premiere on subscription streaming services like Apple Music , Amazon Music , and Spotify and will be released on YouTube on September 29.

title: CM Afridi hits back at Centre over criticism of K P s counterterror response
description: Says  policy that you have been implementing for 22 years in Pakistan  especially in K P  is not working
content:
Says 'policy that you have been implementing for 22 years in Pakistan, especially in K-P, is not working'
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday hit back at the federal government over criticism of his administration’s counterterrorism response, calling for a “policy shift” and greater provincial involvement in security policymaking as terrorism continued to challenge the province.
“The policy that you have been implementing for 22 years in Pakistan, especially in K-P, is not working. Peace achieved after two decades of sacrifices was once again lost to unrest following the regime change operation. From the time terrorists moved into the mountains to their subsequent resettlement, we repeatedly warned the federal government, but federal ministers repeatedly dismissed our warnings as propaganda and lies. We repeatedly said that the state’s current policy is wrong and will once again lead to the bloodshed of Pakhtuns,” Afridi said while addressing a meeting on the security situation in the province.
His remarks came after federal ministers Attaullah Tarar and Talal Chaudhry criticised the K-P government over its counterterrorism policies. Tarar accused the provincial government of facilitating terrorists for “political and financial interests”, while Chaudhry said the K-P leadership had “not stood united behind its security forces” and had deliberately maintained a “soft attitude” towards terrorists, creating space for them in society.
CM Afridi said decisions concerning the province should not be made behind closed doors and called for the K-P government, administration, police and other stakeholders to be involved in formulating security policy. “If you implement that policy, there will be peace here, and our people will not be killed.”
The chief minister said that he had repeatedly maintained that peace could be restored within 100 days if the policy he advocated was implemented, but said that the federal government had ignored the province’s position.
“When they (terrorists) came down from the mountains, we again said, ‘Look, they are coming down but federal government nevertheless dismissed the warnings as propaganda and accused the provincial government of lying," he added.
CM Afridi said the province had experienced peace after years of violence, crediting the sacrifices of police personnel, soldiers and civilians for establishing it. “More than 80,000 of our civilians have made sacrifices to establish this peace in K-P,” he said.
وزیراعلیٰ خیبر پختونخوا محمد سہیل آفریدی کی زیر صدارت امن و امان سے متعلق اجلاس سے خطاب پشاور: خیبر پختونخوا کے عوام، پولیس اور فوج نے امن کے قیام کے لیے بے شمار قربانیاں دیں، وزیراعلیٰ سہیل آفریدی پشاور: خیبر پختونخوا کے 80 ہزار سے زائد افراد نے پاکستان کے لیے اپنی جانوں کا… pic.twitter.com/1Gc7BT7k6k
He criticised what he called a mindset that had repeatedly treated K-P and its people as a “laboratory” for policy experiments, arguing that the consequences were again being borne by ordinary residents.
Read: Tarar accuses K-P govt of ‘facilitating’ terrorists for political, financial interests
The chief minister also criticised federal and Punjab government figures over remarks concerning security threats, alleging that political considerations were being prioritised while K-P faced continued attacks.
He said soldiers, police personnel and civilians, including children and women, were being killed in the province while other state institutions were focused on political matters.
CM Afridi said his government had increased spending on the police because of the severity of the security situation. He said Rs35 billion had been diverted from the development budget to the police department after he took office.
For the 2026-27 financial year, he said, the provincial police budget had been increased to Rs191.4 billion — a 103 per cent increase. “We are strengthening our Special Branch, we are strengthening our police, we are acquiring modern equipment and giving them modern weapons in every way,” he said.
However, CM Afridi maintained that additional funding and equipment alone would not resolve the security crisis unless there was a change in policy. He said he had been calling for such a change since October 15, 2025, arguing that the existing approach had failed despite being implemented for more than two decades.
He also accused opponents of using what he called “paid media” and political proxies to construct what he termed false narratives about the province. “What direction are you taking Pakistan in? What direction are you taking it in?” he asked, questioning whether the lives of people in K-P were being treated as expendable.
Read More: 13 martyred in DI Khan checkpoint suicide blast
The chief minister said political disagreements should not be allowed to dictate security policy and insisted that the provincial government had a public mandate that could not be ignored.
“No one can go against the people’s mandate, and no one can afford to do so,” he said.
The chief minister also rejected threats of imposing governor’s rule or emergency in the province, saying he was willing to give up his office rather than compromise on his political position, while calling for a fundamental shift in the state’s approach to terrorism.
His remarks came amid speculation over the possibility of governor’s rule or emergency being imposed in K-P as the federal government and the provincial administration have traded accusations over the deteriorating security situation.
CM Afridi said he would not be intimidated by such threats.
“If anyone tries to frighten me by saying that governor’s rule will be imposed here or an emergency will be imposed, then I curse this chair if it makes me abandon my ideology,” he said.
“I have no concern for this chair,” he added, reiterating that the position he had held from the beginning — which he associated with Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's founder Imran Khan’s political ideology — remained unchanged.
“Change your policy. Bring a policy shift. Save our armed forces personnel, our police department personnel and our ordinary civilians from this bloodshed,” he said.
CM Arridi said reducing violence in K-P was not only in the interest of the province but of the country as a whole. “There is benefit for Pakistan in this, and there is benefit for all of us,” Afridi said.
K-P's worsening security situation has brought the province’s PTI-led government into an increasingly direct confrontation with the federal government, with Islamabad questioning its handling of law and order even as deadly attacks continue.
The latest escalation came after the September 18 attack on Kohat Police Lines, where 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were killed, followed by the September 26 attack on a joint checkpoint in DIK that left at least 12 people dead and 35 injured.

description: Madonna won seven VMAs in 2026  her first wins at ceremony in 27 years  after receiving 13 nominations
content:
Madonna won seven VMAs in 2026, her first wins at ceremony in 27 years, after receiving 13 nominations
Madonna won seven awards at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards, marking her first VMA wins in 27 years after receiving 13 nominations at this year’s ceremony.
The singer also returned to the VMAs stage for the first time in 23 years, opening Sunday’s show with performances of “Bring Your Love” featuring Sabrina Carpenter and “Danceteria Afterhours” featuring Charli xcx.
Madonna won Best Dance, Best Collaboration and Artist of the Year among her seven awards. Accepting the Artist of the Year award, she said, “I spent the last year and a half finding myself, believing in myself and really making the music that I wanted to make. And to me that really is the definition of being an artist.”
Her 13 nominations matched the record for most VMA nominations received by an artist in a single year, previously achieved by Lady Gaga in 2010.
Madonna’s latest VMA success follows the release of her 2026 album Confessions II, described in the supplied report as a sequel to 2005’s Confessions on a Dance Floor.
The album became her latest Billboard 200 chart-topper and made her the first artist of the 2020s to reach No. 1 after previously topping the chart in three earlier decades.
Madonna previously won 20 VMAs between 1986 and 1999. Her performances at the ceremony have included “Like a Virgin” in 1984 and a 2003 performance with Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera.

title: Rain hit Asian Games battles scheduling logjam
description: Cricket quarter finals are washed out  while tennis and surfing face delays
content:
Cricket quarter-finals are washed out, while tennis and surfing face delays
Asian Games organisers faced multiple scheduling headaches on Monday as persistent rain disrupted several competitions at the sprawling multi-sport event.
Tennis, surfing and cricket were among sports hit by poor weather on day nine of full competition.
Both the men's cricket ‌quarter-finals between Pakistan-Hong Kong and India-Afghanistan were washed out after the playing field was drenched at Korogi Athletic Park on the outskirts of Nagoya.
With no contingency built into the schedule, Pakistan and India advanced to the semi-finals of the T20 tournament by virtue of their higher ranking.
It was a bitter pill for Afghanistan, which saw the gold medal go to India due to ⁠the rankings rule three years ago when their Hangzhou Games final was abandoned due to rain.
"The rain started yesterday, so hard luck for us," said Afghanistan opener Mohammed Akram.
"We would have been happy to play here with India – our players are in form.
"But unfortunately the rain has ruined everything."
Powerful typhoon Surigae lashed Japan's southern Okinawa prefecture on Monday and was projected to track northeast toward central Japan and the Tokyo region by midweek, raising the prospect of strong winds and heavy rain further disrupting the Games.
Typhoon Dujuan hit the Games early on week one, causing equestrian events in Tokyo to be suspended, though most ‌competitions ⁠were unaffected.
The continental sporting showpiece is mainly based in the city of Nagoya and Aichi Prefecture but Tokyo is also hosting diving events while Osaka has soccer matches.
The rain saw several tennis matches scrapped on Sunday and caused match delays on Monday.
Fans hoping to catch Filipino headliner Alex Eala's opening match against Thai opponent Patcharin Cheapchandej ⁠were repeatedly frustrated at the Higashiyama Park Tennis Centre.
Eala, the women's top seed, had her match shifted off centre court amid the scheduling logjam but was yet to start by mid-afternoon.
Poor wave conditions saw the surfing called off ⁠early at the Long Beach venue southeast of Nagoya, with medal finals having already been pushed into the final scheduled day on Tuesday.
India's Kishore Kumar Anbarasu was able to complete his heat before ⁠it was abandoned, beating China's Ma Wensong to make it into the quarter-finals on the sport's Asian Games debut.
“It was not the easiest conditions. It was very hard to find the good waves," said Anbarasu.

title: Rahat Fateh Ali Khan praises Diljit Dosanjh   s rendition of Nusrat classic
description: Khan applauds the Indian singer for performing  Sanson Ki Mala   saying he sang  from the heart
content:
Khan applauds the Indian singer for performing 'Sanson Ki Maala', saying he sang 'from the heart'
Rahat Fateh Ali Khan has praised Indian Punjabi singer and actor Diljit Dosanjh for his rendition of his uncle, legendary qawwali singer Ustad Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan’s classic Sanson Ki Maala .
Speaking at an exclusive meet-and-greet in Toronto on Sunday, Khan was asked about Dosanjh’s performance of the iconic song.
He applauded the Punjabi star for taking on a Nusrat classic, noting that many artists may hesitate to perform songs associated with the late qawwali maestro.
“A lot of artists get afraid to perform a Khan saab song, but Diljit bhai sang it from the heart with all the power he could. We can see that and hear it, so I will appreciate it,” Khan said.
Dosanjh performed Sanson Ki Maala on September 12 at Wembley Stadium in London as part of his AURA World Tour, becoming the first Punjabi artist to headline the iconic venue.
The performance served as a tribute to Ustad Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, whose music has continued to resonate with audiences across generations and borders. Dosanjh’s interpretation quickly drew attention online, with fans praising his vocals and the emotion he brought to the classic.
One fan who attended the Wembley show wrote, “I had goosebumps watching this live in Wembley, absolutely amazing concert. Can this version be released on Spotify soon?”
Another commented, “What were you thinking when you decided to recreate this masterpiece? Goosebumps!!!”
Others described Dosanjh’s rendition as a “true tribute to Ustad Nusrat” and said the performance “hit the soul to another level”.
Khan’s appreciation adds to the response surrounding Dosanjh’s performance, highlighting the continued reach of Nusrat’s music and its influence on artists beyond Pakistan and the traditional qawwali space.
For Dosanjh, the Wembley performance offered an opportunity to bring a Nusrat classic to a global audience while showcasing his Punjabi musical identity on one of the world’s most recognisable stages.

title: Foreign woman records statement before Lahore magistrate in alleged gang rape case
description: DIG Operations Lahore Kamran says probe undertaken jointly by the CCD  operations and investigation wings
content:
DIG operations Lahore says probe undertaken jointly by the CCD, operations and investigation wings
A 20-year-old Azeri woman on Monday recorded her statement before a judicial magistrate in connection with an alleged gang-rape incident in Lahore.
A day earlier, police apprehended three men and confiscated the vehicle allegedly used during the crime. The developments came in the backdrop of a case registered on the complaint of the Azeri woman under Section 375A (Gang Rape) of the Pakistan Penal Code against three suspects at Defence C police station in Lahore. The young woman subjected to assault said she came to the city on a business trip where she was lured, intoxicated and raped by three unidentified men in a private housing society near Raiwind during the night between September 25 and 26.
The victim appeared before Judicial Magistrate Muhammad Sagheer today at the Cantonment Courts under tight security and recorded her statement under Section 164 (Power to record statements and confessions) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) 1898.
Speaking on the rape incident, Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) Operations Lahore Faisal Kamran said the investigation was being pursued jointly by the Crime Control Department (CCD), operations and investigation wings.
Read: Lahore police identify suspects in alleged gang rape of Azerbaijani woman
The Express Tribune has learnt that the police have also asked federal authorities to place all three suspects on the Provisional National Identification List after they reportedly left Lahore following the incident.
The police said one of the suspects had been traced to Sialkot. Police have also detained two close relatives and a domestic worker of another suspect as part of the investigation.
The incident is the second gang rape case reported involving foreign women within the jurisdiction of Defence-C police station in the past few months. Earlier in June, two foreign women , nationals of the Netherlands and Venezuela, were allegedly abducted and sexually assaulted in the same area.
According to the FIR in that case, five suspects, including a close relative of a senior political personality, allegedly abducted the two women, demanded ransom and subjected them to sexual assault in captivity.
According to the First Information Report (FIR), the victim had arrived in Lahore a few days before the alleged incident.
The report said two unidentified women had lured her to a cafe, where three male friends of the women were already present. After spending some time at the cafe, the group allegedly took the Azeri woman to an apartment.

The FIR further alleged that the victim was given a drink containing an intoxicating substance at the apartment and then gang raped by three men.
The suspects allegedly sexually assaulted her throughout the night before leaving her near the airport and fleeing, according to the FIR. They also allegedly took an iPhone and another expensive mobile phone belonging to the victim, it said.
Police subsequently launched an investigation and began searching for the suspects.
They recovered a vehicle allegedly used in the incident and transferred it to Defence C police station. Investigators used the vehicle as part of their efforts to trace the main suspects.
According to police, a team headed by Superintendent of Police Iftikhar conducted raids to arrest those wanted in the case.
Police said the victim underwent a medical examination following the alleged assault and maintained that further facts were expected to emerge from the medical report.

Pakistan captain Jehan says this is not the only mismanagement that athletes are facing here
Complaints of logistical mismanagement continued to mount at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Monday, with Pakistan volleyball captain Murad Jehan saying his team ‌were taken to the wrong venue ahead of their Pool A match against Uzbekistan.
A glum-looking Jehan took to Instagram to vent his frustration at what he termed "another mismanagement" at the Games.
"We have a very important match and the bus driver doesn't ⁠know which gymnasium we are going to play," he said in a video from the bus.
"He took a wrong way and came to a wrong gymnasium and now we are short of time. It's an embarrassing situation," he added. "We did not expect this from Japan. This should not have happened."
Games organisers did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
Jehan said the detour left the ‌squad ⁠with no time for a proper warm-up, forcing players to change into their playing kit on the moving bus.
"Really disappointing situation. This is not the only mismanagement that athletes are facing here," he said, adding ⁠food was not always available to athletes at dining areas following their training sessions.
Pakistan brushed off the disruption once they reached the Okazaki Chuo Sogo ⁠Park Gymnasium, cruising to their second successive victory with a 3-0 win over Uzbekistan.
On Saturday, the Games' chief organiser apologised for widespread ⁠logistical glitches , explaining that a late influx of approximately 2,000 additional athletes and team officials had overwhelmed operational planning.

title: Hareem Farooq urges fans to embrace their bodies  reject beauty standards
description: Actor encourages people to value themselves beyond appearance and respect others    bodies without judgement
content:
Actor encourages people to value themselves beyond appearance and respect others’ bodies without judgement
Hareem Farooq has urged people to embrace the bodies that have carried them through life’s highs and lows, arguing that physical appearance should neither determine self-worth nor become an invitation for public commentary.
The actor shared a series of pictures of herself posing on a rooftop in a brown dress designed by Manal Saleem. Alongside the photos, she opened up about the insecurities many people experience over acne, hair loss, weight changes, body shape and skin tone, encouraging her followers to look beyond conventional ideas of beauty.
Addressing the physical changes people can experience throughout their lives, Farooq listed the features and fluctuations that are often unfairly scrutinised, from stretch marks and acne to weight changes and different body types.
“Stretch marks. Acne. Marks. Hair loss. Weight gain. Extreme weight loss. Flabby arms. Toned arms. Back rolls. Thick bodies. Thin bodies. Tan, fair or golden skin. Thin or voluminous hair. Straight or curly hair and what not. None of these determines your beauty or your worth,” she wrote.
Rather than defining beauty through physical appearance, Farooq highlighted qualities such as empathy, courage, kindness and resilience as the traits that give a person greater meaning.
“Your deepest beauty lives in your empathy, honesty, courage, helpfulness, character, perseverance, joy, faith, kindness and fearlessness, in the love you carry in your heart, the intelligence of your mind, the purity of your soul, the glimmer of hope in your eyes, the way you face adversity, the desire to always do and be better than yesterday, how you treat others, owning your roots, your values, lifting others, being happy for others and how you cherish the rare, beautiful things only you may see,” she said.
The actor also acknowledged that bodies are not static and can change significantly through different stages of life. She pointed to pregnancy, hormonal changes, illness, stress, trauma and grief, saying these experiences are often overlooked when society imposes rigid expectations about how women should look.
Farooq wrote that bodies can change through “pregnancy, hormones, illness, stress, trauma, grief and survival”, while also highlighting the pressure created by patriarchal beauty standards that encourage women to conform to particular sizes or shapes to be considered acceptable.
Rather than viewing such changes as flaws that need to be explained, Farooq encouraged her followers to recognise their bodies for everything they have endured. “Accept, embrace and honour your body. It has carried you through the good, the bad, the extraordinary and the unbearable. Be grateful for it,” she continued.
Farooq also challenged the culture of unsolicited commentary surrounding people’s appearances, arguing that individuals should not have to explain changes in their bodies or defend the way they choose to look, dress or exist.
“Your body is not a public debate, a cautionary tale or an invitation for commentary. No one owes the world an explanation, apology or performance of acceptability. Let everybody exist without needing permission. Let people dress, age, change, heal and take up space without being measured against someone else’s standards,” she wrote.
She further called on people to examine not only what they say about others’ bodies, but also the assumptions and attitudes that allow such judgement to continue. “Break the cycle, in your words, your gaze, your assumptions and your silence. Choose respect over judgment, freedom over conformity and compassion over control,” she said.
Farooq ended her message by reinforcing the idea that self-acceptance and acceptance of others should go hand in hand. “Your body is yours. Your life is yours. Be unapologetically yourself and make room for everyone else to do the same. You are beautiful just the way you are.”
Fans praised Farooq for her message, with some sharing their own experiences with body image and personal insecurities.
“Just saw the description, I have experienced both severe acne and 105 kg weight gain in my life, and also financial constraints. All these things have just perished now. The fact is that none of them are the parameters of judging a person,” one fan wrote.
Another user praised Farooq for staying true to herself despite her fame. “Literally a decade ago, I started loving you for this very reason, and it still remains the same. Nothing has ever come close to her. She owns it, and she knows it,” they wrote.
The actor has also spoken about standing up for herself and others throughout her career. In a 2017 interview with The Express Tribune , Farooq discussed the importance of women staying true to their core beliefs and building their careers through respect and hard work.
Farooq is set to star in the upcoming Punjabi film Mango Jutt alongside Faysal Quraishi.

title: Ravens grab last second win in Rio
description: Baltimore seals a 34 31 thriller as Commanders stop Seahawks
content:
Baltimore seals a 34-31 thriller as Commanders stop Seahawks
The Baltimore Ravens beat the Dallas Cowboys 34-31 in the NFL's first-ever game in Rio de Janeiro as the Washington Commanders and backup quarterback Marcus Mariota stunned Seattle 33-31 Sunday.
The first NFL game at Brazil's iconic Maracana, where the build-up had been dominated by concerns over the soccer stadium's patchy surface, proved to be a breathless thriller decided by a last-gasp 56-yard field goal from Baltimore's Tyler Loop as the clock expired.
With Derrick Henry at his unstoppable best, rushing for two early touchdowns, the Baltimore Ravens opened a 24-13 lead in the third quarter.
The Cowboys scored 15 without reply to edge ahead, before Ravens rookie Matt Hibner grabbed a touchdown back. Deep in the red zone, Dallas could not force a touchdown, but a field goal with seven seconds remaining appeared to force overtime.
Instead, Baltimore quarterback Lamar Jackson hurled the ball 26 yards to Zay Flowers, and immediately called a timeout with one second left -- allowing Loop to kick the Ravens to victory.
"Major, major credit to those guys straining all the way till the end," said Ravens coach Jesse Minter.
"We felt like we had time to maybe get the ball in range. Unbelievable play by Lamar and Zay, and then obviously Tyler Loop."
Earlier Sunday, reeling from two losses and an injury to franchise quarterback Jayden Daniels, the Washington Commanders turned to 32-year-old journeyman Mariota.
He completed three passing touchdowns to hand the reigning Super Bowl champion Seahawks their first loss of the season, and snap Seattle's 12-game winning streak.
Seattle's loss came despite their own star quarterback Sam Darnold returning from injury to pass for 379 yards and four touchdowns, with two interceptions.
Mariota sent early touchdown passes Rachaad White and Treylon Burks, before his 30-yard hurl to Terry McLaurin opened a 14-point advantage.
Seattle fought back to 24-24. But after a Commanders field goal, Darnold's pass was picked by Kain Medrano, a special teams player and backup linebacker, who raced 50 yards to make it 33-24.
Seahawks pulled back a touchdown but Washington held on.
"That was unbelievable... the more that adversity hits, the more that circumstances pin us against the wall, these guys find a way," said Mariota.
On a Sunday packed with tight finishes, Jahmyr Gibbs and the Detroit Lions saw off a spirited Jets fightback, winning 31-24.
New York's Garrett Wilson took a superb 4th down catch from Geno Smith that was ruled a touchdown on video review, tying the game 24-24.
But the joy was short-lived. Gibbs rushed for his third touchdown, Wilson departed injured, and Jets quarterback Smith was sacked on 4th down to snuff out any hope.
In the late game, the Denver Broncos recovered from a 16-0 half-time deficit to score a thrilling 30-26 defeat of the Los Angeles Rams.
Denver quarterback Bo Nix stretched into the end zone for a close-range touchdown with 47 seconds remaining for what turned out to be the winning score.
Earlier, Cleveland quarterback DeShaun Watson, making his home season debut after being booed by his own fans in the offseason, led the Browns to a last-gasp 21-18 win over Carolina.
In the final year of a $230 million five-year contract ravaged by injuries and off-field controversy, Watson threw for two touchdowns, including a go-ahead 14-yard sling to Harold Fannin Jr. under two minutes left.
Pittsburgh bagged a late win against Cincinnati. Veteran Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers shook off recent offensive woes with three touchdowns.
The Bengals took a fourth-quarter lead, but two field goals and a late strip-sack of Joe Burrow sealed the Steelers win 30-27.
The Indianapolis Colts needed a 53-yard field goal with 21 seconds remaining to beat the Houston Texans 19-17.
The Buffalo Bills defeated the winless Los Angeles Chargers 24-16, despite committing five turnovers.
The San Francisco 49ers never trailed the Arizona Cardinals in a 36-30 win featuring four touchdown passes from Brock Purdy and two endzone receptions for George Kittle.
Kansas City were comfortable 24-10 winners over Miami, while New England -- last year's Super Bowl loser -- was thrashed 35-6 by Jacksonville.
Quarterback Kyler Murray returned from concussion in a 23-16 Minnesota win at Tampa Bay, while Las Vegas beat New Orleans 35-27.
The Tennessee Titans remain 0-3, as quarterback Cam Ward threw a disastrous interception on a potentially winning drive against the New York Giants, who won 12-7.
