title: AJK police arrest 122 over attacks on law enforcement personnel  property damage
description: IGP says 69 FIRs have been registered over unrest that left police  security personnel and civilians injured
content:
IGP says 69 FIRs have been registered over unrest that left police, security personnel and civilians injured
At least 122 people have been arrested in cases related to attacks on police personnel, injuries to law-enforcement officials and damage to public property during unrest in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), Inspector General of Police (IGP) Captain (retd) Liaquat Ali Malik said on Monday.
Speaking at a press conference alongside AJK Chief Secretary Khushal Khan in Muzaffarabad, Malik said 69 FIRs had been registered against groups involved in the unrest and that 122 “disruptive elements” had so far been arrested in connection with the 2025 Chamyati incidents.
He said the cases related to attacks in which police personnel were killed or injured and public property was damaged, adding that the state had exercised “patience and restraint” while attempting to resolve the situation peacefully.
The IGP said the press conference was held to pay tribute to police and other law-enforcement personnel who had been killed during the unrest, as well as to their injured colleagues and families. He said the personnel had sacrificed their lives for the security and peace of Kashmir while trying to prevent armed groups from disrupting public order and “Kashmiriyat”.
According to Malik, some groups had used demands for public rights as a cover to pursue personal loyalties or act at someone else’s direction. He said such groups had repeatedly called for “total closure”, attempted to hold the state hostage, attacked law-enforcement agencies and burned government property.
The state had repeatedly shown “patience and restraint” and given peace a chance, including during the latest unrest, he said. “Despite this, up to today, no entry or exit point has been closed. Life is continuing normally, traffic is moving, and markets are open,” he added.
Azad Jammu and Kashmir Chief Secretary Khushal Khan and Inspector General of Police Captain (Retired) Liaquat Ali Malik are addressing a news conference in Muzaffarabad #News #RadioPakistan https://t.co/Bkp9f3sbV0
Malik further said efforts to pursue an agenda aimed at disrupting the elections had failed, with elections held and an elected government subsequently formed. The IGP said the government had accepted demands it considered “reasonable” and “logical” and had continued efforts to maintain law and order peacefully.
From October 1, 2025 to June 4, 2026, he said, the message accompanying every speech and activity had been “total closure”.
The situation escalated again on the night of June 4-5, when law-enforcement personnel were attacked and several were killed, he said. “After that, to maintain the writ of the state, maintain law and order and exercise its authority, the state used the minimum use of force and tried to maintain peace,” he added.
Police, Rangers, Frontier Constabulary (FC) personnel and civilians suffered casualties during the unrest, with more than 1,000 people injured, according to the IGP. “After so many sacrifices, peace is visible in Kashmir, and the police and other law-enforcement agencies are still standing firm and performing their duty for the peace of Kashmir,” he said.
Malik also referred to an incident in Chamyati almost a year earlier, saying groups had similarly attempted to hold the state hostage and attacked police.
Three police personnel, Constable Tahir Rafiq, Constable Muhammad Jameel and Head Constable Muhammad Khurshid, were killed by gunfire, he said. He added that the bodies of the martyred personnel were later desecrated and that video evidence of the incident existed.
Read: PML-N's Naqi takes oath as AJK president
The IGP said 409 police personnel had been subjected to violence during the unrest, with some shot and others beaten with sticks. “This is not a one-sided state narrative. Anyone can go to the Joint Awami Action Committee’s Facebook pages and see what they themselves are saying and showing,” he said.
He said videos posted by the groups showed people expressing pride in attacks on police, the alleged desecration of bodies, the burning of government vehicles and attacks on other law-enforcement agencies. He urged people to examine what he described as the groups’ “real face” through videos posted on their Facebook pages.
Malik also said some videos showed armed groups confronting the state, inciting people, attempting to disrupt the education system, calling for rebellion, attacking law-enforcement agencies and abducting or holding personnel hostage.
The IGP then showed a short video prepared for the press conference depicting what he described as “violence and brutality”. He said several other graphic videos had not been shown because of ethical and media considerations.
Chief Secretary Khushal Khan said the situation had deteriorated in June following a series of earlier incidents, eventually leading to a complete shutdown, strikes and road blockades across AJK. “Thank god, the people of Kashmir not only foiled this but, while cooperating with the government, we confined these disruptive elements to a very small area,” he said.
He further stated that the government’s writ had since been restored and an elected constitutional government had been established, with the prime minister and president having taken their oaths of office. “Our markets and public life have been restored,” he added.
Read more: Man arrested during IBO for 'supplying illegal weapons' to banned JAAC in AJK: Talal Chaudhry
Khan also said police had remained vigilant against disruptive elements and that law-enforcement agencies had worked jointly to contain the situation.
He added that the press conference was also being held as the state marked one year since the deaths of law-enforcement personnel, adding that the occasion was meant to pay tribute to the martyrs. He also expressed hope that the remaining gaps across Kashmir would be addressed in the coming days.
Malik further said the state had continued to exercise restraint despite what he described as “armed terrorism against the state”.
He also said the government had accepted demands it considered “reasonable” and “logical” and had continued to pursue peace while exercising its authority. “This demonstrates that the state exercises patience and restraint, but the state does not forget,” he added.
He warned that the state did not forgive disruptive elements and that the restraint shown towards them had been temporary and in the “larger interest”. “If anyone thinks that they can wear a mask, martyr police, FC, Rangers and the state will not act or will close its eyes, that does not happen,” he said.
The IGP said the state would identify and pursue those responsible for killing police and other law-enforcement personnel and injuring officials. “There can be a delay, there will be no forgiveness,” he said. He added those who had fired on the state would be punished according to law and “will not be forgiven”.
Also Read: 47 shops destroyed as fire sweeps through Kappa Gali Bazaar in AJK
Maintaining peace and law and order remained the responsibility of police and other law-enforcement agencies, Malik said, adding that they would continue to fulfil that responsibility.
The IGP paid tribute to the martyrs of Chamyati, Dhabla Courts and other incidents across AJK, saying their sacrifices had helped establish peace. He also paid tribute to the families and heirs of the fallen personnel. “We will not forget the sacrifices of our martyrs, and we will not let their blood go in vain,” Malik said.
He said the bloodshed for peace in AJK would be honoured and that the state would do everything possible within the law to maintain peace and protect the lives, property and dignity of the people.
The unrest in AJK followed protests led by the JAAC over demands for constitutional and governance reforms, including the abolition of 12 refugee-reserved seats in the AJK Legislative Assembly, an end to privileges for the political elite and changes to the quota system.
Demonstrations in September and October 2025 escalated into clashes with law-enforcement personnel, leaving at least nine people dead, including three police officers. The government and JAAC reached an agreement in October covering 12 core and 13 additional points, including the formation of a high-level committee to examine the issue of refugee representation.
Tensions resurfaced in June after the government banned the JAAC, and the group called for fresh protests, with subsequent clashes in which police said four law-enforcement personnel were killed and more than 20 were injured in Rawalakot. JAAC disputed the police account and accused security forces of firing on protesters.

title: 11 teenagers wounded in mass shooting at birthday gathering in US state of Georgia
description: 11 teenagers wounded in mass shooting at birthday gathering in US state of Georgia
content:
Two victims remain in critical condition after argument between groups escalates into gunfire at park
Eleven teenagers were wounded in a mass shooting at a birthday gathering in the US state of Georgia, with two of them in critical condition, media reports said on Monday.
The shooting occurred around midnight during a “large gathering” at Carolyn Crayton Park in Macon, about 85 miles (137 kilometres) southeast of Atlanta, CBS News reported, citing the Bibb County Sheriff’s Office.
The victims were four 18-year-old men, two 18-year-old women and five 17-year-old boys.
An 18-year-old man and a 17-year-old boy remained in critical condition, while the other nine victims were stable.
Bibb County Sheriff David Davis said the gathering appeared to be a birthday party that had originally been planned at another location before attendees moved to the park.
Another group later arrived, and an argument between the two groups escalated into gunfire, Davis said.
All 11 people wounded were part of the birthday gathering.
No arrests had been made, and the investigation remained ongoing.
The FBI was assisting in the investigation due to the number of people involved, although Davis said evidence gathered so far indicated the shooting was a local incident.

title: Padel takes Olympic step with Asian Games debut
description: The fast paced sport attracts curious fans in Japan
content:
The fast-paced sport attracts curious fans in Japan
Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Carlos Alcaraz are all obsessed with it, and on Monday the fast-growing racquet sport of padel made its Asian Games debut with officials hoping a place at the Olympics is getting closer.
Padel, a cross between tennis and squash on courts surrounded by glass walls, is played by an estimated 38 million people and has ambitions to become a major global sport.
It took another step towards that goal at the Asian Games in Nagoya after being added to the continent's biggest sporting spectacular as a medal event.
After winning her opening match with doubles partner Danna Abad, Philippines player Joshea Malazarte told AFP: "Padel in Europe is really big and it has just started here, so we're just glad that they added padel."
Padel originated in Latin America and has exploded in popularity in the last decade, notably in Europe.
Officials say the sport is played in 170 countries and territories, with 85,000 courts around the globe.
It is still relatively unknown in Games host Japan, and there was curiosity among some of the crowd at the modest Higashi Sports Centre.
Tickets for the event were free, and one spectator told AFP that she and her friend had dropped in to take a look before heading off for lunch.
Another, 60-year-old Yuko Hiraiwa, said she enjoyed the action but thought the crowd was "a bit quiet".
"I play padel but this was the first time I've seen it live," she said.
The sedate atmosphere in Nagoya was a far cry from padel's popularity in other parts of the world.
The sport has a professional tour circuit and an event held at the Roland Garros tennis stadium in Paris this month attracted over 80,000 people.
A galaxy of padel-playing sports stars including football icons Ronaldo and Messi and Formula One driver Max Verstappen have also given it a boost.
Padel has already appeared at the European Games, and International Padel Federation (IPF) official Donatella Del Gaudio said the next goal is the Olympics.
"We are working hard to make it happen soon," she said.
"We just need to be patient, diligent and respect the Olympic timeline."
Padel is usually played as a doubles game and uses solid rather than stringed racquets.
The courts are much smaller than in tennis and enclosed by glass walls, which can be used to hit balls off similar to squash.
Philippines player Malazarte said padel was "more like a chess match" than tennis.
"You have to open up the angle in order to win, you don't rush the points," she said.
"Whereas in tennis if you have a really good forehand, really good backhand, you can win a point."
Padel officials say the sport is enjoyed by people of all ages, and that 50 percent of the worldwide playing population are women.
But not all sports that enjoy high playing numbers translate into successful spectator events.
Despite millions of players around the world squash failed with four bids to become an Olympic sport until it was finally added to the programme for the 2028 Los Angeles Games.
So is padel as much fun to watch as it is to play?
"When I watch tournaments live, from the first rounds, every year is getting more and more full," said Kuwaiti player Mariam Al-Sarraj.
"Now it's almost fully booked, so I feel like people like to watch it."
The sport certainly won some new converts in Nagoya, with the crowd gasping in appreciation at some of the shots and rallies.
Interest was raised by the involvement of Japan's Teruaki Ando and Shinnosuke Nakamura, who won a tense thriller against a pair from Lebanon.
IPF official Del Gaudio said padel's Asian Games debut was "a source of pride" for everyone in the sport.
"It's confirmation of padel's growth worldwide," she said.
"It represents a closer step to the Olympics."

Kaia Gerber has reportedly delayed work commitments following death of her brother, Presley Gerber, aged 27

“Kaia had a packed schedule, and she has delayed a lot of her work stuff to deal with this. Everyone has been understanding,” the source said. “I don't know when she will go back to work.”

The source added that the family is concerned about Kaia but said she has support from longtime friends. “Everyone in the family is worried about Kaia; they fear she won't be able to handle this, but she has a good network around her. She has old friends that are making her feel better,” the insider said.
Kaia is reportedly being supported by her parents, Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber, boyfriend Lewis Pullman and longtime friends. “Her biggest allies are her parents and her boyfriend Lewis, even his dad Bill,” the source said.
The siblings reportedly shared a close relationship, with the source saying, “She and Presley were best friends.”
Presley was found unresponsive at Resolutions Living, a recovery facility in Santa Monica, California, on September 20. Police are investigating his death as a suspected overdose, but the official cause and manner of death remain undetermined.

The biennial Olympiad is one of the largest events in the sport's calendar
Pakistan have won a gold medal in category D at the 46th FIDE Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, in one of the country's most notable achievements in international chess.
The biennial Olympiad is one of the largest events in the sport's calendar, with teams from nearly 200 countries taking part in 2026.
The Pakistan delegation raised the national flag, the Green Crescent, at the tournament as the result was confirmed. Officials described it as a showcase of the strength and talent of Pakistani chess on the global stage.
Syed Zeeshan Ali Naqvi, president of the Chess Federation of Pakistan, was in Samarkand throughout the campaign, supporting the national players.
After the result, he congratulated the team and praised their hard work, determination and fighting spirit.
He said the players had brought great pride to Pakistan by demonstrating their skills at international level, and urged them to keep working hard and represent the country with the same passion in future competitions.
Federation vice-president Malik Rehan Azam and secretary general Raja Gauhar Iqbal were also at the Olympiad, carrying out their duties alongside the rest of the delegation.
The success is likely to be welcomed by players and supporters at home, where chess has long had a dedicated following but a far smaller international profile than in many other countries. Officials hope the result will encourage more young players to take up the game.

description: Dolly Parton   s manager has sought restraining order against nephew Bryan Seaver over alleged threats and intimidation
content:
Dolly Parton’s manager has sought restraining order against nephew Bryan Seaver over alleged threats and intimidation
Dolly Parton’s longtime manager, Danny Nozell, has asked a court for a temporary restraining order against the late singer’s nephew, Bryan Seaver, alleging threats and intimidation.
According to the supplied report, Nozell filed the case on Tuesday, September 22, through the entity She’s Alive, LLC.
The filing seeks to prevent Seaver from interfering with Parton’s business or contacting its business partners. It also asks that he be required to stay 1,000 feet away from the company’s offices.
Seaver previously ran security at Parton’s properties for more than two decades. Nozell alleges that Seaver referred to his work as a military contractor, access to weapons and capacity for violence while pressuring him to provide money.
The filing reportedly includes messages attributed to Seaver, including: “I'm not an entertainment person. I'm a killer,” and “All I do is warfare ... everyone needs to be worried about what I might do.”
It also quotes an alleged message in which Seaver threatened to discuss the dispute publicly: “I'm going to set up a podcast dedicated to ruining Dolly's brand partnership and telling the violations these people have done on us.”
Seaver reportedly confirmed his military and security background while rejecting the description of his comments as threats. “I am a career soldier and military contractor and do conduct arms deals for foreign governments. I am a security professional and I am a killer... However, nothing in this lawsuit were threats and most of the comments I stand by.”
Seaver is the son of Parton’s sister, Cassie Parton, and announced the singer’s death on August 25. He said at the time, “Dolly has lived in the light and is in the arms of Jesus.”
Nozell alleges the intimidation began weeks before Parton’s death and continued afterwards. Seaver was terminated on September 15, with a new security team taking over several Parton properties.
The dispute concerns the DP Dean Trust, which holds Parton’s properties and business interests. Seaver’s beneficiary interest in the trust remains intact.

Gad also criticised the reported disciplinary measures, particularly claims that some accused students were required to submit essays. He wrote, “There is NO SUCH THING as white collar rape.”
One of the accused has denied the allegations through his attorney. The Tompkins County District Attorney’s Office reportedly found “insufficient evidence” to support criminal charges.

title: CD Projekt Red explains why The Witcher does not get crossover content
description: CD Projekt Red explains why its games avoid platform exclusive crossover content though open to future collaborations
content:
CD Projekt Red explains why its games avoid platform-exclusive crossover content though open to future collaborations
CD Projekt Red has explained why its games generally do not receive crossover content from other franchises, despite The Witcher and Cyberpunk appearing in collaborations with other games.
At BlizzCon, level design lead Miles Tost discussed the studio’s approach after being asked whether Diablo-themed content had been considered for The Witcher games.
Tost said that “we haven't really thought about this yet”, but explained that CD Projekt Red prioritises keeping the same content available regardless of where a game is purchased.
“One thing we really value is to not have content that is purely exclusive depending on where you buy,” he said.
“Usually, when we need to do something exclusive for [partners], what we've done in the past are things like an exclusive physical hoodie. I can recall we did this for Xbox. Xbox pre-orders for The Witcher 3 got an exclusive set of cards. For us, it's really important to preserve that, if you buy the game and play it, you always get the full version of it.”
The approach means CD Projekt Red is comfortable with its characters appearing in other games as platform-exclusive content. A Geralt-inspired Barbarian skin is coming to Diablo 4, while Cyberpunk: Edgerunners outfits are heading to Overwatch next year.
However, the studio does not currently want similar collaborations to create exclusive in-game content for particular versions of its own titles. For example, The Witcher 3 Remastered does not include Diablo-themed content when purchased through Battle.net.
Tost said the studio remains open to changing its approach. “It's not that we are of a mindset where we'll do one thing and then never do another,” he said. “Honestly, we'll listen to what feedback we'll get from these [BlizzCon announcements], how the responses are, and then we'll see about this with an open mind.”
He added that CD Projekt Red is “always sort of open-minded with figuring out cool ways to collaborate”, leaving open the possibility of crossover content appearing in its games in the future.

title: Tarar accuses K P govt of  facilitating  terrorists for political  financial interests
description: Accuses K P government of maintaining ambiguity regarding Kabul  says it has not stood united behind security forces
content:
Talal Chaudhry questions PTI leadership's 'soft attitude' towards Afghanistan, terrorists
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Monday accused the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) government of facilitating terrorists for political and financial interests, saying that the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) leadership was the "B team of the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP)."
"You facilitate terrorists because of your political and financial interests. They have two interests. One is financial, and the other is political. K-P government don't care that people are dying because the government's politics are dear to them. The money that they are making in K-P from illegal mining and through contracts, that's dear to them," said Tarar alongside Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry, speaking during a press conference in Islamabad.
Tarar urged the K-P government to "say these words with your mouth that we will eliminate terrorists from Pakistan and from K-P."
He also argued that if the provincial government cared, "they would have sat in Kohat to hold a meeting on law and order; they would have called a meeting of the whole of Dera Ismail Khan (DIK) on law and order."
Tarar further said that the "current leadership of K-P has bad intentions and a bad nature." He added, "I stand by my position that the PTI leadership in K-P is the "B" team of the banned TTP."
Saying that K-P was "burning in the fire of terrorism," Tarar accused the province's leadership of having placed it's entire focus "on getting one prisoner released from jail."
The information minister also accused K-P CM Sohail Afridi of failing administratively and politically as well, adding that "devastation and ruin" had spread across K-P and that the "provincial government itself spread terrorism and did not counter it."
Discussing Balochistan, he said the province's government "is taking effective measures to deal with terrorism in the province," adding that Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti "is a brave and capable chief minister."
پی ٹی آئی اپنے سیاسی اور مالی فوائد کے لیے دہشت گردوں کی سہولت کاری کرتی ہے. عطاء اللہ تارڑ #PTI #Terrorism #CounterTerrorism #PoliticalDebate #AttaullahTarar pic.twitter.com/cxFfXo97wQ
Drawing a comparison between the two terrorism-riddled provinces, Tarar said Bugti "should be saluted," and that the chief minister was "using all resources to confront terrorism." On the other hand, Tarar claimed that the K-P government was "spending funds on sit-ins instead of the police," and that it wanted to "make the police the political wing of the PTI."
Earlier in the press conference, Chaudhry accused the leadership of the PTI of maintaining a "soft attitude" towards Afghanistan, questioning why the K-P provincial government didn't condemn attacks from the neighbouring country or its proxies.
"Why do you have a soft attitude towards Afghanistan? Why, deliberately, do you maintain such an ambiguous attitude towards Afghanistan that who the real enemy is, or from where all these proxies are operating, you do not condemn them or say their name publicly," Chaudhry questioned.
According to Chaudhry, a political leadership maintained three things in the war against terrorism - leadership, resources, and power. He argued that K-P's political leadership "for the past 14 years, has not supplied leadership to its security forces," adding that the provincial government "has not stood united behind its security forces and has deliberately maintained a soft attitude for the terrorists, and has created space for them in society."
The minister noted further that "this was cowardice, this was the plan."
خیبر پختونخوا نے کاؤنٹر ٹیررازم کی مد میں ملنے والے کئی سو ارب روپے کہاں خرچ کیے؟ عطاءاللہ تارڑ #KhyberPakhtunkhwa #CounterTerrorism #SecurityFunds #Accountability @TararAttaullah pic.twitter.com/wltAyVWcak
He also alleged that "if Pakistan is burning in terrorism, it is because of K-P's incompetent leadership, because of their deliberately maintaining such an attitude, that it is burning."
Read: Talal hopes 'better sense' will prevail
Chaudhry further said investigators had examined an image of one of the suspected attackers of the DIK blast and said that Pakistan’s identification databases had no record matching him.
He said investigators used open-source intelligence and found an image showing the same person at Kabul’s Pakhtunistan Square, which he presented as evidence of an Afghan connection.
"This is not the first incident. In Pakistan, we have been saying for a long time that the terrorist incidents that are happening, most of the groups and organisations come from Afghanistan,” he added.
The minister said that Afghan nationals accounted for about 70% of those involved in these terrorist activities and operations over the past two-and-a-half to three years.
Arguing that Pakistan had "made every effort" through international forums, bilateral contacts, and through friendly countries regarding Afghanistan, he noted that "this neighbour had continued this work."
"This is Afghanistan's true face," Chaudhry said.
افغان شہری نے خیبر پختونخوا میں دہشت گردی کی کارروائیوں میں حصہ لیا، عطاءاللہ تارڑ #AttaullahTarar #KhyberPakhtunkhwa #Terrorism #AfghanCitizen @TararAttaullah pic.twitter.com/IR3waKonhO
Referring to civilians killed in the DIK attack and the subsequent targeting of rescue workers, he asked: “Is this Jihad?” According to the minister, "even enemies who have some principles" don't conduct such attacks or engage in such behaviour. The attacks are "to destabilise us," Chaudhry said, "whenever Pakistan takes off, moves forward, such attacks also increase."
The minister added, "Afghanistan works as a super-proxy."
He further criticised the K-P government, saying that the province had failed to adequately equip its Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) with bulletproof jackets, cars, training, forensic labs or a Safe City network. “Tell me why you did not provide resources,” he said.
Chaudhry also criticised changes to the Police Act, saying the provincial government weakened the force’s institutional authority. The minister also argued that K-P received 1% of the NFC which amounts to around Rs800 billion, but questioned why that amount was not used to provide resources to the people of K-P. "Even today, your counter-terrorism forces live in rented homes; they don't have resources to this day," he said.
He also rejected complaints that the federal government had excluded the K-P leadership from counter-terrorism policymaking, saying provincial representatives had failed to attend national security and counter-terrorism meetings despite being invited to come.
"If you don't come to the sessions, if you don't take interest, and if you can't even condemn with your own mouth when our kids and civilians are being martyred, can't take the enemy's name, what war will you even fight?" Chaudhry asked.
PTI hits back at Tarar, says K-P stands on front line in war against terrorism
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf hit back at Tarar’s criticism of the K-P government, urging him to focus on the performance of the federal and Punjab governments instead of “levelling allegations” against the province.
In a statement issued by the party’s Central Media Department on X, the PTI said, “Attaullah Tarar should remember that the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa stand on the front lines against terrorism, and PTI will never forget the sacrifices of its martyrs.”
“The information minister should first look into his own collar, account for the performance of his governments at the federal level and in Punjab, and then lecture the people of K-P,” the statement added further.
It rebuked Tarar and asked him to highlight the basis for labeling the entire provincial government as facilitators of terrorists adding that the people of K-P, police, security personnel, and political workers have given the greatest sacrifices in the war against terrorism.
The party rejected the allegations, questioning the basis for holding the entire provincial government responsible for facilitating terrorists while, according to the party, the province continued to bear the brunt of militant violence.
The party cited the killing of its provincial law and parliamentary affairs minister Israrullah Gandapur in a suicide attack in Dera Ismail Khan on October 16, 2013, as evidence of the sacrifices made by its representatives. Gandapur was among at least eight people killed in the attack at his residence.
“PTI workers, elected representatives, police and ordinary citizens have given countless sacrifices against terrorism,” the statement said, urging political leaders to avoid what it described as political point-scoring over the issue.
It said the security situation in the province required cooperation between the federal and provincial governments rather than political confrontation.
“The war against terrorism continues in K-P, and the province's people and police are giving sacrifices. In such circumstances, it is a national responsibility for the Federal Minister to cooperate with the province instead of leveling accusations.”

content:
Rana Waheed scores hat-trick as Greens-shirts seal 7-2 victory in men’s hockey
Pakistan produced a commanding attacking display at the Asian Games on Monday, beating Oman 7-2 in their men’s Pool B hockey match at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium to progress to the semi-finals.
Rana Waheed led the scoring with a hat-trick, converting penalty corners in the 34th, 44th and 59th minutes to cap a dominant performance by Pakistan.
Sufyan Khan opened Pakistan’s scoring from a penalty corner in the 22nd minute and doubled the advantage six minutes later. Waheed then struck to give Pakistan a 3-1 lead before the interval.
Ghazanfar Ali extended Pakistan’s advantage in the 40th minute, scoring from open play, before Waheed added his second four minutes later.
Muhammad Ammad landed Pakistan’s sixth goal in the 46th minute before Waheed completed his treble late in the match.
Oman’s goals came from Al Baraa Al Nofli in the 27th minute, while Aiman Madit scored in the 36th..
Pakistan had 58 percent possession and earned 11 penalty corners, compared with none for Oman. Oman had two video referrals and Pakistan three.

content:
The Indian badminton star says back-to-back matches leave her hurting
India's two-time Olympic badminton medallist P.V. Sindhu said Monday she was "hurting" after defeat following three matches in 18 hours at the Asian Games.
The former world champion is the latest badminton player to take aim at the scheduling at the Games in Nagoya.
Sindhu battled to defeat over three gruelling games against China's Chen Yufei in Sunday's quarter-finals.
The 31-year-old played both her second- and third-round matches on Saturday, and was back on court the next day to face former Olympic champion Chen.
Following the gruelling last-eight clash, which Chen won 11-21, 21-18, 21-10, Sindhu took to social media to voice her pain at her exit.
"I needed a little time to put this into words. My Asian Games campaign is over, and I'm hurting," she wrote on X to her three million followers.
"Three points from closing out that quarter-final. I keep coming back to those three points."
Sindhu, who clinched Olympic silver in 2016 and bronze in 2021, added: "Letting it slip hurts.
"Three matches in 18 hours. Back at 3:00 am, out again at 8:30 am. It took a toll."
Sindhu's India teammate H.S. Prannoy has similarly condemned the scheduling for badminton players at the Games.
"It's cruel because everybody is aiming for a good Asian Games, which comes once in four years," Prannoy said at the weekend.
"To have two singles games in a day, I haven't seen it like that in ages."

title: BLACKPINK Lisa s VMA win for Best Pop sparks debate over chart performance and fan voting

content:
The win came ahead of nominees including Ariana Grande, Taylor Swift, Charli XCX and Olivia Rodrigo
BLACKPINK’s Lisa won Best Pop for “Dream” at the MTV VMAs 2026, but the result has sparked debate online over the song’s chart performance and the role of fan voting.
Lisa received the Moon Person on September 27 for “Dream”, featuring Kentaro Sakaguchi, from her debut solo album Alter Ego .
The win came ahead of nominees including Ariana Grande, Taylor Swift, Charli XCX and Olivia Rodrigo.
The victory quickly drew criticism from sections of social media, with some users questioning how “Dream” won despite its limited performance on major US charts.
The song did not enter the US Billboard Hot 100 and peaked at No. 122 on the Billboard Global Excl. U.S. chart. However, it surpassed 100 million streams and gained traction on Spotify and iTunes. Its short-film music video also reached No. 1 worldwide on YouTube.
Some critics described the win as an “attendance award”, while others questioned the result by saying, “nobody knows this song”. Lisa’s supporters argued that the VMAs are determined through voting and said they had voted to support her.
The debate also included claims on social media that Lisa had bought awards, although these remain allegations rather than established facts.
Lisa also performed her new single, “SaWaDiKa”, at the ceremony, appearing inside a life-sized traditional Thai tuk-tuk. Fans praised the staging, while some critics questioned whether she performed live.
The controversy has placed Lisa’s VMAs 2026 win at the centre of a wider discussion about chart performance, fan voting and award recognition.

title: China  US agree tariff cuts on  60 billion of goods including agriculture  household items
description: Beijing will also look to reduce levies on US fish and seafood  logs and wood products  cosmetics and medical devices
content:
Beijing will also look to reduce levies on US fish and seafood, logs and wood products, cosmetics and medical devices
China and the United States have agreed to cut tariffs imposed on $60 billion worth of goods ‌imported from each other, on an array of products ranging from US corn to cosmetics, and from Chinese household appliances to toys.
Under the US-China Board of Trade, both countries have each recommended $30 billion of trade in non-sensitive goods for more favourable tariff treatment, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement on Sunday.
For the United States, that was "unlocking improved market access" for about 30% ​of US exports to China, he said.
The reciprocal tariff reduction as well as an extension of a trade truce were among the key takeaways from the ​second summit this year between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, hosted in Washington last week.
One of two lists from ⁠the White House showed that China planned to trim duties on a variety of US agricultural goods including corn, wheat, sorghum, meat, dairy, vegetable oils and meals. It ​did not include soybeans.
Beijing will also look to reduce levies on US fish and seafood, logs and wood products, cosmetics and medical devices.
Read: Trump cuts China tariffs after ‘amazing’ meeting with Xi
In another list were Washington's reciprocal tariff ​cuts for Chinese small appliances such as coffee makers and toasters, tableware, blankets and bed linens.
The lists also included toys, fireworks, artificial flowers, Christmas tree lamps and other holiday decorations, and children’s car seats.
China's commerce ministry said on Monday a two-month extension of a trade truce with the United States through to January 10 would provide room for both sides to evaluate their ​ongoing arrangement to resolve economic and trade issues, while considering how to advance on those fronts.
The extension also provides a "relatively stable and predictable policy environment" for cooperation ​among companies and continued active discussions.
Both sides will hold regular talks on potential investment opportunities and barriers, enhancing policy transparency and predictability, and responding to enterprises' concerns, the ministry said.
Stocks fell ‌sharply in ⁠China on Monday, with investors having few concrete details to cheer from the leaders' summit and underlying tensions resurfacing. Technology stocks fell on a bipartisan US push to ban Chinese components from data centres and the benchmark blue-chip index slid more than 2% to a one-year low.
China's choice of products for tariff cuts looks designed to help Beijing meet what the White House says is a $17-billion commitment to buy agricultural goods. China has already resumed large-scale buying of US soybeans under a deal ​struck last year to buy 25 million ​metric tons annually.
Both countries will set ⁠up an agriculture working group under a trade council, which will hold its first meeting before the year ends to discuss two-way market access and regulation, the commerce ministry said.
Read more: China's space diplomacy lifts Pakistani astronaut toward orbit
The presidential summit also yielded an agreement for China to import 10 million ​metric tons of coal annually from the United States in 2027 and 2028, the White House release showed. That amount ​roughly equals 2% of ⁠China's coal imports each year.
Liquefied natural gas and oil were not on the list.
"Importing US coal is not only a beneficial supplement to China's domestic coal market, but also brings stable economic income and employment to the US coal industry," the Chinese ministry said.
On artificial intelligence, both sides have agreed on a communication channel ⁠for incidents ​and will hold a follow-up dialogue by the end of November.
China will also examine and approve foreign ​financial services institutions, including those with US capital, to conduct business and open branches in China.
There will also be continued communication on increasing flights between China and the United States, the ministry statement said.

title: Gold price drops Rs12,800 per tola in Pakistan | The Express Tribune
description: Gold falls 3% to touch its lowest ‌in more than seven weeks in international bullion market
content:
Gold falls 3% to touch its lowest ‌in more than seven weeks in international bullion market
Gold prices declined sharply in the local market on Monday, with the price of gold per tola falling by Rs12,800 following a major decrease in the international market.
In the international bullion market, gold prices decreased by $128 per ounce, settling at $4,156 per ounce.
According to rates released by the All Pakistan Sarafa Gems and Jewellers Association, the price of gold per tola fell to Rs438,136, while the price of 10 grams of gold dropped by Rs10,973 to Rs375,631.
Silver prices also declined in the domestic market, with the price of silver per tola falling by Rs325 to Rs6,578. The price of 10 grams of silver decreased by Rs279 to Rs5,639.
Gold fell 3% to touch its lowest ‌in more than seven weeks, as higher oil prices stoked inflation fears, bolstering the case for elevated interest rates.
Spot gold was down 3% at $4,156.45 per ounce, as of 0814 GMT, hitting ​its lowest since August 5. US gold futures for December delivery fell ​3.1% to $4,188.80.
The dollar held firm, making greenback-priced bullion more expensive for ⁠holders of other currencies, while US Treasury yields extended gains.
"Higher oil prices and ​the increased probability of further US rate hikes being priced in by market participants ​are the main drivers behind gold's recent weakness," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo.
"This backdrop could keep US real yields and the US dollar elevated, raising the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding ​gold and contributing to further near-term volatility in the precious metal."
Brent crude oil ​rebounded after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace deal from Iran to resolve their conflict and ‌reopen ⁠the Strait of Hormuz, keeping tensions in the Middle East elevated. Rising energy costs tend to drive inflation higher by lifting prices across the economy.
Traders see a 70.3% chance of a Fed rate hike in October, CME's FedWatch Tool showed. The ​US central bank earlier ​this month lifted ⁠rates by a quarter percentage point and indicated that additional increases are likely.
On Friday, Cleveland Fed chief Beth Hammack said she ​is concerned that persistently high inflation risks could condition the ​American public ⁠to accept elevated prices as the norm, adding the central bank cannot let that happen.
Focus is now on a series of US economic releases scheduled for this week, ⁠including job ​openings, the ADP employment report, Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) ​readings and nonfarm payrolls.
Among other metals, spot silver fell 4.8% to $61.17 per ounce, platinum declined 2.4% to $1,735.88 ​and palladium lost 2.2% to $1,239.60.

title: Kasim Khan claims govt blocked visa travel to use him as leverage against Imran
description: PTI founder s son says he and his brother were urged to enter country on NICOPs  raising fears of arrest and detention
content:
PTI founder's son says he and his brother were urged to enter country on NICOPs, raising fears of arrest and detention
Kasim Khan, son of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan, has claimed that Pakistani authorities did not allow him and his brother Sulaiman to travel to Pakistan on visas, alleging that officials wanted them to enter the country on National Identity Cards for Overseas Pakistanis (NICOPs) so they could be arrested and used as leverage against their father.
In an interview with CBC News , Kasim said the authorities “don’t want us to go over as British citizens” and instead wanted the brothers to travel on NICOPs. “Travelling on the NICOPs makes it almost certain they'll arrest us as they threatened,” he said.
Kasim alleged that the authorities had prevented him and Sulaiman from visiting Pakistan because they were “petrified of foreign intervention”.
Asked whether he would still visit Pakistan, Kasim said he would “love to go on a visa”, arguing that it would provide a degree of protection if he and his brother were arrested. “It would give us that safety net where if we did go and they did arrest us, there may even be hope that there would be foreign intervention,” he said.
Kasim said he was approaching the issue from a humanitarian standpoint and did not want to be seen as a politician. “I want to see my dad basically,” he said.
He also appealed to the British government to recognise his request as humanitarian rather than political, saying he believed British officials were concerned that supporting him or his father could be interpreted as a political statement.
“It should be a humanitarian statement,” Kasim said, referring to his father’s imprisonment and describing the cases against him as “bogus”.
Earlier in the interview, Kasim said he had last spoken to his father in March, more than seven months ago. He said he and Sulaiman had recorded the call and listened to it often, but declined to disclose much about their conversation.
Kasim said Imran appeared “more frustrated than any calls in the past” and told his sons that “they're not treating his eye properly”. He said his father urged them “to be strong and keep doing what we're doing”.
Asked whom Imran was able to speak to in Pakistan, Kasim said it was mainly his lawyer. He claimed that Zoom calls between his father and his lawyers from his cell, which concern court proceedings, were being counted as visitations.
He said there had also been occasions when Imran was able to see his sisters, but “those times are gone”.
Responding to claims by government spokespeople that Imran had received 900 telephone calls and 400 visits, Kasim said: “It's nonsense.”
He said the Supreme Court had ordered that the family be allowed to speak to Imran, “along with many other things that haven't been followed”. “We have no genuine medical reports on what his situation is like,” he said, adding, “No one knows his conditions.”
Kasim said he was appealing to the British government, as well as “the Canadian government” and “whoever will speak out”, over his father's situation.
He said the United Nations had described Imran's situation as torture, while Amnesty International had described it as “inhumane” and arbitrary detention. “It's very, very clear that what's happening is not justice,” he said.
Kasim also claimed that Pakistan was “terrified of foreign intervention”, describing it as “the one thing that makes them tremble”.
Also Read: Jemima Goldsmith urges UK govt to intervene over Imran Khan’s rights
Referring to Pakistan's dealings with US President Donald Trump, he said: “They just gave away everything, you know, the cryptocurrencies, natural resources, Nobel Peace Prizes.”
Asked whether he would want his father to accept a deal under which he would leave Pakistan and stay out of politics, Kasim said that “from a selfish perspective” he would like him to accept it.
However, he said he did not know enough about his father's current situation to know what decision he would make. “I don't even know if he would take it at this point because he might die tomorrow or the next day,” he said.
Kasim described his father as “a very, very strong-willed person” who understood that there were “many other political prisoners”, including more members of their family. This, he said, made it difficult for Imran to agree to a deal.
Rejecting the suggestion that his father had “made a deal with the devil”, Kasim said Imran had entered politics to challenge existing political parties and spent 22 years building PTI because he believed the other parties were corrupt.
He claimed that other political parties had united against PTI when the party began gaining political traction because they viewed Imran as a threat.
Kasim also alleged that the current government had sought to dismantle PTI, claiming that party leaders had been jailed or “tortured into submission”. He said foreign countries needed to intervene to secure the release of political prisoners.
Discussing Pakistan's geopolitical position, Kasim said the country had “played their cards well” in the region, but argued that developments inside Pakistan should not be overlooked. “The world needs to look over to Pakistan, to what's going inside of it, not what they're doing in terms of geopolitics,” he said.
Asked whether he could imagine not seeing his father again, Kasim said: “I find it hard to imagine that I will see him again.” He said this was why the family had stepped up its campaign. “I don't like it. I don't enjoy it,” he said, adding: “If there's any way that we can support and try and get him out of this situation, we will.”

title: Three traffic wardens martyred after gunmen attack police vehicle in K P s Tank
description: Interior minister condemns incident  says invaluable sacrifices of martyrs will not go in vain
content:
Interior minister condemns incident, says invaluable sacrifices of martyrs will not go in vain
Three traffic wardens were martyred, and at least one other was seriously injured when unidentified armed men opened fire on a traffic police vehicle in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's (K-P) Wazirabad area of Tank district on Monday, District Police Officer Abdul Samad said.
The incident took place near Shehzada Market in Wazirabad, where the attackers opened fire on the vehicle carrying traffic police personnel, according to police. The three officers who were killed were identified as Constable Saleem Shah, Constable Gul Ameen, and driver Pir Fayyaz.
One injured officer was identified as Qaiser Mohammad Walid Khan, a resident of Barwand, while another injured person was identified as Zafri Garha Baloch, according to the details provided by officials.
Police said the attackers also took the traffic police vehicle with them after the shooting. The whereabouts of traffic police in-charge Ismatullah remained unknown, police said.
Police and army personnel launched a search operation to trace the attackers and the stolen vehicle after receiving information about the incident. The vehicle was later found abandoned near a bridge under construction in Garha Budha, officials said.
Police said the attackers had been identified as members of Fitna al-Khawarij, while the bodies of the martyred officers and the injured were shifted to Tank Hospital.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi condemned the firing incident by Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists. Naqvi expressed grief over the martyrdom of three traffic police personnel in the attack and offered his condolences and heartfelt sympathies to the families of the deceased.
وفاقی وزیرداخلہ محسن نقوی کی ٹانک کے علاقے میں خوارجیوں کی جانب سے ٹریفک پولیس گاڑی پر فائرنگ کے واقعہ کی مذمت وزیرداخلہ کا فائرنگ سے 3 اہلکاروں کی شہادت پر اظہار افسوس شہداء کے لواحقین سے دلی ہمدردی و اظہار تعزیت
“We salute the sacrifice of the martyred personnel,” Naqvi said. “We stand with the families of the martyrs in this hour of grief,” he said.
“The invaluable sacrifices of the martyrs in the war against terrorism will not go in vain,” the minister added.
The latest attack came days after a suicide bombing at a joint Customs, police and Excise checkpoint in Darazinda tehsil of Dera Ismail Khan on September 26, in which 13 people, including two women, a minor girl and a Customs inspector, were killed and 26 others were injured. The blast was followed by separate attacks on a police Quick Response Force vehicle and a Rescue 1122 ambulance, killing two rescuers and injuring two others.
The Darazinda attack came a week after a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers on September 18 killed 23 people, including 15 police personnel, while eight terrorists were killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, later claimed responsibility for the bombing and subsequent attacks involving multiple assailants.
In September, two Frontier Constabulary personnel, Havaldar Ishaq and Sepoy Umar Hayat, were allegedly abducted by unidentified armed men in Bannu before their bodies were recovered from a graveyard in Palosi.
Earlier this month, a police constable was martyred and another injured when unidentified armed men opened fire on their vehicle during a routine patrol in Karak's Shatakai Dam area.
In August, a police patrol vehicle in Karak was targeted with a remotely controlled improvised explosive device, killing its driver and injuring six other policemen.

title: Kacey Musgraves pays emotional tribute to Dolly Parton at 2026 MTV VMAs
description: Musgraves performed a cover of Parton   s signature song  I Will Always Love You  at the ceremony held in LA
content:
Musgraves performed a cover of Parton’s signature song 'I Will Always Love You' at the ceremony held in LA
Kacey Musgraves honoured the late Dolly Parton with a performance of “I Will Always Love You” at the MTV VMAs 2026 on Sunday, September 27.
The “Architect” singer performed a cover of Parton’s signature song while wearing a fuchsia crystal gown with feather trim.
The ceremony, held at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater, incorporated archival footage of Parton, creating the appearance of a duet between the two artists.
Musgraves had prerecorded the tribute in Los Angeles earlier in the week because of a scheduled Middle of Nowhere Tour date at Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena.
The memorial segment opened with an archival clip of Parton offering advice to the audience. “I’d like to leave you fellas with a bit of advice,” she said. “Don’t criticize your wife’s judgment; after all, she picked you!”
VMAs host Snoop Dogg praised the performance afterwards, saying, “Wow, now that’s how you honor a legend.”
The tribute came just over a month after Parton’s family announced her death at 80 on August 25. Her spokesperson later confirmed that the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inductee had died following a “brief battle with cancer.”
Musgraves had previously shared her grief on social media, writing that “the world feels a lot less sparkly all of a sudden”. She has also honoured Parton during several tour performances.
The MTV VMAs 2026 aired live on MTV, CBS and Paramount+ from the Peacock Theater.

title: UK police question five men held at airbase used by US to attack Iran
description: Police impose 400 metre cordon around RAF Fairford  evacuate 85 homes as security stepped up at US bases in Britain
content:
Police impose 400-metre cordon around RAF Fairford, evacuate 85 homes as security stepped up at US bases in Britain
British police were questioning five men on Monday on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences after they were detained near an air base that has been used by the United States to strike Iran.
Officers detained the five men in the early hours of Sunday after they received a tip-off that three large white vans had been seen heading to the military airfield of RAF Fairford in the west of England.
US President Donald Trump said the suspects had been looking to do "big damage" and had been under investigation by British and US authorities. However, a local farmer said she had tipped off police after seeing a group of "hooded and masked men" running into the fields.
British counterterrorism detectives have not yet publicly stated who they assessed was involved but a source familiar with the investigation said an Iranian-linked motive was considered the most likely, while a Russian sabotage operation or an Islamist plot were also being looked at as possibilities.
Read: Mediators press Iran for nuclear concession to revive ceasefire talks with US: report
Defence minister Wes Streeting told BBC News on Monday that he would not speculate about motives of a live investigation. But he added on the general Iranian threat to the country: "We know that Iran and their proxies wish to do us harm. We know that they hate our democracy, and we know that we regularly have to thwart Iranian attempts to threaten either our interests or indeed our allies."
In May, Britain sanctioned 12 individuals and entities linked to Iran, accusing them of involvement in hostile ‌activity including plotting attacks and providing financial services to groups seeking to destabilise the UK and other countries.
Iran has repeatedly denied involvement in attacks or plots in the UK and elsewhere.
The British government had given authorisation to the US to use bombers based at Fairford to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
The government has said Prime Minister Andy Burnham is being regularly updated on the incident and he cancelled attending at least two events at his Labour Party's annual conference on Sunday.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards had warned Britain in July not to allow US bombers to ‌fly from Fairford, saying any base used to launch attacks would be a legitimate target.
Read More: British PM Burnham says it is right to ‘move beyond’ past criticism of Trump
In Fairford, police have imposed a 400-metre cordon around the base and evacuated residents from 85 homes.
A bomb disposal robot could be seen on Sunday operating around the three white vans, while security was stepped up around the base. Armed police stood guard at the main entrance while large machinery was used to block other access points.
Security was also stepped up at other US bases in Britain.

title: EU foreign policy chief claims Russia planning  more sabotage acts  against Europe
description: EU foreign policy chief claims Russia planning  more sabotage acts  against Europe
content:
Kaja Kallas urges member states for greater vigilance and preventive action
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas claimed on Monday that Russia was planning "more sabotage acts" and attacks against European democracies, calling for greater vigilance and preventive action.
"We see in the intelligence that Russia is planning more sabotage acts and attacks against our democracy to divide our society, to intimidate our societies from refraining to help Ukraine. So, this is something that they have in mind, and we have to keep this in mind as well to be standing up to these threats," Kallas said ahead of an EU defence ministers' meeting in Brussels.
European countries, she added, should be able to act before such attacks take place.
EU defence ministers are to discuss the bloc's response to hybrid attacks, including a proposed emergency protocol that would be activated in response to any threat targeting member states.
She said the meeting would also address European defence readiness, support for Ukraine, and the security situation in the Middle East.
On European defence capabilities, Kallas said EU investment in defence has increased, but significant capability gaps remain, and the focus should now be on filling those gaps.
On the Middle East, Kallas said the EU's naval Operation Aspides requires additional assets, particularly ships capable of escorting vessels through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
She said the EU would discuss whether ships offered to a separate "coalition of the willing" could temporarily be assigned to Operation Aspides.

title: PSX down over 339 points amid uncertainty  failed US Iran diplomacy
description: Index settles at 170 425 62  after profit taking erases early gains
content:
Index settles at 170,425.62, after profit-taking erases early gains
Volatility persisted at the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) on Monday as investors were worried about the unending uncertainty surrounding a US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough over the strategic water lane of the Strait of Hormuz.
The index had opened the week on a positive note, climbing to 171,038.58, up 273.36 points, or 0.16%, by 9:33am. However, profit-taking soon erased the early gains, with the market turning volatile and moving lower. The index fluctuated between an intraday high of 171,126.52 and a low of 170,120.50.
The pressure came as Brent crude prices rebounded more than 3% in Asian trading after US President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal aimed at resolving the conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, keeping tensions in the Middle East elevated.
Consequently, the benchmark KSE-100 index lost 339.60 points or 0.20% and settled at 170,425.62.
According to Arif Habib Limited (AHL) analyst Ali Najib, PSX experienced another range-bound trading session, with the benchmark KSE-100 index sliding 340 points (-0.20% DoD) to settle at 170,426.
Investor sentiment remained fragile throughout the session as persistent geopolitical uncertainty kept market participants on the sidelines, particularly following media reports that Trump had rejected an Iranian ceasefire proposal regarding the Strait of Hormuz, while declining to comment on potential post-midterm military actions.
On the index contribution front, positive momentum from TRG Pakistan, Fauji Fertiliser, Oil & Gas Development Company, Attock Refinery, and Hub Power collectively added 264 points.
However, the gains were offset by selling pressure in United Bank, Habib Bank, Lucky Cement, Engro Holdings, and Mari Energies that dragged the index down by 321 points.
Going forward, market sentiment was expected to remain volatile, with selective buying likely if geopolitical tensions continued to ease and oil prices trended lower. However, elevated energy prices, external-sector risks and the upcoming IMF review would remain key factors influencing market direction, Najib wrote.
Overall, trading volume decreased to 421 million shares from Friday’s total of 482.7 million. The value of traded shares stood at Rs17.7 billion. In the ready market, shares of 496 companies were traded. Of these, 181 stocks jumped, 267 fell, and 48 remained unchanged. Cnergyico PK was the volume leader, with trading in 61.6 million shares, rising Rs0.14 to close at Rs13.32.

title: Heavy rain hit twin cities  disrupts traffic and flight operations
description: Miles long queues of vehicles reported on Islamabad Expressway  commuters say they were stuck for several hours
author_name: Jamil Mirza, Saleh Mughal, Usama Iqbal
content:
Miles-long queues of vehicles reported on Islamabad Expressway
Heavy rain and thunderstorms disrupted traffic in Islamabad and Rawalpindi on Monday, with long queues reported on the Expressway and a Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) flight from Paris diverted to Multan because of adverse weather.
The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) recorded 33mm of rain in Saidpur Village, 25mm in Golra, 22mm in Bokra and 23mm at its station in H-8/2. Shamsabad received 29mm, Kuri 15mm, Peerwadhai 28mm and Gawalmandi 27mm.
PMD data showed that water levels in Nullah Leh at Katarian and Gawalmandi were falling, at about eight and nine feet, respectively. A pre-alert was in place at Gawalmandi, while the pre-alert threshold at Katarian was 11.4 feet and the alert level at Gawalmandi was 14.1 feet.
The public was advised to stay away from Nullah Leh and follow instructions issued by the relevant authorities.
Rain had been continuing in the twin cities since about 3:45am, while authorities deployed staff and heavy machinery to deal with water accumulation in low-lying areas.
Latest rainfall figures of Islamabad and Rawalpindi. #RainAlert #PMD #IslamabadRain #RawalpindiRain pic.twitter.com/Bt0QDg9p5X
PIA flight PK750, travelling from Paris to Islamabad, was diverted to Multan and landed safely at 5:44am, according to a post by PIA on X. The aircraft later departed for Islamabad at 8:21am.
Due to adverse weather (thunderstorm/rain) at Islamabad, PIA flight PK750 (Paris - Islamabad) was diverted to Multan, landing safely at 05:44 AM. The aircraft departed for Islamabad at 08:21 AM. pic.twitter.com/XAKV4IF1DC
Rain caused severe traffic disruption on Islamabad’s Expressway, with miles-long queues of vehicles reported and commuters saying they had been stuck for several hours.
Islamabad Traffic Police on X said it was working to keep traffic moving during the rain and urged commuters to follow traffic advisories and cooperate with its personnel.
اسلام آباد ٹریفک پولیس بارش میں ٹریفک رواں دواں رکھنے میں مصروف عمل۔ شہریوں سے گزارش ہے کہ ٹریفک ایڈوائزری پر عمل کریں اور ٹریفک پولیس کے ساتھ تعاون کریں۔ #WeRIslamabadPolice #ICTP #ITP #Islamabad pic.twitter.com/tvrH1iNDYN
The Islamabad district administration said additional staff, including assistant commissioners, had been deployed in the field to monitor drainage in low-lying areas. Additional personnel were also deployed by Islamabad Traffic Police to help maintain traffic flow on major roads.
The Capital Development Authority (CDA) said its sanitation, environment, Islamabad Water, rescue and district administration teams were carrying out field operations, including dewatering at various locations.
In Rawalpindi, the district administration, Rescue 1122, the waste management company and other departments were placed on high alert following heavy rain. The Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA) imposed a rain emergency and mobilised its field officers and heavy machinery to low-lying areas.
WASA Managing Director Azizullah Khan said water was flowing at normal levels in Nullah Leh, with the level at five feet at Katarian and two feet at the Gawalmandi bridge at about 9am.
Dewatering pumps and other necessary machinery were moved to sensitive locations, while WASA teams remained deployed to drain accumulated rainwater and provide assistance to residents.
The Rawalpindi commissioner directed all departments to remain on high alert and ordered continued monitoring of Nullah Leh. Heavy machinery was deployed in low-lying areas around Liaquat Bagh, Committee Chowk Underpass, Murree Road, Dhok Khabba, Circular Road and Sadiqabad.

title: Former NADRA chief Tariq Malik named among 50 global leaders shaping digital public infrastructure
description: Malik resigned from NADRA in 2023 due to a NAB investigation in procurement payments
content:
Malik resigned from NADRA in 2023 due to a NAB investigation in procurement payments
Former National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) chairman Tariq Malik was named among the Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) 50, a global list recognising people working to shape the future of digital public infrastructure.
The list was launched by Apolitical in collaboration with the World Economic Forum Global Future Council on GovTech and DPI on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
Malik said he was “humbled” by the recognition and described himself as “a student” and “a lifelong learner”.
“My journey with digital identity and public infrastructure has taken me from Pakistan to Malawi and across continents, over the years, to advising more than two dozen countries,” he said in a LinkedIn post .
He said his experience had reinforced his belief that Digital Public Infrastructure was ultimately not about technology but “people, trust and the relationship between a citizen and the state”.
“Every country has taught me something. Every implementation has challenged an assumption,” Malik said.
He said the next generation of DPI would raise harder questions around sovereignty, artificial intelligence, privacy and inclusion. “We will need to remain students of these changes and, above all, students of the people these systems are meant to serve,” he said.
The DPI 50 recognition followed Malik being named among Okta’s Identity 25 earlier in 2026, according to his LinkedIn post.
In a separate post on X, Malik said he had attended Digital Collaboration Day in New York, where he discussed the future of artificial intelligence.
#Science illuminates the path, #Policy sets the guardrails, & #CapacityBuilding ensures no one is left behind. Honored to be at the #DigitalCollaborationDay in NYC discussing the future of #AI We aren't just building #technology ; we are building a global ecosystem @ODET_UN @UN … pic.twitter.com/ZKlj4mOIXH
“Science illuminates the path, policy sets the guardrails, and capacity building ensures no one is left behind,” he said. “We aren't just building technology; we are building a global ecosystem,” Malik added.
Malik previously served as NADRA chairman, a position he resigned from in June 2023, after leading NADRA for approximately two years.
His resignation came while the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) was investigating the procurement of NADRA’s Iris recognition system. NAB had summoned Malik over procurement records relating to the system, including $3.5 million in payments, the PC-1, tenders and newspaper advertisements.
In his resignation letter, Malik cited what he called a “politically charged and polarised environment” as a growing obstacle to his work at NADRA. He said it was difficult for professionals to maintain their integrity and independence in an environment where political loyalty was privileged over competence.
Malik later told The Express Tribune that there was “no pressure on me and any such impression is wrong”. He also said he intended to remain in Pakistan to complete projects associated with the United Nations.
Malik continued working in digital identity and public infrastructure after leaving NADRA. He said his work had included advising more than two dozen countries and working with governments and public institutions on digital systems.

title: Pakistan whip Uzbekistan to reach quarters

National volleyballers dominate Uzbeks to record 3-0 win at Asian Games
KARACHI: Pakistan on Monday blasted their way into the quarter-finals when they whipped Uzbekistan 3-0 in their Group A second round game of the volleyball event of the 20 th Asian Games in Nagoya.
Pakistan sealed 25-18, 25-18, 25-20 victory, their second which put them in the last eight.
At the Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park Gymnasium Pakistan controlled the contest from the opening set, establishing an early advantage and maintaining enough pressure to prevent Uzbekistan from mounting a sustained comeback.
Pakistan took the first set 25-18, building a seven-point cushion. Uzbekistan struggled to close the gap as Pakistan kept control of the exchanges and moved in front in the match.
The second set followed a similar pattern. Pakistan again reached 25 points while limiting Uzbekistan to 18, putting the match within reach of a straight-sets victory.
Uzbekistan showed greater resistance in the third set, but Pakistan remained in control and managed it 25-20 to complete the sweep.
Pakistan manager Naseer Ahmad was happy with the outcome.
“Today we played well,” Naseer told The Express Tribune from Japan.
“We could win 3-0 even against Kazakhstan but you know it was the first game and boys needed some adjustment,” said Naseer, also a former Pakistan captain. However he was hopeful that they would also be able to beat tough Japan.
“Our charges have the capability to beat Japan and you know how tough team Japan is but we will try our level best to beat them,” said Naseer, who has massive experience of playing professional leagues.
The Pakistani lineup included setter Abu Bakar Siddique, outside hitters Afaq Khan and captain Murad Jehan, opposites Muhammad Yahya, Murad Khan and Fahad Raza, setters Hamid Yazman and Siddique, middle blockers Jabran, Muhammad Hamad and Musawer Khan, and libero Khizar Hayat.
Usman Faryad Ali also featured among Pakistan's outside hitters.
Hong Kong's Leung Yin Yan served as first referee and Qatar's Fahad Mohammed I A Alawadhi as second referee. Pakistan will now meet hosts Japan in their last group show on Tuesday.
Pakistan had defeated Kazakhstan 3-1 in their opener on Sunday. Top two teams from each four groups progress to the quarter-finals.

title: China s space diplomacy lifts Pakistani astronaut toward orbit
description: The voyage into space would be a first for the    South Asian nation
content:
The voyage into space would be a first for the ‌South Asian nation
Two Pakistani pilots are memorising Mandarin, spinning in centrifuge drills and learning to eat, sleep and repair equipment while weightless ​as a decision nears on which one will become the first foreign astronaut aboard China's Tiangong space station.
The voyage into space would be a first for the ‌South Asian nation. It is part of broader cooperation with Beijing that straddles the Belt and Road Initiative and has produced Chinese-launched Pakistani satellites, a joint satellite-navigation system and a Pakistani-built rover due to fly on China's Chang'e 8 lunar mission around 2028.
Pilots Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud have spent months training at the China Astronaut Research and Training Centre in Beijing for a mission that was conceived by the two countries in 2019, said Amer Gilani, who ​oversees human spaceflight cooperation at Pakistan's space agency, SUPARCO.
China has not said which of the two will fly or when, but Gilani said a final astronaut selection decision is expected ​in mid-to-late October.
Pakistani pilots Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud are training in China, hoping one will become the country's first astronaut aboard China's Tiangong space station. Ariba Shahid explains https://t.co/et7eroNba0 pic.twitter.com/ZcOxoX3wfM
Whoever is chosen will not return to Pakistan before launch, setting off into space directly from training in China and returning home ⁠after a recovery period following the return to Earth, Gilani told Reuters in an interview.
Training includes intensive Chinese-language instruction, learning spacecraft systems, and adapting to both the microgravity of orbit and the g-forces ​of liftoff, he added.
Read: NASA, ESA astronauts set for spacewalk to replace key antenna
The two men beat out roughly 20 finalists culled from an initial Pakistani pool of pilots and scientists, screened for medical fitness, psychological resilience and, according to SUPARCO's director of ​artificial intelligence Uzair Ansari, a tolerance for g-forces that few scientists possess.
"You cannot easily find scientists who are familiar with travelling and facing high-level g-forces," he said, explaining this is why the two men with backgrounds in high-speed flying were chosen.
The details shared by Gilani and Ansari are the first insight provided by SUPARCO to foreign media since the pilots were selected and deployed to China.
China's space agency did not respond to a request for comment about ​the selection process.
Once in space, the chosen pilot will carry the title of "payload specialist", which is astronaut-speak for someone whose job in orbit is running Pakistan's science experiments rather than flying ​the ship, Ansari said.
Of more than 300 proposals SUPARCO fielded from universities in Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad after a year-long campaign, Gilani said Chinese institutes picked four for this flight: biotechnology experiments that will help combat food ‌insecurity and ⁠climate change.
Every experiment is built and pre-tested in SUPARCO's own labs before Chinese engineers sign off — a rare case, Ansari said, where Pakistani technology gets validated on an international platform.
The scientific payload is modest next to a station that has already hosted more than 180 experiments and produced over 500 research papers and 150 patents, Ansari added.
Read more: SpaceX piece 'slammed' into Moon
Tiangong's three modules — Tianhe, Wentian and Mengtian — weigh about 77 metric tons combined and house roughly 14 experiment racks spanning life sciences, materials, fluid physics, combustion and radiation exposure, Gilani said, including some mounted outside the station and exposed directly to space for materials and biotechnology ​payloads.
The astronaut will fly aboard a ​Chinese-built spacecraft, launched from a Chinese site, ⁠trained by Chinese instructors and communicating in Mandarin in orbit.
Pakistan has no independent launch vehicle or crewed spacecraft of its own, and the stay itself will be about a week, a fraction of the roughly six-month rotations of career Chinese crew members.
The Pakistani astronaut is due to return with two ​members of a Chinese crew that arrived at the space station in May because the third member is expected to stay for a year ​to enable the study of ⁠long-duration human physiology in space.
Since Yuri Gagarin's 1961 first flight, citizens of about 50 countries have flown in space, but only three nations — Russia, the US, and China — have launched their own crewed spacecraft. China's invitation to Pakistan is the first time it will transport a foreign astronaut.
Asked whether Islamabad had secured any promise to send an astronaut to the moon under the same partnership, Gilani said "there is no official commitment ⁠or discussion on ​this matter," adding that what comes next will depend on how "our maiden mission" turns out.
The Pakistani-built lunar rover that ​is due to fly on China's Chang'e 8 lunar mission around 2028 is a separate strand of that cooperation: it will use AI-based stereo imaging to detect obstacles, judge depth and plan its own path across the lunar surface, since Earth-based ​controllers cannot guide it in real time, Ansari said.
Still, Ansari was clear that the mission is a "once-in-a-lifetime opportunity" for Pakistani scientists.

description: Toxanbayeva is disqualified for wearing shoes not approved by World Athletics
content:
Toxanbayeva is disqualified for wearing shoes not approved by World Athletics
Kazakh race walker Yasmina Toxanbayeva's Asian Games gold medal has been annulled following ‌disqualification from the women's marathon event for wearing unsanctioned shoes.
Toxanbayeva crossed first in the event on Sunday in three hours, 22 minutes and 20 seconds, nearly four minutes ahead ⁠of China's runner-up Danzengquzong, but the results remained provisional pending a protest.
"Athletes must wear only those shoes approved and listed on a World Athletics platform. She was not wearing one, which is why we wrote to World Athletics," a technical official said on Monday.
"Cancelling the gold was their ‌decision, ⁠which we conveyed to the athlete. The athlete has a right to appeal to the jury, and she has done that."
Toxanbayeva confirmed the annulment on social ⁠media.
"We fought until the end," she said in an Instagram post. "Thank you to all my super-heroes who fought ⁠with me to the very end."
Danzengquzong was upgraded to the gold, with compatriot Ma Li ⁠earning silver ahead of Japan's bronze-winner Yukiko Umeno.
