content:
Brent rose $1.32, or 1.27%, to $105.64 a barrel by ​0536 PKT; US WTI was at $93.11 a barrel, up 70 ​cents, or 0.76%
Oil prices rebounded more than 1% on ‌Monday after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace deal from Iran to resolve their conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, keeping tensions in the Middle East elevated.
Brent crude futures rose $1.32, or 1.27%, to $105.64 a barrel by ​0536 PKT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $93.11 a barrel, up 70 ​cents, or 0.76%.
Iran announced a peace proposal last week at the UN ⁠General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the Americans via Qatari ​mediators. Trump said on Saturday he rejected the plan, but told Axios in a phone ​interview on Sunday that he expected US negotiators to engage in more talks this week.
Read: Iran Guards claim seizure of US underwater drone in Hormuz, US denies
"Geopolitical risks remain elevated, as the Houthis and Iran continued their attacks on Saudi Arabia, leaving regional supply flows vulnerable," ANZ ​analysts said in a note.
Yemen's Saudi-led coalition said early on Saturday it had intercepted two ballistic ​missiles and two drones launched by the Houthis towards the kingdom.
Brent edged up 0.4% last week, but ‌WTI lost 7.9% on concerns that the US may ban diesel exports to ease record prices, which could curb US refining output.
"Refined oil products remain a pressure point, with record US diesel prices intensifying inflation risks and prompting renewed debate over potential export curbs," ANZ analysts said.
Any restriction ​on US diesel exports ​would tighten supply outside ⁠the US, with European prices reacting to the prospect of reduced American supply, they added.
Read more: Oil slips ahead of US announcement
Meanwhile, crude oil exports from key Middle East producers rebounded ​in September to 12.8 million barrels per day, the highest since ​the war ⁠started in February, preliminary data from Kpler showed on Monday, as Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates boosted exports.
The rebound came following a recovery in shipments via the Strait of Hormuz, ⁠which were ​set to hit about 7.4 million bpd this month, ​the data showed, as Saudi Arabia diverted exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu to its eastern Ras ​Tanura port following attacks that damaged its East-West pipeline.

title: Messi scores but Miami suffer Columbus defeat
description: Thiare strikes in stoppage time to lift Crew to a 2 1 victory
content:
Thiare strikes in stoppage time to lift Crew to a 2-1 victory
Lionel Messi scored a brilliant equalizer but could not prevent Inter Miami suffering a costly 2-1 defeat to Columbus Crew in Major League Soccer on Sunday.
Argentina superstar Messi curled in a superb free-kick in the 33rd minute to silence the Columbus home crowd after Josef Martinez had fired Crew ahead from the penalty spot five minutes earlier.
But Messi's 21st goal of the regular season proved to be in vain as Crew dug deep to frustrate Inter Miami for long periods.
Messi almost put Miami ahead in the 62nd minute when he burst forward and shot at goal, only to see his effort tipped over by Crew goalkeeper Patrick Schulte.
Miami thought they had taken the lead moments later when substitute David Ayala darted clear of the Columbus back four and crashed a shot past Schulte at the near post.
But the goal was chalked off after Ayala was ruled fractionally offside.
Columbus meanwhile looked lively at the other end, and new Moroccan signing Anass Zaroury twice hitting the woodwork, including with one spectacular long-range effort that cannoned off the underside of the bar.
The game looked to be heading for a draw but deep into stoppage time Columbus grabbed a winner.
Brais Mendez unleashed a curling shot from the edge of the area which Miami goalkeeper Rocco Rios Novo failed to secure.
Senegalese substitute Jamal Thiare reacted quickest and lashed home the close-range finish to secure all three points for Columbus.
The defeat dealt another blow to Miami's already faint hopes of catching Nashville at the top of the Eastern Conference.
Miami now trail leaders Nashville by 14 points with seven games of the regular season remaining.
Columbus meanwhile remain in the hunt for a playoff place, and are in 12th spot on 29 points - four points outside the postseason places.

title: Rain sends Pakistan  India into Asian Games cricket semis
description: Both quarter finals are washed out without a ball bowled as higher seeded  Pakistan and India advance to the last four
content:
Both quarter-finals are washed out without a ball bowled as higher-seeded Pakistan and India advance to the last four
Pakistan and India advanced to the Asian Games men’s cricket semi-finals on Monday after rain forced the abandonment of their quarter-finals without a ball being bowled.
Pakistan’s match against Hong Kong was called off at the scheduled toss after incessant showers left large parts of the Nisshin ground under covers.
Pakistan, one of four seeded teams alongside India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, progressed on the basis of their higher ICC ranking and will face the winners of Tuesday’s quarter-final between Bangladesh and Malaysia on Thursday.
Hong Kong reached the last eight after finishing second in Group B, beating Malaysia by eight wickets before losing to Oman by 41 runs.
The abandoned match would have been the third T20 meeting between Pakistan and Hong Kong, with Pakistan winning the previous two at the 2022 Asia Cup and 2023 Asian Games.
India also advanced after their quarter-final against Afghanistan was washed out before the toss.
India’s higher seeding secured their place in the last four, while Afghanistan exited the tournament after another rain-affected encounter with India at the Asian Games.
India will meet the winners of Tuesday’s quarter-final between Nepal and Sri Lanka in Thursday’s second semi-final.
Sri Lanka, another seeded team, will advance if their match against Nepal is also abandoned. They are among the four teams, with India, Pakistan and Bangladesh, that entered the quarter-finals directly.
Afghanistan won silver at the 2023 Hangzhou Games after their final against higher-seeded India was abandoned following 18.2 overs of the first innings.

title: M 1  GT Road reopen between Islamabad  Peshawar after PTI postpones march
description: Restoration work underway on the M 14 motorway between Hakla and Kundal
content:
Authorities remove containers, spiked metal sheets, other barriers along major routes
The M-1 motorway between Islamabad and Peshawar was reopened to all traffic in both directions on Monday, while the N-5 Grand Trunk Road between the two cities was also restored, the motorway police spokesperson said.
The reopening eased restrictions that had been imposed on major transport routes connecting Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) with the federal capital ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) planned march on Islamabad. The roads were reopened after PTI postponed its march from September 27 to October 4.
However, restoration work remained under way on the M-14 motorway between Hakla and Kundal, as well as on the link road connecting the M-1 with the Hazara Motorway, the spokesperson said.
Traffic from Islamabad to Abbottabad via the M-1 could exit at Burhan Interchange, use the GT Road through Hassan Abdal and rejoin the Hazara Expressway at Jhary Kas Interchange, the spokesperson added.
Read: Protest postponement: govt reopens GT Road
The National Highways and Motorway Police (NHMP) had earlier listed the M-1 as closed in both directions between Swabi and Islamabad Toll Plaza, with southbound traffic diverted from Swabi Interchange.
The E-35 Hazara Motorway, too, had been closed in both directions between Jharikas and Burhan, while the entire Hakla-to-Yarik section of the M-14 was affected by restrictions.
Restrictions were also imposed on the M-2 North , including the Islamabad-bound route for heavy transport vehicles between Kot Momin and Islamabad. On the N-5, traffic restrictions were imposed in both directions at Attock Khurd, with diversions provided through HPT, Deser Star and Suzuki Motors.
The restrictions affected movement between Islamabad and several areas of K-P and northern Punjab including Haripur, Taxila, Hassan Abdal, Attock and Rawalpindi.
Reports from Haripur had indicated that routes towards Taxila, Hassan Abdal, Attock, Rawalpindi and Islamabad had been blocked with containers. Traffic queues were also reported around Jharikas and Hassan Abdal.
The major routes had been closed or restricted at several points last week as authorities took security measures ahead of the PTI march, which was originally scheduled for September 27. Authorities had cited security and law-and-order concerns for the restrictions.
Following the postponement of PTI's march, authorities began removing containers , spiked metal sheets and other barriers placed along the GT Road and the M-1 and M-14 motorways.
Read More: Punjab seals routes as PTI march nears
The operation to clear barriers at Attock Khurd on the N-5 was completed late Saturday night, allowing traffic on the GT Road to resume. The M-1, which had been blocked in both directions with containers and mud bags between Swabi and Islamabad, was subsequently reopened for traffic.
The prolonged closure of major routes had disrupted commercial activity in Rawalpindi and Islamabad, with transport terminals reporting reduced activity and daily-wage workers affected by the disruption.
Transporters said goods terminals had remained largely empty while hotels, motels, inns, marriage halls and private hostels had either closed or experienced a sharp decline in business.
Transport Federation Patron-in-Chief Haji Zahoor Arain had called for transport stands inside the cities to be reopened, saying transporters had been badly affected by the closures.

title: Greece hand Klopp first defeat as Germany manager
description: Kourbelis    74th minute strike gives the visitors a historic 1 0 win
content:
Kourbelis’ 74th-minute strike gives the visitors a historic 1-0 win
Jurgen Klopp tasted defeat for the first time as Germany manager as his side lost 1-0 to Greece in Augsburg on Sunday, with Dimitrios Kourbelis scoring the only goal.
In his first game on home soil, Klopp's side offered little in attack and lacked the energy they had displayed on the former Liverpool coach's debut in a 1-1 away draw with the Netherlands on Thursday.
The Germans had struggled to find a way through the Greek defence for the opening hour before the visitors broke through on the counter, with Kourbelis scoring in the 74th minute.
It was Greece's first ever win against Germany.
"Personally, I'm completely unbothered by it. I've lost far more matches in my life than I would have liked," Klopp told ARD.
"But as long as you draw the right conclusions, a loss is ultimately just a piece of information -- no different from a win.
"We absolutely need these kinds of matches -- they are exactly the games we wanted to have."
Germany captain Joshua Kimmich added: "He's been very clear about what he wants -- as players, we need to implement it."
Several regulars missed out with Klopp trying to get a better idea of the talent at his disposal, but the defeat illustrated the scale of his task in reviving the flagging giants.
The 59-year-old took over Germany in July after the four-time World Cup winners were eliminated at the last-32 stage of the global showpiece in North America, their third consecutive early exit from the tournament.
"I think the important thing is that we stand together and that won't change," said Germany centre-back Jonathan Tah.
"Of course, with the enthusiasm surrounding the new coach, things can get very hyped up from the outside, but ultimately, it comes down to what we do on the pitch and how we perform."
Klopp had included 16 uncapped players in his 44-man squad as he warned that he would be using the competition to have a look at the players at his disposal.
Among the five alterations to his starting XI was Hoffenheim forward Bambase Conte, a shock call-up after playing just four top-flight matches.
Conte looked sharp and shot just wide with two minutes gone.
Barcelona forward Karim Adeyemi had the best chance of the opening half when he stormed past the Greek defence on the counter, but sprayed his shot just over the crossbar.
Conte was again dangerous after the break, forcing a low fingertip save from Greek goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis.
With Germany dominating possession but offering little in attack, the visitors grew bolder and more incisive on the counter and should have taken the lead when Fotis Ioannidis blasted wide of the goal with just Alexander Nuebel to beat.
Greece broke through moments later, however, when Kourbelis's low shot took a wicked deflection off Joshua Kimmich and rolled into the bottom left corner.
Greece then held firm for a breakthrough win over Germany, after seven defeats and three draws dating back to 1960.

title: Ireland beat Israel but no handshakes
description: The visitors strike three times before the break to secure victory
content:
The visitors strike three times before the break to secure victory
Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in a Nations League clash on Sunday amid an eerie and sombre atmosphere that saw the Irish players wear black armbands over the war in Gaza.
Ireland's players came out for the match in Hungary wearing black armbands and bowed their heads as the Israeli national anthem was played.
The teams skipped the traditional pre-match handshakes and did not exchange pennants either in a near-empty stadium in Debrecen.
Troy Parrott made a heart sign with his hands after opening the scoring on 14 minutes, while Jack Moylan kissed the Irish badge on his jersey and his black armband after netting the third goal 25 minutes in.
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar accused Ireland of being "on the wrong side of history" over the players' actions.
In a lengthy post on X, Saar referenced the Irish team of 1939 giving the Nazi salute ahead of a match against Germany in Bremen.
He also referred to Irish neutrality during the Second World War and the condolences offered by then-prime minister Eaemon de Valera to the German representative in Dublin following Adolf Hitler's death.
"Almost 90 years have passed. Ireland's unique talent for finding itself on the wrong side of history remains intact," he added.
The game, in which Israel were the nominal hosts, had been in doubt earlier in the week until Ireland's players voted overwhelmingly to fulfil the fixture, despite pressure from back home to boycott the match.
Only one player, goalkeeper Gavin Buzunu, pulled out, saying "it would be wrong to participate" in either this match or the return fixture in Serbia on October 4 due to the "killing of innocent people".
Ireland has long been a strong supporter of the Palestinian cause, with sympathy often linked to the country's own history of British rule.
Dublin formally recognised a Palestinian state in 2024 alongside Spain and Norway, and has repeatedly criticised Israel over the Gaza conflict.
Israel strongly rejects allegations its conduct in Gaza amounts to genocide.

Jorge Jesus's men have responded well to their tame World Cup last-16 loss to Spain, having also beaten Wales 1-0 in Group A4 on Thursday.
The 41-year-old Ronaldo was named among the substitutes for the first time for Portugal since a Nations League game against Scotland in September 2024, and did not get onto the pitch as Jesus looks to manage his minutes across an expanded international break.
World Cup quarter-finalists Norway were left to rue some wasteful finishing in front of goal as they failed to build on their opening 3-2 win over Denmark.
The first big chance fell to Erling Haaland, but the Manchester City striker mishit his attempted volley after being picked out by Martin Odegaard, and Portugal goalkeeper Diogo Costa was able to make the save.
The away team quickly made Haaland pay as Joao Felix stroked a fine finish into the bottom corner from the edge of the box in the 17th minute.
Haaland looked certain to equalise shortly afterwards when Costa spilled the ball into his path, but he was denied by a superb block from his City teammate Ruben Dias.
The Norway talisman was foiled by Costa again 10 minutes before half-time as the 'keeper made an excellent stop from his downward header.
Haaland finally converted six minutes into the second half, tapping in from Patrick Berg's header across goal.
But Norway gave back the lead immediately to their opponents, as goalkeeper Orjan Nyland passed the ball straight to Ramos, who coolly chipped it into the net.
Rafael Leao had a shot deflected onto the crossbar as Portugal pushed to make the game safe.
Nyland had his blushes spared when a VAR review ruled out another opportunistic Ramos effort for the tightest of offsides.
The 'keeper waited for a long pass over the top to reach him, then took a swipe at thin air as Ramos got to the ball before him and rolled it into an empty net.
Norway threw everyone forward, including Nyland, in the closing stages, but could not find another leveller.

title: Zverev stars as Team Europe win Laver Cup
description: The world number two beats Tien 7 6  6 3 to seal the trophy
content:
The world number two beats Tien 7-6, 6-3 to seal the trophy
Alexander Zverev clinched Team Europe's Laver Cup victory over Team World as the two-time Grand Slam champion beat Learner Tien at London's 02 Arena on Sunday.
World number two Zverev battled to a 7-6 (7/3), 6-3 win against Tien, ensuring Team Europe regained the Laver Cup with tournament co-founder Roger Federer watching in the stands.
Team Europe wrapped up their 13-5 success against Team World on the final day of the exhibition event, which started on Friday.
Zverev's Team Europe colleague Carlos Alcaraz this week said the German was the best player in the world after his French Open and US Open victories this year.
The 29-year-old struggled to live up to that billing when he lost in the doubles on Friday and let slip multiple match points in a defeat against Alex De Minaur on Saturday.
But world number three Alcaraz wrestled back the initiative on Saturday before Zverev teamed up with Casper Ruud to win in the doubles.
That left Team Europe only two victories from the trophy in Sunday's session.
Flavio Cobolli and Jakub Mensik moved Team Europe a step closer by beating Team World duo Taylor Fritz and De Minaur in the doubles.
Zverev saved a set-point in the first set against Tien before overwhelming the 20-year-old American in the second set to seal the silverware for Yannick Noah's squad.
It was only the second victory for Team Europe in the last five editions of the Ryder Cup-style event, which started in 2017 and does not award ranking points.
"I haven't won a match here in two years, so I'm happy that I did it today," Zverev said.
"Massive credit to the entire Team World. They pushed us all the way again. They were champions last year.
"This year, we had a great team chemistry and I'm very happy that we won."

title: USA captures 11th consecutive Presidents Cup
description: Bridgeman sinks a four foot par putt on 18 to seal a 1 up win over Min Woo Lee
content:
Bridgeman sinks a four-foot par putt on 18 to seal a 1-up win over Min Woo Lee
The United States made a stunning rally to capture an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup on Sunday, defeating the Internationals 17-13 in a victory dedicated to US President Donald Trump.
Jacob Bridgeman secured the clinching point at Medinah Country Club by sinking a four-foot par putt at the 18th hole to defeat Australian Min Woo Lee 1-up.
"I'm just so damn proud of this team," US captain Brandt Snedeker said. "All these guys, they fought for each other. They fought for this country. They fought for this team."
Snedeker said Trump -- who visited the Chicago-area course for Sunday's final day -- should take credit for the win.
"He told me (he) was going to bring some energy today for you guys. You guys need it," Snedeker said. "And I told him if we did this, he gets all the credit. So thank you, President Trump."
The Americans improved to 14-1-1 in the biennial rivalry after trailing 10.5-7.5 entering 12 concluding singles matches, the Internationals poised to end a 28-year win drought but failing.
"It was on a knife edge all day," Internationals captain Geoff Ogilvy of Australia said. "It's a very difficult thing to beat the US in singles in the US. They all played great."
The Americans had nine wins and a draw on the final day.
"I don't think I'd do anything differently," Ogilvy said. "It sort of drifted the wrong way all day."
The non-European side's lone win was in 1998 at Australia with a shared trophy at South Africa in 2003.
The Americans, boasting eight of the world's 11 top-ranked golfers, won on the same suburban Chicago layout where Europe took the 2012 Ryder Cup with the famed "Miracle at Medinah" fightback.
"These guys never lost faith," Snedeker said. "I told the guys last night that funny stuff happens here. Medinah's got a history of funny things happening, and sure enough, they went out there and played their asses off. I'm so damn proud of those guys."
Drama built with every match and ended with Bridgeman, who won his second PGA Tour title last week, falling behind for the first time with a bogey at 15 only to win 16 and 18 with pars.
"It was the coolest moment," he said. "I felt like I held in my emotions all day. To let it out on the last hole is pretty sweet."
Cameron Young secured the first US point, beating Japan's Ryo Hisatsune 3&2. He won holes 11-13 for his first lead and made a 32-foot birdie putt at 16 to win.
Justin Thomas, 0-3 in Cup singles, won the first four holes and never trailed in beating Canada's Corey Conners 5&3, sinking a 15-foot birdie putt at 15 to win.
South Korea's Tom Kim answered with a 3&2 victory over reigning US Open champion Wyndham Clark.
"I was second off. I really felt it was a responsibility to put a point up," said Kim, who will fly to Japan for the Asian Games.
Top-ranked Scottie Scheffler, 3-1 this week, birdied five of the first 10 holes and never trailed in beating Colombian Nico Echavarria 2&1.
South Korean Im Sung-jae rattled in birdies on four of the last six holes to beat Sam Burns 3&1, while Chris Gotterup beat South Africa's Christiaan Bezuidenhout 1-up.
The Americans seized a 13.5-12.5 lead when Patrick Cantlay edged Australian Adam Scott 2&1 and moments later Collin Morikawa beat Japan's Hideki Matsuyama 1-up.
Cantlay was never behind but needed a 57-foot birdie putt at 16 and a seven-foot par putt at 17 to win.
Morikawa tied his match at 15 on a 30-foot birdie putt and won when Matsuyama missed a 15-foot par putt at 18.
"I'm happy about that closing point," Morikawa said. "That was huge."
Jackson Koivun, a 21-year-old rookie, beat South Korean 2-up.
Canada's Nick Taylor tied Russell Henley and Xander Schauffele edged New Zealand's Ryan Fox 2&1 after the Cup was decided.

title: Terrorist commander killed in Lakki IBO
description: Terrorist commander killed in Lakki IBO
content:
A local terrorist commander wanted in seven serious terrorism cases was killed during a joint operation by police and the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) in the Abdul Khel area of Lakki Marwat, police said on Sunday.
The slain militant was identified as Manzoor, son of Izzat, a resident of Abdul Khel. Police said he was allegedly involved in attacks on civilians and was wanted by the CTD in seven cases registered in connection with serious acts of terrorism.
The operation was launched after terrorists attacked a group of young men travelling in a loader rickshaw after returning from a cricket match near Abdul Khel. The attack left three youths dead and three others injured.
Following the incident, a heavy contingent of police and CTD personnel reached the area on the directives of District Police Officer Lakki Marwat Sajjad Ahmad Sahibzada and cordoned it off. A search and combing operation was subsequently launched under the supervision of the DPO.
The joint operation continued for several hours, during which security personnel exchanged fire with suspected terrorists. During the encounter, Manzoor was killed, police said. His body was taken into custody and shifted for further legal proceedings. According to police records, the slain terrorist commander was wanted by CTD Bannu in seven serious terrorism cases registered between December 2024 and September 2026. The cases involve charges related to terrorism, attempted murder, attacks on police personnel, damage to property and other serious offences.
Police and CTD personnel have continued an extensive search and combing operation in the surrounding areas to locate and apprehend other suspected terrorists involved in attacks in the region.
Officials said the operation would continue until the area had been thoroughly searched and the presence of other militants had been ruled out.

title: Razmak hospital faces alarming neglect  decay
description: Razmak hospital faces alarming neglect  decay
content:
Rusting equipment, poor sanitation and unsafe medical waste disposal raise serious health concerns
Despite the allocation of millions of rupees in funds and resources, the Category-D hospital in Razmak, a remote and mountainous area of North Waziristan, is grappling with severe neglect.
Disturbing images circulating from the facility have sparked serious questions about hygiene standards, the upkeep of medical equipment and the provision of basic amenities under the management of HANDS Foundation.
Local residents express deep concern over the hospital's condition, warning that the situation poses risks of infectious diseases, including hepatitis and AIDS. They have urged senior officials to take strict notice and ensure immediate remedial measures.
Photographs from the hospital reveal clear signs of rust on various medical instruments, beds and trolleys. In one image, surgical tools lie in a tray with visible corrosion and stains on their metallic surfaces. Another shows patient beds in a dilapidated state, accompanied by worn-out and damaged furniture and medical supplies. The presence of a used syringe near the floor in one section of the hospital further highlights deficiencies in the safe disposal of medical waste and overall cleanliness protocols.
Social activist Noor Jamal, a local resident, noted that Razmak is an extremely remote area where this hospital serves as a vital source of healthcare for the public. "If the medical equipment and environment here are not properly maintained, it will directly affect patients and the people of the region," he said.
He pointed out growing public anxiety over contagious diseases, particularly hepatitis B and C as well as HIV/AIDS, stressing the urgent need for rigorous hygiene, sterilised instruments and the secure disposal of used syringes.
Another local resident, Malik Mudasir Khan, questioned how basic facilities and sanitation could remain so poor despite substantial funding allocated to the health sector. "The government and relevant institutions should not merely allocate funds; they must also regularly monitor their utilisation and the quality of services provided at the hospital so that the public genuinely benefits," he added.
Residents emphasise that used syringes and medical waste left in open or unsecured areas can endanger public health. Proper cleaning and sterilisation of medical instruments rank among the fundamental requirements of any hospital. The issue carries particular weight for the people of Razmak and adjoining areas because the difficult terrain makes it hard to transfer patients quickly to larger hospitals. In emergencies, the local Category-D facility remains the primary centre for initial medical care.

title: Early winter chill grips Shangla district
description: Early winter chill grips Shangla district
content:
Artisans begin preparing traditional stoves and heaters
A noticeable change in weather has gripped Shangla during the final week of September, signalling the early arrival of winter conditions across the district. In the upper mountainous regions, the intensity of cold has begun to rise sharply, prompting residents to prepare their homes for the colder months ahead.
Following recent spells of rain and hail in the higher elevations, temperatures have dropped considerably. The sudden dip has increased the severity of the chill, forcing families to take proactive measures against the approaching cold. In homes across the upper areas, the traditional process of preparing and installing iron stoves, locally known as 'angheethis', and heaters or 'bukharas' has already started. These time-tested heating devices remain essential for keeping living spaces warm during the harsh winter that Shangla typically experiences.
Local artisans who specialise in handcrafting these iron stoves, heaters and other heating appliances have also become active once again. In various parts of the district, skilled craftsmen have resumed work to meet the rising demand. Markets in Alpuri, Bele Baba, Dherai, Shahpur Kana and other localities are witnessing renewed activity as these artisans reopen their shops and set up temporary workshops.
The early preparation reflects the community's familiarity with the region's climate. Residents understand that delays can leave households vulnerable once heavy snowfall and prolonged cold set in. By starting arrangements now, families aim to ensure their homes remain comfortable throughout the winter season.
As the weather continues to cool, the sight of glowing stoves and the sound of hammers shaping metal in local workshops are becoming more common. The coordinated efforts of residents and craftsmen highlight how Shangla is steadily gearing up for the cold months, blending traditional methods with timely practical steps to face the changing season.

title: Vegetable  fruit prices stay above official rates

content:
Consumers in Lahore continued to face high food prices this week as most perishable vegetables' rates increased and retail prices of several essential items remained substantially above government-notified rates.
Despite reductions or no change in official rates for several commodities, consumers continued to pay substantial premiums in the markets, with significant gaps recorded in vegetables, poultry and fruits.
The poultry market highlighted the disparity between official price lists and retail rates. Live chicken remained officially priced at Rs294308 per kg, while chicken meat was fixed at Rs446 per kg. However, chicken meat continued to sell for Rs500560 per kg.
Live birds remained largely unsold across the city.
The vegetable market recorded a predominantly upward trend, with several essential perishables becoming more expensive during the week.
Sugar-free potatoes remained unchanged at Rs2730 per kg on the official list but sold for Rs5070 per kg. Tomato rates were reduced by Rs35 on the official list to Rs110150 per kg, but retailed at Rs200240 per kg.
Official onion rates increased by Rs15 to Rs185195 per kg, while the vegetable sold for Rs220250 per kg.
Local garlic increased by Rs20 per kg to Rs185195 per kg but retailed at Rs250300 per kg. Thai ginger recorded a sharp Rs55 per kg increase, reaching Rs370385 per kg officially, but sold for Rs450500 per kg. China ginger also sold for Rs450500 per kg.
Fruit prices also remained significantly higher than official rates.
Apples were officially priced at Rs155395 per kg but sold for Rs300500 per kg. A-grade bananas were fixed at Rs160175 per dozen but retailed at Rs200250, while B-grade bananas were fixed at Rs120130 but sold for Rs150180 per dozen.

Kandhari pomegranate increased by Rs10 to Rs352370 officially but sold for Rs700800 per kg. Local pomegranate remained unchanged at Rs335350 per kg but retailed at Rs450600 per kg.

The universities organising the test were required to provide candidates the sheets carrying carbon copies and to preserve the examination record for a specified period.
The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) had also directed the universities to provide a mechanism for rechecking and to display the official answer key.
One of the most likely sources of an apparent discrepancy is improper marking of the sheet. The MDCAT instructions had stated that an improperly filled bubble would be treated as an incorrect response. Since the sheet is processed electronically, an incomplete or unclear marking can produce a result different from expected.

title: rooftop Solarisation
description: Solarisation transforms rooftop life
content:
Energy needs encroach on summer family gatherings
For generations, rooftops remained a cherished part of family life, particularly in Multan, where the fierce summer heat sent families upstairs at dusk to welcome the cooling breeze, gather under the fading light and in many homes, surrender to sleep beneath the vast, star-studded sky.
But that cherished summer ritual is now quietly giving way to a new rooftop reality, as gleaming rows of solar panels increasingly spread across residential buildings, turning once-open family spaces into sources of power.
What was once an open space for family gatherings, children' s play and sleeping during hot nights is now being used by many households to generate electricity. In several residential areas, large portions of rooftops are covered with rows of solar panels, mounting structures and related equipment.
For many families, the decision to install solar systems is primarily linked to rising electricity costs and the desire to generate their own power. However, the growing use of solar energy has also changed the way residents use and view their rooftops.
People used to see the rooftop mainly as an open family space. Now they also see it as an opportunity to generate electricity, a solar system installer, Muhammad Asif, said.
He said homeowners were increasingly planning the placement of solar panels carefully to make maximum use of available rooftop space while keeping some portion open for household activities.
For families that traditionally slept on rooftops during summer, the change has been particularly noticeable. With solar systems helping households run air conditioners and other appliances during the day, some residents said they were relying less on rooftops at night.
A government employee, Antique Chaudhary, said members of his family had reduced or stopped sleeping on the roof because much of the available space was now occupied by solar panels.
He said the daytime use of air conditioning also helped keep rooms cool, reducing the need to move upstairs after sunset.
The difference is also being felt by older residents who remember when the rooftop was considered a natural extension of the home.
During hot summer nights, families used to carry charpoys and bedding upstairs after sunset. Children played around while elders sat and talked late into the night, said a local NGO worker, Rana Arif.
He said spending time on the rooftop was once part of normal summer life for many families. Today, the same rooftops often look very different.
Solar panels, metal mounting structures, wiring and other equipment have become permanent features of many homes. Some residents are also cautious about using areas close to the panels for sleeping or recreational activities.
Yet, for most homeowners, solar energy offers a practical benefit that outweighs the loss of open rooftop space. The ability to generate electricity from sunlight has encouraged families to make a different calculation about how their rooftops should be used.
Muhammad Asif said some households had adapted by leaving a portion open or creating sitting areas beneath the panels.
In this way, the rooftop is not completely disappearing from family life; its purpose is changing, he explained.
The shift reflects changing priorities among urban households. A generation ago, rooftops were valued mainly for open space, ventilation and family activities. Today, they also have economic value as locations for electricity generation.
For Multan, where summers are long and sunlight is abundant, rooftops offer readily available space for solar installations. The trend is visible in both newly constructed houses and older homes, where residents are modifying existing rooftops to accommodate solar systems.
The change has created a challenge for the families of balancing the economic benefits of solar power with the traditional uses of their rooftops.
While some households have made electricity generation their priority, others are retaining small open areas for sitting, relaxing and spending summer evenings together.
The transformation is increasingly visible, with rooftops that once came alive after sunset with charpoys, family conversations and children's games now spending much of the day generating electricity.
The city's solar transition is therefore changing not only how homes consume power but also how families use one of the most familiar spaces in their homes.

title: HFH gets 15 probes for cancer treatment
description: HFH gets 15 probes for cancer treatment
content:
Cases of liver, lung, breast and kidney cancer being filtered at four Pindi hospitals
After the installation of a cryoablation machine, 15 probes have reached Holy Family Hospital for the treatment of cancer patients. Each probe, costing Rs1.6 million, will be used for one patient.
The process of filtering cases of patients suffering from liver, lung, breast and kidney cancer has been started at four hospitals in Rawalpindi.
According to details, patients suffering from breast, lung, liver and kidney cancer whose cancer tumour is up to two centimetres in size can be treated through the cryoablation machine.
For this purpose, cancer tumour cells found in the four organs will first be frozen at a temperature of minus 180 degrees Celsius.
Once the cancer cells are frozen and rendered ineffective, they will be heated to a temperature of 100 degrees Celsius and burnt.
This will enable patients suffering from breast, lung, liver and kidney cancer to get rid of the disease.
In this regard, a formal circular has been issued to Holy Family Hospital Rawalpindi, Benazir Bhutto General Hospital, Rawalpindi Teaching Hospital and Pakistan Kidney and Liver Institute (PKLI) Rawalpindi, directing them to filter cases of patients suffering from the four types of cancer whose tumour size is up to two centimetres and send their cases to Holy Family Hospital.
Before treatment is started on the cryoablation machine at Holy Family Hospital, consultation will be sought from doctors at Noor Hospital Islamabad.
After this, the treatment process of patients found fit for cancer treatment will be started.
Sources said that in the first phase, 15 probes have been handed over to Holy Family Hospital for 15 cancer patients who are to be treated through the cryoablation machine. One probe, costing Rs1.6 million, will be used for each patient.
Complete cancer treatment through the cryoablation machine will be provided free of charge and no fee will be charged. Coordination between Noor Hospital and Holy Family Hospital has also started in this regard.
Medical Superintendent of Holy Family Hospital Rawalpindi Dr Ijaz Butt said the protection and maintenance of the cryoablation machine would be the responsibility of the company that installed the machine at Holy Family Hospital. Security cameras are also being installed for the protection of the machine.

title: When the Leaves Speak  opens
description: When the Leaves Speak  opens
content:
Exhibit explores climate change, ecological vulnerability through miniature painting
"When the Leaves Speak," an exhibition by Pakistani artist Farrah Mahmood Rana, has opened at Zwischenraum at MARKK – Museum am Rothenbaum in Hamburg.
Farrah Mahmood Rana is a Pakistani artist working with the visual and technical language of South Asian miniature painting. Her practice develops contemporary narratives around nature, memory, identity, and ecological relationships.
The exhibition presents 16 artworks alongside a hands-on workshop in traditional miniature painting, bringing South Asian artistic knowledge into dialogue with contemporary concerns about climate change, ecological vulnerability, memory, and interdependence.
In Rana's work, nature is not a passive backdrop but a narrative voice. On hand-prepared wasli paper, she uses trees, lotus flowers, fish, eggs, and connecting dots as recurring symbols of vulnerability, resilience, renewal, and interconnectedness.
The exhibition approaches climate change as both an ecological and emotional crisis, encouraging audiences to consider the relationships between human life and the natural systems that sustain it.
This emphasis on interconnected vulnerability aligns with international climate assessments that examine impacts across ecosystems, biodiversity, and human communities.
The lotus represents renewal, resilience, and transformation, while eggs evoke birth, fertility, and the continuing cycle of life. Connecting dots form an underlying visual network that links these motifs and suggests the often-unseen relationships among living beings, environments, memories, and experiences.
The project also demonstrates how miniature painting can function as a contemporary language while retaining the discipline of its historical practice.
South Asian miniature traditions are known for meticulous drawing, carefully prepared paper, controlled brushwork, and layered pigment application. Rana reworks this detailed visual vocabulary into an ecological narrative in which craftsmanship becomes a means of reflecting on care, coexistence, and responsibility.
"When the Leaves Speak" connects past and present, cultural tradition and contemporary storytelling. Its intimate scale and detailed imagery invite close looking, while its subject expands outward to questions of collective responsibility and the fragile relationships that connect people with the natural world.
An integral part of the exhibition is a workshop led by Rana, designed to introduce participants to traditional miniature painting techniques.
During the workshop, she taught the Sufaid Qalam technique, giving participants an opportunity to work directly with the disciplined processes of South Asian miniature painting.
The sessions focused on precision, patience, observation, material handling, and the detailed application of line and form, while showing how a time-honoured technique can evolve through contemporary practice.
Participants came from diverse cultural backgrounds, including Kenya, China, Japan, and Iran. Their participation transformed the workshop into a space of international cultural exchange, where miniature painting became a shared point of learning and dialogue. The project therefore extends beyond the display of finished artworks: it also creates an opportunity for artistic knowledge to be transmitted through practice and encountered by an international community.
Curated by Gabriel Schimmeroth and co-curated by Dagmar Rauwald, the project brings exhibition-making, artistic practice, and public learning together. Rauwald's curatorial framework emphasises the workshop as an immersive introduction to a sophisticated South Asian art form and recognises the international connections through which miniature painting continues to develop.
Rana's central proposition is that trust is a living network formed through vulnerability, care, reciprocity, and shared survival.
Fish, lotus motifs, eggs, trees, and connecting dots operate together as a symbolic field in which human and non-human relationships become visible. Through this layered vocabulary, the exhibition proposes that care for nature is inseparable from the relationships through which human life is sustained.

title: Smog hits twin cities before season
description: Smog hits twin cities before season
content:
Government orders action against brick kilns, polluting vehicles and factories
Even before the start of the smog season, the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad, as well as Rawalpindi Division and major cities of the province, have started experiencing smog, prompting the Punjab government to take strict notice and order the Environment Protection and Climate Change Department, Regional Transport Authority, Civil Defence and district administrations to launch an immediate crackdown.
The authorities have been directed to demolish or seal, from October 1, all brick kilns operating without environment-friendly zigzag technology, and take action against smoke-emitting vehicles and factories, as well as those burning garbage and tyres.
At present, Islamabad's air quality index (AQI) has reached 101 and Rawalpindi's 97, while air pollution is being recorded at higher levels in Punjab ahead of the smog season.
Lahore's overall AQI has reached around 210, falling in the unhealthy range, while different areas of the city are recording AQI levels between 207 and 210, placing it among the most polluted cities. In Rawalpindi, the current air pollution index is 97, which falls in the moderate category.
Fluctuations in air quality are also being observed in Faisalabad, Rahim Yar Khan and other areas. At present, the AQI in Murree is 115, Attock 105, and Chakwal district 103.
Under the pre-smog operation, the Punjab government and Environment Protection Department have intensified measures to prevent smog. A crackdown is under way against kilns operating without zigzag technology and industrial units causing pollution.
Hotspots are being monitored round the clock through drone and night squads. Enforcement of the strict ban on burning crop residue and using or burning plastic has also been intensified, with challans and heavy fines being imposed for violations.
Orders have also been issued for strict action against smoke-emitting vehicles, motorcycles, factories and bakeries.

title: Gunmen kill 27 in two shootings in S Africa
description: Gunmen kill 27 in two shootings in S Africa
content:
Gunmen killed at least 27 people in two mass shootings in South Africa's two main cities, Johannesburg and Cape Town, police said on Sunday, in the latest criminal violence to hit the country.
Eight gunmen armed with assault rifles and pistols stormed a bar southwest of Johannesburg at around 1930 GMT on Saturday, killing 17 people and wounding 15 others.
The dead included 13 males and four females.
The suspects opened fire on customers drinking outside and then moved inside to continue shooting, police said.
The shooting took place in Wedela, a semi-rural township of brick houses and small businesses, surrounded by wide expanses of land used for mining. The suspects torched two vehicles before fleeing.
The area has been a focus of a government crackdown on illegal mining, with soldiers deployed alongside police to tackle criminal networks operating around abandoned mine shafts.
"The criminals think it's a fashion. They want to make it something which we need to get used to, but that cannot be allowed and tolerated," deputy provincial police commissioner Major General Fred Kekana said at the scene.
"We managed to get clear pictures of the suspects and we will get them," he said, adding that the attack appeared to have been retaliation for an incident last month.
One of the victims was being sought by police in connection with an incident at the same tavern last month in which one person was killed and another wounded, Kekana said.
In a separate shooting at a barbecue venue in a township outside Cape Town early on Sunday, gunmen killed 10 people and wounded 11 more.
In video clips shared on social media, revellers can be seen dancing and drinking before a burst of gunfire rings out, sending people scrambling for cover.
Five of the victims were declared dead at the scene while the others died while being transported to hospital. Two of those killed were female, police said. AFP

title: Russian strikes on Ukraine  including Kyiv  kill 8
description: Russian strikes on Ukraine  including Kyiv  kill 8
content:
Russian strikes on Ukraine -- including in Kyiv -- killed eight people, Ukrainian authorities said Sunday, a day after Moscow vowed to achieve its war aims "no matter the circumstances."
Russia has stepped up attacks on Ukraine's capital in the fifth year of its invasion, as the country braces for another winter of war, with Ukraine charging that Moscow is deliberately hitting civilian targets.
Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi announced the latest deaths on Sunday afternoon, saying Russian strikes had hit a children's centre in the northern city of Sumy, killing three people including a 16-year-old girl.
Earlier, President Volodymyr Zelensky said three people had been killed in night-time strikes on the southern Zaporizhzhia region and a Russian drone strike had killed one man in Kyiv.
Kyiv Mayor Vitalii Klitschko said a woman and two 16-year-olds had also been wounded and hospitalised in the capital.
"The enemy continues to relentlessly attack the Kyiv region with strike drones," the city's administration said.
"Sixteen sites have been damaged," including 12 private houses in Kyiv's outskirts, as well as a warehouse and production facility, it added.
And authorities in the Odesa region said a "massive strike" on the south of the Black Sea region had killed one more person.
Russian strikes damaged housing, a shop, a hotel, a medical building and a warehouse storing grain, said regional head Oleg Kiper.
"This past week, the Russians launched more than 2,200 attack drones against Ukraine, as well as around 1,650 aerial bombs and 38 missiles of various types, a significant number of them ballistic missiles," Zelensky posted Sunday on social media.
The strikes had targeted housing "and other civilian infrastructure" in various parts of the country, he added.
On Saturday, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told the UN Moscow intended to continue its military campaign "to the end". AFP

Pope Leo XIV on Sunday said assisted dying was not "normal", as he continued a landmark visit to France, where parliament has legalised the practice for certain patients.
"No human law should ever make you lose the certainty of your dignity," he told believers who were sick or suffered from disabilities, at the French pilgrimage site of Lourdes.

title: Iran says Guards seize US drone in Hormuz
description: Iran says Guards seize US drone in Hormuz
content:
Tehran's plan calls for a cessation of all hostilities in ME, including in Lebanon
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Sunday that they seized an American submarine drone in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran has blockaded in the months-long Middle East war.
"Through a coordinated, complex operation involving intelligence oversight and electronic warfare, IRGC naval forces' personnel successfully captured an advanced unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) belonging to the terrorist US military," the IRGC naval forces said in a statement, according to state TV.
They added that the drone was "operating in the Strait of Hormuz for espionage purposes", identifying the model as a Remus 600 autonomous underwater vehicle that was "now in the hands of the force's specialists for data recovery".
US Central Command spokesperson Captain Tim Hawkins denied the claim, saying US maintained "positive control of all of our operational drone assets", describing the IRGC claim as "clearly desperate".
Earlier this month, the Guards said they captured another US submarine drone in the strait that was crucial for oil and gas trade before the Middle East war started in late February and choked off shipping. Iran has maintained a blockade of the Hormuz strait since the outbreak of the conflict, while the United States has imposed a counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump said he anticipated his envoys would take part in negotiations with Iran in the coming days, while adding that Tehran had yet to offer acceptable terms to resolve the ongoing conflict.
"I expect more talks with Iran (this week)," Trump told US news website Axios in an interview, adding: "They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make. It is what we would have maybe agreed to a year ago. They overplayed their hand."
Asked whether Washington was considering resuming military strikes against Iran, Trump said the option remained active.
Iran said it remained firm on its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, despite Trump rejecting the proposal, which had raised hopes of breaking the deadlock in the Middle East war.
The waterway is key to the world's energy supply and is now central to the conflict between Washington and Tehran, which was triggered nearly seven months ago with deadly strikes on Iran.
Iran's plan called for a cessation of all hostilities in the Middle East, including in Lebanon, according to Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, and fulfilling conditions in the ceasefire deal that fell apart months ago. AGENCIES

title: Floods  landslides kill 56 in India  14 in Nepal
description: Floods  landslides kill 56 in India  14 in Nepal
content:
Uttar Pradesh recorded 66.5 mm of rain between Sept 25 and morning of Sept 27
Heavy rain and ?storms have triggered floods and landslides that killed 56 people in India, while in Nepal, 14 have died and another 11 are ?missing, with authorities there warning on Sunday that more flash floods are possible.
India's northern state of Uttar Pradesh recorded 66.5 mm of rain between September 25 and the morning of September 27, compared with a normal 7.6 mm for the period, Hrishikesh Bhaskar Yashod, the state's relief commissioner, said on ?Sunday.
Authorities are carrying out rescue operations in waterlogged areas and distributing relief, while officials have been told to assess crop damage and provide compensation. In addition to the 56 deaths, 46 people have been injured and more than 1,000 houses have been damaged.
Nepali authorities warned of possible flash floods in 49 ?of the country's 77 districts, with more than half facing high flood or flash-flood risks as water levels in major rivers and tributaries continued to rise.
Shanti Mahat, a spokesperson for the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, said Rasuwa and Nuwakot, areas hit by last month's deadly floods that killed more than 1,450 people and left thousands still missing, should remain "alert" but were not currently considered high-risk areas.
Power supply has been completely disrupted in the Manang, Mustang, Myagdi and Baglung districts, with authorities working to restore electricity, energy ministry officials said.
Flooding of the Rahuganga River damaged the structure and transmission-line towers of a 40-megawatt hydropower project, Water Resources and Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said.
In India, the Central Water Commission said 30 river-monitoring stations across seven states indicated a "severe situation". Several major rivers, including the Ganga, Gandak, Kosi, Bagmati and Narmada, were above danger levels.
Floods and landslides also disrupted telecommunications in parts of Nepal after damage to optical fibres and power supplies, Communications Minister Bikram Timilsinha said.
In a separate incident in Nepal, 10 local workers were also missing after an avalanche buried the base camp of the 7,126-metre (23,379-ft) Himlung Himal in the northern Manang district, hiking officials said.
The workers had been setting up tents for foreign climbers, who were not present when the avalanche struck. REUTERS

title: China  US agree on trade  AI cooperation
description: China  US agree on trade  AI cooperation
content:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump have agreed to build a "constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability" based on respect, fairness and reciprocity, according to a statement issued by China's Embassy in Washington, DC.
The understanding was reached during Xi's state visit to the United States from September 23 to 25, during which the two leaders held "in-depth discussions" on bilateral ties and major international and regional issues, the ministry said in a statement.
The two sides reached eight "deliverables and understandings", it added.
Under the first understanding, China and the US agreed to work towards a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on "respect, fairness and reciprocity".
The two countries also agreed to support each other in hosting the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and the G20 Summit. Xi and Trump intend to attend each other's meetings, according to the statement.
On Iran, the two leaders agreed that Tehran should honour its commitment not to develop nuclear weapons. They also agreed that "no country or institution can be allowed to impose tolls on international waterways", without elaborating on the specific waterways or arrangements involved.
China and the US further agreed to establish a China-US AI Dialogue to exchange views on the risks and benefits associated with artificial intelligence.
The next round of the dialogue is scheduled for November 2026, while the two countries will also establish a bilateral communication channel for AI-related incidents.
The announcement comes amid growing international efforts to develop mechanisms for managing the risks associated with increasingly advanced AI systems.
Meanwhile, the Chinese and US militaries agreed to conclude a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on crisis communication and prevention "as soon as possible".

title: Over 70 terrorists killed in Balochistan
description: Over 70 terrorists killed in Balochistan
content:
President, PM pay tribute to security forces for successful operations
Security forces have killed more than 71 terrorists in Operation Shaban and other intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan over the past 96 hours, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Sunday.
According to the military's media wing, 23 of the terrorists were killed during the last 72 hours. It said security forces had cleared a vast area and relieved local communities of the threat posed by terrorists.
"As the Army's operation progresses, more than 71 terrorists have been killed so far in Operation Shaban and other areas of Balochistan in the last 96 hours, delivering a serious blow to Indian-backed Afghan proxies," the ISPR said.
Operation Shaban was launched following credible intelligence about multiple hideouts of Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan terrorists in the general area of Shaban in Quetta district, which posed a threat to the local population.
The term Fitna al-Khawarij is used for terrorists affiliated with the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, while Fitna al-Hindustan refers to banned outfits sponsored by India in Balochistan.
"Security forces launched a swift operation in Ziarat and surrounding areas on September 21. During the operation, troops engaged the terrorists and cleared multiple hideouts. Following intense exchanges of fire, 33 Indian-sponsored terrorists were killed, while a significant quantity of weapons, ammunition and explosives was also recovered," the ISPR said.
According to the ISPR, the operation was further intensified over the past 72 hours, resulting in the killing of 23 terrorists. Security forces cleared a vast area and relieved local communities of the threat posed by Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan. "The clearance operation is continuing until complete neutralisation of the threat," it said.
In a separate IBO in Nushki district on September 25, security forces engaged a terrorist hideout and killed 11 Indian-sponsored terrorists. In another operation in Mand, six Fitna al-Hindustan terrorists were killed, while a large quantity of weapons and ammunition was recovered, the ISPR said.
The ISPR also said the involvement of the Afghan Taliban regime in terrorist activities in Pakistan, backed and sponsored by India, continued to cause loss of precious lives and threaten peace and stability.
"The counter-terrorism campaign under the vision of Azm-e-Istehkam, approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, will continue with full resolve," it said. "Security Forces and Law Enforcement Agencies remain committed to eliminating foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country," the ISPR added.

title: Islamabad rejects Taliban s Nuristan allegations
description: Islamabad rejects Taliban s Nuristan allegations
content:
The Ministry of Information on Sunday rejected allegations by the Afghan Taliban regime linking its security forces and intelligence agencies to violence in Afghanistan's Nuristan province, calling the claims "frivolous, baseless and devoid of any truth".
"Pakistan categorically rejects the fabricated claims of involvement by its security forces or intelligence agencies in any internal clashes in Nuristan or elsewhere in Afghanistan, including allegations of recruiting or training former Afghan security personnel or facilitating Daesh or any other terrorist group operating in Afghanistan," said the ministry in a statement.
The statement came in response to allegations levelled by the Afghan Taliban's Ministry of Defence, which claimed that groups affiliated with Daesh, along with what it described as "elements of subversion", had crossed the Durand Line into Nuristan's Kamdesh district with the support of Pakistan. The ministry claimed that its security forces had killed 28 of the alleged infiltrators and captured 32 others, while the remaining fighters fled back across the Durand Line.
The ministry further responded to the allegations, stating that not a shred of evidence had been produced to substantiate Pakistan's involvement
"There were no identities, documents, communications, forensic evidence or independent verification to support the allegations," it said.
The statement also rejected a video being circulated on social media to support the false claim, saying that it "only shows a few unarmed individuals who are not even properly dressed or equipped.'
The ministry described the footage as appearing to be "a pre-planned video shoot by the Afghan Taliban regime well known for lies and fabricated claims".
The fact-check graphic attached to the post carried the text, "Afghan Defence Ministry claims arrest of Pakistani military personnel and fighters in Nuristan." It marked the claim as "false and fabricated" and displayed a document by the Afghan Ministry of Defence dated September 27.
The ministry said the presence and activities of terrorist groups inside Afghanistan were "well documented", including in successive reports by the United Nations and other international organisations.
"Attempts to manufacture a Pakistani connection cannot obscure the reality that these terrorist groups continue to find sanctuary and a permissive environment for growth in Afghan territory," it said.
"It is particularly ironic for the Afghan Taliban regime to accuse Pakistan of supporting terrorism while terrorist organisations operating from Afghanistan continue to pose a direct threat to Pakistan and regional security," the ministry added.
"Instead of externalising responsibility for its internal security challenges through fanciful allegations, the Afghan Taliban regime should take credible and verifiable action against terrorist organisations operating from its territory," the ministry said.
It also called on the Afghan authorities to fulfil their commitments that Afghan soil would not be used for terrorism against Pakistan or any other country, "rather than attempting to deflect responsibility through fabricated accusations".
The statement further added that the allegations were "reflective of lies to externalise internal dissent and oppression of women, children and minorities".
This is not the first time the Afghan Taliban regime has levelled allegations against Pakistan. In the past, it has accused Pakistan of facilitating infiltration, carrying out airstrikes and smuggling weapons into Afghanistan, allegations that Islamabad has repeatedly rejected.
According to security officials, the Afghan Taliban regime has been providing sanctuary, support and patronage to terrorist groups. They said documented evidence contradicted Kabul's repeated denials and pointed to an entrenched terrorist network operating from Afghan soil.
Pakistan maintains that the terrorist nexus extended beyond the movement of terrorists across the border to their training, arming and operational support.
Security officials estimate that up to 70 per cent of the Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists infiltrating Pakistan were of Afghan origin. They further claim that the Taliban regime had allowed leftover US and NATO weapons to reach terrorist groups, including Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan.
In 2026 alone, terrorism emanating from Afghan soil claimed the lives of 1,327 Pakistanis and injured another 2,484, according to figures cited by Pakistani authorities.
The United Nations estimated the strength of TTP in Afghanistan at around 6,000 to 6,500 terrorists. UN reporting had also documented more than 600 terrorist attacks against Pakistan during 2025, including attacks launched from Afghan territory.
According to Pakistani security officials, the TTP had established training facilities in Afghanistan's Kunar, Nangarhar, Khost and Paktika provinces.
The government has maintained that the issue was fundamentally one of Pakistan's national security and that continued attacks from Afghan soil cannot be addressed through denials alone.
Pakistan says it expected the Taliban regime to fulfil its commitments by taking verifiable action against terrorist groups operating from its territory rather than defending or denying their presence.

title: Prospects for Pak Afghan ties reset appear bleak
description: Prospects for Pak Afghan ties reset appear bleak
content:
Official says relations between neighbours have reached 'a point of no return'
Pakistan's already troubled relations with the Afghan Taliban regime appear to have reached a point where a diplomatic reset is becoming increasingly difficult, as officials privately acknowledging that the relationship could deteriorate further.
There had been hopes that a recent diplomatic push involving Türkiye and Qatar might open the door to some form of engagement between Islamabad and Kabul.
The Turkish intelligence chief and Qatar's deputy national security adviser travelled to Kabul in a bid to explore ways of easing tensions between the two neighbours.
The Turkish intelligence chief also travelled to Islamabad as part of the regional effort. But the diplomatic initiative appeared to collapse before it could get off the ground.
A day after the Turkish and Qatari officials held engagements in Kabul, the Kohat police lines were rocked by a deadly terrorist attack. One of the suicide attackers was identified as an Afghan national.
For Pakistani officials, the attack reinforced their longstanding concern that terrorist groups operating from Afghan soil continue to pose a direct security threat to Pakistan. Islamabad subsequently launched what it described as calibrated strikes against terrorist hideouts inside Afghanistan.
The Taliban regime responded by sending rudimentary drones towards Pakistani territory, according to Pakistani officials, but the drones were neutralised before causing casualties or significant damage.
Pakistan then carried out a fresh series of strikes against what officials described as drone storage facilities and launch sites at around 10 locations inside Afghanistan. One of the sites was in Kandahar, the spiritual headquarters of the Afghan Taliban.
"They (Taliban) may have taken some steps to address Pakistan's concerns, but those measures are not enough and are cosmetic in nature," said a senior Pakistani official dealing with the matter.
The latest escalation has also cast a shadow over Türkiye's efforts to facilitate communication between Islamabad and Kabul. There have been reports that the Turkish intelligence chief was not accorded the level of access expected during his visit to Kabul.
According to the source, the Turkish delegation had initially expected to meet Taliban Amir Haibatullah Akhundzada in Kandahar. However, Akhundzada later deputed a member of his staff to meet the visiting delegation. The move was not well received by the Turkish side, the source said.
The outcome of the latest diplomatic push did not surprise Pakistani policymakers. "We know the Taliban so well. They are not going to mend their ways," the official said.
The official acknowledged that, given the current trajectory, relations between the two neighbours were likely to become even more strained. "We have, I think, reached a point of no return," the official said in a candid assessment.
Another factor increasingly shaping Islamabad's calculations is the emergence of armed resistance against the Taliban regime in parts of Afghanistan.
The recent developments in Nuristan are particularly significant. Hundreds of fighters belonging to the Afghanistan Freedom Front (AFF), an anti-Taliban group, claimed to have captured several Taliban positions in Kamdesh district.
The Taliban offered a different account, saying the attack had been repulsed and alleging that the fighters had crossed from Pakistan. Islamabad rejected the allegation, saying Kabul had provided no evidence to substantiate the claim.
Pakistani policymakers, however, believe the Taliban regime's repeated accusations against Pakistan could have an unintended consequence: further weakening its own position against armed opposition groups.
For years, some anti-Taliban elements had viewed the Islamabad-Kabul tensions as largely tactical, believing that Pakistan remained, in one form or another, an ally of the Taliban. That perception, an official said, discouraged some of these groups from openly challenging the Taliban regime.
But as tensions between Islamabad and Kabul deepen, and the Taliban leadership itself increasingly accuses Pakistan of supporting or facilitating its opponents, anti-Taliban groups may conclude that the old understanding no longer exists.
The result, according to the official, could be greater pressure on the Taliban's writ in parts of Afghanistan. "If the Taliban regime's writ is challenged further, it won't be a surprise," the official said.

title: Over 70 terrorists killed in Balochistan
description: Over 70 terrorists killed in Balochistan
content:
President, PM pay tribute to security forces for successful operations
Security forces have killed more than 71 terrorists in Operation Shaban and other intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan over the past 96 hours, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Sunday.
According to the military's media wing, 23 of the terrorists were killed during the last 72 hours. It said security forces had cleared a vast area and relieved local communities of the threat posed by terrorists.
"As the Army's operation progresses, more than 71 terrorists have been killed so far in Operation Shaban and other areas of Balochistan in the last 96 hours, delivering a serious blow to Indian-backed Afghan proxies," the ISPR said.
Operation Shaban was launched following credible intelligence about multiple hideouts of Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan terrorists in the general area of Shaban in Quetta district, which posed a threat to the local population.
The term Fitna al-Khawarij is used for terrorists affiliated with the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, while Fitna al-Hindustan refers to banned outfits sponsored by India in Balochistan.
"Security forces launched a swift operation in Ziarat and surrounding areas on September 21. During the operation, troops engaged the terrorists and cleared multiple hideouts. Following intense exchanges of fire, 33 Indian-sponsored terrorists were killed, while a significant quantity of weapons, ammunition and explosives was also recovered," the ISPR said.
According to the ISPR, the operation was further intensified over the past 72 hours, resulting in the killing of 23 terrorists. Security forces cleared a vast area and relieved local communities of the threat posed by Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan. "The clearance operation is continuing until complete neutralisation of the threat," it said.
In a separate IBO in Nushki district on September 25, security forces engaged a terrorist hideout and killed 11 Indian-sponsored terrorists. In another operation in Mand, six Fitna al-Hindustan terrorists were killed, while a large quantity of weapons and ammunition was recovered, the ISPR said.
The ISPR also said the involvement of the Afghan Taliban regime in terrorist activities in Pakistan, backed and sponsored by India, continued to cause loss of precious lives and threaten peace and stability.
"The counter-terrorism campaign under the vision of Azm-e-Istehkam, approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, will continue with full resolve," it said. "Security Forces and Law Enforcement Agencies remain committed to eliminating foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country," the ISPR added.
