title: Iran Guards claim seizure of US underwater drone in Hormuz  US denies
description: Trump says they want to make deal to open Hormuz Strait immediately because they re losing so badly
content:
Trump says he expects more talks with Iran this week, warns Tehran 'overplayed' hand
The US military on Sunday denied a claim by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) that it had seized an advanced US underwater drone conducting surveillance in the Strait of Hormuz, Al Jazeera reported.
US Central Command spokesperson Captain Tim Hawkins said that the US maintained “positive control of all of our operational drone assets”, describing the IRGC claim as “clearly desperate”.
Earlier in the day, the IRGC Navy said it had seized a United States Remus 600 autonomous underwater vehicle operating in the Strait of Hormuz and that the vessel was “now in the hands of the force’s specialists to retrieve its information”.
IRGC said the vehicle had been captured using intelligence and electronic warfare capabilities and was being examined by Iranian specialists to recover its data.
Footage showing a second US underwater drone seized in the Strait of Hormuz. pic.twitter.com/8U1balrhLg
Trump says he expects more talks with Iran this week, warns Tehran 'overplayed' hand
US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that he anticipated his envoys would take part in negotiations with Iran in the coming days, while adding that Tehran had yet to offer acceptable terms to resolve the ongoing conflict.
"I expect more talks with Iran (this week)," Trump told US news website Axios in an interview, adding: "They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make. It is what we would have maybe agreed to a year ago. They overplayed their hand."
Asked whether Washington was considering resuming military strikes against Iran, Trump said the option remained active.
After nixing Iran proposal, Trump tells Axios he expects talks this week https://t.co/YREe8GfiKT
The remarks follow indirect diplomatic exchanges last week on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, where Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner via Qatari mediators.
Tehran reportedly offered to reopen the strategic Strait of Hormuz and restart nuclear talks within a week on the condition that Washington lifted its naval blockade, removed sanctions on oil sales, and reinstated a regional ceasefire.
Trump rejected the proposal on Saturday, as the two nations remain locked in the seven-month Iran war that began with large-scale strikes by the US and Israel in late February.
Iran's army voices readiness for potential renewed US attack
Iran's armed forces were prepared for any ​renewed US attacks, state media quoted ‌army spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia saying on Sunday, after US President Donald Trump said he rejected an ​Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait ​of Hormuz and end fighting.
Akraminia said Iran's ⁠armed forces were fully prepared for ​confrontation and warned that the US would ​suffer greater damage if it launched another attack on his country.
Iran’s Army spokesperson: Should the enemy perpetrate further aggression, Iran's armed forces shall, with enhanced preparedness and capability, deliver a response more devastating, more extensive, and more resolute than ever before. pic.twitter.com/u7tnCnyIj4
War with US 'not over', says Iran's army commander
Separately, Iranian Army Commander-in-Chief Amir Hatami said the war with the US was at a "critical and decisive" stage, Al Jazeera reported.
According to Al Jazeera , Hatami added, “The war is not over; we have won, but we must consolidate this victory, and the aggressor enemy, which has suffered severe blows, must still be ready to receive severe blows from the dear Iranian soldiers.”
Iran’s army chief, Major-General Amir Hatami, says the war with the US is not over and is now in its “critical and decisive” stage. 🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/3wmSBiCp3Y pic.twitter.com/mdieHuuZKt
“We are proud to be the soldiers of a country that today stands against the embodied evil of the United States and the Zionist regime and has humiliated them,” he stated, adding, “This is Iran, and it is not a place for their excesses and arrogance.”
Responding to the notion that the Iranian government would fall after the series of assassinations that the US and Israel carried out at the beginning of their war, Hatami said that this was a “miscalculation by the enemy,” Al Jazeera reported.
The commander highlighted the assassination of Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei on February 28, the first day of the war.
He also said Tehran would not accept a situation where it could not trade while foreign powers used the region's strategic waterways. "If Iran cannot trade, if Iran cannot live, no one will be able to trade or live. The Strait of Hormuz is the strait of our dignity and honour, and it will not be allowed for the country's enemies to use this major logistical chokepoint. At the same time, the Iranian people are deprived,” he said, according to Al Jazeera.
Seven killed in strike on market in Yemen, Houthi-run health ministry says
Yemen's Houthi-run health ministry said seven people were killed and 40 injured, including children, in a strike on shops at a market in the Mawiya junction in Taiz province.
Later, Yemen's internationally recognised government said its forces had targeted a Houthi military camp and vehicles at the same junction.
Three military sources within the Yemeni government told Reuters that Houthi militants had recently established a military camp near the market.
Military support to Saudi Arabia ‘defensive’: French FM
French military support being given to Saudi Arabia to help it confront attacks from the Houthis was “strictly defensive,” French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said on Sunday.
Barrot's comment, made on state television network France 2 , followed President Emmanuel Macron’s announcement on Thursday of French troops, radar units and “defence systems” being sent to Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia has come under repeated missile and drone attacks from the Houthis, after Yemen’s war reignited in July after a years-long truce, adding another front to the Middle East war.
The attacks have targeted Saudi oil installations and the key oil terminal of Yanbu.
Asked whether France’s aid meant that Paris had become a partner in Saudi Arabia’s war against the Houthis, Barrot said: “Absolutely not... This is strictly defensive.”
French military support to Saudi Arabia is “strictly defensive,” says French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot. Read more: https://t.co/LzmSebe8Ah
He added that “since the start of the (US-Israeli) war against Iran, we have deployed military assets to protect our allies, our partners”.
“Does that mean at any time we can be considered co-belligerents? Never.”
Barrot said the scale of the French deployment to Saudi Arabia would depend on what Riyadh requested, as well as “our own capacities and how the situation develops”.
Bessent says Operation Economic Outcast 'delivering results'
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in a statement on X early Sunday morning, said that following the launch of Operation Economic Outcast, the Treasury Department "imposed targeted financial measures against banks and aviation service providers."
"At my direction, teams were dispatched across the globe to engage with countries and demand action against the Iranian regime," Bessent said. He added that the efforts "are delivering results."
Following the launch of Operation Economic Outcast, @USTreasury imposed targeted financial measures against banks and aviation service providers. At my direction, teams were dispatched across the globe to engage with countries and demand action against the Iranian regime. These…
According to the treasury secretary, Turkiye and Oman "announced the cessation of Mahan Air flights to their countries," while the UAE "has halted all flights by Iranian airlines." Bessent also added that "top commercial banks in the UAE and Turkiye have stopped transacting with Iran."
"Even Iran’s leadership has acknowledged the economic toll of the war, as the value of the rial has fallen to record lows," he said.
Bessent concluded his post with writing, "I appreciate the governments of the UK, Turkiye, Oman, and the UAE. We will continue working together as there is more to be done to prevent Tehran from carrying out its terrorist agenda."
Earlier, Iran insisted that only diplomacy ​can solve its conflict with the US and Israel after US President Donald Trump said he rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait ‌of Hormuz and end fighting.
"Our conditions are clear, and any move toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent on these conditions being met," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi posted on social media. "Only a negotiated solution can get them out of this deadlock."
Iran announced a peace proposal last week at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the Americans via Qatari mediators. ​Trump said on Saturday he rejected the plan and argued that desperation was driving the Iranians’ push for an agreement on the key waterway.
"They want to make ​a deal to open the Hormuz Strait immediately because they're losing so badly," Trump told reporters at the White House.
Despite Trump's ⁠public statements, mediators facilitating Iran's talks with the United States have not officially relayed a US rejection of the plan, according to Araqchi.
"We are waiting for the mediators to ​convey the definitive views to us, and we will make a decision based on them," Araqchi posted.
Read: Iran awaits US move after WSJ report says Trump rejects peace plan
The US has imposed an economic blockade on Iran to put pressure on ​Tehran to stop Iranian attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, which have drastically reduced shipping through the area even as Trump repeatedly asserts that the US controls the waterway.
The Wall Street Journal first reported that Trump had rejected the Iranian proposal, citing unnamed US officials.
It said Trump was privately skeptical that Iran would meet his demands and had told his staff that he sees ​a renewed bombing campaign as likely after the November US midterm elections.
A US official had said earlier that discussions with Iran through mediators were "positive and constructive."
Pezeshkian says Iran cannot be ''besieged", praises China and Russia
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, during an interview with Al Jazeera , said China and Russia had provided Iran with significant political and economic support, adding that the country could not be “besieged”, IRNA reported.
President @drpezeshkian to Al Jazeera: China and Russia helped us big time politically and economically. Iran can't be besieged. pic.twitter.com/WdzqE6AB04
He also said that "the attack on Saudi Arabia's pipelines was carried out neither by Iran nor by the Resistance groups" during the interview.
In an interview with Al Jazeera, Iranian President @drpezeshkian said: The attack on Saudi Arabia's pipelines was carried out neither by Iran nor by the Resistance groups. pic.twitter.com/I3Zldehew7
Iran says Hormuz reopening hinges on conditions, diplomacy remains open
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that Tehran’s main message during meetings on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly was that reopening the Strait of Hormuz would depend on conditions set by the Supreme National Security Council (SNSC), stressing that Iran had never closed the door to negotiations, while maintaining its rights, IRNA news agency reported.
Speaking to Iranian reporters in New York, Araghchi said Iran had maintained an active diplomatic presence at this year’s UN gathering. President Masoud Pezeshkian returned to Tehran after holding multiple meetings, giving interviews and delivering a major address, the minister said.
The foreign minister noted that he also met with foreign officials and counterparts.
Iran says Hormuz reopening hinges on conditions, diplomacy remains open https://t.co/b1L9eeXjD6 pic.twitter.com/qJgv3SVMDi
He said Iran’s conditions for reopening the strait were clearly presented and defended in all meetings and conveyed to mediators, who then communicated them to the US side.
Araghchi said Iran had also presented several diplomatic proposals, but had yet to receive a formal response through the mediators. He noted that statements by the US president had been contradictory and said Tehran was awaiting a definitive position before deciding its next steps.
The minister said Iran had demonstrated its strength in military, diplomatic and economic spheres and argued that a negotiated solution based on dignity, justice and legitimate rights was the only way forward.
IRGC Navy warns US warships could be targeted in Indian Ocean
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy has warned that US warships, including those operating in the Indian Ocean, could be targeted if Washington launches a new war against Iran, Al Jazeera reported.
The navy of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has threatened to attack US warships, including in the Indian Ocean, if Washington launches a new war against Iran. 🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/3wmSBiCWTw pic.twitter.com/Edb1yEI70Z
Oman pledges to safeguard Strait of Hormuz navigation, urges Iran-US settlement
Oman pledged on Saturday to continue safeguarding navigation through the Strait of Hormuz while urging Iran and the US to resolve their disputes through a lasting political settlement.
Addressing the 81st UN General Assembly in New York, Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi said the conflict that erupted earlier this year with US-Israeli strikes on Iran has threatened regional security and disrupted shipping and trade through the strategic waterway.
He said the disruption affected energy security, prices and confidence in the international system.
Albusaidi said Oman is committed to protecting navigation through the strait in line with international law and the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.
He urged all parties to cooperate with Muscat in efforts to ensure passage through the chokepoint while respecting the interests of countries that depend on it.
The foreign minister also urged Tehran and Washington to resolve outstanding disputes and pursue political understandings that could provide a lasting way out of the crisis.
Albusaidi voiced solidarity with neighboring countries on measures taken to protect their security, sovereignty and territorial integrity.
Conflict has disrupted oil flows, harmed global economy
The Iranians also engaged their Saudi rivals regarding the Strait of Hormuz, underscoring the stakes of a seven-month-old conflict that has disrupted oil flows through a critical shipping ‌lane and ⁠taken a toll on the global economy.
Araghchi told reporters at the United Nations on Friday the proposed deal would trigger a seven-day countdown to reopening the strait and a pause in regional fighting.
"If there is seriousness on the US side to come to a deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, everything is now prepared," Araghchi said. If the US were to agree, the warring parties could start wider talks "on mutually agreed subjects."
That could potentially include discussions of Iran's nuclear program. Trump has said Tehran must never acquire a ​nuclear bomb, while a senior Iranian official told ​Reuters that Iran would show no flexibility ⁠over its nuclear program even if the US accepted its peace deal.
Read More: Iranian flights cancelled as new US 'D-Day' sanctions take effect
Iran would grant no concessions over its rights, including enriching uranium or shipping its highly enriched uranium out of the country, the official said.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, in an interview with the ​ CBS show "Face the Nation", said Tehran was ready for talks on its nuclear program and other issues, but would not accept "bullying ​or coercion".
"Iran is not ⁠seeking war, but will defend itself against pressure, threats and attacks,” Pezeshkian said, adding that it had already agreed that "we're not supposed to develop nuclear weapons".
Previous attempts at diplomacy have failed to end the war, which began on February 28 with US and Israeli attacks.
Since then, the war has alternated between pauses and renewed strikes, killing thousands while degrading the conventional ⁠forces of Iran ​and damaging its already ailing economy.
Iran and its allies have retaliated by extending the conflict throughout the ​region. Iran has struck US allies in the Gulf with drones and missiles while its Houthi allies in Yemen have targeted Saudi interests.

title: University Road project to be completed within two months  Sharjeel
description: Says University Road has reached the final stages and that  difficulties faced by commuters has largely been overcome
content:
Says University Road has reached the final stages and that difficulties faced by commuters has largely been overcome
University Road is finally within touching distance of completion, Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon said, announcing that the entire project would be completed within two months. “Now we can say University Road has been built.”
Sharjeel made the announcement while inaugurating the Mosamiyat Flyover, a key component of the Red Line BRT project, on Sunday. Sindh Minister Saeed Ghani and Karachi Deputy Mayor Salman Abdullah Murad were also present at the inauguration.
Memon said work on University Road had reached the final stages and that the difficulties faced by commuters had largely been overcome. He said the Sindh government was working round the clock for Karachi’s development, with different departments engaged in infrastructure and other development projects across the city.
“Those who say that no work is being done in Karachi, I want to tell them that work is taking place,” he said. The senior minister said Karachi’s size brought challenges on an equally large scale, but maintained that the city was also home to the country’s best healthcare system.
On the Red Line project, Sharjeel said the Mosamiyat Flyover was an important part of the corridor and would soon be available for public use after the necessary formalities. Work on stations and other components of the BRT was also progressing, he added.
He acknowledged the delay in the project and apologised to the residents, saying several issues had contributed to the delays. Despite increases in the cost of the dollar, cement and petrol, he said, work had continued.
Responding to questions about political protests, Sharjeel Memon criticised the PTI over protests that, according to him, had brought Islamabad to a standstill. He urged political parties to adopt a mode of protest that did not cause hardship to ordinary citizens.
Memon said the PPP had also staged protests in the past and its workers had faced arrests, but claimed that the party had never held demonstrations by putting the public through unnecessary trouble.
When asked about criticism from MQM-P leader Wasim Akhtar, Sharjeel said the provincial government did not give importance to such statements and accused the MQM of political point-scoring.
He further added that the government's responsibility was to deliver projects rather than engage in blame games, adding that political parties should also consider the inconvenience caused to ordinary citizens by their actions.

title: Robert Pattinson reacts to  Joker  fan casting after Primetime role
description: Robert Pattinson addresses  Joker  fan casting after his Chris Hansen role in Primetime and praises Barry Keoghan
content:
Robert Pattinson addresses 'Joker' fan casting after his Chris Hansen role in Primetime and praises Barry Keoghan
Robert Pattinson has responded to fan calls for him to play the Joker in the DC Universe following his performance as Chris Hansen in Primetime .
Pattinson portrays Hansen, the host of the reality series To Catch a Predator , in the new film. His performance has sparked discussion among DC fans, with some suggesting that the actor could take on the role of Batman’s iconic nemesis.
Asked about the fan casting by Entertainment Weekly , Pattinson acknowledged that the Joker is a major role but pointed to Barry Keoghan, who has already portrayed the character in Matt Reeves’ The Batman .
Robert Pattinson declines the possibility of playing the Joker — following comparisons to his performance in 'Primetime' 🃏 “Oh, Jesus. I mean, it’s such a great part… but Barry’s the man. I loved doing that scene with him so much ... I think he’s such a phenomenal actor. It… pic.twitter.com/xadMI2YPe9
“Oh, Jesus. I mean, it’s such a great part,” Pattinson said, before praising Keoghan. He recalled enjoying working with the actor and said he would rather see Keoghan continue as the Joker.
Pattinson currently plays Bruce Wayne and Batman in Reeves’ The Batman franchise. The first film ended with a brief encounter between Keoghan’s Joker and Paul Dano’s Riddler, while an extended scene released after the film showed Batman visiting the Joker in Arkham Asylum.
It remains unclear whether Keoghan will return as the Joker in The Batman: Part II . The sequel has been in production since June 2026 and is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on February 18, 2028.
Pattinson is confirmed to reprise his role as Batman, alongside Jeffrey Wright as Jim Gordon, Andy Serkis as Alfred Pennyworth and Colin Farrell as the Penguin. Scarlett Johansson is also part of the cast in an undisclosed role.
Meanwhile, Primetime has brought Pattinson renewed attention for his portrayal of Hansen, while the actor continues to balance projects outside the DC franchise. His comments make clear that, despite the Joker speculation, he is not currently seeking to replace Keoghan in the role.

Chris Rock teases 'Grown Ups 3' and discusses working with his daughter Zahra, who joins the comedy sequel
Chris Rock has teased what fans can expect from Grown Ups 3 , revealing that the long-awaited comedy sequel is going well and giving a glimpse into working with his youngest daughter, Zahra Rock.
Speaking at the New York Film Festival premiere of Misty Green on September 26, Rock said the cast is having a great time filming the third instalment of the Grown Ups franchise. He also raised expectations for the upcoming movie, saying fans will be surprised by how good it is.

Rock previously revealed Zahra’s casting earlier this month while discussing his daughters, Zahra and 24-year-old Lola, in a video for Variety. He recalled that both girls grew up around the Grown Ups films and said it was special to now have Zahra appearing in the latest instalment.
Zahra also has a small role in Misty Green , which premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival earlier this month. She attended the New York Film Festival screening with her father.
The returning Grown Ups cast will also include Salma Hayek, Maria Bello, Maya Rudolph, Joyce Van Patten, Steve Buscemi and Shaquille O’Neal, along with Jackie Sandler. Sunny Sandler and Sadie Sandler are also expected to appear.
New additions include Bailee Madison, Deon Cole and Julie Bowen.
Grown Ups 3 does not yet have an official release date. The film’s story will follow the longtime friends as their now-grown children join them for what has been teased as their ultimate adventure.

title: Bill Gates says global AI framework    more difficult    to create than cold war nuclear limitations
description: The tech pioneer said AI monitoring would not hamper the US race with China to develop superior technology
content:
The tech pioneer says AI monitoring will not hamper the US race with China to develop superior technology
Microsoft co-founder and billionaire Bill Gates warned on Sunday that getting countries to agree to a global framework on artificial intelligence could be “more difficult” than Cold War-era negotiations to limit nuclear weapons.
“This is more difficult than that was,” Gates told NBC News ’ “Meet the Press” during a wide-ranging discussion on AI.
Gates also addressed US President Donald Trump’s stance against regulating AI, with Trump rejecting calls for the federal government to impose guardrails for companies building AI models.
The tech pioneer argued that regulating AI companies with monitoring systems would not hamper the US in any race with China to develop superior technology.
Read More: OpenAI, Anthropic CEOs called to appear at Australian AI probe
“What he said is fine, but I think after he hears from me and other people, including that this does not handicap us in whatever he thinks the nation-state race is, that, you know, we will come to a consensus,” he said.
The billionaire later highlighted other times the US led the world in coming up with broad agreements to protect humanity since World War II, with its friends and allies, citing the global challenges of “aviation safety, ozone layer, nuclear weapons, a lot of things where we played the fair actor, not aggrandizing whatever our unique strengths were.”
He added: “And AI is one we’re going to have to go back to this:, ‘Hey, humanity is all in this together’.”
The debate comes in the wake of recent incidents of AI agents going beyond what many experts thought possible, spurring industry insiders to issue warnings and call for stricter regulation of the sector.

title: The Love Hypothesis stars address possible Reylo fanfic Easter Egg
description: What a little link  What a little Easter egg that would be   Reinhart said
content:
“What a little link. What a little Easter egg that would be," Reinhart said
The Love Hypothesis stars Lili Reinhart and Tom Bateman have addressed a possible Easter egg in the Prime Video adaptation that could reference author Ali Hazelwood’s fan fiction roots.
Before Hazelwood published The Love Hypothesis as a novel in 2021, the story originated as a “Reylo” fan fiction featuring Star Wars characters Rey and Kylo Ren. The original story was titled Head Over Feet and was published on Archive of Our Own.
The film adaptation includes a romantic montage featuring the Go-Go’s song “Head Over Heels”. Given the similarity between the song title and the original fanfic’s title, fans have wondered whether the music choice was an intentional nod to Hazelwood’s early writing.
Reinhart, who plays Olive Smith in the film, was asked by Entertainment Weekly whether the song was an Easter egg for fans familiar with Hazelwood’s fanfic history. “It’s a good question,” she said, before suggesting that director Claire Scanlon would be the person to answer it.
Reinhart explained that music supervisor Julia Michels worked closely and intentionally with Scanlon on the film’s music. She also recalled that Scanlon had already selected “Head Over Heels” while they were filming the montage.
Bateman, who plays Dr. Adam Carlsen, similarly remembered Scanlon being very certain that the Go-Go’s track would accompany the scene. He said she played the song for the actors while they were shooting.
Reinhart acknowledged that the connection would make for a fitting Easter egg, saying, “What a little link. What a little Easter egg that would be.” Neither actor, however, confirmed that the song was deliberately chosen as a reference to Head Over Feet.
The actors also discussed their own potential fan fiction interests during the interview, with both joking that they would be interested in Shrek and Donkey fan fiction. Bateman, who is married to Star Wars actress Daisy Ridley, has previously discussed the fan fiction origins of The Love Hypothesis.
The Love Hypothesis is now streaming on Prime Video.

title: SHO martyred in gunfight with smugglers in Malagori
description: Funeral prayer of the martyred SHO is offered with full state honours at Police Lines Khyber
content:
Funeral prayer of the martyred SHO offered with full state honours at Police Lines Khyber
Station House Officer (SHO) of Malagori Police Station, Riaz Hussain Afridi, was martyred after sustaining serious injuries in an exchange of fire with smugglers of non-customs-paid vehicles in the Khyber tribal district of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.
According to District Police Officer (DPO) Khyber Waqar Ahmad, SHO Afridi was critically wounded during an operation against the smugglers. He was immediately shifted to a hospital in Peshawar for medical treatment but later succumbed to his injuries.
Police said two non-customs-paid vehicles were seized from the scene after the firing. A search operation was underway in the area to arrest the accused. The vehicles were being transported to Mohmand district via the Malagori route. Further investigations into the incident were continuing.
The funeral prayer of the martyred SHO was offered with full state honours at Police Lines Khyber. A large number of high-ranking civil and military officials, the martyr’s family members and local residents attended.
Among those who participated were Chief Secretary Shahab Ali Shah, DPO Khyber Waqar Ahmed, Deputy Commissioner Khyber Shahid Ali, military officials, Special Assistant to the Chief Minister Azmat Saeed and Member of the Provincial Assembly Abdul Ghani.
Mourners paid tribute to the services of the martyred officer. After the funeral prayer, his body was taken to his ancestral village, Ghandi, for burial.

title: England rout Sri Lanka to seal ODI series
description: Tom Banton   s maiden ODI century powers England to a crushing win at The Oval
content:
Tom Banton’s maiden ODI century powers England to a crushing win at The Oval
LONDON: ​England’s ​Tom Banton struck a first One Day International century before England’s bowlers romped through the Sri Lanka line-up to ensure a 2-1 series ‌victory, winning the deciding clash by an imposing 223 runs at The Oval on Sunday.
Banton scored 126 ‌after England chose to bat ⁠and ​laid the foundation for a formidable ​total of 355-7 before ‌dismissing Sri Lanka for a ​modest 132. Banton’s innings, which highlighted his expansive range of shots, included five sixes and 16 fours as he mercilessly took ⁠to the visiting bowling after fellow opener Ben Duckett had been ‌castled in the second over.
England captain Harry Brook, who was dropped when he had seven runs, punished Sri Lanka’s poor fielding display with ⁠77 off 66 balls while Jordan ⁠Cox, replacing the injured ​Jos Buttler, ‌made 76 from 52 balls on his return to the ODI side for the first time in almost two years.
England had won the first ODI at Chester-le-Street on Tuesday by 89 runs but lost by 16 runs in Leeds two days later, setting up ⁠Sunday’s deciding tie which turned into a one-sided contest with Sri Lanka bowled ⁠out in 29.1 overs.
Sonny Baker took two balls on his second ODI appearance, one year after his debut, to snag the wicket of Pathum Nissanka, who touched one behind to wicketkeeper Cox, beginning a steady stream of dismissals.
Six of the seven bowlers that England used got among the wickets, ⁠with Liam Dawson finishing with 3-26 in eight ​overs and Gus Atkinson taking 2-26 from five overs.
Captain Kusal Mendis, who scored a ton in the second ODI, top-scored for the visitors with 36 as Sri Lanka never ​looked like being able to chase down ‌the imposing target. (Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Clare Fallon)

title: Miller  Bavuma star in South Africa   s win over Australia
description: Bavuma   s 103 and Miller   s 142 lift Proteas to 365 9 before they bowl visitors out for 333 to seal series
content:
Bavuma’s 103 and Miller’s 142 lift Proteas to 365-9 before they bowl visitors out for 333 to seal series
JOHANNESBURG: Temba ​Bavuma ​and David Miller both struck centuries as South Africa defeated Australia by 32 runs in a high-scoring second one-day international in Johannesburg on Sunday to claim the three-match series with a game to ‌spare.
Australia sent their hosts in to bat and South Africa amassed 365 for nine in their 50 overs, before bowling the visitors out ‌for 333 in 49.5 overs ⁠as they ​continued their dominance over their rivals with a 19th ​ODI win in their last ‌25 meetings.
Australia were again undone by ​spin in the middle of the innings after a fast start to their reply and were not helped by the continued absence of seamer Pat Cummins and ⁠a side strain suffered by Nathan Ellis in the match that meant he bowled ‌only four overs.
"It's really disappointing," Australia captain Mitch Marsh said. "We came here determined to level the series at 1-1 and take it into the final game but fair play to South Africa. ⁠I thought they played really well and outplayed us ⁠again.
"We just want to ​keep improving. We ‌certainly don't want to be whitewashed, so we'll go to Potchefstroom determined to win that final game and play some good cricket." Bavuma scored his 103 from 116 balls for his sixth ODI century, while Miller was more explosive, with nine sixes in his 142 from 93 balls, clearing the ropes with ease as he struck his career-best score and eighth ODI ⁠ton.
Jack Edwards, playing in his second ODI, was the pick of the Australia bowlers with 5-67 in 10 ⁠overs. In a carbon copy of Thursday’s 67-run win for South Africa in Durban, Australia made a lightning start to their reply as Marsh (84 from 53 balls) and Travis Head (84 from 76 balls) put on 130 in 17 overs for the first wicket.
But the middle order struggled and South Africa’s three spinners tightened the screw. Keshav Maharaj (2-54), Bjorn Fortuin (2-70) and Aiden Markram (1-55) were all effective in their 10 overs. Xavier Bartlett ⁠kept Australia in the game with a fine 50 runs ​from 28 deliveries. "It was another really good all-round team performance," Bavuma said.
"It started with the bat. Conditions were a little tricky up front but we managed to get through that period and build towards a good total. "David played an unbelievable ​innings and then the bowlers did their job as ‌well." The final match is in Potchefstroom on Wednesday.

title: Olivia Rodrigo breaks her own chart record with 13 weeks at No  1
description: Olivia Rodrigo   s latest album has spent 13 weeks at No  1 on two Billboard charts  surpassing her Guts record
content:
Olivia Rodrigo’s latest album has spent 13 weeks at No. 1 on two Billboard charts, surpassing her Guts record
Olivia Rodrigo’s third album, You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love, has broken her own Billboard record after spending 13 weeks at No. 1 on two album charts.
The album remains at the top of Billboard’s Top Alternative Albums chart, which ranks the most-consumed albums and EPs in the US that fit within the alternative genre.
Its latest week at No. 1 moves it ahead of Rodrigo’s previous record with her second album, Guts.
Guts debuted at No. 1 on the Top Alternative Albums chart in September 2023 and spent 12 weeks at the top during its run.
You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love had been tied with the album at 12 weeks before taking the record outright.
Rodrigo’s latest album has also spent 13 weeks at No. 1 on Billboard’s Top Rock & Alternative Albums chart. Guts previously held the record on that ranking with nine weeks at the top.
The album appears on six Billboard charts this week and remains within the top five on all of them. It ranks No. 3 on the Billboard 200, No. 4 on Top Streaming Albums and No. 5 on Vinyl Albums. It also rises three places to No. 5 on Top Album Sales.
Rodrigo also has Guts on both the Top Alternative Albums and Top Rock & Alternative Albums charts. The album rises to No. 7 on the former and moves from No. 13 to No. 11 on the latter.
All three of Rodrigo’s studio albums appear on the Billboard 200 this week. You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love ranks No. 3, while Sour rises to No. 38 and Guts moves to No. 51.

title: Anna Kendrick excited to direct  The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
description: Anna Kendrick discusses directing  The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo  and friendships with  Pitch Perfect  co stars
content:
Anna Kendrick discusses directing 'The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo' and friendships with 'Pitch Perfect' co-stars
Anna Kendrick has spoken about directing The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo, describing herself as “over the moon and so excited” about the upcoming Netflix adaptation of Taylor Jenkins Reid’s novel.
Kendrick discussed the project during the Zurich Film Festival, where she attended the European premiere of Lauren Miller Rogen’s Babies.
Netflix announced in June that Kendrick would direct the film, which is adapted from Reid’s best-selling novel.
The screenplay was written by Liz Tigelaar, with current revisions by Francesca Sloane. Reid is attached as an executive producer.
Kendrick also reflected on her first experience directing and the support she received from Pitch Perfect co-star Brittany Snow, who had directed Parachute .
Kendrick recalled being “really in a panic” before stepping onto her first set. She said Snow helped calm her by giving her straightforward advice.
“[Snow] is normally so emotionally attuned and sensitive and has all the room in the world for your big feelings,” Kendrick said. “She went: 'You're gonna get on set and know what to do, stop it.' It was just so cut and dry and exactly what I needed to hear.”
The actor also discussed her Pitch Perfect co-stars and the friendships that developed through the franchise.
Kendrick said the group gave her “10 girls who are family, in the truest sense”, including Snow, Rebel Wilson, Anna Camp and Hailee Steinfeld.
“When someone in the group chat tells us something difficult is happening, it's like, ok: who is going over to her house tomorrow? What are we doing? How are we figuring this out? It's beautiful,” she said, comparing the group’s support to “Avengers, assemble”.
Kendrick also recalled the unexpected success of the Cup Song from the first Pitch Perfect, which she said became a major part of the film’s legacy.
She said the franchise’s success helped her secure later projects, while describing the experience as having brought “nothing but positive things” to her career.

title: UHS opens MDCAT 2026 recount  review portal for result verification
description: Applications will be processed within five working days  with no complaints accepted after September 30
content:
Applications will be processed within five working days, with no complaints accepted after September 30
The University of Health Sciences (UHS), which conducted the Medical and Dental College Admission Test (MDCAT) 2026 in Punjab on September 20, has activated an online Recount and Review Portal for candidates seeking verification of their results.
The applications are to be processed within five working days and no complaints will be entertained after September 30. The university’s decision in recounting will be final.
"A candidate may question the calculation of marks, reading of the response sheet, an answer contained in the official key or even a particular question. Each matter requires a different form of verification,” said a health department official.
Under the UHS procedure, a candidate seeking recounting or review has to provide the reason for the application and upload the result card. A carbon copy of the bubble sheet can also be uploaded.
The applicant then generates the bank challan, pays the fee and uploads proof of payment before final submission.
The application is subsequently forwarded to the UHS Examination Cell.
The carbon copy gives candidates a personal record of the responses marked during the examination, said the official.
Read More: MDCAT 2026 concludes across Pakistan as thousands of candidates sit exam
The universities organising the test were required to provide candidates the sheets carrying carbon copies and to preserve the examination record for a specified period.
The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) had also directed the universities to provide a mechanism for rechecking and to display the official answer key.
One of the most likely sources of an apparent discrepancy is improper marking of the sheet. The MDCAT instructions had stated that an improperly filled bubble would be treated as an incorrect response. Since the sheet is processed electronically, an incomplete or unclear marking can produce a result different from expected.
The UHS has published separate answer keys for different paper codes and opened an answer key complaint facility. Candidates are required to identify the disputed question and provide evidence for their objection.
If a candidate believes the official answer to a multiple-choice question is incorrect, the matter concerns the answer key, while if the responses were not properly reflected in the score, the issue falls within result verification.
The UHS information booklet provided for validation of questions by subject experts and stated that an MCQ found inappropriate or invalid for assessment could be deleted with the score adjusted according to policy.
In tests like the MDCAT, small differences in marks can influence admission prospects.

title: Kohli powers India to a big win over West Indies
description: Seasoned batsman hits unbeaten 139 and skipper Shubman Gill scores 110 as India take a 1 0 series lead
content:
Seasoned batsman hits unbeaten 139 and skipper Shubman Gill scores 110 as India take a 1-0 series lead
THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Virat Kohli hit a record-extending 55th one-day international century to lead India to a dominant eight-wicket win over the West Indies in the series opener on Sunday.
Kohli, who hit an unbeaten 139, put on 151 runs for the second wicket with skipper Shubman Gill (110) as India chased down their victory target of 296 with 50 balls to spare in Thiruvananthapuram.
Kohli hit the winning six, the ninth in his 88-ball knock as India went 1-0 up in the three-match series, which is being seen as a step in the team's preparations for the 2027 ODI World Cup.
The 37-year-old Kohli made the evening his own as he went past 15,000 ODI runs to become only the second batter after icon Sachin Tendulkar to achieve the feat.
Kohli reached the milestone with a boundary in his 303rd ODI innings, while Tendulkar, who finished his illustrious career with 18,426 runs, took 377 innings to get to 15,000.
Gill reached his 10th ODI hundred but the spotlight soon shifted back to Kohli, who reached his 100 with a six as a raucous home crowd stood up to applaud the star cricketer.
The top-order batter is leading century-maker in ODIs with Tendulkar next with 49 hundreds. Rohit Sharma is third with 34 tons.
Kohli and the 39-year-old Rohit are both playing only in the 50-over format after their Test and T20 retirements, as they look ahead to the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.
Kohli on Saturday told broadcasters JioStar that that the 2027 showpiece would be his last World Cup appearance.
Rohit put the team off to brisk start in his 32 as he put on 74 runs with opening partner Gill.
Earlier Justin Greaves made 101 and put on 135 runs for the opening stand with left-hander John Campbell, who made 62, to guide West Indies to 295-7.
Left-arm wrist spinner Kuldeep Yadav struck crucial blows to return figures of 4-40 including one maiden over as India hit back in the middle overs.
Kuldeep also struck on successive balls, sending back Greaves and Jewel Andrew before Roston Chase avoided the hat-trick.
Chase steadied the innings with Amir Jangoo, who made an unbeaten 58, as the pair put on 52 runs for the sixth wicket. The second ODI is on Wednesday in Guwahati.

A repost by Pop Fusion HQ attracted more than 1.4 million views, prompting discussions about whether the interaction was inappropriate or simply awkward.
Some viewers criticised Spears’ behaviour, with one commenter claiming she “desperately needs help”.

Some social media users described the scene as potentially inappropriate workplace behaviour, while others argued that viewers lacked sufficient context to make that judgement.
The apparent worker has not publicly commented on the video, and there is no confirmation that he felt uncomfortable or objected to Spears’ behaviour.

title: Robert Pattinson reveals his favourite meme of himself and admits he still doesn   t get it
description: Pattinson said that the meme makes him feel    very  like  boomer    because he does not understand the joke behind it
content:
Pattinson said that the meme makes him feel “very, like, boomer” because he does not understand the joke behind it
Robert Pattinson has revealed his favourite meme of himself, although the Primetime star admits he still does not understand why the image became so popular online.
While promoting his new film Primetime, Pattinson told Entertainment Weekly that his favourite meme comes from a fitting for his 2017 film Good Time. The image shows the actor standing awkwardly in a kitchen wearing an Adidas track jacket and camouflage trousers.
“There’s one from a fitting from Good Time, which I still to this day do not understand,” Pattinson said. He added that the meme makes him feel “very, like, boomer” because he does not understand the joke behind it.
The photograph, commonly referred to online as “tracksuit Robert Pattinson”, was originally posted by Good Time director Josh Safdie in 2017. It became a viral meme several years later after users began adding captions to the image, including jokes about a boyfriend arriving at someone’s house and a cousin being asked to fetch folding chairs from a garage.
Pattinson remains puzzled by the image's popularity. During the interview, he compared his confusion over the meme to newer internet trends, saying he does not understand why something where “nothing is happening” can become such a major online phenomenon.
The actor previously discussed the same image during a 2026 Vogue interview with Zendaya. When asked about a viral meme or conspiracy theory involving himself, Pattinson brought up the photograph and described it as a bizarre example of how something can unexpectedly become an internet phenomenon.
Pattinson's meme status has also become part of the promotion for Primetime, in which he plays To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen. Director Lance Oppenheim told EW that the film's own promotional material has already generated memes, continuing the actor's long-running relationship with internet culture.

title: Sylvester Stallone recalls eating disorder and steroid use during  Rocky  fame
description: Sylvester Stallone recalls eating disorder and steroid use during his Rocky fame and their lasting effects on health
content:
Sylvester Stallone recalls eating disorder and steroid use during his Rocky fame and their lasting effects on health
Sylvester Stallone has spoken about his struggles with body image, an eating disorder and steroid use while making the Rocky films, saying the pursuit of physical fitness had lasting effects on his health.
In a New York Times interview published on September 26, the 80-year-old actor recalled becoming increasingly focused on his appearance during the 1980s.
Stallone said his physical transformation for Rocky and Rambo eventually became an obsession.
“It was my armor,” Stallone said. He explained that he wanted Rocky’s physique to change as the character became more vain, while Rambo’s appearance reflected his role as a warrior.
“And then it became an obsession, really bad,” he said. “It became to the point where I became bulimic … I got down to 2.6% body fat when I was doing Rocky III … and I couldn't hold anything down.”
Stallone also acknowledged using steroids while working on the Rocky films. “I became so obsessed with staying at that point of fitness … it got to me,” he told the Times.
Discussing the methods used to maintain a highly muscular physique, Stallone said, “Nobody does it without additives or drugs; I don't care what they say … bulls---,” while also describing what he considered a controlled approach to steroid use.
“But you do it the sensible way — six weeks on, six weeks off,” he said. “People say, 'You don't get that way naturally.' No, you don't, unless you're a freak of nature.”
Stallone said his steroid use “took a terrible toll” on his body and that he continues to deal with the consequences decades later.
“I've abused [my body]. I've had nine back operations, two shoulder operations, three neck fusions, everything,” he said. “I'm held together with baling wire, but I still have the want to stay in good shape.”
Stallone added that he takes medication to maintain his health and said he would approach his career differently if given another chance.

Watts already has experience working within the Star Wars universe through Skeleton Crew
Jon Watts, the director behind Tom Holland’s Spider-Man trilogy, has been tapped to direct the first film in a new Star Wars trilogy written by Simon Kinberg.
Watts directed Spider-Man: Homecoming, Spider-Man: Far From Home and Spider-Man: No Way Home for Marvel and Sony. His new Star Wars project will also mark a return to the franchise, having previously directed the Disney+ series Star Wars: Skeleton Crew.
Kinberg is writing the new trilogy and will also produce the films. The filmmaker has previously worked extensively with the X-Men franchise, producing several Fox Marvel projects and directing 2019’s Dark Phoenix. He also consulted on J.J. Abrams’ Star Wars: The Force Awakens and co-created the animated series Star Wars Rebels with Dave Filoni.
According to reports cited by Entertainment Weekly, Kinberg’s trilogy is expected to continue the Skywalker Saga. However, there have been conflicting reports about whether the films will introduce a completely new story or bring back Daisy Ridley’s Rey from the sequel trilogy.
Watts already has experience working within the Star Wars universe through Skeleton Crew, the coming-of-age series he created with Christopher Ford. The show follows four children who become caught up in an adventure across the galaxy and stars Jude Law.
The new trilogy is part of Lucasfilm’s plans to expand the Star Wars film franchise after the conclusion of the Skywalker Saga in 2019’s Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker. No release date has been announced for Watts’ film, and Lucasfilm has not yet publicly commented on the director’s involvement.

content:
Minecraft will add The Sift as its fourth dimension in 2027, following its debut in Minecraft Dungeons II
Minecraft is set to receive its first new dimension in more than 14 years, with Mojang revealing The Sift during Minecraft Live on September 26.
The Sift will become the fourth dimension in Minecraft, joining the Overworld, the Nether and the End. The Nether was introduced in 2010, followed by the End in 2011.
According to Mojang’s official Minecraft Live recap, The Sift is “beautiful, vibrant, and teeming with souls.”
The dimension was shown in a trailer featuring pink blocks, blue-green vegetation and a new mob that inhabits the area.
However, Mojang has not yet revealed how players will access The Sift when it arrives in the main game.
The Sift will first appear in Minecraft Dungeons II, the upcoming action RPG spin-off scheduled to launch on September 29.
Players will be able to explore locations within the dimension, including the Meadow and the Carapace.
Minecraft Java Edition and Bedrock Edition will not receive The Sift until 2027. Mojang has not announced a more specific release date or explained how the new dimension will be incorporated into the main game.
Minecraft Live also confirmed that Minecraft will launch on Nintendo Switch 2 on October 27. The update will arrive alongside a new Ice Caves drop.
The broadcast additionally revealed plans for the world’s first Minecraft rollercoaster and official hotel at Chessington in the UK.

title: China  US agree on strategic stability  trade and AI cooperation
description: Two countries reach eight  deliverables and understandings  during the Chinese president   s state visit to Washington
content:
Two countries reach eight 'deliverables and understandings' during the Chinese president’s state visit to Washington
Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump have agreed to build a “constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability” based on respect, fairness and reciprocity, according to a statement issued by China’s Embassy in Washington, DC.
The understanding was reached during Xi’s state visit to the United States from September 23 to 25, during which the two leaders held “in-depth discussions” on bilateral ties and major international and regional issues, the ministry said in a statement.
The two sides reached eight “deliverables and understandings”, it added.
China and the United States Reach Eight Deliverables and Understandings 🇨🇳🇺🇸 https://t.co/qYOVo31tOM pic.twitter.com/QU2XPWX4f1
Under the first understanding, China and the US agreed to work towards a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on “respect, fairness and reciprocity”.
The two countries also agreed to support each other in hosting the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting and the G20 Summit. Xi and Trump intend to attend each other’s meetings, according to the statement .
On Iran, the two leaders agreed that Tehran should honour its commitment not to develop nuclear weapons. They also agreed that “no country or institution can be allowed to impose tolls on international waterways”, without elaborating on the specific waterways or arrangements involved.
The leaders also recalled that China and the US had been allies during World War II and fought together to defeat the Axis powers.
On trade, Xi and Trump recognised the “positive role” of the China-US economic and trade consultation mechanism and endorsed the outcomes of recent talks between their economic teams.
The outcomes include establishing and advancing a Board of Trade and other mechanisms, as well as an arrangement for a $30 billion reciprocal tariff reduction, the ministry said.
According to the statement, the two leaders also agreed to extend the outcomes of economic and trade consultations held in Kuala Lumpur and instructed their respective teams to implement the agreements.
The two sides also welcomed progress in counter-narcotics and law-enforcement cooperation. According to Beijing, Chinese and US agencies had jointly cracked several cases involving new psychoactive substances and precursor chemicals and arrested dozens of suspects in the two countries.
China and the US further agreed to establish a China-US AI Dialogue to exchange views on the risks and benefits associated with artificial intelligence.
The next round of the dialogue is scheduled for November 2026, while the two countries will also establish a bilateral communication channel for AI-related incidents.
The announcement comes amid growing international efforts to develop mechanisms for managing the risks associated with increasingly advanced AI systems.
In a symbolic gesture, the United States also welcomed the arrival of two giant pandas leased by China to Zoo Atlanta.
Meanwhile, the Chinese and US militaries agreed to conclude a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on crisis communication and prevention “as soon as possible”.
China and the United States agreed to establish a channel for handling AI-related incidents and accelerate work on military crisis communications following a three-day summit between President Xi Jinping and President Trump in Washington, the two governments said Saturday.…
The two militaries will also continue cooperation to search for the remains of US service members who went missing in China, according to the statement.
The ministry said the agreements and understandings were reached as Xi and Trump discussed the future of China-US relations as well as major international and regional issues during the Chinese president’s September 23-25 state visit.
A day earlier, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said that President Xi’s US state visit had led to new progress in a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, according to Xinhua news agency.
Read: Xi's visit boosts strategic stability in China-US ties, says FM
Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks while briefing reporters on Xi’s state visit to the United States from September 23 to 25.
President Xi and President Trump had a candid and in-depth exchange of views in a friendly atmosphere of mutual respect on strategic and overarching issues concerning China-US relations and the broader global landscape, Wang said.
President #XiJinping 's state visit sets right path for China, US to get along, says Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi #ChinaUS More: https://t.co/1PQuWk6JSO pic.twitter.com/GKUQr1UMvy
Since President Trump began his second term, the two heads of state have maintained close exchanges, including three in-person meetings and five phone talks, and fostered a pattern of interaction marked by mutual respect and sincerity, said Wang, noting this has become the most valuable strategic asset in China-US relations.
An important political outcome of the visit was that President Xi and President Trump further enriched the substance of the new positioning of China-US relations and have agreed to build a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity, Wang said.
Respect means respecting each other's sovereignty and territorial integrity, respecting each country's choice of social system and development path, and respecting the other side's core interests and major concerns, Wang said.
Fairness, Wang continued, means pursuing mutually beneficial cooperation and handling differences through consultation, rejecting a zero-sum game in which one side's gain comes at the expense of the other's, and not seeking unilateral absolute advantage.
Reciprocity means that the two countries are equal in sovereignty, that neither side stands above the other, that neither engages in hegemonic nor bullying behaviour, that each side's concerns are addressed on an equal basis, and that cooperation across various fields develops in a balanced manner, Wang said.
Noting that President Xi has pointed out that a stable China-US economic and trade relationship requires both expanding the list of cooperation and shortening the list of problems, Wang said that the US side should treat Chinese companies fairly, resolve problems through dialogue and negotiations, and promote the sustained, stable and positive development of China-US economic and trade relations.
The fentanyl abuse problem in the United States is not caused by China, but China has always acted with the utmost goodwill and made every effort to assist the US side in addressing the fentanyl crisis, Wang noted, adding that the two heads of state tasked the law enforcement agencies of the two countries with continuing to strengthen cooperation and jointly combat transnational crime.
To promote people-to-people exchanges between China and the United States, President Xi has announced a series of new measures, including inviting 100,000 young Americans to visit China for exchange and study programs over the next five years, Wang said.
One piece of good news that has been particularly welcomed by the American public is that two pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, will soon arrive at Zoo Atlanta, Wang added.
The Zoo Atlanta will be getting two pandas from China. During his state visit with President Trump on Thursday at the White House, Chinese President Xi Jinping said he is sending two giant pandas to the U.S. https://t.co/rYFan6yLsB pic.twitter.com/A9GZwoe2M4
During the visit, Wang said, the two heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on major international and regional issues of common concern and agreed to strengthen coordination to make due contributions to world peace and development.
President Xi also encouraged relevant parties to stay committed to peace, supported the United States and Iran in returning to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding , resuming dialogue and negotiations at an early date, and ultimately reaching a comprehensive agreement covering the nuclear issue, Wang said.
During the visit, President Xi and President Trump also had an in-depth exchange of views on AI, pointing out that the two countries should leverage respective strengths rather than guard against each other, Wang said.
The two heads of state agreed to make good use of AI dialogue mechanisms between the two countries and jointly prevent the misuse and abuse of AI, Wang added.
Noting that this year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials, Wang said that China and the United States are both permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, and it is their shared responsibility to uphold the postwar international order and prevent the resurgence of militarism.
China and the United States will respectively host the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and the G20 Leaders’ Summit in the fourth quarter of this year, Wang said, adding that the two heads of state confirmed their mutual support, which will continue to inject momentum into cooperation in the Asia-Pacific and global governance.

title: Trump says men arrested at US air base in UK were looking to do  big damage
description: Police cordoned off 400 metres around the base as bomb disposal experts examined vans and residents evacuated
content:
Police cordoned off 400 metres around the base as bomb disposal experts examined vans and residents evacuated
British police arrested five men near a US air base on suspicion of explosive and terrorism offences on ​Sunday after a tip-off that three vans had been heading to the military airfield which has been used to strike Iran.
US President Donald Trump ‌said the suspects had been looking to do "big damage" and had been under investigation by British and US authorities.
British counter terrorism detectives leading the investigation said police had received a call about three suspicious vehicles which appeared to be travelling towards RAF Fairford in the west of England in the early hours of Sunday.
Five men were arrested by armed officers and later held on suspicion of preparing ​a terrorist act. Police said they believed the incident was now contained.
Police working to understand circumstances
"We are in the early stages of an investigation, and five ​men remain in custody," Counter Terrorism Policing Senior National Coordinator Vicki Evans said in a statement.
Read More: Iran says it seized US sea drone in Strait of Hormuz
"As you would expect, we are working ⁠closely with our partners to understand the circumstances of the incident."
Police said a 400-metre cordon was in place around the base as the bomb disposal unit investigated the vans. ​Local residents in 85 homes in a nearby village were evacuated, and armed officers were patrolling the site.
The British government, which has given authorisation to the US to use ​bombers based at Fairford to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz, said Prime Minister Andy Burnham was being updated on the incident.
Burnham thanked the police and armed forces, saying on X: "I know today's incident near RAF Fairford will be deeply concerning for local residents and for many people following developments across the country".
I know today's incident near RAF Fairford will be deeply concerning for local residents and for many people following developments across the country. My thanks go to Gloucestershire Police, Counter Terrorism Policing, our Armed Forces and all those working to keep the public…
Britain said in July its armed forces were ready ​to protect the country from any attack after Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned it not to allow US bombers to fly from Fairford, saying any base used to launch attacks ​would be a legitimate target.
Read More: Iran says it seized US sea drone in Strait of Hormuz
Police have not said who they believed was involved in Sunday's alleged incident. An Iranian-linked motive is considered the most likely, a source familiar with the investigation said, ‌while a ⁠Russian sabotage operation or an Islamist plot are also being looked at.
"The arrest in the UK was fantastic," Trump told reporters, saying it was "an amazing job".
"We had them under investigation. They were looking to do big damage to our port and working with the British worked out great ... We had them under view for a long time, and we got them," Trump added.
On Sunday morning the base was blocked by armed police while large machinery also prevented access and Reuters witnesses said security had been increased at other bases ​used by the US, with armoured vehicles ​and soldiers at the gates of RAF ⁠Lakenheath and RAF Mildenhall in eastern England.
"A cordon is in place as a precaution and the public can expect to see an emergency services presence in the area for some time," Gloucestershire Police Assistant Chief Constable Richard Ocone told reporters
The ​ Daily Mail website carried a photograph of five men without shirts who it said had been arrested.
A spokesperson for the ​US Air Force declined to ⁠discuss specific force protection measures.
"The 501st Combat Support Wing and our fellow UK-based Wings remain vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, civilians, contractors, and their families," the spokesperson said.
"We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their ⁠families."
British ministers ​have also previously briefed providers of critical infrastructure on the threat posed by Russia , with the government increasingly ​concerned about possible sabotage operations and cyberattacks.
Russia denies mounting hybrid attacks on Western nations.
A British military air base in central England was broken into in June 2025 by the Palestine Action protest group, which has since ​been proscribed as a terrorist organisation.

title: Don   t Breathe 3  is happening  but who is coming back
description: Don   t Breathe 3  is in development  with Jane Levy and Stephen Lang set to return to the horror franchise
content:
'Don’t Breathe 3' is in development, with Jane Levy and Stephen Lang set to return to the horror franchise
Fede Álvarez has confirmed that Don’t Breathe 3 is in development, with Jane Levy and Stephen Lang set to return to the horror franchise.
Álvarez revealed the news during a 10th-anniversary screening of Don’t Breathe at Beyond Fest on September 26. The filmmaker said he has written a script for the third instalment, which is expected to bring Levy back as Rocky and Lang as the Blind Man.
The announcement comes a decade after the original Don’t Breathe was released in August 2016. The film followed three burglars who break into the home of a blind veteran, only to find themselves trapped with a dangerous and unpredictable opponent.
Levy played Rocky, a young woman who participates in the burglary while hoping to escape an abusive home with her younger sister. Lang portrayed the Blind Man, whose abilities and secrets turn the robbery into a fight for survival.
The original Don’t Breathe became a box-office success, earning more than $157 million worldwide against a reported production budget of about $10 million.
The film ended with Rocky escaping Detroit, while a television report revealed that the Blind Man had survived. The sequel, Don’t Breathe 2 , was released in 2021 and focused on Lang’s character, with Levy not returning.
The third film could reunite Rocky and the Blind Man following their separate stories in the first two movies. Further details about the plot, director and production schedule for Don’t Breathe 3 have not been announced.
Álvarez previously directed the original film and co-wrote Don’t Breathe 2 . His latest announcement marks the first official confirmation of the third movie and Levy’s return to the franchise.

title: Govt not financing purchase of new PIA aircraft  says finance adviser
description: Govt s involvement limited to facilitating access to international financing  tech and suppliers  Khurram Schehzad
content:
Govt's involvement limited to facilitating access to international financing, tech and suppliers: Khurram Schehzad
Adviser to the Finance Minister, Khurram Schehzad, clarified on Sunday that the government was not financing the purchase of any aircraft for Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) after its privatisation and had not issued any sovereign guarantee for loans to fund the airline’s fleet expansion.
The clarification came in the backdrop of a recent meeting held between Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and Chair of the US Export-Import (Exim) Bank John Jovanovich on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on September 25, in which Aurangzeb held discussions seeking financing opportunities for procurement of aircraft for PIA.
Read : Aurangzeb seeks US financing for PIA
In a post on X, Schehzad said that "certain circulating comments" had failed to accurately grasp the roles of privatisation and the export credit agency.
"The government is neither purchasing aircraft for PIA after privatisation nor has any announcement been made of a government guarantee or loan funded by taxpayers' money for that purpose," Schehzad remarked.
پی آی اے اور امریکی ایکسپورٹ امپورٹ بینک کے حوالے سے حقائق گردش کرنے والے بعض تبصروں میں نجکاری اور برآمدی قرضہ فراہم کرنے والے ادارے کے کردار کو درست طور پر نہیں سمجھا گیا۔ حکومت نہ تو نجکاری کے بعد PIA کے لیے طیارے خرید رہی ہے اور نہ ہی اس مقصد کے لیے کسی حکومتی ضمانت یا…
He noted that the primary objective of the US Exim Bank was to promote US exports and employment. "Boeing aircraft are US exports. Therefore, the US Export-Import Bank provides financial assistance to foreign buyers purchasing US-made aircraft, including airlines, under established financial mechanisms".
Schehzad said the US agency’s framework allowed for asset-backed aircraft financing, under which the aircraft itself could serve as security, while the creditworthiness of the airline, lessee or any guarantor could also be assessed.
“A government guarantee is not a mandatory condition,” he said.
Schehzad said the government’s involvement was limited to facilitating access to international financing, technology and suppliers, as well as promoting commercial opportunities for Pakistani businesses.
He added that the finance minister’s discussions with US Exim Bank were broader than PIA and included potential financing in areas such as aviation, refinery expansion and the Reko Diq project.
The adviser also rejected suggestions that the proposed aircraft financing would create a "hidden subsidy" or transfer PIA’s commercial risks to taxpayers. "Therefore, claims such as "public debt," "hidden subsidy," "state financial backing," or taxpayers bearing PIA's commercial risk should not be presented as facts, as no such arrangement has been announced".
Read More : Arif Habib Consortium takes over PIA management as govt formally completes privatisation process
He said no government borrowing for PIA or sovereign guarantee had been announced and that references to potential US Exim financing should not be treated as confirmation of a state-backed loan. "No announcement has been made by the Government of Pakistan to take out a loan for PIA or issue any government guarantee".
Schehzad stated that PIA was privatised following an auction in December last year, with the transaction aimed at transferring ownership and commercial management of the national flag carrier to the private sector.
"Privatisation means the transfer of ownership, commercial management and operations. It does not mean that the Government of Pakistan abandons its role in creating opportunities for Pakistani companies and opening international doors," he said.

A US jury ruled that Apple owes San Diego-based Taction ​more than $5.7 billion for using its patented ‌technology to power the haptic feedback in iPhones and Apple Watches. Apple said it would ​appeal the country's largest such verdict, to ​date.

title: Where Lahore meets Brooklyn  Inside BK Jani s burger scene
description: From mint chutney to nihari sandwiches  the restaurant blends Pakistani flavours with the familiar comfort of a burger
content:
From mint chutney to nihari sandwiches, the restaurant blends Pakistani flavours with the familiar comfort of a burger
Walking into BK Jani in Brooklyn feels a little like stepping into a conversation between Lahore and New York. The restaurant is small and casual, but its walls carry an identity that is much bigger than its footprint.
Traditional Pakistani visual elements sit alongside the energy of Brooklyn, while the menu takes something as universally recognisable as a burger and gives it a distinctly South Asian point of view.
Their instagram page termed 'Jani' as a 'form of endearment', with the restaurant saying they serve the best Pakistani burgers in all of New York.
What immediately caught my attention was the atmosphere. The walls weren't simply decorated; they felt lived in. Pakistani-inspired artwork and photographs gave the space a sense of place, while handwritten messages from customers created another layer of personality.
There was an entire wall filled with people's reactions to the food—compliments, jokes, and desi references written by diners who clearly wanted to leave a little piece of their experience behind.
Some of the phrases by customers read, " Itni khawari ke baad maza aaya (The pain was worth the wait)", " Dil jeetliya bhai (You won my heart, brother)", and "Pakistan Zindabad!!".
It almost felt like a guestbook, except instead of signatures, the walls were filled with food memories.
That sense of community is part of what makes BK Jani interesting. You can see how different audiences have found their way into the same room.
There were young Gen Z diners, South Asians who seemed immediately familiar with the flavours and references, and people from outside the culture who had simply heard about the burgers and wanted to understand what the hype was about.
And then there was the music. The soundtrack moved between Pakistani and Indian music from Ali Sethi, Samar Jafri to Arjit Singh, creating another bridge between the traditional and the contemporary.
For someone familiar with South Asian music, hearing those songs in a Brooklyn burger joint creates an unmistakable feeling of nostalgia. For someone encountering it for the first time, it becomes part of the experience of discovering another culture through food.
That is perhaps what BK Jani does particularly well: it doesn't separate the food from the culture that produced it.
According to The Hugh, the restaurant was founded by Sibte Hassan, a Lahore native, and that background is important to understanding the concept. Hassan brought the flavours and food traditions he grew up with into a Brooklyn setting, rather than trying to reproduce a conventional American burger joint.
Earlier accounts of BK Jani describe Hassan personally running the grill and explaining the idea behind the restaurant, including the preference for eating the food with your hands—a practice deeply familiar in South Asian dining culture.
Take chutney. In an American burger context, the expected companions are usually ketchup, mustard, mayonnaise, or perhaps barbecue sauce. At BK Jani, chutney changes the entire equation. The signature Jani burger is built around a beef patty with mint chutney, grilled tomato, and a touch of raita.
Mint chutney isn't simply a sauce replacing mayonnaise. It brings heat, freshness, acidity, herbs, and the unmistakable flavour profile of South Asian cooking. Raita adds another familiar element, traditionally associated with yogurt-based accompaniments that help balance spicy foods. Together, those ingredients transform the idea of what a burger can be.
The Lahori burger pushes that idea even further. The menu describes it as spicy ground beef with mild raita and fresh cucumber, essentially building cooling and spicy elements into the same sandwich.
And then there is the Nihari sandwich, which takes another distinctly Pakistani food tradition and puts it into a handheld format. Nihari is a slow-cooked beef dish associated with richly spiced, long-simmered meat; BK Jani turns that tradition into a sandwich rather than serving it in its more familiar form.
That is what makes the menu more interesting than simply calling it "Pakistani burgers." It is really a conversation between food traditions. The burger is Brooklyn. The chutney is Lahore. The format is familiar, but the flavours carry a different history.
And that may be the most compelling thing about BK Jani. It isn't trying to make Pakistani food feel distant or overly formal. It puts those flavours right in the middle of Brooklyn's everyday food culture.
The walls preserve the memories. The music preserves the nostalgia. The chutney preserves the flavour. And the customers—Pakistani, Indian, Brooklyn-born, immigrant, Gen Z, or simply curious—keep adding to the story, being a perfect example of how food travels.

title: Liam Payne   s sister Nicola was in the crowd as Niall Horan played his voice during  End of an Era

content:
Nicola later shared an emotional statement on social media thanking Horan for inviting her and her family
Liam Payne’s sister Nicola Payne was among the audience when Niall Horan paid tribute to her late brother during his Manchester concert.
Horan played a recording of Liam’s voice at the end of his performance of End of an Era during his Dinner Party Live on Tour show at Manchester’s Co-op Live on September 25. The emotional moment left the arena silent as Liam’s voice reflected on his journey and achievements.
Nicola later shared an emotional statement on social media thanking Horan for inviting her and her family to the concert. She described the night as an “emotional” experience for the four of them and said hearing Liam’s voice fill an arena again was difficult to put into words.
“Knowing that this may be the last time we ever hear his voice played out across an arena made it incredibly difficult, but at the same time, there was something so beautiful and comforting about it,” Nicola wrote.
She added that Liam would “always be a part” of such moments for the family and said hearing his voice brought back memories while also making it feel as though “a little piece of him was right there with us.”
Nicola also mentioned an orb she noticed while filming Horan’s performance of End of an Era. She said she would “like to think that was Liam joining us for a moment too.”
Horan’s tribute has become a significant part of his current tour following Liam’s death in October 2024. The former One Direction bandmates remained close after the group’s split, and Horan has previously spoken about rewriting End of an Era following Liam’s death.
Nicola concluded her message by congratulating Horan on his show and thanking him for giving her family such a “special and emotional night.”
