content:
Calls for indiscriminate action against organised groups involved in online financial fraud, harassment and blackmail
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Sunday directed the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) to further intensify operations against online financial fraud, harassment, digital blackmail and organised cybercrime networks.
During his visit to the NCCIA Central Zone Headquarters in Lahore, the interior minister reviewed ongoing cybercrime operations and investigations in detail. He inspected the complaints cell, forensic laboratory and investigation wing and reviewed the entire process from registration of citizens’ complaints to investigation and action against accused persons.
وفاقی وزیر داخلہ محسن نقوی کا این سی سی آئی اے سنٹرل زون ہیڈکوارٹرز کا دورہ، سائبر جرائم کے خلاف کارروائیاں مزید تیز کرنے کا حکم وفاقی وزیر داخلہ نے سائبر کرائمز کے خلاف جاری آپریشنز اور تحقیقات کا تفصیلی جائزہ لیا pic.twitter.com/GCX7yFrvY8
Chairing a special meeting, Naqvi directed that indiscriminate action be taken against organised groups involved in online financial fraud, fake accounts, digital blackmail and online harassment.

“Wherever a cybercriminal may be operating from, he must be brought within the ambit of law,” he said.
The interior minister directed authorities to strengthen the immediate response mechanism for financial fraud complaints so that timely coordination with relevant institutions could help secure victims’ funds and improve the chances of tracing the suspects.
“A citizen should not have to wait for months after filing a complaint. Timely progress should be visible on every complaint,” Naqvi said.

He ordered a case-by-case review of pending cases and complaints and directed officials to eliminate unnecessary delays. He also called for enhanced digital forensic capabilities, the use of modern forensic tools and specialised training for investigation officers.
“New methods of cybercrime cannot be countered through traditional investigations; modern technology and trained human resources are required,” Naqvi stated.
The interior minister said the NCCIA was to be developed into a modern cyber police force capable of protecting citizens in the digital world through advanced technology. He directed that complaints involving online harassment, blackmail and digital exploitation of women and children be accorded special priority.

Naqvi further underlined that protecting citizens’ data, privacy, and financial interests was a fundamental responsibility of the NCCIA, adding that the agency was being provided with modern technology, necessary resources, and training to fulfil this responsibility.
He also directed the NCCIA to make its public awareness campaign against cybercrime more effective and ensure that citizens were promptly informed about new methods of online fraud.
The Director General (DG) NCCIA briefed the interior minister on the performance of the central zone, cases under investigation, emerging cyber fraud trends and ongoing operations.
DG FIA, inspector general Islamabad Police, director FIA Lahore Zone and other relevant officials were also present.

Zoe Saldaña says 'Lioness' is enough for now, explaining why she is not ready to join another Taylor Sheridan series
Zoe Saldaña has said she is not ready to join another Taylor Sheridan series, explaining that her work on Lioness already requires a significant time commitment.
The actress, who stars as CIA operative Joe McNamara and serves as an executive producer on the Paramount+ series, discussed her workload in a recent interview with PEOPLE .
“I think that Joe McNamara and Lioness is all that I can handle at this time,” Saldaña said when asked about appearing in another show from Sheridan’s television universe.
Saldaña explained that her responsibilities begin months before filming, while her position as the lead actor means she is typically first on set and among the last to leave.
“I’m number one on the call sheet. I am first one in, last one out,” she said. “I can’t imagine me taking on more of a Taylor Sheridan world.”
The actress said she appreciates Sheridan’s approach to creating complex characters and praised his ability to write roles that are not restricted by gender or race.
Saldaña also discussed the possibility of Lioness season 4, although she said she does not know whether the series will return or what direction Sheridan could take Joe’s story.
Season 3 placed Joe in a more vulnerable position after she became a target and had to escape herself. Saldaña described the storyline as demanding but said she was proud of how the character’s journey developed.
Her Lioness costar Michael Kelly has expanded his role in Sheridan’s universe, joining the cast of Landman season 3. Saldaña joked that if Lioness returns, Kelly’s role as Byron Westfield should remain a priority.

title: Hina Parvez Butt uses  Dar e Nijaat  to share message on marriage
description: Punjab lawmaker stresses communication  honesty  respect and trust when dealing with misunderstandings
content:
Punjab lawmaker stresses communication, honesty, respect and trust when dealing with misunderstandings
Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) politician Hina Parvez Butt has used the drama Dar-e-Nijaat to share a message about marriage, urging couples to communicate openly, avoid making decisions in anger and not allow past relationships or mistakes to damage their present.
The Member of the Provincial Assembly (MPA) shared a video on Instagram discussing how experiences from past relationships can affect future ones, particularly when they surface during a marriage.
“Your past relationships and mistakes can affect you later in life for future relations. When you are in a difficult situation like this, it is better to not act out of anger,” she said, urging people to respond to difficult circumstances with patience rather than anger.
Butt stressed the importance of communication between spouses when misunderstandings arise.
“A husband and wife should properly communicate their misunderstandings and fix the problem,” she said, adding that the past should not be allowed to overshadow a new relationship.
“Live in the present. A good marriage is built on respect and trust,” Butt said. “The past cannot define you. You can make your present better.”
In the caption accompanying the video, Butt elaborated on how private aspects of a person's past can affect a marriage if they come to light.
“After marriage, there may be things from the past, an old relationship, or something personal that you would prefer to keep private. But if such a secret comes to light, it can have an impact on your relationship,” she wrote.
She again cautioned against making decisions in anger and encouraged couples to address difficult revelations through honest communication.
“In such situations, making decisions in anger is not the solution. Husband and wife should talk openly with each other. Instead of hiding things or lying, try to address the matter together. If there is a misunderstanding, resolve it through honest communication.”
Butt's latest comments come as Dar-e-Nijaat explores the complications that can arise when experiences from the past intersect with a present relationship. Her message centres on communication, honesty, respect and trust as couples navigate such challenges.

title: PM Shehbaz says UNGA engagements advanced Pakistan s diplomatic  economic interests
description: Premier says engagements focused on regional security  defence cooperation and Pakistan s economic priorities
content:
Premier says engagements focused on regional security, defence cooperation and Pakistan's economic priorities
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has described his diplomatic engagements on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) as a significant success, highlighting discussions with Iran as well as Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on regional security and the implementation of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA).
Speaking to The Express Tribune , the prime minister said his meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and trilateral discussions with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye were among the key engagements during his stay in New York.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed Makkah pact, a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
The prime minister said the discussions on the sidelines of the UNGA focused on implementing the agreement and strengthening coordination among the three countries.
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar separately met his Saudi and Turkish counterparts in New York to review progress on establishing the agreement's institutional structures, including its secretariat, committees and working groups. The three ministers also discussed regional and international security issues.
The security discussions came amid heightened regional tensions, including the conflict involving Iran, the United States and Israel and attacks targeting Saudi Arabia.
Also Read: Makkah pact military chiefs condemn attacks on holy city at Riyadh meeting
PM Shehbaz also held a meeting with Pezeshkian, while Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi separately met with Pakistani officials. The discussions focused on regional developments and efforts to promote dialogue.
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said the meeting with Pezeshkian was held in an open and candid manner and that the Iranian president had assured the Pakistani side that he would hold further discussions.
Pakistan also conveyed its position on attacks in the region, expressing understanding of Iran's concerns while condemning US and Israeli attacks on Iran. Islamabad also condemned Iranian attacks on what it described as US bases in Gulf countries, maintaining that such actions should not take place.
The discussions also touched on attacks by the Houthis, with Pakistani officials asking Iran to use its influence to persuade them to step back. Pakistan, according to the discussion, was "in a sense, operationally involved" in efforts to address the issue.
The Makkah pact remained a central part of Pakistan's security diplomacy during the visit.
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir also met the Saudi and Turkish military chiefs as the three countries moved towards operationalising the agreement. A secretariat has been established under the arrangement to facilitate future coordination.
The three countries' military leadership subsequently met in Riyadh to review security threats and discuss intelligence sharing, military coordination and capability integration under the pact.
Turning to his UNGA address, PM Shehbaz said US President Donald Trump had praised his speech. He also highlighted his meeting with the International Monetary Fund's managing director, particularly discussions over the impact of higher petroleum prices and the possibility of targeted subsidies for poorer sections of society.
The prime minister had earlier said Pakistan remained focused on diplomatic efforts to help end the conflict involving the United States and Iran. His UNGA address also covered Palestine, Kashmir, Gaza and wider regional tensions, including attacks on Saudi Arabia.
Rana Sanaullah, who was among the prime minister's aides involved in discussions during the visit, described the address as concise, saying there was "more sincerity and pain than rhetoric" in the speech.
Before the prime minister's arrival in New York, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi travelled to Tehran for bilateral discussions. On his return, he briefed PM Shehbaz and Field Marshal Munir on his meetings. The following day, US Chargé d'Affaires Natalie Baker also met Naqvi and sought an update on the developments.
Economic issues were another major focus of the prime minister's discussions in New York.
During his meeting with the IMF, Shehbaz said the Fund had expressed satisfaction with Pakistan's economic reform programme and had no objection to targeted fuel subsidies aimed at protecting poorer sections of society.
The prime minister said the subsidies were not intended for the entire population but were being considered specifically in response to the impact of higher petroleum prices on low-income people.
The IMF team was, meanwhile, in Pakistan for discussions ahead of the next instalment under the country's programme.
Read More: FM Dar reviews Makkah pact implementation with Saudi, Turkish counterparts
The prime minister also discussed his longer-term economic legacy, reflecting on his previous tenure as Punjab chief minister and considering what he could accomplish during the remaining years of his second term as prime minister.
The discussions also covered provincial issues and concerns over limited employment opportunities for young people. While some young Pakistanis leave the country for education, the discussion noted that employment opportunities remain limited for graduates returning with degrees.
Political stability was identified as another priority, with the view that sustained economic stability would require a stable political environment.
The prime minister's diplomatic engagements also took place against the backdrop of domestic political tensions.
PM Shehbaz was aware of the proposed long march in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Jamaat-e-Islami chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman's planned march over the petroleum levy.
After arriving in New York, the prime minister spoke to Rehman and asked him to postpone the Islamabad march, while members of his team, including Rana Sanaullah and Ahsan Iqbal, also held discussions with the JI leadership.
The government requested that the march be put on hold, while Shehbaz offered to discuss the petroleum levy issue with the party.
Overall, the prime minister's engagements in New York brought together Pakistan's immediate diplomatic concerns over the Middle East, the implementation of the Makkah defence pact, economic discussions with the IMF and efforts to manage domestic political pressures.

title: Assefa misses women s world record at Berlin Marathon
description: The Ethiopian clocks 2 11 04 despite limping through the closing stages
content:
The Ethiopian clocks 2:11:04 despite limping through the closing stages
Ethiopia's Tigst Assefa narrowly missed out on breaking the women's world record at the Berlin Marathon on Sunday, battling through injury to cross the finish line after being on record pace for much of the race. Assefa was on track to break the record and accelerated in the final 10 kilometres, but faded in the closing stages, visibly limping across the finish line before collapsing on the road. The Ethiopian missed the podium ceremony as she was receiving medical treatment at the time the honours were handed out. She finished in a time of 2hr 11min 04min, the third best in history and breaking her personal best and course record of 2:11:53, set in 2023. Assefa's late fade means the women's world record of 2:09:56 remains in the possession of Ruth Chepngetich, a mark clouded by the Kenyan's three-year doping ban handed down in 2025. It was an all-Ethiopian podium as Bedatu Hirpa finished second in 2:16:53 and Dera Dida came third in 2:16:55. Ethiopia's Guye Adola won the men's race in 2:02:50, adding another Berlin crown after his 2021 victory in the German capital. Adola's time was off world record pace and outside the course record of 2:01:09, set in 2022 by five-time Berlin winner Eliud Kipchoge. The 35-year-old did not take the lead in the race until the 30-kilometre mark but was able to emerge with a lead of almost 30 seconds when he crossed the finish line. "My goal was to hold back a bit and see what the pacemakers did so I could know exactly what was happening -- and that worked wonderfully well," Adola said to Germany's RTL. "I love Berlin, totally. I love being back here and there's a pretty good chance I'll be back again." Gemechu Dida took second in 2:03:19, continuing an impressive event for the Ethiopians, with Gabriel Geay of Tanzania third in 2:03:59.
Held in temperate September, the Berlin marathon is considered the fastest of the major courses. The world record has been broken 13 times in Berlin, more than anywhere else. The late withdrawal of men's world record holder Sabastian Sawe, the 2025 Berlin winner who became the first man to crack the two-hour barrier earlier this year, meant hopes of another world mark shifted to Assefa. Paris Olympics silver medallist Assefa, now a three-time winner in Berlin, pledged to run "better than my best" before Sunday's race, which would put her on track for a shot at the world mark. Assefa began strongly and had already opened up a lead of 25 seconds by the 5km mark which grew to a minute at 15km. Assefa largely stayed on world record pace throughout, only dropping below around the 25km mark at the flat course's only incline, before returning to record speed. The Ethiopian was still on track for the record at 35km, pulling 15 seconds clear of the pace needed. She was still 10 seconds ahead of the required tempo with just two kilometres to go. But with the finish line almost in sight, Assefa began to be troubled by a foot problem and started limping. She gamely fought on but her hopes at the record were dashed.

title: New York on screen  A movie lover   s guide to the city   s iconic film locations
description: From  Kal Ho Naa Ho  and Spider Man to Gossip Girl  explore the locations that became part of cinematic memory
content:
From 'Kal Ho Naa Ho' and Spider-Man to Gossip Girl, explore the locations that became part of cinematic memory
For generations of movie lovers, New York's bridges, avenues, subway stations, parks, museums and neighbourhood cafés have existed not merely as landmarks, but as pieces of cinematic memory.
A walk through Manhattan can feel strangely familiar: perhaps you have never lived there, yet you know the corner where a heroine hurried to work, the park where two characters fell in love, or the bridge where a movie star stood against the skyline.
For Bollywood audiences, New York has long carried a particular romance. From Shah Rukh Khan and Preity Zinta wandering through Manhattan in Kal Ho Naa Ho to the complicated love stories of Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna , the city became part of the emotional vocabulary of Hindi cinema.
Hollywood, meanwhile, has turned the same streets into everything from a fashion editor's playground in The Devil Wears Prada to a superhero's battleground in Spider-Man .
And then there are films such as Past Lives , which use the city more quietly, allowing its bridges, waterfronts and ordinary streets to hold the weight of memory.
For film fans visiting New York, the result is almost a cinematic treasure hunt.
When Shah Rukh Khan made New York feel like Bollywood in Kal Ho Naa Ho
Few films have connected Bollywood and New York as memorably as Kal Ho Naa Ho .
Released in 2003, the Nikkhil Advani-directed film follows Naina, Aman and Rohit, played by Preity Zinta, Shah Rukh Khan and Saif Ali Khan, through a New York that feels both enormous and intimate. The movie's locations became almost as recognisable as its stars.
Bethesda Terrace in Central Park is among the most evocative stops. The terrace, fountain and surrounding walkways appear in the film's musical sequences, while the Brooklyn Bridge and Manhattan's skyline provide another unmistakable visual backdrop.
According to location research by On the Set of New York , Kal Ho Naa Ho also used Times Square and Bow Bridge, and frequently filmed by the pier showcasing the East River.
The film's pizza restaurant is another particularly interesting stop: location research identifies the former setting of Jenny's restaurant at 82 Reade Street in Tribeca.
For Bollywood fans, however, the appeal is not simply standing in the same place as the actors. It is the sensation of seeing a familiar film world suddenly become three-dimensional.
Karan Johar's Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna gave New York an altogether different mood.
Released in 2006, the film placed its characters' complicated relationships against a city of skyscrapers, parks, railway stations and winter streets. But there is an important detail for movie-location hunters: although the story is set in New York, not every supposedly New York location was actually filmed there.
According to location records , significant portions of the film were shot elsewhere in the United States. The production used locations in New York, New Jersey, Connecticut and Pennsylvania, with New Haven's Union Station and Philadelphia's 30th Street Station standing in for some scenes associated with Grand Central.
The song Tumhi Dekho Naa , meanwhile, made extensive use of recognisable locations in and around New York. Location accounts identify Columbia University, Wall Street, St Patrick's Cathedral and Pier A Park in Hoboken among the places used for its colourful sequences.
That distinction is part of the fun of film tourism: sometimes the place on screen is exactly where you think it is, and sometimes the magic of filmmaking has quietly moved it somewhere else.
Bollywood's relationship with New York is not limited to romance.
In Gauri Shinde's English Vinglish , New York becomes the setting for Shashi Godbole's personal transformation. Sridevi's character arrives in Manhattan uncertain and uncomfortable, gradually learning to navigate the city and an English-language environment on her own.
The film was shot primarily in New York, and Manhattan is not treated simply as a postcard. It is initially overwhelming for Shashi before gradually becoming a place she can navigate with confidence.
The song Manhattan captures that transformation through a lively tour of the city, turning shopping streets, skyscrapers and Manhattan's famous urban landscape into part of Shashi's journey. Contemporary coverage of the film also highlighted the sequence's playful references to New York shopping and its city-tour quality.
For Hollywood fans, few New York film trails are as instantly recognisable as Spider-Man .
The Roosevelt Island Tramway became part of the visual language of Sam Raimi's 2002 Spider-Man . In the film, the tram and the Queensboro Bridge form the setting for the climactic confrontation involving Spider-Man, the Green Goblin and Mary Jane. The tramway has subsequently become one of the city's most recognisable film-related attractions.
The Roosevelt Island Tramway itself is worth taking even without the superhero connection. The aerial ride crosses the East River between Manhattan and Roosevelt Island, offering a perspective of the skyline that is difficult to reproduce from street level.
In Spider-Man 2 , Peter Parker works as a pizza deliveryman and eventually loses his job after a late delivery. The pizza shop used for those scenes was Joe's Pizza in Greenwich Village at 233 Bleecker Street; the famous Joe's Pizza operation is now associated with its Greenwich Village location at 7 Carmine Street.
Joe's Pizza has therefore become an easy stop for anyone wanting to recreate a very different kind of New York movie moment: less romance, more "friendly neighbourhood Spider-Man".
Jane's Carousel: where Past Lives found its quiet New York
Not every cinematic New York moment needs a skyscraper.
One of the most beautiful examples is Jane's Carousel in Brooklyn Bridge Park, featured in Celine Song's Past Lives .
The film brings Nora and Hae Sung together in New York after years apart, and their conversation beside the carousel is charged with the awareness of their childhood selves and the lives they have since built.
Sung has explained why the location mattered to her. In an interview about the film, she described the carousel as something that represented where the characters were emotionally — their childhood selves still existing in their memories, even though they are now adults. She was also drawn to the delicate glass enclosure surrounding the carousel.
The Met steps and the Upper East Side belong to Gossip Girl
For a different version of New York glamour, head uptown.
The Upper East Side became almost inseparable from Gossip Girl , the television series that transformed Manhattan's young elite into a world of private schools, designer clothes, penthouses and carefully guarded secrets.
The steps of The Metropolitan Museum of Art became one of the show's most recognisable gathering points. Blair Waldorf, Serena van der Woodsen and their friends famously occupied the steps, turning an entrance to one of the world's great museums into a piece of teen-TV mythology.
According to NYC Tourism, the Met's Fifth Avenue steps were used as the place where Blair and her friends took lunch breaks before heading to their fictional schools. The series also used locations including the Lotte New York Palace.
For visitors, the Upper East Side offers something different from the frantic energy of Times Square. Here, the cinematic fantasy is quieter: Fifth Avenue, Central Park, grand apartment buildings and museum steps become the backdrop to a polished New York life.
Fashion's New York: The Devil Wears Prada
If Gossip Girl presented the fantasy of Manhattan's social elite, The Devil Wears Prada took viewers inside the city's fashion-and-media machinery.
Anne Hathaway's Andy Sachs moves through a recognisable Manhattan, travelling between her Lower East Side home and the fictional Runway magazine headquarters.
The building used for the exterior of the fictional Elias-Clarke/Runway headquarters is 1221 Avenue of the Americas, while Smith & Wollensky appears as the restaurant where Andy has to pick up Miranda Priestly's lunch. The American Museum of Natural History also serves as the exterior of the museum gala.
The movie was shot primarily in New York and Paris, with New York providing much of its visual identity.
A film fan can therefore build an entire fashion-themed walk around the movie: Lower East Side streets, Midtown, Madison Avenue, Central Park and the Upper East Side.
And, appropriately, the city itself becomes the ultimate accessory.
Before social media turned every New York street into a backdrop for a photograph, 13 Going on 30 gave audiences another glossy version of Manhattan.
Jennifer Garner's Jenna Rink wakes up as an adult and discovers a life as a successful magazine editor. Her fictional workplace, Poise magazine, was represented by locations including 444 Madison Avenue, while her apartment was filmed at 51 Fifth Avenue. The movie also used Times Square, Central Park, the New York Public Library and several Greenwich Village locations.
For visitors, this is perhaps one of the most satisfying movie trails because the film jumps naturally between the city's neighbourhoods: Fifth Avenue glamour, Greenwich Village streets, Central Park and Midtown.
It is New York as seen through the eyes of someone suddenly given permission to experience everything at once.
For an entire generation of children, the American Museum of Natural History was not simply a museum. It was the place where dinosaurs could roar, statues could talk and a night watchman could suddenly find himself surrounded by a world that had come alive.
Ben Stiller's Night at the Museum turned the museum at Central Park West and 79th Street into one of the most recognisable cinematic landmarks in New York.
The real museum was used for exterior filming, while many of the elaborate interior sequences were recreated on soundstages in British Columbia. But for moviegoers, that distinction almost does not matter.
Walk up to the museum today and the memories arrive immediately: Larry Daley beginning his first night shift, Rexy the T-rex, the miniature cowboys and Romans, Teddy Roosevelt appearing in the darkness, and the entire museum becoming a world of its own.
The American Museum of Natural History has even highlighted the real exhibits that inspired the Night at the Museum films, giving visitors the chance to connect the movie's fantasy with the actual museum collections.
And that may be one of the reasons New York works so well on screen: it can represent different things to different characters.
To one person, it is a place to fall in love. To another, it is a place to reinvent yourself. Perhaps the greatest pleasure of following New York through movies is discovering that the real city is both more ordinary and more extraordinary than the cinematic version.
But for movie lovers, the real magic begins when the screen ends and you find yourself standing inside the frame.

title: Netanyahu   s UN broadside draws sharp backlash
description: Officials  political figures  Israeli voices push back on Netanyahu   s attacks  defence of Gaza war
content:
Officials, political figures, Israeli voices push back on Netanyahu’s attacks, defence of Gaza war
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu used the United Nations General Assembly podium last week to lash out at governments and public figures critical of Israel, but his accusations were quickly turned against him as he was criticised for deflection and political scapegoating.
Netanyahu’s speech had already been thinned by a massive walkout in the chamber as he approached the podium, to which he responded by calling departing delegates “moral cowards.”
He then spent much of his address defending Israel’s conduct in the Gaza Strip — where Israel’s genocidal attacks since October 2023 have led to tens of thousands of Palestinian deaths — and attacking critics ranging from Turkiye and Qatar to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani .
Netanyahu portrayed criticism of Israel as the product not only of opposition to its policies but also of disinformation, political hostility and organised efforts to influence public opinion. Others rejected that framing.
Turkiye’s Communications Director Burhanettin Duran asserted that Netanyahu was using the UN platform for “baseless accusations” against Ankara and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan while seeking to draw attention away from Gaza.
Netanyahu’s criticisms of Ankara included hostility toward Israel and taking aim at its regional policies and political record. Duran said the remarks could not obscure the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza or international legal proceedings that had led to an arrest warrant against the Israeli prime minister.
Read: Six big takeaways from a turbulent week of UN diplomacy
“Netanyahu’s insolent and vile remarks targeting our president cannot cover up his massacres, the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, and the proceedings before international law,” Duran said in a statement issued by Turkiye’s Directorate of Communications.
The International Criminal Court issued the warrant for Netanyahu in November 2024 over allegations of war crimes and crimes against humanity.
Qatar, another major focus of Netanyahu’s speech, challenged his contention that Doha was helping drive growing anti-Israel sentiment abroad.
Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed Al Ansari said Qatar “categorically” rejected the accusation that it was orchestrating a campaign to turn public opinion against Israel . Instead, he argued that Netanyahu was attempting to explain away a deterioration in Israel’s international standing by blaming outsiders.
“Reducing the growing shift in global public opinion, particularly among young people, to allegations of ‘influence campaigns’ is an insult to the awareness and judgment of a generation that is witnessing, in real time and before the entire world, what is taking place on the ground,” Al Ansari said.
He said Israeli leaders seeking to change perceptions of the country should change their policies, respect international law and take responsibility rather than search for “scapegoats.”
Qatar’s deputy ambassador in Washington, Hamad Al-Muftah, went further, pointing directly to the reception Netanyahu received at the UN. “Speaking to a half-empty room during his UN remarks says plenty about the support for this message,” Al-Muftah wrote on X, sharing a black-and-white photo of Netanyahu beside a scowling President Donald Trump as he called Qatar to apologise for deadly Israeli airstrikes earlier this year.
@IsraeliPM speaking to half-empty room during his UN remarks says plenty about the support for this message. Blaming Qatar for a political failures does not change the facts. Qatar’s reported funding of American universities has overwhelmingly supported the operation of U.S.… pic.twitter.com/r8MXgZE7QC
He disputed Netanyahu’s description of Qatari financing of American universities, saying much of the funding supported United States universities operating campuses in Doha’s Education City and that the institutions retained control of their academic programs.
Al-Muftah also rejected Netanyahu’s criticism of Qatar for hosting representatives of Palestinian group Hamas, noting that Doha’s contacts with the organisation had enabled it to serve as a mediator in negotiations also involving Israel, the US and Egypt.
“Attacking one of the countries doing the difficult work of mediation does nothing to solve the problem,” he said.
Besides states and leaders, Netanyahu’s broadside also included individuals. Standing in the city Mamdani governs, Netanyahu called him “the antisemitic mayor of New York,” accused him of spreading lies about Israel and claimed Jewish residents had felt less safe since his election.
He also rebuked Mamdani for describing Israel’s actions in Gaza as genocide and for his past statements about the ICC warrant . “You tried to stop me from coming here. You tried to silence me. Well, you can’t silence me,” Netanyahu said.
Read More: Inside the UN walkout: Who left and who stayed for Netanyahu’s speech
Mamdani rejected the accusations, accusing Netanyahu in turn of repeating “baseless lies” to defend Israel’s conduct toward Palestinians.
The mayor had already offered a symbolic response before Netanyahu spoke. Hours earlier, he posted footage of himself planting an olive tree at Gracie Mansion alongside Palestinian families from Gaza, writing: “May peace be our future.”
Netanyahu also pulled US political streamer Hasan Piker into his attack on Mamdani, citing Piker’s controversial 2019 remark that “America deserved 9/11.” Piker has said the remark, for which he later expressed regret over the wording, referred to what he viewed as consequences of US foreign policy rather than the victims of the attacks.
He reacted to his mention during a livestream, questioning why an Israeli prime minister addressing the world body had devoted part of his speech to him while calling attention to Netanyahu’s own comments after the September 11, 2001 attacks.
Little standing to lecture on ‘barbarity’
Criticism of the speech also came from within Israel. Writing in the newspaper Haaretz following Netanyahu’s address, Israeli journalist Gideon Levy challenged the prime minister’s repeated framing of Israel as confronting “barbarity.”
Levy argued that Netanyahu’s focus on the conduct of Israel’s enemies left unaddressed what the columnist described as a profound moral crisis within Israel itself.
He was blunt in his criticism of Netanyahu, arguing that the premier had little standing to lecture others about “barbarity” after the destruction in Gaza.
“If 1,000 babies under the age of a year who were killed by pilots and soldiers aren't a sign of barbarity, then what is barbarity?” he questioned.

title: SCO meeting to begin in Islamabad under Pakistan s chairmanship on Monday  FO
description: Session to contribute to preparations for SCO Council of Heads of State meeting that Pak will host in August 2027
content:
Session to contribute to preparations for SCO Council of Heads of State meeting that Pak will host in August 2027
Pakistan is set to hold the first meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s (SCO) Council of National Coordinators (CNC) under its chairmanship in Islamabad from Monday, with the three-day session set to contribute to preparations for the SCO Council of Heads of State meeting that Pakistan will host in August 2027, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Sunday.
According to a statement on X, the meeting will be held from September 28 to 30 and will be chaired by Pakistan’s National Coordinator for the SCO, with national coordinators from SCO member states and representatives of the SCO Secretariat in attendance.
The national coordinators will discuss a “wide range of issues relating to SCO cooperation and coordination”, including the “programme of activities under Pakistan’s Chairmanship”, preparations for upcoming SCO meetings and events, and other matters on the organisation’s agenda, the FO said.
The meeting would mark an “important initial engagement” under Pakistan’s chairmanship and would contribute to preparations for “various high-level engagements and activities” to be undertaken during the chairmanship, including the SCO Council of Heads of State meeting to be hosted by Pakistan in August 2027.
🔊PR No.2️⃣6️⃣8️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Curtain Raiser: First Meeting of SCO Council of National Coordinators, Islamabad (28-30 September 2026) 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/lONYHH2K0V
Pakistan, which holds the chairmanship of the SCO Council of Heads of State for 2026-27, would seek to advance the organisation’s objectives under the theme “Turning Vision into Action: Connectivity, Innovation and Shared Prosperity”, according to the FO.
“In this regard, Pakistan’s Chairmanship would focus on promoting greater connectivity, fostering innovation, enhancing economic cooperation, and strengthening people-to-people contacts,” it said.
The FO said the aim would be to “translate the shared vision of Member States into practical and mutually beneficial initiatives”.
“Pakistan would work closely with all Member States and the SCO Secretariat to advance these priorities and further strengthen cooperation within the SCO,” it said.
Read: Water is 'lifeblood of our region', must never be weaponised: PM Shehbaz at SCO summit
The CNC meeting will therefore provide an early forum for coordination among member states as Pakistan begins its programme of activities as chair of the SCO Council of Heads of State, the FO said.
According to the statement, the meeting would contribute to preparations for various high-level engagements and activities during Pakistan’s chairmanship, including the August 2027 meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of State.
Earlier this month, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif travelled to Bishkek for a three-day official visit to attend the SCO Council of Heads of State meeting and the SCO Plus Summit, where Pakistan assumed the organisation’s chairmanship for 2026-27.
Under the chairmanship, Pakistan will lead the SCO’s top-level deliberations and host the organisation’s summit in Pakistan in 2027.
During the visit, Shehbaz proposed an “ excellent plan ” focused on key sectors including information technology and artificial intelligence, energy development, poverty reduction, disaster management, health, culture and sports.

title: Did Johnny Depp take dig at Amber Heard with plant eating moment  Actor draws attention for bizarre act at Vegas event
description: Depp has recently returned to public appearances to promote his upcoming film  Ebenezer  A Christmas Carol
content:
Depp has recently returned to public appearances to promote his upcoming film 'Ebenezer: A Christmas Carol'
Johnny Depp sparked speculation at a Las Vegas food and beverage festival after appearing to bite a decorative plant while posing for photographers, with some fans linking the moment to Amber Heard’s famous flower scene in Aquaman .
The 63-year-old actor attended Drink Las Vegas, a four-day festival running from September 24 to 27 across several MGM resorts.
According to reports, Depp was seen at Park MGM on Thursday night, September 25.
Video obtained by TMZ showed Depp posing for photographs before turning towards the foliage backdrop and taking a bite.
Johnny Depp showed up in Vegas for a food and drink festival but apparently couldn’t wait for the main course 🤣 The Pirates of the Caribbean star, 63, began chowing down on the floral backdrop as he posed on the red carpet at Drink Las Vegas 🍹 📽️: @jpasc24 #johnnydepp pic.twitter.com/idkYwAAhqw
He then returned to the cameras with a leaf in his mouth, dropped it and appeared to signal for photographers to wait before taking another bite. He later raised his glass while still posing.
The moment drew comparisons with a scene from Aquaman in which Heard’s character, Mera, mistakes a red rose for food while walking through a Sicilian market with Arthur Curry, played by Jason Momoa.
Some fans have therefore questioned whether Depp’s plant-eating moment was a reference to the scene, although there is no confirmation that it was intentional.
The comparison comes against the backdrop of Depp and Heard’s highly publicised legal battles. Heard accused Depp of abuse, which he denied.
Their 2022 US defamation trial ended with both parties found liable for defamation, with Depp awarded $15 million in damages and Heard awarded $2 million.
The pair later settled the case in December 2022.
Depp has recently returned to public appearances, including a San Diego Comic-Con appearance in July to promote his upcoming film Ebenezer: A Christmas Carol .

title: Aap Ki Izzat  finale divides viewers over Tabish and Beena s reunion
description: Fans praise Ahsan Khan and Urwa Hocane for their compelling performances in the drama
content:
Fans praise Ahsan Khan and Urwa Hocane for their compelling performances in the drama
Aap Ki Izzat has ended on an emotional note, with Tabish and Beena finding their way back to each other in a finale that divided viewers over whether their reunion offered a satisfying resolution to the couple’s troubled relationship.
The final episode brought the two characters together after a series of painful experiences and misunderstandings, ultimately reuniting their family.
While some viewers welcomed the emotional ending and praised Ahsan Khan and Urwa Hocane for their performances, others felt the resolution made forgiveness seem too easy and did not fully address the consequences of Tabish’s actions.
Khan took to Instagram to share clips and reactions from the final episode, with fans flooding his Stories with messages of appreciation for the lead actors and their performances throughout the drama.
One viewer defended the decision to give the couple a positive ending, describing their reconciliation as an imperfect but meaningful portrayal of marriage.
“Best believe we all were in tears. This is marriage. This is the relationship between a husband and wife. They fight, they quarrel, they get upset, there’s distance but in the end, there’s no bigger peace. Everything is complete when they are together,” the fan wrote.
Another viewer acknowledged that the finale might not have been what everyone wanted, but argued that the drama’s depiction of a damaged relationship still had value.
“It’s ever so easy to tell a woman or man who has betrayed one another, especially if they were married, to leave. Leave him. Leave her. Do they deserve it? Yes. Especially the one who betrayed first,” the fan wrote.
“Do we agree with everything in the story? Maybe not. Did we want this happy ending? Again, maybe not. But was this broken mess of a relationship, which found a not-so-perfect but happy ending, beautiful? Yes. This was beautiful,” the viewer added.
Not everyone was convinced, however. Some viewers felt the finale glossed over the consequences of Tabish’s actions and made reconciliation appear too straightforward. One fan described the resolution as “too easy and unrealistic”, drawing comparisons with the ending of Mere Paas Tum Ho .
Despite the disagreement over the conclusion, viewers broadly praised Khan and Hocane for portraying the emotional complexities of their characters, particularly their experiences with marital conflict and strained family relationships.
Khan later shared further reactions on Instagram, with one viewer writing, “I honestly don’t know how to put Ahsan Khan’s performance in Aap Ki Izzat into words. I’m simply speechless.”
Another praised the performances across the cast, writing, “Superb performance by the actors, Ahsan Khan, Urwa Hocane, and Sania Saeed.”
Bushra Ansari also took to Instagram to applaud the drama, praising its script and the performances of its lead actors.
“What a brilliant performance by Ahsan Khan and Urwa Hussain. You both actually shook the world and showed when the artists get a good script it really transforms the real person into the character they are playing,” she wrote.
The drama followed Tabish, a wealthy man married to Beena, with whom he had two children. Over the course of the story, Tabish became increasingly dismissive and hurtful towards Beena, with his remarks about her appearance and age further damaging their relationship.
The strain extended beyond their marriage, as Beena also felt unappreciated by her children and other members of the family. Tabish eventually married another woman, leaving Beena to rebuild her life.
She later sought a fresh start with a vegetable seller, only to discover that he was not the person she had believed him to be. After facing the consequences of their choices and confronting the issues that had driven them apart, Tabish and Beena eventually reconciled.
The finale ultimately left viewers with contrasting interpretations of what their reunion represented. For some, it was an emotional portrayal of forgiveness and the complexities of marriage; for others, it did not go far enough in exploring the consequences of betrayal.
Either way, the ending generated considerable discussion, with Khan and Hocane’s performances emerging as one of the most consistently praised aspects of the drama.

title: Floods  landslides kill 56 in India and 14 in Nepal
description: Nepal warns of flash floods in 49 districts as major rivers and tributaries rise  posing risks nationwide
content:
Nepal warns of flash floods in 49 districts as major rivers and tributaries rise, posing risks nationwide
Heavy rain and storms have triggered floods and landslides that killed 56 people in India, while in Nepal, 14 have died and another 11 are missing, with authorities there warning on Sunday ​that more flash floods are possible.
India's northern state of Uttar Pradesh recorded 66.5 mm of ​rain between September 25 and the morning of September 27, compared with a ⁠normal 7.6 mm for the period, Hrishikesh Bhaskar Yashod, the state's relief commissioner, said on Sunday.
Heavy rain and storms affected 63 districts, with the state recording 19 times its normal rainfall in the 24 hours to Saturday.
Read More: Nepal flood recovery bill to hit $4.78b
Authorities are ​carrying out rescue operations in waterlogged areas and distributing relief, while officials have been told to assess ​crop damage and provide compensation.
In addition to the 56 deaths, 46 people have been injured and more than 1,000 houses have been damaged.
Nepali authorities warned of possible flash floods in 49 of the country's 77 districts, with more than half ​facing high flood or flash-flood risks as water levels in major rivers and tributaries continued to rise.
Shanti ​Mahat, a spokesperson for the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, said Rasuwa and Nuwakot, areas hit by ‌last month's deadly ⁠floods that killed more than 1,450 people and left thousands still missing, should remain "alert" but were not currently considered high-risk areas.
Power supply has been completely disrupted in the Manang, Mustang, Myagdi and Baglung districts, with authorities working to restore electricity, energy ministry officials said.
Flooding of the Rahuganga River damaged the structure and ​transmission-line towers of a ​40-megawatt hydropower project, Water ⁠Resources and Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said.
Read: Nepal PM says floods 'a warning to the world' about climate change
In India, the Central Water Commission said 30 river-monitoring stations across seven states indicated a "severe situation".
Several major rivers, including ​the Ganga, Gandak, Kosi, Bagmati and Narmada, were above danger levels.
Floods and ​landslides also disrupted ⁠telecommunications in parts of Nepal after damage to optical fibres and power supplies, Communications Minister Bikram Timilsinha said.
In a separate incident in Nepal, 10 local workers were also missing after an avalanche buried the base camp ⁠of the ​7,126-metre (23,379-ft) Himlung Himal in the northern Manang district, hiking officials ​said.
The workers had been setting up tents for foreign climbers, who were not present when the avalanche struck.

title: Pakistan eye strong Asian Games start
description: Sahibzada Farhan   s charges face Hong Kong in quarter final
content:
Sahibzada Farhan’s charges face Hong Kong in quarter-final
Pakistan will begin their Asian Games cricket campaign on Monday when they face Hong Kong in the quarter-finals, with captain Sahibzada Farhan confident his side are prepared to negotiate unfamiliar conditions in Japan. Pakistan travelled to Japan after a four-day training camp in Karachi, where the squad practised on surfaces prepared to replicate the expected conditions and worked through a series of scenario matches. The team then trained in Nisshin on Sunday, although overnight rain left a wet outfield and disrupted the session. Farhan said the squad had focused heavily on adapting to conditions and preparing for spin during their camp. “We prepared wickets according to the conditions we expect in Japan and tried to practice against spin as much as possible,” Farhan told reporters before the team’s departure. “We also worked on different match scenarios during the camp.” The Pakistan captain said the squad’s mix of international, domestic and Pakistan Super League experience would help them adjust to conditions beyond their control. “As professional cricketers, we have to be mentally prepared for all conditions because the weather and playing conditions are not in our control,” he said. Farhan, who will lead Pakistan in the tournament, said the team would approach the competition one match at a time. “Every match is important for us. We will focus on our first match and take every game seriously,” he said. The captain also described the leadership role as a source of pride, while stressing that his approach would remain unchanged. “It is a proud moment for me and my family to captain Pakistan,” Farhan said. “Whether I am playing as captain or as a player, my mindset remains the same.” Pakistan have selected a 15-member squad featuring a blend of established and emerging T20 players, including vice-captain Abdul Samad, Saim Ayub, Haider Ali, Abrar Ahmed, Mohammad Wasim Jnr and wicketkeeper Usman Khan. Mike Hesson is the team’s head coach, supported by bowling coach Ashley Noffke and fielding coach Mansoor Amjad. The semi-finals are scheduled for October1, with the bronze-medal and gold-medal matches to be played on October 3. Squad: Sahibzada Farhan (captain), Abdul Samad (vice-captain), Abrar Ahmed, Ahmed Daniyal, Akif Javed, Ali Raza, Arafat Minhas, Haider Ali, Hasan Nawaz, Maaz Sadaqat, Mohammad Wasim Jnr, Saad Masood, Saim Ayub, Sufyan Moqim and Usman Khan (wicket-keeper) Support staff: Mike Hesson (head coach), Ashley Noffke (bowling coach), Mansoor Amjad (fielding coach), Muhammad Tahir (physiotherapist), Imran Ullah (trainer), Usman Hashmi (analyst-cum-team operations coordinator)

title: Mahira Khan marks 15 years of  Humsafar  with heartfelt tribute to her character
description: Actor celebrates drama   s anniversary while reflecting on Khirad  her career journey and fans who have stayed with her
content:
Actor celebrates drama’s anniversary while reflecting on Khirad, her career journey and fans who have stayed with her
Fifteen years after Humsafar first aired, Mahira Khan has marked the anniversary of the drama that introduced her as Khirad to audiences with a heartfelt tribute to the character, the journey that followed and the fans who have stayed with her along the way.
Khan shared a video on Instagram featuring herself dancing and twirling in a black dress, interspersed with clips from her role as Khirad in Humsafar . The video also featured her latest drama, Mitti De Baway , which premiered on the same day as the Humsafar anniversary.
“My dearest… my most precious Humsafars. 15 years. 15 years of loving and twirling in that love. Of surrendering to life, to the characters I picked and those that were picked for me,” Khan wrote in her Instagram post.
She added, “It is surreal to have Mitti De Baway air on the same day that Humsafar was aired that many years ago.”
While much has changed in Khan’s life and career since she played Khirad, she said her fans had remained a constant source of support.
“And even though so much has changed… all of you have remained the same for me. My constants. My backbone and my strength. From Khirad to Bilo… I am filled with nothing but shukr ,” she wrote.
Khan ended her message by thanking her fans for standing by her throughout her career.
“Here’s to all of you… here’s to a lifetime of being each other’s humsafars, may there never be judaai … may there never be bewafaai :) Ameen. Yours forever.”
Fans responded to the tribute with messages celebrating both her portrayal of Khirad and her return to television as Billo in Mitti De Baway .
“Some characters are remembered. Some are timeless. 15 years ago, you gave us Khirad, a performance that still holds a special place in our hearts. Today, you return as Billo, fearless, powerful, daring, unapologetic and unlike anything we’ve seen from you before. From Khirad to Billo, you continue to leave your mark,” one fan wrote.
Others became emotional while watching Khan’s Humsafar tribute, describing the drama as their “baby show” and a source of comfort and nostalgia.
BBC Asian Network also revisited a memorable interview with Khan from the Humsafar era, in which she spoke about the connection she shared with her co-star Fawad Khan, who played Ashar in the drama.
“There’s one thing I think about me and Fawad, this is a rare quality,” she said. “We come into a scene together and we sort of know each other’s beats, which is really lovely. It’s really nice that someone gets you and you get that person.”
Khan also spoke about the personal connection she felt with the drama, saying, “It’s my most untainted work. It’s me. There’s nothing not real about it.”
Written by Farhat Ishtiaq and based on her novel of the same name, Humsafar first aired in 2011 and went on to become one of the most recognisable dramas of its era.
For Khan, the role of Khirad became a defining early chapter in her acting career. Fifteen years on, her anniversary tribute offered a glimpse back at the character that helped shape her television journey, even as she begins a new chapter in Mitti De Baway .

title: How many VMAs has Taylor Swift aon  A look at Her MTV Awards history
description: Swift is tied with Beyonc   as the most awarded musician in MTV VMA history  with 30 Moon Person trophies each
content:
Swift is tied with Beyoncé as the most-awarded musician in MTV VMA history, with 30 Moon Person trophies each
Taylor Swift is set to add another honour to her collection at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards, where she will receive the inaugural Artist Director Honors.
Before the September 27 ceremony, Swift is tied with Beyoncé as the most-awarded musician in MTV VMA history, with 30 Moon Person trophies each. She is also nominated for 11 awards at this year's ceremony, including Artist of the Year and Best Direction.
Swift won her first VMA in 2009 for Best Female Video with You Belong with Me. She returned to the winners' list in 2013, taking home the same award for I Knew You Were Trouble.
Her biggest night came in 2015, when she won four awards, including Video of the Year and Best Collaboration for Bad Blood featuring Kendrick Lamar. In 2017, she won Best Collaboration alongside Zayn Malik for I Don't Wanna Live Forever, although she did not attend that year's ceremony.
Swift earned three more trophies in 2019, including Video of the Year and Video for Good for You Need to Calm Down, before winning Best Direction for The Man in 2020.
In 2022, All Too Well (10 Minute Version) won Video of the Year, Best Direction and Best Long Form Video. The Video of the Year victory made Swift the first artist to win the category three times.
Swift's Midnights era dominated the 2023 VMAs, earning her nine awards. She won major categories including Album of the Year, Artist of the Year and Video of the Year, while Anti-Hero collected six trophies.
At the 2024 VMAs, Swift won seven awards, with Fortnight featuring Post Malone taking Video of the Year, Song of the Summer, Best Direction, Best Collaboration and Best Editing. She also won Best Pop and Artist of the Year, bringing her career total to 30.
Swift is already guaranteed another addition to that total in 2026 through the Artist Director Honors. The new award recognises artists whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music videos and visual storytelling.
If Swift wins any of her 11 competitive nominations as well, her total will rise further. The 2026 MTV VMAs are scheduled to air live from Los Angeles on September 27.

title: Three local cricketers killed in firing on loader rickshaw in Lakki Marwat | The Express Tribune
description: Police say local youths returned fire after the attack, with reports that one of the attackers was killed
content:
Police say local youths returned fire after the attack, with reports that one of the attackers was killed
Three members of a local cricket team were killed and three others injured when unidentified armed men opened fire on a loader rickshaw near Abdul Khel after the group returned from a cricket match in Lakki Marwat's Shah Hasan Khel, Station House Officer (SHO) Aslam Khan said on Sunday.
The victims were travelling back to their village of Abdul Khel after playing a cricket match in Shah Hasan Khel when armed men intercepted the loader rickshaw and opened fire, according to police.
Three of the occupants, identified as Umer, Siddiq and Aliyan, were killed on the spot, while three others — Asifullah, Imdadullah and Ejaz — sustained bullet wounds in the attack.
Police said most of the victims were either cricket players or members of a local peace committee. The incident caused panic in the area, while residents rushed to the scene following the firing.
Police officials said that after the initial attack, some local youths present in the area returned fire at the assailants. They said there were reports that one of the attackers had been killed in the exchange of fire.
However, police said the identity of the alleged attacker could not immediately be established, and the report of his death had yet to be independently confirmed.
Read: Bodies of two missing FC personnel recovered in Bannu
The injured were shifted to a nearby hospital for medical treatment, while the bodies of the deceased were also taken to the hospital for medico-legal formalities.
Hospital spokesperson Wali Khan confirmed that three bodies and three injured people had been brought to the hospital following the incident. He said the injured were being provided medical treatment, while the bodies had been kept at the hospital for completion of medico-legal formalities.
Following the incident, a heavy contingent of police reached the area and cordoned it off. A search operation was launched to trace the attackers and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident.
Police officials said further investigation was under way and that details about the motive for the attack and the identity of those responsible would be established after completion of the investigation.
The incident came amid heightened security concerns in parts of Bannu, where tensions had recently escalated in the mountainous Hathi Khel area of Wazir subdivision.
Also Read: 13 held hostage by terrorists in Hathi Khel
Local sources had reported that 13 people were allegedly taken hostage while trying to leave Hathi Khel with their belongings. Police had not issued an official statement, although police sources had privately confirmed the reported hostage-taking.
Several families had reportedly moved to safer areas amid fears of violence and restrictions on movement. Sources had also alleged that armed militants were preventing residents from leaving the area, although the claims had not been officially confirmed.
The attack came amid heightened security concerns in parts of Bannu, where local peace committees and police personnel had been involved in efforts to maintain security in areas affected by militant activity.
The security situation in Bannu has remained under considerable pressure in recent weeks, with police, FC and other security personnel coming under attack in different parts of the district.
Read more: 13 held hostage by terrorists in Hathi Khel
Earlier this month, an Elite Force constable, Ahmadullah, was killed in a firing incident within the jurisdiction of Cantt police station. In another incident in the Paing area of Domel, a civilian was killed during an exchange of fire between members of a peace committee and armed men.
Similarly, a recent alleged quadcopter attack in the Hathi Khel area of Wazir subdivision left a woman and another civilian dead and two others injured. Police and security personnel, including the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD), Elite Force and members of a local peace committee, subsequently conducted an operation in the area. Police claimed that a suspected militant was also killed during the operation.
Meanwhile, authorities have also been considering additional security arrangements for the protection of vital installations in Bannu and Lakki Marwat. The provincial government had recently sought additional FC platoons for the protection of important installations in the two districts.
The latest incident once again highlighted security challenges in rural and sensitive areas of Bannu, particularly the movement and protection of security personnel and the need for effective measures to counter militant activity.

description: Men arrested on suspicion of explosives offences as Army bomb disposal teams examine vehicles near RAF Fairford
content:
Men arrested on suspicion of explosives offences as Army bomb disposal teams examine vehicles near RAF Fairford
British police said on Sunday they had arrested several men on suspicion of explosives offences and Army bomb disposal experts were examining a number of vehicles in a "major incident" near an air base used by the United States in southwest England.
Police said nearby residents had been evacuated from their homes.
The British government gave authorisation to the US to use RAF Fairford to carry out strikes on Iranian missile sites that are attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz . Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned in July that any base used in strikes would be a legitimate target.
A Reuters eyewitness said armed police had blocked access to the main gate of the base, while equipment had been positioned in front of access points and residents of a nearby village were evacuated to a leisure centre.
Read: US F-16 crashes at Spangdahlem air base in Germany
Around 30 emergency vehicles, including police cars, ambulances and fire engines, were stationed in the village of Fairford near the base.
"A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident. It follows the arrest of several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act," Gloucestershire police said in a statement, referring to a village near the air base.
"The Army's specialist explosive ordnance disposal team are currently examining a number of vehicles."
Police said they believed the incident was now contained.
A spokesperson for the US Air Force declined to discuss specific force protection measures. "The 501st Combat Support Wing and our fellow UK-based Wings remain vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, civilians, contractors, and their families," the spokesperson said.
Read More: Italian aircraft hit during air base attacks in Saudi Arabia
"We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families."
Britain said in July its armed forces were ready to protect the country from any attack after Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned the United Kingdom not to allow US bombers to ‌fly from Fairford.
British ministers have also briefed providers of critical infrastructure on the threat posed by Russia, with the government increasingly concerned about possible sabotage operations and cyberattacks . Russia denies mounting hybrid attacks on Western nations.

title: Over 70 terrorists killed in Balochistan in last 96 hours  ISPR
description: Military   s media wing says weapons  ammunition and explosives were also recovered during the operation
content:
President Zardari, PM Shehbaz pay tribute to security forces for their successful operations
Security forces have killed more than 71 terrorists in Operation Shaban and other areas of Balochistan over the last 96 hours, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Sunday.
According to the military’s media wing, "as the Army’s operation progresses, more than 71 terrorists have been killed so far in Operation Shaban and other areas of Balochistan in the last 96 hours, delivering a serious blow to Indian-backed Afghan proxies."
The statement further added that the operation was launched following credible intelligence about multiple hideouts of Indian-sponsored Fitna Al-Khawarij and Fitna Al-Hindustan terrorists in the general area of Shaban in Quetta district, which posed a threat to the local population.
The state uses the term Fitna Al-Khawarij for terrorists affiliated with the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, while Fitna Al-Hindustan refers to banned outfits sponsored by India in Balochistan.
"Security forces launched a swift operation in Ziarat and surrounding areas on September 21. During the operation, troops engaged the terrorists and cleared multiple hideouts. Following intense exchanges of fire, 33 Indian-sponsored terrorists were killed, while a significant quantity of weapons, ammunition and explosives was also recovered," the ISPR said.
According to the ISPR, over the past 72 hours, the operation was further intensified, resulting in the killing of 23 terrorists. Security forces cleared a vast area and relieved local communities of the threat posed by Fitna Al-Khawarij and Fitna Al-Hindustan .
Read: Security forces eliminate 16 Indian-sponsored terrorists in Balochistan IBOs: ISPR
"The clearance operation is continuing until complete neutralisation of the threat," it said.
In a separate intelligence-based operation in Nushki district on September 25, security forces engaged a terrorist hideout and killed 11 Indian-sponsored terrorists. In another operation in Mand, six Fitna Al-Hindustan terrorists were killed, while a large quantity of weapons and ammunition was recovered, the ISPR said.
The ISPR also said that the involvement of the Afghan Taliban regime in terrorist activities in Pakistan, backed and sponsored by India, continued to cause loss of precious lives and threaten peace and stability.
“The counter-terrorism campaign under the vision of " Azm-e-Istehkam ," approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, will continue with full resolve,” it said.
“Security Forces and Law Enforcement Agencies remain committed to eliminating foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country,” the ISPR added.
Read more: Security forces kill one terrorist in Balochistan's Kech
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif paid tribute to security forces for their successful operations in Balochistan.
In separate statements, they said the killing of more than 71 terrorists in different areas of Balochistan over the past 96 hours demonstrated the professionalism and bravery of the security forces.
President Zardari said the operations would continue until the complete elimination of terrorism allegedly fuelled by foreign patronage and support.
PM Shehbaz said Pakistan was determined to completely eliminate terrorism being carried out on its soil with foreign patronage and support.
President @AAliZardari and Prime Minister @CMShehbaz have paid tribute to security forces for their successful operations against terrorists belonging to Fitna Al-Khawarij and Fitna Al-Hindustan, operating with Indian patronage in Balochistan #News #Balochistan #RadioPakistan … pic.twitter.com/qMXlb3OeV5
The development came two days after security forces killed 16 terrorists in two separate intelligence-based operations in Balochistan on September 24 and 25, according to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR).
Five terrorists were killed during an operation in the Shaban area on September 24, taking the number killed in the ongoing Operation Shaban to 22 at the time, the military’s media wing said. Weapons, ammunition and explosives were also recovered from the hideouts, while the clearance operation was to continue until the “complete neutralisation of threat from the area”.
Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022, and over the same period, TTP attacks increased more than sevenfold to 838 from 118.
Although Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa has borne the brunt of terrorism, Balochistan has also remained a major target of Indian proxies, which often target civilians and military installations in the province.
In one such attack on the last day of 2025, terrorists targeted innocent civilians in Balochistan’s Gwadar and Kharan districts, where 18 people, including women, children, the elderly and labourers, embraced martyrdom.
The forces continued operations across the provinces against what the state describes as Indian-sponsored terrorists and their proxies. Still, despite these efforts, the groups have continued to target civilian and defence installations.
Last month, in another such attack, at least 30 people, including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. The attackers also abducted several civilians and police personnel after the assault.
In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation , which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

title: Newly inducted HANGOR conducts maiden live weapon firing in Arabian Sea  ISPR
description: Naval chief witnesses firing and praises the submarine   s combat power
content:
Naval chief witnesses firing and praises the submarine’s combat power
Pakistan Navy’s newly inducted submarine PNS/M HANGOR conducted its maiden live weapon firing in the North Arabian Sea, accurately engaging a designated long-range target with an anti-ship cruise missile, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Sunday.
According to the military's media wing, "Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf witnessed the firing and praised the submarine’s combat power," while emphasising the strategic importance of enhancing subsurface capabilities for credible maritime deterrence.
"The milestone underscores the Pakistan Navy’s commitment to maintaining a modern, combat-ready force to safeguard national maritime frontiers and regional peace", the statement added.
Pakistan Navy’s newly inducted submarine PNS/M HANGOR successfully conducted its maiden Live Weapon Firing in North Arabian Sea, launching an anti ship cruise missile and engaging the designated target with precision at extended range. 1/2 pic.twitter.com/bHn4VE9L79
On Saturday, Pakistan Navy ships HUNAIN and YARMOOK seized more than 2,800 kilogrammes of narcotics, valued at approximately $750 million, during a joint counter-narcotics operation in the Arabian Sea, the ISPR said.
According to the ISPR, the ships were conducting a routine patrol when they intercepted a suspicious boat. A boarding operation was subsequently carried out, during which narcotics were recovered from "concealed compartments," it said.
Admiral Ashraf commended the officers and crew for their "professionalism and vigilance", ISPR added.
Pakistan Navy Ships HUNAIN and YARMOOK conducted a joint counter narcotics operation in the Arabian Sea. During routine patrolling, a suspicious boat was intercepted and over 2,800 kg of narcotics, valued at approximately USD 750 million, were seized. 1/2 pic.twitter.com/QSpTwWViRL
The naval chief also reaffirmed Pakistan Navy's commitment to maritime security and combating illicit trafficking at sea, according to the statement.
Earlier on Wednesday , the Pakistan Navy and Coast Guard, in coordination with the Joint Maritime Information Coordination Centre (JMICC), confiscated "a sizeable quantity" of liquor and illegal medicines in the Pishukan area of Balochistan, ISPR said.
According to the ISPR, the joint intelligence-based operation "thwarted an attempt to smuggle a large cache of contraband items" in the area. The operation was carried out on "actionable intelligence," the ISPR said, adding that the "seized contraband items have been handed over to the Pakistan Coast Guard for further legal proceedings."
The military's media wing noted that the "successful joint operation underscores the effectiveness of inter-agency coordination in countering smuggling while highlighting the resolve of the Pakistan Navy and Pakistan Coast Guard to prevent the use of Pakistani waters and land for illicit activities."

title: K P CM demands armoured personnel carriers from federal govt
description: Afridi says province    bears brunt    of terrorism  criticises false narrative against people of K P
content:
Afridi says province ‘bears brunt’ of terrorism, criticises false narrative against people of K-P
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Sunday called on the federal government to provide the province with armoured personnel carriers (APCs), saying K-P was bearing the brunt of the ongoing wave of terrorism.
The statement came a day after a blast struck a joint checkpoint near Aman Mela in Dera Ismail Khan’s Darazinda area, killing at least 12 people and injuring 35 others, police said.
The Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) had claimed responsibility for the attack, while a Rescue 1122 official was also killed and two others were seriously injured when an ambulance transporting victims came under fire near Daraban.
Speaking at a press conference at Al-Amin House in Dera Ismail Khan alongside former K-P chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur, Afridi condemned the recent incident in Darazinda and said both civilians and Pakistan Army personnel were being martyred in the attack.
“We had seen it coming, which was why we were raising our voices,” he said, referring to warnings about terrorism in K-P.
He said the provincial government had allocated Rs35 billion to the police for maintaining peace and stressed that the people of K-P wanted peace.
Read: 12 killed, 35 injured as TTP strikes anti-smuggling checkpoint in K-P's DI Khan
“We realised that our children, women and young people were being martyred,” he said.
CM Afridi criticised the federal government, alleging that it was controlled by “a gang of thieves” and that K-P was not being provided with APCs despite having already made the required payment.
“We told the federal government to give us our APCs because your APCs were being used for us,” he said. “We were carrying the coffins; our province was wounded.”
The chief minister said the provincial government did not accept policies made behind closed doors and argued that lasting peace could not be established without taking the people of K-P into confidence.
“We were serious about eliminating terrorism,” he said. “Anyone who took up arms against Pakistan was a terrorist.” He also said the security situation in K-P and Balochistan had deteriorated to a point beyond the government's control.
Afridi said anyone killed in the current wave of terrorism would be provided with a martyr's compensation package.
Read more: Afridi warns of 'unprecedented' reaction if governor's rule imposed in K-P
He also criticised the false narrative against the people of K-P, saying residents of the province knew the standing of those promoting it.
K-P has witnessed a significant rise in terrorist activities since last week, after 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred in a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation.
Later, the Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
In a separate incident, a captain and a lieutenant were among six security personnel martyred in an exchange of fire in Hangu district, while eight terrorists were killed.
Following a series of deadly attacks in K-P, Pakistan carried out “calibrated” air strikes against terrorist hideouts near the Afghan border and conducted intelligence-based ground operations that killed a total of 37 terrorists.
Pakistan’s air defence systems also shot down eight drones after they entered the country’s airspace from Afghanistan. Security sources said four of the drones were brought down in areas adjoining the Torkham border, while another four were shot down in mountainous areas near the border with Kohat.
Reacting to the attack, Pakistan carried out “precision” air and drone strikes against 10 locations in Afghanistan.
