title: US immigration officers instructed to halt arrests of non criminal immigrants  report
description: Reported directive also ends  collateral arrests  of undocumented immigrants encountered during operations
content:
Reported directive also ends 'collateral arrests' of undocumented immigrants encountered during operations
United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers have been instructed to stop arresting immigrants who do not have criminal convictions or pending criminal charges, according to agency sources.
Under the reported directive, federal immigration agents may arrest immigrants with criminal convictions or pending criminal charges, while those with final deportation orders but no criminal convictions or charges would not be arrested, The Daily Wire reported.
The reported change would also end so-called “collateral arrests,” under which officers may detain others without legal status encountered while pursuing a criminal target, according to sources.
Read: US judge blocks Trump limits on how long foreign students, journalists can stay
The reported directive comes amid increased scrutiny of the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement policies and ICE operations.
Several ICE officers expressed frustration about the reported change, with one source suggesting it could be linked to the upcoming midterm elections . “We believe it has something to do with the midterms coming up,” said one source. “They’re trying to calm things down before the elections.”
“We’ll see the arrest numbers go down,” said another source.
Read More: Trump posts map appearing to show North America, other territories as part of US
The reported change comes about a week after an ICE officer shot and wounded a Venezuelan man in the state of Texas during an attempted traffic stop. The officer, who was reportedly hired by ICE last year after previously working for another federal law enforcement agency, had been issued a body camera but was not wearing it during the incident, according to US media reports citing federal officials.
ICE subsequently reminded officers that they “must activate” their body cameras during enforcement activities, according to an internal notice cited by The Washington Post .
A federal judge ordered Wilber Rafael Garces Perez from Venezuela to appear at a September 30 hearing, temporarily preventing his deportation.
An ICE source questioned whether Trump was aware of the reported directive. “I hope Trump finds out about this sh*t and puts an end to it,” said the source.

content:
India’s badminton medallist criticises logistics and a gruelling schedule
India badminton medallist H.S. Prannoy has criticised Asian Games organisers for putting on a "sad" event for athletes and arranging a "cruel" competition schedule for his sport.
Prannoy, who won a men's team bronze at the Aichi-Nagoya Games, said ‌the lack of a dedicated athletes' village had taken away the joy of mixing with other competitors, who had been spread across hotels, temporary wooden units and a cruise ship.
"The whole fun and the whole point of multi-sport events is you get to meet the rest of the players," he said in a video interview posted on ⁠the Badminton Association of India's YouTube channel on Saturday.
"There is an opportunity to mingle with them. There is an opportunity to have a conversation with them. We only felt that when we went for the opening ceremony.
“It was literally sad to be in such a situation."
Prannoy said the Games compared poorly to his experience at the last Asian Games in Hangzhou, China, where he was part of the silver medal-winning men's team.
"Straight from China, you expect things to be better three-four years later but in this event, (it went) downwards. A lot of (athletes) ‌had ⁠difficult experiences in terms of accommodation and transport.
“It was just a mediocre event, to be honest."
Aichi-Nagoya organisers did not immediately respond on Sunday to a request for comment on Prannoy's remarks.
On Saturday, an Aichi-Nagoya Games organising committee official apologised for logistical mistakes that have affected athletes, saying accommodation and transport had ⁠improved and that staff were working "to identify the causes of each mistake and make sure they don't happen again".
A number of athletes and teams have complained of logistical problems at the Games, ranging from ⁠long waits to check in to their rooms, to transport glitches.
Prannoy also criticised the badminton scheduling, noting players in the singles tournament had competed in two matches a day, one ⁠more than usual.
"It's cruel because everybody is aiming for a good Asian Games, which comes once in four years. To have two singles games in a day, I haven't seen it like that in ages," said Prannoy.

title: Six dead after explosion destroys building in Athens
description: Mayor says blast likely linked to gas infrastructure as building  reduced to twisted metal  shattered tiles  concrete
content:
Mayor says blast likely linked to gas infrastructure as building reduced to twisted metal, shattered tiles, concrete
Six people have died after a two-storey residential building in a tourist area of central Athens collapsed, the Greek fire brigade said on Saturday, following an explosion that the mayor said was likely linked to gas infrastructure.
The explosion killed four Americans, United States officials said.
Emergency crews in heavy gear and red helmets assisted by rescue dogs, cameras and sensors found the bodies of six people, fire brigade spokesman Vassilis Vathrakogiannis said in a televised briefing. They were looking for an elderly couple who lived in one apartment and four tourists who were staying in another as they removed debris from the building.
The fire brigade's crime investigation unit was also on site to identify the cause of the blast after reports of a gas smell in an area that is home to hotels and short-term rentals.
Read: Two dead, hundreds evacuated from fires on island near Athens
The tourists, two American couples, had been expected to catch a flight from Athens airport at 3pm on Friday but did not show up, a police source said.
Ambulances stood by on Saturday to take the bodies to the hospital for identification.
"I am deeply saddened to learn of the death of four American citizens in yesterday’s explosion in central Athens," Kimberly Guilfoyle, the US ambassador to Greece, posted on X.
I am deeply saddened to learn of the death of four American citizens in yesterday’s explosion in central Athens. My thoughts and prayers are with the families and the loved ones of those killed and injured in this horrific incident. Our hearts are with them during this difficult… pic.twitter.com/DffTSG1qEv
The blast destroyed the building in Plaka, near some of Athens' most visited sites, including the Acropolis and the Temple of Zeus, damaging nearby houses, shops and cars and sending rubble and broken glass as far as three blocks away.
The building was reduced to twisted metal, shattered tiles and concrete, strewn with household items and clothing.

title: How young is too young as child prodigies win big at Asian Games
description: Kurihara beats his opponent 10 2 in the Puyo Puyo Champions final
content:
Kurihara beats his opponent 10-2 in the Puyo Puyo Champions final
The Asian Games has crowned teenage champions before, but this edition has witnessed stunning successes by child prodigies, culminating in Yuki Kurihara standing atop the podium aged just 11.
The Japanese primary school student demolished opponents three times his age on the way to a historic gold in eSports in Aichi-Nagoya.
He is Japan's youngest Asian Games champion in history and almost certainly the youngest the Games have ever seen.
Kurihara did not even react after winning Saturday's final in Puyo Puyo Champions, a puzzle game where players try to clear their screen of coloured blobs by lining them up and popping them.
The boy, who does not turn 12 until June and wants to be a train driver when he grows up, later explained that he felt "embarrassed".
Kurihara's face was splashed across national newspapers on Sunday.
There is no publicly available official list of the youngest medallists ever at the Games, which were first contested in 1951.
But the introduction in recent editions of events intended to attract younger viewers has resulted in some eye-catching displays by children.
In skateboarding, Taiwan's 12-year-old Ku Yong-yan took home silver on Friday in the "men's" park final.
The winner, Japan's Izuru Nagahara, was a relative veteran at 15.
Nagahara had anaesthetic injections in his knee to dull the pain from injury before his winning run.
Also in the skateboarding was Mazel Paris of the Philippines, who was just nine when she competed at the previous Asian Games.
Asked what has changed since Hangzhou in 2023, the 12-year-old replied: "I got taller for sure."
This week will see another teenage phenomenon enter the fray with India's 15-year-old cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.
But the presence of young children competing on the international stage against adults and under expectations to win for their country comes with a caveat.
Kanae Doi, Japan director at Human Rights Watch, said ahead of the Games that "moments of triumph do not come easily. They are built on years of disciplined training, often beginning in childhood".
"At its best, that journey should provide children with the joy of play and competition, along with opportunities for physical, mental and personal growth," she wrote in the Japan Times.
"Many young athletes instead encounter physical, verbal and even sexual abuse in the very environments meant to help them develop."
She said that in Games host Japan, children "frequently experience abuse in sports training within Japanese schools, federations and elite sports programmes".
In 2024, the International Olympic Committee released its consensus statement on youth athletes at the Olympic Games.
It noted that 50 percent of common mental health conditions first emerge before 18.
Adolescent athletes are also more susceptible to certain injuries, it said.
Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi became the youngest medallist in world championships history last year with bronze aged 12.
Now a teenager and hotly tipped to make a splash at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, Yu is one of the faces of the Nagoya Games with three golds, all in record times.
But when it came to reporters swarming around her after races, she looked all of her 13 years.
"Interviews are way harder than the race," she said.
Each sport has its own rules on minimum age.
For World Aquatics, the minimum age for major international championships is 14 but exceptions can be made for younger swimmers if, like Yu, they are fast enough.
Yu has spoken previously about struggling to balance her swimming with school work.
Yu's team-mate Zhang Yufei, 28, a multiple Olympic gold medallist and world champion, said the youngster's stunning displays were no longer a shock.
But she cautioned: "I hope she can withstand that pressure."

title: Ansar Abbas qualifies for Asian Games long jump final
description: Pakistan   s seasoned athlete records 7 28m to progress  shooter Rabia Kabir finishes 41st in pistol event
content:
Pakistan’s seasoned athlete records 7.28m to progress; shooter Rabia Kabir finishes 41st in pistol event
Pakistan’s Ansar Abbas qualified for the men’s long jump final after recording 7.28 metres at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium on Sunday.
Abbas finished 12th in the qualification round, securing a spot in the final. His 7.28-metre effort also marked a personal best, according to the official results.
However sources said that Ansar had done 7.69m in Karachi National Games and 7.55m in National Championship.
“These people don’t take our national championship statistics. And I think they have considered this keeping in view his international record and I think its personal best in international circuit,” the source said.
Uzbekistan’s Anvar Anvarov topped the qualification with a jump of 8.00 metres, while India’s Murali Sreeshankar finished second at 7.84 metres. Japan’s Yuki Hashioka was third with 7.74 metres.
Abbas’s performance put him among the 12 athletes advancing to the final. Hong Kong’s Wong Pak Hang also recorded 7.28 metres but missed qualification after finishing 13th.
The final will be held on Monday (tomorrow).
Pakistan’s Rabia Kabir finished 41st in the women’s 25-metre pistol qualification at the Aichi Prefecture General Shooting Gallery in Nagoya on Sunday.
Kabir scored 278 points with four inner tens (278-4x) in the precision stage, placing her 41st among 44 shooters listed in the official results.
South Korea’s Yang Jiin led the qualification with 292-11x, followed by Iran’s Haniyeh Rostamiyan and Vietnam’s Trinh Thu Vinh, who both scored 291 points.
Qatar defeated Pakistan 7-5 in fencing men’s epee team competition at the Aichi Sky Expo Hall F on Sunday.
The closely fought bout featured three relay periods, with Qatar establishing an early advantage and maintaining it through the final exchange.
Muhammad Abdulali gave Qatar a strong start in the opening relay, outscoring Pakistan’s Abdul Musawir 5-2 and putting Qatar ahead. Abdulrahman Aljadra then extended the advantage in the second relay, with Qatar reaching 7-5 against Baryal Khan.
The third relay between Ali Alkhlif of Qatar and Muhammad Waqas of Pakistan ended without either side adding to the score, leaving Qatar with the overall 7-5 victory.
Qatar’s Youssef AbdelTawab was also listed among the team’s fencers, while Pakistan’s Muhammad Yaseen Khan completed its lineup.
The match recorded no yellow or red cards. Both teams received a passivity card during the contest.
Qatar now moved into the next stage while Pakistan was eliminated.

title: Optical fibre cable cut disrupts internet services in twin cities
description: PTA says repair of optical fibre cable  complete restoration of services can take several hours
content:
PTA says repair of optical fibre cable, complete restoration of services can take several hours
Internet services were partially disrupted in parts of Islamabad and Rawalpindi on Sunday after a telecom operator's optical fibre cable was cut, the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) said.
Mobile data and Wi-Fi services were affected in some areas of the twin cities, causing difficulties for residents. The PTA said the cable cut had caused partial disruption to the networks of some service providers.
“The internet service disruption was limited to some local and surrounding areas,” it added.
It said internet services in the central and southern parts of the country were operating normally, while some areas in the northern region had also been affected.
The PTA advised residents not to be concerned about the partial disruption, saying technical teams were working to repair the damaged optical fibre cable and restore services.
“Efforts were underway to restore internet services in the affected areas as soon as possible,” it said.
The PTA said the repair of the optical fibre cable and complete restoration of services could take several hours.
Read: PTA warns of intermittent internet issues after submarine cable fault
The PTA had previously reported disruptions to internet traffic on July 2 after a fault developed in the SEA-ME-WE 5 (SMW5) international submarine cable system.
The regulator had said some users could experience intermittent deterioration in internet service quality and connectivity, while Transworld Associates (TWA) worked with the SMW5 consortium to identify the cause of the fault and estimate the restoration time.
Internet traffic had been rerouted through alternative international links to minimise the impact and maintain continuity of services.

title: OpenAI  Anthropic CEOs called to appear at Australian AI probe
description: Altman  Amodei to appear at Senate inquiry after rogue OpenAI bot hacks country s health system database
content:
Altman, Amodei to appear at Senate inquiry after rogue OpenAI bot hacks country's health-system database
The CEOs of OpenAI and Anthropic have been called to appear at an Australian Senate inquiry on AI, the head of the probe said on Sunday, days after the revelation that a rogue OpenAI bot had hacked the country's health-system database .
The Medicare breach, condemned by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, is one of the highest-profile incidents of AI agents accessing external systems outside the United States.
OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei have been sent written requests to appear at the inquiry, which is to hold public hearings in the capital Canberra on Thursday, said a spokesperson for Senator Sarah Hanson-Young of the Australian Greens party, who chairs the probe.
Read: OpenAI agents accessed information from US govt sites, company says
OpenAI and Anthropic did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside business hours.
The OpenAI agent's incursion on one of the country's most used government agencies may prompt Albanese's Labor government to toughen AI-specific laws it is readying for next year, adding pressure to Australia-US relations already tested by Canberra's ban on social media for teens, tech policy experts say.
The Senate inquiry is examining the potential impacts of AI and data centres on Australian communities, industries, water and energy. It is one of several state and federal probes into AI.
Read More: Bill Gates warns AI is powerful enough to 'cause a billion deaths'
"There are serious questions for Sam Altman to answer about the OpenAI hack of Australian government websites," Hanson-Young said in a statement. Altman and Amodei "must front up, face the Senate's questions and have an honest conversation about what effective, lasting regulation of this industry should look like", she said.
Albanese, who revealed the June breach of Medicare on Thursday, called it "unacceptable", saying he had voiced "extreme concern" to Altman.
OpenAI says it only learned of the breach — one of at least four of Australian government websites — in August. It says the incident was not intentional and did not compromise any private information.

title: Swiss voters overwhelmingly reject initiative to enshrine stricter neutrality rules
description: Opposition to neutrality initiative reached 70 15   with voters in all 26 cantons rejecting it
content:
Opposition to neutrality initiative reached 70.15%, with voters in all 26 cantons rejecting it
Swiss voters on Sunday roundly rejected an initiative seeking to enshrine stricter neutrality rules in the country's Constitution, according to official results.
Official results showed 70.15% voting against the "Safeguard Swiss neutrality" initiative, while just 29.85% backed it.
Results broken down by the country’s cantons – which played a role in the overall vote – mirrored the rejection, as "no" votes led in all 26 of Switzerland's cantons.
To pass, the initiative had to secure a majority of both voters nationwide and Swiss cantons.
Read: Is NATO ready to fight? The Ukraine war is raising doubts among military analysts
he rejection reached over 70% in cantons such as the capital Bern and Zurich, as well as Basel Landschaft, Jura, Lucerne, Solothurn, Vaud, Neuchatel, and Zug, while results were closer in some, such as Ticino, where the opposition stood at 51.75%
Voter turnout for the referendum was at 47.06%.
The initiative sought to enshrine "perpetual and armed" neutrality in the Constitution and restrict Switzerland from cooperating with military alliances or imposing sanctions on warring states, except for UN sanctions and measures.
The Federal Council and parliament opposed the initiative, arguing that it would restrict Switzerland's maneuvering room in protecting its security, independence, and prosperity.
Supporters argued that constitutional safeguards were needed to protect the country's neutrality from external pressure and preserve its credibility as a mediator and provider of good offices.
Voters also decisively rejected a food initiative, with 72.52% voting against and 27.48% in favor.
The initiative sought to strengthen sustainable domestic production, promote more plant-based foods, and protect clean drinking water.

title: South Africa police hunt suspects after 27 killed in two separate shootings
description: Gunmen strike Lwandle venue  Wedela tavern hours apart with no arrests made yet
content:
Gunmen strike Lwandle venue, Wedela tavern hours apart with no arrests made yet
South African police were on Sunday hunting the perpetrators of two separate shootings that killed 27 people within hours of each other, in stark reminders of the country's problem with gun violence.
The motives for the shootings near Johannesburg and Cape Town were unknown, but gang violence and organised crime remain rife in South Africa, despite government efforts to curb one of the highest per-capita murder rates in the world.
Onlookers gathered behind police lines at the scene of the shooting in Lwandle, on the outskirts of Cape Town, where gunmen opened fire in a venue selling grilled meat around 2:00am on Sunday (12:00 GMT), killing 10 people and injuring 11 more.
Read: Three students killed in Philippine school shooting, including gunman, officials say
In Wedela township, about 80 kilometres (50 miles) from Johannesburg, 17 people were killed and 15 injured at a tavern when suspects armed with AK-47 rifles opened fire at around 9:30pm on Saturday, according to police.
Two burnt vehicles could be seen outside the tavern as authorities cordoned off the area on Sunday morning.
No arrests have been made yet and detectives are working to find the perpetrators, police said in statements.
"South Africa has a serious illegal firearms problem, and firearms are frequently used by organised criminal groups as well as in gang-related and other violent crimes," said crime expert Yusuf Abramjee.
Read More: Gunman fires inside Thai government office as country reels from school shooting
"Every mass shooting should therefore trigger more than an investigation into the immediate perpetrators," he told Reuters . "Authorities need to look at the wider networks behind the violence."
Crime is expected to be a major issue for voters in municipal elections in November, when the African National Congress is facing further erosion of voter support.
President Cyril Ramaphosa said earlier this year that organised crime had become the biggest threat to South Africa's democracy, and deployed the army to help police in some areas.
A shooting at a house party near Durban last week killed 11 people, while a series of women's bodies found near Johannesburg since July has renewed fear and anger over high rates of femicide.

title: Lahore police find vehicle  detain three suspects in alleged gang rape of Azerbaijani woman
description: DIG says those involved in the serious incident will face legal action without discrimination
content:
DIG says those involved in the serious incident will face legal action without discrimination
Police investigating a case of sexual assault on a foreign national woman on Sunday found a vehicle allegedly used in the incident and detained three people for questioning.
The development came as investigators continued efforts to arrest the assaulters in the case lodged by the 20-year-old woman from Azerbaijan.
Earlier in the day, Lahore Police identified suspects allegedly involved in the gang rape and launched efforts to arrest them, police said.
The woman, identified as Diana, had filed a complaint against three unidentified men, following which a case was registered at Defence C police station.
Lahore Investigation Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Syed Zeeshan Raza took immediate notice of the incident and formed special teams headed by Cantt Investigation Superintendent of Police (SP) Asim Iftikhar to arrest the suspects.
Police said the suspects had been identified and that all available resources were being used to apprehend them. DIG Raza said those involved in the serious incident would face legal action without discrimination.
He said all stages of the investigation would be completed on merit and in accordance with the law, adding that all possible aspects of the case were being examined to ensure the suspects were arrested soon.
“I am personally and continuously monitoring progress in the investigation,” Raza said. He also said the suspects would be arrested and dealt with according to the law.
According to the First Information Report (FIR), Diana had arrived in Lahore a few days before the alleged incident.
Read: Lahore police arrests 4 suspects for kidnapping, sexual assault of two foreign women
The report said two unidentified women had lured her to a cafe, where three male friends of the women were already present. After spending some time at the cafe, the group allegedly took Diana to a flat.
The FIR alleged that she was given a drink containing an intoxicating substance at the flat, after which three men allegedly gang-raped her.
The suspects allegedly sexually assaulted her throughout the night before leaving her near the airport and fleeing, according to the FIR. They also allegedly took an iPhone and another expensive mobile phone belonging to Diana, it said.
Police subsequently launched an investigation and began searching for the suspects.
They recovered a vehicle allegedly used in the incident and transferred it to Defence C police station. Investigators were using the vehicle as part of their efforts to trace the main suspects.
A team headed by SP Iftikhar conducted raids to arrest those allegedly involved, police said.
Read more: Four suspects in alleged Peshawar gang rape case killed in attack by unidentified gunmen
Diana underwent a medical examination following the alleged assault. Police said further facts were expected to emerge from the medical report.
This is the second such case registered in the Defence C area in the past months. In July, police rescued two foreign women - one Dutch and one Venezuelan - after receiving an emergency complaint, arrested four suspects, and launched an investigation into allegations of abduction and sexual assault.
The victim said that the women travelled to Pakistan after being invited by an acquaintance they had met in Singapore in October 2025. She added that on June 29, they were abducted by the acquaintance and four accomplices, who demanded money for their release. The complaint further contained allegations of repeated sexual assault, threats with weapons, physical abuse, and extortion.
Reports circulating on social media alleged that one of the suspects was related to an influential political figure.

title: Pakistan down Kazakhstan in volleyball opener
description: Green shirts beat Kazakhs 3 1 as the men s tournament gets under way in Nagoya
content:
Green-shirts beat Kazakhs 3-1 as the men's tournament gets under way in Nagoya
Pakistan on Sunday made a winning start to their men's volleyball competition in the 20th Asian Games, beating Kazakhstan 3-1 in their Pool A opener at the Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park Gymnasium.
Pakistan took the match 25-16, 25-22, 17-25, 25-20 in one hour and 26 minutes, overcoming a Kazakhstan fought back in the third set before folding the show in four sets.
Murad Khan was Pakistan's leading scorer with 21 points, including 17 successful spikes and four blocks. Usman Faryad Ali added 14 points, while Murad Jehan contributed 11.
Pakistan dominated the opening two sets, winning them 25-16 and 25-22, but Kazakhstan responded emphatically in the third, taking it 25-17 to extend the match.
Pakistan regained control in the fourth set and finished 25-20 to claim the victory.
Pakistan's attacking display was a treat to watch. They scored 55 points from spikes compared with Kazakhstan's 48 and converted 13 per cent of their 56 blocking attempts, while Kazakhstan recorded 23 per cent from 44 attempts.
“We should have won 3-0,” Pakistan team manager and former captain Naseer Ahmed told The Express Tribune from Nagoya.
“After taking two sets boys took it a bit easy and Kazakhs did well at that point by winning that set. I am hopeful we will also beat Uzbekistan and Japan,” Naseer said.
Pakistan will now face Uzbekistan on Monday and Japan on Tuesday.
As many as 16 teams are contesting in the event, which have been placed in four groups. Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Japan have been bracketed in Group A while Group B carries Iran, Kyrgyzstan, Indonesia and Thailand. Similarly, Group C contains Qatar, Hong Kong, India and Vietnam while Korea, Philippines, China and Chinese Taipei have been clubbed in Group D.
The top two teams from each pool will progress to the October 1 quarter-finals. The semi-finals will be conducted on October 2 with the final and bronze medal match to follow on October 3.

title: Promoter dispute threatens Fury Joshua blockbuster
description: The highly anticipated Cardiff clash faces uncertainty
content:
The highly anticipated Cardiff clash faces uncertainty
An angry Tyson Fury said Saturday his long-awaited 'Battle of Britain' bout with fellow former world heavyweight champion Anthony Joshua is at risk because of a row between rival promoters.
The much-anticipated clash was announced earlier this week, with Cardiff's Principality Stadium set to stage what could be the most lucrative fight in British boxing history on December 11.
After months of negotiations that threatened to scupper the fight as Fury called for a rematch with Oleksandr Usyk, Saudi Arabian boxing powerbroker Turki Alalshikh announced the venue and date for the bout on Thursday.
The event, which will be broadcast on Netflix, was confirmed as a collaboration between Alalshikh's The Ring and UFC president Dana White.
But Eddie Hearn, Joshua's promoter, has been in dispute with White and says the UFC chief's involvement represents a breach of contract.
Fury, however, believes this is simply an excuse for Joshua to withdraw.
"Anthony Joshua and Eddie Hearn are trying to pull out of this fight," said Fury in an expletive-filled Instagram post. "They're saying they're not going to fight now.
"It's mainly to do with Eddie Hearn's ego. He's making up a million different things and threatening 'we're not gonna fight, we're not gonna fight, we're not gonna fight'. He's cost us the biggest fight in boxing history. Clown... Eddie Hearn has cost us the biggest fight in boxing history."
Hearn has been feuding with UFC president White since the launch of Zuffa Boxing earlier this year.
Speaking to IFL TV, Hearn said White's involvement in the promotion of the Fury and Joshua fight "ain't happening".
"Dana White cannot be involved with this fight promotion. Netflix clearly didn't get the memo. No-one talks to each other," said Hearn.
More than a decade in the making, the bout between the former two-time world champions has been subjected to numerous false starts and spats between the rival camps.
The fight could reportedly take place in the early hours UK time in a bid to satisfy television audiences in the United States.
Fury, 38, defeated 46-year-old Mariusz Wach in Thailand in his most recent bout in July.
Joshua, 36, survived a pair of first-round knockdowns to beat the unheralded Kristian Prenga in his last fight two months ago.
Fury has won 36 of his 39 fights and held the WBC, WBO and IBF heavyweight belts during his colourful career.
The self-styled 'Gypsy King' was twice beaten by Usyk in world title bouts in 2024.
Joshua has 30 wins from 34 fights, holding the WBO and IBF titles at various stages before a pair of losses to Usyk in 2021 and 2022.

title: Ireland squad vote to play Israel tie
description: The match will go ahead in Hungary despite ongoing concerns over Gaza
content:
The match will go ahead in Hungary despite ongoing concerns over Gaza
Ireland's football team voted on Saturday to fulfil a Nations League tie with Israel despite goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu pulling out of the match due to unease over the war in Gaza.
"We carried out a vote amongst the squad to establish their sentiment on fulfilling the fixtures," Football Association of Ireland (FAI) head David Courell told reporters in Debrecen, Hungary, where the game will take place on Sunday.
"It was a significant majority that was returned with the intention to continue.
"Based on that, the association took the decision on behalf of Irish football, that this fixture would continue as we have always intended to fulfil the fixtures," he added.
Ireland are scheduled to play two Nations League ties against Israel, with the first -- officially Israel's home fixture - at the neutral venue in Hungary.
Ireland's designated home match on October 4 has been moved from Dublin's Aviva Stadium to Backa Topola, Serbia, following concerns over disruption and security.
"I have reached a decision that I have not taken lightly," Bolton's Bazunu said on Instagram.
"I feel it would be wrong to participate in the upcoming fixtures against Israel. My decision is based purely upon my personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong," the 24-year-old added.
Ireland has long been a strong supporter of the Palestinian cause, with sympathy often linked to the country's own history of British rule.
Dublin, alongside Spain and Norway, formally recognised a Palestinian state in 2024, and has repeatedly criticised Israel over the Gaza conflict.
Israel strongly rejects allegations its conduct in Gaza amounts to genocide.
"Football has won, the separation between football and politics must be maintained," said a statement by the Israeli FA later Saturday hailing the Irish decision.
"The ones who have certainly lost today are those who wanted to intimidate, to separate and to turn the football pitch into a political arena," it added.
Since Ireland were drawn in the same Nations League group as Israel, prominent Irish figures including sportspeople, fan groups and pro-Palestinian campaigners have protested against the ties going ahead.
Bazunu's decision triggered the delay of a scheduled press conference on Saturday, followed by a vote among the squad on whether to fulfil the fixture or not.
"Nobody is comfortable playing these games for many reasons," said Ireland's Icelandic manager Heimir Hallgrimsson.
"We are trying to tackle it in the best way we can at the moment," he added.
Ireland players will not fulfil any media duties tomorrow, or against Austria in Dublin on October 1, or around the game against Israel in Serbia three days later, said Courell.
The players will wear black armbands "for all lives lost in the conflict" during Sunday's match, with profits from the Austria game to be donated to charity, he said.
Sunday's match comes days after national broadcaster RTE confirmed Ireland would again boycott the Eurovision Song Contest next year because of Israel's participation.
In a rare move for a state broadcaster, RTE said earlier it will show the Israel game without Irish commentary or pundits.

Ben Affleck has revealed that his children are quick to question his relationship advice, with the actor admitting his past marriages have made him an easy target at the dinner table.

Affleck shares Violet, 20, Fin, 17, and Samuel, 14, with ex-wife Jennifer Garner. The pair married in 2005 and divorced in 2018.

title: Germany selects Munich for Olympics host bid
description: The Bavarian capital beat the Cologne Rhine Ruhr region in the national selection process
content:
The Bavarian capital beat the Cologne/Rhine-Ruhr region in the national selection process
Munich was on Saturday selected ahead of the Cologne/Rhine-Ruhr region by the German Olympic Committee (DOSB) as part of a bid to host the 2036, 2040 or 2044 Summer Games.
The decision was announced by German president Frank-Walter Steinmeier in the south-western spa town of Baden-Baden.
Launched as a race between four candidates, the DOSB was given a choice between two after Berlin withdrew on Thursday after Hamburg pulled out in May.
"We're thinking about all of Germany," Bavarian state premier Markus Soeder said on stage after the announcement of Munich's successful bid.
"The Cologne bid made things really tough for us and pretty tense until the end.
"I want that we work jointly to bring the games to Germany. It is a chance at something historic and we want to give everything to present ourselves as a united country -- from north to south and from east to west.
"That's our goal and what we're working towards. Thank you for the trust."
The Munich bid centres on the Olympic Park in the north of the city. Built for the 1972 Games, it has undergone extensive renovations in recent years.
In a statement issued moments after the announcement, German chancellor Friedrich Merz congratulated Munich.
"Germany has an Olympic candidate. Munich will enter the race on our behalf, and I warmly congratulate the state capital and the Free State of Bavaria on this," he said.
"Now, together with our Olympic candidate, we eagerly look forward to this major event... Germany is ready for the Olympics."
In order to shore up support for the bid, Munich held a referendum in the autumn of 2025. Almost two-thirds (66.4 percent) of voters cast their ballot in support of hosting the games, on a turnout of 44 percent.
The positive result was a stark contrast to previous Olympic referenda, with votes to host the 2022 Winter Games in Munich or the 2024 Summer Games in Hamburg failing to win support.
Hamburg's hopes were undermined by a negative public consultation while another hopeful, Berlin, decided against holding a referendum.
The DOSB is set to begin a "continuous dialogue" with the IOC ahead of a shortlisting process in March 2027.
The IOC will designate one or more preferred hosts in late 2028, with an eventual bid to be selected by the IOC in mid 2029.
The Bavarian capital has become accustomed to hosting major sporting events in recent years.
In the 10 days leading up to the DOSB's decision, Munich was chosen as the host of the 2028 Champions League final -- having done so in 2012 and 2025 -- along with the 2031 World Athletics Championships.
Munich's Allianz Arena was selected to host the first regular-season NFL match on German soil in 2022 and will do so for a third time in November.
Since the last time the Summer Games were on German soil in 1972, Germany has launched seven unsuccessful bids to play host.
If Munich is chosen by the IOC, it will be the third time Germany has hosted the Olympics. Berlin held the Games in 1936 with Germany then under Nazi leadership, while Munich welcomed the 1972 Games, then as part of West Germany.
The 1972 edition in Munich was marred by the attack on the Israeli delegation in the Olympic Village, which resulted in the deaths of 11 members of the Israeli Olympic team.
The only other Games held on German soil were the 1936 Winter Olympics, held in the southern town of Garmisch-Partenkirchen.

title: Russell seals eighth F1 win in Baku
description: The Mercedes driver finishes 0 196 seconds ahead of Verstappen
content:
The Mercedes driver finishes 0.196 seconds ahead of Verstappen
George Russell resisted a late charge from Max Verstappen to claim his first lights-to-flag victory with a composed drive for Mercedes in Saturday's thrilling Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
The 28-year-old Briton came home just 0.196 seconds ahead of the four-time champion with his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar third on his return after a broken wrist in a race punctuated by two safety cars.
It was Russell's first win on the fast, challenging streets of Baku, his first since the Austrian Grand Prix in June,and the eighth of his career. It trimmed team-mate Kimi Antonelli's lead in the drivers' championship to 66 points.
Antonelli finished fifth behind Ferrari's Charles Leclerc after slicing through the field from 16th on the grid. Seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton was sixth in the second Ferrari.
"It's amazing to be back on the top step so I want to say a big thank you to the team for helping me through a tough moment," said Russell.
"The first half of the race felt pretty plain sailing, getting the gap, but after the safety car I saw Max behind me and I knew it wasn't going to be easy.
"When the yellow flag came out, I lifted off the power and when I came back I had no turbo and Max nearly got me on the line."
"We had a good race," he said. "In the final lap, George lost a bit of boost so that's why I caught up quite a bit. It got close, but it wasn't enough."
"It's been a very long six weeks since I injured myself, but it felt like the right moment to come back. I felt strong and this is my first proper podium finish on pure pace so I am delighted."
Racing Bulls' rookie Arvid Lindblad was seventh, Esteban Ocon eighth ahead of his Haas team-mate Oliver Bearman and Williams' Carlos Sainz.
Russell made a near-perfect start from his 12th pole position to draw clear while, behind him, Oscar Piastri took advantage of a slow-starting Leclerc to take second. Antonelli dropped from 16th to 17th.
Verstappen also enjoyed the opening lap and passed both Alpines before powering past Hamilton, Norris, Leclerc and finally team-mate Hadjar to rise to third.
The Dutchman was grumbling about his tyres, but Russell on the same medium compound was already five seconds ahead of Piastri on softs.
By mid-distance, Russell led by 10 seconds, but grazed the wall at Turn 15.
Team-mate Antonelli was up to ninth as the Red Bulls scrapped for third, making life easy for Piastri in second.
The processional action ended on lap 30 when Williams' Alex Albon crashed at Turn Five, triggering a Safety Car deployment during which the leaders all pitted.
After five laps, the race resumed with the Dutchman passing Piastri at Turn One .
Behind him Franco Colapinto lunged up the inside but ran out of space entering the next corner. He locked up and went sideways pushing Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly into Lando Norris in a McLaren. The three went off the track in a synchronised slide.
Both drivers for the struggling French team were in position for top-10 finishes.
"Oh my God! Oh my God! I don't believe it," said Gasly on team radio adding a swear word. "So many points gone."
A second safety car came out for three laps. After the restart Piastri locked-up,dropping to 14th and gifting Hadjar third.
Antonelli passed Hamilton with 10 laps to go to take fifth.

title: Smells like teen spirit as US thrash Peru
description: Ellis and Hall mark their debuts with goals in the 4 1 victory
content:
Ellis and Hall mark their debuts with goals in the 4-1 victory
Teenage debutants Justin Ellis and Julian Hall both scored as a youthful United States team defeated Peru 4-1 in a friendly international at Orlando on Saturday.
Ellis was one of three teenagers named in United States coach Mauricio Pochettino's starting line-up for his team's first game since the World Cup.
Philadelphia Union's 16-year-old prodigy Cavan Sullivan and New England Revolution's 18-year-old Peyton Miller both started alongside 19-year-old Orlando City striker Ellis in a team showing seven changes to the side beaten 4-1 by Belgium in the World Cup's last 16 in July.
The infusion of youth was quick to make its mark, with Ellis glancing in an inviting free-kick from Gio Reyna after just four minutes in a dream start at his home stadium.
"I've probably been dreaming about this day, like, 500 or 1,000 times in my life since I was five years old," Ellis said afterwards. "I can't even describe. It's just crazy."
Peru got back on level terms after just 15 minutes when veteran striker Gianluca Lapadula cleverly headed home a Yoshimar Yotun cross.
The United States regained the lead in the second half when another teenager –- the 17-year-old substitute Mathis Albert –- burst clear down the left and was knocked to the ground by Jesus Pretell.
Despite the foul beginning just outside the area, Jamaican referee Steffon Dewar pointed to the spot and Malik Tillman stepped up to fire home the penalty for 2-1.
It got better for Pochettino's side on 72 minutes when 18-year-old substitute Hall bundled in a Sebastian Berhalter cross to make it 3-1.
Berhalter then completed the scoring with a thunderous effort from just outside the area in the dying minutes to put the seal on an impressive display for the hosts.

title: Gisele B  ndchen reportedly ended marriage with Tom Brady with three words about compatibility
description: Lars Anderson details the breakdown of Brady and B  ndchen   s 13 year marriage in a new book
content:
Lars Anderson details the breakdown of Brady and Bündchen’s 13-year marriage in a new book
Gisele Bündchen reportedly told Tom Brady they were “not compatible” before their 2022 divorce, according to a forthcoming book about the retired NFL star.
Author Lars Anderson details the breakdown of Brady and Bündchen’s 13-year marriage in Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness , which was obtained by Daily Mail.
“One day, Gisele, who is really into astrology, basically looked into the stars and told Tom, ‘We’re not compatible,’” the source told Anderson. “And just like that, she was done.”
According to the book, Bündchen had reportedly encouraged Brady to retire for years, including after the New England Patriots’ 2017 Super Bowl victory.
Per Anderson, she allegedly asked, “Would now be the perfect time to retire?” Brady reportedly replied, “Too bad, babe. I’m having too much fun right now.”
The book also describes tensions surrounding Brady’s decision to return to the NFL after announcing his retirement in February 2022.
He later wrote on X, “I’ve realized my place is still on the field and not in the stands. That time will come. But it’s not now.”
Anderson cites former teammates and coaches describing Brady as distracted after his return to training camp, while Bündchen reportedly left for Costa Rica.
Brady and Bündchen announced their divorce on October 28, 2022.
Bündchen said at the time, “We have grown apart and while it is, of course, difficult to go through something like this, I feel blessed for the time we had together and only wish the best for Tom always.”
The former couple share two children, Benjamin and Vivian.
Bündchen has since remarried Joaquim Valente.

title: Taylor Swift   s  Showgirl  Encore  becomes second worst rated pop album of the decade on Metacritic
description: The score for the new release is reportedly comparable  to Katy Perry   s  143   which received 35 on Metacritic in 2024
content:
The score for the new release is reportedly comparable to Katy Perry’s '143', which received 35 on Metacritic in 2024
Taylor Swift’s The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore is currently rated 43 on Metacritic, making it the second-worst-reviewed album by a pop star this decade, according to TV Fandom Lounge.
Released on September 25, the album features four new tracks including "Babylon", “Patient Zero”, “Cleveland!” and “Pink Clouding”.
The score for the new release is reportedly comparable to Katy Perry’s 143 , which received 35 on Metacritic in 2024.
Critics from several outlets also questioned Swift’s latest songs and their creative direction.
The Telegraph review described the release bluntly, “I’m a Swiftie, and even I think these new songs are terrible. The Life of a Showgirl: Encore Edition is just as derivative and flat as the original album.”
The reviewer added, “She no longer has the incentive to take creative risks. No producer or record label boss would dare offer a critical opinion. It’s a crying shame. Modern pop’s greatest voice risks rubbishing her own legacy because she’s scared to take a day off.”
The Guardian, meanwhile, criticised Swift’s recurring focus on her critics, writing, “For all that she laments the haters, she sure does write a lot of songs about them.”
The Independent also criticised “Cleveland”, calling it “some of her worst writing”.
Consequence offered another assessment, describing Swift as a “predictable, bordering-on-bland caricature” and arguing that the songs lack a distinct identity.
Despite the critical response, Swift’s previous Showgirl release achieved 4.002 million album-equivalent units in its first week, highlighting the continued strength of her commercial reach.

content:
Dimoldenberg also joked about her 'Chicken Shop Date' interviews and the lessons behind her career in the monologue
Amelia Dimoldenberg used her SNL UK opening monologue to joke about Ed Sheeran, her Chicken Shop Date interviews and the lessons behind her career.
Dimoldenberg recently announced that Chicken Shop Date would be ending. Addressing the decision, she joked, “I found out something devastating. Apparently, these celebrities weren’t coming on to date me. They were coming on to promote their work!”
She then referenced Andrew Garfield, saying, “It makes so much more sense now. Andrew Garfield had a film out! When he kept saying, ‘I’m looking forward to the big release,’ I thought that was a sex thing.”
The monologue then turned to Sheeran, who has faced controversy after dropping Macklemore from his tour following a political speech in which Macklemore said “free Palestine”.
“I’m incredibly privileged to have done so many interviews with people like Idris Elba, Cher, and even a world famous red-headed puppet with a hand up his arse telling him what to say,” Dimoldenberg said, as an image of Elmo appeared.
“No, the other one!” she added as Sheeran’s face appeared on screen.
Dimoldenberg also reflected on her early experiences at a youth centre in London, saying, “I am an awkward girl, and there’s no shame in that. Just huge profit.”
She continued, “I am proof that you don’t have to stop being awkward to be successful … I am proof that you should always be yourself.”
She encouraged viewers to embrace that approach across Chicken Shop Date , the Oscars red carpet, The Devil Wears Prada 2 , her upcoming rom-com and SNL UK.
“Just like the chickens I love to eat,” Dimoldenberg concluded, “you don’t have to have range.”

title: PTI delays long march as political strategy
description: PTI delays long march as political strategy
content:
Shaukat Yousafzai says federal authorities planned violence, urges talks instead of force
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf provincial spokesman Shaukat Yousafzai has described the party's decision to postpone its long march to Islamabad as a calculated political strategy aimed at compelling the federal government to yield.
Speaking to the media outside the Peshawar High Court, he insisted that the move was not a retreat but a deliberate shift to keep the pressure on while remaining committed to peaceful struggle.
Yousafzai alleged that the federal government had prepared a plan to cause casualties during any protest and that PTI had therefore changed its approach. "The government claims the public will not come out onto the streets. Then why have 65,000 police personnel and thousands of containers been deployed?" he asked. He maintained that PTI continues to believe in peaceful political struggle and that its demands remain legitimate and constitutional.
The spokesman urged the government to abandon arrogance, stubbornness and the intoxication of power. While federal leaders speak of negotiations on television channels, he said, they show no serious intent on the ground. "If the government truly wants practical talks, we are ready," Yousafzai stated. He pointed to Barrister Gohar's clear formula that the solution to the country's current problems lies in negotiations and political dialogue, adding that the government must move in that direction.
Yousafzai accused the centre of pursuing a policy of exhausting and eliminating PTI through heavy deployments of police and containers. He reiterated the party's demand that the founder of PTI be provided medical treatment facilities in accordance with Supreme Court orders. The spokesman also stressed PTI's commitment to ensuring the independence of the judiciary and the implementation of court decisions.
Turning to federal-provincial relations, Yousafzai said that after the 18th Amendment, the centre has no authority to interfere in provincial matters, yet provincial ministers continue to face arrests. He accused the federal government of imposing jungle law. He strongly condemned Federal Information Minister Attaullah Tarar's recent remarks about the K-P chief minister. Referring to earlier comments by Maryam Nawaz about feeling threatened by the provinces, he warned that such narratives weaken rather than strengthen the state.
On the police legislation controversy, Yousafzai asserted that the Police Act falls squarely within provincial jurisdiction. He expressed regret that a federal minister had claimed the province could not legislate on the subject. "The provincial government has the authority to legislate in the public interest, and whatever law serves the people of the province will be enacted," he said. He challenged critics to identify any clause in the K-P Police Act that does not exist in the police laws of Punjab or Sindh, and to explain what exactly is objectionable in the provincial legislation.
Yousafzai noted that the Inspector General of Police had been summoned by the provincial assembly speaker but failed to appear. He said the purpose of the legislation was to free the police from political and administrative pressure so that it could function independently.

title: Speaker defends parliamentary privileges

Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, reacting to a statement by the federal interior minister, said parliamentary privileges of legislators were not a new invention but an established part of parliamentary traditions.
He said the privilege requiring the speaker's permission before the arrest of a provincial assembly member was meant to protect the independence of the legislature and elected representatives, and did not place lawmakers above the law.
"An accused member remains subject to investigation, legal proceedings and the judicial process," the speaker said, adding that the speaker's role was to ensure that arrests were not used as a tool of political victimisation.
He said police should not be used to intimidate or silence elected representatives. "When the government legislates for itself, it is considered legitimate, but when the assembly does so, questions are raised," he remarked.
Swati said the relevant law had been passed with the consensus of both treasury and opposition parties.

title: 13 held hostage by terrorists in Hathi Khel
description: 13 held hostage by terrorists in Hathi Khel
content:
Residents abandon homes amid standoff between peace committee, police and TTP
Local residents have begun abandoning the mountainous Hathi Khel area of Wazir subdivision in Bannu as tensions escalate between a local peace committee, police and terrorists, with sources confirming on Saturday that 13 people were allegedly seized as hostages while trying to reach safer ground.
According to local sources, the group was intercepted as they transported household belongings in vehicles out of the area. The militants stopped the convoy and took the travellers captive, sources said. Those identified so far include Rehmanullah, Farmanullah, Laiq and Sadiq, sons of Shahabuddin; Mir Ali, son of Hazrat Ali; Muhammad Raziq; Azim Khan, son of Hamblis Khan; and Sameen, Hamidullah and Rakhidullah, sons of Shereen Gul. Three others remain unidentified.
Police have issued no official statement on the incident. Responsible police sources, however, privately confirmed that the reported hostage-taking had occurred.
A photograph purporting to show the captives has circulated widely on social media. The image also appears to include Nasir alias Gidarh, a local commander of the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). Neither the photograph nor the identities of those depicted in it could be independently verified.
Sources said the militants were actively trying to prevent residents from leaving Hathi Khel and had imposed specific conditions on families seeking to relocate. Some households that failed to meet those conditions allegedly had their houses demolished. These claims have not been officially confirmed by authorities.
The broader security situation in Hathi Khel and the surrounding mountainous terrain has grown increasingly difficult for civilians. Several families have already moved to safer locations in recent days, citing fear of further violence and restrictions on movement. Residents describe a climate of uncertainty in which ordinary travel and the simple act of packing up a household can expose people to risk.
Local accounts suggest the standoff involves competing claims of control and enforcement between the peace committee, security forces and armed militants. The presence of a known TTP figure in the circulating image has heightened concern among those still in the area. Yet without an official police briefing or independent confirmation, many details remain provisional.
For now, the exodus continues. Families load what belongings they can into vehicles and attempt to leave under conditions that sources describe as fraught. Those who remain face the dual pressures of insecurity and the militants' reported efforts to keep residents in place. The 13 alleged hostages stand as the most concrete illustration yet of the human cost of the present tensions.
As of Saturday evening, no further information had emerged on the condition or whereabouts of the captives. Appeals for an official clarification from police and other authorities have so far gone unanswered. Residents and local observers continue to monitor developments closely, aware that any misstep in the fragile environment of Hathi Khel can quickly escalate.

content:
Trains departing Peshawar for Rawalpindi, Attock, Nowshera, Jahangira and Taxila are leaving fully loaded
The closure of major land routes for the Islamabad Long March has triggered a severe shortage of railway tickets on the Peshawar - Rawalpindi corridor, with tickets now being sold on the black market and trains packed far beyond capacity.
Tickets for popular services including the Jaffer Express, Awami Express, Khyber Mail and Rehman Baba Express have become virtually impossible to obtain for Rawalpindi. As a result, large numbers of citizens have turned to railway stations as their only viable alternative.
Trains departing Peshawar for Rawalpindi, Attock, Nowshera, Jahangira and Taxila are leaving fully loaded. The reverse flow is equally heavy, with passengers travelling from Rawalpindi to Peshawar also filling every available space. Many travellers are forced to stand throughout the journey because of the intense overcrowding.
Train schedules have also been disrupted. Services are arriving in Peshawar between one and three hours late, compounding the hardship for passengers already struggling with limited seating and long waits.

title: Safdar steps up campaign against pro govt lawyers group
description: Safdar steps up campaign against pro govt lawyers group
content:
CM's husband questions credentials of Amjad Shah, Ahsan Bhoon; files complaints with JCP and NCCIA
With the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) election approaching, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz's husband Capt (retd) Muhammad Safdar has intensified his campaign against the government-backed Independent Group, raising questions over the professional credentials of its presidential candidate Syed Amjad Shah and prominent leader Ahsan Bhoon.
The PML-N Lawyers Forum has already announced its support for the Independent Group in the upcoming SCBA election. Safdar, however, has publicly questioned Shah's law degree and has now also challenged the educational and professional credentials of Bhoon, who is a member of the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP).
Safdar has submitted a complaint to the JCP secretary seeking an inquiry into Bhoon's "educational certificate, enrollment and professional credentials".
In his complaint, Safdar alleged that information had come to his knowledge raising questions about the authenticity of the law degree on the basis of which Bhoon entered the legal profession. He said the degree could allegedly be "fake, bogus or otherwise incapable of lawful verification".
Safdar urged the commission to call for and independently verify the original record, arguing that the matter could not be ignored because Bhoon was a sitting member of the JCP.
"The Commission considers the persons who may ultimately sit in judgment over the rights, liberties, property, and disputes of the people of Pakistan," Safdar said in his complaint.
He maintained that membership of the JCP was not merely ceremonial and that every member participated in the discharge of sensitive constitutional functions. He said the alleged issue concerning Bhoon's qualifications therefore required authoritative verification.
Safdar further pointed out Bhoon's prominent role in the organised Bar and his association with the Independent Group, commonly known as the Asma Jahangir Group.
He argued that Bhoon's prominence within the legal fraternity made institutional scrutiny necessary if questions had arisen regarding the foundation of his professional status. Bhoon, meanwhile, has announced that he will file a defamation case against Safdar over the allegations concerning his law degree.
"Captain Safdar must be taken to task," Bhoon told media persons.
The campaign has generated debate within legal circles over Safdar's repeated targeting of Amjad Shah and Bhoon and whether his campaign is being conducted independently or has the backing of the PML-N leadership.
Members of the Independent Group maintain that Safdar has no backing from the PML-N, particularly the Sharif family, for his campaign against Amjad Shah and Bhoon. One senior member of the group claimed that the Sharif family was embarrassed by the situation.
Safdar and Amjad Shah both belong to Hazara division and, according to lawyers familiar with the matter, their relationship has remained tense for around five years.
With the Independent Group fielding Amjad Shah as its candidate for SCBA president, Safdar has announced support for Professional Lawyers Group candidate Sardar Amaan, who also belongs to Hazara division.
The dispute has acquired a broader political dimension because of the Independent Group's relationship with the present government and its position on constitutional and political issues.
Bhoon is known for his association with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, while the Independent Group has backed the campaign for the creation of new provinces.
A section within the PML-N that opposes the division of Punjab is also concerned that an Independent Group victory in the SCBA election could result in stronger support for what its members describe as a "reforms agenda of powerful circles".
Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and Bhoon have also played prominent roles in mobilising Bar support for the present government, according to lawyers familiar with the political dynamics within the legal community.
Bhoon had also approached the Supreme Court after then-prime minister Imran Khan dissolved the National Assembly following then-deputy speaker Qasim Suri's ruling. The proceedings concerned completion of the no-confidence process against Khan under Article 95 of the Constitution.
The Independent Group also endorsed the February 8 elections, while the government subsequently secured support from the group's associated lawyers for two constitutional amendments.
Safdar has separately accused the superior courts of conducting "done-based" cases.
Meanwhile, in Lahore, Safdar has approached the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), seeking an inquiry against lawyer Mian Daud over what he described as abusive, defamatory and reputation-harming material allegedly published against him on social media.
In a complaint submitted to the NCCIA director general, Safdar alleged that Daud published a video concerning him on X and Facebook on September 23 at around 5:18pm. He claimed the video had attracted approximately half a million views by the time the complaint was filed.
Safdar said that earlier the same day, during a press interaction, he had raised questions about the authenticity of Bhoon's law degree.

Police subsequently registered a case on her complaint and launched an investigation.

title: Power bill hike riles citizens
description: Power bill hike riles citizens
content:
Rising petrol expenses adding to financial pressure on households
Consumers of the Lahore Electric Supply Company (LESCO) have complained of sharp increases in their electricity bills, with some saying their dues have doubled compared with the previous month.
Several consumers said they had received bills significantly higher than those paid in the preceding month despite no significant increase in their electricity consumption. They questioned the basis for the increases and said the higher bills had placed an additional financial burden on already stretched household budgets.
One consumer, Muhammad Irshad, said he had paid around Rs18,000 for electricity in the previous month, but the latest bill amounted to Rs36,354. "I paid Rs18,000 last month, but this month I have received a bill of over Rs36,000. I cannot understand how the amount has doubled," he said.
Another consumer, Rafiq Qureshi, said, "I live in a one-room portion, yet LESCO has sent me a bill of Rs10,000. It is extremely difficult for an ordinary consumer to pay such a high bill."
Consumers also raised concerns over disconnection notices appearing on their electricity bills.
They said many bills carried a prominent warning that consumers must clear their dues before the due date or face disconnection of their electricity supply.
"The disconnection notice is printed on the bill and consumers are warned that their connection will be removed if they fail to pay by the due date," a consumer said.
The complaints come amid broader concerns over the rising cost of living, with consumers also pointing to the high cost of petrol as another factor making it increasingly difficult for households to manage their monthly expenses.
Citizens argue that higher petroleum prices have a direct impact on household budgets as well as the cost of transportation and other daily expenses.
They questioned the government's policy of passing on increases in international crude oil prices to domestic consumers.
The government has maintained that changes in petroleum prices reflect the impact of fluctuations in crude oil prices in the international market. The consumers, however, argue that the burden could be reduced if the government lowered what they describe as an unjustifiably high Petroleum Development Levy (PDL) on products.
They say the government should consider reducing the levy instead of passing the full burden of higher international oil prices on to consumers, particularly when households are already struggling with high electricity bills and other expenses.
The consumers also demanded greater transparency in the electricity billing process and urged LESCO to review bills where charges appeared disproportionately high compared with previous months.

Advocate Abdul Qayyum Qadri said they were shop owners and wanted to be made parties to the case. The court observed that they were neither complainants nor witnesses and asked whether they had recorded statements under Section 164 of the Criminal Procedure Code.

The shop owners' counsel said the investigation had not yet been completed and the charge sheet had not been approved. He said they wanted to join the investigation as complainants or witnesses.
Defence counsel Mahmood Hussain argued that the petition had been filed on behalf of only three shopkeepers and suggested that they either file a recovery suit or approach the committee responsible for providing financial assistance.
Investigating officer DSP Amir Warak said the shop owners had neither contacted him nor recorded statements. He said he had recorded statements from five people associated with Gul Plaza.
The shop owners' counsel alleged that the funds distributed as compensation had been misappropriated on a large scale.
The court reserved its decision on the maintainability of the petition and adjourned the hearing until October 2.

title: AI  social media drive self medication trend
description: AI  social media drive self medication trend
content:
Youths increasingly consult AI before doctors; students use antibiotics sans medical advice
A headache, sore throat, acne flare-up or sleepless night no longer always prompts young Pakistanis to consult a doctor. Increasingly, many turn to AI chatbots, social media platforms or search engines for quick answers, compare symptoms online and visit pharmacies for medicines.
Although AI tools repeatedly caution users that they cannot replace medical professionals, health experts say many people ignore such warnings and use digital information as a substitute for proper diagnosis.
As artificial intelligence, TikTok, Instagram and Google become increasingly common sources of health advice, Dr Khalid Islam, former Medical Superintendent of Benazir Bhutto General Hospital (BBGH) said Pakistan's Generation Z was increasingly treating symptoms rather than seeking medical evaluation.
"Easy access to medicines, rising healthcare costs and the influence of online personalities have contributed to a growing culture of self-medication," he said.
For many young people, online reviews, influencer recommendations and advice from friends appear to offer quick and affordable solutions. However, medical professionals caution that unsupervised use of medicines can cause serious consequences, including antibiotic resistance, harmful drug interactions, delayed diagnosis and complications arising from inappropriate treatment.
A case from Rawalpindi highlights these risks. Dua, 28, began using Slim Fast Drops for weight loss while taking antibiotics for a throat infection. Weeks later, she developed severe liver pain and was diagnosed with hepatitis A. Doctors said such cases demonstrated the dangers of combining medicines and supplements without professional guidance.
Dermatologist Dr Nida Rizwan said social media had significantly influenced how young people selected skincare products. Many users purchase creams, serums and medicated products after watching online reviews without understanding their own skin conditions or the risks associated with such products.
She said products suitable for one person could damage another's skin by weakening the skin barrier, worsening acne, causing irritation or triggering other complications. She advised people to consult qualified dermatologists before using medicated skincare products rather than following online trends.
The problem extends beyond skincare. Health experts are also concerned about the growing number of unqualified individuals on TikTok, Facebook and other platforms who present themselves as health experts, traditional healers or Hakeems despite lacking recognised medical qualifications.
Through dramatic before-and-after videos, sponsored promotions and exaggerated claims, such individuals often market herbal remedies, weight-loss products and cosmetic treatments as quick solutions. Pharmacists say they are witnessing the impact directly.

The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA), which received more than Rs900 million in departmental charges as the executing agency for the Metro Bus project, has not been paid departmental charges for the Rawalpindi Ring Road project and will also have to face audit objections on the completed Metro Bus project.

However, the provision for payment of the charges was later removed from the PC-I.
As a result, the RDA was deprived of its entitlement to two per cent departmental charges on completion of the Rawalpindi Ring Road project.

title: Cops flag poor facilities ahead of long march
description: Cops flag poor facilities ahead of long march
content:
Complain of inadequate toilets, water and stale food while seniors stay in luxury
Around 32,000 police personnel brought from distant districts of northern Punjab and deployed at different points in Attock district to stop the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) long march are reportedly facing a shortage of facilities, severe lack of washrooms, inadequate drinking water and poor-quality food.
Meanwhile, reports suggest that higher ranking officials deployed ahead of the march have been accommodated at the well-equipped properties of high-profile traders and political leaders.
Regular police personnel deployed on site have reportedly suffered from cold, flu, cough, dysentery, diarrhoea, fever and sore throats due to the weather and lack of facilities.
Constable Zulfiqar, who had come from Dera Ghazi Khan, died of a heart attack, while Constable Zain Bosan, a resident of Mandi Bahauddin, drowned in the Ghazi Barotha canal after slipping.
The police personnel have been accommodated in government schools and dispensaries, where they are forced to sleep on the floor with blankets. At one school accommodating nearly 1,000 personnel, there is reportedly only one washroom.
The severe shortage of washrooms has caused distress among police personnel. In the absence of washrooms, a large number of personnel use bushes and fields beneath the Attock River bridge, which, according to them, is worsening their problems.
The contract for providing meals and breakfast to the police has reportedly been awarded to a person named Sheikh Ajmal. Police personnel said breakfast, tea and curry were often served stale.
They said food cooked at night was packed in small plastic containers and distributed in the afternoon, by which time it had become stale.
"Since we came to Attock for duty, fresh tea, food and breakfast have become a dream," they said.
They said 200 police personnel at a time had to wait for hours outside a single washroom. Due to the change in weather, every fifth or sixth police official was reportedly suffering from cold, flu, cough or fever. They also said there were not enough medical teams to examine them.
At night, personnel are made to sleep on school floors with one blanket underneath and another on top. Space has been provided in school corridors, while some personnel have converted school benches into makeshift beds. They said their duties were also very demanding.
With the postponement of the march, their deployment period has also been extended.
The Punjab Inspector General of Police visited Attock to assess the situation and encourage the personnel. RPOs and DPOs have been directed to make daily visits.
Personnel from Dera Ghazi Khan, Multan and Khanewal, including Irfan, Faisal, Nauman and Qaiser Malik, said they had come after being told they would receive an additional salary and serve for two or three days, but their duty had now been extended.
"We have no problem with duty, nor are we afraid or going to abandon it. Stopping the workers by using force is our duty, but we should at least be provided facilities," they said.
They said washrooms were a basic human necessity and had become a serious problem. "Everyone has started using open spaces. There is no water for bathing or ablution, and even prayers are being missed," they said.
They described the sleeping arrangements and food as difficult to tolerate but said the shortage of washrooms and water was unbearable.
They said they spoke to their families daily and their parents had started telling them to return if facilities were not available.
They appealed to the Punjab IG, Rawalpindi RPO and Attock DPO to arrange sufficient washrooms and drinking water as well as water for bathing and ablution, saying, "We will handle the long march."
Meanwhile around 250 senior-ranking officers have reportedly been divided into groups of 10 to 20 and accommodated, allegedly through use of pressure tactics and requests, at the residences, guest houses, agricultural farms and offices of prominent traders, political leaders and affluent individuals in Attock.
The officers have reportedly been provided with luxury accommodation in air-conditioned rooms, along with meals, tea and breakfast, with these individuals hosting them until the long-march issue is resolved.
A prominent businessman in Attock told The Express Tribune that 16 police officers were staying at his residence and agricultural farm under his supervision and with facilities provided by him.

description: Xi s visit boosts strategic stability in China US ties  says FM
content:
Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to the United States has led to new progress in a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said after Xi wrapped up his US visit on Friday.
Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks while briefing reporters on Xi's state visit to the US from Sept. 23 to 25.
President Xi and President Donald Trump had a candid and in-depth exchange of views in a friendly atmosphere of mutual respect on strategic and overarching issues concerning China-US relations and the broader global landscape, Wang said.
Since President Trump began his second term, the two heads of state have maintained close exchanges, including three in-person meetings and five phone talks, and fostered a pattern of interaction marked by mutual respect and sincerity, said Wang, noting this has become the most valuable strategic asset in China-US relations.
An important political outcome of the visit is that President Xi and President Trump further enriched the substance of the new positioning of relations and have agreed to build a constructive China-US ties of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity, Wang said.
Respect means respecting each other's sovereignty and territorial integrity, respecting each country's choice of social system and development path, and respecting the other side's core interests and major concerns, Wang said.
Fairness, Wang continued, means pursuing mutually beneficial cooperation and handling differences through consultation, rejecting a zero-sum game in which one side's gain comes at the expense of the other's, and not seeking unilateral absolute advantage.
Reciprocity means that the two countries are equal in sovereignty, that neither side stands above the other, that neither engages in hegemonic nor bullying behaviour, that each side's concerns are addressed on an equal basis, and that cooperation across various fields develops in a balanced manner, Wang said.
Noting that President Xi has pointed out that a stable China-US economic and trade relationship requires both expanding the list of cooperation and shortening the list of problems, Wang said that the US side should treat Chinese companies fairly, resolve problems through dialogue and negotiations, and promote the sustained, stable and positive development of economic and trade relations.
The fentanyl abuse problem in the United States is not caused by China, but China has always acted with the utmost goodwill and made every effort to assist the US side in addressing the fentanyl crisis, Wang noted, adding that the two heads of state tasked the law enforcement agencies of the two countries with continuing to strengthen cooperation and jointly combat transnational crime. The government of Maharashtra, a huge western state whose capital Mumbai is India's financial and commercial centre, said drought was present across 74 percent of the territory. AFP
