title: Deluge triggers Bangkok  disaster
description: Deluge triggers Bangkok  disaster
content:
Roads waterlogged; residents wade through waist-deep water
Bangkok authorities declared a flood disaster across the Thai capital on Saturday after almost 48 hours of heavy rain left homes, shops and roads waterlogged and residents wading through waist-deep water.
Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul cut short a trip to London to return home after more than 300 millimetres (11.8 inches) of rain fell in some areas between Thursday afternoon and Saturday morning, according to officials.
"The water keeps coming in. It's hard to go out now. It's like at my waist level now," said Somkid Pheuk-ngam, 67, a vendor who lives near a canal just north of central Bangkok.
"I cannot go anywhere. I have been closing my shop for two days now," she told AFP.
Bangkok is no stranger to wet weather, and September is the peak of the rainy season, but several residents said it felt worse than usual.
"I feel like in all the many years I've lived here, I've never encountered anything like this, where it rains continuously for days," said 63-year-old resident Anutin Meechamnan.
The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) declared a disaster for all the city's 50 districts, a move that gives local organisations special powers to act.
Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said on Saturday afternoon that the situation had "stabilised", adding: "If more rainwater doesn't fall in the area, it will be solved."
"If the rain stops, it is expected that it will take two to three days to drain the floodwater," he said in an update broadcast on social media.
Almost continuous rain since Thursday afternoon has swelled Bangkok's network of canals, sending murky water into surrounding homes, restaurants, shops and alleyways.
"Our problem is that the canals are full," Chadchart said.
"We are cooperating with nearby provinces and try to drain water out through other sides, minimising the amount that flows into Bangkok."
Once dubbed the "Venice of the East", Bangkok is built on former marshland and rests about 1.5 metres (five feet) above sea level.
The BMA said earlier the city's pumping stations were operating at full capacity, drawing some 1,200 cubic metres per second combined.
AFP reporters saw residents wading or pushing their motorcycles through high waters in several districts of eastern Bangkok, while parked cars were partially submerged on one major road. AFP

title: India election body orders voter roll review
description: India election body orders voter roll review
content:
The Election Commission of India ordered a review of its voter-roll software on Saturday after a newspaper reported that its chief had been questioned by his deputies over changes to voter lists that excluded millions of voters.
Opposition parties have said the lists have been manipulated to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
The Election Commission of India has said differences are normal in any institution, and that all its actions were lawful.
The Indian Express newspaper reported this week that two election commissioners had raised questions or expressed concerns to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at least 14 times in 10 months, mostly in connection with the process of updating voters' lists that began last year.
Opposition parties and the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party have demanded Kumar's resignation. The CJP said it would launch nationwide protests on October 2 if he did not quit by Saturday.
The Commission said on Saturday that a committee led by a senior election official and including an independent technology expert would examine whether the software complied with election laws and rules.
It also said local officials would visit voters flagged for discrepancies instead of routinely requiring them to appear at government offices.

title: Pakistan  KSA reaffirm Makkah s joint defence
description: Pakistan  KSA reaffirm Makkah s joint defence
content:
Saudi defence minister commends alliance military chiefs' meeting outcome
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia reaffirmed their commitment to continue joint efforts aimed at confronting attacks targeting Makkah Al-Mukarramah, as well as civilian and economic facilities in the kingdom, in accordance with the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence.
"We commended the outcomes of the meeting of the Chiefs of Staff of the countries party to the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence, and discussed the sinful attacks that targeted Makkah Al-Mukarramah, as well as civilian and economic facilities in the Kingdom," Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman said in a post on his social media platform X.
"I met with His Excellency the Chief of the Pakistan Army, Field Marshal Asim Munir, Commander of the Pakistan Armed Forces," he further said.
Saudi Minister of State, Cabinet Member and National Security Adviser Dr Musaad bin Mohammed Al-Aiban, Chief of General Staff General Fayyadh bin Hamed Al-Ruwaili, and the Minister of Defence's adviser for intelligence affairs, Hisham bin Abdulaziz bin Saif, among other senior officials, also attended the meeting, according to the post.
The meeting came a day after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday held an urgent meeting of their top military commanders in Riyadh under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), marking the first exclusive high-level military coordination between the three countries since the trilateral defence pact was signed last month.
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Turkish Chief of General Staff Gen Selcuk Bayraktaroglu and Saudi Chief of General Staff Gen Fayyadh bin Hamed Al-Ruwaili attended the meeting in the Saudi capital, according to a statement issued by the ISPR on Friday.
The chiefs of defense forces and chiefs of general staff reviewed the security situation and the threats facing the kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
They strongly resented the attacks targeting the holy city of Makkah and civilian and economic infrastructure, the Inter-Services Public Relations said.
They appreciated the vigilance and professionalism of the Saudi armed forces for ensuring safety of the people and security of the kingdom, it added.
The participants also discussed ways to further advance cooperation among the armed forces of the three countries and to enhance intelligence sharing, military coordination, and capability integration, thereby strengthening deterrence and collective defense.
The participants commended the longstanding relations and mutual trust that bind the people and the armed forces of the three countries. They noted that their meeting in Riyadh reflects the strength of their defense partnership and their shared determination to immediately translate the commitments of the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement into effective military cooperation.
The participants strongly affirmed their commitment to collective defense thereby demonstrating the resolve of the three countries in defending the security, sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

title: Trump rejects Iran s proposal on Hormuz
description: Trump rejects Iran s proposal on Hormuz
content:
Tehran's latest offer would reopen strait, end fighting in seven days
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday he had rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end fighting in the Middle East.
Iran raised the initiative at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the Americans via Qatari mediators and that it could reopen the strategic waterway and put an end to hostilities in the region within seven days.
But in comments to reporters at the White House, Trump said: "I reject their proposal. ... I rejected their deal.
"They want to make a deal to open the Hormuz Strait immediately because they're losing so badly," he said before leaving for Tennessee. "We're winning tremendously.
"They want to make a deal and I think that's fine, I like making a deal too. What they want to do is immediately open the Hormuz Strait ... because they have no money coming in, because they get their money from the Hormuz Strait," Trump said.
The US has imposed an economic blockade on Iran to put pressure on Tehran to lift its blockade of Hormuz, which has drastically reduced shipping through the strait, even though Trump again asserted that the US had control of the waterway.
The Wall Street Journal first reported that Trump had rejected the Iranian proposal, citing unnamed US officials.
It said Trump was privately sceptical that Iran would meet his demands and had told his staff that he sees a renewed bombing campaign as likely after the November US midterm elections to Congress.
A US official had said earlier that discussions with Iran through mediators were "positive and constructive".
The Iranians also engaged their Saudi rivals regarding the Strait of Hormuz, underscoring the stakes of a seven-month-old conflict that has disrupted oil flows through a critical shipping lane and taken a toll on the global economy.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi told reporters at the United Nations on Friday the proposed deal would trigger a seven-day countdown to reopening the strait and a pause in regional fighting.
"If there is seriousness on the US side to come to a deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, everything is now prepared," Araqchi said. If the US were to agree, the warring parties could start wider talks "on mutually agreed subjects."
That could potentially include discussions of Iran's nuclear programme. Trump has said Tehran must never acquire a nuclear bomb, while a senior Iranian official told Reuters that Iran would show no flexibility over its nuclear programme even if the USaccepted its peace deal.
Iran would grant no concessions over its rights, including enriching uranium or shipping its highly enriched uranium out of the country, the official said.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, in an interview with the CBS show "Face the Nation", said Tehran was ready for talks on its nuclear programme and other issues, but would not accept "bullying or coercion".
"Iran is not seeking war, but will defend itself against pressure, threats and attacks," Pezeshkian said, adding that it had already agreed that "we're not supposed to develop nuclear weapons".
Previous attempts at diplomacy have failed to end the war, which began on February 28 with US and Israeli attacks.
Since then the war has alternated between pauses and renewed strikes, killing thousands while degrading Iran's conventional forces and damaging Iran's already ailing economy.
Iran and its allies have retaliated by extending the conflict throughout the region. Iran has struck US allies in the Gulf with drones and missiles while its Houthi allies in Yemen have targeted Saudi interests.

title: PTI faces heavy odds
description: PTI faces heavy odds
content:
The opposition alliance on Saturday downplayed its differences with the PTI as insignificant and vowed to support the party.
"Our differences are over unilateral decisions by the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa chief minister regarding the movement. But we will not withdraw our support for the march and will participate whenever it is held," a source within the TTAP said.
The source cast doubt on the date announced by the chief minister, saying there was strong support within the group for a strategy of attrition aimed at wearing down the government.
A senior PTI leader said such a strategy could prove more damaging to the party than to the government, adding that what the leader described as abduction-style arrests of ministers, lawmakers and party office-bearers, as well as firing at the residences of party leaders, had spread fear among party members.
A TTAP leader told The Express Tribune that differences over what he described as "impulsive decisions" by PTI leaders remained, saying the alliance's leadership regularly engaged with the government and was weakened in negotiations when it was kept in the dark about planned street movements.
He said TTAP leaders Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Nasir objected to the sudden announcement of the delay, but the alliance would support the PTI's long march whenever it was held. TTAP had, in fact, proposed repeatedly delaying the march to wear down the government in Islamabad if the strategy appeared to be yielding results, he said.
Achakzai would join PTI leaders on the protest container in Islamabad, he added.
A senior PTI leader endorsed the account given by TTAP leaders but said the party had little room to maneuver in the movement. "The government is crippling PTI on its home ground. Our ministers are being rounded up, parliamentarians whisked away by unknown men and the residences of more than a dozen PTI leaders have come under fire. All of this is happening on our home ground. The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister and his team cannot even hold a news conference about it because they are so scared," he said.
He said there was a wave of fear among PTI leaders and workers in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. "The PTI cannot exhaust the establishment, so delaying the long march will not work at all," he said.
"If Sohail Afridi pursues this strategy, he could end up being disqualified. The powers that be have many options at their disposal, and this time they are not in the mood to give PTI any political room," he added.
He said the war-of-attrition strategy appeared workable on social media, but the reality on the ground was far more difficult for PTI and the provincial government.
"First, I do not see any long march taking place. Even if it does, the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa chief minister's march will stop at the first picket line it encounters, where it will stage a sit-in to press its demands," he said.
He said around 20 PTI lawmakers had either been attacked or had their residences targeted by known or unknown assailants, while several had also been arrested. Among them was Charsadda MNA Fazal Khan, who he said was arrested during the day, while Waziristan MNA Muhammad Zubair Khan was allegedly abducted following a crossfire that could have cost him his life.
He said PK-9 lawmaker Sultan Room was also recently abducted, while Mardan MNA Mujahid Ali Khan and PTI MPA from Swat Dr Amjad Ali had faced attacks on their residences.
Even Tariq Saeed, the chief minister's special assistant for home and tribal affairs, recently survived what he described as an abduction attempt by unknown men, he said. Provincial Minister Fateh Khan was also abducted by unknown men, while another provincial minister, Shakeel Khan, survived an alleged abduction attempt but was later booked in a police case, he added.
Rameez Abbasi, president of PTI's Hazara Division, was also abducted by unknown men, he said.
Provincial ministers Shakeel Khan, Meena Khan Afridi and Shafi Jan were also staying at the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister's residence for fear of arrest, he said.
"Where MNAs and MPAs cannot even sleep at home or visit their constituencies, how can they rally support for a long march? If an elected government is not safe, how can workers follow its lead in the hope that it will protect them? The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government is in deep waters," he said.
The senior PTI leader said the party had been demoralised in Punjab, where it had faced similar arrests and other measures against its leaders and workers for the past three years, and that the same situation was now unfolding in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.
"This time around, they have done the very same thing in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa that Punjab has faced for the last three years. This is a huge blow to our provincial autonomy and the provincial structure of government. It severely affects the PTI government's ability to operate and govern the province despite being in power and having control," he said.
He said no provincial minister had so far spoken publicly about the issue or provided figures for the number of people allegedly abducted or the residences that had come under attack.
"This shows how fearful they are of what is happening and how badly they want to keep themselves out of the crosshairs of the powers that be," he said.
He said successive arrests and other coercive measures allegedly carried out by the establishment had weakened PTI's resolve to mount a meaningful political movement.
Sheikh Waqas Akram, the party's central information secretary, said the odds were against the PTI but that it would follow the plan announced by the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa chief minister. TTAP Spokesperson was reached multiple times but was unavailble for comments.

title: Afridi offers olive branch with a sting
description: Afridi offers olive branch with a sting
content:
K-P CM warns against imposing governor's rule
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Saturday offered the federal government a fresh opportunity for dialogue ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) October 4 long march, saying his party had never refused negotiations even as preparations for the mobilisation remained complete.
Speaking to senior journalists, Afridi said there were still seven days before the march and urged the federal government to use the time for talks. He questioned why negotiations could not begin immediately if dialogue would eventually be required after the protest as well.
The chief minister said PTI had been ready to talk the previous day and remained ready to talk now, adding that the party had never backed away from negotiations. However, he alleged that the rulers were not allowing an understanding to be reached between PTI and the establishment.
His offer of dialogue comes after PTI postponed the planned September 27 mobilisation to October 4 following a political committee decision.
Afridi said PTI had approached every relevant institution for the past nine months but had received no response, forcing it, according to him, to announce the September 27 protest call.
He again referred to court orders concerning meetings with PTI founder Imran Khan, saying orders allowing 18 people to meet him every week had not been implemented.
The chief minister said there was still time to resolve the matter before the march and urged the government to use the remaining days for negotiations.
He also slammed the federal government's handling of K-P, alleging that it had closed routes into the province and interfered in its affairs.
Afridi said PTI had been labelled "wild" and "terrorist", referring to comments by Federal Information Minister Attaullah Tarar calling the provincial government the TTP's "B-team" and the Afghan Taliban's "C-team".
Tarar made those allegations on Friday while accusing the K-P government of failing to maintain law and order and of facilitating terrorist elements.
The chief minister said such remarks were part of a pre-planned narrative and claimed that the extensive preparations being made against the march reflected opposition to PTI among sections of the public.
Afridi said PTI would proceed with the march on October 4 and would return only after achieving "real freedom", adding that the party was not an armed group but a political movement.
He reiterated that PTI had never rejected negotiations and said the participation of JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman in any dialogue would be welcomed.
Afridi said the party had discussed the September 27 date with TTAP chief Mahmood Khan Achakzai and that preparations for the march were complete, adding that the delay was a political strategy.
He also slammed the atmosphere inside the provincial civil secretariat and other institutions, saying action would be taken against those who spread fear and rumours.
Afridi said he had himself visited the mosque in question and offered Friday prayers. He also referred to containers that had been brought into the Red Zone and later removed, while maintaining that preparations for the October 4 march had been completed.
The chief minister alleged that interference in the provincial government's work was continuing. Referring to the Shakil Khan matter, he claimed a deputy commissioner had been forced to register a first information report.
He questioned how government employees could stand up to "uncontrolled elements", while praising the assistant commissioner of Kohat for adopting a policy of restraint.
He also alleged that the country's debt had risen from Rs43 trillion to Rs97 trillion.
The chief minister said PTI would have to hold the march under any circumstances and that preparations were complete. He warned that if a "misadventure" occurred, the party could come out even before October 4.
Afridi alleged that a one-man policy was being pursued in the country, with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi acting as its representative. He said that, for him, the government itself was of little consequence and that he considered himself a soldier of Imran Khan.
Afridi also warned that imposing governor's rule in K-P or disqualifying him would provoke an unprecedented public reaction, saying neither option was something the government would be able to afford.
He said that if he ceased to be chief minister, the decision on his replacement would rest with Imran Khan.

title: 13 martyred in DI Khan checkpoint suicide blast
description: 13 martyred in DI Khan checkpoint suicide blast
content:
Women, a child, Customs inspector among dead 2 rescue personnel carrying injured also martyred Security tightene
A suicide bomber struck a joint Customs, police and Excise checkpoint in Darazinda tehsil of Dera Ismail Khan on the inter-provincial highway on Saturday, killing 13 people, including two women, a young girl and a Customs inspector, while 26 others were reported injured.
The attack was followed by separate assaults on those responding to the blast. A police Quick Response Force vehicle heading to the site was targeted, injuring a policeman, while armed assailants later opened fire on a Rescue 1122 ambulance carrying the injured to Dera Ismail Khan, killing two rescuers and wounding another.
According to sources, the suicide bomber targeted the joint checkpoint established on the inter-provincial highway in Darazinda, triggering a powerful explosion.
Two women and a minor girl were among the 13 people died in the blast. A Customs inspector was also among the dead.
The explosion spread fear and panic in the area. Security agencies and rescue teams immediately reached the scene and began relief and rescue operations.
The area was cordoned off after the blast, while authorities also began collecting evidence from the site.
According to sources, a police Quick Response Force vehicle heading towards the scene after receiving information about the attack was also targeted. A police official identified as Zohaib was injured in the attack.
In a separate incident, armed men opened fire on a Rescue 1122 ambulance transporting the injured to hospitals in Dera Ismail Khan.
The firing killed the Rescue 1122 driver and another member of the rescue staff, while one additional Rescue 1122 official was wounded.
Following the attacks, security was further tightened in Darazinda and surrounding areas.
Law-enforcement agencies have launched an investigation into the motive for the attacks and the identities of those involved.
Authorities were also working to establish the identities of those killed and compile further details of the incident, while the injured were receiving medical treatment.
Condemning the terrorist attack in a statement, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed deep sorrow and grief over the loss of precious human lives in the blast.
He expressed heartfelt sympathy and condolences to the families of the martyrs and prayed for speedy recovery of the injured.
"We will never let the sacrifices of the nation's protectors go in vain in the war against terrorism," he said, adding that the government was determined to completely eradicate terrorism from the country.
President Asif Ali Zardari also strongly condemned the bomb blast.
In a statement, he expressed deep sorrow and grief over the loss of innocent precious lives in the blast.
The president expressed his heartfelt condolences to the families of the martyrs, praying that Allah Almighty bless the departed souls with the highest ranks and grant patience and strength to the bereaved families.
He also prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured in the blast.
The president directed the concerned institutions to provide the best medical facilities to the injured and make the relief operations more effective.
Targeting innocent citizens and law enforcement officials in incidents of terrorism was highly condemnable, he added.
He said operations against Fitna al-Hindustan and Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists, who were committing heinous and brutal acts under foreign patronage, should be made more effective.

title: Twelve labourers abducted in Duki
description: Twelve labourers abducted in Duki
content:
Local tribesmen, forces kill 13 terrorists in Dera Bugti
Unidentified terrorists on Saturday abducted twelve labourers of a road construction company's camp in Duki district of Balochistan. Separately, volunteers of a peace force in Dera Bugti eliminated 13 terrorists who attacked a gas exploration company's camp.

title: IHC strikes down PCL placement provision
description: IHC strikes down PCL placement provision
content:
Declares part of Rule 22(2)(b) ultra vires
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has declared unconstitutional and without legal effect a provision of the Passport Rules, 2021 that allowed the names of citizens to be placed on the Passport Control List (PCL) based on recommendations from government agencies or departments.
The court held that the provision imposed an unguided restraint on the constitutional right to travel.
In a detailed judgment on a writ petition filed by a citizen, IHC's Justice Inaam Ameen Minhas also set aside an order refusing to remove the petitioner's name from the PCL and declared his placement on the list without lawful authority.
The court directed the relevant authorities to remove the petitioner's name from the PCL within 15 days of receiving a certified copy of the judgment and restrained them from interfering with his lawful foreign travel on the basis of the impugned placement.
The petitioner, Moin Ud Din, had challenged an order dated January 26, 2026, which rejected his request for removal from the PCL.
He had earlier been offloaded at Islamabad International Airport on December 18, 2025, while travelling to Saudi Arabia for Umrah despite holding a valid passport, a valid Saudi visa and a confirmed air ticket. According to the judgment, the authorities gave him no reason when they stopped him.
The petitioner had previously approached the IHC, which on January 15, 2026 directed the authorities to decide his pending applications through a speaking and well-reasoned order after providing him an opportunity to be heard.
He was subsequently given a personal hearing on January 23. However, the authorities communicated no order within the stipulated period, prompting him to file a contempt petition. Following issuance of notice in that matter, the authorities placed the impugned order before the court.
The record showed that the petitioner's name had been placed on the PCL on December 24, 2024, following a recommendation from the National Central Bureau of INTERPOL, which was forwarded by the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA).
The recommendation was based on his deportation from the United Kingdom following his conviction for causing death by dangerous driving while under the influence of alcohol. He had been sentenced to three years in prison.
The authorities defended the PCL placement on the grounds that the petitioner's conduct adversely affected Pakistan's international reputation and that such placement served as a deterrent.
The petitioner's counsel argued that he had already served his sentence and been deported, and no criminal case, inquiry or investigation was pending against him in Pakistan. He was neither a proclaimed offender nor the subject of an extradition request, and his passport had never been impounded, confiscated or cancelled.

title: PM reaffirms support for China s GDI
description: PM reaffirms support for China s GDI
content:
Hails platform as vital for fostering solidarity
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday reaffirmed Pakistan's steadfast commitment to the Global Development Initiative (GDI), hailing it as a vital platform for fostering solidarity, enhancing South-South cooperation and delivering tangible results for the developing nations.
Addressing a high-level GDI meeting hosted by Chinese Vice President Han Zheng on the sidelines of the 81st UNGA session in New York, the prime minister praised the initiative's foresight.
He noted that three years ago, at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, Chinese President Xi Jinping introduced the landmark proposal when it was uniquely needed.
In a statement broadcast on national Tv channels, the prime minister highlighted that the goals of GDI also complemented their own national economic transformation plan.
"Our cooperation with China also continues through the Belt and Road Initiative and its flagship project, the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, which is now entering into its second phase. As we approach 2030, Pakistan stands ready to deepen cooperation with all partners under the GDI by replicating successful projects at scale and identifying new and innovative areas of cooperation," he added.
The prime minister said three years ago, at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, President Xi Jinping had put forward the landmark Global Development Initiative (GDI), a proposal that was far ahead of its time.
Today, he opined the wisdom and vision of President Xi Jinping behind that decision is recognized by the world, adding with only six years left to the 2030 deadline, progress on the Sustainable Development Goals remained inadequate and slow.
The prime minister underlined that the growing SDGs financing gap, frequent and severe climate disasters, rising food and fuel prices, intensified by the resurgence of geopolitical tensions, continued to reverse decades of gains in the developing countries.
Responding to these challenges, he called for strengthened multilateral cooperation, as advocated by the People's Republic of China; terming its GDI as very timely.
The prime minister said that they could bear witness that the framework of the GDI has already translated into substantial and practical benefits across the developing world, delivered in the true spirit of 'win-win cooperation'.
He further said the Global Development Initiative also remains essential for accelerating progress on the 2030 Agenda.

title: Islamabad  the contained city
description: Islamabad  the contained city
content:
Containers stay put as federal capital remains on alert
Rows of shipping containers have once again become a defining feature of Islamabad's political landscape, lining major junctions, entry points and approaches to the Red Zone as the capital remains on alert for possible protests.
The barriers, placed ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) march, have stayed in position even after the party pushed the mobilisation back to October 4. The protest was originally scheduled to descend on the federal capital today, September 27.
The container cordon remains visible at Faizabad, 26 Number Chungi, T-Chowk, Margalla Avenue and other key entry points, while barricades continue to guard several approaches to the Red Zone.
Some traffic has been diverted to alternative routes, although major roads across the capital have not been completely closed and traffic continues to flow on several important routes.
According to sources, the administration had moved the containers to various locations in advance so that key roads could be closed immediately if required. Police and other law-enforcement personnel have also been deployed at sensitive locations. The arrangements were originally made ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's September 27 protest and long march. Following the party's decision to postpone the mobilisation to October 4, the security arrangements are expected to remain in place for longer, increasing the cost to the national exchequer.
According to a media report, the capital police had initially sought Rs820 million for security arrangements, including container rentals, accommodation and meals for police personnel being brought in from Punjab and Sindh.
The estimate was calculated for one week, with police expecting the protest and march to disperse by October 4.

Prime Minister's Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah on Saturday said that everyone had a constitutional and legal right to protest, but Islamabad should be off-limits for demonstrations and urged people to "end the practice" of staging long marches and protests in the federal capital.
"If anyone needs to protest, they can do so in Faisalabad, Hyderabad, Karachi, Peshawar, or Multan. This practice needs to end," Sanaullah said while talking to private TV channel.
He pointed out that the ban on protests in Islamabad did not apply only to the PTI. Gatherings in the capital without prior permission are also banned under the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act 2024, which had been rushed through the National Assembly ahead of a PTI gathering that month.
"Peaceful protest is everyone's constitutional and legal right, but they need to minus Islamabad from that," Sanaullah stated. "It is everyone's right, but minus attacks on Islamabad. This must be ensured."
He highlighted that a message had been sent that no protests would be allowed within Islamabad, as foreign diplomats were present in the federal capital and demonstrations would send a "bad message".
The PML-N leader accused PTI of aiming to overthrow the government, alleging that their goal is to "erect ladders next to the walls of Adiala jail and break in to meet Imran Khan", who has been incarcerated there since an Aug 5, 2023 conviction.

title: Ord promulgated to protect Islamabad CCTVs
description: Ord promulgated to protect Islamabad CCTVs
content:
Up to Rs2m fine for damage to surveillance infrastructure
President Asif Ali Zardari, on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, has approved an ordinance aimed at protecting Islamabad Capital Territory's Safe City cameras and surveillance infrastructure and ensuring compensation for any damage caused to them.
The ordinance seeks to safeguard Safe City cameras and surveillance systems from damage and ensure recovery of the cost in case of any loss, President Secretariat Media Wing, Saturday, said in a press release.
Under the ordinance, financial penalties may be imposed for damaging, instigating damage to, or encouraging damage to Safe City cameras and surveillance infrastructure.
"A fine of up to Rs2 million per camera or piece of surveillance infrastructure may be imposed in case of damage," it was added.
Organizers may also be held responsible for damage caused to the infrastructure during rallies, processions, sit-ins, protests, strikes or other gatherings.
The amount of the fine and the cost of the damage will be determined by an authorized officer after providing the relevant person with an opportunity to be heard.
The relevant person will have the right to appeal against the determination of the fine or damage cost before the District and Sessions Judge, Islamabad, within 30 days.
In case of non-payment of the imposed fine or damage cost, the amount may be recovered as arrears of land revenue.
The funds recovered through fines and compensation for damage will be utilized for the repair and replacement of Safe City cameras and surveillance infrastructure.

title: Dar warns against altering East Jerusalem status
description: Dar warns against altering East Jerusalem status
content:
DPM raises concern over ME security situation
DPM/FM Ishaq Dar on Saturday expressed concern over the continued violations against Al-Aqsa Mosque/Al-Haram Al-Sharif and attempts to alter the historical and legal status quo in Occupied East Jerusalem.
He reiterated Pakistan's steadfast support for the Hashemite Custodianship over the Islamic and Christian Holy Sites in Jerusalem.
The DPM/FM participated in Joint Arab League- Group of 4 Islamic Countries (Pakistan, Turkiye, Malaysia, Indonesia) Ministerial Meeting on Jerusalem in New York.
The meeting, convened by the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, was a follow-up to the Ministerial Meeting on Jerusalem held in Amman on 5 August 5 this year, the Foreign Spokesperson said in a press release.
The DPM/FM reaffirmed Pakistan's unwavering support for the Palestinian people's right to self-determination and for the establishment of an independent, sovereign and contiguous State of Palestine, based on the pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar, in the meanwhile, had a cordial exchange with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Jordan Ayman Safadi on the sidelines of the 81st UNGA in New York.
Dar expresses concern over continued violations; attempts to alter Occupied East Jerusalem legal status quo
The two leaders exchanged views on matters of mutual interest and regional developments and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening Pakistan-Jordan relations.
Dar also expressed deep concern over the prevailing security situation in the region and the Middle East, and reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to the peaceful resolution of disputes in accordance with international law.
He underscored the need for Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) Member States to harness their collective potential to promote peace, resilience, and shared prosperity for the region's nearly half a billion people.
The DPM/FM chaired the 27th Informal Meeting of the Council of Ministers (COM) of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in New York, on the sidelines of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly, the Foreign Office Spokesperson said in a press release.
Pakistan is currently chairing the ECO Council of Ministers for 20262027 under the theme "Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO."
The meeting was attended by Foreign Ministers and senior representatives of ECO Member States, including Foreign Minister of Azerbaijan Jeyhun Bayramov, Foreign Minister of Iran Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of the Kyrgyz Republic Zheenbek Kulubaev, Foreign Minister of Tajikistan Sirojiddin Muhriddin, Deputy Foreign Minister of Turkiye Berris Ekinci, Permanent Representative of Turkmenistan to the UN Vepa Hajiyev, Deputy Permanent Representative of Uzbekistan to the UN Laziz Karaev, and Director General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan Beibut Kulatayev. Secretary General of ECO Dr. Asad Majeed Khan also briefed the Council.
The Deputy Prime Minister expressed gratitude to ECO Member States for reposing confidence in Pakistan and reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to advancing the Organization's objectives and strengthening regional cooperation.

title: Amitabh Bachchan recalls his quick, no-frills marriage | The Express Tribune
description:
Amitabh Bachchan recalls his quick,
no-frills marriage
content:
Actor says he tied the knot the day after deciding to get married
Amitabh Bachchan has shared a surprising account of how his marriage to actress Jaya Bachchan came together with almost no advance planning. The veteran actor revealed that the decision was made so quickly that the couple tied the knot just a day after discussing marriage.
According to Gulf News, Bachchan spoke about his wedding while interacting with Kolkata contestant Aheli Roy on Kaun Banega Crorepati 18. During the conversation, Aheli asked him how he had convinced Jaya's family before their marriage.
Bachchan said there was no lengthy discussion or elaborate planning between the families. Instead, he simply suggested to Jaya that they should get married, and she agreed. "I told Jaya one day that we should get married, and that was it - the decision was made", he said.
He added, "After the marriage was decided, Jaya ji must have gone and told her parents. We don't even know what she must have said, but they agreed and came over. Then there was some discussion, and we got married the very next day".
Bachchan said the couple did not get caught up in the elaborate preparations that often accompany weddings today.
"Honestly, shouldn't it be this way? Who wants to get into all that hassle of deciding the date, choosing what to wear, going here and there, making all these arrangements, having bands play and everything? There's really no point to all that. We simply accepted that she was going to be my wife, and nothing could be more meaningful than that", he said.
The couple married on June 3, 1973, following the success of Zanjeer. According to Khaleej Times, they celebrated their 52nd wedding anniversary in June 2025.

title: US cities  states celebrate  Dolly Parton Day
description: US cities  states celebrate  Dolly Parton Day
content:
Singer-songwriter, philanthropist had died last month aged 80
Cities and states across the US celebrated the inaugural Dolly Parton Day on Friday -- 9/25 -- a date that recalls one of the late country icon's most beloved hits.
Parton died last month at the age of 80, plunging her fans into mourning for a singer-songwriter, philanthropist and businesswoman whom many saw as a unifying figure in a divided America.
This week, California Governor Gavin Newsom said he was establishing the day to encourage citizens of America's most populous state to take inspiration from the "9 to 5" singer, who starred in the 1980 film of the same name with Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin.
The movie's signature song, written and performed by Parton, has become a workplace empowerment anthem.
"We could all afford to live a little more like Dolly. Be kind, be humble, and have some fun... Be a diamond in a rhinestone world," Newsom said.
"With this bill, we are not just establishing a day to celebrate Dolly Parton, we are creating an annual reminder to us, every year, to live the way she did -- joyfully, graciously, and with a whole lot of heart."
Events around the Golden State were to include musical performances and giveaways in downtown Los Angeles.
At sunset, Santa Monica was to light up its 90-foot (30 meter) -tall Pacific Wheel on the pier in pink, with "DOLLY" and "WE WILL ALWAYS LOVE YOU!" displayed along with pink hearts, stars and spiral animations.
Los Angeles County Library was planning to hold a series of activities in honor of a woman whose literacy drive brought books to millions of underprivileged children.
The New York borough of Manhattan proclaimed the date to be Dolly Parton Appreciation Day, while New Orleans designated Friday as Dolly Day.
There were also due to be community events in Lexington, Kentucky, to celebrate Parton's legacy and the work she did to improve literacy.
In her home state of Tennessee a number of counties proclaimed Dolly Parton Day to go alongside the state-wide recognition on her January 19 birthday.
Parton rose from grinding poverty to become a rhinestone-studded legend with hits like "Jolene" and "I Will Always Love You."
She also starred in multiple films and donated millions of dollars to charities as she built a vast business empire that includes her popular Dollywood theme park in Tennessee, cosmetics, pet apparel, baking mixes and even a truck stop.
Born and raised in East Tennessee, Parton wrote her first song at age six, performed regularly on television by age ten, made her first recording a year later, and became a professional songwriter at sixteen. After writing songs for others, she released her debut album, Hello, I'm Dolly in 1967, starting her nearly sixty-year career. Parton released 49 studio albums and wrote more than 3,000 songs, including "I Will Always Love You" – a two-time US country chart-topper and an international success for Whitney Houston. afp

content:
Newly launched drama explores love, family tensions
Express Entertainment's newly launched drama 'Ranjish' has begun its journey on television, with three episodes on aired. The family drama revolves around love, marriage, family bonds and the misunderstandings that can gradually create distance between people who are otherwise close.
The story centres on Farhad, played by Mohib Mirza, a married man who runs a fashion boutique and shares a loving relationship with his wife, Muattar, played by Hina Choudhry. Farhad is shown as a caring husband who tries to support his wife, but his married life becomes complicated because of tensions within the family.
Mohib Mirza started off as a theatre actor in 1999. He also won the award in Best Supporting Actor category at the International Filmmaker Film Festival held in England.
In 'Ranjish', at the centre of this conflict is Farhad's mother, Ruqaiya, played by Sakina Sammo. While she maintains a pleasant image in front of others, her behaviour towards her daughter-in-law inside the house is considerably different. Her taunts, complaints and treatment of Muattar gradually become a source of tension between the couple.
The situation is familiar to many viewers who may recognise the dynamics of households where disagreements between a 'Saas' 'Bahu' eventually place the husband in an uncomfortable position. Farhad finds himself caught between his mother's complaints and his wife's grievances, leaving him increasingly puzzled about how to maintain peace between the two relationships.
Muattar, meanwhile, is portrayed as someone who largely remains patient despite the circumstances. Her attempts to deal with the situation without constantly escalating the conflict add another layer to Farhad's dilemma. As the story progresses, the pressure on him appears to come not only from his marriage but also from his responsibilities towards the wider family.
The drama expands beyond the central couple, bringing in a number of characters from both families, including siblings and other relatives. Their relationships and individual perspectives are expected to add further complications to the unfolding story.

title: Humaira Channa  Ghulam Abbas win music lovers  hearts
description: Humaira Channa  Ghulam Abbas win music lovers  hearts
content:
Pakistan Film Festival features established, emerging singers; draws large number of music enthusiasts, families
Renowned singers Humaira Channa and Ghulam Abbas won the hearts of music lovers with their memorable performances as the three-day Pakistan Music Festival 2026 continued at the Arts Council of Pakistan Karachi, bringing together established singers and emerging musical talent on one platform.
Held at Jaun Elia Lawn at the Arts Council Karachi, the festival featured a diverse mix of classical, folk and contemporary music, with performers presenting songs from different traditions and genres. The event drew a large audience of music enthusiasts and families, who responded warmly to the performances.
On the second day, Humaira Channa captivated the audience with her melodious voice and evergreen songs. The veteran singer received enthusiastic applause as she performed some of her popular numbers, creating one of the evening's most engaging moments.
Humaira Channa entered the Pakistani entertainment industry influenced by her father who was a filmmaker. She first sang for her father's film at the age of nine. Then she was given an opportunity to sing folk songs of Sufi Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai on Pakistan Television, Karachi. She rose to fame in the early 1990s. She sings in Urdu, Punjabi, Saraiki and Sindhi languages. She has sung over a thousand songs in her career.
Initially, she was a substitute singer for Naheed Akhtar during the 1980s, after Naheed Akhtar retired from the Pakistani film industry. In 2017, some of the iconic playback singers of Pakistan were complaining about lack of work due to introduction of new trends in Pakistani film industry where the emphasis now was on pop musicians and music bands instead of film songs that these playback singers used to sing.
Humaira Channa has also gone on concert tours to the United States, Canada, United Arab Emirates, Bangladesh and across Europe.
Ghulam Abbas, known for his distinctive voice and contribution to Pakistani music, was among the performers who received an enthusiastic response from the audience. Playback singer Mehdi Hassan had first noticed him as a young boy and introduced him to his mentor Ismail Khan. Abbas got advanced classical training in singing from him.
Ghulam Abbas started his playback singing career with a Punjabi film "Aashiq Loag Soudai" in 1975. His first breakthrough was a song in the film "Ajnabi" (1975), under the musical direction of Nisar Bazmi. The song was "Wo aa to jaye magar intezar hi kam hai" and its popularity established him as a playback singer. Then musician Robin Ghosh gave him a career-boosting song, "Aise wo sharmaye jaise megha chaye" for movie "Do Saathi" (1975). From there on, Abbas gave voice to 129 songs in 120 films.
Apart from playback singing for movies, Abbas has also sung many ghazals, semi-classical songs, and national songs for Radio Pakistan and Pakistan Television. His ghazal "Main ne roka bhi nahin aur wo thehra bhi nahin" won the award of having most broadcasts on Radio Pakistan.
The festival's second day also featured performances by Salman Alvi, Imran Abbas Khan, Sagheer Ahmed, Imran Javed, Muzhar Amrao, Bindu Khan, Aziz Warsi, Muhammad Zubair, Arman Rahim, Uroosa Ali, Maham Tahir, Waqar Hussain, Shah Rukh Abbas, Faisal Latif, Narodha Malani and Shoukat Faqeer.
The evening was hosted by Noman Khan, while Chairman of the Music Committee Amjad Hussain Shah attended the event along with a large number of music lovers.
The festival opened with a Grand Melodies Night, featuring veteran singers as well as emerging artists, including performers who gained recognition through the Pakistan Idol platform.
Ghulam Abbas, Mehmood Ali Khan, Rashid Ali Haidri, Akhlaq Bashir, Noman Khan, Intizar Hussain, Mumtaz Sabzal, Kamran Saggu, Imran Nashad, Shehbaz Ali, Hira Qaiser, Kashia Kaif, Naila Saleem, Sonia Khan and Esha Adhiwal performed on the opening day.
The opening night set the tone for a festival celebrating the country's varied musical traditions.
Speaking at the opening, the Arts Council of Pakistan Karachi President said the festival aimed to provide opportunities to new and emerging singers while bringing different musical traditions together.
He said Pakistan had no shortage of young musical talent and that emerging artists needed platforms and encouragement to develop their abilities. He also highlighted the participation of singers associated with Pakistan Idol.
The Pakistan Music Festival aims to showcase the diversity of Pakistani music by bringing together different languages, regions and musical styles. Alongside established voices, the inclusion of emerging singers gives younger artists an opportunity to perform before a live audience.
The three-day Pakistan Music Festival 2026 will continue at the Arts Council of Pakistan Karachi until September 27, offering audiences another opportunity to experience performances by established names and rising talent.

title: Wall Street ends higher on AI stocks buying
description: Wall Street ends higher on AI stocks buying
content:
Gains cap volatile week driven by uncertainty about AI winners and losers, war concerns
Wall Street ended higher on Friday, lifted by Microsoft and other AI-related technology stocks, while high oil prices and a recent surge in US Treasury yields kept investors on edge.
Gains in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq capped a volatile week driven by uncertainty about what industries will win and lose from artificial intelligence, and by concerns about the US war with Iran and a surge in US Treasury yields.
Microsoft rallied 3.7%, lifting its 2026 gain to 7%, after the software giant unveiled several new capabilities in its Copilot app, including a coding tool and an always-on AI agent.
Chipmaker Qualcomm gained 4% and Dell advanced 5%. Akamai Technologies rallied 3.2% after an $11.6 billion cloud services deal with AI leader Anthropic. The deal includes a warrant that could give Anthropic up to 5% of Akamai.
"That's a positive from the standpoint that people are still investing, deals are still being done," said Thomas Martin, Senior Portfolio Manager at Globalt Investments in Atlanta. "It's another circular deal, so ok ... but Akamai stock is up."
Meta Platforms dipped 3.3%. The social media company's stock soared about 13% this week amid a strong reception to its Muse AI agent, which analysts say could benefit tech infrastructure stocks, while challenging banks, online shopping platforms and other consumer businesses.

title: Geopolitics keeps PSX range bound
description: Geopolitics keeps PSX range bound
content:
KSE-100 index ends week lower as uncertainty weighs
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) remained range bound during the outgoing week as geopolitical uncertainty and domestic developments kept investors cautious, with the benchmark KSE-100 index closing at 170,765, down 119 points, or 0.1%, week-on-week.
On a day-on-day basis, the bourse commenced the trading week with range-bound activity. The KSE-100 gained 269 points (+0.16%) to close at 171,153. Tuesday saw further consolidation amid falling oil prices. The index gained 250 points (+0.15%) at 171,402. The market further extended its advance on Wednesday, when it closed higher by 830 points (+0.48%) at 172,233.
However, geopolitical uncertainty dampened PSX sentiment on the second last day of the trading week, Thursday. The index declined 1,734 points (-1.01%) to close at 170,499. Friday was a range-bound day with the KSE-100 gaining 266 points (+0.16%) and settled at 170,765.
"Overall, geopolitical developments kept the market flat," observed Arif Habib Limited (AHL) in its commentary. The KSE-100 closed at 170,765 points, down 0.1% from 170,885 points in the previous week, as hopes of progress in US-Iran talks and softer oil prices supported the market early in the week before geopolitical concerns resurfaced and crude prices rose.
Power generation rose 5.1% year-on-year to 14,943 gigawatt hours (GWh) in Aug'26, the third-highest August generation on record, supported by higher hydel, coal, gas and wind output. Generation cost increased 38% YoY to Rs10.01/kWh due to higher RLNG and furnace oil mix and elevated oil prices, prompting power distribution companies to seek a positive fuel cost adjustment of Rs1.73/kWh, mentioned AHL.
Oil production improved 1.4% WoW to 68.5k barrels per day, mainly due to higher flows from Makori East, Maramzai and Mardankhel, while gas production decreased 2.5% WoW to 2,934 million cubic feet per day, driven by lower production from Mari, Uch, Kandhkot and Shewa.
Pakistan's oil and gas reserves reached 3,720 million barrels of oil equivalent in Jun'26, with oil reserves up 15% YoY to 276 million barrels and gas reserves up 9% to 20,664 billion cubic feet. Newly discovered fields added 53.5 million barrels of oil and 773 billion cubic feet of gas, while the country's estimated reserve life stood at around 19 years.
Pakistan's total liquid foreign exchange reserves rose 0.07% WoW to $26.8 billion, while the State Bank reserves increased 0.05% to $21.4 billion and banks' reserves grew 0.15% to $5.41 billion. Import cover remained unchanged at 3.03 months.
Attock Refinery, Pakistan Refinery, National Refinery and Cnergyico signed upgrade agreements with Inter State Gas Systems (ISGS) under the Pakistan Oil Refining Policy for Upgradation of Existing/Brownfield Refineries 2023, as amended in Feb'24 and Aug'26.
Petroleum prices were mixed in the latest revision under the daily pricing mechanism, with high-speed diesel falling to Rs412.12/litre during the week, while motor spirit reached Rs389.28/litre, added AHL.
Local and geopolitical uncertainty drove caution, noted Wadee Zaman of JS Global, stating that the KSE-100 remained broadly flat during the week, closing at 170,765 (-119 points), as geopolitical uncertainty and domestic political developments continued to weigh on investor sentiment.
Brent crude averaged $103.1/barrel, down 2.2% WoW, while domestic MS and HSD prices declined by Rs1.51/litre and Rs12.80/litre to Rs389.28/ltr and Rs412.12/ltr, respectively, following five consecutive weekly increases. On the external front, Pakistan and the IMF commenced talks for the fourth review of the $7 billion Extended Fund Facility, potentially paving the way for the release of the fifth tranche of $1 billion, mentioned Zaman.
Meanwhile, the ADB revised down Pakistan's FY27 GDP growth forecast to 3.7% from 4.5% previously. Pakistan secured $4.7 billion in foreign loans during 2MFY27, while profit and dividend repatriation declined 13.4% YoY to $557 million.
In a key development, four of Pakistan's five local refineries signed formal upgrade agreements with the government, paving the way for an estimated $6 billion investment over the next five years. In the latest Pakistan Investment Bond auction, the government raised Rs181 billion, with yields increasing by 20-75 basis points across different tenors. The State Bank's foreign exchange reserves remained stable at $21.4 billion, he said.

title: India orders coal plants to run at full capacity
description: India orders coal plants to run at full capacity
content:
Ministry invokes emergency provisions to meet expected rise in electricity demand
India has ordered more than 100 captive coal-fired power plants to operate at maximum capacity from October 1 through year-end to meet what it expects will be a rise in electricity demand.
The federal power ministry's order, invoked under emergency provisions of the Electricity Act, applies to plants with installed capacity of at least 50 megawatts. The aim is to meet an "expected rise in electricity demand in the coming months," showed the order dated September 25 and seen by Reuters. Nearly 40% of coal-fired plants are operating with critically low fuel stock due to a surge in power demand as the El Nino climate phenomenon raises temperatures more than usual.
The plants primarily serve industrial facilities such as aluminium smelters, steel manufacturers, cement factories and oil refineries. The power ministry has directed generators to sell surplus electricity through power exchanges.
The order covers 112 plants belonging to companies including Vedanta, Tata Steel, Hindalco Industries, JSW Steel, UltraTech Cement, Reliance Industries, Indian Oil, Bharat Aluminium, Hindustan Zinc and Nayara Energy.
The ministry has ordered plants to report weekly to the Central Electricity Authority detailing generation, captive consumption, power sales, available capacity and coal stocks.
Separately, the ministry has extended an earlier emergency order requiring Tata Power's imported coal-fired plant in Mundra, Gujarat to operate at full capacity until December 31, citing the demand situation.
Section 11 of the Electricity Act allows the government, under extraordinary circumstances, to direct generators to operate power stations in accordance with its instructions.

title: Azerbaijan signs  10b plus investment deals

content:
President says 2nd phase of Absheron field will increase gas production by 5b cubic metres
Azerbaijan signed agreements representing more than $10 billion in potential investment at an international forum in Baku, a presidential aide said on Saturday, as the country also announced a series of energy deals.
State oil company Socar, France's TotalEnergies and Abu Dhabi's XRG reached a final investment decision on the full-field development of the Absheron gas and condensate field.
President Ilham Aliyev said the second phase of Absheron, one of the largest offshore fields in the Caspian Sea, would increase Azerbaijan's gas production by around 5 billion cubic metres within three to four years.
"Oil and gas will continue to dominate our economy and to generate wealth, which will be reinvested," Aliyev told the Azerbaijan International Investment Forum. He said the non-oil sector now accounted for more than 70% of GDP, while oil and gas still made up more than 90% of exports.
Azerbaijan exports gas mainly to Europe and Turkey, with about half of its 25 billion cubic metres of exports last year going to EU countries. The expansion comes as disruptions to global energy supplies have heightened concerns over security of supply, although further growth in Azerbaijani exports to Europe would require additional pipeline capacity.
Socar and US energy major ExxonMobil signed a production-sharing agreement for the exploration, development and production of unconventional hydrocarbon resources in Azerbaijan's Middle Kura basin, with each company holding a 50% stake and ExxonMobil serving as operator.
Aliyev also said transit cargo volumes through the country are expected to reach 16 million metric tons this year, with a target of 25 million tons or more by 2030, while the government was negotiating with international companies, which it did not name, to develop data centres and AI in Azerbaijan.

title: REITs new gateway to real estate
description: REITs new gateway to real estate
content:
18 funds worth Rs2tr take shape as Pakistan seeks to formalise property market
Pakistan's real estate investment trust (REIT) sector is gaining traction, with 18 funds established and projects worth more than Rs2 trillion under development, according to Arif Habib Dolmen REIT Management Company CEO Muhammad Ijaz.
Speaking on a Tribune podcast, Ijaz said REITs could help formalise Pakistan's largely informal real estate sector while allowing investors with relatively modest capital to participate in property-related businesses.
He said the REIT framework addressed two major challenges associated with real estate investment – the need for substantial capital and the illiquidity of property assets.
Under the model, real estate assets are divided into units that can be purchased by investors, making participation possible for both small and large investors.
Ijaz said Dolmen City REIT, Pakistan's first REIT, had an asset value of around Rs22 billion when it was launched, with 2.2 billion units issued at Rs10 each. "Those who want to invest Rs5,000 can do so, and those who want to invest Rs5 billion can also do so," he said.
Explaining the regulatory framework, he said the title of REIT assets remained with the trustee, while investors held REIT units that effectively represented their ownership interest. Trustees are licensed entities, including the Central Depository Company (CDC) and Digital Custodian Company, while REIT management companies are responsible for managing the underlying business.
Ijaz said five REITs were currently listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange, with additional listings expected soon. Rental REITs are required to be listed within their first year, while developmental and hybrid REITs are required to be listed within three years, he said.
He distinguished between rental and developmental REITs, saying rental REITs generally acquire built-up properties and generate income by leasing them, while developmental REITs develop land or projects for sale or lease.
According to Ijaz, REITs are required to distribute 90% of distributable income to unit holders. He said Dolmen City REIT had initially offered a yield of around 10%, while its yield for investors who bought units at around Rs11 had subsequently risen substantially as the unit price increased.
He also highlighted the emergence of property-share schemes aimed at people who could not afford to purchase an entire apartment.
Under the model, investors can purchase a fractional share of a property. For example, a 1,800-square-foot apartment valued at Rs30 million could be divided into 100-square-foot shares worth Rs1.8 million each.
Ijaz said investors could accumulate additional shares over time and potentially sell them later. The model is being developed initially in Naya Nazimabad, with the ownership and rental arrangements managed through institutional and contractual structures.
He said the REIT sector was no longer confined to Karachi. Of the 18 REIT funds, 10 were in Karachi while eight were in Lahore and Islamabad. Projects include developments associated with Naya Nazimabad, Surjani Town, Lahore's Central Business District, Ravi Urban Development Authority and Rifah Medical City.
Ijaz said a 150-acre project in Surjani Town had been divided into two REIT funds, focusing on horizontal and vertical development, with emphasis on environmentally friendly urban development.
He argued that construction and real estate development could play a significant role in Pakistan's economic growth because the sector relied heavily on local labour and locally available raw materials.
However, he cautioned against speculative trading in property files, saying the sector needed greater professionalism, institutional participation and regulatory clarity.
Ijaz also called for greater availability of mortgage finance and institutional funding for professionally managed housing projects. He said "build-to-rent" could emerge as an important business model, allowing people to access professionally managed rental housing rather than bearing the financial and administrative burden of constructing their own homes.
He said Pakistan's real estate sector had significant potential if supported by better taxation policies, institutional investment and professional project management.
"Construction and real estate development should be kept in priority," Ijaz said, stressing that the sector could generate employment and stimulate economic activity across multiple industries.

title: Low exports  grower woes mar paddy season
description: Low exports  grower woes mar paddy season
content:
Secretary advocates safe use of pesticides, machine harvesting to reduce crop losses
Punjab Agriculture Secretary Shakeel Ahmad Mian on Saturday painted an optimistic picture of the province's paddy sector at a meeting of the Rice Management Committee, but the claims sit uneasily against a season marked by falling exports, persistent stubble burning and unresolved complaints from growers.
Chairing the meeting at the Civil Secretariat, Mian said paddy had been cultivated over 6.7 million acres this season and called Basmati rice "Punjab's identity," urging coordinated steps to improve its production, quality and exports. He directed officials to guide farmers on modern harvesting techniques, ensure safe use of pre-harvest pesticides and promote machine harvesting to reduce crop losses.
The official narrative, however, does not fully match the numbers coming out of the sector. According to the latest US Department of Agriculture's grain outlook, Pakistan's rice exports for the current marketing year are projected at 4.8 million tons, about 8% lower than last year.
The decline is attributed to a stronger rupee, costlier export financing, regulatory hurdles and intensifying competition from India, which has removed its minimum export price on Basmati. Basmati prices had averaged around $1,100 per ton through mid-year, but exportable stocks have been thinning since April.
On the environmental front, the secretary reiterated that the government's strategy to curb air pollution from crop-residue burning was being implemented "as formulated," and pointed to 10,000 subsidised super seeders distributed to farmers to encourage residue management over burning.
Independent estimates, though, suggest the scale of the problem remains large. Researchers tracking crop-residue burning in Pakistan's wheat-rice belt, which covers more than 80% of Punjab's cropped area, estimate that between 3.6 and 5 million tons of rice residue out of a total of 8.5 million tons are still burnt each winter, contributing to air quality that costs Pakistanis an average of 4.3 years of life expectancy.
A farmer associated with a growers' body in central Punjab, speaking on condition of anonymity, said that every year "we are told about subsidies and machines, but by the time paddy is ready, the wheat sowing deadline is already on our heads."
"Renting a super seeder or a harvester is not the same as owning one, and not every farmer can afford the wait," the grower said, adding that many still find burning residue faster and cheaper than alternatives.
Exporters, meanwhile, have separately flagged concerns over financing costs and competitiveness that go beyond what the provincial minister addressed. The Rice Exporters Association of Pakistan was urged by the secretary to play a more active role in expanding access to global markets, but the association's representatives at the meeting did not publicly respond to questions about the financing and currency pressures cited in trade data.

The Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (Smeda) and Daraz Pakistan will explore new avenues of collaboration to help Pakistani small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) build digital capabilities, expand their access to e-commerce and unlock new opportunities for growth.
The initiative aligns with Smeda's broader efforts under the Ministry of Industries' strategic direction to strengthen digital capabilities of SMEs, especially women entrepreneurship and inclusive SME development, in line with Pakistan's economic vision.

They also explored opportunities for Daraz to contribute its e-commerce expertise to the development of a specialised curriculum that could help entrepreneurs navigate the online selling journey.

The collaboration will also explore dedicated opportunities for women entrepreneurs, with a focus on helping more women-led businesses develop digital skills, market access and confidence needed to establish and grow their presence online.

Smeda is working to strengthen the capabilities of entrepreneurs through practical and accessible programmes and e-commerce will be an important part of this journey."
She said collaboration with industry leaders such as Daraz could help ensure that entrepreneurs receive relevant, market-oriented skills. title: CCOE weighs debt reduction
description: CCOE weighs debt reduction
content:
Delay in payments prevents Rs175b decrease in power-sector circular debt
The Power Division has said that the reduction in financial allocation by K-Electric has caused an increase in circular debt in the power sector.
The Ministry of Energy (Power Division) recalled that the Cabinet Committee on Energy (CCOE), in its meeting held on January 14, 2025, had directed the division to present figures of billing, collections and circular debt every quarter for its consideration.
It was informed in a recent meeting of the CCOE that the committee had also directed the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) to ensure the integrity of data contained in the report. It was pointed out that the circular debt report for January, February and March 2026 had been shared with Nepra and the Finance Division. Later, the Finance Division communicated that the dispute with K-Electric may be resolved under the relevant Nepra Act/regulations.
Meeting participants reviewed the performance of power distribution companies vis-a-vis Nepra targets and compared to last year. It noted that circular debt statistics as of the end of financial year 2025-26 had been finalised.
The Power Division submitted the verified data of circular debt for the third quarter (January-March 2026) and the full financial year 2025-26, which ended on June 30, for consideration of the CCOE.
During discussions, the division gave details of circular debt targets and the actual results by June 2026. It was highlighted that the circular debt position was positive as it stood at Rs1,798 billion, which was lower than the target of Rs1,802 billion, with a positive variance of Rs4 billion.
The actual gross flow of circular debt was Rs420 billion against the target of Rs400 billion, with a negative variance of Rs20 billion, while DISCOs' inefficiency, comprising transmission and distribution losses and under-recoveries, was calculated at Rs176 billion against the target of Rs254 billion, which reflected a favourable variance of Rs78 billion.
The energy committee was informed that the major factors constraining debt reduction were mainly the non-payment by K-Electric of Rs171 billion (CPPA-G invoice of Rs148 billion plus late payment surcharge of Rs23 billion), and the fuel cost power surcharge of Rs13 billion. Had full payments been received, the circular debt would have decreased by Rs175 billion.
The cabinet body on energy reiterated its directives to the Power Division to seek all organisational ways to improve the financial performance through improved operational efficiency and reduction in expenditures, particularly in the power sector, to slash the cost of electricity for consumers. The Power Division assured the committee that all necessary steps would be taken to address the circular debt.
The CCOE considered the circular debt report for January, February and March 2026 and the annual report for the year ended June 2026. It also examined a summary titled "Circular Debt Report for the months of January, February and March 2026" and directed the Power Division to expedite reforms to check future slippages and deficits in the sector.
After deliberations, the Ministry of Energy (Power Division) concurred that it would accelerate the pace of power-sector reforms.
