title: 12 killed  35 injured as TTP strikes anti smuggling checkpoint in K P s DI Khan
description: Rescue 1122 spokesperson says injured people shifted to hospitals
content:
K-P governor seeks report, says 'attack is a nefarious conspiracy by Fitna al-Hindustan'
At least 12 people were killed and 35 others injured when a blast struck a joint checkpoint near Aman Mela in the Darazinda area of Dera Ismail Khan on Saturday, with the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) claiming responsibility for the attack, police said.
Radio Pakistan reported that the blast was extremely powerful after a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device (VBIED) rammed into the checkpost.
Regional Police Officer (RPO) Ghulam Mubashir Maken said in a statement that 12 people were killed and 35 injured in the blast at the joint checkpoint.
One Customs official was among those killed while the remaining victims were civilians, he said, adding that no Pakistan Army or police personnel were among the deceased.
Makan said the dead included nine men, two women and a child.
Of the 35 injured, he said, 25 were referred to the District Headquarters Hospital in Dera Ismail Khan, while efforts were under way to provide immediate medical aid to the wounded and shift them to hospitals.
Reuters reported that the TTP claimed responsibility for Saturday’s attack.
K-P Inspector General of Police (IGP) Zulfikar Hameed, in a statement, said that the blast occurred at a “joint checkpoint established for anti-smuggling operations” near the Darazinda Aman Mela in DIK.
He said police, security forces and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) teams rushed to the site immediately after receiving information about the explosion.
"Police and CTD personnel cordoned off the area and launched a search and clearance operation," the IGP said, adding that evidence was being collected from the scene and efforts were underway to determine the nature and cause of the explosion.
Rescue 1122 spokesperson Bilal Ahmad Faizi said its Darazinda station team reached the site shortly after receiving information about the explosion and immediately launched relief and rescue operations.
"Additional ambulances and rescue personnel from Karak and Hangu have also reached the site to assist with the search and rescue operation," he added.
According to the emergency service, 18 injured people have so far been provided medical assistance and shifted to hospitals.
“The bodies of 11 people killed in the blast have also been recovered from the site,” Faizi said.
"Six Rescue 1122 ambulances, one firefighting vehicle, and more than 25 personnel are taking part in the rescue and relief activities at the site," the spokesperson added.
Meanwhile, a Rescue 1122 ambulance came under fire while transporting the bodies. According to the Rescue 1122 spokesperson, one person was killed and two others were seriously injured in the firing.
The ambulance came under fire near Daraban while it was transporting the injured from the blast site, he said.
The martyred rescue official was identified as Sharifullah, while Inis and Imtiaz sustained serious injuries, according to the spokesperson..
Despite coming under fire, rescue operations continued, including the transportation of the deceased and other emergency response activities in the area.
On the instructions of DIK Emergency Officer Muhammad Arif Khan, four additional ambulances along with rescue personnel were dispatched from DIK to assist in the emergency response and ensure the injured were provided immediate medical treatment and transported to hospitals.
K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi sought a report from senior officials regarding the blast.
“The attack is a nefarious conspiracy by Fitna al-Hindustan ,” Kundi said in a statement issued by his office.
Kundi also condemned the firing on Rescue 1122 personnel who were transporting the bodies of those martyred in the Darazinda attack, calling it “the height of brutality”.
The firing on Rescue 1122 personnel while they were transporting the bodies of those martyred in the Darazinda Aman Mela attack is the height of brutality. I pay tribute to the two Rescue officials who embraced martyrdom while carrying out their duty to save lives. I have…
In a post on X, the governor paid tribute to the two Rescue officials who were martyred while “carrying out their duty to save lives” while directing the authorities to provide the iunjured officials with every possible medical care.
Customs claims 15 personnel killed in DI Khan blast
Meanwhile, Pakistan Customs, in a statement, said 15 personnel of Pakistan Customs, Excise and Police were martyred in JCP Aman Mela checkpost attack.
According to the statement, a suicide attacker detonated an explosives-laden vehicle near the checkpost, triggering a massive fire at the post.
It said a second attack took place while relief and rescue teams were carrying out operations following the blast, leaving the drivers of rescue vehicles injured.
The injured personnel were immediately shifted for medical treatment, while a medical emergency was declared at the District Headquarters Hospital in Dera Ismail Khan, Pakistan Customs said.
President Asif Ali Zardari strongly condemned the blast in Dera Ismail Khan, expressing grief over the loss of precious lives in the attack.
“Targeting innocent citizens and law enforcement personnel in terrorism is highly condemnable,” he said.
صدرِ مملکت آصف علی زرداری کی ڈیرہ اسماعیل خان میں دہشتگرد حملےکی شدید مذمت۔ صدرِ مملکت آصف علی زرداری نے ڈیرہ اسماعیل خان میں پولیس چیک پوسٹ پر بم دھماکے کی شدید مذمت کی ہے۔ صدرِ مملکت نے دھماکے کے نتیجے میں معصوم قیمتی جانوں کے ضیاع پر گہرے دکھ اور افسوس کا اظہار کیا ہے۔ صدرِ…
He prayed for the elevation of the martyrs’ ranks and directed the relevant authorities to provide the injured with the best possible medical facilities and make relief efforts more effective.
The president also directed that operations against terrorists of Fitna al-Hindustan and Fitna al-Khawarij involved in “nefarious and brutal acts under foreign patronage” be made more effective.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also condemned the attack, expressing deep grief over the loss of precious lives in the blast.
“We will never let the sacrifices of the nation’s protectors in the fight against terrorism go in vain,” he said, adding that the government was determined to completely eradicate the menace of terrorism from the country.
The prime minister conveyed his condolences and sympathies to the families of those killed and prayed for the early recovery of those injured in the attack.
وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف نے ڈیرہ اسماعیل خان میں پولیس چیک پوسٹ پر دہشت گرد حملے کی مذمت کی ہے۔ وزیراعظم نے دھماکے میں قیمتی انسانی جانوں کے ضیاع پر گہرے دکھ اور افسوس کا اظہار کرتے ہوئے شہدا کے لواحقین سے دلی ہمدردی و اظہار تعزیت کیا اور زخمیوں کی جلد صحتیابی کے لیے دعا بھی کی۔… pic.twitter.com/TmArDtPnDY
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi strongly condemned the suicide attack.
In a statement issued by the ministry, Naqvi extended his heartfelt sympathies and condolences to the families of those martyred in the blast and prayed for the early recovery of those wounded in the explosion.
“The cowardly actions of the Khawarij cannot weaken the nation’s firm resolve against terrorism,” the interior minister vowed, noting that K-P remained on the frontline in the fight against terrorism.
"People from every segment of society have made countless sacrifices in the war against terrorism. We hold these sacrifices in the highest regard,” the federal minister stated.
The minister pledged that the sacrifice of security personnel and civilians "would not be forgotten".
وفاقی وزیر داخلہ محسن نقوی کی ڈیرہ اسماعیل خان کے علاقے میں انسدادِ سمگلنگ ’'امن میلہ پولیس چیک پوسٹ‘' پر خودکش حملے کی پرزور مذمت وزیر داخلہ کا دھماکے میں قیمتی انسانی جانوں کے ضیاع پر گہرے دکھ اور افسوس کا اظہار وزیر داخلہ کا شہداء کے لواحقین سے دلی ہمدردی و اظہار تعزیت
Naqvi strongly condemned the firing on the ambulance and expressed grief over the death of the rescue worker.
He extended his heartfelt sympathies and condolences to the family of the martyred official, saying the firing on an ambulance was an “extremely deplorable” incident.
“The brutal militants demonstrated the worst form of savagery,” Mr Naqvi said, adding that the firing on the ambulance could not be condemned strongly enough.
K-P Chief Minister Muhammad Sohail Afridi denounced the terrorist attack in Dera Ismail Khan and expressed deep remorse over the loss of lives in the blast.
In a video message, Afridi said the incident was not an isolated one, describing it as part of a “new wave of terrorism” in which Pakhtuns were being killed on a daily basis.
The chief minister said his government had previously raised concerns over “a policy of resettling terrorists”.
“We were sure that once again we would have to pick up bodies,” Afridi said, referring to the consequences of the policy. He said his government opposed decisions taken behind closed doors, arguing that their consequences ultimately affected the entire country.
“In the war against terrorism, our soldiers, police personnel and ordinary citizens are being martyred,” the chief minister said, expressing disdain.
Afridi further said that the same policy had been pursued for the past 22 years but had failed to establish lasting peace in K-P.
“We have repeatedly said that this policy needs to be changed, but our concerns are not being heard.”
The chief minister maintained that the provincial government was taking every possible step on its own to establish peace in the province.
He reiterated his condemnation of the Dera Ismail Khan attack and expressed solidarity with the families of those killed and affected by the blast.
وزیراعلیٰ خیبرپختونخوا @SohailAfridiISF کا ویڈیو پیغام: ”ڈی آئی خان میں دہشتگردی کے بزدلانہ حملے کی مذمت کرتے ہوئے وزیراعلیٰ نے کہا کہ ہمارے نوجوان، پولیس اہلکار، فوجی جوان اور عام شہری مسلسل شہید ہو رہے ہیں۔ گزشتہ 22 سال میں 22 بڑے اور 14 ہزار سے زائد چھوٹے آپریشنز کے باوجود… pic.twitter.com/N21EFXmcTC
K-P Information Minister Shafi Jan also decried the explosion.
In a statement, the minister called the incident “extremely tragic and condemnable” and condoled with the death of civilians.
“We stand with the families of those who lost their lives in this tragic incident and share their grief,” Jan said, while praying for the speedy recovery of those wounded.
“K-P police, security forces and the people of the province had made countless sacrifices in the fight against terrorism,” he said, adding that effective measures will be taken to eliminate terrorism and protect the lives and property of the people.
He also asserted that terrorists could not undermine the resolve of the people of K-P through their “nefarious designs”.
درازندہ ڈیرہ اسماعیل خان میں امن میلہ کے قریب چیک پوسٹ پر دھماکہ انتہائی افسوسناک اور قابلِ مذمت ہے، دھماکے کے نتیجے میں قیمتی انسانی جانوں کے ضیاع پر دلی افسوس ہے، شہید ہونے والوں کے اہل خانہ کے غم میں برابر کے شریک ہیں، زخمیوں کی جلد صحتیابی کے لیے دعاگو ہیں،زخمیوں کو بروقت طبی…
Former K-P chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur also expressed sorrow over the loss of precious lives in the attack, while extending his condolences to the families of the martyred personnel and civilians.
He prayed for the elevation of the martyrs’ ranks and patience for the bereaved families. Gandapur also prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured in the attack.
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari also condemned the terrorist attack in Dera Ismail Khan, saying the incident, following the recent bloodshed in Kohat, was a “painful reminder” of the terrorism threat confronting the country.
In a statement on X, he expressed condolences to the families of those killed and prayed for the recovery of the injured. “The nation stands firmly with our courageous police, law-enforcement agencies and security forces,” he said.
The terrorist attack in Dera Ismail Khan, following the recent bloodshed in Kohat, is another painful reminder of the terrorism threat Pakistan continues to confront. My deepest condolences to the families of our martyrs and prayers for the injured. The nation stands firmly with…
Bilawal said Pakistan had defeated terrorism in the past and would do so again, adding that terrorists, their facilitators, financiers and sponsors would be held accountable.
He further said that no territory beyond Pakistan’s borders would be allowed to serve as a sanctuary for terrorism against the country.
“We will neither be intimidated nor divided. Pakistan will prevail,” the PPP chairman said.
Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah also strongly condemned the blast.
He expressed deep concern over the deaths of police personnel, customs officials and civilians in the attack.
CM Shah conveyed his heartfelt condolences and sympathies to the families of those killed in the blast.
“Police and customs personnel who sacrifice their lives for the country and the nation are our pride. The entire nation stands with the security forces in the fight against terrorism,” Shah said.
He described those who target innocent civilians and dutiful security and government personnel as “enemies of humanity”, adding that such attacks would not weaken the country’s resolve against terrorism.
K-P has witnessed a significant rise in terrorist activities since last week, after 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred in a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation.
Later, the Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
In a separate incident, a captain and a lieutenant were among six security personnel martyred in an exchange of fire in Hangu district, while eight terrorists were killed.
Following a series of deadly attacks in K-P, Pakistan carried out “calibrated” air strikes against terrorist hideouts near the Afghan border and conducted intelligence-based ground operations that killed a total of 37 terrorists.
Pakistan’s air defence systems also shot down eight drones after they entered the country’s airspace from Afghanistan. Security sources said four of the drones were brought down in areas adjoining the Torkham border, while another four were shot down in mountainous areas near the border with Kohat.
Reacting to the attack, Pakistan carried out “precision” air and drone strikes against 10 locations in Afghanistan.

title: Pakistan suffer ASEAN Cup defeat
description: Poeiphimai hat trick gives Thailand 4 0 win in Pakistan   s historic tournament debut
content:
Poeiphimai hat-trick gives Thailand 4-0 win in Pakistan’s historic tournament debut
Pakistan began their historic FIFA ASEAN Cup campaign with a 4-0 defeat by Thailand on Saturday, with Teerasak Poeiphimai scoring a hat-trick to give his side a convincing victory.
Pakistan showed defensive discipline during the opening stages but struggled to contain a better-ranked Thailand.
Pakistan defended in numbers during a cagey opening half-hour, with Mohibullah making an important interception and Ali Raza producing a timely sliding tackle to keep Thailand at bay.
Goalkeeper Yousuf Butt also made a fine save as Thailand looked for an opening.
But Pakistan’s resistance was broken when Yousuf saved again, only for Poeiphimai to react quickest to the rebound and put Thailand ahead.
Thailand doubled their advantage ten minutes later after Pakistan captain Abdullah Iqbal misplaced a pass. Jude-Bell Soonsup capitalised on the mistake and finished from close range.
Thailand thought they had added a third soon afterwards, but the effort was ruled out for offside.
Pakistan made three changes at halftime, with Shayek Dost, Hayyan Khattak and Alamgir Ghazi coming on as coach Nolberto Solano sought a response.
The changes brought greater attacking intent, with full-backs Mohammad Fazal and Haris Ali Zeb pushing forward.
Pakistan came close when Abdul Samad Arshad’s shot narrowly wide, but Thailand struck again on the hour mark. Poeiphimai produced a looping volley to make it 3-0.
Veteran Kaleemullah Khan was introduced as Pakistan searched for a way back, but Thailand remained in control.
Poeiphimai completed his hat-trick six minutes from time after a defensive mix-up, calmly dinking the ball into the net.
The defeat leaves Pakistan needing to regroup quickly before their next Group B match against the Philippines on Tuesday.

Two sides agree to set up trade council, extend outcomes of earlier talks
China said on Saturday it had agreed with the United States on a $30 billion reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement and on launching a ​ dialogue on AI , under an eight-point consensus reached during President ‌Xi Jinping's visit to Washington .
The two sides have also agreed to set up a trade council and extend the outcomes of earlier talks in Kuala Lumpur, the Chinese ​Foreign Ministry said.
The agreement follows an earlier move by ​the world's two largest economies to extend by two months ⁠a trade truce that had been due to expire on November 10, ​allowing more time to work on a potentially bigger trade deal, US ​Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday.
Read: US, China buy time with trade truce as pressure builds
The three-day summit between Xi and President Donald Trump, which ended on Friday, showcased personal diplomacy rather than big public breakthroughs. ​Xi has since landed in Beijing, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported ​on Saturday.
On artificial intelligence, the two sides agreed to hold a dialogue on the technology's risks ‌and ⁠benefits, with the next round of discussions set for November, and to set up a communication channel for AI-related incidents, the Chinese Foreign Ministry said.

Beyond the economy, they also agreed to support each other in ​hosting the Asia-Pacific ​Economic Cooperation leaders' ⁠meeting and the Group of 20 summit, with both leaders planning to attend the gatherings hosted by ​the other, as Trump had earlier said in a ​social ⁠media post.
On foreign policy, the leaders agreed that Iran should fulfil its commitment not to develop nuclear weapons, and that no country or entity ⁠should ​impose transit tolls on international waterways, the ​ministry said.

title: One killed  two wounded as gunmen abduct 12 workers in Balochistan s Duki
description: SP Buzdar says initial information indicated that 10 of the abducted workers are from Punjab
content:
SP Buzdar says initial information indicated that 10 of the abducted workers are from Punjab
One private security guard was killed, two people were wounded and 12 workers were abducted when heavily armed assailants raided a construction company's base in the Palari area of Nana Sahib Ziarat in Duki district on Saturday, Duki Superintendent of Police (SP) Mansoor Ahmed Buzdar said.
According to Buzdar, the attackers stormed the site and opened fire, triggering a gunfight with the private security guards stationed there.
"During the exchange of fire, security guard Muhtajur-Rehman, who was originally from Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), suffered fatal bullet wounds," Buzdar said.
He added that another guard, Imran Wazir, and a local bystander, Latif Tareen, were also wounded and taken to a nearby medical facility for treatment.
"The attackers rounded up workers inside the camp and checked their identity cards before taking 12 labourers with them. Initial information indicated that 10 of the abducted workers were from Punjab, while two were ethnic Pashtuns," he said.
Buzdar said that the assailants also set fire to heavy construction machinery at the site before fleeing into the surrounding hills.
Security forces, including local police and Frontier Corps personnel, have cordoned off the area and launched a joint search operation across the district to locate the abducted workers and apprehend those responsible, according to the police.
Read: Security forces eliminate 16 Indian-sponsored terrorists in Balochistan IBOs: ISPR
Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022, and over the same period, TTP attacks increased more than sevenfold to 838 from 118.
Although K-P has borne the brunt of terrorism, Balochistan has also remained a major target of Indian proxies, which often target civilians and military installations in the province.
In one such attack on the last day of 2025, terrorists targeted innocent civilians in Balochistan’s Gwadar and Kharan districts, where 18 people, including women, children, the elderly and labourers, embraced martyrdom.
The forces continued operations across the provinces against what the state describes as Indian-sponsored terrorists and their proxies. Still, despite these efforts, the groups have continued to target civilian and defence installations.
Last month, in another such attack, at least 30 people, including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. The attackers also abducted several civilians and police personnel after the assault.
In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation , which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

title: Japan organisers  not satisfied  as empty seats blight Asian Games
description: The 100m sprints are one of the highlights of any Games
content:
The 100m sprints are one of the highlights of any Games
Asian Games organisers admitted on Saturday they were "not satisfied" with ticket sales after swathes of empty seats were seen at the main stadium and other venues in Japan.
The 100m sprints are one of the highlights of any Games, but the 30,000-capacity Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium appeared to be only about one-quarter full on Friday night for the blue-riband events.
Even the prospect of a women's pole vault gold for Japan's Misaki Morota could not pull in the home punters in big numbers at the start of the weekend.
The Aichi-Nagoya Games said that less than 60 percent of tickets had been snapped up for eight sports, including football, with a similar amount unsold for the closing ceremony in eight days' time.
"We are not satisfied," said Satoshi Murate, secretary-general of the Games organising committee in response to a question from AFP.
"We will keep aiming for full stadiums, keep selling tickets and work to make sure people who have secured seats actually come."
He said more than 90 percent of tickets were sold for the opening ceremony a week ago, but blamed no-shows for large sections of empty seats greeting the parading athletes and lighting of the Games torch.
"Overall I think sales are strong," he said.
"But it has been pointed out that there are noticeable empty seats at some competitions.
"There are several reasons. First, some sessions include several matches in one day. Everyone focuses on the headline match."
He said tickets that had been given away to Games stakeholders, such as sponsors, were not always used.
"Seats have been allocated but some people can't come.
"As a result, some competitions do have noticeable empty seats, and we find that regrettable."
Murate also apologised for mix-ups with accommodation and transport.
Several teams have rounded on the organisers with Thailand likening it to a "chaotic" game of "musical chairs" and South Korea saying "they deserve a failing grade."
The biggest issue has been a shortage of rooms for the 17,000 participants, a problem compounded by delays at airports and hours-long waits to board a cruise ship acting as a floating hotel.
No traditional athletes' village has been built, as a cost-cutting measure.
Teams have instead been staying in temporary container-style huts, hotels and the Costa Serena cruise ship.
Erratic transport services have seen competitors' buses to training and venues turning up late or, in some cases, not at all.
"There have been mistakes in accommodation and transport, for various reasons," admitted Murate.
"Whatever the cause, AINAGOC (the organising committee) is responsible for providing the service and I sincerely apologise for the mistakes.
"Our staff work every day to identify the causes of each mistake and make sure they don't happen again."

title: Alcaraz helps Team Europe take 3 1 Laver Cup lead
description: World No  3 is competing in his second tournament after the US Open
content:
World No. 3 is competing in his second tournament after the US Open
Team Europe took a 3-1 lead over defending champions Team World ​on the opening day of the Laver Cup on Friday, with Carlos Alcaraz and Jakub Mensik closing out ‌the night with a straight sets doubles victory at The O2.
World No. 3 Alcaraz, competing in his second tournament after the US Open following a four-month injury layoff, joined Mensik to beat Alexander Bublik and Taylor Fritz 6-4 6-4.
The Spaniard and Czech, who also partnered at last year's Laver Cup in San Francisco, fended off ​three early break points before Alcaraz found his range and fired an overhead smash to secure the first break.
They ​broke again early in the second set and held firm from there, with Mensik serving out the ⁠match, with Alcaraz sealing victory at the net.
"I'm just trying to have fun in every place that I go and on every court ​that I play on," Alcaraz said.
"I don't usually play doubles ... I just try to enjoy and be better at things. I use ​doubles to try and improve my tennis, a couple of adjustments. Having a partner like Jakub, it's really easy to have fun on the court."
The victory gave Europe three points from Friday's four matches, after Norwegian Casper Ruud got them off to a winning start by edging Francisco Cerundolo 6-7(4) 6-4 ​10-8.
Brandon Nakashima levelled the contest for Team World by beating Mensik 6-1 3-6 10-7, before Rafael Jodar restored Europe's lead with ​a commanding 6-2 6-3 victory over Alexander Bublik in the Spaniard's Laver Cup debut.
Jodar, who was watched from the stands by Roger Federer and John ‌McEnroe, ⁠said he was thrilled to have the tennis greats at his first appearance in the competition.
"It's a pleasure that they are in the stands watching me," Jodar said. "It's a pleasure to see them watching these types of matches."
Earlier on Friday, Ruud and Cerundolo were locked in a tight opening set, with neither player able to break before the Argentine edged the tiebreak 7-4.
Ruud responded by breaking for a ​5-4 lead in the second ​set which he claimed before forcing the ⁠match tiebreak, where the Norwegian held his nerve after the players traded points until 8-8.
"I have to thank my team and my bench. They pushed me all the way. They kept me in ​it, really ... Europe can build on this," Ruud said.
Nakashima then produced a composed performance on his ​Laver Cup debut, ⁠racing to a 5-0 lead against Mensik before the Czech fought back to take the second set, leaving the American to wrap up victory in the match tiebreak.
"This guy... I'm not convinced he's real. I think he's AI," Team World captain Andre Agassi said, praising Nakashima's ability ⁠to stay ​calm under pressure. "He just goes about his business point after point after point."
The ​three-day Laver Cup pits six players from Europe against six from the rest of the world, with victories worth one point on Friday, two on Saturday and three ​on Sunday.
The first team to reach 13 points wins the title.

content: Members of the Makkah Defence Alliance and Iran on Monday agreed to continue further dialogue in an effort to ramp up cooperation for regional peace and security after a high-level meeting in Tehran. "The participants agreed to continue the dialogue to strengthen cooperation amongst the four regional countries, including for peace and security in the region," said a statement issued by Iran's Press TV after the meeting concluded. A senior Iranian official said the meeting was initiated by Pakistan during CDF Munir's visit to Tehran, as he met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and other senior officials. During the visit, Iranian officials told him there would be no talks with Washington until Tehran's demands were met, according to Iranian media. Earlier ​mediation efforts involving both Pakistan and Qatar helped produce an interim peace agreement in June, but the deal quickly unravelled as fighting between Iran and the United States resumed weeks later. The ​deputy secretary of Iran's top security body, Ali Baqeri-Kani, told state TV that Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid, Pakistan's Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin would visit Tehran for consultations with Iran’s Supreme National Security ‌Council on ⁠regional security. title: Iran says US ‘not serious’ about talks, rejects claims over nuclear programme
description: Foreign ministry spox Esmaeil Baghaei says regional security talks must address US aggression, Israeli expansionism
content: Iran accused the US on Monday of lacking seriousness in negotiations, saying Washington has repeatedly confused diplomacy with imposing demands on Tehran. “The American side is not serious about negotiations,” Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said during his weekly news conference, as cited by the state-run IRNA news agency. He accused Washington of repeatedly making false claims, recalling that US President Donald Trump had expressed support for negotiations shortly before the US military attacks on Iran in June 2025. “What do you call this? Do you see any goodwill in this approach?” he asked. Baghaei said Tehran had not received any new European proposal for negotiations beyond a political statement, criticising Britain, France and Germany for their positions during the conflict. He accused the three countries of following Washington’s lead on the restoration of UN sanctions and failing to condemn military attacks against Iran. No nuclear weapons Baghaei reiterated that Iran had never possessed nuclear weapons or sought to acquire them, accusing Washington of using allegations about Tehran’s nuclear programme to justify military action. He said Iran had negotiated in good faith and signed the 2015 nuclear agreement, but the US withdrew from it three years later. The spokesman accused the US administration of being influenced by Israeli claims about Iran’s nuclear programme, describing allegations that Tehran was developing a nuclear bomb as a justification for military aggression. Missing Iranian pilots Baghaei said Iran continued to hold Qatar responsible for clarifying the fate of three Iranian pilots whose aircraft were hit in the Gulf country. “Until we have evidence of their deaths or receive precise information and documentation, we assume that the country where their aircraft were hit must be held accountable,” he said. He added that Tehran was pursuing the matter in coordination with its military leadership and through technical delegations and legal discussions. Baghaei also confirmed that a Qatari delegation recently visited Tehran, saying the trip involved bilateral cooperation and regional mediation efforts. He described such visits as normal during regional conflicts, noting that Qatar had sought to convey messages and present its positions. Commenting on Israel’s upcoming elections and threats of military action against Iran, Baqaei accused Israeli politicians of competing over who could commit more crimes. “It makes no difference to us who takes charge of a regime with a history of violence and killings,” he said. Russia visit The spokesman confirmed that President Masoud Pezeshkian would travel to Russia on Monday night to attend a summit of gas-exporting countries. He said the visit would provide opportunities to strengthen energy cooperation with Moscow and hold consultations with other major energy-producing countries. Baghaei also addressed border-related difficulties with Pakistan and Iraq, saying discussions with Islamabad were progressing positively. He said Pakistan had described the issue as technical while also raising security concerns, including reports of planned attacks. Regarding Iraq, he said Iranian diplomatic missions were pursuing the matter, warning that US pressure on Baghdad could harm the Iraqi population and bilateral relations. Baghaei said Iran summoned the Italian ambassador on Sunday to express concern over the authorities’ handling of protests in European countries. He accused France, Belgium and Italy of using excessive force and restricting the right to protest, saying such measures were inconsistent with their human rights obligations. The French ambassador had also been summoned previously, he added. Saudi Arabia and Yemen On the conflict involving Saudi Arabia and Yemen, Baqaei said regional security was interconnected and instability in one country could affect others. He stressed that the dispute should be resolved between Saudi Arabia and Yemen, reiterating Tehran’s readiness to help facilitate a settlement. “Military approaches make problems more complicated and cause extensive damage,” he said, expressing hope that Saudi Arabia would pursue a negotiated solution. Tensions between Washington and Tehran have persisted since the US and Israel launched military attacks on Iran on February 28, triggering a regional conflict and disrupting shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. On June 18, Trump and Pezeshkian signed a Pakistan-mediated memorandum of understanding, aimed at ending hostilities, reopening the strategic waterway and paving the way for a broader agreement. However, disagreements over the implementation of the understanding, including the US naval blockade, sanctions and navigation through the strait, have continued to hinder diplomatic efforts. Earlier this month, Iran said restoring security to the Strait of Hormuz remained central to negotiations with Washington, insisting that the US must take specific steps to resolve the standoff. Baghaei also said the meeting between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Iran would tackle the US war on Iran as well as Israel's "expansionist policies" and turmoil in Lebanon, according to Press TV. In a press briefing, he said that the CDF "had proposed holding a four-country meeting." “Iran agreed to the four-country meeting following Field Marshal Asim Munir’s proposal,” Baghaei said. Baghaei said that the meeting between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, Iran and Pakistan would mark the first talks between Iran and the three Makkah Pact countries since they signed the agreement in August, according to IRNA. “Naturally, the meeting is expected to address the most important issues affecting regional security, including the Zionist regime’s expansionism, developments in the occupied Palestinian territories, and the areas surrounding Lebanon. Such a meeting cannot take place without considering the implications of the US military aggression against Iran for security across the region. This, too, is an important issue that should be addressed in this context,” he said. Baqaei: Tehran meeting to focus on endogenous securityhttps://t.co/g6GwogtXd6 pic.twitter.com/J5iv1Eqn5g — IRNA News Agency ☫ (@IrnaEnglish) October 26, 2026 He said the meeting could pave the way for further steps toward establishing a regional security framework based on the interests and priorities of regional countries, according to IRNA. “This meeting could pave the way for further steps toward establishing an indigenous security framework, a goal we have consistently advocated for decades, stressing that regional security can only be ensured by relying on the will and security considerations of the countries in the region themselves,” he said. No European proposal received on negotiations The spokesperson said Tehran had received no specific proposal from European officials while responding to a question about Iran’s readiness to negotiate with European countries that have called for diplomacy, according to IRNA. “We have not received any proposal, except for the political statement they issued. Regarding the importance of negotiations, we have not yet received any specific proposal from European officials either,” he said. Asked whether European countries had placed greater emphasis on diplomacy, Baghaei said, “I am not sure we can call it a change in approach. It could be a political gesture.” He pointed to European countries' refusal to explicitly condemn the US-Israeli aggression against Iran. “Instead, they took a stance implying support for the aggression or at least appeasement and inaction toward it. This behaviour is not acceptable at all,” Baghaei said, expressing hope that European countries would assess developments in West Asia more realistically. Opportunity for gas exporters to consult in Pezeshkian's Russia visit Baghaei said that Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s visit to Russia to attend the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) summit on Tuesday would be an opportunity for energy suppliers, particularly gas exporters, to hold talks and consultations. The visit would also be important as it would include President Pezeshkian’s bilateral meetings with his counterparts attending the summit, according to IRNA. Winner of Israeli elections unimportant for Iran Regarding Israeli officials’ claims ahead of Knesset elections that Iran might launch a preemptive military strike to disrupt the vote, Baghaei said that it made no difference to Iran who led the Israeli regime, as the elections were merely a competition among different groups to commit greater atrocities. “I do not think there are elections there in the true sense of the word. What is actually taking place is a competition among different factions to commit more mischiefs. It is a race among individuals, each trying to prove that they can commit more crimes, aggression and killings than the others.” “Therefore, it makes no difference to us who ultimately takes the helm of the Israeli regime in this climate and through these elections,” he further said, adding that the regime’s history shows that it has brought nothing to the region but violence and killings. Baghaei added that the Israeli regime’s frequent threats against others, which he described as stemming from desperation, and its rhetoric were part of its mischief. “The Zionist regime is highly skilled at carrying out false-flag operations.” Accusations against Iran show desperation Asked about accusations by the Albanian government that Iran interfered in their country's ongoing protests, Baghaei said the protests stemmed from public opposition to corruption, mismanagement, and the transfer of the country’s land to foreign businesspeople. “Accusing Iran and Russia of interference under such circumstances implies that the two countries oppose corruption in Albania. If that is the basis for these accusations, then it is a source of credit for us to stand in support of those who oppose corruption,” he said. “These empty threats and boasts are a sign of desperation. They demonstrate no strength or authority; they only further undermine the credibility of those making them in the eyes of regional public opinion and the Iranian people,” he added. Baghaei also addressed other issues raised by reporters at his press conference, according to IRNA. He reaffirmed Iran's support for the Lebanese people and said that Iran would spare no effort in strengthening capacities in "various fields in Lebanon", IRNA reported him as saying. Regarding elections in Serbia, Baghaei said that Iran respected the choice made by the majority of people in any country that held elections. He said that Iran and Iraq were seriously pursuing these issues, which will "hopefully be resolved soon", as per IRNA. He added that both sides should focus on their nations’ interests, particularly as Iraqi officials themselves have pointed to US pressure, according to IRNA's coverage. Iran expressed solidarity with the Cuban people in the face of increasing US pressure and its economic blockade. Washington is exerting pressure only because the Cuban people seek independence and want to choose their own system of government. He also said that Iran summoned the Italian and French ambassadors to Tehran to express its concern over widespread human rights violations during recent protests in several European countries, and criticised institutions which claimed to defend human rights for remaining silent about violations by European governments, according to IRNA. Additionally, regarding the Brazilian elections, he said that the Brazilian people showed that they do not give in to pressure and choose what is in their country’s interests. Other issues raised at the press conference included the fate of the Iranian pilots in Qatar, Iran’s nuclear programme and the allegations of Iran pursuing a nuclear weapon, the Iranian Armed Forces’ readiness to defend the country, and the Yemen-Saudi Arabia war. Meanwhile, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Monday that the Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir is visiting Tehran today on an official visit. In an interview carried by ISNA, he is reported to have said that Saudi Arabia's Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, CDF Munir, and Turkish Intelligence Chief Ibrahim Kalin will "attend a joint meeting during their trip to Tehran". Ali Bagheri, Deputy Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, announced that senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey will travel to Tehran as part of efforts to implement the idea of endogenous security in West Asia. pic.twitter.com/XU0ByEdsJv — IRNA News Agency ☫ (@IrnaEnglish) October 26, 2026 "Asim Munir had previously announced their meeting with the Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council during his encounter with Lieutenant General Mohsen Rezaei." باقری: خالد بن سلمان وزیر دفاع عربستان، عاصم منیر فرمانده ارتش پاکستان و ابراهیم کالین رئیس دستگاه اطلاعاتی ترکیه در سفر به تهران در نشستی مشترک حضور خواهند داشت؛ عاصم منیر در دیدار با سرلشکر محسن رضایی از دیدار آنها با دبیر شورای عالی امنیت ملی خبر داده بود pic.twitter.com/HtOblyE5ta — خبرگزاری ایسنا (@isna_farsi) October 26, 2026 Israel’s Netanyahu clashes with army chief over Iran-linked operation ahead of election Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Army Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir clashed over a proposed military operation that could trigger fighting with Iran ahead of Israel’s election, Channel 12 reported on Sunday. Zamir requested a detailed discussion and signed legal authorisation from political leaders before carrying out their instructions, the broadcaster said. It did not disclose the nature of the operation. The report cited military concerns that the political leadership could exploit tensions with Iran for electoral gain before the October 27 parliamentary vote. A security official warned that the operation could rapidly escalate into a confrontation with Iran and lead to a miscalculation at a particularly sensitive time. Netanyahu denied any dispute with Zamir during an interview with Israel’s Channel 14 later Sunday. “There is no confrontation,” he said. Also Read: Trump rules out Sunday military strikes on Iran Political officials also rejected the claim that the Iranian issue was being used for electoral purposes, according to Channel 12. In the same interview, Netanyahu said he had instructed the Mossad intelligence agency and the military to work toward toppling Iran’s government. Channel 12 did not establish whether the undisclosed operation was connected to those instructions. Netanyahu also claimed Iran had resumed its nuclear programme and portrayed the election as a matter of Israel’s survival. Earlier on Sunday, he posted an AI-generated image of a nuclear explosion over Tel Aviv alongside a warning about Iran obtaining nuclear weapons. Opposition party leaders Gadi Eisenkot and Yair Golan accused him of spreading fear and panic before the vote. Trump reiterates his endorsement of Netanyahu, urges Israel to ‘finish the job’ in Iran US President Donald Trump on Sunday reaffirmed his strong support for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, urging Israelis to re-elect him in the upcoming election and calling for Israel to press ahead with its military campaign against Iran until it is completed. In a post on his Truth Social platform, he referred to an endorsement letter he published on October 18, praising Netanyahu as an “outstanding Warrior Prime Minister” and emphasising their close relationship in military operations against Iran. https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/117504022227510179 “As everyone is aware, including the enemy, Bibi and I have had a great relationship in winning together,” Trump wrote, citing the US military operation against Iran, dubbed Operation Epic Fury, as an example. Trump claimed that Iran had lost its navy and air force and that its military and economy were in disarray. He also said Iran's inflation had reached 301% and that a naval blockade had prevented the country from exporting oil. He further claimed that two levels of Iran's leadership, both military and civilian, had been eliminated. Urging Israeli voters to support Netanyahu, he said: “Vote for Bibi Netanyahu for Prime Minister. We have to finish the job that we started!” In his October 18 letter to the Israeli public, Trump described Netanyahu as a “Great Warrior Prime Minister” and an “even greater Partner for Peace” in confronting Iran, referring to what he called Iran's decades-long threats against Israel and the US.

title: Houthis say they attacked East-West oil pumping stations; no Saudi confirmation
description: Saudis say Riyadh airport partly reopens despite renewed Houthi threats
content: The Houthi ​group in Yemen said ‌on Monday it had attacked Saudi Arabia's East-West crude ​oil pumping stations ​and Riyadh airport, but there ⁠was no immediate ​Saudi confirmation. The Saudi-led coalition in ​Yemen said earlier it had destroyed two ballistic missile launchers in ​the capital Sanaa, ​including one used to fire a ‌missile ⁠towards Riyadh that the coalition said it had intercepted. The Houthis have been ​firing ​ballistic ⁠missiles and drones at Saudi airports, ports ​and oil installations, ​turning ⁠US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point ⁠in ​the wider war. Saudis say Riyadh airport partly reopens despite renewed Houthi threats Saudi Arabia said its main airport resumed operations at two terminals ​on Sunday even as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis vowed to keep striking the facility, which they called a "military target". King ‌Khalid International Airport in Riyadh had halted operations on October 10 following an attack claimed by the Houthis that killed 13 people, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade. Saudi Arabia said it intercepted another wave of missiles and drones on Sunday as fighting with the militant group continued unabated. The Houthis ​said they had launched attacks on the air hub among other sites in the kingdom, including in Khamis Mushait ​and Jazan. It was not immediately clear if those were the strikes the kingdom said it had ⁠blocked. The conflict has become an increasingly destabilising element in the US-Israeli offensive against Iran, turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure ​point in the wider war. Flight tracking data shows little traffic After Saudi authorities announced the partial resumption of operations at the airport, Houthi ​military spokesperson Yahya Saree vowed the facility would "never be safe" and urged airlines, airport staff and travellers not to use it. Late on Saturday, the airport said it would designate Terminal 1 for domestic flights and Terminal 2 for international flights operated by national carriers starting Sunday. Despite the announcement, Flightradar24 data showed little traffic at the airport on Sunday. The Saudi-led coalition said earlier this month that the Houthis had ​carried out 20 attacks on the airport between October 1 and 11. Missile and drone attacks continue Saudi civil defence said on Sunday that shrapnel from ‌the interception ⁠of two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis over Khamis Mushait and Ahad Rafidah injured two people and damaged residential buildings and vehicles. Civil defence authorities earlier issued emergency alerts for Riyadh and the cities of Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran on Sunday, before saying minutes later that the danger had passed. The coalition said two drones and a ballistic missile were launched towards Riyadh, and a ​cruise missile towards the southern city ​of Khamis Mushait. It ⁠later said it intercepted 10 ballistic missiles fired towards southern Saudi Arabia. The Houthis said they attacked the airport and Saudi oil facilities on Saturday. Saudi authorities did not comment directly on the Houthi statements. Saudi ​Arabia has stepped up its strikes against the Houthis after the group seized strategic territory along ​the Red Sea ⁠coast last month, closing in on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait – a global maritime chokepoint and shipping route for Gulf oil producers on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula to the Strait of Hormuz. The renewed fighting in Yemen has shattered a UN-brokered truce that had largely ⁠held since ​2022. Saudi Arabia intervened in Yemen's civil war in 2015 at the head ​of a coalition supporting the internationally recognised government, after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa a year earlier.

title: Pakistan condemns 'reprehensible' Houthi attacks in Makkah, Madinah regions
description: FO says Oct 24 attacks in vicinity of holy sites 'blatant disregard of sanctity', safety of civilians
content: Pakistan on Monday strongly condemned "reprehensible" Houthi ballistic missile attacks on October 24 which targeted the Makkah and Madinah regions of Saudi Arabia, including areas in the vicinity of the holy sites, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said. In a statement on X, the Foreign Office stated that the attacks constituted "a grave violation of Saudi Arabia's sovereignty and territorial integrity." It added that the attacks demonstrated "a blatant disregard for the sanctity of Islam's holiest sites and the safety of civilians." On October 24, Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence briefly issued alerts warning of potential danger in Taif and Yanbu, as well as the holy city of Makkah and its second-largest city Jeddah. A Saudi-led ​coalition fighting Yemen's ‌Houthis said it destroyed two ballistic missiles fired ​by the ​group towards Taif and Yanbu, as fighting between the sides continued. The Houthis and Yemen's internationally recognised government, which is backed by ​a Saudi-led coalition, have been trading attacks since the group advanced in September ​towards territory near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a shipping chokepoint at the ⁠mouth of the Red Sea. "Pakistan reiterates its unwavering solidarity with the kingdom of Saudi Arabia," the FO said, noting its "firm commitment to the Makkah alliance." The statement further reiterated Islamabad's "steadfast support for the security, stability and defence" of Saudi Arabia, "including the protection of the two holy mosques, against any external aggression or threat." "Pakistan also commends the vigilance and efficiency of Saudi air defence forces in countering the attacks," the FO concluded. 🔊 PR No. 3️⃣0️⃣9️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Pakistan Strongly Condemns Houthi Missile Attacks on Saudi Arabia 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/mtZtB5f1j7 — Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Pakistan (@ForeignOfficePk) October 26, 2026 Earlier this month, the FO strongly condemned an attack by the Houthis on the Taibah power distribution station in Madinah on September 29, saying the "reprehensible attack" on civilian infrastructure supplying electricity to the Holy Prophet's (PBUH) Mosque was a “grave provocation.” The FO said the attack was a matter of “deep concern and anguish” for millions of Muslims worldwide, emphasising that the “sanctity of the Two Holy Mosques and the safety of worshippers and pilgrims must be respected under all circumstances.” Pakistan called for an immediate and unconditional end to reckless actions, saying they also constituted a grave threat to regional peace and security. Read: Makkah pact ratification completed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia: FO The condemnations came following the September 2025 Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, which established a framework for joint defence, and the subsequent trilateral Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed on August 7 involving Turkiye. According to the Makkah agreement, an armed attack against any one of the three signatory states would be regarded as an attack against all three, establishing a framework for collective deterrence and expanded defence cooperation. The agreement has since been followed by efforts to translate its commitments into closer military coordination. In September, senior military commanders from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye met in Riyadh to review the regional security situation and discuss intelligence sharing, military coordination and the integration of defence capabilities.

title: After Vucic defeat, Serbia waits to learn how student-backed leaders will govern
description: Student-backed candidates won 52.7% of votes, ahead of Vucic's alliance on 39.2%, with 99% counted
content: Serbia woke to a new era on Monday after a student-backed protest movement unseated longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic in a historic landslide election that sparked nationwide celebrations, although few had an idea of how they would govern. Tens of thousands took to the streets of Belgrade and other cities and towns across Serbia after Vucic conceded defeat late on Sunday, capping two years of peaceful anti-government protests calling for the populist ruler to step down. With almost 99% of votes counted, the students' candidates had secured a commanding 52.7% of the vote, according to the State Election Commission, versus 39.2% for Vucic's Serbia Progressive Party (SNS)-led alliance. That gives the students 139 seats in the 250-seat parliament, leaving the SNS alliance with 97, and the remainder held by minority parties. The constitution allows up to 90 days for the creation of a government, once the parliament is convened after the announcement of final results by the State Election Commission. "I thought it was unbelievable, I still do not believe it. It was too long, and (Vucic) was pressuring us for a long, long time," said university administrator Marijana Radovanovic Pajovic. Vucic dominated Serbian politics as prime minister or president from 2014. But he was swept from power by a list of student-backed candidates born out of anti-corruption protests following the deaths of 16 people in the collapse of a train station canopy in the city of Novi Sad. Profound political shift The students' win marks a profound political shift in the country of some 6 million people and is reminiscent of the defeat of Hungary's Viktor Orban in April. It may also offer inspiration to other student movements that have cropped up across Europe in recent weeks demanding better education standards and prospects. Read More: Lula says bus cuts hinder voters in Brazil While the students' candidates include university professors, actors and farmers, the movement is without a leader - a strategy employed during protests to avoid any smear attempts by the government. It is unclear who will become prime minister and assume other key positions in order to enact the students' domestic agenda, which aims to root out graft and improve schooling, and manage the country's place on the international stage. "This corruption that has entered into all pores of our lives...of course it will change, we are hoping we will slowly go into that direction of a normal community," said 60-year-old insurance worker Svetlana Karagkozidou. Prominent figures include the head of the students' candidate list, cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic, former central bank governor Dejan Soskic and Radomir Sajcic, a professor at Belgrade University, who spoke on behalf of the students following their victory. However, not everyone welcomed the change. "Changing the country like that so suddenly and all at once, I don't like it. I don't even know who is standing behind, who those people are, who will be leading the country," said 60-year-old civil worker Senka Radakovic. Meanwhile, supporters of the student movement set about cleaning up a park near the parliament building in Belgrade that had long been used as a camp by Vucic's supporters. They removed metal barricades and tents and cleaned stickers off children's play equipment. "I think it is one of Belgrade's most beautiful parks, that they took from us for a year or a year-and-a-half, and this is the least we can do right now," said one of the cleaning volunteers, Filip Beselinovic. Vucic and the SNS repeatedly denied accusations of repression and corruption.

title: Pakistan rejects ‘baseless’ civilian casualty claims by Afghan Taliban
description: FO says regime must stop its soil being used for terrorist attacks in Pakistan, reaffirms right to self-defence
content: Pakistan on Monday rejected what it called “baseless and unsubstantiated allegations regarding civilian casualties attributed to its counter-terrorism operations”, reaffirming its right to take necessary measures to defend its sovereignty and protect its citizens against terrorism originating from Afghan soil. Last month, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar stated that Pakistan had carried out “precision” aerial and drone strikes against 10 locations in Afghanistan after drones launched from Afghan territory entered Pakistani airspace, describing the strikes as a response to a “deliberate and unlawful incursion”. The development came amid fighting ​between Pakistan and Afghanistan that started in October 2025. Islamabad accuses the Afghan Taliban of harbouring ⁠militants ​who launch attacks in Pakistan, ​although Kabul denies this, calling the militancy its neighbour's domestic problem. In a statement posted on X, the Foreign Office (FO) said disinformation and misleading narratives would neither obscure the threat posed by terrorist networks operating from Afghanistan nor absolve the Afghan Taliban regime of its responsibility to prevent Afghan territory from being used to plan and launch attacks against Pakistan. It added that such attacks had resulted in more than 3,500 casualties in 2026 alone. Read More: Pakistan refutes former US envoy's 'unsubstantiated' allegations of arming Afghans to fight Taliban The FO called on the international community to “hold the Taliban regime accountable for its failure to uphold its obligations under relevant UN Security Council resolutions and other related commitments to prevent Afghan soil from being used as a launchpad for terrorism”. It also reiterated Pakistan’s right to “take all necessary measures in order to safeguard its sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the safety and security of Pakistani nationals”. Citing reports by relevant UN mechanisms, including the Monitoring Team, the FO said the Taliban regime continued to shelter a large number of terrorist organisations with impunity, a situation it described as a serious concern for the international community. These organisations included the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Fitna al-Khawarij, the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and Fitna al-Hindustan, along with their affiliates, the statement said. It added that the groups continued to pose a serious threat to regional and international peace and stability. 🔊 PR No. 3️⃣0️⃣8️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Pakistan Rejects Baseless Allegations by the Afghan Taliban Regime, Reaffirms Right to Self-Defence Against Terrorism 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/O8e7sNkzQ9 — Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Pakistan (@ForeignOfficePk) October 26, 2026 The FO further said thousands of Pakistanis had been martyred in terrorist attacks planned, financed, supported and carried out from Afghan soil, with the alleged involvement and facilitation of the Afghan Taliban regime. “No responsible state can remain passive when its civilians and security forces are repeatedly targeted,” the statement said. It added that Islamabad’s actions in response to such attacks were undertaken in exercise of its right to self-defence, in accordance with the principles of necessity and as a measure of last resort. The FO maintained that the actions had been directed “only and exclusively against terrorists and their logistical support bases in Afghanistan”. It also said Pakistan’s response had been proportionate to the level of threat and had strictly adhered to the principles of distinction and precaution. It added that the scale and scope of the action reflected restraint, particularly given the severity and frequency of terrorist attacks faced by the country. “Pakistan rejects any insinuations otherwise,” the statement said. Amid continued tensions between the neighbours, Operation Ghazab Lil Haq was launched around the end of February following renewed clashes along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border, after Afghan Taliban forces fired on multiple locations, prompting swift military retaliation by Pakistan. The clashes intensified after Afghanistan launched a border offensive in response to Pakistani air strikes targeting terrorist positions. The two sides had agreed to a week-long ceasefire on the eve of Eidul Fitr on March 18, following requests from Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Qatar. Pakistan in April put forth three core demands to the Afghan Taliban during peace talks in Urumqi, China, including Kabul formally declaring the TTP a terrorist organisation, dismantling its infrastructure, and providing verifiable proof of the action. These demands form the basis of Pakistan's negotiating position, which sources say has hardened amid persistent security concerns.

title: Former army chief Abdul Waheed Kakar passes away in Rawalpindi: ISPR

content: Chief of Army Staff (COAS) and Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Field Marshal Asim Munir on Monday expressed deep sorrow over the passing of former COAS (Retd) General Abdul Waheed Kakar who passed away in Rawalpindi, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said. According to the military's media wing, CDF Munir, along with all ranks of the Pakistan Army, paid tribute "to the late general's distinguished military career, leadership and invaluable services to the Pakistan Army." "The Pakistan Army shares the grief of the bereaved family and offers its heartfelt condolences," the ISPR said, adding, "May Allah Almighty grant the departed soul highest the place in Jannah and give the family strength and patience, Ameen." title: Netanyahu faces reckoning for October 7 in Israel's first vote since attack
description: Opponents see election as an opportunity to ​hold Netanyahu responsible for the worst security failure in generations
content: Gal Cohen walks along a memorial wall engraved with the names of the men, women and children slain in the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack on his kibbutz. For him, the idea that the man leading Israel, then and since, may be ​re-elected on Tuesday is painful. One-in-ten residents of his kibbutz, Be'eri, were among the 1,200 people killed in Hamas' surprise attack. Dozens were among the 251 taken hostage to ‌Gaza. It was Israel's deadliest single day. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu should have taken responsibility and stepped down, said Cohen, 61, and the fact that he has fulfilled a full term in office is a slap in the face. Tuesday's election, he said, is critical for Israel. Read: Israel elections to be held on October 27 "If this government will stay, many hearts and minds will be broken. It will be really hard to continue," said Cohen. Many of Netanyahu's opponents see the election as an opportunity at last to ​deliver a long-postponed reckoning for the worst security failure in generations. But even if Israel's longest-serving prime minister loses his majority, he could well escape the decisive verdict his foes are ​seeking. Israelis will head to the polls on Tuesday in the first legislative election since the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks and Israel’s subsequent genocidal war on Gaza. Here are five things to know: https://t.co/zYTVfY95dV pic.twitter.com/QOC0bPT24C — Al Jazeera English (@AJEnglish) October 26, 2026 Netanyahu has rejected blame for the breach and resisted calls for an independent investigation. He maintains that Israel's wars against Hamas in Gaza and its allies ⁠in Lebanon and Iran will result in a more peaceful Middle East. The task will be complete only with the downfall of Iran's clerical rulers, Netanyahu has said on the campaign trail, and only ​he has the conviction and standing to deliver. Opinion polls have for months predicted a sharp drop for Netanyahu's Likud party. But a rival alliance of parties on the right, left and centre looking to unseat him also ​has no clear path to power, suggesting months of political stalemate with Netanyahu potentially at the helm of a caretaker government. 'Two clicks to the right' In the days after October 7, Be'eri was crawling with Israeli soldiers patrolling through burnt and shattered homes, floors stained with blood, doors pierced with bullet holes. In some spots, the stench of dead bodies still hung in the air. The sounds of shelling and Israeli warplanes flying over Gaza were incessant. Three years on, ​the kibbutz is up and running, and the sound of construction on brand-new houses echoes across the leafy green grounds. Most members, now residing in another kibbutz, are expected to return ​by summer. A collective community established in 1946, now with around 1,000 residents, Be'eri exemplifies the socialist values that dominated Israel's politics in its early decades. Nearly all its votes went to the centre-left in the previous 2022 ‌election, when only ⁠around 4% voted for parties in Netanyahu's nationalist-religious coalition. The attack has made residents question longstanding views that there could be peace with the Palestinians in this generation. "Everyone in Be'eri has moved two clicks to the right. But I still think that most of us will stay with the opposition, the parties that want to replace this government," he said. Miri Gad Messika, 48, third generation in Be'eri, hasn't yet decided how to vote. But it won't be for Netanyahu. "He failed as a leader so many times. And he shouldn't be in politics anymore," she said. "I'm looking for a leader. Unfortunately, it's hard for me ​to see any leader in Israel at the moment." "I ​want to be optimistic," she added, "and I ⁠can only hope for a better change." 'Hope is stronger than pain' Through much of the past three years, opposition to the Netanyahu government gravitated around families of hostages taken to Gaza, some of whom accused the government of dodging responsibility and doing too little to secure their freedom. Israel will hold its first parliamentary elections since the October 7, 2023 terror attacks on Tuesday. Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot is Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s main challenger in the race. CBS News’ @DovLieber reports from Eisenkot’s final campaign… pic.twitter.com/gq5JgkhRUj — CBS News (@CBSNews) October 26, 2026 A Tel Aviv open space came to ​be known as "Hostages Square", site of constant rallies and vigils. Although the last of the hostages were released under a US-brokered ceasefire reached a ​year ago, the families are ⁠still among those most prominently calling for accountability now. "I don't see any legitimate reason why this government is running again for election," said Ofri Bibas, whose young nephews, a 4-year-old and a 9-month-old, were slain in captivity in Gaza along with their mother. Their father, Ofri's brother Yarden, was released in an early 2025 truce. Bibas said her goal now is to make every Israeli remember October 7, "to take it with them to the ⁠day of the ​election and remember what happened here and who still hasn't taken responsibility". Read More: The wider impact of the Hamas-Israeli conflict On Saturday, thousands of Israelis rallied in Hostages Square. ​One of the speakers was Danielle Alony, who was kidnapped from Nir Oz with her 5-year-old daughter and freed from Gaza in a brief truce weeks later. "Go vote," Alony urged the crowd. "In three days we can start writing a new chapter for ​our children. One in which truth is stronger than fear, responsibility stronger than dereliction and hope is stronger than pain."

title: JI to march on Islamabad in mid-November if govt fails to end petroleum levy: Hafiz Naeem
description: Says party will continue campaign until government abolishes levy; demands withdrawal of K-P emergency
content: Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) Pakistan Ameer Hafiz Naeem ur Rehman on Monday warned that his party would march towards Islamabad in mid-November if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy and provide relief to the public. He also condemned the imposition of an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), describing it as a violation of human rights, and demanded its withdrawal. Speaking at a press conference at Mansoorah, Naeem said JI would continue its campaign against the petroleum levy until the government accepted its demands. He acknowledged that the government had provided some relief in petroleum prices following the party’s protests but maintained that the measures were insufficient. لاہور: امیر جماعت اسلامی پاکستان حافظ نعیم الرحمان پیٹرولیم لیوی کے حوالے سے اہم پریس کانفرنس سے خطاب https://t.co/AIkPjaT319 — Jamaat e Islami Pakistan (@JIPOfficial) October 26, 2026 The JI chief said government ministers had again contacted the party’s negotiating committee, but the party remained firm on its demand for the complete abolition of the levy. He added that he would make an important announcement on the evening of his meeting with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif if progress was made towards providing relief to the public. Criticising the government’s economic policies, Hafiz Naeem said the tax burden on ordinary citizens was increasing while the profits of certain business groups continued to rise. Read More: JI laments inflation, tax burden He called for a reduction in the profit margins of oil refineries and oil marketing companies so that consumers could benefit from lower fuel costs. He also demanded a reduction in the policy rate and measures to eliminate interest-based economic practices. Turning to the judicial system, the JI chief said millions of cases were pending in courts and alleged that the 26th Constitutional Amendment had weakened the judiciary. He maintained that extrajudicial killings could not resolve the country’s systemic problems and criticised the government for failing to formulate effective policies to provide relief to ordinary citizens. On Palestine, Naeem said the destruction caused by Israel in Gaza had resulted in food shortages, while global powers and Muslim countries had failed to play an effective role in addressing the crisis. He questioned the role of Muslim rulers and the Peace Board in supporting Palestinians, calling for a stronger international voice in defence of their rights and greater unity among Muslim countries. Jamaat-e-Islami’s campaign against the petroleum levy intensified in August, when the party organised demonstrations and sit-ins across the country against rising fuel prices, inflation and what it described as an additional tax burden on consumers. On August 16, JI workers staged sit-ins outside governors’ houses in the provincial capitals, demanding the withdrawal of the levy and a reduction in petrol prices. The party subsequently expanded its protests to other cities, including Karachi, where it established additional protest camps across Sindh. JI maintained that the government should abolish the levy rather than offer limited reductions in fuel prices. On September 3, the government and JI agreed to establish technical committees to examine proposals for reducing the petroleum levy and fuel prices. During the first round of negotiations on September 7, the party submitted six proposals to the government, while insisting that its protests would continue until meaningful relief was provided. However, the negotiations failed to resolve the dispute. On September 12, JI chief announced a long march towards Islamabad for September 20, warning that the party would intensify its campaign if the government did not abolish the levy. The march began on September 20, with participants travelling from Karachi by train. The caravan moved through Sukkur towards Multan, where Naeem addressed supporters. The march was subsequently suspended after PM Shehbaz telephoned the JI chief and requested that the party postpone its protest to allow further negotiations. Read More: JI announces September 20 long march on Islamabad over petroleum levy JI agreed to give the government an opportunity for talks but maintained that it had not abandoned its demand. The party’s position was that negotiations and protests could continue simultaneously, with any agreement required to address the complete abolition of the levy.

title: Jordan arrests three suspects in deadly church attack, state media says
description: No security ​personnel were injured, and a number of firearms and ammunition were found in the suspects' possession
content: Jordanian security forces arrested three armed suspects after a shootout on Monday in connection with an attack ​on a church in the US-allied country that killed nine people, state television ​reported. Friday's attack during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in ⁠the village of Hamoud in Karak governorate, about 120 km (75 miles) southwest of ​the capital Amman, also wounded 40 others. Witnesses said the shooting lasted several minutes. Jordan's Public ​Security Directorate said the suspects were located while hiding in an abandoned house in Karak. They refused to surrender and attacked security forces, who returned fire and arrested all three after wounding ​them, the directorate said in a statement published on state media. No security ​personnel were injured, and a number of firearms and ammunition were found in the suspects' possession. Jordanian ‌authorities ⁠have said the violence was carried out by "extremist terrorists". There has been no claim of responsibility. Read: Jordan king orders 'iron fist' response to deadly church attack "Terrorism has no place among us," the directorate said, adding that the suspects had met their "just fate". King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against militant ​groups, has ordered security ​forces to respond ⁠with an "iron fist" to the rare attack on the Christian minority. Such violence is highly unusual in Jordan, a relatively stable ​state in the Middle East, though authorities say they have ​foiled several ⁠Islamist militant plots over the years. The Public Security Directorate did not name the suspects or publicly identify possible affiliations with any Islamist militant groups. Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya ⁠said ​authorities were reviewing the circumstances that led young ​people towards extremism and would hold accountable anyone found to have participated in the attack.

title: Brazil’s Lula wins historic fourth term, Flavio Bolsonaro refuses to concede
description: Bolsonaro led the election's first round but lost in the runoff by over 4 million votes
content: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a historic fourth term on Sunday, the country's electoral court said, in a shock result that defied polls, precedent and global anti-incumbent ​sentiment to put the brakes on a wave of right-wing election victories across Latin America. However, his opponent, Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, refused to accept defeat and said ‌he would ask for the result to be annulled due to a Sunday ruling from a Supreme Court justice that extended voting for two hours. Bolsonaro led the election's first round but lost in the runoff by over 4 million votes, rattling Brazilian financial markets which had bet on his victory. His refusal to concede defeat has echoes of his father's reaction after losing to Lula in 2022. Jair Bolsonaro never accepted his loss and was later sentenced by the Supreme Court to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup to remain in power. The scale of Flavio Bolsonaro's loss to ​Lula — by more than twice his father's losing margin — and the fact his campaign also asked for an extension due to rains in the conservative-leaning south make any annulment unlikely, analysts said. Read: Lula says bus cuts hinder voters in Brazil Mario Braga, a Latin America analyst at ​the risk consultancy RANE, said there could be right-wing protests in coming days, but "it's very improbable that it will lead to the reversal of the result." Comeback king Investors expect recent bets ⁠on a change of government to unwind in a volatile week ahead on financial markets. A Tokyo-listed exchange-traded fund tracking Brazil's Bovespa index dived nearly 15% in Asian trading on news of Lula's victory, while the Brazilian real was set to fall ​sharply against the US dollar. The victory marks another comeback in a career full of them for Lula, an icon of the global left and the most dominant force in Brazilian politics this century. The 80-year-old was jailed from 2018 to 2019 on ​corruption charges that were later overturned, paving the way for him to beat Jair Bolsonaro in the 2022 election. "He is a statesman, a giant," leftist federal lawmaker Erika Hilton, who was with Lula in Sao Paulo during the vote count, told Reuters. At times, Lula's reelection looked like a long shot, as voters soured on him and his Workers' Party after years of corruption scandals and rising prices, while sweeping social changes left the former metalworker and union leader looking out of touch with an increasingly app-based economy and its growing ranks of informal workers. Pollsters said better-than-expected turnout ​had powered Lula to victory. Leonardo Barreto, the co-founder of consultancy Think Policy, said voters had chosen Lula's familiar embrace over Bolsonaro's novelty. "People today are choosing between change, with some apprehension, and a known path, which guarantees certain rights," he said. During ​the campaign, Lula pointed to a track record of falling poverty and inequality, while unemployment, illiteracy and deforestation hit record lows during his third term. He warned Bolsonaro would cut welfare spending, backslide on social advances and hand over Brazil's sovereignty to US President Donald Trump, ‌whose State Department led ⁠a campaign to get the Bolsonaros back to power. Lula's win deprives Trump of a major addition to what has been a growing bloc of friendly right-wing Latin American governments that have embraced Washington's agenda on security and migration. Read more: Brazil rivals seek disqualification of each other There was no immediate comment from Trump or the US State Department, while Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Latin American leaders were quick to offer their congratulations. Celso Amorim, a former Lula foreign minister, told Reuters the leftist "would be very important for establishing a point of balance in Latin America. Lula is that balance." Late-campaign boost Lula becomes the first candidate since Brazil's return to democracy in the 1980s to be elected after finishing second in the first round.
