His campaign this year mixed the kind of pragmatism and populism that has ​shaped his career in national politics for half a century, ​rolling out a slew of reforms aimed at improving ⁠the lives of workers and poor Brazilians. These gained steam with late-campaign pledges that ranged from free nationwide weekend public transport, which has to be formally submitted to Congress, to a 15% increase in his trademark welfare program that is already being implemented. Lula also championed a constitutional amendment that became Brazil's biggest labour reform in decades, which passed with wide support in Congress. Challenges ahead Still, ​Lula's fourth term could be his most difficult yet, after Brazil elected its most conservative Congress since returning to democracy in the 1980s. Combined, Bolsonaro's Liberal Party and allied parties ​could control over 280 seats ⁠in the lower house and up to 50 seats in the Senate, enough for comfortable opposition majorities in both chambers. That may deepen recent trends of presidents ceding power to Congress on the budget, major legislation and key nominations. Lula faces an economy that his government forecasts will grow just 2.3% next year, adding to fiscal concerns tied to high interest rates and public debt that has risen past 82% of GDP, the highest since the pandemic. Also read: Brazil's Bolsonaro says not considering father for govt post Goldman Sachs said it expects Lula to make modest progress at most to contain spending ⁠in a fourth ​term, as he stays committed to a state-led growth model. Surging household debt also concerns economists. Trying to address the issue, Lula rolled out a ​provisional ban on online betting and unveiled a new debt relief program during the campaign. The incoming right-wing Congress will try to pass structural reforms that favour businesses, experts say, prompting spending cuts that could trigger popular backlash.

title: Dictionary.com names 'maxxing' its 2026 Word of the Year
description: 'It was everywhere,' says lexicography director, adding the word evolved from internet slang into mainstream culture
content: Dictionary.com named “maxxing” its 2026 Word of the Year, highlighting a growing internet-driven culture focused on optimising different aspects of life, the Guardian reported on Monday. “Maxxing,” sometimes written as “-maxxing,” is short for “maximising” and refers to doing something to the fullest or optimising it as much as possible, according to the online dictionary. The term gained popularity among Gen Z and Gen Alpha and has evolved into a flexible slang expression that can function as a noun, verb, adjective, or adverb. Examples include “gymmaxxing” for optimising workout routines, “healthmaxxing” for maximising health and wellness practices, “sleepmaxxing” for optimising sleep and “tokenmaxxing” for deliberately maximising the use of artificial intelligence tools. “Maxxing really stood out this year because not only was it everywhere, in all types of articles, but it crossed a lot of different domains,” Steve Johnson, director of lexicography for Dictionary Media Group, which operates Dictionary.com, told CBS News. The term has also appeared in political messaging, including the use of “homelandmaxxing,” while “cozymaxxing” has been used to describe efforts to optimise leisure and comfort. Dictionary.com said its selection was based on an analysis of search data, social media trends and news coverage, as well as the word's cultural significance. Johnson said the dictionary's lexicographers maintain a list of words to monitor throughout the year, examining their frequency and how they reflect broader cultural developments. The choice marks a contrast with Dictionary.com's 2025 Word of the Year, “67,” a viral expression whose meaning often remained unclear to users. Other 2026 Finalists Dictionary.com selected finalists from internet culture, politics, technology and wider media trends. They included “affordability,” reflecting concerns over housing, groceries, childcare and other rising costs; “data centre,” amid the expansion of infrastructure supporting artificial intelligence; “unc,” a Gen Z and Gen Alpha slang term for an older person perceived as uncool or out of touch; and “odyssey,” referring to a long and eventful journey that gained renewed cultural attention following Christopher Nolan's 2026 film adaptation of Homer's epic.

title: US singer Chris Brown spared jail for UK nightclub attack
description: Brown given suspended sentence after pleading guilty to affray, fans cheered outside as he was allowed to walk free
content: US singer Chris Brown was ​spared an immediate prison sentence in Britain on Monday for attacking a music producer with a tequila bottle ‌in a London nightclub in 2023, with his fans cheering as the musician walked free from court. Brown, 37, was given an eight-month suspended sentence at London's Southwark Crown Court over the attack on Abraham Diaw at the Tape nightclub in February 2023 that lasted around 20 seconds. Diaw was hit twice in the head ​with a bottle, which was then swung twice more at him in what prosecutors described as "a vicious and unprovoked attack". The ​R&B star and his vocal coach Omololu Akinlolu, 40, pleaded guilty to a charge of affray in July, ⁠having denied more serious charges of attempting to inflict grievous bodily harm and assault causing actual bodily harm. No speical treatment Judge Tony Baumgartner said: "This was ​serious, public violence. In your case, Brown, it involved the repeated use ... of a bottle, including twice striking Diaw to his head." The judge told ​Brown: "Your fame, commercial success and professional standing do not entitle you to special treatment – the law applies equally to everyone." But Baumgartner said he could suspend Brown's sentence for 12 months, meaning he will not go to prison unless he commits another offence in that period. Akinlolu was also spared an immediate jail ​sentence. "Violence will not be accepted on the streets of London," Detective Chief Superintendent Christina Jessah from the Metropolitan Police said in a ​statement. "Regardless of an individual's profile or status, we will pursue those responsible and work tirelessly to bring them before the courts." US singer Chris Brown arrives at Southwark Crown Court where he is due to be sentenced after pleading guilty to affray over an incident in which prosecutors said he attacked a music producer with a bottle in a London nightclub in 2023, in London, Britain, October 26, 2026. PHOTO: Reuters Brown's fan cheer suspended sentence Brown, ‌winner of ⁠Grammy awards for best R&B album in 2011 and 2025, has previously admitted other violent offences in the US, having been charged with assaulting his then-partner, singer Rihanna, in 2009, with a photo of her bruised face making headlines around the world. Prosecutor Heidi Stonecliffe said Brown pleaded guilty to the 2009 assault of Rihanna and was sentenced to five years' probation. He also admitted a 2013 assault on a fan he ​was accused of punching when he ​asked for a photograph. Brown remains ⁠hugely popular and has sold tens of millions of records worldwide, with dozens of fans queuing outside court from around 0700 GMT, about an hour before the building opened. His lawyer Sallie Bennett-Jenkins said Brown ​was profoundly sorry for the incident and described him as "a dedicated, loving and loyal father to four ​children". "This was an ⁠ugly and unattractive incident, we would be the first to accept," she added. "It was, however, an incident that was very short-lived." Brown thanked the judge before leaving the dock and nodding towards about two dozen of his supporters in the public gallery. Other fans who gathered outside the building cheered ⁠as Brown ​left and went into a waiting car. Brown was arrested in May 2025 having ​returned to Britain for the first time since the attack and was initially denied bail, throwing his worldwide "Breezy Bowl XX" tour into doubt. But Brown was eventually released after promising to pay ​a £5 million ($6.7 million) security fee, allowing the tour to go ahead.

title: Mawra Hocane highlights refugee families’ struggles during UNHCR visit
description: Actor shares stories of children leaving schools and friends behind during a visit to a repatriation centre with UNHCR
content: Actor Mawra Hocane highlighted the emotional challenges faced by refugee families preparing to return home, sharing reflections from her visit to a repatriation centre in an Instagram collaboration with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR). In the video, Hocane acknowledged the efforts of countries that have welcomed people fleeing conflict, highlighting the importance of providing them with shelter, education, healthcare and a sense of belonging. “What very few countries have been able to do. We've opened our doors, our schools, hospitals, our neighbourhood, to millions of people fleeing the war,” she said. Alongside the video, Hocane shared a heartfelt caption reflecting on her visit to the repatriation centre, where she met families and their children as they prepared for their journey home. “No matter what we do for them… it’ll never be enough… but it’s always better to do something… however little it may be,” she wrote. Describing the encounters, the actress noted that adults were concerned about their future, while children were sad to leave their schools and friends behind, highlighting how displacement affects family members differently. View this post on Instagram “During my visit to the Repatriation Centre, I had the opportunity to meet families and their children. I listened to their stories as they prepared for their journey home. Where adults were worried about their future, children were sad to leave their schools and friends behind,” she said. Hocane also acknowledged UNHCR’s role in assisting families who have chosen to return to their home countries, emphasising the importance of ensuring that the process is safe and dignified. “UNHCR is there to support families who have chosen to return by helping to make the process safe and dignified,” she added. Through her message, Hocane drew attention to the human stories behind displacement, highlighting the uncertainty and difficult adjustments that can accompany a return home. While adults may be focused on rebuilding their lives and securing their families’ futures, children may struggle with leaving behind familiar surroundings, friendships and education. Her post also stressed that even small acts of support can make a difference, encouraging greater awareness of the challenges faced by people affected by conflict and displacement. Hocane recently welcomed a baby boy with her husband, Ameer Gillani, adding a personal dimension to her message about the importance of ensuring children receive care and support.

title: Ayesha Omar, Nabeel Zafar celebrate 17 years of ‘Bulbulay’
description: Actors thank fans of the sitcom across generations, reveal filming will continue for six more months
content: Seventeen years after Bulbulay first aired, actors Ayesha Omar and Nabeel Zafar celebrated the sitcom’s enduring popularity, sharing nostalgic clips, a cake-cutting celebration and heartfelt tributes to the viewers who have supported the show since its debut. The actors marked the milestone through collaborative Instagram posts featuring fellow cast members Hina Dilpazeer, Mahmood Aslam and Shagufta Ejaz. One post showed the cast posing together with a celebratory cake. “17 years of laughter, legends, and unforgettable moments. Long live Bulbulay,” read the caption accompanying the post. Another collaborative post shared by Omar, Dilpazeer, Zafar and Aslam featured a clip from the sitcom’s wedding episode, revisiting a memorable chapter in the show’s history. Reflecting on the milestone, Omar wrote that the cast had spent 17 years tolerating and loving one another on screen, while the affection they received from viewers continued to grow. “Mashallah. Today we are celebrating 17 years of tolerating and loving each other, and being on your television screens. And the love keeps growing. Thank you from the core of our hearts for allllllll the love you all continue to give our #bulbulay family,” she wrote. View this post on Instagram Omar thanked audiences around the world for their continued support, saying the sitcom had brought families and communities together through moments of joy and laughter amid everyday stresses. “We feel blessed that we are able to impact millions of lives all over the world and bring entire families and communities together for a few moments of joy and laughter, every day for some of you, amongst all the stressors around,” she added. The actress also reflected on the show’s cross-generational appeal, recalling encounters with young fans who credited it with making their childhoods special, children who watched it before going to sleep and older viewers who turned to its humour to unwind. She further highlighted the connection the cast shared with viewers with Down syndrome and autism, as well as blind fans who listened to episodes and memorised the dialogue. “Almost every day I meet a Gen Z or Gen Alpha human who thanks me for enriching their childhood with this show, or a child who won’t go to sleep without watching it, an elder who can only destress through this show, people with Down syndrome or autism who believe and take joy in us being their own family members, blind people who listen to each and every episode and know entire dialogues, serious political figures who are addicted to it, and it all continues to blow us away,” she continued. View this post on Instagram Omar also revealed that filming was scheduled to continue for another six months, suggesting that more episodes were in the pipeline. She paid tribute to actor Khaled Anam, whom she affectionately called “Papa”, saying the cast missed him dearly and expressing hope that he was resting in peace. “P.s. Papa we miss you dearly. Hope you’re enjoying and resting in peace,” she concluded. The throwback clips came from the sitcom’s wedding episode, during which Dilpazeer joined the show as Momo before becoming a permanent cast member. Omar previously revealed that Bulbulay was originally planned for just 26 episodes. First aired in 2009, Bulbulay became a familiar fixture of Pakistani television through its family-centred humour, comic misunderstandings and distinctive characters. The sitcom stars Zafar, Omar, Aslam and Dilpazeer, whose performances have helped sustain its popularity across generations.

title: Danyal Zafar announces break from showbiz after reaching ‘breaking point’
description: Actor-musician says two years of constant travel, TV shoots and album recordings have taken a toll on his health
content: Actor and musician Danyal Zafar has announced a temporary break from work after two years of constant travel and professional commitments across acting and music took a toll on his health. The artist shared the update on his Instagram story on Sunday, alongside a photograph of an intravenous infusion bag, saying he had reached what he described as a “breaking point”. “Dear all. I believe I’ve reached a breaking point. 2 years of being on the road consistently. 3 days here, 2 days there, 1 day here, 4 days there. This has been life for me for the past 2 years,” he wrote. Zafar described the demands of balancing his acting and music careers, saying his schedule had revolved around television shoots, live performances, album recordings and other professional commitments, leaving him with little time to stay in one place. “Between shoots, shows, album recordings and everything in between, I’ve barely remained in one place for more than a few days,” he added. Acknowledging the strain of maintaining both careers, Zafar described the experience as “a tumultuous feat” and said he had been instructed to prioritise his health. “I’ve been ordered to put my health above everything else for now. And for once, I think I need to listen. Everything must go on hold,” he wrote. The actor-singer said he would step away from work to focus on his recovery. “I’ll be taking a little break to rest, recover and find my way back to full health,” he added. Screengrab: danyalzee/Instagram The announcement came two days after Zafar shared another Instagram post reflecting on his identity as an artist and his desire to move beyond conventional commercial expectations. In the post, he described himself as “an outlier”, “an outcast”, “a problem” and “a frequency”, expressing his desire to create music that reflected his inner state rather than conforming to industry expectations. “I feel like my sound owes you something beyond a ‘song’,” he wrote, adding that his work should be “something that moves me” and “something truly representing my inner state”. He also urged listeners to look beyond commercial considerations when evaluating his music. “If u see me / save me the ‘u need to make something commercial’ speech and sit down / I’m here to push bounds and bend the mind,” he wrote. View this post on Instagram The post also promoted his forthcoming full-length album, STORMS & serenity, which Zafar said was due out “this szn”. He teased a “31st surprise” and said further details about the tracklist and featured artists would be announced soon. He identified “DEAR DEATH” as the track accompanying the video. Together, the two posts offered a glimpse into the demands of Zafar’s parallel careers and his ambition to pursue a more personal, experimental musical direction. He has not announced a specific date for his return to professional commitments. Zafar, also known by his musical moniker Danny Zee, is a singer-songwriter, composer and actor. He gained wider recognition through his appearance on Coke Studio season 10 in 2017, where he performed “Muntazir”. Alongside music, he has built an acting career through television projects including Tanaa Banaa, Baarwan Khiladi and Standup Girl. His more recent work includes Raqaas and Zanjeerain.

title: SBP hikes policy rate to 12% on Middle East risks
description: Governor says economic outlook has changed significantly amid rising global commodity prices, geopolitical uncertainty
content: The State Bank of Pakistan’s Monetary Policy Committee on Monday raised the policy rate by 50 basis points to 12 per cent, effective October 27, with nine of ten members voting in favour. The decision aims to keep inflation expectations anchored and limit second-round effects from the ongoing supply shock so inflation returns to the 5–7 per cent target range over the medium term. The Committee cited the intensification of the Middle East conflict and low prospects of near-term resolution, which have kept global energy prices elevated. While the domestic impact has so far remained contained due to earlier monetary adjustments and fiscal discipline, the inflation outlook has worsened relative to the previous assessment. External account and growth projections remain broadly unchanged, but risks have increased. Since the last meeting, SBP’s foreign exchange reserves stayed stable around $21.5 billion, equivalent to three months of import cover, supported by continued purchases. A staff-level agreement was reached with the IMF. Consumer inflation expectations rose while those of businesses declined, and confidence indicators weakened for both groups. Revised real GDP growth for FY26 was reported at 3.7 per cent, nearly unchanged from the initial estimate. FBR tax collection in Q1-FY27 grew 7 per cent year-on-year and exceeded the target by Rs33 billion. Major central banks have also raised rates amid higher inflation, and the IMF revised its global inflation projections upward. Economic activity is recovering gradually. Large-scale manufacturing grew 1.9 per cent year-on-year in July-August FY27, up from 0.4 per cent in Q4-FY26. Cement and petroleum sales, private-sector credit, the Purchasing Managers' Index, nighttime lights, and nitrogen dioxide emissions all point to improvement. Kharif crop estimates were better than expected, and services indicators, including ICT exports, are gradually strengthening. The MPC projects real GDP growth of 3.5–4.5 per cent in FY27, subject to risks from further Middle East escalation and adverse climate events linked to El Niño conditions. The current account recorded a deficit of $874 million in Q1-FY27. Exports of rice, high-value-added textiles and services are recovering, while workers’ remittances remain resilient and are now expected to exceed earlier projections. Imports, particularly non-energy goods, are rising with activity. The full-year current account deficit is still assessed at 0–1 per cent of GDP, with reserves projected to rise further, though subject to commodity price, financing and supply risks. On the fiscal side, contained expenditures and the transfer of SBP profit are expected to keep the overall and primary balances in surplus for Q1-FY27. Broad money growth accelerated to 12.7 per cent year-on-year as of October 9, driven by reserve accumulation, while private-sector credit expanded 14.1 per cent across working capital, fixed investment and consumer segments. Headline inflation stood at 10.3 per cent in September, higher than expected, with core inflation steady near 8.4 per cent. Elevated energy and wheat prices remain key drivers. The Committee judged the rate increase necessary to maintain a positive real policy rate on a forward-looking basis. The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) decided to increase the policy rate by 50 bps to 12 percent in its meeting today, with the majority decision of nine out of ten members, with effect from October 27, 2026. For details: https://t.co/9AzpnhseRS pic.twitter.com/FsR8gt2WMX — SBP (@StateBank_Pak) October 26, 2026 Addressing a press conference following the MPC meeting, SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad said crude oil prices hovering around $100 per barrel had increased pressure on domestic prices. He said nine of the MPC's 10 members voted in favour of increasing the policy rate, reflecting growing concerns over inflation and external economic risks. The governor said the economic outlook had changed significantly since the previous monetary policy meeting, with rising global commodity prices and geopolitical developments adding to uncertainty. Ahmad said earlier assessments during July and August had suggested that inflation would remain around 7% towards the end of the year, adding that recent developments had altered that outlook, and bringing inflation down to the previously anticipated level was now expected to take longer. He said core inflation had shown improvement, but warned that higher energy prices could generate secondary inflationary effects in the coming months. The governor noted that global oil and commodity price increases were affecting domestic inflation and putting additional pressure on Pakistan's external account. Ahmad said rising global commodity and oil prices were expected to affect the country's current account deficit projections, saying despite these pressures, the central bank expected the current account deficit to remain between 0% and 1% of gross domestic product (GDP). He said workers' remittances were expected to improve, supported by measures aimed at encouraging overseas Pakistanis to send money through formal banking channels. According to the governor, Pakistan received $10.9 billion in remittances during the first quarter of the current financial year. He said full-year remittances were now expected to reach between $44 billion and $45 billion. Ahmad also referred to a remittance reward scheme, saying the initiative was expected to support inflows in the coming months. The governor said Pakistan's export performance had shown signs of improvement, although growth remained below expectations, adding that projected exports of between $32.5 billion and $33 billion during the current financial year. However, he warned that the country was facing considerable pressure on imports due to rising international commodity and energy prices. Ahmad said the import bill was expected to reach approximately $71 billion during the financial year, saying that the higher import costs could complicate efforts to manage the external balance, despite anticipated improvements in remittances and exports. Last month, the MPC kept the policy rate unchanged at 11.5%, in line with market expectations. The decision was the third consecutive hold after the 100-basis-point increase in April, the first hike in nearly three years. The July meeting had also left the rate at 11.5%, citing an improved macroeconomic outlook tempered by risks from renewed conflict in the Middle East. In July, the MPC decided to maintain the policy rate at 11.5%, citing an improved macroeconomic outlook tempered by elevated risks from the renewed conflict in the Middle East. The committee assessed that earlier de-escalation had lowered global oil prices and eased supply-chain pressures, contributing to some improvement in recent indicators. The MPC noted that proactive policy management and fiscal consolidation had helped absorb the ongoing supply shock and preserve stability. It reiterated its commitment to bringing inflation into the 5-7% medium-term target range and said the current stance remains appropriate. The MPC in June kept the policy rate unchanged at 11.5%, in a cautious approach amid mixed signals on inflation and external risks. Market experts had shown divided opinions ahead of the announcement. According to a poll by Topline Securities, 49% of respondents anticipated no change, while another 49% expected a hike, with 34% forecasting a 50bps increase and 15% a 100bps rise. Only 2% predicted a cut of up to 50bps. In March, amid the outbreak of the United States-Israeli war against Iran and heightened regional geopolitical tensions, the MPC decided to maintain the policy rate unchanged at 10.5%. The stance reflected caution over potential imported inflation pressures from surging global energy prices, triggered by the US-Iran tensions that drove Brent crude up sharply to around $108 per barrel. The cautious pause in March was seen as support for ongoing macroeconomic stability efforts, building on prior rate reductions (including the 50 bps cut to 10.5% in December 2025), while allowing time to monitor energy price dynamics, domestic inflation trends, and external account resilience. Later, in a move that defied market expectations, the MPC announced a sharp 100 basis point increase in the policy rate in April, raising it to 11.5%. The SBP’s move signalled a decisive pivot, prioritising inflation anchoring over near-term growth support, even as the economy posted a 3.89% GDP expansion in Q2 and a $1.07 billion current account surplus in March.

title: PSX recovers 664 points after rate-driven sell-off
description: KSE-100 Index closes at 163,038.5 points after SBP raises interest rates by 50 basis points
content: Bulls returned to the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) on Monday as buying interest in index-heavy sectors during the latter half of the session reversed early losses, despite investor uncertainty over the State Bank of Pakistan’s (SBP) monetary policy decision. The benchmark KSE-100 Index initially fell to 162,347.31 points, down 27.56 points, or 0.02%, within minutes of the opening bell. Sentiment remained subdued amid a lack of positive triggers, while uncertainty over the Monetary Policy Committee’s (MPC) interest rate decision weighed on the market. The index subsequently recovered, gaining 663.59 points, or 0.41%, to close at 163,038.47. It had touched an intraday low of 161,250.07 before buying momentum in the latter half of trading lifted it to a high of 163,477.09. The recovery came as the SBP raised its policy rate by 50 basis points to 12%, a move expected to increase borrowing costs for businesses and potentially weigh on investment and economic activity. According to KASB KTrade equity trader Ahmed Sheraz, the KSE-100 closed at 163,083 points, up 663 points, or 0.41%, day-on-day, recovering from its intraday low of 161,250 to a high of 163,477. Trading remained volatile amid earlier concerns over a possible 100-basis-point increase in the policy rate. Buying interest subsequently emerged, particularly in the cement sector, helping the benchmark recover and close in positive territory, Sheraz said. Sector-wise performance was mixed, with cement, investment banking, and oil and gas stocks contributing positively. United Bank Limited (UBL), Engro Holdings and Lucky Cement supported the recovery, while Meezan Bank closed lower. Meanwhile, Brent crude hovered near $115 per barrel, fuelling inflationary concerns. Pakistan, alongside Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, was pursuing mediation efforts with Iran, with a delegation visiting Tehran on Monday. Despite the positive close, investor sentiment was expected to remain cautious amid elevated oil prices, the outcome of regional mediation efforts, Israeli elections scheduled for Tuesday and the upcoming US midterm elections on November 3. Sheraz said the market was likely to remain volatile and driven by headlines following the 50-basis-point policy rate increase, with its near-term direction depending on geopolitical developments and changing macroeconomic expectations. Cumulatively, trading volume fell to 376 million shares from 398.9 million on Friday, while the value of traded shares stood at Rs16.1 billion. In the ready market, shares of 495 companies were traded. Of these, 196 stocks closed higher, 251 declined and 48 remained unchanged. LSE Financial (R) led trading volumes, with 25.5 million shares changing hands. Its share price fell by Rs0.01 to close at Rs0.78.

title: Oil drops from near six-month highs on hopes Iran war hostilities to ease
description: Brent crude down $2.21, at $114.51 per barrel; US WTI down $2.23, at $101.04 per barrel
content: Oil prices fell on Monday after surging last ‌week to near six-month highs, amid hopes of easing hostilities between the United States and Iran, although persistent attacks on key producer Saudi Arabia kept investors wary. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down $2.23, or 2.16%, at $101.04 per barrel by 0926 ​PKT. Brent crude futures were down $2.21, or 1.89%, at $114.51. On Friday, prices settled nearly $3 higher after Houthi attacks ​in Saudi Arabia stoked energy supply concerns. Brent finished the week up 6% and ⁠WTI ended 2.3% higher. On Sunday, Qatari mediators travelled to Tehran as part of an effort to de-escalate regional ​tensions in coordination with the United States, an official briefed on the situation said. "Concerns over renewed military hostilities in ​the Middle East, which drove much of last week’s crude rally, have eased this morning, but the reprieve may prove temporary," said Vandana Hari, founder of oil market analysis provider Vanda Insights. Read: PSX sheds 715 points as investors brace for policy rate decision Hari said US President Donald Trump has not dispelled ​market expectations that strikes on Iran could still follow after the November 3 midterm elections. "We therefore expect volatility ​to remain elevated, with risks still skewed to the upside," she added. Despite the mediation talks, attacks continued over the weekend with the ‌Iran-backed Houthis saying ⁠they struck an airport and oil facilities in Saudi Arabia on Saturday. Saudi Arabia said on Sunday it had intercepted more missiles and drones. The effects of the US-Israeli war on Iran that began on February 28 continue to reverberate as companies adjust to the disruptions of commercial shipping through the key Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb ​Strait caused by the conflict. On ​Monday, the energy ministers ⁠from Saudi Arabia and Singapore said state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco will start storing crude oil in Singapore from the second half of 2027, to shore up the resilience of Aramco's supply chain ​in the region. "While supply risks surrounding the Strait of Hormuz remain firmly entrenched, ​the current pullback ⁠appears more reflective of position adjustments and risk management rather than any meaningful improvement in the underlying supply situation," said Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insight at Phillip Nova. The head of the International Energy Agency, Fatih Birol, reinforced ⁠the concerns ​about the supply situation, saying on Monday at an industry event ​in Singapore that he does not expect energy markets in 2027 to return to where they were before the Iran war.

title: Egypt approves military support for Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks escalate
description: Saudi Arabia is a major ‌political, financial partner of Cairo, providing billions of dollars in aid, energy supplies
content: Egypt's parliament authorised the military on Monday to provide support to help defend Saudi Arabia, parliamentarians said, and local media reported, a move that could push Cairo directly into the regional conflict ​that has expanded with intensified attacks by Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis on the Gulf kingdom. President ‌Abdel Fattah al-Sisi had asked parliament last week to approve defending its Gulf Arab ally and the world's biggest oil exporter if Riyadh requests help against the Houthis, whose advances also threaten the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait — a gateway to Egypt's Suez ​Canal. Egypt has frequently condemned Iranian and Iranian-backed attacks on Gulf countries but has not publicly ​engaged in direct combat or joined the Makkah mutual defence pact between Saudi Arabia, ⁠Pakistan and Turkiye that was signed in August. The approval followed closed-door discussions on authorising military support to the kingdom, including the possible deployment of troops, amid escalating regional tensions. Parliament said the two-thirds-majority authorisation allows Sisi to take measures, in coordination with Saudi Arabia, to defend the kingdom’s territory, sovereignty and holy sites. The decision followed closed-door sessions held on Oct 18, 19 and 26 at the president’s request, the statement said. Lawmakers discussed regional developments and their implications for Egyptian and Arab national security, with representatives from different political parties and independent lawmakers participating, it added. Parliament said the authorisation was consistent with decisions taken by Egypt’s National Defence Council at its Oct 18 meeting. The statement did not specify the measures to be taken or explicitly announce a deployment of Egyptian troops. Earlier today, lawmakers resumed deliberations in a third closed-door session chaired by Parliament Speaker Hisham Badawi, following two meetings held last week at Sisi’s request. البرلمان المصري يوافق على تفويض الرئيس السيسي بإرسال تعزيزات دفاعية إلى السعودية "إذا طلبت" ======== 🔴 مراسلة العربية: برلمان مصر يوافق على تفويض الرئيس السيسي بإرسال تعزيزات دفاعية للسعودية "إذا طلبت". 🔴 الرئيس المصري عبد الفتاح السيسي دعا البرلمان إلى عقد جلسة طارئة… pic.twitter.com/JDz0jc839K — العربية عاجل (@AlArabiya_Brk) October 26, 2026 Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said this month that Egyptian membership in ​the pact remained "under serious consideration". Read: Egypt's Sisi seeks parliament's backing to help defend Saudi Arabia if asked Egypt, the Arab world's most populous state with one of the region's largest ​militaries, joined the Saudi-led coalition in an earlier phase of Yemen's war in March 2015 mainly as a naval partner, sending warships to secure Red Sea shipping lanes while pledging air support. It also deployed around 800 ground troops but ​played only a limited combat role. Egypt was involved in a costly military intervention in Yemen in the ​1960s and has not undertaken a large-scale foreign ground deployment since the 1991 Gulf War. Saudi Arabia is a major ‌political and ⁠financial partner of Cairo, providing billions of dollars in aid, deposits at the central bank and energy supplies under Sisi. Fighting between the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government and the Houthi militia, which controls the capital Sanaa, has escalated in recent weeks, becoming a volatile front in the US-Israeli war on Iran. The ​Houthis have attacked Riyadh's international ​airport and the state ⁠oil giant Saudi Aramco, disrupting flights and oil exports, while aid agencies have warned of worsening conditions in Yemen, already suffering one of the world's worst humanitarian ​crises. Abdelatty and Egyptian intelligence chief Hassan Rashad travelled to Riyadh on Wednesday ​to deliver a ⁠letter to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman from Sisi, who said Egypt's support would be limited to defending Saudi territory and borders rather than attacking Yemen. Abdelatty said after that visit that Cairo advocates exploring "every ⁠opportunity" to ​resolve the Yemen conflict diplomatically. Read More: Egypt's Sisi says Saudi defence role would not include attack on Yemen The Saudi crown prince visited Sisi in ​Cairo on September 15 to discuss security and navigation in the Red Sea after the fighting in Yemen reignited.

title: Norway joins the list of countries Trump has abused in vulgar terms
description: Says he will welcome immigrants from some ​countries but not from Norway 'because I didn't get the Nobel Prize'
content: US President Donald Trump on Sunday escalated ​his invective against Norway, calling it a "shit house country" and ‌saying Norwegian immigrants were not welcome in the United States because the Nobel committee, based in the capital Oslo, had not awarded him a Peace ​Prize. Trump made the comments at a political rally in Port ​Huron, Michigan, ahead of next week's mid-term elections. Attributing recent unrest in ⁠France to immigration, Trump said he would welcome immigrants from some ​countries but not from Norway "because I didn't get the Nobel Prize ... ​So I don't want anybody from Norway" There was no indication that the Trump administration was adopting new official policy on Norwegian immigrants. "He knows very well that ​the Nobel Committee is independent. We have reminded them of that, ​if anyone is wondering, and that is still the case," Norwegian Foreign Minister ‌Espen ⁠Barth Eide told national broadcaster NRK on Monday. His ministry declined to comment further. Read More: South Africa's Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize "Norway has become a shit house country, actually," Trump said, using a term that he has previously applied to Haiti, ​Libya, Somalia and Yemen. Norway ​is among ⁠the highest-income countries as measured by GDP per capita, according to International Monetary Fund data. Norway's sovereign wealth fund posted ​a record profit of 1.75 trillion Norwegian crowns ($184.3 ​billion) for ⁠the first half of 2026 The Norwegian Nobel Committee did not immediately return requests for comment Trump earlier this month called the failure to give ⁠him ​a Nobel Peace Prize an "indelible stain" on ​Norway.

title: In China, the AI bubble has already burst
description: Lofty valuations collapse under worries about AI demand and curbs on Chinese exports
content: While global tech stocks teeter, in China they have already crashed as lofty valuations collapse under worries about AI demand and curbs on Chinese exports. The meltdown, tanking the mainland STAR50 index of AI and semiconductor leaders by 40% in less than four months ​and vapourising some $480 billion in market value, is an ill omen for wobbly world markets and a dampener on China's efforts at encouraging its savers into stocks to ‌fund the AI boom. It has also slammed the brakes on a rally running two years, since economic stimulus promises sent shares soaring, and has stalled Beijing's push to break with a long boom-bust pattern and drive a "slow bull" market that delivers reliable performance. China's broad blue-chip index has dropped about 20% from highs made in June. "The stock market later evolved into a speculative crazy bull," said Beijing-based fund manager Dong Baozhen. "And now we see the bubble bursting." The reversal reflects a rally ​that ran to higher heights than markets in the West or elsewhere in Asia, and compares with a mere prick to US AI stocks, which have led a 6% drawdown in ​the Nasdaq from a record high scaled three weeks ago. Read: Meta to raise up to $95 billion in equity to fund costly AI expansion There has been no obvious selling trigger in China, although traders said high prices, tax bills ⁠and the threat of the US or other nations banning Chinese equipment in data centres all contributed. With AI stocks running to 42% of China's market capitalisation and 57% of turnover across mainland-listed A-shares and ​Hong Kong's H-shares, according to Goldman Sachs, few in a market dominated by small investors have escaped pain. Retail favourites slide Shares in robot-maker Unitree, 8,000 times oversubscribed by retail buyers at listing, have halved since they ​started trading in August, and chipmaker CXMT has lost more than a quarter of its value in the past month. Chipmakers MetaX Integrated Circuits and Moore Threads Technology, which leapt 700% and 400% respectively on their market debuts last year, have also halved in value since July. Chen Wensheng, a small business owner and investor from China's southern Hainan, said he bought into the rally emboldened by what he felt was official support for the likes of Unitree, which counted state-backed ​funds as investors. But Chen and his friends are now nursing losses. Frustration that an investment theme backed by Beijing has ended so badly has driven many investors into defensive assets and is likely to ​slow equity fundraising by tech firms. Shares in optical parts makers Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink Technology are down roughly 60% from highs in June and July, in part as Washington moves towards banning the one-time darlings from supplying US ‌data centres. With the ⁠STAR50 index still at around 100 times trailing earnings, albeit down from a high of nearly 250, investors compare the Nasdaq 100's multiple of 30 and worry the selloff could get worse before it gets better. "What's happening is now going to put a stop for many of the companies trying to get themselves listed," said Hong Hao, managing partner and chief investment officer at Lotus Asset Management in Hong Kong. 'All bubbles inevitably burst' The frenzy and its fallout contrast with a push by authorities to improve returns and dampen volatility by cracking down on leverage and high-frequency trading. State-backed investors were sellers into rallies to keep gains ​in check. China's market regulator, the China Securities Regulatory Commission, ​did not immediately reply to questions faxed ⁠by Reuters last week. CRSC Chairman Wu Qing met with market participants earlier this month to hear suggestions on improving capital markets, the regulator said on its website, and some in the investment community say the boom has been bad for the market's structure. Also Read: SpaceX enters $40 billion deal with Apollo for AI chip financing "Overemphasising the 'technology content' — that is, the weighting of tech companies ​by market value in major indexes — leads to a deviation, even a distortion, in capital behaviour," said Leo Wang, partner at Beijing-based Qianchuang Capital. "This created ​a severe bubble in ⁠certain sectors and a serious drain on others." Some see value in the selloff, saying it is neither surprising nor detrimental to market reforms that are geared for the long term and have gained traction in driving up returns, particularly income, in recent years. Although they have been sellers over the past three months, Asia funds in general are overweight on China, according to HSBC research. Goldman Sachs has Innolight and CXMT among dozens of Chinese AI ⁠stocks on a ​revamped recommendation list it published earlier this month, and BNP Paribas Securities strategist William Bratton has said the market offers ​buying opportunities for the careful. Still, on the mainland many are looking at other sectors or for even lower valuations before they turn buyers. "Just like all other Chinese manufacturers, (chipmakers and AI suppliers) will eventually end up in a price war," said fund manager Wang ​Zhuo, partner at Shanghai Zhuozhu Investment Management. "There's no exception," he said. "All bubbles inevitably burst."

title: Meta to raise up to $95 billion in equity to fund costly AI expansion
description: Launches public offerings of about $35 billion in common stock and convertible preferred stock
content: Meta Platforms said on Monday it plans to raise up to $95 billion in equity to fund its costly AI-related expansion ​of data centres, cloud computing power and other infrastructure. The ‌company launched public offerings of about $35 billion in common stock and convertible preferred stock. It also said it plans to launch a separate at-the-market share sale program of ​up to $60 billion after its new non-voting Class C ​shares begin trading, which is expected in the first quarter ⁠of 2027. Meta has stepped up spending on data centres, computing capacity and ​AI products to compete with rival AI heavyweights OpenAI and Anthropic. The social media ​company had cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $82.45 billion, slightly exceeding its long-term debt of $80.92 billion as of September 30, according to its quarterly filing ​from last week. Read: Wall St week ahead earnings flood, Fed meeting will test rickety AI market rally The company has committed to spend about $825 billion in ​the future, primarily driven by its growing investments in data centres, AI-related infrastructure ‌and ⁠cloud computing power. Meta said chip companies Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom have expressed interest in purchasing up to $5 billion of Meta's Class A common stock in the offering. Last week, Meta raised ​the lower end ​of its annual ⁠spending forecast, now expecting capital expenditure to be between $135 billion and $145 billion this year, up from $130 billion ​to $145 billion expected previously. Meta reported a $2.12 billion cash burn ​in ⁠the third quarter, marking its first negative free cash flow in over ten years, compared with a positive cash flow of $10.63 billion a ⁠year ​ago. The company reported third-quarter revenue of $64.60 billion, ​ahead of Wall Street estimates of $63.37 billion. It also projected fourth-quarter revenue between $73 billion ​and $76 billion.

title: SpaceX enters $40 billion deal with Apollo for AI chip financing
description: Each lease ​will run a little over five years ​from the day the equipment arrives, according to ⁠a regulatory filing
content: SpaceX said on Monday an affiliate of Apollo Global Management will buy AI chips and server hardware ‌and lease them to the rockets-to-AI firm, in a deal with total principal payments of about $40 billion. Each lease ​will run a little over five years ​from the day the equipment arrives, according to ⁠a regulatory filing. The deal highlights SpaceX's heavy ​spending, as it tries to capitalise on surging ​demand for computing power to help bankroll its Moon and Mars ambitions. The company aims to finalise the deal by ​the end of the year. The leases are ​expected to start in the first half of 2027, once ‌the ⁠chips are delivered. Read: Bill Gates warns of 20 years of turmoil from artificial intelligence On Sunday, CEO Elon Musk said on X that SpaceX had "closed" $40 billion in debt financing for graphics processing units. Musk said the funding ​mainly targeted ​chips arriving ⁠in the first and second quarters and would not be "a major factor ​this quarter." CFO Bret Johnsen had said ​SpaceX still ⁠expects fourth-quarter capital expenditure of $35 billion to $40 billion. Reuters reported earlier this month that SpaceX was in ⁠talks ​with banks and asset managers ​to raise $40 billion to buy Nvidia chips.

title: Changes on cards as Pakistan face Sri Lanka
description: Hosts weigh team reshuffle; Saim Ayub exits squad over poor form
content: Pakistan, who have already qualified for the final, are expected to make changes to their playing XI when they take on Sri Lanka in their last league game of the ODI tri-series at Gaddafi Stadium Lahore on Tuesday. The match starts at 1pm PST. Left-handed opener Saim Ayub, who was under an immense pressure due to his poor form, was released from the squad on Monday and replaced by Sahibzada Farhan. Farhan had led his T20 side to a 2-1 victory in the three-match series against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi. Farhan was in sublime form during that series as a skipper, but the ODI squad had been announced earlier, ruling him out of selection at the time. He has now been given an opportunity and could feature in Tuesday’s game. Maaz Sadqat, another hard-hitting left-handed opener, is also in the squad as cover for players carrying minor niggles. Although Pakistan have managed totals of more than 300 in their first two games against Sri Lanka and England, they have major concerns at the top of the order. Fakhar Zaman has also been out of form, scoring only 26 runs in three matches. Babar Azam failed to convert promising starts in the first two games before falling for just ten against England on Sunday, a match Pakistan won by one wicket thanks to Shadab Khan’s maiden ODI century. Pakistan urgently need to promote Agha Salman in the batting order. The former Pakistan captain is in prolific form and could provide greater stability in the top order if given the opportunity to bat higher. Babar, Pakistan’s Test captain, will need to raise his game. He should play straight and go deep to make the things easier for his side. Naseem Shah, who has dislocated a finger on his left hand, is unlikely to return. Young pacer Razaullah impressed on his debut against England on Sunday, taking 2-38. It would be interesting to see what changes the team management will make for a game which will serve only as a practice show for the hosts ahead of their October 31 final. The Gaddafi Stadium pitch offered assistance to fast bowlers on Sunday, and Shaheen Shah Afridi made the most of the conditions, taking 4-46. He had also claimed 3-55 against Sri Lanka earlier in the series. Tuesday’s match is crucial for Sri Lanka, as a victory would secure their place in the final against Pakistan. If Sri Lanka lose, England will have another opportunity to qualify when they face the islanders in their final league match on Thursday. Sri Lanka are in excellent form after completing a record chase of 430 against England in their previous match, the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history. Pavan Rathnayake (130), Avishka Fernando (97), Dasun Shanaka (97) and Janith Liyanage (61) were the key contributors to that remarkable victory. The triumph also highlighted the superb batting intelligence of Sri Lanka’s batsmen at a time when they prepare for the 2027 ODI World Cup. Sri Lanka will need to bowl well against a Pakistan side featuring in-form batsmen Hasan Nawaz, Agha Salman and all-rounders Arafat Minhas and Shadab Khan, who has been in prolific form with the bat.

title: Shadab credits faith for comeback
description: Pakistan all-rounder reflects on match-winning innings against England
content: Pakistan all-rounder Shadab Khan credited the team management for maintaining faith in him despite a recent run of poor performances after playing a match-winning innings in Pakistan's one-wicket victory over England in the ODI tri-series on Sunday. “Obviously, in the recent past, I did not have such good performances. Criticism was directed at me and, obviously, at the management. Obviously, there was faith. I think they deserve more credit for having faith in me,” Shadab said. “As a professional, you keep trying to do your best. Unfortunately, I could not do that. But Allah gave me the courage, and He set the stage for me.” Shadab played a crucial role and his maiden hundred to guide Pakistan to victory, holding his nerve under pressure while batting alongside the tail as the hosts chased down 242 at Gaddafi Stadium. Reflecting on the moment when he appeared to have edged the ball, only for a review to save him, Shadab said he had believed the match was over. “I think I was so frustrated because, according to the situation and the way I received the ball, it was a boundary ball and I missed it.” “To tell you the truth, I did not think it was an edge. I was frustrated that I had missed the boundary and thought the match was over, because you work so hard to reach this stage. Haris had his own frustration, which he took out on me by asking for a review.” Shadab also praised tail-ender Haris Rauf for his composure during their decisive partnership, saying the fast bowler's patience and confidence had helped Pakistan cross the finish line. “To tell you the truth, we did not have any special cricketing plans. We were trying to have fun, and we were having fun. The situation was such that we were going with the flow.” “I think Haris deserves a lot of credit for the way he played because, obviously, a tail-ender wants to hit a six off every ball. But he had the patience that I wanted,” he said. “He had belief in himself and was telling me that if I did not get out, he would not get out either,” he was quick to add. “He had confidence and self-belief. Our last series was also difficult, and we had a long partnership, so I had a lot of confidence in him.” Shadab said he had remained focused on his plans despite the pressure of the occasion and the reaction of the crowd. “I honestly don't hear anything from outside when I am batting. You are in that zone where you are focused on your plans. As far as the crowd is concerned, I couldn't hear anything. I was in my zone.” The all-rounder said innings played on major international stages could have a greater impact on a team's fortunes, drawing a comparison with Australia's Glenn Maxwell and his remarkable World Cup performance. “If we talk about Maxwell, he played such an innings in the World Cup, and then the Australian team won the World Cup. I think a lot of things changed for that team because of that innings.” “Hopefully, if our team plays a series and performs well, that will help. But I think if you play such innings on a bigger stage, the team will benefit more.” Shadab said his approach was guided by the match situation rather than any particular motivation or anger, adding that batting positions should not prevent players from contributing to the team. “No, there was no particular motivation or anger.” “The situation was such that we were struggling. As a senior player, we had to assess the pressure and then play our innings. So, it was a simple plan. Whatever the batting position, I feel that you have a lot of options in ODI cricket. Wherever you bat, you can benefit the team.” Looking ahead to the World Cup, Shadab said Pakistan would aim to make the most of the opportunity if selected, while acknowledging the challenge of performing on the biggest stage. “It's still a long way off. When we are selected for the World Cup, we will try to play like this,” he signed off. “We have never played on such a big stage. But if we get the opportunity, we will do our best to win.” Shadab also credited his family for their support and said he wanted to contribute with both bat and ball whenever the team needed him. “Obviously, I want to give credit to my family. I want to name them. “After that, obviously, as I play in an all-rounder team, I expect to contribute in both departments. If I get a chance to bowl, I should bowl well and take wickets when the team needs me. And with the bat, I should perform when the team needs me.”

title: Australia eye Renshaw for final Test
description: Renshaw is in contention to open alongside Travis Head as Australia prepare for South Africa showdown
content: Australia are considering a change at the top of their batting order for the decisive third Test against South Africa, with Matthew Renshaw in contention to partner Travis Head after Nic Maddinson struggled in the opening two matches of the series. Maddinson, who managed only one score above ten in four innings following his recall to the Test squad, has been released alongside reserve wicketkeeper Sam Harper ahead of the series decider, which begins in Cape Town on Tuesday. The potential change follows Australia's batting difficulties in the second Test at Gqeberha, where South Africa responded emphatically to their defeat in the series opener by securing an innings and 31-run victory. Head has openly assessed Australia's struggles with the bat, increasing the prospect of a reshuffle as the visitors seek to regain control of the series and strengthen their position in the 2025-27 ICC World Test Championship. Australia won the first Test in Durban by 214 runs before South Africa levelled the series with their commanding performance in Gqeberha. The third Test, scheduled for October 27-31 in Cape Town, will determine the outcome of the series. Renshaw's possible inclusion offers Australia an alternative at the top of the order as they look to produce a more consistent batting performance against a South African attack that proved decisive in the second match. Australia could also face a late fitness concern over Steve Smith, who reported neck stiffness during the team's match-eve training session. The batsman is expected to be available for the series decider, although he is set to undergo a fitness test. Cameron Green and Josh Inglis are also available after recovering from their respective injuries, giving Australia additional options as they finalise their playing eleven. Captain Pat Cummins will lead a 16-member squad that includes Scott Boland, Alex Carey, Cooper Connolly, Green, Josh Hazlewood, Head, Inglis, Matthew Kuhnemann, Marnus Labuschagne, Nathan Lyon, Michael Neser, Renshaw, Smith, Mitchell Starc and Beau Webster. South Africa have also made an adjustment to their squad, with fast bowler Anrich Nortje ruled out after sustaining a groin injury during the second Test. The hosts will enter the decider with renewed confidence after their dominant display in Gqeberha, where they overturned the momentum of the series with a comprehensive all-round performance. For Australia, the challenge will be to address their batting inconsistency while managing fitness concerns ahead of a match that could prove significant in the wider World Test Championship campaign. With the series level at 1-1, both teams have an opportunity to finish strongly in Cape Town. Australia's decision over the opening partnership will be among the key selection calls as they attempt to prevent South Africa from completing a comeback victory.

title: McCullum urges England to learn
description: Coach targets improvement after narrow Pakistan defeat as World Cup looms
content: England head coach Brendon McCullum said his team must learn from their narrow defeats after Pakistan beat England by one wicket in the ODI tri-series at Gaddafi Stadium Lahore on Sunday, leaving their fate in the tournament out of their hands. The defeat was England's third in a series of games McCullum believed they could have won, with the coach acknowledging that his inexperienced side needed to improve ahead of next year's World Cup in South Africa. “Look, the boys are gutted to be honest. They were gutted after the last game and they're even more gutted after this one I think. Fought so hard for so long throughout that game, I thought we had an under par total,” McCullum said. “But we only got 240 because of some fight and some scrap towards the end of our batting innings. Started well with the ball, got ourselves in a very good position. And then found a way to be able to obviously be put under pressure again.” McCullum praised Pakistan’s batter Shadab Khan for his composed innings, saying his ability to manage the strike while batting with the tail provided valuable lessons for England's young players. “I thought Shadab was outstanding. I thought it was an incredibly poised innings that was full of cricket intelligence. And also I thought his ability to be able to manipulate his way to get enough access to the ball as he could,” he said. “Batting alongside the tail was a great example for our boys who are still young and inexperienced. But look, overall I think the boys are just gutted. We've now lost three games I think we could have won. And now our fate in this tournament is not really in our hands.” McCullum said England would review their performance through video footage, data and analytics, with the aim of improving their decision-making and composure under pressure before the World Cup. “We've been open to admit that we need to get better and we need to get experiences into these guys as quick as we could. It would be nice if those experiences were winning games like we found ourselves in the last three. But it's not the case.” He said England had limited opportunities to prepare for the global tournament, making it essential to learn from difficult situations. “When you've got an inexperienced line-up and you know you've got a big World Cup in 12 months' time and you've only got 20 games between now and then, you need to have that level of communication and those examples of real-time experiences.” Despite the disappointment, McCullum highlighted the fight shown by his players, praising Jamie Overton's bowling effort, Liam Dawson's spell and Ben Duckett's batting on a surface that did not necessarily suit his style. “I was very proud of the fight that our boys showed,” he said. “We knew we were behind the game at the halfway mark. But we fought our way to a total which gave us somewhat of a chance through a 40 run last week at partnership. And then we fought a lot throughout with the ball as well.” “I thought Jamie Overton bowling ten straight was a significant effort. Liam Dawson was obviously brilliant with his spell. And Ben Duckett on a surface which probably would not normally suit his style of batting.” “I thought he was able to find the right tempo to be able to at least kind of give us something to bowl at. But there was some other positive stuff as well. But sometimes it's just you take a little bit of time to be able to review those.” McCullum also backed captain Harry Brook, describing him as a brilliant player and an outstanding tactician, while saying England's plans to dismiss Pakistan's lower order had been frustrated by Shadab's ability to retain the strike. “We just weren't able to get enough access at them to be able to put them under that pressure. And a lot of that comes down to how well Shadab Khan was able to hold on to the strike.” England will have another opportunity to respond in their next match, with McCullum insisting his players remained motivated to represent their country and improve. “The guys are so proud to play for England. And they're gutted that they weren't able to get across the line in the last few games. They're incredibly motivated to keep getting better and to do all the fans proud as well. And that's what the opportunity is in a few days' time,” he signed off.

title: Saudi Arabia to face Palestine in Asian Cup opener
description: The hosts launch the 24-team tournament in Riyadh on January 7
content: Saudi Arabia will kick off next year's Asian Cup against Palestine in Riyadh on January 7, the Asian Football ‌Confederation (AFC) said on Monday after confirming the tournament schedule and venues. The 24-team continental championship will run from January 7 to February 5, with the opening match and final both ⁠scheduled at Riyadh's King Fahd Sports City Stadium. The tournament remains under scrutiny amid regional security concerns. AFC President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa earlier said that postponement to 2028 remained a possibility if required. The tournament will feature 51 matches across eight stadiums in three cities: Riyadh (five venues), Jeddah (two) ‌and ⁠Al Khobar (one). Defending champions Qatar begin their title defence against Thailand on January 11, while Japan open their campaign against Indonesia the same day. South Korea face ⁠Yemen, Australia take on Singapore and Iran meet China in their opening matches. The group stage concludes on January ⁠20, with the knockout rounds beginning on January 22. Saudi Arabia will host the Asian ⁠Cup for the first time, seven years before it stages the 2034 World Cup.

title: Imaan Mazari, Hadi Chattha move SC seeking suspension of ATC trial
description: In their petition, they argue that the trial court initiated proceedings in haste without granting them adequate time
content: Human rights lawyers Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chatha on Monday approached the Supreme Court against an Islamabad High Court (IHC) decision concerning their request to halt trial proceedings in an anti-terrorism case. In their petition, the applicants contended that unless the trial was immediately stayed, their pending application before the high court would become ineffective. They argued that the trial court initiated proceedings in haste without granting them adequate time and recorded the statements of prosecution witnesses in a single day. The petition further maintained that removing security barriers did not constitute terrorism, alleging that the trial was intended to harass the accused and subject them to political victimisation. The applicants claimed that the objective was to keep them behind bars. The Islamabad ATC framed charges against Imaan and Hadi on October 7 in a case relating to the alleged removal of security barriers and disruption of a designated route during the visit of an international cricket team. The court subsequently recorded statements from all seven prosecution witnesses, and the case has reached the cross-examination stage. The trial was shifted to Adiala Jail amid disputes over the accused’s production in court and defence lawyers’ access to their clients. Read: ATC orders jail authorities to facilitate lawyers' meetings with Imaan, Hadi Separately, Imaan and Hadi approached the IHC seeking to suspend the trial, alleging procedural violations in the framing of charges, including that they had not been physically present when indicted and had not received copies of relevant documents. The IHC heard their appeals on October 19 and said it would issue an order after hearing the respondents. The court dismissed their request for an interim order on petitions seeking the removal of anti-terrorism provisions from the case. However, it issued notices to the relevant parties on their separate plea seeking suspension of the trial proceedings. Background In January, the couple was handed a combined 17-year sentence on multiple charges linked to controversial social media posts that the prosecution argued amounted to an anti-state narrative under cybercrime laws. The same month, they filed applications for suspension of their sentences. Later, Imaan and her husband Hadi were rearrested on September 17, shortly after the Supreme Court granted them bail and suspended their sentences in the social-media posts case. They were produced before an Islamabad ATC in connection with a case registered at Kohsar Police Station. Police sought 30-day physical remand, but ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain rejected the request and sent the couple on judicial remand. The judge noted that although they had been nominated in the FIR as members of an unlawful assembly, no weapon had been attributed to either accused. Read More: Imaan may get case questionnaires On September 27, the court issued a contempt notice to the Adiala jail superintendent after the authorities failed to facilitate the signing and transmission of the documents and also failed to produce the accused through video link. Two days later, the issue was resolved after Imaan and Hadi signed the required powers of attorney. On September 29, the ATC ended the contempt proceedings against the jail authorities and separately confirmed that notices had been issued on the couple’s bail applications, with arguments scheduled before Judge Abul Hasnat. On October 7, the ATC had framed charges against Imaan and Hadi in the case related to the alleged violation of a designated route and incitement during the arrival of an international cricket team, despite defence objections that legal requirements had not been fulfilled.

title: LHC disposes of petition seeking release of Imran Khan's sisters after detention extended
description: Separately, Rawalpindi ATC defers verdict in Aleema Khan's November 26 protest case for fifth time
content: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Monday disposed of a petition for the release of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan’s three sisters after the Punjab government confirmed that their detention had been extended by another 30 days. Imran’s sisters were detained in September under Section 3 of the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance, 1960, as the PTI prepared for a planned protest march towards Islamabad. Aleema was detained on September 20, while Uzma and Noreen were taken into custody on September 21. Their initial detention orders were issued for 30 days. Appearing before Justice Abher Gul Khan, an assistant advocate general informed the court that the provincial government had approved the fresh detention period for Aleema Khan, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi following a recommendation by the Lahore deputy commissioner. The government’s lawyer also presented a report from the home secretary, confirming that the detention orders had been renewed on October 7. During the proceedings, the judge noted that the deputy commissioner had issued the detention orders but had not been included as a respondent in the case. He said the court could not grant relief beyond the scope of the petition. The judge subsequently disposed of the plea brought by Shahrez Khan, Aleema’s son. The petitioner was represented by lawyer Rana Mudassar Umar. The petition maintained that the sisters were still being held at Kot Lakhpat jail after their original detention periods ended; October 19 in Aleema’s case and October 20 for Uzma and Noreen. Challenging their continued confinement, the petitioner argued that none of the women was wanted in a criminal case and that preventive detention should not be used in place of proceedings under ordinary criminal law. He asked the court to secure their immediate release and direct authorities to present them before the bench. Uzma’s husband, Ahad Khan, and Shahraiz Khan were also present during the hearing. Last week, the LHC summoned the Punjab home secretary and the superintendent of Kot Lakhpat Jail over the continued detention of Imran’s sisters despite the expiry of their 30-day detention orders. Justice Khan adjourned further proceedings until October 28 and directed the two officials to appear before the court and explain why Aleema, Uzma and Noreen remained in custody after the expiry of their detention period. The Lahore deputy commissioner issued the 30-day detention orders. The orders cited police reports alleging that the women’s activities posed a threat to public safety and the maintenance of public order. The sisters subsequently challenged their detention in the Lahore High Court, seeking the annulment of the orders and their immediate release. On September 25, the court declined to suspend the detention notifications against Uzma and Noreen at that stage and sought responses from the relevant authorities. Rawalpindi ATC defers verdict in Aleema's Nov 26 protest case for fifth time An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Rawalpindi on Monday deferred its verdict for the fifth time in a case against Aleema Khan, sister of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan, over the November 26, 2024 protest. ATC Judge Amjad Ali Shah deferred the verdict, which will now be announced on November 26. The case against Aleema was registered at Sadiqabad police station and relates to a protest held at D-Chowk in Islamabad on November 24, 2024. Aleema could not appear in court as she remains detained. All 11 other accused in the case were present in the courtroom, along with defence counsel Faisal Mahmood Malik and the prosecutor. Also Read: LHC closes Aleema Khan facilities petition The case relates to the “final call” by Imran for nationwide demonstrations demanding restoration of PTI’s electoral mandate, the release of jailed party leaders and reversal of the 26th Constitutional Amendment, which he said had empowered a “dictatorial regime”. Supporters from across the country gathered at D-Chowk. The government ruled out negotiations and launched an operation against protesters, prompting PTI leaders to flee. The protest ended on November 26. Aleema, along with Imran's other two sisters, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan, were detained in September under Section 3 of the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance, 1960. The Lahore deputy commissioner issued the 30-day detention orders. The orders cited police reports alleging that the women’s activities posed a threat to public safety and the maintenance of public order. The sisters subsequently challenged their detention in the Lahore High Court (LHC), seeking the annulment of the orders and their immediate release. On September 25, the court declined to suspend the detention notifications against Uzma and Noreen at that stage and sought responses from the relevant authorities.

title: China's Xi opens Communist Party plenum, aims for firm governance measures
description: Meeting to address challenges party faces, including guarding against complacency, combating corruption
content: China's Communist Party ​began a meeting of senior cadres on Monday aimed at tightening discipline and pressing officials to implement Beijing's orders, ‌paving the way for a leadership reshuffle next year expected to extend President Xi Jinping's rule for another five years. Xi briefed the party's four-day Central Committee meeting on a draft document centred on "full and rigorous party self-governance" that state news agency Xinhua said addressed the challenges the party faced, including ​growing its governing capacity, as well as guarding against complacency and combating corruption, the president's signature campaign. The implementation of ​major decisions and plans of the Central Committee, the largest of its top decision-making bodies, must not ⁠be empty rhetoric, the Xinhua commentary read. The Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee on Monday started a four-day plenary session in Beijing, which focuses on strengthening Party self-governance. This marks the latest move by the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core to strengthen the Party… pic.twitter.com/ZOTQsQJk3k — China Xinhua News (@XHNews) October 26, 2026 "It is essential to both refine institutional rules and regulations to close loopholes and strengthen ​safeguards, and ensure their effective implementation," it said. Read: China's Communist Party ousts former ministers from Central Committee The Central Committee will convene in a closed-door meeting from Monday to Thursday, the fifth ​such gathering since the current cohort was formed in 2022 and therefore known as the "fifth plenum". Analysts say this could be the last major party gathering before its 2027 leadership reshuffle, when Xi is expected to hold on to the top job for a fourth term. "The plenum will present Xi as ​in control, and able to continue his command," said Kerry Brown, director of King's College London's Lau China Institute. "It is likely ​everything will be centred on him, to dispel any rumours or doubts about his physical fitness and ability to continue in his role." China’s Communist Party is gathering for its most important meeting of the year: the fifth plenum. Xi Jinping’s leadership purges and efforts to tighten party control are set to take center stage. Here’s what to watch for. https://t.co/TasreYLghF — Bloomberg (@business) October 25, 2026 With substantive ‌policy issues ⁠already largely set in previous gatherings, "this will be a plenum where appearances will matter as much, if not more, than substance," Brown added. Rooting out corruption for market predictability Xi has overseen a vast anti-corruption campaign in recent years which has led to the purge of hundreds of senior officials and top generals, even the president's one-time allies. Read More: China purges third Politburo member in deepening anti-graft drive While some say the purges, particularly those targeting the highest ranks of ​the armed forces, are destabilising and ​undermine combat readiness, the party ⁠has portrayed the campaign as both necessary and regenerative, saying the military must undergo a phoenix-like rebirth and "bathe in flames and be forged anew". The Xinhua commentary presented the anti-corruption drive as a ​demonstration of "sustained and systemic" self-governance to "ensure officials dare not, cannot and do not want to commit ​corruption". "For global investors ⁠and policymakers, this signals greater predictability," it said, arguing that China was also creating a more transparent environment for international cooperation as merit and the rule of law prevail over connections and bribery. Typically, seven plenums, each usually associated with a particular agenda, are held between ⁠major party ​congresses, which convene twice a decade. The party's constitution requires at least one ​plenum to be held every year. The fifth plenum usually deliberates the country's strategic blueprint, the five-year plan, but an unusually late third plenum, delayed for more than half a year ​until mid-2024, has disrupted the conventional scheduling.

title: Study in Switzerland finds over half of participants see fake news as 'major' social issue
description: More than half of respondents regularly encounter misleading information on social media
content: More than half of research participants in Switzerland consider disinformation a "major" social problem, expressing concern over misinformation, according to a study released Monday. The findings were published in the University of Zurich's Research Centre for the Public Sphere and Society 2026 Quality of the Media Yearbook, Swissinfo reported. Some 56.5% of the participants view "fake news as a major social problem," the report noted. The latest percentage represents a "significant" increase compared with five years ago, it added. The study found that more than half of respondents regularly encounter misleading information, particularly through social media, video-sharing platforms, and artificial intelligence chatbots. Some 42% were classified as "news-deprived," referring to people who rarely follow current affairs or rely on fragmented information from social media, making them more vulnerable to conspiracy theories. Read More: Meta to raise up to $95 billion in equity to fund costly AI expansion Researchers found that relying exclusively on platforms such as TikTok and Instagram offered no greater protection against conspiracy theories than avoiding news altogether. While overall news quality remained stable in 2025, media diversity declined, with 44.7% of national political coverage appearing across multiple German-language publications. The study also found that 57.7% of respondents considered public broadcasting important or very important. Meanwhile, technology platforms captured up to 2.5 billion Swiss francs ($3 billion) in annual advertising revenue, while domestic media revenues fell to 1.94 billion francs ($2.3 billion). The researchers called for countermeasures, such as media vouchers for young adults.

title: Ambani, Adani outlets among Indian publishers contesting Modi’s privacy law
