description: The October 6 lawsuit is the most high-profile challenge to Modi’s privacy law
content: A group of 21 news publishers, including companies owned by billionaires Mukesh Ambani and Gautam Adani, has challenged India's privacy ​law in court, arguing it would trample investigative work and let New Delhi identify journalists' sources, documents show. Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government last year announced ‌implementation of a privacy law to protect digital personal data of users, raising compliance requirements for platforms like Meta and Google. The publishers have said that since media outlets were not exempt, the law was an invasion of press freedom. Media companies received assurances in an August meeting with the government that the law would protect press freedom, but not having a written carve-out for journalists like in the European Union, Singapore and Britain was alarming, India's Digital News ​Publishers Association (DNPA) said in a confidential filing at the Supreme Court, reviewed by Reuters. The October 6 lawsuit, being reported for the first time and due to be ​heard on Tuesday, is the most high-profile challenge to Modi’s privacy law. Until now, only free speech activists and a group of smaller ⁠news outlets had challenged it. It also marks an unusual challenge to the government from businesses headed by Ambani and Adani, who opposition parties allege are close to Modi and get ​favourable treatment - charges the businesses and the government vehemently deny. DNPA and the media groups did not respond to requests for comment from Reuters, and neither did India's information technology ministry. The publishers ​are demanding that most of the law's contentious provisions, which kick in from May 2027, should be quashed. They are arguing the law could force a journalist to get prior consent from a person they want to investigate and force publishers to erase stories. They also say powers granted by the law to demand information could expose reporters' sources. The law would "render investigative journalism a benign and neutered recorder of events," ​the 698-page filing said. The provisions "constitute pre-censorship which is anathema to any democracy worth its name". The lawsuit comes amid accusations of declining press freedom in India since Modi took office ​in 2014. Critics say many mainstream media outlets have not done enough to scrutinise Modi’s government. India's ranking in Reporters Without Borders’ World Press Freedom Index fell to 157th out of 180 countries this year, ‌from 140th in ⁠2014 - but the government rejects the rankings. Modi's government says it respects press freedom and says India, which has a "vibrant press and media ecosystem" of hundreds of newspapers and TV channels, does not need validation from foreign bodies. Concerns over consent DNPA's members include Ambani's Network18, which has seven digital news platforms, Adani's NDTV (NDTV.NS), opens new tab and other marquee media groups including the Indian Express and Times Internet, which is part of the Times of India group, publisher of India's largest-selling English-language daily. A key concern in the law is the requirement of consent, the group's filing says. A ​social media platform or online retailer can seek ​consent from users when they sign up, ⁠but the DNPA has argued that requiring a journalist to notify the subject of an investigation and seek consent "would allow that subject to destroy evidence, intimidate witnesses". The law also lets people withdraw consent at any time and demand that their data be erased, without any ​public-interest safeguard, which DNPA says could force its members to unpublish or heavily redact a factual news report. Fear of sources at risk News ​publishers are concerned that ⁠a federal authority created under the law can impose fines for non-compliance, and grants powers to New Delhi to block access to any information in the "interests of the general public", which would curtail press freedom, DNPA said. Read More: India’s vanishing voters In an August letter to the government attached to the lawsuit, the group said India "has chosen to grant broad exemptions to the state, while failing to extend any corresponding ⁠protection to ​the press". No response was cited. From next year, the law will also let New Delhi order any organization ​handling personal data “to furnish such information as it may call for”, putting newsrooms at risk of having to divulge sources, the filing said. It can also deter whistleblowers from sharing information on corruption, corporate wrongdoing or electoral malpractice with ​reporters, the DNPA argued. The “nakedly unguided” provision must be quashed, the DNPA said, adding that the power “can extend to privileged communications in possession of a reporter or the informant.”

title: UK's Burnham says he agrees with principle of migration reform
description: Burnham became Prime Minister on July 20, after being elected leader of the Labour Party on 16 July
content: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday he stood by the principles of reform to the immigration system set out by his Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, following speculation that a political backlash could force them to be watered down. Asked if he agreed with Shabana's policy of extending the time it takes to secure indefinite leave to remain to 15 years from five for some migrants, Burnham told ITV's Good Morning Britain he stood by the principle of what she had put forward. "The Home Secretary is right, in my view, to bring forward changes that are based on the principle that settlement is a right to be earned, not just something that is granted automatically," he said. "And she'll set out the final conclusion soon." “I would like to see that happen in my lifetime.” Prime Minister Andy Burnham tells Good Morning Britain he believes Brexit has weakened the UK economy and its control over immigration. But he insists the British public must have the final say, ruling out a move to rejoin the… pic.twitter.com/ekqozF2USj — Good Morning Britain (@GMB) October 26, 2026 Burnham became Prime Minister on 20 July 2026, after being elected leader of the Labour Party on 16 July. He previously served as Mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 and returned to Parliament in June 2026 after winning the Makerfield by-election. The immigration proposals stem from reforms announced by the Secretary of State in November 2025. The plans would replace the existing five-year qualifying period for indefinite leave to remain with a system of earned settlement, under which the time required could vary according to migrants' circumstances and contributions. The proposals have faced criticism, including over the potential impact on migrant workers and whether the changes should apply to people already living in the UK.

title: Israel extends military barrier through farmland in southern Syria
description: Israeli forces continue bulldozing land for fortifications despite Syrian demands to halt project
content: Israeli forces continued bulldozing farmland in southern Syria on Sunday to extend a military barrier that Damascus has condemned as a violation of the 1974 disengagement agreement, the official SANA news agency reported. The work west of al-Hanout Farm in southern Quneitra province involves building an earth berm across privately owned agricultural land as part of the “Sufa 53” fortification project, according to the agency. Residents fear the work will affect extensive farmland west of the berm, SANA said. Read: Israeli strike on Gaza university kills three On October 18, Israeli forces bulldozed around 13 dunams (1.3 hectares) of olive groves in al-Hanout, near Saida village, and prevented farmers from reaching their remaining fields to harvest olives, the agency reported. Syria’s Foreign Ministry has called for the project to stop, describing it as a breach of the disengagement agreement and international resolutions. Sufa 53 comprises a military road, trenches and earth berms. Israel began construction in mid-2022 near Hadr in northern Quneitra before extending the project south through the province along the separation line with the occupied Syrian Golan Heights. Separately, Israeli troops entered northern Quneitra on Sunday and set up a temporary checkpoint on the road between Jubata al-Khashab and Ain al-Bayda, SANA said. Read more: Pak wants Israeli withdrawal from Syria The force, comprising several military vehicles, stopped and searched passersby before withdrawing. Israeli forces carried out a similar incursion near Jubata al-Khashab on Saturday, according to the agency. Since the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s regime in December 2024, Israel has carried out repeated incursions into southern Syria after declaring the 1974 disengagement agreement void and occupying the demilitarised buffer zone.

title: Pakistan, US agree to enhance cooperation in energy sector
description: Natalie Baker expresses desire to work with Pak to address energy needs, establish long-term energy supply contracts
content: Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik on Monday held a meeting with United States Chargé d’Affaires (Cd'A) Natalie Baker to discuss avenues for strengthening bilateral cooperation in the energy sector. During the meeting, Malik briefed Natalie on the measures taken by Pakistan to ensure energy security amid the evolving geopolitical situation. He highlighted that the ongoing conflict in the Middle East had created challenges for fuel availability, requiring proactive measures to maintain uninterrupted supplies. Read: Pakistan, US agree to deepen energy ties Natalie congratulated Pakistan on efficiently managing the fuel supply situation, noting that the country had not experienced a fuel shortage despite the challenging regional circumstances. Federal Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik met US CDA H.E. Natalie A. Baker to discuss enhanced energy cooperation. Both sides explored opportunities in LNG supplies, refinery upgradation and long-term energy contracts to strengthen Pakistan’s energy security and attract US investment. pic.twitter.com/TBjxCBu4CH — Petroleum Division, Ministry of Energy (@Official_PetDiv) October 26, 2026 The minister underscored Pakistan’s commitment to securing its energy needs and highlighted the ongoing engagement between the teams of both countries to explore opportunities for cooperation. He further noted that Pakistan’s refinery upgradation programme could offer investment opportunities for US financial institutions. Cd'A Baker expressed the desire to work closely with Pakistan to address its energy needs. She emphasised the importance of creating opportunities for US companies in Pakistan and expressed optimism about establishing long-term energy supply contracts, noting that such arrangements would be mutually beneficial and create opportunities for American businesses. The managing directors of Pakistan State Oil and Pakistan LNG Limited briefed the participants on the interest shown by US companies in LNG supply to Pakistan. Malik invited US companies to participate in the upcoming Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum, highlighting the investment opportunities available in Pakistan. Read More: US eyes investment in IT, mining, energy He also expressed deep appreciation for US support and emphasised that enhanced bilateral engagement would help strengthen energy cooperation and contribute to Pakistan’s long-term energy security. On October 25, Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Advocate Amjad Hussain Azar said that the US had shown interest in investing in the region's energy sector, and that a public-private partnership unit had been established for that purpose. On September 2, Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL) signed a contract with Baker Hughes, a US energy technology company, to deploy Mature Assets Solutions aimed at revitalising ageing oil and gas wells and increasing Pakistan's indigenous hydrocarbon production. Also Read: OGDC turns to US firm to boost oil output Mature Assets Solutions was designed to unlock greater value from established fields experiencing natural production decline. Baker Hughes would bring technical expertise, advanced technologies and integrated capabilities to support OGDCL in identifying production opportunities across mature assets. The partnership was part of OGDCL's comprehensive Production Optimisation Drive. Natalie, who attended the signing ceremony, described the agreement as a milestone in the US-Pakistan energy partnership, saying energy was a foundation of economic security and that collaboration would advance the shared goal of strengthening Pakistan's energy security. On February 22, in a meeting between Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and US Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick in Washington, the US expressed interest in investing in Pakistan's IT, mining, minerals and energy sectors.

title: James McAvoy  Juno Temple and Joey King team up for sci fi comedy  Almost You
description: Juno Temple  Joey King and James McAvoy star in  Almost You   a sci fi comedy exploring AI  grief and family bonds
content:
Juno Temple, Joey King and James McAvoy star in 'Almost You', a sci-fi comedy exploring AI, grief and family bonds
Juno Temple, Joey King and James McAvoy are set to star in Almost You , a science-fiction comedy exploring artificial intelligence and grief.
The film is directed by Matt Lipsey, known for his work on Ted Lasso and Inside No. 9 , and is currently shooting in Glasgow, Scotland, Variety reported.
The film follows Phoebe, a brilliant robotics engineer struggling to cope with the death of her younger sister, Edie. Using years of messages, videos and social media posts, Phoebe creates a lifelike artificial intelligence replica of her sister, defying the protocols of the technology company where she works.
Initially, the invention brings Phoebe comfort and happiness. However, the experiment soon forces her to confront difficult questions about grief, technology and the ethics of recreating deceased loved ones through AI.
Temple, known for Ted Lasso and Fargo , King, whose credits include The Act and We Were the Lucky Ones , and McAvoy, known for Atonement and The Last King of Scotland , will lead the cast.
Bankside Films has acquired worldwide sales rights to the project and will co-represent the UK and North America with UTA Independent Film Group.
Matt Lipsey said the film had initially been conceived as a story about the future but had become increasingly relevant to the present. He added that the cast would balance humour with emotional moments.
The project reunites McAvoy with producer Danny Page, who previously worked with the actor on California Schemin’ and Faith . Page will produce alongside Matt Schichter and Rory Stewart, with the film made in association with Parker Films, founded by McAvoy and Lisa Liberati.
Financing comes from Blazing Griffin, Homefront Productions, Yeti Entertainment and Head Gear Films.
With its combination of science fiction, comedy and emotional drama, Almost You explores the growing influence of artificial intelligence on human relationships and the boundaries of technology.

title: Faysal Quraishi  Hareem Farooq raise concerns over alleged paid campaign against  Mango Jutt
description: Warn coordinated negative publicity could hurt struggling film industry as movie reportedly loses cinema screenings
content:
Warn coordinated negative publicity could hurt struggling film industry as movie reportedly loses cinema screenings
Actors Faysal Quraishi and Hareem Farooq have raised concerns over alleged paid negative publicity targeting their Punjabi-language film Mango Jutt , arguing that coordinated online narratives could hurt not only an individual production but also Pakistan’s already struggling cinema industry.
Quraishi addressed the issue in an Instagram video, questioning the practice of publishing negative reviews without watching a film and warning that paid propaganda could undermine the industry’s efforts to bring audiences back to cinemas.
In his video, he questioned the broader consequences of what he described as paid propaganda, asking how many people were being harmed by those pursuing their own gains.
“Because it is a negative thing, which has been fed [to them], you’re saying the same thing. But seriously, while focused on your gains, how many people are you harming?” he said.
The actor also questioned the speed with which some reviews appeared after a film’s release, contrasting them with the approach of critics who took time to watch a production before assessing it.
“I know a lot of such serious film critics who wait for two to three days, for Friday, Saturday and Sunday to pass, before writing a review. But when there’s paid propaganda, the reviews start pouring in from the next day,” he said.
Quraishi maintained that a film’s commercial fate should ultimately be determined by audiences, acknowledging that mixed responses were a normal part of cinema. He argued that differences in taste should not be confused with deliberately manufactured negativity.
“Paid propaganda against anything, whether it’s a drama or a film, causes loss to the industry. We [already] have a very small industry,” he said.
He also highlighted the financial considerations involved in going to the cinema, suggesting that misleading or coordinated online narratives could further undermine moviegoers’ confidence in their choices.
Meanwhile, Farooq, who produced and stars in the film, shared screenshots on Instagram that appeared to raise questions about whether some negative posts about the film had been paid for.
In a separate Instagram post, Farooq highlighted reports that several cinemas had dropped the film, while others had reduced its showtimes or moved screenings away from prime-time slots. The post attributed the reported decline to competition from Hollywood releases and negative word of mouth.
Screenshots shared in connection with the discussion included an exchange about whether a negative post concerning the film was paid content. One message asked, “And is it a paid post?” The reply was affirmative, followed by the question, “Will you share the cost or budget?”
As both the film’s producer and a lead actor, Farooq has a direct stake in its performance. However, the concerns raised by the screenshots also touch on a wider challenge for filmmakers: distinguishing genuine audience feedback from content that may be commercially motivated.
Negative reviews remain a legitimate part of film culture, and audiences are entitled to express disappointment with a production. The concern raised by the actors is whether criticism is being presented as independent opinion when payment or coordination may be involved.

title: Rangers beat Guangdong in hockey
description: Sohail  Sami  Hammad seal Rangers    victory
content:
Huge crowd packs Narowal Stadium to witness thrilling clash
Pakistan Rangers scored twice in the second half to beat China’s Guangdong 3-1 in their hockey series match at the Sports City Hockey Stadium in Narowal on Monday.
A huge crowd thronged the stadium to witness the game.
The teams were levelled 1-1 at half-time after a tightly contested opening two quarters, but Pakistan Rangers gave a breakthrough in the 37th minute through Muhammad Sami, who struck a fine goal from short corner.
Guangdong responded three minutes later when Fong Xiang Xuan scored from a penalty corner in the 40th minute to level the match 1-1.
Pakistan Rangers put in their concerted efforts and regained the lead in the 45th minute as Aamir Sohail scored a fine field goal to put his side 2-1 ahead.
Muhammad Hammad then sealed the victory with another field goal in the 55th minute, giving Pakistan Rangers a two-goal cushion in the final quarter.
Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal and Pakistan Hockey Federation's (PHF) President Mohyuddin Ahmed Wani also witnessed the match as guests of honour.
Wani, who is also the secretary of the IPC, thanked Ahsan Iqbal and people of Narowal for supporting the successful staging of the showdown.
He said the enthusiastic reception from local hockey fans offered encouragement for the future of the sport in Pakistan. It was the fifth fixture of the series.
Earlier, Mari Energies defeated Guangdong 5-2 and Customs downed them 3-2.
Navy conquered Guangdong 3-1 at the Naseer Bunda Hockey Stadium Islamabad. The visitors defeated Army 4-2 in a shootout in a thrilling encounter.
PHF is making concerted efforts to bring back the lost glory of the country in hockey. Pakistan once ruled the world in the sport but now struggling in international circuit. However recent steps from the PHF have created hope of resurrection of the sport.

title: The Walsh Sisters  lands Disney  deal as Irish drama expands globally
description: Disney  acquires UK rights to The Walsh Sisters as the BBC and RT   drama expands globally ahead of its second season
content:
Disney+ acquires UK rights to The Walsh Sisters as the BBC and RTÉ drama expands globally ahead of its second season
Disney+ has acquired second-window UK rights to The Walsh Sisters , the comedy-drama based on the bestselling book series by Irish author Marian Keyes, Deadline reported.
The series will arrive on the streaming platform after its broadcast on the BBC.
The deal was secured by international distributor Cineflix Rights, which has also sold the series to broadcasters and streaming platforms across several territories. The show will air on TV2 in Norway, TV4 in Sweden and MTV Oy in Finland. Pickbox has acquired the series for the Balkans, while Yes has secured the rights for Israel.
Produced by RTÉ and the BBC, The Walsh Sisters became RTÉ’s highest-rated drama of the past two years following its first season. The broadcasters have renewed the series for a second season, which is currently in production.
The comedy-drama follows the dysfunctional but close-knit Walsh family, comprising five sisters, their mother and their bemused father. Set and filmed in Dublin, the series explores family conflicts, personal secrets and the complicated experiences of the sisters as they navigate everyday life.
Season 2 will see Caroline Menton, Danielle Galligan, Máiréad Tyers, Stefanie Preissner and Louisa Harland reprise their roles as the five Walsh sisters. Preissner also adapts Keyes’ books for television. Aidan Quinn and Carrie Crowley will return as the sisters’ parents.
The series has also secured distribution deals in Australia through Stan, while Roku’s Howdy streaming service has acquired US rights.
Sandra Piha, Cineflix Rights’ senior vice-president of sales for the UK, Ireland and Nordic markets, said the series had resonated with audiences through its blend of comedy, drama and emotion. She added that the latest agreements would bring the show to more international viewers.
The Walsh Sisters is produced by Cuba Pictures, part of Vice Studios, and Metropolitan Pictures for RTÉ, in association with the BBC, Screen Ireland and Cineflix Rights.

title: Strikers crowned National T20 champions
description: Masooma Zahra holds nerve in final over to seal thrilling win
content:
Masooma Zahra holds nerve in final over to seal thrilling win
Strikers clinched the National Women’s T20 Tournament title with a dramatic one-run victory over Stars in the final on Monday, defending a modest total of 115 at Iqbal Stadium in Faisalabad.
Led by Natalia Parvaiz, Strikers held their nerve in a tense finish as pacer Syeda Masooma Zahra defended 11 runs in the final over, restricting Stars to 114-8 in their 20 overs.
The victory capped an unbeaten campaign for Strikers, who won all nine of their matches in the tournament. They received a cash prize of Rs1.5 million, while runners-up Stars earned Rs1 million.
Stars appeared within reach of victory through Sadaf Shamas, the tournament’s leading batter, who scored 37 from 38 balls, including three fours and two sixes. Diana Baig added an unbeaten 16 from 17 deliveries to keep the chase alive.
Diana struck a four off the first ball of the final over, but Stars could not find the runs needed to complete the chase.
Off-spinner Rameen Shamim played a decisive role in Strikers’ defence, returning figures of two wickets for nine runs from four overs. Fellow off-spinner Omaima Sohail conceded only 11 runs in her four overs and took two wickets.
After opting to bat, Strikers made a brisk start through Eman Naseer, who scored 20 from 12 balls, and Aqsa Habib. The team subsequently lost five wickets for 58 runs before captain Natalia steadied the innings with a top score of 30 off 31 balls.
Contributions from Huraina Sajjad (16) and Rameen (15) helped Strikers reach 115 all out in 19 overs.
Leg-spinner Hafsa Khalid led the Stars attack with 4-29, while captain leg-spinner Tuba Hassan claimed 2-17. Diana also took two wickets.

title: Chris Brown avoids prison as London court suspends sentence over nightclub attack
description: Judge Tony Baumgartner cited Brown   s guilty plea and mitigating circumstances when explaining the ruling
content:
Judge Tony Baumgartner cited Brown’s guilty plea and mitigating circumstances when explaining the ruling
Chris Brown has avoided immediate prison time after a London court sentenced him for attacking music producer Abraham Diaw with a tequila bottle at a nightclub in February 2023.
The Grammy winning singer, 37, received an eight month prison sentence suspended for one year at Southwark Crown Court on October 26, according to the Associated Press . The ruling means Brown will not serve the sentence immediately, provided he complies with the conditions of the suspension.
Brown had faced up to three years in prison after pleading guilty in July to one count of affray over the incident at Tape, a private nightclub in London’s Mayfair district.
During sentencing, Judge Tony Baumgartner described the use of a glass bottle against Diaw’s head as dangerous, warning that the attack could have caused more serious injuries. Footage shown in court captured Brown being pulled away from Diaw after striking him twice with the bottle.
Despite the seriousness of the offence, the judge said a custodial sentence was not warranted in the circumstances. Brown’s guilty plea and other mitigating factors were considered, alongside his previous convictions. The judge also noted that the singer had maintained a clean record in recent years.
Brown left the United Kingdom after the 2023 incident. He was arrested at a Manchester hotel in May 2025 after travelling to the city for a concert. He had been released on bail of £5 million, allowing him to tour Europe and North America while the case proceeded.
The sentencing marks the latest development in Brown’s long history of legal troubles. He rose to fame as a teenager in 2005 and won Grammy Awards for his albums F.A.M.E. and 11:11 (Deluxe) .
His past legal history includes a felony conviction for assaulting Rihanna in 2009. Brown has also faced other legal incidents in the United States and abroad.
The latest ruling concludes the sentencing stage of the London nightclub case, following Brown’s guilty plea earlier this year.

content:
The thriller adapts Colleen Hoover’s bestselling novel about a ghostwriter who uncovers disturbing secrets
Anne Hathaway’s psychological thriller Verity is arriving on digital platforms this week after earning $162.7m worldwide at the cinema.
The film, based on Colleen Hoover’s bestselling novel of the same name, will be available to purchase or rent from Tuesday, October 27, according to the release information cited by Forbes . Viewers will be able to access it through Prime Video, Apple TV, Fandango at Home and YouTube Movies and TV.
Directed by Michael Showalter, Verity stars Hathaway as Verity Crawford, a successful author whose career takes a disturbing turn. Dakota Johnson plays Lowen Ashleigh, a struggling writer hired to complete Verity’s books.
When Lowen arrives at Verity’s remote estate, she discovers troubling notes that appear to reveal unsettling details about Verity’s relationship with her husband, Jeremy, played by Josh Hartnett. As Lowen investigates, she begins to question what is real and what may have been invented.
The film opened in cinemas on October 2 and attracted audiences despite a mixed critical response. It received a 31% critics’ score on Rotten Tomatoes, based on 186 reviews, while its audience score reached 71%.
Its box office performance proved considerably stronger than its critical reception. Verity earned $71.5m in North America and $91.2m internationally, bringing its worldwide total to $162.7m. The reported production budget was $40m, before marketing and distribution expenses.
The adaptation is the latest film based on Hoover’s work to perform well commercially despite criticism from professional reviewers. Her previous adaptations include It Ends With Us , Regretting You and Reminders of Him , which also attracted substantial cinema audiences.
For viewers who missed Verity in theatres, the digital release offers an opportunity to watch the thriller at home. The film is also continuing its theatrical run in North America, according to the report.

title: Brad Pitt reflects on overcoming difficult times amid Angelina Jolie divorce
description: Brad Pitt credits close friends and family with helping him through difficulty as he reflects on lessons from new film
content:
Brad Pitt credits close friends and family with helping him through difficulty as he reflects on lessons from new film
Brad Pitt has opened up about navigating difficult periods in his life, crediting close friends and family with helping him cope amid his long-running separation from Angelina Jolie.
The 62-year-old actor discussed the importance of trusted relationships while promoting Heart of the Beast , an upcoming survival thriller in which he plays a retired Special Forces veteran stranded in the Alaskan wilderness.
"When I think of the darker days, it was certainly my close relationships that I relied heavily on. Friends, dear close friends — a handful — close family, and was very open about my struggle," Pitt said, according to The Sun.
He added that being able to share his struggles with people who supported him had made a significant difference.
"And being able to be that free with people who love you and have your back, and that you love back, is everything. It's everything," he said.
Pitt's comments come amid continued public attention surrounding his separation from Jolie. The former couple, who share six children, separated in September 2016 following an incident aboard a private plane. Their divorce proceedings and family circumstances have remained subjects of media coverage.
The actor also discussed how working on Heart of the Beast influenced his perspective on dealing with challenges.
The film follows James Belmont, a retired Special Forces veteran who must survive in the Alaskan wilderness alongside Odin, his traumatised former combat dog, after a plane crash.
Pitt said survival experts involved in preparing the production offered advice that could also apply to everyday difficulties.
"The survivalists would tell us it's all about little wins," he recalled.
"You're going to suffer losses, you're going to suffer pain, but it's just getting to the next little win," he added.
Pitt explained that the approach helped him consider personal challenges as a series of manageable steps rather than focusing on the entire situation at once.
"I thought that equated to life in that way, in the sense of when we are struggling and going through many challenges, just getting to that next little win, not thinking about the big picture, just that next little win," he said.

title: Why Netflix users are watching less and opening app less often
description: Despite adding subscribers  Netflix has seen total viewing growth driven by its larger audience
content:
Despite adding subscribers, Netflix has seen total viewing growth driven by its larger audience
Netflix users are opening the streaming app less often and spending less time watching, raising questions about whether the service is keeping audiences interested as competition grows.
According to a report by Bloomberg , citing people familiar with Netflix’s internal figures, customers are using the app on fewer days each month than they did a couple of years ago. The company tracks how often people watch through a measure called qualified play days.
Although Netflix’s total viewing time increased slightly during the first half of 2026, the rise was linked to its growing subscriber base. Individual users, however, were spending less time watching.
One possible reason is that Netflix has struggled to produce as many major hits as it did in previous years. The company has also found it harder to bring viewers back for later seasons of some existing shows. With rival streaming services and free video platforms competing for attention, audiences have more choices about what to watch.
The trend reportedly began after Netflix introduced its password sharing crackdown in 2022. Executives initially expected the change in viewing habits to be temporary, but the decline continued.
There are some positive signs for the company. The report said Netflix has not experienced a major wave of cancellations, and its US cancellation rate remained steady at 2%, according to research firm Antenna. Netflix also said recent price increases had not triggered an unusual rise in cancellations.
Still, slower growth has worried investors. Netflix shares have fallen around 29% this year, while its share of US television viewing has struggled to grow as services such as YouTube attract audiences.
Netflix is trying to bring viewers back by investing in new programming and expanding into areas such as live sports and podcasts. The company has also made changes to its content leadership, with Peter Rice taking charge of its content strategy following the reported departures of senior executives Bela Bajaria and Dan Lin.
Netflix co-chief executive Greg Peters acknowledged that the company has more work to do to encourage growth, while maintaining that its business remains profitable.
The challenge now is giving subscribers enough reasons to keep opening the app.

title: Holland Taylor says    Two and a Half Men    never gave her a raise despite four Emmy nominations

content:
The actress continued appearing as Evelyn Harper after her six year contract ended, but only when she chose to
Holland Taylor has revealed that poor pay was a key reason she chose not to renew her contract on Two and a Half Men , despite earning four Emmy nominations for her performance on the long running CBS sitcom.
Taylor played Evelyn Harper, the mother of Charlie Harper, portrayed by Charlie Sheen, and Alan Harper, played by Jon Cryer. She appeared as a regular cast member for six years before deciding to step away from her contract.
Speaking on the Alchemy with Anthony Mason podcast, Taylor said her salary had remained at a level she had earned on a television series years earlier. She also expressed disappointment that her Emmy recognition did not lead to a pay rise.
“They never paid me very well on that show,” Taylor said, adding that she had received four supporting actress Emmy nominations during her time on the sitcom but had never been given a raise.
When her six year contract came to an end, Taylor told the production team she did not want to continue under the same arrangement. Instead, she offered to return for guest appearances when she felt like doing so.
The actress recalled that the producers were surprised by her decision and initially believed she was negotiating for better pay. She said they told her they could not afford to increase her salary, but insisted that money was not the point of her choice.
“I loved a lot about that show, but they were not full of courtesies,” she said, reflecting on her experience.
Taylor explained that leaving the contract gave her greater control over her schedule. She could accept guest appearances when convenient and decline them when she had other commitments.
Her departure from the regular cast did not mean she had completely severed ties with the sitcom. She returned occasionally as Evelyn, maintaining her connection to the characters and the series.
Two and a Half Men premiered in 2003 and ran for 12 seasons, ending in 2015.

Comedian Josh Johnson criticised Art of Play’s response to Kelly Clarkson following their dispute over mechanical bird
Comedian and The Daily Show host Josh Johnson has criticised Brooklyn toy shop Art of Play over its handling of a dispute with singer Kelly Clarkson concerning a mechanical singing bird named Molly.
The controversy began after Clarkson visited the store and expressed interest in purchasing the animatronic bird, which had a $15,000 price tag displayed beside it.
Art of Play said Molly was not for sale but claimed the Seattle-based artist who created it could make an identical version for that price.
The store also said an employee offered Clarkson a cheaper alternative that she could take home immediately. Clarkson subsequently accused the shop of giving her the "Pretty Woman" treatment and claimed it had lost a significant sale.
On October 20, Johnson shared a stand-up performance recorded at Milwaukee’s Riverside Theatre, in which he discussed the dispute and criticised the store’s response.
"Just because she's in plain clothes, just cause she's chilling, people look her up and down like she can't afford it and say I'mma show you something cheaper. That's wild. You know?" Johnson said.
The comedian, who lives in Brooklyn, added that he had encountered shops where customers were judged by their appearance.
He also questioned the store’s decision to respond to Clarkson’s initial criticism with a reference to her song Stronger (What Doesn't Kill You).
"This is just me. I'm not telling you how to feel. This is just me. When I read that, I was like, no, y'all were rude," Johnson said.
He also argued that the shop’s subsequent explanation differed from its initial response.
"You made it sound like Kelly Clarkson walked in and was trying to buy the cash register," he joked.
Johnson further described the store’s response as "purposely misleading" and said Clarkson could reasonably have assumed the bird was available for purchase because of the displayed price.

Man was arrested after allegedly threatening crew member with knife during 'Miami Vice' filming in Brooklyn
Filming for Miami Vice '85, starring Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler, was reportedly interrupted after a man allegedly threatened a production crew member with a butcher knife in Brooklyn, New York, on Friday, October 23.
According to TMZ , the incident began at around 11pm when a 23-year-old man identified by police as Alex Perez allegedly entered the filming location and disrupted production.
He reportedly became involved in a confrontation with a 43-year-old male crew member before allegedly producing a large knife.
The incident occurred near Bay Parkway and McDonald Avenue, close to Washington Cemetery. The alleged threat was directed at the crew member, and authorities have not indicated that Jordan or Butler was specifically targeted.
Footage obtained by TMZ reportedly showed a production staff member escorting Perez away from the filming area before he allegedly removed a knife from his sweatshirt pocket. Police arrived at the scene and arrested him at approximately 11.17pm.
According to NBC New York, police confirmed that the weapon had been recovered.
"The individual was then taken into custody without incident, and the knife was recovered," police said in a statement.
No injuries were reported, although filming reportedly stopped for the remainder of the night.
Perez was charged with second-degree menacing with a weapon and fourth-degree criminal possession of a weapon. TMZ also reported that he had previously been arrested five times, although details of the outcomes of those cases were not provided.
Miami Vice '85 is directed by Joseph Kosinski, known for Top Gun: Maverick and F1 . Jordan plays undercover detective Ricardo "Rico" Tubbs, while Butler portrays his partner, James "Sonny" Crockett. The characters first appeared in the original NBC crime series, which ran from 1984 to 1989.
The film also features Walton Goggins, John Leguizamo, André Holland, Alden Ehrenreich, Whitney Peak, Camila Morrone and Danny Ramirez.
Production has taken place across New York and New Jersey, with the film scheduled for theatrical release on May 19 2028. It remains unclear whether the Brooklyn incident will affect the production schedule.

content:
Chappell Roan remix helps Rodrigo’s album earn 75,000 equivalent album units in the latest tracking week
Olivia Rodrigo has returned to No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love , securing a third nonconsecutive week at the top of the US albums chart dated October 31, 2026.
The album climbed from No. 2 after earning 75,000 equivalent album units during the tracking week ending October 22, according to Billboard . Its total increased by 15%, helped largely by the October 15 release of a new remix of single “Expectations” featuring Chappell Roan, accompanied by an official music video.
Streaming accounted for most of Rodrigo’s weekly total, contributing 63,000 equivalent album units, up 19%. The album’s tracks generated 67.14 million on demand official streams. Sales contributed 11,000 units, while track equivalent albums added another 1,000.
Rodrigo’s record initially topped the chart for two consecutive weeks in June and has remained within the top five throughout its 19 weeks on the ranking.
Zach Bryan secured second place with Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs , which debuted with 65,500 equivalent album units. The eight song release includes collaborations with Lana Del Rey and Turnpike Troubadours and marks Bryan’s sixth album to reach the chart’s top 10.
Streaming contributed 59,500 units to Bryan’s debut, with the album generating 60.46 million on demand official streams. Download sales accounted for 5,000 units, while track equivalent albums contributed 1,000. CD and vinyl editions are scheduled for release in December.
The album is Bryan’s second release of 2026, following With Heaven on Top , which debuted at No. 1 in January. He is scheduled to begin the Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs Tour on April 28, 2027.
Morgan Wallen’s I’m the Problem held at No. 3, followed by Ella Langley’s Dandelion at No. 4. Taylor Swift’s The Life of a Showgirl fell to No. 5, while Noah Kahan’s The Great Divide moved to No. 6.
The Billboard 200 ranks albums using a combination of sales and streaming activity, with data compiled by Luminate.

Amanda Seyfried’s limited series The Dropout has experienced a major surge in viewership following the theatrical release of Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s documentary You Can See Everything , which examines disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes.
According to entertainment analytics company Luminate, The Dropout attracted approximately 105,000 views between October 16 and October 22, 2026. That figure represented a 700% increase from the roughly 13,000 views recorded during the previous week.

The documentary also features Seyfried discussing her performance with Fielder. In a further twist, the actress reprises her portrayal of Holmes in newly staged scenes that extend the story beyond the events depicted in the miniseries.
These sequences include recreations involving Holmes, her husband Billy Evans and the documentary filmmakers, as well as a scene set in federal prison. Holmes is serving an 11-year sentence following her conviction for defrauding investors in Theranos.
The renewed interest in The Dropout follows the documentary’s strong theatrical performance. According to the figures cited by Forbes , You Can See Everything earned $15.6m during its opening weekend before expanding into wider release. Its reported domestic box office total subsequently reached $45.1m.
Created by Elizabeth Meriwether, The Dropout dramatises the rise and collapse of Theranos, the blood-testing company founded by Holmes. Seyfried won a Primetime Emmy Award for her performance, with the series receiving six nominations overall.

Mercedes driver needs two points to secure maiden title
Kimi Antonelli said his mindset will not change as he heads to next week's race in Mexico seeking the two points he needs to become Formula One’s youngest world champion. The 20-year-old Italian delivered a well-executed and dominant drive to claim his ninth victory this year for Mercedes in Sunday’s United States Grand Prix and move within reach of the title. Antonelli is on the brink of smashing the previous record for youngest champion, held by Sebastian Vettel who was 23 years and 133 days old when he won his first title in 2010 He is also set to become the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953. "The best way, the perfect way, would be to finish off in style and then just enjoy the rest of the season,” he said. "I'm very aware that it's very close but the mindset doesn't change. "I want to finish the season on a high in order to then go with high hopes into 2027. But we'll first focus and worry about finishing this well, and then we'll see." After Sunday’s triumph at the Circuit of the Americas he leads with 365 points ahead of nearest rival and team-mate George Russell on 242 and seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari on 241. He will be champion if he finishes in the top nine or, if he doesn't score, Russell or Hamilton fail to win. But on current form, after winning again for the first time in four races, he looks certain to take the title in his own happy, generous and infectious style. "That was the perfect way to end the weekend,” he said. “It was an incredible team effort, especially from strategy, to believe in me and go for one stop because I wasn't sure whether one or two stop was the quickest. "But I’m really happy that we made it stick. Today was a really important victory for me and for the team, especially after having a couple of difficult races, so being back on top feels very good."

Their engagements included receptions, school visits and charity appearances, which reportedly resembled an official royal visit despite their decision to step back from senior royal duties in 2020.
Speaking to The Mirror in May 2024, Quinn, author of Scandals of the Royal Palaces: An Intimate Memoir of Royals Behaving Badly, described the reported reaction from the King and Prince William.
"All the signs were there, as the couple were greeted with dances, receptions, visits to schools and charities," Quinn said. "William is absolutely furious and determined to find a way to stop this happening in [the] future. Charles is said to be angrier than anyone has ever seen him."
Quinn also claimed that Charles and William had discussed removing the couple’s royal titles but were concerned about the potential consequences.
Quinn said they "have had lengthy discussions about stripping Meghan and Harry of their royal titles, but they are terrified this would backfire and make the situation worse."
Although Harry and Meghan no longer use their His and Her Royal Highness stylings, they have retained their Duke and Duchess of Sussex titles.
Quinn argued that removing the titles would not necessarily prevent the couple from continuing their international activities or receiving public welcomes. He added that the King and William did not want to provide them with further grounds for complaint.
The couple’s relationship with the royal family remains strained. In September, a letter written on Charles’s behalf reportedly clarified that Harry and Meghan would not return as working royals and would live as "private citizens".
Harry has also expressed a desire to reconcile with William. Speaking on GQ’s One More Question podcast, he said, "I want it to work out," adding that reconciliation was important given other events in the world.

title: Anthropic sued over alleged use of 274 Elvis Presley songs to train AI models
description: The lawsuit could add pressure on AI companies over how they use copyrighted music
content:
The lawsuit could add pressure on AI companies over how they use copyrighted music
Anthropic is facing a copyright lawsuit from the company that manages Elvis Presley’s music and likeness, which alleges that the artificial intelligence developer used 274 of the singer’s songs to train its AI models without permission.
Authentic Brands Group, which controls licensing rights connected to Presley’s music and image, filed the lawsuit on Friday, according to The Guardian . The case accuses Anthropic of infringing copyrights belonging to songs from the late singer’s catalogue.
The works named in the allegations include “Can’t Help Falling in Love”, “All Shook Up” and “A Little Less Conversation”. The lawsuit claims Anthropic used copyrighted material to train Claude, its AI model, and alleges that the system can generate outputs that infringe music copyrights.
The plaintiffs are seeking up to $150,000 for each allegedly infringed track, amounting to approximately $41m across the 274 songs. These are claims made in the lawsuit, and the allegations have not been established as facts in court.
The legal action adds to growing disputes over whether AI companies can use copyrighted creative works to develop their systems without obtaining permission or paying rights holders. Music labels and artists have raised concerns that their recordings, lyrics and distinctive voices could be used to produce AI generated material without their consent.
The case could have wider implications for music rights owners seeking to protect their catalogues as AI technology develops. Presley’s catalogue remains commercially valuable decades after his death, making the licensing and control of his work an important issue for the rights holders.
In its complaint, the plaintiffs argue that Anthropic’s business model relies on the use of copyrighted material on a large scale. The lawsuit also questions whether safeguards introduced by the company are sufficient to prevent its AI systems from producing material that allegedly infringes copyright.
Anthropic has faced other copyright disputes involving creative works used in AI training. The Presley case, however, brings the interests of a major music catalogue rights holder directly into the debate.
The outcome may help clarify how copyright law applies when AI developers train models using existing songs and other protected creative material.

In a career retrospective with the SAG-AFTRA Foundation, the 40-year-old actress recalled her initial doubts about the superhero film, which was eventually released in 2014 with Zoe Saldaña playing Gamora.
“I think turning down Guardians of the Galaxy was just so obvious to me at the time,” Seyfried said. “I’m like, ‘This is not going to be a hit. The tree and the raccoon are talking to each other.’ And I was just like, ‘This will ruin my career if this is bad. And there’s a high chance that this could be bad.’”

“I mean, obviously I was wrong. But I still don’t take back that decision. I made it for myself. I made it for my family that I knew I wanted to have,” she said.

Asked whether she would consider appearing in a superhero film in the future, Seyfried replied, “No, unless the superhero’s just, you know, walkin’ a lot.”

title: Kim Novak reveals unusual plans to have her body turned into compost after death
description: The Hollywood icon says painting and spending time in nature have shaped her outlook on life
content:
The Hollywood icon says painting and spending time in nature have shaped her outlook on life
Kim Novak has revealed that she wants her body to be turned into compost after her death, describing the idea as a meaningful way to remain connected to nature and help new life grow.
The 93 year old actress, best known for starring opposite James Stewart in Alfred Hitchcock’s 1958 thriller Vertigo , discussed her plans in an interview with Fox News Digital . She explained that she had made arrangements for natural organic reduction, a process that turns human remains into soil through controlled decomposition.
Novak said the idea appealed to her more than traditional burial or cremation. She described the process as an opportunity to continue being part of the natural world, explaining that trees and plants could grow with the help of the resulting soil.
The actress also revealed that she wanted friends and family to receive some of the compost after her death. She hopes they will use it to plant trees or shrubs, preferably trees, as a way of continuing her connection with nature.
Novak has reportedly chosen forget me nots as part of her plans, explaining that she sees the process as an honest and natural expression of life continuing after death.
Her outlook reflects a longstanding appreciation for the outdoors. After stepping away from Hollywood, Novak devoted much of her time to painting and living closer to nature. She has spoken about how art allows her to express herself while remaining connected to the environment.
Although she continued acting intermittently after the height of her fame in the 1950s and 1960s, Novak officially retired following the 1991 film Liebestraum . Her best known credits also include Picnic and Bell, Book and Candle .
Novak’s plans come as natural organic reduction has become an alternative to conventional funeral practices in some parts of the United States. The process is subject to local laws and regulations, and availability varies by location.

title: Kane favourite for Ballon d Or
description: The Bayern Munich striker s 73 goals in 65 games put him ahead of Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe
content:
The Bayern Munich striker's 73 goals in 65 games put him ahead of Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe
England captain Harry Kane is the favourite to win a wide open race to be crowned Ballon d'Or winner at a glitzy London ceremony on Monday, with Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe also in the running to be named the world's best footballer.
The 70th edition of the award, established by the magazine France Football, will be hosted in England for the first time in recognition of the first winner Stanley Matthews and fittingly could have a first English winner for 25 years.
Bayern Munich striker Kane struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, leading the German giants to a league and cup double and England to the semi-finals of the World Cup.
"I'd love to be able to achieve something like that. I would be a massive milestone in my career," said the 33-year-old.
But semi-final exits in both the Champions League and World Cup for Kane means the outcome is far from certain.
"I think my wife would prefer to know and my family … it’s very stressful for everyone," he added.
"I can see why they don't tell people. They want everyone to go, all the big names, and there will be more people watching it if they don't know."
Yamal finished second to Paris Saint-Germain's Ousmane Dembele last year and the 19-year-old Barcelona superstar seems destined to be a Ballon d'Or winner one day.
However, after a hamstring injury ended his club season early, he was far from the shining light of Spain's World Cup triumph that was built on being the best collective unit.
Yamal was pipped to both the player and young player of the tournament by his Barcelona team-mates Rodri and Pau Cubarsi.
That has not diminished his bullish confidence ahead of the ceremony.
"For me, Mbappe and me, we're the two best players in the world," Yamal said last month.
"I honestly think that, as the best in the world, maybe there are two of us, and this year I would deserve it because of what I've won."
Mbappe, by contrast, boasts plenty of personal milestones without medals for either Real Madrid or France.
The 27-year-old was top goalscorer in La Liga, the Champions League and the World Cup without winning any of those trophies.
His 10 World Cup goals made him the top goalscorer in the competition's history on 22.
"Being the all-time top scorer in World Cup history, overtaking all the great legends in the history of the sport in the most important tournament there is, is something that really stands out," said Mbappe.
One football journalist from each of the 100 top nations in FIFA's rankings is invited to cast votes for their top 10 players from a 30-man shortlist, allocating a maximum of 15 points down to one based on their ranking.
The Ballon d'Or goes to the player who accrued the most points.
Although the award carries no cash prize, it can generate huge bonuses from clubs and commercial partners as well as increasing a player's overall marketing value.
Alexia Putellas is the frontrunner to win the women's award for the third time with Aitana Bonmati's three-year reign to come to an end after an injury-hit year.
Putellas, winner in 2021 and 2022, was part of the Barcelona side that regained the Champions League last season before moving to London City Lionesses.
Her former club team-mate, Poland's Ewa Pajor is the main challenger to Putellas after she netted 11 Champions League goals in Barca's latest triumph.

title: Manchester United battered by Bournemouth
description: The Red Devils drop to 16th  just one point above the relegation zone
content:
The Red Devils drop to 16th, just one point above the relegation zone
Manchester United slumped further into crisis with a 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday that plunged Michael Carrick's future as manager into doubt.
Carrick's bold decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes backfired as defeat stretched United's winless run to eight games and left them 16th in the Premier League, just one point above the relegation zone.
For the third time in four seasons, the Cherries won 3-0 at Old Trafford as goals from Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson secured a fully deserved win for Marco Rose's side.
"What is next? I don't know," said Carrick.
"I'll always do what's best for this football club. I've said it all along, I don't change that now. I love what I do. I love the responsibility, but we'll have to wait and see."
Fernandes was critical of Carrick's tactics in a 4-1 thrashing by Champions League debutants Como on Wednesday.
The United boss said the decision to leave out last season's Premier League player of the year was a "purely football" driven, but it was hard to believe Fernandes was not being punished as he was left on the bench for the entire match.
Carrick was taunted with chants of "you're getting sacked in the morning" from the Bournemouth fans.
But on this evidence, dismissing another manager is far from a quick fix for a club that has fallen dramatically from grace since Alex Ferguson's retirement 13 years ago.
A strong finish to last season during Carrick's interim spell in charge secured third place in the Premier League, but was aided by a lack of European or domestic cup football.
United have won just twice -- against newly-promoted Ipswich and Azerbaijani side Sabah -- in 12 games in all competitions this season.
"I definitely knew that we hadn't cracked it and there was a lot of work to be done, but that doesn't mean to say that it should have gone this way," added Carrick on the contrast between this season and last.
Bournemouth began the day behind the Red Devils in the table after a difficult start for Rose.
But just three days after beating AC Milan 3-0, they outclassed another giant of the European game.
Rayan opened the floodgates when he connected sweetly with Justin Kluivert's free-kick on 38 minutes.
Five minutes later, Leny Yoro stumbled under pressure from Adrien Truffert and the French full-back had a simple task to square for Tavernier to tap into an empty net.
Many expected Fernandes to be stripped and ready for the start of the second half, but he remained on the bench and the United performance got no better.
Inside the first minute of the restart Evanilson found the net, but was flagged offside.
That let-off mattered little as Bournemouth could have run out even more convincing winners.
Senne Lammens denied Rayan before the Brazilian winger fired wide after racing past Lisandro Martinez.
Evanilson did finally add a third 20 minutes from time when he rounded Lammens before curling in an exquisite finish from a narrow angle.
The United support unleashed their fury at the club's unpopular owners, the Glazer family, rather than Carrick in the closing stages.
Carrick applauded the Stretford End and touched his chest as he made his way down the tunnel.
However, it is the manager who will likely be the fall guy after another miserable afternoon for the 20-time English champions.

title: Inter rally late to down Fiorentina
description: The Nerazzurri reclaim top spot with two stoppage time goals
content:
The Nerazzurri reclaim top spot with two stoppage-time goals
Inter Milan struck twice in stoppage time to complete a remarkable 2-1 comeback win over Fiorentina and return to the summit of Serie A on Sunday, while Juventus and AC Milan both bounced back with victories.
Alex Jimenez's rocket strike had struggling Fiorentina heading for a shock win at San Siro, but Marcus Thuram levelled in the 91st minute before winning a penalty that Piotr Zielinski converted in the 98th minute.
The result lifted Inter to first place, level with surprise fellow pace-setters Lazio on 22 points, while the Florence club's winless run stretched to four games to keep them in 18th spot.
Later, Juventus claimed a 2-0 win over Lecce that lifted them into seventh place after a poor recent run of form and AC Milan bounced back from a heavy Europa League defeat to Bournemouth by beating Udinese 2-0 to go fourth.
Inter's fifth comeback win of the season saw them concede for the 10th time, but head coach Cristian Chivu was unconcerned by his side's defensive issues.
"That's football: sometimes you concede," Chivu told DAZN. "The important thing is not to let your heads drop and to maintain the same mentality. Ever since I arrived here, I've always said that games last 90 minutes."
"I don't want to see people feel sorry for themselves," Chivu added. "I want to see players respond to setbacks."
Chivu's side had the better of the first half but could not find a way past David de Gea, and it was the visitors who struck first against the run of play after 65 minutes.
Former AC Milan player Jimenez took debutant Inter goalkeeper Ivan Provedel by surprise with an audacious angled strike from distance that flew into the top corner.
Inter piled forward in search of an equaliser and eventually found it in added time when Thuram guided a shot into the bottom corner.
The France international then won a penalty in the dying seconds, which Zielinski converted to complete a pulsating victory.
Milan continued their unbeaten start to the league season and responded to their midweek drubbing in Bournemouth by claiming a confident win away to Udinese.
"We need time to work on several things, but we don't have time sometimes even to address the problems we had in the last game," Milan coach Ruben Amorim told DAZN.
"We are learning in the games, with videos, in team meetings, because for three weeks we have barely had any training. I am proud of these lads, because they are paying attention to everything."
Christian Pulisic put the Rossoneri in front by plucking a long Luka Modric pass out of the air and finishing calmly after six minutes, and Omari Hutchinson doubled their lead with his first Milan goal from close range in the second half.
Milan moved level with third-placed Roma on 18 points after claiming their first away league win.
It continued a desperate run of form for Udinese, whose losing run was extended to six games to leave them in 17th place.
Juventus claimed a much-needed win away to Lecce to relieve some pressure on head coach Luciano Spalletti.
Last weekend's humbling 3-0 defeat at home to Lazio left Juve in mid-table with one win in five league games, and a 2-2 midweek Europa League draw with Rennes did little to improve the mood in Turin.
But they bounced back as Weston McKennie steered home a Douglas Luiz free-kick before the Brazilian midfielder scored one of his own by whipping a shot into the bottom corner before the break.
Lecce threatened in the second half but their evening ended on a sour note when Kialonda Gasper was sent off in the final minute.
"We had a very good game in terms of playing quick, heads-up football," Spalletti said to Sky Sport.
"We dropped off a bit with our management of the second half and then everything became more difficult because we had less courage. We needed to do the same things we did in the first half."
There was an eight-goal thriller in Bergamo as Atalanta and Frosinone played out a 4-4 draw, while Genoa beat bottom side Venezia 1-0 to climb out of the relegation zone.

title: Monaco hold Lille as Rennes go top of Ligue 1
description: Marseille survive a late fightback to beat Le Havre 4 3
content:
Marseille survive a late fightback to beat Le Havre 4-3
Lille were made to pay for Tanguy Nianzou's red card as Monaco fought back to hold them to a 1-1 draw in Ligue 1 on Sunday, opening the door for Rennes to take the summit of the table thanks to a 3-0 win over struggling Strasbourg.
With Paris Saint-Germain and Lyon's match pushed back to Monday due to protests taking place across France this weekend, a winner in the principality would have gone three points clear at the top of the table.
But Lille have to content themselves with second spot on goal difference in the standings ahead of Monaco as both sides moved to 15 points -- one ahead of Lyon, reigning champions PSG and Paris FC.
Rennes then took full advantage of the draw as they eased past 16th-placed Strasbourg in Brittany to climb to 16 points.
At the Stade Louis II, Ethan Mbappe's goal midway through the first period put Lille in the driving seat but a straight red for Nianzou just after the hour was swiftly punished by Edan Diop as the hosts forced a draw.
"The plan worked well in the first half," Lille coach Davide Ancelotti said.
"We managed to stick together," he added of his side following the dismissal of Nianzou.
"The mood in the dressing room is positive because we held on until the end."
The younger brother of France and Real Madrid star Kylian showed the crisp finishing instincts associated with the Mbappe name as he darted into the box and whipped a first-time shot with his left foot past Lukas Hradecky on 24 minutes.
Monaco rarely threatened through the rest of the opening period but the match burst into life in the second half as Monaco's Paris Brunner passed up a golden opportunity in the 65th minute, before Lille defender Nianzou was given his marching orders for a reckless challenge.
The hosts then levelled in the 74th minute as Diop's cross toward Brunner evaded everyone and nestled in the far corner.
First-half goals for Boulaye Dia and Sebastian Szymanski put Rennes in the driving seat against Strasbourg.
Polish midfielder Szymanski netted just after the hour to secure the points for Franck Haise's team as they moved into top spot in Ligue 1.
That situation could change on Monday when PSG take on Lyon, although Luis Enrique's team will be without Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembele, captain Marquinhos and winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who suffered an anterior cruciate ligament tear during the team's 4-2 Champions League victory against Barcelona in midweek.
Elsewhere on Sunday, eighth-placed Marseille held on to beat bottom-of-the-table Le Havre 4-3 at the Stade Velodrome.
The home side were cruising at 4-0 up with just under 15 minutes remaining, until a Josh Maja brace either side of a Lamine Ndiaye goal set up a grandstand finale.
Toulouse and Troyes, as well as Angers and Lorient, played out goalless stalemates, while Auxerre drew 1-1 with Le Mans.

title: Real Madrid beat Barcelona in La Liga Clasico
description: Mbappe strikes twice in a 2 1 victory
content:
Kylian Mbappe struck twice to earn Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid a 2-1 Clasico victory over La Liga leaders Barcelona on Sunday at Camp Nou, cutting the gap to three points.
French superstar Mbappe opened the scoring before the interval and then slotted home late on to inflict Barca's first domestic defeat of the campaign after Raphinha had equalised for the champions.
Real Madrid remain third, behind Atletico Madrid and Hansi Flick's Barca, who had won their first nine games before a chastening week.
The Catalans suffered a second straight defeat after losing on Tuesday against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League.
Mourinho was delighted with his team's display in his first Clasico back at the helm of Madrid.
"My team had an extraordinary game, very organised, good concentration, with courage to play out from the back against a team that presses you a lot," Mourinho told reporters.
"We had chances for the second goal... obviously Barca had a strong reaction but we were calm and organised and at 1-1 we never lost our tranquility."
Barca had won six of the seven previous Clasicos since Flick arrived but were surprisingly subdued against Mourinho's side.
"You saw today, we lacked freshness," said Flick of his team's performance.
"It's the first defeat in La Liga, we won nine in a row. This is what we have to see.
"Defeats are a part of the game. We have to analyse, we have to make things better. Now it's important that we make a reaction."
Los Blancos, without suspended winger Vinicius Junior, won their fifth straight game across all competitions and are finding their footing under veteran Portuguese coach Mourinho.
After two trophyless seasons Madrid turned back to Mourinho to try and stop Barca's dominance, and this result will give them hope they are on the right track.
The opening period of the game was cagey, with few opportunities.
Barca defender Pau Cubarsi twice reacted well to shut down Mbappe, while Real Madrid's Marc Cucurella took a rapid liking for Lamine Yamal's shirt, constantly grabbing at the 19-year-old winger.
Anthony Gordon, playing in his first Clasico since joining Barcelona from Newcastle, backheeled the ball to Raphinha, who fired narrowly wide as Barca threatened.
The hosts were dealt a setback when young defender Xavi Espart pulled up hurt and needed to be replaced by Alejandro Balde before the half-hour mark.
Andriy Lunin, playing in goal for Madrid after Thibaut Courtois pulled out of the squad with flu, saved at his near post from Gordon before the visitors took the lead.
Mbappe scored his 10th league goal of the season and also his easiest, with Barca's Gerard Martin clearing a cross straight at the Frenchman, who deflected it into the net.
Barca responded by carving out a glorious chance for an equaliser but teenage sensation Yamal for once miscued in front of goal, firing wide when poised to level.
The game opened up and Yan Diomande came close to doubling Madrid's lead before half-time, drilling into the side-netting.
Martin redeemed himself early in the second half as he held off Jude Bellingham, who could neither beat the defender nor find a free Mbappe.
Raphinha, who had a quiet first half, pulled Barcelona level just after the hour mark.
Pedri fed the Brazilian, La Liga's top goalscorer with 13, who fired through Bellingham's legs and Lunin could not keep the shot out.
The Ukrainian goalkeeper did make a superb save to deny Martin at a corner, as Barcelona flowed forward with the wind finally in their sails.
Yamal bent an effort wide with Lunin at full stretch and Barca substitute Frenkie de Jong had a shot desperately blocked by Dean Huijsen.
There was a sting in the tail for the Catalans though as substitute Gabriel Jesus lost possession and Madrid raced through on goal.
Eduardo Camavinga beat Cubarsi and unselfishly cut the ball back for Mbappe to tuck home his second of the night into an empty net with Joan Garcia drawn out of position.
It brought up a century of goals since Mbappe joined Madrid from PSG in 2024, although the trophies to match have not yet followed.
"(Winning) is a good message today, but we can't think the season is done -- next week (at Racing) Santander we have to put in the same intensity," Mbappe told Real Madrid TV.

title: Antonelli wins US Grand Prix
description: The Mercedes driver triumphs by 13 078 seconds over Charles Leclerc
content:
The Mercedes driver triumphs by 13.078 seconds over Charles Leclerc
Kimi Antonelli claimed his ninth win of the season, but not quite the drivers' title on Sunday when he drove his Mercedes to a convincing triumph ahead of Ferrari's Charles Leclerc in an intriguing and strategic United States Grand Prix.
The precocious 20-year-old prodigy, seeking to be the youngest champion in F1 history and the first Italian since Alberto Ascari for Ferrari in 1953, came home 13.078 seconds clear of the Monegasque with four-time champion Max Verstappen finishing third for Red Bull.
Antonelli would have become the youngest ever champion, smashing the current record of Sebastian Vettel who was 23 years and 133 days when he won his fist title in 2010, if his Mercedes teammate George Russell had finished lower than eighth and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton failed to make the top four.
Seven-time champion Hamilton came on strong at the end to take that fourth spot while Russell took eighth which means Antonelli heads to next week's race in Mexico needing just to finish ninth to claim the two points he need to sew up the title.
"Good job everyone, that's the result we needed," said Antonelli on team radio. "Let's keep pushing.
"The whole team deserved it so much," he added later. "They put in so much work bringing this new package and finally to see the result is very pleasant.
"It was also a perfect execution from strategy to call for a one-stop and I'm pleased to see it stick.
"We are very close now (to the title) but we will try to finish on a high and hopefully we can clinch it very soon."
It was a strong showing from both Ferraris who would likely have fared better if they had followed up their dominant performances in practice with better qualifying.
"It was a good race, but unfortunately, we came up just short of our target which was victory, but it's positive for us," said Leclerc. "We had good pace."
Verstappen's third place means that mathematically he is now out of the running for a fifth championship title.
"I think our overall pace was not good enough and the tyres we had available were not the right ones," said the Dutchman. "But we are still on the podium even if we were a bit lucky at the end."
World champion Lando Norris of McLaren came in fifth with Isack Hadjar sixth in the second Bull.
Oscar Piastri was seventh for McLaren ahead of Russell, Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Pierre Gasly of Alpine.
Antonelli started the race in pole position and after a clean start already had a 2sec lead by the end of the opening lap, at which point the result never seemed in doubt, mechanical failure and pit stop disasters notwithstanding.
Verstappen was beaten off the start by Leclerc, who started in third, but the four-time world champion wasted no time in reclaiming second spot.
Leclerc, however, overtook him in the latter part of the race and Verstappen was left hanging on for third as Hamilton also closed.
Russell, who has had some terrible luck all season, was hit with a 5sec penalty for running off the track on the opening lap and struggled to get past McLaren's Oscar Piastri who came in seventh.
Norris, the outgoing champion, was running second until the closing laps when his tyres appeared to give up and he had to settle for fifth with Hadjar sixth in the second Red Bull.
While the other leaders all pitted early, Antonelli stayed out until lap 24 and rejoined fourth but he quickly picked off the cars ahead to reclaim the lead.

title: Eric Bauza dies at 46   Looney Tunes  actor s cause of death and estimated net worth
description: Bauza   s death was announced by his family in a statement posted to his Instagram account
content:
Bauza’s death was announced by his family in a statement posted to his Instagram account
Eric Bauza, the Emmy-winning voice actor behind Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and other Looney Tunes characters, died aged 46 from hypertensive cardiovascular disease, according to Los Angeles County Medical Examiner records cited by Variety .
Bauza’s death was announced by his family in a statement posted to his Instagram account.
“Eric Bauza, Emmy Award-winning voice actor and the modern voice of iconic Looney Tunes characters Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, along with dozens of other beloved cartoon characters, has passed away suddenly,” the family wrote. “More details to come.”
Born on December 7, 1979 in Scarborough, Toronto, Bauza built a successful career in animation, accumulating more than 400 acting credits since his first role in The Ripping Friends in 2001.
His credits included Coyote vs. Acme , Space Jam: A New Legacy and Looney Tunes Cartoons . He also voiced characters in Avatar: The Last Airbender , Rick and Morty and Minions & Monsters .
Bauza received multiple industry honours, including three Children’s & Family Emmy Awards, and earned five Daytime Emmy nominations.
At the time of his death, he was preparing to voice Daffy Duck in Bye Bye Bunny: A Looney Tunes Musical .
Regarding Eric Bauza’s net worth, online estimates place his wealth between $1 million and $5 million. However, this figure has not been independently verified, and no confirmed financial disclosure establishes his actual assets or earnings.
Warner Bros. Television Group chairman Channing Dungey paid tribute to Bauza, describing him as a unique talent who brought joy to audiences worldwide and helped continue the legacy of legendary voice actor Mel Blanc.
