title: Businesses will not be harassed  PM aide
description: Businesses will not be harassed  PM aide
content:
Adviser says unnecessary FIRs, freezing of accounts must be avoided
Prime Minister's Adviser on Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan has said that strengthening the industrial sector, attracting new investment, increasing exports and providing a conducive business environment are essential for sustainable economic growth.
He said the government was working with the business community to promote industrial development, facilitate businesses, create employment opportunities and remove unnecessary hurdles.
Addressing a meeting at the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI), Khan said the business community was playing a fundamental role in the national economy and policies must be designed to build investor confidence and support the growth of industry and trade.
He said the government was working on industrial policy and regulatory reforms to protect businesses from harassment, unnecessary inspections and unwarranted official action. He stressed that the unnecessary use of FIRs in business-related matters and measures such as freezing of business accounts should be avoided, while transparency and due process must be ensured in legal proceedings.
The adviser stressed that government institutions should adopt a cooperative approach towards the business community. He added that the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) and other relevant departments must consider the importance of business growth alongside revenue collection as a strong business sector contributed to employment generation, investment and economic stability.
Speaking on the occasion, LCCI President Ali Hussam Asghar said that although the business community was playing a vital role in economic development, traders and industrialists often faced difficulties due to the discretionary powers and actions of government departments.
He clarified that the Lahore Chamber was not opposed to the enforcement of laws and regulations; however, harassment of businesspeople and the registration of FIRs over minor violations were detrimental to commercial and industrial activities.
Asghar proposed that fines and corrective measures should be preferred over FIRs for minor violations. He also called for giving advance notices and reasonable time to businesses to rectify environmental compliance issues, which would ensure that regulations were enforced without unnecessarily disrupting business operations.
LCCI Senior Vice President Sardar Usman Ghani said strong relations between the government and business community were essential for economic progress. He emphasised that the private sector should be consulted during policymaking and obstacles hindering business activities must be removed.

title: Staples  fuel keep SPI near 12  YoY
description: Staples  fuel keep SPI near 12  YoY
content:
Weekly inflation rises 0.57%; flour jumps 5.69%; onions up 100%
The Sensitive Price Indicator (SPI) stayed elevated at almost 12% year-on-year in the week ended October 8, 2026, as wheat flour, chicken and petrol kept short-term inflation under pressure, Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) data showed.
The weekly SPI rose 0.57% from the previous week and 11.97% from the corresponding week of last year. The combined index stood at 372.58, against 370.46 a week earlier and 332.75 on October 9, 2025.
Wheat flour led the weekly rise, up 5.69% to Rs2,851 for a 20-kilogramme bag, from Rs2,697 a week earlier and Rs2,150 a year ago. Chicken followed with a rise of 4.93% to Rs383 a kg, gram pulse with 3.99%, and petrol and tomatoes with 2.40% each. Petrol averaged Rs398.87 a litre.
Masoor pulse rose 1.29%, prepared tea 1.08%, cooked daal 0.98%, mash pulse 0.91% and LPG 0.57%. An 11.67kg LPG cylinder averaged Rs5,132. Prices of bananas fell 2.81%, diesel 1.37% to Rs397.02 a litre, potatoes 0.89%, sugar 0.37%, gur 0.19% and moong pulse 0.03%. Of the 51 items tracked in 50 markets across 17 cities, prices of 20 items increased, six declined and 25 remained unchanged.
The year-on-year reading was driven by energy and a few staples. Onion prices more than doubled, up 100.24% to Rs190 a kg from Rs95 a year earlier. LPG rose 68.55%, electricity charges for Q1 58.59%, petrol 47.52% and diesel 42.52%. Wheat flour was 32.60% higher.
Chilli powder rose 15.55%, mutton 15.02%, beef 12.60%, chicken 9.44%, plain bread 8.99% and curd 8.08%. Potatoes fell 39.51%, tomatoes 37.07%, sugar 22.44% and eggs 18.88%. Salt, masoor pulse, gur and moong pulse were also cheaper than a year ago.
The burden was uneven. The SPI for the highest consumption quintile rose 12.48% year-on-year, against 9.41% for the lowest. Week-on-week, the top group rose 0.60% and the bottom 0.52%.
The weekly print sits above the broader August trend. The CPI inflation rose 11.1% year-on-year in August 2026, against 9.2% in July and 3.1% in August 2025. On a monthly basis, it was unchanged at 1.2%. Urban CPI rose 10.4% year-on-year and 0.9% month-on-month, while rural CPI rose 12.2% and 1.6%.

Ryan Murphy’s legal drama All’s Fair Season 2 is set to premiere at the Rome Film Festival, with Kim Kardashian, Naomi Watts, Niecy Nash-Betts and Sarah Paulson expected to attend.

Following its Rome Film Festival premiere, All’s Fair Season 2 is scheduled to debut in November on Disney+ in Italy and internationally, while Hulu will carry the series in the United States. An exact release date has not yet been announced.
Kardashian, Watts, Nash-Betts and Paulson will return alongside Teyana Taylor, Matthew Noszka and Glenn Close. The series is produced by 20th Television in association with Ryan Murphy, who also directs.
All’s Fair premiered in November 2025 and became a strong performer for Hulu despite receiving mixed reviews from critics. The series debuted at No. 1 on the platform’s viewership chart and became Hulu’s biggest original scripted series premiere in three years based on its first three days of streaming.
Ryan Murphy, Jon Robin Baitz, Joe Baken, Jamie Pachino, Lyn Greene and Richard Levine executive produce the series, alongside Kardashian, Close, Watts, Nash-Betts and Paulson.

title: Amanda Seyfried says    The Housemaid    success made her finally feel like a movie star
description: The 2025 thriller earned  400m worldwide and has a sequel in development
content:
The 2025 thriller earned $400m worldwide and has a sequel in development
Amanda Seyfried says the success of The Housemaid in 2025 marked a major shift in how she viewed her career, leading her to finally embrace the description of herself as a movie star.
The 40 year old actress discussed her changing perspective during an appearance at Hamptons International Film Festival on October 4, where she spoke with moderator and festival co chair Alec Baldwin. Seyfried reflected on her career, which began with soap operas before she made her feature film debut in Mean Girls in 2004.
She later appeared in major films including Mamma Mia! , Jennifer’s Body , Letters to Juliet and Les Misérables . Despite those successes, Seyfried said she had traditionally resisted describing herself as a movie star because her career had included periods of varying levels of work.
When asked whether she had expected Mamma Mia! to become a hit, Seyfried said she never felt able to predict that kind of success. She also acknowledged becoming increasingly focused on the financial performance of studio films.
However, her attitude changed following The Housemaid , the thriller adaptation of Freida McFadden’s bestselling novel. The film starred Seyfried alongside Sydney Sweeney and Brandon Sklenar and earned $400m worldwide.
Discussing the impact of its performance, Seyfried said she now considers herself a movie star because of The Housemaid . The film’s commercial success also led to a sequel being announced.
Seyfried is currently promoting The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd , directed by Tim Blake Nelson. The film premiered at Toronto International Film Festival before screening at Hamptons International Film Festival.
Seyfried plays a teacher in an abusive relationship who takes a job at a maximum security prison, where she develops feelings for a charismatic inmate played by Scoot McNairy. The film currently has no theatrical release date announced.

content:
Event features more than 220 fragrance exhibitors, major beauty names and the latest innovations shaping the industry
Beautyworld Dubai has opened its landmark 30th edition, bringing together professionals from across fragrance, skincare, cosmetics, haircare and beauty technology at Dubai World Trade Centre from October 6 to 8.
Organised by Messe Frankfurt Middle East, the three-day trade event is showcasing the latest products and technologies while offering industry professionals a look at the trends, innovations and personalities shaping the future of beauty.
According to Khaleej Times , fragrance remains one of the event's biggest highlights, with its dedicated section expanding significantly in recent years. The fragrance area has grown to more than 19,000 square metres this year and features more than 220 exhibitors.
Major regional fragrance companies, including Lattafa, Afnan, Armaf and French Avenue, are taking part alongside Kuwait's Gissah and Saudi Arabia's Al Majed for Oud, which is exhibiting at the event for the first time.
British beauty brand Lush is also using the event to introduce a new fragrance collection. Meanwhile, Scentronix, known for its AI-powered perfume technology and its work on the scent experience at Dubai's Museum of the Future, is demonstrating how artificial intelligence is influencing modern perfumery.
The Next in Fragrance conference is another key attraction, with master perfumer Aurélien Guichard appearing on October 6 and Louis Vuitton's Jacques Cavallier Belletrud scheduled for October 7. Discussions are expected to explore evolving consumer preferences, alcohol-free perfumes and the growing influence of younger fragrance buyers.
The event's programme extends well beyond fragrance, with prominent makeup artists and hairstylists conducting demonstrations and masterclasses.
Makeup artists Mary Phillips and Patrick Ta are among the featured names, while hairstylists Mounir, Dimitris Giannetos and Josh Lamonaca are showcasing their techniques on the live stages.
Phillips is also participating in the Next in Beauty conference, where discussions will cover investment opportunities, luxury beauty retail and the expanding GCC market.
Visitors can also explore Korean skincare brands such as SKIN1004, Medicube and Meditherapy, alongside companies working in beauty technology and packaging. Natural Notes is returning as a platform connecting producers of natural ingredients with fragrance companies.
The Beautyworld Dubai Awards will be held on October 7 at Le Méridien Dubai Hotel & Conference Centre. The awards recognise achievements across 17 categories.
Among this year's honourees is Huda Kattan, founder of Huda Beauty, who will receive the Beautyworld Icon Award. The honour recognises her contribution to the international beauty industry and the growth of the Dubai-founded brand.
Beautyworld Dubai is a trade-focused event rather than a consumer shopping exhibition. Entry to the exhibition halls is restricted to those aged 18 and above.

title: Two sisters  one sea  a path less travelled
description: Two sisters  one sea  a path less travelled
content:
Dua, Aleena charting a new course for Pakistani women in merchant navy
The sea has never been known for making life easy. Its waves can be unforgiving, voyages can stretch for months and the horizon can become a lonely companion when home is thousands of miles away. For two sisters from Karachi, however, the challenges of life at sea were not a warning - they were an invitation.
Dua and her younger sister Aleena chose a career that few Pakistani women have traditionally considered: the merchant navy.
Their journey has taken them from the classrooms and training facilities of Karachi to the City of Glasgow College in Scotland, and from navigation simulators to the deck of a ship. Along the way, their performance earned them certificates of appreciation during their overseas training.
For the sisters, however, the real achievement is not the certificates. It is proving that the sea does not have to be a man's world.
Dua completed the first year of the National Diploma in Nautical Science at the Pakistan Marine Training Institute in Karachi before travelling to Scotland for the second year of her education and training.
The programme was far removed from conventional classroom learning. Alongside academic study, the sisters underwent practical maritime training and gained experience aboard ships - learning the skills needed to navigate vessels safely and operate at sea.
"It is certainly not an easy life," Dua told The Express Tribune. "Sea life is a little difficult, but once we decided to pursue this career, we did not allow the challenges to stand in our way."
Then came the thought that, perhaps, mattered most. "Someone had to take the first step. Some Pakistani woman had to become a pioneer," she added.
In Pakistan, the merchant navy remains relatively unfamiliar as a career option for women. Dua believes that is partly because young girls simply do not know what opportunities exist. "Women in other countries can choose this field. Why not Pakistani women?" she asked.
The sisters want to change that perception.
For them, a career is not necessarily confined to the familiar choices of medicine, engineering or architecture. "There is a whole world beyond medicine, engineering and architecture," the siblings told The Express Tribune.
And the world they chose comes with responsibilities far greater than simply standing on a ship's deck.
As deck cadets, they are being trained in watchkeeping, navigation, route planning, determining a vessel's course and other technical aspects of ship operations. Their training also includes the use of simulators to develop practical navigation and deck-handling skills.
Eventually, their responsibilities will include helping ensure that vessels follow the correct routes, alter course when necessary and navigate safely under changing conditions.
Choosing the same profession was no coincidence.
For Aleena, having her sister beside her was a source of strength in an unfamiliar and demanding environment. "One of the main reasons we chose the same field was so that we could stay together, support each other and make our country proud," she told The Express Tribune.
Their shared journey also made the difficult periods easier.
Training was demanding. Life away from home was unfamiliar. But having a sister experiencing the same challenges meant neither had to face them alone.
Perhaps the most surprising part of their story is that the sisters did not come from a maritime family. No one in their family had worked in the merchant navy. Their family background was primarily connected with medicine.
It was their parents who first introduced them to the field.
The sisters, who had been fascinated by adventure since childhood, found themselves drawn to the idea of a career that promised something very different from the conventional. Their parents supported the decision, allowing the sisters to turn an unusual idea into a professional journey.
Dua and Aleena are not the first Pakistani women to venture into the merchant navy. Another Karachi woman, Neelam, had entered the profession before them. But the sisters hope their journey will encourage many more to follow.

title: Christopher Abbott opens up about    nightmare    Professor X casting reveal
description: Christopher Abbott recalls his Professor X casting reveal at D23  calling the moment both a dream and nightmare
content:
Christopher Abbott recalls his Professor X casting reveal at D23, calling the moment both a dream and nightmare
Christopher Abbott has opened up about the reaction to his casting as Professor X in Marvel’s upcoming X-Men reboot, describing the D23 reveal as both exciting and uncomfortable.
Abbott, known for Girls and East of Eden , was announced as the iconic X-Men character during Disney’s D23 event in August. Speaking to New York Magazine, the actor said the moment felt like “a bit of a dream and a nightmare” because he initially believed some attendees did not recognise him.
Abbott recalled walking onto the stage with enthusiasm before noticing what he described as a muted response from the audience. He said his energy quickly changed and he became more reserved during the reveal.
The actor was introduced alongside Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Maya Boyd as Storm and Adam Driver as Mr. Sinister. Other previously announced cast members include Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Kit Connor as Cyclops and Samara Weaving as Emma Frost.
Marvel’s new X-Men movie is scheduled to arrive in May 2028. The film will reboot the mutant superhero team following 2019’s Dark Phoenix , which starred James McAvoy as Professor X alongside Michael Fassbender, Jennifer Lawrence and Nicholas Hoult.

title: Spain beat England in Nations League
description: La Roja extend unbeaten run to 39 as Yamal  Baena and Oyarzabal score in 3 2 win
content:
La Roja extend unbeaten run to 39 as Yamal, Baena and Oyarzabal score in 3-2 win
World champions Spain came from behind to beat England 3-2 in an entertaining Nations League encounter at Wembley on Saturday, denying the hosts a cathartic win after their painful World Cup exit.
Victory for Luis de la Fuente's men extends Spain's astonishing unbeaten run to 39 matches -- a record for a European team.
England got off to a nightmare start when Lamine Yamal pounced on a gaffe by defender Marc Guehi, and they could easily have been three goals down as silky Spain created multiple chances.
But England, criticised for their ultra-defensive tactics in their World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina, showed adventure of their own and got their reward in the 36th minute when Barcelona winger Anthony Gordon finished a fine team move.
Four minutes later Thomas Tuchel's men were ahead after captain Harry Kane headed home Nico O'Reilly's cross via a Marc Cucurella deflection.
Kane had a golden chance to give England a two-goal cushion from the penalty spot 10 minutes into the second half but slipped slightly, crashing his shot against the bar.
Spain, who beat England in the Euro 2024 final, took full advantage, with substitutes Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal both scoring to turn the match around.
De la Fuente said he felt his team had largely been in control against "superpower" England and he was confident they would have come back even from 3-1 down.
Asked about his side's long unbeaten run, he said: "These are sensational moments.... Numbers are one thing, objective indicators are what we see. But what is important is that we still want to grow, we still want to improve."
Kane bemoaned England's inability to sustain their best level for the whole game.
"I spoke before that we reached good levels at the World Cup but didn't quite put a full 90 minutes together," he told ITV. "Probably similar again today."
England boss Thomas Tuchel was adamant ahead of the match that it did not signal a new start but will have been dismayed at his team's nervy start.
Manchester City's Guehi, with a chance to clear in the second minute, inexplicably turned back towards goalkeeper James Trafford, apparently unaware that Yamal was just behind him.
The teenager pinched the ball and curled a left-footed effort off the inside of the post.
Ferran Torres was in the thick of the action, with an effort ruled out for offside and another shot saved by Trafford, in for long-time number one Jordan Pickford.
He also squandered a golden opportunity with just the goalkeeper to beat.
Yamal then set up Dani Olmo, who flashed wide as Spain rued yet another miss.
England, who had showed plenty of promise down the wings, made the visitors pay with an incisive counter-attacking goal after winning the ball back deep in their own half.
Gordon was involved early in the move and surged forward, collecting Jude Bellingham's pass to steer the ball decisively past goalkeeper Unai Simon.
And, with the atmosphere now totally changed, England were in front when Kane rose to head home.
Tuchel's men started the second half brightly and had a chance to extend their lead from the spot when they were awarded a penalty for a Rodri foul on Bellingham following a VAR check.
But Kane hit the bar and England paid the price when Baena steered home on the hour mark after O'Reilly had given the ball away to Olmo.
Worse was to come for the home side when Baena turned provider for Oyarzabal, who dinked the ball over Trafford.
Spain host Croatia in their next Nations League Group A3 match on Tuesday while England travel to the Czech Republic.

title: Pakistan seeks more investment  trade with Portugal
description: Pakistan seeks more investment  trade with Portugal
content:
Emphasises greater Portuguese stake in textiles, agriculture, IT
The Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) and Ambassador of Portugal Paulo Domingues on Saturday discussed ways to enhance bilateral economic, trade and investment cooperation, with particular focus on textiles, agriculture, information technology, pharmaceuticals and Special Economic Zones (SEZs).
The SIFC hosted the ambassador for a wide-ranging discussion focused on strengthening economic, trade and investment ties between Pakistan and Portugal, according to a press release issued by the SIFC. The engagement provided an opportunity to explore areas of mutual interest and identify promising avenues for greater collaboration between the business communities of both countries.
Discussions covered investment opportunities in textiles, agriculture, information and communication technology, pharmaceuticals and Special Economic Zones, highlighting the potential for enhanced commercial engagement and investment partnerships.
The SIFC informed the ambassador about Pakistan's investment potential across priority sectors and its investor-centric facilitation framework aimed at providing coordinated support to domestic and international investors.
As a whole-of-government platform, the SIFC works to facilitate engagement between investors and relevant federal, provincial and sector-specific stakeholders, helping streamline investment processes and support the development of viable business opportunities.
The meeting also highlighted opportunities emerging from Pakistan's growing connectivity with international businesses and institutions.
In this context, the SIFC acknowledged the launch of FC Porto's Dragon Force Academy in Sialkot, established in partnership with Forward Sports. The initiative brings the renowned Portuguese football club's youth development programme to Pakistan and represents an additional avenue for strengthening institutional and commercial linkages between the two countries. The engagement underscored the scope for expanding Pakistan-Portugal cooperation through investment, business partnerships and sector-specific opportunities. The SIFC emphasised the importance of continued engagement with international partners to identify commercially viable projects and create stronger linkages between Pakistani and Portuguese investors and businesses.
It reaffirmed the commitment to facilitating international investors through coordinated government support, providing greater clarity on investment opportunities and promoting an enabling environment for mutually beneficial partnerships.

title: K P police to establish dedicated help desks for transgender people
description: Mardan DIG pledges to protect the rights of the community
content:
Mardan DIG pledges to protect the rights of the community
Amid growing incidents of violence, killings, and social challenges faced by transgender people in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), the provincial police have decided to establish dedicated desks for the community at police facilitation centres across the province.
“Along with women, the elderly and persons with disabilities, providing facilities for transgender people and resolving their issues is also a priority,” Mardan Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Qasim Ali Khan told The Express Tribune .
In July, the Peshawar High Court passed directions restraining cops from harassing members of the transgender community and issued notices to the provincial government, police, and other relevant authorities, seeking their replies on a petition alleging illegal evictions and harassment. The province has seen a number of cases of aggression and violence reported against the community.
Highlighting the purpose of the initiative, DIG Khan said the initiative would provide members of the marginalised transgender community with a dedicated platform where they can lodge complaints, seek assistance and have their grievances addressed.
Read: PHC restrains police from harassing transgenders
Speaking about the first such police facilitation desk being established for transgender people, Charsadda District Police Officer (DPO) Rifatullah Khan said transgender people were an “honourable part of society and denial of their basic rights, including registration of First Information Reports (FIRs), or violence against them would not be tolerated”.
He vowed that the desk would address the community’s problems and provide them with all-out assistance.
The DPO further outlined that the Police Sahulat Markaz (PSM) already had dedicated desks for women, members of minority communities, senior citizens and persons with disabilities, and that a separate desk for transgender people would help redress the grievances of the community.
Transgender social activist Rehano welcomed the initiative, describing the establishment of a dedicated desk as a positive development.
“This will help ensure respect and dignity for transgender people and recognition of their separate identity,” Rehano told The Express Tribune .
Sobia Khan, one of the first transgender jail warders in K-P, said members of the community often faced rejection within their families as well as violence outside their homes.
Read more: Transgender community decries job discrimination
“Transgender people are often expelled from their homes, and then they also suffer discrimination and violence in the outside world,” she lamented.
Speaking on the host of issues faced by the community, Sobia said representatives of the transgender community met with senior police officials following a rise in incidents of violence. The meetings, she said, led to the decision to establish a dedicated transgender desk at police facilitation centres.
According to data obtained by The Express Tribune from the K-P Transgender Association, an organisation working for the rights of transgender people, around 170 transgender persons have been killed in the province since 2015.
The association also reported more than 700 incidents of violence against transgender people during the same period, which demonstrates an average of 63 incidents of violence per year.

title: Afridi warns of  unprecedented  reaction if governor s rule imposed in K P
description: K P CM says preparations for PTI s Oct 4 long march complete  says could set out sooner in event of  misadventure
content:
Says PTI never refused negotiations, 'if govt wants to hold talks we are ready'
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi warned on Saturday that the public reaction would be "unprecedented" if governor's rule were imposed on the province, saying neither governor's rule nor disqualification was something the government could "afford."
"Government means nothing to me, I am a soldier of Imran Khan," Afridi told senior journalists in Peshawar, adding that if he ceased to be the K-P chief minister, the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder would decide his replacement.
CM Afridi’s statement came amid reports that the federal government was considering governor’s rule or other legal options for the K-P government, as the interior minister warned PTI against a long march towards Islamabad and said the government was consulting the Law Ministry on legal options, including imposing governor’s rule, amid the security situation.
During today's media talk, CM Afridi said that "if the chair comes between me and my objective, I will kick it away."
Turning to PTI's planned march, which was initially to start on September 27 but was postponed to October 4, CM Afridi said preparations were complete, and that the convoy would "return only upon achieving real freedom."
"We are not an armed group, we are political people," the chief minister said.
He also noted that the party had never refused negotiations, stating, "Seven days remain until the long march; if they want to hold talks, they should hold them now." "We were ready for talks yesterday, and we are ready today as well," the chief minister added.
Read: Afridi says police must fight terrorism
Regarding the postponement of the march, the chief minister stated that it had been "a matter of strategy." He noted, however, "We have to march no matter what; preparations are complete."
CM Afridi also warned against any "misadventure," saying the party could set out even before October 4 in such an event.
Regarding the September 27 call, he noted that PTI had been "approaching every institution for nine months" without a hearing, which was why it was forced to issue the call. "There are court orders for weekly meetings," he said, regarding Imran, which he argued were not being implemented.
CM Afridi further alleged that the country was being run according to the policy of "one man," whose representative was Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi. He added that nothing could be done against the "establishment's narrative," while also taking aim at the federal information minister's statement, which he said was meant to brand him as the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan's "B-team." The statement, CM Afridi said, was pre-planned.
Further, the chief minister said "unnecessary disputes" were being created with Afghanistan, and that the closure of the Pakistan-Afghanistan border had caused a loss of Rs7 billion this year, against an expected annual revenue of Rs10 billion if the border remained open.
Read More: Afridi calls for review of anti-terror policy
"Despite restrictions on people coming from there, infiltration is still occurring," he added, noting that "good relations with Afghanistan are in our interest." The chief minister said the province had prepared and shared a provincial action plan with the relevant authorities, and called for talks with Afghanistan to be held through a national jirga, saying Kabul had no choice but to sit with Pakistan.
The chief minister's remarks came a day after he confirmed that PTI's long march to Islamabad would kick off from Peshawar on October 4 instead of the previous September 27 date.
Afridi said all matters had been discussed in the political committee meeting and described the decision to defer the march as part of the party’s “political strategy”, further adding that negotiations would continue even after the march.
The PTI had announced last month that it would march to Islamabad on September 27 to press for the release of party founder Imran. The party had been preparing a central convoy from K-P, with caravans from other parts of the country expected to join before proceeding towards the federal capital. The federal government warned the party against going ahead with the march.

content:
Athens mayor ​Haris Doukas says it was likely linked to gas infrastructure, 'Something went terribly wrong'
Six people have died, ‌the Greek fire brigade said on Saturday, after a two-storey residential building in a tourist area of central Athens collapsed following an explosion which the capital's ​mayor said was likely linked to gas infrastructure.
Emergency crews in ​heavy gear and red helmets assisted by rescue dogs, cameras ⁠and sensors found the bodies of six people, fire brigade ​spokesman Vassilis Vathrakogiannis said in a televised briefing. They were looking for ​an elderly couple who lived in one apartment and four tourists who were staying in another as they removed debris from the building.
Emergency personnel work at the site where an old building partially collapsed following an explosion, at the touristy Plaka area in central Athens, Greece. Photo: Reuters
The fire brigade's crime ​investigation unit was also on site to identify the cause of ​the blast after reports of a gas smell in an area which is home ‌to ⁠hotels and short-term rentals.

The tourists, two American couples, had been expected to check in to catch a flight from Athens airport at 3 p.m. local time on Friday but did not show up, a ​police source said.
Ambulances ​stood by on ⁠Saturday to take the bodies to the hospital for identification.
Friday's blast destroyed the building in Plaka, near ​some of Athens' most visited sites including the ​Acropolis and ⁠the Temple of Zeus, damaging nearby houses, shops and cars and sending rubble and broken glass as far as three blocks away.
The building was ⁠reduced ​to twisted metal, shattered tiles and concrete, ​strewn with household items and clothing.

title: 2027 World Cup will be my last for India  Kohli
description: 37 year old batter has scored 14 941 runs in one day internationals
content:
37-year-old batter has scored 14,941 runs in one-day internationals
Virat Kohli said next year's 50-overs World Cup would be his last for India and he is ready to give his all to help lift the ​trophy.
Kohli, the leading century-maker in ODIs with 54 hundreds, retired from T20 ‌internationals and Test cricket earlier and now represents India only in the 50-over format.
The 37-year-old batter, who has scored 14,941 runs in one-day internationals, second only to Sachin Tendulkar's 18,426, won the ​World Cup on home soil in 2011 before suffering defeat in the 2023 ​final against Australia.
The 2027 edition, to be jointly hosted by South ⁠Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia in October to November, will be Kohli's fifth ODI World ​Cup.
"For me, it's the last World Cup I'm going to play for India," Kohli ​told broadcaster JioStar on Saturday.
"That is my motivation and like, you know, to leave everything out there. And of course, the goal is absolutely to win the World Cup and whatever it takes, ​I'm absolutely ready."
Kohli said the demands of a 50-over World Cup made it ​one of cricket's toughest challenges, particularly with the tournament set to be played away from home.
"The intensity ‌of ⁠a 50-over World Cup is greater than anything. Because now, it's about 10 games at a Twenty20 level of intensity," he said.
"But you are playing 2.5 T20 games in one day. And to maintain that intensity for 10 games in a big ​tournament and World Cup ​is a big ⁠deal. Also now, it's in foreign conditions. It takes a lot out of you."
Former captain Rohit Sharma, who also plays only ODIs ​for India, said he remained fully motivated by the prospect ​of another ⁠World Cup campaign.
"The thought will never cross my mind that the business I had is finished," Rohit said.
"As long as you're playing, there is always something to look forward to. ⁠And ​I'm looking forward to the World Cup."
Kohli and Rohit ​were both named in India's squad for the three-match ODI series against West Indies. The opening match will ​be played in Thiruvananthapuram on Sunday.

content:
Pakistan face Hong Kong, India meet Afghanistan as knockout stage takes shape
The quarter-finals line-up for the men’s cricket competition at the Asian Games has been confirmed, with Bangladesh, India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka joining the knockout stage after receiving automatic entry as the tournament’s top-seeded teams.
Pakistan will face Hong Kong in the first quarter-final on September 28, while India take on Afghanistan later the same day. Nepal meet Sri Lanka on September 29 before Bangladesh play Malaysia in the fourth quarter-final.
The four teams that advanced through the group stage were Afghanistan and Nepal from Group A, while Malaysia and Hong Kong progressed from Group B.
The group stage, however, was disrupted by rain, with the weather now threatening to play a major role in determining the semi-finalists.
Japan’s final Group A match against Nepal could not be completed because of rain, while Malaysia’s game against Oman in Group B was abandoned without a ball being bowled. The results left Japan and Oman eliminated from the competition.
Forecasts suggest further interruptions could be possible during the quarter-finals. Rain is forecast for both Monday and Tuesday, the two days on which the knockout matches are scheduled.
The outlook is more encouraging for the latter stages of the competition, with conditions expected to be more favourable for cricket on Thursday, when the semi-finals are scheduled, and Saturday, when the medal playoffs will take place.
India enter the knockout stage as defending champions after winning the gold medal at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou. They defeated Afghanistan in the final, while Bangladesh claimed the bronze medal after beating Pakistan in the third-place playoff.

title: Pakistan boxing ends on a frustrating note as Fatima Zehra bows out
description: Tajikistan   s Mijgona Samadova beats Pakistan   s last boxer 5 0 in women   s 60kg preliminaries
content:
Tajikistan’s Mijgona Samadova beats Pakistan’s last boxer 5-0 in women’s 60kg preliminaries
Pakistan ended their boxing journey on a frustrating note when their last boxer and a slim hope Fatima Zehra also went down in her preliminary bout at the 20th Asian Games on Saturday.
Zehra was beaten 5-0 by Tajikistan’s Mijgona Samadova in the women’s 60kg round of 16 at Nishio Gymnasium, bringing Pakistan’s boxing campaign to an end without a medal.
Samadova dominated the three-round contest, winning all five judges’ scorecards by margins of 30-25, 30-24, 30-26, 30-25 and 30-24.
Zehra, who had won bronze in the Glasgow Commonwealth Games recently, struggled to match the Tajik boxer’s pace and pressure, with Samadova establishing a clear advantage from the opening round. The Pakistani was also knocked down once during the bout, according to the official scoring record.
Earlier South Korea's Kim Gichae knocked out Pakistan debutant Irfan Khan in the men's 90kg.
Kim won the round-of-16 bout at Nishio Gymnasium when the referee stopped the contest in the second round.
Irfan, making his debut at the event, was knocked down twice before the contest was halted. The judges scored the opening round in Kim's favour, with four judges giving the South Korean a 10-9 advantage and one scoring it 10-8.
Kim also scored an additional knockdown in the second round before the stoppage.
Pakistan coach Tariq Sidiqui was happy despite Irfan’s loss.
“To be honest Irfan boxed extremely well. His opponent got tired but in the second round a long swinging punch hit him on his chin and he fell,” Tariq said.
“It was the first international fight from Irfan but he has shown his guts. He can turn out to be a very good boxer as he is bold and don’t afraid. The Korean had got tired in the second round,” said Tariq.
Maria Rind and Sumama Rehman were the other boxers who faced first round exits.

title: Israeli forces use phosphorus shells in southern Lebanon attacks
description: Artillery fire hits areas in Nabatieh  Tyre districts as Lebanese army clears unexploded Israeli bombs
content:
Artillery fire hits areas in Nabatieh, Tyre districts as Lebanese army clears unexploded Israeli bombs
Israeli forces used phosphorus munitions while shelling several towns in southern Lebanon on Friday, state news agency NNA reported.
Artillery struck the outskirts of Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, Mayfadoun and Nabatieh al-Fawqa in the Nabatieh district.
Phosphorus shells were used in Nabatieh al-Fawqa, while Israel later renewed attacks on Zawtar al-Sharqiyah with similar munitions.
Read: Pakistan, Lebanon agree to enhance intelligence sharing, security cooperation
In the Tyre district, artillery fire also targeted Wadi Zibqin and the outskirts of Haris and Haddatha.
Lebanese army specialists dismantled two unexploded Israeli aerial bombs in Majdal Selm and Al-Ghandouriyah in the Marjayoun and Bint Jbeil districts and moved them to a safe location.
The Israeli offensive in Lebanon has killed at least 4,386 victims, wounded 12,407 and displaced more than 1 million others since early March, according to Lebanese authorities.
The attacks continue despite a June framework deal that provides for a gradual Israeli withdrawal from occupied Lebanese territory in exchange for the deployment of the Lebanese army there and the disarmament of Hezbollah.
Peace in southern Lebanon remains ‘elusive’: UN mission
The UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) said on Tuesday that peace in southern Lebanon remains "elusive," stressing that permanently ending the conflict requires political will from the parties.
The remarks came in a statement marking the International Day of Peace, observed annually on September 21, which UNIFIL commemorated Monday evening with a ceremony at its headquarters in the southern Lebanese town of Naqoura.
“Today, peace in south Lebanon remains elusive, but the hope for peace endures,” UNIFIL said, stressing that lasting peace requires “political commitments and solutions from the parties themselves.”
“Peacekeepers can help restore stability, avoid misunderstandings, and reduce the risk of escalation -- but they cannot replace the political will and decisions needed to end the conflict permanently,” it said.
Read more: UN chief stresses smooth Lebanon pull-out
"Peace is not something we address once a year; it is an enduring responsibility," UNIFIL Head of Mission and Force Commander Major General Diodato Abagnara said.
“We patrol, we keep channels of communication open with the parties to reduce the risk of misunderstanding and escalation. We work with the Lebanese Armed Forces as they assume greater responsibilities in the south,” Abagnara said.
He stressed that responsibility for reaching a political solution rests with the parties, while “UNIFIL will continue to do its part, keeping communication open, reducing the risk of escalation, and supporting diplomatic efforts.”
The full implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701 "remains the objective and the basis for lasting peace and stability in south Lebanon," Abagnara added.
“Continued cooperation between the Lebanese Armed Forces and peacekeepers remains central to maintaining stability and supporting the extension of state authority in the south,” he added.

title: DPM Dar reiterates need to eliminate terrorist threat from Afghanistan at ECO meeting
description: Says Pakistan has always sought a peaceful  prosperous and stable Afghanistan that is at peace with its neighbours
content:
Says Pakistan has always sought a peaceful, prosperous and stable Afghanistan that is at peace with its neighbours
Deputy Prime Minister (DPM) and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Saturday reiterated the need to eliminate the terrorist threat from Afghanistan, saying terrorism emanating from Afghan soil was undermining efforts to promote peace, prosperity and development in the region.
Chairing the 27th Informal Meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, DPM Dar said Pakistan had always sought a peaceful, prosperous and stable Afghanistan that was integrated into the region and at peace with itself and its neighbours.
“Regrettably, the issue of terrorism emanating from Afghan soil undermines these efforts,” he added.
The foreign minister said Pakistan had pursued constructive engagement with the Taliban regime, extending bilateral and transit trade concessions to Afghanistan and making the signing of a framework agreement for a feasibility study on the Uzbekistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan (UAP) railway project a key priority.
🔊 PR No. 2️⃣6️⃣5️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Remarks by the Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 at the Informal Meeting of ECO Council of Ministers Meeting in New York 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/3VI1UGDJ8i
DPM Dar said Pakistan's expectation was that the Taliban regime would address its security concerns, including through “concrete and verifiable actions” against the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and their affiliates.
“These groups continue to threaten Pakistan's sovereignty and the lives of its citizens,” he said.
He said peace and development in the region could only be achieved with the elimination of the terrorist threat from Afghanistan.
According to a statement from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA), the foreign minister "expressed deep concern over the prevailing security situation in the region and the Middle East, reaffirming Pakistan’s commitment to the peaceful resolution of disputes in accordance with international law."
Read: Security forces foil Afghan Taliban incursion, kill several terrorists at Balochistan border: state media
DPM Dar underscored the need for ECO member states to "harness their collective potential to promote peace, resilience, and shared prosperity for the region’s nearly half a billion people."
He also expressed gratitude to ECO member states for "reposing confidence in Pakistan and reaffirmed Islamabad's commitment to advancing the organisation's objectives and strengthening regional cooperation," the statement by MoFA read.
DPM Dar also outlined Pakistan’s priorities for the ECO chairmanship, including deepening intra-regional trade and economic integration; strengthening connectivity and transit corridors linking Central Asia with the Arabian Sea, advancing a digitally enabled ECO Free Trade Area; and enhancing regional cooperation on climate resilience.
“Pakistan looks forward to working closely with all ECO Member States to translate the Organization’s shared vision into tangible outcomes and further strengthen regional economic cooperation, connectivity, and integration,” MoFA noted.

The meeting was attended by foreign ministers and senior representatives of ECO member states including FM of Azerbaijan Jeyhun Bayramov, Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi, Kyrgyz FM Zheenbek Kulubaev, Tajik FM Sirojiddin Muhriddin, Deputy FM of Turkiye Berris Ekinci, Permanent Representative of Turkmenistan to the UN Vepa Hajiyev, Deputy Permanent Representative of Uzbekistan to the UN Laziz Karaev, and Director General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan Beibut Kulatayev.
The participating ministers and heads of delegation also exchanged views on regional and global developments and expressed support for enhanced regional cooperation. The meeting also provided an opportunity to build momentum towards the 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting, scheduled to be held in Islamabad in November 2026.
Secretary General of ECO, Dr Asad Majeed Khan, also briefed the council.

Pakistan’s top squash players Mohammad Ashab Irfan and Noor Zaman had to settle for bronze medals when they lost their men’s singles semi-finals of the 20 th Asian Games on Saturday.
Irfan, World No49, lost to World No 26 India’s Abhay Singh 3-0 while World No 29 Noor Zaman suffered 3-0 defeat at the hands of World No 18 Malaysia’s Eain Yow Ng in the men’s singles semi-finals.
Singh produced a composed performance to beat Irfan 11-3, 12-10, 11-6 in 35 minutes at the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena, securing his place in the gold medal match while ending Irfan’s hopes of a place in the final.
For Irfan, the defeat brought an end to a strong singles campaign but still earned him a place on the podium.
The Pakistani struggled to impose his game in the opening game as Singh quickly established control. Irfan found greater resistance in the second, pushing his Indian opponent into a tight contest before Singh edged it 12-10.
The third game again went Singh’s way, with the Indian maintaining his composure to complete a 3-0 victory.
Irfan on Friday had defeated India’s Veer Chotrani 3-1 to advance to the semi-finals.
Meanwhile Noor Zaman also had to settle for a bronze medal after Malaysia’s Eain Yow ended his run in the semi-finals with a straight games victory.
Eain Yow defeated Noor 11-7, 11-2, 11-4 in 26 minutes. Noor made a competitive start in the opening game, scoring seven points, but Eain Yow gradually took control of the rallies and closed out the game 11-7.
The Malaysian then stepped up the pressure. Zaman struggled to find a response in the second game, winning only two points as Eain Yow moved within one game of the final.
The third followed a similar pattern. Eain Yow maintained his momentum to win 11-4 and complete a 3-0 victory.
Noor had defeated Hong Kong’s Leung Chi Hin Henry 3-1 in the quarter-finals.

title: New Saudi ambassador arrives in Islamabad to assume duties
description: He was received by Khushaan Saeed  Assistant Director of the Protocol Department at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
content:
He was received by Khushal Saeed, Assistant Director of the Protocol Department at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
Saudi Arabia's newly appointed ambassador to Pakistan, Dr Rajeh bin Tami Al-Baqami, arrived in Islamabad on Saturday to commence his duties, the Royal Embassy of Saudi Arabia in Islamabad said in a post on X.
The embassy said the ambassador, appointed to Pakistan by the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, arrived in Islamabad to "commence his duties".
He was received by Khushal Saeed, Assistant Director of the Protocol Department at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA), along with several members of the Saudi diplomatic mission's staff, according to the embassy's post.

On July 29, Saudi Arabia appointed Al-Baqami as its new ambassador to Pakistan, replacing Nawaf bin Said Al-Malki, Arab News reported, as the two longstanding allies deepen cooperation in defence, investment and regional security. According to the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Al-Baqami was among eight newly appointed envoys who took the oath of office.
“On behalf of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, and before His Royal Highness the Crown Prince, the newly appointed ambassadors to several brotherly and friendly countries took the oath,” the ministry said in a statement on Tuesday, sharing photographs of the diplomats, including the new envoy to Pakistan.
Read: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye sign joint defence pact in Makkah
A retired major general, Al-Baqami, later joined the Saudi Foreign Ministry with the rank of ambassador. He holds a doctorate in Human Resource Management from Brunel University London.
Saudi Arabia has also expanded economic engagement with Pakistan, pledging billions of dollars in investment under Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s Vision 2030 initiative, while continuing to provide financial support to help stabilise Pakistan’s economy during recurring balance-of-payments challenges. Riyadh remains one of Pakistan’s largest sources of oil on deferred payment and has repeatedly placed deposits with the State Bank of Pakistan to bolster foreign exchange reserves. Bilateral ties have further strengthened in recent months as both countries coordinate closely on regional security issues, including tensions involving Iran. Pakistan also deployed military assets to Saudi Arabia earlier this year following heightened security concerns in the Kingdom, according to a Reuters report.
Al-Baqami succeeds Al-Malki, who served as Saudi ambassador during a period marked by increased political engagement, enhanced security cooperation and growing Saudi investment in Pakistan.

title: US  China buy time with trade truce as pressure builds
description: Trump s top trade official to host G20 trade ministers next week  discuss US tariff threats  issue of excess capacity
content:
Trump's top trade official to host G20 trade ministers next week, discuss US tariff threats, issue of excess capacity
Washington and Beijing may have bought themselves breathing space with an extended trade truce , but analysts warn that time is running out for the world's two biggest economies to resolve their strategic rivalry.
President Donald Trump and Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping concluded a pomp-filled summit Friday, with the US leader confirming they would meet twice more this year.
But even as Trump and Xi "are making nice," their countries "remain locked in a bitter competition over trade, tech, Taiwan, defence, rare earths and industrial policy," said Daniel Russel of the Asia Society Policy Institute.
Daniel Kritenbrink, a former US official now with The Asia Group consultancy, said there's "no doubt that both leaders would like to see stability in the relationship, at least through the end of the year." However, "you'd have to see further tangible outcomes for this truce to extend in the long run."
Read: Xi calls for new chapter in China-US ties at White House dinner
Some feel Beijing has "largely not lived up to the commitments it made" at earlier meetings, he added, noting many US officials "have articulated their profound frustration with the Chinese."
Xi and Trump agreed to a trade truce last year during a meeting in South Korea, after a bitter tit-for-tat fight that saw tariffs soar over 100% at one point.
As part of the agreement, Beijing agreed to buy more US soybeans and other agriculture products, and to suspend rare earths restrictions for a year.
The pact was originally due to expire in November but both sides agreed this week to extend it until January 10, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said.
Trump's top trade official Jamieson Greer told CNBC on Friday that Washington views such extensions as "compliance periods."
"I think US officials would say China is doing just barely enough to maintain the agreement and no more," Kritenbrink said. "That's unsustainable over the long run," he added.
The brief extension "was the preferred position of the Americans," Mary Lovely of the Peterson Institute for International Economics told AFP .
Read More: How Trump's diplomatic week exposed the limits of his power
She added that while Beijing would have preferred a longer rollover, the current situation points to Washington's anxiety about the delivery of rare earth magnets and how officials "want to keep this on a short leash."
"It's not clear anymore how much their threats of high tariffs actually move China," she said.
For now, Greer said that both countries have made "progress" on other economic outcomes and expect to release more details Monday.
"We want to have some subset of goods that we can trade with the Chinese on a more preferential basis," he said.
He added that both sides have agreed on products that can be left aside in future trade disputes.
Greer is set to host G20 trade ministers in Wisconsin next week, with US tariff threats and the issue of excess capacity — a key concern surrounding Chinese industry — expected to be discussed.
Washington and Beijing have also agreed to set up some kind of notification system for artificial intelligence threats between the two countries, Bessent said.
Also Read: China, US find new trade ties in services
Peter Richardson of Counterpoint Research said the channel could be as simple as a hotline, but it will be tough to define what triggers it. "It is often very difficult to tell quickly whether an AI incident was state-directed, a rogue actor or an accident," he said.
"Given the rivalry we don't expect this to lead to any comprehensive international framework for AI regulation, but it would be the first practical guardrail," he added.
Kritenbrink, for his part, said the summit has done "nothing to curb the competitive instincts of both sides on AI."
"I don't think you'll see any slowing down."

title: Netanyahu failed to relay UAE warning of possible Hamas attack to security chiefs  NYT
description: Meeting minutes show the premier pushed to maintain calm in Gaza  citing Saudi normalization prospects
content:
Meeting minutes show the premier pushed to maintain calm in Gaza, citing Saudi normalisation prospects
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu failed to pass on a warning from United Arab Emirates President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan about a possible major Hamas attack to Israel’s security chiefs before October 7, 2023, the New York Times reported on Friday.
The Times , citing two people familiar with the conversation, said Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed called Netanyahu in late September 2023 and warned him that Hamas was considering a major attack.
Read: Israeli army admits unpreparedness for Oct. 7 Hamas attack
The warning, however, did not specify whether Hamas was planning rocket fire or a ground assault.
Five former senior Israeli officials told the newspaper that the warning never reached the heads of Israel’s security establishment.
Read more: 5 Netanyahu claims at UN that clash with documented findings
Netanyahu convened security chiefs days later, on October 1, to discuss Gaza but did not mention the Emirati warning, according to meeting minutes reviewed by the newspaper.
The minutes showed that Netanyahu instead pushed to maintain calm in Gaza and resisted proposals by some security officials to consider strikes against senior Hamas figures. He argued that military action in Gaza could jeopardise efforts to establish diplomatic relations with Saudi Arabia.
Netanyahu had denied receiving the warning after the Haaretz newspaper in Israel first reported the alleged call earlier this month.
The Times also reported that Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed later referred to the September 2023 call in a conversation with then-CIA Director William Burns, saying he warned Netanyahu about a looming threat from Hamas in Gaza or the occupied West Bank.

title: A pioneer  but still a lonely one
description: Mahoor Shahzad   s Asian Games exit exposes the uncomfortable reality of Pakistan badminton
content:
Mahoor Shahzad’s Asian Games exit exposes the uncomfortable reality of Pakistan badminton
Mahoor Shahzad has spent years carrying the weight of Pakistani badminton on her shoulders. On Saturday, that weight looked heavier than ever.
Pakistan’s leading women’s shuttler and an Olympian, Mahoor suffered a bruising defeat at the Asian Games, losing 21-5, 21-11 to Indonesia’s Putri Kusuma Wardani in just 23 minutes.
The scoreline was unforgiving. Mahoor won only 16 of 58 points and never found a foothold against an opponent who dictated the rallies from the start.
For a player who has been Pakistan’s most recognisable badminton name for years, it was a painful performance.
But the disappointment goes beyond one match.
Mahoor’s career has been remarkable in a country where badminton has struggled for international relevance. She became Pakistan’s first badminton Olympian, reaching a stage few of her compatriots had imagined.
Yet her longevity also exposes an uncomfortable weakness in the system.
When one player remains the dominant figure in the national women’s circuit year after year, success can become a paradox. The champion keeps winning, but the competition behind her does not appear to develop quickly enough to challenge her or eventually replace her at international level.
Mahoor cannot be blamed for filling that vacuum. She has kept competing, winning and representing Pakistan.
But Saturday’s defeat showed the enormous distance between domestic dominance and the standards demanded at the Asian level.
There was something touching about watching an Olympian return to the court for another campaign, still carrying expectations that should belong to an entire sporting system rather than one athlete.
Mahoor has been a pioneer. Her journey opened a door for Pakistani badminton.
The sadness is that, years later, Pakistan still appears to be waiting for the players who will walk through it behind her.
For Mahoor, Saturday was another defeat.
For Pakistan badminton, it was a reminder that one player cannot build a pipeline alone.

title: President approves ordinance imposing up to Rs2m fines for Safe City camera damage
description: The amount of fine will be determined by authorised officer after providing opportunity for hearing
content:
The amount of fine will be determined by authorised officer after providing opportunity for hearing
President Asif Ali Zardari, on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, has approved an ordinance aimed at protecting Islamabad Capital Territory's Safe City cameras and surveillance infrastructure and providing compensation for any damage, said a statement by the President's Office on Saturday.
"The objective of the ordinance is to safeguard the Safe City cameras and surveillance system from damage and to ensure compensation in the event of any damage," it stated.
According to the statement, under the ordinance, financial penalties may be imposed for damaging Safe City cameras or surveillance infrastructure, as well as for "inciting or encouraging such damage".

It further added that a penalty of up to Rs2 million may be imposed for damage to each Safe City camera or piece of surveillance infrastructure.
"The ordinance also provides that if damage occurs during rallies, processions, sit-ins, protests, strikes or gatherings, the organisers may also be held responsible for the damage," the statement from the presidency said.

The statement said that the amount of the fine and the cost of the damage would be determined by an authorised officer after providing an opportunity for a hearing.
"The relevant person will have the right to appeal against the determination of the fine or damage cost before the District and Sessions Judge, Islamabad, within 30 days," it added.
It stated that if the imposed fine or damage amount was not paid, it may be recovered as arrears of land revenue. The amounts collected through fines and damage compensation would be used for the repair and replacement of Safe City cameras and surveillance infrastructure.
Acknowledging the difficulties and potential consequences of holding a long march amid extensive security and traffic restrictions imposed by the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N)-led federal and Punjab governments, the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) on Friday announced postponing its much-touted long march on Islamabad, originally scheduled for September 27, until October 4.
The decision appeared to render the federal government in a bind as it with the coordination of the Punjab government made an extensive security operation, which included blocking access points to Islamabad for traffic from Punjab with nail-studded metal barriers, erecting walls of shipping containers across the city, and deploying Rangers and large contingents of police.
Addressing a news conference in Peshawar, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, after securing formal approval from the party's political committee, announced that a "sea of people" would leave Peshawar on the new date as part of the party's political strategy.
He said the decision had been taken purely as a political strategy and that the march would now depart from Peshawar on October 4.
The decision had not, however, been endorsed by PTI's allies in TTAP as of the filing of this report, according to sources, who attributed the disagreement to a lack of coordination. K-P CM Afridi said TTAP leaders would join him on stage during the march, while acknowledging differences between PTI and the alliance.
Speculation over a possible postponement had circulated for about 40 hours, with the proposal first discussed at the K-P level during a Zoom meeting, according to party sources. A political committee meeting was subsequently convened to formally approve the decision, which sources said was endorsed without significant debate.
One party leader suggested not announcing a new date for the march, arguing that this would keep the government uncertain about PTI's plans. Asad Qaiser disagreed, saying that postponing the march without announcing a new date could be interpreted as a withdrawal, according to the sources.
The party also informed opposition leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai about the decision. The postponement to October 4 was also reported by multiple outlets following the political committee's decision.
Interestingly, Afridi held two news conferences on Friday. At the first, during the day, he vowed to proceed with the march at all costs but remained vague about its date. At a second news conference after the party meeting, he announced that the march had been postponed to October 4.
Based on Afridi's remarks, the move appeared aimed at allowing the party to mark PTI founder Imran Khan's birthday, which falls on October 5, in Islamabad.
Afridi said October 5, the birthday of PTI founder Imran, would be observed by party workers, who would cut cakes and celebrate a "Victory Day".
The decision to postpone the September 27 march was taken by the PTI political committee. Afridi said a proposal had been placed before the committee two days earlier to defer the march until the first week of October. Following lengthy consultations, the committee agreed to postpone it until October 4.
He said the decision was unanimous and reiterated that the postponement was part of a political strategy.
Afridi claimed that the federal government had become unnerved by the planned march and alleged that all routes leading into K-P had been blocked.
He likened the government's actions to the "same conspiracy" that had preceded the events surrounding East Pakistan and alleged that the measures were aimed at breaking up Pakistan. He questioned what the government hoped to prove by closing the routes.
"We are political people and will pursue a political struggle," Afridi said, adding that those expecting a repeat of the May 9-style operation against PTI were mistaken and that his party would foil "a conspiracy" against it.
He said that if the authorities wanted to arrest people or stop the march, they should come in uniform.
Afridi said PTI respected uniformed personnel, but those arriving in plain clothes would be dealt with differently.
He claimed that Imran could be released within a minute if the courts began functioning properly, adding that the Supreme Court (SC) had ordered the PTI founder's transfer to hospital but the order had not been implemented.
Afridi said all relevant issues had been discussed by the political committee and that the committee had agreed that the march would depart from Peshawar on October 4.
He also referred to a statement made some time ago by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz that she feared other provinces rather than India, and questioned the message such remarks sent to K-P.
Afridi criticised Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah for calling PTI members terrorists and asked what message the federal government was giving to the province.
He alleged that PTI members of the provincial assembly were being picked up and that roads had been blocked along the K-P border.
Afridi insisted that PTI was a political and peaceful movement and alleged that the government wanted to build cases against the party again in a manner similar to those following May 9.
"Our fight is for the supremacy of the Constitution and the law," he said.
The K-P chief minister alleged that efforts were being made to keep PTI and the establishment locked in confrontation, while planes and vehicles were being purchased.
He further accused the PML-N of effectively becoming the Punjab police and alleged that PML-N leaders were creating a "terrorist" narrative against PTI.
Afridi alleged that some people were being brought into PTI ranks and said he was warning in advance that anyone planning any action against the party should come in uniform.
He said PTI would not raise sticks against uniformed personnel.
Afridi appealed to the chief justice of the SC to take action over "efforts to cut K-P off from Pakistan".
He said the political struggle was a "Test match" and added that PTI had already won the toss.
Afridi said negotiations would continue after the long march and criticised the extensive use of containers in Islamabad, saying the federal capital had effectively been turned into a "container city".
He warned that those who came out on October 4 would not be under anyone's control.
The decision to postpone the march and the new date were also conveyed to Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas by PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, Afridi said.
He reiterated that postponing the long march was part of PTI's political strategy.
The postponement followed days of uncertainty over the September 27 schedule. PTI had previously been preparing for a nationwide protest and long march towards Islamabad, while opposition leaders had been consulting over the timing and political strategy surrounding the mobilisation.
It is pertinent to note that the decision came amid an internal debate over the feasibility and timing of the march, as party sources said there had been a proposal to "exhaust" the federal government and law-enforcement agencies because the federal capital and several routes had already been closed or restricted.
The sources claimed that the PTI had already achieved what it wanted through the march, with roads shut and hundreds of millions of rupees being spent on law enforcement.
The announcement was welcomed by PTI and some members of TTAP, who said the decision recognized the cost to the government of either maintaining the security arrangements until Oct. 4 or redeploying them closer to the new date.
A TTAP leader described the move as a significant setback for the government, saying the chief minister had gained an advantage simply by postponing the march. The leader said measures introduced to restrict PTI's planned mobilisation could ultimately impose a greater burden on the government if they had to be maintained or reinstated.
According to PTI leaders, the march will now leave Peshawar on October 4. Earlier discussions within the party had also considered October 5 to 10 as a possible new window.
The party sources said the decision had nothing to do with the Jamaat-i-Islami (JI), whose own protest march against the petroleum levy had been postponed at the request of the prime minister.
A senior PTI leader said the postponement offered the party two main advantages: it would increase pressure on a government that had taken extensive measures to prevent the march, while also creating an opportunity for negotiations to resume. PTI leaders have, however, said no meaningful negotiations were currently under way.
The decision was rejected by TTAP, whose leader said Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Nasir Abbas had been repeatedly sidelined by the K-P chief minister during consultations on major decisions. The leader said TTAP had also not been consulted before the Sept. 27 date was announced and was again left out of consultations over the latest postponement, describing it as adding "insult to injury."
Asked about the criticism, Afridi said PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan had communicated the party's decision to both leaders.
According to sources, PTI leadership had contacted Achakzai and requested that he announce a new date for the long march. At the time, however, Achakzai had refused to announce its postponement and maintained that the countrywide movement would begin on September 27.
Sources said Achakzai's position was that the movement would begin in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and other provinces on September 27 and would gradually move towards Islamabad.
The disagreement over postponing the long march between PTI leadership and Achakzai remained unresolved for a time, while efforts to persuade the opposition leader continued.
PTI leadership also continued consultations with opposition leaders over the date of the long march.
Against this backdrop, PTI Chairman arrived in Islamabad from Mianwali to meet Achakzai and other opposition leaders.
Gohar subsequently met Achakzai and briefed him on the PTI's position regarding the long march, according to sources.
The sources said PTI leadership wanted the long march postponed and wanted Achakzai, as opposition leader, to announce the decision.

title: Bill Gates warns AI is powerful enough to  cause a billion deaths
description: NBC News says philanthropist urges US lawmakers to step in  regulate development of technology
content:
Philanthropist urges US lawmakers to step in, regulate development of technology
Microsoft co-founder and billionaire philanthropist Bill Gates stated that artificial intelligence (AI) "is certainly powerful enough to drive events that cause a billion deaths," NBC News reported on Friday.
According to the television network, Gates added that "there’s never been a weapon as powerful as the combination of people with ill intent using the latest AI tools.”
He also called for United States lawmakers to regulate the development of AI. “No one thinks self-regulation is enough,” Gates told NBC News ’ Meet the Press in an interview, the television network said.
It added that the philanthropist noted, “You need law enforcement and the politicians to get into the discussion about what safeguards and monitoring look like,” NBC News said. It added that according to Gates, “that has to be a required thing. And it will be a little bit of overhead for the industry, but not a dramatic slowing of what they’re doing.”

The US television network also noted that Gates "didn't downplay the risk that AI could wipe out humanity in several years, but called for Americans not to ignore the risks that AI could be used by bad actors to cause large-scale harm as soon as today."
Gates' warning came after executives from three of the world's leading AI companies briefed the United Nations Security ​Council amid warnings that increasingly powerful AI systems could soon improve themselves, slip beyond human control and pose a ‌threat to international security.
Among those addressing the 15-member council during the annual General Assembly gathering were OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and Hugging Face co-founder Clément Delangue, three of the industry's most prominent executives.
"If managed poorly, I even believe that AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole," Anthropic's Amodei told the Security ​Council.
Governments have grappled with how to oversee AI systems that are advancing faster than regulators can keep up while the US ​and China — the two dominant players in AI development — remain divided over whether the technology needs global guardrails or ⁠should be left largely to market forces.

Yoshua Bengio, a Canadian considered one ​of the "Godfathers of AI" and co-chair of the Independent International Scientific Panel — created by the UN General Assembly last year — told the Security Council: "The ​dangers are real and imminent."
"This council faces an unprecedented threat, one that none of its members would choose, that none can contain alone, and that does not ‌respect the ⁠borders we defend," he said.
Despite warnings by industry leaders, US President Donald Trump maintained that he "rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control" AI, describing the technology as amazing.
The president noted that the US would be careful, but stated, "I'm not going to stifle ​growth of something ⁠that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution."

title: OpenAI probes unauthorised activity by AI agents as rogue ChatGPT agents leak user images
description: OpenAI said its agents leaked 53 images belonging to ChatGPT users
content:
OpenAI said its agents leaked 53 images belonging to ChatGPT users
OpenAI is still investigating the full extent of unauthorised activity by its artificial intelligence agents two months after one of its agents inadvertently hacked AI platform Hugging Face, TRT World reported , citing Reuters and people briefed on the matter.
The latest disclosure came on Friday, when OpenAI said its agents had leaked 53 images belonging to ChatGPT users. The company did not disclose whether the images were AI-generated or depicted real people, nor when they had been posted.
TRT World reported that The New York Times had also said on Friday that OpenAI's agents interacted with websites belonging to the US Commerce Department and the Securities and Exchange Commission in unusual ways this summer without the company's knowledge. Security researchers identified the incidents, and OpenAI said it had notified the two government agencies in recent weeks.
Read: OpenAI agents accessed information from US govt sites, company says
The incidents have raised concerns about autonomous AI agents, which can perform tasks and interact with external systems with limited human involvement, as companies face growing challenges in monitoring their behaviour.
OpenAI said it had begun alerting third parties, including universities, after determining that some of its AI models likely interfered with their online services during company testing.
According to TRT World , the company said in a statement that the notifications formed part of a broader internal review into how models behaved on the internet during training and evaluation.
Read more: China fuels rush to turn AI video into an industry
OpenAI said it had contacted organisations where its systems may have reduced service availability, bypassed security safeguards, or otherwise caused unintended harm.
"We are continuing to review agent activity in research and evaluation runs, working backward month by month starting from the Hugging Face incident," the company said in a statement.
The continuing investigation underscored the difficulties involved in monitoring increasingly capable AI systems and identifying unauthorised behaviour during testing and evaluation.

content:
Green-shirts face 5-4 defeat despite Sufyan Khan’s four goals in Pool B hockey thriller
Pakistan’s unbeaten run ended with a 5-4 defeat by Malaysia on Saturday in their Group B match of the men’s hockey competitions of the 20th Asian Games.
In a fast-paced game Pakistan took the lead in the third minute through Sufyan Khan who hit from the spot .
However two minutes latter Malaysia leveled when Shello Silverius needed a well-controlled field goal.
Malaysia kept the pressure and it paid dividends when they struck through Saari Faizal in the 23rd minute who hit it from short corner to take 2-1 advantage.
However it did not deter the Green-shirts and they staged a superb fight-back when Sufyan struck two back-to-back goals through penalty corner in the 39th and 43rd minute to put the Green-shirts 3-2 ahead.
Two minutes latter Malaysia brought the parity through a strike from Fitri Saari.
However a minute latter Sufyan landed his fourth goal to once again put Pakistan 4-3 ahead.
And it seemed that Pakistan would be able to keep the upper hand but Malaysia had thought otherwise.
Shello Silverius struck in the 56th minute via short corner before Azari Abu Kamal landed the winner in the 57th minute to seal a thrilling win for Malaysia.
This was the fourth straight win for Malaysia and it took them to 12 points at the summit.
The loss left Pakistan on the second spot of the group with nine points.
Sufyan’s four goals also propelled him to the summit with nine goals, all coming through penalty corners.
India’s Dilpreet Singh follows also with nine goals.
Pakistan will now face Oman while Malaysia will meet China in their group final matches on Monday.
Two teams from this group will make it to the semi-finals. China trail third with six points from three matches.
India lead Group A with nine points, followed by Japan also with nine points.
