title: A dangerous precedent
description: A dangerous precedent
content:
Karachi's residents deserve both security and justice
The recent incident involving the grisly murder of a married woman and her three children in Karachi's Surjani Town neighbourhood must have shocked millions of people in the metropolis and across the country. Equally shocking was the subsequent 'encounter' killing of the accused while he was in police custody. According to media reports, police said the suspect was already in custody and was being taken to recover the alleged murder weapon when he snatched an officer's pistol, opened fire and injured the officer. Other policemen then returned fire and killed him.
The incident comes about two months after three suspects, arrested in connection with the robbery and murder of a doctor in the Clifton neighbourhood, were shot dead in crossfire after law-enforcement personnel took them to the city's outskirts to arrest their alleged accomplices.
In July, two policemen from the Awami Colony police station were arrested and charged with attempted murder for allegedly shooting and injuring two youths in what was described as a staged encounter near the Double Road Football Ground in Korangi.
In April, the Sindh High Court expressed serious concern over the killing of a suspect in a suspicious encounter. The court warned that allowing police to continue such actions would undermine the very purpose of the courts and erode public confidence in the judicial system.
Anyone who talks to Karachi's residents will hear widespread anguish over the deteriorating law and order situation, particularly the persistent problem of street crime and the rising incidence of mobile-phone snatching.
Yet extrajudicial killings cannot be presented as a solution to the city's law and order problems. The state cannot afford to replace due process with the barrel of a gun, regardless of the seriousness of the crime with which a suspect is charged. Every accused person has the right to a fair trial, and it is for the courts to determine guilt and award punishment on the basis of evidence.
The killing of suspects in custody, particularly when police describe their deaths as the result of encounters, raises serious questions about accountability and the credibility of investigations. It also deprives victims' families of the opportunity to see a case properly tried and a conviction secured through the judicial process. A dead suspect cannot stand trial, challenge the evidence against him or disclose the possible involvement of other accomplices.
The focus, therefore, should be on strengthening the entire criminal justice system rather than relying on encounters as a measure of police effectiveness. The police must conduct professional investigations, preserve evidence, obtain forensic support and prepare cases that can withstand scrutiny in court. Prosecutors, in turn, must be adequately resourced and closely involved in building cases, while courts must have the capacity to dispose of criminal cases expeditiously.
The ultimate measure of effective policing is not the number of suspects killed in encounters but the number of cases in which perpetrators are identified, arrested, prosecuted and convicted on the basis of solid evidence. A functioning criminal justice system must ensure that those responsible for heinous crimes are punished, but that punishment must follow a judicial process rather than an encounter.
Karachi's residents deserve both security and justice. Sacrificing one at the expense of the other is no solution. If the authorities are serious about restoring public confidence, they must ensure that every allegation of an extrajudicial killing is impartially investigated and that police officers found responsible for unlawful killings are held accountable. At the same time, greater investment is needed in investigation, prosecution, forensic capacity and witness protection so that suspected criminals can be brought before the courts and convictions secured on the basis of credible evidence.
Only then can the state demonstrate that it is capable of combating crime without compromising the rule of law.

content:
Chris Hansen responds to 'Primetime' with the trailer for 'I’m Chris Hansen', a documentary years in the making now
Chris Hansen is pushing back against the A24 film Primetime with the trailer for his upcoming documentary I’m Chris Hansen , which explores the career of the former Dateline NBC journalist.
Hansen’s TruBlu streaming network released the trailer on Friday, September 25. According to The Hollywood Reporter , the documentary has been in production for three years, meaning it was not created specifically in response to Primetime , which stars Robert Pattinson as Hansen.
The documentary arrives as Primetime opens in theatres. Hansen has been publicly critical of the film, calling it “a complete work of fiction attached to a real name” in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter.
Hansen said the film presents a darker and more dramatic version of the work associated with his To Catch a Predator investigations. He also argued that the movie could misrepresent efforts by people working to protect children from predators.
Hansen had not watched Primetime before the interview because he declined to sign a nondisclosure agreement connected to the project. However, he promoted TruBlu around the film’s theatrical release by purchasing advertisements that appeared ahead of screenings.
Despite his criticism of the movie, Hansen said he has no personal issue with Pattinson. He described the actor as talented and said Pattinson had been gracious when discussing him.
Hansen also questioned why the Primetime filmmakers did not contact him while developing a film in which Pattinson portrays him. He suggested the filmmakers had their own interpretation of the story, though that characterization reflects Hansen’s view.
Meanwhile, I’m Chris Hansen will give viewers a documentary focused on Hansen himself and his career in investigative television and true crime.

title: 5 Netanyahu claims at UN that clash with documented findings
description: Israeli premier s claims on Gaza conflict with UN  US and Israeli military linked findings
content:
Israeli premier's claims on Gaza conflict with UN, US and Israeli military-linked findings
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has repeatedly used the UN General Assembly podium to defend Israel’s actions in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, making claims that have been challenged by international bodies, humanitarian agencies and, in some cases, data from Israel’s own military.
In speeches between 2024 and 2026, Netanyahu rejected allegations of genocide, described civilian casualties as exceptionally low, blamed Hamas for Gaza’s aid crisis and played down Israeli occupier violence in the occupied West Bank.
A review of five such claims shows substantial discrepancies between Netanyahu’s account and documented findings.
Genocide allegation is ‘the greatest lie of the century’
In his 2026 UN address, Netanyahu called accusations that Israel was committing genocide in Gaza “the greatest lie of the century”, arguing that warnings to civilians, vaccinations and food deliveries were incompatible with genocide.
A UN-mandated Independent International Commission of Inquiry reached the opposite conclusion in September 2025. After examining witness testimony, satellite imagery, official statements and other evidence, it found reasonable grounds that Israeli authorities and forces had committed four of the five acts defined as genocide under the Genocide Convention.
Also Read: Inside the UN walkout: Who left and who stayed for Netanyahu’s speech
The commission also concluded that statements by Netanyahu and other senior officials were evidence of genocidal intent. Israel rejected the findings.
People carry the body of a Palestinian who was killed in Israeli strikes, according to medics, during a funeral in Gaza City, September 1, 2026. REUTERS
The International Court of Justice has not issued a final judgment in South Africa’s genocide case, but has ordered Israel to prevent acts covered by the convention and enable urgently needed humanitarian assistance.
Civilian casualty ratio is exceptionally low
Netanyahu told the General Assembly in 2025 that Gaza’s civilian-to-combatant casualty ratio was below two to one, calling it exceptionally low.
He also said in his Sept 27, 2024 UN address: “And no army has done what Israel is doing to minimise civilian casualties.”
A joint investigation by The Guardian , +972 Magazine and Local Call, based on a classified Israeli military intelligence database, found that as of May 2025 about 8,900 named Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad fighters were listed as dead or probably dead, compared with an overall death toll of about 53,000.
The figures suggested roughly 83% of those killed were civilians.
Read More: Gaza students return to in-person schooling for first time in three years
Since Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza began in October 2023, more than 73,000 Palestinians have been killed and around 175,000 injured, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry.
Hamas stole much of Gaza’s humanitarian aid
Netanyahu has repeatedly accused Hamas of stealing large quantities of aid entering Gaza.
In his 2026 UN address, he said Hamas “stole much of the food we let into Gaza”, as he argued that the group was keeping Palestinian civilians in harm’s way.
An internal US Agency for International Development review found no evidence of systematic diversion of US-funded aid by Hamas. It examined 156 cases of theft or loss between October 2023 and May 2025 and found no indication that Hamas benefited.
Senior Israeli military officials were also reported to have said they found no evidence that Hamas systematically stole UN aid, describing the UN distribution system as largely effective.
Two million tonnes of food disproves starvation claims
Netanyahu told the UN that Israel had enabled the distribution of two million tonnes of food into Gaza, or about one tonne per resident, presenting the figure as evidence against allegations of starvation and genocide.
“What genocidal regime enables the distribution of 2m tonnes of food into Gaza? That’s a tonne for every person."
A Palestinian girl holds a container at a food distribution point in the Nuseirat camp for refugees in the central Gaza Strip on May 21, 2025. PHOTO: AFP
But aid entering Gaza is not the same as food reaching civilians. UN agencies have documented restrictions, insecurity, damaged roads and military operations that hindered collection and distribution.
Israel completely halted the entry of goods and humanitarian supplies from March 2 to May 18, 2025, and has repeatedly blocked, restricted, and paused the entry of humanitarian supplies over long periods throughout the conflict
In August 2025, the UN-backed Integrated Food Security Phase Classification confirmed famine in Gaza Governorate, saying more than half a million people across Gaza faced catastrophic conditions marked by starvation, destitution and death.
The latest IPC assessment says 1.4 million people are still projected to face high levels of acute food insecurity through December 2026.
Occupier violence is the work of a small fringe
In his 2026 address, Netanyahu described violence by Israelis in the occupied West Bank as the work of about 150 “juvenile delinquents” and suggested only “two or three” Palestinians had been killed.
UN monitoring shows a far wider pattern.
By July 20, 2026, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs had recorded more than 1,330 occupier attacks resulting in casualties or property damage since the start of the year — more than six a day.
OCHA also recorded 18 Palestinian deaths linked to occupier attacks by that date: 12 killed by occupiers, three by Israeli forces and three in cases where responsibility was disputed.
Between January 2023 and July 2026, OCHA said occupier attacks and related access restrictions had caused full or partial displacement in 121 Palestinian communities.
The figures contrast with Netanyahu’s portrayal of occupier violence as a marginal phenomenon.

title: Tehran will make no nuclear concessions  Iranian official says
description: Hormuz is a key bargaining chip  with Iran seeking sanctions relief and Washington demanding free ship passage
content:
Hormuz is a key bargaining chip, with Iran seeking sanctions relief and Washington demanding free ship passage
Iran will show no ​flexibility over its nuclear programme even if the United States accepts its proposal to reopen ‌the Strait of Hormuz, which calls for steps including the lifting of a US naval blockade on Iranian ports, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Friday.
The official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the waterway would remain closed until “all of Iran’s conditions ​are met” by the United States.
Under Iran’s proposal , Tehran has offered to reopen the strategically vital Strait of ​Hormuz. Within seven days, hostilities would end on all fronts, including Lebanon, the United ⁠States would lift its blockade on Iranian ports, release Iran’s frozen funds and waive its oil sanctions, Iran's ​Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Thursday.
Read More: UAE bars Iranian airline flights as US sanctions bite
The proposal follows a sharp escalation in Middle East tensions after seven months ​of war between Iran and the United States, with Iran-backed Houthi militias in Yemen launching missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia.
The strait has become the central bargaining chip in efforts to end the US-Iran conflict, with Iran seeking relief from the US blockade ​that is choking its economy and Washington seeking free passage for ships on the global oil supply route ​now blocked by Tehran.
In a meeting with journalists on Thursday on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly , Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said ⁠he hoped a deal with Washington to end the hostilities could be reached before the US midterm elections on November 3.
Tehran said it would be prepared to engage in detailed negotiations over its nuclear program only after its conditions are met by the US.
But the official said Iran would give no concessions over its rights, including ​enriching uranium or shipping its ​highly enriched uranium out ⁠of the country, one of the main US demands.
Israel, the United States and other Western states have long accused Iran of seeking nuclear weapons, including pointing to its ​move to enrich uranium to 60%, far higher than needed for civilian uses and ​closer to ⁠the 90% needed for a weapon. Iran denies seeking nuclear weapons.
The International Atomic Energy Agency estimates that Iran had 440.9 kilogrammes of uranium enriched to 60% when Israel and the US attacked Iranian nuclear facilities in June 2025. How much ⁠of ​that has survived is unclear.
Iranian authorities have said that Iran could agree ​to dilute its most highly enriched uranium.
In May, Reuters reported that Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has issued a directive that the country's ​HEU should not be sent abroad, according to two senior Iranian sources.

title: Charles Spencer reveals his biggest regret about Princess Diana
description: Spencer said he believes he could have done more to help her manage the intense attention surrounding her public life
content:
Spencer said he believes he could have done more to help her manage the intense attention surrounding her public life
Charles Spencer has revealed the one thing he wishes he had done differently for his late sister, Princess Diana, nearly 30 years after her death.
The 9th Earl Spencer opened up about his relationship with Diana in an exclusive interview with PEOPLE, published as he promotes his new memoir, Swan Song: Diana, My Sister. Looking back on Diana's final years, Spencer said he believes he could have done more to help her manage the intense attention surrounding her public life.
“Could I have done more to help her with her public life? I probably could,” Spencer told PEOPLE. He explained that he did support Diana in some ways towards the end of her life, including helping her with a major libel case against a British newspaper and quietly fighting some battles on her behalf.
Spencer's reflection comes as he speaks openly about his sister for the first time in decades. His memoir revisits their childhood, their complicated family history, Diana's marriage and divorce from then-Prince Charles, and the events surrounding her death in August 1997.
The memoir has also prompted Spencer to address a longstanding claim about his relationship with Diana. He pushed back against suggestions that he refused to give his sister a home at Althorp after her 1996 divorce.
According to Spencer, Diana had asked to live at the Garden House on the Althorp estate, where their sister Jane Fellowes had previously lived with her children. Spencer said he wanted to clarify that security concerns prevented Diana and her sons, Prince William and Prince Harry, from living there.
“The local police went around there with me and they said, they just couldn’t protect William and Harry,” Spencer said. “She could not have lived at the Garden House. It was not a viable option.”
Diana instead remained at Kensington Palace following her divorce and lived there with William and Harry until her death in a car crash on August 31, 1997. Spencer later delivered her eulogy at Westminster Abbey, where he publicly honoured his sister and criticised the intense media attention she had faced.
Now, as the 30th anniversary of Diana's death approaches in 2027, Spencer says writing Swan Song gave him an opportunity to tell his version of their relationship and preserve his memories of his sister. The memoir was released on September 22, 2026.

title: PM Shehbaz urges Middle East peace  warns India against weaponizing water at UNGA
description: PM to highlight Pakistan   s peace efforts  cross border terrorism and other wide ranging issues
content:
Says any attempt to stop Pakistan’s water will be treated as 'act of war'
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif on Friday called for renewed diplomacy to end escalating conflicts in the Middle East while warning India that any attempt to stop, impede or divert Pakistan’s share of river waters would be treated as an act of war.
Addressing the General Debate of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, the prime minister urged a world fractured by war, occupation and mistrust to rediscover the courage of diplomacy, declaring that Pakistan had chosen dialogue over confrontation, cooperation over coercion and peace over war.
“We live at a dangerous moment. But our future is certainly not predetermined,” he told leaders of the 193-member body.
“War is a choice. Peace is also a choice. And sometimes, the greater courage lies not in starting a war, but in preventing one,” he said. “Pakistan has made its choice. We have chosen dialogue over confrontation. We have chosen cooperation over coercion. We have chosen peace over war.”
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif strongly condemns recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, saying the attempted drone attack on Makkah Mukarramah has outraged Muslims worldwide. Addressing the UN General Assembly in New York, he says threats to the safety and sanctity of holy sites… pic.twitter.com/2p2v2UY4LP
Speaking under the session’s theme, “Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations That Delivers for All,” PM Shehbaz presented Pakistan’s position on conflicts in the Middle East, Palestine and Jammu and Kashmir, tensions with India, terrorism emanating from Afghanistan, climate change, economic inequality, debt distress and reform of the United Nations.
He opened his address with traditional salutations and a verse from the Holy Quran on peace, followed by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah’s declaration of Pakistan’s steadfast support for the UN Charter.
Turning to the escalating conflicts in the Middle East, PM Shehbaz said diplomacy must not be drowned out by the sounds of war.
“Amid the roar of missiles, drones and guns, the voices for diplomacy must echo even louder,” he said.
Pakistan brought US, Iran ‘under one roof’: Shehbaz
The prime minister said Pakistan had moved swiftly after the outbreak of the regional conflict to help bring Washington and Tehran to the negotiating table in Islamabad, ultimately leading to the signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding.
He praised Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir for their efforts to create space for diplomacy under exceptionally difficult circumstances.
Also Read : Islamabad MoU remains acceptable to Iran, Pezeshkian tells PM Shehbaz in UNGA meet
Calling the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb vital arteries of the global economy, he said they must remain open as passages connecting nations rather than becoming flashpoints of confrontation.
“These waters must carry the promise of prosperity, not the perils of war,” he said.
Makkah pact not against any country: PM Shehbaz
The premier strongly condemned recent Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, particularly what he described as an attempted strike on the holy city of Makkah.
“Any threat to the safety and sanctity of the Haramain Sharifain is a red line that must never be crossed,” he said, reaffirming Pakistan’s solidarity with Saudi Arabia.
Referring to the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement among Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, the prime minister said the alliance was not directed against any country but represented a collective commitment to regional defence, stability and peace.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif says the historic Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye Joint Defence Agreement reflects Pakistan’s longstanding commitment to peace. Addressing the UN General Assembly in New York, he stresses that the alliance is not directed against any country and is a… pic.twitter.com/NDEmslIWQK
On South Asia, PM Shehbaz recalled last year’s conflict between Pakistan and India, saying Pakistan had exercised its inherent right to self-defense and that its armed forces, led by Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, had responded with precision and professionalism.
“They silenced the enemy, repulsed its attacks and taught it a lesson it shall never, ever forget,” he said.
The prime minister praised US President Donald Trump, saying his “resolute and visionary” intervention at a critical moment had helped prevent a potentially catastrophic confrontation between the two nuclear-armed neighbors and saved hundreds of millions of lives.
“And who knows the extent of devastation that could have taken place had President Trump not stepped in at this critical moment with clarity of thought and action,” he said.
Kashmir remains Pakistan’s ‘jugular vein’: Shehbaz
PM Shehbaz told the General Assembly that lasting peace in South Asia remained inseparable from a just settlement of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute.
He said the Kashmiri people had waited for decades for the United Nations to fulfil its commitment to a free and impartial plebiscite. He accused India of arbitrary detentions, extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, sexual violence, and collective punishment in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir.
He also accused New Delhi of attempting to alter the disputed territory’s legal status and demographic character through unilateral measures.
“Helpless Kashmiri mothers and fathers yearn for their sons and daughters who never return,” PM Shehbaz said. “Their homes lie silent, under curfew and in deep grief. For many, there is no closure — only a lifetime spent searching for graves that bear no names.”
He reaffirmed Pakistan’s diplomatic, political and moral support for the Kashmiri people until they attained their inalienable right to self-determination.
“Kashmir has, and always will be, Pakistan’s jugular vein,” he said.
The prime minister said South Asia must not reach that “precipice” again, but added that this required a “just and fair solution” to the Jammu and Kashmir dispute.
Any attempt to stop water ‘act of war’: PM Shehbaz
Turning to water security, the prime minister strongly opposed the weaponization of water and described the Indus River system as the “lifeblood” of Pakistan and the wider region.
He said India’s unilateral decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance had no legal basis, adding that the position taken by UN experts and the Court of Arbitration had vindicated Pakistan’s stance on the treaty’s continuing validity.
“Water must never be weaponized. Rivers should nourish nations, not divide them,” PM Shehbaz said.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif says water must never be weaponized, warning that any attempt to stop, impede or divert Pakistan’s share of Indus waters will be treated as an act of war. Addressing the UN General Assembly in New York, he says India’s decision to hold the Indus… pic.twitter.com/xsb41dolMo
He warned that Pakistan would regard any attempt by India to stop, impede or divert its rightful share of the waters as an act of war.
“India must make no mistake about it,” he declared.
He also expressed concern over what he called an alarming rise in Islamophobia, saying Muslims faced hate speech, discrimination, attacks on mosques and desecration of the Holy Quran.
He alleged that the RSS-driven Hindutva ideology in India was fuelling religious hatred and leading to lynching, communal violence, attacks on places of worship and restrictions on religious freedom.
He also referred to the demolition of a 150-year-old mosque in Saharanpur earlier this month as a “case in point”.
“Religious hatred must have no place in this world,” he said.
PM Shehbaz decries world’s silence on Gaza
The prime minister devoted a significant portion of his address to the suffering of Palestinians, invoking the deaths of children, including Hind Rajab and eight-year-old Wafaa Akila, as symbols of what he called the international community’s silence and failure.
“Does not a child born in Gaza deserve the same life, the same future and the same dream as a child anywhere else in the world?” he asked.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif says children in Gaza deserve the same lives, dreams and futures as children anywhere else, calling their deaths an indictment of the world’s collective silence and inaction. Addressing the UN General Assembly in New York, he condemns Israeli… pic.twitter.com/65IJUUFhkN
“The tragedies of Hind Rajab, Wafaa Akila and countless others will echo through history as an indictment of our collective silence and inaction.”
Condemning the widening violence in the West Bank, Lebanon and Syria, PM Shehbaz reiterated Pakistan’s position that an independent and viable Palestinian state based on the pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital, offered the only just and lasting solution.
Shehbaz calls for ‘verifiable, decisive action’ against terrorists
On terrorism, the prime minister said Pakistan had lost nearly 100,000 civilians and members of its armed forces and suffered economic losses exceeding $150 billion in the fight against militancy.
He said the world was safer because of Pakistan’s sacrifices and warned that Afghan territory continued to be used by the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan and the Balochistan Liberation Army — groups Islamabad officially refers to as Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan — to destabilize the country.
“This must come to a grinding halt,” he said.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif says Pakistan has sacrificed nearly 100,000 lives and suffered over $150 billion in economic losses fighting terrorism. Addressing the UN General Assembly in New York, he pays tribute to the armed forces and civilians whose sacrifices have made the… pic.twitter.com/rhQ91y1K5A
PM Shehbaz urged Afghanistan’s Taliban authorities to meet their international obligations and take verifiable and decisive action to prevent Afghan territory from being used against Pakistan or any other country.
He also called on Kabul to respect the fundamental rights of the Afghan people, particularly women and girls, under all circumstances.
Turning to Pakistan’s economy, PM Shehbaz said difficult structural reforms and stringent fiscal discipline had restored macroeconomic stability and laid the foundation for sustainable and inclusive growth.
He outlined efforts to modernize agriculture and industry, develop mineral resources, digitize the economy, equip young people with artificial intelligence and information technology skills, and strengthen regional connectivity.
He praised Chinese President Xi Jinping’s leadership in advancing the Global Development, Global Security, Global Civilization and Global Governance initiatives.
Developing countries, PM Shehbaz said, urgently required timely debt relief, affordable long-term financing, and a stronger voice in international financial institutions.
He said Pakistan was opening new avenues of economic cooperation with China through the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor and expanding connectivity with the Gulf, Central Asia, and regions beyond.
On climate change, the prime minister said Pakistan contributed less than one per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions but continued to endure some of the crisis’s most devastating consequences.
He called on developed countries to fulfil their climate finance commitments, accelerate funding for loss and damage, and provide adequate support for adaptation and resilience.
While addressing the UN General Assembly in New York, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said Pakistan contributes less than 1% of global emissions yet repeatedly bears the devastating consequences of climate change. He urged developed countries to honour their climate finance… pic.twitter.com/bLdPspaJkp
“The theme of this session calls upon us to restore trust. But trust cannot be restored by simple words alone. It must be earned through actions and behavior,” PM Shehbaz said.
“We will restore trust when rivers become lifelines of cooperation, not fault lines of conflict. We will restore trust when those who fueled the climate crisis protect those who suffer most from its devastating consequences. And, above all, trust will be restored when the guns are silenced and replaced by handshakes, embraces, and smiles.”
Calling for a stronger and more effective United Nations, PM Shehbaz said the Security Council must become more representative, democratic, and accountable. Reform, he stressed, should reflect the aspirations of the majority of nations rather than protect the privileges of a select few.
He reaffirmed Pakistan’s guiding principle: “Reform for All, Privilege for None.”
Concluding his address, the prime minister returned to the defining choice confronting the international community.
“Let this 81st General Assembly make the same choice — for us, for our children and for generations yet unborn,” he said.
“Let us restore trust. Let us preserve peace. And let us prove that, even in a divided world, humanity can still choose to stand together”

title: PTI s long march to Islamabad to kick off from Peshawar on Oct 4  K P CM Afridi
description: Says it is a unanimous decision of the party s political committee to postpone Sept 27 start
content:
Says it is a unanimous decision of the party's political committee to postpone Sept 27 start
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Friday night confirmed that the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) long march to Islamabad would kick off from Peshawar on October 4 instead of the previous September 27 date.
It said it was the unanimous decision of the party's political committee.
لانگ مارچ 4 اکتوبر بروز اتوار پشاور سے اسلام آباد روانہ ہو گا۔ یہ سیاسی کمیٹی کا متفقہ فیصلہ ہے۔ وزیر اعلی @SohailAfridiISF #LongMarchOnOctober4th pic.twitter.com/xmYNPZgzzu
While addressing a press conference at the Chief Minister House in Peshawar, Afridi stated that the march would leave Peshawar on October 4, while the birthday of PTI founder Imran Khan would be marked in Swabi on October 5.
Afridi said all matters had been discussed in the political committee meeting and described the decision to defer the march as part of the party’s “political strategy”, further adding that negotiations would continue even after the march.
He further stated that Barrister Gohar had informed National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Achakzai and Senate Leader of Opposition Allama Raja Nasir Abbas about the political committee’s decision.
Criticising the federal government, the chief minister questioned the purpose of blocking roads and alleged that PTI lawmakers were being picked up and routes along the K-P border had been closed.
Afridi alleged that the authorities wanted to launch cases against PTI workers similar to those registered after the May 9 events. "PTI is a political and peaceful party, and its struggle is for the supremacy of the Constitution and law".
The chief minister also criticised the federal government over what he described as the purchase of aircraft and vehicles, and alleged that the Pakistan Muslim League Nawaz (PML-N) had effectively become the "Punjab police".
Afridi further said that Imran would secure bail within half an hour if the courts started functioning properly. "The Supreme Court ordered Imran to be shifted to hospital, but that order has not been implemented".
He also alleged that the government was creating a “terrorist” narrative against PTI and warned that some people were being inducted into the party’s ranks.
یہ پنجاب کے کیپیٹل لاہور کا الیکشن ہار چکے ہیں ، ان کو ملک پر آپ (اسٹیبلشمنٹ) نے مسلط کیا ہے ان کا جو بیانیہ ہوگا وہ آپ کا بیانہ سمجھا جائے گا ۔ یہ جو انتشار پھیلانا چاہتے یہ چاہتے تحریک انصاف اور اسٹیبلشمنٹ لڑتے رہیں ان کے تو مزے ہیں گیارہ ارب کے جہاز خرید رہے ، ایک ایک ارب کی… pic.twitter.com/J2ztfGLY8E
Afridi pledged to "respect those who wear the uniform, but if they commit illegal and unconstitutional acts, we will stop them with words, we will stop them by speaking out, we will stop them even by embracing them, we will not raise a stick against them, nor a stone nor a baton, we will remind them of their duty".
جن کے بدن پر وردی ہو گی، ہم اُن کی عزت کرینگے، وہ غیر قانونی و غیر آئینی کام کرینگے تو ہم اُنہیں زبان سے بھی روکیں گے، بول کر بھی روکیں گے، گلے لگا کر بھی روکیں گے، ہم اُن کیخلاف نہ ڈنڈا اُٹھائیں گے، نہ پتھر نہ ڈنڈا، ہم اُنہیں اُن کی ڈیوٹی کی یاد دلائیں گے، سُہیل آفریدی… pic.twitter.com/QSRBxrsnIG
The chief minister also said that around 65,000 police personnel had been appointed to oversee the situation in K-P, but had not been provided basic facilities such as food and housing. He said the provincial government was ready to host and feed them, if asked. "The people of K-P are welcoming towards guests."
Afridi also sought the attention of Islamabad High Court Chief Justice (CJ) Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar. "CJ Dogar, your orders have been flouted. You said Islamabad would not be closed. It is closed right now. Kindly oversee that your directions are implemented".
He also requested Supreme Court Chief Justice Yahya Afridi to look into the matter while stating that K-P was his province and it had been disconnected from the rest of the country. “You should look into the rights of the people of this province”.
Responding to questions regarding the security situation, Afridi said, “The province has been under threat since the terrorists were rehoused in K-P.”
He also lamented that the NFC share of K-P had not been updated since 2018, even after the merger of tribal areas.
“This is a Test match, and we have already won the toss,” Afridi said, adding that the Test match had already begun.
He further said Islamabad had been turned into a “container city” and reiterated that negotiations would continue after the march.
“This time, what we are going to see has never been witnessed in Pakistan’s history,” Afridi said. “The anger and hatred visible in the eyes of the people is something I have never seen in my 18 to 20 years in politics.”
Afridi said those taking to the streets on October 4 would not remain under anyone’s control and would not return until their demands were met, while insisting that the mobilisation would remain peaceful.
“Our political decision is clear,” he said, adding that the relevant leadership had been informed of the plan.
Afridi also described the delay in the planned mobilisation as part of a "political strategy", arguing that the reaction from government ministers and “pro-government journalists” demonstrated the significance of PTI's strategy.
The chief minister said that a “sea of people” would emerge from across Pakistan on October 4 and claimed that October 5 would be observed as a “day of victory” under the leadership of the PTI founder.
The PTI leadership earlier decided to postpone its planned long march on Islamabad until October 4 or 5, according to party sources.
The PTI had announced last month that it would march to Islamabad on September 27 to press for the release of party founder Imran Khan. The party had been preparing a central convoy from K-P, with caravans from other parts of the country expected to join before proceeding towards the federal capital. The federal government warned the party against going ahead with the march.
The decision was taken by the party’s political committee after consultations on whether to proceed with the march on the previously announced date of September 27. A majority of the leadership had favoured holding the march as scheduled, but the committee ultimately agreed to defer it until October 4, party sources added.
The source also revealed that Tehreek Tahaffuz-e-Ayeen Pakistan (TTAP), led by National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai, has refused to back the proposal to delay the march.
Achakzai has made it clear that the march should begin on September 27; otherwise, the TTAP will not support the march. The source said attempts are being made to convince the TTAP chief.
Earlier, K-P CM Afridi, speaking at a press conference at the Chief Minister’s House in Peshawar, said that the planned long march on Islamabad would go ahead despite road blockades and other measures. “Our long march will definitely take place. This time, we will definitely come out,” he said.
وزیراعلیٰ خیبرپختونخوا محمد سہیل خان آفریدی کی 27 ستمبر بالقسط لانگ مارچ کے حوالے سے اہم پریس کانفرنس! pic.twitter.com/6UPL9CzRuC
The chief minister criticised the placement of nails on roads at the K-P boundary, saying the move raised questions about whether the province was being cut off from the rest of the country. “No matter how many nails they put in the roads, this long march will not be stopped,” he said.
Afridi also questioned what he called a growing narrative that one province faced threats from other provinces rather than India. He also said that officials from one province had entered another and clashed with government employees.
“A narrative has been created for the past month that one province faces a threat from the other three provinces,” he said, asking whether the people of K-P were being portrayed negatively.
He added that PTI parliamentary leader Shahid Khattak and the provincial information minister had been barred from appearing in the media.
شاہد خٹک تحریک انصاف کے پارلیمانی لیڈر ہیں خیبرپختونخوا سے تعلق ہے اسے میڈیا پر بین کر دیا گیا ہے اس کا کیا مطلب لیا جائے ؟ انفارمیشن منسٹر خیبرپختونخوا کو بین کیا گیا ہے کیا مطلب لیا جائے ؟ ابھی مجھے اطلاع ملی ہے کہ وزیر اعلیٰ خیبرپختونخوا کی کوریج سے روک دیا گیا ہے اس کا کیا… pic.twitter.com/G3flVPM6Cj
He also said that K-P ministers were being taken away by people in plain clothes and that the province was being pushed in a different direction.
Afridi also criticised the closure of the provincial secretariat following a security alert, questioning why government operations had been halted when the area was already under security control. “The entire cantonment is under their control. How can there be a threat here?” he asked.
He said he had personally reopened the mosque inside the secretariat after it was closed over the rumoured security threat and offered prayers there. He also walked around the premises before urging people in K-P not to be afraid. “Till your CM is with you, no one will look at the province with an evil eye,” he added.
کیا آپ خیبرپختونخوا میں دوسرے صوبے کی ایڈمنسٹریشن لانچ کرنے جا رہے ہیں دوسرے صوبے کی ایڈمنسٹریشن خیبرپختونخوا کی حدود میں گھس کر کاروائی کر رہی ہے اسکا کیا مطلب لیا جائے ؟ یہ جو کیلیں آپ سڑکوں پر کھود رہے ہو یہ اس نظام کے طابوت میں آخری کیلیں ثابت ہوں گی ہم پاکستان کی حفاظت کریں… pic.twitter.com/A0L8VWE6ct
Meanwhile, all hotels within the Faizabad area have been ordered to close ahead of the possible PTI long march. Restaurants and shopkeepers have also been directed to close their businesses by this evening.
Guest houses and transport terminals at Faizabad have been ordered to close from tonight, according to police sources.
All hostels in and around Faizabad have also been directed to be vacated by tonight. Hotel, restaurant and hostel owners have been asked to submit affidavits to the relevant police stations, stating that their commercial buildings have been completely vacated.
Police have directed that action be taken against owners who fail to submit the affidavits by tomorrow evening, according to police sources.
The Centre on Thursday moved swiftly to deploy paramilitary Pakistan Rangers in several Punjab districts and the federal capital to assist police in maintaining law and order and responding to potential security threats, according to a notification issued by the Ministry of Interior.
The move came as PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan urged the government to open negotiations over the party's planned September 27 long march, warning that political workers should not be confronted with force.
He said his party did not want the public and law-enforcement personnel to come face to face.
Speaking to the media outside Parliament, Gohar said dialogue was essential given the seriousness of the situation and the fact that a major political party was preparing for a long march. He urged the government not to use net launchers against those taking part in the protest.
Read: Rule of law, supremacy of Constitution to prevail during PTI long march to Islamabad: Gohar
He said political workers were not supposed to be dealt with through such measures. Instead, their grievances should be heard and resolved, they should be provided justice and their concerns considered seriously, with both sides putting their egos aside.
Gohar said the entire issue had been turned into a battle of egos and that the government would have to set aside its ego.
He said the use of net launchers should be abandoned and a way found to ensure serenity, adding that PTI did not want the public and law-enforcement personnel to confront one another.
"We are saying that our voice should be heard. We are peaceful and are coming out for our rights. We are raising the voice for justice and have repeatedly said that we were not heard and were not given justice," he said.
Gohar said ministers could issue whatever statements they wished, but no minister had said that the government had listened to PTI's concerns and delivered justice.
He said the party had announced its programme well in advance and there would be no change in it.
Hazara road links with Punjab have been severed as authorities took measures to prevent the PTI from holding its proposed long march on September 27, causing difficulties for passengers and residents travelling towards Rawalpindi and Islamabad.
The Hassan Abdal Road linking Haripur with Punjab has been blocked with containers at Jhari Kas, while the Haripur-Khanpur-Taxila Road has been closed at Gangu Bahadur by placing containers.
Containers have also been brought to the bridge over the Haro River at Ahata Taxila to block the Haripur-Hattar-Taxila Road. However, traffic on the route remains open for now and is expected to be blocked by Thursday night.
Preparations to deal with the PTI's September 27 long march have entered the final phase in Rawalpindi Division, with more than 43,000 personnel to be deployed in Attock, Rawalpindi, Murree, Jhelum and Chakwal to prevent protesters from entering the twin cities.
Police authorities have decided to keep Rawalpindi and Islamabad open, with all preparations in place until the march enters Punjab territory.
Officials will assess the situation under a "wait and see" policy and take a response according to the situation if marchers cross barriers in Punjab and move closer to the twin cities.
In Rawalpindi Division, more than 43,000 police personnel will perform march-related duties in Attock, Rawalpindi, Murree, Jhelum and Chakwal. Of these, 30,000 personnel will be deployed in Attock.
Read more: Govt draws line ahead of PTI march
Around 14,250 personnel will be deployed at sealing points on the M-1 motorway, including Haroon Bridge, Ghazi-Barotha Motorway Bridge, Tower Hill, Hazara Motorway and Pathar Garh.
Another 11,450 personnel will be deployed at sealing points on the N-5 and N-80 routes, including Attock Khurd, Tarbela Road Jhansa, Haro Bridge, Jablat Bridge, Chaska Point and Khushal Garh. Around 5,000 personnel will be deployed at sealing points on the M-14 CPEC route, including Dhok Syedan Interchange and other M-14 points.
All personnel have been directed to perform duty equipped with riot-control equipment and kits.
For transport and logistics, six armoured personnel carrier (APC) vans, two water cannons, 20 prison vans, 50 megaphones and 12 quadcopters, along with operators, have also been requested. Additional surveillance equipment includes 12 quadcopters and their operators.

title: Makkah pact military chiefs condemn attacks on holy city at Riyadh meeting
description: Foreign ministers of Pakistan  Saudi Arabia and Turkiye condemn attacks targeting Saudi Arabia in a joint statement
content:
Reviews security threats, reaffirms collective defence, and vow to strengthen military cooperation
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye on Friday strongly condemned attacks targeting the holy city of Makkah as senior military leadership from the three countries reaffirmed their commitment to the collective defence of the Kingdom under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, the military media wing said.
According to a statement issued by the Inter Services Public Relations (ISPR), the meeting of the Chiefs of Defence Forces and Chiefs of General Staff of the three countries was held in Riyadh on Sept 25, with the participation of Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye.
It added that the participants reviewed the security situation and threats facing Saudi Arabia and “strongly resented” the attacks targeting the holy city of Makkah as well as civilian and economic infrastructure.
Türkiye's Chief of General Staff, General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu, attends meeting within scope of Mecca Joint Defence Agreement alongside Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan, General Asim Munir, and Chief of General Staff of Saudi Arabia, General Fayyadh bin Hamed Al-Ruwaili, in Riyadh pic.twitter.com/LlQHjpGcIN
They also appreciated the “vigilance and professionalism” of the Saudi Armed Forces in ensuring the safety of the people and security of the Kingdom.
The participants also discussed ways to further advance cooperation among the armed forces of the three countries and enhance intelligence sharing, military coordination and capability integration to strengthen deterrence and collective defence.
Commending the longstanding relations and mutual trust between the people and armed forces of the three countries, the statement noted that the Riyadh meeting reflected the strength of defence partnership between the three countries and their shared determination to immediately translate the commitments of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement into effective military cooperation.
Reaffirming their commitment to collective defence, the participants demonstrated the resolve of the three countries to defend the security, sovereignty and territorial integrity of Saudi Arabia.
Earlier in the day, the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye strongly condemned attacks targeting the holy city of Makkah and civilian and economic facilities in Saudi Arabia, according to a joint statement released on Friday.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan met on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York on Thursday under the framework of the MJDA between the three countries, which was formed last month.
During the meeting, the foreign ministers reviewed progress toward establishing the agreement's general secretariat, committees, and working groups, as well as preparations for them to begin their work, according to a Turkish foreign ministry statement.
🔊PR No.2️⃣6️⃣2️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Foreign Ministers of the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement Meet on the Margins of the United Nations General Assembly in New York 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/04Oi2Z3gGn
They condemned the attacks in the strongest terms and commended the vigilance of the Saudi Armed Forces and their ability to defend the kingdom's security. They also reaffirmed Saudi Arabia's right to take measures it deems appropriate to defend its security in line with Article 51 of the UN Charter.
The foreign ministers discussed plans to convene an urgent meeting of the three countries' military chiefs to explore ways to assist Saudi Arabia under the agreement, which stipulates that an attack against any one of its parties shall be considered an attack against all.
They also discussed the current situation in the region, emphasising the importance of upholding international law, good neighbourliness, mutual respect for state sovereignty, and non-interference in internal affairs, as well as ensuring the security and freedom of navigation.
The foreign ministers reiterated their determination to work together to achieve sustainable peace and stability in the region, support de-escalation efforts, and encourage the peaceful resolution of crises.
Met with my brothers, Foreign Minister of Saudi Arabia Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud @FaisalbinFarhan and Foreign Minister of Türkiye Hakan Fidan @HakanFidan , along with our respective delegations, on the sidelines of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly in… pic.twitter.com/OOwWdMVZtl
Earlier in a statement, Dar said he reviewed progress on establishing institutional structures under the MJDA with his Saudi and Turkish counterparts on the sidelines of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. According to a post on X, FM Dar met Saudi and Turkish foreign ministers along with their respective delegations.
“Under the framework of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, we reviewed progress towards establishing the institutional structures under the Agreement,” Dar said. The three foreign ministers also “exchanged views on regional and international security issues”, the minister added.
On Wednesday, the appointment of Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood marked the first formal step towards operationalising the MJDA, with Pakistan providing the alliance’s inaugural secretary general.
The post will head the general secretariat being established in Riyadh and oversee the implementation of the agreement, coordination of joint activities, and expanded defence cooperation among the participating countries.
An “urgent” meeting of the chiefs of staff of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye was also being arranged to discuss ways of supporting the kingdom under the MJDA, Saudi Arabia’s foreign ministry said on Friday.
The ministry said the development was discussed during the meeting between the three foreign ministers. The ministers also reviewed progress on establishing the secretariat, committees and working groups under the agreement and preparations for them to begin their work.
#نيويورك | سمو وزير الخارجية الأمير #فيصل_بن_فرحان @FaisalbinFarhan يعقد اجتماعاً مع معالي نائب رئيس الوزراء وزير خارجية جمهورية باكستان الإسلامية السيد محمد إسحاق دار، ومعالي وزير خارجية الجمهورية التركية السيد هاكان فيدان، وذلك في إطار اتفاقية مكة للدفاع المشترك.… pic.twitter.com/FqSWVfY17z
The meeting came as the ministers “strongly condemned” attacks targeting Makkah and civilian and economic facilities in Saudi Arabia, while affirming the kingdom’s right to take measures it deemed appropriate to defend its security under Article 51 of the UN Charter.
The ministers also discussed the regional situation, stressing the importance of international law, good neighbourliness, mutual respect for states’ sovereignty and non-interference in their internal affairs, as well as the security and freedom of maritime navigation.
They renewed their commitment to working towards “sustainable peace and stability” in the region and supporting efforts to reduce tensions and find peaceful solutions to ongoing crises, the ministry said.
Significance of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
The MJDA was the latest step in longstanding military and strategic cooperation between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. Signed in Makkah, the pact established a framework for collective deterrence and stipulated that an armed attack on any one of the three countries would be considered an attack on all three, while providing for wider cooperation across defence.
The agreement followed nearly a year of negotiations and came amid heightened instability across the Middle East. Turkiye and Pakistan had sought closer regional security cooperation, while Saudi Arabia had faced growing security concerns as conflicts spread across the region, threatening its territory, energy infrastructure and ambitious economic development plans.
For Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the trilateral pact is built on their Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed in September 2025. That agreement stated that “any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both” and committed the two sides to strengthening defence cooperation and joint deterrence.
Read More: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye sign joint defence pact in Makkah
The three countries already had extensive military links. Pakistan had provided training and technical assistance to Saudi forces for decades, while Islamabad and Ankara had maintained close defence ties through military training, naval cooperation and defence equipment. In 2023, Saudi Arabia agreed to purchase Turkish drones in what Ankara described as its largest defence export contract.
Pakistan had also expanded its military and security cooperation with the kingdom, deploying about 8,000 troops, fighter jets, drones and an air-defence system to Saudi Arabia, according to Reuters . Pakistan deploys troops to Saudi air base under defence pact . Islamabad had also been pursuing wider security and economic ties in the Gulf, including negotiations with Kuwait on an expanded cooperation pact linked to energy and investment. Pakistan-Kuwait agree to boost cooperation across key sectors
The signing in Makkah, Islam’s holiest city, added symbolic weight to an agreement that brought together three countries with significant military and strategic capabilities. It also came as Pakistan sought to avoid becoming directly involved in the Iran conflict, instead pursuing diplomatic efforts to mediate, while strengthening its broader regional security partnerships.

title: Heather Matarazzo reveals she could lose health insurance without more work
description: I am literally in the same boat right now     Matarazzo wrote on Threads   lots of my fellow actors are
content:
“I am literally in the same boat right now,” Matarazzo wrote on Threads, "lots of my fellow actors are"
The Princess Diaries star Heather Matarazzo has revealed that she could lose her health insurance if she does not secure more acting work soon, saying she is in the same position as many other actors.
Matarazzo, who played Lilly Moscovitz in The Princess Diaries, made the disclosure while responding to actor Jack Haven, who recently appealed publicly for work after falling short of the earnings requirement for SAG-AFTRA health insurance.
“I am literally in the same boat right now,” Matarazzo wrote on Threads. “Lots of my fellow actors are.” She also recalled a time when actors did not have to earn a minimum amount to qualify for insurance and expressed relief that Haven had received an offer that would allow them to qualify for coverage in 2027.
Under the SAG-AFTRA health plan, members must meet an annual minimum earnings requirement or an alternative workday requirement to qualify for coverage. The minimum earnings threshold for 2026 is $28,090, while the figure is set to rise to $28,933 for 2027.
Haven, known for Atypical and I Saw the TV Glow, had shared a video asking for work after discovering they were $4,000 short of the amount needed to qualify for health insurance. They later said they had received numerous offers following the appeal.
Matarazzo's comments highlight the difficulties some actors face in maintaining union health coverage as television production has shifted towards shorter seasons and fewer episodes. Despite having an extensive acting career, including roles in Welcome to the Dollhouse, Scream 3 and Netflix's Wednesday, actors still need to meet the current eligibility requirements to maintain coverage.

Jodie Turner-Smith faces a lawsuit over allegations involving her brother Richard Smith, which she has denied
Queen & Slim star Jodie Turner-Smith and her brother, Richard Smith, are facing a lawsuit filed by three anonymous women who allege they were subjected to drug use and nonconsensual sexual activity at parties involving Richard.
The lawsuit, filed Thursday, September 24, names Richard Smith as a defendant over allegations including sexual battery, false imprisonment, emotional distress and fraud. Jodie Turner-Smith is separately accused of property-related negligence, negligence per se, child endangerment and aiding and abetting.
According to the lawsuit, the three Jane Does claim Richard invited them to gatherings where they allegedly encountered narcotics, firearms and people engaging in sexual activity.
Jane Does 1 and 3 allege Richard pressured them to use drugs and participate in sexual activities. Jane Doe 3 further claims she was allowed to stay at Richard's Los Angeles home in exchange for sex.
Jane Doe 1 alleges she later discovered the property was owned by Jodie Turner-Smith. Jane Doe 2 makes similar allegations and claims Richard told her that Jodie knew about his alleged drug activities, used cocaine with him and helped pay for additional narcotics.
Jane Doe 2 also alleges Richard said Jodie gave him an Audi that he allegedly used to transport packages containing narcotics across state lines.
Jodie Turner-Smith has denied the allegations through her representative, who told TMZ that the lawsuit is "fictional" and claimed it was filed by someone who had previously harassed the actress.
The representative also disputed the claims made against Turner-Smith, calling the lawsuit an alleged abuse of the legal system and saying the accusations are not true.
The lawsuit identifies three anonymous accusers, while Turner-Smith's camp claims one person is presenting themselves as three separate Jane Does. The allegations have not been proven in court.

title: Govt increases petrol by Rs2 02  cuts diesel by Rs3 59 till Sept 28
description: Petrol price increases to Rs391 30 per litre  while HSD will cost Rs408 53
content:
Petrol price increases to Rs391.30 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs408.53
The federal government on Friday increased the price of petrol by Rs2.02 per litre, while decreasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.59 per litre till September 28.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs391.30 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs408.53 per litre from September 26 to September 28.
The latest revision comes a day after the government decreased the price of petrol and HSD by 84 paisas and Rs2.63 per litre, respectively, for September 25.
Read : Govt decreases petrol by 84 paisas, HSD by Rs2.63 for Sept 25
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
Earlier this month, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices fell about 3% on Friday, on mounting hopes for a truce between the US and Iran , even as traders worried that increasing attacks against Saudi Arabia by Houthi fighters could disrupt supply from the Middle Eastern producer.
Brent futures fell $2.96, or 2.8%, at $103.64 a barrel by 12:12 pm EDT (1612 GMT). West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude fell $2.86, or 3.0%, ​to $91.75.
US and Iranian negotiators in New York are exploring a ​phased path out of war that would involve Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifting its economic ⁠blockade of Iran, sources close to the talks said.
In the Middle East, however, Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani military chiefs are to discuss help for Saudi ​Arabia as it faces attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis.
"Diplomatic hopes are essentially helping oil prices weather the latest military strikes in the Middle East , with ​crude trading moderately softer despite the attacks," said Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade.

title: AI messaging scam costs Italy s top bank Intesa millions  sources say
description: Fraudsters used AI to clone a senior lawyer s voice and confirm a fake payment instruction
content:
Fraudsters used AI to clone a senior lawyer's voice and confirm a fake payment instruction
Fraudsters using AI to impersonate senior executives stole €95 million ($108 million) from Fideuram, the private banking arm of Italy's biggest lender ​Intesa Sanpaolo, two sources familiar with the matter said on Friday.
More ‌than half the funds were later recovered, but some €36 million remains missing, the sources said.
The scheme, first reported by Corriere della Sera, began in February when then-Fideuram Chairman ​Paolo Molesini received what appeared to be a WhatsApp message from ​Intesa Sanpaolo CEO Carlo Messina seeking urgent help with an overseas ⁠transaction.
The fraudsters followed up with a phone call that appeared to come ​from a senior partner at a prominent law firm, confirming the instruction. According ​to the sources, the callers used AI technology to replicate the lawyer's voice.
Believing the request was genuine, Molesini instructed his finance department to arrange a series of transfers to ​foreign accounts, mainly in China and Hong Kong, the sources said.
Read More: Financing of historic AI buildout raises systemic risks in US, researcher says
Intesa Sanpaolo ​and Fideuram declined to comment.
Fideuram quickly detected irregularities in the transfers and alerted banks and ‌authorities ⁠in several countries. Roughly €53 million was later recovered through cooperation between authorities in China, Portugal and Italy, according to the sources.
The remaining funds have not been traced after passing through a network of overseas accounts and being ​converted into cryptocurrencies, they ​said.
Neither Molesini nor ⁠any other Fideuram executives are under investigation, the sources said. However, Milan prosecutors have placed a foreign national living ​outside Europe under investigation on suspicion of computer fraud, ​one of ⁠the sources said.
Molesini resigned as chairman in March citing personal reasons. At the time, Fideuram gave no further explanation for his departure.
Last year, fraudsters using AI to ⁠mimic ​the voice of an Italian minister persuaded businessman ​Massimo Moratti to transfer nearly €1 million to an overseas account. The money was later recovered.

Before Off Campus , Bright portrayed a young Kate Middleton in Netflix’s The Crown and appeared in the historical drama series Malory Towers . She is also set to star alongside Finn Cole and Ben Foster in Gable , an upcoming drama based on a true story involving wrestling.
Narcs adds another major project to Bright’s growing film and television slate, while Thames continues to build his profile following his role in The Black Phone .

Microsoft on Friday unveiled several new capabilities in its Copilot app, including a coding tool and ​an always-on AI agent, as the software giant seeks to transform ‌its AI assistant into a one-stop shop for office workers.
The company is also embedding its Office applications Word, Excel, and PowerPoint directly within Copilot, allowing users to work collaboratively ​on these apps without having to leave the AI tool.

Microsoft ⁠is racing to expand Copilot beyond its chat-based roots to boost adoption ​as it competes with AI chatbots such as ChatGPT and Claude.
The Windows maker ​unveiled "Code" to let users build apps, dashboards and other software using natural language prompts. The tool, powered by the same technology as Microsoft's GitHub Copilot, will roll out to early-access ​customers at the end of the month, while 365 Premium and Pro ​subscribers can preview it later this year.

Microsoft is also rolling out "Autopilot", a revamp of the "Scout" ‌AI ⁠agent it unveiled in June, in a private preview at the end of the month. The so-called digital coworker agent will carry its own identity in the company directory and have specific permissions that users can control.
"I think it's ​been very hard ​for many organizations ⁠to bring agents into the enterprise because of security, compliance and governance concerns," Annie Pearl, corporate vice president of ​Copilot Product, said in an interview.
"So we've worked... to make ​sure ⁠that we were building this in a way that would really be able to be used in the enterprise."
Microsoft also unveiled cost-management capabilities to allow employees to ⁠have ​direct insight into costs tied to their AI ​usage. The move comes at a time when enterprises are increasingly worried about rapid AI usage ​racking up unexpected costs.

title: First US trial against TikTok to test claims platform fueled teen mental health crisis
description: TikTok says teen safety is a priority and Section 230 shields platforms from liability over user content
content:
TikTok says teen safety is a priority and Section 230 shields platforms from liability over user content
An Alabama jury will hear the state's claims that TikTok and ​its Chinese parent company ByteDance made the platform addictive to young users and misled consumers about its safety, in the ‌first case against the company to reach trial in the sweeping litigation over social media's impact on teen wellbeing.
The trial, which is scheduled to kick off Monday in Montgomery state court and expected to last two to three weeks, could provide a rare look inside TikTok, which has settled prior cases selected for trial and ​sought to keep details of its operations from public view.
Alabama’s lawsuit was filed last year by state Attorney General Steve Marshall, a ​Republican. At least 27 other states and Washington, D.C., have also sued.
TikTok has said it designed its platform ⁠with teen safety as a key priority and argued that Section 230 of the federal Communications Decency Act shields online platforms from liability ​over user-generated content.
Representatives for the Alabama attorney general's office and TikTok, whose US operations were transferred this year to an entity led by US ​investors and 20% owned by ByteDance, did not respond to requests for comment about the trial.
Alabama claims TikTok's endless stream of videos makes it the most addictive social media platform and that its algorithm pushes young users toward increasingly intense content about violence and self-harm, contributing to a teen mental health crisis and causing the ​number of emergency room visits for self-harm in the state to "skyrocket."
Read More: Meta's Charm gadget carries CEO Zuckerberg's big AI ambitions
The lawsuit accuses TikTok of falsely claiming it limits access to sexual and violent ​content for young users in order to have its app rated safe for teens in app stores run by Google, Apple and Microsoft and of misleading ‌users about ⁠the Chinese government's access to US users' data.
The state seeks penalties and other relief.
TikTok’s decision to settle key cases and efforts to seal or heavily redact court records have kept much of the evidence about the privately held company's operations out of public view.
In addition to the states' cases, TikTok faces thousands of lawsuits by individuals, school districts and municipalities over its alleged impact on young users' mental health. Meta ​Platforms, Snap Inc and Alphabet's YouTube are ​also defendants in many of these ⁠cases.
TikTok had settled all cases selected for trial against it, including claims by five young people and a Kentucky school district .
Alabama’s lawsuit claims TikTok asks users to self-report their ages, but it also allows users to evade its ​questions about their age by viewing videos without creating an account, which still allows the company to ​collect data on ⁠their viewing habits. The lack of an effective age restriction makes things like “Kids Mode,” which curates content for young users, entirely useless, according to the lawsuit.
