title: Kundi urges KP govt to abandon long march  says ground reality    not in favour
description: Downplays chances of governor rule  refuses to assent to police act in its current form
content:
Downplays chances of governor rule; refuses to assent to police act in its current form
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Friday urged the provincial government to abandon its planned long march towards Islamabad, claiming that the “ground reality is not in favour” of the protest and alleging that some people were either in hiding or had opted for voluntary arrests to avoid participating in it.
The PTI had announced last month that it would march to Islamabad on September 27 to press for the release of party founder Imran Khan. Today it said the party has postponed the march to take place on October 4 instead. The party had been preparing a central convoy from K-P, with caravans from other parts of the country expected to join before proceeding towards the federal capital. The federal government warned the party against going ahead with the march.
“I would recommend the provincial government to abandon the long march,” Kundi said while addressing a press conference in Peshawar.
“The ground reality is not in favour at all. Some people are in hideouts, while others have offered voluntary arrests to skip joining the long march,” he alleged.
He also said that the chief minister had failed to gather support during his recent visit to Punjab and that should have made him course-correct.
The governor accused the PTI-led provincial government of diverting its attention and resources towards the planned march instead of addressing the issues confronting K-P.
Read: PTI postpones Islamabad march to October 4: party sources
He said the provincial government should focus on the deteriorating law and order situation, particularly in southern K-P, the merged districts and Malakand division, along with problems related to healthcare, education, electricity, potable water, tourism and the mining sector.
“All resources have been channelled towards the long march,” Kundi lamented.
He also questioned the purpose of the proposed protest, saying that PTI had repeatedly changed its demands. According to Kundi, the party initially sought relief for its incarcerated founder, claiming that he had been wrongfully punished, but later changed its demands to judicial issues and, subsequently, quicker hearings and access to healthcare for him in custody.
He warned the provincial government against using state resources and officials for what he described as a political agenda.
“You cannot use state machinery for forwarding personal agendas,” he said. He asserted that the provincial government planned to keep the police at its disposal during the long march towards Islamabad.
The governor said he supported the constitutional right of citizens to hold peaceful protests but stressed that it was necessary to determine whether a particular demonstration remained peaceful.
“I second the right of the people to protest under the democratic right ordained to them under the Constitution, but it is important to see if the protest is actually peaceful or not,” he said.
Kundi highlighted that PTI leaders had previously caused disruptions in Islamabad, damaged government property and harmed military installations during protests.
He also referred to remarks by a PTI president and an MNA about politics involving casualties, saying such statements did not correspond with peaceful political activity. He criticised a recent speech by the K-P chief minister in the provincial assembly, saying the provincial government should concentrate on governance rather than political confrontation.
Citing previous long marches organised by the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), Kundi said his party did not use government officials or departments for political demonstrations.
“We neither took government officials, cops, fire department staff or any other state official to back our protest.”
The governor also praised the Jamaat-e-Islami for what he described as peaceful protests, saying the party had not damaged state or government property.
Speaking on the imposition of governor rule in K-P, Kundi said the president and the federal government ought to decide on it. He said the constitution provides for its imposition under special circumstances that need to be assessed by the relevant authorities.
“It was imposed in the past as well. It is not unconstitutional,” he said about the governor rule, but refrained from announcing its imposition in the province.
A major part of Kundi’s criticism centred on the proposed K-P police law.
The governor said the provincial government was seeking to increase its control over the police department, despite what he described as a February ruling of the Peshawar High Court (PHC) concerning the command structure of the force. He said the court had made it clear that the police department was headed by the inspector general of police and that transfers and promotions should be based on merit rather than political considerations.
“PTI always sloganeered against politicisation of police, but now they themselves wish to convert the police force into PTI’s Tiger Force,” the governor remarked during the press conference.
Read more: Police hunt PTI leaders, activists
Expressing concern over provisions in the proposed police legislation, Kundi said it would give the provincial government unfair control over police affairs. According to him, the draft reserves 25% of the quota for direct DSP appointments for the chief minister.
He also questioned the proposed police policy board, saying that if all matters relating to the police were brought under the control of the K-P government, there would be little purpose in maintaining an independent police department.
Kundi also assailed the proposal to place the finances of the police department under the provincial finance ministry.
“The ministry of finance always says that the treasury is empty,” he said, arguing that a force fighting terrorism and crime should not be subjected to excessive political and administrative interference.
“The force which is fighting [terrorism and crime] and laying down lives is being tossed around in the province — under the cabinet, home secretary and chief minister,” he lambasted the provincial government's approach.
Kundi further highlighted that the proposed police law would bear negative consequences on judicial processes, outlining, “They have even directed the reports submitted to courts by police to go through them [provincial government].”
“The proposed system would allow the government to manipulate police reports for political purposes,” he expressed concern.
“Everyone knows PTI is behind the May 9 attacks and yet the new law will allow them to manipulate reports to suit their politics,” Kundi claimed.
He further alleged that under the proposed law, police officers could be rewarded or punished on the basis of their willingness to comply with political demands.
“They will award promotions to those cops who give in to their demands and punish those who don’t.”
Governor Kundi also declared the proposed police legislation “illegal and unconstitutional”, while clarifying that he would examine the legislation formally once it had been passed by the provincial assembly.
“I will scrutinise the act when I receive it after it gets passed by the assembly,” he said, adding, “The current provisions of the act that I have come across are absolutely unacceptable.”
The governor remarked that he would not assent to the new police legislation unless relevant amendments were incorporated.
He also predicted that the legislation could face a legal challenge, saying he expected the court to strike it down if the federal government approached the judiciary for relief.
The governor urged the K-P lawmakers to “not pass the act through the assembly”, stressing previous court decrees against the use of state assets for personal or political agendas.
Kundi said the debate over police administration could not be separated from the security situation in K-P and recalled the sacrifices made by police personnel in the province.
The governor also referred to a recent Counter-Terrorism Department operation in which a suicide bomber allegedly planning an attack in Peshawar was eliminated. He said the sacrifices of security personnel should be recognised and their families provided with the facilities and benefits they deserved.
“Previously, our military officers and sepoys were killed in Kohat, following a recurring pattern,” he said.
Kundi urged the provincial government to look at the security situation in southern K-P, the merged districts and Malakand division, where, he said, law and order remained a major concern.
He also criticised the provincial government for, in his view, devoting political energy to the long march while neglecting the demands of families of police personnel killed in the line of duty.
Instead of providing facilities to the families of those who had sacrificed their lives for the country and helping them secure their right to receive presidential awards, he said, the government had focused its attention elsewhere.
Governor Kundi further stressed that the provincial government should concentrate on problems affecting ordinary citizens rather than the planned political campaign.
He took a jab at the government for overlooking protests by members of the medical community seeking an increase in remuneration. He also raised concerns over the reported increase in dengue and polio cases, the condition of the education sector, electricity-related problems and the availability of potable water.
The governor also pointed to what he described as the decline of the tourism sector and the underdevelopment of mining in the province.
He alleged that financial allocations meant for the former FATA and PATA regions had not been properly utilised for the benefit of local communities. Kundi said police personnel in these areas were protesting.
“If they are protesting, who will look after law and order?” he asked.
Kundi also took apart the provincial government for failing to secure what he described as the province’s due share of oil and gas royalties from the federal government.
“K-P produces the most oil and gas for the country, but we have failed to acquire royalty for it,” he stated during the press conference.
“We have failed to seek relevant resources from the centre to uplift our people,” he added.
Despite his criticism of the proposed legislation, Kundi said the provincial police had received equipment and vehicles required to improve its operational capabilities. He said several items requested for the K-P police had already been provided to the province, while additional equipment would be delivered according to the government’s commitments.
“We will receive 23 anti-drone guns in October, and the rest will be given in December,” he said.
Kundi maintained that strengthening the police and addressing the province’s security challenges should be prioritised over political mobilisation.
He urged the PTI-led administration to focus instead on overcoming what he described as provincial governance lapses.

Shrinking is produced by Warner Bros. Television, with Lawrence, Segel and Goldstein among its executive producers. The series follows therapist Jimmy Laird as he deals with grief while attempting to help his patients.

title: Security forces eliminate 16 Indian sponsored terrorists in Balochistan IBOs  ISPR
description: Says 33  Indian sponsored  terrorists have been killed in Balochistan since Sept 21
content:
Says 33 'Indian-sponsored' terrorists have been killed in Balochistan since Sept 21
Security forces have killed 16 “Indian-sponsored” terrorists in two separate intelligence-based operations in Balochistan on September 24 and 25, the military’s media wing said on Friday.
In a statement, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said five terrorists were killed on Thursday during an operation conducted as part of the ongoing Operation Shaban when security forces busted their hideouts..
Read More : Security forces kill one terrorist in Balochistan's Kech
“After an intense fire exchange, five Indian-sponsored Khwarij were killed,” the statement said, adding that the latest casualties had taken the total number of militants killed in the operation to 22.
“Weapons, ammunition and explosives were also recovered from the Khwarij locations,” it said while adding that a clearance operation would continue “till complete neutralisation of threat from the area”.
Meanwhile, security forces engaged a militant hideout in another intelligence-based operation in Nushki district today, the statement said.
“During the conduct of the operation, own troops effectively engaged terrorists’ hideout and after an intense fire exchange, 11 terrorists were sent to hell,” it added.
According to the ISPR, at least 33 “Indian-sponsored Khwarij/terrorists” have been killed since Sept 21.
Sequel to comprehensive counter terrorism operation by security forces against Indian backed Fitna Al Khawarij & Fitna Al Hindustan in Balochistan. Thirty three Indian sponsored Khwarij/ terrorists, has been sent to hell, since 21 September 2026. On 24 September, in continuation… pic.twitter.com/tq12uHCtod
It said the “relentless counter-terrorism campaign” under the vision of “Azm-i-Istehkam”, as approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, would continue at full pace.
Also Read : Captain, lieutenant among six martyred as eight terrorists killed in Hangu fire exchange: ISPR
The campaign, it added, would continue to “wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism” from the country.
Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022, and over the same period, TTP attacks increased more than sevenfold to 838 from 118.
Although Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa has borne the brunt of terrorism, Balochistan has also remained a major target of Indian proxies, which often target civilians and military installations in the province.
In one such attack on the last day of 2025, terrorists targeted innocent civilians in Balochistan’s Gwadar and Kharan districts, where 18 people, including women, children, the elderly and labourers, embraced martyrdom.
The forces continued operations across the provinces against what the state describes as Indian-sponsored terrorists and their proxies. Still, despite these efforts, the groups have continued to target civilian and defence installations.
Last month, in another such attack, at least 30 people, including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. The attackers also abducted several civilians and police personnel after the assault.
In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation , which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

title: Trump  Xi wrap up summit with tea and tour of US archives
description: Three day state visit concludes as Xi departs  details of agreements to be released on Monday
content:
Three-day state visit concludes as Xi departs, details of agreements to be released on Monday
President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping drank tea at the White House on Friday and visited the National Archives, capping a three-day summit that showcased personal diplomacy ​rather than big breakthroughs in economic relations.
The two leaders praised each other in remarks while they had tea in the White House Red Room. Trump said the summit between ‌the world's two largest economies had produced great strides and that "I think our farmers are going to be happy" but did not provide details.
. @POTUS : "I think our farmers are going to be very happy — a lot of very positive things happened... Great things for both countries. It's just been very, very productive." https://t.co/nUByGPElXk pic.twitter.com/69wDC0xWCj
"America is very happy about this visit, and I'm sure China is very happy also," he said.
Trump: America is very happy about this visit, and I'm sure China is very happy also. Great things for both countries. It's been just very, very productive. pic.twitter.com/PNtyt7afvd
Xi said the US-China relationship had developed into a constructive one of "strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity".
Xi Jinping: Trump and I are like two people that's charting the course for the great ship of China-U.S. relations. When Trump visited China in May, we agreed on the vision of building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability. This time, we've agreed to… pic.twitter.com/zLPxjNSlRK
Xi also said he and Trump would have two more opportunities to meet this year, the APEC summit in China and a G20 summit in ​Miami.
"I do welcome you, Mr President and the First Lady to visit China," he said.
The lavish state summit, with flyovers, tours and a glittering state dinner, has been heavy on symbolism but light ​on substance.
Read : Xi calls for new chapter in China-US ties at White House dinner
Still, Trump highlighted progress under a bilateral trade mechanism, citing what he described as increased market access for US farmers and ranchers, while both leaders identified ⁠artificial intelligence as an area for cooperation.
Details of the limited agreements the two sides struck regarding their tense trade relationship would be released on Monday, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC on Friday.
Trump: President Xi and Madam Peng have just left D.C., heading for China. The meeting was one of Friendship, Strength, and Success, for both China and the U.S.A. We will be meeting again in November, in China, and then at the G20 in December, in Miami, Florida. Much has been,… pic.twitter.com/iAgliJXyil
"We're in ​a managed trade situation. ... We've had progress, and we will release on Monday, I think, a lot more details about what we've accomplished over the past few weeks in negotiating with the Chinese," he said.
The US ​has agreed with China on exempting some key goods from arguments over trade, Greer said, including exports to China of agricultural products and medical devices and imports of consumer and non-sensitive goods.
The summit concluded at the National Archives, where Trump and Xi appeared to review the US Declaration of Independence and the Constitution and the Bill of Rights.
President Trump, First Lady Melania Trump, Chinese President Xi and First Lady Peng Liyuan at the National Archives. pic.twitter.com/IxyFJOT95R
They would also see "artefacts testifying to the long and cherished relationship" between China and the US and their "cultural exchanges", Trump said in remarks ​welcoming Xi on Thursday.
Read More : Trump to wrap up Xi summit with a tour of US archives
"Just as our ancestors reached across the ocean centuries ago to trade, to learn, and to build a better world, our two countries do really the same thing, and we're very proud ​of it and the relationship," Trump said.
China has not commented on the visit to the archives, but analysts say Xi may be keen to see records relating to the US switch of recognition to communist China from Taiwan in 1979.
Responding ‌to a question, ⁠Trump said he and Xi had discussed Iran and said "I think we're going to do great" without elaborating. Beijing has denied US allegations of helping Iran's leaders in the conflict launched by Trump in February.
Q: Did you discuss the war with Iran with Xi? Trump: We did. I think we're gonna do great. pic.twitter.com/Jawn3DgAUL
China claims democratically governed Taiwan as its own, and Xi has long sought to persuade Trump to state publicly that the US opposes Taiwan's independence, rather than saying only that it does not support independence, which has been Washington's formulation for decades.
He is also keen to get the US to halt arms sales to the island.
As expected, Xi pressed Trump on Taiwan on Thursday, saying he hoped the US would "handle the Taiwan question ​with prudence". China's state news agency also reported that ​Xi "hopes the US side will adhere to the ⁠correct position of opposing 'Taiwan independence'".
While the US, like most countries, has no formal diplomatic relations with Taipei, Washington is its most important international backer and is bound by US law to provide it with the means to defend itself.
Washington's Asian allies will watch closely to see how Trump talks about Taiwan following Xi's ​visit.
After his May summit with Xi, Trump, whose administration in December approved an $11 billion arms sale package to Taiwan, said he was holding a second ​package, worth some $14 billion, in ⁠abeyance and described it as a "very good negotiating chip".
Craig Singleton of the Foundation for Defence of Democracies think tank said Beijing may believe it has established a new baseline on Taiwan with Trump.
He said Xi's use of the word "adhere" was revealing because "it implies Beijing believes Washington is already behaving in ways it wants".
"In the context of the current standdown on Taiwan arms sales, China may increasingly view that restraint as a new baseline rather than a ⁠temporary pause," he ​said.
"Beijing's objective is to get Trump to absorb Chinese red lines into his own definition of a stable relationship."
On Thursday, Senate ​Democrats criticised the summit, saying Trump had failed to secure meaningful concessions from Beijing on trade, security, artificial intelligence or human rights.
They also criticised Trump for failing to publicly address China's military pressure on Taiwan and called for the immediate delivery of approved military ​aid and arms sales to the island.

title: UAE bars Iranian airline flights as US sanctions bite
description: The UAE faced thousands of Iranian missiles and drones before suspending trade and financial ties with Iran
content:
The UAE faced thousands of Iranian missiles and drones before suspending trade and financial ties with Iran
The United Arab Emirates said on Thursday it would no longer accept flights by Iranian airlines as it joins US sanctions aimed at raising economic pressure during the Middle East war.
Dubai, the UAE's commercial hub, is a major destination for Iran's carriers, with multiple daily flights, a large Iranian community and close business links.
Several other countries have suspended Iranian flights, although routes to Turkey and China were among those that remained open.
"The General Civil Aviation Authority announced the suspension of all flights operated by Iranian airlines to and from the UAE," said a statement carried by the official WAM news agency.
The suspension, from Thursday, was "based on the US sanctions imposed on Iranian airlines preventing them from using airports around the world", the statement said.
The UAE was targeted by thousands of Iranian missiles and drones in the war's early stages. Last month, the oil-rich monarchy suspended trade and financial exchanges with Iran.
On Wednesday, the UAE central bank blocked transactions to and from Iran by branches of Iran's Bank Melli, accusing it of violating laws on money laundering, terrorism and arms proliferation.
Read More: Inside the UN walkout: Who left and who stayed for Netanyahu’s speech
Iranian media had reported the UAE's suspension earlier on Thursday.
An Iran Airtour flight from Tehran to Dubai was cancelled shortly before its scheduled departure in the morning, after tickets had been issued, one passenger told AFP.
Dubai airport, which offers connections to Europe, Asia and Africa, often serves as a transit point for Iranian travellers and is a common destination for business trips.
In early September, the US imposed sanctions on Iran's aviation sector and vowed to come down hard on companies that work with it.
Those companies had until Wednesday to comply — by stopping refuelling Iranian planes, for example — or face the possibility of being cut off from the dollar-based financial system.
Starting on Wednesday, the main Iranian airlines were forced to cancel their international flights as neighbouring countries adopted restrictive measures.
Turkmenistan also joined the list on Thursday, turning back a flight from Tehran to Dushanbe.
"Turkmenistan's refusal to allow the Iranian aircraft to pass through its airspace meant the flight could not continue on its route and had to return," Iran's Civil Aviation Organisation spokesman Majid Akhavan told state news agency IRNA.
Regarding the UAE, he said "diplomatic and aviation talks are underway to remove the restrictions and restore flights" to the country.
Despite the sanctions, several small Iranian carriers continue to fly abroad, notably to China, which refuses to bow to US pressure, as well as to Armenia.
Iran has nearly 30 airlines, most operating domestic regional routes.
Iran Air, the national carrier, and Mahan, a private company, are the largest for international travel.

title: 5 missing after explosion collapses building in historic heart of Athens
description: An elderly couple lived on the second floor  while three tourists  possibly Americans  stayed downstairs
content:
An elderly couple lived on the second floor, while three tourists, possibly Americans, stayed downstairs
Five people are missing after an explosion caused a building to collapse in Athens’ historic Plaka district on Friday morning, Greece’s Fire Department said, according to the Greek state news agency AMNA, as search operations continued at the scene.
The explosion and subsequent fire broke out on Lysikratous Street shortly after 7.30 am local time (0430GMT).
A large number of firefighters, including personnel from the Special Disaster Response Unit, were searching the rubble using specialized equipment, thermal imaging cameras and a trained search dog.
The five missing people are believed to have been staying on the first and second floors of the building, according to the Fire Department.
Members of emergency personnel work at the site where an old building collapsed following an explosion, in the Plaka area, which is popular with tourists, in central Athens, Greece, September 25, 2026. REUTERS
Read More: Fatal crash takes suspicious turn
An elderly couple was believed to have been living on the second floor, while three tourists, possibly Americans, were staying in short-term rental accommodation on the first floor, according to the latest information from the department.
It was not immediately known whether they were inside the building when the explosion occurred. “There are missing persons. This is a very complex situation, and the search is in full progress,” Athens Mayor Haris Doukas said after arriving at the scene.
Drones were also being used to assess the situation, while municipal services remained at the scene to assess damage to neighboring buildings, Doukas said.
Asked about the cause of the explosion, Doukas explained: “I understand that it was caused by gas, and the force of the explosion was terrifying. This means that there was a very serious fault. Something went completely wrong,” he said.
Police officers and ambulances from Greece’s National Centre for Emergency Care were also at the scene.
Construction machinery provided by the Municipality of Athens was being used to remove debris from the collapsed building.

Macklemore was removed from the Gillette Stadium dates after controversy surrounding comments he made during an earlier performance. Sheeran’s backing band and other tour openers subsequently withdrew from the tour in solidarity with Macklemore, leaving Sheeran to perform solo at a recent Philadelphia concert.
A protest had also been planned outside the Gillette Stadium concert on Saturday by Massachusetts Peace Action in connection with the controversy surrounding Macklemore. However, the concerts have now been canceled because of the severe weather rather than the planned demonstration.

title: HSY opens up about his difficult childhood and learning to fend for himself
description: Designer talks about his battle with blindness  his mother   s sacrifices and the experiences that shaped his career
content:
Designer talks about his battle with blindness, his mother’s sacrifices and the experiences that shaped his career
Fashion designer and television personality Hassan Sheheryar Yasin, popularly known as HSY, revealed that he completely lost his eyesight in both eyes for nearly a year, an experience that left him in deep depression and changed the way he experienced life.
In a recent interview with Frieha Altaf, HSY spoke candidly about losing his vision, the difficult circumstances of his childhood, being raised by his mother after his parents’ divorce, his complicated relationship with his father and the struggles he faced before establishing himself in Pakistan’s fashion industry.
He also reflected on his mother’s sacrifices, his early years of working different jobs and his plans to launch a separate ready-to-wear brand.
HSY recalled that the incident that led to the loss of his eyesight happened while he was returning from getting food with his best friend.
“One day we were sitting and we were all fasting, and we thought, ‘Let’s get food.’ We went to get food and were coming back. My best friend was driving the car, and we were listening to the azaan. When I took my bag, the steam came out and blocked everything. When he cleaned the screen, he swerved off the road. I lost my eyesight in both my eyes,” he said.
The sudden loss of his eyesight had a profound effect on him. With his vision gone, he found himself relying heavily on his other senses. “When your eyes go, your other senses grow. I used to hear my mom crying from four rooms away as if she was near me,” he said.
His eyesight remained affected for nearly a year before he eventually sought treatment. He later underwent multiple surgeries with the support of the Layton Rahmatulla Benevolent Trust (LRBT). “I gave myself up as a surgical case to LRBT, and they helped me get my eyesight back.”
The experience eventually led to an enduring association with the organisation. “Today, I am a global ambassador for an eye hospital. I had 14 surgeries performed on me,” he said.
HSY also spoke about a childhood shaped by his mother. He shared that he was born in Islamabad into a family with connections to politics and the armed forces, but his parents’ early separation led to a difficult upbringing.
“I was born in Islamabad. My father’s side and my mom’s side were both connected to politics and the armed forces. My parents got divorced when I was two, and we left Pakistan. It was very hard for my mom to raise me alone. It was more difficult for her because she had grown up in a relaxed, luxurious life,” he added.
He spent much of his childhood in New York City, where his mother worked multiple jobs to support him. “She ran away, and I spent most of my life in New York City with an incredible mom.”
For HSY, watching his mother rebuild her life became one of the biggest sources of his ambition.
“The reason for my ambition is my mom and the difficulties she went through, which I saw — a woman who had never done anything like that before, doing four jobs. I used to see times when I wouldn’t see her the whole day.”
His mother worked wherever she could, from babysitting and working at a petrol station to serving as a secretary and working in a store. “She was babysitting, working in a gas station, working as a secretary or working in a store. Any job, whether it was big or small, my mom was my mom. She was my hero.”
HSY’s sister was also initially with him, but the siblings were separated when they were young. “My sister was with me, but not for long. We got separated when I was around four or five and she was nine or ten. She had gone to England. I hadn’t seen her for eight years, and I was alone.”
Much of what he learned, he said, came from observing the people around him and figuring things out himself. “I don’t necessarily remember learning from a specific person. It was like learning on the job. I used to see my friends shave, so I would start shaving. If there was a way to eat, I’d learn it.”
His experiences also shaped his approach to independence. “I live a positive life because I don’t expect anything from people. I think if you want to do something, do it yourself.”
Despite everything he experienced, HSY said he considered himself fortunate. “I am also very lucky. Allah gave me a lot,” he said.
Before becoming a fashion designer, HSY said he was willing to take on whatever work was available.
“I used to teach English when I was 15. Later, I would go and knock on people’s doors, saying, ‘I’ll teach you English.’ I even worked as a cashier in Lahore. I’ve picked up wood. I used to come to places on a rickshaw. Getting Rs30 was a lot for me at the time.”
He said he never viewed any of those jobs as something that made him less than anyone else.
“Whether I worked somewhere small or whatever, I didn’t think less of myself because my mother was not less than anyone else. Whether she was a tutor or doing something smaller, she was respected. She was working and raising me.”
That perspective, he said, came directly from watching his mother.
His complicated relationship with his father
HSY also opened up about his relationship with his father, describing it as complicated and saying the relationship eventually became distant. “My father — the end with him was not good, which is why I don’t speak much about him.”
He said his mother never encouraged him to resent his father. “My mother never said anything bad about him. She just told me about him and said he would ask about me when I was younger and wanted me back.”
When HSY returned to Pakistan at 16, his father offered for him to stay with him, but by then he had already grown up with his mother.
“My mother wanted to raise me. But my dad was in a position where, when I came back to Pakistan at 16, he said I could come to him. But I didn’t really want that. I had grown up with my mother.”
HSY said his father had not contributed to his education or upbringing, although there was a point when he himself asked his father for financial assistance. “When I was 35 or 36, he called me. He had become paralysed after a stroke and had lost all his money and his ability to take care of himself.”
It was his mother who encouraged him to help his father despite their past. “Then my mom told me, ‘Maybe he hasn’t done anything for you, but he is your father and you’ll regret it later for not helping him. So thank Allah that you can help him.’”
HSY said he ultimately supported his father for 15 years, an experience that changed his understanding of their relationship. “I helped him for 15 years, and in those years I gained the understanding that each person doesn’t have everything, and every human being isn’t perfect or capable of being a father.”
HSY’s entry into the fashion industry was far from conventional. With limited access to established circles, he decided to approach magazines himself.
“We used to have six or so magazines, and I sent them handwritten letters. I said, ‘You don’t know me. I’m sending you some work. If you can print them, I’ll be a big designer in Pakistan.’”
His persistence paid off. “Out of seven, five of them took my covers,” he shared.
He soon began receiving calls from some of the most recognisable names in the country. “My first phone calls were from Tahira Syed and Babra Sharif.”
While couture remained a significant part of his career, HSY revealed that he was preparing to enter the ready-to-wear space with a separate brand.
“I’m about to launch a ready-to-wear brand, and I’m excited about it. It’s going to be separate from HSY. I’ve always been into couture, but ready-to-wear is a space that also requires direction,” he shared.
He also spoke about the need for greater structure within Pakistan’s fashion industry, particularly when it came to shows and schedules. “There need to be the right shows. I feel like right now everything is all over the place. We need to bring things back and bring people down to a schedule.”
For HSY, the journey to becoming a household name was shaped by far more than fashion. From watching his mother work multiple jobs and learning to fend for himself from a young age, to losing his eyesight and rebuilding his life, his story was inseparable from the person behind the public name.
His experiences remain an important part of how he sees himself today. “If people are judging you, don’t judge them. I think you should tell people every single thing about you. You’re a whole human being of experiences,” he concluded.

title: Taylor Swift fans think  Patient Zero  is about Joe Jonas and Sophie Turner
description: In the song  Swift tells the woman that she understands what she is going through because she was  patient zero
content:
In the song, Swift tells the woman that she understands what she is going through because she was "patient zero"
Taylor Swift's new song Patient Zero has sparked fan theories about Joe Jonas and Sophie Turner, with listeners analysing the lyrics for clues about the identity of the relationship at the centre of the track.
Released on Friday, September 25, as part of The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore, Patient Zero sees Swift sing from the perspective of a woman who has experienced a toxic relationship and is warning another woman about the same man.
In the song, Swift tells the woman that she understands what she is going through because she was "patient zero". She describes the man as having "the devil on his shoulder under his halo" and sings about his ability to charm those around him.
The lyrics have led some fans to speculate that Swift could be referring to Joe Jonas and his former wife, Sophie Turner. The theory is partly based on Swift's friendship with Turner and the support she offered the actor following her 2023 separation from Jonas.
Turner and Jonas were married for four years and share two daughters. Following their separation, Turner was photographed spending time with Swift, and the Game of Thrones star and her children stayed at Swift's New York City home during the divorce proceedings.
Fans have connected those circumstances to the song's storyline, particularly the lyrics about a woman reaching out after hearing there is "trouble in paradise". Swift sings that she would understand the situation because she had previously experienced the same man's behaviour.
However, the Joe Jonas and Sophie Turner theory has not been confirmed by Swift. In fact, the singer has explained that the idea for Patient Zero came from a conversation among friends about relationships rather than identifying a specific former partner.
Swift told Capital FM that the song was inspired by a friend who had been contacted by the new girlfriend of one of her exes. The woman was seeking guidance about whether the friend had experienced similar behaviour from the man, prompting others in the group to share their own experiences.
Swift said the conversation made her interested in writing the song from the perspective of someone receiving that phone call from another woman who is experiencing a similar relationship.
The lyrics have nevertheless led to several other theories. Some fans believe Patient Zero could reference Swift's former partner Joe Alwyn, while others have suggested that the song could draw from multiple relationships rather than being about one particular person.
Swift has not confirmed that any of those interpretations are correct. Her representative also did not immediately respond to Entertainment Weekly's request for comment.
The song is the first of four new tracks on The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore. Swift also released Cleveland!, Pink Clouding and Babylon as part of the expanded edition.
Meanwhile, the Patient Zero music video is set to premiere during the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards on Sunday, September 27. The video stars Swift alongside Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell.
For now, the identity of the man referenced in Patient Zero remains unconfirmed, leaving fans to interpret the song's lyrics while Swift's own explanation points to a broader experience of women sharing warnings about relationships.

description: Kaia Gerber   s missing cat Tony has been found after friends  including Lewis Pullman  helped search for him this week
content:
Kaia Gerber’s missing cat Tony has been found after friends, including Lewis Pullman, helped search for him this week
Kaia Gerber’s missing cat, Tony, has been found after her boyfriend Lewis Pullman and several friends helped search for the pet during a difficult week for the model.
Tony reportedly went missing as Gerber was mourning the death of her brother, Presley Gerber, who died on September 20 at age 27. Friends and loved ones, including Pullman and comedian Jake Shane, were seen helping put up posters seeking information about the grey cat. The posters offered a reward for Tony’s safe return.
PEOPLE has since confirmed that Tony was found.
The news comes days after Presley Gerber’s death at a rehabilitation facility in California. The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner confirmed his death, while Santa Monica police said they were investigating it as a suspected overdose.
According to a statement from the Santa Monica Police Department, officers responded to a possible overdose report on September 20 and found an adult male deceased. Police said there was no indication of foul play at the time, while the official cause and manner of death would be determined by the Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner.
Presley’s autopsy has been completed, but PEOPLE reported that his cause of death remains listed as deferred.
Kaia Gerber, the daughter of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber, had previously spoken publicly about her brother’s struggles with addiction. His death has also prompted messages of support for the Gerber family from friends and fans.
For Kaia, the discovery of Tony comes during a particularly difficult period following her brother’s death. The cat’s disappearance had prompted a search involving people close to her, including Pullman.
Tony’s safe return was confirmed this week, bringing some positive news amid the family’s ongoing mourning.

title: Islamabad rejects  fake and fabricated  Kabul   s claim of destroying Pakistani post near Spin Boldak
description: Ministry of Information disputes Afghan account  saying Taliban posts were heavily punished and 13 personnel killed
content:
Ministry of Information disputes Afghan account, saying Taliban posts were heavily punished and 13 personnel killed
The Ministry of Information on Friday rejected Afghanistan’s Ministry of Defence’s claim that a Pakistani outpost near Spin Boldak in Kandahar had been destroyed, describing the assertion as “fake and fabricated”.
In a statement posted on X, the Afghan Ministry of Defence said that a day earlier, a Pakistani outpost near Spin Boldak had been “punished and destroyed” after it opened fire towards Afghanistan.

“The Afghan forces suffered no casualties or losses in the clash,” it said, adding that the “propaganda” circulated by the Pakistani side regarding the incident was false.
Read : Security forces foil Afghan Taliban incursion, kill several terrorists at Balochistan border: state media
Rejecting the Afghan account, the Ministry of Information’s fact-checking account said the Afghan Ministry of Defence had “as usual” falsely claimed that a Pakistani post near Spin Boldak was destroyed and that Afghan forces suffered no casualties, while dismissing Pakistan’s account as propaganda.
“The claim is fake and fabricated,” it said, adding that security forces had thwarted an attempted “Afghan aggression” in the Gulistan sector on the night of Sept 24-25.
It said that during the operation and the subsequent “heavy punishment” inflicted on opposing Taliban posts, at least 13 Afghan Taliban personnel were killed and several others injured.

“Some visuals of the incident are also attached, which have already been widely covered by media and circulated extensively across social media,” the statement said.
It said the visuals provided evidence of the border engagement and the “punishment inflicted on the Afghan Taliban after their cowardly attack”.
The ministry added that the Afghan Ministry of Defence’s “fabricated” claim was “no surprise”, alleging that the Taliban were “habitual liars” with “no moral and reputational standing”.
The recent tension started between the neighbouring countries after a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers, in which 23 people, including 15 police personnel , were martyred. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
A day earlier, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said Pakistan carried out “precision” aerial and drone strikes against 10 locations in Afghanistan after drones launched from Afghan territory entered Pakistani airspace, describing the strikes as a response to a “deliberate and unlawful incursion”.
The strikes were in response to drone attacks from Afghanistan. A day earlier, Pakistan’s air defence systems had shot down eight drones after they entered the country’s airspace from Afghanistan. Security sources said four of the drones were brought down in areas adjoining the Torkham border, while another four were shot down in mountainous areas near the border with Kohat.
Pakistan has repeatedly raised concerns on international forums over terrorist attacks being launched from Afghan soil.
On September 23, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar called for “concrete and verifiable” action to prevent Afghan soil from being used for terrorism against neighbouring countries, particularly Pakistan, while addressing the OIC Contact Group on Afghanistan on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York.
In a separate warning following the terrorist attack in Kohat, Pakistan said it had the “will and capability” to eliminate terror threats “wherever they are” and urged the international community to press the Afghan Taliban regime to take decisive action against terrorism.
Attributing the attack to “the vilest of Khwarij with roots in Afghanistan,” the Information Ministry noted that the attack was a reminder that “terrorism has no religion and no justification”. It added that Islamabad had repeatedly raised “grave concerns” over the alleged use of Afghan territory by the banned TTP and other terrorist groups to plan and launch attacks inside the country.
“The presence of terrorist sanctuaries, alongside their recruitment and support infrastructure in Afghanistan, poses a direct threat to Pakistan’s security,” the ministry had said. It added that these concerns had repeatedly been conveyed to the Afghan Taliban regime and its interlocutors. “They must dismantle these networks rather than deflect responsibility,” Pakistan said.
United Nations Security Council report formally implicated the banned Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and terrorist entities operating from Afghanistan , highlighting tactical collaboration and shared operational logistics between the groups.
Member-state reporting confirmed that BLA terrorists were trained alongside TTP members at facilities in Afghanistan, according to the report, which also described growing operational links among various terrorist groups operating across the border.
This was not the first time a UN report pointed to the threat posed by terrorist groups operating from Afghanistan. In 2023, a UN report also revealed that the TTP had established a new base in K-P in mid-2023, shedding light on close ties between the TTP and the Afghan Taliban, as well as between the TTP and anti-Pakistani groups and Al Qaeda.

title: Irrefutable evidence    links Afghan soil to terror attacks in Pakistan
description: Pakistan cites 260 terrorists killed in attacks  cross border infiltration  training camps as proof of terror network
content:
Pakistan cites 260 terrorists killed in attacks, cross-border infiltration, training camps as proof of terror network
The Taliban regime in Afghanistan was providing sanctuary, support and patronage to terrorist groups, Pakistani officials said on Friday, adding that documented evidence contradicted Kabul’s repeated denials and pointed to an entrenched terrorist network operating from Afghan soil .
According to security officials, the identities of 260 Afghan terrorists killed while carrying out attacks in Pakistan had been established, with records containing their names, addresses and family details.
Officials said the figure did not include unidentified terrorists currently operating in Pakistan, suggesting that the documented fatalities represented only part of the involvement of Afghan nationals in cross-border terrorism.
Read : Afghan soil must not be used for terrorism, Pakistan tells UN
They also pointed to the funerals of Afghan terrorists killed in Pakistan, which were held in their hometowns with the participation of Taliban regime officials. “An administration that claims it has no connection with terrorists cannot explain why its officials attend the funerals of terrorists killed while attacking Pakistan,” one official said.
Pakistan maintains that the terrorist nexus extended beyond the movement of terrorists across the border to their training, arming and operational support.
Security officials estimate that up to 70 per cent of the Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists infiltrating Pakistan were of Afghan origin. They further claim that the Taliban regime had allowed leftover US and NATO weapons to reach terrorist groups, including Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan .
Weapons and equipment recovered from militants include M4 assault rifles, Remington sniper rifles and night-vision devices, according to Pakistani officials.
The security establishment also linked the escalation in attacks to the presence of terrorist infrastructure inside Afghanistan.
In 2026 alone, terrorism emanating from Afghan soil claimed the lives of 1,327 Pakistanis and injured another 2,484, according to figures cited by Pakistani authorities.
Read More : Pakistan warns Afghanistan after Kohat attack, says it can eliminate terror threats ‘wherever they are’
The United Nations estimated the strength of TTP in Afghanistan at around 6,000 to 6,500 terrorists. UN reporting had also documented more than 600 terrorist attacks against Pakistan during 2025, including attacks launched from Afghan territory.
According to Pakistani security officials, the TTP had established training facilities in Afghanistan’s Kunar, Nangarhar, Khost and Paktika provinces.
Officials further alleged that personnel associated with the Afghan Taliban regime were also joining the terrorist group at some of these training centres, describing the development as evidence of an increasingly blurred line between elements of the Taliban regime and terrorist infrastructure.
Pakistan has repeatedly accused the Taliban regime of failing to take action against militant sanctuaries despite being provided with information about their locations and activities.

Officials said that whenever Pakistani forces targeted terrorist hideouts, the Taliban regime instead moved to defend the militants and their sanctuaries rather than dismantling the infrastructure. The issue, Pakistan has argued, was not confined to TTP.
UN assessments have continued to document the presence of several other militant organisations in Afghanistan, including al Qaeda, the East Turkestan Islamic Movement (ETIM) and Islamic State-Khorasan, reinforcing concerns about the broader militant ecosystem operating from Afghan territory.

Pakistani officials say the continued presence of these groups, combined with training facilities, cross-border infiltration and access to sophisticated weapons, demonstrates that Afghanistan remains an important base for terrorist activity affecting Pakistan.
Islamabad has rejected Taliban assurances that Afghan territory would not be used against neighbouring countries, arguing that the ground situation and documented militant activity tell a different story.
Pakistan's position, according to officials, remains that Kabul must take concrete steps to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries, eliminate training infrastructure, prevent cross-border infiltration and ensure that Afghan territory is not used for attacks against Pakistan.
The government has maintained that the issue was fundamentally one of Pakistan's national security and that continued attacks from Afghan soil cannot be addressed through denials alone.
Pakistan says it expected the Taliban regime to fulfil its commitments by taking verifiable action against terrorist groups operating from its territory rather than defending or denying their presence.

The sale comes as Jolie’s children have moved out and reports suggest she plans to leave Los Angeles
Angelina Jolie has sold her Los Feliz mansion for $24.75 million as the actress prepares for a new chapter after her children have begun moving out .
Jolie’s 11,000-square-foot property, which has six bedrooms and 10 bathrooms, had been on the market for five months. She initially listed the home in May for almost $30 million.
Jolie purchased the property in 2017 for around $24.5 million following her split from Brad Pitt.
The former Cecil B. DeMille estate sits on two acres and includes a library, tea house, wine cellar, fitness studio, swimming pool and pool house.
The property’s listing is being handled by Sotheby’s International Realty and The Agency, with a contract currently pending, according to the Sotheby’s website.
The sale comes as Jolie’s children have moved out and reports suggest she plans to leave Los Angeles.
A source told TMZ that Jolie has yet to establish a new home base and will return to work in different parts of the world, including Cambodia, where she owns a residence.
Jolie previously discussed her plans to leave California in a 2024 interview with The Hollywood Reporter.
“I grew up in this town. I am here because I have to be here from a divorce, but as soon as they're 18, I'll be able to leave,” she said.
Earlier this month, Jolie and Pitt’s son Maddox legally removed Pitt from his surname, becoming Maddox Chivan Jolie. Zahara is also due to have a name-change hearing on September 28.

content:
The 'Fault In Our Stars' author spoke with Vanity Fair, saying Rowling's views make him feel 'very, very sad'
John Green has spoken about JK Rowling’s views on the trans community, saying they are “heartbreaking” for trans Harry Potter fans who feel connected to the author’s work.
The Fault In Our Stars author discussed Rowling in an interview with Vanity Fair, saying her views make him feel “very, very sad”.
“I think it’s important when we talk about her to talk about the fact that supporting her work now is directly supporting efforts at the erasure of trans people, and that makes me really sad.”
Green also referred to trans friends who have Deathly Hallows tattoos, saying he thinks about “all the trans friends I have who have Deathly Hallows tattoos and how heartbreaking it is for them to have someone who created something that matters so much to them really betray them”.
He also confirmed that he will not watch HBO’s upcoming Harry Potter remake, responding: “No. No. No.”
The comments come amid continued debate over Rowling’s views on transgender rights.
Earlier in September, her agent, Neil Blair, denied claims that the author supported “legal actions aimed at harming transgender people or efforts to limit trans rights”.
Blair said Rowling’s views should be represented “accurately, fairly and respectfully” and described allegations made against her as “clearly fabricated and not based on any evidence”.
Rowling’s website also denies that she is transphobic, stating: “JK Rowling clearly states trans people need and deserve protection. She wants trans women to be safe but not to the detriment of natal girls and women’s safety and for their rights to single sex spaces to remain protected.”
As of yet, Rowling does not appear to have responded to Green’s comments.

KSE-100 edges higher to close at 170,765 as geopolitical risks weigh in
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) benchmark KSE-100 Index witnessed a range-bound day, gaining only 266.15 points on Friday to close at 170,765, as investors remained cautious amid geopolitical uncertainty and elevated oil prices.
PSX witnessed a mixed session today, with the KSE-100 Index gaining 266 points (+0.16% DoD) to close at 170,765. During the trading hours, the benchmark index traded in both directions before ending on a flattish note ahead of the weekend, noted Ali Najib, Deputy Head of Trading at Arif Habib Ltd.
The KSE-100 Index touched an intraday high of 171,160 (+661 points; +0.39%) and an intraday low of 169,891 (-608 points; -0.36%), reflecting cautious investor participation amid prevailing uncertainties.
Investor sentiment remained cautious due to uncertainty on the geopolitical front. According to Reuters , Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan are expected to hold an urgent, high-level meeting under their joint defence pact to discuss measures to support the Kingdom amid attacks by Yemen’s Houthis, while Tehran sought to distance itself from the rapid advance of its Houthi allies.
Meanwhile, PTI has decided to delay its long march to Islamabad, following the deployment of thousands of security personnel, road blockades and restrictions on public gatherings.
Also Read: PTI postpones Islamabad march to October 4: party sources
On the corporate front, PSO PA (+0.94%) reported FY26 EPS of Rs32.10/share, down 28% YoY, primarily due to lower sales volumes, higher inventory losses, elevated petroleum prices and a weaker contribution from the LNG segment amid geopolitical tensions. The company also announced a final cash dividend of Rs10/share in 4QFY26, taking its FY26 payout ratio to 31%.
On the index contribution front, HBL, UBL, BAFL, BAHL and PSO collectively added 207 points, while MEBL, FFC, HUBC, PTC and CNERGY dragged the index by 151 points.
Market activity remained subdued, with 481.6 million shares changing hands, while total traded value stood at Rs19.2billion.
CNERGY remained the volume leader, with 108.2 million shares traded during the session.
The KSE-100 Index ended the week on a flattish note, declining 119 points (-0.07% WoW) to close at 170,765. During the week, the index traded between an intraday high of 172,762 and a low of 169,891, reflecting range-bound activity amid selective profit-taking.
Going forward, market sentiment is expected to remain volatile, with selective buying likely if geopolitical tensions continue to ease and oil prices trend lower. However, elevated energy prices, external-sector risks, and the upcoming IMF review will remain key factors influencing market direction.

title: Aamir Khan to receive Screen Icon Award at Singapore film festival
description: Actor also set to reunite with  Lagaan  director Ashutosh Gowariker for a 25th anniversary screening of the film
content:
Actor also set to reunite with 'Lagaan' director Ashutosh Gowariker for a 25th-anniversary screening of the film
Bollywood star Aamir Khan was set to receive the Screen Icon Award at the 37th Singapore International Film Festival, where he was also scheduled to join director Ashutosh Gowariker for a special screening marking 25 years of Lagaan: Once Upon a Time in India .
According to Gulf News , Khan was to be recognised for his contribution to Asian cinema with the award, which honours actors whose work has made a significant creative impact on the region’s film industry.
Khan was also scheduled to participate in the festival’s “In Conversation With” programme, giving audiences an opportunity to hear from him as part of the anniversary celebrations.
The Singapore International Film Festival is scheduled to take place from October 21 to November 1, with the 2026 edition being held earlier than its traditional schedule.
Released on June 15, 2001, Lagaan emerged as one of the most ambitious Hindi films of its era. Directed by Gowariker and starring Khan, the film combined a period drama set during British colonial rule with the unlikely setting of a cricket match.
The film’s international journey became a defining chapter in Indian cinema when Lagaan was selected as India’s entry for the Academy Awards and earned a nomination for Best Foreign Language Film at the 74th Academy Awards.
Its anniversary screening in Singapore therefore marked 25 years since the film helped introduce a major Hindi-language production to a much wider global audience.
According to Gulf News , Khan had attended a screening at the London Indian Film Festival in July, where he spoke about the success of Lagaan .
“As Lagaan completes 25 years, it’s hard to put into words what this journey has meant. We made the film with a lot of belief, passion, and honesty, never imagining the kind of love it would receive and continue to receive all these years later,” he said.

UN chief commends Islamabad's efforts for regional peace, stability, sacrifices in countering terrorism

According to a post on X by the Government of Pakistan, the premier warmly welcomed Prince Rahim and fondly recalled their meeting earlier this year during the Aga Khan’s visit to Pakistan.
“The prime minister appreciated the commitment of Prince Rahim Aga Khan to maintaining longstanding friendly and positive relations with Pakistan and reiterated his resolve to continue close cooperation with him for achieving the shared objectives of peace, stability and development,” the statement said.
It added that PM Shehbaz “appreciated the longstanding services of the Ismaili community in Pakistan’s socio-economic development and highlighted its valuable tradition of service to society and civic engagement.”

The premier also appreciated the contributions of institutions affiliated with the Aga Khan Development Network (AKDN) in promoting financial inclusion, tourism, the preservation of cultural heritage and economic empowerment through the participation of local communities.
According to the statement, PM Shehbaz “emphasised the importance of fully leveraging the vast potential for further cooperation in these areas to promote sustainable and inclusive development in Pakistan.”

title: NDMA warns of heavy rain  flash floods across upper regions from Sept 25 to 30
description: Authorities place emergency teams on standby as thunderstorms threaten vulnerable districts  low lying areas
content:
Authorities place emergency teams on standby as thunderstorms threaten vulnerable districts, low-lying areas
The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) on Friday issued an alert over expected rainfall and weather-related hazards across the country’s upper regions from September 25 to 30, warning of possible flash floods in mountainous areas and urban flooding in several districts.
According to the National Emergencies Operation Centre (NEOC), a westerly weather system is expected to intensify on September 25 and 26, bringing thunderstorms and rainfall to parts of upper Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) and Islamabad.
The anticipated rainfall could trigger flash floods in mountainous areas, as well as sudden rises in seasonal streams and nullahs, the alert said.
In Gilgit-Baltistan, Astore, Skardu, Roundu, Ghanche and Shigar have been identified as areas at risk. In AJK, Neelum Valley, Haveli, Poonch and Sudhanoti may face flooding, while Swat, Bajaur, Lower and Upper Dir, Kohistan, Kolai-Palas, Battagram and Mansehra have been identified as vulnerable areas in K-P.
The NEOC said thunderstorms and heavy rainfall were also expected in parts of the Potohar region, Punjab and K-P through September 30, with hailstorms possible at some locations.
The weather system could cause urban flooding in Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Attock, Chakwal, Jhelum, Murree, Galiyat, Mianwali, Khushab, Bhakkar, Layyah, Sialkot, Lahore, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Sargodha, Faisalabad, Okara, Sahiwal and Jhang, among other areas.
Several other districts in K-P are also expected to receive heavy rainfall, including Dir, Swat, Buner, Malakand, Shangla, Battagram, Kohistan, Mansehra, Abbottabad, Haripur, Nowshera, Swabi, Mardan, Peshawar, Kurram, Hangu, Karak, Bannu, Lakki Marwat, Dera Ismail Khan and Waziristan.
The NDMA has directed relevant departments and local authorities to take advance measures to deal with possible flooding and other weather-related hazards.
Emergency response teams and essential resources have been ordered to remain on standby in potentially affected areas. Authorities have also been instructed to continuously monitor rainfall, water levels and conditions in rivers, streams and nullahs.
The NDMA advised the public to avoid crossing seasonal streams, mountain torrents and roads submerged by floodwater, warning that rapidly rising water levels could pose a serious danger.
Residents of low-lying and other vulnerable areas have been urged to remain vigilant and take necessary safety precautions.
The authority also advised citizens to use the Pak NDMA Disaster Alert mobile application for verified weather updates, information on potential hazards and guidance on precautionary measures.

title: Ireland s Gaza stance spills from Eurovision into football
description: They face Israel in Hungary on Sunday
content:
No Irish supporters in the stadium, no home match in Ireland and no pundits or Irish commentary on television: the country's strong support for the Palestinian cause is increasingly reshaping its sporting and cultural calendar.
Ireland face Israel in football's Nations League in Hungary on Sunday before a designated Irish "home" game in Serbia on October 4, amid protests and calls for a boycott over Israel's war in Gaza.
Sunday's match comes days after national broadcaster RTE confirmed Ireland would again boycott the Eurovision Song Contest next year because of Israel's participation.
But contractual obligations mean it must show the football matches.
The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) has, meanwhile, declined its ticket allocation for Irish supporters for Sunday's fixture.
The game is being staged in Debrecen, Hungary, because Israel cannot currently host international matches, while the reverse fixture was shifted from Dublin to Backa Topola, Serbia, and will be played behind closed doors.
"It is highly unusual for a state broadcaster to show a major international match while stripping away punditry" and the other usual elements, said Neil O'Boyle, an associate professor at Dublin City University specialising in sport and media.
RTE faced "a unique dilemma", he told AFP, between its contractual obligations and "intense pushback from the Irish public and some of its own staff".
"The 'silent' broadcast is intended as a kind of moral compromise," he said.
Ireland has long been a strong supporter of the Palestinian cause, with sympathy often linked to the country's own history of British rule.
Research published this year by political scientist Liam Kneafsey and colleague Miceal Canavan found Ireland a clear outlier in western Europe.
Their study, based on a representative survey conducted in late 2023, found 53 percent of Irish adults sympathised more with Palestinians and 11 percent with Israel, compared with around 27 percent pro-Palestinian sympathy in the next-highest western European country.
"Ireland's history of colonisation, partition and displacement gives people a ready-made template for understanding a distant and complex conflict," Kneafsey told AFP.
Such attitudes were "rooted in history and identity, not just a reaction to headlines", he added.
Dublin formally recognised a Palestinian state in 2024 alongside Spain and Norway, and has repeatedly criticised Israel's conduct in Gaza.
More than 160 Irish sportspeople have signed a letter urging the national team to boycott the football games, while protests have targeted the FAI and players.
Manager Heimir Hallgrimsson has acknowledged players are uncomfortable about the fixtures, saying: "We're not playing with genocide. We're playing against genocide."
Israel's football federation accused him of "stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy", remarks Taoiseach (prime minister) Micheal Martin on Tuesday called "unacceptable".
Amnesty International Ireland's executive director, Stephen Bowen, said UEFA should have suspended Israel, arguing that Israeli clubs operating in occupied Palestinian territory breached football's rules.
"It shocks the conscience that Ireland has to play these fixtures," he told AFP.
"Upset and outrage here in Ireland at these matches is palpable."
But former Irish justice minister Alan Shatter strongly rejected the boycott campaign.
"It's a scandal that a group of obsessed political activists have created a situation where our home game is now taking place behind closed doors in Serbia," he told AFP.
Shatter said the FAI should have staged the fixture in Dublin with police protection and accused campaigners of placing players under unacceptable pressure.
The FAI itself requested last year that UEFA suspend Israel but received insufficient support from European football's governing body.
It says refusing to play could bring sporting and financial sanctions.
Israel strongly rejects allegations that its conduct in Gaza amounts to genocide.
It launched war on Gaza in response to a Hamas attack inside Israel on October 7, 2023, that resulted in the deaths of 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.
Its bombardment and ground offensive in Gaza has killed more than 73,900 people there, according to the occupied Palestinian territory's health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

title: In West Bank art centre  Palestinian children paint hopes beyond checkpoints
description: Art centre helps children process violence and raids  Hebron youngsters paint dreams beyond checkpoints
content:
Art centre helps children process violence and raids, Hebron youngsters paint dreams beyond checkpoints
On the outskirts of Hebron in the occupied West Bank, a Palestinian woman has transformed her home into an art centre where children use drawing to process their experiences of settler violence and Israeli military raids.
Artist Sarah Abu Madi says she founded the centre - Rommana, meaning pomegranate in Arabic - in 2020 to give local children a place to express their feelings and talk about what they had experienced.
The centre's work has taken on greater urgency as violence by Israeli settlers has surged in recent years amid a major expansion of Jewish settlements in the territory.
"If a settler or a soldier does something, we ask: 'How did that make you feel? What did it make you think about? How does that affect you?'," Abu Madi said. "If there is a raid on a home, we ask: 'What did that make you feel? What do you think? How does that affect you? What do you wish there would be?'."
This week, the children were asked to sketch the things most important to them. Talia Sabah, 10, drew a picture of birds flying from a cage, saying it represented freedom.
"I feel freedom is the most important thing in life," Sabah said. "I wish the military would stop being in our lives and there would be freedom, and we could do what we want with life."
'Art creates a space that tells them: You can dream'
Israel captured the West Bank in 1967 and since then the territory has been under Israeli military occupation. Hundreds of thousands of Israeli Jewish settlers have moved to the territory, with settlement expansion accelerating rapidly under the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
The United Nations and most countries regard the settlements as illegal under international law governing military occupations. Israel disputes that interpretation and says the territory's status is disputed.
The Rommana studio is located in Wadi Al-Samen, a Hebron quarter isolated from the rest of the city by six military checkpoints, according to Abu Madi. The area sees frequent military raids as well as incursions from nearby Israeli settlements and settler outposts.
Children spoke about encounters with Israeli settlers and soldiers with a familiarity unusual for children their age.
"My grandfather on my mother's side owns land in the mountains, but the settlers established a settlement there, and anyone who goes up to the mountain gets arrested," said Karam Sabah, 11.
When Rommana first opened, it consisted of a few carpets laid on the floor of an old storage room. Today, children sit around low plastic tables beside colourful murals they helped paint.
Their artwork has begun travelling beyond the West Bank, with one exhibition held in Canada and another planned in Mexico, Abu Madi said.
Around 600 children attend the centre, she said. Her goal is to expand the project so that all 3,000 children living in the neighbourhood can take part.
One of the paintings by the children showed three children sitting on the back of a winged horse, representing a dream of being able to fly freely, no longer trapped behind checkpoints.
"Art also creates a space that tells them: you can dream. You can imagine and build a reality different from the one you're living in," said Abu Madi.

title: Bono reveals Dolly Parton got out of bed rest to record her final song with U2
description: Parton recorded  Torn  with U2 in June  just two months before her death at the age of 80 on August 25
content:
Parton recorded 'Torn' with U2 in June, just two months before her death at the age of 80 on August 25
Bono has revealed that Dolly Parton got out of bed while ill to record what became her final vocal performance, a duet with U2 titled Torn.
The country music icon recorded the song with Bono in June, just two months before her death at the age of 80 on August 25. The track will appear as the closing song on U2's upcoming 16th studio album, Carnaval De Luz.
Speaking to Rolling Stone, Bono recalled how Parton made the effort to record the song despite being unwell.
"When she got ill, she got out of her bed to sing this song," Bono said. He added, "And you can hear that. And I can't even listen to it now."
Torn was co-written by Parton, U2 and Snow Patrol's Johnny McDaid. Bono had initially approached Parton about contributing to another project inspired by Irish folk music, but she felt the material was "a little too Irish" for her. Instead, she suggested her own song, Torn, and asked Bono whether he could take it in another direction.
Bono and McDaid subsequently reworked the lyrics around a mother watching her family fall apart. Parton agreed to record the revised version, with Bono recalling that she "sang her heart out" during the session.
Parton was able to hear the finished track before her death and approved the final mix. Producer Garret "Jacknife" Lee said she was proud of her vocal performance and pleased with the finished recording.
The song also features Daniel Lanois on pedal steel, while U2 drummer Larry Mullen Jr. contributes a drum part inspired by Bob Dylan's Most of the Time.
U2 announced Carnaval De Luz on September 24, marking the band's first album of new material in nine years. The 12-track record is scheduled for release on November 13 and will be the band's 16th studio album.
Parton's final recording adds another layer to the upcoming album, with Torn becoming a posthumous collaboration between the country legend and Bono. The song will give fans one final new vocal performance from Parton when Carnaval De Luz arrives in November.

title: Dakota Johnson says thriller  Verity  puts truth and trust to the test  much like real life
description: Adaptation is the latest of Colleen Hoover s novels to reach the big screen  following  It Ends With Us
content:
Adaptation is the latest of Colleen Hoover's novels to reach the big screen, following 'It Ends With Us'
Psychological thriller Verity taps into the real-world challenge of knowing what's true and who to trust, actor Dakota Johnson said at the film's ‌UK premiere on Thursday.
Based on Colleen Hoover's bestselling novel, the film follows struggling writer Lowen Ashleigh, played by Johnson, who is hired to complete a series of books for renowned author Verity Crawford after an accident leaves her unable to write.
The assignment draws Lowen into the Crawford family's secluded estate, where she uncovers what appears to be Verity's autobiographical manuscript. As its unsettling secrets unfold, the line between truth and deception begins to blur.
"It's so thrilling, it's so ⁠sexy," Johnson said. "You are constantly trying to figure out what the truth is and who the good people are and who the bad people are. It's kind of a lot like life."
The adaptation is the latest of Hoover's novels to reach the big screen, following the attention generated by Justin Baldoni's It Ends With Us .
Directed by actor-turned-filmmaker Michael Showalter, the film stars Academy Award winner Anne Hathaway as Verity and Josh Hartnett as her husband, Jeremy.
The Big Sick director said he was captivated by the darkly seductive allure Hoover created. "It felt like this very glamorous, hypnotic, inviting world that I wanted to lose myself into, but also very scary and suspenseful," he said.
For Hartnett, the film's refusal to provide straightforward answers drew him to the project. "What I love about ‌this ⁠story is that it's kind of a choose-your-own-adventure about who is the villain," the Oppenheimer actor said, adding that many modern films "spoon-feed" audiences conclusions.
He said he hopes the film's open-ended nature will spark debate among cinemagoers. "I want to hear lots of arguments. I want to see people throwing popcorn in other people's faces," he joked.
Hartnett said he was "mesmerised" watching Hathaway and Johnson portray their characters. "These two are just right up there ⁠with all the very best in our industry," he said. "This whole film exists on their two faces."
For Johnson, Verity's dark themes have only increased her appetite for villainous roles. "I would love to be a villain. It's so fun to play a crazy person," the Fifty Shades of Grey actor ⁠told Reuters .
Showalter said Hoover remained closely involved throughout the filmmaking process and even makes a cameo appearance. While the movie remains largely faithful to the novel, the director acknowledged it leans further into erotic themes. "We are sexual creatures and this story explores ⁠that," he said.
More broadly, Showalter said he wanted to make a mainstream film that trusted audiences to engage with uncomfortable ideas.
"We can handle things that don't feel everyday," he said. "I think that's important…in commercial film and Hollywood film, to take on difficult subject matter."
Verity begins its global cinematic rollout on September 30.
