title: The Script offers gigs to Ed Sheeran tour acts who left in support of Macklemore
description: Frontman Danny O   Donoghue extended the invitation to Aaron Rowe and Beoga saying that    they showed immense backbone
content:
Frontman Danny O’Donoghue extended the invitation to Aaron Rowe and Beoga saying that “they showed immense backbone"
The Script have offered work to two Irish acts who left Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour after Macklemore was removed from the line-up.
Frontman Danny O’Donoghue extended the invitation to Aaron Rowe and Beoga during an appearance on Ireland’s The Late Late Show, praising the musicians for their decision to walk away from the tour.
“They showed immense backbone,” O’Donoghue said, while expressing particular admiration for Rowe, who left the stadium tour despite having the opportunity to perform at major US venues.
O’Donoghue then directly addressed Rowe and Beoga, inviting them to join The Script at their upcoming Dublin shows.
“The Script are playing the 3Arena on the dates that you were supposed to play Tampa,” he said. “If you want to come, if you want to support, then The Script are there for you. You’re more than welcome to come down.”
The Script are scheduled to perform at Dublin’s 3Arena on October 30 and 31. Those dates coincide with the Tampa show that Rowe and Beoga had originally been scheduled to perform as part of Sheeran’s tour. Sheeran’s official tour schedule lists Tampa for November 7, while the tour also has two Florida dates in Hollywood on October 29 and 30.
Rowe and Beoga were among several supporting acts who left Sheeran’s Loop Tour after Macklemore was removed from the remaining US dates. Finneas and Danish band Lukas Graham also withdrew from the tour.
Macklemore's removal followed his September performance at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium, where he voiced support for Palestinians and led the audience in saying “Free Palestine”. Sheeran later said that the decision to remove Macklemore was made by the tour’s promoters and was not his own.
Rowe said at the time that he could not continue with the tour while what he described as the silencing of voices speaking about Palestine was taking place. Beoga similarly announced its departure, while Finneas said artists should not be silenced when speaking about oppressed people.
The fallout left Sheeran without several of his planned supporting acts. He addressed the controversy during his September 19 concert in Philadelphia, where he spoke about freedom of speech and the wider conflict surrounding the situation in Gaza.
Sheeran said he had tried to speak with venues about Macklemore’s removal but ultimately said the decision by the venues and promoter was final. He also said he did not want to abandon fans, touring crew members and musicians who depended on the shows for work.
Meanwhile, O’Donoghue said he is a “massive believer in free speech” while discussing the controversy on The Late Late Show. The Script singer is now preparing to take his band back on the road in support of their latest album, The User’s Guide to Being Human.
It remains unclear whether Rowe and Beoga will accept O’Donoghue’s invitation to perform with The Script in Dublin. The offer, however, gives the two Irish acts an opportunity to appear on stage in their home country after stepping away from Sheeran’s US stadium tour.

title: Haaland breaks Ibrahimovic s scoring record
description: He also surpasses Ronaldo   s international scoring tally
content:
He also surpasses Ronaldo’s international scoring tally
Erling Haaland marked another milestone on Thursday after a double in Norway's 3-2 Nations League victory over Denmark made him the highest-scoring Nordic man in international football history, surpassing Sweden's Zlatan Ibrahimovic.
Haaland took his tally for the national team to 64 goals in 56 appearances, eclipsing Ibrahimovic's 62 goals in 122 matches for Sweden.
The Manchester City striker completed his double in the ⁠74th minute, sealing Norway's first competitive victory over Denmark.
"It is not possible to explain, nor is it possible to learn. He is born with it. It is instinct," Norway manager Stale Solbakken said.
Haaland, who made his senior international debut in 2019, has scored at a rate of more than 1.1 goals per game for Norway.
"It's madness," Norwegian midfielder Sander Berge said. "It's everyday business that Haaland scores goals, so it's reasonable that he is up there, but it's powerful."
The 26-year-old also moved past Brazil ⁠great Ronaldo, who scored 62 international goals before retiring in 2011. Former Sweden women's forward Lotta Schelin holds the overall Nordic international record with 88 goals.
Haaland's clinical finishing dominated the reaction in Denmark.
"Norway has him, and they should be thankful for that on a night where ⁠his sheer ruthlessness ensured the Norwegians secured the bragging rights," Danish broadcaster DR analyst Michael Sten Jensen said.
Danish newspaper B.T. wrote that Denmark were "brutally punished by Norway's most dangerous man."
Denmark striker Rasmus ⁠Hojlund acknowledged the unique threat posed by the forward.
"Erling has a way of finding the path to the goal," Hojlund said. "So in that sense it comes as no ⁠surprise, but at the same time it frustrates me."
Denmark will have a chance for revenge when they host Norway on the final matchday of the Nations League group stage on November 17.

The Tampa International Airport Police Department received a call for assistance at 2:20pm on September 23, according to Page Six.
No arrest was made, no medical transport was required and police did not create a report.
Law enforcement sources told the US Sun that officers were contacted after “multiple females said they needed police ASAP”.
Officials were reportedly told Milania, who was travelling with Teresa, Gia and a counsellor, had “just [been] released from the hospital.”
Milania was described as a white female wearing a tan hat and yellow tracksuit, with brown hair, and carrying a cat in a pink animal carrier.
She was located within around 12 minutes and subsequently boarded a flight with her family.
A now-deleted social media video showed officers surrounding the group. During the exchange, Milania repeatedly asked her mother and sister, “This is what we do now?” Teresa was also heard telling her daughter, “I love you.”

When Gia reportedly told Teresa to “just let [Milania] do what she wants to do”, Milania responded, “Shut the f**k up.”
The airport incident comes four months after Milania was arrested on a simple assault charge following a domestic dispute.
It was previously reported that she later enrolled in anger management classes.

title: Sindh crucial to growing America Pakistan ties  says US consul general
description: Goodman traces the friendship between the two countries back to Pakistan   s independence
content:
Charles Goodman traces friendship between the two countries back to Pakistan’s independence
Sindh has remained crucial to the longstanding relationship between Pakistan and the United States, with growing commercial engagement between the two countries offering further opportunities for cooperation, US Consul General Charles Goodman said on Thursday.
Speaking at a reception hosted by the US Consulate General in Karachi to mark the 250th anniversary of American independence, Goodman traced the friendship between the two countries back to Pakistan’s independence and highlighted Sindh’s role in strengthening bilateral ties.
“Lasting stability is built on economic prosperity, and our consulate team in Karachi plays a vital role in unlocking that potential across Sindh and Balochistan,” Goodman said, according to a statement issued by the Public Diplomacy Section of the US Consulate General Karachi.
250 years of American history. 🇺🇸 Nearly 80 years of U.S.-Pakistan partnership. 🤝 One unforgettable night. This week, the U.S. Consulate General Karachi hosted “Freedom 250: The American Brand,” a special reception celebrating America’s milestone. The evening brought together… pic.twitter.com/u8TfzHmDJu
He said the US government supported more than 80 American companies operating in Pakistan, while bilateral trade in goods and services had surpassed $11 billion last year.
The reception, organised under the “Freedom 250” campaign, brought together representatives of the government, business community, academia, civil society, media, diplomatic corps and US exchange programme alumni.
Sindh Assembly Speaker Syed Awais Qadir Shah attended as chief guest, while Sindh Governor Syed Nehal Hashmi was the guest of honour. Speaking on the occasion, Governor Hashmi underscored the importance of expanding cooperation between the two countries, particularly in education, technology, creativity and entrepreneurship.
Joined the “Freedom 250” reception hosted by U.S. Consul General Karachi Charles Goodman to commemorate 250 years of American independence. Extended congratulations to the American people and reaffirmed our commitment to further strengthening Pakistan–U.S. relations. pic.twitter.com/OpVhnIRcvq
“For our generation, contributing [to the future of our nations] increasingly means knowledge, education, creativity, and technology,” he said, calling for stronger links between American innovation and Pakistani talent, US universities and Pakistani students, and entrepreneurs in both countries.
Speaker Shah congratulated the United States on its 250th anniversary and highlighted the contribution of Pakistan-US cooperation to Sindh in education, economic opportunity and cultural exchange.
He expressed confidence that bilateral collaboration could be expanded further in a sustainable manner.
Also Read: How Trump's diplomatic week exposed the limits of his power
The “Freedom 250” campaign is being observed by US diplomatic missions worldwide to commemorate the 250th anniversary of the signing of the US Declaration of Independence. President Trump launched the celebration under the banner, “A New Era of American Greatness,” which was carried forward by the US embassies and consulates across the globe.
The Karachi event also featured the theme “The American Brand”, highlighting American innovation, enterprise, and creativity.
The celebration also paid tribute to the foundational ideals of July 4, 1776, and echoed President Trump’s emphasis on America’s lasting principles while reaffirming Chargé d’Affaires Natalie Baker’s message that a strong Pakistan benefits America, and a strong America benefits Pakistan.

title: Fact check  Italian PM Meloni did not attend UNGA  viral video criticising Israel is from 2025
description: Video is from her speech during the 80th UNGA session  Italian PM will not attend this year   s meeting
content:
Video is from her speech during the 80th UNGA session, Italian PM will not attend this year’s meeting
Multiple pro-Palestinian users, based on their past posts, across social media platforms have been sharing a video since September 23, 2026, allegedly showing Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni criticising Israel at the ongoing 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York. However, the clip is old, from her speech during the 80th UNGA session in 2025.
The 81st UNGA Session opened in New York on September 8, 2026. The high-level General Debate, considered the highlight of the annual gathering, commenced on September 22. More than 150 heads of state and government addressed the UNGA over the week, outlining their positions on pressing global issues ranging from peace and security to climate change and sustainable development.
While traditionally a close ally of Israel, Italy recently suspended the renewal of a defence agreement, reflecting growing unease over the escalation. At the same time, Italy has supported efforts to secure global energy routes and protect maritime trade amid disruptions caused by the conflict.
On September 23, an X user, who appears to be pro-Palestinian based on its past posts, shared a clip that allegedly shows Meloni delivering a speech at the United States session.
The caption of the post read, “Italian Prime Minister Meloni: ‘I am accusing Israel of crossing the red line, I condemn the massacre of Palestinian civilians, and I am announcing that Italy will support European sanctions against Israel.“
The transcription of the viral video translates: “The reaction to an aggression must always respect the principle of proportionality. It is valid for individuals, it is valid for states, and Israel has exceeded that limit with a large-scale war that is involving the Palestinian civilian population beyond measure. And it is on this limit that the Jewish state has ended up breaking humanitarian norms and causing a massacre among civilians.”
She further said, “A choice that Italy has repeatedly called unacceptable, which will lead to our favourable vote on some of the sanctions proposed by the European Commission towards Israel. Italy is, and will be, there for anyone willing to work on a serious plan for the release of hostages, a permanent ceasefire, the exclusion of Hamas from any government dynamics in Palestine, the gradual withdrawal of Israel from Gaza, the commitment of the international community in the management of the next phase of the ceasefire, up to the realisation of the two-state prospect.”
Another user shared the same clip with the same caption, gaining 218,000 views.
The same video was posted by another pro-Palestinian account with the same caption, accumulating 245,000 views.
Another pro-Palestinian user shared the same clip with the following caption: “‘I accuse Netanyahu of crossing all limits, disregarding the principle of proportionality, provoking a breach of humanitarian norms, and causing a massacre of Palestinian civilians. Italy considers this absolutely unacceptable and will vote in favour of European sanctions against Israel.’
"Excellent speech by Italy’s Prime Minister, Giorgia Meloni, at the United Nations General Assembly. Netanyahu the terrorist has no one left; he is increasingly alone and cornered. The criminal must be stopped, tried, and condemned for his crimes against humanity.” The post further wrote.
Another user shared the same video with the following caption, “I accuse Israel of crossing the red line, I condemn the massacre of Palestinian civilians, and I declare that Italy will support European sanctions against Israel.“ (Giorgia Meloni, Prime Minister of Italy) Even a woman of the FAR RIGHT having a moment of lucidity.”
Several other users also shared the clip across Instagram , Facebook , LinkedIn, and X, as can be seen here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , and here ; collectively accumulating 187,300 views.
A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to its high virality and keen public interest in the ongoing 81st General Assembly of the United Nations in New York.
A keyword search yielded several mainstream international media outlets, such as The Governance Post , Fox News , The Economic Times , Deutsche Welle , and First Post , reporting that PM Meloni will not attend this year’s high-level meeting of UNGA, citing a busy schedule.
Reports further said this will be the first time in around 15 years that Italy’s prime minister will not attend the UNGA’s annual high-level meeting. Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani will represent Italy instead.
Furthermore, the Italian government’s official website published a video message by PM Meloni for a high-level education event held on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly. The video shows Meloni addressing the event remotely rather than attending it in person.
A report by The Sun , a Nigerian media outlet, also said Meloni delivered a video presentation at the event, where Italy and Nigeria co-hosted an initiative on global education financing.
A reverse image search conducted to trace the source of the video yielded a similar video of PM Meloni speaking at the podium of UNGA, shared by the official YouTube channel of the United Nations on Sep 25, 2025.
The video was titled: “Italy - President Addresses United Nations General Debate, 80th Session”, which shows the video is from UNGA’s 80th session in 2025.
The viral video starts at the 3:47-minute mark of the original speech.
However, the portion from the 4:23-minute mark to the 5:25-minute mark, in which Meloni condemns Hamas, has been cropped out. The viral video then resumes with footage appearing immediately after the omitted portion.
The transcription of the cropped part is as follows: “But we do not side with those who heap all the blame for what is happening in Gaza and Israel, because it was Hamas that unleashed the war."
"It is Hamas that could end the suffering of Palestinians by immediately releasing all the hostages. It is Hamas that seems intent on thriving on the suffering of the people it claims to represent. Israel must free itself from the trap of this war. It must do so for the history of the Jewish people, for its democracy, for the innocent, and for the universal values of the free world of which it is part. And to end the war, concrete solutions are needed. Peace is not built only with appeals or with ideological proclamations embraced with enthusiasm by those who in truth do not want peace."
"Peace is built with patience, with courage, with reasonableness. The children of Gaza, like those Italy is proudly receiving and treating in its hospitals, are asking for answers that can improve their condition. And to that we are committed.”
The same speech was reported by other UN websites such as UN General Debate and UN Web TV .
The claim that a viral video shows Italian PM Giorgia Meloni criticising Israel during the ongoing UNGA 81 session is false .
The video is old, from PM Meloni’s speech during the 80th UNGA session in 2025. Moreover, Meloni will not attend this year’s UNGA meeting.

title: China s Zhang wins record seventh Asian Games swimming gold
description: The 19 year old clocks 3 41 28 in the 400m freestyle
content:
The 19-year-old clocks 3:41.28 in the 400m freestyle
Chinese teenager Zhang Zhanshuo won a record seventh swimming gold at the Asian Games on Friday and said it had been the "perfect conclusion" to his week in Tokyo.
The 19-year-old wrapped up a scintillating campaign with victory in the 400m freestyle in a Games-record 3min 41.28sec.
No swimmer had previously won seven golds in one Games.
Japan's Rikako Ikee won six in Jakarta in 2018 before China's Zhang Yufei matched her achievement in Hangzhou five years later.
Zhang Zhanshuo went one better and said he was "calmer than I imagined I would be".
"The moment I touched the wall was probably the most exciting," said the towering teenager, who stands 198cm (6ft 6in).
"It was also my final race of the competition. Today feels like a perfect conclusion."
Zhang also won individual golds in the 200m, 800m and 1,500m freestyle events, as well as three relays.
He was far too hot for the 400m freestyle field to handle, coming home 4.27sec ahead of Japan's silver-medallist Kazushi Imafuku.
He sat on the line divider after the race and slowly counted off all seven medals he had won on his fingers.
Zhang now has the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and world records in his sights.
"I think the most important thing is to stay grounded and focused, because the Asian Games are not my ultimate goal," he said.
"I need to face my shortcomings honestly and recognise the gap between myself and the world's best athletes."
It was another successful night in the pool for China, who won five of the day's seven finals.
They topped the overall swimming medal table with 30 golds. Japan were a distant second with seven.
Li Bingjie won her fifth gold of the Games, in the women's 800m freestyle, while Zhang Yufei picked up her fourth in the 50m butterfly.
There was success for Taiwan with their first men's swimming gold in Asian Games history.
Wang Kuan-hung came home to win the 200m butterfly in a time of 1min 55.05sec, pipping China's Xu Fang to the line.
"It feels unreal," said the 24-year-old.
"I'm very happy and grateful for this achievement."
Japanese teenager Shin Ohashi failed to claim a hat-trick of golds, one night after smashing the world record in winning the 200m breaststroke.
The 17-year-old finished third in the 50m breaststroke, 0.33sec behind gold-medallist Qin Haiyang of China.
"To be perfectly honest, I thought it was impossible to get gold," said Ohashi, who also won 100m breaststroke gold this week after a dead heat with China's Dong Zhihao.
"I was aiming for second but I lost out on that by 0.02sec, so I'm not happy."
Ohashi's success this week has marked him out as the man to beat at the LA Olympics, where he could face French superstar Leon Marchand.
His new 200m breaststroke world record of 2min 04.83sec sliced more than half a second off the previous mark.
Japan's Kodai Nishiono won the men's 200m backstroke, while China claimed their final gold in the women's 4x100m medley relay.

title: Alia Bhatt backed  Don   t be shy  offers a glossy new take on coming of age romance
description: Hindi campus drama puts four young actors at the centre of a story about friendship  first love and finding your place
content:
Hindi campus drama puts four young actors at the centre of a story about friendship, first love and finding your place
Alia Bhatt is backing a new generation of actors with Don’t Be Shy , a Hindi coming-of-age film that takes audiences into the familiar but complicated world of college friendships, first love and figuring out who you are.
Written and directed by Sreeti Mukerji, the film is produced by Alia and Shaheen Bhatt and stars Aarushi Bajaj, Piyush Khati, Bianca Arora and Ansh Duggal in the lead roles. The film began streaming on Amazon Prime Video on September 25.
Bhatt announced the release on her Instagram Story, writing: “Our little film, our core four and our amazing director… all yours from tonight.” The message put the spotlight on the film’s four young leads and Mukerji as the movie made its way to audiences.
At the centre of Don’t Be Shy is 20-year-old Shyamili “Shy” Das, played by Bajaj, who enters college convinced that she has her life and future completely mapped out. But college quickly proves less predictable than she imagined.
Her carefully planned existence gives way to first love, close friendships, heartbreak and unexpected complications, forcing Shy to confront the gap between the life she thought she wanted and the person she is actually becoming.
Piyush Khati plays Mayank, Bianca Arora plays Tara and Ansh Duggal plays Dhruv, forming the film’s central group as Shy’s college life becomes increasingly messy and unpredictable.
Variety India places Don’t Be Shy within a recognisable international campus-romance tradition, describing it as having the sharp social satire of Mean Girls , the modern charm of The Kissing Booth and the sensibilities of Off-Campus .
The publication also notes that the film ticks many of the familiar coming-of-age boxes, including “awkward adolescent romance, inevitable heartbreak, and a final-act realisation where the protagonist tries to mend broken ties with family and friends”.
But Variety also takes issue with the film’s reliance on those familiar conventions. Its review describes the campus clichés as heavy, pointing to characters who fit recognisable archetypes — from wealthy elitists and the warm, loving Das family to the stereotypical college counsellor, the nerd crushing on the popular girl, the new girl and the cheating boyfriend.
Where Don’t Be Shy distinguishes itself is in putting relatively new actors at the centre of the story.
Rather than relying on a cast of established Bollywood stars to play college students, the film allows Bajaj, Khati, Arora and Duggal to carry its central friendships and romances.
Variety notes that some of the casting does not necessarily correspond literally to the characters’ ages, but instead reflects a familiar convention of American coming-of-age films, where actors can be older than the young characters they portray.
That choice also gives the film a slightly heightened, lived-in quality: the campus is less a documentary depiction of college life and more a colourful backdrop for the emotional chaos of growing up.
For Bhatt, meanwhile, the project is another move into producing stories that give new performers and filmmakers a platform.
The Hollywood Reporter has previously highlighted her expanding work as a producer and her interest in supporting newer creative voices.
For Mukerji, Don’t Be Shy marks an opportunity to put a distinctly Hindi spin on a genre audiences around the world already know well.
The result, as Variety ’s review suggests, is a film that embraces many of the conventions of the campus rom-com rather than trying to completely reinvent them, while giving its four young leads the chance to become the new faces audiences associate with the genre.
Meanwhile, the first look at Sanjay Leela Bhansali’s upcoming epic romantic drama Love & War , featuring Bhatt alongside Ranbir Kapoor and Vicky Kaushal, was also unveiled.
Gulf News reported that the official poster revealed Bhatt in a “cabaret-inspired avatar, seated on a chair in a dramatic slit skirt and elaborate headpiece. A rich, retro-styled backdrop complements her glamorous look, offering a glimpse into the distinctive world Bhansali has created for the film”.
The production company also revealed further details on its social media account.
Don’t Be Shy is now streaming on Amazon Prime Video, while Love & War is expected to release on January 21, 2027.

title: European football leagues push for FIFA changes
description: They say major initiatives should undergo independent assessments before being put to a decision
content:
They say major initiatives should undergo independent assessments before being put to a decision.
The four main European football leagues -- the English Premier League, Spain's La Liga, Italy's Serie A and Germany's Bundesliga -- called on Friday for a reform of FIFA.
The sport's governing body has been mired in crisis since the revelation of a plan, since shelved, to create a commercial company FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would be open to private investors.
"Fundamental governance reform is essential to restore clear constitutional boundaries within FIFA, including confidence that individual disciplinary matters remain demonstrably insulated from political interference," the four leagues wrote in a statement sent to AFP.
"We are speaking up together, as founding members of European Leagues and the World Leagues Association, because we understand how FIFA’s relentless expansionism affects everyone."
The statement comes just days after FIFA president Gianni Infantino -- who has come under fire since the FFE plan to bring private investment into the men's and women's World Cups -- proposed "a consultation" of the national federations in order to reform the body’s governance.
"The FIFA president has now acknowledged the need for reform, but it is not enough for surface-level, process changes to be explored in the aftermath of FFE," stated the four main European leagues, who went on to describe the project as "one of the biggest abuses of power in FIFA’s history".
The four leagues, however, steered away from putting all the blame on Infantino's shoulders.
"FIFA’s governance problem goes far beyond the role of one individual," they said.
They propose the creation of a permanent body representing national associations, leagues, clubs and players, from across men’s and women’s football.
"This new body must be fully informed about new initiatives and have a meaningful role in FIFA’s decision-making process," they added.
"Any major FIFA proposal must begin with a clearly defined rationale, supporting evidence and an independent assessment, published in advance of any decision, covering players, clubs, leagues and supporters, and evaluating the impact on all stakeholders and the development of football."
They also called for the protection of FIFA’s role "as regulator and guardian of the game" from its commercial activities.
The four leagues put a call out for candidates for the FIFA presidency who will endorse their principles "within the first 100 days of the next presidential mandate".
For now, Infantino is the sole candidate for the FIFA presidential election scheduled for March 18, 2027, with the submission of candidacies open until November 18.
UEFA, alongside North American body CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), issued a no-holds-barred joint letter against Infantino in August.
"Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding -- or demanding -- power to be held," they wrote.
However, Infantino is not without friends -- 2034 World Cup hosts Saudi Arabia came out in support last month, with African football's governing body CAF and South America's CONMEBOL also supportive.

title: Xi calls for new chapter in China US ties at White House dinner
description: Xi urges Beijing  Washington to act as responsible powers  keep competition within bounds  build strategic stability
content:
Urges Beijing, Washington to act as responsible powers, keep competition within bounds, build strategic stability
Chinese President Xi Jinping has called for a new chapter in China-US relations, urging Beijing and Washington to act as “responsible major countries,” manage their differences and build a constructive relationship of strategic stability.
Speaking at a state dinner hosted by US President Donald Trump at the White House on Thursday, Xi said his talks with Trump had produced “sincere and in-depth exchanges” and a common understanding on a number of issues, providing fresh strategic guidance for the relationship between the world’s two largest economies.
The Chinese leader said the two countries should strengthen communication, cooperate with sincerity and coexist peacefully rather than allow competition to spiral into confrontation.
“China and the United States must act as responsible major countries, meet the expectations of our peoples, keep pace with the trend of our times, and explore a new approach for major countries to get along with each other,” Xi said according to a text of the Chinese president’s speech released by Xinhua news agency.
The White House state visit, which began with an unusually high-profile welcome by Trump, marked a significant moment in engagement between Beijing and Washington. The US president personally received Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, at Joint Base Andrews before hosting a formal arrival ceremony at the White House. The visit is Xi’s first to the White House in more than a decade.
President Donald J. Trump and First Lady Melania Trump greet President Xi Jinping of China and Madame Peng Liyuan upon their arrival in Washington, D.C., ahead of the state visit at the White House. pic.twitter.com/nm2vGonChM
Xi recalled that he and Trump had agreed during Trump’s May visit to China to work towards a “constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability”.
He described the reciprocal visits by the two presidents within less than six months as unprecedented in the history of bilateral ties and said the two leaders had maintained communication through multiple channels while working to steer the relationship towards a more stable course.
At the White House arrival ceremony earlier on Thursday, Xi said he was ready to work with Trump to “steer the giant ship” of China-US relations towards the future.
. @POTUS salutes as the Star-Spangled Banner is played during the official state welcome ceremony 🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/NBbio4sbX3
He said cooperation between Beijing and Washington could not resolve every problem facing the world, but without cooperation between the two countries, many global problems would be difficult to solve.
Xi also called for closer coordination among government departments dealing with foreign affairs, economic affairs, financial cooperation, law enforcement and people-to-people exchanges.
One of the central themes of Xi’s remarks was the need to manage strategic competition without allowing it to turn into conflict.
China and the United States, he said, did not need to avoid discussing competition, but competition should be “healthy” and remain within bounds. “It should be a race of catching up with one another, not a wrestle in which one either wins or loses,” Xi said.
He urged both countries to maintain a firm commitment to avoiding conflict and confrontation and said the two militaries should maintain regular dialogue and improve mechanisms for crisis communication and prevention.
. @POTUS and @FLOTUS welcome Chinese President Xi Jinping and Madame Peng to the United States pic.twitter.com/RPCM1ofEql
Xi also argued that the so-called Thucydides Trap — the historical tendency for rivalry between an established power and a rising power to lead to conflict — could be overcome. “We can certainly find the right path for our two great countries to get along on this planet we both call home,” he said.
The emphasis on military communication comes as Beijing and Washington continue to navigate disagreements over security, technology, trade and other strategic issues. Xi’s remarks placed crisis management alongside economic and diplomatic engagement as key components of the relationship.
Xi also highlighted the economic interdependence between the two countries and called for expanding the areas in which they can cooperate.
China, he said, would keep its doors open to American businesses and welcomed US companies seeking to invest and operate in the Chinese market.
At the same time, he called for Chinese companies to receive fair treatment in the United States. “Working together, we can lengthen the list of cooperation and shorten the list of issues,” Xi said.
Trade and investment have remained among the most sensitive aspects of the relationship as Beijing and Washington seek to manage years of tariff disputes and disagreements over technology, supply chains and strategic industries.
US President Donald Trump holds a binder as he stands next to Chinese President Xi Jinping before Xi delivers a speech during a state dinner at the White House in Washington, DC, US. Photo: Reuters
The summit was therefore closely watched for indications of whether the recent improvement in bilateral engagement could translate into concrete economic cooperation. Analysts have described the meeting as an effort to consolidate a fragile thaw while acknowledging that deep disagreements remain.
Artificial intelligence also featured prominently in Xi’s remarks, reflecting the growing importance of the technology to the economic and strategic competition between the two countries.
Xi said China and the United States were both leading nations in AI and had both the capability and responsibility to develop and manage the technology for the benefit of humanity. He called for ensuring that AI development remained under human control and served the well-being of people.
. @FLOTUS hosts Madame Peng for a cultural visit at the Smithsonian Museum of Asian Art pic.twitter.com/anHkakwSIk
The comments come as Washington and Beijing compete for technological leadership while simultaneously confronting questions over AI safety, regulation, computing power, data and access to advanced technology.
Xi’s call for cooperation suggests Beijing wants AI to become an area where competition can be managed through dialogue rather than another front in the broader strategic rivalry.
Law enforcement and people-to-people links
Xi also proposed expanding cooperation in counternarcotics and law enforcement and called for greater people-to-people exchanges.
He suggested that the two countries could increase direct flights to facilitate travel and trade, linking stronger human contact with the broader effort to stabilise bilateral relations.
The Chinese president placed particular emphasis on the role of ordinary citizens in sustaining ties between the two countries.
Recalling the long history of interaction between Chinese and American peoples, he referred to trade links dating back more than two centuries, cooperation during World War II and the “Ping-Pong diplomacy” that helped reopen bilateral exchanges more than five decades ago.
. @FLOTUS and Madame Peng listen to a children's choir during the cultural visit https://t.co/xZpS69faxu pic.twitter.com/XcIjCHDmfG
He also recalled cooperation during the war against Japanese militarism, including the Hump air route over the Himalayas and instances in which Chinese civilians and soldiers rescued American pilots.
Xi said the friendship forged during that period should continue “through the generations”.
He cited environmental cooperation and other people-to-people exchanges as examples of how practical cooperation could create lasting bonds beyond government-to-government relations.
100,000 young Americans invited to China
Xi said the future of China-US relations ultimately depended on younger generations and announced an invitation for 100,000 young Americans to visit China over the next five years for exchanges and study.
“The hope of the China-US relationship lies in our people, and its future lies with the young,” Xi said.
An epic White House flyover! pic.twitter.com/qyHQ26Ss9h
The initiative is intended to increase direct contact between younger Americans and Chinese society at a time when relations between the two countries have increasingly been defined by strategic rivalry.
Xi argued that greater exchanges could strengthen public support for cooperation and provide a foundation for more stable relations in the future.
In a symbolic gesture accompanying the broader diplomatic message, Xi announced that two giant pandas would soon arrive at Zoo Atlanta. The pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, are expected to become new “envoys of friendship” between the Chinese and American peoples.
Panda exchanges have long been associated with Chinese diplomacy and have periodically featured in US-China relations. The new arrivals will return pandas to Zoo Atlanta after the previous pair was sent back to China in 2024.
. @POTUS and @FLOTUS join President Xi and Madame Peng in observing a silent drill platoon review from the Blue Room balcony pic.twitter.com/O6hfCtIgRI
Xi’s announcement offered a softer dimension to a summit otherwise dominated by questions of trade, technology, security and strategic competition.
At the state dinner, Xi sought to frame the current moment as another historic juncture in the relationship.
He said Trump had pledged to “make America great again”, while China was pursuing national rejuvenation through modernisation. “These two goals are both ambitious and can surely be mutually reinforcing,” Xi said.
He urged the two sides to “join hands and move forward side by side”, arguing that the interests of the Chinese and American peoples could provide a basis for cooperation despite differences between their governments.
Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump speak during a state dinner at the White House in Washington, DC, US. Photo: Reuters
The Chinese president ended his toast by raising his glass to the health of Trump and First Lady Melania Trump, the prosperity of China and the United States, and the friendship between the two peoples.
The carefully choreographed state visit underscored the importance both governments attach to managing their relationship even as major differences persist. Trump’s decision to give Xi an elaborate welcome and host him for a state dinner reflected the high political and diplomatic significance attached to the summit.
For Beijing, Xi’s message was that strategic competition with Washington need not become a zero-sum struggle. For Washington, the challenge remains balancing competition with a relationship that has significant consequences for global trade, technology, security and economic stability.
Xi’s appeal for a “constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability” therefore represents not an end to competition but an effort to establish mechanisms through which the two powers can compete while avoiding conflict.
Whether that vision can be translated into sustained cooperation will depend on how Beijing and Washington handle the disagreements that have repeatedly strained their relationship.
For now, Xi has presented dialogue, economic engagement, military communication and people-to-people exchanges as the principal tools for keeping the “giant ship” of China-US relations on a steady course.

title: Inside the UN walkout  Who left and who stayed for Netanyahu   s speech
description: Nearly 70 delegations left the chamber as Israeli PM began speaking  while the US  UK  France and others remained
content:
Nearly 70 delegations left the chamber as Israeli PM began speaking, while the US, UK, France and others remained
Delegations from nearly 70 countries walked out of the United Nations General Assembly hall or left their seats vacant Thursday as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began his address, staging a mass protest over Israel’s genocide in Gaza and its attacks across the region.
An Anadolu review of footage from the 81st UN General Assembly showed dozens of delegations leaving the chamber together after Netanyahu approached the podium.
Some countries left a single representative or junior diplomat behind, while others did not attend the address.
Turkiye, Palestine, Tunisia, Syria, Algeria, Yemen, Egypt, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Iran, Qatar, Lebanon, Malaysia, Indonesia and Kuwait were among the countries whose representatives joined the protest.
Delegations from Spain, Brazil, Peru, Cuba, Nigeria, Ghana, Libya, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Oman, Niger, Madagascar, Botswana, the Bahamas, Antigua and Barbuda, Cabo Verde and several other countries also walked out or remained absent.
Dozens of UN delegates walked out as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took the stage amid stark divisions over the war in Iran, Gaza's future and illegal settler violence. pic.twitter.com/Jvwe1lB8L8
The protest came amid continuing international condemnation of Israel’s assault on Gaza, its policies in the occupied West Bank and its attacks on Lebanon and Syria .
A UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry concluded in September 2025 that Israel had committed genocide against Palestinians in Gaza. Israel has rejected the finding.
Netanyahu is also the subject of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant issued on November 21, 2024, for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity committed in the Gaza Strip.
Representatives of the United States, Germany, Argentina, Hungary, Serbia, Ukraine, Czechia and Greece remained in the General Assembly hall during Netanyahu’s address.
The United Kingdom, France, Ireland, Belgium and Norway, whose relations with Israel have faced increasing tensions over Gaza, also kept representatives in the chamber, as did the European Union delegation.
Read: Macron denounces Trump's Gaza diplomacy as spectacle of shame
China, which has repeatedly criticised Israel’s actions in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, was represented by a single diplomat.
Delegations from the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain, which normalised relations with Israel under the Abraham Accords, also remained in their seats.
Other countries represented during the speech included Australia, Austria, Canada, Portugal, Poland, Denmark, Romania, Slovakia, Estonia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Iceland, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Mexico, Kenya and El Salvador.
The walkout left large sections of the General Assembly chamber visibly empty as Netanyahu continued his address.

Head coach Solano urges Shaheens to embrace stern challenge
Pakistan begin their FIFA ASEAN Cup journey with a Thailand outing on Saturday with head coach Nolberto Solano urging his players to use the tournament as a test against some of Asia’s stronger sides. The Group B match at Bandung’s Si Jalak Harupat Stadium kicks-off at 2pm PST and marks Pakistan’s first appearance in an official FIFA tournament. Pakistan will also face the Philippines on September 29 before completing their group campaign against Vietnam in Jakarta on October 2. “We want to use this opportunity to test ourselves against teams like Thailand, Philippines and Vietnam,” Solano told a pre-match news conference. “It’s an honour to be here and we know it will be a tough competition.” The Peruvian coach said Pakistan were taking a gradual approach as they look to develop as a national team. “We are slowly growing, we try to go step by step,” Solano said. “We will try to prove ourselves as a national team and see how far we can go in this competition.” Pakistan arrive after winning the Diamond Jubilee International Tournament in the Maldives in June, their first standalone football tournament title in 74 years. Captain Abdullah Iqbal said the tournament represented an opportunity for Pakistan’s players to measure themselves against higher-ranked oppositions. “It is a great opportunity for us to compete against teams at another level,” Abdullah said. “We will try to give our best.” Pakistan completed their preparations with an official training session on Friday, with Azerbaijan-based defender Easah Suliman joining the squad. title: JI to set up 25 protest camps across Karachi over power woes  petroleum levy from tomorrow
description: Welcomes the government   s decision to terminate agreements with five IPPs
content:
Welcomes the government’s decision to terminate agreements with five IPPs
Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) Karachi chief Munim Zafar on Friday announced the establishment of 25 demonstration camps across Karachi from tomorrow onwards to protest against the city's power woes and the petroleum levy.
A day earlier, K-Electric top brass shied away from a call for a meeting at the Sindh Assembly. The company's absence did little to cool lawmakers' anger over Karachi's persistent power cuts, and instead the no-show pushed a special house committee closer to punitive action, with possible privilege proceedings and even arrest on the cards.
Speaking at a press conference at Idara Noor-e-Haq in Karachi, Zafar criticised the government’s failure to address the power disruption issues in the provincial capital as well as its insistence on collecting the petroleum levy from the already burdened citizens.
The JI Karachi emir described the levy as an “extortion tax” and a “burden” on ordinary citizens. He blamed it for worsening inflation and the rising cost of living in the country and called on the government to do away with it.
Addressing the gathering, Zafar claimed that the petroleum levy had made it increasingly difficult for people to afford basic necessities, including food, rent, electricity bills and education for their children.
He alleged that Rs1,566 billion had been collected from the public through the levy during the last financial year, describing the amount as an excessive burden on citizens.
According to Zafar, workers, farmers and motorcyclists were among those bearing the impact of the levy.
Read: Oil slides as US-Iran truce hopes outweigh Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
“A motorcyclist consuming approximately one litre of petrol a day pays around Rs131 in petroleum levy,” he claimed during the press conference. He further argued that Pakistan had approximately 25 million motorcycle users and argued that a significant portion of the levy imposed on petroleum products had no direct connection with an ordinary citizen.
The JI leader reminisced that his party had organised protests against the petroleum levy by blocking roads at 710 locations across the country as part of the campaign to raise awareness of the issue. He also said sit-ins were held nationwide on August 16.
Zafar reiterated his call for the immediate withdrawal of the petroleum levy to provide relief to the citizens bogged down by inflation.
Moving on to the power sector, Zafar assailed the policy regarding independent power producers (IPPs), alleging that the government was paying billions of rupees to companies despite some plants generating little to no electricity.
He welcomed the government’s decision to terminate agreements with five IPPs, but called for further action to address the capacity payments issue.
Read more: K-Electric faces assembly heat
“Consumers are being forced to pay for electricity generation capacity even when some power plants were not producing electricity,” he highlighted, adding that this should not be tolerated.
The JI Karachi chief also criticised K-Electric over prolonged power outages in the city.
He alleged that some areas were experiencing up to 18 hours of “load-shedding”, describing the situation as a collective punishment for Karachi’s residents.
Zafar claimed that only 2-3 per cent of consumers were not paying their electricity bills and argued that K-Electric should take action against those consumers rather than disconnecting electricity to entire neighbourhoods.
He said prolonged power outages were causing difficulties for children, elderly people and women.
He called on the government to take immediate measures to end load-shedding and provide relief to Karachi’s residents.
Two days ago, JI chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman announced the suspension of the party's train march toward Islamabad at the request of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. The party has repeatedly called on the government to ease the burden on citizens by abolishing the petroleum levy and reducing the interest rate to pull down inflation.

title: Nadia Khan s gym questions overshadow Parishae Adnan s NYFW achievement
description: Designer discusses self expression  sustainability and the craft behind her New York Fashion Week collection
content:
Designer discusses self-expression, sustainability and the craft behind her New York Fashion Week collection
TV host Nadia Khan faced criticism over her interview with designer Parishae Adnan, with viewers questioning why a conversation following the designer’s New York Fashion Week achievement repeatedly focused on her clothing, gym videos and whether her parents approved of her choices.
Parishae recently appeared on Rise and Shine , co-hosted by Khan and Zohaib Hassan on 365 News , following her appearance at New York Fashion Week, where she closed Flying Solo’s showcase with her collection Second Skin . The collection centred on sustainability and the reworking of existing garments, bringing Pakistani craftsmanship and fashion heritage to an international runway.
Yet rather than keeping the conversation primarily focused on the collection or the technical aspects of her work, the interview repeatedly moved towards Parishae’s personal choices — including how she dresses, her gym videos, her boundaries and whether her parents object to her appearance.
Despite the direction of the conversation, Parishae remained composed and continued trying to bring the discussion back to fashion, creativity and the reasons behind her choices. “It is expressive, whether that is to be in the gym, dressing a certain way, doing your hair or whatever someone does,” Parishae said.
“Humans are multifaceted. You can’t take one thing and run. We are all multidimensional. You might like cooking or running, so I don’t put myself in a label either. What is more important is people don’t define us,” she added.
The discussion around Parishae's appearance became one of the most striking parts of the interview.
Khan questioned Parishae about the way she dresses, including references to her dressing “like a man”, and asked her to show off her muscles before the conversation moved towards the broader question of how she expresses herself.
Parishae resisted the idea that one element of her appearance should be used to define her. For her, clothing is simply another form of expression.
She also described herself as having “always been a rebellious kid” and later added, “I am a very religious person too by the way”, after the hosts continued to question her way of dressing.
The discussion eventually moved towards boundaries and whether they can be defined universally. “I don’t think anything is rigid. Art is subjective. What is your boundary isn’t always mine or someone else’s,” Parishae said.
It was a point that became particularly relevant when Khan returned to the subject of Parishae’s gym videos.
“Being in society, the gym videos you make, there is criticism, so does that not worry your parents?” Khan asked.
Parishae's response, however, moved the conversation away from what she wears and towards why she shares her fitness journey publicly.
“Yes, maybe, but I think safety is a concern. But besides that, what gets me up and takes me to the gym is when I get messages in my inbox from all those girls, women, even women who get inspired by seeing it and go to the gym themselves. That’s a big thing,” she said.
She also explained that representation was something she had lacked growing up. “When I was young, I didn’t have anyone like that to show me I can have those genetics or who is a close Pakistani I can follow who has body-ideal.”
For her, sharing the journey is therefore not simply about displaying her own body or lifestyle. It is also about showing other people that such a journey is possible.
The repeated return to her gym clothes nevertheless stood in contrast to the reason she had been invited onto the programme in the first place. However, Parishae used the opportunity to talk about her work.
One of the recurring assumptions Parishae addressed was the idea that coming from a prominent fashion family meant her career was simply given to her.
Parishae is the daughter of designers Amir Adnan and Huma Adnan, but she explained that fashion was not initially the career she chose. “Never once have my mother or father told me to take on this career. I did everything besides this field at first. Consulting, business, hospitality, management, even hospital care during COVID.”
Her eventual return to fashion, she explained, changed the way she viewed the profession. “When you do the full circle and come back, it is a different kind of love for craft.”
Parishae also addressed the “nepo-baby” label, offering a different perspective on children entering family businesses.
“When I was growing up, people used to call me ‘nepo-baby’, but I thought about it in the past 10-15 days. If you look back at the old days, these kids were called ‘apprentices’. So going from one generation to the next is by putting their kids into the business.” “I feel like this has been my journey too. It was not handed to me, but I grew up in clothes and sewing.”
For her, being raised around fashion did not mean automatically inheriting a creative identity. “Even education-wise, my father told me that you can’t teach creativity, it is just naturally there. It shows more when you work on it and ‘do it’ rather than learning it.”
A bigger conversation about Pakistani fashion
The interview also offered Parishae an opportunity to discuss what she believes is missing from conversations around fashion and other creative industries in Pakistan.
She questioned why discussions about creative work in Pakistan can sometimes focus on the spectacle surrounding it rather than the technical work involved.
“We were talking on boundaries. We often talk about art and not these things and we are here on TV discussing boundaries. I wanted to make an interesting point. I believe going to NYFW is a big accomplishment, but the bigger thing was that whatever appreciation you get from there was more technical, but here there is not that kind of technicality discussed.”
Parishae compared the discussion around fashion to the way acting is often treated. “For example, when acting is discussed, people don’t discuss it as a craft. Over there, same things are discussed, like in my line of work: strutting, stitching, line of flow. If you sit in craft, you have to know it.”
Her comments highlighted a broader frustration: that audiences can spend more time discussing personalities, appearances and spectacle than the actual craft behind creative work.
The collection behind the NYFW appearance
Parishae's New York Fashion Week appearance itself was rooted in a concept she had explored previously, which she said was not discussed during the interview. Fans subsequently criticised the hosts for what they viewed as a lack of research.
“This is not a new concept. I did a show like this in 2020 in Pakistan, which I got a lot of criticism for. Very similar work. Concept, philosophy, technique, structure — almost all identical.”
She said she had previously presented the same philosophy and approach in Pakistan, where the concept of reusing old clothing was not necessarily understood in the same way. “People here in this society didn’t understand the concept of reusing old clothes.”
For Parishae, this is particularly relevant as thrifting and reuse become increasingly important to younger generations.
To conclude, she said: “In our generation, thrifting culture is important too because we teach this generation and next that we can’t make old stuff again how it is.”
The criticism surrounding the interview largely stemmed from the contrast between the occasion and the direction of the questioning.
Parishae was appearing after taking Second Skin to New York Fashion Week and closing Flying Solo’s showcase. Yet some of the most prominent questions directed at her centred on what she wears to the gym and whether her parents are concerned about it.
The exchange subsequently drew criticism on social media. Parishae herself shared clips of her reactions to the interview, while her mother, Huma, described the questions as “uncalled for”.
What makes the interview particularly notable is that Parishae did not respond by turning the exchange into an argument. Instead, she continued answering even when the conversation moved into questions about her appearance, boundaries and gym videos, trying to explain the thinking behind her choices.
And when the discussion moved towards fashion, she offered a detailed account of craft, sustainability and the technical aspects of her work. For Parishae, that meant not being reduced to a designer with famous parents, a woman who works out, someone who dresses a certain way, or even a designer who has just appeared at NYFW.
She was making a case for being seen as all of those things at once. And perhaps that was the conversation worth having in the first place.

title: Israeli patrol enters southern Syria  opens fire  state media
description: Israeli army planned move comes despite June framework deal with Lebanon that provides for gradual Israeli withdrawal
content:
Israeli forces perform incursion into Kfar Shuba in southern Lebanon, surrounding farm with shepherds
An Israeli military patrol entered the Wadi al-Ruqad area in the western countryside of Syria's southern Daraa province on Friday and opened fire, Syrian state media reported.
An Israeli patrol "opened fire indiscriminately during its incursion into the Wadi al-Ruqad area, causing tension among residents," Alikhbariah TV reported.
No casualties were immediately reported.
Wadi al-Ruqad lies within the Yarmouk Basin in western Daraa and has witnessed repeated Israeli incursions in recent months, including one on September 18 that ended with the detention of a shepherd.
The incursion comes amid escalating Israeli violations of Syrian territory, which President Ahmad al-Sharaa addressed Wednesday in his speech before the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.
Read: Syria, Kuwait condemn Netanyahu’s incursion into Mount Hermon in occupied Syrian territory
Al-Sharaa said Israel had carried out around 500 airstrikes and artillery attacks, more than 1,200 incursions and around 300 arrests and detentions since late 2024.
He rejected attempts to impose a fait accompli, reaffirmed Syria's commitment to the 1974 Separation of Forces Agreement and called for Israeli forces to withdraw to the positions they held before December 8, 2024.
Israeli forces perform incursion into Kfar Shuba in southern Lebanon, surrounding farm with shepherds
An Israeli army force carried out an incursion on the outskirts of Kfar Shuba town in southern Lebanon on Friday and surrounded a farm where several shepherds were present, as Israeli strikes, artillery shelling, and gunfire targeted several areas in the south.
The Israeli force raided the Sadana area on the outskirts of Kfar Shuba in Hasbaya district and surrounded a farm belonging to the family of Ghazi Nabaa, where several shepherds were present, Lebanon's National News Agency NNA reported.
Israeli soldiers opened fire around the farm, while several artillery shells landed near the Sadana area, the agency added.
In the Arqoub area of the same district, the outskirts of Hebbariyeh came under intermittent Israeli artillery shelling, accompanied by heavy machine-gun fire and movements of Israeli military vehicles in the area.
In Nabatieh district, an Israeli drone targeted an area between the towns of Kfar Tibnit and Nabatieh al-Fawqa, while intermittent artillery shelling hit the outskirts of Kfar Tibnit.
Israeli artillery also targeted Wadi al-Hujair overnight.
In Tyre district, Israeli artillery shelling targeted the town of Majdal Zoun and nearby valleys overnight.
Earlier, the Israeli army was preparing to enter a new phase of fighting in southern Lebanon in the coming days, Israeli media reported on Friday .
The report came as the army continued its attacks in southern Lebanon, in violation of a US-brokered framework deal signed with Beirut in June.
The army will reorganise its forces in what it called the “yellow zone,” including reducing and redeploying troops stationed along the line, Israel's Channel 12 said.
In April, Tel Aviv announced it established what it calls the “yellow line” in southern Lebanon. It is an imaginary line separating an Israeli-occupied “buffer zone” from the rest of Lebanese territory, extending up to 10 km (around 6.2 miles) into Lebanon in certain sections.
Israel considers the area between the “yellow line” and the border a “security buffer zone,” while Lebanon rejects the continued presence of Israeli forces on its territory and insists on their withdrawal.
Read more: Peace in southern Lebanon remains ‘elusive’: UN mission
According to the outlet, the army is preparing to remain in the area for an extended period by establishing and completing a new line of forward positions.
The preparations also include continuing operations against what Israeli officials claim are Hezbollah members, the report said.
The Israeli offensive in Lebanon has killed at least 4,386 people, wounded 12,407 and displaced more than 1 million others since March 2, according to Lebanese authorities.
The attack comes despite the June framework deal that provides for a gradual Israeli withdrawal from occupied Lebanese territory in exchange for the deployment of the Lebanese army there and the disarmament of Hezbollah.

title: Mamdani slams  lies  in Netanyahu s UN speech  cites ICC warrant for his arrest
description: Qatar  Turkiye reject Israeli premier s accusations as delegates walk out  protesters rally in New York
content:
Qatar, Turkiye reject Israeli premier's accusations as delegates walk out, protesters rally in New York
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Thursday hit back at Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's criticisms in his United Nations General Assembly address , pointing to the international warrant seeking the visiting prime minister’s arrest.
Netanyahu’s “lies” in his UN address cannot erase the warrant for genocidal war crimes issued by the International Criminal Court (ICC), said the mayor.
“As he has done time and again, Prime Minister Netanyahu used his speech to repeat baseless lies meant to sanitise his genocide of Palestinians," Mamdani said in a statement, local media reported. "Yet no lie can change the fact that he remains the subject of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant alleging war crimes and crimes against humanity.”
In November 2024 the ICC, based in The Hague, issued arrest warrants for Netanyahu and former Israeli Defence Minister Yoav Gallant for war crimes and crimes against humanity in the Gaza Strip.
This July, Mamdani urged United States federal authorities to enforce the ICC arrest warrant for Netanyahu, acknowledging that New York City authorities lack the legal power to carry it out.
Read: UN chief says Israeli actions in occupied West Bank raising ‘spectre of ethnic cleansing'
Netanyahu mounted a forceful defence of Israel's actions in the region at the UN, seeking to counter growing international isolation ahead of elections he could lose, as dozens of delegates streamed out. The walkout underscored the competing pressures facing Netanyahu, who is battling mounting criticism abroad over the Gaza war while campaigning for reelection at home ahead of an October 27 vote .
The divisions over Israel's conduct were on display as Netanyahu began speaking, with dozens of delegates walking out in protest. He called them "moral cowards," while supporters in the gallery chanted in Hebrew: "The people of Israel live."
Netanyahu used his address to berate Mamdani for calling him a war criminal, Western European leaders for what he called succumbing to "antisemitic mobs," and to accuse both Qatar and Turkiye of spreading lies about Israel.
"You tried to stop me from coming here. You tried. You tried to silence me. Well, you can't silence me. You can't silence the truth," Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving leader, said of Mamdani. He accused Mamdani of supporting Hamas militants, something Mamdani has denied.
"To all those spreading these lies about my country and about our brave soldiers, whether they sit in this hall or in the office of the antisemitic mayor of New York, I say this: Shame on you!" Netanyahu said.
Qatar rejects Netanyahu's accusations, calls on Israel change its policies
Qatar rejected Netanyahu’s accusation that it is conducting a campaign aimed at influencing public opinion against Israel, calling the allegation an attempt to divert attention from Israel’s actions in the occupied Palestinian territories .
"We categorically reject Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s accusation, made in his address to the UN General Assembly, that the State of Qatar is conducting a campaign to influence public opinion against Israel."
"This continuing rhetoric against Qatar is nothing more than an attempt to divert attention from the attrocities committed by his government in the occupied Palestinian territories and their grave humanitarian consequence ," Foreign Ministry Spokesman Majed al-Ansari said in a statement.
He pushed back against claims that the growing criticism of Israel around the world, particularly among younger people , is the result of organised influence campaigns.
Read More: Macron denounces Trump's Gaza diplomacy as spectacle of shame
“Reducing the growing shift in global public opinion, particularly among young people, to allegations of ‘influence campaigns’ is an insult to the awareness and judgment of a generation that is witnessing, in real time and before the entire world, what is taking place on the ground and forming its views accordingly,” al-Ansari said.
He said if Netanyahu and other Israeli politicians want to change how Israel is viewed internationally, they should focus on government policies rather than blaming Qatar or other outside actors. "Attempts to hold Qatar, or anyone else, responsible for a global shift in public opinion shaped by what people themselves are witnessing are no longer persuasive," the spokesman said.
He called on Israel to change its policies, respect international law and take responsibility for its actions.
Turkiye dismisses Netanyahu's accusations as baseless
Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan's communications director dismissed Netanyahu's accusations against against Turkiye and Erdogan as baseless.
"Netanyahu’s insolent and despicable remarks targeting our president cannot obscure his massacres, the humanitarian catastrophe unfolding in Gaza, or the legal proceedings before international law," Burhanettin Duran said in a post on X.

Several hundred protesters gathered near the UN, with dozens blocking traffic and chanting, "Stop arming Israel, let Gaza live" and "Stop arming Israel, let Iran live." Police detained them.
Netanyahu was making a short visit to the US for his UN address and, unusually, without a planned meeting with US President Donald Trump, whom he praised during his speech.
"We will continue to defend our state. We will continue to win because we have no other choice. In this battle against the barbarians, we've had no greater partner than President Trump. I thank him. I thank him for his bold leadership," he said.

title: Taylor Swift drops new single    Patient Zero    about escaping a toxic relationship
description: In  Patient Zero   Swift appears to address a woman involved with a charismatic but damaging man
content:
In 'Patient Zero', Swift appears to address a woman involved with a charismatic but damaging man
Taylor Swift has released her new single Patient Zero, a track that explores escaping a toxic relationship and offering support to another woman who may be experiencing the same situation.
The 36-year-old singer released the song on Friday, September 25, as the lead single from The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore, a surprise expanded edition of her 2025 album featuring four new tracks.
In Patient Zero, Swift appears to address a woman involved with a charismatic but damaging man. Rather than simply reflecting on her own past, the song's narrator tells the woman that she understands what she is going through because she experienced the relationship herself.
Swift describes the man as someone with a "devil on his shoulder under his halo", while using the idea of toxins taking hold to describe the effect of the relationship. She then offers herself as someone the woman can turn to, saying she has already been through the same experience.
The song later makes clear that Swift's narrator had the man before eventually walking away from the relationship. The lyrics centre on recognising harmful patterns, recovering from them and helping someone else who may now be caught in the same situation.
Swift has not publicly confirmed that Patient Zero is about a particular former relationship. However, the song has already prompted fan speculation about which of her past relationships may have inspired its storyline.
The release follows several days of clues from Swift. She changed the "o" letters in her Instagram bio to zeroes, writing, "And, baby, that's sh0w business f0r y0u," before announcing the single following a countdown on her website.
The singer also teased the Patient Zero music video on September 24, revealing that it stars Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell. A 13-second preview aired on CBS Mornings, while the full video is scheduled to premiere during the MTV Video Music Awards on September 27.
Patient Zero is one of four songs featured on The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore. The expanded edition also includes Cleveland!, Pink Clouding and Babylon. Swift said the songs were written during a trip to Sweden with her longtime collaborators Max Martin and Shellback, who also worked on the original The Life of a Showgirl.
The new material comes less than a year after Swift released The Life of a Showgirl, which became a major commercial success. Patient Zero also marks her latest original release following I Knew It, I Knew You, her contribution to the Toy Story 5 soundtrack.
With its focus on toxic relationships, recovery and female solidarity, Patient Zero introduces a different perspective to Swift's latest run of new music while leaving the identity of the relationship at the centre of the song open to interpretation.

title: Margot Robbie officially changes name after 10 years of marriage to Tom Ackerley
description: The change has prompted mixed reactions from fans online with some supporting the actress while others are critical
content:
The change has prompted mixed reactions from fans online with some supporting the actress while others are critical
Margot Robbie has officially changed her surname to Ackerley, nearly a decade after marrying British film producer Tom Ackerley.
Documents published by the couple’s production company, LuckyChap Entertainment , now list the Australian actress as Margot Elise Ackerley.
However, reports suggest that she is likely to continue using Robbie professionally, the name associated with her Oscar-nominated performances in I, Tonya , Bombshell and Barbie .
The name change has prompted mixed reactions from fans on X, with some questioning why the actress chose to alter her surname while others said she would always be known as Margot Robbie.
“She can be whatever she wants, but she will always be Margot Robbie to her fans,” one fan wrote.
Another said waiting to change her name had been “good for her career”, while another asked, “I’m curious if she’ll keep the Robbie name for her professional work regardless of the name change?”
A further fan joked, “I’m sorry, but you marry a Margot Robbie or a Zendaya Coleman, you take THEIR name.”
Robbie married Ackerley in a Byron Bay ceremony in 2016. The pair first met while working on the 2014 film Suite Française , where Ackerley was an assistant director and Robbie had a supporting role.
The couple co-founded LuckyChap with Josey McNamara and Sophia Kerr in 2014. The production company has since been behind films including I, Tonya , Saltburn and Barbie .
Robbie and Ackerley welcomed their first child in 2024 and continue to balance family life with their work in the film industry.

title: Hannah Einbinder speaks out after arrest outside UN  calls Benjamin Netanyahu  butcher of Gaza

content:
The 'Hacks' star was among protesters detained while demonstrating against the Israeli PM's arrival at the UN

“If the pictures of my friends and me getting arrested in protest of Netanyahu’s shameful visit to New York draw attention to anything, let it be to the devastating genocidal war Israel is waging against the people of Palestine and Southern Lebanon — to the settler attacks, the home demolitions, the bombing of people as they sleep; to the crimes that happen every SINGLE day but garner almost no international press coverage,” she wrote.

title: Who is Taylor Swift s  Babylon  about  New song sparks theories about Joe Alwyn  Sophie Turner and more

content:
Since the song's release, fans have focused on themes of leaving home, regret, and nostalgia to identify its subject
Taylor Swift’s new song “Babylon” has prompted fan theories about who inspired its lyrics, with names including Joe Alwyn, Justin Bieber, Sophie Turner and Joe Jonas emerging in online discussions.
Released as part of The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore, “Babylon” is one of four new tracks alongside “Patient Zero”, “Cleveland!” and “Pink Clouding”.
Since its release, fans have focused on the song’s themes of leaving home, regret, relationships, and nostalgia while trying to identify its subject.
Some fans have interpreted the lyrics as potentially referencing Swift’s former relationship with Alwyn, with one Reddit user writing, “Man this song seems inspired from Joe. Benjamin Button is the son.”
Swift and Alwyn were together from 2016 until their split in 2023.
Another theory connects the song to Justin Bieber, with a fan pointing to similarities involving fame, money, relationships and family.
A separate theory links the song to Sophie Turner and Joe Jonas, with one Reddit post describing it as “Babylon: The Sophie and Joe Story”.
The song’s title also carries historical symbolism. Babylon was an ancient city on the Euphrates in what is now Iraq, and Swift uses the term as a metaphor for a life that initially appears liberating but eventually becomes restrictive.
For now, the theories remain fan interpretations rather than confirmed explanations from Swift herself.
