Fighting has intensified in recent weeks along fronts between Taiz and Lahj provinces
China helping Iran would be ‘totally unacceptable,’ Trump told Xi during visit: US ambassador
US President Donald Trump told visiting Chinese President Xi Jinping this week that Beijing providing any assistance to Iran would be “totally unacceptable,” according to the US ambassador to China.
Speaking to CNBC on Friday, David Perdue said Chinese support for Iran had been a recurring subject in US-China discussions and was raised again during Trump and Xi’s White House talks on Thursday.
“We made it very clear to them weeks ago that any help that they would give Iran, whether it be direct or indirect, whether it be intelligence, or parts, or military equipment, was totally unacceptable,” Perdue said. “President Trump made that very clear again yesterday.”
Perdue said Washington remains concerned about what he described as possible indirect Chinese support for Iran, while acknowledging that the US has no direct evidence of China helping Tehran keep the contested Strait of Hormuz closed.
“There’s been indirect support, we think, but there’s no direct evidence,” he said, adding that Washington has made its concerns clear to Beijing.
Perdue said Trump and Xi had agreed that Iran must never obtain a nuclear weapon and that the Strait of Hormuz should remain open, describing the understandings as significant progress.
He also said Washington had seen indications that Beijing is paying attention to US warnings over Iran. “We've seen evidence that they have listened to us, they've pulled some things down,” Perdue added.
On Thursday, Trump and Xi held talks and attended a state dinner. Trump said the two countries have “never gotten along better,” while acknowledging that they “represent different systems.”
Xi said the leaders held “sincere and in-depth exchanges” and reached a common understanding on several issues, adding that the discussions provided “new strategic guidance” for China-US relations.
Iran's Araghchi appreciates Pakistan's 'constructive' mediation efforts in US talks
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has expressed appreciation for Pakistan’s “constructive efforts as a mediator in the negotiations with the United States”, according to a statement from Iran’s foreign ministry on Friday.
During a meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Iran’s top diplomat said breaches of commitments by the United States undermined the position of the mediating institution.
Araghchi specifically referred to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, saying the US violation of the MoU had heightened insecurity and tensions in the region. He held Washington responsible for the continuation of the consequences arising from the situation.
Araghchi also briefed Dar on the latest status of negotiations and an understanding between Iran and Oman on determining an appropriate route for the safe passage of vessels through the Strait of Hormuz.
Dar was also briefed on Iran’s interactions with the United States through Qatar.
Qatari PM, Iranian president discuss de-escalation and dialogue
Qatar’s Foreign Minister and Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, who has been mediating in the Middle East conflict, spoke with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian about de-escalating tensions and creating conditions for dialogue, according to a statement from Qatar’s foreign ministry.
The two met on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, where they “reviewed the latest developments in the region and the efforts being made to de-escalate tensions and create a conducive environment for dialogue”.

Britain warns Iran it will not tolerate hostile activity on UK soil
Britain's foreign minister met his Iranian counterpart on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York and told him his country would "not tolerate intimidation, threats or hostile activity on UK soil" from groups linked to Iran.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi also discussed the war in the Middle East, the importance of reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Britain's "unwavering resolve to combat threats from Iranian-linked groups on UK soil," a Foreign Office statement said.
"The Foreign Secretary reiterated the UK's unwavering resolve to combat threats from Iranian-linked groups on UK soil," it said.
In July, Britain banned support for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and a linked group following a series of antisemitic attacks, using new legal powers designed to stop the use of state-sponsored proxies.
Iran has previously denied using proxies. The British statement did not say how Araghchi responded to Miliband.
A statement on Araghchi’s Telegram account said he had used the meeting to call for a correction to "the destructive and irresponsible approaches of some European governments towards Iran and regional developments."
He also said an "insistence on interfering in countries’ internal affairs and the instrumental use of human rights concepts is in no way acceptable."
Britain's National Cyber Security Centre said last week Iranian state-linked cyber actors had used a spyware family known as "CHOSEN BRICK" to steal emails, messages and other sensitive information through "spear-phishing" campaigns on messaging platforms including WhatsApp and Telegram.
"The Foreign Secretary made clear that Britain will not tolerate intimidation, threats or hostile activity on UK soil and set out the measures the Government has taken in response," the Foreign Office statement added.
Iran proposes reopening Hormuz within seven days
Iran submitted a proposal to the United States to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, its foreign minister told media outlets in New York, AFP reported.
“If certain conditions are met, the strait will be open within seven days and talks will start,” Abbas Araghchi, who is in the US for the UN General Assembly, told media outlets including the New York Times and The Guardian .
Japanese news agency Kyodo reported the proposal citing a senior Iranian official. Iranian media, however, denied the Kyodo report, while authorities in Tehran have not clarified their position.
Iran seeks deal with US, not war: Pezeshkian
Iran does not seek war with the US and remains prepared to pursue a negotiated agreement, President Masoud Pezeshkian said late on Thursday as tensions between the two countries continue.
In an exclusive interview with Fox News' Bret Baier, Pezeshkian was asked if Iran was choosing war or a deal.
“We do not choose war. The war was imposed on us. We do not seek war,” Pezeshkian said.
"So is Iran choosing war or a deal?" @BretBaier presses Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in an exclusive @SpecialReport interview as U.S.-Iran negotiations continue amid heightened tensions. "We do not choose war. The war was imposed on us. We do not seek war," Pezeshkian… pic.twitter.com/CIusXvkRyY
He said Iran remains willing to move forward with an agreement with Washington, referring to the June memorandum that called for a final peace deal within 60 days but collapsed due to differences over navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.
“We did reach an agreement with your president (Donald Trump),” he said. “Based on that, we are willing and still wish to move forward.”
The Iranian president said it is America that must choose whether it wants to end the war or not.
Asked whether Iran would give up its 60% enriched uranium, Pezeshkian said the country would comply with its obligations under international law and the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.
"Do you want a nuclear bomb or not?" @BretBaier cuts to the chase in an exclusive interview with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, directly questioning the leader about his country's nuclear ambitions. "Not at all. Not at all," Pezeshkian responds, insisting Iran does not… pic.twitter.com/jkFEyi9rWd
“Yes,” he said. “Within the framework of international law, based on the Non-Proliferation Treaty, whatever we are supposed to adhere to, we will.”
Pezeshkian also rejected the suggestion that Iran had closed the Strait of Hormuz, a strategically important waterway through which a fifth of the world's oil passed before the war.
Baier questioned Pezeshkian about Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, who has not been seen publicly since replacing his father, Ali Khamenei, killed in US-Israeli strikes in late February.
Pezeshkian said he met Khamenei in person almost a month earlier, and spent about seven hours with him.
EXCLUSIVE: @BretBaier grills the Iranian president on where the Supreme Leader is after not being seen in public in months and whether he is in good health: BAIER: "You saw him in person a month ago?" PEZESHKIAN: "Yes." BAIER: "And is he healthy? Is he able to govern?"… pic.twitter.com/oNpHSzBiSO
Asked whether the supreme leader was healthy and able to govern, Pezeshkian responded: “Very much so, completely.”
Three Iraqi airports suspend Iranian flights starting Friday, sources and state media say
Iraq's Erbil and Sulaimaniya airports suspended Iranian flights starting on Friday, two sources told Reuters , after other Iraqi airports took the same step earlier in the week.
The move means that, according to sources and state media, flights to and from Iran are suspended from all four Iraqi airports at which they were operating — Baghdad, Najaf, Erbil and Sulaimaniya.
Iraq's state news agency reported the suspension at Najaf International Airport earlier on Friday.
Two separate sources told Reuters earlier in the week that Iraq ordered its civil aviation authority to halt Iranian flights to Baghdad airport from Wednesday. The sources said at the time that the government was discussing diverting Iranian flights from Baghdad to Najaf.
Washington had announced it would impose sanctions on any global companies doing business with Iranian airlines after September 23, to ground Iran's entire civilian fleet worldwide.
The United Arab Emirates, the Middle East's biggest travel hub, also said on Thursday it was suspending all flights by Iranian airlines to and from the country until further notice.
Adviser to the Iranian leader Mohammad Mokhber said in response to the flight suspensions that if Iran cannot have flights and receive airport services, then no one in the region can either, according to Nour News.
Crude oil exports via Hormuz at 33.7 million barrels this week, data shows
Crude oil flows out of the Strait of Hormuz reached 33.7 million barrels so far in the week starting September 20, preliminary ship-tracking data from Kpler showed on Friday, putting exports roughly on track with the previous week's levels.
The traffic comprised 19 tankers, of which 17 are very large crude carriers (VLCCs) that can carry 2 million barrels of oil, the data showed. Most of the tankers are laden with crude from Saudi Arabia, followed by Iraq.
For the full previous week, 49.2 million barrels of crude were shipped out via Hormuz, according to Kpler.
On Wednesday, some 60 commercial vessels of all types transited the Strait of Hormuz carrying the highest daily volume of crude oil since early July, a US official told Reuters, speaking on condition of anonymity.
State-run Saudi Aramco 2222.SE has boosted its exports via Hormuz after attacks on its East-West Pipeline earlier this month halted shipments from the Red Sea port of Yanbu.
On Thursday, the number of commodity vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz fell to nine from 14 the day before, Kpler data showed, although an unknown number of ships sail through the waterway with their transponders turned off and are not counted.
Of the nine, eight ships exited. The 10-day average of transits is 18, according to Kpler data.
Before the Iran war started on February 28, the strait typically handled about 125 large commercial vessels per day, including tankers, gas carriers, bulk carriers and container vessels, accounting for some 20% of global oil and liquefied natural gas supply.
Top Russian diplomat meets Iranian counterpart, UN chief on sidelines of General Assembly
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov held talks with his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on the sidelines of the 81st General Assembly session in New York, according to official statements.
During the meeting between Lavrov and Araghchi late Thursday, the two parties discussed pressing regional and international issues, focusing on the evolving situation surrounding Iran, a statement by the Russian Foreign Ministry said.
“They emphasised that there is no alternative to a diplomatic resolution of the crisis triggered by the unlawful actions of the United States and Israel,” it said.
The statement further said that both sides also paid attention to the implementation of bilateral deals reached following the meeting of the Russian and Iranian presidents in the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek on September 1, held on the sidelines of the summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.
“The ministers reviewed the schedule of upcoming Russian-Iranian contacts at various levels,” it added.
In a separate statement on Lavrov’s meeting with the UN secretary-general later that evening, it was stated that their discussions focused on current issues regarding the UN’s activities, particularly on the results of Guterres’ tenure as the organization’s chief.
Lavrov highlighted the importance of “carefully considered UN reform” to adapt the organisation to “the realities of a multipolar world order,” the statement said, adding that he stressed the need to broaden representation of nationals from the "global majority" within the secretariat and for UN personnel to perform their duties in an "impartial and even-handed" manner.
“He also stressed the impermissibility of eroding the organization’s intergovernmental character or violating the established division of labour among its principal organs,” it noted.
The Russian foreign minister arrived in New York late Tuesday, where he is scheduled to address the UN General Assembly on Saturday.
Turkiye chief of staff to attend military chiefs meeting in Saudi Arabia under defence pact, ministry says
Turkiye Chief of General Staff General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu will travel to Saudi Arabia to meet his Saudi and Pakistani counterparts as part of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, the Defence Ministry said on Friday.
Earlier, the Saudi Foreign Ministry said the chiefs of staff would hold an urgent meeting to discuss ways to support Riyadh under the defence pact following attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis. Ankara has said it could help meet Riyadh's military needs if necessary.
Allies unite behind Saudi Arabia as Houthis step up attacks
Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan will hold an urgent, high-level meeting under a joint defence pact to discuss ways to support the kingdom amid attacks by ​Yemen's Houthis, while Tehran seeks to distance itself from the rapid advance of its Houthi allies.
The Houthis have launched strikes on the Saudi-backed government in Yemen and repeatedly fired ‌into Saudi Arabia, disrupting oil flows from the world's largest energy exporter, as part of a wider Middle East war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February.
The Houthis said they had fired dozens of missiles and drones at Saudi targets on Thursday, while authorities in Saudi Arabia said they had intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Houthi fighters.
Read: US and Iran discuss phased deal to reopen Hormuz and end US blockade, sources say
Saudi Arabia earlier had issued emergency alerts for areas including the holy city of Makkah, Jeddah and Yanbu, the main Saudi Red ​Sea oil port.
Saudi Arabia's top religious authority called on soldiers in the kingdom to be ready to lay down their lives to fight the Houthis until the group is ousted from power, ​a statement posted on the Saudi state news agency said.
Amid the fighting, the Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish foreign ministers met within the framework of the Makkah Joint ⁠Defence Agreement, according to a Saudi foreign ministry statement. They condemned the attacks targeting Makkah and other civilian sites, while affirming Saudi Arabia's right to defend itself, the statement said.
"The ministers also discussed arrangements for ​holding an urgent meeting of the chiefs of staff of the three countries to discuss ways to support Saudi Arabia under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which stipulates that an attack against any one of the ​parties constitutes an attack against all parties," the statement said.
The meeting was announced shortly after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian sought to distance Iran from the Houthis in an American television interview on Thursday.
"The Houthis are responsible for their own actions," Pezeshkian told the Fox News program "Special Report with Bret Baier" a day after he appeared before the UN General Assembly in New York.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Yemen: The Houthis are responsible for their own actions. They don't take direction from us. As those who are resisting in the region, based on the situations that have been imposed on them, we have contacts with them. There is no… pic.twitter.com/Tr3cdLoPZL
The Pezeshkian interview and speech took place amid a pause in fighting between the US and Iran and a brief attempt ​at diplomacy in New York, with Qatar serving as an intermediary between the warring parties.
Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told reporters on Thursday that Tehran had conveyed a proposal to the United States via intermediaries under ​which the Strait of Hormuz would be reopened if Tehran’s conditions were met.
Under Iran’s proposal, hostilities would end on all fronts, including Lebanon, within seven days. The United States would lift its blockade on Iranian ports, release Iran’s frozen ‌funds and ⁠waive its oil sanctions, he said.
“The Strait of Hormuz will be reopened on the last day,” Araghchi said, adding that talks with the United States on other issues, including Iran’s nuclear issue, would then start.
A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Wednesday that Tehran was reviewing Washington's response to its peace proposals.
The war, which US President Donald Trump launched alongside Israel in February, has killed thousands of civilians in Iran and Lebanon and disrupted global energy supplies, pushing up oil prices.
While the US and Iran have largely stood down from direct combat, Iranian allies are engaged in the region with Hezbollah confronting Israel in Lebanon and the Houthis advancing in Yemen.
Iran and its allies have ​significantly pressured oil exports from Saudi Arabia, a US ​ally. The Houthis have disrupted ship traffic at ⁠the mouth of the Red Sea while Iran has effectively limited tanker traffic at the Strait of Hormuz, the conduit for 20% of the world's oil exports before the start of the war. An attack by Iranian-backed militias in Iraq also temporarily knocked Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline out of service.
Security experts have debated exactly ​how much Iran directly influences the Houthis, a Shi'ite Islamist movement that evolved from a local insurgency into a powerful armed group controlling much of ​northern Yemen.
However, the Yemeni government, Iranian ⁠and regional sources have said the Houthis' advance down Yemen's Red Sea coast was carried out with direct guidance from Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
Read more: Islamabad MoU remains acceptable to Iran, Pezeshkian tells PM Shehbaz in UNGA meet
With the US-Israeli war against Iran largely stalemated for months on the battlefield, Washington has announced a shift in tactics to extend the reach of its financial sanctions by targeting companies from third countries that do business with Iranian firms, a practice known as "secondary sanctions".
Iranian airlines were barred from neighbouring countries, including the UAE ⁠and Oman, on ​Thursday in response to new US sanctions, the first big impact of a shift in US policy to target companies in ​third countries that do business with Iran.
A flight ban, if sustained, could deepen Iran's isolation and worsen an economic crisis in the country, which is already facing a US blockade of its ports at sea.
"We are living in an open-air prison," a retired teacher ​in Tehran told Reuters by text message on condition her name not be used.
Europe must confront US aggression: Araghchi
Araghchi held talks with his counterpart from Spain, placing US's war of aggression, the insecurity it has manufactured in West Asia, and the Israeli regime’s ongoing occupation and genocide in Gaza at the centre of his discussions, according to IRNA .
Araghchi met with Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares Bueno.
Araghchi: Europe must confront US aggression https://t.co/Lo4ScTj3Qe pic.twitter.com/ZUMdiKiS00
Araghchi defended the rights and sovereignty of the Iranian nation after a cowardly war of aggression by the United States and the Zionist regime, and pressed European and regional governments to abandon double standards and act in accordance with international law.
Outlining current developments in West Asia, he stressed the importance of European countries adopting a responsible approach, consistent with international law, toward the aggressive and illegal actions taken by the United States against Iran.
The Iranian foreign minister pointed to the continuing occupation, the genocide of the Palestinian people, and the Zionist regime’s aggressive expansionism in the region, and underscored the responsibility of all governments to halt these acts of aggression and to hold the Zionist perpetrators accountable and punish them.
Europe's 'complicity will not go unanswered': Gharibabadi
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said in an X post early on Friday that NATO's Secretary-General Mark Rutte’s "admission of conducting 5,000 sorties from European bases in support of the U.S. military aggression against Iran revealed that Europe was part of the aggression's infrastructure", and that Europe's "complicity will not go unanswered."
“Governments that placed their territory at the disposal of the United States cannot evade their responsibility,” he said.
اعتراف دبیرکل ناتو به انجام ۵۰۰۰ سورتی پرواز از پایگاههای اروپایی در حمایت از تجاوز نظامی آمریکا علیه ایران، نشان داد اروپا بخشی از زیرساخت تجاوز بوده است. دولتهایی که قلمرو خود را در اختیار آمریکا قرار دادند نمی‌توانند از مسئولیت خود شانه خالی کنند. این مشارکت، بی‌پاسخ نمی ماند.
Rutte has repeatedly acknowledged that thousands of US military flights, between 4,000 and 5,000, departed from bases in Europe during the US-Israeli war of aggression against the Islamic Republic, according to IRNA .
. @Gharibabadi : Europe was part of infrastructure of US aggression against Iran https://t.co/bsIpH1sGYl pic.twitter.com/WVD5UgHzOL
He described Europe as a “platform of power projection” without which Washington could not have conducted the operation.
Colombia said on Thursday that it formally severed diplomatic relations with Iran due to "national and hemispheric security concerns," alleged links to international terrorist and narcoterrorist groups, and human rights violations.
In a statement, the Foreign Ministry said the decision took effect on September 19 and was based on the government's foreign policy priorities, including "the fight against transnational crime and the protection of national security."
The ministry said "Colombia also took into account confirmed human rights violations, verified attacks against countries not involved in the Middle East conflict, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and the authorities' obstruction of the International Atomic Energy Agency's (IAEA) efforts to verify the scope of Iran's nuclear program."
"These facts deteriorated Colombia’s trust in the government of the Islamic Republic of Iran," the ministry added.
Colombia’s new president, Abelardo de la Espriella, has redrawn alliances since taking over in August. He fast-tracked efforts to restore the South American nation’s ties with Israel, reversing predecessor Gustavo Petro’s strong stance on the genocide in Gaza.
Hormuz commodity ship transits fall to nine, shiptracking data shows
Vessel transits at the Strait of Hormuz fell on Thursday to 9, compared with the previous day's 14, preliminary ship-tracking data showed on Friday.
Of those, eight ships exited, according to the data.

At the Bab el-Mandeb strait, ship transits on Thursday were little different from Wednesday, at 26, with 12 ships entering and 14 exiting, Kpler data showed.
Of the ships that entered, one was a laden VLCC carrying Iraqi Basrah crude bound for Egypt with its transponder switched on.
US Senate rejects resolution curbing Trump's Iran war powers
The US Senate ​on Thursday narrowly ‌rejected a Democratic-led resolution aiming to ​stop the ​Iran war until hostilities ⁠are authorized ​by Congress.
The Senate ​voted 50 to 49 to reject the resolution, ​which had ​passed the House of ‌Representatives ⁠in July. The vote was largely along party ​lines, ​with ⁠most of President Donald ​Trump's Republicans rejecting ​the ⁠measure and almost every Democrat ⁠voting ​for ​it.
France to send 'military means' to protect Saudi oil port: Macron
President Emmanuel Macron said France would send “military means” to help shield the key Saudi oil terminal of Yanbu from attacks by Houthis, according to AFP .
“We are going to send military assets, meaning soldiers, radars, and defence systems to protect this site,” he says during an interview with TF1 and France 2 during the evening news.

title: Afridi says police must fight terrorism
description: Afridi says police must fight terrorism
content:
CM urges police to stay focused on counterterrorism, avoid politics
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Muhammad Sohail Afridi on Thursday declared that the province's police and people have waged a continuous war against terrorism for the past 22 years, and that their unmatched sacrifices have secured peace even in other parts of the country, including Islamabad and Rawalpindi.
Addressing a meeting on law and order, Afridi said the provincial government has provided the police force with unprecedented financial resources, modern equipment and an enhanced martyrs' package to enable effective action against terrorists. He stressed that the primary duty of the police remains the protection of the lives and property of the people, and that the force cannot be allowed to become entangled in political disputes or actions against any political party.
Afridi recalled that his party had protested and raised its voice at every forum against the resettlement of terrorists.
The chief minister expressed serious concern over extraordinary delays in the supply of equipment despite payments having already been made.
He added that payments have also been made to the National Radio and Telecommunication Corporation for a defensive system against jammers and drones. Afridi demanded that both NRTC and Heavy Industries Taxila immediately supply jammers, armoured vehicles and other essential equipment so that the police can effectively continue the fight against terrorism.
Drawing a sharp contrast between federal and provincial priorities, the chief minister said that instead of eliminating terrorism, the fake government at the centre has made the elimination of Tehreek-e-Insaf and the subjugation of Imran Khan its priority. "Our interest is not to eliminate any political party; our priority is to deal with terrorism," he said. "If the police's interest also becomes the elimination of a political party, where will the people of K-P go? The police cannot be allowed to have their attention diverted from the war on terror towards anyone's political objectives."
Afridi made clear that since taking the oath as chief executive on 15 October 2025, he has never issued any wrong order to any police officer, never directed political or personal victimisation, and never ordered the registration of a false FIR.

title: Balochistan imposes province wide curbs
description: Balochistan imposes province wide curbs
content:
Section 144 bans weapons, gatherings and face coverings for 30 days
The Balochistan government has imposed strict restrictions across the province with immediate effect to maintain law and order.
According to an order issued by the Home Department under Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the display of weapons, gatherings of five or more people, and covering of faces in public places have been completely banned for 30 days.
An official notification states that the government has received information about possible activities and gatherings that could adversely affect public peace, law and order, and the safety of citizens. In view of this, the following restrictions have been enforced with immediate effect:
The display, carrying, possession or use of any kind of weapons in public places is strictly prohibited, except in cases specifically permitted by law.
Any gathering, meeting, procession, rally, demonstration or similar activity involving five or more persons at any public place is completely banned.
Covering or concealing the face in public places, particularly with a muffler, mask or any other means that hinders identification, is also prohibited.
These restrictions are effective immediately and will remain in force throughout the province for 30 days. All relevant law-enforcement agencies and district administrations have been directed to ensure strict compliance with the order. Anyone found violating it will face legal action.
The order has been signed by Additional Chief Secretary (Home) Muhammad Hamza Shafqat. Copies have been sent to the Registrar of the Balochistan High Court, the Principal Secretaries to the Chief Minister and the Governor, the Inspector General of Police, all Divisional Commissioners, Deputy Inspectors General and Superintendents of Police.
Government sources said the measures have been taken to improve the law-and-order situation in the province and to prevent possible disruptive activities. The public has been urged to respect the restrictions and play their role in maintaining peace by abiding by the law.

title: CM  four former ministers named in May 9 case
description: CM  four former ministers named in May 9 case
content:
Forensic, NADRA reports confirm their alleged presence during Radio Pakistan attack
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and four former provincial ministers have been formally nominated as accused in the case of the attack on Radio Pakistan during the violent protests that erupted in the city on May 9 and 10, 2023, following the arrest of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder and chairman Imran Khan.
The investigation officer of the case submitted a detailed report before the Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) on Thursday, stating that the presence of the five individuals at the scene and their alleged involvement in the incident had been confirmed through scientific evidence.
The hearing was conducted by ATC Judge Wali Muhammad Khan. Radio Pakistan's counsel Shabbir Hussain Gigyani and investigation officer Khushhal Khan appeared before the court.
According to the investigation officer, the probe into the May 9 events has been completed in the light of reports received from the Punjab Forensic Science Agency and the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA). Both agencies examined videos and photographs of the incident that were sent to them on the court's earlier orders. The reports confirmed that Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, Taimur Saleem Jhagra, Kamran Bangash, Irfan Saleem and Aamir Chamkani were present at the Radio Pakistan premises when the building was attacked and property damaged.
After receiving the forensic and NADRA findings, investigators reviewed the available evidence. The Director of Radio Pakistan subsequently recorded a statement nominating the five individuals as accused in the case.
When the court inquired about the timeline for submitting the formal challan (charge sheet), the investigation officer requested additional time to prepare the document in light of the new reports. He informed the court that the complete challan would be filed through either the special prosecutor or the district public prosecutor as soon as it was ready.
Counsel for Radio Pakistan, Shabbir Hussain Gigyani, told the court that the police report from Thana Sharqi also recorded the presence of the accused at the site. He noted that more than 100 PTI workers, in addition to the chief minister, have already been nominated in the same case relating to the arson and damage to the Radio Pakistan building and its property on May 9 and 10, 2023. Their trials are under way, and further investigation remains pending.
The Anti-Terrorism Court directed the prosecution to submit the complete challan by September 28 and adjourned the proceedings until that date.
The May 9-10 violence in Peshawar formed part of the widespread unrest that followed Imran Khan's arrest. Several government and media installations across the country came under attack during the protests. The Radio Pakistan case has remained under investigation for more than three years, with authorities relying on video footage, photographic evidence and forensic analysis to identify those allegedly involved.
With the latest forensic and NADRA confirmations now on record, the nomination of the chief minister and the four former ministers marks a significant development in the long-running case. The submission of the complete challan by the end of this month is expected to pave the way for the next stage of legal proceedings against the newly named accused.

title: President  PM  CMs laud newspapers  role
description: President  PM  CMs laud newspapers  role
content:
Stress credible news and informed debate
President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and the chief ministers of Sindh, Balochistan, and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have felicitated newspaper readers, publishers, editors and journalists on the National Newspaper Readership Day, falling on Friday (today).
National Newspaper Readership Day is observed annually across Pakistan on September 25 to promote reading habits and counter digital disinformation. In their messages on the occasion, the leaders paid tribute to the enduring role of newspapers in promoting public awareness, informed opinion, democratic discourse and responsible journalism.
They emphasised that although the media landscape has changed rapidly with the emergence of digital and social media, newspapers continue to provide credible information, context, diverse perspectives and informed analysis, particularly at a time when fake news, misinformation and disinformation are spreading rapidly.
President Zardari reaffirmed his faith in a free press and its role in protecting citizens' rights, reminding them of their duties towards the State and society and holding decision-makers accountable. He observed that newspapers continued to hold an important place in shaping public opinion and promoting an informed citizenry.
"Rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, targeted dissemination of fake news and disinformation campaigns are also influencing our social values, cultural outlook and behaviour," he said. "In this environment, credible and balanced reporting, supported by responsible editorial oversight, is more important than ever."
The president urged young Pakistanis to develop the habit of reading newspapers, whether in print or through digital platforms, while equipping themselves with modern technological skills.
He urged the All Pakistan Newspapers Society (APNS), and the Council of Pakistan Newspaper Editors (CPNE) to continue to contribute to informed national discourse and greater public understanding of regional and global developments.
Prime Minister Shehbaz, in his message, paid tribute to newspapers and the entire journalistic community, particularly members of the APNS, as well as newspaper readers. He highlighted the contribution of newspapers to Pakistan's political, economic and social life, noting their historic role in promoting awareness, shaping public opinion and providing access to reliable information and diverse viewpoints.
He recalled their historic role in promoting political awareness and unity during the freedom movement and their continued contribution after independence to strengthening democracy, promoting transparency and keeping citizens informed on matters of national and international importance.
He further stressed that in an age of fake news and misleading information, professional journalism, responsible reporting and credible editorial systems had become even more important. He also encouraged the younger generation to make newspaper reading a habit as a means of expanding knowledge and understanding current affairs.
Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti, while referring to Balochistan's geographically diverse communities, said reliable and credible information was especially important for the province. He encouraged the youth of the province to read newspapers regularly, saying that it broadens knowledge, strengthens awareness and develops critical thinking.
Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah highlighted the historical and cultural significance of the press in Sindh, observing that newspapers had reflected the province's diverse communities, languages, culture, heritage and traditions while highlighting local issues, achievements and aspirations.
He said while digital platforms have transformed access to news, they have also increased the need to verify information and understand it in context. "Newspapers, backed by professional journalism, editorial responsibility and in-depth reporting, continue to play a vital role in providing credible and well-informed perspectives," he said.
K-P chief minister Sohail Afridi said that in an age when news travels instantly, understanding issues in their proper context has become increasingly important, with newspapers enabling readers to go beyond headlines and examine different perspectives.
He also described a free, responsible and independent media as "an essential pillar of democracy and an important bridge between citizens, institutions and the state," while urging the younger generation to make newspaper reading part of their daily routine.
The leaders extended warmest greetings to the APNS, appreciated its continued efforts to promote newspaper readership and acknowledged the valuable contribution of the newspaper industry to the society.

title: Robbers strike across Khanewal after police deployment to Islamabad
description: Robbers strike across Khanewal after police deployment to Islamabad

title: Probe fails to substantiate allegations against faculty member
description: Probe fails to substantiate allegations against faculty member
content:
Varsity withdraws lecturer from teaching, administrative duties
A probe committee constituted by Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering and Information Technology (KFUEIT) has concluded that allegations levelled against a faculty member through anonymous social media accounts could not be substantiated, and has submitted its findings and recommendations to the university administration.
According to the committee's report, the inquiry included examination of the mobile phone and laptop used by the faculty member, compilation of details of SIM cards registered in his name, and access to his email and WhatsApp records.
The committee also interviewed students from all classes currently taught by the faculty member, as well as students working with him on final-year projects.
The Quality Enhancement Cell assisted the committee in conducting confidential surveys to protect students' privacy.
According to the report, none of the students interviewed came forward with a complaint corroborating the allegations.
The faculty member was also given an opportunity to submit his position in writing. According to his statement to the committee, he has been serving as a lecturer at the university since 2016 and is among its earliest instructors.
He told the committee that after becoming aware of the social media posts on Sunday, September 20, he lodged a complaint with the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), bearing Complaint CMO-260921-9CD886.
He also voluntarily handed over his electronic devices to the committee for forensic examination, denied the allegations and expressed his willingness to cooperate with the inquiry.
The committee noted that, so far, neither the concerned department nor the Director of Student Affairs had received any formal complaint against the faculty member.
Regarding screenshots circulated on social media, the report observed that their authenticity could not be established without a forensic examination of the mobile phones and other devices of all parties concerned.
The committee said that, in the absence of corroborating evidence or forensic confirmation, the allegations could not currently be substantiated.
It added that its findings should be considered preliminary pending the forensic analysis report from law-enforcement authorities.
Among its recommendations, the committee proposed that the university formally approach the relevant law-enforcement agency, the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), to identify those allegedly responsible for circulating the material and proceed against them in accordance with the law.
Following the recommendations, the university administration has withdrawn the faculty member from teaching and administrative responsibilities and barred him from contact with students, according to the report.
The administration has also reiterated that it would take steps to maintain a safe and conducive learning environment for students.

title: Make FIRs readable   LHC pulls up police over tiny fonts
description: Make FIRs readable   LHC pulls up police over tiny fonts
content:
The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Thursday expressed displeasure over the use of extremely small fonts in First Information Reports (FIRs) and directed Punjab Police to ensure that computerised FIRs are prepared in a uniform and legible font across all police stations in the province.
Chief Justice Aalia Neelum issued the directions while hearing a contempt petition against former Chung station house officer (SHO) Rashid Amin Butt.
Punjab Inspector General of Police Abdul Karim and other senior officers appeared before the court. Additional Advocate General Muhammad Naveed Sheikh and Assistant Advocate General Waqas Umar also attended the proceedings.
Expressing annoyance over the submission of FIRs printed in small fonts, the chief justice remarked, "Have you seen the FIR? It cannot be read even with glasses." She questioned whether the court would be expected to "read or understand" such FIRs, adding that the issue was being observed in almost every case.The chief justice observed that the font would inevitably become too small when material meant for three pages was compressed onto a page. "They say they are saving paper, but while saving paper, they have ruined our eyesight," she remarked.
The court directed the IGP to ensure that FIRs across the province were prepared using a uniform and appropriate font.
It also ordered the preparation of a standard computerised FIR format to be circulated among all police stations in the province.
IGP Abdul Karim told the court that a letter had been sent to the chairman of the Punjab Information Technology Board (PITB) regarding increasing the font size of FIRs. He said assistance had been sought from the PITB and the FIRs would now be capable of being enlarged through the zoom function by up to 70 per cent.
The chief justice observed that at least a standard font should be prescribed, adding that the matter was not complicated and could be resolved within a day or two.
The court directed the IG to submit a report on the measures taken regarding the FIR font by September 29, adjourning further proceedings.

title: From Class I to XII  Punjab puts AI on the curriculum
description: From Class I to XII  Punjab puts AI on the curriculum
content:
The Punjab government has approved a major overhaul of the school curriculum, promising to reduce the volume of textbooks by 25 per cent, introduce artificial intelligence (AI) education from Class I to XII and attach QR codes to books to give students access to video lessons.
The government has also proposed new measures to address corporal punishment and student mental health.
The decisions were taken in a meeting on education reforms chaired by Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Thursday amid what authorities termed an attempt by the government to shift classroom teaching away from rote memorisation towards concept-based and technology-assisted learning.
As per details presented at the meeting, the new curriculum will cover subjects including English, mathematics, Urdu, social studies and early childhood education. The Punjab Education Curriculum, Training and Assessment Authority (PECTAA) gave a briefing on the proposed changes. The authority describes its curriculum mandate as promoting deeper learning, higher order thinking and innovation rather than merely revising textbook content.
One of the most visible changes will be an attempt to reduce the amount of material students have to carry and study. The government says textbook volume will be cut by 25% with the objective of discouraging rote learning and allowing greater emphasis on understanding concepts.
However, the implementation will be crucial. A smaller textbook does not automatically mean lighter academic workload if examination requirements, homework and classroom assessments continue to demand the same volume of preparation.
An educationist said the government would face the challenge of ensuring that the curriculum reduction was reflected in teaching and assessment practices rather than size of books
According to an education ministry official, the new textbooks will also contain quick-response (QR) codes that students can scan to access video lessons related to the relevant topic.
The move could provide children an additional learning resource outside conventional classroom teaching, particularly where teachers have limited time to explain difficult concepts. The effectiveness of the system, however, will depend on access to smartphones or other devices, internet connectivity and the availability of quality digital material in schools and homes.
Regarding introduction of AI education from Class I, the chief minister directed officials to prepare a curriculum and stressed the need for laboratories for the new subject.
The proposal represents a substantial expansion of technology education because it envisages exposing children to AI concepts from the earliest years of schooling. The relevant officials will have to determine how AI content is differentiated according to age, teachers will be trained and infrastructure will be required before the programme can operate effectively across Punjab's government schools.
The government has set the deadline to complete printing of the new textbooks before March, putting pressure on the education authorities to complete curriculum development, review, production and distribution within a tight schedule.
The reform package also moves beyond academic content as for the first time in Punjab, the government has decided to initiate mental health training for teachers.
A proposal to place visiting faculty psychologists in every district was also considered while the chief minister directed authorities to develop online counselling facilities for students.
The measures indicate an attempt to address behavioural and emotional issues within schools through counselling and trained personnel rather than punishment. The model will require sufficient professional staff, referral mechanisms and confidentiality safeguards.
It was agreed in principle to initiate legislation aimed at eliminating corporal punishment in schools. A proposal was discussed to establish "discipline corners" in classrooms as an alternative to physical punishment.
The chief minister said physical violence against children could leave lasting effects on their lives.

title: SC puts brakes on Dr Kumbhar trial days before hearing
description: SC puts brakes on Dr Kumbhar trial days before hearing
content:
Complainant challenges transfer to sessions court, questions prosecution's role in plea by accused cops
The Supreme Court has stayed the trial of Dr Shahnawaz Kumbhar's alleged custodial killing and desecration of his body, days before proceedings were due to begin at the Mirpurkhas district and sessions court, throwing into question the Sindh High Court's order shifting the case from the Anti-Terrorism Court.
The apex court issued the stay on a petition by Dr Ibrahim Kumbhar, complainant in the FIRs concerning Dr Shahnawaz's alleged custodial killing and desecration. The petitioner has sought restoration of the ATC's jurisdiction, challenging the SHC's April 7 order directing the transfer of the case to the sessions court.
The sessions court was scheduled to commence the trial on September 29. Advocate Sajjad Ahmed Chandio, representing the complainant, argued before the Supreme Court that the case should continue before the ATC and objected to the circumstances in which it was transferred.
In a further twist, Chandio told the apex court that Sindh's deputy prosecutor general, who was expected to prosecute the case against the accused police officers, had instead filed an application on behalf of a DIG and two SSPs accused in the FIR, seeking transfer of the case from the ATC.
The counsel argued that since one of the FIRs under trial had been registered with the FIA, the Sindh deputy prosecutor general had no jurisdiction to represent the accused in seeking transfer of the case. According to him, the matter was supposed to be handled by the federal law officer. The Supreme Court has issued notices to the Prosecutor General Sindh, Advocate General Sindh and Attorney General for Pakistan for October 13, fixing the matter before a three-member bench.
Dr Shahnawaz Kumbhar was shot dead in what the complainant describes as a staged police encounter on September 19, 2024, after he surrendered to Mirpurkhas police in Karachi in connection with a blasphemy FIR. After his death, his body was allegedly set on fire by a mob while it was being transported to a graveyard in Umerkot district for burial.

title: You botched the case  you re also suspicious
description: You botched the case  you re also suspicious
content:
Justice Sial grills SSP Samiullah Soomro over Mir Raza probe
The judicial commission probing the death of Mir Raza came down hard on the police investigation on Thursday, with Justice Umar Sial telling SSP Samiullah Soomro that the case had been "botched" in its crucial early days and questioning whether the police officer himself had become a subject of suspicion.
The commission also grilled senior health officials over the abrupt replacement of a medical board, including the decision to replace Karachi-based specialists with doctors from Hyderabad, and questioned the legal authority behind the changes.
The proceedings, headed by Justice Sial, produced a series of pointed exchanges over the handling of CCTV footage, Mir Raza's mobile phone and smartwatch, the crime scene, witness statements and the police's apparent focus on a possible suicide and financial-pressure narrative.
During questioning, Justice Sial told SSP Soomro that the first six days of the investigation were crucial and appeared to have seriously compromised the case. "You botched the case. You are also suspicious," the judge remarked, according to the proceedings.
Soomro told the commission that he had been assigned the investigation on August 2 and headed a team that included SSP East Zubair Nazir, East Investigation SSP Usman Saduzai and, later, officers from the Citizens-Police Liaison Committee.
The commission repeatedly questioned why the family's statements had not been formally recorded. Soomro said he had directed SSP Zubair Nazir to meet the family, but was told that they had initially declined.
Family members disputed that account during the proceedings, saying they had met police officers on August 3.
Justice Sial questioned Soomro over the failure to personally ensure that the family's statements were recorded, saying that he was the head of the investigation team regardless of the administrative control exercised by other officers.
The commission also challenged the police's handling of CCTV footage. Soomro acknowledged that only footage from one street had been examined showing Mir Raza travelling in the area, despite the presence of multiple streets and dozens of cameras around the location.
Soomro said more than 30 CCTV clips had been collected, but Justice Sial demanded the relevant memos and questioned why investigators had not systematically secured footage from all surrounding streets before it became unavailable.
The judge also questioned a video circulated in the media in which Mir Raza appeared to throw something away. Police had suggested that he was throwing his mobile phone, but Soomro conceded that the footage did not establish this conclusively.
The handling of the mobile phone came under further scrutiny. Soomro said he had neither seen the phone nor the officer who recovered it, while the commission questioned why the recovery and subsequent transfer of such a crucial piece of evidence had not been properly documented.
The smartwatch was another major point of contention. Soomro said it had been seized before he took charge and that he had not personally seen it.

The confrontation was recorded by the female passenger on her mobile phone as well as by a camera installed in the taxi. The driver subsequently handed the footage to police, while a video statement recorded by the complainant has also emerged.
The incident has drawn attention to the alleged movement of a vehicle without a number plate and the open display of firearms by the security guard during the confrontation.

title: Suspects denied bail in Ayat Noor case

content:
Probe declares accused innocent, prompting protests by their parents, relatives
Bail applications filed by suspects arrested in the five-year-old Ayat Noor brutal murder case have been rejected, while the police investigation team has declared three arrested suspects innocent.
The children's parents protested against the police, blocked Hattar Road and demanded action against police officials and officers over what they described as inhuman and un-Islamic treatment of the children.
On Thursday, bail applications of three arrested suspects, Talha, Usman and Qasim, in the five-year-old Ayat Noor murder and brutality case were filed in a local court in Haripur, which rejected them.
On the occasion, Ayat Noor's father Shafiq also appeared and did not raise any objection to the granting of bail. However, after arguments by the lawyers, the honourable court dismissed the bail applications.
Following the arrest of 11-year-old minor suspect Hassan in the case, the investigation team and heirs have declared the three suspects innocent, further complicating the Ayat Noor case.
The parents came out of the court and blocked Hattar Road during a protest. Following the investigation team and Ayat Noor's father, Shafiq, announcing that the arrested suspects had been declared innocent, the protesters questioned why the bail applications of alleged suspects Talha, Usman and Qasim were dismissed.
Relatives of the three children blocked Hattar Road and protested, demanding immediate release of their innocent children. The parents also alleged that their children were subjected to sexual abuse among themselves during custody and staged a strong protest against the police.
They demanded action against police officials and officers who had implicated innocent children in the case.
Later, the children's parents and other citizens dispersed peacefully.
Human rights activist and lawyer Jawad Habib Naqshbandi, while giving his legal opinion outside the court on the Ayat Noor case, said the case could have become a source of pride for the police but had instead been turned into a stain.
He said the case should have gone to the United Nations.

title: Police hunt PTI leaders  activists
description: Police hunt PTI leaders  activists
content:
Prepare lists of active party workers; nearly 150 detained under MPO
Police in Rawalpindi Division have intensified a crackdown on Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) leaders and workers ahead of the party's September 27 long march to Islamabad, with nearly 150 people detained under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) and confined in different jails across the division.
Police are also carrying out door-to-door searches and monitoring PTI leaders and active workers. According to police sources, lists have been prepared for the arrest of 463 prominent leaders and active workers categorised into three tiers, while 91 leaders and workers affiliated with the Insaf Students Federation (ISF) and Insaf Lawyers Forum are also being monitored.
The sources said 2,019 door-knocking operations had so far been conducted at the homes and offices of PTI leaders and workers during the past 20 days and that the exercise was continuing.
Police and the administration in all five districts of Rawalpindi Division - Rawalpindi, Attock, Chakwal, Murree and Jhelum - are making arrangements to deal with the PTI march, including road closures and deployment of police personnel.
The sources further said police had been mobilised at district level to detain prominent PTI and ISF leaders and active workers under Section 3 of the MPO Ordinance on the grounds of apprehended threats to public order and to minimise the impact of the march.
According to a detailed survey conducted by the police and administration, 463 PTI leaders and active workers in Rawalpindi Division, including 180 in Rawalpindi district, have been identified as people who could play a role in mobilising other workers. They include 59 Tier-I, 178 Tier-II and 226 Tier-III leaders and workers
Similarly, 91 leaders and workers of the ISF and Insaf Lawyers Forum have been identified, including 11 in Tier-I, 14 in Tier-II and 66 in Tier-III. The lists have reportedly been handed over to the police, which has been mobilised for arrests and monitoring.
On the other hand, Hazara's road links with Punjab have been severed as authorities took measures to prevent the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) from holding its proposed long march on September 27, causing difficulties for passengers and residents travelling towards Rawalpindi and Islamabad.
The Hassan Abdal Road linking Haripur with Punjab has been blocked with containers at Jhari Kas, while the Haripur-Khanpur-Taxila Road has been closed at Gangu Bahadur by placing containers.
Containers have also been brought to the bridge over the Haro River at Ahata Taxila to block the Haripur-Hattar-Taxila Road. However, traffic on the route remains open for now and is expected to be blocked by Thursday night.

title: Handcuffing of female suspects sparks outcry
description: Handcuffing of female suspects sparks outcry
content:
Lawyers call practice unconstitutional, illegal and unethical
For the first time in Pakistan's 79-year judicial history, women accused being brought from Adiala Jail to courts in Rawalpindi have started appearing with their both hands tightly secured in handcuffs, prompting strong protests from the District Bar Association and senior criminal lawyers.
The lawyers said women could not be sentenced to death under Pakistani law and that handcuffing women was unconstitutional, illegal, unethical, un-Islamic and inhuman.
The women accused, while speaking to The Express Tribune in tears, said that from the time they were brought from the jail to court, presented before the court from the temporary lock-up and taken back to jail, they remained in handcuffs for six to seven hours.
They said they had started becoming unveiled because of the handcuffs. If their dupatta or shawl slipped from their heads, they could not adjust it. They said urination was a natural human need, but using washrooms had become difficult, while meeting children who came from their homes to the courts had also become difficult.
The women said getting into and getting out of police vans had become difficult with both hands handcuffed.
They alleged that male policemen, under the pretext of helping them, held them from behind while getting them into the van and held their hands while helping them get down, resulting in women becoming exposed.
They said women were being handcuffed only in Rawalpindi and that no woman had ever escaped from police custody.
Senior lawyer Shan Zaib Khan Advocate said the Constitution and law prohibited, and even criminalised, handcuffing women and children. He said they were approaching the high court against the police officer who had issued the order.
He said the Constitution of Pakistan did not allow a woman to be sentenced to death and the order to handcuff women with both hands was illegal and should immediately be withdrawn.
He said women accused who were their clients, as well as their relatives, were facing severe distress and suffering.
According to him, the order had been issued by the CPO Rawalpindi and was wrong.
District Bar Association President Malik Sajid Tariq Awan termed the handcuffing of women with both hands a violation of the Constitution and said the bar was protesting against it. He said if the practice was not stopped, they would directly approach the chief justices of the Supreme Court and high court.
Meanwhile, women accused, whose hands were handcuffed, told The Express Tribune that they had protested against the practice but police told them it was the CPO's order and that their jobs would be at risk if they did not comply.

title: India s CJP trains guns at polls chief

content:
Opposition Congress announces nationwide marches against voter-list manipulation
Leaders of an Indian youth movement on Thursday threatened nationwide protests if Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar does not resign within 48 hours, escalating a political dispute over alleged disagreements within the Election Commission and changes to voter lists.
The announcement followed a report by the Indian Express newspaper that two election commissioners had raised questions or expressed concerns at least 14 times over 10 months, mostly regarding the process of updating voter lists that began last year.
The report triggered a fresh political backlash against the commission, which opposition parties have accused of bias. They allege that millions of voters were removed without warning and that new names were added without proper verification to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
"If Gyanesh Kumar does not resign within 48 hours, the Cockroach Janta Party will start a nationwide agitation ... we will not back down without Gyanesh Kumar's resignation," CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke told a press conference.
The movement recently emerged from youth demonstrations in July that resulted in the resignation of Modi's education minister over allegations involving examination-paper leaks, marking one of the government's significant political setbacks since Modi came to power in 2014.
Meanwhile, the main opposition Congress party announced protest marches at election offices across all Indian states on Friday.
It is demanding Kumar's arrest and removal from office, as well as an independent review of decisions and voter-list changes made during his tenure.
In a statement on Wednesday, the Election Commission rejected the allegations, saying that "differing views and
observations are a normal part of deliberation in any institution" and are part of the process before a final decision is reached.

CNN, MS NOW and Politico seek urgent hearing after reporters turned away
CNN, MS NOW and Politico requested an urgent court hearing on Thursday after their reporters were barred from the White House despite a judge's order that their access be restored.
"This morning journalists from each of CNN, MS NOW, and Politico attempted to enter the White House and were turned away," the news outlets said in a court filing. "Plaintiffs respectfully request that the Court set a hearing by videoconference or teleconference as soon as possible," they said.
District Judge Timothy Kelly ruled overnight that the three news organisations banned by President Donald Trump last week should have their access to the White House immediately restored.
On last Friday, CNN, MS NOW and Politico were barred from the White House for distributing what the president branded "fake news" and "fiction and lies".
They filed a joint lawsuit asking for a temporary restraining order against the ban on the grounds that it violates the First Amendment of the US Constitution, which upholds the right to a free press. The Department of Justice had argued that "access to the White House is a privilegenot a right."
However, Judge Kelly, who was appointed by Trump during his first term, appeared unconvinced.
"The Court is skeptical at least on this recordthat Defendants' interest in safeguarding national security is the actual motivation for, or is even advanced by, the revocation of Plaintiffs' hard passes," the judge said.
In their fresh request to Kelly to hold an emergency hearing, the media outlets said the "defendants have already repeatedly violated the Court's order," adding: "Time is of the essence. CNN is scheduled to be the television pool this evening for (Chinese) President Xi Jinping's visit to the White House."

title: Saudi defences down six Houthi missiles
description: Saudi defences down six Houthi missiles
content:
Civil Defence issue brief alerts for Makkah, Yanbu, Taif, Jeddah and Tabuk
Saudi Arabia intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles on Thursday after issuing warnings for several regions including Makkah, as
on the kingdom amid raging clashes with the forces belonging to the Internationally-backed Yemeni government.
The missiles were the latest in a series of escalating Houthi attacks since July, when renewed hostilities shattered a years-long truce and embroiled Yemen in the wider Middle East war. Houthis have imposed a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, hitting its tankers in the Red Sea and its territory.
The Saudi-led coalition said six ballistic missiles had been intercepted, thwarting attacks on Taif and Yanbu. "Escalations and violations by the terrorist Houthi militia will be dealt with firmly," said coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki in a series of posts on X.
Defence had issued a brief series of alerts including one for the
Sea governorate of Yanbu as well as the Taif, Jeddah and Tabuk
regions. The alerts were lifted a few minutes later.
In recent weeks, alerts have often preceded attacks by the Houthis. Last week, Riyadh accused the group of targeting Makkah for the first time since 2017 with a drone that was downed, an accusation the Houthis denied. A few days later, the group attacked the Saudi capital Riyadhthe first in years.
As the Houthi attacks targeted Saudi Arabia on Thursday, battles raged on the ground in Yemen. At least 150 Houthi fighters and government troops have been killed in the past 24 hours, sources from both sides told AFP, including in clashes over hilltops overlooking the Bab al-Mandab strait at the mouth of the Red Sea.
At least 98 soldiers and government forces members were killed, according to an AFP tally compiled from five military sources. Most were killed in Houthi ballistic missile and drone attacks, with dozens of Yemeni troops killed on the Saudi side of the border that they are tasked with guarding.
At least 52 Houthi fighters were also killed, two sources from the group said. Many on both sides were also killed in clashes in the Kahboub Mountains and in
regions, as the Houthis seek to dominate the highlands overlooking Bab al-Mandab to protect newly seized territory.
In July, a fragile 2022 truce between the Houthis and Yemen's government fell apart after the group allowed an Iranian plane to land in Sanaa in defiance of Riyadh's control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks. The Houthis later announced a
maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began attacks.

title: Walkout greets Netanyahu at UNGA
description: Walkout greets Netanyahu at UNGA
content:
A small section of audience, including Israeli delegation, remains seated; hundreds protest outside UN
Dozens of delegates walked out of the UN General Assembly Hall on Thursday as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu arrived at the podium to begin his address at the 81st session, underscoring the growing diplomatic tensions surrounding Israel's war in Gaza and the wider Middle East conflict.
Video from the assembly showed large numbers of delegates leaving their seats as Netanyahu prepared to speak. The incident followed a series of walkouts during the UN General Assembly's high-level debate this week involving Cuba, Iran and others.
Dozens of envoys from across the world left the General Assembly Hall, some jeering and booing, while Netanyahu's own team stood and the speaker of the session called for order. Netanyahu responded by criticising the departing envoys.
Locked in a tight race to stay in power in the October 27 elections, Netanyahu used the global platform at the UN General Assembly to attack everyone from the leaders of Iran to New York's first Muslim mayor, as well as partners Britain, France and Turkey.
In his 40-minute speech, he attacked Zohran Mamdani, who has called him a war criminal and previously said he would seek to enforce an International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant if legally able to do so.
Mamdani rejected Netanyahu's allegations and accused him of repeating claims intended to justify Israel's conduct in Gaza. Netanyahu also criticised Western governments, particularly Britain and France, which have imposed sanctions targeting Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
He also accused Qatar and Turkey of spreading falsehoods. He devoted particular attention to Iran, saying that its leadership would eventually be toppled by its own people.
The speech came amid protests outside the UN headquarters, where several hundred demonstrators gathered, chanting slogans including "Stop arming Israel, let Gaza live". Police detained several protesters, including actors Susan Sarandon and Hannah Einbinder.
Netanyahu's appearance also highlighted Israel's growing diplomatic isolation. The prime minister faces restrictions on travel to several countries following an ICC arrest warrant issued in 2024 alleging war crimes and crimes against humanity.

title: Europe turns back to coal amid energy crunch
description: Europe turns back to coal amid energy crunch
content:
80 countries call for restoration of Gulf navigation
Eighty countries on Thursday called for the full restoration of maritime navigation in the Gulf, as the conflict involving Iran continued to disrupt energy markets, push up fuel prices and encourage European power producers to turn back towards coal.
"We call for the full restoration of navigational rights and principles without delay," Bahrain's Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid al-Zayani said while reading a joint statement to journalists at the United Nations.
The appeal came as three Iran-linked oil tankers seized by the United States and carrying nearly six million barrels of Iranian crude were tracked crossing the Atlantic towards the United States. The cargo is valued at nearly $600 million.
The vessels were seized after Washington imposed a blockade of Iranian ports in response to Tehran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The closure of the Strait the passage for one-fifth of global oil supplies – has rippled throughout the World.
Europe's electricity sector is particularly affected. Soaring gas prices, driven partly by reduced liquefied natural gas shipments through Hormuz, have made coal and lignite plants more profitable than gas-fired power stations for the first time since at least 2024.
European benchmark gas prices climbed above 80 per megawatt hour this month, their highest level in three years. Analysts expect coal-fired power generation to rise by about 25% over the next six months as gas-fired generation declines by a similar amount.
The energy shock has also pushed European diesel prices to records. The EU average reached 2.23 per litre, up from 2.16 the previous week, with 19 member states recording new highs. The United States supplied about half of EU diesel imports in August.
The European Commission warned that a possible US ban on diesel exports would harm both sides. Brussels said the measure was a "bad idea", particularly as Europe remains heavily dependent on imported fuel amid continuing global supply disruptions.

title: China s Xi calls on US  Iran to return to negotiating table
description: China s Xi calls on US  Iran to return to negotiating table
content:
Chinese president sets red lines for Trump at White House reception
Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called on the United States and Iran on Thursday to return to the negotiating table to end their war, according to a report by state-run news agency Xinhua on Xi's closed-door meeting with US President Donald Trump as the US president gave his Chinese counterpart a lavish welcome to the White House.
Xi told Trump that China "has always maintained that the sovereignty and security of all countries should be respected" and said Beijing had played a constructive role in easing tensions between the two sides and pushing them toward talks.
The Chinese leader said "Beijing supports Washington and Tehran returning to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding", expressing hope the two sides would resume negotiations as soon as possible.
Xi said he hoped the countries could reach a comprehensive agreement, including on the nuclear issue, and ultimately achieve peace.
The Chinese president told Donald Trump that Beijing and Washington must peacefully manage their superpower rivalry.
While Trump hailed their "truly great friendship" on a day of sweeping pomp and circumstance, Xi used his state visit to lay down China's red lines on AI, Taiwan and the Iran war. Behind the pageantry and symbolic gestures, like Trump taking Xi inside his Marine One helicopter, the talks were focused on tensions that continue to divide the world's two largest economies.
In his opening remarks with Trump, Xi said the two countries must ensure there is "no conflict and no confrontation between us." Xi also warned that the development of artificial intelligence should be "always under human control," in contrast to Trump, who has repeatedly dismissed warnings that AI could threaten humanity itself.
Trump's remarks struck a warmer tone, underscoring the US president's long-term efforts to woo the Chinese leader. "President Xi and I have made tremendous strides on the issues facing our two countries," Trump said after greeting Xi for his first visit to the White House in over a decade.
Earlier on Thursday at the White House, Trump touted his "truly great friendship" with Xi and said the two powers had made strides on trade since his trip to China in May.
"During this visit, we will also discuss pressing issues concerning security, technology, and 'super intelligence,'" Trump said, using his alternative name for artificial intelligence. "The decisions we make in these areas today can promote peace and prosperity for decades and decades to come."
Speaking after Trump, Xi said the competition between the US and China should be a "healthy one." US companies were welcome in China, he said, adding that he hopes "Chinese companies are treated fairly here in the United States."
Xi also said both militaries should maintain regular dialogue to improve crisis prevention.
"The Thucydides trap can be overcome," he said, referring to the academic theory that sees a risk of rivalry between a rising and an established power spiraling into open conflict.
The summit, Xi's first visit to Washington in more than a decade, is the second meeting this year between the leaders of the world's two biggest economies.
For Trump, who relishes ceremony and prizes his ties with powerful leaders, the visit is as much a matter of national prestige as an opportunity for high-stakes diplomacy. The US president aimed to reciprocate the grand welcome he received in China in May.
But Trump and Xi's remarks were not carried live by any US television networks, which have collectively declined to provide footage in protest of the White House's ban of CNN, MS Now and Politico.
Trump greeted Xi on arrival on Wednesday evening with a red carpet on the tarmac, the first time a US president has welcomed a foreign leader at Joint Base Andrews since President Barack Obama met Pope Francis in 2015, according to C-SPAN, which tracks presidential events.
Following their remarks on Thursday, the two leaders observed a military ceremony including a flyover at the Rose Garden, with Chinese flags waving from the Oval Office roof alongside US flags, before a scheduled bilateral meeting.
Trump's embrace of Xi could complicate his campaign message at home ahead of November's midterm elections, when Republicans' narrow congressional majorities are at stake as voters fret about inflation and the war on Iran.
The president for months has labeled Democrats "communists" in an effort to paint them as too extreme, but he welcomed Xi, the head of the Chinese Communist Party, on Thursday as a dear personal friend.
