title: Gohar urges govt to listen before Sept 27 showdown
description: Gohar urges govt to listen before Sept 27 showdown
content:
Rangers deployed in Islamabad, Punjab districts
The Centre on Thursday moved swiftly to deploy paramilitary Pakistan Rangers in several Punjab districts and the federal capital to assist police in maintaining law and order and responding to potential security threats, according to a notification issued by the Ministry of Interior.
The move came as PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan urged the government to open negotiations over the party's planned September 27 long march, warning that political workers should not be confronted with force.
He said his party did not want the public and law-enforcement personnel to come face to face.
Speaking to the media outside Parliament, Gohar said dialogue was essential given the seriousness of the situation and the fact that a major political party was preparing for a long march.
He urged the government not to use net launchers against those taking part in the protest.
He said political workers were not supposed to be dealt with through such measures. Instead, their grievances should be heard and resolved, they should be provided justice and their concerns considered seriously, with both sides putting their egos aside.
Gohar said the entire issue had been turned into a battle of egos and that the government would have to set aside its ego.
He said the use of net launchers should be abandoned and a way found to ensure serenity, adding that PTI did not want the public and law-enforcement personnel to confront one another.
"We are saying that our voice should be heard. We are peaceful and are coming out for our rights. We are raising the voice for justice and have repeatedly said that we were not heard and were not given justice," he said.
Gohar said ministers could issue whatever statements they wished, but no minister had said that the government had listened to PTI's concerns and delivered justice.
He said the party had announced its programme well in advance and there would be no change in it.
On the issue of trust in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, Gohar said Afridi was the party's chief minister and that Imran Khan had confidence in him.
He said Afridi would remain chief minister and enjoyed the support of the entire party upon Imran Khan's instruction.
Gohar also accused the government of imposing an undeclared governor's rule in K-P, saying such a situation should not exist.
He said the province was autonomous and its people, mandate, chief minister and lawmakers should be respected.
He said ministers were never supposed to disappear in their own province, nor should members of provincial assemblies be arrested on political grounds.
Gohar said political rivals should not be physically confronting one another on political grounds and that the practice had to end. "We have repeatedly made it clear that we are peaceful."
The PTI chairman also rejected an "attempt by a section of the government" to portray the party's march as a threat to state institutions and Islamabad.
He said PTI had been peaceful, remained peaceful and would continue to be peaceful, and would not attack institutions or Islamabad. He said the government needed to address the narrative and impression being created about the party.
Gohar warned that if the government continued to create such an impression, a major political party with substantial public support could effectively be pushed out of the political arena.
He cautioned that excluding political parties from the political process could have "very dangerous consequences".
The approval came a day after the Punjab government sought Rangers assistance in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali until October 5, with the deployment approved by the provincial cabinet's Standing Committee on Law and Order on September 20 following a request from Punjab Police. The deployment was to be carried out under Article 245 of the Constitution and relevant provisions of the Anti-Terrorism Act 1997 and Pakistan Rangers Ordinance 1959.
The ministry approved the deployment following requests from the Chief Commissioner Islamabad and the Punjab government. Rangers personnel were deployed under Sections 7(b) and 10 of the Pakistan Rangers Ordinance 1959 and Sections 4 and 5 of the Anti-Terrorism Act 1997.
The notification authorised the Rangers to provide full assistance to police in maintaining law and order and responding to violent activities or security threats. It also directed Rangers and police personnel to take all appropriate and necessary action in self-defence in the event of attacks by armed or violent groups.
The ministry instructed the security forces to take all necessary measures to deal with any violent activity or threat and ensure the protection of public property and lives.
The deployed Rangers personnel would perform security duties and assist police authorities in maintaining peace and order in the areas concerned, according to the notification.

title: Pakistan strikes ten drone sites in Afghanistan
description: Pakistan strikes ten drone sites in Afghanistan
content:
Islamabad says precision strikes followed Afghan drone incursions
Pakistan carried out "precision" aerial and drone strikes against 10 locations in Afghanistan after drones launched from Afghan territory entered Pakistani airspace, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said on Thursday, describing the strikes as a response to a "deliberate and unlawful incursion".
"In exercise of its sovereign right to self-defence, Pakistan conducted precision aerial and drone strikes against 10 locations in Afghanistan used for launching and storing these drones. The strikes were deliberate, precise, calibrated and proportionate and strictly limited to identified military objectives directly linked to the attempted attacks against Pakistan," said Tarar in a post on X.
The strikes were in response to drone attacks from Afghanistan. A day earlier, Pakistan's air defence systems had shot down eight drones after they entered the country's airspace from Afghanistan. Security sources said four of the drones were brought down in areas adjoining the Torkham border, while another four were shot down in mountainous areas near the border with Kohat.
Tarar said the drone incursion on September 23 was a "blatant violation" of Pakistan's sovereignty and territorial integrity and a "grave and unacceptable act of aggression".
"Pakistan condemns in the strongest possible terms the deliberate and unlawful incursion into Pakistan by drones on September 23, launched from Afghan territory," he said.
The minister said that Pakistan's Air Defence systems detected, tracked and neutralised all intruding platforms before they could reach any of their intended targets, comprehensively thwarting the attempted attack.
The minister said Pakistan for years had repeatedly conveyed its concerns to the Afghan Taliban regime and its interlocutors over the continued presence of terrorist sanctuaries and support networks on Afghan soil.
"Instead of dismantling these networks and taking credible and verifiable action against those using Afghan territory to perpetrate terrorism against Pakistan, the Afghan Taliban regime has chosen to escalate the situation through hostile drone operations against Pakistan," he said.
Tarar warned that Pakistan would not tolerate attacks launched from Afghan territory, "whether by terrorist groups or by the Afghan Taliban regime itself."
"Any violation of Pakistan's sovereignty will be met with an immediate and decisive response," he added.
He called on the Afghan Taliban regime to immediately cease all hostile activity against Pakistan and take effective, concrete, verifiable and sustained action against terrorist entities operating from Afghan soil.
"Afghan territory must not be used to launch attacks or conduct hostile operations against Pakistan," Tarar said. He added that Pakistan did not seek escalation and remained committed to "regional peace, dialogue and constructive engagement".
"This commitment must not be mistaken for weakness or an unlimited tolerance of hostile actions," he said. "Pakistan will defend its sovereignty, territorial integrity and the lives of its citizens with full resolve and will take all necessary measures to protect them," Tarar added.
In a separate post, Tarar said, "Through precise aerial and drone strikes, as seen in the attached clip, terrorist hideouts and support infrastructure, including drone launching and storage sites across 10 locations in areas under the control of the Afghan Taliban regime, were comprehensively destroyed," Tarar said.
"Pakistan will continue to defend its territorial integrity and protect the lives and property of its citizens against any externally sponsored, sheltered and abetted threat by terrorist proxies," he added.
Moreover, security forces killed several Afghan Taliban while foiling their attempt to carry out aggression in the Gulistan sector along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.
Security sources said that the Afghan Taliban attempted to enter Pakistani territory and carry out an act of aggression. However, Security Forces responded effectively, resulting in the killing of several Afghan Taliban.
Intermittent exchange of fire between Security Forces and Afghan Taliban is still continuing, while troops remain fully alert and vigilant in the border area, the sources said.
Security forces remain fully prepared to respond promptly and effectively to any infiltration or aggression from Afghan territory into Pakistan, the sources added.

description: Islamabad MoU fully acceptable to Iran  PM
content:
Shehbaz, Pezeshkian discuss ME conflict Situation in Hormuz, Red Sea figure in talks
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday said Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian had hailed Pakistan's efforts for peace in the region and conveyed that the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) remained fully acceptable to Iran.
The prime minister was speaking to media representatives alongside his Lebanese counterpart Nawaf Salam after he met with the Iranian president on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
Asked about the Islamabad MoU, under which Pakistan had mediated between Iran and the United States, the prime minister said Pakistan's entire leadership was united in its resolve to further accelerate efforts for peace under the memorandum.
The premier also expressed particular concern over the situation in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, saying brotherly and friendly countries were making efforts to reduce the tensions there.

title: FCC stopwatch for lawyers sparks debate
description: Currently  230 409 cases are pending in the apex court of the country
content:
Currently, 230,409 cases are pending in the apex court of the country
The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan's recent step of installing a digital stopwatch in Courtroom No 1, allowing lawyers 10 minutes each to present their arguments, has triggered a legal debate over the implications of the move and the balance between speedy disposal and effective representation.
Despite the passage of 10 months, lawyers are also questioning why six vacant seats in the FCC have not been filled to help reduce pendency. Currently, 230,409 cases are pending in the apex court of the country.
Under the new system, lawyers representing the parties in a case will initially be given 10 minutes each to present their arguments. If more time is required in an important or complex case, the court may extend the allotted time at its discretion.
In major and significant cases, the time may be extended up to 30 minutes through a judicial order.
Under the timer system, once the allotted time for a lawyer expires, the timer will automatically sound an alarm, immediately informing both the lawyer and the court that the prescribed time has ended. The lawyer will then be required to leave the rostrum.
However, the court will retain the authority to grant additional time where necessary. Hearings of cases under this system have already started in the court of Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan.
Meanwhile, lawyers are divided over the unusual step taken by the FCC chief justice.
Former law officer Waqar Rana believes that the pressure of huge pendency and a lack of credibility in the administration of justice are forcing the chief justice of the FCC to adopt such a policy.
Rana says that the right of audience before a court of law is part of the right to a fair trial under Article 10-A of the Constitution.
"Judges now rely upon their inexperienced law clerks and their brief in the judgements and this practice is against the law. The Bar Councils must agitate this matter and protect their rights."
'Justice cannot be reduced to stopwatch'
Lawyer Waqas Ahmad states that speedy disposal is important, but constitutional justice cannot be reduced to a stopwatch.
"The right to a fair hearing requires that counsel be given a meaningful opportunity to present the case, particularly where fundamental rights and questions of constitutional interpretation are involved."
"Efficiency should facilitate justice, not come at the expense of effective representation and due process," he adds.
Supreme Court lawyer Hafiz Ehsaan Ahmad Khokhar observed that the introduction of a countdown mechanism for concluding oral arguments by counsel before the FCC is a constructive and modern initiative aimed at promoting time-bound hearings, disciplined advocacy and efficient disposal of constitutional litigation.
Similar case-management and time-management practices are followed by constitutional and superior courts in various jurisdictions.
However, such a mechanism should facilitate effective case management rather than unnecessarily restrict the court's ability to examine substantial constitutional questions.
In view of the fact that more than 22,000 cases have reportedly been transferred to the FCC, many involving questions of considerable constitutional and public importance, there is an urgent need to increase the strength of FCC judges immediately and by a substantial number.
This expansion should include, within the constitutional framework, the appointment of highly experienced and distinguished constitutional lawyers and jurists, in addition to serving or former judges, so that the court possesses sufficient judicial capacity, diverse constitutional expertise and institutional experience to deal with its exceptionally heavy docket.
The lawyer further stated that important constitutional questions should ordinarily be heard by benches comprising at least three judges, while matters involving exceptional constitutional significance, conflicting constitutional interpretations or questions having far-reaching legal and public consequences may appropriately be placed before larger benches of around five judges, subject to the Constitution and applicable law.
Such a structure would promote broader judicial deliberation, consistency and the development of authoritative constitutional jurisprudence.
"The significance of this institutional requirement is further enhanced by Article 189 of the Constitution, under which decisions of the Federal Constitutional Court, within the constitutional scheme, are binding upon all other courts, including the Supreme Court. It is, therefore, essential that the FCC develops a coherent, carefully reasoned and enduring body of constitutional jurisprudence capable of providing clear guidance to the entire judicial system."
He also stressed the need for a transparent, predictable and well-established case-fixation, roster and bench-allocation system in accordance with the applicable constitutional and statutory framework, particularly the relevant practice and procedure law.
"Since the FCC is a specialized constitutional court, its principal registry at Islamabad should remain the central forum for hearing constitutional matters, while hearings at other registries may be arranged where genuine judicial or administrative necessity so requires," he adds.
Meanwhile, the FCC judges are also facing what some lawyers call a "battle of perception", particularly because they were appointed by the federal government, which is expected to be the primary litigant before the court in several politically sensitive matters.

title: IMF chief satisfied with Pak economic reform
description: IMF chief satisfied with Pak economic reform
content:
IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva has expressed satisfaction with Pakistan's economic reform programme, saying the implementation of the government's reform agenda has helped achieve macroeconomic stability, Arab News reported.
Georgieva said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's government had made progress through a strong reform programme, which had contributed to improvements in fiscal discipline, external reserves and investor confidence.

The remarks came as the IMF began discussions with Pakistan for the fourth review of the country's $7 billion economic programme.
Talks have also started on the third review of Pakistan's $1.4 billion climate resilience programme.
Successful completion of both reviews could pave the way for around $1.2 billion in financing for Pakistan, including about $1 billion under the economic programme and $200 million under the climate facility.
During the reviews, the IMF will assess Pakistan's progress on reforms and commitments made under the programmes.

title: Talal hopes  better sense  will prevail
description: Talal hopes  better sense  will prevail
content:
State minister raises concerns over K-P police act
Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry on Thursday said the government's priority was to resolve the issue with the PTI through dialogue and hoped that better sense would prevail before the party's planned march on Sep 27.
Talking to a private television programme, Capital Talk, while recalling the previous PTI protest, the minister admitted that it had not been managed properly last time but said things would be different this time.
"The government believes in minimum use of power, but one thing is very clear this time ... Islamabad is very far away in this manner," Talal said.
He said the protesters would be treated respectfully, escorted and sent back in the same manner, but warned that if they wanted to come to turn Islamabad into "Somnath", they would neither be allowed to come nor be able to take anything back.
"The route that can be opened through talks cannot be opened through a march," he said.
Meanwhile, the minister expressed concerns over the new Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Police Act approved by the provincial cabinet, saying the legislation could affect the police command structure, discipline, morale, and the force's role in maintaining law and order and combating terrorism.
Speaking at a news conference, he said policing and law and order are provincial subjects under the Constitution following the 18th Amendment, but provincial legislation must remain within the constitutional and legal framework governing the Police Service of Pakistan (PSP).
Talal said provinces do not have unrestricted authority to legislate on matters that fall outside the constitutional framework. He noted that just as provinces cannot create separate armed forces, railways, or naval services, they also cannot introduce laws that override established PSP rules and principles.
He said the PSP rules were developed under Pakistan's federal system and have been upheld through decisions of the high courts and the Supreme Court.
According to him, these rules provide the basis for the command and administrative structure of the police force and cannot be set aside through provincial legislation.
The minister said the K-P Police has been engaged in the fight against terrorism for many years and has made continuous sacrifices. He argued that the new law does not only reduce the authority of the Inspector General (IG) but also affects the wider chain of command within the police force.
He stated that powers relating to the appointment and posting of officers from the rank of DSP and above, which were previously exercised by senior police officers, have now been shifted.

title: LHC declines stay on Imran sisters  detention
description: LHC declines stay on Imran sisters  detention
content:
Seeks replies from relevant authorities on petitions
The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Thursday declined an immediate request to suspend the detention notifications issued against PTI founder Imran Khan's sisters, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, and sought replies from the relevant authorities on their petitions challenging the detentions.
Uzma and Noreen had been taken into custody a few days earlier for 30 days under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance 1960 (MPO), a day after their sister Aleema Khan was detained. The detentions of Imran's sisters and other PTI leaders came ahead of the party's planned countrywide protest on September 27 and march to Islamabad.
Justice Abher Gul Khan heard the petitions, while lawyers Rana Mudassar Umar and Barrister Taimur appeared on behalf of the petitioners.
During the proceedings, Umar asked the court to suspend the detention notifications, saying he wanted to place certain facts before the bench.
"Both women are housewives, and Dr Uzma has already been found innocent in the case registered against her," the counsel submitted. He also told the court that a copy of the trial court's decision had been attached to the petition.
The court declined to suspend the notifications at this stage and instead directed the relevant authorities to submit their reports and replies. "Let us seek reports from the relevant parties," Justice Khan observed.
The petitions sought the annulment of detention notifications issued by the deputy commissioner. The court subsequently issued notices to the respondents, seeking their replies on the pleas. The respondents included the Lahore deputy commissioner, capital city police officer, secretary of the Home Department and superintendent of Kot Lakhpat jail.
Noreen's daughter, Sakina, and others had also approached the high court through Umar, challenging the detention orders.
A few days earlier, Justice Gul, while hearing a petition challenging the detention of Aleema and her driver, had sought arguments on the maintainability of the plea.

title: CTD foils terror attack in Peshawar
description: CTD foils terror attack in Peshawar
content:
Constable martyred in exchange of fire with suicide attackers
The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) on Thursday foiled a major terrorist attack in Peshawar, killing one terrorist during an intelligence-based operation in the Garhi Sherdad area of Warsak Road.
According to a CTD statement, the department had received "credible intelligence" that three suicide attackers had entered the provincial capital and were preparing to target a sensitive installation.
Acting on the information and following a detailed technical analysis, CTD teams, district police and personnel from a relevant intelligence agency launched an operation in the area.
The area was cordoned off and monitored with the help of drones during the operation. The terrorists opened fire on the CTD personnel, leading to a gunbattle.
The CTD said Constable Muhammad Afaq was martyred while three other personnel were injured in the exchange of fire.
One of the terrorists reached a rooftop and opened fire on the CTD team while attempting to escape. The personnel returned fire and killed him, the statement said.
A search and clearance operation was underway to apprehend the remaining two terrorists, while additional security personnel had been deployed in the area. The search operation was also being expanded in view of possible threats.
The operation was supervised by the K-P CTD additional inspector general.
Investigators traced the terrorist network involved in the attack on Kohat Police Lines, according to officials familiar with the probe.
Officials said a joint CTD team made progress in the investigation and traced the network behind the attack.
According to the investigators, two terrorist organisations had jointly planned the attack on the Kohat Police Lines. The attackers intended to free their associates being held at the CTD compound.

title: Pakistan warns against AI driven inequality
description: Pakistan warns against AI driven inequality
content:
Dar says emerging technology must not become 'another facet of ongoing arms race'
Pakistan on Thursday warned the UN Security Council that an unregulated artificial intelligence boom risks widening global inequalities and threatening international peace.
"Concerted efforts are required to erect the necessary guardrails, regulations and governance frameworks," Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar told the 15-member Council which held a briefing on 'Artificial Intelligence and International Security.
Stressing the need for restraint and confidence-building in the military domain to address risks of miscalculation and compressed decision-making, he underscored the importance of international cooperation to ensure that AI is representative, transparent and inclusive.
Convened by France, Council President for September, the meeting was chaired by French Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs ean-Noël Barrot.
In his comments, Dar said the impact of AI, as a force multiplier and cross-cutting dual-use technology, was sharply evident on international and regional peace and stability.
Dar said Pakistan welcomed the recognition that no single company or country can manage these risks alone, and that competitive pressures are driving a race that no one can win safely.
Today's asymmetries and divides, he said, would aggravate and a safety agenda would turn into a strategy of technological exclusion. The risks of uncontrolled AI would be borne by all; decisions on how to manage them cannot rest with a handful of companies or capitals.
DPM/FM called for avoiding fragmentation in AI development and governance, and all relevant issues concerning the development and deployment of AI as well as its broader implications should be taken up comprehensively in representative and inclusive forums with universal participation under the UN auspices.
Pakistan, he said, was joining as a founding member of China's initiative to establish the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, as this represents a concrete step toward promoting the development of artificial intelligence, "for good, and for all.
"Confidence-building measures, Senator Dar said, play a vital role in the maintenance of international and regional peace and security.
"Practical tools designed to reduce mistrust, prevent accidental escalation, and manage risks related to military and foundational AI systems are necessary for peace and security," he said.
"We look forward to working closely with member states in efforts to help bridge the global AI divide and promote equitable access to advance peace and development for all."

content:
KSE-100 down around 1,740 points on mounting ME, oil concerns
Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) fell sharply on Thursday as renewed geopolitical tensions, a spike in global oil prices and profit-taking outweighed positive developments in the refinery sector.
The benchmark KSE-100 index declined 1,733.57 points, or 1.01%, to settle at 170,498.95, reversing the previous session's gains. The market remained under pressure as Brent crude moved above $100 per barrel, raising concerns over inflation, the external account and broader macroeconomic stability.
Arif Habib Limited (AHL), in its report, noted a broad-based decline that kept the KSE-100 inside its July low consolidation zone, with 11 shares rising and 87 falling. Engro Fertilisers, HBL and Ghandhara Automobiles were the main positive contributors while UBL, Lucky Cement and Mari Energies dragged the index most.
The report also mentioned Geely's planned entry into Pakistan with three SUVs via Bestway Automotive and separate plant upgrade agreements signed by Attock Refinery and Cnergyico with Inter State Gas Systems. The KSE-100 closed down by 1,733.6 points (-1.01%), remaining under pressure while keeping in view the July lows and the September 11 low near 166,100.
Topline Securities, in its market review, observed that the KSE-100 closed at 170,499, down 1,734 points, after trading between the intra-day high of 172,491 and the low of 170,418. The market witnessed a pronounced reversal from early gains as profit-taking intensified in the latter half of the session, exerting considerable pressure on the benchmark index.
Following three consecutive sessions of gains, investors moved to lock in profits, resulting in a broad-based retreat that erased a substantial portion of the market's recent advances, as per Topline. Market sentiment remained fragile and risk-averse, amid heightened geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and renewed concerns over elevated global crude prices, with Brent crude trading above the $100 per barrel threshold.
Trading activity was moderate as total volumes reached 760 million shares, while traded value stood at Rs27.5 billion, it added.
Commenting on the market's performance, KTrade noted that Brent crude moved towards $107 a barrel on the back of geopolitical tensions, keeping macroeconomic concerns elevated. That reversed Wednesday's 830-point advance, which had been supported by hopes around US-Iran talks and the arrival of an International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission.
A genuine structural positive did not save the session. National Refinery, Attock Refinery and Cnergyico signed upgrade agreements with Inter State Gas Systems under the amended brownfield refinery policy – part of a roughly $6 billion modernisation push aimed at producing Euro-V fuels and lower import dependence. Refinery stocks still closed lower with the broader market, KTrade said.
Overall trading volumes were recorded at 759.97 million shares compared with the previous session's tally of 773.59 million. The value of shares traded during the day was Rs27.54 billion.
In the ready market, shares of 495 companies were traded. Of these, 101 stocks closed higher, 358 fell and 36 remained unchanged.
Cnergyico Pk was the volume leader with trading in 158 million shares, losing Rs0.84 to close at Rs13.47. It was followed by K-Electric with 72 million shares, losing Rs0.48 to close at Rs6.05 and First National Equities with 60 million shares, losing Rs0.07 to close at Rs1.12.
Foreign investors bought shares worth Rs17.7 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

The finance minister also participated in the Digital Cooperation Organisation's High-Level Ministerial Dialogue, where he described digital transformation as a key part of Pakistan's transition from economic stabilisation to sustainable growth.
He highlighted the development of digital public infrastructure and cashless payments, while stressing that connectivity must be accompanied by upskilling and reskilling to help freelancers and other digital workers move into higher-value services.
Noting the widespread adoption of virtual assets, Aurangzeb outlined Pakistan's work on legislation, oversight and licensing, and underscored practical uses beyond cryptocurrency, including cheaper and more seamless remittances and the potential tokenisation of public debt and real estate.

title: Meeting reviews fuel relief payments
description: Meeting reviews fuel relief payments
content:
Over 5m register under scheme; oil minister vows uninterrupted supplies
Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik on Thursday chaired a meeting to review payments under the Prime Minister's Fuel Relief Scheme as well as supply chain, transportation and logistics arrangements to ensure uninterrupted availability of petroleum products across the country.
The minister appreciated the petroleum dealers' associations for their cooperation and support for the fuel relief scheme. Ali Pervaiz said that the government was taking all necessary measures to ensure uninterrupted fuel supplies in case of any law and order situation or road closures. He directed all relevant stakeholders to make advance arrangements and ensure smooth movement of petroleum products.
The meeting was attended by the representatives of Pakistan Railways, Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra), Oil Companies Advisory Council (OCAC), oil marketing companies, Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association, All Pakistan Petrol Pump Owners Association and other relevant officials.
Additional secretary railways assured the meeting that Pakistan Railways would make maximum number of train bogies available for transportation of high-speed diesel (HSD), particularly to maintain supplies in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) during any disruption to road transportation.
The petroleum minister directed Pakistan State Oil (PSO) to make advance arrangements for adequate fuel availability at its depots. PSO told the meeting that, anticipating possible disruptions, additional stocks had already been arranged at critical depots for seamless petroleum supplies.
An Ogra representative revealed that a dedicated control room had been established for crisis management and coordination to ensure continued availability of petroleum products at retail outlets. The federal minister also gave directives that steps be taken for uninterrupted crude and petroleum product supply to Attock Refinery to avoid any shutdown arising from logistical constraints.
While reviewing the payment mechanism under the relief programme, the meeting was informed that out of approximately 10,000+ petrol filling stations, payments had been made to over 8,500 pumps by Thursday, with the number increasing every day.
The minister emphasised that minor issues, including account number mismatches, must be resolved immediately so that payments to remaining filling stations were processed without delay and the public continued to receive relief under the scheme. Ali Pervaiz directed Ogra to take action against any petrol pumps found denying fuel relief to eligible customers.
Speaking at the meeting, Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association Chairman Malik Khuda Bakhsh said that the scheme was working successfully and assured the government of the association's continued support. He said that dealers were cooperating with the government in implementation of the initiative. OCAC Chairman Nawed Tanwir Abbasi said that the scheme was working successfully and termed it a good initiative aimed at providing relief to the public. The petroleum minister reiterated that close coordination among all stakeholders was essential for smooth fuel supplies and effective implementation of the fuel relief scheme.
According to a statement, a meeting of the National Steering Committee on Fuel Subsidy was held under the chairmanship of Minister for Economic Affairs Ahad Cheema to review implementation of the PM Fuel Relief Scheme. The committee was informed that registrations under the scheme had crossed 5 million and 3.7 million fuel tokens had been redeemed at petrol stations across the country. Punjab alone made 400,000 registrations on Wednesday following an intensified awareness campaign.
The State Bank of Pakistan reported that of the 43,036 claims received from petrol stations, 41,744 were settled, amounting to Rs1.350 billion, with a settlement rate of 97%.
Taking note of the difficulties faced by three-wheeler and loader rickshaw operators in registering under the scheme, the chair directed that the Punjab Excise Department engage rickshaw associations directly, identify the barriers to registration and open a dedicated registration window. A complaint window will also be established at the provincial excise offices so that unresolved vehicle registration queries were routed for case-by-case resolution.
The committee was informed that an automated complaint resolution mechanism was operational and complaints were routed directly to deputy commissioners for field enforcement, to the Excise Dept for vehicle data correction, to Ogra for matters concerning petrol stations and to the Pakistan Digital Authority for technical issues.
The chair called for constituting a working committee, headed by Ogra chairman, with the Department of Explosives and the Pakistan Digital Authority, to harmonise petrol station records.

title: Oil refineries ink plant upgrade agreements
description: Oil refineries ink plant upgrade agreements
content:
Will inject $6b over 5 years to modernise plants for production of cleaner Euro-V fuels
Oil refineries have signed plant upgrading agreements with the government-nominated entity – Inter State Gas Systems (ISGS) – paving the way for around $6 billion in investments aimed at producing high-efficiency fuels under the new oil refinery policy.
According to industry officials, Attock Refinery, National Refinery, Pakistan Refinery and Cnergyico Pk inked the agreements on Thursday whereas Pak Arab Refinery (Parco) is expected to sign it soon. The government, especially Minister of Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik, took the lead in removing bottlenecks to the new refinery policy.
Cnergyico Pk CEO Amir Abbassciy told The Express Tribune that the signing of the refinery up-gradation agreement was a remarkable achievement and a long-awaited milestone for Pakistan's refining sector.
"We extend our appreciation to the prime minister, the federal minister of petroleum and all government officials and stakeholders whose dedicated efforts and continued support have made this landmark development possible," he said, adding that Cnergyico was fully committed to the successful implementation of the project.
In line with the refinery policy framework, the company has structured its up-gradation project into three phases. The first phase will focus on shift to Euro V-compliant fuels, the second phase will target a reduction in fuel oil output, while the third phase will involve enhancement of refinery capacity.
He added that Cnergyico was already at an advanced stage of project implementation and remained committed to moving forward expeditiously. "We believe this project will play an important role in modernising Pakistan's refining infrastructure, improving the quality of locally produced petroleum products, reducing dependence on imported refined fuels and strengthening the country's long-term energy security."
Attock Refinery CEO Adil Khattak said the signing of up-gradation agreements by Pakistan's refineries, namely Attock Refinery, National Refinery, Cnergyico and Pakistan Refinery, and later by Parco, marked a historic milestone for the refining industry and the tangible commencement of what was arguably the largest coordinated industrial investment programme ever undertaken in Pakistan, involving around $6 billion of investment over the next five years.
He said those projects would fundamentally modernise Pakistan's refining infrastructure, enable production of cleaner Euro-V fuels, substantially reduce furnace oil production, replace significant quantities of imported petroleum products and strengthen the country's energy security.
"For those of us who have remained involved with this initiative from its inception, today's (Thursday's) achievement has particular significance. The journey began with the first draft of the refining policy in December 2019, followed by its approval in August 2023 and subsequent amendments before finally reaching implementation today – almost seven years later."
The delay has come at a considerable cost. Industry estimates indicate that refinery up-gradation can save Pakistan around $1.5 billion annually in foreign exchange. Recent geopolitical developments have also reinforced something the refining industry has emphasised for years: domestic refining capacity is not merely a commercial consideration; it is a strategic national asset. Khattak stressed that reaching the milestone deserved recognition and celebration. It would not have been possible without the passionate, persistent and resilient leadership of Federal Minister of Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik, his team in the Petroleum Division and the support of other relevant government institutions. "Their efforts to remove the remaining impediments have been instrumental in translating a long-pending policy into implementation," he said.
"The signing, however, is not the end of the journey. It is the beginning of an even more challenging phase as the five refineries translate their commitments into financing, engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning of complex projects within the stipulated five-year period," he observed, adding that having personally remained involved in the formulation of the policy from the beginning and witnessed its many ups and downs, "I can fully appreciate the significance of this occasion".
"For Pakistan's refining industry, our energy security and the industrial development of the country, this is truly a golden day," he added.

title: OICCI seeks capital  export push
description: OICCI seeks capital  export push
content:
Says FDI slumps 32%, urges investor-friendly reforms in meeting with IMF team
The Overseas Investors Chamber of Commerce and Industry (OICCI) has underlined the importance for Pakistan to use the gains from macroeconomic stabilisation to accelerate private investment, exports, energy security and structural reforms during a meeting with a visiting delegation of the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
The delegation, comprising Iva Petrova, Adviser, Middle East and Central Asia Department, IMF, and Mahir Binici, Resident Representative, IMF, met senior OICCI leadership and representatives of member multinational companies on Thursday.
The chamber highlighted the decline in FDI despite improvements in Pakistan's external position and sovereign credit profile, noting that net FDI fell by around 32% to $1.7 billion in FY26. OICCI called for lower regulatory and compliance burdens, stronger investor protection and clearer coordination among federal and provincial authorities. It also emphasised that domestic industry must lead by reinvesting in Pakistan, as foreign investors take cue from the confidence demonstrated by local businesses.
Amid higher oil prices linked to the Middle East conflict, the OICCI called for immediate energy conservation and a medium-term plan for greater energy self-sufficiency. It also called for a coherent energy security strategy covering power, gas and petroleum, citing high regional energy costs, circular debt, the need for investment in refining and opportunities for regional energy cooperation.
On the external sector, the OICCI stressed that Pakistan could not sustain higher growth without expanding its capacity to earn foreign exchange. It underscored the need for greater competitiveness and productivity, stronger export-oriented sectors, deeper trade and investment ties with key markets and greater regional trade where commercially viable.
On structural reform, the chamber sought faster SOE reforms and credible privatisation where continued state ownership had no compelling policy rationale. It also advocated the separation of state's roles as a policymaker, regulator, facilitator and commercial operator to create greater space for private-sector investment and competition.
The chamber emphasised the broadening of tax base to cover under-taxed segments, including agriculture, real estate, SMEs and retail, rather than repeatedly increasing the burden on documented businesses.

title: SBP s FX rises by  11m to  21 4b
description: SBP s FX rises by  11m to  21 4b
content:
Total reserves stand at $26.8b; gold price falls Rs5,600 per tola
Pakistan's foreign exchange reserves increased marginally during the week ended September 18, with reserves held by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) rising by $11 million to $21.4 billion.
According to data released by the central bank on Thursday, the country's total liquid foreign reserves stood at $26.81 billion as of September 18, compared with the previous week. The total reserves included $21.4 billion held by the SBP and $5.41 billion held by commercial banks.
Furthermore, the Pakistani rupee gained Rs0.03 against the US dollar in the inter-bank market on Thursday, closing at 277.17, compared with 277.20 a day earlier.
Internationally, the US dollar held near a two-month high after strong manufacturing data revived inflation concerns and expectations of higher rates, while a weak US Treasury auction pushed yields higher.
Meanwhile, gold prices in Pakistan fell sharply, extending their decline for the fifth consecutive session, as international bullion prices came under pressure from rising crude oil prices, a stronger US dollar and expectations of higher rates from the Federal Reserve.
The price of gold per tola fell Rs5,600 during the day to Rs448,336, according to rates released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association (APGJSA). The price of 10-gram gold declined by Rs4,801 to Rs384,375. Gold had closed at Rs453,936 per tola on Wednesday after losing Rs1,800.
In the international market, spot gold fell 0.9% to $4,249.37 per ounce by 11:20 am ET (1520 GMT), after touching its lowest level since September 16, as per Reuters. US gold futures for December delivery declined 0.8% to $4,285 an ounce.
The decline came as higher oil prices reinforced concerns over inflation, potentially limiting the scope of monetary easing by the US central bank. Oil prices rose more than 1% on Thursday, adding to inflationary pressures.
Meanwhile, the US dollar climbed to a two-month high, while the yield on the 10-year US Treasury note rose to its highest level in two decades. A stronger dollar generally weighs on gold by making the dollar-denominated metal more expensive for holders of other currencies. Higher Treasury yields also reduce the appeal of non-yielding bullion.
Market participants have increasingly focused on the US Federal Reserve's rate outlook following a more hawkish shift in expectations. Higher-for-longer interest rates tend to put pressure on gold, which does not generate any yield. In the domestic market, silver prices also declined, falling Rs171 to Rs6,837 per tola.

title: Austerity steps to save only Rs17b
description: Austerity steps to save only Rs17b
content:
Secretary tells NA panel IMF programme implementation 'pretty strong'
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) conditions on sugar-sector liberalisation and spending on education and health have been missed but overall implementation of the programme remains "pretty strong", said the federal government's chief negotiator on Thursday.
In a briefing to the National Assembly Standing Committee on Finance on the IMF programme, Secretary Finance Imdad Ullah Bosal disclosed that new austerity measures would save only Rs16.8 billion. But he ducked a question from PPP MNA Hina Rabbani Khar whether the austerity scheme was merely rhetoric.
Bosal revealed that the reduction in fuel allocation for official vehicles by 50% would save Rs700 million during the three-month implementation period, while savings on account of a 5% cut in non-salary expenses for one year were Rs16.1 billion.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had announced the austerity policy in response to public criticism of the government's decision to pass on the financial burden of Middle East war to the people. The monthly petroleum levy collection is projected at Rs139 billion.
Headed by PPP's Syed Naveed Qamar, the standing committee got a detailed briefing from the finance ministry about the status of the IMF programme on the completion of two years.
Bosal, who is also the chief negotiator, stressed that there was pretty strong implementation of the IMF programme; therefore, there had not been many difficulties in reaching staff-level agreements in the past. He shared the implementation status report of the previous three reviews but did not give the final status of implementation of conditions for the fourth review due to ongoing parleys with the IMF. However, he did share the final status of a couple of conditions.
Three provinces had agreed on sugar-sector liberalisation but one province had certain reservations, said Bosal. He did not name the province but a member of the committee said it was Sindh. Bosal said discussions with the province were ongoing to address its concerns.
According to the IMF condition, the federal and provincial governments will agree and the federal cabinet will adopt a national policy for sugar-market liberalisation on licensing, price controls, import, export permissions and zoning, and clear timelines for implementation. But in breach of the condition to approve the policy by June this year, the federal government is still exercising export and import controls and allowed export of 308,000 metric tons of sugar in recent days.
The government is advancing work towards full liberalisation of the sugar sector and has shared draft recommendations for a national policy with provincial governments, according to the finance ministry.
The IMF had also imposed a condition to collect agricultural income tax from landlords and farmers but its implementation too remains slow. The IMF on Thursday held a meeting with the Sindh government to review the implementation status. Naveed Qamar said the fate of traders' scheme and agricultural income tax scheme was the same as the increase in tax rates from 15% to 45% on agricultural income could not force people to pay taxes.
Chairman of the standing committee also observed that the federal government was dragging its feet on making public the declarations of civil servants. The secretary finance said the condition would now be fully implemented by December this year. The committee decided to take a briefing from the Establishment Division and the FBR on assets declaration.
The secretary finance said the health and educational spending targets could not be met because of some provinces and it remained a recurring concern in almost every review. Against the target of spending Rs3.47 trillion on health and education in the last fiscal year, the five governments spent Rs3.1 trillion. As the FBR missed tax collection targets, Bosal said, the federal government had to request provinces to curtail their expenses.
The condition to amend the Sovereign Wealth Fund (SWF) Act and other legislation to adopt appropriate governance mechanisms and safeguards following international standards and good practices has also been missed. Bosal said the IMF mentioned that Pakistan was neither Qatar nor Norway, which could make investment through the SWF.
Special Secretary Finance Qumar Abbasi said the current law empowered the SWF to retain 50% of dividends of companies but it had now been proposed that the income would first go to the government and it would then decide about any further distribution.
The condition on amending laws for nine additional statutory SOEs to bring them in line with the SOE Act could also not be met. The secretary finance said the laws of Port Qasim Authority, Gwadar Port Authority, Karachi Port Trust, State Life Insurance Corporation, National Telecommunication Corporation and Pakistan Railways would be amended. Qumar Abbasi said out of the nine, three laws had already been passed but the rest were at various stages of approval.
There was also an IMF condition for making a comprehensive assessment of the anti-corruption regime. The secretary finance informed the meeting that the PM had tasked the law minister and the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) to lead the development of an action plan to mitigate corruption vulnerabilities in the top 10 government departments having the highest corruption risks.
The secretary finance said NAB was undertaking a corruption assessment to which Naveed Qamar expressed concern that it could again empower NAB under the guise of the IMF. The condition on amending the SECP Act remains unimplemented. The government is required to submit in parliament legislative amendments to the Companies Act 2017 to strengthen compliance for unlisted firms, modernise corporate governance structures and align corporate regulations with international best practices. Bosal said about 114 amendments would be made subject to approval by parliament.
The conditions for putting a floor on the net tax revenues collected by the FBR from retailers under the Tajir Dost scheme and the floor on the net tax revenues collected by the FBR were also missed. On a question about the failure of the fixed tax scheme for traders, the secretary finance said the response had so far been very slow and there was a need to take remedial measures.

title: Tom Cruise gets outrageous in 'Digger' | The Express Tribune
description:
Tom Cruise gets 
outrageous in 'Digger'
content:
Royal premiere brings Inarritu's mysterious new film to London spotlight
Tom Cruise described his character in 'Digger' as "totally outrageous" and unlike any role he had encountered before, as he spoke at the world premiere of the film in London this week.
"He's the kind of character that says things that some people think, some people can't imagine thinking," the Hollywood star told Reuters. "I've never read a character like it. I've never read a film like this."
The film's release was celebrated with a royal premiere attended by Britain's Prince William and Princess Kate, following what actor Sandra Huller described as nearly a decade of work by Oscar-winning director Alejandro G Inarritu.
'Digger' has generated considerable anticipation since its trailer showed Cruise transformed into eccentric oil tycoon Digger Rockwell, complete with grey hair, facial prosthetics and a padded bodysuit.
Cruise said the physical transformation was far from the most demanding aspect of the role, pointing instead to a 10-minute monologue that was filmed in a single take.
'Anatomy of a Fall' star Huller said it was "remarkable" to watch Cruise's performance. "It feels like all the things that he has learned in 46 years of acting have come into this character," she said.
In the film, Rockwell inadvertently triggers an ecological disaster that pushes the world to the brink of nuclear war before scrambling to save the planet. Filmmakers have revealed little else about the story, fuelling speculation about the plot and rumours that the film could be a musical, something Cruise has dismissed.
"If you experience the film without knowing anything about it, it's much better than if you knew before," Huller said, adding that the secrecy was not intended to create intrigue for its own sake.
Cruise described the story as an exploration of "power and greed...responsibility and irresponsibility", while Australian actor Sophie Wilde said it also carried a message about art being "a vessel for catharsis".
Inarritu, whose previous credits include 'Birdman' and 'The Revenant', compared the process of making 'Digger' to painting, saying every frame was carefully crafted to immerse audiences in the world of the film.
For Emma D'Arcy, that attention to detail made working with the Mexican filmmaker feel like being part of an orchestra led by a conductor. "With 'Digger', musicality was really, really important...it's a comedy, and so rhythm is kind of key," D'Arcy said.
'Call Me by Your Name' star Michael Stuhlbarg recalled scenes constantly evolving during filming, with new dialogue, alternative versions and unexpected additions emerging from one day to the next.
The actor joked that so much unusual material was shot that he hoped a DVD containing additional footage from the production might one day be released. "There was a lot of fun to be had," he said.
'Digger' will begin its global cinematic rollout on September 30 and will be released in cinemas in the United States and the United Kingdom on October 2.

content:
285 objects generate funds almost 20 times the estimate
An auction of French screen legend Brigitte Bardot's personal items, ranging from straw hats, sunglasses, nightgowns to tableware and furniture, fetched nearly €1 million in Paris, almost 20 times the estimate, the Millon auction house told AFP.
At the auction of a total of 285 objects generated tremendous enthusiasm, an AFP journalist said. The proceeds will go to Bardot's animal welfare foundation and to Nicolas-Jacques Charrier, her only child.
Bardot died in December aged 91. The Brigitte Bardot Foundation, founded by the actor in 1986, said it has taken in 13,000 animals through four shelters and 150 partner facilities, supports 350 groups in France and operates in 70 countries.
Some 3,000 French and international bidders had registered for the auction. "Brigitte Bardot has once again proved to be a remarkable alchemist: she transformed about 50,000 in estimates into nearly a million euros including fees," said auctioneer Alexandre Millon.
Two dog collars, with an ID tag bearing Bardot's name and the telephone number for La Madrague, estimated at 30 euros for the pair, were sold for €9,400 to a Russian buyer. A self-portrait fetched nearly €40,000.
The typewriter she used to write an autobiography sold for €4,634. Estimated at between €300 and 500, two of her guitars soared to 8,600 and €11,900 euros while three stuffed toys representing baby seals sold for nearly €2,200 euros.
"This sale is the logical continuation of the one she herself organised in 1987 with her most precious belongings to create her foundation. Today, her fight continues through this auction," Ghyslaine Calmels, managing director of the Bardot Foundation, told AFP after the sale.
Two days before the auction, Bernard d'Ormale, Brigitte Bardot's last husband, slammed it as a "joke". "These are personal items. Why hold this sale? For the animals? It's a joke," Bernard d'Ormale told AFP, adding it amounted to a "disrespect to Brigitte's memory".
Her belongings should have been preserved as part of her legacy rather than sold to raise funds for the foundation she created, d'Ormale argued, adding that Bardot "would not have agreed to this sale".
The Brigitte Bardot Foundation rejected the criticism, saying the auction was approved by the board in June, including Bardot's widower, who was then its president. However, d'Ormale said he had not understood the auction would involve such personal items.
The dispute comes days after he was removed as head of the foundation, a role he had held since the star's death.

title: Gerwig brings Narnia back to big screen

content:
'The Magician's Nephew' marks first screen adaptation of CS Lewis' origin story
A new chapter in the beloved world of Narnia is coming to cinemas on February 12, 2027, with Oscar-nominated filmmaker Greta Gerwig bringing CS Lewis's 'The Magician's Nephew' to the big screen for the first time.
Written for the screen and directed by Gerwig, 'Narnia: The Magician's Nephew' will open in IMAX and cinemas worldwide, with exclusive IMAX previews beginning on February 10. The film will also arrive on Netflix on April 2.
The film explores the origin of Narnia and the events that precede 'The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe'. The cast combines newcomers David McKenna and Beatrice Campbell with established performers including Emma Mackey, Carey Mulligan, Ciarán Hinds, Daniel Craig, Meryl Streep, Kobna Holdbrook-Smith, Denise Gough and Susan Wokoma.
For Gerwig, the project carries a personal connection. She has spoken of reading 'The Magician's Nephew' as a child. "I was a child when I first read 'The Magician's Nephew', and I fell in love with the gorgeously improbable but completely brilliant concept of a cosmic lion singing the world of Narnia to life," she said.
Gerwig revealed why she cast Streep as Aslan. "I wanted someone who was profound but not pretentious, who had gravitas but not morose self-seriousness. Someone who could communicate depth and pathos as well as joy and delight," Gerwig told Empire in an interview.
First published in 1955, 'The Magician's Nephew' explores how the links between our world and Narnia began. The seven Chronicles of Narnia books have sold more than 120 million copies across 70 countries and have been translated into more than 60 languages.
Gerwig described the opportunity to bring Lewis's world to the screen as "the honour of a lifetime", recalling how the books made her believe in magic, hidden worlds and adventure. With Gerwig now at the helm, the latest Narnia adventure is set to introduce Lewis's fantastical world to another generation of audiences.

description: Taylor Swift keeps  Showgirl  curtain open
content:
Four new songs arrive as the pop superstar heads into a high-profile MTV Video Music Awards week
Taylor Swift is extending the life of her record-breaking album 'The Life of a Showgirl' with a new edition featuring four previously unreleased songs, including 'Patient Zero', as the pop superstar enters another high-profile week ahead of the MTV Video Music Awards.
Swift announced 'The Life of a Showgirl: Encore', revealing that the new edition will be released on Friday (today) with 'Patient Zero', 'Cleveland!', 'Pink Clouding' and 'Babylon'. The songs, she said, were written during a trip to Sweden with collaborators Max Martin and Shellback to celebrate the success of the original album.
The trip, Swift said, was a chance "to reflect and take in how grateful we were for the moment we were in". She described the four songs as having been "born out of pure gratitude" for the enthusiasm and celebration shown by her fans.
The announcement followed another characteristically cryptic Swift rollout. On Tuesday, she launched a countdown clock on her website, displayed against a red curtain and set to expire at 2pm. Swifties quickly began searching for clues, particularly after her Instagram bio was changed to read "And, baby, that's sh0w business f0r y0u", with the letter 'o' replaced by zeros.
Once the countdown ended, Swift's website revealed limited-edition CD versions of 'Patient Zero', including one with a double-sided cover and acoustic and piano versions. Each was priced at $3.99.
'Patient Zero' marks Swift's first new song since she contributed 'I Knew It, I Knew You' to the 'Toy Story 5' soundtrack in June. It is also the latest release surrounding an unusually active period for the singer following her wedding to Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce at Madison Square Garden in July. The new edition will become the 29th variation of 'The Life of a Showgirl' since the album was released last October. The original release was followed by 11 CD variants, 11 vinyl variants and six cassette or digital versions, featuring different artwork and extras including poems, voice memos and acoustic tracks.
The album made history by earning 3.5 million equivalent album units in less than a week, breaking Adele's record for the biggest opening week for an album. The scale of the releases, however, drew criticism online from some fans and critics who argued that Swift was using multiple editions to chase industry records and capitalise on the willingness of her audience to spend heavily.
'The Life of a Showgirl', Swift's 12th studio album, was described by The New York Times as her "conscious return to straight-up pop music". Its opening track, 'The Fate of Ophelia', has surpassed 1.67 billion streams on Spotify.
The new songs have already prompted speculation among Swifties about their possible themes. 'Cleveland!', with its exclamation mark, recalls earlier titles such as 'Cancelled!' and is widely expected by fans to draw on Swift's personal life and her connection to Kelce, who is from Cleveland Heights, Ohio.
'Pink Clouding' has been linked by fans to the phrase "pink cloud syndrome", which describes feelings of euphoria and elation. 'Babylon', named after the ancient city associated with eventual decline, is being interpreted as potentially fitting the album's existing themes of fame and navigating the global spotlight.
'Patient Zero', meanwhile, has been speculated to have a darker connection to the album's idea of 'The Death Of A Showgirl'.
Swift's music announcement also arrives just days before Sunday's MTV Video Music Awards, where she is due to receive the inaugural Artist Director Honors. The award recognises artists whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music videos and advanced visual storytelling.
Swift is currently tied with Beyonce at 30 VMA awards and has nine nominations this year, behind Madonna's 11. If the new honour is counted alongside her existing haul, Swift will become the most awarded artist in VMA history.
Her appearance at the ceremony had already fuelled speculation among fans that she might use the event for another announcement, given her history of unveiling projects around major appearances.
That speculation intensified after a pretaped Swift appearance in an Emmys skit last week. Playing a rookie in the 'Law & Order: Special Victims Unit' office, Swift appeared alongside Mariska Hargitay's Olivia Benson as characters investigated whether the singer would attend the ceremony.
At one point, Swift appeared to offer a series of cryptic clues: "Saccharide. Ares. From the Vineyard. North or South." Fans immediately began trying to decode the message.
Swift ultimately did not attend the Emmys telecast, instead watching the Kansas City Chiefs open their NFL season against the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium alongside actor Tom Cruise. With 'Patient Zero' now confirmed, at least one mystery surrounding Swift's latest clues has gained a clearer meaning.
And as the singer heads towards the MTV Video Music Awards, the new release adds another chapter to the continuing 'Showgirl' era - one that has already broken records, generated debate and now has four more songs to its name.

title: The colours of a living heritage | The Express Tribune
description:
The colours of a 
living heritage
content:
Quetta celebrates Pashtun Culture Day with traditional dress, crafts and performances
Pashtun Culture Day was observed in Quetta and other parts of Balochistan on Wednesday with traditional enthusiasm, with cultural events showcasing the community's traditional dress, handicrafts, jewellery and heritage.
Various cultural programmes were organised at different locations across Quetta, where stalls displaying traditional clothing, jewellery, handicrafts and other cultural items attracted visitors.
Women, young people and children dressed in traditional Pashtun attire to express their connection with their cultural heritage, while traditional Attan performances added colour to the celebrations.
Speaking to The Express Tribune, women and young participants said Pashtun Culture Day was more than a cultural occasion, describing it as an important opportunity to highlight the centuries-old history, traditions and cultural heritage of the Pashtun people.
Participants said the Pashtun people had a long history and were known for traditions including hospitality, tolerance and bravery. They said the jirga system and other traditional values had also held an important place in Pashtun society.
Women said the observance of the cultural day also aimed to familiarise younger generations with their language, traditional dress, customs and cultural heritage. They said preserving these traditions would help future generations remain connected to their identity and history.
Young participants said preserving cultural traditions had become particularly important in the modern era. They said the day provided an opportunity for the younger generation to learn about and take pride in its history and cultural heritage.
Similar celebrations were held in Pishin, Qila Abdullah, Qila Saifullah, Chaman, Loralai, Zhob and other parts of Balochistan, where various cultural programmes and events were organised.

title: The other good side of social media | The Express Tribune
description:
The other good side 
of social media
content:
How women are turning online platforms into thriving businesses and sources of income
Women entrepreneurs in Islamabad and Rawalpindi are turning smartphones and laptops into sustainable businesses, running successful online stores, freelance services and digital brands from home and becoming financially independent.
With growing internet access, digital payment solutions and government training programmes like DigiSkills and e-Rozgaar, a new generation of women business owners is emerging, proving that a small online idea can become a big enterprise.
Women are emerging as queens of their own online enterprises, earning handsome incomes and becoming financially independent, often as sole breadwinners for their families. From home-based bakeries and Instagram clothing stores to freelancing and YouTube channels, they are transforming mobile screens into thriving shops and offices.
Islamabad-based Aneela Tariq, 30, owner of 'Aneela's Bake O'Clock', started baking cakes at home during Covid-19 and began taking orders on Instagram. Today she receives 20 to 30 orders daily and earns over Rs 200,000 a month.
"I started with one oven and a Facebook page. Now I have three staff members, all women from my neighborhood. Online business gave me identity and income without leaving my home," she told APP. She added that many who were once dependent on others are now covering school fees, managing household expenses and supporting their parents.
Similarly, Zara Ahmed, founder of 'Zara- Handmade Jewelry' based in Rawalpindi, sells handmade earrings and clutches through Daraz and Instagram to customers across Pakistan and Dubai. "My shop is online, my customers are online. I don't need a big plaza. I started with Rs 10,000 and now my monthly turnover is Rs 300,000," she said.
Sumbal Sheikh, who runs 'Modest Wear by Sumbal', an online abaya store, said women feel more comfortable selling online. "Many women cannot go to markets daily due to family responsibilities. Online work allows us to manage both home and business. I manage my store, parcels and payments from my mobile."
Experts say if provided better internet access, digital literacy and safe online payment mechanisms, women-led online businesses can significantly contribute to Pakistan's e-commerce economy.
For these women, the screen is no longer just for scrolling, it is a shop, an office and a path to self-reliance.

title: Is moving on really moving too fast
description: Is moving on really moving too fast
content:
Stars and fans debate changing attitudes towards the end of marriage
A candid discussion about divorce has turned into one of the latest celebrity debates in Pakistan, after veteran actor Saba Faisal questioned how society now responds to the end of marriages, prompting strong reactions from fellow actors and fans over grief, stigma and women's right to leave difficult relationships.
Faisal made the comments during an appearance on a TV's talk show, where she reflected on what she described as a significant change in social attitudes towards divorce.
"Before, when someone used to get divorced, there used to be a 'Sog' happening for months," Faisal said, referring to the mourning and grief that traditionally followed a divorce within a family. She contrasted that response with what she sees today, saying that divorced women could now casually mention their separation during conversations before moving on with their lives.
"Dads couldn't do anything, but now when we find out girls have got divorced, it's mentioned casually over a phone call," she said, adding that she had travelled abroad afterwards and tried to figure things out.
Her comments quickly spread online, with celebrities and social media users divided over whether the changing response to divorce represents a loss of sensitivity towards marriage or a greater willingness to acknowledge that marriages can end for different reasons.
Actor Hira Khan was among the strongest voices to respond. In an Instagram story, she wrote, "It's better to go through this than to be carried through a grave," before adding, "She needs help."
Khan argued that divorce should not be confused with celebration and highlighted the circumstances that can make leaving a marriage a matter of safety and dignity. "No one celebrates divorce," she wrote, adding that women have a religiously recognised right to seek it.
She also criticised what she described as the policing and shaming of women who choose to leave marriages. "I'm half your age, but I understand this much," Khan wrote. "Perhaps I was raised to understand that a woman's dignity, safety and right to choose matter."
Faisal's daughter, actor Sadia Faisal, subsequently appeared to respond to Khan, writing, "I wish I could see this so-called actress someday."
Actor Zoya Nasir also entered the discussion, writing in the comments, "Oh. My. God. I have SO much to say, with all due respect. What a dangerous and twisted narrative."
Not everyone, however, agreed with the criticism directed at Faisal. Dr Ejaz Waris offered a more conciliatory perspective, agreeing that divorce should not be celebrated while arguing that its emotional impact can extend to both families.
Fans similarly debated whether discussions about divorce had unfairly focused on the woman's family. Some pointed out that the husband's family can also experience grief, while others argued that the depth of that pain is difficult to understand until a divorce involves one's own daughter.
At the same time, some users defended Faisal, saying her central point was simply that divorce had become more normalised and that people could now return to their everyday lives more quickly following a separation.
The controversy comes shortly after Faisal spoke at length in another interview about the way her comments are handled online. She criticised the practice of editing remarks into short clips designed to generate viral reactions.
"The respect and honour we have built over our entire lives gets severely disturbed when a couple of words are spliced together and edited into the video," she said. Calling virality "a strange illness", Faisal said she had begun taking longer breaks from public appearances because of the way apparently ordinary remarks could be repackaged into controversy.
The actor has also previously attracted criticism for her views on marriage and family, making her latest comments part of a broader public discussion around traditional expectations and changing attitudes among younger generations.
At the heart of the latest debate is a distinction that has emerged repeatedly in the reactions: acknowledging divorce as a painful experience does not necessarily mean treating it as something desirable, while reducing stigma does not necessarily erase the grief associated with the end of a marriage.
For some of Faisal's critics, a woman being able to move forward after divorce is a sign of greater acceptance rather than indifference. For those defending her, the actor was drawing attention to what she sees as a decline in the social and familial gravity once attached to the breakdown of a marriage.
