title: Amazon bets  3b on India s fast delivery boom  sources say
description: India s  19 billion quick commerce market is expected to more than double to  41 billion by 2030
content:
India's $19 billion quick-commerce market is expected to more than double to $41 billion by 2030
US e-commerce retailer Amazon will invest $3 billion to expand ​its India quick commerce business by 2030, two sources said, its biggest bet yet on a sector where rivals have raced ahead by ‌popularising deliveries within minutes.
The instant deliveries sector, dubbed "quick commerce", has become a rapidly growing force and reshaped how urban Indians shop for everything from milk and chocolates to iPhones and electronics, which were once only bought from retail stores or major e-commerce websites where deliveries took time.
Walmart's Flipkart and Amazon, which dominate India's e-commerce space, are late entrants in quick commerce . The $19 billion sector is set ​to more than double in size to $41 billion by 2030, according to Datum Intelligence.
Amazon plans to invest $1 billion in the quick commerce sector by the ​end of 2027, and another $2 billion by 2030, two people with direct knowledge of the plans said. The planned investment has ⁠not previously been reported.
Amazon declined to comment on the planned investment numbers. The retailer, however, said its quick commerce business has crossed $1 billion in annualised gross sales over ​the past three months, "making it the fastest-growing e-commerce business in Amazon India's history."
A key focus of the planned investment will be adding new small neighbourhood ​warehouses to the current Amazon Now service network from where deliveries are shipped quickly, said both sources, who declined to be identified as the plan is confidential.
"Expansion needs money," the first source said.
Amazon counts India as a key growth market, where it is expanding its data centre, cloud and e-commerce businesses.
Read More: Meta's Charm gadget carries CEO Zuckerberg's big AI ambitions
But it also faces India's tight regulations for foreign e-commerce companies and a pending 2024 case ​in which it was found by the antitrust watchdog to have given preference to select sellers in breach of the law — allegations it denies.
The sector's rise since ​2022 coincided with growing concerns about rider safety as bikers zip through residential areas to deliver orders fast. India's government in January ordered companies to stop promoting such operations as "10-minute" services.
Domestic giants Eternal's Blinkit, ‌Swiggy and ⁠IPO-bound Zepto control 77% of the market, together operating more than 4,500 stores, while Walmart's Flipkart has more than 1,000 and an 11% market share, Datum data shows.
Amazon has only a 6.2% market share. The first source said Amazon was targeting around 1,300 stores by April next year, from around 750 now.
The other key areas of spending, the first person added, will be strengthening inventory management software at stores, deploying AI tools for demand prediction and expanding product selection.
"The focus will ​be daily essentials. If the order is ​unlikely to be repeated, Amazon does ⁠not plan to stock it right now in quick commerce," said the person, explaining why Amazon does not stock iPhones like its quick commerce rivals.
Bernstein in a July note warned that groceries alone cannot cover the high costs of quick commerce as average ​order values are low, and "non-grocery items carry higher prices and higher margins."
Amazon does not agree with critics who say it ​missed the bus, one ⁠of the sources said. The company wanted to get the model right, such as having a cold storage room in each store and not just a refrigerator.
Satish Meena, founder of Datum Intelligence, said it will not be easy for Amazon to catch up with rivals who offer quality service and have loyal customers, but it could lure their shopping website ⁠customers to ​fast deliveries.
The Amazon Now service, which sits within the main Amazon app, is currently offering a ​20% cashback discount on some initial orders above 499 rupees ($5.20), and free delivery above 99 rupees ($1) for select customers.
"It took some time for Amazon to commit. There appears to be a realisation that this is ​a model they have to invest in," Meena said. "They are doing discounts, which can help lure current Amazon customers to quick commerce."

title: Karachi Port freight plan sparks sustainability debate
description: As Sindh plans a Rs64b road corridor for port freight  experts call for greater use of rail  sea and vacant KPT land
content:
As Sindh plans a Rs64b road corridor for port freight, experts call for greater use of rail, sea and vacant KPT land
A proposed Rs64 billion road corridor for heavy freight between Karachi Port and Qayyumabad has revived a long-running question: should the city keep expanding roads for port traffic or invest more heavily in rail and sea transport?
The Sindh government plans to develop the 16.5-kilometre Karachi Port–Qayyumabad Corridor Project (KPQCP) under a public-private partnership. But experts and officials say the project may provide only a short-term answer to Karachi’s growing freight movement, while greater use of rail, sea routes and existing port land could offer longer-term benefits.
Around 80 per cent of Pakistan’s freight is currently transported by road and only 20 per cent by rail. Experts say the heavy dependence on roads increases fuel consumption, infrastructure and maintenance costs, while adding to congestion and pollution.
At a recent Sindh Environmental Protection Agency hearing on the project’s environmental impact, residents of Defence, Clifton and Qayyumabad and representatives of social and environmental organisations raised concerns over the proposed corridor. Environmental experts suggested using the railway network and Northern Bypass to move Karachi Port freight instead.
Several Karachi Port Trust (KPT) officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, said another option was available within the port itself. According to the officials, KPT owns hundreds of acres of vacant land in Mai Kolachi and other areas that could be developed into low-cost container storage and terminal facilities.
The officials noted that such facilities could reduce storage and handling costs for importers and exporters and eventually lower the prices of imported food, machinery, computers, vehicles and other goods.
The officials said KPT had previously proposed using its vacant land for container storage, but the plan was not approved. They alleged that housing schemes and commercial projects were given priority instead.
They also raised concerns about private off-dock facilities. According to the officials, shipping companies have obtained KPT land on leases ranging from 30 to 50 years at relatively low rates, while charging importers and exporters higher daily storage fees.
Read More: Aurangzeb highlights Pakistan's climate vulnerability, calls for faster climate financing at UNGA
Exporters pay until containers are loaded onto ships, while importers continue paying until they are moved by truck or train, creating pressure for quick clearance and adding to congestion. Heavy freight vehicles are generally restricted to 11pm-6am, yet congestion remains common on Shahrah-e-Pakistan, Clifton and Defence.
Rail could ease the pressure, but Pakistan Railways lacks the infrastructure to handle large container volumes. Only 52 commercial freight trains operate annually from Karachi Port, according to the report.
The proposed Pipri Marshalling Yard would store containers before they are sent to other cities, but KPT officials said importers and exporters have concerns because it is about 50 kilometres from the port. They said 47 per cent of Karachi Port’s commercial activity is linked to Karachi, meaning transport to Pipri could increase costs for local businesses.
A Pakistan Railways officer said the Pipri project dates back to the British era and remains necessary. He believed modernising the East and West Wharf stations could also allow direct freight movement to industrial areas such as S.I.T.E.
The Pakistan Railways spokesperson added that the Pipri project had not been cancelled but incorporated into ML-1, for which an international advertisement has been issued.
Dr Muhammad Ahmed of NED University opined that Karachi’s ports needed both road and rail links, but in a balanced manner. He described the KPQCP, which will connect with Shahrah-e-Bhutto and the M-9, as a short-term measure that could ease congestion but would not meet future growth in port traffic.
"Railway infrastructure should be upgraded because rail requires less fuel and generally has lower construction and maintenance costs, while reducing the number of heavy vehicles on city roads," explained Dr Ahmed, who further endorsed greater use of rail for Karachi Port and Port Qasim freight and the development of dry ports at suitable locations.
Railway Workers Union central chairman Manzoor Zia called for early completion of ML-1 and the Pipri Marshalling Yard. He urged that the Karachi-Lahore railway track should be upgraded even before ML-1 so both passenger and freight trains could operate at higher speeds.
Climate Action Center Director Yasir Hussain believed Karachi needed an integrated freight system, with sea, rail and road networks used according to their strengths. “Greater reliance should be placed on sea and rail for freight transportation,” he opined.
Hussain suggested using small vessels to move containers between Karachi Port, Port Qasim and other locations. Strengthening the railway system, he added, could reduce pollution and traffic congestion while saving fuel.
The KPT spokesperson was contacted several times for their comments, but they failed to respond.

title: Macklemore announces  Free Palestine  tour with proceeds going to charity
description: The Free Palestine tour will currently include three European dates  beginning in Dublin on October 26
content:
The Free Palestine tour will currently include three European dates, beginning in Dublin on October 26
Macklemore has announced a new Free Palestine tour, with all ticket proceeds set to be donated to organisations supporting Palestinians.
The rapper announced the new run of shows on September 24, just days after being removed from the remaining US dates of Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour following his onstage statements in support of Palestine.
The Free Palestine tour will currently include three European dates, beginning in Dublin on October 26. Macklemore will then perform in Paris on October 29 before concluding the announced European leg at London’s OVO Arena Wembley on October 30. Further US dates are expected to be announced at a later date.
Macklemore said he had spent the past week contacting artists who had publicly supported Palestinians and were willing to use their platforms despite potential consequences. He added that additional artists would be announced for the tour.
The announcement comes after Macklemore was removed from Sheeran’s US stadium tour earlier this month. The rapper had used his performances at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium to speak about the situation in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, including leading the crowd in saying “Free Palestine”. He also performed his protest song Hind’s Hall, accompanied by images related to the destruction in Gaza.
Tour promoter Messina Touring Group subsequently announced that Macklemore would no longer perform on the remaining dates after venues indicated that they would not allow concerts featuring him to take place. The promoter said keeping him on the line-up could have resulted in the cancellation of the remaining shows.
Macklemore has continued to speak publicly about the decision. He previously announced that he would donate the $1 million in net earnings he received from his work on Sheeran’s tour to organisations supporting Palestinians. He also invited New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft to match the donation.
For the new tour, Macklemore has selected 12 organisations to receive proceeds from the shows. They include Anera, Glia, Gaza Soup Kitchen, Taawon, HEAL Palestine, Palestinian Youth Movement, Middle East Children’s Alliance, Jewish Voice for Peace, Medical Aid for Palestinians, the Institute for Middle East Understanding, Palestine Children’s Relief Fund and UNRWA USA.
The organisations work across areas including medical assistance, humanitarian aid, education, community support, advocacy and Palestinian-related media and organising.
In announcing the tour, Macklemore said the events of the past few weeks had reinforced his view that artists were increasingly being asked to use their platforms for issues beyond entertainment. He also said the controversy surrounding his removal from Sheeran’s tour was part of a wider discussion about who gets to speak on major concert stages.
Tickets for the newly announced shows will go on general sale on September 30, with presale access beginning earlier. Macklemore has also indicated that more dates and performers will be announced.
The Free Palestine tour represents Macklemore’s first announced run of shows since his departure from Sheeran’s tour and comes as the controversy surrounding his political statements continues to draw attention across the music industry.

title: Meta s Charm gadget carries CEO Zuckerberg s big AI ambitions
description: Zuckerberg now sees  personal superintelligence  as a bigger breakthrough after his costly metaverse bet faltered
content:
Zuckerberg now sees "personal superintelligence" as a bigger breakthrough after his costly metaverse bet faltered
Mark Zuckerberg ​took repeated digs at Apple during Meta's annual event on Wednesday, only to borrow a page from Steve Jobs' playbook for a surprise ‌reveal: a pocket-watch-sized device that carries Meta's viral Muse AI agent into the real world.
The device, called Muse Charm, highlights a broader shift at the social media giant that has long sought to escape Apple and Google's operating systems with a platform of its own. Users can tap the gadget to access Muse directly, bypassing AI apps on smartphones.
Having once championed the metaverse — the immersive digital world ​that inspired the company's name change in 2021 — as the next computing platform, Zuckerberg now sees "personal superintelligence" as the bigger and more immediate breakthrough, after ​his previous costly wager failed.
"It is actually quite clear personal superintelligence will not only come first; it will be much bigger and ⁠more important," Zuckerberg said at the company's annual Meta Connect conference.
"So we have shifted our focus to building the best devices for personal superintelligence," he said, adding that ​Muse would also soon be available across Meta's smart glasses lineup.
The remarks follow a blockbuster few days for Muse, which has drawn millions of downloads in what some analysts have ​said could be the biggest app launch in the US since ChatGPT arrived in November 2022 and kicked off the AI boom.
Investors have embraced Muse's potential to automate tasks ranging from booking flights to filing taxes, lifting shares of partners such as Shopify while dumping companies seen as vulnerable to disruption, including online travel agency Booking and TurboTax software creator Intuit.
Read More: German court rules Meta liable for fake ads on Instagram, Facebook
Meta shares climbed more than ​3% on Thursday after rising nearly 24% since the launch of Muse on September 8. The company was on track to add about $56 billion in market value, after ​gaining roughly $324 billion through Wednesday's close.
May appeal to Gen Z, mass adoption difficult
Muse Charm could resonate with younger consumers at a time when digital cameras, flip phones and MP3 players are enjoying ‌nostalgic comebacks, ⁠analysts say.
Gen Z consumers, aged about 14 to 29, treat AI assistants as companions or brainstorming partners rather than simply search tools. Many interact with technology through voice notes, short videos and AI chatbots, unlike older users who are often more comfortable with PCs and smartphone apps.
"Muse Charm could find some traction among Gen Z and younger consumers. The combination of AI, fashion and personalization could appeal to younger users, especially if it is affordable and easy to use," said Linda Sui, founder of Smart Analytics Global, ​a market research firm.
The device features a ​roughly 2-inch (5-cm) screen that can be navigated ⁠with a thumb, with a customizable Muse character at its center. A built-in 5G modem allows access to Muse even without Wi-Fi, though it cannot make calls.
"They are appealing to people who might not want to wear glasses or might not trust glasses," ​said IDC director Jitesh Ubrani.
"Some people might remember Tamagotchi and this might evoke that," Ubrani said, referring to colorful virtual ​pets that became a ⁠cultural phenomenon in the late 1990s. "They might be able to run a small language model locally. So you can run AI on such a small package."
Whether Muse can sustain its momentum and the device can amplify that appeal is a question for the months ahead.
Similar devices have had limited success. The Rabbit R1, a handheld generative AI device from startup Rabbit ⁠Inc with ​a screen and a button, had a buzzy launch in early 2024 only to flop because it ​overpromised on AI features and delivered an unreliable experience.
"I would be cautious about its mass-market potential," Sui said. "Unless Muse Charm can offer unique functions that smartphones, watches, earbuds or smart glasses cannot easily replace, it is ​more likely to remain a nice-to-have device for early adopters than become a mainstream product."

title: Google plans first test of AI chips in space under Project Suncatcher
description: Google said it tested TPUs at UC Davis but needed orbital tests to assess their performance in space
content:
Google said it tested TPUs at UC Davis but needed orbital tests to assess their performance in space
Alphabet's Google said on Thursday it will launch a prototype satellite next week in its first in-orbit test of Project Suncatcher, ​a research effort to explore whether space could potentially host ‌large-scale AI computing infrastructure.
Companies including SpaceX and Starcloud are pursuing plans to deploy data centers in low Earth orbit, aiming to harness near-continuous sunlight to power ​energy-intensive AI computing and sidestep terrestrial constraints on electricity supplies.
The ​new mission, scheduled to fly on SpaceX's upcoming Transporter-18 rideshare ⁠launch in partnership with satellite company Planet Labs, will assess how ​Google's AI hardware withstands launch forces, radiation and extreme temperatures in ​LEO.
After the launch, it will send a prototype satellite carrying Google Tensor Processing Units into low Earth orbit to assess if the AI chips can operate reliably ​in space.
Space radiation can disrupt or degrade electronics, including by causing ​data errors known as bit flips.
Read More: Anthropic mulls releasing new AI model
Google said it tested its TPUs while running AI ‌workloads ⁠in a facility at the University of California, Davis, but that orbital testing was needed to understand how the hardware performs in the real environment.
The company will also evaluate its design to cool the power-intensive ​chips in the ​vacuum of ⁠space, where conventional airflow cooling is impossible, by combining heat pipes with radiators.
But experts have said that the ​concept remains years from being commercially viable given ​high launch ⁠costs, engineering constraints and satellite production bottlenecks.
The first Suncatcher mission is designed to gather in-orbit data and identify potential failure points, rather than demonstrate ⁠an ​operational orbital data center, Google said.
It aims ​to launch two satellites in 2027 to test the high-bandwidth laser links needed to connect ​future computing clusters.

title: Iranian flights cancelled as new US  D Day  sanctions take effect
description: US has announced to extend reach of its financial sanctions by targeting companies doing business with Iranian firms
content:
US has announced to extend reach of its financial sanctions by targeting companies doing business with Iranian firms
Iranian flights to Gulf neighbours, including travel hub Dubai, appeared to have been cancelled on Thursday after a US deadline passed for global firms to halt work with Iran's airlines, ​a major step in a campaign President Donald Trump calls "economic D-Day".
With the US-Israeli war against Iran largely stalemated for months on the battlefield, Washington has announced a shift in tactics to extend the reach of its financial sanctions by targeting companies from third countries that do business with Iranian firms, a practice known as "secondary sanctions".
Trump referred to the new strategy last month as "economic D-Day", comparing it ​to the assault on Nazi-controlled France in World War Two by the United States and its allies.
The US Treasury had set September 23 as the deadline for companies ​worldwide to comply with an order to stop doing business with Iranian airlines. Washington says the aim is to ground the entire global ⁠Iranian civilian fleet.
Read: Saudi Arabia reports fresh Houthi attacks, issues warning for Makkah
Iran threatened on Wednesday to retaliate against any neighbouring countries that comply with the US ban on its flights, by making their airports "unusable".
There were no immediate public announcements from countries ​that they were halting flights, but Iran's ISNA news agency said all flights to the United Arab Emirates, the Gulf's biggest travel hub, had been halted as of midnight.
No arrivals or departures ​to Iran were visible on the websites of Dubai or Abu Dhabi airports on Thursday. Websites of at least two Iranian airlines, Qeshm and Varesh, showed UAE flights had been cancelled.
State-run WAM news agency reported the UAE suspended flights by Iranian air carriers to and from the country until further notice.
The General Civil Aviation Authority said the decision took effect today.
In a statement carried by WAM , the authority said that “the decision was made in light of the US ban imposed on Iranian airlines from using airports in various countries around the world.”
The authority said it would continue to update relevant authorities and the public on any developments until air traffic between the UAE and Iran returned to normal.
It also urged the public to rely only on official sources for information.
The website of Iran's Imam Khomeini Airport in Tehran showed departures and arrivals on Thursday were still scheduled to and from countries including Afghanistan, Armenia, ​China, Iraq, Pakistan, Tajikistan and Turkey, but not nearby Gulf states. ISNA said a flight to Tajikistan had also been turned back because Turkmenistan had closed its airspace.
A flight ban, if ​sustained, could deepen Iran's isolation and worsen an economic crisis in the country, which is already facing a US blockade of its ports at sea.
"We are living in an open-air prison," a retired teacher in ‌Tehran told ⁠Reuters by text message on condition her name not be used.

title: Hacked FBI data has sensitive information about employees    intelligence roles
description: FBI says it is aware of a cyber criminal enterprise group claiming a compromise of the FBIJobs gov portal
content:
FBI says it is aware of a cyber-criminal enterprise group claiming a compromise of the FBIJobs.gov portal
FBI data allegedly stolen by the hacking group ShinyHunters carries granular detail about scores of bureau officials’ ​job assignments, including sensitive work against Chinese spies, Russian intelligence, drug cartels, and more, Reuters has found.
The 5,000-line spreadsheet — said by the hackers to represent only a small piece of ‌their claimed two- to three-terabyte trove — includes names, addresses, telephone numbers, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, and emergency contact details for what they claimed were thousands of FBI employees. It also includes details of assignments to specific field offices and, in some cases, to units engaged in high-stakes intelligence, security, or counterespionage work.
In a statement, the FBI said it was aware of "a cyber-criminal enterprise group claiming a compromise of the FBIJobs.gov portal and alleged impact to FBI employee personally identifiable information".
The bureau ​said the cause of the breach was still undetermined, but that it was "actively and aggressively investigating the matter".
The hackers said that they had breached the FBI, stealing data on a ​large number of current and former FBI employees. ShinyHunters said it is holding the data hostage until the bureau rescinds an unflattering statement about the group issued ⁠in May.
Read: FBI chief discusses specialised training to combat counterterrorism financing with Naqvi, hails 'critical' Pak-US partnership
Former FBI counterintelligence operative Eric O’Neill said the data allegedly stolen by ShinyHunters was “a foreign intelligence service goldmine”.
“China would be incredibly interested to know the individuals who are working against it,” said O’Neill, who founded ​the cybersecurity company Nexasure AI after his stint at the bureau. He predicted that other hostile intelligence services would be eager to get their hands on the data, along with disgruntled extremists in the United States.
“If I ​were on that list, I would be very concerned,” he said.
ShinyHunters said in a statement on Wednesday that it was trying to keep the personnel information from circulating widely in the meantime.
“If the 5,000 sample data records leak, it’s not because of us,” the group said.
Although Reuters has not been able to authenticate the entire spreadsheet, it has been able to individually verify the details of more than 22 people by cross-referencing information in the hacked data with credit records and previous data leaks ​carried by the dark web intelligence platform District 4 Labs.
Counterterrorism, counterintelligence and surveillance
Some of the assignment details in the ShinyHunters’ data are indistinguishable from what employees themselves might say publicly, noting agents at field offices in ​Baltimore or Newark, New Jersey, for example.
But in some cases, the data referred to FBI units or initiatives that were sensitive or whose existence has not previously been disclosed.
The data names 14 staffers focused on China-related matters, including members ‌of the “China criminal ⁠enterprise unit”, the “China tech transfer analysis unit” and the “China intelligence section”.
Nine others are listed as serving in Russia-related roles, including two in the “Russia Operations Section” and one working on “Russia Critical Infra and Tech Threat”. Three people are listed as working in Iran- or Hezbollah-focused intelligence roles.
Eighteen others are listed as working with “data intercept” or “telecom intercept” technologies, or in the FBI’s “clandestine technical operations” unit, or its “covert access section” or in video, audio, or electronic surveillance roles.
A further 11 FBI staffers are listed as working in HUMINT, or human intelligence, jobs, including several listed as working in the “Humint programme management section”.
Read more: ‘Extreme concern’ as OpenAI’s ‘rogue agent’ breached Australian govt health database
Trevor Hilligoss, a former army investigator who worked with the FBI, said ​the information tying specific named people to human intelligence ​work was particularly troubling.
“You don’t have to look ⁠far to find examples of undercover agents being harmed when their cover is blown,” he said.
Hilligoss, now the chief intelligence officer for cybersecurity company SpyCloud, said his concerns were heightened by the inclusion of emergency contacts — often spouses or children — “who may have less operational security knowledge than their relative that works in a sensitive ​field”.
Reuters could not verify that all the job assignments were authentic or up-to-date, but it was able to match the career details or titles of eight ​people whose data was leaked ⁠to information in court filings, news articles, or public profiles on LinkedIn or to online posts on sites such as Instagram.
ShinyHunters previously claimed credit for the purported theft of millions of business records from video game developer Rockstar Games, the maker of "Grand Theft Auto", and an intrusion focused on the education tool Canvas that triggered widespread disruption across US schools.
In May, the FBI said ShinyHunters sometimes used “exaggerated claims of access to sensitive or personal information to prompt payment from ⁠victims”.
ShinyHunters said ​its "threats and claims are very real”, adding that the FBI's statement was why it targeted the bureau.
Reuters has not been able to ​verify what else the hackers are holding. ShinyHunters previously told Reuters they obtained files related to the vetting of employees and applicants, the contracting of background investigations, and agents' sensitive medical data, but said on Wednesday it would not release any further data.
O’Neill, the ​former FBI operative, cautioned against drawing conclusions about what the hackers hold.
“They’re really trying to scare the hell out of the FBI,” he noted.

title: Fact check  Major roads including M1 and GT road leading to Islamabad are still closed ahead of PTI march
description: Claim by State Minister for Interior  Talal Chaudhry that all 125 roads to Islamabad are open to the public is false
content:
Claim by State Minister for Interior Talal Chaudhry that all 125 roads to Islamabad are open to the public is false
In a press conference on Sep 24, 2026, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry claimed that all 125 roads to Islamabad were open to the public. However, several major arteries to the federal capital are still closed.
The PTI had announced a long march towards Islamabad for September 27. The announcement came after the PTI observed a nationwide “black day” to mark three years of party founder Imran Khan’s imprisonment, demanding his immediate release and that of his wife, Bushra Bibi, restoration of what it termed constitutional rule and democracy, and relief from inflation.
As PTI gears up for Sept 27 protest in the federal capital, the Islamabad administration on Sep 23 reminded citizens that Section 144 was in force for two months, barring gatherings, rallies and demonstrations, and urged them to stay away from illegal activities and cooperate with security institutions.
The government has since set up impediments, cracked down on the party’s supporters and brought in containers as well.
On Sept 24, Chaudhry claimed in a press conference that all 125 roads to Islamabad were open to the public.
Chaudhry said: “You must have seen some WhatsApp status update, not the original situation. No road is closed. None are closed. No road was closed until this afternoon”
He further added, “Not a single road was closed. Until 12pm this afternoon, no road was closed, and as for the coming routes, 125 routes lead to Islamabad — how many? 125. All 125 routes are open.”
However, reporters in the room challenged his claims, citing conflicting ground realities and official notifications regarding motorway closures. Despite repeated questions about the disruptions and restrictions in place, Chaudhry dismissed the objections and rejected the reporters’ assertions about the blocked routes.
A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to keen public interest in the traffic situation and any roadblocks towards Islamabad due to the PTI’s long march.
A keyword search conducted to ascertain the road and traffic conditions of the capital yielded a news report from Dawn , dated September 23, 2026, with the following headline, “KP motorways, GT Road ‘closed indefinitely’”.
As per the news report, the government closed the Islamabad-Peshawar Motor­way (M1), the Islamabad-Dera Ismail Khan Motorway (M14) — also known as the CPEC road — and GT Road (N5) for an indefinite period from Sept 23 to stop the PTI protesters from reaching the federal capital on Sept 27. A spokesperson for the Nati­onal Highways and Moto­rway Police (NHMP) shared the closure would come into effect from Wednesday night.
Al Jazeera also reported the same on Sept 23 with the following headline, “Pakistan seals roads to Islamabad before protests for Imran Khan’s release”.
According to the report, police in Islamabad announced on Wednesday that the Islamabad-Peshawar Motorway, the Islamabad-Dera Ismail Khan Motorway, and the Grand Trunk Road would be closed at several points from the evening onwards. The public was advised to plan their travel accordingly.
Ary News also reported that the Islamabad Traffic Police (ITP) had announced the closure of the M-1 Peshawar Motorway, M-14 CPEC route, Hazara Motorway and sections of the GT Road and other key routes from 11pm on Wednesday until further notice.
Traffic Advisory – Road Closures from 23 Sep 2026, 2300 hrs M-1 (Peshawar Motorway), M-14 (CPEC), Hazara Motorway (E-35), GT Road (N-5), and connecting roads (Rawalpindi–Kohat, Abbottabad–Hassanabdal) are being closed from various points. Please plan travel accordingly and use… pic.twitter.com/3j5vYQddVr
The official page of the Islamabad Police on X also shared a traffic advisory on Sept 22, 2026, which read, “Peshawar Motorway (M-1) will remain closed to all types of traffic from 11pm tonight until further orders on September 23, 2026. Avoid travelling on Peshawar Motorway (M-1) from the twin cities of Islamabad and Rawalpindi, including other districts, and postpone non-essential travel.”
It continued, “In contrast, M-2 (Lahore/Islamabad) Motorway will remain open for all types of traffic. Travellers are advised to plan their journey in accordance with the traffic advisory and ensure compliance with the instructions of the traffic police.”
اہم ٹریفک ایڈوائزری پشاور موٹروے (M-1) کل 23 ستمبر 2026 رات 11 بجے تاحکم ثانی ہر قسم کی ٹریفک کے لیے بند رہے گی۔ جڑواں شہروں اسلام آباد و راولپنڈی سمیت دیگر اضلاع سے پشاور موٹروے (M-1) پر سفر کرنے سے گریز کریں اور غیر ضروری سفر مؤخر کریں۔ اس کے برعکس ایم 2 ( لاہور/اسلام آباد)…
A further keyword search led to the official website of the National Highway and Motorway Police, which showed that several sectors in the Motorway North Zone Sector M1 (Peshawar to Islamabad Motorway) and N-5 North Zone Sector North-I (GT Road Peshawar to Islamabad) were either closed or diverted due to the law and order situation.
Express News correspondent Naeem Asghar told iVerify Pakistan that he was present in the press conference when the reporters had asked the minister about the road situation. He added that they had further pressed Chaudhry on the status of the roads later on, but the state minister avoided answering them and departed without responding.
Moreover, even after Chaudhry’s claim that all 125 roads to Islamabad were open to the public, several media outlets such as Express News, Hum News , and Aaj News continued to report that the M1 motorway and some routes were still closed.
A news report from international wire agency AFP titled, “Pakistan blocks roads around capital ahead of planned pro-Khan protest”, said that authorities blocked main access routes to Islamabad with double-stacked shipping containers today.
“Key highways, entry points, and major intersections were obstructed, completely severing transport links and bringing movement to a virtual standstill,” it said.
The outlet reported that its journalists saw the toll plaza for the Islamabad-Peshawar highway on the capital’s outskirts “completely cut off” in the afternoon, with barriers and containers blocking the major road.
It also provided pictures of the traffic diversions and road closures on the Islamabad–Peshawar Motorway.
A police officer diverts traffic on the Islamabad–Peshawar Motorway blocked with trucks placed by authorities in Islamabad on September 24, 2026 ahead of PTI protest demanding the release of founder Imran Khan.
A general view shows the Islamabad–Peshawar Motorway blocked with trucks placed by authorities in Islamabad on September 24, 2026, ahead of PTI protest demanding the release of founder Imran Khan.
The Express Tribune also reported the same .
The claim by the state minister for interior that all 125 roads to Islamabad were open to the public is false .
Major roads such as M1, M14 and N5 (GT road) are still closed to traffic.

title: Taylor Swift set to become most awarded artist in VMA history with new honour
description: Taylor Swift will become most awarded artist in VMA history after receiving inaugural Artist Director Honours
content:
Taylor Swift will become most awarded artist in VMA history after receiving inaugural Artist Director Honours
Taylor Swift is set to become the most awarded artist in MTV Video Music Awards history when she receives the inaugural Artist Director Honors at Sunday’s ceremony.
CBS and MTV announced that Swift will receive the new award, which recognises music artists whose work behind the camera has pushed creative boundaries and advanced visual storytelling.
Swift currently shares the record for most VMA wins with Beyoncé, with both artists entering this year’s ceremony with 30 Moon Person awards. Her Artist Director Honors will take Swift’s total to 31.
Swift’s relationship with the VMAs began in 2008, with her first major milestone coming the following year when she won Best Female Video for “You Belong With Me”.
Her acceptance speech was interrupted by Kanye West, who said Beyoncé had made “one of the best videos of all time”. Beyoncé later invited Swift back to the stage to finish her speech.
Swift has since recorded several major moments at the ceremony. She opened the 2019 show with performances of “You Need to Calm Down” and “Lover”, before announcing her album Midnights in 2022 while accepting Video of the Year for All Too Well: The Short Film.
The nearly 15-minute film, which Swift wrote and directed and starred Sadie Sink and Dylan O’Brien, won Video of the Year, Best Longform Video and Best Direction at the 2022 VMAs.
Swift first won Best Direction in 2020 for “The Man”, followed by victories for All Too Well: The Short Film, “Anti-Hero” and “Fortnight”. She has four Best Direction wins from seven nominations.
Her directing credits also include “cardigan”, “willow”, “Bejeweled”, “Lavender Haze”, “Karma”, “I Can See You”, “The Fate of Ophelia” and “Opalite”.
Swift also announced The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore, an expanded edition of her 2025 album featuring four new songs, due Friday.
The 2026 MTV Video Music Awards will air live from Los Angeles on Sunday, Sept. 27, at 7:30 p.m. ET/4:30 p.m. PT on CBS, with a simulcast on MTV and streaming on Paramount+ Premium in the US.

title: Netanyahu s fleeting visit to New York mirrors strained US ties
description: Netanyahu will spend under eight hours in New York  meet nine leaders  but hold no announced talks with US officials
content:
Netanyahu will spend under eight hours in New York, meet nine leaders, but hold no announced talks with US officials
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's unusually brief trip to the United States to address the UN stands in stark contrast to his week-long visit last year that included a meeting with President ​Donald Trump, reflecting rocky times in US-Israeli ties.
Netanyahu is expected to be in New York for ‌less than eight hours before returning to Israel, two Israeli officials said.
His office said he would meet nine world leaders, five of them from Latin American nations with which Israel has sought to deepen ties as relations with traditional partners in Europe have been strained by ​the Gaza war and West Bank settlement expansion.
But a statement from Netanyahu's office made no mention of meetings ​with US officials at the annual UN General Assembly.
Israel's former ambassador to Washington, ⁠Michael Oren, said he could not recall a time when an Israeli prime minister visited the US without meeting ​the president, describing this as a blow for Netanyahu ahead of Israel's October 27 general election .
Trump has met Netanyahu eight times during ​his second term as president. Their last encounter was in July.
"It's a campaign speech. Now it would be much better if that campaign speech were accompanied by a meeting with the president, or another world leader, or at least the secretary of state, but apparently it's ​not," Oren said.
Read More: Israel’s US envoy says son was injured in West Bank ramming attack
"I don't recall a time when the prime minister came to the United States and didn't meet with ​the president ... So I'm sure that he was disappointed by that."
Netanyahu's office said many world leaders requested to meet him "during the visit, ‌but due ⁠to a tight schedule and the need to return before the onset of (the Jewish holiday of) Sukkot, the prime minister was only able to accommodate some of them".
Netanyahu's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Oren's remarks.
Opinion polls indicate Netanyahu could lose the election, his security credentials still shaken by the October 7, 2023 attacks by ​Hamas ​on Israel, though he ⁠cannot be written off.
Netanyahu is to meet the presidents of Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay, Panama, Ethiopia and the vice president of Colombia, and the prime ministers of Greece, Slovenia and Papua ​New Guinea, his office said.
Trump and Netanyahu jointly launched a war on Iran in February, ​but the ⁠allies found themselves at odds as Trump sought to extricate the United States from the conflict with key goals unmet. Washington struck an interim deal with Tehran in June that was opposed by Israel before it unravelled a few weeks later.
US public backing ⁠for Israel ​has fallen since the Gaza war began, particularly among Democrats .
Israel has faced deepening ​diplomatic isolation since launching its war in Gaza in response to the October 7 attacks.
Earlier this month, once-steadfast allies Britain, France and Canada announced sanctions ​targeting Israeli settlements in the West Bank, which drew a muted response from Washington.

title: Mahershala Ali says he sustained knee injury training for  Blade
description: Mahershala Ali agrees with Kevin Feige   s  failure  assessment over  Blade  after years of delays and training
content:
Mahershala Ali agrees with Kevin Feige’s 'failure' assessment over 'Blade' after years of delays and training
Mahershala Ali has agreed with Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige’s assessment that the cancellation of Blade was a failure, after the actor spent a year preparing to play the Marvel character.
Ali was announced as the MCU’s Blade in 2019, but the reboot never entered production. Speaking to GQ , the two-time Oscar winner said he still does not know why the project failed to move forward.
“That’s a Kevin Feige question,” Ali said. “They had, as you said, a two-time Oscar-winning actor under contract and you got billions of dollars. That’s a question for them, like why it didn’t happen.”
“To this day, I don’t know why it didn’t happen,” he added.
Interviewer Zach Baron then referred to Feige’s previous comments about Blade , in which the Marvel boss said he felt like a “giant loser and failure” over being unable to get the film made with Ali.
“I agree with him,” Ali responded. “I agree with him 100%. 100%. He should feel that way.”
Ali also described the preparation he undertook for the role. He said he trained extensively for a year, including sword work and martial arts, while the film was repeatedly delayed.
“I spent a year training,” he said. “I trained so hard till I blew my knee out.”
The actor also said he “uprooted” his family and moved to Atlanta while preparing for production. However, filming continued to be postponed.
“We’re there waiting to go and they just keep pushing it back, pushing it back, pushing it, and it doesn’t happen,” Ali said.
Ali said the project also affected his career outside the MCU, explaining that Blade “definitely impacted how things unfold in your trajectory”.
“I was working on it,” he said. “I was doing what I needed to do to prepare myself. It just didn’t happen.”

title: Kit Harington says  Games of Thrones  Jon Snow return remains possible
description: Kit Harington says future Jon Snow story could still work after planned  Game of Thrones  spin off was cancelled
content:
Kit Harington says future Jon Snow story could still work after planned 'Game of Thrones' spin-off was cancelled
Game of Thrones star Kit Harington says there is still a possibility that he could return as Jon Snow, despite the cancellation of the character’s planned sequel series.
The proposed Jon Snow spin-off was intended to continue the character’s story after Game of Thrones season 8, following his exile beyond the Wall. The project reportedly spent around two years in development before being cancelled.
Harington previously explained that the team “couldn’t find the right story to tell”. However, speaking on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, the actor said he remains open to revisiting the character if the right story emerges.
“We developed it for two years or so, and I still think there’s a world in which something could work. I wouldn’t have gone into it in the first place if I didn’t,” Harington said.
“I was very insistent at the start, and they were as well, HBO and George of like, ‘If this doesn’t, if we don’t find the right thing, let’s not do it,’” he continued.
“It’s much, much better we don’t. After a little while of thinking about it, I kind of was ‘Look, I think this isn’t quite the right time.’”
Harington said his decision was influenced by the other projects he pursued after Game of Thrones , including Marvel’s Eternals. He suggested that the time away from the character has changed how he views a potential return.
“I think I was right, because I’ve gone and done all these other things, and now I feel more comfortable with [Jone Snow] and that world again, in where it sits in my life.”
The cancelled series would have focused on Jon Snow’s life following the events of Game of Thrones , although HBO and George R.R. Martin agreed that the project should not proceed without a suitable story.
For now, there is no confirmed Jon Snow revival. Harington’s comments indicate that he has not ruled out returning to the role if a future project provides the right opportunity.

title: Ed Sheeran loses almost 500 000 Instagram followers amid Macklemore row
description: The drop comes after Macklemore was removed from Sheeran s tour following his support for Palestinians
content:
The drop comes after Macklemore was removed from Sheeran's tour following his support for Palestinians
Ed Sheeran has lost almost 500,000 Instagram followers in the space of a week as controversy continues to surround the removal of Macklemore from the British singer's US tour.
According to Social Blade data cited by The Independent, Sheeran's Instagram account lost almost 150,000 followers on September 15, the day he first addressed Macklemore's removal from his Loop Tour. Another 150,000 followers were reportedly lost the following day, followed by a further 98,000 the day after. By Tuesday, his follower count had fallen to around 47.2 million.
The drop comes after Macklemore was removed from the remaining US dates of Sheeran's tour following his outspoken support for Palestinians. The rapper had used performances at New Jersey's MetLife Stadium to speak about Gaza and the occupied West Bank and declare his support for Palestine.
Macklemore was scheduled to perform at eight of the final 10 US shows on Sheeran's Loop Tour. However, promoter Messina Touring Group said venues had indicated they would not allow the rapper to perform, warning that keeping him on the line-up could result in the cancellation of concerts.
Macklemore subsequently criticised the decision and said the focus should remain on Palestinians affected by the conflict. The dispute also intensified after he alleged that Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, had pressured Sheeran and other stadium owners over his participation.
Kraft defended the decision to prevent Macklemore from appearing at Gillette Stadium, saying the rapper's recent actions and material shared during Sheeran's shows had crossed a line. Kraft also said the decision was not intended to diminish Palestinian suffering.
The controversy widened when several other artists associated with Sheeran's US tour withdrew from upcoming performances. Pro-Palestinian protesters also gathered outside Sheeran's first concert without Macklemore in Philadelphia.
Sheeran addressed the situation during his September 19 concert, apologising for how he had handled the controversy and saying he had been forced to make difficult decisions. He also spoke directly about Gaza, describing the situation there as "catastrophic, unjustifiable and disproportionate" and referring to what he described as systemic injustice in the occupied West Bank.
Sheeran has maintained that the decision to remove Macklemore was made by the tour's promoter rather than by him personally. The controversy has nevertheless continued to affect his US tour, with the dispute prompting wider debate around freedom of expression, artists' political statements and the role of venues in deciding who can perform.
The latest figures show that the fallout has also extended to Sheeran's social media following, with his Instagram audience declining by almost half a million within a week as the dispute continues to attract attention.

title: Carrot Top   s legal battle with Brian Evans escalates as judge warns of jail time
description: Carrot Top   s legal team has accused Evans of attempting to extort money by threatening to release the recording
content:
Carrot Top’s legal team has accused Evans of attempting to extort money by threatening to release the recording
Carrot Top’s ongoing legal battle with former opening act Brian Evans has escalated, with a Florida judge warning both sides that violating court orders could result in jail time.
The dispute centres on an alleged sexually explicit recording involving the comedian, whose real name is Scott Thompson. Carrot Top’s legal team has accused Evans of attempting to extort money from him by allegedly threatening to release the recording, claims Evans has repeatedly denied.
During a September 22 hearing in Florida, Carrot Top’s lawyers asked the court to restrict Evans from filing additional documents in the case without prior approval. His attorney argued that Evans’ filings contained damaging and salacious allegations that were subsequently picked up by the media.
The judge did not grant the request to prevent Evans from filing future motions. However, the court ordered that future filings in the case would remain confidential and warned the parties about the consequences of violating court orders.
According to a transcript obtained by TMZ, the judge warned that anyone who disobeyed the court's orders could face incarceration, saying the court had authority to go beyond financial sanctions.
The legal dispute has continued for more than two years, according to Carrot Top’s attorney. His legal team has alleged that Evans threatened to release private information, including the purported explicit recording, unless he was paid money.
Evans has denied the allegations. He told TMZ that he never threatened to release a video in exchange for money and claimed that the recording had already been deleted under the terms of a previous settlement.
Evans also pushed back against claims that he was responsible for Thompson’s recent personal crisis, saying he was glad the comedian survived and denying responsibility for his actions.
The latest hearing came after Thompson was hospitalised following an incident at his Las Vegas home on September 18. His representative has said that the comedian is improving, while his return to performing remains uncertain.
Meanwhile, Evans told the court that he had received death threats from people he said were supporters of Carrot Top. He claimed that people had threatened to harm him if they encountered him in public.
The judge's decision to keep the case filings confidential means further details of the dispute may not immediately become public. For now, the legal battle between Carrot Top and Evans remains ongoing, with both sides continuing to dispute key allegations surrounding the alleged recording and the wider case.

title: Major routes to Islamabad closed ahead of PTI protest
description: NHMP travel advisory shows multiple road closures and restrictions
content:
NHMP travel advisory shows multiple road closures and restrictions
Major highways and motorways leading to Islamabad have been closed or restricted at several points ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) long march planned for September 27, disrupting interprovincial and intercity movement of passenger and goods transport and affecting key links between the federal capital and surrounding regions.
The National Highways and Motorway Police (NHMP) travel advisory on Thursday listed multiple road closures and restrictions ahead of the opposition party's planned long march.
The advisory, however, cited the reason for the closures and restrictions as a “law-and-order situation”.
A police officer diverts traffic on the Islamabad–Peshawar Motorway blocked with trucks placed by authorities in Islamabad on September 24, 2026 ahead of opposition party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) protest demanding the release of Imran Khan. Photo: AFP
It further stated that the M-1 motorway had been closed in both directions between Swabi and the Islamabad Toll Plaza, with southbound traffic diverted from the Swabi Interchange. The E-35 Hazara Motorway was also closed in both directions between Jharikas and Burhan due to the “law-and-order situation”.
Similarly, the advisory noted that the entire Hakla-to-Yarik stretch of the M-14 was affected by law-and-order restrictions in both directions.
The advisory also cited restrictions on the M-2 North, including the closure of the Islamabad-bound route for heavy transport vehicles between Kot Momin and Islamabad.
The restrictions also affected the N-5 Grand Trunk Road. At Attock Khurd, traffic restrictions had been imposed in both directions, with diversions listed through HPT, Deser Star and Suzuki Motors.
Read: Rangers deployed in Islamabad, Punjab districts to maintain law and order
The latest NHMP advisory, updated at different times on Thursday, also listed a number of separate roadwork-related lane closures on the M-2, M-3 and M-4.
Several major routes elsewhere in Punjab and the country, including sections of the M-5 and the southern N-5, remained open, with road and weather conditions reported as clear.
The closures come as PTI prepares for its September 27 march towards Islamabad, which the party says aims to seek the release of its founder, Imran Khan.
The Express Tribune has learnt that Islamabad authorities have also imposed restrictions on public gatherings, while major entry routes to the city have been sealed at several points.
The measures have caused disruption for commuters in the Hazara, Taxila, Haripur, Attock and Rawalpindi-Islamabad regions. Reports from Haripur said routes towards Taxila, Hassan Abdal, Attock, Rawalpindi and Islamabad had been blocked with containers, while traffic queues were reported around Jharikas and Hassan Abdal.
A separate report said the main road from Haripur through Hattar towards Taxila had also been blocked with containers. Traffic approaching Taxila and Rawalpindi from the University of Engineering and Technology (UET) Gate No. 1 side was also reportedly blocked.
So far, the authorities have cited security and law-and-order concerns for the restrictions, while PTI has characterised the measures as an attempt to prevent its supporters from reaching Islamabad.
With the protest still two days away, the continuing closure of major transport corridors has already disrupted movement between Islamabad and several parts of K-P and northern Punjab. Commuters have been advised to check official travel advisories before undertaking journeys.
A general view shows the Islamabad–Peshawar Motorway blocked with trucks placed by authorities in Islamabad on September 24, 2026, ahead of opposition party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) protest demanding the release of former Prime Minister Imran Khan. Photo: AFP
Earlier today, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry rejected a reporter's reference to road closures in Islamabad, saying the WhatsApp status being cited was old. “No road was closed,” he said, adding that all 125 routes into Islamabad were open until noon.
The minister also said that whenever security measures were required, both the federal and provincial governments would follow court orders and the law “in letter and spirit” to protect lives and property.
“Attackers cannot be allowed to attack here,” he said.
The Punjab government also sought additional security deployments in areas including Rawalpindi and Attock, while officials said the measures were intended to maintain law and order ahead of the expected political activity.
PTI alleges targeting of party leaders ahead of March
The party said that the homes and offices of party leaders were being targeted as part of a wider crackdown ahead of the protest.
In Mandi Bahauddin, the party alleged that police and unidentified plain-clothes personnel raided the residence of PTI district senior vice-president Faisal Imran Gondal and damaged furniture, doors, windows, electric motors, Imran billboards and other property.
PTI also condemned what it described as a raid and vandalism at the hujra of former party leader Murad Saeed. A party statement alleged that unidentified personnel damaged property there and accused the authorities of harassing Saeed and his family.
Read More: Uproar in K-P Assembly over minister 'abduction'
Separately, PTI leaders in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) reported a series of raids and arrests involving party lawmakers and provincial ministers. The provincial government and PTI have described the actions as an attempt to restrict the party’s political activity ahead of the planned march.
PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, speaking in Lahore on Wednesday, claimed that four members of Imran’s family and eight PTI MNAs were under arrest, while several provincial ministers remained missing. He alleged that the situation in K-P had effectively become similar to Governor’s Rule despite no formal declaration.
Gohar called for the resolution of disputes through political dialogue.
The allegations could not be independently verified by The Express Tribune .
In today’s press conference, when asked about the footage showing a K-P provincial minister allegedly being picked up or arrested by police, Minister Talal Chaudhry rebuked the provincial government for being unable to protect its own minister.
“If there are dozens of incidents every day, an incident involving a minister or anyone else can happen,” he said.

title: Shutdown in India s Ladakh marks anniversary of deadly autonomy protests
description: Shops and businesses closed and streets emptied in Leh on Thursday after a Buddhist group called for a shutdown
content:
Shops and businesses closed and streets emptied in Leh on Thursday after a Buddhist group called for a shutdown
Residents in India's Ladakh staged a virtual shutdown of the main city on Thursday to mark a year since four people were killed during protests demanding greater regional autonomy.
On September 24, 2025, security forces opened fire as demonstrations turned violent in the sparsely populated, high-altitude Himalayan region.
The discontent stems from a 2019 decision by the Indian government to revoke Ladakh's partial autonomy and impose direct rule.
Shops and businesses in the city of Leh remained shut and streets were deserted on Thursday, witnesses said, following calls for a shutdown by a Buddhist group.
"The shutdown is to commemorate those who laid down their lives for Ladakh and express solidarity with their families, and ... to highlight our demands for autonomy," a member of the Ladakh Buddhist Association told AFP , declining to be named.
Residents organised special Buddhist prayers to commemorate those they called the "martyrs" of the protests.
Ladakh is strategically important to India as it borders regional rivals China and Pakistan.
The vast desert region is sparsely populated, with around 300,000 residents, half of them Muslim and about 40% Buddhist.
Read More: India's 'cockroach' movement says will launch protest if poll panel chief doesn't quit in 48 hours
Since Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government split Ladakh from Indian-occupied Kashmir in 2019, residents have said the end of semi-autonomy has stripped them of protections over land, jobs, resources and cultural identity.
New Delhi now makes most development decisions, which officials from outside Ladakh tend to implement, sidelining the locally elected council.
On Wednesday, Ladakh's New Delhi-appointed top administrator said some of the 89 people charged after last year's protests would no longer face criminal prosecution.
"In the larger interest of peace, public tranquility, and social harmony in Ladakh, I have approved the withdrawal of criminal cases against 20 individuals, related to the unfortunate violence that erupted in Leh on September 24 last year," Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena said.
"The decision aims at fostering a more peaceful, united, and harmonious society in Ladakh."
Negotiations with the federal home ministry have continued since the protests, but residents have secured only limited gains so far.
The government has reserved 85% of jobs for locals and said Indians from outside Ladakh will not be able to acquire domicile status in the region until 2036.
But residents are demanding comprehensive autonomy under the "Sixth Schedule" of India's constitution, which would allow a local legislature to make laws on land use, jobs and traditional livelihoods.

The 21-year-old singer discussed Swift’s mentorship and how her guidance has reshaped his perspective on fame
Sombr has revealed the unexpected advice Taylor Swift gave him about dealing with online criticism as he navigates his growing music career.
In an interview with Elle Magazine , published on September 23, the 21-year-old singer-songwriter discussed Swift’s mentorship and how her guidance has reshaped his perspective on fame.
Swift hand-selected Sombr earlier this year to perform her songs “Cardigan” and “Dear John” at her Songwriters Hall of Fame induction ceremony.
Reflecting on “Dear John”, Sombr said the song’s lyrics resonated with him because Swift wrote it at around the age he was when he signed his record deal.
He described the connection as particularly meaningful given their experiences at similar stages of life.
However, it was Swift’s perspective on online hate that made a lasting impression. Sombr shared: “One of the best pieces of advice the legend has given me—The person I look up to most has given me. The amazing pop star. Is that if these hate comments go away, maybe you’re not at your peak anymore. I think it’s a privilege to be receiving these and rise above it.”
“Ever since she gave me that advice, it’s really changed my perspective and has helped,” he added.
Sombr also reflected on facing viral criticism as a teenager, admitting he once felt compelled to defend himself publicly.
He told Elle , “I wouldn’t respond now,” explaining that reacting to criticism can make situations worse.
Swift has publicly praised Sombr’s songwriting, calling him “the future” of the music industry and expressing confidence in his independent approach to making music.

title: Saudi Arabia reports fresh Houthi attacks  issues warning for Makkah
description: Houthi attacks escalated after renewed hostilities shattered a year long truce in July
content:
Houthi attacks escalated after renewed hostilities shattered a year-long truce in July
Saudi Arabia intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles on Thursday after issuing warnings for several regions, including Makkah, as the Iran-backed group ramps up attacks on the kingdom.
The attacks were reported as fighting raged in Yemen between the Houthis and Riyadh-backed government forces, killing dozens on both sides, according to a tally from seven sources who spoke to AFP .
#BREAKING : Saudi Arabia's National Early Warning Platform announced the potential danger has passed in Makkah, Taif and Jeddah pic.twitter.com/1VhD0fEcLh
The missiles were the latest in a series of escalating Houthi attacks since July, when renewed hostilities shattered a years-long truce and embroiled Yemen in the wider Middle East war.
Since then, the Houthis have imposed a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, hitting its tankers and territory and seizing swathes of Yemen's Red Sea coast, which is vital for Saudi oil exports.
The Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen's government since 2015 against the Houthis said six ballistic missiles had been intercepted, thwarting attacks on Taif and Yanbu.
"Escalations and violations by the terrorist Houthi militia will be dealt with firmly," said coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki in a series of posts on X.
التحالف : تصعيد وإنتهاكات الميليشيا الحوثية الإرهابية سيتم التعامل معها بحزم.
Earlier, the Saudi Civil Defence had issued a brief series of alerts including one for Makkah, with separate warnings for the Red Sea governorate of Yanbu as well as the Taif, Jeddah and Tabuk regions.
Read More: Saudi Aramco chief says disrupted oil operations can be restored 'within days'
The alerts were lifted a few minutes later. In recent weeks, alerts have often preceded attacks by the Houthis.
Last week, Riyadh accused the group of targeting Mecca for the first time since 2017 with a drone that was downed, an accusation the Houthis denied.
A few days later, the group attacked the Saudi capital Riyadh, the first in years, marking a new escalation in the conflict.
As the Houthi attacks targeted Saudi Arabia on Thursday, battles raged on the ground in Yemen.
At least 150 Houthi fighters and government forces members have been killed in the past 24 hours, sources from both sides told AFP , including in clashes over hilltops overlooking the Bab al-Mandab strait at the mouth of the Red Sea.
At least 98 soldiers and government forces members were killed, according to an AFP tally compiled from five military sources.
Most were killed in Houthi ballistic missile and drone attacks, with dozens of Yemeni troops killed on the Saudi side of the border that they are tasked with guarding.
At least 52 Houthi fighters were killed, two sources from the group said.
Many on both sides were also killed in clashes in the Kahboub Mountains and in areas between the Lahj and Taiz regions, as the Houthis seek to dominate the highlands overlooking Bab al-Mandab to protect newly seized territory.
In July, a fragile 2022 truce between the Houthis and Yemen's government fell apart after the group allowed an Iranian plane to land in Sanaa in defiance of Riyadh's control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks.
The Houthis later announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its tankers and territory.
Their gains cement the hold of Iran and its allies on the two waterways that the wider Gulf, including top crude exporter Saudi Arabia, relies on to ship out its oil and other fuel products.

This is the first time that Green-shirts will return empty-handed from Asian Games
It was a disappointing day for Pakistan’s kabaddi at the Asian Games in Japan on Thursday.
The Green-shirts were eliminated when Iran defeated them 51-30 in their Group B match at the continental event in Aichi-Nagoya.
This was the second defeat tasted by Pakistan following an upset loss at the hands of Thailand on Wednesday.
Since making their debut in 1990 Beijing Asian Games Pakistan never returned empty-handed. Pakistan had won two silver and seven bronze medals in their previous nine editions of the Asian Games.
“Yes it’s unfortunate,” Pakistan Kabaddi Federation’s (PKF) secretary Mohammad Sarwar told The Express Tribune following Pakistan’s loss.
Pakistan led 14-20 at halftime but struggled to contain Iran after the break.
Iran scored 31 points in the second half compared with Pakistan’s 16, turning a six-point halftime deficit into a 21-point winning margin..
Iran’s second-half surge proved decisive as Pakistan were unable to maintain the momentum they had built before the interval.
Iran and Thailand have qualified for the semi-finals from this group.

The Witcher 3 Remastered gameplay comparison has drawn mixed reactions, as fans point out atmosphere differences
CD Projekt Red has shared a new gameplay comparison between The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and its upcoming remaster, prompting mixed reactions from players who compared the two versions.
The side-by-side footage, shared on X on September 23, shows Geralt using the Igni sign against Drowners in Crookback Bog. Some players questioned whether the remastered version represented an improvement over the original.
“Why does it look worse?” one of the top replies asked, while another user wrote, “Are you sure you didn’t swap the footage around?” Other responses similarly said they preferred the original footage.
Players highlighted differences in the fire effects, colours and lighting. Some argued that the fire in the remastered footage does not illuminate its surroundings or reflect in the water in the same way as the original. Others criticised what they described as more muted colours and the absence of fog.
However, the fog difference is partly explained by the footage itself. A Foglet is present in the original comparison but not in the remastered version, creating a different appearance between the two scenes.
Choose your cast - wisely. #TheWitcher3Remastered pic.twitter.com/zcgLSvLvDi
Reactions on the The Witcher 3 subreddit were more varied, with some players preferring the remastered fire effects while describing the comparison as a “strange comparison”.
The footage also carries a disclaimer stating, “Work in progress – does not represent the final look of the game.” This means the visuals shown may differ from those in the finished remaster.
The Witcher 3 Remastered is scheduled to arrive as a free upgrade on September 29. It will introduce overhauled combat, a new skill system and upgraded visuals and performance.
The remaster will also lead into the Songs of the Past expansion, planned for 2027. The expansion is set in Dandelion’s homeland and is intended to connect Wild Hunt with The Witcher 4.

title: Beauty brands face eye patch moment as Fenty  Huda Beauty and Glow Recipe unveil similar products

The brands have responded playfully online, turning the coincidental launches into a viral beauty conversation
The beauty industry is facing an unexpected eye-mask moment, as Fenty Skin, Huda Beauty and Glow Recipe unveil remarkably similar sliced hydrogel eye patches—months after Korean brand Wonder Bath introduced the concept.
Fenty Skin teased its Dew N Plump Fresh-Sliced Hydrogel Eye Patches on September 17. The cylindrical dispenser releases a single-use under-eye patch with a twist.
Glow Recipe soon revealed its Exopeptide Caffeine Brightening and Depuffing Fresh Slices Eye Mask, followed hours later by Huda Beauty’s Undereye Jelly Patches.
However, Wonder Bath’s “Slice Serum” line debuted in July 2026, making the Seoul-based brand the earliest launch among the four.
Its range includes targeted variants and around 60 slices per tube, priced at approximately $29.
The near-simultaneous Western launches have raised questions about packaging exclusivity.
Huda Kattan said, “I think it’s pretty obvious that we all got screwed over by the same packaging supplier. Formulas are different, but we were lied to on the exclusivity with the packaging supplier. Pretty crazy."
Glow Recipe co-founders Sarah Lee and Christine Chang stressed that the formulas remain distinct, saying, “We worked tirelessly to make sure that the formula would deliver results and the actives we used were infused into the hydrogel itself."
Fenty highlights fruit juices, niacinamide and hyaluronic acid, while Glow Recipe focuses on caffeine and peptides.
The brands have also responded playfully online, turning the coincidental launches into a viral beauty conversation.
The episode illustrates how shared suppliers, emerging packaging trends and social media can bring similar beauty products to market within weeks.

title: Gucci s new  Made in China  sneaker models break with Italian tradition
description: Demna s first Gucci sneaker  the Drip  carries a  Made in China  label as the brand chases price sensitive shoppers
content:
Demna's first Gucci sneaker, the Drip, carries a 'Made in China' label as the brand chases price-sensitive shoppers
Gucci has begun selling new luxury sneaker models labelled "Made in China", a ​break with its Italian manufacturing tradition that some industry watchers say could undermine the brand's high-end image as it races to win ‌back middle-class shoppers.
The move highlights the challenge facing Gucci designer Demna, who must create innovative products while keeping costs under control to attract so-called aspirational shoppers, the bulk of luxury consumers who are more price-sensitive than the super-rich.
Demna will present his latest collection at a Milan runway show on Friday. His success is crucial for parent Kering and CEO Luca de Meo, ​who took over last year to lead a turnaround but has seen an early share price bounce fall flat this year.
Gucci, Kering's flagship ​brand, has seen sales halve over the past three years, squeezing margins and forcing the group to close dozens of ⁠stores.
In a move reminiscent of his tenure at Balenciaga, Demna has created a futuristic sneaker model called Drip. The shoe is labelled as "Made in China", according ​to Gucci's website. Reuters also observed Drip models displayed in a Gucci store in Paris carrying the same label.
In a statement, Gucci said that Italy would "always ​be at the heart of Gucci's manufacturing model and identity" but that it had decided to work with the Chinese manufacturer just as it had worked with Swiss and Japanese suppliers for products like watches and eyewear in the past.
"The partner selected offered the technological know-how and capabilities most appropriate for achieving the performance and quality standards we were seeking," it ​added.
There were no broader plans to move Gucci production outside Italy, a Gucci spokesperson said.
The Drip sneaker, described on Gucci's website ​as "Demna's first sneaker for Gucci", went on sale last month as part of the designer's Primavera collection.
Retailing at around €800 in Europe and $1,000 in the United States, it is cheaper than ‌many other ⁠Gucci shoes, though still firmly in the luxury category.
Georgian fashion designer and Creative Director of Gucci, Demna. Photo/Reuters
The laceless design is made from nylon, canvas or suede.
The Drip is a break from Gucci's more traditional white leather laced Ace sneakers, and its sock-like shape is reminiscent of Demna's chunky sneaker designs at Balenciaga, which were a streetwear hit in the late 2010s.
A second slip-on sneaker model, made of leather, from the same Primavera collection is also labelled as "Made in China", the Gucci website shows. The brand spokesperson said ​that model was produced in China ​for similar technical reasons linked to ⁠the shoe's design.
All other Gucci shoes carrying a country-of-origin label on the website are made in Italy.
China is a global hub for sneaker production, and its manufacturers have earned strong reputations among mass-market and premium brands. Some analysts say ​that in Gucci's case, however, breaking with "Made in Italy" could spark a backlash.
"We think this creates a potential tension ​between provenance and the ⁠luxury positioning Gucci is seeking to reclaim," Berenberg analysts said in a note.
Simon Whitehouse, a Milan-based luxury business consultant, was more blunt. "Made in China is not a good look," he said.
Two Kering sources told Reuters the brand has also begun cutting prices on a select number of products, including in China, as part of efforts to ⁠regain market ​share.
Barclays analyst Carole Madjo said the price cuts surprised some investors, who are now paying increased ​attention to any further moves that could affect Gucci's image with shoppers.
"Some people are wondering: should we keep buying Gucci if the price is coming down?" she said. "Having Chinese-made products could fuel ​the debate around the brand's price value equation."

title: Colleen Hoover discusses  It Ends with Us  after Blake Lively and Justin Baldoni settlement
description: Colleen Hoover says she remains proud of  It Ends with Us  after Blake Lively and Justin Baldoni settled legal dispute
content:
Colleen Hoover says she remains proud of 'It Ends with Us' after Blake Lively and Justin Baldoni settled legal dispute
Colleen Hoover has addressed the legal dispute surrounding the film adaptation of It Ends with Us, four months after Blake Lively and Justin Baldoni reached a settlement.
Speaking to Variety while promoting the upcoming adaptation of her novel Verity, Hoover said she remained proud of the 2024 film, which starred Lively and Baldoni alongside Brandon Sklenar.
“I feel for everyone, you know?” Hoover, 46, said of the legal dispute.
“As the author, I was — and am — so proud of that movie. I think they did a great job,” she continued.
“I think Blake [Lively] was great in it, Justin [Baldoni] was great in it, Brandon [Sklenar] was great in it, and I saw the completed film before any of that happened, or I knew it was happening, so I was proud of the film! And I still am. It was a huge hit.”
The legal dispute began in December 2024, when Lively filed a sexual harassment complaint against Baldoni, alleging misconduct on the set and a retaliatory smear campaign.
Baldoni denied the allegations and later filed a $400 million countersuit against Lively, her husband Ryan Reynolds and others, alleging defamation and breach of contract. The lawsuit was later dismissed.
Lively’s case was subsequently narrowed before both sides announced a settlement on May 4. Their attorneys said in a joint statement that “The end product, the movie It Ends With Us, is a source of pride to all of us who worked to bring it to life.”
A judge later partially granted Lively’s request for more than $8 million in legal fees and costs, ordering Baldoni and his company, Wayfarer Studios, to pay just over $400,000.
Hoover said she was focusing on the film’s success while moving on to her next adaptation, Verity , starring Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett. The film is due in cinemas on Oct. 2.
