title: The new face of South Asian representation at Vogue
description: Manish Malhotra  Simone Ashley spotlight a new era of South Asian influence  style and representation at Vogue
content:
Manish Malhotra, Simone Ashley spotlight a new era of South Asian influence, style and representation at Vogue
South Asian representation in fashion is no longer confined to the margins of the industry. Across the pages, covers, runways and social feeds of the world’s most influential fashion publications, a new generation of South Asian talent is increasingly impossible to overlook.
A recent Vogue Instagram post brings together six names that capture different facets of that changing landscape: Manish Malhotra, Rashmika Mandanna, Simone Ashley, Natasha Poonawalla, Dhruv Kapoor and Jaya Raheja.
Together, they reflect the breadth of South Asian influence in contemporary fashion—from couture and cinema to global celebrity, luxury and emerging creative talent.
What makes the group particularly interesting is that there is no single definition of what South Asian representation looks like anymore.
Few names demonstrate the evolution of Indian fashion on the global stage quite like Manish Malhotra.
He first became widely known through his work as a Bollywood costume designer before establishing his eponymous label in 2005.
His work has long occupied the space between cinema, celebrity and couture, bringing Indian embroidery, embellishment and traditional silhouettes into the vocabulary of contemporary glamour. Vogue has described his career as a journey from costumes to couture, with hundreds of film credits shaping his visual language.
In 2026, that journey reached another significant milestone when Malhotra made his debut on the official Paris Haute Couture Week calendar.
His couture collection drew heavily on Indian craftsmanship, including zardozi, resham, crystal work and hand embroidery, while experimenting with ways to take traditionally Indian techniques into an international luxury context.
For Rashmika Mandanna, representation is inseparable from the idea of crossing borders.
Her career has moved across India's regional film industries and languages, making her part of a new generation of Indian stars whose audiences are increasingly national and global. Vogue India recently described her as someone who has had to navigate different languages, industries and ideas of regional identity throughout her career.
Mandanna's presence in fashion reflects the increasing visibility of Indian popular culture internationally, while also demonstrating how celebrity style can become a form of cultural representation. She represents an India that is multilingual, regional and global all at once.
Few contemporary actors have become as closely associated with a new generation of South Asian representation in Western popular culture as Simone Ashley.
Her breakout role as Kate Sharma in Bridgerton placed a British Indian woman at the centre of one of the world's biggest television franchises. Ashley has spoken openly about what it means to represent Indian women on screen, telling Vogue India that representing Indian women has been a joy.
Her relationship with fashion has expanded that visibility beyond the screen. From Vogue World to international magazine appearances and luxury fashion campaigns, Ashley occupies a space where British, Indian and global identities intersect.
Her significance lies partly in what she makes possible for the women who come after her. As she told Vogue recently, there is still substantial room for progress in representation, even as she sees more women from diverse backgrounds receiving major roles.
Natasha Poonawalla represents another side of South Asian influence: the fashion insider and tastemaker who moves comfortably between Indian design and the international luxury establishment.
A fixture on major fashion and red-carpet circuits, Poonawalla has become known for highly considered, often experimental fashion choices. Vogue India has repeatedly documented her appearances, including her collaborations with Indian designers and her Met Gala looks.
Her fashion choices also demonstrate how South Asian heritage can operate within global luxury without necessarily being presented as costume or nostalgia.
Her 2025 Met Gala ensemble, for example, incorporated vintage Parsi Gara saris into a look created by Manish Malhotra, bringing an element of Parsi textile history into one of fashion's most visible international stages.
Dhruv Kapoor represents a younger, more contemporary vocabulary of Indian fashion.
Rather than relying exclusively on familiar ideas of Indian luxury, designers of this generation are questioning what South Asian fashion can look like in the first place.
Vogue 's recent coverage of the region's fashion landscape has highlighted precisely this shift: younger designers are taking local craft and heritage and placing them into silhouettes and ideas that speak to a global contemporary audience.
This is an important distinction. Representation is not simply about putting a South Asian person in a fashion photograph. It is also about allowing South Asian designers to define their own aesthetic language.
Jaya Raheja represents another part of this changing ecosystem: the emerging South Asian fashion voice.
Her inclusion alongside established figures such as Malhotra and Poonawalla, and globally recognised performers such as Ashley and Mandanna, points toward a fashion landscape that is becoming broader and more generational.
That matters because South Asian representation is no longer a story that can be told through a handful of established names. It is increasingly an ecosystem made up of different generations, professions, aesthetics and identities.
Perhaps the most interesting thing about these six names is what they collectively say about the meaning of South Asian representation.
For decades, international fashion's relationship with South Asia was often filtered through a narrow set of visual references: embroidery, bridalwear, saris, jewellery and craftsmanship. Those elements remain enormously important, but they are no longer the whole story.

title: Netherlands to return to Eurovision in 2027 after boycotting 2026 contest over Israel
description: The decision comes after broadcaster AVROTROS withdrew from the 2026 competition
content:
The decision comes after broadcaster AVROTROS withdrew from the 2026 competition
The Netherlands will return to the Eurovision Song Contest in 2027 after boycotting this year's competition over Israel's participation.
The country's public broadcasting organisation NPO confirmed that the Netherlands will take part in the 2027 contest, with an independent team responsible for selecting and supporting the Dutch entry. The decision comes after broadcaster AVROTROS withdrew from the 2026 competition, saying Eurovision could no longer be considered neutral while a participating country remained involved in a large-scale military conflict.
AVROTROS had previously been responsible for both selecting the Netherlands' Eurovision entry and broadcasting the contest. From 2027, those responsibilities will be separated.
The NPO will coordinate the Dutch entry, while broadcaster NOS will provide coverage of the Eurovision semi-finals and final. The NPO said this structure would allow NOS to report on the competition independently while an external team oversees the selection of the Dutch act.
NPO chair Jet de Ranitz said the organisation recognised that the decision to participate could prompt mixed feelings in the Netherlands. She said the NPO had asked the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) to place Eurovision's unifying purpose at the centre of the event again, particularly amid ongoing geopolitical tensions and conflict.
The decision follows changes introduced by the EBU after controversy surrounding voting and political campaigning at previous Eurovision contests. The organisation reduced the maximum number of public votes that could be cast per payment method from 20 to 10 and brought professional juries back into the semi-finals.
The EBU has also introduced a rule preventing a winning country from hosting Eurovision if it is involved in an armed conflict or a sensitive geopolitical situation.
The Netherlands was among several countries that withdrew from the 2026 Eurovision Song Contest following the EBU's decision to allow Israel to compete. Ireland, Spain, Slovenia and Iceland also announced boycotts in December 2025, although their positions for 2027 have since differed.
Ireland has confirmed that it will not participate in or broadcast the 2027 contest, citing the ongoing humanitarian crisis and loss of life in Gaza. Spain is also considering maintaining its suspension, while Iceland and Slovenia have yet to confirm their positions.
The 2027 Eurovision Song Contest will take place in Burgas, Bulgaria, with the semi-finals scheduled for May 11 and 13 and the grand final on May 15. The Netherlands' representative will be announced at a later date.

title: Russell on top in Baku practice
description: He finishes ahead of Verstappen and both Ferraris
content:
He finishes ahead of Verstappen and both Ferraris
George Russell topped the times for Mercedes ahead of Red Bull's Max Verstappen and the two Ferraris in Thursday's opening practice at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
World championship leader Kimi Antonelli, in the second Mercedes, was fifth-quickest after pulling up during the session with hydraulics failure in hazy, warm conditions.
Russell clocked a best lap in one minute and 45.387 seconds to outpace four-time champion Verstappen by 0.400sec, with Charles Leclerc, chasing a fifth pole position in Baku and first win, adrift by a further 0.004sec.
Seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton was fourth with Oscar Piastri sixth for McLaren.
World champion Lando Norris endured a tricky session in the second McLaren with various car problems before winding up 14th, having run only 14 laps compared to 25 by both Ferraris. Antonelli only completed nine laps.
On his return to action with Red Bull, after a broken wrist, Isack Hadjar also had brake and engine problems on his way to running only eight laps to finish 20th.
Leclerc initially topped the times in 1:54.395, but they fell rapidly with Verstappen taking over as the pair traded best laps on hard tyres until after 20 minutes Antonelli took command in 1:46.265.
The Italian then came to a halt at Turn Seven, having lost hydraulics. As he evacuated, the marshals chose to squirt fire extinguisher into the car without clear reason as a Virtual Safety Car (VSC) was deployed for two minutes.
The track gradually 'rubbered in' to deliver more grip and incidents, with Verstappen locking up at Turn One before Russell avoided a crash at Turn Three with a spectacular reflex save into a run-off area.
Verstappen, seeking his third win on the fast streets of Baku, went top again before being leapfrogged by the Briton, thanks to a generous tow from two-time champion Fernando Alonso's Aston Martin.

title: Mancini s Italy facing battle to  win back  dispirited fans
description: Low ticket sales highlight the growing apathy surrounding the national team
content:
Low ticket sales highlight the growing apathy surrounding the national team
Roberto Mancini embarks on his bid to turn around Italy's fortunes for a second time as coach this week, but he also needs to win over sceptical fans left apathetic towards the Azzurri after an unprecedented series of setbacks.
The four-time world champions, for so long the sporting pride of the nation, have hit one embarrassing low after another, while the likes of tennis world number one Jannik Sinner, runaway Formula One championship leader Kimi Antonelli and Italy's Olympic athletes have delivered history-making successes.
The men's national football team failed to qualify for the past three World Cups, having not missed out previously since 1958.
Luigi Giaquinto wistfully watched a video of Giorgio Chiellini lifting the European Championship trophy five years ago three times on a loop.
"It all feels like so long ago," says the 27-year-old Italy supporter and electrician at the national team's museum in Coverciano, near Florence.
"It's incredible to think that our national team won the Euros just five years ago, yet failed to qualify for the last World Cup. It's tough being an Italy fan."
Alessandro Maurillo, who accompanied Giaquinto to the small museum next to the Italian football federation's national training centre, used to follow "international football more than club football", until recently.
Italy have not even played a World Cup knockout match since winning the 2006 final against France, and also suffered a last-16 exit at the hands of Switzerland at Euro 2024.
The one bright spot during their miserable 10-year stretch was the brilliant Euro 2020 triumph, with Mancini at the helm, as part of a then-world record unbeaten run of 37 matches.
Mancini has admitted that his team need to "win back" supporters, starting with Friday's Nations League match against Belgium in Rome.
The former Manchester City boss will also have some personal persuading to do, after abruptly ending his first spell as coach in 2023 to take over the Saudi Arabia national side.
"We will achieve this by taking the national team back to where it deserves to be, by playing with enthusiasm, and by giving our all," Mancini said.
But recent results have shattered fans' optimism.
The Euro defeat by the Swiss was disappointing, but losses in qualifying play-offs for the 2022 and 2026 World Cups, by North Macedonia and Bosnia and Herzegovina respectively, were real low points.
"When you can't beat so-called 'small' teams like Switzerland and Bosnia, there's a problem," says Maurillo, pointing out the Azzurri pale in comparison to the country's other sports teams "where Italy excels".
Italian clubs have also struggled to scale previous heights in recent years -- a Serie A team has not won the Champions League since Inter Milan's 2010 victory under Jose Mourinho.
"The problems facing the national team -- and Italian football more broadly -- mirror those of Italian society," added Maurillo, a 29-year-old insurance agent.
"Young people aren't given a chance. Young players struggle to break through because they get little to no playing time in Serie A.
"It's a bit like the job market, where many young people are forced to go abroad to find work."
As he examines one of the earliest official Italy jerseys, a woollen one worn in 1928 by Elvio Banchero, Giacomo Benevento criticises the lack of character among the key players.
"Players like (Nicolo) Barella and (Gianluigi) Donnarumma -- the experienced ones -- don't have the balls that Chiellini, (Andrea) Barzagli, or (Gennaro) Gattuso had," bemoans the 57-year-old physiotherapist.
"They don't bring that extra spirit to the pitch, they don't strike fear into their opponents."
Supporters may be about to vote with their feet, as only 32,000 of the 70,000 tickets available for Friday's Group A1 game against Belgium at the Stadio Olimpico had been sold as of Wednesday.
Italy face a daunting trip to Turkey on Monday before hosting France, then play the reverse fixture against the Turks to conclude the expanded international break.

title: Amitabh Bachchan recalls how he and Jaya married just a day after deciding
description: Veteran actor says the couple skipped elaborate wedding plans and tied the knot the day after deciding to get married
content:
Veteran actor says the couple skipped elaborate wedding plans and tied the knot the day after deciding to get married
Amitabh Bachchan has shared a surprising account of how his marriage to actress Jaya Bachchan came together with almost no advance planning. The veteran actor revealed that the decision was made so quickly that the couple tied the knot just a day after discussing marriage.
According to Gulf News , Bachchan spoke about his wedding while interacting with Kolkata contestant Aheli Roy on Kaun Banega Crorepati 18 . During the conversation, Aheli asked him how he had convinced Jaya’s family before their marriage.
Bachchan said there was no lengthy discussion or elaborate planning between the families. Instead, he simply suggested to Jaya that they should get married, and she agreed. "I told Jaya one day that we should get married, and that was it - the decision was made", he said.
He added, "After the marriage was decided, Jaya ji must have gone and told her parents. We don’t even know what she must have said, but they agreed and came over. Then there was some discussion, and we got married the very next day".
Amitabh Bachchan and Jaya Bachchan's wedding in June, 1973. PHOTO: Khaleej Times
Bachchan said the couple did not get caught up in the elaborate preparations that often accompany weddings today. Reflecting on the simplicity of their own ceremony, he questioned the need for lengthy planning and elaborate celebrations.
"Honestly, shouldn’t it be this way? Who wants to get into all that hassle of deciding the date, choosing what to wear, going here and there, making all these arrangements, having bands play and everything? There’s really no point to all that. We simply accepted that she was going to be my wife, and nothing could be more meaningful than that", he said.
The couple married on June 3, 1973, following the success of Zanjeer . According to Khaleej Times , they celebrated their 52nd wedding anniversary in June 2025.
The couple later welcomed two children, Shweta Bachchan Nanda and actor Abhishek Bachchan, and have remained one of Bollywood’s most prominent married couples.

title: Zverev  Agassi defend  spectacular  Laver Cup
description: Tennis stars unite Friday for the three day team event
content:
Tennis stars unite Friday for the three-day team event
Grand Slam champion Alexander Zverev and American legend Andre Agassi led a staunch defence of the Laver Cup ahead of the latest edition of the polarising event in London this week.
In the midst of the packed tennis calendar, Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, Taylor Fritz and rising stars Rafael Jodar and Jakub Mensik are among the stars appearing in the exhibition at the O2 Arena from Friday to Sunday.
The Laver Cup is a three-day tournament on hard courts, pitting players from Europe against opponents from the rest of the world in a rare team event in a sport dominated by singles competition.
Although the Davis Cup is well established as the number one team competition in tennis, the Laver Cup was launched in 2017 as the brainchild of Roger Federer and Tennis Australia.
The plan was to emulate the drama of golf's Ryder Cup -- which featured teams from the United States and Europe.
Unlike the Ryder Cup, the Laver Cup has yet to capture the imagination of the sporting public.
There are also concerns about cramming another tournament in the already hectic schedule for players at risk of burnout.
But to hear two-time major winner Zverev, and Agassi, who is serving as captain of Team World, speak with such conviction about the Laver Cup tells a different story.
"It's really exciting. The arena is spectacular. It is one of the great events of the year," Agassi told reporters in London on Wednesday.
Agassi, an eight-time Grand Slam champion, added: "All these players are out there, maybe on some level trying to impress each other.
"The competition and intensity is always high."
World number two Zverev could have been forgiven for opting out of the Laver Cup after winning the US Open on September 13 to cap a golden year.
The 29-year-old German, who had never won a major until this year, wanted to show solidarity with an event that has supported him in the past.
"The Laver Cup is something I always try to play. I am a person that values loyalty quite a lot and the event has been loyal to me. I try to be loyal to them," said Zverev, who will be with seven-time Grand Slam winner Alcaraz on Team Europe.
"I enjoy being here. I enjoy being among these team-mates, great guys. I hope to have a great week."
Just four years ago, Britain's Arthur Fery was in the stands at the O2 watching Novak Djokovic in the Laver Cup and now he is part of the show himself.
Fery is an alternate for Team Europe -- on standby to compete if any players are ruled out -- and his presence at the event is the latest milestone in his remarkable rise.
The 24-year-old burst onto the scene with a remarkable run to the Wimbledon semi-finals as a wildcard in July.
"Really pleased to be here. I've had a really good year. It's something that has come with the good results," he said.
"It's amazing to be around all these tennis greats. It's going to be great to be around those guys here. Spend some time with them and pick their brains.
"It's all a little surreal obviously. I am taking the positives out of it and trying to feel like I belong here," he said.

title: Farhat Ishtiaq to bring  Zanjeerain  to audio with new series
description: Writer will revisit the hit drama in an audio series set to launch on her official YouTube channel in October
content:
Writer will revisit the hit drama in an audio series set to launch on her official YouTube channel in October
Farhat Ishtiaq is taking Zanjeerain beyond television and into the world of audio storytelling, with an audio version of the drama set to launch on her official platforms in October.
The acclaimed writer announced the upcoming series on Instagram following the conclusion of the television drama, directing viewers towards the audio adaptation on her official YouTube channel.
The announcement read, "We are extremely pleased to announce that we are going to start the audio series of the blockbuster drama Zanjeerain on Farhat Ishtiaq’s official YouTube channel from October. We hope that you will enjoy this audio series just as much".
Zanjeerain premiered in April, with Sajal Aly, Ameer Gilani, Danyal Zafar, Sahar Hashmi and Ahsan Khan among its principal cast. Written by Ishtiaq, the drama was set against a mountainous backdrop and brought together romance, family conflict, tradition, power and long-standing rivalries.
At its centre was Rabiya, played by Sajal Aly, whose life became intertwined with Muddasir and Sar Buland as the story explored questions of family honour, loyalty and the consequences of decisions made by previous generations.
The drama’s sprawling ensemble of characters and interconnected relationships placed individual choices within a broader web of family history and social expectations, giving the story a narrative that extended well beyond its central romance.
With the television series now complete, the audio adaptation offers audiences a different way to experience the story. Without the visual elements of locations, costumes and performances, the audio format places greater emphasis on dialogue, narration, characterisation and Ishtiaq’s writing.
The announcement was met with enthusiasm from fans, with several viewers taking to the comments to praise the writer and express their excitement about the new format. One user wrote, “Please write part two”, while another described the drama as “Unforgettable”.
For audiences familiar with Ishtiaq’s work, the move into audio storytelling is not entirely new. Her official YouTube channel has previously featured audio versions of stories, including Meem Se Mohabbat , published as part of the "Awaz Kahani Series".
The upcoming Zanjeerain audio series therefore continues Ishtiaq’s exploration of a format that allows her stories to be experienced with a greater focus on the written narrative and the conversations between her characters.
Rather than simply revisiting the television drama, the audio adaptation gives Zanjeerain another life — this time through voices, dialogue and storytelling rather than the screen.

title: Alcaraz wants end to late-night matches at Grand Slams | The Express Tribune
description: The Spaniard says players need more time to recover between matches
content:
The Spaniard says players need more time to recover between matches
Carlos Alcaraz has called on tennis chiefs to end late matches at Grand Slams after his record-breaking US Open exit in the middle of the night.
Alcaraz's reign as US Open champion was shattered by Ben Shelton in a five-set thriller that finished at 3.33am local time in New York.
The quarter-final started on a Tuesday evening and finally came to a conclusion after four hours and 28 minutes on a Wednesday morning in the latest finish in US Open history.
The cut-off for matches at Wimbledon is 11pm local time, but the US Open, French Open and Australian Open do not have an alloted time to halt play.
Novak Djokovic's 2024 win against Lorenzo Musetti ended at 3.07am in Paris, with matches in New York and Melbourne often stretching late into the night.
Many leading players have bemoaned the brutal schedule and Alcaraz, a seven-time Grand Slam winner, insists the time has come to make a change at the four majors.
"For an athlete finishing at 3.30 in the morning, it means we had to leave the courts at 4.30, then back to the hotel," he told reporters in London on the eve of this week's Laver Cup.
"You don't go to bed until 6.30 or 7 in the morning. To recover for the next match, the person you play has an advantage.
"It is too much. They are going to have to do something. I'm not saying 3.30 but (even) finishing at 12 is too late already."
Alcaraz was left physically and mentally spent after the gruelling loss to Shelton, which came in his first tournament after over four months out with a wrist injury.
The 23-year-old believes matches that last late into the night are damaging for players and hinder the sport because many fans have to leave the stadium, while the television audience also drops.
"100 percent. It is a shame a match like this didn't reach a lot of people because they have to go to bed, they have to work in the morning," the world number three said.
"If that match had started at 7 or 8pm, at the maximum finishing at 11, the stadium would have been packed. A lot had to miss it because of the schedule."
One way to reduce the number of late matches would be to cut Grand Slam contests from the current best-of-five sets format to the three-set system used elsewhere on the ATP and WTA Tours.
Djokovic, a 24-time Grand Slam champion, recently proposed slashing sets from the first to win six games to the first to win four to reduce match length.
But American legend Andre Agassi insists players who achieve Grand Slam glory are admired for pushing their body to the limits.
Agassi, who won eight majors in his iconic career, said: "I absolutely believe we should have it (five sets). I believe it's possible to get lucky and win two out of three. I don't think you can get lucky and win three out of five.
"I think you really have to earn it. There should be a delineation between winning the Slams, the biggest tournaments, versus other weeks of the year."
Agassi, serving as Team World captain in the latest edition of the Laver Cup, believes cutting back on the length of matches would do a disservice to the history of the sport.
"You don't want it going that late. It's unfortunate. I have been in that position plenty of times," he said.
"But the last thing you want to have is an asterisk next to the history of our sport. You don't want somebody just getting hot for an hour and a half and going through some tough matches.
"We are doing what we can but it is still gladiator stuff. I like it."

title: Shahzad smashes Pakistan   s fastest first class century
description: PTV batsman reaches 100 off 49 balls  breaking Misbah   s record for the fastest first class ton by a Pakistani batsman
content:
PTV batsman reaches 100 off 49 balls, breaking Misbah’s record for the fastest first-class ton by a Pakistani batsman
Pakistan Television batsman Muhammad Shahzad on Thursday scored the fastest first-class century, reaching the milestone in just 49 balls on the opening day of the President’s Trophy third round against Kingsmen Academy at the Diamond Club Ground in Islamabad.
Dera Ghazi Khan-born Shahzad surpassed the previous record held by former Pakistan captain Misbah-ul-Haq, who had scored a 56-ball century against Australia in 2014.
The century is also the world's eighth-fastest in domestic first-class cricket history.
Shahzad went on to score 114 off 62 balls, smashing 12 fours and eight sixes. The innings marked his sixth first-class century which also enabled PTV reach 285-7 in their first innings.
Mohammad Taha hit 43 off 72 deliveries, including six fours, while Yasir Khan made 13 off 40 balls with one boundary. Sharoon Siraj contributed 16 off 46 deliveries, hitting three fours, while Ammar and Waqar Hussain scored five and two runs respectively.

title: Yulo completes gymnastics gold collection at Asian Games
description: The Filipino star earns 14 666 for a historic victory in Nagoya
content:
The Filipino star earns 14.666 for a historic victory in Nagoya
Double Olympic champion gymnast Carlos Yulo said he was "overwhelmed" on Thursday after winning Asian Games floor gold in Japan to complete his collection of major titles.
Yulo became the only multiple Olympic gold medal-winner in Philippines history when he won the floor and the vault in Paris two years ago.
The 151cm (4ft 11in) Yulo sealed his first Asian Games gold with a score of 14.666 to complete a clean sweep of Olympic, World, Asian and South-East Asian Games titles.
"Having this in my collection ... it's all complete now," said the 26-year-old, who will go for a second gold in the vault on Friday.
"We can just relax and hope for the best tomorrow. I will make sure I enjoy tomorrow's competition," he added.
"I'm just overwhelmed right now. I can't process it yet."
Yulo, who shot to fame in Paris, is the first Philippines gymnast to win an Asian Games gold.
"It feels like it's kind of the Olympics for me," he said.
"It's my first time winning the Asian Games, and I'm really happy and excited to go home and share this blessing to the people in the Philippines."
Yulo was especially pleased his breakthrough Asian Games gold came in Japan, where he spends much of his time training.
"Competing here feels home to me," said Yulo, whose brother Karl was also competing in the floor exercise final, finishing in seventh place.
"I'm really comfortable here, doing my gymnastics. Maybe because I stayed here for a long, long time and trained with them.
"It's nothing new for me to perform my best here. The challenge is just to perform well. It came today. It was a good routine for me today."

title: Rangers deployed in Islamabad  Punjab districts to maintain law and order
description: Interior ministry directs all necessary action in self defence in event of attacks by armed or violent groups
content:
Interior ministry directs all necessary action in self-defence in event of attacks by armed or violent groups
The federal government on Thursday approved the deployment of Pakistan Rangers in Islamabad and several districts of Punjab to assist police in maintaining law and order and responding to potential security threats, according to a notification issued by the Ministry of Interior.
The approval came a day after the Punjab government sought Rangers assistance in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali until October 5, with the deployment approved by the provincial cabinet’s Standing Committee on Law and Order on September 20 following a request from Punjab Police. The deployment was to be carried out under Article 245 of the Constitution and relevant provisions of the Anti-Terrorism Act 1997 and Pakistan Rangers Ordinance 1959.
The ministry approved the deployment following requests from the Chief Commissioner Islamabad and the Punjab government. Rangers personnel were deployed under Sections 7(b) and 10 of the Pakistan Rangers Ordinance 1959 and Sections 4 and 5 of the Anti-Terrorism Act 1997.
The notification authorised the Rangers to provide full assistance to police in maintaining law and order and responding to violent activities or security threats. It also directed Rangers and police personnel to take all appropriate and necessary action in self-defence in the event of attacks by armed or violent groups.
The ministry instructed the security forces to take all necessary measures to deal with any violent activity or threat and ensure the protection of public property and lives.
The deployed Rangers personnel would perform security duties and assist police authorities in maintaining peace and order in the areas concerned, according to the notification.
The move came amid heightened security concerns in Islamabad and parts of Punjab, with authorities seeking additional security support to deal with potential disturbances and threats.
Read: Punjab imposes Section 144 across province, seeks Rangers deployment and mobile service suspension
The Punjab government had on Wednesday imposed Section 144 across the province for 13 days, from September 23 to October 5, banning gatherings of five or more people in any public place, street, road, highway, motorway or open space.
The Punjab Home Department said the restrictions were imposed in view of a “serious and imminent threat” to public peace, tranquillity and the safety of life and property across the province from terrorist organisations and hostile intelligence agencies.
The department said intelligence agencies had issued multiple alerts about possible terrorist attacks involving suicide bombers and vehicle-borne improvised explosive devices. It warned that rallies, gatherings, sit-ins, processions, demonstrations and other assemblies could become potential targets for such attacks.
The restrictions did not apply to marriage ceremonies, funeral prayers, burial gatherings or prayers at mosques and other places of worship. Courts, government institutions and events held with formal permission were also exempt.
The Home Department said law-enforcement agencies had requested immediate security measures to address possible terrorism threats. The restrictions were imposed under Section 144(6) of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898.
The Punjab Home Department had also asked the Ministry of Interior and Narcotics Control to downgrade or jam mobile and internet services at selected locations in Rawalpindi and Attock from September 27 for law and order purposes.
The department had requested 2G, 3G and 4G network jamming at selected locations in Rawalpindi, while also seeking a downgrade of mobile and internet services in Attock. The requested locations included parts of Rawalpindi along the motorway from Barahma Bahtar to M1, Gango, Ahata, Taxila City, Wah Saddar, Thallian and Chakri.
The department said mobile and internet services would remain downgraded at the specified locations from September 27.

title: Extreme concern    as OpenAI   s    rogue agent    breached Australian govt health database
description: Model accessed public  non public files during June evaluation  Canberra says no patient records were compromised
content:
Model accessed public, non-public files during June evaluation; Canberra says no patient records were compromised
An artificial intelligence (AI) agent developed by US tech giant OpenAI breached an Australian government health statistics system during an internal evaluation, accessing both public and non-public files and writing files into the system, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Wednesday.
According to CNN , the incident is believed to be the first publicly disclosed case of an AI agent breaching an Australian government network and comes amid growing concern over the ability of increasingly autonomous AI systems to circumvent safeguards and undertake actions beyond those intended by their human operators.
Albanese said the AI agent had accessed an Australian Medicare statistics database and bypassed restrictions after failing to obtain information through normal channels. He said there was no evidence that patients’ personal medical information had been accessed.
“Nonetheless, this situation is obviously unacceptable,” Albanese told reporters on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
The prime minister said he had spoken by telephone with OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman on Wednesday to convey Australia’s “extreme concern” over the incident.
Albanese also criticised the company for the delay in notifying Australian authorities. According to the government, OpenAI discovered the activity in August but did not inform Canberra until September 10, when it sent an email to a generic government mailbox.
Read: AI leaders warn UN of security risks as systems grow more powerful
“It took the company way too long to inform the government what had occurred, and the nature of the way that notification occurred as well was unacceptable,” Albanese said.
The disclosure came as governments, technology companies and researchers grapple with the security implications of AI agents capable of independently browsing the internet, executing tasks and adapting their behaviour when they encounter restrictions.
The breach occurred in June while OpenAI was conducting an internal evaluation of its models, according to the company and Australian officials.
The model had been asked to search the internet for information about Australian government spending on medicines and healthcare, including statistics that could be used to answer questions about public expenditure.
When it encountered restrictions on the information it could access, however, the AI agent attempted to circumvent them, Australian officials said.
Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles described the behaviour in unusually simple terms. “It asked a question, the information was not given and rather than leaving at that point, it scaled the fence,” Marles said.
OpenAI spokesman Drew Pusateri said the company became aware of the activity in August while conducting an extensive review of its models’ activity.
“During this review, we identified activity involving several Australian government websites and services as our models attempted to look up answers and available statistics for questions about Australia during an internal evaluation,” Pusateri said. “In the course of that, our models took actions we did not intend.”
OpenAI said its investigation found no evidence that patient records had been accessed in the Medicare incident. The information accessed included aggregate health statistics and internal file names, according to the company.
Australian officials said the breach involved an older health statistics website rather than a system containing individual medical records.
Government Services Minister Katy Gallagher said the notification from OpenAI was sent to a public mailbox that was checked only once a day.
“That email address is looked at once a day,” Gallagher said, adding that such mailboxes can receive large numbers of notifications, including hoaxes.
The delay has become a central concern for Canberra because the government was not immediately aware that an AI system had penetrated restricted areas of a government service.
Albanese said three other government systems may also have been affected by AI activity.
They included the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, the New South Wales Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research and the Victorian Department of Health.
The Australian government said there was no indication that the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare system had been breached, although the website was among those targeted. A forensic investigation, assisted by the Australian Signals Directorate, is now examining the incident and determining whether any other government systems were affected.
Marles announced a taskforce investigation and sought to reassure the public that the impact appeared to be limited. “No individuals’ medical data was accessed here.
The system itself has not been in any way compromised,” he said.
The investigation is nevertheless significant because the incident involved an AI system acting beyond the boundaries of the task it had been assigned. Rather than simply searching publicly available information, the model attempted to overcome technical restrictions when it could not find the information it wanted. That behaviour has heightened concerns among cybersecurity specialists that AI agents could increasingly become capable of finding and exploiting vulnerabilities without being explicitly instructed to do so.
The Australian breach was disclosed at the same time as research organisation Transluce reported several earlier instances in which AI agents apparently attempted to exploit computer systems after failing to obtain information through conventional web searches.
The incidents, dating back to at least March, suggest that the phenomenon may have emerged earlier than some of the high-profile cases disclosed by AI companies in recent months.
Transluce said the incidents it identified involved relatively mundane research tasks rather than deliberate cyberattacks.
Read more: Anthropic, OpenEvidence partner to bring medical AI worldwide
In May, AI agents attempting to retrieve a photograph from a University of New Mexico library collection sent a “flood” of requests but were unsuccessful.
Later that month, agents targeted Data USA while attempting to obtain visualisation data relating to the University of Iowa.
In June, agents seeking statistics from the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare attempted to exploit vulnerabilities after normal methods failed. Transluce said no non-public data was exposed, although the agents bypassed anti-bot controls.
The Australian government acknowledged that AIHW was among the sites targeted but said it did not believe a breach had occurred.
The latest revelations follow a more serious incident disclosed by OpenAI in July, when the company said its models had created a swarm of AI agents during cybersecurity testing that breached systems belonging to Hugging Face, a platform widely used by AI developers to store and share code and models.
The models were operating in what was intended to be a controlled testing environment but managed to escape the restrictions placed on them and access real-world systems.
The incident became a prominent example in the AI industry of the potential risks associated with increasingly autonomous systems.
Other major AI developers have since reported similar concerns.
Anthropic said its models had gained unauthorised access to systems belonging to three unidentified organisations during testing intended to prevent them from interacting with real-world systems.
Google has also said its Gemini model was able to gain access to multiple systems by guessing login credentials.
The incidents have contributed to growing calls for stronger safeguards as AI systems move from answering questions to independently carrying out complex tasks across the internet.
Walayat Hussain, an associate professor of information technology at Australian Catholic University in Sydney, said the Australian incident and the earlier Hugging
Face breach appeared to form part of a broader pattern.
“Today’s AI agents are becoming brilliant at getting things done, but they are still poor at knowing where the line is,” he said.
Hussain said companies and governments could not assume that AI systems would reliably police their own behaviour, while warning that many government systems had not been designed with sophisticated autonomous AI agents in mind.
For Canberra, the immediate focus remains on determining precisely what the OpenAI system accessed and whether any other government infrastructure was affected.
Albanese said Australia’s investigation would establish the full extent of the incident, while the government would also examine OpenAI’s handling of the disclosure.
The episode has added a new dimension to the debate over AI safety: not simply whether increasingly powerful models can be prevented from generating harmful content, but whether autonomous agents can be reliably constrained when given access to real-world computer systems.
The Australian government has so far stressed that no individual medical records were accessed. But the incident has raised questions about whether existing safeguards, monitoring systems and notification procedures are adequate as AI agents become increasingly capable of acting independently online.

title: Farhan sets sights on Asian Games cricket gold
description: Pakistan   s brigade trains for Japan   s conditions  with spin to play a key role
content:
Pakistan’s brigade trains for Japan’s conditions, with spin to play a key role
Pakistan Asian Games-bound men’s cricket team captain Sahibzada Farhan on Thursday said that he is confident his charges can win gold at the continental event.
However he stressed that the side would not allow a potential clash with India to overshadow its wider campaign in Japan.
Farhan said Pakistan have a balanced squad featuring several promising young players and would approach every match with equal importance.
“We will try our best to claim gold for Pakistan,” Farhan told reporters at the National Stadium.
Farhan was happy with the way his charges have undergone training for the past four days.
“As a captain I am happy that all boys are working hard. We had requested for such pitches keeping in view Japan’s conditions and we also tried to play against spinners mostly. Haider Ali is in fine touch along with Abdul Samad and I am happy that all boys look in good shape,” Farhan said.
Pakistan are scheduled to arrive in Japan two days before their campaign begins, with Farhan saying the early arrival would allow the players to adjust to the local weather and conditions.
“We are focused on our first match. Every team is important for us and we will give equal importance to all our matches,” he said.
Farhan said Pakistan cricket team would not make the India fixture the sole focus of its Asian Games campaign, despite the significance traditionally attached to matches between the two countries.
“Our focus will be on each match rather than only the game against India,” he said.
Farhan also praised solid talent in the squad, identifying Saim Ayub, Maaz Sadaqat and Hasan Nawaz among players who could become important figures for the national team.
He said strong performances at the Asian Games could help emerging players secure more opportunities in the future.
“These players are a ray of hope for Pakistan,” Farhan said, adding that consistent performances in Japan could open the door to further opportunities at international level.
Pakistan have also tailored their preparations to the unusual playing conditions they are expected to encounter in Japan.
Farhan revealed that head coach Mike Hesson had travelled to Japan to inspect the rugby ground where the cricket matches are scheduled to be played and had discussed various aspects of the venue and conditions with the players and coaching staff.
The team’s four-day training camp in Karachi also took the expected conditions into account, he said.
The captain also stressed the importance of domestic cricket in developing Pakistan’s players and urged those who struggle at international level to return to domestic competition rather than allowing their form to deteriorate.
“Players who are unsuccessful at international level should go back and play domestic cricket,” he said.
Farhan said regular domestic cricket could help players sharpen their skills and regain confidence before attempting to return to the international stage.
The Asian Games will also represent an important leadership opportunity for Farhan, who said he remained optimistic about his own role while making clear that his priority was to contribute through his performances.
“I am very hopeful as captain. Whether I remain captain or not, my priority is to maintain consistency in my performance,” he said.
Farhan added that he would seek to repay the confidence shown in him by the Pakistan Cricket Board.
“I will try to live up to the PCB’s trust,” he said.

title: Block the Merger Coalition files emergency motion against Paramount Warner Bros  deal
description: The legal action comes after growing opposition to the deal from parts of Hollywood
content:
The legal action comes after growing opposition to the deal from parts of Hollywood
The Block the Merger coalition has filed an emergency legal request seeking to stop Paramount’s proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.
The coalition, made up of organisations and individuals opposing the $111 billion deal, submitted the emergency motion as efforts continue to challenge the proposed merger. The transaction would bring Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery under the same ownership.
The legal action comes after growing opposition to the deal from parts of Hollywood, with concerns centred on media consolidation and its potential impact on competition, employment and the wider entertainment industry.
More than 1,000 Hollywood figures previously signed an open letter opposing the proposed merger, including Joaquin Phoenix, Ben Stiller and Kristen Stewart. The letter argued that further consolidation could reduce opportunities for creators and jobs across the production industry.
The coalition has continued to challenge the transaction even as the legal situation surrounding the merger has shifted. In July, a federal judge temporarily paused the deal after a group of 12 state attorneys general argued that the merger could violate federal antitrust law. The states alleged that combining the two companies could reduce competition in the theatrical and basic cable markets.
Paramount has disputed those arguments, maintaining that the merger would be pro-competitive and would create a stronger competitor to major streaming companies including Netflix and Amazon. The company has also argued that the combined business would be able to invest more heavily in content production.
The latest emergency request comes as the wider legal battle over the merger continues to develop. The proposed acquisition has faced scrutiny from government officials, entertainment unions and industry figures since Paramount Skydance announced its plans to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery.
The deal has since progressed through several legal challenges. Most recently, Paramount reached a settlement with 12 state attorneys general on September 22, removing a major obstacle to the acquisition. The settlement followed an antitrust lawsuit that had threatened to delay the transaction.
The settlement did not end opposition to the deal. The Writers Guild of America also previously filed a lawsuit seeking to block the merger, while the Block the Merger coalition has continued to oppose the transaction.
The Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery deal remains one of the largest proposed mergers in Hollywood history, with its outcome carrying implications for film production, television, streaming and the broader US entertainment industry.

title: Nadia Khan regrets turning down Shoaib Mansoor s  Bol  role
description: TV host says family circumstances and social expectations around films influenced her decision to turn down the role
content:
TV host says family circumstances and social expectations around films influenced her decision to turn down the role
Television host Nadia Khan has opened up about a career decision she now wishes she could have made differently: turning down a role in Shoaib Mansoor’s acclaimed film Bol .
Speaking in an interview alongside actor Atiqa Odho, Khan said she had genuinely wanted to be part of the project, but circumstances surrounding her personal life ultimately influenced her decision. “I regret turning down 'Bol'. I really wanted to do it and he really wanted me to do it,” Khan said, referring to director Shoaib Mansoor.
Khan recalled that Mansoor was particularly disappointed by her decision and made several attempts to persuade her to reconsider. “Mansoor was very upset and had many meetings to try to convince me,” she said.
Looking back, she said her decision was also shaped by the social expectations surrounding film and television at the time. For women who had established themselves on television, making the transition to cinema could carry additional scrutiny.
“My generation was different and I wasn’t strong enough to do films or to convince other people of why I should,” she said.
Odho, who was part of the conversation, agreed that the distinction between television and cinema was much more pronounced at the time. “Doing films was very different from being on television, for our society back then,” she said.
Khan later revealed that family circumstances had also played a significant role in her decision. Asked directly about what had held her back, she acknowledged that her then-husband was a factor. “It was also my ex. I just wanted peace in my family,” Khan said.
Despite Khan’s decision too, Bol went on to feature a cast including Mahira Khan, Humaima Malik, Iman Ali and Atif Aslam, becoming one of Mansoor’s most widely recognised films.
Khan has remained a prominent figure in Pakistan’s television and entertainment industry for decades. She first gained recognition as a television host before expanding into acting and other areas of media, with credits including Pehchaan , Dolly Darling , Kam Zarf and Aisi Hai Tanhai .
She is also set to appear in Pakistan’s first Netflix production, Jo Bachay Hai Sang Samait Lo.
Nadia Afgan also revealed that she had turned down two other projects around the same time: Faraar and Jo Bichar Gaye .
“I refused the projects because there were too many projects I was doing at the same time, and I wasn’t going to work for what felt like 2 rupees when I deserve more,” she said.
Looking back, Afgan said that while she sometimes wished she had been part of certain projects, she still stood by her decision not to accept those roles. She later revealed that both the roles went to Nadia Jamil.
Previously, she has discussed the changing landscape of Pakistan’s entertainment industry, her evolving relationship with younger actors and the unlikely turn of events that launched her career decades ago.
Afgan has been part of many successful projects recently, including Aik Aur Pakeezah and Dar-e-Nijaat . She also starred in Jinn Ki Shadi Unki Shadi , Sharpasand , and Kabuli Pulao previously.

title: LHC declines immediate suspension of detention orders against Noreen  Uzma
description: Seeks replies from the relevant authorities on their petitions challenging the detentions
content:
Seeks replies from the relevant authorities on their petitions challenging the detentions
The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Thursday declined an immediate request to suspend the detention notifications issued against Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan’s sisters, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, and sought replies from the relevant authorities on their petitions challenging the detentions.
Uzma and Noreen had been taken into custody a few days earlier for 30 days under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance 1960 (MPO), a day after their sister Aleema Khan was detained. The detentions of Imran’s sisters and other PTI leaders came ahead of the party’s planned countrywide protest on September 27 and march to Islamabad.
Justice Abher Gul Khan heard the petitions today, while lawyers Rana Mudassar Umar and Barrister Taimur appeared on behalf of the petitioners.
During the proceedings, Umar asked the court to suspend the detention notifications, saying he wanted to place certain facts before the bench.
“Both women are housewives, and Dr Uzma has already been found innocent in the case registered against her,” the counsel submitted. He also told the court that a copy of the trial court’s decision had been attached to the petition.
Read: Imran's sisters challenge 30-day detention in LHC, seek immediate release
The court declined to suspend the notifications at this stage and instead directed the relevant authorities to submit their reports and replies. “Let us seek reports from the relevant parties,” Justice Khan observed.
The petitions sought the annulment of detention notifications issued by the deputy commissioner. The court subsequently issued notices to the respondents, seeking their replies on the pleas. The respondents included the Lahore deputy commissioner, capital city police officer, secretary of the Home Department and superintendent of Kot Lakhpat jail.
Noreen’s daughter, Sakina, and others had also approached the high court through Rana Mudassar Umar, challenging the detention orders.
A few days earlier, Justice Gul, while hearing a petition challenging the detention of Aleema and her driver, had sought arguments on the maintainability of the plea.
Uzma and Noreen were detained for 30 days under Section 3 of the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance 1960, a day after their sister Aleema Khan was detained under the same law. The detentions came ahead of the PTI’s planned September 27 countrywide protest and march towards Islamabad.
The Lahore deputy commissioner’s orders cited police reports alleging that the two women’s activities were “prejudicial to the public safety and maintenance of public order” and linked them to the May 9, 2023 protests and road blockades. The orders also said multiple cases had been registered against them.
On September 21, Aleema’s son Shahraiz Khan approached the LHC challenging the detention orders against his mother and her two sisters. The petition argued that the orders were unlawful and failed to establish any specific conduct warranting preventive detention.
A day later, the LHC sought further arguments on the maintainability of a separate petition challenging Aleema and her driver Muhammad Ameer’s detention. Their counsel argued that the detention proceedings appeared to have been initiated after they had already been taken into custody, pointing to the timing of the District Intelligence Committee meeting and the issuance of the detention notification.

title: IMF chief expresses satisfaction over Pakistan s economic reform programme
description: Says sustained reforms could support faster economic growth in Pakistan
content:
Says sustained reforms could support faster economic growth in Pakistan
International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva has expressed satisfaction with Pakistan’s economic reform programme, saying the implementation of the government’s reform agenda has helped achieve macroeconomic stability, Arab News reported .
Georgieva said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s government had made progress through a strong reform programme, which had contributed to improvements in fiscal discipline, external reserves and investor confidence.
She said Pakistan’s efforts included the introduction of a new national tariff policy, increasing domestic revenues and advancing the privatisation process.
“Strong reforms have helped Pakistan maintain economic stability and restore confidence,” Georgieva was quoted as saying.
She added that Pakistan had regained access to international financial markets, while continued implementation of reforms could help accelerate economic growth and improve living standards.
Read More: IMF fourth review next major test
The IMF chief said sustained reforms could support faster economic growth in Pakistan.
The remarks came as the IMF began discussions with Pakistan for the fourth review of the country’s $7 billion economic programme.
Talks have also started on the third review of Pakistan’s $1.4 billion climate resilience programme.
Successful completion of both reviews could pave the way for around $1.2 billion in financing for Pakistan, including about $1 billion under the economic programme and $200 million under the climate facility.
During the reviews, the IMF will assess Pakistan’s progress on reforms and commitments made under the programmes.
Also Read: PM Shehbaz says IMF raises no serious concerns over Rs100 fuel subsidy after meeting Georgieva at UNGA
A day earlier, PM Shehbaz said the IMF had not expressed any serious concerns over Pakistan’s targeted subsidy of Rs100 per litre during his meeting with the Fund’s managing director on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly session in New York.
Speaking to The Express Tribune after meeting Georgieva, the prime minister said he had briefed her in detail on the pressure Pakistan faces and the difficulties confronting low-income people.
“We drew the IMF chief’s attention to the question of where the poor man would go,” the premier said, adding that the targeted subsidy was being distributed through a comprehensive and transparent mechanism.
Later, in a post on X, the IMF managing director hailed Pakistan’s implementation of reforms, saying they had helped preserve stability, restore confidence and regain market access.
“I had the opportunity to meet with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on the margins of UNGA to discuss Pakistan’s reforms,” she said.
“Continuing reforms will help boost economic growth and improve the living standards of the people," said the IMF chief.

title: India s  cockroach  movement says will launch protest if poll panel chief doesn t quit in 48 hours
description: Election    Commission    of India says differences are normal in any    institution    and that all    its actions are legal
content:
Election ​Commission ⁠of India says differences are normal in any ⁠institution ​and that all ​its actions are legal
India's 'Cockroach' youth movement leaders said on Thursday ​that they would launch ‌protests across the country if India's chief election officer does ​not resign in ​48 hours, a day after ⁠a newspaper report pointed ​to differences among top officers ​leading the poll panel.
The Indian Express newspaper said on Wednesday that ​two election commissioners had ​raised questions or expressed concern at ‌least ⁠14 times in 10 months, mostly in connection with the process of updating ​voters' lists ​that ⁠began last year, with Chief Election Commissioner ​Gyanesh Kumar.
The Election ​Commission ⁠of India said that differences were normal in any ⁠institution ​and that all ​its actions were legal.
In July , Indian youth protesters called off ​weeks of demonstrations and celebrated in the streets after the education minister quit and Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government bowed to demands including calls to fix ‌a cheating-prone exam system.
The worst political crisis of Modi's third term in office had peaked when thousands of protesters marched on parliament, with police using tear gas to control them.
Youths calling themselves "cockroaches" had taken to the streets since late June, after national exam papers were leaked, forcing a resit which affected 2 million students and galvanised anger about the lack of prospects for young ​Indians.
The resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, the students' primary demand, came as a surprise because Modi has a reputation for refusing to act under pressure.
Read: Actor Imran Khan, singer Arijit Singh join celebrities backing New Delhi student protests
Modi's party faces key state ​elections next year. Similar youth-led protest movements brought down governments in neighbouring Sri Lanka, Nepal and Bangladesh in recent years.
Celebrations erupted at the Jantar Mantar protest site ⁠in the capital Delhi, with thousands of youngsters chanting victory slogans and dancing.
The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement, which spearheaded the demonstrations, said it would end its protests.
Roads around the central business district of Connaught Place ​near the protest site were shut amid celebrations and a swelling crowd of thousands of protesters.
Health Minister JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, a junior minister in Modi's office, held a joint press conference with two CJP spokespersons after another round of talks following Pradhan's resignation.
Nadda said the government had accepted all demands of the protesters, which included reforms in the exam system, dropping police cases filed against protesters and compensating families of students who ​died by suicide after the exam paper leaks.
"The Cockroach Janta Party declares that we withdraw the agitation in good faith," CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said.

title: US launches online portal to report suspected visa fraud
description: Says will hold individuals accountable  including by revoking visas and referring fraud for further investigation
content:
Says will hold individuals accountable, including by revoking visas and referring fraud for further investigation
The US State Department launched an online portal for the public to report suspected visa fraud and misuse, saying it would help authorities identify and act on fraudulent visa applications and travel schemes, according to a statement issued by the US Department of State that emerged on Thursday.
The statement said that the new tool would provide a “convenient and reliable way” for people to submit information for prompt review and action.
“Many of the tens of thousands of visa fraudsters the Department has identified and held accountable during President Trump’s second term were discovered thanks to tips provided by upstanding and concerned members of the public,” the statement said.
Under the leadership of President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the department’s Bureau of Consular Affairs had been conducting “rigorous fraud detection and prevention activities” to prevent attempts to travel to the US through fraudulent means or for illegal purposes, the statement said.
Visa fraud could involve falsified documents or travel plans, brokers arranging sham marriages, shell companies and fabricated job offers. It could also include “engaging in or facilitating birth tourism”, the handout read.
Read: Xi receives rare US airport welcome from Trump, First Lady
The statement said visa fraud schemes not only defrauded the US government but also “hurt American communities”, “undermine the US economy and American workers” and jeopardise national security and public safety.
“The Department of State is fully enforcing US laws and will hold accountable all those who violate them, including by revoking visas and referring fraud for further law enforcement investigation,” the statement said.
The department said the portal was intended to help the public provide information about suspected visa fraud and misuse, allowing reports to be submitted for review and possible action. People with information about suspected visa fraud or misuse were encouraged to use the new online portal, the statement concluded.
A day earlier, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met with US Chargé d’Affaires Natalie Baker in Islamabad and discussed ways to strengthen Pakistan-US relations, investment opportunities, regional security and efforts for peace and stability.
Pakistan and the US have ramped up efforts to contain visa fraud since the start of the year.
In January , Pakistan and the US mulled to launch joint operations under comprehensive SOPs against networks involved in fake and fraudulent visa activities. The decision was taken during a meeting between Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and US Chargé d'Affaires Natalie Baker. According to the interior ministry, the two officials held detailed talks on enhancing collaboration, particularly in curbing illegal immigration and improving the effectiveness of the pre-immigration clearance system. Both sides also agreed to increase cooperation at all levels in law-enforcement training, especially for the police.
Later, on March 3, the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) Anti-Human Trafficking Circle Islamabad arrested the main accused involved in a US visa fraud case. According to officials, a case was registered against Sheikh Syed Saifuddin Arefi following a tip-off from the US Embassy. Police investigation revealed that the accused tried to send several visa applicants to the US using fake documents. The accused and his accomplices provided fake invitations, fake letters from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other documents to the applicants on the pretext of attending the "Festival of Sufi Wisdom" alleged to be held in the US.
Read more: Naqvi, US Chargé d’Affaires discuss regional security
In May, the FIA’s Anti-Human Trafficking Circle in Karachi arrested two suspects for attempting to obtain US visas using forged medical documents . According to an FIA spokesperson, the arrests were made following a complaint from the US Consulate. The two suspects, identified as Muhammad Tauseef Khan and Imran Nazir Silhari, were taken into custody outside the consulate premises.
Then, in August, the US revoked more than 600 visas from foreign nationals as part of a major offensive against "birth tourism" rings, the State Department said.
“American citizenship is not for sale,” Secretary Marco Rubio wrote on the US social media company X.

title: PML-N's Najeeb Naqi takes oath as 23rd president of AJK  | The Express Tribune
description: AJK Supreme Court Chief Justice Raja Saeed Akram Khan administers the oath
content:
AJK Supreme Court Chief Justice Raja Saeed Akram Khan administers the oath
Dr Muhammad Najeeb Naqi of Pakistan Muslim League Nawaz (PML-N) on Thursday took the oath as the 23rd President of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) at a ceremony held at the President House in Muzaffarabad.
The AJK Supreme Court Chief Justice Raja Saeed Akram Khan administered the oath to the newly elected president.
AJK Prime Minister Iftikhar Gilani, PML-N AJK President Shah Ghulam Qadir, Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam, Federal Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry, Adviser to the Prime Minister Rana Sanaullah, Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq, AJK High Court Chief Justice Justice Sardar Liaqat Hussain, former prime ministers Raja Farooq Haider Khan and Sardar Tanveer Ilyas, former federal minister Khurram Dastgir Khan, members of the AJK Cabinet and Legislative Assembly, Chief Secretary Khushhal Khan, Inspector General of Police, senior government officials and other prominent people attended the ceremony.
At the outset, Chief Secretary Khushhal Khan read out the notification declaring Dr Najeeb Naqi as the newly elected president. The oath was then administered by the AJK Supreme Court chief justice.
Following the oath-taking ceremony, a police contingent presented President Najeeb Naqi with a guard of honour.
Read: AJK's electoral road ends with new PM
Dr Muhammad Najeeb Naqi Khan of Pakistan Muslim League Nawaz (PML-N) was elected AJK president after securing 32 votes, while Chaudhry Latif Akbar of Pakistan People’s Party (PPP) received only 13 votes.
Reportedly, one PPP lawmaker from Mirpur, Qasim Majeed, did not attend the Assembly session.
President Khan’s political career, which began in Sudhnoti in Poonch division more than three decades ago, has taken him from the Legislative Assembly to the Kashmir Council and several key ministerial portfolios. The 62-year-old leader comes from a prominent political family. His grandfather, Colonel Khan Muhammad Khan, is remembered in AJK’s political history as the “Baba-e-Poonch”, while his father, Colonel Muhammad Naqi Khan, was also a politician.
Following his father’s death, Naqi entered politics in the 1990s and was first elected to the AJK Legislative Assembly in the 1991 elections. During that term, he served as parliamentary secretary for health and planning and development.
He was re-elected to the assembly in 1996 on the Muslim Conference (MC) ticket and subsequently served as a member of the AJK Council from 2001 to 2006.
In the 2006 elections, he again won an assembly seat on the MC ticket and served in the government, holding portfolios including health, population welfare, colleges and information technology.
Read More: PML-N nominee Najeeb Naqi Khan submits papers for AJK president
Naqi joined the PML-N and was elected to the AJK Legislative Assembly on the party ticket in the 2011 elections. He retained his seat in 2016 and served as a minister for several key departments, including health, finance and planning and development, until 2021. The PML-N’s central leadership nominated him this month as its candidate for the AJK presidency.
His political career has thus spanned multiple roles as an elected legislator, parliamentary secretary, Kashmir Council member and cabinet minister, culminating in his election as president for the AJK’s highest constitutional office.

title: Ohashi smashes 200m breaststroke world record
description: The 17 year old Japanese swimmer clocks 2 04 83
content:
The 17-year-old Japanese swimmer clocks 2:04.83
Japanese teenager Shin Ohashi smashed the men's 200m breaststroke world record at the Asian Games on Thursday, setting a new mark of 2min 04.83sec.
The 17-year-old cut more than half a second off the previous mark of 2:05.48 held by China's Qin Haiyang.
Ohashi had already won the 100m breaststroke gold this week in Tokyo after a dead heat with China's Dong Zhihao.
"My target has always been to break the world record and I'm so happy to have done it," said Ohashi.
"A lot happened before this competition but a lot of people helped me get to this point and I am very grateful to them.
Ohashi finished 3.84sec faster than silver medallist Denis Petrashov of Kyrgyzstan.
The Japanese teen took control from the off and from then it was a race against the clock.
He will now be the man to beat at the Los Angeles Olympics in two years' time.
"My next goal is to win gold at next year's world championships and then go on to win gold at the Olympics," he said.
"I don't want to be satisfied and I want to feel these emotions again."
Previous world record holder Qin did not swim the 200m at this year's Asian Games.

title: Starc wary of  unknown  conditions on Australia tour of South Africa
description: The 36 year old expects recent wet weather to influence the pitches ahead of the Test series
content:
The 36-year-old expects recent wet weather to influence the pitches ahead of the Test series
Australia pace spearhead Mitchell Starc said an unusually timed tour of South Africa presents an element of the unknown for both teams, with rain and unfamiliar early-season conditions likely to shape the series.
South ‌Africa host Australia in a three-match one-day series starting on Thursday before the teams meet in a three-test series next month, Australia's first test tour of the country in eight years.
With the tests scheduled for October, when rain is often a major factor in parts of South Africa, ⁠Starc said conditions could differ significantly from those traditionally associated with the country.
"There's an element of the unknown," Starc told reporters on Tuesday. "It's part of test cricket and you just adapt to what's in front of you."
The 36-year-old, who took nine wickets in Australia's last test at Durban, said recent wet weather could produce a different surface from the dry conditions that traditionally aid reverse swing.
"It's quite muggy and humid," Starc said. "There has been talk about the rain ‌before ⁠we got over here. It's probably not that typical dry part of the season just yet.
"It could be interesting to see what the weather does over the next couple of days and then for the game as well."
Starc also praised fast bowler Nathan ⁠Ellis, who impressed during Australia's one-day series in Zimbabwe while several senior quicks were rested.
Ellis helped lead the attack in the absence of Starc, Pat Cummins and Josh Hazlewood ⁠and strengthened his case for a regular place in Australia's one-day side.
"He is really pushing his case as a lock as a pick in the ⁠one-day team, and no doubt he'll look to perform in these three as well," he said.
The first test of the three-match series begins in Durban on October 9.

title: Russia  Ukraine renew accusations over overnight airstrikes  killing 8
description: Russia  Ukraine renew accusations over overnight airstrikes  killing 8
content:
Local authorities say warehouses, residential buildings in Ukrainian capital damaged in overnight strikes
Russia and Ukraine on Thursday renewed their accusations concerning overnight airstrikes, with Kyiv saying that eight people were killed in the country’s capital and northeastern Kharkiv region.
Overnight, the Kyiv City Military Administration issued a missile alert in the Ukrainian capital, after which it reported that two warehouses were damaged in the city’s Sviatoshynskyi and Solomianskyi districts, while also reporting damage in other locations.
Ukraine’s State Emergency Service (DSNS) said on Telegram today that two people were killed and at least eight others were injured in the attack.
“All necessary emergency services are working at the sites,” the DSNS said, which also reported that two people were injured in the country’s southern Odesa region following overnight Russian strikes.
It said the strikes in the Odesa region caused a fire at a previously attacked shopping centre, while a two-story private residential building caught fire at another location, where the injuries occurred.
It also said that the roof of a seven-story city hospital building and a 10-story non-residential building were damaged.
Separately, Kharkiv Governor Oleh Synyehubov said that six people were killed and 12 others injured following a morning strike on a farm in the village of Stara Hnylytsia.
Ukraine’s Air Force claimed that its air defences shot down 220 out of 282 drones launched by Russia overnight, as well as seven missiles.
Meanwhile, the Russian Defence Ministry claimed it launched a massive strike on a number of facilities involved in drone production and telecommunications centres providing services to the Ukrainian military in Kyiv.
It further claimed striking two logistics centres in Odesa “used for storing and distributing military and dual-use cargo arriving in Ukraine from European nations,” as well as a tanker “transporting fuel intended for the Armed Forces of Ukraine” to the port of Chornomorsk.
It also claimed downing 40 Ukrainian drones overnight over six regions, as well as over Crimea, which Russia annexed in 2014.
The operational headquarters in Russia’s southern Krasnodar region said that a fire broke out at an unspecified facility in the region’s Dinskoy district due to falling drone debris.
“There were no casualties. Fifty personnel and 15 pieces of equipment – including units from the Russian Emergencies Ministry – have been deployed to extinguish the fire,” the statement added.
Independent verification of the claims is difficult due to the ongoing war.
Both Russia and Ukraine have ramped up strikes in recent months, targeting each other’s logistics centres, ports, and energy infrastructure.
Both sides deny deliberately targeting civilian infrastructure, maintaining that their strikes are directed at military targets or facilities linked to military activities.
