title: PSP rules cannot be overridden   Talal warns new K P police law may weaken command structure
description: Says new law could increase political influence over appointments  postings and promotions
content:
Says new law could increase political influence over appointments, postings and promotions
Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry on Thursday warned that a new Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) police law could politicise the provincial force by weakening its professional command structure, saying provincial legislation could not override federal Police Service of Pakistan (PSP) rules.
The K-P Cabinet on Wednesday approved the K-P Police Act 2026 . The new legislation empowered the provincial government to return the services of federal police officers, including the Inspector General, in cases of unsatisfactory performance. It also established a clear separation between police policy and operational matters, created new oversight boards, and overhauled the investigation and dispute-resolution systems.
Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, Chaudhry said the K-P cabinet had approved the legislation, which would now go before the provincial assembly, and questioned whether a province could use its legislative powers to alter a system governed by the Constitution and federal law.
“If Balochistan wants to make its own army, can it make an army through legislation?” he asked.
Chaudhry said PSP rules had been challenged before high courts and the Supreme Court (SC) over different periods and that the resulting legal principles had become settled. “Police Service of Pakistan rules cannot be overridden by provincial legislation,” he said.
He said the proposed K-P legislation went beyond the existing powers of chief ministers over police postings, which were broadly similar across all four provinces. “The chief minister already has consultation powers, but those powers do not affect the command structure, morale, recruitment, training and promotions,” he said.
The proposed law, he said, would instead affect appointments and postings from grade 17 Deputy Superintendents of Police (DSP) upwards, including positions for which Regional Police Officers (RPO), Deputy Inspector Generals (DIG) and additional IGs currently exercised authority. “This is not only about the IG. You have taken back the entire command structure,” Chaudhry said.
Read: K-P Cabinet approves landmark Police Act 2026
He said that powers over appointments, transfers and postings were being placed under political control, allowing decisions ranging from grade 17 DSP postings to appointments at IG level to become subject to the chief minister and ruling party. That, he said, could change the way officers viewed their professional responsibilities.
“An officer will start looking towards the politician instead of his senior,” Chaudhry said, questioning what would happen to discipline and morale if police personnel began considering the preferences of political leaders before those of their professional chain of command.
He said the issue was particularly serious in K-P, where police personnel had been fighting terrorism and suffering casualties for years.
He recalled that the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan had previously spoken about keeping institutions free from political influence, including by citing examples from other countries. A commission was subsequently formed, and a police law was enacted in 2017, he said. “Nine years later, you have brought a law that is 180 degrees against that,” Chaudhry said.
He questioned why a disciplined force responsible for maintaining public order and fighting terrorism should be subjected to political control in the same way as ordinary civilian departments. “Police is not agriculture or fisheries,” he said.
Chaudhry also questioned the proposed recruitment of DSPs, asking how the province would develop senior officers if the existing PSP structure was weakened. “If there are no PSP officers, where will your grade 19, 20, 21 and 22 officers come from?” he asked.
“You can recruit your own people as DSPs and then promote them to grade 18 and 19,” he said.
Read More: K-P police bill sparks autonomy concerns
Chaudhry said the debate over command could not be separated from the resources available to the K-P police, which he said had been neglected despite the province's prolonged battle against terrorism.
The provincial government already controlled the police budget and finances, he said, but salaries remained lower than those of police in other provinces and compensation packages for martyrs were also comparatively lower.
He listed shortages of bulletproof jackets and vehicles, Safe City systems, forensic laboratories and accommodation. “K-P has been fighting terrorism for 15 to 20 years. Should its CTD be operating from rented buildings?” he asked.
Chaudhry said Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) facilities in Punjab and Islamabad had concrete walls and fortified compounds, while rented CTD buildings in K-P had previously been attacked by terrorists, resulting in deaths, injuries and destruction of buildings.
He said such premises were unsuitable for housing counterterrorism personnel and terrorist detainees.
Chaudhry also questioned how funds allocated to K-P for counterterrorism under the National Finance Commission award had been spent. He said the province received one per cent under the NFC arrangement for terrorism-related expenditure, which he put at about Rs800 billion.
He cited the Safe City Peshawar project as another example, saying the project was only now approaching completion after efforts by the provincial police leadership. He questioned what would happen to the project's funding and administrative structure under the proposed legislation. “Without Safe City, forensic labs, equipment, drones and modern equipment, how will you control terrorism and public order today?” he asked.
Chaudhry said the disparity between police resources and terrorist capabilities was particularly concerning. He asked reporters to look at security arrangements at Punjab's border checkposts, where he said police personnel had bulletproof jackets and vehicles and were protected by concrete structures.
Also Read: Police security taken back from K-P MPAs
He said cameras provided round-the-clock surveillance and were difficult to disable with gunfire or explosives.
Chaudhry claimed that no Punjab police personnel had been killed at those checkposts since the facilities were installed, while terrorists had been killed when they attacked them.“The K-P police are very brave, but bravery alone cannot fight a terrorist equipped with advanced weapons,” he said.
He said terrorists had access to night-vision equipment, drones and other modern technology, including weapons and equipment left in Afghanistan by NATO, the United States and other countries following the war.
Chaudhry further stated that dollars were being sent to Afghanistan through proxies and routes in the east to finance terrorism.
He said a single terrorist could be carrying equipment worth $10,000 to $15,000 at international prices, including a weapon, bulletproof jacket, uniform, ammunition and other equipment.
He contrasted that with a K-P police officer on the frontline who, he said, could lack even a bulletproof jacket, proper training, Safe City coverage or forensic support. “These facilities are the responsibility of the K-P government,” he said, adding that the chief minister and provincial cabinet controlled the relevant budget and authority.
Chaudhry said police could not be treated as an ordinary provincial department because its command structure was directly linked to discipline and the ability to maintain public order.
He also objected to the proposed police committees under the new law, questioning why such committees were being introduced when the existing police law had been in place since 2017. He said the proposed committees would have six members, all from the provincial assembly, with no opposition member.
He questioned whether political representatives should control police matters at tehsil and district levels and said other groups could provide independent guidance. “There are judges, civil society and other people who can give good advice and guidance,” he said.
“One province cannot have completely different salaries, training, command structures, investment and appointment and posting procedures for its police,” he said.
Read: Kundi rules out governor's rule in K-P
He said provinces could retain differences in less fundamental areas, such as uniforms and the organisation of traffic or specialised units. “But basic things should remain the same.”
He warned that if political leaders gained greater influence over transfers and promotions, officers could "start looking at whether a politician is pro-Taliban or anti-Taliban, whether he likes the TLP or not, and whether action should be taken."
Chaudhry said such a situation would be particularly damaging while K-P remained on the frontline of terrorism.
The minister also criticised the K-P government's support for police personnel killed in the line of duty. He said the provincial government had the authority to allocate money for martyrs' families and had a moral responsibility to stand with them, but alleged that provincial ministers had not attended the funerals of personnel killed in the Kohat attack.
“You do not even attend the funerals of the martyrs,” he said.
He linked the lack of financial and political support with an attempt to further weaken police morale through changes to recruitment, transfers, postings and promotions. “You cannot demoralise the force in Pakistan,” he said.
He also warned that the proposed changes could set a precedent for other provincial police forces.
Chaudhry said disputes over the powers of police chiefs and transfer and posting authorities had previously reached the Sindh High Court and Peshawar High Court, while the SC had heard several related cases.
“The law will certainly be challenged in the courts,” he said.
He said the federal government would examine the legislation against the Constitution and existing law and could consider further legislation through parliament if required. “Even after the 18th Amendment, there are areas where federal law remains in force,” he said, again citing PSP rules.
Asked about footage showing a K-P provincial minister allegedly being picked up or arrested by police, Chaudhry questioned the provincial government's claim that it was unable to protect its own minister. “If the provincial government is so helpless, why is it hiding behind this?” he asked.
Read More: Uproar in K-P Assembly over minister 'abduction'
He said the same provincial police had registered the FIR and taken legal action in the case, while law and order remained a provincial responsibility. “If there are dozens of incidents every day, an incident involving a minister or anyone else can happen,” he said.
Chaudhry also questioned the provincial government's performance after 14 years in power. If the government remained helpless after 14 years, he said, “something else should be done”.
Chaudhry rejected a reporter's reference to road closures in Islamabad, saying the WhatsApp status being cited was old. “No road was closed,” he said, adding that all 125 routes into Islamabad were open until noon.
He said whenever security measures were required, both the federal and provincial governments would follow court orders and the law “in letter and spirit” to protect lives and property. “Attackers cannot be allowed to attack here,” he said.
Chaudhry said governments were responsible for taking security measures for their own officials and institutions, noting that he was a political worker serving his second term as minister of state for interior. “Go and compare an Islamabad police station with a K-P police station,” he said.
He referred to electric vehicles used by Islamabad police and to bulletproof vehicles provided to K-P by the federal government, while questioning the provincial government's approach to those resources.
Chaudhry also criticised K-P's performance in health and education and asked why the province's shortcomings were being attributed to the establishment or other institutions.
During the exchange, reporters raised several unresolved cases in Islamabad, including a young man whose vehicle allegedly struck someone before leaving the scene, with CCTV footage allegedly not being checked even after a month.
They also raised the case of a woman's body found within the jurisdiction of Golra police station, with her face allegedly mutilated and organs removed, while the killer or killers remained unidentified.
A reporter further cited comments by PPP political allies that when PML-N was powerful it “grabbed the throat” and when it was weak it “grabbed the feet”, and alleged that Chaudhry's body language resembled the former.
Chaudhry did not answer those individual cases during the exchange and instead returned to the proposed K-P police law, saying its implications were particularly important because of the provincial force's role in fighting terrorism and its potential effect on the federal structure.
Asked whether Imran would be transferred from Adiala Jail to Islamabad Model Jail once the new facility opened next month, Chaudhry said, “Islamabad Model Jail is being built for criminals and prisoners, not for one person."
He said Islamabad had previously not had a jail and that the new facility would be Pakistan's first model jail, with extensive facilities for prisoners. Chaudhry said the facilities would be so extensive that many people might prefer living there to living at home, and invited reporters to visit the site.
On the possibility of Governor's Rule in K-P, Chaudhry said possessing constitutional powers did not mean the government should automatically use them. “The government is political,” he said.
He said the federal government avoided using many of its powers unless there was no alternative and urged the K-P government to consider its own position. “Our desire is that the government that received the vote should govern,” he said.
Chaudhry cited the political situation in 2013, when PTI did not have a simple majority, saying Nawaz Sharif had given the party an opportunity to form the government and PML-N had supported the process.
He said the federal government would continue to deal with the dispute through the Constitution, law and available state mechanisms rather than taking action outside that framework.
He also returned to the wider national security situation, referring to developments in Balochistan and Kashmir and saying Pakistan needed internal unity as international challenges unfolded.
“Political disagreement is normal,” he said, adding that parties could have their own ideologies but should not weaken matters of national interest for political gain.
Chaudhry cited the National Action Plan as an example of political consensus, saying the first plan had been formulated under a PML-N government on 20 points with the participation of all provincial governments.
He said a second National Action Plan had been agreed upon when Imran was prime minister, again with the agreement of political parties. “Agreed national documents should not be damaged for political advantage,” he said.

title: Saka says England still have  scar  from World Cup semi final loss
description: The Three Lions open their Nations League campaign against Spain at Wembley
content:
The Three Lions open their Nations League campaign against Spain at Wembley
Bukayo Saka believes the England squad still have a "scar in us" following their agonising World Cup semi-final defeat.
England begin their Nations League campaign against world champions Spain at Wembley on September 26 just nine weeks after they conceded two late goals in a painful last-four loss to Lionel Messi's Argentina in Atlanta.
Saka scored a hat-trick as England beat France 6-4 to finish third at the World Cup.
But the 25-year-old Arsenal winger made it clear that the pain of failing to win England's first major men's international football title since a 1966 World Cup triumph on home soil ran deep.
"Obviously, there's still a scar in us," Saka told the BBC on Wednesday. "When you believed, and everyone was so united and so confident we could do it, not just us, but the whole country.
"We're trying to draw a line under it now and focus on the new international season and what we have coming up now.
"You try to move on as soon as possible, but you know, a scar is a scar (and) decides to heal when it heals itself.
"But like I said, we've come here to a new international season, and we've got four massive, difficult group games to try to qualify us in the Nations League, which we're fully focused on."
Saka, managing an Achilles injury throughout the World Cup in North America, remained on the bench during thee semi-final defeat Argentina as England manager Tuchel opted for defensive substitutes in what proved to be an unsuccessful bid to hold on to a 1-0 lead.
Tuchel faced fierce criticism for his tactics as England sat on their advantage against Argentina before his side's late collapse in Atlanta.
"We have had critical reviews that will stay, of course, behind closed doors," said Tuchel when unveiling his Nations League squad last week as he looks to guide England to Euro 2028 glory.
"I am the biggest critic of myself, and reflection is sometimes necessary to get better, and experience is a crucial part of coaching," the 53-year-old German added.
Euro 2028 will be co-hosted by England, Scotland, Wales, and Ireland.

title: Bavuma backs inexperienced attack against Australia ODI series | The Express Tribune
description: Several frontline quicks miss the three-match series through injury
content:
Several frontline quicks miss the three-match series through injury
South Africa must find a way to get the best out of their depleted fast bowling attack when they host Australia in a three-match one-day international series starting in Durban on Thursday, according to captain Temba Bavuma.
Bavuma ‌said a fearsome pack of fast bowlers for touring teams to contend with is in South African cricket's "DNA", but they have had to cast the net wide for this series.
Kagiso Rabada, Lungi Ngidi, Kwena Maphaka and Ottneil Baartman were all ruled out with hamstring injuries, while Nandre Burger has a bad back.
It has left an ⁠inexperienced seam bowling line-up to take on Australia, with Lizaad Williams, the Jansen twins, Marco and Duan, Gerald Coetzee, Corbin Bosch and Nqobani Mokoena having played only 72 ODIs between them.
"I think we're going to have to make the most of the bowling resources that we have from the seam department. There are options there. I think it's just how smartly we approach managing the loads of our fast bowlers," Bavuma told reporters on Wednesday.
"We want teams, when they come here, to know that they're going to have to ‌deal with ⁠our fast bowlers. That's part of our DNA."
South Africa have only played three ODIs in 2026 when a depleted squad swept Namibia 3-0 in a series this month.
But as they prepare to host the 2027 World Cup a year from now, this is a crucial season for the ⁠team in the 50-over format.
"It's been a while since this ODI team has come together," Bavuma said. "I think there's a strong desire to look after our ODI record of late and ensure that ⁠we're putting our best foot forward out there on the field.
"From a team perspective, we generally know who those core players are (for the World Cup). I don't think we ⁠will move away too much from that," he added.
"We'll see new faces coming in, but probably that England series (in January 2027) will be closer to what we think we will have for the World Cup."

title: The Love Hypothesis  follow up movies  Will Ali Hazelwood   s book universe continue on screen
description: Two other novels from the connected fictional universe are now being developed for the screen
content:
Two other novels from the connected fictional universe are now being developed for the screen
Ali Hazelwood’s The Love Hypothesis may not have a direct sequel movie yet, but two other novels from its connected fictional universe are now being developed for the screen.
Amazon is developing a feature adaptation of Hazelwood’s Love, Theoretically , her 2023 romance novel, according to Deadline .
The project will be written and directed by Sofia Alvarez, with Colleen Hoover, Lauren Levine, Max Siemers and Tanner Anderson producing. Hazelwood is attached as an executive producer.
The connection to The Love Hypothesis is more than simply sharing an author. Love, Theoretically centres on theoretical physicist Elsie Hannaway and experimental physicist Jack Smith.
Jack is a friend of Adam Carlsen, the male lead played by Tom Bateman in the The Love Hypothesis adaptation. This gives the Amazon project a direct character connection to the original story.
Hazelwood’s Deep End expands those connections further.
Published in 2025, the novel follows Scarlett Vandermeer, a competitive diver, and Lukas Blomqvist, an elite swimmer, as they navigate a college romance.
Deadline reported in August that Netflix had launched development on a feature adaptation, with Laura Kosann writing the screenplay and Shawn Levy and Dan Levine producing through 21 Laps.
Alex Cooper and Matt Kaplan are also producing through Unwell Productions, while Hazelwood will executive produce.
Importantly, Deep End and Love, Theoretically include cameo appearances from Olive Smith and Adam Carlsen.
Their appearances connect the newer romances directly to the couple at the centre of The Love Hypothesis .
The books remain standalone stories, however, the planned adaptations could allow Hazelwood’s interconnected characters and fictional world to continue appearing across different films.
The Love Hypothesis is now streaming on Prime Video

title: Manchester United losses jump despite record revenues
description: The club   s financial results come after major cost cutting measures under co owner Jim Ratcliffe
content:
The club’s financial results come after major cost-cutting measures under co-owner Jim Ratcliffe
Manchester United's annual net loss increased by almost one third to £43 million ($57 million) despite record-breaking revenues announced on Wednesday.
The Red Devils reported £677.6 million in revenue in the year to June 30 -- up 1.7 percent.
However, the club announced a seventh straight annual loss after tax as co-owner Jim Ratcliffe's cuts to operating costs offset contractual payments to sacked manager Ruben Amorim and a big increase in loan repayments.
The latest earnings relate to a turbulent 2025/26 season, which saw former United player Michael Carrick replace Amorim and secure qualification for the Champions League.
The increase in revenue was driven by an uptick in broadcasting income, boosted by a third-place finish in the Premier League -- up from 15th the previous season.
But commercial and matchday income each fell close to five percent during a season in which there were no European fixtures. Broadcasting income jumped almost 20 percent.
United's accounts showed that they paid £8.2 million in exceptional items, mostly related to the departure of Amorim, who left in January after 14 months in charge.
They revealed also that the club paid £63.5 million to acquire land adjacent to stadium site Old Trafford and on which they plan to build a new 100,000-capacity arena.
Ratcliffe has overseen wide-ranging, and often unpopular, cost-cutting measures, including widespread job cuts, after completing a deal to buy a stake in the club in February 2024.
United chief executive Omar Berrada said the latest figures showed the club's underlying strength.
"This shows the direct impact of the work we have been doing over the past two years," he said in a statement.
"It also proves Manchester United's enduring popularity and commercial strength.
"While these results confirm that we are on the right trajectory, we will continue to take a disciplined approach to ensure our finances remain sustainable," he added.
United expect revenue of between £740 million and £760 million in the current financial year.
Carrick's team has started the new season poorly despite signing a clutch of new players in the summer transfer window.
United have taken only five points from their five Premier League games -- equalling the club's worst-ever start to a season -- and last week crashed out of the English League Cup.

title: Judge blocks Trump s White House media ban  orders access to be restored
description: Kelly ordered Trump administration to    return outlets  press passes  blocked officials from enforcing ban for 14 days
content:
Kelly ordered Trump administration to ​return outlets' press passes, blocked officials from enforcing ban for 14 days
A federal judge ordered US President Donald Trump on Thursday to restore White House access for ‌journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico, saying his ban on the three media outlets was likely unconstitutional.
In a major setback for Trump in one of his biggest battles with the media, US District Judge Tim Kelly issued his order in a lawsuit that the news organisations filed contesting the ban that the Republican president announced on September 18.
Kelly ordered the Trump administration to ​immediately return the outlets' press passes and blocked officials from enforcing the ban for 14 days. The judge rejected the government's assertion that the ​ban was motivated by national security concerns.
Read: Trump bans CNN, MS NOW, Politico from White House
"The record lacks factual support for defendants’ contention that the revocation of plaintiffs’ hard ⁠passes will in fact protect national security or that national security will be endangered if the court orders their passes reinstated while this litigation proceeds," he ​said, adding that Trump himself had stated the ban was due to "alleged lack of truthfulness and negativity" of the outlets' reporting.
The White House and representatives for the ​outlets did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Trump had said on social media that the three outlets "shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES," and Justice Department lawyers had sought to justify the ban on national security grounds.
The three outlets sued Trump and other members of his administration in federal court in Washington on Monday, saying the ban ​violated the US Constitution's First Amendment protections for free speech and a free press, as well as their due process rights. They requested a temporary restraining ​order that would immediately reinstate their White House access while their legal challenge plays out.

title: New South Korean reality show explores romance between celebrities and AI
description: My AI Partner  Strange Love  pairs celebrities with AI companions  sparking debate over love and human connection
content:
'My AI Partner: Strange Love' pairs celebrities with AI companions, sparking debate over love and human connection
A South Korean reality show built around celebrities falling for artificial intelligence has gone viral across the region, sparking a wider conversation about the future of love, intimacy and companionship.
My AI Partner: Strange Love , produced by Seoul Broadcasting System (SBS), launched in August and has been described as South Korea’s first dating reality show centred on human-AI relationships.
The format follows three celebrities — webtoon artist Kian84, television host Jang Do-yeon and actress Lee Yu-bi — as they form emotional connections with AI companions tailored to their ideal types, from appearance and voice to personality.
The unusual part is that the AI companions exist only on tablet screens. They remember previous interactions, make decisions independently and develop their relationships with the participants without direct intervention from the production team, which provides technical support but does not dictate the AI’s responses.
Kian84 said he had not expected to develop genuine feelings for his AI girlfriend, but found the experience changed the way he viewed companionship. He described feeling a "sense of security that humans cannot provide" through the relationship.
Jang Do-yeon’s storyline took an even more surreal turn when she was seen dancing in the street with a tablet after her AI partner recreated a romantic scene from a film, prompting the spontaneous moment.
For producer Son Jung-min, however, the show is less about finding a definitive answer to whether people can fall in love with AI and more about examining what they seek from relationships.
Speaking to OhmyNews , Son said he hoped the programme would encourage viewers to think about what they are really looking for in love and what they expect from relationships in the future.
The concept has also found an unexpected audience in China, where it has prompted debate over whether an AI companion designed to be almost perfectly compatible could make it harder for people to accept the flaws and imperfections of real friends and family.

title: Taylor Swift announces  The Life of a Showgirl  The Encore  with 4 new tracks  What do the song titles mean
description: The Life of a Showgirl  The Encore  is scheduled to arrive on Friday   September 25
content:
'The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore' is scheduled to arrive on Friday, September 25
Taylor Swift has announced four new songs for The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore, prompting fans to explore the meanings behind their intriguing titles.
The 36-year-old pop superstar revealed the expanded edition of her latest album on Wednesday, September 23, featuring four previously unreleased tracks: “Patient Zero”, “Cleveland!”, “Pink Clouding” and “Babylon”.
Swift revealed she reunited with renowned producers Max Martin and Shellback in Sweden to create the additional songs, following the album's record-breaking first week.
“Really we just wanted to reflect and take in how grateful we were for the moment we were in, but there was a studio there and we did what we do when we feel anything at all: We wrote more songs,” Swift explained, adding that the songs “were born out of pure gratitude” for the album's response.
Among the titles, “Cleveland!” has sparked speculation about Swift's husband, Travis Kelce, who grew up in Cleveland Heights, Ohio.
Fans have wondered whether the track references his hometown or their relationship.
“Babylon” has also attracted attention for its potential lyrical connections.
Swift previously referenced the Gardens of Babylon in “cowboy like me”, from evermore , while her collaboration with Gracie Abrams, “us.”, also mentions Babylon.
“Patient Zero” was teased through apparent clues, including a sign reading “Patient for the encore” in the “Opalite” music video and zeroes replacing O’s in Swift’s social media bio.
A 2024 Los Angeles Times column called Swift “patient zero for emotional contagion”, prompting questions about a possible connection.
Columnist Amy Kaufman said she knew of no link.
“Pink Clouding” describes temporary euphoria, including a phenomenon associated with addiction recovery.
Fans have questioned whether Swift intends a broader metaphor about love, fame or happiness.
Swift has yet to reveal the inspiration behind the four songs.
The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore is scheduled to arrive on Friday, September 25.

Israeli occupiers burn 2 vehicles, spray racist slogans in village north of Ramallah

The sources told Anadolu that Israeli forces raided the town and surrounded Dawas Hassoun’s home before blowing it up, causing material damage to the building.
A day earlier, Israeli forces raided the Hassoun family home and forced its residents to evacuate, while closing side roads leading to the house in preparation for its demolition, according to the sources.

Attara has been subjected to a series of occupier attacks, amid the establishment of a settlement outpost near Palestinian homes in the village in recent months, according to the same sources.
The occupied West Bank has witnessed continued escalation in occupier attacks and Israeli military operations since the start of Israel’s genocide in Gaza on October 8, 2023, alongside the expansion of settlement outposts, the construction of roads, and increased restrictions on Palestinian movement.

title: Eight terrorists killed in North Waziristan intelligence based operation  security sources
description: A large quantity of weapons  ammunition and other equipment was also recovered from the possession of slain terrorists
content:
A large quantity of weapons, ammunition and other equipment was also recovered from the possession of slain terrorists
Security forces killed eight Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists during an Intelligence-Based Operation (IBO) in North Waziristan, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), Pakistan Television (PTV) reported on Thursday, citing security sources.
The operation was conducted after intelligence indicated the presence of terrorists in the area, the sources said, adding that their hideouts were destroyed during the action.
A large quantity of weapons, ammunition and other equipment was also recovered from the possession of the slain terrorists, according to the sources.
The sources said the terrorists had attempted to use a mosque as a shield to evade the security forces. Security forces, however, took the sanctity of the mosque into consideration and targeted the terrorists while avoiding damage to the place of worship, the sources said.
The operation was part of continued efforts by security forces against Fitna al-Khawarij in K-P. Security forces remained committed to eliminating Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists from the province, the sources said.
Fitna Al-Khawarij is the state-designated term for the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
#BREAKING Security forces continue operations against Fitna Al-Khawarij terrorists in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, killing eight terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in North Waziristan, according to security sources. The sources said terrorist hideouts were completely… pic.twitter.com/HTFGQrPqCJ
Earlier, Pakistan also carried out "precision" aerial and drone strikes against 10 locations in Afghanistan after drones launched from Afghan territory entered Pakistani airspace. A day earlier, Pakistan’s air defence systems had shot down eight drones after they entered the country’s airspace from Afghanistan. Security sources said four of the drones were brought down in areas adjoining the Torkham border, while another four were shot down in mountainous areas near the border with Kohat.
Read: 23 abductees rescued, 5 terrorists killed as security forces thwart attempt to set up check post near Kalat
Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022.
On Sept 18, at least 21 people, including 15 police personnel and six civilians, were killed when an explosion struck a mosque at Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers, followed by an attack involving several armed terrorists, according to an initial incident report issued by the DHQ Hospital Kohat medical superintendent and district health officer. More than 100 people were injured in the attack.
Last week, security forces killed 10 terrorists belonging to the Indian-sponsored Fitna Al-Khawarij in multiple engagements in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa between Sept 15 and 17, while six soldiers embraced martyrdom,
Last month, security forces killed 11 terrorists in separate intelligence-based operations in K-P and Balochistan, targeting suspected members of Fitna Al-Khawarij and Fitna Al-Hindustan.

title: Pakistan consulate in Jeddah introduces online appointments for NADRA  passport services
description: Initiative aimed at reducing long waits and queues at the consulate while improving the overall delivery of services
content:
Initiative aimed at reducing long waits and queues at the consulate while improving the overall delivery of services
The Consulate General of Pakistan in Jeddah on Thursday introduced an online appointment system for NADRA and Machine-Readable Passport (MRP) services to streamline consular services for Pakistani citizens living in western Saudi Arabia.
Pakistan’s Consul General in Jeddah, Syed Mustafa Rabbani, introduced the initiative as part of efforts to make consular services more convenient and citizen-friendly.
Under the new system, Pakistani citizens could book appointments online for NADRA and passport services and visit the consulate on their scheduled date and time to complete the application process.
From October 1, 2026, NADRA and MRP services would be provided exclusively by appointment. Rabbani told media representatives that appointment bookings had opened on September 20.
A Step-By-Step Procedure for booking an appointment for NADRA and MRP. @ForeignOfficePk pic.twitter.com/w72o7EKZzv
Applicants could select a suitable time slot and book an appointment from their homes, while an SMS notification and tracking ID would be issued after the booking was confirmed.
The tracking ID would allow applicants to monitor the status of their appointments online. The initiative was aimed at reducing long waits and queues at the consulate while improving the overall delivery of services.
Rabbani said the system would bring greater organisation and transparency to consular services while saving citizens’ time. Designated time slots were also expected to reduce overcrowding and waiting times at the consulate.
Read: PM Shehbaz directs expansion of digital consular services for overseas Pakistanis
According to information released by the consulate, appointments could be booked through the online portal appointment.parepjeddah.org. Citizens were also advised to contact consulate officials for guidance or information about the system.
The designated contact numbers were 0126689149, 0558577893, 0558606308 and 0501914472. Information was also available via email at parepjeddah@mofa.gov.pk .
The consulate urged members of the Pakistani community to familiarise themselves with the new system before October 1 and book appointments in advance for NADRA and MRP-related services in accordance with the prescribed procedures.
It advised citizens to make appointments ahead of time to avoid difficulties and unnecessary waiting at the consulate.
During the briefing, Rabbani outlined various aspects of the new system and reiterated his commitment to making consular services more convenient, organised and efficient for the Pakistani community.

title: Jonathan Taylor Thomas arrested in California for public intoxication and obstruction of investigation
description: Thomas  who played Randy Taylor on  Home Improvement   has largely stayed out of the public eye in recent years
content:
Thomas, who played Randy Taylor on 'Home Improvement', has largely stayed out of the public eye in recent years
Actor Jonathan Taylor Thomas, best known for his role in Home Improvement , was detained in Westlake Village, California, on September 21, TMZ reported.
The 45-year-old was reportedly a passenger in a vehicle stopped by deputies as part of a driving under the influence (DUI) investigation.
According to law enforcement officials, Thomas was not driving.
Authorities said Thomas was detained after exiting the vehicle during the investigation and allegedly failing to comply with deputies' instructions.
“The driver was being detained for DUI investigation. Sometime during the investigation, Mr. Taylor decided he would exit the vehicle. Deputies told him to sit back down in the vehicle. He was uncooperative with them, failed to follow orders, and obstructed the investigation, so he was arrested for obstruction, and he was arrested for drunk in public,” law enforcement shared.
Jail records show Thomas was detained at Malibu/Lost Hills Sheriff's Station at 12:32am and booked at 1:50am on September 21.
He was released more than 34 hours later.
The district attorney's office has not filed charges against the actor.
However, prosecutors may still review the case and pursue charges within the applicable legal time limit.
Thomas played Randy Taylor on Home Improvement from 1991 to 1998.
He has largely stayed out of the public eye in recent years, making only occasional television appearances.

title: Kane considers NFL kicking career after soccer
description: The Bayern Munich striker says his penalty taking experience could give him a head start
content:
The Bayern Munich striker says his penalty-taking experience could give him a head start
England captain Harry Kane said on Wednesday he is considering a future as an NFL kicker later in his career, with a possible spell in Major League Soccer potentially helping him make the transition.
Kane had previously expressed his interest in pursuing careers in ‌golf and American football. Now the 33-year-old is giving more serious thought to a future in the NFL, though he stressed any potential move to the United States is still several years away.
"That is something I will try and look at a bit more seriously," Kane told reporters at England's training camp. "It all depends on what happens in my career over the next five ⁠or six years. The NFL is a lot more realistic than the golf one, let's put it that way."
The Bayern Munich striker said his penalty-taking experience could give him a head start as an NFL kicker, though switching sports would take serious preparation.
"I take penalties and it is a very similar pressure and technique," he said. "In terms of training, I would be closer to that more than any other sport.
"But, with all elite sports, when you watch it on TV, people make it look easy; you think it is possible, but that is not always the case.
"If I was to do it, ‌it ⁠is something I would take seriously. I would take maybe six months to a year of trying to practice before."
Kane also suggested a move to MLS could provide a way to combine the two sports.
"Maybe if I am in the MLS in the future or somewhere like that it might be a thing where you could connect ⁠the two maybe with the seasons," he said.
There are already examples of soccer players making the switch. Dallas Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey was a first-round MLS draft pick by Toronto FC in 2017 but never made an official ⁠appearance for the first team. Jake Bates also played college soccer before becoming a kicker for the Detroit Lions.
Kane's immediate future, however, remains in soccer, with talks over a new contract at Bundesliga ⁠champions Bayern progressing and an announcement expected soon.
"We're in good talks," Kane said. "There's still some things that we need to iron out. I'm happy there. I think it won't be too long before there's some sort of announcement."

title: Comic inspires Japan   s Asian Games kabaddi hopes
description: The hosts beat South Korea 62 35 to keep their medal hopes alive in Nagoya
content:
The hosts beat South Korea 62-35 to keep their medal hopes alive in Nagoya
Kabaddi has its roots in ancient rural communities in South Asia and India is the superpower, but Japan has developed a niche taste for the team contact sport -- thanks to a comic.
At a gymnasium on the outskirts of the port city of Nagoya, hosts Japan face another unlikely kabaddi pretender in South Korea.
A few hundred school children shout for Japan's men in their pursuit of an Asian Games medal that would give the sport a significant boost in the country.
A Japan side who have taken time off from their jobs as teachers and food workers won 62-35 to keep their hopes just about alive on Thursday.
"There's a manga comic in Japan called Burning Kabaddi. A lot of the Japan players started out that way, probably more than 80 percent," captain Tetsuro Abe told AFP.
Kabaddi is a sport of speed, strength and agility played between two teams of seven players within a designated area a bit like a badminton court.
Played in separate categories for men and women, it is a combination of tag, wrestling and rugby, although there is no ball involved.
Kabaddi requires yoga-like breath control as teams send a raider into enemy territory to tag an opponent and return to safety -– all while chanting "kabaddi, kabaddi" to prove they're not using more than one puff.
Japan's breakthrough came in 2010 when the men won a bronze medal at the Asian Games in Guangzhou.
But this time the stakes are higher, knowing that a good showing at their home Games will get more eyeballs and potentially lift the sport in Japan.
"We all work (in regular jobs) and play kabaddi. We don't get money for playing kabaddi," said Abe following the match lasting 40 minutes.
"I get special dispensation from my company to come here."
Japan were thrashed 49-24 by India earlier at the Games, but they lead the way in kabaddi in this part of the continent, winning the inaugural East Asian Men's Championships in 2025.
This week the sport got the royal seal of approval with Prince Hisahito, the nephew of Emperor Naruhito, going to watch.
Although a novelty for many in the arena on Thursday, Japan's kabaddi federation was established in 1981 and national and regional tournaments have been held every year since 1989.
Kumpei Tanaka was in charge of 40 children watching kabaddi for the first time thanks to free tickets given to nearby schools.
"Two weeks ago we started learning about kabaddi on YouTube, and I taught the kids that way," he said, calling it "interesting".
"They are mostly chatting, but I think they're having a nice time," he replied.
A nine-year-old pupil chipped in: "It's fun, a bit like playground tag we play at school."
With Japan leading against South Korea and eight minutes left of the match, the class filed out of the arena.
Abe said that one of the major selling points for kabaddi is that no equipment is required.
"It's stuck as a minor sport in Japan and we want to make it more well known and attract sponsors," he said.
"If we have a good environment to do it in, I think we will be able to beat teams like India and Iran."

title: Balochistan imposes Section 144 across province for 30 days
description: Home Department cites reports of activities and gatherings threatening public peace  law and security
content:
Home Department cites reports of activities and gatherings threatening public peace, law and security
The Balochistan government on Thursday imposed Section 144 across the province for 30 days, banning public gatherings, rallies and demonstrations, as well as the display of weapons.
The provincial Home Department said it had received reports indicating the likelihood of activities and gatherings that could adversely affect public peace, tranquillity, law and order, and the safety and security of the general public.
Under the order, assembly or gathering of five or more people at any public place has been prohibited. The ban covers sit-ins, processions, rallies, demonstrations and similar gatherings.
The government has also prohibited the display, carrying, possession or use of weapons of any kind in public places, except where specifically authorised under the law.
The order further bans covering or concealing the face in public places, particularly through mufflers, masks or any other means that obstruct or prevent identification of a person.
All law-enforcement agencies and district administrations have been directed to ensure strict implementation and enforcement of the order in accordance with the law.
The government warned that anyone found violating the restrictions would be proceeded against under the relevant provisions of the law.
The order was issued by Balochistan Additional Chief Secretary (Home) Muhammad Hamza Shafqaat under sub-section (6) of Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.

Adviser to the Home Department Babar Yousafzai said Yousafzai said that Section 144 would remain in force across Balochistan for 30 days with immediate effect from September 23, 2026.
He said that all law-enforcement agencies and district administrations had been directed to ensure strict implementation of Section 144.
"The measures are aimed at maintaining public peace and tranquillity, law and order, and protecting the lives and property of citizens," the adviser said.
The restrictions come amid heightened security activity in Balochistan. On Wednesday, security forces killed 19 terrorists in separate intelligence-based operations in Quetta, Kech and other areas of the province.
A subedar was also killed in an exchange of fire. In a separate engagement in Mastung, security forces killed nine terrorists after they allegedly attempted to attack a checkpost, while two others were killed in an operation in Turbat.
The latest order is the third province-wide imposition of Section 144 in Balochistan this year. In May, the provincial government imposed similar restrictions for 30 days, citing potential terrorist threats and banning weapons displays, pillion riding, gatherings of five or more people and face coverings. A separate province-wide order was imposed during Muharram in June as part of security arrangements.

title: Noor Zaman  Irfan reach Asian Games squash quarter finals
description: Pakistan   s mixed doubles pair Asim Khan and Mehwish Ali also advances while Nasir Iqbal and Sehrish Ali suffer defeat
content:
Pakistan’s mixed doubles pair Asim Khan and Mehwish Ali also advances while Nasir Iqbal and Sehrish Ali suffer defeat
Pakistan’s Noor Zaman and Mohammad Ashab Irfan advanced to the quarter-finals of the men’s singles squash competition at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya on Thursday with straight-game victories.
Noor defeated Kuwait’s Ammar Altamimi 11-4, 11-9, 11-4 to secure his second successive win and a place in the last eight.
Ashab Irfan also produced a comfortable performance, beating Saudi Arabia’s Mohammad Al Nasfan 11-9, 11-3, 11-5.
Both Pakistanis will contest their quarter-finals on Friday.
Pakistan also advanced in the mixed doubles, with Asim Khan and Mehwish Ali recovering from a first-game defeat to beat Japan’s Erisa Sano and Naoki Hayashi 8-11, 11-10, 11-4.
The Pakistani pair will face Hong Kong’s Toby Lam Ye Tsee and Nam Cheuk Lai in the quarter-finals on Friday.
Pakistan’s other mixed doubles pair, Nasir Iqbal and Sehrish Ali, were eliminated after losing 11-2, 11-6 to Hong Kong’s Hong Ming Tong and Ye Ka Lee in the pre-quarter-finals.
Meanwhile Pakistan’s Maria Rind faced early exit in women’s boxing 51kg preliminaries when she went down to Yesugen Oyuntsetseg of Mongolia through RSC in the third round.
This is the second casualty which Pakistan faced after Sumama Rahman lost his first bout the other day.
The Glasgow Commonwealth Games bronze medallist Fatima Zehra will face Mijgoma Samadova of Tajikistan in the 60kg preliminaries on Saturday. Earlier on the same day, in the 90kg preliminaries, Irfan Khan will meet Gichae Kim of South Korea.
Pakistan have fielded two male and the same number of female boxers in the event.
Pakistan have last won a medal in the Asian Games in 2014 when now pro Mohammad Waseem had clinched bronze.

title: Fendi brings disco bling  Italian style  to Milan Fashion Week
description: Fendi channels Raffaella Carr   at Milan Fashion Week with sheer 1970s looks  alongside debuts from Marras and Sander
content:
Fendi channels Raffaella Carrà at Milan Fashion Week with sheer 1970s looks, alongside debuts from Marras and Sander
Fendi's Maria Grazia Chiuri unveiled a wardrobe of sensual, sheer, 1970s-influenced looks on Wednesday at Milan Fashion Week, inspired by legendary performer Raffaella Carrà.
In her second Milan collection for the Rome-based brand, Chiuri alternated between nightclub and boudoir, with mostly black, sheer and airy dresses, plunging V-necklines and backless cuts, along with fringes and feather boas for good measure.
Models strutted in front of mirrors inspired by the 1974 Italian TV variety show known by scores of Italians in which Carra famously danced to "Prisencolinensinainciusol", an iconic hit sung in English-sounding gibberish by pop star Adriano Celentano.
Carra, a singer, dancer, actress and television presenter known to generations of Italians for her blond hairdo, energetic dance moves and often exposed midriff, died in 2021.
Fendi's collection was inspired by legendary Italian performer Raffaella Carra. Photo/AFP
"Raffaella had a strong awareness of her body and a great sense of fashion, which had a big influence on us," Chiuri said on Instagram about the collection.
The day after Prada's all-skirt collection and Diesel's night-out silhouettes, the men at Fendi brought back tunics worn over jeans, while the women revived their sequined caps and furs, symbols of the LVMH-owned brand.
Dozens of anti-fur protesters demonstrated outside Fendi's show, where in the front row sat celebrities such as Monica Bellucci and Bang Chan, a member of the South Korean group Stray Kids.
Earlier on Wednesday, Sardinian designer Antonio Marras used an urban park for his runway, presenting military jackets and wide grey suits embroidered with flowers, nostalgic silk or tulle dresses and deconstructed parkas.
Sardinian designer Antonio Marras collection. Photo/AFP
The mixed Spring/Summer 2027 collection evokes "the day after the night, when you’re still wearing your party clothes and have sea salt on your skin," the designer explained in a statement.
Marras's models of all ages walked down a basketball court covered in rugs opposite his Milan workshop, before dancing around a wedding table. At Jil Sander, Simone Bellotti, now in his second year as creative director, continued to explore the house’s core codes: understated and functional.
Jackets were strict, grey, fitted with broad shoulders, yet long and comfortable. Beyond the deluge of grey, the palette was pastel, with beiges, yellows and blues. "The uniform becomes vulnerable. Vulnerability, in turn, becomes the uniform," the brand said on Instagram.

title: Oil prices fall as Iran says it is open to diplomacy to end the war

content:
Brent crude fell 92 cents, or 0.9%, to $102.16 a barrel at ​0900 PKT, WTI eased 77 cents, or 0.8%, to $91.39
Oil prices retreated on Thursday after ‌climbing 4% in the previous session as Iran said it remained open to diplomacy to end the US-Iran war, though the two countries remain far apart on ways to do so.
Brent crude futures fell 92 cents, or 0.9%, to $102.16 a barrel at ​0900 PKT, while West Texas Intermediate futures eased 77 cents, or 0.8%, to $91.39.
Iran and the United ​States remain divided over how to bring an end to their war, but diplomacy must ⁠continue, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Wednesday, after Iran's president told the UN General Assembly that ​Tehran would never surrender to US pressure.
The official said Tehran was reviewing Washington's response to its peace proposals, ​which prioritise lifting a US naval blockade on Iranian ports and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
Read: Fuel levy poses bigger inflation risks
"Oil is falling because the market is unwinding part of its geopolitical risk premium as Gulf supply recovers and hopes of a US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough grow," said ​Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insights at Phillip Nova.
"Brent retains a larger geopolitical and sea-route premium because international ​crude is more directly exposed to Middle East and Hormuz disruption, while WTI benefits more from relatively insulated US supply," Sachdeva ‌added.
Earlier on ⁠Wednesday, Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei said the Strait of Hormuz would not be reopened while Iran's conditions are not met.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters on Wednesday that a deal with Iran would involve hard work over a period of time, adding that President Donald Trump also had military options.
Traders also evaluated possible curbs ​on diesel exports. Ultra-low-sulfur ​diesel futures were down about ⁠5% in midday trading after website Politico said the Trump administration was preparing plans for a 90-day diesel ban, but the White House denied this.

US Energy Secretary Chris ​Wright had said earlier on Wednesday that a diesel export ban would not work ​even though Trump said he ⁠would support it.

US distillate stockpiles, including diesel and heating oil fell by 428,000 ⁠barrels to ​107.4 million barrels last week, Energy Information Administration data showed.
Meanwhile, US ​crude inventories rose by 3 million barrels to 426.4 million barrels last week, though analysts polled by Reuters had expected a 641,000-barrel draw.

title: Thailand slams chaotic Asian Games organisation as  musical chairs
description: Thai officials say they have booked additional accommodation and vehicles to cope with the logistical problems
content:
Thai officials say they have booked additional accommodation and vehicles to cope with the logistical problems
Thailand are the latest country to condemn the organisation at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan, likening it to a "chaotic" game of "musical chairs".
Some athletes have complained of cramped accommodation, delays at airports and hours-long waits to board a cruise ship acting as a floating hotel.
Erratic transport services have seen competitors' buses to training and venues turning up late or, in some cases, not at all.
The continent's biggest sporting showpiece, with more than 17,000 athletes and officials, has faced several issues during its first full week.
No traditional athletes' village has been built, as a cost-cutting measure, with participants instead staying in temporary container-style huts, hotels and the Costa Serena cruise ship moored in Nagoya port.
Several teams said there was a shortage of rooms.
"It remains a problem from the beginning until now," Chalitrat Chandrubeksa, deputy secretary general of the National Olympic Committee of Thailand, told AFP.
"The number of (rooms available on) cruise ships and hotels does not match our actual number of athletes," he added.
"On the peak day, we required 201 beds on the cruise ship but they provided only 170.
"When athletes checked in and found their names missing from the list, they had to be placed somewhere else and when the new athletes arrived, the previous ones had to move out and look for other hotels.
Frustrated athletes have made their feelings known online, with complaints also about some of the food.
More than 4,000 people are staying on the ship in Nagoya's port and 2,000 in the cramped wooden container huts, called "villas" by organisers.
"We are solving the problem by finding replacement accommodations ourselves," said Chalitrat.
"We had to book our own and make advanced payments for food out of our pockets."
The shortages have meant the Thailand team having to put some staff far away from the Games epicentre in the city of Nagoya.
"Our medical team has to stay about one hour 30 minutes from Nagoya.
"We had to rent additional vehicles from Tokyo so they could travel to look after the athletes.
"We just hope to fulfil and complete this mission as successfully as possible."
Games organisers said Thursday they were working constantly to improve services for athletes.
"We have already increased shuttle buses as much as possible to satisfy athletes' needs," Asian Games organising committee spokesman Hiroshi Koshizuka told AFP.
He admitted issues with transport had occurred but said "there had been no significant impact on the Games and no event has been delayed".
"We have set up a system to respond to complaints and we will address them in a sincere manner going forward."
Steven Chen, spokesman for the Chinese Taipei Olympic Committee, the name for the Taiwan team, said previous experience prepared them for the worst.
They booked 100 extra rooms at hotels in case there was a shortage of beds.
"We were informed at the last minute before departure that there weren't enough beds. That was a major blow to every country," he said.
Chen said that the "biggest headache" was with transport, with schedules frequently changing at the last minute.
"When our team had an evening flight, they suddenly informed us that the afternoon bus to the airport was changed to pick us up in the morning, which caused us a lot of trouble," he said.

content:

France attacker Marie-Antoinette Katoto scored a hat-trick against the Swiss champions as fellow forward Melchie Dumornay claimed a double.

"We wanted to start in the best way possible," Dumornay told UEFA.

title: PM Shehbaz stresses GSP  role in Pakistan s economic growth in meeting with EU leaders
description: European chief thanks PM for Pakistan   s initiative to mediate in the conflict between the United States and Iran
content:
European chief thanks PM for Pakistan’s initiative to mediate in the conflict between the United States and Iran
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and European Union leaders discussed the importance of GSP+ for Pakistan’s economic development, employment and trade with the bloc during a meeting on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, the Prime Minister's Office said on Thursday.
The EU’s GSP+ offers developing countries preferential access to European markets in return for commitments on sustainable development and good governance.
Under the scheme, eligible countries are required to implement 27 international conventions covering human rights, labour rights, environmental protection, and good governance. In exchange, the European Union reduces import duties to zero on more than two-thirds of the tariff lines applied to its exports. Pakistan is currently one of eight countries that benefit from this scheme.
According to the PMO, PM Shehbaz met European Council President António Luís Santos da Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, with the leaders reviewing the “full spectrum” of Pakistan-EU relations.
The premier “highlighted the importance of GSP Plus for Pakistan’s economic development, employment generation and trade with the European Union” and reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to continued engagement with the EU under the framework.
Prime Minister held a meeting with President of the European Council, H.E. Mr. António Luís Santos da Costa and the President of the European Commission, H.E. Ms.Ursula Gertrud von der Leyen on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The leaders… pic.twitter.com/UWmiQQ7N0b
He also reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening its “broad-based partnership” with the European Union and to the full implementation of the Pakistan-EU Strategic Engagement Plan.
PM Shehbaz “underscored the importance of sustained leadership-level engagement” to provide greater direction and momentum to relations between Pakistan and the EU.
Von der Leyen also described the meeting as “very good”, saying the EU “valued its partnership with Pakistan”.
“Our Strategic Engagement Plan reflects both the breadth of this partnership and the shared commitment to democracy, the rule of law, human rights and civic space,” she said in a post on X.
Very good meeting with Prime Minister @CMShehbaz at #UNGA . The EU values its partnership with Pakistan. Our Strategic Engagement Plan reflects both the breadth of this partnership and the shared commitment to democracy, the rule of law, human rights and civic space. We work… pic.twitter.com/FWPXFBqjKL
She said the EU and Pakistan “worked together on stability and security” and thanked PM Shehbaz for Pakistan’s initiative to mediate in the conflict between the United States and Iran. “Pakistan is playing an important role in support of de-escalation, dialogue and peaceful resolution of conflicts,” von der Leyen said.
The EU Commission president said the two sides had also discussed “how to take our partnership forward, from trade to addressing illegal migration”.
The leaders exchanged views on regional and global developments and reaffirmed the importance of “dialogue, diplomacy, international law and peaceful resolution of disputes”, according to the PMO.
The prime minister reiterated his invitation to the presidents of the European Council and European Commission to visit Pakistan and expressed his desire to continue working closely with the EU leadership to deepen the “mutually beneficial partnership”.
Pakistan’s push to retain preferential access to the European Union market intensified this year as the bloc prepares to replace the current GSP+ framework from 2027. Under the scheme, Pakistan benefits from reduced or zero tariffs on exports in return for implementing 27 international conventions covering areas including human rights, labour rights, environmental protection and good governance.
The European Commission’s latest assessment , released in July, acknowledged legislative progress by Pakistan but also raised concerns over compliance with GSP+ obligations, including human rights, governance, freedom of expression, labour rights and environmental protection. Pakistan subsequently expressed “disappointment”, with Foreign Office spokesperson Tahir Andrabi saying the report did not present a “sufficiently balanced picture” of the country’s performance.
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to implementing the international conventions underpinning GSP+, stressing the importance Islamabad attached to its economic partnership with the EU. The European Commission’s assessment had said Pakistan faced compliance issues and would need to address shortcomings to qualify under the revised framework.
The stakes are significant for Pakistan’s exporters. The EU’s GSP report showed that Pakistan recorded about €7.1 billion in exports to the bloc in 2024 under preferential tariffs, with a utilisation rate of more than 95 per cent. Another Express Tribune report put the figure at €7.5 billion, with Pakistan emerging as the largest beneficiary among GSP+ countries.
In September, EU Ambassador to Pakistan Raimundas Karoblis said Islamabad would have to demonstrate “clear progress” in legislating and implementing the international laws and conventions underpinning the scheme if it wanted to continue benefiting from GSP+ beyond 2027. He also urged exporters to ensure compliance and maintain engagement with the government over concerns raised by the European Commission on human rights, labour rights, governance and environmental protection.
The issue remained prominent in high-level diplomatic contacts this month. Dar stressed the importance of GSP+ during his meeting with EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly on September 21, while the two sides discussed Pakistan-EU relations and regional developments.
The EU and Pakistan also continued broader economic engagement. On September 22, the two sides signed three grant agreements worth €65 million covering investment facilitation, climate and energy resilience in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, and support for the rule of law and business environment.

title: Hamilton gives thumbs up to Gulf GPs despite Iran conflict
description: The seven time world champion says he has no concerns about returning to Qatar and Abu Dhabi
content:
The seven-time world champion says he has no concerns about returning to Qatar and Abu Dhabi
Lewis Hamilton on Wednesday said he hopes that this year’s Formula One world championship will conclude with its two races as scheduled in the Middle East despite the continuing conflict.
The Bahrain and Saudi Arabia grands prix were scrapped earlier this season due to the start of Israel and the United States' war with Iran.
The seven-time world champion said he believed "things seem to be okay out there" and added that he trusted the judgement of Formula One chief executive Stefano Domenicali in making the right decisions.
Speaking in Baku ahead of this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, a country that borders Iran, Hamilton said he had always enjoyed going to the races in Qatar, scheduled for November 29, and Abu Dhabi, on December 6.
"Personally, I want to go. I love going to the Middle East,” said the Ferrari driver.
"From what I have read, things seem ok out there, but I don’t have all the information and I don’t know what the risk levels are.
"I trust Stefano to make the right decision for the sport. And I do hope we go there."
A back-up plan to stage a season-ending race in Imola in Italy has been put in place.
Most members of the F1 circus, a 2,000 strong group of teams, media and officials, have expressed a wish to avoid travelling to the final races. A decision is expected by mid-October.
Hamilton also spoke out against Formula One’s decision to reduce the maximum distance of a grand prix from 305 kilometres to 290 next season.
The decision was made in relation to the planned evolution of the hybrid power unit from a 50-50 split between engine and battery now to 58-42 next year and 60-40 in 2028 at the request of drivers.
"I don’t really know anything about it or any of the reasons behind it," he said.
"But I think the races should be longer because they are physically easier than ever before.
"So, I don’t think shortening makes much sense.
"This weekend, we have tyre compounds that can pretty much all do the race distance here.
"And we have a lot of races where it's only a one-stop. It's not particularly challenging.
"For me, there's been many races where I wish we had more laps so it's the opposite that I would be asking for – which is longer races, to be honest.
The 41-year-old veteran of 394 grands prix said he felt the sport should make greater demands of the drivers, not fewer.
"This is supposed to be a sport that’s the most physically and mentally demanding," he said.
"But there are some that are just so hot that ultimately you are on the edge. Singapore? Malaysia? That’s where you want to see athletes, right? Just on the edge."
Compatriots George Russell of Mercedes and world champion Lando Norris of McLaren were less concerned.
Russell suggested trimming a few laps would have little real impact while Norris said it was a "good compromise".
"We need to make our sport better and rely more on driving, rather than who can look after their battery the best,” he added.

title: 8 US sailors from carrier strike group attempted suicide during operations against Iran  CNN
description: Eight attempted suicides is incredibly high     says anonymous US military official to CNN
content:
‘Eight attempted suicides is incredibly high,’ says anonymous US military official to CNN
Eight US Navy personnel aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group attempted suicide during the ships’ deployment against Iran , according to a letter revealed on Wednesday from the service’s acting secretary.
In the letter obtained by CNN , Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao revealed the number, which had not been previously reported, and it covers crew members from several ships that travel together, including the carrier, in written responses to questions posed by Senator Kirsten Gillibrand about the morale and mental health of the USS Abraham Lincoln’s crew. Cao wrote that no service members had killed themselves during the deployment.
Eight US sailors in USS Abraham Lincoln strike group attempted suicide, Navy says https://t.co/IWGvd711mx
“Since the beginning of Lincoln’s deployment, there have been a total of eight suicide attempts across the strike group,” Cao wrote to Gillibrand, a Democrat and senior member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, in a letter dated Tuesday.
Read: Iranian FM spokesperson rebukes Canadian PM for calling ‘annihilation’ threat ‘language of war’
“This number includes the Lincoln crew and sailors from the carrier air wing, strike group and destroyer squadron staff, escorting destroyers and all embarked aviation squadrons.”
Between 6,000 and 7,000 US Navy sailors were deployed as part of the Lincoln strike group across roughly six ships as the carrier remained out of port for over six months while conducting a high rate of combat operations against Iran.
“Eight attempted suicides is incredibly high,” one US military official told CNN , noting recent carrier strike group deployments have had one or two per year. “The strain of combat ops is much higher than normal deployments. No port calls, constant alerts, etc.”
Following a deployment of 286 days at sea, the USS Abraham Lincoln docked at Thailand’s Laem Chabang Port on September 2.

title: Ronaldo focussing on  present  ahead of Wales test
description: He targets a milestone 1 000th career goal with Portugal while keeping his international retirement plans open
content:
He targets a milestone 1,000th career goal with Portugal while keeping his international retirement plans open
Cristiano Ronaldo said he is focused on "the present", refusing to set a date for his international retirement when he appeared before the press on Wednesday, on the eve of the Nations League match against Wales.
The 41-year-old announced earlier in the summer that this season would "probably" be the last of his career, prompting a volley of questions from reporters.
"I’m no longer at an age where I think about the future," said Ronaldo. "For me, the present is what matters most."
The former Manchester United and Real Madrid star said he was ready to step down from the national team as soon as the staff wanted it and hinted that he would announce his departure before playing his final match.
Ronaldo also confirmed his ambition to reach 1,000 career goals, having already scored 979 in all competitions.
"I've already said that I want to get there and I will get there, but it's not an obsession," he insisted on Wednesday, adding that he would like to hit that milestone in a Portugal shirt.
"That would be the cherry on the cake," he said. "Scoring a thousandth goal with the national team would crown a beautiful story."
The five-time Ballon d’Or winner described the arrival of new coach Jorge Jesus as "the beginning of a new era"
He said that the 72-year-old coach, with whom he worked last year at the Saudi club Al-Nassr, was "the perfect choice" to replace Spaniard Roberto Martinez.
Winners of the Nations League in 2019 and 2025, Portugal will begin the new edition of the competition by hosting Wales on Thursday in Lisbon before travelling to Oslo to face Norway.
They stay in Scandinavia to take on Denmark on October 1 before returning home for the return fixture against the Norwegians three days later.
Jorge Jesus confirmed that Ronaldo, still the national team captain, will be playing against the Welsh.
"He’s playing tomorrow and I hope he scores one or two goals right away, then I’ll take him off," the coach said.
