title: Xi starts high stakes US visit with call to be    partners  not rivals
description: Xi   s first trip to the US in nearly three years was not expected to deliver breakthroughs
content:
Trade truce, Taiwan, AI and wider geopolitical tensions dominate talks between world’s two biggest economies
Chinese President Xi Jinping is in Washington for a state visit at the invitation of US President Donald Trump, opening a high-stakes round of diplomacy between the leaders of the world’s two largest economies as the Chinese leader said their two countries should be “partners, not rivals” because the interests of their two peoples “are deeply intertwined.”
Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday afternoon for a state visit to the United States at the invitation of U.S. President Donald Trump https://t.co/A8ZhoSuOIo pic.twitter.com/hijqUp1zAF
Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, were greeted by Trump and first lady Melania Trump at Joint Base Andrews in an unusually elaborate planeside welcome. American children presented flowers to the Chinese couple while honour guards lined the red carpet. The ceremony featured a 21-gun salute, the national anthems of both countries and a military flyover.
US children present flowers to Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan at Joint Base Andrews in the United States, Sept. 23, 2026. PHOTO: XINHUA
Trump’s decision to greet Xi personally at the airport marked the first time in 11 years that a US president had welcomed a foreign leader at Joint Base Andrews, according to C-SPAN. Xi’s visit is his first to Washington in more than a decade and comes just months after Trump travelled to China in May for talks with the Chinese president.
The exchange of visits underscores the importance both sides attach to maintaining high-level communication despite persistent strategic rivalry.
In a written statement issued after his arrival, Xi called on China and the United States to be “partners, not rivals”, saying the interests of the two peoples were deeply intertwined. “China and the United States should be partners, not rivals,” Xi said, adding that the rejuvenation of China and Trump’s goal of “making America great again” could proceed alongside each other. He said the two countries could help each other succeed while contributing to global well-being.
Read: China says opposes 'illegal unilateral sanctions' as US pressures Iran with secondary sanctions
Xi also referred to the understanding reached during Trump’s May visit to China to build a “constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability”. He said the agreement had provided strategic guidance for the future development of bilateral relations.
The Chinese president said Washington and Beijing should work in the same direction and pursue a relationship in which cooperation remained the mainstay, competition was moderate and differences were manageable.
Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump standing for a photo on the red carpet. PHOTO: XINHUA
He said the two countries needed to find the “right way to get along in the new era”, arguing that although the world was changing, the historical logic of peaceful coexistence between China and the United States remained unchanged.
Xi said he looked forward to detailed discussions with Trump on bilateral relations and the international situation, as well as to expanding exchanges and cooperation in different fields. He also said he hoped to engage with people from different sections of American society to strengthen ties between the two peoples.
A gun salute is fired to welcome Chinese President Xi Jinping upon his arrival at Joint Base Andrews for a state visit to the United States at the invitation of US President Donald Trump, September 23, 2026. PHOTO: XINHUA
The summit comes against a backdrop of intense economic competition and a fragile trade truce between Washington and Beijing.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday, following talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, that an agreement suspending a trade war had been extended until January 10. The confrontation had previously seen mutual tariffs rise above 100%, according to the material supplied for the report.
The extension could provide temporary relief to businesses while giving negotiators additional time to address unresolved trade disputes.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer has said Washington and Beijing are expected to make announcements concerning agriculture and non-tariff barriers. China is also reportedly making progress on a commitment to purchase 200 Boeing aircraft, although no additional orders were indicated as imminent.
People familiar with the plans said the discussions could also produce agreements on reducing some tariffs, combating drug trafficking and expanding military-to-military communication. Trump is also expected to raise the issue of Americans and others detained in China.
Artificial intelligence is another potential area of discussion. Officials from both countries have explored mechanisms to prevent AI-related incidents from escalating into wider conflicts.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has referred to the possibility of a mechanism comparable to the Cold War-era hotline, intended to avert dangerous incidents involving increasingly powerful technologies.
Read more: China's Xi to visit the US this week, with bilateral ties, trade, world peace on agenda
The guest list for Thursday’s state dinner reflects the importance of technology and business ties. It includes senior executives from Apple, Amazon, Alphabet, OpenAI, Tesla and Nvidia.
Beyond trade and technology, Taiwan remains one of the most sensitive issues confronting the two governments.
Sources briefed on the discussions told Reuters that Xi was expected to press Trump to halt US arms sales to Taiwan, potentially during a planned visit by the two leaders to the US National Archives on Friday.
Trump had said after the May summit that he was holding an arms package worth about $14 billion in abeyance, describing it as a negotiating tool.
The leaders are also expected to discuss the war with Iran, which has disrupted energy supplies and trade. The wider geopolitical environment adds pressure to the summit.
For Trump, the Washington meeting comes at the end of a week of diplomacy that began with his two-day stay in New York for the UN General Assembly. The supplied material says the nearly seven-month war with Iran has pushed up energy prices in the United States, while Republicans face difficult congressional elections in November.
Analysts expect the immediate results to centre on extending the trade truce and possibly establishing cooperation on AI-related risks. Former US Deputy Secretary of State Kurt Campbell characterised the summit as an opportunity for the two leaders to project strength as much as a forum for substantive negotiations.
The two leaders could have another opportunity to meet later this year, potentially on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China in November or the G20 meetings in the United States in December.
The summit comes at a pivotal moment in China-US relations and could provide an opportunity to place bilateral ties on a more stable footing. Xi’s visit, coming only months after Trump’s trip to China, marks a rare exchange of visits between the two leaders within a short period and could open a new chapter in relations, although a single meeting is unlikely to resolve the countries’ longstanding disputes.
Chinese President Xi Jinping is welcomed upon his arrival in the United States on September 23, 2026. PHOTO: XINHUA
Economic and trade ties remain a major pillar of the relationship despite Washington’s protectionist policies. More than 7,000 Chinese enterprises operate in the United States, while US companies have established more than 84,000 enterprises in China. Bilateral trade and investment support millions of jobs in the United States.
Also read: Iran may expand war to Indian Ocean if US attacks again: supreme leader's adviser
A 2026 survey by the US-China Business Council found that 95% of respondents described their China operations as somewhat to very important to maintaining global competitiveness. The figures underscore the depth of commercial links between the two economies and the continuing interests of businesses in maintaining access to each other’s markets.
Economic differences, meanwhile, could be addressed through continued consultations based on equality, mutual respect and mutual benefit. Turning trade and economic ties into instruments of political or security competition risks fracturing supply chains, distorting markets and raising costs for businesses and consumers.
Greater stability does not necessarily mean eliminating competition. The challenge for both sides is to manage competition through established rules while preventing disputes from escalating into confrontation.
Taiwan remains a central concern in the bilateral relationship. Beijing regards the Taiwan question as a core interest, while Washington maintains its own longstanding policy toward Taipei. How the two governments manage their differences over the island will remain a key test for the broader relationship.
People-to-people exchanges could provide another avenue for stabilising ties. Xi proposed in 2023 that 50,000 young Americans be invited to China over five years for exchanges and study, a target that was reached ahead of schedule this year.
Global stakes extend beyond Washington and Beijing
Beyond their immediate bilateral interests, the two countries’ ability to maintain a stable relationship carries wider implications. As the world’s two largest economies, their cooperation or confrontation can affect global trade, supply chains, investment, technology and international efforts to address common challenges.
The Washington summit therefore offers both leaders an opportunity to keep dialogue open, manage differences and explore areas of practical cooperation, even as major disagreements over trade, Taiwan, technology and strategic competition remain unresolved.

title: FM Dar  Araghchi stress importance of dialogue  diplomacy for regional stability on UNGA sidelines
description: The two sides also agreed to remain in close contact
content:
The two sides also agreed to remain in close contact
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister (FM) Ishaq Dar and his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi discussed the importance of dialogue, diplomacy and sustained engagement to promote regional peace and stability during a meeting in New York, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Thursday.
The ministry said that the two ministers met on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, where they also discussed bilateral relations and exchanged views on regional and international developments.
“FM underscored the importance of dialogue, diplomacy and sustained engagement in promoting regional peace and stability,” the FO said. The two sides also agreed to “remain in close contact”, it added.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 met with Foreign Minister of Iran, H.E. Seyed Abbas Araghchi @Araghchi , on the sidelines of the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly in New York. The two counterparts discussed bilateral relations… pic.twitter.com/6IuMoY1PJJ
Dar holds meeting with South Korean counterpart
Later, FM Dar met South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun, and the two reviewed bilateral relations and discussed ways to strengthen cooperation, particularly in trade, investment and economic ties, according to a post by the FO.
Dar emphasised the importance of greater business-to-business engagement to unlock new opportunities.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 met with Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea Cho Hyun on the sidelines of the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly in New York. The two sides reviewed bilateral relations and… pic.twitter.com/0JEY8HgOe2
The Korean foreign minister also appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting dialogue and diplomacy to address regional issues.
“The two Foreign Ministers also underscored the importance of the multilateral system and reaffirmed their commitment to working together at the UN and other multilateral fora on issues of mutual interest,” the Foreign Office said.
FM Dar and Araghchi last met in Bishkek on September 1, on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit, where they discussed bilateral relations and regional developments and reaffirmed the importance of continued engagement. Dar stressed that “dialogue and diplomacy remain essential” to regional peace and stability and said implementation of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding between the US and Iran was the “only way forward”.
Earlier this month, FM Dar and Araghchi also spoke by telephone, agreeing to maintain close contact and meet in New York. During the 19 September call, Dar stressed the need for uninterrupted energy supplies and the safe passage of ships, while saying that “dialogue and diplomacy remain the only viable means” of ensuring peace and stability in the region.
Pakistan had also been involved in efforts to facilitate dialogue between Tehran and Washington. In June, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi travelled to Tehran and met Araghchi as Pakistan sought to support the diplomatic track following the US-Iran memorandum.
Pakistan had hosted the Islamabad Talks in April , with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif affirming Islamabad’s role as a mediator between the US and Iran. The Iranian delegation was led by parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and included Araghchi, while Dar, Naqvi and CDF Asim Munir represented Pakistan.
Following the signing of the Islamabad MoU in June, Pakistan continued to facilitate US-Iran engagement. Four-party talks involving the US and Iran, with Pakistan and Qatar as mediators, were subsequently held in Switzerland to discuss implementation of the agreement.
More recently, Iran said it had exchanged messages with the US through Qatari mediation on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, with Tehran conveying conditions for reviving diplomacy. The development came after Trump said US officials had held talks with Iranian representatives in New York.

Tay thanked Hill on Instagram , describing her as someone with “the biggest heart” and saying she would be “the best auntie ever”.

The Border Military Police (BMP) claimed to have foiled an attempt to smuggle a large quantity of drugs from Balochistan into Punjab and arrested two alleged inter-provincial drug smugglers in the Boawata border area.
The operation was carried out on the directives of Dera Ghazi Khan Deputy Commissioner and Senior Commandant BMP Muhammad Usman Khalid, amid stepped-up surveillance at provincial border check posts to curb drug smuggling from Balochistan into Punjab.
According to BMP officials, personnel intercepted a tractor-trolley in the Boawata area and recovered more than 1.5 maunds of hashish and 7kg of ice (crystal methamphetamine) allegedly being transported into Punjab.
The two suspects were arrested and a case was registered against them at Boawata police station. Further investigation is under way.
The operation was conducted under the supervision of BMP Commandant Hamza Anjum. Risaldar Tuman Leghari Sardar Abdullah Khan Leghari, along with Station House Officer Ashfaq Ahmed Leghari, supervised the operation.
BMP officials said the suspects were being interrogated to trace the wider drug-supply network and identify other alleged facilitators involved in the smuggling operation.

title: 19 5k subsidised tractors in a year promised
description: 19 5k subsidised tractors in a year promised
content:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Wednesday launched the fourth phase of the Green Tractor Scheme through digital balloting and opened the application portal for the next phase, announcing plans to provide 19,500 tractors to farmers during the current fiscal year.
The chief minister pressed a button to conduct the balloting, with the first tractor of the phase going to Masood Khan of Attock.
According to a briefing, 10,000 tractors of 50 to 65 horsepower will be provided under phase IV, with the Punjab government offering a subsidy of Rs750,000 each.
Under phase V, 9,500 high-powered tractors ranging from 75 to 125 horsepower will be offered with a subsidy of Rs1 million each.
The provincial government has allocated Rs17.6 billion for the Green Tractor Scheme, while 24,000 tractors have already been provided to farmers under the programme with a subsidy of Rs1 million per tractor.
The chief minister inspected tractors being offered under the scheme, including locally manufactured 90-horsepower and locally assembled 100-horsepower models.
Officials said only 10,000 tractors had been provided to farmers over the previous 20 years, while 35,000 had been distributed in the past two-and-a-half years.
Similarly, Rs3 billion had been spent on agricultural mechanisation over two decades compared with Rs20 billion during the rule of the current government.
Punjab has also witnessed, for the first time, local manufacturing of 90-horsepower and assembly of 100-horsepower tractors.
At least 213,637 farmers applied for the programme, of whom 128,757 were declared eligible for the balloting after verification through the Punjab Land Records Authority and National Database and Registration Authority.

title: Chenab belt struggles to bridge mango gap
description: Chenab belt struggles to bridge mango gap
content:
Replantation under way in flood-ravaged orchards
Along the riverine belt stretching nearly 380 kilometres from Chiniot to Head Panjnad, where rows of mango trees once stood as a sign of the region's agricultural wealth, the devastating floods of last year left behind a landscape of destruction and an uncertain future.
The floodwaters not only swept away large numbers of mango trees but also erased years of orchard growth, leaving growers with a challenge that cannot be overcome in a single season.
From saplings to fruit-bearing trees, orchards across the belt suffered extensive damage, creating a long-term gap in the mango-producing capacity that could take several years to bridge.
The loss is measured not only in this season's fruit but in the future harvests that trees would have continued to provide for years.
A mango grower, Shahid Hameed Bhutta, said replacing the destroyed orchards and restoring their productive capacity would be a long-term process.
He said a large number of mango trees had been lost, leaving a huge gap in the region's productive tree population.
New plantations require at least eight years to reach productive age, he said.
The reduced number of trees has contributed to lower mango output, affecting marketing and export.
Shahid Bhutta said the restoration of the mango belt would require extensive replanting over the coming years. However, newly planted trees would not be able to immediately replace the production lost from mature orchards.
He explained that mango trees pass through different stages of growth before reaching commercial production, while the destruction of mature orchards creates a production deficit that cannot be addressed within a season.
Another local grower, Laique Sheikhana, said the floods had caused a setback to the belt's production capacity for years to come.
He said the growers now faced a stretch of lean seasons even as they invested in replanting, with income from their orchards reduced when they needed money to buy new plants.
He said the challenge was rebuilding the productive capacity of the orchards that had been lost.
A grower from Nawabpur, Malik Arif Kalrou, has begun replanting part of his orchard. He said many growers were competing for a limited supply of healthy saplings as the planting season had begun.
He said the growers believed that sustained plantation and orchard management would be essential to gradually bridge the production deficit created by the floods, while the impact of the disaster would remain visible in the mango sector for several years.

title: Boy held for seeking AI help to poison father
description: Boy held for seeking AI help to poison father
content:
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) has arrested a 17-year-old student from Bahawalpur for allegedly attempting to poison his father after seeking guidance from an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot, officials said.
The action was taken after the agency received information about the teenager's alleged online activity. A team traced him and arrested him in Bahawalpur.

title: Lahore enjoying dengue ebb
description: Lahore enjoying dengue ebb
content:
Public cooperation to prevent resurgence urged
The metropolis has recorded a sharp decline in dengue cases and deaths in recent years, according to data compiled by the Metropolitan Corporation of Lahore.
The data shows that Lahore had witnessed a major outbreak in 2021, when 20,042 dengue cases and 118 deaths were reported. Most cases were recorded in the areas of Cantonment, DHA, open spaces and rural localities.
The number of cases fell to 8,252 in 2022, while deaths dropped to 24. In 2023, 7,031 cases and six deaths were reported. The situation improved further in 2024, with only 475 cases recorded and no deaths. Last year, 781 dengue cases and three deaths were recorded.
Available data for the ongoing year shows 23 cases so far, with no death reported.
Officials attributed the decline to coordinated action against mosquito breeding sites. Lahore DC Mohammed Ali Ejaz said all necessary measures, including efforts to prevent larval breeding, were continuing.
He stressed the importance of public cooperation, saying timely identification and cleaning of potential breeding sites could help reduce the risk of a resurgence. Awareness campaigns were being conducted to encourage citizens to take preventive measures, he added.
A former deputy commissioner, Syed Musa Raza, said the administration had focused on practical measures.
He said surveillance and cleanliness at cemeteries, lakes, ponds, residential and commercial areas and other potential mosquito-breeding sites had been strengthened.
According to Raza, authorities had also directed the hospitals to report dengue patients and laboratory results. Whenever dengue larvae or a patient was identified, preventive measures were initiated in the affected area, including spraying around the infected household and neighbouring homes.
He said more than 200 open ponds and stagnant-water sites across the city had been cleared, while the cleaning of drains was also carried out in coordination with the Water and Sanitation Agency.
Former Mayo Hospital medical superintendent Dr Ehteshamul Haq said dengue could only be effectively controlled by ensuring that both larvae and patients were identified and reported rather than concealed.

title: Police chief faces LHC grilling over contempt
description: Police chief faces LHC grilling over contempt
content:
CJ summons IGP over pleas alleging non-compliance
The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Wednesday summoned Punjab Inspector General of Police Rao Abdul Kareem in person along with the relevant record on Thursday in two contempt proceedings involving alleged non-compliance with judicial orders by officials.
Chief Justice Aalia Neelum passed the orders while hearing petitions concerning illegal registration of a case and harassment of citizens by police, with the court expressing strong displeasure over the handling of the matters.
Hearing a contempt petition filed by a citizen, Mian Muhammad Jameel, against Chung police officials and others, the court summoned the IGP after a superintendent of police who appeared on behalf of the department failed to read out a First Information Report (FIR) when directed by the chief justice.
"It's not possible to read the FIR; it is not clear what has been written. SP sahib, please read the FIR," the chief justice stated.
Despite the direction, the officer could not read the FIR, prompting the court to express strong displeasure over the manner in which police records were prepared.
"The entire Punjab has been ruined; this is the situation in Punjab," Justice Neelum remarked, observing that FIRs were not even written in a readable manner.
According to the petitioner, a sessions court had in 2021 ordered registration of a case against him. He had challenged the decision before the LHC, where a single bench had suspended the order for registration of the case.
The petitioner contended that despite the high court order, the police had proceeded to register a case against him illegally, leading him to file the contempt petition.
In another contempt case filed by citizen Momin Khan against Lahore Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Bilal Siddique Kamyana, the court rejected an inquiry report submitted by the police and summoned the IGP along with the relevant record.
The petitioner contended that the court had earlier forwarded his application to the CCPO for redressal against harassment and intimidation by police officials.
He alleged that despite the court's directions, Ichhra police had continued to harass him and conduct illegal raids at his home.
The petitioner contended that the court order was not being complied with and requested the LHC to initiate contempt proceedings against the Lahore CCPO.
The court rejected a police inquiry report and directed the Punjab Police IG to appear in person with the relevant record in the next hearing.
The LHC also set aside the death sentence handed down to one Muhammad Hassan in a murder and attempted murder case and acquitted him, observing that the prosecution had failed to prove the charges beyond reasonable doubt. A bench ordered his immediate release from jail.
The bench comprising Chief Justice Aalia Neelum and Justice Abher Gul Khan issued a detailed 22-page judgment on Hassan's appeal, which also set out principles regarding the assessment of evidence in criminal cases.
The case had been registered in 2021 at Mandi Ahmadabad police station in Depalpur on charges of murder and attempted murder. The trial court had sentenced the accused to death and 10-year imprisonment. The death sentence was subsequently referred to the LHC for confirmation through a murder reference.
Justice Abher Gul, who authored the judgment, observed that delay in registration of the FIR and the course adopted in this regard raised doubts about consultation and deliberation after the incident.

title: Kirthar faces ecological threats
description: Kirthar faces ecological threats
content:
Kirthar National Park is more than a rugged expanse of mountains and wildlife; it is also a repository of ancient history and a fragile ecosystem increasingly under pressure from human activity, experts said at a conference on Wednesday.
The warning came at the third annual conference held at the Arts Council of Pakistan in memory of late journalist, historian and researcher Gul Hassan Kalmati. Titled "Kirthar National Park: A Human-Made Crisis," the conference brought together wildlife experts, archaeologists, researchers and environmentalists to examine the threats facing Sindh's only national park.
Speakers traced Kirthar's story from its biodiversity and natural resources to its archaeological and cultural wealth, while highlighting the legal, environmental and economic challenges that threaten the park's future.
Wildlife researcher and environmentalist Salman Baloch highlighted the ecological and biological diversity of Kirthar, Sindh's only national park, and discussed the environmental threats confronting the protected area. He also pointed out gaps in the existing legal framework for its protection.
Archaeologist and archaeozoologist Syed Ali Shah Lakiari shed light on the historical sites and ancient heritage of Kirthar, saying the park was not merely a habitat for mountains and wildlife but also contained a rich historical and cultural legacy.
Saeed Chandio discussed economic activity and data related to Kirthar and the surrounding region, highlighting the close links between natural resources, local communities and economic activity.
Wildlife photographer Zohaib Ahmed stressed the importance of education and public awareness for the sustainable future of Kirthar. He called for wildlife education to be made part of the formal education system so that younger generations could develop a stronger connection with nature and biodiversity.
Chief Conservator of the Sindh Wildlife Department Javed Mehr presented findings and data from a detailed survey of the Kirthar mountain range and briefed participants on the area's current condition.
The conference brought together researchers, academics, environmentalists and other experts, including Dr Kaleemullah Lashari, Dr Asma Ibrahim, Dr Rukhman Gul Palari, Kamal Palari and Shahid Moso.
The event also highlighted the legacy of Gul Hassan Kalmati, who belonged to Karachi's historic Kalmat tribe and hailed from Gadap. A journalist, researcher, historian and anthropologist, Kalmati authored several books on the history, culture and heritage of Karachi, Sindh and the wider region. He died in 2023 due to complications from dengue.

title: K Electric faces assembly heat
description: K Electric faces assembly heat
content:
House panel warns of privilege proceedings, possible arrest over load-shedding
K-Electric's top brass stayed away from the Sindh Assembly on Wednesday, but the company's absence did little to cool lawmakers' anger over Karachi's persistent power cuts. Instead, the no-show pushed a special house committee closer to punitive action, with possible privilege proceedings and even arrest being discussed.
The committee had summoned the CEOs of K-Electric, HESCO and SEPCO to explain the continuing load-shedding, but none of the three showed up. K-Electric sent its head of distribution and other officials instead - a move that failed to satisfy lawmakers and eventually saw the company's representatives shown the door.
Chaired by PPP MPA Fayyaz Butt, the committee warned that the power utilities could face the maximum action allowed under the law if the crisis remained unresolved. Butt also took aim at Nepra, questioning why the regulator had failed to enforce its orders and warning that he would approach the federal government over what he described as the regulator's inability to rein in the distribution companies.
Speaking after the meeting, Butt said the committee would initiate proceedings through the Privileges Committee against K-Electric. "K-Electric did not provide answers. If the law provides for arrest, they will be arrested," he said. He said a final meeting with the CEOs would be held and warned that failure to resolve the issue could lead to the imposition of the maximum penalties permissible under the law.
The meeting also saw lawmakers question the authority and effectiveness of the Nepra in regulating power distribution companies. Butt lashed out at Nepra officials, asking why the regulator did not cancel licences if it was unable to enforce its orders. "If Nepra cannot get its orders implemented, why does it not cancel licences?" he asked, adding that he would write to the federal government over what he described as the regulator's admission that it lacked powers.
PPP lawmaker Saleem Baloch said the meeting minutes should record that Nepra was unable to rein in K-Electric, HESCO and SEPCO. He said the closure of feeders and PMTs would not be tolerated and added that consumers who paid their bills should not be subjected to power cuts.
"According to Nepra, load-shedding is illegal," he added.
Lawmakers also raised complaints about billing and alleged irregularities. PPP MPA Yousuf Baloch claimed that a meter had been registered in his name six years before he was born. "I'm a sitting MPA. If a fake bill can be generated in my name, imagine what happens to the public," he said.
Meanwhile, K-Electric has warned of a significant financial setback after the Nepra Appellate Tribunal verbally rejected the company's appeals against regulatory decisions issued on October 20, 2025, saying the ruling could have a substantial adverse impact on its multi-year tariff for the 2024-30 control period. According to a spokesperson, the verbal order was conveyed on Wednesday in compliance with directions issued by the Nepra Appellate Tribunal in connection with the company's appeals against Nepra's decisions. However, the tribunal has yet to issue its detailed written order.

The Judicial Commission probing the Mir Raza Ali case has ordered a comprehensive cyber investigation into a social media campaign against Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed, while raising questions over the failure to provide the complete record of a private conversation involving her and Dr Osama.
Justice Umar Sial, presiding judge of the commission, issued the written order of Wednesday's proceedings, directing the Karachi director of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) to nominate a senior officer to investigate the online harassment campaign against the police surgeon.
The NCCIA has also been directed to examine the messages exchanged between Dr Summaiya and Dr Osama, conduct a forensic examination of allegedly defamatory material available online and identify those responsible for disseminating it.
According to the order, Dr Summaiya had complained to the commission that Dr Osama leaked edited portions of a private conversation in an attempt to damage her reputation. She said the campaign had caused her severe mental distress and could set a dangerous precedent by discouraging senior professionals from helping juniors correct mistakes.
Dr Osama has appeared before the commission three times but has not submitted the complete recording of the conversation, the order stated. Some portions were allegedly provided to specific media outlets and digital platforms. The commission observed that presenting a private conversation out of context could divert attention from the actual issue. Dr Summaiya said she was willing to submit the complete recording before the commission if permitted, arguing that its review would eliminate the possibility of misunderstanding or misinterpretation.
The commission also addressed the dispute over the post-mortem reports, saying that Dr Osama had endorsed the interim report while refusing to accept the final report. The order said that when an initial post-mortem is conducted by a single doctor and a subsequent examination is carried out by a multi-member medical board, the earlier report assumes secondary status. It further observed that Dr Osama's initial conclusions regarding the bullet's entry and exit wounds amounted to disregarding scientific evidence.
The commission described Dr Summaiya as an experienced and distinguished professional and said harassment of her was unacceptable. It termed her an asset to the government and said she was being subjected to a campaign to discredit her instead of having her services recognised.
The order also stated that the commission had, in an earlier order, raised questions about Dr Osama's motives and the apparent targeting of institutions. It said his efforts appeared aimed at undermining and making the commission controversial.

title: JI keeps Islamabad march option open
description: JI keeps Islamabad march option open
content:
Hafiz Naeemur Rehman says march postponed temporarily at PM's request
Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) will not abandon its right to march on Islamabad until the petroleum levy is abolished, and will expand its protest campaign if the government fails to provide relief to the masses, JI Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman said on Wednesday.
Addressing a press conference in the federal capital, Rehman said the long march had been postponed for a few days at Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's request. He said he would meet the prime minister after returning to Pakistan and that the party's next course of action would depend on the outcome of the meeting.
"The better option is to abolish the petroleum levy. Otherwise, people will come out to seek the removal of the government," the JI chief maintained.
The JI has been staging sit-ins and protests against the petroleum levy since August. The party initially launched road blockades at 510 locations before holding sit-ins at 42 locations across the country on August 16. The campaign later developed into a train march towards Islamabad before the long march was postponed following a telephone conversation between Rehman and the prime minister.
Rehman said the JI would continue its protests during the pause and hold public meetings, including in Lahore and other cities. He said the party had held several rounds of negotiations with the government and presented workable proposals, but had not received a convincing response.
He said reducing the interest rate by three percentage points could save the national exchequer more than Rs1.5 trillion and called for cuts in government privileges and expenditure. The JI leader also demanded taxes on large landowners, an end to capacity payments to independent power producers (IPPs) and action against corruption in the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR).
The JI emir rejected the government's argument that the petroleum levy was necessary to meet International Monetary Fund (IMF) requirements. He said the IMF agreement did not specifically require Pakistan to meet revenue targets through the levy, arguing that the government should instead reduce expenditure and broaden the tax base.
On September 3, the government and JI agreed to constitute expert committees to examine measures for reducing the petroleum levy and providing relief to consumers.
Rehman said consumers were paying about Rs140 per litre in taxes on petrol and described the burden as unacceptable. He also criticised the government for borrowing heavily from private banks and paying billions of rupees in interest, linking the issue to what he described as an unfair economic system.

Police sources said the arrested suspect, Waheed, allegedly kept Anosh at his house after his abduction. Police used technical and human intelligence to trace the suspect and arrested him after receiving information about his whereabouts.

content:
Capital police arrange 110k tear-gas shells; rangers deployment sought
Preparations to deal with the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) Sept 27 long march have entered the final phase in Rawalpindi Division, with more than 43,000 personnel to be deployed in Attock, Rawalpindi, Murree, Jhelum and Chakwal to prevent protesters from entering the twin cities.

title: PHC seeks update in minister s abduction
description: PHC seeks update in minister s abduction
content:
Says FIR limits court's role to investigation directions
Once an FIR is registered in a criminal incident, the court's jurisdiction becomes limited and it can only issue directions concerning the investigation, Peshawar High Court (PHC) Justice Ijaz Anwar observed on Wednesday while hearing a writ petition related to the alleged abduction of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Provincial Minister Fazal Shakoor.
A two-member bench comprising Justice Ijaz Anwar and Justice Kamran Hayat Mian Khel heard the case. The petition was filed by the minister's brother, Anwar Ali.
Counsel for the petitioner, Advocate Bashir Wazir, informed the court that on Monday the provincial minister was abducted in broad daylight from a motorway interchange. He pointed out that police, excise and other departmental checkpoints stood on the opposite side of the road and personnel present there merely watched the incident unfold.
The lawyer further stated that the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, Inspector General of Police, had been summoned by the Speaker during the provincial assembly session but remained absent. Justice Ijaz Anwar remarked that this reflected a weakness of the provincial government.
Advocate Bashir Wazir told the bench that Fazal Shakoor has been a member of the provincial assembly since 2013. Armed men in plain clothes opened fire on the tyres of the minister's vehicle. Reacting to the account, Justice Ijaz Anwar asked: "Who are these people? What was the police doing?"
The judge then inquired from Additional Advocate General Bilal Khalil whether an FIR had been registered. Upon receiving an affirmative reply, Justice Anwar observed that once the FIR stood registered, the court's scope was restricted. "Tell us if the abductee is somewhere; we can send someone," he said.
Counsel for the petitioner argued that the manner of the firing was unprecedented, stating it had not been witnessed even in Palestine. He questioned how the police could protect ordinary citizens if they failed to safeguard a provincial minister. He urged the court to summon senior police officers and demand an account of the investigation conducted in the two days since the incident, warning that a wave of abductions had begun in the province.
Additional Advocate General Bilal Khalil submitted that in view of the recurring incidents the government desired a judicial inquiry. Justice Ijaz Anwar replied that the court would examine the matter if the provincial government formally requested it.

title: K P cabinet approves broad police reforms
description: K P cabinet approves broad police reforms
content:
New law separates policy, operations and strengthens oversight
The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Cabinet on Wednesday approved the K-P Police Act 2026, introducing sweeping reforms aimed at making the provincial police force more accountable, professional and efficient.
The new legislation empowers the provincial government to return the services of federal police officers, including the Inspector General, in cases of unsatisfactory performance. It also establishes a clear separation between police policy and operational matters, creates new oversight boards, and overhauls the investigation and dispute-resolution systems.
Provincial Minister for Information, Science, Technology and Information Technology Shafi Jan briefed the media after the cabinet meeting, describing the proposed law as an important step towards introducing key reforms in the police system. He said the legislation would make the police more accountable to the public, strengthen the investigation system, improve officers' professional development, and distinctly separate policy from operational affairs.
Under the new Act, a Police Policy Board will be set up under the chairmanship of the Chief Minister, while a Police Operations Board will be headed by the Inspector General of Police. The provincial police chief will be required to prepare an annual policing plan outlining priorities, performance targets and future actions, and present it to the Policy Board for approval.
The law also provides for the appointment of Regional Investigation Officers across the province after its passage by the provincial assembly. Minister Shafi Jan said this measure is designed to enhance the police's investigative capacity and professional competence. Appointments and transfers of Regional Police Officers and District Police Officers will be regulated under the K-P Rules of Business 1985 to ensure greater accountability.
The cabinet meeting, chaired by Chief Minister Muhammad Sohail Afridi, was attended by Chief Secretary Shahab Ali Shah, the Inspector General of Police, departmental secretaries and cabinet members.
Afridi alleged that all routes into the province were being sealed off, warning that such a move would effectively cut K-P off from the rest of the country while leaving other parts of Pakistan open.
"If all routes to the province are closed, the rest of Pakistan will remain open, but no one will be able to enter or leave Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa," Afridi said while addressing the meeting. He questioned the motive behind the alleged blockade, asking what it meant to sever the province from the rest of Pakistan and whether a conspiracy was underway to repeat the tragedy of East Pakistan.
The chief minister issued a clear message to those he said were behind any such plot: "Pakistan is ours. Whoever conspires to divide Pakistan or separate Khyber Pakhtunkhwa from it should know that we were Pakistanis, we are Pakistanis, and InshaAllah we will remain Pakistanis."
Afridi further claimed that for the past three to four days, "thugs in plain clothes" had been targeting PTI workers, organisational office-bearers and elected representatives across the province.

title: Pakistan calls for end to Israeli occupation
description: Pakistan calls for end to Israeli occupation
content:
Reiterates support for independent State of Palestine
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar has called for an end to Israel's occupation of Palestinian territories at a high-level meeting convened by France, the United Kingdom (UK) and Canada.
Dar delivered Pakistan's statement at the High-Level International Meeting on the Two-State Solution, titled "The Road Ahead: One Year After the New York Declaration and the Comprehensive 20-point Peace Plan", the Foreign Office (FO) said on Wednesday.
The meeting was convened by France's President Emmanuel Macron, Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney, and the UK's PM Andy Burnham. The opening statements were also delivered by Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres.
Highlighting several initiatives that Pakistan has been a part of on the Palestine issue, Dar said: "Ultimately, all these efforts must converge on one objective: ending the occupation and realising the Palestinian people's inalienable right to self-determination."
He reiterated Islamabad's call for an independent, sovereign and contiguous State of Palestine on the pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital.
"Pakistan will continue to play its constructive role towards this objective," the deputy premier reaffirmed.
"Diplomacy must respond to the realities on the ground," he emphasised to the attendees, which included various heads of states and Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas (via video).
Spain's President Pedro Sánchez, Qatari PM and FM Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani, Egypt's PM Mostafa Madbouly, Jordan's DPM and FM Ayman Safadi, Norway's PM Jonas Gahr Støre and Ireland's Taoiseach (prime minister) Micheál Martin also attended the meeting.
Other participants included European Council President António Costa, Finland's President Alexander Stubb, the Netherlands ' PM Rob Jetten, Türkiye's Hakan Fidan, and High Representative for Gaza of the Board of Peace Nickolay Mladenov.
Dar recalled that Pakistan had endorsed the September 2025 "New York Declaration" that backed the two-state solution, was part of the Group of Eight Arab-Islamic countries that supported the Gaza peace plan, and had voted for a UN Security Council resolution that supported that plan.
The deputy premier emphasised that these processes were "complementary elements of a broader political and diplomatic pathway towards peace, and these must reinforce one another".
He declared: "Our objective throughout has been clear: to end the killing and suffering of innocent Palestinians, ensure unhindered flow of humanitarian assistance and advance a credible political horizon leading to Palestinian statehood."
Dar stated that violations of the ceasefire and the "catastrophic human toll in Gaza, alongside the expansion of illegal settlements and settler violence in the West Bank, remain matters of grave concern".
"This machinery of occupation is eroding the territorial and political foundations on which a viable Palestinian state must be built. It must stop, and stop immediately," he asserted.
Dar noted that the New York Declaration provided an "important political framework for translating international consensus into concrete action".
"Its implementation, together with the Gaza Peace Plan and Resolution 2803, must ensure a permanent ceasefire, safe and sustained humanitarian assistance, immediate recovery and reconstruction, and create the conditions for a credible, irreversible and time-bound political process."

title: Pakistan among countries vulnerable to  super  El Ni  o
description: Pakistan among countries vulnerable to  super  El Ni  o
content:
Weather pattern could cause 451,000 excess deaths
Extreme heat caused by this year's "super-El Niño" could result in as many as 451,000 excess deaths across the globe from June this year to February 2027, researchers with the University of Chicago's Climate Impact Lab said on Wednesday.
The number of extremely hot days is likely to rise by 44% compared to normal years, Climate Impact Lab said in a report.
The country likely to suffer the most excess heat-related fatalities from September 2026 to February 2027 is Nigeria with 31,400, followed by Indonesia with 19,300 and Sudan with 17,600. Heat in Africa's Sahel region, including Niger and Chad as well as Nigeria and Sudan, is likely to cause an additional 66,800 deaths over the six-month period.
The researchers project the Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand and Cambodia to see an additional 19,400 deaths combined.
The number of excess deaths could even climb higher if El Niño extends further into 2027, with key areas of the northern hemisphere, including India and Pakistan, especially vulnerable during their summer months.
Climate Impact Lab described this year's El Niño as a "postcard from the future", delivering temperatures that will become normal in just a few decades.
It said emergency response efforts should be directed to high-priority regions to tackle heat-related mortality in the coming months.
"This report allows decision makers to see exactly where emergency actions can be taken now to save tens of thousands of lives in the coming months," said Michael Greenstone, economist at the University of Chicago and co-founder of the lab.

title: Gaza board pitches  2 45b plan
description: Gaza board pitches  2 45b plan
content:
Board of Peace plan would consist of 66 rehabilitation programs
Trump's Board of Peace unveiled a $2.45 billion plan on Wednesday to begin rebuilding Gaza, but officials acknowledged it faces an uncertain future as Israel and Hamas remain at odds over terms of a US-backed ceasefire.
The proposal, laid out by board officials at an event during the UN General Assembly in New York, consists of 66 programs that would rehabilitate Gaza's infrastructure and economy, destroyed by two years of full-scale Israeli military assault.
It was the latest plan aimed at advancing Trump's Gaza ceasefire, which was announced nearly a year ago but has failed to halt Israeli attacks on Gaza, including one on Wednesday that killed four people including a Hamas official.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters in New York: "Obviously this is a longterm project. It's not something that can happen in six months. But at least gives people a hope. Here's the future that awaits you if everyone does their part."
Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, who devised the Gaza plan while backing Israel's right to "finish the job" in Gaza if Hamas does not disarm, acknowledged the proposal faced "different delays on different things, for whatever reason."
"We're just refining, sharpening the axe, getting ready for when we get to the time to cut the tree," Kushner said. "And hopefully, that will be very, very soon."
Nearly a year after a ceasefire ended major fighting in Gaza, reconstruction has yet to begin with negotiators failing to agree conditions for Hamas to lay down its weapons and Israel to withdraw its troops.
Most buildings have been destroyed and more than 2 million residents are confined to around a third of the enclave's territory, mostly in tents or crowded rooms in damaged buildings among the ruins.
The Board of Peace plan announced on Wednesday estimates physical damage in Gaza at $35.2 billion and says full recovery and reconstruction will require about $71.4 billion over the next decade.
Its plan calls for repairing border crossings, restoring electricity and water infrastructure, deploying 25,000 portable solar power kits and permanently filling tunnels beneath sites needed for priority reconstruction projects.

title: Who is Dr Najeeb Naqi
description: Who is Dr Najeeb Naqi
content:
Dr Muhammad Najeeb Naqi Khan's political career, which began in Sudhnoti in Poonch division more than three decades ago, has taken him from the Legislative Assembly to the Kashmir Council and several key ministerial portfolios. He is now the PML-N's candidate for president of Azad Jammu and Kashmir AJK.
The 62-year-old politician comes from a prominent political family. His grandfather, Colonel Khan Muhammad Khan, is remembered in AJK's political history as the "Baba-e-Poonch", while his father, Colonel Muhammad Naqi Khan, was also active in politics.
Following his father's death, Dr Naqi entered practical politics in the 1990s and was first elected to the AJK Legislative Assembly in the 1991 elections. During that term, he served as parliamentary secretary for health and planning and development.
He was re-elected to the Assembly in 1996 on the Muslim Conference MC ticket and subsequently served as a member of the AJK Council from 2001 to 2006.
In the 2006 elections, he again won an Assembly seat on the MC ticket and served in the government, holding portfolios including health, population welfare, colleges and information technology.
Dr Naqi joined the PML-N and was elected to the AJK Legislative Assembly on the party ticket in the 2011 elections. He retained his seat in 2016 and served as a minister for several key departments, including health, finance and planning and development, until 2021.
The PML-N's central leadership nominated him this month as its candidate for the AJK presidency.
His political career has thus spanned multiple roles as an elected legislator, parliamentary secretary, Kashmir Council member and cabinet minister culminating in his nomination for the AJK's highest constitutional office.
MUZAFFARABAD, September 24: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir AJK Legislative Assembly will elect the new president today (Thursday), with PML-N nominee Dr Muhammad Najeeb Naqi Khan facing PPP candidate Chaudhry Latif Akbar in a two-way contest.
All 46 members of the Assembly will cast their votes, with the ruling PML-N and its ally holding 32 seats against the PPP's 14.
Polling will be held at the Legislative Assembly Secretariat from 10am to 1pm followed by counting and announcement of the result.
Dr Naqi has submitted his nomination papers on behalf of the PML-N, while Chaudhry Latif Akbar is contesting on the PPP ticket.

A newly launched €54.24 million project will expand access to clean water, renewable energy and climate-resilient infrastructure across the remote mountainous regions of Gilgit-Baltistan, benefiting more than 325,600 residents.
The Gilgit-Baltistan Rural Development and Climate Resilience Project was formally launched at the Chief Minister Secretariat in Gilgit by the Government of Gilgit-Baltistan, the European Union, Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and the Aga Khan Foundation.

The project will include 216 water-supply and sanitation schemes, climate vulnerability assessments in all 110 union councils, and micro-hydropower and other clean-energy systems with an expected generation capacity of between 1.2 and 1.3 megawatts. It will also support the green retrofitting of 3,000 existing homes and the construction of 700 climate-resilient and energy-efficient houses. Communities and public institutions will receive training in climate-responsive planning, enterprise development and sustainable infrastructure management.
Speaking at the launch European Union Ambassador to Pakistan described the launch as an important milestone in the shared commitment to a sustainable and climate-resilient future for Gilgit-Baltistan. He reaffirmed the European Union and its European partners' support for translating the project into practical improvements in the lives of local communities and supporting an inclusive transition towards a greener economy.
The project will be implemented through Aga Khan Rural Support Programme (AKRSP) and other agencies of the Aga Khan Development Network, drawing on their experience in community-led integrated development.

description: At UNGA  Iran s president vows  no surrender to US
content:
Two crew dead after cargo ship hit by projectiles in Hormuz
Iran and the United States remain far apart on how to end their war but diplomacy must continue, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Wednesday, after Iran's president told the UN General Assembly that Tehran would never surrender to US pressure.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, in his speech in New York, condemned what he called "signs of a bullying mentality" from US President Donald Trump, who had used the same forum on Tuesday to threaten to "annihilate" Iran.
The duelling speeches at the annual UN gathering bookended the first shuttle talks between the US and Iran for months, though they appeared to have yielded no concessions in the public stance of either side towards ending the war.
The senior Iranian official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Tehran was reviewing Washington's response to its peace proposals, which prioritise lifting a US naval blockade on Iranian ports and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
"There are still many differences between the Iranian and US positions, but diplomacy is continuing," the official said.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters on Wednesday that a deal with Iran would involve hard work over a period of time, adding that Trump also had military options.
The US has also said it will impose so-called secondary sanctions against any country that allows Iranian flights after Wednesday. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, told state TV Iran would ensure neighbouring countries' airports could not function if they stop Iranian flights.
In his address to the 193-member General Assembly, Pezeshkian homed in on the US blockade of Iranian ports and on the Strait of Hormuz, conduit for a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments before the war.
"It cannot be the case that everyone benefits from the Strait of Hormuz while we are denied access to shipping through this waterway. The permanent deployment of hostile fleets and the expansion of the war will not lead to peace," he said.
"The Iranian people will not bow to pressure," he added.
Iran wants to exert control over the strait and collect fees from ships that use it. Washington rejects this and says the strait must remain fully open to international shipping.
Oil prices were up almost 2% on Wednesday in choppy trade as traders weighed the comments of Pezeshkian and Trump.
Trump on Tuesday argued that he had prevented Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and could "annihilate the Islamic Republic" if no deal is reached to end the conflict.
Pezeshkian on Wednesday reiterated Iran's line that it is not seeking nuclear weapons.
Iranian and US officials held their first known indirect talks on Tuesday since a ceasefire collapsed in July, with Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner communicating through mediators.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said Tehran had conveyed conditions during a two-hour exchange of messages with Washington via a Qatari mediator. These included an end to the war on all fronts, a halt to US "acts of aggression" and the release of frozen Iranian assets.
The diplomatic contact in New York caused a backlash in Iranian media associated with hardliners.
An opinion piece run by the semi-official Tasnim news agency, associated with the Revolutionary Guards, said Araqchi was wrong to have contacts with Witkoff and Kushner, "a major gift to Trump", as Iran had already conveyed its terms.
Iranian sources told Reuters the delegation had been ordered not to meet the Americans face-to-face by the Supreme National Security Council, a body that includes figures selected by Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, the supreme leader. Khamenei has yet to appear in public since replacing his father, who was killed on the war's first day.
One Iranian journalist covering the visit told Reuters that some hardliners viewed the trip to New York itself as an insult to the memory of the slain leader, Ali Khamenei.
The war, launched by Trump in February alongside Israel as "Operation Epic Fury", has lasted nearly seven months, killing thousands of people, disrupting global energy supplies and spreading to other countries in the region - particularly to Lebanon and more recently to Yemen.
In the latest reported attack in the Strait of Hormuz, Britain's UKMTO maritime security agency said a cargo ship had been hit by projectiles, causing two casualties among the crew. The crew was evacuated and the ship was on fire and adrift.
Despite near-daily attacks, traffic through the strait has picked up in recent weeks. Oil producers pay shipping companies fees of as much as a quarter of a cargo's value to take the wartime risk of sailing through the strait with transponders switched off, before transferring crude to other vessels on the far side.
Exports from the United Arab Emirates have already recovered to pre-war levels, and Saudi Arabia has sold 60 million barrels of Gulf oil for both this month and next, to be delivered beyond the strait off the coast of Oman.
Nevertheless, a third of Gulf oil is estimated to be missing from global supplies. Shortages have particularly hit refined products such as diesel, causing inflation, pushing up interest rates and hurting Trump's Republicans.

title: Taliban  proxies hit in the air and on the ground
description: Taliban  proxies hit in the air and on the ground
content:
Eight drones shot down after crossing from Afghanistan
Pakistan's air defence system shot down eight drones after they entered the country's airspace from Afghanistan on Wednesday, while security forces killed 19 Indian-sponsored terrorists in separate operations in Balochistan, intensifying security activity along the western frontier.
Security sources said four of the drones were brought down in areas adjoining the Torkham border, while another four were shot down in mountainous areas near the border with Kohat. The wreckage of the destroyed drones was being taken into custody, they added.
The sources said the Pakistan Army and Pakistan Air Force (PAF) had thwarted an attempt by the Afghan Taliban regime to target public places, with the country's "active and alert air defence system" detecting and bringing down all eight drones.
They described the drone incursion as "further evidence" of the Afghan Taliban regime's direct support and patronage of terrorists, while reiterating that the Pakistan Armed Forces remained prepared to defend the country and its people.
"The Pakistan Armed Forces remain fully prepared at all times to defend Pakistan and its people," the sources said, adding that the PAF's surveillance, assessment and defence systems along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border remained operational and on alert.
According to the sources, the downing of the drones demonstrated the PAF's determination and capability to thwart any ground, aerial or terrorist incursion by the Afghan Taliban regime. They said the developments reflected "severe panic" within the Afghan Taliban regime.
The sources said the PAF's surveillance and defence systems along the border remained fully operational to detect and respond to any further incursions amid heightened tensions and exchanges of fire along the frontier.
The drone incursions followed an attempted infiltration by terrorists affiliated with Fitna al-Khawarij into the Kurram sector from Afghanistan, which security forces had earlier foiled. The term Fitna al-Khawarij is used for the terrorists affiliated with the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
The developments came after Pakistani forces destroyed terrorist hideouts operating under the Afghan Taliban regime. According to the sources, the infiltration attempt was made from Afghan Taliban posts in Nangarhar and Paktia provinces but was effectively thwarted by Pakistani troops deployed along the border.
Following the failure of the infiltration attempt, the Afghan Taliban opened unprovoked fire on Pakistani border posts using heavy weapons, mortars and other arms. Pakistani security forces responded by targeting several Afghan Taliban border posts, the sources said.
Separately, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said security forces had killed 13 Indian-sponsored terrorists during a clearance operation in the Shaban area of Quetta district in Balochistan.
The operation began on September 21 after intelligence agencies reported multiple hideouts of Indian-sponsored Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan in the area, which were assessed as posing a threat to the local population.
ISPR said security forces effectively engaged and cleared multiple terrorist hideouts during the operation. Following an intense exchange of fire, 13 terrorists had been killed so far, while weapons, ammunition and explosives were recovered from the cleared hideouts.
The military's media wing said the clearance operation would continue until the complete neutralisation of the threat in the area, indicating that security forces were maintaining their presence in the affected area.
In separate engagements on September 22 and 23, security forces also conducted pre-emptive intelligence-based operations in Kech district and Quetta West district. During the operations, troops effectively engaged the terrorists, killing six and recovering weapons and ammunition.
ISPR said a soldier, Subedar Muhammad Jamil, 39, a resident of Taunsa Sharif in Dera Ghazi Khan, was martyred during the intense exchange of fire. The military said security forces and law-enforcement agencies remained committed to eliminating the menace of foreign-sponsored terrorism from the country.
The latest operations form part of the security forces' continuing counter-terrorism campaign under the vision of "Azm-e-Istehkam", approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, according to ISPR.

title: IMF has no issue with fuel subsidy  PM
description: IMF has no issue with fuel subsidy  PM
content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday said the International Monetary Fund (IMF) had not expressed any serious concerns over Pakistan's targeted subsidy of Rs100 per litre during his meeting with the Fund's managing director on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly session in New York.
Speaking to The Express Tribune after meeting IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly, the prime minister said he had briefed her in detail on the pressure Pakistan faces and the difficulties confronting low-income people.
"We drew the IMF chief's attention to the question of where the poor man would go," the premier said, adding that the targeted subsidy was being distributed through a comprehensive and transparent mechanism.
Earlier this month, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws, and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Later, in a post on X, the IMF managing director hailed Pakistan's implementation of reforms, saying they had helped preserve stability, restore confidence and regain market access.
"I had the opportunity to meet with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on the margins of UNGA to discuss Pakistan's reforms," she said.
"Continuing reforms will help boost economic growth and improve the living standards of the people," said the IMF chief.
PM Shehbaz, IMF chief discuss reforms, subsidy: PMO
Meanwhile, PM Shehbaz appreciated the IMF's continued support for Pakistan's economy and reaffirmed his government's "unwavering commitment" to the successful implementation of the IMF-supported reform programme, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office.
In meeting with the IMF chief, the prime minister particularly appreciated Georgieva's role in strengthening Pakistan's constructive partnership with the Fund.
He reaffirmed the government's strong ownership of the economic reform agenda and reiterated Pakistan's resolve to maintain the momentum of reforms and advance structural measures aimed at strengthening the economy and laying the foundations for sustainable and inclusive growth.
"Despite regional conflict and external inflationary pressures, Pakistan is successfully transitioning from macroeconomic stabilization towards a recovery path, supported by prudent fiscal and monetary policies," the prime minister noted.
Highlighting the improvements in fiscal discipline, external buffers and investor confidence, the premier cited the National Tariff Regime, enhanced domestic revenue mobilisation and progress on privatisation as examples of Pakistan's efforts.
He also underscored the government's commitment to protecting vulnerable segments of society alongside maintaining economic reforms.
The IMF managing director appreciated Pakistan's performance under the IMF programme and the government's efforts for economic stabilisation, saying these were yielding tangible results.
The two leaders also discussed Pakistan's forthcoming IMF programme review and continued cooperation between Pakistan and the Fund in advancing reforms, strengthening economic resilience and supporting sustainable growth.
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, Adviser on Privatisation Muhammad Ali, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Tariq Fatemi and other senior officials were also present during the meeting.

title: Pakistan hasn t given up on US Iran d  tente
description: Pakistan hasn t given up on US Iran d  tente
content:
 Shehbaz vows continued efforts to end war  Steps up diplomatic engagements on UNGA fringes
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday said Pakistan was "completely focused" on mediating an end to the Middle East war.
"Pakistan is playing the role of a sincere and honest mediator between Iran, our neighbourly country, and the United States," the prime minister told reporters at the United Nations, adding that he signed the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding along with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and US President Donald Trump.
"Unfortunately, events after that got a bit unpredictable, but Pakistan is completely focused. We have not lost hope; we [are] absolutely determined that we will further make efforts and make progress to de-escalate the situation," the premier added.
Asked if there are plans for another meeting, the prime minister said it is a "conscious process" and that all friendly countries are contributing to achieve peace.
The prime minister reiterated Pakistan's principled support for Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity and expressed readiness to contribute to the country's reconstruction and economic recovery.
The prime minister made the remarks during a meeting with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office.
Separately, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif held multiple meetings on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York.
PM reaffirmed Pakistan's strong commitment to its historic and fraternal relations with Syria and reiterated its support for Syria's sovereignty, unity, territorial integrity and political independence.
The two leaders discussed ways to further strengthen bilateral relations, including through enhanced high-level exchanges, activation of institutional mechanisms and cooperation in trade and investment, education, information technology and other areas of mutual interest.
The prime minister reaffirmed Pakistan's readiness to contribute to Syria's reconstruction and economic recovery, while reiterating its principled support for the country's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
The two leaders also exchanged views on the regional situation, with the prime minister underscoring the importance of dialogue, diplomacy and respect for the principles of the UN Charter in promoting peace and stability in the region.
The prime minister reaffirmed Pakistan's steadfast support for the Palestinian people's right to self-determination and for a just and lasting resolution of the Palestine issue in accordance with relevant UN resolutions and international law.
He also expressed good wishes for the Syrian people in their efforts towards national stabilisation, cohesion, peace and economic recovery.
The meeting provided an opportunity to reaffirm the longstanding bonds of friendship between Pakistan and Syria and to further strengthen bilateral cooperation in the years ahead.
The prime minister met with Gates Foundation Chair Bill Gates, who stressed that polio eradication efforts in Pakistan were "vital to protect future generations".
PM Shehbaz appreciated Gates Foundation's engagement with Pakistan to support polio eradication, maternal and child health, nutrition, immunisation, digitisation and financial inclusion, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said in a post on X.
"The prime minister complimented the Gates Foundation for being a trusted partner in Pakistan's socio-economic development and expressed interest in broadening collaboration in areas including public health, agriculture, digital innovation and AI," PMO said.
PM Shehbaz and Gates also "agreed to explore opportunities for collaboration in the development of improved seeds, livestock genetics and emerging agricultural technologies", according to PMO.
The two committed to "further strengthening and expanding partnerships that support sustainable development, technological advancement and improved social sector outcomes for the people of Pakistan".
PM Shehbaz invited the Microsoft co-founder to visit Pakistan.
Pakistan is one of the last two countries in the world, alongside Afghanistan, where polio remains endemic.
During his ongoing New York trip, PM Shehbaz also met with world leaders of Kuwait, Kenya, Austria, Somalia, Syria and Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Meanwhile, in a meeting with Bosnian Presidency Chairman Denis Becirovic, the prime minister congratulated him on the formal opening of Bosnia and Herzegovina's European Union accession talks.
According to PMO, Becirovic praised Pakistan's mediation efforts for de-escalation in the Gulf, adding that "he also fully supported Pakistan's position" on the illegality of holding the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance.
In the meeting with Kuwait's Crown Prince Sheikh Sabah Khaled Al-Hamad Al-Sabah on Tuesday, PM Shehbaz highlighted the potential for "enhanced cooperation in trade, investment, energy and human resource development" between the two countries, PMO said.
Furthermore, PM Shehbaz and Kenyan President William Ruto "reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the longstanding and cordial ties between the two countries".
The premier invited Kenyan investors to explore investment opportunities in Pakistan, while Ruto lauded Pakistan's mediation efforts in the US-Iran war.
PM Shehbaz also met Austrian Federal Chancellor Christian Stocker and Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud on Tuesday on the sidelines of the UNGA session.
PM Shehbaz also addressed a high-level meeting at the UN headquarters on Wednesday, in which he said that a country's right to development could not be realised where the means to do so were denied, and called for a proactive approach.
The premier was addressing a meeting marking the 40th anniversary of the UN's Declaration on the Right to Development.
He called attention to the "stark reality" that debt servicing was shrinking fiscal space and consuming "scarce resources that should have been directed towards human development around the globe". He added that climate disasters were erasing "hard-earned gains" and warned of technological inequalities threatening to perpetuate existing socio-economic divides in a digital age.
"A right cannot be realised where the means to realise it are denied," PM Shehbaz said. "Therefore, a proactive approach is required."
He highlighted Pakistan's development pursuits, saying that they were anchored in a "homegrown economic transformational plan" that was built on enhancing exports, embracing digital technologies, taking effective climate action, enhancing energy infrastructure and ensuring equity and empowerment. He also noted that the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) complemented this agenda.
Shehbaz also called for debt distress to be addressed and for international financial architecture to be reformed to "provide concessional finance, deliver climate adaptation and loss and damage support".
He expressed Pakistan's support for the early adoption of the international covenant on the right to early development.
"The true measure of development is not how far the world advances, but whether humanity advances together in a collective mode," he said.
