title: Prince Harry returns to US for Clinton Global Initiative Event weeks after UK move
description: Harry spoke about the potential impact of rapidly developing technology and artificial intelligence on children
content:
Harry spoke about the potential impact of rapidly developing technology and artificial intelligence on children
Prince Harry has returned to the United States just weeks after moving back to the United Kingdom with his wife Meghan Markle and their two children.
The Duke of Sussex, 42, travelled to New York City to attend the Clinton Global Initiative annual meeting on Wednesday, September 23. His appearance marks his second time taking part in the event, following his participation in 2024.
Harry arrived in New York on Tuesday, September 22, after spending the previous week attending a series of engagements in the UK. His latest US trip comes less than a month after he and Meghan, 45, relocated to Britain with Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, on August 26.
The family has established a new base outside London while continuing to maintain their home in Montecito, California, where they had lived for around six years. Harry's return to the US therefore marks a brief trip back to the country where the couple previously based their family life.
At the Clinton Global Initiative meeting, Harry spoke about the potential impact of rapidly developing technology and artificial intelligence on children. During his speech, he highlighted his perspective as a parent, saying, "I come to this as a father."
The 2026 Clinton Global Initiative meeting, held under the theme "How Do We Get It Right?", brings together public figures and leaders to discuss issues including artificial intelligence, climate and energy resilience, democracy, humanitarian response, economic opportunity and health.
Other participants at this year's meeting include Chrissy Teigen, Bill Nye and LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman. The gathering is taking place during United Nations General Assembly week in New York.
Harry's New York appearance follows a busy period of public engagements in Britain since the family's move. He recently attended the inaugural Invictus Spirit Gala Dinner and Awards in London, where he spoke about settling back into life in the UK, before attending the WellChild Awards on September 21.
Speaking at the Invictus event, Harry described the family's first weeks back in Britain as "eventful" and said they were happy and getting settled, while their children had started school.
Despite Harry and Meghan's return to Britain, the couple are not resuming their former roles as working members of the Royal Family. King Charles' office reaffirmed their status as non-working royals earlier this month, while the couple continue to pursue their charitable and commercial work independently.
Harry is expected to continue balancing engagements in the UK with international commitments as he maintains his work with organisations including the Invictus Games and WellChild.

title: Crew member killed, 27 evacuated after ship targeted near Strait of Hormuz: Oman | The Express Tribune
description: Royal navy of Oman vessel evacuates the crew of the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged commercial ship CAPE DAO
content:
Royal navy of Oman vessel evacuates the crew of the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged commercial ship CAPE DAO
One crew member was killed, and 27 others were evacuated after a commercial vessel was targeted near Oman’s Musandam Governorate overlooking the Strait of Hormuz, Omani authorities said Wednesday.
The Omani Maritime Security Centre said in a statement on X that a Royal Navy of Oman vessel, in coordination with relevant authorities, evacuated the crew of the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged commercial ship CAPE DAO.
“Twenty-seven crew members were evacuated and provided with the necessary medical care after the vessel was targeted 2.5 nautical miles off Musandam Governorate,” the centre said.
The attack caused a fire in the engine room and killed one crew member, it added.

title: Disney  and Hulu raise subscription prices again
description: Disney is also preparing to combine Disney  and Hulu  with the company expected to launch an app by the end of 2026
content:
Disney is also preparing to combine Disney+ and Hulu, with the company expected to launch an app by the end of 2026
Disney+ is raising its subscription prices again, with the streaming service increasing the cost of its premium ad-free plan to $21.49 a month in the US.
The latest increase takes effect on September 23 for new subscribers, while existing customers will see the higher prices reflected on their next monthly bill. It marks Disney’s fourth streaming price increase in four years.
The ad-free Disney+ Premium plan is increasing by $2.50, or around 13%, from $18.99 to $21.49 per month. The standalone ad-supported plan is also going up by 50 cents, from $11.99 to $12.49 a month.
Hulu is facing similar increases. Its ad-free Premium subscription is also rising to $21.49 a month, while the ad-supported plan will cost $12.49. The ad-free Disney+ and Hulu bundle is increasing by $2 to $21.99 per month, while the ad-supported bundle remains at $12.99.
Disney is also increasing the price of some of its combined Disney+, Hulu and ESPN packages. The Disney+, Hulu and ESPN bundle with ads will rise to $21.99, while the Premium version will cost $32.99 a month. The Disney+, Hulu and ESPN Unlimited plans will remain at their existing prices.
The latest changes come as major streaming companies continue raising subscription prices while placing greater emphasis on profitability. Disney reported a significant increase in operating income from its entertainment division in its most recent quarterly results, with its streaming business contributing to the improvement.

title: Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years in prison after New York sexual assault retrial
description: Weinstein has already spent more than six years behind bars as his cases have moved through the courts
content:
Weinstein has already spent more than six years behind bars as his cases have moved through the courts
Harvey Weinstein has been sentenced to 15 years in prison following his conviction for sexually assaulting former production assistant Miriam Haley in New York.
The sentence was handed down on September 23, more than a year after New York’s highest court overturned Weinstein’s original conviction. He was initially sentenced to 23 years in prison in 2020 after being found guilty of sexually assaulting Haley and raping actress Jessica Mann.
Weinstein was retried in 2025 and was again convicted of a first-degree criminal sexual act involving Haley, stemming from an incident at his Manhattan apartment in 2006. The charge carried a maximum sentence of 25 years.
During Wednesday’s sentencing, Haley addressed the court and described the lasting impact of the assault and the legal proceedings. Weinstein also spoke, expressing remorse for Haley’s pain while continuing to maintain his innocence.
The latest sentence follows a complicated legal battle. New York’s Court of Appeals overturned Weinstein’s 2020 conviction in 2024, ruling that testimony about allegations that were not part of the charges had unfairly prejudiced his trial.
At his 2025 retrial, Weinstein was acquitted of a separate criminal sex act charge involving former model Kaja Sokola, while jurors could not reach a verdict on the rape allegation involving Mann. Prosecutors later dropped the rape charge rather than pursue another trial.
Weinstein, 74, has already spent more than six years behind bars as his cases have moved through the courts. He is also facing a separate legal situation in California, where he was convicted of rape and sexual assault in 2022. A California appeals court upheld that conviction in June but ordered the lower court to reconsider his sentence.
Weinstein has repeatedly denied raping or sexually assaulting anyone and is expected to appeal the latest New York conviction and sentence.

content:
Petrol price set at Rs390.12 per litre and HSD at Rs414.75 after latest daily fuel price revision
The federal government on Wednesday decreased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.93 and Rs4.21 per litre, respectively, for September 24.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs390.12 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs414.75 per litre for Thursday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government decreased the price of petrol by Rs1.7 per litre while reducing the price of HSD by Rs3.12 per litre for September 22.
Read : Govt decreases petrol by Rs1.7, HSD by Rs3.12 for Sept 23
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
Earlier this month, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices rose on Wednesday as Brent crude prices climbed over 3% after five straight sessions of declines, bouncing off a ​near two-week low.
"Saudi Arabia is acting, not waiting," said Phil Flynn, senior analyst at Price Futures Group. "After Houthi hits on the East-West pipeline forced a shutdown of Yanbu loadings, Aramco loaded about 14 million barrels of crude onto seven VLCCs inside the Gulf. Satellite and tracker data showed ​Saudi oil moving through Hormuz, averaging about 2.9 million barrels a day over the last six days, up from roughly 700,000 barrels ​a day in August.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said at the UN that Tehran would never surrender to the US, but still believes in diplomacy, a day after President Donald Trump threatened to "annihilate" Iran.
The dueling speeches bookended the first US-Iran shuttle talks in months, underscoring the lack of progress ​toward ending the Middle East conflict.

title: Rubio says Russia and Ukraine have both voiced interest in  limited ceasefire
description: US secretary of state asserts Washington will  consistently prioritise its national interest over international order
content:
US secretary of state asserts Washington will consistently prioritise its national interest over international order
Ukraine and Russia have both ​voiced an interest in a limited ceasefire involving grain and energy-related targets, US Secretary of State ‌Marco Rubio said on Wednesday after meeting Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov in New York.
Ukraine, which fears Russia plans to pound power and heating facilities with missiles and drones this winter, has been pressing for ceasefires covering energy infrastructure and Black Sea shipping.
"I think both ​sides have expressed an interest in some limited ceasefire that involves grain and energy. Obviously, you know, that ​won't be easy either," Rubio told reporters.
Marco Rubio on Russia-Ukraine: Both sides have expressed an interest in some limited ceasefire that involves energy. Zelensky has done so publicly. pic.twitter.com/101wosUXfs
Russia has given no public indication it is ready ⁠to agree to a maritime or energy truce with Ukraine, and it was not immediately clear if Rubio was suggesting ​there had been movement on the Russian side after his talks with Lavrov.
Read : Russia is ready for new ideas on Ukraine peace, but with conditions, senior diplomat says
Rubio noted that it was a particular challenge ​that energy strikes were at the core of both countries' tactical priorities in their war, which is now in its fifth year.
World leaders converged on New York this week for the annual UN General Assembly debate.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who was expected to address ​the General Assembly later on Wednesday, met US President Donald Trump on Tuesday and said they had discussed a ​ceasefire on energy-related targets.
The Ukrainian president told leaders at the United Nations earlier that Kyiv was ready for a maritime truce in ‌the Black ⁠Sea based on proposals such as those by Egypt, India and Turkey and said it was now up to Russia to respond.
Zelenskiy spoke at Ukraine's Crimean Platform summit ahead of a Security Council meeting on Russia's war in Ukraine.
"We are waiting for Russia's response. Ukraine is ready ... to ensure safe shipping and food security in the Black Sea if Russia ​is ready to take real ​steps towards de-escalation too. We ⁠have to start somewhere," he said.
Top wheat importers in Asia, the Middle East and Africa that count on the Black Sea region for wheat have been finding it hard ​to secure supplies. Global wheat prices have soared.
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot told the Security ​Council that ⁠France backed moratoriums on attacks against energy infrastructure and in the Black Sea as a first step toward de-escalation.
Ahead of the Lavrov-Rubio meeting, the Kremlin said there were no grounds for wider Ukraine peace talks, while saying it remained open to such ⁠talks.
"For now, ​there are no prerequisites for moving on to a peaceful negotiating ​track, although we, as the Russian side, remain open to peace talks," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters.
Zelenskiy said on Tuesday that he would be ​ready to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin at a trilateral meeting with Trump.
Rubio slams international order, says US will always act in its national interest
Meanwhile, Rubio criticised the current international system as "failing" and asserted that Washington would consistently prioritise its national interests over the international order.
Marco Rubio: We will never put the international order above the interests of the U.S. pic.twitter.com/cY7BJ8FfEz
Addressing journalists on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, Rubio argued that multilateral bodies had lost their core purpose and failed to resolve major global flashpoints.
"The international system is not in good shape right now, and these international norms people talk about," Rubio said. "At the end of the day, the president (Donald Trump) and I reflected this going back to the very beginning. The view of this administration is that the number one obligation of every government is the national interest of their country."
Marco Rubio: Look, the international system is not in good shape right now. pic.twitter.com/5pUWJ9DckV
Rubio pointed out that world leaders increasingly shared a consensus that global institutions were no longer working as intended. "Multiple leaders pointed to the fact that the international system is failing, and it's failing because it has grown beyond its mandate," he said.
"It has grown beyond its intent. It's involved in all kinds of things it shouldn't be involved in, and it's unable to solve virtually any major conflict in the world."
Highlighting ongoing global tensions, Rubio questioned the efficacy of global institutions in managing disputes such as clashes between Thailand and Cambodia, tensions between India and Pakistan, conflicts in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda, and maritime friction in the Strait of Hormuz involving Iran.
In the absence of a functional system, nation-states must look out for their own security, Rubio said, emphasising the administration's foreign policy approach.
"At the end of the day, the United States will always act. At least as long as President Trump is in office, we will always act in the national interest of our country, not in the interest of the international order," he stressed. "We will never put the international order above the interest of the United States."

title: Naval chief calls for action to unlock Pakistan   s maritime potential on World Maritime Day
description: Admiral Naveed Ashraf stresses stronger oversight  sustainable practices and capacity building to drive growth
content:
Admiral Naveed Ashraf stresses stronger oversight, sustainable practices and capacity building to drive growth
Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS) Admiral Naveed Ashraf on Wednesday called for translating maritime policies, regulations and international commitments into practical action, stressing that Pakistan’s maritime potential could only be realised through a safe, secure and sustainable maritime environment.
In a message issued on the occasion of World Maritime Day 2026, being observed on September 24, the naval chief extended his felicitations to Pakistan’s maritime community and the international maritime fraternity.
CNS Ashraf acknowledged the contributions of seafarers, maritime professionals, fishermen and coastal communities, saying their efforts remained vital to maritime connectivity, economic prosperity and the country’s overall economy.
He said Pakistan’s coastline and Exclusive Economic Zone offered significant opportunities for growth in shipping, shipbuilding, ship recycling, fisheries, offshore resources, energy, tourism and other activities linked to the blue economy.
“Realising this potential requires not only a safe, secure and sustainable maritime environment but also effective institutional oversight, responsible practices and continued investment in developing maritime capacity,” he said.
Read: Naval chief recalls 'Operation Somnath' on Navy Day, says legacy of courage continues as reflected in Marka-e-Haq
The chief of naval staff highlighted this year’s World Maritime Day theme, “From Policy to Practice: Powering Maritime Excellence”, saying for Pakistan, this meant continued efforts to strengthen maritime safety, protect the marine environment, enhance professional capacity and ensure that the maritime sector operates in accordance with international standards.
He also emphasised cooperation, knowledge sharing and capacity building among maritime stakeholders. “Pakistan Navy remains committed to safeguarding Pakistan's maritime interests and contributing to a secure and stable maritime environment,” CNS Ashraf said in a statement.
“Through continuous surveillance of our maritime areas, protection of sea lines of communication and contribution to regional maritime security, Pakistan Navy plays a vibrant role in creating an environment conducive to the growth of maritime trade and other economy-related activities,” he added.
The naval chief stressed that sustainable development of Pakistan’s maritime sector required a national approach, with greater awareness, protection of the ecosystem, responsible use of resources and stronger linkages among government institutions, industry, academia and coastal communities.

He said the Pakistan Navy would continue supporting national endeavour for sustainable development of the sector and the fulfilment of relevant national and international obligations.
Reaffirming the Navy’s commitment to the International Maritime Organisation’s vision of safer, secure and environmentally sustainable seas, CNS Ashraf said Pakistan would continue to promote excellence across the maritime sector.
“Guided by our national maritime objectives, we shall continue to safeguard Pakistan’s maritime interests and contribute towards a secure, prosperous and sustainable future,” he said.
The naval chief expressed hope that World Maritime Day 2026 would inspire stakeholders to translate maritime aspirations into practical action and harness the opportunities offered by the seas for the prosperity of the country and its people.

title: K P Cabinet approves landmark Police Act 2026
description: New law gives the province power to recall underperforming federal officers  separates policy from operations
content:
New law gives the province power to recall underperforming federal officers, separates policy from operations
The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Cabinet on Wednesday approved the K-P Police Act 2026, introducing sweeping reforms aimed at making the provincial police force more accountable, professional and efficient.
The new legislation empowers the provincial government to return the services of federal police officers, including the Inspector General, in cases of unsatisfactory performance. It also establishes a clear separation between police policy and operational matters, creates new oversight boards, and overhauls the investigation and dispute-resolution systems.
Provincial Minister for Information, Science, Technology and Information Technology Shafi Jan briefed the media after the cabinet meeting, describing the proposed law as an important step towards introducing key reforms in the police system. He said the legislation would make the police more accountable to the public, strengthen the investigation system, improve officers’ professional development, and distinctly separate policy from operational affairs.
Under the new Act, the chief minister will chair the Police Policy Board, while the Inspector General of Police will lead the Police Operations Board. Furthermore, the provincial police chief will be required to prepare an annual policing plan outlining priorities, performance targets and future actions, and present it to the Policy Board for approval. The law also provides for the appointment of Regional Investigation Officers across the province after its passage by the provincial assembly.
Read: K-P police bill sparks autonomy concerns
Minister Jan said the measure is designed to enhance the police’s investigative capacity and professional competence. He further stated that appointments and transfers of Regional Police Officers and District Police Officers will be regulated under the K-P Rules of Business 1985 to ensure greater accountability.
To address long-standing barriers to career progression, the Act rebalances promotion, fast-track promotion and direct recruitment quotas. The minister said this would expand opportunities for officers and establish a more structured system of career advancement.
In a significant move towards transparency and uniformity, all existing Dispute Resolution Councils will be dissolved and reconstituted under the new law. Jan noted that the current legal framework lacks a clear procedure for these councils; the new Act introduces a standardised mechanism applicable across the province.
The cabinet meeting, chaired by Chief Minister Muhammad Sohail Afridi, was attended by Chief Secretary Shahab Ali Shah, the Inspector General of Police, departmental secretaries and cabinet members.
In addition to the Police Act, the cabinet approved the K-P Stamp (Amendment) Bill 2026. It also gave the green light to the revised cost estimates for the intake structure and tunnel (up to daylight) under the Peshawar Water Supply Scheme, and approved the release of remaining funds and a supplementary grant for land acquisition under an Annual Development Programme scheme for the construction of sports complexes in District Chitral.
The reforms mark one of the most comprehensive overhauls of the provincial police framework in recent years, with the government positioning the new law as a foundation for improved public service delivery and institutional accountability.

title: Niall Horan plays Liam Payne   s voice at End of an Era performance
description: We thought something might happen  but never anything like this     Payne could be heard saying
content:
“We thought something might happen, but never anything like this,” Payne could be heard saying.
Niall Horan honoured his late One Direction bandmate Liam Payne with an emotional surprise at the opening night of his Dinner Party: Live on Tour in Birmingham on September 22.
After performing End of an Era, Horan stepped away from the microphone as a recording of Payne’s voice began playing through the Utilita Arena. In the recording, Payne reflected on the extraordinary success he and his One Direction bandmates experienced.
“We thought something might happen, but never anything like this,” Payne could be heard saying. “I’m always trying to remind myself of where I’ve come from and where I’ve managed to get to in my life. It’s amazing, really.”
Fan-shot footage showed Horan standing quietly on stage as Payne’s voice played, before the lights eventually went dark. The unexpected addition came at the end of End of an Era, a song that already holds special significance for Horan because he rewrote it following Payne’s death in October 2024.
Horan originally began writing the song with Julian Bunetta and John Ryan years ago, but revisited it while working on his fourth album, Dinner Party. He previously said rewriting the track became a therapeutic process and that he wanted the song to capture both the sadness of losing Payne and the happy memories they shared.
“End of an Era” includes lyrics reflecting on the passage of time and the memories of Horan and Payne’s years together in One Direction. The group formed in 2010 after the five members were brought together on The X Factor and went on to become one of the biggest acts in pop music before beginning their hiatus in 2016.
Payne died aged 31 in October 2024. Horan had reunited with him in Argentina just weeks before his death and later said he felt fortunate that their last meeting gave him a happy final memory of his friend.
The Birmingham concert marked the beginning of Horan’s Dinner Party: Live on Tour, with the singer set to continue the tour across Europe and North America.

Baghaei says New York talks focused on Tehran’s demands to end US pressure, secure safe shipping route
Iran said on Wednesday that it conveyed its conditions for reviving diplomacy with the US during a two-hour exchange of messages and clarifications mediated by Qatar on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.
Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei wrote on X that the exchange took place Tuesday “as a continuation of the discussions” mediated by countries between Tehran and Washington.

He said Iran used the process to communicate its positions and conditions for reviving diplomacy “in a manner that leaves no doubt or ambiguity and provides no excuses or pretexts for any party.”
Baqaei said Tehran’s conditions include an end to US “aggressive actions,” including the naval blockade and “economic terrorism,” as well as ending the war on all fronts and releasing Iranian assets that are frozen or restricted.

title: Pezeshkian accuses Israel  US of  double standards  over Iran s nuclear programme
description: Iranian president says Iran is not pursuing nuclear weapons  has  inherent  right to peaceful nuclear technology
content:
Iranian president says Iran is not pursuing nuclear weapons, has 'inherent' right to peaceful nuclear technology
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Wednesday accused Israel and the US of applying ‘double standards’, pointing to Israel’s nuclear arsenal and its actions in Gaza while Iran faces inspections and sanctions. He called for equal treatment under international law.
Addressing the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York, Pezeshkian said Iran was ready for dialogue but would not submit to pressure.
He said that Tehran remained open to dialogue and negotiations but would not accept what he described as the “language of force” or talks conducted under threats. “We will never bow our head,” he said, adding that Iran was prepared for negotiations provided they were not accompanied by threats.
Addressing the UN General Assembly, Pezeshkian displayed images of victims of an American strike on a school in Minab at the start of the war, along with images of a sports hall in Lamerd destroyed by US bombardment.
The ​United States delegation walked out at the ⁠start of Pezeshkian's speech. The US mission to the ​United Nations did not immediately respond to a request ​for comment.
🔴 LIVE: Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian delivers a speech at the UNGA on the second day of the annual general debate in New York. https://t.co/wo8MrOIloL
“The United States, by using weapons with multiple warheads, targeted that sports hall. They martyred and assassinated our scientists, our men, women and children. Innocent children who in truth had committed no crimes, no sins,” he said.
Pezeshkian stressed that while Iran had responded to strikes by the United States and Israel, it had not targeted civilian areas.
“Yes, they did hit us, but we did not bend the knee. We did not bow our head,” he said. “We responded, but we did not hit civilian populations.
“They came into surrounding territories and targeted our universities, our healthcare centres, our schools, our hospitals, our infrastructure; all of it against international law,” Pezeshkian added.
He also said that Hamas chief Ismail Haniyeh had been assassinated in Tehran by Israel on the day of his inauguration as president.
Pezeshkian said there was clear hypocrisy in the fact that Israel possessed nuclear weapons and was not a signatory to the Nuclear Nonproliferation Treaty, “but the inspectors are requested to come to Iran.”
"Israel has the bombs, has weapons of mass destruction but is not a member of the non-proliferation treaty and, during her shameful life, has not allowed a single inspection. I will repeat: the nuclear weapon is in Israel, but the inspectors are in Iran," he underlined. “They (Israelis) kill, we are sanctioned, we are punished.”
“Israel has murdered savagely over 70,000 innocents in Gaza, but Iran, while behind the table of negotiation, was bombed.”
Pezeshkian reiterated Iran’s claim that it was not pursuing nuclear weapons. However, he said Iran had an “inherent” right to peaceful nuclear technology.
“We will not bow our head and give up the right that is inherently ours,” said the Iranian president. “We say it clearly: No nuclear weapons and no limitations to peaceful nuclear technology,” he added.
'We are not terrorists, we are victims of terrorism'
He also rejected US President Donald Trump’s characterisation of Iran as a sponsor of terrorism.
“Yesterday, Trump said we are terrorists. We are not terrorists; we are victims of terrorism,” Pezeshkian told the General Assembly, referring to Trump’s address a day earlier in which the US president described Iran as the “number one sponsor of terror.”
Pezeshkian said Iran’s leader had been killed “without any justification,” referring to the US-Israeli military attacks against Iran that began earlier this year.
He also accused Israel of targeting neighbourhoods across Iranian cities and provinces and carrying out assassinations, describing such actions as “true terrorist” behaviour.
“The people of Iran have been defending their country for the past seven months,” Pezeshkian said.
In the first part of his speech, the Iranian leader held up an image of the Islamic Republic's late supreme leader Ali Khamenei, who was killed in an airstrike on his compound in Tehran on the first day of the US-Israeli assault on Iran.
He also held up images of children killed in a strike on a school.
A UN fact-finding mission on Iran said earlier this month that it had reasonable grounds to believe that the US was behind two military strikes on a school and a sports facility in Iran, and that these constituted war crimes.
Hormuz cannot be used for passage of weapons used against Iran: Pezeshkian
Pezeshkian said Iran wants to have "strong neighbours" near the Strait of Hormuz, but cannot allow those who seek to impose "insecurity" on Iranians to have access to it.
"We cannot let some have free access and gain their interest from a waterway, while at the same time using that waterway to impose their aggressions upon us, to impose insecurity upon us, to forbid us access to our own waterways," he stated.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian: Iran does not see her neighbors as security rivals — we want to have strong neighbors. In the waters of the Strait of Hormuz, we do not want to impose insecurity. We cannot let some have free access and gain their interest from a waterway,… pic.twitter.com/q9YcnRREJw
"It cannot be the case that everyone benefits from the Strait of Hormuz while we are denied access to shipping through this waterway. The permanent deployment of hostile fleets and the expansion of the war will not lead to peace," Pezeshkian said.
Iran needs nuclear energy, not a nuclear bomb, Pezeshkian says
Pezeshkian said Iran needs peaceful nuclear energy, not a nuclear bomb.
"For our country, peaceful nuclear technology is part of our inherent progress," he said, adding, "Iran does not accept nuclear technology to be at the exclusive disposal of some, of a handful."
"We say it clearly: no nuclear weapons and no limitations to peaceful nuclear technology," he said.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian: We will not bow our head and give up the right that is inherently ours. We say it clearly: no nuclear weapons, and no limitations to peaceful nuclear technology. pic.twitter.com/YsMSrKNuw0
Pezeshkian ⁠addressed the 193-member General Assembly a day after US President Donald Trump spoke. ​Trump used his speech on Tuesday to ​make ⁠the case for his war on Iran, arguing he has prevented Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and ⁠warning ​that he could "annihilate the Islamic ​Republic" if no deal is reached to end the conflict.
After agreeing to a Pakistan-mediated ceasefire in April, the US and Iran signed the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding in June, which gave the two sides 60 days to discuss a long-term agreement.
But the two sides soon engaged in retaliatory attacks, and the US reimposed its military blockade of Iranian ports while Tehran closed the Strait of Hormuz.

Rebecca Black will join Duff as a special guest for all European dates, while Dashboard Confessional will support select U.S. shows. Tegan and Sara will also appear on the final U.S. leg.
Duff originally launched The Lucky Me Tour in the United States in June 2026, marking her first global headlining trek in almost 20 years. She is scheduled to perform in New Zealand and Australia through October before continuing with Canadian and Mexican dates in early 2027.
Artist presales for the newly announced European and Latin American dates begin September 29, while U.S. presales start September 28. General ticket sales begin October 2.

title: Ian McEwan announces first nonfiction book  Between Books
description: Between Books will be published on May 25  2027  one year after McEwen s last book
content:
Between Books will be published on May 25, 2027, one year after McEwen's last book
Ian McEwan is moving into nonfiction with Between Books, his first work in the genre, as his acclaimed novel Atonement marks its 25th anniversary.
Publisher Alfred A. Knopf announced the new book on Wednesday, September 23, revealing that Between Books will be published on May 25, 2027. McEwan described the project as beginning as a collection of unrelated pieces before developing into what he hopes will be an “emotional and intellectual journey”.
The announcement also comes exactly one year after the publication of McEwan’s latest novel, What We Can Know. Released in September 2025, the book became a national bestseller and was named among The New York Times Book Review’s 100 Notable Books of 2025.
McEwan has previously spoken about his approach to writing, saying he tends to follow his own interests rather than focus on what he believes readers might currently want. He recalled taking a similar approach with Atonement, which he initially thought might appeal mainly to other writers because of its focus on the literary imagination.
Published in 2001, Atonement went on to become one of McEwan’s best-known works. The novel was shortlisted for the Booker Prize and received several major literary awards, including the Los Angeles Times Book Prize for Fiction and the National Book Critics Circle Award.
The novel was adapted into a 2007 film starring Keira Knightley, James McAvoy and Saoirse Ronan, bringing McEwan’s story to an even wider audience.
Between Books is now available for preorder ahead of its May 25, 2027 release.

title: Hina Dilpazeer on acting and the pitfalls of chasing stardom
description: Veteran actor opens up about surrendering the ego for a role and the shortcomings of Pakistani television
content:
Veteran actor opens up about surrendering the ego for a role and the shortcomings of Pakistani television
Veteran actor Hina Dilpazeer offered a candid take on acting and the state of Pakistani television in an interview with Vasay Chaudhry.
She said acting required complete surrender of the ego. “True acting requires breaking one's ego and completely shedding the self to step into another's life,” she said, describing the profession as a “sea of fire” that newcomers must be prepared to dive into fully if they want to succeed.
She added that she gives her full effort to every role, regardless of genre, noting that a serious performance can bring “a flood of grief”, while a comic one can help audiences forget their sorrows.
Dilpazeer also recalled the most difficult performance of her career, which came just days after her father’s death, when she had to return to the set of a comedy.
“Maintaining the character and the illusion of happiness for the audience while grieving,” she said, “was the most difficult acting task she has ever faced.”
The actor also criticised current trends in Pakistani television, arguing that many dramas are being let down by weak writing.
“Many dramas today lack strong, well-written stories. That television's reach makes it powerful enough to shape public sentiment, and that filling it with weak filler content wastes both time and money.”
She was equally critical of what she described as the industry’s “blind race” towards stardom, warning that chasing superstar status can become a “black hole” for a serious acting career, pulling actors away from the depth their work requires.

title: PTI s Gohar calls for dialogue as party decries arrests  raids in K P
description: CM Afridi vows peaceful protests will continue  says remove protest right from Constitution if you oppose it
content:
CM Afridi vows peaceful protests will continue, says remove protest right from Constitution if you oppose it
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Wednesday criticised what he described as political victimisation of the party leadership and the family of PTI founder Imran Khan, calling for dialogue to resolve the country’s prevailing political crisis.
In August, the PTI announced that it would march to Islamabad on September 27 to stress for the release of party founder Imran Khan. The party has been preparing a central convoy from Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), with caravans from other parts of the country expected to join before proceeding towards the federal capital. The federal government has warned the party against going ahead with the march.
Speaking to the media during a visit to Lahore to express solidarity with Imran’s arrested sisters, Gohar lamented the arrest of the founder's family members, saying that four members of the PTI founder’s family and eight members of the National Assembly were currently in custody, while some provincial ministers remained missing.
Read: Warrants out for arrest of PTI's Gandapur
He also called for the disputes to be resolved through political means while keeping the doors for negotiations open. “Political disputes can only be settled through political means. In politics, no word is final,” he added.
Gohar said the PTI leadership was aware of the stakeholders who could be engaged to address the political crises and stressed that political disputes should be resolved through dialogue. He also revealed that Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party (PKMAP) Chairman Mehmood Khan Achakzai, Majlis Wahdat-e-Muslimeen (MWM) Chief Allama Raja Nasir Abbas Jafri and PTI leaders were prepared to engage in talks to end the deadlock.
Moreover, the PTI chairman expressed disdain that the party’s public offers of negotiations were not met with grace by the federal government.
“There is currently no meaningful dialogue,” Barrister Gohar stated, adding that the government did not demonstrate seriousness about resolving the political impasse.
He said political disputes should not be regarded as permanently settled and warned that the consequences of attempts to weaken political opposition were known to all. The PTI leader also said that the situation in K-P amounted to “unannounced Governor’s Rule.”
“The federal government has effectively assumed control of the provincial apparatus despite the PTI holding a democratic mandate,” Gohar asserted, warning that such encroachment on provincial authority could set a dangerous precedent for the country’s democratic system.
Gohar also rejected the allegations that his party plans to attack state institutions in Islamabad during the planned September 27 march. He said PTI aims to maintain peace during the demonstrations.
Meanwhile, PTI condemned what it described as raids on the residences of two provincial ministers in K-P and the arrest of a party-backed Member of the National Assembly (MNA) from South Waziristan.
According to a statement issued by PTI’s Central Media Department on X, a raid was conducted at the residence of K-P Minister for Excise, Taxation and Narcotics Control Syed Fakhar Jehan last night.
The party said that, in a separate operation, a heavy contingent of police raided the residence of K-P Irrigation Minister Riaz Khan in Bannu.
پریس ریلیز پاکستان تحریک انصاف 23 ستمبر 2026 پی ٹی آئی خیبر پختونخوا کے وزراء کے گھروں پر چھاپوں اور ایم این اے زبیر خان وزیر کی گرفتاری کی مذمت کرتی ہے پاکستان تحریک انصاف خیبر پختونخوا کے دو بیٹھے ہوئے صوبائی وزراء کے رہائش گاہوں پر کیے گئے چھاپوں اور صوبے سے تعلق رکھنے والے…
PTI also alleged that the residence of MNA Muhammad Zubair Khan Wazir, elected from NA-42 (South Waziristan Upper and Lower), was “besieged for several hours by unidentified individuals” and “family members present in the home were taken hostage”. The statement further claimed that a heavy police contingent later raided Wazir’s home and arrested him after an exchange of fire.
PTI called the incidents a grave assault on democratic traditions, parliamentary privilege and the rule of law.
“Targeting sitting ministers and an MNA, and holding their families hostage, is unacceptable,” the party said in its statement.
The party demanded that the police officers allegedly involved in the raids be identified and action taken against them. It also called on the K-P government to constitute a comprehensive and impartial inquiry to establish the facts surrounding the incidents, and determine responsibility to ascertain justice.
PTI further urged the authorities to ensure the safety, dignity and wellbeing of the affected families and appealed to state institutions to act in accordance with the Constitution and law. It also asked the authorities to “refrain from the use of force and intimidation against elected representatives and their families”.
The allegations made by PTI could not be independently verified from the statement.
CM Afridi vows to continue peaceful protests
Separately, K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi said protest was the constitutional and legal right of every citizen and vowed to exercise that right peacefully.
“The Constitution itself allows us to hold peaceful protests, and we will exercise this right at all costs. If someone says we should not protest, let them remove this provision from the Constitution. If it is no longer there, we will not hold peaceful protests,” he said while addressing a meeting of the provincial cabinet.
He said that they would continue to protest peacefully as long as the provision remained part of the Constitution.
The chief minister claimed that “goons in plain clothes” had been targeting the party workers, office-bearers and elected representatives across the province over the past few days.
وزیراعلیٰ خیبر پختونخوا محمد سہیل خان آفریدی کا صوبائی کابینہ اجلاس سے خطاب! گزشتہ تین چار دنوں سے سادہ کپڑوں میں ملبوس غنڈا گرد ہمارے کارکنوں، تنظیمی عہدیداروں اور منتخب نمائندوں کو نشانہ بنا رہے ہیں، مواصلات و تعمیرات کے وزیر شکیل خان پر قاتلانہ حملہ اور انہیں اغوا کرنے کی… pic.twitter.com/AygGmyKVdq
Afridi said that Shakil Ahmad Khan, the provincial minister for communications and works, recently survived an attempted abduction and murder bid.
He further claimed that “goons dressed in plain clothes” also approached the residence of Irrigation Minister Riaz Khan yesterday, while similar incidents of intimidation against other party members and representatives were also reported from Dera Ismail Khan and other districts.
The chief minister alleged that MNA Fazal Muhammad Khan had been abducted in Mardan and unidentified people had raided the residence of K-P Minister for Excise, Taxation and Narcotics Control Syed Fakhar Jehan.
Read more: Rule of law, supremacy of Constitution to prevail during PTI long march to Islamabad: Gohar
He said targeting PTI elected representatives and provincial ministers was “absolutely unacceptable”.
“If provincial cabinet ministers are not safe from these goons, we can only imagine what happens [to the people] in the rest of the country,” he argued.
CM Afridi further said the aforementioned actions highlighted that these people were “afraid of people’s power”; otherwise, no sensible person would go to such lengths.
He urged government officials, police officers, deputy commissioners and district police officers not to be intimidated by goons approaching them in plain clothes.
“If the provincial government is not asking you to do anything wrong, do not follow illegal orders issued by any other institution or department,” he told provincial government officials during the speech.
The chief minister also voiced concern over what he described as statements by federal officials regarding K-P.
He lamented that Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political and Public Affairs in Pakistan Rana Sanaullah described the people of K-P as terrorists and Punjab CM Maryam Nawaz expressed more fear from neighbouring provinces compared to India.
According to the CM, roads to and from K-P were being closed while the rest of the country enjoyed uninterrupted movement. He said that those behind any attempt to divide Pakistan or separate K-P from the rest of the country should be sent a clear message that “Pakistan belongs to all of us”.
“We were Pakistanis, we are Pakistanis and, God willing, we will remain Pakistanis,” he said.
Also Read : Do not 'desire' any confrontation, long march to remain peaceful: CM Afridi
The chief minister also defended the PTI’s right to protest, saying that peaceful protest was a constitutional and legal right.
“Wherever we go, we are not being heard,” he said, adding, “In such a situation, the Constitution allows us to hold peaceful protests, and we will continue this protest at all costs.”
He said PTI would continue its peaceful struggle as long as the Constitution guaranteed the right to peaceful protest.
Addressing the people of KP and the rest of Pakistan, CM Afridi urged them not to be afraid and called for continued efforts for their rights and what he termed “real freedom”.

The singer shared the clip through his secret TikTok account, @thelastofthebugs, which has previously been used to share cryptic updates and snippets connected to his music. The new video features woodland scenery, a campfire and Kahan playing guitar, accompanied by a previously unheard song.

Kahan also shared lyrics in August that are now believed by fans to be connected to the project. The lyrics begin with “I carry you on” and include the line “I draw you out”, leading fans to connect the unreleased song to a track titled Draw You Out.

Fans have also pointed to Kahan's repeated use of insect imagery through his @thelastofthebugs account as another possible clue.
Kahan's potential involvement in the film has been rumoured for months. He previously appeared to reference The Hunger Games while performing in Texas and later acknowledged during the 2026 Emmys that he had been working on a film-related project, although he did not name the project.
While neither Kahan nor the Hunger Games team has officially confirmed that Draw You Out is his song, the latest video has given fans another major clue that the singer could be part of the Sunrise on the Reaping soundtrack.

The accuser, whose name was redacted from the charging documents, said that after about a week of talking, Peters ordered her an Uber ​to his family's residence ​in Chatham on May ⁠23, 2025.

The girl told police she became increasingly intoxicated. In a clip from Peters’ livestream that police reviewed, the girl at one point ⁠said, "wait ​I’m so drunk" before the two kissed, according to ​the police report.

title: Memoir by Princess Diana s brother flies off the shelves
description: Charles Spencer s book about his sister released on Tuesday
content:
Charles Spencer's book about his sister released on Tuesday
British shoppers snapped up copies of a memoir by the ​brother of Princess Diana on Tuesday after their interest was piqued by incendiary allegations about her troubled marriage to ‌the now-king, including the claim he was "giddily elated" at her death.
Charles Spencer, who delivered a much-lauded eulogy at the 1997 funeral of his sister, has sparked global headlines with a book that accuses the then-Prince of Wales of sounding like a "lottery winner" in the hours after her death.
Buckingham Palace ​hit back immediately, saying the king was "mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, judgment and memory", ​as it sought to prevent the king from being dragged back into one of the royal ⁠family's most damaging periods.
Charles Spencer, the brother of Britain's late Princess Diana is interviewed by journalist Laura Kuenssberg, as part of the documentary "Princess Diana: My Sister’s Story" at the Althorp Estate, Britain, in this handout picture released on September 19, 2026. PHOTO: Reuters
The book, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister", was released in Britain on Tuesday, where allegations contained ​in pre-released excerpts have dominated newspaper front pages for almost a week, helping send it straight to the top of the ​bestseller list on Amazon.
Outside a central London bookshop, Chris Imafidon, 71, said he bought a copy after being intrigued by some of the allegations, which he did not see as credible. "There's a desire for one to be protective of your sister," he said.
For others, Diana, one of the most ​photographed women in the world, remains an icon, and the appeal of the "People's Princess" endures 29 years after she died ​in a car crash. "I just hope to hear more about her life with her family, growing up, and with her children," said Mary Scheible, ‌69.
Spencer ⁠said he wrote the book to set the record straight and because it was his duty "as an eyewitness to history".
He said in the book that he spoke to Charles shortly after Diana's death was confirmed. "Unlike my other callers, who were stunned, barely able to articulate their condolences and offers of help, he sounded giddily elated – like a lottery winner, I remember thinking at the ​time," he wrote, according to pre-released ​excerpts.
Charles Spencer, the brother of Britain's late Princess Diana is interviewed by journalist Laura Kuenssberg, as part of the documentary "Princess Diana: My Sister’s Story" at the Althorp Estate, Britain, in this handout picture released on September 19, 2026. PHOTO: Reuters
"Looking back now, I ⁠suspect the prince's first reaction must have been to think more of how this event might free him to marry the woman he loved, rather than appreciating the loss of one he ​did not."
Diana was just 20 when she married the heir-to-the-throne Prince Charles in 1981, a ​fairytale wedding watched ⁠around the world. They had two children, William and Harry, but the relationship soon soured and, following years of briefing against one another in the media, they finally divorced in 1996.
That was a year after Diana told the BBC that "there were three of us in ⁠this marriage, ​so it was a bit crowded" in reference to Charles' relationship with ​Camilla Parker Bowles, whom he married in 2005.
Spencer describes his book as an intimate, loving and honest portrait of his sister, who he said became a ​global icon overnight.

The album re-entered the UK Official Physical Albums chart at No. 77 and the Official Albums Sales chart at No. 79
Harry Styles’ latest album Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally. has returned to the UK bestseller charts following the announcement of additional dates for his Together, Together tour.
The album re-entered the Official Physical Albums chart at No. 77 and the Official Albums Sales chart at No. 79 this week. It also climbed on the Official Albums Streaming chart, rising from No. 38 to No. 19, while the Official Albums chart saw it jump from No. 44 to No. 27.
The renewed chart activity comes after Styles announced a major expansion of his Together, Together tour earlier this month. The additional 25 dates will take the singer across North America, Europe and the UK in 2027, beginning with two shows at State Farm Stadium in Phoenix, Arizona, in April.
The expanded tour will also include stops in cities such as Dallas, Los Angeles, Toronto and Atlanta before Styles heads to Europe for performances in Berlin, Paris, Madrid, Rome and Dublin. The tour will conclude with three shows at Wembley Stadium in London beginning August 25, 2027.
Styles’ current tour began in May 2026, with the singer opting for a more concentrated run of shows across a smaller number of cities. The initial schedule included 67 performances across Amsterdam, London, São Paulo, Mexico City, New York, Melbourne and Sydney. His current run includes 30 nights at New York’s Madison Square Garden.
Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally. originally debuted at No. 1 across all four UK album charts on which it has appeared. The album has now spent around six months on both the Official Physical Albums and Official Albums Sales charts.
The album has also remained one of the biggest releases of 2026 in the UK. Official Charts previously reported that the record had earned more than 183,000 chart units during its opening week, giving Styles his biggest opening week to date. It was also ranked as the second-biggest album of 2026 so far in the publication’s latest update.
Styles’ latest album has continued to perform particularly strongly on vinyl. Official Charts reported that Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally. had sold more than 75,000 vinyl copies by the end of the second quarter, making it the biggest-selling vinyl album of 2026 in the UK at that point.
Meanwhile, “American Girls”, the album’s second official single, remains on the UK charts. The song currently sits at No. 55 on the Official Streaming chart and No. 76 on the Official Singles chart, while Styles’ debut solo single “Sign of the Times” ranks higher at Nos. 21 and 52 on the respective charts.
The return of Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally. to the UK’s physical and sales charts comes as Styles prepares for another extensive run of live shows, giving the album a renewed presence several months after its release.

Ghana face a stern test against the hosts in Bouake on Thursday
High-profile coaches Herve Renard and Carlos Queiroz face each other on Thursday when Ivory Coast host Ghana as 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying kicks off.
This blockbuster west African showdown in Bouake between former champions is the highlight of the 24 matchday one fixtures.
Ghana have won the AFCON four times, but not since 1982. Renard led Ivory Coast to the second of their three African titles 11 years ago.
Renard also won the AFCON with Zambia in 2012 -- one of the biggest shocks in the history of the 69-year competition.
Queiroz came closest to AFCON glory in 2022 with Egypt, who lost the final after a penalty shootout against Senegal. He watched from the stand due to a suspension.
After working with clubs in France, England and Vietnam, Renard has concentrated on national teams, also coaching Angola, Morocco, Saudi Arabia twice, France women and Tunisia.
He took charge of Tunisia at the 2026 World Cup after fellow Frenchman Sabri Lamouchi was axed following a 5-1 hiding from Sweden. They also lost to Japan and the Netherlands under Renard.
Ivory Coast did not renew the contract of 2024 AFCON-winning coach Emerse Fae after a last-32 World Cup loss to Norway, paving the way for Renard to return.
The Queiroz CV includes managing Real Madrid and he has been assistant twice to former Manchester United boss Alex Ferguson.
He took charge of Ghana just before the 2026 World Cup, transforming a struggling team into a combative, defensively strong unit. They were the only team to hold England goalless.
That defensive resilience is set to be tested again in the Ivory Coast, with the strike force options of Renard including Yan Diomande of Real Madrid and Bazoumana Toure of Newcastle.
A blow for Ghana was the withdrawal of injured Mohammed Kudus. The inventive Tottenham Hotspur midfielder also missed the World Cup.
Only four of the 10 coaches who began the 2026 World Cup in charge of African qualifiers remain -- Queiroz, Hossam Hassan of Egypt, Mohamed Ouahbi of Morocco and Sebastien Desabre of the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Those who quit, retired or were fired include Renard, Lamouchi, Fae, Vladimir Petkovic of Algeria, Hugo Broos of South Africa, Pape Thiaw of Senegal and Bubista of Cape Verde.
Patrick Vieira, a 1998 World Cup winner with France, has replaced Thiaw. His debut for Senegal has suffered a setback due to the lack of an international-standard stadium in the country.
Instead of hosting Mozambique on Friday, they will travel to the southern Africa nation for a match that may prove more challenging than the ranking gap of 85 places suggests.
Vieira must do without two of the four stars who have been the core of the team. Goalkeeper Edouard Mendy has retired and striker Sadio Mane is injured.
Centre-back Kalidou Koulibaly and midfielder Idrissa Gueye remain for Senegal, who beat Morocco in the 2026 final only to be stripped of the title.
Most of the Senegalese team temporarily left the field to protest an added-time penalty awarded to Morocco, which was missed after a lengthy delay.
Senegal have appealed the decision to declare Morocco champions. It will be heard by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on October 8.
Pitso Mosimane gets a second chance as coach of South Africa after being sacked at midnight following a 2014 World Cup qualifying draw with Ethiopia.
He has since excelled at club level, winning the CAF Champions League with Mamelodi Sundowns of South Africa and twice with Al Ahly of Egypt.
South Africa will lack injured defenders Mbekezeli Mbokazi and Khuliso Mudau on Saturday in Soweto against Guinea, who boast a prolific scorer in Serhou Guirassy from Borussia Dortmund.
Bubista worked wonders with Cape Verde at the World Cup. They held eventual champions Spain and took Argentina to extra time.
He has joined Moroccan club Renaissance Berkane and assistant Humberto Bettencourt takes over. Cape Verde are away to Mali on Friday.

Thailand's Puripol Boonson will look to prove himself as Asia's pre-eminent sprinter when he bids for the 100 metres gold medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Games, three years after taking silver at Hangzhou.
Boonson became ‌Southeast Asia's first runner to break the 10-second barrier when he ran 9.94 on home soil in December and enters the Japan meet in decent form after posting 9.99 seconds at a race in the Czech Republic last month.
He made a splash at Hangzhou as a 17-year-old runner-up behind Xie Zhenyi, and the veteran ⁠Chinese sprinter may again be Puripol's biggest threat at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium this week.
Boonson is a hero in his home nation after winning the 100-200m double at the 2025 Southeast Asian Games, and an Asian Games gold would send Thai athletics fans into a frenzy.
Home fans will be focused on Olympic javelin champion Haruka Kitaguchi and her rivalry with China's 18-year-old sensation Yan Ziyi.
Kitaguchi became the first Japanese woman to win an Olympic field event at the Paris Games but Yan has taken the athletics world ‌by ⁠storm this year.
She produced the second-longest throw in history (71.74) on home soil in Xiamen in May on the day after her 18th birthday, one of five Diamond League titles for the year.
Czech Barbora Spotakova's world record of 72.28 may be at Yan's mercy.
In the men’s high jump, Bahrain's ⁠former Olympic champion Mutaz Barshim will defend his title and bid for a fourth Asian Games gold, having also won at Hangzhou, Incheon 2014 and Guangzhou in 2010.
Barshim's compatriot Winfred Yavi, Olympic ⁠champion in the women’s 3,000m steeplechase, will aim for a third consecutive Asian Games gold in the event.
The Kenya-born Yavi will also take on the women’s 5000m and 10,000m, ⁠targeting a middle distance hat-trick.
China's Feng Bin, the Olympic runner-up at Paris, heads into the women's discus as favourite after claiming her first Diamond League title in Brussels this month with a throw of 67.46m.

The "Homewrecker" singer also discussed his struggles at school, revealing that his focus on music affected his studies.
After his song “Caroline” gained traction online, several record labels approached him. Sombr ultimately signed with Warner Records, which he described as the “hungriest” label pursuing him, and left school to pursue music full-time.

title: Antonelli eyeing third straight win
description: He looks to extend his 81 point Formula One championship lead
content:
He looks to extend his 81-point Formula One championship lead
Kimi Antonelli has another opportunity to extend his runaway lead in this year's Formula One title race as he heads into this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, the first in a potentially decisive triple-header, bidding for a third straight win.
Buoyed by eight victories this year and a lead of 81 points ahead of Mercedes team-mate George Russell, the 20-year-old Italian has been irrepressible as he seeks to become Italy's first champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953.
But he and Mercedes know they have to temper his enthusiasm on a fast street track with a reputation for creating chaos.
"Recent results have been encouraging, but they don't guarantee anything," said Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff.
"Baku will expose any weakness very quickly. We have to approach the weekend with humility, do the basics well and earn every point."
Having won in Italy and Spain, Antonelli will be seeking a hat-trick which could tighten his grip on the title.
But he admitted after winning in Madrid that he was lucky with a virtual safety car which denied McLaren's Lando Norris victory.
"The last two races brought us good results," said Wolff.
"But they don't change our assessment of where we stand... There are several teams capable of fighting at the front.
"This will be a demanding period for the team, both in the factory and track-side, with little time to reset between the races.
"So, preparation, reliability and operational execution become even more important.
"These are the moments when our championship position can be strengthened or lost."
The high-speed Baku street track can deliver unexpected incidents and results while the following events in Malaysia and Singapore will be physically draining for everyone, with three grands prix in as many weeks.
The Baku race this year takes place on Saturday because Azerbaijan is marking its Remembrance Day on Sunday.
The race is the 10th in Baku, which joined the calendar in 2016 initially as the European Grand Prix, but was cancelled in 2020 due to the Covid pandemic.
While Mercedes hope to set the pace again, McLaren, Ferrari and Red Bull will all have reason to be confident.
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc has a brilliant qualifying record in Azerbaijan, only having his run of four consecutive pole positions in the race ended last year when he crashed in final qualifying and failed to set a time.
The Monegasque has never won the race, though.
His team-mate, seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton, has ruled himself out of the title race, sitting third in the drivers' standings but 101 points adrift.
However, the former Baku winner may be a threat if he and Ferrari rediscover their form.
Max Verstappen will be hunting his third Baku triumph for Red Bull, who have enjoyed five wins on the circuit, and Oscar Piastri of McLaren his second.
"It's a challenging and technical street circuit," said Verstappen, who last week beat 100 amateur racers to win a karting challenge at Silverstone.
"But it is really exciting to drive and I have good memories here."
He also welcomed back team-mate Isack Hadjar who has recovered from a broken wrist and will race again this weekend with his deputy Liam Lawson returning to Racing Bulls.

title: Zach Cregger reveals  Resident Evil  ending was changed using  Plan B  footage
description: Zach Cregger reveals  Resident Evil   s  ending was changed after test audiences saw original version
content:
Zach Cregger reveals 'Resident Evil’s' ending was changed after test audiences saw original version
Zach Cregger has revealed that the theatrical ending of Resident Evil was changed after test audiences felt the original conclusion left the story with little reason to continue.
Cregger’s Resident Evil follows Bryan, a medical courier trapped in Raccoon City during an outbreak. Rather than directly adapting one of the games, the film features a new protagonist while incorporating familiar locations, monsters and mechanics from the franchise.
The director told Collider that the ending audiences see was effectively his “Plan B”, created using contingency footage from filming.
In the film, the T-Virus begins taking control of Bryan’s body as he attempts to find a cure. His focus remains on a syringe containing the treatment, even as the virus alters his senses and transforms him.
The syringe eventually falls from the upper levels of Raccoon City General Hospital, but Cregger said the original version of the sequence would have removed that possibility much earlier.
“Originally in the script, that scientist pulls the needle out and as soon as Austin grabs the woman’s face, he drops it, it shatters, and then the rest of the movie is just Austin killing the scientists.”
According to Cregger, test audiences responded to the original ending as though the story had already finished. With the cure destroyed, there was no longer a possibility of Bryan saving himself.
Cregger had anticipated that the sequence might need to change and filmed an additional shot showing the scientist putting the syringe in his pocket.
“I shot that shot of the scientist putting the needle in his pocket just cuz I had a feeling. I was like, I feel like I’m going to need that. So then we were able to build a new sequence of the end.
“Thank God I shot for this as a contingency plan. It was like my Plan B,” Cregger said.
The additional footage allowed the filmmakers to keep the cure available for longer before the final sequence. Cregger also said the original ending is unlikely to be released, describing the existing film as the “Cregger cut”.

Tina Knowles has opened up about a frightening onstage incident involving her daughter, Beyoncé, during the singer’s Cowboy Carter Tour, describing the experience as a terrifying moment for their family.
Speaking on ITV’s This Morning on Tuesday, September 22, the 72-year-old fashion designer recalled the June 2025 Houston concert, where Beyoncé’s suspended car prop tilted mid-air during her performance of ‘16 Carriages’.
Knowles was watching from a platform when the incident unfolded and had to push through the crowd to reach her daughter.
"It was terrible. I was on a platform, so I had to fight my way through the crowd because I knew what was going on but other people didn't," she said.
Knowles explained that Beyoncé continued singing as the vehicle tilted, holding on to prevent herself from falling.
"Because she's a professional, she kept singing through it, and the car was turning...she's holding that car up. And she literally was holding herself in it cause she would have fallen out," she recalled.
Beyoncé’s company, Parkwood Entertainment, previously described the incident as a "technical mishap".
The singer was quickly lowered to the stage and was not injured. The concert continued without further incident.
Beyoncé was safely lowered after her flying car unexpectedly tilted mid-air at the Cowboy Carter tour in Houston while performing ‘16 CARRIAGES.’ pic.twitter.com/FOgl9DIfFR

Recalling the moment she reached Beyoncé, Knowles said her daughter reassured her: "Momma, I got a show to do" and told her to "let go".
"I was so happy that turned out that way; it could have been bad," Knowles concluded.

title: Lt Gen  retd  Nauman Mahmood appointed first secretary general of Makkah pact
description: The secretary general will lead the General Secretariat of the alliance being established in Riyadh  MoFA
content:
The secretary general will lead the general secretariat of the alliance being established in Riyadh: FO
The government on Wednesday appointed Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood, Hilal-e-Imtiaz (Military), as the first Secretary General of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
In a statement, the Foreign Office said Lt Gen Mahmood would lead the general secretariat of the alliance, which is being established in Riyadh.
The appointment marks the formal establishment of the MJDA's secretariat and its administrative leadership, the statement added.
The government had earlier announced the MJDA as a framework for enhanced defence cooperation among the participating countries.
🔊PR No.2️⃣5️⃣9️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Press Release 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/kzzhEa61oo
The appointment came less than a month after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agreed in Istanbul to establish a permanent secretariat for their joint defence pact in Riyadh, with Pakistan set to provide its first secretary general.
The decision was taken at the inaugural meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee, held under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which brought together the foreign and defence ministers and military chiefs of the three countries in Istanbul on August 31.
Under the arrangement agreed in Istanbul, the secretary general would head the alliance's General Secretariat, based in the Saudi capital and tasked with overseeing implementation of the agreement, coordinating joint activities among the three militaries and supporting expanded defence-industrial cooperation. Pakistan was designated to hold the post for an initial three-year term.
Read: Riyadh to host Makkah alliance secretariat
In August, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed a landmark "Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement" , declaring that "any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both". On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed "Makkah Joint Defence Agreement", a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
Significance of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
The MJDA was the latest step in longstanding military and strategic cooperation between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. Signed in Makkah, the pact established a framework for collective deterrence and stipulated that an armed attack on any one of the three countries would be considered an attack on all three, while providing for wider cooperation across defence.
The agreement followed nearly a year of negotiations and came amid heightened instability across the Middle East. Turkiye and Pakistan had sought closer regional security cooperation, while Saudi Arabia had faced growing security concerns as conflicts spread across the region, threatening its territory, energy infrastructure and ambitious economic development plans.
Read More: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye sign joint defence pact in Makkah
For Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the trilateral pact is built on their Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed in September 2025. That agreement stated that “any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both” and committed the two sides to strengthening defence cooperation and joint deterrence.
The three countries already had extensive military links. Pakistan had provided training and technical assistance to Saudi forces for decades, while Islamabad and Ankara had maintained close defence ties through military training, naval cooperation and defence equipment. In 2023, Saudi Arabia agreed to purchase Turkish drones in what Ankara described as its largest defence export contract.
Pakistan had also expanded its military and security cooperation with the kingdom, deploying about 8,000 troops, fighter jets, drones and an air-defence system to Saudi Arabia, according to Reuters . Pakistan deploys troops to Saudi air base under defence pact . Islamabad had also been pursuing wider security and economic ties in the Gulf, including negotiations with Kuwait on an expanded cooperation pact linked to energy and investment. Pakistan-Kuwait agree to boost cooperation across key sectors
The signing in Makkah, Islam’s holiest city, added symbolic weight to an agreement that brought together three countries with significant military and strategic capabilities. It also came as Pakistan sought to avoid becoming directly involved in the Iran conflict, instead pursuing diplomatic efforts to mediate, while strengthening its broader regional security partnerships.

PewDiePie ends his family vlogs, saying son Bjorn deserves privacy as he grows up
Felix ‘PewDiePie’ Kjellberg has ended his family-focused YouTube vlogs, saying he wants to give his son Bjorn more privacy as he grows up.
The Swedish creator announced in May that the monthly vlogs documenting his family life in Japan would end in September.
In a video on September 22, Kjellberg explained that the decision was influenced by Bjorn getting older and the family’s desire not to continue documenting his childhood indefinitely.
“The reason we’re stopping is because we didn’t want to go on forever. I also felt that, with Bjorn growing up, it’s a good time to stop,” Kjellberg said.
Although the family vlogs are ending, PewDiePie confirmed that he will continue making videos. He said he enjoys creating content and maintaining a connection with his community, while also discussing the difficulties that come with being a well-known creator.
“I love making videos, and I’m going to keep making videos obviously, and I love sharing videos, and I love the community aspect, but I do not love being famous. I actually kind of hate it. I hate that I can’t go to certain kinds of places, and I always have to be mindful of other people staring, sneaking photos, and following you around.”
Kjellberg said protecting Bjorn’s privacy was an important factor in ending the vlogs.
“For Bjorn, I want him to make his own choices. He deserves his own privacy, and that’s why we felt like now is a good time to stop.”
Kjellberg and his wife, Marza, will still share some aspects of their family life, but he said they will be more “intentional” about what they post. The couple will also continue their monthly newsletter.
PewDiePie previously said the vlogs had put pressure on Bjorn’s “appearance online” and that the family had considered whether to continue them.
