title: Saba Faisal s divorce remarks spark debate among Pakistani celebrities
description: Hira Khan  Zoya Nasir and others weigh in as stars and fans debate shifting attitudes towards divorce
content:
Hira Khan, Zoya Nasir and others weigh in as stars and fans debate shifting attitudes towards divorce
Pakistani celebrities have voiced differing views on actor Saba Faisal’s remarks about divorce, arguing that the end of a marriage should not simply be framed as something being “normalised”, but also recognised as a difficult experience that people navigate in different ways.
Faisal recently came under fire after appearing in an interview , where she spoke about what she described as the changing attitudes towards divorce in society.
Her comments have since sparked a debate among celebrities and fans over whether greater acceptance of divorce reflects a loss of sensitivity towards marriage or a changing willingness to acknowledge difficult circumstances.
“Before, when someone used to get divorced, there used to be a ‘ sog ’ happening for months,” she said, referring to the period of mourning and grief that would traditionally follow a divorce.
“Dads couldn’t do anything, but now when we find out girls have got divorced, it’s mentioned casually over a phone call. ‘Oh, I got divorced many months back,’ when someone asks about their husband. After that, I went abroad and tried to figure stuff out,” she added.
Her remarks prompted a strong reaction online, with celebrities including Hira Khan and Zoya Nasir speaking out, while fans also joined the discussion.
Taking to her Instagram story, Khan responded to Faisal’s comments, writing, “It’s better to go through this than to be carried through a grave. I said it once before and will again. She needs help.”
Khan went on to write, “In a country — in fact, subcontinent — where women are burned to death every day because they chose to remain in marriages they should have been allowed to leave alive; where infants are raped and tortured and women and children aren’t even safe in their graves, it is astonishing that there are still people on social media who find endless reasons to police, shame and condemn women.”
She further clarified, “No one celebrates divorce,” adding that “even Allah gave women the right to it.”
Khan also wrote, “I’m half your age, but I understand this much. Perhaps I was raised to understand that a woman’s dignity, safety and right to choose matter.”
She continued, “And honestly, it isn’t your fault that you weren’t.”
The exchange escalated when Faisal’s daughter, Sadia Faisal, appeared to respond to Khan, writing, “I wish I could see this so-called actress someday.”
Khan was not the only celebrity to challenge Faisal’s remarks.
Zoya Nasir also weighed in, writing in the comments, “Oh. My. God. I have SO much to say, with all due respect. What a dangerous and twisted narrative.”
Dr Ejaz Waris offered a different perspective, pointing out that divorce can affect families on both the husband’s and wife’s sides.
Waris agreed with Faisal on one point, saying that “divorce shouldn’t be celebrated”, but added that regardless of whether a family is “modern, lives in DHA or in Anarkali, they share the same grief.”
He said he respected Faisal’s opinion, while also stressing that Khan is “half her age” and that people in the industry should learn to respect their elders.
Fans also questioned the assumption that divorce affects only the woman’s family, pointing out that both sides can experience grief.
Others echoed the sentiment that “One can’t understand the pain unless it's their daughter at stake”.
At the same time, some users defended Faisal’s comments, arguing that “All she meant to say is that divorce is normalised” and that people can now return to their everyday lives more quickly after a separation.
The debate has ultimately highlighted a generational shift in how divorce is discussed.
Faisal’s comments focused on what she sees as the changing social response to the end of a marriage, while her critics emphasised that greater acceptance does not necessarily mean divorce is celebrated or that the emotional toll has disappeared.
For many, the conversation reflects a broader tension between preserving the sensitivity traditionally associated with marriage and recognising that people’s experiences of marriage, separation and divorce can differ significantly.

title: Outgoing UN chief makes climate push at New York summit
description: Guterres calls out  Big Oil  for treating atmosphere like  open sewer  ahead of hosting his final climate summit
content:
Guterres calls out 'Big Oil' for treating atmosphere like 'open sewer' ahead of hosting his final climate summit
Fresh from accusing fossil fuel interests of treating the atmosphere like an "open sewer," outgoing United Nations chief Antonio Guterres is set to host his final climate summit Wednesday at the world organisation's New York headquarters.
The stakes are clearer than ever, as the impacts of climate change surge around the world — from heat waves and wildfires in Europe to catastrophic flooding in Nepal and Tibet triggered by a glacier collapse.
Extreme weather impacts are set to worsen with an El Nino weather pattern that has tied for the most intense ever. And the world is set to shoot past — at least temporarily — 1.5C of warming, beyond which scientists say it will see worse catastrophes from climate change.
The "High-level Event on Climate Action and the Just Transition" will have opening remarks by Guterres followed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.
The two countries are co-hosting COP31 climate talks in Antalya in November in an unusual arrangement, with Australia running the talks but Turkiye hosting the event and rallying support for voluntary pledges.
Read: Aurangzeb highlights Pakistan's climate vulnerability, calls for faster climate financing at UNGA
Guterres, who made climate change a defining issue of his tenure that ends on December 31, set the tone on Tuesday when he called out "Big Oil" for treating the atmosphere like an "open sewer."
"Since Russia's invasion of Ukraine , five major Western oil companies have pocketed nearly half a trillion dollars in profits," he continued. He compared the amount with the just $34 billion in financing that has been mobilised to help developing countries adapt to a warming world.
"Guterres is an extraordinary climate champion," Rachel Cleetus of the nonprofit Union of Concerned Scientists told AFP . She praised the former Portuguese prime minister for using his position "to elevate the voices of the less powerful and highlight the need for climate justice."
Emissions cuts, financing, electrification
The meeting agenda calls on leaders to focus on areas like accelerating action to green their economies and mobilising financing for developing countries to help them achieve their carbon goals and build resilience against a warming world.
Momentum is also gathering for electrification: switching combustion-based systems, like in heating and vehicles, to electricity.
Turkiye has advanced a "35x35" target to increase electricity's share of global final energy consumption to 35% by 2035. However, it has not specified that the electricity should be generated by renewables, which is key to tackling climate change.
Read More: Europe's hottest town says climate change is reshaping daily life
There are some glimmers of hope, as global renewable power capacity grew by a record amount last year. But as energy demand increases from AI data centres and air conditioning in a warming world, clean energy is not rising fast enough to displace fossil fuels.
Observers will be watching the level of ambition the two hosts — both fossil fuel-dependent economies — bring in the run-up to COP31.
"We need to come together to meet the problem head-on. There's no avoiding the scale of our responsibility or the cost of inaction," Albanese said at the start of the week, extolling his nation's rising share of renewables in its energy mix. Yet his climate change and energy minister Chris Bowen is traveling to India and Saudi Arabia this week for talks on strengthening Australia's oil supplies.
Pledges for Nepal — where thousands remain missing — could also feature. Nepalese Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal recently told Kantipur TV that financial support "is not a matter of charity; it is a matter of legal and moral liability" for his climate-vulnerable country, which produces negligible emissions.
Cleetus said the response for Nepal would be a credibility test for the Loss and Damage Fund, created to help the nations most vulnerable to the ravages of climate change, but so far vastly underfinanced.

title: Dolly Parton   s estate sues nephew Bryan Seaver over alleged violent threats
description: The estate also alleges that Seaver referred to himself as an    international arms dealer and mercenary
content:
The estate also alleges that Seaver referred to himself as an “international arms dealer and mercenary
Dolly Parton’s estate has filed a lawsuit against her nephew Bryan Seaver, accusing him of making violent threats against people associated with the late singer’s estate and attempting to damage her business legacy.
Seaver, who worked as Parton’s head of security for nearly two decades, was recently dismissed from his position following her death on August 25, 2026. Parton’s manager, Danny Nozell, filed the lawsuit on behalf of She’s Alive, LLC, the entity responsible for protecting and managing aspects of the singer’s legacy.
According to court documents obtained by Entertainment Weekly, the estate claims Seaver’s alleged threats began several weeks before Parton’s death and continued afterwards. The filing accuses him of threatening estate personnel, legal representatives and business partners, while allegedly vowing to “destroy the entire brand”.
The estate also alleges that Seaver referred to himself as an “international arms dealer and mercenary” and invoked his background as a military contractor while making the alleged threats. One message cited in the filing allegedly included the statement, “I’m not an entertainment person. I’m a killer.”
The legal documents claim that some people connected to Parton’s estate resigned because of the alleged conduct, while the singer’s trusts and estates attorney withdrew after allegedly being targeted. Other individuals associated with the estate have reportedly hired private security as a result of the situation.
The estate sought a temporary restraining order against Seaver, which was granted on Tuesday, September 22. The order restricts Seaver from contacting or approaching certain employees, attorneys and business partners and from interfering with the estate’s business relationships.
Seaver has disputed the characterisation of his messages as threats. Speaking to TMZ, he said his comments had been taken out of context and maintained that he was speaking privately with Nozell, whom he considered a friend. He described the conversations as two people grieving and engaging in what he called “rage talk”.
Seaver is the son of Parton’s sister Cassie and had provided security services for the singer’s properties for nearly 20 years. His father, Larry Seaver, previously held a similar security role for Parton.
Seaver was also the family member who publicly announced Parton’s death in August. At the time, he said Parton had asked him years earlier to make the announcement when the time came.
The latest lawsuit follows his dismissal from the estate earlier this month. The legal dispute now places the future management and protection of Parton’s business interests under increased scrutiny as her estate continues handling her legacy following her death at 80.

title: Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years for sexual assault
description: Ex Hollywood mogul became face of  MeToo movement after dozens of women accused him of sexual misconduct
content:
Ex-Hollywood mogul became face of #MeToo movement after dozens of women accused him of sexual misconduct
A court in New York sentenced Harvey Weinstein, a former Hollywood film producer whose case sparked a worldwide movement against sexual abuse, to 15 years in prison on Wednesday, according to a report by NBC News .
Weinstein, 74, was found guilty last year of sexually assaulting Miriam Haley, a former production assistant on a US television show, at his New York apartment in 2006.
Judge Curtis Farber told Weinstein that he had used force against the victim and had never accepted responsibility for his actions. After serving his prison term, Weinstein will be monitored by authorities for five years and must register as a sex offender.
Haley spoke in court and said the assault had seriously harmed her life. Weinstein, who attended the hearing in a wheelchair, again denied the accusations but apologised to anyone he may have hurt, according to the report.
For decades, Weinstein was one of the most influential figures in Hollywood. His companies produced and distributed well-known films such as Pulp Fiction , The King's Speech and The Artist. He won an Academy Award, the film industry's top prize, as a producer of Shakespeare in Love .
His career collapsed in 2017, when The New York Times and The New Yorker magazine published investigations into allegations that he had sexually harassed and assaulted women for years. More than 80 women, including actresses and former employees, have since accused him of sexual misconduct.
The reports led to the #MeToo movement, in which women around the world shared their experiences of sexual harassment and abuse, often by powerful men in business, politics and entertainment. The movement led to investigations and firings in many countries.
Weinstein said all his sexual relationships were consensual.
Weinstein was arrested in 2018 and has since remained in custody.
A New York jury first convicted him in 2020, and he was sentenced to 23 years in prison. In 2024, however, New York's highest court overturned the conviction and ordered a new trial.
Meanwhile, a New York judge in May declared a mistrial in a separate case after jurors failed to reach a verdict on allegations he sexually assaulted actor Jessica Mann. It was the third time Mann had taken the stand against Weinstein after a 2020 guilty verdict was overturned due to mishandling of witnesses, and a 2025 case ended in mistrial after a jury-room feud.
Also Read: Influencer publicly accuses Los Angeles casting director of rape and drugging
Prosecutors later said they would not pursue a fourth trial in Mann's case.
Weinstein is also to be resentenced in California for the 2013 rape and assault of an actress in a Los Angeles hotel room, after an appeals court in June upheld the conviction but vacated his 16-year prison term.
Weinstein, who is wheelchair-bound due to health issues , has continued to deny all allegations against him. He underwent a spectacular fall from his position astride the world of show business when the first allegations against him exploded into public view.

title: LHC summons Punjab IGP in two contempt cases over police non compliance
description: Summons ordered after rejecting a police inquiry report and expressing displeasure over an unreadable FIR
content:
Summons ordered after rejecting a police inquiry report and expressing displeasure over an unreadable FIR
The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Wednesday summoned Punjab Inspector General of Police (IGP) Rao Abdul Kareem in person, along with the relevant record, on Thursday in two separate contempt proceedings involving alleged non-compliance with court orders by police officials.
LHC Chief Justice Aalia Neelum passed the orders while hearing separate petitions concerning the alleged illegal registration of a criminal case and harassment of citizens by police. The court expressed strong displeasure over the police’s handling of both matters.
In a contempt petition filed by citizen Mian Muhammad Jameel against Chuhang police officials and others, the court summoned the Punjab IGP after Superintendent of Police (SP) Abdullah, who appeared on behalf of the police, failed to read out the FIR when directed to do so by the chief justice.
“It’s not possible to read the FIR; it is not clear what has been written. SP sir, please read the FIR,” the chief justice remarked.
Despite the court’s direction, the police officer was unable to read the FIR, prompting the court to express strong displeasure over the manner in which police records had been prepared.
Read: Lahore police to begin using body-worn cameras after training
“The entire Punjab has been ruined; this is the situation in Punjab,” Justice Neelum remarked, observing that FIRs were not even being written in a readable manner.
According to the petitioner, a sessions court had ordered the registration of a case against him in 2021. He challenged the decision before the LHC, where a single bench subsequently suspended the order for registration of the case.
The petitioner contended that despite the High Court’s order, the police proceeded to register a case against him illegally, prompting him to file the contempt petition.
In a separate contempt petition filed by citizen Momin Khan against Lahore Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Bilal Siddique Kamyana, the court rejected an inquiry report submitted by the police and summoned the Punjab IGP along with the relevant record.
Read more: Cause of deaths in custody being probed
The petitioner alleged that the court had earlier forwarded his application to the Lahore CCPO for redressal against alleged illegal harassment and intimidation by police officials.
He contended that despite the court’s directions, Ichhra police continued to harass and intimidate him and conducted illegal raids at his residence.
The petitioner further alleged that the court’s order had not been complied with and requested the LHC to initiate contempt proceedings against the Lahore CCPO for alleged non-compliance with its directions.
The court rejected the police inquiry report and directed the Punjab IG to appear in person with the relevant record at the next hearing.

title: Trump s Board of Peace to unveil  2 45 billion Gaza recovery plan  Axios reports
description: White House and US Department of State did not immediately respond to requests for comment
content:
White House and US Department of State did not immediately respond to requests for comment
US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace will unveil a six-month, $2.45 billion recovery plan for Gaza at a meeting of its members on Wednesday, Axios reported.
The 66-project proposal includes estimated spending for temporary housing, rubble removal, hospital repairs, economic recovery and the deployment of a multinational security force, the report added, citing a copy of the plan.
The White House and US Department of State did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Read: Board of Peace reiterates Gaza objectives ahead of UN General Assembly
The plan estimates physical damage in Gaza at $35.2 billion and says full recovery and reconstruction will require about $71.4 billion over the next decade, the Axios report added.
It also calls for repairing border crossings, restoring electricity and water infrastructure, deploying 25,000 portable solar power kits and permanently filling tunnels beneath sites needed for priority reconstruction projects.
Trump's administration told Congress in late July it is sending more than $206 million for a proposed Gaza peacekeeping force, the first significant funding for the stalled US plan to rebuild the devastated enclave.
Trump set up a Board of Peace to oversee his plan to end Israel's genocide in Gaza.
But since the announcement of an agreement in late July, the effort has stalled, with Israel refusing to fulfil conditions that would allow the deal to move ahead.
The report said the Board of Peace and the Palestinian government have not secured the entire $2.45 billion but are confident that, once political hurdles are cleared, donor countries will step up.

title: Thailand shock Pakistan in Asian Games kabaddi
description: The winners pull off stunning upset  edge strong Green shirts 48 45
content:
The winners pull off stunning upset, edge strong Green-shirts 48-45
Thailand produced a major upset at the Asian Games on Wednesday, edging Pakistan 48-45 in a closely fought Group B men’s kabaddi match at the Tokai Citizen Gymnasium.
Pakistan, who had opened their campaign with a dominant 65-22 victory over Malaysia before demolishing Nepal, led Thailand 32-31 at halftime but were unable to maintain their advantage in the second period
Thailand turned the match around after the break, scoring 17 points to Pakistan’s 13 to secure their second victory of the competition.
The result marked a striking turnaround for Thailand, who had also beaten Nepal 59-48 in their opening Group B match.
The defeat leaves Pakistan needing a strong response in their remaining Group B fixture against Iran. The top two teams from each group advance to the knockout stage.
Pakistan will now face Iran in do-or-die battle on Thursday (tomorrow).
"Our players did not play the way they should have after half time," Pakistan Kabaddi Federation (PKF) secretary Mohammad Sarwar told The Express Tribune from Japan.
"We don't have more exposure as others like Thailand ho abroad doe matches. You need international match experience," Sarwar said.

title: Abrar storms to No1 in T20I rankings
description: Spinner becomes the country   s fifth bowler to top the T20I bowling table
content:
Spinner becomes the country’s fifth bowler to top the T20I bowling table
Pakistan leg-spinner Abrar Ahmed has become the fifth bowler from the country to top the ICC men’s T20I bowling rankings, replacing Afghanistan’s Rashid Khan at the summit, the ICC said on Wednesday.
Abrar moved one rating point ahead of Rashid, who finished with 736 points after a six-month stint at No. 1.
The Pakistan spinner joins Umar Gul, Saeed Ajmal, Imad Wasim and Shahid Afridi as Pakistani bowlers who have topped the T20I rankings.
England captain Harry Brook climbed five places to a career-best fourth among T20I batters after a successful home series against Sri Lanka.
Brook scored an unbeaten 114 in the opening match in Southampton and accumulated 170 runs as England completed a 3-0 series sweep. He was named Player of the Series.
Brook, who is the top-ranked Test batter, also climbed three places to 12th in the ODI batting rankings and has a chance to break into the top 10 in all three formats.
His England team-mate Jos Buttler moved up two places to fifth after scoring 172 runs in the Sri Lanka series.
India captain Shreyas Iyer climbed seven places to joint-22nd, while England’s Tom Banton jumped 30 places to 60th in the T20I batting rankings.
Among bowlers, England’s Jamie Overton made the biggest gain, rising 47 places to a career-best sixth after taking five wickets in the series against Sri Lanka.
England’s Liam Dawson moved up 12 places to 11th, while India’s Axar Patel rose 12 places to 15th and Ravi Bishnoi five places to 35th. Afghanistan’s Azmatullah Omarzai climbed three places to 49th.
England all-rounder Will Jacks moved to 58th among T20I bowlers and third in the all-rounders’ rankings.
In the ODI rankings, Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza climbed five places to 24th after scores of 45 and an unbeaten 81 in the final two matches of the three-game series against Australia.
Australia fast bowler Nathan Ellis moved three places to a career-best 17th after taking nine wickets in the series, while Sri Lanka’s Asitha Fernando climbed from 39th to 30th after figures of three for 53 against England.

title: Hesson backs youngsters for Asian Games challenge
description: Squad heads to Nagoya after Karachi camp with captain Farhan set to gain leadership experience
content:
Squad heads to Nagoya after Karachi camp with captain Farhan set to gain leadership experience
Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson said on Wednesday that the Asian Games will provide valuable international and leadership experience to a young Pakistan side.
Pakistan on Wednesday also did training at the Oval Ground of the National Stadium ahead of the cricket tournament at the 20th Asian Games, with Hesson saying the players had worked extensively to prepare for different pitches and playing conditions.
The brigade is scheduled to fly out for Japan on Thursday.
“The players have been given extensive practice over the past three days to prepare them for different pitches and conditions,” Hesson told reporters on the third day of the camp.
Pakistan squad was selected from a 30-member preliminary list finalised around five months ago in accordance with the regulations governing the Asian Games, Hesson said.
Fast bowler Shahnawaz Dahani was not part of the preliminary squad and therefore could not be included in the current group.
Despite the absence of established stars including Babar Azam, Shaheen Shah Afridi and Mohammad Rizwan, Hesson described the squad as balanced and aggressive, adding the tournament would offer emerging players an important opportunity to prove themselves.
“The Asian Games provide an excellent platform for new and talented players to showcase their abilities,” he said.
Particular attention will be on opener Sahibzada Farhan, who will captain Pakistan at the tournament.
Hesson said the assignment would give Farhan valuable experience of leading the national side and an opportunity to perform under pressure.
“For Farhan, the Asian Games are an excellent opportunity to gain captaincy experience,” he said.
However, he stressed that Farhan’s role in Japan would not determine Pakistan’s long-term leadership plans saying future captaincy decisions would be made by the selection committee and the Pakistan Cricket Board chairman.
Pakistan are also expected to make detailed preparations for a possible meeting with arch-rivals India, who have enjoyed a strong record against Pakistan in recent encounters.
“India have beaten us several times which is a benchmark for Pakistani fans,” Hesson said.
The Asian Games campaign comes as Pakistan seek improvement across all three formats following an inconsistent period.
Hesson said Test cricket remained an area of concern, particularly after Pakistan’s recent series defeat against England, but argued that the team’s progress should not be judged identically across formats.
“It is not appropriate to judge the team's performance across all three formats in the same way,” he said. “Test cricket is an area where Pakistan are struggling.”
He pointed instead to progress in T20Is since his arrival, saying Pakistan had climbed from eighth to fifth in the rankings during the past 15 months.
“When I came in, the T20I team was ranked eighth. At the moment, Pakistan are fifth,” Hesson said.
He added that Pakistan had gained 30 ranking points during that period and won T20I series away from home, contributing to the improvement.
Pakistan had previously held the top position in the T20I rankings in 2017.
Hesson also said the team had improved in one-day internationals over the past year as preparations continue for the 2027 World Cup.
“We have improved in ODI cricket over the past year. Our team is preparing for the 2027 World Cup,” he said.
The coach acknowledged the importance of developing Pakistan’s next generation of fast bowlers, while praising Shaheen as an experienced and high-quality bowler.
“Our current focus is on developing young and emerging attacking bowlers,” Hesson said, adding that the team was also working to bring greater consistency to its top-order batting.
Hesson also praised selector Aaqib Javed for efforts to strengthen Pakistan’s cricket system.
With the Asian Games offering a platform for emerging talent, Hesson said Pakistan’s intensive Karachi preparations had left him confident ahead of Thursday’s departure for Nagoya.

title: Kylie Jenner faces backlash over solo  73 million private jet flight to St  Tropez
description: The reality TV star documented the journey in a new vlog while travelling to the French destination for a wedding
content:
The reality TV star documented the journey in a new vlog while travelling to the French destination for a wedding
Kylie Jenner has faced online criticism after showing that she travelled alone on her $73 million private jet during a trip to St. Tropez.
The 29-year-old reality TV star documented the journey in a new vlog while travelling to the French destination for a wedding.
The video showed Jenner aboard her customised aircraft, which features pink and cream interiors, leather seating, a full bar, multiple living areas, a master suite and two bathrooms.
Jenner highlighted that she had the aircraft to herself, despite the plane reportedly being capable of carrying 19 passengers.
She has owned the private jet since 2020, with its interior featuring personalised Kylie branding.
The footage prompted criticism from viewers concerned about the environmental impact of private aviation.

title: Godzilla Minus Zero  receives first R rating in franchise history
description: Godzilla Minus Zero  receives franchise   s first R rating ahead of its November theatrical release
content:
'Godzilla Minus Zero' receives franchise’s first R rating ahead of its November theatrical release
Godzilla Minus Zero has received an R rating from the MPA, making it the first film in the 72-year history of the Godzilla franchise to receive the classification.
The upcoming film is a sequel to Takashi Yamazaki’s Godzilla Minus One, with Yamazaki returning as writer and director. Godzilla Minus Zero is scheduled to open in Japanese cinemas on November 3 and in the United States on November 6.
Set in 1949, two years after the events of Godzilla Minus One , the sequel follows Godzilla and the Shikishima family in post-World War II Japan.
According to Film Ratings, Godzilla Minus Zero has been classified R. By comparison, Godzilla Minus One received a PG-13 rating, as did the Monsterverse films Godzilla, Godzilla: King of the Monsters, Godzilla vs. Kong and Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire.
The original Godzilla , released in 1954, does not have an MPA rating because the ratings system was not introduced until 1968. Later entries have received classifications including G and PG, with Destroy All Monsters rated G and 2004’s Godzilla vs. Hedorah receiving a PG rating.
The R classification marks a change from the rating given to Godzilla Minus One . ScreenRant’s review of that film previously noted that the monster’s “design brings about an equal amount of horror and curiosity” and that “the film also reminds us of how terrifying Godzilla is, a component that has been lacking in recent films.”
Godzilla Minus Zero stars Ryunosuke Kamiki as Kōichi Shikishima and Minami Hamabe as Noriko Shikishima. The cast also includes Yuki Yamada, Kuranosuke Sasaki, Jun Kunimura, Miou Tanaka, Sakura Ando, Masami Nagasawa, Min Tanaka, Hidetaka Yoshioka and Sae Nagatani.

title: Microsoft cuts hundreds more jobs as next Halo game moves to Activision
description: Microsoft cuts around 600 jobs as Xbox moves next Halo game to Activision amid restructuring
content:
Microsoft cuts around 600 jobs as Xbox moves next Halo game to Activision amid restructuring
Microsoft is cutting fewer than 600 jobs globally as part of its ongoing restructuring, including 268 positions across Xbox Game Studios. The changes also include moving development of the next Halo game to Activision.
Around 300 of the latest job cuts are in Washington state, according to Microsoft. The Xbox reductions affect Halo Studios, other first-party studios, as well as management and operating teams.
The latest cuts follow Microsoft’s announcement in July that Xbox would eliminate around 3,200 roles by the end of its fiscal year. The company said the Xbox restructuring is now about 75% complete.
“The goal is to strengthen our franchises and games by operating fewer business units, aligning groups that already work closely together, and focusing our publishing expertise,” Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty wrote in a memo to employees.
As part of the restructuring, the next Halo game will move to Activision, which Microsoft acquired in 2023.
A new team separate from Call of Duty will lead development, while a smaller team at Halo Studios will continue supporting existing Halo games, the community and esports.
Activision president Rob Kostich said the company has “already begun assembling a purpose-built team, unique in capability and talent.”
He added that the aim is to “make the greatest Halo game ever, worthy of its universe and legacy, while staying true to what made players love it in the first place.”
Activision will also take control of World’s Edge, the studio behind Age of Empires, and Rare, which develops Sea of Thieves.
Obsidian Entertainment will move under Bethesda, while Microsoft Casual Games will move under King. Turn 10 Studios and Playground Games will merge into a single studio handling Forza and Fable.
Undead Labs, meanwhile, has been spun off, with State of Decay 3 still set to launch on Game Pass on day one under a new publisher.
Ninja Theory could close after two potential handoff agreements fell through, while Arkane in France remains without an announced outcome.

title: 19 terrorists killed  subedar martyred in Balochistan IBOs  ISPR
description: President Zardari  PM Shehbaz laud security forces for successful operations against terrorists  pay tribute to martyr
content:
President Zardari, PM Shehbaz laud security forces for successful operations against terrorists, pay tribute to martyr
Security forces killed 19 terrorists during intelligence-based operations in separate engagements in Balochistan, while a subedar embraced martyrdom in an exchange of fire, the military’s media wing said on Wednesday.
According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), intelligence agencies reported the presence of multiple hideouts of Indian-sponsored Fitna Al-Khawarij and Fitna Al-Hindustan in the general area of Shaban, Quetta district, posing a threat to the local population.
The state uses the term Fitna Al Khwarij for terrorists affiliated with the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, while Fitna Al Hindustan refers to banned outfits sponsored by India in Balochistan.
Read : 21 terrorists killed in multiple engagements across K-P: ISPR
“In order to safeguard the local populace and clear the area of terrorists, Security Forces have been conducting a clearance operation in the general area of Shaban, District Quetta, since 21 September 2026,” the ISPR said.
During the operation, security forces effectively engaged and cleared multiple terrorist hideouts.
“Following an intense exchange of fire, 13 Indian-sponsored terrorists have been killed so far,” it said.
Intelligence agencies reported the presence of multiple hideouts of Indian-sponsored Fitna Al Khawarij and Fitna Al Hindustan in the general area of Shaban, District Quetta, posing a threat to the local population. In order to safeguard the local populace and clear the area of…
Weapons, ammunition and explosives were also recovered from the cleared hideouts, according to the statement, adding that the clearance operation would continue until the complete neutralisation of the threat in the area.
In separate engagements on September 22 and 23, security forces conducted pre-emptive intelligence-based operations in Kech and Quetta West districts.
“During the operations, troops effectively engaged the terrorists and, following an intense exchange of fire, six terrorists were killed,” the ISPR said.
Weapons and ammunition were also recovered during the operations.
During the exchange of fire, Subedar Muhammad Jamil, 39, a resident of Taunsa Sharif, Dera Ghazi Khan district, made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty and embraced martyrdom, the statement said.
The ISPR said the counter-terrorism campaign under the vision of “Azm-e-Istehkam”, as approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, would continue at full pace.
“Security Forces and Law Enforcement Agencies remain committed to eliminating the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country,” it said.

President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif lauded the security forces for the successful operations against terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan in Quetta and Kech districts of Balochistan.
In their separate statements, they paid tribute to Subedar Muhammad Jamil Shaheed for rendering the supreme sacrifice in defence of the motherland.
The president, in his statement, said the killing of terrorists operating under Indian patronage reflects the professional capabilities of the security forces.
Paying tribute to Subedar Muhammad Jamil Shaheed, President Zardari said, “His sacrifice is a symbol of the security forces' unwavering commitment to maintaining peace and protecting the country.”
In a statement issued by PMO, PM Shehbaz said the elimination of foreign-backed terrorists demonstrated the effective strategy of the security forces.
He said operations by security forces and law enforcement agencies would continue until the complete eradication of terrorism from the country.
“Foreign-sponsored terrorism will be eliminated at all costs,” he vowed.
PM Shehbaz said the nation stands firmly shoulder to shoulder with its brave security forces and law enforcement agencies in the war against terrorism. He also expressed condolences and solidarity with the family of Subedar Muhammad Jamil Shaheed.
He said Subedar Jamil's sacrifice was a matter of immense pride for the whole nation.
Earlier, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also paid tribute to security forces for killing 19 terrorists during successful operations against terrorists belonging to Fitna Al-Hindustan and Fitna Al-Khawarij in Balochistan.
Lauding the courage and professional capabilities of security forces for killing terrorists, the minister said the operations against elements seeking to undermine peace were continuing with full force in Balochistan.
“The brave sons of the security forces are the pride of the nation,” the interior minister said.
Naqvi also paid tribute to Subedar Muhammad Jamil, who embraced martyrdom while bravely confronting the khawarij.
“Subedar Muhammad Jamil set an example by sacrificing his life today for the peaceful tomorrow of the nation,” he said.

title: With reconstruction stalled  Gazans shelter in buildings at risk of collapse
description: UN says 84  of Gaza s structures damaged or destroyed as civil defence warns 2 000 buildings risk collapse
content:
UN says 84% of Gaza's structures damaged or destroyed as civil defence warns 2,000 buildings risk collapse
In her Gaza City apartment, Heba Arafat walks uphill across a living room slanted at a steep angle after Israeli airstrikes caused the building's foundations to collapse, leaving the entire structure tilted.
Like thousands of people in Gaza, Arafat chose to risk living in an apartment building damaged during nearly three years of war between Israel and Hamas , with countless Israeli airstrikes on the Palestinian territory.
"We were forced to live here because we had nowhere else to go. All of our homes were destroyed, our land was razed and we have nothing left," said Arafat, 47.
According to the United Nations, 84% of all structures in Gaza had been damaged or destroyed by October 2025, and Gaza's civil defence says 2,000 buildings across the territory are at risk of collapse.
Last week, 21 people including 12 children died in Gaza City after a six-storey building that local authorities said had been hit repeatedly by Israeli airstrikes collapsed. Israel denied having struck the building.
Read: Israeli fire kills three more Palestinians in latest Gaza ceasefire violations
Arafat lives with her six daughters and husband in their old apartment building in Gaza City's Al-Shati Refugee Camp, which they left at the height of the war that began in October 2023 with Hamas's massive attack on Israel.
The family returned after an October 2025 ceasefire , which has reduced but not ended Israeli strikes. They found that their four-storey building, in which 30 people now live, had collapsed inward at the ground floor, the result, she said, of an Israeli ground operation in the area. Like most buildings in Gaza City, the windows were blown away by blasts, with makeshift bedsheets spread across the frames providing little privacy.
As she spoke, Arafat illustrated her building's slant by leaving a water bottle sideways on the floor, only for it to quickly roll away to the other end of the room.
While no territory-wide estimate exists, Ramiz Alakbarov, the UN humanitarian coordinator for the Palestinian territories, said last week that people across Gaza were living in "hundreds of damaged and unsafe shelters".
"Where can we go? Even though this house is dangerous," Arafat said. "We have been terrified ever since we heard about houses collapsing. The danger has become even greater" than we thought.
Gaza City municipal staff patrol the streets to identify buildings at risk of collapse and mark them with stencils. "These homes pose a genuine threat to the lives of the displaced persons sheltering inside them, as well as to residents in the vicinity and those in nearby displacement camps," said Hosni Muhanna, a Gaza City spokesman.
Read More: Gaza students return to in-person schooling for first time in three years
But Muhanna knows that people are likely to remain in these buildings for lack of better options. "Thousands of displaced people are forced to seek shelter in these dilapidated buildings which are on the verge of collapse to escape the hardships of displacement camps that offer no protection against the summer heat or winter cold."
Most residents of Gaza were displaced at least once during the war, and many of them remain in enormous camps for the displaced, in tents provided by humanitarian organisations or in improvised shelters.
With diseases such as the skin infection impetigo rampaging through certain camps due to the lack of waste disposal and general overcrowding, many Gaza residents have found it safer to take the risks of moving into the damaged buildings.
And with Gaza's economy in tatters, many remain dependent on aid, which Israel has allowed into Gaza with restrictions since the declaration of the United States-brokered ceasefire in October 2025. But Israel has kept carrying out airstrikes, and has restricted the entry of a range of equipment that it says could also have military use, but which Gazans and international NGOs say are needed for the territory's vast reconstruction needs.
Also Read: Board of Peace reiterates Gaza objectives ahead of UN General Assembly
These can include large machinery needed to clear rubble from the site of destroyed buildings, or spare parts and lubricants needed to keep other tools running, UN spokesman Stephane Dujarric said in August.
With the ceasefire process stalled for months, reconstruction efforts planned under the ceasefire have yet to begin. According to a joint assessment published by the UN, World Bank and European Union in April, Gaza will require $71.4 billion in recovery and reconstruction spending over the next decade.
"We're afraid a wall or the roof might fall on us, so we huddle together, afraid that one of us might get hurt," Arafat said.

The ideal candidate should possess strong planning, management, analytical and problem-solving abilities. Good communication skills, professionalism, integrity and the ability to work with people from different backgrounds are also highlighted. Familiarity with Microsoft Office and coaching software would be an added advantage.
Interested candidates have been invited to apply by 5pm on October 8, 2026, through the PCB jobs portal.

title: Kartik Aaryan wins first National Film Award for  Chandu Champion

content:
Indian actor credits parents' blessings, support as constant anchor, dedicates honour to country's Paralympians
Indian actor Kartik Aaryan won his first National Film Award, receiving the Best Actor in a Leading Role honour for his performance in Chandu Champion .
In a lengthy note shared on Instagram, Aaryan reflected on growing up in Gwalior as a self-described "mumma's boy," in an environment where such acting ambitions were often dismissed rather than encouraged.
The actor described himself as "still feeling numb with excitement and nerves even after living through the moment." He also called the achievement a dream shared by every actor in the country, referencing his film's own tagline — that he wasn't just Chandu, but a champion.
Further, Aaryan thanked the director and producer of Chandu Champion for entrusting him with the role of Murlikant Petkar, India's first Paralympic gold medallist in freestyle swimming. The actor noted that he would "always be grateful and indebted" to them for the responsibility.
He credited his parents' blessings and unconditional support as his constant anchor through his journey, alongside encouragement from friends during moments of doubt and the tireless work of his team. "I dedicate the honour to every Paralympian in the country and to anyone who dares to chase what seems impossible," he added.
Aaryan closed his note expressing hope for more milestones ahead.
Chandu Champion was released in 2024 and traces Petkar's journey as an athlete. Aaryan underwent an extensive physical transformation for the role.
The actor first rose to prominence with films such as Pyaar Ka Punchnama and Sonu Ke Titu Ki Sweety , before establishing himself as one of Bollywood’s leading performers, with successful projects including the second and third instalments of Bhool Bhulaiyaa .

title: Eight drones shot down after entering Pakistan from Afghanistan  security sources
description: Sources say 4 drones brought down in areas close to Torkham border  another 4 shot down near the border with Kohat
content:
Sources say 4 drones brought down in areas close to Torkham border, another 4 shot down near the border with Kohat
Pakistan’s air defence system shot down eight drones after they entered the country’s airspace from Afghanistan on Wednesday morning, security sources said.
"Four of the drones were brought down in areas adjoining the Torkham border, while another four were shot down in mountainous areas near the border with Kohat," the sources said.
The sources said the Pakistan Army and Pakistan Air Force (PAF) had thwarted the attempt by the Afghan Taliban regime to target public places, adding that the country’s “active and alert air defence system” had detected and brought down all eight drones.
The sources described the incursion as “further evidence” of what they said was the Afghan Taliban regime’s direct support and patronage of terrorists.
“The Pakistan Armed Forces remain fully prepared at all times to defend Pakistan and its people,” the sources said.
افغان طالبان رجیم کی عوامی مقامات کو نشانہ بنانے کی بزدلانہ کوشش ناکام #AfghanTaliban #SecurityForces #PublicSafety #SecurityOperation pic.twitter.com/2OqeUIYwTL
The sources said that the assessment and defence systems monitored by the PAF along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border remained operational and on alert at all times.
It said the downed drones further demonstrated that the PAF were fully determined and capable of thwarting any ground, aerial or terrorist incursion by the Afghan Taliban regime.
The wreckage of the destroyed drones was also being taken into custody, the sources said. The sources said that the developments reflect the Afghan Taliban’s “severe panic”.
The sources added that the PAF’s surveillance and defence systems along the border remained fully operational to detect and respond to any further incursions.
Earlier, security forces also foiled an infiltration attempt by terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij to cross into the Kurram sector from Afghanistan and responded promptly to firing by the Afghan Taliban.
The term Fitna al-Khawarij is used by the state to refer to terrorists affiliated with the banned TTP.
The sources added that the provocative firing in the Kurram sector along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border since Tuesday night, followed by Wednesday’s drone attack, came after Pakistani forces had destroyed terrorist hideouts operating under the Afghan Taliban regime.
According to security sources, the infiltration attempt was made from Afghan Taliban posts in Nangarhar and Paktia provinces but was effectively thwarted by Pakistani troops deployed along the border.
Following the failure of the attempt, the Afghan Taliban opened unprovoked fire on Pakistani border posts using heavy weapons, mortars and other arms, sources added.
They further added that security forces responded effectively and targeted several Afghan Taliban border posts, mortar positions and defensive positions with small and heavy weapons, including artillery.
The development emerged two days after Pakistan carried out “calibrated” air strikes against terrorist hideouts near the Afghan border and conducted intelligence-based ground operations that killed a total of 37 terrorists following a series of deadly attacks in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).
On September 20, security forces conducted an intelligence-based ground operation against a group of terrorists in Kohat and Hangu districts. "As a result of precise and skilful engagement, nine khwarij belonging to the Indian proxy Fitna al-Khawarij were sent to hell, while several were injured."
The statement said three targets were destroyed in precision strikes, including a training centre for suicide bombers. It said 28 terrorists, along with several suicide bombers, were killed, while large quantities of weapons and ammunition stored at the centres and hideouts were also destroyed.
The airstrikes were carried out in response to a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers, in which 23 people, including 15 police personnel , were martyred. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
Pakistan had reported previous incidents involving drones crossing from Afghanistan into its airspace.
On July 1, security forces had shot down four “rudimentary drones ” launched from Afghanistan into Balochistan on June 30. The military accused the Afghan Taliban regime of supporting terrorist groups operating from territory under its control and warned that further cross-border provocations would draw a strong response.
In March, armed forces intercepted few rudimentary drones launched by the Afghan Taliban in what officials described as a failed attempt to harass civilian populations, according to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations.
The military’s media wing said the drones were detected and neutralised through a combination of defensive measures before they could reach their intended targets. However, falling debris from the intercepted drones caused injuries to civilians in multiple cities.
Two children were injured in Quetta, while one civilian each sustained injuries in Kohat and Rawalpindi. All injured individuals received medical attention and were reported to be in stable condition.
Pakistan has repeatedly raised concerns on international forums over terrorist attacks being launched from Afghan soil.
A day earlier, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar called for “concrete and verifiable” action to prevent Afghan soil from being used for terrorism against neighbouring countries, particularly Pakistan, while addressing the OIC Contact Group on Afghanistan on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York.
In a separate warning following the terrorist attack in Kohat, Pakistan said it had the “will and capability” to eliminate terror threats “wherever they are” and urged the international community to press the Afghan Taliban regime to take decisive action against terrorism.
Attributing the attack to “the vilest of Khwarij with roots in Afghanistan” the Information Ministry noted that the attack was a reminder that “terrorism has no religion and no justification”. It added that Islamabad had repeatedly raised “grave concerns” over the alleged use of Afghan territory by the banned TTP and other terrorist groups to plan and launch attacks inside the country.
“The presence of terrorist sanctuaries, alongside their recruitment and support infrastructure in Afghanistan, poses a direct threat to Pakistan’s security,” the ministry had said. It added that these concerns had repeatedly been conveyed to the Afghan Taliban regime and its interlocutors. “They must dismantle these networks rather than deflect responsibility,” Pakistan said.
United Nations Security Council report formally implicated the banned Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and terrorist entities operating from Afghanistan , highlighting tactical collaboration and shared operational logistics between the groups.
Read More: Pakistan carries out 'calibrated' air strikes against terrorist hideouts
Member-state reporting confirmed that BLA terrorists were trained alongside TTP members at facilities in Afghanistan, according to the report, which also described growing operational links among various terrorist groups operating across the border.
This was not the first time a UN report pointed to the threat posed by terrorist groups operating from Afghanistan. In 2023, a UN report also revealed that the TTP had established a new base in K-P in mid-2023, shedding light on close ties between the TTP and the Afghan Taliban, as well as between the TTP and anti-Pakistani groups and Al Qaeda.
K-P had witnessed a significant rise in militant violence last year, with more than 500 attacks reported, marking a 50% increase compared to the previous year.
The fighting ​between Pakistan and Afghanistan that started in October ​has ⁠killed scores of people on both sides, with Afghans taking the brunt. Islamabad accuses the Afghan Taliban of harbouring ⁠militants ​who launch attacks in Pakistan, ​although Kabul denies this, calling the militancy its neighbour's domestic problem.
Operation Ghazab Lil Haq was launched around the end of February following renewed clashes along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border, after Afghan Taliban forces fired on multiple locations, prompting swift military retaliation by Pakistan.
The clashes intensified after Afghanistan launched a border offensive in response to Pakistani air strikes targeting terrorist positions. The two sides had agreed to a week-long ceasefire on the eve of Eidul Fitr on March 18, following requests from Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Qatar.
Also Read: Info ministry rejects Afghan Taliban-linked claims of cross-border drone strikes
Pakistan in April put forth three core demands to the Afghan Taliban during peace talks in Urumqi, China, including Kabul formally declaring the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan a terrorist organisation, dismantling its infrastructure, and providing verifiable proof of the action. These demands form the basis of Pakistan's negotiating position, which sources say has hardened amid persistent security concerns.

title: British PM vows not to stand by as  horrific suffering continues to grow  in Gaza  West Bank
description: Burnham defends sanctions on Israeli settlements in West Bank  terms two state solution  best hope for peace
content:
Burnham defends sanctions on Israeli settlements in West Bank, terms two-state solution 'best hope for peace'
Britain’s prime minister vowed Tuesday not to stand by as "horrific suffering" continues to grow and the prospect of a two-state solution "comes under attack" in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
In his address at the United Nations General Assembly in New York, Andy Burnham said recent sanctions targeting illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank recognise that the Israeli occupation of the Palestinian territory is unlawful.
The October 7, 2023 attack on Israel by the Palestinian group Hamas "does not justify the Israeli government's actions in Gaza or the West Bank," he noted, saying that "far too many people have died, including so many children ."
"We will not stand by as the horrific suffering continues to grow and the prospect of a two-state solution -- the best hope for peace and stability for both nations -- comes under attack," he added.

Burnham said trust will erode if the international community fails to back its support for a two-state solution with concrete action.

KSE-100 holds positive course throughout session as hopes for diplomatic resolution bolster sentiment
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) maintained a firm footing on Wednesday, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index climbing 830.43 points, or 0.48%, to settle at 172,232.51.
The index remained in the green from start to finish, holding above the previous close throughout the trading session as investors responded positively to developments around US-Iran talks and softer oil prices.
The benchmark index touched an intraday high of 172,762.41 and a low of 171,843.51. Investor sentiment was supported by hopes that ongoing US-Iran talks could pave the way for a diplomatic resolution, reducing fears of further disruption to global crude supplies.
Meanwhile, oil prices remained near their lowest level in more than two weeks on Wednesday as improving Gulf crude supplies weighed on the market. However, a sharp rise in diesel refining margins, which reached a record high amid potential restrictions on US diesel exports, provided a counterweight.

The improved geopolitical tone and lower oil prices helped sustain buying interest in the local market, with gains seen across major sectors including automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, oil and gas exploration companies, oil marketing companies and refineries.
The session's advance marked a notable recovery for the benchmark as investors continued to track developments at the United Nations General Assembly, where diplomatic efforts around the US-Iran conflict have remained a key focus.
According to Ismail Iqbal Securities, the benchmark closed on a positive note, supported by improved investor sentiment amid declining oil prices, with buying concentrated in select sector-specific stocks. Fertiliser, banks, and E&Ps sectors were the major contributors in today's session, cumulatively adding 497 points to the index, it noted.
Cumulatively, trading volume increased to 773.5million shares versus Tuesday’s total of 641.8million. In the ready market, shares of 496 companies were traded. title: Punjab imposes Section 144 across province  seeks Rangers deployment and mobile service suspension
description: Home Department seeks Rangers in four districts  mobile and internet suspension in Rawalpindi and Attock
content:
Home Department seeks Rangers in four districts, mobile and internet suspension in Rawalpindi and Attock
The Punjab government on Wednesday imposed Section 144 across the province for 13 days, from September 23 to October 5, banning gatherings of five or more persons in any public place, street, road, highway, motorway or open space, while also seeking Pakistan Rangers’ services for security assistance in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali and requesting the federal Ministry of Interior to downgrade mobile and internet services at selected locations in Rawalpindi and Attock from September 27 for law and order purposes, according to a notification issued by the Punjab Home Department.
According to the notification, the restrictions had been imposed in view of “serious and imminent threat to public peace, tranquility, and the safety of life & property across the Province of Punjab by militant/ terrorist organizations and Hostile Intelligence Agencies (HIAs).".
Multiple threat alerts have been received from Intelligence Agencies (IAs) regarding possible terrorist activities being planned by such hostile agencies by employing suicide bombers and Vehicle-Borne Improvised Explosive Devices (VBIEDs), the notification stated.
It further stated that assemblies of persons, rallies, gatherings, sit-ins, processions, demonstrations, and Jalsas may present potential targets for such terrorist attacks.
However, the ban will not apply to marriage ceremonies, funeral prayers, burial gatherings, and prayers in mosques and other places of worship, according to the Home Department. Courts of Law, government institutions, and events held with formal permission will also be exempt.
The law-enforcement agencies had requested immediate security measures to help address possible terrorism threats, according to the notification.
The Home Department said the Secretary Home imposed the restrictions on public gatherings under Section 144(6) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
The Punjab Home Department said the protection of the lives and property of citizens was the provincial government's top priority.
Punjab seeks mobile, internet service downgrade at selected sites
The Punjab Home Department has requested the Ministry of Interior and Narcotics Control to downgrade mobile and internet services at selected locations in Rawalpindi and Attock from September 27 for law and order purposes, according to a notification issued by the department.
The department had sent a letter to the Interior Ministry requesting the downgrade and jamming of mobile and internet services at specified locations.
In Rawalpindi, the department has requested 2G, 3G and 4G network jamming at selected locations, according to the notification.
A request has also been made to downgrade mobile and internet services in Attock, it added.
According to the Punjab Home Department, the department has requested the downgrade and jamming of mobile and internet services along the motorway at Barahma Bahtar to M1, Gango, Ahata, Taxila City, Wah Saddar, Thallian and Chakri.
The department said mobile and internet services would remain downgraded at specified locations in Rawalpindi and Attock from September 27.
The Punjab government has also sought the services of Pakistan Rangers for security assistance in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali, with the troops to remain deployed until October 5, 2026, the Punjab Home Department said.
According to the Punjab Home Department, a letter had been sent to the Interior Ministry seeking the deployment of Rangers troops in the four districts. The request includes the deployment of three Rangers companies in Rawalpindi, five wings in Attock and one company each in Jhelum and Mianwali.
The department said the deployment had been approved at the 59th meeting of the Standing Committee of the Cabinet on Law & Order (SCCLO) of the Punjab government, held on September 20.
According to the department, the deployment will be carried out under Article 245 of the Constitution of Pakistan, Sections 4 and 5 of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, and Sections 7(b) and 10 of the Pakistan Rangers Ordinance, 1959.
The Punjab Home Department said the letter to the federal Ministry of Interior was sent following a request from Punjab Police for assistance in maintaining security.
The department said the protection of the lives and property of the public was the Punjab government's top priority.

title: Macron denounces Trump s Gaza diplomacy as spectacle of shame
description: Macron faced criticism among politicians  activists in France that he has done little since recognising Palestine
content:
Macron faced criticism among politicians, activists in France that he has done little since recognising Palestine
France's President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday dismissed US President Donald Trump's claims of having ​secured peace in Gaza, saying not a single humanitarian corridor had been reopened in the enclave despite the proclaimed peace.
In ‌his final address to the United Nations before leaving office next year, Macron said the world was witnessing a spectacle that should shame everyone, rebuking Trump's portrayal of his Gaza peace plan as a diplomatic triumph.
He spoke at the United Nations General Assembly hours after Trump had, from the same rostrum, hailed his Gaza peace plan as a diplomatic ​triumph.
"A year ago, here in this very hall, about a dozen states had recognised Palestine. I hear the cynicism of some people: 'Recognition ​is just a piece of paper; look at the reality,'" Macron said, banging his fist on the podium in ⁠his last speech at the United Nations before stepping down next May.
"But what credibility do we have if we continue to remain inactive in ​the face of Gaza? Some boast of a supposed peace. But that peace has not reopened humanitarian access for a single second. Are we simply ​to stand by and watch this spectacle that should shame us all?"
In response to Macron's criticism, White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said: “President Trump ended the war between Israel and Hamas, freed all living hostages, returned the bodies of the deceased to their loved ones, and is now leading the implementation of the 20-Point Plan for Peace ​in Gaza. While others talk, this president took this complex problem head-on. No one has done more for peace and stability in the ​region.”
Read: Board of Peace reiterates Gaza objectives ahead of UN General Assembly
Macron has faced criticism among some politicians and activists in France that he has done little since recognising a Palestinian state last September.
Despite the criticism, Paris has toughened ‌its stance ⁠on settler violence against Palestinians in the West Bank, imposing some national sanctions and launching a process to ban products from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
"Look at what is happening in the West Bank, where every day violations are committed. In whose name? Hamas has never operated in the West Bank," Macron said.
"What is happening there is building, day by day, the impossibility of a project that should be based on respect for ​the legitimate right of the Palestinian people ​to exist."
France's ties with Israel ⁠have been particularly strained over the last year. Macron said those who believed that violating the sovereignty of all of Israel's neighbours would ensure its security were mistaken.
"They are weakening Israel's security, both today and in the future," ​he said.
Seven months from France's next presidential election, Macron was making his last ​appearance after first taking ⁠to the rostrum in 2017.
Often showing a keen eye for the trappings of diplomacy — the grand settings, the symbolism, the personal connections — he has at the same time failed to translate this into lasting strategic gains, analysts say.
However, he has always been a staunch defender of the multilateral system and the United Nations.
Read More: Europe cannot claim support for rule of law while supporting US-Israeli aggression against Iran: Araghchi
Macron ⁠warned against ​a global "return to the law of the jungle", saying countries faced a choice between a ​world governed by power and coercion and a "civilised international society."
"Our duty, more than ever, is to stand alongside the United Nations. We cannot accept the new order of impunity that some ​would like to build," he said.
He ended his speech with "Long Live the United Nations!"

title: Russia kills eight in strikes on Ukraine as Trump meets Zelenskiy
description: Attacks target fuel  energy sector  port infrastructure as Moscow  Kyiv trade long range strikes
content:
Attacks target fuel, energy sector, port infrastructure as Moscow, Kyiv trade long-range strikes
Russia killed eight people in strikes on Ukraine's industrial heartland and other frontline areas, Ukrainian officials said on Tuesday as President Volodymyr Zelenskiy was meeting United States President Donald Trump at the United Nations .
Moscow stepped up airstrikes over the summer, and has been attacking economic targets ranging from businesses and ports to logistics hubs, with its advances on the ground largely stalled more than four-and-a-half years into its war in Ukraine.
"Russia deliberately targets businesses, farms, warehouses , railways, energy facilities and residential buildings," Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said on Telegram.
Ukraine has also increased long-range strikes in recent months, targeting Russian oil refineries and big online retailers in an effort to undermine Moscow's war effort.
Read: Is NATO ready to fight? The Ukraine war is raising doubts among military analysts
The Ukrainian military said on Tuesday it had hit a Russian oil refinery in the city of Ufa, more than 1,300 kilometres (800 miles) from the border with Ukraine. It also said it had struck the Kuibyshev oil refinery in the Samara region on the Volga river.
The Samara region governor said Ukrainian drones hit civilian targets in the region, killing one person and injuring four. Both sides deny targeting civilians.
Trump said last week that Ukraine and Russia had agreed not to strike energy targets , but any semblance of a truce disappeared when Russia hit petrol stations in Kyiv the following day and Ukraine bombed a Russian oil refinery.
Continuing attacks on Ukraine's economic infrastructure, Moscow hit industrial enterprises in the cities of Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih and Pavlohrad in the southeastern region of Dnipropetrovsk, regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha said on Telegram. The region is home to machine building, steelmaking and other major production.
A Russian missile strike on a facility in Dnipro owned by Interpipe, Ukraine's largest pipe producer, killed four people and wounded seven, the company said. Prosecutors said Russian attacks on the southern region of Kherson killed two people and the regional governor said one person was killed near the Black Sea port of Odesa.
Police in the eastern Donetsk region, the focal point of much of the frontline fighting, said Russian aerial bombs killed one person in Kramatorsk, one of the "fortress towns" that Russia would like to capture.
Read More: 'Ukraine will support energy ceasefire if US ensures Moscow's intent'
A mass airstrike on the town of Izium, in northeastern Kharkiv region, injured seven people, local officials said. The overnight Russian barrage included an unspecified number of Oniks anti-ship and ballistic missiles, as well as four cruise missiles and 212 drones, Ukraine's air force said.
Russia's defence ministry said its forces hit industrial and military facilities in Ukraine, targeting the fuel and energy sector as well as port infrastructure facilities and sea vessels serving the Ukrainian military.
Businesses were also damaged in Pavlohrad and Kryvyi Rih, Zelenskiy's hometown, Hanzha added.
A Russian attack on an energy facility in a neighbouring region cut power supplies to nearly 100,000 consumers in the northern region of Chernihiv, an electricity distributor said.
Ukrainian energy company Naftogaz said at least five ballistic missiles had hit idle technological facilities at an oil and gas site in the central region of Poltava. The attack caused critical damage and in effect made it impossible to restore and operate the facility, it said.
The facility, which it did not name, had been a frequent target of Russian drone and missile attacks since 2022, it said.

Actor Mahira Khan penned an emotional note to director Wajahat Hussain ahead of the premiere of Mitti De Baway , thanking him for his work on the drama and for shaping her character Billo.
The show, written by Faiza Iftikhar and directed by Hussain, marks Mahira and Wahaj Ali's first on-screen pairing.

Screengrab: wajahathussain.syed/Instagram
Mitti De Baway is set in rural Punjab in 1999. The story follows Billo and Baala through a romance that unravels into separation: Baala is imprisoned on an undisclosed charge, while Billo, by the time the story resumes in 2002, has transformed into a pir, or spiritual guide, with a following of her own.
The show's first trailer drew praise from across the industry, with Kinza Hashmi saying "everything looks incredible," and Bilal Abbas describing it as one of "the best trailers I have seen in a long time." Industry peers including Maya Ali, Iqra Aziz, Hina Afridi, Yasir Hussain and Shuja Asad also weighed in with their excitement for the drama.
A later teaser added layers to Billo and Baala's story, hinting at past marriages and unresolved secrets. It also showed a hardened, prison-toughened Baala re-entering a life Billo had long since moved on from — leaving viewers to question whether the two find their way back to each other.

title: China edge Japan for Asian Games gymnastics gold
description: Zhang Boheng seal victory with a 14 20 high bar routine
content:
Zhang Boheng seal victory with a 14.20 high-bar routine
Zhang Boheng produced another powerful display at the Asian Games gymnastics competition on Wednesday as China took revenge for their Olympic defeat to Japan to beat the hosts in a clash of heavyweights for the men's team ‌gold.
Needing a high score on the final rotation to secure victory for Team China, 26-year-old Hunan native Zhang was nerveless in the finish, posting 14.20 in a clean routine on the high bar.
It was the second time Zhang has turned the tables on Japan at the Aichi-Nagoya Games, having edged injury-hampered Shinnosuke Oka for the all-around gold, just two years after ⁠taking silver behind him at the Paris Olympics.
Zhang and teammates Zou Jingyuan, Lan Xingyu, Sun Wei and Tian Hao kept the continental gold in Chinese hands for a third time in succession with a winning score of 259.095.
Japan settled for silver for a third consecutive time.
The hosts were up against it with talisman Oka needing painkilling injections on his back to compete.
He lowered the difficulty of his routines to give him the best chance of being fit for the world championships in Rotterdam in October, and it showed as he slumped to low scores in the pommel horse ‌and rings.
In ⁠the final round, he fell flat on his back after a botched catch on the high bar, drawing gasps from the crowd in the Nagoya General Gymnasium.
He rose to complete the routine, but his score of 12.666, later upgraded to 12.966, all but took Japan out of the equation.
That was despite a brilliant ⁠all-round performance from his Olympic champion teammate Daiki Hashimoto.
Hashimoto battled hard to carry the team on his back and had home fans roaring in the terraces with his pommel horse and vault efforts.
But China also had a ⁠vital cameo from parallel bars specialist Zou, who struck a key blow in the penultimate rotation.
Zou went for broke with the highest difficulty routine and his score of 15.40 was nearly a ⁠point higher than Oka's next-best effort (14.566), a gap that ultimately proved insurmountable for Japan.
China's gold put them at the top of the gymnastics medal table, one better than Japan, ahead of the women's team gold final later on Wednesday.

title: Italy hope for new dawn under Mancini
description: The Azzurri begin their UEFA Nations League campaign against Belgium
content:
The Azzurri begin their UEFA Nations League campaign against Belgium
After months of soul-searching, controversy and debate, Italy are ready to let football do the talking again as Roberto Mancini kickstarts his second spell in charge.
On Friday, the Azzurri begin their UEFA Nations League campaign against Belgium at the Stadio Olimpico in Rome.
It will be Italy's first competitive match since a play-off defeat to Bosnia and Herzegovina in March sealed a humbling third consecutive failure to reach the World Cup.
The four-time world champions have been through something of a revolution since that grim night in Zenica.
Mancini, the architect of Italy's last major triumph at Euro 2020, is back as head coach, bringing a refreshed squad featuring plenty of young and untested players.
"We have to take the national team back to where it deserves to be," Mancini said on Monday.
"I'm here to win and I'm sure we'll enjoy some great moments."
Off the pitch, Claudio Ranieri and Gianfranco Zola have assumed roles as technical director and youth projects coordinator, respectively, while Milan-Cortina Olympics boss Giovanni Malago was elected as the new Italian Football Federation (FIGC) president in June.
This raft of changes came following widespread calls for root-and-branch reform of the Italian game in the wake of a qualifying calamity that ensured an entire generation has grown up without seeing their country at a World Cup.
But the road to get there was far from smooth.
Heads rolled after the defeat in Bosnia, with coach Gennaro Gattuso, delegation head Gianluigi Buffon and FIGC president Gabriele Gravina leaving.
When Malago became FIGC president, his first major move was to appoint AC Milan legend Paolo Maldini as technical director to oversee the hunt for a new coach.
After being turned away by Brazil boss Carlo Ancelotti, Maldini set his sights on Pep Guardiola.
"We went to meet him in Barcelona, we had lunch together, we talked for an entire day. He was very tempted," Maldini told Corriere della Sera.
"He came very close to accepting. He even started writing line-ups down on sheets of paper."
Maldini insisted that "money was never an issue" and Guardiola's refusal came down to "exhaustion" after a decade-long spell with Manchester City ended this summer.
The next name on Maldini's list was his former team-mate Andrea Pirlo. However, Pirlo pulled out of the running when controversy erupted over his role as a global ambassador for a Russian betting company, something he insisted was "exclusively commercial and sporting in nature".
The Pirlo saga led to Maldini and his advisor Leonardo sensationally quitting after just 16 days in post.
Maldini subsequently explained that "the conditions of trust no longer existed" with Malago, who was left back at square one.
Mancini soon emerged as the chosen one and was appointed in July in what proved to be a divisive move.
While the 61-year-old's track record speaks for itself, his decision to step down as Italy coach in August 2023 and take a lucrative job with Saudi Arabia angered many Italians.
When Mancini's return was confirmed, Rome-based newspaper Corriere dello Sport published an open letter accusing him of a "betrayal" and saying "apologies are not enough", while Sky Sport pundit Paolo Condo said his decision to "abandon the national team for a lavish payday" should have been a "road of no return".
Mancini immediately addressed these criticisms at his presentation.
"I'm very sorry. The Italy shirt was always very important to me. It was like losing the love of my life," he said.
Mancini's first squad underlined that a new era was underway, with nine new faces included in an intriguing 34-man selection.
Youngsters like Alessandro Romano and Eddy Kouadio were called, as well as players from outside Italy like Sporting Lisbon midfielder Issa Doumbia, Brentford's Michael Kayode and Nuernberg striker Mohamed Ali Zoma.
"I think it's right to have young players so we can get to know them directly, because that's the most important thing to have a very strong squad in the future," Mancini said.
