title: Security forces foil terrorists infiltration attempt in Kurram  state media
description: Intense retaliatory action forced Afghan Taliban personnel to abandon several posts  flee  sources say
content:
Intense retaliatory action forced Afghan Taliban personnel to abandon several posts, flee, sources say
Security forces on Wednesday foiled an infiltration attempt by terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij to cross into the Kurram sector from Afghanistan and responded promptly to firing by the Afghan Taliban.
The term Fitna al-Khawarij is used by the state to refer to terrorists affiliated with the banned TTP.
According to security sources, the infiltration attempt was made from Afghan Taliban posts in Nangarhar and Paktia provinces but was effectively thwarted by Pakistani troops deployed along the border.
Following the failure of the attempt, the Afghan Taliban opened unprovoked fire on Pakistani border posts using heavy weapons, mortars and other arms, sources added.
They further added that security forces responded effectively and targeted several Afghan Taliban border posts, mortar positions and defensive positions with small and heavy weapons, including artillery.
The intense retaliatory action forced Afghan Taliban personnel to abandon several posts and flee, it added.
Security forces continue to maintain complete control over the border areas and remain fully alert to respond promptly and decisively to any further provocation, the sources said.
Read: 6 personnel martyred in Balochistan Customs House attack, 21 terrorists killed across province: ISPR
On September 3, Security forces killed 15 terrorists who were trying to infiltrate through the Pakistan-Afghanistan border opposite North Waziristan District.
According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), security forces detected the "movement of a group of khawarij belonging to Indian-sponsored Fitna al Khawarij during the night of August 31 and September 1."
“Own troops responded professionally and with patience to engage them successfully,” the statement said. The ISPR further added that as a result of "precise and skillful engagement" that lasted for 36 hours, 15 terrorists were killed.
Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022, and over the same period, TTP attacks increased more than sevenfold to 838 from 118.

title: North Korea weightlifter sets three world records for Asian Games gold
description: Ri wins gold with a record breaking 215kg total in the 49kg class
content:
Ri wins gold with a record-breaking 215kg total in the 49kg class
North Korea's Ri Song Gum gave her country their first gold of the Asian Games on Wednesday in style, setting three world records in the women's 49kg class in Nagoya.
In the process she joined an elite club of just four weightlifters who have won three Asian Games gold medals.
Ri hauled 94kg above her head in the opening snatch discipline, one kilogramme more than the previous world standard mark of 93kg.
She then smashed the clean and jerk world mark of 115kg twice by hoisting 116kg and then 121kg.
Her total of 215kg obliterated the old world mark by 7kg.
India's Mirabai Chanu, the silver medallist at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, finally won an Asian Games medal at the third time of asking.
She had a total of 198kg after a snatch of 87kg and clean and jerk of 111kg while Indonesia's Diana Tri Wijayana took bronze on 191kg, with 88kg and 103kg respectively.
Ri became only the fourth lifter, and first woman, to win three Asian Games weightlifting golds.
She joined Iran's Mohammad Nassiri (1966-74), South Korea's Kim Tae-hyun (1990-98) and Iran's Behdad Salimi (2010-2018) who all won three golds. No one has ever won four.

title: AI risks  US Iran war to take center stage at UN
description: industry leaders are set to brief an emergency meeting of the UN Security Council
content:
Industry leaders are set to brief an emergency meeting of the UN Security Council
The future of artificial intelligence and the stalled US war against Iran, with its ripple effect on the global economy, are expected to dominate the UN gathering of world leaders on Wednesday.
Following weeks of worldwide headlines about risks of uncontrollable AI -- and calls for a slowdown -- industry leaders are set to brief an emergency meeting of the UN Security Council.
Sam Altman of OpenAI, Dario Amodei of Anthropic and Clement Delangue of Hugging Face will brief the 15-member Council, the United Nations' top body.
Hugging Face, a repository of AI models, was the target of a recent cyberattack by autonomous OpenAI software, the first in a series of incidents that have raised alarm bells over the rapidly evolving technology.
Read: OpenAI's rogue agents probed Hugging Face for weaknesses two months before major hack
Meanwhile, the annual parade of UN General Assembly speeches is set to continue, with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian arriving late on Tuesday, according to Iranian state media, to address the world body for the first time since the United States and Israel launched attacks on his country.
The strikes in late February sparked a war that engulfed the Middle East, and the Trump administration has so far yet to reach a deal with Tehran to end the conflict.
Tehran retaliated by blocking the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for energy transit, sparking a surge in global oil prices.
The recent Houthi takeover of Yemen's Red Sea coast has also heightened fears over global trade and shipping through the vital Bab al-Mandab Strait.
Pezeshkian's speech will come a day after Trump raised the possibility that he could "annihilate the Islamic Republic" and "drive them into hell." During his remarks, all but one member of the Iranian delegation walked out.
Read more: Iran says it conveyed conditions for end to war to US through Qatari mediator, IRNA reports
Trump made the comments in a fire-and-brimstone speech on Tuesday, but he also revealed that there were talks between the two sides for the first time in months.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Trump's roving envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner on the sidelines of the UN's signature diplomatic gathering.
Araghchi said that Tehran's demands included "the immediate lifting of the (US) naval blockade, the prompt payment of all Iranian assets that have been frozen, and an end to the war on all resistance fronts," state news agency IRIB reported.
Outside the UN on Tuesday, there was a vigil with protesters demonstrating against Tehran's use of the death penalty.
Besides conflict in the Middle East, Russia's war against Ukraine will again be raised among global diplomatic circles on Wednesday.
A Security Council meeting on Ukraine is scheduled for 11:00 am (2000 PKT), while President Volodymyr Zelensky is due to address the UN General Assembly as well.
Zelensky, after meeting with Trump on Tuesday, said that Washington and Kyiv want the war with Russia to end "before winter."
He added that he is ready to halt strikes on Russian energy sites if Moscow agreed to do the same.
In his speech on Tuesday, Trump rejected international regulation of AI, calling such proposals a "globalist scheme."
Also read: Trump says there will be a deal with Iran after the midterms
"The very same people who said we'll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming... are now saying that AI is going to kill us all," Trump said.
But just hours after Trump spoke, Macron took to the rostrum and defiantly called for the creation of an open-source AI model not dependent on the United States or China.
"I don't want anyone to become the vassal of one of the great powers," he said. "Rather, we must come together to build an open-source frontier model, a cutting-edge model."

title: La Liga president hits out at Real Madrid refereeing  conspiracy  claims
description: The dispute follows Madrid   s 2 1 derby defeat to Atletico  with referees later admitting a VAR error
content:
The dispute follows Madrid’s 2-1 derby defeat to Atletico, with referees later admitting a VAR error
La Liga president Javier Tebas hit out on Tuesday at what he deemed accusations of a refereeing "conspiracy" by Real Madrid following their derby loss to Atletico Madrid.
Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho brought two printed screen-shots of what he thought were red-card tackles committed by Atletico players to his post-match press conference following Sunday's 2-1 defeat.
Tebas responded to a pro-Real article on social media with a lengthy riposte to allegations of a "conspiracy" against the 15-time European champions.
"Here they go again, the mouthpieces and the regime's television, building the same old narrative -- the permanent conspiracy," said Tebas, who has often been at odds with Real Madrid and the club's outspoken president Florentino Perez.
"This article goes further -- it claims that referees harm 'The business that feeds them'.
"What exactly is it asking for? Refereeing based on revenue, viewership, or the badge? What a way to understand equality in the competition.
"Real Madrid are crucial to La Liga. But claiming that 'La Liga is worth nothing' without them reveals the disdain for the other clubs, their fans, and their history. The competition belongs to no one."
Madrid have made a stuttering start to the season and already sit six points behind champions and early leaders Barcelona in the La Liga table.
"Claiming that referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy," added Tebas.
"That narrative serves as an excuse to cover up other shortcomings that are plain to see in these first matches of the season.
"It's more comfortable to point to a conspiracy than to explain what's happening on the pitch."
Madrid responded to Tebas's comments later Tuesday, calling them "intolerable".
"Our club considers it intolerable that the president of La Liga uses his institutional position to continue discrediting and attacking Real Madrid in the manner he does in each of his public interventions," the club said in a statement.
"Given this inappropriate behavior, which has persisted over time, we believe that professional football in Spain urgently needs a leader capable of managing it and developing its full potential with the fundamental duty of neutrality."
Mourinho returned for a second spell in charge at the Santiago Bernabeu in the close-season, tasked with ending a two-year spell without a major trophy.
On Tuesday, the technical committee of referees acknowledged "a clear and obvious error" regarding one of the fouls cited by Mourinho, adding that VAR should have intervened.

The 27-year-old tops the scoring charts at the World Cup, Champions League and La Liga
France and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe continued his media push to win the Ballon d'Or by insisting on Tuesday that he feels confident he will claim the prestigious award.
The 27-year-old was top scorer at the World Cup in the summer and both last season's Champions League and La Liga.
But he won nothing as France lost in the World Cup semi-finals and Real finished second in La Liga and were bundled out of the Champions League by Bayern Munich in the quarter-finals.
"They won't announce a team in the envelope, they will announce a player," Mbappe told RFI radio station.
"The ability to perform individually and produce eye-catching moments, that's what stands out to people for an award like this.
"I was top scorer in all the biggest competitions and I think that this could be a good year for me, and I really feel it."
The former Monaco and Paris Saint-Germain player scored 25 La Liga goals last season, 15 in the Champions League and another 10 at the World Cup, enabling him to become the all-time leading goalscorer in the tournament, with 22 strikes in total.
But he faces tough competition for the Ballon d'Or, particularly from players who enjoyed success with their club or country in 2026.
Spanish pair Lamine Yamal and Ferran Torres won La Liga with Barcelona and the World Cup, PSG duo Ousamne Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia won the French Ligue 1 and the Champions League, while Harry Kane was a Bundesliga champion with Bayern Munich.

title: ADB projects Pakistan s FY2027 growth at 3 7   inflation at 8 3
description: Says govt consumption increased by 11 2   while real exports rose 5 9  and real imports fell 6 8
content:
Says govt consumption increased by 11.2%, while real exports rose 5.9% and real imports fell 6.8%
Pakistan’s economic growth was projected to remain at 3.7 per cent in fiscal year 2027 while inflation was expected to rise to 8.3 per cent, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) said on Wednesday, warning that higher energy and import costs and prolonged geopolitical tensions could weigh on the outlook.
In its Asian Development Outlook (ADO) September 2026 edition , the flagship biannual publication – the bank retained its growth forecast for Pakistan at 3.7 per cent for FY2027, while projecting inflation above the State Bank of Pakistan’s medium-term target range of 5-7 per cent.
The bank said Pakistan’s economy had expanded by 3.7 per cent in FY2026, which ended on June 30, up from 3.2 per cent a year earlier, with the recovery supported by improving credit conditions and broad-based growth.
“Growth strengthened in fiscal year (FY) 2026, although the Middle East conflict curbed activity in the last quarter,” the ADB said.
ADB Growth Projections 2026: People’s Republic of China: 4.6% India: 7% Indonesia: 5.2% Thailand: 2% Philippines: 3.3% Vietnam: 7.8% Bangladesh: 3.7% Malaysia: 4.9% Pakistan: 3.7% Türkiye: 2.8% Kazakhstan: 4.8% 🔗 More in our #ADO2026 September update:… pic.twitter.com/Who5VAmNEk
It said economic expansion had averaged 4 per cent during the first three quarters of FY2026, supported by the lagged effects of monetary easing and improved business confidence, but slowed in April-June as the government’s response to the Middle East conflict weakened domestic spending.
The recovery was broad-based, with services, manufacturing and agriculture all contributing to growth. Agriculture expanded by 2.9 per cent, industrial output increased by 3.5 per cent, and services grew by 4.1 per cent during FY2026.
Manufacturing was a major contributor to the industrial recovery, with growth of 6.6 per cent, while information and communications expanded by 7.5 per cent on the back of stronger service exports.
“Private investment propelled growth,” the ADB said, noting that private investment rose 8.6 per cent in real terms in FY2026 as borrowing costs fell and business confidence improved.
Household consumption, however, grew by only 0.8 per cent, compared with 2.1 per cent in FY2025, as higher global energy prices reduced real incomes. Government consumption increased by 11.2 per cent, while real exports of goods and services rose 5.9 per cent and real imports fell 6.8 per cent.
Read: Fixed tax draws only 2 new traders
The bank said inflation had become a growing constraint, averaging 7.1 per cent in FY2026 compared with 4.5 per cent a year earlier. Price pressures accelerated sharply in the second half of the fiscal year as food and energy costs increased.
Headline inflation reached 11.7 per cent in May 2026 after a record fuel price increase in April, before easing to 11.1 per cent in June and 9.2 per cent in July as global energy pressures moderated.
For FY2027, the ADB expected inflation to remain above the central bank’s target range as elevated fuel, logistics and agricultural input costs continued to feed into domestic prices. “Inflation is projected to reach 8.3% in FY2027, above the central bank’s medium-term target range, complicating monetary policy,” the bank said.
The ADB said the forecast assumed inflation would gradually moderate from 11.1 per cent in June 2026 and return to the 5-7 per cent range in the second half of FY2027.
It warned that domestic fuel and logistics costs were likely to remain elevated during the first half of the fiscal year because of disruptions to global energy supplies, while higher international fertiliser prices could push up agricultural input and food costs.
Read More: PM unveils austerity measures as Gulf conflict spirals
A recovery in economic activity and rising import costs could also put pressure on the exchange rate and contribute to imported inflation, the bank said.
The ADB said the central bank would face a difficult balance between supporting economic activity and bringing inflation back within its target range, with the real policy rate having fallen close to zero by the end of FY2026.
On the fiscal side, Pakistan’s consolidated budget deficit narrowed to 2.6 per cent of GDP in FY2026 from 5.4 per cent a year earlier, while the primary surplus reached 2.9 per cent of GDP, exceeding the 2.6 per cent target under the International Monetary Fund’s Extended Fund Facility programme.
However, the improvement was driven mainly by lower interest payments rather than a broadening of the tax base. Federal Board of Revenue collections increased 10.8 per cent year-on-year but fell short of the IMF programme benchmark by about Rs969 billion.
“The improvement came mainly from interest savings rather than a broadening of the revenue base,” the ADB said.
The bank said Pakistan’s current account remained broadly balanced in FY2026, recording a deficit of $304 million, or 0.1 per cent of GDP, compared with a surplus of $1.8 billion a year earlier.
Also read: ADB cuts growth forecast to 3.7%
The merchandise trade deficit widened to $33.7 billion from $26.8 billion as exports weakened and imports increased faster than workers’ remittances. Merchandise exports fell 4.7 per cent to $30.8 billion, while imports rose 9 per cent to $64.5 billion.
Workers’ remittances, however, increased 8.6 per cent to $41.6 billion, while the services deficit narrowed to $2 billion as service exports grew 18.6 per cent, led by information technology, business services and travel receipts.
“Workers’ remittances grew by 8.6% to $41.6 billion, underpinned by external stability and a market-determined exchange rate,” the ADB said.
The bank also noted improved access to international financing, with the government issuing a $750 million Eurobond and a $250 million Panda bond in April-May 2026.
Gross international reserves increased from $14.5 billion at the end of June 2025 to $18.5 billion at the end of June 2026, raising import cover to 2.9 months.
The ADB said sustained implementation of the IMF programme, renewed access to international capital markets and sovereign credit-rating upgrades had improved investor confidence and reduced financing costs.
For FY2027, private investment was expected to remain the main driver of demand, supported by lower input tariffs under the National Tariff Policy 2025-2030 and a reduced corporate tax burden following a cut in the super tax.
The bank said services were likely to remain resilient, particularly because of information technology exports, while manufacturing could face slower momentum as higher energy prices raised production costs.
Construction was expected to benefit from budget incentives, including reduced property transaction taxes and a higher interest subsidy under the prime minister’s housing scheme.
However, the ADB warned that Pakistan remained particularly vulnerable to external shocks because of its dependence on imported petroleum and remittances from Gulf economies.
“External factors provide downside risks,” it said, warning that an escalation of the Middle East conflict could raise energy import costs, intensify domestic inflation and disrupt labour markets in Gulf countries, limiting workers’ remittances.
The bank also identified weaker-than-targeted tax collection, weather-related agricultural shocks, tighter global financial conditions and delays in structural reforms as risks to the outlook.
It said Pakistan could strengthen its medium-term growth prospects through reforms in taxation, energy, state-owned enterprises and tariffs, while expanding its information technology and digital services sectors.
“Sustained performance under the EFF provides a credible macroeconomic anchor, but realising medium-term potential growth will depend on the consistent implementation of structural reforms,” the ADB said.

title: Klopp promises fresh approach as Germany reign begins
description: The former Liverpool boss starts his tenure with a trip to the Netherlands on Thursday
content:
The former Liverpool boss starts his tenure with a trip to the Netherlands on Thursday
Germany coach Jurgen Klopp has promised to bring a "new approach" to the country's flagging fortunes, as the four-time world champions begin their latest tilt at a maiden Nations League title.
On Monday, just days out from his side's opening match away against the Netherlands in Amsterdam on Thursday, Klopp recorded a video appealing to Germany fans at home and abroad.
Speaking English, the former Liverpool manager introduced himself as "the new one" in charge and thanked fans who "support us from all over the world".
The "new one" quip was a tip of the hat to the "normal one" quote from his Liverpool unveiling which became intimately entwined with his nine-year Anfield stint.
Now back in the dugout for the first time since leaving Merseyside in 2024, Klopp has promised a "new approach" as he hopes to return the fallen giants to the summit of the game.
"We will try everything to make our new approach visible. I expect more immediately," Klopp said Thursday.
"It might get a bit wild, but I'll take that; it just has to be lively."
After the trip to Amsterdam, Klopp will make his Germany home debut in Augsburg on September 27 against Greece, before hosting Serbia four days later and then concluding his opening taste of international football in Thessaloniki the following Sunday.
Klopp's consistent success at Mainz, Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool have given him a degree of standing shared by nobody else in modern German football.
Plenty of high-profile coaches have taken the Germany job, but few have been given so much control or so much scope to shake up the status quo.
His first step -- naming a 44-man squad including 16 uncapped players which will be split into two match-day groups, while leaving out fan favourite Deniz Undav -- showed a willingness to think differently.
Freiburg right-back Philipp Treu is one of those new call-ups. Not previously on the radar for German selection, the 25-year-old has never played under Klopp but summed up the attitude of many of those players who have been transformed by the coach over the years.
"You feel like you'd walk through fire for him," Treu said Tuesday, adding Klopp "is an incredible guy".
Another newcomer, Eintracht Frankfurt striker Younes Ebnoutalib, was courted by African champions and 2022 World Cup semi-finalists Morocco.
The Frankfurt-born forward opened up on his decision to choose Germany, while summing up Klopp's appeal.
"When Klopp calls, you have to go. He's one of the best coaches in the world and he brings a really positive energy," he said.
Semi-final regulars at major tournaments for more than a decade, Germany have won just one knockout game at the World Cup or Euros since 2016.
Klopp's task of breathing life into Germany's flagging fortunes is a mammoth one, but the 59-year-old is no stranger to resuscitating fallen giants.
Dortmund had only just beaten bankruptcy when Klopp took over. Inside five years, Klopp's Dortmund had won two league titles and played in a Champions League final.
At Liverpool, Klopp took a side who had made the Champions League just once in the past five seasons to three finals, winning one. And most important of all, he brought the league title back to Anfield for the first time in the Premier League era.
With a fractured media made up of former players eager to criticise the German FA (DFB), Klopp has set about uniting the country towards a common cause.
At his squad announcement, Klopp handed out sponsor hats in German flag colours with the message "one of 83 million".
Klopp has also contacted members of the DFB All-Stars -- former players with at least one cap -- asking for support, saying "we are all the national team".
Former player turned influential commentator Lothar Matthaeus was clearly won over by Klopp's charm offensive, writing in his Sky Germany column that "everything will be better" with Klopp in the main job.
"That wasn't always the case in recent years, but trust is important," the former Ballon d'Or winner wrote.

title: UNSC condemns Kohat terrorist attack  calls for perpetrators to be held accountable
description: Members of Security Council express their deepest sympathy and condolences to families of victims
content:
Members of Security Council express their deepest sympathy and condolences to families of victims
The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) on Wednesday condemned in the strongest terms a terrorist attack at a mosque in Kohat, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) province, describing it as a “heinous and cowardly suicide bombing terrorist attack”.
At least 23 people , including 15 police personnel , were martyred in the blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers on September 18 . Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
According to a statement issued by Council President Jérôme Bonnafont (France), the members of the Security Council condemned in the strongest terms the “heinous and cowardly suicide bombing terrorist attack” at a mosque in Kohat.
"The members of the Security Council expressed their “deepest sympathy and condolences” to the families of the victims and to the government and the people of Pakistan and wished a “speedy and full recovery” to those who were injured," the statement added.
"The members of the Security Council reaffirmed that terrorism in all its forms and manifestations constitutes one of the most serious threats to international peace and security," it added.
UN SECURITY COUNCIL PRESS STATEMENT ON TERRORIST ATTACK IN KOHAT, KHYBER PAKHTUNKHWA, PAKISTAN The following Security Council press statement was issued today by Council President Jérôme Bonnafont (France). The members of the Security Council condemned in the strongest terms…
They underlined the need to hold “perpetrators, organisers, financiers and sponsors of these reprehensible acts of terrorism accountable and bring them to justice”. They urged all States, in accordance with their obligations under international law and relevant Security Council resolutions, to cooperate actively with the Government of Pakistan in this regard.
The statement further added that the members of the Security Council reiterated that “any acts of terrorism are criminal and unjustifiable, regardless of their motivation, wherever, whenever and by whomsoever committed”.
They reaffirmed the need for all States to combat, by all means, in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations and other obligations under international law, including international human rights law, international refugee law and international humanitarian law, threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts, the statement concluded.
Read: President Zardari, PM Shehbaz strongly condemn Kohat Police Lines blast
Islamabad has repeatedly asked the Taliban regime to deny the use of Afghan soil for terrorist attacks inside Pakistan. However, the de facto rulers in Kabul have been reluctant to take action against terrorist groups operating from their territory.
Yesterday, Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Field Marshal Asim Munir directed formations to remain vigilant and uphold the highest standards of operational preparedness during a visit to Corps Headquarters Peshawar.
The visit took place days after Pakistan carried out airstrikes on terrorist hideouts in various locations in the regions bordering Afghanistan following brazen terror attacks in K-P.
According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the CDF was briefed on the prevailing security situation in K-P, ongoing counter-terrorism operations, border management measures and operational preparedness of formations deployed in the province.
The chief of army staff commended the high morale, readiness and professionalism of officers and troops, acknowledging their steadfast commitment to safeguarding the country and its people.

title: Pakistan Navy  Coast Guards foil smuggling attempt in Balochistan s Pishukan
description: PM Shehbaz praises operation  highlights importance of institutional coordination to  uproot menace of smuggling
content:
PM Shehbaz praises operation, highlights importance of institutional coordination to 'uproot menace of smuggling'
The Pakistan Navy and Coast Guards in coordination with the Joint Maritime Information Coordination Centre (JMICC), confiscated "a sizeable quantity" of liquor and illegal medicines in the Pishukan area of Balochistan, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Wednesday.
According to the military's media wing, the joint intelligence-based operation "thwarted an attempt to smuggle a large cache of contraband items" in the area. The operation was carried out on "actionable intelligence," the ISPR said, adding that the "seized contraband items have been handed over to the Pakistan Coast Guards for further legal proceedings."
The military's media wing noted that the "successful joint operation underscores the effectiveness of inter-agency coordination in countering smuggling while highlighting the resolve of the Pakistan Navy and Pakistan Coast Guards to prevent the use of Pakistani waters and land for illicit activities."
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised the Navy and Coast Guards for "successfully foiling a major smuggling attempt in the Pishukan area of Balochistan."
According to the Prime Minister's Office (PMO), the premier noted that as a result of the joint action, carried out under a joint anti-smuggling operation, a large stockpile of prohibited items, including liquor and illegal medicines, were confiscated.
Praising the operation, PM Shehbaz stated that "mutual coordination and cooperation between institutions is of utmost importance for uprooting the menace of smuggling from the country."
The prime minister also praised the "professional capabilities, alertness, and preparedness of the personnel who took part in the operation," the PMO's statement noted.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also commended the Pakistan Navy and Coast Guards for foiling the smuggling attempt, appreciating "the professional expertise of the entire team involved in the joint operation."

پاکستان نیوی اور پاکستان کوسٹ گارڈز نے ​جوائنٹ آپریشن کے تحت بڑی مقدار میں غیر ممنوعہ اشیاء کی سمگلنگ کی کوشش ناکام بنائی۔ سمگلنگ کے خاتمے کے لیے اداروں کے مابین موثر باہمی رابطہ اور تعاون سے مشترکہ آپریشن نتیجہ خیز ثابت ہوا۔

"A zero-tolerance policy against the mafia involved in smuggling will continue to be strictly enforced," the interior minister said.
سمگلنگ ملکی معیشت کے لیے زہرِ قاتل ، خاتمے کے لیے ادارے متحرک ہیں، ​سمگلنگ میں ملوث مافیا کے خلاف زیرو ٹالرنس پالیسی پر سختی سے عملدرآمد جاری رہے گا، محسن نقوی
Earlier this year, in April, the Pakistan Maritime Security Agency (PMSA) confiscated foreign liquor worth Rs200 million during a joint intelligence-based operation in the Arabian Sea.
A maritime interdiction operation had led to the interception of a stateless vessel carrying a large quantity of illicit liquor that was concealed onboard and intended for unlawful distribution.
The operation was carried out through the coordinated efforts of the Pakistan Navy, PMSA, the JMICC, and the Anti-Narcotics Force of Sindh.
Even earlier in the year, in February, the Border Military Police seized silver and narcotics worth more than Rs100 million during a major crackdown on smuggling along the inter-provincial border, as part of a broader campaign against drug trafficking and illegal trade.

During the operation, authorities recovered 41 kilogrammes of silver, 13kg of crystal meth (ice) and 55kg of hashish, with the contraband allegedly being smuggled from Balochistan into Punjab.
Towards the end of last year, too, agencies continued coordinated action against the smuggling of contraband items. In November 2025 , the ANF seized narcotics worth more than $154 million from an LPG container during an intelligence-based operation in Balochistan.
The operation was launched after credible evidence indicated that a Drug Trafficking Organisation operation out of Panjgur was preparing to transport a large consignment of narcotics to the Gwadar-Pasni coastline for onward smuggling by way of sea.

title: Milne returns to New Zealand squad for India T20 series
description: The Black Caps include 13 players from their World Cup runners up squad
content:
The Black Caps include 13 players from their World Cup runners-up squad
New Zealand speedster Adam Milne will return to the Black Cap's T20 squad for next month's home series against India after more than a year out of international cricket, coach Rob Walter said Wednesday.
India's tour of New Zealand will include five T20s, five ODIs and two Test matches, with the opening T20 set for Christchurch on October 22.
Thirteen of the 16-strong squad were part of the New Zealand side that finished runners-up to India at the T20 World Cup in March.
"We've got a near full-strength squad that covers all bases and I'm excited to see how we compete against the current T20 world champions," Black Caps coach Walter said.
Milne, 34, last played for New Zealand more than a year ago and has amassed 56 international caps.
He missed the World Cup due to injury, as did off-spin all-rounder Michael Bracewell who also returns to the squad.
Walter confirmed Rachin Ravindra will miss the series due to an injury suffered during a promotional shoot last week, but it is hoped he might return for the ODI series.
T20 specialists Tim Seifert and Finn Allen were named in the squad, as Walter said he sought to pick the strongest team possible.
"Our priority is winning games and putting the best team on the park, but we also have to keep in mind the volume of cricket in the coming months," he said.
"We're very fortunate with the depth that we've got to call upon, so we'll look to use all 16 squad members throughout the series as we manage workloads."
New Zealand: Mitchell Santner (capt), Finn Allen, Michael Bracewell, Mark Chapman, Devon Conway, Jacob Duffy, Lockie Ferguson, Zak Foulkes, Matt Henry, Bevon Jacobs, Kyle Jamieson, Adam Milne, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Tim Seifert, Nathan Smith.

title: MLS coach axed for telling female ref  It s a man s game
description: Columbus dismiss Higuain after his conduct towards a female referee
content:
Columbus dismiss Higuain after his conduct towards a female referee
Columbus Crew sacked Argentine reserve team coach Federico Higuain for telling a female referee "Don't forget this is a man's game" while refusing to release her from a handshake, the Major League Soccer club said Tuesday.
Higuain, the brother of former Argentina and Real Madrid forward Gonzalo Higuain, had already received a red card and a two-match suspension for the incident before the team dismissed him.
"We determined it's in the best interest of our Club, players and support staff to dismiss Federico Higuaín from his responsibilities," said Columbus Crew general manager Issa Tall.
"After conversations this week and further assessing the past month, our Club's standards of what's expected from a leader for one of our teams have not been met."
Higuain during follow-up talks with the club was "unwilling to reflect or take accountability for his actions, nor did he offer a public apology," the Athletic reported, citing anonymous club sources.
The incident occurred during a game in MLS's developmental MLS NEXT Pro league.
According to the referees' union, Higuain "committed two deliberate acts of physical abuse and sexism against a female official -- squeezing her hand and refusing to let go after being told to stop three times.
"This physical intimidation was compounded by a demeaning, sexist remark to the official: 'Don't forget, this is a man's game,'" said the Professional Soccer Referees Association.
The union criticized the league's initial two-game suspension as falling "drastically short," and called for at least a six-game suspension.
"Women make every level of this game better. They should not have to endure intimidation or degrading comments to prove it," it said in a statement.
"Our female officials have proven their excellence on the world stage. They deserve the same respect, dignity, and safe working environment as every other official."

title: India s unilateral attempt to suspend IWT has introduced  dangerous dimension   FM Dar
description: Says the May India  Pakistan conflict highlighted the dangers of leaving the Kashmir dispute unresolved
content:
Says international obligations cannot be set aside when they become inconvenient
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister (FM) Ishaq Dar on Wednesday said India’s unilateral attempt to hold the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance had introduced another “dangerous dimension”, adding that international obligations cannot be set aside when they become inconvenient.
“India’s unilateral attempt to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance has introduced another dangerous dimension. The Treaty is a binding international agreement and contains no provision permitting its unilateral suspension,” FM Dar said while addressing the OIC Contact Group’s ministerial meeting on Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK) in New York, on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.
He said the Court of Arbitration had reaffirmed that unilateral action by one party could not deprive the court of its competence and had underscored the continuing force of the Treaty’s obligations, including those governing the Western Rivers.
“International obligations cannot be set aside when they become inconvenient. India cannot invoke domestic law to negate Security Council resolutions on Jammu and Kashmir, any more than it can resort to unilateral measures to evade its binding obligations under the Indus Waters Treaty,” the foreign minister said.
FM Dar further said treaties and international commitments must be respected in good faith.
🔈 PR No. 2️⃣5️⃣6️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Remarks by the Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 at the Ministerial Meeting of the OIC Contact Group on Jammu and Kashmir, on the sidelines of the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly, New York 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/LcT2Uf5eU1
FM Dar urged the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) to intensify diplomatic efforts over IIOJK, saying the bloc’s “principled solidarity” needed to be translated into “sustained diplomatic action”.
He urged OIC member states to maintain a “unified and visible OIC position” at the UN and other international forums.
The foreign minister called for intensified efforts to implement relevant UN Security Council resolutions and urged the OIC to press India to reverse “illegal measures” taken since August 2019.
FM Dar also called for the release of “all political prisoners and those arbitrarily detained” and demanded unrestricted access to the disputed territory for the OIC special envoy, fact-finding missions, UN special procedures, international media and independent observers.
He said the people of IIOJK had waited for almost eight decades for the international community to honour what he called a “solemn promise” — their right to determine their own future through a free and impartial process under UN auspices.
According to FM Dar, India, since August 2019, pursued measures to change the “demographic, political and cultural character” of Jammu and Kashmir.
He said that political and civic space had been systematically restricted, with Kashmiri leaders, activists, journalists and young people facing arbitrary detention and persecution under laws including the Public Safety Act and Unlawful Activities Prevention Act.
Video of the remarks by the Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 at the Ministerial Meeting of the OIC Contact Group on Jammu and Kashmir, on the sidelines of the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly in New York. pic.twitter.com/bwzNScL5fr
FM Dar also said changes to domicile and land laws, electoral constituencies and voter rolls, along with property demolitions and measures affecting the region’s cultural and religious heritage, were used to alter “realities on the ground”.
On media freedoms, he said journalists faced “intimidation, surveillance and detention”, while the Kashmir Press Club had been forcibly closed and social media accounts blocked.
“These are not isolated violations. Taken together, they reveal a sustained effort to silence a people, transform the identity of their homeland and foreclose their right to self-determination and their own future,” he said.
FM Dar cited a joint communication by UN special procedures in October 2025, which he said had referred to the detention of about 2,800 people, including journalists and human rights defenders, as well as home demolitions, the blocking of about 8,000 social media accounts and incidents of hate speech, intimidation and dehumanisation targeting Kashmiris and Muslims.
He also referred to the Pakistan-India military conflict in May 2025 following the Pahalgam incident, saying it had highlighted the dangers of leaving the Kashmir dispute unresolved.
Read: Pakistan, seven other Muslim countries demand Israel to fulfil Gaza ceasefire commitments
The minister said the confrontation between the two countries had demonstrated the risks of allowing the dispute to remain unresolved.
“Two nuclear-armed states came into direct military conflict over a dispute that has remained unresolved for almost eight decades,” he said.
FM Dar said the confrontation showed that “military force cannot resolve long-standing political disputes”, while “dialogue, diplomacy and the just resolution of the root causes in accordance with international law” remained the sustainable way forward.
Read More: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia sign visa waiver agreement for diplomatic, official passport holders
He said Kashmir remained an “internationally recognised dispute” on the UN Security Council agenda and argued that no domestic legislation, judicial verdict, electoral exercise or demographic change could replace the Kashmiri people’s “inalienable right to self-determination”.
"Pakistan remained committed to a just and peaceful settlement of the dispute in accordance with relevant Security Council resolutions and the wishes of the Kashmiri people," he said.
He urged the OIC to strengthen coordinated diplomacy in New York and Geneva and support its call for an updated report on Jammu and Kashmir.
“The Kashmiri people are only asking the international community to deliver what was provided to them decades ago,” FM Dar said.
He said their right to self-determination was already recognised and that the mechanism for its exercise had been prescribed by the UN Security Council.
FM Dar urged the OIC to maintain its “unwavering solidarity” with the Kashmiri people while keeping Jammu and Kashmir high on the international agenda.
The meeting concluded with the OIC Contact Group considering a joint communique, FM Dar said.

title: Oil falls  1 on better supply outlook  hopes for US Iran talks
description: Brent crude futures fall  1 09  or 1 1   to  98 16 a barrel
content:
Brent crude futures fall $1.09, or 1.1%, to $98.16 a barrel
Oil prices extended declines on Wednesday as investors eyed improved ​Gulf supply after Saudi Arabia restarted operations at a critical pipeline.
Hopes for a diplomatic solution to ‌the US-Iran war also weighed on prices.
Brent crude futures fell $1.09, or 1.1%, to $98.16 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate futures fell $1.50, or 1.67%, to $89.01 per barrel.
Both contracts have declined for six consecutive sessions to around two-week lows.
While US President Donald Trump warned on Tuesday ​that he could "annihilate" Iran, he also said his envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner had held productive talks with mediators ​of Iran to end the war.
"I think there's a lot of momentum for them to ⁠make a deal," Trump said.
Optimism around improved supply and a push to end the nearly seven-month conflict drove benchmark ​Brent down to close below $100 a barrel on Tuesday for the first time since September 8.
“The market is currently feeling ​more constructive about the global oil supply picture than it was a few weeks ago,” said Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade.
“The meeting of US and Iranian delegations in New York has given traders a glimmer of hope ... Despite the continued tough rhetoric, including threats ​of ‘annihilation,’ the market is choosing to price in the possibility of talks.”
On Tuesday, Saudi Arabia restarted operations on its East-West ​Pipeline to the Red Sea, three sources briefed on the matter said, with signs of an increase in Middle Eastern oil flows.
Drone ‌attacks, which ⁠Saudi Arabia has blamed on Iraqi militia, forced the kingdom to shut the pipeline on September 11, halting crude loadings at the kingdom's Yanbu port.
Since the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupted oil flows from Saudi Arabia and its Gulf neighbours through the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh has been using the pipeline to reroute around 4 million barrels per day — around ​4% of global supply — to ​Yanbu.
Saudi on Tuesday also offered ⁠more barrels to Asian refiners for lifting from locations outside of the Strait of Hormuz.
Iraq, too, is increasing oil exports, its oil minister, Basim Mohammed, said on Tuesday. The country ​is exporting more than 3 million bpd, he said, and expects to boost exports via ​Turkey to more ⁠than 600,000 bpd.
Provisional data from ship-tracking firms Vortexa and Kpler pegged Iraqi crude exports in August at 2.3 million and 2.17 million bpd, respectively, up from July's level but below February's pre-war level of 3.7 million and 3.362 million bpd.
Adding to downward pressure ⁠on ​oil prices, industry data showed US crude inventories rose by 1.8 million barrels ​in the week to September 18. Analysts polled by Reuters had expected a decline.
Official weekly inventory figures from the US Energy Information Administration are due at 10:30 ​am ET (1430 GMT).

The Koreans reach the last eight after a 3-1 victory over India in Seoul
South Korea's reward for reaching the Davis Cup finals for the first time ever is a quarter-final tie against hosts and holders Italy, following the draw in Bologna on Tuesday.
The Italians have been kept on the opposite side of the draw from Spain, the team they beat in last year's final.
South Korea reached the finals courtesy of a 3-1 win over India at the weekend when Kwon Soon-woo brushed Sumit Nagal aside 6-1, 6-2 to clinch the decisive point.
"I am very pleased to be able to create history with the fans today," Chung said after the match. "
I am just very grateful for this opportunity. In individual matches, I believe, there is a certain happiness to winning, but given that it’s Davis Cup and it’s a team sport, it gives winning a better meaning. With Korea now as part of the biggest eight countries in tennis, there is some value to the name of the country."
"It means a lot to qualify for the Final 8 in Bologna," added Kwon. "I feel very prideful for my country and every team I play against, I give my best. When I play in a team, I know that I can’t let my teammates down. Given the fanbase of Davis Cup, the players have great motivation to keep the momentum on their side, the fans in Seoul brought that momentum in my favour."
The Italians are three-time defending champions but may be without world number one Jannik Sinner who missed the recent US Open because of a knee injury.
Sinner featured in the 2024 win over the Netherlands but was absent for the victories in 2023 and 2025.
The winner of that match-up will then meet either the Czech Republic or Canada in the semi-finals.
On the other side of the draw, last year's runners-up Spain will open with a quarter-final against Austria, before a possible semi-final against Britain or Germany.
World number three Carlos Alcaraz also did not play in last year's finals but Germany's Alexander Zverev, the winner of the US Open, played for Germany at the weekend and is expected to lead his country's bid for a first Davis Cup title since 1993.

title: England beat Sri Lanka in 1st ODI
description: Jacks    maiden five wicket haul and Brook   s 67 help the hosts take a 1 0 lead in the series
content:
Jacks’ maiden five-wicket haul and Brook’s 67 help the hosts take a 1-0 lead in the series
Will Jacks starred with both bat and ball as England overwhelmed Sri Lanka by 89 runs in the first one-day international at Chester-le-Street on Tuesday.
His quickfire 46 not out helped guide England to a competitive 265 all out after they lost momentum following the exit of captain Harry Brook for 67.
Off-spinner Jacks then took a fine 5-22 in seven overs, including three dismissals in what became the final over.
The tourists were bowled out for 176 with 13 overs to spare as England went 1-0 up in this three-match series following a 3-0 whitewash of Sri Lanka in the preceding T20 campaign.
Jacks's figures, his maiden five-wicket haul at this level, were the second-best by an England spinner in ODI cricket, surpassed only by Vic Marks's 5-20 against New Zealand in Wellington back in 1984.
"I think I am getting used to this role now. It is more about playing the situation and playing what is out there," said player-of-the-match Jacks after a win which followed seventh-placed England's 2-1 series success at home to top-ranked India in July.
Brook, meanwhile was heartened by another encouraging performance ahead of next year's 50-over World Cup in southern Africa.
"It wasn't the easiest of surfaces, but we want to be a team that can adapt to conditions as well as possible and manufacture wins where the conditions aren't quite in our favour," said Brook.
Turning to the "outstanding" Jacks, he said: "The way he's come in in this middle order and played this role in the middle order, taking a heavy part of the bowling on; he has been an awesome player to have in the side."
After Josh Tongue had Pathum Nissanka caught behind for 27 to leave Sri Lanka 48-2, the innings stalled, with Pavan Rathnayake taking 23 balls for his 13.
And 84-3 then became 85-4 when Jacks had Charith Asalanka lbw missing a sweep.
Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis fell in similar fashion when he too was lbw attempting to sweep Jacks for 42 off 60 balls, with his side faltering at 105-6.
Jacks's treble strike then ended the match.
Dunith Wellalage tried to revive the innings with 45 until he skyed Jacks to mid-on.
Two balls later, Jacks dismissed Asitha Fernando for nought before clean bowling No 11 Dilshan Madushanka for a golden duck with a classic off-break.
"I think our middle order is struggling with their batting," said Kusal Mendis. "Their batters started really well, and that is how they got their score... We needed more boundaries and earlier."
One consolation for the tourists came with leg-spinner Sachindu Colombage taking an impressive 3-44 on his Sri Lanka debut, including the prize wickets of Joe Root and Jos Buttler.
England, despite a tricky pitch on which the ball was not coming onto the bat, were on course for a large total at 182-3 in the 32nd over after Brook won the toss.
Sri Lanka, however, then took three quick wickets to reduce them to 199-6.
But Jacks's 47-ball innings, featuring four consecutive fours off Dushmantha Chameera, bolstered the total.
Test skipper Root had previously been dismissed for the first time in five ODI innings -- a sequence spanning 404 runs -- when he was bowled playing back for 44 to Colombage to end a stand of 68 with Brook.
Brook continued his fine form from the T20 series with a 49-ball fifty including six fours before he carved seamer Chameera straight to deep cover.
The second game of the series takes place at Headingley in Leeds on Thursday.

title: PM Shehbaz  Bill Gates discuss efforts to eradicate polio in Pakistan
description: PM  Bosnian counterpart agree to exchange of high level visits between the two countries in the coming period
content:
PM, Bosnian counterpart agree to exchange of high-level visits between the two countries in the coming period
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met Bill Gates in New York on Wednesday to discuss Pakistan’s efforts to eradicate polio, as he was in the US to attend the UN General Assembly session, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said.
According to the statement issued by the PMO, PM Shehbaz reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to completely eradicating polio and thanked the Gates Foundation for its longstanding support for the country’s efforts.
Bill Gates praised Pakistan’s ongoing efforts to eliminate the disease under Shehbaz’s leadership, saying eradication was crucial to protecting future generations from polio, the PMO said.
Gates also appreciated PM Shehbaz’s personal guidance to provincial governments on the nationwide polio vaccination programme.
Read: Two cops guarding polio team martyred in Balochistan's Noshki
The prime minister also discussed the Gates Foundation’s recent visit to Pakistan and its cooperation with the country in areas including polio eradication, maternal and child health, nutrition, immunisation, digitalisation and financial inclusion, according to the PMO.
PM Shehbaz welcomed the foundation’s role as a trusted partner in Pakistan’s socio-economic development and expressed interest in expanding cooperation in public health, agriculture, digital innovation and artificial intelligence.
He also briefed Gates on reforms in Pakistan’s agriculture sector, with a focus on innovation, biotechnology, climate resilience, research, and improving farmers’ capacity.
The two sides agreed to explore cooperation in developing improved seeds, livestock genetics and emerging agricultural technologies.
PM Shehbaz also invited Gates to visit Pakistan again soon, the PMO said.
PM Shehbaz holds meeting with Bosnian counterpart
Later, the prime minister held a meeting with Chairman of the Bosnia and Herzegovina Presidency Denis Bećirović on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.
The two sides reviewed the full spectrum of bilateral relations, including political, economic, defence, skilled labour mobility, education and cultural cooperation, and exchanged views on regional and international issues of mutual concern.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif met with the Chairman of Bosnia and Herzegovina Presidency H.E. Dr. Denis Becirovic on the sidelines of UN General Assembly 2026. On the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, Prime Minister of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan… pic.twitter.com/Jntwl2aCkP
PM Shehbaz reiterated the importance Pakistan attaches to its “historically close and fraternal ties” with Bosnia and Herzegovina and expressed his desire to elevate them into a broad-based partnership anchored in trade and economic cooperation.
The prime minister also reaffirmed Pakistan’s strong support for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina, saying regional stability depended on a “strong, stable and prosperous” Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Congratulating Bećirović on the formal opening of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s European Union accession talks, PM Shehbaz said Pakistan viewed the country as a potential regional trade and connectivity hub for Pakistani goods entering European and Western Balkan markets.
Bećirović praised Pakistan’s role in facilitating de-escalation and normalisation in West Asia and the Gulf region, according to the PMO.
He also fully supported Pakistan’s position on the “illegality of holding the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance”.
The two leaders agreed to remain in contact to further advance bilateral relations, including through an exchange of high-level visits between the two countries in the coming period, the PMO said.
Pakistan’s latest polio case was detected in an eight-month-old child in Bannu district, taking the national tally to four in 2026. The child was from Noor Union Council in Miryan tehsil, where vaccination teams had struggled to reach children consistently since 2025 because of security constraints. Three of the four cases reported this year have come from Bannu Division.
The persistence of the virus has been linked to children missing vaccinations in areas where insecurity restricts access. While overall transmission had declined, poliovirus continued to circulate in southern K-P, with access constraints allowing children to miss critical doses. Pakistan recorded 74 cases in 2024 and 31 in 2025, after cases had fallen sharply in previous years.
Security is therefore a major challenge for eradication efforts, with vaccination teams requiring protection to reach children in high-risk areas. The Express Tribune has also reported continuing concerns over vaccination gaps, community resistance and misinformation, while officials have stressed that children who are missed during campaigns remain vulnerable to infection.
Also read: The dilemma of our polio workforce
After a significant reduction in cases, from 147 in 2019 to just one in 2021, Pakistan has witnessed a resurgence. Since September 2023, there has been an increase in polio activity, particularly in Karachi.
While overall poliovirus transmission in the country has been declining, with cases falling from 74 in 2024 to 31 in 2025 and three so far in 2026, reflecting the impact of high-quality vaccination drives, virus circulation in southern K-P persists.
Polio is a highly contagious and incurable disease that can cause lifelong paralysis and, in some instances, death. However, the disease can be prevented through polio vaccines, which are safe and effective and have been used safely in 195 countries, including all Muslim countries.

title: Rate of glacier area loss increases to 4 9
description: Rate of glacier area loss increases to 4 9
content:
Expensive monitoring tools limit data reliability
The rate of glacier area loss in the Karakoram Highway region had increased from 3.2 per cent in the 1990s to 4.9 pc during 2010-2020, while Karakoram glaciers had declined by around 12pc between 1990 and 2020.
The startling fact was revealed in the Senate Standing Committee on Climate Change on Tuesday.
Officials informed the committee that there were 115 potentially dangerous glacial lakes, of which 105 had unfrozen as of Aug 5.
They said reliable data on the rate of glacier melt in Pakistan remained limited because glacier monitoring was an expensive exercise.
Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination Dr Musadik Malik glacier melt and flooding were two different phenomena and required different responses.
"Dams can help control floods, but glaciers cannot be stopped," he said, adding that glacier-related disasters could involve movement of land and terrain and were therefore not simply a matter of water flow.
The minister said the government was exploring the use of digital twinning for better understanding and modelling of climate- and glacier-related risks. He also stressed the need for establishing a digital laboratory.
Dr Malik said glaciers were disappearing across the region at an estimated rate of around 9 pc.
The minister said data from areas where conventional monitoring was difficult was increasingly being obtained through satellite systems.
He said towers had also been installed at locations where data was previously unavailable.
The climate change minister told the committee that Pakistan needed a coordinated mechanism under which relevant departments could automatically share data instead of waiting for formal requests from one another.
He said Prime Minister had constituted a committee under the Ministry of Defence to bring relevant departments and institutions onto a common platform.
Dr Malik said a virtual platform had already been developed as part of efforts to integrate available information.
He said glacier and water systems were dealt with by the Ministry of Water Resources, while the Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda) was responsible for devices monitoring snowfall and glacier melt.
Early warning systems, he said, fell under the Ministry of Defence, satellite data was handled by the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco), while disaster-related matters were dealt with by the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA).
"Whether civilian or defence-related, satellite data is with Suparco, while disaster management is the responsibility of NDMA. We need to bring these systems together so that the country can receive integrated and timely data," the minister said.
Dr Malik said the government was also working towards establishing a new authority to deal with civilian weather-related matters. The proposed authority, he said, would also serve as the Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination's think tank.
He added that proposals in this regard would be finalised and presented before the federal cabinet shortly.

title: M 1 Motorway closed indefinitely
description: M 1 Motorway closed indefinitely
content:
PTI divided over route, timing for Islamabad March
As the deadline for PTI's decisive long march on Islamabad approaches, the Centre has begun taking precautionary measures to prevent protesting caravans, particularly those from Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, from reaching the federal capital and to block major roads linking the province with the federal territory.
In this regard, the federal government has imposed a complete ban on traffic and advised motorists to avoid travelling on the Peshawar Motorway (M-1), which will remain closed to all types of traffic from 11:00pm on Wednesday, September 23, until further orders.
However, the M-2 Motorway (Islamabad-Lahore) would remain open to all types of traffic.
Motorists were advised to plan their journeys in accordance with the traffic advisory and strictly follow the directions issued by traffic police.
Meanwhile, the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) has decided to revise its strategy for a planned march on Islamabad on Sept 27, with differences emerging within the opposition party over whether to move directly towards the capital or stage sit-ins along the Punjab border first, party sources said.
PTI's leadership has proposed holding sit-ins at several points along the Punjab border on Sept 27 before advancing towards Islamabad in phases. However, lawmakers and some party leaders have called for the protesters to move towards the capital on the same day, the sources said.
The issue was discussed at a parliamentary party meeting at the chief minister's residence in Peshawar, where the party leadership consulted lawmakers and office-bearers on its strategy for the planned protest, according to the sources.
The meeting was told that the federal government had closed parts of Islamabad and neighbouring Rawalpindi to prevent PTI supporters from reaching the capital, which the party described as an early success for its protest campaign.
Under the proposed plan, PTI supporters would stage sit-ins at the Attock Bridge, near Hazro on the motorway, in Haripur, at Khushalgarh in Kohat and in Nathia Gali. The party would then consider moving towards Islamabad in the first week of October, the sources said.
Some lawmakers opposed the proposal, arguing that the Sept. 27 protest should not be confined to sit-ins and that the convoy should proceed towards Islamabad on the same day.
The meeting, which lasted about two hours, failed to reach a consensus. The party is expected to hold another meeting on Sept. 25 to finalise the protest strategy, the sources said.
Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar have previously described the planned protest as a "Test match" rather than a "T20", suggesting that the party expects the campaign to continue over an extended period.
PTI's leadership has nevertheless decided to launch the march from Peshawar on Sept. 27, the sources said. A convoy led by Afridi is expected to travel from Peshawar along the Grand Trunk Road to Attock, with the strategy for the onward journey to Islamabad to be announced on Sept 25.

The panel also addressed grievances surrounding delayed financial relief for the families of those killed in the assault. Responding to the inquiry, the Assistant Inspector General (AIG) Legal explained that technical errors within succession certificates had stalled the final distribution of funds.
To resolve these administrative hurdles, the commission instructed officials to organize a specialized open court session (Khuli Kutchery). The bench emphasized the need for direct, streamlined communication between the victims' legal heirs, the Home Department, and law enforcement legal teams to ensure prompt disbursement without further hardship.
In a concurrent matter, the head of the Directorate General for Religious Education appeared before the tribunal to request additional time for compiling data on religious seminaries.

Corruption is endemic in Nigeria, one of Africa's largest economies and its top oil producer.
The report's findings thrust graft back into the spotlight months before January's presidential election, which economic hardships and growing insecurity will define.
Since coming to office in 2023, President Bola Tinubu, who will seek re-election, declared war on graft but high-profile corruption trials are grinding slowly through the courts.
In the report, the investigative NGO Platform to Protect Whistleblowers in Africa (PPLAAF) lists "284 United States properties" collectively worth around $271 million and "linked to 61 current and former high-level Nigerian officials".
The investigation, which examined properties acquired since the end of military rule in 1999, also alleged the war against jihadists continues to enrich the "military elites".
More than half of the properties were bought by the officials during tenure "at precisely the moment when their access to state resources and influence was greatest".

title: Guterres calls for stronger UN  global cooperation
description: Guterres calls for stronger UN  global cooperation
content:
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres made a final appeal for global cooperation on Tuesday, calling for a "world built on interdependence" as he delivered his last address to the UN General Assembly before leaving office at the end of the year.
With roughly 100 days remaining in his decade-long tenure, Guterres said the world's crises were linked to a broader struggle over how power is
exercised and by whom. "The greatest power is not the power to dominate. It is the power to build a future that
Warning that "cracks have become canyons", the secretary-general said international norms had eroded as civilians and humanitarian workers were killed, international law was disregarded and trust between nations weakened.
He warned against a "Great Fracture" in which rival blocs develop separate economic and security systems, urging countries instead to strengthen cooperation and shared rules. He said the international system was struggling against the present-day challenges to the world.
Turning to major conflicts, Guterres renewed calls for compliance with International Court of Justice orders regarding Gaza and warned that Israeli settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank threatened to extinguish the two-State solution. He also condemned Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine as a violation of the UN Charter.
Guterres called for reform of the Security Council, describing the continued absence of permanent African representation as "unjust and indefensible". On inequality, he urged faster debt relief for developing countries, stronger multilateral development banks and fairer access to IMF Special Drawing Rights.
On artificial intelligence, Guterres called for international safeguards, warning that "life-and-death decisions must never be surrendered to machines" and that "killer robots must have no place in our future".
Concluding his farewell address, Guterres pledged to continue defending the UN Charter's principles. "The world does not need a weaker United Nations," he said. "It needs a UN strong enough to face the world as it is."

title: 900 suspected bogus property registrations uncovered
description: 900 suspected bogus property registrations uncovered
content:
ACE alleges Rs114.86m revenue loss, launches inquiry against officials
The Anti-Corruption Establishment (ACE) has uncovered 900 suspected bogus property registrations in a single revenue estate in Gujranwala, allegedly causing more than Rs114.86 million in losses to the provincial exchequer in the form of taxes and duties.
ACE Gujranwala Region Director Amjad Shehzad said on Monday that revenue officials, including tehsildars and patwaris who served in the area during the period under investigation, would be questioned in connection with the alleged fraud.
He said assistant commissioners posted in Gujranwala Sadar during the relevant period would also be included in the inquiry.
Addressing a press conference, the ACE director said the investigation was launched after complaints were received regarding alleged irregularities in revenue records in Mouza Ladhiawala Warraich.
He said ACE teams had taken the relevant record into custody and conducted a detailed examination.
Of the 4,987 mutations involving large and small land transactions carried out during the past two years, 900 were found to involve suspected bogus registrations, he claimed.
According to Shehzad, some documents showed stamp papers with a declared value of more than Rs3,000, while online verification showed that the actual stamp papers had a value of only Rs500.
He said verification of property numbers mentioned in the documents also revealed discrepancies, with the names of buyers and sellers recorded in the physical documents differing from those appearing in the online record.
The suspected bogus registrations allegedly resulted in a loss of Rs114.865 million to the government in taxes and other revenue, the ACE director said.
He said an inquiry was under way against revenue officials and patwaris posted in the area during the relevant period, particularly those whose signatures appeared on the disputed registrations.
Shehzad named Tehsildars Sarfraz Cheema, Altaf Hussain Tarar, Arshad Dhullo and Imtiaz Sahi, as well as Patwaris Bilal Butt and Mustafa Mann, as officials being investigated in connection with the alleged fraud.
He also alleged that a private team or mechanism had been used to conduct site verification. According to him, the team would record videos during visits and allegedly raise objections deliberately, after which additional fees were reportedly charged.
The ACE director said assistant commissioners who served in Gujranwala Sadar from July 1, 2024 to May 4, 2026 would also be questioned to determine why the large number of mutations and the alleged shortfall in revenue collection had not been detected earlier.
He said around 1,800 buyers and sellers could be affected by the investigation and would be heard by the authorities.

title: City gasps under unhealthy air
description: City gasps under unhealthy air
content:
Pre-smog pollution level causes environmental fears
Big cities of Punjab have entered the pre-smog season with air pollution already reaching unhealthy levels.
The situation has caused fear that the provincial capital could face another winter pollution crisis.
Enforcement agencies are struggling to monitor pollution from small units, workshops and commercial activities scattered through residential and industrial areas.
The Punjab Environmental Protection Agency's real time monitoring system in Lahore recorded an AQI of 187 at 8am on Tuesday, placing the city in the "unhealthy for sensitive groups" category.
The update at 11am showed Lahore's overall AQI at 167, in the same category.
Lahore stood fourth among the monitored cities of Punjab, behind Chiniot with an AQI of 183, Narowal 174 and Gujrat 170.
The situation was worse at several locations in the metropolis with DHA Phase 6 recording an AQI of 224 and Multan Road 221, falling in the unhealthy category. Safari Park recorded 199, Kahna Nau 197, GT Road 196, Wagha Border 195 and Shahdara 192.
The city's seven-day peak had reached 246 a couple of days ago.
A separate ranking reportedly placed Lahore at the top of the world's most polluted cities with an AQI of 207. The reading was different from the EPA's monitoring figures, underlining how rankings can vary with monitoring networks and the time of measurement.
The deterioration has occurred well before the traditional peak of the smog season.
The EPA identifies the smog season broadly as October to February with crop residue burning vehicle and industrial emissions, brick kiln smoke and construction dust among the major contributors.
Pollution is being generated simultaneously by traffic, factories, brick kilns, construction, road dust, commercial kitchens, waste burning and agricultural activities in and around the city.
One of the least visible challenges is the large number of small industrial units and workshops operating at different locations. While large factories can be identified and inspected easily, small manufacturing units, furnaces, metal workshops, foundries, chemical businesses and other combustion-based activities are spread across industrial estates as well as mixed residential and commercial areas.
Authorities are struggling in implementing anti-pollution steps, including sealing of industrial units over violations.
The enforcement challenge is whether the regulatory machinery has sufficient manpower, equipment and continuous surveillance to identify every significant source of emissions.
The department has also deployed thermal drones, day and night enforcement squads and technology-based monitoring to locate sources of emissions.
Officials have intensified action with 37 brick kilns and 11 industrial units inspected over a 24-hour period. Several were sealed for violations, while legal action against one unit resulted in an FIR and a Rs500,000 worth of fine. Authorities also inspected 34 barbecue and other commercial cooking sites with nine sealed for non-compliance.
However, a limited number of inspections cannot by themselves establish continuous compliance across the entire urban and peri-urban industrial network.
An environmentalist, Dr Munawar Sabir, said, "Normally, the pre-smog season begins in Lahore and other big cities of the province in the last week of September. Small factories operate intermittently, particularly those producing visible smoke during evening or night hours, posing a monitoring challenge.

title: Aror University VC gets four year extension
description: Aror University VC gets four year extension
content:
Sindh PA speaker's recommendation leads to reversal of earlier decision to advertise post
The Sindh government has approved a four-year extension for Aror University of Art, Architecture, Design and Heritage Vice Chancellor (VC) Dr Zahid Hussain Khand, reversing an earlier decision to advertise the post and appoint a new VC through a selection process.
The extension was reportedly approved following a recommendation by Sindh Assembly Speaker Owais Qadir Shah, according to sources in the Universities and Boards Department.
The development comes amid a series of extensions granted to incumbent VCs of public sector universities in Sindh. The provincial government has also recently approved extensions for Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences VC Dr Ikramuddin Aijaz and Shaheed Allah Buksh Soomro University of Art, Design and Heritage VC Dr Arbela Bhutto.
Sources said the chief secretary had earlier opposed an immediate extension for Dr Khand and recommended that the post be advertised and a new VC appointed through a selection board.
According to the sources, Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah had initially agreed with the chief secretary's recommendation and approved the issuance of an advertisement for the appointment of a new VC.
The Universities and Boards Department subsequently initiated the process, with Secretary Abbas Baloch writing to the relevant authorities for issuance of the advertisement.
However, sources said the summary concerning Dr Khand's reappointment was subsequently called back following intervention by Speaker Owais Qadir Shah. The chief minister then approved the summary, granting Dr Khand another four-year term without making his reappointment conditional on the outcome of a selection process.
Following the reversal of the decision, Secretary Universities and Boards stopped the advertisement for the appointment of a new VC at Aror University.
Sources said the chief secretary had proposed that Dr Khand could be considered for reappointment if the selection process failed to produce a suitable candidate. The recommendation, however, was not retained in the final decision granting him a four-year extension.
The development also paved the way for the extension of Dr Arbela Bhutto's tenure as VC of Shaheed Allah Buksh Soomro University. Her current term is due to expire in February 2027.
Sources said the chief secretary had similarly recommended that the post at Allah Buksh University be advertised and filled through the prescribed selection process.
The Sindh government had earlier approved a four-year extension for LUMHS VC Dr Ikramuddin Aijaz. Last month, it also approved an extension for Dr Nusrat Shah, VC of Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto Medical University, Larkana.
The Express Tribune contacted Universities and Boards Secretary Abbas Baloch for the government's position on the matter. Baloch said the department had not issued an advertisement for the Aror University VC's post. "If the controlling authority has granted an extension, we will issue the notification," he added.
