title: SHC puts brakes on SIDA s GM appointments
description: SHC puts brakes on SIDA s GM appointments
content:
Around 20 SIDA employees challenge market-based hiring, citing denied promotions, flaws
The Sindh High Court has stopped the Sindh Irrigation and Drainage Authority (SIDA) from finalising appointments to three key general manager positions, granting a stay in a legal challenge brought by around 20 of the authority's employees against the proposed market-based hiring.
"The subject appointments should not be finalised without permission of this court," the court ordered in constitutional petitions D-253 and D-3691 filed by SIDA employees led by Syed Muhammad Ali Shah through advocate Muhammad Saulat Rizvi.
The stay covers the posts of GM Transition, GM Operations and GM Research and Development (R&D), which have become the latest flashpoint in a long-running dispute between SIDA's existing employees and external candidates for senior positions.
The petitioners contend that hiring candidates from outside the authority has effectively blocked their prospects for promotion. They also challenged the legality of the latest advertisements, arguing that although SIDA's board reverted the three posts from BPS-20 to BPS-19 earlier this month, the change had not been gazette-notified.
The same positions had previously been filled through market-based recruitment in 2024 despite opposition and a legal challenge by the same employees.
Sadiq Khaskheli was appointed GM Transition on a one-year contract, while Sajjad Soomro and Asghar Mahesar were appointed GM Operations and GM R&D respectively. The contracts of all three were subsequently extended for another year.
A SIDA official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the authority had initially wanted at least two of the GMs to continue but was forced to advertise the posts after their grades were reverted.
The official said Khaskheli and Mahesar appeared likely to be considered for reappointment, while Soomro could potentially be replaced.
The High Court has issued notices to SIDA and the provincial government and fixed September 30 for further proceedings.
Established in 1997 as an autonomous organisation, SIDA was given a statutory framework through an ordinance in 2002. The authority was placed in charge of managing four of Sindh's 14 irrigation canals originating from the Guddu, Sukkur and Kotri barrages.
Under a model conceived with World Bank assistance, SIDA was intended to gradually assume responsibility for additional canals while devolving functions to local stakeholders to promote transparency and institutional development. That broader objective, however, remains incomplete.

title: Shame on you   Raza commission tears into police probe

content:
Summons health secretary, DG health, former SSP as super medical board plan also comes under scrutiny
The Mir Raza judicial commission on Tuesday subjected the police investigation to intense scrutiny, exposing contradictions in witness statements and sharply questioning ASP Nida Junaid over her unexplained involvement in the probe, her handling of a sensitive audio note and her contacts with witnesses despite not being part of the investigation team.
The commission, headed by Justice Umar Sial, also questioned the credibility of the police's financial-distress narrative after business associates contradicted portions of their statements attributed to them by investigators.
During proceedings, Raza's business partner Abid Farooq told the commission that he had made two investments of Rs7 million each in Raza's business but had no written agreement with him. He said the two relied on WhatsApp correspondence.
Asked whether Raza had ever complained about financial difficulties or business losses, Farooq said he had not. He said their relationship was friendly.
The commission later recorded the statement of Sarmad, a witness appearing through video link from Malaysia. He said Raza contacted him on July 27 and urgently sought Rs30 million, telling him that his life depended on the money. He declined to provide the money and later found that a message from Raza had been deleted. By July 28, he said, Raza's WhatsApp was no longer available.
The most contentious portion of the proceedings centred on ASP Nida Junaid. Nida said she became involved because she was the only female ASP in the zone and had been asked by the then investigation-team head, SSP Samiullah Soomro, to assist in interviewing women. Justice Sial repeatedly questioned why she had been involved in the case when she was not formally part of the investigation team. He also questioned why Ali Shahzad, a male witness, had approached her and why she had received a sensitive audio note from him. Nida said Shahzad came to her office voluntarily on August 6 and offered to assist the investigation. She said she made it clear that the case did not fall under her jurisdiction and directed him towards the investigation officer. However, she said she considered an audio note Shahzad provided potentially relevant evidence and forwarded it to SSP Samiullah Soomro. The judge also questioned how the audio subsequently reached the media. Nida maintained that she had not shared it with anyone except SSP.
The commission also questioned Nida over her alleged request for Raza's phone password from his fiancée. Nida said she had sought it on the instructions of SSP Soomro, although the phone itself was never in her possession. Justice Sial then remarked, "shame on you."

title: Five lives  one empty kitchen  Ahsanabad deaths baffle police

content:

An almost empty kitchen, a lone egg in the refrigerator and five members of a family found dead - a grim scene inside a flat in Ahsanabad has left police searching for answers.
The deaths of Dr Umar, his wife and their three children have prompted a police probe, with investigators recording statements from neighbours and examining the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. Neighbours told police that Dr Umar was last seen on Thursday.
Investigators are now awaiting the preliminary post-mortem report, which is expected to help determine the circumstances surrounding the deaths. Police said a decision on registration of a case, as well as the constitution of an investigation committee, would be taken after the report is received and examined.
The decomposing bodies of 45-year-old Dr Omar, his wife Mehwish, aged between 30 and 35, and their three daughters were found inside their locked flat located in Lakhani Tower after neighbours alerted police to a foul smell emanating from the residence. The family is believed to have been dead for several days.
A detailed inspection of the flat by police indicated the family had been facing financial difficulties. Police said there was only one egg in the refrigerator, while the kitchen contained almost no flour. No other food or edible items were found in the apartment.
Police have been recording statements from people living in the vicinity as part of the probe. Kamran Bukhari, former president of the Lakhani Tower Union, told The Express Tribune that he lived on the 6th floor while Dr Umar's family occupied a flat on the 7th floor.
Bukhari said Dr Umar had moved to Lakhani Tower in February 2024 and subsequently opened a clinic near his residence. However, the clinic could not operate successfully and was eventually closed. He added that Dr Umar and his wife had been estranged from their relatives for a long time.
The bodies were taken into custody by Dr Umar's brother, Abu Bakr, and his father-in-law, Jamshaid, after they contacted the police on Monday night. The five deceased were later buried following funeral prayers held under police supervision.

title: PPP pushes through mayor administrator amendment
description: PPP pushes through mayor administrator amendment
content:
MQM, JI and PTI oppose provision allowing outgoing mayors, chairmen to remain in charge until fresh local body electio
A proposed amendment to Sindh's local government law has emerged as the sole point of disagreement between the government and opposition parties, with the Pakistan People's Party (PPP) insisting on retaining existing mayors and chairmen as administrators after their terms expire until fresh local government elections.
The provision was among several amendments proposed by the PPP to the Sindh Local Government Act. However, all opposition parties represented in the Sindh Assembly, including the Muttahida Qaumi Movement (MQM), Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), opposed it.
Members of all parties were part of a special committee constituted to examine the proposed amendments. The committee reviewed the changes clause by clause, with the government and opposition showing flexibility on most provisions. As a result, several additional proposals were also incorporated into the bill.
However, neither side was willing to compromise on the provision allowing existing mayors and chairmen to continue as administrators until new elections. The PPP subsequently used its numerical majority in the Sindh Assembly to get the amendments passed, including the contentious provision.
Opposition representatives said they opposed the amendment on principle, arguing that neutral administrators should be appointed between the expiry of local governments' terms and fresh elections.
Speaking to The Express Tribune, MQM Deputy Parliamentary Leader in the Sindh Assembly Taha Ahmed said the amendment would allow existing mayors and chairmen to serve as administrators until the new elections.
"These are political people. How can they be neutral?" he said, adding that the MQM would challenge the amendment in court.
JI Sindh Assembly member Muhammad Farooq also said the provision was the only point on which his party had disagreed with the government.
Farooq pointed out that JI-affiliated chairmen currently head nine towns and 87 union councils in Karachi. Despite this, he said, his party opposed the amendment because political figures should not be appointed as administrators during an interim period. He said government officials had traditionally been appointed as administrators after local governments' terms expired.
PPP Sindh Assembly member and Sindh government spokesperson Sukhdev Asardas Hemnani, however, defended the amendment, saying government officials had traditionally been appointed during interim periods but political parties had repeatedly criticised the practice.
According to Hemnani, opposition parties had argued that government officials could not be neutral because they worked under the provincial government.
"To avoid this criticism, the PPP introduced this amendment," he said.
Hemnani said that during the interim period, mayors and chairmen serving as administrators would only carry out essential day-to-day functions. He added that election-related powers would remain with the Election Commission of Pakistan.
He also claimed that opposition representatives had not offered an alternative and were instead seeking to delay the amendment bill.
However, he maintained that the government remained open to further changes in the law. "Laws change with time. If the opposition comes forward with good proposals, the government can introduce further amendments to the local government law," he said.
Hemnani added that the government was willing to discuss with opposition parties granting further powers to local government institutions.
The terms of the existing local government bodies are due to expire in mid-2027. Under the amended law, the Sindh government will have to inform the Election Commission of Pakistan three months before their terms expire, after which the commission will begin preparations for new elections.
The Election Commission will also have to carry out fresh delimitation of local government constituencies at least six months before the elections. The exercise could increase the number of union councils, towns and other local government units across Sindh, including Karachi.

A proposal to execute the development scheme for carpeting 13 roads in the inner city through the Communications and Works Department from the Rs2.86 billion development funds of the Rawalpindi Municipal Corporation is under consideration.
According to sources, political interference in the municipal corporation and its alleged lack of capacity to execute such a major development scheme have emerged as issues under discussion.
Sources said the Rawalpindi Municipal Corporation has Rs2.86 billion in development funds from its own resources, which are to be used to launch a development scheme for carpeting, rehabilitation and expansion of 13 roads in the inner city.
At this stage, however, a proposal has emerged under discussion between the Municipal Corporation and the competent authorities that execution of the said development scheme should be carried out through the Communications and Works Department instead of the Municipal Corporation.
The reason emerging during the discussion is that the Municipal Corporation does not have the capacity to execute such a large development scheme and that political interference also exists in the institution.
However, it is also noteworthy that if a development scheme funded by the corporation is executed through another department, the municipal corporation could face audit objections. When the matter was discussed with newly appointed Chief Officer Municipal Corporation Faisal Shehzad, he said the matter was still under discussion and no decision had so far been made in black and white.

Justice Tariq Mehmood Bajwa of the Rawalpindi Bench of the High Court has accepted a petition filed by hotel owners against the indefinite closure of all hotels, restaurants, motels, inns and guest houses across Rawalpindi city and the Cantonment for hearing.
The order to close hotels was issued by the district administration as part of security measures being taken during the upcoming long marches organised by Jamaat-e-Islami and Tehreek-e-Insaf.
Notices have been issued to the Divisional Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, and City Police Officer (CPO) of Rawalpindi, seeking their responses and comments, while the hearing of the petition has been adjourned indefinitely.
The petition was filed by a central leader of the Markazi Anjuman-e-Tajiran (Central Traders' Association), Ehtesham-ul-Haq. Respondents named in the petition include the Chief Secretary of Punjab, the Home Secretary, the Deputy Commissioner, the City Police Officer (CPO), Rawal SP and the Pirwadhai Police Station SHO.
The petition argues that the Islamabad High Court has already issued orders to keep roads and businesses open during the protests. It notes that the Rawalpindi administration has forced the closure of hotels, motels and rest houses twenty times so far this year and has now ordered their indefinite closure merely on the basis of verbal command. It adds that with business already suffering, the closure of hotels will render thousands of employees jobless and will completely ruin businesses. Ehtesham-ul-Haq said that since hotel owners have no political affiliation, they should not have to bear the consequences of the marches.
The petitioners requested that this order be declared null, void and illegal, and any move to close hotels in the future be banned.

title: Lawmakers seek audit of repatriated artefacts
description: Lawmakers seek audit of repatriated artefacts
content:
Call for stronger technical checks, monitoring & accountability in heritage projects
The Standing Committee on National Heritage and Culture has appreciated the Ministry's efforts to secure the repatriation of 1,252 precious archaeological artefacts from abroad, but directed it to provide a comprehensive account of existing preventive mechanisms and technical capacity for authenticating antiquities at its next meeting.
The direction was issued at the ninth meeting of the committee, held at Parliament House under the chairpersonship of MNA Syeda Nosheen Iftikhar.
The committee was informed that, following sustained efforts and continuous follow-up, the Ministry had secured the repatriation of 1,252 artefacts from the United States, Australia, Italy and other countries during the past year.
Expressing concern over the illicit excavation, trafficking and unauthorised export of archaeological artefacts, the committee directed the Ministry to furnish details of artefacts repatriated during the past five years, along with information on preventive mechanisms and technical capacity available for their authentication.
Regarding international cooperation and foreign assistance for the preservation and conservation of Pakistan's cultural heritage, the Ministry informed the committee that Pakistan was a state party to the 1954 Hague Convention and its Protocol, the 1970 UNESCO Convention concerning the Means of Prohibiting and Preventing the Illicit Import, Export and Transfer of Ownership of Cultural Property, and the 1972 World Heritage Convention.
The committee was informed that, under UNESCO assistance, $75,000 each was received in 2022 for the Moenjodaro and Makli World Heritage Sites for post-disaster response to monsoon-related hazards. In 2025, $49,139 was provided for the conservation and restoration of Takht-i-Bahi and the neighbouring city of Sahr-i-Bahlol.
The committee stressed that all conservation work undertaken with external or foreign assistance must undergo qualified technical inspection and systematic, documented monitoring, while the utilisation of funds must remain transparent and accountable.
The committee also endorsed the Ministry's initiative to provide voluntary academic guidance to CSS aspirants at the National Library of Pakistan through experienced officers and resource persons. The proposed sessions will cover compulsory subjects, including English, Pakistan Studies, General Knowledge, Pakistan history and Everyday Science.
It particularly appreciated the focus on English grammar and composition, précis and report writing, and official writing skills. However, it stressed that the initiative should remain within the National Library's mandate and available resources and should not create any undue financial or administrative liability.
The committee also called for an appropriate mechanism to maintain attendance and participation records and periodically assess the effectiveness and outcomes of the initiative.
The meeting was attended by committee members Samar Haroon Bilour, Saeeda Jamshid, Ghazala Anjum, Shahnaz Saleem Malik, Mahtab Akbar Rashdi, Natasha Daultana, Saba Talpur, Sanjay Perwani and Naeema Kishwer Khan, as well as Federal Minister for National Heritage and Culture Aurangzeb Khan Khichi, Secretary National Heritage and Culture Division and senior officials of the Ministry and its subordinate departments.

title: Scores dead in Yemen fighting | The Express Tribune
description:
Scores dead in 
Yemen fighting
content:
UK agrees military support for Saudi Arabia
As many as 169 people have been reportedly killed in Yemen in the last three days as Iran-aligned Houthis battle Saudi-backed government forces for control of strategic heights on the Red Sea coast, while thousands flee the violence.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has agreed to give military support to Saudi Arabia to help it tackle attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis, media reports said on Monday.
British planes will provide "defensive" air-to-air refuelling for Saudi jets, he told reporters as he travelled to the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
The UK mission will be limited to supporting Saudi aircraft defending the country from attack from drones and missiles rather than supporting strikes against the Houthis, the PA news agency reported.
The use of the Voyager tanker is expected to start within days and the mission will be time-limited, with officials indicating it could last for "weeks".
The refuelling mission is in addition to the UK Sky Sabre air defence system already deployed in Saudi Arabia.
Burnham told reporters he was "acting to secure the interests of Britain and the wider region because, of course, Saudi Arabia has been experiencing attacks, is looking at potential further disruption, and we need to keep those pathways open, and hence our agreement to the request", according to the reports.
Houthi military officials said at least 118 people had been killed in clashes as well as Saudi air and artillery strikes on Taiz, al-Jawf, Marib and Saada provinces since Sunday, Agence France-Presse reported. Yemeni government sources have said at least 36 people have been killed on their side of the conflict.
The clashes have compounded an already dire humanitarian crisis, where about 22 million people need humanitarian assistance and 5.2 million people are already internally displaced.
Members of the G7 have called on Iran to stop arming the Houthis. In a joint statement released ahead of the UN general assembly, member states urged the Houthis to stop their strikes on Saudi Arabia, which have damaged key oil infrastructure and wounded dozens.
"We call on the Houthis to immediately cease all military actions, all threats and attacks against civilian shipping, and to return to the political process in good faith," the statement read.
The clashes have killed about 700 people and displaced more than 100,000 people, pushing some Yemenis to flee the fighting via sea. Civilians have fled westwards across the Red Sea to Djibouti, while aid groups warn conditions for those remaining in Yemen are deteriorating.

title: Erdogan calls for wider recognition of Palestinian state
description: Erdogan calls for wider recognition of Palestinian state
content:
Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan told the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday the UN had become unable to fulfill its duty of preserving peace and called for reform of the Security Council.
Erdogan has for years called for a more comprehensive and inclusive structure at the Security Council.
"Let's recognise that a system in which the will of more than 190 countries is subject to the whims of five countries is neither fair nor capable of fully establishing trust," he said.
"The United Nations, established 81 years ago to maintain peace and security, has become unable to fulfil this mission, or rather it has been made unable to do so," he added.
Erdogan also condemned the situation in Gaza, saying "no one who holds humanity, compassion and mercy in their heart, with a sense of justice and conscience can turn a blind eye" to what was happening there.
"(Palestinian President) Mahmoud Abbas, has been unable to take his place in this hall for two consecutive years. This injustice against our Palestinian brothers and sisters wounds the consciences," Erdogan said.
He urged countries that do not recognise a Palestinian state to review their position and for all nations to increase pressure on Israel to end the war in Gaza, which he called "our time's most inhumane, most embarrassing concentration camp".
NATO member Turkey has been one of the most vocal critics of Israel and its war on Gaza, saying its attacks amounted to genocide. It has repeatedly urged for international measures against Israel. Israel denies accusations of genocide.

title: EU renews Russia sanctions
description: EU renews Russia sanctions
content:
Drops Russian billionaires Usmanov and Fridman
European Union envoys agreed to drop two high-profile billionaires, Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, from the EU's Russian sanctions list in a compromise deal to roll over the roughly 3,000 other listed individuals and entities, EU diplomats said on Tuesday.
Earlier this month, France shocked other EU members when it pushed for Russian-Uzbek metals tycoon Usmanov to be removed from EU sanctions, citing national security concerns. Luxembourg then demanded the same treatment for Fridman, who has launched a $16 billion claim against the country.
As a compromise, EU envoys agreed to remove the two billionaires in exchange for a three-year renewal of measures against the other sanctioned individuals and entities instead of the usual six months.
Latvia was the last holdout in an unusually fraught process. The deadline to renew the sanctions was at midnight on September 22 after an extension from the original expiry on September 15.
Sanctions require unanimity among EU countries to be approved. Latvia ultimately abstained, diplomats said, which allowed the deal to pass. The decision was formally approved via a process known as a written procedure later on Tuesday.
"The decision to delist Usmanov and Fridman is shameful and unjustifiable. Moscow is celebrating," Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said in a post on X, urging EU countries to impose their own national restrictions on the two men.
Latvia's Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs said Riga would look to impose its own sanctions while abstaining from this sanctions procedure. He added that France had agreed to start talks with Latvia about joining a French nuclear deterrence initiative.
The episode has roiled European leaders who had hoped to present a more united front against Russia since a recent change of government in Hungary. Former Hungarian leader Viktor Orban was a frequent obstacle on sanctions and support for Ukraine.
It took high-level meetings in Europe and on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York this week to iron out the agreement, diplomats said.
The EU imposed sanctions on both men in 2022, following Moscow's invasion of Ukraine, which include transaction and travel bans in the EU and a freeze on assets held in the bloc.

title: SC affirms wife s right to dower
description: SC affirms wife s right to dower
content:
Says dower is mandatory, exclusive property of wife
The Supreme Court has ruled that dower is a mandatory legal incident of marriage imposed by Islamic law, and has held that it is neither the price of the wife nor consideration in the technical common-law sense, as it constitutes her exclusive proprietary right.
The court has further held that courts must protect a wife's lawful entitlement to dower effectively while remaining faithful to the agreement established by the evidence, stressing that the institution of marriage must not be reduced to a transaction in which the wife's rights become an afterthought.
A 26-page judgment authored by Justice Shahid Waheed noted that courts must interpret laws affecting dower in a manner that gives practical and effective protection to the wife's lawful entitlement while remaining faithful to the actual agreement proved by the evidence.
A four-judge bench of the Supreme Court hearing the matter emphasised that the court must not allow the institution of marriage to be reduced to a transaction where the wife's rights are an afterthought.
"We must not allow husband to treat dower as a weapon to be used in later disputes. I will pay you if you behave; I will pay you if you do not ask for divorce. That is not dower. That is coercion. True dower is given with a good heart, at the time agreed, without conditions that demean the wife. And when it is not given, the courts must step in, not with hesitation, not with apology, but with the full authority of the law."
The judgment further stated: "Because to fail to enforce dower is to tell every woman in this jurisdiction that her rights are theoretical. It is to tell every man that he can make promises before Allah and before the law and then ignore them. It is to weaken the family and, through the family, to weaken the nation. Therefore, in every case that comes before a court involving dower, the court must begin with this premise: the wife's dignity is at stake."
"Her right is not a favour. It is a command of the Shari'ah, a command of the statute, and a command of justice. The Court's task is to determine, on evidence, what that right is, and then to ensure that it is fulfilled. Let no husband think that he can escape this liability by silence. Let no court think that it can dispose of this matter lightly."
"For in protecting dower, we are protecting the home. By protecting the home, we protect society. And in protecting society, we are fulfilling the promise of a nation that claims to be founded on the principles of Islam, justice, and human dignity. The law is clear. The religion is clear."
The judgment further stressed that the conscience of society was clear, adding that what remains is only the determination of fact: what was the dower, and how did the husband agree to pay it? Once that is determined, the decree must follow, and it must be enforced with grace if the husband complies, and with the full force of law if he does not.
"That is the only way to ensure that the dignity of a wife, which begins at the Nikah, is protected until the very end."
The court noted that ownership of the dower vests in the wife immediately upon its becoming payable according to law.
"It is because she has become its owner that she possesses legal capacity to waive, remit or gift it back. This principle has profound consequences. Neither the husband nor his relatives may compel the wife to relinquish her dower. Any remission must proceed from her free consent. The Holy Qur'an thus safeguards not merely the existence of the right but also the freedom with which it may subsequently be exercised."
"A wife who receives dower does not receive charity. She receives no favour. She receives no benevolence. She receives that which the law has declared to be her own. The distinction is fundamental. One who receives charity remains dependent upon the generosity of another. One who enforces dower vindicates a legal right."
The court said Nikah is a unique legal institution (sui generis), formed through contract, regulated by Shariah, recognised by statute and protected by the Constitution. Its contractual features facilitate its formation.
"The wife is not the subject matter of sale; her consent is not purchased; her personality is not transferred; and her dignity is not commodified."
"Dower is imposed because marriage honours her; it is not paid because she is being acquired."

title: Army chief reaffirms resolve to stamp out terror
description: Army chief reaffirms resolve to stamp out terror
content:
Says armed forces are resolute to defeat terrorism, ensure lasting peace
Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir on Tuesday directed formations to remain vigilant and uphold the highest standards of operational preparedness during a visit to Corps Headquarters Peshawar.
The visit took place days after Pakistan carried out airstrikes on terrorist hideouts in various locations in the regions bordering Afghanistan following brazen terror attacks in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.
According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the CDF was briefed on the prevailing security situation in K-P, ongoing counter-terrorism operations, border management measures and operational preparedness of formations deployed in the province.
The chief of army staff commended the high morale, readiness and professionalism of officers and troops, acknowledging their steadfast commitment to safeguarding the country and its people.
He emphasised that the armed forces, with the unwavering support of the nation, remain resolute in their determination to defeat terrorism and ensure lasting peace and stability across the country.
Field Marshal Munir also laid a floral wreath at Yadgar-e-Shuhada and offered Fateha, paying rich tribute to those who laid down their lives in defence of the motherland and in the fight against terrorism.
He reaffirmed that their supreme sacrifices would never be forgotten. Upon arrival, the COAS was received by Commander Peshawar Corps Syed Omer Ahmed Bokhari.
The visit came days after 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred in a blast at a mosque in Kohat's Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation.
Later, Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
Two days after the blast, two officers among six security personnel were martyred in an exchange of fire between a security forces convoy and terrorists in K-P's Hangu district. Eight terrorists belonging to the Fitna al-Khawarij were also killed during the exchange.
Following these attacks, Pakistan carried out "calibrated" airstrikes against terrorist hideouts near the Afghan border and conducted intelligence-based ground operations that killed a total of 37 terrorists.

title: JI suspends train march at  PM s request
description: JI suspends train march at  PM s request
content:
JI suspends train march at 'PM's request'
The JI, which is running a campaign against the petroleum levy and inflation, has decided to suspend its train march toward Islamabad at the request of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.
The party workers will stay in Multan until a formal interaction between the prime minister and the party leadership and will decide their future course of action based on those talks.
JI chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman announced this decision in a press conference held in Multan on Tuesday. According to Rehman, the prime minister called him on Monday and requested him to defer the protest movement.
"I informed the prime minister that people are suffering [due to economic conditions]. The prime minister assured me that he will hold a meeting with us as soon as he arrives in the country and will announce relief for the people," the JI chief said.
Rehman said he told the prime minister that he would inform him about the party's decision after consultation. "During our long consultation, we decided neither to withdraw our demands nor our long march. We will, however, listen to what the prime minister has to say," he added.
According to Rehman, the JI workers will stay in the field, but he added that the party's agenda is to ensure relief for the people and not to create chaos and mischief.
"We only want to give the prime minister an opportunity to be heard," he said, adding that the party would seek written assurances from the government.
"Let the prime minister come so that talks can begin. Until then, our long march will remain camped in Multan," he said, describing the opportunity as the government's "last chance" for negotiations.
Rehman said people were suffering from inflation and claimed that the party's shutter-down strike had put pressure on the government.
He said JI had presented various proposals for reducing petrol prices, but the government maintained that it could not reduce the levy because Pakistan was implementing the IMF programme.
Earlier, a statement issued by the Prime Minister's House said PM Shehbaz Sharif had spoken to Hafiz Naeemur Rehman and asked him to postpone the sit-in in Islamabad.
The prime minister said the government was providing relief on petroleum products to economically vulnerable and middle-class segments amid difficult circumstances and would continue to provide as much relief to the public as possible.
Rehman welcomed the prime minister's proposal and said JI was considering postponing the sit-in. Both leaders agreed to meet after the prime minister's return and continue consultations on the matter.

title: Very good  US Iran talks crack open diplomatic door
description: Very good  US Iran talks crack open diplomatic door
content:
 Trump says both sides hold three-hour talks  Hints at settlement after midterm elections  Uses UN address to th
The United States and Iran held a three-hour meeting on Tuesday as Tehran signalled a willingness to revive diplomacy and potentially reopen the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz, even as US President Donald Trump warned that he could "annihilate" the Islamic Republic if no agreement was reached.
Trump told reporters at the United Nations that US officials had held a "very good" three-hour meeting with the Iranian delegation. He gave few details, saying the talks had ended about an hour before he spoke to reporters. "It was a meeting that lasted for three hours. It was a very good meeting," Trump said.
"I can't imagine why they wouldn't want to do it; it's greatness or obliteration," he remarked hours after his address to the UN General Assembly. Trump used the speech to issue a stark warning to Tehran, saying he faced a choice between reaching a deal and destroying Iran's ability to attacking against other countries.
"I have a big decision to make," the US president told the General Assembly, asking whether a deal could allow Iran to rebuild or whether he should "annihilate the Islamic Republic" and drive it "into hell with no chance of survival". The Iranian delegation did not attend the session when Trump spoke.
However, talking to the media persons after a meeting with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham in New York on the sidelines of UNGA session, Trump adopted a conciliatory tone, saying Washington and Tehran had been talking even on Tuesday.
He expressing his confidence that a settlement with Iran could eventually be reached. "They want to talk to us. They have been talking to us, even today they've been talking to us, and the relationship is developing," Trump said.
He reiterated that US would not allow Iran to obtain a nuclear weapon, saying the issue remained central to any possible agreement. He called for the economic isolation of Iran until it stopped attacks on commercial shipping, abandoned its nuclear ambitions and ended support for what he described as terrorism.
Earlier, Trump told the General Assembly that he believed a deal with Iran could be reached after the US midterm elections in November, saying Tehran was waiting to see how he performed in the vote before making a decision.
The Iranian side, meanwhile, signalled that diplomacy remained possible but insisted that Washington would need to change its approach. A senior Iranian official said that Tehran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if US military pressure was eased and the blockade on Iranian ports lifted.
The official described the UN General Assembly as a "golden opportunity" for Washington to return to diplomacy, saying the United States should formally declare that it wanted to resolve the dispute diplomatically and then agree on a timetable.
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who led Iran's negotiating team in previous talks, struck a harder line, saying Tehran would never surrender and that Trump could not impose his power on the Iranian people and armed forces.
The contrasting positions came against the backdrop of an almost seven-month-old conflict that has disrupted regional security, commercial shipping and energy markets. The Strait of Hormuz, through which a major share of global oil and gas shipments normally passes, remains at the centre of the confrontation.
At the UN, Trump was also due to meet leaders of Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, all of which have a direct interest in restoring secure navigation through Hormuz while balancing their relations with Washington and Tehran.
The developing diplomatic activity came as Trump used much of his UN address to defend his administration's record and its handling of several international conflicts. He said the United States had restored its strength and portrayed his administration as an active force for ending wars.
In his address, Trump also singled out Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, calling him a "terrific man" while repeating his claim that his administration's diplomatic efforts helped end the May 2025 Pakistan-India conflict. He said world leaders had sent him letters thanking him for his mediation efforts.
"The Prime Minister of Pakistan, terrific man, said that Donald Trump was responsible for saving thirty million lives and probably many more than that," the president noted, as he credited his administration's diplomatic efforts to end multiple global conflicts and received letters of thanks from world leaders.
For now, the three-hour meeting between the US and Iranian officials has produced no announced agreement, but it marked the latest direct indication that diplomatic channels remain active despite the increasingly severe rhetoric surrounding the conflict.

title: Two cops on polio duty martyred in Noshki
description: Two cops on polio duty martyred in Noshki
content:
Yousafzai said polio was a dangerous disease that could cause permanent disability in children
Two police officers providing security to a polio vaccination team were killed after unidentified armed men opened fire in Noshki district of Balochistan, officials said on Tuesday.
The incident came as a week-long sub-national polio vaccination campaign was underway in 115 districts across Pakistan. More than 31 million children under the age of five were due to receive polio drops during the campaign, with activities focused on high-risk and hotspot areas in Balochistan, Gilgit-Baltistan, Islamabad, Khyber- Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Sindh.
The attack took place in Killi Jamalabad, where police personnel had been deployed to protect the vaccination team. The two officers were identified as Muhammad Yasar and Abdul Rauf.
The attackers fled with the officers' official weapons after the shooting, officials said. Police subsequently cordoned off the area and launched a search operation to arrest those responsible.
Balochistan Special Assistant on Home Affairs Babar Yousafzai confirmed the incident and condemned the attack, blaming Fitna al-Hindustan for the deaths.
"Fitna al-Hindustan opened fire on two police personnel deployed to protect a polio team in Nushki and martyred them," Yousafzai said.
He said the attack on a polio team was effectively an attack on the future of children in Balochistan. "They do not want the children of Balochistan to move towards a healthy and secure future," he said.
Yousafzai said polio was a dangerous disease that could cause permanent disability in children, while vaccination was an effective means of preventing it. "Those who target polio teams are, in fact, trying to deprive the children of Balochistan of their right to health and a secure future," he said.
"Polio workers are going from door to door to protect our children from disease, and their security is the shared responsibility of the state and society. Children in Balochistan need education, health, peace and a bright future, not terrorism and disease," he added.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi strongly condemned the firing and expressed grief over the deaths of constables Muhammad Yasar and Abdul Rauf.
Naqvi paid tribute to the two officers and offered condolences to their families. "Constables Yasar and Abdul Rauf attained the great rank of martyrdom while performing their duties," Naqvi said.
"Attacking a team working to secure the future of children is a heinous and unforgivable act by brutal elements. The beasts who attacked the anti-polio team deserve an exemplary punishment," Naqvi added.
It is pertinent to note that polio vaccination teams have been targeted in the past, including incidents reported in Quetta and several other districts of Balochistan, highlighting the persistent security challenges faced by frontline health workers and their protectors.
Despite these threats, authorities have reiterated their commitment to continuing the anti-polio campaign and ensuring the safety of vaccination teams through enhanced security measures.

title: Top court allows bail for specialised medical care
description: Top court allows bail for specialised medical care
content:
The Supreme Court has held that an undertrial prisoner suffering from an ailment requiring specialised treatment and medical supervision unavailable in jail may be granted post-arrest bail on medical grounds, particularly where continued detention could pose a serious risk to his health or life.
A three-member bench headed by Justice Shahid Waheed passed the ruling while allowing two petitions filed by Zeeshan Majeed Bhatti seeking bail on medical grounds, granting him post-arrest bail in both cases.
In its detailed judgment, the court observed that medical reports submitted by the Medical Officer of Central Jail, Rawalpindi, showed that the accused was suffering from serious ailments and was not receiving the specialised treatment required at the jail hospital.
The accused was suffering from hypertension, diabetes and cardiac problems, besides complaints of chest pain. Cardiologists had recommended specialised medical examination and treatment, the judgment noted.
The apex court observed that the ailments suffered by the accused required specialised treatment and continuous medical supervision, which could not be adequately provided by the jail authorities.
It held that continued detention without the required specialised treatment could adversely affect the accused's health and could also pose a danger to his life.
Referring to its earlier judgments concerning bail on medical grounds, the court held that post-arrest bail could be granted.

title: Panel orders bridging PSM security gaps
description: Panel orders bridging PSM security gaps
content:
Subcommittee of Senate orders audit report, probes 36-tonne theft case
A parliamentary panel on Tuesday ordered Pakistan Steel Mills (PSM) to strengthen security and submit its latest audit report within a week amid concerns over repeated theft, open portions of the sprawling premises and encroachments on its land.
The Senate subcommittee on Industries and Production, chaired by Senator Syed Masroor Ahsan, also reviewed the theft of 36 tonnes of material from the PSM and directed strict action against employees allegedly involved.
The panel ordered that such individuals be barred from entering the premises.
The committee was told that police had already submitted a challan in the 36-tonne theft case. However, recovery of the stolen material remained pending.
The subcommittee was further told that, besides administrative action through the relevant authorities and courts, criminal proceedings were also underway in the theft cases, and the stolen material had been recovered in some cases.
The panel was informed that DSF personnel were currently deployed at PSM, while the Ministry of Defence had recently sought their withdrawal.
The Ministry of Industries and Production has taken up the issue of a phased withdrawal of DSF personnel with the Defence Division so that PSM has sufficient time to put alternative security arrangements in place.
The subcommittee was told that PSM covers around 1,000 acres, a substantial portion of which remains open and lacks a boundary wall or fencing, creating further security challenges.
The committee expressed serious concern over the shortage of security personnel required to protect machinery and equipment worth billions of rupees.
It was further informed that a proposal to recruit essential administrative, accounts, and security staff had been taken up with the Ministry of Finance.
After detailed deliberations, the subcommittee directed the PSM management to provide comprehensive justification for the number of employees required.
The convenor also directed the Ministry of Finance to ensure that its representative attends the next meeting to discuss recruitment of the necessary staff for PSM and work towards a practical solution to the issue.
The committee members recommended installation of modern surveillance cameras to improve security monitoring across PSM.
They also directed the identification and permanent closure of underground tunnels that could be used for unauthorised entry into the premises, saying this was necessary to prevent theft and illegal access.
The convenor further directed the FIA to complete its pending inquiry into a recovery case relating to PSM.
The subcommittee also expressed concern over encroachments on PSM land, terming the land a valuable national asset that required protection.

title: NA Secretariat tightens belt after fuel price hike
description: NA Secretariat has also decided to reduce its non ERE budget by 5  monthly during the 2026 27 financial year
content:
NA Secretariat has also decided to reduce its non-ERE budget by 5% monthly during the 2026-27 financial year
The National Assembly Secretariat has begun implementing austerity measures in the wake of a surge in petroleum prices, introducing a new duty system under which half of its officers and staff will work from offices while the other 50% will work from home on a rotational basis.
According to the NA Secretariat, the new arrangements are being implemented under the austerity notification issued on September 18. Employees working from home will remain available by telephone, email and WhatsApp and may be called to the office at one hour's notice whenever required.
Under the notification, 50% of employees working from home will not be entitled to a diet allowance or overtime. Employees will also be prohibited from leaving their station without prior permission.
As part of the austerity measures, fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50%, with the reduction to remain in effect for three months. A complete ban has also been imposed on the purchase of all types of new vehicles.
The NA Secretariat has also decided to reduce its non-ERE budget by 5% on a monthly basis during the 2026-27 financial year.
Meetings will preferably be held through video conferencing, although intra-city meetings will remain exempt from the restriction. Standing committee meetings have also been encouraged to be held virtually.
Under the austerity policy, the number of meetings is to be kept at the minimum possible level until the situation returns to normal.
To implement the September 18 notification, the National Assembly Secretariat has also assigned duties to a number of officers, including additional secretaries, joint secretaries and director generals.
Under the instructions, officers will be permitted to call one subordinate officer and one staff member from their respective wing. Additional staff may also be called in when required, subject to approval from the relevant authorities.
Requests to call more than 50% of the staff will be subject to valid reasons and recommendations from the concerned authorities.

title: Minister rules out governor s rule in K P
description: Minister rules out governor s rule in K P
content:
Tarar says it is unclear whom in PTI govt to engage
The federal information minister on Tuesday ruled out the possibility of imposing governor's rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) province, whose ruling party, the PTI, plans to march on Islamabad on September 27 to seek the release of incarcerated party founder Imran Khan.
Addressing a press conference in K-P's provincial capital, Federal Information Minister Atta Tarar clarified that the federal government had no plans to remove the PTI government. "The province needs people's rule not the governor's rule," he said.
A day earlier, Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, while responding to a question during a press conference in Lahore, stated that the government had already made it clear to the PTI that the prime minister, in consultation with our law ministry, would utilise whatever legal options were available.
The minister said the PTI talked about dialogue, but it was unclear with which responsible person in the party the federal government should engage. "The government has repeatedly offered talks. Political tensions can only be resolved through dialogue and constitutional and legal means," he added.
Tarar reiterated that the PTI would not be allowed to disrupt law and order in Islamabad, rejecting what he described as politics of violence and confrontation.
"We reject the politics of violence and confrontation," he said, adding that nobody would be allowed to block roads or affect citizens' rights in violation of Islamabad High Court (IHC) orders.
The minister said If the provincial government believed that people had voted for it to secure the release of an imprisoned individual, such an approach could take the province decades backward.
Tarar said the release of the personformer prime minister Imran Khanfor whom "illegal means" were allegedly being adopted could only take place in accordance with the law.
Criticising the K-P government, the federal minister said the same party had been in power in the province for a long time, but he did not see significant development work there. He said questions should also be raised about issues relating to deforestation and mining.
He said the people were paying taxes but were not receiving the facilities that fell within the provincial government's responsibilities. "The chief minister's job is to serve the province, improve governance and provide facilities to the people, not to incite them for protest activities," Tarar said.
He also questioned the absence of provincial government leaders from the funerals of security personnel and civilians martyred in terrorist incidents. "Public resources should not be spent on rallies, processions and protest activities by the PTI. Public resources should be spent on the public," he said.
Tarar said the K-P government had been provided a substantial amount under the National Finance Commission for the National Action Plan and should give a complete account of its utilisation.
Referring to the Kohat incident, Tarar said counterterrorism operations would continue and nobody would be allowed to disturb peace and order. He claimed that evidence had emerged that Afghan territory was being used in some terrorist incidents and said Pakistan had responded to it.

content:
PTI chairman stands firm on Sept 27 march; lawyers back movement
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Tuesday said the party had never closed the door to negotiations, but its political struggle would continue until progress was made on its basic demands.
Gohar met with National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Achakzai and discussed with him the prevailing political situation, the September 27 march, cooperation among opposition parties and the future political strategy.
Speaking outside Parliament, later, Gohar said the September 27 long march would take place and remain peaceful. He said that protests could not simply be ruled out when justice was not provided, concerns were not heard and demands were not addressed.
He stressed the situation could improve if judicial orders were implemented and issues concerning meetings with and medical treatment of PTI founder Imran Khan were resolved. He also expressed concern over the arrest of Imran's sisters.
In Lahore, meanwhile, PTI leader Hamid Khan and the office-bearers of the Lahore High Court Bar Association (LHCBA) and the Lahore Bar Association (LBA) condemned the detention of Imran's sisters and the cases registered against lawyers.

LHCBA President Babar Murtaza also condemned the "illegal detention" of the PTI founder's sisters. He said that peaceful protest was a fundamental right. Babar Murtaza demanded the immediate release of all political prisoners.
Former LHCBA president Ishtiaq Ahmed Khan said lawyers had to play their role for the supremacy of the Constitution. He criticised the alleged disregard of court decisions and said the government was damaging the country because of hostility towards one person.

title: Gaza  Muslim states seek coordination
description: Gaza  Muslim states seek coordination
content:
Dar meets regional counterparts on fringes of UNGA
Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and his counterparts from Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Egypt on Tuesday expressed full support for efforts aimed at peacefully resolving the latest regional situation, while calling for stronger diplomatic coordination to protect Palestinians.
Dar participated in a ministerial meeting of the Regional-4 (R-4) group on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, where the ministers discussed regional developments and exchanged views on the latest situation.
According to the Foreign Office, the ministers expressed "full support" for efforts aimed at a peaceful resolution of the situation. Dar reaffirmed Pakistan's strong commitment to the R-4 framework and stressed the need for continued engagement to enhance regional peace and prosperity.
The ministers also reiterated their support for the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, including their inalienable right to self-determination. They backed the establishment of an independent, sovereign, viable and contiguous State of Palestine.
Earlier, Dar, addressing the OIC Committee of Six on Palestine on the sidelines of the UNGA, urged stronger coordination among OIC member states at the United Nations and other international forums to protect Palestinians and uphold international law.
He said the Committee of Six had an important responsibility to mobilise political and diplomatic support for Palestinians and ensure that the international community did not lose sight of their legitimate and human rights.
"The humanitarian situation remains dire, and the security environment is extremely fragile," Dar said, while welcoming efforts by the United States, Qatar and Turkiye to advance implementation of the comprehensive plan to end the Gaza conflict.
Meanwhile, foreign ministers of Pakistan, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) expressed deep concern over the humanitarian crisis in Gaza in a joint statement issued after their September 21 meeting in New York.
The ministers urged Israel to fulfil its Phase One commitments by ensuring unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid, supporting early recovery and rehabilitating critical infrastructure. They stressed the imperative of preserving the ceasefire and ending all violations.
The ministers categorically rejected measures aimed at expelling or forcibly displacing Palestinians from their homeland. They also rejected attempts to alter the territorial or demographic character of the Occupied Palestinian Territory.
The ministers deplored the Israeli measures take against the Palestinians, including expansion of Jewish settlements, confiscation of Palestinian lands, demolition of Palestinian homes, settler violence and forced displacement.
The ministers reaffirmed that Gaza must remain an integral part of Palestinian territory and called for a credible and irreversible pathway towards Palestinian self-determination and the establishment of a sovereign, viable and independent Palestinian state with East Jerusalem as its capital.
Separately, Dar held a bilateral meeting with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud in New York in which both sides reaffirmed their commitment to strengthen bilateral cooperation under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. (WITH INPUT FROM APP)

The detention of the Khan sisters came amid a crackdown on Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) ahead of the party's planned march on Islamabad on September 27. Shahraiz Khan, Aleema's son, had filed the petition through advocate Rana Mudassar Umar, challenging the detention of his mother and aunts.

title: France appreciates Pak Gulf mediation
description: France appreciates Pak Gulf mediation
content:
Two countries hold Joint Security Commission talks
France has expressed appreciation for Pakistan's diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions in the Gulf and is looking to deepen bilateral ties with Islamabad despite its longstanding strategic relationship with India, diplomatic sources said on Tuesday.
The assessment came as Pakistan and France held the eighth round of their Joint Security Commission in Islamabad, with the talks focusing on defence and security cooperation as well as regional developments.
French Secretary General for Defence and National Security (SGDSN) Nicolas Roche led the French delegation, while Pakistan's Defence Secretary Lt Gen (retd) Muhammad Ali headed the Pakistani side.
Diplomatic sources said France viewed Pakistan's efforts to promote diplomacy and dialogue in the Gulf positively, particularly at a time of heightened regional tensions.
They said Paris was also interested in developing closer relations with Islamabad, although France's strategic partnership with India remained an important element of its South Asia policy.
The sources pointed out that high-level exchanges between Pakistan and France had been relatively limited in recent years.
Roche's visit is particularly significant because the last French secretary general for defence and national security to visit Pakistan was in 2019.
The sixth round of the Joint Security Commission was held in Rawalpindi in July 2019. The mechanism has been meeting since 2011 to maintain high-level exchanges on security cooperation and counterterrorism.
A senior Pakistani foreign office official described Roche's visit as important, saying it reflected "steady progress" in bilateral ties.
"France is an important European and international player and has a permanent seat on the UN Security Council. We want to continue making strides in our relationship," the official told The Express Tribune on condition of anonymity.
The official, however, cautioned against expecting any major breakthrough from the current engagement.
"Nothing dramatic is expected, but the effort is to keep the relationship moving forward," the official said.
The two sides agreed to continue bilateral dialogue and engagement under the Pakistan-France Roadmap for Bilateral Cooperation adopted in 2023. They also agreed that the next round of the Joint Security Commission would be held in France on mutually agreed dates.
The discussions covered security and defence cooperation, regional security developments, counterterrorism, drug trafficking, piracy and other forms of transnational organised crime.
The official also highlighted the longstanding defence relationship between Pakistan and France, particularly in the naval domain.
France has historically played an important role in the development of Pakistan's submarine capability. Pakistan acquired Daphné-class submarines from France in the 1960s and later obtained Agosta submarines. In 1994, Islamabad signed a contract with the French company DCN for three Agosta 90B submarines, with technology transfer allowing two of the vessels to be built at Karachi Shipyard.
The French-origin Agosta 90B programme also involved technology transfer and training for Pakistani engineers, creating an industrial link between the two countries that continued beyond the original acquisition.

Alexis Bledel has expressed her appreciation for the original Gilmore Girls fans who continued watching the series as its characters and storylines evolved.
Bledel, who played Rory Gilmore on the popular television series, discussed the show’s lasting appeal in an interview with The New York Times . The interview was conducted as part of the publication’s list of the best TV shows of the 21st century.
“I started working on Gilmore Girls when I was 18, so I’m very grateful for it,” Bledel said. She added that she appreciates fans “sticking with us as we evolved and grew within our roles.”
Created by Amy Sherman-Palladino, Gilmore Girls premiered in 2000 and ran for seven seasons until 2007. The series followed Rory and her mother, Lorelai Gilmore, played by Lauren Graham, as they navigated family relationships, romance and life in the fictional town of Stars Hollow.
Bledel also reflected on the elements that have helped Gilmore Girls remain popular years after its original run. She pointed to the show’s fast-paced dialogue, which she compared to classic films from the 1930s and 1940s, as well as its themes of teenage angst, single motherhood and multigenerational family drama.
The series gained a new generation of viewers after becoming available on Netflix in 2014. In 2016, Bledel and much of the original cast reunited for the Netflix revival Gilmore Girls: A Year in the Life .
Gilmore Girls was recently ranked No. 99 on The New York Times’ list of the best TV shows of the 21st century. Bledel’s other television work includes The Handmaid’s Tale , for which she won an Emmy.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday urged the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) to press the Afghan Taliban to take concrete and verifiable steps to prevent their soil from being used for terrorist attacks against neighbouring countries.
Dar appealed while addressing a meeting of the OIC Contact Group on Afghanistan on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
Recalling the withdrawal of US troops from Afghanistan in August 2021, Dar described it as a “watershed moment” for the country.
Read More : Pakistan warns Afghanistan after Kohat attack, says it can eliminate terror threats ‘wherever they are’
“Pakistan was the first country to open its doors to our Afghan brethren at the time,” he said, adding that Islamabad had also hosted the 17th Extraordinary Session of the OIC-CFM on Dec 19, 2021, to garner the solidarity of Islamic countries and mobilise international support to address the humanitarian situation in Afghanistan.
“It was hoped that the Taliban would honour Afghanistan's international obligations and their own commitments by eliminating terrorism, promoting inclusivity and protecting the human rights of its citizens,” the foreign minister said.
However, he said, the expectations of OIC members and the wider international community had remained unfulfilled.
Dar said the Taliban had consequently “failed to seize the opportunity to integrate Afghanistan with the wider world and to improve the lives of the Afghan people” because of what he described as their “misplaced priorities and flawed ideologies”.
“As fellow OIC members, regional partners and neighbours, we can help Afghanistan integrate with the international community. But the Taliban must first take the steps necessary to create a conducive environment,” he said.
Dar said the foremost requirement was “concrete and verifiable actions” to prevent Afghan soil from being used for terrorism against neighbouring countries.
Read : Pakistan carries out 'calibrated' air strikes against terrorist hideouts near Afghan border after K-P attacks
He particularly referred to attacks against Pakistan that, he said, were planned and orchestrated from Afghanistan with external backing to destabilise the region.
“Pakistan is seriously concerned over the presence of more than two dozen terrorist groups inside Afghanistan, particularly the TTP, BLA and Majeed Brigade, ISIL-K (Daesh), Al-Qaida and ETIM that threaten regional and international peace and security,” he said.
He said Pakistan’s law enforcement agencies were making “enormous sacrifices” to counter terrorism as Pakistanis continued to be targeted and martyred by terrorist groups operating with impunity from Afghan soil.
Dar recalled the suicide bombing at a mosque in Kohat in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa the previous week, saying it had “martyred at least 24 Pakistanis”.
He also thanked Qatar, Türkiye and Saudi Arabia for their mediation and “sincere efforts” to counsel the Taliban and find amicable solutions.
Dar said the OIC, as “a collective voice of the Muslim world”, had a vital role in addressing the situation in Afghanistan and urged the group to call on the Taliban to take several steps, foremost among them eliminating terrorism and ending the patronage of terrorist groups.
“They must not allow Afghan soil to be used for orchestrating terrorist attacks against neighbouring countries,” he said.
He also called on the Taliban to honour their international obligations and commitments and curb trafficking through illegal smuggling networks, including narcotics, weapons and human trafficking.
Dar further urged the Taliban to lift restrictions on women and girls that were contrary to Islamic principles and norms of Muslim society and to reconsider policies that denied fundamental freedoms to ordinary Afghans.
He said Afghans had “already suffered enough from civil war and conflict”.
Dar referred to the ninth OIC Ministerial Conference on Women, held in Islamabad on July 12-13, 2026, which had expressed “deep concern” over continued restrictions on girls’ education and women’s employment in Afghanistan.
He also called for governance through a politically inclusive process involving all ethnicities and minorities.
Also Read : No change in Pakistan's Afghan policy
The foreign minister urged the Taliban to facilitate the resettlement and integration of Afghan returnees in their homeland, while saying the international community also had a responsibility to share the burden.
Dar said international donors must provide adequate funding to meet Afghanistan’s humanitarian aid requirements and support its socio-economic development.
In this regard, he commended the work being done by the OIC Office in Kabul, as well as humanitarian support provided through the Afghanistan Humanitarian Trust Fund and the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre.
“No country desires normalcy and stability in Afghanistan more than Pakistan, and no country has suffered from the consequences of instability and insecurity in Afghanistan more than Pakistan,” he said.
Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to supporting efforts aimed at achieving a stable and prosperous Afghanistan at peace with itself and its neighbours, but stressed that this would require “mutual respect, sincerity and demonstration of necessary political will by the Taliban.”
Tensions between the two countries have escalated over the last year amid mutual accusations over cross-border militancy. Islamabad has long maintained that terrorists linked to the TTP operate from Afghan territory, while Kabul has denied the allegations and accused Pakistan of violating its sovereignty through alleged strikes.
Pakistan has maintained that meaningful engagement with the Taliban government cannot resume unless Kabul takes concrete and verifiable action against banned terrorist groups, particularly the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), which Islamabad says operates from Afghan territory to plan and carry out attacks inside Pakistan.
The issue of terrorist sanctuaries remains the central source of friction between the two countries. Islamabad has repeatedly conveyed to Kabul that assurances alone are insufficient and that Pakistan wants to see demonstrable action against groups it considers responsible for attacks on its territory.
The Pakistani position also extends to other terrorist organisations operating from Afghan territory, including the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA).
The deterioration in bilateral ties, particularly over the TTP issue, has significantly narrowed the space for diplomatic initiatives.
Pakistan appears to be keeping diplomatic channels and limited institutional contacts open while refusing to resume substantive engagement with Kabul until it sees concrete and verifiable action against militant groups operating from Afghan soil.

title: AI a powerful engine for financial inclusion
description: AI a powerful engine for financial inclusion
content:
Saqib argues gap not due to technology, but because of rules
Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority Chairman Bilal Bin Saqib has said that artificial intelligence and tokenisation can become the developing world's most powerful engines for financial inclusion, provided they are built for people left outside of the financial system.
He delivered a keynote address on financial inclusion, AI and tokenisation at a forum marking 50 years of microcredit at the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly.
Speaking at the Social Business, Youth and Technology Forum, Saqib, who is also the minister of state, spoke about the choice now facing emerging economies as the rules of global finance were rewritten.
The address placed Pakistan's own journey within a wider story. Worldwide, an estimated 1.3 billion adults remain without an account at any financial institution, while close to 900 million of them already own a mobile phone. The gap, he argued, was no longer one of technology but of rails and rules, and of the willingness to build them.
It was highlighted that in 2018, Pakistan closed its banking system to digital assets. With the passage of the Virtual Assets Act 2026, that door was reopened under a clear regulatory framework, followed by the establishment of a regulatory sandbox and the launch of licensing regulations for virtual asset service providers.

title: Selective buying lifts PSX after mid session fall
description: Selective buying lifts PSX after mid session fall
content:
Index gains 249 points amid hopes of easing geopolitical tensions, softer oil
Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) on Tuesday overcame a bout of profit-taking in the afternoon and ended trading on a firmer note as renewed buying helped the market recoup losses.
Investor interest was bolstered by expectations of a breakthrough in efforts to resolve the US-Iran conflict, although profit-booking later in the session trimmed gains. The decline proved temporary as buyers returned to lift the market back into the green The benchmark KSE-100 index closed up 248.92 points, or 0.15%, at 171,402.08. During the proceedings, it hit the intra-day high of 171,680.74 and the low of 170,866.94. Oil and gas exploration, cement and power stocks led the recovery, while weakness in commercial banks and fertiliser shares kept the advance modest.
According to Ahmed Sheraz at KASB KTrade, the KSE-100 closed up 249 points (+0.15%), with 123 milllion shares traded. The market remained mildly positive as easing geopolitical concerns and lower international oil prices supported sentiment. Oil and gas stocks staged a recovery after Brent crude slipped below $100 and traded around $98, easing concerns over inflationary pressures.
Investor confidence was further supported by reports that Iran had conveyed to the US administration that it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if Washington lifted the blockade. The development raised hopes of improved oil flows and a reduction in the geopolitical risk premium, supporting recovery in the oil segment, Sheraz added. He anticipated that the market would remain cautiously positive, with Brent prices, US-Iran developments and Hormuz shipping traffic being key drivers.
"Oil & gas and cement sectors provided notable support during Tuesday's session while buying interest was also visible across pharma, power, technology and engineering stocks," commented JS Global analyst Mubashir Anis Naviwala.
On the other hand, banks and fertiliser stocks remained relatively subdued. International oil prices eased to a two-week low amid expectations of improving supply from the Gulf region. Overall, the session reflected selective buying with a cautious tone as investors continued to monitor regional developments and oil-market conditions, Naviwala added.
Arif Habib Limited Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib said sentiment was initially fragile but the KSE-100 gained 249 points, or 0.15%, to close at 171,402. Value hunters showed renewed interest as oil prices fell on easing supply concerns and diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz gained momentum.
In corporate news, Sitara Petroleum Service posted FY26 earnings of Rs4,976 million, up 69% year-on-year, while 4QFY26 profit fell 10% to Rs570 million due to inventory losses, lower supplies and the absence of volumetric discounts. Dealer margins stood at Rs8.64/litre. The company declared a final cash dividend of Re1/share, taking FY26 payout to 34%.
Mari Energies, PPL, Hub Power, Fauji Cement and Lucky Cement added 233 points, while Bank AL Habib, Fauji Fertiliser, MCB Bank, Bank Alfalah and Askari Bank dragged the index down by 216 points. He expected the market to stay volatile, with selective buying if geopolitical tensions eased further and oil prices declined. Cumulatively, trading volumes decreased to 641.8 million shares compared with Monday's tally of 692.9 million.
In the ready market, shares of 494 companies were traded. Of these, 226 stocks closed higher, 221 fell and 47 stood unchanged.
Tasdeeq Information led the volumes with trading in 133.2 million shares, losing Rs0.09 to close at Rs4.91. Foreign investors bought shares worth Rs323.7 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

title: USF approves Rs32 9b to push 4G projects
description: USF approves Rs32 9b to push 4G projects
content:
Clears rural connectivity plan for 15 schemes to advance tech to 3.7m people
The Universal Service Fund (USF) policy committee approved a Rs32.90 billion budget for fiscal year 2026-27 on Tuesday and advanced 15 4G projects that target 3.66 million people across 1,893 mauzas in 21 districts.
Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja chaired the meeting. USF Chief Executive Officer Mudassar Naveed and senior management presented the programme portfolio and budget priorities.
The committee allocated Rs24.89 billion for payments on ongoing work and set aside Rs6.56 billion for new initiatives. It also released Rs5.57 billion for the first quarter so teams could execute the approved programme without delay.
USF currently runs 28 projects – 17 Next Generation Broadband Service Delivery schemes and 11 Next Generation Optical Fibre Network Services schemes. The new allocation covers nine additional NG-BSD projects, four NG-OFNS projects and block funds for small lots that reach remote settlements.
Official project data shows that 15 contracted 4G schemes carry a combined subsidy of Rs14.008 billion and cover a target population of 3.66 million. The Kurram project leads progress with 75% completion. It covers 40 mauzas and 251,980 people with a Rs92.25 million subsidy.
Five projects stand at 50%, which include Pishin, Chiniot, Abbottabad, Badin and Kohat. Pishin spans Pishin, Killa Abdullah and Quetta, covers 306 mauzas and targets 574,545 people with a Rs1.32 billion subsidy – the largest population among the 15 schemes.
Chiniot covers 117 mauzas and 333,267 people. Abbottabad covers 61 mauzas and 157,473 people. Badin covers 144 mauzas and 432,666 people. Kohat, including the former Frontier Region Kohat, covers 24 mauzas and 41,404 people. Umar Kot and Khuzdar stand at 25%. Umar Kot covers 142 mauzas and 243,695 people with a Rs914.61 million subsidy. Khuzdar covers 144 mauzas and 75,637 people and holds the largest subsidy of about Rs2.945 billion.
Work continues on Small Lot P-15, Gujranwala, Muzaffargarh, Mansehra, Haripur, Rajanpur and Sujawal. Small Lot P-15 covers nine mauzas in Bahawalnagar, Faisalabad, Sheikhupura and Hafizabad and targets 15,700 people.
Gujranwala and Mandi Bahauddin cover 160 mauzas and 234,573 people. Muzaffargarh targets 498,927 people across 138 mauzas. Rajanpur covers 215 mauzas and 301,512 people. Sujawal covers 144 mauzas and 246,759 people.
These projects extend 4G coverage, open online services and create connectivity-enabled opportunities in underserved communities. The Ministry of IT and Telecom and USF pursue digital inclusion and close the digital divide through sustained, targeted investment. WITH ADDITIONAL INPUT FROM APP
