content:
Warns Iran it faces a stark choice between 'obliteration' and 'potential greatness'
US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that members of his team held a "very good" three-hour meeting with an Iranian delegation in New York that concluded an hour before his news conference, ahead of his bilateral meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
"Yeah, today. About an hour ago," Trump said when asked if anyone from his team had met with the Iranian delegation, describing the meeting as "very well."
"It ended an hour ago. It was a meeting that lasted for three hours," he said, noting that "it was a very good meeting. I mean, I must tell you it was a very good I can't imagine why they wouldn't want to do it."
. @POTUS says his representatives met with the Iranian delegation to the United Nations earlier today: "I can't imagine why they wouldn't want to do it... In one case, it's obliteration and the other alternative is potential greatness. It could be a great country." pic.twitter.com/yTBO2ZGBuu
Arguing that Iran was facing a stark choice, he said: "In one case it's obliteration, and the other alternative is potential greatness. It could be a great country."
Asked who attended the meeting, Trump directed the question to US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, and asked if they wanted to comment.
He later said, "They had a very good meeting, very productive meeting, and they have another one scheduled in the very near future."
Trump on Iran: They have another meeting scheduled in the very near future. pic.twitter.com/kjdTjEoYKx
"There are two alternatives," Trump said. "One is a very bad thing, and another, it could lead to greatness for the country."
For his part, Witkoff said: "I feel very good right now. I feel very good. It's a blessing working for President Trump."
Earlier, Iran and the United States had hinted at the prospect of reviving negotiations to end their conflict, with ​the presidents of both countries due at the UN General Assembly in New York.
The event would be the first attended by Trump and Masoud Pezeshkian since Trump launched "Operation Epic Fury" against ‌Iran in February, alongside Israel. Trump had said on Sunday he would be open to a meeting with the Iranian president.
A senior Iranian official said there were no plans for the two leaders to meet directly, but that Iran's delegation had full authority to revive talks.
Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz to Gulf shipping within seven days if the US fulfilled Tehran's demands to ease military pressure and lift an American blockade on Iranian ports, the Iranian official said, adding that Iran had conveyed its latest proposal to Washington via ​mediators last week.
"The US needs to announce that it wants to resolve the issue diplomatically, make that official, and then agree on a timeline for how the process will move forward," the official said. "The UN General ​Assembly is a golden opportunity for the US to return to diplomacy."
Read: Bab al-Mandeb tensions test Egypt’s Suez Canal
Secretary of State Marco Rubio told NBC the US was open to speaking with the Iranians, "especially ⁠if it has the prospects of leading to something positive and ultimately achieving the goal of what this is all about".
No face-to-face meetings between Iran and the United States are known to have taken place since July, when an ​agreement on an interim deal to end the war collapsed just weeks after it was signed by Trump and Pezeshkian.
Asked by Fox and Friends about the prospect of a meeting between the presidents, Rubio said of Trump: "He's a businessman ​who comes from the world of practicality and common sense. And common sense tells you there's no harm in engaging and talking to someone."
But Rubio also noted that Pezeshkian is subordinate under Iran's ruling system to Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, "and the supreme leader is a radical Shia cleric and we need to remember that when we talk".
"The central issue here is Iran is run by lunatic clerics," he told Fox . "These people can never have nuclear weapons."
In a reminder of Iran's firm position so far, ​Parliament Speaker Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf, who headed Iran's negotiating team at previous talks, said on Tuesday that Iran would never surrender: "Trump must understand that he cannot impose his power on the Iranian people and its armed forces."
Trump is due ​to meet on Tuesday with leaders of the six Gulf Arab states: Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.
All are keen to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz but wary of giving their longstanding rival Iran too much ‌power. All apart ⁠from Oman also host huge US military bases that have come under repeated Iranian attack throughout the war.
The biggest of them, Saudi Arabia, has been drawn deeper into the war this month, with Houthi fighters aligned to Iran advancing in Yemen, routing forces of a Saudi-backed government there and threatening Saudi oil exports through the Red Sea.
There was some relief on oil markets on Tuesday, after sources told Reuters that Saudi Arabia had restarted operations at its East-West Pipeline and could resume exports within hours, albeit at reduced volume, from the Red Sea port of Yanbu.
The pipeline, Saudi Arabia's main alternative route for exports to bypass wartime disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, was shut down ​after attacks this month that Riyadh blamed on Iranian allies ​in Iraq.
The Houthis have routed Saudi-supported government forces ⁠along the Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at its mouth, and have attacked Saudi Arabia directly with missiles and drones. The fighters are now pushing to seize the strategic heights of the Kahboub Mountains that overlook the Red Sea coast.
Read More: Saudi king denounces Houthis as 'terrorist militia' after Makkah attack
The US, which bombed the Houthis for two months last year, has so far rebuffed repeated pleas from Saudi Arabia's ​Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to rejoin the fight. The New York Times reported that Trump called off US strikes against the Houthis on Sunday at the ​last minute, after troops had already ⁠begun loading bombs onto planes.
Asked why Washington had so far held back from striking the Houthis, Rubio said: "Ultimately, if it comes down to it, the United States will always stand with Saudi Arabia and support them because we have an agreement with them to do so.
"That said, that is a very dangerous and complex conflict that pre-exists... We have a history with the Houthis as well, and that's something we don't want to see impacted either."
On the table at ⁠the Gulf states' meeting ​with Trump is a Qatari proposal for a framework to bring Iran and the Arab Gulf states into a common security architecture, regional ​sources said. One source said Iran was reviewing the proposal.
Speaking at a Qatar Economic Forum in New York on Sunday, Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani said any such arrangement would need to provide security guarantees for the Gulf states and expand economic interdependence with Iran.
"Lasting ​security cannot be built through repeated cycles of escalations and retaliation, or arrangements that leave any state permanently exposed to insecurity," Sheikh Mohammed said.

title: Yu Zidi  fearless swimming prodigy  13  with Olympics in her sights
description: She becomes youngest ever medallist at the swimming world championships
content:
She becomes youngest-ever medallist at the swimming world championships
China's Yu Zidi made history last year aged 12 when she became the youngest-ever medallist at the swimming world championships. Now a teenager, she is dominating the Asian Games and has Olympic glory in her sights.
The 13-year-old school girl with a pixie hair cut stunned the sporting world last year with a series of eye-popping times.
At the 2025 World Aquatics Championships in Singapore she helped China reach the 4x200m women's freestyle relay final.
She did not swim in the final but China came third, earning Yu a historic bronze for swimming in the heats.
Yu just missed out on medals in the 200m and 400m individual medley events and the 200m butterfly, coming fourth in all three races.
In November at China's National Games, having just turned 13, she clocked a blistering 2:07.41 in the women's 200m medley for what was then an Asian record.
Now she is cleaning up at the Asian Games in Japan, winning gold in all three individual events she entered.
She won the 200m butterfly and 200m individual medley, then completed the hat-trick with victory in the 400m IM on Wednesday.
All three victories were in Games-record times.
While training with the China team in Beijing before the Games, she told local media she was "excited" for her Asian Games debut.
"Train well, don't slack off. Demonstrate the level of your training and work hard to break past yourself," she said, according to state news agency Xinhua.
A coach, Ha Sinan, once described Yu with a Chinese saying that translates as "a newborn calf fearless of tigers".
But the teenager has spoken of struggling to deal with the heavy load placed on her.
Yu grew up in the city of Baoding, about 150 kilometres (90 miles) south of Beijing.
She was discovered by a swimming coach while at a water park aged six and since then has juggled schoolwork with training.
"Being in class all day and still having to train was really tiring," she said in January.
"Sometimes I was so tired I could fall asleep even while eating," she said at an event celebrating Hebei province's National Games wins.
Yu said she "never considered quitting" and always dreamed of being a national champion.
But during the tune-up to last year's National Games she said the pressure of wanting to win the 400m medley nearly became too much.
"It was like a big stone that weighed on me and made it hard to breathe," she said.
Yu eventually told her coach she wanted to do anything other than train.
Her coach told her to persevere and "believe in yourself", she said.
Yu went on to win four medals at the National Games.
Some in the swimming world have questioned the mental and physical impact of high-level training and competing on Yu at such a young age.
Under World Aquatics rules, the minimum age for international championships is 14 but exceptions can be made for younger swimmers if -- like Yu -- they are fast enough.
It seems certain that Yu will compete at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, when she will be 15, and if she can sustain her current trajectory will be a major medal threat.
She is aware that her success for someone so young has made international headlines.
But she knows hard work outweighs innate talent.
In June she won the women's 400m medley in 4:30.79 at China's national championships, a time which would easily have earned her silver at the Paris Games in 2024.
"Although talent determines where you start, going further and standing taller is dependent on perseverance and effort day after day," Yu said at the January event.
"There is still a long road ahead," she added.
"I will keep holding fast to my original dream, drawing strength from my team, to stand on the Olympic podium."

title: Aslam Khan set to join Bangladesh s Abahani Limited
description: The club seeks six month multiple entry visa for Pakistan goalkeeping coach as it strengthens its coaching setup
content:
The club seeks six-month multiple entry visa for Pakistan goalkeeping coach as it strengthens its coaching setup
Pakistan goalkeeping coach Muhammad Aslam Khan is set to take up a coaching role with Bangladesh club Abahani Limited after signing a contract with the Dhaka-based side for the 2026-2027 Bangladesh Football League season.
Aslam will proceed to Bangaldesh after he will get Bangaldesh visa.
Aslam's move to Abahani comes after his involvement with Pakistan's national football setup. He has worked as a goalkeeping coach within Pakistan's senior team structure and brings experience from the country's international football programme to one of Bangladesh's best-known clubs.
Abahani have retained head coach Maruful Haque for a third successive season, while former Bangladesh international Shahid Hossain Swapan has taken on a managerial role as the club looks to rebuild its squad and coaching structure.
The club finished runners-up in the previous two Bangladesh league campaigns and is seeking to mount another challenge for domestic honours in the 2026-2027 season.
Aslam's arrival is particularly significant for Abahani's goalkeeping department. As a specialist coach, he will be responsible for working with the club's goalkeepers and helping prepare them for the demands of domestic competition.
Aslam was recently ignored by Pakistan for its senior team’s ASEAN Cup campaign in Indonesia despite being part of a recent title-winning campaign.
For Aslam, the move represents an opportunity to continue his coaching career outside Pakistan while working in one of South Asia's established football leagues.
Abahani was founded in 1972 by Sheikh Kamal, eldest son of Bangladesh’s founding leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, after reorganising Iqbal Sporting Club. The club became a limited company in 1989. Abahani won its first Dhaka First Division title in 1974 and developed a major rivalry with Mohammedan SC, known as the Dhaka Derby. The club continued to grow and became one of Bangladesh’s most successful football institutions. Abahani remains a prominent club in Bangladeshi football, with a long history of domestic success and strong fan support.

title: Cindy Crawford    heartbroken    following son Presley Gerber   s death at 27
description: Presley  the only son of Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber  died at a rehabilitation facility in California
content:
Presley, the only son of Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber, died at a rehabilitation facility in California
Cindy Crawford is “heartbroken” following the death of her son, Presley Gerber, who died on September 20 at the age of 27, according to a source close to the supermodel.
“Cindy is completely in shock over Presley's devastating death,” the source told PEOPLE. “She is heartbroken.”
Presley, the only son of Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber, died at a rehabilitation facility in California. The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner has confirmed that an autopsy was completed, but the official cause and manner of death have been deferred while additional testing is carried out.
Santa Monica police records indicate that officers responded to a report of a possible overdose and cardiac arrest on the morning of September 20. However, the medical examiner has stressed that the investigation remains ongoing and that it could take months before an official determination is made.
A source close to Presley’s sister, model and actress Kaia Gerber, previously told PEOPLE that the family is “in total shock” following his death. The source said they were “saddened beyond words” and praised Presley for being open about his struggles and for using his experiences to help others.
Another source who has been close to Crawford said the model and Rande were consistently involved in their son’s life throughout his struggles and were deeply supportive of him.
“This was never a situation involving two absent Hollywood parents,” the source said. “Cindy and Rande could not have been more supportive of Presley. They were always there for him and did everything they could to help him.”
Presley had previously spoken publicly about his experiences with mental health and substance use. In a 2023 appearance on the Studio 22 podcast, he discussed his struggles with depression and said he hoped his experiences could help other people facing similar challenges.
“I think that whether I help one person or a hundred people get out of that place that I was in at one point in my life, that's all I need to do,” he said at the time.
Presley’s final public appearance came in June 2026 at a mental health awareness event in Malibu, where he appeared alongside his parents. During a panel discussion, he spoke about the pressure of growing up in the public eye and the freedom he found in being open about his experiences.
The Gerber family has asked for privacy as they mourn Presley’s death. The medical examiner’s investigation remains ongoing, with further testing required before his official cause and manner of death can be determined.

title: J K  Simmons joins Will Poulter in Apple TV   s thriller  Beat the Reaper
description: J K  Simmons joins Will Poulter in Apple TV   s  Beat the Reaper   a crime thriller based on Josh Bazell   s novel
content:
J.K. Simmons joins Will Poulter in Apple TV’s 'Beat the Reaper', a crime thriller based on Josh Bazell’s novel
J.K. Simmons has joined Will Poulter as a series regular in Beat the Reaper , an upcoming Apple TV crime thriller based on Josh Bazell’s novel of the same name.
Simmons will play Dr. Friendly, an incompetent surgeon who works at the same Boston hospital as Poulter’s character, Dr. Peter Brown. The series comes from Apple Studios and New Regency, with Sam Catlin serving as showrunner and executive producer.
Beat the Reaper follows Brown, an intern working at one of Boston’s toughest hospitals who has a hidden past. His life changes when a patient recognises him from his previous life, forcing him to flee from government agents, mob hitmen and other threats while trying to survive an increasingly dangerous situation.
Tim Van Patten, known for directing episodes of The Sopranos , Boardwalk Empire and Black Mirror , will direct the pilot and executive produce the Apple TV series.
Catlin will executive produce the project under his overall deal with Apple TV. Arnon Milchan, Yariv Milchan, Natalie Lehmann and Laura Delahaye will also executive produce for New Regency, while Rachel Toffler will serve as co-executive producer.
Simmons won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor in 2015 for his performance as jazz instructor Terence Fletcher in Whiplash . He later received an Oscar nomination for playing William Frawley in Being the Ricardos . His television credits include MGM+ series The Westies .
Van Patten won an Emmy for Outstanding Directing for a Drama Series in 2012 for Boardwalk Empire . He has also directed projects including The Pacific , Franklin , The Sopranos , Black Mirror and Perry Mason .
The Apple TV series does not yet have a confirmed release date.

title: Saudi Arabia restarts East West oil pipeline  sources say
description: Saudi Arabia blamed Iraqi militia for drone attacks that forced a pipeline shutdown and halted Yanbu crude loadings
content:
Saudi Arabia blamed Iraqi militia for drone attacks that forced a pipeline shutdown and halted Yanbu crude loadings
Saudi Arabia ‌has restarted operations at its East-West Pipeline and could resume exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu later on Tuesday, three sources briefed on the matter said, as signs mounted of an increase in Middle Eastern oil flows.
The resumption of supplies on Tuesday helped ​to drive selling on global oil markets. Global oil benchmark Brent crude fell by more than $2 a ​barrel towards $97, its lowest since September 8.
Drone attacks, which Saudi Arabia has blamed on an Iraqi ⁠militia, forced the kingdom to shut the pipeline on September 11, halting crude loadings at the kingdom's Yanbu port.
Since the U.S.-Israeli war ​on Iran disrupted oil flows from Saudi Arabia and its Gulf neighbours through the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh has been ​using the pipeline to reroute around 4 million barrels per day — around 4% of global supply — to Yanbu.
State oil firm Saudi Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Full resumption could take weeks, sources say
The pipeline was pumping at a low rate after ​its restart, two of the sources said.
Read More: G7 leaders condemn Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia
Aramco was seeking to get the pumping rate back to four million bpd, ​one of the sources said. The pipeline has a capacity of 7m bpd.
Reaching a rate of 40% of capacity will take ‌a ⁠couple of days and a full restart will take six to eight weeks, a security source said. A separate oil industry source said a return to full pumping rates would take up to six weeks.
Three pumping stations serving the pipeline were damaged in the drone attack, according to satellite imagery and industry sources. The line is serviced by 11 ​pumping stations and two separate ​pressure relief stations, according ⁠to industry assessments.
The pipeline will resume crude supply to Aramco refineries located on the Red Sea coast, one of the sources said, adding that one cargo was scheduled to load ​at Yanbu later on Tuesday. The person said it would be bound for China.
Traders ​were getting ⁠ready for Saudi oil loadings by moving tankers to Egypt's Mediterranean Port Said for ship-to-ship transfers and also to Sidi Kerir, another two trading sources said.
Oil prices have also dropped this week after Iran said it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz ⁠within seven ​days and because Saudi Arabia has loaded more ships at its Ras ​Tanura port, raising expectations of increased exports through the Strait.

title: UN chief says Israeli actions in occupied West Bank raising    spectre of ethnic cleansing
description: Guterres urges world leaders to use UN General Assembly week to pursue Middle East de escalation and dialogue
content:
Guterres urges world leaders to use UN General Assembly week to pursue Middle East de-escalation and dialogue
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned on Tuesday that Israeli violence, displacement and illegal settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank are undermining prospects for peace and raising the risk of “ethnic cleansing”.
“Violence, displacement, and settlement expansion by Israel in the occupied West Bank are bulldozing the path to peace and raising the spectre of ethnic cleansing,” Guterres said in an address to the 81st UN General Assembly in New York.
“We cannot allow the two-state solution to disappear before our eyes,” he added.
Guterres said the devastating situation in the occupied Palestinian territories must not be overlooked amid the broader turmoil engulfing the Middle East.
He described the October 7, 2023 attacks by Hamas as “abhorrent” but said they were followed by “an onslaught on Palestinians in Gaza, with a scale of killing and destruction unlike anything I’ve witnessed in my years as secretary-general”.
He recalled that the International Court of Justice had issued legally binding provisional measures in the case concerning the application of the Genocide Convention in the Gaza Strip.
The UN chief also referred to an advisory opinion issued by the court, saying the UN must be allowed to carry out its mandates in Gaza and that its staff and humanitarian personnel must be protected.
“All parties must comply with international law and the court’s orders,” he stressed.
Turning to the wider region, Guterres said conflicts were “cascading” across the Middle East, while so-called ceasefires had amounted to “little more than lesser fires”, with civilians continuing to bear the cost.
“I appeal to the leaders in this chamber to maximise this high-level week for de-escalation and dialogue,” he said.
Guterres urged the international community to send a clear message that the fighting must end, humanitarian assistance must be allowed to flow, and navigational rights and freedoms must be fully restored in line with international law.
On Ukraine, Guterres said Russia’s war had subjected a sovereign country to “a brutal war in blatant violation” of the UN Charter.
He described the conflict in Sudan as “a war on civilians”, pointing to mass displacement, hunger, attacks on hospitals and homes, sexual violence and ethnically driven attacks.
Read More: Pakistan, seven other Muslim countries demand Israel to fulfil Gaza ceasefire commitments
The UN chief also said that Myanmar’s crisis risked slipping from global attention.
He called for reform of the UN Security Council, saying: “A 21st-century Security Council without permanent African seats is unjust and indefensible.”
Guterres said today power was increasingly derived from data, computing capacity and algorithms, while control of those resources was highly concentrated.
“The danger is not technology. The danger is technology without accountability, capability without oversight, decision-making without transparency,” he said.
Countries with the greatest AI capabilities also carry the greatest responsibilities, he said, urging them to share information on emerging safety risks, cooperate on testing and work toward common safeguards.
Guterres called for a multilateral AI risk-management framework supported by credible and independent oversight, while ensuring that no country is left behind.
“Artificial intelligence must be shaped by humanity, with humanity, and for all humanity,” he said, adding that “children must never become the test subjects for unregulated systems.”

title: Govt decreases petrol by Rs1.7, HSD by Rs3.12 for Sept 23 | The Express Tribune
description: Petrol price decreases to Rs392.05 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs418.96
content:
Petrol price decreases to Rs392.05 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs418.96
The federal government on Tuesday decreased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.7 and Rs3.12 per litre, respectively, for September 23.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs392.05 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs418.96 per litre for Wednesday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government increased the price of petrol by Rs4.61 per litre while reducing the price of HSD by Rs1.96 per litre for September 22.
Read : Govt increases petrol price by Rs4.61, cuts diesel by Rs1.96 for Sept 22
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 18, in a bid to provide relief to the public, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed the immediate inclusion of 20-year-old motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqi rickshaws in the Prime Minister Fuel Relief Scheme, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said.
The statement further added that all motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqi rickshaws registered after January 1, 2006, would be eligible for registration in the Prime Minister Fuel Relief Scheme.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices rose on Tuesday as traders worried about global supplies after US President Donald Trump told ‌the United Nations General Assembly in a speech that a peace deal with Iran could come after the US midterm elections, which are not until early November.
The Brent crude futures November ​contract was down 40 cents, or 40%, to $99.94 a barrel at 10:07 am CDT (1507 GMT). The WTI October ⁠contract, which expires on Tuesday, was down 36 cents, or 0.37%, to $95.43 a barrel.
"Saudi Arabia is acting, not waiting," said Phil Flynn, senior analyst at Price Futures Group. "After Houthi hits on the East-West pipeline forced a shutdown of Yanbu loadings, Aramco loaded about 14 million barrels of crude onto seven VLCCs inside the Gulf. Satellite and tracker data showed ​Saudi oil moving through Hormuz, averaging about 2.9 million barrels a day over the last six days, up from roughly 700,000 barrels ​a day in August".

title: Lionel Richie cancels three concerts after heart procedure
description: Richie was hospitalised this week after experiencing the heart condition  which causes an irregular heartbeat
content:
Richie was hospitalised this week after experiencing the heart condition, which causes an irregular heartbeat
Lionel Richie has canceled his next three concerts after undergoing a heart procedure to treat atrial fibrillation.
The 77-year-old singer was hospitalised this week after experiencing the heart condition, which causes an irregular heartbeat. His representative confirmed that Richie underwent a procedure for atrial fibrillation and said it went successfully.
“The doctor said everything went perfectly,” Richie’s representative said in a statement. “Lionel is doing great but will take some time off and will be back on stage soon.”
As a result, Richie and Earth, Wind & Fire have canceled three upcoming performances on their Sing a Song All Night Long tour. The shows were scheduled for September 26 at Chase Center in San Francisco, September 30 at United Center in Chicago and October 2 at Schottenstein Center in Columbus, Ohio.
Fans affected by the cancellations will receive refunds through their original points of purchase. The San Francisco concert had already been rescheduled from August after Earth, Wind & Fire drummer John Paris experienced a medical emergency.
Richie's latest health setback follows several interruptions to his touring schedule this year. In June, he ended a concert in St. Paul, Minnesota, early after telling the audience that he felt dizzy and unwell. Several performances were subsequently postponed while he recovered.
The singer later returned to the stage, but after an August 29 performance in St. Louis, he was hospitalised again for cardiac testing. He was released from hospital on September 2.
Despite the latest cancellations, Richie is expected to return to performing after taking time to recover. His representative has said that he will be back on stage soon, while his remaining Las Vegas performances beginning October 14 are still listed as scheduled.

title: British PM Burnham says it is right to    move beyond    past criticism of Trump
description: Burnham criticised Trump in 2017  saying he would not meet him as a matter of principle over his posts
content:
Burnham criticised Trump in 2017, saying he would not meet him as a matter of principle over his posts
The UK is "ready to play our part in the Middle East" conflict, British Premier Andy Burnham told US President Donald Trump during their first meeting in New York on Tuesday.
Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Burnham said the UK was prepared to help with efforts to stop the conflict and "open the Strait [of Hormuz]."
"We're with you that Iran must never be a nuclear power," he told Trump.
Burnham said the two discussed "issues on trade" and "the Falklands," as well as immigration. He said he had spoken about his "commitment to get [immigration] to a controlled approach."
The prime minister also welcomed Trump's earlier statement that progress was possible on peace in Ukraine.
UK PM Burnham says he and US President Trump have established 'good connection'
NEW YORK, Sept 22 (Reuters) - British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Tuesday he and US President Donald Trump had "established a good connection in our early discussions" despite their differences on some foreign policy issues as they met for the first time in New York.
Trump called Burnham a "natural business person" after their meeting, where they discussed issues including Ukraine, the status of the Falkland Islands and trade.
"This relationship matters so much to us and we'll build on that," Burnham said.
One of the biggest foreign policy challenges facing Burnham will be managing Britain's relationship with the United States, but he and his officials are likely to be relieved that their first public meeting passed off smoothly.
Long regarded as one of the world's closest alliances, the partnership has been strained by Trump's foreign policy agenda, including the US-Israeli decision to attack Iran this year.
After their meeting, Trump again criticised Britain's plan to resolve the status of a US-British military base on the Indian Ocean island of Diego Garcia, calling it a "terrible deal".
Britain last year agreed a deal to cede sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius after more than two centuries of control, while retaining a 99-year lease over its biggest island, Diego Garcia, and its strategic military base.
But the legislation required to implement the agreement was paused because of opposition from the United States.
"I don't support it. It was a terrible deal," Trump said on Tuesday.
"Somebody has ownership that never showed up before after decades and centuries. I think it's ridiculous."
Earlier British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Tuesday played down his previous criticism of US President Donald Trump, ahead of a meeting with him in New York.
Speaking to journalists on his flight to the US, Burnham said politicians make comments throughout their careers, but the focus should be on the current relationship.
Burnham has previously been critical of Trump. In 2017, he said he would not meet Trump as a “matter of principle”, citing the president's “hateful, extremist material” posted online.
Following the storming of the US Capitol by Trump supporters in January 2021, Burnham said: “Any UK politician who gave Trump the time of day should be ashamed right now.”
Burnham said it was now time to move on from them. “Politicians say things throughout their career, but now the important thing is to focus on the moment you are in,” he said.
He said he raised Trump's previous description of him as “the mayor of a town” in their first phone call.
Read More: Trump says there will be a deal with Iran after the midterms
“I did say to the president in our first phone call, I said Mr president, Manchester isn’t ‘some town’. I said ‘this is Manchester’.”
“And so yes, the right thing to do is to have a laugh about it, isn’t it, and move beyond it.”
Asked whether he could trust Trump, Burnham said the relationship between the UK and US was deeper than individual political disagreements.
“When you come into this job, you realise how deep this relationship is. We trust our allies. Of course, we do.”
Asked specifically whether he trusted Trump personally, Burnham replied: “Yes.”

Seize crystal meth worth $21m after containers bound for Colombo raise suspicion
Pakistan and the United States have seized approximately 463 kilogrammes of crystal methamphetamine, valued at $21 million, in a coordinated operation targeting an illicit narcotics network originating in Afghanistan, the US Embassy in Islamabad said on Tuesday.
In a statement, the embassy said the seizure took place on August 30 after its Drug Enforcement Administration office in Islamabad (DEA Islamabad) coordinated with the Anti-Narcotics Force (ANF), in cooperation with Sri Lanka’s Police Narcotics Bureau and the DEA’s New Delhi office.
“Between August 14-29, ANF’s Karachi-based Port Control Unit identified containers scheduled for transport from Pakistan to Colombo, which ANF suspected to be carrying illicit narcotics that originated in Afghanistan,” the statement said.

The identification of the containers prompted the ANF to alert DEA Islamabad, which worked with authorities across the countries involved to seize the narcotics and arrest several suspects, including those of Pakistani origin, according to the embassy.
The embassy said the US government had provided foreign assistance to sustain training for Pakistan’s ANF, enabling it to serve as a key partner in advancing US priorities in counternarcotics interdiction.
“The Trump administration has made halting the flow of illicit narcotics a key component of helping make America more secure,” it said.
The United States remained committed to working with Pakistan to dismantle transnational criminal organisations to protect US citizens from the dangers of narcotrafficking, the statement added.

title: Ella Langley   s    Choosin    Texas    breaks Mariah Carey   s Billboard Hot 100 record
description: The hit has reached its 23rd week at No 1 on the Billboard Hot 100  overtaking Carey   s All I Want for Christmas Is You
content:
The hit has reached its 23rd week at No 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, overtaking Carey’s All I Want for Christmas Is You
Ella Langley has made Billboard history as Choosin’ Texas becomes the longest-running No. 1 song in the history of the Hot 100, surpassing a record previously held by Mariah Carey.
The country star’s hit has reached its 23rd week at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, overtaking Carey’s All I Want for Christmas Is You, which previously held the record with 22 weeks at the top.
Released in October 2025 as the lead single from Langley’s album Dandelion, Choosin’ Texas initially reached No. 1 on the Hot 100 in February 2026. It has remained at the top ever since, turning the track into one of the defining commercial hits of the year.
The song’s record-breaking run follows an earlier milestone in September, when it tied Carey’s 22-week record. Langley has now moved ahead of Carey to claim the all-time record for the most weeks spent at No. 1 on the US singles chart.
Choosin’ Texas has also accumulated significant streaming numbers. According to Luminate data reported by the Associated Press, the track had generated 911 million on-demand streams in the US and 1.26 billion globally by mid-August.
The song was co-written by Langley, Miranda Lambert, Luke Dick and Joybeth Taylor. Its story centres on heartbreak and romantic rejection, with Langley singing from the perspective of someone whose love interest chooses another woman.
The track’s unusual journey began with a story involving Lambert and a kangaroo. Langley previously explained that Lambert told the story during a writers’ retreat, where the incident inspired the group to develop the song around the idea of someone choosing another person.
Beyond its success in the US, Choosin’ Texas has also made an impact in the UK. The song reached No. 1 on the UK Singles Chart in September, making Langley the first country artist in more than two decades to achieve the feat with a solo country single, according to Music Week.
With its 23rd week at the top of the Billboard Hot 100, Langley’s Choosin’ Texas has now surpassed one of Mariah Carey’s most enduring chart achievements and entered the record books as the longest-running No. 1 song in US chart history.

title: Amnesty urges UEFA to suspend Israel  calls Nations League participation    unconscionable
description: Amnesty said Palestinian families face displacement and land loss  while olive trees are uprooted and histories erased
content:
Says Palestinian families face displacement and land loss, while olive trees are uprooted and histories erased
Human rights organisation Amnesty International on Tuesday called on UEFA and FIFA to suspend Israel’s football association, saying its Nations League participation was “unconscionable” because the association supports settlement-based clubs.
“It’s unconscionable that the Israel men’s football team will participate in the UEFA Nations League this autumn despite clear evidence that Israel’s football association continues to support illegal settlements,” Steve Cockburn, Amnesty International’s regional director for Europe, said in a statement.
“UEFA and FIFA should have suspended the Israel Football Association (IFA) over its refusal to exclude clubs based in illegal settlements in the Occupied Palestinian Territories,” Cockburn said.
As the Israel team travels to Europe where they will play against Austria, Ireland and Kosovo between 24 September - 6 October, Palestinian families are being displaced and dispossessed, their land stolen, their olive trees uprooted, and their histories erased by settlers with… pic.twitter.com/0VTr1ol7KL
He said the continued participation of settlement-based clubs in Israeli leagues “violates FIFA statutes and international law”.
He added that UEFA and FIFA funding to the IFA “risks contributing to the sustainability of Israel’s illegal occupation, settlements and violations of international law”.
Israel is set to play in League B's, Group B3, alongside Austria, the Republic of Ireland and Kosovo.
The league phase begins on Thursday, with Austria hosting Israel, according to UEFA.
Read More: Board of Peace reiterates Gaza objectives ahead of UN General Assembly
Israel will also play the Republic of Ireland on Sept 27 and Oct 4, and Kosovo on Oct 1 and Nov 14, before hosting Austria on Nov 17.
Amnesty said opposition to Israel’s participation has grown in Ireland, where football associations, players, activists, trade unions and politicians have called for sanctions, a boycott or suspension.
The Football Association of Ireland has also asked UEFA to consider suspending Israel, according to the rights group.
“Sport should never be used as a public relations spectacle for states committing atrocities,” Cockburn said.
“As the Israel team travels to Europe, Palestinian families are being displaced and dispossessed, their land stolen, their olive trees uprooted and their histories erased by settlers with the support of the Israeli military,” he said.
“The beautiful game should bring people together, not rubber-stamp apartheid,” Cockburn added.
Amnesty said it wrote to FIFA and UEFA in October 2025 to call for the IFA to be suspended unless clubs based in Israeli settlements were excluded from Israeli competitions.
FIFA announced in March 2026 that it would take no action against the IFA over the participation of settlement-based clubs, according to Amnesty.
The Palestinian Football Association subsequently appealed the decision to the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

title: Saoirse Ronan jokes she may have spoken too soon about wanting to play a Bond villain
description: Ronan first expressed interest in playing a Bond villain in 2024  saying she would prefer a female antagonist
content:
Ronan first expressed interest in playing a Bond villain in 2024, saying she would prefer a female antagonist
Saoirse Ronan is joking that she may have spoken too soon about wanting to play a Bond villain, especially now that her husband, Jack Lowden, has been linked to the role of James Bond.
The Lady Bird actress previously made no secret of her interest in joining the 007 franchise as a villain. But when PEOPLE asked her about those comments and reports connecting Lowden to the next Bond role, Ronan admitted she may now be “eating” her words.
“I’ve eaten my words after saying that now,” Ronan said.
Ronan first expressed interest in playing a Bond villain in 2024, saying she would prefer a female antagonist with her own agenda rather than a character whose main purpose was to fall in love with Bond.
She reiterated that ambition in an August 24 interview with Empire, saying she was “dead serious” about wanting to play the bad guy. Ronan also explained that she was particularly interested in portraying a young female villain who could channel “pent-up anger” into something more dramatic.
The timing has since become more complicated because Lowden, 36, is among the actors whose names have been linked to the next James Bond role. Amazon MGM Studios has not announced who will play 007 or the film’s villain.
Denis Villeneuve is set to direct the next Bond film, with Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight writing the screenplay. Other actors reportedly linked to the role include Callum Turner, Jacob Elordi, Tom Holland, Aaron Taylor-Johnson and Harris Dickinson.
Despite the speculation surrounding her husband, Ronan declined to discuss whether Lowden has actually landed the role. She did, however, say she would be enthusiastic about working with him again.
“We met through work and we’ve produced stuff together, and we’re very much a part of one another’s work life as well as personal life,” she told PEOPLE. “So it just feels like when the right thing comes along, it would be the obvious choice for us to do it together.”
The next James Bond film is currently planned for a 2028 theatrical release. Ronan’s latest film, Bad Apples, was released in the U.S. and U.K. on September 18, 2026.

Field Marshal Munir meets French official Nicolas Roche, discusses regional security and bilateral defence cooperation
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir on Tuesday reaffirmed Islamabad’s commitment to strengthening bilateral ties and expanding defence and security cooperation with France during talks with French Secretary General for Defence and National Security Nicolas Roche.
According to a statement issued by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), Roche, accompanied by French Ambassador to Pakistan Jean-Noël Poirier, called on Field Marshal Munir at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi.
“During the meeting, matters of mutual interest, including regional security and bilateral cooperation in defence and security domains, were discussed,” the statement said.

During the interaction, Field Marshal Munir reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening bilateral ties and further enhancing defence and security cooperation.
Roche acknowledged Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and stability and reciprocated France’s interest in expanding cooperation in areas of mutual interest, according to the ISPR.
France’s Secretary General for Defence and National Security Nicolas Roche met Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces, at GHQ in Rawalpindi. Separately, Pakistan and France reiterated their commitment to further strengthening and implementing cooperation under the Pakistan-France Roadmap for Bilateral Cooperation (2023) during the eighth round of the Pakistan-France Joint Security Commission.
According to a statement issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Defence Secretary Lt Gen (retd) Muhammad Ali led the Pakistani delegation at the meeting in Islamabad, while the French delegation was led by Roche.
The commission provided an opportunity for high-level exchanges on matters relating to security and defence cooperation, while also reviewing the status of issues discussed during the seventh round of the Joint Security Commission held in Paris in 2022.

“They reaffirmed their commitment to enhancing cooperation in countering terrorism and addressing related security challenges, including drug trafficking, piracy, and other forms of transnational organised crime,” the statement said.
The Joint Security Commission is an institutionalised mechanism for consultations on security and defence matters, providing a platform for regular exchanges on matters of mutual interest.

Sarah Paulson and Cody Fern reunite for 'Closing Night' after first bonding on 'American Horror Story' season eight
Sarah Paulson and Cody Fern are teaming up for Closing Night , marking their first feature film together after developing a close professional bond while working on American Horror Story .
The actors first met during American Horror Story: Apocalypse , the eighth season of Ryan Murphy’s anthology series. Paulson played Wilhemina Venable, while Fern portrayed the Antichrist, Michael Langdon.
Speaking at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival, Paulson recalled their first scene together and described their early dynamic as “two tigers in a cage.” She said she quickly recognised Fern as an actor who was present, inventive and truthful, making their collaboration particularly exciting.
Paulson said the pair developed what she called an “acting platonic love affair” that eventually led to their work together on Closing Night .
Fern, who is making his feature directorial debut with the film, said he knew after working with Paulson on American Horror Story that he wanted to collaborate with her again. He described directing Paulson as a major privilege and praised her range as an actress.
Closing Night , written by Fern and Devon Bostick, follows a movie star who invites her estranged family to the opening night of her Broadway play. Paulson leads the cast alongside Naomi Watts and Odessa A’zion.
The film had its world premiere at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival.
Paulson and Fern have previously appeared together in multiple seasons of American Horror Story , including Apocalypse and Double Feature . They have also both worked across Ryan Murphy’s American Crime Story franchise.
Paulson said she was moved by the opportunity to star in Fern’s directorial debut, while also feeling pressure to meet the expectations of the filmmaker and the role. Closing Night does not yet have a release date.

Ackles will play Lucas Davenport, a Minneapolis police detective at the centre of the series
Jensen Ackles is set to return to crime television with a leading role in Rules of Prey, a new thriller series that has been greenlit at MGM+.
The Supernatural and The Boys star will play Lucas Davenport, a brilliant and unconventional Minneapolis police detective at the centre of the series. Rules of Prey is based on John Sandford’s long-running Prey crime novel series.
The series will be based on the first novel, Rules of Prey, which follows Davenport as he investigates a string of murders committed by a serial killer known as “Maddog”. The killer follows a personal set of rules, including never knowing his victims, never leaving a motive and never repeating a pattern, turning the investigation into a psychological battle between the two men.
Bruce Terris is attached as showrunner, writer and executive producer. The series is being produced by Amazon MGM Studios alongside Zaftig Films, Howard Braunstein Films and Modern Literary Arts.
The Prey novels have followed Davenport through numerous investigations since Sandford published Rules of Prey in 1989. The television adaptation will bring the character to the screen as Ackles takes on another crime-focused role following his Prime Video series Countdown.
Production is currently taking place in Toronto, with filming scheduled to continue through December 2026.
Ackles is also known for playing Dean Winchester in Supernatural and Soldier Boy in The Boys. He recently appeared in Prime Video’s Countdown, which was cancelled after one season.
Rules of Prey does not yet have a premiere date announced.

description: A two member bench comprising Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram and Justice Muhammad Jawad Zafar hears the appeal
content:
Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram and Justice Muhammad Jawad Zafar hear the appeal
The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Tuesday sought arguments from the prosecution on the admissibility of electronic evidence in the appeal of former Bahauddin Zakariya University (BZU) lecturer Junaid Hafeez, who was sentenced to death in a blasphemy case.
Hafeez was arrested in 2013 after students accused him of uploading blasphemous material on social media and using blasphemous language during lectures.
A two-member bench comprising Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram and Justice Muhammad Jawad Zafar heard the appeal, where Hafeez’s counsel, Asad Jamal, and prosecution lawyer Ghulam Mustafa Chaudhry were present.
The bench particularly sought the prosecution’s position on electronic evidence presented in the case, including a Facebook page allegedly linked to Hafeez.
The court subsequently adjourned the proceedings, initially indicating that the matter would be heard on October 7.
Read : Why is Junaid Hafeez still languishing in jail?
However, following a request from Hafeez’s counsel for additional time to prepare arguments, the judges said the next hearing date would be announced later.
At the outset of the proceedings, the bench noted that formal notices had not previously been issued to the parties after Hafeez’s appeal was transferred from the LHC’s Multan bench to its principal seat.
The appeal was moved to Lahore in December 2021 at the request of Hafeez’s lawyer. During Tuesday’s hearing, the required notices were issued and received in court by both lawyers.
Hafeez, who served as a visiting lecturer in the English literature department at BZU, was arrested on March 13, 2013.
His trial, relating to alleged Facebook uploads, commenced in 2014 and was later shifted to Multan Central Jail in April that year because of security concerns.
On December 21, 2019, a Multan district and sessions court sentenced Hafeez to death on blasphemy charges.

title: Pakistan  seven other Muslim countries demand Israel to fulfil Gaza ceasefire commitments
description: Reject Palestinian displacement and call for full implementation of the Gaza Road Map
content:
Reject Palestinian displacement and call for full implementation of the Gaza Road Map
Pakistan and seven other Muslim countries on Tuesday expressed deep concern over the continued humanitarian suffering in Gaza, calling on Israel to fulfil its outstanding commitments under the first phase of the Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict and stressing the need to preserve the ceasefire and end all violations.
The Gaza peace plan, officially the Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict, is a multilateral agreement between Israel and Hamas that aims to address the ongoing Gaza war.
The foreign ministers of Pakistan, Egypt, Türkiye, Indonesia, Jordan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates met in New York on Sept 21 on the margins of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.
In a joint statement, the ministers called on Israel to “immediately fulfil its outstanding commitments” under the first phase of the plan, including ensuring the “immediate, safe and unhindered delivery” of humanitarian assistance and early recovery supplies and facilitating the rehabilitation of critical infrastructure.
🔊PR No.2️⃣5️⃣2️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Joint Statement by the Foreign Ministers of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Qatar, Saudia Arabia, Turkiye and the United Arab Emirates 🔗⬇️ pic.twitter.com/Zgs4nK7Gvr
They stressed “the imperative of preserving the ceasefire and ending all violations”.
The ministers said the Road Map constituted an “integral part” of the Comprehensive Plan and provided the implementation framework for advancing its second phase.
They said the second phase included “decommissioning alongside full Israeli withdrawal”, the deployment of the International Stabilisation Force (ISF), the assumption by the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG) of its responsibilities throughout the Gaza Strip, and the launch of early recovery and reconstruction across Gaza.
Read More : Pakistan, seven others condemn Israel’s rejection of Gaza roadmap
They called on all parties to fulfil their respective commitments “in good faith and without delay”.
The ministers also reiterated their “categorical rejection” of any measures aimed at the expulsion or forced displacement of the Palestinian people from their homeland or attempts to alter the territorial or demographic character of the Occupied Palestinian Territory.
They deplored what they described as illegal measures aimed at consolidating Israeli control and annexation, including accelerating settlement expansion, land confiscation, demolition of Palestinian homes, settler violence and terrorism, and forced displacement.
The ministers called for the immediate reversal of such measures.
They also expressed “grave concern” over measures undermining the historical and legal status quo of the Muslim and Christian holy sites in Jerusalem.
The ministers welcomed recent measures taken by the United Kingdom, as well as broader national and European efforts, in response to illegal Israeli settlement activity.
Also Read : Pakistan, seven Muslim nations condemn 'inflammatory' Israeli remarks calling to displace Palestinians from Gaza
These included measures to halt trade with illegal Israeli settlements, while the ministers called for further effective measures to end settlement expansion and ensure accountability for settler violence.
They also stressed that “Gaza must remain an integral part of the Palestinian territory” and reaffirmed that implementation of the Comprehensive Plan must contribute to the reunification of the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip.
The ministers said implementation of the plan must also contribute to a “credible and irreversible pathway” towards the exercise of the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination and the realisation of a “sovereign, viable, and independent Palestinian State with East Jerusalem as its capital” through implementation of the two-state solution.
While commending the leadership of US President Donald Trump, they underscored the “indispensable role” of the United States in ensuring implementation of the Comprehensive Plan.
They called for “sustained and active US engagement” to ensure that all parties, including Israel, fulfil their commitments and obligations and to overcome obstacles to implementation of the Road Map.
The ministers stressed that “tangible progress on the ground” would strengthen the credibility of the Board of Peace and the authority of the plan and create “deeply needed momentum”.
They reaffirmed their readiness to continue working collectively with the United States, the Board of Peace, the Palestinian Authority and all relevant parties to advance the full implementation of the Comprehensive Plan and its Road Map.
The ministers said the collective efforts would seek to alleviate the suffering of the Palestinian people, fulfil their right to self-determination and independent statehood, and achieve “just, lasting and comprehensive peace in the region”.

title: UN chief calls for AI curbs and end to wars in his last assembly address
description: Guterres has pushed for global AI governance  the UN formed a 39 member AI advisory body in 2023
content:
Guterres has pushed for global AI governance; the UN formed a 39-member AI advisory body in 2023
United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres used his final address to the General Assembly on Tuesday to urge world leaders to regulate artificial ​intelligence, end wars, focus on climate change and overhaul UN institutions he warned are struggling to confront mounting global challenges.
The former ‌Portuguese prime minister, whose second five-year term ends on December 31, reiterated his calls for global oversight of AI risks, just as the UN's 15-member Security Council prepares to host AI leaders for a briefing on the powerful technology.
Guterres also reflected on the gridlock within the organisation, as nearly 130 world leaders gathered in New York, and Chinese President Xi Jinping and others — ​including leaders from South Africa, India and Germany — skipped the diplomatic meeting.
Delegates responded with sustained applause when Guterres defended a two-state solution for ​Israelis and Palestinians, demanded that "polluters must pay" for climate change and pressed for reforms to international institutions, causes he ⁠has championed throughout his decade leading the United Nations.
The address capped a decade-long tenure in which Guterres sought to position the UN as a mediator in ​conflicts and a forum for governing emerging technologies, even as major powers increasingly bypassed the organization and Washington slashed its funding.
"Those countries leading this technological revolution ​must share information on emerging safety risks, cooperate on testing and evaluation – and work towards common safeguards that protect us all," Guterres told the assembly.
He called on the leaders gathered in New York to "advance the conditions for the responsible pacing of AI and the additional safeguards needed to address risks" and to "work towards a multilateral AI risk management framework, supported ​by credible and independent oversight."
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that Washington had proposed a new AI safety notification mechanism for US President Donald ​Trump and Chinese President Xi to consider at their summit this week. The proposal emerged from talks on establishing a US-China AI dialogue and would cover AI-related incidents with ‌national security ⁠implications.
Guterres has long pushed for global governance of AI. In 2023, the UN created a 39-member advisory body on AI, with members including tech company executives, government officials and academics from countries such as the US, Russia and Japan.
Read More: I nt'l banks warn AI shopping bots raise scam, fraud and data-privacy risks
The Security Council, which is charged with maintaining international peace and security, met for the first time on the risks of artificial intelligence the same year, when China said the technology should not become a "runaway horse" ​and Washington warned against its use ​to censor or repress people.
On the ⁠Middle East, where the conflict has widened as Houthi gains along the Red Sea coast threaten shipping routes and tensions persist in the Strait of Hormuz, Guterres called for "de-escalation and dialogue."
"Together, let's send a clear message from this hall: The ​fighting must stop. Humanitarian aid must flow. And navigational rights and freedoms must be fully restored in accordance with ​international law," Guterres ⁠said.
On the UN system, criticized by Trump and others as bloated and ineffective after Washington withdrew from several UN agencies and slashed funding, Guterres said, "our mechanisms for collective action are under growing strain" and global institutions "continue to reflect the power realities and interests of a largely bygone age."
Guterres used the address to bid farewell to ⁠most of the ​global leaders he has worked with over the last 10 years.
"So, on January 1st, when ​I am no longer Secretary-General, be sure of this. Wherever I will be, whatever I will be doing – I will keep championing the conviction that peace is possible," he said. "I will continue ​to stand up for the values of the United Nations Charter and I will never, ever give up. Thank you."

Row shows how the legacies of nationality, religion and language that shaped Bangladesh are politically potent
Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah died nearly eight decades ago, but his photograph has become the centrepiece of a fresh battle over history at Bangladesh's top university.
The image of Jinnah was shown at a new museum display this month at Dhaka University — only to be torn down, exposing a bitter dispute over how Bangladesh remembers its complicated history.
Abu Tayyab Habildar, the university student who ripped the photograph, called Jinnah a "villain".
The row shows how the legacies of nationality, religion and language that shaped Bangladesh are politically potent — and how the 2024 revolution that toppled Sheikh Hasina has upended old narratives.
Pakistan and Bangladesh were once the western and eastern wings of a single country, created by the violent partition of British-ruled India in 1947.
They were separated by more than 1,500 kilometres of Indian territory.
Bangladesh won independence from Pakistan after the bitter 1971 war.
Hundreds of thousands were killed — Bangladeshi estimates say millions — and many in Dhaka still demand Islamabad apologise for the killings.
Jinnah was not an Islamist, but his campaign for a separate Muslim homeland makes him a potent symbol for Bangladesh's opposition Islamist politicians, who seek to emphasise the country's Muslim identity.
"In Bangladesh, Jinnah was never celebrated," said political analyst Altaf Parvez.
"The ground is fertile for the rise of the Islamists. They need a suitable leader, and that is why there is so much fuss around Jinnah."
The Dhaka University Central Students Union (DUCSU), led by Bangladesh Chhatra Shibir, the student wing of the country's largest Islamist political party, said the photograph was part of a chronological display tracing the university's history.
Read More: Bangladesh sentences to death seven key aides of ousted premier Hasina
DUCSU leader SM Farhad criticised what he called the "mob attack" that ripped the picture down.
This photograph taken on September 17, 2026 shows Dhaka University student Abu Tayyab Habildar, who ripped Jinnah's photograph, speaking during an interview with AFP in Dhaka. — AFP
"You can correct us if we make any mistake, though we haven't made any," he told AFP .
Critics accused the student union of trying to reshape that history by highlighting Jinnah — while diminishing Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, Bangladesh's founding president and independence leader.
"Jinnah is the father of Pakistan," Habildar, the student who ripped the picture down, told AFP .
"But that same Jinnah, when he stood against Bengali and Bangla language, he is a villain."
But Rahman's legacy is also deeply controversial.
His daughter is Sheikh Hasina, whose iron-fisted rule as prime minister ended in a bloody student-led 2024 revolution, and is reviled by those who overthrew her.
Hasina has been sentenced to death in absentia, and the activities of her former ruling Awami League have been banned.
Rahman's former home, later turned into a museum, was torched during the uprising.
Farhad, the DUCSU leader, said the university museum also needed an update.
"They left no stone unturned to establish the narrative of the Awami League ... so we thought we would renovate it," he said.
But student Mahafuzur Rahman, 19, said removing photographs was not the answer.
"I don't think it's good to remove his photo ... He is also part of history."
The space where Jinnah's photograph hung remains empty.

title: Hayden Panettiere cause of death revealed weeks after her passing
description: Hayden Panettiere   s cause of death confirmed as toxic effects of multiple substances  ruled an accident by coroner
content:
Hayden Panettiere’s cause of death confirmed as toxic effects of multiple substances, ruled an accident by coroner
Hayden Panettiere’s official cause of death has been confirmed by the Greenville County Coroner’s Office in South Carolina, more than a month after the actor died at age 36.
According to the coroner’s findings, Panettiere died from the toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, alprazolam, methocarbamol and quetiapine. Her death was ruled an accident.
Fentanyl is a powerful synthetic opioid, while 4-ANPP is a chemical precursor associated with the production of fentanyl. Alprazolam, commonly known by the brand name Xanax, is a benzodiazepine. Methocarbamol is a prescription muscle relaxant, while quetiapine is an antipsychotic medication.
Panettiere died on August 16 after a friend called 911 to report an unresponsive woman. Emergency responders attempted to revive her using advanced cardiac life support, but she was pronounced dead at the scene.
The actor had previously spoken publicly about her struggles with addiction and depression. In an interview with People, she discussed being introduced to medication as a teenager and later struggling with alcohol and opioids.
Panettiere began her career as a child actor, appearing in commercials and television shows before making her film debut with a voice role in A Bug’s Life . She later appeared in Remember the Titans and gained widespread recognition as Claire Bennet on NBC’s Heroes .
She went on to star as Juliette Barnes in ABC’s Nashville and also played Kirby Reed in the Scream franchise, appearing in Scream 4 , Scream and Scream VI .
Her death was initially reported in August, with the official findings now confirming the cause and manner of death.

title: China says opposes  illegal unilateral sanctions  as US pressures Iran with secondary sanctions
description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Iranian commercial airlines worldwide would be halted from Wednesday
content:
Says they lack a basis in international law and are not authorised by the UN Security Council
China on Tuesday said it was against “illegal unilateral sanctions” as Washington moves to impose sweeping secondary sanctions targeting Iran’s commercial aviation network.
“China consistently opposes illegal unilateral sanctions that lack a basis in international law and are not authorised by the UN Security Council,” Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said , responding to the latest US measures against Tehran.
Beijing has repeatedly opposed US sanctions on Iran and what it calls Washington’s “long-arm jurisdiction”.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Monday that operations of Iranian commercial airlines worldwide would effectively be halted beginning on Wednesday under the sanctions campaign.
“On September 23rd, all the Iranian airlines will be shut down around the world,” Bessent told CNBC on Monday.
Read More: US open to meeting Iran at UN, no meeting scheduled yet: Rubio
He warned that foreign airports and companies providing Iranian aircraft with fuel, landing services or ticketing could lose access to the US banking system and dollar clearing.
Bessent said Washington had also discussed enforcement with China, adding that Chinese financial authorities, including People's Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng, were “very engaged in the process”.
He said Washington had identified financial intermediaries helping Tehran evade restrictions and would target them as part of its pressure campaign.
The measures come under Washington's Operation Economic Fury as the Iran war, which began with coordinated US-Israeli strikes in late February, enters its seventh month.

title: Ayesha Omar calls for greater mental health support after Peshawar grave desecration case
description: Actor urges schools  colleges and workplaces to make psychological support more accessible
content:
Actor urges schools, colleges and workplaces to make psychological support more accessible
Actor Ayesha Omar has called for greater access to mental health support in Pakistan following reports of a 19-year-old man being arrested in Peshawar for allegedly exhuming and desecrating the bodies of deceased girls.
In an Instagram Story, Omar shared a report about the disturbing incident and used it to highlight what she described as a wider need to address psychological trauma and emotional wellbeing across society.
“The entire nation of Pakistan needs immediate psychiatric and psychological therapy at varying degrees,” she wrote, adding that she included herself because of “all the PTSD and traumas” she had experienced.
Omar also called for mental health professionals to be made more accessible in educational institutions and workplaces.
“I think it should [be] mandatory in schools and colleges and workplaces. We need experts coming in, instead of financial aid,” she said. “Give us therapy. Not dollars.”
Her comments came after police in Peshawar arrested a 19-year-old Afghan national who was allegedly caught while exhuming the body of a girl from a grave in the Shaikhan area. According to police, the suspect had allegedly dug up several other graves containing the bodies of girls. Authorities said investigations into the case were continuing.
The disturbing reports prompted concern and condemnation on social media, while Omar’s response shifted the conversation towards the psychological impact of violence and trauma and the need for greater access to mental healthcare.
Omar has previously spoken publicly about mental health and emotional wellbeing. She has discussed the importance of acknowledging emotional vulnerability and working on one’s emotional reactions, while also taking part in conversations aimed at increasing awareness around mental health.
The actor has also spoken about her own experiences with stress and trust, saying she had struggled with overthinking and stress and describing healing as an ongoing process.
Her latest remarks have once again brought mental health into the spotlight, particularly the question of whether schools, colleges and workplaces should provide greater access to qualified psychological professionals.

title: Pakistan army kicks off joint military exercises with Russian and Omani forces
description: Pak  Russian and Omani armies to share operational experience  refine counter terrorism drills in two week exercises
content:
Pak, Russian and Omani armies to share operational experience, refine counter-terrorism drills in two-week exercises
The Pakistan Army commenced joint military exercises with Russian and Omani forces at Cherat and the National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC) Pabbi, respectively, the military’s media wing said on Tuesday.
According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the ninth edition of the Pakistan-Russia Joint Exercise Druzhba-IX and the second edition of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Exercise Washaq Al Jabal-II (Mountain Lynx-II) commenced today.
"The two-week exercises bring together contingents from Pakistan Army and their counterparts from the Russian Army and the Royal Army of Oman to share operational experience, refine counter-terrorism drills, procedures and enhance interoperability," the ISPR said.
Read : Pakistan-Russia exercise Druzhba-VII kicks off to boost counter-terrorism expertise
The military's media wing further stated that through joint training and the exchange of best practices, the participating forces would hone their combat skills and tactical expertise while further strengthening bilateral defence cooperation.
Pakistan Army has begun joint military exercises with Russian and Omani forces at Cherat and NCTC Pabbi, respectively, ISPR says. Druzhba IX with Russia and Washaq Al Jabal II with Oman will run for two weeks, focusing on counterterrorism drills, sharing operational experience… pic.twitter.com/sSLqklgZ62
The Pakistan Army routinely conducts joint military exercises with foreign militaries to improve operational readiness and enhance combat capabilities.
On May 7, Pakistan and Sri Lanka concluded a two-week-long joint counter-terrorism exercise at Tarbela, focused on enhancing counter-terrorism skills and strengthening their longstanding military-to-military relations.
"The two-week exercise began on April 27 and concluded today. Combat teams from the Special Services Group (SSG) of the Pakistan Army and the Sri Lankan Special Forces participated in the exercise," ISPR said.
ISPR also said that the exercise aimed to refine the drills, procedures and techniques involved in counter-terrorism operations through joint training, while also reinforcing the historic military-to-military relations between the two friendly countries.
On April 20, Pakistan and Egypt successfully concluded a joint counterterrorism exercise called “Thunder-II”.
According to ISPR, combat teams from the Pakistan Army’s Special Services Group (SSG) and the Egyptian Special Forces participated in the exercise, “demonstrating exceptional professionalism and operational skill throughout”.
Pakistan-Egypt Joint Exercise Thunder-II, focused on counterterrorism operations, was successfully conducted at Cherat @OfficialDGISPR #News #RadioPakistan https://t.co/X2bkieoz92 pic.twitter.com/OJQCW3WWY0
ISPR added that the exercise “served to further strengthen the longstanding and historic military-to-military relations between the two friendly nations”.
In September 2025, "Druzhba-VIII" between the Pakistan and Russian armies was conducted from September 15–27 in the counter-terrorism domain.
"The exercise was aimed at refining the drills, procedures and techniques involved in counterterrorism operations with a focus on drone warfare, fighting in built-up areas and counter-improvised explosive devices," ISPR had said in a statement.

The troops from both countries displayed the highest standards of professional excellence during the exercise, ISPR added.
