title: NCCIA arrests 212 in international fraud probe after raids on 3 illegal Islamabad call centres
description: NCCIA spokesperson says agency has recovered 306 mobile phones  383 computers CPUs  299 monitors and laptops
content:
NCCIA spokesperson says agency has recovered 306 mobile phones, 383 computers/CPUs, 299 monitors and laptops
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Tuesday raided three alleged illegal call centres in sectors E-11 and G-10 in Islamabad during the last 24 hours, taking 212 Pakistani and Chinese men and women into custody in connection with an alleged international online fraud network.
NCCIA is tasked with protecting digital infrastructure, enforcing cyber laws, and promoting cyber awareness and resilience.
An official told APP that the raids were conducted as part of a major operation against illegal call centres involved in different forms of online fraud.
An NCCIA spokesperson said the agency recovered 306 mobile phones, 383 computers/CPUs, 299 monitors and laptops during the operations.
این سی سی آئی اے اسلام آباد کا گزشتہ 24 گھنٹوں میں غیر قانونی کال سینٹرز کے خلاف بڑا کریک ڈاؤن سیکٹر E-11 اور G-10 میں قائم 3 کال سینٹرز پر چھاپے، مجموعی طور پر 212 افراد تحویل میں،ترجمان نیشنل سائبر کرائم انویسٹیگیشن ایجنسی تحویل میں لیے گئے افراد میں چینی اور پاکستانی...
According to the spokesperson, the suspects allegedly used different methods to target people online, including Google-related fraud, loan and dating schemes, fake social media profiles and fraudulent trading offers.
Read : Rs300m call centre extortion case debated in Senate IT committee
The initial investigation also indicated alleged links of the network with India and Brazil, while Chinese nationals were among those taken into custody, the spokesperson said.
مرد و خواتین شامل، ترجمان این سی سی آئی اے کارروائیوں میں 306 موبائل فونز، 383 کمپیوٹرز / سی پی یوز، 299 مانیٹرز اور لیپ ٹاپ برآمد،ترجمان ملزمان گوگل فراڈ اور لو ڈیٹنگ سکیم کے ذریعے بین الاقوامی فراڈ میں ملوث، نیٹ ورک بھارت اور برازیل سے لنکڈ نکلا، مقدمہ درج، تفتیش جاری
In G-10, NCCIA teams raided two alleged illegal call centres, where investigators found that different online schemes were allegedly being used to deceive people. The detained persons also included Pakistani women.
Read More : Foreigners among 65 held in NCCIA raid
Due to the large number of detained suspects, the call centre premises were declared a sub-jail for further legal proceedings.
A case had been registered under relevant sections of law against 212 suspects, including seven Chinese nationals, while further investigation was underway to determine the network’s operations, financial links and the role of each suspect.
On August 14, NCCIA raided an alleged call centre and an illegal digital centre operating in Sparco Plaza in Gulberg Greens, Islamabad and arrested 114 foreign nationals, including 111 Chinese and three Vietnamese, for allegedly gaining financial benefits through online immoral activities.
On December 25, 2025, NCCIA dismantled an organised international online fraud network in an intelligence-based operation, arresting 34 suspects, including 15 foreign nationals and 19 Pakistanis.
Sindh Interior Minister Zia-ul-Hassan Lanjar, accompanied by NCCIA Sindh chief Tariq Nawaz, disclosed the details during a press conference at the Salim Wahidi Auditorium, Clifton License Branch. He said the arrests were made during raids conducted in DHA Phase I and Phase VI.
Also Read : 34 arrested, including 15 foreigners, in Karachi cyber fraud crackdown
The minister said the group was operating fake investment platforms to trap victims. Using automated bots, the suspects created artificial activity in Telegram groups to make the platforms appear legitimate. Victims were shown fake online dashboards that displayed fabricated investment figures and profits, convincing them that their money was growing, whereas the entire system was controlled by the fraudsters.
He further revealed that more than 10,000 foreign SIM cards and six illegal gateway exchange setups were recovered from the suspects. These SIM cards were used to create fake social media and Telegram accounts, receive PIN and OTP verification codes and maintain communication through WhatsApp when required.
According to the investigators, the network’s operations involved managing Telegram groups and social media accounts, persuading victims to invest, collecting money in bank accounts in targeted countries, converting the funds into cryptocurrency and transferring the proceeds to the main beneficiaries across borders.
The minister said the seized material included 37 computers, 40 mobile phones, over 10,000 international SIM cards and six illegal gateway exchange devices. He added that the crackdown was carried out on December 18 during a raid on a fraudulent call centre in Karachi.

title: Noah Kahan appears to tease his  Sunrise on the Reaping  song with new clip
description: Kahan shared a short video featuring a meadow filled with dandelions while haunting  ethereal music plays
content:
Kahan shared a short video featuring a meadow filled with dandelions while haunting, ethereal music plays
Noah Kahan may have just given fans their first glimpse of his long-rumoured song for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.
The singer-songwriter shared a short video on his TikTok account, @thelastofthebugs, featuring a meadow filled with dandelions while haunting, ethereal music plays in the background. Fans quickly began speculating that the clip could be the first snippet of his contribution to the upcoming Hunger Games soundtrack.
The dandelions have added fuel to the theory. The flower is a recurring symbol throughout Suzanne Collins’ Hunger Games series, particularly in relation to Katniss Everdeen and themes of resilience, rebirth and hope.
Kahan has been linked to the Sunrise on the Reaping soundtrack for months, with reports previously suggesting he was in talks to contribute to the film. The musician also appeared to tease the project during the 2026 Emmys earlier this month.
During an interview at the ceremony, Kahan was asked about his interest in creating music for films or soundtracks. He confirmed that he had recently been given an opportunity to do so, but declined to reveal further details.
“We actually just had the opportunity to do so, which I'm really excited about,” Kahan said, adding that he had “something in the works”.
He had already fuelled speculation days earlier by sharing another cryptic video through the same TikTok account, featuring a sunrise and the caption, “the birds sound louder than the bugs tonight”. Fans interpreted the reference to birds as a possible nod to The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, the previous Hunger Games prequel.
Sunrise on the Reaping, based on Collins’ 2025 novel, is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on November 20, 2026. While Kahan has not officially confirmed that he is contributing to the soundtrack, his increasingly frequent hints have led fans to believe an announcement could be approaching.

title: Supreme Court rules dower is a wife s enforceable right  not her  price
description: Court rules if property promised as dower cannot be transferred  the husband must pay the wife its agreed value
content:
Court rules if property promised as dower cannot be transferred, the husband must pay the wife its agreed value
The Supreme Court (SC) on Tuesday ruled that it was "a serious doctrinal error to describe dower as the price of the wife," noting that a wife's right to dower did not lapse merely because property that had been agreed upon was not transferred to her. The SC held that the husband remained liable to pay the agreed value of the property.
"The underlying principle to address such a dispute is that a husband's first duty is to pay dower with grace; a court's first duty is to enforce it without delay, for in the dower lies the dignity of the wife, and in the home lies the strength of the nation," read a detailed judgement by a four-member bench headed by Justice Shahid Waheed.
The bench noted that where property was stipulated as dower but could not be transferred, the husband could not be absolved of his obligation, with the value of the property agreed as dower to be paid to the wife. The court further held that where the value of property was not specified in the Nikahnama, a court could determine its market value on the basis of admissible evidence.
Also Read: SC affirms women’s right to dowry, gifts post-divorce
Pushing back against the notion that dower was "the price of the wife," the SC noted in its judgement "the distinction between marriage and sale." In a contract of sale, it noted, "the principal object is the transfer of ownership of property from one person to another in consideration of price," with rights and obligations "generally exhausted upon completion of the exchange except where the parties agree otherwise."
Marriage, however, achieves no such transfer, the court said. "Neither spouse becomes the property of the other. Neither acquires proprietary rights over the personality of the other; each retains an independent legal identity, independent ownership of property and independent capacity to sue and be sued," it said.
The SC thus observed that marriage was not merely an ordinary civil or commercial contract but constituted a unique legal institution. Neither was dower the price of a wife nor commercial consideration for marriage, but a mandatory, specific and enforceable financial right belonging to the wife, it ruled.
The judgement also examined the legal status and interpretation of the Nikahnama, describing it as the official record of a marriage that comes into existence through offer and acceptance.
The court said the Nikahnama was the primary documentary evidence of the marriage contract, describing it as "a statutory instrument forming an integral part of the legal framework."
At the same time, it added, the Nikahnama was an "authentic record of the marriage contract, preserving the rights and obligations agreed upon by the spouses and serving as the primary documentary evidence for resolving disputes concerning the terms of their marriage."
Read More: LHC says nikahnama alone cannot prove valid marriage in forced marriage disputes
According to the ruling, entries made in the Nikahnama would carry a legal presumption of correctness, although that presumption was not conclusive and could be rebutted through strong evidence. Where entries were ambiguous or contradictory, courts could examine other admissible evidence to determine the parties' actual arrangement.
The court directed that Columns 13 to 16 of the Nikahnama be read together rather than in isolation, with the former recording the amount of dower which may "consist of any lawful object of value."
Column 14, the court said, concerned prompt and deferred dower while Column 15 "records whether any portion of the dower was paid at the time of marriage and, if so, the amount or value thereof." Column 16, the judgement said, recorded whether any property was given in lieu of the whole or any portion of the dower.
Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan agreed with the judgement and authored a separate additional note, writing that dower was "not simply a customary payment or a voluntary gift, rather, it is a recognised obligation arising from the marital relationship and belongs exclusively to the wife."
He added that once dower was due, "the wife alone has the right to receive and deal with it, and neither the husband nor his family can claim ownership over it."
Read More: Child Protection Court stops underage marriage
The justice further noted that the parties' intention should primarily be determined from the Nikahnama and that subsequent oral claims should not be given precedence over its contents.
He observed that the Nikahnama was a mandatory legal form in which every column had a specific purpose, directing Nikah registrars to complete all relevant columns carefully, particularly where property was stipulated as dower, with its complete details and value recorded.
Justice Hassan further said important terms and conditions should be read out to the parties before they signed the Nikahnama and that no column should be left blank without reason.
The SC ruled that Nikah registars should read out or explain the relevant entries of the Nikahnama to both husband and wife before obtaining their signatures "particularly where the Nikahnama contains entries relating to dower, special conditions, delegated right of Talaq [divorce] or any property given as dower." "The object should be to ensure that the document reflects the parties' actual agreement," the judgement read.
The SC also clarified that individual cases would be heard and decided on their own merits by separate benches.

title: King Charles braces as memoir by Diana s brother goes on sale
description: Memoir on Princess Diana reveals explosive claims about her marriage  death  and family tensions
content:
Memoir on Princess Diana reveals explosive claims about her marriage, death, and family tensions
Charles Spencer's book about his late sister, Princess Diana, packed with explosive revelations is published on Tuesday, after searing extracts prompted a rare and sharp rebuttal from King Charles III.
Almost three decades after Diana was killed in a car crash in Paris in 1997, people remain fascinated by her life and tragic death.
"Swan Song: Diana, My Sister", a memoir written by Diana's younger brother, has been published by Penguin and translated into 12 languages.
But extracts serialised in the British tabloid the Daily Mail over the past few days have triggered sensational headlines.
Spencer has said he wrote the book to "speak on Diana's behalf" and correct "untruths that have become accepted over time".
"Diana would be cheering from the rafters at this book, I have no doubt about that," he told the Mail on Sunday at the weekend.
Published excerpts claimed her ex-husband Charles, then Prince of Wales, and now the king, told Spencer in a phone call shortly after Diana's death: "Rest assured, we'll forget her soon enough."
Princess Diana died in a car crash in Paris aged 36. PHOTO: AFP
Her death, aged just 36, sparked an outpouring of grief in Britain for the woman dubbed "the people's princess".
And it triggered accusations that the then monarch, Queen Elizabeth II, failed to respond swiftly with empathy and understanding.
Spencer claimed Charles had "sounded giddily elated, like a lottery winner" at the news of Diana's demise.
And he said Charles "went ballistic" after he insisted Diana would not have wanted her sons, princes William and Harry, then aged 15 and 12, to walk behind her coffin in her funeral procession.
A Buckingham Palace spokesperson issued a rare reaction from the 77-year-old king, saying: "His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgement and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss."
"The king is plainly furious, Buckingham Palace almost never issues any statement like that," BBC journalist Laura Kuenssberg said during a Friday interview.
"Those are exactly the words he said," Spencer assured her, adding: "I don't hear (King Charles) saying he didn't say that."
Charles Spencer's book was serialised in the Daily Mail newspaper. PHOTO: AFP
Spencer criticised the palace's implication that his grief had affected his recollection, telling The Mail on Sunday: "It is not every day you wake up to find you've been gaslit by the king."
He also dubbed it a "rather poor imitation" of the palace's response to Prince Harry and his wife Meghan's claims of royal racism five years ago -- which was that "recollections may vary".
Charles and Diana's tumultuous marriage between 1981 and 1996 was regularly featured in British newspapers.
And Spencer reveals Diana had at times contemplated suicide, driving down to Beachy Head, a notorious clifftop in southern England where people used to deliberately fall to their deaths.
But her love for her sons "stopped her from going further," he writes.
Spencer also recalled Diana told him she and Charles were divorcing because he was "in love with his valet", adding he did not ask why "she would believe such an improbable thing".
Charles later married his long-time mistress, Camilla Parker Bowles, who is now the queen.
But royal experts have questioned some of the book's claims.
Royal biographer Robert Hardman wrote on X that he witnessed Charles, rather than elated, "distraught and in tears" at Diana's funeral.
Andrew Morton, author of the 1992 book "Diana: Her True Story," in a comment in The Times wrote that Spencer's claims about the phone call with Charles were "incendiary and disputed".
While royal commentator Jennie Bond told the BBC the memoir was a "vindictive account".
Spencer, 62, has worked as a US television journalist and calls himself an historian.
He inherited the Spencer family's stately home Althorp, where he and Diana grew up. She is buried on an island in the grounds.
After her death, he accused the media of having "blood on their hands" and in his raw eulogy at Diana's funeral, he vowed to always look out for her two sons.
But he did not mention her beau Dodi Fayed, who was also killed in the Paris crash, even though in the memoir he praised the son of Harrods owner, Mohamed Al-Fayed, for being "kind to Diana".
But in a shocking claim, Spencer wrote Diana had felt "revulsion" for Mohamed Al-Fayed who had squeezed her buttocks and said "in a leery, suggestive tone, 'and in Egypt, father-in-law gets first go'."
Spencer also told the BBC the media's "cancerous influence" on Prince Harry and his wife, Meghan, recalled Diana's hounding by the British press.

title: From smart glasses to AI pins  privacy fears challenge tech s next big bet
description: Meta glasses face privacy lawsuits  venue bans as rivals push camera free designs
content:
Meta glasses face privacy lawsuits, venue bans as rivals push camera-free designs
Companies betting AI devices will usher in a post-smartphone era are fueling privacy fears around the globe that could slow adoption of the emerging technology.
The backlash against devices that can see, hear and respond to the world around them has been strongest against Meta's Ray-Bans, which made smart glasses mainstream by pairing EssilorLuxottica's trendy designs with AI from the social media giant chasing "personal superintelligence."
The glasses have become a lightning rod for growing unease over AI-powered devices, drawing scrutiny from courts weighing privacy lawsuits, users fearing covert recordings and critics warning of a future in which ubiquitous AI eyewear erodes expectations of anonymity and consent. Several United Kingdom venues, including one of the country's biggest pub chains, Wetherspoon, have restricted the use of the frames.
Meta is expected to unveil camera-free smart glasses as early as Wednesday at its Connect conference, according to media reports, highlighting the balancing act facing companies seeking a share of the more than $600 billion smartphone market.
Read: France probes misuse of smart glasses in sexual harassment cases
Device makers are trying out a range of form factors to get past those concerns, from glasses and pins to pendants and voice recorders that clip magnetically to a phone, according to Reuters interviews with nearly a dozen technology executives, analysts and legal experts. Some firms are finding faster traction with businesses than consumers.
The outcome of the privacy debate could shape a market that tech firms see as the next major computing platform. If companies fail to win public trust, the same features that make AI-powered wearables useful — always-on cameras, microphones and environmental awareness — risk becoming the barrier to their adoption.
"The winning form factors will be the ones that make interaction more natural, useful and trusted," said Jay Kim, executive vice president at Samsung's mobile division, in an interview with Reuters in July. As AI takes on more tasks, he said, users will demand systems that remain secure and under their control.
Samsung plans to enter the smart-glasses market later this year through partnerships with Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, but does not view the devices as replacements for smartphones.
For some startups, however, solving the privacy problem may be existential.
Speaking with journalists in December, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman described his vision for an always-on device capable of understanding a user's surroundings while knowing when to help and when to stay silent. He argued that such products would ultimately need to process data locally rather than continuously send information to the cloud.
"You want a device that you can trust ... that can have full context and know when to be helpful, when not to," he said. "If a device is going to be listening to your whole life and watching your whole life, most people will not want that running on a cloud server."
Read More: UK cinemas restricting Meta AI and other smart glasses over piracy concerns
He added that local AI processing "may take a couple of years longer" depending on how quickly OpenAI can scale its processors.
Experts say the central challenge is that AI devices become more useful as they collect more information about their surroundings. That information can include footage of people who never consented to being recorded.
"It's not always obvious to the consumer what it is they're giving up in terms of privacy to enjoy these new, efficient consumer products that make their lives more productive and more frictionless," said Ryan Clarkson, whose firm represents consumers suing Meta and Luxottica of America over allegedly misleading privacy claims involving their smart glasses.
The lawsuit alleges that human annotators viewed and labeled recordings of people changing clothes, using bathrooms and handling financial information after footage captured by the glasses was uploaded to Meta's servers to train its AI systems.
Those recorded often appeared unaware they were being filmed, Clarkson said. "No reasonable consumer who was promised privacy could ever have concluded these devices would intentionally or inadvertently capture them in their most private moments," he told Reuters .
Luxottica and OpenAI did not immediately respond to requests by Reuters for comment.
Meta said a light that cannot be turned off during filming protects the privacy of people around the user, and that the camera is disabled if the light is covered or tampered with.
The company also said it disagrees with the allegations in the lawsuit and will contest them, adding that reviewing user data to improve products was a common practice across the industry and that Meta filters out identifying information.
The privacy backlash has led other companies to consider glasses without cameras.
Even Realities, a Shenzhen-based startup founded by former Apple engineer Will Wang, who worked on the Apple Watch, introduced its camera-free G1 glasses in 2024. Its latest flagship, the G2, launched in November 2025.
Wang told Reuters in July that consumers increasingly associate smart glasses with covert recording and that cameras should wait until companies can put stronger safeguards in place. The company, whose valuation hit $1 billion in July, expects to end the year with a few hundred thousand users. Consumers account for about 90% of its sales, Wang said.
Also Read: Ten days that changed the course of AI
San Francisco-based Pocket is betting that a phone-mounted recorder that requires users to press a button to capture conversations can ease privacy concerns around audio-only devices by making recording as deliberate and visible as using a phone camera. The company said that about 170,000 Pocket devices were in use eight months after launch, including by workers at firms such as DoorDash, Michelin and Santander.
Plaud, which sells card-shaped and wearable AI recorders, has also prioritised privacy with Plaud One, a $249.99 Explorer Edition earbud-and-case system that records only when activated and alerts bystanders through lights or an audio announcement. The company has 2.5 million users and more than $100 million in annual recurring revenue.
Privacy concerns sparked by AI devices are not unprecedented, said Jitesh Ubrani, director at research firm IDC, noting that smartphones faced similar unease when cameras and microphones first became ubiquitous. "As a society, we want to make sure there’s consent and awareness when people are being recorded," Ubrani said. "That’s different from being opposed to recording altogether."

title: Mir Raza case  Commission says Dr Usama targeted Dr Summaiya with smear campaign
description: Family   s counsel questions reports of a proposed    super medical board    after current board completes examination
content:
Commission grills ASP Nida over role despite not being part of probe team
A judicial commission probing the death of Mir Raza Ali on Tuesday said Dr Usama was running a smear campaign against Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya, who told the panel that it had caused her severe mental distress.
At a September 14 hearing, Dr Summaiya told the commission that she had faced threats and a social media smear campaign over her post-mortem findings. She said she had been stalked for two days, while her personal information and details about her family were circulated online, and claimed the campaign had put her “career and job at risk”. She also said she had approached police over security concerns and lodged a complaint with the NCCIA.
During today's hearing, the commission heard further arguments over the medical examination of Raza. Dr Summaiya appeared before the panel and submitted an application concerning what she described as a malicious negative campaign against her.
According to the commission, Dr Summaiya said the campaign was being conducted by Dr Usama and that it had caused her severe mental distress. The panel asked, “Is Dr Usama threatening the police surgeon?” The commission told Dr Summaiya that it would issue orders on her application.
“You are already very brave,” the commission told her, while observing that criticism and allegations were being directed at the panel as well. “Mud will be thrown at you; mud is being thrown at us too,” the commission remarked.
The judicial commission also grilled Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Nida Junaid over her involvement in the case despite not being part of the investigating team, questioning who authorised her role and why she was present at key meetings, dealt with witnesses, and handled material linked to the investigation.
Raza, 25, was allegedly found dead in the bushes near a wedding hall in Gulistan-e-Johar on July 29. The case had initially been surrounded by uncertainty over whether he had been murdered or died by suicide. The court ordered a second post-mortem exam of the victim after the first report failed to determine the circumstances surrounding his death. The findings of the second post-mortem consolidated his family’s longstanding claim that he had been murdered. The police probe is under constant scrutiny by the public because of earlier lapses that were even admitted by the Sindh Police chief.
The commission during today's hearing also questioned Nida over her presence during meetings with the police surgeon, her visits to the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), her involvement in recording the family’s statement and whether she had ever been formally associated with the investigation.
Nida told the commission that the investigation was still under way and that it was not her case when asked whether she believed Raza’s death was a murder or suicide. “You followed the case so closely. Did you consider this case to be murder or suicide?” the commission asked. “We want to know your opinion,” the panel added.
The questioning turned particularly pointed when the commission examined Nida’s handling of an audio message provided by Ali Shaz, which was leaked in the media.
Nida said Shaz had appeared before her voluntarily on August 6 and that she had forwarded his audio message to Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Samiullah Soomro as she considered it potentially relevant evidence.
The commission questioned why Shaz had not instead been sent directly to the investigating officer. “Ferozabad police station is not the White House,” the commission remarked while questioning the decision.
Read: Judicial commission formed to probe Mir Raza Ali’s death
The panel also questioned Nida over how the audio recording subsequently became public and whether she had played a role in facilitating a particular narrative about Raza’s financial affairs.
The commission noted that the audio had contributed to a “loan/debt narrative” and questioned Nida over the manner in which the material had been handled. The panel also asked whether Nida had been shielding Shaz and whether she had been asked to influence the investigation or damage evidence.
Nida said she had acted on the instructions of senior officers.
The commission questioned her about her attendance at a meeting involving Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed on August 5, as well as her visits to the NCCIA. Nida said Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Amir Farooqui had directed her to visit the agency.
She was also questioned about her presence when statements of Raza’s family were being recorded. Nida said she had been instructed to sit in and take notes, while the statement itself was recorded by the investigating officer.
Counsel for the family Jibran Nasir told the commission that the family had objected to Nida’s presence.
The commission asked Nida whether police had ever formally recorded her statement or entered her involvement in the daily diary. She replied that neither had been done.
The questioning came as the commission continued to examine discrepancies between police records and statements attributed to witnesses. In an earlier hearing , Justice Umar Sial observed that several witnesses had disputed statements attributed to them by investigators and directed the registrar not to obtain further documents from police amid concerns that witness statements had been altered.
The commission also recorded the statements of several people who had known or dealt with Raza. Witness Sarim told the commission that he had met Raza in December 2025 and had spent around three to three-and-a-half hours with him. He said he had never invested in Raza’s business.
Sarim said Raza had asked him about cryptocurrency trading and later discussed investing Rs3 million in a cloud kitchen. He went on to say that Raza subsequently sent him a message on July 27 seeking Rs30 million and wrote that his “life depends on this”.
Sarim said he declined the request and that Raza later deleted the message. Around 2am on July 28, he said, Raza’s WhatsApp account was no longer available.
The commission questioned how the deleted message had subsequently reached the media. Sarim said he had received it on his Apple Watch and that its contents had become known to others that night.
The witness told the commission that police contacted him on July 30 or 31 through Station House Officer (SHO) Adeel Afzal. He said his statement relating to his first meeting with police had not been recorded.
Read more: Police surgeon alleges pressure, threats to hide evidence suggesting murder before Mir Raza judicial commission
He told the commission that he had handed over screenshots of the conversation from his Apple Watch to two police teams and provided printouts to the investigating officer, but the material had not been presented before the commission.
Sarim said he believed Raza had been seeking a financial bailout and suggested that his requests may have been connected to loans or cryptocurrency rather than a business investment.
Another witness, Faiz, told the commission that he had known Raza since around 2015-16 through events and had become closer to him after Raza started his business.
Faiz said Raza had borrowed Rs200,000 from him in June 2025 because an online food-delivery payment had been delayed around Eid. He said Raza returned the money on June 30 and later asked for another loan, which Faiz declined.
Faiz said he was contacted by police on August 25 after returning from abroad on August 20. He stated that the police told him that Raza had sought money from Ali Shaz and Aaqib, and that Aaqib had declined a request for Rs1 million.
Also read: Sindh govt again seeks SHC judicial commission to probe Mir Raza murder case
Faiz also told the commission that Raza had asked him for the contact details of Ahsan, the son of a private builder whose wife was a social media influencer. He said Raza later asked his nephew for Rs1 million for 10 to 15 days because of family problems, but his nephew declined.
Faiz disputed portions of the statement attributed to him by police, particularly claims concerning Ali Shaz. He said he had no knowledge of Raza asking Shaz for money and did not know about his cryptocurrency dealings.
Nasir pointed out that police had attributed a statement concerning Aaqib to Faiz, while Ali Shaz had not been made a witness in the interim challan.
Business partner Abid Farooq also appeared before the commission and described his financial dealings with Raza.
Abid said he was involved in investment, cattle farming and mobile-import businesses and had invested Rs7 million on two occasions in Raza’s business without a written agreement, although WhatsApp conversations existed between them.
He said he had also invested Rs5 million in August 2025 and Rs10 million in March 2026 in his father’s business at Raza’s request.
According to Abid, returns on the investment had been satisfactory until April 2026, after which they declined. Raza and another partner, Ahmed, had told him payments would resume.
Read more: Govt denies interference in Mir Raza probe
Abid said he had been on good terms with Raza and that Raza had never told him that he was facing financial or other difficulties.
He said police contacted him around August 16 and recorded his statement. DIG Amir Farooqui questioned him about cryptocurrency, his business partner Ahmed and Mir Raza.
Abid said police had asked about his WhatsApp conversations but had not recorded them.
The commission also questioned why Abid had not gone to Raza’s family after learning about his disappearance despite their financial dealings.
Abid said his statement had been recorded on camera but was not read back to him. The commission noted that references to cryptocurrency and Ahmed appeared during questioning but were not reflected in the statement. Abid said he did not know why.
The commission subsequently called Abid’s second partner, Asif, who said he had a very good relationship with Raza and broadly confirmed his brother Abid’s account.
There were also reports of a proposed “super medical board” being formed after the medical board headed by the police surgeon completed its examination.
Nasir told the commission that the medical board had been constituted on the orders of the court and questioned whether a new board could effectively override those orders. “Can a super medical board supersede the court’s orders?” he asked.
The commission observed that if a new board was constituted, any challenge to it would lie before the Sindh High Court (SHC). Nasir also said the family’s questions regarding the medical examination had still not been answered.
Also read: Home minister apologises to Mir Raza probe commission
The medical controversy stems from discrepancies identified in the first post-mortem examination. The commission previously heard that several important details were absent from the original report, while the police surgeon had pointed to deficiencies including the absence of an X-ray and scientific examination of the bullet wounds.
The commission also observed that Dr Usama’s further statement appeared to contain allegations against Dr Summaiya and the Sindh chief minister, saying the proceedings should not become a forum for allegations.
Commission seeks more records, witnesses and time
The panel continued to seek information from senior health and police officials, issuing notices to Health Secretary Tahir Sangi, current Director General Health Shehryar Memon and SSP Samiullah Soomro.
The commission also questioned the timing of the change in the DG Health position while proceedings concerning the medical board were under way. “You changed the DG Health while the statement was being recorded,” the commission observed.
“It may be that you have no ill intentions, but the public is watching everything. People are not fools,” the commission remarked. The panel also said people might remain silent because of circumstances and warned against assuming that they did not understand what was happening.
The commission also sought an extension of its term from the SHC chief justice until October 15, citing the emergence of additional witnesses and delays caused by some witnesses being abroad.
It also directed that DSP Siraj Lashari, the investigating officer, and Citizens-Police Liaison Committee (CPLC) representative Kashif appear before it. Questionnaires were to be sent to AIG Azad Khan, DIG Amir Farooqui and DIG Farrukh Lanjhar.
The commission adjourned the proceedings until Thursday.

title: Netflix   s  Best of the Best  faces backlash over Kabul evacuation joke
description: The show  directed by Lena Khan and written by Hasan Minhaj has come under fire for the  last plane out of Kabul  joke
content:
The show, directed by Lena Khan and written by Hasan Minhaj has come under fire for the 'last plane out of Kabul' joke
Netflix’s Best of the Best has sparked online criticism over a joke referencing the 2021 Kabul evacuation during the Taliban’s return to power in Afghanistan.
The comedy, directed by Lena Khan and co-written by Hasan Minhaj and Prashanth Venkataramanujam, features a line delivered during a conversation involving Maitreyi Ramakrishnan’s character, Maya.
She tells a friend, “Guys throw themselves at you like you're the last plane out of Kabul.”
A film directed by Hasan Minhaj and Lena Khan to “celebrates south asian culture” is monetising the suffering of Afghans on @netflix . One must be truly sick to the core to find amusement in someone’s tragedy. You find the "last flight from Kabul" funny? a tragedy that affected… pic.twitter.com/qTzeDe7LOC
The dialogue has prompted objections from viewers who say it makes light of a traumatic episode in Afghanistan’s recent history.
Thousands of Afghans attempted to flee the country in August 2021, with chaotic scenes at Kabul airport drawing global attention.
One critic addressed Minhaj on X, writing, "You should be embarrassed, Hasan Minhaj. Explain the joke. Is the funny part the Afghans falling from planes? The terrified families at the airport? The people desperately trying to escape the Taliban? Because “the last flight out of Kabul” actually happened to real human beings. Our trauma isn’t your cheap punchline."
Other social media users have called on Netflix and the filmmakers to acknowledge the backlash and apologise, arguing that the reference trivialises the suffering experienced by Afghans.
The evacuation saw crowds gather at Hamid Karzai International Airport as people sought to leave Afghanistan.
Images of people clinging to departing aircraft, alongside a deadly ISIS-K suicide bombing outside the airport, became defining moments of the crisis.
Best of the Best began streaming on Netflix on September 18.
The film follows childhood friends Maya and Anjali as they join UCLA’s competitive Bollywood-fusion dance team.
Netflix, Khan and Minhaj had not publicly addressed the criticism at the time of publication.

title: London Fashion Week 2026  Five trends set to define spring 2027
description: From  messy girl  styling to  gardencore   flowing silhouettes  London   s runways embraced a more playful mood
content:
From 'messy girl' styling to 'gardencore', flowing silhouettes, London’s runways embraced a more playful mood
London Fashion Week 2026 ended on a high note as Burberry brought the British capital’s fashion calendar to a star-studded close. But the biggest takeaway from the week may have been what it revealed about the season ahead.
According to the BBC , designers moved away from the polished minimalism and “quiet luxury” that have dominated recent seasons, instead embracing more expressive, playful and deliberately imperfect looks.
From intentionally chaotic styling and gardening-inspired clothing to flowing silhouettes and bold colour, here are five trends expected to define spring 2027.
Rejecting "quiet luxury" uniforms, Chopova Lowena, Sinead Gorey, and Conner Ives led London Fashion Week's embrace of the "messy girl". PHOTO: BBC
Forget perfectly coordinated outfits. London Fashion Week embraced a more carefree approach to dressing, with designers experimenting with unexpected combinations of colours, textures and silhouettes.
The “messy girl” aesthetic emerged as one of the strongest trends of the season, with labels including Chopova Lowena, Sinead Gorey and Conner Ives incorporating deliberately untidy styling and combining pastel shades, florals and contrasting textures.
The look represents a departure from the carefully curated “clean girl” and quiet-luxury styles that have dominated social media and fashion in recent years.
The result is fashion that feels less polished and more spontaneous, with clashing pieces becoming part of the appeal.
Erdem, Yuhan Wang, and Bora Aksu channelled a "gardencore" vibe, trading quiet luxury. PHOTO: BBC
The garden may be an unexpected source of inspiration for your spring wardrobe.
Designers including Erdem, Yuhan Wang and Bora Aksu brought elements of gardening and outdoor work to the runway, incorporating practical silhouettes and materials into their collections.
The trend moves beyond the traditional cottage-core aesthetic. Instead of gingham dresses and woven accessories, the new interpretation features aprons, waterproof fabrics, structured outerwear and trench coats.
The influence also follows the growing appearance of garden-inspired accessories in fashion. The BBC noted that Loewe had previously introduced a watering-can-shaped handbag, helping turn an everyday gardening object into a luxury fashion statement.
For spring 2027, the look suggests that practicality and fashion can comfortably share the same wardrobe.
Dujancourt channeled a free-spirited aesthetic with organic draping, trailing ribbons, and delicately hitched slip skirts. PHOTO: BBC
Another major direction emerging from London Fashion Week was a return to flowing, romantic dressing.
Designers looked towards classical Greek-inspired silhouettes, with draped fabrics, loose shapes, trailing details and breezy materials creating what the BBC described as a "modern goddess" aesthetic.
Pauline Dujancourt’s collection captured the trend particularly well, using billowing fabrics and generous volumes to create an ethereal effect.
The trend also arrives as ancient Greek imagery receives renewed attention through Christopher Nolan’s film The Odyssey . Fashion, once again, appears to be borrowing inspiration from the wider cultural landscape.
After seasons dominated by restrained tailoring and minimalist luxury, the softer and more dramatic silhouettes offer a noticeably different direction.
Mulberry, Justin Cassin, Enny Atelier and Vin, Omi showcased 'orange'. PHOTO: BBC
If there is one colour to watch for spring 2027, orange could be it.
From bright tangerine and vivid melon to softer coral and deeper ginger shades, designers across London incorporated the colour into their collections.
Mulberry, Justin Cassin, Enny Atelier and Vin + Omi were among the names showcasing orange during London Fashion Week.
The colour has also been appearing in celebrity fashion, further pushing it into the spotlight.
Whether designers opt for an eye-catching head-to-toe orange look or use the shade as an accent, the colour is set to bring plenty of energy to spring wardrobes.
A school sports hall is transformed into a ballet stage for Edeline Lee's latest collection. PHOTO: BBC
Ballet continues to influence fashion, and its presence was particularly visible at London Fashion Week.
Designer Edeline Lee drew directly on the discipline and physical demands of classical dance for her latest collection. The presentation even transformed a school sports hall into a stage, with models appearing en pointe.
The influence extends beyond clothing. Ballet flats remain an important part of the trend, while smaller, delicate shoe silhouettes are expected to continue appearing next season.
The renewed interest also reflects ballet’s wider presence in fashion, with dancers appearing in major fashion publications and working with leading luxury brands.
For those wanting to experiment with the look, vintage and charity shops could offer an accessible way to incorporate ballet-inspired pieces without committing to a complete wardrobe overhaul.
The trends emerged against a backdrop of major moments for British fashion.
Burberry closed London Fashion Week with a collection from creative director Daniel Lee that combined the brand’s recognisable check with contrasting florals and soft leather.
The collection was developed with textile designer Celia Birtwell, who contributed hand-painted designs to pieces including check trenches and playful knitwear.
The show also attracted a major celebrity audience, with Romeo Beckham, Skepta, Jonathan Bailey and Rosie Huntington-Whiteley among those attending. Central Cee also made a surprise appearance on the catwalk.
Elsewhere, Alexander McQueen marked a significant return to London after 25 years of presenting its shows in Paris. Designer Seán McGirr revisited elements of the house’s darker aesthetic through lace corsets, chainmail-inspired designs and dramatic styling.
Mulberry also returned to the spotlight after a nine-year absence, with Christopher Kane presenting a collection built around the brand’s Baywater bag and extensive use of leather.
Taken together, the collections suggested that London designers were moving towards fashion that was more expressive, tactile and willing to embrace contradiction.

title: Infantino proposes consulting federations to reform FIFA
description: He asks for the initial proposals to be considered at the council meeting
content:
He asks for the initial proposals to be considered at the council meeting
FIFA president Gianni Infantino on Monday suggested a "consultation" with the member federations to reform the world football governing body's decision-making processes, in a letter addressed to the 211 member associations, and seen by AFP.
"I will propose that the Council establish a direct, structured and time-limited consultation with confederations, Member Associations and relevant stakeholders on how FIFA's decision-making can be further strengthened," Infantino wrote.
The 56-year-old Swiss has come under fire since his now-abandoned plan to bring private investment into the men's and women's World Cups.
"The consultation would invite specific proposals on earlier institutional involvement, the respective roles of the President, the Bureau, the Council and the Congress, and practical ways to strengthen transparency, participation and accountability in major strategic initiatives," the letter continued.
Infantino asked for the initial proposals to be considered at the council meeting scheduled for October 15.
Infantino replaced Sepp Blatter as president of FIFA in 2016. He has come under severe pressure since the announcement in late July of proposals to create a commercial subsidiary to run its biggest events, such as the World Cup and Club World Cup.
The plan would have allowed private investors to acquire stakes in a company created under the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) initiative. The backlash that followed led to the proposals being quickly shelved.
European football's governing body UEFA threatened to boycott FIFA competitions. It later suspended that threat, but has urged Infantino to resign and has been preparing possible legal action against him for alleged "criminal mismanagement".
Infantino addressed FFE in his letter on Monday and wrote that "FIFA's democratic processes, independence and sporting authority were never for sale".
The plan also "did not involve relinquishing FIFA's control or authority over sporting decisions", he insisted.
He further lamented the fact that the scheme "entered the public domain before FIFA's planned institutional process had been completed and before it could be presented in full to the Council and the Member Associations".
"I recognise that, without the full context, this caused concern and created the impression that decisions had already been taken. They had not," Infantino added.
"Major ideas must be developed, tested and communicated through clear and trusted institutions. That is a responsibility I take seriously."
UEFA, alongside North American body CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), issued a no-holds-barred joint letter against Infantino in August.
"Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding -- or demanding -- power to be held," they wrote.
However, Infantino is not without friends -- 2034 World Cup hosts Saudi Arabia came out in support last month, with African football's governing body CAF and South America's CONMEBOL also supportive.
FIFA confirmed earlier in September that Infantino will stand for re-election as president next March.
At this stage, he is the only candidate. However, CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is widely seen as a likely challenger.
Candidate nominations for next year's election must be submitted by November 18.

title: Piers Morgan threatens legal action over Charles Spencer   s Diana memoir claims
description: The dispute centres on Spencer   s allegation that Morgan published  intrusive  photographs of Diana at a gym
content:
The dispute centres on Spencer’s allegation that Morgan published 'intrusive' photographs of Diana at a gym
Piers Morgan has threatened legal action against Charles Spencer, Princess Diana’s brother, over claims made about him in Spencer’s memoir, Swan Song.
The dispute centres on Spencer’s allegation that Morgan published “intrusive” photographs of Diana at a gym while editing the Daily Mirror.
Morgan rejected the claim on his YouTube show, Piers Morgan Uncensored , calling it “all bulls***” and insisting it was easy to disprove.
'It's all bullsh*t... you'll be hearing from my lawyers.' BREAKING: Piers Morgan plans to take legal action against Earl Spencer over “fabricated inaccuracies” made about him in his bombshell book on Diana. Watch more 👇 📺 https://t.co/ZWOoVI5C3O @piersmorgan pic.twitter.com/3w66CTrwZc
Morgan said the photographs appeared in the Sunday Mirror on November 7, 1993, before he joined the Daily Mirror in October 1995. He added that he was working for The Sun at the time.
Questioning Spencer’s credibility, Morgan said, “If Earl Spencer can be so incredibly defamatorily wrong about such basic facts involving me, well why should we believe anything else that he puts in this book?”
He also warned Spencer and the book’s publisher, Penguin Michael Joseph, that his lawyers would be in contact.
Morgan said he wanted the allegation removed from the memoir and requested a donation to the King’s Trust over the damage he claims the statement caused.
Spencer’s memoir has also attracted attention for his account of a 1997 conversation with King Charles about Princes William and Harry walking behind Diana’s coffin. Spencer alleges Charles said, “Rest assured, we’ll forget her soon enough.”
Buckingham Palace responded that grief can affect memory and judgement, while declining to comment on books as a matter of principle.

title: Int l banks warn AI shopping bots raise scam  fraud and data privacy risks
description: Google  Meta envision future in which shoppers can ask AI agents to select products  make purchases
content:
Google, Meta envision future in which shoppers can ask AI agents to select products, make purchases
Using AI agents for online shopping could increase the risk of scams, fraud and data-privacy breaches , banks including NatWest and Bank of America said on Tuesday, as they set out principles for developing the technology.
Technology companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta are increasingly promoting AI chatbots as shopping tools, envisioning a future in which shoppers use AI agents to select products and make purchases on their behalf. Retailers, meanwhile, are racing to influence chatbots' recommendations.
British retailer John Lewis said in September that searches ​originating from AI agents had risen to 2.5% from 0.3% a year ​earlier, with the trend accelerating.
The group of banks, which also includes ING, New Zealand's ASB Bank, US lender Capital One and Commonwealth Bank of Australia, said in a report that customers were enthusiastic about the potential of agentic commerce and keen to enable it.
However, they warned that the technology was advancing faster than industry standards and consumer protections. "Consumers are unclear if AI will act in their interests," the report said.
Read: Anthropic faces scrutiny over AI rules, data practices
"They are concerned that AI agents may buy the wrong thing or spend too much – or even worse, lose their money to scams and fraud. They are not sure whether they will be protected or who they will need to go to if things go wrong."
The report highlighted risks including AI agents requesting customers' card details and entering them directly into websites, or steering users towards payment methods that offer weaker protections.
The banks plan to discuss a series of proposals with policymakers, including requiring disclosure when an AI agent is involved in a transaction, greater transparency over how AI agents make decisions, and safeguards to protect customer data.
Consumers and merchants should also be free to choose which AI-powered e-commerce services they use, while different systems should be interoperable, the report said.

title: Pietersen teaching England how to face spin  says Brook
description: He is appointed as a specialist mentor to the white ball teams
content:
He is appointed as a specialist mentor to the white-ball teams
England's players have been learning how to play spin from Kevin Pietersen, captain Harry Brook said, as he hailed the former Ashes and Twenty20 World Cup-winning ​batter's impact on the side.
Pietersen, England's third-highest run scorer across all formats, ‌was appointed as a specialist mentor to the white-ball teams this month, in the lead-up to next year's World Cup.
In the 46-year-old's first series as part of the set-up, England completed a 3-0 whitewash ​of a spin-heavy Sri Lanka side to replace India at the top ​of the Twenty20 world rankings.
"KP has been very good," Brook told ⁠reporters on Monday. "He's enjoying the role, he's enjoying himself ... He was a hero to ​many of us growing up, so it's good to have a man of his ​calibre in our side."
The 27-year-old said Pietersen had held a masterclass for the squad on playing spin, adding: "A lot of it was about picking the length of spin. That is key to facing ​spin and being able to rotate strike as well as possible.
"In ODI cricket ​that's an area we probably need to improve as a side. It can make a massive difference ‌to ⁠winning games of cricket.
"He (Pietersen) was a hell of a player against spin, alongside (Joe) Root and (Marcus) Trescothick. They were very good players at playing spin, so it's about picking their brains and asking them what worked for them and putting that into your ​game."
England next host Sri ​Lanka in a ⁠three-match one-day international series, beginning later on Tuesday.
"We can take a hell of a lot of confidence from being unbeaten in ​the T20s," Brook said.
"Going into this ODI series we want more ​of the ⁠same. We're trying to play a higher-octane style of cricket and put them under pressure with bat and ball.
"We want to be one of the fittest sides in the ⁠world. ​To do that, we've got to work hard on ​and off the field. We are trending in the right direction. There are a few touches here ​and there which we can improve."

title: Wood retires from international cricket
description: England quick brings curtain down on an 11 year career
content:
England quick brings curtain down on an 11-year career
England fast bowler Mark Wood announced his retirement from international cricket on Tuesday, saying he had "lost the battle" after a career repeatedly disrupted by injuries.
The 36-year-old, one of the quickest bowlers to play for England, took 253 wickets in 146 international matches across all formats, including 119 wickets at 30.79 in his 38 Tests.
Wood, who made his England debut in 2015, played a key role in the team's 50-over World Cup triumph in 2019.
He was also in the England squad that won the T20 World Cup in 2022, although injury ruled him out of the semi-final and the final.
Wood last played for England in an eight-wicket defeat by Australia in the first Test of the 2025/26 Ashes series -- his first Test for 15 months -- but his comeback lasted just 11 overs.
Swelling in his knee forced him out of the second Test, and he was subsequently ruled out of the rest of the series.
"Although this may not come as a surprise given the past year, it just feels like a natural time at the end of my contract," Wood said in a statement on social media.
"I've always tried to be resilient and come back from injury to prove people wrong and show everyone what I can do. Unfortunately, this time I lost the battle.
"On medical advice, Test cricket and 50-over cricket are not possible, so the England dream has slowly been ground out of me over the last year.
"Playing for England has been the greatest honour I could have ever wished for and a dream come true."
England managing director Rob Key said: "It's been a privilege to watch the latter part of a great career.
"To have been a point of difference in Ashes series wins, a World Cup, and to have thrilled crowds every time he got the ball in his hand is something very few players achieve."

title: New Witcher book in development from author Andrzej Sapkowski
description: Andrzej Sapkowski confirms he is working on new Witcher book  with Geralt expected to return
content:
Andrzej Sapkowski confirms he is working on new Witcher book, with Geralt expected to return
A new Witcher book is in development, with author Andrzej Sapkowski confirming that he is working on the next instalment in the fantasy series.
Sapkowski confirmed at a recent convention appearance in Poland that he is writing another Witcher book and expects to finish it by the end of 2027.
The book is expected to feature Geralt of Rivia again, with Sapkowski saying he does not intend to write Witcher books centred on other characters such as Yennefer.
The next book will follow 2025’s The Witcher: Crossroads of Ravens, a prequel focusing on a young Geralt and his first major adventure as a Witcher.
The Witcher series has previously explored different periods of Geralt’s life, leaving years of his history open for further stories. Sapkowski has also previously discussed the possibility of returning to Geralt’s earlier years.
In an interview with IGN , Sapkowski said, “Sky is the limit,” when asked whether there was room for additional Geralt prequels. He also said, “I am considering writing more short stories.”
Sapkowski began The Witcher series with short stories before publishing two collections ahead of the first novel, Blood of Elves. However, he has described writing short fiction as particularly demanding.
“It is not an easy thing to create a good short story. This is much more difficult than writing a novel,” Sapkowski said.
If Sapkowski completes the new book by the end of 2027, Polish readers could potentially receive it in late 2027 or early 2028. International readers could receive the book later, based on the release schedule for Crossroads of Ravens.
The Witcher franchise has also expanded into video games and television, with The Witcher 4 currently expected in 2028 and Netflix continuing its adaptation of the books.

title: Bab al Mandeb tensions test Egypt   s Suez Canal
description: Growing pressure on Bab el Mandeb threatens global supply chains   logistics expert tells Anadolu
content:
'Growing pressure on Bab el-Mandeb threatens global supply chains,' logistics expert tells Anadolu
Nearly three years after tensions in Bab el-Mandeb disrupted shipping through the Red Sea and inflicted billions of dollars in losses on Egypt's Suez Canal, renewed regional tensions are once again putting the strategic waterway to the test.
Yemen's Houthi group threatened navigation through Bab el-Mandeb, the gateway from the Red Sea to Egypt's Suez Canal and onward to the Mediterranean, nearly three years ago. At the time, Houthi attacks on ships in the Red Sea caused losses of around $11 billion to the canal, one of Egypt's main sources of foreign currency, according to Egyptian officials.
The Houthis resumed targeting shipping in the Red Sea about two months ago, prompting Egyptian warnings over the repercussions of any disruption to international maritime routes, including the canal linking Asia and Europe.
Territorial control in Yemen has also shifted recently, with the Houthis advancing along the western coast and taking control of strategic areas, including Red Sea islands such as Mayyun Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Read: Iran offers to reopen Hormuz within 7 days if US takes initial steps to ease military pressure: report
Tensions in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden have escalated since July 20, when the Houthis announced a "maritime blockade" on vessels linked to Saudi Arabia in response to what they claim is a Saudi blockade on areas under their control in Yemen.
The Houthis have targeted oil tankers and Saudi vessels along regional shipping routes and attacked sites inside the kingdom, including civilian airports and energy production facilities, causing civilian casualties and material damage.
Saudi Arabia has led a coalition supporting Yemen's internationally recognised government since 2015, while Iran is accused of backing the Houthis, who have controlled provinces and cities, including the capital Sanaa, since 2014.
Last week, Egypt and Saudi Arabia stressed the importance of ensuring freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb and the Red Sea following talks between Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Cairo.
Days earlier, Sisi called during a BRICS summit in India for safeguarding freedom of navigation through international waterways amid current developments, particularly as a significant share of global trade passes through the Red Sea and Suez Canal.
The Red Sea tension comes amid regional escalation following US and Israeli attacks on Iran in February, which responded with missile and drone strikes across the region. Tehran also effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic route for energy supplies.
Egypt's calls for calm and stability in Bab el-Mandeb stem from the passage’s position as a "strategic chokepoint" and from economic and strategic considerations directly affecting the country's national security, logistics expert Nasreddine Bougashish told Anadolu .
"Any disruption in Bab el-Mandeb will immediately and automatically affect the Suez Canal, Egypt's vital artery, as ships would divert away from the canal," Bougashish said.
"This would mean a direct blow to canal revenues, which constitute a fundamental source of the country's foreign currency," he added.
"The situation in Bab el-Mandeb remains open to difficult scenarios, and growing pressure on the passage now threatens the efficiency of global supply chains and weighs directly on the economic resources of countries in the region, including Egypt," Bougashish warned.
Cairo moved to reassure the public about the Suez Canal amid growing global concern over the escalating tensions in Bab el-Mandeb.
Read more: G7 leaders condemn Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia
"The canal is safe, navigation is regular, its services are operating efficiently, and its pilots are at the highest levels of performance and readiness," Suez Canal Authority Chairman Osama Rabie said during a World Maritime Day 2026 event, as cited in an authority statement on Sept. 20.
He said navigation through the canal saw 1,358 vessels transit in August, with a total net tonnage of 68.3 million tons and revenues of $567.1 million.
“Previous challenges directly affected global supply chains, with their repercussions extending to navigation through the Suez Canal,” Rabie said. “But these challenges demonstrated the canal's importance in securing global supply chains, reinforced its leading global position and proved that there is no sustainable alternative route to the canal,” he added.
Rabie was referring to Houthi attacks on commercial vessels linked to Israel in the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb following the Gaza war in October 2023. The attacks prompted major shipping companies to reroute vessels around the Cape of Good Hope, causing around $11 billion in losses to the Suez Canal.
“The canal diversified its sources of income during the crisis by localising the production of marine vessels, establishing partnerships with the private sector and introducing new maritime services,” Rabie said.
The assurances came as Danish shipping company Maersk and Germany's Hapag-Lloyd announced in separate statements on Sept. 14 that four joint container services would resume passage through the Suez Canal instead of using the Cape of Good Hope route around South Africa.
The security tensions around Bab el-Mandeb in 2023 placed financial pressure on the Suez Canal but did not undermine its operational structure, Khaled al-Shafei, head of the Capital Centre for Economic Studies, told Anadolu .
"The canal withstood the crisis because it has the geographic and economic flexibility that ensures its continuity, limiting the losses to temporary financial impacts until security conditions stabilised," al-Shafei said.
“The canal also offered incentives and discounts on transit fees and diversified maritime services as part of its efforts to address the crisis at the time,” he added.
“The decision by Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd to return to the Suez Canal reflected the importance of relying on the waterway,” al-Shafei said.
He expects the canal to “withstand again” because of its geographic and economic advantages, particularly as it normally handles around 12% of global trade and about 30% of global container traffic.
Al-Shafei did not rule out Egyptian mediation to end the maritime tensions, describing it as a possible option to prevent economic repercussions affecting Egypt, Saudi Arabia and other Red Sea countries.
Maritime transport and logistics economist Ahmed al-Shami said risks continue to threaten Bab el-Mandeb.
“Their direct impact on the Suez Canal, however, remains limited so far as navigation through the canal continues to grow,” he told Anadolu .
“The current threats differ from previous tensions, particularly because the Houthis have identified Saudi vessels as their targets this time,” al-Shami said.
“However, the threat remains, and future developments will determine the extent of the impact on shipping,” he added.
Also read: UN Security Council condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
“Continued attacks on vessels would force shipping companies to adjust their routes,” al-Shami warned.
“Maersk's return to the Suez Canal reflects an economic assessment that passage through the waterway is more viable than sailing around the Cape of Good Hope,” he said.
“An expansion of Houthi attacks on vessels could lead to a full-scale military escalation affecting global trade, not just the Suez Canal, by as much as 25%-30%,” al-Shami warned.
“The Suez Canal is currently recording gradual growth in maritime traffic compared with the previous two years,” he added.
Al-Shami expects canal revenues to rise above $7.5 billion by the middle of next year, compared with less than $4 billion in 2024, while also not ruling out Egyptian mediation to contain the current crisis.

title: Typhoon Dujuan leaves four dead in Japan  45 000 houses without power
description: Search continues for six missing as torrential rain triggers landslides  floods areas near Tokyo
content:
Search continues for six missing as torrential rain triggers landslides, floods areas near Tokyo
Typhoon Dujuan left at least four people dead and 22 injured in Japan, while thousands of houses near Tokyo were without power after the storm swept through the region, authorities said Tuesday.
The typhoon moved away from Japan's coast and out into the Pacific by morning, allowing authorities to lift or downgrade most heavy rain and landslide warnings.
Dujuan had already led to the early closure in the capital of the one of the world's biggest video game trade fairs.
Japan often sees strong typhoons in the late summer and early autumn, with other storms this season disrupting some events at the Asian Games being held in the country.
The Fire and Disaster Management Agency said three people died in Chiba prefecture and one in Kanagawa region, both near Tokyo. Search operations were continuing for six people missing after landslides triggered by torrential rain, the agency said.
Read: 1 dead, 11 missing after mudslide in eastern China
More than 45,000 households in Chiba near Tokyo were still without electricity on Tuesday afternoon, while over 460 houses were damaged.
Although Dujuan weakened as it moved northeast, it dumped record rainfall in parts of the Tokyo area.
Oshima, an island about 120 kilometres (75 miles) south of central Tokyo, recorded 832 millimetres of rain over 48 hours, more than double its average rainfall for the whole of September, public broadcaster NHK reported. Rainfall in Tokyo's Edogawa Ward reached a record 282.5 millimetres over 24 hours.
Scientists say human-driven climate change is intensifying the risk posed by heavy rains because a warmer atmosphere holds more water.

title: Hina Parvez Butt speaks out against AI misuse after Jannat Mirza video
description: Punjab MPA urges women targeted by fabricated content to preserve evidence and report cases to cybercrime authorities
content:
Punjab MPA urges women targeted by fabricated content to preserve evidence and report cases to cybercrime authorities
Punjab Assembly member Hina Parvez Butt has raised concerns over the growing misuse of artificial intelligence to violate women’s privacy and dignity, shortly after content creator Jannat Mirza spoke out after becoming a victim of fabricated AI-generated content.
Butt took to X to address the issue, describing the fake video involving Mirza as a serious warning about the misuse of technology.
“The fake video generated by AI of Jannat Mirza has highlighted an extremely serious issue. Technology is for progress and convenience, not for violating anyone's honour, dignity, and privacy. Using women's images or faces without permission is unacceptable.”
She added, “No compromise on the honour and protection of women!”
جنت مرزا کی AI سے تیار کردہ جعلی ویڈیو نے ایک انتہائی سنگین مسئلے کی طرف توجہ دلائی ہے۔ ٹیکنالوجی ترقی اور سہولت کے لیے ہے، کسی کی عزت، وقار اور پرائیویسی پامال کرنے کے لیے نہیں۔خواتین کی تصاویر یا چہروں کا بغیر اجازت استعمال ناقابلِ قبول ہے۔ ایسے عناصر کے خلاف مؤثر اور فوری… pic.twitter.com/rfzDIbkn5H
Butt’s remarks came a day after Mirza shared an AI-generated video depicting her alongside a male figure, drawing attention to the increasing circulation of fabricated content online.
Mirza noted that, as a social media personality, she was able to publicly clarify whether content involving her was genuine or fabricated. For women who do not use social media, however, the situation could be considerably more difficult, she stressed, as they may not even know that their images or faces are being misused.
She also highlighted the serious consequences such fabricated videos can have for a woman’s reputation, dignity and sense of privacy, pointing to the broader risks posed by the misuse of AI-generated content.
Butt echoed those concerns in a video clip shared alongside her post. “Today, AI has become an important part of life, but its misuse without anyone’s, especially women’s, permission should not be allowed. It is very concerning. Today, it is one woman and tomorrow it can be anyone else. Digital rights violation is a crime as well if a woman’s face is used without her consent,” she said.
The MPA also outlined steps women could take if they became victims of such content. She advised them to immediately take a screenshot of the material or save the relevant link, while cautioning against circulating it further.
She urged victims to report the material to the relevant cybercrime authorities and said women in Punjab could also contact the Punjab Women Protection Authority helpline. “This is an important issue that we must tackle, as there can be no threat to women’s integrity and respect,” she concluded.
The incident has once again brought attention to the challenges posed by AI-generated and manipulated content, particularly when women’s images are used without their consent. As such technology becomes increasingly accessible, questions surrounding privacy, consent and digital safety continue to form an important part of the conversation around women’s rights online.

title: Peace in southern Lebanon remains    elusive     UN mission
description: Lasting peace requires political will  commitments from parties  UNIFIL says
content:
Lasting peace requires political will, commitments from parties, UNIFIL says
The UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) said Tuesday that peace in southern Lebanon remains "elusive," stressing that permanently ending the conflict requires political will from the parties.
The remarks came in a statement marking the International Day of Peace, observed annually on Sept. 21, which UNIFIL commemorated Monday evening with a ceremony at its headquarters in the southern Lebanese town of Naqoura.
“Today, peace in south Lebanon remains elusive, but the hope for peace endures,” UNIFIL said, stressing that lasting peace requires “political commitments and solutions from the parties themselves.”
“Peacekeepers can help restore stability, avoid misunderstandings, and reduce the risk of escalation -- but they cannot replace the political will and decisions needed to end the conflict permanently,” it said.
Read: UN chief stresses smooth Lebanon pull-out
"Peace is not something we address once a year; it is an enduring responsibility," UNIFIL Head of Mission and Force Commander Major General Diodato Abagnara said.
“We patrol, we keep channels of communication open with the parties to reduce the risk of misunderstanding and escalation. We work with the Lebanese Armed Forces as they assume greater responsibilities in the south,” Abagnara said.
He stressed that responsibility for reaching a political solution rests with the parties, while “UNIFIL will continue to do its part, keeping communication open, reducing the risk of escalation, and supporting diplomatic efforts.”
The full implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701 "remains the objective and the basis for lasting peace and stability in south Lebanon," Abagnara added.
“Continued cooperation between the Lebanese Armed Forces and peacekeepers remains central to maintaining stability and supporting the extension of state authority in the south,” he added.
The UN Security Council adopted Resolution 1701 in August 2006 following a 33-day war between the Israeli army and Hezbollah.
Read more: Pakistan, Lebanon agree to enhance intelligence sharing, security cooperation
The resolution calls for a complete cessation of hostilities between Lebanon and Israel and for an area between the Blue Line and the Litani River in southern Lebanon to be free of weapons and armed personnel except those of the Lebanese army and UNIFIL.
UNIFIL said the current conflict has forced thousands of people from their homes, with many remaining displaced.
“It has disrupted livelihoods, caused widespread damage to homes and infrastructure, and resulted in civilian deaths and injuries,” it added.
This year's International Day of Peace is the last UNIFIL will observe before its mandate expires at the end of 2026, following a UN Security Council decision in 2025 to end the mission.
The UN General Assembly established the International Day of Peace in 1981 to promote ceasefires, nonviolence, tolerance, justice and human rights.
Also read: 4 killed, 20 injured in Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon despite US deal
Israeli attacks on Lebanon since March 2 have killed at least 4,386 people, injured 12,407 others and displaced more than 1 million, according to Lebanese authorities.
The attacks have continued despite the two countries signing a US-brokered framework agreement on June 26 providing for a gradual Israeli withdrawal from occupied Lebanese territory in exchange for the deployment of the Lebanese army and the disarmament of Hezbollah.
Israel occupies areas in southern Lebanon, some for decades and others since the 2023-2024 war, while Israeli forces have advanced more than 10 kilometres (6.2 miles) during the current offensive.
