title: Saudi defence fund speeds up maritime sector push following Houthi advance
description: MASNA Ventures seeks to plough more money into local manufacturing of US  allied defence tech
content:
MASNA Ventures seeks to plough more money into local manufacturing of US, allied defence tech
Saudi Arabia's first defence-focused venture capital fund, MASNA Ventures, is seeking to plough more money into local manufacturing of United States and allied defence technology as conflict in the Gulf exposes the region's military gaps.
The fund, anchored by a prominent Saudi family office and sharia-compliant, has asked the Capital Markets Authority to raise its capacity to $150 million from $100 million, General Partner Lucien Zeigler told Reuters .
Committed capital so far includes only Saudi nationals, and the firm is weighing whether to bring in international capital, Zeigler said, declining to comment further on amounts or investors, citing regulations. "This is a bet on Saudi sovereignty, and we want Saudis who believe in the sector sharing in the wins," he said.
The firm is speeding up collaboration with so-called Prime Original Equipment Manufacturers and startup unicorns "whose connected, autonomous platforms were designed for exactly what is happening in the Gulf and the Red Sea ," Zeigler said. He declined to name the companies, citing non-disclosure agreements.
The Prime manufacturers term refers to major defence firms such as Lockheed Martin and Boeing.
MASNA's focus is on autonomous systems including unmanned aerial, surface and underwater vehicles.
"Maritime is absolutely a priority...we are actively accelerating that domain right now," Zeigler said.
Venture capital firms have invested $19.4 billion in defence tech globally this year, double last year's total, according to PitchBook. Saudi Arabia has recorded VC deals worth about $200 million in 2026, the data platform said.
Zeigler has spent most of the last 15 years working in the Kingdom with Saudi and US business, and in venture capital, defence, and investments. He previously headed Middle East and North Africa operations at Silicon Valley's Pilatus Venture Capital.
Read: How Yemen's Houthis went from a small mountain militia to a big regional threat
MASNA has partnered with SR2 Defence Systems, a local manufacturer that Zeigler co-founded, to develop advanced defence technology on Saudi soil.
The fund is targeting three operational joint ventures and six capital investments in 2026. It has already backed a joint venture between SR2 and US drone maker Vector Defence that is "ramping up now," with MASNA leading a funding round that is three times oversubscribed, Zeigler said.
The firm also plans to back another joint venture producing anti-drone systems built around "world-leading US hard-kill technology."
Drones have played a central role in the Houthi campaign in Yemen and the broader Gulf conflict involving Iran, the US and their allies. Saudi Arabia was hit by strikes from groups in recent weeks that threatened its oil exports, while a new Houthi presence near the Bab el-Mandeb strait risks further disrupting Red Sea shipping routes.
"Right now, it is drones and aerial defence above all else," Zeigler said. "The events of this past week emphasise those needs."

In a Vogue October cover story, Jordan discussed his long-standing interest in anime and his plans to explore the medium through new projects.
“I might just quit it all and make anime the rest of my life,” Jordan said.
Anime has been a long-standing interest for the actor, who grew up watching Dragon Ball Z. Jordan would reportedly sometimes sneak into the basement of his church to watch episodes.
His interest has also influenced his work outside acting. In 2019, Jordan collaborated with Coach on a Naruto-inspired fashion collection featuring clothing, footwear and bags incorporating imagery and symbols from the anime series.
Jordan later brought anime influences into his 2023 directorial debut, Creed III. The film's climactic fight incorporated elements inspired by anime, while Jordan also worked with Japanese animation studio TMS Entertainment on an anime short that screened after Creed III in Japanese cinemas.
Earlier this year, Jordan continued his work in animation by voicing Ollie in Netflix's Swapped .
Despite his comments about potentially leaving acting, Jordan has several film and television projects in development.
He is directing, producing and starring in a new adaptation of The Thomas Crown Affair alongside Adria Arjona and Kenneth Branagh, with the film scheduled for next spring.
Jordan is also set to begin filming a Miami Vice reboot with Austin Butler this autumn and is producing Delphi, a Creed spin-off series centred on a boxing gym.
Jordan's anime projects follow his Best Actor Oscar win for Sinners , in which he played twins Smoke and Stack. The Ryan Coogler-directed film received 16 Academy Award nominations and won four awards.

title: Tom Cruise praised for discussion around AI and human filmmaking at BAFTA event
description: Tom Cruise discussed AI and human filmmaking at BAFTA event  saying audiences want to see real things
content:
Tom Cruise discussed AI and human filmmaking at BAFTA event, saying audiences want to see real things
Tom Cruise discussed the impact of artificial intelligence on filmmaking during a BAFTA: Life in Pictures event in London, arguing that audiences continue to value human-made experiences.
Speaking at BAFTA’s Piccadilly headquarters on Monday, Cruise reflected on his film career before moderator Edith Bowman asked about the role of AI in the film industry.
The actor acknowledged that wider use of the technology is approaching but emphasised the importance of human creativity and craft.
“Here's the thing: There is nothing like human,” Cruise said during an impromptu six-minute speech that received applause from the audience.
Cruise also discussed the relationship between filmmaking technology, cinema and audiences. He said the success of the summer cinema season, including engagement from younger audiences, demonstrated continued interest in shared theatrical experiences.
“But people want to see real things,” he said.
“What you put attention on, you give life,” Cruise told the BAFTA audience. “People wanna see real things.”
Cruise has previously discussed artificial intelligence during the 2023 SAG-AFTRA negotiations, when he pushed for protections relating to the technology. He has also repeatedly highlighted the role of people in filmmaking.
The actor’s comments came as he promotes his upcoming film Digger , which was the focus of the BAFTA event.
Cruise described the film as “one of the most original and moving” films he has worked on. The film is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on October 2.
Cruise also acknowledged that AI will become increasingly involved in filmmaking, saying its broader use “is coming, and it's going to happen.”
“People want that experience. They're going to movie theaters,” Cruise said at the event. “I always believe in humanity.”

title: Taylor Swift advised on her friendship with Ed Sheeran amid Macklemore tour controversy
description: Swift and Sheeran have maintained a close friendship since meeting in 2012
content:
Swift and Sheeran have maintained a close friendship since meeting in 2012
Taylor Swift has been advised to remain quiet rather than distance herself from Ed Sheeran as the singer continues to face backlash over Macklemore’s removal from his US Loop Tour.
The longtime friends have been close for around 14 years, but Sheeran has found himself at the centre of controversy after Macklemore was dropped from the remaining tour dates following his public support for Palestinians. Sheeran has said the decision was made by the tour’s promoter.
Following Sheeran’s recent performance in Philadelphia, The Mirror spoke to PR expert John Kwatakye-Atiko of Popularity PR about how Swift might respond to the situation. He said he would advise his clients “not to say anything” and argued that this was not a situation requiring Swift to publicly distance herself from her friend.
Kwatakye-Atiko said the controversy involved stadium owners, promoters and liability concerns rather than an allegation of personal misconduct against Sheeran. He also suggested that Swift would be unlikely to take a public side in the dispute.
Swift and Sheeran have maintained a close friendship since meeting in 2012. The pair first collaborated on “Everything Has Changed”, which appeared on Swift’s Red album, and have since worked together several times. Sheeran also joined Swift onstage during her Eras Tour at Wembley Stadium in 2024.
The two musicians have continued to speak warmly about their friendship over the years. Swift previously described Sheeran as one of her “absolute favorite people”, while Sheeran has spoken about their ability to have long conversations because they understand the pressures of each other’s careers.
The latest controversy began after Macklemore made pro-Palestinian remarks during a concert at MetLife Stadium, after which he was removed from Sheeran’s remaining US shows. Several other support acts subsequently withdrew from the tour.
As Sheeran continues the remaining dates, Swift has not publicly commented on the dispute. According to the PR expert quoted by The Mirror, keeping her distance publicly while maintaining her longstanding friendship privately would be the approach he would recommend.

title: UK backed AI system strengthens FBR tax monitoring across cement sector
description: High Commissioner Jane Marriott says Digital Eyes exemplifies UK Pakistan working together to deliver practical change
content:
High Commissioner Jane Marriott says Digital Eyes exemplifies UK-Pakistan working together to deliver practical change
An artificial intelligence-powered system "Digital Eye" is now monitoring production at all 27 cement factories in Pakistan, helping the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) strengthen tax compliance and improve visibility of output, according to officials statement
The system, first piloted in 2023, uses advanced video analytics to monitor production lines in real time, providing factories and the FBR with an independent record of production. Working alongside FBR's existing Track and Trace System, the "Digital Eye" system gives tax authorities greater visibility of output while reducing reliance on manual inspection and paperwork, the statement said.
While track and trace records products leaving the production line, "Digital Eye" independently monitors production through AI-powered video analytics, allowing the two systems to be cross-checked and increasing confidence in reported output, the release stated.
British High Commissioner Jane Marriott visited Fecto Cement alongside senior FBR officials to see the technology in operation. During her visit, the group toured the production line, observed the monitoring system, and received a briefing on how the technology was supporting tax administration reforms.
Read: IT minister formally inaugurates ‘The Innovation Hive’ established by USEFP
"Digital Eye is a strong example of the UK and Pakistan working together to deliver practical change," Marriott said. "Built in Pakistan and now operated nationwide by the FBR, it shows how innovation can be scaled to strengthen tax compliance, support fair competition and improve transparency," she added.
The high commissioner noted, according to the official statement, that the UK was proud to have supported the journey through technical expertise, while helping build the institutional capability needed to sustain it.
Separately, the FBR's Chief of Reforms and Modernisation, Dr Najeeb Ullah, said real-time production monitoring had already strengthened compliance in the cement and sugar sectors without adding to the burden on compliant taxpayers. "The results speak for themselves," he said, adding that the FBR's focus was now on consolidating what had been built, improving accuracy, deepening the skills of its teams, and extending the system to more sectors.
"Accurate production data protects the businesses that declare honestly, and we are grateful to the UK for its technical support through REMIT, and we intend to take this approach into further sectors," he added.
Read More: US Embassy completes STEAM programme for 100+ Pakistani innovators
According to the official statement, the solution was developed by a Pakistani technology company and was tested, refined and rolled out nationwide with UK technical support. The release stated that the project demonstrated how Pakistani innovation could be scaled through international partnership to deliver reforms at the national level.
The technology and the wider reform behind it were also attracting interest from countries across Africa, which were looking to Pakistan's experience for lessons on modernising tax compliance, the statement said.
It added that UK support had also helped the FBR "build the capability to operate, maintain and further develop the system independently."
As per the release, the government also reported that wider reforms had helped recover Rs32 billion from the cement sector and increased recorded sugar production by 31% during the most recent crushing season. The release noted that these results "reflect a range of policy and compliance measures, of which 'Digital Eye' forms one part."

Usman finished 19th out of 31 riders in dressage with 36.70 penalty points.
China’s Tian Hua topped the race with 26.90 pp, and was followed by Korntawat Samran of Thailand with a 29.70pp and Japan’s Toshiyuki Tanaka at the third place with 29.90pp.

title: Two cops guarding polio team martyred in Balochistan s Noshki
description: Naqvi condemns incident  saying attacking team working to secure future of children is heinous and unforgivable act
content:
Naqvi condemns incident, saying attacking team working to secure future of children is heinous and unforgivable act
Two police officers providing security to a polio vaccination team were killed after unidentified armed men opened fire in Noshki district of Balochistan, officials said on Tuesday.
The incident came as a week-long sub-national polio vaccination campaign was underway in 115 districts across Pakistan. More than 31 million children under the age of five were due to receive polio drops during the campaign, with activities focused on high-risk and hotspot areas in Balochistan, Gilgit-Baltistan, Islamabad, Khyber- Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Sindh.
The attack took place in Killi Jamalabad, where police personnel had been deployed to protect the vaccination team. The two officers were identified as Muhammad Yasar and Abdul Rauf.
The attackers fled with the officers’ official weapons after the shooting, officials said. Police subsequently cordoned off the area and launched a search operation to arrest those responsible.
Balochistan Special Assistant on Home Affairs Babar Yousafzai confirmed the incident and condemned the attack, blaming Fitna al-Hindustan for the deaths.
“ Fitna al-Hindustan opened fire on two police personnel deployed to protect a polio team in Nushki and martyred them,” Yousafzai said.
He said the attack on a polio team was effectively an attack on the future of children in Balochistan. “They do not want the children of Balochistan to move towards a healthy and secure future,” he said.
Read: Fourth polio case of 2026 detected in K-P's Bannu
Yousafzai said polio was a dangerous disease that could cause permanent disability in children, while vaccination was an effective means of preventing it. “Those who target polio teams are, in fact, trying to deprive the children of Balochistan of their right to health and a secure future,” he said.
“Polio workers are going from door to door to protect our children from disease, and their security is the shared responsibility of the state and society. Children in Balochistan need education, health, peace and a bright future, not terrorism and disease,” he added.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi strongly condemned the firing and expressed grief over the deaths of constables Muhammad Yasar and Abdul Rauf.
Naqvi paid tribute to the two officers and offered condolences to their families. “Constables Yasar and Abdul Rauf attained the great rank of martyrdom while performing their duties,” Naqvi said.
“Attacking a team working to secure the future of children is a heinous and unforgivable act by brutal elements. The beasts who attacked the anti-polio team deserve an exemplary punishment,” Naqvi added.
وفاقی وزیرداخلہ محسن نقوی کی نوشکی کے علاقے میں انسداد پولیو ٹیم پر فائرنگ کی پرزور مذمت وزیرداخلہ کا فائرنگ سے دو کانسٹیبلز محمد یاسر اور عبدالروف کی شہادت پر اظہار افسوس وزیر داخلہ کا جام شہادت نوش کرنے والے کانسٹیبلز محمد یاسر اور عبدالروف کو خراج عقیدت
It is pertinent to note that polio vaccination teams have been targeted in the past, including incidents reported in Quetta and several other districts of Balochistan, highlighting the persistent security challenges faced by frontline health workers and their protectors.
Despite these threats, authorities have reiterated their commitment to continuing the anti-polio campaign and ensuring the safety of vaccination teams through enhanced security measures.
In May 2026, two officers were killed in separate attacks in Bajaur within a single day. Constable Syed Aziz was shot by unidentified gunmen in the Qila Nazakai area of Salarzai and died at the scene, while constable Syed Qadir Shah was shot while returning from polio duty in the village of Tabei and later died of his injuries. The attacks coincided with the launch of a week-long polio campaign across 79 high-risk districts, targeting more than 19 million children.
On April 13, a police officer was killed, and four others were wounded when gunmen struck personnel protecting polio teams in Hangu, near Chapri Waziran , within the jurisdiction of Thall Police Station. The martyred officer was named Israrul Haq, a resident of Shangla who was undergoing police training; the Kohat deputy inspector general said police had killed two attackers in a retaliatory operation, though others escaped.
Two days later, in Dera Murad Jamali, Balochistan, constable Farman Bashir Behrani was shot dead by armed men on a motorcycle while standing guard outside a house where a polio team was administering drops to children.
Read more: Police officer martyred in attack on polio team in Chaman
Earlier still, on February 6, a police officer guarding a polio team was fatally wounded when unidentified gunmen opened fire in the Roghani area of Chaman, Balochistan. The polio workers escaped unharmed, but the officer later succumbed to his injuries.
Last year, similar attacks were reported through much of 2025. The year closed with an attack in Bajaur on 16 December, when constable Sajjad, assigned to protect polio workers, and a civilian were killed when armed attackers opened fire on the team in the Tangai area of Salarzai tehsil.
In October 2025, three attacks struck K-P in as many days. Constable Maqsood, 35, was killed in the Kaahi area of Nizampur while female polio workers were administering drops inside a house; Levies constable Abdul Kabeer was shot dead in Swat district despite additional police deployed for security; and a further constable was killed in Nowshera, where a local police official said two armed terrorists had targeted the officer, killing him on the spot.
At the end of May 2025, in Killi Jamalabad, Noshki — the same locality struck in the latest attack — officer Waheed Ahmed, part of the security detail protecting polio workers, was killed when unidentified assailants opened fire on the vaccination team.
Pakistan’s latest polio case was detected in an eight-month-old child in Bannu district, taking the national tally to four in 2026. The child was from Noor Union Council in Miryan tehsil, where vaccination teams had struggled to reach children consistently since 2025 because of security constraints. Three of the four cases reported this year have come from Bannu Division.
The persistence of the virus has been linked to children missing vaccinations in areas where insecurity restricts access. While overall transmission had declined, poliovirus continued to circulate in southern K-P, with access constraints allowing children to miss critical doses. Pakistan recorded 74 cases in 2024 and 31 in 2025, after cases had fallen sharply in previous years.
Security is therefore a major challenge for eradication efforts, with vaccination teams requiring protection to reach children in high-risk areas. The Express Tribune has also reported continuing concerns over vaccination gaps, community resistance and misinformation, while officials have stressed that children who are missed during campaigns remain vulnerable to infection.
Also read: The dilemma of our polio workforce
After a significant reduction in cases, from 147 in 2019 to just one in 2021, Pakistan has witnessed a resurgence. Since September 2023, there has been an increase in polio activity, particularly in Karachi.
While overall poliovirus transmission in the country has been declining, with cases falling from 74 in 2024 to 31 in 2025 and three so far in 2026, reflecting the impact of high-quality vaccination drives, virus circulation in southern K-P persists.
Polio is a highly contagious and incurable disease that can cause lifelong paralysis and, in some instances, death. However, the disease can be prevented through polio vaccines, which are safe and effective and have been used safely in 195 countries, including all Muslim countries.

title: Mandhana s 79 powers India to Asian Games gold
description: India women secure a 147 run victory in the gold medal match over Sri Lanka
content:
India women secure a 147-run victory in the gold medal match over Sri Lanka
Smriti Mandhana's whirlwind 79 helped India crush Sri Lanka by 147 runs and win a second consecutive women's cricket gold at the Asian Games on Tuesday.
India smashed 216-3 off their 20 overs, the highest women's total in Asian Games history, with 18 fours and 13 sixes.
Richa Ghosh and Bharti Fulmali plundered 25 off the final over from the hapless Mithali Ayodhya, who did not help her cause by conceding eight wides.
Sri Lanka were never in the hunt and captain Chamari Athapaththu's 29 was their only innings of note as they were skittled for 69 in 15.4 overs and had to settle for silver.
Opening batter Mandhana hit seven sixes and five fours in a 45-ball knock that sent the ball to all parts of the Korogi Athletic Park ground in Nagoya.
After India captain Harmanpreet Kaur won the toss and opted to bat, Shafali Verma, who made an unbeaten century in the semi-final, and Mandhana put on a blistering opening partnership.
The pair had raced to 99 in the 10th over when Verma had a rush of blood, playing a needless reverse sweep which she top-edged to Kawya Kavindi at point to fall for 48 off 29 balls.
Mandhana, the greatest run scorer in women's T20 cricket history, had reached her fifty earlier in the over and sailed on in style, clubbing anything loose to the boundary.
Harmanpreet joined her and the pair took the score to 141 before the captain holed out to long-off for 19.
Mandhana, looking to accelerate further in the latter overs, skied an attempted six and was out in the 17th over with the score on 163.
Ghosh clattered 49 off 22 balls with three sixes and six fours to take India past 200 in the final over.
Earlier, some lusty late-order hitting by Pakistan captain Fatima Sana set up a 31-run win over Bangladesh in the bronze medal match.
Sana came in with her side rocking at 67-5 in the 12th over but plundered 45 off 30 balls including three fours and three sixes and was out off the last ball of the 20 overs after seeing Pakistan to 145-8.
Her 67-run partnership with Aliya Riaz (25) for the sixth wicket proved the turning point and Bangladesh could only muster 114-7 in reply.

title: India narrowly survive huge scare against minnows Japan
description: Japan fell just two run short from target
content:
Japan fell just two-run short from target
World champions India narrowly survived being on the end of a huge upset as they edged a spirited Japan by two runs in a rain-shortened first-ever T20 international between the teams on Tuesday.
The historic match celebrating 75 years of diplomatic relations took place at Japan's modest Sano International Cricket Ground outside Tokyo.
It was Japan's first T20 game against a full-member nation.
India, who retained their T20 World Cup crown at home earlier this year, opted to bat first after rain and wet outfield delayed the start and forced a five-overs-a-side shootout.
India, captained by Shreyas Iyer, struggled to score on a sluggish pitch as they made 32-4.
Japan -- ranked 41st by the International Cricket Council (ICC) -- pushed their more illustrious opponents all the way as they threatened a massive shock.
They were in the game until the last ball but finished on 30-3, falling agonisingly just short.
"Yeah, extremely proud, as I think I've been saying to a few other guys, that when it gets that close, it's actually a little bit tougher to take, and the emotions are running pretty high in our group," Japan skipper Kendel Kadowaki-Fleming said.
"But the fact that we were able to run the best team in the world, in my opinion, to the last ball of a game is pretty special."
Japan's 17-year-old spinner Charlie Hara-Hinze stood out with figures of 2-17 in his two overs after he opened the attack and sent back opener Abhishek Sharma for a golden duck.
Kadowaki-Fleming attempted to pull off the chase in his run-a-ball 12, but India's experienced spinners saved the heavyweights from embarrassment.
"It doesn't matter how good a team you are, because the oppositions are also competitive, and the attitude and approach the Japanese team showed today was impeccable, and kudos to them," India skipper Iyer said.
"The approach was outstanding. So I'm sure that they are on the right track right now."
The build-up to what should have been a mismatch was affected by Typhoon Dujuan, with heavy rain in Sano forcing training to be cancelled on Monday.
The venue, which is also used for baseball and has a capacity of around 2,000 spectators, was dominated by India fans who had been expecting a rout.
Japan will play the opening match of men's T20 cricket at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games against Afghanistan on Thursday at a converted baseball field.

title: A ten rupee photograph
description: From ten rupee photographs and packed domestic grounds to empty stands and forgotten stars
content:
From ten-rupee photographs and packed domestic grounds to empty stands and forgotten stars
“When the match is over, the players will meet all of you. For now, please step aside and wait.”
When the security guard stationed at Karachi’s Bakhtiyari Youth Centre said this in a booming voice, all the spectators gathered around the players moved a little farther away. I was one of them.
This was sometime after 1992. Pakistan had just won the World Cup, and cricket fever had reached its peak across the country. Cricketers were not merely famous; they were genuine superstars.
Whenever my teammates and I at the club found out that a member of the Pakistan team was going to be at the KCCA Stadium or any nearby ground, we would immediately head there. That day at the Youth Centre, when the match ended, Aaqib Javed and Aamer Sohail, who were playing for Allied Bank, came out to meet their fans.
A Pathan gentleman standing there was telling everyone: “If you want a picture, I’ll charge you ten rupees. Come back here in a week and collect it.”
I asked him to take my picture with Aaqib and Aamer Sohail. I still have both photographs. Every day, when I look at them, I am reminded of my past.
Back then, the crowds that came to watch domestic matches were so large that today you do not even see such numbers at Test matches. In those days, all eleven members of the Pakistan team were stars. Today, apart from Babar Azam, hardly anyone seems to be widely recognised.
Even Babar’s own performances have been far from what they once were. He has not scored a Test century for four years, yet people continue to think, “If not Babar, then who?”
Look at where we have come from. We were once winners of the ODI and T20 World Cups and the Champions Trophy. Today, we lose even to a team like the United States. Bangladesh, a team we once used to mock, has beaten us at home and then invited us to their own country and defeated us there as well.
The consequence is that cricket fans in the country are rapidly disappearing. Stop ten people at random today and ask them whom Pakistan are playing, and perhaps only one or two will know.
We used to say about hockey that nobody even knew the captain’s name. Now ask someone to name all eleven members of the Pakistan cricket team and offer them an iPhone for getting it right; even then, perhaps only five or six names would come to mind.
The decline of cricket in Pakistan cannot be blamed solely on the current board. Its foundations were laid much earlier.
The biggest damage was caused by moving away from first-class cricket. These days, the headlines are saying, “Babar Azam to play domestic cricket after seven years.”
But come on—what favour is he doing? Playing cricket is his job.
When you begin to consider yourself a superstar and abandon the foundation on which your career was built, this is what happens to our players. Our national team probably plays only four or five Tests a year, perhaps a few more. Yet many players make their way into the Test side on the basis of their performances in T20 cricket.
Then, when they face Test cricket, they cannot even see the ball properly. And while bowling, after just four overs they are gasping for breath and shouting, “Water, water!” like desperate travellers lost in the desert under a scorching sun.
Now even the PCB’s patience appears to have run out, and the authorities have begun taking a tougher line. If a player does not play domestic cricket, he will neither receive a central contract nor be considered for national selection.
In the past, if a player had even a little performance to his name, he could pressure the board and secure the kind of remuneration he wanted. They are no longer in a position to do even that.
That is why you are now seeing some of the biggest names in domestic cricket. Yet nobody is going to the grounds to watch them.
Why aren’t people queuing up to meet them? Why is nobody stepping forward for a selfie or an autograph?
If the cricketers look honestly into their own hearts, they will find the answer easily.
There was a time when people would wait for hours just to catch a glimpse of Babar Azam. When he returned from England, nobody even went to the airport to meet him. He quietly got into a car and went home. A video of the incident is also available on social media.
Cricketers will have to earn back their respect.
And they do not need to spend money on social media for that. The solution is simple: perform on the field. Win matches for Pakistan, and these same people will once again follow you everywhere.
A few poor performances can be understood. But this decline has now stretched over years. Fans have begun to feel that this team is not going to win anyway, so why waste their time following it?
Cricket has always brought the entire Pakistani nation together. It has also played a role in giving Pakistan a positive image around the world. Today, instead of envy and admiration, foreigners sometimes express sympathy.
Is this really the story you want to tell your grandchildren when you grow old?
“Son, look at this picture. We won this title.”
“This must be an AI-generated picture. Or wait—our cricket team actually won a World Cup once? Wow!”
It is much like today, when you tell children that Pakistan’s hockey team has won the World Cup four times, the most by any team and they think you must be joking.
Our story is not over yet. Pakistan can rise again in cricket.
But simply blaming the board will achieve nothing. The PCB, current players, former cricketers, officials and the media must all play their positive part.
Cricket is the “bread and butter” for all of us. We must not allow it to be destroyed.
The decline came because of mistakes. Now we must play our part in such a way that the glory returns.
Otherwise, our story too will disappear from the pages of history.

title: Mbappe calls Zidane era    like a film
description: France star embraces new chapter under his former Real Madrid mentor as Zidane takes charge of Les Bleus
content:
France star embraces new chapter under his former Real Madrid mentor as Zidane takes charge of Les Bleus.
MADRID: Kylian Mbappe said on Monday playing under new France coach Zinedine Zidane, 15 years after the French football icons first met, is like "something from a film".
Former Real Madrid boss Zidane will take charge of Les Bleus for the first time since replacing Didier Deschamps on Friday in their Nations League match against Turkey in Izmit.
"He was the first person who picked me up to take me to Real Madrid, to the training complex. I was 13 or 14, so it was a long time ago," Mbappe said in an interview with Spanish daily AS of meeting Zidane at a trial for Real Madrid's youth teams.
"Now he's my national team coach. It's like a film, but it's amazing. It's real."
Deschamps's final tournament of a 14-year stint in charge ended in disappointment as France were well beaten by Spain in the World Cup semi-finals in July.
The two-time world champions start their preparations for Euro 2028 with four Nations League matches in the expanded international break, also facing Belgium twice and Italy at the Stade de France.
"We're starting a new process with France. We have two years to prepare for the European Championship and that's what we're focused on now," Mbappe said.
"It's a new era with a new coach. We have the Nations League coming up, four games, and we'll see how they go.
"It's going to be new for everyone because all we've known is Deschamps. It's going to be a change for us, but I think everything is going to go very well."
Mbappe has enjoyed a strong start to the season with Real Madrid, scoring eight goals in as many games in all competitions, but he failed to find the net in Sunday's derby defeat by Atletico Madrid.
Jose Mourinho returned to the Santiago Bernabeu tasked with ending two seasons without a major trophy, but Madrid are already six points behind reigning champions Barcelona in La Liga.
"Other people can talk, but we have to do more and work to bring the excitement back to Real Madrid and bring the trophies back," he added.
Mourinho hit out at the refereeing in the 2-1 loss to Atletico, but Mbappe was not as forthright in his criticism.
"I have my thoughts, but I keep them to myself. I've never been that kind of player and I'm not going to start now," he said.
"The referee is human and makes mistakes, and there were mistakes, but I don't want to get into that."

Assailant detained, reportedly used grandfather's gun as two injured in critical condition
A student opened fire in front of their high school in Turkiye's western province of Manisa early on Tuesday, wounding at least 11 other pupils, Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said.
Two of the wounded were in a critical condition, Gurleksaid. The assailant was caught and their mother, father, and grandfather — who owned the weapon used in the attack — have been detained, the minister added.
"When the security of our children is the issue, it is not possible for any negligence, any irresponsibility to be overlooked," the minister said on X.

"The circumstances under which the child obtained the gun used in the attack, the conditions of the weapon's storage, the parents' obligations regarding care and supervision, and allegations of bullying prior to the incident are being investigated thoroughly and from multiple angles," Gurlek added.
Images and video posted online showed a male figure walking on a street near the school with a rifle in his hands. He was then seen running back from the same street. Video outside the school showed police pushing away families and others outside the premises.
The motive for the attack was not immediately clear.

The local governor's office has said the attack took place at around 8:00am (0500 GMT) at the Inci Uzmez Vocational and Technical Anatolian High School in the Turgutlu district.
Two deadly school shootings in April caused outrage in Turkey and prompted officials to bring in new security measures for the 2026-2027 academic year, including tighter gun controls. Before then, the country had not had a history of such attacks.
Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz said Interior Minister Mustafa Ciftci and Education Minister Yusuf Tekin were going to Manisa to carry out inspections.

His family, including sister Kaia Gerber, has requested privacy during this difficult period.

content:
Ed Sheeran’s Gillette Stadium concerts are expected to face protests following Macklemore’s tour exit
Ed Sheeran’s upcoming concerts at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, are expected to draw protests following Macklemore’s removal from the singer’s US tour.
According to the supplied report, Massachusetts Peace Action is sponsoring a demonstration near Gillette Stadium on Saturday, September 26, ahead of Sheeran’s second show at the venue. Sheeran is also scheduled to perform at the stadium on Friday.
The organisation reportedly said the demonstration is “centered around the fight against 'billionaire censorship' and 'genocide in Palestine.'”
Protesters also attended Sheeran’s Philadelphia concert over the weekend, according to the report.
Macklemore was removed from the remaining US dates of Sheeran’s tour after his “Free Palestine” speech at MetLife Stadium earlier this month.
Other scheduled performers, including Finneas, Lukas Graham, Aaron Rowe and Beoga, subsequently withdrew from the tour.
Sheeran addressed the controversy before performing in Philadelphia, telling the audience: “This is not usually how I open a show, but before I play some songs tonight I hope it's OK if I say a few words about this last week.”
He continued, “I'm used to my music being criticized, and I'm always happy to take that because I'm lucky a lot of you like my stuff… But this week the criticism was about something much more important. And I've had to take and make difficult decisions, and I am making mistakes, and I'm so sorry.”
Sheeran said the dispute had placed him “in the middle of an important and passionate argument about freedom of speech and the most complex political issue on the planet.”
He also expressed concern about venues controlling performers’ content.
“Honoring my commitment to my fans is completely central to who I am, and that is why I'm here tonight on my own and continuing my current tour,” Sheeran said.
“But I am deeply worried about the idea of venues pre-approving content of performers. This happens in so many places I perform around the world, but it should never happen in the free world.”
He concluded, “My heart has been broken by the scale of devastation and loss of civilians' lives, of children's lives, and the systemic injustice we're seeing unfold in the West Bank cannot be overlooked.”

title: Police investigating overdose as Presley Gerber cause of death
description: Presley Gerber  27  has died  with police investigating suspected overdose at rehabilitation facility
content:
Presley Gerber, 27, has died, with police investigating suspected overdose at rehabilitation facility
Presley Gerber, the son of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber and older brother of Kaia Gerber, has died aged 27, with police investigating a suspected overdose.
The Santa Monica Police Department said officers responded to a possible overdose at a rehabilitation facility at around 9:35am local time on Sunday, where they found Gerber dead.
“Detectives are investigating the death as a suspected overdose,” Santa Monica Police Lt. Lewis Gilmour said. “At this time, there is no indication of foul play.”
The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner performed an autopsy on Monday. Its office said the “cause and manner of death have been deferred, which means additional testing and/or studies were requested in order to make a determination.”
A representative for the Gerber family said they were “asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time.”
Gerber had spoken publicly about his experiences with mental health and addiction. In 2020, he explained a “misunderstood” tattoo on his face by saying: “It says misunderstood, because that's how I felt my entire life.”
Speaking on the Studio 22 podcast in 2023, Gerber said, “Having struggled with mental health, depression and some other things that come along with that, I think that whether I help one person or a hundred people get out of that place that I was in at one point in my life, that's all I need to do.”
He added, “[Mental health] is an issue. It is such a big part of my life. It's a 24/7 job, and there's so much to it. That's really what I want to do: help people.”
In a December 2025 Instagram video, Gerber discussed his experiences with psychiatrists and medication, saying, “Every psychiatrist I've had, and I've had 15, are just like, 'Well, here's 20 medications and take this if you feel like this.' And I'm like, 'No, don't give me that much leeway.' I need some direction.”
Gerber also said he had stopped drinking, saying, “That is no longer serving me.”

title: Marchand fears Japanese rivals ahead of LA Olympics
description: French swimming star praises Shin Ohashi and Tomoyuki Matsushita as major threats at the 2028 Games
content:
French swimming star praises Shin Ohashi and Tomoyuki Matsushita as major threats at the 2028 Games
TOKYO: France's Olympic hero Leon Marchand said Tuesday that Japanese swimmers will be his main rivals at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, admitting he was "scared" and "stressed" about racing them.
Marchand ruled the pool with four individual golds at his home Paris Olympics in 2024 and he remains the man to beat heading towards the Games in two years' time.
Marchand is attending the Asian Games in Japan, where he has had a first-hand look at swimmers including Shin Ohashi and Tomoyuki Matsushita.
Marchand is likely to lock horns with both in LA and the Frenchman said he was "really excited to race them".
"I always look at what they do during the season because I need to keep informed of what's happening in the swimming world," he said.
"They've been doing so well the past couple of years. It's scary, but also exciting for me."
Matsushita won gold in the 200m individual medley at the Asian Games and is set to race in Tuesday's 400m IM final.
Marchand won both events at the Paris Games and is world record holder in both, having beaten Michael Phelps's long-standing marks.
Ohashi, 17, won Asian Games gold in the 100m breaststroke in a dead heat with China's Dong Zhihao and has been tipped to break the world record in the 200m breaststroke.
Marchand, who won the 200m breaststroke in Paris, said he was "very scared" of Ohashi.
"He's still so young, his coach is really good, his entourage, the people around him are really good," said Marchand.
"I hope he's going to keep improving, I think his breaststroke is amazing.
"I'm very excited and also stressed about racing him."
Marchand also had warm words for Matsushita, who is shaping up to be his nearest competitor in the individual medley.
"I feel like the whole country is behind him, so I think it's really cool," said Marchand.
"And I'm really excited to race him in the next month and a couple next year.
"I think he will be one of my main rivals, so I'm really excited for the future and I wish him the best."
Marchand gave a swimming clinic to children in the Tokyo pool in the gap between the morning heats and the evening finals.
He said being in Tokyo "brings back a lot of memories and emotions" of his first Olympics in 2021.
"I had a lot of emotions in that pool, I made my first Olympic final," he said.
"I was very stressed but also very happy to be here, to meet all those people, all those athletes that have different stories, different sports."

content:
Dolly Parton’s nephew Bryan Seaver has reportedly been removed from his longtime security role at her properties
Dolly Parton’s nephew Bryan Seaver has reportedly been removed from his longtime role overseeing security at the late singer’s properties, according to TMZ .
Seaver and his security company, SAPS, were reportedly sent a notice on September 16 informing them that their services were no longer required.
His team were allegedly asked to leave Parton’s properties immediately, including her primary home in Nashville, museum and warehouse.
According to the report, a new security company has since replaced Seaver’s team. Seaver was reportedly told that his removal from the security services would not affect his personal interest in Parton’s estate.
A representative for SAPS told TMZ that the company was “dismayed by the unexpected and, so far, unexplained actions” taken by the executors of Parton’s estate following her death.
“We remain unshakably resolved to fulfil her final directive to protect her family, and we refuse to be intimidated by those whose actions we believe are being taken in bad faith and with the intent to profit from the life of someone who willingly gave so much,” the spokesperson added.
Seaver is the son of Parton’s sister Cassie and had worked as her head of security for more than two decades. His father, Larry, previously held the position.
Following Parton’s death at the age of 80 on August 25, Seaver was responsible for announcing the news in a video posted to her official Instagram account.
“As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment but haven't truly felt it until now,” Seaver said.
“It is an honour, an honour that is mixed with absolute pride and great sadness. But sadness lies with us, not with Dolly. Dolly has lived in the light and is in the arms of Jesus.”

title: LHC seeks arguments on plea challenging Aleema Khan s MPO detention
description: Aleema s son Shahrez  files petition through advocate Rana Mudassar Umar  challenging the detention orders issued
content:
Aleema's son Shahrez, files petition through advocate Rana Mudassar Umar, challenging the detention orders issued
The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Tuesday sought further arguments on the maintainability of a plea challenging the detention of PTI founder Imran Khan’s sister Aleema Khan and her driver, Muhammad Ameer, under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance.
LHC's Justice Abher Gul Khan heard the petition filed by Shahrez Khan, Aleema’s son, challenging the detention orders.
On a point, the court asked the petitioner’s counsel whether he had approached the relevant authority first against this detention order. To which the counsel replied that the case is quite different from others, further arguing that it appeared that the detention proceedings were initiated after Aleema and her driver had already been taken into custody.
He submitted that the District Intelligence Committee (DIC) meeting and issuance of the detention notification took place on the same day. He implored the court that "it appears that the arrest was made first and the DIC meeting was held afterwards". The detention notification was issued after the arrest had already taken place, he argued.
At which point Justice Khan observed that the court will examine the issue. The court is going to reserve its decision on this petition's maintainability, the judge said.
Read: Aleema says public backs Imran's release
On counsel’s request, however, the judge adjourned the hearing until September 25 for further arguments.
Shahrez filed a petition through advocate Rana Mudassar Umar, challenging the detention orders issued on September 20 by the Lahore Deputy Commissioner Capt (retd) Muhammad Ali Ijaz against his mother and two aunts. He argued in his petition that the DC unlawfully issued the detention orders and failed to follow the procedure prescribed under Section 3 of the MPO Ordinance.
It further argued that the orders contain no specific allegations and demonstrate no application of mind.
The petition also said that ordinary criminal law and less restrictive measures were not considered and contended that the grounds for detention were not communicated within the required period, alleging that the detention orders were issued after the arrests.
It asked the court to set aside the detention orders issued by the Lahore DC and declare them unlawful.
On Sunday, it is pertinent to mention that Aleema was detained by the authorities after the Lahore DC office ordered her detention or arrest for 30 days.
The DC’s order was based on a letter from the Lahore Capital City Police Officer (CCPO), which referred to police reports alleging that Aleema and Ameer “are prejudicial to the public safety and maintenance of public order”.

According to the order, the reports also alleged that the two were involved in roadblocks and protests on May 9, 2023, when PTI supporters and workers took to the streets following Imran’s arrest.
The order further stated that multiple cases had been registered against the two and described them as posing a potential threat to public peace and tranquillity.
Aleema was detained amid a crackdown on PTI ahead of its planned countrywide protest and march to Islamabad on September 27 . The party has announced the protest to demand Imran’s release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.
It is also pertinent to mention that following Aleema’s detention, her two sisters, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, were also detained under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) law.

The Board of Peace on Tuesday reiterated its key objectives for Gaza as world leaders prepare to gather in New York for the UN General Assembly, calling for international support to advance a roadmap for ending the conflict.
In a statement on US social media platform X, the board said its shared objectives include the demilitarisation and deradicalisation of Gaza, sustained humanitarian aid and reconstruction, effective Palestinian civilian and security administration, and lasting security for Palestinians and Israelis.

The board, chaired by US President Donald Trump, said the plan had paved the way for the release and return of all Israeli hostages, the Gaza Peace Summit in Sharm El-Sheikh, and subsequent steps including UN Security Council Resolution 2803 and the establishment of the Board of Peace.
It also said an agreement reached with Hamas on July 30 provides a roadmap for the next stages of the ceasefire, including demilitarisation, Israeli withdrawal, Palestinian administration and reconstruction.
The board called on all parties to uphold their commitments and avoid actions that could undermine the ceasefire, while urging international partners to translate political support into practical commitments.

“UNGA provides an opportunity to consolidate the international community behind one agreed framework,” the statement said, emphasising diplomacy as a means toward lasting peace and security in Gaza.

title: PSX gains 249 points on US Iran optimism
description: KSE 100 Index closes at 171 402 as hopes for diplomatic progress  easing oil supply concerns support buying
content:
KSE-100 Index closes at 171,402 as hopes for diplomatic progress, easing oil supply concerns support buying
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) overcame an afternoon bout of profit-taking on Tuesday to finish higher, as renewed buying helped the market recover its losses and close in positive territory.
The sentiment was also bolstered by optimism over a possible breakthrough in the US-Iran conflict, although profit-taking later in the session trimmed the market’s advance. The benchmark KSE-100 Index gained 248.92 points, or 0.15%, to settle at 171,402.08. It hit an intraday high of 171,680.74 and a low of 170,866.94.
The session began with a solid rally, but the momentum faded as investors moved to book profits, briefly pushing the index below its previous close. The decline proved temporary, with buyers returning later in the session to lift the benchmark back into the green.
Oil and gas exploration, cement and power stocks led the recovery, while weakness in commercial banks and fertiliser shares kept the advance modest. The easing of crude supply concerns also influenced the sentiment, with oil prices falling to a two-week low as Iran signalled it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and Saudi Arabia prepared to resume exports from its Red Sea port of Yanbu.
Also Read: PSX rises 269 points as oil market steadies
According to Ahmed Sheraz at KASB KTrade, the market remained mildly positive as easing geopolitical concerns and lower international oil prices supported sentiment. Oil & gas stocks witnessed recovery as Brent crude slipped below $100, trading around $98, easing concerns over inflationary pressures.
Sentiment was further supported by reports that Iran has conveyed to the US administration that it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if Washington lifts the blockade. The development raised hopes of improved oil flows and a reduction in the geopolitical risk premium, supporting recovery in the oil segment, Sheraz added.
He predicted the market to remain cautiously positive, with Brent prices, US-Iran developments and Strait of Hormuz traffic remaining key drivers. A sustained decline in oil prices could provide relief to Pakistan’s external account and support market sentiment, while any renewed geopolitical escalation could bring volatility back to the PSX.
Cumulatively, trading volume decreased to 641.8 million shares from Monday’s volume of 692.8 million. In the ready market, shares of 494 companies were traded. Of these, 226 stocks closed high, 221 fell and 47 remained unchanged. Tasdeeq Information led the volume with trading in 133.2 million shares, losing Rs0.09 to close at Rs4.91.

title: Saba Faisal calls virality an  illness   slams out of context edits
description: Actor also opens up about industry etiquette  punctuality  role selection and the career milestone that was  Humsafar
content:
Actor also opens up about industry etiquette, punctuality, role selection and the career milestone that was 'Humsafar'
Veteran actor Saba Faisal has addressed the culture of viral clips in a recent interview with Vasay Chaudhry, describing how her words are routinely edited out of context and the toll it has taken on a reputation she has spent decades building.
Faisal, who has never shied away from speaking her mind on shows and has previously weighed in on debates surrounding marriage and family, said the problem was less about what she said and more about how her remarks were repackaged online.
"I don't even say anything, and yet it still happens," she said, adding that she had started taking longer breaks from public appearances because of how often innocuous remarks were spliced into controversy.
She was blunt about the damage such editing could cause. "The respect and honour we have built over our entire lives gets severely disturbed when a couple of words are spliced together and edited into the video," she said, describing a practice that prioritised virality over the truth of what was actually said.
For Faisal, the trend had curdled into something closer to a sickness. "Virality is a strange illness that has become so widespread. People have such an obsession with going viral, and becoming viral is the easiest thing in the world."
Her concerns extended beyond social media to what she viewed as a breakdown in professional courtesy within the entertainment industry. Faisal argued that criticism of senior artists had become too casual and too public, particularly when disagreements on a set could be handled privately.
"You sit and criticise artists, and those people criticise who have no standing here, who have achieved nothing, who have nothing to their credit," she said, arguing that internal issues should be resolved privately rather than aired on television.
"Whether it is Sajal [Aly] or anyone else, a seasoned artist whom a major production house invests money in, you cannot just sit on a channel and criticise them like that. We are all people from within the same industry; we are all here for one another," she said.
Faisal then turned to a quality she considers essential to professional success: punctuality.
"A successful person is always someone punctual, who values time, and who knows how to subtract their personal ego from their work," she said, calling consistency "the ultimate secret to success" while lamenting that fewer people in the industry seemed to prioritise it.
Asked about the industry's enduring appetite for saas-bahu dramas, Faisal pushed back against the idea that the genre was simply a reflection of actors' creative choices.
"It's not for me; it's because of people's approach and mindset," she said. "The segment of society that watches television has these exact problems and ways of solving them, which is why production houses invest money in them."
She was equally candid about her own approach to choosing roles. "Whichever character offers me a good margin, good pay, and maximum screen time, I will do it."
Looking back on her career, Faisal singled out Humsafar as the project that changed the way she approached acting.
"I was always cast as a good-looking lady wearing sarees with heavy makeup," she said of her earlier roles. "When I got Humsafar , I learned what an actor's true thirst is, what an actor wants, and how to perform. That proved to be a milestone in my acting career."
Away from industry politics, Faisal credited a deliberately positive outlook with helping her navigate setbacks.
"A positive mindset should be a weapon for everyone. It gives you support during difficult times and when you hit rock bottom," she said, adding that she had come to see hardship as something that ultimately refined character rather than broke it.
That philosophy also shaped how she viewed time itself. "The present moment is the best; it is the most supreme," she said, arguing that nostalgia could often make the past appear better than it actually was.
It was an outlook she carried into her personal life as well, where she remained a firm believer in traditional family values and mutual respect — a stance she had voiced before and continued to stand by despite the criticism it had sometimes drawn.

Zidane and Klopp face their first tests against Turkey and the Netherlands
The 2026/27 Nations League kicks off on Thursday but all eyes will be on the touchlines as a starry cast of new coaches, including Zinedine Zidane and Jurgen Klopp, prepare to make their debuts in international football.
The end of World Cup cycles usually herald in a host ofnew faces, however, the 2026 vintage is particularly bountiful, with no fewer than 10 European nations having appointed a new coach since this summer's tournament in North America.
Most notable are 1998 World Cup winner and France legend Zidane, who succeeds Didier Deschamps as Les Bleus boss, and former Liverpool manager Klopp, who takes over his native Germany.
When Deschamps announced the 2026 World Cup would signal the end of his 14-year reign as France boss, only one name was on the lips of football fans in the country: 'Zizou'.
They got their wish when it was announced in July that the three-time Champions League-winning coach was replacing his old team-mate and captain at the helm of Les Bleus.
"He was the first person who picked me up to take me to Real Madrid, to the training complex. I was 13 or 14, so it was a long time ago," Mbappe said in an interview with Spanish daily AS of meeting Zidane at a trial for Real Madrid's youth teams.
"Now he's my national team coach. It's like a film, but it's amazing. It's real." Mbappe said.
Finally, the 54-year-old will oversee his first matches as coach away to Turkey on Friday and in Belgium three days later, before making his touchline bow at the Stade de France on October 2 against Italy.
A second meeting against the Belgians in Paris the following Monday will bring the curtain down on Zidane's opening salvo in international management.
"The France job was the only one I wanted," former Real Madrid coach Zidane said in July.
"I've had offers over these four or five years to take charge of a club and I turned them all down for the French national team.
"I'm ready for the challenge, that's what drives me."
If Zidane's appointment marks the long-awaited return of an iconic figure to the national team in France, Klopp's has been greeted with no less excitement in Germany, even if it is the former Mainz defender's first taste of the Nationalmannschaft.
Uncapped as a player, Klopp made his name in football as a coach. After legendary spells at Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool, and a period away from the touchline as Red Bull's global sports director, Klopp will begin an adventure many in Germany thought would never happen.
"This is ideally the high point of my career, of my life, my professional life. I will give it everything I have," Klopp said at his unveiling after Julian Nagelsmann departed following Germany's disastrous World Cup.
The charismatic 59-year-old Klopp has already shown he will do things his way by calling up 44 players, divided into two squads, for his first matches in charge.
Those games will be against the Netherlands in Amsterdam on Thursday and at home to Greece three days later, before a meeting with Serbia in Munich on October 1 and a trip to Greece on October 4.
Other arrivals for this opening round of Nations League matches include Jorge Jesus, who will make his Portugal debut when the competition's reigning champions welcome Wales on Thursday.
Ex-Barcelona metronome and 2010 World Cup winner Xavi Hernandez replaces Ronald Koeman as Netherlands coach.
Roberto Mancini, who masterminded Italy's Euro 2020 victory, returns to try and right the course of the floundering Azzurri.
Former Bayern Munich and Netherlands midfielder Mark van Bommel will oversee his first Belgium match against Italy and Slaven Bilic takes over the Croatia reins for a second time, following a successful six-year spell in charge of the Vatreni between 2006 and 2012.
Spain's World Cup and European Championship-winning coach Luis de la Fuente is staying put. He was on Monday rewarded with a contract extension until 2032.
His world champions will begin their tilt at a second Nations League title with an eye-catching clash against Thomas Tuchel's England at Wembley on Saturday.

title: JI gives PM talks a chance  keeps Islamabad march on table
description: JI say if situation worsens  government will be responsible  our sit ins  protest camps will continue
content:
JI say if situation worsens, government will be responsible, our sit-ins, protest camps will continue
Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman said on Tuesday that the party would give Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif a chance to hold talks on public relief but would not back down from its protest movement or planned long march towards Islamabad, while maintaining that its wider protest movement would continue.
According to a post on X, Rehman said that following lengthy consultations, the party had decided to keep its sit-ins and protest camps active while allowing the prime minister time to meet the JI and discuss measures to provide relief to the public
Speaking at a press conference in Multan, Rehman said the party had held an extensive consultation before deciding to give the prime minister an opportunity to discuss its demands.
ملتان میں پریس کانفرنس کرتے ہوئے حافظ نعیم الرحمن کا کہنا ہے کہ کل وزیر اعظم نے فون پر کہا اپنے لانگ مارچ کو ملتوی یا مؤخر کریں، وزیر اعظم کو بتایا عوام پریشان ہیں، ہمیں احتجاج کا کوئی شوق نہیں ہے۔ وزیر اعظم نے کہا وہ بیرون ملک ہیں، آؤں گا تو ریلیف دوں گا۔ آج طویل مشاورت سے فیصلہ… pic.twitter.com/tDALjc29ME
“We will not withdraw from our protest, nor will we withdraw from our long march,” he said.
Rehman said PM Shehbaz had contacted him while he was speaking at Multan railway station and requested that the march be cancelled or postponed. The prime minister told him he would meet the JI leadership after returning to Pakistan and discuss measures to provide relief to the public, he said.
“I told him that your ministers have been making these promises for so many days, and we have been forced into this situation,” Rehman said, adding that the party had no interest in continuing protests in severe heat if the issue could be resolved.
The JI chief said the government’s relief package was inadequate and maintained that the party’s main demand was the abolition of the additional levy on petroleum products.
“Our agenda is not disorder; it is to provide relief to the people,” Rehman said.
He said JI workers would remain active during the period before the prime minister’s return, while the party would seek a written assurance from the government.
Rehman said the long march would remain stationed in Multan until the prime minister returned and talks took place. “This will be the government’s last chance for talks,” he said, adding that the petroleum levy must be abolished.
The JI chief said the party had launched its protest movement over rising electricity, gas and petrol prices and had held demonstrations across the country.
He said the party had staged protests before holding sit-ins at 510 locations nationwide from August 7, while allowing ambulances to pass. From August 16, the sit-ins began at four provincial headquarters and later expanded to 42 cities, he said.
The JI also held a shutdown strike on September 3 with public and traders’ support, after which the government came under pressure and negotiations began, Rehman said.
He said the JI had presented proposals to the government’s committee on ways to abolish the levy, but the government had cited pressure from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for its inability to remove it.
Rehman said the JI’s Islamabad march began on September 20, with the first phase involving a train march from Karachi to Rohri and the second phase from Rohri to Multan.
“Our agenda is absolutely clear. We have no personal agenda and no party agenda. We want nothing for ourselves,” he said.
Rehman rejected the government’s relief package, saying it amounted to Rs26 billion to Rs30 billion a month while the government was collecting Rs150 billion in levy.
“The ultimate solution is to abolish the additional levy on petrol,” he said.
The JI chief said the party would continue its preparations for the Islamabad march while waiting for the prime minister’s meeting and would not limit its planned entry into the capital to a single point, and also referred to conditions in Balochistan, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Azad Kashmir, saying the JI wanted to bring people from those areas into the mainstream through national unity.
“If the prime minister tells us on that day what relief we are providing, then it is fine. If relief is not provided, we have the first week and first ten days of October, and we will continue our long march against the same government in the same manner.”
“If the situation worsens, the government will be responsible. Our sit-ins and protest camps will continue,” he said.
According to a statement issued by the JI media wing, PM Shehbaz contacted Rehman after the JI chief reached Multan while leading the party’s train march towards Islamabad.
“I have already announced a relief package for the nation. However, as soon as I return to Pakistan, I will meet the JI chief and announce a better relief package for the public,” PM Shehbaz was quoted as saying by the JI in a post on X.
In response, Rehman said the announced relief package was “not acceptable in any way” and that the party would continue its struggle.
“The JI chief said the party has been protesting against the petroleum levy for the past one-and-a-half months and would not withdraw from the protest until the levy was abolished,” the statement said.
Rehman said he had told the prime minister that he would consult the party leadership over his request for a pause of a few days in the long march before making a decision.
وزیر اعظم شہباز شریف کا امیر جماعت اسلامی حافظ نعیم الرحمان سے رابطہ وزیر اعظم نے امیر جماعت اسلامی سے درخواست کی کہ مارچ کچھ دن ملتوی کردیں۔ عوام کے لیے ریلیف پیکج کا اعلان کیا ہے۔ وزیراعظم اعلان شدہ ریلیف پیکج کسی صورت قبول نہیں، ہم جدوجہد جاری رکھیں گے۔ امیر جماعت… pic.twitter.com/NslYkSiIDx
On Sunday, JI launched the party's Karachi-to-Islamabad " super train march " against the petroleum levy, "cruel" agreements with independent power producers (IPPs), warning that the ongoing campaign could intensify into a movement to oust the government if its demands were not accepted.
Read: JI raises alarm over delay in protest train
Thousands of JI workers and participants gathered at Karachi Cantonment Railway Station for the departure, while women office-bearers of the party bade farewell to the marchers with prayers.
Rehman said the caravan would reach Islamabad as the voice of the people's demands, while other caravans from Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan were also due to set off for the capital.
He said JI had chosen to take to the streets for the rights of the people. The party had staged a 35-day sit-in in Karachi, while sit-ins were continuing in Sukkur, Larkana and Hyderabad, with marches and protest sit-ins also under way in different parts of Punjab.
The PM’s Fuel Relief Scheme, announced on September 13 and rolled out across the country at midnight on September 16 amid a continuous rise in fuel prices due to a war in the Gulf, provides a Rs100-per-litre petrol subsidy to eligible motorcycles, rickshaws, other two- and three-wheelers, and cars of up to 800cc.
The prime minister directed the establishment of facilitation desks comprising administration officials, volunteers and petrol pump staff to assist citizens in easily obtaining the subsidy.
Read more: Fuel relief scheme to go nationwide at midnight tomorrow
He directed that personnel deployed at the facilitation desks should guide eligible citizens and provide them with all possible assistance in registration and other necessary procedures.
PM Shehbaz also asked the relevant authorities to remain proactive in creating public awareness about the scheme.

title: Afghan cyclist who disguised herself as man wins Asian Games silver
description: Hashimi hopes her medal inspires Afghan women to pursue their dreams
content:
Hashimi hopes her medal inspires Afghan women to pursue their dreams
An Afghan cyclist who disguised herself as a man to pursue her sporting dreams won an Asian Games silver medal on Tuesday, hoping it inspires other women in a country where Taliban authorities have sharply curtailed their freedoms.
Italy-based Fariba Hashimi powered home second in the women's road race near Nagoya in Japan, calling the triumph "something special".
"I can't explain my feelings now," said the 23-year-old, before reflecting on how she was attacked with stones and trained disguised as a man when she started out in the sport as a teenager along with sister Yulduz, who is also now a pro cyclist.
"I was born inside a country where the women who dream are getting attacked, and I'm really happy that I have fought against that," she said.
"I hope that the next generation will come here and represent their country without any fear."
The Taliban authorities returned to power in 2021 and have since imposed a series of rules limiting women's access to education and public life, including sport.
"They took away our freedom, they took away everything from us," said Hashimi, who hails from Faryab province in northern Afghanistan and left the country after the Taliban authorities took over.
"This silver medal can show a lot of resilience from Afghan women, and I'm really happy.
"I'm not alone, I know that behind me millions of women, from many countries, have the same dream and they are standing with me."
After fleeing Afghanistan with the help of Italian former world champion Alessandra Cappellotto, Hashimi relocated to Italy, where she now lives and trains.
She and her sister competed at the Paris Olympics two years ago, and the 2028 Los Angeles Games are now looming into view.
"I never want to give up and hopefully we can see (what can happen) again in Los Angeles," she said.
Hashimi reserved a special thanks for the Japanese team for playing a part in her silver medal.
"I'm here without a mechanic, without any preparation. We brought one guy with us from the national federation, and he just drove the car," she said.
"We were fixing the bike ourselves. I was the mechanic for myself. I was washing the bike myself.
"Thank you to the Japanese team. They were really, really nice to me, fixed my bike."

title: Trump set for whirlwind UN meetings with wars in Iran  Ukraine on agenda
description: US Israeli war against Iran particularly consequential  driving up fuel prices  dragging down    Trump approval ratings
content:
US-Israeli war against Iran particularly consequential, driving up fuel prices, dragging down ⁠Trump approval ratings
Donald Trump is set for a whirlwind schedule of meetings with leaders from four continents at ‌the UN General Assembly on Tuesday, against the backdrop of an unstable Middle East and a four-and-a-half-year-old war in Ukraine that shows no signs of abating despite the US president's repeated attempts at mediation.
Trump is expected to start the day with a speech to assembled delegates, before meeting with no fewer ​than 11 world leaders, bilaterally or in group settings. While the contents of his speech are unknown, Trump last year caused ​a stir with a combative speech, saying that their countries were "going to hell" for, among other things, ⁠climate policy and mass migration.
Read: PM Shehbaz arrives in New York to attend 81st UNGA session amid Middle East crisis
Later in the day, Trump will meet with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, Venezuela's ​interim leader Delcy Rodriguez, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen, and the representatives of the Gulf states of ​the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, Kuwait and Qatar.
In the evening, he may meet dozens more leaders, albeit briefly, during a leaders' reception. Trump met with French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday. Additions to his Tuesday schedule are possible.
The long list of foreign leader meetings reflects the US president's ​focus on foreign affairs during his second term, during which he has started multiple wars, questioned longstanding alliances, threatened allies with ​invasion and sought to broker well over a dozen conflicts, with mixed success.
The US-Israeli war against Iran has been particularly consequential, driving up fuel prices ‌globally, dragging down ⁠Trump's approval ratings and presenting a challenge for Republicans running in the November congressional midterm election. On Monday, a Reuters / Ipsos poll showed Trump's approval rating falling to an all-time low of 32%, as his fellow Republicans soured on his handling of the cost of living.
Read more: We will forcefully raise Iran's positions in international forums: Pezeshkian
Among the closely watched meetings will be the seven-way gathering with the Gulf leaders, many of whom are alarmed by the recent advances ​of the Houthis who ​have captured wide swathes of ⁠Yemen, attacked US ally Saudi Arabia and threatened shipping through the strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait.
Political allies and opponents will also be closely watching Trump's first-ever meeting with Venezuela's Rodriguez, who rose to power ​with the Trump administration's blessing after US forces snatched President Nicolas Maduro in January and took ​him to New ⁠York to face drug trafficking charges.
Trump's allies say the US is working with Rodriguez to open Venezuela's oil sector to US investment, but Democrats and some Republicans say his administration has not done enough to press for new elections in the South American nation.
During the meeting ⁠with the ​leaders of Denmark and Greenland, its overseas territory, Trump will ink an accord ​designed to increase US military presence on the island while limiting that of geopolitical adversaries. Danish and Greenland officials hope the accord will put an end to Trump's ​past comments suggesting he might take Greenland by force.

description: Green shirts continue strong run with victory over Nepal in second outing
content:
Green-shirts continue strong run with victory over Nepal in second outing
Pakistan on Tuesday continued to deliver when they whipped little known Nepal in their Group B men’s kabaddi match of the 20th Asian Games at the Tokai Citizen Gymnasium in Aichi Perfecture.
Nepal, who are not known for kabaddi, did a good job to extend some laudable resistance to the Green-shirts who have a strong legacy in the sport.
Pakistan won it 58-43. The victory also took the last edition’s bronze medallists Pakistan to the top of the group with four points from two wins.
Pakistan on Monday had crushed Malaysia 65-22 in their opener. Pakistan will now face Thailand on Wednesday before facing Iran.
Meanwhile in Group A show India crushed South Korea 63.31.
Japan, Chinese Taipei and Bangladesh are the other teams in the group.
Top two teams from each group will qualify for the semi-finals. India will defend the title. India had defeated Iran 42-32 in the final of the 2023 Asian Games held in Hangzhou.
