UNGA should restore global trust and end wars: Pezeshkian
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian showed hope that a UN General Assembly meeting convened under the banner of trust could restore confidence worldwide and work toward ending war and bloodshed, according to IRNA.
Speaking to reporters before departing for New York, Pezeshkian hoped that the world’s people would come to recognise the oppressive actions unfolding across the region.
President @drpezeshkian : UNGA should restore global trust and end wars https://t.co/FEFqbZHTWT pic.twitter.com/2fhETTY8UW
“We will express the oppression of the Iranian children in Minab and Lamerd and the brutality of the perpetrators of these crimes,” he added.
Human beings do not commit such acts, and these behaviours are a source of regret, he said.
Saudi Arabia restarts East-West oil pipeline, to resume exports from Yanbu, sources say
Saudi Arabia has restarted operations at its East-West Pipeline and could resume exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu later on Tuesday, three sources briefed on the matter said.
The pipeline was pumping at a low rate, two of them said.
State energy firm Saudi Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Drone attacks forced Saudi Arabia to shut its East-West Pipeline on September 13, halting crude loadings at the kingdom's Yanbu port.
Negotiations a separate battlefield; enemy lacks capacity for new conflict: IRGC spokesperson
The spokesperson for the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) said Iran was fully prepared for war but could also pursue negotiations if national interests required it, saying that talks can constitute “another battlefield.”
“Negotiation does not mean compromise; negotiation is another scene of war,” Second Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbisaid said in an interview with IRNA on Tuesday, adding that negotiations involve “war with words, arguments and diplomatic methods.”
Negotiations are another battlefield; enemy lacks capacity for new war: IRGC spokesperson https://t.co/QGNjSEFiYO pic.twitter.com/f46MZDD1Iq
He said the IRGC has prepared itself for a prolonged war and that Iran’s Armed Forces are fully ready for war.
“What is correct in this matter is that we should have 100-percent readiness for war, and we have this capability and readiness. [Iranian] Armed Forces are now 100 percent ready to fight, and the IRGC has prepared itself for a long war. But this does not mean rejecting negotiations.”
Mohebbi said that decisions on war and negotiations were not made solely by the IRGC, clarifying that such decisions were made within the framework of Iran’s political system and under the command of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces.
The spokesperson said Iran’s approach should be determined by national interests.
“We must see when and through what action our national interests are served. If our national interests require us to fight, we must fight. If our national interests require us to negotiate alongside the war, we must negotiate,” he said.
He maintained that Iran should have both military preparedness and the ability to use diplomacy, describing them as complementary instruments in pursuing national interests.
Separately, Iranian Navy commander Rear Admiral Shahram Irani said that any aggression against national interests would trigger a “firm, decisive and appropriate response,” according to Press TV .
We will forcefully raise Iran's positions in international forums: Pezeshkian
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian left for New York on Tuesday morning to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, saying that the Iranian delegation will "forcefully raise Iran's positions in international forums", according to ISNA .
پزشکیان پیش از عزیمت به نیویورک: با قدرت، مواضع ایران را در مجامع بین‌المللی مطرح خواهیم کرد -مواردی که در سازمان ملل مطرح خواهیم کرد، بیان مظلومیت ملت ایران، جنا،یت‌هایی که رخ داده و بی‌اعتمادی‌هایی است که ایجاد شده است ۱/۲ pic.twitter.com/u4YrwZBfRw
"The issues we will raise at the United Nations are expressing the oppressed state of the Iranian nation, the crimes that have occurred, and the distrust that has been created," he is reported to have said.
He added that Iran "went to the negotiating table several times and signed agreements", but the agreements were not adhered to and were "trampled underfoot."
Separately, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that they will "express Iran's legitimate positions from the UN podium," referring to the "oppression of the Iranian people, the martyrs of Iran, the martyrs of the Minab school, and at their forefront, our martyred leader and commander."
عراقچی: در تریبون سازمان ملل مواضع بر حق ایران را بیان می‌کنیم امسال پس از جنگی که صورت گرفت، طبیعی است که تریبون سازمان ملل، محلی خواهد بود برای اینکه مظلومیت مردم ایران، شهدای ایران، شهدای مدرسه میناب و در راس آنها قائد و رهبر شهیدمان بیان شود ۱/۲ https://t.co/dF3liUcguZ https://t.co/Gen0SDLtX9
According to Al Jazeera , Pezeshkian added that "people cannot be forced into submission by force."
BREAKING: Iran’s President Pezeshkian says ‘people cannot be forced into submission through force’ as he flies to attend the UN General Assembly 🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/VFabQ58AG8 pic.twitter.com/TC4cSICLmY
'Public's memory' will not forget who initiated 'war of aggression': Iranian FM spokesperson
Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said on Tuesday that the US was attempting to shift blame onto Iran for rising fuel prices, adding that the public would not forget "who actually initiated the war of aggression, and whose actions created the crisis that led to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz."
U.S. officials blame Iran for rising fuel prices, as if the public's memory is short enough to forget who actually initiated the war of aggression, and whose actions created the crisis that led to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the disruption of commercial shipping.…
He likened the US' shifting of blame to how "Hitler similarly framed his invasion of Poland as a defensive action."
Read: All Iranian airlines to shut down worldwide by Sept 23, US Treasury chief says
"When the instigator of an unlawful 'war of choice' blames the victim for the fallout, should this be viewed as 'strategic brilliance', or is it simply a textbook symptom of 'The March of Folly'?!"
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said trust in the United Nations has been lost, according to Al Jazeera , which cited his Telegram channel.
He made the remarks upon his arrival in New York before the UN General Assembly (UNGA) meeting.
“This visit takes place following the cowardly war waged against us by the US and the Zionist regime, the subsequent developments, and in reality, amidst a situation that effectively remains a state of war,” he said.
“Naturally, our primary objective is to utilise a major international platform to defend the legitimacy, rights, and interests of the Iranian people."
Araghchi stated that the UN had lost credibility and trust due to its failure to uphold world peace and security, and pointed out that the UNGA is set to open on Tuesday under the theme “restoring trust”.
“This reflects a universal acknowledgement that trust in the organisation has eroded, or vanished entirely, due to its failure to effectively maintain international peace and security,” Araghchi said.
“Certain nations arrogate to themselves the right to act with impunity, disregarding international institutions, international law, and even the collective conscience of humanity; they claim immunity for themselves and their allies.”
“Consequently, we see a criminal entity like the Zionist regime given free rein to commit whatever acts it chooses, while Western and European nations, which style themselves as champions of human rights and humanitarian law, remain silent.”
Primary objective to advocate for 'legitimacy, rights, and interests' of Iran's people: Araghchi
Araghchi said in comments carried by IRNA that the primary objective in taking part in the summit in New York was to "advocate for the legitimacy, rights, and interests of the Iranian people."
As he began his journey to New York, Iranian Foreign Minister @araghchi stated that their primary objective is to take part in a significant international forum in order to advocate for the legitimacy, rights, and interests of the Iranian people. pic.twitter.com/zPNQ7pbnkU
Earlier, Baghaei released a statement on X regarding Araghchi's visit, saying that "In addition to participating in the various agenda items of the United Nations General Assembly [UNGA]... Foreign Minister will hold talks and consultations with a large number of officials and foreign ministers attending the summit."
ورود وزیر امور خارجه به نیویورک جهت شرکت در اجلاس سالانه مجمع عمومی سازمان ملل متحد سيد عباس عراقچی وزیر امور خارجه جمهوری اسلامی ایران، بعد از ظهر امروز دوشنبه در راس یک هیات دیپلماتیک برای مشارکت در مباحث اجلاس سالانه مجمع عمومی سازمان ملل متحد وارد نیویورک مقر سازمان ملل…
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in New York on Monday to participate in the 81st session of the UNGA.
Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran @araghchi , arrived in New York on Monday local time to participate in the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly. pic.twitter.com/IJsgPyKkOd
The top diplomat, who is leading a high-level delegation, was received at John F. Kennedy International Airport by Gholamhossein Darzi, Iran’s permanent representative and charge d’affaires to the United Nations, according to Iran's state-owned news agency IRNA .
ورود عراقچی به نیویورک https://t.co/7DO4GO03dQ pic.twitter.com/sQ5T6OtnWj
On his way to New York, Araghchi made a brief stop in Doha, where he held discussions with Qatari officials about the latest developments in the region.
Read more: Naqvi assures Iranian president of Pakistan's determination to expand multisector cooperation
Foreign Minister @araghchi in New York to take part in the UN General Assembly's annual meeting. pic.twitter.com/hKe04c9sSd
During the summit, he is expected to meet and consult with several world leaders and officials on the sidelines.
China says it opposes ‘illegal’ US sanctions on Iranian airlines
China said on Tuesday it opposed “illegal” US sanctions on Iranian airlines, a day after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent threatened potential measures in a televised interview.
Bessent told CNBC on Monday that “all the Iranian airlines will be shut down around the world” in a matter of days under the weight of American sanctions, as the Trump administration seeks to ramp up pressure on Tehran.
Beijing, a top economic partner and diplomatic backer of Iran, slammed the threats on Tuesday, calling such measures “illegal”.
“China consistently opposes illegal unilateral sanctions that lack a basis in international law or authorisation from the UN Security Council,” foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a news conference, according to AFP .
Saudi Arabia sends all-clear after alert issued for southern province
Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence sent an all-clear on Tuesday after issuing an alert for potential danger in the southern Najran province.
Civil Defence said the danger had passed in Najran, without specifying the nature of the threat.
The agency earlier issued an emergency alert for potential danger in Najran through the National Early Warning Platform.
On Saturday, the Civil Defence issued alerts for potential danger in the capital Riyadh, Al-Kharj and Farasan provinces in the country’s south. It came amid escalating tensions with the Houthi group in Yemen, which has announced what it called a “maritime blockade” on Saudi shipping in the Red Sea and launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi territory.
Macron, Trump hold talks on Ukraine, Red Sea, Hormuz
French President Emmanuel Macron said Monday that he and US President Donald Trump discussed diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, increase shipping through the waterway and ease tensions in the Middle East.
Speaking after their meeting in New York, Macron said the two leaders also discussed securing oil routes in the Red Sea without escalating tensions, as well as support for Ukraine and efforts to address energy-related issues in the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
There is a shared desire to "do everything to open (...) Hormuz" and "free up volumes," he said.
They also discussed the need to help Ukrainians "even faster and stronger" in terms of interceptors for defence.
The two leaders also revisited "the initiatives that could be taken to find a moratorium on energy issues."
Macron said he was scheduled to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and that further exchanges were planned for Tuesday with the American and Ukrainian sides.
Iran weapon test on US aircraft carrier 'went well': IRGC spokesperson
An IRGC spokesperson said that the test of a "new Iranian weapon" on a US aircraft carrier "went well", according to ISNA .
سخنگوی سپاه: تست سلاح جدید ایرانی روی ناو هواپیمابر آمریکایی به خوبی جواب داد -اگر تهاجم جدیدی صورت بگیرد غیر از این سلاح، سلاح‌های دیگری را هم به میدان خواهیم آرود pic.twitter.com/MsvtiWrbER
"If a new aggression occurs, besides this weapon, we will bring other weapons into the field as well," he said in the interview.
Latest Yemen clashes kill more than 150: Military sources to AFP
Fighting in Yemen between the Iran-backed Houthis and government forces supported by Saudi Arabia has killed 154 people in the past two days, military sources from both sides told AFP on Tuesday. "The death toll from Saudi airstrikes, clashes and artillery fire in the governorates of Taiz, Al-Jawf, Marib and Saada stands at 118," Houthi military sources said, while government sources reported 36 killed in their ranks.
Saudi airstrikes on port city of Mokha kill 6, says Houthi-affiliated news agency
Saudi airstrikes on the strategic Red Sea port city of Mokha killed at least six people and injured eight others, according to a report on Tuesday by the Houthi-affiliated Saba news agency.
“Six civilians, including two children and a woman, were killed and eight others, including a child and a woman, were injured in Saudi-led airstrikes on Mokha,” Saba said.
💥 Saudi airstrikes on the strategic Red Sea port city of Mokha killed at least six people, according to media report Eight others injured, including woman and child https://t.co/K53wWwMgnr pic.twitter.com/kzbSXsxp5q
The Houthis are fighting Yemen's internationally recognised government in a civil war, with Saudi Arabia backing the government.
In recent days, the Houthis have claimed responsibility for drone and ballistic missile attacks targeting the Saudi capital Riyadh as well as energy facilities along the country's Red Sea coast.
G7 foreign ministers call on Iran to stop arming Houthis
G7 foreign ministers called on Iran on Tuesday “to end its arming of and support for the Houthis,” warning that the escalating attacks threaten international trade and global stability, according to Al Jazeera .
BREAKING: G7 foreign ministers have called on Iran to stop arming and supporting Yemen’s Houthis, warning that the escalating attacks threaten international trade and global stability. 🔴 More on https://t.co/OwhgaIGyGh pic.twitter.com/k5sEeCF1H8
They also called on the Houthis to "immediately cease all military actions, all threats and attacks against civilian shipping, and to return to the political process in good faith,” the leaders representing Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States said in a statement.
They alleged that Tehran was in violation of past UN Security Council resolutions.
US eyes $5B fund to rebuild Gulf energy sites hit in war against Iran
The US has floated committing $5 billion to a new multinational fund aimed at repairing Gulf energy facilities hit during the war with Iran and helping regional states find export routes that bypass the Strait of Hormuz, according to a media report on Monday.
The Wall Street Journal , citing US and Middle Eastern officials and documents it reviewed, said Washington is seeking a matching $5 billion contribution from eight Middle Eastern partners -- Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Iraq and Jordan -- which would bring the total to $10 billion.
The initiative is called the Partnership for Allied Trust and Construction (Pact).
The US Development Finance Corporation would run the fund, according to the report. The agency's past work has mostly centred on developing countries rather than rich Gulf monarchies.
US officials stressed that discussions are still underway, the terms may change, and it remains uncertain whether any country will sign on.
Some regional officials viewed the plan as an effort to portray the Strait of Hormuz as less critical and show a united front against Tehran, the Journal said. They also argued that funding reconstruction before a peace deal would be premature because Iran could target new facilities.
"This strategy has risk written all over it," said Bilal Saab of the consulting firm TRENDS US.
Since the seven-month war began, Iranian missiles and drones have struck dozens of refineries, oil fields and gas export terminals, according to the report. A drone attack earlier this month also knocked out Saudi Arabia's bypass pipeline, sending more crude through the Hormuz Strait and pushing tanker rates to record highs.
Umer Karim, a Gulf security researcher at the University of Birmingham, warned that the scheme could make some participants dependent on others and strain bilateral relations.
Repair costs are estimated at tens of billions of dollars, The Wall Street Journal added.
France working on UN Security Council resolution on Hormuz: diplomatic source
France is working on a new UN Security Council resolution to unblock the Strait of Hormuz, a diplomatic source told reporters, AFP reported.
“France wants to work with the Americans and its partners on a Security Council resolution guaranteeing freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz,” the source said.
In April, Russia and China vetoed a draft resolution — spearheaded by Bahrain and backed by Gulf states and the United States — that also called for the Strait of Hormuz to be unblocked.
France seeks India's role on Hormuz Strait, welcomes Pakistan's Iran-US mediation
France sought to work with India to ensure freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and welcomed Pakistan’s mediation efforts between Iran and the US, according to the French Foreign Ministry on Monday.
Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot met separately with his Indian and Pakistani counterparts on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York.
Also read: PM Shehbaz arrives in New York to attend 81st UNGA session amid Middle East crisis
During his meeting with Indian External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar, the two ministers “underscored the imperative of ensuring freedom of navigation” in the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Barrot proposed that India work jointly with France on the issue, which is “crucial to the stability and prosperity of Europe and Asia."
He also recalled the Franco-British initiative launched to ensure freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.
Barrot and Jaishankar reiterated France and India’s commitment to international law and their joint support for “effective and reformed multilateralism.”
They also recalled their intention to reform the UN Security Council.
The two ministers reaffirmed their support for a ceasefire in Ukraine and for “a comprehensive, just and lasting peace in accordance with international law.”
They also welcomed progress in the “comprehensive and special Franco-Indian strategic partnership,” particularly in defence, new technologies and higher education.
Barrot separately met Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, with whom he discussed regional developments.
Also read: FM Dar stresses importance of GSP+ status in meeting with EU foreign policy chief
Barrot welcomed Pakistan’s mediation efforts between Iran and the US and stressed the need for “the most inclusive negotiations possible” to help secure energy supplies in particular and “sustainably address the threats posed by Iran in the nuclear, ballistic and regional spheres.”
The two ministers agreed to continue developing bilateral relations, particularly in university cooperation, cultural cooperation and sustainable development.
EU's Kallas says Red Sea mission needs more than 10 warships
The European Union's naval mission to protect shipping in the Red Sea would need to boost its numbers to more than 10 warships, its foreign policy chief said on Monday, adding that for now there were not that many in the area.
The EU's Aspides mission was launched in 2024 to protect shipping from attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis, and diplomats have said there are currently six warships operating.
"When Aspides was put in place, then the indication was that it needs at least 10 ships. The situation, I think, is even more grave right now," Kaja Kallas told reporters on the sidelines of the annual gathering of world leaders at the United Nations.
The Houthis have made rapid advances in recent weeks along the Red Sea coast, further complicating routes in a region that also includes the Strait of Hormuz, where traffic had already dwindled because of the US-Iran war.
Italy, one of the key countries in the Aspides mission, announced on Thursday it was preparing a naval mission in the area for its own ships, saying it could not wait for the EU to respond to the new crisis.
Kallas said the Houthi attacks were affecting European interests and impacting the global economy.
"The EU operation Aspides is making a crucial contribution to security in the region and global shipping, but the operation needs more naval assets and more air assets to address the increased level of threats in the region," she said.
Kallas sent a letter to the EU's 27 member states on September 19 asking them to up their contributions. The issue would be discussed at upcoming defence and foreign ministers' meetings, she said in the letter.
"This situation, which is still evolving as we speak, is already affecting European interests with repercussions on our supply chains and could have implications for our ability to support our economies which were already hit by rising fuel prices," she said in the letter.
"For the moment, although the Houthis communicate that they would only target Saudi-linked interests, there is uncertainty over their course of action with respect to vessels that transit through the Strait. Regardless, they are now in a better position to potentially harm maritime shipping."
UK's Burnham agrees to Saudi request for refuelling support
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday he had agreed to a request from Saudi Arabia to provide defensive ​air-to-air refuelling for a limited time period, a move ‌he described as helping to stabilise the wider region.
Riyadh requested support after the Houthis, who control the most populous parts of Yemen, intensified their attacks on Saudi ​Arabia, a new front in the wider war that began ​with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in late February.
"We ⁠have received a request from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia ​for military support, and on the advice of the defence secretary and ​the foreign secretary, last night I agreed to that request for defensive air-to-air refuelling," he told reporters as he travelled to New York for a meeting ​of the United Nations General Assembly.
"Because, of course, Saudi Arabia has ​been experiencing attacks... and we need to keep those pathways open, and hence our ‌agreement ⁠to the request," he said.
Britain and Saudi Arabia have been close military allies for decades, with Britain serving as one of the kingdom's largest arms suppliers.
Earlier this year, Britain deployed its Sky Sabre air ​defence system to ​Saudi Arabia to ⁠help protect it from Iranian missile attacks during the US-Israeli conflict with Iran.
For the new air-to-air refuelling ​support, Britain will deploy one Voyager plane in ​the coming ⁠days.
"That is a time-limited agreement in terms of the assistance that we will provide, but we will keep it under review," he said, adding ⁠that ​Britain was "playing our part" in the Middle ​East also by supporting efforts to keep the Strait of Hormuz open.

title: Uproar in K P Assembly over minister  abduction
description: Uproar in Assembly over minister  abduction
content:
Attack on Shakeel Khan also condemned; Speaker demands loyalty oath for federal officers
The alleged abduction of provincial minister Fazal Shakoor from the Peshawar Toll Plaza and attack on fellow minister Shakeel Khan dominated an emergency session of the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Assembly on Monday, prompting Speaker Babar Saleem Swati to demand a mandatory loyalty oath for federal officers deputed to the province.
Law Minister Aftab Alam informed the House that Shakeel Khan had been targeted the previous day, after which an FIR was registered against him, while Fazal Shakoor was abducted in broad daylight. "What message is being sent to the provincial executive, that we have no importance? Alam asked. He also cited the picking up of MPA Fatehul Mulk from Islamabad as further evidence of pressure tactics by forces seeking to convey that the PTI government and party have no status.
The late-night session, chaired by Swati and attended by Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and the Chief Secretary, heard government members charge that the arrests, cases and the tearing of PTI banners were designed to derail the planned 27 September long march.
"On 27 September we will come out for real freedom in any case," Alam declared, insisting the march would remain completely peaceful. He recalled that the provincial government, upon assuming office, had decided against revenge, provided extra funds to the police and raised the martyrs' package from Rs4 million to Rs11 million. Despite past shortcomings, the government had shown restraint; continued criminal negligence by police would, however, invite the strictest action.
Provincial ministers Riaz Khan described the incidents against ministers and MPAs as deeply regrettable, saying the open violation of law left little room for dialogue.
Speaker Swati separately pressed for a formal loyalty oath. When the Advocate General confirmed that the Police Act 2017 contains no such requirement for officers posted on deputation, Swati insisted the provision be added. He accused the current Inspector General of having already violated the law on two occasions.
Interior Minister Tariq Saeed informed the House that he had directed the IGP to inquire into the Shakeel Khan case and to ensure registration of an FIR in the Fazal Shakoor abduction. On the Speaker's instruction, a committee under the minister's supervision is to oversee a transparent investigation.
Swati observed that despite the presence of police and district administration, elected members continued to face abduction attempts by armed groups. "These incidents create the impression that martial law is in force in the province," he remarked, adding that guns breed hatred while the people of K-P prefer dialogue. He reminded the House that legislation protecting members' privileges had already been passed and circulated to the Chief Secretary, IGP, judges and deputy commissioners, and ordered strict implementation of the rules under the Constitution.

title: Tarar warns PTI against march on Islamabad
description: Tarar warns PTI against march on Islamabad
content:
Federal Information Minister Attaullah Tarar has said that Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) never stages peaceful protests, asserting that peaceful citizens do not leave their homes carrying spiked sticks. He declared that such groups will not be allowed to enter Islamabad.
Addressing party workers and speaking to the media in Kohat, Tarar said the city's atmosphere was one of mourning following the recent incident.
Tarar questioned the whereabouts of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi during the Kohat incident, alleging that the provincial chief executive was busy scoring political points on the streets of Lahore. "He has time for the politics of chaos but none for the people of his own province. He circled over the area in a helicopter for 15 minutes and left. What has he done for education, health and public welfare?" the minister asked.
He accused the PTI-led provincial government of knowing only how to post on social media, pointing out the absence of even a forensic laboratory for police facilities. Contracts, he claimed, were awarded to favourites while kickbacks were collected, and new records of corruption were being set in the province. Tarar made it clear that no one would be permitted to shut down Islamabad and that armed groups would not be allowed to advance towards the federal capital.

title: Shafi Jan rejects Naqvi s PTI protest warnings
description: Shafi Jan rejects Naqvi s PTI protest warnings
content:
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Minister for Information and Science & Information Technology Shafi Jan on Monday strongly reacted to Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi's press conference, urging him not to turn the funerals of martyrs into a subject of political rhetoric.
"Using the funerals of martyrs for political point-scoring is highly regrettable," Shafi Jan said.
The provincial minister claimed that the continuous press conferences by federal ministers made it clear they were severely frightened of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's protest and long march scheduled for September 27.
"When the federal minister talks about the law, he should also remember the fundamental rights of the people guaranteed in the Constitution," he added.
Shafi Jan said the federal government must also answer questions regarding the deprivation of Imran Khan's basic constitutional and legal rights, the ban on meetings with him, and the non-implementation of court orders.
Referring to Naqvi's statement that a permanent strategy would be devised to deal with PTI, the K-P minister asked why the same permanent strategy had not been formulated for the stability of the national economy.
"Mohsin Naqvi may have forgotten that the damage to the national economy is not because of PTI but due to the poor policies of their so-called experienced economic team," he said.

description: Over 5m displaced Sudanese return home
content:

"Many are going back to a country still wracked by conflict, where damaged homes, schools and clinics cannot meet the needs," the UN's International Organization for Migration said in a statement. "Without urgent support, families risk being uprooted again." AFP

title: Berlin s far left vote winners reject anti semitism charges
description: Berlin s far left vote winners reject anti semitism charges
content:
Germany's far-left Die Linke party, winners of Berlin city-state elections, on Monday rejected charges that pro-Palestinian activists among its base have veered into antisemitism or hate for Israel.
The party faced criticism about the presence of two controversial figures at a victory party Sunday night, including an allegedly militant activist and the head of an extended family with Middle Eastern roots that is often linked to organised crime.
"Celebrating violence and terrorism is absolutely unacceptable," said Die Linke lead candidate Elif Eralp, who hopes to become Berlin mayor in a coalition with the Social Democrats (SPD) and Greens.

title: US  Denmark  Greenland to sign security deal
description: US  Denmark  Greenland to sign security deal
content:
The United States, Denmark and Greenland will on Tuesday sign the announced US security deal for Greenland on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, Denmark's government said.
US President Donald Trump said last Friday that the arrangement will give America "permanent control" over security for Greenland, an autonomous Danish territory in the Arctic that he has long coveted.
The office of Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said that she, Trump and Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen would sign the deal at 1430 GMT in the UN building in New York.
Frederiksen said Monday that the agreement, which has not been published, "recognises" the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Denmark, as well as the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination.
"It is a good agreement from a Danish point of view," she told Danish radio DR from New York.
"And when it benefits the Nordic countries and security in the Arctic region, it also benefits NATO and Europe."
Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has repeatedly insisted that the United States needs to control Greenland for strategic reasons, alarming NATO ally Denmark and sparking fierce pushback from the alliance.
According to Washington, the agreement ensures that China and Russia will not be able to establish military bases in Greenland or carry out sensitive investments there without its consent.
"This is something we have agreed on with the Americans for a very, very long time: the Arctic region, the North Atlantic, constitute an important defence zone for all members of the NATO alliance," Frederiksen said. AFP

title: Polio free Punjab needs a united effort
description: Polio free Punjab needs a united effort
content:
Parents, health workers, global partners pursue virus eradication
The Punjab CM's Focal Person for Polio Uzma Kardar has said that a continued partnership among the government, parents, frontline health workers and international partners was essential to achieving the goal of eradication of the virus.
"The support of our international partners is extremely important in our collective efforts to end polio and protect every child," she added at the inauguration of a special vaccination campaign in 13 districts of the province to protect them against poliovirus and prevent its reintroduction.
The campaign was inaugurated at the Nawaz Sharif Centre for Excellence, with the participation of international partners and representatives of the Girls Guides, teachers and young leaders.
"There is no room for complacency or negligence in the fight against polio. Every eligible child must receive the full protection offered by vaccination," the focal person said.
She urged parents to ensure that all children under five receive polio drops during every campaign.
Punjab Emergency Operations Centre Coordinator Khalid Parvaiz said directions had been issued to ensure effective monitoring and coverage during the campaign.
"Given the risk of poliovirus reintroduction, no child should be missed during the campaign. Reaching children in hard to reach areas, mobile populations and those who may have been missed is our priority," he said.
He said particular attention was being given to microplanning, training, field team performance and monitoring to ensure that every campaign was implemented effectively.
"Keeping Punjab free of poliovirus requires every campaign to be fully effective. Vaccinating every eligible child, strong surveillance and a rapid response are essential to sustaining progress against polio," he said.
He reiterated that polio eradication was a shared national responsibility and called for continued cooperation among communities, parents, health workers, government institutions and partners to ensure that every child was protected from polio.
The campaign that began on Monday will continue till September 27 in Lahore, while the duration varies in other districts. Polio teams will visit homes to vaccinate children under five, with particular focus on hard to reach communities, mobile populations and children who may have been missed earlier.
Polio vaccination teams will visit households to administer vaccine drops to children, while fixed and transit teams will also perform duties at health centres, bus terminals, railway stations and other important locations. Mobile, fixed and transit teams have been constituted for the campaign, while area in-charges and monitoring officers at the union council level will supervise the campaign. Special arrangements have been made for effective monitoring of polio teams, verification of vaccination coverage and reaching children who may have been missed. Particular attention will be given to high-risk areas, nomadic settlements and children who have received no dose of polio vaccine, ensuring that no child is left without vaccination.
Instructions have been issued to maintain effective field monitoring to achieve the assigned target.

content:

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah on Monday launched a seven-day anti-polio campaign across the province, warning that the threat of the crippling disease had not been eliminated and urging parents to ensure that every child under five receives the vaccine.
The campaign will run from September 21 to 27 across all 30 districts of Sindh, targeting around 10 million children under five. A full campaign will be conducted in 23 districts, while seven districts will receive partial coverage according to programme requirements.
Speaking at the inauguration ceremony at the Rotary Club Community Centre in Gulistan-e-Jauhar, CM Shah said Pakistan and Afghanistan remained the only countries where wild poliovirus continued to circulate.
Pakistan reported 31 polio cases last year compared with 21 in Afghanistan, he said. So far this year, Pakistan has reported four cases - one in Sujawal and three in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa - while Afghanistan has reported 29 cases.
"Although we have made significant progress towards eradication, our work is not yet complete," CM Shah said, stressing that the presence of the virus anywhere in the world remained a threat to children everywhere.
He said environmental surveillance in Sindh had shown improvement, with the positivity rate falling from 62% in August to 20%. Of six positive samples detected during the month, four were reported from Karachi Division and two from Hyderabad Division.
More than 80,000 trained vaccinators, social mobilisers and supervisors will take part in the campaign, while more than 26,000 police personnel, including around 2,300 female constables, have been deployed to provide security.
"There is no room for complacency in the fight against polio," CM Shah said, urging parents to have their children vaccinated during every campaign.
The chief minister also visited the centre's prosthetics unit, where polio-affected children are provided artificial limbs and callipers. He met Huma, a polio survivor who lost the use of both legs, and was briefed on Rotary International's assistance in providing her with prosthetic legs.
Talking to the media, CM Shah said he preferred to personally inaugurate polio campaigns to demonstrate the government's commitment to eradication. He appreciated the support of the Gates Foundation, UNICEF, Rotary International and other national and international partners.

title: City sizzles past 9 year September heat record
description: City sizzles past 9 year September heat record
content:
Mercury hits 40.7°C as humidity makes feel even hotter
September has turned into a furnace for Karachi, with the metropolis enduring its hottest September day in nine years as the mercury soared to 40.7°C on Monday.
The sweltering heat, compounded by rising humidity, pushed the heat index several degrees above the actual temperature, leaving Karachiites to endure conditions far hotter than the thermometer suggested.
The temperature recorded at the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD)'s Pehlwan Goth weather station surpassed the previous September high of 40.5°C recorded in 2017, while Karachi's all-time September record remains 43°C, recorded on September 30, 1951. According to PMD spokesperson Anjum Nazir Zaigham, the city had experienced a steady rise in temperatures over the past several days after relatively moderate weather at the beginning of September.
He told The Express Tribune that Monday's temperature was the highest recorded in September since 2017, when the maximum temperature had reached 40.5°C. However, Karachi's all-time September heat record remains 43°C, recorded on September 30, 1951, Zaigham said.
Temperatures varied across the city's weather stations, with Jinnah Terminal recording 41.2°C, Gulistan-e-Jauhar 41°C, Sharae Faisal 39.5°C and Maripur 39°C. The lowest maximum temperature of 34.5°C was recorded at the Bin Qasim weather station.
Zaigham attributed the recent spell of intense heat to a circulation that had developed over the Arabian Sea, which altered wind patterns. He said weak southwesterly sea breezes had also contributed to the rise in temperatures.
The PMD forecast that temperatures could reach 38°C on Tuesday, while the intensity of the heat is expected to ease from Wednesday, when the maximum temperature could fall to around 35°C.
According to the PMD's Early Warning Centre, Karachi's weather is expected to remain hot and humid on Tuesday and Wednesday. Humidity could rise to 55%, making temperatures feel several degrees higher than the actual readings. Sea breezes are expected to continue, accompanied by winds from the west.
Other parts of Sindh will also remain in the grip of hot weather. Maximum temperatures of 42°C were recorded in Shaheed Benazirabad, Khairpur and Hyderabad city, while Chhor recorded 41.5°C.

title: College directorate unsealed after four days
description: College directorate unsealed after four days
content:
Offices resume activities, legal teams to resolve Education Complex dispute
The Rawalpindi College Directorate was temporarily unsealed on Monday, Sept 21, after remaining sealed for four days. Deputy Commissioner Nadeem Nasir played a key role in getting the building reopened.
The legal teams of the Evacuee Trust Property Board (ETPB) and the College Directorate will consult each other to resolve the legal issues, while the dispute over the historic Education Complex building housing the College Directorate has been temporarily resolved.
On the directions of Deputy Commissioner Nadeem Nasir, the ETPB and the FIA unsealed the Education Complex.
Director Colleges Professor Dr Shehnaz Mohsin Sial and the All Pakistan Clerks Association (APCA) met the deputy commissioner on Monday and requested him to get the College Directorate unsealed.
The deputy commissioner directed the ETPB to immediately unseal the College Directorate, which was temporarily restored. The College Directorate will become a party to the case involving the ETPB.
Director Colleges Professor Dr Shehnaz Mohsin told the deputy commissioner that the Education Department had purchased the building from the ETPB in 1970 for Rs180,000. She also presented the deputy commissioner with the bank challan and receipt for the amount paid.
Following talks with the director colleges and APCA, the deputy commissioner directed the ETPB to unseal the College Directorate. FIA and police personnel left the premises after the directorate was unsealed on Monday afternoon, and the College Directorate was completely opened at 3pm, with office work also resuming.
From Tuesday, Sept 22, routine office activities of colleges and educational offices will resume at the Education Complex.
Earlier, the legal battle between the School Education Department and the ETPB was being fought in courts. The Higher Education Commission's College Directorate will now formally become a party to the case. The parties will accept whatever decision the court makes regarding the dispute, and the ETPB will not seal the College Directorate by force in future.
Director Colleges Professor Dr Shehnaz said the deputy commissioner had made an excellent decision.

title: Smartphones reshape children s lives
description: Smartphones reshape children s lives
content:
Social media, modern technology and Wi-Fi facilities have completely transformed the lives of children and elderly people.
According to experts, smart TVs and cinemas were popular in the past. Television provided an opportunity for every member of a family to sit together, while elders consulted their children, discussed different issues and tried to find solutions to them. However, smartphones, the internet and Wi-Fi have changed the culture of human life.
An elderly woman, Mukhtar Begum, said her son lived in London and she asked him to bring her a phone with a large screen.
"I spend a lot of time on my phone. It often happens that I pick up the phone absent-mindedly and then keep scrolling without realising how much time has passed," she said.
"Everyone remains worried about this habit of mine. After reciting the Holy Quran and offering prayers, the smartphone has become a part of my life during my free time."
Talking to The Express Tribune, she said her grandsons told her that she was always looking at her phone and asked them not to do the same, leaving her with no answer.
According to a survey, people aged 50 or above who use social media said, "It has become a kind of epidemic. We have become addicted to scrolling. The use of social media increased during the lockdown to pass the time."
Maryam, a nurse working at a private hospital, said she watched news, sports and fashion videos on social media during her free time while on night duty.
A few days ago, she had limited her use and also deleted some social media apps from her phone, but she said she could not pass the time.

title: Stroke patients get new lease on life
description: Stroke patients get new lease on life
content:
Holy Family Hospital's Stroke Centre saves 150 patients from lifelong disability
The Stroke Centre at Holy Family Hospital has saved 150 people who reached the hospital on time after suffering a stroke from lifelong disability caused by paralysis.
Patients brought to the Stroke Centre were administered TPA injections to prevent the formation of blood clots.
According to sources, the stroke centre was established in a section of the emergency department of Holy Family Hospital in 2024 on the directions of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz.
Patients brought to the centre within three to four hours of suffering a stroke are given a TPA injection as a treatment to prevent the stroke attack. The injection prevents a blood clot from forming in the brain of a stroke patient, helping protect the patient from paralysis. The patient recovers within three to four days and is discharged home.
Since the establishment of the Stroke Centre at Holy Family Hospital in 2024, 150 patients who were brought to the hospital within three to four hours of suffering a stroke have been administered injections to help them recover from the attack, keeping them safe from paralysis.
Holy Family Hospital Medical Superintendent Dr Ijaz Butt said a team of specialist doctors was working at the hospital's Stroke Centre under the supervision of Dr Mohammad Fateen Rashid, head of the neurology department.
He said patients brought to the Stroke Centre were not only given the TPA injection free of cost but were also provided complete free treatment before being discharged home. They were also given awareness about ways to remain safe from stroke attacks.
On the other hand, the Punjab government has approved the establishment of the first 100-bed cancer treatment tower at Holy Family Hospital (HFH), the largest hospital in the city, for patients across Rawalpindi Division.
A cryoablation machine for cancer patients has already arrived in Rawalpindi.
The Punjab chief minister has approved the construction of the 100-bed cancer treatment tower at HFH, for which the relevant departments have formally begun preparing the PC-I.
Sources said, at a video-link meeting chaired by the Punjab health secretary on the chief minister's directives, representatives of the Health Department, Communication and Works Department and other relevant departments were informed that cancer treatment towers would be constructed at HFH for Rawalpindi Division and at government hospitals in Faisalabad, Sargodha and Bahawalpur.
They said, before completion of the construction work, the appointment of specialist doctors and staff and procurement of the necessary equipment would be completed so that treatment could begin at the towers immediately after their construction.
Meanwhile, a cryoablation machine for patients suffering from breast, lung, liver and kidney cancers has already been delivered to HFH. Its installation is currently under way.
Once its test run is completed, formal registration will begin for patients suffering from the four types of cancer for treatment through the machine.

title: Pro Putin party wins polls
description: Pro Putin party wins polls
content:
The pro-Putin ruling United Russia party won a record number of seats in the national parliament, according to near-complete official election results on Monday, while the anti-war Yabloko party appeared to have won a tiny foothold in one regional parliament.
President Vladimir Putin had cast the three-day election to the State Duma - the first since Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022 - as a test of support for the war. Elections for some regional parliaments and governors were held at the same time.
In a tightly controlled political system, which critics say does not tolerate genuine dissent, under which many of Yabloko's candidates were barred, few surprises were expected.
But political analysts said it was important to the authorities that the process itself was seen to be relatively smooth. Officials from Putin down had cast the vote as a way of showing enemies that Russia was united.
With over 95% of the vote counted, Ella Pamfilova, chair of the Central Electoral Commission, said United Russia had scored 57.83%, up from the 49.8% that it won in the last parliamentary election, in 2021.
United Russia was set to control 355 seats or nearly 80% of the 450-seat Duma, a total that includes results in individual constituencies. That would maintain its constitutional majority - enabling it to pass laws and initiate amendments to the constitution without the support of other parties. It would also be an all-time high, outstripping its 2016 record of 343 seats.
Four other parties had made it into parliament - the Communists with 13.81%, the ultra-nationalist LDPR with 8.98% and the New People party with 7.96%. The Just Russia party narrowly made the 5% threshold needed to enter parliament.
All of those parties have voted in the same way as United Russia on major issues in recent years.
In Chechnya, Ramzan Kadyrov, a close Putin ally, was re-elected to a fifth term as leader with an official tally of near 100%.

China has expelled two top military leaders, Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli, from the Communist Party and the military, an official announcement showed on Monday, citing alleged disloyalty, corruption and other serious disciplinary breaches.

title: World Bank  IMF back debt framework for poor countries
description: World Bank  IMF back debt framework for poor countries
content:
The World Bank and International Monetary Fund said on Monday that both their executive boards had approved proposed reforms of their joint framework for evaluating the debt of low-income countries to reflect a more complex and riskier environment.
A joint review, the first since 2017, recommended changes in several areas, including better analysis of domestic debt and broadening the analysis of long-term development challenges, including climate change.
The reforms will work to improve the analysis of risks to debt sustainability by refining how countries' debt-carrying capacity is measured, and introducing new tools to assess debt sustainability.
Finally, the World Bank and IMF will work to enhance the "realism tools" and stress tests used to ensure the consistency and accuracy of forecasts, while encouraging countries to improve debt data transparency, the World Bank said.
The IMF and World Bank use the debt sustainability framework to analyze and assess a country's ability to take on new debt without jeopardizing its ability to service existing loans. Changes were recommended since many low-income countries have seen rising debt levels and a shift in financing sources to include more domestic and external borrowing on commercial terms.
The revised framework is expected to become operational in the second half of 2027, it added.
A review completed in July confirmed that the debt sustainability framework had worked well to identify debt distress episodes ahead of time and help countries make informed borrowing and lending decisions.

title: UK man charged over genocide
description: UK man charged over genocide
content:
A 65-year-old Rwandan man has been charged with genocide-related offences allegedly committed during the 1994 Rwanda Tutsi killings, British prosecutors said on Monday.
Vincent Brown, formerly known as Vincent Bajinya, was charged with one offence of conduct ancillary to genocide and six offences of conduct ancillary to murder as a crime against humanity.
Britain's Counter Terrorism Policing War Crimes Team said Brown was accused of encouraging others to kill Tutsis in Kigali in April 1994. The investigation began in 2019 following a request from the Rwandan government and involved years of international cooperation, it added.
Brown was accused of having "directed and incited acts of murder and genocide carried out by others", the Crown Prosecution Service said.
The charges against Brown were the first brought in the United Kingdom relating to the Rwandan genocide, the CPS added.
Brown, who is remanded in custody, is due to appear at London's Westminster Magistrates' Court on Tuesday.

title: Houthis push for control of highlands
description: Houthis push for control of highlands
content:
Fighting intensifies in mountains between Red Sea and Indian Ocean coasts
Houthi fighters pushed to seize strategic heights in Yemen on Monday to cut off the Red Sea coast from remaining areas held by Saudi-backed forces, after a report that President Donald Trump had called off US strikes on the group at the last minute.
The New York Times reported that the Trump administration had prepared to launch airstrikes on Sunday against the Houthis after fresh pleas from the Saudi crown prince. But the newspaper said Trump called off the airstrikes at the last minute, even as troops were loading bombs onto aircraft.
Reuters could not immediately verify the Times' report. The US military's Central Command referred questions to the White House. The White House did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment.
Rashid al-Alimi, the Riyadh-based president of Yemen's Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government, asked Trump by phone on Sunday for US military help, four sources told Reuters. Two of the sources, one Yemeni and one Western, said Trump made no direct pledge of support during the call.
According to the United Nations, nearly 700 people have been killed and thousands injured in the flare-up in fighting. Nearly 130,000 Yemenis have fled homes within Yemen, and more than 3,000 have fled by boat across the Red Sea to Africa.
Five Yemeni military sources told Reuters the Houthis were now seeking to seize strategic heights, known as the Kahboub Mountains, in two provinces, Taiz and Lahij, which separate the Red Sea coast from the government-held south.
Fighting has centred on the outskirts of the remote mountain Al-Wazi'iyah district in Taiz province, and Ras al-Ara along the Indian Ocean coast between the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at the Red Sea's mouth and the government's base in Aden, the sources said.
"The government forces appear to remain largely in a defensive posture following the loss of the Bab el-Mandeb area, while the Houthis are seeking to maintain the momentum of their advance, despite being exposed to intensive air strikes," said Mohammed Al-Qadhi, a veteran Yemeni journalist now working as a political analyst.
"These mountains could become critical to determining whether the Houthis succeed in
consolidating their recent territorial gains or whether government
forces will be able to retain the positions necessary to mount a counteroffensive."

title: Rare earths force Trump to be less hostile before Xi summit
description: Rare earths force Trump to be less hostile before Xi summit
content:
Two presidents to meet in Washington this week
US President Donald Trump has taken a less combative approach than usual ahead of his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping this week - a sign of Beijing's growing power thanks to critical minerals, China experts said.
The Trump administration has so far not threatened to slap steep tariffs on Chinese imports or to ban exports of US technology, in contrast to the aggressive stances that preceded previous summits.
The reason, experts said, is largely due to China's near-total control of rare earth minerals, a key input for tech and auto manufacturing. Last year, in retaliation against Trump's tariffs, China curbed rare earth exports and sent shockwaves through world markets.
The move effectively imposed a limit on how much Washington can threaten Beijing, empowering China in its years-long tech war with the United States, experts said.
"The US and the Trump administration are just fundamentally in a different position with China where they can't use that overly coercive, over-reaching approach, knowing that they are going to walk some stuff back, because of everything that happened last summer and because of the rare-earth export controls," said Emily Kilcrease, a former trade official now at the Center for a New American Security think tank.
The White House, the Commerce Department, United States Trade Representative and the Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
China controls up to 70% of global rare-earth mining, 85% of refining capacity, and about 90% of rare-earth metal alloy and magnet production, according to consultancy AlixPartners.
Rare earths, such as yttrium and dysprosium, underpin strategic industries such as automakers, chipmakers and defense contractors, representing a critical chokepoint in supply chains.

title: With Gulf on edge  Naqvi makes whirlwind Iran trip
description: With Gulf on edge  Naqvi makes whirlwind Iran trip
content:
Meets Pezeshkian, Momeni during Tehran visit
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday assured Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian that Pakistan was determined to expand multisector cooperation during his visit to Tehran.
Iranian media outlet Press TV reported that Pezeshkian stated that Pakistan and Iran could meet many of their needs by tapping their "domestic and regional capabilities".
Pezeshkian further noted that continued engagement between the two countries could further strengthen bilateral cooperation across all areas, adding that "US pressure on the region had contributed to greater convergence and interaction among Muslim countries".
"Pakistan is determined to further expand bilateral cooperation in trade, economy, tourism, politics, culture, and science," Naqvi was in turn quoted as saying by Press TV.
Naqvi earlier met Iranian counterpart Eskandar Momeni and exchanged views on bilateral relations and the latest situation in the region.
In a post on X, the interior ministry noted that progress was reviewed in the meeting on the ongoing cooperation between the interior ministries of both countries in various sectors.
According to the ministry, Momeni stated that Naqvi's recent visit was "very beneficial" and thanked Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir for their efforts towards regional peace and stability.
He further added that Iran was grateful for Pakistan's "continuous efforts" to establish peace in the region.
The statement added that Naqvi said that "in the coming times, bilateral relations would become even stronger".
Pakistani government sources earlier told Anadolu that Naqvi, who has been actively involved in the mediation process alongside CDF Munir, would discuss matters related to attacks by the Yemeni Houthi group on Saudi Arabia's oil and economic infrastructure, and how to revive the stalled peace talks with the US.
Islamabad had already warned that the recent escalation in Yemen would further complicate the already complex regional scenario.
This was Naqvi's sixth visit to Tehran since the US and Israel launched war against Iran in February.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei on Saturday said Naqvi's visit to Tehran would focus on bilateral relations, and there was no plan to exchange any specific messages regarding mediation.
Pakistan has remained the primary mediator between Iran and the US throughout the war, and has maintained close contact with both sides.
The US and Iran signed the Islamabad memorandum of understanding in June and launched negotiations toward a final agreement. However, the talks later collapsed over disagreements on security guarantees and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most strategic routes for global energy supplies and trade.
The US and Iran then exchanged military strikes in July.
Trump on Sunday said he was contemplating three possible paths for Iran: continue targeting it economically, destroy the regime or make a deal.
After securing a ceasefire in April, Pakistan hosted the first high-level direct talks between the US and Iran since they broke diplomatic ties in 1979.

title: Govt  PTI on warpath after  once   for all  threat
description: Govt  PTI on warpath after  once   for all  threat
content:
K-P CM gives a blistering response to interior minister's presser
A blistering war of words between Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi over the former's "once-and-for-all solution" and the latter's explosive counter-attack has brought the country to the brink of a major political showdown on September 27.
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) has announced a long march on Islamabad for Sunday, while the government has vowed to deal with the marchers with an "iron hand", as authorities have launched a crackdown, allegedly arresting several PTI lawmakers and workers.
Though PTI leaders and the heads of allied parties insist that dialogue with the government through elected representatives could help resolve their differences, they have categorically refused to call off their planned march.
Naqvi, the country's top security czar, addressed a press conference in Lahore on Monday amid a crackdown against the opposition party, warning that protesters would be "taken care of" this time if they entered Islamabad.
"As I am telling you, this time we will find a once-and-for-all solution," Naqvi told reporters while responding to a question about whether the government planned to ban the PTI. "We cannot afford this every time."
The interior minister did not even rule out the option of imposing governor's rule in PTI-led K-P. "The government had already made it clear to them that the prime minister, in consultation with our law ministry, would utilise whatever legal options were available," he said, in response to another question.
K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi took exception to Naqvi's remarks. "Do not tell us, the terrorists that you people have resettled in Pakistan, deal with them once for all," a visibly angry Afridi told the provincial assembly session.
"Deal with them once for all with those who say we do not face a threat from India. They have changed the state's narrative. Deal with that once for all. Those who carried out Dawn Leaks against Pakistan, deal with them once for all," he added.
He warned that the people of Pakistan would deal with them. "Dealing with them once for all will be done by the people of Pakistan themselves, Inshallah, because you people have to win every single time, whereas the Pakistani people only have to win once, and that will be once for all."
Later, talking to the media after a parliamentary party meeting in Peshawar, the chief minister made it clear that the party would not withdraw from its constitutional and democratic right. "The September 27 announcement will not be withdrawn," Afridi stated.
Afridi insisted that the proposed march would be a sustained political movement rather than a brief protest, adding that a detailed plan would be announced on September 25. "The long march is not a T20; it will be a Test match," he said.
Speaking on the occasion, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said that the party was democratic and peaceful and wanted political issues resolved through constitutional means. He emphasised that the party was not seeking any confrontation.
"We are still in contact. We are peaceful and will remain peaceful," Gohar said, adding that the PTI was not seeking confrontation with the state. He said the party wanted Imran Khan to receive medical treatment, have his cases heard and be allowed to meet his family and lawyers.
Gohar's offer for dialogue was echoed by Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, who urged Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to constitute negotiating teams so that both sides could understand each other's positions and take talks forward.
"We are ready for negotiations," Abbas said, adding that the opposition had kept the door open for talks whenever the government was ready, but maintained that negotiations should involve political representatives rather than individuals.
He criticised the government for obstructing the path to dialogue. He said his recent discussions with Naqvi had failed after the minister insisted that the September 27 protest call be withdrawn. The opposition, he added, had conveyed that only PTI founder Imran Khan could withdraw the call.
Gohar rejected suggestions that the planned march represented an attempt to "conquer" Islamabad. He alleged that five PTI MNAs and a Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa minister had been arrested, describing the situation as unacceptable for a party governing the province.
"Our 1,500 workers have been arrested, and lists have been made for the rest. Five MNAs, a senator, our MPAs, including one from Islamabad, and ministers from Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa are currently under arrest," he said.
K-P Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati told the house that a provincial minister, Shakeel Khan, had been "targeted", while another, Fazal Shakoor, had been "abducted". "These incidents create the impression that there is martial law in the province," Swati remarked.
Reports from Islamabad suggested that Senators Saifullah Niazi, Sanaullah Mastikhel, Jamal Ahsan Khan, Dawar Khan and Mian Muhammad Ghaus had been arrested from Islamabad's Red Zone. According to sources, former MNA Aurangzeb Khan and 33 PTI workers were also detained in Rawalpindi.
Police said the PTI parliamentarians had been detained under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO). The police action was condemned by the PTI and the opposition alliance, Tehreek Tahaffuz Aain-e-Pakistan (TTAP), as "political victimisation".
Security, meanwhile, was tightened across Islamabad, Punjab and K-P ahead of the march. The federal capital administration sealed the Red Zone, D-Chowk and major entry points with containers, while barriers were erected on routes linking Punjab and K-P.
In Islamabad, police, Rangers and Frontier Corps personnel were deployed in large numbers, while Metrobus services between Rawalpindi and Islamabad were suspended. A high alert was also declared at PIMS and Polyclinic, with medical staff placed on round-the-clock duty.
Islamabad's educational institutions will remain closed from Tuesday amid heightened security measures. In Peshawar, roads leading to the Chief Minister's Secretariat and Governor House were blocked, while security arrangements were intensified in Rawalpindi's Red Zone.
Naqvi said in Lahore that if the PTI "besieged" the federal capital, it would harm itself. "Protest will not be beneficial for anyone and will only cause harm to the country's economy," he said. "If the PTI chooses that course, we will implement the Islamabad High Court (IHC) order," he said.
The IHC on September 1 virtually put brakes on the PTI's capital march as it barred political parties, political leaders, provincial governments and public office holders from occupying public roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas, buildings or other public places within or leading to the capital.
When asked if the federal government had any "long-term solution" to PTI's frequent protest calls, he said, "This time we will find a permanent solution; we will not leave it halfway." He added that no one would be allowed to suspend life in the country for a prolonged period.
He said that if the PTI wanted a medical check-up for Imran Khan, this had already happened. He claimed that the party itself did not know what it wanted to achieve. Referring to remarks by PTI's Junaid Akram that the PTI would turn Islamabad into "Somnath", Naqvi said the threats were hollow.
(With additional input from Our Peshawar correspondent Shahid Hameed)

title: US networks halt Trump coverage over ban
description: US networks halt Trump coverage over ban
content:
US networks halt Trump coverage over ban
US television networks staged an extraordinary revolt Monday when they effectively boycotted coverage of President Donald Trump in protest at his decision to ban three leading outlets from the White House.
CNN, MS NOW and Politico also went to court after Trump on Friday ordered them to be barred, as the 80-year-old Republican stepped up his years-long assault on the US media.
As a result of the row, Trump's opening of his cherished new White House helipad and his trip to the United Nations General Assembly were proceeding without live television coverage.
In a rare move, the top five US broadcasters said on Monday that they were halting "pool" coverage of the White Housewhere a broadcaster films on behalf of all television outlets for the dayin solidarity with CNN.
CNN had been scheduled to serve Monday as the White House TV pool.
"The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting," ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox and NBC said in a statement.
The result is an almost unprecedented test of wills between the Trump administration and the press, in a critical week during which Chinese President Xi Jinping is visiting the White House.
There will be no live TV of Trump's meetings with foreign leaders at the UN in New York, an annual forum that is closely watched around the world.
Meanwhile the ribbon-cutting ceremony for the giant granite helipad on the South Lawn was only streamed on the White House's websiteand Trump's comments were completely inaudible.
Several photo news organizations working at the White House, including AFP, decided to delay the release of photographs of Trump at the helipad in solidarity with the three banned media organizations.
Trump was unrepentant, branding the media a "cancer" and a threat to national security.
"The White House is not instituting an assault on the Free Press, something which I cherish," Trump said on his Truth Social network.
"It is instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS, something that has grown like Cancer in our beloved United States of America."
Vice President JD Vancea former CNN commentator before his move into politicsaccused the outlets of disseminating "left-wing propaganda."
"They can still report. They still have the access to free speech. They're just not going to get an office in the White House anymore," he told reporters.
Trump's ban however went further than simply revoking office space from the outlets.
Journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico were denied any access to the White House grounds on Saturday and had their passes confiscated.
In their lawsuit, the three organizations asked for a temporary restraining order against the ban on the grounds that it violates the First Amendment of the US Constitution, which upholds the right to a free press.
"This ban could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles," the organizations said in a court filing.
A US district judge set a hearing on the complaint for Wednesday.
Trump's sudden announcement of the ban on Friday stunned the mediaand reportedly many in his own administration.
The president has not detailed what prompted the ban, but said in response to a question from an AFP reporter in the Oval Office on Friday that it was "really just cumulative stories over the last two years."
Trump warned Friday that other outlets could face a similar fate, without saying which.
The billionaire former reality TV star has long attacked media outlets that have aired critical coverage of his campaigns and administrations, repeatedly blasting the press as the "enemy of the people."
But the ban comes at a time when his approval ratings are at record lows, his Republican Party risks losing control of Congress in November's midterm elections, and the Iran war drags on with no end in sight.

title: Air strikes destroy three terror redoubts
description: Air strikes destroy three terror redoubts
content:
Cross-border action follows terror surge in K-P 28 Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists killed in strikes 9 more terrori
Pakistan on Monday carried out "calibrated" air strikes against terrorist camps and hideouts inside Afghanistan, killing 28 terrorists, including several suicide bombers, in a major escalation following a series of deadly attacks in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).
The strikes, according to the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, targeted three locations belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij – a term used for the outlawed Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) – and affiliated terrorist groups. One of the targets was identified as a training centre for suicide bombers.
The ministry said large quantities of weapons and ammunition stored at the targeted facilities were also destroyed.
The air strikes came a day after security forces conducted intelligence-based ground operations in Kohat and Hangu. According to the ministry, nine terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij were killed and several others injured during the operation.
Taken together, the government put the death toll from the ground and air operations at 37 terrorists.
The action followed the deadly terrorist attack on a police facility in Kohat last Friday, when a suicide bomber and armed attackers targeted a mosque and police compound. The assault resulted in heavy casualties and was followed by a prolonged security operation.
Pakistan has blamed terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory for the broader escalation, as one of the suicide bombers has been identified as Afghan national. The Information Ministry statement said that the latest operation was launched "in the aftermath of recent multiple terrorist incidents inside Pakistan against the innocent people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa".
It said the ground operation around Kohat, Hangu and Thal was followed by selective targeting of terrorist camps and hideouts in the border region with Afghanistan on the basis of "credible intelligence".
"Pakistan has always strived for the maintenance of peace and stability in the region. However, the safety and security of our citizens remains our foremost priority," the ministry said.
It added that Afghanistan continuing to serve as a "hub of terrorism" was a matter of grave concern for Pakistan, arguing that the threat to the country emanated from Afghan territory.
The ministry said maximum precautions had been taken to prevent collateral damage.
The Afghan Taliban government, however, has disputed Pakistan's account. Afghan officials said the strikes hit areas in Kunar and Paktika provinces and reported civilian casualties, with Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid condemning the action and warning of a response.
The latest strikes mark another serious deterioration in Pakistan-Afghanistan relations after a period of relative calm along the border. Islamabad has for months maintained that the central problem in its relationship with Kabul is the presence of the banned TTP and other terrorist groups on Afghan soil.
Pakistan has repeatedly demanded that the Taliban government take verifiable action against these groups, particularly the TTP, which Islamabad holds responsible for a sustained campaign of terrorism inside Pakistan.
Kabul has consistently rejected the allegations that it allows Afghan territory to be used against Pakistan and has instead accused Islamabad of violating Afghan sovereignty through cross-border strikes.
The latest military action also comes at a particularly sensitive moment diplomatically.
Turkey and Qatar have recently stepped up efforts to mediate between Pakistan and Afghanistan, while China has also been engaged through the Urumqi channel. Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin and Qatar's deputy national security adviser recently held talks aimed at easing tensions between Islamabad and Kabul.
The Kohat attack and Pakistan's subsequent military response have therefore placed those diplomatic efforts under considerable pressure.
For Islamabad, the argument is increasingly that dialogue cannot produce results unless Kabul addresses the presence and activities of terrorist groups operating from its territory. Pakistan has also maintained that it does not seek a confrontation with Afghanistan but will act when attacks inside the country are traced to terrorist sanctuaries across the border.
The ministry said the latest action was part of Pakistan's counterterrorism campaign, Ghazab lil Haq, being conducted under the broader Azm-e-Istehkam framework. The government said the campaign would continue "at full pace" to eliminate what it described as foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism.

title: Fazl sees no room for talks with govt
