content:
Accuses rulers of being unwilling to listen or understand peoples problems, using force indiscriminately
Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Monday expressed concern over the country's internal situation, accusing the government of refusing to listen to the people, using force indiscriminately and denying political parties their right to protest, while claiming that Islamabad had been "filled with containers" to prevent demonstrations.
Speaking at a press conference in Islamabad, Fazl said the law and order situation was alarming, saying there was a "reign of dacoits" in Sindh while banks were being looted in broad daylight in Balochistan, yet no effective system was visible to prevent such incidents.
He said powerful institutions were effectively running the country and, according to him, appeared to be accountable neither to the law and Constitution nor to any moral code.
Fazl said the previous government had been criticised over its borrowing, but the debt burden on the country had now increased much further, while inflation had also risen and the public was facing growing hardship.
He accused the rulers of being unwilling to listen to the people or understand their problems, alleging that force was being used indiscriminately and that people were being denied their right to protest. He said Islamabad had been filled with containers after political parties announced demonstrations.
The JUI-F chief said ministers were being "picked up" in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, banks were being robbed in broad daylight in Balochistan and there was a "reign of dacoits" in Sindh.
He called for effective measures to establish law and order, uphold the Constitution and the law, and protect the basic rights of citizens.
Fazl said the present government was representing the establishment rather than the people and warned that the country had reached a dangerous situation.
He criticised the rulers for remaining preoccupied with tours and tourism while the country, in his words, was sitting on a "barrel of gunpowder".
He said peaceful protest was the right of every political party and that inflation had reached a level where people could no longer afford even their medical treatment.
According to Fazl, the rulers' eyes and ears were closed and they were neither seeing nor hearing the problems confronting the public.
He said the country had effectively become a "besieged state", arguing that while the house was already on fire, new disputes were being created.
Fazl said the country was currently sitting on a "barrel of gunpowder", yet issues relating to the provinces and mineral resources were being opened up.
He maintained that it was not possible to form a government without JUI-F and, even if one was formed without it, it could not function.
He said cooperation with all political parties inside Parliament and the formation of a united opposition had been endorsed.
Fazl also made clear his position on dialogue with the government, saying JUI-F regarded the present setup as a representative of the establishment and therefore talks were not possible with it.
He said dialogue could take place if there were a representative government.

title: Protocol rows unsettle PPP leaders
description: Protocol rows unsettle PPP leaders
content:
Complaint reaches Zardari's office as senior party figures face protocol hurdles
The Punjab Governor House, occupied by a PPP-nominated governor, has witnessed a series of distasteful episodes involving senior leaders of the party over protocol-related issues, causing concern within the provincial chapter.
A complaint in this regard has also reached the office of President Asif Ali Zardari, according to information received by The Express Tribune.
Sardar Saleem Haider's appointment as Governor of Punjab had, in theory, opened up an opportunity for the party to reorganise its ranks and file and strengthen its position in the province, using the influence that comes with the exalted office.
The expectations that the party in Punjab had attached to his appointment, however, appear to have taken a hit following a series of distasteful episodes at the Governor House.
Two most notable incidents, both occurring in September, involved PPP Central Punjab General Secretary Hasan Murtaza and, most recently, Lahore Division President Faisal Mir. Both are considered among the key players of the party in the province.
When asked about the episodes involving the PPP leaders and their reluctance to visit the Governor House, spokesperson for the president of Pakistan, Murtaza Solangi, said the matter had recently come to his attention and that he would raise it with President Zardari.
A PPP Punjab office-bearer, meanwhile, claimed that the matter had also reached the Party chairman's Office.
According to the party, the first incident took place in early September when PPP Central Punjab General Secretary Hasan Murtaza arrived at the Governor House with a convoy of around three cars.
One of the vehicles was carrying a team of media persons accompanying him to record his daily routine for their programme. Soon after crossing the main entrance gate, Murtaza was stopped by a traffic sergeant and directed towards the right lane leading to the visitors' parking area.
Murtaza introduced himself and pointed out that his name was on the list permitting him to drive directly in front of the Governor House, adding that he was a regular visitor. Despite this, he was denied entry, prompting Hasan to call Governor Punjab to inform him of the situation and request that he address this confusion. As per leaders, instruction were conveyed to the staff to let Murtaza proceed ahead.
However, the sergeant continued to refuse entry even after the governor intervened, saying that new rules issued by the Governor House's security in-charge, the military secretary, required his explicit consent before any unauthorised person could access the area.
The PPP youth leader accompanying Murtaza, upon learning that he had been denied entry despite the governor's intervention, became infuriated and pushed his way through.
According to party leaders, the incident was initially viewed by many as an attempt by the officer to assert his authority within the Governor House. However, the events that followed changed that perception entirely.
Hasan Murtaza, when approached for comment a day later, tried to play down the episode, saying politicians are used to such hardships. He confirmed that the episode had taken place and said he had called the governor, after which the matter was eventually resolved.
When asked about the party officials' claim that he had been denied entry despite the governor's intervention, Murtaza said a new officer had taken charge, so there might have been some confusion at that end.
This was followed by multiple instances of party leaders being denied access even to the visitors' parking area, forcing them to walk all the way from the main gate to the Governor House, according to some party officials.
On last Monday, another episode appeared to take the matter a step further when Lahore Division President Faisal Mir was allegedly snubbed for merely carrying his phone while standing in the lobby outside the governor's office, allegedly by a senior-most level staff member. Faisal, who had brought Saleema Hashmi, daughter of the late revolutionary poet Faiz Ahmed Faiz, former principal of the National College of Arts (NCA), and Hina Jilani, former chairperson HRCP, was left red-faced even before this unsavoury episode.
Both guests were denied entry to the main parking area, ahead of the main entrance, despite their status and age and were made to walk from the guest parking area. Halfway through, they were again sent back to their vehicles to leave their phones behind.
This was followed by a long wait outside the governor's office, without even being offered a place to sit, according to the party leaders.
Later, party leaders said that, after much back and forth and an earnest request to the Principal Secretary, Mir found them a place to sit. It was while Mir was waiting for the meeting that he was allegedly snubbed, followed by an order from a staffer at the Governor House to surrender his phone, according to Faisal Mir himself.
Talking to The Express Tribune, Mir acknowledged the entire episode, saying he was first snubbed for merely carrying a phone, followed by an attempt to confiscate it. He termed the incident unfortunate.
Other leaders, particularly those from Lahore, have also been heard complaining about what they describe as an unwelcoming attitude at the Governor House, particularly with regard to parking and carrying their phones.
These episodes were followed by a shake-up in Lahore, where two people deemed close to the governor were abruptly removed from their positions on Tuesday for violating party discipline.
It is pertinent to mention here that the Punjab Governor had earlier shown reluctance to offer the premises of his residence for a party event of 25 July, organised to mark the president's birthday after the district administration denied access to Greater Iqbal Park.
Even after the venue was secured for the event, party workers were made to wait in long queues outside the Governor House for security checking.

title: GSP  remains key to Pak EU ties  Dar says

content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar stressed the significance of GSP+ status for Pakistan's trade relations with the European Union (EU) in a meeting with EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas on Monday.
According to a statement issued by the Foreign Office, the meeting took place on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), currently underway in New York.
The deputy premier highlighted the importance Pakistan attaches to its partnership with the European Union, particularly in trade and economic cooperation. He stressed the significance of GSP+ for Pakistan's trade relations with the EU, the FO said.
The two sides also exchanged views on regional and global developments, with DPM Dar appreciating the EU's constructive engagement with Pakistan during recent regional developments, as well as its recognition of Pakistan's efforts towards de-escalation and dialogue.
He called for a return to "the path of dialogue and diplomacy" and full implementation "by all parties" of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding signed between the US and Iran earlier this year, according to the statement.
"Both sides agreed to maintain close engagement on matters of mutual interest," the FO added.
The meeting took place against the backdrop of an intense engagement between Islamabad and Brussels over a trading scheme and its future.
DPM Dar also met French Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of France Jean-Noël Barrot on sidelines of the UNGA session. They reviewed the bilateral relations and agreed on utilising regional forums to address regional challenges and promote dialogue.
The FM reiterated Pakistan's desire to further strengthen bilateral ties, including through enhanced political engagement, trade and investment, educational linkages and people-to-people exchanges.

title: Imran sisters  detention challenged in LHC
description: Imran sisters  detention challenged in LHC
content:
Plea seeks release of Aleema, Uzma and Noreen
A petition was filed before the Lahore High Court (LHC) on Monday challenging the 30-day detention of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan's sisters Aleema Khan, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO), seeking their immediate release.
The petition was filed by Aleema's son, Shahraiz Khan, through advocate Rana Mudasar Umar, challenging the detention orders issued by the Lahore deputy commissioner on September 20 and seeking the immediate release of the three women.
The detentions came as authorities stepped up action against PTI ahead of the party's planned September 27 march in Islamabad. The petition said Aleema was picked up while travelling with her driver for personal work and that both were currently confined at Lahore Central Jail.
According to reports, police also detained Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi for 30 days under the 3 MPO. The petitioner said there was no public gathering or situation suggesting any threat to public order when Aleema was detained.
Challenging the grounds for detention, the petition said the allegations were linked to a police case in which Aleema had sought pre-arrest bail. It said the matter had remained pending for around one-and-a-half years before police ultimately declared her innocent.
The petition further argued that the grounds of detention must contain sufficient particulars to enable a detainee to make an effective representation, and alleged that constitutional safeguards governing communication of those grounds had not been properly observed.
Reacting to the detentions, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said the "unjustified arrest" of the Khan sisters, with along attacks on and arrests of party workers, ministers and parliamentarians in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Islamabad, had increased their responsibilities.
"We will have to move forward with prudence and unity," Raja said in a social media post. He added that a committee had been formed to run party affairs in Lahore through consultation and consensus, with a consultation meeting scheduled for Tuesday.
PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said Imran Khan's family members had been placed in an armoured vehicle and taken to an undisclosed location. He alleged that Punjab police had arrested both sisters along with their children and Aleema Khan's sons.
In a separate statement, PTI condemned what it called the "illegal and high-handed action" of Punjab police, alleging that the arrests amounted to an abuse of authority, violation of fundamental rights and "political victimisation".
Imran's son Kasim Khan also criticised the arrests in posts on X, calling the detention of his aunts "a disgrace". He alleged that people had entered their homes and forced family members into vehicles without explanation. He later said some children were safe but alleged that two more cousins, Azeem and Sakeenah, had been arrested without their whereabouts being disclosed.

title: New platform opens US market to startups
description: New platform opens US market to startups
content:
Innovation Hive to connect entrepreneurs with mentors, investors
Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja on Monday formally inaugurated "The Innovation Hive", established by the United States Educational Foundation in Pakistan (USEFP).
The ceremony was attended by US Embassy Chargé d'Affaires Natalie Baker, STEPI Pakistan CEO Dr Mazhar H Qureshi, USEFP Alumni Affairs Director Mazhar Awan and other prominent personalities.
"Talent exists everywhere in Pakistan; it just needs a place where opportunity can find it. That's what the Innovation Hive is for. This partnership reflects President Trump's vision that America's relationships abroad should deliver real results, more trade, more investment, and more prosperity for both our countries," Baker said.
Baker added that over its first year, the Innovation Hive would connect over 250 American mentors with entrepreneurs at every stage, and the US government would invest to support top Pakistani entrepreneurs.
Addressing the ceremony, Shaza thanked the US Embassy and USEFP, saying that 'The Innovation Hive' was not merely a building or an office, but a strong bridge that would provide Pakistani entrepreneurs with direct access to the US market and investors without having to leave the country, while also creating broader opportunities for young people to advance.
Highlighting the historical ties and economic cooperation between the two countries, the minister said that the US was Pakistan's largest export market, accounting for around 20 per cent of Pakistan's total exports during fiscal year 2025-26.
Shaza said that bilateral trade exceeded eight billion dollars in 2025, while under the Pakistan-US trade agreement reached in July 2025, US import duties on IT services, textiles and other sectors were reduced.
She added that Pakistan had, as a goodwill gesture, abolished the five per cent Digital Services Tax.
The minister also said that the combined enterprise value of Pakistan's VC-funded startups had exceeded four billion dollars.
She said startups raised 74.2 million dollars in funding in 2025, while funding for startups founded or co-founded by women increased from 5.5 million dollars in 2024 to 10.1 million dollars in 2025.
'The Innovation Hive' would serve as a permanent platform connecting Pakistani talent directly with the US market, mentorship opportunities and the alumni network.
Referring to key institutions and initiatives of the Ministry of IT and Telecommunication, the minister said that through nine National Incubation Centres, Ignite had supported more than 2,350 startups and created over 185,000 employment opportunities.
She said the Pakistan Startup Fund had restored the confidence of US investors by providing funding of up to 30 per cent without taking any government equity.
The Special Technology Zones Authority provided technology and AI companies with 10-year tax and customs incentives.
Concluding her address, Shaza told entrepreneurs: "The US market you want to reach is no longer across the ocean; its address is now in Islamabad. This bridge reflects the shared commitment of both countries."
At the conclusion of the ceremony, the minister also visited various sections of the USEFP, where she was briefed on the organisation and its activities.

title: Online grooming puts Pakistani children at risk
description: Online grooming puts Pakistani children at risk
content:
UNICEF report highlights widespread abuse, sexual extortion
Zara Shah was targeted by a stranger while playing a computer game, drawn into a conversation that would expose her to terrifying online sexual exploitation.
Zara, whose name has been changed by AFP for safety reasons, is one of an estimated 1.5 million children in Pakistan who experienced online sexual abuse in one year, according to a report published by the UN children's agency this month.
"We started chatting while playing an online game, and he began acting like a friend. Later, he wanted to meet and, after, started asking me for nudes," 17-year-old Zara said.
"When I refused, he threatened to find my family online and tell them that we had been talking," she added.
According to the UNICEF report, around 85% of perpetrators were known to the victims, aged between 12 and 17.
"The abuse may start with a friendly conversation, a gaming interaction, a promise of gifts, money or romance," Daniel Kardefelt, lead author of the global UNICEF report, told AFP.
"Perpetrators may spend months building trust using information that they find on social media," Kardefelt said.
In Pakistan, 71% of victims did not tell anyone, according to the UNICEF report, while no child surveyed reported the abuse through formal channels, including police, helplines or social workers.
Their silence was mostly because of stigma, shame and fears over how their families or society may react.
"Around 44% of reported abuse was entirely online, with Snapchat and WhatsApp among the most common settings," said Mehek Naeem, director of PAHCHAAN, a children's rights organisation based in the eastern city of Lahore.
Girls can face heightened risks of sexual extortion in society, which can lead to restrictions on their mobility or withdrawal from school.
For Zara, the threat of being exposed to her family was enough to keep her silent.
"I could have been stopped from going to school or leaving the house altogether," she said.
"Staying quiet felt like the better option than speaking up. But anxiety kills me every day."
With around 74% of children aged 12 to 17 in Pakistan estimated by UNICEF to be internet users, concerns over online safety are growing as their access to digital platforms expands.
Echoing other policies around the world, the Punjab government this month passed a resolution to bar children under 16 from using social media.
"I disagree with the ban," said Usama Khilji, a digital rights activist.
"It will be a challenge to implement, and children can circumvent the ban through VPNs. Children have the right of freedom of expression, and a ban takes that away," he said.
Pakistan has a legal framework addressing tech-facilitated offences against children, but "there is no implementation", said Tahira Afrasiyab, a spokesperson for non-profit organisation Muslim Hands.
And, according to experts, there are loopholes in existing laws.
Human rights lawyer Salman Afridi said this issue shows how "economic vulnerability can be weaponised" for amounts as small as Rs10,000 in exchange for the production of sexual content.

title: JI raises alarm over delay in protest train
description: JI raises alarm over delay in protest train
content:
Hafiz Naeem demands railways explain disruption as Shalimar Express heads to Multan
Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman on Monday questioned a four-hour delay in the Shalimar Express that was to carry his protest caravan from Sukkur to Multan, asking whether the disruption was linked to his party's march towards Islamabad, as the "second phase" of the mobilisation got under way.
JI had set its protest caravan in motion from Karachi towards the federal capital on Sunday, reached Sukkur late Sunday aboard the Rehman Baba Express and was scheduled to continue to Multan on the Shalimar Express.
However, the train was around four hours late reaching Sukkur on Monday.
"Does this delay have anything to do with our train march? Shalimar Express, which is not only a popular train but has been privatised, is delayed by four hours today," he said.
"If this delay in its [Shalimar Express] is a usual delay, then the federal government should explain the performance of Pakistan Railways," Rehman said.
He said that if four- to five-hour delays and their impact on the wider railway system had become routine, then the government's performance was there for everyone to see.
The Shalimar Express eventually left Rohri railway station at around 5:45pm. Rehman was scheduled to address supporters after the train reached Multan, from where the JI caravan would proceed towards Islamabad by road.
In a video shared by JI showing Rehman travelling by train, the party chief said the "first phase" of the march had ended and the second phase had begun with the journey towards Multan.
He said separate caravans had also set out for Islamabad from Balochistan and Bab-i-Khyber.
An official at the Karachi chief controller's office, meanwhile, said the Shalimar Express had reached Karachi late, arriving at 7:20am, which delayed its return journey towards Hyderabad. The official attributed the late arrival to an engine fault that developed at Tando Adam in Sanghar district.
The train consequently reached Hyderabad at 1:25pm instead of its usual 9:20am arrival time, delaying its onward journey to Rohri railway station, where Rehman's caravan was waiting.
The Pakistan Railways Karachi division, in a separate statement, said delays were expected in the departure of some up trains "due to delays in the arrivals of several down trains".
The railway disruption came as Rehman used his stop in Sukkur to renew his demand for withdrawal of the petroleum levy. He said it was time Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif "put his foot down" and scrapped the levy to provide "much-needed relief" to the people.

title: Olivia Rodrigo ties  Guts  record with her latest album
description: Olivia Rodrigo ties  Guts  record with her latest album
content:
It remains inside top 10 across six US charts
Olivia Rodrigo has matched a major chart milestone from her own catalogue as You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love spends its 12th week at No. 1 on the Billboard Top Alternative Albums chart.
The result puts Rodrigo's latest studio album level with Guts, which also spent 12 weeks at the summit of the alternative ranking following its release in 2023. Her newest album has therefore equalled the longest No. 1 run Rodrigo has achieved on that particular Billboard chart.
You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love is also at No. 1 on the Top Rock & Alternative Albums chart. According to the chart figures reported by Forbes, the album has spent 13 weeks on that ranking and has led it for 12 of those weeks. The album was released on June 12, 2026, through Geffen Records.
The project has also maintained a strong position across Billboard's broader US album rankings. The report states that it appears in the top 10 on all six Billboard charts where it is currently listed, including the Billboard 200, where it has risen to No. 2.
That performance follows a strong opening for Rodrigo's third studio album. The record debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 after earning 485,000 equivalent album units in the United States during its opening tracking week, according to Luminate figures reported by Billboard. It became Rodrigo's third album to reach the top of the main US albums chart, following Sour and Guts.
Rodrigo's debut album Sour does not appear on the Top Alternative Albums or Top Rock & Alternative Albums charts. Her later releases have been represented on those rock and alternative rankings, reflecting the classification of her newer material.
Guts remains present on both alternative focused charts as well. The album continues to occupy a top 10 position on the Top Alternative Albums chart while also remaining within the upper portion of the Top Rock & Alternative Albums ranking.
With You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love continuing its strong chart run, Rodrigo has now matched one of her own established milestones while extending the commercial performance of her third studio album.
Rodrigo began her career as a child actress. She rose to prominence with her leading roles in Disney Channel series.
She shifted her focus to music and signed with Geffen Records in 2020. Her debut studio album, Sour (2021), topped the US Billboard 200 and nine other charts worldwide. It was preceded by the US Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles "Drivers License" and "Good 4 U". She was the subject of a documentary, Olivia Rodrigo: Driving Home 2 U (2022). Her next two studio albums, Guts (2023) and You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love (2026), produced the US number-one singles "Vampire" and "Drop Dead" respectively, making her the first artist to have each lead single from their first three albums debut atop the chart.
Rodrigo's accolades include three Grammy Awards, four MTV Video Music Awards, and seven Billboard Music Awards. She was named Time's Entertainer of the Year in 2021, Billboard's Woman of the Year in 2022, and ASCAP's Pop Music Songwriter of the Year in both 2022 and 2024.

title: Noor Jehan remembered on her birth anniversary
description: Noor Jehan remembered on her birth anniversary
content:
'Melody Queen' enjoyed celebrated career packed with prestigious accolades
Renowned singer and actress Noor Jehan was remembered on her birth anniversary on Monday. Popularly known as the "Melody Queen," Noor Jehan was born on September 21, 1926 in Kasur and also established herself as an actress in the film industry. Her notable films included Chan Wey, Dopatta, Mirza Ghalib, Qaidi, Baaji and Khandaan. Besides being a celebrated playback singer, she was also a gifted ghazal vocalist and sang in several languages, including Urdu, Punjabi and Sindhi. She recorded over 10,000 songs during her illustrious career. She received the Lifetime Achievement Award twice and was also honoured with Pakistan's highest civilian awards, including Pride of Performance, Tamgha-e-Imtiaz and Sitara-e-Imtiaz. Regarded as one of the most prominent singers of her time in South Asia, she was bestowed with the title of Malika-e-Tarannum. Noor Jehan died of heart failure on December 23, 2000, and was laid to rest in Karachi.
Noor Jehan's six-decade career spanned both British Indian and Pakistani cinema. She had proficiency in Hindustani classical music, as well as in other genres including ghazals. She made her directorial debut with the film Chann Wey in 1951, becoming the first female film director in Pakistan. She is recognized for her contributions to music in South Asia, particularly in Pakistan.
Along with Ahmed Rushdi, she holds the record for having given voice to the largest number of film songs in the history of Pakistani cinema. She recorded about 10,000 songs in various languages, including Urdu, Punjabi, and Sindhi. She sang a total of 2,422 songs in 1,148 Pakistani films during a career that lasted more than half a century.
Noor Jehan began to sing at the age of five and showed a keen interest in a range of styles, including traditional folk and popular theatre. Realising her potential for singing, her parents sent her to receive early training in classical singing under Ustad Ghulam Mohammad. Noor Jehan's mother arranged for her to receive musical training under famous classical singer Kajjanbai. Kajjanbai had her receive 12 hours of "riyaz" every day, she also had a teacher who taught her literature lessons every day. She started her training at age 11 in Calcutta, where ustads instructed her in the traditions of the Patiala Gharana of Hindustani classical music and the classical forms of thumri, dhrupad, and khyal.
As a child, Noor Jehan and her two sisters performed on stage in a rural theater troupe called "Taka Theater". At the age of nine, she drew the attention of Punjabi musician Ghulam Ahmed Chishti, who would later introduce her to the stage in Lahore. He composed some ghazals, na`ats, and folk songs for her to perform, although she was keener on breaking into acting or playback singing. Once her vocational training finished, Jehan pursued a career in singing alongside her sister in Lahore..

title: California introduces annual  Dolly Parton Day
description: California introduces annual  Dolly Parton Day
content:
US state to observe it on September 25 following singer's death
California will observe Dolly Parton Day annually on September 25 following the death of the country music singer at the age of 80.
California Governor Gavin Newsom signed a bill on Sunday establishing the annual day of remembrance in honour of Parton, who died on August 25 in Nashville.
The date was selected as a reference to Parton's famous song "Nine to Five". Written numerically, September 25 becomes 9-2-5, creating a connection to the 1980 hit.
"With this bill, we are not just establishing a day to celebrate Dolly Parton, we are creating an annual reminder to us, every year, to live the way she did - joyfully, graciously, and with a whole lot of heart," said Newsom in the announcement.
The new law recognises Parton's work as a singer, songwriter, actress and philanthropist. She was one of country music's most commercially successful artists, with the Californian government stating that she sold more than 100 million records worldwide.
Parton was also recognised for her charitable work through the Dolly Parton Imagination Library. The foundation has distributed more than 300 million books to children around the world.
Parton's career included songs such as "Jolene", "Nine to Five" and "I Will Always Love You". Her work across music, film and charitable initiatives made her a prominent figure beyond the country music industry.
Parton's music received 52 gold, platinum, and multi-platinum certifications from the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Her accolades include eleven Grammy Awards and three Emmy Awards. She logged 25 No. 1 Billboard country singles (tied with Reba McEntire for the most by a woman). She was honoured with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame (1984) and the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award (2011).

title: Anti Assad music star makes triumphant return to Syria
description: Anti Assad music star makes triumphant return to Syria
content:
Assala Nasri entertains thousands at her sold-out concert in Damascus following 15 years of exile
Syrian singer Assala Nasri has made a triumphant return to Damascus with a sold-out concert following 15 years of exile due to her opposition to ousted ruler Bashar al-Assad.
Thousands of fans welcomed the 57-year-old, known mononymously as Assala, at a venue in the Syrian capital where she bowed and opened the show with songs hailing the Syrian people.
"Souls of my heart, I missed you," she repeatedly said to endless cheers on Thursday night.
"My loves, my people, I swear, until this moment I could not believe that I am among you. I want to tell you how much I dreamt of this."
There was a heavy security presence for the concert, after some religious conservatives launched a campaign calling for its cancellation.
Half of the show's proceeds will be donated to charity.
Syria's new Islamist authorities, who overthrew Assad in 2024, have welcomed Assala. Culture Minister Mohammed Yassine Saleh has dubbed her "the daughter of Damascus".
Joining her on stage, he said her return was that of "every honest Syrian and every free person".
Assala was among the first artists to express support for the peaceful anti-Assad protests that erupted in 2011, refusing to partake in events supporting his government.
She was booted from the Syrian artists' union for her stance and was the target of media campaigns.
She went into exile, living in Cairo with her family and playing shows in various Arab countries.
The bloody repression of the protests led to a 13-year civil war that killed more than half-a-million people.
At Assala's show, small Syrian flags rippled in time with the music, with many in the crowd unable to hold back their tears.
"I never thought this day would come. It's like a beautiful dream," concert-goer Sawsan Wadha, 56, said.
"We are very happy that our country is moving forward," added 40-year-old Lynn Nahas.
On her new record, "The Syrian Album", Assala covers folk songs from all 14 of Syria's provinces as an homage to her country's cultural diversity.
She sings for the cities scarred by war, but also for the coastline in mourning after last year's killing of hundreds of members of Assad's Alawite minority, and for Druze-majority Sweida, which also saw sectarian violence.
Assala's piercing, powerful voice rang out as she made her way through the album's tracks at Thursday's concert.
She also performed fan favourites like "Samehtak" and "Sandooq", with the jubilant, tearful crowd singing along.
Assala and her family only returned to Damascus this week. An antiques dealer in the capital returned the oud, or Oriental lute, that had belonged to her father, a celebrated musician.
Conservative Muslim figures had expressed criticism in the run-up to the concert.
Egyptian preacher Hani Dahab, who lives in Syria, launched a social media campaign with the slogan "Cancel the Sinful Concerts". He accused the culture ministry of seeking to "give society a secular character".
Syrian Salafi preacher Abdul Razzaq al-Mahdi condemned what he called a "concert of music and debauchery", while a group of preachers in Damascus called on the culture minister to take into account "the religious identity of society".
While not addressing the critics directly, Assala said at the show that "recovery will only happen with art and music".
Syria has seen a cultural boom since 2025, but also the rise of preachers and conservative religious movements in public spaces and at universities, raising fears of restrictions on freedom.
Farah Al-Atassi, political advisor to the government, said poetry, language and thought were "an integral part of Syrian identity".
"This is the Syria that we know and that will endure," she told AFP.
Assala publicly supported the Syrian revolution and opposed Bashar al-Assad. She went into exile and settled in Cairo, Egypt with her family while continuing to perform in various Arab countries. In 2014, she was selected as a peace ambassador for the Middle East by the organization MasterPeace in connection with an event marking International Day of Peace.

content:
British musician Jethro Sheeran weighs in on Macklemore controversy
Ed Sheeran's cousin, Jethro Sheeran, has publicly criticised the singer amid controversy over Macklemore's removal from the Loop Tour.
Jethro, a British musician known professionally as Alonestar, shared his comments on Instagram on September 17, saying he was "ashamed" of his cousin.
He also alleged that Ed had mistreated him personally and professionally.
"Finally it's all coming out! I'm ashamed of my Cousin Ed," Jethro wrote. "Finally the world and all his fans see through him. He's not a good person, I don't like his music so I can't say he's even a good artist."
Jethro further accused the singer of being selfish and making fun of his mental health. He claimed he had supported Ed's early music career, including taking him to a studio and performing on early songs.
Addressing Macklemore's removal from the tour, Jethro added, "He is shady and he's dropped Macklemore himself I believe 100% he's a coward."
The controversy followed Macklemore's performances at Ed's MetLife Stadium concerts, where he chanted "Free Palestine" and performed his protest song
The rapper was subsequently removed from the remaining eight Loop Tour dates.

"This week, the criticism was about something much more important, and I've had to take [it in] and make difficult decisions, and I am making mistakes, and I'm so so sorry."

Sheeran has sold 200 million records worldwide, making him one of the world's best-selling music artists. He has 119 million RIAA-certified units in the US, and two of his albums are in the list of the best-selling albums in UK chart history. In December 2019, the Official Charts Company named him its artist of the decade, with the most combined success in the UK album and singles charts in the 2010s. As of September 2026, he is the fourth-most-followed artist on Spotify. Several of his tours are amongst the most-attended concert tours, and his ÷ Tour became the highest-grossing of all time in August 2019. An alumnus of the National Youth Theatre in London, Sheeran's acting roles include appearing in the 2019 film Yesterday, playing himself. title: Rangeen  brings youthful romance to Coke Studio Nu WAV
description: Rangeen  brings youthful romance to Coke Studio Nu WAV
content:
Singers Hasan Raheem, Izzchugtai uniquely blend contemporary pop, traditional music in fascinating new collaboration
Coke Studio Nu.WAV has released Rangeen, a new collaboration between singers Hasan Raheem and Izzchugtai, produced by Umair.
The track blends hip-hop and contemporary pop with more traditional musical elements, building its story around longing, infatuation and the imagined possibilities of young love.
According to the team behind the song, Rangeen began with a beat created by Umair and shared with Hasan Raheem. The melody eventually took shape during Hasan's drive home, with the artists choosing to retain some of the spontaneity of the original idea rather than heavily rework it.
Izzchugtai joins the track later, adding another vocal layer and shifting its mood.
The accompanying music video, directed and edited by Arham Ikram, places the song in a stylised version of Lahore. It follows Hasan as he spots a girl from a rooftop during Basant and begins imagining a relationship with her.
The video deliberately draws on the visual language of classic Pakistani film romances, while adding references to an early-2000s childhood. Pastel-coloured buildings, patterned tiles, old computers, CDs, cassette tapes and film posters form much of its visual world.
As Hasan's imagined romance develops, the setting becomes increasingly exaggerated, blurring the line between what is happening and what exists in his imagination.
Speaking about the project, Kamal Khan, executive producer of Coke Studio Nu.WAV, said the collaboration came together relatively naturally, with Hasan and Umair already having the song and the team believing Izzchugtai would fit into it.
He described Arham Ikram's approach to the video as having a "filmy, coming-of-age feel".
The fantasy eventually gives way to reality when the arrangement opens into a shehnai performance by Muhammad Salim, introducing a wedding sequence that changes the direction of the story.
Rather than ending on a purely tragic note, the video leaves the possibility of another romance open.
Rangeen brings together three artists from different points in Pakistan's contemporary pop, R&B and hip-hop scene.
Hasan Raheem has become known for his work in indie-pop and R&B, with songs including Aisay Kaisay and Joona. He was also the inaugural artist selected for Spotify RADAR Pakistan and previously appeared on Coke Studio Season 14's Peechay Hutt with Talal Qureshi and Justin Bibis.
Izzchugtai is part of a newer generation of Pakistani artists working across production and performance. His releases include Ghuroor, LOVE BOMB, AWAY FROM ME, Junoon and Nadiyan Paar.
Umair, who was born in Karachi, began producing music as a teenager and has since worked on more than 150 releases and collaborations. His previous work with Hasan includes Radha, OBVIOUS and MAKE YOU MINE. He has also collaborated with artists including Young Stunners, Asim Azhar and Talwiinder.
For Rangeen, Umair handled production, composition, mixing and co-arrangement alongside Hasan. Hasan also worked on the vocal arrangement, vocal composition and lyrics, while Sean Tallman handled mastering.
The music video was produced by Gali Films, with Iman Khan as producer, Aamir Mughal as director of photography and Hashim Ali responsible for production design and art direction.
The song is the latest release from Coke Studio Nu.WAV, which has continued to bring together emerging and established artists from Pakistan's contemporary music scene.
Coke Studio Pakistan is a part of the international music franchise, Coke Studio, which features studio-recorded music performances by established and emerging artists. It is the longest-running annual television music show in Pakistan, airing annually since 2008. The programme's concept originated in Brazil and has subsequently expanded its reach worldwide.
The show combines a myriad of musical influences, from traditional Pakistani classical, folk, Sufi, qawwali, ghazal and bhangra music to contemporary hip hop, rock and pop music. It is noted for promoting Pakistan's multiculturalism by inviting artists from various regions and languages to collaborate musically.
The show features artists in each episode, by a house band and guest artists. Coke Studio tracks are officially available on their YouTube channels and various streaming platforms. The music is recorded live by artists at Coke Studio.
Following success in Pakistan after its first launch, Coke Studio has become an international franchise. The Pakistani show has amassed a large fan base in neighbouring India. Christina Applegate shares first video after months in hospital, thanking fans for support amid her ongoing MS battle
Christina Applegate has shared her first video following a months-long hospitalisation, giving fans an update on her life outside the hospital.
The Married… with Children star posted the video on Instagram, where she showed off her newly coloured blonde hair while wearing a black zip-up hoodie. Applegate also thanked hairstylist Dave Stanwell for helping brighten her day and acknowledged the support she has received from fans.
The update comes several months after Applegate’s hospitalisation was first reported in March. In April, the Emmy-winning actor shared a message on Instagram saying she was focusing on her health and was “getting stronger and better every day”.
Applegate was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in August 2021. She publicly revealed her diagnosis that year and later discussed how the condition had affected her daily life and career.
The actor made her first public appearance after the diagnosis at her Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony in November 2022. During the ceremony, Applegate became emotional while speaking about her daughter and thanking those who had supported her.
Applegate has continued to speak openly about living with multiple sclerosis. Her latest social media update provides another glimpse into her recovery following her recent hospital stay.
The actor is best known for her roles in Married… with Children and the Netflix comedy series Dead to Me , for which she received multiple Emmy nominations.
In her latest post, Applegate thanked her followers for their continued support, ending the message by expressing her love to those who had reached out to her.

content:
Charlie Hunnam returns as Andrew Borden in Netflix’s 'Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story' after playing Ed Gein
Charlie Hunnam has returned to Netflix’s Monster anthology series for its fourth season, Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story , following his role as serial killer Ed Gein in the previous season.
In Season 4, Hunnam plays Andrew Borden, the wealthy father of Lizzie Borden, portrayed by Ella Beatty. Andrew and his wife, Abby Borden, became victims in the infamous 1892 murders for which Lizzie was accused and later acquitted.
Monster showrunner Ian Brennan explained that bringing Hunnam back was a straightforward decision after the actor’s work on Monster: The Ed Gein Story . Brennan said the production had enjoyed working with Hunnam and did not want to “say goodbye to him” after the third season.
Brennan also highlighted the contrast between Hunnam’s two roles. While Ed Gein was portrayed with a softer demeanour, Andrew Borden is presented as a hostile and troubled father. According to Brennan, Hunnam’s performance brings additional complexity to the character.
Director Max Winkler, who worked on both seasons, also discussed Hunnam’s return. He said playing Andrew allowed the actor to work without carrying the same intensity associated with his portrayal of Gein.
Hunnam said the role offered him greater creative freedom because relatively little is known about the historical Andrew Borden. He explained that the limited historical record allowed the production to develop aspects of the character for the series.
The fourth season stars Beatty as Lizzie Borden, alongside Rebecca Hall as Abby Borden, Vicky Krieps as Bridget Sullivan and Sarah Paulson as Aileen Wuornos.
Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story is currently available to stream on Netflix.

title: One Health central to livestock productivity
description: One Health central to livestock productivity
content:
Rome conference focuses on addressing animal, plant disease challenges
Federal Minister for National Food Security and Research Rana Tanveer Hussain is attending the FAO Global Conference for Actions on One Health in Agrifood Systems, being held in Rome from September 21 to 23. The event focuses on turning the One Health approach into concrete action across agrifood systems, bringing together international stakeholders to address challenges ranging from animal and plant diseases to food safety, environmental sustainability and public health.
Addressing the opening plenary session, Hussain said One Health was fundamental to Pakistan's food security, livestock productivity, rural livelihoods and sustainable agriculture. He stressed that global commitments must translate into practical action at the national level, backed by effective coordination and implementation.
The minister said Pakistan was focusing on healthier and more resilient livestock and food production systems. He highlighted disease prevention, improved biosecurity, responsible antimicrobial use and stronger veterinary services as essential measures to protect animal and human health and sustain agricultural productivity.
Speaking about rangelands and pastoral communities, he said pastoralists were central to Pakistan's livestock economy and deserved greater support. Improved access to animal health services, water, feed and markets, he noted, would help strengthen their livelihoods while promoting the sustainable management of rangelands.
On food safety, the minister emphasised the need to protect consumers at every stage of the food chain, from farm to table. He called for stronger surveillance of food-borne diseases and antimicrobial resistance, alongside responsible antimicrobial use.
Hussain also highlighted the vital contribution of women to livestock production and household nutrition. He stressed that improving women's access to knowledge, services, technology, finance and markets was important for strengthening rural livelihoods.

content:
Saudi supply recovery offers some relief; investors closely monitor regional risks
Pakistan equities opened the week on a firmer footing on Monday, with the benchmark KSE-100 index gaining modest ground as easing oil prices and hopes for diplomatic progress on the US-Iran conflict encouraged buying interest.
Although the early rally lost some momentum, the KSE-100 still closed with thin gains of 268.58 points, or 0.16%, at 171,153.17. It traded between the intra-day high of 171,732.62 and low of 170,902.76. The positive sentiment was aided by the decline in crude prices as traders monitored the pace of Saudi Arabia's oil shipment recovery following missile and drone attacks by Yemen's Houthis on Saturday.
The improvement in Saudi shipments offered some relief to markets worried about prolonged disruptions to regional supplies, although continuous attacks by the Houthis kept concerns over the security of energy flows in focus. Meanwhile, Pakistan's power demand showed a meaningful recovery in Aug'26, rising 5.1% year-on-year to 14,943 megawatts and standing 1.4% above the seven-year August average. "While still below the 16,176 MW peak recorded in Aug'21, the rebound is encouraging for power-sector activity and broader economic growth," Arif Habib Limited (AHL) reported.
AHL's Ali Najib wrote that investor sentiment remained mixed amid declining oil prices as expectations of additional Saudi crude supply eased concerns. However, renewed tensions involving Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthi forces kept investors cautious.
Lucky Cement, Attock Refinery, Fauji Fertiliser, Mari Energies and Engro Fertilisers added 255 points, while Pakistan Services, Meezan Bank, Systems Ltd, UBL & OGDC dragged the index down by 172 points.
"The market is expected to remain volatile, with selective buying if geopolitical tensions continue to ease and oil prices move down. However, elevated energy prices, external-sector risks and the upcoming IMF review will remain the key factors influencing market direction," he added.
According to KTrade Securities, the KSE-100 index closed up by 269 points (+0.16%) with 162 million shares traded. Sentiment remained mildly positive as Brent crude slipped towards $101 per barrel amid hopes for easing Red Sea tensions following US intervention, but stalemate continued at the Strait of Hormuz.
The upcoming UN General Assembly session could provide a platform for diplomatic engagement. Lower oil prices could support the PSX and Pakistan's external position; however, geopolitical developments around Hormuz remain the key risk. "Overall, the market may remain cautiously positive with volatility intact," KTrade expected.
JS Global analyst Mubashir Anis Naviwala commented that buying interest was observed at the PSX, where the benchmark index gained 269 points at close. The index remained volatile, moving within a relatively narrow range during the session. Cement and fertiliser were among the key positive contributors while refinery and oil & gas stocks also provided support.
International oil prices slipped to their lowest level in over a week amid hopes for diplomatic progress on the Middle East conflict. The market also eyed a partial recovery in Saudi oil shipments despite regional tensions. Overall, the session reflected selective buying and a cautious improvement in sentiment, Naviwala mentioned.
In the ready market, trading volumes increased to 692.9 million shares versus Friday's tally of 576.3 million. Shares of 494 companies were traded, out of which, 238 stocks closed higher, 213 fell and 43 stood unchanged.
Tasdeeq Information topped the volumes with trading in 119.6 million shares, rising Rs0.93 to close at Rs5. Foreign investors sold shares worth Rs333.3 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

title: LNG buyers  sellers target supply diversity
description: LNG buyers  sellers target supply diversity
content:
Amid US-Iran war, importers looking for fuel alternatives from West Africa to Indonesia
Liquefied natural gas (LNG) buyers are looking to diversify sourcing as the US-Israel war against Iran cuts Gulf shipments, with importers seeking alternatives for the fuel from other suppliers ranging from West Africa to Indonesia.
While Asian governments look to lock in LNG from sellers with access to various sources, producers and trading firms want to widen supply pools by taking stakes in gas projects and buying from different countries, officials and industry executives said during last week's Gastech conference.
"A lot of governments are thinking not just diversification of the suppliers, but diversification of supply routes," Sue-Ern Tan, the Head of the International Energy Agency's regional cooperation centre in Singapore, said at Gastech.
The diversification push could boost projects outside the US and Qatar, which dominate planned capacity additions, although Qatar's LNG infrastructure was damaged early in the war.
Thai state firm PTT is looking to Oman, North America and West Africa for supplies, Bandhit Thamprajamchit, Chief Operating Officer of its upstream petroleum and gas business, said. Its trading arm inked a long-term deal with Norway's Equinor for supply on Friday.
Before the Iran war effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, Bangladesh was reliant on Qatar for the bulk of its LNG imports. Now, it is looking at Indonesia, Australia and China, Bangladesh's Power Minister Iqbal Hasan Mahmud told the conference.
Early in the Iran war, Asian state energy buyers were forced to buy replacement cargoes from the spot market, with the likes of PetroChina and India's GAIL able to swing to other regions for replacement supply, but paying premiums to do so.
Despite the loss of 36 million metric tons of supply from the Middle East, new capacity additions meant that the net supply loss this year is only around 5 million tons, or 1%-1.5% of global supply, Tom Summers, Executive Vice President for LNG Marketing and Trading at Shell, said at the conference. An additional 70 to 80 new LNG vessels each year also provides more shipping flexibility, he said.
High LNG prices and demand for diversified supplies have boosted the prospects for new producers such as Argentina, East Timor and Tanzania, according to the conference speakers.

title: Power demand rebounds 5 1   driven by incentives
description: Power demand rebounds 5 1   driven by incentives
content:
Hydel, coal boost electricity generation in August; FCA pressure persists
Pakistan's power demand showed a strong recovery in August 2026, rising 5.1% year-on-year to 14,943 megawatts (MW), as lower tariffs, industrial incentives and improving economic activity supported electricity consumption.
August demand was 1.4% higher than the seven-year average for the month, although it remained below the peak of 16,176 MW recorded in August 2021, according to an analysis of the power sector by AHL.
"Power demand showed a meaningful recovery in Aug'26, rising 5.1% YoY to 14,943 MW, and standing 1.4% above the seven-year Aug average," noted the report. "While still below the 16,176MW peak recorded in Aug'21, the rebound is encouraging for power-sector activity and broader economic growth."
Power generation also exceeded the level envisaged under the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) reference, a development that could support future quarterly tariff adjustments (QTAs). The increase was attributed to lower tariffs, the shift of industrial consumers towards the national grid, incremental consumption packages for industrial and agricultural users and improving economic activity.
Large-scale manufacturing (LSM) output increased 3% year-on-year in July 2026, providing further support to electricity demand. However, the recovery has been accompanied by persistent fuel-cost pressures. Adjusted fuel cost stood at Rs8.83 per kilowatt-hour (kWh) in August, against a reference cost of Rs7.10/kWh, prompting distribution companies (DISCOs) to seek a positive fuel cost adjustment (FCA) of Rs1.73/kWh.
The higher FCA was primarily driven by increased reliance on re-gasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) and furnace oil (FO), while elevated international oil prices added to generation costs. FO-based generation jumped 49% month-on-month to 321 gigawatt-hours (GWh) in August following disruptions to RLNG supplies and stronger summer demand. The higher utilisation is expected to support earnings of companies operating under hybrid take-or-pay arrangements.
Meanwhile, LNG-based generation fell 51.7% year-on-year to 1,052 GWh amid a sharp reduction in LNG imports linked to geopolitical disruptions. Of seven long-term cargoes scheduled for August, Pakistan State Oil imported only one under its long-term contract at 13.37%.
The cargo cost was also pushed higher by international oil prices, lifting RLNG fuel cost to Rs45.93/kWh, the second-highest level on record. Overall generation cost increased 37.6% year-on-year. RLNG and FO together accounted for 42% of the unadjusted fuel cost, contributing Rs3.23/kWh and Rs0.97/kWh, respectively, out of the total Rs10.01/kWh.
Lower-cost sources partly offset the pressure. Hydel generation rose 2.5% year-on-year to 5,654 GWh, 17% above the long-term August average. Coal generation surged 53% to 3,956 GWh, its highest August output, as imported-coal generation more than doubled. Nepra currently projects power demand growth of 1% year-on-year for calendar year 2026.

title: Iqbal seeks role in IMF talks
description: Iqbal seeks role in IMF talks
content:
Says loan programme will have implications for people, economic development
Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal has sought Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's intervention to include his ministry in parleys with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), saying that the $7 billion programme is not just about numbers but about people and economic development.
His remarks came as Jamaat-e-Islami began a march towards Islamabad, demanding relief from double-digit inflation. While addressing a press conference, the minister also urged Jamaat-e-Islami, farmers, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) and the defunct Awami Action Committee to cancel their rally towards Islamabad and said that the consequent political instability would serve India's agenda.
"I have recommended to the prime minister that a representative of the Planning Commission should also be included in the team that will negotiate with the IMF," said Iqbal while responding to a question.
Pakistan-IMF talks for the fourth review of the $7 billion programme will begin on Wednesday and continue through October 7. A successful completion of the review will lead to the release of the fifth loan tranche of $1 billion under the Extended Fund Facility and another $210 million under the climate support facility.
The planning minister said that the IMF programme was not just about numbers but it would have implications for economic growth, development and people. The statement underscores the strong role of the finance ministry in the IMF programme, which has resulted in criticism from government circles and independent experts about viewing the financing facility only in relation to fiscal numbers.
The finance ministry has kept a tight control over the programme design and negotiations, which caused problems such as commitments about the agriculture sector and focusing too much on fiscal stabilisation.
The finance ministry has made petroleum levy the central point of the programme, although there is no explicit condition in the IMF document about the rate of the levy. As a result, the government has managed to improve fiscal numbers but it fueled inflation, unemployment, poverty and low economic growth.
To a question about when the prolonged economic stabilisation would end, the planning minister said that it would depend on both the positive sentiment and domestic economic structure. The government is in the fifth year of economic stabilisation, which has caused immense pain to the common man.
But the minister hoped that Pakistan may achieve over 4% economic growth in the next fiscal year, ending the low growth cycle.
Responding to a question about whether the government was facing any threat because of the upcoming four major protest movements, Iqbal labeled such agitation as fulfilling India's agenda under its Operation Sandoor-II.
The minister said that after facing defeat at the hands of Pakistan in May last year, India launched Sandoor-II to politically destabilise Pakistan. He urged all political movements not to indirectly support the Indian agenda.
Jamaat-e-Islami on Sunday began its march towards Islamabad against the unjustified petroleum prices. AJK's defunct Awami Action Committee has also planned to march towards Islamabad while farmers have threatened to start the march on September 25 against the government's "anti-farmer" policies. The PTI has announced plans for a long march from September 27.
To a question, Ahsan Iqbal said that JI's demand to reduce fuel prices was not justified as the prices were driven by international events. When he was told how India and Bangladesh were managing low fuel prices despite the Middle East conflict, the minister said that India had large buffers to absorb such shocks while the Bangladesh state-owned company took a hit.
Iqbal said that the federal government could not meet JI's demand for interest rate reduction by 2% as the monetary policy was set by the central bank. He was hopeful about finding a solution, saying that the government was still engaged with JI and its demands would again be presented to the PM on his return from a 10-day foreign visit.
The minister said that PTI's youth should ask its leadership why it did not deposit 190 million pound sterling in the national kitty instead of giving it to the owner of Bahria Town projects. A money laundering case should be registered against Imran Khan, said the planning minister.
Iqbal stressed that Pakistan's political disputes should be resolved through constitutional and democratic institutions, adding that the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz had pursued its political and legal cases in parliament and courts and it never conspired against Pakistan.
He added that no one would be allowed to play with Pakistan's future and emphasised that instability and disorder could undermine the country's economic development process.
The minister noted that the external sector had started showing signs of improvement with both remittances and exports growing during July and August and foreign exchange reserves reaching $21.3 billion.
Tola Associates on Monday released a paper, which stated that Pakistan could meet its external financing needs without the IMF. By adopting a rationalisation policy, Pakistan can achieve a net benefit of $21 billion against the requirement of $27 billion, which can be used for repaying the rollover amount in one year.

title: Auto profits surge 39  on higher sales  financing
description: Auto profits surge 39  on higher sales  financing
content:
At PAAPAM conference, PM coordinator underscores faster transition to electric mobility
The combined profitability of automobile companies listed on the KSE-100 index increased by 39.2% year-on-year to Rs28.4 billion during the quarter ended June 2026, supported by strong vehicle sales, new model launches and a substantial rise in auto financing, according to an Arif Habib Limited (AHL) research report.
The sector's cumulative revenue grew by 33.7% to Rs310.9 billion, while gross profit increased by 29% to Rs46.9 billion. The sector posted an overall gross margin of 15.1% and a net margin of 9.1%.
Sales of passenger cars, light commercial vehicles and 4x4s rose by 32.4% to 62,416 units during the quarter, compared with 47,155 units in the same period of last year.
Improved access to financing also supported demand. Outstanding auto financing climbed by 38% year-on-year to Rs381.69 billion by the end of June 2026, compared with Rs277 billion a year earlier. The sector's other income increased by 53.5% to Rs11.4 billion, mainly due to one-off gains related to the Sindh Infrastructure Development Cess and higher returns on cash balances. Sazgar Engineering Works emerged as the sector's largest earnings contributor, posting a 150.6% increase in quarterly profit to Rs8.7 billion. Its revenue surged by 180.7%, supported by a more than twofold rise in four-wheeler sales to 6,549 units and deliveries of the Tank 500.
Atlas Honda's earnings rose by 25.2% to Rs6 billion, while Honda Atlas Cars recorded a threefold increase in profit to Rs2.5 billion. Millat Tractors' earnings increased by 36.3% to Rs1.8 billion as its sales volume grew by 42.4%.
Indus Motor's profit, however, declined by 5.4% to Rs6.1 billion amid lower revenue and growing competition. Ghandhara Automobiles' consolidated profit fell by 14.6% to Rs1.6 billion, while Ghandhara Industries' earnings remained broadly unchanged at Rs1.7 billion.
Industry-wide tractor sales grew by 42.6% to 8,499 units, while truck sales rose by 37.2% to 2,561 units. Two-wheeler sales advanced by 27.4% to 530,481 units during the period under review.
Coordinator to the Prime Minister for Commerce and Industries Rana Ihsan Afzal Khan has underscored the need for competitive localisation, technological advancement and a faster transition towards electric mobility to secure the future of Pakistan's automotive industry.
He expressed these views while addressing the automotive industry leaders, government stakeholders and representatives of academia at the Paapam Symposium, held on the second day of the Pakistan International Auto Show 2026 at the Lahore International Expo Centre.
Organised by the Pakistan Association of Automotive Parts and Accessories Manufacturers (Paapam), the symposium was held under the theme "Competitiveness – Localisation and Electric Mobility."
Before speaking at the conference, the coordinator visited the stalls of local and international exhibitors and held discussions with industry representatives. He toured stalls of leading automobile companies, including emerging electric vehicle manufacturers.
Rana Ihsan Afzal appreciated the exhibitors and manufacturers for their vital contribution to the growth, innovation and development of Pakistan's automotive industry.
Addressing the gathering, he said localisation must go beyond domestic production and be strategically aligned with global competitiveness, affordability, quality and reliability. He stressed that consumers must be provided with greater choice and confidence through a competitive and technologically advanced automotive ecosystem.
Highlighting the sector's substantial economic footprint, the PM coordinator said every vehicle produced in Pakistan supported an extensive value chain comprising manufacturers, vendors, engineers, technicians and workers. The automotive sector contributes nearly 4% to the national GDP and provides employment to millions of Pakistanis.
He reaffirmed the government's resolve to work closely with industry stakeholders on developing policies that would be inclusive, future-oriented, consistent and fair.
Commending the auto industry for its resilience and continued growth despite challenging economic conditions, Rana Ihsan Afzal said the time had come for the sector to prepare decisively for emerging technologies, particularly electric vehicles. "The future of Pakistan's automotive industry lies in competitive localisation, innovation and electric mobility. The government remains committed to creating an enabling environment in which the industry can grow, invest and compete internationally," he said.

title: Strong dollar pulls gold down
description: Strong dollar pulls gold down
content:
Bullion falls Rs2,700 as Fed rate hike bets lift greenback; rupee gains three paisa
Gold prices in Pakistan fell on Monday, tracking a decline in international bullion prices, as expectations of further monetary tightening by the US Federal Reserve strengthened the dollar and weighed on the precious metal.
The price of gold per tola dropped Rs2,700 to Rs457,536, according to rates released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association. The price of 10-gram gold declined Rs2,315 to Rs392,263.
The latest fall followed a Rs100 decline in the per-tola gold price on Saturday, when bullion closed at Rs460,236.
In the international market, spot gold was down 0.6% at $4,350.39 per ounce by 11:40 am ET (1540 GMT), after falling more than 1% earlier to a session low of $4,322.19, as per Reuters. US gold futures were down 0.8% at $4,388.40.
Market expectations for further US monetary tightening have increased pressure on gold by supporting the dollar. Traders now see an 88% chance of a December rate hike, according to the FedWatch Tool. Gold generally faces pressure when expectations of higher interest rates increase, while a stronger dollar makes bullion more expensive for holders of other currencies.
The market is also assessing comments from US Federal Reserve officials on persistent inflation. Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari has said inflation remains too high across sectors of the US economy, adding to expectations that monetary policy could remain restrictive. Interactive Commodities Director Adnan Agar said international gold prices traded within a broad range of around $4,250 to $4,400 in the past 10 to 15 days, with the market yet to establish a clear new direction. He said gold touched a high of $4,383 and a low of $4,322 during Monday's session and was trading around $4,354.
According to Agar, movements in oil prices are also influencing bullion sentiment. Although oil declined on Monday, the possibility of another increase in energy prices was keeping gold from establishing a stronger upward move. He said physical demand for gold continued to increase, which could provide support to prices despite short-term volatility. Agar added that there was a possibility of gold entering another upward leg in the coming month or thereafter, potentially reaching $5,000 or above. He also said he expected downside to remain limited, with $4,100 representing a potential lower level under his market assessment.
Meanwhile, the price of silver remained unchanged at Rs7,100 per tola in the domestic market. Moreover, the Pakistani rupee gained Rs0.03 to close at Rs277.22 against the US dollar in the inter-bank market.

title: 65m EU grants signed
description: 65m EU grants signed
content:
Funding to support development, renewable energy, rule of law, dispute resolution
The government of Pakistan and the European Union on Monday signed three grant agreements worth a total € 65 million (Rs20.64 billion) to launch three programmes: the "Global Gateway Development Facilitation for Pakistan", "Energy and Natural Environment Resilience in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa" and "EU Support to the Rule of Law and Business Environment in Pakistan".
The agreements were signed by EU Ambassador Raimundas Karoblis and Economic Affairs Division Secretary Muhammad Humair Karim.
Funded under the EU's Multiannual Indicative Programme 2021-2027, the initiatives focus on three main aspects of Pakistan's development. The "Global Gateway Development Facilitation for Pakistan: Investment Management and Financial Enabling Environment" project aims to attract more foreign investment by improving the tax system and strengthening the Pakistan government's long-term financial planning.
The "Energy and Natural Environment Resilience Programme in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa" is designed to expand renewable energy in rural communities that are not connected to the electricity grid. It will also provide training to help attract private investment and increase private-sector involvement in K-P's energy sector.
Building on the previous EU assistance, the "EU Support to the Rule of Law and Business Environment in Pakistan" will further help people to access the police, prosecution, courts and legal aid in K-P and Balochistan. The programme will also support Punjab and Sindh in expanding the use of alternative and commercial dispute resolution mechanisms in legal cases so that more European and other companies show interest in investing in these provinces.
The EU's development cooperation with Pakistan remains focused on economic development, climate resilience, governance and the rule of law, human rights and sustainable natural resources.
Speaking on the occasion, Karim expressed his appreciation for the EU's continued support and partnership. He highlighted the timely nature of interventions, highlighting their strong relevance to Pakistan's goals of increased foreign investment, improved access to electricity in off-grid rural areas in K-P and more advanced standards in the rule of law and the resolution of commercial disputes.
Ambassador Karoblis stated, "These agreements demonstrate the EU's commitment to supporting Pakistan's economic development and investment ambitions under our flagship Global Gateway initiative. They will also support the authorities in K-P to build a stronger and resilient energy sector while promoting the sustainable management of natural resources."

title: Closed steel mill causes Rs79b loss
description: Closed steel mill causes Rs79b loss
content:
PSM incurs Rs57b in interest over 3 years; pays Rs3.9b in salaries, Rs9.1b in bills
The closed Pakistan Steel Mills (PSM) cumulatively caused a whopping loss of over Rs79 billion in the past three fiscal years, of which Rs57.5 billion was booked in interest expenses, as the finance ministry ignored advice to restructure the debt of the closed unit.
According to statistics provided by the Ministry of Industries, a loss of Rs24 billion was booked in the last fiscal year 2025-26 alone, despite the fact that the factory had been shut down by the government of Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz in June 2015.
Details revealed that employees were still getting salaries; there were also expenses on fuel, electricity, water and gas and above all, the government was paying a huge interest on past loans.
From fiscal year 2023-24 to fiscal year 2025-26, the PSM caused Rs79.3 billion losses, which was the period when Shehbaz Sharif was the prime minister, except for a brief period of eight months for the caretaker setup, according to the official statistics.
Out of these losses, Rs57.4 billion, or 72%, was because of interest costs of past loans. The statistics further disclosed that the annual cost on interest payments was Rs17.7 billion in the last fiscal year, which was about Rs1.3 billion less than the preceding year due to low interest rates.
Out of the Rs17.7 billion, Rs11.8 billion was paid in interest on the government loan. Another Rs5.2 billion was paid as interest cost on commercial banks' loans.
In the Review TV programme – Pakistan's only prime time show on the economy – it had been highlighted that in the first half of the last fiscal year, the closed mill caused a loss of nearly Rs13 billion.
More alarming was that the federal government did not restructure the PSM debt, which was mainly in the shape of a cash development loan by the finance ministry and the National Bank of Pakistan. The finance ministry ignored the advice of its own Central Monitoring Unit (CMU), which traces the progress of state-owned companies.
As of fiscal year 2024-25, the cash development loan for PSM stood at Rs108 billion, on which the finance ministry was charging around Rs11.5 billion in annual interest cost, according to the CMU. It also reported over Rs40 billion in bank loans, mainly from the government-owned NBP.
The Express Tribune had reported in 2016, a year after the closure of PSM, that the government and NBP were in negotiations for the settlement of PSM loans. However, after the lapse of a decade, the government was still paying interest on those loans.
The CMU report on the performance of state-owned enterprises for fiscal year 2024-25 revealed that the unit had recommended debt restructuring for PSM. "Debt restructuring, including debt-to-equity swaps and negotiated write-downs, is essential to reduce the liabilities blocking potential strategic investment (in PSM)," reported the CMU, but it was never implemented.
There was also heavy debt on the balance sheet – contingent liabilities like fuel, utilities and pensions. The PSM plant was obsolete. The CMU had advised that a government-led debt cleanup exercise should be undertaken and liabilities should be carved out into a holding company.
The CMU further said that interest was accruing despite zero operations and legacy debt accumulating purely as a fiscal deadweight. It added that Rs40 billion guarantees were required to prevent default, but the entity remains non-operational.
The CMU said that PSM was saddled by unsustainable debt and liabilities accrued over decades of non-operational status, creating an ongoing fiscal drain through wage subsidies and debt servicing. Technological obsolescence, absence of modernisation, and the lack of production capacity have rendered PSM uncompetitive against imported steel, leading to a complete loss of domestic market share.
It recommended that forming joint ventures with global steel manufacturers could bring technical expertise, foreign capital, and access to the export market as well as facilitate integration into regional value chains.
Without reforms in subsidy governance, debt management, and operational modernisation, Pakistan's trading SOEs and PSM will remain persistent fiscal liabilities, according to the CMU.
The Ministry of Industries' statistics showed that in the past three fiscal years, Rs3.9 billion was paid in salaries to employees of the closed mill. But compared to the preceding year, there was a 50% reduction in salary payments in fiscal year 2025-26.
Moreover, in the past three years, Rs9.1 billion was paid on account of fuel, power, water and gas charges of a closed factory. But compared to the preceding year, there was a one-third reduction in these charges in the last fiscal year.
