'Daredevil: Born Again' will end with Season 3 as Charlie Cox returns for the final Disney+ Marvel chapter in 2027
Marvel’s Daredevil: Born Again will conclude with its upcoming third season on Disney+, bringing the latest chapter of Charlie Cox’s return as Matt Murdock to an end.
The series, which stars Cox as the blind lawyer and vigilante Daredevil, has been confirmed to end after Season 3. The third and final season has already completed production and is expected to premiere on Disney+ in 2027.
The news marks the end of Daredevil: Born Again after three seasons on the streaming platform. The series is part of the Marvel Cinematic Universe and continues the story of Cox’s Matt Murdock, who first appeared as Daredevil in Netflix’s Marvel series.
Production on Season 3 wrapped several months ago, although Disney+ and Marvel Studios have not yet announced an exact release date. Further details about the final season’s storyline and its place within the wider Marvel Cinematic Universe have also not been revealed.
Cox returned to the role of Daredevil in Daredevil: Born Again , which brought the character back into the MCU following the conclusion of the original Daredevil series in 2018. The Disney+ series also features several returning cast members from the earlier show alongside new characters.
The upcoming third season will therefore serve as the conclusion to Daredevil: Born Again , rather than continuing into a fourth season.
The Hollywood Reporter first reported that the Marvel series would end with Season 3, while Variety subsequently confirmed the news.
With production already complete, Daredevil: Born Again Season 3 is currently slated to arrive on Disney+ in 2027. Marvel has yet to announce additional details about the final season or its release schedule.

title: Presley Gerber   s family breaks silence after his death at 27
description: Presley Gerber   s family mourns his death at 27 as Cindy Crawford  Rande and Kaia Gerber ask for privacy
content:
Presley Gerber’s family mourns his death at 27 as Cindy Crawford, Rande and Kaia Gerber ask for privacy
Presley Gerber’s parents, Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber, and his sister, Kaia Gerber, are mourning his death at the age of 27.
The model died on September 20 at a rehabilitation facility, according to the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. An autopsy has been completed, but his cause of death has been deferred. His family confirmed his death and requested privacy during the difficult time.
A source close to Kaia told PEOPLE that the family is “in total shock” and “saddened beyond words” following Presley’s death. Another source who has been close to Crawford said the family remained consistently supportive of Presley throughout his struggles.
Presley had spoken publicly about his mental health and substance use in recent years. In November 2025, he launched a social media series called “Mental Health Mondays”, aiming to encourage more open conversations about mental health.
His family also supported his efforts to discuss his experiences publicly. In June, Presley attended a mental health-focused event in Malibu with Crawford and Rande, where he spoke about vulnerability and his personal journey.
Kaia also discussed her brother’s struggles with addiction in an August interview with Vogue, describing him as a “teacher” because of his openness about his experiences.
Presley, who was 27 at the time of his death, was the only son of Crawford and Rande. He followed his mother and sister into modelling, signing with DNA Models at 15 and later working with several major fashion brands. He also appeared alongside Crawford in a Pepsi Super Bowl commercial in 2018.
As the family mourns Presley, those close to them say his efforts to encourage open conversations about mental health remain an important part of how he is remembered.

title: Everyone is an expert on awareness
description: Everyone now carries a phone with a camera
content:
Everyone now carries a phone with a camera
In a government hall in Karachi, a heatwave awareness seminar is underway. Four speakers sit on stage, a hundred chairs are filled, a banner carries the sponsor's logo, and a photographer moves through the room. By the end there is applause, a flurry of social media posts, and a newspaper photo announcing that an awareness campaign has been held.
Nobody asks the only question that matters. Did anyone's awareness change? Did the daily wage labourers working outside at noon, the people genuinely at risk, get anything out of it? Usually nobody knows, because nobody asked.
I have spent nearly twenty-eight years working in environmental public awareness in Pakistan, and this scene has played out, in one form or another, for most of that time. Technology changed. Social media arrived. Everyone now carries a phone with a camera. But the underlying method has stayed almost exactly the same: pick a topic, print a poster, hold an event, take a photo, publish a post. If the tools changed but the method never did, are we actually learning, or just repeating ourselves?
Here is the deeper problem. In Pakistan's environmental sector, an unusual confidence is common. Journalists, activists, advocacy groups, teachers, officials and corporate social responsibility teams will all happily explain how public awareness should be done. Almost nobody says, this is not my area. That is not an accusation, it is an observation. Caring about the environment and knowing how to design environmental public awareness are two different skills. A person can be an excellent reporter, an effective campaigner or a gifted teacher, without ever having learned how a real awareness intervention is designed, delivered and measured.
Start with a distinction that keeps getting lost. Environmental awareness simply means a person knows something, say that plastic is harmful. Environmental public awareness is different: a communication process someone deliberately designs around one specific problem, for one specific audience, with one clear goal. Knowing plastic is harmful is just a fact about a person's mind. Asking why shopkeepers in one part of Karachi still use plastic bags, and what would make them switch, is a plan. Turning that plan into reality takes concrete steps: defining the true problem, gathering solid evidence instead of a few internet facts, identifying which audience must change and which audience can help or block that change, ordering the message, picking the right channel and measuring results before and after. Skip a step and what is left is not public awareness. It is only information handed out, mistaken for being something more.
This confusion shows up everywhere. A cleanup walk branded 'Say No To Plastic' generates good photographs but does nothing to change the daily shopping habit that created the waste. Air quality numbers get shared with no accompanying action a person can take, so they generate anxiety instead of change. Tree plantation drives announce impressive numbers of saplings planted in a day, and almost never report how many survived six months later. Waste segregation instructions are handed to households with no explanation of what happens after the truck arrives, and often the answer is that everything gets remixed anyway. In every case, the professional version is not more expensive. It simply asks a different first question: who needs to change, why haven't they already, and how will we know if they did.
Part of the reason this keeps happening is that the sector rewards the wrong things. Attendance counts, photographs, banners, media coverage and social media likes are treated as results. They are not. They are signs that an event occurred, nothing more. A genuine outcome assessment looks at what changed in people's knowledge, perceived risk, intention and practice, measured before an intervention and again afterward. This is not complicated work, usually just a short set of questions asked twice. The barrier has never been the difficulty of measurement. It has been the absence of any will to measure at all.
There is also a quieter problem worth naming honestly. Public relations and environmental public awareness are not the same thing, even though they get treated as interchangeable. Public relations build an institution's reputation. Public awareness changes public understanding and behaviour on a defined issue. Confusing the two is one of the most damaging habits in this field, because it lets an institution declare victory the moment it gets a good photograph, regardless of whether anyone's behavior actually moved.
There is also a stranger phenomenon worth admitting. People with only partial environmental knowledge, enough to speak confidently, not enough to tell science apart from advocacy, from public relations, from public awareness, often resist correction harder than complete newcomers do. A little knowledge convinces someone he already knows everything.
None of this requires an imported theory. It requires government agencies to fund permanent awareness units instead of one off events, universities to teach environmental communication as its own discipline, NGOs to separate awareness work from general event management, media houses to distinguish journalism from campaigning, professionals to accept that working around a topic does not make one an expert in it, and donors to demand measurable outcomes instead of headcounts and photographs.
We have spent decades running activities in the name of environmental awareness. We have rarely stopped to ask whether that awareness actually works, on whom, and why. That is the question this field now has to face, well beyond the photographs, the numbers and the banners.

title: Nothing happened at midnight
description: Programmers worked overtime  examining systems and correcting the suspected fault
content:
Programmers worked overtime, examining systems and correcting the suspected fault
The development of full artificial intelligence could spell the end of the human race. Stephen Hawking
In late 1999, at PIDC House, Karachi, a task force at Pakistan Petroleum Limited was probably worrying about what would happen when the clock struck midnight on December 31. Around the world, similar meetings were taking place in banks, airlines, power plants and government offices. The fear was that computers, programmed to recognise the year through its last two digits, would mistake 2000 for 1900. A century-old error, it was feared, could bring modern life to a standstill.
Billions of dollars were spent. Programmers worked overtime, examining systems and correcting the suspected fault. Then midnight arrived. The lights remained on, aircraft continued to fly and the world carried on as usual. The catastrophe did not come. The most memorable mishap attributed to the occasion was reportedly a malfunctioning slot machine in Delaware.
The episode has since become a convenient joke about the human tendency to exaggerate the dangers of new technology. It is tempting, therefore, to place today's warnings about artificial intelligence in the same category: another expensive exercise in apprehension, another prophecy destined to disappear beneath the next day's headlines.
There is some justification for such scepticism. When Anthropic's chief executive warns that artificial intelligence could take over the internet within six months to a year, the prediction carries the urgency of a Y2K memorandum. It also comes from a company developing the safety tools that might be needed to prevent such an outcome. When those sounding the alarm are simultaneously seeking greater investment, public confidence and regulatory influence, the public is entitled to ask whether genuine concern and commercial interest are being presented as one and the same thing.
Yet the comparison with Y2K has a serious limitation. The millennium bug was a known technical defect. Its cause could be identified, its consequences tested and its correction implemented. Engineers knew what they were looking for. The world was not saved by a miracle at midnight. It was saved, in large measure, by years of painstaking work that prevented the anticipated failures.
Artificial intelligence presents a different challenge. Nobody, including those who develop the most advanced systems, fully understands how a model trained on vast quantities of human knowledge will behave when given a complicated objective and considerable freedom to pursue it. It may find solutions its creators did not anticipate, or pursue an instruction in a manner its designers never intended.
That is not a calendar error waiting for a software patch. It is an open question about the behaviour of increasingly capable machines. Anyone who declares with absolute confidence that artificial intelligence will destroy civilisation, or that it will certainly remain harmless, is perhaps revealing more about his temperament than about the technology itself.
There is, nevertheless, room for a little humour. Consider the dramatic picture sometimes offered by the more excitable commentators: artificial intelligence awakens in a distant data centre, seizes control of the internet and proceeds to take command of humanity. But what happens next? Does it spend the afternoon arguing with another machine over a coding error? Does it fail a traffic-light security test and politely request another attempt? The prospect of humans wandering about in smart glasses and wireless earbuds, awaiting instructions from a server rack, sounds at times less like a security assessment than a conversation in a university hostel after midnight.
But ridicule is not an argument. The sceptics are right that fear attracts attention and that dramatic predictions can serve commercial purposes. Humanity has a long history of panicking over new inventions. The telephone, radio and television were all once accused of threatening the human mind. Not every warning about a new invention deserves to be treated as a forecast of disaster.
The concern about artificial intelligence, however, rests on a difference that should not be dismissed. A conventional computer generally follows instructions written by people. An advanced AI system learns patterns from enormous quantities of information and may discover ways of pursuing a task that its creators did not foresee. During testing, Anthropic and OpenAI have both reported instances in which their models behaved outside the boundaries of the tasks assigned to them. Such incidents do not prove that machines are about to seize control of the world. They do, however, demonstrate that these systems deserve serious examination.
The sensible response lies somewhere between panic and complacency. We need the discipline with which the aviation industry approaches a new aircraft: confidence supported by evidence, careful records, repeated testing and a refusal to overlook a warning simply because the journey has so far been uneventful.
Nothing happened at midnight in 1999, and that was a triumph of preparation rather than proof that the fears had been foolish. Artificial intelligence may yet benefit humanity enormously. It may also create dangers that are difficult to anticipate. We can laugh at the extravagant predictions while taking genuine risks seriously. That may be the wisest way to enter an age in which machines are becoming cleverer, and humans are still trying to understand what they have created.
Perhaps the deeper question is not whether artificial intelligence will become a Frankenstein, but whether its creators will have the wisdom to keep it under human control. In the end, the matter may be summed up in a modest couplet of my own which, though metaphysical in its wider meaning, carries a potent metaphorical connotation in the context of AI.
Hum ko to banaya tha faqat aik Khuda nai
Hum nai to bana dalai kaee aik khuda aur

title: Listening to the Universe s whisper
description: Mavalvala is scheduled to deliver the University of Karachi s ORIC Distinguished Lecture
content:
Mavalvala is scheduled to deliver the University of Karachi's ORIC Distinguished Lecture
The return of Professor Nergis Mavalvala to Karachi in September 2026 is more than a distinguished scientist's homecoming. It is a reminder that curiosity nurtured in an ordinary childhood can eventually reach the farthest corners of the universe - and that geography need never define the boundaries of intellectual ambition.
Born in Lahore and raised in Karachi, Mavalvala attended the Convent of Jesus and Mary before leaving Pakistan in 1986 to study in the US. Her journey subsequently took her from Wellesley College to MIT, Caltech and the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory, better known as LIGO. Today, she is Dean of MIT's School of Science and one of the world's leading experimental physicists.
Yet the most inspiring part of her story may lie in its modest beginnings. As a child, she enjoyed taking things apart, understanding mechanisms and repairing bicycles. These activities may have appeared unremarkable, but they cultivated the instincts essential to experimental science: curiosity, patience, mechanical intuition, confidence with tools and the willingness to try repeatedly after failure.
On Sept 22, Mavalvala is scheduled to deliver the University of Karachi's ORIC Distinguished Lecture, "Listening to the Universe Above the Quantum Din", in collaboration with the Department of Physics and the Institute of Space Science and Technology. Three days later, she will deliver Habib University's 10th Yohsin Lecture, "The Joy of Discovery: Curiosity, Science, and the Pivotal Role of Universities".
Since both lectures are yet to take place, their precise arguments remain to be heard. Nevertheless, their titles illuminate two complementary dimensions of Mavalvala's career: the experimental physicist attempting to measure some of nature's faintest signals, and the academic leader concerned with creating institutions in which curiosity can flourish.
Mavalvala's scientific work forms part of the extraordinary collective endeavour that transformed gravitational waves from a prediction of Einstein's general theory of relativity into observable signals. These waves are minute disturbances in space-time produced by violent cosmic events, such as colliding black holes. By the time they reach Earth, their effects are almost unimaginably small.
Detecting them required LIGO to measure changes in distance far smaller than an atomic nucleus. Scientists had to control seismic vibrations, thermal motion, laser instability, environmental disturbances and even quantum fluctuations in light. Mavalvala contributed to this effort through research in precision measurement and techniques involving "squeezed" light, which help reduce quantum noise and improve detector sensitivity.
In 2015, LIGO detected gravitational waves from two merging black holes. Humanity had acquired an entirely new means of observing the cosmos. We were no longer dependent solely upon light; we had learned, metaphorically, to listen to the universe.
That achievement offers a powerful lesson for Pakistan. Breakthroughs rarely emerge from impatience. They grow through decades of sustained inquiry, institutional support, collaboration and repeated failure. Fundamental science may not always promise immediate commercial returns, yet it frequently produces technologies and insights that could never have been predicted at the beginning.
Our universities must therefore become more than degree-awarding institutions. They should be places where questions are encouraged, laboratories function, merit is protected, mentors inspire, and young researchers are permitted to fail intelligently.
Mavalvala's visit should inspire celebration, but it should also provoke reflection. Pakistan must not be content merely to honour its talented people after other countries have provided them with the ecosystems necessary to succeed. We must create those conditions at home.
For every young person who has dismantled a machine, repaired a bicycle, stared at the night sky or asked one question too many, Mavalvala's journey carries a hopeful message: curiosity is not a distraction from achievement. It is where achievement begins. Karachi will soon listen to a scientist who helped humanity hear the universe. Our greater responsibility is to ensure that the curious minds listening to her are given every opportunity to discover their own worlds.

title: Beyond brick and mortar
description: Government must recruit qualified teachers  ensure basic facilities like toilets  clean drinking water  electricity
content:
Government must recruit qualified teachers, ensure basic facilities like toilets, clean drinking water, electricity
It's indeed good news. The Sindh government, per the Chief Minister, has almost completed the construction, rehabilitation or upgradation of as many as 838 schools with plans underway to launch a massive enrollment drive targeting 250,000 students. This offers a rare glimmer of hope for the province's embattled education sector. As the CM himself noted, while brick-and-mortar investments are commendable, the true gauge of educational progress lies not in the concrete poured, but in the children enrolled and retained.
The scale of the challenge ahead cannot be overemphasised: out of Pakistan's 26.2 million out-of-school children, a staggering 7.4 million reside in Sindh alone. If these new structures are to become beacons of actual learning, the government must ensure an enabling environment for learning. Introducing 250,000 students to these classrooms requires a dual approach: a targeted, urgent enrollment campaign and an aggressive retention strategy. First, the enrollment drive must go straight to the doorstep. The government should partner with local lady health workers, civil society groups and community leaders to find and register out-of-school children. To incentivise poor families, the government must expand targeted conditional cash transfers and provide free school transport. Second, getting children through the door is only half the battle; keeping them there is the real measure of success. The government must recruit qualified teachers and ensure basic facilities like toilets, clean drinking water and electricity.
While this infrastructure is a vital first step, much more remains to be done. Only by cultivating community trust, offering financial incentives and ensuring strict institutional accountability can Sindh hope to bring 250,000 children back to school.

title: Online predators
description: Pakistan must therefore avoid the temptation to substitute prohibition for protection
content:
Pakistan must therefore avoid the temptation to substitute prohibition for protection
The internet has become another hunting ground for sexual predators, and Pakistan's children are paying a heavy price for the failure to protect them. A recent Unicef report estimates that 1.5 million children in the country experienced online sexual abuse in a single year. More disturbing is the finding that 71% of victims never disclosed their ordeal, while none of the children surveyed who experienced abuse approached formal reporting channels.
Children are being exploited in an environment where perpetrators can operate with relative impunity, while victims are silenced by the fear of social condemnation. Nearly three-quarters of children aged between 12 and 17 now use the internet, and methods employed by predators are becoming increasingly sophisticated. What begins as an innocent conversation or an interaction on a gaming platform can develop into months of calculated manipulation, culminating in sexual extortion and blackmail. Yet, the greater tragedy is that children often have more to fear from the reaction to their abuse than from reporting the crime itself. Girls, in particular, risk being withdrawn from school or subjected to restrictions on their freedom if their ordeal becomes public. Such attitudes punish the victim while allowing the offender to escape scrutiny. The growing menace has prompted governments across the world to reconsider children's access to social media. However, a blanket ban is neither a comprehensive solution nor a substitute for effective regulation.
Pakistan must therefore avoid the temptation to substitute prohibition for protection. The responsibility for ensuring children's safety cannot rest solely with parents or young internet users. Technology companies must be compelled to introduce stronger safeguards against predatory contact and age-appropriate protections. At the same time, the state must ensure that such measures do not become a pretext for indiscriminate surveillance or restrictions on legitimate digital access.

title: The capital at a standstill
description: Compounding these tensions  the federal government says it is mulling Governor s rule in K P
content:
Compounding these tensions, the federal government says it is mulling Governor's rule in K-P
The political stakes are hitting a fever pitch as the government and the opposition engage in a fierce war of narratives. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has issued a stern warning against letting the PTI besiege the federal capital - a stance backed up by the preemptive arrest of Imran Khan's three sisters in Lahore under the MPO Ordinance. The upcoming September 27 march has triggered a massive security clampdown. Entry routes to Islamabad are heavily sealed, while security forces have been placed on high alert with 22,000 additional personnel requested from Punjab, AJK and Sindh.
Compounding these tensions, the federal government says it is mulling Governor's rule in K-P. Such a drastic measure will undoubtedly invite further trouble, pushing political instability to a new high. It is also a given that political parties on the fringes - and even some within the ruling coalition, including the PPP - will take exception to it, forcing the government into a challenging new zone of discomfort.
Outlawing the PTI is an equally unworkable option for a party that has already been pushed to the wall and is operating in full agitating mode. The crisis necessitates a middle ground, where the PTI can display political foresight by stepping back from the brink. Postponing the protest in favour of a meaningful dialogue represents the only viable way forward. Crucially, TTAP, the six-party opposition alliance, already holds a mandate from the PTI chief to negotiate with the power wielders. This opens a window to strike a deal centred on restructuring the governance framework and resolving constitutional lacunas in the larger national interest.
The residents of twin cities find themselves in a nail-biting predicament, waiting to see how three overlapping protest campaigns - by Jamaat-e-Islami, farmers and the PTI - will unfold within the span of a single week. This prolonged standstill is dealing a severe blow to the local economy, as recurring threats to hold the federal capital hostage fly in the face of acceptable norms for the freedom of association.

title: The joy in the journey
description: AI companies announced solving some of the most high profile problems in mathematics
content:
AI companies announced solving some of the most high-profile problems in mathematics
As a graduate student, nearly a quarter century ago, one of my projects focused on developing computational models to study protein design. At one point, our lab had a visiting scientist who knew several professional software developers. He told my adviser that he could get one of his contacts to quickly develop software for us, something that I was struggling with. This professionally made software would not cost much (because of the contacts of the visiting scientist) and quickly get us the answers we were looking for through my research.
I still remember that conversation in my adviser's office. My adviser told the visiting scientist that while the offer was most generous and kind, he wanted me to learn myself – to struggle, figure out, make mistakes and come up with a solution. It would take time, sure, but it would give me as a young graduate student valuable knowledge, train me, and in doing so would open new worlds for me, and chart out new paths for others.
My adviser was right – the process of struggle, failure, missteps, and ultimately something meaningful was long, at times painful and uncertain, but critical for my own intellectual development. Among the research papers that came out of that journey, one was on the cover of a prestigious journal, highlighted as a major discovery in my field, and indeed opened up new worlds of research for me. Among the many things that I owe to my research adviser, recognising the value of the journey, and not just the destination, remains a cherished one.
A few weeks ago, when AI companies announced solving some of the most high-profile problems in mathematics, over two dozen Fields Medal winning mathematicians raised alarm in an eloquently written piece. The point of mathematics, they argued, is not to simply solve a problem, instead they argued "solving problems is only a tool and proxy for achieving the primary goal of conceptual understanding and insight".
Like other colleagues in research professions all across the world (including my own adviser who lived by this ideal), they recognised something precious in training, thinking, navigating and debating ideas and solutions. "The most precious resources of our profession are students and ideas and these we nurture with great care. We feel responsible to let them grow to their full potential until they can live a life of their own in the mathematical world. For students we often suggest problems with the core intention of developing skills making them well-positioned for advances in research and elsewhere. Our ideas we disseminate in talks private discussions and careful writeups connecting them to the previous ideas of others. These processes invariably take time and are based on human interaction."
I believe that the issue here is not just about the brute force approach of AI to solving problems and claiming the prize, but also asking how we view research and training in the current moment. In a research world so fixated on the next grant, and where ideas are increasingly undervalued and the entire emphasis is on 'results' (even those that do not stand up to serious intellectual scrutiny) – the world of research has become one permanent race, where 'winning' (whatever that may mean) is everything. This notion on winning means that students are told to do specific experiments, to expect certain results, and in most cases to write those results in a pre-existing format with little room for thought, doubt or curiosity. A lot is lost on this path that has no room for wonder or wander.
Sometimes modern research journey feels very much like ordering books online through one's favourite retailer. It is indeed efficient, but offers something very different from going to a bookstore. Online, you can quickly click on a button and order what you wanted to get, but in a bookstore, it may take you a little while to get what you were looking for, but while browsing the shelves there is a finite chance you may come across something that you had never expected, and that may change your life. A world where that chance disappears completely seems awfully unpleasant to me.

title: Melissa McCarthy opens up about her challenging  Gilmore Girls  role
description: Melissa McCarthy reflects on Gilmore Girls calling its dialogue    really hard    while recalling her first major TV role
content:
Melissa McCarthy reflects on Gilmore Girls calling its dialogue ‘really hard’ while recalling her first major TV role
Melissa McCarthy has reflected on her experience starring in Gilmore Girls , describing the series as “really hard” while recalling the demanding dialogue she had to perform.
McCarthy played Sookie St. James, Lorelai Gilmore’s best friend and a chef at the Independence Inn, in the series created by Amy Sherman-Palladino. Speaking to Variety on September 21, the actress discussed how the show became her first major television role.
McCarthy said Sherman-Palladino’s scripts were particularly challenging because of their lengthy, reference-filled dialogue. She recalled that the scripts could run to 93 pages and that actors were expected to follow the dialogue closely, even when they received lengthy scenes shortly before filming.
Despite the difficulty, McCarthy said the experience was valuable training. She also praised Sherman-Palladino for creating a distinctive world and maintaining her creative vision throughout the series.
Gilmore Girls premiered in 2000 and followed Lorelai and her daughter Rory, played by Lauren Graham and Alexis Bledel, as they lived in the fictional town of Stars Hollow, Connecticut. The series ran for seven seasons and 153 episodes.
McCarthy said she remains surprised that the show continues to attract younger viewers and that people still recognise her as Sookie despite her extensive career since the series ended.
The actress briefly returned as Sookie for the 2016 Netflix revival Gilmore Girls: A Year in the Life . She said she enjoyed reuniting with the cast and remains close to former co-stars Lauren Graham and Yanic Truesdale.
In August, HBO Max announced that a Gilmore Girls documentary was in development, featuring insights from Sherman-Palladino, Daniel Palladino and Graham.

content:
Premier to address UNGA on September 25, will present Pak's stance on evolving regional, global security landscape
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif arrived in New York on Monday to represent Pakistan at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), amid the Middle East crisis that threatens to embroil more countries.
The high-level segment of the 81st UNGA will be held from September 22 to 26 and on September 28, with this year's general debate theme set by the newly elected president as 'Restoring trust, managing transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all'.
The PM Office said that Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and Special Assistant Tariq Fatemi would also accompany the premier during the visit.

The prime minister will address the UNGA on September 25.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif arrives in New York to attend the 81st session of United Nations General Assembly. New York, 21 September, 2026. pic.twitter.com/6Z8t111KEf
In his address, the premier will present Pakistan's stance on the evolving regional and global security landscape, emphasising the importance of dialogue, diplomacy, and the peaceful resolution of conflicts.
PM Shehbaz will highlight Pakistan's active diplomatic and mediation efforts to de-escalate regional tensions and promote peace and stability, while also outlining the country's priorities regarding key global issues such as sustainable development, climate change, the fight against terrorism, Islamophobia, and global economic challenges.
Read More : PM trims UN delegation under austerity
The premier will also draw the international community's attention to the issues of long-standing occupation and the denial of the right to self-determination in occupied Jammu and Kashmir and Palestine.
Prime Minister @CMShehbaz arrives in New York to attend the 81st session of United Nations General Assembly @ForeignOfficePk @PakPMO @UN #UNGA #RadioPakistan pic.twitter.com/WpDzFIeFMM
On the sidelines of the UNGA session, the prime minister will participate in various high-level meetings concerning development, climate action, and other significant matters, where he will present Pakistan's position.
He will also hold bilateral meetings with world leaders and the UN secretary-general.
The Pakistani delegation was significantly streamlined as part of the government's austerity measures, and several federal ministers who had initially been expected to travel had been dropped from the trip, according to sources at the country's UN mission.
Information and Broadcasting Minister Attaullah Tarar, Minister for Climate Change and Environment Dr Musadik Malik and Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal were among those not attending, the sources added.
US President Donald Trump, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, French President Emmanuel Macron and Qatar Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani are among the leaders set to address the General Assembly on the opening day.
According to the UN's programme, the opening session will begin at 9am on September 22. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva will be the first speaker, followed by President Trump.
Nearly 130 heads of state will meet in New York as the post-World War Two order comes under strain, and the UN struggles to remain relevant while weathering attacks from Trump, who has long expressed disdain ​for the institution and has slashed US funding for many of its agencies.

title: LHC orders NCCIA not to harass Rizwan amid online betting inquiry
description: Rizwan challenged the NCCIA notice and inquiry  seeking annulment and protection from coercive action
content:
Says NCCIA may proceed with the inquiry but must not harass or unnecessarily inconvenience the cricketer
The Lahore High Court on Monday dismissed cricketer Muhammad Rizwan’s petition challenging an inquiry by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) into alleged online betting and gambling relating to cricket, holding that the probe could not be stopped at its initial stage.
Chief Justice Aalia Neelum, in a five-page order issued on Monday, ruled that the inquiry concerning allegations falling within Section 14 (Wrongful Gain) of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016, was neither without jurisdiction nor tainted with malice or mala fide intent.
However, the court directed Rizwan to join and cooperate with the proceedings, while ordering the agency not to harass or unnecessarily inconvenience him.
Rizwan had challenged the NCCIA call-up notice and the inquiry proceedings, seeking their annulment and an order restraining the authorities from taking any coercive action against him.
The record showed that the agency had issued him a notice on September 8, requiring him to appear on September 10 to record his version and clarify the allegations.
The court noted that Rizwan appeared before the agency on the specified date and subsequently submitted a written statement on September 14.
Read More: LHC refuses to hear Rizwan’s plea against NCCIA proceedings
According to the order, the NCCIA is investigating allegations of online betting and gambling relating to cricket in Pakistan. The law officer submitted that the inquiry concerned alleged electronic fraud under Section 14 of PECA and had originated from information purportedly obtained through cyber patrolling, which allegedly connected Rizwan with the matter.
Rizwan’s counsel argued that the International Cricket Council’s Anti-Corruption Unit (ACU) was the relevant authority for dealing with such allegations and that the matter had not been reported to it.
The court, however, observed that the ICC Anti-Corruption Code itself did not bar criminal proceedings by state authorities. Referring to Section 1.11 of the Code, it held that the disciplinary framework was intended to supplement, rather than undermine, applicable laws and regulations.
The judgment further noted that the ICC Code requires participants, upon request, to cooperate with the prosecuting authority, the ICC and any criminal or regulatory authority investigating matters covered by the Code.
The court held that the existence of the ICC’s disciplinary mechanism therefore did not prevent a competent state agency from conducting an inquiry under Pakistani law.
Explaining the legal nature of the call-up notice, the court said such a notice was a procedural mechanism for gathering information and did not, by itself, constitute an accusation of wrongdoing.
The court observed that the inquiry was still at an initial stage and the competent authority had yet to complete the process or determine whether any further action was warranted. It therefore declined to interfere with the proceedings.
Rizwan was given liberty to avail himself of an appropriate legal remedy if he had any grievance with the final outcome of the inquiry.
Regarding his request for the return of articles seized or confiscated from him, the court directed him to seek an appropriate remedy before the competent court.
The petition was dismissed with no order as to costs.

title: IT minister formally inaugurates    The Innovation Hive    established by USEFP
description: Innovation Hive  is a bridge that will  provide entrepreneurs from Pak with direct access to US market  investors
content:
'Innovation Hive' is a bridge that will provide entrepreneurs from Pak with direct access to US market, investors
Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja on Monday formally inaugurated "The Innovation Hive", established by the United States Educational Foundation in Pakistan (USEFP).
The ceremony was attended by US Embassy Chargé d’Affaires Natalie Baker, STEPI Pakistan CEO Dr Mazhar H Qureshi, USEFP Alumni Affairs Director Mazhar Awan and other prominent personalities.
“Talent exists everywhere in Pakistan; it just needs a place where opportunity can find it. That's what the Innovation Hive is for. This partnership reflects President Trump's vision that America's relationships abroad should deliver real results, more trade, more investment, and more prosperity for both our countries," Baker said .
Read : Federal IT minister highlights youth-led digital growth
Baker added that over its first year, the Innovation Hive would connect over 250 American mentors with entrepreneurs at every stage, and the US government would invest to support top Pakistani entrepreneurs.
Addressing the ceremony, Shaza thanked the US Embassy and USEFP, saying that ‘The Innovation Hive’ was not merely a building or an office, but a strong bridge that would provide Pakistani entrepreneurs with direct access to the US market and investors without having to leave the country, while also creating broader opportunities for young people to advance.
Highlighting the historical ties and economic cooperation between the two countries, the minister said that the US was Pakistan’s largest export market, accounting for around 20 per cent of Pakistan’s total exports during fiscal year 2025-26.
Shaza said that bilateral trade exceeded eight billion dollars in 2025, while under the Pakistan-US trade agreement reached in July 2025, US import duties on IT services, textiles and other sectors were reduced.
She added that Pakistan had, as a goodwill gesture, abolished the five per cent Digital Services Tax.
The minister also said that the combined enterprise value of Pakistan’s VC-funded startups had exceeded four billion dollars.
She said startups raised 74.2 million dollars in funding in 2025, while funding for startups founded or co-founded by women increased from 5.5 million dollars in 2024 to 10.1 million dollars in 2025.
‘The Innovation Hive’ would serve as a permanent platform connecting Pakistani talent directly with the US market, mentorship opportunities and the alumni network.
From ideas in Islamabad to ambitions in Silicon Valley, a new opportunity opens for Pakistani entrepreneurs. The US Embassy has launched Innovation Hive at USEFP in Islamabad, offering practical training, mentorship from American experts and connections to technology and… pic.twitter.com/tX8c2isb9q
Referring to key institutions and initiatives of the Ministry of IT and Telecommunication, the minister said that through nine National Incubation Centres, Ignite had supported more than 2,350 startups and created over 185,000 employment opportunities.
She said the Pakistan Startup Fund had restored the confidence of US investors by providing funding of up to 30 per cent without taking any government equity.
The Special Technology Zones Authority provided technology and AI companies with 10-year tax and customs incentives.
Read More : Iqbal sets $1tr digital goal for 2035
Concluding her address, Shaza told entrepreneurs: “The US market you want to reach is no longer across the ocean; its address is now in Islamabad. This bridge reflects the shared commitment of both countries.”
At the conclusion of the ceremony, the minister also visited various sections of the USEFP, where she was briefed on the organisation and its activities.

title: FM Dar stresses importance of GSP  status in meeting with EU foreign policy chief
description: Foreign minister s packed agenda includes discussions on Kashmir  Palestine  AI alongside talks with counterparts
content:
Dar highlights importance Pak attaches to its partnership with the EU, particularly in trade, economic cooperation
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar stressed the significance of GSP+ status for Pakistan’s trade relations with the European Union (EU) in a meeting with EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas on Monday.
According to a statement issued by the Foreign Office, the meeting took place on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), currently underway in New York.
The deputy premier highlighted the importance Pakistan attaches to its partnership with the European Union, particularly in trade and economic cooperation. He stressed the significance of GSP+ for Pakistan’s trade relations with the EU, the FO said.
The two sides also exchanged views on regional and global developments, with DPM Dar appreciating the EU’s constructive engagement with Pakistan during recent regional developments, as well as its recognition of Pakistan’s efforts towards de-escalation and dialogue.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 met EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy/Vice-President of the European Commission Kaja Kallas @KajaKallas on sidelines of 81st UN General Assembly in New York today.… pic.twitter.com/dB1qS7RgGx
He called for a return to “the path of dialogue and diplomacy” and full implementation “by all parties” of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding signed between the US and Iran earlier this year, according to the statement.
“Both sides agreed to maintain close engagement on matters of mutual interest,” the FO added.
The meeting took place against the backdrop of an intense engagement between Islamabad and Brussels over a trading scheme and its future.
The current EU GSP+ framework is set to expire at the end of this year, and Pakistan must seek inclusion in the successor regime, which would carry more stringent requirements.
Though the new trading framework would take effect with the turn of the year, Pakistan and other existing beneficiaries will continue to receive preferences during a two-year transition period ending on Dec 31, 2028.
But the transition does not automatically extend the facility for the two years or roll it over into the new scheme.
DPM Dar also met French Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of France Jean-Noël Barrot on the sidelines of the UNGA session. They reviewed the bilateral relations and agreed on utilising regional forums to address regional challenges and promote dialogue.
The FM reiterated Pakistan’s desire to further strengthen bilateral ties, including through enhanced political engagement, trade and investment, educational linkages and people-to-people exchanges.
He appreciated France’s efforts in support of the two-state solution, including its decision to restrict imports of goods from Israeli settlements.
Both ministers stressed that the Palestine issue must remain high on the international agenda and underscored the importance of sustained international efforts towards a just, lasting and comprehensive resolution.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 met Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of France Jean-Noël Barrot @jnBarrot , on sidelines of the 81st Session of UNGA in New York. Both sides reviewed Pakistan-France bilateral relations and… pic.twitter.com/EL6VpkwEpt
Regarding Iran, both sides exchanged views on the importance of continued diplomatic engagement and regional efforts to address the crisis, and highlighted the importance of implementing the Islamabad MoU.
Both ministers also stressed the need to ensure the safety and free flow of maritime traffic and uninterrupted energy supplies, given the wider economic implications of the disruptions.
The French foreign minister appreciated Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts for peace and stability in the region and agreed on the importance of utilising regional forums to address regional challenges and promote dialogue
Both sides agreed to maintain close engagement on bilateral and regional matters of mutual interest.
Dar arrived in New York earlier today to participate in the upcoming high-level week of the 81st session of the UNGA, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement.
According to the Foreign Office, Dar was received by Pakistan’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, Ambassador of Pakistan to the United States Rizwan Saeed Sheikh, Consul General New York Aamer Ahmed Atozai and officers of Pakistan’s Mission to the UN and Consulate in New York.
According to the FO, FM Dar "has a full programme of high-level engagements in the week ahead." The foreign minister "will participate in ministerial forums and deliver Pakistan’s statements and interventions on key issues of importance to Pakistan, including bilateral, regional and international priorities across the UN agenda."
Alongside accompanying Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, FM Dar "will hold a series of bilateral meetings with his counterparts and participate in a range of high-level engagements on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly," the FO said.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 arrived in New York to participate in the High-Level Week of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly. He was received by Pakistan’s Permanent Representative to the UN Ambassador Asim… pic.twitter.com/yZ4lqRjL9y
The foreign minister departed for New York from Islamabad yesterday. The FO had said that FM Dar would be in New York from September 21 to 25 to attend the UNGA, adding that he had an “extensive and wide-ranging programme” planned during the high-level week.
As part of his engagements, the FO said that FM Dar will attend a meeting of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) Contact Group on Jammu and Kashmir, where he will highlight Pakistan’s “unwavering support for the right to self-determination of the Kashmiris.” He will also attend several OIC ministerial meetings on the sidelines of the UNGA, including the OIC Foreign Ministers’ Annual Coordination Meeting and other OIC Contact Group meetings.
Read: Mideast turmoil, AI set to dominate UN gathering of world leaders
The FO added that FM Dar will attend several high-level meetings on Palestine “as a reflection of Pakistan’s strong support for the Palestinian cause.” These will include a meeting of the Group of Eight Arab Islamic countries and a high-level ministerial meeting of the Global Alliance for the Implementation of the Two-State Solution.
FM Dar is also scheduled to address a UN Security Council high-level briefing on artificial intelligence, and will additionally attend a high-level meeting on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response. The foreign minister will also chair the meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers.
Further, FM Dar will hold bilateral meetings with foreign counterparts from several countries during his visit to New York.
“During his extensive engagements, he will highlight Pakistan’s ongoing efforts for regional and international peace and stability,” the FO had said.

title: Taylor Frankie Paul quits  The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives  amid ongoing controversy
description: Taylor Frankie Paul leaves  The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives  amid legal issues and criticism from castmates
content:
Taylor Frankie Paul leaves 'The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives' amid legal issues and criticism from castmates
Taylor Frankie Paul has announced that she is stepping away from Hulu’s The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives following months of legal controversy and public disputes with cast members.
Paul announced her decision in an Instagram post on September 21, according to Variety . She thanked the networks that had supported her return to the reality series but said she no longer wanted to move forward with the show.
In the post, Paul also criticised some of her castmates, accusing them of bullying and saying that comments involving her children were “disgusting”. She said she had previously been willing to leave the series so production could continue with less tension.
The announcement comes after reports that Paul allegedly failed a court-ordered drug test during ongoing custody disputes involving her former partners, Dakota Mortensen and Tate Paul. Paul did not address the allegation in her Instagram statement, while Hulu and her representatives had not immediately responded to requests for comment.
Paul was ordered to take the test following a Utah court ruling in July. The results were initially placed under a protective order and were not publicly available. Tate Paul later filed court documents seeking to have the results unsealed.
The legal disputes began after Paul and Mortensen made domestic violence allegations against each other in March. Their relationship also became the subject of a separate video showing a physical altercation. Neither faced criminal charges, while a court granted mutual restraining orders.
Paul’s departure also follows disagreements among the cast over her planned return. Mikayla Matthews announced she had left the show, while Mayci Neeley and Layla Taylor expressed uncertainty about their futures.
Season 5 of The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives premiered on September 10, while Season 6 has been filming without Paul since July.

title: Govt increases petrol price by Rs4 61  cuts diesel by Rs1 96 for Sept 22
description: Petrol price increases to Rs393 75 per litre  while HSD will cost Rs422 08
content:
Petrol price increases to Rs393.75 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs422.08
The federal government on Monday increased the price of petrol by Rs4.61 per litre while reducing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.96 per litre for September 22.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs393.75 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs422.08 per litre for Tuesday.
The latest revision comes after the government decreased the price of petrol and HSD by Rs1.65 and 88 paisas per litre, respectively, from Sept 19 to Sept 21.
Read : Govt decreases petrol price by Rs1.65, HSD by 88 paisas till Sept 21
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 18, in a bid to provide relief to the public, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed the immediate inclusion of 20-year-old motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqi rickshaws in the Prime Minister Fuel Relief Scheme, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said.
The statement further added that all motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqi rickshaws registered after January 1, 2006, would be eligible for registration in the Prime Minister Fuel Relief Scheme.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices eased on Monday to their lowest level in 12 days, ‌as investors hoped for diplomatic progress on the Iran war due to this week's United Nations meeting and eyed a partial recovery in shipments from Saudi Arabia.
The Brent crude futures November contract fell to its lowest since September 9 at $99.51 a barrel at 1:16 pm ET (1716 ​GMT), down $4.36, or 4.2%.
On Sunday, Iran and the US exchanged new threats, although President Donald Trump said he would be open to meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who was expected to be in New York this week for the United Nations General Assembly.
Investors are pinning their hopes on ​a breakthrough in peace talks this week, said Tamas Varga, analyst at PVM Oil Associates.

title: Trump administration prepares sanctions against International Criminal Court  sources say
description: Rubio urged countries to quit the ICC as Washington sanctioned judges and prosecutors but spared the court itself
content:
Exact timing of announcement remains unclear
President Donald ‌Trump's administration has prepared sanctions against the entire International Criminal Court and plans to announce them soon, two sources familiar with the matter said on Sunday, a move that would step up its attack on the global tribunal that prosecutes war crimes and genocide worldwide.
The Trump administration ​has made no secret of its disdain for the court and has worked to undermine it. US officials ​want the court to drop its arrest warrants against Israeli leaders as well as a past ⁠probe into American troops in Afghanistan .
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in July announced a campaign to isolate the court , calling ​on other countries to withdraw from the tribunal. Washington has imposed sanctions on several ICC judges and ​prosecutors but has so far held off from imposing sanctions on the court itself, although the move has long been considered as one of the options.
The State Department did not respond to a request for comment.
Sanctions against the court have been prepared, the sources said, ​even though the exact timing of an announcement remained unclear. The Wall Street Journal cited officials who said the ​decision could be finalised as soon as this week during the United Nations General Assembly meeting.
Targeting the entire organisation directly, as well ‌as entities ⁠that cooperate with it, could severely undermine the court's work.
Read More: ' Trump administration prepares ICC sanctions'
Any entity-wide sanctions imposed by the US Treasury would prohibit US citizens and companies from providing funds, goods, or services to the court without a licence from the US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). Banks often over-comply with such US sanctions because they depend on access to the American ​financial system.
Among the court's operations ​that could be affected ⁠by sanctions against the entire organisation are the purchasing of IT services and insurance, the hiring of investigators and conducting everyday financial transactions, such as paying dozens of American ​employees, the ICC's registrar and president have warned .
Trump's opposition to the court goes back to ​his first term. ⁠It surfaced again with a plan to penalise ICC officials, an idea developed in November 2024 when Trump was reelected and the ICC issued an arrest warrant for Netanyahu for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in the Gaza conflict.
The ⁠ICC was ​established in 2002 by the international community to prosecute war crimes, genocide ​and crimes against humanity. It asserts jurisdiction only if a member state is unable or unwilling to prosecute atrocities itself.
The United States has never ​been a member.

title: Anne Hathaway to campaign for supporting actress for Christopher Nolan   s    The Odyssey
description: Universal will position Hathaway alongside co star Samantha Morton in its awards campaign for the film
content:
Universal will position Hathaway alongside co star Samantha Morton in its awards campaign for the film
Anne Hathaway is set to campaign for supporting actress for her performance as Penelope in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey , with Universal Pictures positioning the Oscar winner in the category for the upcoming awards season. Variety reported the decision exclusively.
Hathaway plays Penelope, the wife of Matt Damon’s Odysseus, in Nolan’s adaptation of Homer’s ancient Greek epic. The film follows Odysseus as he attempts to return home after the Trojan War, with Hathaway appearing alongside an extensive ensemble that includes Damon, Tom Holland, Zendaya, Robert Pattinson and Samantha Morton.
Universal’s decision settles the category in which the studio will campaign Hathaway after her placement had been a subject of awards season discussion. Morton, who plays Circe, will also be part of the film’s supporting actress campaign, creating the possibility of two acting contenders from the same production in the category.
Hathaway already has an Academy Award in the supporting actress category. She won for her performance as Fantine in the 2012 musical drama Les Misérables , making another supporting actress campaign particularly notable as The Odyssey enters the awards conversation.
The new campaign also arrives during a significant box office run for Nolan’s film. The Odyssey has earned more than $1.6bn worldwide and became Universal Pictures’ highest grossing film of all time in September. It also surpassed Deadpool & Wolverine to become the highest grossing R rated film ever.
Hathaway’s Penelope is one of the central figures in the film’s story, as Odysseus remains separated from his family for years during his journey home. Nolan’s version features Hathaway alongside Holland, who plays Telemachus, the son of Odysseus and Penelope.
The campaign comes during a particularly busy period for Hathaway. She also appeared in Mother Mary and returned as Andy Sachs in The Devil Wears Prada 2 earlier this year. Her upcoming projects include Verity , in which she stars alongside Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett.
For Universal, Hathaway’s supporting actress placement forms part of a broader awards campaign for The Odyssey . The studio is also expected to pursue recognition across major technical categories, while Damon is being positioned in the lead actor field.
With the awards season still developing, Hathaway’s campaign now gives her a defined path for consideration following her acclaimed Oscar winning performance in Les Misérables . Her category placement will be closely followed as nominations approach.

title: Karachi city sizzles past nine year September heat record
description: Mercury hits 40 7  C as humidity makes the city feel even hotter  relief expected from Wednesday
content:
Mercury hits 40.7°C as humidity makes the city feel even hotter; relief expected from Wednesday
September has turned into a furnace for Karachi, with the metropolis enduring its hottest September day in nine years as the mercury soared to 40.7°C on Monday.
The sweltering heat, compounded by rising humidity, pushed the heat index several degrees above the actual temperature, leaving Karachiites to endure conditions far hotter than the thermometer suggested.
The temperature recorded at the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD)’s Pehlwan Goth weather station surpassed the previous September high of 40.5°C recorded in 2017, while Karachi’s all-time September record remains 43°C, recorded on September 30, 1951.
According to PMD spokesperson Anjum Nazir Zaigham, the city had experienced a steady rise in temperatures over the past several days after relatively moderate weather at the beginning of September.
He told the Express Tribune that Monday’s temperature was the highest recorded in September since 2017, when the maximum temperature had reached 40.5°C. However, Karachi’s all-time September heat record remains 43°C, recorded on September 30, 1951, Zaigham said.
Read More: Talk climate in rupees, not rainfall
Temperatures varied across the city’s weather stations, with Jinnah Terminal recording 41.2°C, Gulistan-e-Jauhar 41°C, Sharae Faisal 39.5°C and Maripur 39°C. The lowest maximum temperature of 34.5°C was recorded at the Bin Qasim weather station.
Zaigham attributed the recent spell of intense heat to a circulation that had developed over the Arabian Sea, which altered wind patterns. He said weak southwesterly sea breezes had also contributed to the rise in temperatures.
The PMD forecast that temperatures could reach 38°C on Tuesday, while the intensity of the heat is expected to ease from Wednesday, when the maximum temperature could fall to around 35°C.
According to the PMD’s Early Warning Centre, Karachi’s weather is expected to remain hot and humid on Tuesday and Wednesday. Humidity could rise to 55%, making temperatures feel several degrees higher than the actual readings. Sea breezes are expected to continue, accompanied by winds from the west.
Other parts of Sindh will also remain in the grip of hot weather. Maximum temperatures of 42°C were recorded in Shaheed Benazirabad, Khairpur and Hyderabad city, while Chhor recorded 41.5°C.

title: Amanda Seyfried opens up about seeking complex characters as her career evolves
description: Seyfried plays prison teacher Karen in Tim Blake Nelson   s new film  which premiered at TIFF
content:
Seyfried plays prison teacher Karen in Tim Blake Nelson’s new film, which premiered at TIFF
Amanda Seyfried is embracing complex characters as she enters a new stage of her acting career, telling PEOPLE that she feels privileged to be offered roles with greater depth.
Speaking during the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival, Seyfried discussed the kinds of characters she is now interested in portraying. The actress said she has consistently looked for opportunities that allow her to explore different perspectives as a performer.
“I mean, I’ve always been looking for complexity and to get as much perspective as I possibly can as an artist,” Seyfried said.
The actress explained that her approach was also important during the early years of her Hollywood career. After gaining attention through projects including Mean Girls , Seyfried said she deliberately pursued a diverse range of roles because she wanted to establish herself as a serious performer within the industry.
That experience helped her build a broad repertoire and demonstrate her range from a relatively young age. Now, she believes the industry is increasingly providing opportunities for older women to portray characters with nuanced stories and complicated experiences.
“I feel like right now people are seeking me out to play these roles, which is just a real privilege,” she said.
Her comments came as The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd made its world premiere at TIFF on September 13. Directed by Tim Blake Nelson, the film follows Karen, the teacher Seyfried portrays at a maximum security prison.
Karen encounters Wilson, played by Scoot McNairy, an inmate whose charisma and unexpected tenderness affect her after years of an abusive marriage. According to the film’s synopsis, their connection leads Karen to take significant risks in the hope of securing Wilson’s freedom.
The film explores crime, punishment, desperation and retribution while also focusing on the unexpected connection between two isolated people. Seyfried’s role therefore gives her an opportunity to portray a character dealing with personal conflict, emotional vulnerability and difficult choices.
Seyfried has continued to build a varied filmography across comedy, drama, musical projects and more challenging dramatic material. Her upcoming work includes Octet , Lin Manuel Miranda’s musical film, in which she stars alongside Rachel Zegler.
With The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd marking another dramatic role for the actress, Seyfried’s latest comments offer insight into the kinds of characters she is interested in pursuing as her career continues to develop.

Medical exam scheduled after Presley Gerber died at 27, with authorities saying the investigation remains ongoing
New details have emerged following the death of model Presley Gerber, who died on September 20 at the age of 27, according to PEOPLE .
The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner’s Office said on September 21 that an examination was scheduled for the day as authorities continue investigating Gerber’s death. Officials said limited information is currently available and confirmed that the Santa Monica Police Department is handling the investigation.
According to the medical examiner, Gerber’s death was pronounced at 9:45am on September 20 by responding paramedics. The cause and manner of death have not been publicly determined.
Gerber, the son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber, was at a rehabilitation facility when he died, according to a previous medical examiner report. He was also the older brother of model Kaia Gerber.
A representative for Crawford, Rande Gerber and Kaia Gerber said the family is asking for privacy during this difficult time.
Before his death, Gerber had spoken publicly about his struggles with mental health, depression and addiction. During a 2023 appearance on the Studio 22 podcast, he said he hoped sharing his experiences could help others dealing with similar challenges.
Gerber also discussed his experience with ibogaine, a naturally occurring psychedelic compound that has been studied for its potential role in addiction treatment. In a social media post shared in March, he described undergoing an ibogaine treatment and reflected on the fear he experienced before it.
The medical examiner’s investigation remains ongoing, and further details about Presley Gerber’s cause and manner of death may be released following the examination.

title: Olivia Rodrigo ties    Guts    record with latest album at No  1 on Billboard chart
description: You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love    remains inside top 10 across six US charts
content:
‘You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love’ remains inside top 10 across six US charts
Olivia Rodrigo has matched a major chart milestone from her own catalogue as You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love spends its 12th week at No. 1 on the Billboard Top Alternative Albums chart.
The result puts Rodrigo’s latest studio album level with Guts , which also spent 12 weeks at the summit of the alternative ranking following its release in 2023. Her newest album has therefore equalled the longest No. 1 run Rodrigo has achieved on that particular Billboard chart.
You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love is also at No. 1 on the Top Rock & Alternative Albums chart. According to the chart figures reported by Forbes , the album has spent 13 weeks on that ranking and has led it for 12 of those weeks. The album was released on June 12, 2026, through Geffen Records.
The project has also maintained a strong position across Billboard's broader US album rankings. The report states that it appears in the top 10 on all six Billboard charts where it is currently listed, including the Billboard 200, where it has risen to No. 2.
That performance follows a strong opening for Rodrigo's third studio album. The record debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 after earning 485,000 equivalent album units in the United States during its opening tracking week, according to Luminate figures reported by Billboard. It became Rodrigo's third album to reach the top of the main US albums chart, following Sour and Guts .
Rodrigo's debut album Sour does not appear on the Top Alternative Albums or Top Rock & Alternative Albums charts. Her later releases have been represented on those rock and alternative rankings, reflecting the classification of her newer material.
Guts remains present on both alternative focused charts as well. The album continues to occupy a top 10 position on the Top Alternative Albums chart while also remaining within the upper portion of the Top Rock & Alternative Albums ranking.
With You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love continuing its strong chart run, Rodrigo has now matched one of her own established milestones while extending the commercial performance of her third studio album.

title: Mir Raza commission warns businessman over media interviews
description: Commission calls interviews an attempt to derail proceedings  Dr Usama backs autopsy report  five witnesses summoned
content:
Commission calls interviews an attempt to derail proceedings; five witnesses summoned
The judicial commission probing the Mir Raza Ali murder case warned businessman Ahmed on Monday over his media interviews, terming them an apparent attempt to undermine the commission’s proceedings, while the doctor who conducted the first post-mortem stood by his findings that the bullet entered the body from the front and exited through the back.
The commission issued its written order for Monday’s proceedings, stating that the statements of Umer Khan, Ali Shaz, Kazim Hussain, Ahmed Hassan Sheikh and Health Services Director General Pervez Ahmed Sheikh were recorded. DG Sheikh also submitted documents relating to the formation and replacement of the medical board.
According to the order, Ahmed was allowed to answer questions raised by Mir Raza’s family and provide relevant information. However, he could not provide anything beyond the statements he had already made before the commission.
The commission observed that Ahmed’s social media interviews apparently appeared aimed at undermining its proceedings and warned him against such conduct in future. It also noted that he had failed to use an opportunity to provide information through an affidavit.
During the proceedings, a lawyer who had taken a journalist’s mobile phone apologised, which was accepted by the journalist.
Read More: Mir Raza commission summons first IO
Mir Raza’s fiancée also contacted the commission and informed it about the confiscation of the mobile phone and the alleged transfer of data by the investigating officer. The commission said it would question DSP Siraj Lashari when his statement is recorded.
Dr Usama also appeared before the commission and later spoke to the media. “I stand by my first post-mortem report,” he said, adding that the bullet had entered from the front and exited through the back.
Dr Usama said he personally conducted the post-mortem on July 29 and that no other person had performed the examination. He said he had not known Mir Raza and had shared his findings with Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed, adding that he had acted on her instructions.
He said the physical copy of the report was submitted on August 3 and had been prepared to the best of his professional ability based on his findings from July 29.
Dr Usama also clarified that he did not intend to declare Mir Raza’s death a suicide, saying he wanted to explain his position regarding the bullet wound to the chest.
Regarding his observations about hydrochloric acid and decomposition, he said acid could cause certain changes to a body, including reddening of the face, while decomposition could appear differently on different parts of the body.
He said he had informed Dr Summaiya about the matter at around 5 pm and maintained that if acid had been used, its effects would not necessarily have appeared uniformly across the entire body.
However, the commission observed that Dr Usama’s further statement appeared aimed at levelling allegations against Dr Summaiya and the Sindh chief minister. It said the commission should not become a forum for allegations and that it had sufficient information to establish the facts of the case and determine whether any negligence had occurred.
Dr Usama said he had brought all his July 29 findings before the commission and remained satisfied with his original report. He added that doctors generally had 24 hours to submit a post-mortem report and that he had not anticipated the matter would become such a major controversy.
He said photographs taken during the autopsy were kept for his professional record, adding that Dr Summaiya was the signing authority for the first report. “My family has been worried since the first day,” he said, adding that his clinic had also remained closed for a month.
The commission has issued notices to ASP Nida, Asif, Abid, Faizur Rehman and Sarim to appear during proceedings scheduled for September 22.
