title: Red Sea Film Festival cancels 2026 edition and confirms return in 2027
description: The festival says logistical considerations surrounding its international event prompted the decision to pause this year
content:
Festival says logistical considerations surrounding its international event prompted the decision to pause this year
Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea Film Festival has cancelled its 2026 edition and will return in the fourth quarter of 2027, according to an announcement reported by Variety .
The sixth edition had been scheduled to take place from December 3 to 12. Organisers said the decision followed a review of several considerations concerning the timing and logistical requirements involved in staging an international film event of its scale.
In a statement, the Red Sea Film Festival Foundation said the pause was intended to ensure that the festival could return under the appropriate conditions and continue its programme celebrating filmmakers from Saudi Arabia, the wider region and around the world.
The foundation said the 2027 edition would have a renewed vision. It also confirmed that its Red Sea Fund and Red Sea Labs initiatives would continue during the festival's absence.
Year round programming is also planned for Culture Square in Jeddah from November. The foundation said the venue would host film screenings, cultural events and specialised film industry programmes.
The Red Sea Film Festival was established in 2019, with its inaugural edition held in 2020, following Saudi Arabia’s decision to lift its decades long ban on commercial cinemas. The festival has since developed into a major event for the Saudi and wider Arab film industries, while its Red Sea Souk market has attracted international film executives and regional industry professionals.
The cancellation comes after several changes within the festival’s leadership. Faisal Baltyuor became CEO of the Red Sea Foundation in May 2025, overseeing the festival as well as the Red Sea Fund and Red Sea Labs. Shivani Pandya Malhotra, who had served as the festival’s general manager and played a major role in developing the event, left her position in June 2026.
Variety reported that her replacement had not yet been announced. The publication also cited sources who said Baltyuor’s approach to the festival had differed from Pandya Malhotra’s way of operating.
The 2025 edition featured Sean Baker as jury president and welcomed international names including Dakota Johnson, Uma Thurman, Ana de Armas, Queen Latifah, Vin Diesel and Michael Caine.
With the 2026 edition cancelled, some Arab films originally expected to receive regional premieres at the festival may instead seek launches at other upcoming regional events. The Red Sea Film Festival is scheduled to return in 2027.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday assured Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian that Pakistan was determined to expand multisector cooperation during his visit to Tehran.
Iranian media outlet Press TV reported that Pezeshkian stated that Pakistan and Iran could meet many of their needs by tapping their "domestic and regional capabilities”.
Pezeshkian further noted that continued engagement between the two countries could further strengthen bilateral cooperation across all areas, adding that "US pressure on the region had contributed to greater convergence and interaction among Muslim countries".
“Pakistan is determined to further expand bilateral cooperation in trade, economy, tourism, politics, culture, and science,” Naqvi was in turn quoted as saying by Press TV .

In a post on X, the interior ministry noted that progress was reviewed in the meeting on the ongoing cooperation between the interior ministries of both countries in various sectors.
وفاقی وزیر داخلہ محسن نقوی کی ایرانی وزات داخلہ آمد، ایرانی ہم منصب اسکندر مومنی سے ملاقات پاک ایران دوطرفہ تعلقات اور خطے کی تازہ ترین صورتحال پر تبادلہ خیال ملاقات میں دونوں ممالک کی وزارت داخلہ کے درمیان مختلف شعبوں میں جاری تعاون پر پیش رفت کا جائزہ لیا گیا pic.twitter.com/bEjeAaTKj5
According to the ministry, Momeni stated that Naqvi's recent visit was "very beneficial" and thanked Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir for their efforts towards regional peace and stability.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni in Tehran to discuss bilateral ties, regional developments and cooperation between their ministries. Islamabad had already warned that the recent escalation in Yemen would further complicate the already complex regional scenario.

Pakistan has remained the primary mediator between Iran and the US throughout the war, and has maintained close contact with both sides.
The US and Iran signed the Islamabad memorandum of understanding in June and launched negotiations toward a final agreement. However, the talks later collapsed over disagreements on security guarantees and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most strategic routes for global energy supplies and trade.
The US and Iran then exchanged military strikes in July.
Trump on Sunday said he was contemplating three possible paths for Iran: continue targeting it economically, destroy the regime or make a deal.
After securing a ceasefire in April, Pakistan hosted the first high-level direct talks between the US and Iran since they broke diplomatic ties in 1979.

title: PHC stays deportation of Afghan medical students
description: Issues notices  seeks replies in 14 days  directs petitioners to continue studies till next hearing
content:
Issues notices, seeks replies in 14 days; directs petitioners to continue studies till next hearing
The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Monday halted the forced deportation of Afghan students enrolled in various medical and dental colleges across Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, issued notices to the concerned parties and sought their written replies within 14 days.
A division bench comprising Justice Waqar Ahmad and Justice Farah Jamshed was hearing a writ petition filed by 14 Afghan students. Advocate Waseemuddin Khattak appeared for the petitioners, while Assistant Attorney General Ishaq Khalil and National Database & Registration Authority Law Officer Muhammad Mubarak Jan represented the respondents.
Counsel for the petitioners informed the court that the students, all Afghan nationals, had been granted admission under the Afghan quota in different medical and dental colleges through the prescribed legal process. The Higher Education Commission (HEC) had also issued them no objection certificates (NOCs) to facilitate the grant of visas.
Read More: LHC extends stay for Afghan medics
The students are currently pursuing education in various disciplines. However, following the launch of the government’s repatriation plan for Afghan refugees, the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) issued notices on 31 July and 1 September cancelling the admissions of all Afghan students and directing them to return to their country.
Advocate Khattak argued that the cancellations were ordered without any show-cause notice, in clear violation of Article 25 of the Constitution as well as other constitutional provisions and international law. He further contended that the PMDC notices and letters contradicted the NOCs earlier issued by the HEC and that the Council lacked the authority to take such action.
The counsel also drew the court’s attention to a similar case in which the Lahore High Court, on September 11, had suspended the PMDC’s orders and directed Afghan students to continue their studies. He prayed that the authorities be restrained from harassing or pressuring the petitioners.
The bench stayed the forced deportation of the 14 students, issued notices to the respondents seeking replies within 14 days, and adjourned the matter to October 12. The court also directed that the petitioner Afghan students be allowed to continue their education in the meantime.

Kaylee Hottle crash driver tested negative for drugs and alcohol, while excessive speed was cited as a factor
The driver involved in the fatal car crash that killed Godzilla vs. Kong actress Kaylee Hottle was not impaired by drugs or alcohol, according to local authorities.
The Frederick County Sheriff’s Office confirmed that toxicology results for the 19-year-old driver came back negative for drugs and alcohol. The results are part of the ongoing investigation into the July crash in Maryland that claimed Hottle’s life.
Hottle, who was 18, was a passenger in a Honda Accord when the vehicle veered off the road and crashed into a ditch. Investigators previously said excessive speed was believed to have been a factor in the accident.
The medical examiner determined that Hottle died from multiple blunt force injuries. Her death was officially ruled an accident.
Hottle was best known for playing Jia in the 2021 film Godzilla vs. Kong . The role marked an important part of her acting career, and she had continued pursuing film opportunities before her death.
The actress was also known for being deaf and bringing representation to the screen through her work in the Godzilla vs. Kong franchise. Her sudden death prompted tributes from fellow actors and members of the entertainment industry, including her co-star Millie Bobby Brown.
The latest toxicology findings clarify that investigators found no evidence of drug or alcohol impairment on the part of the driver. However, authorities have previously indicated that the circumstances surrounding the crash included excessive speed as a suspected contributing factor.
The investigation follows the loss of a young actress whose career was still developing. Hottle’s family and fans have continued to remember her work and her contribution to the Godzilla vs. Kong franchise.

title: OGDCL conquer Kingsmen Academy in President   s Trophy Grade 1
description: The match between KRL and IT Solutions ends in a draw  PTV hold SBP as second round concludes
content:
The match between KRL and IT Solutions ends in a draw; PTV hold SBP as second round concludes
Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL) romped to a nine-wicket win over Kingsmen Academy while the match between Khan Research Laboratories (KRL) and Markhor IT Solutions and that of PTV and State Bank of Pakistan ended in a draw at the President’s Trophy on Monday.
Earlier on Sunday, Ghani whipped Sui Northern Gas Pipelines by an innings and 14 runs to go top of the table with 35 points from two matches. OGDCL’s win means they are now second with 31 points.
OGDCL reached the 121-run target after resuming their second innings from overnight score of 85-1 in 23 overs against Kingsmen Academy.
It took them 5.1 overs on day four to scale the target with opener Waqar Ahmed scoring unbeaten 75 off 94 balls striking six fours and one six. He also shared a 116-run unbeaten stand with Umar Siddiq (40 not out, 74b, 7x4s).
At Shoaib Akhtar Stadium in Rawalpindi, KRL resumed their first innings from overnight score of 423-5 in 133 overs and were bowled out on 490 in 158 overs. Faheem Ashraf converted his 28 not out from previous day to 69 off 135 balls hitting tne fours in total to register his 16th first-class half-century.
MIT pacers Mohammad Imran Junior, Mohammad Ismail, Mohammad Nabeel and Samama Riaz toiled for 34, 32, 25 and 22 overs, respectively, accounting for seven wickets together as KRL managed a first innings lead of 170.

title: Humanoid robot sales tally hit 7 000 globally last year
description: Bank of America sees humanoid robot shipments reaching 90 000 this year and 1 2 million by 2030
content:
Bank of America sees humanoid robot shipments reaching 90,000 this year and 1.2 million by 2030
Around 7,000 humanoid robots were sold worldwide last year for industrial and professional service use, figures compiled by the International Federation of Robotics showed.
The relatively small number contrasts with forecasts for a boom in the coming years, particularly in China, the world's largest market for industrial robots, which last month showcased humanoid running and boxing at its robot games.
To qualify as humanoid under the IFR's criteria, a robot must have a human-like appearance and operate autonomously in an environment designed for humans. Legs are not required.
The IFR data, reviewed by Reuters ahead of publication, offer one of the first industry-wide measures of a technology that is attracting billions of dollars in investments and producing impressive demonstrations.
However, the numbers of humanoids remain "a fraction" of the overall robot population globally, Susanne Bieller, secretary general of Frankfurt-based IFR, told Reuters .
Read More: Founder of Chinese startup Spirit AI says robot brains set for 2027 breakthrough
This compares with around 542,000 regular industrial robots installed in 2024 and another estimated 199,000 service robots sold that year for use in transport, hospitality and cleaning.
FILE PHOTO: An engineer works on a Tiangong Omni humanoid robot in the research and testing area of the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center, also known as X-Humanoid, in Beijing, China, September 4, 2026. REUTERS
The 2025 data for industrial and service robots will be published September 24.
Bieller said that among humanoids sold in 2025, many were not doing productive work but were bought by research institutions or companies using them to generate data for improving AI models.
Carmakers, key early adopters, are running pilots with "single-digit or sometimes double-digit numbers of robots in their plants," Bieller said.
IFR has compiled robotics statistics for three decades, and has begun collecting humanoid data alongside its much larger industrial robot and service robot figures for the first time.
Bank of America Global Research estimates that 90,000 humanoid robots will be shipped this year and 1.2 million by 2030.
The IFR's tally is based on supplier and national industry association data, and excludes consumer and military humanoid robots, while medical robots are classified separately.

title: Pope Leo calls for AI systems that don t foster divisions
description: US born Pope Leo makes AI risks a major theme of his papacy  first raising the issue on his third day
content:
US-born Pope Leo makes AI risks a major theme of his papacy, first raising the issue on his third day
Pope Leo , who has warned of the risk that AI could lead the world ​down a path of unending war, on Monday ‌urged the development of AI systems that do not foster divisions in society but strengthen peace initiatives.
"In a world ​marked by conflict and division, the development of ​artificial intelligence calls for a vision inspired by ⁠wisdom and charity," the pontiff said in a ​message to a conference on AI issues held in ​Rome.
The pope called for development of AI systems that "serve the dignity of every person and strengthen the bonds that unite the ​human family".
Leo, the first US-born pope, has made ​addressing the possible dangers of AI development a major theme of ‌his ⁠16-month-old papacy, first discussing the issue publicly on his third day as pope.
Read More: US Treasury's Bessent, China's He to launch talks on AI, trade, critical minerals
In his first major document, issued in May, Leo warned that AI systems spread misinformation ​and prioritise conflict. ​He urged ⁠international regulation of the industry.
Monday's conference, hosted at Rome's Pontifical Lateran University, was ​titled "AI4Peace." Speakers included US economist Jeffrey Sachs, ​Rome city ⁠council president Svetlana Celli and Francisco Rojas Aravena, rector of the UN's University for Peace, based in Costa ⁠Rica.
Leo's ​brief message was read aloud ​to attendees by Rev. Andrea Ciucci, chancellor of the Vatican's Pontifical Academy ​for Life.

Actor shares an emotional tribute to her character and thanks viewers, co-stars and the drama's team for their support
Actor Kinza Hashmi has said goodbye to her Leader character, Rubab Agha, in an Instagram post marking the end of the political drama's run.
Hashmi shared a carousel of behind-the-scenes pictures and production clips featuring her character, alongside a farewell note reflecting on her time as Rubab. "What a rollercoaster this journey has been. It feels strange knowing I won’t be stepping into Rubab’s world again," she wrote.
Reflecting on the experience, Hashmi said the character had become a meaningful part of her journey.
"I lived her, felt her, and somewhere along the way, a little part of her stayed with me," she wrote, before thanking viewers for their support. "The way you all loved and supported LEADER means more than I can put into words. Thank you for being a part of this beautiful journey with us."
Hashmi also thanked the director, her co-stars and the entire Leader team, signing off with, " Yeh safar hamesha yaad rahega. "
Leader premiered on March 28 and revolved around politics, love and resilience, with a story centred on standing against injustice.
Hashmi played Rubab, a woman of strength and pride whose heart was tested by political turmoil and love, while Ali Raza played Mansoor, a determined voice who stood against every challenge.
The drama also marked the first on-screen pairing of Hashmi and Raza, whose chemistry drew praise from fans following the release of the trailer.
Hashmi is known for Ishq Tamasha (2018) and Ruposh (2022), while Raza has earned praise for Meesni (2023) and Dastak (2025).

title: Rebel Wilson appears in court as    The Deb    producers pursue claims over delayed release
description: The producers claim Wilson   s social media posts damaged their finances and reputation
content:
The producers claim Wilson’s social media posts damaged their finances and reputation
Rebel Wilson has returned to court in Sydney as producers of The Deb pursue claims that she interfered with the release of her directorial debut. AI Film Production Limited is suing Wilson and her company, Camp Sugar Productions, in the New South Wales Supreme Court, alleging that statements made by Wilson contributed to financial and reputational damage.
The dispute centres on Wilson’s falling out with producers Amanda Ghost, Greg Cameron and Vince Holden. According to the producers, Wilson made allegations about inappropriate conduct towards lead actor Charlotte MacInnes, financial misconduct and attempts to prevent the film from being released. They claim her statements to her large social media following breached contracts and consumer law.
The producers also allege that Wilson interfered with negotiations involving potential distributors and threatened an injunction that could have prevented the film from being shown in Australia. AI Film is seeking damages, an apology and corrective advertising, although the amount of damages has not been specified.
Wilson and Camp Sugar have denied the allegations and filed a cross claim against the producers. Their case alleges that Ghost, Cameron and Holden were involved in conduct including theft, bullying and sexual misconduct. Wilson has also alleged that agreements concerning writing credits and a soundtrack album were broken, while claiming that Cameron and Holden embezzled A$900,000 from a joint venture established to make the film. Those allegations are disputed.
During Monday’s hearing, Holden gave evidence about the film’s financing and budget. The court heard that AI Film had planned a substantial investment in The Deb , with the production budget eventually rising above $20m. Holden also discussed a 2023 dispute over fees, including Wilson’s proposal to reduce her acting and directing fee to $1m.
The Deb , adapted from the Australian stage musical, was initially scheduled for release before its launch was delayed amid the dispute. It was eventually released in April 2026.
The latest case follows a separate defamation action brought against Wilson by MacInnes. In July 2026, a Federal Court judge dismissed MacInnes’s case over Wilson’s social media posts, finding that the relevant material was not defamatory under the legal test applied.
The producers’ case is continuing in the New South Wales Supreme Court, with the hearing adjourned until Tuesday.

title: I live in fear   1 5 million Pakistani children sexually exploited online
description: In Pakistan  71  of victims told no one  while none reported abuse through formal channels  UNICEF says
content:
In Pakistan, 71% of victims told no one, while none reported abuse through formal channels, UNICEF says
Zara Shah was targeted by a stranger while playing a computer game, drawn into a conversation that would expose her to terrifying online sexual exploitation.
Zara, whose name has been changed by AFP for safety reasons, is one of an estimated 1.5 million children in Pakistan who experienced online sexual abuse in one year, according to a report published by the UN children's agency this month.
"We started chatting while playing an online game, and he began acting like a friend. Later, he wanted to meet and, after, started asking me for nudes," 17-year-old Zara said.
"When I refused, he threatened to find my family online and tell them that we had been talking," she added.
According to the UNICEF report, around 85% of perpetrators were known to the victims, aged between 12 and 17.
"The abuse may start with a friendly conversation, a gaming interaction, a promise of gifts, money or romance," Daniel Kardefelt, lead author of the global UNICEF report, told AFP .
"Perpetrators may spend months building trust using information that they find on social media," Kardefelt said.
In Pakistan, 71% of victims did not tell anyone, according to the UNICEF report, while no child surveyed reported the abuse through formal channels, including police, helplines or social workers.
Their silence was mostly because of stigma, shame and fears over how their families or society may react.
"Around 44% of reported abuse was entirely online, with Snapchat and WhatsApp among the most common settings," said Mehek Naeem, director of PAHCHAAN, a children's rights organisation based in the eastern city of Lahore.
Girls can face heightened risks of sexual extortion in society, which can lead to restrictions on their mobility or withdrawal from school.
For Zara, the threat of being exposed to her family was enough to keep her silent.
"I could have been stopped from going to school or leaving the house altogether," she said.
"Staying quiet felt like the better option than speaking up. But anxiety kills me every day."
With around 74% of children aged 12 to 17 in Pakistan estimated by UNICEF to be internet users, concerns over online safety are growing as their access to digital platforms expands.
Echoing other policies around the world, the Punjab government this month passed a resolution to bar children under 16 from using social media.
Read More: Aidaah Sheikh calls out ‘cyber-bully casters’ over body-shaming
"I disagree with the ban," said Usama Khilji, a digital rights activist.
"It will be a challenge to implement, and children can circumvent the ban through VPNs. Children have the right of freedom of expression, and a ban takes that away," he said.
Pakistan has a legal framework addressing tech-facilitated offences against children, but "there is no implementation", said Tahira Afrasiyab, a spokesperson for non-profit organisation Muslim Hands.
And, according to experts, there are loopholes in existing laws.
Human rights lawyer Salman Afridi said this issue shows how "economic vulnerability can be weaponised" for amounts as small as Rs10,000 in exchange for the production of sexual content.
"What we are seeing is the use of technology to facilitate an entire chain of grooming, inducement, coercion, blackmail, production, distribution and commercialisation," he said.
"There is a strong basis for describing this as a commercial ecosystem of exploitation," Afridi added.
For Zara and many others like her, the consequences of an encounter that began with an online game remain difficult to escape.
"I was, and am, scared," she said. "I live in fear."

title: Bryce Dallas Howard opens up about navigating perimenopause and using hormones
description: The actress says she feels grateful to be part of a generation receiving greater attention around perimenopause
content:
The actress says she feels grateful to be part of a generation receiving greater attention around perimenopause
Bryce Dallas Howard has opened up about her experience with perimenopause, describing the stage of life as a new and positive experience while discussing the subject with PEOPLE .
The actress spoke to the publication at the opening night gala for the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles on September 19, where she attended alongside her father, filmmaker Ron Howard.
At 45, Howard said she is doing well while navigating perimenopause, which refers to the period when the body begins its natural transition towards menopause. The transition can last several years and involves hormonal changes that may cause a range of symptoms.
“That’s been a new exploration for me, and it’s been very, very positive,” Howard told. She also expressed gratitude for being part of a generation of women who are receiving greater attention and treatment around the subject.
Howard revealed that she has been using hormones to manage symptoms associated with perimenopause. Hormone replacement therapy is one treatment option used to address certain symptoms during perimenopause and menopause, although treatment decisions vary between individuals and should be discussed with a healthcare professional.
The actress also pointed to what she sees as a broader change in how women approach medical care during this stage of life.
“There’s been a generational shift, I think, that’s really, really powerful,” Howard said when discussing the increasing openness around seeking medical advice and treatment for perimenopause.
Her comments come as a number of public figures have spoken about their own experiences with perimenopause and menopause in recent years. Celebrities including Naomi Watts, Gabrielle Union and Gwyneth Paltrow have discussed aspects of the transition publicly, contributing to wider conversations about symptoms and treatment.
Howard has previously spoken about personal topics including body image and ageing, while continuing her work as an actress, director and producer.
Her recent acting credits include Deep Cover and Argylle . She is also known for roles in films including Jurassic World , The Help and Spider-Man 3 . Howard is expected to return to the big screen in Anything But Ghosts , a horror comedy scheduled for 2027.
During her conversation at the Lucas Museum gala, Howard also provided an update on her family, saying her children Theodore, 19, and Beatrice, 14, are doing well. The children are her two children with actor Seth Gabel.

title: Rule of law  supremacy of Constitution to prevail during PTI long march to Islamabad  Gohar

content:
CM Afridi says PTI has raised its voice through provincial, national assemblies, but has received no positive response
Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said on Monday that the rule of law and supremacy of the Constitution would prevail during the party's long march to Islamabad on September 27, further stating that it would never take "law and order" into its own hands.
The PTI had announced last month that it would march to Islamabad on September 27 to press for the release of party founder Imran Khan. The party has been preparing a central convoy from Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), with caravans from other parts of the country expected to join before proceeding towards the federal capital. The federal government has warned the party against going ahead with the march.
In a press conference today at the Chief Minister's House in Peshawar, Gohar emphasised that the party was not going to Islamabad to conquer it or turn it into “Somnath”, adding that “when we go to Islamabad, the supremacy of the Constitution and the law will prevail” and there would be an environment of festivity.
He stressed that PTI would never take "law and order" into its own hands, adding that Pakistan would always come first and peace and order would always come first. “Are we terrorists? We are being told that we will be dealt with like terrorists. We are political figures, and we will not arrive like terrorists”.

While talking about the planned long march to Islamabad, Gohar enquired whether protesting was not the PTI’s democratic and constitutional right.
Gohar added that during PTI's tenure, 14 long marches were allowed to take place in three years and their paths were not blocked. “We have not been allowed to hold a long march for four years since our government ended.
“Our 1500 workers have been arrested, and lists have been made for the rest. Five MNAs, a senator, our MPAs, including one from Islamabad and ministers from Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa are currently under arrest,” he said.

Gohar underlined that this had been done to show that while PTI held the government in K-P, someone else called the shots in the province. “The people of the province should call the shots”.
He added that PTI had not severed ties and communication channels remained open, noting that the party’s demands were medical treatment for Imran, hearings for his cases, and permission for meetings.
K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi said that PTI had faced persistent injustice, coercion and oppression not only in the aftermath of November 26 2024, but ever since April 9 2022.

“This oppressive government is responsible for the killing of every party worker, but despite that, we have not submitted, and Imran Khan has not bowed down, even though his wife and family have been targeted. Yesterday, all three of his sisters were abducted,” Afridi remarked.
The chief minister noted that the PTI remained the most “popular party” in the country and Imran remained the most “popular political leader”, adding that in the last two years, since November 26, 2024, PTI had not held any long march or protest rally outside of K-P.

The chief minister underscored that “we are people of the masses and follow democratic paths”, adding that protesting remained their right.
“Those who come to power through the back door resort to oppression and coercion. When they get caught, they play the woman card,” he said.
Afridi stated that it was decided in today’s meeting that the PTI would set out in September and would mobilise peacefully with full force, adding that detaining its ministers would not halt the movement.

Harington is taking over the role from Nicholas Hoult, who left the series because of scheduling conflicts. Lockhart, a self-absorbed wizard and Hogwarts’ Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher, is expected to appear when the series reaches its second season.
The actor also joked about how easily he could relate to Lockhart’s personality, describing the character as someone who is “addicted to himself”.
Production on Harry Potter Season 2 is already underway, although Harington remained tight-lipped about his character’s appearance. He also confirmed that he considers himself a Gryffindor.
Harington said filming at Warner Bros. Studios Leavesden is particularly appealing because it allows him to remain close to his two young children while working on a project he loves.

title: AI    actress    Tilly Norwood suddenly glitches and speaks Cantonese during Piers Morgan interview
description: Tilly Norwood later called the unexpected language switch a technical    hiccup    during the viral exchange
content:
Tilly Norwood later called the unexpected language switch a technical “hiccup” during the viral exchange
AI-generated character Tilly Norwood sparked a viral moment during an appearance on Piers Morgan Uncensored after she abruptly switched from English to Cantonese while discussing her upcoming film Misaligned . The exchange took place during the September 18 episode, with actor and director Tom Conti also appearing alongside Piers Morgan.
Conti asked Norwood whether the other performers in Misaligned were real actors or computer-generated characters. Norwood initially described the project as a hybrid production involving human directors, writers and editors.
When Conti pressed her for a direct answer, Norwood said the other performers were "all digital twins, just like me". She then appeared to lose track of the conversation and began speaking Cantonese for roughly 15 seconds. Morgan and Conti appeared surprised by the sudden change.
Morgan subsequently questioned Norwood about the unexpected switch, asking why she had started speaking Chinese without warning. Norwood responded by apologising and describing the incident as a "little hiccup", adding that her "wires" had become crossed. The clip was subsequently shared by the programme's official social media account and attracted millions of views.
EXCLUSIVE: AI actress Tilly Norwood glitches and starts speaking CHINESE during her interview with Piers Morgan and real-life actor Tom Conti... Watch the full interview at 7pm (BST)👇 📺 https://t.co/1nTb79BH8D @piersmorgan | @TillyNorwoodX pic.twitter.com/DDkveWvVzz
The unusual exchange has drawn renewed attention to Norwood, a computer-generated character developed by Particle 6 and its AI talent division. She first became a major talking point in 2025 after creator Eline Van der Velden said talent agencies had shown interest in representing the character. The announcement prompted criticism from sections of the acting community over the implications of synthetic performers.
SAG-AFTRA subsequently issued a statement describing Norwood as a computer-generated character rather than an actor and reiterated its position that synthetic performers should not replace human performers. The union also highlighted contractual requirements concerning the use of synthetic performers by signatory producers.
Norwood is being promoted as the lead of Misaligned , described as a comedy-drama centred on a coming-of-age story involving artificial intelligence. A release date for the film has not been announced. The Cantonese incident has therefore added another widely circulated moment to the ongoing public discussion surrounding Norwood and the expanding use of AI-generated performers in film and television.

title: Katrina Kaif on how motherhood changed her approach to beauty and wellbeing
description: Indian actor says pregnancy made her more attentive to her skin  health and daily habits that help her feel her best
content:
Indian actor says pregnancy made her more attentive to her skin, health and daily habits that help her feel her best
Bollywood actor Katrina Kaif says motherhood has changed the way she approaches beauty, skincare and her overall wellbeing, with the actor now paying closer attention to what her body and skin actually need.
In an interview with The Hollywood Reporter India , Kaif discussed her experience following pregnancy, her evolving skincare routine and the thinking behind Kay Beauty's entry into the skincare market. Gulf News later reported on those comments, placing them in the context of the online scrutiny Kaif faced following a recent public appearance.
Kaif said her skin had become more sensitive after pregnancy and that she had to reconsider which products worked for her. "Post-pregnancy, my skin became even more sensitive, so it was a really tricky time because I had to understand what products were working for me. I found myself looking for products that felt soothing, calming and restorative," she said.
Her approach to skincare has since become more responsive to the condition of her skin, with factors such as stress, inflammation, travel and long working hours influencing what she feels she needs.
Kaif also emphasised that her understanding of beauty has evolved over the course of her career. Having started out as a model before moving into films, she said beauty expectations were accompanied by numerous stereotypes when she was beginning her career.
"It's changed a lot. When I started out early through my modelling and acting career, there were a lot of stereotypes about what the beauty standards were. Now for me, looking my best is really about feeling my best, and that comes from taking care of myself as a whole."
Rather than focusing simply on maintaining a particular appearance, Kaif said she now connects looking her best with feeling well and taking care of herself more broadly.
She identified several everyday habits that she believes make a difference to how she feels and, consequently, how her skin behaves.
"A healthy diet, keeping the inflammation in your body under control, staying active, meditation, a phone-free daily hour of your morning and getting natural light first thing in the morning. It all makes a huge difference to how I feel, and ultimately how my skin behaves. I think when you feel healthy, that confidence naturally reflects on the outside."
Beyond skincare, Kaif spoke about the difficulty of stepping away from work and the importance of making time to disconnect.
"Having downtime with your family and friends always helps you find your centre. For me, I have to discipline myself to switch off sometimes. It's ingrained in me to constantly be working and creating something, whether with films or with Kay Beauty, so learning to have moments where you disconnect is important to recharge and reset," she added.
For Kaif, creating periods of quiet has become particularly important in an environment where digital entertainment and information are constantly available. "In today's fast-paced world where there is limitless information and entertainment available through digital mediums, creating moments of stillness and quiet for the mind to be calm is important."
Gulf News reported that Kaif's interview came days after photographs from her appearance with husband Vicky Kaushal at the Ambani family's Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations in Mumbai prompted online comments about her postpartum appearance. The couple welcomed their son, Vihaan, in November 2025.

title: CNN  MS NOW and Politico suing Trump over White House ban
description: Trump defends media ban  calls news outlets a security threat without providing evidence after lawsuit is announced
content:
Trump defends media ban, calls news outlets a security threat without providing evidence after lawsuit is announced.
CNN , MS NOW and Politico said on Monday they are suing President Donald Trump and other ​members of his administration to protect their rights under the US Constitution's First Amendment after he banned the news outlets from the White House building grounds.
The three news ‌organizations said they have notified the government that they were filing their lawsuit in the US District Court for the District of Columbia and could see emergency hearings in the case as soon as this week.
"Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists' credentials because it objected to our reporting. Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public's right to independent journalism free from government interference," they wrote in a joint statement.
The ​lawsuit aims "to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes," they added.
The First Amendment protects the ​freedom of the press and speech.
Representatives for the White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Trump first announced his action on ⁠Friday in a social media post. The Republican president defended the ban in another social media post on Monday after the lawsuit was announced, calling the news media a security threat, without ​providing any evidence.
"The White House is not instituting an assault on the Free Press, something which I cherish. It is instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS," Trump wrote. "It is corrupt, purposeful, pervasive, ​fully coordinated, and totally out of control. It is a threat to our National Security, and must be stopped, NOW!"
Read More: Trump says CNN, Politico, MS NOW banned from White House
His administration has upended decades of tradition in dealings between the White House and press, denying the access many major news organizations have had to the president while elevating new media outlets seen as more sympathetic to the administration. He has also filed a number of lawsuits against news organizations.
CNN had been scheduled to cover ​Monday's White House events for the broader press corps, including Trump's trip to New York for the United Nations General Assembly. It was not immediately clear what television footage of the president ​would be provided to the public.
"The ban is unconstitutional and should be immediately restrained," the news outlets said in a copy of their lawsuit, adding that the ban was already impeding coverage that could have wider ‌impact.
"The ban ⁠inflicts an injury on all news media organisations — who now risk a similar fate if they engage in reporting the President deems insufficiently favorable," the three wrote in their complaint, which seeks a temporary restraining order to block Trump's action.
Trump's latest move comes as his fellow Republicans seek to defend their narrow majorities in Congress in the November midterm elections as polls show the public souring on Republicans and Trump's own approval ratings stand near historic lows.
On Saturday , all three outlets said their journalists were turned away from the White House grounds and their press credentials confiscated, ​a day after Trump initially announced his ban ​in a social media post and threatened ⁠to block other outlets.
Also Read: CNN, MSNOW journalists denied access to White House after Trump announces ban
MS NOW and CNN over the weekend instead set up their journalists across the street from the White House and continued to broadcast coverage.
Trump on Friday addressed what he called his "ban on the free press" with reporters at an event in the Oval Office and said ​there was no particular incident that provoked the move. Asked what other news organizations could be targeted, Trump cited The New York Times ​and The Washington Post as "fake ⁠news" but said they had not been removed yet.
The Associated Press , the White House Correspondents' Association and others have criticized Trump's ban, citing the fundamental American right to free speech and calling for access to be immediately restored.
"The American people, through a free and independent press, must be able to scrutinize those elected to power, regardless of whether government officials view it favorably," the correspondents' association said in a ⁠statement.
The AP filed ​its own lawsuit after being barred along with Reuters last year from the group of reporters that cover the president's ​daily movements.
During his first term in office, Trump sought to revoke or suspend White House credentials of two correspondents for CNN and Playbo y magazine but federal judges ordered their press passes restored.

title: Fact check  Gohram Bugti has not announced any long march  viral video is from April 2025
description: Keyword searches yielded no recent announcement of any such march
content:
Keyword searches yielded no recent announcement of any such march
Multiple social media users, who appear to be pro-PTI based on past posts, shared a video on Sunday showing Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti’s grandson, Gohram Bugti, announcing a long march demanding the release of Dr Mahrang Baloch and others. However, the video is old from April 2025.
Dr Mahrang Baloch, chief organiser of the Baloch Yakjehti Committee (BYC), was arrested in Quetta on March 22, 2025, along with other activists during a crackdown on a BYC protest. She was initially detained under the Maintenance of Public Order law and was subsequently booked in cases carrying terrorism and other charges.
Last month, the PTI announced a long march to Islamabad for September 27, with Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi saying the party leadership and allied Tehreek Tahaffuz-i-Ayeen Pakistan (TTAP) had agreed on the date. PTI has said the march is aimed at securing Imran Khan’s release and pressing for constitutional supremacy and rule of law.
Meanwhile, the Jamaat-e-Islami has kicked off its own long march to Islamabad to protest against the high petroleum levy.
On September 20, an account that appears to be pro-PTI based on its past posts shared a video on X of Gohram announcing a long march for the release of Dr Mahrang and others.
The post was captioned: “Gohram Bugti, grandson of Nawab Akbar Bugti, has too announced a long march for the release of Mahrang Baloch and others.”
Another X user who describes himself as a journalist and appears to post pro-PTI content shared the same clip on the same date with the following caption: “From Balochistan, Nawab Akbar Bugti’s grandson has announced a long march for Dr Mahrang’s release. This has become the fifth long march.”
The post garnered more than 63,100 views.
On the same date, the video was also shared by multiple pro-PTI accounts on Facebook and X with the same or similar captions, as can be seen here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here and here .
A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to its virality and keen public interest in the political situation amid the multiple long marches.
A reverse image search to trace the origin of the video led to a YouTube video published on April 1, 2025, showing the same footage.
A keyword search led to Gohram’s official Facebook page, where he had posted the same video on April 1, 2025. He had stated that a long march would be launched if the detained women were not released within 72 hours.
It also led to the official Facebook page of his political party, the Jamhoori Watan Party (JWP), which also shared the same video and announcement on April 1, 2025.
A subsequent Dawn report published on April 4, 2025, referred to his 72-hour ultimatum and the JWP’s plan to launch a long march from Dera Bugti to Quetta for the release of Dr Mahrang Baloch and other detained women.
A further keyword search to determine whether any credible domestic media outlets had reported any such similar recent remarks yielded no recent announcement of such a march from Balochistan.
The claim that a viral video shows Gohram Bugti announcing a new long march for the release of Dr Mahrang Baloch and others is misleading.
The video is old from April 1, 2025, when he announced plans for a long march if the detained women were not released.

title: US refusal to issue visas to Palestinian delegation violates international agreements  Hamas
description: UN General Assembly allows Palestine to address its 81st session s general debate through a prerecorded speech
content:
UN General Assembly allows Palestine to address its 81st session's general debate through a prerecorded speech
Hamas on Monday condemned the US refusal to grant visas to a Palestinian delegation seeking to attend UN General Assembly meetings.
“The decision constitutes a flagrant violation of the international conventions and agreements governing the work of the UN headquarters and a continuation of the policy of complete US bias toward the Zionist occupation,” Hamas spokesperson Hazem Qassem said in a statement.
The restriction has continued for a second year. In 2025, Washington denied visas to Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas and other officials to attend the meetings, forcing Abbas to participate by video link .
On Thursday, the UN General Assembly adopted a resolution allowing the State of Palestine to participate in the general debate of its 81st session through a prerecorded address by its president to be shown in the Assembly Hall.
The resolution was backed by 152 countries, opposed by three, with four abstentions.
Read More: US extends visa sanctions on Palestinian officials ahead of UN General Assembly in New York
On Thursday, the Palestinian Foreign Ministry rejected Washington’s decision to extend visa restrictions on Palestinian officials over alleged failures to meet commitments toward the US, calling for the measure to be halted and for direct Palestinian-US dialogue to begin.
Under the 1947 UN Headquarters Agreement between the organisation and the US, Washington, as the host country, is required to facilitate access to the UN headquarters in New York for representatives of states and entities participating in UN activities.
Palestine has held the status of a non-member observer state at the UN since 2012.
Of the UN’s 193 member states, 160 recognise the State of Palestine, which is also a member of more than 100 international organisations and treaties, according to the Palestinian Foreign Ministry.
Israel and the US oppose such recognition, while Washington has used its veto power at the UN Security Council to block Palestine from obtaining full UN membership instead of its current status.
Since October. 8, 2023, Israel has killed more than 73,000 Palestinians and injured over 174,000 others in its genocide in Gaza, most of them women and children.
Successive US administrations have provided Israel with military, financial and diplomatic support, including protection from accountability at the UN Security Council through the use of the veto.
In 1948, Israel was established on lands seized by armed Zionist groups that carried out massacres and displaced at least 750,000 Palestinians. Israel later occupied the remaining Palestinian territories and continues to reject withdrawal and the establishment of a Palestinian state as stipulated in UN resolutions.

title: Gaza students return to in person schooling for first time in three years
description: Children celebrate return to class as 98  of Gaza schools are damaged or destroyed  UNICEF says
content:
Children celebrate return to class as 98% of Gaza schools are damaged or destroyed, UNICEF says
Hundreds of thousands of children in Gaza returned to in-person teaching on Saturday for the first time in nearly three years, albeit in damaged or makeshift school buildings and tents, and with uniforms, notebooks and pens unaffordable for many families.
The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) says 98% of schools in Gaza were either destroyed or damaged during the war, and Gaza education officials say about 660,000 students have been deprived of in-person learning and regular participation in education.
The reopening is a fragile milestone for Gaza after a conflict that has killed around 22,000 students and more than 770 education workers, including 532 teachers, according to Ibrahim Ramadan, director of education for East Khan Younis.
And they're back, finally! Some hope for more than 330,000 children across the #Gaza Strip on the first day of term at 200 learning centres supported by @UNICEF . Routine, stability & social connection - being in class restores some sense of childhood. #GenerationHope pic.twitter.com/TwA0g5BvCj
"The last time I have been to school was three years ago. Now, we are starting the school year, it is year of joy, happiness and success," said Moayed Abu Mustafa in Khan Younis.
Mustafa said he was determined to learn even though he will sit on the floor in a tent lacking ventilation, has no decent shoes, notebook or pen, and lost friends during the war.
"Despite all of this we will learn, we will learn even in a tent."
A displaced Palestinian child lies inside a classroom-turned-shelter in Khan Younis, in the southern Gaza Strip, September 10, 2026. REUTERS
Fifteen-year-old displaced student Samar Abu Salmi, who lives with her family in a tent, is also returning to class.
"We studied on phones and we haven't seen our teachers... now, we are back pursuing our dream... from one tent to another," she said, speaking in the yard of her new makeshift school.
She also lacks much of the essential equipment, which has become unaffordable for her family.
Displaced Palestinian student Samar Abu Salmi, 15, sits with other female students inside a tent classroom in Khan Younis, in the southern Gaza Strip, September 20, 2026. REUTERS
"Before the war, everything was available for us - notebooks, pens, goods, clothes, outings, things that we could get cheaply," Salmi said.
Despite the devastation in the enclave, the Ministry of Education, backed by international and local organisations, has moved ahead with the 2026-27 academic year, establishing dozens of temporary schools made of tents, tarpaulins, sheet metal and wood to accommodate pupils.
Some are built on sandy ground, while others have classrooms with only some mattresses and a blackboard, into which students cram. Others are still housing dozens of displaced families.
Attending another school was 14-year-old Yamen Abu Samra.
"We used to wake up happy to go to school... Now, when we come to school, we're afraid of stray bullets, rockets, strikes, everything," he said.
"Now, I'm sitting in a tent that has absolutely nothing, just the sun and the heat," he added.
At least 540,000 students are expected to attend in-person classes this year in makeshift private schools, temporary learning centres and educational points, with UNICEF support, according to education officials. Online learning will continue for those who cannot attend classes or who left Gaza during the war.
Israeli forces remain in control of more than 60% of Gaza despite last year's ceasefire, which halted major fighting but failed to end the conflict.
Palestinian students attend their first day of the new school year at an UNRWA school in Nuseirat, in the central Gaza Strip, September 19, 2026.PHOTO: REUTERS
Palestinian authorities say more than 73,000 people have been killed in Israel's assault on Gaza, launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel in October 2023.
Stationery trader Khaled Aliyan, 30, said Israeli import restrictions have reduced supplies and hiked prices.
"This notebook, which used to cost 3 shekels ($1), now costs 15 (shekels). All stationery items are expensive," he said.
Israel's COGAT military agency, which controls access to Gaza, did not respond to a Reuters request for comment on restrictions on supplies and strikes on schools. Israel has repeatedly accused Hamas of using schools for military purposes, which Hamas denies.

content:
Drake appears to reference Gaza with 'Pray for Gaza' in song featured in his new FOMO short film
Drake appears to reference Gaza in a song featured in his new FOMO short film, with the track including the phrase “Pray for Gaza”.
The snippet appears around the 17:47 mark of FOMO, described as Drake’s “not so short film”. The project includes appearances from his mother, Sandi, and other performers, alongside several new tracks and musical moments.
The meaning of the “Gaza” reference remains unclear. The phrase could refer to Gaza in the Middle East, or it could reference Jamaican dancehall artist Vybz Kartel, who has used “Gaza City” as a name for his home region of Portmore and refers to his supporters as “Gaza nation”.
Drake has previously shown a connection to Kartel and made a surprise appearance during the dancehall artist’s first show in Canada.
Drake has also publicly supported calls for a ceasefire in Gaza. The Canadian rapper was an early signatory of an open letter from Artists4Ceasefire calling for a ceasefire in Gaza and Israel before another life was lost. He signed the letter before the end of October 2023.
The letter states: “We ask that, as President of the United States, you and the US Congress call for an immediate de-escalation and ceasefire in Gaza and Israel before another life is lost.”
Drake’s longtime producer Noah “40” Shebib previously discussed how the rapper came to sign the letter. Shebib said a friend approached him about signing, after which he asked whether Drake would also participate.
“A friend came to me and asked me if I want to sign and I said, of course. He asked if Drake would and I went to talk to him and the team,” he said. “That simple really.”
The new “Pray for Gaza” lyric therefore has two possible contexts based on Drake’s previous association with both Gaza-related advocacy and Vybz Kartel’s use of “Gaza” terminology. The FOMO track itself does not clarify which meaning Drake intended.

title: Tarar visits families of Kohat attack victims  vows to eliminate terrorism
description: Criticises PTI s government over  shortcomings in policing  governance and development
content:
Criticises PTI's government over shortcomings in policing, governance and development
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Monday visited the families of police personnel martyred in last week’s deadly attack in Kohat, offering condolences to the bereaved and vowing that the government would not rest until terrorism was eliminated.
At least 21 people, including 15 police personnel and six civilians, were killed when an explosion struck a mosque at Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers, followed by an attack involving several armed terrorists, according to an initial incident report issued by the DHQ Hospital Kohat medical superintendent and district health officer. More than 100 people were injured in the attack.
Tarar visited the residence of policeman Faheemullah, the only brother of three sisters, who was among those killed. He met his father, Ikramullah, and offered Fateha for the departed soul, state-run Radio Pakistan reported.
Minister for Information and Broadcasting @TararAttaullah visited the residence of policeman Faheemullah, the only brother of three sisters, who was martyred in Kohat incident. He met with Faheemullah Shaheed’s father, Ikramullah, and offered Fateha for the departed soul #News … pic.twitter.com/0kie4EPKVX
Speaking at a press conference later, Tarar said the victims had sacrificed their lives for the safety of the country and that their families would not be left alone. “They sacrificed their lives so that this province and this country could remain safe,” Tarar said. “They orphaned their children but saved hundreds of children from being martyred.”
The minister also visited the injured at CMH Kohat, where he said he was impressed by the morale of the injured personnel. “I cannot describe how high their morale was,” he said. “The young men of our army and police who took part in this operation fought the terrorists bravely. Even personnel who were on leave put on their uniforms and joined the operation,” he added.
Read: 15 police personnel among 21 martyred in Kohat Police Lines terrorist attack; over 100 injured
Tarar said the attack would not weaken the resolve of the security forces or the public. “These terrorists are cowards. They strike from behind,” he said. He stated that the government would continue the fight until terrorism was eliminated “from its roots”.
“On behalf of the prime minister, I say that until and unless we defeat terrorism from its root, we will not rest,” he said, adding that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had said the time was not far when the terrorists would be defeated.
Tarar then criticised Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi over his response to the attack, asking where he had been when the incident occurred.
“You have time for the politics of chaos, but not for the people of your province,” he said, adding, “What have you done for education, health and public welfare?”
Minister for Information and Broadcasting @TararAttaullah is talking to media in Kohat https://t.co/2q2bQIL9hf
Tarar also criticised the PTI-led provincial government over shortcomings in policing, governance and development, saying that the province did not even have a forensic laboratory to facilitate police investigations.
The minister said that contracts were being awarded to favoured individuals in return for payments and that new records of corruption were being set in the province. He also questioned who had been awarded gold-mining contracts and where the province’s development funds were being spent.
Turning to PTI’s planned September 27 protest in Islamabad, Tarar said, “No one will be allowed to shut down Islamabad. Armed groups will not be allowed to come towards Islamabad.”
Read More: Captain, lieutenant among six martyred as eight terrorists killed in Hangu fire exchange: ISPR
Tarar rejected PTI’s claims that its protests were peaceful, saying, “Peaceful people do not leave their homes carrying sticks fitted with nails.” He also said PTI members would be held accountable and would not be allowed to “hide behind excuses” involving funds.
He said projects such as the Kohat Tunnel and motorway had been built during the government of former prime minister Nawaz Sharif, while alleging that forests were being cut down and factories producing counterfeit cigarettes had been found in the province.
At least 21 people, including 15 police personnel and six civilians, were killed in the blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers, according to an initial incident report issued by DHQ Hospital Kohat medical superintendent and the district health officer.
The report said the blast occurred at approximately 1:20pm during Friday prayers at a mosque located at Police Lines on Hangu Road in Kohat, followed by a terrorist attack involving around five to seven terrorists.
Of the 21 people killed, 15 were police personnel and six were civilians. The report identified one of the deceased civilians as Dr Israel Khan Aurakzai, Chief District Specialist (Paediatrics) at Liaqat Memorial Hospital, Kohat.
It further said 103 injured people had been received at the two hospitals, including 13 at Liaqat Memorial Hospital and 90 at DHQ Hospital Kohat. The injured comprised 73 police personnel and 30 civilians.

Of the total injured, 34 were admitted for treatment, while five patients underwent laparotomy, a surgical procedure involving an incision into the abdomen. The report said four of the patients who underwent laparotomy had been referred to tertiary care facilities in Peshawar for further treatment.
It added that the situation was being closely monitored and all possible medical assistance was being provided to the injured at the relevant health facilities.
According to the police, seven armed terrorists infiltrated the police lines following the explosion at the mosque. The police said six terrorists, including the suicide bomber, had been killed so far. Initially, a suicide attacker blew himself up near the Special Branch building after the explosion, it added.
Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, has claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers. Islamabad has repeatedly asked the Taliban regime to deny the use of Afghan soil for terrorist attacks inside Pakistan. However, the de facto rulers in Kabul have been reluctant to take action against terrorist groups operating from their territory.

title: Pete Davidson and Colin Jost bring comedy show to Staten Island Ferry
description: Pete Davidson and Colin Jost hosted free comedy show aboard their Staten Island Ferry project with Snapple
content:
Pete Davidson and Colin Jost hosted free comedy show aboard their Staten Island Ferry project with Snapple
Pete Davidson and Colin Jost have brought their long-discussed Staten Island Ferry entertainment project to life with a one-night comedy show aboard the decommissioned vessel they bought in 2022.
The comedians joined a group of investors who purchased the John F. Kennedy ferry for $280,000 at a city auction. Built in 1965, the ferry was the oldest vessel in the Staten Island fleet when it was retired because of mechanical failures.
Davidson and Jost initially planned to transform the ferry into a floating entertainment venue, but the project attracted criticism after the purchase was announced. Four years later, they partnered with Snapple for a free, one-night comedy event aboard the vessel.
The ferry was temporarily renamed the Snapple Island Ferry for the event, which was designed as a promotional activation for Snapple's return to its glass bottles in select New York retailers.
Limited free tickets were released daily from September 3 to 8, creating demand among attendees hoping to secure a place at the comedy show.
The event featured performances from several comedians, including Matt Richards, Sal Vulcano and Caitlin Peluffo.
Davidson and Jost opened the event, addressing the criticism surrounding their ferry purchase. Davidson said, "The amount of shit that people have talked," before adding, "Well, suck it!"
Davidson also thanked attendees for coming and said the pair had wanted to stage the event for around five years. "This is something we've wanted to do for like five years, so thank you guys for coming out," Davidson said.
The event also marked Snapple's glass-bottle revival, following the brand's limited return to glass bottles in 2025 after years of using plastic packaging.

title: California introduces annual Dolly Parton Day on September 25
description: California will observe Dolly Parton Day every September 25 following country music singer   s death at 80
content:
California will observe Dolly Parton Day every September 25 following country music singer’s death at 80
California will observe Dolly Parton Day annually on September 25 following the death of the country music singer at the age of 80.
California Governor Gavin Newsom signed a bill on Sunday establishing the annual day of remembrance in honour of Parton, who died on August 25 in Nashville.
The date was selected as a reference to Parton’s famous song “Nine to Five”. Written numerically, September 25 becomes 9-2-5, creating a connection to the 1980 hit.
“With this bill, we are not just establishing a day to celebrate Dolly Parton, we are creating an annual reminder to us, every year, to live the way she did - joyfully, graciously, and with a whole lot of heart,” said Newsom in the announcement.
The new law recognises Parton’s work as a singer, songwriter, actress and philanthropist. She was one of country music’s most commercially successful artists, with the Californian government stating that she sold more than 100 million records worldwide.
Parton was also recognised for her charitable work through the Dolly Parton Imagination Library. The foundation has distributed more than 300 million books to children around the world.
Parton’s career included songs such as “Jolene”, “Nine to Five” and “I Will Always Love You”. Her work across music, film and charitable initiatives made her a prominent figure beyond the country music industry.

Jethro further accused the singer of being selfish and making fun of his mental health. He claimed he had supported Ed’s early music career, including taking him to a studio and performing on early songs.
Addressing Macklemore’s removal from the tour, Jethro added, “He is shady and he’s dropped Macklemore himself I believe 100% he’s a coward.”
The controversy followed Macklemore’s performances at Ed’s MetLife Stadium concerts, where he chanted “Free Palestine” and performed his protest song “Hind’s Hall”.

title: MQM P chief calls for new administrative units  says time to end dynastic politics
description: Khalid Maqbool calls for fresh census  six administrative units in Sindh while Farooq Sattar reaffirms party s call
content:
Khalid Maqbool calls for fresh census, six administrative units in Sindh while Farooq Sattar reaffirms party's call
Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) Chairman Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui on Monday called for the creation of new administrative units in Pakistan, saying the time had come to end hereditary and dynastic politics and that the issue would not be resolved through parliament.
Speaking at a press conference at the party’s temporary headquarters, Siddiqui described a large rally held in Karachi a day earlier as a referendum by the city’s people. “Yesterday, the people of Karachi came out onto the streets and gave their verdict,” he said, adding that “feudal democracy cannot be Pakistan’s future.”
Siddiqui said administrative units were needed in Pakistan and called for an end to what he described as the practice of “enslaving the people”. “This rally was held for Pakistan’s survival,” he said. “We have seen the way of the streets. This will not pass through the assemblies.”
He also called for a fresh census and urged the courts to take notice of what he described as the manner in which Sindh had been governed since 1917.
The MQM-P chairman said the party had faced pressure over its demand for new administrative units for decades, alleging that “taking MQM’s name has been turned into a crime”. “Even after 40 years, MQM is being made a means for [pressuring on] the matter of administrative units,” he said, adding that several senior party leaders had served jail terms.
Also Read: Palijo warns against 'playing with fire' over Sindh division
Siddiqui said the party had consistently declared its allegiance to Pakistan since August 22, despite which, he said, its offices had been shut down.
The chairman also said the party was being threatened in an attempt to intimidate it, while stressing that its demand was not merely for the MQM-P. “This is not our need, it is Pakistan’s need,” he said.
Siddiqui further said that some people within the party’s ranks needed to separate themselves from the organisation.
Meanwhile, senior MQM-P leader Dr Farooq Sattar said six administrative units would eventually be created in Sindh. “You snatched one governor from us; now we will have six governors,” Sattar said.
The press conference was attended by senior MQM-P leaders, including Sattar, Waseem Akhtar, Nasreen Jalil, Ali Khursheedi, Muhammad Hussain and Waseem Aftab. Siddiqui also announced that the party’s convention would be held on October 4 in District West.

title: Houthis push for control of Yemen highlands as Trump reported to have called off airstrikes
description: A lightning advance by the group this month has extended the wider Middle East conflict to a new theatre
content:
A lightning advance by the group this month has extended the wider Middle East conflict to a new theatre
Houthi fighters were pushing to seize strategic heights in Yemen on Monday to cut off the Red Sea coast from remaining areas held by Saudi-backed forces, after a report that President Donald Trump had called off US strikes on the group at the last minute.
A lightning advance by the group this month has extended the wider Middle East conflict to a new theatre and further threatened global energy supplies.
Washington has so far rebuffed repeated pleas from Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to join the fight in Yemen. The Houthis said on Saturday they had fired on Riyadh, where loud booms were followed by columns of smoke visible near the airport.
Saudi Arabia has not commented on the first apparent strikes on the capital since the escalation began.
The New York Times reported that the Trump administration had prepared on Sunday to launch airstrikes against the Houthis after fresh pleas from the Saudi crown prince. But the newspaper said Trump called off the airstrikes at the last minute, even as troops were loading bombs onto aircraft.
Read: Mohsin Naqvi received by Iranian interior minister on arrival in Iran: Iranian media
Reuters could not immediately verify the report, and the US military's Central Command did not respond to an email seeking comment.
The Houthis, who have controlled Yemen's capital since 2014, seized the country's Red Sea coast this month in a lightning advance that routed forces of an internationally recognised Yemeni government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia and based in the south.
Saudi Arabia has launched hundreds of strikes in recent days on the fighters' positions in the highlands, according to the Houthis. But the air power advantage has so far done little to slow the advance of the fighters as Saudi-backed government forces have melted away.
According to the United Nations, nearly 700 people have been killed and thousands injured in the flare-up in fighting. More than 120,000 Yemenis have fled homes within Yemen, and thousands more have fled by boat across the Red Sea to Africa.
Five Yemeni military sources told Reuters the Houthis were now seeking to seize strategic heights, known as the Kahboub Mountains, in two provinces, Taiz and Lahij, which separate the Red Sea coast from the government-held south.
Fighting has centred on the outskirts of the remote mountain Al-Wazi'iyah district in Taiz province, and Ras al-Ara along the Indian Ocean coast between the mouth of the Red Sea that the fighters captured last week and the government's base in Aden.
Read more: Saudi Arabia warns of 'firm' response after Houthi missile, drone attacks injure 13 civilians
The Houthis aim to secure the rear of their forces around the Bab al-Mandab Strait leading into the Red Sea by taking control of the heights, which would allow them to open new fronts, according to the sources. That would help protect exposed positions the Houthis captured during their advance around Dhubab on the Red Sea and on Perim Island in the strait.
The surge in fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis creates a new dilemma for Trump, under pressure to help defend Washington's close Saudi allies but anxious not to further expand the deeply unpopular war he launched in February against Iran.
The United States bombed the Houthis for two months in early 2025, but Trump called off those strikes after reaching a ceasefire with the group and has kept out of the conflict since.
The Houthis' newfound control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait risks cutting off the main alternative route that Saudi Arabia has used for oil exports that bypass disruption in the Strait of Hormuz.
Saudi Arabia has responded by increasing shipments through Hormuz, where a small number of tankers are increasingly shuttling back and forth to bring out oil with their transponders off, charging record fees of as much as a quarter of the value of the cargo to brave the wartime risk. They then transfer the oil to other ships in the Indian Ocean, bound for customers in Asia or elsewhere.
Satellite data shows Saudi exports through Hormuz reaching 2.9 million barrels per day in recent days, up from just 700,000 in August, partially making up for a halt to Saudi loadings at its Red Sea port of Yanbu.
Also read: Oil prices slide on hopes of diplomacy in Iran war
That has helped put a cap on the global price of crude oil, which has retreated closer to $100 a barrel after approaching $110 last week. But consumers and industry are still paying record prices for refined fuels.
The US retail price of diesel, politically sensitive for Trump with midterm elections in six weeks, hit another all-time high on Monday above $6.51 a gallon. It was around $3.75 before Trump launched the war alongside Israel in February.
In the latest reported attack in Hormuz, Britain's UKMTO maritime security agency said a ship sailing into the strait had been hit with a projectile, causing minor injuries to crew.
Diplomacy in the wider conflict has largely been stalled since a June interim agreement between the United States and Iran collapsed within weeks. Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian is due to fly on Tuesday to New York to attend the UN General Assembly, the first such visit since Trump launched "Operation Epic Fury" against his country alongside Israel in February.

title: Resident Evil  opens to  60m at box office  setting new franchise record
description: Resident Evil  opens with  60m domestically  giving Zach Cregger his biggest opening weekend yet
content:
'Resident Evil' opens with $60m domestically, giving Zach Cregger his biggest opening weekend yet
Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil reboot opened with $60 million (£44.5 million) in North America, giving the video game adaptation the biggest opening weekend of the franchise.
The horror film grossed $60 million across its first three days, exceeding Sony Pictures’ initial $40 million projection and the $53 million to $55 million estimate given on Saturday.
Resident Evil opened in 3,684 North American cinemas and has a reported production budget of $75 million.
The film received a B+ CinemaScore from audiences, with 65% of its domestic audience identifying as male and 74% aged under 35. It also earned $43.8 million from 62 international markets.
The opening surpasses the previous franchise record held by Resident Evil: Afterlife , which grossed $60.1 million across its entire North American run. The Resident Evil series has collectively earned more than $1.2 billion worldwide.
Cregger’s reboot follows a medical courier, played by Austin Abrams, who attempts to deliver a valuable item during a deadly viral outbreak in Raccoon City. The film also stars Zach Cherry, Kali Reis and Paul Walter Hauser.
Resident Evil marks Cregger’s biggest opening to date, surpassing Weapons, which debuted with $43.5 million in August 2025. The film also currently holds a 96% approval rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes, alongside a 92% audience score.
Cregger has previously discussed the possibility of continuing the franchise. Before the film’s release, he said: “I can't help thinking about other places this story could go” when asked about potential future involvement with Resident Evil.
Elsewhere at the box office, Practical Magic 2 is expected to take second place with around $12.2 million in its second weekend, bringing its North American total to approximately $50 million.
Spider-Man: Brand New Day is projected to rank third with $6.5 million, taking its domestic total to around $944.5 million.
