title: Michael Jackson s bedazzled glove   Bad  jacket heading to Abu Dhabi auction
description: Julien   s Auctions bring music  fashion and pop culture artefacts with 11 highlights estimated at up to Dh3 86m
content:
Julien’s Auctions bring music, fashion and pop culture artefacts with 11 highlights estimated at up to Dh3.86m
A collection of memorabilia linked to some of the world's most recognisable cultural figures, including Michael Jackson and Princess Diana, is set to go under the hammer in Abu Dhabi this December, with the currently announced highlights carrying combined estimates of up to Dh3.86 million.
According to Gulf News , Julien's Auctions will host its inaugural regional Celebrity & Culture Week at Rosewood Abu Dhabi on Al Maryah Island from December 5 to 10. The event will feature three separate auctions bringing together fashion, music, film and other pieces associated with major international figures.
Among the most closely watched items is a crystal-covered glove worn by Michael Jackson during a 2002 Vibe magazine cover shoot. The glove carries an estimated value of between $40,000 and $60,000, or approximately Dh147,000 to Dh220,000.
The auction will also offer the loafers Jackson wore in the iconic Thriller music video. They are expected to fetch between $20,000 and $40,000 and are accompanied by a personal letter to choreographer Michael Peters.
Two jackets associated with Jackson's Bad era will also be offered. One, designed by his longtime costume designers Michael Bush and Dennis Tompkins, was signed and donated by Jackson to the TJ Martell Foundation. It is estimated at between $60,000 and $80,000.
Another is one of only six light-up Thriller performance jackets produced and carries an estimate of $30,000 to $50,000, according to Gulf News .
Princess Diana's memorabilia forms another major part of the Abu Dhabi auction programme, with the standout piece being a midnight-blue Catherine Walker gown she wore at the 1995 CFDA Fashion Awards in New York, where she presented fashion editor Liz Tilberis with an award.
According to Gulf News , the gown is expected to command between $200,000 and $400,000, making it the most valuable individual lot among the highlights announced so far. At the upper end, that translates to roughly Dh1.47 million.
Other Diana items are linked to some of her most significant public appearances during the final years of her life.
A pair of suede Selfridges driving loafers worn during her 1997 visit to a landmine field in Angola carries an estimate of $20,000 to $30,000. A Ralph Lauren shirt worn by Diana while visiting landmine survivors in Bosnia that same year is expected to bring between $10,000 and $20,000.
The auction house's own announcement describes the Diana collection as its largest Diana-focused auction to date, highlighting the links between the garments and the late princess's public life and humanitarian work.
The third sale, titled Pop Culture Legends, broadens the collection beyond Jackson and Diana.
According to Gulf News , the auction will include memorabilia connected to figures including Bruce Lee, Banksy, Amy Winehouse, Kurt Cobain, Madonna, Eddie Van Halen and Sabrina Carpenter.
A guitar once owned by American author Mark Twain is currently the most highly valued highlight in this section, with an estimate of $100,000 to $200,000.
Kurt Cobain memorabilia includes a guitar played by the Nirvana frontman, estimated at $60,000 to $80,000, along with a stage-worn jacket valued at $20,000 to $40,000.
Meanwhile, the yellow nunchaku used by Bruce Lee in the 1978 film Game of Death are estimated at between $30,000 and $50,000.
Julien's Auctions has also promoted the Abu Dhabi event on its official Instagram account, announcing "Celebrity & Culture Week" in Abu Dhabi as "a new international platform celebrating the people, stories, and artifacts that have shaped global popular culture".
The event will combine the live sales with a museum-style exhibition, allowing visitors to view selected memorabilia before the pieces are offered to bidders.
Julien's has not yet released the complete catalogues for all three auctions, meaning the final value of the entire collection remains unknown.
Gulf News reports that the 11 highlight lots announced so far have combined estimates ranging from $590,000 to $1.05 million, equivalent to approximately Dh2.17 million to Dh3.86 million.
Julien's Auctions co-founder and executive director Martin Nolan told Artnet that the choice of Jackson and Diana reflected their international appeal, while also pointing to their connections with the UAE.
Both stars visited the country during their lifetimes, and Nolan said their presence at Julien's inaugural regional auction was particularly significant because of their popularity in the region.
The auction house is also looking to Abu Dhabi's expanding collector community. Nolan said the Middle Eastern collector base was becoming younger and more diverse, with interest extending beyond traditional Western pop culture.
The event will take place alongside a growing calendar of cultural and luxury events in Abu Dhabi. Gulf News noted that it follows the debut of Frieze Abu Dhabi in November and comes just before the opening of the Guggenheim Abu Dhabi on December 11.

title: Fire Emblem  Fortune   s Weave wins over critics with 89 Metacritic score
description: Fire Emblem  Fortune   s Weave has received strong reviews  with 89 score on Metacritic and OpenCritic
content:
Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave has received strong reviews, with 89 score on Metacritic and OpenCritic
Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave launched on Friday and has received strong reviews from critics, with the game currently holding an 89 score on both Metacritic and OpenCritic.
Metacritic’s score is based on around 70 critic reviews, while OpenCritic reports that 97% of critics recommend the game.
Fortune’s Weave follows 2023’s Fire Emblem: Engage and returns to the social-simulation elements associated with Fire Emblem: Three Houses.
Rather than locking players into one route, the game allows them to move between four main character paths, providing different perspectives on its story.
The game is set centuries before Three Houses in the Dagdan Empire, south of Fodlan. Players can travel through time and guide different Flame Lords, including Leda, Theodora, Dietrich and Cai, each pursuing different goals before the Heroic Games in the capital city of Dagsion.
According to reviews, the game expands on the structure of Three Houses with activities between battles, including finding allies, completing quests, improving combat skills and exploring the continent.
Players can also restart chapters and replay completed sections while developing their armies in different ways.
The game also introduces extensive character-specific skills and build options. Each character has abilities that reflect their individual traits, while classes, combat arts and weapon specialisations provide further opportunities to customise units.
The reviews also highlight Fortune’s Weave’s technical improvements on Nintendo Switch 2. Battle animations, cinematics, character models and portrait movements have been improved compared with Three Houses and Engage, while loading times are described as significantly shorter.
With more than 120 hours spent playing the game, Polygon's review described Fortune’s Weave as a “monumental achievement for Nintendo and Intelligent Systems”.

title: Brigitte Bardot s personal belongings to go under hammer in Paris
description: Sale includes Repetto ballet flats  jewelry  furniture  photographs and everyday objects
content:
Sale includes Repetto ballet flats, jewelry, furniture, photographs and everyday objects
Personal belongings of late French actress and singer Brigitte Bardot, including the ballet flats that inspired an iconic Repetto shoe and a diamond-set ring, will go under the hammer on Monday in Paris.
French auction house Millon will offer 285 lots from Bardot's homes in Paris and the southern French resort town of Saint-Tropez at Hotel Drouot, one of France's best-known auction venues.
The collection includes clothing, furniture, photographs, jewelry, musical instruments and everyday objects, as well as memorabilia from Bardot's career and her later life devoted to animal protection.
Among the highlights are Repetto ballet flats. Millon said Bardot asked French shoemaker Rose Repetto in 1956 to create a flat, flexible shoe inspired by ballet footwear but suitable for everyday wear. The resulting Cendrillon model became associated with Bardot after she wore it in the 1956 film "And God Created Woman."
Jewelry in the sale includes a Mellerio ring set with a 3.67-carat diamond, while other lots include guitars, an Olivetti Lettera 22 typewriter, hats, perfume bottles and furniture from Bardot's homes.
The sale also features objects from La Madrague, Bardot's famous seaside home in Saint-Tropez, which she acquired in 1958 and that became closely associated with her public image.
Bardot became an international film star in the 1950s, particularly after "And God Created Woman," directed by Roger Vadim. She retired from acting at 38 and increasingly used her public profile to promote animal protection.
She founded the Fondation Brigitte Bardot in 1986. The French animal protection organization says it now operates in 70 countries.
Millon said the proceeds from Monday's auction will go to the Fondation Brigitte Bardot and Bardot's only son, Nicolas-Jacques Charrier.

title: Safety first as mixed martial arts grapples for recognition at Asian Games
description: Mixed martial arts makes Asian Games debut in Nagoya
content:
Mixed martial arts makes Asian Games debut in Nagoya
With no cage, no elbows and no appetite for blood on the mat, the Asian Games' mixed ‌martial arts competition is not quite the visceral experience of a UFC fight night.
The athletes battle in traditional martial arts uniforms, wear shin guards for protection and dropping knees ‌onto prone opponents is very much ⁠out of ​bounds.
The only octagon at the Nagoya City Inae Sports Centre is a ​grey one marked on the open ‌mat. The competition's organisers know the modifications ​may not be to the liking of hard-core fans of a sport once dubbed "human cockfighting" but they are part of an attempt to make it more palatable for a longer-term tilt at Olympic inclusion.
"It's ⁠a sport, a rule-set that we believe is more suitable for the Olympic programme," Galastein Tan, director ‌general of the Federation of International Mixed Martial Arts (FIMMA), told Reuters.
"A rule-set that we think is very athlete safety-centric."
Modifications aside, the fighting at the sport's Asian Games debut remains intense and bruising.
South Korea's Lee Bo-mi was in tears ⁠and clutching her shoulder after a heavy takedown from Bahrain's Russian-born fighter ⁠Diana Pogosian in the ​women's 54kg semi-final. Off the ‌mat, there is a bigger fight in the background as the sport's rival governing bodies grapple for influence and global supremacy.
FIMMA, established last year, was born out of the Asian Mixed Martial Arts Association set up by Chinese billionaire Gordon Tang.
With Tang a vice-president of the Olympic Council of Asia, FIMMA's brand of MMA was endorsed for Nagoya and will be retained on the programme of sports for subsequent Asian Games, FIMMA officials told Reuters.
Getting ⁠MMA to the Olympics will be a far more complex journey. FIMMA has another rival shooting for Olympic recognition in the Global Association of ⁠Mixed Martial Arts (GAMMA), which describes itself as the sport's international federation and organises its own championships.
"When you talk about governing bodies, anybody can set up an association or international association," said Tan.
"The ultimate one is who gets the recognition by the International Olympic Committee."
There were banks of empty seats at the venue and no visible sponsor logos on day two of the Asian Games competition.
But FIMMA is hopeful IOC officials will take notice of the tournament and see the potential of including a ⁠sport with a massive global following on the Olympic programme. With no universally accepted ​rule-set for the sport, it may be some time before MMA can be looked at as a serious option, though.
Until then, FIMMA will look to build momentum and influence by staging more regional and continental competitions, pushing a format they say is more accessible than cage fighting. "There is always ​a judo mat or a karate mat you can use -- it's ‌more easy for training and to set up competition," said FIMMA Executive Vice-President Alexander Engelhardt.

title: Jannat Mirza speaks out against misuse of women   s faces in fake videos
description: Influencer calls for stronger measures against those responsible after her face was used without her consent
content:
Influencer calls for stronger measures against those responsible after her face was used without her consent
Influencer Jannat Mirza has taken to social media to demand strict action against individuals misusing people’s faces to create fake and misleading content.
Mirza shared a video of herself and a male friend joking around and holding hands, calling out creators for allegedly using her face to make a fake video without her permission and putting her dignity at risk.
“This video is not funny at all. Using someone’s face and creating videos like this is extremely concerning. Today, it may be my face being used, but tomorrow it could be any girl’s face and her dignity could be put at risk,” she said.
The influencer added, “I’m someone who is active on social media, and even I felt extremely uncomfortable seeing this. Imagine girls who aren’t on social media at all — their pictures can also be misused in ways they may never even know about.”
Mirza’s comments about the misuse of AI and people’s identities were applauded by fans online, with many also calling for stronger laws to address the issue.
“She is absolutely right in this matter. There should be proper laws on this. AI is dangerous, especially in a society like Pakistan where respect is important. It is a place where people can be subjected to violence in the name of tradition,” one user wrote.
Another added, “There must be strict rules to punish people who make such videos using AI.”
As a public figure, Mirza has repeatedly raised concerns about online harassment and personal attacks, urging authorities to take stronger action against individuals who target women on social media.
With her latest remarks, she has once again highlighted concerns surrounding AI-generated content, privacy and the misuse of women’s identities online.

title: What is Ibogaine  Presley Gerber received psychedelic therapy in Mexico months before his death
description: In March  Gerber shared a video documenting a  pre Ibogaine Flood Dose  in Cancun  Mexico
content:
In March, Gerber shared a video documenting a 'pre Ibogaine Flood Dose' in Cancun, Mexico
Presley Gerber underwent psychedelic drug treatment in Mexico months before his death at the age of 27.
The son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber died on Sunday at a rehabilitation facility. His official cause of death has not been announced.
In March, Gerber shared a video documenting a “pre Ibogaine Flood Dose” in Cancun, Mexico.
Ibogaine is a naturally occurring psychedelic that has drawn attention for its potential use in treating substance use disorders, particularly opioid and alcohol dependence.
Reflecting on the experience, Gerber wrote: “Pre Ibogaine Flood Dose – quiet moment before everything changed.”
He described feeling frightened before the treatment and discussed his efforts to confront personal challenges and work towards recovery.
“My mantras were love yourself and lis gotta be the last time for this reason. letting go of control didn’t come easy, but I trusted there was something bigger than me guiding it. I knew why I was there.”
Gerber also expressed gratitude to the people who supported him during the experience. His mother, sister Kaia and father publicly shared messages of encouragement beneath the post.
Ibogaine is illegal in the United States, while possession and administration are permitted in Mexico.
In the UK, it remains an unlicensed experimental drug and is not available through the NHS.
Gerber, who signed with IMG Models at 15, had spoken openly about depression and substance abuse.
In a 2023 appearance on the Studio 22 podcast, he described mental health as a significant part of his life and said he wanted to help others facing similar struggles.
An autopsy had not been completed at the time og reporting.

title: Kojima Productions comments on PlayStation relationship after PHYSINT split
description: Kojima Productions says its relationship with PlayStation remains strong after Sony left PHYSINT
content:
Kojima Productions says its relationship with PlayStation remains strong after Sony left PHYSINT
Kojima Productions has addressed speculation surrounding Sony’s decision to end its involvement with PHYSINT, saying its relationship with PlayStation “remains strong” as development continues with Xbox.
Sony announced on September 10 that it was stepping away from the action-espionage game, first announced alongside Kojima Productions in 2024.
Hideo Kojima later revealed that PlayStation Studios had informed the developer in mid-June that it planned to cancel the project.
Kojima Productions spent around three months looking for another publishing partner before reaching an agreement with Xbox.
Reports following the announcement claimed Sony had concerns about PHYSINT’s budget, missed deadlines, potential profitability and its lack of permanent PlayStation exclusivity. Reports also cited the commercial performance of Death Stranding and Death Stranding 2 as a factor in Sony’s decision.
Kojima Productions said those claims did not come from official or on-the-record sources.
“Normally, we would not comment on unsubstantiated speculation on the internet, but these aspersions around our relationship with PlayStation, the commercial performance of the DEATH STRANDING franchise, and the broader production planning and investment for PHYSINT, have reached beyond the studio and have touched our fans, our creative partners, and colleagues we have worked alongside with for three decades,” the studio said.
It added: “None of the claims written came from any official or on-the-record source, and as such we encourage you to take them with a dose of scepticism.”
The developer acknowledged that losing PlayStation as PHYSINT’s publisher was a “serious situation” but said it remains profitable.
“The studio is in a healthy, profitable state, development for PHYSINT continues to move forward with XBOX, and our relationship with PlayStation remains strong.”
Kojima also said he was “shocked and surprised” by Sony’s decision but confirmed there was no ongoing dispute: “We’re not in dispute. We’re not fighting with them.”

title: Merz clings on after German election  disaster
description: AfD tops state election for second time in a month as chancellor s coalition partners clash over unpopular reforms
content:
AfD tops state election for second time in a month as chancellor's coalition partners clash over unpopular reforms
Chancellor Friedrich Merz was clinging to power on Monday after his conservative party tumbled to its worst regional election defeat in postwar Germany and members of his coalition clashed over his unpopular reform agenda.
Merz himself described Sunday's loss in the northeastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania as a "disaster" as his party for the first time missed the 5% threshold for entering a state parliament.
The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) took first place. While it fell well short of a majority, it was the second time the party had topped a state election within a month, which it sees as building momentum towards national power.
Merz's party also bled votes in a second election in the state of Berlin, which could see the far-left Die Linke party, the descendants of the Communist party that once ran East Germany, take power in a coalition after winning most seats.
German chancellor's future in the balance
Sunday's results may not prove a knock-out blow for Merz, but his low approval ratings, unpopular reforms and the AfD's surge have left his future in the balance.
Several conservative state premiers met on Sunday to take stock after having publicly backed Merz in an open letter last week. "The meeting was not about a revolt or a plot against Chancellor Merz," one of the participants of the meeting told Reuters . "However, there was agreement that the chancellor needs to deliver more following the CDU's difficult results in the state elections."
Read: Thousands protest in Germany as far-right AfD sets sights on power
Within minutes of the results coming in on Sunday, Merz in televised remarks vowed to press on with his reform agenda that he says is vital to revive sluggish growth in Europe's largest economy and keep it globally competitive.
But members of his centre-left coalition partner, the Social Democrats, pushed back. That includes Manuela Schwesig, the popular incumbent state premier of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, who has sharply criticised the federal government's pension reforms.
Schwesig said she was "very irritated" by Merz's remarks. "I think more humility is actually called for on the part of the chancellor," she told the ARD broadcaster.
Bitter pill for Germany's immigrant communities
The AfD party leads in national opinion polls but has been kept from power by the other main parties' refusal to work with it, in a policy known as the "firewall" that has been increasingly scrutinised as the AfD gained strength. Its hardline stance on immigration has left some in Germany of migrant background questioning their future.
"The fact that the AfD is in the lead is quite a bitter pill to swallow," said Yasmin Goudarzi, an educational scientist who attended an election event hosted by a migrant organisation in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania's capital Schwerin.
In Berlin, Die Linke topped the polls in a state election for the first time on a campaign to nationalise housing from corporate landlords and put a cap on rents, echoing the rise of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani. "From today, we're changing Berlin together," said Die Linke's lead candidate Elif Eralp, the 45-year-old daughter of left-wing Turkish parents who fled a coup in Turkey in 1980.
Read More: As history returns, Germany sees echoes of its past
Elected last year on a promise of reforms to return Germany's stagnant economy to growth, Merz has struggled to win over voters, as a stream of communication missteps served to compound resentment over unpopular pension, tax and healthcare reforms. Disillusionment with his government has hung over the campaigns in both Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin, where voters have focused on soaring energy and housing costs.
Schwesig, sometimes seen as a potential next SPD national leader, is likely to remain in power in her state.
"Yes, I would have imagined a different outcome as well because, let's say, the troublemakers who voted for the AfD clearly weren't paying attention in history class," said Detlef Spelker, a passerby in Schwerin. "We've been in a similar situation before, almost 100 years ago. Inflation, problems with jobs, nobody had any money. We'll see what this brings now. I don't know whether they'll deliver."

title: Syrian duo chase dreams with Asian Games refugee team
description: Muhammad and Hunaidi make history as the OCA   s first dedicated refugee athletes
content:
Muhammad and Hunaidi make history as the OCA’s first dedicated refugee athletes
Living in exile at Jordan's Azraq refugee camp was never the life Mahmoud Jasem Muhammad or ‌Tala Hasan Hunaidi chose for themselves.
So when taekwondo offered an escape from the trauma of fleeing war-torn Syria — and the chance to compete alongside the continent's elite fighters at the Asian Games — the pair seized the opportunity.
For the first time in the history of its flagship event, the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) is fielding a dedicated refugee team containing the two Syrian taekwondo athletes
"Being here today isn't just about competing in ⁠another tournament," Muhammad, who is set to compete in the men's 80- kg kyorugi, told reporters on Monday.
"I'm carrying a story with me — a story that, God willing, will become a success story. I carry that story with me into every fight.
"We didn't leave our country by choice. It was because of the difficult living conditions and the wars that took place, so we were forced to leave and move to another country to build a life there."
The 24-year-old said he is not at the Games merely to make up the numbers.
"The preparations were really intense, and our goal isn't just to participate — we're hoping to achieve something, God willing."
Hunaidi ‌also expressed ⁠gratitude to the International Olympic Committee, the OCA, and World Taekwondo for helping her live out this dream.
"Sport has changed me for the better. I've become a different person. I have hope now, and I have dreams and ambitions for the future," the 18-year-old said.
"We've seen a different side of life, and we now have hope. We've learned that nothing is ⁠impossible. Things can be difficult sometimes, but with time, you can overcome them and move forward."
Shiva Kesavan, vice chair of the OCA Athletes' Committee, praised the pair as role models, who have been integrated into the wider Asian Games community.
"It can be ⁠overwhelming for them to come straight into the Asian Games and see the top continental talents here," Kesavan told Reuters.
"They have their personal goals, but more importantly, they're now part of a community. They will make friends, ⁠who'd support them and this is the human connection that sport is all about.
"So I tell them 'No pressure, you are already role models. We all look up to you. So just go there, have a good time, and express yourself through your sport.' "

title: Taylor Swift set for special MTV VMA honour recognising her music video directing
description: The new honour recognises artists whose work behind the camera has shaped music video storytelling
content:
The new honour recognises artists whose work behind the camera has shaped music video storytelling
Taylor Swift is set to receive the inaugural MTV VMA Artist Director Honors at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards, recognising her work directing music videos throughout her career. CBS and MTV announced the new honour ahead of this year’s ceremony, which will take place on September 27 in Los Angeles.
The award has been created for artists who direct some or all of their own music videos. According to the announcement, it celebrates artists whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music videos, advanced visual storytelling and established a distinctive directorial voice.
Swift has increasingly taken control of the visual direction of her music in recent years. Her directing credits include "The Man", "Cardigan", "Willow", "All Too Well: The Short Film", "Anti Hero", "Bejeweled", "Fortnight", "I Can See You", "Karma" and "Lavender Haze". Her latest music video, "The Fate of Ophelia", is also among the nominated videos at this year’s ceremony, with Swift receiving nominations across several categories.
The 2026 VMAs will also mark another significant moment for Swift at the ceremony, as she is among the nominees for Video of the Year and Artist of the Year. MTV’s official voting site lists "The Fate of Ophelia" among the Video of the Year nominees, alongside videos from Ariana Grande, Bruno Mars, GENER8ION, Madonna and Sabrina Carpenter.
Swift previously used the VMAs as a major platform for an announcement in 2022, when she revealed the title and release details of her album Midnights during her acceptance speech. However, any suggestion that she could make another major announcement at the 2026 ceremony remains speculation and has not been confirmed by MTV or Swift.
The ceremony is scheduled to air live from Los Angeles on September 27 at 7:30pm ET and 4:30pm PT on CBS and MTV, with streaming available on Paramount+ in the United States. Snoop Dogg is set to host the event.
Swift’s new Artist Director honour adds another recognition to a year in which her work as a songwriter, performer and music video creator continues to feature prominently across the awards ceremony.

Pakistan’s white-ball cricket squad began a four-day training camp on Monday here at the Hanif Mohammad High Performance Centre National Bank Stadium ahead of the men’s cricket tournament at the 2026 Asian Games in Japan.
The players worked on batting, bowling and fielding.

title: PSG beat 10 man Marseille in Ligue 1
description: Torres and Marquinhos score in a 2 1 victory
content:
Torres and Marquinhos score in a 2-1 victory
Ferran Torres continued the impressive start to his Paris Saint-Germain career by scoring the opener as the French and European champions won 2-1 at bitter rivals Marseille in Ligue 1 on Sunday.
Spain World Cup final hero Torres came off the bench to replace Khvicha Kvaratskhelia just before the hour mark and headed in a Desire Doue cross to give PSG the lead in the 66th minute at the Velodrome.
That brought the game to life, with England midfielder Angel Gomes scoring an excellent equaliser for Marseille on 72 minutes only for PSG captain Marquinhos to win the game for the visitors three minutes later.
The Brazilian defender met a Nuno Mendes cross and had his initial effort saved by Marseille goalkeeper Jeffrey de Lange before bundling in the rebound.
United States star Timothy Weah, a former PSG player, was then sent off for a second booking as Marseille finished the game a man down.
Torres scored PSG's winning goal in Brest last weekend and now has seven goals in six appearances in all competitions since joining the reigning European champions from Barcelona. He has only started three times.
"We knew that for us it was one of the most important matches of the season. We knew it wouldn't be easy but we managed to get the victory," Torres said at full-time, with PSG now up to sixth in the table, five points behind leaders Monaco after five fixtures.
"Now we can go away and play for our countries and disconnect from club football for a bit."
Torres, whose extra-time goal gave Spain victory over Argentina in the World Cup final in the United States in July, is in the squad as La Roja play their first game since that tournament away to England in the UEFA Nations League next weekend.
Struggling Marseille have now suffered four straight Ligue 1 defeats, and five losses in a row in all competitions. They therefore find themselves in the relegation zone as club football takes a three-week break.
Monaco extended their unbeaten start to the campaign by beating Lens 2-1 on Friday, and the principality side are two points clear at the top of Ligue 1 from both Lyon and Paris FC.
Lyon hammered Rennes 4-0 on Saturday, while Paris FC won 2-1 against Strasbourg.
Lille missed the opportunity to move level on points again with Monaco as they lost 2-1 at Nice on Sunday.
Algerian international Mohamed Amoura got what proved to be the winner for Nice, with Japan's Ayase Ueda scoring for Lille, his third goal in four games since signing from Feyenoord.
Former Aston Villa striker Cameron Archer scored in a third straight game for Auxerre as Will Still's team defeated Brest 2-1.
Marseille head coach Bruno Genesio dismissed speculation over his future on Monday after Paris Saint-Germain won 2-1 at the Vélodrome to inflict a fourth consecutive defeat on his side.
"There is no question of resigning," said Genesio after Sunday night's match in front of 62,000 spectators.
"I'll take stock with the management, with my staff, and with the players, because for now what matters to me is helping the team improve."
Genesio, who took over at Marseille in July following two years at Ligue 1 rivals Lille, added: "On the team's spirit and commitment, I don't have much to criticise since the start of the season."

title: Pakistan carries out  calibrated  air strikes against terrorist hideouts near Afghan border after K P attacks
description: Over 30 terrorists killed in operations across Hangu  Kohat  Thal  Information Ministry says
content:
Over 30 terrorists killed, including suicide bombers, in operations: MoIB
Pakistan carried out “calibrated” air strikes against terrorist hideouts near the Afghan border and conducted intelligence-based ground operations that killed a total of 37 terrorists following a series of deadly attacks in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MoIB) said on Monday.
"In the aftermath of recent multiple terrorist incidents inside Pakistan against the innocent people of K-P, a well-planned intelligence-based ground operation was carried out by security forces around Kohat, Hangu and Thal, followed by calibrated Air Strikes against the hideouts and safe havens of terrorist organisations responsible for these attacks, said MoIB in a statement.
The development emerged after 23 people, including 15 police personnel , were martyred in the blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
The ministry, in a statement, further said that on September 20, security forces conducted an intelligence-based ground operation against a group of terrorists in Kohat and Hangu districts. "As a result of precise and skilful engagement, nine khwarij belonging to the Indian proxy Fitna al-Khawarij were sent to hell, while several were injured."
"Moreover, based on credible intelligence, selective targeting of terrorist camps and hideouts belonging to Fitna al-khwarij and its affiliates has also been carried out in the border region with Afghanistan with precision and accuracy," it added.
The statement said three targets were destroyed in precision strikes, including a training centre for suicide bombers. It said 28 terrorists, along with several suicide bombers, were killed, while large quantities of weapons and ammunition stored at the centres and hideouts were also destroyed.
In the aftermath of recent multiple terrorist incidents inside Pakistan against the innocent people of Khyber Pakthunkhwa, a well planned intelligence based ground operation was carried out by security forces around Kohat, Hangu and Thal, followed by calibrated Air Strikes…
The ministry said Pakistan had always strived to maintain peace and stability in the region, but the safety and security of its citizens remained its foremost priority.
“It is a matter of grave concern that Afghanistan continues to remain a hub of terrorism. The threat to Pakistan emanates from Afghanistan. In this context, our action precisely targeted the terrorist hubs. Maximum precautions were taken, and it was ensured that no collateral damage occurred,” the MoIB said.
It further stated that the counterterrorism campaign, Ghazab lil Haq , being carried out by Pakistan’s security forces and law enforcement agencies under the “Azm-e-Istehkam” framework, would continue at full pace to eliminate what it described as the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country.
Operation Ghazab Lil Haq was launched in February following renewed clashes along the Pakistan–Afghanistan border, after Afghan Taliban forces fired on multiple locations, prompting swift military retaliation by Pakistan.
Pakistan earlier in the year also carried out air strikes targeting camps of the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and Islamic State Khorasan Province inside Afghanistan after a wave of attacks in Pakistan, including a suicide bombing in Islamabad.
A day earlier, two officers among six security personnel were martyred in an exchange of fire between a security forces convoy and terrorists in K-P's Hangu district. Eight terrorists belonging to the Fitna al-Khawarij were also killed during the exchange.
Read: No change in Pakistan's Afghan policy
In response to continued attacks across the province, Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, warned that Islamabad would respond in self-defence to terrorism emanating from Afghanistan “as and when needed.”
The Pakistani envoy, while addressing the UN Security Council, stated that Islamabad would not sit idle in the face of this terrorist onslaught, saying that Pakistan had made sustained efforts to alleviate the suffering of Afghans despite reservations over certain policies of the Taliban.
“Afghanistan has once again become a safe haven for numerous terrorist groups operating with impunity from its soil,” Ahmad had said, linking Pakistan’s security concerns to what he described as ties between the Taliban and terrorist groups, including the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). “Over the last three years alone, more than 4,700 innocent Pakistanis have lost their lives to terrorism emanating from Afghanistan,” the envoy had said.
Read More: Five years of Taliban rule defined by failures, broken promises, security risks: report
In a separate warning following the terrorist attack in Kohat, Pakistan said it had the “will and capability” to eliminate terror threats “wherever they are” and urged the international community to press the Afghan Taliban regime to take decisive action against terrorism.
Attributing the attack to “the vilest of Khwarij with roots in Afghanistan” the Information Ministry noted that the attack was a reminder that “terrorism has no religion and no justification”. It added that Islamabad had repeatedly raised “grave concerns” over the alleged use of Afghan territory by the banned TTP and other terrorist groups to plan and launch attacks inside the country.
“The presence of terrorist sanctuaries, alongside their recruitment and support infrastructure in Afghanistan, poses a direct threat to Pakistan’s security,” the ministry had said. It added that these concerns had repeatedly been conveyed to the Afghan Taliban regime and its interlocutors. “They must dismantle these networks rather than deflect responsibility,” Pakistan said.
United Nations Security Council report formally implicated the banned Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and terrorist entities operating from Afghanistan , highlighting tactical collaboration and shared operational logistics between the groups.
Member-state reporting confirmed that BLA militants were trained alongside TTP members at facilities in Afghanistan, according to the report, which also described growing operational links among various militant groups operating across the border.
This was not the first time a UN report pointed to the threat posed by militant groups operating from Afghanistan. In 2023, a UN report also revealed that the TTP had established a new base in K-P in mid-2023, shedding light on close ties between the TTP and the Afghan Taliban, as well as between the TTP and anti-Pakistani groups and Al Qaeda.

title: China s Xi to visit the US this week  with bilateral ties  trade  world peace on agenda
description: Xi s first visit to Washington since 2015 comes as two countries seek to ease tensions over tech  strategic issues
content:
Xi's first visit to Washington since 2015 comes as two countries seek to ease tensions over tech, strategic issues
Chinese President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to the United States from September 23 to 25, Beijing confirmed on Monday, in the latest high-level effort to manage tensions between the world’s two largest economies.
“At the invitation of President of the United States of America Donald J Trump, President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to the United States from September 23 to 25,” the Foreign Ministry said in a brief statement without elaborating.
At the invitation of President of the United States of America Donald J. Trump, President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to the United States from September 23 to 25. pic.twitter.com/Gq3hDql3pa
The visit will be Xi’s first state visit to the US since September 2015, when he travelled to Washington at the invitation of then-president Barack Obama. Xi later met Trump during his first term in 2017 and visited the US in 2023 for talks with then-president Joe Biden on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.
Xi has visited the United States five times since becoming China’s president in 2013. The upcoming trip follows Trump’s state visit to China in May, with Beijing describing the exchange of visits by the two leaders within six months as having “historic significance”.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Xi and Trump would hold an “in-depth exchange of views” on major issues concerning bilateral ties, as well as peace and development.
“Head of state diplomacy plays an irreplaceable role in providing strategic guidance to China-US relations,” Guo said, adding that Beijing would work with Washington to strengthen dialogue and cooperation, manage differences and contribute to global peace, stability and prosperity.
Xi is expected to be received by Trump at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland, according to US media reports. He is also expected to be accompanied by senior Chinese business executives, including representatives of electric vehicle maker BYD and smart manufacturing company Xiaomi.
President Xi has repeatedly spoken about the importance of the relationship between China and the United States. “Recalibrating the direction of the giant ship of China-US relations requires us to take the helm and set the right course. It is particularly important to steer clear of the various disturbances and disruptions,” he said during talks over the phone with President Trump in June 2025.
Again, during his meeting with President Trump in Busan, South Korea, in Oct 2025, he said: “You and I are at the helm of China-US relations. In the face of winds, waves and challenges, we should stay the right course, navigate through the complex landscape, and ensure the steady sailing forward of the giant ship of China-US relations.”
The upcoming summit comes as the two countries seek to ease tensions over trade, technology and other strategic issues. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday described an eight-hour meeting with Chinese officials on trade and artificial intelligence as “very successful”. The talks, held in New York, involved Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer.
Bessent said Washington had proposed a notification mechanism to address security incidents involving artificial intelligence. The two sides agreed to establish a “US-China AI dialogue” and meet again, he said. Greer said it was “imperative” for the two countries to work together.
The discussions could pave the way for agreements on trade and AI ahead of the leaders’ summit. Washington is also seeking arrangements to ensure the continued supply of rare-earth magnets and other critical minerals essential to US manufacturers.
The two sides are additionally considering an extension of their trade truce and possible guardrails for artificial intelligence development. The economic relationship gives the summit significance beyond government-to-government diplomacy. According to the US-China Business Council’s 2025 report, US exports to China support more than 530,000 jobs across the country.
Despite years of trade tensions and talk of “decoupling”, economic links between the two countries remain substantial. China-US trade exceeded $570 billion in 2025, while the two economies together account for more than 40% of global GDP.
A 2026 survey of 175 US companies by the US-China Business Council found that 95% considered their operations in China somewhat or very important to maintaining their global competitiveness. The companies cited China not only as a major market but also as a manufacturing and innovation base.
The economic relationship also extends to Chinese consumers, where American brands, restaurants, films and music have become increasingly familiar parts of everyday life.
The scale of interdependence means that changes in trade and technology policy can affect manufacturers, retailers, workers and consumers in both countries. Any disruption, therefore, can have consequences extending well beyond negotiating tables and official statements.
With competing interests and persistent disagreements on trade, technology and security, Xi’s visit is expected to test whether high-level diplomacy can keep communication open and manage differences between the two economic powers.

title: Islamabad MoU opened path towards de escalation  settlement  President Zardari
description: Says there can be no durable peace where the right of peoples to self determination is denied
content:
Says there can be no durable peace where the right of peoples to self-determination is denied
President Asif Ali Zardari said the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding had opened a path towards de-escalation and a negotiated settlement of the conflict between Iran and the United States, as the world community observed the International Day of Peace on Monday.
In his message on the day, observed annually on September 21, Zardari said Pakistan remained engaged in efforts to sustain dialogue and achieve durable peace for the people of the region and the wider world. He said the subsequent high-level talks at Bürgenstock, Switzerland, had carried the diplomatic effort forward by focusing on implementation of the Islamabad MoU.
Message of the President of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan on the International Day of Peace (21 September 2026) The International Day of Peace reminds us that lasting peace can only be achieved through dialogue, diplomacy, justice and full respect for international law and… pic.twitter.com/a6E0K0FxsM
The president said lasting peace could only be achieved through dialogue, diplomacy, justice and full respect for international law and the purposes and principles of the UN Charter.
“Pakistan remains firmly committed to international peace and security and to a strong, effective and inclusive multilateral system with the UN at its core,” he said, reiterating that the country supported the peaceful settlement of disputes and a comprehensive approach to conflict prevention and resolution based on dialogue, diplomacy and collective action.
He highlighted that for decades, Pakistani peacekeepers had served in UN missions across the globe, helping protect civilians, support communities affected by conflict and create conditions in which peace could take root.
“Their service, often in difficult and dangerous circumstances, reflects Pakistan’s enduring commitment to international peace. We honour those who have given their lives in this cause and remain committed to supporting UN peacekeeping and peacebuilding efforts,” he added.
President Zardari said Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to end the conflict between Iran and the United States had been acknowledged internationally.
Read: Leaders stress dialogue for lasting peace
The president said the unanimous adoption of UN Security Council Resolution 2788, sponsored by Pakistan during its presidency of the Council last year, had been a significant reaffirmation of the Security Council’s commitment to strengthening mechanisms for the peaceful settlement of disputes.
He reaffirmed that Pakistan believed there could be no durable peace where the right of peoples to self-determination was denied, and Security Council resolutions remained unimplemented, including in situations of foreign occupation such as Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir and the Occupied Palestinian Territory.
The president said this year’s International Day of Peace theme, “Invest in Peace: For Everyone, Everywhere, Every Day”, reminded the world that peace required sustained efforts at every level.
On the Day of Peace, he called upon the international community to shoulder its responsibility by upholding the UN Charter, respecting international law and promoting just and durable resolutions of disputes through peaceful means.
“We call for continued support for de-escalation in West Asia and beyond. Pakistan stands ready as a trusted partner in this collective endeavour for a more peaceful and prosperous world,” President Zardari remarked.

title: PSG president Nasser al Khelaifi under investigation
description: French prosecutors examine his role in a TV rights deal
content:
French prosecutors examine his role in a TV rights deal
Nasser al-Khelaifi, the Qatari president of French football club Paris Saint-Germain (PSG), is under investigation in France on suspicion of an illegal conflict of interest, prosecutors in Paris said on Sunday.
The preliminary probe is linked to his twin stewardship of the Champions League title holders and the beIN Media Group and involves a meeting on broadcasting rights with the French football league's representatives in July 2024, the prosecutor's office said, confirming a report in L'Equipe sports newspaper.
The meeting was held the day after beIN Sports made a 100-million-euro ($115-million) offer for rights to broadcast one Ligue 1 match per week. France's professional football league later accepted the beIN offer.
The latest investigation into al-Khelaifi was launched in April after a tip-off from the anti-graft Anticor association, with proceedings entrusted to the anti-corruption and finance police.
According to a source close to the case, Anticor alleges that al-Khelaifi took part in discussions on the validation of beIN Sports' bid despite also serving as chairman of beIN Media Group, creating a conflict of interest.
Anticor also alleges that al-Khelaifi exerted pressure on other Ligue 1 club presidents to support the beIN Sports proposal, the source said.
Al-Khelaifi's lawyer, Renaud Semerdjian, rejected the claims.
"The allegations made against Mr Nasser al-Khelaifi are without basis, neither legally nor factually," he told AFP.
The lawyer said his client had "always acted in an independent, impartial and objective manner".
The PSG chief, who has led the French Ligue 1 champions since its 2011 takeover by Qatar Sports Investments with the dream of making the team Europe's best, has faced several legal cases in recent years.
In February 2025, he was charged with complicity in abuse of power concerning shareholder voting at a company.
Previous charges against Al-Khelaifi for alleged corruption over Qatar's bids for the 2017 and 2019 World Athletics Championships were definitively annulled in mid-February 2023 by France's Court of Cassation, which ruled the French justice system did not have the right to prosecute him.

title: US has deported 25 000 to third countries under secretive deals  report
description: Trump administration strikes agreements with 35 countries  with at least  410m earmarked to support deportation deals
content:
Trump administration strikes agreements with 35 countries, with at least $410m earmarked to support deportation deals
The United States has deported more than 25,000 people under secretive agreements with 35 countries to take migrants with no ties to those nations, according to an investigation published Monday.
Since US President Donald Trump took office in January 2025, Washington has been signing deals with developing countries to take migrants who cannot legally be sent home. The investigation by Forbidden Stories found the administration has earmarked $410 million to be paid directly to the receiving countries, or to United Nations agencies to facilitate the returns.
At least 25,447 people had already been deported to third countries by August 31, 2026, according to data compiled by Forbidden Stories with a consortium of international journalists. The vast majority – around 20,000 – were sent to Mexico, but the rest were dispersed to 27 other countries across Latin America, Africa, and the Pacific, and agreements have been finalised with seven more.
The deals vary, including over which nationalities can be deported and whether people with criminal records can be accepted.
An AFP investigation earlier this year found Washington is using visa bans and restrictions on African countries to strongarm them into accepting deportees. Lawyers told AFP that deportees were being thrown into a "legal black hole", held without charge in countries where they have no ties and few if any rights.
Read: Afghan woman deported from US in first use of secretive terrorism court
Forbidden Stories said 49 of Africa's 54 countries had been approached about accepting third-country deportees.
A little-known State Department division called the Office of Remigration, created in May 2025, has handled most of the negotiations and payments, according to Forbidden Stories . The office is headed by Christian Jove Ehrhardt, a 41-year-old diplomat who previously worked as a security officer.
The report details his visits to Cameroon, which signed a memorandum of understanding with the US in December on accepting deportees. A week later, it also signed a five-year health assistance programme worth nearly $400 million.
The following month, the State Department said it would provide a further $30 million to the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) in Cameroon to "facilitate the voluntary return of refugees and combat illegal immigration." The first plane carrying deportees arrived in Cameroon on January 14.
Read More: Far-right commentator Milo Yiannopoulos deported to UK
Other agreements have involved direct payments to governments.
Palau, a small Pacific island nation with a population of under 18,000, signed an agreement in December 2025 to accept up to 75 third-country nationals in return for $7.5 million. However, only three people have so far been sent under the agreement.
In Eswatini, 32 people have arrived since July 2025 out of a possible 160 under an agreement worth more than $5 million. It has accepted deportees with criminal records, the investigation found.
Of the $410 million planned for the agreements, internal State Department records showed that $81 million was earmarked for signatory governments. The rest was intended for aid organisations, including more than $178 million for the UN's International Organisation for Migration, and $123 million for UNHCR.
The agencies have faced criticism over their involvement, although UNHCR told Forbidden Stories that it was not party to the bilateral agreements and that US funding was being used in line with its mandate to strengthen asylum systems.
An IOM spokesperson told Forbidden Stories that the agency's decisions to accept funding rested "on a single question: whether our engagement will improve the lives of the migrants affected. In these instances, we believe strongly it does."

title: Falcons clinch maiden CPL title
description: Sufyan Moqim   s four wicket haul and an unbeaten 89 run stand guide the Falcons to an eight wicket final victory
content:
Sufyan Moqim’s four-wicket haul and an unbeaten 89-run stand guide the Falcons to an eight-wicket final victory
Antigua and Barbuda Falcons claimed their maiden Caribbean Premier League title in just their third season after beating tournament debutants Jamaica Kingsmen by eight wickets in Sunday’s final in Bridgetown.
Sufyan Moqim took 4-14 to restrict the Kingsmen to 170-9 despite a sensational 114 from Maaz Sadaqat, before Amir Jangoo and Hasan Nawaz completed a comfortable chase with 20 balls to spare.
Sadaqat’s 58-ball assault featured nine sixes and eight fours, accounting for more than half of the Kingsmen’s total. Saim Ayub’s 29 was the only other significant contribution, with three of the top six dismissed for ducks.
The Kingsmen appeared set for a much bigger total after losing Kirk McKenzie for a four-ball duck in the opening over and Keacy Carty for nine in the fourth.
Sadaqat and Ayub then put on 80 for the third wicket, taking the Kingsmen from 30-2 to 110-2 as the scoring rate hovered around 10 an over.
But Moqim turned the innings on its head in the 12th over, removing Ayub and Rovman Powell in quick succession. The Kingsmen collapsed from 110-2 to 113-6 over three overs.
Sadaqat continued attacking until he fell off the penultimate ball, but the damage was done as the Kingsmen finished on 170-9.
The Falcons made light work of the target from the outset. Rahkeem Cornwall smashed two fours and two sixes in a 20-run opening over from Ayub before being bowled by the final delivery.
Evin Lewis and Jangoo then added 64 for the second wicket to put the chase firmly in control. Lewis departed for 38 with the Falcons already close to halfway to their target and more than 12 overs remaining.
Jangoo and Nawaz finished the job in style, combining for an unbeaten 89-run partnership featuring seven fours and six sixes.
Jangoo ended on 57 not out and Nawaz 47 not out, with the result beyond doubt with four overs remaining. Nawaz then sealed the title with two sixes in the 17th over.
Falcons allrounder Shadab Khan was named tournament MVP after scoring 132 runs and taking 11 wickets.

title: Bodies of two missing FC personnel recovered in Bannu
description: The deceased personnel were identified as Havaldar Ishaq and Sepoy Umar Hayat  both belonging to Platoon No 59
content:
The deceased personnel were identified as Havaldar Ishaq and Sepoy Umar Hayat, both belonging to Platoon No 59
The bodies of two Frontier Constabulary (FC) personnel who went missing from the Saifan Kozi Khel area of Kuram Garhi in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) on Sunday evening were recovered from the Kamali graveyard in Palosi, Rescue 1122 spokesperson Nahid Khan said on Monday.
The deceased personnel were identified as Havaldar Ishaq and Sepoy Umar Hayat, both belonging to Platoon No 59.
Police confirmed that the two FC personnel, identified as Havaldar Ishaq and Sepoy Umar Hayat, had gone missing from Saifan Kozi Khel within the jurisdiction of Cantt police station, and that an investigation into the incident was initiated.
Later, the bodies of the two personnel were recovered from the Komali graveyard in Palosi. Rescue 1122 teams shifted the bodies for identification and completion of legal formalities, the spokesperson said.
Following the incident, security was tightened in the area, while a search for the unidentified assailants involved in the abduction and killing of the two personnel was launched.
According to sources, the two FC personnel were allegedly taken away by unidentified armed men from Saifan Kozi Khel in the Karam Garhi area on Sunday evening, following which a search operation was launched for them.

The security situation in Bannu has remained under considerable pressure in recent weeks, with police, FC and other security personnel coming under attack in different parts of the district.
Earlier this month, an Elite Force constable, Ahmadullah, was killed in a firing incident within the jurisdiction of Cantt police station. In another incident in the Paing area of Domel, a civilian was killed during an exchange of fire between members of a peace committee and armed men.
Similarly, a recent alleged quadcopter attack in the Hathi Khel area of Wazir subdivision left a woman and another civilian dead and two others injured. Police and security personnel, including the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD), Elite Force and members of a local peace committee, subsequently conducted an operation in the area. Police claimed that a suspected militant was also killed during the operation.
Meanwhile, authorities have also been considering additional security arrangements for the protection of vital installations in Bannu and Lakki Marwat. The provincial government had recently sought additional FC platoons for the protection of important installations in the two districts.
The latest incident once again highlighted security challenges in rural and sensitive areas of Bannu, particularly the movement and protection of security personnel and the need for effective measures to counter militant activity.

title: Bessent proposes US China AI safety notifications in talks with Chinese vice premier
description: Talks lay groundwork for Trump Xi summit this week as Beijing s response to proposal remains unclear
content:
Talks lay groundwork for Trump-Xi summit this week as Beijing's response to proposal remains unclear
United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng concluded talks in New York on Sunday with the US side proposing a new AI safety notification mechanism for US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to consider at their summit this week.
Bessent told reporters that the two sides discussed setting up a new US-China AI dialogue, with a particular emphasis on national security concerns with a notification system for common goals and common threats that would cover AI-related incidents that rise to a national security level.
"We think that, just like with any cross-border activity, that moving from opaque to more transparency between the number one and the number two AI powers in the world is very important," Bessent said at the conclusion of the talks.
Trump and Xi first discussed potential consultations on AI development in May in Beijing , but that forum was never formalised.
The Chinese response to the US proposal was unclear with a state news agency Xinhua readout only briefly acknowledging that both sides spoke about AI. Xinhua characterised the officials as having had "frank, in-depth and constructive exchanges on key economic and trade issues", including implementing agreements reached in earlier rounds of trade and investment consultations.
"Obviously, one or two meetings cannot resolve every issue, but the fact that both sides agreed to continue the dialogue is significant," said George Chen, partner and chair in Digital Practice at The Asia Group consultancy in Hong Kong. "The US–China AI talks will move forward, with future sessions expected to tackle more sensitive topics such as the weaponisation of AI, principles for AI safety, protection of critical infrastructure, and cyber‑attack prevention."
Read: Trump says he will appoint a new AI adviser, without providing details
Chen added that prospects for cooperation on AI remain limited due to the low level of trust between both countries, and Beijing's perception that Washington seeks to contain China's AI development.
Vice Premier He and China's chief trade negotiator Li Chenggang left the talks at JPMorgan Chase headquarters in New York without speaking to media.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said US export controls on sophisticated AI chips and semiconductor manufacturing equipment were not on the agenda for the AI mechanism talks.
Greer added that Sunday's discussions would prepare the groundwork for a "successful summit" between Trump and Xi next Thursday and Friday in Washington. "These are the two most powerful countries on earth, whether it's in trade or AI, and it's imperative that they're able to work together. It doesn't mean there aren't challenges in the relationship. A lot of these are obvious," Greer said.
Read More: Founder of Chinese startup Spirit AI says robot brains set for 2027 breakthrough
The meeting covered other key topics, including plans to "operationalise" a process agreed in May for each side to identify potential tariff cuts on non-strategic goods, called the "Board of Trade."
Greer did not identify a specific list of products that could see such reductions, but he repeated his desire for a "relatively small subset of American and Chinese goods that can be traded in a balanced way, that are non-sensitive." These would be considered as "a class unto themselves."
Potential candidates among Chinese exports include "consumer goods, low-tech items," he said, while US exports for this treatment could include energy, agricultural goods and medical devices, he added.
Greer and Bessent did not mention any progress on improving the flow of critical minerals to US companies, which US officials have said are insufficient despite Beijing's prior commitments to ease restrictions under last year's US-China trade truce .
The discussions point to more incremental progress in avoiding an escalation of tensions in a delicate trade relationship that has major consequences for the global economy.
Bessent and Greer did not provide updates on other issues that are unresolved after the May meeting in Beijing between Trump and Xi, including Chinese pledges to increase purchases of US agricultural goods by $17 billion a year and to purchase more than 200 Boeing aircraft.
Trump and Xi must reach a deal that covers AI safety, said US Representative Ro Khanna, the ranking Democrat on the US House Select Committee on Strategic Competition Between the US and the Chinese Communist Party.
Also Read: China, US find new trade ties in services
"The first ask is of Trump and Xi Jinping to come up with an international agreement, and two of the core principles should be one banning any self-improving AI, recursive self-improving AI.…The second is to have safeguards so that AI can't be misused by people for biological nuclear weapons," Khanna said on Sunday, speaking on CBS ' Face the Nation program.
China's Ministry of Commerce said on Saturday that He would also lead a delegation of Chinese companies to the US that would participate in economic and trade consultations ahead of the summit.
The business delegation, which mirrors a group of US CEOs that Trump brought to Beijing in May, was announced as Trump expressed openness to Chinese automakers building US factories.
US auto industry groups on Friday urged Trump to maintain an effective ban on Chinese vehicle sales in the US on national security grounds.

title: Atletico Madrid beat Real Madrid in tense derby clash
description: Grimaldo and David strike after the break to hand Atletico a 2 1 derby win
content:
Grimaldo and David strike after the break to hand Atletico a 2-1 derby win
Atletico Madrid edged 10-man Real Madrid 2-1 in a La Liga derby clash on Sunday to leave Jose Mourinho's side trailing leaders Barcelona by six points.
Dean Huijsen was sent off early in the second half for Los Blancos before Alejandro Grimaldo and Jonathan David's goals earned Diego Simeone's Atletico victory, with Antonio Rudiger pulling one back late on.
Atletico rose to second, five points behind Barca and one ahead of Real Madrid, who chalked up a second defeat of the campaign.
The game hinged on Huijsen's red card early in the second period, for pulling down Giuliano Simeone in the box which led to a penalty, tucked away by Grimaldo to set Atletico on their way.
Mourinho started with Aurelien Tchouameni in midfield over Bernardo Silva, opting for defensive clout over creativity.
There was more tension than footballing quality in the first half, with neither side capable of creating any clear chances.
The main talking point was an incident between Jude Bellingham and Atletico defender Cristian Romero.
The England international threw himself into a tackle and Romero trod on his leg, with Bellingham booked initially, but after a VAR review the referee removed the card and issued it to the Atletico man.
Madrid were also unhappy with a heavy tackle by Lee Kang-in on Federico Valverde which went unpunished just before half-time.
It was a scrappy battle, intense but lacking excitement comparative to the star power on the pitch, especially in Madrid's front line, with Vinicius Junior, Kylian Mbappe and Bellingham kept quiet.
The game burst into life early in the second half when Huijsen pulled back Giuliano Simeone's arm as the forward ran through on goal and Atletico were awarded a penalty.
Huijsen was dismissed after a VAR review and Grimaldo beat Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois from the penalty spot.
Mourinho reacted immediately by replacing the underwhelming Vinicius and Arda Guler and sending on club record signing Yan Diomande and Rudiger.
It was Atletico who struck next, though, with Canada international David tucking away Giuliano Simeone's raking low cross on 59 minutes for his third goal in three matches.
The hosts came close to getting a third but Courtois made an excellent save to deny Julian Alvarez and Ibrahima Konate reacted brilliantly to head Grimaldo's effort from the rebound off the line.
Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak saved from Diomande and Bellingham rowed with Giuliano Simeone as Madrid's frustrations showed, impotent to change the course of the game.
Madrid pulled a goal back in the final stages with Rudiger heading Bernardo Silva's cross past Oblak. However, it was too little too late for Mourinho's side.

title: Man City outgun Sunderland despite Brobbey hat trick
description: Haaland seals a 5 3 victory
content:
Manchester City went top of the Premier League despite Brian Brobbey's hat-trick in a 5-3 thriller on Sunday as Matheus Cunha rescued Manchester United from another damaging defeat at Fulham.
City took advantage of Arsenal's shock 3-0 defeat at Brighton on Saturday but made life hard for themselves despite taking the lead three times at the Etihad Stadium.
Enzo Fernandez opened the scoring with his first goal since equalling the Premier League transfer record with a £125 million ($167 million) move from Chelsea.
The Argentine midfielder's free-kick caught out Robin Roefs at his near post.
Sunderland won their first European match for 53 years against AZ Alkmaar in midweek but showed little sign of tiredness as City could not shake off the Black Cats.
Brobbey slotted home Enzo Le Fee's pass for the first of his treble.
Quick feet and a slick finish from Rayan Cherki restored City's advantage, but Brobbey again replied within four minutes at the end of a fine Sunderland move.
Antoine Semenyo smashed City back in front before half-time and thought he had settled the game with another accurate left-footed finish just before the hour mark.
Brobbey completed his hat-trick after Nilson Angulo beat Gianluigi Donnarumma to a ball over the top.
A couple of nervy moments from the Italian goalkeeper nearly led to a Sunderland equaliser as Ruben Dias was forced to clear off his own line.
However, Erling Haaland finally got involved in the goalfest to seal the three points and ensured he has scored against every side he has faced in the Premier League.
Victory extends Enzo Maresca's perfect start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola at City boss.
"To be honest, I prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3 but I expected a very difficult game," said Maresca.
United head into a three-week international break just two points outside the relegation zone as they failed to ease the pressure on manager Michael Carrick in a 1-1 draw.
But it could have been even worse for the Red Devils after a calamitous Lisandro Martinez own goal put Fulham on course for their first league win of the season.
Senne Lammens parried Calvin Bassey's strike back into the danger area and then could not clear when Martinez inadvertently turned the ball towards his own goal.
Cunha's 89th minute equaliser also took a wicked deflection off David Affengruber to save United's blushes.
The Red Devils have taken just five points from their opening five games and were dumped out of the League Cup by Brighton in midweek after surrendering a 2-0 lead at home for the first time in 50 years.
"We came to get the win of course, the way it panned out and the way we finished is the positive we take from it," said Carrick.
"We don't think things are perfect by any means. We need to win football matches."
A point is enough to edge Fulham off the foot of the table as Tottenham drop to the bottom.
Liverpool won 1-0 on Andoni Iraola's return to Bournemouth thanks to Alexander Isak's winner.

title: Cindy Crawford s shared emotional message to son  Presley Gerber  before his death at 27
description: Cindy Crawford   s messages to son Presley Gerber reflected her support for him  2 months before his death
content:
Cindy Crawford’s messages to son Presley Gerber reflected her support for him, 2 months before his death
Cindy Crawford shared a message of support for her son Presley Gerber two months before his death at the age of 27, recalling the bond between them as he publicly discussed his struggles and recovery.
In July, Crawford marked Presley’s 27th birthday by sharing two childhood photographs of her eldest child on Instagram.
Alongside the images, the model wrote, “I'm so proud of the man you've become, but I'll always see you as my little boy! Love you.”
Presley died on September 20 at a rehabilitation facility, according to Los Angeles County Medical Examiner records. His cause of death has not been determined, as an autopsy had not yet been completed.
A family representative said, “The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time.”
Crawford had also publicly supported Presley as he spoke about his experiences with addiction and recovery. In March, Presley shared an Instagram video about undergoing treatment, prompting a message from his mother.
“You are a warrior! Walked thru the fire to find yourself! So proud!” Crawford wrote in the comments.
Presley’s father, Rande Gerber, also responded to the post, writing, “I'm so proud of you and your courage. Facing what's hard takes real strength, and watching you find your way back to yourself is everything. I love you so much.”
Presley had previously spoken publicly about his mental health and substance use. In one Instagram video, he said, “Unfortunately, I've had a lot of loss in many different forms recently, so that is not an excuse, but it's the reason why I am where I'm at now.”
His sister, Kaia Gerber, also discussed his struggles in an interview with Vogue published in August.
“When something like that happens in a family, it kind of levels everyone,” Kaia said. “I think that's also why I started to self-identify as the easy one and never wanted to ask for help. Because it felt like too much to have two children who were needing.”

title: Denmark says NATO shares responsibility for Arctic security under Greenland deal
description: Trump claims pact grants US  permanent control  over security in Greenland as key details not yet public
content:
Trump claims pact grants US 'permanent control' over security in Greenland as key details not yet public
Denmark, Greenland and the United States are set to sign a deal on Greenland 's security on Tuesday, an agreement Denmark says will put Arctic security under NATO's watch rather than leaving it solely to Washington and Copenhagen.
The agreement, expected to be signed at the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Tuesday, has not been made public, though President Donald Trump says it grants the United States "permanent control". Denmark and Greenland have not commented on Trump's claim but said the deal will benefit the Arctic island and respect its sovereignity .
The deal follows months of pressure from Trump, who has said the US should control Greenland and at times refused to rule out using military or economic force to acquire the semi-autonomous Danish territory.
Read: EU chief in Greenland to boost Arctic ties
His threats, which peaked in January, triggered a diplomatic crisis within NATO and pushed Denmark and Greenland into negotiations with Washington aimed at defusing the pressure.
"It (the agreement) will be in a form where responsibility for security in the Arctic is not only Danish or American," Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen told national broadcaster TV2 on Sunday. He added that to a large extent "it would be NATO that looks after the Arctic".
Promoting 'security, stability and cooperation'
A NATO spokesperson said on Saturday that the alliance welcomed the agreement, which would "help advance security, stability and cooperation in this vital region".
Rasmussen, who travelled to New York overnight, declined to discuss the contents of the agreement. "But we have said from the start that we are open to accommodating the United States' legitimate security interests," Rasmussen told Danish news agency Ritzau on Monday.
Trump said in a post on Truth Social on Friday the agreement gives the US "permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland," and that no US adversary could have a base or military presence there without Washington's written approval.
Denmark has not responded to Trump's claim, though Copenhagen has earlier acknowledged it underinvested in Greenland's defence for decades and has pledged to expand its military presence on the island, including more NATO troops .
Key details have not been made public, including whether the deal amends the 1951 defence agreement that is the legal basis for the US presence in Greenland.
Greenland's government has sought to reassure the public about the deal.
Erik Jensen, an opposition lawmaker in Greenland, wrote on Facebook that he had read the draft agreement: "I feel reassured and am not worried," he said, adding that the island's foreign minister was handling the work well.
