title: Milan and Juventus end blips with home wins
description: Napoli held 1 1 by Fiorentina as Como suffer 2 0 shock defeat
content:
Napoli held 1-1 by Fiorentina as Como suffer 2-0 shock defeat
AC Milan and Juventus ended short Serie A slides on Sunday, as Fiorentina held Napoli and high-flying Como suffered a shock defeat to Frosinone.
Milan beat Lecce 3-0 at the San Siro to rise to fifth, two points behind early pace-setters Roma, Inter and Lazio.
Juventus returned to form with a 2-0 home win over Atalanta as Francisco Conceicao and Gleison Bremer struck either side of half-time.
The comfortable victory relieved pressure on Milan head coach Ruben Amorim after a three-match winless run in all competitions had stalled his side's early progress.
"We still have a lot to do, but we are playing better and improving. The most important thing, though, is that we are learning," Amorim told DAZN.
"In the last few games, we had some trouble because our positional structure was too rigid, whereas today the players had a bit more freedom and played better."
Christian Pulisic marked his first start of the season with his first Milan goal of 2026, making the breakthrough in the 14th minute with an exquisite finish.
He plucked a long pass out of the air with a deft first touch before finishing calmly.
Adrien Rabiot scored at the end of a flowing move after the break, before substitute Diego Moreira struck with his third goal in two league games.
Juventus had picked up one point in their previous two league games but went in front in the 28th minute in Turin when Conceicao scored his first goal of the season with a low shot.
Chances fell at both ends in the second half as both goalkeepers were called into action and Juve striker Randal Kolo Muani made a goal-line clearance.
Bremer sealed the three points by guiding home a header from a corner with 13 minutes remaining as Juventus moved up to seventh and inflicted a third straight defeat on their former coach Maurizio Sarri.
Atalanta, who hired ex-Lazio, Chelsea and Napoli coach Sarri in the summer, sit 11th.
Earlier, Fiorentina maintained their unbeaten run under coach Paolo Vanoli with a 1-1 draw against Napoli.
Vanoli, who led the Florence club to safety in the second half of last season before being let go, returned as head coach when Fabio Grosso was sacked after losing the first three games of the new campaign.
La Viola showed improvement under Vanoli by beating Venezia in Serie A and Pisa in the Coppa Italia in his first two games, and the upturn in form continued as they fought back to claim a draw which kept them two points above the relegation zone.
Billy Gilmour put Napoli in front with a cushioned volley after Fiorentina hit the woodwork twice early on, but the home side drew level through a deflected Alex Jimenez strike in the second half.
"If we are not angry today, after failing to win against a good team like Fiorentina, it certainly means we need to improve," Allegri told DAZN. "It is not enough to keep possession if you do not take your chances."
Como had the chance to move joint-top when they travelled to newly-promoted Frosinone, but Cesc Fabregas's side suffered their first loss of the season as a 2-0 reverse ended their four-match winning run in all competitions.
First-half goals from Giacomo Calo and Giorgi Kvernadze, and a heroic goalkeeping display by Italy Under-21 international Lorenzo Palmisani, sealed a famous win for the hosts.
"Today was our first poor game in five months, the last being in the semi-final of the Coppa Italia against Inter (in April). It was a Frosinone masterpiece today," Fabregas said.
The win extended Frosinone's three-match unbeaten run and took them up to sixth.
Parma beat Genoa 2-1 to claim their first victory of the season and leave Daniele De Rossi's side winless after five games.

content:
Pakistan’s fighter submits Angola’s Leonela Isabel Blaiye in the second round at the IMMAF World Cup in Luanda
Pakistan’s Manesha Ali secured gold at the IMMAF World Cup in Luanda after submitting Angola’s Leonela Isabel Blaiye in the second round, the Pakistan MMA Federation said on Sunday.
With 30 seconds remaining in the round, Blaiye moved forward throwing a flurry of punches as fatigue set in. Ali, who trains at Brave Gym Lahore, caught her opponent in a standing guillotine and held the submission until the referee stopped the bout with 15 seconds left.
Manesha celebrated by roaring before dropping to her knees, while her sister Maleeha cheered from the crowd. The victory brought an emotional response from the fighter as her hand was raised.
The tournament brought together 15 top-ranked teams and some of the leading amateur mixed martial arts talent from around the world.
Manesha, who is from Gilgit-Baltistan, now turns her attention to the Pakistan Open before the IMMAF World Championships in Georgia, which begin on Nov. 1.
“I believe completely in my training and in the mentorship of Omar Ahmed,” Ali said in a statement released by the Pakistan MMA Federation. “In less than a year, I have developed enormously as a fighter, but this is only one step.”
Her stated goal is to win the IMMAF world title and become the first Pakistani female fighter to compete in the UFC.
Pakistan MMA Federation chief Omar Ahmed said Ali’s success offered a reward for the work involved in developing the sport in Pakistan.
“Running a sports federation in Pakistan is extremely tough,” Ahmed said, citing policy challenges and administrative hurdles. “But when you see one of our kids standing on top of an international podium, the Pakistan flag going up and the national anthem playing, everything becomes worth it.”
Manesha’s next major test will come at the world championships in Georgia, where she will seek to turn her World Cup success into a bid for a global amateur MMA title.

title: Fleming backs Stokes retirement decision
description: The 53 year old coach says he respects the all rounder   s choice and has no intention of questioning it
content:
The 53-year-old coach says he respects the all-rounder’s choice and has no intention of questioning it
Newly-appointed England Test coach Stephen Fleming says it would be "wrong" to ask former captain Ben Stokes to reverse his international retirement before next year's Ashes.
Stokes dramatically announced the end of his England career -- and four-year spell as Test skipper -- during a defeat by New Zealand at Trent Bridge in June that condemned his team to a 2-1 series loss.
The 35-year-old has continued playing for his county side Durham and has also signed up for a stint with the Adelaide Strikers in Australia's Big Bash League.
But Fleming, who met with Stokes soon after arriving in England, played down the prospect of a fairytale return.
"I went up to Durham and spoke to Ben, which was good. He's really happy and seemed to be really at peace with his decision," Fleming, who previously worked with Stokes at Chennai Super Kings in the Indian Premier League, told reporters.
"I've worked with Ben quite a bit. We've got a really good relationship... He seems really happy and comfortable with what he's doing."
Fleming, speaking later to the BBC, insisted he would not ask Stokes to perform a U-turn.
"I respect his decision too much," he said. "To try to turn that around and question that is wrong."
Former New Zealand captain Fleming was appointed in July but has only just taken charge after missing England's recent 3-0 whitewash of Pakistan due to family commitments.
On Saturday, Fleming witnessed England complete a T20 series rout of Sri Lanka in Manchester.
While at Old Trafford, he spoke with predecessor and fellow ex-New Zealand skipper Brendon McCullum, still in charge of England's white-ball teams despite being sacked as Test boss.
Fleming said his ambition was to take England from sixth in the rankings back to the summit for the first time since 2012 and improve their woeful record in the World Test Championship.
"I would love to be in charge of the number one Test team in the world," said Fleming. "There have been some really good moments (for this side) but I think there's more to give."
England have never come close to reaching any of the three finals in the history of the WTC and are unlikely to qualify for next year's showpiece match at the Oval.
"England could do much better than that," added Fleming.
"If that's one of the pinnacle trophies in world cricket, why would we not be trying to get it along with every other marquee event that comes our way?"
Fleming's relationship with McCullum is hoped to be key to the success of England's latest split-coaching regime, with the duo not only former team-mates but close friends and business partners.
"It's nice to be in a position to work with him, it's been a while," said Fleming, at 53 nine years older than McCullum.
"It is an advantage that we will be able to talk fairly openly and be robust... we don't have to spend time getting to know each other as coaches."

content:
Dreyer scores twice as the visitors earn a 2-2 draw in Florida
Lionel Messi and Inter Miami's hopes of overtaking Nashville at the top of Major League Soccer's Eastern Conference suffered a blow on Sunday after the champions were held to a 2-2 draw by San Diego in Florida.
Two goals from Danish forward Anders Dreyer secured a share of the points for San Diego at Miami's Nu Stadium –- a result which left Miami 11 points adrift of Nashville with eight regular season games remaining.
Denmark international Dreyer fired San Diego into a shock lead after 12 minutes, latching on to a superb through ball from compatriot Jeppe Tverskov before lifting a delicate chip over Miami goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair.
But Miami, who dominated territory and possession for long periods thereafter, were back on level terms in the 24th minute when Messi curled in his 101st goal for Miami.
Messi's wicked curling free-kick from the edge of the area somehow threaded its way through a crowded six-yard box and clipped the inside of the post before ending in the net.
From there Miami laid siege to the San Diego goal and it seemed only a matter of time before they took the lead.
Messi, Luis Suarez, and Rodrigo De Paul all had good chances but somehow San Diego managed to hold on.
The deadlock was broken in the 74th minute when De Paul released Suarez with a clever pass on the edge of the area and the 39-year-old Uruguayan veteran lashed home the finish for 2-1.
That looked like it would be enough as the game entered the final 10 minutes, but San Diego stunned the home crowd with a goal that echoed their first.
Tverskov once again found Dreyer with a pinpoint pass over the top and the Dane finished coolly to make it 2-2.
A frenetic finish saw San Diego almost snatch victory deep into stoppage time, but St. Clair blocked Kieran Sargeant's late effort on the counter.

Oil prices slid to their ​lowest in more than a week on Monday as investors hoped for diplomatic progress on the Iran war due to this ‌week's UN meeting and eyed a partial recovery in shipments from Saudi Arabia despite ongoing attacks by Yemen's Houthis.
Brent crude futures and US West Texas Intermediate crude touched their lowest since September 10 earlier on Monday. The Brent contract for November was at $102.09 a barrel at 0655 GMT, down $1.78, or 1.71%, ​after settling 0.91% lower on Friday.

"It seems that a degree of risk premium is ⁠being removed from oil prices on hopes that a diplomatic path to de-escalate the US-Iran war may arrive this week," said Tim ​Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.
"Whether that hope proves to be warranted or not is another question. Time will tell."

Iran has conveyed its conditions to mediators ​for re-engaging in negotiations aimed at ending the war with the US , Al Jazeera cited Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, as saying in an interview ‌on Saturday.

title: Durefishan Saleem addresses debate over Zaryab s journey in  Dar e Nijaat
description: Actor says drama explores redemption and double standards surrounding how men and women are expected to heal  move on
content:
Actor says drama explores redemption and double standards surrounding how men and women are expected to heal, move on
As Dar-e-Nijaat continues to spark debate online, lead actor Durefishan Saleem has responded to questions surrounding the drama’s central story — particularly why her character, Zaryab, appears to need Abu Bakr’s help to recover from heartbreak.
The conversation gathered pace after the latest episode, in which Zaryab, a woman once willing to give up her admission to Harvard University to comfort Zamil (Nameer Khan), discovers that her long-time partner and childhood sweetheart has married somebody else without telling her.
When Zaryab confronts him, Zamil dismisses their years together as his “era of ignorance”. He says he needs a “pious, pure and innocent” partner and believes God accepted his repentance by giving him his new wife. He tells Zaryab to find someone “like herself”. When she asks whether only a man has the right to repent, he dodges the question.
The fallout soon catches up with Zaryab. She suffers an emotional breakdown, with Abu Bakr (Sheheryar Munawar) arriving to help her up and steady her.
As Zaryab’s story progressed, some viewers questioned whether the drama was suggesting that a woman needs another man to recover from a toxic relationship. Durefishan appeared to address the debate on her Instagram Stories, urging women to heal and find themselves again. “The right person always comes along, and even if they don't, it is never the end of the world,” she wrote. Sometimes, she added, “finding yourself is the love story you needed all along.”
Durefishan went on to say that she believes in women finding themselves, knowing their worth and never feeling that they need a man to complete them. At the same time, she cautioned against assuming that “our version of what is right is the only right”.
In her view, the story is “less about telling women that they can't, or shouldn't, heal on their own” and more about “questioning the double standard around redemption”.
She pointed to how easily a man can make mistakes, seek redemption and be given another chance, while women are often expected to carry the weight of their choices for much longer.
She also encouraged viewers to approach the drama as a story about something that “happened to someone”, arguing that one does not have to agree with every choice a character makes to understand their emotions or empathise with their journey.
“Human beings are complicated,” she said. “Stories should be allowed to explore that complexity without fitting neatly into a morally correct box.”
The discussion around Durefishan’s performance has also extended to the comments section of her post about the drama, where fellow actors Hira Mani, Zara Noor Abbas and Meerub Ali praised her acting. Influencers Momina Munir and Ayla Nusrat Raza also shared their appreciation for the actor’s performance.
Viewers, too, were emotional about Zaryab’s latest turn in the story. One fan said she “cried with Zaryab the whole time”, adding, “May no one ever have to go through this kind of pain.” Another praised Durefishan, saying she “doesn't just portray a character; she breathes life into her”, making “every silence speak”.
Another viewer said she was “literally crying” during the latest episode and defended the actor against those who question her acting: “She absolutely nailed it!” Others said her expressions “have a language of their own”.
Much of the audience’s frustration, meanwhile, was directed at Zamil. One viewer called him a red flag “from the start”, while another jokingly appointed themselves “Zamil hate club president”. Another said the drama reflects “what our society actually thinks”.
Earlier , actor Nameer Khan, who plays Zamil, used his character’s troubled arc to highlight the importance of men treating women with respect and taking responsibility for their actions. Following the latest episode, Khan took to Instagram to reflect on where Zamil went wrong and draw attention to behaviour he said he had witnessed in real life. “Zamil is Zalim” he wrote, adding a red flag emoji.
Khan explained that beyond the story being told through the drama, he wanted to address the behaviour of some men towards women.“Growing up, I have seen boys objectifying girls, getting into relationships, playing with their feelings and then feeling proud about it, while their friends cheer them on,” Khan said.
His comments came after the latest episode, in which Durefishan’s character, Zaryab, was betrayed by her longtime fiancé.
Reflecting on the storyline, Khan shared a direct message for men. “My message to all the boys: stop this nonsense! Your desire to be known as a hero or playboy can become someone else’s trauma. Hurting a girl and breaking her trust is nothing to be proud of,” he wrote.
He concluded his message with three simple reminders: “Be respectful. Be honest. Be a better man.”
With the debate now extending beyond the characters themselves, Durefishan’s comments offer her perspective on what the story is attempting to explore: not simply whether Zaryab needs someone to help her heal, but how redemption, choice and expectations are viewed differently for men and women.

content:
Inglis’ ton and Ellis’ unbeaten 36 snatch a thrilling one-wicket win over Zimbabwe
HARARE: Josh ​Inglis ​scored his second One-Day International century and Nathan Ellis his highest score in the format with an unbeaten 36 from 44 balls as Australia claimed a dramatic one-wicket victory over hosts Zimbabwe with a ball to ‌spare in Harare on Sunday. When Ellis was joined at the crease by number 11 Spencer Johnson (7 from 13 balls), the tourists needed 27 runs to ‌reach their victory target of ⁠272, something ​the pair managed at a run-a-ball to take their side ​to the win.
imbabwe will rue Wessly ‌Madhevere dropping Ellis in the penultimate ​over when he could have sealed victory for them, as he then failed to defend nine runs in the final over when Ellis hit a six off the first ball. Australia, ⁠who rested several of their regulars for the tour, claimed the series 3-0 and ‌now move on to South Africa for three ODI fixtures that begin in Durban on Thursday.
"Great game of cricket," Australia captain Mitchell Marsh said. "I thought Zimbabwe probably deserved to win but the boys got the ⁠job done at the end there and that was fantastic ⁠to see. "We're aware we ​need to keep ‌improving as a team. I thought the way we played over the three matches, albeit today we got lucky, but there's lots of positive signs with our group. We've got some young talent which is exciting for the future.
" After the home side elected to bat first, Zimbabwe’s innings was anchored by an unbeaten 81 from 72 balls by captain Sikandar Raza, to go with half-centuries for Craig ⁠Ervine (59 from 79 balls) and Innocent Kaia (55 from 66 balls). Kaia retired hurt with a hamstring injury, with the score ⁠on 148 for three, as he could no longer run between the wickets. Seamer Ellis was also the pick of the Australian bowlers with 3-50 in his 10 overs.
Australia were always up with the run rate in their reply but when openers Travis Head (6) and Marsh (8) fell early, it set the tone for an innings where they lost wickets at regular intervals. But Inglis scored a superb 103 from 102 balls as he struck 11 fours, ⁠with the next highest scorer Ellis on his unbeaten 36. Zimbabwe ​all-rounder Brad Evans was the pick of the home bowlers with 4-47 in 10 overs.
"I thought 280-290 was par with the bat so to make a game out of 272 was a great effort," Raza said. "As a captain I'm really proud. Plenty to learn. ​I'd rather have a game like that than for the ‌Aussies to just chase it down in 40 overs."

title: Asim settles for a bronze after semi final defeat at Asian Games
description: Tajikistan   s Mirzobek Umarov beats Pakistan   s lone MMA fighter 3 0 in Aichi Nagoya
content:
Tajikistan’s Mirzobek Umarov beats Pakistan’s lone MMA fighter 3-0 in Aichi-Nagoya
Pakistan’s Asim Khan secured a historic bronze medal at the Asian Games on Monday after losing 3-0 to Tajikistan’s Mirzobek Umarov in the men’s Modern Mixed Martial Arts (MMA) -60kg semi-final. Asim, Pakistan’s lone MMA representative at the Aichi-Nagoya Games, was unable to match Umarov’s level in the last-four contest, bringing his bid for a place in the gold-medal bout to an end. Despite the defeat, the result marked a landmark moment for Pakistani combat sports, with Asim becoming the country’s first MMA athlete to win a medal at the Asian Games. The 2026 edition is also the first Asian Games in which MMA has been contested. Asim had entered the semi-final with confidence after producing a commanding performance against Cambodia’s Sopanha Pheng in the quarter-finals on Sunday. He defeated Pheng 3-0 to reach the last four and, with only ten fighters entered in the Modern -60kg category, guaranteed Pakistan at least a bronze medal. But against Umarov, Khan found the challenge significantly tougher. The Tajik fighter controlled the contest sufficiently to earn a unanimous 3-0 decision, ending Pakistan’s hopes of advancing to the final. Asim’s coach Dilawar Khan said the experience of competing against professional-level opponents had presented an additional challenge for the Pakistani fighter. “For the first time in the Asian Games pros had been allowed and you know they have other level. Their training and diet are different,” Dilawar told The Express Tribune. “Still we are happy to compete with them. We won a bronze on our debut as this is the first time that a Pakistani fighter took part in the Asian Games.” Pakistan is competing across 23 sports disciplines at the Games.

title: Naqvi warns PTI against Islamabad march  says governor s rule among options for K P amid security concerns
description: Says the situation in K P over past 10 days is in front of everyone  none of the PTI leadership came to the funerals
content:
Says the situation in K-P over past 10 days is in front of everyone; none of the PTI leadership came to the funerals
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday warned the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) against pressing ahead with its planned September 27 march on Islamabad, saying the government was consulting the Law Ministry on legal options for Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), including imposing Governor’s Rule, amid the security situation.
“See, we have already told them that whatever legal option we have, we will consult the Law Ministry and the prime minister will decide. But it won’t happen that they (PTI) come (to Islamabad) and shut down the country for 10 days. That will never happen, I can assure you,” Naqvi said at a press conference in Lahore when asked whether Governor’s Rule was being considered in K-P.
Naqvi's statement followed a series of attacks in the K-P over the past week. Six Pakistan Army personnel were killed on Sunday in an exchange of fire with terrorists in Hangu. A day earlier, a vehicle explosion near a mosque inside the Kohat Police Lines was followed by an armed assault in which at least 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred. On the other hand, the PTI has announced plans to march on Islamabad on September 27, with the party demanding the release of its founder, Imran Khan. The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has issued directions concerning the planned protest, including barring the use of state resources to facilitate the march.
The interior minister during the press conference criticised the PTI for the September 27 march in Islamabad, saying that "Neither you nor any minister came to the funerals."
"The situation in K-P over the past 10 days is in front of everyone. There was a suicide attack on a mosque, and two or three other attacks besides. Our captains have been martyred, our soldiers have been martyred, our police personnel have been martyred — and we are preparing to march on one city," he said.
Read: Tarar warns no violent group will be allowed to enter Islamabad
Naqvi added the protest would not benefit PTI and would instead damage the economy, saying that "They will hurt themselves, and they will hurt the people."
He said PTI's leadership had repeatedly been told that political demands could not be won through such means, and urged the party to reconsider while it still could.
"I would say they still have time. They should not go into a situation from which there is no way back," Naqvi said.
On enforcement, the interior minister stated that the government would implement the IHC order on the march, which barred political parties from occupying roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas or public buildings, and directed provincial governments not to allow state resources to be used for the protest.
"This time it will not happen that they come and the road is blocked for 10 or 20 days. That possibility does not exist — I'm telling you this in advance," he stated.
Naqvi added that authorities would also leave "no loophole" if the march went ahead, though he said he believed most PTI leaders did not favour it: "The majority of people in their leadership do not want to do the long march."
Read more: Long marches, strikes, sit-ins may cost Pakistan’s economy Rs120b a day: Aurangzeb
Asked whether rising fuel prices could add to public anger and boost support for the protest, Naqvi pointed to volatility in international oil markets. "Do you know where petrol prices are going in the world? Do you know the current situation?" he asked, adding that maintaining supply had been difficult amid global shortages.
"It does not suit anyone that we increase prices," he said. The interior minister added, "I think the prime minister is in great pain over this — that somehow we should bring it down. We are looking for other ways to bring petrol prices down."
Naqvi said he remained optimistic about the overall situation, citing support from traders, farmers and chambers of commerce for keeping economic activity running.
Later, K-P Information Minister Shafi Jan, responding to Naqvi's press conference, said that “Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf will never give up its constitutional and democratic rights," adding that the September 27 protest could not be stopped through threats.
In a statement, the provincial minister stated that the government should remember the fundamental rights guaranteed to citizens under the Constitution when talking about the law.
Shafi Jan also criticised Naqvi for referring to the funerals of martyrs, saying they should not be made a subject of political rhetoric. “Using the funerals of martyrs for political point-scoring is highly regrettable,” he said.
“If the federal government is not afraid of the long march, why has Islamabad already been turned into a ‘container city’?” Shafi Jan asked.
He also questioned Naqvi’s statement that a permanent strategy would be devised to deal with PTI, "We want to ask why the same strategy was not devised for economic stability."
Shafi Jan said the federal government should not blame PTI for the country’s economic difficulties "but by their so-called experienced economic team."
“We will not be intimidated by threats from the federal government,” Shafi Jan added. He said PTI had faced government pressure and coercion for a long time and would continue to exercise what it considered its constitutional and democratic rights.
Govt says no violent group allowed to come
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said on Sunday that "no violent group will be allowed to come to Islamabad," citing the IHC order against road closures. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb also warned the same day that sustained protests and road closures could cost the economy roughly Rs120 billion a day, with the services sector bearing the largest share.
Also on Sunday, PTI K-P President Junaid Akbar warned the government against using force during the party’s planned September 27 Islamabad protest. “We will turn Islamabad into Somnath ,” he said in Peshawar, adding that PTI workers would reach Islamabad through multiple routes, including the motorway, GT Road, Margalla Hills and Dera Ismail Khan.
Responding, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry called the plan a “conspiracy” and said the government would not allow illegal activity or anything that threatened lives.
“The right to protest does not give the right to attack,” Chaudhry said, adding that peaceful protesters would be provided protection, but “if you come as a terrorist, then you will not go back”.
Referring to Akbar’s remarks, Chaudhry said, “He says he will make Somnath. We know that he makes Somnath. He has made K-P Somnath."

title: Four terrorists killed in exchange of fire in Balochistan s Panjgur  state media
description: A large quantity of modern weapons and ammunition was also recovered from the possession of the dead terrorists
content:
Large quantity of modern weapons, ammunition also recovered from possession of slain terrorists
Four terrorists were killed in an exchange of fire with security forces in Balochistan's Panjgur district, state-run Radio Pakistan said, citing security sources, on Monday.
The operation was carried out in the Aphan Koh area of Prom Paroom in Panjgur, on intelligence reports about the presence of terrorists belonging to the Fitna al-Hindustan . The operation was conducted as part of the security forces' ongoing Operation Radd-ul-Fitna 3 against terrorists in Balochistan, Radio Pakistan said.
Security forces exchanged heavy fire with the terrorists during the operation, resulting in the deaths of four of them, the sources said. A large quantity of modern weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the possession of the slain terrorists, the security sources added.
Four terrorists of Fitna al-Hindustan have been killed by security forces during an operation in Paroom area of Panjgur district @OfficialDGISPR #News #RadioPakistan https://t.co/8oj1SuVwpl pic.twitter.com/yai4mT4rDZ
The sources said security operations against terrorists were continuing in the area and would continue until the last terrorist was eliminated.
The federal government last year officially designated all terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as Fitna al-Hindustan , accusing India of sponsoring a proxy war through the outfits.
The high-tempo intelligence-driven operations are being conducted as part of the ongoing " Radd-ul-Fitna-3 " campaign, which the military's media wing described as a counterterrorism operation aimed at eliminating Indian proxies.
The development came a day after security forces killed seven terrorists affiliated with the Fitna al-Hindustan in two separate operations in Balochistan under Operation Radd-ul-Fitna 3 , according to security sources.
Read: Security forces kill 11 terrorists in Balochistan operations: state media
Five terrorists were killed during an operation in the Fatah Ali area of Panjgur, while two more were killed in a separate operation in the Dhadar area of Kachhi district, the sources said.
Several terrorists were also reported to have been injured during the operation, the sources said.
Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022.
Although Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) has borne the brunt of terrorism, Balochistan has also remained a major target of Indian proxies, which often target civilians and military installations in the province.
Security forces have continued operations across the provinces against what the state describes as Indian-sponsored terrorists and their proxies, but despite these efforts, the groups have continued to target civilian and defence installations.

title: Imran s sisters challenge 30 day detention in LHC  seek immediate release
description: Party says founder s family members placed in armoured vehicle  taken to undisclosed location
author_name: Web Desk, Ahtesham Bashir, Rana Yasif
content:
Party says founder's family members placed in armoured vehicle, taken to undisclosed location
A petition was filed before the Lahore High Court (LHC) on Monday challenging the 30-day detention orders issued against Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan’s sisters Aleema Khan, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance, seeking their immediate release.
The petition was filed by Aleema’s son, Shahraiz Khan, through advocate Rana Mudasar Umar, challenging the detention of his mother and her two sisters. It sought the annulment of the detention orders and the immediate release of all three women.
The arrests came as authorities stepped up a crackdown on PTI in response to the party's planned September 27 march in Islamabad.
The petition contended that the detention order issued by the Lahore deputy commissioner on September 20 was illegal and unlawful, alleging that Aleema was picked up while travelling with her driver for personal work and that there was no public gathering or situation suggesting any threat to public order.
According to the petition, Aleema was detained along with her driver, Muhammad Ameer, and both are currently confined at Lahore Central Jail.
The petitioner claimed that she was a peaceful and law-abiding citizen and had never engaged in any activity prejudicial to public safety, public interest or maintenance of public order.
Read: Imran's sisters Uzma, Noreen also detained under MPO ahead of Sept 27 PTI protest
The plea further challenged the grounds cited for their detention, stating that they were allegedly linked to FIR No 96/23, but the relevant case was registered at Sarwar Road Police Station rather than Race Course Police Station.
It added that Aleema had sought pre-arrest bail in the case, which remained pending for around one and a half years, and that police had ultimately declared her innocent, observing that she was not present at the place of occurrence.
The petitioner alleged that despite this, she was subsequently detained on the basis of the same case, claiming that the detention order was issued on the verbal recommendation of local police and at the instigation of rivals.
The petition argued that the detention order did not identify any specific conduct by Aleema that could legally justify preventive detention or establish an actual threat to public order.
It further contended that vague allegations, political association, peaceful protest, or registration of criminal cases, by themselves, cannot establish such a threat.
It also said that no credible, specific or independently verifiable material was disclosed to establish the necessity of detention, while the order allegedly uses general and formulaic language without an individualised assessment of the detenue’s conduct.
Read more: Naqvi warns PTI against Islamabad march, says governor's rule among options for K-P amid security concerns
The plea maintained that the grounds of detention must contain sufficient particulars to enable the detenue to make an effective representation and stated that the constitutional safeguards relating to communication of the grounds of detention were not properly observed.
The petitioner also argued that preventive detention cannot be used as punishment for an alleged past offence or as a substitute for ordinary criminal proceedings, and that no reasons were recorded to explain why ordinary legal proceedings or less restrictive measures were inadequate.
The petition asked the LHC to declare the detention order dated September 20 null and void. It also sought suspension of the operation of the detention order during pendency of the writ petition.
In the petition, the secretary, Home Department, Lahore deputy commissioner, capital city police officer and superintendent of Lahore Central Jail were made Respondents.
Earlier, police detained Uzma and Noreen, along with his nephews, for 30 days under the MPO Ordinance, a day after Aleema was detained under the same law.
Aleema was detained by authorities in Lahore under the same Section 3 of the MPO, and transferred to Kot Lakhpat Jail for 30 days.
According to an order available to The Express Tribune , dated September 20, the detention was based on reports submitted by the SP Civil Lines Division and the District Intelligence Branch, which alleged that the two women’s activities were “prejudicial to the public safety and maintenance of public order”.
In the order, police and intelligence officials state that Niazi and Uzma had been involved in the May 9 protests and road blockades and had “motivated the workers to damage public and Government property”.
The order further states that the two were “again mobilising the workers through social media and public meetings to create law and order situation” and were raising or chanting “objectionable slogans amongst the general public against the Government/institution in order to provoke and incite them”.
“Accordingly multiple cases including 96/23 PS Race Course were registered,” the order said, adding that the two women were “potential dangers to public peace and tranquility”.
The police reports recommended their detention under Section 3 of the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960, for 30 days, saying this was necessary “in order to keep the law & order situation in the city intact”.
The request was subsequently placed before the District Intelligence Committee at a meeting chaired by the Lahore deputy commissioner on September 20. The order said the matter was “discussed in detail” and that committee members “endorsed the evidence/material provided/shared by the Police Department”.
The committee then “unanimously recommended that a detention order may be issued” against Noreen and Uzma to maintain the law and order situation in Lahore, according to the order.
The deputy commissioner said that, after reviewing the material submitted by the Lahore police chief and the committee’s recommendation, he was “convinced” that the presence of the two women “at any public place will pose a grave threat to the public safety and will likely cause breach of public peace and public order”.
The order directed that Noreen and Uzma “be arrested and detained for a period of 30-days from the date of arrest”, with their custody placed under the Superintendent of Central Jail, Kot Lakhpat.
The order said they “shall be at liberty to make a representation to the Provincial Government against this order”.
PTI members alleged that the two sisters of party founder Imran, along with their children, were arrested by Punjab Police. PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said the family members had been placed in an armoured vehicle and were being taken to an undisclosed location.
“Punjab Police have arrested both sisters of Imran Khan, along with their children and the sons of Aleema Khan. They have been placed in an armoured vehicle and are being taken to an unknown location,” Akram said in a post on X early Monday.
Punjab Police have arrested both sisters of Imran Khan, along with their children and the sons of Aleema Khan Sahiba. They have been placed in an armoured vehicle and are being taken to an unknown location. Shame on the Government of Punjab and Punjab Police. This action is…
In a separate statement, PTI condemned what it called the "illegal and high-handed action" of Punjab Police, alleging that the arrests amounted to an abuse of authority, a violation of fundamental rights and "political victimisation."
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf strongly condemns the illegal and high handed action of Punjab Police in arresting both sisters of former Prime Minister Imran Khan, their children, and the sons of Aleema Khan Sahiba. According to information received, they have been placed in an…
"Targeting women and children of a political family in this manner exposes the true face of the Punjab Government and Punjab Police," the party said, adding that the conduct was "illegal, unconstitutional" and should be condemned.
The party demanded the immediate disclosure of the family members' whereabouts, their safe return and their production before a court of law.
The allegations were followed by a series of posts from Imran's son Kasim Khan. “This is a disgrace,” Kasim wrote on X at around 2:55am. “Now my Aunts Dr Uzma and Noreen, along with my cousins Shershah and Shahrez have now been abducted as well.”
This is a disgrace. Now my Aunts Dr. Uzma and Noureen, along with my cousins Shershah and Shahrez have now been abducted as well. They have broken into my aunties and cousins houses and forced them into vehicles with no explanation. No reasons for arrest have been stated. No… https://t.co/8uIrTAcVhV
He alleged that people had entered the homes of his aunts and cousins and forced them into vehicles without providing an explanation. “They have broken into my aunties and cousins houses and forced them into vehicles with no explanation,” he wrote. Kasim added, “No reasons for arrest have been stated. No news has been released as to where they have been taken.”
He called the alleged detentions “criminal behaviour” and “inexcusable”, and said: “The Pakistani people are petrified of their own leaders.”
The situation appeared to take another turn when Kasim said two of Shahrez’s children, aged four and six, could also not be located.
And it get’s worse. My cousin Shahrez’s 2 children of 4 and 6 years old are now missing. There is no limit to their cruelty. Complete disregard for humanity. https://t.co/oUF0ummxOO
“And it gets worse,” he wrote in a subsequent post, adding, “My cousin Shahrez’s two children of 4 and 6 years are now missing. There is no limit to their cruelty. Complete disregard for humanity.”
About an hour later, Kasim said he had received news that the children were safe, but alleged that two more of his cousins had been arrested.
Hearing news that my cousin’s children are now safe 🙏. Meanwhile two more of my cousins have been arrested. Azeem and Sakeenah. No reasons given. No location given. https://t.co/rkgzrw8Yul
“Hearing news that my cousin’s children are now safe,” he wrote. “Meanwhile, two more of my cousins have been arrested. Azeem and Sakeenah. No reasons given. No location given.”
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi also said he had travelled to Lahore after receiving information that Noreen and Dr Uzma were at risk of arrest.
In a video message recorded near Lahore on the motorway in the early hours of Monday, CM Afridi said he had been in contact with the two women and had asked them to remain inside their homes until he arrived.
"I was informed that Noreen and Uzma Bibi were being arrested," he said. "I left for Lahore to pick up Noreen Apa." The chief minister stated that he had told the two women he would take them to K-P, but alleged that unidentified people subsequently entered their homes and allegedly abducted them.
"The kidnappers attacked their homes, vandalised their houses and have now taken them away," he said, adding that his contact with the two women had since been cut off. "I am repeatedly trying to contact them, but I have not been able to get through," he said.
"If you will not respect someone's mother, sister or daughter, if you will pick up the entire family of a former prime minister, then where will Pakistan go?" CM Afridi questioned.
Read More: PTI to finalise capital march strategy
The chief minister also alleged that PTI workers and their families had faced similar treatment in recent days. He claimed that people in "plain clothes" had been tearing down PTI banners, burning party materials and entering its conventions.
He also alleged that a provincial minister had been targeted and an attempt made to abduct him, accusing authorities of violating the sanctity of homes.
Police also detained Imran's niece Hajra Niazi and her husband on Sunday, according to sources. They were later released after being taken to separate police stations.

content:
Presley Gerber died aged 27 at rehab facility, medical examiner confirms, with cause of death yet to be determined
Presley Gerber was at a rehabilitation facility when he died aged 27 on September 20, according to the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. His cause of death has not yet been determined, as an autopsy has not been completed.
Gerber, the son of model Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber, had previously spoken publicly about his mental health and substance use struggles. He was also the brother of model and actress Kaia Gerber.
His family has asked for privacy following his death. A representative for Crawford, Rande Gerber and Kaia Gerber told PEOPLE, “The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time.”
Kaia discussed her brother’s struggles in her September 2026 Vogue cover story, which described Presley’s experience as a “decade-long struggle with drug addiction”.
“When something like that happens in a family, it kind of levels everyone. I think that’s also why I started to self-identify as the easy one and never wanted to ask for help. Because it felt like too much to have two children who were needing,” she explained.
She continued, “My parents for most of our lives were very, very private and didn’t share anything—and now we have this absolute teacher, my brother, who says, ‘I’m gonna be very human for everyone.’ There’s only so much you can hide from the world. And trying to put a lid on something just makes the person feel like you’re ashamed of them.”
The Vogue profile also said Kaia was “deeply proud of him”.
Presley was charged with a DUI in December 2019. In later years, he discussed his mental health publicly and began sharing “Mental Health Mondays” videos on Instagram.
“Having struggled with mental health, depression and some other things that come along with that, I think that whether I help one person or a hundred people get out of that place that I was in at one point in my life, that's all I need to do,” he said on the Studio 22 podcast.
In December 2025, Presley also discussed several medications he had been prescribed for panic attacks in a since-deleted Instagram video.

title: All Iranian airlines to shut down worldwide by Sept 23  US Treasury chief says
description: In a    phone call with Fox News  Trump said Iran s leaders should make a deal  rot economically or be wiped out
content:
Mohsin Naqvi arrives in Tehran, meets Iran's interior minister, says Iranian media
United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Monday that operations of all Iranian commercial airlines would shut down globally beginning on September 23.
"On September 23rd, all the Iranian airlines will be shut down around the world," Bessent told CNBC, outlining broad secondary sanctions aimed at isolating Tehran's civil aviation network.
Bessent explained that international hubs servicing Iranian planes would face complete exclusion from the American banking system. Foreign operators could not refuel the aircraft, provide landing facilities, or sell passenger tickets without risking their access to dollar clearing, he warned.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has warned Iranian airlines will have trouble functioning globally in two days under the weight of American sanctions, in an interview with US broadcaster CNBC. 🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/htTiBaVLz2 pic.twitter.com/CsX80Fx8Lj
Iranian officials did not immediately issue a public response regarding the planned aviation restrictions.
Bessent also warned third-party entities assisting Tehran that Washington had identified financial intermediaries facilitating transactions. "We've seen enablers throughout the world. We know who they are. They know who they are, and we are putting a stop to it," he said.
Asked whether discussions covered potential Chinese enforcement, Bessent confirmed that the matter was addressed during meetings. He noted that Washington conducted "quiet, behind-the-scenes discussions" with multiple nations rather than public spectacles, adding that Chinese financial authorities, including People's Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng, remained “very engaged in the process.”
Regarding the duration and intensity of the campaign, Bessent did not specify whether the pressure would last "one week, one month, or six months" but noted the strain was “like never before.”
Mohsin Naqvi arrives in Tehran, meets Iran's interior minister: Iranian media
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met with Iran’s Interior Minister, Eskandar Momeni, and emphasised finalising agreements to expand bilateral relations during their meeting on Monday, according to IRNA .
Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni and his Pakistani counterpart, Mohsen Naqvi stressed expansion of bilateral relations. pic.twitter.com/p0TpvZ9FvS
Earlier, Naqvi arrived in Tehran and was welcomed by his Iranian counterpart and officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, according to ISNA .
سیدمحسن نقوی وزیر کشور پاکستان در راس هیاتی با استقبال همتای ایرانی خود وارد تهران شد https://t.co/K0LKKZxIcX pic.twitter.com/dDPPtZ9GXT
Regarding the visit, Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmail Baghaei had earlier said that the visit was taking place within the framework of bilateral relations.
He described the relations between the two countries as very good and said: "Our relations, especially in the last few months, have been growing in all areas."
Baghaei added that "During this visit, it is planned to discuss the understandings that have already been made between the two countries, including at the level of presidents."
Baghaei on Saturday said there was no plan to exchange any specific messages regarding mediation.
Naqvi, who has been actively involved in the mediation process alongside Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir, is slated to discuss matters related to attacks by the Yemeni Houthi group on Saudi Arabia's oil and economic infrastructure, and how to revive the stalled peace talks with the US, official sources who spoke earlier to Anadolu added.
Islamabad has already warned that the recent escalation in Yemen would further complicate the already complex regional scenario.
This was Naqvi's sixth visit to Tehran since the US and Israel launched war against Iran in February.
According to an official source who spoke with an IRNA reporter in Islamabad, Pakistan's Interior Minister Seyyed Mohsen Naqvi made a trip to Iran on Monday. pic.twitter.com/TkpBYuQwoq
Pakistan has remained the primary mediator between Iran and the US throughout the war, and has maintained close contact with both sides.
Trump spoke with Yemen's president on Sunday, sources say
US President Donald Trump spoke by phone with Yemeni President Rashad al-Alimi on Sunday, four people familiar with the matter said, discussing the advances of the Iran-backed Houthis around a vital global waterway.
Alimi requested US support for his Saudi-backed government in its fight against the Houthis, who this month took key areas along the Bab al-Mandeb strait in a lightning offensive.
Two of the sources, one Yemeni and one Western, said Trump had made no direct pledge of military support during the call.
The White House and Yemen's information minister did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Tanker struck by projectile in Strait of Hormuz, two crew injured, UKMTO says
A tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz was struck by a projectile, injuring two crew members, United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said on Monday, citing military authorities.
UKMTO WARNING 140-26 Click here to view the full product.⤵️ https://t.co/WVkFIoPW0l #MaritimeSecurity #MarSec pic.twitter.com/CVFhhsDnvU
The two crew members sustained minor injuries, while the vessel continued to its next port of call, it added.
Iran says it downed US MQ-1 drone over Strait of Hormuz: report
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Monday that it intercepted and destroyed a US Army MQ-1 drone over the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian media.
The IRGC said the drone was brought down by its new advanced aerospace air defence system, operating as part of Iran's integrated air defence network, Mehr News Agency reported.
The force claimed Washington had returned the MQ-1 to service after suffering heavy losses among its MQ-9 fleet.
It said the MQ-1, known as the "Beast of Kandahar" after logging about 20,000 flight hours over Afghanistan, had been retired from US military service and replaced by the MQ-9.
After the destruction of a large portion of the MQ-9 fleet, the US has been forced to use this drone, the IRGC said.
US says 'door is open' for Iran to return to negotiations
US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said on Sunday that the “door is open” for Iran to return to negotiations to end the conflict in the Middle East.
Speaking at an Al-Monitor Live event in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, Waltz said the Trump administration believes time is on its side in the conflict with Iran, which began February 28.
“I do believe that to be the case,” Waltz said when asked by Al-Monitor senior adviser Andrew Parasiliti whether Washington believes time is on its side.
He added that the “door is open for Iran to come back to the negotiating table,” while dismissing as “fantastical” reports that Tehran has demanded an end to US sanctions and reparations as conditions for renewed talks.
Waltz also said that Iran "can never [be allowed to] hold the world hostage with a nuclear weapon."
Mike Waltz, the US envoy to the UN, says US President Donald Trump is determined to ensure Iran never acquires a nuclear weapon and will continue to apply “maximum pressure to that end”. 🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/htTiBaWjoA pic.twitter.com/Q0R6UJ1po1
“The Iranian regime is at its weakest point since 1979, and it’s getting weaker,” Waltz said, citing economic pressure and the collapse of Iran’s currency. “They’re going to come back [to talks], I hope peacefully and diplomatically.”
US denies visas to Iranian president’s media team, official says
The United States has refused to issue visas to President Masoud Pezeshkian’s media team, forcing him to travel to New York for the UN General Assembly without them, an Iranian official said on Monday, according to Iran International .
Habibollah Abbasi, director-general of public relations in the president’s office, described the decision as a “hostile act.”
Iranian military command said on Monday that it received information that the US planned to resume strikes on the country, according to Al Jazeera .
Iran would use new weapons and target locations not previously attacked if the United States launched a new offensive against it, Revolutionary Guards spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi said on Monday, according to the Fars news agency .
"If a new aggression occurs, we will certainly change the weaponry and the geography of the war," Mohebbi said, adding that Tehran was prepared for a prolonged conflict.
Iran’s military command says it has received information that the US is preparing to resume strikes on the country, after months of reduced direct attacks. 🔗 https://t.co/OtKGMk7AFX pic.twitter.com/ILzV3gKkny
Earlier, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said that Tehran's "messages and conditions have been conveyed explicitly" to the US through intermediaries. He reiterated that the conditions must be met before negotiations resume.
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said that Tehran's "messages and conditions have been conveyed explicitly" to the US through intermediaries. He reiterated the conditions must be met before negotiations resume. 🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/qJleYbnwN8 pic.twitter.com/VYgZvxBhxB
Vessels trickle through Strait of Hormuz as Middle East conflict persists
A dozen commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on the weekend, down from 35 the prior weekend, shipping data showed on Monday, as tension in the Gulf persisted with the US and Iran in stalemate.
Visible traffic through the strait, the conduit for a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas before the war, has dwindled to a trickle. However, Middle Eastern producers continue to export oil on tankers travelling with their transponders off.
Among trackable ships, four vessels — two tankers carrying refined oil products and two empty carriers for bulk goods and gas — exited the strait on Sunday, while another two small-sized oil tankers entered the Gulf, provisional data from analytics firm Kpler showed.
On Saturday, five vessels left the Gulf carrying agricultural products, liquefied petroleum gas and fertiliser while an empty very large gas carrier entered, the data showed.
Before the US-Israeli war with Iran started on February 28, the strait typically handled about 125 large, commercial vessels per day, including tankers, gas carriers, bulkers and container vessels.
Iran and US trade threats after Houthi attacks escalate regional conflict
Iran and the United States exchanged new threats on Sunday, with President Donald Trump warning Iran would fail ‌economically or face its leadership being wiped out if it didn't make a deal, and the Iranian military saying it would retaliate harshly to any fresh attack.
The conflict has looked stalemated for months, with no sign either side was ready for concessions even as it has deepened a global energy crisis, cratered swathes of Iran's economy and spilt over into new regional escalations.
In a ​phone call with a Fox News reporter, Trump said Iran's leaders should make a deal, rot economically or be wiped out, the reporter said.
However, ​with Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian expected in New York this week for the United Nations General Assembly, Trump said he would ⁠be open to meeting him, the Fox reporter added.
Read: Trump warns he has entered 'deciding mode' on Iran, says 'big things' are in store
Trump has repeatedly made vague threats of major military escalations during the conflict that began with US and Israeli ​strikes on February 28, without carrying them out.
Earlier, Iran's military central command said any new attack would trigger sustained retaliation against US bases and interests and that ​Washington's regional allies would be considered parties to the conflict.
The Iranian military added that it had information that an attack was being prepared, without elaborating on what that information might be.
Yemen's Giants Brigades say 5 Houthi military vehicles destroyed near Bab al-Mandab Strait
Yemen’s government-affiliated Giants Brigades said on Sunday that they destroyed five Houthi military vehicles on the Kahbub front overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait, killing all those inside.
"The Giants Brigades destroyed five Houthi military vehicles, killing everyone aboard them," the brigade's media centre said in a Facebook statement, without giving a death toll.
It said one vehicle belonged to an unidentified commander, and another carried a 23mm weapon.
The media centre released video purportedly showing the vehicles engulfed in flames.
The Houthis did not immediately comment.
The Kahbub Mountains in Lahj governorate near the Bab al-Mandab Strait are strategically important because they overlook a major international shipping route connecting the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.
Qatar says mediation efforts underway to revive US-Iran talks
Qatar said on Sunday that its mediation team has been discussing proposals for nearly two weeks aimed at restarting talks between the United States and Iran.
🧵 1/7 Qatar’s Foreign Ministry says mediators are working 'around the clock' to restart talks between Iran and US. This follows comments by Iran’s security chief, who confirmed to Al Jazeera that Iran’s terms have been conveyed to the US through mediators Qatar and Pakistan. pic.twitter.com/CB0K2UAgyg
“We have been exchanging various ideas for nearly two weeks on resuming talks between Washington and Tehran,” said Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari, according to Qatari media.
Qatar, alongside Pakistan, has been mediating between the two sides.
“We are working through our mediation team with Tehran and Washington to see whether talks can resume, and our mediators are currently moving between different capitals in the hope of making progress on this track,” al-Ansari said.
He added that Qatar had heard assurances from officials in the US administration that Washington wanted to reach an agreement.
Al-Ansari said there is a need for “a regional solution that achieves stability and an international understanding that protects waterways such as the Strait of Hormuz.”
“Subjecting waterways to the sovereignty of a single state and using them as a weapon will set a dangerous precedent for all of us,” he added.
The US has recently carried out military attacks on sites in Iran amid a deadlock in negotiations over disagreements concerning navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world’s most important routes for energy supplies and global trade, despite a memorandum of understanding signed by the two sides in mid-June.
Iran responded with attacks on what it said were US military facilities and equipment in Arab countries, including Saudi Arabia. Some of the attacks caused civilian casualties and damage to civilian infrastructure, drawing condemnation from the affected countries and calls for them to stop.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28, leaving more than 3,000 people dead. Iran responded with attacks that it said killed Americans and Israelis.
US Gulf allies have already been badly scarred by a war that the US and Israel launched with no warning, bringing their cities under Iranian fire and hammering their economies with the ​crucial Strait of Hormuz waterway blockaded.
On Saturday, their predicament worsened further, with Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi group launching missile and drone strikes at the Saudi capital after having ​made sudden military gains in Yemen's reignited civil war earlier this month.
Reuters video showed a massive plume of black smoke billowing from the area of Riyadh's main international airport following booms ‌overnight.
Read more: UN Security Council condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
The US ⁠State Department issued a security alert citing the Houthi hostilities. It said there was potential for unforeseen escalation in the Middle East, and Americans should exercise more vigilance and be aware of possible flight cancellations and airspace closures.
Saudi Arabia did not comment on the incident, though a Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had foiled other attacks on the kingdom.
Recent escalation by the Houthis has forced Riyadh into a painful dilemma: continue airstrikes on the group to stop it seizing more Yemeni ​territory or step back in the hopes ​of averting drone strikes on critical ⁠infrastructure.
The Houthi gains along the coast mean the group's forces now sit on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, giving them easier control over shipping travelling between the Red Sea and Asia and the ability to blockade the crucial waterway.
With Iran already ​having blockaded most shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, the oil-rich Gulf's energy exports are now almost entirely cut ​off from global markets, ⁠adding to pressure on oil prices.
A US blockade of Iranian ports is meanwhile stopping Iran from selling its own oil, contributing to major problems in the Islamic Republic's economy.
Despite the economic damage, there is little sign of a return to the interim ceasefire agreement that was struck in June but fell apart in July amid disputes over its terms.
Iran reiterated ⁠on Sunday that ​it would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the terms of that June agreement, as ​it interpreted them, were met.
Ghalibaf said Iran would have to keep on fighting as well as negotiating, to push back its enemies and to consolidate any gains with diplomacy.

He also shared mental health awareness videos on Instagram, discussing recovery, healthy habits and the importance of finding support without judgement.
In a September 2026 Vogue interview, Kaia reflected on her brother’s openness about his struggles, describing him as “this absolute teacher”.
Presley Gerber is survived by his parents, Cindy and Rande, and his sister, Kaia.

title: Upper Dir s healthcare system under strain
description: Upper Dir s healthcare system under strain
content:
Doctor shortages, cholera outbreak expose critical gaps in public healthcare
A severe shortage of doctors and healthcare facilities has raised serious concerns over the state of public health in Upper Dir, where around 1.08 million people are being served by only 207 doctors, including just 13 female doctors for an estimated 530,000 women.
According to available figures, each female doctor in the district is responsible for the healthcare and gynaecological needs of approximately 40,770 women. Meanwhile, 195 male doctors are serving around 550,000 men, with each doctor catering to nearly 3,000 patients.
The shortage has particularly affected maternal and child healthcare, with deaths of mothers and infants during childbirth reportedly remaining high compared with other districts. A large number of Upper Dir residents are compelled to travel to Timergara, Swat, Mardan, Peshawar, Islamabad and Lahore for diagnosis and treatment.
The sight of ambulances carrying critically ill and injured patients from Upper Dir towards Timergara and Peshawar, often with sirens blaring along the Dir-Peshawar GT Road, has become common.
Concern has also been growing over a reported rise in deaths from heart attacks in the district. Residents have demanded that the authorities determine the causes and ensure immediate and free treatment for affected patients.
The entire district is currently facing an outbreak of cholera. Reports suggest that 200 to 300 cholera patients are being brought daily to District Headquarters Hospital Dir alone. A water-testing laboratory team established a camp at the RHC Chooran and collected samples from different areas of Ashiri Dara, but the outbreak has yet to be brought under control.
Upper Dir has one Category-B District Headquarters Hospital in Dir, two Category-C hospitals at Wari and Barawal Banda, five Category-D hospitals at Patrak, Sheringal, Bibior, Chooran-Taptar and Nahag Dara Banda, besides 32 basic health units and several dispensaries in rural areas.
The government claims that 54 per cent of the required healthcare facilities are currently available in the district. However, the continued movement of thousands of patients to hospitals outside Upper Dir has raised questions about the adequacy of these facilities.
The situation became particularly serious when staff at Timergara Headquarters Hospital reportedly issued a written directive refusing treatment to patients referred from Upper Dir. The decision was withdrawn following protests on social media.
District Health Officer Upper Dir Dr Khalid Khan, who also holds the additional charge of Medical Superintendent at DHQ Hospital Dir, said the government was making efforts to improve healthcare services.
He said 32 BHUs had been made functional, with two doctors posted at each facility, while 207 doctors, including 50 to 60 specialists and 13 female doctors, were currently performing duties in the district.
According to Dr Khan, DHQ Hospital Dir provides initial and emergency treatment for cardiac, orthopaedic, psychiatric, trauma, prostate and hernia cases, besides conducting major and minor surgeries.
He said work was underway at a cost of Rs980 million to upgrade DHQ Hospital Dir with modern technology and facilities to Category-A level. Work was also in progress to upgrade the Category-C hospital at Wari to Category-B level and equip it with modern healthcare facilities.
Dr Khan said a new referral mechanism was being developed to reduce pressure on major hospitals. Under the proposed system, patients would first visit their nearest BHU. If the case could not be treated there, the patient would be referred electronically to the appropriate higher-level hospital.
He acknowledged that providing adequate healthcare and protecting the lives of mothers and children remained a priority, but admitted that the authorities had not yet achieved complete success in this regard.
Responding to concerns over only 13 female doctors serving nearly half a million women, he said the shortage was a challenge not only for Upper Dir but for the entire province and country.
He added that referrals to Timergara and Peshawar could not be completely eliminated because some patients were in critical condition and required specialised treatment. However, he said efforts were underway to expand local facilities and reduce unnecessary referrals.

title: Rising costs push Shangla flour prices
description: Rising costs push Shangla flour prices
content:
Traders blame fuel hikes and alleged Punjab restrictions
Like the rest of the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, flour prices have risen sharply in Shangla, with a 20-kilogram bag now selling for between Rs2,950 and Rs3,000, while prices in several remote areas have crossed the Rs3,000 mark, traders said.
The increase has added to the difficulties of people already struggling with rising inflation, as repeated increases in fuel prices have pushed up the cost of food and other essential commodities. Low-income households and employees working in the private sector are facing particular financial pressure, with many finding it increasingly difficult to meet household expenses, support their children and afford basic food.
Traders from different parts of Shangla said they were purchasing a 20kg flour bag for around Rs2,900 and selling it for Rs2,950 to Rs3,000. In remote areas, transportation and other additional costs had pushed the price above Rs3,000, they added.
The traders expressed concern over the increase, claiming that alleged restrictions or obstacles imposed by the Punjab government on inter-provincial transportation and trade were affecting markets in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. They said the situation could further affect the availability and prices of flour in the province.
They said that while fuel prices continued to rise, flour, cooking oil, sugar, pulses and other essential commodities were also becoming increasingly unaffordable for ordinary consumers. Rising daily expenses have disrupted household budgets, particularly for middle- and low-income families, while limited business activity and unemployment have prevented any significant increase in incomes.
According to the traders, employees working in private institutions, shops, markets and other sectors on low salaries are among the worst affected. Many low-paid workers earn around Rs30,000 a month or even less, making it extremely difficult to meet the basic expenses of a household under the prevailing inflationary conditions.

title: PTI to finalise capital march strategy
description: PTI to finalise capital march strategy
content:
K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to consult lawmakers, announce protest plan at press conference today
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi has convened a meeting of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) lawmakers and party office-bearers in Peshawar today (Monday) to finalise the strategy for the September 27 Islamabad long march, after which he is expected to announce the schedule for the planned protest.
PTI has announced a march on Islamabad on September 27 to demand the release of its founding chairman, Imran Khan. The party has referred to the planned protest as the "March in Phases".
Sources said the PTI leadership had prepared several plans for the September 27 protest and would finalise the course of action after consultations with members of the provincial assembly and party leaders.
According to the sources, all PTI lawmakers and party office-bearers have been asked to attend the consultative meeting at the Chief Minister's House in Peshawar at 2pm.
The meeting is expected to discuss arrangements for the Islamabad march, participation from different districts and the role of party workers and lawmakers.
The chief minister is scheduled to hold a press conference at the Chief Minister's House at 5:30pm, during which he is expected to announce the final plan and schedule for the September 27 protest.
Meanwhile, the PTI leadership has reportedly advised its members of the provincial assembly against leaving K-P ahead of the protest amid concerns over possible arrests.
Party sources said PTI lawmakers had been instructed to avoid travelling outside the province before September 27. The decision was reportedly taken in view of the possibility of arrests of party leaders and workers in Punjab ahead of the planned Islamabad protest.
The sources said PTI leaders from Punjab could also seek refuge in K-P if arrests intensify in the province. Invitations have reportedly been extended to senior PTI leaders from Punjab to travel to K-P before the protest.
The development comes after the reported arrest of Imran Khan's sister, Aleema Khan, which has heightened concerns within the PTI leadership over possible action against its leaders and workers.
Party leaders are now focusing on consolidating their organisational arrangements in K-P and ensuring the participation of lawmakers and workers in the September 27 protest.
The final decisions regarding the route, mobilisation and other arrangements for the Islamabad march are expected to be announced by Chief Minister Sohail Afridi at his scheduled press conference later today.
Lawmakers have been assigned to mobilize maximum number of party workers and supporters to make the Islamabad march a real success. Workers have also been asked to carry food, water and mattresses with them and come fully prepeared.

title: Kohat suicide attack case registered

Case includes charges related to terrorism, murder, attempted murder and other offences
A case has been registered with the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) police station over the suicide attack on the old Police Lines in Kohat, police said.
The FIR was registered on the complaint of the Station House Officer of City Police Station Kohat against unidentified terrorists. The case includes charges related to terrorism, murder, attempted murder and other offences.
According to the FIR, militants belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan faction identified in the report as Fitna al-Khawarij carried out a suicide attack at the Police Lines mosque using an explosives-laden vehicle. The attackers subsequently opened indiscriminate fire and hurled hand grenades.
The FIR stated that the militants used the mosque route as an entry point and forced their way into the Police Lines while firing. Police personnel and civilians suffered casualties during the attack.
Police personnel confronted the attackers and engaged them in a gun battle. Officers from the army, police and CTD also reached the scene and took charge of the operation.
According to the FIR, the suicide blast, gunfire and grenade attacks left 21 people martyred, while a large number of others were injured. Government and private property was also damaged in the attack.

title: Italy to ban veils in schools  limit foreign students per class
description: Italy to ban veils in schools  limit foreign students per class
content:
Italy is preparing to ban face coverings in schools and to cap the number of foreign students per class, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said on Sunday as she played up her right-wing credentials at a youth event organised by her party.
Italy is among the European countries most exposed to migrant arrivals because of its central Mediterranean location, making migration a hot-button issue and a major challenge for successive governments.
The integration of migrants, particularly those from Muslim-majority countries, remains contentious in Italian politics and society. Debates over religious symbols, cultural integration, citizenship rules and immigration policy frequently polarise public opinion.
"A measure will soon be presented to a Cabinet meeting to legally establish a maximum number of foreign students per class. It also requires parents of foreign students facing serious difficulties integrating into the school system to learn Italian and bans burqas and niqabs in schools," Meloni told an annual gathering of the youth wing of her Brothers of Italy party.
"If there is only one child in a class who doesn't understand Italian, that child will likely be able to learn the language and integrate quickly with the help of classmates and teachers.
However, if the number of children who don't understand the language becomes large - or even the majority - that is no longer integration; it is neglect," she added.
Meloni did not specify what the maximum number of foreign students per class would be.
Students who are not Italian citizens account for 11.6% of those enrolled in Italian schools - nearly 12 in every 100 students - according to Fondazione ISMU, a research institution.
"You must go to school with your face uncovered, and in Italy no one, in the name of a real or supposed tradition, can decide that a young woman must hide herself, " Meloni said.
