title: We will turn Islamabad into Somnath   PTI   s Junaid warns govt against use of force ahead of Sept 27 protest
description: Terrorists won   t return   Talal warns PTI over Islamabad protest
content:
'Terrorists won’t return,' Talal warns PTI over Islamabad protest
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) president Junaid Akbar on Sunday warned the government against the use of power during the party’s planned protest on September 27, saying that the party knew the state would open fire during its planned Islamabad march, but warned that this time its workers would not simply collect bodies and return.
“We will turn Islamabad into Somnath,” he said while addressing a gathering in Peshawar.
Akbar said PTI workers would approach Islamabad through multiple routes, including the motorway and Grand Trunk Road, while some would descend from the Margalla Hills and others would come from Dera Ismail Khan.
He urged the people of Islamabad and nearby areas to join the march, while suggesting that people from Lahore, Multan, Karachi and Faisalabad should instead mobilise in their respective cities.
He said PTI workers from K-P would go to Islamabad and, if people from Attock, Rawalpindi and Islamabad wanted to join them, “it is a very good thing”.
Akbar also called for the closure of Lahore, Faisalabad, Quetta and Karachi on the day of the march, saying people in those cities should come out in large numbers.
He said PTI workers had faced arrests and injuries during previous protests and claimed that thousands of party workers had been arrested in different provinces.
“We also get shot, we also get hurt,” he said, adding that he had been going through “the worst situation” for a year.
Akbar said the party had tried to find a way out of its differences but had failed. “We put our credibility at stake, but we tried to find a way. But the way did not come out,” he said.
He said the party had no other option and urged workers to make a decision about whether they wanted to “die or make a new Pakistan”.
Akbar said the party did not want the state to weaken or hatred to increase, adding that he respected state institutions despite his differences with their leaders.
“We do not want the state to weaken. We do not want hatred to increase,” he said.
He also raised the issue of finances for the planned protest, saying the party would need funds for its mobilisation.
Akbar said he would carry out any responsibility assigned to him and suggested that Ali Amin Gandapur and Shahid Khattak jointly lead the march, with the K-P chief minister Sohail Afridi leading it.
He said PTI workers had been warned that transport would not be available for them, but added: “We will go on foot on the 27th, but we will go to Islamabad.”
Meanwhile, responding to Akbar's remarks, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry described the plan as a “conspiracy” and said the government would not allow any activity that was illegal or threatened people's lives.
Talking to a private news channel, Chaudhry described the PTI's plan as a “conspiracy”.
“This is a conspiracy. This is a conspiracy of the so-called political right. This is their conspiracy,” he said.
He alleged that the plan involved deaths, attacks and violence, saying the PTI had demonstrated such behaviour in the past, referring to the events of May 9 and Nov 26.
Chaudhry said that on May 9, PTI leaders led people out of their homes and an attack took place, after which they tried to distance themselves from what had happened.
He alleged that PTI workers were asked to perform duties during the protest and that some security personnel were run over by vehicles, leaving many workers injured. He said the protesters attacked Islamabad and later described it as their right.
“The right to protest does not give the right to attack,” Chaudhry said, adding that peaceful protest had to be conducted in its proper manner.
“If you are a peaceful citizen, you can come to Islamabad from any direction. You will be given protection and all kinds of facilities,” he said. “But if you come as a terrorist, then you will not go back.”
He said there should be no doubt about the government's position this time, adding that there was “absolutely no scope” for such actions.
Chaudhry said the government would act not only under the law but also in accordance with the Islamabad High Court's order.
“We will follow it with clarity, letter and spirit,” he said.
He said Islamabad housed foreign embassies, international institutions and their offices, as well as major businesses and important government offices, and was the capital of Pakistan.
“No such thing will be tolerated here which is illegal and which is a threat to people's lives or which can affect ordinary life,” he said.
Referring again to Junaid's remarks about turning Islamabad into Somnath, Chaudhry said the PTI leader's statement reflected what he described as the party's approach.
“He says he will make Somnath. We know that he makes Somnath. He has made K-P Somnath,” he said.
Chaudhry said that the PTI had failed to stop terrorism in K-P and had also failed to bring the promised improvement in health, education and other facilities.
He said the party had spoken of bringing change if it came to power, but alleged that it had instead turned K-P into “Somnath”.
The minister said the government would not allow such thinking to move forward.
“These are the things that the government was saying before,” he said and described it as the PTI's “real plan”, saying the remarks had revealed what the government had previously been warning about.

title: Israeli forces blow up former regime military sites in southwestern Syria  shell Quneitra countryside
description: Southwestern Syria has seen repeated Israeli raids  arrests  land clearing and shelling  Damascus says
content:
Southwestern Syria has seen repeated Israeli raids, arrests, land clearing and shelling, Damascus says
Israeli forces on Sunday blew up military sites formerly used by the former regime of Bashar al-Assad near Jandal Castle on Mount Hermon (Jabal al-Sheikh) in southwestern Syria, Syrian state television reported.
Alikhbariah TV said Israeli forces also shelled an area southeast of the town of Al-Rafid in the southern Quneitra countryside in southwestern Syria.
In a separate attack, Israeli forces fired several artillery shells at the Bir Ajam woodland west of the village of Zubaida in the central Quneitra countryside, the broadcaster added.
No information was immediately available on casualties or damage from the attacks.
Read More: Israeli fire kills three Palestinians in Gaza
Southwestern Syria has seen repeated Israeli incursions involving raids, arrests, land clearing and shelling, which Damascus denounces as violations of its sovereignty and the 1974 Disengagement Agreement.
Syria has repeatedly demanded the withdrawal of Israeli forces from its territory and called on the international community to press Israel to fully withdraw from southern Syria.
Despite the Syrian government posing no threat to Israel, Israeli forces have repeatedly carried out incursions into Syria and launched airstrikes that have killed civilians and destroyed military sites, vehicles, weapons and ammunition belonging to the Syrian army.
During a visit to Syria in July, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said violations of Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity were “unacceptable,” calling on Israel to abide by the 1974 disengagement agreement.

title: Fact check  Viral video does not show Saudi imam arrested for criticising US policies in region
description: Video is from 2018 and is unrelated to claims of an imam being arrested over criticism
content:
Video is from 2018 and is unrelated to claims of an imam being arrested over criticism
Several people, the majority of whom appear to be Saudi based on their display profiles and past posts, have been sharing a video on social media platform X since September 13, 2026, allegedly showing a mosque imam being arrested in Saudi Arabia for criticising the United States’ policy in the region. However, the video is old and shows a mentally ill person.
The ongoing US-Iran war in the Middle East began on February 28, 2026, when the United States and Israel launched strikes against Iran. The conflict has since expanded across the region, with Iran launching attacks against US and Israeli interests and several US allies in the Middle East.
In early September, the conflict also intensified between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthi movement. The Houthis have launched missile and drone attacks targeting Saudi military and energy infrastructure, while Saudi Arabia has carried out retaliatory strikes in Yemen. The escalation has further widened the regional conflict and disrupted vital energy and shipping routes.
On Sept 13, a Saudi Arabia-based user shared a video on X, claiming that it showed the arrest of a mosque imam in Saudi Arabia. The Arabic caption accompanying the video translates to: “Arrest of the mosque imam in Saudi Arabia for his condemnation and criticism regarding America’s policy in the region. They didn’t even wait for him to finish the sermon.”
Another Saudi Arabia-based user shared the same video with the same caption on Sept 14.
On September 15, another user shared the same clip with the same caption. The post attracted 255,800 views.
Several other users also shared the video in a similar context, as seen here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , and here , collectively accumulating 23,240 views.
A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to its high virality and keen public interest in the matter.
A keyword search was conducted to corroborate whether any credible local or international media outlet has reported on such an incident recently yielded no results.
A reverse image search of the video was conducted to trace the video yielded a Facebook post published on March 3, 2018, containing the same footage.
The Arabic caption accompanying the video claimed that during a Friday sermon at a mosque in Saudi Arabia, the preacher criticised the Al Saud family and its attempts to normalise relations with Israel before security personnel forcibly removed him from the pulpit.
The post also included a response attributed to Saudi authorities, which stated that an elderly man had climbed the pulpit before the official preacher and insisted on delivering the sermon.
According to the statement, security officials intervened and removed him from the pulpit, while a spokesperson for the Ministry of Islamic Affairs said the man was mentally ill.
Another Facebook post from the same date made a similar claim in its Arabic caption, which reads: “The preacher of the Friday sermon spoke about Jewish people and corruption, due to which he was arrested.”
A keyword search conducted to corroborate the claim yielded several Saudi Arabia-based Arabic media outlets, including Shehab News , Okaz , Al-Riyadh and Khabarni and a Turkish news agency, Anadolu Agency , that reported on this particular incident in 2018.
Shehab News published an article on March 2, 2018, titled: “Video: Sheikh forcibly removed from the pulpit during Friday sermon in Saudi Arabia”.
The report stated that an elderly man was forcibly removed from the pulpit at Al-Jabriya Mosque in Yanbu after refusing to leave.
It cited a source from Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Islamic Affairs, which described the man as “mentally ill”, while noting that social media users had shared different accounts about the reason for his removal.
On March 3, 2018. Okaz published an article titled “Medina Police: Yanbu preacher is mentally ill and was handed over to his family” on March 3, 2018.
The article had an official comment from the Medina Police spokesperson; it said the man was in his seventies, had a medical record for psychological disorders, and was handed over to his family for continued treatment and care.
Al-Riyadh also posted the official statement of the Medina police on the incident on March 3, 2018.
In the statement, the police spokesperson Major Hussein Al-Qahtani confirmed the same.
None of the reports reviewed identified the man as the mosque’s imam. Instead, they described him as an elderly man and “mentally ill” who attempted to deliver the Friday sermon before the official preacher.
The claim that a viral video shows an imam being arrested for criticising US policies in the region is false.
The video is from 2018 and shows an elderly mentally ill person.

title: Nameer Khan calls out Zamil s behaviour in  Dar e Nijaat
description: Actor reflects on his character s mistakes in the series  urges men to respect women
content:
Actor reflects on his character's mistakes in the series, urges men to respect women
Actor Nameer Khan, who plays Zamil in the popular drama Dar-e-Nijaat , has used his character’s troubled arc to highlight the importance of men treating women with respect and taking responsibility for their actions.
Following the latest episode, Khan took to Instagram to reflect on where Zamil went wrong and draw attention to behaviour he said he had witnessed in real life. “Zamil is Zalim” he wrote, adding a red flag emoji.
Khan explained that beyond the story being told through the drama, he wanted to address the behaviour of some men towards women.
“Growing up, I have seen boys objectifying girls, getting into relationships, playing with their feelings and then feeling proud about it, while their friends cheer them on,” Khan said.
His comments came after the latest episode, in which Durefishan’s character, Zaryab, was betrayed by her longtime fiancé. After years together, Zamil decided that he wanted someone more religious and secretly married someone else in Pakistan.
Reflecting on the storyline, Khan shared a direct message for men.
“My message to all the boys: stop this nonsense! Your desire to be known as a hero or playboy can become someone else’s trauma. Hurting a girl and breaking her trust is nothing to be proud of,” he wrote.
He concluded his message with three simple reminders: “Be respectful. Be honest. Be a better man.”
Khan’s post was praised by fans, who appreciated the contrast between the actor’s personal message and the flaws of his character on screen.
One fan wrote that the message was “better than Zamil”, describing it as a reminder that “character, accountability and respect matter far beyond the screen”.
They added that turning a character’s flaws into a meaningful conversation about how men should treat women was powerful.
Other fans also filled the comments with reactions to Khan’s post, with one writing, “Zamil, you nailed the caption,” while another joked, “Zamil in a parallel universe.”
Another viewer commented that “this drama triggers the wounds of many”, reflecting how the storyline has resonated emotionally with audiences.
As Dar-e-Nijaat moved deeper into its second half, Zamil and Zaryab’s relationship reached a major turning point, with the latest episodes shifting the story towards the consequences of Zamil’s choices. title: Jennifer Garner nearly reunited with ex Ben Affleck in  Animals
description: Ben Affleck reveals Jennifer Garner was nearly cast as his wife in Animals before Kerry Washington joined the film
content:
Ben Affleck reveals Jennifer Garner was nearly cast as his wife in Animals before Kerry Washington joined the film
Ben Affleck has revealed that his ex-wife, Jennifer Garner, was initially considered to play his character’s wife in his upcoming Netflix thriller Animals .
Affleck, who directed, co-wrote and stars in the film, told Entertainment Weekly that he initially thought Garner would be a strong choice for the role of Abigail. He also noted that working together could have allowed the former couple to coordinate their schedules around their children.
“I thought, God, Jen Garner would be amazing for this role,” Affleck said.
The actor and filmmaker eventually decided against the casting after taking over the lead role of Mark Kimball. Affleck said Garner had concerns about the “baggage” audiences might bring to seeing the former couple portray husband and wife on screen.
Affleck said he remains close to Garner and would be interested in working with her in the future. The pair were married from 2005 to 2018 and share three children.
The production also underwent other casting changes. Affleck initially planned to have his longtime friend Matt Damon play Mark, but Damon became unavailable while working on Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey . Affleck subsequently decided to take on the role himself.
Kerry Washington was ultimately cast as Abigail after Affleck got to know her during the 2023 Hollywood strikes. He said her combination of professionalism and warmth made her a strong fit for the character.
Animals follows Mark Kimball, a Los Angeles mayoral candidate whose son is kidnapped. He and Abigail are forced to find the ransom money while navigating the dangerous situation.
Co-written by Affleck, Connor O. McIntyre and Billy Ray, Animals is scheduled to premiere on Netflix on October 9.

title: Frankie Muniz spends time with wife and son after hitting    rock bottom
description: Frankie Muniz shares family photo with estranged wife Paige Price and son Mauz after discussing struggles
content:
Frankie Muniz shares family photo with estranged wife Paige Price and son Mauz after discussing struggles
Frankie Muniz has shared a family photo with his estranged wife Paige Price and their son Mauz, following his recent social media post about reaching “rock bottom” during a difficult period.
The Malcolm in the Middle star shared a selfie on Instagram on Saturday showing himself with five-year-old Mauz and Price.
Muniz captioned the photo: “Post soccer shenanigans with the fam. Our little dude got a medal for excellence in sportsmanship.”
The family reunion comes after Muniz, who is also a professional stock car racing driver, discussed his recent struggles in a lengthy statement shared on social media on Friday.
“The last 6 weeks of my life have been a nightmare I'm praying to wake up from. Everything felt heavy, unclear, and like it was falling apart at the same time. I wouldn't wish this season on anyone,” Muniz wrote.
He said the experience had also given him an opportunity for self-reflection.
“The unexpected gift in the middle of it is that I've had nowhere to hide. I've had time to sit with myself, do real self-reflection, and finally see the areas of my life that need work if I want to become a better version of me. Not the polished version I show the world...the actual one,” he continued.
Muniz said he believed he would eventually look back on the period differently, adding: “In five years I believe I'll look back at this exact low point and feel grateful for it, because the high I'll be standing on then only exists because I went through this.”
He ended his statement by writing: “This isn't the end of the story. It's the part where I start doing the work...the uncomfortable, unglamorous, necessary work. I'm choosing to treat this season as the foundation, not the finish line.”
Muniz and Price announced their separation in July after 10 years together. The couple eloped in October 2019 before holding a formal wedding ceremony in February 2020. They welcomed Mauz in 2021.
In July, Muniz also wrote: “Man, I hate saying goodbye to my son. You'd think I'd be used to it by now, but it just gets harder and harder. Trusting in God to help get through this not so fun patch while trying to be fun for him.”

title: Sylvester Stallone says he turned down Trump   s Hollywood ambassador role because it was    impossible
description: Trump announced Stallone  Mel Gibson and Jon Voight as special ambassadors to Hollywood in January 2025
content:
Trump announced Stallone, Mel Gibson and Jon Voight as special ambassadors to Hollywood in January 2025
Sylvester Stallone has revealed that he turned down the role of special ambassador to Hollywood offered to him by Donald Trump, saying the position proved impossible to carry out.
Trump announced Stallone, Mel Gibson and Jon Voight as special ambassadors to Hollywood in January 2025, describing them as advisers who would help bring film production and business back to the US.
Nearly two years after the announcement, Stallone said he ultimately decided not to take on the role. According to Variety, he explained that the position did not come with a clear or workable way to accomplish what was expected.
“I said thank you and ciao,” Stallone said, describing his response after deciding the assignment was “impossible”.
The actor had initially been named alongside Gibson and Voight as part of Trump's effort to address Hollywood's decline in domestic production and the industry's growing reliance on filming overseas. Trump said the three actors would serve as his “eyes and ears” and bring him suggestions for revitalising the entertainment business.
The appointment was never a formal government ambassador position with clearly defined statutory powers. The trio were instead presented as special envoys and advisers to the president on Hollywood-related issues.
While Stallone has now distanced himself from the assignment, Voight has remained involved in efforts connected to Trump's Hollywood agenda. In 2025, Voight and producer Steven Paul submitted a plan to the administration proposing measures intended to support the US film industry.
Stallone's comments clarify that although he accepted Trump's announcement publicly at the time, he ultimately concluded that the role itself was not workable.

title: Diana   s    Revenge Dress    goes on display ahead of Sotheby   s auction
description: Princess Diana   s    Revenge Dress    is on display at Sotheby   s ahead of its December auction
content:
Princess Diana’s ‘Revenge Dress’ is on display at Sotheby’s ahead of its December auction
Princess Diana’s iconic ‘Revenge Dress’ has gone on public display at Sotheby’s in London ahead of its upcoming auction, while her brother Earl Spencer prepares to release a memoir containing allegations about the days following her death.
The black silk evening gown, designed by Christina Stambolian, is being displayed at Sotheby’s Bond Street location from September 18 to September 24.
It will later travel to Hong Kong and Geneva before arriving in New York on December 2.
The dress will remain on public display at Sotheby’s Breuer Building until December 8 before going under the hammer on December 9. It is expected to sell for up to $300,000.
Diana wore the strapless gown to a Vanity Fair fundraising dinner at the Serpentine Gallery in London on June 29, 1994. She wore it hours after then-Prince Charles admitted to adultery during their marriage.
The dress was previously auctioned in 1997 as part of a sale of 79 of Diana’s dresses, with proceeds raised for cancer- and AIDS-related charities.
Sotheby’s Global Head of Handbags and Fashion Morgane Halmi said, “What makes this dress extraordinary is not merely that it was worn by the princess, nor that its appearance at the Serpentine event made headlines around the world. It is what it communicated.”
Earl Spencer’s memoir, Swan Song: Diana, My Sister , is due for release on September 22. Spencer alleges that King Charles III reacted to Diana’s death by saying, “Rest assured, we'll forget her soon enough.”
Buckingham Palace disputed the account, saying, “While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss.”
Spencer rejected the statement, telling the BBC, “Those are exactly the words he said. I've only ever had two calls on the line with Prince Charles. I was hyper alert to what he was saying, and those are precisely the words that he said.”

Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Sunday said making the province clean and green and ensuring a healthy population was the government’s top priority.

She stressed that keeping the environment clean was essential for protecting the planet and preventing diseases, adding that a clean environment guaranteed a better quality of life.

title: Initial probe reveals terrorists planned prolonged siege in Kohat Police Lines attack
description: Use of drone technology  timely response by the police plays a crucial role in monitoring the terrorists  movements
content:
Use of drone technology, timely response by the police plays a crucial role in monitoring the terrorists' movements
Significant revelations emerged on Sunday from the initial investigation into the terrorist attack on the Kohat Police Lines. According to the investigation team, the attackers did not limit themselves to a mere suicide bombing and had planned to enter the Police Lines and maintain a siege of the compound for several hours.
On Friday, at least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred when an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines, followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities.
Sources indicate that the terrorists brought hand grenades, sniper rifles, and other weaponry and explosives with them. After entering various sections of the Police Lines during the attack, the terrorists opened fire and used hand grenades. The FIR registered by the police also documented the use of gunfire and hand grenades during the assault.
Read : CTD registers terror case over deadly Kohat Police Lines attack
Investigative officials stated that the attack began when an explosives-laden, rickshaw-style vehicle was rammed near the Police Lines, causing a massive blast. Immediately following the explosion, armed terrorists entered the Police Lines and advanced toward key buildings. According to the police, seven armed terrorists, including a sniper, entered the compound after the initial attack.
According to the investigation team, the terrorists intended to scatter the police force following the initial explosions and gunfire, aiming to remain inside the compound for as long as possible. However, police personnel maintained their resistance despite sustaining injuries and facing heavy fire, thereby preventing the attackers from advancing according to their plan.
Speaking to The Express Tribune , a senior police officer stated that the use of drone technology and the timely response by police and other forces played a crucial role in monitoring the terrorists' movements and conducting the operation. He noted that the forces quickly brought the situation under control and prevented the terrorists from spreading further.
Officials reported a prolonged standoff after the terrorists entered the Police Lines buildings. A joint clearance operation involving the police, Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD), Elite Force, and other security forces lasted approximately 20 to 21 hours. By the end of the operation, eight terrorists had been killed.
Read More : Kohat Police Lines blast death toll rises to 23 as clearance operation concludes
The initial attack resulted in the deaths of 21 people, including 15 police personnel, and left over 100 others injured. Additional casualties were reported during the subsequent clearance operation, bringing the total death toll to 23, according to the latest official figures.
Police officials state that a comprehensive investigation into the attack was underway, with all aspects, including terrorist facilitators, the planning of the attack, the supply of weapons and explosives, and potential links, being examined.
Earlier today, a case was registered with the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) police station over the suicide attack on the old Police Lines in Kohat, police said.
The FIR was registered on the complaint of the Station House Officer (SHO) of City Police Station Kohat against unidentified terrorists. The case includes charges related to terrorism, murder, attempted murder and other offences.
Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers. Islamabad has repeatedly asked the Taliban regime to deny the use of Afghan soil for terrorist attacks inside Pakistan. However, the de facto rulers in Kabul have been reluctant to take action against terrorist groups operating from their territory.

Sorkin also addressed the film’s legal review, saying Sony hired an outside law firm to verify factual claims because the movie is based on real events. He said representatives for Meta had contacted the studio seeking tickets to the film.

title: Looksmaxxing  vibe coding and cuffing season among 1 400 new Merriam Webster dictionary entries
description: Merriam Webster said the additions reflect words and meanings that have demonstrated widespread use over time
content:
Merriam-Webster said the additions reflect words and meanings that have demonstrated widespread use over time
Merriam-Webster has added 1,400 new words and definitions to its dictionary, bringing a range of internet slang, technology terms and cultural phrases into its pages.
The new additions include “looksmaxxing”, a term associated with efforts to maximise physical attractiveness, alongside “parasocial”, “Rickroll” and “meme coin”. Other internet and cultural terms added include “glow-up”, “Mandela Effect”, “cuffing season”, “Sunday scaries” and “crashout”.
Technology has also influenced the latest update, with “vibe coding”, “AGI”, or artificial general intelligence, “compute” as a noun and “uncanny valley” among the new entries.
Food and lifestyle terms have also made the dictionary, including “superfood”, “cake pop”, “shishito”, “bao” and “chilli crisp”. “Yacht rock”, “neckbeard” and “shapewear” are also among the newly added words and definitions.
Merriam-Webster said the additions reflect words and meanings that have demonstrated widespread use over time. Its editors research how frequently terms are used and whether their meanings are broadly understood before adding them.
The dictionary publisher noted that a word does not make the cut simply because it becomes temporarily popular. Instead, it needs to demonstrate sustained usage across industries or regions, meaning an average adult is likely to encounter it and need to understand its meaning.
The latest additions arrive ahead of Merriam-Webster’s expected announcement of its 2026 Word of the Year. Last year, the publisher selected “slop”, referring to low-quality digital content produced, usually in quantity, using artificial intelligence.

title: Backrooms storms past  400 million at the global box office
description: Backrooms surpasses  400 million globally  becoming A24   s highest grossing film after a strong theatrical run
content:
Backrooms surpasses $400 million globally, becoming A24’s highest-grossing film after a strong theatrical run
Backrooms has surpassed $400 million at the global box office, marking a major milestone for the low-budget horror film and A24.
After nearly four months in cinemas, the movie has earned $197.5 million in North America and $202.57 million internationally, bringing its worldwide total to $400.07 million. The film was reportedly produced on a $10 million budget.
Directed by YouTuber Kane Parsons, Backrooms has become A24’s highest-grossing release to date. It has also emerged as one of the year’s most profitable films, exceeding the previous studio record held by Marty Supreme , which earned $192 million worldwide.
The movie’s commercial success has been driven by strong word of mouth and interest among younger audiences. Its performance has also highlighted the growing influence of online creators in theatrical filmmaking.
Backrooms contributed to A24’s strongest summer at the box office, with the distributor finishing the season ahead of Paramount and Warner Bros. in market share. The film also set an A24 record for its opening weekend, earning $81 million domestically and $118 million worldwide.
Parsons, who was 20 when the film topped the box office, also became the youngest filmmaker to direct a movie that opened at No. 1.
Internationally, China was the film’s biggest market outside the US and Canada, generating $27.8 million, followed by Mexico with $17.8 million and the UK with $17.6 million.
Based on Parsons’ web series about eerie liminal spaces, Backrooms stars Chiwetel Ejiofor, Renate Reinsve and Mark Duplass. A sequel has not been confirmed, although Parsons has expressed interest in developing the story into a film franchise.

title: Carrot Top spoke about loving his life in Las Vegas one year before suicide attempt
description: Carrot Top said the change helped him realise the physical toll that life on the road had taken
content:
Carrot Top said the change helped him realise the physical toll that life on the road had taken
Carrot Top spoke about how much he enjoyed his life in Las Vegas roughly a year before he was hospitalised following a reported suicide attempt.
The comedian, whose real name is Scott Christopher Thompson, had previously opened up about the benefits of settling in Las Vegas after years of travelling for work. He described being at home as having “giant advantages” and said the change helped him realise the physical toll that life on the road had taken.
“You don’t realize, like, how much you’re destroying your body until you stop doing it,” Thompson said, reflecting on the difference between touring and having a more settled routine.
At the time, Thompson said he had little desire to return to the constant demands of touring, instead enjoying a slower and more ordinary routine in Las Vegas. His comments have resurfaced following his hospitalisation on Friday, September 18.
Thompson was taken to a Las Vegas-area hospital after a reported suicide attempt, according to multiple reports. His representative later confirmed that he was recovering in hospital and receiving care and support, while asking for privacy on behalf of his family and those closest to him.

title: Trump says he will appoint a new AI adviser  without providing details
description: Washington lawmakers fear AI risks  while Trump has downplayed concerns and opposed additional regulation
content:
Washington lawmakers fear AI risks, while Trump has downplayed concerns and opposed additional regulation
US President Donald Trump said in a social media post on Saturday that he plans to appoint ​a new artificial intelligence adviser, known as an "AI czar," and create an "AI force," though ‌he did not provide details about either initiative or how they would be implemented.
Fears are growing in Washington among lawmakers about the risks posed by AI technology on humans and property. Earlier this month, former Anthropic researcher ​Jacob Coxon said that "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all ​by the end of the decade." Trump has repeatedly downplayed concerns about AI and ⁠argued that additional regulation is unnecessary.
"We will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth ​of this incredible Industry," Trump wrote on Truth Social, his social media platform. "Rather, we will cherish it, ​help it, and watch over it, as it grows! However, we will also be looking for BAD, and we can do that, very easily, with our already existing Criminal and Civil Justice System."
If Trump follows through on ​the pledge, it would be his second AI czar. Venture capitalist David Sacks previously served in ​the role before stepping down in the spring and moving into an external advisory position.
Read More: US Treasury's Bessent, China's He to launch talks on AI, trade, critical minerals
Sacks has echoed Trump's scepticism of ‌new ⁠AI regulation. Speaking at a Politico event on Wednesday, he said AI developers should be responsible for ensuring the safety of their products and could be held liable if problems arise, adding that new federal rules are unnecessary.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on ​Trump's post.
Trump's post comes ​ahead of his scheduled ⁠meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday. Washington and Beijing are competing for leadership in artificial intelligence, which both governments view as vital ​to their economic and military strength.
Trump and technology executives have argued ​that excessive regulation ⁠would slow US AI development and undermine American companies' ability to compete with Chinese rivals, a claim that safety advocates often refute.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will meet with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng ⁠on ​Sunday at JPMorgan Chase headquarters in New York to discuss ​AI security, trade and other economic issues, a person familiar with the planning said on Saturday.

Says sanitisation operations underway in the surrounding areas to clear any remaining terrorists
Two officers were among six security personnel martyred while eight terrorists were killed in an exchange of fire in Hangu district, the military’s media wing said on Sunday.
According to a statement from the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), an exchange of fire took place between a security forces convoy and terrorists in Hangu district on Sept 20.
“Eight Khwarij belonging to Indian-sponsored Fitna-al-Khwarij were killed due to effective engagement by own troops,” it said.
Fitna Al-Khawarij is the state-designated term for the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
However, during the intense exchange of fire, two officers leading their troops from the front also lost their lives along with four other personnel, the ISPR said.

The officers were identified as Captain Abuzar Farooq, 23, a resident of Gujranwala district, and Lieutenant Sheraz Babar, 22, a resident of Chakwal district.
The ISPR said the officers “fought gallantly and paid the ultimate sacrifice and embraced shahadat” along with their four men.
The statement said sanitisation operations were underway in the surrounding areas to clear any remaining terrorists and ensure the security of local residents and vital national highways, adding that the counterterrorism campaign under the government-approved “ Azm-e-Istehkam ” framework would continue with full resolve.
“Security forces and law enforcement agencies remain committed to eliminating the menace of foreign-sponsored and foreign-supported terrorism from the country,” the statement said, adding that the sacrifices of the country’s brave soldiers further reinforce our unwavering commitment to safeguarding our nation at all costs.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi paid tribute to the six security personnel, including Captain Farooq and Lieutenant Babar, who embraced martyrdom while bravely confronting the terrorists in Hangu.
Paying tribute to the “great sacrifice” of officers and the four other personnel, the minister said the martyrs had bravely confronted the terrorists of Fitna-al-Khawarij and killed eight terrorists.
“The martyrs are the pride of the nation and their eternal sacrifices will always be remembered,” Naqvi said, adding that the nation can never repay the debt owed to the great sacrifices of the martyrs.

“Security forces have rendered eternal and unprecedented sacrifices for the sake of peace and security in the country,” Shah said.
He said the great sacrifices of the security forces would always be remembered.
“The martyrs are the pride of the nation and the crown on our heads,” he said while praying for the high ranks of the martyrs.
Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022.

title: Big cats continue to appear at fairs despite tighter restrictions
description: Amendments made to the law in 2025 introduced stricter conditions for keeping lions  tigers  pumas and jaguars
content:
Amendments made to the law in 2025 introduced stricter conditions for keeping lions, tigers, pumas and jaguars
Despite stricter restrictions on keeping lions, tigers and other dangerous wild animals in urban areas and using them for public display, big cats continue to be seen at fairs and circuses across Punjab, raising questions about enforcement and oversight of wildlife laws.
Videos recently surfaced from a fair in Chawinda, Pasrur tehsil of Sialkot district, showing lions performing tricks during a Lucky Irani Circus show. The videos show the animals being made to perform various acts in front of an audience. Reports of Lucky Irani Circus shows have also emerged in recent weeks from Kanganpur, Burewala, Sargodha and other cities.
Under Punjab’s wildlife laws, keeping wild animals, transporting them and displaying them to the public require prescribed permissions and compliance with specific conditions. Amendments made to the law in 2025 introduced stricter conditions for keeping big cats, including lions, tigers, pumas and jaguars. The law also prohibits keeping wild animals at locations where their safety or that of the public may be at risk.
Legal action can also be taken against those who subject animals to cruelty, keep them in unsuitable conditions or use them in ways that endanger their welfare. Some violations can carry fines of up to Rs5 million and imprisonment of up to seven years.
Last year, after a lion escaped into a residential area in Lahore and injured a woman and children, Punjab authorities launched a major crackdown on privately kept big cats. Wildlife Rangers Punjab carried out operations in Lahore, Jhelum, Multan, Gujranwala, Sialkot and other cities, taking dozens of lions and tigers into custody.
Several of these cases subsequently reached the courts. In some instances, animals were returned to their owners on the basis of court orders and affidavits, subject to conditions that they be kept at registered breeding farms and not brought into urban areas. A number of cases remain pending before the courts.
Read More: Punjab home to 587 privately owned big cats
Deputy Chief Wildlife Ranger Punjab Asim Bilal said action against people keeping wild animals illegally was continuing. He said Lucky Irani Circus and other individuals and organisations had previously faced challans, seizure of animals and criminal cases. He added that further amendments had been proposed to make the conditions for keeping wild animals stricter and had been sent to the provincial cabinet for approval.
Badr Munir, a member of the Punjab Captive Wildlife Management Committee and a wildlife expert, said lions experience stress when exposed to noise, crowds and bright lights or when repeatedly transported from one place to another. "Even a minor failure in safety arrangements could lead to an accident. The risk is particularly high for children attending fairs," said Munir.
Ayeza Haider, focal person for the Pakistan Animal Rights Activist Group (PARAG), questioned under what legal permission big cats were being publicly displayed at fairs and circuses if authorities were taking strict action against their private ownership and presence in urban areas.
Besides Lucky Irani Circus, Dhoom, Great Pakistani Circus and Janbaz Circus are also operating in Punjab. Lucky Irani Circus and Great Pakistani Circus have previously advertised the display of lions and other wild animals on social media.
The continued use of big cats in public performances highlights a gap between the restrictions contained in Punjab’s wildlife laws and their implementation on the ground. While authorities say enforcement action is continuing, wildlife experts and animal rights activists are calling for consistent application of the rules governing the keeping, transport and public display of dangerous wild animals.

Barrera was fired from Scream 7 after Spyglass said her social media posts crossed its policy regarding antisemitism
Melissa Barrera has praised the support Macklemore received from fellow artists after he was removed from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour, saying the reaction made her emotional because she did not receive the same solidarity when she was fired from the Scream franchise.
Speaking to the Associated Press, Barrera reflected on the response to Macklemore after the rapper was dropped from Sheeran’s remaining US tour dates following his public comments supporting Palestine.
“It made me emotional, you know,” Barrera said. “I didn’t get that when it happened to me. I didn’t have any of that happen. It was too soon. People were too scared. But it’s good to see that almost three years later, at least things have changed.”
Barrera was fired from Scream 7 in 2023 after Spyglass said her social media posts crossed its stated “zero tolerance” policy regarding antisemitism and hate speech. Barrera had posted about the war in Gaza and expressed support for Palestinians. Spyglass denied that her support for Palestinians itself was the reason for her departure, while the company said at the time that it had “zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate in any form”.
Macklemore was removed from Sheeran’s tour after making pro-Palestinian comments during his performances at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey earlier this month. Sheeran later said the decision was made by the tour’s promoter after venues indicated they would not host shows with Macklemore on the lineup.
Several other artists subsequently withdrew from the remaining Loop Tour dates, including Finneas, Lukas Graham, Aaron Rowe and Beoga. Macklemore has also announced that he will donate $1 million in net earnings from the tour to organisations supporting Palestinians.
Barrera’s comments come as she continues to discuss her departure from Scream and the response to Macklemore’s situation, which she described as evidence that the reaction from artists and audiences has changed in the years since her own exit.

Matt Kalil plans to appeal after judge dismissed his lawsuit against ex-wife Haley Baylee over intimacy comments
Former NFL player Matt Kalil plans to appeal after a judge dismissed his lawsuit against his ex-wife, Haley Baylee, over comments she made about their marriage and sex life.
“We are not going to comment at this time other than to say we intend to appeal this decision,” Kalil’s attorney, Ryan Saba of Rosen Saba LLP, told Page Six.
A judge ruled on Thursday that Baylee’s comments were protected because she was discussing her own life, marriage and divorce, which the court found to be matters of legitimate public concern.
Baylee, 34, said she was “so relieved this is over” in a statement to TMZ and expressed hope that the ruling would encourage women to speak openly about their experiences.
Her attorney, Matthew Bialick, said they were “very pleased” that the court dismissed every count against her.
The legal dispute began after Baylee discussed her nearly seven-year marriage to Kalil, 37, during a November 2025 livestream with internet personality Marlon Garcia.
During the conversation, she spoke about their sex life and claimed intercourse with her then-husband would leave her “in tears”.
Baylee also compared Kalil’s penis to “two Coke cans, maybe even a third” and claimed it was “like .01 percent of the population.”
“We’ve tried, impossible unless you’re going to be in tears,” she continued.
Kalil filed the lawsuit in January, accusing Baylee of invasion of privacy and unjust enrichment. He alleged that her comments led to widespread ridicule and unwanted attention for him and his family.
He also claimed Baylee financially benefited from renewed attention surrounding the livestream and said his new wife, Keilani Asmus, received disturbing messages.
Baylee asked the court to dismiss the case, arguing that her comments were part of a truthful, autobiographical account of her own marriage and experiences.
Kalil’s legal team argued that she had no right to disclose private marital and sexual details publicly for financial gain.

Italy's central Mediterranean location makes it highly exposed to migrant arrivals, challenging governments
Italy is preparing to ban face coverings in schools and to cap the number of foreign students per class, Prime Minister Giorgia ​Meloni said on Sunday as she played up her right-wing ‌credentials at a youth event organised by her party.
Italy is among the European countries most exposed to migrant arrivals because of its central Mediterranean location, making migration a ​hot-button issue and a major challenge for successive governments.
The integration of ​migrants, particularly those from Muslim-majority countries, remains contentious in Italian politics ⁠and society. Debates over religious symbols, cultural integration, citizenship rules and ​immigration policy frequently polarise public opinion.
"A measure will soon be presented to a ​Cabinet meeting to legally establish a maximum number of foreign students per class. It also requires parents of foreign students facing serious difficulties integrating into the school system to ​learn Italian and bans burqas and niqabs in schools," Meloni told an ​annual gathering of the youth wing of her Brothers of Italy party.
Read More: Mosque vandalised with swastikas, hate messages in Belgium
"If there is ‌only ⁠one child in a class who doesn't understand Italian, that child will likely be able to learn the language and integrate quickly with the help of classmates and teachers. However, if the number of children who don't understand ​the language becomes ​large - or even ⁠the majority - that is no longer integration; it is neglect," she added.
Meloni did not specify what the maximum number ​of foreign students per class would be.
Students who are ​not Italian ⁠citizens account for 11.6% of those enrolled in Italian schools — nearly 12 in every 100 students — according to Fondazione ISMU, a research institution.
"You must go to ⁠school ​with your face uncovered, and in Italy ​no one, in the name of a real or supposed tradition, can decide that a young ​woman must hide herself, " Meloni said.

title: Doctor  wife and three children found dead in Karachi s Ahsanabad
description: Police say bodies are four to five days old  investigators suspect that deaths could be case of collective suicide
content:
Police say bodies are four to five days old, investigators suspect that deaths could be case of collective suicide
The bodies of five members of the same family were recovered from a flat in Karachi's Ahsanabad area on Sunday, with police claiming that the bodies were several days old.
The deceased included a doctor, his wife and their three children. The husband was identified as Dr Umar.
According to police, the bodies were four to five days old and had badly decomposed. Residents of the building informed police after noticing a foul smell coming from the locked flat. Police subsequently broke open the door, which was locked from the inside.
The bodies of Dr Umar and his wife were recovered from one room, while the bodies of their three children were found in another room. The body of one child was found on a bed, while the other two were found on a mattress.
All five appeared to be lying in positions suggesting that they had been sleeping normally. Police found no apparent signs of resistance, violence, theft or robbery inside the flat.
Police have therefore raised the possibility that Dr Umar and his family might have died after ingesting some form of poison. Investigators also suspect that the deaths could be a case of collective suicide. However, the exact cause of death would only be determined after chemical examination.
The bodies were shifted to a hospital for post-mortem examinations. Doctors withheld the post-mortem report until the chemical examination report was received, after which the final cause of death would be established.
Based on statements from neighbours, police learned that Dr Umar and his family had good relations with those living in the area and were known for helping others. However, Dr Umar had reportedly been ill for some time and had been diagnosed with cancer. Following the diagnosis, he left his hospital job and was planning to move to Bahawalpur, Punjab.
According to preliminary police investigation, Dr Umar's wife had attempted to sell their oven for Rs10,000 last week, but a neighbour did not buy it and instead provided financial assistance of Rs2,000.
Police said they contacted Dr Umar’s brother in Bahawalpur and informed him about the incident. However, the brother reportedly expressed his estrangement from Dr Umar. Police were now searching for the deceased's family’s relatives living in Karachi.
Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah expressed grief over the deaths of five individuals and sought a report from the Inspector General (IG) of Police.
Shah said that a complete and transparent investigation into the incident must be conducted and all aspects of the incident examined, adding that the culprit must be brought to justice and face the strictest legal action.
Meanwhile, Sindh Home Minister Zia-ul-Hassan Lanjar sought details of the incident, instructing Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) East to immediately provide a briefing on all initial police actions taken.
Lanjar said that the investigation and inquiry into the incident must bring the final facts to light, adding that the underlying factors and motives behind the incident must be determined by taking into account the eyewitness accounts and circumstantial evidence gathered from the scene.
The minister said that SSP East should ensure the investigation was effective and well-coordinated under his personal supervision, further instructing SSP East to update him on the investigation and progress of the case on a real-time basis.

Washington and Tehran reached an agreement in June providing for a halt to military operations and arrangements to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to navigation.

description: Wai Khin Hnin wins 10 12  12 8  12 9 against Indonesia   s Sumaya
content:
Wai Khin Hnin wins 10-12, 12-8, 12-9 against Indonesia’s Sumaya
Myanmar's Wai Khin Hnin on Sunday became the first Asian Games gold medallist in teqball, an acrobatic football-table tennis hybrid making its debut at this year's event in Japan.
Watched by Barcelona and Spain football legend Carles Puyol, Wai Khin Hnin beat Indonesia's Sumaya, who goes by one name, 2-1 in the final to capture the inaugural women's singles title.
Teqball was invented 14 years ago in a garage in Hungary and features players kicking a ball over a curved table, incorporating elements of the southeast Asian sport sepak takraw.
The sport has grown quickly and featured at the 2023 European Games.
Wai Khin Hnin lost the first set of the final but came back to win 10-12, 12-8, 12-9 and claim gold.
"I'm delighted, I'm thankful to my head coach for believing in me and selecting me to play in the women's singles. I believed that I could do it," she said.
"My next goal is to win the gold medal for Myanmar at the 2027 SEA Games."
The competition has seen a diverse range of players vying to become the Asian Games' first teqball medallists.
The Philippines men's team featured three 14-year-olds including Prince Agustin, who lost in the singles bronze-medal match.
Japan were represented by Takahiro Nodomi, who also works as a comedian.
"I played football until high school, gave up, started teqball in my late 30s, and made it to this big stage at 40," he said.
"If the message that 'even old guys can work hard' reached everyone, then I feel I was able to release some 'old guy power'."
Indonesia's Husni Uba represented his country in sepak takraw at four previous Asian Games.
"After I was done with the sepak takraw competition at the 2018 Asian Games I didn't expect to be back again, especially for teqball," said the 44-year-old.

title: Comedians rally around Carrot Top following hospitalisation
description: Dane Cook  Brad Garrett and Jeff Ross were among those who publicly reached out to Carrot Top after hospitalisation
content:
Dane Cook, Brad Garrett and Jeff Ross were among those who publicly reached out to Carrot Top after hospitalisation
Several comedians and entertainers have shared messages of support for Carrot Top following the comedian’s hospitalisation in Las Vegas.
Dane Cook, Brad Garrett and Jeff Ross were among those who publicly reached out to Carrot Top, whose real name is Scott Thompson, after he was hospitalised on Friday. His representative confirmed that the 61-year-old comedian is recovering and receiving care and support.
Cook shared a video message on Instagram, describing Thompson as an “outstanding human being” and praising his talent and contributions to the comedy community. He wished his fellow comedian a “beautiful recovery” and said he hoped to see him return to performing.
Garrett also posted a message alongside a photograph of himself with Thompson and Ray Romano. He called Carrot Top a “beautiful, talented friend” and said they were all grateful that he was recovering, adding that he wanted Thompson to remember how appreciated he is.
Ross shared a photograph with Thompson and asked people who care about the comedian to leave messages of support in the comments. The post attracted thousands of likes and comments.
Debbie Gibson also shared a message, encouraging people to check on their friends, particularly those who regularly bring joy to others. Actress Erin Murphy similarly sent Thompson “thoughts, prayers and healing wishes”, reminding her followers that people may be dealing with struggles others cannot see.
Thompson’s representative, Jami Schlicher, previously said that he is recovering in hospital and that his family and those closest to him are grateful for the concern and prayers, while asking for privacy. His Friday and Saturday performances at the Luxor in Las Vegas were cancelled following his hospitalisation.
Carrot Top has been a longtime Las Vegas performer, with his residency at the Luxor becoming one of the city’s longest-running comedy shows. He has not publicly commented on his hospitalisation.

title: Iran secure Asian Games basketball bronze
description: They hold off China 79 70 to claim the men   s bronze after a hard fought campaign
content:
They hold off China 79-70 to claim the men’s bronze after a hard-fought campaign
Iran withstood a late fightback to beat China 79-70 and win Asian Games men's basketball bronze on Sunday, an achievement that left their players "speechless" after months of war back home.
China led 31-29 at half-time in Nagoya, but Iran took charge in the third quarter to lead 55-46 going into the fourth and held on to spark wild celebrations and an emotional place on the podium.
"To be honest with you I'm just speechless," said 202cm (6ft 8in) power forward Arsalan Kazemi, who in 2013 was the first Iranian to be drafted in the NBA by the Washington Wizards, but never made a regular season appearance.
"The pressure that we had on us is just out of this world," he added.
"Not a lot of athletes can say that, with the way that it has been since almost six months ago, what we have been through, what our families have been through.
"I just congratulate the people of Iran because they deserve much better.
"And I think my teammates and I put our hearts out on the court today just to get this win and make them happy."
Teammate Arman Zangeneh said the squad had been through a lot but it was worth it.
"If you get the medal at the Asian Games you don't need to go to the army any more, so it's huge for some players," said the 203cm tall forward.
"We had a very tough two months. We went to the Philippines to play the qualifiers, then immediately we came here.
"It was really difficult. And living in a container, with the food and everything, it was hard, very hard.
"At the end, we get to the point that we go home with a medal, and it means a lot."

title: Nadeem   s treble gives Pakistan a blistering start
description: Striker   s hat trick helps Green shirts demolish Thailand 9 0 in Pool B opener
content:
Striker’s hat-trick helps Green-shirts demolish Thailand 9-0 in Pool B opener
Pakistan opened their Pool B campaign with a commanding 9-0 victory over Thailand at Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium on Sunday, scoring in every quarter to underline their dominance.
Pakistan led 2-0 after the first quarter before adding three goals in the second to take a 5-0 advantage into halftime. They continued to control the contest after the break, scoring twice in the third quarter and twice more in the final period.
Ahmad Nadeem was Pakistan's leading scorer with three field goals, finding the net in the 20th, 37th and 43rd minutes. Sufyan Khan added two goals from penalty corners, while Moin Shakeel, Ammad Butt, Waheed Rana and Abdul Shahid each scored once.
Pakistan enjoyed 57 percent possession and earned seven penalty corners to Thailand's two, according to the match statistics. Thailand failed to register a goal during the 60-minute contest.
Shakeel opened the scoring in the eighth minute before Butt doubled Pakistan's lead four minutes later. Nadeem then scored from open play in the 20th minute, followed by two penalty-corner conversions from Khan in the 22nd and 23rd minutes.
Rana struck in the 31st minute and Shahid added another three minutes later as Pakistan extended their lead to 7-0. Nadeem completed his hat-trick in the 43rd minute before Pakistan added their ninth goal later in the match.
Nadeem converted three of his four attempts, while Shakeel and Butt were both clinical with one goal from one attempt. Khan scored twice from six attempts.
Pakistan next face Uzbekistan on September 22, while Thailand meet China later the same.

title: The Last of Us director apologises to God of War Laufey developers for comments
description: Last of Us director Bruce Straley apologises after using God of War Laufey to discuss AAA game innovation
content:
Last of Us director Bruce Straley apologises after using God of War Laufey to discuss AAA game innovation
The Last of Us and Uncharted 4 director Bruce Straley has apologised to the developers of God of War Laufey after using the upcoming PlayStation 5 game as an example while discussing a lack of innovation in triple-A games.
Straley praised the technical work on God of War Laufey during an interview with Edge , but said he was not excited by what players do in the game.
He later said mentioning the title was a mistake after his comments attracted attention online.
“God of War Laufey, I look at that game, and every pixel is mindblowing,” Straley said. “The amount of work and skill that’s gone into every single frame… I’ve made those kinds of games, and I’m still blown away.”
“But when I actually look at what you’re doing in the game? I’m not excited. And that’s nothing against the God of War team. Just, across the board in triple-A, it feels like there’s no opportunity to inject fresh, innovative ideas.”
Straley subsequently apologised directly to the Laufey team on X.
I want to apologize to the Laufey team for dragging you all into this uninvited & unnecessary negative attention. I was trying to illustrate an industry concern & my mistake of naming your game is being used out of context & for clickbait. You don’t need this. I’m sorry. 🧵 pic.twitter.com/Ri2KgfJ4yY
Straley then expanded on his concerns about the triple-A industry, saying he fears players are becoming tired of “playing the same verbs for the last 20 years.”
He cited Half-Life 2, Gears of War, BioShock, Uncharted 2 and The Last of Us as games that helped establish the “modern AAA” model while introducing different experiences at the time.
He also criticised attempts to recreate the success of Overwatch, Fortnite and Roblox, arguing that decisions at the top have limited developers’ ability to innovate.
Straley, who now runs Wildflower Interactive, ultimately acknowledged his example was misplaced.
“In trying to have a thoughtful conversation, I stuck my foot in my mouth & mentioned Laufey, and that was my mistake.”
God of War Laufey releases on February 16, 2027, for PlayStation 5.

title: Irish TD backs    half Irish    Macklemore after Ed Sheeran tour removal
description: Daly described the situation as    unfortunate  because Macklemore   s comments reflected views he has expressed publicly
content:
Daly described the situation as “unfortunate" because Macklemore’s comments reflected views he has expressed publicly
Sinn Féin TD Pa Daly has voiced his support for Macklemore after the rapper was removed from the US leg of Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour following comments supporting Palestine.
Speaking as the Dáil returned from its summer recess, Daly described the situation as “unfortunate”, particularly because Macklemore’s comments reflected views he had expressed publicly for several years.
“I support Macklemore on what he’s saying,” Daly said. “Of course, he’s half Irish as well, isn’t he? So we have skin in the game with him too.”
Macklemore, whose real name is Ben Haggerty, has previously spoken about his Irish heritage. After receiving a warm reception during a Dublin performance, he said his family history came from Ireland and described the experience as a “homecoming”.
The rapper was removed from the remaining US dates of Sheeran’s tour after saying “Free Palestine” during a concert at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. Macklemore later said Sheeran and his team had made the decision to remove him, while Sheeran said the decision had been made by the tour’s promoter.
The dispute has also prompted several artists to withdraw from the remaining tour dates. Irish acts Aaron Rowe and Beoga pulled out, while other supporting acts including Finneas and Lukas Graham also left the tour.
Daly’s comments came as Macklemore continued to receive support from Irish musicians, including CMAT, Hozier and Kneecap. Meanwhile, Macklemore has said he plans to donate $1 million from his earnings from the tour to organisations supporting Palestinians.

title: Macklemore honoured with Gaza mural following Ed Sheeran tour removal
description: Macklemore has been honoured with Gaza mural following removal from Ed Sheeran   s tour after speaking out for Palestine
content:
Macklemore has been honoured with Gaza mural following removal from Ed Sheeran’s tour after speaking out for Palestine
Macklemore has been honoured with a mural in Gaza City following his removal from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour after speaking about Palestine during a concert.
The mural was created by Gaza artists Anne Redwan and Qusai al-Helo. Painted on a cracked concrete slab surrounded by rubble, it depicts Macklemore wearing a Palestinian flag and raising his fist. A message beside the portrait reads, "Thank you for using your voice for Palestine."
The artwork follows Macklemore’s appearance on Sheeran’s tour, where he performed his song "Hind's Hall" while wearing a keffiyeh and called for a "Free Palestine".
His participation was subsequently removed from the remaining US dates of the tour after venue owners reportedly objected to his public statements about the conflict.
Macklemore also addressed Jewish concertgoers following criticism of his comments, saying, "Criticism of Israel…in no way is a criticism of you. My message is for peace; love for all human beings to be treated with dignity, respect, and equality."
Redwan told Reuters that the mural was intended to express gratitude towards the rapper.
"We wanted to send a message to thank rapper Macklemore in this simple way," she said.
"As an artist living under siege here in Gaza, we are waiting for support from anyone who can see the persecution we live under," Redwan added. "We can paint murals bigger than this to express our feelings."
Following his removal from Sheeran’s tour, Macklemore pledged $1 million in net earnings from the tour to six humanitarian aid organisations operating in Gaza.

title: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan on how South Asian representation is changing in Hollywood
description: Best of the Best  star reflects on authentic storytelling  cultural diversity and the pioneers who helped open doors
content:
'Best of the Best' star reflects on authentic storytelling, cultural diversity and the pioneers who helped open doors
Maitreyi Ramakrishnan has spoken about the changing landscape of South Asian representation in Hollywood, saying that while the industry still has work to do, the growing presence of varied and authentic stories has helped move the conversation forward.
Speaking to Gulf News about her new Netflix film Best of the Best , Ramakrishnan reflected on how representation has evolved in recent years. “In recent years, representation has gotten strides farther than where we were before. It's personality first, and then the non-changeable factors of their cultural backgrounds is additional information,” she said.
For Ramakrishnan, progress does not necessarily mean dismissing the work that came before. “But I have to give the dues where it's deserved. We did have past representations that might not have necessarily been what we fully resonated with or saw ourselves in, but sometimes even just existence, though might not be reflective of your experience, still moves the needle,” she said.
She added that projects such as Best of the Best are part of a much longer journey, built on the efforts of performers and creators who pushed for South Asian characters and stories to have a place in Western entertainment.
“A project like ours stands on the backs of all those past projects that you know paid their dues and fought the good fight to get that side role, because it all builds together. That's the only way we're going to continue,” Ramakrishnan said.
That idea of moving beyond surface-level representation is also reflected in the film's dance sequences. Best of the Best centres on a university Bollywood-fusion dance team, allowing the filmmakers to incorporate multiple South Asian dance traditions rather than treating them as a single style.
Ramakrishnan was particularly emphatic about the care taken with the choreography. “All these dance styles come from very rich cultures and histories and our choreographers kept it real. We're not settling for just waving our hands in the air anymore. That's not happening,” she said.
Director Lena Khan has similarly spoken about the multicultural nature of the project.
In a previous interview with Variety , Khan noted that the world around the characters reflects the reality of a country where people from different cultural backgrounds live alongside one another. “At some point this country and the world is just full of people in different cultures,” she said.
According to Variety , the production's choreography drew from styles including Kuthu, Bharatanatyam and Pakistani-influenced dance, reflecting the different cultural backgrounds represented by the fictional university team.
The film, which began streaming globally on Netflix on September 18, follows childhood friends Maya, played by Ramakrishnan, and Anjali, portrayed by Priyanka Kedia, as they arrive at UCLA and join its competitive Bollywood-fusion dance team.
What initially appears to be an exciting new chapter quickly becomes a tougher journey as the pair set their sights on the US championship.
The ensemble includes Lilly Singh, Janina Gavankar, Ankur Rathee, Chaneil Kular, Nico Greetham, Nihar Duvvuri, Shreya Navile, Amryn Khurana, Tanishq Joshi, Saara Chaudry and Sasha Bhasin.
For Ramakrishnan, the project also represents another stage in a career that began with one of Netflix's most visible South Asian-led coming-of-age series.
Her breakout came with Never Have I Ever , which premiered during the Covid-19 pandemic and quickly became a global streaming success. Reflecting on the unusual circumstances surrounding her sudden rise to fame, Ramakrishnan told Gulf News that the timing initially made the experience feel somewhat unreal.
“ Never Have I Ever season one came out in COVID and because everything was online, it kind of felt a little fake at first. It was right after Tiger King , Love is Blind , and Too Hot to Handle . So, everyone's bars were really low, and we slid right in there with a nice little comedy that's actually a story about grief,” she said.
Ramakrishnan was only 18 when Never Have I Ever arrived, thrusting her into an industry she was still learning to navigate. She credits creator Mindy Kaling with helping her adjust to the sudden attention and the demands that came with it.
“I got the biggest gift in having the best first boss in the world with my icon and one of the first true faces and pioneers of South Asian representation in the West, Mindy Kaling,” she added.
She recalled Kaling as someone who did not simply make the transition into fame easier, but remained direct with her while looking out for her as a young newcomer.
“She always kept it real and never went easy on me. She would always lead with her heart and truly saw me as a young kid who she realised she plucked out of nowhere and doesn't know this world. She really took such good care of me,” Ramakrishnan said.
With a characteristic touch of humour, she added: “So, I didn't crash out, I'm not shaving my head yet. We're still here. So, I guess we're all right.”
Now, with Best of the Best , Ramakrishnan is stepping into another story rooted in South Asian culture while playing a character navigating friendship, ambition, identity and the pressures of competition.
For an actor whose career began amid a major shift in how South Asian teenagers were portrayed on screen, the film offers another opportunity to expand what that representation can look like — this time through friendship, collegiate life and the energetic world of competitive dance.

title: Mural of rapper Macklemore painted in Gaza after Ed Sheeran tour furore
description: Macklemore pledges  1 million for Gaza  matched by children s TV personality Ms Rachel
content:
Macklemore pledges $1 million for Gaza, matched by children's TV personality Ms Rachel
Artists in Gaza ‌have painted a mural of Macklemore wrapped in a Palestinian flag on a huge slab of concrete in the ruins of Gaza City, after the US rapper was kicked off Ed Sheeran's upcoming tour for calling for a "Free Palestine".
The mural, on a slab that leans against ruined buildings surrounded by rubble, depicts the "Thrift Shop" rapper raising a ​fist in the air. "Thank you for using your voice for Palestine," it reads.
"We wanted to send a message to thank rapper Macklemore ​in this simple way," said Anne Redwan, 26, who designed and painted the mural with fellow artist Qusai ⁠al-Helo.
"As an artist living under siege here in Gaza, we are waiting for support from anyone who can see (the) persecution we live under," she ​told Reuters . "We can paint murals bigger than this to express our feelings."
Macklemore, who has long supported Palestinian causes, was cut from British pop star Sheeran's ​musical lineup over remarks on stage criticizing Israel's military assault in Gaza, which was launched after Hamas-led fighters attacked Israel in October 2023.
Sheeran said he was unable to keep Macklemore on the tour after stadium owners refused to let him appear. US billionaire Robert Kraft, owner of Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts where his New England Patriots ​football team plays, said he had barred Macklemore from appearing there for antisemitism, which the rapper denies.
Nearly a year after a ceasefire ended major ​fighting in Gaza, reconstruction has yet to begin. Most buildings have been destroyed and more than two million residents are confined to around a third of the ‌enclave's territory, ⁠mostly in tents or crowded rooms in damaged buildings among the ruins.
A US-brokered plan to end the war has stalled, with negotiators failing to agree conditions for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops.
The furore over Sheeran's tour has led to a series of pledges from those involved to send money. Macklemore said on Wednesday he would donate his $1 million in net earnings from the tour to six aid groups supporting Gaza.
Kraft, in turn, ​said Sheeran had told him he ​would donate $2 million for aid ⁠in the region, and had asked him to match the pledge. Sheeran has not commented on any donations. Macklemore's donation drew a matching $1 million pledge from Ms Rachel, a popular children's TV personality.
Aid agency officials said the ​boost in celebrity attention could help bring more support to Gaza, where nearly all residents rely on ​aid for food, water, ⁠medical care and shelter.
"But what's really most important is that people who have been so generous keep funding over a sustained time," said Toby Fricker, a local official with UNICEF. "That's why we really call for sustained support, not one-off peaks, but sustained."
Hussein Murtaja, who runs a Gaza humanitarian group that provides mental ⁠health support ​to children, said Macklemore's solidarity matters more than the money he donated.
"When artists of this ​stature, with this many followers or fans, all come to know more about the cause, and support reaching a political solution, support achieving peace for the people of Gaza... That ​means a great deal to us."
