title: Prince William and Karan Johar discuss Earthshot Prize ahead of Mumbai awards
description: Pair discuss India s growing role in the prize and how environmental solutions can combine innovation with business
content:
Pair discuss India's growing role in the prize and how environmental solutions can combine innovation with business
The Earthshot Prize , founded by Prince William in 2020, will come to India for the first time this November, with the sixth annual Awards Night taking place in Mumbai on November 17. Fifteen finalists will be celebrated, with five winners ultimately receiving £1 million each to help scale their environmental solutions.
The Prize is built around five environmental goals: Protect and Restore Nature, Clean Our Air, Revive Our Oceans, Build a Waste-Free World and Fix Our Climate. This year, those ambitions will take centre stage in Mumbai.
As Mumbai prepares to host the Earthshot Prize Awards, Indian filmmaker Karan Johar and Prince William discussed the power of environmental innovation, India's growing representation among the finalists and why the solutions of tomorrow must also work as viable businesses.
Johar, who has been confirmed as host of this year's Awards Night, recently sat down with Prince William to discuss the Prize, its finalists and the significance of bringing the event to India.
One idea emerged throughout their conversation: many of the solutions to the planet's biggest environmental challenges already exist, but they need the right support to grow and reach a wider scale.
Johar described the Prize as a platform capable of bringing people together around that shared challenge.
“I think what's very special about the Earthshot Prize is how it’s bringing the world together to fight one common cause. And for that, sir, I have to really, truly, truly congratulate you for supporting, for backing this, and giving it your heart, because I can tell whenever you speak about it, you can manufacture many things, but you can’t manufacture passion”, he said.
William said his own enthusiasm for the initiative came from meeting the people behind the solutions. “The passion comes from the genuine fondness of the winners. You only have to spend 10 minutes talking to them and you realise not only how dedicated they are, but how brilliant their ideas are.”
The conversation also turned to the significance of the Prize's trophy, which has already travelled around the world. “It's amazing it's been around the world a fair bit already. It was marking the point that we've all got a part to play in and how we look after the planet,” William said.
India's role in the Prize has been particularly significant, with William highlighting the country's record among the finalists and winners. “I remember very clearly the energy and vibrancy of Mumbai and, most importantly for the Earthshot, is that we've had more finalists and more winners from India than from any other country”, he said.
He added, “I'm really excited to see what comes from actually being in India and hosting the awards this year there.”
India's representation also gave Johar an opportunity to highlight another aspect of the Prize: the potential for environmental solutions to operate alongside commercial models.
“The fact that there's so much Indian representation makes my heart full. With some of them, there's also a deep business, a possibility which I think combines philanthropy with business incentives so beautifully with the Earthshot Prize,” he said.
William agreed that the finalists represented more than charitable initiatives. “There are proper businesses that are going to make investors money,” he noted.
Among the finalists is 'Satellites on Fire', an Argentine initiative that uses satellite technology and artificial intelligence to detect wildfires and warn communities at risk. “These guys are absolutely brilliant. Genius young guys who set up this organisation to use satellites to be able to predict and warn early communities that might face wildfires,” William said.
Another finalist, India's 'Mahindra Last Mile Mobility', is working in the transport sector, where the shift towards cleaner vehicles could have significant implications for urban air quality. Johar pointed to the project's ambition. “Making all rickshaws electric, that is massive to control the levels of pollution.”
The third project discussed was 'Yellowstone to Yukon', a major conservation initiative spanning the United States and Canada. It focuses on protecting and restoring connected landscapes and wildlife corridors across the Rocky Mountain region and is one of the 2026 finalists under the Protect and Restore Nature category.
William described the scale of the project as “A huge landscape restoration project from America to Canada. A real large-scale story about environments being protected and restored.”
Taken together, the projects discussed by Johar and William illustrate the breadth of the Earthshot Prize, from artificial intelligence and electric transport to large-scale conservation.
The initiative seeks not only to recognise environmental solutions but also to help them expand by connecting finalists with investors, businesses, philanthropists, policymakers and other potential partners.

Carrot Top has been performing professionally since the early 1990s and became known for his distinctive red hair and prop-based comedy. He has maintained his Las Vegas residency for decades.

title: Macron  Carney to meet in French Atlantic archipelago in signal to Trump
description: Trip marks first by French president since 2014  days after Trump posts image showing archipelago covered by US flag
content:
Trip marks first by French president since 2014, days after Trump posts image showing archipelago covered by US flag
President Emmanuel Macron visits the French territory of Saint Pierre and Miquelon on Sunday, where he is due to meet Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, weeks after United States President Donald Trump posted an image on social media showing the archipelago covered by the American flag.
Macron's visit, the first by a French president since Francois Hollande travelled there in 2014, comes as Canada seeks to deepen ties with the European Union amid trade tensions with the US and a deterioration in relations with Washington under Trump.
Located off Canada's Atlantic coast, Saint Pierre and Miquelon is France's only remaining territory in North America. French officials said the trip would underscore France's sovereignty over the archipelago and highlight its close relationship with Canada.
Read: Pentagon weighs pulling at least 25,000 US troops from Europe: NBC report
"For a territory of 5,800 inhabitants, it is rare to find so many issues that are important for France as a whole concentrated in a place of this size: France's geostrategic presence in the North Atlantic, at the doorstep of the United States and the Arctic, maritime sovereignty, adaptation to climate change; and cooperation with Canada," a French presidency official told reporters.
Diplomats said the visit, which Macron was undertaking on his way to the annual United Nations General Assembly gathering of world leaders, would also carry symbolic weight after Trump posted a map depicting the US, Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean draped in the US flag and labelled "United States of America".
The image included Saint Pierre and Miquelon and several French Caribbean territories. France chose not to publicly respond to the post at the time.

Macron and Carney are expected to discuss the energy crisis and Canada's increasingly close relationship with the European Union after the bloc opened the door to Ottawa becoming its first associate member .
Any move towards deeper integration is likely to face hurdles. More than a decade after the EU and Canada agreed the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), and nine years after its provisional application began, several EU member states have yet to ratify the accord, including France.

title: Tarar warns no violent group will be allowed to enter Islamabad
description: JI begins long march towards capital as PTI prepares for Sept 27 protest  govt warns against public disruption
content:
JI begins long march towards capital as PTI prepares for Sept 27 protest; govt warns against public disruption
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Sunday warned that “no violent group will be allowed to come to Islamabad” as Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) began mobilising supporters for a long march towards the federal capital and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) prepared for a separate protest.
Tarar said the government and administration were responsible for maintaining public order and ensuring that no disruption took place during the planned protests.
“There are clear orders of the Islamabad High Court regarding road closures and disruption to the movement of the public,” Tarar told reporters, adding that government roads would remain open and protesters would not be allowed to reach the capital in a manner that disrupted public movement.
اسلام آباد، وزیر اطلاعات عطاء اللہ تارڑ کی وزیراعظم فیول ریلیف سکیم اور مجموعی سیاسی صورتحال پر اہم گفتگو pic.twitter.com/jMbpRKVGii
The warning came as JI launched its “Super Long March” towards Islamabad, with supporters travelling from different parts of the country by road and rail.
JI Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman said people had begun travelling towards the federal capital according to the party’s strategy, while mobilisation was under way in Punjab and other parts of the country.
“People have started travelling towards Islamabad through different means. Road caravans have also departed, while the process of travelling by train is also beginning,” he said.
Hafiz said marches would begin from Khyber and other areas, while supporters in cities across Punjab were also being mobilised.
He added that the march was not being organised for the party or its leadership but to highlight the difficulties faced by poor and middle-class Pakistanis, whom he said were struggling because of government policies and rising petrol prices.
Read: Government, JI talks end without breakthrough on long march
“This march is not for ourselves or for our party,” Hafiz said, adding that higher petrol prices had made it increasingly difficult for people to afford basic necessities.
The JI emir also alleged that white-collar workers were being pushed into debt and forced to borrow money to meet household expenses.
He alleged that powerful business interests were benefiting from the existing economic system, claiming that the same interests were linked to banks, oil marketing companies, refineries, flour and sugar businesses. “This is a mafia, this is a cartel,” he said, alleging that the groups were exploiting people across Pakistan.
جماعت اسلامی نے "سپر لانگ مارچ" کے شیڈول کا اعلان کردیا۔ کراچی کینٹ اسٹیشن پر جلسہ عام شروع، اس کے بعد ٹرین مارچ امیر جماعت اسلامی حافظ نعیم الرحمان @NaeemRehmanEngr کی زیر قیادت روانہ ہوگا۔ رحمان بابا ایکسپریس دوپہر بارہ بجے کراچی کینٹ اسٹیشن سے روانہ ہوگی۔ ٹرین مارچ کے… pic.twitter.com/0sEN4LfSUx
Hafiz said limiting the campaign to social media would allow the situation to continue. “There is only one way — to come out into the field,” he said, explaining JI’s decision to continue its street mobilisation.
He added that the party had been holding sit-ins across the country for 36 to 37 days, including a 35-day sit-in outside the Governor House in Karachi. He said sit-ins were continuing at other locations and claimed that the movement had spread across Sindh.
JI’s march was centred on its demand for the withdrawal of the petroleum development levy. The party has maintained that its protest campaign will continue until the levy is abolished.
The government and JI held five rounds of talks over the issue, but negotiations ended on Saturday without an agreement. The government delegation had asked the party to defer the march, citing security concerns, while JI maintained that it would continue its protest until the levy was withdrawn.
The party subsequently proceeded with its planned march towards Islamabad. JI launched the march from Karachi on Sunday, with Hafiz leading the train contingent. The march is expected to reach the federal capital later in the week.
Hafiz had previously said JI would not block roads during the march and that the party was travelling to Islamabad to seek relief for the public rather than to confront anyone.
Read more: CM Afridi meets opposition leaders as PTI readies for Sept 27 protest
Meanwhile, the government has introduced the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme to provide targeted assistance to people affected by rising international fuel prices.
Tarar said petrol and diesel prices had increased globally amid regional tensions and that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had issued timely directions to provide relief to the public.
He said the prime minister had personally monitored the scheme and that its registration process had been completed with the cooperation of the Ministry of Information Technology.
The government subsequently expanded the eligibility criteria, increasing the age limit for motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqi rickshaws from 15 to 20 years. Vehicles registered on or after January 1, 2006, were therefore eligible for the scheme, Tarar said.
Registration through SMS had also been made free, while the previous condition limiting beneficiaries to five litres of petrol per token had been removed.
Under the scheme, motorcycle, Qingqi and rickshaw users could receive four tokens a month, with one token available every week. Each token provided Rs500 in fuel relief.
The scheme also covered vehicles with engines of up to 800cc, which were eligible for a Rs100-per-litre discount on up to 10 litres of petrol every 10 days, allowing three tokens a month.
The facility was available at petrol stations across Pakistan, including Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan, while the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) had issued instructions for its implementation.
Tarar said all provincial governments had supported the scheme and were cooperating with the federal government in its implementation.
More than 2.2 million people had registered for the relief scheme, with 92 per cent of them being motorcycle, Qingqi and rickshaw users, he said.
More than 557,000 registrations had been recorded in a single day, while around 1.9 million fuel tokens had been issued. Of these, around 1.8 million tokens had been issued to motorcycle, Qingqi and rickshaw users, while 152,000 had been issued to owners of vehicles with engines of up to 800cc.
More than 545,000 tokens had been issued on the previous day alone, according to Tarar.
The government had also removed the ownership condition for motorcycles, Qingqi rickshaws and rickshaws so that people actually using the vehicles could benefit from the scheme.
A smartphone was not required for registration, he added, as the process could be completed through SMS using the relevant vehicle and identification details.
Tarar said the government had established a separate technological system to monitor the scheme in real time. Petrol pumps and oil marketing companies had been brought into the system, while banners and awareness material had been placed at fuel stations to guide beneficiaries.
The Ministry of IT had established a control room and war room for monitoring, with data being collected continuously to track registrations and token redemptions.
Tarar said the system allowed the government to identify where tokens were being used and monitor implementation around the clock.
Complaints about the scheme were being received and addressed, he said, while an awareness campaign and tutorials had also been launched to help people understand the registration and token process.
Representatives from all provinces had participated in meetings of the implementation committee, while the prime minister was being kept informed about the scheme’s implementation.
Tarar said the relevant ministries, including IT, information and petroleum, along with OGRA and the Prime Minister’s Office, were coordinating the implementation.
He added that the scheme had been modified in response to public feedback and was intended to provide relief to the “most deserving” sections of society.
The JI, however, has maintained that the fuel-relief package does not address its central demand for the abolition of the petroleum levy and has continued with its protest campaign.

title: Ruby Rose remembers Hayden Panettiere  calling her    best friend    in emotional tribute
description: Ruby Rose spoke about her friendship with Panettiere  saying the actress wanted her story told on her own terms
content:
Ruby Rose spoke about her friendship with Panettiere, saying the actress wanted her story told on her own terms
Ruby Rose has spoken emotionally about her friendship with Hayden Panettiere, who died on August 16 at the age of 36.
Speaking to Entertainment Tonight , Rose described Panettiere as her “best friend” and said the pair “spoke every day for five years.”
“I didn’t even think we were going to be friends,” Rose said, becoming emotional. “I didn’t know if I wanted to have any celebrity friends, because I didn’t have a great experience with the industry.”
Rose also recalled their first meeting and how Panettiere approached her despite Rose initially being uncertain about becoming friends.
“I saw her, she saw me, and I just remember thinking, ‘Oh, no.’ And then she ran up anyway and was like, ‘Hey, I’m Hayden. Can we go talk somewhere? We’ve got a lot in common.’ I just laughed.”
The pair soon became close after discovering they “had everything in common”, according to Rose. They remained in regular contact throughout their five-year friendship and texted each other every day to check in.
“Hayden, all that she ever wanted was to have her story told her way, on her terms,” Rose said.
Panettiere was known for roles in Heroes , Nashville , Scream 4 and Scream VI . She also discussed her experiences with drug and alcohol addiction in her 2026 memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning .
Following her death, the Drug Enforcement Administration joined an investigation with South Carolina’s Greenville Police Department to determine her cause of death.
Several Hollywood figures paid tribute, including her Heroes co-star Jack Coleman, who described their long-standing bond.

title: Zara Noor Abbas on body confidence and finding her action hero side
description: Actor recalls overcoming body image concerns while filming  Sheroes  and embracing a physically demanding new chapter
content:
Actor recalls overcoming body-image concerns while filming 'Sheroes' and embracing a physically demanding new chapter
Actor Zara Noor Abbas has opened up about filming Gear Up , an action segment of the upcoming anthology film Sheroes , revealing that she weighed 12kgs more when she shot the project than she does now.
In an interview with Arab News , she discussed how her weight initially made her conscious of what she wore on screen. But director Saqib Khan encouraged her to embrace her body, challenging her perception of what an action heroine should look like.
“When I shot for that film, I was 12kgs higher than what I am right now. And I did feel that there was a certain inhibition to my body. I was really reluctant about what to wear,” the actor said.
Zara recalled raising her concerns with Khan, who reassured her that her physique was exactly what he wanted for the character.
“I was like, ‘No, Saqib, you don’t understand. This is not going to look good on my body.’ He was like, ‘No, you don’t understand. You look at your body in a very negative way. From where I am seeing, I think you are fit for the role, and I want someone who looks like this and who has a build like this,’” she added.
The conversation, she said, also reinforced the importance of representing different body types when portraying powerful female characters in action films. “Not everyone can be a size zero and look a certain size. No, women have different bodies, and we are telling different stories from different ethnicities,” she said.
Zara stars in Gear Up , one of three segments in the anthology film Shereos , which follows three women from three different worlds. She plays a police officer and takes on a series of action sequences, including high-speed car chases, a bomb-disposal sequence and a scene in which her character arrives at a police station on a motorbike.
The other segments feature Kinza Hashmi in Artist a nd Ushna Shah in Punch .
For Zara, the role also offered an opportunity to explore a side of female characters she feels is often underrepresented on television. “In dramas, we are not able to show our physical strength. As characters, we do not show the emotional resilience, persistence and perseverance that women have. But I really wanted to project a role where I could look badass,” she said.
That experience appears to have left Zara keen to explore more physically demanding roles. “I think I’d like to take up roles around the spy verse and the police and the cool cop verse,” she said.
She is already preparing for another project, revealing that she is undergoing intensive training that includes early-morning workouts.
“As we speak, I am also training for a new role. I wake up at 7 in the morning. From 7 to 12, I train for that. Then I go to my work on a drama set. I am also doing MMA right now and learning street fighting. I am really liking this whole dimension of my new self,” she shared.
With Gear Up , Zara is moving into a genre that gives her room to explore physical strength and a more action-driven side of her performance.
Her experience filming the project has also prompted her to question the conventional image of what a female action hero is expected to look like — and, judging by her current training, it may not be the last time audiences see her in that space.

title: Merz under pressure as two more German states go to the polls
description: Chancellor s approval sinks to 14  with CDU support in Mecklenburg Western Pomerania at just 6
content:
Chancellor's approval sinks to 14% with CDU support in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania at just 6%
German voters went to the polls on Sunday in two state elections that look likely to heap more pressure on struggling Chancellor Friedrich Merz, whose future has been in the balance since the far right's triumph in another regional vote this month.
The elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, a largely rural state in the formerly communist east, and the capital Berlin follow the September 6 election in Saxony-Anhalt , where the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) came close to the rare feat of winning an absolute majority.
Polls were scheduled to close at 6pm (1600 GMT), with the first exit polls expected soon after.
Regional elections would not usually draw much interest outside Germany, but the AfD's success in Saxony-Anhalt, which it sees as the first step towards winning federal elections due in 2029, has sent shock waves through Europe.
In just over a decade, the party, which wants to take tough action to deport foreigners with no right to stay in Germany, restore energy ties with Russia and quit the euro, has transformed itself from a fringe eurosceptic movement to the country's most popular party.
Read: Thousands protest far right in Germany
Opinion polls indicate it is unlikely to repeat its victory in Saxony-Anhalt in either of Sunday's votes. But they are both expected to underscore the advances it has made in recent years and raise fresh questions over the "firewall" strategy, under which the other main parties refuse to enter coalition agreements with it.
For Merz, whose approval ratings have plunged as low as 14%, according to the latest polls, the result was the most recent in a series of blows that have raised doubts in his conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) party about whether he can continue to lead.
In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the CDU looks likely to suffer its worst-ever election result, with the most recent opinion poll by the Forschungsgruppe Wahlen on Friday putting it at just 6% and at risk of failing to clear the minimum threshold to enter the state parliament.
Elected last year on a promise of reforms to return Germany's stagnant economy to growth, Merz has struggled to win over voters, compounding resentment over unpopular pension, tax and healthcare reforms with a stream of communication missteps.
For the moment at least, senior CDU figures have rallied behind him, aware that replacing the chancellor - which would in any case be difficult on constitutional grounds - would leave any successor facing the same deep economic problems.
But disillusion with his government has hung over the campaigns in both Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin, where voters have focused on issues including soaring energy and housing costs. Merz presented a consumer relief package on Friday that included tax cuts on gas and diesel.
Several people heading to vote in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania said living costs were a major concern.
"Here in Schwerin, with these wages, you can hardly afford anything anymore," voter Carlotta Heick told Reuters in the state capital. One elderly man criticised funding for foreign aid. "We need our money here, for our country, for children and pensioners," he said, asking not to give his name.
Read More: As history returns, Germany sees echoes of its past
In the rural state, polls have shown the race narrowing over recent weeks as the centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) have centred their campaign around popular state premier Manuela Schwesig. The Wahlen poll on Friday showed the SPD edging in front of the AfD for the first time in months.
The poll put the SPD on 37%, the AfD on 36%, the far-left Left Party on 9% and the environmental Greens on 5%, just at the threshold for entering parliament. Both parties would be potential coalition partners for Schwesig.
At her closing campaign rally, Schwesig warned of "dark clouds" as she referred to the AfD, calling it a dangerous party.
Wrapping up the AfD's campaign in the state, national party leader Alice Weidel took aim at Merz. "From next week, the chancellor's tone will become very quiet," she said, telling supporters they had the power to unseat him in Sunday's election.
In Berlin, the Wahlen poll showed the far-left Left Party moving ahead of the CDU, threatening the conservative hold on the mayor's office. Even in liberal Berlin, however, the AfD has made strong gains, moving into third place.
The poll put the Left Party on 22%, the CDU on 20%, the Greens on 15% and the SPD on 12%. The AfD sits on 18%, while the far-left BSW, the only party that has said it might work with the AfD, is just under the parliamentary threshold on 4%.

title: Cate Blanchett asks London audience to stop filming during National Theatre play
description: The comments were met with an enthusiastic response from the audience and have been widely shared online
content:
The comments were met with an enthusiastic response from the audience and have been widely shared online
Cate Blanchett has asked audiences at London’s National Theatre to stop filming during performances, saying theatre should remain a place where people can be present together.
Blanchett made the remarks from the stage of the Lyttelton Theatre following the curtain call for Electra/Persona , the new production written and directed by Benedict Andrews.
Still wearing her stage costume, Blanchett addressed the audience calmly after the performance, saying, “There are few places on this planet where we can simply be together and be present. I understand you like filming the curtain call – and it is kind of flattering in a way – but for anyone who is filming the show, please don’t, because it spoils it for the next group of people who come in and are present with us. So thank you very much.”
The comments were met with an enthusiastic response from the National Theatre audience and have since been widely shared on social media.
Electra/Persona combines Sophocles’ tragedy Electra with Ingmar Bergman’s Persona .
Blanchett stars opposite Nina Hoss, with the pair sharing the roles of Electra/Elisabeth and Clytemnestra/Alma. A coin toss determines which roles they perform on each night.
The National Theatre describes the production as “a thrilling production [that] fuses ancient myth and modern psychology in a powerful exploration of identity, and the fragile line between who we are and who we play.”
The play runs at the Lyttelton Theatre through October 10 and also features Ella Lily Hyland.

The comedian was allegedly threatened over a sex tape before his reported suicide attempt, court documents say
American comedian Scott Thompson, known professionally as Carrot Top, was hospitalised in Las Vegas on Friday following a reported suicide attempt, according to TMZ .
His Friday night performance at the Luxor was subsequently cancelled.
His representative, Jami Schlicher, told TMZ , “Mr. Thompson is recovering in the hospital and is receiving the care and support he needs.” She added that his family and those close to him appreciate the public’s concern and have requested privacy.
Carrot Top, 61, was born on February 25, 1965, in Rockledge, Florida. He began performing stand-up comedy while attending Florida Atlantic University and later became known for his distinctive red hair, props and visual comedy.
According to Celebrity Net Worth, his estimated net worth is around $70 million, although Thompson has not publicly confirmed his financial details.

His career includes appearances on The Tonight Show with Jay Leno and The Late Show with David Letterman .
He also hosted Carrot Top's AM Mayhem on Cartoon Network from 1994 to 1996 and appeared in films including Chairman of the Board and Dennis the Menace Strikes Again .
Carrot Top grew up primarily with his father, Larry Thompson, after his parents separated when he was 13.
“I was at the age where you don't get it; I was surprised at it, and it wasn't a happy thing,” he said in an interview with the Las Vegas Sun.
Larry Thompson, who worked at NASA facilities as an engineer and astronaut trainer, died in 2016 aged 76.

title: PTI condemns Aleema Khan s arrest as Lahore DC orders 30 day detention
description: Party s central Punjab spokesperson says she had been shifted to an undisclosed location
content:
PTI, TTAP demand Aleema’s release, urge an end to political restrictions
Police in Lahore on Sunday arrested Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan’s sister Aleema Khan and detained her for 30 days under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance, days before the party’s planned Sept 27 protest march.
According to a copy of the order available to The Express Tribune , Lahore Deputy Commissioner Capt (retd) Muhammad Ali Ijaz issued the detention order on September 20 under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance, 1960. The order also named Aleema’s driver, Muhammad Ameer, directing that both be detained for 30 days from the date of their arrest at Central Jail, Kot Lakhpat.
The order cited concerns over public safety and the maintenance of public order.
The order stated that the Lahore Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) forwarded a request based on reports submitted by the SP Civil Lines Division and the In-charge District Intelligence Branch.
The reports said that Aleema and Ameer had been involved in the May 9 protests and road blockades and had motivated workers to damage public and government property.
The police and intelligence reports further stated that the two were again mobilising workers through social media and public meetings, potentially creating a law and order situation.
The reports also accused them of raising what the order described as “objectionable slogans” against the government and institutions in an attempt to provoke or incite members of the public. Multiple cases, including FIR No. 96/23 registered at Race Course police station, were cited in support of the request for detention.
The authorities described the two as “potential dangers to public peace and tranquillity” and recommended their detention for 30 days under the MPO to maintain law and order in Lahore.
The matter was subsequently placed before the District Intelligence Committee at a meeting held on September 20 under the chairmanship of the Lahore deputy commissioner.
According to the order, the committee discussed the matter and endorsed the evidence and material provided by the police department before unanimously recommending detention of both individuals to maintain the law and order situation in the city.
Read: Aleema says public backs Imran's release
The deputy commissioner said he was satisfied, based on the material submitted by the CCPO and the committee's recommendation, that the presence of the two individuals at any public place would pose a “grave threat to public safety” and was likely to cause a breach of public peace and order.
The order was issued under powers conferred through a 2017 Punjab Home Department notification and Section 3(1) of the Punjab MPO Ordinance, 1960.
The order also states that the detainees may make a representation to the provincial government against their detention.
According to the family sources, Aleema was travelling towards Gymkhana Club when police intercepted her vehicle and took her into custody along with her driver and the car. They said she had left her residence around 1:15pm to 1:20pm after offering Zuhr prayers.
The family sources said that she was subsequently taken towards Lytton Road and was expected to be shifted to Kot Lakhpat Jail under the MPO law.
PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan has condemned the arrest of Aleema, saying it was the first step towards worsening the situation. “Our march will be peaceful and political. We do not want any confrontation or violence,” he said, adding that the party’s objective was to pursue a peaceful struggle for constitutional and political demands.
Gohar said arresting Aleema or detaining her under the MPO amounted to fuelling tensions. He called on the government to immediately stop such measures and release her. He added that the party would soon announce its course of action against such measures.
The Tehreek Tahafuz Aain Pakistan (TTAP) also strongly condemned the detention of Aleema, terming it an escalation of the ongoing crackdown on political workers and their families.
In a statement, TTAP said Aleema had been detained under the 3-MPO and alleged that her detention had been carried out despite there being no charge against her. The alliance said the action had created an atmosphere of fear among political workers and their families.
Read more: Aleema says Imran will not bow
The statement further alleged that the Punjab government’s actions against political workers were aimed at disrupting political activity ahead of the September 27 protest. TTAP has announced the September 27 protest as part of its campaign for protection of the Constitution, Parliament and provincial rights.
“The relentless crackdown on political workers in Punjab has now reached families. Aleema’s detention under 3-MPO, with no charge and days before September 27, is repression at its peak. It will not break our resolve. Resisting it is our duty,” said TTAP provincial leader Shayyan Bashir.
TTAP demanded the immediate release of Aleema and other political prisoners, saying the government should end what it described as a series of arrests and restrictions on political activity.
Aleema’s son, Shahrez Khan, said his mother was abducted after leaving home on Sunday morning, adding that the family had had no contact with her or information about her whereabouts.
Shahrez wrote on X, “My mother, Aleema Khan, was abducted after leaving home this morning. Our family has had no contact or news of her whereabouts. She is on bail in all cases against her in Lahore. We demand the government immediately disclose her whereabouts and ensure her safe return."
My mother, Aleema Khan, was abducted after leaving home this morning. Our family has had no contact or news of her whereabouts. She is on bail in all cases against her in Lahore. We demand the government immediately disclose her whereabouts and ensure her safe return.…
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi also condemned Aleema’s arrest, saying the treatment of women in Punjab in the presence of a woman chief justice was “shameful”.
He said the sanctity of the veil and four walls was being violated “without any fear”.
“Once again, the way Aleema Khan was abducted and transferred to jail” was condemnable, Afridi said, describing her arrest as nothing but “the worst form of political victimisation”.
“If they have differences with the founding chairman, they should compete with the ideology and politics of the founding chairman,” the chief minister said.
“What kind of politics, law and morality is it to target his wife, sisters and women of his family?” he asked.
Noreen Niazi urges stronger participation in Sept 27 march
Imran’s sister Noreen Niazi urged people to put even greater emphasis on the September 27 protest march, further stating that everyone across Pakistan should participate in the movement.
Talking to reporters in an emergency press conference, Noreen stated that the orders of the Supreme Court were not being followed and that Imran was being kept in isolation and not shifted to the hospital. “My family is part of this movement and the entire country is also involved in this movement”.
Noreen emphasised that if the authorities believed that arresting Aleema would “frighten” them or prevent them from participating, then they were mistaken. “We will all come out, remain steadfast, and will not be afraid regardless of who they arrest or how many people are arrested.
Noreen further alleged that Aleema had been “abducted,” saying that the authorities had not shown any warrant or document before taking her and had instead taken her from the street. “We do not know where Aleema Khan has been taken or where she is being kept, and the family has neither been contacted nor informed about her whereabouts”.
She added that “we initially thought that we will proceed in a measured manner, but now, we will come out with even greater force”.
Noreen called on people to stand up more resolutely than before to secure their own freedom and that of the country and also for the release of Imran, adding that the “oppression and injustice taking place had now reached every household”.
PTI Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram also condemned the detention of Aleema, saying the government had abducted an elderly woman from outside her home.
Akram wrote on X, “Maryam Nawaz says women are a red line. Today, their government abducted Aleema, an elderly woman, from outside her home. This is not justice; it is cowardice. A sister is being imprisoned as punishment for speaking for her brother. If women are a red line, then present Aleema in court right now.”
مریم نواز کہتی ہیں خواتین ریڈ لائن ہیں۔ آج ان کی حکومت نے علیمہ خانم ، ایک بزرگ خاتون ، کو گھر کے باہر سے اغوا کر لیا۔ یہ انصاف نہیں، بزدلی ہے۔ بہن کو قید بھائی کی بات کرنے کی سزا دی جا رہی ہے۔ اگر خواتین ریڈ لائن ہیں تو علیمہ خانم کو ابھی عدالت میں پیش کرو۔
PTI founder Imran’s sister Noreen Khan held a telephone conversation with Opposition Leader in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas.
Abbas said the government had become nervous and that the determination of Imran's sisters was encouraging workers and the nation. He said the struggle of Imran and his sisters represented resistance against oppression in Pakistan. He added that they were standing with the Constitution of Pakistan and the people while enduring hardships.
He condemned the arrest of Aleema, saying the detention of a sister exposed the government’s nervousness. He alleged that the government had become fearful of September 27 and was therefore now arresting the sisters as well.
Noreen said they were working for the Pakistani people and their brother.
She said such arrests could not break their resolve and instead made them stronger. Noreen added that Aleema’s arrest could not weaken them and that they would continue their efforts.
It is pertinent to mention that the area where she was allegedly intercepted does not fall under the jurisdiction of Lytton Road Police Station.

title: World leaders return to UN amid wars in Middle East and Ukraine
description: Organisation to convene amid waning relevance  financial strain  no clear successor to Guterres
content:
Organisation to convene amid waning relevance, financial strain, no clear successor to Guterres
World leaders gather in New York this week for the United Nations General Assembly, bracing for President Donald Trump's return to the rostrum for a second year running, with talks centering on the widening conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine and the risks of artificial intelligence .
Nearly 130 heads of state meet with the post-World War Two order under strain and with the UN itself struggling to remain relevant and weathering attacks from Trump, who has slashed America's contributions and withdrawn from dozens of UN bodies.
Chinese leader Xi Jinping, who last addressed the diplomatic jamboree via video in 2021, will skip New York in favour of one-on-one talks with Trump in Washington on Thursday, fueling debate about the UN's relevance in addressing global crises.
Compounding the crisis of morale and finance are questions about the next leader of the 80-year-old organisation: Secretary-General Antonio Guterres completes his term at the end of 2026, with no clear frontrunner in the race to replace him.
Read: Rebeca Grynspan ahead in informal poll for UN chief
The 15-member UN Security Council may hold high-level meetings on Ukraine, AI and the Middle East, including talks with Arab leaders, diplomats said.
More than a year into Trump's second term, "we would no longer say that the UN is in freefall, but we would say that it's stuck in an open-ended crisis," said Richard Gowan of the International Crisis Group. "The UN may not be in emergency care like it was last year, but it seems to be trapped in a trauma centre for the foreseeable future," Gowan said.
The US avoided losing its vote at the assembly by paying $725 million in contributions to the regular budget this week, but it still owes the organisation more than a billion dollars and makes ongoing demands for cuts and reforms.
The assembly meets shortly after several artificial intelligence industry leaders called for a coordinated slowdown of the development of the technology, warning that it could soon improve on its own and escape human control .
Guterres has said that AI will be a major topic, adding that countries pushing its frontiers should set up "common guardrails in order to avoid this race to the bottom that could lead one day to a gigantic disaster at the global level."
Read More: Ten days that changed the course of AI
The secretary-general has long proposed global governance of AI. In 2023, the UN created an advisory body on the technology, with members including tech executives, government officials and academics.
The warning has put Guterres at odds with Trump, who dismissed AI risks as a "hoax," saying there is a "sick conspiracy" against it and that China would benefit from the doubt being cast on its development.
The Middle East will again be a focus of discussions, as the US-Israeli war on Iran continues to drive global inflation and destabilise the region. Recent gains by the Houthis threatens shipping in ​the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait and could further spike energy prices .
"It's very difficult to have a military solution for that problem, and the experience of fighting in Yemen demonstrated how complicated it is to have successful interventions," said Guterres, adding that the UN's envoy on Yemen was making a "huge effort" to advance talks.
Peace talks remain stalled, however, as Iran and the US continue to exchange strikes and Trump threatens a major escalation of the war. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is scheduled to address the assembly on Wednesday.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu – wanted by the International Criminal Court over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza that Israel denies – is to speak on Thursday.
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas will for the second year running not be at the gathering in person. The US, a close Israeli ally, again denied him a visa. On Thursday, the General Assembly voted to allow Abbas to appear via video.
There is likely to be a high-level meeting on the conflict in Sudan on the sidelines, diplomats said, although a diplomatic breakthrough is unlikely.
Also on the agenda is Russia's more than four-year-old war in Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov will address the General Assembly. Zelenskiy will likely seek to shore up Ukraine's position ahead of what is expected to be another tough winter, diplomats said.
The Security Council has been unable to take action to end the conflict because permanent member Russia holds a veto.
Also Read: UN rights chief says uncovered remains in Gaza raise concerns of war crimes
Trump has at times appeared frustrated that he has been unable to broker an end to the war, a goal he declared a priority when he began his second term in January last year. The US president spoke with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin earlier this month, but it was unclear whether he plans to meet Zelenskiy in New York.
Guterres highlighted the impact the war was having on civilians but also on food security and energy prices.
"The effective blockade existing in the Black Sea is creating enormous problems that add to the problems generated by the Middle East crisis, and I think it would be very important to find a way to allow Ukrainian exports and Russian exports of food, fertilisers and energy to take place in a safe way through the Black Sea," he said.

title: Why did Prime Video cancel  Ride or Die   Buddy spy comedy now being shopped by Paramount
description: Starring Hannah Waddingham and Octavia Spencer   Ride Or Die  premiered in July and quickly gained traction
content:
Starring Hannah Waddingham and Octavia Spencer, 'Ride Or Die' premiered in July and quickly gained traction
Prime Video has opted not to renew Ride Or Die for a second season, despite strong viewership and positive reviews, Deadline reports.
Paramount Television Studios, the series’ lead studio, is now shopping the buddy spy comedy to other potential buyers.
Starring Hannah Waddingham and Octavia Spencer, Ride Or Die premiered on July 15 and quickly gained traction.
The series reached No. 1 in the daily US rankings and recorded 927,000 views in its first two days, according to Luminate data.
The show also performed well on Nielsen’s streaming charts, debuting with 869 million minutes viewed before rising to 922 million minutes in its second week.
It remained in Prime Video’s Global Top 10 more than two months after release. It has also earned a 96% critics’ score and an 85% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes.
Created by Tessa Coates, the series follows best friends Debbie Claybourne (Spencer) and Judith Burton (Waddingham).
Their friendship is thrown into turmoil when Debbie discovers that Judith is an international assassin, forcing them to go on the run after a hit goes wrong.
Although the series reportedly came in under budget, the reasons for its cancellation remain unclear.
Deadline suggests its focus on middle-aged women may have influenced the decision, while stressing that the explanation is uncertain.
The first season ended on several cliffhangers, leaving major storylines open for a potential continuation.
Paramount Television Studios is now seeking another platform to carry the series forward.

title: Govt launches competitive power market for large consumers
description: Energy minister says electricity producers  consumers would be able to buy and sell directly
content:
Energy minister says electricity producers, consumers would be able to buy and sell directly
Energy Minister Awais Leghari on Sunday announced the launch of a competitive electricity market in Pakistan, saying the new system would initially allow industrial and other large consumers using more than one megawatt to purchase electricity directly from producers before being extended to ordinary consumers in the coming years.
“The government is practically withdrawing from electricity procurement,” he said in a video message, explaining that electricity producers and consumers would instead be able to buy and sell power directly through a transparent mechanism.
The announcement came as the Independent System and Market Operator of Pakistan (ISMO) issued a request for proposals (RFP) for Pakistan’s first 400-megawatt wheeling auction under the Competitive Trading Bilateral Contract Market (CTBCM) framework.
وفاقی وزیر توانائی سردار اویس احمد خان لغاری کا CTBCM کے تحت بجلی کے مسابقتی نظام کی جانب اہم پیغام۔ اب بجلی پیدا کرنے والے اور بڑے صارفین مسابقتی بنیادوں پر بجلی کی خرید و فروخت کر سکیں گے، جبکہ پہلے مرحلے میں ایک میگاواٹ سے زیادہ بجلی استعمال کرنے والے صارفین اس نظام سے مستفید… pic.twitter.com/hrGGmX56Pb
Leghari also shared the ISMO public notice on X, saying he was “proud to announce” that the RFP had been issued and that a “decades-old commitment” of successive governments had now been practically implemented. “Suppliers and consumers of power can now transact with each other,” he said in his post.
Under the existing electricity market structure, the government purchases the power generated by producers and supplies it to consumers. The terms and rates under which electricity is procured have long been a subject of scrutiny, particularly in relation to independent power producers (IPPs).
He said the new system would fundamentally alter that arrangement, with producers and consumers able to enter into transactions directly rather than relying on the government as the central buyer and seller. “Electricity producers and users will buy and sell directly through a transparent mechanism,” he added.
Also Read: Power companies faulted for crippling outages
The first phase of the competitive market will cover industrial and other large consumers using more than one megawatt of electricity. Ordinary consumers will be brought into the system at a later stage, with Leghari saying the expansion was expected to take place over the next few years.
The minister said the eventual expansion would give consumers greater choice over their electricity suppliers and allow them to seek cheaper power. “For an ordinary consumer, this will mean that they will have the choice of buying cheaper electricity,” he said.
Leghari further stated that lower electricity costs would also help Pakistani industry compete in international markets and support exports. “If electricity becomes cheaper, our industry will be able to compete internationally, and our exports will increase,” he added.
I am proud to announce that the RFP for 400 MW of wheeling has been issued today. Decades old commitment of different governments has been practically implemented by PM Shahbaz Sharifs Team Power. Suppliers and Consumers of Power can now transact with each other. No more… pic.twitter.com/SaRPwQhEtv
The wheeling mechanism allows eligible electricity producers and consumers to enter into direct power transactions while using the existing transmission network to deliver the contracted electricity.
It is intended to provide the infrastructure needed for consumers and suppliers to trade power outside the government’s traditional procurement arrangement.
Under the first auction, interested participants have been asked to submit their proposals by November 20, 2026. Potential participants must also register on ISMO’s electronic auction platform to take part in the process.
Leghari described the launch as the practical implementation of a reform that successive governments had sought to introduce for decades.
Read More: DISCOs seek Rs1.7 raise in power tariff
“Every government for the last 25 to 30 years wanted a competitive electricity market,” he said, adding that the present government had moved towards putting the system into practice.
He said the initial eligibility threshold of more than one megawatt was part of a phased rollout and did not represent the final scope of the market, with smaller consumers expected to be brought into the system in the coming years.
Leghari congratulated Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and the nation on the development, saying the government had fulfilled a long-standing reform commitment by moving towards a competitive electricity market.
The 400MW wheeling auction is expected to serve as an initial step in the transition, with the new market beginning with large electricity users before being expanded to smaller consumers.

title: Ed Sheeran calls Israel s treatment of Gazans  unjustifiable
description: Singer apologises for Macklemore s removal from his US tour  says his concerts should remain safe space for everyone
content:
Singer apologises for Macklemore's removal from his US tour, says his concerts should remain safe space for everyone
Pop star Ed Sheeran apologised on Saturday for his handling of a controversy that erupted this week when ‌rapper Macklemore was removed as an opening act over comments on the occupied Palestinian territories.
Breaking his silence on the issue, the British singer decried Israel's treatment of residents in Gaza as "unjustifiable."
"I've had to take and make difficult decisions and I am making mistakes and I'm so, so sorry," Sheeran told ​an audience in Philadelphia, where he performed for the first time since Macklemore was taken off the concert tour.
🎤 Ed Sheeran admits making ‘mistakes’ after Macklemore was dropped from his US tour over pro-Palestinian remarks, as he addresses controversy surrounding Israel’s war on Gaza ➤ Sheeran calls war ‘catastrophic, unjustifiable and disproportionate’ and apologizes over recent… pic.twitter.com/4YOl7sOrZi
At ​the start of the concert at Lincoln Financial Field, Sheeran called the October 2023 Hamas attack ⁠that killed 1,200 Israelis "horrific." But he called Israel's subsequent war, which has killed thousands in Gaza and displaced almost all of the ​population, "catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate."
Sheeran also decried "systemic injustice" in the West Bank, where Israel's right-wing coalition government has allowed a massive expansion ​of Jewish settlements.
“My heart has been broken by the scale of devastation and loss of civilians’ lives, children’s lives,” he said, adding that “systemic injustice” in the West Bank could not be ignored.
Sheeran also apologised for recent decisions. “This week, the criticism was about something much more important and I’ve had to take and make difficult decisions, and I am making mistakes, and I’m so, so sorry.”
The pop star's opening statement offered a stark change from his statements earlier in the week, when Sheeran posted on Instagram that his concert audiences "do not expect a political forum."
“I don’t want to disappoint fans, and I’ve never wanted to be an activist musician, but this has put me in the middle of an important and passionate argument about freedom of speech and the most complex political issue on the planet,” he told the crowd in the city of Philadelphia.
Controversy has surrounded Sheeran since Macklemore posted on Instagram that New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft had told ​Sheeran that Macklemore would not be allowed to perform at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, where Sheeran has shows on September ​25 and 26.
Macklemore said Kraft and other stadium owners had told Sheeran he would not be allowed to perform in their venues if Macklemore ‌remained ⁠on the tour after saying "Free Palestine" during a September 4 concert at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The tour's other supporting acts subsequently quit to show solidarity with Macklemore.
Despite acceding to stadium owners' demand for Macklemore's removal, Sheeran on Saturday said he was "deeply worried" about concert venues vetting performers' content. "This happens in so many places that I perform around the world, but it should never ​happen in the free world," ​Sheeran said.
Pro-Palestinian protesters demonstrate near the venue of pop star Ed Sheeran's concert after rapper Macklemore was cut from the musical lineup over his "free Palestine" remarks on stage criticizing Israeli government actions in Gaza and the West Bank, near Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, US, September, 19, 2026. PHOTO: Reuters
Dozens of pro-Palestinian protesters gathered about half a mile from the ​concert venue ahead of Sheeran's performance. Organizers said they were there to talk to people about the conditions on the ground in Gaza and to highlight local ​groups advocating for Palestinians.
Billboard also reported that Sheeran removed the B stage from his concert, regarding safety concerns.
"To be honest, I didn't know what the audience would be like tonight. I didn't know if things would have been thrown at me. I didn't know if people would be angry with me. Today, is not the usual Loop show because I was afraid of what would happen if I stood in the middle," said Sheeran mid-concert.
Later during the show, Variety also reported that Sheeran introduced violinist Alicia Enstrom alongside temporary backing musicians Mike, CJ , Eric, and Clay to replace Beoga, the traditional Irish folk group that pulled out of his remaining US tour dates.
“There are certain songs that just don’t work on the loop pedal, so when my friends dropped out of the show, I was thinking, ‘How am I gonna keep the show the same, and how am I gonna get musicians to stand on stage with me in a week when no one wants to stand on stage with me?" Sheeran said.
He added, "I just wanna say before they come on stage [that] they said yes to being on stage with the knowledge that the world thought I was a certain type of person. They said yes with the knowledge that the world may hate them too for standing on stage with me and I am so grateful for them being on stage tonight and standing on stage with me in front of you guys."
Palestinians walk near a mural painted in honour of American rapper Macklemore, amid buildings destroyed during the war, in Gaza City, September 18, 2026. PHOTO: Reuters
The Philadelphia Police Department said it was monitoring the event and making “any necessary adjustments based on public safety needs.”
Sheeran told the crowd that “everyone is welcome” at his concerts and that people with opposing views can still come together through music. “My concerts have always been a safe space for everyone, and that matters hugely to me,” he said.

title: Asim Khan powers into Asian Games semis
description: Pakistan MMA fighter beats Cambodia   s Sopanha Pheng to set semi final bout with Tajikistan   s Umarov
content:
Pakistan MMA fighter beats Cambodia’s Sopanha Pheng to set semi-final bout with Tajikistan’s Umarov
Pakistan’s Asim Khan powered into the men’s Modern -60kg semi-finals at the Asian Games on Sunday, defeating Cambodia’s Sopanha Pheng 3-0 in a commanding quarter-final performance.
Khan produced a strong display at the Nagoya City Inae Sports Centre to advance to the last four of the mixed martial arts competition.
The Pakistani will face Tajikistan’s Mirzobek Umarov in Monday’s semi-final, with victory putting him into the gold-medal bout.
Khan is guaranteed at least a bronze medal if he loses the semi-final, with only ten fighters entered in the Modern -60kg category.
His coach Dilawar Khan said that bronze is not their target.
"Bronze has been ensured but this is not our target. We eye gold and will be fighting for that inshaAllah," Dilawar told The Express Tribune from Nagoya.
He said that Asim has been a solid fighter and has been regularly featuring in international events.
"He has featured in so many international events also including the World Championship and then he came here while in perfect rhythm," Dilawar said.
He said that his semi-final opponent is also very good and he expects a solid fight in Monday's show.

title: Does Channing Tatum have a burner account  Theory goes viral after comments about Zo   Kravitz and Harry Styles
description: The account s comments have prompted fans to question whether the actor could be behind the profile
content:
The account's comments have prompted fans to question whether the actor could be behind the profile
Channing Tatum has become the subject of online speculation after social media users spotted a little-known account leaving comments about him, his former fiancée Zoë Kravitz and her rumoured relationship with Harry Styles.
The Instagram account, named Nonya Bidness, reportedly has just one follower: Tatum himself.
Its comments have prompted social media users to question whether the actor could be behind the profile.
Kravitz and Tatum became engaged in 2023 after dating for around two years, but their engagement ended in 2024.
Since their split, Kravitz has been romantically linked to Styles, prompting renewed interest in her past relationship with Tatum.
One comment from the account referred to Kravitz as Tatum’s “former fiancé” and described her as “the most intentional person he knows”.
Another defended Tatum, writing that his ex-wife had allegedly tried to take his money.
The account has also left complimentary remarks about Tatum, including, “He's so genuine. No false pretenses with this guy. And funny as hell, too.”
Another comment referenced Shawn MacArthur, the character Tatum played in the 2009 film Fighting .
Some Reddit users considered the specific 'niche' reference a possible clue, while others suggested the account could belong to a friend or family member.
The discussion has drawn mixed reactions, with some users convinced the account belongs to Tatum and others cautioning against jumping to conclusions based on a follow.

title: Carrot Top hospitalised after reported suicide attempt amid extortion allegations  court docs reveal
description: The comedian was allegedly threatened over a sex tape before his reported suicide attempt  court documents say
content:
The comedian was allegedly threatened over a sex tape before his reported suicide attempt, court documents say
Carrot Top, whose real name is Scott Thompson, was allegedly extorted over a sex tape before his reported suicide attempt, according to court documents obtained by Page Six.
The comedian’s attorney, Ronnie Bitman, claimed in a September 3 filing in Broward County, Florida, that musician Brian Evans threatened to release an explicit video unless Thompson paid him.
Evans previously opened for Thompson’s long-running Las Vegas residency at the Luxor Hotel and Casino.
The filing included an email in which Evans allegedly demanded $500,000 “in immediately available funds” in exchange for resolving claims against Thompson.
Evans denied threatening to publish any video, telling Page Six the email was “intended to be confidential”. He also claimed the footage “was deleted a long time ago” under a previous settlement.
Evans has alleged that Thompson sent him unsolicited sexual footage in 2022 or 2023. He is seeking to overturn a 2024 settlement, claiming he lacked the mental capacity to enter into a binding agreement after suffering psychiatric injuries linked to the 2023 Maui wildfires.
Thompson’s representative, Jami Schlicher, told the outlet that Evans had been declared a “vexatious litigant”. A federal judge cited at least 15 cases Evans had filed since 2025, which “appear frivolous”.
The report follows news of Thompson’s hospitalisation on Friday following a reported suicide attempt, according to TMZ .
Schlicher confirmed he was “recovering in the hospital and is receiving the care and support he needs”, while requesting privacy for his family.
His weekend performances at the Luxor were cancelled.

title: India romp into Asian Games cricket final
description: Verma   s unbeaten 100 and Mandhana   s 37 help India post 195 4 before bowling Bangladesh out for 81
content:
Verma’s unbeaten 100 and Mandhana’s 37 help India post 195-4 before bowling Bangladesh out for 81
Smriti Mandhana became the highest run-scorer in women's T20 international cricket on Sunday as India crushed Bangladesh by 114 runs in the Asian Games semi-finals with fellow opener Shafali Verma hitting her maiden hundred.
Mandhana scored 37 off 19 balls with five fours and two sixes in her side's 195-4 in 20 overs at the Korogi Athletic Park ground in Nagoya.
In the process she went past New Zealand all-rounder Suzie Bates's 4,758 runs at the top of the all-time list to stand on 4,788 runs from 171 innings.
Verma was the star on the day for India, scoring 100 not out off 49 balls with three fours and nine sixes -- her maiden T20 international century.
Verma reached her hundred off the final ball of the 20 overs, and was clearly emotional as she took off her helmet and raised her bat in celebration towards her applauding teammates on the boundary.
India then skittled Bangladesh for 81 in 15.4 overs.
India will meet Sri Lanka in Tuesday's final after they earlier chased down Pakistan's 177-4 with more than two overs to spare.
Sri Lanka raced to 178-2 off 17.5 overs largely thanks to captain Chamari Athapaththu's sparkling unbeaten 83 off 50 balls, laced with six sixes and seven fours.
Pakistan will play Bangladesh for the bronze medal, also on Tuesday.

title: Czechs conquer USA to reach Davis Cup finals
description: Lehecka seals dramatic victory in Prague as South Korea make history by reaching last eight
content:
Lehecka seals dramatic victory in Prague as South Korea make history by reaching last eight
Jiri Lehecka downed Learner Tien in a deciding rubber as the Czech Republic stunned the United States 3-2 in Davis Cup qualifying for a second straight year, while South Korea reached the last eight for the first time on Saturday.
The Czechs knocked out the Americans at the same second qualifying round stage in a deciding rubber in Delray Beach a year ago, when Jakub Mensik beat Frances Tiafoe to secure a surprise victory.
Tomas Berdych's men repeated the feat in similarly dramatic fashion, to the delight of a raucous home crowd in Prague, as Lehecka clinched a 6-3, 7-5 win over world number 13 Tien.
The USA are record 32-time winners of the competition but their wait for a first title since 2007 goes on.
The Czechs advance to the November eight-team finals in Bologna, where hosts Italy will bid for a fourth straight title.
"The wins in Davis Cup are always a little bit different because this is a team competition," said Lehecka.
After starting the day locked at 1-1, the USA nudged ahead as Christian Harrison and Austin Krajicek saved four match points to outlast Adam Pavlasek and Patrik Rikl in a thrilling 5-7, 6-3, 7-6 (10/8) win.
Mensik then fought back from a set down to keep the tie alive by defeating recent US Open runner-up Ben Shelton 5-7, 6-4, 6-3.
Shelton took a tense first set after saving a set point when trailing 5-4, reeling off the last three games.
Mensik created a set point at exactly the same stage of the second, but this time made no mistake with a booming forehand to level the match.
The 21-year-old, a semi-finalist at this year's French Open, forced the tie into a deciding rubber on his second match point in a tense final game.
Lehecka, who beat Shelton in straight sets on Friday, recovered after giving an early break back to take the first set.
Tien forged 3-0 ahead as he attempted to force the tie all the way to a final set, but fell away and Lehecka clinched a brilliant win on his fourth match point.
"I must say it has been a great week. But, most importantly, we made it through as a team. Without Jakub winning against Ben, I would not have the chance to play the final match," added Lehecka.
Earlier, South Korea made history by beating India 3-1 in Seoul.
Kwon Soon-woo brushed Sumit Nagal aside 6-1, 6-2 to clinch the decisive point for the Koreans, who won both of Friday's singles rubbers before India triumphed in the doubles.
"I feel very proud for my country and every team I play against, I give my best," said Kwon.
Austria also booked their spot as Jurij Rodionov sealed a 3-1 win for the hosts in Vienna with a 7-6 (8/6), 6-3 victory over Zizou Bergs, Belgium's number one in the absence of Alexander Blockx.
Rodionov got Austria on the board in Friday's opening singles before Bergs pulled Belgium level.
Doubles pair Lucas Miedler and Neil Oberleitner then beat Sander Gille and Joran Vliegen in straight sets to put Austria back on top.
France kept their tie with Canada alive, as Benjamin Bonzi and Pierre-Hugues Herbert beat Felix Auger-Aliassime and Duncan Chan in straight sets in the second day's opening doubles match to cut their deficit to 2-1.
Newly-crowned US Open champion Alexander Zverev gave Germany a 1-0 lead over Croatia in Halle, making a quick return to action as he beat Matej Dodig 6-4, 7-6 (7/3).
But Germany, who have not won the Davis Cup since 1993, were pegged back to end the first day level as Croatian youngster Dino Prizmic brushed aside Daniel Altmaier 6-4, 6-3.
Spain continued their tilt at a seventh title by seizing a 2-0 lead over Chile in Santiago courtesy of singles wins for Daniel Merida and Davis Cup debutant Rafael Jodar over Alejandro Tabilo and Cristian Garin, respectively.
Britain's Toby Samuel overcame Andres Andrade of Ecuador and Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery saw off Alvaro Guillen Meza as the hosts took a 2-0 advantage in London.

title: Anthem mix up sparks Asian Games apology
description: Organisers mistakenly play North Korea   s anthem before South Korea   s hockey match
content:
Organisers mistakenly play North Korea’s anthem before South Korea’s hockey match
Asian Games organisers offered "deepest apologies" on Saturday for playing the North Korean national anthem for the South Korean men's hockey team.
South Korean officials were left angered by the latest mishap to hit the Nagoya-Aichi Games, which officially opened after a troubled build-up.
At their Friday contest against Bangladesh, South Korea's players lined up for the traditional playing of the anthems, only to look bemused as North Korea's song rang out.
Organisers then played Bangladesh's anthem and later the South Korean one, the South's Yonhap news agency said. South Korea went on to win 5-0.
"During the men's hockey match between (South) Korea and Bangladesh on September 18, an incorrect national anthem was mistakenly played before the match," the Asian Games organising committee told AFP on Saturday.
The statement said that, on Friday, "officials responsible for (National Olympic Committee) relations visited the delegation of the Republic of Korea and offered their sincere apologies for the incident".
"We will also work to prevent a recurrence and would like to express our deepest apologies to all those affected by this matter."
A stadium announcer apologised for the blunder but Min Tae-seok, coach of South Korea, was unimpressed.
"This is a really serious problem. When we protested, they said, 'We're sorry. It wasn't that it wasn't prepared, there was a mistake on the part of those responsible for playing it'," he said.
"But this is something that simply should never happen."
The build-up to the Games has been overshadowed by complaints from teams about the quality and amount of accommodation.
Some teams were also stranded at the airport for up to six hours when they landed this week.

title: Malaysian ex PM Najib working on conditions to start house arrest  his lawyers say
description: Najib must pay  12m fine as many assets  bank accounts remain frozen amid corruption proceedings
content:
Najib must pay $12m fine as many assets, bank accounts remain frozen amid corruption proceedings
Malaysia's jailed former prime minister, Najib Razak, is working to fulfil the conditions to leave jail and begin his house arrest, including paying a 50-million-ringgit ($12-million) fine, his lawyers said on Sunday.
Najib's ability to satisfy the condition "do not lie in his own hands" as a significant part of his assets, bank accounts and properties remain subject to freeze orders and enforcement proceedings by the government, the lawyers said in a statement.
Najib, prime minister from 2009 to 2018, was found guilty of corruption in relation to the embezzlement of billions of dollars tied to 1Malaysia Development Berhad, a state investment fund he co-founded while in power. He has consistently denied wrongdoing.
Malaysia's king agreed on Friday to let Najib Razak leave jail and serve the remainder of his ‌sentence under house arrest. It was the second royal pardon over his conviction for his involvement in a multi-billion-dollar financial scandal.
Read: South Korea court sentences ex-president to 2 years in jail in political funding case, media says
Malaysia's Prisons Department said in a statement on Sunday that it and the home affairs ministry were waiting for official written confirmation of the pardon before taking any action.
By law, the home affairs minister has the power to gazette any premises as a prison, which could be used to designate Najib’s home as a place to serve his sentence.
Najib has been "deeply moved" by the support he has received from the public, the lawyers said.
The president of Najib's UMNO party, Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, said on Friday that a collection fund would be launched for party members and supporters to help Najib pay for the fine. The party had raised almost 1 million ringgit by Saturday noon, local media reported.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's multi-party government, which includes the DAP as well as Najib’s UMNO, has seen growing rifts over the government's response to issues of corruption.

title: Navy chief visits units at sea  Creeks Area to review SEASPARK 2026
description: Exercise designed to test Navy   s operational preparedness  ability to rapidly transition from peace to wartime
content:
ISPR says exercise was designed to rehearse the 'full spectrum of maritime operations'
Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf visited units at sea and in the Creeks Area on Sunday to review Exercise SEASPARK 2026, the military’s media wing said.
According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), The biennial exercise, which has been underway since September 1, rehearses the full spectrum of maritime operations and tests the operational preparedness and ability to transition rapidly from peacetime to wartime operations.
"Reflecting the changing character of warfare, this year’s exercise integrates Operations in the Information Environment, Multi-Domain Operations and extensive use of unmanned systems," the statement added.
Read: Pakistan summons Indian Cd'A to protest INS Kolkata warship’s ‘provocative’ manoeuvres in EEZ
During his visit, Admiral Ashraf interacted with personnel participating and commended their “professionalism, high morale, operational readiness and resolve to remain invincible at sea”, ISPR said.
Pakistan protests Indian navy vessel's EEZ incursion
Pakistan and India on Wednesday lodged tit-for-tat diplomatic protests against each other over a naval incident in the Arabian Sea after vessels from the two countries came into contact during a Pakistani maritime exercise.
The Foreign Office summoned the Indian Charge d'Affaires in Islamabad and lodged a "strong protest" over what it described as a provocative and unacceptable action by an Indian Navy vessel inside Pakistan's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) on September 15.
According to the Foreign Office, the Pakistan Navy has been conducting its biennial exercise, SEASPARK-26, in Pakistan's EEZ since September 1. It said that since September 7, the Indian naval ship INS Kolkata and a helicopter deployed on it had repeatedly attempted to enter the area where the Pakistani exercises were being conducted.
The Foreign Office said INS Kolkata carried out "dangerous and provocative manoeuvres" close to Pakistan Navy vessels despite multiple warnings.
It said the Indian vessel's activities were not a routine deployment but constituted a violation of the 1991 India-Pakistan Agreement on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Manoeuvres and Troop Movements.

title: IOC president impressed by Asian Games wooden huts
description: Some countries have criticised the wooden cabins as too small
content:
Some countries have criticised the wooden cabins as too small
IOC president Kirsty Coventry called the shipping container-style huts for Asian Games athletes "beautiful" on Sunday -- but conceded they were "a little tighter" than similar accommodation at the Milan-Cortina Winter Olympics.
Asia's biggest sporting spectacle, which opened on Saturday in the Japanese city of Nagoya, has split with past Games by having no traditional athletes' village.
To save costs, the more than 17,000 Asian Games participants will stay in temporary huts, hotels and a cruise ship.
Some countries have criticised the wooden cabins as too small, with beds that are too short.
But after touring the lodgings, International Olympic Committee president Coventry said she could not understand the negativity.
"We had similar cabins in Milan-Cortina (Winter Games this year) and the athletes were very happy. And the cabins here are really nice," said the Zimbabwean former Olympic champion swimmer.
"They're a little tighter. So, you know, if you want something negative, it's a little smaller.
"But I don't think it's a negative thing. I love the village."
About 2,000 participants are staying in the lodgings by the water in Nagoya.
Coventry said: "The cabins are quiet, they're very cool. The air conditioning is working well.
"The flooring and the walls are beautiful. It's better than some of the villages I've stayed in.
"So I think to be very fair to Japan and to the organising committee, I was really impressed.
"I had only been reading everything that had been said. And I was expecting something completely different to when I walked in."
Asked by AFP if she would happily see the temporary cabins and also a cruise ship serve as accommodation at the Olympics, she said she had not been to the vessel.
But she pointed to the accommodation at Milan-Cortina, and said those "very closely" resembled the ones in Nagoya.
"And it is a concept that I think, for me, when we talk about an athlete experience, being an athlete... as soon as I go in, I'm not necessarily concerned about the look."
