title: Pakistan warns Afghanistan after Kohat attack  says it can eliminate terror threats    wherever they are
description: Pakistan calls on Taliban to dismantle terror sanctuaries as Kabul warns against military action inside Afghanistan
content:
Pakistan calls on Taliban to dismantle terror sanctuaries as Kabul warns against military action inside Afghanistan
In a veiled warning to Afghanistan following the deadly terrorist attack in Kohat, Pakistan on Saturday said it had the “will and capability” to eliminate terror threats “wherever they are” and urged the international community to press the Afghan Taliban regime to take decisive action against terrorism.
The warning came a day after at least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred in a terrorist attack at Kohat Police Lines during Friday prayers. According to the statement provided by the Ministry of Information, an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque, followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities.
The Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers. Islamabad has repeatedly asked the Taliban regime to deny the use of Afghan soil for terrorist attacks inside Pakistan. However, the de facto rulers in Kabul have been reluctant to take action against terrorist groups operating from their territory.
“We strongly condemn the barbaric terrorist attack on civilians and police officials offering Juma prayers in Kohat,” the Ministry of Information said in a post on X.
We strongly condemn the barbaric terrorist attack on civilians and Police officials offering Juma prayers in Kohat. The attack, perpetrated by the vilest of Khwarij with roots in Afghanistan, reminds us that terrorism has no religion and no justification. Those who perpetrate,…
It said the attack, which it attributed to “the vilest of Khwarij with roots in Afghanistan”, was a reminder that “terrorism has no religion and no justification”.
“Those who perpetrate, facilitate or shelter such acts are the worst among humankind,” it added.
Pakistan said it had repeatedly raised “grave concerns” over the alleged use of Afghan territory by the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan and other terrorist groups to plan and launch attacks inside the country.
“The presence of terrorist sanctuaries, alongside their recruitment and support infrastructure in Afghanistan, poses a direct threat to Pakistan’s security,” the statement said.
It said these concerns had repeatedly been conveyed to the Afghan Taliban regime and its interlocutors.
“They must dismantle these networks rather than deflect responsibility,” Pakistan said.
Read : Kohat Police Lines blast death toll rises to 23 as clearance operation concludes
The statement made clear that it considered itself capable of responding to terrorist threats irrespective of their location.
“Pakistan has both the will and the capability to eliminate terrorist threats wherever they are,” it said, adding that Islamabad would take all necessary measures, in accordance with international law, to protect its citizens, territory and sovereignty.
The ministry also warned of wider consequences from the continued presence and activity of terrorist groups in Afghanistan.
“Pakistan has repeatedly warned that the continued presence and activity of terrorist groups in Afghanistan will aggravate instability, with serious regional and global repercussions,” it said.
The government also called on the international community to push the Afghan Taliban regime to take action against terrorism.
“The international community should push the Afghan Taliban regime to act decisively and verifiably to counter this menace before the threat spreads further across the region and beyond,” it said.
Pakistan said it had taken note of the Afghan Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ condemnation of the Kohat attack and its expression of sympathy for the victims’ families, but pointed out that the Afghan statement did not mention terrorism.
Read More : Pakistan vows response to Afghan-based terrorism in self-defence 'as and when needed'
“Notwithstanding, condemnation must be matched by concrete action,” Pakistan said.
It called on the Afghan Taliban to take “credible, verifiable and sustained measures” to dismantle what it described as terrorist sanctuaries, disrupt recruitment and training networks, and prevent terrorist groups from planning, facilitating or launching attacks against Pakistan.
“Pakistan has consistently pursued dialogue and constructive engagement with the Afghan Taliban, but we would not allow pretence of dialogue to shield those who threaten our people,” the statement said.
The ministry also criticised Afghan Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid for warning Pakistan against military action, saying it was “reprehensible” that he had threatened Pakistan with a “crushing response”.
“The Afghan Taliban must address the terrorist ecosystem thriving under their patronage instead of trying to deflect responsibility and malign Pakistan,” it said.
“Such antics cannot obscure their counterterrorism obligations under the Doha Agreement or their responsibility to prevent Afghan territory from being used to threaten other countries,” Pakistan added.
In an interview with Al Arabiya English earlier, Mujahid had warned Pakistan against carrying out military operations inside Afghanistan and called for dialogue and stronger intelligence mechanisms between the two countries.
“If Pakistan invokes Article 51 to violate the sanctity of Afghan territory, Afghanistan has the right to defend its country, and we will do so,” he said, warning of a “crushing response” to any violation of Afghan sovereignty.
Tensions between the two countries have escalated over the last year amid mutual accusations over cross-border militancy. Islamabad has long maintained that terrorists linked to the TTP operate from Afghan territory, while Kabul has denied the allegations and accused Pakistan of violating its sovereignty through alleged strikes.
Pakistan has maintained that meaningful engagement with the Taliban government cannot resume unless Kabul takes concrete and verifiable action against banned terrorist groups, particularly the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), which Islamabad says operates from Afghan territory to plan and carry out attacks inside Pakistan.
The issue of terrorist sanctuaries remains the central source of friction between the two countries. Islamabad has repeatedly conveyed to Kabul that assurances alone are insufficient and that Pakistan wants to see demonstrable action against groups it considers responsible for attacks on its territory.
The Pakistani position also extends to other terrorist organisations operating from Afghan territory, including the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA).
The deterioration in bilateral ties, particularly over the TTP issue, has significantly narrowed the space for diplomatic initiatives.
Pakistan appears to be keeping diplomatic channels and limited institutional contacts open while refusing to resume substantive engagement with Kabul until it sees concrete and verifiable action against militant groups operating from Afghan soil.
Officials insist that any future policy change would depend primarily on developments on the ground rather than isolated diplomatic or academic interactions.

title: Abu Aleeha disputes  Mango Jutt  final cut  says he refused to sign off
description: Filmmaker says he quit over disputed edit and criticises trailer
content:
Filmmaker says he quit over disputed edit and criticises trailer
Filmmaker Abu Aleeha, credited in earlier promotion as the director of Mango Jutt , has said he walked away from the project over disagreements about its final edit, days after the film's trailer dropped without his name in its visible credits.
The trailer, featuring Faysal Quraishi, Hareem Farooq and Shamoon Abbasi, was released on Wednesday. In an Instagram story on Friday, Aleeha called it "cringe-worthy" and said the film itself was worse.
Aleeha said the project was his brainchild and that he began work on it about three and a half years ago. He said he wrote the script, cast the roles and brought Farooq on board as both actor and co-producer. According to him, filming wrapped around two and a half years ago, and he locked the edit about four months later.
Further adding, he said, Farooq's team then suggested sending the film to India for further editing. He claimed the version that came back a year later was "very bad" and cut more than half of Ayesha Jehanzeb's scenes, while Maira Bangash's role was similarly trimmed. He further described the cut as a "C-grade edit lock" and said he refused to approve it.
He also said the Punjab government granted the team Rs30 million during this period, after which he was asked to shoot additional scenes to justify the funding. Aleeha said he refused, calling the proposed opening scene unfeasible.
Aleeha said the disagreements led him to withdraw while the film continued without him, and that he would not have raised the grievances had Farooq not spoken first. He maintained that the story, dialogues, characters and footage came from his work, while acknowledging the wider team, and said he still believes the film has potential.
The film marks Farooq's first Punjabi-language project and her first big-screen appearance since 2019's Heer Maan Ja . No release date has been announced.

title: CM Afridi meets opposition leaders as PTI readies for Sept 27 protest
description: Afridi  Achakzai and Abbas discuss strategy for Sept 27 protest and ways to advance joint opposition efforts
content:
Nasir Abbas meets Naqvi, says no one except Imran can postpone Sept 27 march
As the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) steps up preparations for its nationwide September 27 protest, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Saturday held meetings with opposition leaders to discuss the planned mobilisation.
The PTI has announced a Sept 27 march on Islamabad to press for the release of Imran Khan. The party has been preparing a central convoy from K-P, with caravans from other parts of the country expected to join before proceeding towards the federal capital.
According to a statement issued on X by the Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Ain Pakistan (TTAP), CM Afridi held an “important meeting” with Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Leader of the Opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas.
Read : IHC says political protests cannot infringe citizens’ fundamental rights ahead of PTI march
“The meeting included detailed political consultations on the Sept 27 call, with the participants discussing various aspects of the future course of action, political strategy and ways to effectively advance the democratic struggle,” the statement said.
It added that the leaders discussed moving forward with the Sept 27 call as an effective and organised political struggle for the supremacy of the Constitution, democratic rights, provincial rights and protection of the public mandate.
وزیراعلیٰ خیبر پختونخوا سہیل آفریدی کی قائدِ حزبِ اختلاف قومی اسمبلی محمود خان اچکزئی اور قائدِ حزبِ اختلاف سینیٹ علامہ ناصر عباس سے اہم ملاقات ہوئی۔ ملاقات میں ترجمان تحریک تحفظ آئین پاکستان حسین احمد یوسفزئی بھی موجود تھے۔ ملاقات میں 27 ستمبر کی کال کے حوالے سے تفصیلی سیاسی… pic.twitter.com/HeRdE1z5mU
It was the second meeting between the three leaders this week. They had also discussed plans for the Sept 27 protest on Thursday after Afridi concluded his visit to Punjab.
The meeting came a day after the Islamabad High Court (IHC) ruled that any activity resulting in a violation of citizens’ fundamental rights would constitute a breach of the Constitution.
The PTI has been seeking to turn its Sept 27 mobilisation into a joint opposition campaign and had begun reaching out to opposition parties last month. On Aug 20, the TTAP and Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) announced plans to form a “united opposition” following consultations on cooperation and future political strategy.
Abbas also met Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi. In a post on X by the TTAP, Abbas said the meeting had not been held at his request and that he had made no demands or contacted anyone for it.
“There is no complication in this meeting. If someone wants to talk about the justice that Imra Khan is not getting, the basic rights that are not being granted to him, then a solution should be found for that,” he said.
محسن نقوی سے ملاقات میری ڈیمانڈ پر نہیں ہوئی تھی، نا میں نے کسی سے ڈیمانڈ کی ہے اور نا ہی کوئی رابطہ کیا ہے، اس ملاقات میں کوئی پیچیدگی نہیں ہے، عمران خان کو جو انصاف نہیں مل رہا ، بنیادی حقوق نہیں مل رہے تو اس پر کوئی بات کرنا چاہے تو حل ہونا چاہیے، قائد حزب اختلاف سینٹ علامہ… pic.twitter.com/WR5rnNQeFD
“This system has collapsed and this system has fallen on the heads of the public, and against this, the public is coming out to protest while staying within constitutional limits,” Abbas said, adding that the PTI’s demands were before the authorities and should be discussed.
He said he had informed Naqvi that “no one except Imran Khan can postpone the long march on September 27, and no one can sideline Imran Khan."
ہم نے محسن نقوی کو بتا دیا ہے کہ 27 ستمبر کا لانگ مارچ عمران خان کے علاوہ کوئی بھی ملتوی نہیں کرسکتا ، عمران خان کو کوئی مائنس نہیں کرسکتا قائد حزب اختلاف سینٹ سینٹر علامہ راجہ ناصر عباس pic.twitter.com/kLaltAaE79
The meeting came a day after Naqvi warned that anyone violating the IHC judgment and attempting to create unrest in the federal capital or any province would face legal action, including contempt of court proceedings.
Naqvi said the IHC’s detailed judgment had left no room for any attempt to create unrest in the federal capital or any province.
He said all law enforcement agencies had been given clear instructions that anyone attempting to come out in violation of the court’s judgment would first face legal action in the form of contempt of court proceedings.
“Secondly, we will stop them through any means possible,” he said.
Under a preliminary strategy announced in August, the party planned to bring workers from across the country to K-P at least five days before the march. The main convoy was expected to remain at the Punjab-Khyber Pakhtunkhwa border for two to three days before moving towards Islamabad once other caravans had assembled.
The PTI had also planned protests and shutdowns in several major cities, including Lahore, Karachi, Hyderabad and Quetta, as well as demonstrations along important national highways.
The PTI’s August plan also included a funding and mobilisation structure for the protest. A committee headed by party Secretary-General Salman Akram Raja was tasked with overseeing finances, while lawmakers were directed to mobilise supporters in their constituencies.
The party had estimated that the first day of the march would cost around Rs450 million, with subsequent days expected to cost approximately Rs14.5 million each. It had also sought financial contributions from lawmakers and party figures to fund the campaign.

title: UK actor Naomi Watts honoured at Spain film festival
description: Actress says she still seeks challenging roles as San Sebastian gives her the Donostia Award
content:
Actress says she still seeks challenging roles as San Sebastian gives her the Donostia Award
British actor Naomi Watts is to receive a special honour on Saturday at the San Sebastian Film Festival in Spain, where she declared an unwavering appetite for challenging roles that make audiences think differently.
The festival will present Watts with its top prize, the Donostia Award, previously handed to actors such as Gregory Peck, Julia Roberts, Johnny Depp, Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, Sigourney Weaver and Penelope Cruz. "It feels like such an incredible honour to get this award at this point in my life," the 57-year-old told a news conference at the festival in the northern Spanish coastal city.
"I've been working hard for the last nearly four decades and had the fantastic opportunity to work with cinema greats," she added. "I continue to try and do interesting things with my work, to shift thinking, alter narratives and help the human psyche be understood better."
Watts rose to stardom with her role in David Lynch's 2001 psychological thriller "Mulholland Drive" and received two Oscar nominations for "21 Grams" and "The Impossible".
An advocate for women ageing naturally, she said attitudes in the film industry had changed in recent years.
"I was told at the beginning that I better get my skates on because it all finishes at the age of 40 and here we are today. I'm in my late 50s now. I do think things have changed."
Films in competition at the Spanish festival include a new adaptation of Victor Hugo's novel "Les Misérables" by French filmmaker Fred Cavaye and "Ashes" by Mexican director Diego Luna.

title: How Lili Reinhart got her hands on Jennifer Garner   s 13 Going on 30 iconic coat
description: The story began when a video of Savage wearing the cropped coat around New York appeared on Reinhart s feed
content:
The story began when a video of Savage wearing the cropped coat around New York appeared on Reinhart's feed
Lili Reinhart turned 30 in the middle of her The Love Hypothesis press tour, but instead of marking the milestone with a traditional birthday celebration, the actress found a way to pay tribute to the romantic comedies that have inspired her promotional looks.
Reinhart tracked down the vintage Nanette Lepore coat Jennifer Garner wore in 13 Going on 30, with the exact piece becoming part of her rom-com-inspired wardrobe.
On September 17, a few days after her birthday, Reinhart was spotted in New York City wearing a brown lace-trimmed slip dress from Fleur du Mal, vintage Jimmy Choo kitten heels and an ivory polka-dotted coat. Fans of the 2004 film quickly recognised the single-breasted style as the same coat Garner wore as Jenna Rink in the film and on its original poster.
But getting the piece was far from straightforward. Violet Savage, daughter of New York-based designer Nanette Lepore and the person who protects her mother's archives, explained to Marie Claire how the coat eventually made its way to Reinhart.
The story began when an Instagram video of Savage wearing the cropped Spring 2003 coat around New York appeared on Reinhart's feed. Wish You Love Vintage, the archival collector that Reinhart's stylist Ib Abdel Nasser had sourced for the vintage Jimmy Choos, then connected the pair.
With the rom-com-inspired concept behind Reinhart's The Love Hypothesis press tour, Nasser and Savage began communicating about the coat. After Lepore "gave her blessing", Savage loaned Reinhart what she described as the "only copy of the jacket".
The timing was particularly fortunate. Savage told Marie Claire that she had pulled the coat from Lepore's archives only a few months earlier and happened to have immediate access to it. It had been stored in a box that was not labelled as containing jackets.
Savage also praised Reinhart's stylist for going directly to the source instead of attempting to recreate the iconic design. The decision not only helped create a viral fashion moment but also brought renewed attention to Lepore's work and its appearances in popular media, including Gossip Girl and Gilmore Girls.
Lepore closed her independent design studio six years ago and is now the lead designer at Maria Cecilia. According to Savage, many of her current clients are longtime customers who have followed her work for decades. She continues to incorporate the femininity associated with her original brand through day-to-night tailoring, matching sets, bright colours and distinctive patterns.
For Reinhart, however, the story of the coat began with a simple Instagram discovery and ended with her wearing a rare piece of 13 Going on 30 history decades after it first appeared on screen.

title: Greenland  Denmark say US deal will not cede sovereignty
description: Denmark and Greenland hope a UN deal will end months of uncertainty over Trump s threats to seize Greenland
content:
Denmark and Greenland hope a UN deal will end months of uncertainty over Trump's threats to seize Greenland
Denmark and Greenland on ​Saturday said any agreement with the United States would not compromise Greenland's sovereignty, after President Donald Trump said the deal would give ‌Washington "permanent control" over the Arctic island's security, leaving its precise scope unclear.
The United States, Denmark and Greenland said late on Friday they had entered into an agreement for the US to develop a significant military presence on Greenland, while prohibiting US adversaries from building their own bases on the island.
Key details of the agreement have not been made public, including the degree ​of US military presence in the self-governing Danish territory and whether any formal power over foreign policy and resources would be ceded to ​Washington.
Denmark and Greenland expressed hope that a deal, which is expected to be signed during the UN General Assembly next ⁠week, would end months of uncertainty triggered by Trump's threats to seize control of Greenland.
"Next week could be a good week — for Greenland, Denmark, and the United ​States," Denmark's Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said in a statement posted on Facebook on Saturday.
"A time of uncertainty will hopefully give way to a binding ​agreement that strengthens security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic, and thereby our shared security within NATO and Europe — while respecting the (Danish) Kingdom's red lines," he said.
Denmark and Greenland have repeatedly insisted that Washington respect the sovereignty of the Danish kingdom and accept that Greenland is not for sale.
Trump said on Truth Social late on Friday ​that under a deal, "the United States will forever have the complete ability to do what is necessary in Greenland in order to secure and defend ​the security of Greenland, and the United States of America."
The deal "gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland", Trump said, adding that no adversary ‌would ever ⁠be permitted to have a base or military presence in Greenland, or make sensitive investments there, without Washington's express written approval.
Trump made the announcement after Reuters exclusively reported that the US and Denmark were closing in on a deal.
"This is probably not the end of President Trump’s ambitions for Greenland and certainly not the end of US strategic interest in the territory and its resources," said Mikkel Vedby Rasmussen, a political science professor at the University of Copenhagen.
Read More: Trump signs bill authorising sweeping Russia sanctions
If Copenhagen cedes ​any formal power to Washington, it ​raises the question in Greenland of ⁠whether "this is the beginning of replacing the colonial relationship with Denmark with a colonial relationship to the United States", he said.
Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen said on Saturday that he was pleased with the proposed deal: "The agreement recognises the ​sovereignty and territorial integrity of our Kingdom and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination," he said in ​a post on Facebook.
Trump's threats, which peaked in January, triggered a diplomatic crisis that strained relations within NATO and pushed Denmark and Greenland into negotiations aimed at defusing the pressure.
A NATO spokesperson on Saturday said the alliance welcomed the agreement, which would "help advance security, stability and cooperation in this vital region".
Steffen Nielsen, a 49-year-old sales worker living in ⁠Copenhagen, told ​ Reuters : "I think that the US is probably going to get what they could have had the ​whole time, if they just asked nicely."
"I don't like it," Kaj Jorgensen, an 80-year-old pensioner also living in Copenhagen, said of the news. "I don't wish the United States to be present anywhere ​in the Danish Kingdom. I really don't trust Donald Trump."

content:
Asks stations found permanently closed, dealing exclusively in diesel removed from the list
Deputy Prime Minister (DPM) Ishaq Dar on Saturday directed authorities to bring all operational fuel stations “onto the system” to ensure proper rollout of the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme.
On September 16, the PM’s Fuel Relief Scheme , which was already operational in Islamabad, was rolled out across the country at midnight.
A statement issued today by the office of DPM Dar said he chaired a meeting of the National Steering Committee on Fuel Subsidy to review the implementation of the scheme.
Addressing the meeting, Dar said, “Every fuel station which is open and operating be brought onto the system, and that stations found permanently closed or dealing exclusively in diesel be identified and removed from the list,” adding that the coverage of the scheme should reflect the position on the ground.
Read: PM orders expansion of fuel relief scheme
According to the statement, the committee members were informed that an “overwhelming majority” of fuel stations across the country were operational on the system, and citizens were redeeming fuel tokens.
It also said that the committee approved the redemption of fuel tokens through SMS for stations located in areas deprived of internet access.
It further outlined that registration through SMS could be availed by messaging on 9771.
“Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Gilgit-Baltistan and the provinces shall furnish lists of such (operational) stations so that they may be brought onto the scheme without delay,” the statement read.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar chaired a meeting of the National Steering Committee on Fuel Subsidy to review the implementation of the Prime Minister's Special Relief Scheme. The Committee was informed that overwhelming majority of fuel… pic.twitter.com/ts8PexUP46
During the meeting, the State Bank of Pakistan deputy governor informed the committee members that all payment claims received over the past three days were settled in full.
“Claims received each day, processed the same day.”
DPM Dar praised the efforts of the provincial administrations and acknowledged the cooperation extended by the State Bank of Pakistan, noting that the relief must continue to reach the intended beneficiaries without hindrance.
The meeting was attended by the ministers for Petroleum, Economic Affairs, Information and Broadcasting, and Information Technology and Telecommunication; the State Bank of Pakistan Deputy Governor, Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority chairman, Pakistan Digital Authority chairman, Petroleum Ministry secretary, Islamabad Capital Territory chief commissioner, the Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa additional chief secretaries, and Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Gilgit-Balitistan, and Balochistan senior officials, as well as other relevant federal and provincial departments.

On the day the scheme was rolled out nationwide, Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination Dr Musadik Malik said the PM’s Fuel Relief Scheme had been designed to support low-income citizens , including delivery riders, rickshaw drivers and families dependent on motorcycles and small cars.
The minister had said eligible motorcyclists would receive Rs100 per litre in fuel relief on up to 20 litres of petrol per month, providing maximum monthly assistance of Rs2,000. He added that 800cc car owners would be eligible for relief on up to 30 litres of petrol, translating into Rs3,000 in monthly assistance.

title: Frankie Muniz says he hit  rock bottom  after split from Paige Price
description: The last 6 weeks of my life have been a nightmare I   m praying to wake up from     Muniz wrote
content:
“The last 6 weeks of my life have been a nightmare I’m praying to wake up from,” Muniz wrote
Frankie Muniz has opened up about a difficult period in his life following his split from wife Paige Price, describing the past six weeks as a “nightmare” and saying he has reached “rock bottom”.
The Malcolm in the Middle star shared an emotional message on Instagram on September 18, revealing that the recent weeks had left him feeling as though everything was happening at once.
“The last 6 weeks of my life have been a nightmare I’m praying to wake up from,” Muniz wrote. “Everything felt heavy, unclear, and like it was falling apart at the same time. I wouldn’t wish this season on anyone.”
Muniz said the experience had also forced him to spend more time reflecting on himself and the parts of his life that he wants to change. He described that self-reflection as an “unexpected gift”, saying he had been able to confront the areas that needed work rather than presenting a polished version of himself to the world.
The actor, 40, said he had recently read that sometimes “hitting rock bottom” can be the experience that forces people to make changes they have been putting off. He added that he hopes he will eventually look back on this period with gratitude because it helped him build a better life.
Muniz’s comments come around two months after he and Price announced that they were ending their marriage. The couple had been together for 10 years and share a five-year-old son, Mauz. Muniz has not directly said that his recent struggles were caused by the separation.
Despite describing the period as one of the lowest points in his life, Muniz said he sees it as the beginning of a rebuilding process rather than the end of his story.
“This isn’t the end of the story. It’s the part where I start doing the work,” he wrote, adding that he wants to treat the difficult period as “the foundation, not the finish line”.

title: Trump signs bill authorising sweeping Russia sanctions
description: Bill targets companies and foreign actors aiding Russia s military and extends sanctions against Iran
content:
Bill targets companies and foreign actors aiding Russia's military and extends sanctions against Iran
US President Donald Trump signed a bill on Friday authorising new sanctions designed to pressure Russia over its war in Ukraine, after Congress gave its approval after months of delay.
Washington is pushing to revive a mediated path towards ending the conflict as Moscow intensifies attacks against Ukraine, even though much of its attention — and munitions — are focused on the ongoing war against Iran.
The legislation, which US lawmakers approved this week, takes aim at Russia's energy and defense sectors, alongside President Vladimir Putin and other senior officials.
It also targets Moscow's so-called shadow fleet of tankers used to evade Western sanctions, and allows Trump the authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 percent on major buyers of Russian oil and gas.
That could potentially cover China and India, and further efforts to cut off revenue financing Moscow's war.
The Republican-led House of Representatives passed the package by a 262-159 vote on Wednesday.
The bill would also target companies and foreign actors supporting Russia's military, and extend sanctions involving Iran.
But the broad powers to impose tariffs sparked an unusual split among Democrats, who largely support Ukraine but have resisted handing Trump wider authority over trade.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky earlier hailed the legislation as "symbolic" and thanked US lawmakers.
The bill is "an extremely powerful tool that can stop this terrorist war and bring Russia to the point where it has to make peace", Zelensky wrote on X.
It is symbolic that the U.S. House of Representatives passed the Lindsey Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act on the night of yet another Russian attack on Ukraine with ballistic and other missiles and drones. Once again, civilian infrastructure was targeted, with damage… pic.twitter.com/xFz458d4AN
"Sanctions must be strong so that all efforts for peace — including our joint diplomatic efforts with the United States, Europe, and our other friends — can succeed," he added.
Read More: Putin says Russia has no aggressive intentions toward Europe, ready to restore relations
India said on Thursday it would continue buying oil "through diversified sourcing".
New Delhi — which counts Russia as one of its most important strategic partners — has navigated the energy crisis sparked by the US-Iran conflict in part by turning to Moscow, despite pressure from Western countries.
Supporters of the legislation argued that tougher economic pressure is needed against Moscow, which launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
The Congress vote was celebrated by pro-Ukraine activists, who pointed to continuing Russian attacks, including drone strikes on Wednesday on civilian transport in the south that officials in Kyiv said killed five people.
Trump has generally preferred to retain control over sanctions and tariffs rather than have Congress dictate policy, helping delay the measure for more than a year.
The president's signing of the bill comes a week before he is due to meet with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in Washington.

title: Japan   s emperor opens Asian Games
description: Pakistan   s contingent joins opening ceremony as competition gets underway in the quadrennial spectacle
content:
Pakistan’s contingent joins opening ceremony as competition gets underway in the quadrennial spectacle
The 20th Asian Games were declared open by Japan's emperor on Saturday following a troubled build-up to the multi-sport spectacle that has more athletes than the Olympics.
There were a large number of empty seats at the 30,000-capacity stadium in Nagoya, where a subdued crowd saw a colourful opening ceremony on a heart-shaped stage.
Japan's emperor and empress were given a respectful reception as they took their seats alongside International Olympic Committee’s (IOC) president Kirsty Coventry.
There was polite applause when emperor Naruhito declared the Games open.
The first gold medal will be won on Sunday morning, likely in the men's individual triathlon, as the continent's finest athletes compete in more than 40 sports before the curtain comes down on October 4.
The event in Nagoya and Aichi prefecture has 2028 Olympics places up for grabs in seven sports and will be graced by global stars and fast-rising prodigies.
But it has been dogged by a series of problems as more than 11,000 athletes and 6,000 officials stretched organisers to the limit as they tried to accommodate all.
To save money there is no traditional athletes' village, competitors instead staying in a combination of temporary container-style huts, hotels and cruise ship the Costa Serena.
There was a record deluge last week which flooded parts of Nagoya and now a typhoon is approaching eastern Japan threatening further disruption in the coming days.
Some athletes were left stranded at the airport when transport failed to turn up and several teams have complained about the quality of the huts, including the beds being too short.
In the latest mishap, North Korea's national anthem was played on Friday for South Korea's men's hockey team.
Two-time Asian Games silver medallist Zahra Kiani was a flag-bearer for Iran and hopes to win another medal in the Chinese martial art of wushu by watching how it's done on YouTube.
"I have been training with movies. I watch videos of Chinese athletes and I try to copy them," she said.
The Olympic Council of Asia said the continent's premier sporting event, featuring 45 countries and territories, had found the perfect host.
"When the world has needed it most, Japan has always answered," OCA president Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al-Thani said, referring to the Covid-delayed Tokyo Olympics in 2021.
He called those Games "a remarkable showcase of resilience, hospitality and commitment".
Apart from Japan's athletes, the biggest cheer was reserved for China's competitors as they filed into the arena.
China will again expect to top the medals table after winning a whopping 201 golds and 383 medals on home soil in Hangzhou last time.
As always at the Asian Games which started in 1951, Olympic staples such as athletics and swimming will sit side-by-side with regional favourites like sepak takraw and kabaddi.
There will be eSports, breakdancing and BMX cycling. Padel and MMA will make their Asian Games debuts.
Among those competing will be Philippine tennis sensation Alexandra Eala and a pair of prodigies in 15-year-old Indian cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and 13-year-old Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi.
Taiwan boxer Lin Yu-ting will also be competing, two years after she won Paris Olympics gold in the middle of a major gender row that saw her eligibility questioned.
North Korea will have more than 100 athletes competing across 14 sports, aiming to "bring joy to Marshal Kim Jong Un".
Sooryavanshi will be part of an India cricket team looking to make a statement before the sport returns to the Olympics in Los Angeles after an absence of 128 years.
India could face bitter rivals Pakistan in the final at Nagoya's new purpose-built cricket ground if rain does not intervene.
Meanwhile Asian Games organisers offered deepest apologies for playing the North Korean national anthem for the South Korean men's hockey team.
South Korean officials were left angered by the latest mishap to hit the Nagoya-Aichi Games, which officially opened after a troubled build-up.
At their Friday contest against Bangladesh, South Korea's players lined up for the traditional playing of the anthems, only to look bemused as North Korea's song rang out.
Organisers then played Bangladesh's anthem and later the South Korean one, the South's Yonhap news agency said. South Korea went on to win 5-0.
"During the men's hockey match between (South) Korea and Bangladesh on September 18, an incorrect national anthem was mistakenly played before the match," the Asian Games organising committee told AFP on Saturday.
The statement said that, on Friday, "officials responsible for National Olympic Committee relations visited the delegation of the Republic of Korea and offered their sincere apologies for the incident".
"We will also work to prevent a recurrence and would like to express our deepest apologies to all those affected by this matter."
A stadium announcer apologised for the blunder but Min Tae-seok, coach of South Korea, was unimpressed.
"This is a really serious problem. When we protested, they said, 'We're sorry. It wasn't that it wasn't prepared, there was a mistake on the part of those responsible for playing it'," he said.
"But this is something that simply should never happen."
The build-up to the Games has been overshadowed by complaints from teams about the quality and amount of accommodation.
Some teams were also stranded at the airport for up to six hours when they landed this week.
Members of Pakistan's contingent wave national flag during a march-past at the opening ceremony of the 20th Asian Games at Nagoya. Photo: AFP
As many as 55 Pakistani athletes and officials attended the opening ceremony of the Asian Games in Nagoya, with women’s cricket captain Fatima Sana and squash player Noor Zaman carrying the national flag during the parade.
The contingent included athletes from women’s cricket, kabaddi, mixed martial arts, rowing, squash, table tennis and wushu.
Fencing and badminton were initially included in the delegation for the ceremony but could not take part because of their delayed departure from Pakistan.
Only athletes staying in Nagoya were invited to the ceremony, while those based in other cities did not attend.
Pakistan face Sri Lanka in the women’s T20 semi-final on Sunday at Nisshin, with the teams having a closely matched record.
Of their 25 previous T20 internationals, both sides have won 12 matches, with one ending without a result.
Sri Lanka defeated Pakistan in the recent Asia Cup, while Pakistan reached the semi-finals after surviving a late scare against Thailand in the quarter-finals. They chased a target of 92 with two balls to spare after losing seven wickets.
Pakistan will look to strengthen their batting against Sri Lanka, with captain Fatima Sana expected to play a key role with both bat and ball.
Wicket-keeper Muneeba Ali is absent from the tournament because her mother is ill, leaving Gull Feroza to take over behind the stumps.
Sri Lanka will rely on experienced batter Chamari Athapaththu, who has been a consistent performer for the side.
Nilakshika Silva is unavailable after fracturing a finger during the Asia Cup, while Vishmi Gunaratne was left out of the squad. Batter Hansima Karunaratne and seamer Rashmika Sewwandi were given opportunities in Sri Lanka's opening match.
The other semi-final pits India against Bangladesh at the same venue, with the winners of the two matches meeting for the gold medal.
Pakistan begin their men’s hockey campaign against Thailand at the Kawasaki Juko Stadium on Sunday.
They are in Group B alongside Malaysia, China, Oman and Uzbekistan. Defending champions India are in Group A with Japan, South Korea, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Indonesia.
The top two teams from each group will advance to the semi-finals on October 1, with the gold and bronze medal matches scheduled for October 3.
Pakistan recently completed a training tour of South Korea after finishing 11th at the FIH World Cup.
Malaysia are regarded as the strongest opponent in Pakistan’s group, while a potential semi-final against Japan could provide a tougher test if Pakistan finish top of their pool and India win Group A.
Pakistan eventer Usman Khan will make his Asian Games debut in the eventing competition with his horse Mirage.
Usman had qualified for the previous three Asian Games but was unable to participate because of financial constraints.
He and Mirage have been performing well in recent competitions and are expected to deliver at the Games.

title: IMF tells EU ministers AI could boost growth but increase economic strains
description: IMF says 60  of workers in advanced Europe face AI exposure  with some gains and others risking job losses
content:
IMF says 60% of workers in advanced Europe face AI exposure, with some gains and others risking job losses
Artificial intelligence ‌could lift European productivity by about 1% over five years, but risks widening inequality, straining power networks and increasing dependence on foreign technology unless governments deepen economic integration, an International Monetary Fund paper said.
The ​background note, prepared for an informal meeting of European Union finance ministers in Dublin ​on September 18-19, said the benefits and costs of AI were likely ⁠to be distributed unevenly across countries, regions and workers.
It said completing the EU single market ​would help spread AI adoption and its gains more evenly across the 27-nation bloc.
The paper ​echoes concerns raised by former European Central Bank President Mario Draghi and the European Commission that Europe's fragmented capital, labour and energy markets are holding back investment and innovation.
Read More: Gemini hacked three companies in first known breakout by Google's AI
The IMF estimated that around 60% of ​workers in advanced European economies are employed in occupations highly exposed to AI. While some ​could become more productive through AI tools, others faced displacement as routine tasks become automated, it said, ‌particularly ⁠in jobs where AI is more likely to replace labour than complement it.
The paper said Europe's data centres already consume roughly 3% of the continent's electricity and that demand would rise sharply as AI use expands. Major technology hubs such as Frankfurt, London, Amsterdam, Paris and ​Dublin are among the ​areas most exposed, with ⁠data-centre clusters already putting pressure on local power networks.
To address that, the EU should invest in cross-border grid infrastructure and deepen integration ​o.f the European energy market, the IMF said.
The paper also warned that ​Europe risks ⁠developing another strategic dependency because the US and China dominate the development of AI models. It said Europe would need significant investment in its own AI industry to avoid becoming reliant on ⁠foreign ​technology.
AI's gains are also likely to be unevenly distributed ​across and within the EU, the paper said. More advanced economies are expected to benefit disproportionately because they are ​better prepared for and more exposed to the technology.

title: China s StarWhisper Telescope earns place in Stanford AI Index Report
description: The system simulates telescope components and observations to test controls  train agents and optimise procedures
content:
The system simulates telescope components and observations to test controls, train agents and optimise procedures
China's StarWhisper Telescope has been cited in Stanford University's AI Index Report 2026 as a leading 2025 example of AI agents in physics, astronomy, chemistry and materials science, signaling growing international recognition for the country's AI-driven observation efforts.
Led by the National Astronomical Observatories of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (NAOC), the telescope explores how large models and AI agents can be integrated with telescope control systems, enabling agents to help plan tasks and carry out observations based on researchers' requirements, scientific objectives, equipment status and observing conditions.As large models, AI agents and embodied intelligence advance rapidly, AI is moving beyond data analysis into the operation of scientific instruments and the conduct of research. The NAOC launched its AI for Astronomy program to seize this shift.
The program explores AI applications in astronomical data processing, scientific discovery, telescope control and coordinated observations across multiple facilities. Its goal is to move from isolated algorithms to an intelligent tool system spanning the entire research process.
Recently, the team reported new progress centered on the StarWhisper Telescope in three areas: digital simulation of research-grade telescopes, coordination between scientific models and observation-control systems, and autonomous observation by AI agents.
The telescope has expanded its simulation capabilities with a digital simulation system for large-aperture research telescopes, creating an experimental environment where AI agents can take part in observation planning and validate control strategies.
China's StarWhisper Telescope has been cited in Stanford University's AI Index Report 2026 as a leading 2025 example of AI agents in physics, astronomy, chemistry and materials science, signaling growing international recognition for the country's AI-driven observation efforts… pic.twitter.com/qgjsG04Rlm
Research-grade telescopes are complex instruments whose observation processes are shaped by the optical tube, mount, camera, sensors, control systems and weather. For AI agents to play a substantive role in telescope operations, they first need an environment that can sense equipment status, understand observation conditions and test control strategies.
Read More: Alibaba open-sources AI model detecting cancer, 150 medical conditions
rawing on its long experience in telescope operation and control, along with an agent toolchain developed in recent years, the NAOC research team built the digital simulation environment quickly.
Without consuming actual telescope observing time, the system can simulate telescope components, sensor states, environmental changes and observation workflows, laying a foundation for testing control strategies, training agents and optimizing observation procedures.
The team is also exploring a system that links scientific models, environmental models, telescope control systems and AI agents, enabling agents to monitor and invoke different tools and devices.
AI agents can further weigh scientific-target priorities, the telescope's real-time status and target visibility windows to autonomously complete a closed loop of state perception, task planning, plan generation and workflow validation.
To date, the agents have flagged eight very early supernova candidates, two of which triggered follow-up observations when weather conditions permitted.

title: Alibaba open sources AI model detecting cancer  150 medical conditions
description: AI model analyses CT scans of 18 abdominal organs  detecting diseases  abnormalities and malignant tumours
content:
AI model analyses CT scans of 18 abdominal organs, detecting diseases, abnormalities and malignant tumours
Alibaba has open-sourced an artificial intelligence (AI) model capable of identifying nearly 150 abdominal conditions, including cancers, from computed tomography (CT) scans.
The vision-language model, called Damo Radar, was developed by Alibaba's research arm, Damo Academy, the institute said Friday, according to the Hong Kong-based South China Morning Post.
The model analyzes contrast-enhanced CT scans covering 18 abdominal organs and can identify a broad range of diseases and abnormalities, including malignant tumors.
Also Read: China's AI supercluster completes 10-day global forecast in under an hour
Damo Radar achieved an average area under the curve (AUC) score of 0.913 across 146 clinical findings in nearly 40,000 real-world examinations, approaching the maximum score of 1.0.
The research team described it as "the world's first expert-level generalist medical imaging model," adding that it could eventually be expanded to other types of medical imaging.
In a study involving 26 radiologists from multiple hospitals, the model outperformed 23 participants on average.
With the model's assistance, radiologists also reduced missed diagnoses by 10% and cut diagnosis time by more than 30%.

title: Protesters form human chain at Kennedy Centre after Trump threat
description: Main building remains shuttered as judge reviews long term closure to accommodate Trump s renovations
content:
Main building remains shuttered as judge reviews long-term closure to accommodate Trump's renovations
Protesters formed a human chain on Friday around the Kennedy Centre, the Washington arts hub that United States President Donald Trump threatened to demolish unless his name is restored to it .
The complex's main building has been shuttered since Wednesday — temporarily, according to its leadership — while a judge is also reviewing plans for a long-term closure to accommodate Trump's desired renovations of the aging facility.
Crowds waved placards reading "hands off Kennedy Centre" and broke out into song beneath the scaffolding and tarps that have remained in place since workers removed Trump's name from the building in June following a court order.
Read: Kennedy Center ordered to pay $250,000 to jazz musician it sued after he cancelled performance
Trump took control last year of the Kennedy Centre — inaugurated in 1971 following the assassination of US president John F Kennedy — and has pushed for a major renovation, claiming the building had been left in a state of disrepair by previous leaders.
Like other projects around the US capital, the president has shown an unprecedented keenness to put his personal touch on plans, while testing the legal bounds of executive authority.
Trump's handpicked Kennedy Centre board voted last year to officially rename the institution as the Trump-Kennedy Centre, with corresponding updates to building signage and online logos. The move — later reversed by a judge — led to a major decline in ticket sales, artist boycotts and an exodus of donors, according to The Washington Post .
"It makes me sick to my stomach," said Neal Racioppo, a Washington resident who runs marketing and communications for a theatre. Trump "can't get his name on this cherished building, so he is depriving the world of what it could be."
Racioppo, 57, joined a human chain that formed as night fell on the imposing, white, marble building, with crowds sprawling out onto the esplanade overlooking the Potomac River.
Demonstrators were zigzagged around the barriers installed after the centre closed this week, with some waving placards reading "hands off Kennedy Centre" and "Donny, you are no JFK".
"It has been an important home for the arts for this city and this country and the world," Racioppo said. "What President Trump is doing is despicable."
Read More: Trump bans CNN, MS NOW, Politico from White House
Lizzy Andrew, who has performed several times at the Kennedy Centre, including singing with the National Symphony Orchestra, said she was angered at Trump's threat to tear down the venue.
"He does not have a right to decide that an institution, a living memorial to a past president, can be demolished," the 30-year-old told AFP . "I think you can see tonight that the people of DC and the people of America do not agree with that decision."
Lela Agnew, who regularly brings her children to visit the centre, said she came to defend an institution that "belongs to the people".
"I've been coming here for about 50 years," she said. "It's not a place that needs to be demolished." "It's just not a political place."

title: Gwyneth Paltrow reveals how she and Chris Martin decided to    consciously uncouple
description: Paltrow has previously acknowledged that the phrase attracted significant criticism
content:
Paltrow has previously acknowledged that the phrase attracted significant criticism
Gwyneth Paltrow has opened up about the decision she and Chris Martin made to end their marriage while remaining a family for the sake of their children.
Speaking on the Friends Keep Secrets podcast, Paltrow explained that she and the Coldplay frontman were living in London when they began considering how to separate without creating the kind of lasting tension she had seen in other families.
Paltrow said she spoke to friends who had grown up with divorced parents and asked what had affected them most. She said their answers focused less on the divorce itself and more on the years of tension and strained family relationships that followed.
That led Paltrow and Martin, who share daughter Apple and son Moses, to look for a different approach. They worked with a therapist who introduced them to the concept of “conscious uncoupling”, ultimately committing to putting their children first and remaining a family even though they would no longer be a couple.
The arrangement required effort from both of them. Paltrow recalled that after moving from London to Los Angeles, the family would have Sunday brunch together. On one occasion, when tensions began to rise, she and Martin stepped outside, hugged and agreed to put the disagreement aside before returning to the meal.
Paltrow and Martin announced their separation in 2014, using the phrase “conscious uncoupling”, which quickly became part of popular culture. Their divorce was finalised in 2016, and Paltrow later married Brad Falchuk in 2018.
Paltrow has previously acknowledged that the phrase attracted significant criticism. In January, she revealed that the backlash even contributed to her losing a film role after a distributor reportedly considered her “too hot to touch” following the announcement.
More than a decade after their separation, Paltrow continues to describe the decision as an effort to protect her children from the prolonged conflict she had seen divorce create in other families.

title: Hammad Azhar s mother  wife move LHC for access during 21 day physical remand
description: The petitioners express concern over PTI leader s safety  well being  and lawful treatment in custody
content:
The petitioners express concern over PTI leader's safety, well-being, and lawful treatment in custody
The mother and wife of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) leader Hammad Azhar on Saturday approached the Lahore High Court (LHC), seeking permission for access and visitation by family and legal counsel during the suspect’s 21-day physical remand.
The petition, filed by Ishrat Azhar and Mariam Hammad, challenges the September 17 order of the Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) that directed the petitioners to approach the police for access to the held PTI leader.
In their petition, the applicants said that denying them access to Azhar during physical remand was “unlawful” and sought directions from the high court to allow them and his counsel to meet him in accordance with the law.
It further said that the ATC “misinterpreted” Punjab Police Rule 1934 Chapter 26 clause 28 (Interview with prisoners), by directing the petitioners to approach the station house officer (SHO) for a meeting with Azhar. The petition claimed that the rule provides an alternative, rather than cumulative, avenue for obtaining permission to communicate with a prisoner in police custody.
Read: May 9: 47 PTI leaders, workers get 10 years
According to the plea, the ATC granted a 21-day physical remand of Azhar on September 7. His mother and wife subsequently moved an application before the ATC on September 10, seeking permission to meet him and requesting access for his lawyers as well.
A week later, the ATC disposed of their application and directed them to approach the Sarwar Road Police Station SHO for the requested meeting. The petitioners have challenged this order before the LHC, describing it as contrary to constitutional and procedural safeguards.
The petition further argued that Article 10 of the Constitution protects an arrested or detained person’s right to consult a legal practitioner of choice, while Article 10-A guarantees fair trial and due process.
It maintained that meaningful access to legal counsel is particularly important while an accused is in police custody and cannot be denied merely because he is on physical remand.
The petitioners further relied on Rule 12(ii), Part B of Chapter 11, Volume III of the Lahore High Court Rules and Orders, arguing that it recognises an accused person’s right to assistance from counsel and communication with relatives and friends.
The petitioners also submitted that the ATC failed to harmonise the aforementioned provision with Rule 26.28 of the Police Rules and instead imposed an unwarranted restriction on their access to the suspect.
The plea outlined that after being directed by the ATC to approach the SHO, the petitioners submitted an application to the police, but the SHO allegedly refused to receive it, leaving them without an effective means of securing the access contemplated by the ATC order.
Read more: SC seeks AGP’s assistance on FCC jurisdiction over Imran Khan's hospital transfer case
The petitioners have expressed concern over the PTI leader’s safety, well-being, and lawful treatment in custody, arguing that continued denial of access to his family and lawyers was depriving him of an opportunity to obtain legal advice and pursue remedies.
They have asked the LHC to grant “reasonable and regular” access to the suspect’s family and lawyer during the remand period.
Azhar was arrested in Multan on September 6 and handed over to Lahore police for further proceedings, police sources told The Express Tribune .
According to police, Azhar was involved in several cases related to the May 9 events and had been declared a proclaimed offender since May 9, 2023.
The sources further claimed Azhar was detained near the RA Bazaar area and was taken into custody from the home of a close friend. The PTI leader was wanted in the May 9 case involving an attack on the Government Officers’ Residence (GOR) Gate, they said.
ATC had declared Azhar a proclaimed offender over his non-appearance, while the court had also issued his permanent arrest warrants, according to police sources. The sources also said Azhar had been handed over to the investigation wing.
"He is a nominated accused in more than 50 cases related to the May 9 events."

title: Gemini hacked three companies in first known breakout by Google s AI
description: AI agents  growing autonomy and system access have raised questions over safeguards needed to manage risks
content:
AI agents' growing autonomy and system access have raised questions over safeguards needed to manage risks
Google's Gemini model accessed the internet and hacked other companies during a test of its cybersecurity capabilities, ​the first known example of the company's AI systems autonomously committing ‌such an act.
The hacks occurred in May during a cybersecurity test conducted by Irregular, an independent company that conducts cybersecurity evaluations.
During a standard testing evaluation, Gemini found public information ​online and guessed credentials to access three websites it thought were ​within the scope of its test, Heather Adkins, Google's vice president ⁠of security engineering, said in a statement.
"We ensured the three entities were ​made aware, and we worked with our training partner on the changes they’ve ​now made to their testing processes," Adkins said. "These events highlight the importance of training powerful AI models to act responsibly."
Read More: Founder of Chinese startup Spirit AI says robot brains set for 2027 breakthrough
An Irregular spokesperson said the incident involved the same issue ​that affected other AI labs and that all relevant labs were notified ​in late July. "All known issues on our end were remedied and resolved weeks ago," the ‌spokesperson ⁠said.
Similar incidents linked to Irregular were disclosed by Meta, Anthropic and OpenAI. Meta said in August the incident did not involve a sandbox escape or sophisticated cyberattack, while Irregular said it was working on best practices for securely conducting ​AI cybersecurity evaluations.
The incidents ​have raised questions ⁠about the safeguards needed as AI agents gain greater autonomy and access to the internet and computer systems.
In one ​of the cases, the Gemini model guessed passwords until ​it gained ⁠access to a protected system. In the other two cases, the model found credentials in a public repository that allowed it to then access protected systems, according to ⁠the ​Wall Street Journal, which first reported the news ​on Friday.
Adkins said that in all three instances, the model ceased its hacking.

title: Putin says Russia has no aggressive intentions toward Europe  ready to restore relations
description: Accuses Ukrainian govt of turning into dictatorship  names strengthening nuclear triad  absolute priority
content:
Accuses Ukrainian govt of turning into dictatorship, names strengthening nuclear triad 'absolute priority'
Russia has no aggressive intentions toward Europe and is ready to restore relations and cooperate with its European neighbours, said President Vladimir Putin.
Speaking at a meeting of the Military-Industrial Commission on Friday, Putin accused some European leaders of preparing for war with Russia and said they were using the conflict in Ukraine and the alleged Russian threat to justify their policies.
“I want to state once again: Russia has no aggressive intentions toward Europe or European countries,” he said. “There are simply no grounds for this whatsoever. We are ready for cooperation and for restoring relations with our European neighbours.”
He criticised European countries for holding military exercises in the Baltic Sea, saying they included preparations to seize civilian vessels.
“They constantly talk about defending international law and upholding its norms, yet they prepare to seize civilian vessels,” Putin said. He said Moscow would respond if necessary. “Let us live in peace — otherwise, we, too, will be forced to respond.”
Read: Russia accuses US of viewing Europe as potential nuclear battlefield
Putin criticised European leaders for portraying Ukraine as a defender of European values, civilisation and democracy, questioning how Kyiv could defend democracy when its government had “degenerated into a dictatorship.”
He said elections were not being held in Ukraine, and its authorities were using martial law and the war to remain in power, and accused officials of corruption and embezzlement. “And this thoroughly corrupt regime — is it really the main defender of democracy in Europe? That sounds a bit odd,” he said.
Putin accused Ukraine of attempting to interfere with elections in Russia, citing a recent attack on the home of a precinct election commission chairwoman in the village of Oktyabrskoye in the Zaporizhzhia region, in which he said she was killed.
“Representatives of the Kyiv regime — its leadership — speak of peace and propose resuming so-called negotiations . Yet, by committing crimes of this nature, they themselves do everything to ensure that there is no peace and no negotiations,” he said.
Read More: Is NATO ready to fight? The Ukraine war is raising doubts among military analysts
Putin also outlined priorities for Russia’s new State Armament Program, saying it would focus on modernising the armed forces and defence industry amid what he described as evolving global threats.
He identified strengthening Russia’s nuclear triad as the program’s “absolute priority,” saying it guarantees sovereignty and helps maintain the global balance of power.
Putin said 92% of Russia’s Strategic Missile Forces are equipped with modern weapons. He listed strengthening air defence, expanding unmanned and robotic systems, developing precision-strike weapons and completing Russia’s orbital satellite constellation among key priorities.
The satellite network, he said, would improve space-based reconnaissance, navigation, communications and broadband internet capabilities while enabling real-time command and control of troops and weapons.

description: Says it has  completely liberated  Sindh  PPP receiving Rs2 5 billion annually from the federal treasury

Says it has 'completely liberated' Sindh, PPP receiving Rs2.5 billion annually from the federal treasury
Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) leader and Health Minister Mustafa Kamal on Saturday said the 18th Amendment had created “four new countries” within Pakistan, rather than empowering the four provinces.
“I say again and again that this 18th Amendment has not given power to four provinces, but has made four countries. This 18th Amendment has made four new countries,” Kamal said while speaking at a press conference at the MQM headquarters in Bahadurabad, Karachi.
Lamenting the impact of the 18th Amendment, Kamal said that it had “completely liberated” Sindh, questioning why the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) would declare independence when it received Rs2.5 billion annually from the federal treasury.
“You say the country will break, but the country is broken. Your 18th Amendment has broken the country. We want to re-establish this country,” he said.
“After the 18th Amendment, rivers of blood are flowing, instead of the promised rivers of milk,” Kamal added.
He said the federal government had made a mistake by leaving provincial governments “to their own devices” after devolving powers to them.
He also criticised the central government for transferring all institutions and responsibilities to the provinces.
“Even Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre, which was run by the federal government, has been taken over by the provincial authorities.”
Kamal spoke primarily about MQM-P’s demand for the creation of new provinces, particularly the division of Sindh into additional administrative units.
The MQM-P leader said his party wanted to “reunite” the country rather than divide it. He maintained that the creation of new provinces would provide greater administrative access and representation to marginalised communities.
The federal minister said opposition to new provinces was either based on ideological grounds or vested interests. According to him, some opponents of new provinces “do not even acknowledge Pakistan”, while others were resisting the proposal because of their own interests.
He emphasised that the creation of new provinces should not be portrayed as a harbinger of violence.
“Those who say that new provinces will lead to bloodshed are completely wrong,” he stressed.
Kamal also rejected the argument that the demand for new provinces was directed against Sindhis. He said the people of Sindh were “brothers and sisters” and argued that the distinction between “Sindhi and Mohajir (immigrant)” should no longer be used to promote prejudice.
He reminded the Sindh government that the Constitution introduced by PPP founder and former premier Zulfikar Ali Bhutto outlined the provision for dividing provinces.
The MQM-P leader argued that the Sindh government had failed in providing relief to the people, adding that the current ground reality exposes the immense suffering of the citizens.
He quoted examples of children dying after falling into open manholes, shortage of potable water and other problems plaguing Karachi and other parts of Sindh.
He also criticised the Sindh government over what he described as failures in public services and development projects.
Referring to the Yellow Line Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) project, he alleged that funds provided by the World Bank had been “misused” and subsequently returned by the provincial government.
The Yellow Line BRT project spanning over 21 kilometres, from Dawood Chowrangi to Numaish Chowrangi, has suffered constant setbacks. Two months earlier, Senior Minister for Transport and Mass Transit Sharjeel Inam Memon, acknowledging the delay, had asked all relevant authorities to remove all utility-related bottlenecks to ensure early completion of the project.
Kamal also spoke on the government’s delayed response to the Gul Plaza fire incident that took the lives of at least 80 people.
“The building continued to burn for five days, and the mayor decided to visit the site two days after the incident was first reported,” he alleged during the speech.
The federal minister also expressed reservations about the rights of farmers and other marginalised groups in Sindh and said his party would work for the uplift of these people after the new administrative units proposed by the government offer more room for participation.
“New provinces would bring greater empowerment to the people of Sindh.”
He opined that the people of Sindh were among the most vulnerable sections of society, while pointing out that kidnappings and consequent protests by affected families confirmed his viewpoint.
The federal minister further claimed that violence that had once plagued Karachi had ended, attributing the change to MQM-P. He said the party abandoned its own leader, Altaf Hussain, when it realised that it was in “public interest”.
Read more: UN Security Council condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
Responding to questions about the federal government, Kamal said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif was putting in all efforts to help the public despite constraints. He highlighted that the country was heavily indebted and the federal government was bound to comply with conditions attached to loans from the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
“Those who provide loans also impose conditions,” he said, adding that unemployment had increased even before the IMF's involvement.
When probed about the stance of the Punjab government on the creation of new provinces, Kamal said, “Their silence meant consent.” He added that Punjab authorities were governed by “sensible people”.
Kamal also spoke about the recent flurry of attacks on Saudi Arabia by the Houthis.
Expressing solidarity with the Saudi people and condemning attacks against the kingdom, he said MQM-P stood with the government and the armed forces and was ready to act on any instruction received from the state.
Sindh govt rejects calls for new provinces, defends provincial autonomy
The provincial government on Saturday rejected the call for the creation of new provinces and administrative units in Sindh, saying such proposals could undermine provincial autonomy and create divisions.
Reacting to a press conference by Federal Minister Mustafa Kamal on the issue of new provinces, Sindh government spokesperson Sadia Javed said the PPP’s political philosophy was rooted in the slogan, “ Pakistan Khappay (Long live Pakistan)”.
She said those who seek to divide Sindh into administrative units should not claim to be working for the unity of the country, warning, “Those who changed their faces for political expediency should stop dreaming of dividing Sindh.”
Taking a jab at the MQM-P, the spokeswoman also said they resurrected from the “politics of corpses” and are now claiming innocence. She lamented that the party continued to launch attacks on provincial autonomy.
Defending the 18th Amendment, Sadia said, “It strengthened the federation while granting greater rights to the people.”
The spokeswoman also rejected what she described as attempts to create animosity between Sindhis and Muhajirs, and accused MQM-P of reviving politics of division. She maintained that Sindh was a land associated with Sufi traditions and the provincial government would resist all attempts to incite “hatred” for political gains.
Criticising the MQM-P’s past record, she alleged that its politics had contributed only to violence and confrontation in Karachi.
Sadia further accused opposition leaders of using press conferences and controversial statements for publicity, stating that the Sindh government would oppose any attempt to create a rift between the federation and the province.
Referring to criticism of the province’s healthcare system, Sadia said those questioning the performance of Sindh’s hospitals should first account for their own failings.
She also said the Sindh government represents farmers, workers and other sections of the public.
The spokesperson rejected the characterisation of the Sindh administration as a government fuelled by feudal interests.
Sadia emphasised that citizens were now "politically aware" and could no longer be persuaded by emotional slogans and false claims.

title: Brentford hammer neighbours Chelsea
description: This is the third straight defeat for Xabi Alonso s men in Premier League
content:
This is the third straight defeat for Xabi Alonso's men in Premier League
Brentford beat their big-spending west London rivals Chelsea 3-0 on Friday with second-half goals by forwards Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and Fabio Carvalho condemning Xabi Alonso's men to their third straight Premier League game without a win.
Anthony pounced in the 61st minute when he nodded in from close range after Jannik Schuster headed a corner back across the goal which extended Chelsea's long run of league games without a clean sheet to 21.
Thiago made it 2-0 in the 83rd minute when Emiliano Martinez saved from Kevin Schade on a breakaway but the ball dropped to the ⁠Brazilian who made no mistake. Substitute Carvalho wrapped up the win when he turned in a cross by Schade in added time.
Schuster said he and his colleagues had turned up the pressure on Chelsea after the break and the approach paid off.
"I think when the second half began we played it more directly forward and we scored after that so I’m just happy," the Austrian told Sky Sports.
Brentford's win pushed the Bees, who are unbeaten so far in the league, up to third in the table ahead of the remaining weekend fixtures. Chelsea sit in seventh place.
It was the ‌first ⁠home win for Brentford over Chelsea since 1938 and manager Keith Edwards and his players celebrated at the final whistle, with their fans dancing along in the stands.
The usually free-scoring Blues - who had racked up a total of 10 goals in the first four games of the ​season, behind only Brighton & ​Hove Albion on 13 - ⁠came close early on when Pedro Neto's curling shot was saved by Caoimhin Kelleher.
Cole Palmer almost weaved his way through Brentford's defence on ​two occasions but overall Chelsea, missing in-form Brazil striker Joao Pedro ​through injury, ⁠were comfortably held at bay by the home defence.
Alonso made five changes, with captain Reece James also injured. Danny Welbeck got his first league start for the Blues and fellow veteran Jordan Henderson ⁠made ​his Chelsea debut against the club he played for last ​season.
Moises Caicedo remained sidelined due to an injury that has made him miss all but a few minutes of ​the season so far, contributing to Chelsea's defensive fragilities.

title: Visa delay keeps Solano out of national camp
description: Former Peru international will join squad directly in Indonesia after applying for wrong visa category
content:
Former Peru international will join squad directly in Indonesia after applying for wrong visa category
Pakistan head coach Nolberto Solano will join his team directly in Indonesia after a visa delay kept him away from the squad’s training camp in Islamabad ahead of the FIFA ASEAN Cup.
The former Peru international and Newcastle United player was unable to obtain a Pakistani visa in time after applying under the wrong category, the Pakistan Football Federation (PFF) spokesman told The Express Tribune on Saturday.
“He had applied himself for Pakistan visa but had applied for a wrong category and when we came to know we reapplied but you know delays come,” the spokesman said.
The spokesman said Solano would travel directly to Indonesia to join the squad before the tournament, which runs from September 25 to October 5.
Junior coaches are currently overseeing Pakistan’s training camp in the absence of the head coach, with the team preparing for a demanding group stage campaign.
Pakistan have been drawn in Group B alongside Vietnam, Thailand and the Philippines, while hosts Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Bangladesh make up Group A.
Pakistan will open their campaign against Thailand on September 26 at the Si Jalak Harupat Stadium in Bandung before facing the Philippines on September 29 and Vietnam on October 2.
The top team from each group will advance to the final on October 5 at Jakarta’s Gelora Bung Karno Stadium, while the runners-up will meet in the third-place playoff at the same venue earlier that day.
