title: Ed Sheeran changes Philadelphia concert time as protests planned after Macklemore fallout
description: The concert was originally scheduled to begin at 5 30pm local time  but the start time has since been moved to 8pm
content:
The concert was originally scheduled to begin at 5:30pm local time, but the start time has since been moved to 8pm
Ed Sheeran has changed the start time of his Philadelphia concert as the fallout from Macklemore’s removal from his Loop Tour continues, with pro-Palestinian protesters also planning a demonstration outside the venue.
Sheeran is scheduled to perform at Lincoln Financial Field on Saturday, September 19. The concert was originally scheduled to begin at 5:30pm local time, but the start time has since been moved to 8pm on Ticketmaster. The change follows the withdrawal of the tour’s supporting acts, leaving Sheeran without announced opening performers for the Philadelphia show.
Macklemore was removed from the remaining US dates of the tour after making pro-Palestinian comments during his performance at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium earlier this month. Sheeran has said the decision was made by the promoter after upcoming venues communicated that they would pull the shows if Macklemore remained on the line-up.
Following Macklemore’s departure, Finneas, Lukas Graham, Aaron Rowe and Sheeran’s backing band Beoga all withdrew from the remaining dates. Beoga said it fully supported Macklemore’s message, while the other departures further reshaped the remaining tour schedule.
The Philadelphia concert is also expected to draw protests. Local pro-Palestinian groups have announced plans to rally outside Lincoln Financial Field ahead of the show, with organisers saying the demonstration will focus on Palestinian advocacy and concerns over the treatment of Macklemore’s comments.
Ticket resale prices for the Philadelphia show have also fallen as the concert approaches. Tickets that were listed at $91 on Thursday were available for as little as $66.30 on Friday, while other reporting put the cheapest available ticket at around $67. TicketData founder Keith Pagello cautioned that falling resale prices are common immediately before concerts and do not necessarily indicate an effect from the controversy.
Sheeran has said he has personal views about the Israel-Palestine conflict but does not want his concerts to become political forums. He has also denied being responsible for Macklemore’s removal from the tour.

title: Israel seeks  compensation  from US following Saudi F 35 deal  Report
description: Tel Aviv to seek purchasing weapons that Washington previously declined to approve  Israeli media reports
content:
Tel Aviv to seek purchasing weapons that Washington previously declined to approve, Israeli media reports
Israel planned to ask for US additional defence capabilities as "compensation" after Washington agreed to sell F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia, according to Israeli media.
Tel Aviv will seek to purchase weapons systems that US President Donald Trump's administration had previously declined to approve, Israeli news website Walla reported on Friday.
Israel’s military focus extends beyond advanced fighter jets and next-generation stealth aircraft to space-based weapons and the development and production of interceptor aircraft, the outlet said.
Weapons to be demanded by Israeli officials also include "bunker-busting munitions and underground systems capable of operating deep beneath rocky mountains,” it added.
The move is intended to secure a “compensation” from Washington following the F-35 deal with Riyadh, the website said.
Read: US bases in Middle East suffer severe damage from Iranian attacks: report
On Thursday, the US State Department approved a possible $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia.
The package also includes 49 Pratt & Whitney F135-PW-100 engines, along with cryptographic equipment, electronic warfare support, training and logistics packages, according to a notification sent to the US Congress.
If completed, the deal would make Saudi Arabia the first Arab country to acquire F-35 fighter jets, while Israel is currently the only operator of the aircraft in the Middle East.
Israeli officials have repeatedly criticised Saudi Arabia over its refusal to normalise relations with Tel Aviv before the establishment of a Palestinian state along the 1967 borders, a condition which the international community supports while Israel continues to reject.

title: Kingsmen storm into CPL final as Powell powers stunning chase
description: Hetmyer s unbeaten 102 goes in vain as Jamaica overhaul 207 to eliminate table toppers Amazon Warriors
content:
Hetmyer's unbeaten 102 goes in vain as Jamaica overhaul 207 to eliminate table-toppers Amazon Warriors
Rovman Powell produced a blistering late assault as Jamaica Kingsmen chased down 207 to beat Guyana Amazon Warriors by five wickets in Qualifier 2 on Friday and book a place in the Caribbean Premier League final.
Shimron Hetmyer's magnificent unbeaten 102 from 45 balls, featuring eight sixes, appeared to have put Guyana in control after they posted 206 for seven. But a succession of crucial partnerships and Powell's explosive finish carried the Kingsmen home with two balls to spare.
The result completed a remarkable turnaround for the Kingsmen, who are playing their first CPL season, while ending the campaign of the league's top-ranked side.
Jamaica's chase began strongly as Maaz Sadaqat and Kirk McKenzie (34) added 42 in only three overs. Sadaqat fell to Dwaine Pretorius for a 17-ball 41 which contained three sixes and five fours. McKenzie and Keacy Carty steadied the innings with a 48-run stand before Imran Tahir dismissed McKenzie.
Carty then combined with Saim Ayub for 62 from 41 balls, keeping the required rate within reach. Saim's dismissal in the 16th over brought Powell to the crease with Jamaica needing 55 from 29 balls.
Powell initially took his time before attacking Khary Pierre, hitting two sixes in the 17th over. Carty was run out for 56 from 40 balls, but Powell continued the assault, taking another six off Tahir before smashing Shamar Joseph for a four and six in the 19th.
He finished unbeaten on 40 from 17 deliveries, sharing the Player-of-the-Match award with Hetmyer.
Earlier, Guyana stumbled early after Mohammad Haris and Mavendra Dindyal fell inside five overs. Hetmyer then transformed the innings, adding 96 with Shai Hope for the third wicket, with 55 of his runs coming from just 23 balls.
Hetmyer followed with a 65-run partnership with Quentin Sampson, who made 29 from 17, before reaching his second century of the season with a boundary from the final ball of the innings.
The Amazon Warriors, who had won eight of their 10 league matches, were eliminated after losing their third successive game.
The Kingsmen will face Antigua and Barbuda Falcons in Sunday's final.

title: Israeli fire kills three more Palestinians in latest Gaza ceasefire violations

content:
Son of Gaza health ministry director-general among those killed in attacks, medical source says
Three Palestinians, including the son of Gaza Health Ministry Director-General Munir al-Bursh, were killed by Israeli army fire in the enclave on Saturday, as Tel Aviv continues its violations of a truce in place since October 2025 , a medical source said.
Basir al-Bursh was killed in a strike targeting him in the al-Zahra neighbourhood west of the Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza, the source told Anadolu .
Another Palestinian was killed in an Israeli drone strike on the Shujaiya neighbourhood east of Gaza City, the source added.

A Palestinian girl also died of wounds she sustained earlier from Israeli army fire north of the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, the source said.
Meanwhile, Israeli military vehicles intermittently opened fire east of the Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza, witnesses said. No injuries were reported.
Israeli army forces also opened fire in the al-Shakoush area southwest of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, while drones dropped bombs in the area. Israeli helicopters opened heavy fire south of the al-Mawasi area west of Khan Younis and in adjacent areas of Rafah, witnesses said.

According to the latest figures from Gaza’s Health Ministry, Israeli violations of the October 10, 2025 ceasefire agreement have killed 1,386 Palestinians and injured 4,784 others.
Since October 2023, the Israeli army has killed nearly 74,000 Palestinians and injured over 174,000 others in a genocidal war that has also destroyed about 90% of Gaza’s civilian infrastructure.

title: Bob Veldhof targets Pakistan hockey revival
description: Dutch coach says rebuilding is his passion  eyes top level return in two to three years
content:
Dutch coach says rebuilding is his passion, confirms one-year PHF contract with option to extend
KARACHI: Pakistan hockey coach Bob Veldhof has said that rebuilding the national team is his passion and he wants the country to return to the top of the world hockey within two to three years, insisting that becoming head coach was never his primary objective.
“And it's not my goal to be head coach; I am there because we need to bring Pakistan back to the top in two to three years,” Bob told The Express Tribune on Saturday.
The Dutch coach will not accompany Pakistan during the Asian Games, with Herman Kruis set to act as head coach in his absence. Bob's name had initially been included in the squad's list for the Games.
After several weeks of intensive training in Islamabad, Bob handled the Green-shirts at the FIH World Cup in Amstelveen where Pakistan finished 11th.
Bob, who also has business commitments in Europe, said his schedule made it difficult for him to remain with the team for extended periods.
“I was not asked to go to Japan first and in my schedule it was difficult and they have now made another choice,” Bob said.
“It was impossible for me to go with the team to Korea. Japan was possible but without schedule I cannot manage things upfront,” he added.
“I will come back but we still have to discuss,” Bob was quick to add.
Despite his absence from the Asian Games, Bob said he remained committed to Pakistan hockey and praised the Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF) for what he described as positive recent steps towards developing the sport.
“PHF is on the track I believe,” Bob said.
“The changes done in two months are bigger than I saw before and that's a good step,” he added.
Bob also expressed confidence that Pakistan could qualify for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, although he acknowledged that rebuilding the team would take time.
“But I have good relations with the PHF chief Mohyuddin Ahmad Wani and all want us to win the World Cup.”
The Dutch coach said Pakistan needed patience as it worked to rebuild its squad and broaden its options.
“Nothing can happen overnight and time will tell how we get more selection options and how we strengthen the team. I am hopeful that hockey in Pakistan can grow and regain its top status in the world in the next few years,” Bob said.
Bob also clarified the length of his agreement with the PHF, saying he had signed a one-year contract that could be extended.
“I have an agreement for one year which can be extended. PHF wanted two years but I wanted one year and so it happened,” Bob said, dispelling an impression that he had been hired only for four months.
The coach's immediate absence from the Asian Games is therefore not being presented as an end to his association with Pakistan hockey. Instead, Bob said he expected to return, although the schedule and terms of his future involvement still need to be discussed.
For a Pakistan team seeking to rebuild its international standing, Bob's stated objective is longer term; developing greater depth, expanding selection options and creating a side capable of competing at the highest level again within the next few years.

title: Kane hits Bundesliga century as Bayern rout Union
description: He scores a brace a dominating victory
content:
Harry Kane scored twice in Bayern Munich's 7-0 demolition of Union Berlin on Friday, becoming the fastest player to reach 100 Bundesliga goals.
Kane scored his 100th and 101st goals in just 98 domestic games, obliterating the previous record set by Cologne's Dieter Mueller in 1977 by 31 games.
It's the latest record that the England captain has torn up during his time in Munich, having already become the fastest Bayern player to reach 75, 100 and 150 goals in all competitions.
Kane’s double means he now has scored 156 goals in 156 games for Bayern in domestic and international games combined — an unparalleled statistic.
"I'm very proud to reach 101 Bundesliga goals," Kane told Sky Germany.
"In the short time I've been here, I've loved every second of it. When I'm playing with these players - Michael (Olise), Luis (Diaz) and Jamal (Musiala), I'm going to get chances.
"To have more goals than games is obviously a great stat to have," he added.
When asked about his Bayern contract, which expires at the end of the season, and whether he'll still be at the club when the Champions League final returns to Munich in 2028, Kane said: "I'm extremely happy here.
"The talks are ongoing and they'll be ongoing for the near future. You can see the way I'm playing and the way I connect with the fans.
"Munich in 2028? Maybe. It'll be a special one."
Despite Kane's record-breaking exploits, Michael Olise was the main attraction in Munich with the France star scoring a fine hat-trick against the winless Bundesliga strugglers.
Wearing a special kit to celebrate the start of Oktoberfest, it was clear that Bayern were in party mood from the start.
They took the lead in the 18th minute with an explosive opener by Jamal Musiala. Alphonso Davies cut the ball back to Musiala on the edge of the box, and the German let fly with a bullet shot.
Kane's moment arrived in the 39th minute from the penalty spot after Olise was tripped. Kane slammed home the spot-kick for his milestone strike.
Bayern quickly turned two into three before half-time through a fine first-time strike by Olise, who stylishly caressed his shot into the top corner from the edge of the box — but the best from Olise was yet to come.
An early second-half flurry forced Manuel Neuer into two saves in quick succession. The first saw him deny a golden chance for Janik Haberer, whose miss was as good as it got for the visitors.
Union went 4-0 down in the 54th minute when Olise was allowed to pick out Kane with a sumptuous cross from the right, inviting Kane to glance in his second of the night.
Bayern coach Vincent Kompany sent on Ismael Saibari just after the hour and within seven minutes he scored his first Bayern goal. Davies found the Morocco star, who shrugged off his marker and thumped in Bayern's fifth.
Olise added his second of the night three minutes later to make it six, rounding Ronnow and sending his shot in off the near post.
The Frenchman secured his hat-trick another three minutes later bending in a stunning shot from outside the box.
"We're a bit sad that there's now a short break coming up, as we might lose our rhythm a little," Bayern's sporting director Max Eberl told reporters.
"We wanted to go into the international break with an impressive result. We managed that.
"The team showed that when we play at that level, it's hard to keep up with us."
This ruthless victory is Bayern's biggest margin of victory since their 8-1 win over Wolfsburg in January and, for now, puts the champions top of the table.
Freiburg and Borussia Dortmund, the only teams with 100% records this season, can return to the Bundesliga summit on Saturday when they take on Eintracht Frankfurt and Stuttgart respectively.

title: Inam Butt set to return after two month doping ban
description: Pakistan wrestler completes backdated suspension  earns Asian Games clearance  Asian Beach Games silver medal withdrawn
content:
Pakistan wrestler completes backdated suspension, earns Asian Games clearance
Pakistan’s ace-wrestler and administrator Mohammad Inam Butt has completed a two-month suspension imposed over an anti-doping violation and has been cleared to resume wrestling activities, paving the way for him to represent Pakistan at the Asian Games as a coach.
According to documents and sources familiar with the case Inam's suspension was effective from July 19 to September 18 and he has now been informed by the International Testing Agency (ITA) and international wrestling authorities that he is eligible to return to his wrestling duty.
The development comes at a cost, however, with Inam's silver medal from the Asian Beach Games being withdrawn as a consequence of the anti-doping case.
Inam had tested positive for a prohibited substance after taking medication for an eye condition. He told anti-doping authorities that the medicine had been taken for legitimate medical treatment and was not intended to enhance his sporting performance.
The authorities accepted his explanation regarding the medical use of the drug, but Inam had not informed the relevant anti-doping officials in time about the medication, according to the sources.
Under anti-doping rules, athletes are responsible for ensuring that prohibited substances used for legitimate medical purposes are properly declared and authorised where required.
The ITA subsequently accepted Inam's position and has granted him permission to use the medication for one year, according to the sources.
The case nevertheless resulted in the withdrawal of his Asian Beach Games silver medal which he had won in beach wrestling at the event in China early this year.
The wrestler had temporarily stepped away from his administrative responsibilities after the doping issue emerged. He is the secretary of the Pakistan Wrestling Federation and head of the Pakistan Athletes Commission of Pakistan Olympic Association (POA), positions from which he voluntarily separated while the case was being reviewed.
Now, according to sources, he has returned to his work and will be proceeding to Japan with his wrestling squad as a coach.
Earlier Pakistan Wrestling Federation (PWF) president Arshad Sattar was due to proceed with the team to Japan but now when Inam has returned to the fold the federation’s chief will not go.

title: PML N nominee Najeeb Naqi Khan submits papers for AJK president
description: President will be elected by the members of the AJK Legislative Assembly through a vote
content:
President will be elected by the members of the AJK Legislative Assembly through a vote
Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) nominee Dr Muhammad Najeeb Naqi Khan on Saturday formally submitted his nomination papers for the office of president of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), setting the stage for the September 24 presidential election. The AJK Assembly is the electoral college for presidential elections.
The completion of the presidential election will fill the remaining major constitutional office following the recent formation of the new government and the election of the prime minister, speaker and deputy speaker.
The presidential election will complete the formal process of constituting the region’s principal constitutional offices following the 2026 general elections.
Dr Naqi submitted his papers at the office of Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal, who is also serving as the Returning Officer for the presidential election. He was accompanied by PML-N AJK president Shah Ghulam Qadir, Prime Minister Iftikhar Gilani, former prime minister Raja Farooq Haider Khan, Minister and Legislative Assembly member Sardar Mir Akbar Khan, and other members of the Assembly.
Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal received the nomination papers. According to the election schedule, scrutiny of the papers will also be conducted at the office of the Returning Officer on Saturday.
Read: Nawaz Sharif nominates Najeeb Naqi Khan as AJK president candidate
The nomination papers were filed between 10:00am and noon on September 19, while candidates have until 11:30am on September 23 to withdraw their nominations. The final list of candidates will be issued after the withdrawal deadline.
The PML-N President Nawaz Sharif had nominated Dr Naqi as the party’s candidate for the AJK presidency on September 16 and directed him to submit his nomination papers. The nomination was announced by Punjab Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb.
پاکستان مسلم لیگ (ن) کے صدر جناب محمد نواز شریف نے ڈاکٹر محمد نجیب نقی خان صاحب کو آزاد ریاست جموں وکشمیر کے صدر کے منصب پر نامزد کیا ہے اور انہیں صدر آزاد جموں وکشمیر کے عہدے کے لئے کاغذات نامزدگی جمع کرانے کی ہدایت کی ہے۔ جماعت اور اس کی قیادت کی جانب سے ڈاکٹر محمد نجیب نقی کو…
Dr Naqi, who belongs to Sudhanoti district, has previously served as a member of the AJK Legislative Assembly and held several important ministerial portfolios, including health, education, information technology, finance and planning and development.
The office of the AJK president has remained vacant since January 2026 following the death of Barrister Sultan Mahmood Chaudhry. Then-Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Latif Akbar initially performed the duties of acting president. Following the election of Chaudhry Tariq Farooq as speaker on August 25, he subsequently assumed the responsibilities of acting president.
The AJK Election Commission has scheduled the presidential election for September 24. Polling will be held at the AJK Legislative Assembly Secretariat from 10:00am to 1:00pm, followed immediately by counting of votes and announcement of the result.
The president will be elected by the members of the AJK Legislative Assembly through a vote.
Read more: Nawaz shares 100-day uplift plan with AJK PM
The AJK elections were held in three phases between July 27 and August 10, 2026. Of the 45 directly contested constituencies, polling was held on 38, with the PML-N securing 25 seats and the PPP winning 12. The lone MLA of the Awami Dast-o-Bazu party joined hands with the PML-N.
The PML-N increased its strength in the house after securing six of the eight reserved seats. The party won three women's reserved seats as well as the seats reserved for Ulema and Mashaikh, overseas Kashmiris and a technocrat. The PPP secured the remaining two women's reserved seats.
Later, the PML-N announced that Barrister Gillani had been nominated as the party’s candidate for the office of AJK PM. Gillani secured 30 votes against Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) candidate Sardar Mukhtar Ahmed Abbasi, who received 14 votes.
On August 28, Gillani took the oath as the 17th prime minister and Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) leader Chaudhry Muhammad Yasin was appointed Leader of the Opposition.

title: Houthis say they targeted    sensitive sites    in Riyadh  oil sites in Saudi port city Yanbu
description: Council affirms Saudi Arabia s right to self defence  demands release of 73 detained UN personnel in Yemen
content:
Smoke rises from fuel storage depot at Riyadh's King Khalid airport after attack
Yemen's Houthis said they attacked "sensitive" sites in the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday with missiles and drones, hours after flames and a ‌large plume of smoke were seen near the city's main airport.
“In response to the Saudi enemy’s criminal attempts to target the capital Sanaa… the Yemeni Armed Forces carried out two successful military operations using a large number of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones,” Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree says, in a statement on Telegram. “The first targeted sensitive sites in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, and the second targeted Aramco facilities in Yanbu.”
The Saudi government has yet to confirm the blasts.
Earlier, Saudi Arabia had sent alerts overnight warning of potential danger around Riyadh, amid an escalation in attacks by the Houthis in the kingdom.
Smoke rises over Riyadh airport after Houthi strike
A large plume of smoke was visible near Riyadh's main airport on Saturday after booms were heard around the capital, amid an escalation in attacks by Yemen's Houthi group.
Reuters video and photographs showed a huge pillar of black smoke rising in the area, with the airport highway, main terminal building and other facilities in the foreground.
Video footage shows smoke plumes seen near Riyadh's main airport in Saudi Arabia. There has been an escalation in attacks by Yemen's Houthi group since July, with strikes on land in the Red Sea. pic.twitter.com/iKZ3sNJUUs
There was no immediate comment from the Saudi government's media office in response to Reuters questions about the smoke and the overnight alerts.
Saudi civil defence sent the alerts by phone overnight for potential danger in Riyadh and the city of Al-Kharj east of the capital, before issuing an all-clear on Saturday morning. A Reuters journalist in Riyadh's Olaya area heard booms before the all-clear was sent.
Although some alerts had been issued in Riyadh this year after the start of the US-Iran war, these were the first since the escalation began with the Houthis in July.
The Houthis, who ⁠control ​the most populous parts of Yemen and much of the north, ​have been launching attacks towards Saudi Arabia since declaring a naval blockade against Riyadh in July, with strikes targeting Saudi vessels in the Red ​Sea.
The attacks have created new threats to global oil supplies, putting at risk the main alternative Red Sea route for Gulf exports while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains blockaded.
On Friday, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had foiled unspecified "criminal attempts" in the Yemeni capital Sanaa, blaming Saudi Arabia and vowing a response.
The group, which seized Yemen's entire Red Sea coast in a lightning advance this month, says the Saudi Air Force has conducted hundreds of airstrikes against it ​in recent days.
BREAKING: Report of smoke rising near Riyadh airport 🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/yYwONI0AlL pic.twitter.com/4BrDG6slhu
UN Security Council condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
The UN Security Council condemned attacks by Yemen's Houthi group on Saudi Arabia, including strikes on civilian and energy infrastructure that injured civilians, among them women and children.
Council members noted that their August 7 statement condemned Houthi missile attacks on the kingdom and assaults on commercial vessels. They reiterated their condemnation of attacks and threats against shipping in the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb, stressing the importance of safeguarding vessels and their crews.
The council demanded that the Houthis "immediately cease their military escalation" and attacks affecting civilians and civilian objects.
Members expressed grave concern about reports of civilians killed and injured and noted that at least 125,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since the start of September, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs. They warned that further escalation would worsen the country's dire humanitarian situation.
Read: China presses Iran to help rein in Houthis after Saudi appeal, sources say
They called for full, safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access and demanded the unconditional release of detainees, including 73 UN personnel and staff of NGOs, civil society groups and diplomatic missions.
The council further called for practical cooperation with the Yemeni government to prevent the Houthis from acquiring arms, technical assistance, training and financing for military activities. It reminded all member states of their obligations under the targeted arms embargo.
Members expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and affirmed its inherent right to self-defence under international law.
They also reaffirmed their commitment to Yemen's unity, sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, stressing that sustainable peace "cannot be achieved through violence, coercion, or the use of force."
Read more: CDF Munir urges Iran to persuade Houthis not to target Saudi energy facilities: officials
Noting their support for UN Special Envoy Hans Grundberg in pursuing a negotiated, inclusive, Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned political settlement, they also urged the parties to engage constructively with UN efforts.
Saudi Arabia has faced missile and drone attacks attributed to the Houthis in recent days amid escalating regional tensions.
Fighting between Yemeni government forces and the Houthis has also intensified since early July.
The renewed fighting ended a period of relative calm that had largely held since a UN-brokered truce took effect in April 2022.

title: Samar Jafri dedicates new track  Phir Mileinge Hum  to his younger self
description: Song draws support from industry peers including Raamis  Merub Ali  Nameer Nawaz Khan
content:
Song draws support from industry peers including Raamis, Merub Ali, Nameer Nawaz Khan
Singer and actor Samar Jafri released a new single, Phir Mileinge Hum , dedicated to his younger self. Announcing the song on Instagram with a childhood photo of himself holding a toy guitar, Jafri wrote that the track was "for the baby Samar".
In the caption, Jafri reflected on how people often lived up to others' expectations and lost sight of who they were. "I wish I could return to being the carefree child whose biggest worry was getting to school on time," he wrote, urging fans to stay grateful and keep their inner child alive.
Lyrically, the track is a ballad of heartbreak and acceptance. The verses dwell on the uncertainty of life and why love is fleeting, while the chorus turns to spiritual surrender.
The release of Phir Mileinge Hum drew support for Jafri from entertainment industry peers. Some even posted childhood pictures of themselves set to the song, in keeping with the track's sentiment.
Singer Raamis shared Jafri's post on Instagram. "Dropping such beautiful melodies randomly on a Friday like it's nothing," he wrote.
Actor Merub Ali also posted the song on her story alongside a childhood photograph of herself.
Actor Nameer Nawaz Khan followed suit, sharing the song on his Instagram with an AI-generated image of himself gazing at his younger self in a mirror.
Phir Mileinge Hum followed Jafri's previous single Chalo Door Kahin , released in October 2025, and came after Spotify named the singer its RADAR Pakistan artist for Q4 2025.
Jafri first drew attention as a child actor in the drama Parwarish , which also launched his music career. He most recently featured on Express Entertainment’s Raja London Ka , where his on-screen chemistry with Ameema Saleem won fans over.

title: Security forces kill 11 terrorists in Balochistan operations  state media
description: Significant cache of arms and explosive material was also seized during the operations
content:
Significant cache of arms and explosive material was also seized during the operations
Security forces killed 11 terrorists belonging to Fitna-al-Hindustan during targeted operations in Balochistan’s Panjgur and Chagai districts under Operation Radd-ul-Fitna-3 , Radio Pakistan reported on Saturday.
"Eleven terrorists belonging to Fitna-al-Hindustan were killed during targeted actions in Panjgur and Chagai districts," Radio Pakistan quoted security sources as saying.
In the Gowargo area of Panjgur, security forces neutralised five terrorists and recovered a large quantity of weapons and ammunition from their possession, it added.
Meanwhile, security forces conducted operations in the Aminabad and Siah Chang areas of Chagai district, where six terrorists were killed.
A significant cache of arms and explosive material was also seized during the operations, it added.
Security forces kill 11 terrorists in #Balochistan under Operation Radd-ul-Fitna 3 @OfficialDGISPR #News #RadioPakistan https://t.co/c6fTC6qyrh pic.twitter.com/RnWpCc18gr
The federal government last year officially designated all terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as Fitna al-Hindustan , accusing India of sponsoring a proxy war through the outfits.
The high-tempo intelligence-driven operations are being conducted as part of the ongoing " Radd-ul-Fitna-3 " campaign, which the military's media wing has described as a counterterrorism operation aimed at eliminating Indian proxies.
Read: Security forces kill three terrorists during IBO in Balochistan's Awaran: state media
The development came a day after security forces killed seven terrorists affiliated with Fitna al-Hindustan in two separate operations in Balochistan under Operation Radd-ul-Fitna 3 , according to security sources.
Five terrorists were killed during an operation in the Fatah Ali area of Panjgur, while two more terrorists were killed in a separate operation in the Dhadar area of Kachhi district, the sources said.
Several terrorists were also reported to have been injured during the operation, the sources said, adding that a large quantity of weapons and ammunition was recovered from the possession of the dead terrorists.
Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022.
Although Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) has borne the brunt of terrorism, Balochistan has also remained a major target of Indian proxies, which often target civilians and military installations in the province.
In one such attack on the last day of 2025, terrorists targeted innocent civilians in Balochistan’s Gwadar and Kharan districts, where 18 people, including women, children, the elderly and labourers, embraced martyrdom.
Read More: 11 terrorists neutralised in Balochistan
Security forces have continued operations across the provinces against what the state describes as Indian-sponsored terrorists and their proxies, but despite these efforts, the groups have continued to target civilian and defence installations.
On August 21, security forces, in coordination with police, killed 49 terrorists in a series of IBOs across K-P and Balochistan over several days.
In Balochistan, 37 terrorists affiliated with Fitna al-Hindustan were killed in 10 IBOs in Mastung, Mach, Khuzdar and Panjgur districts. The operations had also resulted in the seizure and destruction of weapons, explosives and remote-detonation equipment.

title: Real Madrid lacking control before Atletico derby
description: Los Blancos trail unbeaten champions Barcelona at the top of the table
content:
Los Blancos trail unbeaten champions Barcelona at the top of the table
Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho admitted his team does not know how to control matches ahead of Sunday's La Liga derby clash against Atletico Madrid.
Before the first major test of Mourinho's second spell at the helm, Los Blancos have shown attacking dynamism the coach called "frenetic", but the Portuguese veteran acknowledged his team cannot shut the door on opponents.
Madrid trail unbeaten champions Barcelona at the top of the table by three points, after losing one of their six opening games and winning the other five, with Atletico third.
However they needed late strikes by back-up striker Carlos Espi to secure wins at Espanyol and Elche to cling to Barcelona's tail.
"The problem seems obvious to me. It's harder to know why, but it's easy to understand that there are matches that seem over and, in the end, aren't," said Mourinho.
"(There are) matches where we have three, four, five chances to finish them and don't.
"After failing to do so, it feels like we go from ease, because it seemed easy, to losing control."
Wily Atletico coach Diego Simeone will aim to punish Madrid if they take their eye off the ball in the derby.
Mourinho said his team's defensive issues were of concern for that game and beyond.
"Not just for Sunday's match, but for every match. I like my team to score goals... but I also like controlling matches," explained Mourinho.
"I don't like gifting control. It's not about the goals, it's about giving away control of the match."
Bernardo Silva is likely to start against Atletico after being rested against Elche on Tuesday, which could help Madrid take a firmer grip on the game, although Mourinho's squad does not seem ideally equipped to control matches despite a lavish summer spending spree.
"We're a frenetic side, who gets the ball back and accelerates," said Mourinho.
Madrid's team is defined by their star attacking trio of Vinicius Junior, Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham, which effectively ensures they will play at great pace, regardless of the scenario, which can leave them exposed at the back.
Vinicius Junior is often jeered by Atletico Madrid fans and that could be exacerbated in Sunday's away trip after the forward, along with team-mates Kylian Mbappe and Ibrahima Konate, did not fully wear a t-shirt supporting the people of Ceuta.
The Madrid trio partially obscured a message on the shirt reading "we are all Ceutans", regarding the Spanish territory in north Africa affected by a migration crisis with Morocco.
La Liga president Javier Tebas criticised the three players on Wednesday for not wearing the shirt properly ahead of Madrid's late win against Elche.
Mbappe said his decision to roll up the shirt was to make a gesture in support of immigrants who had lost their lives while trying to cross the border, but also supported Ceutans.
Vinicius has been whistled by his own fans in recent weeks for poor goalscoring form, and he could not find the net again in the narrow victory at Elche.
Mourinho said he is waiting for the Vinicius that "kills" games and led Madrid to two Champions League triumphs to return, and Sunday would be the perfect occasion.
"The goals will come back, I can't miss so many (chances)," wrote Vinicius on Instagram after the Elche game, in which he spurned three good opportunities.
The forward has one goal this season, in contrast to Mbappe, who boasts eight across all competitions.
Mourinho hailed the lethal French striker as "not normal" and the red-hot Mbappe will see the derby clash as another opportunity to pick up votes in his Ballon d'Or campaign, as well as keeping the pressure on Barcelona.
Since Mbappe arrived in Madrid in 2024, the Spanish giants have failed to win a major trophy.
To stop Flick's free-scoring Barca, who have won La Liga two years running, Madrid cannot afford to drop many points, let alone against Simeone's side.
The coaches clashed four times during Mourinho's first spell in charge, three of which he won, but Simeone's one victory came in the 2013 Copa del Rey final.
If Madrid take the lead at the Metropolitano on Sunday Mourinho will hope his side can heed his warnings not to let Atletico back in.

title: Iraq sees September 30 end of coalition military mission as step toward sovereignty  bilateral ties
description: Date represents    sovereign milestone     relations with coalition states shift to bilateral partnerships  govt spokesman
content:
Date represents ‘sovereign milestone,’ relations with coalition states shift to bilateral partnerships: govt spokesman
Iraq said on Friday that the September 30 end of the military mission of the US-led international coalition against ISIS (Daesh) will pave the way for bilateral relations with coalition member states based on respect for Iraqi sovereignty and mutual interests.
Government spokesman Haider al-Aboudi told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the date represented a “sovereign milestone” for the Iraqi state based on official understandings and commitments.
He said it would pave the way for Iraq’s relations with coalition countries to transition to bilateral ties based on respect for Iraqi sovereignty and mutual interests.
Read: Iraq proposes strategic economic ties
Al-Aboudi said Iraq had constitutional, political and diplomatic tools, as well as the ability to manage security through its institutions and armed forces.
“The government is proceeding with completing the termination of the coalition’s military mission according to the agreed timelines and mechanisms, and there will be no change to this course outside the will of the Iraqi state,” he said.
He said Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi has placed Iraqi sovereignty at the forefront of his government’s priorities and designated “Sovereignty Day” to mark the transition to a new phase characterised by full state authority over its territory, unified security decision-making and state control over the instruments of force.
Al-Aboudi added that the government was seeking to consolidate stability and confidence in state institutions to provide a secure investment environment, attract companies and capital, and establish balanced and productive partnerships in line with the state’s priorities and national interests.
Read more: Iraqi parliament approves partial govt
Al-Zaidi said last month that Sept. 30 would be the “fixed and final” deadline for ending the international coalition’s military mission and completing the withdrawal of forces from Iraq.
The US-led international coalition was established in 2014 to fight ISIS (Daesh) after the group seized large areas of Iraq and neighbouring Syria.
Iraq declared victory over ISIS in December 2017 after retaking territory held by the group, while coalition forces remained in the country in an advisory and training role at Baghdad’s request.

title: Iran  China used AI agents in novel influence campaigns  NYT report
description: Campaigns used freely available Chinese AI models to create autonomous    agents  capable of carrying out online task
content:
Campaigns used freely available Chinese AI models to create autonomous ‘agents' capable of carrying out online task
Iran and China, along with groups in Israel, have used artificial intelligence (AI) in novel social media influence campaigns in recent months, The New York Times reported on Friday.
It raises concerns for US officials and cybersecurity researchers about the technology’s growing ability to operate with limited human involvement.
The report said the campaigns used freely available Chinese AI models to create autonomous “agents” capable of carrying out online tasks. Hundreds of the agents were reportedly deployed to establish networks of fake accounts on US social media platforms including Instagram, Facebook, X and TikTok.
The AI agents then populated the accounts with posts about politics and current events, while coordinating messaging and interactions online.
Read: Founder of Chinese startup Spirit AI says robot brains set for 2027 breakthrough
US officials and researchers described the activity as among the first known cases in which AI agents powered by Chinese models were used in nearly the entire process of an influence campaign.
The campaigns were described as relatively crude but significant because they demonstrated how publicly available AI systems can automate operations that previously required substantial human involvement.
The report said US intelligence agencies, technology companies and security researchers investigated the activity and traced the Chinese and Iranian operations to state-backed actors.
The Iranian campaign targeted US audiences, with AI-generated accounts posing as ordinary Americans in major cities. The accounts reportedly posted popular memes, tagged journalists and politicians and promoted views critical of the Republican Party.
Read more: Anthropic's Claude helped cybersecurity researchers breach OpenAI: report
Nearly 80,000 people followed the AI-generated accounts, which were active during the first half of the year, according to the report.
The report also detailed two Israeli campaigns attributed to private companies. One, linked to Tel Aviv-based IntelEye, involved AI agents controlling thousands of social media accounts and engaging with discussions surrounding Israel’s upcoming elections.
The company said the activity was a defensive research experiment designed to test how AI models could be misused.

title: US warns allies of weapons delivery delays due to stocks depleted by Iran war  Bloomberg
description: Several European countries are facing delays in receiving missile and air defense systems
content:
Several European countries are facing delays in receiving missile and air defense systems
The US has warned its allies to expect delays of up to five years in deliveries of key weapons as Washington works to replenish munitions stocks depleted during its war with Iran, Bloomberg reported Friday.
Several European countries are facing delays in receiving missile and air defence systems, while Germany has asked Washington to accelerate deliveries of Tomahawk cruise missiles and Typhon launchers. However, shortages of the weapons mean Raytheon, a unit of the RTX Corp., may not be able to fulfil the order within five years, according to the report.
The shortages are also affecting Ukraine, which has sought additional Patriot air defence interceptors ahead of an expected difficult winter. US President Donald Trump has said Washington was discussing either providing Ukraine with a less advanced version of the Patriot system or allowing European countries to manufacture the weapons under license.
Read: Iran war exposed 'strategic' US munitions shortfalls: Pentagon watchdog
In the conflict with Iran, now in its seventh month, the US is estimated to have used more than half of its advanced Patriot missile variants , about one-third of its Tomahawk missiles, and nearly half of its precision strike missiles and THAAD interceptors.
Pentagon officials have acknowledged that heavy weapons use has created strategic inventory shortfalls and exposed production bottlenecks. Defence companies are now increasing output, including Lockheed Martin, which plans to raise annual production of PAC-3 MSE Patriot interceptors from about 600 to 2,000.
European leaders are expected to press Trump next week for additional Patriot support for Ukraine during meetings at the UN in New York.
EU officials also hope to secure US licenses allowing European countries to produce Patriots for Kyiv.

Farooq reached his century in just 67 balls, combining 11 fours with his record haul of sixes to surpass Majid Khan’s mark for the most sixes by a Pakistan batter in a first-class innings.
His assault set the platform for Markhor IT Solutions, who closed on 476-4 against Khan Research Laboratories at the Shoaib Akhtar Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi.

Shoaib Akhtar Junior claimed 5-34 and Khurram Shahzad took 4-42 to share nine wickets for Ghani.
At Peshawar, Kingsmen Academy skipper Mohammad Tayyab Arif marked only his second first-class appearance with his maiden century, scoring 105 as his side were bowled out for 215 by Oil and Gas Development Company Limited.
OGDCL pacer Mohammad Amir Khan took 5-51, his fifth five-wicket haul in first-class cricket, while Mohammad Hasnain claimed 3-36. OGDCL reached 57-3 by the close.
State Bank of Pakistan finished the day on 278-9 against Pakistan Television in Abbottabad, with Hasan Raza scoring 75 and Mohammad Ghazi Ghori making 66. Rameez Aziz was unbeaten on 42 at stumps.

title: US and Denmark reach deal on Greenland  Trump says
description: US president writes no US enemies will be able to make sensitive investments on island without America s approval
content:
US president writes no US enemies will be able to make sensitive investments on island without America's approval
The United States, Denmark and Greenland have entered into an agreement for the US to ‌develop a significant military presence on Greenland, while prohibiting US adversaries from building their own bases on the island, US President Donald Trump said on Friday.
In a Truth Social post, the US president wrote that no US enemies would be able to make sensitive investments on the island without the approval of the US and that the agreement had no expiry date.
"At my ​direction, we worked with representatives of Denmark and Greenland to guarantee that the United States will FOREVER have the complete ability to do ​what is necessary in Greenland to secure and defend the security of Greenland, and the United States of ⁠America," Trump wrote.
Earlier on Friday, Reuters exclusively reported that the US and Denmark were closing in on a deal that would result in an increased ​US military presence in Greenland, an autonomous territory of Denmark, but would stop well short of Trump's long-held dream of acquiring the island for the US.
Read: Trump reiterates at NATO summit that Greenland should be controlled by US, not Denmark
The US already has nearly total overflight and basing rights in Greenland due to a 1951 treaty.
Trump's announcement suggests he was nonetheless pleased with the outcome of the negotiations and that he might not revive his territorial claims, at least in the near future. He said, without elaborating, that the US would soon be rolling out a large military presence ​on the island, which already hosts one Space Force base in its remote northwest.
"This is a dream come true for the United States of America," Trump ​wrote.
The Danish prime minister's office said on Friday that the agreement would strengthen North Atlantic and Arctic security.
Greenland's Prime Minister, Jens-Frederik Nielsen, said in a ‌statement that ⁠the agreement recognised Greenland's interests and the Arctic island's place in international cooperation. "This benefits us all," he said.
Much was unclear as of Friday night, including whether any new US bases would be constructed as a result of the agreement. Trump's Truth Social posts about negotiations or agreements often lack context or specifics.
Imran Bayoumi, a former Pentagon official now with the Atlantic Council think tank, said it would be new if the US can build bases without the approval of ​Greenland or Denmark but that largely "it seems ​that Washington could have achieved ⁠a lot of these objectives through diplomacy and dialogue without straining the broader US-NATO relationship.”
It was also unclear how the agreement would be received in Greenland, an autonomous territory of Denmark. The island's residents aspire to independence and have bristled at ​US attempts to assert control.

In a separate statement, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that the deal "permanently ​and completely" addressed Washington's ⁠national security concerns with respect to the island.
"Greenland will forever be part of the strategic defence area of North America and exclude any adversary from it and the surrounding area," he wrote.
A State Department official, speaking on condition of anonymity to discuss specific terms, said the deal prohibits non-NATO countries from building a base in ⁠Greenland and will ​allow only the US and its allies to make unspecified "sensitive investments."
The official said the ​agreement grants the US permanent access, basing and overflight rights, and would continue to apply even if Greenland becomes independent.

title: Kohat Police Lines blast death toll rises to 23 as clearance operation concludes
description: K P IGP says law enforcement agencies completed the operation after working through the night
content:
K-P police say eight terrorists killed in retaliatory action, operation concluded after 20 hours
The death toll from the blast and subsequent attack at the mosque in Kohat Police Lines rose to 23 on Saturday after the body of another police officer was recovered from the site and shifted to the District Headquarters Hospital (DHQ).
"Rescue teams and ambulances transported a total of 91 injured people and patients to various hospitals, while the bodies of 23 people martyred in the attack were also shifted to hospitals, said Rescue 1122 spokesperson Bilal Ahmad Faizi.
On Friday, at least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred when an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines, followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities.
In a statement issued today, Faizi said that the operation was supervised by District Emergency Officer Kohat Noor-ul-Amin Khattak, with medical teams, ambulances and other rescue resources taking part.
"The operation involved 24 ambulances, rescue vehicles and a recovery vehicle, along with more than 60 rescue personnel. Additional ambulances and personnel were sent from neighbouring districts, including Karak and Hangu," the statement added.
It said that following funeral prayers, the bodies of 15 victims were transported by Rescue 1122 ambulances to their native districts of Kohat, Karak, Lakki Marwat, Bannu and Mardan.
"Seven critically injured people were transferred to Peshawar for further treatment. Five were taken to Lady Reading Hospital, while two were shifted to Hayatabad Medical Complex," it added.
Faizi said Rescue 1122 teams carried out search, rescue and medical operations in difficult, sensitive and dangerous conditions.
He said the personnel demonstrated professionalism, dedication and commitment while carrying out their duties.
Meanwhile, Kohat hospital Medical Superintendent Dr Tahir Shah also confirmed the rise in the death toll, saying another police officer’s body had been shifted to the DHQ Hospital.
Earlier, a search and clearance operation following the blast at a mosque was completed after around 20 hours, with eight terrorists killed
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Inspector General of Police (IGP) Zulfiqar Hameed said that Elite Force commandos, Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) teams and security forces cleared key sections of the buildings.
He said a suicide bomber had attempted to target law enforcement personnel but failed.
The IGP remained at the scene and encouraged the personnel involved in the operation, while Additional IGP CTD, the Kohat regional police officer and the Kohat district police officer led the operation. The Kohat GOC was also present, he added.
He further added that "the law enforcement agencies completed the operation after working through the night."
Hameed praised the officers who took part in the operation and announced rewards for them. “The police, CTD and security forces fought bravely. The brave personnel are the pride of the nation,” he said.
“The terrorists’ nefarious designs have been foiled, and we will ensure their complete elimination,” the IGP said.
Following the blast at the Old Police Lines Mosque in Kohat, terrorists attempted to infiltrate; 8 terrorists were killed in retaliatory action by police and security forces. IG KP Zulfiqar Hameed lauded the officers who took part in the operation and announced rewards. pic.twitter.com/OYvB81LjyF
K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi met the families of those killed in the terrorist attack at Kohat Police Lines and paid tribute to police, CTD personnel and other officials who confronted the attackers.
“I pay tribute to the police, CTD and all personnel who bravely fought the terrorists in the Kohat incident,” Afridi said.
“Our martyrs who fought bravely against the terrorists sacrificed their lives for the protection of the nation,” he said, praying that Allah Almighty elevate the ranks of the martyrs and grant patience to their bereaved families.
Afridi said K-P had been fighting a war against terrorism continuously for 22 years, since 2004, and further added that peace had prevailed in Pakistan during the government of Imran Khan despite what he described as an India-friendly government in Afghanistan.
“Today, meetings over tea have been held with the government present in Afghanistan, but despite this, relations have not improved,” he said.
Afridi said relations with Afghanistan remained strained and the border was closed, claiming that K-P had suffered a loss of more than Rs8 billion during the last financial year. He added that the continued closure of the border would also cause economic losses to the province during the current financial year.
“For 22 years, a policy has been followed that is not producing results. Now is the time to change the policy,” Afridi said. His government was presenting a policy to eliminate terrorism but claimed that no one was prepared to pay attention to it, he said.
Afridi further claimed that the federal government and institutions were focused on eliminating the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) and keeping Imran Khan in jail.
“The priority of the federal government is political revenge, while the elimination of terrorism and protection of the people are not their priority,” he said.
Referring to a statement by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, Afridi said the “fake chief minister of Punjab” had said she was not threatened by India but by Pakistan’s three smaller provinces. He also said that since his government came to power, an additional Rs35 billion had been provided to equip the police with modern weapons.
He said the police budget had been increased to Rs190 billion for the 2026-27 financial year. “Without strengthening the police, sustainable peace cannot be established in the province,” he said.
Afridi added that members of the provincial assembly had reduced their development budgets to provide resources for the police. The federal government’s policy on terrorism had “completely failed,” he added.
The chief minister also announced financial assistance for the families of those killed in the Kohat incident who were not covered by the government’s martyrs’ package and said all necessary and important medical equipment would be provided to Kohat DHQ Hospital.
Afridi also said the mosque damaged in the blast and the Special Branch police station would be reconstructed. “I have already announced a 1,000-bed hospital in Kohat, and it will be completed in the shortest possible time,” he said.
Members of the National Assembly, Shehryar Afridi and Dawood Afridi, and provincial ministers Shafi Jan and Aftab Alam were also present on the occasion.
Read: President Zardari, PM Shehbaz strongly condemn Kohat Police Lines blast
According to the report, the blast occurred at approximately 1:20pm during Friday prayers at a mosque located at Police Lines on Hangu Road in Kohat, followed by a terrorist attack involving around five to seven terrorists.
Of the 22 people killed, 16 were police personnel and six were civilians. The report identified one of the deceased civilians as Dr Israel Khan Aurakzai, Chief District Specialist (Paediatrics) at Liaqat Memorial Hospital, Kohat.
It further said 103 injured people had been received at the two hospitals, including 13 at Liaqat Memorial Hospital and 90 at DHQ Hospital Kohat. The injured comprised 73 police personnel and 30 civilians.
Of the total injured, 34 were admitted for treatment, while five patients underwent laparotomy, a surgical procedure involving an incision into the abdomen.
The report said four of the patients who underwent laparotomy had been referred to tertiary care facilities in Peshawar for further treatment.
It added that the situation was being closely monitored and all possible medical assistance was being provided to the injured at the relevant health facilities.
According to the police, seven armed terrorists infiltrated the police lines following a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device (VBIED) detonated at the boundary wall near the mosque.
Read more: Kohat Police Lines blast kills 21, including 15 police personnel
Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, has claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers. Islamabad has repeatedly asked the Taliban regime to deny the use of Afghan soil for terrorist attacks inside Pakistan. However, the de facto rulers in Kabul have been reluctant to take action against terrorist groups operating from their territory.

title: Australia beat Zimbabwe to seal ODI series
description: Head   s  dazzling century powers the visitors  to an emphatic  victory
content:
Head’s dazzling century powers the visitors to an emphatic victory
HARARE: Australia ​registered another ​emphatic win over hosts Zimbabwe to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in their One Day International series as Travis Head hit a century in Friday's 84-run win.
Head bludgeoned 112 runs off ‌84 balls as the visitors' top order laid the platform for victory in the second of three ODIs at the Harare Sports ‌Club with Australia put to ⁠bat ​first and scoring 356-6 before dismissing Zimbabwe for 272 ​in 48.3 overs.
t was Australia's ‌highest score against Zimbabwe in ​an ODI. Australia won the opening clash of the series by 59 runs on Tuesday and quickly took command on Friday as Head and captain Mitchell Marsh put ⁠on 130 runs for the opening stand and then Head added another 60 ‌with Cooper Connolly for the second wicket. Marsh, who was dropped first ball of the game, scored 53 from 63 balls while Connolly hit 78 off 69 balls to go past ⁠fifty for a third successive ODI.
But the most brutal ⁠batting came at ​the end of the ‌innings as 20-year-old Ollie Peake scored an unbeaten 41 runs from 18 balls including three sixes in the final over as Zimbabwe pacer Brad Evans was hit to all corners. Evans did get three wickets in the innings but for an expensive 86 runs off his nine overs. In reply, Zimbabwe quickly fell behind the required run rate ⁠as Australia pegged them back despite a good batting top with the home side taking 14 overs ⁠to get to 50 runs.
Captain Sikandar Raza top scored for Zimbabwe with 45 while 40-year-old Brendan Taylor, who only on Tuesday replaced India great Sachin Tendulkar as the longest-serving one-day international player, scored 39. Spinner Adam Zampa took 2-62 to go past 200 ODI wickets while opening bowler Josh Hazlewood returned from injury to take 2-48 in nine overs as the wickets were spread around the ⁠Australia attack, which lost Billy Stanlake to injury.
"I thought ​it was a complete performance from the boys and when Big Billy went down, our part-time bowlers stepped in," said Marsh. "They all loved it and were keen for it." The last ODI of the series is on Sunday after ​which Australia head to neighbouring South Africa for another ‌three-match series, starting next Tuesday in Durban.

title: OCA chief tells politicians to stay out of sports
description: OCA president urges focus on athletes after Taiwan official faces delay at Games flag raising ceremony
content:
OCA president urges focus on athletes after Taiwan official faces delay at Games flag-raising ceremony.
Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) President Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani said on Saturday that politicians should not be involved in sports, following a diplomatic incident involving a Taiwan government official at the Asian Games.
Taiwan sport minister Lee Yang, a former Olympic badminton champion, was initially blocked from attending a flag-raising ceremony at ⁠the Games on Friday, triggering a standoff as the Taiwan delegation refused to participate in protest.
Lee was eventually permitted entry, with the ceremony taking place more than an hour after scheduled.
Taiwan's cabinet complained Lee had been subject to "unreasonable obstruction" in a statement ⁠and that he had obtained the required access credentials.
Sheikh Joaan said at a press conference he was unaware of the incident but that politicians needed to stay out of sports at the quadrennial Games. "I think that our focus here is on ⁠the athletes and on making sure that everyone, ⁠all the athletes, have the equal rights in competing and in having their freedom," the Qatari told reporters in Nagoya.
"So I don't think the politicians or politics should be involved in sports. That's my opinion." OCA Director General Husain Al-Musallam added that the flag-raising ceremony was meant for the participants in the Games.
"(It's) not for the delegation from the ministry or ⁠from the government," he said. Lee claimed back-to-back badminton gold medals in the men's doubles at the ⁠Tokyo and Paris Olympics.
The buildup to the Aichi-Nagoya Games has been overshadowed by complaints from national team delegations over organisational issues, including transport and the accommodations provided for athletes.
Sheikh Joaan defended the local organisers saying they had been solving accommodation issues as they arise.
"I think everything is hopefully being back on track," he said.
The organisational problems have underscored the massive ⁠size of the Games, which include a record 43 sports and 469 medal events, dwarfing the summer Olympics' 32 sports and 329 events.
The OCA defended the size of the programme at Nagoya, which will see the debut of "virtual" taekwondo while retaining breaking (breakdancing) and esports.
"We are very proud that the Asian Games (are) bigger than any other games with low cost," said Al-Musallam.

title: Iran  Oman agree on safe shipping lane in Hormuz
description: Araghchi tells French FM to    stop crocodile tears    over human rights allegations
author_name: Anadolu Agency, Reuters, AFP, Web Desk
content:
Araghchi tells French FM to ‘stop crocodile tears’ over human rights allegations
Iran and Oman have reached an understanding on establishing a safe shipping lane through the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said.
The understanding concerns a transit route through the strategic waterway, with the two sides continuing discussions on technical aspects of the arrangement.
Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson: Iran and Oman have reached an understanding on establishing a safe shipping lane in the Strait of Hormuz.
The negotiations have focused on establishing safe shipping routes while safeguarding the sovereign rights and security interests of both Iran and Oman, according to Iran’s Foreign Ministry.
Iran says it has conveyed conditions to re-engage in talks
Earlier, Iran said it has conveyed its conditions to mediators for re-engaging in negotiations aimed at ending the war with the US, Al Jazeera cites Iran’s Security Chief Mohsen Rezaei as saying in an interview.
The conditions include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian funds, and ending the naval blockade, Rezaei says, adding that consultations were continuing with Qatari and Pakistani mediators and that Tehran was awaiting a response from US President Donald Trump.
Araghchi tells French FM to ‘stop crocodile tears’ over human rights allegations
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi hit back at recent statements by his French counterpart Jean-Noël Barrot where Barrot accused Iran of human rights violations, criticising Paris for its silence over the killing of Iranian schoolchildren by the United States.
Addressing Barrot in a post on X, Araghchi said, “1.5mn Algerians were slaughtered by France in their War of Independence. Less than 1/10 of them have been recorded by Paris, which refuses any apology for its colonial crimes.”
“Stop your crocodile tears @jnbarrot. Your silence when the US massacred our schoolkids said it all,” he added.
1.5mn Algerians were slaughtered by France in their War of Independence. Less than 1/10 of them have been recorded by Paris, which refuses any apology for its colonial crimes. Stop your crocodile tears @jnbarrot . Your silence when the U.S. massacred our schoolkids said it all. pic.twitter.com/IZrp8tCmWg
The Minab school strike killed 168 people, including 120 students and 26 teachers. More than 110 people were wounded.
Investigations indicate three precision-strike Tomahawk missiles hit the school . The school was struck three separate times, according to Press TV .
South Korea to contribute 'substantively' to Hormuz navigation efforts, top diplomat tells US counterpart
South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun on Friday reiterated Seoul's willingness to contribute "substantively" to efforts to restore freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz in a meeting with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the State Department.
Cho called on Rubio to maintain close communication on the issue, the Foreign Ministry said in a statement, according to Yonhap news agency.
The remarks come after South Korean President Lee Jae Myung ruled out sending combat troops to the Strait of Hormuz, as Seoul considers contributing to efforts to ensure freedom of navigation there amid pressure from Washington.
The two sides also reaffirmed their "solid" commitment to the bilateral alliance and agreed to continue efforts to achieve the "denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula" and promote peace and stability through dialogue and diplomacy.
Meanwhile, Cho said Seoul would act as a peacemaker to actively support the Trump administration's efforts to resume dialogue with North Korea.
"The minister and secretary agreed to continue close communication and cooperation regarding North Korea policy, including efforts for North Korea-U.S. dialogue," the ministry said.
Cho also told reporters that he called on Rubio to work together to ensure that ongoing consultations on South Korea's strategic investment projects in the US produce positive results.
Under last year's bilateral trade deal, Seoul committed to investing $350 billion in the US.
"Secretary Rubio said that the State Department will also make its efforts to ensure that the consultations will be successfully concluded," he added.
State Department Spokesman Tommy Pigott said in a statement that both sides pledged ongoing collaboration across key strategic sectors, including semiconductors.
Rubio reiterated the importance of "cooperating to secure freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and also underscored the critical need for a fair, transparent, and equitable business environment for American companies operating in the Republic of Korea."
He also stressed the importance of securing supply chains for key industries.
The two sides reaffirmed their commitment to North Korea's "complete denuclearisation" and stressed the importance of US-Japan-South Korea cooperation in regional security, Pigott said.
US bases in Middle East suffer severe damage from Iranian attacks: report
US military bases in the Middle East have sustained heavy damage from Iranian strikes, according to photos and videos obtained by ABC News , as the Pentagon assesses the toll of a war Washington launched more than six months ago.
The report said the images show damaged buildings and an aircraft at three bases in Kuwait and a Saudi base hosting US assets, some of which were evacuated.
One photo appears to show an E-3 Sentry surveillance aircraft, valued at $270 million, damaged in late March at Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia, the report noted.
"These bases have been irreparably damaged. And if we choose to rebuild them, it's going to be a decades-long undertaking," said a senior US service member, who spoke on condition of anonymity.
Read: Trump says Iran seeking deal as US considers next move
The service member accused the Pentagon of a lack of transparency, saying: "There are drone strikes and ballistic missile strikes actively landing on bases every day."
A Pentagon inspector general report released Monday indicated "hundreds of buildings and structures" were damaged. The watchdog estimated the war's cost at $33 billion, while the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office put it at $38 billion.
The Defence Department said 18 US service members have been killed and 824 wounded since the war began on February 28. The deadliest attack came on the second day, when six soldiers were killed at Port Shuaiba in Kuwait.
Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has said force protection is a top priority, though he acknowledged that some Iranian weapons get through.
Efforts ongoing to return to Islamabad MoU: Iranian interior ministry
Ali Zeynivand, a spokesperson for Iran’s interior ministry said on Saturday that, “Efforts and international diplomatic mediations to resolve issues and return to the Islamabad agreement are ongoing.”
BREAKING: Efforts ongoing to return to Islamabad MoU, says Iran's interior ministry 🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/iRiRvinNaJ pic.twitter.com/JEl2ZLbwDm
Iran demands that “the other party adhere to its commitments in this agreement”, said Zeynivand in a press briefing, according to Al Jazeera , which cited the semi-official Tasnim news agency .
The official stressed it was an “agreement that has been approved by the Supreme National Security Council and confirmed by the supreme leader, and is considered an official decision of the system”.
“Active diplomacy continues with the president’s participation in the Shanghai and Brics meetings in India and Kyrgyzstan, and through intensive consultations,” Zeynivand added.
Yemeni forces claim Houthi drone shot down in Al Jawf
Yemeni government forces say they shot down a Houthi drone in the Al-Jawf governorate, Al Jazeera reported on Saturday.
BREAKING: Yemeni government forces say they shot down Houthi drone in al-Jawf governorate 🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/QSozbHLmys pic.twitter.com/Hx5ALK8wEG
Yemeni government forces say they have shot down a Houthi drone in the northern governorate of al-Jawf.
Yemeni warplanes strike Houthi positions east of Taiz city
Yemeni government warplanes carried out airstrikes on Houthi positions around the Al-Qasr roundabout east of Taiz city, state-run Aljoumhouriya TV reported on Friday.
The broadcaster did not provide details on casualties or damage from the strikes.
The airstrikes came amid intensified fighting across Taiz province in southwestern Yemen, including areas west of the city near the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Read more: Yemeni airstrikes hit Houthi sites as clashes intensify in Taiz, Lahj: official
The Taiz Military Axis said government forces repelled a Houthi attack on the Al-Kadahah front in western Taiz.
It said troops forced the attackers to retreat after inflicting casualties, without providing figures.
Al-Kadahah is strategically located along the road linking Taiz with Mokha, near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
There was no immediate comment from the Houthis on the government accounts.
Earlier on Friday, the Yemeni army said 30 Houthi fighters were killed and 60 wounded in clashes and airstrikes around the Al-Dharifah junction in the Al-Wazi’iyah district in western Taiz.
Fayyad Alnoman, assistant undersecretary at Yemen’s Information Ministry for television affairs, later told Anadolu that government forces and the Popular Resistance recaptured Jabal al-Bazilah and the Madkhulah area on the Aghbarah front following heavy fighting.
The developments come amid rapidly shifting front lines in Yemen, particularly along the western coast.
The Houthis have recently advanced in parts of Al Hudaydah and Taiz provinces, and taken strategic areas, including Mokha, as well as Red Sea islands including Perim Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, according to media reports.
Government forces, meanwhile, have reported advances in Al-Jawf province toward Al-Hazm, the provincial capital, while fighting continues on fronts in Marib, Al-Dhalea and Al-Bayda.
The latest escalation began in early July and is the most intense since years of relative calm following the April 2022 truce.
Fighting has accelerated in September, particularly along the western coast and areas surrounding the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Yemen has been engulfed in conflict since the Houthis seized the national capital, Sanaa, and several provinces in September 2014. That prompted a Saudi-led Arab coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.
Saudi Arabia issues air raid alert in Riyadh, explosions heard
Explosions were heard in Riyadh, AFP journalists reported, after an air raid alert is issued by Saudi Arabian authorities, regularly targeted in recent days by Houthis in Yemen.
This is the first time the capital has been directly affected since a conflict in neighbouring Yemen intensified in July.
“The area is under a hostile aerial threat,” a message received shortly before 3am local time (5am PKT) by residents of the Saudi capital warned, urging them to stay indoors.
AFP journalists then heard two explosions, and the alert was lifted about half an hour later by Saudi Arabia’s civil defence agency.
US troop deaths during Iran war exceed Pentagon count by at least four: WSJ
More ​US troops have died during ‌the US-Israeli war with Iran than the Pentagon has publicly disclosed, the Washington Post reported ​on Friday.
Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth ​denied the report.
The Post , citing five unidentified ⁠officials, reported that there had been ​at least 22 military fatalities, four ​more than were listed in the data available on the Pentagon's public database.
The newspaper also reported, ​citing another unidentified official, that not ​all of the undisclosed deaths were directly tied ‌to ⁠the months-long conflict but involved US personnel who were in the Middle East amid ongoing hostilities.
Hegseth, in a ​post on ​X, called ⁠the report "a complete LIE."
This is DISGUSTING and FAKE. A complete LIE. Shame on the Washington Post — they’re worse than Iranian state media. https://t.co/vU9OkSOnLB
The Post did not immediately respond ​to a request for comment. ​In ⁠its story, the newspaper said the Pentagon had declined to address its questions ⁠about ​the discrepancy in casualty ​accounting.
Yemeni official says government forces retook 2 positions between Taiz, Lahj
Yemeni government forces have retaken two positions between the western provinces of Taiz and Lahj following clashes with the Houthis, a government official said on Friday.
“The armed forces and Popular Resistance on the Al-Aghbara front, located between Al-Wazi'iyah district in Taiz province and the Al-Subaiha area in Lahj province, regained Al-Bazla mountain and the Madkhula area after fierce battles with the Houthi militia,” Fayyad al-Numan, assistant undersecretary at Yemen’s Information Ministry, told Anadolu.
Government forces inflicted casualties and equipment losses on the Houthis during the fighting and targeted reinforcements belonging to the group, said Al-Numan.
“The armed forces also targeted other positions and military vehicles belonging to the Houthi militia in Al-Hartha village in the Al-Dharifa area of Al-Wazi'iyah district, west of Taiz,” he added.
The Al-Aghbara front is considered strategically important because of its location between Lahj and Taiz, linking it operationally to fronts across both provinces, according to media reports.
There was no comment from the Houthis on the fighting, which comes amid shifts in territorial control and escalating fighting on several fronts in Yemen.
