title: Pakistan plans fresh diplomatic push
description: Pakistan plans fresh diplomatic push
content:
High-level Tehran visit expected amid Yemen escalation
Pakistan is preparing to send another high-level delegation to Tehran in a fresh diplomatic push aimed at breaking the stalemate between Iran and the United States as well as containing rapidly escalating tensions between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis, officials said on Friday.
There was no official confirmation of the planned visit from Islamabad or Tehran. However, a senior government official told The Express Tribune that another visit to the Iranian capital was being planned and could take place very soon.
The official did not disclose the composition of the delegation, but diplomatic and government sources indicated that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi was likely to lead the delegation.
The proposed visit comes at a particularly sensitive moment for Pakistan, which has been trying to maintain its role as a bridge between Iran and the United States while simultaneously managing its growing security commitments to Saudi Arabia.
Pakistan's diplomatic efforts have now acquired another dimension as fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned Houthis has intensified.
Saudi Arabia and the Houthis exchanged fresh attacks this week, with Riyadh carrying out airstrikes against Houthi positions while the group launched drone and missile attacks against Saudi territory. The escalation has raised concerns about the security of Saudi energy infrastructure and shipping routes around the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb.
The latest diplomatic initiative also follows a telephone conversation between Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir. Iranian media reported that the two discussed the latest regional developments while Araghchi was in Beijing.
According to the Financial Times, Munir subsequently conveyed Pakistan's concerns to Iranian officials over the Houthi attacks and urged Tehran to restrain the group. The report said Islamabad had warned that the situation could have implications for Pakistan's defence commitments to Saudi Arabia.
Pakistan's position has become more consequential following the signing of the Pakistan-Saudi Arabia-Türkiye defence agreement in August, under which an attack on one of the signatories is to be treated as an attack on all.
Islamabad has since repeatedly stressed its commitment to Saudi Arabia's security. On Friday, Director General Inter-Services Public Relations Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said Pakistan's commitment to the kingdom's security was "unconditional", amid the escalating Houthi attacks.
The possibility of Pakistani military involvement, however, has not been formally raised by Riyadh, and Islamabad has continued to emphasise diplomatic efforts.
The proposed Naqvi visit could, therefore, serve two parallel objectives: conveying Pakistan's concerns to Tehran over the Houthi escalation while also trying to revive the broader diplomatic track between Iran and Washington.
Pakistan has already made several mediation attempts during the seven-month-old conflict. Islamabad hosted indirect contacts between the United States and Iran and has continued to argue that the dispute cannot be resolved through military means.
Those efforts have gained urgency as the conflict has begun affecting both major maritime energy routes in the region. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains severely reduced, while the security situation around Bab el-Mandeb has also deteriorated. Reuters reported on Friday that only four commodity vessels transited Hormuz on Thursday, compared with a 10-day average of 16.
The latest escalation has also pushed up global energy prices and increased pressure on Gulf states to find a diplomatic way out. Reuters reported that oil prices eased on Friday after diplomatic outreach, including efforts to persuade Iran to rein in Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure.
Meanwhile, Washington and Tehran remain far from resolving their differences. US President Donald Trump has said he hopes the war with Iran is nearing an end, but negotiations remain stalled.
Against this backdrop, Islamabad appears to be attempting a delicate balancing act: maintaining its strategic relationship with Saudi Arabia while keeping channels open with Iran and using its access to both sides to push for de-escalation.
Meanwhile, Pakistan has strongly condemned Houthi attacks on merchant shipping in the Bab al-Mandab Strait and called for their immediate cessation, as the UN Security Council holds its second major discussion this week on the escalating threat to the strategic waterway and its wider implications for regional security and global trade.
"We call upon [the] Houthi militia for immediate cessation of these provocative acts which could have dire consequences for maritime security, and regional peace and stability," Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, tells a Security Council Arria Formula meeting convened by Bahrain.
The ambassador says Houthi attacks seriously undermine maritime security and threaten peace and development in regional countries, "especially the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia", which he adds is facing "blatant and unprovoked aggression" by the Houthis.
Yemen's Houthis claim that Saudi Arabia launched 26 strikes against areas under their control over the past 24 hours, as the group and Yemen's Riyadh-backed government clash in the country's revived civil war, AFP reports.
The group adds that the number of Saudi strikes on its positions reached 300 over the last week, saying they targeted areas across Houthi-held Yemen.
Global trade is facing its worst disruption in 80 years as supply chain bottlenecks in the Strait of Hormuz threaten global food and fertiliser prices, Anadolu reports citing the World Trade Organisation's (WTO) director-general.
Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, speaking on the sidelines of the WTO's Public Forum in Geneva, tells Anadolu that the global trading system remains resilient, but the ongoing Middle East conflict presents a major test for the organisation's 166 member countries.
She notes that global trade in goods has grown by an unexpectedly strong 4.6 per cent this year despite geopolitical pressures, while 72pc of all global commerce continue to operate under WTO rules.
The initial projection for overall goods trade growth is 1.9pc for the entire year, but the first-quarter growth rate of 3.2pc outpaced expectations.
An Italian aircraft was hit during attacks on airbases in Saudi Arabia, Anadolu reports quoting Defence Minister Guido Crosetto.

title: IHC sets limits on right to protest
description: IHC sets limits on right to protest
content:
Waqas Ahmed, had challenged the planned move on the grounds that the protest could disrupt routine life
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has ruled that any act resulting in the infringement of citizens' fundamental rights constitutes a violation of the Constitution, warning that public office holders responsible for such violations would also be deemed to have breached their oath of office.
The ruling came in a detailed 37-page judgment on a petition concerning the proposed nationwide PTI protest towards Islamabad on September 27, 2026. PTI had announced the march to demand release of party founder Imran Khan and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.
A citizen, Waqas Ahmed, had challenged the planned move on the grounds that the protest could disrupt routine life, traffic and business activities in the federal capital.
A three-member bench headed by Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and comprising Justice Muhammad Asif and Justice Muhammad Azam Khan issued the judgment.
The bench had announced its short order on September 14 after hearing Attorney General for Pakistan Mansoor Awan, Additional Attorney General Amir Rehman, the advocate generals of the four provinces and Islamabad, and counsel for the petitioner, Barrister Akhter Cheena.
The court described the case as requiring an "unusual degree of constitutional balance" between the right of political parties and citizens to assemble peacefully and express dissent, and the rights of other citizens to life, liberty, dignity, free movement, trade, business, property, and access to hospitals, educational institutions, courts and workplaces.
"The question is not whether a political party is entitled to protest. It plainly is, subject always to the Constitution and law," the judgment observed.
The court held that the right to peaceful assembly could not be exercised in a manner that infringed the fundamental rights of other citizens.
A key objection raised by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa advocate general concerned the territorial jurisdiction of the IHC over provincial authorities functioning outside Islamabad.
Rejecting the objection, the court held that Article 199(1)© empowered a high court to issue directions where a governmental power or function was being exercised "in, or in relation to" territory within its jurisdiction.
The court clarified, however, that the provision did not confer general supervisory jurisdiction over another province. A high court could issue directions to an authority outside its territorial seat where the governmental function had a direct and proximate legal relation with territory within its jurisdiction and intervention was necessary to protect fundamental rights there.
The bench also observed that where executive action or inaction was likely to infringe the fundamental rights of citizens within Islamabad, the court was under a "bounden duty" to assume jurisdiction under Article 199(1)©.
The court also rejected the objection that the petition was not maintainable because KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had not been impleaded as a respondent. It noted that the Advocate General KP was representing both the provincial government and the chief minister.
The court further rejected the argument that the petitioner had an adequate alternate remedy under the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act, 2024.
It noted that no application had, admittedly, been filed under Section 3 of the Act and observed that its provisions had not been adhered to by the KP chief minister and others who had announced their intention to march towards Islamabad.
The judgment extensively referred to the Supreme Court's decision in the Faizabad sit-in case, observing that the constitutional right to assemble and protest was protected but remained subject to restrictions where its exercise infringed the fundamental rights of others.
The IHC also referred to the Supreme Court judgment concerning the PTI march of May 25, 2022, noting that assurances regarding a peaceful rally and non-obstruction of the Srinagar Highway had not been honoured.
The judgment referred to damage to public and private property, fires in the Blue Area greenbelt, injuries to police personnel and the subsequent invocation of Article 245 to call in the armed forces in aid of civil power.
The court also cited its November 21, 2024 order directing that no protest, rally or sit-in be allowed in violation of the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act. It observed that the order had also been flouted.
During the proceedings, the court allowed the Islamabad deputy commissioner/district magistrate to place electronic material on record. Video clips of the 2022 and 2024 protests were played before the bench, which described the conduct shown in the footage as "highly disturbing and reflective of violence and aggression".
The court noted that PTI was in power in K-P during both episodes and observed that provincial government resources had been used in pursuit of political objectives.
Regarding the proposed September 27 march, the court held that the petitioner's apprehension was not merely speculative. It noted that the date and destination of the proposed gathering were known and that statements attributed to the K-P chief minister indicated that the date was firm and that he intended to lead the march.
While disposing of the petition, the court directed that no political party, political leader, provincial government or public office holder could lawfully occupy roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas, buildings or similar public places within, or leading to or from, Islamabad in a manner that obstructed free movement or hindered trade, business, professions or access to medical and educational facilities.
The provincial governments and chief ministers were directed to ensure that no government resources, public funds, officials, vehicles, machinery or equipment were used directly or indirectly to facilitate any march, rally or procession towards Islamabad.
They were also directed to ensure that no public servant was compelled, coerced or induced to participate in such activities.
The chief secretaries, police chiefs, federal interior secretary, chief commissioner and IG Islamabad were ordered to issue instructions prohibiting officials from complying with orders requiring them to facilitate such marches.
Officials facing coercion were directed to report the matter to the relevant authorities, while helplines or other communication mechanisms were ordered to be established for this purpose.
The court further directed the authorities to take departmental action against officials who violated the directions.
In a significant finding, the court held that any person whose activity resulted in a violation of the fundamental rights of citizens in Islamabad would be deemed to have violated the Constitution and would be liable for consequences under the law.
It further declared that any public office holder whose activity resulted in a violation of citizens' fundamental rights would be deemed to have violated both the Constitution and his or her oath of office.

title: Govt cracks whip as PTI  JI gear up for capital marches
description: Govt cracks whip as PTI  JI gear up for capital marches
content:
Naqvi says violators of IHC order will face contempt proceedings
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has made it clear that, following the detailed judgment of the Islamabad High Court (IHC), no attempt to storm the federal capital or advance on the city in groups will be allowed under any circumstances.
He warned that those violating the court's orders would immediately face contempt of court proceedings.
Addressing a news conference alongside Minister of State for Interior Senator Talal Chaudhry and Islamabad Advocate General Manzoor Ahmad, Naqvi said security forces and law-enforcement agencies had been given clear instructions and fully prepared to prevent any attempt to disrupt public order.
He said that if protesters took the law into their own hands, security personnel would not remain silent spectators and will respond effectively.
Referring to the prevailing law-and-order situation (terrorist attack in Kohat) in the country and the sacrifices made by security personnel, Naqvi said that while the nation was attending the funerals of martyrs, preparations were simultaneously under way for sit-ins and an advance on the capital.
He urged the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government and the chief minister to focus on eliminating terrorism and ensuring the rule of law in the province instead of spending resources on a march towards Islamabad.
The interior minister distinguished between political rallies and an attempt by groups to advance on the capital, saying that peaceful protest was a democratic right of every political party.
However, he said, such protests should remain within the respective areas and provinces rather than being used to besiege the capital and paralyze daily life.
Naqvi warned that if even a single person lost their life as a result of the confrontation, the organizers of the protest would be directly responsible.
He also appealed to responsible opposition leaders to reconsider their decision, saying that politics of confrontation would only harm the country. He added that the government's foremost priority was to ensure the safety of citizens while minimizing disruption to life in the federal capital.
In a detailed judgment issued today, the IHC ruled that any activity resulting in infringement of citizens' fundamental rights amounts to a violation of the Constitution.
It warned that public office holders responsible for such violations would also be deemed to have breached their oath of office.
The court also held that the right to peaceful assembly could not be exercised in a manner that infringed the fundamental rights of other citizens.
Meanwhile, Islamabad Advocate General said security personnel would ensure that no protestors would move towards Islamabad.
The government machinery will not be allowed to be used in Islamabad for the protest, he said.
He said action against anyone violating their constitutional responsibilities was provided under the Constitution, adding that proceedings could be initiated under Article 5.

title: Mosque blown up as terrorists storm Kohat police facility
description: Mosque blown up as terrorists storm Kohat police facility
author_name: SHAHID HAMEED, Ahtesham Khan  , Shahabullah Yusufzai
content:
15 cops among 21 martyred in suicide blast Gunmen open fire after blast breaches wall Police say all seven attac
At least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred on Friday when an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines, followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities, according to an initial incident report issued by DHQ Hospital Kohat medical superintendent and the district health officer.
All seven attackers were killed in the explosion and the gun battle that followed, police said in a statement.
The interior ministry said the "cowardly actions" of the attackers could not weaken the "nation's firm resolve".
The report said the blast occurred at approximately 1:20pm during Friday prayers at a mosque located at Police Lines on Hangu Road in Kohat, followed by a terrorist attack involving around five to seven terrorists.
Of the 21 people killed, 15 were police personnel and six were civilians. The report identified one of the deceased civilians as Dr Israel Khan Aurakzai, Chief District Specialist (Paediatrics) at Liaqat Memorial Hospital, Kohat.
It further said 103 injured people had been received at the two hospitals, including 13 at Liaqat Memorial Hospital and 90 at DHQ Hospital Kohat. The injured comprised 73 police personnel and 30 civilians.
Of the total injured, 34 were admitted for treatment, while five patients underwent laparotomy, a surgical procedure involving an incision into the abdomen.
The report said four of the patients who underwent laparotomy had been referred to tertiary care facilities in Peshawar for further treatment.
It added that the situation was being closely monitored and all possible medical assistance was being provided to the injured at the relevant health facilities.
According to the police, seven armed terrorists infiltrated the police lines following vehicle-borne improvised explosive device (VBIED) detonated at the boundary wall near the mosque. The police said six terrorists, including the suicide bomber, had been killed so far. Initially, a suicide attacker blew himself up near the Special Branch building after the explosion, it added.
Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, has claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers. Islamabad has repeatedly asked the Taliban regime to deny the use of Afghan soil for terrorist attacks inside Pakistan. However, the de facto rulers in Kabul have been reluctant to take action against terrorist groups operating from their territory.
In a statement, K-P Police Public Relations director said the operation against the terrorists had entered its final stages under the direct supervision of the K-P Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed, with security personnel carrying out a clearance operation in the area.
Hameed said authorities were tracing the terrorists and their facilitators and would ensure their complete elimination. He stated that police and the Counter Terrorism Department were engaged in an operation against Fitna al-Khawarij inside the police lines compound.
"Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Police is standing as an iron wall against terrorism. Cowardly attacks cannot weaken our resolve," he said. "The blood of the martyrs will not go to waste. The terrorists and their facilitators will meet an exemplary fate," he added.
Earlier, Rescue 1122 spokesperson Bilal Ahmed Faizi stated that 14 ambulances, rescue vehicles, a recovery vehicle and more than 45 rescue personnel were participating in the operation.
District Emergency Officer Noor-ul-Amin was personally supervising the rescue operation, he said, adding that relief activities would continue until the operation was completed. He added that further details would be issued as more information was received.
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif strongly condemned the bomb blast in Old Police Lines, Kohat, Radio Pakistan reported on Friday.
In separate messages, they expressed deep grief and sorrow over the injuries suffered by several people in the blast.
The president said that the complete elimination of Fitna-al-Khawarij and terrorists operating with foreign backing was inevitable for national security.
The prime minister sought a report from the authorities concerned on the blast and directed them to expedite relief operations.

title: EU envoy says GSP  comes with caveats
description: EU envoy says GSP  comes with caveats
content:
Pakistan will have to demonstrate clear progress in legislating and effectively implementing various international laws and conventions if it is to continue benefiting from the European Union's GSP+ facility, EU Ambassador to Pakistan Raimundas Karoblis said on Friday.
He urged the business community, particularly exporters, to ensure compliance with the relevant conventions without delay.
Karoblis made the remarks during a visit to the All Pakistan Textile Mills Association (APTMA) House, where the association's office-bearers held detailed discussions with the EU envoy on the strategy, prospects and challenges surrounding the extension of the GSP+ facility beyond 2027.
The EU identifies implementation of the international conventions underpinning GSP+ as a condition for continued preferential access.
The EU ambassador was accompanied by First Secretary Kurt Ajama, Development Cooperation Manager Thies Munkgaard-Hansen and Senior Economist and Trade Adviser Hasnain A Iftikhar.
Speaking on the occasion, Karoblis said Pakistan would have to demonstrate effective legislation and tangible progress in the implementation of various international laws and conventions to continue benefiting from GSP+.
He urged the business community in general and exporters in particular to ensure immediate implementation of the relevant international conventions and maintain active engagement with the government on issues raised by the European Commission concerning human rights, labour rights, governance and environmental protection.
Such engagement could help pave the way for an extension of GSP+ for the next 10 years, he said.
The ambassador appreciated the efforts of Pakistan's textile industry towards meeting sustainability requirements, saying sustainability remained a highly important priority for the European Union and that the progress made by the industry in this regard was commendable.
The current GSP+ arrangement remains in place through 2027, while the EU and Pakistan have continued discussing the conditions and framework for the next phase.

title: Russians vote in parliamentary polls
description: Russians vote in parliamentary polls
content:
Elections are seen as war barometer, as anti-war candidates squeezed out
Russians began voting on Friday in a three-day parliamentary election that President Vladimir Putin has described as a measure of public support for his war in Ukraine, despite most anti-war candidates being barred from contesting.
The election will determine the make-up of the 450-seat State Duma and is widely expected to see the ruling United Russia party retain its dominance. The result is likely to be presented by the Kremlin as evidence of widespread public backing for Putin's policies.
Most anti-war candidates were excluded from the ballot. The Supreme Court last month ruled that the liberal Yabloko party, which supports a ceasefire in Ukraine, had breached electoral rules, a charge the party denied.
Some Yabloko candidates are still contesting individual constituencies, which account for half of the 450 seats. Senior party figure Lev Shlosberg was jailed for 11 years over comments about the war, while deputy leader Maxim Kruglov received a seven-year sentence in June.
The vote is also being closely watched for signs of war fatigue as Russia's economy faces pressure from Western sanctions, high interest rates, labour shortages and disruptions caused by Ukrainian drone attacks. Initial partial results are expected from Sunday, with near-complete results due on Monday.

title: Nigeria orders probe after 37 die in custody
description: Nigeria orders probe after 37 die in custody
content:

Survivors of a Nigerian disaster that saw 37 suspected illegal gold miners die while in the custody of a paramilitary civil defence group recounted their panic on Friday as they struggled to breathe inside the cell.
Police fired shots to disperse protests as tensions spilled onto the streets of Minna, the capital of mineral-rich Niger state in central Nigeria. It was not immediately clear whether police were firing anti-riot pellets or live ammunition.
The Nigeria's government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew in Minna to curtail the unrest that saw the mobs blocking a main street and attacking a transport depot, a bank, political party offices and private businesses. The government suspended a civil defence commander.
President Bola Tinubu has ordered a "thorough", "urgent and "full and transparent investigation" over Thursday's deaths. But anger erupted among sympathisers as testimony from survivors suggested the miners may have suffocated in packed cells.
A 40-second video shared online purporting to show the victims of Thursday's incident featured bodies of dozens of young men clad only in shorts. Most of them appeared to be teenagers and were sprawled on the ground out in the open.
An intelligence report seen by AFP suggested the 37 died as a result of overcrowding and poor ventilation in the detention facility, though the civil defence initially blamed the deaths on disease.

title: California moves to create AI  kill switch
description: California moves to create AI  kill switch
content:
Cyberattacks and fears over advanced AI grow
California Governor Gavin Newsom on Friday ordered officials to explore the creation of a "kill switch" for advanced artificial intelligence (AI) systems, while fresh research showing sophisticated cyberattacks and growing safety concerns added pressure on the rapidly expanding industry.
The move came as security researchers said they had used Anthropic's latest software to breach OpenAI's internal systems, highlighting how rapidly advanced AI technology can be deployed in sophisticated cyberattacks.
"I just issued an executive order to accelerate the implementation of safety checks and advance the creation of a 'kill switch' within frontier AI programs," Newsom, a Democrat, wrote on X, while accusing President Donald Trump of doing nothing on the issue.
Researchers from security firm Hacktron said they exploited a security flaw in OpenAI's public help forum that enabled them to take control of the site, underscoring concerns about the potential misuse and security implications of increasingly capable AI systems.
Concerns intensified after Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon resigned while warning that the industry was "gambling with our lives". Coxon, who previously worked at OpenAI, received support from former colleagues, including one who raised concern that AI could cause humanity's extinction.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei last weekend called for AI development to slow. However, OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar dismissed concerns that slowing the release of state-of-the-art technology would hurt its business, saying the amount of intelligence already available was "massive".
Amodei argued that AI development is moving faster than governments can regulate and urged leading developers to submit to oversight by permanent embedded evaluators. title: Cuba power grid suffers nationwide collapse
description: Cuba power grid suffers nationwide collapse
content:
Cuba's electricity grid suffered a total collapse on Friday, plunging the island into a nationwide blackout as fuel shortages, deteriorating infrastructure and prolonged power cuts continue to strain its ageing energy system.
"A total disconnection of the electrical system has occurred," the energy ministry said in a post on X, without specifying the cause of the latest failure. The blackout is the seventh major nationwide power outage reported in Cuba this year and the 12th since late 2024.
The outage underscores the deepening difficulties facing the island's electricity sector. Cuba, home to about 9.4 million people, has endured frequent power cuts for years as its ageing thermoelectric plants struggle to meet demand.
The situation has deteriorated sharply since January, when Washington imposed what Havana describes as a de facto energy blockade in an effort to pressure the Cuban government. Severe fuel shortages have made it increasingly difficult to keep power plants and backup generators operating.
Cuba relies heavily on imported fuel, including diesel, to run generators used when the national grid is unable to meet demand. Even when the grid remains operational, rolling blackouts frequently affect large parts of the country, leaving millions without electricity for prolonged periods.
In recent weeks, outages in Havana have lasted more than 30 hours, while blackouts in some outlying provinces have extended beyond 60 hours. The power crisis also disrupted essential services, affecting water supplies and phone networks and adding to the difficulties faced by households and businesses.

title: Rebeca Grynspan ahead in informal poll for UN chief
description: Rebeca Grynspan ahead in informal poll for UN chief
content:
Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett remains runner-up in voting at UNSC
Rebeca Grynspan narrowly topped an indicative poll of the UN's most powerful body, the Security Council, on Friday as it chooses the embattled organisation's next leader, according to a diplomatic source.
Grynspan – Costa Rica's former vice president who has taken leave from her post at the UN trade and development body (UNCTAD) to campaign for secretary-general – also came top in the first secret straw poll. Guyanese ex-foreign minister Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett pulled ahead in the second.
Several countries on the 15-member Council have declared their desire for the embattled UN to have its first ever woman leader when the current Secretary-General Antonio Guterres concludes his term at the end of December.
Grynspan won nine "encourage" votes, but still faced a groundswell of opposition receiving five votes of "discourage," and one of "no opinion," the diplomatic source said. Rodrigues-Birkett received eight votes of encouragement, six of discouragement and single vote of no opinion, the source added.
Just one vote of "discourage" from a veto wielding permanent council member – Britain, China, France, Russia or the United States – would scupper a candidate's chances. There is speculation that a compromise candidate could be parachuted into the process at the behest of the five permanent members.
Others in the race are the current head of the UN nuclear watchdog, Rafael Grossi, Macky Sall of Senegal, Ecuador's Ivonne A-Baki, Chile's Michelle Bachelet, Ecuador's Maria Fernanda Espinosa and Uganda's Olara Otunnu.
International Crisis Group's Daniel Forti said it was thought there would be another straw poll at the end of the UN's signature high-level week due to get underway Tuesday. Once a candidate clears the Security Council's hurdles, their name will go to the General Assembly of all UN members for confirmation.

title: Opposition alliance announces APC
description: Participants discuss country s political situation  ongoing crisis in Middle East  its impact on Pakistan
content:
Participants discuss country's political situation, ongoing crisis in Middle East, its impact on Pakistan
The opposition alliance on Friday decided to convene an all-parties conference to help address the country's political and economic crises and declared that its September 27 long march would be a "peaceful, constitutional and democratic" struggle.
According to a statement issued after a meeting chaired by Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Aain Pakistan (TTAP) chief and opposition alliance leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai, the bloc has agreed to bring all democratic political forces onto a single platform to address the country's crises.
Burning issues such as inflation, unemployment, petrol prices and law and order will be made central issues for the September 27 protest, the meeting agreed.
The participants also agreed on the protection of the Constitution, Parliament, the federal system, provincial rights, the National Finance Commission (NFC) and the resources and powers of the provinces.
The meeting was attended by Senate Opposition Leader Allama Nasir Abbas, Balochistan National Party chief Sardar Akhtar Jan Mengal, Zain Shah and Mustafa Nawaz Khokhar.
Participants discussed the country's political situation, the ongoing crisis in the Middle East and its impact on Pakistan.
The meeting also deliberated on the law and order situation in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the proposed 28th Amendment and the creation of new provinces.
The participants were briefed on the September 27 protest and the visits of K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to Sindh and Punjab.
The statement said that after all doors to justice had been completely closed, peaceful protest remained the only option.
It said that on September 27, the people's right to rule would be reclaimed through the strength of public support.
The opposition alliance decided to convene an all-parties conference to help end the political and economic crises and called on all democratic political forces to unite on one platform to pull the country out of its difficulties.
Responsibilities and committees have also been assigned for contacting other political parties.
The participants agreed on the protection of the Constitution, Parliament, the federal structure and provincial rights, including the NFC and the resources and powers of the provinces.
The statement maintained that a "non-representative government" had no authority to break up provinces or divide them merely into administrative units, denouncing such proposals as harmful to the federation, the national units and the federal structure.
It further said that provinces could not be deprived of their constitutional rights through a referendum or by any other means.
The meeting particularly stressed maintaining Sindh's existing geographical and administrative status.
On the treatment of PTI founder Imran Khan, the opposition alliance said that instead of implementing the Supreme Court's decision regarding his treatment, the matter had been turned into another crisis. It demanded direct access to the founder and accurate information about his health.
The meeting also expressed concern over severe water shortages in the Indus River system, saying Pakistan's environment, agriculture and the Indus Delta faced serious threats.
The participants demanded that no new canals or water projects be initiated and that controversial projects already under construction be scrapped.
The meeting called for the immediate recovery of forcibly disappeared persons and demanded that the bodies of those missing persons who had died be handed over to their families.
It also called for an end to target killings, fake encounters, extrajudicial killings and death squads.

title: 4m girls out of school as gender divide persists
description: 4m girls out of school as gender divide persists
content:
Women still knocking at the door, make up just 4.34% of police force, reveals first-ever gender equality report
Sindh has taken its first province-wide measure of the gender divide - and the numbers paint a picture of progress alongside some stubborn gaps, with millions of girls still out of school and women remaining heavily underrepresented in the police and judiciary.
The province's first-ever gender equality report, released by the provincial government on Friday, records gains in maternal health, women's employment and political participation, but flags persistent disparities in literacy, school enrolment, economic opportunities, digital access and representation in decision-making.
Unveiling the report, Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah directed all provincial departments to undertake targeted reforms based on its findings, strengthen gender-sensitive governance and improve women's and girls' access to education, healthcare, employment and public representation. The report was presented at the Chief Minister House by CM's Special Assistant on Human Rights Rajveer Singh Sodho.
Describing the report as a new policy tool for the province, CM Shah said its findings would help the government identify areas where progress had been made and those requiring urgent intervention, while guiding evidence-based planning, resource allocation and institutional reforms.
"Gender equality is not only a matter of social justice but also a fundamental requirement for sustainable development," CM Shah said, adding that the findings would help strengthen policies and programmes aimed at empowering women and girls.
According to the report, Sindh's population reached 55.69 million in 2023, growing at an annual rate of 2.57%. There were 108.76 men for every 100 women.
The health sector recorded progress, with the provincial health budget rising from Rs214.5 billion in 2023-24 to Rs267.54 billion in 2024-25 and estimated to reach Rs318.22 billion in 2025-26.
The maternal mortality ratio fell from 314 to 224 deaths per 100,000 live births, while the neonatal mortality rate stood at 24 deaths per 1,000 live births, the report said.
Education, however, remained a major challenge. The literacy rate stood at 68% for men and 47% for women, while female literacy in rural areas was only 27.52%. More than 4.08 million girls aged between five and 16 remain out of school, according to the report.
Women's representation in the justice and law-enforcement sectors also remained low. Women account for only 4.34% of the police force, 18.3% of prosecutors and 13.7% of judges.
The report recorded 3,085 reported cases of gender-based violence in 2024, underscoring the need for stronger protection mechanisms and improved access to justice.
The report also highlighted gains in political participation. The number of registered female voters has crossed 12 million, while the number of women contesting elections increased from 23 in 2018 to 53 in 2024.
Women's labour-force participation rose from 43.8% to 46.2%, while the number of employed women increased from 2.48 million to 3.32 million.
Despite the gains, the report identified barriers to women's full economic participation, including limited access to digital connectivity, financial inclusion, skills development, entrepreneurship and decent employment.

title: Experts call for sustainability reporting in agriculture
description: Experts call for sustainability reporting in agriculture
content:
Speakers say LCA can identify environmental hotspots
Climate change, water scarcity, soil degradation and rising energy demand are increasing the environmental costs of conventional production systems, highlighting the need for environmental due diligence, sustainability reporting and life cycle assessment (LCA) to identify risks, reduce carbon emissions and promote sustainable agriculture and allied industries, experts said at a workshop at the University of Agriculture Faisalabad (UAF).
The workshop on "Environmental Due Diligence, Sustainability Reporting and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA)" was organised by the UAF Department of Rural Sociology in collaboration with Northumbria University, Newcastle, UK, and Fruit of Sustainability (SMC-Private) Limited under the UKRI-funded Super-Efficient Sustainable Cooling Solution for All Applications (S2Cool) project.
Dr Muhammad Wakil Shahzad of Northumbria University, who leads the S2Cool project, highlighted the importance of international research collaboration in developing innovative responses to extreme heat and energy challenges. He said such technologies could have wider applications in agriculture, food preservation and supply-chain efficiency amid a changing climate.
Dr Sadaf Mahmood, chairperson of the Department of Rural Sociology, stressed the need for practical knowledge of environmental assessment, sustainability reporting and climate-conscious decision-making. She said scientific research should be translated into practical solutions for farmers, industries and communities.
Dr Asif Kamran said environmental assessment should not be confined to industrial activities as agriculture was closely linked with soil, water, energy, biodiversity and greenhouse gas emissions. He said improved environmental information could help identify resource-efficient farming practices and technologies while supporting long-term food and environmental security.
Industrialist Nasir Zia said reliable environmental data was essential for identifying risks and measuring progress in reducing environmental footprints. He highlighted the importance of environmental due diligence in making production and investment decisions more environmentally responsible.
Sarim Mehmood, CEO and founder of Fruit of Sustainability, said environmental sustainability should be integrated into business decisions, product development and supply chains rather than treated as a separate activity.

title: LHC seeks arguments on anti terror bill s legality
description: LHC seeks arguments on anti terror bill s legality
content:
Lawyer asked the court to declare the amendment approved by the Punjab Assembly illegal
The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Friday sought arguments on the maintainability of a petition challenging the Punjab Assembly-approved Anti-Terrorism (Amendment) Bill 2026, questioning how the legislation was prima facie unconstitutional and how the petition itself was maintainable.
Justice Shahram Sarwar Chaudhry heard the petition filed by Punjab Assembly Opposition Leader Muhammad Moeenuddin Riaz.
During the hearing, the petitioner's counsel argued that the amendment was unlawful and that provisions allowing the identities and faces of judges, prosecutors and witnesses to be concealed during trials were contrary to the Constitution.
The lawyer asked the court to declare the amendment approved by the Punjab Assembly illegal.
Justice Shahram Sarwar Chaudhry, however, asked the counsel to explain how the legislation was prima facie unconstitutional and also questioned the maintainability of the petition.
The counsel sought time to assist the court on the issue. The court directed him to advance arguments on maintainability at the next hearing and adjourned further proceedings.
Riaz has challenged the constitutional validity of newly inserted Section 21AAA of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, which provides for "special security cases" in which the identities of judges, prosecutors, defence lawyers, police officers and witnesses may be kept secret and the entire trial record sealed.
The petitioner, an elected MPA from PP-215, Multan, has sought the striking down of Section 21AAA, arguing that it undermines fundamental rights relating to fair trial, due process, dignity, access to information and equality before law guaranteed under Articles 4, 9, 10-A, 14, 19-A and 25 of the Constitution.
According to the petition, the provision inserted through the Anti-Terrorism (Punjab Amendment) Act 2026 allows a government-designated officer not below BS-20 to declare a case or class of cases a "special security case" if extraordinary protection is considered necessary.
Under the challenged mechanism, the identities of judges, public prosecutors, police officers, witnesses, defence counsel and other persons involved in proceedings are not to be disclosed. Judicial orders may be signed without the personal identities of judges, witnesses may be assigned specific identities and the names of judges and prosecutors are not to be published in the official Gazette, the petition states.

The Supreme Court on Friday warned Sindh police officials of possible contempt proceedings over delays in registering FIRs, reiterating that any future defiance of its directions on prompt registration would invite action against the responsible officers.
The warning came as a two-judge bench comprising Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar and Justice Salahuddin Panhwar upheld the life sentence of a man convicted of a 2012 murder in Sindh's Dadu district.
While dismissing the jail petition of Ali Raza Siyal against the Sindh High Court's August 24, 2023, judgment, the court also ordered the Sindh prosecutor general to submit a report on murder cases in which FIRs were registered more than 24 hours after the alleged occurrence.
"We observe with dismay, once again, the consistent practice of delayed registration of FIRs in the province of Sindh," Justice Panhwar observed in a seven-page judgment, adding that despite earlier directions - and even after the Sindh inspector general had appeared before the court - the practice showed no sign of abating.
In the case before the court, the FIR was registered after a delay of more than three days, although information about the incident had been furnished the same night.
The judgment expressed regret over the delay and recalled that the issue had also been highlighted by the SC in its 2026 Muhammad Bux judgment.
The court directed all IGPs across Pakistan to ensure prompt registration of an FIR once the officer in charge of a police station was informed about an incident.

title: Pak takes big leap in green ranking
description: Pak takes big leap in green ranking
content:
Country moves up 22 places in 2026 Environmental Performance Index
Pakistan has improved its position by 22 places in the 2026 Environmental Performance Index (EPI), moving from 179th in 2024 to 157th among 177 countries, according to the latest index released by the Yale Center for Environmental Law & Policy.
Pakistan recorded an EPI score of 29.03 in the 2026 assessment, compared with 22.46 for India, which was ranked 176th. The EPI assesses countries on 47 indicators, covering 12 environmental issue categories. These are grouped under three broad policy objectives: environmental health, ecosystem vitality and climate change.
Pakistan's improved ranking comes as provincial authorities have increased efforts to address environmental pollution, particularly in Punjab, where measures targeting air pollution and environmental enforcement have been expanded ahead of the smog season.
The Punjab Environment Protection and Climate Change Department and its environmental protection agency have intensified inspections of industrial units, brick kilns and other sources of pollution. Authorities have also increased enforcement against vehicles emitting excessive smoke.
Punjab has expanded technology-based environmental monitoring, including real-time air-quality monitoring and local forecasting systems. The systems are being used to identify pollution hotspots and support enforcement and public advisories.
Authorities have also introduced measures to monitor vehicular emissions and require industrial units to comply with emission-control standards. Brick kilns are being monitored for compliance with approved technologies and environmental regulations.
Efforts to reduce plastic pollution have also continued, including action against prohibited plastic bags and inspections in markets and commercial areas.
Environmental education and climate-related initiatives have also been incorporated into provincial programmes. The Green School Certification initiative focuses on environmental awareness and practical measures in educational institutions.
The EPI provides an international benchmark for comparing environmental performance, but the overall ranking reflects performance across a wide range of indicators and does not eliminate the environmental challenges faced by individual countries.
Pakistan's 22-place improvement between the 2024 and 2026 rankings comes amid continuing challenges related to air pollution, environmental health, ecosystem protection and climate change.

title: IHC questions FIA power to offload passengers
description: IHC questions FIA power to offload passengers
content:
The Islamabad High Court on Friday allowed a citizen, who had been placed on a travel restriction list and offloaded at the airport, to travel abroad, while questioning the Federal Investigation Agency's (FIA) authority to take such measures under its internal standard operating procedures (SOPs).
Justice Inaam Ameen Minhas, while hearing a petition filed by citizen Rab Nawaz, expressed displeasure with FIA officials and directed the agency's additional director to submit a response explaining the legal basis for offloading passengers and placing their names on travel restriction lists.
The judge remarked that the petitioner could travel abroad and said that if anyone stopped him, "we will see," adding that the petitioner's case would remain pending before the court. During the hearing, the government lawyer told the court that the FIA has its own SOPs under which it takes such actions.
Justice Minhas questioned what those SOPs were, observing that the law did not permit such measures. He termed the matter highly sensitive and noted that the Supreme Court had already passed an order on the issue.
The judge warned that he would write to the secretary of the Establishment Division against officers involved in unlawfully offloading people. "I will ask the secretary to stop the promotion of the officer found responsible," he added.
The judge asked the FIA how it could offload someone who has a passport, visa and return ticket. The FIA lawyer maintained that the agency had internal regulations under which passengers were offloaded.
Justice Minhas said he would summon the FIA director general and ask him which SOPs authorised the agency to act in a manner that appeared to place internal regulations above the law.
The judge questioned whether the FIA had the authority to make laws. "You are standing in the high court. Why do you not understand?" he remarked, asking whether an FIA SOP could override the law.
He warned that if government departments were allowed to formulate their own procedures without regard to the law, every bureaucrat could make his own SOPs.

title: DISCOs seek Rs1 7 raise in power tariff
description: DISCOs seek Rs1 7 raise in power tariff
content:
Proposed hike attributed to fuel charges adjustment
Power distribution companies (DISCOs) have sought approval from the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) to charge consumers an additional Rs1.7267 per unit in their October bills.
This proposed hike is attributed to the fuel charges adjustment (FCA) for August.
Following July's FCA, Nepra authorized DISCOs to collect an additional Rs2.058 per unit, which consumers are currently paying in their September bills.
Nepra has scheduled a public hearing on September 29 to review this petition submitted by the Central Power Purchasing Agency (CCPA) on behalf of DISCOs.
Of the total demand, these companies also agree to forego and refund Rs10.097 billion as previous adjustments and another Rs10.617 billion as RLNG fuel rate adjustment.
The power generation in August 2026 increased by 5.1%, while its cost increased by a whopping 37.63% when compared with the cost in August 2025.
The major contributor was the 111% increase in RLNG-based power, followed by a 43.3% increase in nuclear power cost and a 21.4% increase in imported coal-based power generation price.
The CPPA's petition indicates that a total of 14,943 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of electricity was generated in August 2026, with an associated cost of Rs149.596 billionequivalent to Rs10 per unit.
Hydel generation stood at 5,654 GWh, making up 37.84% of the total generation pie. This was followed by imported coal-power generation of 2,330 GWh costing Rs17.088/unit.
Local coal-power generation increased by 12.76% to 1,626 GWh from 1,442 GWh in August last year. Interestingly, local coal generation cost decreased by 54.3% to Rs5.495/unit from Rs12.0146/unit last year.
Generation from nuclear sources stood at 1,528 GWh, which is 28.76% less than August 2025's generation of 2,145 GWh. During the month, the generation cost from nuclear sources climbed to Rs3.1468/unit from Rs2.195/unit in the same month last year depicting a 43.3% increase.
RLNG-based generation in August 2026 stood at 1,311 GWh. It declined by 39.86% from 2,180 GWh in August 2025. The RLNG per unit generation cost was Rs45.928/unit, while last year in the same month its cost was Rs21.73/unit.
Interestingly, during the month under review, 80 GWh of power was generated from expensive high-speed diesel at Rs54/unit and another 321 GWh was generated from RFO at Rs45.25/unit.
The petition outlines that in August, the consumers were charged a reference fuel cost of Rs7.1 per unit, while the actual fuel cost incurred was Rs8.8 per unit. The CPPA argues that the additional cost burden of Rs1.7 per unit should be transferred to consumers.
In Pakistan, the FCA is a regulatory mechanism administered by Nepra to pass month-to-month variations in fuel expenses directly to electricity consumers. At the start of each fiscal year, Nepra establishes a baseline reference fuel cost per unit (kWh) based on projected generation costs. Power in Pakistan is generated through a diverse mix of energy sources, including hydel, local and imported coal, RLNG, nuclear, furnace oil, solar, and wind. Because the actual cost of these fuels changes continually, the CPPA and DISCOs submit their actual monthly fuel spending to NEPRA for formal audit and public review.

title: Experts warn of growing South Asia instability
description: Experts warn of growing South Asia instability
content:
Arms-control erosion and shrinking diplomacy raise risks
Strategic experts have cautioned that the changing global and regional strategic environment is posing growing challenges to strategic stability in South Asia, citing the erosion of traditional arms-control frameworks, modernisation of nuclear capabilities and shrinking space for diplomacy.
Former and current officials of the Strategic Plans Division (SPD) made the observations during the seventh edition of the "Training of the Trainers" (ToT) workshop on strategic matters organised by the Centre for International Strategic Studies (CISS), Islamabad.
The workshop brought together senior professors and academics from universities across Pakistan, along with think-tank professionals, foreign policy experts and diplomats. It aimed to strengthen understanding of contemporary strategic issues and build the capacity of academics and trainers to contribute to informed discourse on strategic stability, nuclear deterrence, arms control and non-proliferation.
Speaking on the occasion, the officials also pointed to the selective application of non-proliferation norms, disruptive technologies and increasing reliance on hard power as factors complicating efforts to reduce risks and prevent conflict in the region.
Lt-Gen (retd) Mazhar Jamil, adviser to the National Command Authority (NCA) and former director general of the SPD, said the global and regional strategic environment was becoming increasingly complex, with the erosion of traditional arms-control frameworks, diminishing diplomatic space and the growing role of hard power and emerging technologies creating new challenges for strategic stability.
Persistent threat perceptions, unresolved disputes such as Kashmir and India's aggressive military posturing had contributed to continuing security tensions in the region, Jamil said in his concluding keynote address, according to a statement issued here.
"Strategic stability cannot be separated from the underlying political realities," he added, cautioning that Indian military adventurism and hegemonic approaches in a nuclearised South Asia carried unacceptable risks. Referring to the experience of May 2025, Jamil stressed that there was no space for war between two nuclear-armed states.
He also highlighted Pakistan's credible nuclear deterrence, conventional capabilities, national resilience and cohesive response framework, including the principle of "quid pro quo-plus", saying these were aimed at ensuring that no aggressor could achieve its political or military objectives through force.
Earlier, Maj-Gen (retd) Syed Shahab Shahid, director general of Arms Control and Disarmament Affairs at the SPD, said the global arms-control, disarmament and non-proliferation architecture was facing growing challenges. He called for a balanced, equitable and non-discriminatory approach that took into account the legitimate security concerns of all states.
Shahid said the continued modernisation and diversification of nuclear and strategic capabilities, alongside emerging developments in South Asia, were reshaping the strategic environment and creating new challenges for strategic stability.
He warned that the selective application of non-proliferation norms and security arrangements could undermine confidence in the existing international security architecture, stressing the need for a consistent and inclusive approach to strengthening strategic stability, reducing risks and advancing meaningful arms-control and non-proliferation objectives.
In his opening remarks, CISS Executive Director Ambassador Ali Sarwar Naqvi reflected on Pakistan's strategic environment, tracing its regional relevance and the opportunities and challenges shaping its security landscape.
He highlighted Pakistan's role as a diplomatic actor and its stated commitment to regional stability, while underscoring the importance of effective strategic responses to an increasingly complex security environment.
Senator Mushahid Hussain Sayed, in his keynote address, said Pakistan was emerging as a credible middle power in the evolving international order. He said Pakistan's ability to mediate, engage and build partnerships in an increasingly fragmented world reflected what he described as the country's growing strategic weight.

title: Public servants told not to feed sensitive data into AI
description: Public servants told not to feed sensitive data into AI
content:
Employees warned against sharing confidential information
Government employees have been barred from uploading classified documents and other sensitive information to public artificial intelligence (AI) tools under the National Cyber Security Handbook 2026-27 issued by the National Cyber Emergency Response Team.
The handbook, issued under the Pakistan Information Security Framework 2026, lays down a set of rules governing the use of AI in government affairs.
Officials will be required to use only AI tools and platforms approved by their respective departments, while government emails, software source code and citizens' personal information have also been prohibited from being shared on public AI platforms.
According to the National CERT, providing sensitive information to AI platforms carries the risk of data leaks and unauthorised use.
The handbook directs government employees not to upload classified documents to public AI tools. They have also been instructed not to share government email content or software source code on such platforms.
Citizens' personal information is also not to be uploaded to public artificial intelligence tools.
Government officials will be allowed to use only those AI tools and platforms that have been approved by their departments.
The handbook further instructs employees to remove names and other sensitive information from AI prompts and files before submitting them to such tools.
Any accidental disclosure of confidential information must be reported immediately to the relevant IT or cybersecurity team, according to the National CERT.

title: Consumer court orders clothing brand to refund bag charge
description: Consumer court orders clothing brand to refund bag charge
content:
Judge Gandapur observed that the receipt annexed with the complaint clearly showed the extra Rs30 charge
A consumer protection court has accepted a complaint against a leading clothing brand, directing the company to refund Rs30 charged to a customer for a shopping bag, pay her Rs25,000 in compensation, and deposit a fine of Rs25,000 to the government.
Consumer Case No 84/CC of 2026 was decided by Judge Nasrullah Khan Gandapur of the Consumer Protection Court, who heard arguments from complainant's counsel Ahsan Sardar and the brand's counsel Muhammad Omea.
The complainant, Shafaq Aamir, had filed the case on February 14 under Section 13 of the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Consumer Protection Act, 1997, alleging that on December 20, 2025, she purchased clothing worth Rs7,000 from the outlet of the clothing brand on Peshawar's University Road and was additionally charged Rs30 for a carrying bag printed with the brand's promotional logo.
The respondent did not deny the allegation, but contended that it was not obligated to provide bags free of cost and offered them only on specific customer demand.
In his judgment, Judge Gandapur observed that the receipt annexed with the complaint clearly showed the extra Rs30 charge, and that customers were under the belief that purchased items would be delivered in a carrying bag without charges.
The court observed that the bag, bearing the brand's logo, was "obviously provided for promotion of the brand and that too at the cost of the consumers," noting that the company would otherwise have to provide ordinary bags to customers.
"The respondent not only charged the complainant an extra amount but also used the bag for promotion of its brand," the judgment read, holding the practice to be an unfair trade practice under Section 2(O)(xii)(xiii) of the Act.
The decision was announced on September 16 after the court perused the record and heard both sides under Section 14(2)(b) of the Act. The file has been consigned to the record room after completion.

title: LHC suspends PMDC medical fee hike
description: LHC suspends PMDC medical fee hike
content:
PMDC restores four-year BDS, easing students' fee burden
The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Friday suspended a Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) notification allowing an increase in fees charged by medical colleges.
Justice Khalid Ishaq issued this order while hearing a petition filed by Lahore's Central Park Medical College challenging the PMDC notification.
Advocate Ramzan Dhuddi, representing the petitioner college, argued that the college had charged students Rs2.1 million in fees at the time of admission. He submitted that the PMDC subsequently issued a notification allowing medical colleges to increase their annual fees by five per cent.
According to the petitioner, the PMDC also issued a notification allowing the collection of fees linked to the Consumer Price Index (CPI). The counsel argued that the PMDC lacked the authority to issue a notification increasing medical students' fees.
He contended that parliament could amend the relevant laws governing the PMDC and issue directions concerning an increase in medical education fees. The counsel requested the court to declare the PMDC notification allowing an increase in medical students' fees illegal and set it aside.
After hearing the arguments, the court suspended the PMDC notification.
Meanwhile, the PMDC has withdrawn an earlier notification that extended the duration of the Bachelor of Dental Surgery (BDS) programme to five years and revived the original four years tenure, providing relief to students from paying an additional year's fees.
According to a notification issued by the PMDC, the BDS framework notification issued on July 8, 2026 has been withdrawn following concerns raised by the Pakistan Dental Association and directions from parliamentary committees.
"The BDS degree will be completed in four years, but one year of clerkship will be mandatory," PMDC President Dr Rizwan Taj said, speaking to The Express Tribune. "The decision will provide relief to students as they would no longer have to pay fees for the additional year."
Separately, the PMDC's decision to collect question papers from candidates immediately after the Medical and Dental College Admission Test (MDCAT) has triggered fresh concerns over examination transparency and the mechanism for challenging disputed questions.
In the latest letter addressed to the vice chancellors of all universities conducting MDCAT, the PMDC Examination Department directed that question papers be collected from candidates immediately after completion of the test.
The letter further stated that no question paper should be given to any candidate, explaining that this measure is intended to ensure the safe and smooth conduct of the examination process.
The directive is significant because more than 138,000 candidates are scheduled to appear in MDCAT 2026 across the country on September 20.
The central concern being raised is what happens if a candidate believes that a question is ambiguous, contains an incorrect option, has more than one apparently correct answer or falls outside the prescribed syllabus.

title: PKLI marks kidney transplant milestone

The Pakistan Kidney and Liver Institute and Research Centre (PKLI&RC) Rawalpindi successfully performed its first kidney transplant, a top official said on Friday.

title: Bari Imam anti slums drive rolls into phase II
description: Bari Imam anti slums drive rolls into phase II
content:
Red notices issued to residents of six localities; drive launched in Saidpur, E-11 & E-12
The Capital Development Authority (CDA) and administration have resumed operations against Islamabad's slums and illegal constructions after a three-month break.
After demolishing more than half of the 14 localities of Bari Imam and Noorpur Shahan, red notices have been issued to residents of all six localities behind the Bari Imam shrine, ordering them to vacate their houses within 72 hours.
Meanwhile, all temporary and permanent encroachments in Saidpur village, E-11 and E-12 have been demolished.
Residents were not even given time to remove their household belongings, prompting strong protests. Demonstrations and protests were also held, but the administration, with the help of police, foiled all resistance and removed the encroachments. Police also made announcements over loudspeakers asking residents to vacate their homes.
More than 50 kanals of land was reclaimed and the operation continued throughout the day.
Three months ago, an operation had been conducted in the Bari Imam area in front of and on both sides of the shrine, during which houses and shops in all streets and localities, as well as the main Bari Imam Bazaar, were completely bulldozed.
Preparations have now been completed for the second phase of the operation in the localities behind the Bari Imam shrine. Red notices have been issued to all houses in the areas behind the shrine, including Opar Mohalla Shehar, Banan Mohalla and those along the Margalla Hills.
After receiving the notices, residents who had been living there for more than 100 years began removing their valuables. Residents of the areas also started removing expensive tiles and iron fittings installed in their houses.
Meanwhile, a large number of contractors dealing in old building material have reached the localities behind the Bari Imam shrine and started purchasing debris from double-storey houses for Rs500,000 to Rs800,000.
The contractors, along with dozens of labourers, have started removing wood and iron windows, cupboards, doors and ventilators from the houses.
They have also started removing tiles and fixtures from kitchens and bathrooms. Old tiles, bricks, windows and doors from houses have been placed in the areas for sale.
Residents Faizullah, Hamid Khan and Haji Ibrahim said no alternative place or compensation was being provided to any resident, while the operation team maintained that no compensation was payable for encroachments.
After the operation, only the Bari Imam shrine will remain in the entire Noorpur Shahan area, with residential settlements on all four sides completely removed. In the third phase, several acres of government land around the Bari Imam shrine will also be separated from the shrine.

The Grocery Merchants Association has strongly rejected the order to close grocery shops, supermarkets and general stores across the country at 9pm under the "smart lockdown", saying it would resist the decision.
"We condemn the decision and will also resist it. Businesses across the country have already been devastated. If shops are again forced to close at 9pm, the remaining businesses will be completely destroyed and thousands of employees working at these shops will have to be laid off to enforce the lockdown," the association said.
It said "businesses should be given free time" to keep the wheel of the national economy moving.
Central President Hafiz Arif Gujjar and divisional president Sheikh Saleem Parvez Butt said that over the past four years, all businesses, including grocery stores, had reached the brink of destruction. They said daily increases in petroleum prices had raised goods transportation fares, dealing another blow to the economy.
They said the smart lockdown would completely destroy the remaining business activity and increase unemployment. "We strongly condemn it," they said.
They said closing shops, markets, plazas and business establishments early under the smart lockdown would make it impossible to achieve tax targets.

title: Directorate sealing leaves staff on road

content:
Officials work from roadside as records of over 100 colleges remain locked inside
The Directorate of Colleges has been left without an office after the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) and Evacuee Trust Property Board sealed the Directorate of Education Colleges at the Education Complex on Murree Road.
The entire record of 101 colleges in the division, including that of professors and employees, has also been sealed.
On Friday, the director and deputy director of colleges set up their offices by the roadside on Murree Road.
Employees and officers marked their attendance on plain paper on the road outside the sealed directorate, while the director of colleges performed official duties standing on the footpath.
The commissioner and deputy commissioner refused to provide any assistance to the college directorate, saying the matter was completely beyond their control.
Directorate employees approached the secretary higher education at 11am on Thursday after the sealing, but even after 36 hours no response had been received.
The highest authorities have also refused to restore the Directorate of Colleges, offering only two to three hours under tight police security to remove equipment.
The directorate has been given a final message that its presence at the site is now a thing of the past. Two or three rooms are being temporarily provided in a girls' or boys' college from Monday.
Meanwhile, permanent police and FIA personnel have been deployed at the sealed directorate, and education officers and employees have been barred from standing in front of its gate.
All Pakistan Clerks Association (Apca) Education Colleges president Malik Jameel Awan strongly condemned the sealing, saying Apca Rawalpindi condemned the forcible eviction of officers and employees from the building, its takeover and the seizure of government machinery and records.
He said the building had been used for the administrative affairs of the education sector for several decades, and administrative matters of 101 government colleges in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Chakwal districts of the Rawalpindi division were being handled from there.
"Important educational and administrative matters concerning thousands of employees as well as millions of students are associated with this office. Vacating and taking over such an important educational and administrative centre in this manner is highly regrettable and a cause for concern," he said.
He said the seizure of government records, computers, machinery and other office equipment could seriously affect routine government affairs and matters concerning employees and students.

title: ATC rejects May 9 Radio Pakistan report
description: ATC rejects May 9 Radio Pakistan report
content:
Orders police to submit full forensic, NADRA record
An anti-terrorism court in Peshawar on Friday rejected an investigation report submitted by police in the case relating to the May 9 attack on Radio Pakistan Peshawar, declaring it incomplete and inconclusive and directing the investigating officer to submit a comprehensive final report.
The court ordered the investigating officer to place the complete investigation record before it on September 24 in light of reports obtained from the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA), Lahore, and the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA).
The case relates to violence and protests that erupted on May 9 following the arrest of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Imran Khan, during which Radio Pakistan Peshawar was attacked and damaged.
Radio Pakistan was represented by Advocate Shabbir Hussain Gigyani, while Additional Advocate General and Special Prosecutor Nauman Haq Kakakhel appeared for the prosecution. DSP Khushal Khan, the investigating officer, was also present.
During the proceedings, the court was informed that merely placing PFSA and NADRA reports on record would not be sufficient. The investigating officer was required to incorporate the findings of the reports into the investigation and submit all supporting evidence and relevant records along with the final report.
After hearing the arguments, the court observed that the report submitted by the investigating officer on September 12 was opinion-based and inconclusive. It also noted that the report did not correspond with the application submitted by Radio Pakistan.
The court therefore declined to treat the report as the final investigation report and directed the investigating officer to complete the investigation on the basis of the forensic and NADRA findings.
The court specifically directed the investigation team to include details of all investigative steps undertaken, their findings and the relevant documentary and other evidence in the final report.
The proceedings also covered the police's move to nominate certain political and other individuals in the case on the basis of crime videos, forensic laboratory reports and NADRA records. However, the court stopped short of accepting the existing report as conclusive and directed police to place the complete investigation process and final findings before the court.
The court adjourned further proceedings until September 24.
Separately, the Peshawar High Court suspended a provincial government notification concerning land acquired for the proposed Bannu Gul City housing project and issued notices to the relevant authorities seeking their replies.
A two-member bench comprising Justice Tariq Afridi and Justice Sabitullah Khan heard a petition filed by Noor Afzal and others. Advocate Pir Hamidullah Shah represented the petitioners.
The petitioner's counsel said the government planned to acquire more than 10,000 kanals for the housing project, which he described as one of the province's largest schemes after the Peshawar Valley project.

title: Sindh urged to prioritise people in clean energy shift
description: Sindh urged to prioritise people in clean energy shift
content:
Experts demand land rights protection; projects face scrutiny over livelihoods
Experts, civil society representatives, policymakers and energy-sector stakeholders have called for a community-centred and inclusive transition towards clean and renewable energy in Sindh, stressing that livelihoods, land rights and well-being of local communities must not be compromised by new energy projects.
The call was made at a strategic stakeholder dialogue titled "Just Energy Transition in Sindh: Ensuring Community-Centred and Inclusive Clean Energy Development". The dialogue was jointly organised by The Citizenry, an online media platform focused on research-based journalism, and The Knowledge Forum, a think tank working on human rights and development.
The consultation focused on four themes: upcoming renewable energy projects at 13 sites in Thatta, Sujawal, Badin and Tharparkar; potential for green jobs; community benefit-sharing and corporate social responsibility in renewable energy; and land laws, resettlement and rehabilitation related to energy projects.
Oonib Azam of The Citizenry presented the organisation's study, "Socio-Economic Evidence from Umerkot and Policy Recommendations for Renewable Energy Development." Based on a survey of 204 respondents in 12 villages, field observations and expert interviews, the study found gaps in basic services and infrastructure, land insecurity, limited community participation and unequal access to development benefits.
Residents expressed concern about displacement, informal land tenure and their limited role in decisions on renewable energy projects. The Citizenry noted that existing and planned projects were not consistently aligned with the Power Generation Policy 2015, Nepra Social Investment Guidelines 2021 and, where applicable, the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, which promote community engagement, local jobs, skills development, gender inclusion, healthcare, livelihoods, fair compensation and livelihood restoration.
Zehra Shallwani of New Energy Nexus highlighted that technical training was essential as solarisation expanded in off-grid and energy-deprived areas. She noted that poor solar-system design, installation and maintenance had caused financial losses to communities, while young people from Thatta often migrated to larger cities for employment.
Kamal Pallari, a local community member from Jhimpir, said wind power plants had provided little employment or social services to local residents. Instead, he said, projects affected livelihoods through land acquisition, flattening of productive land and restrictions on communities' privacy and mobility.
Abira Ashfaq of Green Chamber said communities in Sindh faced infringement of land rights, loss of livelihoods and displacement, while indigenous people were sometimes described as "encroachers" in energy-project reports.
