At the height of the price surge in early April, petrol reached a record Rs458.40 per litre , after the government raised it by Rs137 in a single revision.
The federal government on July 17 announced that petroleum product prices would now be reviewed and notified on a daily basis, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continue to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
The decision had come after the government had already shifted from fortnightly to weekly fuel price revisions following the first phase of the US-Iran conflict.
The move, however, drew criticism from transporters , businesses and opposition lawmakers, who argued that frequent price revisions would create uncertainty, drive up transport and freight costs, and make it difficult for businesses and consumers to plan expenses. Petrol pump owners also threatened a nationwide strike before suspending the protest after the government assured them their concerns would be addressed.

title: Lena Khan brings competitive Bollywood fusion dance to Netflix with  Best of the Best
description: Filmmaker discusses on screen South Asian representation  urges community to be proud of own culture
content:
Filmmaker discusses on-screen South Asian representation, urges community to be proud of own culture
Competitive Bollywood-fusion dance takes centre stage in Lena Khan’s latest Netflix film Best of the Best , a coming-of-age story that brings South Asian dance culture, friendship and fierce campus competition to the screen.
The film follows childhood best friends Maya and Anjali as they join a competitive dance team and set their sights on the US Championship. However, what initially appears to be an exciting college experience soon becomes an intense and sometimes cutthroat battle.
According to Variety , Lena was drawn to the project partly because of what she felt the story could represent for South Asian audiences. The director recalled telling a childhood friend about the film, only to be met with a dismissive response: “Bollywood competitions, really?”
For Lena, the reaction reflected a larger issue within the South Asian diaspora. “I think South Asians, especially in the diaspora, are so used to not even having our own self-respect,” she told Variety .
That idea ultimately influenced the film’s tone. Rather than treating South Asian culture as something that needed to be introduced or explained to audiences, Lena wanted the film to embrace it with confidence.
“We have so much respect for the skill sets of other cultures. We’re looking at kung fu, we’re looking at these different arts. But when we look at our own, we’re used to seeing ourselves as Apu or as the funny nerdy side characters,” she said. “We can be proud of things that we do as South Asians,” the filmmaker added.
The director’s previous work on Netflix’s Never Have I Ever also informed her approach to representation.
“When you have more than one of a minority character, then there’s suddenly become real characters,” she said, explaining that greater representation allowed stories to move beyond tokenism and focus on relationships and human experiences.
“You get to focus on the humanity between them, the things that become relatable to everybody else,” she stated.
The film’s writers, Hasan Minhaj and Prashanth Venkataramanujam, also brought personal experience to the screenplay. Both had connections to competitive performance circuits while growing up, giving the story a grounding in the intensity and commitment required by such teams.
Hasan Minhaj on set of Best of the Best. Photo: Variety
Variety reported that Minhaj’s wife also competed in dance, while Venkataramanujam performed with an a cappella group called Chai Town.
However, working with Minhaj and Venkataramanujam, who were both writing their first feature screenplay, was not always straightforward for Lena. The filmmaker shared that the trio frequently disagreed during the creative process, but those disagreements were rooted in meaningful discussions about the story.
“There would be such a thoughtful reason that we were always fighting over why we’re doing a certain thing, but it was never for a vapid reason,” she said, adding the two “are also just the most gracious people.”
Lena also immersed herself in the world she was preparing to portray, spending time with UCLA’s dance team and travelling to North Carolina to observe competitions.
For the cast, too, the film demanded more than acting ability. Several performers had little or no competitive dance experience before they joined the project, meaning extensive preparation was required.
Lena specifically pushed the Never Have I Ever star Maitreyi Ramakrishnan to undergo a major physical transformation for the role. “I need you to give me some Channing Tatum energy. And then I was like, no, actually, I need you to do a Christian Bale on me. I need a complete athletic transformation,” the filmmaker recalled telling Maitreyi. The actor subsequently underwent months of intensive dance training before filming began.
Discussing the dance numbers, Lena shared that rather than approaching the sequences simply as large-scale spectacles, each one began with a central creative question: “What is the essence we are trying to bring out in this particular moment?”
The production also faced a tight shooting schedule, with choreography styles that included Kuthu, Bharatanatyam and Pakistani-influenced dances, reflecting the varied cultural backgrounds represented within the fictional team.
“At some point this country and the world is just full of people in different cultures,” Lena said.
For the filmmaker, the goal was not simply to make films that featured South Asian characters, but to reach a point where those stories could exist without constantly being treated as cultural lessons.
She pointed to broader changes in the entertainment industry since her 2016 independent feature The Tiger Hunter , while noting that gaps remain. “We still don’t have that many romances or romantic comedies with South Asians,” Lena said, adding that South Asian men in particular were often not given opportunities to play romantic leads.
Best of the Best played with those conventions in its own way. Lena noted that the film’s “nerdy minority character” is instead a white character. “Like we have a token white guy,” she said.
The filmmaker also credited the growing visibility of South Asian performers and musicians with helping create space for projects such as Best of the Best . Among the artists she highlighted was British-Sri Lankan singer Joy Crookes, whose music she fought to include in the film’s soundtrack.
The director said the larger cultural shift had brought South Asian representation to a different point. “And now we’re like, well, we’ve really made it when we make a movie that’s just good,” she said.
Looking beyond Best of the Best , Lena said she remained interested in stories about overlooked people and subjects, particularly projects she wished already existed. “I’m always on the hunt for that,” she said, describing an ongoing search for stories that could introduce audiences to subjects that had not received enough attention.
Best of the Best, which premiered on Netflix on September 18, also stars Lilly Singh, Nihar Duvvuri, Nico Greetham, Amryn Khurana, Tanishq Joshi, Saara Chaudry and Sasha Bhasin, alongside Maitreyi.

title: Asim Azhar expresses support for Hania Aamir s  Pablo   calls song  banger

content:
Singer says he relates to Hania's expressiveness, wants more Pakistani women breaking into pop music
Singer Asim Azhar described actor Hania Aamir as "an amazing artist" and termed her new song Pablo a "banger."
Discussing the track in a clip shared by the BBC Asian Network , Azhar noted that he related to Hania "with the expressiveness," adding that he was excited to see this side of the actor.
Pushing back on listeners judging her foray into music too harshly, the singer argued, "Just because she's known as an actor doesn't mean she can't also write and release music as a genuine outlet for her feelings," urging fans to take it in that spirit rather than critiquing it like a talent show.
He singled out her self-written lyrics as especially sharp, noting that each line tackled a different controversy she'd faced.
Azhar also stated, " Pablo, hopefully, marks the start of more Pakistani women breaking into pop music; I see real potential for Hania's debut to inspire more women across Pakistan, South Asia and beyond to do the same."
"I want to see Pakistani pop girlies outnumbering Pakistani male pop stars," the singer added.
This wasn't the only time Azhar showed love for Hania's track this week. Earlier, he shared a video of himself in London, set to Pablo .
The clip landed just as Azhar closed out the British leg of his Asim Ali album tour in London on September 20 at the Troxy — a show he had earlier billed as his biggest international concert to date.
Pablo marked Hania's debut into the music world. Released on September 9, the track features Hania addressing criticism regarding her public image in a mix of Punjabi rap and singing. The song closes with a surprise voice message from Indian television personality Rakhi Sawant.

title: Brad Pitt returning for World War Z sequel with Edward Berger directing
description: Berger will direct from a screenplay by Dennis Kelly  with Pitt returning to reprise his role as Gerry Lane
content:
Berger will direct from a screenplay by Dennis Kelly, with Pitt returning to reprise his role as Gerry Lane
Brad Pitt is set to return for a sequel to World War Z, with Conclave director Edward Berger attached to direct the long-awaited follow-up for Paramount.
Berger will direct from a screenplay by Dennis Kelly, with Pitt returning to reprise his role as Gerry Lane, the former United Nations investigator at the centre of the 2013 zombie thriller. The project marks another collaboration between Pitt and Berger after they recently worked together on The Riders for A24.
The sequel has been in development for years, with Paramount previously attempting to bring the project to the big screen with Pitt and director David Fincher. That version ultimately fell apart, but the studio confirmed in April that another World War Z film was in active development.
The original World War Z, released in 2013, was directed by Marc Forster and based on Max Brooks’ 2006 novel. Pitt starred as Gerry Lane, who travels across the globe searching for a way to stop a rapidly spreading zombie pandemic.
The film became a commercial success, earning around $540 million worldwide and becoming one of Paramount’s notable releases of the year.
The new sequel is currently being developed at Paramount, with further details about its story, production schedule and release date yet to be announced. Berger’s involvement reunites him with Pitt following their work on The Riders, which is scheduled as another major collaboration between the filmmaker and actor.

title: Macklemore ticket prices surge after Ed Sheeran tour fallout
description: The cheapest available ticket for Macklemore   s solo October concert went from  108 to  157 over three days
content:
The cheapest available ticket for Macklemore’s solo October concert went from $108 to $157 over three days
Macklemore’s ticket prices have surged following his removal from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour after the rapper spoke publicly in support of Palestine.
According to ticket-tracking company TicketData, the cheapest available ticket for Macklemore’s October concert at Colorado’s Red Rocks Amphitheatre rose 45% over three days, climbing from $108 to $157. TicketData founder Keith Pagello told CNBC the increase would not have happened without the events surrounding Macklemore’s departure from Sheeran’s tour.
Macklemore was removed from the remaining US dates of Sheeran’s tour after making pro-Palestinian comments during a performance at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium on September 4. He later said he had been told stadium owners had threatened to cancel shows if he remained on the line-up.
The fallout has also affected Sheeran’s ticket market. Resale prices for nine of the 10 remaining venues on the Loop Tour have declined, according to TicketData, although Pagello cautioned that falling prices are common as concert dates approach and may not necessarily be connected to the controversy.
There has, however, been an increase in resale activity for Sheeran’s upcoming shows. TicketData reported that tickets have been changing hands at a higher rate than at previous tour stops at a similar point in their sales cycle.
The dispute has continued to escalate, with all of Sheeran’s other supporting acts, including Finneas, Lukas Graham, Aaron Rowe and Beoga, withdrawing from the remaining dates after Macklemore’s removal.
Sheeran has maintained that Macklemore’s departure was the promoter’s decision rather than his own. Meanwhile, Macklemore announced that he would donate $1 million from his net earnings from the tour to organisations supporting Palestinians.
The ticket-market changes add a financial dimension to the growing fallout surrounding the tour, although the available data does not establish whether the shifts are directly attributable to the controversy.

title: France probes misuse of smart glasses in sexual harassment cases
description: France s CNIL received under 10 workplace complaints over smart glasses and growing queries on banning them
content:
France's CNIL received under 10 workplace complaints over smart glasses and growing queries on banning them
Paris prosecutors have opened a criminal probe into suspected sexual harassment involving smart glasses, while French data protection authorities have received complaints from businesses, as countries around the world grapple with the devices' social impact.
There are several smart glasses available, but US ​tech giant Meta's glasses made in collaboration with Essilor Luxottica are the market leader , with a roughly 76% share globally.
Meta's AI-enabled glasses, which ‌have a small embedded camera allowing the wearer to record discreetly, have been a global hit, selling 7 million units last year. Essilor's latest sales figures point to "exponential growth" in 2026.
But their success has led to growing international scrutiny from prosecutors, regulators, rights groups and companies over issues including sexual harassment, corporate wrongdoing and illicit surveillance.
Some UK cinemas ​have banned smart glasses , and a German consumer advocacy group has filed a criminal complaint against Meta and other companies involved in selling the devices ​in Germany, citing privacy laws.
The Paris prosecutor's office told Reuters it had recently opened at least one criminal probe ⁠following sexual harassment complaints related to a social media trend of using smart glasses to film women on the street, without their consent, and posting ​the videos online. The prosecutors did not specify the brand of devices used.
Read More: German court rules Meta liable for fake ads on Instagram, Facebook
It declined to give more details, but said its cybercrime unit tested the devices ​two weeks ago to gain a better understanding of the potential crimes that smart glasses could be used to commit.
A Meta spokesperson said the company had "built privacy into our AI glasses from the ground up," adding that "we will keep strengthening our protections as our glasses become even more capable." EssilorLuxottica declined to comment.
CNIL, France's data protection authority, said ​it had received under 10 complaints around smart glasses being used in the workplace. It did not disclose which brands. It also said it was ​being increasingly contacted by businesses wanting to know whether they could ban smart glasses at work.
Australia said on Thursday it is considering barring the use of camera-equipped smart glasses ‌in government ⁠workplaces due to privacy and security concerns, in what it said could be the first ban of its kind.
Smart glasses pose "real challenges" in terms of informing people that they are being filmed and getting consent when needed, said CNIL's head of economic affairs Nacera Bekhat.
AI-enabled wearable devices are regulated by the European Union's AI Act and the General Data Protection Regulation, or GDPR, which set rules on how people's personal data can be used.
Though French law provides ​privacy protections - including penalties of up to ​a year in prison or ⁠a €45,000 ($51,700) fine - for recording the image of a person in a private place without their consent, enforcement can be difficult, particularly when content is quickly disseminated online, CNIL and other legal sources said.
A small light in the devices' frames ​indicates that filming is taking place, but rights groups said that shifts the responsibility of avoiding being filmed ​onto the individual.
"Seeing ⁠a light come on doesn't mean that you consent to being filmed, nor to have your image distributed to thousands of people afterwards," said Ines Legendre, legal expert at internet safety organisation e-Enfance.
Women are the primary target of abuse done using smart glasses, rights groups say.
Ines Girard, who runs projects relating to technology-facilitated gender-based ⁠violence at ​feminist organisation Hubertine Auclert, said the tech industry should do more to prevent abuse.
"We can't respond ​to a surveillance technology by telling the people being surveilled that they should be more vigilant," she said.
"This places an additional burden on these individuals, particularly women, gender minorities and people ​already exposed to violence, online abuse and scrutiny in public spaces."

title: China s AI supercluster completes 10 day global forecast in under an hour
description: Sugon 8000 combines general and accelerated processors  ensuring consistent results and computing efficiency
content:
Sugon 8000 combines general and accelerated processors, ensuring consistent results and computing efficiency
Most people checking a weather forecast rarely think about the computing power behind it.
But a Chinese-developed artificial intelligence supercomputing system can calculate global atmospheric changes for the next 10 days in less than an hour, according to technology company Sugon and a center under the China Meteorological Administration (CMA).
Sugon and CMA's Earth System Modeling and Prediction Center jointly announced that China's independently developed MCV numerical model completed a 10-day global forecast calculation at a 5-kilometer resolution within one hour.
The model ran on the domestically produced "Sugon 8000" AI supercluster.
At that resolution, the model divides the global atmosphere into grid cells about five kilometers apart. That allows forecasters to show the spiral structure of typhoons and the movement of weather fronts much more clearly.
As grids become denser, computing units must exchange far more data, and simulation results must be written to storage promptly. Communication, storage and task allocation play an increasingly important role in overall efficiency, so simply adding more processors may not speed up the entire forecast proportionally.
Major modeling efforts are turning to accelerated computing platforms as they push toward global kilometer-scale forecasting.
The "Sugon 8000" system combines general-purpose and accelerated processors and verifies that results from different computing units are strictly consistent, meeting requirements for both computing efficiency and result reliability, according to the announcement.
Read More: Founder of Chinese startup Spirit AI says robot brains set for 2027 breakthrough
The achievement is an important collaborative innovation between China's self-developed numerical model and domestically produced computing power, the announcement said. It lays a foundation for continued efforts toward kilometer-scale and hundred-meter-scale forecasting in this field.
Sugon Chairman Li Jun said the company aims to make high-performance computing an important infrastructure for understanding the Earth and foreseeing the future.
"The value of advanced computing should be shown in solving major scientific problems and supporting industrial innovation," Li said.
The applications of the "Sugon 8000" extend beyond weather forecasting.
More refined and timely forecasts affect flood-season preparedness, agricultural production, flight scheduling and power supply, so meeting computing time targets provides an important condition for these fields, according to the announcement.
Large-scale numerical simulation is also necessary for processes that are difficult to observe directly or reproduce through repeated experiments, such as structural changes in proteins and fluid movements in turbulent flows.
The "Sugon 8000" has carried out large-scale computing projects in areas including protein research, molecular dynamics and turbulence simulation. It supports nearly 200 industry applications and more than 500 mainstream large models, covering more than 30 scientific and industrial fields.
Li said Sugon will deepen cooperation with research institutions, closely integrate computing technology with research needs, and provide tools for scientists to explore more complex problems.

title: House of David    to end with Season 3 as biblical drama enters final chapter
description: Production on final season is underway in Greece with Michael Iskander returning as David
content:
Production on final season is underway in Greece with Michael Iskander returning as David
Amazon’s biblical drama House of David will end with its upcoming third season, with production now underway in Greece. The announcement comes after Amazon MGM Studios and Wonder Project previously renewed the series for Season 3 in July without revealing that it would be the final instalment.
The creators had previously envisioned the story as a three season arc centred on David’s rise from an overlooked shepherd to the future king of Israel. Season 3 will now bring that planned story to its conclusion.
Executive producers Jon Erwin and Jon Gunn said the production had returned to Greece with its cast and crew and described the new season as the final chapter of the story they set out to tell. They also expressed gratitude to Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios for supporting the series.
Michael Iskander, who plays David, is returning for the final season alongside Ali Suliman as King Saul and Ayelet Zurer as Queen Ahinoam. The wider cast includes Indy Lewis, Yali Topol Margalith, Ethan Kai, Sam Otto, Oded Fehr, Louis Ferreira, Davood Ghadami, Aury Alby and Alexander Uloom.
Season 3 will follow David after his transformation into a warrior and his selection as future king. However, his path to the throne will not be straightforward. The official story description places David in exile, where he becomes a hunted outlaw and is forced to hide among his enemies while living under another identity.
The final season is expected to explore the personal cost of David’s journey, including betrayals, sacrifices and difficult choices before he can finally claim his destiny.
The series is produced by Wonder Project and Amazon MGM Studios, in association with Nomadic Pictures, Argonauts, Kingdom Story Company and Lionsgate Television. Dallas Jenkins, creator of The Chosen , serves as a shareholder and special adviser to Wonder Project.
The first two seasons of House of David are currently available on Prime Video, giving viewers an opportunity to revisit David’s journey before the final season arrives. No release date for Season 3 has been announced yet.

title: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce face setback over privacy fence at Ohio mansion
description: The couple have reportedly installed a voice warning system around their Lake Erie property
content:
The couple have reportedly installed a voice warning system around their Lake Erie property
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce have reportedly run into a planning obstacle while trying to increase privacy at their new Ohio mansion, with local rules limiting the type of fence they can build around the lakeside property.
According to Page Six , the couple initially sought an 8 foot fence around their Bratenahl estate, which Kelce purchased for $5.35m in March. The property sits along Lake Erie and is reported to cover about 21,000 square feet, with eight bedrooms and 11 bathrooms.
The proposed fencing faced restrictions under Bratenahl regulations. Lakefront fences are generally limited to 2.5 feet unless at least 75% of the structure is see through. The rules are intended to protect views of Lake Erie, the shoreline and surrounding property values.
The proposal reportedly appeared before the Bratenahl Architectural Review Board in August and returned for discussion in September without receiving approval. Following conversations with neighbours and village officials, Swift and Kelce reportedly agreed to consider a shorter fence that would not completely surround the estate. A revised application has reportedly been submitted.
The reported setback comes as the couple take other measures to protect their privacy. Page Six reported that a voice warning system has been installed around the property. One neighbour claimed that approaching the house triggered an automated warning telling the person not to enter the property.
Despite the attention surrounding the mansion, a local real estate agent told Page Six that she had not heard of significant disruption caused by the couple since their arrival.
Kelce purchased the property before his July wedding to Swift. The estate is close to Cleveland Heights, where the Kansas City Chiefs star grew up, adding a personal connection to the Ohio home.
For now, the fencing plans remain subject to the village approval process, leaving the couple to balance their desire for privacy with Bratenahl’s rules for lakefront properties.

title: Brittany Snow marks 17 years of eating disorder recovery with emotional message
description: Snow credited her friends and family for supporting her through the difficult early stages of recovery
content:
Snow credited her friends and family for supporting her through the difficult early stages of recovery
Brittany Snow has marked 17 years of recovery from an eating disorder, reflecting on a period in her life when she could not imagine reaching the future she has today.
The 40 year old actress shared an Instagram post on September 17 marking the anniversary of the decision she described as choosing to stop hurting herself. Snow said she once struggled to picture life beyond her eating disorder and did not know whether she would make it through that period.
Looking back, Snow credited the people around her for helping her during the early stages of recovery. She said her friends supported and listened to her, while her family continued to show her love. She also described an inner voice that encouraged her not to give up.
Snow used the milestone to address people who may currently be experiencing similar struggles. She said they are not alone and encouraged them to hold on to the possibility of a future that may currently be difficult to imagine.
She also reflected on how her own experience has changed the way she views recovery. Snow said being able to share hope with people facing similar circumstances has become one of the greatest gifts of making it through her own difficulties.
The actress has spoken publicly about her mental health and eating disorder history for years. In a 2025 interview with Self , she discussed receiving treatment for anorexia, exercise bulimia, depression and self harm. She also described struggling with negative feelings towards her body when she was younger.
Snow has continued to connect her personal experiences with her creative work. Her 2023 film Parachute , which marked her feature directorial debut, centres on a young woman dealing with body image and an eating disorder.
For Snow, the September 17 milestone represented a significant point in a recovery journey she once could not imagine completing.

title: New US sanctions bill on Russia puts India s Modi in a bind
description: Cutting Russian oil could raise fuel prices  while maintaining imports risks crippling exports to the US
content:
Cutting Russian oil could raise fuel prices, while maintaining imports risks crippling exports to the US
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is caught in an energy policy bind with no easy exit.
Cutting Russian ​oil imports to avoid potential new US tariffs could increase fuel prices ahead of key regional elections, or stress government finances. Maintaining such purchases could cripple Indian exports to ‌its largest market.
India, the world's third-largest oil importer and among the biggest buyers of Russian crude, reacted unusually strongly on Thursday to a US congressional bill that would allow Washington to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries, including India and China, for major purchases of Russian oil.
The sharp response showed how an energy trade that has delivered India billions of dollars in savings since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 is now colliding with its broader strategic and commercial interests.
New Delhi ​said it had warned the United States that the measure could damage bilateral relations and disrupt global energy markets, vowing to keep "ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people" by buying ​from diversified sources.
But holding firm could further strain ties with Washington after a turbulent year marked by repeated disputes over trade and tariffs under President Donald ⁠Trump. A planned trade deal between the two countries has already faced multiple delays.
Two Indian sources said the latest tensions did not mean New Delhi would abandon hopes of striking a ​trade deal with Washington, though they said India may increasingly need to lean on deals elsewhere if additional US tariffs hit exports.
Since last year, India has signed a trade deal with Britain, finalised one with ​the EU and is looking to conclude talks on another one with Canada by the end of the year.
New Delhi is hoping for a breakthrough when Modi travels to the US for the G20 summit in December, where he could meet Trump on the sidelines, said one of the sources.
The White House and the Indian government did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
"The US-India relationship has suffered over the last year for a range of reasons, including US tariffs," said ​Michael Kugelman, a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council in Washington.
"But this new legislation, which enjoyed strong bipartisan support and takes the most maximalist position possible on punishing India for its Russian oil buys, ​may be the biggest blow yet."
If Washington delayed implementing tariffs or applied them only lightly, the damage could be manageable, he said, adding the legislation nevertheless could widen the trust gap in Delhi for a trade deal and make ‌it harder ⁠for Indian negotiators to agree to last-minute concessions needed to secure a deal.
"From the perspective of the trade talks, this new legislation couldn't have come at a worse time," he said. "The two sides are not far from the finish line, but getting there will require careful diplomacy."
The bill has already become a political issue in India, with the opposition urging Modi to adopt a tougher stance. Any hike in pump prices would be risky for Modi, whose party faces elections in India's most populous state, Uttar Pradesh, in Punjab and in Modi's home state of Gujarat starting early next year. Modi's BJP runs both Uttar ​Pradesh and Gujarat.
Before Trump, India was courted by ​the United States for decades as a strategic ⁠counterweight to China, but the world's fifth-largest economy has repeatedly been left reeling over the past year by decisions taken in Washington.
After Russia's invasion of Ukraine, India sharply increased purchases of discounted Russian crude, which now account for more than 40% of India's overall oil supplies. The stepped-up purchases were partly the reason ​Trump imposed tariffs of as much as 50% on Indian goods in August 2025, among the steepest levied on any country.
In February, Trump rolled ​back those duties in exchange for ⁠what he said was India's commitment to halt Russian oil purchases and lower trade barriers.
But New Delhi only briefly reduced purchases from Russia in early 2026. They have since jumped, especially since the supply shock that followed the US and Israeli attack on Iran .
New Delhi has repeatedly resisted pressure to scale back purchases, arguing that its large population and growing economy need secure, affordable and reliable energy supplies. Indian refiners have already secured crude supplies ⁠for September and ​October that include Russian oil, sources familiar with the matter have told Reuters .
Indian analysts said the country's purchases of Russian oil were ​not financing the Ukraine war, but only helping stabilise global supplies and keeping domestic prices in check.
"Tariffs of up to 100% would punish Indian exporters and American consumers, disrupt trade and give the US president excessive power over major partners," said Ajay Srivastava, ​founder of New Delhi-based think tank Global Trade Research Initiative and a former trade ministry official.

title: Aramco halts October crude deliveries to some European refiners after pipeline attack  report
description: Drone attacks forced the shutdown of the company s East West pipeline
content:
Drone attacks forced the shutdown of the company's East-West pipeline
Oil company Saudi Aramco has told at ​least two European refining customers they will receive ‌no crude oil next month following an attack on Saudi Arabia's key pipeline to the Red Sea, Bloomberg reported ​on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.
European ​refiners typically buy Saudi crude under term contracts ⁠that guarantee monthly supplies, but Aramco has informed customers ​that next month's deliveries will not proceed, the report said.
Saudi ​Arabia earlier informed European customers that some crude cargoes would be cancelled after drone attacks forced the shutdown of its East-West pipeline, ​damaging three pumping stations and disrupting oil loadings at ​the Red Sea port of Yanbu.
Read: Oil prices fall for third day on hopes of limited Saudi supply disruptions
The disruption has prompted customers, including Poland's ‌Orlen, to seek alternative crude supplies, with traders saying the refiner bought North Sea grades to replace disrupted Saudi imports.
Reuters could not verify the report. Saudi Aramco did ​not immediately respond to ​a request ⁠for comment outside regular business hours.
Aramco is working to partially restart the pipeline within ​days and return it to full capacity ​within six ⁠weeks, Bloomberg reported, citing a person familiar with the matter.
Separately, Saudi Aramco has boosted crude exports from the Gulf through ⁠ship-to-ship ​transfers off Oman's Sohar port ​to help offset volumes lost from reduced Red Sea shipments.

title: Kelly Macdonald wants    Slow Horses    role after admitting she is obsessed with Gary Oldman

content:
Kelly Macdonald says James Hawes helped bring her into Lanterns after she admired his work
Kelly Macdonald may currently be starring in DC series Lanterns , but the actress has revealed there is another hit show she would love to join.
Speaking to Metro , Macdonald admitted she had previously given Lanterns director James Hawes a hard time for not casting her in Slow Horses , the acclaimed Apple TV spy thriller starring Gary Oldman.
Macdonald said she already wanted to work on the project when Hawes contacted her about Lanterns , explaining that she loved the director and had been vocal about her interest in Slow Horses .
"I had given him a hard time previously for not having me cast in Slow Horses because I love that show," she told. "We love it as a family. I’m obsessed with Gary Oldman as well."
Her comments arrive as Slow Horses has launched its sixth season, with Oldman returning as Jackson Lamb. Apple TV confirmed the new season premiered on September 16, with six episodes scheduled to arrive weekly through October 21.
Macdonald is currently appearing as Sheriff Kerry Kane in Lanterns , where she stars alongside Kyle Chandler and Aaron Pierre. The DC series follows Hal Jordan and John Stewart as they investigate a murder in Nebraska, while Kane becomes increasingly connected to the mystery.
Macdonald also praised Chandler, describing him as easy to work with and saying his preparation created a positive atmosphere on set. She highlighted the contrast between Chandler's Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre's John Stewart, saying the pairing created a special combination.
The actress also addressed the possibility of returning as DCI Joanne Davidson in Line of Duty . Macdonald previously played the character in the sixth series, and the BBC crime drama is now returning for a seventh series. Macdonald has remained coy about whether Davidson will appear, while Robert Carlyle has joined the returning cast.

title: IHC says political protests cannot infringe citizens    fundamental rights ahead of PTI march
description: Says besieging Islamabad  and suspending citizens    rights cannot be claimed as protest rights
content:
Says besieging Islamabad, and suspending citizens’ rights cannot be claimed as protest rights
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has ruled that any activity resulting in a violation of citizens’ fundamental rights would constitute a breach of the Constitution, warning that public office holders responsible for such violations would be liable for consequences under the Constitution and the law.
The ruling came as the PTI announced the September 27 Islamabad march to press for the release of Imran Khan. The party had been preparing a central convoy from K-P, with caravans from other parts of the country expected to join before proceeding towards the federal capital.
A larger bench comprising IHC Chief Justice Sardar Sarfaraz Dogar and Justices Azam Khan and Muhammad Asif made the observations in a 37-page detailed judgment on a petition filed by local trader Waqas Ahmed against the announced PTI long march towards Islamabad on Sept 27.
Read : IHC bars harassment, arrest of PTI leaders ahead of September 27 long march
The bench had announced its short order on Sept 14 after hearing arguments from Attorney General for Pakistan Mansoor Awan, Additional Attorney General Amir Rehman, the advocate generals of the four provinces and Islamabad, and counsel for the petitioner, Barrister Akhter Cheena.
The petitioner sought protection of citizens’ fundamental rights, including freedom of movement, dignity, business and property, arguing that political assembly was subject to reasonable restrictions.
The petitioner’s counsel had contended that the relief sought was preventive and neutral, and aimed at preserving constitutional rights rather than suppressing any political activity.
The court consequently rejected objections to the maintainability of the petition based on the 2024 law, observing that none of the provisions of the law prevented the petition from being brought before the high court.
“To the contrary, the provisions of the aforesaid Act have not been adhered to by the Chief Minister, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and others who have declared their intention to march towards and lay siege to the ICT for purposes which are extraneous to the Constitution and the law,” the judgment said.
“Therefore, instant petition is held to be maintainable, even otherwise too,” it concluded.
The court made it clear that the right to protest was constitutionally protected but remained subject to the Constitution, law and reasonable restrictions.
“The controversy before us requires an unusual degree of constitutional balance,” the judgment said, noting that on one side stood the right of citizens and political parties to assemble peacefully, express political dissent and participate in democratic activity.
On the other side, it said, were the equally constitutional rights of citizens to life, liberty, dignity, free movement, lawful trade and business, property, and access to hospitals, educational institutions, courts and workplaces.
“Therefore, the question is not whether a political party is entitled to protest. It plainly is, subject always to the Constitution and law,” the court observed.
Also Read: 'Shut Karachi for a week, they will hold your feet': CM Afridi urges people to join September 27 protest
The bench said political parties had a constitutional right to peaceful assembly and political dissent, while citizens also enjoyed constitutional rights to life, liberty, dignity, freedom of movement and business.
It said a constitutional balance was therefore necessary between the right to political protest and the fundamental rights of citizens.
The question before the court, it added, was also the extent to which a high court could intervene in a matter concerning a political protest that had yet to take place.
The court observed that continuity of the normal functioning of constitutional institutions in Islamabad was of fundamental importance. Citizens, it said, had the right to access hospitals, educational institutions and courts.
The judgment noted that Article 15 of the Constitution guaranteed citizens the right to move freely throughout Pakistan, while Article 16 provided the right to assemble peacefully and without arms.
Restrictions on assembly could only be imposed under law and to the extent reasonably necessary in the public interest, it said.
Article 17, the court added, gave citizens the right to form associations and unions, while restrictions on freedom of assembly could be imposed under law in the interest of public order.
The bench rejected the contention that the petition was based on a merely speculative apprehension of disruption.
“The material placed before us is substantially different from an entirely speculative apprehension,” it held.
The Islamabad advocate general had placed footage of PTI’s 2022 and 2024 protests before the court, arguing that the demonstrations could not be described as peaceful.
The court considered the material while determining whether the apprehension of disruption from the Sept 27 march was merely speculative.
The bench also referred to assurances given by the PTI regarding its march of May 25, 2022, and their alleged violations.
Read More : Naqvi warns of legal action against violators of IHC protest ruling
It regretted that assurances and court directions had repeatedly been disregarded, saying the party’s founding chairman himself had violated an assurance given before the Supreme Court.
The history of previous protests, the court observed, was relevant to determining whether the apprehension before it was speculative.
“The history has demonstrated the obvious conduct of the political party in disregarding not only the Court orders but also the assurances given by its leadership to remain peaceful during the assembly/sit-ins,” the judgment said.
The court noted that the high court had also issued a judgment concerning the November 2024 protest, but it was not implemented.
“The case before this court is not based on speculation,” it said, adding that there was a history of the political party disregarding judicial orders and assurances.
Referring to the Supreme Court’s judgment in the Faizabad Dharna case, the attorney general argued that it was the state’s duty to ensure that political protest did not degenerate into an obstruction of civic life.
He argued that the state must act cohesively to ensure protection of the constitutional rights of citizens within Islamabad.
The high court, while quoting the Supreme Court judgment, noted that prolonged blocking of roads prevented citizens from exercising their constitutional right to freedom of movement.
Preventing sick people from reaching hospitals could infringe their right to life, it said, while road blockades also affected students, litigants, businesses and daily-wage workers and could result in damage to property.
Read : Sept 27 protest fuels opposition unity drive
The court further held that public roads could not be converted indefinitely into sites for political protests.
“The constitutional right of assembly cannot be interpreted as a right of perpetual occupation of infrastructure which belongs equally to all citizens,” the judgment said.
The bench said the exercise of one constitutional right could not become a licence to infringe another citizen’s rights.
“Constitutional guarantees are thus to be construed harmoniously, so as to preserve the delicate equilibrium between individual liberty and the equal entitlement of others to the protection of their own fundamental rights,” it said.
March using state resources ‘unconstitutional’
The court held that government resources of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa had been used for political purposes during a previous march.
As a result of such marches, it said, it became impossible to ensure protection of the fundamental rights of Islamabad’s citizens.
The bench ruled that any aggression by a provincial unit against the federation, in the form of a march, rally, or procession, was unconstitutional and unlawful.
It further held that government funds, vehicles, machinery or officials could not be used for any political march towards Islamabad.
While peaceful protest was a constitutional right, an armed march or one conducted using government resources did not enjoy constitutional protection, the court said.
The court also issued detailed instructions to the chief secretaries and police chiefs of the provinces, as well as the federal interior secretary, chief commissioner and inspector general of police of Islamabad.
Officials were directed not to comply with any order compelling them to aid or facilitate a march, rally or procession leading towards Islamabad.
The court further ordered that no official should permit anyone to participate in a march towards Islamabad with the intention of obstructing or hindering free movement, trade, business, or commerce, or adversely affecting access to educational institutions, medical facilities, or the peaceful and lawful use of property.
‘Besieging capital not a constitutional right’
The court said disrupting citizens’ lives, businesses, education and freedom of movement to exert political pressure on Islamabad did not fall within the scope of the right to protest.
The right to hold a long march was subject to law, it said, adding that besieging the federal capital or suspending citizens’ rights was not a constitutional right.
The bench also set out the constitutional consequences for anyone whose activities resulted in violations of citizens’ fundamental rights.
“Any person, whether legal or natural, who undertakes any activity which results in violation of fundamental rights of the citizens within the ICT, shall be deemed to have violated the Constitution and shall be liable for the consequences stipulated under the law,” the judgment stated.
In one of its strongest observations, the court said the consequences would also extend to public office holders if their actions resulted in violations of citizens’ fundamental rights.
Also Read : PTI finalises strategy for Sept 27 march
“Any public office holder, who undertakes any activity which results in violation of fundamental rights of the citizens within the ICT, shall be deemed to have violated the Constitution and his/her oath of office under the Constitution and shall be liable for the consequences stipulated under the Constitution and the law.”
The bench concluded that a long march remained subject to constitutional and legal restrictions, and that occupation of public infrastructure or suspension of citizens’ fundamental rights could not itself be claimed as a constitutional right.
The court disposed of the petition with directions.
The PTI last month announced a September 27 march in Islamabad to demand the release of Imran Khan, with caravans from across the country expected to converge on the federal capital. The party also planned protests, shutdowns and demonstrations along major highways in cities, including Lahore, Karachi, Hyderabad and Quetta.
Under a preliminary strategy announced in August, the party planned to bring workers from across the country to K-P at least five days before the march. The main convoy was expected to remain at the Punjab-Khyber Pakhtunkhwa border for two to three days before moving towards Islamabad once other caravans had assembled.
The PTI had also planned protests and shutdowns in several major cities, including Lahore, Karachi, Hyderabad and Quetta, as well as demonstrations along important national highways.
The PTI’s August plan also included a funding and mobilisation structure for the protest. A committee headed by party Secretary-General Salman Akram Raja was tasked with overseeing finances, while lawmakers were directed to mobilise supporters in their constituencies.
The party had estimated that the first day of the march would cost around Rs450 million, with subsequent days expected to cost approximately Rs14.5 million each. It had also sought financial contributions from lawmakers and party figures to fund the campaign.

title: Fact check  Ed Sheeran has not performed solo after opening acts cancelled due to Macklemore incident
description: Viral clip shows Ed Sheeran s 2022 Wembley performance and predates claims about a recent Macklemore incident
content:
Viral clip shows Ed Sheeran's 2022 Wembley performance
Several users and journalists have been sharing a video across social media platforms since September 16, 2026, claiming it shows Ed Sheeran performing after his opening acts pulled out of a tour following the Macklemore controversy. However, the video is old from December 2022.
American rapper Macklemore announced on September 14, 2026, that he had been dropped from Ed Sheeran’s Loop tour after making pro-Palestinian statements on stage.
On September 15, 2026, Ed released an official statement on his Instagram, defending his decision to drop Macklemore from the tour, saying that he was axed following threats from venue owners, including Robert Kraft.
The backlash to his statement was severe, with all the musical artists set to perform with him dropping out from the tour in support of Macklemore.
Many renowned celebrities and singers also showed support for Macklemore. Among them were American singer-songwriter Finneas, Irish singer Aaron Rowe, Irish band Beoga, and Danish pop band Lukas Graham, who announced they would be pulling out of the tour.
On September 16, the producer of Jay Weber Show on News Talk 1130, Gregory Jon, shared a video on X, claiming it shows Ed Sheeran performing after his opening acts cancelled the tour, with the following caption: “So the opening acts cancelled and his own band quit. Ed Sheeran says hold my beer.”
A social media user shared the same clip with the following caption: “Fuck you nig****, he doesn’t need a band!”
Sébastien Mélières, editorial director at news magazine Vistazo, also shared the same video with the following caption: “Ed Sheeran was left without a band and without opening acts at the last minute. Instead of cancelling, he went out alone with the guitar and absolutely smashed it in the stadium. For two hours he was once again the artist of his beginnings.”
Another social media user shared the same video with a similar caption, accumulating 1.1m views.
American journalist Joel M. Petlin posted the same clip with the following caption: “For all the Ed Sheeran haters out there who think he can’t perform on a stadium stage without a few anti-Israel warm up acts and a back up band, I have some really bad news for you.”
Another X account posted the same clip with a similar caption, gaining 1m views.
Another social media user shared the same video with the following caption: “WOW!!! Ed Sheeran had his own band cancel on him and he came out and crushed it in front of thousands of Fans. Absolutely incredible.”
Several other users also shared the clip across Facebook , Instagram , and X, as can be seen here , here , here , and here ; collectively accumulating 1.18m views.
A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to its high virality and keen public interest in the Sheeran-Macklemore controversy.
A keyword search was conducted to verify whether any credible international media outlets had recently reported that Sheeran performed an entire concert alone after his band and opening acts withdrew but no such reports or visuals confirming the recent solo performance were found.
A reverse image search was subsequently conducted to trace the origin of the viral video clip and yielded an earlier video shared on YouTube by a user who appears to be a Sheeran fan on December 7, 2022, with the caption: “Ed Sheeran performing Shivers at Wembley Stadium. Loop pedal close up! Note: this video was extracted from the ‘Full Circle’ documentary about the Mathematics Tour, so unfortunately it’s not a full performance. Not the perfect audio as well, but it was the best I could record.”
The visuals were the same as those in the viral video.
A similar video from another angle, containing the same concert visuals, was also shared by a YouTube fan page dated July 4, 2022, with the following caption: “Ed Sheeran Mathematics Tour (+–=÷x Tour) - Shivers, 1 July 2022 - Wembley Stadium, London.”
The official Wembley Stadium website further confirms that Sheeran performed at Wembley Stadium for five nights in June and July 2022 as part of his + - = ÷ x Tour, also known as the Mathematics Tour. The venue listed June 24, June 25, June 29, June 30 and July 1, 2022, as Sheeran’s concert dates and stated that the shows featured his staging in the round, with the artist performing surrounded by the audience.
The information listed on the official Wembley Stadium website predates the recent viral claim and dates back to Sheeran’s 2022 Mathematics Tour, rather than his ongoing Loop Tour in 2026.
Furthermore, according to the Los Angeles Times report on September 16, 2026, several supporting acts had recently withdrawn from Sheeran’s Loop Tour following the removal of Macklemore from the lineup. However, the report stated that Sheeran’s next scheduled performance was still set to take place at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia on Saturday, September 19, 2026, and that the supporting acts for the concert had not yet been finalised.
The claim that a viral clip shows Ed Sheeran performing after his opening acts cancelled is false.
The viral clip is of Ed Sheeran’s 2022 Mathematics Tour performance at Wembley Stadium and predates the recent claims. Sheeran has not delivered any performance, solo or in a group, since the Macklemore incident.

title: New wild cat species identified in Bolivia for the over 100 years goes viral
description: The small feline was found in Bolivia   s Yungas region  a misty cloud forest located between the Andes and the Amazon
content:
The small feline was found in Bolivia’s Yungas region, a misty cloud forest located between the Andes and the Amazon
A previously unknown species of wild cat has been formally identified in Bolivia, marking the first discovery of a new living cat species in more than a century.
The small feline was found in Bolivia’s Yungas region, a misty cloud forest located between the Andes and the Amazon. Known as Tilcayo by local communities, the species has been given the scientific name Leopardus tilcayo. It measures around 46cm in length, making it smaller than the average domestic cat.
Researchers used genetic analysis to establish that Tilcayo is a distinct species within the tiger cat family. DNA from 38 cats across several South American countries showed that tiger cats previously grouped together actually comprise five genetically distinct species. Researchers estimate that Tilcayo separated from the other lineages around 1.4 million years ago.
Little is currently known about the animal’s behaviour, although researchers believe it is primarily active at night and likely feeds on small rodents. The study was based on two live examples, including one now living at a wildlife sanctuary in Bolivia, as well as photographs captured by camera traps.
The discovery also highlights concerns about the species’ habitat. The Yungas ecosystem faces threats including deforestation, agricultural expansion, human-caused fires and mining. Tiger cats are currently classified as vulnerable, and the International Union for Conservation of Nature is expected to assess the five lineages separately.
Researchers say the discovery demonstrates that new species can still be found even among well-studied groups such as cats. Eduardo Eizirik, an evolutionary biologist and senior author of the study, warned that some undiscovered species could disappear before scientists have the opportunity to identify them.

India's $100 billion food industry faces scrutiny in a crackdown involving factory visits and product testing
India's food regulator said on Friday it had found a Nestle baby food sample to be substandard and was pursuing legal action against the Swiss company in one of its biggest growth markets.
Nestle said its products are "fully compliant with all the applicable regulations" and that it will continue to work closely with the regulator, without specifically commenting on the finding of a substandard sample.
The scrutiny is the latest in a crackdown on India's $100 billion food industry, which has included surprise factory visits and product testing.
Officials found a sample of Nestle "follow-up formula", which is a milk product for infants, was "sub-standard with respect to biotin", the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said.
The regulator specifies a standardised reference range for biotin, more commonly known as vitamin B7, in baby food.
"A re-analysis" of the sample found it was "non-conforming" with respect to prescribed biotin requirements under Indian laws, the regulator said in a social media post.
The FSSAI did not say whether it would order a recall of the product.
Nestle, whose shares in India fell almost 3% following news of the action, counts India as a key growth market.
Milk and nutrition products, including infant formulas and baby foods, were Nestle India's biggest revenue category in the year ending March 2026, generating a third of its product sales worth $2.4 billion.
The FSSAI said it has also filed cases over two other Nestle baby food products, NAN Excella Pro Stage 1 and Lactogen Pro 1, for making misleading claims in breach of regulations.
"Three separate adjudication cases have been filed against Nestle," the FSSAI said.
Read More: Laws on paper, peasants in peril
In response to the notice, Nestle India said it has again submitted its detailed response to the authorities regarding statements appearing on the label, "which are factual in nature, and supported by scientific literature."
The labels "were approved by the expert committee of FSSAI," it added.
Nestle also fell foul of India's food regulator in 2015, when authorities banned its popular Maggi noodles over alleged excess lead levels and labelling lapses, triggering a massive recall.
Maggi later returned to shelves after fresh tests.
Debate over food safety in India has intensified since Reuters reported last month that the government opted for a weaker labelling regime after lobbying by Coca-Cola and groups backing Nestle and PepsiCo, which argued that warning labels were ineffective.
Many companies, however, have implemented such measures voluntarily in European markets.

title: Yemen conflict displaces 112 000 people inside country  thousands flee to Djibouti  says UN
description: Djibouti prepares for up to 10 000 refugees  putting acute pressure on health and education services
content:
Djibouti prepares for up to 10,000 refugees, putting acute pressure on health and education services
At least 112,000 people have been displaced inside Yemen within the last two weeks as fighting continues along the country's west coast amid a renewed conflict, while nearly 3,000 have fled by sea to Djibouti, the United Nations migration agency said on Friday.
Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have stepped up attacks on Saudi cities and energy infrastructure while advancing along Yemen's Red Sea coast towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping route.
Reporting from the ground in Djibouti. 🎥 More than 2,000 people fleeing conflict in Yemen have arrived in Obock in recent days. IOM teams are providing water, hot meals and transport for the most vulnerable, but more support is urgently needed. pic.twitter.com/fG2xBNvcCi
Responding to the Houthi offensive, the Saudi and Yemeni air forces have bombarded Houthi targets.
Nearly 3,000 people have crossed the Gulf of Aden to Djibouti in the Horn of Africa in less than a week as escalating violence has forced more families to flee, Sandrine Desamours, the representative for the UN's refugee agency, UNHCR, told reporters in Geneva via video link from Djibouti.
Women use donkeys to transport water jerrycans to the al-Bireen camp for displaced people who fled fighting between the Houthis and forces of Yemen's internationally recognized government in Taiz province, Yemen, September 17, 2026. REUTERS
The government of Djibouti is preparing for the arrival of up to 10,000 refugees, which will add acute pressure on the country's healthcare and education services, she said.
The UN International Organisation for Migration said people are fleeing on overcrowded boats and arriving with very limited food and water.
Read More: How Yemen's Houthis went from a small mountain militia to a big regional threat
Most fleeing are Yemeni families seeking refuge in Djibouti, but IOM is also beginning to see a small number of migrants, mainly from Ethiopia, heading in the same direction.
Additionally, authorities in Somaliland and Puntland have also reported increased arrivals from Yemen, including Yemeni refugees and Somali refugee returnees, though numbers remain in the hundreds for now, UNHCR said.
UN agencies described the latest fighting as a crisis on top of multiple crises, as the country's health services and economy have been shattered amid a long civil war between forces of the internationally recognised, Saudi-backed administration and the Houthis, creating one of the world's biggest humanitarian crises.
The Houthi advance along Yemen's Red Sea coast is bolstering Tehran's hand in its conflict with the US, as the group tightens its control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a strategic chokepoint for global oil and commodities shipping, more than six months after US and Israeli attacks on Iran.

title: Aidaah Sheikh calls out    cyber bully casters    over body shaming
description: Influencer urges public figures to block and report online trolls  stating that hate says more about the harasser
content:
Influencer urges public figures to block and report online trolls, stating that hate says more about the harasser
Influencer and lifestyle creator Aidaah Sheikh took to Instagram to call out 'haters' on social media, calling them “cyber-bully casters.”
Sheikh posted a video on her Instagram titled “To whom it may concern,” in which she shared her thoughts on people who body-shame women on social media, emphasising that they are inflicted with self-hatred.
“These are not podcasters, they are cyber-bully casters,” she said. “We live in a society where a person might or might not have etiquette, an education, money or credibility, but they always have an opinion,” she added.
Sheikh acknowledged that people were entitled to their views but argued that freedom of expression had its limits when comments became harmful. “Freedom of opinion and expression is good, but there has to be a boundary, as long as it is not harming anybody.”
Using body-shaming as an example, she argued that comments targeting someone’s appearance could not simply be dismissed as an opinion.
“If you say your opinion through body-shaming and harassment, that cannot be normalised. An opinion is to say you do not like to eat burgers, but to say someone else can’t eat it because they are fat is not an opinion. That is body-shaming.”
Sheikh then pointed to what she described as a wider pattern of men feeling entitled to comment on women’s appearances.“I read on the internet that all men have this audacity, and there are live examples,” she said.
She linked her argument to a recent example involving businessman Avinash Singh Rathore, who said Bollywood actress Katrina Kaif “is finished” because she had gained some weight after pregnancy.
“A 20,000-earning man says to a 4,000-crore company owner that ‘she is finished’ all because she has gained a little weight. She has stayed fit all her life,” Sheikh said.
She went on to question the credibility of people who use microphones and social media platforms to make such remarks.
“I think we should show these kinds of people a mirror, day and night, and show them their bank account details so they stare at both those things. Every unemployed man with a mic is not a podcaster,” the influencer said.
For Sheikh, the issue went beyond online criticism, with the negativity directed at others reflecting the insecurities of those making the comments.
“At the end of the day, everyone should show some human decency. If you are really hating on someone, that means you hate yourself so much that you are putting it on others. As a secure human being, when I see hate towards others, I always think about the one hating, not the one being hated on,” she said.
She summed up her point with a simple message: “Happy people aren’t hating, and hating people aren’t happy.”
“In short, you are exposing yourself. I want to ask all public figures, whether you have a large following or a little one. I urge all of you to block such people and make sure you report them,” she concluded.

Stresses intelligence agencies have evidence of terrorist support networks
Balochistan Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langov on Friday said some government officials, politicians and not-for-profit organisations were financing and supporting terrorists in the province.
The minister expressed these views on the security situation of Balochistan while addressing a meeting of the Pakistan Poverty Alleviation Fund (PPAF) held at the Serena Hotel in Quetta.
“Certain government officials, political figures and non-governmental organisations (NGO) are financially supporting and backing outlawed terrorist organisations in Balochistan,” the minister said during the meeting.
Langov, however, did not name any government official, politician or NGO involved.
He further revealed that intelligence agencies had gathered evidence of financial ties between the banned outfits and the individuals, as well as the organisations assisting them.
Read: Security forces kill seven terrorists in two Balochistan operations: state media
The home minister said that the groups were not fighting for the rights of the people of Balochistan but were pursuing a foreign-sponsored agenda aimed at creating unrest in the province and the country.
According to Langov, the terrorist organisations were also relying on organised criminal activities to finance their operations.
He said they were extorting traders, farmers and commercial transporters, besides carrying out highway robberies and looting passengers travelling on major routes.
The minister cited the recent abduction of two members of the Hazara community as an example of what he described as terror financing through ransom. He said the two hostages were released after a ransom payment of Rs7 million.
He added that security agencies had launched intelligence-based operations to trace the financial networks and identify government officials and other entities suspected of facilitating these banned terrorist organisations.

The singer has previously spoken publicly in support of Palestine and recently criticised the White House after her song Midnight Sun was used in a social media video showing immigration arrests. Her comments about Macklemore come as several musicians have publicly supported him following his departure from Sheeran’s tour.

title: Naqvi warns of legal action against violators of IHC protest ruling
description: Salman Akram Raja  says PTI is   marching  towards September 27th  dismisses talk of differences with ally TTAP
content:
Salman Akram Raja says PTI is 'marching' towards September 27th, dismisses talk of differences with ally TTAP
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Friday warned that anyone who violated the Islamabad High Court’s (IHC) detailed judgment and attempted to create unrest in the federal capital or any province would face legal action, including contempt of court proceedings.
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) had announced that it would march to Islamabad on September 27 to press for the release of founder Imran Khan. The party had been preparing a central convoy from Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), with caravans from other parts of the country expected to join before proceeding towards the federal capital.
Speaking at a press conference at Jinnah Convention Centre in Islamabad, Naqvi said a detailed law-and-order meeting had been held to discuss the call for protests in the coming days. The meeting also reviewed the internal security situation, with officers from other provinces and law enforcement agencies in attendance.
Naqvi said the IHC’s detailed judgment had left no room for any attempt to create unrest in the federal capital or any province.
قانون نافذ کرنے والے اداروں کو وضاحت کی ہے کہ اگر کوئی نکلنے کی کوشش کرے تو ہرممکن طریقے سے روکیں گے، وفاقی وزیرداخلہ مزید پڑھیں : https://t.co/BGlyRH06HJ #ExpressNews #MohsinNaqvi #Islamabad #Protest pic.twitter.com/Dj4xEcQy3Q
He said all law enforcement agencies had been given clear instructions that anyone attempting to come out in violation of the court’s judgment would first face legal action in the form of contempt of court proceedings. “Secondly, we will stop them through any means possible,” he said.
The interior minister also referred to losses suffered during previous unrest and said weapons had been used against law enforcement personnel. He noted that discussions were taking place on social media about specific tribes and people belonging to those tribes joining the protests.
Read: IHC bars harassment, arrest of PTI leaders ahead of September 27 long march
“This time, we are informing our youth of very clear rules of engagement, and there is no scenario that if you fire on them, they will sit quietly,” he said.
He urged political leadership to hold protests within their respective areas and cities but warned against bringing demonstrators to the federal capital with plans to shut it down or entering another province to carry out attacks.
“I want to request all leadership that they can protest, protest in your area, in your city, but coming like this to the federal capital with plans to shut it down or going to a province and attacking it like this; this can be in no way permissible to you,” he said.
Naqvi also referred to the terrorist attack in Kohat, saying details of the incident had only recently been received. He said the country was fighting terrorism daily in K-P, and 90% of the government’s attention should be focused on countering terrorism rather than efforts to mobilise people, funds or transport for protests.
“So, especially after incidents like these, it does not suit you to, on one side, carry the funeral processions for the martyrs and on the other side, prepare for protests. It would be better if the chief minister and his cabinet work as hard in fighting these terrorists as they are in trying to organise the Long March. If they do so, then incidents of terrorism would decrease,” he added.
Naqvi underlined that it was the responsibility of the office holder to protect the life and property of citizens and to stop protests in Islamabad. "This is the job of the interior minister, and not of Mohsin Naqvi".
He added that there was a difference between political campaigns and political activity, and armed mobs who resorted to violence and who came “fully equipped”. "This does not reflect a political mindset and is unbecoming of any political party".
The interior minister emphasised that the court’s judgement had made it clear that if there was any loss of life during the protests, then the organisers of the protests would be "responsible".
“There are many sensible leaders in the opposition, and I expect them to understand that there is no benefit in fighting and that these protests will harm the country, the economy and their own province. I hope that sense will prevail and that they will review their decision,” he remarked.
Read More : Afridi vows to lead long march to Islamabad
Naqvi stated that ultimately, political matters were resolved at the negotiating table, as the prime minister had also said in Parliament, noting that if people thought that armed mobs resorting to violence could resolve things, then "we are ready to deal with that, and we have completed our preparations today."
He added that "our law enforcement agencies, both federal and provincial, are ready, and we will not allow any unrest and disorder to take place in Islamabad like in the past".
Responding to a question on possible negotiations, Naqvi said that the judgement of the Court had come and any sensible Pakistani and patriot should and would think about participating in protests in such turbulent and sensitive times. “Even within the PTI, if a survey is held, 80 to 90 per cent of the party would not know the rationale for the protest towards Islamabad”.
“I am personally against placing containers, but when law enforcement agencies ask for this, then you have to use this option. To secure Islamabad, we would need to blockade, but we will try to minimise the difficulty of the common people,” he remarked.
The interior minister further stated that the "current situation in K-P was before us", adding that it was the responsibility of the provincial government to improve the law and order situation, provide resources and focus on the province.
While responding to another question on the right to peaceful protests, Naqvi responded by saying that "you can do peaceful protests in your province and I am not against any protest, as long as it is peaceful".
Meanwhile, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said that PTI was "marching" towards September 27th and the "freedom" of the country, adding that "victory and success will be ours".
While responding to a reporter's question on possible reservations of ally Tehreek Tahaffuz-e-Ayin Pakistan about the march, Raja dismissed any talk of differences, adding that a detailed plan of action would be shared in this regard in the next few days.
”انشاءاللہ 27 ستمبر کی جانب ہم گامزن ہیں اور فتح اور کامرانی انشاءاللہ ہماری ہوگی “- @salmanAraja #LongMarchOnSeptember27th pic.twitter.com/KJ1cCDJ2v0
The press conference came after the Islamabad High Court this past week barred political parties , political leaders, provincial governments and public office holders from occupying public roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas, buildings or other public places within or leading to the federal capital.
Also Read : PTI Sept 27 protest: IHC rules no political party, public office holder can block roads in Islamabad
The court declared that no one had a lawful right to obstruct the free movement of citizens or interfere with their access to trade, business, education and medical facilities.
Islamabad High Court Detailed Judgment on PTI Long March: Constitutional Limits & Restrictions Explained #IslamabadHighCourt #PTI #LongMarch #Fiaz Mehmood #PakistanLaw #Article16 #IslamabadNews pic.twitter.com/mHKtOnlClV
A three-member IHC bench led by Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar issued the directives while disposing of a petition filed by citizen Waqas Ahmed. The petitioner sought directions to stop the PTI from organising a protest march in Islamabad on September 27. The court disposed of the petition, stating that detailed reasons would be recorded later, subject to any amplification or elucidation deemed appropriate.
In its written order, the court directed all provincial governments, including chief ministers, to ensure that government resources, public funds, officials, vehicles, machinery and other equipment were not used directly or indirectly to facilitate any march, procession or rally heading towards Islamabad.
Govt resources barred from PTI’s Sept 27 Islamabad march
K-P Chief Secretary Shahab Ali Shah on Friday directed heads of all government departments and institutions to ensure that official resources were not used to facilitate the PTI's planned long march towards Islamabad on September 27.
The chief secretary issued the directives in light of the IHC’s September 14 order, instructing all government officers and employees not to use public funds, official vehicles, machinery, equipment or other state resources for any march, procession or rally heading towards the federal capital.
According to an official notification, no government employee should comply with any direction requiring him or her to facilitate or assist a march, procession or rally travelling to Islamabad. Any official who was pressured or compelled to provide such assistance had been directed to immediately inform the chief secretary or the inspector general of police.
The notification stated that public funds, government vehicles, machinery and other equipment would not be used to assist or facilitate participants of any march, procession or rally. It also made clear that no government employee would be forced, persuaded or encouraged to participate in such an activity.
The chief secretary further directed that permission would not be granted for participation in any march, rally or procession whose purpose or outcome was to obstruct the peaceful and lawful use of public movement, trade, business, educational institutions, medical facilities or property in Islamabad.
A helpline had also been established at 091-9210068 for government employees facing pressure or coercion to provide official support to the march.
The chief secretary directed all administrative secretaries, heads of departments, commissioners, deputy commissioners and other senior officials to ensure strict compliance with the court’s directions and to communicate the instructions to subordinate staff. The notification warned that departmental action would be taken against any government employee found violating the directives.
