title: England can build on World Cup  spirit   says Tuchel
description: England boss eyes Euro 2028 glory with Spain clash ahead
content:
England boss eyes Euro 2028 glory with Spain clash ahead
Thomas Tuchel said England will build on the "fantastic spirit" of their World Cup campaign as he targets glory on home soil at Euro 2028.
The England boss was speaking at Wembley after naming a 27-man group for a four-game Nations League camp, starting with a clash against world champions Spain on September 26.
It comes just nine weeks after the end of the World Cup, where England conceded two late goals in a painful semi-final defeat by Argentina.
Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold and Chelsea forward Cole Palmer were the headline picks after both were controversially overlooked for the World Cup.
Tuchel also included Liverpool's teenage winger Rio Ngumoha, uncapped Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite in his first squad since the tournament in North America.
A number of players who were in the World Cup squad including John Stones, Djed Spence, Dan Burn, Jordan Henderson and Dean Henderson missed out through injury.
Former Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Tuchel said he did not see the Nations League as a new start, instead focusing on continuity.
"I feel that it's not a new beginning that we are starting now, so we build on a solid and very valuable foundation, and the target is to win the home Euros," he told reporters on Friday.
Euro 2028 will be co-hosted by England, Scotland, Wales, and Ireland.
The German said his side's ultimate failure at the World Cup had left him unfulfilled but stuck by his squad picks.
"I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic," he said.
"I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got."
Tuchel said Palmer had impressed for Chelsea early in the season.
"He has his numbers back, he has assists back, he has decisive goals back, so that's why he's in the squad and I think he has a point to prove," he said.
"The same goes for Trent. He was never off the list, he was never in a non-selectable class, and he has this chance to show, to be the best version of himself."
Tuchel said it was his "duty" to play Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo after he failed to feature for a single minute at the World Cup.
The England boss welcomed the challenge of taking on Spain at Wembley.
"We feel the gap is closing and we feel that we are close and we want a proof of point," he said.
"The stadium is sold out, it will be very exciting, the motivation cannot be higher to play against the world champions."
England also play the Czech Republic twice and Croatia once during the upcoming international window.

title: LHC extends suspension of PMD directive  blocks expulsion of Afghan medical students
description: PMDC  UHS legal counsel asked the court for extra time to submit their written response
content:
PMDC, UHS legal counsel asked the court for extra time to submit their written response
The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Friday extended the suspension of a Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) directive requiring Afghan medical students to return to Afghanistan, after lawyers representing the council and a medical university sought additional time to file their replies before the court.
In earlier proceedings, the LHC Justice Khalid Ishaq had sought replies from the concerned respondents, including the PMDC, the health ministry and the vice chancellors of the medical universities and colleges.
However, during the current proceedings, the legal counsel representing PMDC and the University of Health Sciences (UHS) approached Justice Ishaq for an extension of time to submit their respective written response.
The judge allowed their requests and adjourned the hearing on the case.
Read: LHC halts expulsion of Afghan medical students
During the hearing, Justice Ishaq also heard a plea filed by five Afghan medical graduates yesterday seeking PMDC registration to pursue their house jobs.
The petitioners said they completed a five-year MBBS programme during 2021-26 under the Higher Education Commission (HEC)-administered Allama Iqbal Scholarship, but the PMDC had “left their registration applications undecided for months”.
The petitioners told the court that without PMDC registration, they cannot enrol in the mandatory year-long house job required to practice medicine.
They said the lack of response stalled their careers despite having fulfilled their academic requirements. Building on their case, they said PMDC’s 2025 regulations granted graduating students a right to a house job placement at their affiliated teaching hospital, and that the council’s governing 2022 Act did not empower it to order deportations.
Justice Ishaq clubbed the plea with those filed on September 10.
He asked the counsel for the petitioners to justify “the right” of the applicants to seek a year-long house job in cognisance of Pakistan’s current foreign policy regarding Afghans living in the country.
“Why do the graduates wish to continue their stay in Pakistan despite completing their MBBS programme?” Justice Ishaq asked the applicant’s counsel. The counsel responded that the graduates had a legitimate expectation of a house job after the completion of their degree programme.
Read more: Afghan medical students in limbo
Justice Ishaq directed the counsel to convince the court on the maintainability of the plea in the backdrop of Pakistan’s current foreign policy.
A large number of Afghan medical students were present at the court for the hearing.
It is worth mentioning that the PMDC had issued a notification on September 1, passing directions to the Afghan medical students enrolled in institutions to return to Afghanistan. The notification also barred medical and dental colleges from granting admission or placement to Afghan students for the current academic session.
In response to the directive, a number of petitions were filed by the Afghan students enrolled at different institutions in Lahore, including King Edward Medical University, Shaikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Al Nahyan Medical and Dental College and the Services Institute of Medical Sciences.

Fashion influencer and Instagrammer Zahra Malik has kicked off her wedding festivities, sharing glimpses of her intimate celebrations with followers on social media.
Malik took to Instagram Stories to share pictures with friends, while professional photographers also posted photographs from the celebrations featuring the bride-to-be alongside her husband-to-be, Hashim.
In a recent photography post shared by photographers Anas Shaheen and Basharat Ali Ayan, the couple posed together at an intimate gathering surrounded by close friends.
For the occasion, Malik opted for a pastel-yellow lehenga choli paired with a matching dupatta. She completed the look with flowers in her hair and on her hands, along with a traditional teeka .
Hashim, meanwhile, kept his look understated in a simple black kurta paired with a traditional beige shawl.
The post drew congratulatory messages from several friends and public figures, including fashion blogger Zainab Reza and model Sadaf Kanwal.
Malik further confirmed the wedding celebrations by resharing friends’ posts to her Instagram Stories.
In one post, friends congratulated the influencer with the words, “So it begins,” hinting that more festivities were on the way.
Other content creator friends also shared photo dumps from the evening, offering further glimpses of the celebrations.
Known for her fashion-forward presence on Instagram, Malik regularly shares outfit inspiration, lifestyle content, makeup and skincare recommendations, as well as glimpses from her travels.
With the intimate mehndi marking the beginning of the celebrations, followers can expect more glimpses of Malik and Hashim’s wedding festivities in the days ahead.

title: US Embassy completes STEAM programme for 100  Pakistani innovators
description: Initiative provided participants with hands on experience in digital modelling  coding and 3D printing
content:
Initiative provided participants with hands-on experience in digital modelling, coding and 3D printing
The US Embassy in Pakistan has completed its “STEAM Builder” programme, training more than 100 participants in 3D printing, coding and digital modelling, according to a statement issued by the embassy on Friday.
The programme, delivered in collaboration with Pakistani technology firm AzCorps, brought together participants and trainers from six Lincoln Corners across Pakistan for a closing ceremony at Lincoln Corner Islamabad.
According to the statement, the initiative provided participants with hands-on experience in digital modelling, coding and 3D printing, with the aim of equipping young Pakistanis with skills relevant to the country’s growing digital economy.
Speaking at the ceremony, Acting Minister Counselor for Public Diplomacy David Moyer said the programme demonstrated the role of Lincoln Corners as hubs for technology, creativity and opportunity.
“STEAM Builder is more than a training programme. It is a statement about Lincoln Corners serving as hubs of technology, creativity, and opportunity,” Moyer said, according to the statement.
Participants also displayed a 3D Map of US. PHOTO: US EMBASSAY PAKISTAN/FACEBOOK
The ceremony also featured the unveiling of two 3D-printed items made by programme participants — a Liberty Bell and a map of the United States. The embassy said both items would be permanently displayed at Lincoln Corner Islamabad, located at the United States Educational Foundation in Pakistan (USEFP).
The embassy said the initiative was part of its “Freedom 250” initiative.
It added that the Lincoln Corners network, which comprises 15 locations across Pakistan, would expand its STEAM-focused programming in 2027, coinciding with the 80th anniversary of US-Pakistan bilateral relations.

title: Resident Evil  Rotten Tomatoes score reaches 96  as Zach Cregger film sets new franchise mark
description: The film follows Brian  a medical courier who must survive an outbreak involving infected monsters in Raccoon City
content:
The film follows Brian, a medical courier who must survive an outbreak involving infected monsters in Raccoon City
Resident Evil has opened with a 96% critics’ score on Rotten Tomatoes, giving director Zach Cregger his highest-rated film to date and marking a new benchmark for the video game franchise.
The film also holds a 91% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes.
The critics’ rating places the new Resident Evil well above the previous entries, none of which reached 40% with critics. Resident Evil: The Final Chapter had the franchise’s previous high at 39%.
Cregger’s latest film has also surpassed his earlier directorial work. Weapons , released in 2025, earned a 93% critics’ score, while Barbarian received 92% and Miss March 5%.
Deadline reported that Resident Evil was also recording the franchise’s strongest previews, with Thursday’s opening-night figures estimated at more than $8 million and potentially above $9 million.
The film had been tracking towards a $40 million-$50 million opening weekend.
The preview figure would exceed the previous franchise record held by Resident Evil: The Final Chapter , which made $1 million from previews.
Deadline also noted that the new film’s preview performance was ahead of films including Weapons , Scream 7 , Mortal Kombat 2 and Sonic the Hedgehog 3 .
The Sony and Constantin production follows Brian, a medical courier who must survive a viral outbreak involving infected monsters in Raccoon City.
The R-rated film released on September 18 and plays in premium large formats and IMAX.

title: Ed Sheeran opener contest goes viral as Guitar Center where the prize is opening for Ed Sheeran
description: Guitar Center says only legitimate music entries will be considered for Mexico City performance
content:
Guitar Center says only legitimate music entries will be considered for Mexico City performance
Guitar Center’s competition offering musicians the chance to open for Ed Sheeran is real, despite speculation that the promotion was created in response to the turmoil surrounding his LOOP TOUR.
The competition, called "Open for Legends", gives an undiscovered musician the opportunity to perform before Sheeran at his Mexico City show on December 11, 2026. Guitar Center describes it as a programme designed to support amateur, unsigned and independent musicians. Applicants must be at least 18, hold a valid US passport, have live performance experience and submit original music or material they have the rights to use. Audition videos cannot exceed five minutes, while bands can have up to five members.
The promotion attracted renewed attention after Macklemore was removed from Sheeran’s remaining US tour dates following comments supporting Palestinians during his September performances at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. Sheeran said the decision came from promoters and venues rather than himself. Four other support acts, including Finneas, Lukas Graham, Aaron Rowe and Beoga, subsequently withdrew from the tour.
That timing led online users to treat the Guitar Center contest as a potential search for replacement support. However, recent reports say the competition had been developed before the Macklemore controversy, meaning its existence was not originally connected to the departures.
The public audition page then became a source of further controversy after users submitted political messages, memes and other material unrelated to musical auditions. Guitar Center confirmed that some submissions were not legitimate applications and said they would not be considered. The company said the programme was intended to remain focused on musicians seeking to showcase their talent.
The official competition remains open, with Guitar Center currently listing submissions as due by October 8 at 3:59am UTC. The eventual winner will receive the opportunity to perform at Sheeran’s Mexico City concert, giving the promotion a genuine music industry opportunity despite its unusually timed arrival in the middle of the LOOP TOUR controversy.

title: Salman Toor honoured by TIME100 Art 2026 for shaping future of art
description: Pakistani American artist earns his second recognition as his work on intimacy and isolation draws global attention
content:
Pakistani-American artist earns his second recognition as his work on intimacy and isolation draws global attention
Pakistani-American artist Salman Toor has been named to TIME’s TIME100 Art 2026 list, marking the second time the artist has been recognised by the magazine.
TIME100 Art 2026 was announced on Friday afternoon, with Toor featured among the 100 most influential people shaping the future of art.
The 42-year-old artist was named alongside internationally recognised painters, photographers, artists, museum leaders and philanthropists, bringing together some of the most prominent figures working across the global art world.
Toor was recognised for his work exploring intimacy and isolation, with TIME highlighting the way his paintings depict young brown men experiencing moments of connection and solitude.
In its profile of the artist, TIME described his work as portraying young brown men “in states of convergence and of isolation.” “Sometimes, the men are dancing at a bar, bathed in emerald light; other times, they are alone, lying in bed,” it wrote.
The latest recognition adds to Toor’s growing international profile and follows several notable milestones in his career.
In 2020, TIME reported that Toor’s paintings had sold for more than $1 million at auction, highlighting the growing interest in his work in the international art market.
Since then, he has continued to expand his presence through exhibitions and major international art events. Toor toured a solo exhibition to four museums, bringing his work to audiences in different parts of the world, and also participated in the Venice Biennale, one of the art world’s major international events.
The artist has also held a two-part gallery exhibition that sold out, adding to a series of milestones that have marked his career in recent years.
Another major moment is on the horizon, with Toor’s first solo European exhibition set to open at the Courtauld Gallery in London in October.
His inclusion in TIME100 Art 2026 is also not his first appearance on a TIME list. Toor was previously featured on the magazine’s TIME100 Next list in 2021, making his latest recognition another appearance on one of TIME’s influential annual lists.

title: Monster  The Lizzie Borden Story    faces backlash from critics and audiences
description: Ella Beatty leads eight episodes inspired by one of America   s most notorious unsolved murder cases
content:
Ella Beatty leads eight episodes inspired by one of America’s most notorious unsolved murder cases
Netflix’s Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story has arrived to a divided response, with early Rotten Tomatoes scores showing a sharp gap between the series and some viewers and critics. The fourth instalment of Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan’s anthology stars Ella Beatty as Lizzie Borden, the Massachusetts woman who was tried and acquitted in connection with the 1892 axe murders of her father and stepmother.
According to Forbes , the series had a 50% Rotten Tomatoes critics score and a 26% audience score when its September 18 report was published. Those figures were based on six critic reviews and more than 50 verified audience ratings. Rotten Tomatoes has continued updating the page as additional reviews arrive, meaning the scores are subject to change.
The early critical response has not been completely negative. Aramide Tinubu of Variety gave the season a fresh rating on Rotten Tomatoes and described the fourth entry as offering something distinctive within the Monster franchise. Decider has also highlighted the performances and the series’ comparatively restrained approach to its material.
However, other reviews have questioned the depth of the retelling. Lucy Mangan of The Guardian praised the performances and visual style while arguing that the season ultimately has little to say about Borden herself. Her review gave the series two stars out of five.
The new season runs for eight episodes and features Rebecca Hall as Abby Borden, Charlie Hunnam as Andrew Borden, Billie Lourd as Emma Borden and Vicky Krieps as Bridget Sullivan. Sarah Paulson also appears as convicted serial killer Aileen Wuornos.
The series is also drawing attention for its dramatic interpretation of Bridget Sullivan’s relationship with Lizzie. Historical records do not establish that the pair had a romantic relationship or that Sullivan participated in the murders, making the storyline a clear dramatic interpretation rather than established fact.
With all eight episodes now available on Netflix, the Rotten Tomatoes scores are likely to continue shifting as further reviews and audience reactions are recorded.

title: PCB launches PSL cricket development award
description: Franchises to be assessed on players    pathway  infrastructure  grassroots work and welfare
content:
Franchises to be assessed on players’ pathway, infrastructure, grassroots work and welfare
The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Friday launched a $200,000 award to recognize the franchise that makes the biggest contribution to cricket development, with teams to be assessed on players’ pathways, infrastructure, grassroots programmes and player welfare.
“The PCB has today unveiled the procedure to award one franchise the prestigious and inaugural HBL PSL Cricket Development Excellence Award worth USD 200,000. The 2026 award will consider the development work done by franchises since the HBL PSL 3 season till the HBL PSL 11, i.e. from the period during which a minimum of six franchises participated in the league,” the PCB said in a press statement.
“After the 11th edition of the tournament, only the development work done between two latest editions will be considered and evaluated for this award.”
It said that the franchises will self-assess and mark themselves using a scoring model devised by the HBL PSL in the first phase and submit it to an assessment committee formulated by the PCB.
“The five-member committee includes independent experts as well as internal stakeholders, who will be tasked with the responsibility to verify and confirm each score against the evidence supplied, using verifiable data points. 80 percent of the final score will be assessed through this mechanism. Thereafter, competing franchises will be asked to publish a presentation depicting cricket development work carried by them on official PSL social media handles.” Fans will be entitled to vote and rank the franchises development performance, and their votes will carry 20 percent weightage in the final scores.
The scoring model and the weightage of the scores will feature: player pathway and development (25 percent), player impact and match contribution (10 percent), high-performance infrastructure and innovations (15 percent), grassroots and domestic engagement (20 percent), player welfare and education (10 percent), fan voting via social media (20 percent).
Scoring guidelines will be provided to fans at the time of voting.
“The player pathway and development key performance indicator (KPI) will deal with new or uncapped talent identified by franchises, their development, their progression and cricket exposure provided to them beyond HBL PSL.”
The PCB said that the player impact and match contribution KPI will evaluate a scouted and new found player’s impact trajectory, match deciding impact and role expansion with a respective franchise.
“The high-performance infrastructure and innovations KPI combines institutional capacity, facilities, staffing and systems, with technology-led innovation. The player welfare and education KPI deals with the financial literacy and education support provided by franchises to players along with things like mental health support systems, media training, anti-doping and anti-corruption education and career transition plans.”
“Grassroots and Domestic Engagement KPI will evaluate the work done by franchises in men’s and women’s cricket development, arrangement of coaching clinics for kids, School and club cricket initiatives and participation in PCB-organized cricket,” it said.

title: Ed Sheeran   s tour faces uncertainty after Macklemore fallout
description: Sheeran and his advisers have discussed whether to continue with the remaining dates of his Loop Tour
content:
Sheeran and his advisers have discussed whether to continue with the remaining dates of his Loop Tour
Ed Sheeran’s US stadium tour has faced uncertainty following the removal of Macklemore as a supporting act and the subsequent departure of several other artists in protest.
According to the Financial Times, Sheeran and his advisers have discussed whether to continue with the remaining dates of his Loop Tour. The tour was still scheduled to proceed, with Sheeran due to perform in Philadelphia on Saturday, September 19, although cancelling dates could carry significant financial consequences.
The dispute began after Macklemore performed at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium and said “Free Palestine” during his set. Macklemore was subsequently removed from the tour by promoter Messina Touring Group.
The Financial Times reported that New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft told Sheeran that Macklemore would not be allowed to perform at upcoming dates at Gillette Stadium. According to people familiar with the matter, Kraft also warned that other NFL stadium owners could cancel Sheeran’s scheduled shows if Macklemore remained on the tour.
Following Macklemore’s departure, several other supporting acts also withdrew. Finneas, Lukas Graham and Aaron Rowe quit in protest, while Irish band Beoga, which performs with Sheeran, also dropped out. Finneas said artists should not be silenced when speaking up for oppressed people.
The fallout has also placed renewed attention on Sheeran’s longstanding decision to avoid public political positions. Macklemore argued that the singer’s public neutrality had become difficult to maintain, while Sheeran said he has personal views about the conflict but chooses not to express them publicly.
Sheeran has instead sought to focus on humanitarian aid, pledging $2 million for relief in the region and asking Kraft to match the donation. Kraft said Sheeran planned to approach other venue owners as part of an effort to “build bridges”.
The Financial Times reported that cancelling a stadium show could cost Sheeran an estimated $5 million to $7 million per date, according to music-industry business manager Bill Zysblat.

title: Anthropic s Claude helped cybersecurity researchers breach OpenAI  report
description: Hacktron team says it accessed OpenAI   s internal code repository before reporting vulnerabilities to company
content:
Hacktron team says it accessed OpenAI’s internal code repository before reporting vulnerabilities to company
A three-person cybersecurity research team used Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5 to exploit vulnerabilities in an OpenAI community forum, take control of employee accounts and demonstrate access to the company’s private code repository.
The operation began on July 23 and was carried out by researchers from Hacktron AI, who disclosed the vulnerabilities to OpenAI and stopped testing without examining the company’s source code.
The Wall Street Journal , which interviewed the researchers and first reported the incident, said OpenAI paid the team $6,500 for its discovery.
The researchers reported the OpenAI-side vulnerability through the company’s bug-bounty programme. Testing of the third-party forum software itself, however, was outside the scope of OpenAI’s bounty programme.
Read: OpenAI's rogue agents probed Hugging Face for weaknesses two months before major hack
The researchers, Harsh Jaiswal, Mohan Pedhapati and Rahul Maini, published a detailed technical account explaining how they combined a flaw in the software behind OpenAI’s community forum with a separate problem in the company’s sign-on system.
The attack began at community.openai.com , a help forum powered by the third-party discussion platform Discourse.
Hacktron found that certain uploaded image formats were processed through ImageMagick and a vulnerable version of the image-decoding library libheif. The vulnerability allowed specially prepared image data to trigger remote code execution, meaning an attacker could potentially run commands on the forum’s server.
A separate identity-management flaw then allowed the researchers to move from a compromised forum session to ChatGPT and Codex accounts belonging to active forum members, including OpenAI employees.
Because those accounts could be connected to other services, the potential reach extended to platforms including GitHub, Slack and Outlook, according to Hacktron.
Read more: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google are working to create an AI standards body
To demonstrate the impact without reading confidential material, the researchers instructed a compromised employee’s Codex account, which was connected to OpenAI’s GitHub organisation, to open a harmless pull request in the company’s private “openai/openai” monorepo, the central digital vault housing the core source code for all its AI systems
The team said it stopped testing immediately afterwards and updated its report to OpenAI.

title: Italian aircraft hit during air base attacks in Saudi Arabia | The Express Tribune
description: Military personnel are unharmed, and no other vehicles or infrastructure used by them are damaged, says Guido Crosetto
content:
Military personnel are unharmed, and no other vehicles or infrastructure used by them are damaged, says Guido Crosetto
An Italian aircraft was hit during air base attacks in Saudi Arabia, Defence Minister Guido Crosetto announced Friday.
Crosetto noted that he followed the situation at Saudi Arabia's Ta'if air base, "which was the target of several attacks and where Italian personnel are present as part of Operation Inherent Resolve," according to ANSA news agency.
He reaffirmed that no Italian military personnel were involved.

"During the attack, an Italian F-2000 aircraft was hit. It was inside the base, in a remote area. There is no other damage to vehicles or infrastructure used by our personnel,” Crosetto said.
He noted that he asked to be provided with further assessment of the evolving situation, the condition of their personnel and possible operational options.
Crosetto added that he had been reassured that all security measures to protect military personnel had already been put in place some time ago.
“The situation is being followed with the utmost attention, with the aim of ensuring the full protection of our personnel and operating with the necessary responsibility," Crosetto further said.

Saudi Arabia has faced a series of missile and drone attacks attributed to the Houthis in recent days amid escalating regional tensions.
Fighting between Yemeni government forces and the Houthis has also intensified since early July.
The renewed clashes have ended a period of relative calm that had largely held since a UN-brokered truce took effect in April 2022.

title: Pakistan climbs 22 places in Environmental Performance Index 2026  air pollution keeps it near bottom
description: Pakistan recorded an EPI score of 29 03 in the latest assessment  compared with 22 46 for India
content:
Pakistan recorded an EPI score of 29.03 in the latest assessment, compared with 22.46 for India
Pakistan moved up 22 places in the latest Environmental Performance Index (EPI), improving from 179th in 2024 to 157th in the 2026 global ranking, according to the index biennially published by Yale University.
Pakistan recorded an EPI score of 29.03 in the latest assessment, compared with 22.46 for India, which ranks second-to-last on the index that compared 177 countries on 47 indicators across 12 issue categories representing critical sustainability challenges in environmental public health, ecosystem vitality, and climate change.
According to the report, the country performs particularly poorly on environmental health and air quality, while some areas of ecosystem protection and forest performance show considerably stronger results.
Within South Asia, Pakistan ranks fifth, behind Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal and Afghanistan, according to Yale's regional table. Its score is below the South Asian regional average of 31.81. Bhutan, with a score of 47.74, surpasses the regional average to lead South Asia but ranks 52nd globally.
Read: Remote emission scanning to boost anti-smog fight
Pakistan's overall score changed only modestly over the longer term: Yale records a 10-year change of 1.05 points. That is important because it suggests that, despite individual areas of progress, Pakistan's overall environmental trajectory has not changed dramatically over the period measured by the index.
The worst part of Pakistan's 2026 scorecard is its performance on environmental health. The country ranked 175th globally for Environmental Health, with a score of just 14.57.
In this category, its Air Quality score stood at 7.54, pushing Pakistan to the second-last spot in the global ranking.
The numbers are particularly revealing when compared with the South Asian average.
Pakistan recorded a score of 2.42 for ambient PM2.5, ranking 162nd globally. The index also assessed exposure to nitrogen dioxide, sulfur dioxide, ozone, and carbon monoxide among other air-quality indicators.
Despite the low overall air-quality ranking, Pakistan performed relatively strongly on the EPI’s nitrogen dioxide exposure indicator, ranking 29th globally with a score of 76.71.
For Pakistan's major urban centres, smog episodes, particulate pollution and deteriorating urban air quality have become recurring public concerns, making it one of the most consequential findings in the EPI for ordinary citizens.
The EPI's Environmental Health objective does not measure air pollution alone. It also evaluates sanitation, drinking water, heavy-metal exposure, and other factors affecting human health. This distinction matters for Pakistan.
Also Read: A pathway for Pakistan's agribusiness transformation
According to the report, Pakistan ranks 140 th in the Sanitation and Drinking Water category. Yale University outlined that the category measured how well countries protected human health from environmental risks pertaining to unsafe drinking water and sanitation.
In terms of heavy metal exposure, Pakistan once again ranked towards the bottom of the list at 162, calling for the attention of the government.
The country’s solid waste management also failed to impress the experts, landing the 129 th spot globally.
Pakistan's environmental record is not uniformly poor
There were notable areas of comparatively stronger performance.
Pakistan ranks 14th globally on the EPI's Forests indicator, with a score of 52.16. Its 10-year change on this indicator is also positive. Furthermore, it ranked 95th globally on Terrestrial Biome Protection, scoring 54.05, substantially above the Southern Asian regional average of 38.43.
The findings become mixed when looking at biodiversity. Pakistan ranks 143rd globally on Biodiversity and Habitat, with a score of 25.34. Its regional rank is fourth, but the score remains low in absolute terms.
The country ranked 159th on the Protected Areas Representativeness Index, scoring 13.76.
Pakistan’s agriculture sector, as per the index, performed poorly. Ranked 155th, Pakistan registered a negative change of 2.64% in the last 10 years. It also performed 19.57 points lower than the regional average.
The same record was reflected in relative crop yield. Pakistan fared worse than the regional average.
Climate change remains another difficult front
The EPI's Climate Change Mitigation indicator places Pakistan at 123rd globally, with a score of 29.76. Yale recorded a 10-year change of -3.12 points for this measure.
This is particularly significant because Pakistan is highly exposed to climate-related risks, while its contribution to global greenhouse-gas emissions is relatively small compared with the world's largest emitters. Thereby, EPI primarily assessed environmental performance and progress toward policy targets.
Estonia, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, France and Germany bagged the first five spots in the Climate Change Mitigation category.
United Kingdom assumed the 7 th highest position in the aforesaid category; the United States 43 rd , Bangladesh 120 th , Pakistan 123 rd , China 125 th , and India 130 th .
According to the report, Pakistan’s Projected Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions in 2050 are likely to increase by 1.5 times compared to 2024. The indicator gauged whether countries are on track to reach zero emissions of four greenhouse gases (carbon dioxide, methane, fluorinated gases, and nitrous oxide) by 2050.

title: Punjab grocers reject 9pm shop closure under new austerity measures
description: Association warns restrictions will hurt businesses  raise unemployment and undermine foreign exchange targets
content:
Association warns restrictions will hurt businesses, raise unemployment and undermine foreign exchange targets
The All Punjab Grocers Association on Friday rejected the government’s new austerity measures, saying grocery shops would not close at 9pm and warning that the restrictions would hurt businesses and increase unemployment.
The announcement came hours after the federal government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures on Thursday and directed provincial governments to adopt similar steps. Punjab had previously maintained closing times of 9pm for shops, 10pm for marriage halls and 11pm for restaurants.
In a video message, APGA President Hafiz Arif Gujjar said, “No country in the world closes food shops, even in wartime conditions.” He said the association would not close grocery shops at 9pm and would resist the government’s decision. “The government’s decision to close shops at 11pm was also harmful to businesses,” he added.
Gujjar further said imposing a smart lockdown was “tantamount to taking the country backwards”, warning that the move would damage the business community and make it difficult to meet foreign exchange targets.
“Millions of people will lose their jobs after the lockdown,” he said, adding that the decision would increase unemployment. He urged the government to reconsider the decision and “give businesses unrestricted operating hours”.
Read: PM unveils austerity measures as Gulf conflict spirals
The measures came a day after the federal government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures and asked provincial governments to consider adopting similar steps. The federal package included a 50 per cent cut in fuel allocations for official vehicles for three months, a 5 per cent reduction in the non-ERE budget and a three-month ban on official foreign travel.
Punjab had already retained restrictions on business timings, with shops, markets and shopping malls required to close by 9pm, marriage halls and marquees by 10pm, and restaurants and food outlets by 11pm.
The province had withdrawn several other austerity measures in June, while retaining the restrictions on business timings. The latest decision expanded the measures to include restrictions on official meetings and events, as well as further controls aimed at reducing government expenditure and conserving fuel.
Under the new measures, the provincial government also sought to reduce spending on official events by directing departments to prefer video conferencing for meetings and use government auditoriums and committee rooms where seminars, training programmes or conferences could not be avoided.
The latest austerity measures come against the backdrop of a fuel conservation drive launched by the federal government earlier this year as international energy prices surged amid escalating tensions in the Middle East. The war between the United States, Iran and Israel sent global energy prices up.
In March, the government introduced a broad package of energy conservation and cost-cutting measures aimed at reducing fuel consumption and containing pressure on the economy that were later extended up to June.
The drive included a 50% reduction in fuel allocations for government vehicles, grounding 60% of the official fleet, restrictions on foreign travel and a ban on the purchase of vehicles and several categories of equipment. The government also announced reductions in official expenditure and changes to working arrangements in the public sector.
On June 10, the government extended several austerity measures until June 30 and revised the closing time for standalone grocery and neighbourhood stores.
Nine days later, the government announced a sharp reduction in domestic petroleum prices following an improvement in regional conditions and a decline in international oil prices. The prime minister said the federal government had used savings generated through austerity measures, alongside development budget allocations, to help provide relief to consumers.
Then on June 21, the government formally withdrew most of the austerity measures. Full petrol allowances for officials were restored, and up to 60% of the government vehicle fleet was allowed to return to operation. However, restrictions on the operating hours of markets, shopping malls, wedding halls and restaurants remained in place.
Read more: Austerity drive leaves NA with vehicle headache
The government’s renewed austerity push now comes amid another sharp deterioration in the international fuel market. In a report published on September 15, The Express Tribune said the government was considering bringing back some of the earlier fuel conservation measures as renewed conflict and disruption to oil supply routes in the Middle East pushed up petroleum prices.
The renewed pressure coincided with a sharp increase in domestic petroleum prices.
Yesterday, the government, with the approval of the prime minister , also introduced a targeted fuel-relief scheme for motorcycles, rickshaws, Qingqi rickshaws and cars with engines of up to 800cc.

title: 2026   s    Sense and Sensibility    earns glowing early reactions ahead of cinema release
description: Critics have praised Georgia Oakley   s direction  performances and fresh approach to Jane Austen   s classic
content:
Critics have praised Georgia Oakley’s direction, performances and fresh approach to Jane Austen’s classic
The latest adaptation of Jane Austen’s Sense and Sensibility has received enthusiastic early reactions following its London premiere, with critics praising its performances, visual style and treatment of the beloved novel.
Directed by Georgia Oakley and written by Diana Reid, the Focus Features film stars Daisy Edgar Jones as Elinor Dashwood, Esmé Creed Miles as Marianne Dashwood, Caitríona Balfe as Mrs Dashwood, George MacKay as Edward Ferrars and Fiona Shaw. The film is scheduled for release in UK cinemas on September 25.
The first reactions emerged after the film’s Tuesday premiere in London, with several critics highlighting the cast and Oakley’s approach to Austen’s story.
Tori Brazier of Metro praised the film for remaining faithful to the spirit of Austen’s novel while still feeling fresh. She highlighted the relationship between the Dashwood sisters and singled out Fiona Shaw, while also praising the male cast.
Casey Loving of TheWrap described the film as being for “the yearners” and praised Oakley and Reid for staying true to Austen while making key changes. He also highlighted Edgar Jones and George MacKay, while calling Creed Miles’ performance as Marianne particularly impressive.
Jazz Tangcay of Variety praised the chemistry between Edgar Jones and Creed Miles and described Balfe as wonderful. Tangcay also credited Reid with bringing wit to the screenplay, calling the film “a delight”.
Other early reactions have focused on the film’s romantic qualities. Lyvie Scott of Inverse praised Oakley’s creation of the film’s world and described it as sweet, while also singling out MacKay.
Matt Neglia of Next Best Picture praised the cast, costumes, score and Edgar Jones’ performance, while calling Creed Miles a standout. He also acknowledged the challenge of following Ang Lee’s acclaimed 1995 adaptation, but said Oakley’s version showed considerable care and affection for Austen’s material.
The reactions arrive just days before the film reaches UK cinemas, giving Austen fans an early indication of what critics experienced at its London premiere.

title: Founder of Chinese startup Spirit AI says robot brains set for 2027 breakthrough
description: An industry breakthrough    comparable to OpenAI s landmark GPT 3 0 model could come around mid 2027
content:
An industry breakthrough ⁠comparable to OpenAI's landmark GPT-3.0 model could come around mid-2027
Humanoid robot brains are likely to ​achieve a breakthrough as soon as mid-2027, but their deployment in homes could take at least eight ‌years as model development faces a data bottleneck, leading Chinese embodied AI firm Spirit AI said this week.
Despite impressive hardware advances allowing Chinese humanoids to sprint, dance and do backflips on command, Chinese robot firms are increasingly focusing on the software that determines robots' intelligence and their economic productivity ​in real-world settings.
"The brain is indeed the weakest link in the complete robotics stack," Gao Yang, co-founder and ​chief scientist of Spirit AI, told Reuters at its Beijing offices on Thursday.
An industry breakthrough ⁠comparable to OpenAI's landmark GPT-3.0 model, which powered ChatGPT, could come around mid-2027, said Gao. Spirit AI's robots have achieved ​a 90% success rate for simple tasks in structured living-room environments.
Read: King Charles warns AI leaders of 'existential dangers'
"The next one to two years mark the initial window for ​industrial applications. Two years from now, we'll see robots deployed in commercial service settings doing simpler tasks. Entering homes is far harder than both," said Gao, who is also an assistant professor of robotics at Tsinghua University.
Spirit AI currently has tens of its own ​Moz1 wheeled humanoid robots deployed on production lines at battery maker CATL and retailer JD.com, which is also an investor.
The ​300-person startup has raised over $670 million since its 2024 founding, making it one of China's most rapidly capitalised embodied intelligence firms. It is ‌currently valued ⁠at 20 billion yuan ($2.9 billion). Gao declined to comment on any plans for an initial public offering.
"Progress is extremely fast. When Spirit AI was founded, a robot could perform only one isolated task well, like pouring water or folding a piece of clothing," said Gao.
"Today, robots operate across large spatial areas and execute continuous complex workflows."
Difficulties remain in perfecting fine-motor actions like unscrewing ​a bottle cap and dealing ​with unseen tasks, he said. ⁠Spirit AI overwhelmingly relies on real-world data to train its robot brains instead of virtual simulations, which many competitors use to reduce model training costs.
"Simulators handle rigid bodies well, but ​flexible objects like deformable electric cables remain a problem," said Gao.
The company employs ​around 1,000 contractors ⁠nationwide using wearable data-collection equipment in households and on production lines.
Read more: US Senate blocks AI ‘kill switch’ bill amid debate over superintelligence risks
Its Beijing offices include a robot data training centre where a Reuters witness saw dozens of young people fitted with sensors who repeated motions like opening fridges, unlocking safes, and cutting vegetables with ⁠knives to ​train the humanoid robots.
In other robot-training facilities in China, operators may need to ​repeat a movement more than 50 times to get one "clean" movement with the required precision.
However, Spirit AI found that using "dirty data" with a more diverse ​range of motions enabled its models to improve faster, Gao said.

title: Mideast turmoil  AI set to dominate UN gathering of world leaders
description: Guterres warns of  serious risk of explosion  as leaders also wrangle over organisation s next chief
content:
Guterres warns of 'serious risk of explosion' as leaders also wrangle over organisation's next chief
As wars rage in the Middle East, Ukraine and Sudan, and fears mount over rapidly advancing AI, world leaders descend on the United Nations in New York from Tuesday for the world's signature diplomatic event.
United States President Donald Trump's war against Iran and its worldwide fallout are expected to dominate this year's UN General Assembly High-level Week.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky will meanwhile urge allies not to lose focus on his country's defence needs, as Russia retaliates for long-range drone strikes against its energy infrastructure.
"When we see the Russia-Ukraine war , and when we see the whole Middle East, every day things get a little bit worse," said UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres ahead of the gathering. "There is no improvement anywhere, and when things evolve in a way that every day things get a little bit worse, we are at a serious risk of an explosion."
Artificial intelligence will also be a key topic in talks and speeches, with its potential threats to humanity dominating global headlines after tech leaders sounded the alarm .
An emergency Security Council meeting is set to be held on the issue.
Read: UN assembly approves mandate extension for rights chief, despite US warning
"This year's UNGA could be where a plan starts to take shape to define what the world wants from industry's pledge on safety and who is responsible for monitoring it," said Nicolas Miailhe, an AI governance expert and co-founder of AI Safety Connect. "The harder part will be agreeing on what that plan looks like and moving it into reality."
Amid fierce competition between the United States and China on AI, Guterres urged more global coordination. "The world cannot afford a race to the bottom on AI safety," he said.
Behind the scenes, the world's power brokers will also be wrangling over the UN's future, seeking to thrash out a deal on a candidate to lead the organisation riven with divisions and budget black holes. No breakthrough is expected, but the global powers wielding vetoes over the process — Britain, France, Russia, China and the US —could well use the gathering to seal a deal.
Guterres's second five-year term ends on December 31, 2026 after a tenure marked by surging global conflict, the coronavirus pandemic, mounting inequality and rampant polarisation.
One European diplomat said the selection process was "not very successful so far ... any kind of consensus is not emerging."
The Israeli-Palestinian conflict — from a sputtering Gaza peace process to Israel's expansion of settlements in the occupied West Bank — will once again be among the divisive issues facing world leaders.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is expected to attend for a lightning visit, after New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani admitted he was unable to execute an International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant against him.
The Trump administration has denied US visas to Mahmoud Abbas and other Palestinian leaders for a second year.
China's President Xi Jinping will skip the diplomatic gathering and instead go straight to Washington for a state visit with Trump.
Read More: UN rights chief says uncovered remains in Gaza raise concerns of war crimes
Beijing's support for Russia and Iran will be among the thorny subjects under discussion. "China has long seen high-level week as US turf," said the International Crisis Group's Daniel Forti. "And while the Chinese diplomats at the UN are really intentionally trying to position themselves as a more predictable and stable big power compared to Washington, our assessment is that Xi doesn't need the spotlight at high-level week to make that case," he added.
With heat records being broken around the globe and extreme weather events multiplying, Guterres, as he has throughout his tenure, will continue to push for more global action against climate change .
He will convene a meeting on Climate Action and the Just Transition, followed by a day dedicated to sea-level rise, an existential threat for low-lying island nations.
The climate and environmental harms associated with artificial intelligence — as well as its potentially catalytic benefits — are expected to figure heavily at the UN and the broader Climate Week around it in New York, an annual jamboree of activists, corporations and academics.

title: Ibrahim Ali Khan wants to create his own legacy in the Indian film industry
description: Actor opens up about his career ambitions  fashion  acting process and misconceptions surrounding his public image
content:
Actor opens up about his career ambitions, fashion, acting process and misconceptions surrounding his public image
Ibrahim Ali Khan is keen to write his own story in the world of entertainment, saying he does not want to borrow from his parents’ careers but instead hopes to build his own path as an actor. Speaking to Elle Magazine , Khan discussed his personal style, family legacy, first theatrical release and his journey towards establishing himself in the industry.
“Honestly, I don't want anything from either of their iconic careers. I want to build my own path as an actor,” Khan said when speaking to Elle about his goals. He joked, “Maybe my father's National Award, and my mother's debut, instead of mine.”
According to Elle , the 25-year-old actor spent much of his childhood around film sets, accompanying his father, Saif Ali Khan, behind the scenes of his New York-set film Ta Ra Rum Pum , released in 2007. Years later, Khan said he would still jump at the opportunity to take on similar roles.
His first on-screen appearance came in 2008, when he played the younger version of his father’s character in Tashan . He later made his feature-film debut in the 2025 Netflix romantic comedy Nadaaniyan , opposite Khushi Kapoor. His patriotic drama Sarzameen was also released that year.
Before stepping in front of the camera, Khan began familiarising himself with the entertainment industry by working as filmmaker Karan Johar’s assistant director on Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani , according to Elle .
“Starting on time and finishing on time basically never happens in this industry, no matter what,” Khan said of his experience. He also described what makes a good day on set for him. “A good, long, satisfying day where you feel genuinely good about what you've done in front of the camera.”
Despite his interest in acting, Khan said he does not follow any particular ritual or set of techniques when preparing for a role. Speaking about being a method actor, he admitted that his approach was somewhat unconventional.
“As much as I'd love to be more of a method actor,” he laughed, “my ADHD brain chooses music over anything else. Reaching for my Starbucks constantly, and being caffeinated and wired the entire shoot. I need to calm down a little,” he said.
Khan also opened up about his love for fashion, explaining that while his father’s influence was naturally part of his upbringing, he did not want to imitate Saif’s style. He first clarified that copying his father’s fame and style would be “stupid”, adding that the genetics show up regardless.
“A nice pair of jeans with a bandana, kurtas and jackets worn a certain way as Abba does. I don't see Dad roaming around in baggy jeans and sneakers with an oversized, loose T-shirt, you know what I mean? Dad's too classy for that,” Khan said, emphasising that his own style reflected a more Gen Z, free-spirited approach.
Away from acting and fashion, Khan revealed his passion for PlayStation, admitting that he spends a considerable amount of time playing Call of Duty , FIFA and Trackmania . “The competition is up there, and we're all constantly sweating it out to prove who's the best. Me, obviously,” he joked.
Towards the end of the conversation, Khan addressed what he described as misconceptions about him in the media, saying that many of them were simply untrue.
“That I'm rude. I just have a playful tone, and I think the way I speak can come across differently from how I mean it. I'm really not as serious as people think. Very ‘just a 25-year-old guy’ going through life,” he said.
Khan’s dream role remains a character in the spirit of Robert Downey Jr’s Iron Man or his own father’s role in Race .

title: Top Olympic official wants even bigger Asian Games
description: Al Musallam rejects calls to cap participants despite accommodation concerns
content:
Al-Musallam rejects calls to cap participants despite accommodation concerns
Asia's Olympic chief said Friday that he wished the Asian Games in Japan had an athletes' village and hinted that future editions of the multisport event could be even bigger.
The continent's premier sporting spectacle opens in Nagoya and Aichi prefecture on Saturday but the build-up has been beset by difficulties.
That includes a shortage of rooms for the more than 17,000 athletes and officials -- a bigger number than the Olympics.
To save money there is no athletes' village at this year's Games, organisers instead putting competitors in hotels, temporary wooden huts and on a cruise ship.
Some teams have complained about the quality of the accommodation, including that the beds are too short.
Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) director general Husain Al-Musallam said organisers needed to "be practical" and put on a financially sustainable event.
"We wish that we have an athlete village, number one, but number two we also have to be flexible," he said.
"We need to listen also to the organiser, to the host, how they would look for the future, after the Games, after the closing ceremony.
"It's very easy, you can insist on the athlete village, and then you build the athlete village, you spend an amount of money but then you need to see what's going to happen after the Games," he added.
South Korean officials said earlier this week that there was "a serious shortage of accommodation" at the Games.
Officials from the Philippines said they had resorted to Airbnb.
Al-Musallam said that "every athlete, every official, every coach has accommodation".
"There is no single accredited person without accommodation," he added.
Local organisers initially expected 15,000 athletes and officials and argued last month that they had "neither the manpower nor the budget" to deal with ballooning numbers.
In March, the OCA added teqball and padel to the sporting programme.
Asian Games official Mohammad Tayyab Ikram said as of Friday they were "touching around 17,000-plus participants, which does not include yet the technical officials".
The accommodation crunch in Japan has led to suggestions that participant numbers at future Asian Games could be capped.
Al-Musallam ruled that out, saying he wants to make the event even bigger.
"I am a supporter to increase the number of athletes, not to decrease athletes," he said.
"To support sport because now with the current political crisis and conflicts in Asia and around the world, we need sport."
The Asian Games will be held in Doha in 2030 and Al-Musallam said six countries including India and the Philippines were interested in staging the event in 2034.
"This shows the popularity of the Asian Games," he said.

title: Canada EU  associate membership   What it means for Ottawa and Europe
description: Proposal would stop short of full membership  deepen Ottawa s ties across trade  defence  tech  energy and research
content:
Proposal would stop short of full membership, deepen Ottawa's ties across trade, defence, tech, energy and research
Amid fraying ties with the United States, Canada's push to move closer to Europe is taking shape around a new idea: an "associate member" relationship with the European Union that would stop short of full membership but deepen ties across trade, defence and technology.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen put the idea on the table Wednesday, telling Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney that she wanted to work with him on "opening the door on Canada being the first associate member of the EU."
The proposal, made at the European Parliament in Strasbourg, would break new ground.
The EU currently has no formal category of "associate membership," meaning its precise legal structure, rights and obligations would have to be worked out.
Carney embraced the broader ambition Thursday in his own address to European lawmakers, calling for what he described as an "alliance for the future" spanning critical minerals, defence, artificial intelligence, energy, research, financial services and digital trade.
Neither side is proposing that Canada become the EU's next full member. Carney said after his speech that Ottawa is neither in a position nor seeking to become a full EU member, stressing that the substance of the relationship would matter more than whatever label is ultimately attached to it.
Instead, von der Leyen has proposed building on the Canada-EU Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) to create what she called a "common prosperity and economic security space."
CETA has been provisionally applied since September 2017, eliminating tariffs on the vast majority of goods traded between the two sides. But it has still not fully entered into force because 10 EU member states have yet to complete national ratification.
Read: Canada applies to join UK-led military coalition
Carney's proposals suggest the new relationship could go considerably further. He called for Canada and Europe to work together on critical mineral supply chains, defence industrial capacity, artificial intelligence and computing infrastructure, energy security, space and payment systems.
He also proposed moving toward "seamless, digital trade" in non-agricultural goods and a wide range of services, while also exploring a more integrated market for financial services. Carney also said Canada could participate in the EU's Erasmus+ student exchange program and the next generation of its Horizon research program, arguing that young Canadians and Europeans should have greater opportunities to live, work and study on either side of the Atlantic.
Canada has already moved closer to the EU in defence, becoming the first non-European country to participate in the bloc's SAFE defence procurement initiative.
The push comes as Canada seeks to reduce its heavy economic dependence on the US amid a sharp deterioration in relations with Washington.
The US accounted for 71.7% of Canadian merchandise exports in 2025, according to Statistics Canada, leaving Ottawa particularly exposed to changes in American trade policy.
Washington and Ottawa are now engaged in an escalating tariff dispute , with each side imposing 50% duties on roughly $20 billion worth of selected goods. President Donald Trump has also repeatedly suggested Canada should become the 51st US state, an idea Carney and most Canadians vehemently reject.
Without naming the US in his European Parliament speech, Carney said economic integration was increasingly being used as a weapon, tariffs as leverage and supply chains as vulnerabilities that could be exploited.
He argued that sovereignty now requires countries to have secure access not only to food, energy and defence but also to artificial intelligence, semiconductors, critical minerals, payment systems, clean-energy technology, vaccines and space-based communications. "The objective is not self-sufficiency. It is collective resilience," he said.
Carney also sought to distinguish the proposal from an attempt to create another geopolitical power centre. "I am not proposing a third bloc in order to become a great-power rival — only with better manners," he said, adding that the objective was to build enough resilience to prevent other powers from controlling open markets or dictating national choices.
Trump has directly warned against the emerging arrangement. Speaking in North Carolina on Wednesday, he said the EU's effort to bring Canada closer could be considered a "hostile act" if it was undertaken with what he described as bad intentions.
"If it's a good intention, that's fine," Trump said. He warned, however, that the US could impose heavy tariffs on Europe or restrict trade in certain sectors if he concluded otherwise.
Read More: As Iran war grinds on, Trump to face skeptical world leaders at UN
Carney responded Thursday that Canada would decide for itself which international partnerships to pursue. "Nobody is going to dictate our culture, or with whom we can strike agreements," he told reporters in Strasbourg.
The European Commission has also rejected the suggestion that the initiative is aimed at Washington, saying closer Canada-EU ties are intended to strengthen the two partners rather than target another country.
Republican Senator Susan Collins has separately cautioned that Canada's move toward Europe could make it harder to repair its relationship with Washington and resolve the tariff dispute, while Democratic Senator Chris Coons has said he is seeking to organise a bipartisan congressional visit to Canada.
For now, "associate membership" remains a political proposal rather than a defined EU status.
Carney said Canada welcomed von der Leyen's ambition but stopped short of endorsing a particular institutional model, saying the two sides would define the relationship together. Some EU diplomats have also expressed reservations about creating a new membership category, even as there is broad interest in expanding cooperation with Canada.
The next major milestone is the Canada-EU summit scheduled for October 29-30 in Montreal, where officials are expected to develop the proposed relationship further.
The eventual arrangement could therefore look less like conventional EU membership and more like a customised framework tying Canada more closely to European markets, defence programs, research networks and strategic industries.
Exactly how far that integration would go — and what either side would have to give up or change in return — remains to be negotiated.

In the women’s category, India goalkeeper Bichu Devi Karibam won with 52 percent of the vote for a late reflex save against England.
The 2026 FIH Hockey World Cup was held in Belgium and the Netherlands and concluded on August 30.
Pakistan Hockey Federation’s President Mohyuddin Ahmad Wani congratulated Rehman on the achievement and said his success could inspire young hockey players in Pakistan.

description: The true story behind Netflix s drama centres on one of America s most closely scrutinised murder cases
content:
The true story behind Netflix's drama centres on one of America's most closely scrutinised murder cases
The true story behind Netflix's Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story centres on one of America's most closely scrutinised murder cases.
Lizzie Borden was accused of killing her father, Andrew Borden, and stepmother, Abby Borden, with an axe in 1892.
According to Netflix Tudum, the latest season of Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan's anthology series dramatises the case while adding fictionalised elements.
Ella Beatty plays Lizzie, with Vicky Krieps portraying Bridget "Maggie" Sullivan, the family's housemaid.
Beatty said she researched the case extensively before taking on the role. "When the audition came up, I listened to every true crime [podcast] that I could find to learn the facts of the case," she said.
The real Borden murders remain disputed, although evidence presented in the case pointed towards Lizzie.
The series depicts her as living under strict and repressive parents before the killings.
Historical records show Abby Borden was struck 19 times and Andrew 11, rather than the larger numbers suggested by the famous rhyme about Lizzie Borden.
Several alternative suspects have since been proposed, but none was established as responsible for the murders.
The series also changes elements of the historical record, including its portrayal of Nance O'Neil, who became friends with Lizzie years after the trial rather than coaching her through it.
Netflix Tudum also reports that the season explores connections between Lizzie Borden and later female criminals, including Aileen Wuornos, as part of its wider examination of female violence and social constraints.

title: Hudson Williams struggled to find his way back to Shane Hollander in  Heated Rivalry  season 2
description: After filming his first scene  Williams recalled wondering     Am I doing a Shane impression
content:
After filming his first scene, Williams recalled wondering, “Am I doing a Shane impression?”
Hudson Williams has opened up about the challenge of returning to his Heated Rivalry character Shane Hollander for the highly anticipated second season.
Speaking during a Q&A at the Toronto International Film Festival, Williams said he and co-star Connor Storrie felt “possibly overconfident” when they returned to play hockey rivals Shane and Ilya Rosanov. However, their confidence quickly disappeared after their first days back on set.
After filming his first scene, Williams recalled wondering, “Am I doing a Shane impression?” He said he felt as though he was losing the character he had previously inhabited.
Williams explained that the cultural impact of the first season had changed how he and Storrie remembered their original performances. Rather than simply remembering making the scenes, they were now aware of how the finished episodes had been received, along with fan reactions and edits of their on-screen chemistry.
“It’s weird that our memory of playing season one isn’t just our true memory of showing up and doing the scenes,” Williams said. “Our memory isn’t ours, it’s everyone’s.”
The actor credited showrunner Jacob Tierney with helping him and Storrie settle back into their roles. Williams said Tierney made the set feel as small and familiar as it had during the first season, with the same crew returning for the second instalment.
Season 2 of Heated Rivalry began filming in the Toronto area last month. The first season became a breakout success, generating widespread discussion around its story of two hockey players navigating their relationship, expectations and sexuality.
Williams also discussed his approach to acting, saying he balances research and preparation with a willingness to experiment in front of the camera. He credited making independent short films before Heated Rivalry with helping him remain relaxed during auditions.
The actor is also appearing at TIFF for his new series YAGA, which stars Carrie-Anne Moss, Noah Reid and Clark Backo. The modern retelling of the Baba Yaga myth is set on Canada's west coast and is scheduled to arrive on Crave next month.

title: Venezuela nears deal to move  4b gold reserve to New York  FT says
description: Reserve could serve as collateral for govt borrowings  including for reconstruction following June earthquakes
content:
Reserve could serve as collateral for govt borrowings, including for reconstruction following June earthquakes
The Venezuelan government and the opposition are close to an agreement to transfer the central bank's gold reserves, worth about $4 billion, to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York from the Bank of England, the Financial Times reported on Friday.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report, which cited four people familiar with the discussion.
Under the proposed deal, the interim government of Delcy Rodriguez would gain legal control of the gold but would be unable to sell the holdings immediately, the report said. Instead, the reserve could be used as collateral for government borrowings, including for reconstruction following June’s twin earthquakes , the newspaper added.
A spokesperson for the British foreign office said the government was "not a party in the legal case to determine who should have control of Venezuelan gold held in the Bank of England".
United Kingdom Courts and the Bank of England are independent of government, the spokesperson added.
Gold could be used to try to counter inflation
The Federal Reserve Bank of New York and the Bank of England did not immediately respond to Reuters ' requests for comment outside regular business hours. The Venezuelan government and the opposition could not be reached for comment.
Last month, Venezuela's National Assembly chief Jorge Rodriguez said the country was working on recovering gold ​reserves held in the Bank ‌of England's underground vaults, in an effort to counter surging inflation.
The Bank of England has withheld about 31 metric tons of Venezuelan gold for years, citing its non-recognition of the legitimacy of then ⁠President Nicolas Maduro 's government.
Read: Venezuela's interim president says US energy deal will last 25 years
The BoE's refusal to release the gold goes back to early 2019 when the British government joined dozens of nations in backing then Venezuelan opposition leader Juan Guaido on the basis that Maduro's election win the previous year had been rigged.
The bullion has since been the subject of a prolonged legal dispute in British courts, and has not been released despite Maduro's capture by the US in January and a ​request by acting President Delcy Rodriguez to King Charles.
“The UK maintains its longstanding position of support for a democratic transition of power in Venezuela which reflects the will of the Venezuelan people,” the spokesperson for the British foreign office said.

title: Three students killed in Philippine school shooting  including gunman  officials say
description: Eight injured  four critical as attack marks two fatal gun incidents at country s schools since June
content:
Eight injured, four critical as attack marks two fatal gun incidents at country's schools since June
Three students were killed in a school shooting in the southern Philippines on Friday, including a 16-year-old suspected gunman who turned the gun on himself, provincial officials said.
Eight others were injured, with four in critical condition, and all the victims were students aged 14 to 17, said Albert Palencia, Mayor of Banga town in South Cotabato, where the shooting took place.
The incident follows two fatal gun incidents since June at schools in the Philippines, where school shootings were previously rare.
"The suspect supposedly sat beside his friends and told them to go home 'because after lunch, I will be executing my plan'. His friends laughed because the shooter was a known joker," Palencia told Reuters . "After lunch, he started shooting students. He hit 10 students before killing himself," Palencia added.
Read: Gunman fires inside Thai government office as country reels from school shooting
Last month, a student live-streamed himself shooting and killing another student in a classroom in Zamboanga in the country's south before taking ‌his own life. In June, at least three students were killed and about 20 others injured in an attack at a public high school in Tacloban, where two classmates opened fire on campus.
The Philippines has relatively strict gun ownership regulations, including background checks and psychological evaluation requirements, although illegal firearms remain in circulation.
The Friday shooting also follows a high-profile incident in Thailand in August, where a student went on a shooting rampage at a school on the outskirts of the capital Bangkok.
South Cotabato governor Reynaldo Tamayo urged parents to ensure guns were kept out of reach of minors. "We need to be responsible in storing firearms. Gun owners, in particular, must make sure that minors do not have access to them," Tamayo told Reuters by phone.
"We cannot expect a handful of security personnel to monitor thousands of students. We need to work together because otherwise this will be very difficult for us to address."

title: Lenny Kravitz becomes Barbie s latest Kenbassador with new collectible doll
description: The new Lenny Kravitz Ken doll features the singer s signature tattoos  jewellery and physique and retails for  70
content:
The new Lenny Kravitz Ken doll features the singer's signature tattoos, jewellery and physique and retails for $70
Lenny Kravitz has joined the Barbie universe as the second celebrity to receive the official Kenbassador honour, with Mattel releasing a collectible doll modelled after the Grammy-winning musician.
The new Lenny Kravitz Ken doll features the singer's signature tattoos, jewellery and physique. The doll is dressed in a slinky tank top and is available from major retailers for $70.
The release coincides with Ken's 65th anniversary.
Ken made his debut in 1961 and has since become a popular character among Barbie collectors, with Mattel regularly introducing special-edition versions.
Kravitz follows basketball star LeBron James, who became the first celebrity Kenbassador when his collectible doll was released in 2025.
The musician began his recording career with the 1989 album Let Love Rule and has also built an acting career, including appearances in films such as The Hunger Games .
Mattel said his music, personal style and influence on culture contributed to the decision to honour him.
Nathan Baynard, Vice President and Head of Barbie at Mattel, said in a release: “We’re proud to honour his lasting influence on style and culture through this doll, giving fans a new way to celebrate an artist whose authenticity continues to inspire generations.”
Kravitz also addressed the honour, saying: “Barbie is an institution, and as a kid growing up, I could not have imagined this. To be chosen by Mattel as a Kenbassador, only the second one in history, is an honour and absolutely surreal.”
The new doll has already attracted attention from Barbie collectors on social media and is available through major retailers.

title: James McAvoy nearly became a priest before girls changed his mind
description: James McAvoy says missionary work once appealed to him because it could take him around the world
content:
James McAvoy says missionary work once appealed to him because it could take him around the world
James McAvoy has revealed that acting was not always his first career ambition, recalling how seriously he once considered becoming a Catholic priest while growing up in Glasgow.
Speaking to IndieWire during the Toronto International Film Festival, the 47 year old actor said he was drawn to the priesthood as a child because he wanted to travel. He believed missionary work could take him to places he might otherwise never see, making the religious path particularly appealing to him.
McAvoy said his plans changed when he reached 13 and began thinking about girls. He also admitted that he had not fully understood the implications of celibacy when he was younger. His teenage awakening ultimately pushed the priesthood out of his plans, leaving him to pursue the acting career that would eventually make him internationally known.
The revelation comes as McAvoy promotes Faith , a supernatural drama centred on grief, spirituality and belief. Written and directed by Paul Andrew Williams, the film stars McAvoy alongside Erin Doherty, who plays a grieving single mother whose life becomes connected to McAvoy’s mysterious character. Faith had its world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 11.
McAvoy has also explained that his relationship with religion has changed considerably. He now describes himself as not religious and not particularly spiritual, although he sees parallels between his devotion to acting and the way spirituality can shape a person’s life. He has also reflected on the Catholic guilt associated with his upbringing and acknowledged that some of its effects have remained with him.
His childhood plans give Faith an interesting personal connection, even though McAvoy is not approaching the subject from a place of religious belief.
Following its TIFF premiere, Faith does not yet have a confirmed wider release date. McAvoy also has Meantime and Control among his upcoming projects, while his directorial debut California Schemin’ is scheduled for UK cinemas on October 9.
