title: Anayah Shahid says playing Shireen in  Zanjeerain  was a calculated risk
description: Actor says she deliberately chose a morally grey character  crediting Sajal Aly and Shahzad Kashmiri for their support
content:
Actor says she deliberately chose a morally grey character, crediting Sajal Aly and Shahzad Kashmiri for their support
Actor Anayah Shahid has opened up about the risk she took by choosing a morally grey character for her acting debut in Zanjeerain , saying she knew from the outset that Shireen would likely draw criticism before audiences understood where the story was headed.
Speaking in an interview with FUCHSIA Magazine , Anayah said she was aware that Shireen was far from the conventional choice for a newcomer, but saw the complexity of the role as an opportunity to prove herself. “Most newcomers get roles as a best friend or sister, which don't have much margin for acting. So, I saw this as a huge opportunity, and I kept pushing for it,” she said.
Anayah worked closely with director Shahzad Kashmiri to understand Shireen’s emotional journey and prepare for the character’s eventual arc. “I worked closely with Shahzad Kashmiri to map out Shireen's emotional trajectory, and he reassured me early on that the character would eventually win the audience over,” she said.
Her first day on set, however, was hardly an easy introduction to the production. Anayah recalled that her opening scene involved a technically challenging sequence centred around a necklace, and she relied heavily on Kashmiri’s guidance as she found her footing.
Another demanding moment came during the filming of Shireen’s pivotal confession scene, which was shot during Ramadan while Anayah was fasting and physically exhausted. Rather than allowing the fatigue to work against her, she said the experience helped her connect with the emotional intensity of the scene.
“When I got the character, from the time the shoot began, we all knew this was going to be a hit, and it was going to change all of our lives,” she said.
Anayah also credited co-star Sajal Aly with helping her navigate the nerves that came with entering the industry opposite an established actor. She described Aly as approachable and composed on set, which allowed her to concentrate on her own performance rather than feeling intimidated.
“She makes you feel so comfortable; she doesn't make you feel awkward or worried. Even when lines were being repeated, or a mistake occurred, she remained so calm, which allowed me to deliver my performance comfortably and confidently,” she said.
She recalled that Aly made the first move to put her at ease, making their interactions feel natural from the beginning. “She was very easy to talk to, and I think that was a major reason why I could perform well,” she added.
Away from the set, Anayah spoke about the values she wants to carry into her career, particularly when it comes to independence.
For her, financial stability is closely tied to having the freedom to make choices on her own terms. “If you want to live your life on your own terms, the first step is to become financially independent. After that, you can do whatever you want,” she said.
She also spoke about resisting the pressure to conform to an industry mould, saying she wants to retain a sense of authenticity as her career develops. “I manage to be who I am, which is very important for authenticity nowadays,” she said.
As for what comes next, Anayah said she is being selective rather than rushing into another project simply to remain visible. She named director Kashif Nisar as someone she would like to work with and said she is looking for roles that contribute meaningfully to a story.

title: 15 police personnel among 21 martyred in Kohat Police Lines terrorist attack  over 100 injured
description: Health report states over 100 injured  K P police chief says operation against terrorists in final stages
content:
K-P Police say seven armed terrorists, including a suicide bomber, were killed after infiltrating police lines
At least 21 people, including 15 police personnel and six civilians, were killed in the blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers, according to an initial incident report issued by DHQ Hospital Kohat medical superintendent and the district health officer.
The report said the blast occurred at approximately 1:20pm during Friday prayers at a mosque located at Police Lines on Hangu Road in Kohat, followed by a terrorist attack involving around five to seven terrorists.
Of the 21 people killed, 15 were police personnel and six were civilians. The report identified one of the deceased civilians as Dr Israel Khan Aurakzai, Chief District Specialist (Paediatrics) at Liaqat Memorial Hospital, Kohat.
It further said 103 injured people had been received at the two hospitals, including 13 at Liaqat Memorial Hospital and 90 at DHQ Hospital Kohat. The injured comprised 73 police personnel and 30 civilians.
Of the total injured, 34 were admitted for treatment, while five patients underwent laparotomy, a surgical procedure involving an incision into the abdomen.
The report said four of the patients who underwent laparotomy had been referred to tertiary care facilities in Peshawar for further treatment.
People carry an empty coffin box along a street leading to a police facility following a suicide attack at the facility in Kohat, Pakistan, September 18, 2026. Photo: Reuters
It added that the situation was being closely monitored and all possible medical assistance was being provided to the injured at the relevant health facilities.
According to the police, seven armed terrorists infiltrated the police lines following the explosion at the mosque. The police said six terrorists, including the suicide bomber, had been killed so far. Initially, a suicide attacker blew himself up near the Special Branch building after the explosion, it added.
Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, has claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers. Islamabad has repeatedly asked the Taliban regime to deny the use of Afghan soil for terrorist attacks inside Pakistan. However, the de facto rulers in Kabul have been reluctant to take action against terrorist groups operating from their territory.
In a statement, K-P Police Public Relations director said the operation against the terrorists had entered its final stages under the direct supervision of the K-P Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed, with security personnel carrying out a clearance operation in the area.
Hameed said authorities were tracing the terrorists and their facilitators and would ensure their complete elimination. He stated that police and the Counter Terrorism Department were engaged in an operation against Fitna al-Khawarij inside the police lines compound.
Ambulances are seen at the site of an explosion near the police headquarters in Kohat in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on September 18, 2026. Photo: AFP
“Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Police is standing as an iron wall against terrorism. Cowardly attacks cannot weaken our resolve,” he said. “The blood of the martyrs will not go to waste. The terrorists and their facilitators will meet an exemplary fate,” he added.
Earlier, Rescue 1122 spokesperson Bilal Ahmed Faizi stated that 14 ambulances, rescue vehicles, a recovery vehicle and more than 45 rescue personnel were participating in the operation.
District Emergency Officer Noor-ul-Amin was personally supervising the rescue operation, he said, adding that relief activities would continue until the operation was completed. He added that further details would be issued as more information was received.
President Zardari, PM Shehbaz strongly condemn
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif strongly condemned the bomb blast in Old Police Lines, Kohat, Radio Pakistan reported on Friday.
In separate messages, they expressed deep grief and sorrow over the injuries suffered by several people in the blast.
The president said that the complete elimination of Fitna-al-Khawarij and terrorists operating with foreign backing was inevitable for national security.
The prime minister sought a report from the authorities concerned on the blast and directed them to expedite relief operations.

Afridi sought a report on the incident from police authorities and described the attack as a “cowardly act of terrorism” that was “extremely regrettable and unacceptable”.
He directed officials to use all available resources to provide medical assistance to the injured and ensure hospitals had the necessary facilities for their treatment.
The chief minister also ordered arrangements to transfer critically injured people to other hospitals, if required, and called for all aspects of the incident to be examined before a detailed report was submitted.
“Targeting innocent citizens is extremely regrettable and condemnable,” Afridi said. “The cowardly acts of terrorism cannot break the nation’s resolve,” he added.

K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi condemned the terrorist attack in Kohat, saying the province was facing multiple challenges, including terrorism and a protest by doctors.
Speaking to the media, Kundi said the incident in Kohat was deeply tragic and “cannot be condemned enough”. “On one hand, there is terrorism and, on the other, doctors are protesting in the province,” he said, adding that K-P was currently facing several challenges.
The governor criticised the provincial government for marching towards Islamabad while the law and order situation in the province remained precarious. He said the purpose of the march was to secure the release of “a convicted and disqualified person” from prison, but added that marching on Islamabad would not lead to his release.
I strongly condemn the cowardly blast at the Old Police Lines in #Kohat , Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Such acts of terror cannot break the resolve of our people or weaken our determination to defeat terrorism. My prayers are with those injured, and I urge that they receive immediate and…
Kundi urged the provincial government to focus on governance instead of organising a long march or protests. “This is not the time for a long march and protest; it is time to focus on governance,” he said, urging the provincial government to also pay attention to the situation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.
The governor said young people and businesspeople from Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa were promoting the province’s soft image in Punjab, adding that its youth were excelling in every field. He also referred to the regional situation, saying the conflict between Iran and the United States had created a crisis in the region.
Kundi further said the federal government was asking for marriage halls and hotels to be closed as part of conservation measures. “Punjab may close these facilities, but our province is suffering from terrorism and cannot afford this,” he said.
People gather at a damaged mosque following a suicide attack at a police facility in Kohat, Pakistan, September 18, 2026. Photo: Reuters
K-P Information Minister Shafi Jan also strongly condemned the explosion near the old police lines in Kohat, expressing deep sorrow over the deaths reported in the incident.
According to the information minister, initial reports suggested that several civilians were among those killed and injured in the blast, along with five police personnel. Jan said CM Afridi had taken serious notice of the incident and sought a report from the relevant authorities.
He said emergency measures had been imposed at hospitals in Kohat and directed officials to ensure that the injured received the best possible medical treatment. “Targeting innocent civilians is an extremely regrettable and cowardly act,” Jan said.
He said Islam, like other religions, did not permit such cowardly acts and added that terrorist attacks could not weaken the nation's resolve. “Terrorist elements will never succeed in achieving their nefarious objectives,” the minister said.

Meanwhile, K-P Law Minister Aftab Alam visited DHQ Hospital Kohat to meet those injured in the Police Lines mosque blast and inquire about their condition.

He condemned the targeting of innocent civilians, describing it as an inhumane act, and said the terrorists’ “nefarious designs” would not be allowed to succeed.
Alam also appealed to the public to donate blood for the injured, saying timely medical treatment could be facilitated through blood donations.

description: KSE 100 closes at 170 885  benchmark index gains 1 09  on healthy 575 million share volume
content:
KSE-100 closes at 170,885; benchmark index gains 1.09% on healthy 575 million-share volume
The Pakistan Stock Exchange extended Thursday’s rebound on Friday, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index gaining 1,841 points, or 1.09 per cent, to close at 170,885.
Buying stayed firm through the session. The index traded between 169,400 and 171,037. Ready-market volume reached about 575 million shares, with KSE-100 value at Rs13.2 billion. The All-Share Index rose 1,053 points (1.03%) to 103,297, the KSE-30 added 585 points (1.16%) to 50,883, and the KMI-30 gained 2,523 points (1.05%) to 243,139.
Banks were the biggest index driver, contributing 803 points. Cement added 266 points, fertiliser 257 points, exploration & production 129 points and power 80 points, as per KTrade. Top gainers were Fauji Fertiliser (FFC, +225 points), United Bank (UBL, +208), Meezan Bank (MEBL, +142), Lucky Cement (LUCK, +141) and Habib Bank (HBL, +117).
Losers were limited. Packages (PSEL), Nestle Pakistan, Ghandhara Industries (GHNI), Adamjee Insurance and Attock Refinery trimmed the index.
Read: Oil prices fall for third day on hopes of limited Saudi supply disruptions
Volume was concentrated in lower-priced names: Media Times (MDTL) led with 69.7 million shares (+13.2%), followed by WorldCall, Cnergyico, K-Electric and First Capital Securities. By sector, technology stocks were the most traded on the All-Share board (156 million shares), ahead of power, investment banks, refinery and OMCs.
KTrade said the advance was supported by buying in banks, cement, fertiliser, E&P and power. “A decline in oil prices remains a key positive macro trigger for Pakistan,” the brokerage noted, adding that further moderation in crude could ease external-sector pressure and lift sentiment. Near-term direction, it said, still depends on the evolving Middle East situation.
The two-day rebound has taken the KSE-100 back above 170,000 after Thursday’s 1,021-point rise to 169,043. International crude has fallen for a third session as Saudi supply concerns eased, even as regional tensions persist.

title: Ed Sheeran resale ticket prices fall as Macklemore tour fallout continues
description: The drop comes amid continued fallout from Macklemore s departure from the tour over his support for Palestine
content:
The drop comes amid continued fallout from Macklemore's departure from the tour over his support for Palestine
Resale ticket prices for Ed Sheeran's LOOP Tour have declined across most of his upcoming dates, according to ticket-tracking website Ticketdata, as controversy surrounding Macklemore's removal from the tour continues.
Ticketdata showed that nine of Sheeran's next 10 dates recorded price decreases over the three days to September 16.
Resale prices for his Saturday concert in Philadelphia fell 17% over three days and 25% over seven days.
Prices also declined for Sheeran's two shows at Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts, as well as upcoming concerts in Atlanta, Charlotte, Arlington, Hollywood and Tampa.
Indianapolis was the only city among the dates tracked to record a positive three-day price change.
Ed Sheeran pressured to remove Macklemore from tour over 'Free Palestine' comments
Robert Kraft breaks silence on Macklemore’s removal from Ed Sheeran tour
Macklemore says Ed Sheeran told him ‘Free Palestine’ was ‘hurtful to a lot of people’
Ed Sheeran breaks silence after Macklemore is dropped from his tour
The ticket-price movements come amid continued fallout from Macklemore's departure from the tour.
Macklemore said he was removed after speaking about the situation in Gaza and expressing support for Palestinians during concerts at MetLife Stadium.
Robert Kraft, who owns Gillette Stadium, confirmed that Macklemore was blocked from performing at the venue, saying it does not "provide a platform for hate speech".
Sheeran subsequently said the decision was made by his tour promoter following threats from stadium venues. He also said he was "appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine".
The controversy continued when Sheeran's band and three opening acts withdrew from the tour.

title: Klopp wants German team to help reclaim national pride
description: He says he prefers term positive patriotism because national pride could be misunderstood
content:
He says he prefers term positive patriotism because national pride could be misunderstood
Jurgen Klopp said on Thursday that Germany's football team can help ensure "national pride is not entrusted to the wrong people" after a recent far-right AfD election victory.
In a Frankfurt press conference announcing his first squad as Germany manager, the former Liverpool coach referenced a recent state election landslide win by the anti-immigration Alternative for Germany party.
The AfD won almost 44 percent of the vote in the former East German state of Saxony-Anhalt on September 6 and expects strong results in elections Sunday in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
Klopp took over the Germany job in July after the four-time World Cup winners suffered a third straight early elimination at the tournament.
The 59-year-old has often spoke out about social issues during his time as manager of Liverpool, Borussia Dortmund and Mainz.
While not mentioning the AfD by name, Klopp advocated for adopting "positive patriotism", while saying: "I don't want to entrust national pride to the wrong people.
"A crazy amount of things have happened not that long ago. There was a vote which some people probably found OK, but others would have thought 'good heavens, what's going on here?'"
"From the perspective of someone in sport, I'd like to reclaim the flag for myself and for us. When we wave it, I don't want that someone thinks 'what's going on with you?'
"I want that they think you're happy and you understand how lucky you are to be born in this wonderful country or to have moved here and live here."
Topics involving patriotism and nationalism are often sensitive in Germany, a country still at pains to atone for its dark history of Nazi rule, World War II and the Holocaust.
Speaking of national pride, Klopp said he was "not even sure if one can -- or is allowed to -- use that term anymore without it being misunderstood".
"I can be proud of being German and still be open, diverse, kind and friendly."
The coach said it was more important that the country had enough doctors and caregivers, but said football can "foster a sense of community here, allowing us to truly feel the power of sport".
On Thursday, Klopp took the unusual step of naming a huge 44-man squad for four upcoming Nations League matches, despite matchday lists being restricted to 23 players.
"It's very unusual that you've got four games in two weeks with the national team," Klopp said.
"I want to get to know as many players as possible in that time."
Klopp won the Champions League and Premier League during a trophy-laden nine-year stint at Liverpool.

title: Miley Cyrus opens up about final conversation with godmother Dolly Parton before her death
description: In a new interview  Cyrus said their final conversation centred on her newly released 10th album   Bass Persuades
content:
In a new interview, Cyrus said their final conversation centred on her newly released 10th album, 'Bass Persuades'
Miley Cyrus has revealed details of her final conversation with her godmother, Dolly Parton, who died on August 25, 2026 after a brief battle with cancer.
In an Apple Music interview published on Thursday, Cyrus said her final conversation with Parton centred on her newly released 10th album, Bass Persuades.
"I'm just trying to keep myself together, but the time that we talked, which was the last time we would talk, it was actually me telling her about this record because even though we are so different, that's what made us so perfect for each other," Cyrus told interviewer Zane Lowe.
Cyrus also reflected on the influence Parton had on her life and career, particularly during her years on Hannah Montana .
She said Parton's ability to remain authentic while embracing a public persona helped shape her own approach to fame.
Parton also gave Cyrus advice after watching her become emotional while performing "End of the World" on David Letterman's Netflix series.
"Music is escapism. Let them cry. You need to get through it," Parton told her, according to Cyrus.
Cyrus said Parton had encouraged her to perform at the Grammys and had regularly provided guidance throughout her career. "Dolly was just always right about stuff," she said.
Following Parton's death, Cyrus shared a tribute on Instagram, writing: "One of our last conversations was about music and metamorphosis. I will always love her and want to make her proud."
Cyrus also described Parton as one of the older figures who had helped lay the foundation for her career.

title: Championship rivals brace for renewal of bitter feuds
description: Police deploy heightened security as Millwall West Ham and Wolves West Brom derbies return this weekend
content:
Police deploy heightened security as Millwall-West Ham and Wolves-West Brom derbies return this weekend
Police are on red alert as the English Championship braces for the renewal of two bitter feuds when Millwall face West Ham and Wolves meet West Brom this weekend.
Wolves host fourth-placed West Brom in the Black Country derby on Sunday -- two years after their last meeting was marred by a bloody battle in the stands.
Millwall and West Ham have an especially gory history, with one supporter of each club killed in sickening clashes in 1976 and 1986.
Those horrific incidents came at the height of the hooliganism era that blighted English football.
But the enmity, born a century ago in London's docks, has lost none of its ferocity in recent years.
In 2009, a Millwall supporter was stabbed outside West Ham's former home at Upton Park before a stormy League Cup tie that culminated in several pitch invasions, prompting the government's sports minister at the time, Gerry Sutcliffe, to label the incidents "a disgrace to football".
West Ham were fined £115,000 ($153,000) for failing to prevent their fans entering the pitch, while several supporters were convicted of violent disorder.
Separated by just eight miles across the River Thames, the 100th showdown between the Lions and the Irons will play out against a backdrop of high security across south-east London.
Social media has been rife with threats between rival fans in the build-up to Saturday's game.
"We want fans to enjoy the match safely and have worked with both clubs to help this happen," a Metropolitan Police statement said on X.
"A Section 35 dispersal order will be in place, allowing officers to remove anyone causing disorder."
Adding to the tension around the fixture, some Millwall fans will be housed in the same stand as the 1,774 West Ham supporters in a sell-out crowd of around 19,000 at the Den.
Strict segregation will be in place to keep the rivals apart.
Millwall haven't beaten West Ham since 2004 and Lions boss Alex Neil hopes the hostile atmosphere can help his team stun Nuno Espirito Santo's men.
"It should be a brilliant atmosphere. It means a lot to our fans and everybody connected with both clubs," Neil said.
"It'll be interesting to see how West Ham handle the Den and different things like that."
Just 24 hours after Millwall face West Ham, an equally explosive clash will take place in the west midlands.
The first league meeting between Wolves and West Brom in five years comes after a 2024 FA Cup tie was scarred by crowd trouble.
Wolves' 2-0 win at The Hawthorns two years ago was halted for 38 minutes after fans clashed in the stands, with police assaulted, missiles thrown and flares set off.
There were 43 arrests, with 12 sentenced and five given permanent bans.
In a joint statement, Wolves and Albion said supporters can "expect enhanced stewarding, policing, robust ticketing controls and additional safety measures" on Sunday.
Wolves and Albion emphasised the punishments dished out for the 2024 clashes show "disorder, violence and criminal behaviour carry significant consequences and will continue to be dealt with robustly".
All four clubs will hope the weekend's derbies pass off far more peacefully than some of their previous encounters.

title: Athletes  can t take it any more  as Asian Games issues mount
description: Athletes face lengthy airport delays  accommodation issues and transport problems ahead of Saturday   s opening
content:
Athletes face lengthy airport delays, accommodation issues and transport problems ahead of Saturday’s opening
The Asian Games in Japan were on Friday facing more accusations of poor organisation with a world champion gymnast "totally exhausted", the public drafted in to rescue stranded athletes and South Korea lodging a complaint about a Japanese warlord.
The continent's premier sporting spectacle opens in Nagoya and Aichi prefecture on Saturday, but the build-up has been soured by several issues.
That includes a shortage of rooms for the more than 17,000 athletes and officials -- a bigger number than the Olympics.
Some teams have also criticised the quality of the accommodation, including beds that are too short.
To save money there is no athletes' village, organisers instead putting competitors in hotels, temporary cabins and on a cruise ship.
Organisers say the accommodation is safe, cost-effective and comfortable.
Chinese gymnast Zhang Boheng, who won two silver medals at the Paris Olympics and has two world championship titles to his name, said he and some of his team-mates were left waiting for six hours after landing on Wednesday.
"I'm totally exhausted," he said in a video published Thursday and shared widely on Chinese social media.
"I didn't expect that after breakfast at 7:00 am the next time I could eat would be close to 7:00 pm," the 26-year-old said.
He said the wait was caused by registration and paperwork, before heading to the cruise ship where 4,000 Games participants will be housed in Nagoya's port area.
But when they arrived at the ship, he said heavy rain prevented them from boarding.
"A whole day was basically wasted like this," added Zhang.
"In the end we really couldn't take it any more so we decided to book rooms at a hotel to rest."
The video has since been taken down but Chinese state media said that other Chinese athletes also faced travel delays upon arrival.
Beijing's consulate in Nagoya contacted Chinese citizens in the area to give the badminton team lifts after issues with a shuttle bus and a shortage of public transport tickets, Xinhua reported.
Chinese social media users applauded athletes, including table tennis star Sun Yingsha, for stretching and exercising at the airport.
The hashtag "Asian Games absurd" has since been viewed more than 94 million times on Weibo.
India's team had similar delays at the airport.
"There was an issue in getting accreditation for athletes at the airport during immigration. There were long queues with a lot of other nations there," India's chef de mission and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) treasurer Sahdev Yadav told AFP.
"But these things happen and we have got everything sorted.
He added: "These are all teething problems and our focus is now on performance."
South Korea's Yonhap news agency reported that some of the country's athletes waited at the airport for more than five hours on Thursday.
"We are aware of the situation including reports that athletes have had to wait for hours and we are doing our best to handle it," a Korean Sport and Olympic Committee (KSOC) official told AFP.
Also on Friday, the KSOC said it had filed a complaint with Games organisers for featuring a Japanese warlord at a welcoming ceremony.
The event on Tuesday included a person dressed as Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who led Japan's invasions of Korea in 1592-1598, and the ceremony prompted a backlash in South Korea.
Historical issues are sensitive between South Korea and Japan, with Hideyoshi's invasion a significant episode in Korean history and Korea under Japanese colonial rule from 1910 to 1945.
There was no immediate response from the Olympic Council of Asia or the local organising committee.

title: Nadia Afgan on breaking old drama formulas and finding her place with a new generation
description: Actor discusses changing audience habits  mentoring younger stars and how she got into the entertainment industry
content:
Actor discusses changing audience habits, mentoring younger stars and how she got into the entertainment industry
Actor Nadia Afgan discussed the changing landscape of Pakistan’s entertainment industry, her evolving relationship with younger actors and the unlikely turn of events that launched her career decades ago during her appearnce on Good Morning Pakistan recently.
Reflecting on how much the industry has changed, Afgan said production houses could no longer afford to become complacent as audiences gained more ways to consume entertainment.
“Production houses have become complacent. There are so many more options for viewers now, between digital and social media, that we need to up our game instead of assuming we're still the only place people will come for entertainment,” she said.
For Afgan, her upcoming serial Hey Fam represents the kind of shift she believes the industry needs. The project moves away from familiar family-drama formulas, instead placing a largely new cast at the centre of a story shaped around the realities of the digital generation.
“It takes guts to walk away from the usual saas-bahu formula and put your trust in a fresh story with a cast of mostly new actors,” she said, praising the production for backing untested talent both in front of and behind the camera. The serial is being directed by Zeeshan Ansari, who is making his debut as a serial director.
Her conversation also touched on a subject that extends beyond the entertainment industry: how older generations communicate with younger people.
“One of the biggest mistakes we make as elders is jumping straight to advice or a lecture the moment a young person shares something with us, instead of just listening,” she said. “You have to hear them out completely first, and then ask if they even want your advice. That's what actually builds trust.”
That approach has also shaped the way she interacts with younger actors. Afgan described taking on a mentoring role similar to the one her own mentor, Samina Ahmed, once played in her life, while being mindful of whether the other person actually wants guidance.
“I watch whether a young actor is open to guidance. If they seem receptive, I'll offer it. If not, I step back, because I don't want them to feel overwhelmed,” she explained. “I'd rather be a friend than just a senior colleague; that's what makes them comfortable enough to share what's really on their mind.”
Afgan acknowledged that the world younger actors are entering is markedly different from the one her generation grew up in. Traditional career paths and traditional media have given way to an environment dominated by digital platforms, metrics and follower counts.
“My generation was about traditional career paths and traditional media. Now everything is digital; it's all about metrics and followers,” she said, admitting with a laugh that she is “a bit late” to keeping up with new apps herself.
While she credited younger people with being sharper and more tech-savvy than her generation, Afgan also pointed to the darker side of growing up online. The internet, she noted, exposes young people to material that previous generations were far more likely to encounter with some form of filtering.
“They're smart, they're tech-savvy, but they're also absorbing a very bad world online without any filter,” she said. “You can't control them the way parents used to. What they need from us is soft guidance, not restriction.”
For Afgan, that generational shift inevitably finds its way into storytelling as well. She argued that television dramas need to reflect the experiences of the audiences watching them rather than relying indefinitely on familiar premises.
“Dramas used to open with a simple romance or a college story. Now our stories need to reflect what young people are actually going through; that's what we're trying to do with Hey Fam ,” she said.
Afgan also looked back at the beginnings of a career that, in many ways, started without a carefully laid-out plan. Her first opportunity came while she was studying at Punjab University, where her Head of Department, Shahnawaz Zaidi, was connected to director Ayyub Khawar.
“Zaidi sahab was acting in it too, and he knew I was into theatre at university, so he suggested me for the role of his daughter,” she recalled. “I said yes right away, even though the PTV set was quite intimidating for me at the time.”
Her breakthrough, however, came through an even more unexpected opportunity. Through friends at NCA, Afgan was asked to step into a music video for Jawad Ahmad’s O Kehndi Aay Saiyan .
“The girl who was supposed to model for it didn't show up, and I happened to be around, so I said I'd do it,” she said. “That song became huge. It's genuinely my claim to fame; it's what opened the door for my drama career, including Shashlik .”
Years later, Hey Fam finds Afgan on the other side of that journey, working on a project that deliberately moves away from the familiar tropes that have long dominated television.

title: India  Sri Lanka storm into Asian Games women cricket semis
description: India to face Bangladesh  while Sri Lanka take on Pakistan in Sunday   s semi finals
content:
India to face Bangladesh, while Sri Lanka take on Pakistan in Sunday’s semi-finals
India women on Friday demolished Japan women by eight wickets in their Asian Games event quarter-final, racing to their modest target in just five overs to book their place in the semi-finals in Nisshin.
Chasing 58 for victory after Japan were bowled out for 57 in 19.5 overs, India made light work of the chase as opener Shafali Verma smashed an unbeaten 40 from only 15 balls.
Verma struck six fours and two sixes in a breathtaking assault.
Richa Ghosh added an unbeaten 12 from six balls, including two fours, as India reached 59 for two with 90 balls to spare.
Japan made a cautious start after being sent in to bat and struggled to build momentum against India's disciplined attack.
Ayaka Kato-Stafford top-scored for Japan with 25 from 47 balls, but the innings never gathered pace. Haruna Iwasaki contributed 10 while the remaining batters failed to reach double figures.
India's Shree Charani was the standout bowler, taking four wickets for ten runs from her four overs. Shafali also made an impact with the ball, claiming two wickets for 13 runs, while Deepti Sharma and Shreyanka Patil took one each.
Japan lost wickets regularly after reaching 24 for two, slipping to 46 for four before collapsing to 57 all out in the final over.
Earlier in the third quarter-final at the same venue Sri Lanka demolished Malaysia by 86 runs thanks to a blistering fifty from captain Chamari Athapaththu.
Athapaththu smashed 63 from 37 balls, including seven fours and three sixes, as Sri Lanka posted 160 for four after electing to bat.
Kavisha Dilhari added an unbeaten 44 from 27 balls, while Harshitha Samarawickrama struck 25 from 18 to keep the scoreboard moving.
Malaysia struggled in reply, finishing at 74 for seven from their 20 overs. Winifred Duraisingam top-scored with 28 from 47 balls, while Mahirah Izzati Ismail made 24.
Sri Lanka's bowlers kept Malaysia under constant pressure, with Dilhari taking two wickets for four runs and Mithali Ayodhya claiming two for 15. Athapaththu also chipped in with two wickets for three runs.

title: ICC eyes China in bid to expand cricket
description: The governing body has invested  1 5 million in China over five years to build the sport
content:
The governing body has invested $1.5 million in China over five years to build the sport
China is emerging as a key target for growth as the International Cricket Council (ICC) seeks new fans worldwide, its chief executive says.
While South Asia accounts for about 90 percent of cricket's billion-plus fans, the ICC is seeking to expand the sport's fan base by 500 million and sees China's 1.4 billion people as a potentially huge audience -- helped by the steady progress of its women's team.
"The continued success of their women's team has provided a major boost to cricket in the country," ICC chief executive Sanjog Gupta told AFP.
China became a focus market after hosting cricket at the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou and through the progress of its women's national team, which has climbed 10 places in the world rankings over the past two years.
There is still far to go, however. In the ICC T20 rankings the women are ranked a modest 36th, while the men languish in 92nd place.
The women were also knocked out of the Asian Games on Thursday without a ball being bowled, two days before the opening ceremony.
A sodden outfield caused by days of rain in Nagoya, Japan, prevented any play from taking place in China's morning quarter-final against Bangladesh, who went through to the semi-finals by virtue of being the higher.
Still, China is one of several markets the ICC sees as crucial to broadening cricket's appeal beyond its traditional strongholds of South Asia, England, and Australia.
The ICC has spent $1.5 million in China to boost the sport over the past five years.
The country now has three top-level cricket venues, including a new 1,500-seat stadium in Taicang expected to host domestic and international matches and provide a training base for the national teams.
The ICC has begun testing the appetite for the sport in China.
Some women's T20 World Cup matches were broadcast in Mandarin, and the final week of the 2026 men's T20 World Cup generated 4.4 million video views in China.
The country's potential emergence is particularly significant for the ICC because, unlike several newer cricket nations, its men's and women's teams are made up largely of homegrown players rather than players from South Asian communities.
Indonesia, a country of around 280 million people, has also been identified as a market with growth potential. Its men's team T20 ranking is 63rd, and the women's team, 23rd.
"If even segments of the population in China and Indonesia start engaging with the sport, then they could power the next leap in the scale of cricket's fandom," Gupta said.
"It can play a significant role in the sport's ambition to add 500 million fans to its global fan base, which is the ICC chair's stated ambition."
The ICC believes cricket's return to the Olympics at the 2028 Los Angeles Games could provide another boost, with men's and women's T20 tournaments set to award medals for the first time since the sport's lone previous appearance in 1900.
The ICC's push into new markets has paid off elsewhere.
Italy offered a glimpse of the potential of another non-traditional market when it made its men's T20 World Cup debut earlier this year, beating Nepal and pushing England close.
The ICC push has the backing of the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC), custodian of the game's laws.
"MCC is very pleased to be sending a women's team for an overseas tour of China in 2027," MCC director of cricket and operations Rob Lynch told AFP.
"We see this tour as a huge opportunity to be able to grow the game in China," he added.

title: Manchester United misery puts Carrick under pressure
description: The Red Devils head to Fulham after two straight defeats in all competition
content:
The Red Devils head to Fulham after two straight defeats in all competition
Michael Carrick needs a win at Fulham to ease the mounting pressure on troubled Manchester United while Tottenham are desperate for their first Premier League goal of the season against fellow strugglers Aston Villa.
At the top end of the table, Arsenal and Manchester City aim to maintain their perfect records going into the international break.
AFP Sport looks at three talking points ahead of this weekend's action:
Defiant Carrick confident of Man Utd revival
As Carrick trudged towards the tunnel at Old Trafford after Manchester United's demoralising collapse against Brighton, the rumble of discontent grew louder with each footstep.
United had just lost a home game after holding a two-goal lead for the first time in 50 years and fans at the Stretford End were venting their frustration, with jeers and abuse aimed at Carrick and his players.
The United manager acknowledged Wednesday's 3-2 loss to Brighton in the League Cup third round was unacceptable as he took responsibility for their third defeat in six games this season.
But Carrick's willingness to shoulder the blame will not save him from even greater scrutiny and criticism if United lose at Fulham on Sunday.
United have won just once in four league games and have lost their past two matches in all competitions.
They cannot afford another setback against a Fulham side languishing in the relegation zone and who are yet to win in the league this season.
"Of course we can turn it around. We've got some really good players and it feels bad at the moment because we haven't had a great week, or two or three weeks," Carrick said.
"It's all about what you do next and dealing with the moments, and the ups and downs."
Without a win or even a goal in the league this season, Roberto De Zerbi's expensively rebuilt Tottenham are back in familiar territory.
Spurs have finished one place above the relegation zone in each of the past two seasons -- narrowly avoiding the dreaded drop on the final day of the 2025/26 campaign.
De Zerbi spent more than £300 million ($400 million) in the close season in a bid to ensure the north Londoners would be more competitive.
Instead, they are once again marooned in 17th place, on just two points, ahead of Aston Villa's visit on Saturday.
Beaten 3-1 at Liverpool in the League Cup third round in midweek, Tottenham have already shown the anxious, error-strewn form that condemned them to a relegation battle last season.
Losing to Villa -- who have made an even worse start, with only one point from four games -- would leave Spurs with a sinking feeling again.
Trying to remain positive, Tottenham forward Omar Marmoush said: "These moments build the mentality and the team together. We are all one big family and we push together."
Arsenal have made a perfect start to their bid for the club's first back-to-back titles since the 1930s, with Manchester City emerging as their main rivals after their own flawless run.
Arsenal sit top of the table with four successive wins and City are just behind them on goal difference.
It is little surprise to see the Gunners in pole position given their dominant march to the title last season.
But City's early success is more eye-opening in the first campaign of the post-Pep Guardiola era.
Guardiola's successor Enzo Maresca bolstered his approval rating among City fans by masterminding a 1-0 win at Manchester United last weekend, decided by a goal that should have been ruled out for offside.
"For sure the fans are happy and that's the only thing I care about," Maresca said.
Arsenal, who travel to Brighton on Saturday and City, who host Sunderland on Sunday, will expect to maintain their blistering form heading into the international break.

title: North Korea warns of    more offensive    response to US led military drills
description: Pyongyang to strengthen nuclear deterrence as South Korean president says Seoul should do    utmost    for US dialogue
content:
Pyongyang to strengthen nuclear deterrence as South Korean president says Seoul should do ‘utmost’ for US dialogue
North Korea’s Kim Yo Jong on Friday warned of a stronger response to United States-led multinational military exercises in the Asia-Pacific, saying Pyongyang would continue strengthening its nuclear deterrence.
Kim, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and a senior ruling Workers’ Party official, accused Washington of being the “main source” of worsening tensions on the Korean Peninsula and across the region, according to a statement carried by the state-run Korean Central News Agency ( KCNA ).
She singled out Pacific Vanguard 2026, a multinational naval exercise near Guam involving the US, South Korea, Japan, and other countries.
Kim called the exercise a threatening “war game” and accused Washington of seeking to expand its military influence through alliances in the Asia-Pacific.
She also criticised growing US-Japan-South Korea military cooperation , claiming North Korea was its primary target.
Read: North Korea says hostile US policy unchanged, vows to strengthen nuclear force
“The present situation ... stresses the need to break records in our responsive action, proportional or more offensive in its nature,” Kim said.
She added there would be “never ever change” in North Korea’s course of strengthening its nuclear deterrence and warned Pyongyang could “mobilise all means available” if its sovereignty or security were seriously threatened.
The warning came as South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said Friday that Seoul should make every effort to facilitate renewed dialogue between North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and US President Donald Trump, according to Seoul-based Yonhap News Agency .
“The possibility cannot be ruled out,” Lee told a televised news conference, adding Seoul should do its “utmost” to help make such talks happen. Lee said renewed North Korea-US dialogue could become an important stepping stone toward restarting inter-Korean talks and promoting peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula.

title: FA urges Infantino to release documents
description: Hewitt calls for full disclosure of FIFA documents ahead of its October Council meeting
content:
Hewitt calls for full disclosure of FIFA documents ahead of its October Council meeting
The chair of the English Football Association has called on FIFA president Gianni Infantino to release all the documentation relating to the abandoned plan to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors.
Infantino's proposal was short-lived after a fierce backlash from across the sport, with European governing body UEFA threatening to boycott all FIFA competitions until it was shelved.
FA chair Debbie Hewitt, who is also a FIFA vice-president and a member of the FIFA Council, has written to Infantino asking for full disclosure of all information relating to the scheme before the FIFA Council next meets on October 15.
Hewitt has also called for the release of documents relating to the decision to suspend a ban handed to United States striker Folarin Balogun during the World Cup, which followed a phone call from US President Donald Trump to Infantino.
Infantino apologised over the process in regard to the private investor plan in August and a statement from FIFA's management board pledged there would be a review but has not at any stage confirmed who is undertaking that investigation.
UEFA said it has "lost confidence" in Infantino and has made legal applications in the US court system seeking disclosure of documents related to the private investor plan.
UEFA has also committed to identifying a credible candidate to run against Infantino at the FIFA Congress in March, with November 18 the deadline for candidates to be submitted.
Infantino confirmed earlier this month his intention to seek re-election.

title: England seal series with Cardiff blitz
description: Dawson spins Sri Lanka into trouble before Banton   s 24 ball fifty powers six wicket chase
content:
Dawson spins Sri Lanka into trouble before Banton’s 24-ball fifty powers six-wicket chase
England stormed to a six-wicket victory over Sri Lanka in the second T20I at Sophia Gardens on Thursday, taking an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series with 47 balls to spare.
After opting to field, England restricted Sri Lanka to 145 for nine before racing to 146 for four in just 12.1 overs, completing another emphatic chase and leaving Sri Lanka with only one match remaining to avoid a series whitewash.
Liam Dawson was at the heart of England’s performance, claiming three wickets for 32 runs and taking two catches to earn Player of the Match honours.
Sri Lanka made a flying start through Pathum Nissanka and Lahiru Udara, who put on 56 for the opening wicket. Nissanka struck 37 from 21 balls, including four fours and a six, before Jamie Overton ended the partnership.
Dawson then seized control. The left-arm spinner dismissed Udara for 21 and removed Kamil Mishara without scoring in successive deliveries, before returning later to send Dasun Shanaka back for four. Sri Lanka slipped from 56 for one to 56 for two and then struggled to build sustained momentum.
Captain Charith Asalanka offered resistance with 31 from 31 balls, while Wanindu Hasaranga struck 27 from 22. But England's bowlers kept taking wickets at crucial moments. Overton finished with two for 23, while Jofra Archer also claimed two wickets.
Sri Lanka managed 145 for nine, a total that looked vulnerable on a good Cardiff surface.
England's response was immediate. Jos Buttler and Aneurin Donald raced to a 51-run opening stand, reaching the 50 mark in only 27 balls. Buttler hammered 30 from 16 balls before Chameera dismissed him, while Donald fell for 21.
Harry Brook briefly turned the chase into a fireworks display, smashing 23 from just eight deliveries with three sixes. Hasaranga eventually removed the England captain, but Sri Lanka could not stem the flow.
Tom Banton took over. The right-hander produced a blistering unbeaten 52 from 24 balls, striking two fours and four sixes. He reached his fifty from only 24 deliveries and finished the contest with a boundary-laden assault that left Sri Lanka's attack scrambling for answers.
Jordan Cox added 12 from seven before falling with England needing only 10 runs. Banton remained unbeaten alongside Will Jacks, who hit the winning runs as England reached 146 for four after 12.1 overs.
England's victory was built on disciplined bowling followed by an extraordinary batting surge. Sri Lanka, meanwhile, were left to rue another promising start that failed to translate into a competitive total.
With England now 2-0 ahead in the three-match series, the final T20I will be Sri Lanka's last opportunity to salvage a result from the tour's shortest format.

title: Hania Aamir slams online culture of turning women s bodies into  punchlines
description: Actor urges creators and audiences to stop turning women s appearances and personal lives into online content
content:
Actor urges creators and audiences to stop turning women's appearances and personal lives into online content
Hania Aamir has spoken out against the growing trend of women being trolled over their bodies, appearances and age, calling out creators who disguise misogyny as commentary.
The actor took to Instagram to share a lengthy note aimed at the culture of turning women’s appearances and personal lives into online content.
“In 2026, using women's bodies, faces, appearances, age and personal lives as a punchline is ridiculous,” she wrote, arguing that labelling such remarks as an opinion or a joke did not excuse them. “And 'it's my take' is not a free pass. Neither is calling it humour.”
Aamir drew a clear distinction between criticism and cruelty. “You can have a take. You can be critical. You can be funny,” she wrote, “but there is a very clear line between commentary and turning a woman's existence into content.”
She also pointed to the influence wielded by public figures and content creators, warning that their words could shape how audiences viewed such behaviour.
“Words have consequences beyond the moment they are said. Especially when they come from people with large platforms,” she wrote. “You are not speaking into a void. You are shaping what other people think is normal, funny and acceptable.”
Aamir extended that responsibility to audiences as well, arguing that likes, views and shares could end up rewarding the very content people claimed to oppose. “We cannot keep demanding better from society while simultaneously rewarding the very behaviour we claim to be against,” she said.
Her central message was direct: “Women are not public property. Their bodies are not public commentary. Their faces are not public discourse. And honestly, we should have evolved past this by now.”
She closed by urging people to stop engaging with such content altogether. “Stop giving this kind of content your attention. Stop giving it reach. Stop making a spectacle out of women and calling it entertainment,” she wrote, before adding, “We can do better than this.”
Aamir's note lands amid a run of Pakistani women in entertainment describing similar scrutiny in their own words.
Actor Mamya Shajaffar recently told BBC Urdu that public judgment over a woman's clothing could turn dangerous, recalling how a Berlin red carpet appearance drew commentary on her outfit rather than her work a contrast, she said, to how global stars are covered at the same events.
"When what you have worn becomes an answerable thing and, based on this, whether or not you should live, die, be harassed, [or] raped," she said, "it changes a lot in you."
TV host Anoushey Ashraf also raised her voice in a since-widely-shared Instagram post, describing what she called a constant "audit" of her faith and lifestyle. "Too Muslim for some. Not Muslim enough for others," she wrote, asking her followers, "Can a woman just be a woman without everyone conducting an audit?"

title: Sixes  silence and a record rush
description: Abhishek Sharma   s 34 ball blitz powers India past Afghanistan as hosts complete 3 0 T20I sweep
content:
Abhishek Sharma’s 34-ball blitz powers India past Afghanistan as hosts complete 3-0 T20I sweep
Abhishek Sharma turned the third Twenty20 international into a personal highlight reel on Thursday, smashing a record-laden 108 from 34 balls as India completed a 3-0 series sweep over Afghanistan with a 127-run victory.
Abhishek reached his hundred from 30 balls, the fastest T20I century against a full-member nation and the third-fastest overall, after punishing the Afghanistan attack with 11 sixes and nine fours.
His 100 runs in boundaries alone also gave him the highest percentage of boundary runs in a T20I innings, adding another landmark to a performance that had Delhi's crowd roaring from the outset.
India raced to 100 in the powerplay, their highest score in the first six overs in T20Is, before eventually posting 221 for seven.
Sanju Samson provided the supporting act with a second successive half-century, scoring 56, while Abhishek's assault ensured India had enough runs in the bank when Afghanistan's bowlers found their rhythm with reverse swing.
Abhishek opened his account with an extra-cover drive off Fazalhaq Farooqi before repeatedly punishing anything fractionally short or overpitched. Mohammad Nabi bore the brunt of the onslaught, while even Afghanistan's premier spinner Rashid Khan was charged and lofted over the boundary.
Abhishek reached his fifty in just 16 balls and his century in the ninth over before celebrating in a meditation pose, a gesture associated with his mentor Yuvraj Singh.
Rashid eventually ended the assault, deceiving Abhishek with a wrong'un. The spinner then ran out Tilak Varma and later took a superb catch to dismiss Samson.
India's scoring slowed sharply thereafter as Afghanistan's seamers found their yorkers with the reversing ball. Only 37 runs came in the final five overs, but India's explosive start had already put the match beyond Afghanistan's reach.
Afghanistan, who had struggled to turn promising starts into substantial totals throughout the series, collapsed for 94 in 15.5 overs.
Axar Patel struck twice early, dismissing Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Sediqullah Atal, while Jasprit Bumrah produced a trademark 143 kph yorker to bowl Darwish Rasooli.
Yash Thakur claimed his first wicket of the series when Ibrahim Zadran picked out a fielder, but Nitish Kumar Reddy provided the decisive burst, taking three wickets in an over.
Reddy finished the series with six wickets, the most by any bowler, while Axar conceded only 64 runs in 11 overs for four wickets.

The 17-year-old struck twice on debut in a 5-0 home win
Floyd Samba enjoyed a dream Manchester City debut as the 17-year-old struck twice in a 5-0 thrashing of Norwich to set up a League Cup last 16 meeting against Brighton.
Samba was one of 10 changes Enzo Maresca made to the side that won a dramatic derby against Manchester United with 10 men on Sunday and the 17-year-old made his case for more minutes going forward.
"To get a debut like that is mind blowing. I couldn't believe it myself," said Samba, the son of former Blackburn and QPR defender Chris Samba.
"But that's just the beginning, I've got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut."
Brazilian Allan also struck on his first outing since a £34 million ($46 million) move from Palmeiras, while Rayan Cherki slotted home City's second in characteristically cool fashion.
Norwich also made nine changes with their focus on trying to achieve promotion from the Championship and were completely outclassed even by City's second string.
Samba made sure his debut was one to remember as he stooped to head in Allan's cross after Daniel Grimshaw flapped at a cross.
Ayyoub Bouaddi was given his first Etihad start following a 100 million euro (£86 million) arrival from Lille and marked it with an assist for Cherki to race clear and steer beyond the onrushing Grimshaw.
Amid City's major moves for Bouaddi, Enzo Fernandez, Elliott Anderson and Iliman Ndiaye, Allan's signing was largely overlooked.
But he showed his potential with a fine individual jinking run and finish to fire into the far corner on 48 minutes.
Just moments later Samba made the most of some more slack Norwich defending to curl brilliantly into the far corner.
Another of City's talented crop of teenagers rounded off the scoring when Ryan McAidoo stroked in late on.
Victory extended Maresca's perfect start as Pep Guardiola's successor at City to six consecutive wins across three competitions.

title: As Iran war grinds on  Trump to face skeptical world leaders at UN
description: Houthi advances  Gulf doubts  Iran s defiance test Trump s claims of victory ahead of midterms
content:
Houthi advances, Gulf doubts, Iran's defiance test Trump's claims of victory ahead of midterms
When President Donald Trump addressed the United Nations a year ago, he touted the United States' bombing of Iran’s nuclear sites just months earlier as "totally obliterating everything" and said he had brought peace between Israel and Iran.
Returning to the world body on Tuesday, Trump will face a deeply skeptical audience increasingly rattled by six months of war between US forces and an emboldened Iran , growing regional instability and a nuclear threat that has not disappeared despite his claims.
Though battered militarily and economically, Tehran has remained defiant, obstructing oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and in recent days gaining new leverage as its Houthi allies in Yemen tighten their grip on a Red Sea chokepoint, further spiking global energy prices.
The lightning advance by the Houthis has put Trump in an ever-tighter bind over the unpopular conflict, dealt a blow to US ally Saudi Arabia and exposed the limits of Washington’s ability to protect its regional partners.
Most European and Asian allies have spurned Trump's demands for assistance in a conflict he launched without consulting them and which has had damaging fallout for their economies.
And with US gasoline prices high and his approval ratings low , Trump could pay a price in November’s midterm elections when his Republican Party’s control of Congress is at risk .
Read: Fighting, displacement in Yemen deepen humanitarian crisis along its Red Sea coast
“We are seeing what happens when a president launches a war of choice without anticipating the unintended consequences,” said Aaron David Miller, a former adviser on Middle East policy to Republican and Democratic administrations.
In Trump’s speech to the annual gathering of heads of state and government in New York, he is likely again to frame as a victory a military campaign he promised would be over in weeks. The conflict has instead hardened into an uneasy stalemate that has failed to achieve Trump’s shifting goals while depleting the Pentagon's missile stockpiles .
Trump’s problems have only deepened since the Houthis overcame Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces, sweeping down the Red Sea coast and seizing islands at the mouth of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait , a crucial shipping corridor that allows Iran to further threaten global oil supplies.
In response to Reuters ' questions, a senior Trump administration official said the US is focused on security interests such as ensuring freedom of navigation in the Red Sea "while empowering our regional partners to take the lead in managing and resolving regional security challenges."
Iran took up only a small portion of Trump’s speech at last year's United Nations General Assembly. He recounted how, three months before, he had sent B-2 bombers to drop 30,000-pound bombs that “demolished” Tehran’s uranium enrichment capacity. However, experts determined the strikes had only seriously set back the program.
“No other country on Earth could have done what we did,” Trump said.
The US president – who campaigned on a vow to avoid foreign military entanglements - also presented himself as a peacemaker, repeating claims to have ended conflicts around the world, including a 12-day war between Israel and Iran in 2025, and again insisted he should receive the Nobel Peace Prize.
Events since then stand in contrast to his remarks.
Trump joined Israel in striking Iran on February 28, citing what he said was an imminent nuclear threat to the US. Experts have disputed his claim that Iran was close to developing a nuclear weapon, which Tehran has always denied seeking. But Trump underestimated Iran’s resilience, analysts say. Despite airstrikes that killed many of Iran’s top leaders , it has hit back at Gulf neighbours and the US bases they host.
Read More: Gulf on knife edge as Saudis, Houthis trade blows
At the same time, Iran has retained a stockpile of near-weapons-grade highly enriched uranium believed buried by the US strikes in June 2025.
White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said Trump alone had “possessed the courage” to confront Iran over its nuclear program, that he had achieved all his objectives and Iran's economy was being crippled by stepped-up sanctions and a US maritime blockade.
Trump, meanwhile, has rebuffed Saudi pleas for direct military intervention against the Houthis, who agreed to a ceasefire with the US last year. This has dented confidence about US security guarantees among Gulf states, whose doubts had already been fed by Trump’s decision to go to war over their objections, analysts say.
He plans to meet Gulf leaders on the UN sidelines next week, Axios reported.
The dilemma for Trump is that while the US can ill afford to have the Houthis close a second major shipping corridor, he is reluctant to undertake a dangerous new mission for a US military stretched by the fighting against Iran.
US officials met the Houthis last weekend in Oman, where the group said that while it was targeting Saudi shipping it had no intention of attacking American vessels, according to five people familiar with the matter.
“The US clearly has (military) capacity challenges but even so the cost of inaction here is likely to intensify tensions among Gulf allies,” said Jonathan Panikoff, a former deputy national intelligence officer on the Middle East.
Also Read: How Yemen's Houthis went from a small mountain militia to a big regional threat
The Houthis’ sudden re-emergence as a regional threat has further complicated Trump’s efforts to find a way out of the conflict.
With the war grinding on in a seventh month, the US is mired in a battle of attrition while Trump tries to intensify economic pressure on Tehran.
Trump, who has offered shifting timelines, told reporters on Wednesday that “hopefully we are towards the end.”
But analysts warn that the conflict is likely to drag on well past the midterm elections. “Iran isn’t about to let him off the hook here while they have so much leverage to damage him in the midterms and make him a lame duck,” Brett Erickson, a geopolitical analyst and managing principal at Obsidian Risk Advisors, wrote on X.

title: Juventus  Palace cruise to Europa League wins
description: Italian giants thrash NEC 5 0 as Gonzalez  Alajbegovic and Woltemade score
content:
Italian giants thrash NEC 5-0 as Gonzalez, Alajbegovic and Woltemade score
Juventus began their quest for Europa League glory with a 5-0 thrashing of NEC Nijmegen, while Bournemouth secured an impressive victory at Real Sociedad on their European debut on Thursday.
Crystal Palace were 4-0 winners over Lech Poznan, but Celtic suffered another European embarassment as the Scottish champions were beaten 3-1 at home by Ferencvaros.
Juventus expect to be competing among Europe's elite in the Champions League, but the failure to qualify last season has at least allowed them the chance to end a 30-year wait for a continental trophy.
The Italian giants were far too strong for their Dutch visitors in Turin as Nico Gonzalez, Kerim Alajbegovic and Nick Woltemade, with his first goal since joining on loan from Newcastle, made it 3-0 before half-time.
Zeki Celik and Randal Kolo Muani rounded off the scoring after the break as Juventus made a better start than rivals AC Milan, who lost 2-0 to Benfica in the pick of Wednesday's Europa League action.
Bournemouth had a dream start to their first ever European adventure with a 2-1 win in San Sebastian.
Justin Kluivert opened the scoring before Rayan headed in at the back post to put the Cherries 2-0 up inside 20 minutes.
Blowing leads has been a repeat occurence for Marco Rose's team in the early weeks of the season.
Rose is yet to taste victory in the Premier League despite Bournemouth going ahead in all four matches so far this season.
"It's a brilliant win in our first European game," said Rose. "It's brilliant for the club and the 2,000 fans from Bournemouth."
Sergio Gomez's attempted cross flew into the far corner to bring Sociedad back into the contest, but this time Bournemouth held on for a memorable victory.
Conference League winners last season, Palace proved far too strong for Lech Poznan to complete a clean sweep of eight victories for the English sides in Champions and Europa League action so far this season.
Yeremy Pino pounced on a calamitous Poznan throw-in to open the scoring at Selhurst Park.
Chris Richards added a second before Jørgen Strand Larsen's penalty made it 3-0 and Eddie Nketiah rounded off the scoring.
Just weeks on from crashing out of the Champions League qualifiers to Austrian side LASK, despite at one point holding a four-goal lead, Celtic's defensive flaws were exposed once more.
Martin O'Neill's side also suffered a chastening 3-0 defeat to local rivals Rangers last weekend and failed to deliver on their manager's promise to respond.
"It's a huge frustration, obviously, but it's also psychologically quite damning as well," said O'Neill.
"Tonight was I think a European lesson for us in many aspects."
Daniel Arzani's sensational strike on his return to Celtic Park capped a fine night for Ferencvaros after a Liam Scales own goal and Kristoffer Zachariassen put the visitors in front.
Besiktas inflicted a fourth consecutive defeat on Marseille with a 4-1 win in Istanbul.
Vaclav Cerny, Micahel Amir Murillo and Ernest Poku struck in the second half after Keyliane Abdallah had cancelled out Ilhan Fakili's opener for the Turkish side.

title: PM Shehbaz hails record  21 4b foreign exchange reserves
description: Says Pakistan   s return to international capital markets reflect restoration of global confidence in country   s economy
content:
Says Pakistan’s return to international capital markets reflect restoration of global confidence in country’s economy
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday congratulated Pakistan’s economic team after the country’s foreign exchange reserves reached a record $21.4 billion, calling it another historic milestone towards economic stability, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).
Pakistan's total liquid foreign exchange reserves stood at $26.8 billion as of September 11, 2026, the highest combined stock since September 10, 2021. Of the total reserves, the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) held $21.4 billion, a record for the central bank, while commercial banks had $5.4 billion.
According to the statement, PM Shehbaz expressed gratitude to Allah after the SBP’s foreign exchange reserves reached a record high.
The premier said the increase in reserves was a testament to the economic team’s hard work and measures taken in the right direction.
He said improved remittances and services exports, a better current account position and fiscal discipline had played an important role in increasing foreign exchange reserves.
Pakistan’s successful return to international capital markets had also reflected the restoration of global confidence in the country’s economy, the PMO stated.
The increase in foreign exchange reserves would not only strengthen the country’s capacity to meet external payments but also significantly enhance its ability to withstand global economic challenges, the statement added.
Read: Foreign exchange reserves near $29b
A stable economic position would open new avenues for external confidence, investment and sustainable economic growth in the country, PM Shehbaz said.
The prime minister also congratulated Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, the State Bank governor, the government’s economic team and, in particular, overseas Pakistanis for their contribution to this important achievement, the statement added.
The total deposits of $26.8 billion lifted Pakistan's import cover to 3.03 months , the first clear move above the three-month benchmark since August 2020, according to Arif Habib Limited (AHL). The cover is calculated on a three-month average of imports.
The SBP's reserves rose by $3.061 billion during the week ended September 11, 2026, the largest weekly increase since June 27, 2025. The central bank attributed the jump to the receipt of Pakistan's Eurobond proceeds.
The $26.8 billion foreign currency reserves remain just below the $27.1 billion level recorded in September 2021, but the official slice within it is now at an all-time high. That mix leaves a thicker external buffer than Pakistan has held for most of the past five years.
Furthermore, the rupee closed at 277.26, a gain of Rs0.01 against the greenback. On Wednesday, the Pakistani rupee had settled at 277.27.

title: Oil prices fall for third day on hopes of limited Saudi supply disruptions
description: Brent crude futures fall 79 cents  or 0 75   to  104 a barrel
content:
Brent crude futures fall 79 cents, or 0.75%, to $104 a barrel
Oil prices fell for a third day on Friday as easing concerns over Saudi supply ‌disruptions outweighed anxiety about a widening the Middle East conflict amid fresh fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis.
Brent crude futures fell 79 cents, or 0.75%, to $104 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate futures fell 70 cents, or ​0.69%, to $101.20 a barrel. Both benchmarks closed down about 1% on Thursday.
Brent prices are on track for ​their first weekly loss in three, down 0.5%, while WTI is set to gain ⁠1.2%.
Markets largely shrugged off concerns about new threats to supplies even as Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-backed ​Houthis exchanged fresh strikes across their border on Thursday, expanding the Middle East war front.
Earlier this week, prices climbed to close to ​four-month highs as sources said crude loadings at Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export hub of Yanbu had been suspended and Riyadh cancelled some deliveries to Europe after its East-West pipeline was damaged in an attack last week.
However, prices have cooled off ​on reports that Saudi Arabia was seeking to return about half the capacity of its East-West oil pipeline within ​days and the nation was offering more crude cargoes to Asian refiners through ship-to-ship transfers off Oman's port of Sohar.
Read: Oil dip, late buying lift PSX over 1,000 points
"Recent ‌efforts to ⁠restore Saudi export capacity have reduced some of the immediate supply anxiety," said Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insights at Phillip Nova.
Sources that have spoken to Reuters have given varying estimates of how long it will take to reopen the pipeline and return crude flows to normal.
Oil prices, however, are still up over $100 per barrel ​as the markets are waiting ​for evidence of a ⁠clear supply improvement, analysts said.
"The key question is whether physical flows can normalise and what could be the timeline. If we see a sustained improvement in Hormuz ​traffic, some of the geopolitical premium can unwind further," Sachdeva said.
However, transporting oil ​through the region ⁠remains risky.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said a Togo-flagged oil tanker was struck while attempting to make an "illegal passage" through the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, Iranian state media said early on Friday.
The US and Iran have held no ⁠peace talks ​since an interim agreement reached in June collapsed within weeks. The ​war will come up for discussion at the United Nations General Assembly next week, and an Iranian delegation will be able to ​attend, according to the US State Department.

title: Pentagon weighs pulling at least 25 000 US troops from Europe  NBC report
description: Possible drawdown could reach 40 000 troops as Pentagon reviews US military presence on continent
content:
Possible drawdown could reach 40,000 troops as Pentagon reviews US military presence on continent
The Pentagon is considering withdrawing about 25,000 or more US troops from Europe, potentially reducing the American military presence on the continent by nearly one-third, NBC News reported on Thursday.
The proposed drawdown could be even larger, reaching as many as 40,000 troops, NBC reported, citing current and former US and Western officials familiar with the deliberations. About 80,000 US troops are currently stationed in Europe.
No final decisions have been made, according to the report.
Germany, Italy and Spain, which host some of the largest US deployments in Europe, are among the countries likely to be affected.
The options under consideration are part of a six-month Pentagon review of the US military presence in Europe. Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, who heads US European Command and serves as NATO’s supreme allied commander, is expected to provide an initial analysis to Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Friday, NBC reported.
Read: Iran war exposed 'strategic' US munitions shortfalls: Pentagon watchdog
The assessment is expected to outline several options involving aviation, naval and ground forces, as well as the possible repositioning of some US forces toward NATO’s eastern flank.
Hegseth is expected to receive a final recommendation Nov. 6 before any proposal is presented to President Donald Trump, according to the report.
The Trump administration has long argued that European countries should assume greater responsibility for their conventional defence while the US focuses additional military resources on other regions.
The possible reductions have prompted concern among some lawmakers and European governments, which have warned that a rapid withdrawal could affect NATO’s ability to deter Russia.
Read more: Trump orders Pentagon to cut back military exercises with South Korea
NBC also reported that the State Department and Pentagon have differed over the review process.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly intervened in June after the Pentagon prepared to brief NATO defence ministers on potential large-scale reductions.
The report comes as senators have separately called on Rubio to ensure the State Department and US diplomats are fully involved in the force posture review.
