title: Security forces kill seven terrorists in two Balochistan operations  state media
description: Several other terrorists were also reported to have been wounded during the operations
content:
Several others were also reportedly injured during the operation
Security forces killed seven terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan in two separate operations in Balochistan, Radio Pakistan reported on Friday.
“Security forces killed five terrorists in the Fateh Ali area of Panjgur. A large quantity of weapons and ammunition was recovered from the terrorists killed during the operation,” Radio Pakistan quoted security sources as saying.
In a separate intelligence-based operation (IBO) in the Dhadar area of Kachhi district, security forces killed two terrorists. Several others were also reportedly injured during the operation, it added.
The federal government last year officially designated all terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as Fitna al-Hindustan , accusing India of sponsoring a proxy war through the outfits.
The high-tempo intelligence-driven operations are being conducted as part of the ongoing " Radd-ul-Fitna-3 " campaign, which the military's media wing has described as a counterterrorism operation aimed at eliminating Indian proxies.
Seven terrorists of Fitna al Hindustan have been killed by security forces in two separate operations in #Balochistan @OfficialDGISPR #News #RadioPakistan https://t.co/xFh8ltLT6T pic.twitter.com/3ebbqP2zJp
The development came a day after security forces killed three terrorists during an IBO in the Badrang area of Awaran district, according to security sources. The operation was conducted under Operation Radd-ul-Fitna 3 against terrorists affiliated with Fitna al-Hindustan , with weapons and ammunition recovered from those killed.
Read: Security forces kill three terrorists during IBO in Balochistan's Awaran: state media
Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022.
Although Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) has borne the brunt of terrorism, Balochistan has also remained a major target of Indian proxies, which often target civilians and military installations in the province.
In one such attack on the last day of 2025, terrorists targeted innocent civilians in Balochistan’s Gwadar and Kharan districts, where 18 people, including women, children, the elderly and labourers, embraced martyrdom.
Read More: 11 terrorists neutralised in Balochistan
Security forces have continued operations across the provinces against what the state describes as Indian-sponsored terrorists and their proxies, but despite these efforts, the groups have continued to target civilian and defence installations.
On August 21, security forces, in coordination with police, killed 49 terrorists in a series of IBOs across K-P and Balochistan over several days.
In Balochistan, 37 terrorists affiliated with Fitna al-Hindustan were killed in 10 IBOs in Mastung, Mach, Khuzdar and Panjgur districts. The operations had also resulted in the seizure and destruction of weapons, explosives and remote-detonation equipment.

title: Tay Keith cause of death revealed after Grammy nominated producer dies aged 29
description: The producer  whose real name was Brytavious Lakeith Chambers  was found dead aged 29 in Nashville  Tennessee  in June
content:
The producer, whose real name was Brytavious Lakeith Chambers, was found dead aged 29 in Nashville, Tennessee, in June
Grammy-nominated record producer Tay Keith died from an accidental drug overdose, according to multiple media reports citing his autopsy report.
The producer, whose real name was Brytavious Lakeith Chambers, was found dead aged 29 in Nashville, Tennessee, in June.
According to ABC News , which obtained the autopsy report, and Rolling Stone , Chambers died from a combination of "mitragynine, 7-hydroxy mitragynine, mitragynine pseudoindoxyl and ketamine toxicity". TMZ was the first to report his cause of death.
The National Center for Biotechnology Information describes mitragynine as a naturally occurring compound found in the leaves of Mitragyna speciosa , the plant commonly known as kratom.
The centre notes that mitragynine is frequently regarded as having opioid-like effects.
Grammy-nominated producer Tay Keith found dead at home aged 29
Tay Keith dies at 29: Artists and fans pay tribute to Grammy-nominated producer
TMZ also reported that Chambers had mild coronary artery disease. According to ABC News and Rolling Stone , the medical examiner determined that his death was accidental.
Chambers was found on June 18 after Metro Nashville Police conducted a welfare check at an apartment. Authorities said at the time that no foul play was suspected.
The Memphis-born producer worked with major artists including Beyoncé, Cardi B and Drake. He received two Grammy nominations, including for Travis Scott's "Sicko Mode" in 2019 and Drake and 21 Savage's "Rich Flex" in 2024.
Following his death, Drake paid tribute on Instagram, writin, "Endless and eternal gratitude for your spirit and your contributions to this thing that we all love so much…you will be deeply missed."

title: Trump says Iran seeking deal as US considers next move
description: Iran says Togo flagged oil tanker struck while making an    illegal passage    through Strait of Hormuz
author_name: Anadolu Agency, Reuters, AFP, Web Desk
content:
Iran says Togo-flagged oil tanker struck while making an “illegal passage” through Strait of Hormuz
US President Donald Trump says Iran is seeking an agreement with the United States as he considers whether to take additional military action against the country.
In a phone interview with NewsNation , Trump was questioned about his recent remarks that he was weighing whether to “annihilate” Iran.
Asked what he expects Iran to do before he makes a decision, Trump said Tehran is interested in reaching a deal.
“Right now, they want to make a deal,” Trump said, adding that he believes Iran is “losing in every way” both financially and militarily.
“If the deal’s not a correct deal, then I wouldn’t even think about it,” he said. “But right now, they want to make a deal because they’re losing in every way.”
Trump also said the US is in talks with Yemen’s Houthi group, suggesting that they “would like to see if we can make a deal.”
Trump made the remarks as the US-Iran war is in its seventh month. He has recently expressed hope that the conflict is approaching an end, while warning that he is nearing a decision on whether to carry out another major attack against Iran.
USS Boxer (LHD 4) conducts flight operations in the Arabian Sea. Boxer and its embarked Marine Expeditionary Unit continue to enforce the U.S. blockade against Iran. As of Sept. 18, CENTCOM forces have redirected 105 commercial vessels to ensure strict compliance. pic.twitter.com/OQs8ODY0PS
The United States Central Command (US CENTCOM) said it involved to ensure US blockade against Iran via flight operation in Arabian Sea and Strait of Hormuz. In a statement, CENTCOM said it redirected more than 100 commercial ships.
Hormuz disruption threatens global trade
Global trade is facing its worst disruption in 80 years as supply chain bottlenecks in the Strait of Hormuz threaten global food and fertilizer prices, the World Trade Organization's (WTO) director-general warned.
Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, speaking on the sidelines of the WTO’s Public Forum in Geneva, told Anadolu that the global trading system remains resilient, but the ongoing Middle East conflict presents a major test for the organization’s 166 member countries.
She noted that global trade in goods grew by an unexpectedly strong 4.6% this year despite geopolitical pressures, while 72% of all global commerce continued to operate under WTO rules. The initial projection for overall goods trade growth was 1.9% for the entire year, but the first-quarter growth rate of 3.2% outpaced expectations.
Okonjo-Iweala stated that a significant portion of the momentum was driven by the surging trade in artificial intelligence, which in turn was driven by low-or-zero tariff agreements covering $3 trillion in global semiconductor and chip shipments.
Saudis give European oil buyers no supplies for next month
Saudi Aramco told at least two oil refining customers in Europe that they will be allocated no crude next month under long-term agreements after the kingdom’s key pipeline to the Red Sea was attacked, people informed of the decision said, Bloomberg reported on Friday.
European customers normally receive Saudi Arabian crude on so-called term contracts, ensuring a steady flow of supply every month. Those deliveries will not take place next month, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information isn’t public. The decision applies to all European buyers, they said.
According to Reuters , Saudi ​Arabia earlier informed European customers that some crude cargoes would be cancelled after drone attacks forced the shutdown of its East-West pipeline, ​damaging three pumping stations and disrupting oil loadings at ​the Red Sea port of Yanbu.
US strikes on school, sports ground were 'clear war crimes' not 'operational errors': Iran's deputy FM
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi said on Friday that the United States' attacks in Minab and Lamerd were "clear war crimes, not an operational error."
In a post on X, Gharibabadi stated, "History will not forget; in Minab, a school was painted with the blood of 168 children, and in Lamerd, the sports ground turned into a slaughterhouse for civilians."
تاریخ فراموش نخواهد کرد؛ در میناب مدرسه‌ای با خون ۱۶۸ کودک رنگین شد و در لامرد، زمین ورزش به قتلگاه غیرنظامیان بدل گشت. اکنون همگان تایید میکنند آنچه در میناب و لامرد رخ داد جنایت جنگی آشکار بود، نه خطای عملیاتی. آمریکا نمی‌تواند با خروج از شورای حقوق بشر، از مسوولیت خود بگریزد.
The deputy foreign minister added, "America cannot escape its responsibility by withdrawing from the Human Rights Council."
White House rejects UN report on alleged war crimes in Iran
Separately, a United Nations fact-finding mission on Iran said it had " reasonable grounds " ​to believe the US was behind two military strikes on a school and sports facility in Iran in February, and that ‌these constituted war crimes.
The findings in the report by the Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran, to be submitted to the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva, examined the US's conduct during the Iran war and the Iranian government's response to nationwide ​unrest that began in late December.
The White House rejected the report, according to Al Jazeera . Principal Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly stated that the UN Human Rights Council had "accomplished nothing for human rights while spouting unserious nonsense for decades,” as per remarks carried by The New York Post .
“The only party in this conflict that has committed war crimes is the Iranian regime, which has murdered thousands of its own people, killed Americans overseas, executed acts of terrorism in the Strait of Hormuz, and launched indiscriminate attacks against its neighbours in the region,' the spokeswoman added, according to The New York Post.
Washington assumes nations have neither memory nor capacity for critical thought: Baghaei
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said in a post on X that "Washington still seems to assume that nations have neither memory nor the capacity for critical thought."
Saying that the US treated the world as if it were Pluribus — "a hive in which minds are expected to switch off, eyes lock onto Washington's lips, and its narrative is swallowed whole," Baghaei stated that on one side "stands a brutal economic war, deliberately designed to inflict maximum pain and suffering on every Iranian citizen," while on the other stood "the theatrical announcement of measures to stop Iranian officials from supposedly shopping at an American wholesale club."

"They look past the sanctioning of an entire nation’s livelihood, then issue solemn statements about the sanctioning of a store membership card," the spokesperson added.
"The propaganda is so crude and threadbare that it exposes the naivety of the mindset that launched an unlawful war of choice against the Nation of Iran, and helped deliver the United States to the embarrassing position it occupies today," Baghaei concluded.
Earlier, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they struck an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, according to state news agency IRNA , as a British maritime agency also reported an attack.
IRGC Navy: Last night, the violating tanker "Trend" flying the flag of Togo, incited and deceived by the child-killing US military, attempted to illegally pass through the Strait of Hormuz, where it was struck and came to a halt after catching fire. pic.twitter.com/bDjZVPR0sq
Iran has maintained its stranglehold on the strategic strait as Washington continues pressing its counterblockade of Iranian ports during the Middle East war.
The Islamic Republic wants to charge ships for passage, attacking vessels it accuses of attempting to circumvent its preferred route.
“The Togo-flagged oil tanker ‘Trend’ had been targeted and detained after a fire broke out on board” late on Thursday, the statement said, calling it an attempted “illegal passage”.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said earlier on Friday a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, causing a fire that has since been extinguished, with all crew reported safe and the environmental impact unconfirmed.

The monitoring agency had also reported a “security incident” in Hormuz late on Thursday, without giving details.
It was unclear if the IRGC and UKMTO reports referred to the same incident.
Italian aircraft hit during air base attacks in Saudi Arabia
An Italian aircraft was hit during air base attacks in Saudi Arabia, Defence Minister Guido Crosetto announced Friday.
Crosetto noted he followed the situation in Saudi Arabia's Ta'if air base, "which was the target of several attacks and where Italian personnel are present as part of Operation Inherent Resolve," according to ANSA news agency.
He reaffirmed that no Italian military personnel were involved.
"During the attack, an Italian F-2000 aircraft was hit. It was inside the base, in a remote area. There is no other damage to vehicles or infrastructure used by our personnel,” Crosetto said.
He noted that he asked to be provided with further assessment of the evolving situation, the condition of their personnel and possible operational options.
Crosetto added that he had been reassured that all security measures to protect military personnel had already been put in place some time ago.
“The situation is being followed with the utmost attention, with the aim of ensuring the full protection of our personnel and operating with the necessary responsibility," Crosetto further said.
Shipping traffic via Strait of Hormuz stays below 10-day average, data shows
Four commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf on Thursday, down from six a day earlier and below the 10-day average of about 16, preliminary shipping data showed on Friday.
The figures could change as some ships typically switch off their transponders during the voyage to avoid the risk of detection in the conflict zone.
Of the four vessels, three were entering the strait heading into the Gulf and one was exiting, the data from shiptracker Kpler showed at 0200 GMT.
The vessels included two Panamax tankers, one Supramax ship and one Kamsarmax vessel.
The waterway carried a fifth of the world’s oil and gas before the Iran conflict.
Meanwhile, 23 commodity vessels transited the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Thursday, another maritime chokepoint on the southwest tip of Yemen and a vital trade route for oil between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.
The data showed 13 vessels heading towards the Red Sea and 10 towards the Gulf of Aden. They included a Panamax and a Suezmax tanker, four Supramax vessels and six Aframax tankers.
The number compares with an average of around 26 ships using the strait in the past 10 days.
The Iran-backed Houthis have seized Yemen’s entire Red Sea coastline since last week, prompting the Saudi Arabian air force to conduct airstrikes.
The spread of the war to Yemen and Saudi Arabia has raised new concerns about oil supplies by jeopardising the Red Sea route for exports, the main alternative for Gulf supplies while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is constrained.
Yemeni army says 30 Houthis killed in clashes west of Taiz
Yemen's army said on Friday that 30 Houthi fighters were killed and more than 60 others were wounded in 24 hours of clashes and airstrikes in the Al-Waziyah district west of Taiz.
A military source quoted by the Armed Forces Media Centre said Yemeni warplanes also struck Houthi vehicles and gathering points in the clash zone.
The army said earlier that its air force hit Houthi supply lines and deployment points in Taiz and in the Red Sea city of Mocha.
Government forces also said they previously repelled Houthi attacks in Taiz and struck the group's positions and reinforcements. The army has stepped up strikes on Houthi sites in several provinces in recent days, with Taiz among the main fronts.
Drones fly over Yemen’s Sanaa, Houthis fire anti-aircraft guns
Drones were seen flying over Yemen’s capital Sanaa on Friday as the Houthi group fired anti-aircraft weapons to shoot them down, Yemeni residents told Anadolu .
The residents said they spotted drones flying over several neighbourhoods, including Saawan and Al-Hasaba in the northeast of the city.
The Houthi anti-aircraft fire caused explosions and sparked fear among residents, they added.
Meanwhile, Yemen’s independent Belqees news website also reported that “explosions, air defence fire and gunshots were heard early Friday in the capital Sanaa.”
The website quoted residents as saying that “the sounds of explosions and gunfire did not stop, causing fear and concern among residents, with the reasons remaining unclear.”
It also cited Houthi-affiliated media outlets and social media accounts as saying that the group's "air defence systems were activated to counter drones flying heavily" over Sanaa.
The Houthis did not immediately comment on the incident, while the identity of the drones and the party that launched them was not immediately clear.
Italy ready to escort ships through Bab el-Mandeb without waiting for EU, says defence chief
Italy is prepared to act independently to ensure its merchant vessels can pass through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait rather than wait for an EU naval mission, Defence Minister Guido Crosetto said on Thursday.

Crosetto said he had instructed military officials to assess the security situation and prepare a plan to guarantee safe passage through the strategic Red Sea waterway, according to Italian news agency ANSA .
"Together with the chief of General Staff, we have decided not to wait for (EU Red Sea Operation) Aspides to decide whether ships can pass or not," he said at the Risorsa Mare Forum in La Spezia, a northern coastal city.
Crosetto said Italy would likely take steps allowing its ships to resume transit without waiting for European procedures, arguing that delays would further hurt the economy.
The Italian frigate Bergamini is currently in the African nation of Djibouti, while around a dozen Italian-flagged or Italian-owned merchant vessels are seeking escorted passage, ANSA reported.
Crosetto said authorities are also examining whether existing rules allow Italian military assets already deployed in the region to be temporarily placed under national command or whether fresh parliamentary authorisation would be required.
"When a sea route is interrupted, goods arrive late, costs increase, and prices for families and businesses mount," he said.
Saudis and Houthis exchange strikes, Yemenis flee by boat as Middle East war spreads
Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis exchanged fresh strikes across their border on Thursday, and Yemenis took to boats in the Red Sea to escape fighting, ‌as the spreading Middle East war created new threats to global oil supplies.
Read more: 'Anything could happen': Trump says 'big decision' incoming regarding Iran
Houthi-controlled television reported Saudi airstrikes in Hajjah province close to the Saudi border near the Red Sea coast, and in the vicinity of Taiz further inland to the south.
Saudi Arabia's civil defence said a Yemeni living in Saudi Arabia had been killed by debris from a drone intercepted over the western city of Taif, the first death Riyadh has announced in Houthi attacks since fighting escalated last week. ​It has previously said more than 80 people were wounded.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards Navy said a Togo-flagged oil tanker caught fire after being hit while attempting what it called an ‘illegal passage’ ​through the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported. The tanker came to a halt after the fire, the Guards Navy said.
The spread of the ⁠war to Yemen and Saudi Arabia has raised new concerns about oil supplies by jeopardising the main alternative Red Sea route for Gulf exports while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains constrained.
US President ​Donald Trump has rebuffed pleas from the Saudis for military support to fight the Houthis, who agreed a ceasefire with the United States last year after Washington bombed the group for two months.
The president ​faces the prospect of political losses for his Republican Party in November's midterm elections, partly because of higher energy prices since the United States and Israel attacked Iran in February.
Trump said on Thursday he is approaching a critical juncture over whether to restart massive attacks on Iran.
"I have a big decision coming up. Do I want to go in and annihilate them or do I not? It's a big decision. Anything could happen with me," Trump said ​in an interview with Axios.
Trump has in the past threatened major new attacks that have not materialised.
Global crude prices eased slightly on Thursday but remain well above $100 a barrel after reaching their highest ​levels since May. The average US retail diesel price hit a record high on Thursday, just shy of $6.40 a gallon.
The United States and Iran have held no negotiations to end the war since an interim agreement reached ‌in June collapsed ⁠within weeks. But the war will come up for discussion at the United Nations General Assembly next week, and an Iranian delegation will be able to attend, according to the US State Department.
The fighting has driven Yemeni civilians to flee across the Bab el-Mandeb — Arabic for "Gate of Tears" — the narrow strait at the mouth of the Red Sea.
In Djibouti on the African shore of the Red Sea, Wahida Omer, 50, reached land after crossing on a small boat from Yemen when her village of Dhubab came under attack as the Houthis swept into the area. Her husband had been left behind, ​and she had no idea if he was ​alive, dead or captured by the Houthis.
"The sea ⁠was frightening, difficult," she said in an interview filmed by the International Organisation for Migration. Those on the boat were "crying the whole way, and we arrived still crying" with nothing to eat.
The IOM says more than 100,000 Yemenis have been displaced by the latest fighting, mostly within Yemen.
The Houthis, who ​have seized Yemen's entire Red Sea coast since last week in a lightning advance, say the Saudi Air Force has conducted hundreds of airstrikes ​in recent days. On Wednesday, ⁠the Houthis said they had shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet.
"We want the Saudis to cease their blockade and occupation of our country, and to stop their aggression against us. This is our demand!" Houthi leader Abdul Malik al-Houthi said in a televised speech, seated with a traditional dagger in his belt. Slogans on the wall behind him read: "Death to America, death to Israel, a curse upon the Jews, victory for ⁠Islam."
The US ​Navy is trying to guide ships through the Strait of Hormuz, the outlet to the Gulf along Iran's coast, where ​a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas passed before the war, and is also imposing a blockade of Iranian ports.
Iran says the strait is closed and will remain shut until Washington lifts the blockade. It is seeking an agreement with ​neighbouring Gulf states that would let it collect fees from ships passing through the strait.

title: K P police bill sparks autonomy concerns
description: K P police bill sparks autonomy concerns
content:
Officials fear proposed law could increase political control over police postings and operations
Police officials have expressed serious reservations over the proposed Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Police Bill 2026, fearing that the new legislation could increase political interference in police affairs and undermine the operational and administrative autonomy of the force.
According to official sources, senior police officials conveyed their concerns during a meeting of the committee examining the proposed legislation. The officials reportedly warned that several provisions of the proposed law could result in greater political influence over police postings, transfers, policy-making and operational matters.
Sources said the basic objective of the K-P Police Act 2017 was to empower the police force and reduce political interference in its affairs. However, they said the proposed 2026 legislation could reverse some of the safeguards introduced under the existing law and affect the independence of the police command.
Under the proposed legislation, the administrative, financial and operational powers currently vested in the Inspector General of Police (IGP) are proposed to be transferred to the chief minister. Sources said the move could significantly curtail the authority of the provincial police chief and affect the chain of command within the force.
The proposed law also seeks to give the chief minister powers over the appointment and transfer of police officers from grades 17 to 21. The proposed powers would cover key positions, including deputy superintendents of police (DSPs), district police officers (DPOs), deputy inspectors general (DIGs), regional police officers (RPOs) and additional inspectors general (Addl IGs).
Sources said another major proposed change relates to the Police Policy Board. Under the draft law, the chief minister would head the board instead of the IGP. A provision requiring prior approval from the chief minister for police operations has also reportedly been included in the proposed legislation.
Police officials have expressed concern that transferring key powers from the IGP to the political leadership could affect professional decision-making within the force as well as its ability to respond independently to law-and-order challenges.
Sources also pointed out that the Peshawar High Court had previously struck down amendments involving the withdrawal of powers from the IGP, although the precise legal status and applicability of those earlier rulings to the proposed legislation would depend on the final text of the law.
The draft also proposes changes to the procedure for appointing the provincial police chief. Under the proposed mechanism, the federal government would send a list of police officers' names to the chief minister, who would select and approve one officer for appointment as IGP.

title: Risk persists of poliovirus spreading to Punjab

content:
Punjab Emergency Operations Centre (EOC) Coordinator Khalid Parvaiz has directed the relevant officials of districts along inter-provincial boundaries to re-check their microplans for an anti-polio Special National Immunisation Days (SNID) campaign starting September 21 in the light of coordination meetings held with neighbouring districts and provinces.

The coordinator emphasised the importance of strong microplanning. He stressed that every possible effort must be made to identify and vaccinate children who may otherwise be missed during the campaign.
"Punjab has achieved a very encouraging situation, with environmental samples currently negative for poliovirus. However, sustaining this progress requires us to remain vigilant and close every operational gap," he said.
He said the presence of poliovirus in areas beyond Punjab's borders, including environmental detections and cases in neighbouring provinces, continued to pose a risk of reintroduction.
"Any persistent gap in our vaccination and surveillance efforts can create an opportunity for the virus to cross into Punjab. Our objective is to keep Punjab at zero, and this requires additional and sustained efforts," he said.
The EOC coordinator highlighted transit vaccination as a critical component of the upcoming campaign, particularly for reaching children travelling with mobile and migrant populations.

title: Opposition leader challenges secret trials law
description: Plea contended that Section 21AAA conflicted with the existing  near identical Section 21AA of the Act
content:
Plea contended that Section 21AAA conflicted with the existing, near-identical Section 21AA of the Act
Punjab Assembly Opposition Leader Moeen Riaz Qureshi has approached the Lahore High Court (LHC) against recent amendments to theanti-terrorism law through which cases can be tried while keeping secret the identities of judges, prosecutors, lawyers and witnesses.
The amendments were approved by the Punjab Assembly a few weeks back despite strong protest and a walkout by opposition legislators.
Through the newly inserted section 21AAA of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, a special security case mechanism has been created for cases in which participants are considered to require extraordinary protection.
The petitioner criticised the provision and argued that it was unconstitutional.
The plea contended that Section 21AAA conflicted with the existing, near-identical Section 21AA of the Act, which vested protective powers in courts rather than the executive. Section 21AAA was, therefore, void under Article 143 of the Constitution, he contended.
The petitioner argued that the provision violated the right to open justice and fair trial under Articles 9, 10-A and 14 of the Constitution, equality before law under Article 25, and separation of powers under Article 175(3), by shifting control over trial procedure from judges to an anonymous executive official.
He also alleged excessive delegation of legislative power, arguing that the law provided no objective criteria for when a case would be qualified to be tried under the special regime.
The petitioner urged the court to declare Section 21AAA ultra vires the Constitution and to suspend its operation, including restraining authorities from classifying any case as a "special security" one, during the pendency of the petition.
Under Section 21AAA, a designated officer of at least BS-20 whose identity would remain confidential can declare a case or a class of cases as special security.

Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Thursday expressed displeasure over the poor performance of Class IX students in examinations and ordered immediate action against teachers having results below 20 per cent.

She boarded a bus from the e-bus stop established at Agro Mall on Shujaabad Road and travelled to the venue of the ceremony at Muhammad Nawaz Sharif University of Agriculture. Thousands of citizens gathered to greet her.

title: Cantt residents slapped with borewell fee

Warning notices have been issued to those who fail to pay the charges within seven days, stating that their borewells would be removed and legal action taken against them.
According to sources, residential and commercial water connection holders in Rawalpindi Cantonment Board areas are supplied water every other day despite paying their full monthly bills.
Under the system, consumers receive water for 15 days a month, which is insufficient for their daily needs, but are charged for the entire month.
Frustrated by the situation, residents arranged borewells in their respective areas at their own expense to meet their daily water requirements and adopted an alternative system for meeting their water needs.
However, under Resolution No. 23 of its board meeting, the Cantonment Board imposed charges on groundwater from underground water reserves.
The notices issued to residents state that they are using groundwater illegally for residential and commercial purposes and therefore the said illegal borewells need to be regularised.
For regularisation, they have been directed to deposit Rs55,400 within seven days for each residential borewell and Rs200,000 for a commercial borewell.
Otherwise, the borewells will be removed and legal action will be taken against those responsible.
Several attempts were made to contact Cantonment Board spokesman Imran Habib for his position, but he could not be reached.

title: Historic building reclaimed after 66 years

content:
FIA operation ends Education Department's occupation of building on Murree Road
A decade-long dispute between the Education Department and the Evacuee Trust Property Board (ETPB) over 1 acre and 18 kanals of roadside land at Committee Chowk on Murree Road in the centre of the city has finally reached its conclusion, with the FIA vacating and sealing the "Schools Colleges Education Complex" after a major operation.
Armed police and FIA personnel were deployed outside the building.
After 66 years, the Education Department was removed from the complex, while furniture, valuable teachers' and professors' records and computers were also sealed.
FIA personnel entered the complex at around 10am armed with guns, went into the office of the Grade-19 Director Colleges, Prof Dr Shehnaz Mohsin Sial, pointed guns at her and brought the female director out of her office in what appeared to be an arrest-style manner and onto Murree Road.
Subsequently, the entire staff of the education complex was ordered to put their hands up and leave their offices, after which the whole complex was sealed.
The female director quietly left the premises in tears. She conducted official affairs on the road for two hours and, after requesting the FIA sub-inspector, managed to have her car, which was parked inside the complex, brought out and then went to the district administration office.
The district administration authorities refused to grant her time or provide any relief.
The complex housed the Education Department's schools wing, the Literacy Department and the Directorate of Colleges, which have been permanently removed from the premises from Sept 17.
The ETPB has won the case, while the FIA forcibly vacated the education offices and sealed the Schools and Colleges Directorate after six decades.
The 1 kanal and 18 marla commercial land along Murree Road at Committee Chowk is said to be worth billions of rupees.
Influential political and business groups of Rawalpindi will jointly construct a commercial plaza there, and the land will reportedly be obtained from the ETPB on a 99-year lease on easy terms.
The building was constructed in 1860 by affluent and philanthropist Sikh businessman Sardar Hasrat Singh in memory of his philanthropist uncle.

title: US may have committed war crimes in Iran  UN mission
description: US may have committed war crimes in Iran  UN mission
content:
Also accuses Tehran of crimes against humanity
A UN fact-finding mission on Iran said on Thursday it had reasonable grounds to believe the United States was behind two military strikes on a school and sports facility in Iran in February, and that these constituted war crimes.
It also found that Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity during their deadly crackdown on anti-government protests.
The findings in a new report by the Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran, to be submitted to the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva, examined the US's conduct during the Iran war that began in February and the Iranian government's response to nationwide unrest that began in late December.
The Iranian and US permanent missions in Geneva did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.
US officials have previously said military operations are conducted in accordance with the law of armed conflict, while Iran has consistently rejected allegations of systematic rights violations.
UN Fact-Finding missions are investigative, not judicial bodies, and therefore do not initiate any criminal cases. Their findings, however, can be used in criminal investigations by national courts or international tribunals such as the International Criminal Court. States will discuss the findings of the report when it is presented to the Human Rights Council in Geneva on Monday.
The UN experts said they found reasonable grounds to believe US forces were responsible for an attack on the Shajareh Tayyebeh Primary School in the city of Minab, where more than 150 people were killed, including around 120 schoolchildren, according to Iranian officials.
The attack constituted an indiscriminate attack causing civilian deaths and damage to civilian infrastructure, amounting to a war crime under international law, the mission concluded.
According to the report, the US failure to update information in relation to the school, which was adjacent to an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps naval complex, in its targeting databases and to confirm the building was a military objective amounted to more than mere negligence.
The UN mission probe found that the Iranian authorities carried out a widespread and systematic attack against civilians during protests that erupted in late December last year, involving unlawful killings, torture, arbitrary detention, enforced disappearances and severe restrictions on freedom of expression.

title: Russia  China veto Iran move in UNSC
description: Russia  China veto Iran move in UNSC
content:
Pakistan abstains as envoy urges resolution of N-issue
Pakistan on Thursday abstained from voting on a resolution seeking to extend the mandate of an independent panel monitoring sanctions on Iran, as China and Russia vetoed the measure, reiterating their position that all UN measures against Tehran had been lifted under the nuclear deal with world powers.
All UN sanctions on Iran were reimposed a year ago after France, Britain and Germany accused Tehran of violating the 2015 nuclear pact aimed at preventing it from developing a nuclear weapon. Iran denies seeking nuclear weapons.
The reimposition included the return of an independent panel of experts to monitor and report to the 15-member Security Council on violations and recommend further action. However, the council has operated without the panel for the past year because it has been unable to agree on its appointment, which must be made by consensus.
Beijing and Moscow vetoed the Security Council resolution seeking to extend the mandate of the independent monitoring panel, reviving their argument that all UN measures against Tehran had been removed under the nuclear deal with world powers.
"We strongly urge Western colleagues to stop their very dangerous actions on the Iran front, which threaten further complication of settling of the crisis in the Persian Gulf," Russia's UN Ambassador Vassily Nebenzia told the Security Council. "The only way to resolve disagreements and to alleviate concerns ... pertaining to the Iranian nuclear programme is through political and diplomatic efforts."
Both Russia and China then vetoed the resolution, concerning the Panel of Experts of the 1737 Committee on Iran, which would have extended its mandate for independent monitoring of sanctions. Eleven council members voted in favour, while Pakistan and Somalia abstained.
Explaining Pakistan's position, the Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, stressed that the Iran nuclear issue should be addressed through peaceful means and called for a non-confrontational and cooperative approach to achieving lasting peace.
"Ongoing tensions and hostilities in the region and strikes on nuclear facilities, as well as continued differences amongst permanent members on key aspects of this file, have added to the challenges in addressing the issue through dialogue and diplomacy," he said. AGENCIES

title: Laws on paper, peasants in peril | The Express Tribune
description:
Laws on paper, 
peasants in peril
content:
Report finds low wages, bonded labour persist despite protective legislation
A non-profit organisation's report outlining the state of peasants' rights has depicted a bleak picture of the agriculture workforce's continued exploitation in the face of laws, policies and initiatives aimed at their protection and welfare. The socio-political problems, low wages, landlessness, health, education and gender issues have also been highlighted in the report titled 'State of Peasants' Rights in Sindh in 2025'.
The Hari Welfare Association (HWA) launched this report at an event at Hyderabad press club on Thursday. The 106-page report consists of seven chapters ranging from laws to social safety programmes. Violence against women, tribal conflicts and bonded labour also find separate sections.
Addressing the launch, the HWA's executive director Akram Khaskheli briefed about the Sindh Assembly's legislations which aspired to address vulnerabilities of landless peasants, especially women farm workers. He shared brief insights of the Sindh Tenancy Act, 1950; the Sindh Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 2015; the Sindh Women Agricultural Workers Act (SWAWA), 2019; and the Sindh Water Policy, 2023.
"The 2019 judgment of the Sindh High Court concerning the tenancy act had given a big hope to landless peasants for access to justice but the provincial government challenged that judgment in the apex court where it is still pending," he regretted. The historic judgment had barred the deputy and assistant commissioners from acting as arbitrators between a landlord and a peasant. The jurisdiction to settle disputes between the two was handed over to the courts in the light of the separation of judiciary from the executive.
"It is lamentable that despite its assertions for being pro-peasant, the Sindh government hasn't withdrawn its appeal against the SHC's pro-peasant order," Khaskheli said. The report stated that 51% of rural households remain landless as 64% of farmland is owned by 5% of landlords. Women own only 3% of the land.
Over the last 16 years, the provincial government gradually enhanced the minimum wage from Rs7,000, in 2010, to Rs40,000, in 2025. However, on the ground the peasants earn hardly around Rs15,000 wage per month, the report claimed.
Labours held captives against repayment of debts or wages paid in advance are also yet to reap fruits of the the Sindh Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 2015, as thousands of farm workers undergo this bondage every year.

Cabinet approves 445-bed Edhi Medical Tower for NICH
The Sindh cabinet on Thursday approved a support package for wheat growers, a blockchain-based system for electronic transfer of land ownership and a 13-storey, 445-bed medical tower at the National Institute of Child Health (NICH), as the provincial government moved to expand farmer support, modernise land administration and strengthen healthcare infrastructure.
The cabinet meeting, chaired by Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, considered a 23-point agenda and approved a range of measures relating to agriculture, health, taxation, local government, prosecution, sports and youth development.
Under the wheat support package, farmers owning up to 25 acres will receive subsidies for DAP fertiliser or approved alternatives, while growers supplying wheat to the Food Department will receive an additional incentive linked to the quantity supplied.

The cabinet was informed that 56,741 farmers had supplied more than 2.04 million maunds of wheat to the Food Department during the previous procurement season. The crop was cultivated over 413,507 acres. The approved subsidy package is estimated at Rs14.9 billion, while the additional procurement incentive could take the total allocation to around Rs16 billion, subject to verification and payments.
The chief minister directed the authorities to re-register eligible growers under the Sindh Wheat Growers Support Programme and introduce stronger digital verification to eliminate duplicate and ineligible beneficiaries. Subsidies will be transferred directly into beneficiaries' Benazir Hari Card accounts through Sindh Bank.
The cabinet, however, deferred a decision on the wheat support price for 2026-27 pending further consultations and financial assessments.
In the healthcare sector, the cabinet approved construction of the Bilquis and Abdul Sattar Edhi Medical Tower at NICH under a public-private partnership with the Abdul Sattar Edhi Foundation.

title: A mother resisted  Then came a macabre bloodbath
description: A mother resisted  Then came a macabre bloodbath
content:
Police crack fourfold murder mystery in Surjani Town; arrest family relative over killings of woman, her three childre
A routine afternoon at a Surjani Town home turned into a scene of unimaginable horror when, according to police, a woman's resistance to an attempted sexual assault set off a chain of macabre violence that ended with her and her three young children bludgeoned to death. Three days later, investigators claim they have arrested the man responsible - a relative the family knew and trusted.
Thirty-four-year-old Mahwish was at home with her 18-month-old daughter on September 14 when the suspect, Humayun, her husband Danish's brother-in-law, allegedly arrived at the house in Sector 7-D of Surjani Town. Police say he had previously lived there as a tenant and had been harbouring intentions towards Mahwish. What began with a visit allegedly escalated into an assault after she resisted him. The horror did not end with Mahwish's killing. Police say the suspect then turned on her children - eight-year-old Marha, six-year-old Hasnain, and 18-month-old Ashmira - allegedly killing them one after another and arranging their bodies on the sofas in an attempt to conceal the crime and make it appear as though the family had been killed elsewhere.
"The suspect was sexually attracted towards the woman and wanted to assault her," DIG West Zone Irfan Ali Baloch told a news conference alongside District West SSP Tariq Elahi Mastoi and SP Investigation Masroor Jatoi on Thursday.
According to DIG Baloch, the suspect had lived as a tenant at Danish's house around one-and-a-half years ago, but was evicted after Danish found out that Humayun had allegedly developed an interest in Mahwish. However, Humayun continued visiting the family and allegedly made repeated attempts to contact Mahwish, the DIG added.
On the day of the incident, Humayun allegedly reached Danish's house at around 2pm, knowing that Danish was away. Mahwish served him tea and asked him to bring some items from the market.
When he returned, the woman's two elder children had left for their madrassah, leaving Mahwish and her toddler daughter at home. The suspect allegedly attempted to sexually assault Mahwish, but she resisted and slapped him, leading to a scuffle. During the confrontation, Humayun allegedly picked up an iron rod and struck her, killing her on the spot.
The toddler began crying after witnessing the incident. The suspect allegedly hit the child's head against a wall, leaving her unconscious, and assumed that she had died, the DIG said.
At around 3pm, the two elder children returned from the madrassah and began screaming after seeing their mother and sister. Humayun allegedly attacked both children with the same iron rod before placing all four victims on sofas to make it appear that they had been killed there.
The suspect allegedly washed the iron rod and his hands in the bathroom, cleaned blood stains from the floor and left the house at around 6pm after changing his clothes. He allegedly threw the iron rod into a drain before returning to his home. He further added that the suspect returned to the crime scene after his wife informed him about the killings, pretending that he had no knowledge of the incident.
Police arrested him on the basis of eyewitness accounts and technical evidence, DIG Baloch said, adding that the suspect allegedly confessed during interrogation.
The DIG said Humayun allegedly switched off his mobile phone before leaving for Danish's house, left his motorcycle at home and travelled by a rickshaw. He allegedly got off at a specific point and walked to the house.
He also did not operate his catering stall on the day of the incident, DIG Baloch added.
A neighbour allegedly saw Humayun at the house when he arrived, while another eyewitness saw him leaving the premises after the killings.

title: PM unveils austerity measures as Gulf conflict spirals
description: PM unveils austerity measures as Gulf conflict spirals
content:
Markets to close at 9pm to conserve fuel Fuel quota for official vehicles reduced by half Single dish allowed at
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday approved a nationwide austerity and energy conservation campaign in view of rising global petroleum prices amid tensions in the Middle East.
The decision was taken at a high-level meeting chaired by the prime minister to review austerity and energy conservation measures, a Prime Minister's Office news release said.
The prime minister said the rise in petroleum prices in the international market had triggered inflationary pressures across the world, stressing that sacrifices should first be made by the government and the elite.
He said a fuel subsidy had already been initiated for economically vulnerable and middle-income segments, under which motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles up to 800cc were being provided a subsidy of Rs100 per litre.
The prime minister directed the authorities to ensure immediate and effective implementation of measures aimed at reducing unnecessary government expenditure and ensuring prudent use of national resources.
As part of the drive, the government announced a cut in fuel for official vehicles, bans on vehicle purchases by the state, foreign visits by officials, and official dinners, as part of a slew of austerity measures in a bid to conserve energy as fuel prices spike due to the Gulf conflict.
The austerity measures, being implemented for the second time this year, also include a ban on government purchase of all durable goods except IT procurement and a switch to teleconferencing for meetings.
The government had unveiled similar measures in March, closing down schools for two weeks, cutting fuel use across government and pushing office workers to work more from home in a bid to conserve fuel and cut government spending.
The government has implemented a new policy starting on Wednesday that offers motorcycle, rickshaw and small-car owners a subsidy of Rs100 a litre on a capped monthly quota in a bid to ease the impact of rising prices.
However, the government also kept a backdoor open to relax any of these measures amid escalating Middle East conflict that could disrupt energy supplies.
The austerity and fuel conservation measures will be applicable on the federal government, as the provincial and regional governments of Azad Jammu & Kashmir and Gligit-Baltistan would take their own decisions.
The cabinet division notified 11 austerity measures with immediate effect but did not change the office timing, working hours and number of working days.
It has immediately notified a 50% reduction of fuel provision for official vehicles for three months, excluding operational vehicles of armed forces, civil armed forces, law enforcement agencies, essential services and the Federal Board of Revenue, according to the notification.
But the 50% reduction of the fuel will not apply on development projects a window that could be misused by the ministries, divisions and attached departments.
It was also notified to make a 5% cut in the non-employees related expenses budget for the fiscal year 2026-27, with deduction to be made on a monthly basis. The cabinet division said that the 5% cut will also apply in the case of foreign missions and the officers and officials, belonging to any occupational group or service, posted in these missions.
But fiscal obligations relating to their rents, educational fees and medical care arrangements will be met without any cut, according to the decision. The 5% cut will not apply to development projects, according to the cabinet division.
But the government has also kept a backdoor open to relax any of these 11 measures. According to the notification, requests for exemption from any of these measures may be considered, on a case-to-case basis, by the Committee for Monitoring and Implementation of Fuel Conservation and Additional Austerity Measures.
The committee will submit its recommendation for approval of the Prime Minister and exemptions granted by the committee will not require any further exemption from the Austerity Committee constituted by the Finance Division from time to time.
It is the second time since the Middle East war broke that the government has resorted to austerity and fuel conservation measures. The government has not made public any savings from the first such drive.
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said on Thursday that the central bank and the finance ministry were looking into the possible second and third rounds of impact of the conflict on Pakistan's economy.
However, the government has not done much to save people from the impact of higher fuel prices and a daily change in the rates has gravely impacted the consumers.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has announced Rs100 per litre compensation on 20 litre per month used by motorcyclists and 30 litre by small cars. But the petroleum dealers have refused to become part of the scheme, saying they were not consulted before finalizing the arrangements.
The government has also refused to cut taxes on petrol and diesel and as a result the fuel prices are the highest in Pakistan among all the South Asian countries.
The government notified a complete ban on purchase of vehicles of all types but it exempted the development projects from the ban. There will also be a complete ban on purchase of all durables except information technology procurements but again the ban will not be applicable in the case of development projects.
There will also be a complete ban on foreign visits and travel for three months, even in the case of obligatory visits, except in the case of scholarships offered by international development partners, training and courses arranged through the Economic Affairs Division or under institutional agreements of the Government of Pakistan.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif was scheduled to leave on Thursday for the United Kingdom and the United States on a 10-day visit. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb was already in the United Kingdom.
The notification stated that the Ambassador or High Commissioner of Pakistan would represent in obligatory and important events.
But the government has again provided a backdoor to the foreign visits. "In case of unavoidable visits all ministers, advisers, ministers of state, special assistants to the prime minister, parliamentary and government functionaries shall travel only in the economy class".
During the last phase of austerity measures, the ministers and bureaucrats did undertake foreign visits and those who opted business class paid the difference between the economy and business class ticket from their own pockets.
According to the notification, official meetings will be held preferably through teleconferencing, except intra-city meetings. No official dinners shall be hosted, except in the case of visiting foreign delegations.
There will also be a prohibition on all official seminars, trainings, and conferences funded by the government. In case of unavoidable requirements for such events to be held, the government venues such as auditoriums, committee rooms, and other official facilities will be utilized for such events.
The government said that the single dish shall be served in all marriage-related functions and events in a decision that does not have any implication for the public purse.
The government has also retained the old market closing timings. The shops, markets, shopping malls and bazaars, departmental, grocery, general and kiryana stores will be closed by 9.00 pm. The marriage halls, marquees and all other commercial places where festive events are held will be closed by 10.00 pm.
Restaurants, cafés, eateries, and food outlets standalone fruit and vegetable shop will be closed by 11 pm.
However, there will be exemptions from these timings to pharmacies, medical and medical supplies stores; medical laboratories, clinics, hospitals. Likewise, standalone bakeries, standalone tandoors; standalone milk and dairy shops will also be exempted. The fuel stations, CNG pumps, electrical vehicle charging stations. Gyms, sports facilities and sports/padel courts, information technology companies and call centres will also remain open without any time restrictions.

Hours after being granted bail by the Supreme Court in the controversial social media posts case, lawyers Imaan Mazari and her husband Hadi Ali Chattha were arrested again and sent on judicial remand by an Islamabad anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Thursday night.
ATC judge Abual Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain in his order rejected Investigation Officer (IO) request for granting 30 days physical remand of Imaan and Chattha.
"Investigating Officer through instant application requested for grant of 30-days physical remand of accused persons named above for the purpose of investigation and recovery. Record transpires that accused persons are nominated in FIR with allegation that they were member of unlawful assembly but no weapon has been ascribed to them in the contents of FIR. Therefore, instant request does not appear plausible, the same is turned down. Both accused are hereby sent to Judicial Custody for 14-days," the order issued by the ATC judge read.
"Accused be again produced before the Court on 01.10.2026. IO is directed to submit Report u/s 173 Cr.PC within stipulated time. Attendance of accused persons is dispensed with till submission of Challan. Superintendent Central Prison, Rawalpindi is directed to ensure attendance of accused person through video link," it added.
The re-arrest of both lawyers came after a division bench of the Supreme Court comprising Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim suspended their sentences in a case involving social media posts.
"For the reasons to be recorded later on, while granting leave in both the petitions, the same are converted into appeals and are accepted. The operation of impugned judgment 24.01.2026 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge/Presiding Officer Prevention of Electronic Crimes Court/Model Criminal Court, Islamabad-West in PECA Case No.137935 is suspended and both the petitioners (being practicing Advocates) are ordered to be released on bail till decision of their pending appeals before the Islamabad High Court subject to their furnishing personal surety bonds in the sum of Rs.2,00,000/- each with Additional Registrar (Judicial) of this Court," the written order said.
Renowned lawyer Faisal Siddiqi appeared on behalf of the couple.
The couple was arrested on January 23 near an underpass outside the Serena Hotel while travelling to the district courts and was later sent to 14 days' judicial remand by an ATC.
The next day, a district and sessions court sentenced each of the two to a combined 17 years' rigorous imprisonment: five years under Section 9 of PECA, along with a Rs5 million fine; 10 years under Section 10, with a Rs30 million fine; and two years under Section 26-A, with a Rs1 million fine. Additional jail terms were prescribed in case of non-payment of the fines.
The couple challenged their conviction before the IHC and subsequently filed an application seeking suspension of their sentences pending a final decision on their appeals.
As the matter remained pending before the IHC, Faisal Siddiqi, representing Imaan and Hadi, approached the Supreme Court seeking suspension of their sentences.
On May 12, the Supreme Court directed the IHC to decide their applications seeking suspension of their sentences. However, despite the passage of four months, the IHC could not decide the applications.
Even during Thursday's hearing, the bench raised serious questions about the conduct of the IHC.
Justice Afghan wondered that it was strange that the IHC referred to the Supreme Court's May 12 order but did not comply with it.
Then, when the case comes before the apex court, a new date is fixed in the high court, he said, adding that the IHC is, in its own way, is preventing the Supreme Court from functioning.
Justice Afghan asked what had happened after the Supreme Court's initial order in the case.
Additional Attorney General Rana Asad opposed the suspension of Imaan and Chattha's sentences. He told the bench that the high court had given the prosecution a final opportunity and fixed the matter for September 23. He also argued that the IHC was the appropriate judicial forum to seek suspension of the sentences under Section 426.
However, the bench was not persuaded and granted bail to both.
Imaan's mother Shireen Mazari criticised the rearrest in a post on X.
"They actually took them from inside Adiala because we had not yet gone to get them released as paper work was not complete! Once again totally illegal to take somebody from inside the jail in this manner but then there has never been due process observed for Imaan and Hadi," she stated.

title: Turkish spy chief discusses Yemen in Islamabad visit
description: Turkish spy chief discusses Yemen in Islamabad visit
content:
Turkish spy chief discusses Yemen in Islamabad visit
Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin held talks with Pakistan's top military and intelligence leadership in Islamabad on Thursday amid mounting tensions in the Gulf, including continuing Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and the attempted drone strike targeting the holy city of Makkah.
Kalin, head of Türkiye's National Intelligence Organization (MIT), met Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Inter-Services Intelligence chief Lt Gen Asim Malik, and was also received by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, according to the Turkish state-run Anadolu Agency, which cited Turkish security sources.
There is no official word yet from the Pakistani side.
The talks covered bilateral ties, regional and global developments and, in particular, the security situation that has emerged in the Middle East following the US-Israel war with Iran, according to Anadolu.
The discussions assumed added significance against the backdrop of continuing Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including the attempted drone attack targeting Makkah, as well as strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure.
Anadolu reported that the officials discussed the political, security and economic repercussions of the conflict, the risk of its further expansion and recent developments involving Yemen and Saudi Arabia.
The Turkish side also highlighted the importance of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Türkiye and Saudi Arabia as common ground for efforts to restore regional stability, according to the report. The three countries signed the agreement in Makkah on August 7, describing it as a framework for mutual defence and regional security.
But Islamabad on Thursday remained guarded about what the agreement could mean in operational terms as the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia continue.
The latest crisis escalated further after the attempted drone attack targeting Makkah. Pakistan condemned the attack in the strongest terms, while calling for restraint and an end to further escalation.
The Turkish intelligence chief's visit therefore comes at a particularly sensitive moment for the three countries that constitute the Makkah defence framework. According to Anadolu, Türkiye and Pakistan also discussed their respective roles in reducing regional tensions and keeping diplomatic channels open.
Kalin's Islamabad visit also carried a separate but potentially significant Afghan dimension.
The Turkish intelligence chief travelled to Pakistan after visiting Kabul, where he held talks with senior Taliban officials on security, intelligence cooperation and regional developments, according to Anadolu.
His movement between Kabul and Islamabad coincided with renewed efforts by regional powers to address the worsening relationship between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
A senior Qatari security official also travelled to Kabul, with the two countries having previously played mediatory roles between Islamabad and Kabul.

title: Pakistan will  go to any extent  for Saudi defence
description: Pakistan will  go to any extent  for Saudi defence
content:
DG ISPR says support for KSA unconditional
Pakistan will go "to any extent" to defend Saudi Arabia against attack, DG ISPR Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry told Arab News on Thursday.
Lt Gen Chaudhry reiterated Pakistan's "unconditional" commitment to Saudi Arabia, saying the country would go to any extent required for the security of the Haramain Sharifain and the Kingdom.
He said Pakistan fully stood with Saudi Arabia - both diplomatically and physically.
"We will go to any extent for the security of Haramain Sharifain and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. To any extent as asked and required by our Saudi brothers," he said.
Reiterating Pakistan's commitment to the Kingdom, he said the people of Pakistan stood shoulder-to-shoulder with their Saudi brothers and sisters.
"There should be no doubt about that. So, in a nutshell, we are there and we will continue to defend Kingdom of Saudi Arabia against any aggression," he said.
Highlighting the diplomatic efforts of the country's leadership, Lt Gen Chaudhry said Pakistan, with the help of other regional countries and partners, was working to find a peaceful and negotiated outcome to the complex situation.
He said the political and military leadership remained in continuous contact and engagement with the leadership of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
Underscoring Pakistan's commitment to the Kingdom under the Makkah Defence Agreement and the mutual defence pact between the two countries, he said Islamabad not only remained committed but was already there for the protection of the Haramain Sharifain and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
"We are there to protect them and we will to any extent further as and as required by the Saudi leadership and the people of Saudi Arabia," he said.
He said Pakistan's commitment to Saudi security was unconditional and stemmed from an emotive, deep-rooted historical and unbreakable bond between the people of Pakistan and the people of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, as well as between the political and military leaderships of the two countries.
"Nothing stops us, nothing bars us, nothing is there which hesitates our commitment from going, so whatever is required, whatever is asked, we will go to any extent to that," he said.
Asked whether his statement that Pakistan was "there" meant that the country was physically present in Saudi Arabia at present, Lt Gen Chaudhry said: "I think the words express themselves fully once we say that we are there."
Pakistan said it remained committed in spirit to the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia and the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.
Asked whether any mechanism had been devised for Pakistan to respond to attacks against Saudi Arabia under the Makkah agreement, Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said Pakistan remained committed, "in intent and spirit", to implementing both the agreements.
However, he said decisions concerning the use of force remained an operational matter.
"When, how, where, and what force will be used against which objectives, in which modes, and other matters involving operational confidentiality require us to maintain some discretion at this stage," Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said at his weekly news briefing.
The spokesperson reiterated that the Makkah agreement was defensive in nature, was not directed against any country and did not constitute a new bloc. He said it was intended to strengthen existing defence cooperation, including training, capacity-building, defence technology and research, as well as collective deterrence against acts aimed at destabilising regional security.
Pakistan has meanwhile been pursuing diplomatic efforts to prevent the Gulf crisis from widening.
Field Marshal Asim Munir spoke by telephone with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Wednesday, urging Tehran to use its influence with the Houthis to halt attacks against Saudi energy and economic infrastructure.
Islamabad has also repeatedly called for restraint and diplomacy, while Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif spoke with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on September 13 and reaffirmed Pakistan's solidarity with Saudi Arabia and support for de-escalation.
Asked about the Turkish and Qatari visits, Foreign Office spokesperson said Islamabad was aware of the reports but was not aware of the precise background.
He acknowledged that both Türkiye and Qatar had previously played "a very constructive role" in mediation efforts between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
Pakistan, he said, had engaged Afghanistan through Qatar and Türkiye, while China had also brought the three sides together through the Urumqi process.
But Islamabad remains focused on securing an assurance from Kabul that terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory will not carry out attacks against Pakistan.
"The action now rests on the other side," Sajjad said, adding that Pakistan remained prepared to resolve its differences with Afghanistan through dialogue and diplomacy.
He said Pakistan wanted an Afghanistan that was peaceful internally as well as with its neighbours, but stressed that progress depended on Kabul addressing Pakistan's security concerns.
The spokesperson said that it was ready to reopen border crossings, restore transit trade, and utilise Afghanistan as a regional connectivity hub, provided Kabul takes decisive and verifiable action against anti-Pakistan militant groups.
"If they cooperate on terrorism, there is no reason for Pakistan to continue with this process. We are ready to open our borders, do trade, use Afghanistan as a connecting hub, and the entire region can actually benefit from a peaceful region. Our policy has been a peaceful Afghanistan which is peaceful within as well as peaceful with neighbouring countries," he said.
Referring to last year's visit by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Ishaq Dar to Afghanistan, he said Pakistan offered many concessions on transit trade, reduced tariffs, and asked them to stop terrorism emanating from their side.
"Unfortunately, the action now rests on the other side," he said, recalling that Pakistan had also used the medium of friendly countries like Qatar, Turkiye, and China, though the efforts could not come to fruition due to non-cooperation from the Afghan side.
The spokesperson said that not only Pakistan, but China also had similar observations about terrorist activities taking place, and Central Asian countries were also unhappy over the security situation in Afghanistan.
He said China, Qatar, and Turkey played a very constructive role in terms of mediation, as Pakistan engaged twice with Kabul last year in Qatar and Istanbul, but the Afghan reaction had been negative, and they refused to give assurances of stopping terrorism from Afghan soil.
"Pakistan is keen to resolve all our issues through peaceful means, of course, through dialogue and diplomacy. We have clearly mentioned our red line, and now it is for Afghanistan to see how it can stop terrorism, because you cannot continuously allow terrorists to flow from one side and then expect a different outcome from Pakistan's side."
He told the media that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif would lead Pakistan's delegation to the high-level segment of the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly in New York next week, accompanied by DPM Ishaq Dar and other federal ministers. There, he would highlight Pakistan's perspective on regional and global developments, outline priorities on counter-terrorism and Islamophobia, and draw attention to the situations in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu & Kashmir (IIOJK) and Palestine.
During the visit, he will participate in high-level events and hold bilateral meetings with world leaders and the UN Secretary-General, highlighting Pakistan's commitment to multilateralism, the UN Charter, regional peace, and international cooperation.
The spokesperson rejected India's objections to the 1963 Boundary Agreement and Joint Commission, calling Kashmir a disputed UN-resolved territory and urging India to rescind its Aug 5, 2019, decisions.
"India's claims regarding Jammu and Kashmir are equally untenable, as Jammu and Kashmir remains an internationally recognised disputed territory whose final disposition is to be determined in accordance with United Nations Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people, through a UN-led, UN-sponsored plebiscite," he said, urging India to carry out its own introspection, especially regarding its illegal and unilateral decisions.
He said Pakistan summoned the Indian Chargé d'Affaires over an aggressive manoeuvre and contact by an Indian naval ship in Pakistan's EEZ on Sept 15, violating bilateral and international norms, and that a demarche would be issued by the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi to the Indian Ministry of External Affairs later in the day.
He highlighted that this year Pakistan issued over 2,800 visas to Indian pilgrims for Vaisakhi alone in April, over 700 for Guru Arjan Dev's martyrdom day, and 438 for the death anniversary of Maharaja Ranjit Singh in June, and that Pakistan was also ready to welcome Sikh pilgrims for the upcoming Vaisakhi festival.
He told the media that the Indian Chargé d'Affaires in Islamabad participated in and represented India at the SCO-RATS council meeting held earlier this week, and expressed the hope that Indian participation in SCO would continue as Pakistan is going to host the SCO Heads of State summit next year.
He said that Pakistan's partnership with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in the area of security and defence was well recognised, and the Makkah pact formalised and further strengthened many aspects of ongoing cooperation and existing long-standing bilateral cooperation among these three countries.
"The agreement is purely for defensive purposes; it is neither directed against any country nor formally constitutes a new bloc," the spokesperson explained.

title: Extravagance tweet not about Maryam s daughter  Ahsan
description: Extravagance tweet not about Maryam s daughter  Ahsan
content:
Says post on extravagance was generic message for public representatives
Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal on Thursday denied that his tweet criticising extravagance by people in public office, particularly during private joys and gatherings, was aimed at the wedding of Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz's daughter.
The minister said he had simply read the message and shared it for all public representatives to follow.
The clarification comes amid speculation over the timing of the minister's post, which appeared within hours of reports that Maryam Nawaz's daughter had purportedly worn a designer necklace worth millions of dollars at her wedding.
The post quickly triggered speculation on social media and in political circles that Ahsan Iqbal was indirectly criticising the Punjab chief minister and her family.
Citing the example of Caliph Hazrat Umar bin Abdul Aziz, who denounced extravagance immediately after being entrusted with the leadership of the Muslim Ummah, Ahsan wrote: "Private joys are the right of every human being, but a life associated with public office can never remain entirely private. The true dignity of leadership lies not in display and extravagance, but in living in harmony with the circumstances of the people."
The tweet was almost immediately interpreted as a reference to Maryam Nawaz's daughter's wedding, where, according to social media warriors, she wore a necklace worth over ten million dollars by a high-end designer.
When Adviser to the PM Rana Sanaullah was asked about the post, he said it did allude to what is commonly understood, obviating any need for further explanation. He also said that posting such a message was inappropriate.
He mockingly said that besides being a politician, he was also a professor, a term sometimes used as a euphemism for someone being overly smart. What he had implied was incorrect, Rana said, clarifying that there was nothing in that wedding to that effect. He asked Ahsan whether people should stop celebrating the weddings of their children.
Sources close to him in Narowal revealed that Federal Minister Ahsan was, in fact, unhappy with Maryam Nawaz and her team for not giving senior party members due respect. The source said that Ahsan Iqbal, during a private gathering, had said that even junior Maryam, referring to Maryam Aurangzeb, does not treat them properly.
Iqbal, while responding to questions sent by The Express Tribune, said his tweet was a generic one on simplicity, which he read and shared for "all of us to follow as public reps."
To another question regarding Rana Sanaullah, he said that Rana was his colleague and was free to say what he felt like.

title: Last surviving newborn from PIMS fire dies
description: Last surviving newborn from PIMS fire dies
content:
Rescued baby succumbs to cardiac, respiratory arrest
A newborn girl who survived the fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), in which 14 other newborn babies were killed, has also died after 22 days of treatment, taking the death toll from the incident to 15, according to her death certificate and sources.
The baby, who was rescued alive from the blaze by a nurse, died at PIMS on September 17 after her condition continued to deteriorate following the fire.
The death certificate states that she died after cardiac and respiratory arrest.
According to the death certificate, the newborn had been admitted to PIMS on August 26 and remained under treatment for 22 days.
During her hospitalisation, she developed several serious medical complications, including sepsis, disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) and bleeding in the lungs. The baby's condition continued to worsen after she was rescued from the fire. Despite treatment at PIMS, she could not recover from the severe complications that developed following the incident and eventually died on September 17, the death certificate states.
Sources said the newborn was among the babies who survived the fire that claimed the lives of 14 other newborn children. Her death means that the number of newborn babies killed in the PIMS fire has now risen to 15.
The baby had been rescued alive by a nurse during the fire and was subsequently kept under treatment at PIMS. However, her condition remained critical and later deteriorated amid the development of severe medical complications.
The death certificate records cardiac and respiratory arrest as the cause of death, while also documenting the complications, including sepsis, DIC and pulmonary bleeding, that emerged during her treatment.
