title: Pakistan  China agree on BJC framework
description: Pakistan  China agree on BJC framework
content:
Pakistan and China on Thursday agreed on a framework for future cooperation under the Boundary Joint Commission (BJC)
The inaugural meeting of the BJC concluded in Islamabad on Thursday, with both sides reaffirming their consensus.
According to the Foreign Office, the meeting was held in Islamabad on Sept 16 and 17, marking the formal launch of the commission. The BJC was envisaged under the 2013 China-Pakistan Agreement on the Boundary Management System.
"Both sides described the establishment of the commission as a vital milestone in further strengthening the Pakistan-China All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership," the FO said.
According to the statement, discussions at the inaugural meeting covered a wide range of matters related to border management and cooperation, including cross-border coordination, the movement of goods and people, joint border surveys and people-to-people linkages.
The meeting concluded with the signing of the minutes, reaffirming the two sides' consensus and setting out a framework for future cooperation under the commission, the statement said.
"Both sides agreed to hold the next meeting of the commission in China on mutually convenient dates," the FO said.
The Pakistan delegation was led by Bilal Mahmood Chaudhary, Director General (China) at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, while the Chinese delegation was led by Li Ya, Deputy Director General of the Department of Boundary and Ocean Affairs at China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Other representatives from the ministries of foreign affairs, defence, interior, commerce and communications, as well as customs, survey and other boundary management authorities, also attended the meeting.
The commission has its origins in the 2013 Agreement on the Boundary Management System, signed during the visit of then Chinese Premier Li Keqiang to Islamabad. Article 45 of the agreement provides for the establishment of the joint commission to oversee the implementation of border management arrangements.
The mechanism will provide an institutional framework for dealing with practical issues along the border, including the maintenance and inspection of the boundary, joint surveys, boundary marker issues, the management of cross-border facilities and the handling of incidents involving the border.
Its activation also gives the two countries a mechanism for regular coordination on a border that is important for movement between Pakistan and China, including thr­ough the Khunjerab crossing, and for trade and connectivity linked to the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

title: Pakistan at 143rd on gender parity
description: Pakistan at 143rd on gender parity
content:
Country ranks third-last on WEF's Gender Gap Index 2026
Pakistan has climbed to 143rd out of 145 economies in the World Economic Forum's (WEF) Global Gender Gap Index 2026, with the country closing 59.5% of its gender gap after a slight overall improvement was recorded in education and political sectors.
Last year, Pakistan attained the lowest score among 148 countries scored by the WEF on gender mainstreaming.
According to the WEF's latest Global Gender Gap Report, Pakistan registered an improvement of 2.8% compared to its last year's score of 56.7%. The country's score has risen by 5.2 percentage points since the index was first published in 2006, when Pakistan stood at 54.3%.
The report said, "The 2026 edition marks its strongest year-on-year improvement in a decade [for Pakistan], driven primarily by substantial gains in Educational Attainment."
It also said that Economic Participation and Opportunity remained Pakistan's "weakest-performing subindex and the principal constraint" on overall gender parity.
Compared to other South Asian countries, Pakistan ranked last on the gender gap index in the region despite the registered slight improvement. India ranked second last in the region while Bangladesh assumed the regional lead with its 79th overall rank.
Pakistan remains among the five lowest-ranked economies globally, ahead of only Algeria, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Iran and Chad in the 2026 ranking.
In global rankings, Pakistan leads the world in terms of female enrolment in tertiary education.
Pakistan's Educational Attainment score jumped to a record 91.7%, up by more than six percentage points from the previous edition. The improvement has been substantial over the longer term as well. Pakistan's education parity score has risen from 70.6% in 2006 to 91.7% in 2026, a gain of 21 percentage points.
The WEF said improvements across primary, secondary and tertiary enrolment have been the principal driver of Pakistan's progress in the overall index, with parity across these education indicators increasing by about 20 percentage points over the past two decades.
The sharp improvement in education contrasts with Pakistan's continuing difficulties in translating gains in schooling into greater participation in the economy.
Pakistan recorded a score of just 36.4% in Economic Participation and Opportunity, placing it 144th globally and last in South Asia. The score nevertheless increased by 1.6 percentage points from the previous edition.
The WEF estimates that Pakistan has the "eighth-largest workforce gender gap" among the economies covered by the index. Gender parity in labour-force participation stands at only 34.6%.

Cameras to be installed at 500 immigration counters
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said Pakistan has achieved a 64 per cent reduction in illegal migration towards Europe and reaffirmed the government's commitment to further strengthening measures against human smuggling and unlawful migration.
He made these remarks during separate meetings with Director General of the International Centre for Migration Policy Development (ICMPD) Susanne Raab and Executive Director of the European Union Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex) Hans Leijtens. The meetings focused on enhancing cooperation to prevent illegal migration, improve border management and strengthen joint efforts in the field.
During the discussions, Pakistan, ICMPD and Frontex agreed to expand mutual cooperation aimed at curbing illegal migration and improving border security mechanisms.
The participants also reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening coordinated measures for migration management and border control.
Naqvi said that achieving a 64 per cent reduction in illegal migration despite limited resources was a challenging task. He stated that the government accepted the prevention of illegal migration as a major challenge and that the entire team worked continuously to achieve the result.
The minister said the next target is to bring illegal migration down by 100 per cent and that all efforts would be directed towards achieving this objective.
He emphasized that opening new avenues for legal migration is necessary to further reduce illegal migration.
According to him, legal pathways can help address migration challenges while ensuring safe and regulated movement of people.
Naqvi stressed the need for modern technology and professional training of officers to strengthen efforts against illegal migration. He said the government is focusing on enhancing the capacity of relevant institutions in line with modern requirements to make border management more effective.
He added that practical measures and coordinated cooperation are required to completely eliminate illegal migration. The minister noted that cooperation with ICMPD and Frontex holds significant importance for Pakistan's migration management efforts.
Highlighting future plans, Naqvi said Pakistan aims to install technologically advanced cameras at 500 immigration counters across all airports in the country. He explained that the modern surveillance system would help authorities identify and take immediate action against individuals involved in illegal migration and human smuggling.
Director General ICMPD Susanne Raab appreciated Pakistan's efforts against illegal migration and acknowledged the measures taken by the country to address the issue. She said Pakistan's progress in reducing illegal migration was noteworthy and assured continued support in achieving the goal of completely eliminating the problem.
The ICMPD delegation also appreciated the Federal Investigation Agency's Risk Analysis Report and recognized the work being carried out to improve migration monitoring and enforcement mechanisms.
Frontex Executive Director Hans Leijtens also commended Pakistan's steps to curb illegal migration. He stated that the measures adopted by Pakistan had produced positive results and pledged full cooperation in helping the country achieve its target of completely eliminating illegal migration.

title: Fire scare triggers PIA plane evacuation
description: Jeddah Airport s fire and rescue authorities also rushed to aircraft with fire brigade vehicles following report
content:
Jeddah Airport's fire and rescue authorities also rushed to aircraft with fire brigade vehicles following report
Passengers were evacuated from a Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) Airbus aircraft at Jeddah airport on Thursday after ground staff suspected an engine fire shortly after the plane landed, prompting the crew to initiate an emergency evacuation.
According to sources, the aircraft had landed normally at Jeddah International Airport and reached the jetty when ground staff raised an alarm after suspecting that one of its engines had caught fire. The pilot responded by initiating the emergency evacuation procedure in accordance with SOPs.
They said some passengers left the aircraft through the jet bridge, while others were evacuated through emergency exits using the aircraft's evacuation slides.
Jeddah Airport's fire and rescue authorities also rushed to the aircraft with fire brigade vehicles following the report, while PIA officials in Jeddah informed airport administration and security authorities about the situation.
A PIA spokesperson said all passengers remained safe during the operation and there were no reports of any passenger being injured. Sources, however, said a few passengers sustained minor injuries during the emergency evacuation and were taken to the airport clinic for treatment.

title: Bushra seeks early FCC hearing
description: Former first lady asked the FCC to fix her appeal for hearing in the week commencing September 21
content:
Former first lady asked the FCC to fix her appeal for hearing in the week commencing September 21
Bushra Bibi, wife of incarcerated former prime minister and PTI founder Imran Khan, on Thursday approached the FCC for an urgent hearing of her appeal seeking suspension of her sentence in the £190 million Al-Qadir Trust case, citing a rapidly deteriorating eye condition that she says threatens her remaining eyesight.
In an application filed through her counsel, Barrister Salman Safdar, the former first lady asked the FCC to fix her appeal for hearing in the week commencing September 21, arguing that the prolonged delay in deciding her sentence suspension plea had already caused serious prejudice.

title: Amna Baloch retires as foreign secretary
description: Ambassador Baloch assumed the charge as the 33rd Foreign Secretary of Pakistan on September 11  2024
content:
Ambassador Baloch assumed the charge as the 33rd Foreign Secretary of Pakistan on September 11, 2024
Foreign Secretary Ambassador Amna Baloch on Thursday retried as foreign secretary, passing the helm of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to Ambassador Asim Iftikhar.
Ambassador Amna Baloch assumed the charge as the 33rd Foreign Secretary of Pakistan on September 11, 2024.
Her last appointment was as the Ambassador of Pakistan to Belgium, Luxembourg and the European Union from May 2023 to September 2024, before serving as High Commissioner of Pakistan to Malaysia from 2019 to 2023 and Consul General at Chengdu, China from 2014-2017.
